articles.title: Time to treatment of critical hypertension within 30 minutes and obstetrical outcomes.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate whether treatment of critical hypertension within 30 min, compared to treatment greater than or equal to 30 min, is associated with lower severe maternal morbidity (SMM).

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study analyzed pregnant patients with singleton gestations ≥20 weeks with critical hypertension [defined as persistent HTN with 2 consecutive SBP ≥160 or DBP ≥110 mm HG at least 15 min apart], who delivered between January 2021 and December 2022 at a single tertiary care center. Time to treatment was measured from the confirmatory second blood pressure reading to the time of antihypertensive administration. The study compared Group A (treatment time <30 min) with Group B (treatment time ≥30 min). The primary outcome was composite SMM, and secondary outcomes included composite severe neonatal morbidity (SNM), preterm birth, placental abruption, non-reassuring fetal heart tracing (NRFHT), and postpartum readmission. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for a set of baseline confounders. Statistical significance was set as p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Out of 370 patients screened, 271 met inclusion criteria (214 in Group A and 57 in Group B). Median time to treatment was 11 min (IQR 6-17) in Group A and 47 min (IQR 38-194) in Group B. Compared with Group B, patients in Group A were younger and had higher admission systolic and diastolic blood pressures. SMM occurred in 27 (12.6%) patients in Group A and 11 (19.3%) in Group B (unadjusted odds ratio [OR] for Group B vs. Group A 1.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-3.58; adjusted OR 1.77, 95% CI 0.80-3.91). SNM occurred in 56 (26.2%) and 14 (24.6%) patients, respectively (unadjusted OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.47-1.81). Results were consistent across sensitivity analyses, and no secondary outcome differed significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, we did not detect a statistically significant difference in SMM between patients treated within 30 min and those treated later. The confidence intervals were wide and do not exclude a clinically important benefit of earlier treatment, and these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence. Treatment of acute-onset severe hypertension as soon as reasonably possible should remain the standard, and adequately powered prospective studies, including randomized trials, are needed to define the optimal treatment interval.

articles.title: Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
articles.abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.

articles.title: Rehospitalizations after acute myocardial infarction in patients diagnosed by coronary angiography - the MADDEC study.
articles.abstract: Objectives. The rate of rehospitalizations and fatal adverse events after myocardial infarction (MI) is reportedly high in previous studies and reducing these events is considered an important goal. This study aimed to clarify the rate of serious events leading to hospitalization or death after invasively managed MI in a contemporary setting. Design. In a retrospective registry study, the rate of serious adverse events leading to rehospitalizations or death during the first year after MI was examined from Tampere University hospital records. Study population consisted of all consecutive MI patients who underwent coronary angiography at Tays Heart Hospital between 2012 and 2016. This study focused on bleeding events, cerebrovascular events, exacerbation of heart failure, recurrent MI and unstable angina pectoris leading to rehospitalization. Results. During the five-year period, 2904 consecutive patients were treated for MI and successfully discharged or transferred to a primary health care unit (95.5% of all patients). 4.8% of these patients died during the first year after MI with 66.2% of all deaths due to cardiac causes, fatal bleeds, infections, or cerebrovascular events. Of all patients, 17.8% were rehospitalized for these causes and adding events leading to death without rehospitalization, the rate of serious events was 18.8%. Age but not sex, associated significantly with the rate of serious adverse events with the cumulative incidence exceeding 20% in patients aged 70-79 years and reaching 29% in patients ≥80 years. Conclusions. Cause-specific rehospitalization rates were low, but highly dependent on age.

articles.title: Postoperative atrial fibrillation and use of oral anticoagulants after cardiac surgery: a real-life, single-centre study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication following cardiac surgery and is associated with significant morbidity. This study sought to provide a comprehensive and contemporary evaluation of the clinical course and management of POAF, with particular emphasis on the use of oral anticoagulants (OACs).

DESIGN: This single-centre, retrospective, longitudinal study included patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass at Skåne University Hospital, Lund, between February 2020 and September 2021. Included patients had no prior history of atrial fibrillation (AF) or atrial flutter and survived to hospital discharge. Patients were excluded if they underwent redo surgery, heart transplantation, hypothermic circulatory arrest or had endocarditis. Data on POAF and OAC use were obtained through retrospective chart review.

RESULTS: 1,012 patients were included, of whom 43% developed POAF. Among POAF patients, 8.8% were discharged with ongoing AF. OACs were prescribed to 38% of POAF patients at hospital discharge, with 31% of prescriptions initiated by a cardiothoracic surgeon. The cumulative incidence of documented AF was 7.9% at 3-month follow-up and 8.8% at 1 year. However, 89% of POAF patients remained on OAC therapy at 1-year follow-up, despite the low rates of documented AF recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: POAF is frequently observed after cardiac surgery but typically resolves during the early postoperative period. Nonetheless, a substantial proportion of patients were prescribed and remained on long-term OAC therapy despite an absence of documented AF at follow-up and the heightened bleeding risk of this population.

articles.title: Association of retinal abnormalities and adverse cardiac events in patients with coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to evaluate the association of retinal abnormalities and cardiac mortality in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes (DM).

METHODS: The ARTEMIS study is a prospective cohort study of 1,946 patients (68% male; mean age 66.9 ± 8.6 years) diagnosed with CAD. Type 2 DM was diagnosed in 834 patients (43%), and 525 (27%) of them had retinal images available.

RESULTS: During mean follow-up of 8.7 ± 2.2 years, 54 cardiac deaths occurred. From all analyzed retinal abnormalities, diabetic retinopathy (DR) was associated with cardiac death (p = 0.005). DR was independently associated with increased risk of cardiac death (DR 16.2% vs. non-DR 8.4%; hazard ratio [HR] 2.0, 95% CI: 1.0-4.0, p = 0.04) when adjusted with confounding factors. DR was associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD) (DR 8.5% vs. non-DR 3.8%; HR 2.9, 95% CI: 1.1-7.7, p = 0.03) but not with non-sudden cardiac death (DR 7.7% vs. non-DR 4.6%; HR 1.5, 95% CI: 0.6-3.9, p = 0.5). Interestingly, increased hs-TnT, measured in stable phase of CAD, was also associated with DR (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DR seems to be associated with cardiac death, and more specifically, with SCD in patients with CAD and type 2 DM. DR might be a novel marker of microvascular cardiac disease resulting in ongoing myocardial injury and SCD.

articles.title: Reply to the letter to the editor: "exercise capacity-based risk stratification in adult congenital heart disease: from prognosis to clinical use".
A structured framework for assessment of rehabilitation and sick-listing (STARS) - experiences among healthcare professionals.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: The sick-listing process is often perceived uncertain and unclear by both patients and staff. To improve the process, a framework for structured assessment of rehabilitation and sick-listing (STARS) has been developed in the South-Eastern Healthcare Region in Sweden. STARS consists of seven methodological tools supporting healthcare professionals in sick-listing and rehabilitation. The purpose of this study was to investigate how primary healthcare staff clinically involved in the sick leave process experience working according to STARS.

METHOD: We used a qualitative design conducting focus group discussions (n = 7) with healthcare staff (n = 37). Eligible participants were physicians, rehabilitation coordinators and other healthcare professionals working clinically with patients. The focus group conversations were analyzed with thematic content analysis according to Braun and Clarke. The study was registered in clinicaltrials.gov (number NCT05655962).

RESULT: The participants' experience of working according to STARS were described by the overarching theme 'STARS as an enabling structure' formed by three themes and eight subthemes. The themes were 'Clearer roles and responsibilities through the RECO function', 'Moving from individual work to teamwork' and 'A more active and personalized rehabilitation and sick-listing process'.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that implementing the STARS framework may provide a supportive structure for a uniform and consistent way of working across primary healthcare centers. By clarifying RECOs' roles and strengthening interprofessional collaboration, the framework may support a more patient-centered approach across services.

articles.title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses.

RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02.

CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

articles.title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
articles.abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

articles.title: Sleep EEG oscillations and synaptic plasticity in memory consolidation across NREM and REM sleep.
articles.abstract: Based on a synthesis of recent advances, this review elucidates the distinct yet synergistic roles of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep in memory consolidation. During NREM sleep, cortical slow oscillations (SOs) establish a temporal framework by alternating between UP and DOWN states, facilitating cross-regional communication. SOs phase-couple with thalamic spindles to coordinate hippocampal sharp-wave ripples (SWRs), thereby driving the reactivation and transfer of labile hippocampal memories to neocortical networks for long-term storage. Concurrent synaptic homeostasis optimises network efficiency through global downscaling while selectively strengthening memory-relevant connections. In REM sleep, theta oscillations synchronise limbic-prefrontal-hippocampal circuits, and ponto-geniculo-occipital (PGO) waves further integrate emotional and procedural memories. The cholinergically dominant, monoamine-depleted neurochemical milieu of REM sleep promotes dendritic spine remodelling and sparse neuronal reactivation, enabling affective decoupling and synaptic refinement. Despite progress, key challenges remain in understanding cross-frequency oscillatory coupling among slow oscillations, spindles, ripples and REM-specific rhythms, glial contributions and clinical translation. Future integration of high-density electrophysiology with computational approaches may yield mechanistic models and clinically relevant biomarkers for sleep-based cognitive monitoring and intervention.

articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

articles.title: Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time.

DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016.

RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk.

CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

articles.title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD.

METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset.

RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data.

CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

articles.title: Comparative efficacy of topical garlic extract and 20% podophyllin solution in the treatment of female genital warts: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genital warts caused by human papillomavirus are common sexually transmitted infections, with no single therapy providing consistent clearance. Garlic extract has antiviral and antiproliferative properties and may offer a low-cost treatment.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of topical 5% garlic extract with 20% podophyllin solution in women with genital warts.

METHODS: Seventy-four women were randomized to 5% garlic extract (n = 37) or 20% podophyllin (n = 37), applied weekly for four weeks. Wart size and count were assessed using marginal models (generalized estimating equations). The primary outcome was change in mean wart size and the secondary outcome was change in wart count.

RESULTS: Mean wart size decreased from 1.61 ± 0.81 to 0.60 ± 0.82 mm with garlic extract and from 2.96 ± 7.99 to 0.62 ± 0.73 mm with podophyllin. The between-group p-value at final assessment was 0.756; group × time interaction p values were 0.329 for wart size and 0.583 for count. Among 35 and 37 participants analyzed, complete response occurred in 18 (51.4%) and 19 (51.4%), respectively; complete or partial response occurred in 23 (65.7%) and 25 (67.6%). Itching and burning occurred in 8 (21.6%) garlic-treated participants each.

CONCLUSION: Both treatments reduced wart size and count, with similar response rates. Four-week follow-up precluded assessment of durability and recurrence.

articles.title: Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers.

DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection.

RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

articles.title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33).

CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

articles.title: Gut microbiota and metabolic characteristics in PWHIV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
articles.abstract: The global prevalence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among persons with HIV (PWHIV) is estimated at 34%. This study examined the influence of gut microbial and metabolic alterations in PWHIV with MASLD. We conducted 16S rRNA sequencing on 60 fecal samples (24 from HIV group and 36 from HIV-MASLD group) to assess microbial composition, and employed LC/MS-based metabolomics on both fecal and plasma samples to identify variations in metabolites. An exploratory analysis was performed to compare plasma cytokines and oxidative stress markers between the two groups. Sequencing in the HIV-MASLD group showed lower Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, and higher Klebsiella, Escherichia, and Enterococcus. Metabolomic analysis revealed a reduction in anti-inflammatory metabolites (Dodecanedioic acid, 5-Phenylvaleric acid, Kynurenic acid) and antioxidant metabolites, coupled with an increase in the pro-inflammatory metabolite Gamma-Glutamyl-L-Putrescine in the HIV-MASLD group. And plasma analysis indicated a decline in 20-carboxy arachidonic acid. Additionally, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum correlated positively with anti-inflammatory metabolites, while Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter correlated negatively. Furthermore, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum also showed a moderate negative correlation with MDA levels. A random forest model using plasma metabolites showed the optimal discriminative ability for HIV-MASLD (AUC = 0.819 ± 0.0059). Differences in gut microbiota and metabolites in PWHIV may affect MASLD progression by influencing inflammation and oxidative stress. Modulating gut microbiota, such as adding Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, could be a treatment strategy for HIV-MASLD. Plasma metabolites have potential as noninvasive markers.

articles.title: Reply to the letter-to-the-editor "Percutaneous coronary intervention in nonagenarians".
Mortality patterns over two decades in U.S. adults with both diabetes and hypothyroidism: a retrospective analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypothyroidism and diabetes mellitus frequently coexist and share autoimmune and metabolic pathways, yet population-level data on how their combined mortality burden has changed over time, and how it is distributed across demographic and geographic groups, remain limited. We examined national trends and disparities in mortality among United States (US) adults with both conditions.

METHODS: In this retrospective, population-based analysis, death-certificate data for 1999-2023 were obtained from the Multiple Cause of Death database of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging ONline Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER). US resident decedents aged ≥ 25 years whose death certificates listed both hypothyroidism (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] code E03) and diabetes mellitus (E10-E14) as either the underlying or a contributing cause of death were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population, standardized to the 2000 US standard population, and crude mortality rates were calculated and stratified by sex, age, race and ethnicity, urban-rural status, census region, and state. Urban-rural and state-level analyses covered 1999-2020. Temporal trends were assessed with Joinpoint regression, yielding the annual percentage change (APC) for each segment and the average annual percentage change (AAPC) over the full period. A two-sided p value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: A total of 119,113 deaths were identified over the 25-year period, with annual deaths rising from 2,934 in 1999 to 7,537 in 2023. The overall AAMR rose from 1.67 in 1999 to a peak of 3.10 in 2021 before declining slightly to 2.73 in 2023 (AAPC 1.86; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.88-2.85). Mortality was consistently higher in women than in men (AAMR 3.05 vs. 2.31 in 2023), although men showed a steeper long-term increase (AAPC 2.99; 95% CI 1.68-4.31 vs. 1.48; 95% CI 0.29-2.68). Older adults (≥ 65 years) carried an absolute burden roughly ten times that of middle-aged adults and far higher than that of young adults. The highest single-year rate among racial and ethnic groups occurred in the Hispanic or Latino population (4.28 in 2020), followed by White, Black or African American, and other groups; the long-term increase was significant among White individuals (AAPC 2.04; 95% CI 0.86-3.24) but not among Hispanic or Latino individuals (AAPC 1.95; 95% CI - 0.06 to 4.01). Rural (non-metropolitan) areas were disproportionately affected, peaking at 4.15 in 2020 versus 2.69 in urban areas (1999-2020 AAPC 3.26 vs. 2.14). The highest pooled state-level rates (1999-2020) were in West Virginia (4.16), North Dakota (3.65), and Ohio (3.57); by census region, the South showed the steepest long-term increase (AAPC 2.66; 95% CI 1.21-4.14) and the highest rate by 2023 (2.97), whereas the Midwest showed no significant long-term change.

CONCLUSION: Mortality among US adults with coexisting hypothyroidism and diabetes increased significantly between 1999 and 2023, with a pronounced peak in 2021 and persistent disparities by sex, age, race and ethnicity, and geography. These findings support early thyroid screening in high-risk diabetic populations, equitable access to care, and region-specific prevention to reduce disparities and improve outcomes.

articles.title: Environmental microbial exposure as an under-measured exposome domain: Links to host microbiomes, immune regulation, and disease epidemiology.
articles.journal: Journal of environmental health science & engineering
articles.abstract: Environmental microbial exposure is an under-measured biological component of the exposome and a plausible determinant of immune-mediated disease patterns. Humans encounter microbial communities and products from soil, air, water, vegetation, animals, food systems, farms, indoor dust, healthcare settings, schools, and urban built environments. These exposures may influence gut, skin, airway, oral, and mucosal microbiomes and thereby alter epithelial barrier function, immune tolerance, inflammatory thresholds, and microbial metabolite production. This structured mechanistic narrative review integrates direct environmental-exposure studies, environment-to-host microbiome studies, host-microbiome mechanistic evidence, and translational frameworks. The clearest convergence occurs in asthma and allergic disease, where early-life farm exposure, endotoxin-rich dust, environmental microbial diversity, innate immune modulation, and epithelial A20 regulation support a coherent exposure-response model. Evidence for inflammatory bowel disease and broader respiratory outcomes is biologically credible but less direct, whereas metabolic and systemic inflammatory outcomes remain largely supported by host-microbiome and metabolite mechanisms rather than direct environmental exposure studies. The review therefore distinguishes evidence maturity and mechanistic proximity rather than treating all disease categories equally. It further positions pollution, urbanization, building design, biodiversity loss, diet, antibiotics, and socioeconomic conditions as active modifiers of microbial exposure and host response. Future studies should integrate direct environmental sampling with body-site microbiome profiling, functional multi-omics, immune and barrier biomarkers, geospatial exposure assessment, source tracking, repeated measures, and explicit causal-inference designs. Environmental microbial exposure should be treated neither as uniformly beneficial nor harmful, but as a measurable, context-dependent exposome domain whose health effects depend on composition, dose, timing, route, co-exposures, and host susceptibility.

articles.title: Understanding diabetes through social determinants of health: An umbrella review in the Eastern Mediterranean Region.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes is a main public health concern in the Eastern Mediterranean Region, where social determinants of health are associated with disease occurrence, diagnosis, self-management, complications, and quality of life. Although several reviews have examined diabetes in this region, differences in their scopes, methods, quality, and reporting have limited a consolidated understanding of the social determinants associated with the disease. This umbrella review synthesized evidence from existing reviews on diabetes related social determinants across Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) countries using an ICD-10 Z-code framework.

METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched for review articles published between January 2000 and April 21, 2025. Eligible reviews included narrative reviews, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, umbrella reviews, and scoping reviews that examined social or economic determinants of diabetes in human populations from EMR countries. Titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through consensus or third reviewer adjudication. Methodological quality was assessed using SANRA for narrative reviews and CAT HPPR for systematic, meta-analytic, and scoping reviews. Extracted determinants were synthesized through conceptual mapping to ICD-10 Z-codes Z55 to Z65 and Z70 to Z76.

RESULTS: Of 119 retrieved records, 55 reviews met the inclusion criteria. Reviews were published between 2000 and 2025 and most commonly covered Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Pakistan. The core synthesis identified 343 reported occurrences of social determinants of health mapped to ICD-10 Z55-Z65, with housing and economic circumstances and the social environment most frequently reported. A separate contextual synthesis described 262 Z70-Z76 findings related to behavioural pathways, life-management conditions, and health-service encounters; these were not counted as social determinants of health. Associations were reported across diabetes occurrence, diagnosis, management, complications, and quality of life. Biological and clinical factors were treated as correlates or stratifiers rather than social determinants of health.

CONCLUSION: Across the EMR, diabetes was consistently reported in relation to material disadvantage, food insecurity, limited health literacy, constrained social support, and barriers to timely and continuous care. Behavioural factors and health-service encounters should be interpreted as pathways or contextual conditions, rather than SDH in isolation. The geographically uneven and predominantly narrative evidence supports policies that strengthen financial protection, health literacy, and equitable access to sustained diabetes care, alongside research from underrepresented countries.

articles.title: Next-generation anti-obesity drugs: emerging molecular targets and translational opportunities.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Obesity is a heterogeneous, chronic metabolic disease driven by dysregulation of energy homeostasis across interconnected central nervous system, gastrointestinal, adipose, endocrine, immune, and mitochondrial networks. Despite the established roles of lifestyle intervention and metabolic/bariatric surgery, limitations in accessibility, durability, and interindividual response have stimulated the development of mechanism-based pharmacotherapies. This review critically examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting integrated energy-regulatory pathways and evaluates their translational potential for precision obesity management.

METHODS: Current evidence was synthesized across major biological systems governing appetite, energy expenditure, and metabolic adaptation. Central melanocortin, Neuropeptide Y (NPY)/ Agouti-related peptide (AgRP), serotonergic, dopaminergic, and endocannabinoid pathways were considered alongside gut-derived incretin, amylin, Peptide YY (PYY), ghrelin, Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF), and bile acid signaling. Emerging approaches targeting adipose remodeling, thermogenesis, mitochondrial energetics, AMPK-mTOR-sirtuin signaling, inflammation, and fibrosis were also evaluated. Genetic, epigenetic, and artificial intelligence-based approaches to patient stratification were incorporated to assess prospects for precision therapy.

RESULTS: Obesity pharmacotherapy is shifting from conventional appetite suppression toward coordinated modulation of interconnected metabolic pathways. Incretin-based and multi-agonist therapies provide the strongest clinical evidence for substantial weight reduction and metabolic improvement. However, treatment discontinuation, weight regain, adverse effects, cost, and heterogeneous therapeutic responses remain major challenges. Strategies targeting adipose tissue dysfunction, mitochondrial metabolism, thermogenesis, immune-metabolic signaling, and fibrosis offer additional opportunities for disease modification, although many remain in preclinical or early clinical development. Increasing evidence for biological heterogeneity supports individualized therapeutic selection.

CONCLUSION: The emerging therapeutic paradigm positions obesity as a systems-level disorder requiring mechanism-informed, individualized intervention. Integrating CNS-gut-adipose-mitochondrial biology with multi-omics, biomarkers, and artificial intelligence may enable more durable and precise treatment. Long-term safety, durability, affordability, equitable access, and clinical validation remain essential for translation.

articles.title: Circulating LRG1 in heart failure: association with type 2 diabetes and antidiabetic therapy class.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and share remodelling and inflammatory mechanisms. Although leucine-rich α-2 glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) has been identified as a biomarker associated with vascular remodelling, fibrosis, and inflammation, its role in HF patients with type 2 diabetes and its connection to antidiabetic treatments remains unclear.

METHODS: 115 patients with HF were divided into three groups for this cross-sectional study: HF who had no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and were not receiving antidiabetic medication at enrolment (n = 42), HF with T2DM treated with DPP-4 inhibitors (n = 35), and HF with T2DM treated with SGLT-2 inhibitors (n = 38). The groups' clinical characteristics, metabolic parameters, and circulating LRG1 levels were compared.

RESULTS: LRG1 levels differed significantly across the groups (p = 0.002), with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. A post hoc analysis revealed a significant difference between the SGLT-2 inhibitor group and group of no previously documented diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (p = 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between LRG1 and clinical or metabolic variables.

CONCLUSION: Circulating LRG1 levels in HF patients differed between study groups, with the lowest levels observed in the SGLT-2 inhibitor group. These findings suggest an association between treatment group and LRG1 levels, but the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the effects of antidiabetic medications on inflammatory and remodelling pathways.

articles.title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses.
articles.abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat-methanol cross-adaptation.

articles.title: Pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface coordinates infection control and osseointegration.
articles.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) compromises osseointegration through bacterial colonisation and dysregulated inflammation. Here, we pre-established a living biointerface by seeding immunity-and-matrix-regulatory cells (IMRCs) onto three-dimensional (3D)-printed titanium prostheses modified with silver (Ag) by plasma immersion ion implantation (Ag-PIII) before bacterial exposure, generating an IMRC-seeded Ag-PIII-modified titanium (TAM) construct. TAM was associated with reduced bacterial attachment. The Ag-PIII-modified substrate achieved antibacterial efficiencies above 99% against Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli while supporting IMRC viability and attachment. TAM-conditioned medium favoured an M2-like macrophage profile, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells. In the beagle PJI model, TAM reduced bacterial recovery and peri-implant inflammation and improved bone formation, fixation strength, and locomotor performance at 8 weeks. These findings provide preclinical support for pre-establishing an IMRC-seeded living biointerface to alter the initial conditions of surface competition and integrate early infection control with subsequent osseointegration.

articles.title: Dual-synergistic engineered MXene sonosensitizer with stabilized semiquinone radicals enables biofilm eradication and immunomodulatory bone regeneration in osteomyelitis.
articles.abstract: Deep colonization of drug-resistant biofilms and impaired bone regeneration within the infectious microenvironment represent two major bottlenecks in the clinical management of osteomyelitis. Herein, we design a dually synergistically modified Ti3C2 MXene sonosensitizer. Lattice strain is introduced via Zn2+ substitution doping, while interfacial passivation is achieved by coordination-stabilized dopamine semiquinone radicals. Such engineering extends the carrier lifetime by 86-fold, enabling efficient generation of hydroxyl radicals under ultrasound irradiation. This engineered material exhibits triple biofunctional activities: it eliminates over 99.9% of MRSA biofilms in vitro and downregulates bacterial drug-resistance pathways; sustained Zn2+ release polarizes macrophages toward the pro-repair M2 phenotype to remodel the inflammatory microenvironment of infected tissues; in a rat osteomyelitis model, a single local administration combined with ultrasound eradicates deep-seated infection, facilitates collagen deposition and bone regeneration, with favorable biosafety both in vitro and in vivo. This work offers a strategy based on novel multifunctional bioactive materials for treating infectious bone defects, holding promising potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

articles.title: Long-standing Chronic Diarrhea Associated With Intestinal Spirochetosis Incidentally Diagnosed in a Rectal Adenoma Specimen Resected by Cold Snare Polypectomy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Intestinal spirochetosis (IS) is an uncommon condition that is often asymptomatic and detected incidentally but may occasionally present with chronic diarrhea. We report a case of IS incidentally identified in the adjacent non-neoplastic mucosa of a rectal adenoma specimen resected by cold snare polypectomy. We present a case of a man in his 50s who was referred for a positive fecal occult blood test and had a history of chronic diarrhea. Colonoscopy revealed a 5-mm sessile polyp in the upper rectum, which was removed by cold snare polypectomy. Histopathological examination showed a tubular adenoma. In addition, routine hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed a characteristic false brush border on the adjacent non-neoplastic colorectal epithelium, consistent with IS. A detailed medical interview subsequently revealed chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years and prolonged close contact with a pet dog. Treatment with metronidazole (1500 mg/day for 10 days) resulted in resolution of the diarrhea. This case highlights the importance of careful histopathological examination and detailed history-taking in patients with IS.

articles.title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

articles.title: Defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerfaces enable ultrasound-amplified built-in electric fields for bacterial envelope destabilization and implant infection control.
articles.abstract: Built-in electric fields (BIEFs) at piezoelectric heterointerfaces are widely invoked to assist charge separation, but their contribution to antibacterial activity under ultrasound remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a defect-engineered piezoelectric heterointerface strategy to investigate BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects. Density functional theory (DFT)-guided screening identifies a dual-vacancy piezoelectric heterojunction (BTO3-X/MoS2-X) with enhanced interfacial polarization. Under ultrasound, BTO3-X/MoS2-X efficiently kills Staphylococcus aureus, accompanied by pronounced bacterial envelope destabilization. This response is accompanied by membrane lipid perturbation, increased permeability, respiratory inhibition, and intracellular ROS accumulation. GROMACS simulations show that a model lipid bilayer destabilizes only under a sufficiently strong applied electric field. In infected implant models, ultrasound activated BTO3-X/MoS2-X reduces early peri-implant bacterial burden and promotes a repair-favorable inflammatory microenvironment. These findings highlight the potential contribution of BIEF-related interfacial electrical effects to ultrasound responsive antibacterial activity and offer a defect-engineering strategy for implant infection control.

articles.title: Engineering copper homeostasis for microenvironment-adaptive therapy in inflammation-driven disorders.
articles.abstract: Inflammation-driven disorders (IDDs) arise from distinct initiating events, yet many persist because immune activation, oxidative and metabolic stress, regulated cell death, and tissue remodeling form self-reinforcing local niches. Copper connects these processes through its roles as a cuproenzyme cofactor, redox-active species and dynamically trafficked regulatory metal. Its therapeutic significance, however, is determined by disease stage, cell type, subcellular distribution and chemical state. Copper deficiency, excess or mislocalization may therefore be adaptive, protective or pathogenic in different contexts. This review develops a disease- and copper-state-specific framework that links copper homeostasis to therapeutic platform design. We first examine inflammation-associated remodeling of copper trafficking and compare representative copper states in autoimmune joint disease, metabolic inflammation, fibrosis, inflammation-associated cancer and infection-associated tissue repair. We then critically evaluate copper-dependent and copper-sensitive mechanisms governing inflammatory mediator availability, immune-cell programming and checkpoint regulation, regulated cell death, angiogenesis and stromal remodeling, while distinguishing direct mechanistic evidence from model-dependent inference. Building on this analysis, we compare pharmacological modulators with nanocarriers, copper-containing active materials and local copper-sequestering platforms that implement copper chelation or sequestration, controlled copper delivery or release, intracellular redistribution, and catalytic activation or nanozyme-like redox regulation. We further outline how pathological copper pools, activation cues, release kinetics, speciation, biodistribution and target engagement should be measured so that precision is demonstrated rather than inferred from material composition. This framework positions copper modulation as a context-specific complement to existing therapy and defines the mechanistic, analytical and translational evidence required for microenvironment-adaptive treatment of IDDs.

articles.title: Staged photothermal hydrogel containing manganese-doped bioactive glass nanoparticles promotes infected bone regeneration by engaging Schwann cell PI3K/AKT signaling and neuro-osteogenic coupling.
articles.abstract: Infected bone lesions are characterized by concurrent bacterial infection, persistent inflammatory infiltration, peripheral nerve damage, and impaired osteogenesis. However, most biomaterials address only antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, or osteogenic functions while overlooking nerve-bone crosstalk during tissue repair. Here, we engineered QOMB, an injectable photothermal hydrogel responsive to near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, by embedding manganese-doped bioactive glass nanoparticles (Mn-BGN) within a dynamically crosslinked network of gallic acid-grafted quaternized chitosan (QCSG) and oxidized sodium alginate (OSA). QOMB exerts synergistic photothermal antibacterial effects and promotes anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization within inflammatory microenvironments. More importantly, ions released from Mn-BGN stimulate Schwann cells (SCs) to secrete abundant neurotrophic factors, thereby establishing a pro-regenerative paracrine niche that promotes osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation demonstrated that stimulation with Mn-BGN-derived ionic cues activates PI3K/AKT signaling and enhances neurotrophic factor secretion by SCs. In a rat model of infected femoral condylar defects, QOMB administration combined with sequential NIR irradiation markedly suppressed local bacterial colonization, attenuated chronic inflammation, enhanced neurotrophic signaling, and accelerated de novo bone formation. These results support a material-Schwann cell-bone regulatory pathway that coordinates staged infection control and immune reprogramming with neuro-osteogenic repair.

articles.title: An optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched dual-crosslinkable hydrogel for cell-free remodeling of the corneal stroma.
articles.abstract: Corneal trauma is a leading cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide, yet corneal stromal repair and regeneration remain a significant challenge in ophthalmology because of its limited intrinsic repair capacity and fibrotic scar formation during healing process. Here we report an optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel that enables cell-free corneal stromal remodeling. By integrating dynamic covalent crosslinking with static photocrosslinking strategy, the optimized hydrogel-based substitute achieved high optical transparency, a refractive index of approximately 1.35, and an elastic modulus of 83.8 ± 13.4 kPa, closely resembling the properties of the healthy human cornea. In a rabbit model of deep corneal defects, the optimized in situ-forming hydrogel adapted to the defect geometry, adhered stably to the wound bed, recapitulated the optical and biomechanical properties of the native cornea, and supported scarless corneal stromal remodeling. Incorporation of the antimicrobial peptide HHC36 further endowed the hydrogel with robust antibacterial activity without compromising its optical and biomechanical properties. In a rabbit model of P. aeruginosa-infected deep corneal defects, the HHC36-loaded in situ-forming hydrogel effectively mitigated clinical signs of infection and substantially promoted corneal stromal remodeling within 30 days while reducing fibrosis. Overall, this optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel might be a promising substitute for corneal stromal remodeling.

articles.title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence.

RESULTS: Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

articles.title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy.

METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors.

RESULTS: Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000053211.

articles.title: A 6His-2Flag dual-tag strategy enables high-yield production of antimicrobial peptide N6 in Pichia pastoris to combat multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumonia.
articles.abstract: In response to the global threat posed by multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, this study established an efficient heterologous expression system for the antimicrobial peptide N6 in Pichia pastoris X-33. By employing an innovative 6His-2Flag dual-tag fusion strategy coupled with formic acid-mediated cleavage, we achieved a high-yield production of N6, with a final titer of 1.02 g/L-significantly surpassing previous reports and meeting the threshold for scalable industrial production. The expressed N6 exhibited potent and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against clinical isolates of K. pneumoniae, with MIC values ranging from 2 to 8 μg/mL. Mechanistic studies revealed that N6 exerted rapid bactericidal and biofilm-eradicating effects through a multimodal action involving membrane disruption, metabolic interference, and induction of oxidative stress. In a murine systemic infection model, the N6 treatment significantly improved survival rates of mice to 70% and reduced bacterial burdens in key organs. This work not only identifies N6 as a promising therapeutic candidate against drug-resistant bacterial infections, but also provides a streamlined and cost-effective synthetic biology platform for the high-level production of antimicrobial peptides, thereby facilitating their clinical translation and industrial application.

articles.title: Genetic engineering of cyanophages for harmful cyanobacterial bloom treatment-A mini review.
articles.abstract: Harmful cyanobacterial blooms (HCBs) are a prominent worldwide environmental concern. Proliferation of HCBs outpaces the development of mitigation and management technologies. Recently, cyanophages began to emerge as a potential abundant resource that can be harnessed for target-specific HCB treatment. However, there exist two major technical barriers in applying cyanophage-based treatment to HCB mitigation: host specificity and lysogenic life cycle. This minireview attempts to parse documented studies that developed or applied genetic engineering approaches or technologies to tackle the barriers through expanding host range and bypassing or abolishing the lysogenic life stage. We summarized representative technical approaches that may be extrapolated from bacteriophage to cyanophage, discussed genes and pathways that regulate host binding and infection or determine the switch between lytic and lysogenic lifecycles, identified existing knowledge and technological gaps and challenges, and proposed some attainable solutions and future perspectives for this fast-growing field of engineered cyanophage-mediated HCB remediation.

articles.title: Disseminated Klebsiella pneumoniae Infection Mimicking Multiple Colonic Subepithelial Lesions: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of disseminated Klebsiella pneumoniae infection mimicking multiple subepithelial lesion (SEL)-like elevations throughout the colon. A 73-year-old man was referred for the treatment of diarrhea, edema, and anemia. Colonoscopy revealed numerous SEL-like elevations from the cecum to the rectum, raising suspicion for malignant or infiltrative disease. Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated thickening centered in the deep mucosa and muscularis mucosae, with possible extension into the submucosa. Histological examination showed inflammatory cell infiltration, and bacterial culture of biopsy material identified K. pneumoniae. Further systemic evaluation revealed pacemaker lead infection, infective endocarditis, and pyogenic spondylitis, indicating disseminated infection. The colonic lesions improved after targeted antimicrobial therapy and device management. This rare case underscores the importance of considering disseminated bacterial infection in diffuse SEL-like colonic elevations, particularly when accompanied by systemic infectious manifestations.

articles.title: Endoscopic Injection Sclerotherapy With Pre-deflation Ligation for Prolonged Sclerosant Retention in Esophageal Varices: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Esophageal varices are a common complication of portal hypertension, and prophylactic endoscopic injection sclerotherapy with ligation (EISL) is an established treatment option. Effective variceal thrombosis requires sufficient intravariceal retention of the sclerosant, because ethanolamine oleate exerts its thrombogenic effect through prolonged contact with the venous endothelium. In conventional EISL, endoscopic variceal ligation (EVL) is performed after balloon deflation, leaving a transient interval during which restored blood flow and an open puncture site may permit washout of the sclerosant and bleeding. We describe EIS with pre-deflation ligation (EISpdL), in which EVL of the puncture site is completed while the endoscope balloon remains inflated, and balloon compression is maintained throughout the retention period. A 59-year-old man with medium-sized esophageal varices with a positive red color sign (F2, RC1) secondary to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis underwent EISpdL combined with gel-immersion EIS. The procedure was technically feasible, required no additional skills beyond conventional EISL, and no immediate procedure-related adverse events were observed. Follow-up endoscopy on post-procedure day 7 showed bronze-colored variceal changes indicating thrombosis, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography two months later confirmed obliteration. EISpdL may enable more stable and prolonged sclerosant retention.

articles.title: Bethesda Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Skill Assessment Tool (BESAT)-Based Simulator Training Using a Novel Dry Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Model Improves Technical Proficiency and Self-Efficacy: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Endoscopic sphincterotomy (EST) is a high-risk procedure with a steep learning curve. We previously developed a novel dry simulator capable of reproducing bleeding after an inappropriate incision. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured educational program using the simulator within the Bethesda Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) Skill Assessment Tool (BESAT) framework.

METHODS: This prospective study implemented a standardized training sequence: (1) preliminary video-based learning; (2) an initial attempt at cannulation, EST, and biliary stone extraction; (3) BESAT-based expert feedback focusing on six key technical tips; (4) a second attempt. The primary outcome was the change in EST success, which is defined by an incision in the 11-12 o'clock direction with appropriate length and no bleeding, before and after feedback. Secondary outcomes were procedure completion, including stone removal within 15 min, and subjective self-assessments of procedural understanding and confidence.

RESULTS: Thirty gastroenterology trainees were enrolled. The EST success rate increased from 43.3% to 76.7% (p < 0.05). The completion rate of the procedure tended to increase from 46.7% to 70.0% (p = 0.07). Subjective self-confidence improved from a median of 24.0-53.0 after training and remained at 53.5 at 3 months; other self-assessed domains also improved and were sustained. Post-hoc analysis showed that initial EST success was associated with >50 prior ERCP cases (odds ratio = 7.86, 95% confidence interval: 1.31-47.0, p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: A structured simulator-based program enables trainees to experience failure and improves simulator-based EST performance with sustained gains in self-efficacy. Trial Registration: The trial was prospectively registered in the University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry (UMIN000044823).

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Sensitivity of Endoscopic Ultrasound-guided Tissue Acquisition for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Versus Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Accurate histological differentiation between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is essential for selecting appropriate treatment. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA) is increasingly used for focal liver lesions; however, comparative data on its diagnostic sensitivity for HCC and ICC remain limited. This study compared the diagnostic sensitivity of EUS-TA for these malignancies.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included patients who underwent EUS-TA for focal liver lesions and were ultimately diagnosed with HCC or ICC between 2016 and 2024. Patients with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma were excluded. The primary outcome was overall diagnostic sensitivity. Secondary outcomes were cytological sensitivity and procedure-related adverse events.

RESULTS: Forty-five patients were included (HCC, n = 18; ICC, n = 27). Median lesion size was 41 mm. Baseline characteristics were similar, except that fine-needle biopsy needles were used less frequently in HCC than in ICC (16.6% vs. 48.1%, p = 0.032). Overall diagnostic sensitivity was high in both groups but lower in HCC than in ICC (83.3% [95% confidence interval {CI}, 58.6-96.4%] vs. 100% [95% CI, 87.2%-100%], p = 0.029). The difference was more pronounced for cytological sensitivity (22.2% [95% CI, 6.4%-47.6%] vs. 77.8% [95% CI, 57.7%-91.4%], p = 0.0007). No procedure-related adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: EUS-TA demonstrated high diagnostic sensitivity for both HCC and ICC without procedure-related adverse events. However, diagnostic sensitivity, particularly cytological sensitivity, was lower in HCC, consistent with the known pathological characteristics of HCC and the established role of histological evaluation in its diagnosis. Trial Registration: N/A.

articles.title: Apparent Endoscopic Decrease in the Size of a Large Ulcerated Gastric Schwannoma After Helicobacter pylori Eradication Therapy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Gastric subepithelial lesions (SELs) comprise a heterogeneous group of tumors, among which gastric schwannomas are rare and generally benign. We report a case of a large gastric schwannoma with ulceration and symptomatic anemia that showed an apparent endoscopic decrease in size following Helicobacter pylori eradication. An 85-year-old man presented with iron deficiency anemia. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed a large ulcerated SEL in the lower body of the stomach, along with multiple gastric ulcers. Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated a 56 mm tumor originating from the fourth layer, raising suspicion for a gastrointestinal stromal tumor. Boring biopsy from the ulcer base enabled a definitive diagnosis of gastric schwannoma based on immunohistochemical findings. Although surgical resection was recommended, the patient declined. After successful H. pylori eradication, follow-up endoscopy at 6 months showed healing of the ulcerative lesion and an apparent endoscopic decrease in the size of the tumor. Although objective post-treatment assessment was unavailable, this case suggests that inflammatory or ulcer-related changes associated with H. pylori infection may influence the endoscopic appearance of gastric SELs.

articles.title: Spontaneous Hyperinflation of Intragastric Balloon Presenting as Acute Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract: Obesity is a metabolic disorder with considerable health implications affecting populations worldwide. Intragastric balloon (IGB) placement has gained popularity as a minimally invasive and reversible management option for obesity. Although generally safe, IGBs can sometimes be associated with serious adverse outcomes. We present a case of IGB hyperinflation due to Candida infection, resulting in local compression of the pancreas and causing acute pancreatitis. Urgent endoscopic removal of the balloon led to complete resolution of symptoms. Spontaneous hyperinflation of an IGB due to fungal overgrowth can lead to extrinsic pancreatic compression. Early recognition and timely balloon removal are key to the management of IGB-related acute pancreatitis.

articles.title: Recent Development of Endo-hepatology.
articles.abstract: Endo-hepatology is a rapidly evolving field encompassing endoscopic diagnosis and treatment of hepatobiliary diseases, primarily using endoscopic ultrasound (EUS). Since its conceptualization in 2012, the field has expanded dramatically alongside advances in interventional EUS. A landmark 2024 review broadened the concept to include endoscopic management of hepatobiliary diseases using interventional EUS/endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography and advanced imaging technologies. In portal hypertension (PH), diagnostic applications include EUS-based variceal hemodynamic assessment, EUS-guided shear wave elastography, EUS-guided porto-systemic pressure gradient measurement (EUS-PPGM), EUS-guided liver biopsy (EUS-LB), and portal vein sampling. Therapeutic applications include EUS-guided vascular embolization for gastric, esophageal, and ectopic varices; portosystemic shunt obliteration for refractory hepatic encephalopathy; radiofrequency ablation of hepatocellular carcinoma; and emerging procedures such as intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation and portal vein stenting. EUS-PPGM enables direct, minimally invasive portal pressure measurement and correlates strongly with the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG). It may offer particular advantages in pre-sinusoidal PH, such as porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder, and in conditions with mixed sinusoidal and presinusoidal components, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, where HVPG may underestimate portal pressure. The "one-stop" concept integrates portal pressure measurement, LB, liver stiffness assessment, and variceal evaluation and treatment within a single endoscopic session. EUS-guided coil plus cyanoacrylate injection has demonstrated favorable efficacy and safety for gastric varices, while EUS-LB provides diagnostic accuracy comparable to percutaneous biopsy with less post-procedure pain. By integrating diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, endo-hepatology bridges endoscopy and hepatology and may provide comprehensive, minimally invasive, and personalized management of PH and chronic liver disease.

articles.title: Third Space Endoscopic Therapies for Benign Motility Disorders: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To review the evidence base, evolution, outcomes, adverse events (AEs), and management for third-space endoscopy (TSE) procedures for management of benign motility disorders.

METHODS: This review examines TSE procedures for motility disorders, reviewing the current available techniques, success, outcomes, and long-term outcomes from the literature.

RESULTS: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) for achalasia cardia is now established as first-line therapy, endorsed by the American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy, American College of Gastroenterology, Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons, and international expert bodies, with long-term clinical success exceeding 90% at 7 years. Since 2010, the technique has evolved considerably, with refinements in myotomy length, orientation, and depth, along with intraoperative use of an endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe to optimize outcomes and reduce post-procedure gastroesophageal reflux (GER). The TSE platform has since expanded to spastic esophageal disorders, esophagogastric junction outflow obstruction, Zenker's and epiphrenic diverticula (Z-POEM/D-POEM), refractory gastroparesis (gastric per-oral endoscopic pyloromyotomy), and Hirschsprung's disease. Techniques have also been modified along the way to achieve better results while minimizing AEs. Post-POEM GER, occurring objectively in 40%-55% of patients, remains the principal long-term challenge, and multiple modalities have been explored to address it.
