CONCLUSIONS: TSE has fundamentally transformed the management of benign gastrointestinal motility disorders, with POEM serving as the paradigm for the shift from surgical to endoscopic treatment. Ongoing technical refinement, GER mitigation strategies, and emerging innovations are poised to further advance the field.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

articles.title: Risk of Delayed Post-polypectomy Bleeding in Patients With Antithrombotic Therapy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recent changes in the perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy (ATT), including the discontinuation of routine heparin bridging and the increased use of cold snare polypectomy, may reduce delayed post-polypectomy bleeding (DPPB) rates. However, few recent studies have evaluated these changes. We compared DPPB rates between patients with and without ATT and explored factors associated with bleeding.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adult patients who underwent endoscopic resection of colorectal polyps ≤15 mm between April 2021 and October 2023. DPPB was defined as hematochezia or a hemoglobin drop ≥2.0 g/dL requiring endoscopic hemostasis. Univariable analyses were performed to identify factors associated with DPPB, and exploratory multivariable analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Among 2136 patients with 7025 polyps, 523 patients (1874 polyps) were receiving ATT. The DPPB rates per patient (1.91% vs. 0.25%) and per lesion (0.69% vs. 0.08%) were significantly higher in the ATT group (p < 0.001). In univariable analyses, ATT use (odds ratio [OR] 7.84), ≥3 resected lesions (OR 5.13), and hypertension (OR 3.95) were significant risk factors in the per-patient analysis, while ATT use (OR 8.73), lesion size >10 mm (OR 4.51), and clipping (OR 5.20) were significant in the per-lesion analysis. Among ATT types, warfarin users had the highest DPPB rates.

CONCLUSIONS: Colorectal polypectomy in patients receiving ATT is associated with an increased risk of DPPB. Particular caution is warranted in patients receiving warfarin.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

articles.title: Risk Stratification for Rebleeding in Obscure Gastrointestinal Bleeding After Comprehensive Gastrointestinal Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Background and Aim: Obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB) is defined as bleeding of unknown origin after comprehensive upper, lower, and small-bowel evaluations. However, the incidence and predictors of rebleeding after negative comprehensive gastrointestinal evaluation remain unclear. We aimed to identify predictors of rebleeding and develop a simple risk stratification score for OGIB. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 226 patients diagnosed with OGIB between 2009 and 2024. The primary outcome was rebleeding during follow-up. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis. A risk score was constructed from regression coefficients and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and Kaplan-Meier curves. Results: Among 226 patients, 87 (38.5%) had overt OGIB and 139 (61.5%) had occult OGIB. Rebleeding occurred in 30 (13.2%) patients. Multivariable analysis identified liver cirrhosis (β = 0.59, p < 0.01), overt OGIB (β = 0.69, p < 0.01), and aspirin use (β = 0.51, p = 0.02) as independent predictors. Each factor was assigned one point, yielding a 0-3 point score. The score showed modest discriminative ability (area under the curve = 0.68). Rebleeding rates increased progressively with increasing scores (5.6%, 17.5%, 27.3%, and 100% for scores 0, 1, 2, and 3, respectively) and were significantly higher in the high-risk group (p < 0.01). Conclusion: Rebleeding remained clinically relevant despite comprehensive gastrointestinal evaluation. The proposed risk score provides a simple and practical tool for identifying patients at increased risk of rebleeding and may support risk-adapted follow-up after a negative comprehensive gastrointestinal evaluation. Trial Registration: N/A.

articles.title: Ulcerative Esophagitis With Marked Eosinophilic Infiltration and Fluorodeoxyglucose-Positron Emission Tomography Positivity Requiring Differentiation From Esophagogastric Junction Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration, including eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), can rarely present with ulceration or stricture. We report a rare case of positron emission tomography-positive esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration accompanied by ulceration and stricture, requiring differentiation from esophagogastric junction carcinoma. A 50-year-old man with no history of allergies underwent computed tomography, which revealed para-esophageal lymphadenopathy and circumferential thickening of the distal esophagus. Endoscopy showed an ulcerated stricture with an iodine-unstained area. Positron emission tomography demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose uptake at the lesion site. Multiple endoscopic biopsies (11 specimens) were negative for malignancy but revealed 70 eosinophils per high-power field, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for EoE. Hiatal hernia was also observed, suggesting the possibility of concomitant reflux esophagitis. Significant dysphagia persisted due to the severe stricture. Therefore, endoscopic bougie dilation was carefully performed under general anesthesia. After 8 weeks of proton pump inhibitor therapy, mucosal healing was confirmed, and topical steroids were initiated for persistent eosinophilic infiltration. This case highlights that esophagitis with marked eosinophilic infiltration accompanied by ulceration and stricture may require differentiation from cancer.

articles.title: Consent for intensive care research involving adults who lack decision-making capacity: A jurisdictional analysis of Australia's fragmented framework.
articles.journal: Critical care and resuscitation : journal of the Australasian Academy of Critical Care Medicine
articles.abstract: Critically ill adults frequently cannot consent to research because of sedation, delirium, shock or mechanical ventilation, yet safe intensive care depends on evidence generated in this population; several treatments once regarded as standard care proved harmful when finally tested in randomised trials. The ethical framework for enrolling adults who lack decision-making capacity is national-the National Health and Medical Research Council National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research (2025), in effect since 23 June 2026-but legal authority for substitute consent is conferred by eight state and territory statutes that differ in terminology, in decision-maker hierarchies, in whether they address research at all, and whether they permit enrolment in an emergency. Mapping four representative study archetypes across all eight jurisdictions shows that the lawful basis for enrolling the same patient shifts with study design as much as with geography; differing statutory definitions, tribunal involvement and the transition to the 2025 National Statement produce material and avoidable inconsistency. Contemporary Australian intensive care trials show that practice has converged on the National Statement while the underlying legislation has not; the resulting inconsistency risks inequity, underrepresentation of critically ill patients, and bias in the evidence generated. We set out principles for reform (Box 1): nationally consistent framing of substitute consent for research-common terminology and legal principles, an explicit emergency-research pathway in every jurisdiction, and consistent interpretation within each jurisdiction-developed with consumers and with the clinicians and clinical research nurses who obtain consent, and taken forward with formal endorsement from the relevant professional bodies.

articles.title: Inhaled nanogels ameliorate vascular remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension via normalization of endothelia-smooth muscle cell crosstalk.
articles.abstract: Maintaining appropriate vascular nitric oxide (NO) levels in pulmonary arteries is crucial for the alleviation of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). However, in the injured vascular microenvironment, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) deplete NO to generate peroxynitrite, which aggravates the oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction. Herein, ROS-responsive, zwitterionic nanogels (NGs), containing arginine pendants as NO precursors and encapsulating resveratrol (RSV) as an anti-oxidant, were developed for PAH management via inhalation. Benefiting from their zwitterionic surface that repels mucin adsorption, the inhaled NGs exhibit effective pulmonary mucus penetration and mucosal absorption, enabling robust diffusion to the injured pulmonary arteries. In the oxidative vascular microenvironment, the diselenide crosslinkers within the NGs are cleaved, promoting NGs dissociation and on-demand RSV release. The released RSV scavenges ROS and the arginine pendants are oxidized to generate NO, which cooperate to interrupt the ROS/NO disequilibrium. In a hypoxia/SU5416-induced PAH mouse model, inhaled NGs efficiently alleviate vascular remodeling and reduce pulmonary arterial pressure. This study offers an effective strategy for pulmonary drug delivery, and holds promising potentials for the management of PAH.

articles.title: A topologically engineered hydrogel platform targeting IL11 promotes renal repair after partial nephrectomy.
articles.abstract: Partial nephrectomy (PN) is the gold standard for treating renal tumors and trauma; however, massive nephron loss and persistent fibrosis readily lead to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Current therapeutic options remain non-curative and costly, as nearly half of PN patients inevitably progress to end-stage renal failure. Here, we present an innovative regenerative platform for PN-induced CKD, integrating structural biomimicry with targeted molecular inhibition. Harnessing light-based bioprinting of gelatin and hyaluronic acid methacrylates coupled with removable alginate microfiber, we constructed a hierarchical channel scaffold (HCS) that features precisely patterned macrochannels and template-derived microchannels, which closely mimics native kidney architecture, provides structural support, and remarkably enhances cell migration (∼5.45-fold) and rapid neovascularization (∼7.66-fold) over unidirectional channel structures. Moreover, interleukin 11 (IL11) was identified as a novel therapeutic target in kidney fibrosis after PN. Thus, extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells loaded with IL11 small interfering RNA (siIL11) were homogeneously encapsulated into HCS, achieving over 4-fold higher renal retention than systemic delivery in PN-induced CKD mice. Furthermore, sustained local release of EV-siIL11 and hierarchically channeled HCS guided synergistic regenerative effects that remarkably inhibited fibrosis, cell cycle arrest, and immune responses, thereby potently preventing kidney atrophy and restoring renal structure with newly aligned nephrons and vasculature, ultimately recovering kidney function. Further analysis revealed that IL11 silencing reversed epithelial‒mesenchymal transition by suppressing the STAT3-ERK-GSK3β-SNAI1 axis. This topological multifunctional hydrogel platform offers a localized, sustained, and clinically translatable strategy for postsurgical kidney regeneration.

articles.title: Unified alcoholysis-GC-MS/MS for simultaneous differentiation and quantification of polyester microplastics in water.
articles.abstract: Environmental waters now carry complex mixtures of polyester microplastics that vary in origin and biodegradability, including fossil-based and biodegradable polyesters, yet no method can simultaneously distinguish and individually quantify them. We present a unified alcoholysis method coupled with GC-MS/MS to quantify four polyester microplastics (PEMPs) in a single workflow. By selectively cleaving ester bonds in an alcohol medium, the method converts polylactic acid, polyethylene terephthalate, polyhydroxybutyrate and polybutylene succinate into four distinct, stable monomers. These monomers are directly determined by GC-MS/MS without derivatization. Under unified conditions (190 °C, 5 h), depolymerization efficiencies range from 15% to 90%. We calibrate directly between polymer mass and monomer signal intensity. Detection limits are 0.0462 μg/L for polylactic acid (PLA), 0.103 μg/L for polyethylene terephthalate (PET), 2.92 μg/L for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), and 0.695 μg/L for polybutylene succinate (PBS). Spiked recoveries in lake water are 90-115%. In six lake samples, PLA constitutes over 75% of total PEMPs. This fingerprint points to consumer packaging as the dominant source. By circumventing particle morphology constraints and delivering polymer-specific mass concentrations, the method opens a direct route for source apportionment of coexisting fossil-based and biodegradable polyester microplastics.

articles.title: Oxygen-vacancy-rich LDH sonosensitizers potentiate narrow-spectrum antibiotics via membrane-disruption strategy for mixed bacterial wound infections.
articles.abstract: Mixed bacterial infections, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, remain a major global health concern. Achieving efficient treatment of synergistic polymicrobial infections stills a tremendous clinical challenge due to antibiotic permeability barriers and resistance. Here, we construct a defect-engineered layered double hydroxide (LDH)-based sonosensitizer platform loaded with clindamycin (a-CoW/CLD) for mixed bacterial infection therapy, which not only demonstrates high efficacy against Gram-positive bacteria, but also exploits reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated membrane disruption of Gram-negative bacteria to facilitate CLD penetration, thereby achieving broad-spectrum and highly efficient killing of mixed bacteria. The amorphous a-CoW nanosheets, enriched with oxygen vacancies via acid etching, exhibit a substantially narrowed bandgap (1.22 eV) and markedly enhanced charge separation, producing 22.1-fold higher singlet oxygen under ultrasound (US) irradiation compared with pristine CoW. This ROS burst synergized with CLD achieves potent killing of Staphylococcus aureus (>99.9% at 20 μg mL-1). More critically, ROS disrupt the outer membrane of Gram-negative Escherichia coli, promoting CLD internalization and consequently boosting its lethality by 18.4-fold (from ∼5% to >92.1%). Mechanistic transcriptomics reveals ROS and CLD synergy: ROS disrupt the bacterial membrane via lipid peroxidation, enabling CLD penetration to block protein synthesis and metabolism, while ROS also induce oxidative stress, collectively leading to bacterial death. In a murine wound model co-infected with both pathogens, a-CoW/CLD plus US eradicates >99.9% of mixed bacteria, suppresses systemic inflammation, and significantly accelerates angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. This paradigm establishes a low-dose, broad-spectrum sonodynamic-antibiotic strategy that overcomes antibiotic permeability bottleneck, offering a promising therapeutic avenue against mixed bacterial infections.

articles.title: A spatiotemporally programmed bioactive scaffold for orbital reconstruction.
articles.abstract: Orbital implants are widely used for post-enucleation reconstruction, but poor fibrovascularization and infection risk still limit their clinical performance. Herein, a three-dimensional (3D)-printed copper-doped hardystonite (HT, Ca2ZnSi2O7) scaffold with polar-graded porosity is developed for spatiotemporally programmed orbital reconstruction. By matching the intrinsic orbital regenerative trajectory, small pores promote early immunomodulation and reparative-cell recruitment, medium pores enhance angiogenic activation, and large pores facilitate vascular ingrowth and vascular-network assembly. This design drives a sequential regenerative process involving immune modulation, endothelial activation, interfacial remodeling, and vascular assembly. In rabbit aseptic and infected models, the implant promotes ordered fibrovascularization and suppresses bacterial colonization, showing superior performance to clinical hydroxyapatite implants. Taken together, this study presents a spatiotemporally programmed bioactive scaffold as a promising strategy for orbital reconstruction.

articles.title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

articles.title: An orthogonal transcription system enables high-efficiency rescue of measles virus-based vaccine vectors against multiple pathogens.
articles.abstract: Recombinant measles virus (rMeV) vectors are promising platforms for vaccine development against emerging infectious diseases due to their safety, stability, and potent immunogenicity. However, conventional rMeV rescue systems frequently exhibit low efficiency, thereby constraining their scalability and throughput. In this study, we developed a modular, helper-virus-free and high-efficiency rescue platform based on an orthogonal transcription system utilizing orthogonal promoters and engineered RNA polymerases fused to an mRNA capping enzyme. This innovative system facilitated robust cytoplasmic manufacture of both genomic and auxiliary components, eliminating the need for helper virus co-infection (such as modified vaccinia virus) and enhancing rescue efficiency by more than 50-fold relative to traditional rescue approaches. Utilizing this technology, we demonstrated the versatility of the platform by successfully generating six rMeV-based vaccine antigen candidates from influenza virus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Brucella spp. All rescued vaccine candidates exhibited stable transgene expression, sustained replication, and strong antigen production. Immunization studies in golden Syrian hamsters verified that the vaccine candidates elicited high titers of neutralizing and antigen-specific antibodies without any observable adverse effects. These results demonstrate that our orthogonal transcription-based platform facilitates the efficient and safe production of rMeV vectors and provides a proof-of-concept methodological framework for the rapid development of vaccine candidates.

articles.title: Optimal timing for staged vaccination campaigns: Insights from scenario tree-based stochastic optimization.
articles.abstract: We develop a mathematical modeling framework to address the challenge in launching an effective staged vaccination campaign during a typical viral infection season to avoid an overwhelmed healthcare system for the entire season. Using the COVID-19 pandemic following its acute phase as a motivating example, our model takes into account the willingness of the public to receive vaccines, as well as the uncertainty of vaccination delivery and administration, to achieve the objective of optimizing the timing and distribution of the vaccination campaign, subject to the constraint that hospitalized cases do not exceed healthcare capacity. The integration of a dynamic transmission model with a scenario tree-based stochastic optimization framework enables the evaluation of future scenarios characterized by uncertainty in vaccination rates, contact mixing, and public adherence to safety measures. Accounting for these future scenarios facilitates the identification of strategies to dynamically adjust the timing and scale of vaccine and contact mixing during distinct phases of the viral season. Our study demonstrates that a well-timed, well-phased vaccination campaign, along with other public health interventions, can prevent overcrowding in hospitalization in a typical viral infection season.

articles.title: SLC7A2 regulates the inflammation and apoptosis of LPS-induced human lung epithelial cells through TLR4/NF-κB pathway.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is the most common complication of sepsis and has a high mortality rate among critically ill patients. Its effective treatment still faces huge challenges. SLC7A2, an arginine transporter, is associated with immunity and inflammatory response. However, the action with specific regulation mechanism of SLC7A2 in LPS-treated ALI remains unclear. The key differentially expressed genes (DEGs) related to sepsis-associated ALI were screened out using the data from the GEO database. The interactions of DEGs were analyzed using bioinformatics analysis methods, such as GO, KEGG along with PPI networks. The LPS-treated human lung epithelial cells BEAS-2 B (HLECs-B) damage model was constructed. The mRNA or protein expression in LPS-treated HLECs-B were evaluated through application of RT-qPCR or western blot. CCK-8, EdU, TUNEL staining assay along with ELISA were applied to assess cells viability, proliferation, apoptosis, and inflammatory factors expression, respectively. Bioinformatics analysis of GEO datasets identified the top three DEGs (SLC7A2, TNIP3, and CFB). The mRNA levels of these 3 DEGs were highly raised in LPS-treated HLECs-B, and especially of SLC7A2. Functionally, in LPS-treated HLECs-B, SLC7A2 silencing could improve cell viability and proliferation, block apoptosis, reduce IL-1β, IL-6, along with TNF-α production; Moreover, SLC7A2 silencing could decrease the TLR4, p-NF-κB protein levels. Importantly, overexpression of TLR4 reversed the protective effects of SLC7A2 silencing, whereas knockdown of TLR4 abrogated the detrimental effects of SLC7A2 overexpression, in LPS-treated HLECs-B. SLC7A2 regulates the inflammation and apoptosis of LPS-treated lung epithelial cells through TLR4/NF-κB pathway.

articles.title: Optimizing Eculizumab and Ravulizumab Initiation in Myasthenia Gravis: Infection Risk, Vaccination Timing, and Antibiotic Prophylaxis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fatigable muscle weakness and fluctuating symptoms. Complement component 5 inhibitor therapies (C5ITs) such as ravulizumab and eculizumab are rapidly acting treatments for generalized MG (gMG) but associated with an increased risk of meningococcal infection. As such, an ideal strategy for initiating C5IT requires effective mitigation of meningococcal infection risk that permits timely amelioration of disease burden. While C5ITs are approved for several indications, this review focuses on gMG. The available data on infection risk associated with eculizumab and ravulizumab are discussed, and practical approaches for starting these medications are presented.

RECENT FINDINGS: Previously, C5IT could be started 2 weeks after the initial doses of meningococcal vaccines. The 2024 updates to meningococcal vaccination policies in the United States extended the completion schedule from 2 months to 6 months and allowed for clinical judgment in initiating C5ITs earlier. In treating patients whose severity of gMG necessitates starting C5ITs before the 6-month vaccination schedule can be completed, clinicians need to consider several factors, including the risk of meningococcal infection, whether the expected reduction in disease burden and improvement in quality of life justify the infection risk, and the potential complications of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis as an infection risk mitigation strategy.

SUMMARY: In our opinion, data used to support the change in vaccine schedule did not show a substantial difference in seroresponses. Since C5ITs are likely to remain an important treatment option for gMG, consideration of early vaccination after the diagnosis is recommended to minimize delays in the initiation of C5ITs. Clinical trial data suggest that risk of meningococcal infection in patients with gMG is low, particularly during the first 6 months after C5IT initiation. The evidence supporting the use of extended antibiotic prophylaxis in this patient population is currently scarce. However, clinicians must ensure that the patient is fully aware of the risk, the symptoms of meningococcal disease, and the need for prompt medical attention if those symptoms occur. By taking a comprehensive, individualized approach, clinicians can facilitate the safe and effective use of C5ITs in patients with gMG.

articles.title: Effects of exogenous nitric oxide gas on Mycobacterium tuberculosis in vitro and in mice.
articles.abstract: In 1992, inhaled NO (iNO) at low doses entered the practice of medicine for cardiopulmonary indications. Recently, iNO at higher doses has been tested in diverse pulmonary infections. However, nothing is known about the ability of exogenous NO gas to kill Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the leading cause of death from infection between major viral pandemics. Here, we mimicked exposure conditions used in recent human studies of high-dose iNO to explore the effects of NO gas against Mtb in vitro and in mice. We saw a profound bactericidal effect of NO gas in vitro against Mtb incubated in shallow, mildly acidic fluid. Mtb-infected mice tolerated iNO well, except for developing more methemoglobinemia than humans at the same level of exposure. In Mtb-infected mice with poorly aerated pulmonary infiltrates, iNO had an anti-inflammatory effect but did not reduce the bacterial burden. These results may help inform the decision whether to test iNO as an adjunctive treatment for tuberculosis, and if so, in what settings and with what goals.

articles.title: Regional and national burden and aetiologies of non-COVID lower respiratory infections in Latin America and the Caribbean, 1990-2023: a secondary analysis of the global burden of disease study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income regions. Reliable, up-to-date burden estimates are needed to inform public health strategies in Latin America and the Caribbean, where prevention and management strategies remain heterogeneous. We aimed to characterise temporal and geographical patterns in LRTI mortality, incidence, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and aetiology across the region from 1990 to 2023.

METHODS: We analysed secondary, modelled estimates of mortality, incidence, and DALYs attributable to LRTIs in Latin America and the Caribbean from 1990 to 2023, extracted from the GBD 2023 Results Tool and produced following the standardised GBD protocol coordinated by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME).

FINDINGS: In Latin America and the Caribbean, LRTI mortality declined in most countries between 1990 and 2023, with the steepest reductions among children younger than five years (e.g., Brazil ARC -6·16, 95% UI -6·61 to -5·71). All-age mortality rose in some countries, but age-standardised rates showed that these increases reflected population ageing rather than rising age-specific risk. Following a sustained pre-pandemic decline, incidence showed and overall upward direction in the post-pandemic period across age groups, although the magnitude and statistical relevance of these changes varied by age and country, with the largest increase observed among children in Suriname (ARC +8·84, 95% UI +2·80 to +14·95). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the leading cause of LRTI mortality in 2023 (7·68 per 100,000, 95% UI 7·11-8·24; ARC -2·70, 95% UI -2·96 to -2·45).

INTERPRETATION: LRTIs remain a major cause of death in the region, with substantial progress among children but persistent burden among older adults, driven by population ageing, and evidence of a post-pandemic increase in incidence. There is a great importance of combining clinical interventions with broader public health strategies addressing vaccination coverage, antimicrobial-resistance surveillance, nutrition, housing, and access to primary care, particularly in populations that have experienced less favourable trends.

FUNDING: Wellcome Trust (303666/Z/23/Z); UK International Development (301542-403); the Gates Foundation (INV-063472) and Universidad de La Sabana (MED-289-2020).

articles.title: Structured Peer-Led Biostatistics Education Improves Research Confidence and Applied Competency Among Preclinical Medical Students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early exposure to clinical research methodology and biostatistics remains limited within many medical school curricula despite increasing emphasis on evidence-based medicine and scholarly productivity. Peer-assisted learning models may offer a scalable approach to improving research education while minimizing faculty burden. This study evaluated a structured, peer-led applied biostatistics curriculum for preclinical medical students.

METHODS: The Clinical Data Analysis and Research Team (CDART) curriculum was delivered to two cohorts of first-year medical students at a single medical institution during the 2025-2026 academic year. The curriculum consisted of four core instructional sessions focused on statistical analysis, data interpretation, and practical use of IBM SPSS Statistics software. Pre- and post-session confidence surveys and a curriculum-level Applied Biostatistics Knowledge Assessment were administered. Paired-samples t-tests, Cohen's d effect sizes, and Cronbach's alpha reliability analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Thirty-four first-year medical students completed the curriculum. Confidence scores improved significantly across all instructional sessions, with mean paired increases ranging from 11.27 to 20.27 points (all p < 0.001). Applied Biostatistics Knowledge Assessment performance improved from 2.57% ± 7.40% pre-instruction to 77.57% ± 21.49% post-instruction (95% confidence interval, 67.04-82.96; p < 0.001). Effect sizes were large across all sessions (Cohen's d = 1.55-3.29). Confidence instruments demonstrated good-to-excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.81-0.98).

CONCLUSIONS: Participation in the CDART peer-led biostatistics curriculum was associated with significant improvements in confidence in applied biostatistics tasks and immediate assessment performance among preclinical medical students. Structured peer-led curricula may provide an effective and scalable approach to improving early research preparedness within medical education.

articles.title: Large Language Models in Clinical Neurology: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being evaluated for clinical neurology applications, yet their real-world utility, safety, and deployment readiness remain unclear. This review maps the literature on LLMs applied to text-based and text-derived neurology tasks, characterizing current use cases, evaluation strategies, performance metrics, and reported safety concerns. We identify areas with relatively robust evidence, highlight important evidence gaps, and outline key methodological and clinical barriers that must be addressed before responsible clinical adoption.

RECENT FINDINGS: Following  Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we searched 4 databases (January 2022 to February 2026) and included 32 studies (2023-2026) spanning 7 neurology subspecialties; 9 were simulation or feasibility studies, 17 analyzed retrospective clinical data, and 6 reported prospective evaluation. Proprietary models predominated; 5 studies used retrieval-augmented generation and 1 used a multiagent framework. Performance was highest for constrained tasks, including binary diagnostic classification (area under the curve 0.75-0.94), information extraction (F1 0.89-0.90), patient-education question answering (accuracy 68%-97%), and ischemic stroke thrombectomy decision support (area under the curve [AUC] 0.92) and lowest for open-ended case-based reasoning (accuracy 42%-54%). Recurrent safety signals included hallucinated and fabricated citations, poor calibration with overconfidence (for example, 100% sensitivity with 27% specificity for epilepsy diagnosis), and a systematic bias toward intervention. On adapted Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies Using Artificial Intelligence (QUADAS-AI) charting, overall risk of bias was low in 1 study (3%), moderate in 16 (50%), and high in 15 (47%), driven chiefly by absent external validation (31/32, 97%). Benchmarked against high-reliability and 6 Sigma standards, reported error rates remain orders of magnitude too high for autonomous use.

SUMMARY: Evidence for LLMs in neurology is early, heterogeneous, and limited by scarce external and prospective validation. Current data support only narrow, clinician-supervised uses such as documentation and education, while cautioning against autonomous diagnostic or therapeutic use. Rigorous, prospective, externally validated studies with standardized reporting and explicit safety and ethical evaluation are needed before broader adoption.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251082465.

articles.title: Effects of temporal and parietal cortex non-invasive brain stimulation on memory in healthy older adults, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Memory decline is a common cognitive complaint among healthy older adults, mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) has been investigated as a promising approach for enhancing memory. While most studies target the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, interest is growing in stimulating temporal and parietal areas due to their involvement in episodic and associative memory. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of temporo-parietal NIBS on memory in healthy older adults and patients with MCI and AD. Nineteen studies were included in the systematic review, of which 12 provided data for random-effects meta-analysis. Effects were expressed as Hedges' g, comparing active and sham stimulation. Overall, NIBS significantly improved memory performance (g = 0.67, 95% CI 0.27, 1.07). Analyses stratified by stimulation modality showed a significant effect for transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) (g = 0.81, 95% CI 0.08, 1.53), whereas repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) did not reach statistical significance (g = 0.60, 95% CI -0.0003, 1.19). The difference between modalities was not significant (p = 0.54). Additional analyses showed significant improvements in episodic memory across healthy older adults and patients with MCI and AD (g = 0.60, 95% CI 0.19, 1.01) and in patients with MCI and AD alone (g = 0.61, 95% CI 0.17, 1.06). rTMS did not significantly improve episodic memory in MCI and AD (g = 0.62, 95% CI -0.08, 1.31). These findings suggest potential memory benefits, but substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty of evidence warrant cautious interpretation.

articles.title: A Streptomyces-derived cyclic peptide valinomycin primes two-layered plant local immunity and systemic disease resistance.
articles.abstract: Intensive research has led to the identification of various natural compounds as alternative and complementary agents for the chemical management of plant diseases. Here, we propose that valinomycin, a cyclic peptide produced by Streptomyces bacillaris S8, is a putative biocontrol agent against various plant pathogens with dual functions. The compound demonstrated antifungal activity against the plant pathogenic fungus, Botrytis cinerea (B. cinerea), a necrotrophic fungal pathogen that causes gray mold disease in many plant species. Intriguingly, valinomycin boosted plant immunity with priming activity in response to pathogen infection. Plants treated with valinomycin exhibited an increased flg22-mediated reactive oxygen species (ROS) burst, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) phosphorylation, and callose deposition, known hallmarks of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs)-triggered immunity (PTI). Regarding effector-triggered immunity (ETI), valinomycin potentiated hypersensitive response (HR), a representative phenotype of the ETI responses. Furthermore, ROS burst assay revealed that valinomycin simultaneously facilitated PTI and ETI that mutually strengthen each other. Valinomycin increased the resistance against Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pto DC3000), without antibacterial activity. Valinomycin primes plant immunity by modulating plant hormone crosstalk, extending to systemic resistance in Arabidopsis. Notably, valinomycin also enhanced disease resistance in tobacco and soybean, demonstrating its potential for expanded application to many crop species. Therefore, our study highlights valinomycin as a versatile natural compound with potential as a biocontrol agent, combining direct antifungal activity with plant immune-priming function across multiple plant species.

articles.title: Bacterial extracellular vesicles in metabolic diseases: From pathogenic mediators to therapeutic carriers.
articles.abstract: The incidence of metabolic diseases (e.g. obesity, diabetes, and osteoporosis) is rising year by year worldwide. The gut microbiota, as a complex microbial ecosystem, is closely associated with the onset and progression of various metabolic diseases due to its dysbiosis. Recent studies have shown that extracellular vesicles derived from gut microbiota play a crucial role in bacterial-host communication. However, the specific roles and mechanisms of bacterial extracellular vesicles (bEVs) in metabolic diseases remain to be further explored. This review summarizes the biogenesis and composition of bEVs and critically examines their dual roles in the pathogenesis and treatment of metabolic diseases. We further discuss recent research progress on engineering strategies, including parental strain engineering, cargo loading, and surface functionalization to optimize the therapeutic efficacy of bEVs. Finally, we highlight key translational challenges and future prospects in bEVs-based development. This review aims to provide a theoretical foundation and new intervention strategies for the treatment of metabolic diseases.

articles.title: Pacific Gout Knowledge in Auckland, New Zealand: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.journal: Journal of the Royal Society of New Zealand
articles.abstract: Objective: Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand experience the highest burden of gout and increased understanding is associated with improved adherence and management. The objective of this study is to assess gout knowledge and identify its associated predictors among Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand. Methods: This cross-sectional study was guided by the Tongan Kakala research framework. Data were collected using a culturally adapted online survey of adults aged 18 years and over living in Auckland, New Zealand. Descriptive statistics and multivariable regression analysis were used to show distributions and identify predictors of gout knowledge. Results: A total of 408 Pacific participants were included in this study. Most participants identified as Tongan (43%) or Samoan (36%) and were aged between 18 and 39 years (75.5%). The mean gout knowledge of participants was 4.6 (SD 2.6). Participants demonstrated greater understanding of causes and symptoms of gout, but showed limited knowledge of urate-lowering therapy, target serum urate levels and the life-long treatment of gout. The multivariable linear regression analysis found a significant association between increased gout knowledge and age (p < 0.0001), education (p < 0.0001), total house-hold income (p = 0.03), gout diagnosis (p < 0.0001) and obtaining gout information from health professionals (p = 0.0003). Conclusion: Our results highlight a significant gap in gout knowledge among Pacific adults in New Zealand, particularly in relation to long-term management. There is a need to develop culturally appropriate and relevant educational approaches co-designed with health professionals, communities and families to improve Pacific peoples' understanding of gout and support adherence and management.

articles.title: Hepatic ITGBL1 promotes fibrogenesis and ductular remodeling through integrin-dependent latent TGF-β activation.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a major determinant of chronic liver disease progression and hepatobiliary remodeling. However, extracellular regulators linking fibrogenesis to pathological biliary responses remain incompletely understood. Integrin beta-like protein 1 (ITGBL1) is an extracellular matrix-associated protein implicated in integrin modulation, but its functional role in chronic liver injury remains unclear. A liver-specific doxycycline (DOX)-inducible zebrafish model was established to evaluate the effects of hepatic ITGBL1 gain-of-function in vivo. Fibrogenic and biliary responses were assessed using histologic, molecular, and genetic approaches. Mechanistic studies tested pathway dependence on itgav and ltbp1 using liver-specific genetic ablation, with cilengitide used as a complementary RGD-integrin pharmacologic perturbation. Hepatocyte-specific ITGBL1 induction triggered progressive hepatic stellate cell activation, extracellular matrix accumulation, and chronic fibrotic remodeling. Sustained ITGBL1 expression further promoted ductular reaction and biliary epithelial expansion during chronic liver injury progression. Genetic disruption of itgav or ltbp1 attenuated SMAD3 activation, collagen deposition, fibrogenic transcriptional programs, and associated histological remodeling; cilengitide independently attenuated fibrogenic readouts. These data support a working model in which hepatic ITGBL1 lies upstream of integrin/LTBP1-dependent latent TGF-β/SMAD3 signaling and provide a mechanistic framework for further resolving the molecular interactions among ITGBL1, ITGAV, and LTBP1 and the αv-integrin heterodimer involved. This pathway may represent a therapeutic target for fibrosis-associated biliary remodeling.

articles.title: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 suppresses neuroinflammation and cellular senescence to alleviate diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a devastating complication of diabetes. While neuroinflammation and cellular senescence are known contributors to DPN pathogenesis, the precise molecular mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that advanced glycation end products (AGEs) promote the nuclear-cytoplasmic translocation of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), enhancing its extracellular secretion. This extracellular HMGB1 functions as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), recruiting inflammatory cells and inducing neuroinflammation and cellular senescence in PC12 cells. Consistent with these cellular findings, HMGB1 levels were markedly elevated in STZ-induced DPN mice. Notably, systemic neutralization of HMGB1 effectively suppressed neuroinflammation and senescence, thereby ameliorating DPN. Mechanistically, AGE treatment downregulated Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), resulting in increased HMGB1 acetylation, which facilitated its nuclear export and extracellular release. Consequently, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 attenuated neuroinflammation and delayed cellular senescence, playing a pivotal role in alleviating DPN. Our findings unveil the critical role of the SIRT1/HMGB1 deacetylation axis in orchestrating neuroinflammation and cellular senescence, highlighting targeted inhibition of HMGB1 secretion as a promising therapeutic strategy for DPN.

articles.title: Dismantling the eDNA-mediated H2S barrier with biohybrids against refractory biofilm infections.
articles.abstract: The spatiotemporal distribution of gaseous mediators is critical for maintaining physiological functions. Biofilms both contain gas-producing bacteria and possess complex architectures that reshape gaseous mediator distribution. However, whether biofilm pathogenicity is linked to such gaseous regulation remains unclear. In this study, we reveal that extracellular DNA (eDNA) within the biofilm matrix contributes to the local retention and enrichment of H2S. This enrichment stabilizes eDNA, strengthens biofilm barriers, impedes gas clearance, promotes bacterial persistence, and induces macrophage immunosuppression, creating a reciprocally protective defensive loop. To dismantle this defense, we engineered a stepwise-responsive biohybrid system in which probiotic-derived engineered minicells actively target hypoxic biofilm regions, while H2S-triggered nanoparticle degradation enables deeper matrix penetration and concurrent H2S scavenging. The retained minicells then catalyze in situ glucose oxidation to generate H2O2, which, together with Fe2+-mediated Fenton-like reactions, degrades eDNA and collapses the biofilm. This strategy eradicates persistent bacteria, reverses immunosuppression, and provides a therapeutic strategy to reduce recurrence and optimize refractory infection treatments.

articles.title: Click chemistry-modified cardiomyocytes enhance cardiac contractility and prevent remodeling in ischemia-reperfusion injured hearts.
articles.abstract: One of the challenges in cardiac cell therapy using cardiomyocytes derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSC-CMs) is their poor engraftment and survival rate in infarcted tissues. Click chemistry and lipid insertion are simple methods for modifying the surface of hPSC-CMs with a collagen hybridizing peptide (CHP), providing binding motifs to increase their retention and engraftment in fibrotic hearts after ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury. In this study, we developed CHP-modified CMs (CHP-mCMs) to attach cells to damaged collagen in infarcted tissues. We injected CHP-mCMs into the border zone of infarcted hearts 7 days post-MI and evaluated cardiac function for 6 weeks. Serial echocardiography revealed that CHP-mCMs not only improved cardiac function but also reduced adverse remodeling in I/R-injured hearts. These findings indicate that CHP-mCM transplantation was associated with enhanced engraftment, reduced adverse remodeling, and improved cardiac function in the rat I/R model.

articles.title: Multienzymatic hybrid bio-heterojunction for synergistic microenvironment reprogramming and selenoprotein-activated mitochondrial bioenergetics in diabetic osseointegration.
articles.abstract: Regeneration of diabetic bone defects has always been a significant challenge in clinical treatment. The pathologic diabetic microenvironment, characterized by bacterial infection, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, lactate accumulation, and chronic inflammation, triggers mitochondrial dysfunction and an energy metabolism crisis. To address this issue, we developed a synergistic multienzymatic bio-heterojunction (MoSe2/PtCu@LOx) by integrating molybdenum diselenide (MoSe2) nanosheets with platinum-copper (PtCu) nanoparticles and lactate oxidase (LOx) as a self-cyclic cascade catalysis system. The MoSe2/PtCu Schottky heterojunction enables NIR-responsive photothermal and photodynamic antibacterial activity, while self-cyclic cascade catalysis of PtCu and LOx effectively eliminates excessive ROS and accumulated lactate, thereby ameliorating the pathologic diabetic microenvironment. Crucially, the released selenium species activates SIRT3 signaling, upregulating Gpx1 expression and stabilizing mitofusin 2 (Mfn2), which enhances mitophagic flux and restores mitochondrial bioenergetics. As a result, the MoSe2/PtCu@LOx can synergistically ameliorate the pathologic microenvironment and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby effectively restoring energy metabolism function and promoting infected diabetic bone regeneration. This multienzymatic hybrid bio-heterojunction provides a metabolic-oriented therapeutic nanoplatform for diabetic bone regeneration.

articles.title: Electron-rearranged CuMg@ZIF nanoplatform for pH-Responsive sequential therapy: From infection eradication to neuroangiogenesis in diabetic wounds.
articles.abstract: Pathological microenvironment of diabetic wounds greatly increases bacterial infection, hyperinflammation, vasculopathy and neuropathy, impeding wound healing. To address these issues, a Cu and Mg codoped ZIF-8 (CuMg@ZIF) nanoplatform with pH-responsive degradation and multi-enzyme activities (peroxidase (POD)-like activity, superoxide dismutase (SOD)- and catalase (CAT)- activity) was constructed. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that Cu and Mg doping induce stretching of metal-N bonds and electron rearrangement in ZIF framework, which enhance degradation and subsequent ion releasing in acidic microenvironment, and increase Cu+/Cu2+ ratio to improve multi-enzyme activities. CuMg@ZIF exhibits excellent antibacterial efficiencies (100% against S. aureus and 99.98% against E. coli) at a low concentration (50 μg/ml) via rapid metal ion releasing and •OH generation. After sterilization, the SOD- and CAT-like activities, along with the moderate release of ions from the CuMg@ZIF scavenge ROS and facilitate macrophage recovery and M2 phenotype polarization to inhibit inflammatory reaction and secrete anti-inflammatory cytokines, which further enhance the biofunctions of endothelial cells, neural cells, and fibroblasts. This study provides a promising pH sensitive therapy to eliminate infection, promote immunoregulation, neuroangiogenesis and ECM remodeling, thereby accelerating the diabetic wound repair process.

articles.title: Engineering bioactive citrate-based hydrogels for wound repair: From structure-function design to microenvironmental regulation.
articles.abstract: Chronic non-healing wounds, characterized by a complex microenvironment of persistent infection, chronic inflammation, and defective angiogenesis, pose a significant hurdle to regenerative medicine. Citrate-based chemistry has emerged as a sophisticated platform for engineering bio-instructive materials due to its versatile crosslinking chemistry and intrinsic metabolic bioactivity. This review provides a comprehensive appraisal of hydrogels constructed from citrate-based polymers (PC hydrogels) as a high-performance therapeutic toolkit for wound orchestration. Guided by the biological imperatives of the skin-healing cascade, we delineate the network construction mechanisms and structure-function relationships of PC hydrogels, together with the molecular mechanisms underlying their regulation of the wound microenvironment. On this basis, a modular classification of PC hydrogels is proposed. It encompasses seven functional paradigms including antimicrobial, antioxidant, and pro-angiogenic activities, with a critical focus on their structure-property-function relationships. Finally, we identify the existing bottlenecks in clinical translation and offer strategic perspectives on next-generation PC platforms, emphasizing precision design, mechanistic elucidation through multi-omics, and standardized manufacturing. This work aims to catalyze the development of intelligent, translation-ready PC wound dressings for complex tissue repair.

articles.title: Association Between Serum Amylin, Irisin, and Sirtuin 1 in Male Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Nephropathy.
articles.journal: International journal of endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) is a progressive disease worldwide that leads to various complications. Given the roles of the hormones amylin and irisin and the enzyme sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) in metabolism and oxidative stress, we focused on these parameters in the serum of patients.

OBJECTIVES: We investigated the associations between serum amylin, irisin, and SIRT1 levels and diabetic nephropathy (DN), an important complication of DM.

METHODS: Patients with DM (n = 50) and DN (n = 50) were included in this single-center cross-sectional study. Various parameters were measured from fasting blood and urine samples. Serum amylin, irisin, and SIRT1 levels were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. In addition to demographic characteristics, fasting blood sugar, glycated hemoglobin, serum insulin, urine creatinine, and estimated glomerular filtration rate were used to classify participants.

RESULTS: After adjustment for age, diabetes duration, body mass index, fasting blood sugar, glycated hemoglobin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance, triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, amylin levels were significantly lower, whereas irisin and SIRT1 levels were significantly higher, in the DN group than in the DM group. Multivariable logistic regression showed that higher amylin levels were associated with lower odds of DN, whereas higher irisin and SIRT1 levels were associated with higher odds of DN. Receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the ability of these biomarkers to discriminate between the DM and DN groups. In addition, mediation analysis showed associations among irisin, SIRT1, and DN.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that irisin and SIRT1 are associated with DN status in patients with diabetes and may provide insights into metabolic complications. However, longitudinal studies are needed to establish causality.

articles.title: Long-term trajectories of intrinsic capacity and risk of cardiometabolic multimorbidity and its subtypes in older US adults: A 19-year prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrinsic capacity (IC) changes with aging, but the association between its long-term trajectories and subsequent cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. We examined the associations of long-term trajectories of IC with incident CMM and its subtypes among older US adults.

METHODS: Data were drawn from the Health and Retirement Study. Group-based trajectory modeling identified IC trajectories using five assessments across waves 3-7. Participants with CMM during this period were excluded. Incident CMM, defined as the coexistence of at least two of diabetes, heart disease, and stroke, was assessed over up to 19 years of subsequent follow-up. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 3707 participants, four IC trajectories were identified: very high-late decline (17.53%), high-gradual decline (45.59%), moderate-gradual decline (29.24%), and low-persistent decline (7.63%). During 33,744 person-years of follow-up, 638 participants developed CMM. Compared with the very high-late decline group, fully adjusted HRs were 1.53 (95%CI = 1.19-1.96), 1.75 (1.31-2.33), and 2.38 (1.61-3.52) for high-gradual decline, moderate-gradual decline, and low-persistent decline groups, respectively. Associations were observed across all three CMM subtypes, and generally persisted in sensitivity analyses, including alternative IC scoring approaches.

CONCLUSIONS: Less favorable long-term IC trajectories were associated with higher subsequent CMM risk. Repeated IC assessments may provide useful information for identifying older adults at elevated cardiometabolic risk.

articles.title: When moderate aortic stenosis is not so moderate: toward a multiparametric risk stratification.
TAVI versus SAVR in adults with bicuspid aortic valve and heart failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal valve replacement strategy for adults with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and heart failure remains uncertain. We compared outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) versus surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR).

METHODS: Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we identified adults with BAV and heart failure diagnoses during 2020-2024 who underwent TAVI or SAVR. Patients with endocarditis, heart transplant, ventricular assist devices, concomitant non-aortic valve surgery, or coronary artery bypass grafting were excluded. Propensity score matching incorporated demographics, comorbidities, medications, and clinical measurements. All-cause mortality was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes included acute myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and all-cause hospitalization. Outcomes were assessed over 2 years using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses. Hernia and upper respiratory infection served as prespecified falsification endpoints.

RESULTS: Propensity score matching yielded 383 patients per group, with a mean age of 65.7 years. Mortality occurred in 22 TAVI patients (5.7%) and 14 SAVR patients (3.7%; HR 1.57, 95% CI 0.80-3.07). No statistically significant differences were detected in mortality, acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.34, 95% CI 0.84-2.14), ischemic stroke (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.67-1.83), or all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.79-1.10). Falsification endpoints did not differ significantly. Left ventricular ejection fraction was recorded in 27.4% of matched TAVI patients and 26.4% of matched SAVR patients.

CONCLUSION: The imprecise mortality estimate did not exclude clinically important harm associated with TAVI. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish equivalence or noninferiority.

articles.title: Myocardial infarction risk across cancer subtypes - a nationwide registry-based follow-up study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As cancer survival improves, a growing population of patients is exposed to elevated cardiovascular risk. We compared the one-year risk of myocardial infarction (MI) across 13 cancer types using patients with low-risk skin tumors as a cancer-active reference group.

METHODS: In this nationwide registry-based cohort study, we included 660,531 Danish patients diagnosed with one of 13 cancer subtypes between 2000 and 2023. Patients with prior MI or coronary revascularization were excluded. Standardized one-year absolute risks of MI were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator with inverse probability of treatment weighting, while relative risks were estimated using g-computation based on cause-specific Cox models for MI and all-cause death.

RESULTS: Compared with patients with low-risk skin tumors, the relative risk of MI was highest in multiple myeloma (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.34-2.26), bladder cancer (RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.26-1.78), kidney cancer (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.20-1.82), leukemia (RR 1.45, 95% CI 1.16-1.75), and gastrointestinal cancer (RR 1.37, 95% CI 1.24-1.50). Standardized one-year MI risk remained below 1% across all cancer subtypes, ranging from 0.31% in breast cancer to 0.91% in multiple myeloma. One-year all-cause mortality varied markedly across cancer subtypes, from 2.2% in patients with low-risk skin tumors to 71.9% in patients with hepatobiliary and pancreatic cancer.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year MI risk varied across cancer subtypes. Relative and standardized absolute MI risks were highest in patients with multiple myeloma, with increased risks also observed in several other cancer subtypes. These findings represent MI risk in the presence of substantial competing mortality and should not be interpreted as differences in underlying biological susceptibility to MI.

articles.title: 1-Deoxynojirimycin attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy via PI3K/AKT-mediated mitochondrial protection and anti-apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: 1-Deoxynojirimycin (DNJ), a naturally occurring alkaloid derived from mulberry leaves (Morus alba L.), is a powerful α-glucosidase inhibitor that has notable hypoglycemic effects. Nonetheless, the fundamental molecular mechanisms-especially diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM)-are still not fully understood.

PURPOSE: This study sought to determine the cardioprotective effect of DNJ in diabetic cardiomyopathy and to elucidate the associated molecular mechanism.

METHODS: A high glucose-induced DCM model was established in H9C2 cells and db/db mice. DNJ was administered by gavage or coculture with cells. The molecular mechanism of DNJ activity and changes in the activity of the PI3K/AKT pathway were evaluated by echocardiography, tissue staining, transmission electron microscopy, fluorescence probes, biochemical kits, Western blotting, and transcriptome sequencing, and the pathway was verified by the use of inhibitors.

RESULTS: In vivo tests initially demonstrated that DNJ may lower body weight and fasting blood glucose levels; enhance glucose tolerance and cardiac performance; diminish myocardial fibrosis, myocardial hypertrophy, and lipid accumulation; and reduce myocardial cell death in db/db mice. DNJ therapy improved the HG-induced reduction in H9C2 cell viability, reduced ROS levels, mitigated oxidative damage, and inhibited cell death. DNJ can restore HG-mediated suppression of ATP5B expression and ATP levels, potentially enhancing mitochondrial energy utilization. The therapeutic efficacy of DNJ may be contingent upon the PI3K/AKT pathway, underscoring its regulatory significance, particularly in mediating cellular responses to oxidative stress and promoting cell survival in H9C2 cells.

CONCLUSIONS: Our preliminary findings suggest that DNJ may alleviate diabetic myocardial injury, possibly by triggering the PI3K/AKT pathway. This work offers a preliminary rationale for DNJ as a prospective treatment agent for DCM.

articles.title: Anti-asthmatic effects of Chai-Po-Tang in experimental models: chemical profiling, exploratory network pharmacology, and assessment of NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-related pyroptosis signaling.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chai-Po-Tang (CPT) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from Xiao-Chai-Hu-Tang and Ban-Xia-Hou-Po-Tang, two classical prescriptions historically used for respiratory symptom patterns involving cough, dyspnea, chest oppression, and phlegm obstruction. However, whether the anti-asthmatic effects of CPT are associated with modulation of inflammasome- and pyroptosis-related signaling remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: The present study aimed to evaluate the anti-asthmatic effects of CPT and investigate whether these effects were associated with modulation of pyroptosis-related NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD signaling, while using network pharmacology as a hypothesis-generating approach to identify candidate regulatory targets.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical constituents of CPT were identified using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS). Network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were employed to predict its potential therapeutic targets and signaling pathways. Subsequently, LPS/ATP-induced BEAS-2B cell inflammasome activation model and an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthmatic mouse model were established. The effects of CPT were evaluated using cell viability assays, ROS measurement, transmission electron microscopy, inflammatory mediator quantification, pulmonary function testing, histopathology, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting, while pyroptosis-related proteins were assessed as mechanistic correlates rather than as evidence of direct causal dependence.

RESULTS: A total of 1155 chemical features/components were tentatively annotated in CPT, of which 102 candidate compounds were prioritized for network pharmacology using predefined in silico and literature-based criteria. Among the 102 prioritized candidates, 37 were supported by experimentally acquired MS/MS fragmentation spectra, whereas 65 were tentatively annotated on the basis of accurate mass, isotope distribution, database matching, and literature evidence without complete experimental MS/MS confirmation. Network pharmacology nominated IL6, FN1, and KIT as candidate targets, whereas molecular docking provided in silico support for potential ligand-target interactions only. In vitro experiments demonstrated that CPT-containing serum significantly enhanced the viability of BEAS-2B cells, reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, ameliorated ultrastructural damage, and inhibited the co-localization of NLRP3 with cleaved Caspase-1, as well as the co-localization of cleaved Caspase-1 with GSDMD-N. In vivo studies showed that CPT markedly improved clinical manifestations and pulmonary function in asthmatic mice, alleviated lung inflammation, airway remodeling, and mucus secretion. Additionally, CPT decreased the levels of IL-6, IL-1β, and IL-18, and significantly downregulated the expression of NLRP3, cleaved Caspase-1, and GSDMD-N in lung tissues. Western blot analysis further showed lower NLRP3 and ASC expression, together with lower GSDMD-N/GSDMD and cleaved Caspase-1/pro-Caspase-1 ratios, in CPT-treated lung tissues. These findings indicate that CPT treatment was associated with reduced NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway-related signaling in the experimental models.

CONCLUSION: In OVA-induced allergic asthma and LPS/ATP-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, CPT improved inflammatory and functional outcomes in parallel with reduced NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway-related signaling. These data support further investigation of inflammasome-associated pyroptosis as one plausible contributor to CPT activity, while direct causal dependence and the contribution of other predicted targets require dedicated assessment.

articles.title: Mulberry leaf flavonoids alleviate type 2 diabetes by remodeling the gut microbiota-bile acid axis and activating FXR signaling.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Mulberry leaf (Morus alba L.) has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for treating "Xiaoke" (diabetes), as documented in "Compendium of Materia Medica" compiled by Li Shi-Zhen of the Ming Dynasty. Mulberry leaf flavonoids (MLF) are the major active components and have demonstrated anti-diabetic effects in modern studies. However, whether MLF alleviates type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) by modulating the gut microbiota-bile acid axis and directly activating key metabolic receptors such as FXR remains unclear.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate whether MLF ameliorates T2DM through remodeling the gut microbiota-bile acid axis and activating FXR signaling, and to identify potential flavonoid constituents within MLF that directly interact with FXR.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: db/db mice were treated with low- or high-dose MLF (300 or 600 mg/kg/day) or metformin for 10 weeks. Blood glucose, insulin sensitivity, lipid profiles, and hepatic pathology were assessed. Gut microbiota composition was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, and bile acid profiles in serum, liver, ileum, and feces were quantified by targeted metabolomics. The expression of FXR/TGR5 signaling pathway components was determined by qRT-PCR and Western blot. Molecular docking was performed to screen for potential FXR modulator among MLF constituents, followed by in vitro validation using HepG2 and Caco-2 cells.

RESULTS: MLF treatment significantly reduced fasting blood glucose, improved glucose tolerance and insulin resistance, lowered serum and hepatic lipid levels, and alleviated hepatic steatosis in db/db mice. MLF reshaped the gut microbiota by increasing beneficial genera (e.g., Alloprevotella, Roseburia) and decreasing the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio. Concurrently, MLF reprogrammed bile acid profiles across multiple organs, elevating non-12-OH bile acids (e.g., CDCA) and reducing the FXR antagonist Tβ-MCA, thereby activating intestinal and hepatic FXR/TGR5 signaling, upregulating FGF15 and SHP, and increasing serum GLP-1. Molecular docking identified Morusin as a candidate FXR ligand, and in vitro assays confirmed that both MLF and Morusin activated FXR and modulated downstream targets (BSEP, NTCP, ASBT, CYP7A1) in hepatocytes and intestinal cells.

CONCLUSION: MLF alleviates T2DM by remodeling the gut microbiota-bile acid axis and activating FXR/TGR5 signaling. Morusin, a flavonoid constituent of MLF, is a potential FXR-modulating compound. These findings provide a modern mechanistic rationale for the traditional use of mulberry leaf in treating diabetes and support the development of MLF as a gut-targeted therapeutic strategy for T2DM.

articles.title: Impact of lamiaceae plants on anthropometric indices in patients with metabolic syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The Lamiaceae family, commonly known as the mint or sage family, comprises a vast group of aromatic medicinal plants with a global distribution and a deeply entrenched history in traditional medicine systems worldwide. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the effects of Lamiaceae plants on anthropometric indices in metabolic syndrome patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, ISI Web of Science, ProQuest, SID, and MagIran from inception to July 15, 2025, for RCTs evaluating Lamiaceae plants versus placebo in adults (≥18 years) with metabolic syndrome or related conditions (obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease). Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, with subgroup analyses by intervention duration (≤8 vs. >8 weeks), metabolic status, and Lamiaceae genus. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using NutriGrade. This review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was pre-registered (PROSPERO: CRD420251051273).

RESULTS: Twenty eligible RCTs (n = 2445 participants) met inclusion criteria. Using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool, 50% of studies had unclear allocation concealment, and 10% had high performance bias risk. Random-effects meta-analysis demonstrated statistically significant reductions in size-based indices (BMI, weight) and proxies of central adiposity (WC, WHR), while changes in direct body composition (BFM) were not significant. Both short-term (≤8 weeks) and long-term (>8 weeks) consumption of Lamiaceae reduced BMI, with effects on WC and weight primarily in overweight/obese individuals. Subgroup analyses revealed that specific genera within the Lamiaceae family, particularly Salvia and Zataria, were effective in reducing BMI and WC (only Salvia). Meta-regression analysis revealed no significant linear associations between intervention duration, metabolic status, or Lamiaceae genus and the anthropometric changes. The NutriGrade assessment rated the overall confidence in the meta-evidence as high for the pooled estimates of BMI and weight and moderate for WHR.

CONCLUSION: Lamiaceae supplementation is associated with modest reductions in size-based and central adiposity indices (BMI, WC, WHR) in adults with metabolic syndrome; exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential signals for Salvia and Zataria, though based on limited trials. However, current evidence is insufficient to demonstrate significant changes in BFM or benefits in patients with diabetes, likely due to limited trial numbers, short durations, and indirect measurement methods. Therefore, Lamiaceae may be considered a supportive adjunct within multicomponent lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Jiajian Shuyu Pills ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulation hippo signaling and the lipid metabolism-ferroptosis axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ischemic stroke is a life-threatening cerebrovascular disease characterized by focal injury to the central nervous system. Jiajian Shuyu Pills (JJSYP), a modified traditional Chinese medicine formulation derived from Shuyu Pills, consist of multiple herbs, including Rhizoma Dioscoreae, Polygonum multiflorum Thunb, Rehmannia glutinosa Libosch, Codonopsis pilosula (Franch.) Nannf, Atractylodes macrocephala Koidz, Poria cocos (Schw.) Wolf, Paeonia lactiflora Pall, Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels, Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort, Eucommia ulmoides Oliv, Polygala tenuifolia Willd, Acorus tatarinowii Schott, Lycium barbarum L, and Schisandra chinensis (Turcz.) Baill. JJSYP show therapeutic potential for ischemic stroke; however, their bioactive components and molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently defined.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of JJSYP against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms through comprehensive multi-omics integration, thereby providing a scientific basis for the clinical application of JJSYP and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for CIRI.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic, multi-step experimental strategy was employed. The protective effects of JJSYP against CIRI-induced neurological deficits were evaluated in a transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) mouse model, in which mice underwent 1 h of middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by 24 h of reperfusion. And proteomic analysis was performed to identify differentially expressed proteins and predict the signaling pathways involved in the anti-CIRI effects of JJSYP. Then, the bioactive components of JJSYP were identified through chemical profiling combined with network pharmacology. Untargeted metabolomics was used to characterize changes in metabolic profiles, and a "component-target-metabolite-pathway" network was constructed to clarify their potential associations. Finally, molecular biological experiments and lipidomic analysis were conducted to validate the anti-CIRI mechanisms of JJSYP.

RESULTS: In vivo experiments showed that JJSYP significantly alleviated cerebral tissue injury and improved neurological function in CIRI mice. Proteomic analysis indicated that JJSYP may mitigate CIRI primarily by regulating the Hippo signaling pathway, which is closely associated with cell survival, proliferation, and apoptosis. Integrated network pharmacology and metabolomics analyses identified six core JJSYP components that potentially modulate seven key targets and regulate six critical CIRI-related metabolic pathways. Validation experiments further confirmed that JJSYP modulated Hippo signaling-related proteins, including p-YAP/YAP, SOX2, and YWHAZ, and improved lipid peroxidation- and ferroptosis-related markers, such as 4-HNE, ACSL4, and PLA2G2A, suggesting that JJSYP may exert anti-CIRI effects by regulating Hippo signaling and the lipid metabolism-ferroptosis axis.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to systematically investigate the potential anti-CIRI mechanisms of JJSYP through multi-omics analysis. The findings preliminarily suggest that JJSYP alleviates CIRI by modulating the Hippo signaling pathway and the lipid metabolism-ferroptosis axis. This study provides preclinical scientific evidence for the therapeutic effects of JJSYP and offers a feasible strategy for elucidating the mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine formulas, thereby facilitating their modernization and internationalization.

articles.title: Integrating spectrum-effect relationship, network pharmacology and multi-omics to decipher the mechanism of Cybister chinensis Motschulsky against chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cybister chinensis Motschulsky is a traditional Chinese medicinal insect traditionally used to tonify the kidney, and clinically applied for the management of chronic kidney disease (CKD).

AIM OF THE STUDY: The present work was dedicated to identifying bioactive ingredients in the ethyl acetate fraction of C. chinensis and elucidating their mechanisms underlying the treatment of CKD.

METHODS: Compounds were isolated and used to establish fingerprints. Anti-inflammatory and anti-injury activities in vitro and grey relational analysis were applied to establish spectrum-effect relationships. Network pharmacology combined with molecular docking was employed to identify the candidate bioactive components. The effects of ethyl acetate fraction of C. chinensis were explored in doxorubicin-induced CKD rat model via Western blot, RT-PCR, transcriptomics, and metabolomics. Molecular dynamics simulation was applied to assess binding affinity of bioactive components. Cell experiments verified effects of components on inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis.

RESULTS: The ethyl acetate fraction of C. chinensis was confirmed as the active fraction. Compounds 6, 10, 22, 23 and 27 were screened as the potential active components. Ethyl acetate fraction improved the condition of CKD rats, while multi-omics identified a triple-functional network against inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis, with PI3K-AKT/MAPK/HIF-1 pathways verified. Cell experiments and molecular dynamics simulation identified compound 6 as the key active component, with its regulatory effects validated through PI3K-AKT/MAPK/HIF-1 pathways.

CONCLUSION: Ethyl acetate fraction of C. chinensis and its active component exerted renoprotective effects by suppressing inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis in CKD via regulating PI3K-Akt, MAPK, and HIF-1 pathways.

articles.title: Investigation of anti-asthmatic constituents and mechanisms of Cimicifugae Rhizoma based on LC-MS analysis, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cimicifugae Rhizoma was used for the treatment of asthma in traditional Chinese medicine. The triterpenoid partition of Cimicifugae Rhizoma, named as 'Ximingting', is commercially used for perimenopausal syndrome. However, the anti-asthma constituents and mechanism of Cimicifugae Rhizoma, as well as the therapeutic effect of 'Ximingting' on asthma remain unknown.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to illustrate anti-asthma constituents of Cimicifugae Rhizoma and 'Ximingting', and explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The ethyl acetate fraction of Cimicifugae Rhizoma extract (EAEC) was prepared accroding to the manufacturing process of 'Ximingting'. The chemical composition of EAEC were analyzed by UPLC-MS/MS. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma mouse model was used for evaluating the bioassay in vivo. Network pharmacology was adopted for predicting anti-asthmatic targets/pathways, validated by molecular docking, ELISA, Western blot, qRT-PCR, immunofluorescence, and flow cytometry.

RESULTS: Fifty-eight constituents (mainly triterpenoids) were identified in EAEC.
