While pediatric acute cardiac care is also complex, high-risk, and requires specialized nurses, little is known about nurse characteristics in this care area.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the evolving characteristics of pediatric cardiac nurses in non-ICU settings over 10 years and to compare these characteristics to established benchmarks.

METHOD: Aggregate data were collected from participating pediatric acute cardiac care units and inpatient units in 2016, 2022, and 2025. Benchmarks included the proportion of nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) or higher, ≤2 years of experience, and specialty pediatric certification. Descriptive statistics summarized percentages at the unit and aggregate levels and compared results to a 2015 baseline survey, subsequent time points, and the benchmark.

RESULTS: The median of BSN-prepared nurses increased from 87% (2016) to 96% (2022/2025), with all units meeting the benchmark (2022). Nurses with ≤2 years of experience remained stable (median: 40% to 43%), with 1 unit meeting the benchmark (2025). Specialty certification declined from 44% (2016) to 19% (2025), with 3 units meeting the benchmark (2025).

DISCUSSION: This is the first report describing the characteristics of pediatric cardiac nursing over a 10-year period. While education has increased to benchmark, vulnerabilities remain in experience and certification. Ongoing benchmarking and collaboration are needed to support nursing practice and ensure high-quality care for pediatric cardiac patients.

articles.title: Effect of Chlorhexidine Oral Care on Ventilator-Associated Events in 4 ICU Populations: A Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG) oral care is used to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, but its effectiveness in reducing ventilator-associated events (VAE) remains unclear. VAE encompasses both infectious and noninfectious complications.

OBJECTIVE: To examine the impact of twice daily 0.12% CHG oral care on VAE, length of stay (LOS), mechanical ventilator (MV) hours, and in-hospital mortality in 4 intensive care unit (ICU) populations: cardiac surgical, cardiac medical, multisystem, and neurological.

METHODS: An analysis using an electronic health record clinical database of 1567 mechanically ventilated patients from a quaternary hospital in central Florida was conducted. χ2, ANOVA, logistic regression, linear regression, and mediation analysis using LOS and MV hours as mediators assessed the relationship between CHG oral care and clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: The cardiac surgical population had the highest VAE rate (47.13), whereas the neurological ICU had the lowest (5.87) per 1000 ventilator days. Each additional CHG oral care treatment was associated with a 4.9% increase in VAE odds, a 6-hour increase in MV duration, and a 0.55-day increase in LOS. LOS but not MV hours partially mediated the relationship between CHG exposure and VAE. Mortality analysis was limited by missing data.

CONCLUSIONS: CHG oral care was not associated with reductions in VAE, MV hours, LOS, or mortality. Our analyses suggest that CHG oral care may have served as a proxy for patient acuity rather than a protective intervention. Our cardiac surgical sample may not be representative of this population. Findings from our study did not support the need to continue using routine CHG oral care in MV-ventilated patients.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Therapy on Mortality Rate and Major Clinical Complications in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) with high-risk coronary lesions or cardiogenic shock (CS) is still one of the most common causes of death and morbidity throughout the world. Mechanical circulatory support, such as the intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP), is used to improve hemodynamic stability in such cases, but evidence regarding its impact on survival and long-term outcomes remains inconclusive. The study will be helpful in guiding clinical decisions if a comprehensive synthesis of RCTs becomes available.

OBJECTIVES: To determine through a systematic review the efficacy of IABP in reducing mortality and major clinical complications in patients suffering from AMI with or without CS.

METHODS: In line with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, an electronic search was performed for RCTs published between 2010 and 2025 in PubMed, MEDLINE, CINAHL, ProQuest, Scopus, ScienceDirect, EBSCO, and SAGE Journals. Quality appraisal was done by 2 independent reviewers based on CONSORT guidelines, and risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Key study characteristics, interventions, outcomes, and limitations were extracted and synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs were included. Interventions were elective or rescue IABP support during high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with or without CS. The evidence consistently showed that routine or prophylactic IABP use in patients without shock did not significantly reduce mortality or infarct size. In CS, IABP alone did not improve long-term survival. Percutaneous mechanical circulatory support demonstrated potential short-term survival benefits in carefully selected high-risk populations. Hemodynamic stabilization was generally achieved, but device-related complications and long-term functional outcomes were inconsistently reported.

DISCUSSION: Mechanical circulatory support provides hemodynamic stabilization in AMI, particularly in CS. While IABP shows limited survival benefit in stable patients, alternative devices may offer short-term advantages in selected high-risk cases. Patient selection, timing, and integration with guideline-directed therapy are essential for clinical effectiveness.

STUDY REGISTRATION: PROSPERO Protocol registration ID: CRD420251156209.

articles.title: Say No to Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infections: A Sustained Quality Improvement Initiative in the Neuro Intensive Care Unit.
articles.journal: Dimensions of critical care nursing : DCCN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2022 and 2023, the Neuroscience Intensive Care Unit (ICU) reported 12 catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTIs), a marked increase from previous years, prompting a comprehensive review of catheter use, current urine culture collection practices, and evidence-based practices.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this quality improvement (QI) project was to address gaps in urine culture collection technique, reduce excessive catheter days, foster a unit culture that prioritized evidence-based urinary catheter management, and reduce CAUTI rates over a 3-year period.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary initiative was launched, involving staff education, protocol development, and process changes. Key interventions included direct education sessions on proper urine culture collection, implementation of the Neuroscience ICU Urinary Protocol, the Urinary Catheter Nurse-Driven Removal Protocol, and the Urinalysis (UA) and Urine Culture Collection Protocol. Data management involves monthly audits and real-time education to ensure adherence to protocols.

RESULTS: Indwelling catheter utilization rates and urine culture collections remained high. However, the unit achieved a 100% reduction in reportable CAUTIs in 2024 and 2025. The unit has 1 CAUTI thus far in 2026. This reflects improved adherence to collection protocols and standard urinary catheter care.

DISCUSSION: Ongoing collaboration, education, and use of evidence-based practices may be important for sustaining these results and encouraging further improvements in other units. The initiative fostered a culture of critical thinking and autonomy among nurses, with ongoing audits and celebrations of milestones supporting sustained engagement.

articles.title: Recovery of adrenal function following sequential spontaneous bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: Adrenal hemorrhage is uncommon; bilateral involvement is even rarer and can result in adrenal crisis. A 55-year-old man presented with severe atraumatic flank and low back pain; computed tomography of the abdomen revealed acute left adrenal hemorrhage. He was managed conservatively. Seven days after initial presentation, he returned with contralateral flank pain; repeat imaging demonstrated a new right adrenal hemorrhage with persistent left hemorrhage. He developed nausea, vomiting, headache, and hyponatremia; the morning cortisol was 8.99 µg/dL (248 nmol/L; reference range, 5-25 µg/dL [138-690 nmol/L]). He was admitted to the intensive care unit and treated with stress-dose hydrocortisone. Fludrocortisone was initiated as plasma renin activity was elevated. Extensive evaluation for an underlying etiology for adrenal hemorrhage was unrevealing. Serial imaging showed near-complete resolution of hematomas. Follow-up testing approximately a year after initial presentation demonstrated complete recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, allowing for discontinuation of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case highlights the need for repeat imaging and close biochemical monitoring for adrenal insufficiency and HPA axis recovery following bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.

articles.title: Understanding Emotional Intelligence and Empathy Among Critical Care Nursing Students in Palestine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human interactions and emotions are crucial aspects of nursing care that contribute to overall care quality. The purpose of the study is to assess the relationship between empathy and emotional intelligence among critical care nursing students.

METHODS: A cross-sectional research study was conducted between October and November 2022. The study included a convenience sample of fourth-year critical care nursing students. The research utilized self-administered questionnaires, including the Schutte Self-Reported Emotional Intelligence Test and the Multidimensional Emotional Empathy Scale.

RESULTS: A total of 202 nursing students participated in the survey, with a mean age of 20.8 (2.5) and a majority (59.4%) being female. The investigation revealed a high emotional intelligence mean of 151.6 ± 1.7. The domain with the highest mean score was "perception of emotions" at 47.1 ± 1.12, while "utilizing emotions" had the lowest mean score at 27.6 ± 0.68. The mean empathy score was 3.37. The score for "Responsive crying" was low at 2.65, while "positive sharing" had a high score of 4.10. The analysis revealed a weak but statistically significant association between emotional intelligence and empathy (r = 0.14, P = 0 .04).

CONCLUSION: The study found high emotional intelligence (EI) and moderate empathy levels among nursing students, with a slight positive correlation between EI and empathy.

articles.title: Factors Influencing ICU Nurses' Intention to Use a Manometer for Endotracheal Tube Cuff Pressure Monitoring: An Application of the Theory of Planned Behavior.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maintaining endotracheal tube cuff pressure (20-30 cmH2O) is vital to prevent aspiration and tracheal injury. While manometry is considered the gold standard for monitoring cuff pressure, clinical adherence remains suboptimal among critical care providers, including intensive care unit (ICU) nurses and respiratory therapists, leading to potential patient safety risks. Therefore, this study investigated factors influencing critical care providers' intention to use a manometer, based on the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2024 among 186 ICU nurses working in four public hospitals in Amol, Iran. Nurses were enrolled through census sampling. Data were collected using a demographic checklist, a checklist of ICU ward structural characteristics, and a validated TPB-based scale assessing attitudes, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and intention. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: The mean (standard deviation) score of intention to use a manometer was 17.81 (3.97). Positive attitudes (β = 0.335, P < .001), supportive subjective norms (β = 0.200, P = .005), perceived behavioral control (β = 0.167, P = .013), and access to the manometer (β = 0.192, P = .001) were significant predictors of intention.

CONCLUSION: In addition to TPB components, the availability of manometers significantly influenced nurses' intentions. Interventions to improve access and enhance positive attitudes and social support may promote standard cuff pressure monitoring.

articles.title: Reducing Lines, Drains, Airways Dislodgement in the Surgical Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Reduce lines, drains, airways (LDA) dislodgements by 50% in 6 months, as tracked by situation, background, assessment, recommendation dislodgement forms, and safety incident reports.

BACKGROUND: LDA dislodgement is a significant safety concern leading to extended hospital stays, increased costs, and poorer patient outcomes. From January to May 2024, the SICU experienced 31 LDA dislodgements.

METHODS: The LDA Taskforce, consisting of nursing staff and leadership, implemented several strategies. Door signage categorized patients by risk level, and an in-service binder was developed to educate staff using the "teach-back" method. Key methods included appropriate restraint usage, 2 registered nurse handoffs during transitions, a "time-out" before patient movement, and proper LDA securement. Post-incident debriefings helped identify and address gaps. Data on dislodgements were collected weekly.

RESULTS: Before the project, there were 31 dislodgements from January to May 2024. Post-implementation, dislodgements reduced to 15 from June to November 2024, achieving a 50% reduction. Further success was seen from December 2024 to May 2025, with only 11 incidents.

CONCLUSION: The taskforce effectively reduced LDA dislodgements in the SICU. The in-service training is now part of the SICU orientation, ensuring ongoing improvement.

DISCUSSION/CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS: The LDA Dislodgement Taskforce successfully decreased the amount of LDA dislodgements in the SICU. The LDA dislodgement in-service is now part of the SICU unit orientation.

articles.title: Relationship Between Level of Consciousness, Pressure Ulcer Risk, and Pain Behaviors in Mechanically Ventilated Patients.
articles.abstract: Mechanically ventilated patients are vulnerable to pain, pressure injuries, and decreased levels of consciousness. This descriptive and correlational study examined the relationship between the level of consciousness, pressure injury risk, and pain behaviors in 150 patients treated in the intensive care units of a university hospital between November 2023 and February 2024. Data were collected using the Behavioral Pain Scale (BPS), Jackson/Cubbin Pressure Area Risk Assessment Tool, and Full Outline of UnResponsiveness (FOUR) Score. The mean FOUR Score was 6.78 ± 2.15, the mean Jackson/Cubbin score was 29.68 ± 2.79, and the mean BPS score was 4.73 ± 1.46. Pressure injury risk was significantly related to inotropic support and skin integrity (P < .001). Patients receiving enteral nutrition and those without sedation or inotropic support had higher BPS scores (P < .05). Weak positive correlations were found between the FOUR Score and both BPS (r = 0.190) and Jackson/Cubbin scores (r = 0.306). In conclusion, although patients had low consciousness and pain levels, regular assessment of pain, skin integrity, and consciousness remains essential for preventing complications and guiding individualized nursing care in intensive care settings.

articles.title: The Effect of Multisensory Stimuli on Pain During Eye Examination in Premature Infants: Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the necessity for regular eye examinations for premature infants, these procedures can cause pain and physiological stress in infants, highlighting the need for effective relief strategies. This study investigates the efficacy of a multisensory stimulation care program on pain response during eye examinations.

METHODS: The study was a single-blind randomized clinical trial. Participants included infants aged 2 to 6 months who had prior experience with eye examinations. The intervention group received both pharmacological (topical tetracaine) and nonpharmacological (multisensory stimulation) interventions, while the control group received only pharmacological interventions. Heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, pain scores, and crying duration were assessed before, during, and after the examination.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant increases in heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and pain scores during the examination (P < .001). However, the intervention group had a smaller increase in heart rate and pain scores (P = .04; P < .001). In addition, the intervention group maintained better levels of heart rate, oxygen saturation, and pain scores postexamination (P = .01; P = .03; P < .001). Crying duration was shorter in the intervention group compared with the control group (P = .001).

CONCLUSION: Multisensory stimulation significantly mitigates pain responses in infants undergoing eye examinations, demonstrating its potential as a beneficial nonpharmacological pain management strategy.

articles.title: Exploration of Professional Competence and Moral Sensitivity in Critical Care Unit Nurses.
articles.abstract: Nursing competence is a key aspect of health care quality. This study aimed to explore the relationship between professional competence and moral sensitivity in nurses working in critical care units, utilizing a cross-sectional design. The study was conducted in 2018 and included nurses working in critical care units who met the inclusion criteria of having at least 1 year of experience in cardiac care units and holding a bachelor's degree. Data were collected through a demographic questionnaire, the Competency Inventory for Registered Nurses, and the Moral Sensitivity Questionnaire. The findings revealed a weak positive correlation between professional competence and moral sensitivity (r = 0.319, P = .002). Age, number of shifts, and type of hospital were also significantly correlated with nurses' professional competence and moral sensitivity. Given the direct correlation between professional competence and moral sensitivity, as well as the factors influencing these variables, it is recommended that nursing managers focus on developing programs to enhance them. Nurses should have a solid understanding of ethical principles. As professional competence and moral sensitivity are intertwined, it is crucial for nursing managers to plan initiatives to improve the professional competence of nurses in the intensive care unit ultimately enhancing the quality of care.

articles.title: Assessment of Critical Care Nurses' Knowledge, Compliance, and Barriers Related to Implementation of the Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia Prevention Guidelines.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is the most prevalent serious hospital-acquired infection, contributing to high morbidity and mortality among adult and pediatric patients receiving mechanical ventilation. Critical care nurses (CCNs) are central to VAP prevention, as their knowledge, adherence to evidence-based guidelines, and ability to overcome barriers directly influence patient outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge, compliance, and barriers related to VAP prevention among critical care nurses in Palestine.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, descriptive-correlational study was conducted with 329 CCNs using a self-reported questionnaire. The instrument included sections on sociodemographic characteristics, awareness of VAP prevention guidelines, adherence to preventive practices, and barriers to implementation.

RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 5.12 out of 10. Self-reported adherence to VAP prevention practices ranged from 38.6% to 89.4%, with the highest compliance in maintaining the head of the bed at 30-45 degrees and the lowest in using closed suction systems. The most frequently reported barriers were insufficient nursing staff and limited resources.

CONCLUSION: Findings indicate notable gaps in CCNs' knowledge and practice, largely influenced by organizational and resource-related barriers. Targeted education, adequate staffing, and improved resource allocation are essential to enhance adherence to VAP prevention guidelines and reduce the incidence, morbidity, and mortality associated with VAP in critical care settings.

articles.title: Mobilizing the Critically Ill: The Central Role of Nurses in Preventing ICU Complications and Enhancing Recovery.
articles.abstract: The intensive care unit (ICU) is a high-acuity environment where patients with severe illness receive comprehensive care. Immobility is common among patients with critical disease states and contributes to muscle atrophy, development of pressure ulcers, increased risk of thromboembolic events, and acute respiratory insufficiency. Similarly, delirium is another prevalent complication that further contributes to prolonged ICU stays, increased mortality, and long-term cognitive impairments. Reduced mobility, delirium, and other sequelae of critical illness pose significant challenges to patient recovery and often result in poor long-term outcomes. Early mobility has been shown to improve long-term outcomes of critically ill patients by reducing their length of hospital and ICU stay, reducing ICU-acquired weakness, improving functional outcomes, and improving long-term cognitive function. Given their direct patient contact, nurses are uniquely positioned to serve as the primary facilitators of patient mobility in the ICU. As frontline caregivers, nurses can assess a patient's readiness for mobility, monitor vital signs during activity, and provide hands-on support for safe mobilization. They are instrumental in coordinating interdisciplinary efforts, ensuring effective communication among health care team members, and advocating patient-centered mobility goals. Additionally, nurses contribute to delirium prevention and management by closely monitoring cognitive changes, facilitating family engagement, and promoting nonpharmacological interventions such as sleep hygiene and cognitive stimulation. Through their continuous presence and compassionate care, nurses not only address the physical aspects of recovery but also provide emotional support to patients and families, significantly enhancing psychological well-being in the ICU. By leveraging their clinical expertise and patient advocacy skills, nurses are essential in fostering a culture of mobility and comprehensive care in the ICU, ultimately leading to better patient outcomes and quality of life for critical illness survivors.

articles.title: High fat mass ratio is associated with reduced insulin sensitivity, pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, and elevated glucose excursion in middle-aged Japanese adults.
articles.abstract: The prevalence of a high fat mass ratio (FMR), a candidate marker of lipodystrophy-like phenotypes, body composition, and its cardiometabolic traits were investigated in Japanese female university students and their biological parents, whose mean BMI was less than 25.0 kg/m2. In a subgroup, we also evaluated surrogate indices of insulin sensitivity, insulin secretion, and pancreatic β-cell function assessed using the disposition index derived from serum insulin kinetics during a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). The prevalence of high FMR, defined as trunk fat percentage divided by leg fat percentage, was 3.6% in young women and 28.7% in parents (mothers: 26.4% and fathers: 34.5%). In daughters and parents, high FMR was associated with elevated serum triglycerides and decreased HDL cholesterol. It was also associated with elevated inflammatory markers and serum liver enzyme levels, and reduced serum adiponectin levels. Parents with high FMR, compared with the remainder, had a marginally lower Matsuda index and lower log disposition index and greater glucose excursion after oral glucose loading estimated using the area under glucose concentration curves during OGTT. They had higher blood pressure, adipose tissue insulin resistance indices, a product of fasting insulin and free fatty acid, and OGTT-derived hepatic insulin resistance indices. High FMR, a possible supportive marker of lipodystrophy-like phenotypes, was prevalent in parents of university students and was associated with reduced insulin sensitivity and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, which may help explain why some Japanese individuals develop type 2 diabetes at a lower BMI.

articles.title: Erratum for Moderating effect of professional identity on the relationship between transition shock and career intention among nursing students during clinical internship: a longitudinal ecological momentary assessment.
Expanding the Clinical Nurse Specialist Role Beyond Traditional Settings: A CNS-Led Independent Practice Model.
articles.abstract: The clinical nurse specialist (CNS) role has historically been associated with inpatient leadership, quality improvement, staff mentorship, and systems-level practice within hospital environments. Although CNS education prepares advanced practice registered nurses to function across direct patient care, nursing practice, and organizational leadership spheres, limited literature exists describing CNS-led outpatient or independent practice models. This article describes the development and implementation of a CNS-led nonprofit hybrid telehealth practice established in Michigan in 2025 that provides psychiatric medication management, addiction medicine, harm reduction services, hepatitis C treatment, HIV prevention, sexually transmitted infection care, and limited primary care services for adult populations. The practice demonstrates how CNS competencies may extend beyond traditional inpatient environments to address health care access gaps through innovative community-based care delivery. Operational elements, including payer credentialing, electronic medical record implementation, workflow development, nonprofit formation, interdisciplinary referral partnerships, and hybrid telehealth infrastructure, are discussed through the lens of CNS systems leadership competencies. This article highlights the potential for CNS-led outpatient practice models to expand health care access, strengthen continuity of care, and support population health initiatives while advocating for broader recognition of the CNS role outside traditional health care systems.

articles.title: Faster, Longer, and Smarter: Advancements in Insulin Therapy.
Developing a prediction model for adjuvant immunotherapy post-chemoradiation in stage III inoperable non-small-cell lung cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survival in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has improved with adjuvant durvalumab following chemoradiotherapy (CRT). However, CRT-related toxicities frequently prevent initiation of immuno-oncology (IO) treatment. The objective was to develop a pre-CRT prediction model for post-CRT IO eligibility that incorporates modifiable radiotherapy parameters to support treatment selection and plan optimization.

METHODS: A prospective cohort of stage III NSCLC patients treated with CRT and enrolled in a structured follow-up program between January 2017 and January 2024 was analyzed. A logistic regression model predicting IO eligibility was developed using demographic, clinical, and treatment-related variables, including lung and heart dose-volume metrics. Model performance was assessed by discrimination (AUC) and calibration. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap samples.

RESULTS: Among 452 patients, 216 (48%) received IO after CRT. Independent predictors of IO eligibility were lung volume receiving ≥1 Gy (V1), age, smoking status, clinical T stage, and WHO performance status. The model demonstrated moderate discrimination (bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.71, 95% CI 0.67-0.76) and good calibration (slope 0.89, 95% CI 0.78-1.10).

CONCLUSIONS: A prediction model for IO eligibility after CRT was developed that includes potentially modifiable factors, notably lung V1 and smoking status. Internal performance was clinically acceptable. Following external validation, the model may support personalized treatment planning and identify opportunities for dose optimization. Incorporating lung V1 into radiotherapy planning could increase the proportion of patients eligible for adjuvant IO therapy.

articles.title: Prevalence of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome and Other Hand Pathologies in Cardiac Amyloidosis.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) results from deposition of a misfolded protein, commonly transthyretin amyloid (ATTR), in the myocardial tissue, leading to a restrictive cardiomyopathy progressing to heart failure. Early diagnosis and intervention are critical for disease-modifying therapies to effectively slow disease progression and prevent cardiac involvement. ATTR also deposits in extracardiac tissues such as the transverse carpal ligament, causing carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS). We sought to characterize a cohort of patients with known ATTR CA and assess the association of CTS with cardiac and extracardiac comorbidities in ATTR CA.

METHODS: Patients (≥18 years) diagnosed with wild-type ATTR (wtATTR) or hereditary ATTR (hATTR) CA treated at an outpatient cardiology center from October 2018 to March 2023 were identified and screened. Patient demographics, presence of cardiac and extracardiac comorbidities, and the diagnosis of CTS were extracted via chart review. CTS laterality and history of carpal tunnel release were recorded for patients with CTS. These variables were compared between patients who had been diagnosed with CTS versus those who did not have CTS.

RESULTS: In total, 145 patients with CA were identified, including 69 with wtATTR and 65 with hATTR. Overall, 46% of the cohort had CTS, and all examined extracardiac comorbidities including spinal stenosis and polyneuropathy were more prevalent in patients with CTS. Patients with CTS were also significantly more likely to have heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) as well as an additional hand pathology such as trigger finger.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with ATTR CA, CTS is associated with higher rates of HFpEF as well as additional hand pathology. These patients should be considered for biopsy during minor hand surgery. Further, the presence of CTS may be associated with more severe disease with a high cardiovascular burden, such as HFpEF.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Differential diagnosis or symptom prevalence study II.

articles.title: Shifting contexts, shifting concreteness: Discourse patterns in individuals with schizophrenia.
articles.abstract: Concreteness, the degree to which words evoke perceptible and tangible referents, is central to conceptual abstraction and thought organisation. Individuals with schizophrenia often exhibit a bias toward concrete interpretations also known as concretism. However, most existing evidence derives from proverb-interpretation tasks, which capture only a narrow range of linguistic behaviour. The present study analyzed a corpus of discourse produced by individuals with schizophrenia and healthy controls to examine whether concreteness varies across different communicative contexts, reflecting the distinct cognitive demands of each discourse mode. The corpus included speech samples from 70 participants with schizophrenia and 48 healthy controls who had previously completed three tasks: Autobiographical Narration (AN), Picture Description (PD), and cartoon-based Story Narration (SN). Contextual concreteness was estimated for noun occurrences using a prediction model initially trained on AI-generated Spanish ratings and subsequently fine-tuned with human context-dependent ratings. Results revealed decisive evidence that lexical concreteness varied across discourse tasks. The omnibus analysis did not support either a global group effect or a Group × Task interaction. Nevertheless, planned task-specific comparisons showed higher concreteness in the schizophrenia group during Story Narration, with strong evidence under the directional analysis and moderate evidence under a two-sided sensitivity analysis. Evidence was inconclusive for Picture Description and favoured the null hypothesis for Autobiographical Narration. This pattern is consistent with the possibility that concreteness differences in schizophrenia are more detectable in some discourse contexts than in others. However, because the Task × Group interaction was not supported, the results do not establish that the magnitude of the group difference varies reliably across tasks.

articles.title: Risks of Perioperative Local Corticosteroid Treatment for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome and Trigger Finger: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To define procedure-specific, time-stratified surgical site infection (SSI) risk profiles following perioperative local corticosteroid injections (LCIs) in carpal tunnel release (CTR) and trigger finger release (TFR).

METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library were queried from inception to July 10, 2026, for cohort and case-control studies evaluating SSI following LCI within 6 months of CTR or TFR. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using a 27-item modified Downs and Black checklist. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models pooled odds ratios (ORs) for deep and superficial SSI across discrete preoperative intervals (≤30, 31-60, 61-90, and ≤90 days) and intraoperative administration. Bonferroni corrections (α = 0.05/m) were applied to independent comparisons.

RESULTS: Twelve studies met inclusion criteria. For CTR, LCI ≤30 days showed a nominal association with higher deep SSI odds (OR 1.36, 95% CI 1.00-1.83; P = .048), not surviving Bonferroni correction (α = 0.0083); the ≤90-day composite was not significant (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.79-1.46; P = .66). For TFR, LCI ≤90 days had significantly elevated deep SSI odds (OR 3.88, 95% CI 1.93-7.79; P < .001), driven by the ≤30-day window (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.10-6.43; P = .03); individual windows did not survive family-wise correction. The only comparison surviving Bonferroni correction within a multi-comparison family was increased superficial SSI after TFR with preoperative distant large-/intermediate-joint LCI (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.09-1.38; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Pooled estimates suggest that the risk of postoperative infection may differ by injection timing, with a stronger however imprecise risk signal observed for TFR when LCI is administered within 30 days preoperatively. Surgical timing should be individualized and procedure-specific rather than based on rigid monthly intervals.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic III.

articles.title: Oropouche virus disease across Latin America during the 2023-2025 epidemic: a multi-country case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023-2025 epidemic of Oropouche virus (OROV) disease across Latin America raised public health concerns due to its expansion into previously unaffected regions, alongside reports of increased clinical severity and vertical transmission.

METHODS: We conducted a multi-country case series to characterise the clinical presentation, disease course, outcomes, and virological features of OROV disease during the 2023-2025 epidemic. Analyses were descriptive.

FINDINGS: We describe 2716 OROV disease cases reported between January 31st, 2024, and November 4th, 2025, across ten states in Brazil, Panama, and Peru. Median age was 38 years (IQR 25-51); 1379/2716 (51%) were female. Most common symptoms were fever (89%), headache (88%), and myalgia (59%), followed by retro-orbital pain (47%). One-fourth of participants reported symptoms' duration beyond one week. Most cases were mild (2542/2716; 94%), although severe manifestations and one death occurred. Haemorrhagic manifestations were reported in 41/2716 (2%), and 7/2716 (<1%) developed severe disease temporally associated with OROV infection. Among 108 pregnant women, 15 (14%) had adverse pregnancy outcomes, including abortions, preterm births, stillbirths, and symptomatic newborns; no congenital malformations were observed. Older age, comorbidities, warning signs, and laboratory abnormalities were more frequently observed among participants with complications. Prolonged RNA detection beyond seven days was observed in serum and urine.

INTERPRETATION: Although most OROV disease cases were mild, severe disease and adverse pregnancy outcomes occur and may be under-recognised. These findings support the need for improved clinical recognition, risk stratification, and diagnostics, particularly for high-risk groups, and highlight priorities for surveillance and future research.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: H-shaped sponge positioner prevents pressure injuries during prolonged prone ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome: a single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome, prolonged prone position ventilation is frequently employed to enhance oxygenation but often results in pressure injuries. To protect patients from such injuries, a new H-shaped sponge locator was designed in the study. In this single-center, open-label, randomized controlled trial, 60 patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring extended prone position ventilation (≥ 12 hours per session) were recruited from the General Intensive Care Unit at Xiangtan Central Hospital, Hunan Province, China, between May 2023 and May 2024. Participants were randomly allocated to either the intervention group, which received prone positioning with the assistance of the H-shaped sponge positioner, or the control group, which used conventional soft pillows for support. The primary outcomes included the number of anatomical sites affected by pressure injuries and injury severity, classified according to the revised 2016 National Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel/the European Pressure Ulcer Advisory Panel staging criteria. Secondary outcomes included mean airway pressure, oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2), intravesical pressure, and the frequency of support device adjustments. Data from 29 patients in each group were analyzed. Significant group × time interactions were observed for both the number of pressure injury sites and overall incidence. Although pressure injuries increased progressively across all sessions in both groups, patients in the intervention group consistently had fewer injury sites. There were no significant group × time interactions for mean airway pressure or intravesical pressure. However, both measures increased over time in all patients, with significantly lower values in the intervention group. Oxygenation index improved over time, with no statistically significant differences between groups. The intervention group required markedly fewer support device adjustments. In patients with moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome receiving extended prone position ventilation, the H-shaped sponge positioner significantly outperformed standard soft pillow support in preventing pressure injuries. This cost-efficient device not only minimized the number and severity of pressure ulcers but also reduced mean airway and intra-abdominal pressures and decreased the frequency of nursing interventions. Given its ease of use and affordability, the H-shaped positioner holds substantial promise for clinical application, particularly in resource-constrained settings, and warrants further evaluation in broader implementation studies. This trial was registred at National Health Security Information Platform (Medical Research Registration and Information System, https://www.medicalresearch.org.cn, Registration No. MR-43-23-039592) on March 30, 2023.

articles.title: Abnormal blood gas patterns in heart failure.
Kidney effects of inhaled nitric oxide in critically ill patients: from pathophysiological considerations to clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Inhaled nitric oxide is widely used as a selective pulmonary vasodilator in critical care, yet its renal effects remain controversial. While existing reviews mostly focus on indications for inhaled nitric oxide and its impact on outcomes, limited data exist on its renal effects, since it was thought to act only locally in the lungs. This review examine the clinical evidence regarding kidney outcomes associated with inhaled nitric oxide across major indications and provide an integrated mechanistic analysis of nitric oxide signaling in renal physiology and pathophysiology. Nitric oxide is produced by nitric oxide synthases using L-arginine as a substrate. It acts as a smooth muscle relaxation factor and ultimately causes vasodilation through its effect on cyclic guanosine monophosphate. Nitric oxide plays a pivotal role in renal hemodynamic regulation, glomerular filtration, tubular function, and microcirculatory homeostasis. The net renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide likely reflects the balance between improved nitric oxide signaling and oxidative stress generation. Available clinical data suggest that the renal impact of inhaled nitric oxide is context-dependent. In acute respiratory distress syndrome, higher-level evidence indicates a potential increase in acute kidney injury, possibly related to oxidative and nitrosative stress. Conversely, in cardiac bypass surgery, inhaled nitric oxide may confer nephroprotection by restoring nitric oxide bioavailability during hemolysis and free hemoglobin-mediated nitric oxide scavenging. In other conditions, including organ transplantation, pulmonary hypertension, sepsis, and hemolytic disorders, evidence remains limited or inconclusive. Overall, current evidence does not support a uniform renal effect of inhaled nitric oxide, indicating the need for prospective studies with predefined renal endpoints to clarify its clinical relevance.

articles.title: Infection Rates Following Ultrasound-Guided Microinvasive Carpal Tunnel Release: A Single-Practice Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative infection following carpal tunnel release (CTR) is uncommon, although reported rates vary because of differences in outcome definitions and follow-up methodology. As ultrasound-guided and microinvasive CTR techniques continue to emerge, infection-specific outcomes remain inconsistently reported. The purpose of this study was to determine the rate of clinically significant postoperative infection following ultrasound-guided microinvasive CTR (Micro-CTR) and to contextualize this rate against published benchmarks.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed of consecutive adults undergoing office-based ultrasound-guided Micro-CTR in a single practice. All procedures were performed under local anesthesia using a standardized ultrasound-guided technique with percutaneous access and real-time visualization of the transverse carpal ligament and surrounding neurovascular structures. The primary outcome was clinically significant infection, defined as infection involving the palmar compartment requiring medical or surgical intervention. Secondary outcomes included localized superficial infection at the puncture site. Infection rates were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and compared descriptively with published data across CTR techniques.

RESULTS: A total of 476 patients contributed 533 procedures. Clinically significant infection occurred in one case (0.19%; 95% CI, 0.005-1.04). No localized superficial infections were identified. No cases required hospital admission or additional operative management. The observed rate was interpreted descriptively alongside published infection benchmarks across CTR techniques.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinically significant infection following ultrasound-guided Micro-CTR was rare in this single-practice cohort. The observed rate was interpreted descriptively alongside published benchmarks across established CTR techniques. Standardized, clinically meaningful outcome definitions may improve comparison of infection risk as less invasive approaches continue to emerge.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic IV.

articles.title: Secondary aldosteronism due to premature renal artery atherosclerosis in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
articles.abstract: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD), an uncommon cause of adrenal insufficiency, requires lifelong surveillance of adrenal function. Glucocorticoid deficiency is reported in approximately 80% and mineralocorticoid deficiency in 50% of patients with ALD. In 2014, we took over the follow-up of a 31-year-old man who had been diagnosed with ALD in 1991. In 1995, he was treated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and was supplemented with hydrocortisone 10 mg/m2 and fludrocortisone 0.05 mg daily. In 2015, resistant hypertension and hypokalemia were noticed and persisted despite discontinuation of fludrocortisone. Biochemical analysis showed secondary aldosteronism. Doppler ultrasonography was compatible with a hemodynamically significant right renal artery stenosis. Furthermore, significant aortic atheromatosis was described on abdominal computed tomography, which was disproportionate for the patient's age and risk factors. Spironolactone was added to his antihypertensive medication, which normalized blood pressure and hypokalemia. In 2022, he presented with severe hypotension and acute renal failure. All his antihypertensive medications were stopped because secondary aldosteronism had been resolved. The renal Doppler showed severe right renal artery stenosis with severe renal atrophy. Thus, he spontaneously infarcted his right kidney that was inducing secondary aldosteronism, confirming he had persistent inducible zona glomerulosa cells.

articles.title: Multi‑omic studies on macrophage heterogeneity: Spanning the genome‑transcriptome‑proteome cascade (Review).
articles.abstract: Macrophages are highly plastic innate immune cells that exhibit remarkable heterogeneity in phenotype, function, tissue specificity and ontogeny. Traditional research methods, including flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry and cytokine profiling, have played a foundational role in characterizing macrophage populations. However, classical classification systems, including the M1/M2 polarization paradigm, are insufficient to capture the f2ull spectrum of macrophage diversity. Advances in sequencing, mass spectrometry and spatial profiling have enabled complementary analyses of the molecular processes underlying this heterogeneity. The present review examined how genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic and proteomic evidence connects regulatory architecture with macrophage states and functions across these four dimensions. Integrated analyses reveal how developmental history, tissue signals and stimulation experience interact to shape enhancer activity, gene expression, protein abundance and post‑translational regulation. The genome‑transcriptome‑proteome cascade is considered an organizing framework that accommodates feedback and environmental inputs rather than a strictly linear biological sequence. Throughout the present review, molecularly defined states are distinguished from stable lineages and experimentally demonstrated functions. The present review further discussed challenges in causal inference, temporal and spatial resolution, cross‑omics integration and the applicability of experimental models to human disease. Future translation will require reproducible molecular signatures, functional validation and context‑specific targeting that preserves essential macrophage activities. Together, these advances refine the understanding of macrophage diversity and support the development of biomarkers and therapeutic strategies for inflammatory diseases, fibrosis and cancer.

articles.title: EPB41L4A‑AS1 promotes endothelial dysfunction in preeclampsia through the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy characterized by systemic endothelial dysfunction. Long non‑coding RNA EPB41L4A‑AS1 has been implicated in pregnancy‑related disorders, but its role in PE remains unclear. Our previous work demonstrated that downregulation of miR‑26a‑2‑3p promotes endothelial injury via activation of the 15‑lipoxygenase‑1 (15‑LOX‑1)/p38 mitogen‑activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) pathway. In the present study, whether EPB41L4A‑AS1 contributes to PE pathogenesis by regulating this axis was investigated. EPB41L4A‑AS1 expression was significantly upregulated in placental tissues from patients with PE and negatively correlated with miR‑26a‑2‑3p levels. Functional experiments revealed that EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression suppressed miR‑26a‑2‑3p, activated the 15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK pathway and promoted endothelial dysfunction, effects that were partially reversed by miR‑26a‑2‑3p mimics. In an L‑NAME‑induced PE mouse model, EPB41L4A‑AS1 overexpression exacerbated hypertension, proteinuria, placental apoptosis and oxidative stress, whereas miR‑26a‑2‑3p agomir administration attenuated these effects. Mechanistically, luciferase reporter assays revealed no direct binding between EPB41L4A‑AS1 and miR‑26a‑2‑3p, suggesting an indirect regulatory mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify EPB41L4A‑AS1 as a critical upstream regulator of the miR‑26a‑2‑3p/15‑LOX‑1/p38 MAPK axis in PE and suggest that targeting this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 in acute kidney injury and the acute kidney injury‑to‑chronic kidney disease transition: A key metabolic regulatory hub and potential therapeutic target (Review).
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and heterogeneous clinical syndrome characterised by a rapid decline in renal function and caused by a range of insults, including ischaemia‑reperfusion injury, sepsis, nephrotoxic drugs, hypovolaemia, major surgery and transplantation‑related injury. AKI is prone to progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and no effective treatment is currently available. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4), a regulator of mitochondrial metabolism, phosphorylates the E1α subunit of the pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) complex, thereby suppressing PDH enzymatic activity and limiting pyruvate oxidation. In renal tubular epithelial cells and other renal cell types, increased PDK4 mRNA expression and/or PDK4 protein abundance has been associated with enhanced inhibitory signalling through the PDK4‑PDH complex axis, typically reflected by increased phosphorylation of the PDH E1α subunit, reduced total PDH complex activity and suppressed mitochondrial pyruvate oxidation. These changes contribute to metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammatory activation and cell death. Accumulating evidence suggests that PDK4‑mediated metabolic dysregulation contributes to tubular injury and maladaptive repair during AKI and the AKI‑to‑CKD transition, although its effects remain dependent on disease context and biological stage. The present review summarises the molecular regulation of PDK4, its pathological relevance in experimental AKI and the potential implications of PDK4 for therapeutic intervention and biomarker development. Moreover, the limited evidence supporting PDK4 as a candidate biomarker in AKI and the AKI‑to‑CKD transition is discussed. Although PDK4 protein is biologically linked to tubular metabolic stress and renal injury, its clinical biomarker performance has not yet been validated and further studies are required to determine its diagnostic and prognostic utility.

articles.title: Kidney fibrosis mechanisms in the single‑cell era: From cellular heterogeneity to therapeutic opportunities (Review).
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease affects >13% of adults worldwide, yet no approved antifibrotic therapy is available. Recent advances in single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the understanding of renal fibrosis. These technologies have unmasked unexpected heterogeneity among myofibroblasts and macrophages, identified scar‑associated macrophage subsets and resolved the long‑standing debate over myofibroblast origins by confirming resident fibroblasts as the principal source. Spatial transcriptomics has further defined functional communities and pathologically distinct niches, including maladaptive repair niches centred on SOX9+ epithelial cells, profibrotic microenvironments enriched in tenascin‑C and immune‑activation niches where macrophages and fibroblasts co‑localize. Intercellular crosstalk networks involving TGF‑β, NOTCH and paracrine signals from injured tubules have been systematically mapped. These insights are now being translated into targeted strategies, such as surface marker‑directed agents against CD248 and fibroblast activation protein, epigenetic modulators including HDAC6 inhibitors and advanced 3D bioprinted human models. The present review synthesized these single‑cell and spatial discoveries to provide a conceptual framework for developing precision antifibrotic therapies for progressive kidney disease.

articles.title: A novel role of NOX2 in enhancing HBV replication through ROS‑mediated autophagy activation.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a serious global public health issue. Mounting evidence suggests that NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) plays critical roles in various physiological and pathological processes. However, the underlying mechanisms by which NOX2 affects HBV infection remain to be elucidated. In the present study, the potential role of NOX2 in HBV replication was investigated in cell models. First, it was demonstrated that NOX2 is highly expressed in transiently and stably HBV‑infected cells. Second, by employing inhibitor, RNA interference technique and plasmid overexpression, it was revealed that NOX2 plays an essential role in promoting HBV replication. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of how NOX2 affects HBV replication was illustrated. It was found that NOX2‑mediated ROS induce an increase of intracellular autophagy levels, which result in facilitating HBV replication. These results suggested a previously unrecognized role of NOX2 in HBV replication. Taken together, NOX2 may serve as a novel target for developing treatment strategies against HBV‑related disorders.

articles.title: Regulatory roles of microRNA‑145 in cardiovascular diseases (Review).
articles.abstract: MicroRNA‑145 (miR‑145) is a non‑coding RNA involved in vascular remodeling, myocardial injury and fibrosis, and it contributes to the onset and progression of several cardiovascular disorders. Accumulating evidence indicates that the functions of miR‑145 depend on cell subtypes and pathological microenvironments. miR‑145 exerts dual regulatory effects in atherosclerosis, myocardial ischemia‑reperfusion injury, hypertension, pulmonary arterial hypertension ventricular remodeling and heart failure. In some settings, for example in cardiomyocytes subjected to myocardial ischemia‑reperfusion injury (MIRI), miR‑145 can suppress disease progression and protect the myocardium and vasculature; conversely, it may trigger tissue injury and exacerbate disease in specific cell types and pathological setting; for example, in cardiac microvascular endothelial cells during MIRI. Abnormal expression of miR‑145 is associated with disease severity, risk stratification and the incidence of long‑term adverse cardiovascular events, suggesting its potential as a molecular biomarker for early screening, disease assessment and prognosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Unconjugated or unformulated miR is limited by poor in vivo stability, rapid degradation by ribonucleases and low cellular transfection efficiency. To address these limitations, three major delivery platforms, namely extracellular vesicles, viral vectors and nanoparticles, have been developed for targeted delivery of miR‑145 and these platforms differ in biosafety, delivery efficacy and modifiability. As research advances in nucleic acid‑based targeted therapeutics, several miR‑based agents have entered clinical trials, supporting the development of targeted interventions for CVDs. The present review examined the dual regulatory mechanisms, potential clinical applications and current delivery technologies of miR‑145 across CVDs. The translational progress and limitations of current miR therapeutics were reviewed, as well as unresolved controversies and unanswered scientific questions. The present work aimed to inform further mechanistic studies of miR‑145 and the research, development and clinical translation of cardiovascular nucleic acid‑targeted therapies.

articles.title: Site-specific timing and mode of detection of locoregional recurrence after breast cancer surgery.
articles.abstract: Locoregional recurrence after breast cancer surgery remains potentially curable; however, current guidelines recommend annual mammography (MMG) alone, and recommend against routine ultrasonography (US) or computed tomography (CT). Despite arising in different anatomic locations, intramammary and regional nodal recurrences are typically analyzed together. The present study aimed to examine when and how locoregional recurrence after surgical treatment was detected under a defined institutional surveillance protocol. Among 61 locoregional recurrences verified at Fukushima Medical University Hospital (Fukushima, Japan) between February 2016 and August 2025, 13 were excluded, leaving 48 patients, each of whom contributed one recurrence. The disease-free interval (DFI), mode of detection and examination that first identified the recurrence were extracted from medical records, and intramammary and regional nodal recurrences were compared. Among the 48 recurrences, 32 were intramammary, 13 involved regional lymph nodes and 3 involved the skin/soft tissue. The median DFI was 156 months for intramammary recurrences and 42 months for regional nodal recurrences (P=0.0009), with 59.4% compared with 15.4% of recurrences being diagnosed >10 years after primary surgery. Overall, US was the most frequent detection modality (47.9%), followed by MMG (18.8%), CT (12.5%), positron emission tomography (PET)-CT (10.4%) and palpation (10.4%). Among intramammary recurrences, 75.0% were detected by US or MMG whereas 9.4% were detected by CT or PET-CT. By contrast, among regional nodal recurrences, 46.2% were detected by CT or PET-CT (P=0.0106). Tumor size at detection did not differ between the recurrence sites. In conclusion, in the present single-center series, intramammary and regional nodal recurrences demonstrated distinct patterns of timing and detection modality. Because the number of examinations performed was unavailable, the findings characterize detection patterns rather than the diagnostic performance of individual examinations. Further validation in larger, multicenter studies is warranted.

articles.title: New-onset depersonalization-derealization syndrome following semaglutide therapy.
articles.abstract: Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, acts on central neuropsychiatric pathways beyond its metabolic effects, yet dissociative adverse effects have rarely been reported. We describe a 42-year-old woman with no psychiatric history who developed recurrent, distressing episodes of depersonalization and derealization approximately 7 days after her second 0.5 mg weekly dose of semaglutide prescribed for obesity. The episodes progressed from once daily to 3 to 4 times daily over 10 days, with insight and reality testing preserved throughout. Metabolic, neurological, toxicological, and psychiatric evaluations, including brain imaging, electroencephalography, and laboratory studies, excluded alternative causes. She fulfilled the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition criteria for depersonalization-derealization disorder, and the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score of 6 indicated a probable causal relationship. Semaglutide was discontinued without psychotropic medication, and symptoms resolved completely within 4 weeks, with sustained remission at 3 months. This case suggests that depersonalization-derealization is an underrecognized, reversible neuropsychiatric adverse effect of semaglutide and underscores the need for clinician awareness and patient counseling during therapy.

articles.title: Intestinal ischemia in 2 pediatric patients with new-onset diabetes with mixed ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar state.
articles.abstract: We report 2 pediatric patients-a 4-year-old male (case 1) and a 10-month-old male (case 2)-who presented in mixed diabetic ketoacidosis/hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state in the setting of new-onset diabetes, complicated by intestinal ischemia requiring bowel resection. Case 1 developed nonocclusive mesenteric ischemia requiring ileal resection, and case 2 developed thrombotic mesenteric ischemia requiring subtotal colectomy and small bowel resection, resulting in short bowel syndrome. These cases illustrate intestinal ischemia as a potential complication of pediatric hyperglycemic emergencies, underscoring the importance of prompt surgical evaluation when abdominal findings worsen despite appropriate metabolic resuscitation.

articles.title: Occult virilization: an elusive ovarian steroid cell tumor.
articles.abstract: Rapidly progressive hirsutism or virilization in a postmenopausal woman should prompt evaluation for pathological androgen excess, most commonly arising from an adrenal or ovarian tumor. We report a case of a 58-year-old postmenopausal woman with rapidly progressive severe hirsutism and virilization over 4 months. Examination revealed clitoromegaly, voice deepening, and coarse facial hair growth. Biochemistry demonstrated markedly elevated androgen levels with only slightly elevated dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate, supporting an ovarian source. Ultrasonography, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging were inconclusive because a large fibroid uterus obscured the adnexa. Subsequent fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT (18F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated a metabolically active right adnexal lesion. The patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Histopathology confirmed an ovarian steroid cell tumor, not otherwise specified (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics, FIGO stage IA). Postoperatively, androgen levels normalized with improvement of virilizing features. This case highlights the potential value of 18F-FDG PET/CT as a selective problem-solving imaging tool for localizing occult androgen-secreting ovarian tumors when conventional imaging is inconclusive.

articles.title: Transient hypoparathyroidism and symptomatic hypocalcemia complicating babesiosis.
articles.abstract: Babesiosis, caused by Babesia microti, is a tick-borne intraerythrocytic infection with diverse manifestations, but endocrine complications are rarely reported. We describe a 60-year-old man who presented with fever, chills, and cognitive symptoms and was diagnosed with babesiosis by peripheral smear, serology, and polymerase chain reaction. Despite improvement with atovaquone and azithromycin, he developed confusion, paresthesia, and fatigue, prompting further investigation. Laboratory testing revealed hypocalcemia (total calcium, 6.8 mg/dL [SI: 1.7 mmol/L]; reference range, 8.4-10.4 mg/dL [SI: 2.10-2.60 mmol/L]); ionized calcium, 3.8 mg/dL (SI: 0.95 mmol/L; reference range, 4.7-5.5 mg/dL [SI: 1.17-1.37 mmol/L]), a low parathyroid hormone concentration of 9 pg/mL (SI: 9 ng/L; reference range, 18-88 pg/mL [SI: 1.9-9.3 pmol/L]), and hyperphosphatemia, with phosphate concentration of 5.7 mg/dL (SI: 1.84 mmol/L; reference range, 2.5-4.5 mg/dL [SI: 0.81-1.45 mmol/L]), consistent with hypoparathyroidism, with normal magnesium and vitamin D levels. Other etiologies were excluded. He was treated with intravenous calcium followed by oral calcium and calcitriol, resulting in symptomatic and biochemical improvement. Serial monitoring demonstrated gradual recovery of parathyroid function, allowing discontinuation of calcitriol. At follow-up, calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone normalized, and symptoms resolved. This case describes transient hypoparathyroidism associated with babesiosis, with possible cytokine- or immune-mediated mechanisms.

articles.title: Systematic review of rodent studies on deep brain stimulation targeting the striatum.
articles.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders. Among the most investigated targets are striatal regions, which play central roles in cortico-striatal circuits involved in motivation, emotion, and cognition. However, evidence from rodent studies remains fragmented across target regions, behavioral domains, and stimulation protocols. We systematically reviewed preclinical studies investigating the behavioral effects of striatal DBS in rodents, focusing on anatomical targets, stimulation parameters, and behavioral outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed and Scopus were searched. Experimental studies evaluating striatal electrical DBS in rats or mice with behavioral outcomes were included. Data were extracted on animal characteristics, targeted striatal subregions, stimulation parameters, behavioral assessments, and main findings. Sixty-eight articles met the inclusion criteria. Most targeted the nucleus accumbens, particularly the shell and core, whereas the dorsal and mid striatum were comparatively underrepresented. Behavioral assessments were grouped into seven functional categories, with positive valence, negative valence systems and motor and locomotor activity being the most frequently investigated. Across studies, reported behavioral effects varied according to the stimulated subregion, behavioral paradigm, baseline state, disease model, and stimulation protocol. Qualitative patterns suggested that DBS often attenuated experimentally disrupted behavior, although substantial methodological heterogeneity limited direct comparisons. Overall, the evidence suggests that the behavioral effects of striatal DBS are context-dependent, reflecting the functional specificity of distinct striatal subregions. Future studies incorporating precise targeting, systematic parameter comparisons, adaptive stimulation approaches, and greater consideration of biological sex will strengthen the translational value of rodent DBS research.

articles.title: Nicotine Dependence as a Risk Factor for Complications After Flexor Tendon Repair: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The effects of nicotine on outcomes following flexor tendon repair remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the association between nicotine dependence and the incidence of complications following flexor tendon repair.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, the TriNetX database was queried to identify patients older than 18 years who underwent flexor tendon repair. Patients were categorized into two cohorts based on the presence of preoperative nicotine dependence and further stratified based on tobacco versus nontobacco nicotine dependence. The cohorts were propensity matched based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, and presence of diabetes mellitus. Medical complications were assessed at 90 days, and procedural complications were assessed at 90 days and 2 years.

RESULTS: A total of 20,239 patients undergoing flexor tendon repair were identified, of which 5,645 had a documented history of nicotine dependence. After 1:1 propensity score matching, both cohorts included 5,586 patients. At 90 days, the nicotine-dependent group had statistically significant higher rates of acute kidney injury, adhesion-related complications, emergency department visits, and rehospitalization. At 2 years, nicotine dependence was associated with higher rates of wound infection and lower rates of joint contracture. No statistically significant differences were seen in swan-neck deformity, triggering, or rerupture. Nontobacco nicotine dependence patients had lower rates of adhesion-related complications and higher rates of rerupture than tobacco-dependent patients at both 90 days and 2 years; joint contracture was higher at 90 days but did not differ statistically significant at 2 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Nicotine dependence is independently associated with an increased risk of both early and delayed postoperative complications.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic III.

articles.title: Pediatric intensive care resources in Ibero-Latin America: SPREAD PED Ibero-Latin America, a multinational, multicentre, cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are a cornerstone of child survival, yet their structure, staffing, and adherence to evidence-based protocols vary widely across regions. Comprehensive and contemporary data from Ibero-Latin America are lacking. We aimed to characterize the organization, human resources, and implementation of standardized care practices in PICUs across this region.

METHODS: We conducted an international, multicentre, cross-sectional study including all PICUs admitting patients during a five-day period (Sept 2024) across 21 countries in Latin America, Spain, and Portugal. Unit-level data were obtained through a standardized electronic survey describing hospital characteristics, workforce distribution, monitoring capabilities, and clinical protocols. The primary objective was to characterize the distribution of structural and organizational features of participating PICUs across the región; secondary outcomes examined multidisciplinary coverage and adherence to standardized care practices.

FINDINGS: Among 339 PICUs (70.6% public; 61.4% university-affiliated), nearly half had fewer than ten beds. Median physician-to-patient ratio was 1:5-6 by day and 1:8-10 overnight. Nursing ratios varied widely, most favourable in the Iberian region (≈1:1-2) and least in the Andean block (≈1:3-4), underscoring inequities in bedside care capacity. Only 68% of units had dedicated physiotherapists, with far lower coverage from nutritionists, psychologists, or pharmacists. Basic monitoring and ventilation were nearly universal (>95%), yet advanced technologies-cardiac output, near-infrared spectroscopy, renal replacement therapy-were available in fewer than 40% of centers. Structured protocols for sepsis, mechanical ventilation, sedation, or antimicrobial stewardship were reported in only 56% of PICUs, with adherence highest in the Iberian and lowest in the Andean and Caribbean regions.

INTERPRETATION: This multinational, multicentre assessment provides the first comprehensive and contemporary map of pediatric critical care capacity across Ibero-Latin America, revealing major disparities in infrastructure, human resources, and protocol implementation. Strengthening human capital, multidisciplinary training, and regionally adapted strategies is essential to achieve equitable, high-quality critical care for children across the region.

FUNDING: This work was supported by institutional funding from the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo (FAPESP; Grant No. 2017/21052-0), provided to the Latin American Sepsis Institute (ILAS) to support the conduct of the study, including research assistant and statistical support.

articles.title: Hypoglossal-facial nerve anastomosis for facial nerve injury after vestibular schwannoma surgery: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Facial nerve injury is one of the most common and distressing complications following vestibular schwannoma (VS) surgery. Hypoglossal-facial nerve anastomosis (HFA) is a nerve repair technique used in patients with facial nerve injury. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the techniques, outcomes, and complications of HFA for facial nerve injury following VS resection.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Herdin databases was conducted from inception to September 2025. Studies were included if they reported HFA for facial nerve injury after VS surgery. Data on patient demographics, interval between injury and HFA, surgical techniques, outcomes, complications, and follow-up duration were obtained. A meta-analysis of comparative studies was performed using RevMan software.

RESULTS: Forty-eight studies comprising 866 VS patients were included. The mean age ranged from 35.4 to 56.3 years. The most frequently reported HFA technique was end-to-end, followed by side-to-end, hemihypoglossal-facial anastomosis, and dual nerve transfer (HFA + masseter-facial anastomosis). 91.0% of patients demonstrated improvement in facial function; 46.4% achieved House-Brackmann grade III or better. Meta-analysis conducted on four studies showed significantly greater odds of favorable outcome after HFA versus conservative treatment (OR 6.42, 95% CI 1.74-23.65; p = 0.005). Complications included tongue hemiatrophy (22.5%), eating difficulty (17.0%), synkinesis (14.1%), and speech disarticulation (8.3%).

CONCLUSION: Our review showed that HFA improved the facial nerve function of patients with facial nerve injury after resection of VS, but this procedure carried a notable risk of complications, particularly tongue hemiatrophy.

articles.title: Metacarpophalangeal Joint Arthroplasty in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Outcomes and Challenges.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metacarpophalangeal joint (MCP) arthroplasty is a surgical intervention for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and deformities unresponsive to nonsurgical treatments. This study aims to assess the functional outcomes and complication profile of MCP arthroplasty in patients with SLE.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted of patients with SLE who underwent MCP arthroplasty between 2003 and 2019. Clinical data, including demographics, operative indications, complications, and outcomes, were reviewed. Follow-up data were collected through chart reviews and phone interviews. Patient-reported outcome measures, obtained during telephone follow-up, included pain assessed using the visual analog scale, upper-extremity function using the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand, and hand appearance satisfaction using the HandQ questionnaire.

RESULTS: Thirteen patients with SLE (mean age, 61.92 years) underwent 55 MCP arthroplasties. The main indications for surgery were pain and deformity refractory to nonsurgical treatment. The median follow-up duration was 89.15 months (range, 6.1-259.3 months). After surgery, seven patients had extended follow-up. Complications included eight prosthesis fractures, one infection, and five recurrent deformities. Pain relief was modest (visual analog scale, 2.7/10), functional outcomes were moderate (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand 47.4), and hand appearance satisfaction was low (HandQ 31/100).

CONCLUSIONS: MCP arthroplasty in patients with SLE provides moderate, long-term functional improvement and pain relief. However, patient satisfaction with hand appearance remains low. Given the small cohort size and SLE's heterogeneity, further research is needed to optimize long-term outcomes.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE/TYPE OF STUDY: Therapeutic IV, Retrospective Case Series.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Guided Versus Blind Corticosteroid Injection for Trigger Finger: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Trigger finger is the most common functional hand condition, affecting 3% of the general population and up to 17% of patients with diabetes. Corticosteroid injection is first-line treatment after failed conservative management and may be administered blindly or under ultrasound guidance (USG); however, the comparative clinical benefit of USG remains unclear.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from inception to April 23, 2026, with an updated search through August 20, 2026, per PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies reporting outcomes following USG or blind corticosteroid injection for trigger finger were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomized trials and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series for single-arm observational studies. This review was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261378220). Because of substantial heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria, published between 2009 and 2026, encompassing 226 patients across the three studies reporting patient-level data and 223 fingers/digits across the three studies reporting digit-level data; these denominators are not directly summable given their differing units, with a female predominance and a mean age of 45-55 years. Ultrasound-guided injection was associated with faster early symptom resolution and lower visual analog scale/QuickDASH (Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand) scores in one study (P < .05 at 1-4 weeks), with this advantage attenuating by 12-24 weeks. The higher-quality randomized controlled trial demonstrated no significant difference in resolution rates between USG and blind injection (91% vs 83%, P > .05), a finding not consistently confirmed across comparative studies. Recurrence and surgical conversion findings were similarly inconsistent, and safety profiles were comparable between techniques, with no infections or tendon ruptures reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided corticosteroid injection may offer modest early symptomatic benefit over blind injection in the treatment of trigger finger, but current evidence is limited by substantial risk of bias and does not support its routine use over blind injection as first-line therapy.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic IV.

articles.title: The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee 2026 guidelines for initial management of minimal, mild and moderate head injuries in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis and modified Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several clinical guidelines exist to identify intracranial injury (ICI) after head injury. The Scandinavian Neurotrauma Committee (SNC) published evidence- and consensus-based guidelines in 2000, updated in 2013.
