Random-forest imputation produced similar remission discrimination, whereas models discriminated MADRS response less well than remission. At a 25% threshold, the Base-LR_Simple and Dimensions-SuperLearner configurations yielded 6.0 (95% CI 1.8-10.0) and 7.1 (3.3-10.9) net true-positive decisions per 100 versus treat-all. In this internally validated cohort, richer and ensemble strategies did not demonstrate improved remission discrimination over the a priori three-variable reference model; these findings do not establish equivalence or transportability.

articles.title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia.

METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model.

LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples.

CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

articles.title: Mapping reproducible brain-based depression stratification across clinical, cognitive, and neurotransmitter dimensions.
articles.abstract: Identifying reproducible brain-based stratifications across independent cohorts is critical for parsing heterogeneity in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), yet robust profiles spanning micro- and macroscales remain poorly defined. We applied stability-based clustering to cortical thickness (CT) data from 1531 MDD individuals in UK Biobank (UKB), with replication in 144 inpatients from IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital (HSR). Two stable clusters emerged (normalized stability = 0.125) that generalized to a hold-out UKB sample with 96.5% accuracy (majority-cluster baseline = 59.5%). The clusters differed in widespread CT, largely reflected in global CT, with one showing cortical thinning, childhood trauma, and diabetes comorbidity. A two-cluster structure was independently replicated in HSR (normalized stability = 0.29), with a broadly similar cortical topography, although systematic CT differences between cohorts limited direct cross-cohort comparability. The clinical correlates identified in UKB did not replicate after correction for multiple comparisons. In UKB, mapping the CT differences between strata onto Neurosynth meta-analytic activation patterns revealed a ventral-dorsal gradient linked with emotion regulation, interoceptive, and motivational processes. Spatial correlations with 19 neurotransmitter receptors and transporters obtained from positron emission tomography identified the dopamine transporter as the dominant contributor in UKB, and the histamine H3 receptor in HSR. These findings provide a reproducible framework linking CT-based clusters in MDD to multiscale biological organization, although their clinical relevance warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Pharmacogenetics of inhaled corticosteroids in obesity-related childhood asthma.
articles.abstract: Asthma is a multifactorial disease driven by genetic and environmental factors that influence pathogenesis and therapeutic response. Obesity and asthma share overlapping inflammatory pathways that worsen disease severity and impair medication response. Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) are the cornerstone of long-term persistent asthma management, yet 25-30% of patients exhibit poor response. Genetic variants in the T , GLCCI1 , and CRHR1 genes have been associated with differential ICS response; however, whether obesity modifies these pharmacogenetic relationships remains unexplored. We conducted a candidate gene analysis in the Caucasian Childhood Asthma Management Program cohort to examine whether obesity status (BMI > 95 th percentile; obesity: n = 24, no obesity: n = 176) modifies pharmacogenetic associations with ICS response. The primary outcome was the 2-month change in forced expiratory volume in the first second percentage predicted (FEV1PP) following ICS treatment, evaluated for single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) rs6456042, rs37972, and rs242941. The overall cohort demonstrated a 5.7% improvement in FEV1PP ( P = 0.003). The no-obesity group showed a 6.6% increase ( P = 0.001), while the obesity group experienced a -6.2% change ( P = 0.26). Significant pharmacogenetic associations with ICS response were identified in the no-obesity group, whereas the obesity group exhibited attenuated or reversed effects for all three SNPs, most notably rs37972.These findings demonstrate for the first time that established pharmacogenetic associations with ICS response are differentially expressed by obesity status. Obesity acts as a pharmacogenetic modifier and likely represents a distinct asthma endotype with unique genetic determinants of ICS response. Endotype-based stratification incorporating obesity is a necessary step toward precision pharmacogenomics in asthma and warrants dedicated pharmacogenomic investigation.

articles.title: Anp32e mediates histone variant H2A.Z-regulated TGF-β1 involvement in renal interstitial fibrosis.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF), a key pathological feature of chronic kidney disease, often leads to end-stage renal failure. However, the mechanisms underlying RIF remain unclear, and effective targeted therapies are still lacking. Our prior research identified that acidic nuclear phosphorylated protein 32 E (Anp32e) aggravates RIF, though the mechanism was not fully clarified. Anp32e is known as a histone chaperone regulating the histone variant H2A.Z, yet the role of H2A.Z in RIF and its connection to Anp32e remain largely unexplored. In this study, we observed elevated nuclear Anp32e in renal tubular epithelial cells in an RIF model. We further confirmed that Anp32e forms a protein complex with H2A.Z and showed that Anp32e may facilitates H2A.Z degradation via the proteasome pathway. Mechanistically, this degradation may reduce H2A.Z occupancy at the TGF-β1 promoter, leading to increased TGF-β1 expression and subsequent upregulation of fibrosis markers FN and Col-I. Collectively, our findings suggest that Anp32e may induces the degradation of H2A.Z via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, which contribute to increased transcriptional activity of TGF-β1 and subsequent promotion of RIF.

articles.title: Zinc silicate microspheres-mediated bacterial metabolic interference and microenvironment remodeling for chronic wound repair.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds have presented a significant clinical challenge due to persistent infection, uncontrolled inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Existing therapeutic platforms have failed to integrate these critical aspects into a single, cohesive strategy. To address this, a novel multifaceted agent, zinc silicate flower-like microsphere (ZnSi FMPs), was designed with controlled hierarchical architecture to achieve chronic wound repair by mediating bacterial metabolic interference and microenvironment remodeling. The unique nanosheet structure with sustained Zn2+ release endows ZnSi FMPs with favorable pH-independent antibacterial activity. This activity is mechanistically rooted in metabolic interference against Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), including disruption of ABC transporters and inhibition of the biosynthesis of essential amino acids (valine, leucine, isoleucine) and ribosomes. Concurrently, ZnSi FMPs can promote microenvironment remodeling by modulating inflammatory responses and angiogenesis, evidenced by suppressed inflammation mediated by the complement and coagulation cascades pathway and robust activation of the Areg/HB-EGF-mediated ErbB signaling pathway. Hence, in both S. aureus-infected and diabetic wound models (mice and minipigs), ZnSi FMPs exhibited superior chronic wound healing capacity compared with commercial silver sulfadiazine® (AgSD) and 45S5 bioglass®. This improved healing was achieved through enhanced antibacterial activity, anti-inflammatory effects, and angiogenesis, accompanied by elevated expression of CD163, CD206, CD31 and α-SMA. By synergizing bacterial metabolic interference with microenvironment regulation, ZnSi FMPs effectively facilitate tissue healing and provide a promising candidate for clinical wound treatment.

articles.title: Continuity and Discontinuity in Artefact Distributions from Multi-Period Archaeological Sites.
articles.journal: Journal of archaeological method and theory
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Artefact finds recovered by metal detecting and reported by members of the public are a growing source of archaeological information, with over 1.2 million finds recorded to date by the Portable Antiquities Scheme in England and Wales. Heritage schemes in many other European countries where hobby detecting for archaeology is legal likewise report growing numbers of finds. Using point pattern analysis, this paper presents a worked-out set of computational methods to study diachronic processes within artefact assemblages at field or local (e.g. parish) levels. We present a simulated 'toy' example to illustrate the methodology and test it with two large artefact assemblages from the counties of North Yorkshire and Norfolk that differ in terms of finds record quality and known contextual archaeological landscape information. The proposed approach and example code can be reapplied to other archaeological point patterns. It formalises a spatial statistical workflow that produces an assessment regarding landscape persistence and reuse, and which can be used, for example, to assist fieldwork or planning decisions by identifying areas for further research. The case studies highlight the considerable need for formal analytical workflows in public finds research, which can be easily deployed at different sites and local assemblages. Moreover, while the proposed workflow has been designed with public finds scatters in mind, it is scale-agnostic and can be reapplied to investigate a range of archaeological phenomena from monument distributions across a larger region to investigating artefact scatters within an excavated area.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10816-026-09821-0.

articles.title: Impact of Non-Tobacco Nicotine Products on Postoperative Outcomes in Soft Tissue Hand Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Use of non-tobacco nicotine products (NTNP), including e-cigarettes, nicotine pouches, and oral nicotine devices, has risen sharply, yet their impact on postoperative outcomes across elective soft tissue hand surgeries remains poorly defined. Although nicotine from combustible tobacco impairs wound healing, whether NTNP exposure confers similar risk is unknown. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the association between preoperative NTNP use and postoperative complication rates following elective soft tissue hand surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network identified adults (≥18 years) undergoing elective soft tissue hand surgery from 2004 to 2024. Patients with non-tobacco-specified nicotine dependence diagnoses documented within 1 year before surgery were compared with patients without any documented nicotine dependence. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed based on demographics and comorbidities. Postoperative complications at 1, 3, and 6 months included deep, superficial, and unspecified surgical site infection, wound dehiscence, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism. Odds ratios with 95 percent confidence intervals were calculated, with P < .05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: After matching, 36,811 patients were included per cohort. NTNP use was associated with significantly increased rates of unspecified surgical site infection, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and wound dehiscence at all assessed postoperative time points. Deep and superficial surgical site infection rates did not differ significantly. Effect sizes were consistent across all intervals.

CONCLUSIONS: NTNP use within 1 year is independently associated with higher risks of wound dehiscence, thromboembolic events, and unspecified postoperative infection after soft tissue hand surgery. These findings suggest that nicotine exposure, regardless of delivery method, adversely affects postoperative healing and should be addressed through preoperative screening and cessation counseling.

TYPE OF STUDY/LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Retrospective cohort study III.

articles.title: Gas signaling molecule: a new research focus in the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Gas signaling molecules, including nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide, have recently gained attention in erectile dysfunction treatment research because of their roles in regulating blood vessel function, reducing oxidative stress, and protecting nerves and other cells. This article reviews how nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide are involved in the development of erectile dysfunction and their potential as treatments. The review focuses on how these gases improve blood vessel function, relax smooth muscles, repair nerve function, and reduce tissue scarring. Current research shows that methods of gas delivery, especially those using nanocarriers or prodrugs, greatly increase how well these gases are absorbed and where they act in the body. Early animal studies and initial clinical trials support the effectiveness of these gasotransmitters in treating various causes of erectile dysfunction, including diabetes, aging, and nerve damage. Although challenges remain in controlling the speed of delivery, determining the appropriate dosage, and tailoring treatment to individual patients, there is reason for optimism. The development of responsive delivery systems, combinations of multiple gases, and additional therapies for difficult cases suggests that gas signaling molecules could transform erectile dysfunction treatment.

articles.title: Molecular crosstalk between gas transmitters and catecholamine biosynthesis pathways: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Catecholamines, particularly the hormone and neurotransmitter epinephrine, are important regulators of blood pressure and cardiovascular function. The expression of genes encoding catecholamine biosynthetic enzymes is subject to strict transcriptional regulation through both hormonal and neuronal mechanisms. These genes are also regulated by hypoxia and reactive oxygen species. A class of small gaseous transmitters, known as gas transmitters, serve as potent regulators of blood pressure and hypoxic signaling; however, their roles in catecholamine biosynthesis remain poorly understood. This manuscript reviews the current state of catecholamine and gas transmitter research, particularly their interactions in relation to hypertension. Current evidence shows that the gas transmitters nitric oxide, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen sulfide modulate catecholamine biosynthesis and release through both shared and distinct mechanisms. This regulation is highly dependent on concentration, cellular context, and mode of delivery. Additionally, this review explores hypoxic signaling as a link between catecholamines and gas transmitters. Together, these findings highlight a complex and context-dependent regulatory signaling between gas transmitters and catecholamines. Further mechanistic studies investigating endogenous signaling are required to elucidate these interactions and their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

articles.title: Rectal ozone insufflation modulates gut microbiota: improving lung function in mice with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: Ozone rectal insufflation possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects and is used for the treatment and prevention of diseases. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ozone rectal insufflation on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and explore the potential underlying mechanisms from the perspective of gut microbiology. A mouse chronic obstructive pulmonary disease model was established by intratracheal spraying of lipopolysaccharide and elastase. Mice received ozone rectal insufflation intervention following modeling. We found that ozone rectal insufflation improved pulmonary function, alleviated emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis, and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. Additionally, ozone rectal insufflation modulated the pathogenic-to-beneficial gut bacteria ratio in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice. The treatment also led to an upregulation of short-chain fatty acids. The fecal microbiota transplantation results further confirmed that the gut microbiota of ozone rectal insufflation-treated mice was sufficient to attenuate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease symptoms. In summary, our findings indicate that ozone rectal insufflation enhances lung function and reduces inflammation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease mice by modulating the gut microbiota and its associated metabolites.

articles.title: Hydrogen-rich water combined with traditional Chinese medicine compound in the treatment of kidney stones: a randomized controlled prospective clinical trial.
articles.abstract: The formation and development of kidney stones are related to abnormal urine metabolism, oxidative stress and inflammation. Hydrogen-rich water has clear efficacy in antioxidant and improving inflammatory status, while Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula is a clinically effective traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation for treating kidney stones. This randomized controlled prospective clinical trial from July 2025 to March 2026 at the Seventh People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine examined the effect of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula on kidney stones. The included 100 patients with kidney stones were randomly divided into blank, hydrogen-rich water, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine, and Chinese medicines groups. The patients received drinking hydrogen-rich water and/or Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula daily for 12 weeks. All subjects received basic treatment following the guidelines. Imaging examination, urine metabolism testing, renal function, inflammation and oxidative stress index, blood routine and liver function are used to detect the efficacy and safety of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. Results showed that the total effective rate of kidney stone treatment in blank group, Chinese medicines group, hydrogen-rich water and Chinese medicine group and hydrogen-rich water group was 28%, 76%, 80% and 32%. The Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula can partially alleviate the oxidative stress, uric acid metabolism and urinary magnesium levels of patients with kidney stone and improve the function of renal tubules. The hydrogen-rich water therapy showed only efficacy in improving glutathione reductase but the combination of hydrogen-rich water and Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula has shown superior efficacy in improving oxidative stress and related metabolic factors of blood uric acid and urine stones, as well as in renal tubular function. The results indicate that the addition of hydrogen-rich water can improve urinary metabolism and oxidative stress status in the treatment of kidney stones with Ye-Shi-Shi-Lin-Formula. The study was registered at the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No. ITMCTR2025001446).

articles.title: Ambient particulate matter pollution and stroke burden.
articles.abstract: As a major component of air pollution, ambient particulate matter pollution has rarely been studied with respect to its global stroke burden. This study aims to evaluate the global stroke incidence, mortality, and health inequalities related to ambient particulate matter pollution from 1990 to 2021. Utilizing the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021, we analyzed global stroke-related mortality, disability-adjusted life years, and their age-standardized rates. The estimated annual percentage change was calculated using a linear regression model. Health inequalities were measured using the concentration index and slope index of inequality. Between 1990 and 2021, global ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke deaths and disability-adjusted life years increased by 107% and 101% respectively, yet age-standardized rates declined. China experienced the largest increases in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, Vietnam had the fastest rise in age-standardized mortality rates, the Russian Federation saw the steepest declines in deaths and disability-adjusted life years, and Estonia had the most rapid drop in age-standardized mortality rate. Middle socio-demographic index locations accounted for 46% of the global stroke burden, with age-standardized mortality rates and age-standardized disability-adjusted life years surpassing those in high socio-demographic index locations. From 1990 to 2021, age-standardized disability-adjusted life years rose in low-middle socio-demographic index locations but fell in high socio-demographic index locations. While the concentration index signaled an improvement in global inequality, the slope index of inequality in 2021 worsened compared with that in 1990. Between 1990 and 2021, the global burden of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke declined. However, substantial disparities persisted across different regions, sexes, and nations. For ongoing and future research efforts, priority should be given to high-risk populations and regions, while also developing innovative interventions to further reduce the incidence of ambient particulate matter pollution-related stroke and enhance patient outcomes.

articles.title: Microbeamformer-aware layout optimization of a 2D intracardiac echocardiography array for grating-lobe suppression.
articles.abstract: Three-dimensional intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) has emerged as a promising imaging modality for interventional cardiology. However, catheter-based 2D ICE probes are subject to strict vascular-access constraints, which limit the transducer aperture and independent channel count, leading to spatial undersampling and pronounced grating-lobe (GL) artifacts. This work investigates microbeamformer-aware array-layout optimization for GL suppression in 2D ICE arrays. Using a hybrid analog-digital microbeamformer architecture, the proposed design maps 768 array elements to 64 system channels while retaining the intended transmit focus. Under manufacturable kerf constraints, simulated annealing is used to optimize the element spacing along the elevational direction. With a minimum kerf width of 0.015 mm, the maximum GL level at a focal distance of 50 mm and a common steering angle of θ=φ=45° is reduced from -16.04 dB to -20.97 dB, with the main-lobe full width at half maximum nearly unchanged. Along the evaluated common-angle steering path, θ=φ=0°-45°, the GL reduction increases from 3.15 to 4.93 dB and is accompanied by a 5.60-6.90 dB increase in the maximum near-focus sidelobe level. Numerical phantom imaging simulations further demonstrate reduced GL-related artifacts, with the artifact-to-background contrast ratio decreased by up to 6.98 dB. As an exploratory, layout-preserving alternative to kerf optimization, nonuniform subaperture grouping reduces the maximum GL by 4.07 dB at θ=φ=45° without changing the physical element positions. These results demonstrate the potential of microbeamformer-aware layout optimization for balancing channel reduction, structured GL suppression, and fabrication constraints in miniaturized 2D ICE arrays.

articles.title: Breathing in harm: current insights into the effects of air pollution on cardiorespiratory health.
articles.abstract: Air pollution significantly contributes to cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This review critically examines the mechanisms linking air pollution to higher cardiometabolic risk and cardiovascular death. It examines the impact of air pollution on respiratory health, specifically its role in exacerbating conditions such as heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and asthma. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including pregnant individuals, neonates, children, and patients with pre-existing cardiovascular or respiratory conditions, who are particularly susceptible and experience more severe health effects. Emerging evidence regarding the interactions between air pollution and coronavirus disease 2019 is also presented, showing how reductions in pollution levels during pandemic lockdowns were associated with improved cardiopulmonary health. Furthermore, the review discusses international differences in air quality standards and recent updates to exposure limits for air pollutants, as well as their implications for public health. It evaluates various mitigation strategies, including policy interventions, technological solutions, and approaches to reduce risk-based exposure. Lastly, the review emphasizes the need for comprehensive, evidence-based frameworks to minimize exposure and prevent diseases associated with pollution. Strengthening air quality management is essential for reducing the global burden of cardiovascular and respiratory diseases.

articles.title: ROS-responsive H2S-releasing quaternized chitosan dental implant coating for improved soft tissue integration, antibacterial and immunomodulatory capacities.
articles.abstract: Early and stable soft tissue integration is a prerequisite for the long-term success of dental implants. Crucially, the formation of this biological seal is closely associated with bacterial invasion and the modulation of the local immune microenvironment. Herein, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive hydrogen sulfide (H2S)-releasing quaternized chitosan (QCS) coating on the transmucosal interface of Ti-6Al-4V implants, termed TC4/PQCS/H2S. This coating exhibited favorable biocompatibility, enhancing the adhesion of human gingival epithelial cells (HGECs) and human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs), and improving soft tissue compatibility. Additionally, the TC4/PQCS/H2S possessed potent antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, and oral anaerobic pathogens, with effective suppression of biofilm formation. Furthermore, the TC4/PQCS/H2S enhanced cellular antioxidant defense and activated the Nrf2 pathway. It also promoted macrophage polarization toward the pro-healing M2 phenotype, with the involvement of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway. Overall, this study presents an efficient surface modification strategy that integrates cell-adhesive, antibacterial, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory functions, demonstrating great potential for soft tissue integration.

articles.title: Synergistic antibacterial and osteogenic properties of micro-arc oxidation GO@Ag/SF composite coatings for the repair of infectious bone defects.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration of titanium-based implants remain major clinical challenges. Conventional drug-loaded coatings often fail to simultaneously achieve long-term antibacterial activity and the construction of an osteogenic microenvironment.

METHODS: In this study, a graphene oxide-supported silver nanoparticle/silk fibroin (GO@Ag/SF) composite coating was developed and modified via micro-arc oxidation. By precisely controlling the GO/AgNO3 volume ratio, the antibacterial and osteogenic performances of the coatings were systematically evaluated. A rat model of infectious bone defect was employed to verify the in vivo therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: The optimized GO@Ag-2/SF coating exhibited pH-responsive sustained Ag+ release, with cumulative release increasing from 0.23 μg/mL under physiological conditions to 0.69 μg/mL under acidic conditions over 672 h. Under NIR irradiation, the coating reached 59.8°C within 10 min and achieved potent antibacterial activity against S. aureus and E. coli, with inhibition rates up to 98.3 ± 1.2%. The GO@Ag-2/SF coating also promoted osteogenic differentiation by enhancing ALP activity, collagen secretion, calcium mineralization, and the expression of RUNX-2, ALP, COL-I, and OCN. In vivo, GO@Ag-2/SF reduced inflammatory infiltration and improved peri-implant bone regeneration, with increased BIC, BV/TV, and Tb.Th and reduced Tb.Sp. Moreover, pull-out testing demonstrated the highest bone-implant mechanical fixation in the GO@Ag-2/SF group, confirming enhanced functional osseointegration in the infected bone defect model.

CONCLUSION: Through the synergistic effects of its components, the GO@Ag/SF coating established a dynamic antibacterial-osteogenic balance, offering a promising strategy for the repair of infectious bone defects.

articles.title: Photothermal-magnetic dual-activated Janus dressing for microenvironment purification and wireless electrically triggered healing with reduced scar formation.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic scarring remains a major clinical challenge that impedes functional wound regeneration. Although electrical stimulation (ES) shows great promise in activating endogenous repair pathways and suppressing fibrosis, excessive exudate and bacterial infection in chronic wounds not only exacerbate inflammation but also disrupt interfacial electrical contact, thereby attenuating the efficacy of in situ-generated ES. To address this, we designed an electroactive and antibacterial Janus dressing that integrated active microenvironmental purification with wireless ES, ultimately inhibiting scar formation during wound healing. The dressing featured electroactive cotton gauze with asymmetric wettability, achieved via SiO2 and AgNPs@poly 5-hydroxytryptamine/polyethyleneimine (AgNPs@PHT/PEI) coatings to form a unidirectional fluidic gate. Enhanced by a near-infrared-driven mild photothermal effect, this design enabled rapid exudate pumping and evaporation while achieving > 99% antibacterial efficacy within 15 min. Leveraging electromagnetic induction, it delivered tunable wireless microcurrents (13.44-43.18 μA) that upregulated endogenous fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) secretion, which contributes to the downregulation of TGF-β1-driven myofibroblast activation, as evidenced by reduced α-SMA expression. This strategy achieved 99.37% closure of large infected full-thickness rat wounds, featuring highly ordered collagen remodeling. Collectively, this study presents an innovative platform for rapid healing and scar inhibition in chronic wounds, holding promise for broader applications in mitigating fibrotic disorders.

articles.title: A multifunctional DECM/PLMA hydrogel incorporated with engineered PRP-derived exosomes enabling PHD2 silencing for skin wound repair.
articles.abstract: Skin defect repair remains a formidable clinical challenge, characterized by persistent infection risk, compromised angiogenesis, and dysregulated inflammatory responses. Existing hydrogel-based wound dressings fail to simultaneously address structural integrity, antimicrobial efficacy, and spatiotemporal coordination of tissue regeneration. Here, we report the development of a multifunctional bioactive hydrogel system fabricated by integrating decellularized tendon extracellular matrix (DECM) with Poly-L-lysine Methacryloyl (PLMA), and further functionalized with engineered platelet-rich plasma exosomes (PRP-Exos) loaded with siRNA targeting prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2) via electroporation. The inherent cationic nature of PLMA confers robust, broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, while the sustained release of siRNA-PHD2-laden PRP-Exos achieves efficient PHD2 silencing, thereby stabilizing hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) and potentiating downstream pro-angiogenic signaling. Concurrently, bioactive cues released from the DECM-based matrix promote fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation and type I collagen biosynthesis, fostering a regeneration-permissive microenvironment. In both normal and diabetic murine full-thickness skin defect models, DEPL@E-SI significantly accelerated wound closure by promoting angiogenesis, inflammation resolution, and extracellular matrix remodeling. These findings establish DEPL@E-SI as a promising therapeutic platform with translational potential for skin tissue engineering and clinical wound management.

articles.title: Orally activatable membrane fusion-mitochondria hitchhiking on intestinal macrophages for targeted therapy of bacterial meningitis and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Targeting the formidable physiological barriers and neuronal damage refractory to conventional bactericidal agents for bacterial meningitis, we engineered an infection microenvironment-activatable membrane fusion-mitochondrial formulation (Mito@MFL-Glu). This formulation integrates endogenous macrophage hitchhiking, lysosomal exocytosis-driven cargo release, and in situ mitochondrial transplantation. Orally administered, its glucan shell is recognized by microfold cells, enabling macrophage-mediated transport across the blood-brain barrier and chemotactic accumulation at infectious foci. During macrophage uptake, stimulation of the Dectin-1 by the glucan shell sustains intracellular Ca2+ levels. Upon reaching the infectious lesion, the pro-inflammatory microenvironment induces macrophage polarization toward an M1 phenotype, which further elevates intracellular Ca2+ levels. The synergy of these two sequential Ca2+ concentration events cooperatively triggers TFEB-mediated lysosomal exocytosis, resulting in a cargo efflux efficiency of 43.3%. Elevated local reactive oxygen species (ROS) cleave the ROS-responsive linker, detaching the glucan shell and exposing the fusogenic lipid bilayer. This activated layer then directly fuses with damaged neuron and microglial membranes, delivering exogenous mitochondria into the cytosol while bypassing lysosomal degradation and achieving a transplantation efficiency exceeding 36% within 1 h, whereas naked mitochondria show much lower efficiency. Concurrently, the liberated cefotaxime eliminates pathogens, culminating in a synergistic and non-invasive oral closed-loop bactericidal and neuroreparative strategy in a murine meningitis model.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid-cerium nanocatalysts enable oxygenation-enhanced ROS neutralization and PET imaging-guided therapy for acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is driven by a vicious interplay among excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and persistent renal hypoxia, which collectively disrupt redox homeostasis and exacerbate tubular injury. However, current therapeutic strategies primarily provide supportive care and fail to simultaneously modulate these interconnected pathological stressors. Herein, we report a cerium-doped rosmarinic acid nanosystem (RA/Ce NPs) formed via self-polymerization that catalytically eliminates ROS while simultaneously generating oxygen to reprogram the pathological renal microenvironment. The ultrasmall RA/Ce NPs enable efficient chelator-free 89Zr radiolabeling for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Redox-switchable Ce3+/Ce4+ centers confer robust catalytic activity and ROS-responsive biodegradation, ensuring potent antioxidation with safe clearance. RA/Ce NPs suppress intracellular ROS, preserve mitochondrial membrane potential, and protect against oxidative injury in vitro. In rhabdomyolysis-induced AKI mice, PET imaging reveals pronounced renal accumulation, while treatment markedly alleviates tubular damage, oxidative stress and hypoxia, leading to restored renal function with excellent biocompatibility. This work presents a natural-product-derived catalytic nanoplatform integrating antioxidation, oxygenation, imaging and biodegradability, offering a promising strategy for precision therapy of AKI.

articles.title: Retrievable "sea-island" microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel devices: augmented oxygen transport and anti-fibrosis for sustaining islet survival.
articles.abstract: Islet encapsulation is a transformative strategy for type 1 diabetes (T1D) cellular therapy, enabling islet transplantation without lifelong immunosuppression. However, macroscale encapsulation faces prominent challenges: poor surgical retrieval, hypoxia, and foreign body response (FBR)-induced fibrosis, which severely compromise clinical translation. Herein, we develop a sea-island microstructured zwitterionic-silicone hydrogel device via copolymerization of siloxane monomer SiGMA, zwitterionic monomer carboxybetaine acrylamide (CBAA), and hydrogen-bonding monomer N-acryloyl glycinamide (NAGA). Notably, NAGA enhances hydrogel structural stability via strong H-bonds, reinforcing network and mechanical integrity to facilitate safe retrieval; importantly, NAGA's hydrogen bonding crosslinks allow the hydrogel device to be heat-sealed, preventing cell leakage and maintaining immunoisolation. The incorporation of SiGMA induces hydrophobic phase separation, generating silicone-rich polymer microdomains that enhance oxygen permeability to alleviate islet hypoxia, while zwitterionic CBAA significantly improves antifouling performance and mitigates fibrotic encapsulation by suppressing the host FBR. After 8 weeks of implantation in mice and beagle dogs, the device exhibits minimal fibrotic encapsulation and can be readily retrieved. Notably, even without pre-vascularization or immunosuppression, the transplanted islets in diabetic mice sustain normoglycemia for up to 400 days. These results demonstrate a robust retrievable encapsulation device that addresses key bottlenecks in islet transplantation, advancing its potential translation for T1D.

articles.title: A hierarchical, pH-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform for synergistic microenvironment reprogramming and attenuation of inflammatory periodontal bone loss.
articles.abstract: Conventional periodontitis therapies are limited by their inability to concurrently address the interconnected challenges of persistent bacterial infection, excessive oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. To overcome this, we developed an injectable, pH-responsive nanocomposite polypeptide hydrogel, PepGel@ZnO-PLP, through rational molecular interface engineering. The system is constructed by integrating poly-L-proline (PLP)-functionalized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-PLP) into a poly-L-glutamate containing polypeptide network (PepGel) via dynamic Zn2+-carboxylate coordination. This critical PLP interface ensures colloidal stability of ZnO nanoparticles and enables the formation of a homogeneous, pH-responsive release network. In the acidic periodontal microenvironment, the hydrogel exhibits potent antibacterial and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging activities. Furthermore, via PLP-enabled interfacial engineering, PepGel@ZnO-PLP reprograms inflammatory macrophage immunometabolism by driving a glycolytic-suppressed metabolic state that establishes metabolic homeostasis toward a reparative M2 phenotype, a process in which the PI3K-Akt pathway may be involved. In a murine periodontitis model, PepGel@ZnO-PLP adheres to periodontal defects, effectively disrupting the infection-inflammation cycle and leading to significant alveolar bone preservation. This work underscores the power of precise molecular-level design for holistically reprogramming the pathological microenvironment and offers a novel nanocomposite hydrogel for ameliorating inflammatory periodontal bone loss.

articles.title: Biomimetic stress granules replenish lysosomal repair to reinstate macrophage immunometabolic antibacterial programs.
articles.abstract: Severe intracellular bacterial infection can progressively compromise lysosomal defence in macrophages, yet the underlying repair bottleneck remains unclear. Here we identify a time-dependent exhaustion of stress granule (SG)-associated lysosomal repair during sustained infection: progressive depletion of core SG components, including G3BP1 and galectin-3 (Gal-3), undermines lysosomal membrane resealing, resulting in lysosomal deacidification and persistent cytosolic acidification. This pH imbalance suppresses glycolytic metabolism and blunts macrophage pro-inflammatory antibacterial programs, thereby enabling intracellular bacterial persistence. Since this exhausted repair module cannot be readily reconstituted by conventional pharmacological or genetic approaches, we engineer biomimetic stress granules (BSGs), Gal-3-functionalized nanodiscs cloaked in acid-responsive fusogen-expressing macrophage membrane vesicles (Gal3-NDs@EF-MNVs), to achieve sequential targeting and cytosolic delivery to damaged lysosomes. BSGs stabilize membrane lesions, suppress lysosomal leakage and restore lysosomal acidification, pH homeostasis and metabolic fitness, thereby recapitulating the 'plugging' behavior of native stress granules at sites of membrane injury. This work establishes biomimetic organelle repair as a general, materials-driven paradigm to restore innate immunity against intracellular infections - without escalating antibiotics or genetic manipulation.

articles.title: Exosomes in brain diseases: Mechanisms, advances, and perspectives.
articles.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains a major biological obstacle limiting the effective delivery of therapeutics for central nervous system (CNS) disorders. Although conventional drug delivery approaches have achieved continuous advances, their clinical translation is frequently restricted by limited brain penetration, insufficient target specificity, and systemic adverse effects. Exosomes, endogenous extracellular vesicles (EVs) involved in intercellular communication, have emerged as promising candidates for CNS therapeutic delivery owing to their favorable biocompatibility, relatively low immunogenicity, and potential ability to interact with biological barriers. In this review, we first summarize the structural characteristics of the BBB and the mechanisms underlying exosome-BBB interactions and transport. We then discuss current strategies for exosome isolation, characterization, and engineering, highlighting how these approaches influence therapeutic performance and translational feasibility. Subsequently, we analyze recent advances in exosome-based therapies for major CNS disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases, brain tumors, and ischemic stroke, with emphasis on how distinct pathological environments guide the design of exosome cargos, targeting strategies, and functional modifications. Finally, we discuss key challenges associated with clinical translation, including manufacturing standardization, pharmacokinetic evaluation, safety assessment, and regulatory considerations. This review provides a pathology-driven and engineering-guided perspective for understanding the rational design and future development of exosome-based therapeutics for CNS disorders.

articles.title: Deep Learning-driven synergistic engineering of PET hydrolase for post-consumer PET depolymerization.
articles.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) offers a promising route to mitigate the increasingly severe problem of plastic pollution. However, the development of highly efficient PET hydrolases capable of processing post-consumer PET remains a critical challenge. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) provide new opportunities to accelerate the enzyme engineering of PET hydrolases. Here, we report a systematic computational redesign of the PET hydrolase NI (ThcCut1-AICCG-H185N/F189I) using the deep-learning framework, EITLEM-Kinetics. By integrating mutation free-energy constraints with kinetic parameter prediction, the framework enables simultaneous optimization of catalytic activity and thermostability. A total of nine beneficial substitution sites were identified and experimentally validated that overcoming the activity-stability trade-off. Combinatorial iteration yielded an optimal variant, NI-E65K/H107Y/A2R/L33F (NI-KYRF), which exhibited an 80% and 90% increase in depolymerization activity toward Gf-PET film and one-step pretreated post-consumer PET (pc-PET powder), respectively, along with a 2.61 °C increase in melting temperature (T m). NI-KYRF displayed a specific activity of 665 μmolTPAeq h-1 mgenzyme -1, representing 2.0- and 1.48-fold improvements over representative high-performance PET hydrolases ICCG and TurboPETase. The depolymerization performance of NI-KYRF towards various post-consumer PET wastes and polyester plastics was significantly improved. At 70 °C, it achieved a 95.5% depolymerization conversion of pc-PET powder within 24 h, and for untreated post-consumer PET film, the conversion reached 80.1%, representing a 2.1-fold improvement in depolymerization efficiency over the parental NI. In addition, enhanced activity toward polyesters plastics, including PBAT and PBT, indicates an expanded substrate scope. Molecular dynamics simulations and structural analysis reveal that these mutations enhance enzyme performance through synergistic mechanisms. Overall, this study establishes a deep learning-guided computational design framework based on EITLEM-Kinetics and demonstrates its effectiveness and broad potential for engineering high-performance PET hydrolases.

articles.title: Disability accommodations in medical training: differences by disability type and sexual orientation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Access to reasonable accommodations is associated with improved well-being, performance, and retention among learners with disabilities; however, many medical students and residents with disabilities do not receive accommodations. Prior work suggests that learners with intersecting marginalized identities may face additional barriers; yet, limited research has examined how sexual orientation intersects with disability to shape accommodation access in medical education.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 2020-2022 Graduation Questionnaire (GQ) data from U.S. medical students who self-identified as having a disability. The primary outcome was self-reported receipt of disability accommodations. Students who did not receive accommodations reported whether accommodations were denied, not requested due to lack of perceived need, or not requested for other reasons. Sexual orientation was categorized as heterosexual or LGBQ+. Disability type was categorized as cognitive, motor/sensory, chronic health, or multiple disability types. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to examine differences in accommodation receipt and reasons for non-receipt by sexual orientation and disability type.

RESULTS: Among 3,662 medical students with disabilities (MSWD), 49.8% reported receiving accommodations. A lower proportion of LGBQ+ students reported receiving accommodations (46.1% vs 50.5%, p = 0.038) compared to their heterosexual peers. Accommodation receipt varied by disability type (p < 0.001). Across all disability categories, LGBQ+ students consistently reported lower accommodation receipt. Formal accommodation denial was uncommon (2.4%) but occurred more among LGBQ+ students. LGBQ+ students were also more likely to report reasons other than lack of perceived need for not requesting accommodations.

CONCLUSION: Less than half of MSWD reported receiving accommodations, with lower rates of accommodation receipt reported among LGBQ+ students, particularly those with multiple disability types. Findings suggest that barriers to accommodation access may begin before any formal disclosure and review processes, highlighting the need to address disclosure-related barriers and promote equitable, safe access for medical students with intersecting marginalized identities.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of blood pressure-lowering interventions in adults living with HIV: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is the most prevalent modifiable cardiovascular risk factor among adults living with HIV, and cardiovascular disease has displaced AIDS-defining illness as the leading cause of death in many settings. Although pharmacological, lifestyle, and health-system interventions have been implemented to improve blood pressure control, their comparative effectiveness remains unclear. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) compared and ranked interventions for blood pressure control among adults with HIV.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, WHO Global Index Medicus, WHO ICTRP, ClinicalTrials.gov, and supplementary sources was conducted from inception to 10 May 2026. Randomised controlled trials evaluating blood pressure-lowering strategies in adults living with HIV were eligible. Random-effects frequentist NMA was performed using the netmeta package in R. Primary outcomes were changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Interventions were grouped by the randomised contrast into pharmacological, lifestyle and care-delivery strategies, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE for network meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Database searches identified 3,958 records; 14 randomised controlled trials (13,204 participants, 10 countries) were included, of which nine (5,082 participants) contributed to the systolic blood pressure (SBP) network and four (2,613) to the diastolic blood pressure (DBP) network. Calcium channel blockers (CCB), evaluated in a single trial of 242 adults with prehypertension, reduced SBP compared with control (mean difference [MD] -5.89 mmHg; 95% CI -9.03 to -2.75; low certainty). Care-delivery strategies (six trials, 4,743 participants) reduced SBP (MD -1.51 mmHg; 95% CI -2.70 to -0.32; low certainty); the estimate for lifestyle interventions (two trials, 97 participants) was -4.44 mmHg (95% CI -9.64 to 0.75; very low certainty). All comparisons between active interventions were indirect, and CCB and lifestyle interventions did not differ (MD -1.45 mmHg; 95% CI -7.52 to 4.63). No intervention significantly reduced DBP, for which heterogeneity was considerable (I2 = 79%).

CONCLUSIONS: Randomised evidence on blood pressure-lowering interventions specific to people with HIV is limited. A single trial supports amlodipine in adults with prehypertension receiving dolutegravir-based therapy, and care-delivery strategies produce small but consistent reductions in systolic blood pressure. The data do not show that any intervention is superior to another; adequately powered trials of antihypertensive treatment in people with HIV and established hypertension, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa, are needed.

articles.title: Divergence between historical disease burden and future prevention opportunities in COPD and lung cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and tracheal, bronchus, and lung cancer (TBL) share modifiable risk factors, yet countries differ in historical disease burden and prevention gains.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to distinguish historical respiratory burden from future prevention opportunities.

METHODS: Using Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 (GBD 2021) estimates, we analyzed COPD-TBL burden attributable to smoking, secondhand smoke, ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5), and household air pollution in 204 countries and territories from 1990-2021. Historical burden was derived from COPD prevalence trajectories. Prevention gaps compared projected 2030 burden under national trends with a faster Sociodemographic Index (SDI)-matched peer benchmark. Mortality and welfare differences were estimated for 2022-2030; World Health Organization (WHO) and China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) data provided triangulation.

RESULTS: Historical validation favored the peer benchmark (log-scale mean absolute error 0.178 vs 0.220). Historical burden and prevention gap were weakly correlated after adjustment for SDI and current COPD prevalence (partial Pearson r = -0.253, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.385 to -0.113); 128 of 204 settings (62.7%) were discordant. Higher-historical-burden groups accounted for 79.9% of 2021 welfare losses from the leading risk, whereas higher-prevention-gap groups accounted for 97.4% of attainable 2022-2030 welfare gains. The trajectory difference was 0.98 million deaths, corresponding to US$597.6 billion. In CHARLS, greater chronic lung disease history was associated with subsequent hospitalization beyond current disease status (odds ratio 1.313, 95% CI 1.100-1.566).

CONCLUSIONS: Historical burden and prevention potential were misaligned in nearly two-thirds of settings. Both dimensions can guide respiratory health planning.

articles.title: Assessing the Roles of Two Community-Based Health Professionals in Japan: Public Health Nurses and Community Pharmacists.
articles.abstract: Community-based health professionals play important roles in public health systems but are often less visible than hospital-based providers. In Japan, the roles of public health nurses and community pharmacists have evolved in response to population aging and changing health system needs. We conducted a case study of these two professions. We drew on published literature, policy documents, and government statistics and examined their basic characteristics, historical development, and current work environments to assess their roles in community health systems in Japan. Public health nurses have traditionally focused on community-based prevention and health promotion, while community pharmacists have been oriented toward dispensing and medication management. In recent decades, both professions have experienced role expansion, with public health nurses taking on greater coordination and administrative responsibilities and community pharmacists increasingly expected to contribute to community-based care. However, both groups face challenges, including role ambiguity, workforce constraints, and limited recognition by other professionals and the public. Gaps also remain between policy expectations and practice, particularly in workload, professional positioning, and education. Strengthening Japan's community health system will require policy support and targeted investment in these two community-based health professions, especially for leadership development and interprofessional collaboration.

articles.title: C-peptide specific CD4 + T-cells, associated with T1D, respond to C-peptide presented by HLA-DQ8 and related HLA-DQ allomorphs.
articles.abstract: The HLA class II region is strongly associated with risk of developing type 1 diabetes (T1D). Within this region, the HLA alleles HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 are the strongest associated with risk of developing T1D. However, the relationship between HLA class allomorphs associated with T1D risk and their capacity to stimulate clinically relevant beta-cell antigen-specific CD4+ T-cell responses has not been investigated. Here, we analyzed the capacity of HLA-DQ8-restricted proinsulin C-peptide-specific TCRs to recognize C-peptide presented by other HLA allomorphs. Surprisingly, we found that HLA-DQ7 and HLA-DQ9, allomorphs closely related to HLA-DQ8 could present epitopes derived from proinsulin C-peptide to T-cell avatars expressing HLA-DQ8- restricted, C-peptide-specific TCRs. Despite small differences in amino acid sequence, HLA-DQ7 and -DQ9 are not associated with risk of T1D in Caucasians. In contrast, HLA-DQ8-restricted TCRs, which recognize a C-peptide-IAPP2 hybrid insulin peptide (HIP-6), responded strongly to HLA-DQ8+ APC, but did not respond when HIP-6 was presented by HLA-DQ7+ or HLA-DQ9+ APC. We conclude that CD4+ T-cell responses to C-peptide show remarkable promiscuity, being presented efficiently by antigen-presenting cells that express HLA allomorphs not typically associated with risk of developing T1D.

articles.title: Laxative treatment perturbs gut microbiome composition and metabolism in humans independent of short-term fiber consumption: a randomized controlled crossover intervention study.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal transit time is a major ecological determinant of the human gut microbiome, yet causal evidence that disentangles the effects of diet from those of the gut environment remains limited. Here, we conducted a randomized, controlled crossover trial in healthy adults (nine females, four males) consuming fully standardized high-fiber (40 g/d) or low-fiber (10 g/d) diets to assess how manipulating the gut environment using an osmotic laxative (Movicol) affects gut microbial composition and metabolism. Contrary to our hypothesis, laxative treatment did not affect the saccharolytic-to-proteolytic ratio. Yet, it induced a pronounced microbiome perturbation, explaining 16.3% of the variation in microbial community structure, compared with 1.7% explained by diet. The laxative treatment reduced the absolute abundance of several gram-positive commensals, including butyrate-producing taxa, while increasing gram-negative genera such as Bacteroides, Alistipes, and Phocaeicola. Our findings identify perturbations to the gut environment as a prominent short-term driver of human gut microbiome structure, independent of short-term fiber intake. Together, these results challenge a diet-centric view of microbiome modulation and raise concerns about potential detrimental effects on the gut microbiome in chronic use of gut environment-altering drugs such as macrogol-based laxatives.

articles.title: The gut‒kidney axis.
articles.abstract: Gut-kidney dialog is integral to the holobiont. This review explores the interactions between these two organ-systems across physicochemical, endocrine, immune, and metabolic levels. It is argued that the gut makes physiological concessions favoring the microbiota, which must be assured by the kidneys, extending the concept of renal homeostasis to holostasis. When considering pathological situations, three dimensions of the gut‒kidney axis are identified: (1) the gut causing kidney disease, (2) the effect of renal failure on the gut, and (3) the systemic effects of the gut in renal failure. Causal roles of the gut in enteric hyperoxaluria, IgA nephropathy and diabetic nephropathy are described. The impact of a uremic environment on the gut is discussed. Conversely the intestinal origins of uremic toxins and their impact on distant organs, including the kidneys themselves, are outlined. Special consideration is given to host-microbiota immune interactions, immunosuppressive therapy and kidney transplantation. Therapeutic interventions targeting the gut-kidney axis are appraised.

articles.title: Metabolic phenotypes and female reproductive impairment: cross-sectional associations with infertility and impaired fecundity.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The joint role of adiposity and metabolic dysfunction in female reproductive impairment remains uncertain. We examined cross-sectional associations of metabolic phenotypes with infertility and impaired fecundity in women of reproductive age.

METHODS: We analyzed 4,862 women from pooled 2011-2019 survey data. Normal weight was defined as BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2 and overweight/obesity as BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2. Metabolic unhealth was defined by the presence of at least one of three survey indicators: hypertension, diabetes/prediabetes, or dyslipidemia. Survey-weighted logistic regression, sensitivity analyzes, subgroup interaction tests, and restricted cubic spline models were used.

RESULTS: Among 4,862 women, 575 (11.8%) met the infertility outcome and 774 (15.9%) met the impaired-fecundity outcome. Relative to metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), fully adjusted odds ratios for infertility were 1.28 (95% CI 1.04-1.58) for MUNW, 1.32 (1.00-1.75) for MHO, and 1.43 (1.16-1.76) for MUO. For impaired fecundity, the corresponding estimates were 1.24 (0.95-1.60), 1.28 (1.00-1.65), and 1.40 (1.13-1.74). Exploratory subgroup analyzes did not support a robust age-specific interaction after multiplicity control, and spline analyzes provided mixed evidence for continuous adiposity measures.

CONCLUSIONS: The metabolically unhealthy overweight/obesity phenotype showed the most consistent association with infertility and impaired fecundity. These cross-sectional findings support an association between combined adiposity and metabolic abnormalities and reproductive impairment, but they do not establish causality and require confirmation in prospective studies.

articles.title: Antibiotic effects on gut-derived short chain fatty acid pools in healthy volunteers.
articles.abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are vital microbial metabolites that maintain gut health and immune function. Despite the established deleterious effect of antibiotics on anaerobic bacteria in the gut, the longitudinal effects of antibiotics on SCFA pool dynamics remain poorly characterized in humans. This study aimed to characterize depletion and recovery of linear and branched SCFAs and to explore microbial taxa associated with changes to SCFA pools after antibiotic exposure. This was a secondary analysis of a phase 1, randomized, nonblinded clinical trial in young healthy volunteers given a 10-day course of oral vancomycin, omadacycline, or moxifloxacin. Fecal samples were collected at baseline, during antibiotics, and follow-up visits for SCFA determinations and amplicon-based microbiome characterizations. Mixed effects models demonstrated that vancomycin produced global suppression of SCFAs pool relative to baseline, indicating broad suppression of microbial fermentation. Although all antibiotics reduced SCFA levels during treatment, vancomycin associated changes were most evident for branched SCFAs vs. comparators. Vancomycin shifted the fermentation balance by disproportionately suppressing linear SCFAs, reflected by a lower linear-to-branched SCFA ratio. In parallel, Clostridiales abundance declined most markedly after vancomycin, with more moderate reductions after omadacycline and moxifloxacin. Moxifloxacin and omadacycline but not vancomycin showed early recovery of butyrate-production capacity by qPCR. In this longitudinal analysis of healthy volunteers, vancomycin caused global suppression of microbial fermentation, with marked depletion of linear and branched SCFAs consistent with disproportionate suppression of fiber fermentation relative to amino acid fermentation.

articles.title: Youth perspectives on tuberculosis prevention in South Africa: A qualitative study in faith-based organisations.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading public health challenge in South Africa, with high rates of co-infection with HIV. Faith-based organisations (FBOs) have untapped potential to support TB prevention, particularly by engaging youth who are often overlooked. This study explored youth perspectives on TB prevention and FBOs' roles in advancing youth-led, culturally grounded health promotion strategies in Johannesburg, South Africa. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using five focus group discussions with youth aged 18-30 years from Christian, Muslim, and Rastafarian faith communities. The study was guided by principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and Human-Centered Design, applying the 'Define' and 'Develop' phases of the Double Diamond model. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants demonstrated a blend of biomedical knowledge and persistent TB myths. Youth identified FBOs as trusted yet underutilised platforms and proposed strategies including music, storytelling, drama, peer-led health clubs, and digital campaigns. They expressed readiness to lead within faith institutions but noted barriers, including resistance from traditional hierarchies and limited resources. Youth in faith communities possess the creativity, insight, and commitment to transform TB prevention efforts. Strengthening partnerships between youth and FBOs, and investing in participatory, faith-aligned health promotion models, could yield more equitable and sustainable public health outcomes in high-burden settings.

articles.title: Dietary cinnamon-Rumex nervosus phytobiotic supplementation modulates growth performance, oxidative status, lymphoid organ weights, and cecal histopathology in Eimeria tenella-challenged broilers.
articles.abstract: Eimeria tenella infection can adversely affect broiler growth performance, intestinal integrity, and antioxidant status. This study evaluated the effects of a Cinnamomum verum bark (CVB)-Rumex nervosus leaves (RNL) phytobiotic mixture on productive performance, clinical severity, oocyst shedding, oxidative status, and cecal integrity in Eimeria tenella-challenged broilers. One hundred fifty Ross 308 broilers were assigned to six treatments with five replicates of five birds: challenged untreated control (PC), unchallenged control (NC), toltrazuril (TOL), and CVB-RNL at 2:1, 4:3, or 6:5 g/kg diet. Birds were challenged with 2 × 104 sporulated Eimeria tenella oocysts on day 14 and evaluated until day 21. Growth performance, clinical signs, oocyst shedding, hepatic oxidative-status biomarkers, and cecal histopathology were assessed. Day-14 body weight was included as a covariate. CVB-RNL 2:1 improved post-challenge ADG, FCR, and EPEF by 8.2%, 6.7%, and 14.2%, respectively, versus PC, and over 0-21 d by 5.1%, 6.1%, and 13.0%, respectively (P < 0.05). Oocyst shedding was reduced by 69.0%, 70.1%, and 75.8% relative to PC with the 2:1, 4:3, and 6:5 formulations, respectively (P < 0.0001). Total clinical scores decreased from 15.4 in PC to 5.2, 5.9, and 3.6 in the 2:1, 4:3, and 6:5 groups, respectively (P < 0.001). Compared with PC, CVB-RNL 2:1 reduced malondialdehyde by 42.4% and increased glutathione and superoxide dismutase activity by 11.1% and 72.6%, respectively (P < 0.05). CVB-RNL, particularly the 2:1 formulation, demonstrated marked anticoccidial efficacy and favorable overall growth and oxidative-status responses.

articles.title: Association of postpartum glycemic control with serum MMP-9, ET-1, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between 12-month postpartum glycemic control and serum matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)/endothelin-1 (ET-1) levels, hypertension, and dyslipidemia in women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), and to explore statistical indirect effects involving these biomarkers.

METHODS: A total of 300 women with prior GDM followed up at 12 months postpartum were included. HbA1c, MMP-9, ET-1, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were assessed at the same follow-up visit. Participants were stratified into good (n = 141) and poor (n = 159) glycemic control groups based on a glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) cutoff of 5.7%. General characteristics, vascular biomarker levels, and the prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia were compared between the groups. Correlation and logistic regression analyzes were performed, followed by exploratory regression-based indirect-effect analyzes involving MMP-9 and ET-1.

RESULTS: The poor control group had significantly higher levels of MMP-9 and ET-1. HbA1c was positively correlated with both biomarkers. The prevalences of hypertension and dyslipidemia in the poor control group were 28.9% and 37.1%, respectively, and were significantly higher than those in the good control group. Exploratory analyzes showed significant indirect-effect estimates involving MMP-9 and ET-1, with model-derived proportions of approximately 22% to 26%; however, these contemporaneous associations do not establish causal mediation.

CONCLUSION: Poor glycemic control at 12 months postpartum was associated with higher MMP-9 and ET-1 levels and a greater prevalence of hypertension and dyslipidemia. The observed indirect effects should be interpreted as exploratory statistical associations rather than evidence of temporal or causal mediation.

articles.title: Gut microbiome-based interventions to prevent ICU-acquired infections: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiome colonization with potential pathogens is common and often precedes clinical infection in the intensive care unit (ICU). Two key gut microbiome-based interventions seek to prevent infections yet use opposite approaches: selective digestive decontamination (SDD) utilizes antibiotics to eliminate potential pathogens, whereas biotic supplementation (prebiotics, probiotics, or synbiotics) aims to enrich beneficial microbes. In the absence of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) directly comparing these two interventions, this systematic review and meta-analysis sought to compare the effect sizes of SDD versus biotic interventions for mortality and infection-related outcomes. We searched PubMed for RCTs published between 2000 and 2025. Eligible studies recruited adult ICU patients, assessed SDD or biotics against a comparator (standard care or placebo), and reported on mortality and/or acquired infection-related outcomes. Pooled relative risks (RR) were calculated using random-effects models. Nine SDD trials involving 19,907 subjects and 29 biotic supplementation trials involving 5,483 subjects were included. When compared versus standard care or placebo, neither intervention significantly reduced overall mortality (SDD: RR = 0.96 [95%CI: 0.88-1.05]; biotics: RR = 0.93 [95%CI: 0.87-1.00]).SDD was associated with modestly lower observed risk for ICU acquired all-cause infections compared to biotics (SDD: RR = 0.76 [95%CI: 0.60-0.98]; biotics: RR = 0.82 [95%CI: 0.64-1.05], no statistically significant difference) and specifically lower risk for pneumonia (SDD: RR = 0.50 [95%CI: 0.26-0.96]; prebiotics and synbiotics: RR = 0.70 [95%CI: 0.54-0.90]). In conclusion, neither SDD nor biotics was significantly protective for mortality, but both types of interventions showed similarly promising protective associations with infections, especially pneumonia. The studies selected were heterogeneous, especially those testing biotic interventions.

articles.title: AGR3 drives M1 polarization and glycolytic reprogramming of pulmonary macrophages via stabilizing HIF-1α/PKM2 axis to aggravate CLP-induced sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (sepsis-ARDS) remains a life-threatening critical illness with limited targeted therapeutics, where pulmonary macrophage M1 polarization and aerobic glycolysis act as core drivers of inflammatory lung injury. Anterior gradient 3 (AGR3), an endoplasmic reticulum disulfide isomerase, was recently identified as a dysregulated transcript in human ARDS patient datasets, yet its immunometabolic function in septic lung injury remains undefined. Here, we aimed to characterize the role and molecular cascade of AGR3 in regulating macrophage polarization and glycolytic reprogramming during polymicrobial sepsis, combining the in vivo CLP septic mouse model with an in vitro LPS/IFN-γ-induced M1 polarization model in RAW264.7 macrophages. Bioinformatic mining of GSE66890 RNA-seq dataset revealed prominent AGR3 upregulation in human ARDS lung tissues, which we validated in cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced septic mouse lungs and LPS/IFN-γ-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Lentiviral-mediated AGR3 knockdown suppressed M1 macrophage polarization, reduced glycolytic flux (lower ECAR, higher OCR, diminished lactate secretion), and blunted pro-inflammatory cytokine release in vitro. Mechanistic biochemistry assays demonstrated that AGR3 physically interacts with hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α), extending HIF-1α protein half-life by restraining proteasomal degradation and promoting its nuclear translocation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation confirmed that stabilized nuclear HIF-1α transcriptionally activates pyruvate kinase M2 (Pkm2), a master glycolytic effector. Reciprocal rescue experiments verified that ectopic overexpression of HIF-1α or PKM2 largely reversed the anti-inflammatory, metabolic phenotypes induced by AGR3 silencing. In vivo intratracheal AAV9-shAGR3 delivery mitigated CLP-triggered pulmonary edema, neutrophil infiltration, M1 macrophage accumulation, and restored protective PKM2 tetramer formation, accompanied by significant improvement in pulmonary function and 7-day survival of septic mice. Taken together, AGR3 mediates sepsis-induced lung injury via the HIF-1α/PKM2 signaling. This study provides a novel potential therapeutic target for sepsis-associated ARDS.

articles.title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
articles.abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development. After birth, rapid microbial colonization occurs in the intestine and lungs. Through signaling molecules including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, and bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs), coupled with vagal nerve and mucosal immune pathways, the microbiota maintains intestinal and pulmonary immune homeostasis, preserves blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and modulates microglial activation, thereby regulating neurogenesis, synaptic pruning, and brain functional programming. Early-life dysbiosis is commonly associated with preterm birth, cesarean delivery, infection, and antibiotic exposure. In human observational studies, it accompanies disrupted organ homeostasis and neuroinflammatory signatures, and is linked to an increased long-term risk of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disability; in neonatal animal models, it aggravates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) and encephalopathy of prematurity. Because dysbiosis frequently co-occurs with prematurity, infection, and other confounders, these associations do not by themselves establish causality. This review summarizes early-life colonization patterns of intestinal and pulmonary microbiota and their underlying neuroimmune mechanisms, analyzes the impacts of dysbiosis on neuroimmunity and related diseases, and proposes intervention strategies, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for neonatal health protection and neurodevelopmental disorder prevention.

articles.title: A body shape index and body roundness index in women with and without the polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association of a body shape index (ABSI) and body roundness index (BRI) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), also known as polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS).

METHODS: This study was registered at PROSPERO [CRD420251177545] and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched evidence in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and SciELO databases. Two case-control and seven cross-sectional studies reported ABSI and BRI results in PMOS patients and women without the syndrome.
