articles.title: Identification and profiling of HLA-A*02:01-restricted Toxoplasma gondii peptides through immunopeptidomics in HLA-A2.1 transgenic mice.
articles.abstract: HLA class I presentation of pathogen-derived peptides is essential for CD8+ T-cell recognition of Toxoplasma gondii. While in vitro MHC ligands have been documented, the in vivo ligandome during infection progression remains poorly characterized. Here, we employed an MS-based immunopeptidomics approach to directly profile the T. gondii immunopeptidome presented by HLA-A *02:01 in transgenic mice. By employing a hierarchical discovery funnel, our analysis identified a comprehensive repertoire of 3,744 unique T. gondii-derived peptides. Subsequent filtering for canonical 8-12mers, matching the typical binding length for HLA-A *02:01 ligands, established a high-confidence foundational ligandome of 3,433 peptides. Source protein analysis revealed that these peptides originate from diverse parasite proteins, including a substantial proportion of previously uncharacterized hypothetical proteins. Notably, specific ligands were consistently detected across both acute and chronic stages, suggesting stable MHC-I presentation throughout the infection cycle. By integrating in silico predictions with experimental validation, we prioritized 73 high-affinity candidates, five of which exhibited robust HLA-A *02:01 binding capacity in vitro and in vivo. Specifically, we identified a novel ligand derived from glycogen synthase (PGS) and determined its co-crystal structure with HLA-A *02:01, revealing favorable binding architecture. Overall, these findings expand the known HLA-A *02:01-restricted ligand landscape of T. gondii and provide a high-priority list of candidates for future functional validation of CD8+ T-cell immunogenicity.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of doravirine/islatravir for HIV-1: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of doravirine and islatravir (DOR/ISL) is a novel two-drug regimen for HIV-1. Early development faced challenges due to dose-dependent immunological signals. We aimed to synthesize the evidence on the efficacy and safety of DOR/ISL across all treatment-experience categories, specifically evaluating the impact of islatravir dosage (0.25 mg vs 0.75 mg) on clinical and immunological outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) following PRISMA guidelines. We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from inception through April 2026. Primary outcomes were virological suppression (<50 copies/mL) and mean change in CD4+ T-cell count at week 48. Data were pooled using random-effects models. Islatravir dose was evaluated as a pre-specified moderator. Quality was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and certainty of evidence was graded using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Seven RCTs (n = 3,600 participants) were included. At Week 48, DOR/ISL showed non-inferior suppression rates (RR 1.01 [95% CI 0.99-1.02]; p = 0.516; moderate-certainty evidence) and a statistically significant reduction in virological failure risk (RR 0.55 [0.33-0.92]; p = 0.022) compared to active control. Overall CD4+ gain was lower with DOR/ISL (MD -34.55 cells/μL; low-certainty evidence); however, a profound moderator effect of dose was observed (p < 0.0001). The 0.75 mg dose was associated with significant CD4+ and lymphocyte declines, whereas the approved 0.25 mg dose was immunologically neutral. DOR/ISL was weight-neutral compared to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (MD -0.25 kg [-0.66 to 0.16]; low-certainty evidence).

CONCLUSION: DOR/ISL 100/0.25 mg once daily achieved virological suppression comparable to standard-of-care ART regimens and was associated with lower rates of virological failure compared with active comparators. The immunological safety concerns observed in early trials were successfully resolved by dose optimization. These findings support the use of DOR/ISL (IDVYNSO) as a potential treatment option for both treatment-naïve and virologically suppressed adults while emphasizing long-term safety surveillance.

articles.title: Early risk stratification of late-onset sepsis in very preterm infants by intestinal microbiota profiling: a multicenter case-control validation study.
articles.abstract: Intestinal bacterial translocation to the bloodstream is a route of infection for late-onset sepsis (LOS) in preterm infants, highlighting the potential of fecal microbiota profiling for early risk stratification. We aimed to identify and validate LOS-specific gut microbiota signatures. Fifty-eight preterm infants (gestational age < 30 weeks) with blood culture-proven LOS (excluding coagulase-negative staphylococci) were matched to controls (1:1) across three cohorts (Discovery (DC) n = 18; Validation 1 and 2; VC1 n = 12, VC2 n = 28). Fecal samples collected up to 10 days before LOS onset underwent 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial composition, diversity, and discriminatory taxa were compared across LOS subgroups. Random Forest (RF) models were trained in DC and validated in VC1/VC2. Microbiota variation was largely explained by LOS pathogen (R2 = 17%, P < 0.001). Infants with non-staphylococcal and E. coli-LOS showed a temporal increase in relative abundance of Escherichia/Shigella. The RF model distinguishing E. coli-LOS from controls displayed the highest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.99/0.78/0.61 for DC/VC1/VC2) compared to non-staphylococcal LOS (AUC = 0.96/0.46/0.41). Our findings demonstrate profound microbiota shifts preceding E. coli-LOS, with higher discriminatory ability compared to non-staphylococcal-LOS. While pathogen-specific microbiota-based risk stratification may offer added clinical value, reduced validation performance highlights the limited generalizability and underscores the need for future research before clinical translation.

articles.title: The association between age and mortality in men with adult-onset testosterone deficiency is altered by testosterone therapy.
articles.journal: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Using the Gompertz-Makeham model, we describe associations between age and the probability of mortality in men with adult-onset testosterone deficiency (TD), stratified by testosterone undecanoate (TU) treatment and type 2 diabetes (T2DM).

METHODS: We analyzed a registry of 737 men (353 and 384 men on/not on TU, respectively) with adult-onset TD with nearly 9 years of follow-up. We compared associations between age and mortality using nonparametric and logistic regression models (estimating individual mortality probability) in men stratified by TU treatment and T2DM.

RESULTS: Mortality was lower (p < 0.001) in men on TU compared to men opting against TU. In the men on TU, age was associated with mortality (odds ratio (OR): 1.26, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.40) in the nonlinear pattern expected in the Gompertz‒Makeham model. However, age was not associated with mortality in men not on TU (OR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.98-1.08). T2DM status did not affect these associations.

CONCLUSION: The association between age and mortality differed between men on TU and those opting against treatment. In untreated men, features of metabolic syndrome worsened, which perhaps minimized the relationship between age and mortality. In men on TU, these metabolic risk factors improved, perhaps restoring the association between age and mortality.

articles.title: Hepatitis B virus spreading via Beddington-DeAngelis incidence function and feed-forward neural network with optimal control.
articles.abstract: Using an appropriate mathematical model, this study aims to examine the transmission dynamics and optimal control of hepatitis B virus spreading, employing the Beddington-DeAngelis incidence function, a hybrid method of 4th order Runge-Kutta method (RK4) and feed-forward neural network (FFNN), as the integration of epidemiological models with neural network is particularly important for representing disease propagation. The well-posedness, local and global stability conditions are obtained using the threshold parameter. Some sensitive epidemic parameters and their relative impacts are quantified. Based on the local and global properties of the model and sensitivity analysis, a control problem is formulated to control the infection by minimizing the HBV-infected population and maximizing the recovered population using three control measures. Finally, a hybrid method of supervised FFNN and RK4 with two hidden layers is used to effectively approximate the temporal dynamics of HBV transmission and verify the theoretical results, as well as the effects of controls.

articles.title: The economic burden of preeclampsia: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia is a serious pregnancy complication associated with substantial maternal and infant morbidity worldwide. The adverse outcomes related to preeclampsia increase healthcare costs, highlighting the importance of quantifying its economic burden to inform healthcare policy and resource allocation. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on the economic burden of preeclampsia and identify key cost drivers.

METHODS: MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for English-language studies published between 2014 and 2024. Studies reporting healthcare resource utilization or costs associated with preeclampsia were included. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025650091).

RESULTS: Of 3,107 records identified, 12 studies were included; most were conducted in high-income countries. All cost estimates were converted to 2024 US dollars for comparability. Direct medical costs ranged from US$109.84 to US$87,339.71, with a mean cost of US$33,585.48 per patient. National healthcare system costs were estimated at €6.5-€9.1 million in Ireland and US$2.18 billion in the United States.

CONCLUSION: Preterm birth was identified as a major driver of economic burden, with earlier gestational age significantly increasing maternal and infant costs. Indirect costs and regional disparities remain underexplored, highlighting important gaps for future research.

articles.title: Dnmt1 associated Gja1 promoter methylation changes are implicated in Cx43 remodeling during acute myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: DNA methylation has traditionally been regarded as a stable epigenetic modification. However, emerging evidence indicates that oxidative and genotoxic stress can induce locus-specific methylation changes that modulate transcriptional responses. The contribution of such dynamic regulation to cardiac gene expression during myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury (MIRI) remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether altered methylation changes within the Gja1 promoter region are associated with connexin43 (Cx43) remodeling during MIRI. Male C57BL/6 mice were underwent global hypothermic I/R using a Langendorff-perfused heart model, with or without pretreatment using the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor 5-azacytidine (5-Aza, 3 μg/g body weight, i.p.). Gja1 promoter methylation was analyzed by BSP and MSP, while Dnmt1 enrichment was assessed by chromatin immunoprecipitation. Cx43 expression and localization were examined by qRT-PCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence, together with electrophysiological and histological analyses. MIRI was associated with Dnmt1 upregulation and nuclear enrichment, accompanied by altered methylation signals at selected CpG sites within the examined Gja1 promoter region and transcriptional repression. These changes coincided with reduced Cx43 expression, altered subcellular localization, impaired electrical conduction and increased arrhythmia susceptibility. Pretreatment with 5-Aza partially attenuated Gja1 promoter methylation signals and preserved Cx43 expression and localization during subsequent MIRI. These findings support an association between Dnmt1 enrichment, alteredGja1promoter CpG methylation, and Cx43 remodeling under reperfusion stress, suggesting that methylation-related epigenetic regulation may participate in Gja1 transcriptional responses during MIRI. Further temporal and gene-specific validation will be required to establish the kinetics and causal specificity of this pathway.

articles.title: Effects of combined versus single supplementation of creatine and beta-alanine on aerobic and anerobic performance: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Creatine (Cr) and β-alanine (BA) are among the most studied ergogenic supplements, acting on distinct physiological pathways-Cr facilitates phosphocreatine resynthesis and rapid ATP turnover, while BA elevates intramuscular carnosine to enhance acid-base buffering. Although both compounds improve high-intensity performance independently, the ergogenic potential of their combined use remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate and compare the isolated and combined effects of Cr and BA supplementation on aerobic and anaerobic performance indices using a network meta-analytic approach.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (to August 2025) identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining Cr, BA, or Cr + BA supplementation (≥2 weeks) in healthy adult athletes. Fifty-two RCTs (PEDro ≥ 6) met the inclusion criteria. Standardized mean differences (SMD) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were computed within random effects models. Performance outcomes included sprint, jump, agility, upper- and lower-body muscular endurance (UME, LME), and repeated-sprint ability (RSA).

RESULTS: Cr supplementation significantly improved sprint performance (SMD = -0.64; p = 0.04), jump performance (SMD = 0.33; p = 0.002), RSA (SMD = -0.78; p = 0.01), and UME (SMD = 0.43; p = 0.01) versus placebo, with P scores ≥ 0.90 across these domains. In contrast, BA supplementation produced non-significant or context-specific effects, and combined Cr + BA showed no synergistic benefits. Agility and LME outcomes remained unaffected (p > 0.05). Heterogeneity ranged from low to moderate (I2 = 0-73%), with no global inconsistency or substantive publication bias.

CONCLUSION: Evidence indicates Cr supplementation alone yields the most consistent improvements in high-intensity and anaerobic performance by enhancing phosphocreatine recovery and neuromuscular output. BA's buffering advantage appears task-specific and insufficient to augment Cr's ergogenic efficacy. Co-supplementation of Cr and BA offers no additional advantage beyond Cr monotherapy. Standardized, long-term, multi-arm RCTs are warranted to further clarify potential interactive mechanisms and sex or sport-specific responses.

articles.title: Wedelactone-loaded exosomes for sepsis-induced liver injury: a novel therapeutic strategy.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced liver injury (SILI) is an important cause of death in intensive care patients, which seriously affects clinical prognosis. Wedelolactone (WEL) exhibits hepatoprotective properties, however, its clinical application is constrained by its poor solubility and insufficient targeting ability. Therefore, in this study, an innovative exosome (Exo)-based drug delivery system loaded with WEL (Exo@WEL) was constructed. The aim was to enhance the liver-targeting efficacy and therapeutic performance of WEL. Exo were extracted from the mice macrophages cell line RAW264.7 by differential centrifugation, and WEL was successfully loaded using ultrasonic incubation. Exo@WEL was characterized by TEM, particle size analysis, and NTA, confirming its structural suitability as an exogenous agent. DiR labeling revealed that Exo@WEL had a significantly enhanced liver-targeting ability compared to WEL. Safety was confirmed by HE staining test. In the SILI models, Exo@WEL showed better hepatoprotection over WEL. Beyond entinfinmtory actvity menifested y decreased ro infammatory rokines, Exo@WEL reinforced antioxidant function and efectively restained feroptosis. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of ML385, a selective Nrf2 inhibitor, confirmed the critical regulatory role of the Nrf2 pathway in mediating these multifaceted liver protective effects. This study pioneered the development of a targeted Exo-based nanoplatform (Exo@WEL) for SILI therapy. The mechanism study has revealed a potential therapeutic strategy for inhibiting oxidative stress and ferroptosis by regulating the Nrf2/SLC7A11/GPX4 axis. This preparation provides a novel nanotherapeutic strategy that combines high efficiency and safety for the treatment of SILI. These findings also lay a theoretical foundation for the clinical translation of Exo drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Piperine reverses colistin resistance in multidrug resistant Gram-negative pathogens by membrane disruption and ROS damage.
articles.abstract: The global spread of colistin (COL) resistance, particularly mediated by mcr-1, threatens the efficacy of this last-line antibiotic against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative pathogens. This development underscores the urgency of developing innovative therapeutic strategies to counteract antimicrobial resistance mechanisms. This study demonstrates that piperine (PIP), a natural alkaloid, functions as a potent adjuvant that restores COL efficacy through a multi-target mechanism. The combination of PIP and COL exhibits significant synergism against clinically relevant pathogens, including mcr-1-positive strains (FICI: 0.07-0.281), and was not susceptible to the development of drug resistance. Additionally, this combination effectively inhibits and eradicates biofilms. Mechanism studies and omics analysis confirmed that PIP combined with COL could cause bacterial membrane disruption, proton motive force (PMF) disruption, efflux pumps inhibition, resulting in accumulation of bacterial reactive oxygen species (ROS) and finally cell death. Furthermore, PIP suppresses MCR-1 through dual suppression of gene expression and protein function. The therapeutic potential was confirmed in murine infection models, where the combination significantly improved survival rates, reduced bacterial loads, and attenuated inflammatory responses. This study provides the first comprehensive elucidation of the multi-target synergy between COL and PIP, offering a promising therapeutic strategy that simultaneously overcomes existing resistance and impedes resistance development.

articles.title: Is Fusobacterium nucleatum the key mediator between oral infections and systemic diseases? Mechanistic insights and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum has emerged as a pathobiont that associates oral dysbiosis with systemic diseases through coaggregation, hematogenous dissemination, and immune modulation. This review provides molecular insights through which they are involved in systemic diseases such as colorectal cancer, adverse pregnancy outcomes, cardiovascular diseases, neurodegenerative disorders, and diabetes mellitus. Key virulence factors include the adhesins of FadA, Fap2, and RadD, lipopolysaccharides, and outer membrane vesicles, which mediate epithelial invasion and endothelial permeafbility and facilitate immune suppression through TLR4-NF-κB, β-catenin/Wnt, and MAPK signaling pathways. These interactions result in impaired tissue homeostasis, propagate chronic inflammation, and promote oncogenic and metabolic modulation. Systemic pleiotropy of F. nucleatum is further substantiated by its involvement in chemoresistance, placental dysfunction, vascular inflammation, and neuronal injury, substantiating its systemic pleiotropy. Emerging therapeutic strategies, such as blocking adhesins, neutralizing outer membrane vesicles, microbiome manipulation, and using CRISPR-based clearance, provide precision techniques for mitigating diseases. Therefore, this review identifies F. nucleatum as the primary microbial mediator of oral-systemic pathology and its translational significance in the development of targeted antimicrobial and host-directed therapies.

articles.title: Exploring medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness among Korean medical students: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming healthcare systems and clinical practice, increasing the need to prepare future physicians to work effectively with AI technologies in clinical contexts. Despite growing interest in integrating AI into medical education, empirical evidence regarding medical students' readiness to use AI remains limited. This study aimed to assess medical AI readiness among Korean medical students and explore factors associated with their readiness.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among medical students enrolled in a six-year medical program at a university in Korea. A total of 204 students participated in the study. Medical AI readiness was measured using the Medical Artificial Intelligence Readiness Scale for Medical Students (MAIRS-MS), which assesses four domains: cognition, ability, vision, and ethics. Descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, and Pearson's correlation analyses were performed using SPSS version 27.

RESULTS: The overall mean score of medical AI readiness was 4.19 on a 7-point Likert scale, indicating a moderate level of medical AI readiness. Among the subscales, ethics showed the highest mean score (4.69), followed by vision (4.44), ability (4.18), and cognition (3.92). The frequency of AI use was significantly associated with medical AI readiness, whereas the daily duration of AI use was not. No significant gender differences were observed. When students were divided into the low (pre-medical years 1-2) and high (medical years 1-4) groups, the high group showed significantly higher scores only in the ability subscale.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that medical students are not yet sufficiently prepared to utilize AI technologies in clinical practice, particularly in terms of knowledge and practical competencies related to AI. These results highlight the need for structured and longitudinal AI education in medical curricula to better prepare future physicians for AI-integrated healthcare environments.

articles.title: Emergence of invasive Escherichia coli pathobionts in gut microbiome promotes cancer stemness via targeting Hippo pathways.
articles.abstract: Growing evidence suggests a pivotal role of the microbiome in tumorigenesis, extending beyond genetics. Apc(Min/+) mice exhibit reduced tumor load when housed in germ-free conditions. Nevertheless, how genetic factors shape microbiota and how dysbiosis fits into the genetic paradigm of intestinal carcinogenesis remain elusive. Epithelial stemness is regulated by Wnt/Apc/β-catenin pathway, whereas Apc mutations and Hippo signaling are associated with tumor growth. Invasive pathobionts emerge from microbiota as a result of epithelial barrier dysfunction. We hypothesize that the emergence of invasive pathobionts and dysbiosis of epithelial microbiota contribute to increased cancer stemness. The epithelial and fecal microbiota are longitudinally monitored in Apc(Min/+) and wild-type littermates born to wild-type surrogate dams. Segregation of epithelial microbiota between Apc(Min/+) and wild-type mice was observed as early as eight weeks after birth, whereas fecal microbiota diverged at 20 weeks of age. Epithelial dysbiosis and barrier defects were observed in Apc(Min/+) mice, characterized by intraepithelial Escherichia coli with invasive features. While antibiotic treatment reduced cancer burden, invasive E. coli infection promoted tumorsphere formation. Higher expression of Vgll3 and Tead4 (Hippo effectors) and Cd44 (a cancer stemness marker) was observed in bacteria-infected tumorspheres. Mechanistically, bacteria augmented epithelial clonogenicity by enhancing VGLL3/TEAD4-mediated CD44 promoter activity. Invasive E. coli genetic signatures were verified in 86% of human colorectal carcinoma specimens, and a positive correlation with TEAD4 expression was observed. In conclusion, Apc mutation drives the expansion of invasive pathobionts to promote cancer stemness via a VGLL3/TEAD4/CD44 axis. Bacteria-targeting interventions could be an alternative strategy for patients with hereditary tumors.

articles.title: Consensus and learning climate in temporary versus permanent teams in team-based learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In team-based learning, students are typically placed in fixed teams based on the idea that stable group membership fosters collaboration: as teammates get to know each other, they share more information, resolve differences and feel motivated to contribute. This rationale had not been tested in a randomized controlled trial.

OBJECTIVE: The study compares team-based learning in temporary teams with the default permanent teams regarding individual and team readiness assurance test performance (iRAT, tRAT), reaching team consensus, the learning climate, and intrinsic motivation.

DESIGN: In a randomized controlled trial, first-year medical students were assigned either to permanent TBL teams or to teams that were re-assigned for each problem. The team readiness assurance test (tRAT) votes, submitted individually and covertly, served as an indirect indicator for team consensus (concordant versus discordant tRAT vote).

RESULTS: Discordant tRATs (n = 268, 11.8% of all votes) were submitted more frequently in temporary than in permanent teams, both for correct and incorrect majority decisions. The self-rated learning climate was more cooperative in permanent than in temporary teams, while intrinsic motivation and tRAT scores were similar for both types of teams. A poorer learning climate was associated with a higher proportion of discordant tRATs.

CONCLUSION: Working in temporary teams does not lead to inferior intrinsic motivation; this was previously also shown for knowledge gain. However, the poorer learning climate, together with reaching a consensus less often, might indicate that at least some members of temporary teams feel not adequately appreciated in the discussion and do not accept the majority decision. With instructional strategies promoting a cooperative learning climate in temporary teams, preclinical TBL courses might serve as an early promoter of the relational team competencies required for subsequent clinical workplace learning in temporary teams.

articles.title: Microbiome and metabolites impact enteric and central nervous systems in ALS.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) has been linked to gastrointestinal symptoms and alterations in the gut microbiota. The enteric nervous system (ENS) coordinates intestinal function and sits at the host-microbe interface. The mechanisms by which luminal changes relay to the central nervous system (CNS), where motor neurons reside, have yet to be completely defined. In this narrative review, we first present evidence from ALS patient cohorts and preclinical models alongside mechanistic studies of infection, dysbiosis, and related neurodegenerative diseases to discuss how the microbiota and its metabolites may affect the ENS and CNS in ALS. Next, we propose a plausible mechanism of ALS pathogenesis through the gut-microbiome-brain axis. We further offer a summary of clinical trials that have studied the impacts of the microbiota on human ALS. Finally, we discuss future directions for studies of microbiota-ENS-CNS interactions in ALS. Better understanding of the dynamic interactions among the microbiota, microbial metabolites, neuroactive metabolites, and inflammation through the ENS/CNS in ALS will provide innovative insights into ALS prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Perinatal ampicillin exposure alters murine maternal fecal bile acid and acylcarnitine profiles.
articles.abstract: Maternal intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP) and postpartum maternal antibiotic usage are increasingly common and have been linked to altered growth and immune development in offspring. However, the mechanisms underlying these effects, particularly those arising from indirect early-life exposure to antibiotics, remain poorly understood. Here, using a preclinical murine model, we examined the impact of in vivo antepartum and postpartum maternal ampicillin administration on the maternal fecal microbiome and metabolome. Ampicillin treatment resulted in a significant depletion of bacterial species belonging to the Muribaculaceae family, including Muribaculum intestinale and Duncaniella dubosii, accompanied by a cohort-dependent enrichment of Enterococcus and Prevotella species. These microbial shifts coincided with substantial and reproducible metabolic remodeling, including elevated fecal acylcarnitines and altered bile acid profiles. Notably, we identified two previously uncharacterized trihydroxylated bile acids conjugated to a hexose moiety, which we annotated as cholic acid-galactose and taurocholic acid-galactose and synthesized. These metabolites were consistently associated with antibiotic exposure across public metabolomics data repositories. Finally, alterations in the maternal fecal microbiome and metabolome were associated with increased weight gain in offspring, suggesting potential pathways by which maternal antibiotic exposure may influence early developmental outcomes. These findings highlight microbial and metabolic signatures linked to perinatal antibiotic use and underscore the need to balance infection control with long-term infant health considerations.

articles.title: European society of gynecology (ESG) position paper on the proposed terminology change from PCOS to PMOS.
authors: on the behalf of the ESG Board
articles.journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent endocrine disorder whose terminology inadequately reflects its systemic nature. The proposed renaming to polyendocrine metabolic ovary syndrome (PMOS) aims to better represent its pathophysiology.

OBJECTIVE: To present the European Society of Gynaecology (ESG) position regarding the proposed terminology change and its implementation.

METHODS: Expert consensus and narrative synthesis of current scientific evidence and international recommendations.

RESULTS: ESG supports a structured, patient-centered transition strategy. Recommendations include prioritizing patient communication, implementing a gradual transition with prolonged dual terminology use, and integrating the new terminology systematically into scientific and educational frameworks. The importance of interdisciplinary clarity and the central role of gynecological endocrinology are emphasized.

CONCLUSION: A phased and clearly communicated transition will enhance conceptual accuracy while preserving patient understanding, continuity of care, and clinical coordination.

articles.title: Adiponectin improves the aortic dissection by inhibiting inflammatory cell infiltration and macrophage pyroptosis.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic dissection (AD) is a fatal cardiovascular emergency that is predominantly induced by long-term uncontrolled hypertension.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The mouse AD model was established by combining β-aminopropionitrile with angiotensin II. The incidence rate, rupture rate, and survival status of the mice were evaluated. The structural damage of the aorta was observed using tissue staining technology, the extracellular matrix status, and macrophage pyroptosis were evaluated by immunofluorescence staining, the infiltration of inflammatory cells was detected by immunohistochemistry, the expression of pyroptosis-related molecules, and inflammatory factors was analyzed by Western blotting and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Cell proliferation was detected by EdU staining, and cell apoptosis was detected by flow cytometry.

RESULTS: In the aortic tissues of AD model mice, the expression of APN, and the content of APN in the serum were significantly decreased. APN intervention can alleviate the thickening of the aortic media, rupture of elastic fibers, and degradation of the extracellular matrix. APN inhibits the proliferation, apoptosis, and phenotypic transformation of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). At the same time, it can inhibit the infiltration of neutrophils and macrophages and the inflammatory response. Underlying mechanism, it was found that APN inhibited NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis by reducing the release of inflammatory factors; this effect was dependent on the phosphorylation activation of AMPKα and APN receptor.

CONCLUSION: APN plays a protective role in AD. Its underlying mechanism is related to the activation of the AMPK pathway, which in turn inhibits macrophage pyroptosis and vascular inflammation. This study offers a new perspective for the pathological mechanism of AD.

articles.title: Early antibiotic exposure and vaccine immune responses in preterm infants: potential sex-specific differences.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis represents a major risk in preterm infant care, resulting in widespread early-life antibiotic exposure. While the latter has been linked to immune maturation in term-born neonates, its impact on preterm immune development remains unclear. The aim of this prospective observational study was to investigate the effect of early antibiotic exposure on vaccine titers at a corrected age of four months. To achieve this, blood and stool samples were analyzed from 69 preterm infants (<32 weeks gestational age; 35 with 34 without antibiotic exposure during the first postnatal week) at postnatal day 14 and again at four months corrected age. We assessed vaccine-induced antibody titers against Bordetella pertussis and Haemophilus influenzae, immune cell profiles (flow cytometry), gut microbiome composition (16S rRNA sequencing), and plasma amino acid and acylcarnitine levels (tandem mass spectrometry). Preterm infants exposed to early antibiotics showed reduced antibody titers following vaccination, with differences appearing more pronounced in girls. Antibiotic-exposed girls displayed increased monocytes and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), both of which inversely correlated with antibody titers. Early antibiotic exposure was associated with differences in microbial community types at postnatal day 14, with Klebsiella-dominated and Bifidobacteria-lacking communities occurring more frequently in antibiotic-exposed infants. Antibiotic-exposed girls exhibited distinct metabolomic alterations, including elevated levels of two unsaturated fatty acids that negatively correlated with monocyte and MDSC abundance. Our findings suggest that early antibiotic exposure impairs vaccine responses in preterm infants and indicates a potentially sex-specific susceptibility. Antibiotic-driven changes in the microbiome and metabolome may sustain suppressive innate immune cell populations, which may in turn weaken adaptive responses to vaccination.

articles.title: Effects of a commercially available sugar-free energy drink on hitting exit velocity in experienced baseball and softball players: a randomized crossover trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caffeine is commonly used as an ergogenic aid, with effective doses often reported at approximately 3-9 mg/kg; however, lower doses are also frequently included in multi-ingredient pre-workout supplements, and the effects of these supplements on sport-specific hitting performance in baseball and softball players remain largely unexplored. Thus, we investigated the acute effects of a commercially available, multi-ingredient caffeinated energy drink (ED) on hitting exit velocity, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, barbell velocity, reaction time, perceived energy, and post-running metabolic outcomes in experienced baseball and softball players.

METHODS: Twenty-two experienced baseball and softball players (14 males, 8 females; mean playing experience: 13 ± 2 years) completed this double-blind, randomized, crossover study. Participants consumed either a sugar-free and caffeinated ED (C4 Performance Energy®; 5 kcal, 200 mg caffeine, β-alanine, betaine anhydrous, and vitamin B12) or a low-calorie, flavor-matched placebo (PLA) during two experimental sessions separated by ≥ 5 days. Testing batteries were performed at three within-session timepoints (T0: pre-consumption; T1: 30 minutes post-consumption; T2: post-exercise) and included CMJs, 30 back squat repetitions at 30% of estimated 1RM, a computerized reaction time test, and subjective perceptual questionnaires. Participants also performed 40 tee hits after T1 and before a high-intensity interval treadmill protocol, followed by 15-minute post-exercise indirect calorimetry.

RESULTS: Both average (ED: 71.3 ± 14.0 mph vs. PLA: 70.1 ± 13.5 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.20  ±  1.41 mph, 95% CI: 0.56-1.84, p < 0.001, dz = 0.85) and peak (ED: 76.7 ± 13.9 mph vs. PLA: 75.1 ± 13.6 mph; mean difference ± SD: 1.56 ± 1.70 mph, 95% CI: 0.79-2.33, p < 0.001, dz = 0.92) hitting exit velocity were significantly greater in the ED condition. A significant condition × time interaction was observed for CMJ height (p = 0.003), whereby jump height was maintained with the ED condition but decreased with PLA at T1. Post-exercise recovery energy expenditure was significantly greater with ED (~5%; p = 0.040, d = 0.46). No significant interactions were observed for barbell velocity, reaction time, or subjective perceptual questionnaires.

CONCLUSIONS: Acute consumption of a caffeinated multi-ingredient energy drink resulted in small increases in average and peak hitting exit velocity and attenuated transient decline in CMJ height observed with placebo. These findings warrant future investigations with live-pitching conditions in prolonged game simulation settings.

articles.title: Effects of dietary nitrate supplementation in team sport athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary nitrate (NO3 -), typically provided as beetroot juice, increases nitric oxide availability and may reduce the oxygen cost of exercise, improve muscle oxygenation, and delay fatigue. Evidence in team sport athletes, however, remains limited and has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the effects of NO3 - supplementation on team sport-specific performance and related physiological and biochemical outcomes.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD42022358739). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through March 2025 for randomized, placebo-controlled trials investigating acute (single dose) or chronic (≥2 days, with the final dose taken 2-3 h before exercise) NO3 - supplementation in male or female team sport athletes. Effect sizes (Hedges' g) were synthesized using multilevel random-effects models (REML) with cluster-robust standard errors. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Robustness analyses, including sensitivity to assumed within-person correlations for crossover trials and Monte Carlo simulations to examine the stability of key contrasts under sparse evidence were performed.

RESULTS: Twenty-four trials (n = 365 athletes; 277 males, 88 females) met inclusion criteria. Supplementation increased circulating and salivary NO3 -/NO2 -, indicating elevated systemic concentrations. The overall pooled ergogenic effect on performance was small but statistically significant (g = 0.075; 95% CI 0.026-0.124; p = 0.005). In team sport-specific tasks, NO3 - supplementation produced a small but consistent improvement with low heterogeneity and moderate certainty of evidence (g = 0.143; 95% CI 0.041-0.245; p = 0.011). A significant benefit was observed with chronic protocols (g = 0.145; 95% CI 0.076-0.214; p < 0.001), whereas acute protocols showed no clear effects. The chronic-acute contrast was statistically significant (g = 0.118; 95% CI 0.029-0.207; p = 0.013) but was not robust to more conservative crossover-correlation assumptions, lowering certainty to very low; because chronic protocols also included a final pre-exercise dose, this contrast should not be interpreted as evidence of long-term adaptation. Improvements were most evident in team sport-specific performance tests (moderate certainty), with additional, less certain signals in repeated high-intensity efforts and fatigue-sensitive neuromuscular outcomes (both very low certainty), while single-sprint outcomes and most metabolic/biochemical markers showed no consistent benefit. Cardiorespiratory responses were largely unchanged. Dose-response meta-regressions did not reveal consistent linear or non-linear trends.

CONCLUSIONS: NO3 - supplementation provides small, context-dependent ergogenic benefits in team sport athletes, most consistently for team sport-specific performance (moderate certainty), with preliminary signals for repeated high-intensity efforts and fatigue-sensitive neuromuscular performance (both very low certainty). Evidence for moderation by protocol type, sex, and training status remains suggestive but uncertain and is currently insufficient to support specific dosing recommendations. Well-powered, standardized, sex-stratified trials with harmonized outcome measures are needed to clarify key moderators and strengthen applied guidance.

articles.title: Lower-limb performance and muscle soreness after short-term dark chocolate intake in CrossFit®-trained women: an exploratory secondary analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dark chocolate (DC) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for exercise performance and recovery, but evidence in trained women remains limited. This exploratory secondary analysis examined selected lower-limb performance outcomes and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) in female CrossFit® athletes.

METHODS: This secondary analysis included 15 trained female CrossFit® athletes from a randomized crossover trial. No separate a priori sample-size calculation was performed for these outcomes (minimum detectable paired effect, d_z = 0.78). DC (30 g/day, 85% cocoa), placebo chocolate (PLA), and an open-label control (CONN) were compared at four operationally defined menstrual-cycle assessments after three days of supplementation. DC-PLA allocation was blinded, but blinding success was not assessed. Outcomes were vertical jump height (VJH), knee isokinetic and isometric performance, and muscle-specific DOMS after the Cindy WOD.

RESULTS: Condition effects survived FDR control for VJH and 19 of 22 dynamometry outcomes. Across assessments, VJH was 34.48 ± 5.09 cm with DC and 30.22 ± 2.34 cm with PLA (mean difference 4.27 cm, 95% CI 1.45 to 7.08; Holm-adjusted p = 0.017; g_av = 1.09). No condition-by-assessment interaction survived FDR control (all q ≥ 0.141). DOMS showed significant time effects for all three muscles, peaked at approximately 24 h, remained elevated at 48 h, and declined toward baseline by 72 h. A condition-by-time effect remained significant only for gastrocnemius soreness (Holm-adjusted p = 0.012; ηp2 = 0.212); no DOMS condition main effect or condition-by-assessment-by-time interaction was supported.

CONCLUSION: DC was associated with higher values for selected lower-limb outcomes, but these exploratory findings do not establish phase-specific efficacy, equivalent effects across cycle assessments, or a consistent DOMS benefit. Unusually large performance estimates and unmodeled period and carryover effects warrant caution.

articles.title: Effects of caffeine ingestion on endurance performance in acute hypoxic conditions: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Caffeine is a well-established aid for endurance performance under normoxic conditions. More recently, its ergogenic potential to improve endurance performance in hypoxia has attracted increasing interest, although findings remain inconsistent. This meta-analysis therefore evaluated the effects of caffeine on endurance performance under hypoxic conditions.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to December 2025 for placebo-controlled, randomized crossover studies examining the impact of caffeine on endurance performance (e.g. time-trial and time-to-exhaustion) and physiological and/or metabolic responses (e.g. blood lactate concentration, heart rate, arterial oxygen saturation, and minute ventilation) in hypoxic conditions. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Meta-analyses were conducted in R software, comparing caffeine with placebo, with pooled effects calculated as Hedge's g using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included (n = 117; female: n = 19). Caffeine significantly improved exercise performance in hypoxia, increasing exercise capacity across both time-to-exhaustion and time-trial tests (g = 0.76, 95% CI = 0.34 to 1.18, p < 0.001, low GRADE). Caffeine also increased heart rate, blood lactate concentration, and minute ventilation (g = 0.40 to 0.47, all p = 0.005, low GRADE). No significant effects were observed for ratings of perceived exertion or arterial oxygen saturation (g = -0.25 to 0.17, all p > 0.05, very low to low GRADE) under hypoxic conditions.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that caffeine enhances endurance performance in hypoxic conditions and is accompanied by changes in key physiological and metabolic responses. Consequently, caffeine supplementation may serve as a practical strategy for attenuating hypoxia-induced performance impairments in athletes training or competing at altitude. Future high-quality, rigorously designed studies are warranted to further validate these effects.

articles.title: Anthocyanin-rich black chokeberry (aronia melanocarpa) supplementation modulates exercise-induced changes in iron metabolism in female swimmers.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intense exercise may transiently alter iron metabolism through inflammatory and oxidative mechanisms. Anthocyanin-rich black chokeberry (Aronia melanocarpa) may influence these responses and short-term iron regulation. This study evaluated the effects of black chokeberry supplementation on iron metabolism, inflammation, antioxidant capacity, and hematological status in female competitive swimmers.

METHODS: Twenty-two female swimmers (13.14 ± 1.42 years) were randomly allocated to a supplementation or placebo group. Participants completed two identical swimming tests comprising 800-, 200-, and 50-m efforts before and after 57.32 ± 8.31 days of supplementation. Blood was collected before exercise, immediately after exercise, and after 3 h of recovery.

RESULTS: Most inflammatory markers showed time-dependent changes without significant group effects. C-reactive protein decreased from pre- to post-exercise during the second test in the supplemented group (p = 0.0325; Cohen's d = 1.29), whereas placebo recovery values increased between tests (p < 0.0001; Cohen's d = 3.33). Total antioxidant capacity showed a significant time × group interaction (p = 0.0007), with higher recovery values in the supplemented group. Iron, unsaturated iron-binding capacity, and total iron-binding capacity showed significant time effects (all p < 0.0001). Hepcidin also showed a significant time effect, with significant within-group increases only in the placebo group. Transferrin was lower in the supplemented group at Post II (p = 0.0071; Cohen's d = 1.17), whereas ferritin remained unchanged and hematological parameters showed no consistent between-group differences.

CONCLUSION: Black chokeberry supplementation may influence markers related to short-term post-exercise iron availability, potentially in association with inflammatory and antioxidant responses, without detectable effects on body iron stores or erythropoiesis.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NCT06486623; registration date: 2024-07-03).

articles.title: Dose-specific effects of caffeinated chewing gum on reactive blocking timing, jump mechanics, and neuromuscular responses after volleyball-specific fatigue in elite female volleyball players.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the effects of caffeinated chewing gum at nominal target doses of 3 and 6 mg/kg on reactive blocking timing, block-jump mechanics, and neuromuscular responses in elite female volleyball players under post-fatigue conditions.

METHODS: Fifteen elite female volleyball players completed a randomized, placebo-controlled crossover study implemented with double-blinding procedures. Participants consumed placebo (PLA), caffeinated chewing gum at nominal target doses of 3 mg/kg (CAF3) or 6 mg/kg (CAF6), and were tested after supplementation and warm-up at PRE and immediately after a volleyball-specific repeated blocking fatigue protocol (POST). Primary outcomes were reactive blocking timing-chain indices and block-jump (BJ) peak power. Secondary outcomes included additional BJ mechanical variables and general jump measures from countermovement jump (CMJ) and drop jump (DJ) tests. Exploratory outcomes included synchronized surface electromyography (sEMG) variables of lower-limb muscles. Participant blinding was assessed after each visit.

RESULTS: Fatigue impaired jump-related performance across conditions (p < 0.05). For the primary outcomes, the descriptive decline in BJ peak power was 6.9% in CAF6 versus 13.9% in PLA; the adjusted POST comparison did not establish superiority of CAF6 over CAF3. For timing outcomes, overall sequence time increased by 18.4% in PLA, 6.4% in CAF3, and 3.0% in CAF6; CAF6 therefore showed the smallest descriptive deterioration in the integrated sequence measure, whereas CAF3 showed little change in the mean stationary and movement component times. CAF6 showed a reduction in mean stationary response time and the smallest increase in overall sequence time. For secondary outcomes, caffeine showed more favorable post-fatigue responses in selected CMJ/DJ measures, including CMJ mean propulsive power and DJ contact time (p < 0.05), and CAF6 showed greater preservation of selected stretch-shortening cycle-related mechanical measures, including DJ jump height and DJ vertical stiffness, than PLA (p < 0.05). In contrast, CMJ mRSI showed a divergent pattern and was not interpreted as evidence of caffeine-related attenuation of fatigue-induced decrements. Exploratory sEMG results showed smaller post-fatigue changes in selected frequency-domain and activation-timing variables under CAF6, particularly in measures related to extensor-muscle function. Participant masking was incomplete: perceived caffeine ingestion was reported in 0.0%, 53.3%, and 80.0% of PLA, CAF3, and CAF6 visits, respectively, and adverse effects were more frequent in CAF6.

CONCLUSIONS: The observed responses were outcome-specific: CAF6 showed a smaller decline in BJ peak power and the smallest increase in overall sequence time, whereas CAF3 showed little change in mean stationary and movement response times. These findings do not establish a generally preferable dose or a timing-stability advantage for CAF3. Incomplete participant masking limits attribution of the differences exclusively to caffeine dose.

articles.title: Exploratory serum renal biomarker and eGFR responses to high-protein diets during resistance versus concurrent training in resistance-trained men.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High protein intake is common among resistance-trained athletes, but its association with renal biomarkers across different exercise modalities remains uncertain. This study investigated whether consuming a high-protein diet (3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹) during 16 weeks of resistance training (RT) or concurrent training (CT) affects renal biomarkers and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in resistance-trained men.

METHODS: Forty-eight resistance-trained men (26 ± 6 years; BMI 25.6 ± 2.9 kg·m⁻²) were randomized to 16 weeks of RT or CT (4 sessions·wk⁻¹) while consuming either 1.6 or 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ of protein in a 2 × 2 factorial design. Forty-four participants with complete pre- and post-intervention data were analyzed. Fasting blood samples were assessed for blood urea nitrogen (BUN), BUN/creatinine ratio, cystatin C, and eGFR calculated using the CKD-EPI creatinine (2021), cystatin C (2012), and creatinine-cystatin C (2021) equations. Within-group changes were evaluated using paired t-tests, and factorial effects were assessed using linear mixed-effects models (Time × Training × Protein).

RESULTS: No statistically significant Time × Protein or Time × Training × Protein interactions were detected for any renal biomarker or eGFR estimate (all p ≥ 0.182). No significant within-group changes occurred in the 1.6 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups (all p > 0.05). In both 3.2 g·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹ groups, BUN and cystatin C increased (all p ≤ 0.017), while eGFR estimates decreased (all p ≤ 0.009). The BUN/creatinine ratio remained unchanged (p ≥ 0.614). However, these within-group findings were descriptive because the corresponding interaction effects were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: In resistance-trained men, 16 weeks of high protein intake did not produce statistically detectable differences in renal biomarker or eGFR changes compared with moderate protein intake, irrespective of training modality. Although modest increases in BUN and cystatin C and small decreases in eGFR estimates were observed within the high-protein groups, these findings were not supported by significant factorial interactions. The limited sample size precludes excluding clinically meaningful differences, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

articles.title: Effects of extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training combined with iron supplementation versus iron supplementation alone on postural control in young women with iron deficiency anemia: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent research revealed postural control deterioration in young women with Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). To address this postural deficit, it is crucial to develop intervention strategies for postural rehabilitation in these individuals. This study aimed to explore the effect of 8-week extremely low-volume high-intensity interval training (HIIT) based on plyometric exercises combined with iron supplementation versus simple iron treatment on postural control of young women with IDA.

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial enrolled young women with IDA aged 18-25 years, who were randomly assigned to a training group (TG; n = 16) or a non-training group (NTG; n = 17). All participants received oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulfate, 494.5 mg/day, administered as 247.25 mg twice daily), while the TG additionally completed an 8-week extremely low-volume HIIT program based on plyometric exercises. Hemoglobin (Hb) and serum ferritin concentrations were assessed, alongside muscle endurance, reaction time performance, and postural control. Muscle endurance was evaluated using the Killy test, reaction time performance using an online simple reaction time test, and postural control using a stabilometric platform under bipodal and semi-tandem stance conditions. Postural assessments were conducted with eyes open (EO) and eyes closed (EC) on firm and foam surfaces. All outcomes were measured at baseline and 72 h after the final intervention session.

RESULTS: After the 8-week intervention, this study demonstrated significant improvements across both groups, irrespective of the intervention. However, TG showed significantly greater post-intervention improvements than NTG in Hb concentration (P = 0.042), muscle endurance (P < 0.001), and postural control. Superior postural control in TG was observed during a bipedal stance on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.001); EC: P = 0.035), as well as during semi-tandem stance on a firm surface (EO: P = 0.015; EC: P = 0.040) and on a foam surface (EO: P = 0.019; EC: P = 0.003), compared to the NTG. With a Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold for multiple comparisons (α = 0.00625), between-group differences in postural control remained significant for bipedal foam EO (P = 0.001) and semi-tandem foam EC (P = 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: The study showed that women with IDA improved their postural performance regardless of the intervention used. However, an 8-week program of extremely low-volume HIIT combined with plyometric exercises and iron supplementation had a more beneficial effect compared to traditional iron therapy. These greater improvements in postural control occurred alongside greater improvements in the Hb concentration and muscle endurance in the TG compared to the NTG.

articles.title: Is plant-based protein supplementation as effective as whey protein? A systematic review and meta-analysis in untrained adults undergoing resistance training.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dietary protein supplements are commonly consumed to support increases in lean body mass among healthy adults engaged in resistance training (RT). Although whey protein has been extensively investigated, plant-based protein supplements have emerged as a viable alternative for individuals who avoid animal-derived products.

METHODS: The present study aims to evaluate, through a systematic review and meta-analysis, the effects of plant-based versus whey protein supplementation on body composition in untrained adults (18-59 years) undergoing RT, using Dual-Energy X-Ray Absorptiometry (DEXA). The systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 checklist and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251145410). Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, identifying 5 studies that met the inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis and meta-analysis.

RESULTS: When combined with RT, both plant-based and whey protein supplementation were associated with improvements in lean body mass (LBM) and body fat mass (BFM), with no significant between-group differences observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Thus, soy- and pea-based protein supplements may support favorable body composition changes in adults initiating RT and could be considered practical nutritional options for individuals seeking alternatives to whey protein. Regarding chia-based protein, the available evidence is currently limited to a single study that did not demonstrate significant changes in lean body mass; therefore, firm conclusions regarding its efficacy cannot be drawn at this time.

articles.title: Hematological and biochemical responses to three doses of caffeine during the CrossFit® workout: a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study investigated the effects of three doses of caffeine (CAF) on hematological and biochemical responses during the CrossFit® workout, a protocol known to induce significant physiological fluctuations.

METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo (PLA)-controlled crossover trial, 26 moderately trained CrossFit® athletes received acute doses of 3, 6, or 9 mgCAF/kgbody mass (BM), or a PLA, 70 min before a 17-min CrossFit® workout.

RESULTS: While exercise was the predominant driver of hematological changes, with no CAF-specific modulation of blood cell indices, significant treatment × time point interactions were observed solely for glucose concentration. Specifically, MEDIUM (6 mgCAF/kgBM) and HIGH (9 mgCAF/kgBM) CAF doses produced significantly greater post-exercise glucose elevations compared to baseline and PLA visits. Phosphates concentrations increased over time, particularly post-exercise, with no treatment effect retained after excluding baseline visit in the sensitivity analysis. Calcium level dynamics were influenced by temporal factors rather than CAF, and magnesium concentration remained stable.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that acute CAF ingestion selectively influences post-exercise glucose responses during the CrossFit® workout, whereas hematological variables and most biochemical markers remain unaffected. Significant post-exercise glucose elevations were observed following the 6 and 9 mgCAF/kgBM conditions compared with baseline and PLA visits, while serum mineral concentrations remained largely stable across treatments.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: NCT03822663.

articles.title: Acute caffeine and carbohydrate strategies for fatigue-related sport-specific performance in team-sport athletes: a systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although caffeine and carbohydrate are established ergogenic strategies for physical performance, it remains unclear whether these benefits translate to the decision-making and sport-specific skills that determine team-sport performance under fatigue.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, and SPORTDiscus were searched on 28 July 2026. Thirty-one reports were retained; their reported analyzed sample sizes summed to 441 athletes. Twenty-three independent quantitative study clusters, with reported analyzed sample sizes summing to 341 athletes, contributed 67 effects. Multilevel random-effects models nested effect sizes within studies; primary assumptions were r = 0.5 and rho = 0.80. Inference used CR2 robust standard errors and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom.

RESULTS: Soccer supplied 11 of the 23 quantitative clusters; every other sport category supplied four or fewer. Broad caffeine was centered near zero (Hedges' g = 0.040, 95% CI -0.211 to 0.291; p = 0.691; df = 4.41). Tier 1a perceptual-motor and Tier 1b technical/tactical estimates were imprecise. Broad carbohydrate was positive but uncertain (g = 0.256, 95% CI -0.094 to 0.605; p = 0.118; df = 4.96), and one study cluster materially influenced this estimate. All six GRADE comparisons were rated very low certainty. The two-study mental-fatigue calculation was too fragile for conventional inference.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support assuming that the established physical ergogenic effects of caffeine translate to fatigue-related decision-making or sport-specific skill. Carbohydrate may provide a small benefit, but the evidence remains sparse and highly uncertain. Sensitivity to study composition was driven primarily by one influential cluster, whose omission increased the pooled estimate. The carbohydrate estimates apply only to heterogeneous ingested-beverage protocols and should not be extrapolated to mouth-rinse or gel strategies. Parallel syntheses do not establish intervention superiority or combined-strategy synergy.

articles.title: Selective recovery effects of short-term beetroot juice supplementation after exercise-induced muscle damage in trained female volleyball players.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Beetroot juice (BRJ) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), but evidence in female team-sport athletes is limited. It also remains unclear whether any benefit extends across functional, pain-related, swelling, and strength outcomes.

METHODS: Seventeen female university volleyball players entered a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Four did not complete the second period, so outcomes were analyzed with linear mixed models. After baseline testing, participants performed 200 loaded vertical jumps and consumed BRJ or placebo at 24, 48, and 72 h post-EIMD. Recovery outcomes were countermovement jump (CMJ) height, volleyball-specific agility time, pressure pain threshold, thigh circumference, visual analog scale soreness, and knee isokinetic measures. Holm-adjusted planned contrasts were used.

RESULTS: CMJ height was the clearest BRJ-related functional finding. The treatment × time interaction showed a trend toward statistical significance (P = 0.062), and CMJ height was higher under BRJ than PLA at 72 h post-EIMD (P = 0.033, d = 1.01). Calf pressure pain threshold also favored BRJ at 72 h, accompanied by a significant treatment × time interaction (P < 0.001). In contrast, agility time and soreness changed over time without clear between-condition differences, while thigh pressure pain threshold, thigh circumference, and low-velocity knee isokinetic outcomes showed no consistent BRJ-related advantage.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term BRJ supplementation was associated with selective rather than generalized recovery benefits after EIMD in trained female volleyball players. The clearest findings were higher CMJ height and calf PPT under BRJ than PLA at 72 h, whereas the remaining outcomes showed no consistent treatment-related differences.

articles.title: Pre-sleep milk-derived proteins do not impair sleep or recovery in elite female athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep is essential for athlete recovery and performance, yet athletes frequently experience restricted or poor-quality sleep. Pre-sleep feeding (PSF) has emerged as a strategy to support recovery, but randomized, double-blinded, crossover trials comparing PSF macronutrient options on objective and subjective sleep outcomes in elite female athletes remain limited.

METHODS: Twenty-five National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I female athletes (18-25 years old) were recruited; 21 completed the trial. In a randomized, double-blinded, placebo controlled, crossover design conducted over 4-8 weeks, participants consumed four treatments for three consecutive nights each: 40 g casein protein (CAS; 160 kcal), 40 g α-lactalbumin protein (ALA; 160 kcal), 40 g carbohydrate (CHO; 160 kcal), and 40g of a placebo (PLA; 5 kcal), with a minimum three-day washout between conditions. Supplements were consumed ~2 h after the final meal and ~30 min before bedtime as the last caloric intake of the day. Objective outcomes were obtained from the WHOOP 4.0 device (total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), sleep efficiency (SE), resting heart rate (RHR), and heart rate variability (HRV)). Subjective outcomes were assessed each morning via questionnaires (subjective sleep quality (SSQ), subjective sleep onset latency (SSOL), and subjective recovery (SREC)). Nocturnal interstitial glucose was assessed via blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in a subset (n = 6). Sleep and recovery variables were analyzed using one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate treatment effects across the four supplementation conditions. For CGM data, a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate main effects of treatment and time, as well as the treatment × time interaction. Tukey's post hoc testing was used with significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: No significant treatment effects were observed for TST, SOL, SE, RHR, or HRV (p > 0.05). TST ranged from 7.47-7.62 h, SE from 91.5-92.0%, RHR from 53.5-54.1 bpm, and HRV from 98.2-103.9 ms across conditions. No significant treatment effects were detected for SSQ, SSOL, or SREC (p > 0.05); SSQ ranged from 69-75%, SSOL from 16-20 min, and SREC from 61-66%. In the CGM sub-analysis, a main effect of time was observed for nocturnal glucose (p = 0.008), but no differences among treatments (p = 0.187) or a time × treatment interaction (p = 0.550) were detected.

CONCLUSIONS: In NCAA Division I female athletes, three consecutive nights of pre-sleep ingestion of CAS, ALA, or CHO did not impair objective or subjective measures of sleep or recovery compared with PLA. These findings demonstrate that pre-sleep feeding, regardless of macronutrient type, can be incorporated without negatively affecting sleep quality or recovery metrics.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: STUDY00004409).

articles.title: Placebo effects of caffeine on sport performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A body of research has shown that deceptively administering a placebo described as caffeine can significantly improve sport performance. We aimed to synthesize and estimate the effect size of the deceptive administration of a placebo described as caffeine on sport performance outcomes (e.g. bench press, cycling time-trial, repeated sprint).

METHODS: We searched for studies sampling healthy adults from database creation to July 2026. The standardized mean difference (d) between placebo caffeine and baseline was calculated and Cochrane's risk of bias assessment was used.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included. Nine studies were judged to be of high-risk of bias and eight unclear. Random-effect models revealed a small-to-moderate effect of placebo caffeine benefiting performance (d = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.28 to 0.69) and meta-regressions indicated that pooled effects were more likely to be greater when researchers were blinded (b = 0.52 ± 0.24, 95% CI = 0.01 to 0.99) and in studies sampling more males (b = -0.93 ± 0.38, 95% CI = -1.68 to -0.19).

DISCUSSION: Data highlight that placebo effects of caffeine can significantly affect sport performance with a pooled effect estimate suggesting a small-to-moderate effect. However, as per the GRADE assessment, the overall quality of evidence was low. As such, given the high risk of bias across all studies and the variation in confidence interval, stronger research designs are needed to examine placebo effects of caffeine, whereby researchers are blinded to treatment administration and allocation concealment. No funding was received for the review and the protocol can be found here: doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/W8KY6.

articles.title: Short-term Rhodiola rosea supplementation improves premenstrual symptoms, reaction time, and perceived exertion in female taekwondo athletes: a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premenstrual symptoms may negatively influence psychological readiness, cognitive-motor performance, and perceived exertion in female athletes. Rhodiola rosea (RR) is an adaptogenic herb that has been investigated for its potential effects on fatigue, stress tolerance, mood, and exercise-related outcomes. However, its effects on premenstrual symptoms and performance-related responses in female athletes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of short-term RR supplementation during the estimated symptomatic premenstrual phase on premenstrual symptoms, peripheral serum serotonin and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) concentrations, reaction time, perceived exertion, and aerobic performance-related indices in female taekwondo athletes with premenstrual syndrome (PMS).

METHODS: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 24 female taekwondo athletes with moderate-to-severe PMS symptoms were randomly assigned to receive either 500 mg/day of standardised RR extract (n = 12) or placebo (n = 12) for 10 days during the estimated symptomatic premenstrual phase. Premenstrual symptoms were assessed using the Premenstrual Symptoms Screening Tool (PSST). Visual reaction time, peripheral serum serotonin and GABA concentrations, time to exhaustion (TTE), estimated VO₂max, and rating of perceived exertion (RPE) were evaluated before and after the intervention. Data were analysed using analysis of covariance with baseline values as covariates.

RESULTS: Compared with placebo, RR supplementation significantly reduced several PMS symptoms, including irritability, depression, anxiety, social withdrawal, decreased concentration, hypersomnia, food cravings, crying, skin problems, and abdominal pain (p < 0.05). The RR group demonstrated faster reaction time compared with placebo (adjusted mean difference: -60 ms; p < 0.001). Peripheral serum serotonin and GABA concentrations were significantly higher in the RR group than in the placebo group (p < 0.001). In addition, RR supplementation reduced post-exercise RPE (adjusted mean difference: -1.40 Borg units; p = 0.006). However, no significant differences were observed between groups in TTE or estimated VO₂max (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Short-term RR supplementation during the estimated symptomatic premenstrual phase may improve selected PMS symptoms, visual reaction time, and perceived exertion in female taekwondo athletes with PMS. Larger trials with hormonal confirmation of menstrual cycle phase, longer intervention periods, direct physiological measurements, and sport-specific performance assessments are required to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Impact of different protein sources on acute muscle protein synthesis following resistance training: a systematic review with standard and dose-response network meta-analyses.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of protein intake and resistance training (RT) plays a pivotal role in stimulating muscle protein synthesis (MPS), yet the impact of different protein sources remains an area of active investigation. Therefore, a systematic review incorporating standard and dose‒response network meta-analyses was performed.

METHODS: Systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, EBSCOhost (including MEDLINE, SPORTDiscus, CINAHL), and Scopus. Eligible studies included healthy adults (≥18 years) who were undergoing acute resistance exercise followed by a single protein bolus (any type or dose, except blends or enriched with anabolic agents). Muscle biopsies were required before and after RT/protein intake without additional food in between. Trials measuring hourly MPS rates via tracer techniques were included (n = 51).

RESULTS: In the standard network meta-analysis (NMA), native whey (P-score = 0.81, MD = 0.05% [0.00; 0.10]), pea protein (0.77, MD = 0.05% [-0.02; 0.11]), whole egg protein (0.72, MD = 0.04% [-0.01; 0.09]), mycoprotein (0.66, MD = 0.03% [-0.02; 0.08]), and whey protein (0.58, MD = 0.02% [0.01; 0.04]) ranked highest for estimated efficacy in stimulating post-RT hourly MPS (in descending order) (only whey protein showed a statistically significant effect) with low to moderate certainty of evidence. Dose‒response NMA revealed that certain animal- (native whey and whole egg protein) and plant- (pea and mycoprotein) based protein sources to show the highest predicted MPS responses with doses of 18-25 g.

CONCLUSIONS: Animal- (native whey, whey, whole egg) and plant-based (pea, mycoprotein) proteins ranked similarly for estimated acute MPS stimulation when combined with RT; however, only whey protein showed a statistically significant effect, and protein sources represented by few studies should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Dose-dependent effects of sodium bicarbonate supplementation combined with sprint interval training on performance adaptations in basketball players: a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sprint interval training (SIT) effectively improves physical performance in team-sport athletes, while sodium bicarbonate (Sb) supplementation may enhance training adaptations. However, the dose-dependent effects of Sb during SIT remain unclear in basketball players. Therefore, this study examined the effects of two Sb doses combined with SIT on physical performance adaptations in basketball players.

METHODS: Forty trained male basketball players (age: 21.6 ± 2.0 years, height: 185.4 ± 3.5 cm, body mass: 84.1 ± 4.4 kg) were recruited and randomly assigned to four groups: SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb (n = 10), SIT + placebo (PL) (n = 10), and control (CON) (n = 10). The intervention lasted four weeks during the preparatory phase of the season. Participants in the training groups performed SIT three times per week in addition to their regular basketball training. The SIT protocol consisted of four sets of ten 5-second maximal sprints, with 20 seconds of active recovery between repetitions and 2 minutes of rest between sets. All 40 enrolled participants successfully completed the 4-week intervention, resulting in a 0% dropout rate. Performance assessments conducted before and after the intervention included countermovement vertical jump (CMVJ), standing long jump (SLJ), 20 m sprint, Illinois change-of-direction speed (CODS), Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (Yo-Yo IR1), and Wingate anaerobic power (peak power output [PPO] and mean power output [MPO]).

RESULTS: All training groups showed significant improvements in physical performance variables over time (p < 0.05). Significant group by time interaction effects were observed for all performance variables (p ≤ 0.001), indicating that the SIT groups showed more gains compared with the CON group. Both Sb supplementation groups demonstrated greater improvements than the SIT + PL group in CMVJ, SLJ, sprint performance, CODS, Yo-Yo IR1 distance, PPO, and MPO (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the SIT + 0.45 g·kg-1 Sb group exhibited significantly greater performance enhancements than the SIT + 0.3 g·kg-1 Sb group across all measured variables.

CONCLUSION: Four weeks of SIT improved performance in trained basketball players, with Sb supplementation providing additional dose-dependent benefits (0.45 > 0.3 g⋅kg-1). While the higher dose yielded superior adaptations, its practical application should be balanced against potential gastrointestinal discomfort and individual tolerance to ensure long-term athlete compliance.

articles.title: Acute effects of 3 and 6 mg·Kg-1 caffeine on strength-power performance and isokinetic peak torque in competitive male boxers: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on the dose, timing, and task specificity of caffeine ingestion in combat-sport athletes remains limited. This study examined the acute effects of 3 and 6 mg·kg-1 caffeine on strength-power performance and isokinetic peak torque in male boxers.
