This phenomenon is frequently found in patients with cognitive impairment and has been attributed to frontal lobe dysfunction, although a direct correlation has not been established. This study aimed to explore the correlation between frontal lobe function, as assessed by functional brain imaging, and paratonia, as assessed by electromyography.

METHODS: Memory clinic outpatients with suspected Alzheimer's disease who were prescribed an amyloid PET scan underwent a thorough neuropsychological examination and a paratonia assessment involving surface electromyography recording of the elbow flexors and extensors. PET image acquisition started immediately after tracer injection, and the early phase perfusion amyloid PET was used as a surrogate biomarker of neuronal injury. Multiple regression analysis was performed on amyloid-positive patients to identify the correlation between paratonia and brain perfusion.

RESULTS: Twenty-one amyloid PET-positive participants with a median age of 72 years were diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease and included in the analysis. All participants were right-handed, and paratonia was assessed in the left arm. Whole-brain voxel-wise analysis revealed a significant inverse correlation between the total paratonia score and cortical perfusion in a cluster encompassing the superior frontal gyrus in the left hemisphere (Brodmann areas 6, 8, and 9; P  < 0.006).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates for the first time an inverse correlation between prefrontal perfusion and paratonia. Participants with better-preserved premotor function also show less paratonia, as reflected by reduced electromyographic activation of the muscles undergoing passive mobilization.

articles.title: Wound infections following snake-related injuries in Malaysia: A retrospective analysis of Remote Envenomation Consultancy Services data.
articles.journal: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
articles.abstract: Snake-related injuries (SRI) in Malaysia are a medical emergency. SRI may be accompanied by wound infection requiring medical and surgical intervention. Despite its clinical relevance, local epidemiological and microbiological data remain limited in Malaysia. This was an observational analysis conducted on 72 hospitalised patients with wound infections following snake-related injuries who received consultation from the Remote Envenomation Consultancy Services (RECS). Data were collected using a standardised collection form. Among 559 hospitalised SRI cases, 72 patients (12.9%) developed wound infections. Males accounted for 70.8%, and most patients with wound infections were young adults aged 18 to 44. The most frequent symptoms were swelling (91.7%) and erythema (69.4%). SRI from Naja species were the most frequently identified cause of wound infections. Bacterial cultures were positive in 15.3% of cases, with Enterococcus species being the most frequently identified. Amoxicillin/clavulanate was the most used antibiotic. Wound debridement was performed in 27.8% of cases. Most patients were hospitalised for more than 5 days, and the most common outcome was healed with a scar (34.7%). No mortality was reported. This study emphasises the need for accurate clinical assessments to distinguish between venom-induced inflammation and subsequent bacterial infection. Although the culture-positive rate was low, the presence of pathogens such as Enterococcus species, which are often resistant to standard antibiotics, emphasises the need for cultures and sensitivity testing in snakebite-related infections. Early antivenom therapy, adequate antibiotic usage, and prompt surgical intervention, such as debridement, will improve patient outcomes. These findings provide useful local insights for clinical guidelines and for better management of wound infections following snake-related injuries in Malaysia.

articles.title: Connectivity- and frequency-individualized accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation (aiTBS) is an effective neuromodulatory intervention for treatment resistant depression (TRD). aiTBS delivers repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation sessions over a compressed timeframe and can be individualized to specific locations using resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) to target pathological cortical networks or individualized in time using electroencephalography (EEG) to determine optimal participant-specific stimulation frequencies. In this randomized, placebo-controlled trial, we tested these forms of personalization against sham stimulation. Fifty-one patients with TRD were randomized to one of three arms; 43 completed the protocol per pre-specified criteria and assigned to one of three arms: (1) fMRI-connectivity-individualized aiTBS; (2) frequency- and connectivity-individualized aiTBS; or (3) sham aiTBS. Participants received 10 aiTBS sessions per day for five consecutive days with clinical assessments at baseline, and 1 and 4 weeks post-treatment. The primary outcome was change in depression severity on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale from baseline to 1 week post-treatment. Anhedonia severity measured with the Dimensional Anhedonia Rating Scale was a secondary outcome. No significant differences were observed between active and sham arms on primary MADRS or secondary DARS endpoints for either the intent-to-treat or per-protocol sample. Remission and response rates also did not differ between arms. aiTBS individualized using either rs-fMRI or EEG and rs-fMRI failed to yield significant antidepressant benefits over sham stimulation, with relatively muted overall therapeutic benefits, underscoring the need for further clinical trials evaluating the efficacy of personalized aiTBS in TRD.

articles.title: ETAS reduces wake time after sleep onset in healthy adults who are dissatisfied with their sleep: A randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover study.
articles.abstract: Poor sleep quality is strongly associated with health indicators. Specifically, it increases the risk of developing diseases, including coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes. Our preliminary study suggested that ETAS, a standardized extract of Asparagus officinalis stem, may enhance the proportion of N3, a stage of deep sleep. In this study, we conducted an expanded, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind crossover study to investigate the effect of ETAS on N3 appearance. The study included 38 healthy adult participants with sleep dissatisfaction. Intervention periods involved administration of either placebo or ETAS (300 mg/day as ETAS50) for 14 days, with a 14-day washout period between periods. The primary endpoints were the proportion of N3 sleep after the intervention, as determined by electroencephalogram (EEG) analysis. Secondary endpoints included sleep parameters indices other than the proportion of N3 as determined by EEG analysis after the intervention, as well as OSA-MA and AIS-J scores. 14-day ETAS intake did not result in a statistically significant difference in the proportion of N3. In contrast, wake time after sleep onset (WASO) and the total time of N1 significantly decreased. In addition, ETAS intake improved the following scores for AIS: total score, "awakenings during the night" and "functioning capacity during the day". Furthermore, post-hoc analysis revealed that ETAS intake significantly reduced WASO in individuals who originally had high WASO and significantly improved sleep efficiency in individuals with low sleep efficiency. These results suggest that ETAS may regulate sleep quality in accordance with the individual's sleep stage balance.

articles.title: Rapid screening of physicochemical compatibility between co-administered injectable drugs using thermal and spectroscopic approaches.
articles.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
articles.abstract: The concomitant administration of injectable drugs in hospital settings frequently involves extemporaneous combinations within the same infusion line, often without compatibility evaluation. This practice may compromise drug stability and patient safety, particularly in intensive care units characterized by complex polypharmacy regimens. In this study, a rapid screening protocol based on complementary thermal, spectroscopic, and morphological techniques was applied to investigate potential physicochemical interactions between injectable drugs under accelerated stress conditions. Dopamine, ondansetron, rocuronium, and fluconazole were combined pairwise as binary physical mixtures and subjected to controlled thermal and photonic stress. Differential scanning calorimetry, thermogravimetric analysis, FTIR spectroscopy, and stereomicroscopy were employed to detect early physicochemical interactions and stress-induced instability. Thermal analysis revealed melting point shifts, enthalpy reduction, amorphization, and premature degradation events for several combinations, indicating different levels of intermolecular interaction. FTIR and morphological analyses demonstrated that some changes in thermal profile were accompanied by chemically relevant alterations and progressive discoloration, particularly after combined thermal and light exposure. Dopamine/fluconazole and dopamine/ondansetron mixtures showed evidence of moderate solid-state interaction, while ondansetron/fluconazole exhibited increased susceptibility to stress-induced instability. Mixtures containing rocuronium exhibited greater sensitivity to combined thermal and photonic stress, especially ondansetron/rocuronium, which showed marked light-dependent instability. Overall, the proposed approach proved useful as a rapid preliminary risk-ranking strategy to identify injectable drug combinations requiring further compatibility investigation under clinically relevant conditions.

articles.title: Construction of a sensitive fluorescent probe for convenient hippuric acid and nitrofurazone/nitrofurantoin antibiotics detection based on stable Mn-MOF.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Chemical solvents and antibiotics have been extensively utilized in our daily life. However, the excessive accumulation could cause illness and threaten public health. The accurate monitoring of chemical solvents and antibiotics is critical to hinder their accumulation and mitigate detrimental effects on human health. Herein, a new fluorescent metal-organic framework (MOF) has been designed based on a mixed-ligand method. The designed XYNU-2 features a (4,6)-connected {44·610·8}{44·62} topology, which holds comparatively high chemical stability in water or under varying aqueous pH conditions. Fluorescence spectral studies reveal that XYNU-2 demonstrates exciting photoluminescent properties, and can be served as a versatile multi-target chemosensor for toluene metabolite hippuric acid (HA) and nitrofurazone (NFZ) and nitrofurantoin (NFT) antibiotics through photoluminescence "turn-on" and "turn-off" effects, respectively. Notably, the established methods are labeled with fast response, high sensitivity, wide response concentration range, and importantly, good selectivity in water phase. Detailed mechanistic investigations have substantiated that the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) mechanism is the key determinant in the case of "turn on" response toward HA, while the fluorescence "turn off" mechanisms for monitoring NFZ/NFT involve a synergistic interplay between dynamic PET, the inner filter effect (IFE) and fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET). This research might shed light on the rational construction of MOF-based multi-target fluorescent sensors with high selectivity and sensitivity.

articles.title: A robust cd-based coordination polymer with high sensitivity for fluorescent detection of cefixime in environmental water and milk samples.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Antibiotic misuse and residues can disrupt ecological balance and compromise food safety, making the development of highly selective and sensitive antibiotic detection methods crucial. In this study, a two-dimensional cadmium-based coordination polymer {[Cd₃(ndda)₃(bpy)₁.₅(H₂O)₃]·H₂O} (CP 1) was successfully synthesized via a solvothermal method and applied for the detection of the widely used antibiotic cefixime (CEX). The structure of CP 1 was systematically characterized using multiple analytical techniques, and its fluorescence properties were investigated. The results demonstrate that CP 1 can rapidly (within 1 min) and selectively identify CEX in aqueous solution even in the presence of interfering substances. The material not only exhibits an excellent detection limit (8.49 nM) but also can be reused for up to five cycles. Based on the structural features of CP 1 and experimental evidence, the fluorescence quenching mechanism is proposed to involve a synergistic effect of competitive absorption (CA) and photoinduced electron transfer (PET). Furthermore, when applied to the detection of CEX in environmental water and milk samples, CP 1 achieved satisfactory recovery rates and low relative standard deviations. This study confirms that CP 1, as a fluorescent probe material, holds significant potential for CEX detection in food safety monitoring and environmental analysis.

articles.title: A cucurbit[6]uril-based supramolecular assembly as a sensitive fluorescent Sensor for detecting sunset yellow in beverages.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Employing 1,3,5-benzenetricarboxylic acid (H3BTC) as a structure-directing agent, a novel three-dimensional supramolecular framework, {[NH2(CH3)2][Zn(BTC)(H2O)]·(CB (Cai et al., 2019 [6]))0.5·4H2O}n (CB[6]-BTC-Zn), was successfully constructed via a solvothermal reaction involving cucurbit[6]uril (CB (Cai et al., 2019 [6])), H3BTC, and Zn(II) ion. CB[6]-BTC-Zn emits intense blue fluorescence and exhibits remarkable structure stability in aqueous media; and further it functions as an efficient turn-off fluorescent sensor, enabling highly sensitive and selective detection of a food colorant sunset yellow (SY) with a limit of detection as low as 8.48 × 10-7 M. CB[6]-BTC-Zn can maintain excellent performance even in the presence of some food additives, showcasing its good anti-interference capability. The underlying mechanism for sensing SY involves a synergistic three-step process, an initial electrostatic enrichment of anionic SY molecules on the positively charged assembly surface, following an efficient fluorescence resonance energy transfer process facilitated by significant spectral overlap, and ultimately, a dual-channel photoinduced electron transfer (PET) pathway encompassing both donor and acceptor PET process, as confirmed by the density functional theory calculations. Furthermore, this material was processed into flexible sensing films and functionalized LED devices to achieve a visual SY identification, and it also was successfully applied to the spiked recovery detection of SY in actual beverage samples (recovery rates: 95.43-105.62%). This work offers a strategy for designing cucurbituril-based functional materials for rapid monitoring colorants in the field of food safety.

articles.title: A novel dual-lock-dual-key naphthalimide-based fluorescent probe for the detection of H2S and H2O2.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: H2S and H2O2 participate in various biochemical reactions as active signaling molecules and maintain cellular homeostasis during oxidative stress. Current methods for detecting H2S and H2O2 mostly rely on their respective single-detection systems, while the research on dual-detection systems for both substances remains less explored. Herein, we rationally constructed a new naphthalimide-based fluorescence probe P1 for the simultaneous detection of H2S and H2O2 using the dual-lock strategy. P1 consists of naphthalimide fluorephore, the disulfide bond-containing ferrocene (first lock) and the boronic acid pinacol ester (second lock), which undergoes dual-locked control mediated by ICT and PET mechanisms, resulting in significant quenching of its green fluorescence. Only when H2S and H2O2 coexist to form a molecular "AND" logic gate, the boronic acid pinacol ester in P1 reacts with H2O2 to generate a hydroxyl group, and H2S cleaves the disulfide bond to release the ferrocene moiety, leading to the activated ICT effect and the interruption of the PET process, which prominently enhances the green fluorescence of P1. Moreover, P1 has excellent fluorescence imaging capabilities, enabling it to simultaneously investigate the level fluctuations of H2S and H2O2 in living cells.

articles.title: Application of far-infrared spectroscopy for prediction of silicate mineral content in claystones and clay shales.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Attenuated total reflectance Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FT-IR) in far-infrared (FIR) region combined with partial least squares regression (PLSR) was coupled for the quantitative determination of silicate minerals (chlorite, albite, muscovite, and quartz) in claystones and clay shales. A total of sixty-six samples were employed in this study, including forty-nine calibration samples and seventeen validation samples. FIR spectra were acquired under ambient laboratory conditions, without vacuum or controlled atmospheres. Rietveld-refined X-ray diffraction (XRD) data were used as the reference method for creation of PLSR models. The PLSR models exhibited strong predictive performance (with root mean square error of prediction values below 3.6 wt%). The accuracy of PLSR models was confirmed by three statistical tests. Apart from the chlorite prediction model, the models for prediction of quartz, muscovite, and albite demonstrated excellent precision (confirmed by repeatability testing). The study demonstrated that the combination of ATR-FT-IR spectroscopy in the far-infrared region with PLSR can serve as a rapid and reliable alternative method for predicting the mineral composition of sedimentary rocks.

articles.title: Triphenylamine-derived fluorescent probe: Synthesis and lipid droplet polarity imaging analysis.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Lipid droplets are important parts of cells. They store lipids. They also help control cell balance. Notably, there exists a strong correlation between lipid droplet polarity and the progression of NAFLD. Accordingly, tracking variations in lipid droplet polarity permits the staged assessment of NAFLD. In this study, we picked triphenylamine as the electron donor. We used thiophene as the π-bridge. We also chose benzofuran as the electron acceptor. On this basis, a novel fluorescent probe (MDN) with a typical D-π-A architecture was rationally designed and synthesized for polarity detection. Specifically, the MDN probe showed special fluorescence when the environment was less polar. It had high sensitivity and good selectivity. Meanwhile, MDN had a big Stokes shift of 70 nm and its maximum fluorescence emission wavelength was over 600 nm in the test, which possess excellent optical properties Confocal imaging showed that the MDN probe matched well with intracellular structures. Also, the ClogP value of MDN was 10.876, indicating its favorable capability for lipid droplet targeting. Another study demonstrated that MDN can be used to monitor the changes of intracellular polarity. The experimental results verified that lipid droplet accumulation in liver tissues was significantly higher than that in other organs, accompanied by intense fluorescence signals. In summary, the polarity-responsive probe developed in this work possesses excellent targeting capability toward lipid droplets.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal tracking of cysteine fluctuations during organelle interactions with a lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Cysteine (Cys) is a crucial amino acid and plays a protective role for cells by eliminating superfluous endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS). Organelle interactions are consistently carried out during cellular physiological and pathological activities, and Cys levels change concomitantly with cell viability. Nevertheless, the dynamic fluctuations of Cys during organelle interactions remain largely unexplored to date. To address this issue, we developed a lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe, CSDC, by conjugating a 2,4-dinitrobenzenesulfonyl (DNBS) group onto a coumarin fluorophore, thereby achieving real-time imaging of Cys dynamics during mitochondrial and lysosomal fusion. The fluorescence of CSDC can be lightened by inhibiting the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) effect, and high sensitivity of 19 nM was achieved for CSDC. Leveraging the excellent fluorescence performance of CSDC, endogenous Cys under different cellular state was sensitively imaged. Furthermore, fluorescence imaging results exhibited that the content of Cys increased distinctly at the initial stage of mitophagy because of the cytoprotective effect, then gradually reduced to equilibrium during the following organelle interaction. This work not only provide a practically useful tool for sensing Cys, but also offered a direction in revealing the dynamic change of active molecule during organelle interaction with fluorescent probe.

articles.title: A lipid droplet-targeted viscosity-sensitive fluorescent probe for visualization of tumor and NAFLD imaging.
articles.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and tumors remain major clinical challenges, characterized by aberrant lipid droplets (LDs) accumulation and elevated microenvironmental viscosity as key pathological features. In this study, we developed a series of carbazole-based fluorescent probes, LJL1-LJL6. Through systematic screening of their photophysical properties and bioimaging performance, LJL1 was identified as the optimal candidate due to its superior viscosity sensitivity and LDs-targeting specificity. Specifically, LJL1, featuring a carbazole-thiophene electron-donating unit and a pyridine-based electron acceptor, exhibited an approximately 29-fold fluorescence enhancement in pure glycerol compared to water, with a robust linear correlation between fluorescence intensity and viscosity. Moreover, probe LJL1 demonstrated excellent photostability, low cytotoxicity, and exceptional LDs-targeting specificity. In biological applications, leveraging its wash-free imaging advantage, LJL1 successfully enabled real-time monitoring of dynamic LDs viscosity fluctuations under various physiological and pathological conditions, including oleic acid (OA) stimulation, starvation, pharmacological interventions, inflammatory responses, and ferroptosis. Furthermore, probe LJL1 exhibited outstanding spatiotemporal dynamic tracking capability for the lipophagy process. Mouse imaging studies revealed that LJL1 not only allowed imaging of 4 T1 tumor models but also sensitively monitored increased viscosity in liver tissues of NAFLD models, significantly distinguishing diseased livers from healthy ones. Collectively, this study establishes LJL1 as a high-performance LDs-targeted viscosity probe with substantial potential for mechanistic research of metabolic diseases.

articles.title: In Vivo Topographic Associations Between Tau Pathology, Atrophy, and Symptom Domains in Patients With Progressive Supranuclear Palsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a 4-repeat tauopathy characterized by subcortical atrophy and distinctive motor impairments. Although tau pathology is believed to drive neuronal loss, the spatial relationships among tau deposition, regional atrophy, and domain-specific symptoms remain incompletely understood. We aimed to determine how the topographic distribution of tau pathology and regional brain atrophy relate to distinct motor symptom domains in PSP and to clarify their contributions to clinical manifestations.

METHODS: A single-center, cross-sectional study was conducted. Patients with PSP were recruited after diagnosis at neurology departments and were referred to our institution. All PSP cases underwent neurologic assessments, including PSP Rating Scale. Tau PET imaging with florzolotau (18F) and T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging were obtained from patients and healthy controls to assess associations between domain scores, tau accumulation, and regional brain volumes. Path analysis was used to examine whether cross-sectional associations were consistent with hypothesized relationships among tau deposits, regional atrophy, and symptom domains.

RESULTS: Fifty-eight patients with PSP (mean age, 71.6 years; 43.1% female; Richardson syndrome, n = 43) and 52 healthy controls (mean age, 60.8 years; 45.3% female) were included. Subcortical tau accumulation and atrophy demonstrated significant spatial overlap and were associated with motor deficits. "Ocular motor" domain scores were associated with tau deposition in the midbrain tegmentum and globus pallidus. "Gait and midline" domain scores were associated with tau in the globus pallidus, thalamus, and subthalamic nucleus. "Limb motor" domain scores were associated with tau in the primary motor and somatosensory cortices, as well as atrophy in the angular, supramarginal, and temporal cortices. These findings were identified at a family-wise error-corrected cluster-level threshold of p < 0.05. Path analysis indicated that tau in subcortical structures was associated with local neuronal loss and with impairments in the ocular motor and gait and midline domains.

DISCUSSION: High-contrast tau imaging clarifies the neuropathologic basis of key symptoms and underscores distinct tau-induced neurotoxic effects in subcortical vs neocortical regions. Specifically, tau deposition in the neocortex may contribute to limb motor impairments through local effects and potentially through more distributed neurodegenerative processes. These findings support anatomically distinct tau-neurodegeneration pathways underlying key PSP symptom domains.

articles.title: The Burden of Neurologic Disorders in Canada, 1990-2023: A Systematic Analysis in the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Neurologic disorders are leading contributors to global disability and mortality, yet Canada-specific burden estimates have not been updated with the most recent Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data. We aimed to quantify the burden of 18 neurologic conditions in Canada in 2023, characterize trends from 1990 to 2023, describe age-specific and sex-specific patterns, and compare Canada with the high-income country average.

METHODS: This retrospective epidemiologic modeling study analyzed GBD 2023 data for Canada. Eighteen conditions whose primary health loss manifestation directly affects the central or peripheral nervous system were included. Outcome measures included prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) comprising years lived with disability (YLDs) and years of life lost (YLL). Age-standardized rates are all per 100,000 population. 95% uncertainty intervals (UI) are reported for all estimates.

RESULTS: Modeling evaluated the entire Canadian population across 34 years. In 2023, neurologic disorders accounted for 11.48% (UI: 9.47-14.26) of total DALYs and 16.31% (UI: 10.56-26.24) of deaths. Burden was heavily driven by nonfatal disability metrics (YLDs); Alzheimer disease and other dementias led absolute DALYs at 366,548.5 (UI: 180,491.8-710,281.4), followed by migraine at 232,619.5 (UI: 151,390.4-320,391.1) and ischemic stroke at 223,748.0 (UI: 194,981.3-249,309.6). Migraine led age-standardized DALY rates at 565.8 (UI: 374.0-783.1) per 100,000, driven entirely by nonfatal disability metrics. Dementias drove mortality with 20,108.6 (UI: 4,999.6-50,266.6) deaths. From 1990 to 2023, the steepest age-standardized DALY rate increases occurred in other neurologic disorders (153.6% [UI: 129.0-185.1]), encephalitis (59.2% [UI: 25.1-95.6]), and Parkinson disease (25.4% [UI: 18.9-33.0]), while meningitis declined by 62.6% (UI: 57.4-66.9).

DISCUSSION: Neurologic disorders present a substantial public health challenge in Canada, marked by widespread midlife nonfatal disability from migraine and escalating late-life neurodegeneration. Over 3 decades, the national burden shifted toward chronic neurodegenerative diseases. These findings highlight the need for national strategies to expand care capacity and address chronic disability. A key limitation of this analysis is that GBD estimates for Canada are currently restricted to the national level; because Canada is a vast, geographically and demographically diverse nation, country-wide aggregates do not elucidate critical subnational disparities.

articles.title: APOE Genotype and Amyloid PET in People With Mild Cognitive Impairment or Dementia: Results from Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: APOE genotype is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer disease, but evidence on its utility in clinical practice is limited. We evaluated the predictive value of APOE genotype for PET-measured amyloid positivity and global amyloid burden in older adults with cognitive impairment evaluated in memory clinics as part of their clinical care. We also examined associations between APOE genotype and clinical presentation, including impairment level (mild cognitive impairment [MCI] or dementia) and MCI type (amnestic or nonamnestic).

METHODS: This observational multicenter study included Medicare beneficiaries with MCI or dementia from the Imaging Dementia-Evidence for Amyloid Scanning (IDEAS) study, who were coenrolled in the Amyloid Neuroimaging and Genetics Initiative (ANGI). Participants underwent amyloid PET and APOE genotyping. Amyloid status was determined using local visual reads and a Centiloid threshold (24.4). Logistic regression assessed associations between APOE genotype and amyloid positivity. Analysis of covariance models assessed differences in global amyloid burden (Centiloids) across genotypes. Voxel-wise analyses examined regional tracer uptake.

RESULTS: The study included 1,641 participants (mean [SD] age, 74.3 [5.6] years; 43.6% female), of whom 1,219 had MCI and 422 had dementia. APOE2/4, APOE3/4, and APOE4/4 genotypes had progressively higher odds of visual reads-based amyloid positivity compared with APOE3/3 (APOE2/4, OR = 3.10, 95% CI [1.58-6.47], p = 0.002; APOE3/4, OR = 4.52, 95% CI [3.50-5.86], p < 0.001; APOE4/4, OR = 26.34, 95% CI [12.93-63.39], p < 0.001). The results were similar when scan positivity was defined by a Centiloid threshold. Amyloid burden increased progressively across APOE genotypes, with higher-risk genotypes (APOE3/4 and APOE4/4) showing the highest Centiloids (p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.20). Among amyloid-positive participants, APOE4 genotype was associated with increased tracer uptake across posterior cingulate, precuneus, medial frontal, temporoparietal, and lateral frontal cortices in a dose-dependent manner, whereas APOE2 genotype showed a more focal distribution. A significant APOE3/4-by-sex interaction indicated higher odds of visual reads-based amyloid positivity in APOE3/4 women. Clinically, APOE4/4 was associated with dementia and amnestic MCI.

DISCUSSION: APOE4 genotype was associated with both amyloid PET positivity and quantitative amyloid burden, following a dose-dependent gradient. These findings extend evidence linking APOE genotype to amyloid pathology in clinical settings. Limitations include restriction to cognitively impaired individuals and limited racial and ethnic diversity.

articles.title: Robustness of Plasma P-Tau217 Diagnostic Thresholds for Alzheimer Disease Across Various Clinical Populations and Laboratory Environments.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs), especially plasma tau phosphorylated at threonine 217 (p-tau217), could scale Alzheimer disease (AD) clinical-biological diagnosis, but clinical use requires thresholds transferable across laboratories and populations. We compared Lumipulse p-tau217 with other BBMs; evaluated amyloid-anchored thresholds across centers, analyzers, reagent lots, and clinical populations; and assessed second-line CSF adjudication of gray zone results.

METHODS: This multicenter, cross-sectional diagnostic-classification study included an exploratory Brussels cohort and 3 external validation cohorts. Brussels participants were cognitively unimpaired or impaired and had Aβ status determined by amyloid-PET or CSF Aβ42 and tau status by tau-PET or CSF p-tau181. Validation cohorts comprised consecutive Paris memory-clinic patients, patients with early-onset neurodegenerative dementia in Bordeaux, and individuals with monogenic frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Plasma p-tau217 was measured locally on Lumipulse analyzers. BBMs and ratios were compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. In Brussels, a Youden cutoff and dual 95% or 97.5% sensitivity/specificity cutoffs were derived; intermediate values defined gray zones.

RESULTS: Among 411 participants (mean age 70.5 years; 51.6% female), p-tau217 showed the best diagnostic performance; p-tau217/Aβ42 did not improve performance or reduce gray zones. In Brussels, p-tau217 discriminated Aβ+ from Aβ- status (AUC 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.98; p < 0.0001). The 0.193 pg/mL Youden cutoff (95% CI 0.178-0.213) yielded 91.5% sensitivity (95% CI 84.7-95.5) and 91.6% specificity (95% CI 84.8-95.5) and detected neocortical tau-PET positivity with 98.5% sensitivity and 81.8% specificity. In Paris, sensitivity/specificity for clinical-biological AD were 93.2% (95% CI 85.1-97.1)/93.0% (95% CI 81.4-97.6); in Bordeaux, sensitivity/specificity for clinical-biological AD were 95.7% (95% CI 79.0-99.2)/92.3% (95% CI 66.7-98.6). Specificity in monogenic FTLD was 88.4% (95% CI 75.5-94.9). False-positive classifications were enriched in FTLD with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Dual thresholds yielded gray zones in 15.4%-24.8% of Paris patients; second-line CSF testing resolved 86.2%-88.9% of gray zone cases.

DISCUSSION: Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 thresholds were transferable across centers, analyzers, reagent lots, and heterogeneous clinical populations, supporting evaluation of plasma-first pathways with confirmatory testing for gray zone values. Values below 0.193 pg/mL made neocortical tauopathy unlikely. Limitations include cross-sectional design, specialized Western European recruitment, unavailable race/ethnicity data, heterogeneous reference standards, incomplete AD copathology adjudication in monogenic FTLD, and no cross-platform comparison.

articles.title: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy in Alzheimer Disease Continuum: Prevalence and Clinical Relevance in a Biomarker-Defined Memory Clinic Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) frequently co-occurs with Alzheimer disease (AD), yet the prevalence and clinical significance of comorbid CAA among cognitively impaired individuals on the AD continuum remain unclear. We aimed to determine the frequency of probable CAA (Boston criteria v2.0) in a memory-clinic cohort of symptomatic amyloid-positive individuals and to compare demographic, clinical, cognitive, and biomarker profiles between those with and without comorbid probable CAA.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at the Geneva Memory Center including amyloid-positive patients confirmed by CSF or amyloid PET. Participants meeting the Boston criteria v2.0 for probable CAA were classified as AD-probable CAA, whereas those with possible or no CAA were classified as AD-nonprobable CAA. Group differences were assessed using standard parametric and nonparametric tests, linear mixed-effects models for cognitive trajectories, logistic regression for cerebral microbleed (CMB)-CSF biomarker associations, and voxel-wise Statistical Parametric Mapping for regional amyloid PET differences.

RESULTS: Among 533 participants (mean age 73.8 ± 6.7 years, 59% female), 148 (28%) met criteria for probable CAA. Demographic characteristics, baseline cognition (mini-mental state examination: rank-biserial r = -0.05, 95% CI -0.16 to 0.07, p = 0.410), and longitudinal cognitive decline (β = -0.02, 95% CI -0.05 to 0.02, p = 0.309; median follow-up 28.1 months) did not differ between groups. Lower CSF Aβ42 was associated with lobar CMB burden (odds ratio per 1 SD decrease = 1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.92, p = 0.004). Voxel-wise PET analyses revealed higher cortical amyloid uptake in AD-probable CAA with tracer-dependent patterns (cluster-level family-wise error p < 0.05).

DISCUSSION: More than one-quarter of amyloid-positive patients fulfilled the Boston criteria v2.0 for probable CAA. Probable CAA was not associated with a distinct clinical presentation or trajectory of cognitive decline. Higher cortical amyloid PET uptake in probable CAA and the association of lower CSF Aβ42 with lobar CMB burden suggest more prominent cerebral amyloidosis in this population. The binary probable CAA label may therefore reflect greater amyloid burden without necessarily delineating a clinically distinct subgroup within the AD continuum. Marker-specific approaches targeting cortical superficial siderosis and high lobar CMB burden may prove more informative.

articles.title: A Primer on the Use of Frequentist Confidence Analysis in Neurology Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Clinical researchers are drawn toward Bayesian methods that facilitate probability statements quantifying confidence in particular treatment effects of interest. Although traditional frequentist statistics are not typically used to make such statements, frequentist confidence analysis is an alternative to Bayesian methods, which fully supports confidence statements about observed treatment effects. Despite frequentist confidence analysis dating back to the 1950s and being sometimes used in clinical studies, clinical researchers may not be aware of how to use frequentist confidence to design and analyze clinical trials. Therefore, this Research Methods in Neurology primer describes the application of frequentist confidence to address the practical topic of design and analysis of clinical trials. The primer expands on well-understood ideas around frequentist CIs to describe the notion of confidence distributions, which can be used to flexibly quantify the strength of evidence about any treatment effect of interest. Then, we describe how to use frequentist confidence in a specific treatment effect (e.g., benefit or lack of meaningful benefit) to monitor data in an adaptive trial setting. We illustrate how frequentist confidence-adaptive trials can achieve tight control of Type I error rate. Finally, we provide 2 R software packages ("confidenceCurves" and "confidenceSim"), with a clinician-friendly user interface ("confidenceCurvesApp"), to support frequentist confidence-based reasoning and confidence-based trial design for neurology research.

articles.title: When Systems Talk-Measuring Neurology Care in the Digital Era: Emerging Issues in Neurology.
articles.abstract: Neurology is entering a decade in which rapid growth in diagnostic technologies, data streams, and care delivery models collides with persistent fragmentation of neurologic information across electronic health records, imaging systems, and remote monitoring platforms. As these data sources proliferate, interoperability has emerged as a foundational requirement for high-quality neurologic care. The current landscape limits longitudinal understanding of disease trajectories, impedes care transitions, burdens quality measurement, and constrains research. This article articulates the current and future challenges of interoperability for neurology by characterizing the current state of interoperability; surveying relevant national standards and platforms; identifying key technical, semantic, and organizational barriers; and proposing future goals for improving interoperable neurologic care. Part and parcel of these challenges and goals are the evolving regulatory and policy frameworks, including the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement, provisions of the 21st Century Cures Act, and federal interoperability rules that mandate standardized, Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)-based application programming interfaces (APIs), and a common data foundation such as the United States Core Data for Interoperability Version-3 (USCDI v3). In parallel, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) initiatives have accelerated the transition to digital quality measures (dQMs), increasing the need for automated, multisource, standards-based data exchange aligned with real-time quality improvement. Using hypothetical use cases in vascular and behavioral neurology, we demonstrate how FHIR-based implementation guides could replace manual stroke quality reporting and enable the migration of cognitive assessment measures from legacy electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) to interoperable FHIR eCQMs, laying the groundwork for future dQMs. These examples highlight the potential of shared terminologies, structured neurologic observations, and API-enabled exchange, while underscoring persistent challenges, including limited availability of discrete neurologic data elements and the substantial effort required for mapping and governance. As the neurology ecosystem prepares for USCDI-aligned interoperability mandates taking effect in 2026, the neurology community plays a critical leadership role. Priorities include expanding neurologic data models and terminologies, ensuring that dQMs reflect clinical realities, strengthening governance across registries and networks, and enabling interoperable workflows that support remote monitoring and AI-enabled analytics. Together, these strategies position interoperability as a strategic imperative for the future of neurologic care, quality measurement, and research.

articles.title: Semantic Processing in Unresponsive Patients With Acute Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Early prognostication after acute brain injury (ABI) is challenging because behavioral responsiveness may not accurately reflect preserved cognitive function. Neural responses to semantic incongruity can identify language processing despite the absence of overt behavior. We investigated whether bedside EEG could detect semantic processing in unresponsive patients with ABI and whether its presence was associated with long-term outcomes.

METHODS: In this prospective 2-center cohort study, unresponsive adults with ABI admitted to neurologic intensive care units between 2022 and 2025 underwent bedside EEG during a language paradigm comparing congruent and incongruent sentence endings (e.g., "my favorite color is green/soon"). Semantic processing was defined by differential event-related responses within centroparietal channels (300-500 milliseconds) using cluster-based permutation testing with false discovery rate correction. Outcomes were assessed for recovery of consciousness and functional recovery (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score ≥4) at 12 months by blinded interviewers. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios.

RESULTS: Among 105 patients (mean age 58 ± 19 years; 21% women; 53% Hispanic/Latino), the most common etiologies were intracerebral hemorrhage (45%), traumatic brain injury (43%), and subarachnoid hemorrhage (10%). Withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy occurred in 31%. Semantic processing was detected in 13 patients (12%). Recovery of consciousness occurred in 77% of patients with semantic processing compared with 49% without semantic processing (odds ratio [OR] 3.5; 95% CI 0.9-13.5, p = 0.08). Functional recovery occurred in 42% with semantic processing compared with 14% without semantic processing (OR 4.5; 95% CI 1.2-16.6, p = 0.03). Semantic processing was highly specific but insensitive for predicting both recovery of consciousness (specificity 94%, sensitivity 18%) and functional recovery (specificity 92%, sensitivity 29%). After excluding patients who underwent withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy or died of non-neurologic medical complications, specificity increased to 100% for recovery of consciousness and 95% for functional recovery.

DISCUSSION: EEG evidence of semantic processing can be detected in a subset of unresponsive patients with ABI during the acute phase of injury and is associated with favorable long-term outcomes. Semantic processing was a specific but insensitive biomarker of recovery, suggesting potential utility as a rule-in marker of preserved cognitive function. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Evaluation of Submandibular Gland Biopsies With Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion in Clinical Parkinson Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The definite diagnosis of Parkinson disease (PD) is usually made by the detection of α-synuclein aggregates in the brain postmortem with the rare exception of some genetic forms. Traces of α-synuclein aggregates in extracerebral tissue biopsies may serve as an appropriate biomarker to confirm a clinical diagnosis in vivo. We set out to determine whether the detection of α-synuclein aggregates in submandibular gland biopsies is an effective means for diagnosing patients with PD.

METHODS: In this prospective study, we consecutively acquired and examined submandibular gland biopsies from patients with clinical PD in neurologic care and controls who underwent surgical procedures on the submandibular gland for different reasons. Our index method was the detection of α-synuclein aggregates using the real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) in fresh-frozen tissue. We compared the results with immunohistochemical α-synuclein aggregate detection and paraffin-embedded tissue blot (PET-blot) as reference methods in formalin-fixed tissue from the same biopsy.

RESULTS: The study population included 25 patients with clinical PD (mean age 67.3 ± 9.3 years, 64% male, 36% female) and 25 age-matched controls (mean age 64.6 ± 8.6 years, 48% male, 52% female). The RT-QuIC assay detected α-synuclein aggregates in submandibular gland biopsies (n = 41) with a sensitivity of 81.8%, which increased to 90% after a clinical follow-up, and a specificity of 100%, thus providing an accuracy of 90.2% (95% CI 76.6%-96.4%) and 95.1% (95% CI 82.9%-98.7%), respectively. The PET-blot with mAb5C12 (n = 49) confirmed 50% of the RT-QuIC positives and offered a sensitivity of 45.8% (50% after clinical follow-up) and a specificity of 100%. Immunohistochemical detection (n = 48) using the same antibody confirmed 28% of the RT-QuIC positives but found 2 of the controls to be positive and therefore provided a sensitivity of 26.1% (28.6% after clinical follow-up) and a specificity of 92%.

DISCUSSION: With a sensitivity of more than 80%, which is comparable with the clinical diagnosis when neuropathologic examination serves as gold standard, the RT-QuIC assay on salivary gland biopsies may serve as a valuable instrument to improve the diagnosis of PD. Further validation is necessary to substantiate these findings in larger-scale investigations.

articles.title: Plasma P-Tau217 as a Prognostic, Monitoring, and Risk-Stratification Biomarker of Clinical Progression in Lewy Body Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Although plasma phosphorylated tau-217 (pTau217) detects co-occurring Alzheimer disease (AD) neuropathologic change in Lewy body disease (LBD), relationships with long-term clinical outcomes remain unclear. Our aim was to evaluate plasma pTau217 as a prognostic, risk-stratification, and monitoring biomarker of cognitive and functional decline in LBD.

METHODS: This prospective longitudinal study included Stanford AD Research Center participants enrolled from 2015 to 2023 with plasma pTau217 data and clinical diagnoses of LBD spectrum, AD spectrum, or healthy control (HC). To evaluate prognostic and monitoring utility, respectively, linear mixed-effect models tested whether baseline level and longitudinal change (2-5 years) in plasma pTau217 were associated with longitudinal changes (2-8 years) in daily functioning (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes [CDR-SB]), global cognition (Montreal Cognitive Assessment [MoCA]), and 5 domain-specific cognitive indices. For risk stratification, baseline plasma pTau217 status was defined using an amyloid PET-derived, LBD-specific cut-point to examine whether participants with abnormal levels demonstrated faster clinical progression in separate linear-mixed effects and survival models.

RESULTS: A total of 501 participants (mean[SD] age = 71.1[8.5]; 51.5% female) were included across LBD (n = 131), AD (n = 133), and HC (n = 237) groups. In LBD, higher baseline plasma pTau217 was associated with faster CDR-SB increase (β = 0.30; 95% CI [0.14, 0.45]; p < 0.001), MoCA decline (β = -0.35; 95% CI [-0.57, -0.13]; p = 0.002), and cognitive index decline (all p ≤ 0.028). Participants with abnormal baseline pTau217 had a 0.85 points/year faster CDR-SB increase (95% CI [0.56, 1.15]; p < 0.001), 0.87 points/year faster MoCA decline (95% CI [-1.38, -0.37]; p = 0.001), faster decline on cognitive indices (all p ≤ 0.018), and a three-fold higher risk of diagnostically progressing to mild cognitive impairment or dementia (HR = 3.41; 95% CI [1.60, 7.28]; p = 0.002) compared to participants with normal pTau217. Faster longitudinal pTau217 increase was associated with faster CDR-SB increase (β = 0.24; 95% CI [0.10, 0.38]; p = 0.003).

DISCUSSION: Plasma pTau217 is a promising prognostic, risk-stratification, and monitoring biomarker of clinical progression in LBD, underscoring its utility for clinical practice and trials in mixed pathology groups.

articles.title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain.

METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes.

RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64).

DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Rate of Multiple Sclerosis Onset in a Cohort With Prior Infectious Mononucleosis Identified in Administrative Data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Evidence suggests that Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is a necessary, but not sufficient, exposure for developing multiple sclerosis (MS). Although many cases of EBV infection are asymptomatic, people with infectious mononucleosis (IM) often seek medical attention and thus can be studied on the population level. We aimed to characterize factors influencing the rate of MS development in a large population-based cohort with IM.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, outpatient and inpatient cases of IM (ICD-9 code 075 and ICD-10-CA code B27) were identified from health claims data in Ontario, Canada, from April 1, 1992, to March 31, 2017. MS cases after IM were identified using a validated algorithm from May 1, 1992, to March 31, 2022. We evaluated the rate of MS in an IM-exposed cohort using a cause-specific hazards model incorporating age at IM (younger than 10 years, 10-25 years, and older than 25 years), sex, rural vs urban residence, neighborhood income, immigrant status, and mental health care use.

RESULTS: We identified 671,410 cases of IM, with mean (SD) age of 19.9 (18.8) years; 53.5% were female. Of the 671,410, 2,470 (0.4%) developed MS over a median (interquarile range [IQR]) follow-up of 16.7 (10.1-23.3) years. The median time from IM to MS was 11.4 (IQR 6.5-16.8) years. Female sex (hazard ratio [HR] 1.9, 95% CI 1.8-2.1), age at IM (age 10-25 years vs < 10 years: HR 6.0; 95% CI 5.2-6.9), and mental health care use (HR 1.2; 95% CI 1.1-1.3) were associated with a greater rate of developing MS after IM, while being an immigrant was associated with a lower rate (HR 0.5; 95% CI 0.4-0.7).

DISCUSSION: In a population-based cohort, the median time from IM exposure to MS was just over 1 decade. Mental health conditions may be associated with a higher rate of developing MS, in addition to being a feature of the MS prodrome. Our results may inform risk stratification for developing MS after IM and thus facilitate secondary prevention in high-risk individuals. Limitations include the ability to capture only recognized infectious mononucleosis, which may limit generalizability to asymptomatic or mild cases of EBV infection.

articles.title: Evaluating Age-Related Motor System Changes Using Gait as a Functionally Relevant Marker.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Aging causes gait and mobility decline, which often precedes cognitive impairment and dementia. Biological "age gaps" (the difference between biological and chronological age) are traditionally measured using neuroimaging and electroencephalography, quantified gait metrics have not been used for this purpose. We hypothesize that specific gait metrics can effectively quantify biological aging and predict future cognitive impairment risk.

METHODS: We analyzed gait data from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging, a population-based cohort in Olmsted County, MN. Participants without known gait disorder, recruited between 2007 and 2025, were included. We used these data to develop a machine learning-based age prediction model. This gait-based age prediction model was used to devise the "gait age gap," a quantified metric of gait abnormality defined as the difference between age as predicted by gait performance ("gait age") and chronological age. We used the gait age gap to evaluate the risk of future cognitive impairment.

RESULTS: We analyzed 19,637 walk trials from 5,794 unique participants (49% female), with a mean age of 78 (±8) years. Gait age was primarily driven by changes in measures of stability. A larger gait age gap was associated with impaired cognitive and functional status. In longitudinal analysis, each gait age gap year exceeding chronological age increased the risk of converting from a normal to cognitively impaired (CI) state by 7% per year. Gait age gap outperformed baseline velocity in distinguishing normal from CI groups and was associated with future risk of conversion from normal to a CI state hazard ratio = 1.07 (95% CI 1.03-1.13) for gait age gap vs hazard ratio = 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-1.00) for velocity.

DISCUSSION: The gait age gap is a functionally relevant marker of age-related motor system changes that quantifies deviations from expected gait performance for a given chronological age. It is associated with a higher risk of future cognitive impairment among cognitively normal individuals. This study includes a relatively homogeneous cohort of predominantly Caucasian participants. To assess generalizability and the trajectory of motoric aging across sociodemographic groups, these findings need to be replicated in diverse cohorts. Wearable sensor technologies could also make such measures more scalable.

articles.title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).

DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear.

METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.

DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

articles.title: Right Brain: Climbing an Infinite Mountain.
articles.abstract: This is the story of the events that transpired after I found out I had matched into neurology in the United States. It is not a story of triumph over adversity, but rather an honest admission of vulnerability-of anxiety and fear experienced during this process. It is the story of a migrant in an unfamiliar place, but also of the uncertainty that everyone feels before starting residency. I draw on childhood memories of the majestic Andean mountains to reflect on the idea that the climb never ends-and that with every step, our perspective expands.

articles.title: Toward Personalized Sex-Informed Management of Blood Pressure After Stroke Thrombectomy Reperfusion.
Overlooked Writings of Sir William Gowers on Neurology in General Practice, Shorthand, and Education.
articles.abstract: Sir William Richard Gowers (1845-1915), long hailed as the "Father of Clinical Neurology," has been the subject of 2 biographies and many essays relating to his contributions to the study of nervous disorders. Yet, despite extensive bibliographies, several of his publications have hitherto escaped notice. We reviewed archival sources and digital repositories to identify overlooked works. This led to the discovery of his contributions to George Alexander Gibson's 1901 Text-Book of Medicine, which distilled neurology for the general practitioner, as well as lectures and articles on shorthand and education, reflecting his interest in communication, educational practice, and the process of learning. Gowers advocated cultivating ambidexterity in youth, reasoning that it may confer resilience against neurologic injury later in life. Recovered only through primary source research, these writings broaden our understanding of Gowers' intellectual range, showing him not only as a pioneering specialist in the study of nervous disorders but also as a physician engaged with general medicine and educational reform.

articles.title: Association of LATE-NC With Neuropathologic Lesions and Cognitive Abilities: A Population-Based Autopsy Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Limbic-predominant age-related TDP-43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE-NC) is a common finding in aging brains. However, most previous studies were limited to ethnoracially homogeneous cohorts from high-income countries. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between LATE-NC, cognitive performance, and coexisting neuropathologic lesions in a large, ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample from Brazil.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the Biobank for Aging Studies, a Brazilian population-based autopsy study based at the University of São Paulo. The study included a consecutive series of autopsies performed between 2004 and 2024. Inclusion criteria required participants to be at least 18 years old with a knowledgeable informant. LATE-NC, Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC), Lewy body pathology (LBP), lacunar infarcts, small vessel disease, cerebral amyloid angiopathy, and hippocampal sclerosis were assessed following international criteria. Cognitive abilities were evaluated with the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SOB). Logistic and linear regression models were applied to examine associations of LATE-NC with comorbid neuropathologies and cognitive outcomes, with adjustments for sociodemographic, clinical, and neuropathologic covariates.

RESULTS: The sample comprised 1,860 participants (mean age = 72.6 ± 14.2 years; 49.1% female; 62.2% White; 35.4% Black). LATE-NC was present in 7.4% of participants (stage 1: 3.0%; stage 2: 4.0%; stage 3: 0.4%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, clinical, and other neuropathologic covariates, LATE-NC (stages 2-3) was associated with hippocampal sclerosis (OR = 14.95; 95% CI 7.42-30.27; p < 0.001), advanced Braak NFT stages (OR = 2.23; 95% CI 1.32-3.83; p = 0.003), and LBP (OR = 1.89; 95% CI 1.02-3.37; p = 0.036). Factoring in other pathologies, LATE-NC was associated with the CDR-SOB score (β = 4.06; 95% CI 2.95-5.18; p < 0.001), demonstrating a consistent association with cognition, similar to the one observed for moderate/severe ADNC (β = 3.78; 95% CI 3.14-4.42; p < 0.001) in the same sample.

DISCUSSION: LATE-NC was prevalent and associated with cognitive impairment in this ethnoracially and socioeconomically diverse sample. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and some estimates had wide confidence intervals due to the small number of advanced-stage cases.

articles.title: Impact of 2024 Revisions of Multiple Sclerosis Diagnostic Criteria in People With Radiologically Isolated Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The biological onset of multiple sclerosis (MS) precedes its clinical onset by years, as shown by MRI and CSF biomarkers. The 2024 revisions of the McDonald criteria extend, for the first time, MS diagnosis to selected cases of radiologically isolated syndrome (RIS), that is, to people with incidentally discovered CNS lesions suggestive of autoimmune inflammatory demyelination, in the absence of typical symptoms. The aim of this multicenter study was to assess the proportion of patients with RIS reclassified as MS, after applying the 2024 criteria.

METHODS: Adult participants (≥18 years) fulfilling the 2023 Lebrun-Frénay RIS criteria were selected from 22 Italian MS tertiary centers. Real-world, registry-based data were retrospectively collected at both baseline and follow-up. Reclassification followed 2024 criteria, allowing a MS diagnosis in RIS cases with ≥1 T2-hyperintense lesion in ≥2 typical MS regions (i.e., dissemination in space [DIS]), plus either MRI evidence of dissemination in time (DIT), CSF positivity, or central vein sign (CVS) positivity. Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: Among 236 patients with RIS (mean age 38.9 ± 11.6 years; 70.3% female; median follow-up 3.0 years [interquartile range {IQR}: 1.1-6]), at baseline, 228 (96.6%) fulfilled DIS, 51 (21.6%) fulfilled radiologic DIT, and 152 of 201 individuals with available CSF data were CSF-positive (75.6%). CVS data were available for 5 of 236 individuals; none were CVS-positive. At baseline, the 2024 criteria resulted in a MS diagnosis in 159 of 236 patients with RIS (67.4%). Of 42 patients with RIS experiencing a clinical event during follow-up, 88.1% would have been reclassified as MS a median of 2 years earlier (IQR: 1.0-5.5). During follow-up, 18 of 236 additional participants (7.6%) met the diagnostic criteria through radiologic DIT.

DISCUSSION: The introduction of the 2024 criteria results in an earlier diagnosis of MS, before clinical manifestations of focal CNS damage, in most people formerly classified as RIS. Study limitations include incomplete kappa free light chain index data and nonstandardized MRI acquisition protocols; particularly, retrospective CVS assessment was negligible in this real-life context. Future studies including the full spectrum of asymptomatic individuals with MRI abnormalities and available paraclinical diagnostic tools are needed to better define the impact of 2024 revised criteria in this population.

articles.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: The Price of Patency: Intractable Headache Subsequent to Fourth Ventricular Recanalization.
articles.abstract: Fourth ventricular hemorrhage is a devastating subtype of hemorrhagic stroke that can be primary or secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage. In both cases, inflammatory reactions triggered by blood in the subarachnoid space peak in the first week. This report describes a 61-year-old woman with a secondary fourth ventricular hemorrhage managed with IRRAflow active irrigation and drainage system, which expedited recanalization of the fourth ventricle and clearance of cisternal subarachnoid hemorrhage on days 3 and 5, respectively. However, the patient developed an intractable headache on day 7, despite normal imaging, intracranial pressure, and laboratory investigations. This case highlights caudal sac inflammation as a hidden culprit of unremitting headache after recanalization of the fourth ventricle despite normal investigations.

articles.title: Blocking two host receptors is better than one: Insights from RSV infection in human respiratory organoids.
Runx3 dosage determines liver-resident memory T cell fate.
articles.abstract: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells adopt distinct residency programs across organs, yet the transcriptional logic that separates epithelial and non-epithelial TRM identities is not well defined. Runx3 promotes epithelial TRM differentiation by enabling TGFβ responsiveness, but since TGFβ is dispensable for liver TRM formation, it has been unclear whether Runx3 is required. Enforced Runx3 expression, while enhancing epithelial CD103+ TRM formation, impaired liver TRM development and was accompanied by reduced expression of LFA-1 and CD122, key mediators of liver residency. Although the liver TRM impairment was TGFβ independent and rescued by restoring LFA-1 expression, elevated Runx3 expression diverted cells toward a TGFβ-dependent CD103+ liver TRM state resembling human CD103+ TRM cells enriched in fibrotic liver disease. Together, these findings establish Runx3 dosage as a key determinant of tissue-specific TRM fate and reveal that liver TRM cells operate under transcriptional constraints distinct from epithelial TRM subsets.

articles.title: Hepatic stellate cells remodel liver-resident CD8+ T cells and constrain immunosurveillance.
articles.abstract: The liver constitutes a distinct immunological niche in which CD8+ T cells balance immune protection and tissue integrity. How chronic liver disease (CLD) remodels human liver-resident CD8+ T cells remains poorly understood. We demonstrate that activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) create immunoinstructive fibrotic niches that regulate liver-resident CD8+ T cell differentiation, localization, and function. CD103-expressing liver-resident CD8+ T cells accumulate with increasing fibrosis severity and preferentially localize within collagen-rich scar tissue. HSC-derived and matrix-retained TGFβ promote acquisition of a residency program characterized by upregulation of CD103, ECM-binding integrins, and adhesion molecules. Despite their increased abundance, liver-resident CD8+ T cells in CLD exhibit impaired antigen-dependent effector function, increased inhibitory receptor expression, and a transcriptional program associated with T cell dysfunction. Importantly, responses to PMA/ionomycin remain intact, indicating preserved effector competence. Mechanistically, HSCs directly suppress antigen-specific liver-resident CD8+ T cell function, with partial restoration following PD-L1/PD-L2 blockade. These findings identify the fibrotic niche as a central regulator of liver-resident CD8+ T cells and reveal how fibrosis can limit local immunosurveillance.

articles.title: Early fate bias and TCR sequence shape CD8+ T cell differentiation and expansion.
articles.abstract: When a naive CD8+ T cell encounters an antigen, it proliferates into descendants with identical T cell receptors (TCRs), termed clones. Whether their differentiation toward effector or memory fates is stochastic or TCR-dependent has remained unclear, largely because the vast diversity of TCRs makes individual clones difficult to trace over time. Using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing in acute LCMV Armstrong infection, we found that clonal distributions in blood reflect those in lymphoid organs, enabling nonlethal longitudinal tracking of clonal evolution. Tracing hundreds of clones, we found that memory clonal distribution is surprisingly uncoupled from early dominance; instead, early central memory precursor frequency predicts memory dominance. Leveraging convergent recombination, we identified clones with identical CDR3 amino acid sequences in mice and found that these natural biological replicates were more likely than chance to adopt similar fates, although substantial clone-to-clone variation remained. Applying the TCR distance algorithm, we further identified dominant motifs associated with enhanced expansion and effector-biased transcriptional programs, extending the TCR's role in shaping clonal differentiation.

articles.title: A nematode-trapping fungus orchestrates polarity cues, septins, and NOX signaling for trap formation.
articles.abstract: Reprogramming cell morphogenesis in response to environmental cues is fundamental to microbial adaptation and survival. The nematode-trapping fungus (NTF) Arthrobotrys oligospora exemplifies this plasticity by developing adhesive traps to capture nematodes. However, mechanisms underlying trap morphogenesis and host invasion remain unclear. Using live-cell imaging, genetics, and functional assays, we show trap morphogenesis proceeds through localized redirection of hyphal growth followed by site-specific hyphal fusion, whereas infection development involves a transition from isotropic infection bulb expansion to multipolar invasive growth. These transitions are coordinated by the reorganization of conserved polarity proteins, asymmetric septin localization at the trap cell inner rim, and actin remodeling. Nematode-induced Nox1 signaling is required to recruit polarity and cytoskeletal machinery to the trap cell fusion site. Together, these findings establish NTF as a powerful model for understanding how conserved morphogenetic machinery drives the transition from linear hyphae to hyphal loops to trap nematodes.

articles.title: Senkyunolide a from danggui buxue decoction protects podocytes against diabetic nephropathy via the mir-223-3p/nlrp3 inflammasome axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD), a classical Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula comprising Astragalus membranaceus (Fisch.) Bunge (Astragali Radix) and Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Angelicae Sinensis Radix) in a 5:1 ratio, has been traditionally used to treat "Xiaoke" (wasting-thirst syndrome) and is increasingly applied as an adjunctive therapy for diabetic nephropathy (DN). DN is a major microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus for which effective curative therapies remain limited. Although DBD has demonstrated promising clinical efficacy in the prevention and management of DN, its pharmacologically active constituents and underlying mechanisms of action have yet to be fully elucidated.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to comprehensively profile the blood-entering bioactive constituents of DBD, identify the core active compound through integrated UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and network pharmacology analyses, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the core constituent protects against high glucose-induced podocyte injury, with particular focus on the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 inflammasome axis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was employed to globally characterize the chemical constituents of Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD), and the absorbed components and in vivo metabolites were identified in a DN rat model. Network pharmacology combined with target intersection analysis was used to identify the core active constituents. Subsequently, PPI network construction, GO functional annotation, and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses were performed to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. In a high glucose-induced MPC5 podocyte model, CCK-8, TUNEL, and JC-1 assays were conducted to evaluate the cytoprotective effects of the major active constituents. Furthermore, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the regulatory mechanism of the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 axis.

RESULTS: UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS identified a total of 1584 chemical constituents in DBD, among which 249 absorbed components and 155 in vivo metabolites were detected in the plasma of DN model rats.
