Network pharmacology analysis identified senkyunolide A (SA) as the core active constituent, which targeted 33 NLRP3 inflammasome-related proteins, covering the entire activation cascade of this pathway. PPI network construction and enrichment analyses further revealed that SA-associated targets were involved in key biological processes at the systems level, including oxidative stress and PI3K-Akt/NF-κB signaling pathways. In vitro experiments demonstrated that SA at a concentration of 50 μmol/L significantly ameliorated high glucose-induced podocyte injury, apoptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, SA upregulated miR-223-3p expression, thereby directly inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which in turn suppressed Caspase-1 cleavage and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis. Meanwhile, SA maintained mitochondrial dynamic homeostasis and energy metabolism by regulating DRP1 phosphorylation, upregulating OPA1 and MFN2, and activating the PGC-1α/MnSOD pathway, ultimately exerting multi-level protective effects on podocytes.

CONCLUSIONS: SA is identified as the core bioactive constituent of DBD responsible for its therapeutic effects in DN. SA exerts multi-level renoprotective effects by upregulating miR-223-3p, suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, and maintaining mitochondrial dynamic homeostasis via the PGC-1α/MnSOD pathway. These findings provide a scientific basis for the rational application of DBD in the clinical prevention and treatment of diabetic nephropathy and highlight the miR-223-3p/NLRP3 axis as a promising therapeutic target.

articles.title: Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill.: A comprehensive review of botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, pharmacokinetics, and toxicology.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Saururus chinensis (Lour.) Baill. is a traditional medicinal herb widely used in East Asia, with a long history of use in traditional Chinese medicine and traditional Korean medicine. It is traditionally used to clear heat, detoxify, promote diuresis, and reduce swelling, particularly for damp-heat-related disorders. Given its long-standing ethnomedicinal use, S. chinensis has considerable potential for further development.

AIM OF THE REVIEW: Although studies on S. chinensis have increased rapidly, no comprehensive systematic review dedicated to this species is available. This review summarizes its botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, quality control, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity, with the aim of evaluating its therapeutic potential and identifying current research gaps.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Relevant literature is systematically retrieved from PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and other major databases. The collected studies are screened, organized, and comprehensively analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 232 compounds have been identified from S. chinensis, with lignans as the predominant class of constituents. Available studies indicate that S. chinensis exhibits antitumor, anti-inflammatory, cardiovascular-protective, neuroprotective, multiorgan-protective, metabolic-regulatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, skin-protective, anti-asthmatic, anti-allergic, and bone-protective activities. However, several issues remain, including unclear toxic mechanisms, the lack of a well-defined safe dosage range, insufficient understanding of synergistic effects, low bioavailability, and incomplete quality control.

CONCLUSIONS: S. chinensis shows considerable potential for further development. Future studies should address these issues to support the safe, effective, and standardized development and application of this medicinal plant.

articles.title: Qufeng xuanbi formula attenuates HDM-induced allergic asthma by targeting the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Qufeng Xuanbi Formula (QFXBF), a traditional Chinese medicine prescription used for asthma-like respiratory disorders, has shown anti-asthmatic activity. However, whether it attenuates allergic airway remodeling through innate immune-metabolic regulation remains unknown.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether QFXBF alleviates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway inflammation and remodeling through targeting the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis, and to evaluate the specific inhibitory potential of its constituent tectorigenin on STING-mediated immunometabolic signaling.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An HDM-induced allergic asthma model was established in male C57BL/6 mice by intranasal sensitization and challenge, followed by oral administration of QFXBF at 12.5, 25, and 50 g/kg/day or dexamethasone at 2 mg/kg/day. Airway hyperresponsiveness, lung histopathology, mucus secretion, collagen deposition, α-SMA expression, inflammatory mediators in BALF and serum, and glycolytic metabolic indices were evaluated. BSMCs were stimulated with IL-4 and LPS, both at 5 ng/mL, and treated with QFXBF at 2, 4, and 8 mg/mL. Cell proliferation, migration, glucose consumption, lactate production, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed to assess airway smooth muscle activation and metabolic reprogramming. Transcriptomic analysis of lung tissue, STING overexpression, HIF-1α pharmacological inhibition, LC-MS/MS-based identification of tectorigenin, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were further used to investigate the STING/HIF-1α/glycolysis axis and the potential STING-targeting activity of tectorigenin.

RESULTS: QFXBF markedly reduced airway hyperresponsiveness, inflammatory infiltration, and collagen deposition in HDM-challenged mice, accompanied by decreased asthma-related markers in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and serum. QFXBF also downregulated STING, HIF-1α, and key glycolytic enzymes at both mRNA and protein levels in lung tissue. In IL-4+LPS-stimulated BSMCs, QFXBF dose-dependently suppressed proliferation and migration, reduced glucose utilization and lactate accumulation, and concurrently inhibited STING/HIF-1α and glycolysis-associated factors. Mechanistically, QFXBF attenuated HIF-1α activity and glycolytic flux through suppression of STING. Liquid chromatography-based analysis identified tectorigenin as a bioavailable constituent of QFXBF. In STING-overexpressing BSMCs, tectorigenin significantly reduced STING expression, proliferative activity, and lactate metabolism, supporting STING inhibition as a key pharmacological basis of QFXBF.

CONCLUSION: QFXBF can alleviate allergic remodeling by suppressing the STING/HIF-1α-mediated glycolytic program. Tectorigenin may act as a potential STING inhibitor that disrupts innate immune-metabolic signaling, providing mechanistic support for QFXBF-derived therapeutic strategies in asthma.

articles.title: Iridoids in medicinal herbs for the treatment of cardiovascular diseases: Ethnopharmacology, phytochemistry, and pharmacology.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a major challenge to global public health. Although various pharmacological and surgical interventions are available, their long-term use may be limited by adverse effects and dependence risks. Therefore, the development of safer and more effective therapeutic agents remains an important goal. Iridoids, a class of bioactive constituents widely distributed in medicinal plants, have shown considerable promise in cardiovascular protection.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This review summarizes current evidence regarding the cardioprotective effects of iridoids, explores their underlying mechanisms, and evaluates their prospects for clinical translation, with the aim of providing guidance for future research.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Wanfang, and CNKI from January 2015 to December 2025. A Boolean-based search strategy was used to identify studies involving representative iridoids (e.g., geniposide, catalpol, and aucubin) and cardiovascular disorders, including atherosclerosis, myocardial infarction, and heart failure. Eligible experimental studies were analyzed to clarify their chemical characteristics, pharmacological activities, and associated signaling pathways.

RESULTS: Iridoids exert cardiovascular protective effects through multiple mechanisms, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, anti-endoplasmic reticulum stress, and anti-apoptotic activities. Collectively, the available evidence highlights their potential as multi-target therapeutic agents for cardiovascular disorders.

CONCLUSION: Iridoids represent promising candidates for cardiovascular therapy. However, successful clinical translation will require further advances in improving bioavailability, clarifying toxicological profiles, and generating high-quality clinical evidence to validate their efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Targeting CREB1 in cardiac diseases therapy.
articles.abstract: Cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein 1 (CREB1) family is integral to the regulation of gene expression in response to diverse cellular signals, functioning as both an activator and a repressor depending on the cellular contest. The activity of CREB1 is tightly regulated by phosphorylation, alternative splicing, and co-activator interactions, enabling it to integrate multiple signaling pathways and precisely control processes. In the cardiac diseases, CREB1 emerges as a critical regulator. Evidence indicates that CREB1 upregulation reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis and enhances cardiac function post-infarction. At the same time, its downregulation is linked to impaired contractility and dilated cardiomyopathy, highlighting its role as both a protective factor in cardiac pathology. This review examines the central CREB1-related signaling cascades, such as the CREB1/the homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 3 (HIPK3)/microRNA-17-3p/the adenylate cyclase type 6 (ADCY6) and CREB1- the bone morphogenetic proteins 10 (BMP10)-Smad1/5/8 axes, delineating their upstream activators and downstream targets in cardiac disease. Collectively, these findings underscore the therapeutic potential of targeting CREB1 and its regulatory networks for the management of diverse cardiac conditions.

articles.title: A paper-based electrochemical aptasensor functionalized with silver nanoparticles for the detection of African swine fever virus p30 protein.
articles.abstract: African swine fever (ASF) is a devastating viral disease of domestic pigs and wild boars. The etiological agent, African swine fever virus (ASFV), continues to pose a serious threat to the global swine industry, causing profound economic losses in many countries. Therefore, early and reliable detection of ASFV is essential to curb its transmission and mitigate the economic damage it causes. In the present study, the ASFV protein p30, which is expressed within 2-4 h post-infection and endures throughout the viral replication cycle, was expressed and purified. An aptamer targeting the ASFV p30 protein was screened and validated, which was then used to fabricate an electrochemical paper-based analytical device (PAD) aptasensor. To enhance the aptasensor's conductivity, silver nanoparticles were embedded, and the aptamer was immobilized on the working electrode for ASFV p30 detection. Optimization included testing various protein concentrations and characterizing the resulting electrochemical perturbations using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The optimized biosensor enabled sensitive detection of ASFV p30 at low concentrations, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.09 ng/mL. These findings demonstrate the high sensitivity of the developed aptasensor and highlight its potential as a rapid and reliable platform for ASFV p30 protein detection. Overall, the proposed aptasensor provides a promising technical foundation for the development of rapid, sensitive, and accessible diagnostic approaches for ASFV.

articles.title: Loss of core 1-derived O-glycans disrupts GLUT2 cell-surface localization and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β cells.
articles.abstract: Protein glycosylation is a major post-translational modification that regulates protein function. Core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycans (Galβ1-3GalNAcα1-Ser/Thr) are widely distributed across tissues and are present on membrane-bound and secreted proteins. Their synthesis is catalyzed by core 1 β1,3-galactosyltransferase (C1galt1) and requires the molecular chaperone Cosmc, encoded by C1galt1c1. Although core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycans are abundant on mucin-type glycoproteins, their physiological functions on non-mucin proteins remain poorly understood. Here, we used β cell-specific Cosmc conditional knockout (RIP-Cos) mice to investigate the physiological role of these glycans in pancreatic β cells. RIP-Cos mice exhibited impaired glucose tolerance and defective glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS), despite normal pancreatic insulin content. Because glucose uptake through glucose transporter 2 (GLUT2) contributes to glucose sensing and GSIS in mouse β cells, we examined GLUT2 in RIP-Cos islets. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed an apparent reduction in GLUT2 signal at the plasma membrane. Slc2a2 (GLUT2) mRNA expression was significantly decreased, and immunoblotting revealed a lower molecular weight form of GLUT2. These alterations were accompanied by reduced glucose-analog uptake in primary RIP-Cos islets. RIP-Cos mice also displayed resistance to streptozotocin-induced diabetes. Finally, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry identified O-GalNAc glycosylation sites within the extracellular domain of recombinant mouse GLUT2. These findings suggest that core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycosylation contributes to maintaining GLUT2 molecular properties and localization, thereby supporting β-cell GSIS. Overall, this study supports an important role for core 1-derived O-GalNAc glycosylation in β-cell glucose responsiveness and identifies GLUT2 as a target of O-GalNAc glycosylation.

articles.title: Identification of candidate host susceptibility genes for viral myocarditis through integrated transcriptomic and mendelian randomization analyses.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the genetic mechanisms underlying myocardial inflammatory responses related to Coxsackievirus B3 (CVB3) infection through an integrative transcriptomic and genetic approach. Gene expression profiles from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database were analyzed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between CVB3-infected and control myocardial tissues. These genes were subsequently evaluated using Mendelian randomization (MR) based on publicly available expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data and genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for myocarditis. MR analysis prioritized four candidate genes whose genetically predicted expression levels were significantly associated with myocarditis susceptibility. To ensure the robustness of these findings, multiple sensitivity analyses were performed to assess potential pleiotropy and heterogeneity. Functional analyses suggested that the priority candidate genes (PCGs) were associated with immune regulation, inflammatory signaling, and cellular metabolic processes. In addition, immune cell infiltration analysis suggested alterations in the myocardial immune microenvironment and associations between PCG expression and estimated immune cell proportions. An independent GEO dataset was used for external validation, and in vitro experiments further confirmed the significant upregulation of these genes following CVB3 infection. This integrative strategy combining transcriptomic profiling, human genetic analyses, and experimental validation identified four genetically prioritized candidate genes associated with myocarditis susceptibility and provided preliminary insights into the immune-regulatory mechanisms underlying cardiac inflammatory responses.

articles.title: GAN diet-induced MASLD is associated with compartment-dependent transcriptional alterations in orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma and adjacent liver.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is an important risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet how it is associated with transcriptional changes across tumor and adjacent liver compartments remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated hepatic immune remodeling and orthotopic HCC growth in mice fed a high-fat, high-fructose, and high-cholesterol Gubra-Amylin NASH (GAN) diet, and performed paired transcriptomic analyses of tumor and adjacent liver tissues. GAN feeding induced hepatic steatosis and collagen deposition, accompanied by increased CD4+, CD8+, and F4/80+ cell densities, reduced CD20+ cell density, and increased apoptosis in cells isolated from liver tissues. In the orthotopic HCC model, GAN-fed mice developed larger tumors with increased Ki-67 and reduced cleaved caspase-3 positivity. Notably, CD20+ cell density increased in tumors but decreased in adjacent liver tissues, whereas CD4+, CD8+, and F4/80+ cell densities increased in both compartments. Paired RNA sequencing identified 29 shared differentially expressed genes between the tumor and adjacent liver comparisons, including 27 concordantly downregulated and two concordantly upregulated genes. These shared transcriptional changes were associated with lipid and glutathione metabolism. In contrast, pathway enrichment patterns differed between the two compartments, particularly in fatty acid β-oxidation, bile acid metabolism, complement activation, and antigen processing and presentation. Together, these findings link GAN diet-induced MASLD with enhanced orthotopic HCC growth and hepatic immune remodeling, while revealing shared metabolic transcriptional changes and compartment-dependent pathway enrichment patterns in tumor and adjacent liver tissues.

articles.title: Optimizing early and locally advanced NSCLC: A Portuguese expert consensus on treatment pathways.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Management of early and locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly complex due to expanding therapeutic options, requiring integration of efficacy, safety, and quality of life. As treatment options continue to evolve, structured, multidisciplinary approaches are essential.

RESEARCH QUESTION: This study aims to develop tailored treatment algorithms and clinical recommendations for early and locally advanced NSCLC in Portugal. These recommendations will continue to evolve as the treatment landscape expands.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of 12 experts (4 pulmonologists/oncologists, 4 thoracic surgeons, 4 radiation oncologists) participated in a structured Patient Profile Think Tank. Current diagnostic, staging, and treatment strategies for early and locally advanced NSCLC were reviewed. Consensus statements were generated through iterative discussions and validated via voting. Key decision points were integrated into treatment algorithms, supported by literature.

RESULTS: Consensus was reached on several key treatment decision points, including mandatory molecular testing at initial diagnosis and re-evaluation; standardised criteria for tumour resectability; and the integration of immunotherapy and targeted therapies in NSCLC. Multidisciplinary team discussions were considered essential throughout the patient pathway.

CONCLUSION: This initiative provides the first Portuguese expert consensus on early and locally advanced NSCLC, offering evidence-based recommendations and practical algorithms to standardise care and improve outcomes, while adapting international evidence to the national context. Future efforts should focus on digital clinical implementation and extending approaches to metastatic disease.

articles.title: A pre-procedural machine learning model to predict hypoxemia risk in pediatric flexible bronchoscopy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxemia is a common and potentially serious adverse event during pediatric flexible bronchoscopy (FB), yet reliable pre-procedural risk stratification tools remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate machine learning models to predict hypoxemia.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Clinical data from 1,693 children undergoing elective FB between 1 January 2023 and 31 August 2024 were analyzed retrospectively. The data set was randomly split into training (60%, n = 1,015; 208 events) and held-out test (40%, n = 678; 139 events) sets. Model development, tuning, and 10-fold cross-validation used the training set. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression screened candidate predictors of hypoxemia. Seven models were constructed: logistic regression (LR), decision trees, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, Gaussian Naive Bayes, and XGBoost. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), Brier scores, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis interpreted predictor contributions in the final model.

RESULTS: Hypoxemia (SpO2 <95%) occurred in 347 cases (20.5%). Eight predictors were retained: oxygen therapy via nasal cannula, moderate-to-severe pulmonary dysfunction, fever > 38.0 °C, asthma, ASA-PS, NLR, PCT, and age. LR had the lowest training-set cross-validation Brier score (0.118); in the held-out test set, AUROC was 0.827 (95% CI 0.782-0.867) and Brier score 0.106.

CONCLUSION: The model showed good discrimination, calibration, and potential net benefit. It may aid preoperative risk stratification by identifying high-risk children for more intensive monitoring, complementing clinical judgment. Prospective multicenter external validation is needed before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for early prediction of severe scrub typhus in older patients.
articles.abstract:
RESULTS: Platelet count (PLT), aspartate Aminotransferase (AST), C-Reactive Protein (CRP), Uric Acid (UA), Fasting Blood Glucose (FBG) and pleural effusion were identified as predictor variables. The RF model achieved the highest AUROC in the external validation cohort. with AUROC, accuracy, F1 score, and Brier score of 0.947, 0.857, 0.632, and 0.084 in the internal validation set, and 0.866, 0.842, 0.623, and 0.119 in the external validation set, respectively. SHAP analysis indicated that lower PLT and higher AST and CRP values generally contributed to higher predicted risks of subsequent severe disease.

CONCLUSION: An ML model was developed and validated to predict severe scrub typhus in elderly patients, guiding early clinical decisions.

articles.title: Topical Tranexamic Acid Versus Nasal Packing for Acute Epistaxis Control and Rebleeding Prevention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute anterior epistaxis is a common emergency. Anterior nasal packing (ANP) is standard but is uncomfortable; Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a promising alternative, but these strategies have not been compared simultaneously.

OBJECTIVE: To compare seven treatments for acute anterior epistaxis-placebo, standard-dose topical TXA, high-dose topical TXA, topical vasoconstrictor, ANP with vasoconstrictor, ANP without vasoconstrictor, and ANP plus topical TXA.

METHODS: In a PROSPERO-registered network meta-analysis, PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, the WHO ICTRP and trial registries, were searched to 30 April 2026 for adults RCTs. A frequentist random-effects model (placebo reference) was used, with RoB 2, SUCRA, and CINeMA. The primary outcome was bleeding cessation within 30 min; secondary, rebleeding at 1-3 and 4-7 days.

RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs (n = 2,166) were included. No treatment improved bleeding cessation; high-dose topical TXA (one trial) ranked highest (OR 3.08, 95% CI 0.77-12.32). High dose (OR 0.16, 0.04-0.57) and standard-dose (OR 0.30, 0.11-0.82) reduced rebleeding at 1-3 days. ANP with vasoconstrictor increased rebleeding at 4-7 days (OR 4.63, 2.02-10.61). Certainty was low to very low.

CONCLUSION: Topical TXA may reduce early rebleeding and is a reasonable noninvasive option, though the high-dose ranking rests on one trial. The ANP-with-vasoconstrictor rebleeding signal needs confirmation.

articles.title: Can oral L-citrulline or L-citrulline malate augment the post-exercise hypotension response? A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantitatively evaluate the effect of oral L-citrulline or L-citrulline malate on the post-exercise hypotension (PEH) response in adults through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: Four databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science) were systematically searched through May 25, 2026. Acute randomised controlled trials (RCTs) investigating oral L-citrulline or L-citrulline malate on post-exercise blood pressure (BP) were included. Effect sizes were pooled using a fixed-effects model, yielding weighted mean differences (WMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Six RCTs were included. Moderate-quality GRADE evidence showed that L-citrulline malate significantly reduced the mean 0-60 min post-exercise systolic BP (WMD -9.02 mmHg, 95% CI -16.22 to -1.82), 24-h ambulatory systolic BP (WMD -8.80, -16.66 to -0.95) and diastolic BP (WMD -7.08, -11.01 to -3.16), daytime systolic BP (WMD -9.31, -16.92 to -1.71) and diastolic BP (WMD -7.50, -11.36 to -3.64), and night-time systolic BP (WMD -7.78, -15.14 to -0.42) and diastolic BP (WMD -4.01, -7.81 to -0.21); all statistically significant (p < 0.05). Low- to very low-quality GRADE evidence yielded inconsistent pooled results for BP measured at 5 and 10 min post-exercise. Evidence for oral L-citrulline was extremely limited: only one trial was available, which could not be quantitatively synthesised; that trial suggested that acute supplementation may enhance the PEH response in hypertensive patients.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis provides the first moderate-quality quantitative evidence that pre-exercise oral L-citrulline malate augments the PEH response; however, this evidence primarily derives from hypertensive patients performing aerobic exercise while receiving supplementation.

articles.title: Comparative cardiovascular safety of febuxostat, allopurinol, and benzbromarone in Taiwanese patients with gout: a retrospective time-varying exposure analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The comparative cardiovascular safety of urate-lowering therapies in patients with gout remains controversial. Our previous network meta-analysis suggested a directionally lower cardiovascular risk with benzbromarone than with febuxostat or allopurinol, but direct head-to-head evidence between benzbromarone and febuxostat was limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Taiwan University Hospital integrated Medical Database. Adults with gout treated with febuxostat, allopurinol, or benzbromarone between July 31, 2016 and August 31, 2023 were included. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of myocardial infarction and stroke. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death. Cox proportional hazards models with time-varying exposure were used to evaluate the time to first occurrence of events.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 3,240 patients, with a median follow-up duration of 4.41 years; 151 patients experienced MACE. All-cause mortality rates per 1,000 person-years were 17.99 overall and 11.31, 25.85, and 9.72 in the benzbromarone, febuxostat, and allopurinol fixed-exposure groups, respectively. In fully adjusted time-varying model using benzbromarone as the reference, no statistically significant difference in MACE was detected for allopurinol (HR 1.63, 95% CI 0.85-3.13) or febuxostat (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.81-1.69). Febuxostat was associated with higher all-cause mortality than benzbromarone (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.13-2.04), and allopurinol was associated with higher stroke risk than benzbromarone (HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.04-3.92).

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference was observed in MACE. However, relative to benzbromarone, febuxostat and allopurinol were associated with higher all-cause mortality and higher stroke risk, respectively.

articles.title: Outcomes of trial of labor after two cesarean deliveries: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global rise in cesarean delivery (CD) rates has led to an increasing number of women with multiple prior CDs. Despite growing evidence in support of trial of labor after two CD (TOLA2C), its adoption remains limited in many settings owing to concerns regarding potential complications, particularly uterine rupture. This study aimed to compare maternal and neonatal outcomes between trial of labor after two cesarean sections (TOLA2C) and elective repeat cesarean delivery (ERCD) within a single institution and to characterize maternal and obstetric features among women with successful and failed TOLA2C.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 333 women with two or more previous CDs who gave birth between January 2021 and December 2023. Women with multiple pregnancies were excluded. Patients were categorized according to the intended mode of delivery into ERCD and TOLA2C groups. Maternal characteristics, birth outcomes, and complications were extracted from digital medical records. Continuous variables were summarized using means with standard deviations and medians with interquartile ranges, and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. Group comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test, Welch's two-sample t-test, chi-square test, or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A p value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: In total, 333 women met the eligibility criteria for the study. Among them, 295 (88.6%) underwent ERCD, whereas 38 (11.4%) attempted TOLA2C. The success rate of TOLA2C was 60.5% (23/38), whereas 39.5% (15/38) required an unplanned CD. Uterine scar dehiscence was identified in one woman undergoing TOLA2C (2.6%) and in 10 women undergoing ERCD (3.4%), whereas complete uterine rupture occurred in one woman with schedulded ERCD (0.3%). No uterine scar event was associated with maternal or neonatal death. No maternal deaths or embolic events were reported, one hysterectomy and one case of intrauterine infection occurred. Overall, there were no significant differences in maternal or neonatal complications between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: Among women with two prior cesarean deliveries in our study population, TOLA2C resulted in vaginal birth in 60.5% of attempts. No statistically significant differences in the evaluated maternal and neonatal complications were detected between TOLA2C and ERCD; however, the small TOLA2C sample and potential selection bias preclude conclusions regarding equivalence or comparative safety. TOLA2C may be considered in appropriately selected women following individualized counseling in adequately equipped obstetric centers.

articles.title: Ethical dilemmas and moral distress among critical care nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic in the central hospitals of a South African province: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moral distress, the psychological discomfort experienced when an individual knows the ethically correct action to take but is constrained from doing so, was exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

OBJECTIVES: The study aimed to examine the ethical dilemmas, prevalence of, and factors associated with moral distress among critical care nurses in South Africa during the pandemic.

METHODS: During 2023, a cross-sectional study was conducted in the four central hospitals of a South African province. In addition to demographic information, the self-administered questionnaire included an adapted Moral Distress of Health Professionals Scale. We grouped the ethical dilemmas into three dimensions of patient care, teamwork and interprofessional collaboration, and the health system. For each of the three dimensions, a separate multiple linear regression model was fitted to examine the factors associated with moral distress.

RESULTS: We recruited 180 nurses and obtained a response rate of 88.2%. The mean age of the nurses was 45.3 years [SD = 9.76], the majority were professional nurses (88.9%) and female (91.1%). The most frequently reported ethical dilemma was working with inexperienced team members (66%).The factors associated with moral distress varied for each of the three dimensions of ethical dilemmas but included infection prevention and control training, collegial stigmatisation, age, access to personal protective equipment, and hospital of employment (p≤0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The study underscores the critical role of positive practice environments and the need for investment in nurses' health and well-being.

articles.title: Managing Hypercontractile Esophagus With Eosinophilic Esophagitis: Response to Sequential Biologics Benralizumab and Dupilumab.
articles.abstract: The association between eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) and esophageal motility disorders remains unclear. A 48-year-old man with asthma presented with chest pain, dysphagia, and heartburn unresponsive to proton pump inhibitors. Esophageal biopsies showed eosinophilic infiltration; high-resolution manometry revealed severe hypercontractility. Following diagnosis of EoE and hypercontractile esophagus, benralizumab induced clinical and histologic normalization. Switching to weekly dupilumab further improved symptoms and motility metrics. This case underscores how sequential biologic therapy targeting eosinophilic inflammation can reverse motility abnormalities and highlights the need for research on inflammation-induced neuromuscular disturbances.

articles.title: Obstetric-Neonatal Collaborations to Reduce Adult Red Blood Cell Transfusions in Extremely Low Birth Weight Neonates.
articles.abstract: Among extremely low birth weight (ELBW, less than 1,000 g) neonates, severe morbidities are common and can impose substantial human and economic burdens. These morbidities include severe retinopathy of prematurity, which may result in permanent visual disturbances or blindness, and severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia, resulting in respiratory limitations that often persist into adulthood. Both conditions involve oxidative damage to developing tissues during the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) stay. An important insight into the pathogenesis of these injuries is the recognition that adult hemoglobin, repeatedly transfused into ELBW infants, releases supraphysiological and damaging amounts of oxygen to the developing retinal and pulmonary vasculature. Fetal hemoglobin, which should constitute 85-100% of the hemoglobin of preterm neonates, releases oxygen to tissues much more sparingly. Consequently, transfusing adult donor red blood cells (RBCs) into ELBW infants is associated with a stepwise increase in the incidence and severity of retinopathy of prematurity and bronchopulmonary dysplasia. This Clinical Perspective focuses on three strategies for obstetricians to help avoid transfusing ELBW neonates with adult RBCs. These are 1) delayed cord clamping at ELBW deliveries, which increases the initial neonatal blood volume by 10-15%; 2) preparing a 6-inch double-clamped segment of umbilical cord from which all initial laboratory blood tests can be drawn, thus averting early neonatal phlebotomy; and 3) participating in translational research efforts to collect otherwise-discarded umbilical cord blood from healthy term deliveries and transporting it to select blood services laboratories developing safe transfusion products for ELBW neonates. These strategies can synergize with other transfusion reduction methods utilized in the NICU to decrease the need to transfuse adult RBCs.

articles.title: Pulmonary embolism and pulmonary infarction triggered by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia during physical restraint in a psychiatric inpatient: A case report.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychiatric inpatients have a high risk of venous thromboembolism because of physical restraint, reduced mobility, and sedation. Although subcutaneous unfractionated heparin (UFH) may be used for thromboprophylaxis during physical restraint, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) can occur even during prophylaxis and remains underrecognized.

CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 20 s was emergently admitted for acute transient psychotic disorder and received UFH for thromboprophylaxis during physical restraint. Nine days after UFH initiation, he developed fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxemia, and pneumonia was initially suspected. However, pulmonary embolism (PE) was later suspected because the respiratory findings were not fully explained by the localized opacity on chest radiographic and the D-dimer level was markedly elevated. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed bilateral pulmonary artery thrombi and right lower lobe pulmonary infarction. After PE diagnosis, escalation of UFH therapy produced little clinical improvement and thrombocytopenia developed. Anticoagulation was switched to apixaban, a direct oral anticoagulant. after which, oxygenation improved and the platelet count recovered. The 4Ts score, a clinical pretest probability score for HIT, was 6/8, and the HIT antibody test was positive, supporting the diagnosis of HIT, which became clinically apparent during UFH thromboprophylaxis.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights HIT as an underrecognized complication of thromboprophylaxis during psychiatric restraint and underscores the diagnostic challenge of PE with pulmonary infarction mimicking pneumonia. Careful platelet monitoring during UFH therapy, regular pulse oximetry, and early suspicion of PE, even when pneumonia is initially suspected, are important in resource-limited psychiatric settings.

articles.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Versus Metformin for Adults on Antipsychotics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Evidence for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1s) to treat antipsychotic-associated weight gain is limited. A comparison of 52-week weight loss with semaglutide/tirzepatide versus metformin in adults taking antipsychotics was conducted using nationwide electronic health record data.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Truveta database. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to compare the percent initial weight loss between GLP-1 and metformin users. Weight loss by diabetes status, antipsychotic type, medication adherence, and type of GLP-1 medication (semaglutide vs. tirzepatide) was evaluated.

RESULTS: The cohort included 10,424 adults initiating semaglutide or tirzepatide and 22,788 initiating metformin while taking antipsychotics. Mean weight change was -7.5% ± 0.1% with GLP-1s versus -1.7% ± 0.1% with metformin (p < 0.001). GLP-1 users had greater odds of achieving ≥ 5%, ≥ 10%, and ≥ 15% weight loss across all subgroups. Weight loss was lower among individuals with diabetes, those taking olanzapine or clozapine, and those with lower medication adherence. Mean weight change was -10.6% ± 0.2% with tirzepatide versus -7.0% ± 0.2% with semaglutide (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Semaglutide and tirzepatide were associated with substantially greater weight loss than metformin in adults taking antipsychotics. Improving medication continuity may enhance treatment effectiveness in this population.

articles.title: Cold shock alters MAPK signaling to create a permissive cell state for BK polyomavirus production.
articles.abstract: BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) persists in the kidneys of >75% of adults, and viral reactivation in donor kidneys early after kidney transplantation is a major cause of kidney graft dysfunction and loss. However, the mechanisms that trigger BKPyV reactivation are poorly understood. Here, using primary human renal proximal tubule epithelial cells, the cell type in which BKPyV persists in the kidney, we show that transient cold exposure followed by rewarming enhances BKPyV production independently of viral attachment through mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling during an early postrewarming window. This MAPK-dependent effect is marked by increased viral gene expression, prolonged S phase, and higher viral titers and is abolished by transient MAPK inhibition immediately after rewarming. These findings identify temperature-dependent MAPK signaling as a driver of BKPyV production and suggest a mechanism by which transplant-associated cold storage may contribute to viral reactivation.

articles.title: Temporal Trends of Mortality Due to Obesity in the United States, 1999-2022, an Analysis of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention WONDER Database: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity, the excess body fat, is a chronic problem that disrupts both physical and mental health. Obesity is linked to diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, making it the second most frequent preventable cause leading to death. Contemporary national trends in obesity-related mortality, including the COVID-19 pandemic period, remain incompletely characterized. We therefore examined temporal trends in obesity-related mortality in the United States from 1999 to 2022 by sex, age group, census region, and place of death.

METHODS: Deidentified data from CDC WONDER database were used in our study. The International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) code E66 was used to identify cases in which obesity was recorded as an underlying or contributing cause of death between 1999 and 2022. The data were extracted based on age, gender, year, population size, census region, and place of death. Annual percent changes (APC) and age adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100,000 people were utilized in our study to analyse the mortality trends of Obesity in the United States using Joinpoint regression.

RESULTS: During 1999-2022, obesity caused 840,975 deaths in the United States. The Obesity AAMR was 4.7 per 100,000 in 1999, which rose to 18.9 in 2022, after a peak of 24.73 in 2021. An APC of 6.76 (95% CI 5.68-7.85) was calculated for this increase. Men had an average AAMR of 10.91, while it was 9.03 for women. The young- aged group had an average AAMR of 4.74, it was 19.68 for the middle-aged group, and 27.88 for the old-age group. The South region exhibited the highest mortality burden (most deaths, highest 2022 AAMR [20.35] and steepest APC [7.53%]), although the West had the highest period-average AAMR (10.56), while the Northeast region showed the lowest average AAMR (8.37). Regional differences in mortality rates were observed across all census regions during the study period.

CONCLUSION: Mortality due to obesity has been increasing significantly (more than fourfold) between 1999 and 2022. Mortality rates were higher in men and older adults, and the South bore the highest regional burden. The rate peaked in 2021 and declined in 2022 but remained about fourfold above its 1999 level. Further research using individual-level data is needed to clarify the drivers of this increase, including changes in death-certification practices and the role of COVID-19.

articles.title: Real-World Treatment Trajectories and Outcomes in Adult Secondary Hemophagocytic Lympho-Histiocytosis Identified Through Bone Marrow Hemophagocytosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adult secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) remains a diagnostically complex syndrome with heterogeneous triggers and treatment strategies.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective observational cohort study of adult patients with HLH identified through a hematology laboratory database of bone marrow aspirates showing hemophagocytosis at a tertiary university hospital (2014-2019). HLH was adjudicated using a structured multi-reviewer process; the index date was the bone marrow aspirate date. Baseline clinical and laboratory features (including retrospectively calculated HScore) were captured at index. HLH-directed therapies were abstracted as sequential treatment lines (first through fourth line) with dates, drug classes, and recorded responses when available. Outcomes included 30-day mortality, status at 1, 6, and 12 months (discharged, hospitalized, deceased), 12-month survival, and multivariable models of 12-month mortality.

RESULTS: We analyzed 167 patients (median age 55 years; 62% male); 58% required ICU transfer. Etiologies were malignancy-associated (46%), infection-associated (39%), and autoimmune/inflammatory-associated (12%). Thirty-day mortality was 31% and 12-month mortality 49%, with worse survival in malignancy-associated HLH. First-line therapy most frequently included corticosteroids (44%), while etoposide was used in 23% at any time. Second-line therapy was recorded in 28% and third-line therapy in 5%, highlighting heterogeneous escalation trajectories. In adjusted analyses, ICU transfer, older age, malignancy-associated etiology, and lower platelet counts were independently associated with 12-month mortality.

CONCLUSION: These data underscore the high mortality of adult HLH and the marked variability of treatment trajectories, supporting the need for standardized prospective adult-focused strategies and registries.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Diabetic Complications Among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in Addis Ababa Hospitals, Ethiopia: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a growing public health concern globally and in Ethiopia. Its prevalence is rapidly increasing in urban settings like Addis Ababa, driven by rapid urbanization, changing lifestyles, and dietary habits, which in turn escalates the burden of its complications. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of diabetic complications and identify associated factors among adult type 2 diabetic patients attending diabetes mellitus clinics in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted at the diabetes mellitus clinics of government hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. A total of 362 patients with type 2 diabetes were selected using a systematic random sampling technique. Data were collected using Kobo Toolbox and exported to SPSS version 27.0. Descriptive statistics summarized socio-demographic characteristics, as well as knowledge and attitudes regarding type 2 diabetes mellitus complications. A multivariable logistic regression model was employed to identify independent predictors of type 2 diabetic complications.

RESULT: This study found that the prevalence of diabetic complications was 67.4% (95% CI: 62.6%, 72.3%). Factors significantly associated with these complications included other comorbidities (AOR: 4.64; 95% CI: 1.6-12.9), poor glycemic control (AOR: 8.78; 95% CI: 3.9-19.5), and not strictly adhering to dietary recommendations (AOR: 3.9; 95% CI: 1.7-9.04).

CONCLUSION: Diabetic complications were notably prevalent among adult patients, affecting 67.4%. Poor glycemic control, inadequate dietary adherence, and coexisting chronic illnesses were significantly linked to these complications. These findings underscore the need to strengthen diabetes care by enhancing glycemic control, providing dietary counseling, managing comorbidities, and promoting lifestyle modifications.

articles.title: Self-Care Practices and Influencing Factors Among Adults With Diabetes Mellitus in Rural Vhembe District, South Africa: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes mellitus remains a major public health challenge in South Africa, with rising mortality and complications despite the availability of effective self-care strategies. This study explored and described self-care practices and influencing factors among adults with diabetes in rural Vhembe district.

METHODS: A qualitative, exploratory and descriptive design was employed. Fifteen adult participants were purposively recruited, and semi-structured interviews were conducted in Tshivenda. Data saturation was reached at the 11th interview. Farmer's six-step thematic analysis guided data analysis.

RESULTS: Three themes emerged: diabetes self-care practices, facilitating factors and hindering factors. Medication adherence was the most consistently reported self-care practice, with participants demonstrating knowledge of prescribed medications, dosing schedules and medication collection procedures. Dietary management and physical activity were less evident, with participants relying on available staple foods and routine household or farming activities rather than structured exercise. Financial constraints, limited social support and physical limitations hindered self-care, particularly dietary management and physical activity, whereas home-based care worker support, family support and self-motivation facilitated self-care, especially medication adherence.

CONCLUSION: Although medication adherence was generally well maintained, engagement in other diabetes self-care practices was limited. Self-care was influenced by both facilitating and hindering factors, highlighting the need for supportive social, economic and community environments. Strengthening diabetes education and community-based support programmes may promote comprehensive self-care in dietary management and physical activity, including other vital self-care practices, such as foot care and blood glucose self-monitoring.

articles.title: The COVID-19 Pandemic and Patterns of In-Hospital Death in Cirrhosis: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with cirrhosis are at risk of death not only from complications of liver disease but also from infection and comorbid conditions. We aimed to describe how the interplay between COVID-19 pandemic and reasons for terminal hospitalization in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional retrospective analysis of in-hospital deaths in patients with cirrhosis using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2023. Hospitalizations were classified into 10 primary diagnosis categories, including infection and liver disease without specified complication. COVID-19 hospitalizations were categorized as infection-related. The proportion of terminal hospitalizations attributable to each category was compared between pre-pandemic and pandemic-era hospitalizations. Additionally, the proportions of terminal hospitalizations due to hepatic encephalopathy (HE), hepatorenal syndrome (HRS), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), portal hypertensive bleeding, and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) were compared between eras.

RESULTS: A total of 394,380 in-hospital deaths were identified. Infection accounted for a greater proportion of terminal hospitalizations during the pandemic era compared with the pre-pandemic era (42.3% vs. 40.1%, p < 0.001) and peaked in April 2020 at 53.5%. COVID-19 terminal hospitalizations peaked in September 2020 at 1145. Infection-related terminal hospitalizations returned to pre-pandemic levels in 2023. HE, HRS, HCC, portal hypertensive bleeding, and SBP together accounted for 8.8% of pre-pandemic terminal hospitalizations and 6.0% of pandemic-era terminal hospitalizations (p < 0.001), with each complication declining in proportion and absolute number over time.

CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a marked but transient increase in infection-related terminal hospitalizations among patients with cirrhosis, while terminal hospitalizations due to traditional cirrhosis complications continued to decline.

articles.title: Health Needs Assessment Using the PRECEDE-PROCEED Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Community health needs assessment is a systematic process for identifying and prioritizing health problems, needs, and related determinants at the community level and can provide a basis for responsive health planning. This study aimed to identify and prioritize the major health needs of a community in Ardabil County, Iran, using a mixed-methods approach informed by the PRECEDE-PROCEED model.

METHODS: A community-based mixed-methods health needs assessment was conducted over 10 months in 2025. The assessment integrated three complementary sources of information: local health-system data, a quantitative household assessment of 301 residents aged ≥ 18 years, and eight focus group discussions involving 70 community residents. A structured checklist was used for the quantitative assessment. Qualitative data were analyzed using a framework-based approach informed by the PRECEDE-PROCEED model. Twelve community residents, separate from the focus group participants, participated in the priority-ranking process, in which health problems were ranked and final priorities were identified.

RESULTS: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), cancer, and diabetes were identified as major priority health problems across the overall assessment, with CVDs emerging as the first priority in the community ranking process. The quantitative assessment identified insufficient physical activity (66.1%), limited awareness of CVD risk factors (74.1%), and gaps in preventive health education (53.1%). Qualitative findings identified predisposing, enabling, and reinforcing factors affecting healthy lifestyles and disease prevention, including limited knowledge of CVD prevention, inadequate skills and access to resources, and lack of social support, peer relationships, and support groups.

CONCLUSION: The identified community health needs included major chronic diseases as well as modifiable behavioral, educational, and social factors. Integrating local health-system data with quantitative and qualitative community perspectives within the PRECEDE-PROCEED framework may provide a structured basis for identifying and prioritizing local health needs and informing community-responsive health planning.

articles.title: Toxicity-Weighted Pesticide Exposure in County-Level Cancer Models: Endpoint Matching, Spatial Dependence, and Geographic Validation.
articles.abstract: The objective of this study was to evaluate whether toxicity-weighted pesticide exposure improves county-level cancer models, whether endpoint-matched metrics provide different model performance, and whether observed associations persist after accounting for spatial dependence and geographic validation. Data were collected for 3,107 U.S. counties, including USGS pesticide use estimates for 408 compounds during 2010-2012, cancer incidence from NCI and CDC State Cancer Profiles for 2018 to 2022, diabetes and coronary heart disease (CHD) prevalence from CDC PLACES, socioeconomic indicators from the U.S. Census, and climate variables from NOAA. Pesticide exposure was represented using applied mass, chronic reference dose (RfD) weighted load, cancer slope factor weighted load, and cancer weight of evidence. Model performance was assessed using adjusted R2, AIC, residual Moran's I, spatial error models, and leave-one-state-out cross validation. Although the RfD weighted load improved model fit for cancer incidence relative to applied mass (ΔAIC = -9.1), cancer-specific weighting did not provide a comparable improvement. The socioeconomic block produced the largest increase in model fit, while climate contributed to smaller improvements. Residual spatial autocorrelation remained strong after covariate adjustment, with Moran's I of 0.656 for the saturated cancer model. In the spatial error model, the coefficient for RfD weighted exposure decreased from β = 8.61 to β = 1.35 and was no longer statistically significant (p = 0.26). These findings show that toxicity weighting can change exposure priorities, but better model fit does not establish a toxicological or epidemiological relationship.

articles.title: Evaluating the feasibility of a nurse-informed, context-driven large language model pipeline for social determinants of health in heart failure care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a nurse-informed large language model (LLM)-based pipeline for extracting the presence of social determinants of health (SDOH) from unstructured electronic health record (EHR) clinical notes among patients with heart failure (HF).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We evaluated the feasibility and performance of a prompt-based pipeline using 2 deployable LLMs (GPT-4o-mini and LLaMA 3.1 70B). The models were applied to 90 clinical notes from 90 unique patients, sampled from approximately 3300 notes within a single urban health system (2021-2024). SDOH were operationalized using the Healthy People 2030 framework, with a nurse-informed, context-driven annotation rubric tailored to the HF population. Model performance was assessed using single-domain and all-domain rubric prompting across 6 SDOH domains.

RESULTS: GPT-4o-mini outperformed LLaMA 3.1 70B under an all-domain prompting structure, achieving a weighted F1 score of 0.621. Using this all-domain prompt, domain-level performance for GPT-4o-mini was highest for social support (F1 = 0.895), followed by education (0.703), physical environment (0.621), food insecurity (0.550), and housing (0.540). Access to care showed the lowest performance (F1 = 0.455).

DISCUSSION: Domain-specific performance differences highlight the value of nurse-informed annotation in capturing contextually documented SDOH in HF care, supporting domain-specific prompting strategies for scalable SDOH extraction in clinical informatics. Future model performance improvements may be achieved through prompt refinement and nurse-in-the-loop error analysis.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the feasibility of a nurse-informed, context-driven LLM-based pipeline for SDOH extraction from unstructured clinical notes in HF care.

articles.title: Empirical broad-spectrum antibiotic use, de-escalation, and outcomes in Enterobacterales bloodstream infections: a retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate empirical and definitive antibiotic prescribing practices and outcomes of patients with bloodstream infection (BSI) due to Enterobacterales.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study enrolling all consecutive adult patients admitted to the Emergency Department of Niguarda Hospital, Italy, with a monomicrobial BSI due to an Enterobacterales from January 2019 to December 2023 was performed.

RESULTS: 667 patients with a BSI due Enterobacterales were enrolled, 57.1% with sepsis and 16.5% with septic shock. Third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales (3GCR-E) accounted for 25.6% and were associated with a 10-fold higher risk of inappropriate empirical therapy (OR 10.7; 95%confidence interval (CI) 6.10-18.74). Piperacillin-tazobactam was the most frequently prescribed empiric antibiotic in the entire cohort (54.3%). Among patients with non-3GCR-E BSI, 57.7% received unnecessary broad-spectrum empiric coverage with piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenems, yet de-escalation occurred in only 31.7% of those eligible. Overall, in-hospital mortality was 10.2%, with no difference between 3GCR-E and non-3GCR-E BSI (OR 0.89; 95%CI 0.49-1.6). Mortality was associated with age (OR 1.55; 95%CI 1.17-2.06), Charlson Comorbidity Index (OR 1.24; 95%CI 1.12-1.38), immunosuppression (OR 2.07; 95%CI 1.1-3.95), respiratory infection (OR 3.13; 95%CI 1.28-7.65) and septic shock (OR 5.49; 95%CI 2.95-10.21), whereas urinary tract infection was associated with higher survival (OR 0.43, 95%CI 0.21-0.91).

CONCLUSIONS: 3GCR-E BSIs are common beyond hospital-acquired infections and are strongly associated with inappropriate empirical therapy. Broad-spectrum agents are frequently used empirically, including in non-3GCR-E BSI, while de-escalation remains underused. Improved early 3GCR-E risk stratification and targeted stewardship interventions are needed to optimize empiric prescribing and de-escalation.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of ceftazidime/avibactam-resistant KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae infections: impact of meropenem susceptibility and comparison with ceftazidime/avibactam-susceptible infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ceftazidime/avibactam resistance is an emerging challenge among KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (KPC-Kp). We aimed to characterize ceftazidime/avibactam-resistant (R) infections according to meropenem susceptibility and previous ceftazidime/avibactam exposure and assess the association between ceftazidime/avibactam resistance and outcomes.

METHODS: This single-centre observational study included patients with ceftazidime/avibactam-R KPC-Kp infections, stratified by meropenem susceptibility and previous ceftazidime/avibactam exposure. Outcomes according to definitive treatment were explored in ceftazidime/avibactam-R/meropenem-susceptible (S) infections. Among patients with KPC-Kp bloodstream infection (BSI), outcomes were compared between ceftazidime/avibactam-R and ceftazidime/avibactam-S infections using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW).

RESULTS: Overall, 137 ceftazidime/avibactam-R infections were included: 47 (34.3%) were ceftazidime/avibactam-R/meropenem-S with previous ceftazidime/avibactam exposure, 24 (17.5%) ceftazidime/avibactam-R/meropenem-S without previous exposure and 66 (48.2%) ceftazidime/avibactam-R/meropenem resistant. Among ceftazidime/avibactam-R/meropenem-S infections, 30-day mortality did not significantly differ between meropenem-containing and newer-agent-based regimens, although recurrence and emergence of meropenem resistance occurred more frequently in patients receiving meropenem-containing therapy. The BSI analysis included 235 patients (61 ceftazidime/avibactam-R; 174 ceftazidime/avibactam-S). Thirty-day mortality was similar (18.0% versus 19.5%; P = 0.797), and ceftazidime/avibactam resistance was not associated with mortality after IPTW (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.41-2.45). No significant differences in clinical cure or BSI recurrence were observed after weighting.

CONCLUSIONS: Ceftazidime/avibactam-R KPC-Kp infections comprise distinct profiles according to meropenem susceptibility and previous ceftazidime/avibactam exposure. Retained meropenem susceptibility may have therapeutic relevance; however, recurrence and emergence of meropenem resistance in patients receiving meropenem-containing regimens warrant caution. Ceftazidime/avibactam resistance was not independently associated with adverse outcomes in KPC-Kp BSI.

articles.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Kidney Stone Disease in Northern Iran: A Cross-Sectional Study Based on Data From the Registration Phase of the Tabari Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney stone disease is a common condition with substantial geographic variation in prevalence. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of physician-diagnosed kidney stone history and examine its demographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, anthropometric, metabolic, and clinical correlates among adults participating in the Tabari Cohort Study (TCS) in northern Iran.

METHODS: This analytical cross-sectional study used enrollment-phase data from 9939 adults aged 35-70 years enrolled in the TCS, a component of the Prospective Epidemiological Research Studies in Iran (PERSIAN) Cohort. Kidney stone history was assessed through standardized cohort questioning, with participants asked about a previous physician diagnosis and related treatment. Demographic, behavioral, anthropometric, metabolic, and clinical variables were assessed using standardized cohort procedures. Associations were examined using binary logistic regression, with multivariable models used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Overall, 16.2% of participants reported a history of physician-diagnosed kidney stones. Kidney stone history was more common among men and older participants and was associated with several demographic and cardiometabolic characteristics. In the overall multivariable analysis, older age, male sex (aOR, 2.26; 95% CI, 1.76-2.89), hypertension (aOR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.29-1.76), and cardiovascular disease (aOR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.09-1.64) were associated with higher odds of kidney stone history. In sex-stratified multivariable analyses, hypertension remained associated with kidney stone history in both women (aOR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.13-1.72) and men (aOR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.29-1.91), whereas obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) was associated with higher odds only in the male-specific model (aOR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.07-2.00).

CONCLUSION: Kidney stone history was common among adults in the Tabari Cohort and was associated with older age, male sex, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease in the overall adjusted analysis. Obesity was also associated with kidney stone history in the male-specific model. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal relationships.

articles.title: Prevalence, Outcomes, and Social and Clinical Risk Factors of Preeclampsia: A Population-Based Study in Mashhad, Iran.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Preeclampsia, a multifactorial hypertensive disorder of pregnancy, significantly impacts maternal and neonatal health. While clinical risk factors are established, social and geographic disparities remain underexplored. This analytical cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, outcomes, and risk factors associated with preeclampsia among women covered by Mashhad University of Medical Sciences, focusing on these disparities.

METHODS: Data were reviewed from 82,014 deliveries during 2022, including 354 mothers with preeclampsia and 1062 without. The prevalence of preeclampsia was 0.43%, lower than national estimates, likely reflecting registry-based diagnosis. Inclusion criteria were a registry diagnosis of preeclampsia, defined as systolic blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure ≥ 90 mmHg after 20 weeks of gestation accompanied by proteinuria ≥ 300 mg/24 h. All preeclampsia cases were included regardless of severity; the registry did not subclassify cases as mild or severe.

RESULTS: Mothers with preeclampsia were younger, had higher pre-pregnancy BMI, and were more likely to be multiparous. Histories of hypertension and diabetes were more common. Geographic disparities were evident, with higher rates among rural residents. Affected pregnancies resulted in lower neonatal birth weight, length, and head circumference, along with higher rates of cesarean delivery and preterm birth. Neonatal hospital admissions were higher in the control group, possibly due to other clinical factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is linked to significant complications. Key risk factors include high BMI, preexisting diabetes or hypertension, adverse obstetric history, and rural residence.

articles.title: Factors Associated With Home-Based Management of Hypertension Among Older Adults: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study in the Amansie Central District, Ghana.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Home-based management strategies are crucial for improving hypertension outcomes, yet a complex interplay of knowledge, practices, and socio-demographic factors influences effectiveness. This study examined the factors associated with the home-based management of hypertension among older adults in the Amansie Central District.

METHODS: We conducted a community-based, quantitative cross-sectional study among 309 older adults (aged 60 years and above) with hypertension. Participants were selected via systematic random sampling from health facility and community registers. Data were collected using interviewer-administered self-developed questionnaires. Descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages) and inferential analyzes (binary logistic regression) were performed using R software to identify factors associated with knowledge and practice of home management of hypertension.

RESULTS: Overall, more than half of the participants had poor knowledge of hypertension (52.4%). The factors associated with knowledge of hypertension were marital status (χ2 = 9.595, p-value = 0.007), educational level (χ2 = 12.643, p-value = 0.005), employment status (χ2== 7.034, p-value = 0.008), monthly income level (χ2 = 47.238, p-value < 0.001), and body weight (χ2 = 11.706, p-value = 0.002). Older adults with primary-level education were more likely to have good knowledge than those with no formal education (AOR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.60-11.4, p-value = 0.004). Also, employed individuals were less likely to have good knowledge than the unemployed (AOR = 0.51, 95% CI: 0.27-0.95, p-value = 0.035). Participants earning more than 4000 Ghana cedis (AOR = 10.9, 95% CI: 4.38-29.5, p-value < 0.001) and those earning no income (AOR = 7.9, 95%CI 2.60-27.0 p-value < 0.001) were significantly more likely to have good knowledge than those earning ≤ 1000. Overall, more than half of the older adults had poor practices (51.8%) of home management of hypertension. Participants aged 66-70 years had significantly lower odds of demonstrating good practices compared to those aged 60-65 years (AOR = 0.48, 95% CI:0.26-0.89, p-value = 0.021).

CONCLUSION: There is a need for targeted, behavior-focused interventions that extend beyond education to include practical support, family involvement, and strategies tailored to bridge the gap between knowledge and practice.

articles.title: Association Between Vitamin Knowledge, Practices, and Sleep Quality Among Undergraduate Students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep disruptions are prevalent among university students and negatively impact well-being. Vitamins, including B6, B12, and D, support sleep regulation via neurotransmitter synthesis and circadian pathways. However, empirical data evaluating student literacy and dietary practices regarding these micronutrients remain scarce in low-resource African settings.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate vitamin-related knowledge and practices, examine their associations with self-reported sleep parameters, and determine the sociodemographic factors associated with vitamin knowledge among undergraduate students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted between March and May 2025 among 381 undergraduate students recruited via convenience sampling. A validated structured questionnaire captured sociodemographic data, vitamin knowledge, dietary practices, and sleep parameters using an adapted composite sleep scale based on the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression in SPSS version 26.

RESULTS: Self-reported sleep disturbances were widespread, characterized by short sleep duration (< 7 h: 59.9%), nocturnal awakenings (45.6%), and daytime fatigue (48.8% at least weekly). The mean vitamin knowledge score was 13.39 (±6.22), with 56.4% classified as having good relative knowledge; health program students demonstrated higher knowledge across multiple domains (p < 0.05). The mean practice score was 4.00 (±0.49), with 60.4% categorized as having good relative practices, although food label checking (13.1% always) and healthcare consultation for supplement use (19.7% always) were low. Mean adapted composite sleep problem scores were significantly lower (more favorable) among students with good vitamin knowledge compared to poor knowledge (t = -2.511, p = 0.012), whereas no significant difference was observed by vitamin practice category (t = 1.048, p = 0.48). In adjusted logistic regression, female sex was associated with lower odds of good vitamin knowledge (aOR = 0.605, 95% CI: 0.382-0.958, p = 0.032), while married status was associated with higher odds (aOR = 3.833, 95% CI: 1.058-13.891, p = 0.041).

CONCLUSION: Self-reported sleep disturbances are prevalent among undergraduate students at the University of Cape Coast, Ghana. Although higher vitamin literacy was associated with fewer self-reported sleep problems, self-reported dietary practices showed no direct association, and notable micronutrient knowledge deficits persisted. Integrated campus wellness initiatives should address both sleep hygiene and practical nutritional literacy, while future research requires biochemical validation and longitudinal designs.

articles.title: Authorship of articles from secondary data using global health datasets from low- and middle-income countries: a systematic mapping of publications.
articles.abstract: Secondary analyses of large-scale global health datasets, such as the Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) and Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS), generate vital evidence for public health policy and programming. However, authorship in such studies remains unevenly distributed, with persistent regional disparities that limit inclusivity in global health knowledge production. We conducted a systematic mapping review examining publications from 2000 to 2025 that used publicly available secondary global health datasets originating from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Five databases were searched for articles. Descriptive analysis was conducted while multinomial logistic regression and marginal effect analyses identified factors associated with author position. From 2167 eligible articles, 5925 authors were extracted of which 36.0% (n = 2132) were affiliated with high-income countries (HICs) and 27.4% (n = 1626) with low-income countries (LICs). Multivariable analysis showed that authors with a single institutional affiliation had a 32% lower relative risk ratio of being first author compared with those with dual institutional affiliations (adjusted relative risk ratio, aRRR = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.56-0.83). Compared with female authors, the relative risk ratio of being last (versus second) author was 1.19 times higher for males (aRRR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.02-1.38). HIC-affiliated authors made up the largest share of authors of studies using LMIC data, and author position was associated with institutional affiliation and sex. To increase the contribution of LMIC researchers to global health research using secondary data, deliberate investments are needed in research infrastructure, capacity strengthening, and institutional policies that promote open data use and equitable authorship.

articles.title: War-related post-traumatic stress disorder among conflict-affected civilians: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
articles.abstract: War-related post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a major mental health consequence of armed conflict among civilians, yet reported prevalence estimates vary considerably and the reliability of the underlying evidence remains uncertain. This umbrella review aimed to map and appraise the methodological quality of systematic reviews and meta-analyses addressing war-related PTSD among conflict-affected civilian populations and, secondarily, to re-synthesize prevalence estimates where feasible. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA 2020, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to August 2025. Eligible reviews examined PTSD prevalence, risk factors, or interventions among refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and non-displaced residents of conflict-affected areas. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2. Usable review-level prevalence estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were re-pooled using random-effects models on the logit scale. Eighteen reviews, including 12 meta-analyses, published between 2012 and 2025, covered conflicts across five world regions. Reported PTSD prevalence ranged from 11.6% among Lebanese civilians to 61.9% among Iraqi IDPs. Re-analysis of six reviews yielded a pooled prevalence of 28.0% (95% CI 22.0-34.9%; I2 = 87.8%), with higher estimates among displaced/refugee populations (43.7%; 95% CI 24.6-65.0%) than general samples (23.4%; 95% CI 20.3-26.7%). No review achieved high methodological quality; three were moderate, six low, and nine critically low. Overall, substantial methodological limitations and heterogeneity undermine confidence in existing estimates. Nevertheless, the findings highlight the considerable PTSD burden, particularly among displaced populations, underscoring the need for standardized diagnostic assessments, rigorous evidence synthesis, targeted screening, and accessible trauma-focused care.

articles.title: Clinical testing source is associated with observed HPV burden in hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping: a retrospective study of 36,362 women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospital-based cervical HPV genotyping datasets include women tested through different clinical pathways, so observed HPV burden may vary by source population. We quantified source-specific HPV burden and evaluated cytology-linked context.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational study of 36,362 women with one retained index HPV test per woman. All underwent uniform 23-type cervical HPV genotyping by PCR-reverse dot blot and were classified as health examination attendees or gynecology outpatients by clinical testing source. Primary outcomes were any HPV positivity, 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity, and multiple-genotype infection. Source-group prevalence ratios were adjusted for age group and calendar quarter of testing. Cytology was linked within a prespecified ±3-day window.

RESULTS: The cohort included 9,969 health examination attendees and 26,393 gynecology outpatients; cytology was linked for 34,049 women (93.6%). Compared with health examination attendees, gynecology outpatients had higher any HPV positivity (28.7% vs 17.2%; adjusted PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.54-1.69), 12-type carcinogenic HPV positivity (19.4% vs 10.7%; adjusted PR, 1.75; 95% CI, 1.65-1.86), and multiple-genotype infection (9.2% vs 3.9%; adjusted PR, 2.23; 95% CI, 2.01-2.48). HPV16/18 and HPV52/58 positivity also varied across cytology strata. Source-group contrasts were attenuated but remained in the same direction after exclusion of an HPV/STI-related clinical-label subset and after restriction to women with linked cytology.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical testing source was associated with substantial differences in observed HPV burden within a uniform hospital laboratory workflow, highlighting the importance of clinical setting and source population when hospital-based HPV estimates are interpreted.

articles.title: Phosphate-containing versus phosphate-free replacement solution in critically ill patients requiring continuous renal replacement therapy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
