OBJECTIVE: Hypophosphatemia is a common electrolyte disturbance in critically ill patients receiving continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of phosphate-containing versus phosphate-free replacement solutions in preventing CRRT-associated hypophosphatemia.

METHODS: In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 90 patients requiring CRRT were randomly assigned to receive phosphate-containing or phosphate-free replacement solutions. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypophosphatemia during the first 48 h of CRRT. Prespecified secondary outcomes included phosphate supplementation, hyperphosphatemia, glucose-related safety outcomes, insulin requirements, and exploratory assessments of serum creatinine and SOFA score.

RESULTS: A total of 90 patients were randomized (45 per group), with comparable baseline characteristics, including age, SOFA score, sepsis, CKD, and serum phosphate levels. Patients receiving phosphate-containing replacement solutions had a significantly lower incidence of hypophosphatemia than those receiving phosphate-free solutions (15.6% vs. 68.9%; adjusted OR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.01-0.18). The phosphate-containing group also required less phosphate supplementation. Hypoglycemia was more frequent in the phosphate-containing group than in the phosphate-free group (8.9% vs. 0%; p = 0.042). No significant between-group differences were observed in serum creatinine or SOFA score.

CONCLUSION: Phosphate-containing replacement solutions reduced hypophosphatemia and phosphate supplementation requirements during the first 48 h of CRRT. Given the observed transient hypoglycemia and hyperphosphatemia, particularly in patients with preexisting hyperphosphatemia, careful monitoring of serum phosphate and glucose is warranted. Larger multicenter trials with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these biochemical benefits translate into clinically meaningful patient outcomes.

articles.title: Mapping unsolved lipidomes accelerates lipid discovery in major bacterial pathogens.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic bacteria use specialized lipids to promote virulence. Unlike genomes, the scope of lipids in many bacterial pathogens remains undefined. Here we report a discovery lipidomics platform to generate a resource of mass-defined unnamed lipids in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). From a pool of 312 qualified but unknown features, we developed quality metrics to prioritize mass spectrometry signals consistent with genuine undiscovered lipids for chemical identification. Leveraging this list for molecular discovery, we identified a family of lysine lipoamino acids in Mtb that was also broadly conserved among mycobacteria. Identification and disruption of the biosynthetic gene, lysX, attenuated Mycobacterium marinum infection of zebrafish, demonstrating a role in virulence. Recognition and deletion of the orthologous virulence gene, mprF, in Staphylococcus aureus identified the same lipoamino acids. This lipidomic map of mass-defined unknown molecules represents a resource for immediate follow-up in Mtb and established a discovery framework applicable to any bacterial pathogen.

articles.title: Association between self-reported severe headache or migraine and mortality among chronic kidney disease patients with or without obesity in the United States: a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Migraine and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are both serious public health issues with increasing incidence and mortality rates each year, resulting in a heavy economic burden. While obesity is linked to both conditions, data on the association between migraine and mortality among CKD patients with or without obesity are limited.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted from 1999 to 2004, involving 749 participants. The endpoint for the study was all-cause mortality, with follow-up to December 31, 2019. The association between self-reported severe headache or migraine and mortality was investigated employing the multivariable Cox proportional hazard regression, stratified by obesity status (Body Mass Index < 30 kg/m2 vs. ≥ 30 kg/m2).Results Among 749 CKD participants (mean age 46.5 years, 414 females), 177 had self-reported severe headache or migraine. Over a median follow-up of 204 months, 208 deaths occurred. Adjusted analysis showed higher mortality risk in CKD patients with self-reported severe headache or migraine (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.14-2.16). This association was stronger in the obese group (HR = 3.03, 95% CI: 1.94-4.73) than in the non-obese group (HR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.53-1.47). Significant multiplicative (p = 0.002) and additive interactions (relative excess risk due to interaction [RERI] = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.33-1.76; attributable proportion due to interaction [AP] = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.31-0.97) were observed.Conclusions Self-reported severe headache or migraine was significantly associated with mortality in CKD patients, particularly in the obese population. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Plaque Remodeling Without Significant Regression.
A nanoscale gap junction-perinexus nanodomain governs balance of ephaptic and gap-junctional activation in excitable cell pairs.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Electrical communication between excitable cells depends on gap junction (GJ) currents and field-mediated ephaptic interactions, but their relative contributions have been difficult to quantify, limiting insight into arrhythmia and other disorders of bioelectric signaling. Building on the nanoscale, sodium channel-rich perinexus at the cardiac intercalated disc, we developed a "Single-on-Paired" (SoP) preparation, recording whole-cell sodium current from one adult ventricular myocyte that remains coupled by an intercalated disc to an intact partner. This revealed a composite two-cell sodium current with two rising-phase slopes and an activation jump between closely spaced voltage steps, an "Intercalated Disc Signature" (IDS) absent from isolated single myocytes and providing a direct readout of intercellular activation. Rapid sodium channel activation cannot be resolved under voltage clamp at physiological extracellular sodium ([Na+]o), so SoP recordings used reduced [Na+]o of 25 to 35 mM. Within this nonphysiologic range, graded GJ inhibition, perinexal widening with an Scn1b-derived competitive adhesion peptide, and [Na+]o modulation showed that GJ inhibition abolished the IDS at 25 mM, whereas a modest 10 mM rise to 35 mM restored it despite persistent GJ inhibition. GJ coupling and a perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanism are thus separable contributors to intercellular activation whose relative engagement is set by extracellular sodium. A two-cell computational model constrained by these data reproduces the IDS and predicts that at physiological 145 mM [Na+]o with reduced GJ conductance, perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanisms suffice for intercellular activation. Clamping cleft potential, but not cleft sodium, disrupts this behavior in silico, identifying cleft potential as the proximal ephaptic signal.

articles.title: Developing and Externally Validating Machine Learning Models to Forecast Short-Term Risk of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia.
authors: Northwestern University Successful Clinical Response In Pneumonia Therapy (NU SCRIPT) Study Investigators
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and externally validate supervised machine learning models using routinely collected ICU electronic health record (EHR) data to predict short-term onset of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) before clinical diagnosis.

DESIGN: Prospective observational cohort study with temporal model development and external validation.

SETTING: ICUs.

PATIENTS: Mechanically ventilated adults in a prospective observational cohort (Successful Clinical Response In Pneumonia Therapy [SCRIPT]) who underwent bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) for suspected pneumonia and had BAL-confirmed adjudicated VAP or adjudicated non-VAP status (n = 507). External validation in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV (MIMIC-IV) included mechanically ventilated patients with greater than or equal to 48 hours of continuous invasive ventilation (n = 2681). Additional evaluation was performed in participants from the Inhaled Amikacin vs. Placebo to Prevent Ventilator Associated Pneumonia (AMIKINHAL) randomized trial evaluating inhaled amikacin for VAP prevention, using centrally adjudicated VAP outcomes.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: We extracted 36 day-level clinical features (vital signs, ventilator settings, laboratory values, inflammatory markers, and support devices) from the EHR and trained models to predict VAP within 3, 5, or 7 days before BAL-confirmed diagnosis. Unsupervised clustering identified physiologic states enriched for VAP-labeled days. In internal testing, the best performance reached an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.866 for predicting VAP within 7 days and 0.843 for predicting VAP within 5 days. Predicted risk increased over the days preceding VAP among patients who developed VAP, while remaining low among non-VAP patients. On external validation in MIMIC-IV, the best model achieved an AUROC of 0.817 for predicting VAP within 5 days. Performance was poor in AMIKINHAL, where only nine of 36 features were available. Across models, influential predictors included ventilator duration and mechanics (e.g., positive end-expiratory pressure), platelet count, and inflammatory markers.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models trained on day-level structured ICU data with BAL-confirmed adjudicated labels predicted VAP up to 7 days before clinical diagnosis with strong discrimination and generalized to an external health system when key features were available, supporting future prospective real-time evaluation.

articles.title: A novel electronic health record-based framework for value-based analysis of health interventions: a case use on dapagliflozin in patients with heart failure using the COHERENT model.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Electronic health records (EHRs) rarely capture quality-of-life data, limiting the use of traditional cost-effectiveness analyses in routine practice. We aimed to test whether a value-based analysis (VBA) could be done using EHR and information system data with the Clinical Outcomes, HEalthcare REsource utilizatioN and relaTed costs (COHERENT) model, applied to a theoretical intervention: systematic treatment with dapagliflozin in patients with heart failure (HF).

METHODS AND RESULTS: We built a reference cohort of adult patients with an HF diagnosis seen at a tertiary hospital (2015-17). Clinical events, healthcare resource use, and costs over 1080 days were obtained from EHR, administrative datasets, and mortality registries and analysed with the COHERENT model. Based on trial meta-analytic estimates (10% all-cause mortality and 29% HF hospitalization reduction with dapagliflozin), we simulated a cohort on dapagliflozin using logistic and zero-inflated Poisson regression. Costs, value of statistical life-years, and different VBA parameters were calculated: net cost difference, mean incremental cost per patient, and break-even time. Among 5245 patients (median age 81 years; 54.6% women), there were 2054 deaths and 3110 patients with at least one readmission at 1080 days, with a total care cost of €84.25 million. In the simulated dapagliflozin cohort, deaths decreased to 1849 and patients readmitted decreased to 2997. Total cost fell to €76.37 million, a net saving of €7.88 million, with mean cost per patient-day decreasing from €14.87 to €13.48. The economic break-even point was reached at 479 days.

CONCLUSION: This EHR-based COHERENT framework enables day-by-day, value-oriented assessment of cardiovascular interventions, integrating real-world trajectories, costs and simulated treatment benefits.

articles.title: Temporal Changes in COVID-19 Symptomatology During the Pandemic in Central Mexico: A Repeated Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The clinical presentation of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) was highly variable and changed throughout the pandemic. However, temporal changes in symptom profiles across successive pandemic waves remain underexplored, particularly among ambulatory populations in Latin America. Understanding these changes in clinical manifestations may contribute to refining pandemic preparedness and improving the recognition of evolving patterns associated with emerging respiratory infections. This study aimed to explore temporal changes in COVID-19 symptom profiles among non-hospitalized patients recruited during four distinct pandemic waves from central Mexico.

METHODS: This observational study used repeated cross-sectional samples of independent ambulatory patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection recruited during the second, third, fourth, and fifth pandemic waves. Symptom frequencies were descriptively evaluated in 84 participants. Multivariate analyses were subsequently performed using a reduced dataset including 57 participants and 24 symptoms during the second (Group I), third (Group II), fourth (Group III), and fifth (Group IV) pandemic waves to assess symptom variation. Non-metric multidimensional scaling, PERMANOVA, and SIMPER analyses were used to explore differences in symptom profiles among study waves.

RESULTS: Symptom profiles differed significantly among the four study waves. Earlier waves were predominantly characterized by systemic symptoms, including malaise, headache, and fever, whereas the fifth wave showed a greater frequency of upper respiratory symptoms, particularly pharyngitis and odynophagia. SIMPER analysis identified nine symptoms that collectively accounted for 52% of the observed dissimilarity among study waves.

CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 symptom profiles varied across the different waves of the pandemic in this outpatient population. These findings offer a temporal perspective on changes in clinical manifestations during the pandemic and may contribute to understanding the evolving presentation of emerging respiratory infections.

articles.title: Predicting cardiopulmonary exercise testing performance in patients undergoing transthoracic echocardiography-an artificial intelligence-based, multimodal model.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) performance strongly correlates with survival in several disease states including heart failure, but has limited accessibility. Meanwhile, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is a far more widely available tool. We sought to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm using TTE and data from electronic medical records to predict CPET peak oxygen consumption (peak VO2) ≤ 14 mL/kg/min.

METHODS AND RESULTS: An AI model was trained to predict peak VO2 ≤ 14 mL/kg/min from TTE images, structured TTE reports, demographics, medications, laboratory tests, and vitals. The training set included patients with a TTE within 6 months of a CPET. Performance was retrospectively tested in a held-out group from the development cohort and an external regional validation cohort. A total of 1127 CPET studies paired with concomitant TTE were identified. The best performance was achieved by using all components (TTE images, all structured clinical data). The model performed well at predicting a peak VO2 ≤ 14 mL/kg/min, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.84 (development cohort) and 0.80 (external validation cohort). It performed consistently well using higher (≤18 mL/kg/min) and lower (≤12 mL/kg/min) cut-offs.

CONCLUSION: This multimodal AI model effectively categorized patients into low- and high-risk predicted peak VO2, demonstrating the potential to identify previously unrecognized high-risk patients when CPET is not available.

articles.title: Recurrent Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension With Bilateral Abducens Nerve Palsy in a Prepubertal Child: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension is rare in prepubertal children and may present atypically. We report a recurrent case in a 7-year-old boy with bilateral abducens nerve palsy and papilledema. Refractory symptoms necessitated lumboperitoneal shunting, resulting in complete clinical recovery and sustained remission.

articles.title: Study design to assess women's and children's mortality and child health 13-15 years after exposure to a successful community-based participatory women's group intervention in rural Bangladesh.
articles.abstract: Between 2009 and 2011, a cluster-randomised trial of a Participatory Women's Groups (PWGs) intervention using Participatory Learning and Action (PLA) significantly reduced neonatal mortality. A follow-up in 2013 revealed growth differences in surviving children from highly exposed mothers in intervention groups compared to those from control. Currently, the long-term association between PWG interventions and survival of children, their mothers and younger siblings, as well as broader child health outcomes, remains largely unexplored. We describe the design of a 2024 study following up 18,940 eligible women whose pregnancies were registered during our 2009-2011 trial and their 18,107 liveborn children born within this timeframe. We gathered women's survival status and reproductive history since the intervention ended, including the number of subsequent births and the survival status of these children. For children who were alive at 4 weeks as per the 2009-2011 trial records, we recorded current survival status. For those who died after the age of 4 weeks up to the present survey, we used verbal autopsy to identify probable cause of death. Moreover, nested within our larger follow-up sample, we conducted a cross-sectional survey of growth and health outcomes in a sample of 3,835 children born during the 2009-2011 trial across intervention and control clusters. Intention-to-treat analyses will compare survival between trial arms according to original allocation. Analysis of growth and health outcomes will involve two separate comparisons: children in the high-exposure group versus those in the unexposed group and children in the variable-exposure group versus those in the unexposed group.

articles.title: Feasibility of dynamic blood lactate estimation using sweat biomarkers during exercise under normoxic and hypoxic conditions: a randomized-order crossover study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study investigated the feasibility of dynamically estimating blood lactate concentration during exercise using sweat biomarkers.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a randomized crossover design, 10 healthy adults (8 men and 2 women; age, 22.0 ± 1.9 years) completed cycling trials under normoxia (20.9% O2), moderate hypoxia (16.3% O2), and severe hypoxia (12.7% O2). Participants initially cycled at 30% Wmax for approximately 20-30 min until the device produced valid sweat data, then completed successive 6-min stages at 40%, 50%, 60%, and 70% Wmax, followed by cycling at 80% Wmax until exhaustion. Sweat biomarker profiles and fingertip blood lactate concentrations were measured concurrently throughout each trial, and mapping models were developed to characterize changes in their associations across levels of hypoxic stress.

RESULTS: Across the six sampled exercise stages under the three oxygen conditions, measured blood lactate concentration ranged from 1.97 to 15.58 mmol/L and sweat sodium concentration from 22 to 81 mmol/L. The models showed good in-sample fit under normoxia and moderate hypoxia (R2 = 0.738 and 0.830, respectively), with sweat sodium concentration exhibiting the strongest association with blood lactate. Model fit deteriorated substantially under severe hypoxia (R2 = 0.152).

UNLABELLED: Conclusion: These findings suggest that sweat biomarkers show considerable potential for dynamically estimating blood lactate under normoxic and moderately hypoxic conditions. However, their applicability may be markedly limited under extreme conditions such as severe hypoxia.

articles.title: Fosfomycin in acute and chronic bacterial prostatitis and prostate biopsy prophylaxis: a narrative review in the era of antimicrobial resistance.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bacterial prostatitis remains therapeutically challenging because antimicrobial resistance, variable intraprostatic drug exposure, and persistent anatomical reservoirs limit the number of reliable oral treatment options. Fosfomycin has therefore attracted renewed interest as an oral agent for chronic bacterial prostatitis (CBP) when antimicrobial resistance or intolerance limits standard oral therapy, as well as oral step-down therapy in selected acute bacterial prostatitis (ABP). This narrative review integrates treatment studies, prostate pharmacokinetics, contemporary susceptibility standards, and prostate biopsy prevention evidence identified through October 2026. Its distinctive focus is the separation of observational treatment evidence from randomized prophylaxis evidence and the reduced applicability of historical transrectal prophylaxis studies as transperineal biopsy expands.

DISCUSSION: Observational studies support oral fosfomycin as a potential option for selected chronic bacterial prostatitis (CBP), particularly involving multidrug-resistant (MDR) Escherichia coli, but heterogeneous diagnostic criteria, noncomparative designs, and recurrence limit inference about durable cure. The most extensively studied regimen used was 3 g daily for 1 week followed by 3 g every 48 h for 6-12 weeks; neither dose nor duration has been optimized in randomized trials. Evidence in acute bacterial prostatitis (ABP) is limited and chiefly supports oral step-down after clinical stabilization and usually initial active intravenous therapy. Oral treatment of prostatitis is off-label. The role of fosfomycin in prostate biopsy prophylaxis is less consistent. Earlier transrectal biopsy studies frequently reported benefits in settings with high fluoroquinolone resistance, whereas more recent comparative studies have shown mixed or negative findings. Randomized route comparisons and European guidance favor transperineal biopsy, with antibiotic omission an option for patients without infectious risk factors.

CONCLUSION: Fosfomycin has a selective role in the treatment of bacterial prostatitis, with its use guided by culture and antimicrobial susceptibility results. Current evidence does not support its use as a universal replacement for standard therapy. Increasing use of transperineal biopsy reduces the relevance of historical fosfomycin prophylaxis data. Randomized trials in patients with clearly defined CBP remain the principal evidence gap.

articles.title: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine-leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

articles.title: Lumigolix versus Ganirelix in Controlled Ovarian Hyperstimulation for Assisted Reproductive Technologies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In this trial we aimed to compare lumigolix, a novel oral gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) antagonist, to ganirelix injection in women undergoing controlled ovarian hyperstimulation for assisted reproductive technologies.

METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, noninferiority trial, women 20 to 39 years of age with infertility and an indication for in vitro fertilization or intracytoplasmic sperm injection with embryo transfer were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive one of two GnRH antagonists: 200 mg of lumigolix orally every 12 hours or 0.25 mg of ganirelix subcutaneously once daily, with matching placebos. Co-primary end points were rate of premature luteinizing hormone (LH) surge suppression (noninferiority margin, -10 percentage points) and number of oocytes retrieved after one stimulation cycle (noninferiority margin, -3). The safety profile was assessed.

RESULTS: Three hundred seventeen women were randomly assigned to either lumigolix (n=156) or ganirelix (n=161). Mean age was 32.2 years, mean body mass index (weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) was 22.2, and mean duration of infertility was 37.9 months. The rate of premature LH surge suppression was 99.4% (153/154 women) with lumigolix and 99.4% (160/161 women) with ganirelix (difference, 0.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.8 to 1.8; P<0.0001 for noninferiority). The estimated marginal mean number of oocytes retrieved was 9.9 with lumigolix and 9.9 with ganirelix (difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -1.0 to 1.0; P<0.0001 for noninferiority). Adverse events occurred in 80 patients (51.9%) receiving lumigolix and 71 patients (44.1%) receiving ganirelix; all were mild to moderate. Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome occurred in five patients (3.2%) and four patients (2.5%) in the lumigolix and ganirelix groups, respectively, and serious adverse events occurred in 5 patients (3.2%) and 11 patients (6.8%), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with infertility and an expected normal ovarian response, lumigolix was noninferior to ganirelix in preventing premature LH surges and resulted in a comparable number of oocytes retrieved per cycle, without adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation. (Funded by Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05994378.).

articles.title: A Phase 2 Study of Imlifidase in the Treatment of Guillain-Barré Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a life-threatening neuropathy, results in prolonged disability despite standard-of-care treatment. Imlifidase specifically cleaves immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies and may benefit patients with GBS by rapidly depleting pathologic IgG autoantibodies, resulting in less severe disease and faster recovery.

METHODS: This open-label, single-arm, multicenter, phase 2 study enrolled adults with severe GBS (i.e., GBS disability scale [GBS-DS] grades ranging from 3 to 5; GBS-DS grades range from 0 to 6, with higher numbers indicating more severe disability). It investigated safety, adverse event profile, efficacy, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of one dose of imlifidase within 12 days of symptom onset followed by standard-dose intravenous immune globulin (IVIG). Twenty-seven participants with confirmed GBS were assessed by using standard GBS outcome measures, including GBS-DS and the Medical Research Council sum score (scores range from 0 to 60, with a lower score indicting more severe weakness).

RESULTS: Median (95% confidence interval) time to improve at least one GBS-DS grade was 6 (3.0 to 16.0) days, and time to independent walking was 16 (4.0 to 92.0) days. Within 1 week, 37% of patients were able to walk independently, and the mean improvement in the Medical Research Council sum score was 10.7 points. Twenty-five participants (83%) experienced at least one treatment-emergent adverse event. Most were grade 1 (mild) or grade 2 (moderate). Five were assessed as being grade 3 (severe) and two events as being grade 4 (life-threatening or disabling intensity), including one death.

CONCLUSIONS: A single dose of imlifidase followed by IVIG in participants with severe GBS was associated with rapid functional improvements. These results support a randomized controlled trial to further investigate IgG-depleting strategies in GBS. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03943589.).

articles.title: Sildenafil for Fetal Growth Restriction - An Individual Participant Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR).

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated.

RESULTS: Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29).

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

articles.title: Diagnostic Genetic Testing - Indications, Effectiveness, and Evolving Practice.
articles.abstract: AbstractClinical genetic testing has expanded from cytogenetics and focused assays for rare genetic disorders to an essential component of care across multiple specialties. Exome and genome sequencing are central to current testing approaches. Particularly when performed as trio analysis (simultaneous sequencing of the patient and both biological parents), they achieve higher diagnostic yields than chromosomal microarray analysis or many targeted gene panels in pediatric congenital and neurodevelopmental disorders and are increasingly recommended as first- or second-tier tests. Rapid genomic sequencing has further extended this impact in neonatal intensive care settings where timely genomically informed diagnoses can affect clinical management. Despite these advances, important challenges remain, including incomplete detection of certain variant types, difficulties in variant interpretation, secondary and incidental findings, and uneven access to testing. Appropriate test selection, pretest counseling, and accurate interpretation of genomic findings are therefore essential components of genomic medicine. Emerging technologies including long-read sequencing and multiomic approaches, coupled with robust evidence frameworks and expanded data sharing, have the potential to further improve diagnostic yield and clinical utility. This review summarizes current indications, diagnostic performance, limitations, and evolving applications of clinical germline genetic testing.

articles.title: Waning of hepatitis B surface antibody but no serological evidence of breakthrough infection up to 10 years of age after hexavalent and pentavalent vaccination in infancy.
articles.abstract: Thailand incorporated the hepatitis B (HepB) vaccine into infant combination vaccines. The current available formulations are pentavalent (DTwP-HB-Hib) and hexavalent (DTaP-IPV-HB-Hib) vaccines. The national policy recommends these combination vaccines at 2, 4, and 6 months of age, following a monovalent HepB vaccine at birth. In this study, sera samples of a randomized cohort of children who received hexavalent or pentavalent vaccines at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months were collected (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02408926). This cohort received one more HepB dose than the national schedule (total 5 doses). We evaluated the kinetics of anti-HBs and screened for evidence of breakthrough HepB infection using antibody to HepB core antigen (anti-HBc). Anti-HBs was measured annually from 2 through 10 years of age, and anti-HBc was tested at 10 years. A total of 153 children completed the study at age 10 years. Seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL) at 10 years was 75.8% in the hexavalent group vs. 32.8% in the pentavalent group, with geometric mean concentrations remaining one log higher in the hexavalent group throughout follow-up. Despite the waning of anti-HBs, all children tested negative for anti-HBc at 10 years. This indicates no serological evidence of breakthrough infection, even in children with anti-HBs < 10 mIU/mL.

articles.title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized within the cysteamine domain to IV cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hr for up to 10 d) or control. The dichotomous primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality, analyzed using Bayesian logistic regression. Recruitment to this domain stopped for operational futility before predefined statistical thresholds were met. Thirty-six patients received cysteamine (n = 19) or control (n = 17). Ninety-day mortality was 26% vs. 35%, respectively (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18-2.19), with a 76% posterior probability of benefit. One serious adverse event occurred, unrelated to cysteamine. These preliminary findings suggest possible benefit, but the small sample size precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. Further studies of cysteamine in severe pneumonia are warranted.

articles.title: Effects of Smartphone Use on Forward Head Posture: A ‎Systematic Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Frequent smartphone use may adversely affect cervical posture, particularly forward head posture (FHP). This systematic review aimed to examine the effects of smartphone use on FHP.

METHODS: A comprehensive review was conducted up to January 2025. Eligibility criteria included observational studies, predominantly cross-sectional, that analyzed the impact of smartphone usage during sitting or quiet standing on the craniovertebral angle (CVA), head tilt, neck flexion, and gaze angle. The methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. The meta-analysis was excluded due to substantial heterogeneity among the included studies.

RESULTS: Database searches yielded 5736 articles. Seventeen studies involving 1702 participants aged 6-29 years were included. Smartphone use was classified primarily by self-reported daily duration or validated addiction scales. FHP was mainly assessed using CVA. Evidence suggests that prolonged smartphone use may be associated with adverse postural changes, including increased cervical flexion, anteriorization of the head, and reduced cervical range of motion. According to the JBI appraisal, the methodological quality of the included evidence ranged from low to high. The most common methodological shortcomings were inadequate control for confounding factors and reliance on self-reported duration of use rather than objective tracking.

CONCLUSION: Prolonged smartphone use appears associated with adverse cervical posture (increased FHP and reduced CVA). Yet, cross-sectional designs, self-reported exposure, and unadjusted confounders limit causal inference. Well-designed longitudinal studies with objective measures are required.

articles.title: Assessing Guidance and Counseling Needs of Iranian Dental Students: A Cross-Sectional Study in Kerman University of Medical Sciences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upon admission to the university, students encounter a range of personal, emotional, academic, and occupational challenges that impact their mental health and overall efficiency. This study aimed to evaluate the guidance and counseling needs of dental students at Kerman University of Medical Sciences.

METHODS: This cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study was conducted among dental students at Kerman University of Medical Sciences in 2021. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling, and data were collected from 173 students through the Counseling Needs Assessment Questionnaire, which assesses demographic characteristics as well as guidance and counseling needs. The questionnaire items are scored employing a four-point Likert scale, which spans "no need = 0" to "urgent need = 3." Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. Descriptive statistics, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, and multiple linear regression were used for data analysis.

RESULTS: The average score for students' guidance and counseling needs was 40.06 ± 15.75. Occupational counseling had the highest mean score (9.34), whereas family and marriage counseling had the lowest (6.99). The students' scores for guidance and counseling needs did not reveal any significant differences regarding age, marital status, place of residence, or academic level (p > 0.05). Meanwhile, female participants achieved significantly higher scores on guidance and counseling needs than male participants (p < 0.05). In the multiple linear regression analysis, gender was the only significant predictor of the overall guidance and counseling needs score, with male students reporting lower scores than female students (B = - 7.262, β = -0.231, 95% CI = -11.985 to -2.540, p = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: Dental students needed counseling services most frequently for their occupational needs but least frequently for their marital issues. Moreover, their guidance and counseling needs were associated with their gender.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Towards Monkeypox Among Dental Professionals: Implications for Outbreak Preparedness-An Analytical Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Understanding healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices towards monkeypox is essential for timely recognition and prevention. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of dental professionals in Pakistan regarding the outbreak of monkeypox virus.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 660 dental professionals across Pakistan using a validated questionnaire. Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS, Version 25). Descriptive statistics were computed, and the χ 2 test was used to assess associations between categorical variables and knowledge, attitude, and practice levels. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with knowledge level. A p value ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The majority demonstrated poor knowledge regarding Mpox (95.5%), with only 0.6% exhibiting good knowledge. Similarly, most participants showed a negative attitude (74.2%). Significant associations were observed between knowledge level and age group (p = 0.011) and professional status (p = 0.044), while gender was significantly associated with attitude (p = 0.001) and professional status (p = 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, age remained the only significant predictor of knowledge. Participants aged > 30 years had lower odds of having good knowledge compared to those aged ≤ 30 years (AOR = 0.172, 95% CI: 0.038-0.788, p = 0.023). Gender and professional status were not significantly associated with knowledge after adjustment.

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, this study revealed a markedly low level of knowledge regarding Mpox among dental professionals. Although attitudes reflected concern about the disease, significant gaps remain in preparedness and confidence in managing suspected cases. These findings highlight the urgent need for targeted educational interventions, training programs, and inclusion of emerging infectious diseases in continuing dental education to enhance preparedness and response capacity.

articles.title: Neonatal Mortality in Public Hospitals of Gamo Zone, Southern Ethiopia: A Prospective Cohort Study Using Sequential Multivariable Logistic Regression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Neonatal mortality remains a pressing public health concern in developing countries, with Ethiopia reporting higher rates than the Sub-Saharan African average. Despite progress in reducing overall child mortality, neonatal deaths remain disproportionately high. This study assessed the incidence and predictors of neonatal mortality in selected public hospitals of the Gamo Zone, Southern Ethiopia.

METHODS: A multicenter, facility-based prospective cohort study was conducted between March and September 2025 across three public hospitals in Gamo Zone. A total of 2499 live-born mother-neonate pairs were followed through 28 days post-birth. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25.0. Fixed-effects multivariable logistic regression with sequential block-entry was constructed in three blocks (distal socio-demographic, intermediate healthcare utilization, and proximal factors). Adjusted Odds Ratios (AOR) with 95% Confidence Intervals (95% CI) were reported, with two-sided significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The overall neonatal mortality rate was 50.8 per 1000 live births (127/2499, 5.08%; 95% CI: 42.70-60.38), with 74.8% of deaths (95/127) occurring during the early neonatal period and nearly half taking place within the first 24 h of life (62/127, 48.8%). The perinatal mortality rate was 46.2 per 1000 births (118/2555, 4.62%; 95% CI: 38.53-55.26) and the stillbirth rate was 9.2 per 1000 births (23/2555, 0.90%; 95% CI: 5.97-13.52). In the final multivariable model, primary or lower maternal education (AOR = 5.20, 95% CI: 2.81-9.60, p < 0.001), third-trimester ANC initiation (AOR = 8.29, 95% CI: 3.71-18.52, p < 0.001), severe maternal complications (AOR) = 12.15, 95% CI: 7.12-20.73, p < 0.001), low birth weight (AOR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.05-3.28, p = 0.03), and 5-min APGAR score < 7 (AOR = 4.25, 95% CI: 2.25-8.02, p < 0.001) significantly increased mortality risk.

CONCLUSION: Neonatal mortality in Gamo Zone public hospitals remains high, driven by maternal complications, delayed ANC, low maternal education, low birth weight, and compromised 5-min APGAR scores. Strengthening intrapartum emergency obstetric care and maternal education is essential to accelerate progress toward SDG 3.2.

articles.title: Cause-specific patterns of documented avoidable factors among maternal deaths reviewed through Uganda's national MPDSR system, 2020-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) systems aim to turn maternal death reviews into action, but avoidable factors are often summarised across all deaths, obscuring cause-specific patterns of documented community, transport and health-system factors.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the prevalence of documented avoidable-factor domains across leading assigned causes among maternal deaths reviewed through Uganda's national MPDSR system.

METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of 6,052 maternal death review records from Uganda's MPDSR system, 2020 to 2025. Descriptive analyses included 5,486 cause-assigned records; regression included 5,454 after excluding 32 non-obstetric records. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios relative to obstetric haemorrhage, adjusting for maternal age, parity, antenatal care and year, with an extended model adding referral status and duration of stay.

RESULTS: At least one avoidable factor was documented in 4,577 of 5,486 reviews (83.4%). Health-system factors were most frequent in haemorrhage (65.1%) and anaesthetic complications (64.9%); community factors in abortion-related complications (72.2%). Community-factor prevalence was statistically significantly higher in abortion-related complications (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.33; 95% confidence interval 1.23-1.44), sepsis (1.13; 1.03-1.24), infections or indirect conditions (1.12; 1.04-1.21) and hypertensive disorders (1.10; 1.02-1.18). Health-system prevalence was significantly lower in abortion-related complications, hypertensive disorders, infections and pre-existing disease; sepsis, anaesthetic complications and ectopic pregnancy were not significant. Some comparisons were sensitive to adjustment and clustering.

CONCLUSIONS: Documented avoidable-factor domains varied by assigned cause, though patterns reflect review-team documentation rather than verified occurrence. Cause-stratified summaries may give more specific MPDSR feedback, but whether they improve outcomes requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Digital health interventions for hospitalization, serum albumin, and peritonitis in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) requires complex self-management and frequent monitoring. Digital health interventions may support PD care, but quantitative evidence for critical outcomes is limited.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and SID were searched from inception to 21 June 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomized studies of interventions (NRSIs) with concurrent comparators were included. RCTs and NRSIs were pooled separately (random-effects, Hartung-Knapp CIs) and graded with GRADE.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies (9 RCTs, 9 NRSIs; 16,929 participants) were included. In four NRSIs, digital health was associated with fewer all-cause hospitalizations (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.73, 95% CI 0.58-0.92); randomized evidence (two discordant trials; adding a cluster-randomized trial's hazard ratio: 0.74, 0.37-1.50) was very uncertain; overall certainty was low. Evidence on peritonitis was very uncertain (two RCTs: IRR 0.67, fixed-effect 95% CI 0.38-1.18). For technique failure, RCTs showed no reduction (odds ratio [OR] 1.07, modified 95% CI 0.37-3.08), whereas NRSIs, dominated by one user-versus-non-user cohort, showed fewer transfers (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52-0.92); certainty was low. Evidence for serum albumin (RCTs: mean difference 0.34 g/dL, -0.02 to 0.70), hemoglobin, and burden of kidney disease was very uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Digital health interventions may reduce all-cause hospitalization in PD, but certainty is low and the magnitude and causal basis are uncertain. Effects on technique failure are uncertain, and those on peritonitis, serum albumin, and other outcomes are very uncertain. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized outcomes and transparent intervention reporting are needed.

articles.title: An MRI-based diagnostic model for identifying amyloid- and tau-positive status in patients with dementia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The diagnosis and assessment of disease severity in Alzheimer's disease (AD) mainly rely on biomarkers derived from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. Limited accessibility of samples and high costs restrict their widespread application. In this study, dementia patients were classified into amyloid- and tau-positive (A + T+) and non-A + T + groups based on CSF biomarkers, with the aim of identifying differences in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based brain structural and topological metrics between the groups and developing a diagnostic model.

METHODS: A total of 31 patients in the A + T + group and 49 in the non-A + T + group were recruited. All participants exhibited clinical manifestations consistent with AD. All patients underwent clinical scale assessments, CSF testing, and brain MRI examinations.

RESULTS: Compared to non-A + T + patients, A + T + patients had smaller caudate nucleus volumes and lower whole-brain network topological parameter λ values. There were no differences in cortical thickness, hippocampal volume, or amygdala volume between the two groups. The diagnostic model developed to differentiate A + T + from non-A + T + dementia patients, based on age, gender, disease duration, caudate/estimated total intracranial volume (eTIV), and λ, achieved an AUC of 0.817.

CONCLUSIONS: Combining clinical manifestations with MRI-based structural and topological parameters helps improve the diagnostic ability for A + T + dementia patients. Caudate/eTIV and λ may represent promising noninvasive candidate biomarkers for monitoring AD progression, although their utility requires validation in future longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Expression of GPX4 and redox balance are critical for intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Intestinal intraepithelial lymphocytes (IELs) provide frontline mucosal defense while functioning within a hypoxic epithelial niche characterized by sustained oxidative stress. Their distinctive mitochondrial and metabolic features may predispose them to oxidative damage; however, how IELs maintain viability under these conditions remains unclear. Here we showed that IELs engaged robust antioxidant transcriptional programs and identified glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) as a cell-intrinsic factor selectively required for IEL maintenance. Conditional deletion of Gpx4 in CD8+ T cells or TCRαβ+ T cells caused profound loss of IELs, without affecting peripheral T cell compartments. Gpx4-deficient IELs accumulated reactive oxygen species, underwent lipid peroxidation and succumbed to ferroptotic cell death, a phenotype rescued by vitamin E supplementation. Functionally, loss of Gpx4 increased susceptibility to enteric infection in mice, while reduced GPX4 expression was associated with pathology of inflammatory bowel disease in humans, establishing GPX4-dependent control of ferroptosis as a central mechanism sustaining IEL survival and intestinal barrier immunity.

articles.title: Diverse lung challenges elicit a conserved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation blueprint.
articles.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) form a first line of defense to lung insults. These insults often lead to replacement of fetal-derived tissue-resident AMs (fAMs) by monocyte-derived AMs (mono-AMs) with different functionality, which impacts lung immunity during future lung challenges. However, whether these alterations are conserved or insult specific is not well understood. Here we show that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection remodels the AM compartment long term. We perform comparative analyses of fAMs and mono-AMs after RSV infection, influenza A virus infection or clodronate liposome administration and identify a crucial tissue integration checkpoint of CD11b+ mono-AMs that involves acquisition of proliferative capacity and requires EGR2-mediated transcriptional rewiring. Mono-AMs elicited by RSV, influenza A virus or clodronate liposomes have a hardwired ontogeny-dependent stereotypical profile of transcription, proliferation, metabolism and enhanced immunoreactivity despite a substantially different inflammatory environment during differentiation; accordingly, mono-AMs elicited by sterile or infectious insult protect from subsequent Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. By contrast, fAMs display context-dependent transcriptional alterations. Our findings highlight that long-term changes in the AM compartment show origin-dependent phenotypic divergence and that mono-AM integration follows a hardwired trajectory fine-tuned by environmental factors.

articles.title: Gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells contribute to HIV persistence during ART.
articles.abstract: Antigen specificities of most HIV reservoir cells remain poorly defined. We examined whether CD4+ T cells specific for gut bacterial antigens contribute to HIV replication and persistence. Gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells were markedly reduced in viremic people living with HIV (PWH) and remained incompletely restored despite antiretroviral therapy (ART), with those expressing markers of HIV permissiveness being preferentially depleted. Circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells from PWH on ART displayed lower TCR β diversity and persistent functional disruption, characterized by attenuation of canonical effector programs and a higher proportion of cells with cytotoxic features. By contrast, rectum-localized bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells from the same individuals exhibited a tolerogenic profile, highlighting the compartment-specific function of these cells. Near-full-length proviral sequencing revealed clonal expansions of HIV genomes within circulating gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells from ART-treated participants, with evidence of cross-reactivity across multiple bacterial species. Genetically intact proviruses were enriched in Salmonella Typhimurium-specific CD4+ T cells. These findings suggest that gut-bacteria-specific CD4+ T cells are preferentially targeted during untreated HIV infection and incompletely restored by ART, harboring genetically intact HIV genomes and constituting an antigen-driven reservoir in which chronic stimulation by gut microbial antigens promotes clonal proliferation and long-term HIV persistence during ART.

articles.title: Greater occipital nerve block with local anesthetics alone or combined with steroids to treat migraine: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Greater occipital nerve block (GONB) may be applied using local anesthetics alone or combined with corticosteroids for the treatment of migraine. However, it is uncertain whether the addition of steroids improves the efficacy.

OBJECTIVE: The current systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) aimed at summarizing, synthesizing, and pooling the evidence comparing the efficacy of GONB with or without corticosteroids in the treatment of patients with migraine.

METHODS: Studies comparing the efficacy of GONB with local anesthetics alone and GONB using local anesthetics plus corticosteroids for the treatment of chronic or episodic migraine patients were selected from the PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases until March 3, 2025. The outcomes included mean headache intensity and the absolute number of monthly migraine days. The results were expressed as standardized mean difference (SMD), confidence interval (CI), and mean difference (MD). The Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2; free) tool was used to assess the risk of bias of the studies. The current study was registered on the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO, under registration no. CRD420251032766).

RESULTS: A total of 261 patients from 5 RCTs were included. When GONB with local anesthetics plus corticosteroids was compared with GONB with local anesthetics only, no statistically significant differences were found regarding the headache intensity (SMD: 0.23; 95%CI: -0.14 to 0.59; p = 0.232; I2  = 0%) or monthly migraine days (MD: 0.7; 95%CI: -0.23 to 1.64; p = 0.141; I2  = 0%).

CONCLUSION: Adding corticosteroids to local anesthetics for GONB did not demonstrate additional benefits for migraine frequency or intensity. However, the evidence was of very low certainty and insufficient to exclude a clinically meaningful effect.

articles.title: Clinical analysis of patients with refractory status epilepticus in a tertiary hospital in northern Ceará, Brazil: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory status epilepticus (RSE) is a neurological emergency associated with high morbidity and mortality. Despite its clinical significance, data from regional tertiary centers in Brazil remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical profile of RSE patients and to identify predictors associated with in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: In the current retrospective case series, we analyzed 21 patients hospitalized between 2023 and 2025 in a tertiary hospital in in the northern region of the state of Ceará, Brazil. Cases were identified via electroencephalography (EEG) screening and medical record review, following the diagnostic criteria of the International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) for RSE.

RESULTS: The mean age of the sample was 54.05 (median: 62) years, with 61.9% of female subjects. Hypertension (52.4%) and diabetes (28.6%) were the primary comorbidities. Depressed consciousness occurred in 76% of the cases. Prevalent metabolic disturbances included hypernatremia (85%) and metabolic acidosis (50%). The in-hospital mortality rate was 57.14%. The statistical analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between age and mortality (r = 0.72; p = 0.001). Notably, a significant negative correlation was found between overt motor seizures and death (r = -0.66; p < 0.001), with motor symptoms acting as a survival predictor (odds ratio [OR] = 31.50).

CONCLUSION: In the cohort of the present study, RSE was associated with high lethality, especially in older patients. The inverse association between motor symptoms and mortality suggests that non-convulsive presentations delay diagnosis, leading to worse outcomes. These findings emphasize the urgent need for institutional protocols prioritizing continuous EEG monitoring and early therapeutic escalation in regional tertiary centers.

articles.title: Comprehensive care for acute ischemic stroke in older adults: experience from a geriatric unit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global aging population has led to an increased burden of stroke, which remains a leading cause of mortality and disability. In Mexico, acute ischemic stroke (AIS) prevalence and risk factors are documented, but geriatric-specific management remains underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the clinical, diagnostic, and therapeutic approach to AIS in elderly patients in a Geriatric Unit, aiming to identify trends and areas for improvement.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of patients aged ≥ 65 years with AIS at the Unidad de Atención Geriátrica de Alta Especialidad "Pablo Jiménez Camarena" (UNAGAE) of Antiguo Hospital Civil de Guadalajara Fray Antonio Alcalde, between January 2022 and July 2023. Demographic, clinical, radiological, and etiological data were analyzed. Stroke subtypes were classified using the Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment system. Statistical analyses included logistic regression models to assess mortality predictors.

RESULTS: A total of 119 patients (mean age 75.4 years, 50% male) were analyzed. The most common risk factors were hypertension (76%), smoking (53%), and diabetes (45%). Intravenous thrombolysis was received by 11%, despite 41% arriving during the therapeutic window. Cardioembolism (29%) and large-artery atherosclerosis (16%) were the most frequent subtypes, but 49% remained undetermined (incomplete evaluation). In-hospital and 30-day mortality rates were 24% and 7%, respectively. Higher National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale admission rates (OR = 1.18; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with in-hospital mortality.

CONCLUSION: The present study underscores important gaps in the management of AIS among elderly patients, particularly the underutilization of acute interventions and incomplete diagnostic assessments. Optimizing emergency response times, improving etiological evaluations, and enhancing public awareness of stroke symptoms could improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Gammaherpesvirus infection drives genotype-dependent virus-specific T cell responses in the CNS prior to autoimmune neuroinflammation.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Infection with the gammaherpesvirus Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is the strongest environmental risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS). This risk is driven by poor immune control of viral replication, which is genetically determined. Clonally expanded CD8 T cells are abundant in MS lesions, and some recognize EBV antigens. We previously demonstrated that host genetic variation regulates immune control of the homologous B cell-tropic murine gammaherpesvirus, MHV-68. Here, we investigated how gammaherpesvirus infection and host genotype shape central nervous system (CNS) T cell responses, before and after induction of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE). Chronic infection alone was sufficient to promote a marked accumulation of CX3CR1+KLRG1+ effector CD8 T cells and CX3CR1+KLRG1+ cytotoxic-like T helper cells in the CNS of MHV-68-susceptible C57BL/6 mice. T cells localized to brain border regions and throughout the CNS parenchyma. MHC tetramer analysis demonstrated that CNS-infiltrating T cells were specific for viral antigens, and viral DNA was detectable in CNS-infiltrating leukocytes during early and chronic infection. EAE further amplified cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS of MHV-68-infected C57BL/6 mice. However, CNS T cell infiltration was highly attenuated in genetically divergent wild-derived PWD/PhJ mice, which control MHV-68 more effectively, but not in MHV-68-susceptible 129S1/SvImJ mice. Surprisingly, chronic MHV-68 infection modestly delayed EAE onset in C57BL/6 mice, an effect reversed by B cell depletion. Together with emerging human studies, our results suggest that host genetic variation contributes to poor control of EBV in MS, promoting virus-specific cytotoxic T cell accumulation in the CNS and immune reprogramming both before and during autoimmune neuroinflammation.

articles.title: A decavalent Group B streptococcal biosynthetic conjugate vaccine provides functional immunity to all known serotypes.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Globally, 394,000 cases of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) infection occur each year, leading to significant morbidity and mortality. Vaccination has emerged as an important strategy to limit GBS infections and disease; however, existing vaccine candidates currently in clinical development do not cover all capsular polysaccharide serotypes. Here, we describe the use of a next generation bioconjugation platform to generate a decavalent GBS vaccine (GBS10V) and characterize its immunological evaluation in animals. Using an evolved PglS bioconjugation platform, capsular polysaccharides from all 10 GBS capsular polysaccharide serotypes were individually expressed and bioconjugated to an optimized Pseudomonas aeruginosa exotoxin A (EPA6) carrier protein engineered with six sequons. Multiple biochemical analyses confirmed the identity of each polysaccharide serotype bioconjugated to EPA6. Moreover, intact mass spectrometry (MS) and MS/MS spectra confirmed the presence of sialic acid in each repeat unit of GBS polysaccharides attached to the carrier, an attribute critical for eliciting an optimal immune response. The GBS10V vaccine was used to immunize outbred CD-1 mice and New Zealand White rabbits with doses of 1, 2, or 5 μg per GBS serotype. Sera analyses demonstrated the GBS10V vaccine induced high serotype-specific immunoglobulin titers to all 10 serotypes. Most importantly, interim and postimmune sera from rabbits demonstrated potent opsonophagocytic killing, with median titers ranging from 646 to 6,145 for all serotypes by day 42. Together, these findings establish GBS10V as a global GBS conjugate vaccine candidate for all patient populations, and thus, justify its further preclinical development.

articles.title: NSP1-SAMD9L interactions govern murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Rotavirus replication, pathogenesis, and transmission are host-range restricted, yet the viral and host determinants remain poorly defined. Rotavirus nonstructural protein 1 (NSP1) is a multifunctional innate immune antagonist dispensable for replication in permissive cells. Here, using reverse genetics, neonatal mice, intestinal organoids, and comparative proteomics, we identify mouse SAMD9L as a critical host restriction factor selectively antagonized by murine rotavirus-encoded NSP1. An NSP1-deletion murine-like rotavirus produced progeny efficiently in cell lines but was highly attenuated in neonatal mice with no productive intestinal replication, fecal shedding, and diarrhea. Recombinant monoreassortant viruses carrying NSP1 genes from rhesus, bovine, or human rotavirus strains did not support murine intestinal infection, even in Stat1-/- pups, indicating an additional restriction mechanism beyond STAT1-dependent antiviral signaling. Comparative proteomics identified mouse SAMD9L as a specific interactor of murine NSP1, and NSP1 promoted SAMD9L degradation through a neddylation- and proteasome-dependent pathway. AlphaFold3 guided mutagenesis identified NSP1 residues S364/E366 and SAMD9L residues R455/L462 as functionally important for the NSP1-SAMD9L interaction. Mutations on either side disrupted NSP1-SAMD9L association and prevented SAMD9L degradation. Replication of murine rotaviruses carrying S364A or E366A mutations was undetectable in wild-type mice and was restored in Samd9l-/- mice. Combined deletion of Samd9l and Stat1 permitted replication of otherwise attenuated viruses carrying mismatched NSP1s and enabled fecal IgA seroconversion after a single oral inoculation of Rotarix. These findings identify SAMD9L as a physiologically relevant intestinal restriction factor in mice and show that murine NSP1 antagonism of mouse SAMD9L contributes to murine rotavirus host range restriction in vivo.

articles.title: Molecular Architecture of Noncoding RNA Networks in Stroke.
articles.abstract: Stroke remains the leading cause of long-term neurological disability worldwide, with limited treatment options. Increasing evidence shows that noncoding RNAs, including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs, play crucial roles in shaping the poststroke pathophysiology. Beyond their individual effects, the crosstalk of noncoding RNAs regulates the poststroke pathophysiologic mechanisms. They form competing endogenous RNA networks enabled by direct base-pairing with other RNAs and scaffolding of RNAs with proteins. These interactions coordinate signals across molecular pathways, amplifying or buffering cellular responses to injury. Recent studies have shown that long noncoding RNAs and circular RNAs function as microRNA sponges and epigenetic scaffolds that regulate gene networks in a spatiotemporal manner. By evaluating structural features, mechanisms, and functional outcomes, this review highlights noncoding RNA crosstalk as a novel regulatory layer of poststroke brain damage. Targeting noncoding RNA crosstalk enables modulation of injury responses and provides insights for future RNA-based stroke therapies.

articles.title: [Beyond the ECG-the emotional side of electrophysiology].
Interventional reperfusion for pulmonary embolism.
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: The management of patients with intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) has evolved in recognition of this unique population's potential for circulatory collapse. Systemic thrombolysis, catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT), and mechanical thrombectomy are reperfusion therapies typically reserved for patients with high-risk PE. Intermediate-risk PE represents a dynamic pathophysiologic state, whereby right ventricular dysfunction (RVD) may progress to cardiogenic shock in minutes to hours. More recent evidence suggests that early reperfusion for patients with intermediate-risk PE can have a profound impact on mortality (and adverse bleeding events) compared with anticoagulation alone. Anticoagulation is paramount in PE management, although recent trends highlight a reliance on unfractionated heparin despite evidence favoring alternative anticoagulation strategies. Modern perspectives on PE management emphasize early identification of RVD and escalation to interventional reperfusion, using vasoactive medications as a bridge to therapy.

articles.title: Recognizing and treating Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD).
articles.journal: JAAPA : official journal of the American Academy of Physician Assistants
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) is an increasingly recognized cause of chronic pulmonary infection, yet it remains frequently missed in clinical practice due to its nonspecific presentation and overlap with more common conditions. This clinical review summarizes the pathogenesis, risk factors, clinical presentation, diagnostic criteria, differential diagnosis, pharmacologic treatment, and supportive care of MAC-PD for advanced practice clinicians. Two clinical phenotypes are discussed: fibrocavitary disease, seen more often in older men with structural lung disease, and nodular bronchiectatic disease, seen more often in older women. Diagnosis requires meeting clinical, radiographic, and microbiologic criteria per the 2020 ATS/ERS/ESCMID/IDSA guideline. Treatment consists of a macrolide-based three-drug regimen guided by disease phenotype, severity, and drug susceptibility that is continued for at least 12 months after sputum culture conversion. Airway clearance therapy, nutritional support, and mitigation of environmental and other modifiable risk factors are integral to comprehensive management. Recognizing MAC-PD early and initiating appropriate treatment can prevent progressive lung damage and improve quality of life for affected patients.

articles.title: Diffusion MRI and Inflammation-Nutrition-Based Nomogram for Early Tumor Response to HAIC-Based Triple Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Portal Vein Tumor Thrombus.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative surgery : the official journal of the Academy of Surgical Research
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and evaluate a pretreatment nomogram predicting early objective response to HAIC-based triple therapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus.

METHODS: This retrospective three-center study included 170 patients (training, 82; pooled external validation, 88). The nomogram incorporated ln(SII), prognostic nutritional index, and normalized diffusion-weighted imaging-to-apparent diffusion coefficient ratio. Evaluation included discrimination, calibration, decision curves, 500-bootstrap internal validation, SHAP interpretation, and survival stratification.

RESULTS: Objective response occurred in 27/82 (32.9%) training patients and 30/88 (34.1%) external patients. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879-0.989) and 0.924 (95% CI, 0.869-0.978); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.917. At the training-derived probability cutoff of 0.1933, sensitivity was 92.6% (95% CI, 76.6-97.9%) and 90.0% (95% CI, 74.4-96.5%), respectively. External calibration showed a Brier score of 0.112 and a slope of 1.456. The model had higher AUCs than Child-Pugh class, ALBI grade, and the six-and-twelve category. Higher predicted response probability was associated with longer overall and progression-free survival in both cohorts (all log-rank p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The nomogram showed promising discrimination for early objective response in selected patients with HCC and PVTT receiving HAIC-based triple therapy.

articles.title: FGF23 in chronic kidney disease progression: biomarker or mediator?
articles.abstract: Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) is an important regulator of phosphate balance that rises early in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Evidence suggests that elevated FGF23 is associated with adverse renal outcomes. However, whether FGF23 is merely a biomarker or a direct mediator of CKD progression remains unresolved. In this narrative review, we synthesize current knowledge on the biology of FGF23, evaluate mechanistic and clinical evidence linking FGF23 to CKD progression, and highlight key areas for future research. We included observational and experimental studies indexed in PubMed from inception to March 2026 that examined the relationships between FGF23 and renal outcomes, as well as the underlying biological pathways. Available evidence suggests that elevated FGF23 levels are associated with an accelerated decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate, increased albuminuria, and a higher risk of kidney failure across diverse populations. Longitudinal data further demonstrate that rising FGF23 trajectories are associated with adverse renal outcomes. Experimental studies suggest that FGF23 may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, renin-angiotensin system activation, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. However, the close interplay between FGF23, α-Klotho, phosphate load, and calciprotein particles complicates causal inference. Therefore, the pathogenic role of FGF23 in CKD progression remains unclear, underscoring the need for further research.

articles.title: Infection of Enterovirus D68 clinical isolates in a neonatal mouse model: Viral kinetics, tissue tropism and histopathology.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68), a major cause of respiratory illness, is increasingly associated with neurological complications, including acute flaccid myelitis (AFM). While clinical AFM cases are frequently linked to clade B, the neurovirulent potential across other clades remains under-characterized. In this study, we characterized five EV-D68 clinical isolates from clades A and B using in vitro assays and a neonatal mouse model. We identified a subclade A2 isolate, 12MYKL1607, which exhibited efficient replication and superior binding in rhabdomyosarcoma and neuroblastoma cells compared to other clades. In one-day-old mice, subcutaneous infection with 12MYKL1607 resulted in consistent AFM-like paralysis by 4 to 5 days post-infection. Tissue viral load and histopathological analysis suggested that brown adipose tissue may serve as an initial replication site, followed by robust replication in limb skeletal muscle. The resulting high viral load likely facilitates neuroinvasion of the spinal cord via the neuromuscular junction, with occasional progression to the brainstem as well. Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed the localization of viral antigens within the motor neurons of the spinal cord anterior horns and brainstem. We speculate that the virus travels along somatic motor nerves via retrograde axonal transport, consistent with other neurotropic enteroviruses. Our findings demonstrate that neurovirulence is not clade-specific, as contemporary clade A2 isolates closely recapitulate human CNS infection. This experimental model provides a robust platform for evaluating potential prophylaxis or treatment interventions, and highlights the necessity for broad molecular surveillance beyond clade B to mitigate the ongoing threat of enterovirus-associated neurological disease.

articles.title: AI-derived retinal vascular metrics and MoCA-B-defined mild cognitive impairment in type 2 diabetes: a community-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor for mild cognitive impairment (MCI). As an embryological extension of the brain, the retina offers a unique window into cerebral microvascular health; artificial intelligence (AI) now enables objective, large-scale quantification of retinal vascular parameters to investigate this association.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify retinal vascular metrics using AI in community-managed T2DM patients and examine their association with MCI.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled T2DM patients from four community health centers in Guiyang, China. Fundus photographs were analyzed using an AI platform with established performance in previous studies to derive vascular density (VD), fractal dimension (FD), and other metrics. Cognitive function was assessed using the basic version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-B), with MCI status determined by MoCA-B cut-offs. Separate logistic regression models were constructed for each retinal indicator as the sole exposure variable, with identical DAG-derived covariate sets introduced sequentially. Stratified and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness.

RESULTS: Among 630 community‑dwelling patients with T2DM, the prevalence of MCI was 33.2% (n = 209).
