Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, BMI, educational level, hypertension, and HbA1c showed that VD (per 1% increment: OR = 0.987, 95% CI 0.979, 0.995), FD (per 0.1 increment: OR = 0.221, 95% CI 0.050, 0.982), and fractal dimension of the vessel centerline (FDVC, per 0.1 increment: OR = 0.359, 95% CI 0.131, 0.983) were nominally associated with lower odds of MCI in exploratory analyses. Stratified analyses indicated consistent directions of these associations across subgroups defined by age and diabetes duration. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the associations for VD and FDVC.

CONCLUSION: VD, FD, and FDVC were nominally associated with MoCA‑B‑defined MCI in community‑dwelling patients with T2DM in exploratory analyses, suggesting that these measures may serve as candidate imaging correlates of microvascular alterations underlying MCI.

articles.title: The state of anesthesia service delivery in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review of health system capacity gaps.
articles.abstract: Safe anesthesia is fundamental to surgical, obstetric, trauma, and emergency care, yet anesthesia systems across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remain critically under-resourced, contributing to perioperative mortality rates approximately twice the global average. This systematic review synthesized evidence on anesthesia service delivery capacity across SSA, focusing on workforce, infrastructure, equipment, essential medicines, and training systems. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261404762). Six electronic databases and grey literature sources were searched for studies published between January 2010 and March 2026. Eligible studies reported primary data on anesthesia capacity in SSA. Study selection, risk-of-bias assessment, and data extraction were done by two independent reviewers using Rayyan software. Methodological quality was assessed using appropriate critical appraisal tools, and findings were synthesized using a convergent mixed-methods approach. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Physician anesthesiologist density was critically low (median: 0.38 per 100,000 population), with non-physician providers delivering most anesthetic care. Major system deficiencies included limited functional operating theatres, unreliable oxygen and electricity supply, high proportions of non-functional anesthesia equipment, shortages of essential medicines, and inadequate workforce training and continuing professional development. These collectively compromise the safety, quality, and accessibility of perioperative care across the region. The evidence indicates that strengthening anesthesia services requires coordinated health system investment. Sustainable progress towards Universal Health Coverage and the Global Surgery 2030 targets will depend on integrated strategies to expand the workforce, strengthen infrastructure, improve equipment maintenance and medicine supply chains, and enhance education, governance, and financing for anesthesia services.

articles.title: Melatonin ameliorates calcification in senescent vascular smooth muscle cells under phosphate conditions via the PI3K/AKT pathway.
articles.abstract: In patients with chronic kidney disease, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) senescence and osteogenic transdifferentiation induced by factors such as hyperphosphatemia are key pathological mechanisms underlying vascular calcification. Recent studies have shown that melatonin exerts protective effects by modulating this process. This study investigated whether melatonin improves calcification in hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced senescent VSMCs under phosphate (Pi) conditions through activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) pathway, a critical regulator of cell survival and metabolism. A mouse VSMC line was used to establish an H2O2- induced senescence model. Cell viability was assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay. Senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) staining was used to evaluate cellular senescence. Western blot analysis was performed to determine the protein expression levels of PI3K, AKT, phosphorylated AKT (p-AKT), Runx-2, and p21. Alizarin Red S staining and intracellular calcium content measurements were conducted to assess VSMC calcification. Melatonin significantly reduced SA-β-Gal activity, enhanced VSMC viability, decreased the Alizarin Red S-positivearea, and lowered intracellular calcium levels. Melatonin downregulated Runx-2 and p21 expression while upregulating PI3K, AKT, and p-AKT expression. In contrast, the PI3K/AKT inhibitor LY294002 exacerbated calcification and inhibited activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway.These results suggest that melatonin may mitigate VSMCs calcification associated with aging in a phosphate-rich environment by activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway at the cellular level. LY294002(PI3K inhibitor)blocks this protective effect and aggravates cellular damage and calcification, further suggesting that the PI3K/AKT pathway plays a critical regulatory role incalcification process in cultured VSMCs.

articles.title: Design and rationale of a prospective cohort study integrating cardiovascular, metabolic, and cognitive outcomes across the spectrum of chronic kidney disease: the Vasc-CKD study.
articles.abstract: We present the study design and protocol of a single-center, prospective cohort study in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) (n = 497). The objective of this study is to provide an integrated and comprehensive characterization of cardiovascular disease, oxidative stress, mineral and bone disorder, vascular calcification propensity, and cognitive function across the full spectrum of CKD, including non-dialysis CKD, hemodialysis, and peritoneal dialysis. Participants will be followed systematically for two years, with the collection of hard clinical endpoints, including major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), initiation of dialysis, and all-cause mortality.Previous research in CKD has largely examined these domains in isolation-for example, studies focusing on arterial stiffness and cognitive decline, or investigations into the prognostic value of individual biomarkers of calcification and mineral metabolism, such as fibroblast growth factor-23, fetuin-A, or matrix GLA protein (MGP), for cardiovascular outcomes and renal disease progression. In contrast, the present protocol is designed to integrate these interrelated pathophysiological pathways within a single, unified framework.This protocol provides a transparent methodological reference for planned longitudinal and nested analyses arising from this large cohort. By capturing various phenotypic data across CKD stages, it aims to enhance understanding of the interactions between cardiovascular pathology, metabolic disturbances, and cognitive impairment in CKD. If the proposed associations are confirmed, the resulting dataset may support improved risk stratification, facilitate the identification of high-risk phenotypes, and generate testable hypotheses for future interventional studies targeting oxidative stress, vascular calcification propensity, or arterial stiffness in the CKD population.

articles.title: Vigilance Against Complications of Radiofrequency Ablation Cordectomy in Early-Stage Glottic Cancer.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to systematically evaluate complications of radiofrequency ablation (RFA) cordectomy for early-stage glottic carcinoma and latent risk factors.

METHODS: The early stage glottic carcinoma patients who received transoral surgery by RFA between January 2022 and June 2025 were enrolled in this study. Primary outcomes were incidence of postoperative glottic granuloma and major complications.

RESULTS: In this study a total of 54 patients were included, 38 patients (70.4%) had T1a tumors, 7 (12.9%) had T1b tumors, and 9 (16.7%) had T2 tumors. Based on the extent of cordectomy, the 54 enrolled cases were stratified into three types: Type A (partial cordectomy, n = 30), Type B (total cordectomy, n = 15), and Type C (extended cordectomy, n = 9). The extent of cordectomy was associated with T stage (p < 0.001). The incidence of granuloma was 79.6% (n = 43). Five complication cases (9.3%) were identified, including four thyroid cartilage necrosis and one infection. Five patients who experienced postoperative complications all underwent Type C cordectomy.

CONCLUSION: Although RFA is a novel surgical modality for early-stage glottic carcinoma, its clinical adoption warrants careful consideration. This procedure is associated with a high incidence of granulomas and may lead to complications.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 4.

articles.title: Delayed integration of a documented mitochondrial DNA m.3243A>G result into psychiatric care: Chronic depression, progressive hearing loss, and diabetes in a maternally affected family-A case report.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The maternally inherited m.3243A>G variant produces a continuum of mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) to maternally inherited diabetes and deafness (MIDD).

CASE PRESENTATION: A man with autism spectrum disorder, mild intellectual disability, and progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss presented to psychiatry at age 28 years with a major depressive episode. Two years earlier, a hearing-loss panel had detected m.3243A>G in him, his mother, and his sister. The psychiatrist later recorded the hearing loss as stress-related. The genetic result reached psychiatric care only after the death of his sister, a decade later. Diabetes was first documented the following year; the diabetes service suspected MIDD. He said he had never been told a genetic result and declined diabetes and neurology referrals.

CONCLUSION: This case documents two failure points: non-integration of an existing result and incomplete reformulation after recognition. We propose targeted retrieval of prior reports, accessible explanations, follow-up responsibility, and confirmation of receipt by receiving services. Neuropsychiatric involvement is part of the phenotype, although the specific cause of depression cannot be assigned.

articles.title: Massive ascites with preserved serum albumin in adult anorexia nervosa: Impact on eating behavior and weight-based treatment assessment.
articles.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascites is a rare complication of anorexia nervosa (AN) and is typically associated with hypoalbuminemia. Its influence on eating behavior and on the evaluation of treatment response remains poorly characterized.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 30-year-old woman with AN presented with massive ascites despite a preserved serum albumin level, a presentation not previously reported in adults. Imaging, ascitic fluid analysis, and serological testing excluded cirrhosis, malignancy, infection, and autoimmune serositis. The fluid showed a high serum-ascites albumin gradient (SAAG, 2.1 g/dL) with preserved protein (3.1 g/dL) and normal lactate dehydrogenase. Although the SAAG was high, there was no evidence of portal hypertension, and the mechanism remains undetermined. Serum and ascitic carbohydrate antigen 125 were elevated and normalized as the ascites resolved. Ascites-related symptoms, including early satiety, abdominal pain, and nausea, further reduced oral intake, while fluctuations in body fluid obscured the weight gain expected from nutritional rehabilitation, making weight-based assessment of treatment efficacy difficult. The ascites resolved with nutritional therapy and diuretics.

CONCLUSION: Ascites can develop in adult patients with AN even when serum albumin is preserved. Beyond the psychopathology of AN, somatic symptoms caused by ascites may influence eating behavior and contribute to weight loss. Because fluctuations in body fluid can confound weight-based assessment of treatment response, comprehensive clinical evaluation incorporating abdominal imaging, rather than body weight alone, is warranted.

articles.title: Effect of Cysteamine on 90-Day Mortality in Patients With Severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia: The REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia Investigators
articles.abstract: Cysteamine has antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and antibiotic-potentiating effects. We evaluated IV cysteamine in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia within REMAP-CAP (Randomized Embedded Multifactorial Adaptive Platform for Community-Acquired Pneumonia) trial, an international adaptive platform trial evaluating multiple interventions across several therapeutic domains. Adults requiring respiratory or cardiovascular organ support were randomized within the cysteamine domain to IV cysteamine (5 mg/kg every 8 hr for up to 10 d) or control. The dichotomous primary outcome was 90-day all-cause mortality, analyzed using Bayesian logistic regression. Recruitment to this domain stopped for operational futility before predefined statistical thresholds were met. Thirty-six patients received cysteamine (n = 19) or control (n = 17). Ninety-day mortality was 26% vs. 35%, respectively (odds ratio 0.64, 95% credible interval 0.18-2.19), with a 76% posterior probability of benefit. One serious adverse event occurred, unrelated to cysteamine. These preliminary findings suggest possible benefit, but the small sample size precludes definitive efficacy conclusions. Further studies of cysteamine in severe pneumonia are warranted.

articles.title: Associations between urate‑lowering strategies and kidney function trajectories: a real‑world comparative study.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia contributes to chronic kidney disease progression, yet whether different urate-lowering agents are associated with distinct kidney function trajectories remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study evaluated the associations between dotinurad, a selective urate transporter 1 (URAT1) inhibitor, and kidney function trajectories compared with benzbromarone and allopurinol. Adults treated with uric acid lowering agents (ULAs) at a university hospital between January 2021 and April 2024 were included. The primary outcome was annual change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Secondary outcomes included rapid eGFR decline (≥4 mL/min/1.73 m2/year) and sustained eGFR decline (≥10% from baseline). Among 605 patients (median follow-up 369 days), adjusted mixed-effects analyses estimated annual eGFR slopes of -1.58, -1.87, and -0.78 mL/min/1.73 m2/year for allopurinol, benzbromarone, and dotinurad, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. Rapid eGFR decline occurred in 16.8%, 26.2%, and 12.2% of patients receiving allopurinol, benzbromarone, and dotinurad, respectively. In multivariable logistic regression, compared with benzbromarone, both dotinurad (odds ratio [OR]: 0.34, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.16-0.75) and allopurinol (OR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.31-0.99) were associated with lower odds of rapid eGFR decline. Sensitivity analyses using alternative decline thresholds (≥3 or ≥5 mL/min/1.73 m2/year) yielded similar findings. In Cox analyses, compared with benzbromarone, dotinurad was associated with a lower hazard of sustained eGFR decline (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.46, 95% CI: 0.24-0.88). These findings suggest potential differences in kidney outcomes across urate-lowering strategies.

articles.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endothelial protective effect in bEnd3 cells and mouse renal glomerular endothelial cells (MRGECs) subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Network pharmacology suggested that ferroptosis may be involved in the effects of DHI against cerebral and renal I/R injury. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between selected DHI components and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) or solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11). Molecular dynamic simulations indicated that the selected protein-ligand complexes remained relatively stable, while molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area analyses supported favorable binding free energies. Similar to Fer-1 treatment, DHI improved cell proliferation, reduced Fe2+ levels and lipid peroxidation, and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression in OGD/R-induced bEnd3 cells and MRGECs. In conclusion, DHI attenuated injury in bEnd3 cells and MRGECs subjected to OGD/R, accompanied by reduced Fe2+ accumulation and lipid peroxidation and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression. Together with the shared ferroptosis-related pathways identified by network pharmacology, these findings suggest a common ferroptosis-related endothelial protective response to DHI in cerebral and renal I/R injury.

articles.title: A review on gedunin as an anticancer agent: molecular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gedunin is a limonoid natural product that has demonstrated anticancer activity in preclinical experimental models. However, findings vary across cancer types and experimental systems, and the extent to which its proposed molecular targets have been validated remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review evaluated the preclinical anticancer effects of gedunin, focusing on its reported molecular targets and signaling pathways, effects on cancer stem-cell phenotypes and chemoresistance, formulation and combination strategies, and translational limitations.

METHODS: The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar were searched from database inception to July 2026. Eligible studies were original, peer-reviewed investigations of chemically identified gedunin in in vitro, in vivo, or cancer-related mechanistic and biochemical models. Reviews, conference abstracts, preprints, studies of crude plant extracts without chemically identified gedunin, duplicate publications, and studies without relevant pharmacological or mechanistic outcomes were excluded. Data on cancer models, experimental conditions, gedunin concentrations or doses, molecular findings, pharmacological outcomes, and translational relevance were extracted. Because of differences in cancer models, experimental designs, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively.

RESULTS: The search identified 1048 records. Following removal of 877 duplicates, 171 records were screened by title and abstract, and 149 were excluded. Twenty-two full-text reports were assessed, of which four were excluded, leaving 18 independent original studies. Gedunin was reported to exert antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, cell-cycle-modulating, anti-invasive, anti-stemness, and chemosensitizing effects across several experimental cancer models. Reported molecular associations involved heat shock protein 90 (HSP90)-related proteostasis, phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT), Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT), nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), Sonic Hedgehog/Glioma-associated oncogene (Shh/Gli), focal adhesion kinase/Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (FAK/ROCK), oxidative-stress responses, and mitochondrial apoptotic signaling. Selected studies also reported activity against cancer stem-cell-associated phenotypes and drug-resistant models, while nanoformulation and combination approaches enhanced activity in experimental systems. Evidence for a direct interaction between gedunin and prostaglandin E synthase 3 (p23) was primarily derived from one study and remains insufficiently replicated. Overall, the evidence was dominated by in vitro investigations, with limited characterization of pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, systematic toxicity, and efficacy in clinically relevant in vivo models.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports gedunin as a promising preclinical anticancer candidate, but not as a clinically validated anticancer agent or a compound with definitively validated molecular targets. The p23-HSP90 axis represents a candidate mechanism requiring independent confirmation through genetic perturbation, rescue experiments, direct target-engagement assays such as cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA), and biophysical approaches including surface plasmon resonance (SPR) or isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Future studies should prioritize standardized gedunin preparations, rigorous target validation, pharmacokinetic and biodistribution characterization, optimized delivery systems, systematic toxicological evaluation, biomarker-guided combination strategies, and validation in clinically relevant in vivo models. At present, safety evidence should be regarded as limited preclinical data; systematic toxicology remains unknown.

articles.title: Loureirin D alleviates ischemia-induced blood-brain barrier disruption via CD38-mediated suppression of microglial MAPK/JNK/ERK signaling.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a critical gatekeeper of central nervous system homeostasis, and its disruption represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying secondary brain injury and adverse clinical outcomes following ischemic stroke (IS). Consequently, therapeutic strategies aimed at preserving BBB integrity after ischemia hold substantial promise for IS treatment. Loureirin D, a bioactive flavonoid isolated from Dragon's blood, has demonstrated preliminary neuroprotective efficacy in photothrombotic stroke. However, whether BBB integrity is preserved in clinically relevant models of sustained, severe cerebral ischemia remains unknown, and the underlying molecular mechanisms remains to be elucidated.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate whether Loureirin D protects against ischemia‑induced BBB disruption, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.

STUDY DESIGN: Combined in vivo and in vitro mechanistic studies using rat permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAO) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD)‑exposed microglia‑endothelial co‑culture system.

METHODS: A rat model of pMCAO was established by intraluminal filament insertion. Neurological deficits and BBB integrity were evaluated by Bederson scoring, Evans blue extravasation, brain water content, IgG leakage, and western blot of tight junction (TJ) proteins (zonula occludens-1[ZO‑1], occludin) and matrix metalloproteinase 2/9 (MMP2/9). An OGD model and microglia‑endothelial co‑culture were used to recapitulate the ischemic neuroinflammatory microenvironment, and the endothelial barrier function was assessed using transendothelial electrical resistance and dextran permeability. Transcriptomic profiling, molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), and small interfering RNA mediated knockdown were integrated to identify critical targets and mechanisms, with validation by western blot and immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: Loureirin D markedly ameliorated neurological deficits and attenuated BBB disruption-as evidenced by reduced Evans blue extravasation, brain edema, and IgG leakage-and suppressed the ischemia‑induced upregulation of MMP2/9 in pMCAO rats. Furthermore, it restored the expression levels of ZO‑1 and occludin. In OGD‑exposed bEnd.3 cells, Loureirin D directly attenuated apoptosis, downregulated Bax and Caspase‑3 proteins, and suppressed reactive oxygen species generation. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) analysis identified CD38 and Mapk11 as differentially expressed genes, and their dysregulation was subsequently validated at the mRNA level in ischemic brain tissues. Molecular docking simulations and CETSA, further supported by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay, collectively provided robust evidence for the direct physical interaction between Loureirin D and CD38. In OGD‑exposed BV2 microglial cells, Loureirin D suppressed microglial activation, as evidenced by reduced CD86 expression, and inhibited the phosphorylation of mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK), c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), and p38, thereby attenuating MMP2/9 secretion. In a microglia-endothelial cell co‑culture system, Loureirin D preserved endothelial TJ integrity, as demonstrated by the sustained expression and proper localization of ZO-1 and occludin. These protective effects were abolished by CD38 knockdown, indicating a CD38-dependent mechanism.

CONCLUSIONS: Loureirin D inhibits microglia activation by specifically targeting CD38, thereby suppressing the MAPK-MMP-2/9 signaling cascade and preserving BBB integrity. Concurrently, it directly protects brain microvascular endothelial cells against apoptosis and oxidative stress. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic rationale for the therapeutic potential of Loureirin D in IS and provide a translational foundation for the development of CD38-targeted interventions for neurovascular protection in cerebrovascular diseases.

articles.title: Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for brain diseases: Processing, membrane-derived functions and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Brain diseases such as glioblastoma (GBM), Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and ischemic stroke remain difficult to treat in part because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts and spatially controls the entry of many therapeutic agents. Cell membrane-coated nanoparticles (CNPs) integrate cell-derived membrane shells with nanoparticle cores made of polymeric, lipid-based, or inorganic materials, offering promising biomimetic platforms for brain drug delivery. This review summarizes CNP fabrication and characterization methods and discusses how molecules associated with specific membrane sources and disease-specific delivery barriers inform platform design. Major membrane sources, including red blood cells, immune cells, stem cells, cancer cells, and platelets, are compared in terms of their relevant surface molecules, recognition mechanisms, potential delivery functions, and limitations. We further discuss how preparation and functionalization affect coating integrity, membrane-protein accessibility, and payload retention, and outline key challenges in reproducible manufacturing, biosafety, and clinical translation. This review provides a framework for evaluating CNP design and for assessing the evidence supporting brain-targeted delivery.

articles.title: A microwave-responsive bio-heterojunction via synergistic antibacterial and osteogenic microenvironment temporal regulation for treating periodontitis in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetic periodontitis defects remain challenging to repair due to persistent oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, insufficient vascularization, and poor osseointegration. Herein, a microwave (MW)-responsive bio-heterojunction (BioHJ) composed of a vanadium (V)-cobalt (Co)-doped porphyrin metal-organic framework loaded with calcium peroxide (V-CoTCPP/CaO2) is designed to achieve potent antibacterial activity and temporal modulation of microenvironment. During the infectious inflammatory stage, V-CoTCPP/CaO2 generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) via excellent dielectric loss and microwave thermal effects that exhibit antibacterial properties, effectively disrupting biofilms. This temporal regulation is achieved through externally controlled MW on/off switching: microwave-on drives the antibacterial ROS phase, whereas microwave-off initiates the reparative phase. Importantly, this strategy highlights the critical role of the early-stage M1 macrophage-activated immune response in microbial elimination, which is essential for microbial clearance and subsequent tissue repair. Subsequently, Co ions scavenge residual ROS through redox reactions to alleviate oxidative stress while the released oxygen may additionally suppress periodontal anaerobic bacteria, inducing macrophage polarization toward the reparative M2 phenotype, thereby promoting angiogenesis and osteogenic differentiation with V and Ca synergistically. In vivo experiments reveal that V-CoTCPP/CaO2 significantly ameliorates periodontal tissue inflammation and reduces the loss of alveolar bone by reducing inflammatory infiltration and collagen destruction. Overall, this work establishes a MW-responsive platform that dynamically interacts with the biological microenvironment to orchestrate the complex requirements of consecutive healing stages, offering a promising therapeutic approach for diabetic periodontitis.

articles.title: Influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors, including asthma diagnosis, in Korea: analysis of the Korea national health and nutrition examination survey (2014-2021).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate influenza vaccination coverage and associated factors in the South Korean population, focusing on individuals with asthma across age groups.

METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional study was conducted using Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2014-2021) for 43,191 individuals (aged ≥6 years). Vaccination rates and predictors were examined in the general population and those with asthma across four age cohorts (6-13, 14-18, 19-64, and ≥ 65 years) using survey-weighted logistic regression.

RESULTS: Vaccination coverage was consistently higher among individuals with asthma than those without: 68.2% vs. 62.8% (ages 6-13), 36.8% vs. 27.1% (ages 14-18), 28.5% vs. 27.0% (ages 19-39), 48.2% vs. 32.1% (ages 40-64), and 85.3% vs. 82.5% (ages ≥65). Female sex and chronic comorbidities positively correlated with vaccination. Increasing age was linked to lower coverage in youth but higher coverage in adults. Notably, asthma history independently predicted vaccination in age groups with lower baseline coverage.

CONCLUSIONS: Although individuals with asthma showed higher coverage, vaccination rates remained suboptimal, particularly among adolescents and working-age adults. Proactive age-tailored vaccination strategies are needed.

articles.title: Segmental aortic energy loss in patients with bicuspid aortic valve.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Altered aortic flow dynamics are observed in patients with bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), but their local energetic characteristics remain incompletely understood. The primary objective was to compare total and segmental energy loss (EL) between patients with BAV without significant valve dysfunction and matched controls. The subsequent clinical and structural course of the BAV cohort was described.

METHODS: Sixteen patients with BAV and 16 matched controls underwent baseline four-dimensional flow cardiovascular magnetic resonance. Total and segmental aortic EL were quantified and normalized to flow. Commissural orientation was assessed. Clinical follow-up was available in all 16 patients with BAV, and paired baseline and approximately 10-year CMR assessments of aortic dimensions were available in 14.

RESULTS: Mean flow-normalized EL was approximately twofold higher in patients with BAV from the sinus of Valsalva to proximal ascending aorta (0.78 [0.59-1.14] vs 0.40 [0.29-0.67] mW/[L/min]; P = 0.015) and from proximal to distal ascending aorta (1.26 [0.79-1.59] vs 0.64 [0.39-1.07] mW/[L/min]; P = 0.013). Commissural angle was not significantly associated with segmental EL. No major BAV-related cardiovascular complications occurred during follow-up. In paired examinations, maximum ascending aortic diameter increased from 3.40 ± 0.67 to 3.75 ± 0.67 cm (P < 0.001), whereas the body surface area-indexed increase was attenuated (1.88 ± 0.29 to 1.97 ± 0.33 cm/m2; P = 0.056).

CONCLUSIONS: Segmental aortic EL was increased in patients with BAV despite the absence of significant valve dysfunction. The approximately 10-year follow-up provides descriptive clinical and structural characterization but does not establish a relationship between baseline EL and subsequent outcomes.

articles.title: Multimodal imaging evaluation of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery: A case report.
articles.abstract: Giant coronary artery aneurysm (CAA) is a rare cardiovascular disease characterized by abnormal coronary dilatation and a high mortality rate. It lacks specific clinical manifestations and is often detected incidentally during imaging examinations, so early identification and timely intervention are crucial for improving patient prognosis. Existing studies have rarely documented the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, and clinical diagnostic and therapeutic experience remains to be further enriched. Here, we report a case of a giant aneurysm originating from a branch of the left circumflex coronary artery (LCX), incidentally detected by transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) performed for palpitations. TTE and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), contrast-enhanced echocardiography, and CT angiography (CTA) were combined to accurately evaluate the location, size, and adjacent anatomical relationship of the aneurysm, and a surgical plan was formulated accordingly. The patient recovered well after surgery. This case summarizes the multimodal imaging characteristics of giant CAA, offering a clinical reference for similar rare cases.

articles.title: Nanomedicine for biofilm infections in chronic and diabetic wounds: targeted nanocarriers and energy-activated therapies.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-associated infection complicates the management of chronic and diabetic wounds by combining microbial antimicrobial tolerance with impaired host defense and tissue repair. Nanomedicine offers opportunities to improve local delivery, disrupt extracellular polymeric substances, and activate antibacterial effects using light or ultrasound. However, activity against planktonic bacteria, inhibition of biofilm formation, reduction of established biofilms, and accelerated wound closure represent different outcomes and should not be interpreted interchangeably. This critical narrative review examines bacterial membrane vesicles, metal-organic frameworks, metal and metal oxide nanoparticles, and energy-activated therapies through a common framework linking delivery, bacterial injury, host responses, and the strength of supporting evidence. Particular attention is given to context-dependent redox activity, the distinction between antibacterial immune activation and resolution of inflammation, and the limitations of extrapolating from simplified assays to diabetic wounds. We also distinguish machine-learning-assisted biofilm identification and antimicrobial design from experimentally validated optimization of wound-directed nanoplatforms. Comparative analysis identifies recurring trade-offs involving matrix penetration, local toxicity, activation conditions, manufacturing complexity, and repeated-exposure safety. The evidence supports further development of selected nanoplatforms as adjuncts to wound care, while clinical benefit, durable biofilm control, and generalizable design rules remain insufficiently established.

articles.title: Polyploidy is associated with enhanced S6K1-S6 signaling and improved tolerance to glucose starvation.
articles.abstract: Polyploidy, a condition characterized by the presence of more than two complete sets of chromosomes, is associated with cancer, diabetes, and aging. The mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) is a central regulator of cellular growth, protein synthesis, and metabolism, and its dysregulation contributes to the progression of these diseases. However, the relationship between mTORC1 signaling and polyploidy remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the role of mTORC1 signaling in the generation and maintenance of polyploid cells. Polyploidy was induced in HEK293T cells using cytochalasin B and ZM447439 and evaluated through flow cytometric analysis of DNA content (greater than 4 N), multinucleation, increased cell size, and asynchronous cell cycle. Both treatments promoted polyploidy and were associated with increased phosphorylation of S6K1 and S6, without significantly altering the phosphorylation of 4E-BP1. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of S6 signaling using Torin1 or rapamycin significantly reduced the accumulation of polyploid cells induced by cytochalasin B and ZM447439. Furthermore, under glucose starvation, polyploid cells exhibited improved survival, which was associated with reduced levels of apoptotic markers and increased MEK phosphorylation. Collectively, these findings indicate an association between polyploidy and increased phosphorylation of S6K1 and S6, while pharmacological inhibition of S6 signaling by Torin1 or rapamycin was associated with reduced polyploid cell accumulation. Furthermore, polyploid cells exhibited increased tolerance to glucose starvation, suggesting an association between the polyploid state and improved survival under metabolic stress. These findings suggest that the mTORC1-S6K1-S6 signaling axis may represent a potential therapeutic target in polyploidy-associated cancers.

articles.title: Isolated abdominal wall metastasis of endometrial carcinosarcoma: A case report.
articles.abstract: Uterine carcinosarcoma, formerly called malignant mixed Müllerian tumor, is a rare and aggressive biphasic neoplasm made up of malignant epithelial and mesenchymal elements. Recurrence is frequent even after multimodal treatment, and distant relapses usually involve the lung, liver, or peritoneum. Isolated recurrence in the abdominal wall or subcutaneous tissue is rare and can easily be mistaken for a benign or unrelated soft-tissue lesion. A 71-year-old woman with hypertension and gout was diagnosed with grade 2 endometrioid endometrial adenocarcinoma, staged IA on preoperative MRI. Surgical staging (total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, and bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy) revealed a carcinosarcoma with a predominantly endometrioid carcinomatous component, deep (>50%) myometrial invasion, endocervical stromal involvement, and lymphovascular invasion (pT2 N0). She received adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy with vaginal brachytherapy, followed by 6 cycles of paclitaxel-carboplatin, and remained disease-free for more than 3 years. Routine surveillance imaging then showed a new calcified mass in the anterior abdominal wall with an adjacent para-umbilical nodule. Percutaneous biopsy confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma whose immunohistochemical profile was consistent with the known gynecologic primary. With no disease elsewhere, she underwent wide local excision with mesh reconstruction, achieving clear margins, followed by radiotherapy to the surgical bed. Uterine carcinosarcoma can recur in unusual extra-pelvic soft-tissue sites years after seemingly successful treatment. Any new abdominal wall or subcutaneous lesion in these patients should be biopsied promptly and discussed in a multidisciplinary setting, as isolated recurrences may still be treated with curative intent.

articles.title: Clinical and Patient-Centered Outcomes of Catheter Ablation According to Symptom Status in Very Elderly Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: A Subgroup Analysis of the REHEALTH AF Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation can improve symptoms and functional status in very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation. However, it is uncertain if baseline symptom status can pinpoint those who will benefit the most.

METHODS: This exploratory subgroup analysis examined data from the REHEALTH AF registry, which included patients aged 80 and above with non-valvular atrial fibrillation. Patients were categorized by baseline symptom status and compared based on treatment strategy: catheter ablation versus non-ablation management.

RESULTS: Of 703 patients, 238 were asymptomatic, while 465 were symptomatic. Catheter ablation did not significantly reduce the primary composite endpoint in either asymptomatic (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.39; 95% confidence interval, 0.39-4.92; p = 0.61) or symptomatic patients (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-1.20; p = 0.17), with no significant interaction between treatment and symptoms. Exploratory analyses indicated ablation was associated with more favorable changes in a wider range of 1-year patient-centered measures among symptomatic patients, such as quality of life, self-rated health, Mini-Mental State Examination score, frailty distribution, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide level, and left atrial diameter. In asymptomatic patients, improvements were mainly seen in self-rated health and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide level.

CONCLUSIONS: In very elderly patients with atrial fibrillation, baseline symptom status did not identify those with a clear short-term event reduction following catheter ablation. Nevertheless, exploratory analyses revealed more favorable changes across various patient-centered measures in symptomatic patients, although formal evidence of effect modification was limited.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trials Registry, UMIN000047023.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of TAVI-first versus PCI-first strategies: A meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal sequence of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. Observational studies suggested lower mortality when PCI was performed after TAVI, but these comparisons may be affected by post-baseline selection. This meta-analysis incorporates the first randomized evidence addressing this question.

METHODS: Randomized and observational studies comparing TAVI-first or PCI after TAVI with PCI-first or PCI before TAVI were included. All-cause mortality was analyzed using adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) from observational studies and an HR approximated from 1-year mortality in the randomized trial. Estimates were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp inference and stratified by study design. Secondary clinical outcomes were exploratory.

RESULTS: Six studies were included (n = 4317): five observational studies (n = 3331) and one randomized trial (n = 986). Five studies contributed to the primary mortality analysis, which showed no significant difference between TAVI-first/PCI-after and PCI-first/PCI-before (HR, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-1.63). Mortality in the randomized trial was 9.5% in both groups. No significant differences were observed for stroke, myocardial infarction, major bleeding, or major vascular complications.

CONCLUSIONS: No mortality advantage was demonstrated for either procedural sequence. In selected patients with stable coronary artery disease and suitable coronary anatomy undergoing balloon-expandable TAVI, TAVI-first appears to be a reasonable alternative to routine upfront PCI, although revascularization and timing should remain individualized. Further direct randomized trials are required.

articles.title: Clinical significance of ovarian metastasis in gastric-type cervical adenocarcinoma: a retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric-type cervical adenocarcinoma (GCA) is a rare and aggressive subtype of cervical carcinoma characterised by a relatively high propensity for ovarian metastasis. Nevertheless, the risk factors, metastatic pathway and prognostic implications of ovarian metastasis in GCA remain poorly elucidated. This study aimed to characterise the clinicopathological profiles of GCA patients and clarify the clinical prognostic value of ovarian metastasis in GCA.

METHODS: Clinicopathological and follow-up data of 71 patients with GCA at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Centre from 2011 to 2023 were retrospectively analysed. The chi-square test and Kaplan-Meier's survival analysis were adopted to compare intergroup differences. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to screen independent prognostic factors, while logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors associated with ovarian metastasis.

RESULTS: In this cohort, 66.2% patients presented with FIGO stage III-IV disease. Histologically, most tumours were well-differentiated (43.8%) and exhibited low Ki-67 proliferation index (68.4%). The incidence of ovarian metastasis was 38.3% (23/60), among which 78.3% of cases presented with bilateral ovarian involvement and 52.2% were complicated by synchronous fallopian tube metastasis. Multivariate Cox regression confirmed that ovarian metastasis was an independent adverse prognostic factor for overall survival (OS) (HR = 4.144, 95% CI: 1.539-11.158, p = 0.005). Patients with ovarian metastasis had a significantly lower 3-year OS rate than those without metastasis (20.5% vs. 80.4%, p < 0.001). Furthermore, multivariate logistic regression identified uterine corpus invasion as an independent risk factor for ovarian metastasis in GCA patients (OR = 4.314, 95% CI: 1.264-14.726, p = 0.020).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the typical well-differentiated histology and low proliferative activity, ovarian metastasis occurs frequently and is strongly correlated with poor survival outcomes. Uterine corpus invasion serves as a valuable predictive indicator for elevated ovarian metastasis risk in GCA, which can facilitate clinical risk stratification and individualised treatment decision-making.

articles.title: Increased risk of arteriovenous fistula thrombosis in haemodialysis patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the occurrence and timing of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance haemodialysis (HD) due to ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) and those with non-vasculitic causes of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included patients receiving maintenance HD for AAV-related ESKD and a control group with ESKD attributed to diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis. The AVF thrombosis analysis was restricted to patients with an AVF during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate the association between AAV and AVF thrombosis.

RESULTS: The study included 31 patients with AAV (mean age 71.3 ± 13.6 years; 58% male) and 102 controls (mean age 55.8 ± 17.9 years; 56% male). Among patients with an AVF, thrombosis occurred in 9 of 18 patients (50%) in the AAV group and 6 of 51 patients (11.8%) in the control group (p = .002). In the unadjusted Cox regression analysis, AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis (HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.43-11.97; p = .009). This association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age (HR 4.46, 95% CI 1.39-14.26; p = .012).

CONCLUSION: AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance HD compared with non-vasculitic ESKD, even after adjustment for age. However, the limited number of thrombotic events and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their implications for vascular access management.

articles.title: Concordance and validity of federated versus centralized analyses in treatment-resistant depression.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether federated analyses can reproduce centralized results for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) risk prediction using privacy-preserving statistical models.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 7272 adults with incident major depressive disorder initiating antidepressants (2015-2021) in Maccabi Healthcare Services, Israel. Treatment-resistant depression was defined as progression to third-line regimens within 24 months. Data were geographically partitioned into 2 nodes to simulate federation. Federated generalized linear and Cox models were estimated using privacy-preserving iteratively reweighted least squares with cross-validated feature selection. Agreement with centralized analyses was assessed using coefficient differences, statistical-significance concordance, and confidence interval (CI) overlap. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, and fairness metrics.

RESULTS: Federated and centralized models showed near-perfect concordance. Feature selection produced almost identical predictor sets, and coefficient estimates were strongly aligned, with mean absolute differences <0.01, complete decision agreement among predictors retained by both models, and >95% CI overlap. Predictive performance was modest but consistent across settings (AUC ∼0.65 for logistic; ∼0.62 for Cox), with preserved calibration and similar subgroup patterns. Federated models reproduced major clinical associations observed centrally, including higher TRD risk with prior antidepressant exposure, psychiatric hospitalization, anxiety and personality disorders, and polypharmacy, and lower risk with atrial fibrillation and delayed therapy initiation.

DISCUSSION: Results show that federated implementations of standard epidemiologic models can retain the validity and stability of centralized analyses, even for complex psychiatric outcomes requiring high-dimensional adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Federated analysis can closely replicate centralized statistical model results while preserving privacy, supporting its use for scalable, multi-institutional epidemiologic research.

articles.title: Anxiety and depressive disorders among children and young people following a cancer diagnosis in England: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychiatric conditions are important survivorship outcomes among children and young people (CYP) diagnosed with cancer. However, many population-based studies have examined hospital contacts only, and estimates of absolute risk can be biased when competing mortality is not accounted for. We estimated absolute risks and relative hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based matched retrospective cohort study across 1474 general practices in England using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum primary care records linked to Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care and mortality records. CYP diagnosed with malignant cancer or any central nervous system tumour at ages 0-24 years between Jan 1, 2000, and Dec 31, 2022, were matched by age, recorded sex, and general practice to up to 20 comparators without cancer at the index date. Primary outcomes were first recorded anxiety and related disorders and depressive disorders; secondary outcomes were first-time psychotropic prescribing. Individuals with pre-index records of the respective outcome were excluded from that outcome analysis. Follow-up ended at outcome occurrence, death, practice deregistration, last data collection, or Dec 31, 2022. We estimated cumulative incidence using the Aalen-Johansen estimator and ethnicity-adjusted cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs) using matched-set stratified Cox models.

FINDINGS: There were 9145 CYP with cancer and 178709 comparators. Adjusted cause-specific HRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.61-1.88) for anxiety and related disorders, 1.16 (1.06-1.26) for depressive disorders, 1.27 (1.20-1.35) for antidepressant prescribing, 2.21 (2.05-2.38) for antipsychotic prescribing, and 2.69 (2.53-2.86) for anxiolytic prescribing. At 15 years, cumulative incidence was 14.1% (95% CI 13.0-15.3) versus 12.8% (12.5-13.1) for anxiety and related disorders, and 12.8% (11.6-14.0) versus 14.1% (13.8-14.5) for depressive disorders. Excess hazards were greatest in the early years after diagnosis.

INTERPRETATION: CYP diagnosed with cancer had higher hazards of clinically recorded anxiety and related disorders, depressive disorders, and first-time psychotropic prescribing. These findings support proactive mental health monitoring and timely referral pathways within cancer and survivorship care, particularly early after diagnosis. Further research should evaluate whether timely assessment and tailored psychosocial support improve outcomes.

FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research Manchester Biomedical Research Centre and Greater Manchester Patient Safety Research Collaboration.

articles.title: GPs' and patients' perceptions regarding the quality of remote consultations: a matched survey from Norwegian general practice.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote consultations, via text, telephone, or video, are increasingly used in primary care, yet direct comparisons of matched GP and patient evaluations remain limited. This study examines positive concordance between GPs and patients across three predefined dimensions: (1) consultation suitability, (2) confidence in the GP's professional assessment, and (3) willingness to reuse the modality.

METHODS: In a cross-sectional matched GP-patient study, GPs and patients evaluated the same remote consultations. During enrolment in a Norwegian online course, GPs evaluated their own consultations and invited patients to complete corresponding assessments (n = 580). Descriptive statistics and logistic regression were used to analyse concordance across the three dimensions.

RESULTS: In 85% of consultations, GPs and patients agreed that the modality was suitable for the main reason for contact. Concordance was lower when the issue was new to the GP (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.47, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.28-0.80) and when patients did not receive adequate answers to their questions (aOR = 0.02 (0.002-0.20)). Concordance in confidence in the GP's assessment was 93%, with lower odds in asynchronous text consultations than in video (aOR = 0.06 (0.006-0.50)). 75% of GP-patient pairs were willing to reuse the modality. Concordance in willingness to reuse was higher for scheduled appointments than acute contacts (aOR = 1.62 (1.07-2.46)) and lower when GPs perceived the patient's health literacy as low (aOR = 0.25 (0.08-0.79)). Lower concordance across all three dimensions was associated with patients reporting less opportunity to ask questions or receive answers during the consultation.

CONCLUSION: The matched GP-patient design proved feasible and offers a novel approach to evaluating remote consultations. Positive quality concordance was high, particularly in consultations concerning known problems and in scheduled rather than acute contacts. Consultation quality may be strengthened by addressing modifiable factors, including continuity, scheduling, tailoring consultations to patients' vulnerability and health literacy, and ensuring clear communication.

articles.title: The mediating role of call centers when patients telephone primary care teams with medical questions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Studies describing patients' telephone access to primary care (PC) teams is sparse. We examined communication flows, breakdowns, and telephone contact center contextual characteristics potentially affecting telephone communication processes between patients and their PC teams for non-urgent medical questions.

STUDY DESIGN: Structured observations (n = 8) and semi-structured interviews (n = 47) during site visits at call centers in one VA regional network, and administrative call center performance data.

METHODS: We use qualitative thematic analysis and descriptive statistics to analyze communication processes and contextual characteristics.

RESULTS: We found that administrative call center agents mediate telephone communication between Veterans and their primary care teams. Communication breakdowns in all sites resulted in "callback loops" (cycles of repeated calls) between Veterans, call centers and PC teams. Call centers differed on contextual characteristics, such as variation in organization and spatial layouts, clinic communication policies, and call volume, potentially contributing to complexity of call center environments. We identified two best practices that may reduce callback loops and facilitate communication: 1) an electronic health record note used by primary care teams to communicate messages to call center staff for patients returning their PC team phone calls, and 2) daily instant message chat groups to address environmental complexity (e.g., reduce background noise and facilitate telephone communication with Veterans).

CONCLUSION: This study contributes to the patient care access literature by mapping communication flows and identifying challenges introduced by call center mediation of patient-to-PC team telephone communication. Identifying and addressing communication breakdowns may improve communication between Veterans and their primary care teams.

articles.title: Cancer risk with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists: An umbrella review of meta-analyses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for diabetes and obesity is increasing, but effects on uncommon or long-latency cancers are uncertain. We synthesised meta-analytic evidence for overall and site-specific cancer risk and assessed methodological quality, overlap, outcome-level certainty, and credibility.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 30 June 2026 for meta-analyses of GLP-1RAs or the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide and incident cancer. Randomised and observational evidence was considered separately; review-level estimates were not recombined. We assessed methodological confidence with AMSTAR 2, overlap with corrected covered area (CCA), outcome-level certainty with a GRADE-informed algorithm, and association credibility with Ioannidis criteria.

FINDINGS: We included 38 meta-analyses from 2012 to 2026. The most comprehensive placebo-controlled randomised evidence (48 trials, 94 245 participants, median follow-up 70 weeks) showed no statistically significant association with thyroid cancer (odds ratio [OR] 1·37, 95% CI 0·82-2·31; 1 fewer to 9 more cases per 10 000 treated), pancreatic cancer (0·84, 0·53-1·35), colorectal cancer (1·11, 0·75-1·65), or breast cancer (0·95, 0·60-1·49), and no overall cancer increase (OR 1·05, 0·98-1·13 across 50 trials). Thyroid and agent-specific haematological signals were inconsistent or based on sparse events; between-review discordance for thyroid and colorectal cancer was largely attributable to comparator restriction, choice of estimator, and handling of zero-event trials rather than to differences in cancer ascertainment. Observational syntheses suggested lower hepatocellular carcinoma risk (hazard ratio 0·60, 95% CI 0·41-0·88), but four reviews had very high overlap (CCA 50·0%). Outcome-level certainty was moderate for five outcomes, low for 11, and very low for five; none was high. No association met class I or II credibility criteria.

INTERPRETATION: Randomised evidence shows no evidence of a material increase in overall or site-specific cancer risk over currently observed trial durations (median about 70 weeks, maximum about 5 years), and cancer concerns alone do not justify withholding indicated GLP-1RA treatment. Small, rare, long-latency, dose-specific, or agent-specific effects cannot be excluded, and the evidence cannot address exposure beyond approximately five years, well short of the 8-10 years generally required to evaluate cancer incidence. Observational protective associations should not support causal or cancer-prevention claims.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Reply to letter to the editor regarding: from cardiometabolic risk to kidney protection: extending the DM-HTN-AKI paradigm to critical care in the Philippines.
Membrane lipid-driven gating of TREK-1 channels: Revisiting anesthetic mechanisms beyond protein targets.
articles.abstract: The mechanistic basis of general anesthesia has long been debated between protein-centric and lipid-centric frameworks, and the TWIK-related potassium channel 1 (TREK-1), a member of the two-pore domain K+ (K2P) superfamily, sits at the intersection of the two as a physiologically relevant target of both volatile and intravenous anesthetics. Although the direct interaction of anesthetics with TREK-1 protein has been studied extensively, how membrane lipid composition and lipid-driven conformational dynamics modulate channel gating remains insufficiently explored. In this review, we synthesize evidence retrieved from PubMed, PubMed Central, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (1996-April 2025) to examine how the physicochemical properties of the lipid bilayer - cholesterol content, phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) abundance, lysophospholipids, and membrane tension - collectively govern TREK-1 activity in anesthetic contexts. Converging data from structural biology, electrophysiology, computational modeling, and animal studies indicate that anesthetics alter bilayer fluidity, reshape the lateral pressure profile, and displace lipid ligands such as PIP2 and arachidonic acid from defined sites on TREK-1, thereby tuning channel open probability through a bidirectional lipid-protein allosteric axis that links membrane dynamics to fenestration and selectivity-filter conformations; consistently, TREK-1 knockout and lipid depletion each attenuate anesthetic sensitivity in vivo. We argue that membrane lipids are not passive bystanders but active modulators of the TREK-1 gating landscape, and that integrating this lipid dimension - through cryo-EM, molecular dynamics simulations, and patient-derived membrane lipidomics - may enable isoform-selective drug design and help explain interindividual variability in anesthetic sensitivity.

articles.title: Long-term staged management of an extensive pelvic and right lower-extremity vascular malformation with major venous abnormalities and postprocedural pulmonary embolism: A case report.
articles.abstract: Extensive vascular malformations involving a limb and major named veins may require repeated treatment over many years. Their abnormal venous anatomy may remain clinically important even when local symptoms are controlled, particularly when subsequent interventions are planned. We report the long-term course of a 26-year-old man with a congenital vascular malformation involving the pelvis and right lower extremity, diagnosed at 13 years of age and historically described as an arteriovenous malformation. Historical CT angiography reports described arteriovenous components together with extensive venous abnormalities, including aneurysmal dilatation of the right popliteal and external iliac veins. Staged surgery during adolescence was followed by an approximately 13-year interval without further invasive treatment, during which the patient initially remained clinically stable before gradually developing recurrent symptoms. At 26 years of age, progressive symptoms prompted combined endovenous laser treatment, electrocoagulation, and sclerotherapy. On postoperative day 7, the patient developed occlusive right popliteal venous thrombosis and acute bilateral pulmonary embolism requiring systemic thrombolysis followed by anticoagulation. The patient stabilized after treatment. At approximately 3-month cardiology follow-up, he was asymptomatic, with preserved cardiac function and good exercise tolerance. Longer-term symptom control was maintained with class III compression therapy, therapeutic exercise, and regular physical activity, with improvement in pain and lower-extremity edema. This case illustrates that major venous abnormalities may remain clinically relevant throughout the long-term course of a complex vascular malformation. In patients undergoing further intervention, lesion-specific venous anatomy and pre-existing thrombotic changes within malformed venous spaces should be considered alongside conventional peri-procedural thromboembolic risk factors. Long-term management should remain individualized and focused on symptoms, function, and surveillance of major vascular abnormalities.

articles.title: The Burden of Traumatic Brain Injury in Ghana's Middle Belt-Part 1: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Epidemiological Trends, Care Patterns, and Healthcare Costs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is the leading cause of injury-related mortality and disability globally and a major public health concern. Road traffic accidents are a major contributor to TBI in low- and middle-income countries. The aim of this study was to assess the epidemiological trends of TBI burden and outcomes at a major referral center in Ghana.

METHODS: This study is a subanalysis of a retrospective cross-sectional study conducted at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, Ghana, including adult TBI patients (≥19 years) managed between September 2022 and August 2023. Descriptive statistics were reported for clinical data including mechanism of injury, severity of injury, management, time factors, and cost of care.

RESULTS: A total of 477 patients diagnosed with TBI were included in the study. The most common demographic was men aged 19 to 29 years (32%). 80% of patients were referrals and 18% were transported directly to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital from the site of injury. The most common mechanism of injury was road traffic accidents (72%). 63% of patients had mild TBI, 19% had moderate TBI, and 18% had severe TBI. The median time to neuroimaging was 3 days (IQR: 1, 5). Skull fractures (43%), subdural hematoma (35%), and intraparenchymal hemorrhage/contusions (34%) were the most common radiological findings. 24% of TBI patients underwent surgical management at a median admission-to-surgery time of 3 days (IQR: 1, 7). The median hospital length of stay was 7 days (IQR: 4 12). Total in-hospital mortality rate was 13.2%. The median out-of-pocket hospital charge was GH₵ 2244 (range: GH₵ 292-GH₵ 41 730).

CONCLUSION: Temporal delays were noted in the provision of care for TBI patients. System-wide interventions aimed at optimizing emergency response and surgical infrastructures will improve access to timely and quality treatment.

articles.title: Limited predictive value of second-to-third trimester complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of obstetrics & gynecology and reproductive biology: X
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the discriminatory performance of seven complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices for preeclampsia (PE) and their incremental value beyond a primary maternal clinical comparator.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies with routine CBC testing between 26.0 and 36.9 weeks of gestation at a tertiary hospital in Thailand. Pregnancies with PE or eclampsia were compared with normotensive pregnancies. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis and logistic regression. Incremental value beyond a model comprising maternal age, body mass index, gestational age at CBC measurement, primigravidity, and pregestational diabetes was evaluated, with false discovery rate correction for multiple testing.

RESULTS: Among 8982 pregnancies, 276 (3.1%) were complicated by PE or eclampsia. CBC testing occurred at a median gestational age of 32.1 weeks. Individual indices showed limited discrimination, with AUCs ranging from 0.438 to 0.513 in the primary direction. NLR, MLR, and SIRI were lower among pregnancies with PE. After adjustment, SIRI reached nominal statistical significance, while NLR and MLR showed similar inverse estimates; none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. The primary maternal clinical comparator had an AUC of 0.723. Adding any individual index increased the AUC by no more than 0.0037 and provided minimal incremental net benefit.

CONCLUSIONS: CBC-derived inflammatory indices showed limited standalone discrimination for PE and negligible incremental value beyond the primary maternal clinical comparator. These findings do not support their use as standalone or incremental markers of PE risk at this gestational window.

articles.title: Clone-censor weighting and dementia risk after statin initiation in diabetes: when the analytic population is no longer the observed population-authors' reply.
Dermal-associated schistosomatoidean eggs exhibit a stronger multinucleated giant cell response than intravascular eggs in fibropapilloma tumors of juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas).
articles.journal: International journal for parasitology. Parasites and wildlife
articles.abstract: Schistosomatoidean trematodes are important parasites of sea turtles, and their eggs can embolize to multiple tissues and induce chronic granulomatous inflammation. Although schistosomatoidean eggs have occasionally been reported within fibropapilloma tumors, the influence of their tissue localization on the associated host response remains poorly understood. We characterized schistosomatoidean eggs and associated histopathological changes in fibropapillomas of juvenile green sea turtles (Chelonia mydas) from Guanabara Bay, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and investigated whether inflammatory responses differed between dermal-associated and intravascular eggs. Forty-nine turtles were captured during health monitoring, of which 30 (61.2%) had external fibropapillomas. Histopathological examination was performed on 42 tumor sections from 27 turtles. Schistosomatoidean eggs were detected in 28 sections (66.7%), representing 18 turtles, with 142 eggs identified. Based on histomorphological criteria complemented by von Willebrand factor immunohistochemistry, 87 eggs (61.3%) were classified as dermal-associated and 55 (38.7%) as intravascular. Eggs were frequently accompanied by epithelioid macrophages, lymphocytes, heterophils, Langhans-type multinucleated giant cells, fibroplasia, and disorganized collagen deposition. Generalized linear mixed models accounting for repeated observations within turtles showed that dermal-associated eggs had significantly greater odds of association with multinucleated giant cells than intravascular eggs (OR = 5.41, 95% CI: 2.46-11.90; p < 0.001). Egg localization was not significantly associated with fibrosis or pyogranulomatous inflammation. These findings demonstrate that schistosomatoidean eggs are frequent within fibropapilloma tissues in this population and indicate that their localization within the tumor influences specific components of the local host inflammatory response.

articles.title: Rising Atrial Fibrillation Mortality Trends in Hypertensive Patients Aged 25 and Older: A CDC Wonder Database Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading arrhythmia contributing to cardiovascular mortality, particularly among individuals with Hypertension (HTN), yet long-term trends and disparities remain underexplored. We analyzed national patterns and sociodemographic differences in AF-related mortality among US adults aged 25 years or older from 1999 to 2023.

METHODS: We used CDC WONDER mortality data (1999-2023) to analyze AF-related deaths among US adults aged ≥ 25 with HTN. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100 000 and average annual percent changes (AAPC) were calculated using Joinpoint regression to assess overall and subgroup-specific trends.

RESULTS: AF accounted for 1 108 265 deaths among adults with HTN, with AAMRs increasing from 3.8 in 1999 to 35.9 in 2023 (AAPC: 6.03%). The sharpest rise occurred from 2018 to 2021, with an APC of 14.57%, coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. Men had higher AAMRs than women (20.5 vs. 17.1). Racial disparities were evident, with non-Hispanic Whites having the highest AAMR (20.1), followed by non-Hispanic Blacks (15.1), Hispanics (11.3), and non-Hispanic Others (10.7). Regional variation showed that the West had the highest AAMR (20.8), while Vermont recorded the highest state rate (28.7), and Nevada had the lowest (11.4). Rural areas exhibited higher mortality rates than urban areas (17.8 vs. 16.1), with rural AAMRs increasing at a faster rate (AAPC: 10.61%).

CONCLUSION: The rising burden of AF-related mortality in hypertensive patients, especially among men, non-Hispanic Whites, and rural populations, signals a critical public health concern. Immediate, equity-focused interventions are needed to mitigate disparities and reduce AF-related mortality across the United States.

articles.title: Characterization of human cationic peptide LL-37 activity against multidrug-resistant Enterococcus faecium in the context of bacteriophage-daptomycin-ampicillin combinations.
articles.abstract:
SYNOPSIS: Host defence peptide cathelicidin LL-37 has been shown to synergize with antibiotics in vitro. However, this synergy has not been explored in combination with bacteriophage (phage).

METHODS: We investigated the impact of bacteriophage plus daptomycin (DAP), ampicillin (AMP), or LL-37 against two multi-drug resistant (MDR) Enterococcus faecium isolates: DAP-susceptible dose-dependent HOU503 and DAP-resistant (DAP-R) R497. Assessments included bacterial survival analysis assays (2 and 4 h), 24 h growth suppression kinetics and time-kill analyses (TKAs).

RESULTS: In survival assays, R497 and HOU503 showed significantly greater killing at 4 h versus 2 h (R497: P = 0.0019; HOU503: P = 0.0029) in all regimens containing phage versus antibiotics alone. Against DAP-R R497, LL-37 enhanced phage activity in growth suppression assays, where it significantly reduced lag time compared to phage alone (P < 0.001). Likewise, in TKAs, phage combined with DAP + AMP + LL-37 yielded greater bacterial reduction over 24 h than antibiotics alone (P < 0.0001). LL-37 + phage regimen also outperformed LL-37 monotherapy (P < 0.0001). Against HOU503, the AMP + DAP + phage regimen demonstrated the most substantial bacterial reduction in 24 h TKAs. LL-37 modestly improved some combinations, especially with phage alone.

CONCLUSIONS: LL-37 enhances the rapidity of phage bactericidal activity in the presence of antibiotic regimens, particularly within the first hours of exposure and most notably against R497. Our data support the efficacy of selected combinations against two MDR E. faecium isolates at crucial early stages of infection. These results highlight the need for experimental designs and clinical strategies that optimize and explore the impact of endogenous and exogenous anti-infective synergies in relevant timeframes and contexts.

articles.title: Identification and dissection of the thousand-grain weight gene TaPTC52 and its distal functional variant in wheat.
articles.journal: Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement
articles.abstract: Thousand-grain weight (TGW) is a primary determinant of grain yield in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) and exhibits high broad-sense heritability, making it a critical target for genetic improvement. In this study, we evaluated TGW in a panel of 120 modern bread wheat cultivars across two consecutive growing seasons, and conducted whole-genome resequencing aligned to the gap-free Chinese Spring telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome. Quality filtering yielded 6,313,343 high-confidence, independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Integrating genome-wide association studies (GWAS) across three mixed linear models with selective sweep scans based on population differentiation statistics (Fst), nucleotide diversity ratios (Pi), and cross-population composite likelihood ratio (XP-CLR) tests mapped a major candidate gene, TaPTC52, within a 646.3 to 646.8 Mb interval on chromosome 5A. This gene encodes protochlorophyllide-dependent translocon component 52. We also detected a putative minor candidate gene encoding a sesquiterpene synthase on chromosome arm 2AS. Haplotype analysis revealed that a regulatory SNP at Chr5A: 646,781,924 bp, located 24.4 kb upstream of the TaPTC52 transcription start site, underlies the divergence between the favorable Hap1 and the alternative Hap2. Accessions carrying Hap1 with the T allele produced significantly higher TGW than those carrying Hap2 with the C allele (P < 0.0001). In silico analyses revealed that the T-to-C transition in Hap2 disrupts a canonical W-box cis-regulatory element and abolishes predicted binding affinity for WRKY transcription factors. Crucially, quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) confirmed that accessions harboring Hap1 exhibited significantly elevated TaPTC52 transcript levels compared with Hap2 (P < 0.0001), which positively correlated with TGW. Pedigree tracking revealed that Hap1 reached a frequency approaching 90% in modern elite lines derived from founder parents Zhoumai 16 and Zhoumai 22 through strong positive selection, whereas Hap2 was predominantly retained in direct lineages of Bainong Aikang 58. Together, these findings provide novel insights into the genetic and transcriptional regulation of TaPTC52 in governing grain weight and provide diagnostic functional markers for marker-assisted selection (MAS) and targeted parental selection in wheat breeding programs.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk factors and awareness among adults attending an opportunistic community screening event in Réunion Island.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe cardiovascular risk factors and their awareness among adults attending a community screening event in Réunion Island, a French overseas department with a high cardiometabolic burden.

METHODS: On May 26, 2026, free voluntary screening was offered to adults on the Saint-Pierre seafront, Réunion Island, France. Cardiovascular history, risk factors, treatments, and awareness of cardiovascular risk factors were self-reported through brief verbal questions. Blood pressure, capillary glucose, and lipids (point-of-care analyzer) were measured.
