Hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia were defined by previous diagnosis, current treatment, or predefined screening thresholds.

RESULTS: Forty-one adults were screened (median age, 54.0 years [interquartile range, 40.0-70.0]; 59% men). Five (12%) had a history of cardiovascular disease, and 23 (56%) reported being unaware of cardiovascular risk factors. Hypertension and dyslipidemia were each identified in 18 participants (44%; 95% CI 30, 59) and diabetes in 9 (22%; 95% CI 12, 37). Blood pressure was controlled in five of nine (56%) treated participants.

CONCLUSIONS: Participants had a high burden of cardiovascular risk factors and limited awareness of them. Although based on a small, self-selected sample, these findings are consistent with the known cardiometabolic burden of Réunion Island and support community screening and education to complement routine prevention.

articles.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors for Recurrence of Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps After Endoscopic Sinus Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is a persistent inflammatory condition of the sinonasal mucosa. Endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) is used for refractory cases, but postoperative recurrence remains common. This study determined the pooled recurrence rate after ESS and assessed the impact of asthma, allergy, and aspirin intolerance on recurrence.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were conducted until February 2025, following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. Observational studies reporting postoperative recurrence and/or risk-factor data in CRSwNP patients undergoing ESS were included. Random-effects models estimated pooled recurrence rates and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using I 2, publication bias using Doi plots, and robustness using sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Of 1665 records, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled postoperative recurrence rate was 30.60% (95% CI, 23.82%-38.33%; I 2 = 95%). Recurrence was 29.59% (95% CI, 21.14%-39.72%) at ≤ 12 months, 26.38% (17.34%-37.97%) at 13-36 months, 54.07% (0.34%-99.76%) at 37-72 months, and 42.16% (13.06%-77.95%) at > 72 months. Asthma was significantly associated with recurrence (RR = 2.01, 95% CI, 1.26-3.20), as was aspirin intolerance (RR = 1.74, 95% CI, 1.19-2.54), whereas allergy was not (RR = 1.15, 95% CI, 0.80-1.63). Sensitivity analyses confirmed stability. LFK indices were 0.84 for recurrence and -1.00 for risk-factor analyses, indicating no major asymmetry.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative CRSwNP recurrence after ESS remains substantial. Asthma and aspirin intolerance were significant prognostic factors, whereas allergy was not. Standardized recurrence definitions and consistent reporting of surgical extent, postoperative therapy, inflammatory phenotype, and long-term outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Dissection healing process after drug-coated balloon treatment for de novo coronary lesions assessed with early optical coherence tomography follow-up.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) are currently used for de novo coronary artery lesions. However, the natural course of the dissection after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) at an early stage remains unclear.

AIMS: We sought to examine post-PCI dissection healing in de novo coronary lesions treated with DCBs by serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging.

METHODS: Of 94 de novo coronary lesions treated with DCB, OCT imaging at the pre-, post-PCI, and early follow-up period (< 12 months) were performed, and morphological findings, including residual dissection, were assessed.

RESULTS: The median follow-up period was 231 (interquartile range, 112-314) days (< 3 months; 16 lesions [17.0%], 3-6 months; 23 lesions [24.5%]), and 84.0% of post-PCI dissection was not observed at follow-up. In persistent dissection lesions, more diabetes patients (66.7% vs. 29.1%, P = 0.008), more dual antiplatelet therapy continuation at follow-up (80.0% vs. 46.8%, P = 0.024), and shorter follow-up duration (median 44 days vs 258 days, P < 0.001) were found than in non-persistent dissection lesions. Residual dissection was significantly more common in lesions <3 months post-follow-up, compared to those with 3-6 months and 6-12 months (68.8% vs 8.7% vs 3.6%, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The present study suggests that residual dissection was substantially less frequent beyond 3 months, suggesting progressive healing during the first several months after DCB treatment.

articles.title: Rapidly enlarging pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma with discordant multimodality treatment response.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma (ACC) is a rare malignant epithelial tumor whose imaging appearance can overlap with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and other solid pancreatic neoplasms. We report a man in his 50's with a pancreatic head mass causing biliary and pancreatic ductal obstruction. A noncontrast computed tomography (CT) performed approximately 10 months earlier, retrospectively reviewed, showed a small pancreatic head lesion without secondary signs of malignancy, which subsequently enlarged to approximately 8 cm. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a large expansile heterogeneous mass with prominent enhancement and extensive central necrosis, initially raising concern for PDAC but prompting consideration of ACC, which was confirmed by endoscopic biopsy with immunohistochemistry. Surgical resection was initially considered, but the patient repeatedly declined surgery, and systemic chemotherapy was given after biliary decompression. Follow-up CT showed near-complete morphological resolution of the mass, whereas FDG-PET/CT showed persistent focal uptake (SUVmax 6.2) and MRI showed a residual diffusion-restricting lesion. The patient was subsequently persuaded to proceed to surgery and underwent a Whipple procedure; histopathology confirmed residual acinar cell carcinoma with clear margins and no nodal metastases, indicating that the CT response had underestimated persistent disease. This case highlights the value of reviewing prior imaging for interval growth, recognizing atypical imaging features of a pancreatic head mass, and integrating CT, PET/CT, magnetic resonance imaging and, when feasible, pathological confirmation when assessing treatment response.

articles.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Predicting Risk Factors for Chronic Postsurgical Pain After Cesarean Delivery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) after cesarean delivery can severely impair the mother's quality of life and her ability to care for the infant. The aim of this study was to develop and validate a high-performance, interpretable, machine learning-based prediction model to identify high-risk factors for chronic incisional pain at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively and chronic non-incisional pain at 12 months postoperatively. A total of 678 patients who underwent elective cesarean delivery at our hospital were included in the prospective study. A total of 38 preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative variables, including demographic characteristics, psychological scale scores, and anesthesia/analgesia regimens, were collected. We combined the Boruta algorithm, recursive feature elimination, and the Mantel test for feature selection and constructed a high-performance machine learning-based prediction model (MLPM-CPSP-CD). The incidence of chronic incisional pain at 3, 6, and 12 months postoperatively was 12.39%, 9.73%, and 7.96%, respectively, whereas the incidence of chronic non-incisional pain was 24.04%. The MLPM-CPSP-CD model demonstrated excellent predictive performance. The core high-risk factors for postoperative chronic incisional pain were SQ-6 (history of dysmenorrhea), SH-5 (patient-controlled analgesia [PCA] pump pressing frequency), and SH-6 (PCA opioid consumption). This study provides an important foundation for developing and optimizing perioperative pain management strategies.

articles.title: Bullous Pemphigoid Following Total Hip Arthroplasty With Subsequent Prosthetic Joint Infection: Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is an autoimmune blistering disorder potentially triggered by surgery or perioperative medications. An 88-year-old man underwent uncomplicated anterior total hip arthroplasty for femoral neck fracture. Five weeks later, pruritic tense bullae appeared around the operative site. Histology demonstrated subepidermal blistering with eosinophils; direct immunofluorescence revealed linear basement-membrane IgG and C3, confirming BP. Immunosuppression was initiated. Five weeks thereafter, fever, erythema, tenderness, and effusion developed. Purulent aspirate grew Staphylococcus aureus, confirming prosthetic joint infection. Despite urgent debridement and intravenous antibiotics, persistent infection required explantation and antibiotic spacer placement three weeks later. After clinical improvement over three months, planned second-stage reimplantation was completed without BP recurrence. To our knowledge, this first reported complication highlights prompt dermatologic diagnosis, judicious immunosuppression, and multidisciplinary management following arthroplasty.

articles.title: Practice patterns of midazolam administration in patients undergoing cardiac-related non-operating room procedures: analysis of a US anaesthesia database.
authors: Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group Perioperative Clinical Research Committee
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Midazolam can be administered as an anxiolytic, a cardio-stable sedative, or an anaesthetic agent during non-operating room anaesthesia (NORA) procedures. Guidelines suggest avoidance in older or frail patients, and current practices are unknown. We hypothesised that there would be significant variation in midazolam administration for cardiac-related NORA procedures by attending and institutional characteristics, in addition to patient characteristics.

METHODS: This is a retrospective observational analysis of a multi-institution US-centric electronic health record dataset including all adult patients undergoing cardiac-related NORA procedures in the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group database from 2015 to 2022. The primary aim of the study was to identify the proportion of total variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient-, attending-, and institutional-level factors. The secondary aim was to identify practice pattern variations in the dosage and timing of midazolam administration. The primary outcome was any midazolam administration ≤1 h before anaesthesia start to 1 h after anaesthesia end. Secondary outcomes included total dose and timing of midazolam administration. Variance in midazolam administration attributable to patient, attending, and institutional factors was calculated with intraclass correlation coefficients following multilevel mixed-effects generalised linear models, in which a three-level nesting structure was assumed: patients nested within attendings and attendings nested within institutions. For the primary outcome, a binomial distribution and logit link function was specified. For the secondary outcome of total midazolam, the same three-level nesting structure was used, and covariates were modelled using a multilevel mixed-effects model specifying a Gaussian distribution and identity link function.

RESULTS: A total of 246 918 cardiac-related NORA procedures with care provided by 5212 unique anaesthesia attendings across 63 institutions with a median case volume of 9 (inter-quartile range [IQR] 2-37) were included in the analysis. Midazolam was administered in 33.0% of patients (n=81 602), including 25.5% of patients aged ≥65 yr (n=40 469). Midazolam administration declined from 50.7% of patients in 2015 to 29.0% in 2022 (P<0.001). The median dose was 2 mg (IQR 2-2), with 89.9% administered before procedure start. For transoesophageal echocardiography procedures, it was estimated that 37.0% of midazolam administration (30.4-44.3) was attributable to attending variation and 26.4% (19.2-35.2) to the institution, assuming that 36.6% of the variation was attributable to known patient factors. For transcatheter/endovascular procedures, attending, institution, and patient factors accounted for 45.7% (39.0-52.6), 27.7% (19.7-37.4), and 26.6%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Although patient-level factors accounted for a meaningful proportion of variability, substantial variation in midazolam administration was also attributable to attending- and institution-level factors. Further studies on clinical outcomes and patient experience associated with this type of midazolam administration have the potential to inform future practice.

articles.title: Statement of Retraction: The macrophage-associated microRNA-4715-3p/Gasdermin D axis potentially indicates fibrosis progression in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: evidence from transcriptome and biological data.
Statement of Retraction: Significant role of long non-coding RNA MALAT1 in deep vein thrombosis via the regulation of vascular endothelial cell physiology through the microRNA-383-5p/BCL2L11 axis.
Statement of Retraction: Different responses of cervical intervertebral disc caused by low and high virulence bacterial infection: a comparative study in rats.
DNA methylation signatures from tissue and cell-free DNA in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency mirror clinical pathologies providing a potential non-invasive tool to monitor liver disease progression.
articles.abstract: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is a serpinopathy in which mutations in the SERPINA1 gene cause misfolding of alpha-1 antitrypsin (Z-AAT), leading to hepatic protein accumulation, proteotoxic stress, inflammation, fibrosis, and an increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma. Despite a uniform genetic mutation in most affected individuals, liver disease severity varies, reflecting contributions from environmental exposures and epigenetic heterogeneity (e.g. DNA methylation). As RNA-interference therapy has emerged as a promising treatment, understanding how epigenetic variation relates to the clinical and histopathologic features of AATD may provide insight into disease heterogeneity, progression, and therapeutic response. We analyzed a longitudinal cohort of ZZ-genotype AATD patients with paired liver biopsies, plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and clinical data collected at baseline and 3-y follow-up. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of liver tissue identified 15 CpG clusters associated with liver disease severity, immune pathways, and clinical measures including METAVIR fibrosis score and γ-glutamyltransferase. Parallel methylation profiling of matched plasma-derived cfDNA identified eight analogous CpG clusters enriched for similar biological pathways and associated with clinical parameters. Integration of tissue and cfDNA datasets revealed fifty-one shared CpGs representing disease-associated methylation signatures, including loci such as ZFP57 that tracks with portal inflammation. We also identified a DNA methylation signature associated with fibrosis progression based on changes in METAVIR score. These findings demonstrate that liver- and cfDNA-derived DNA methylation signatures robustly stratify AATD patients by relevant measures of liver injury and fibrosis, supporting their potential as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, and monitoring responses to emerging therapies.

articles.title: Cross-protective immune responses to pneumococcal serotype 6A following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: India bears a pneumococcal disease burden, with serogroup 6 contributing to invasive pneumococcal disease, acute otitis media, and nasopharyngeal carriage. Serotype 6B is included in several pneumococcal conjugate vaccines, with evidence suggesting cross-protection against serotype 6A. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated serotype 6A-specific immune responses following vaccination with 6B-containing pneumococcal conjugate vaccines. Databases were searched for studies reporting IgG geometric mean concentrations, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL, and opsonophagocytic activity titers. Forty-three studies met inclusion criteria; eight contributed quantitative data. Overall, 6B-containing vaccines elicited measurable cross-reactive IgG and functional responses against serotype 6A. Booster-containing 3 + 1 schedules showed numerically higher responses than 3 + 0 schedules, with pooled IgG GMCs of 1.63 vs. 0.59 µg/mL, proportions achieving IgG ≥ 0.35 µg/mL of 92.78% vs. 65.38%, and OPA GMTs of 984.6 vs. 169.2, respectively. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251134118). These findings support 6B-mediated cross-reactive immunogenicity, particularly following booster dosing in vaccinated children.

articles.title: Luteoloside from Crataegus pinnatifida Bunge alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis by restoring mitochondrial homeostasis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a progressive liver disease driven by lipid overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and inflammation, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain limited. The leaves of Crataegus pinnatifida Bunge (Hawthorn) have long been used for metabolic disorders, but its principal anti-MASH constituent and underlying mechanism remain unclear.

METHODS: A flavonoid-rich hawthorn leaf extract (HLE) was optimally prepared and initially evaluated in free fatty acid-induced HepG2 cells. Integrated transcriptomic and network pharmacology analyses were performed to prioritize candidate targets and signaling pathways. Phytochemical profiling, affinity ultrafiltration screening, and molecular docking were used to identify the principal bioactive constituent of HLE. The efficacy and mechanism of the identified compound were further validated in FFA-induced cells and high-fat/high-cholesterol-fed rats.

RESULTS: Flavonoid-rich HLE markedly attenuated free fatty acid-induced lipotoxicity, as evidenced by reduced lipid accumulation, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cytokine expression. Integrated transcriptomic and network analyses prioritized the AMP-activated catalytic subunit alpha 1 (PRKAA1)/AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) axis as a central target. Among compounds identified in HLE, the flavone glucoside luteoloside emerged as the leading AMPKα-targeting candidate based on affinity ultrafiltration and molecular docking analyses. In vitro and in vivo, luteoloside alleviated metabolic dysfunction, hepatic steatosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and steatohepatitic injury. Mechanistically, luteoloside restored AMPKα phosphorylation and promoted peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α)-dependent mitochondrial reprogramming, accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid β-oxidation, and antioxidant defense. Importantly, PRKAA1 silencing markedly blunted these protective effects, establishing AMPKα as a required mediator. Integrated hepatic transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses further supported AMPK-driven mitochondrial reprogramming as a core mechanism underlying luteoloside action.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the flavone glucoside luteoloside as a principal anti-MASH component from hawthorn leaf and demonstrates that its therapeutic effects are mediated through AMPKα-dependent restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis. By activating the AMPKα-PGC-1α axis, luteoloside improves mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative metabolism, and redox balance, thereby alleviating lipotoxicity and steatohepatitic injury. These findings provide both a chemical basis and a mechanistic rationale for the development of hawthorn leaf-derived interventions for MASH.

articles.title: Serious illness care for patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure: A care model and research agenda.
articles.abstract: Patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) often require intensive care and face high mortality. The incidence of ACLF is rising, and the patient population has shifted toward a more medically and psychosocially complex cohort. Despite this, patient-centered communication practices, strategies, and frameworks to provide serious illness care have not yet been developed for patients with ACLF. Only 15%-25% of patients with ACLF ultimately undergo liver transplantation, yet serious illness care has focused predominantly on transplant outcomes, leaving most patients without a model that reflects their clinical course. While national guidelines recommend early engagement in palliative care, palliative care capacity is limited by rotating, multidisciplinary teams without longitudinal accountability. We propose a serious illness care model for patients with ACLF that maps expected clinical trajectories from stabilization through transplant evaluation and potential transplant windows. This model identifies several "checkpoints" that present opportunities for serious illness conversations during which the possibility of death or decline can be discussed alongside the possibility of transplant or recovery. Structured conversations about serious illness at each checkpoint may improve prognostic alignment and communication across multidisciplinary teams and with patients and families. We provide examples of how serious illness conversation frameworks can be adapted for each of these checkpoint conversations. Existing serious illness care frameworks do not account for the unique clinical trajectory and complex physiological and psychosocial challenges experienced by patients with ACLF. We thus propose a structured research agenda to improve serious illness care for this population, addressing priority domains of prognostic uncertainty, liver transplant complexity, and psychosocial challenges.

articles.title: Apixaban reduces hepatic decompensation in patients with cirrhosis (ApiHep): A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evolving data suggest that anticoagulation is safe in cirrhosis and may improve decompensation-free survival in select patients. This study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of the direct oral anticoagulant apixaban in patients with cirrhosis.

METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial with blinded endpoint assessment, adult patients (18-60y) with cirrhosis (Child-Pugh B7-C10) without splenoportal axis thrombosis were randomized (1:1) to receive apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) along with standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone for 12 months. The primary outcome was the comparison of the proportion of patients with hepatic decompensation at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included frequency of liver-related events, overall and liver-related mortality, and adverse events (AEs).

RESULTS: One hundred thirty-four patients (mean age 43.4±9.5 y; Child-Pugh B/C:115/19) were randomized (67 Apixaban+SMT and 67 SMT). Patients receiving apixaban experienced significantly lower rates of hepatic decompensation compared with SMT (33.1% vs. 54.3%; absolute risk reduction 21.2% [95% CI: 4.5%-38.2%]; p=0.013). Although rates of ascites (6.4% vs. 17.4%), HE (21.2% vs. 36.0%), and variceal bleeding (7.5% vs. 14.6%) were lower among patients receiving Apixaban+SMT as compared with SMT alone, the differences were not statistically significant. No significant between-group differences in all-cause and liver-related mortality at 1 year were noted. There were no significant between-group differences in AEs (55.2% vs. 53.7%), any bleeding (41.8% vs. 46.3%), and major bleeding (9.0% vs. 11.9%) events.

CONCLUSIONS: Apixaban significantly reduced hepatic decompensation events without increasing hemorrhagic episodes in Child-Pugh B7-C10 cirrhosis (CTRI/2023/09/058018).

articles.title: Muscle strength and physical activity are independent determinants of quality of life in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality of life (QoL) impairment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is often attributed to liver disease severity and metabolic comorbidities; however, the impact of muscle strength and physical activity remains uncertain. This study aims to examine associations between hepatic, metabolic, and functional factors and QoL in patients with MASLD.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included adults with MASLD evaluated between 2014 and 2026. QoL was measured using the 36‑Item Short Form Health Survey (SF‑36) physical and mental component summary scores. Muscle strength was assessed using handgrip strength and the 5-times sit-to-stand test. Physical activity was evaluated using IPAQ-SF. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was performed using elastography. Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney test, and multivariable linear regression was used to examine associations with physical and mental QoL scores, adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status.

RESULTS: Among 215 participants (56% male; mean age 55.4±15.2 y), LSM ≥8 kPa (51%), diabetes (65%), obesity (72%), physical inactivity (35%), and low muscle strength (29%) were common. Lower physical QoL scores were observed in individuals with diabetes, obesity, low muscle strength, and physical inactivity. Lower mental QoL scores were observed in individuals with low muscle strength and physical inactivity. In the adjusted models, higher BMI (β=-0.41; p<0.001), diabetes (β=-3.14; p=0.036), low muscle strength (β=-5.00; p=0.003), and physical inactivity (β=-4.74; p=0.003) were independently associated with lower physical QoL. Low strength was also independently associated with lower mental QoL (β=-6.62; p=0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Although fibrosis and metabolic traits remain central therapeutic targets in MASLD, reduced muscle strength and physical inactivity are independently associated with reduced QoL, underscoring the importance of routine functional assessments and holistic management strategies in patient-centered care.

articles.title: Alcohol abstinence and liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality, and abstinence is fundamental for treatment. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) is commonly used to assess hepatic fibrosis and inflammation. While studies suggest LSM decreases after alcohol cessation, the magnitude and timing of these changes are poorly understood. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated liver stiffness changes after alcohol cessation.

METHODS: Medline, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were searched from 1996 to 2024 for paired VCTE assessments in adults who underwent alcohol cessation and reported abstinence or relapse. Absolute mean kPa changes were back-transformed estimates from pooled effect sizes and standard deviations. ROBINS-I assessed risk of bias.

RESULTS: A total of 6620 articles were reviewed; 75 underwent full-text review, and 11 studies involving 1557 patients were included. In abstinent patients, a mean absolute LSM change was identified to be -1.95 kPa at 7 days, -2.30 kPa at 30 days, and -2.76 kPa after 56 days. The pooled standardized effect size was -0.13 SD units (95% CI -0.20 to -0.07). LSM reduction was significant within 7 days of abstinence (-0.21 SD units; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.05) but not at later follow-up (-0.11 SD units; 95% CI -0.24 to 0.03). In relapse patients, mean absolute LSM change was +0.86 kPa at 30 days and +0.40 kPa after 56 days; pooled standardized effect size was +0.18 SD units (95% CI +0.02 to +0.33).

CONCLUSIONS: VCTE detected short-term, directionally opposite LSM changes with alcohol cessation or relapse. These changes are consistent with alcohol-associated inflammatory liver injury, while its correlation with histologic fibrosis is uncertain, necessitating further evaluation with paired VCTE and histology during abstinence.

articles.title: Immunosuppressive monocytes promote infection in patients with alcohol-associated hepatitis.
authors: and the TREAT investigators, AlcHepNet investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Broad immune cell dysfunction known as immune paralysis is a hallmark of severe alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). This process may drive susceptibility to infection and contribute to high short-term mortality in these patients. However, the mechanisms of immune paralysis are incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to elucidate the role of myeloid cells in immune dysfunction in severe AH to identify potential biomarkers of infection risk and therapeutic targets.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed the peripheral immune compartment of AH patients, heavy drinkers, and healthy controls and discovered that AH patients at risk for infection had an expanded peripheral monocyte population that was CXCR5+CCR4+ (C-X-C chemokine receptor type 5, C-C chemokine receptor type 4) and had lower activity of pro-inflammatory pathways (eg, Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha, TNF-α, and Interleukin-1 beta, IL-1β) compared with controls. The frequency of circulating CXCR5+CCR4+ monocytes in AH patients negatively correlated with 12-month transplant-free survival. Ex vivo CXCR5+ AH monocytes had reduced phagocytic activity, and they suppressed T-cell proliferation compared with CXCR5- and healthy control monocytes. CXCR5+ AH monocytes expressed PD-L1 (Programmed Death Ligand 1), which is a costimulatory molecule known to inhibit T-cell activation, and TMEM176B (Tolerance-Related and Induced, TORID-1), which is an intracellular cation channel that regulates calcium flux. Inhibition of TORID-1 promoted human monocyte phagocytosis and IL-1β release.

CONCLUSIONS: CXCR5+CCR4+ monocytes arise in patients with severe AH and have impaired phagocytosis, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and suppress T-cell proliferation. These cells may promote susceptibility to bacterial infection and predict outcomes in severe AH. These may represent novel therapeutic targets to alleviate immune dysfunction in severe AH.

articles.title: Longitudinal changes in a blood-based prognostic liver secretome signature and long-term hepatocellular carcinoma risk in cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in patients with cirrhosis can be predicted by cross-sectional assessment of biomarkers and/or clinical scores, including the Prognostic Liver Secretome signature (PLSec)-based PAaM score. However, HCC risk may change over time, potentially limiting the accuracy of cross-sectional risk prediction. We aimed to evaluate whether longitudinal changes in HCC risk biomarkers/scores improve upon one-time risk assessment.

APPROACH AND RESULTS: In this nested case-control study within the multi-center prospective National Cancer Institute HCC Early Detection Strategy (HEDS) cohort of patients with cirrhosis, we evaluated longitudinal changes in PLSec over 1 or 2 years. Paired baseline and follow-up serum samples were available for 31 cases and 93 controls for 1-year changes, and for 25 cases and 75 controls for 2-year changes. Cross-sectional PLSec scores were higher in cases than in controls at baseline, Year 1, and Year 2 (p<0.05). The 2-year change in PLSec score (delta-PLSec-Y2) was higher in cases than in controls (p=0.026; AUROC, 0.65; adjusted odds ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.15]). In multivariable logistic regression, delta-PLSec-Y2 remained significantly associated with HCC risk (p=0.041) along with baseline PAaM.

CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal assessment of PLSec at a 2-year interval may provide additional information to refine cross-sectional HCC risk assessment, warranting further independent validation, evaluation of longer intervals, and exploration of optimal re-testing frequency.

articles.title: Mortality due to sepsis is increasing among patients with cirrhosis compared with other chronic diseases: US trends, 1999-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major contributor to death across chronic diseases, but population-level trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis relative to other chronic conditions remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated US national trends in sepsis-associated mortality among decedents with cirrhosis, congestive heart failure (CHF), and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

METHODS: We analyzed the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause-of-Death database (1999-2024) to identify decedents with cirrhosis, CHF, or COPD, and sepsis as a contributing cause of death. Age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality rates per 100,000 US population were calculated, and Joinpoint regression estimated average annual percent change (AAPC). Prespecified analyses evaluated trends by age, sex, race, liver disease etiology, and infection source.Results:Sepsis-related mortality increased most rapidly in decedents with cirrhosis, with an AAPC more than 4-fold higher than CHF [AAPC 3.29% (95% CI 2.96-3.54) vs. 0.78% (95% CI 0.34-1.21)], while COPD showed no significant increase [AAPC -0.12% (95% CI -0.62 to 0.23)]. Among decedents with cirrhosis, mortality increased across demographics, particularly among American Indian/Alaska Native individuals, White individuals, females, and adults aged ≥65 years. Source-specific increases in cirrhosis were greatest for genitourinary infections, followed by pneumonia and intra-abdominal infections. By cirrhosis etiology, the steepest increases occurred in MASLD [AAPC 11.36% (95% CI 9.46-13.30)], followed by alcohol-associated liver disease [AAPC 5.04% (95% CI 4.45-5.61)].

CONCLUSIONS: At the population level, average age-adjusted sepsis-related mortality increased substantially faster in decedents with cirrhosis than in CHF and COPD, with the greatest increases observed in decedents with MASLD and alcohol-associated liver disease. As the epidemiology of chronic liver disease shifts, cirrhosis is emerging as a critical target for sepsis prevention, earlier recognition, and disease-specific care pathways aimed at improving survival.

articles.title: Alcohol impairs liver adaptation to high-cholesterol diet, leading to advanced disease development.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) heavily contributes to global alcohol-associated mortality. Alcohol synergizes with other causes of liver disease, such as a Western diet rich in fat, fructose, and cholesterol. However, the role of individual dietary components in ALD development is not fully understood. We aimed to study the role of cholesterol in ALD development.

METHODS: Mice were fed ad libitum with a high-cholesterol diet with 20% EtOH in the drinking water for 10 weeks. To assess the drivers of ALD in males, we performed spatial transcriptomics (Xenium, 10x Genomics).

RESULTS: Compared with a high-cholesterol diet alone, alcohol-treated mice showed elevated serum ALT and AST, increased inflammation, fibrosis, ductular reaction, and reduced HNF4α and albumin production. In female mice, we found that alcohol promoted pro-inflammatory cytokine production and Tgfb1 expression, thus driving liver injury and fibrosis. In males, we observed that fibrosis and liver injury were induced by other mechanisms. We found that the liver adapted to a high-cholesterol diet by increasing cholesterol metabolism in hepatocytes. In contrast, alcohol impaired liver adaptation to a high-cholesterol diet by reducing cholesterol metabolism, HDL production, and hepatic cholesterol secretion, thus driving inflammation and fibrosis. Alcohol-treated mice showed a significant decrease in Apoa1, Abcg8, Cyp7b1, Saa1, and Saa2, and reduced serum HDL-C, SAA, and 27-hydroxycholesterol. Low 27-hydroxycholesterol in patients with cirrhosis is associated with increased MELD scores and poor transplant-free survival. Hepatocyte-specific Kdm5b knockout mice were protected from alcohol effects by restoring cholesterol secretion in part through an upregulation of Abcg8. Accordingly, these mice were protected against alcohol-induced fibrosis development.

CONCLUSION: In summary, alcohol impairs liver adaptation to a high-cholesterol diet. Restoring the adaptation by KDM5B inhibition may be beneficial for patients with ALD.

articles.title: Detection of heme-dependent metronidazole resistance in Clostridioides difficile is associated with the nimB genotype and the testing medium.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although metronidazole is no longer recommended as first-line therapy for Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), its use persists. Heme-dependent metronidazole resistance has recently been linked to the PnimBG promoter mutation. We investigated the occurrence of this determinant in clinical C. difficile isolates and evaluated ready-to-use culture media for detecting metronidazole resistance.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventy-five C. difficile isolates carrying PnimBG and/or nimB coding mutations, together with 10 wild-type isolates, were analysed. Metronidazole susceptibility was determined by E-test on ready-to-use Chocolate agar (CA), Fastidious Anaerobe Agar (FAA), and freshly prepared Brain Heart Infusion agar (BHI) with and without 5 mg/L hemin. Resistance was defined as MIC >2 mg/L.

RESULTS: All isolates were susceptible on BHI without hemin. Isolates carrying PnimBG alone remained susceptible on all media. Heme-dependent resistance was associated with the combined presence of PnimBG and nimB coding mutations but varied by medium. CA and BHI with hemin showed comparable performance, whereas FAA substantially underestimated resistance.

CONCLUSION: Our data show that heme-dependent metronidazole resistance in C. difficile was associated with both the PnimBG promoter mutation and specific nimB coding mutations. Ready-to-use FAA substantially underestimates resistance, and clinical laboratories should consider using ready-to-use CA and freshly prepared BHI with hemin for metronidazole susceptibility testing in C. difficile to avoid false susceptible classification.

articles.title: Collaborative APRN stress testing protocols enhance remote cardiology services.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac stress testing is a noninvasive method of detecting coronary artery disease and other cardiac conditions. In rural settings, continued closures of rural hospitals, limited resources, and distance to specialty services can hinder timely diagnostic evaluation.

OBJECTIVE: To address local rural cardiology care gaps and expand access, the objective was to implement a collaborative advanced practice registered nurse-physician cardiology telemedicine stress testing program at a rural critical access hospital.

METHODS: Risk stratification and procedure workflows were developed to formalize supervision and escalation pathways and are described. Data on stress test volumes, coronary artery disease identification, and cardiac rehab enrollment were collected before and after program implementation.

RESULTS: The total volume of cardiac stress tests increased by 62.9%, from 140 to 228. Angiographic obstructive coronary artery disease identification rates doubled from 2% to 4%. Functional exercise stress test completion prior to cardiac rehabilitation and subsequent follow-up enrollment were similar, and enrollment in cardiac rehabilitation remained high. 'Likelihood to recommend' score for noninvasive cardiology postimplementation was 92.2%.

CONCLUSION: Findings indicated that a collaborative advanced practice registered nurse-physician telemedicine program can enhance access to noninvasive cardiology services in a rural setting, possibly enabling earlier detection of obstructive coronary artery disease. The program maintained high cardiac rehabilitation enrollment rates and patient satisfaction scores. These outcomes and the proposed care models support the viability and benefits of such programs in enhancing rural health care delivery.

articles.title: Diabetic retinopathy: Screening and management.
articles.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a significant cause of vision loss among people with diabetes, emphasizing the need for prompt and comprehensive care. Several challenges can impede optimal outcomes in DR, including limited access to specialist services, barriers to treatment, and inadequate follow-up care. In response, the nurse practitioner can assume a vital role in the management of DR, encompassing multiple responsibilities that span the continuum of care. These essential functions include promoting early detection, effectively managing chronic diseases that are risk factors for DR, facilitating timely referrals to specialists, and educating patients about the progression of the disease and treatment options.

articles.title: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement.
articles.abstract: Policy statements and clinical policies are the official policies of the American College of Emergency Physicians and, as such, are not subject to the same peer review process as articles appearing in the journal. Policy statements and clinical policies of ACEP do not necessarily reflect the policies and beliefs of Annals of Emergency Medicine and its editors.

articles.title: Optimizing IUI: evidence-based guidance for use of add-ons and variations in IUI treatment, a British Fertility Society policy and practice guideline.
articles.abstract: Intrauterine insemination (IUI) is a widely used fertility treatment with numerous add-ons and protocol variations, many of which are offered empirically. This guideline systematically reviews the available evidence to provide evidence-based recommendations for their clinical use, aiming to optimise treatment outcomes, standardise practice and facilitate future research. A total of 25 interventions were evaluated, including follicular monitoring, LH surge detection, catheter type, bladder filling, insemination technique, operator experience, cervical mucus aspiration, endometrial scratching, hydrotubation, ovarian stimulation, ovulation triggering and timing, intrauterine infusions, medications affecting endometrial receptivity or uterine contractility, double insemination, ultrasound guidance, bed rest and luteal phase support. A systematic literature search identified 154 randomised controlled trials involving 34,825 participants. Meta-analyses were conducted where feasible. However, the limited availability of adequately powered trials and the predominantly low-quality evidence restrict the certainty of most recommendations. These limitations should be clearly communicated during patient counselling. Future research should prioritise high-quality trials evaluating the effectiveness of IUI add-ons in specific patient populations, considering underlying infertility diagnoses.

articles.title: All About the Meds: Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-aged Female Transplant Recipients.
authors: American Society of Transplantation Women’s Health Community of Practice, Controversies Conference on Contraception, Infertility, and Immunosuppression in Reproductive-Aged Female Transplant Recipients
articles.abstract: The number of reproductive-aged solid organ transplant recipients continues to rise, underscoring the need for comprehensive reproductive health counseling that spans throughout the transplant continuum. Fertility is often impaired in end-stage organ disease but often resumes within months after transplantation, which may cause unintended pregnancy during a period of heightened maternal, fetal, and allograft vulnerability. This review synthesizes the evidence and expert consensus from the American Society of Transplantation Women's Health Community of Practice Controversies Conference on contraception, infertility, and immunosuppression in reproductive-aged female transplant recipients. Recommendations are largely US-based, although reference to international variability is noted, where relevant. We outline contraceptive options with attention to efficacy and safety in transplant recipients. Data on infertility and assisted reproductive technologies in solid organ transplant recipients remain limited, although emerging evidence supports the feasibility and safety of ovulation induction, in vitro fertilization, and single-embryo transfer with careful monitoring for complications such as ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Immunosuppressive regimens require individualized adjustment before, during, and after pregnancy: calcineurin inhibitors, corticosteroids, and azathioprine are generally considered safe, whereas mycophenolate is strictly contraindicated due to teratogenicity; the safety of mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors and belatacept remains incompletely defined. Lactation is supported with most immunosuppressants, although caution is warranted with mycophenolate and mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitors. Ultimately, preconception counseling, shared decision-making, and coordination amongst transplant, maternal-fetal medicine, and reproductive endocrinology specialists are essential to optimize outcomes for recipients, grafts, and infants. Closing persistent knowledge gaps and enhancing access to reproductive care should remain a research and policy priority in transplant medicine.

articles.title: Epidemiology, Fracture Patterns, and Risk Factors Among Motorcycle Crash Victims Treated at Orthopedic Institute, Tanzania.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Motorcycle crashes are a leading cause of injury and death in low- and middle-income countries, yet detailed data on fracture patterns and severity determinants remain limited in East Africa. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiology, fracture patterns, and associated risk factors among motorcycle crash victims treated at Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute (MOI).

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study included 273 motorcyclists with confirmed fractures treated at MOI between January and December 2024. Data on demographics, crash characteristics, injury patterns, and treatment were extracted from medical records using a structured form. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify predictors of open fractures. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Participants were predominantly male (94.5%) and aged 18-40 years (78.0%). Most were self-employed commercial riders (64.8%) paying out-of-pocket for care (86.8%). High-risk behaviors were common: 45.1% were not wearing helmets, 36.6% had consumed alcohol before riding, and 45.4% of crashes occurred at speeds >80 km/h. Lower limb fractures predominated (62.9%), with tibia/fibula fractures accounting for 39.6% and femur fractures 23.4%. Open fractures represented 43.2% of cases. Crashes clustered during night/early morning and morning peak hours (44.1% each), whereas motorcycle-motorcycle collisions were the commonest crash mechanism (50.9%). On chi-square analysis, speed at impact (p = 0.034) and injury type (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with fracture severity, whereas helmet nonuse showed a nonsignificant trend (p = 0.090). In multivariable logistic regression, lower limb injury was the only independent predictor of open fractures (AOR = 3.42, 95% CI: 1.92-6.09, p < 0.001). Higher riding speeds showed a trend toward increased odds of open fractures but did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (p = 0.059 for the overall speed category variable).

CONCLUSION: Motorcycle crashes in this setting predominantly affect young male riders and frequently result in severe lower limb injuries, with a substantial burden of open fractures requiring resource-intensive surgical care. Lower limb injury was the only independent predictor of open fractures. Speeding, helmet nonuse, and alcohol consumption were highly prevalent modifiable exposures but were not independently associated with open fracture status after adjustment. Drawing on external evidence, strengthening enforcement of speed limits and helmet legislation, implementing workplace-based safety programs for commercial riders, enhancing trauma and orthopedic surgical capacity, and expanding financial protection mechanisms for injured riders are recommended.

articles.title: ORBIT: annotation-aware empirical enrichment and semantic reranking for interpretable functional-class recovery.
articles.abstract: To address the long, redundant result tables produced by standard gene-set enrichment tools, we developed the Ontology-Ranked Biological Interpretation Tool (ORBIT), which combines annotation-aware empirical enrichment, semantic reranking, and representative-term selection to generate compact functional summaries linked to supporting genes. On a curated 45-set internal functional-class benchmark, ORBIT achieved a mean reciprocal rank of 0.913 and top-1 recovery of 0.889. Component ablations identified query-level functional consensus as the strongest individual semantic contributor, while coefficient perturbations showed stable recovery across the tested range. Vocabulary controls showed that internal functional labels contributed to benchmark recovery. A GPCR case study demonstrated redundancy reduction, and applications to PBMC3K, IFNB-stimulated immune cells, and TCGA-BRCA recovered cell-identity, interferon-response, and breast-cancer subtype programs. ORBIT integrates enrichment statistics, functional prioritization, and supporting evidence within a single workflow, enabling users to review concise biological summaries while retaining access to the complete results.

articles.title: A descriptive cohort study of Vitis vinifera fruit (grape/raisin/sultana/currant) ingestion in dogs, reported by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service between 1994 and 2023.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Risk factors such as the type and amount of fresh and dried grapes (collectively called Vitis vinifera fruit [VVF]) ingested in cases of VVF toxicosis are understudied. Therefore, this study aimed to characterise and identify risk factors for VVF ingestion in dogs recorded by the Veterinary Poisons Information Service (VPIS). The VPIS is a UK-based service for poison-related queries from owners and veterinary professionals.

METHODS: VPIS database cases of VVF ingestion were cleaned, filtered and coded. Descriptive analysis and risk factor analysis by multivariable logistic regression were performed. The defined primary outcome was clinical signs. Defined secondary outcomes were clinical signs associated with potential renal damage. It was hypothesised that dried VVF would be more toxic than fresh VVF.

RESULTS: A total of 3150 cases of fresh or dried VVF ingestion were reported to the VPIS; 744 received follow-up. Of veterinary professionals' reported cases with follow-up, 4.6% died. Owner-reported cases had no mortalities. Risk factors significantly associated with possible kidney damage-related clinical sign development included type of VVF (fresh vs. dry), the amount ingested and age of the dog.

LIMITATIONS: The dataset lacked consistent follow-up and temporal data, for example, time from ingestion to VPIS contact, meaning not all risk factors could be explored, and hypotheses generated need further testing.

CONCLUSIONS: In the VPIS dataset of followed-up cases, VVF ingestion was commonly associated with a positive prognosis. There is a suggestion that some risk factors (e.g., VVF type, amount) lead to possible kidney damage.

articles.title: Nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) in COVID-19 patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the efficacy of nebulised interferon-β1a (SNG001) in patients with Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19).

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov, without language restrictions. Studies were searched up to November 2025. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on treatment of COVID-19 with SNG001, compared with placebo or standard of care, were reviewed. Data were analysed using the RevMan Version 5.1 (The Cochrane Collaboration). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes.

RESULTS: Four RCTs (enrolling 1055 participants) met the inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with hospitalisations (data extracted from two RCTs) (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.88), and serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) were significantly fewer in SNG001 groups. There was no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.39), patients non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.17), and adverse event (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.04) between the two groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. SNG001 shows a potential benefit for outpatients with COVID-19, but it requires larger clinical trials for future validations, particularly in vaccinated and previously infected populations.

articles.title: Non-pharmacological augmentation of trauma-focused psychotherapy for PTSD: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trauma-focused psychotherapies (TFPs) effectively treat post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), yet patients show variable response or discontinue treatment. Numerous augmentation strategies have been developed to address these barriers, but the field lacks a framework that extends beyond mechanistic categories as well as a meta-analytic synthesis of their effects.

OBJECTIVE: To develop a classification framework for non-pharmacological augmentation strategies of first-line TFP for PTSD and to meta-analytically evaluate whether these strategies improve treatment outcomes.

METHOD: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TFP augmented with a non-pharmacological intervention versus TFP alone or an active control (i.e. sham intervention or dose increase). Eight databases were searched to July 2026. Augmentation strategies were qualitatively categorised. Primary outcomes were PTSD symptom severity and response rate; dropout was a secondary outcome.

RESULTS: Fifty RCTs met inclusion criteria. Their augmentations were categorised within a three-level framework comprising targets, mechanisms, and implementation forms. Of these, 39 trials (40 comparisons; N = 2,853) were meta-analysed and showed no significant overall effects (symptom severity: g = -0.10, p = .062; response: RR = 1.04, p = .111; dropout: RR = 0.94, p = .489). One subgroup targeting sleep disturbance showed an add-on effect.

CONCLUSIONS: The present findings suggest that augmenting TFP with non-pharmacological interventions does not necessarily lead to incremental efficacy at the overall level, even though small benefits were observed for sleep-focused strategies. Our three-level framework provides a structured approach for conceptualising this heterogeneous field. The absence of a robust overall effect should not be mistaken for evidence that augmentation cannot be effective.

articles.title: Cardiorenal biomarker‑enhanced model for left ventricular hypertrophy in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) acts as a key factor for determinant of adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Echocardiography is the standard method for LVH assessment. Yet asymptomatic LVH patients are often overlooked or missed in routine screening. Whether a biomarker-enhanced model improves detection of prevalent LVH in non-dialysis CKD remains unclear.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 647 non-dialysis patients with CKD. We developed a clinical model based on female, age, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and serum phosphorus. Cardiorenal biomarkers, including urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2), were then added to assess their incremental value. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: LVH was present in 131 patients (20.2%). In multivariable analysis, female, hypertension, serum phosphorus, UACR, and sST2 were independently associated with LVH. NT‑proBNP was associated with LVH in univariable but not multivariable analysis. The clinical model had an AUC of 0.789. Adding three biomarkers improved the AUC to 0.812 (95% CI, 0.769-0.856), with lower Brier score and AIC. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.790 and Brier score of 0.129. Decision curve analysis suggested higher net benefit for the biomarker-enhanced model across most threshold probabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: A biomarker-enhanced model incorporating UACR, NT-proBNP, and sST2, have potential clinical applications to help prioritize echocardiography referrals for asymptomatic CKD patients who may have prevalent LVH.

articles.title: Bioactive constituents from Iris domestica attenuate OGD/R-induced PC12 cell injury by suppressing oxidative stress and mitochondrial apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes neuronal injury involving oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Iris domestica (L.) Goldblatt & Mabb (Iridaceae), known as Shegan in traditional Chinese medicine, has potential neuroprotective properties; however, its structurally defined active constituents remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to isolate secondary metabolites from I. domestica and evaluate their protective effects and potential mechanisms in an OGD/R-induced PC12 cell model.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Secondary metabolites were isolated from I. domestica by chromatographic techniques and identified by 1D/2D NMR, high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HR-ESI-MS), and optical rotation. Neuroprotective activity was evaluated in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-injured PC12 cells. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis-related proteins were further assessed, and network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed.

RESULTS: Four previously undescribed compounds, irisdomeones A-C (1-3) and irisdomeoside F (4), with 21 known compounds (5-25), were isolated. Eleven compounds showed protective effects at 10 μM. Irisdomeone A (1) and belamchinoside D (24) exhibited the strongest activity and were further evaluated at 5 and 10 μM. Both reduced intracellular ROS accumulation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, increased the Bcl-2/Bax ratio, and decreased cleaved caspase-3 expression. Network pharmacology and molecular docking suggested involvement of HIF-1 signaling and mitochondrial apoptosis-related targets.

CONCLUSIONS: Irisdomeone A and belamchinoside D exhibited protective effects against OGD/R-induced PC12 cell injury, associated with reduced oxidative stress, attenuation of mitochondrial dysfunction, and inhibition of apoptosis. These findings identify compounds 1 and 24 as promising cytoprotective constituents in this in vitro model.

articles.title: Concurrent Schistosoma mansoni infection suppresses induction of HIV-1 Env-specific antibodies in a DNA-MVA-gp140 Env vaccine regimen in rhesus macaques.
articles.abstract: Helminth infections have been associated with impaired vaccine immunity. In this study, we assessed the immunogenicity and efficacy of a DNA/MVA/gp140 Env HIV vaccine regimen in rhesus macaques (RMs) and the effect of concurrent Schistosoma mansoni (Sm) infection. The vaccine expressed HIV Env derived from HIV-1 CAP256SU and a mosaic HIV-1 gag gene. Sm-free RMs received sequential DNA, MVA and gp140 Env protein immunizations, while a separate group was infected with Sm prior to receiving the same regimen. Sm-infection was confirmed using parasitological and serological assays. HIV-1 gp140 Env-specific binding antibodies (bAb) and neutralizing antibodies (nAb) against MW965.26, 6644, Consensus C, and CAP256SU pseudoviruses, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were longitudinally evaluated. Both vaccinated Sm-free and Sm-infected RMs developed robust bAb and moderate nAb responses to MW965.26 after MVA immunization, which were maintained following protein boosts. However, these antibody responses were significantly reduced in Sm-infected animals. A subset of animals showed modest nAb activity against 6644 and Consensus C, with no consistently detectable neutralization of CAP256SU. Vaccinated Sm-free RMs developed low to moderate IFN-γ ELISpot responses that increased after MVA boosting. Sm-free vaccinated animals were subsequently challenged intrarectally with SHIV-CAP256SU. Before this, SHIV CAP256 replication was confirmed in intravenously challenged RMs. Seven of eight vaccinated animals became viremic, with peak viral loads comparable to controls. While survival rates did not differ significantly, vaccinated RMs demonstrated a lower hazard risk. Overall, this vaccine regimen elicited functional humoral and cellular immune responses, while concurrent Sm-infection significantly suppressed HIV-1 antibody induction.

articles.title: Association of adverse perinatal outcomes of intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy with maternal serum bile acid profiles.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is associated with increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, yet current monitoring lacks predictive accuracy. This study aimed to explore alterations in serum bile acid profiles and their relationship with adverse perinatal outcomes in ICP.

METHODS: This study enrolled 149 pregnant women, including 77 normal pregnant women and 72 cases with ICP, subdivided into ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes and those without according to the perinatal outcomes. Serum concentrations of 15 bile acids were quantified using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and compared among the three groups.

RESULTS: ICP patients exhibited significantly lower gestational age at delivery, Apgar scores, and birth weight, alongside higher rates of cesarean delivery, low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and preterm birth (all p < 0.05). Twelve bile acids were significantly elevated in ICP (all p < 0.01); notably, taurolithocholic acid elevation was exclusive to the ICP with adverse perinatal outcomes. Glycocholic acid (GCA), glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA), taurocholic acid (TCA), taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA), tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA), and total bile acid levels positively correlated with adverse perinatal outcomes (all p < 0.05). The combined indicator of these six indicators demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for adverse perinatal outcomes with an area under the curve of 0.836, sensitivity of 73.0%, and specificity of 82.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: Distinct serum bile acid metabolic signatures characterize ICP patients with adverse perinatal outcomes. Elevated levels of total bile acids and conjugated bile acids, including GCA, GCDCA, TCA, TCDCA, and TUDCA, were associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and might serve as candidate biomarkers for risk prediction. The multi-bile acid combined indicator demonstrated superior exploratory predictive performance over individual markers, offering a potential tool for identifying high-risk ICP patients, which requires prospective external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: A neonatal prediction model for lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheters depth.
articles.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a robust and generalizable prediction model for PICC depth in neonates undergoing lower-extremity catheterization, with the aim of improving the first-attempt success rate of catheter tip positioning and reducing PICC-related complications.

METHODS: A total of 240 neonates who successfully underwent lower-extremity PICC placement in the neonatal intensive care unit of a maternal and child health hospital were enrolled as study subjects. Variable selection was performed using stepwise regression based on the Akaike information criterion, followed by development of a multiple linear regression model. Internal validation was performed using the random split sample method (8:2). Model performance was assessed using root mean square error, mean absolute error, coefficient of determination (R2), and Pearson's correlation coefficient.

RESULTS: The final model included two simple and objective variables: body weight on the day of catheterization and puncture site. The prediction equation was established as follows: insertion depth (cm) = 17.3 + body weight at catheterization (kg) × 2.3 - adjustment value for the puncture site (2.7 for small saphenous vein, 4.5 for popliteal vein, 5.1 for popliteal great saphenous vein, and 10.3 for femoral vein, respectively; reference: ankle great saphenous vein). Internal validation showed that the model achieved an R2 of 0.8789, RMSE of 1.0754, MAE of 0.8157, and Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.9375 between the predicted and observed values. Residual diagnostics indicated good predictive accuracy and stability.

CONCLUSIONS: The prediction model for neonatal lower extremity PICC insertion depth based on body weight at the catheterization and puncture sites demonstrated good fit and reliable predictive performance. It can assist in individualizing and precisely determining the catheter insertion depth in clinical practice, thereby reducing repeated adjustments and complications.

articles.title: The importance of RSV vaccination for at-risk adults aged 18-59: An expert opinion with an Italian perspective.
articles.abstract: This expert opinion reviews the burden of RSV in at-risk adults aged 18-59 years and summarizes available evidence to provide expert considerations that may inform prevention strategies. Adults with comorbidities or immunocompromise frequently experience severe RSV infection, with annual and seasonal rates of 37.6 per 1000 persons/year and 28.4 per 1000 persons/season, respectively. Clinical presentation ranges from being asymptomatic through to acute respiratory distress, with 6.5-32.8% at-risk adults requiring hospitalization for RSV disease. Three preventative vaccines (RSVpreF, mRNA-1345, RSVPreF3) are currently approved in Europe for adults ≥18 years and in the United States for adults ≥60 years and 18-59 years at increased risk. The panel supports RSV vaccination in adults 18-59 years with severe forms of immunocompromise, respiratory disease, cardiovascular disease, neurological/neuromuscular disease, or renal disease. Higher vaccination rates in this population can be achieved by enhancing awareness, empowering health-care professionals, developing consistent policies, and improving access.

articles.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gitelman syndrome (GS), an autosomal recessive tubulopathy caused by SLC12A3 mutations, presents with hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypocalciuria and hypomagnesemia. Pregnancy can exacerbate these imbalances, increasing maternal-fetal risks, yet standardized management remains lacking. This review summarizes complications, management strategies, and outcomes to guide evidence-based care.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CNKI were searched from inception to December 31, 2025, using 'Gitelman Syndrome' AND ('pregnancy' OR 'gestation'). Two reviewers independently performed literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. Core data were analyzed descriptively, categorical variables as frequencies (%), continuous as mean ± SD or median (range).

RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets (HELLP) syndrome (3.1%); fetal/neonatal complications included preterm birth (16.7%), growth restriction (5.2%), and death (4.2%). Preconception diagnosis showed lower GDM (6.3% vs 18.4%) and fetal/neonatal death (0% vs 8.2%); these comparisons were descriptive and exploratory only. Oral potassium and magnesium were the main treatments. Potassium-sparing diuretics were used in 16 pregnancies (18 exposures); no malformations were reported, but safety is unestablished. Vaginal delivery occurred in 51.2% and Cesarean in 48.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Scaling PROMs Implementation Across Clinical Pathways: Lessons from Hospital Moinhos de Vento's Experience with ICHOM Standard Sets.
articles.journal: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
articles.abstract: This case study presents the 7-year experience of Hospital Moinhos de Vento (HMV), a leading private hospital in Brazil, in implementing patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) through the International Consortium for Health Outcomes Measurement (ICHOM) standard sets. The primary objective was to share practical insights into how PROMs were operationalized across multiple departments and conditions, highlighting implementation strategies, scalability, and challenges. Between 2017 and 2024, PROMs were embedded in clinical workflows across nine health conditions, including stroke, heart failure, breast cancer, and prostate cancer. Results showed improved adherence to data collection and enhanced patient-clinician communication. The authors retrospectively applied the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to map barriers and enablers. Although substantial clinical improvements were observed, they present these as contextual trends within a broader quality improvement ecosystem rather than establishing direct causal attribution to PROMs alone. Key factors for successful scaling included strong institutional leadership, the establishment of a Clinical Practice Office (CPO), shared digital infrastructure, and continuous process improvement. The case underscores that effective PROMs implementation requires deliberate planning, cultural change, and investment in interoperable systems. By detailing the who, how, and when of implementation, this article serves as a practical guide for health care organizations aiming to integrate patient-centered outcomes into routine care.

articles.title: Cost-consequence analysis of long peripheral catheters versus midline catheters: a post-hoc model-based analysis of published systematic review data.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To compare expected hospital costs and catheter-related outcomes of midline catheters (MCs) and long peripheral catheters (LPCs) for intravenous therapy lasting more than seven days.

METHODS: A 7-28-day competing-risks renewal model assumed management and replacement after each failure. Inputs were pooled cause-specific complication rates from a systematic review of 5,023 MCs (129,179 catheter-days) and 962 LPCs (11,147 catheter-days). Uncertainty was quantified with 50,000 second-order probabilistic draws (95% credible intervals, CrI). Scenarios addressed between-study heterogeneity, outcome-specific denominators, and confounding by indication. Sensitivity analyses used re-extracted all-cause failure rates and four direct comparisons.

RESULTS: At 14 and 28 days, incremental costs (MC minus LPC) were -€97.9 (95% CrI, -264 to + 21) and -€218.3 (95% CrI, -547 to +14) per patient, respectively. MCs were cost-saving in 93.9% and 96.6% of simulations, respectively. The higher MC insertion cost was offset after 2.6 days. At 14 days, expected failures per patient were 0.064 versus 0.246, and first-device therapy completion was 93.8% versus 78.2% (MC versus LPC). Bloodstream infection and symptomatic thrombosis accounted for 68.2% of the cost difference and 7.9% of the failure difference. All-cause failure rates yielded a 14-day cost difference of -€104.9. With head-to-head evidence, the LPC-to-MC failure rate ratio was 1.97 versus 4.89 using pooled rates, and the 14-day cost difference was -€60.9 (95% CrI, -226 to +54). Without the modeled excess of these complications with LPCs, MCs cost €17.6 more per patient.

LIMITATIONS: Pooled observational data had unequal exposure across devices and were susceptible to confounding by indication. Costs reflected one national setting. The model excluded indirect costs, quality of life, and patient heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: MCs had fewer modeled failures across analyses. Estimated savings diminished with head-to-head evidence and depended on unconfirmed differences in major complications. Adjusted head-to-head studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Education Research: A Novel Clerkship-Level Approach to Disability Education: Integrating Patient and Professional Identity Through Adaptation and Inclusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Persons with disabilities experience inequities in health care, partly driven by clinicians' limited training in disability-competent communication and accommodations. Disability education remains heterogeneous, with few framing disability as both a patient and physician identity. We developed a clerkship-level curriculum to address this gap. Learner objectives were to differentiate the medical and social models of disability; describe disability-inclusive communication; recognize disability as both a patient and physician identity; identify accessibility barriers and accommodations; and support disability-inclusive care.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary team developed a disability curriculum within a required third-year neurology clerkship. Students completed asynchronous preparation and observations, followed by a workshop incorporating team-based simulation and structured debriefing. Anonymous preworkshop and postworkshop surveys assessed understanding, attitudes, and comfort. Quantitative comparisons and exploratory thematic analysis evaluated learner outcomes.

RESULTS: All 267 enrolled third-year medical students completed the preworkshop survey; 204 completed the postworkshop survey, with attrition reflecting clerkship absences. Significant improvements were observed in understanding of the medical and social models of disability (24.7%-98.5%; +73.8%; 95% CI 67.7%-78.7%), comfort discussing disability with patients (53.6%-98.0%; +44.4%; 95% CI 37.9%-50.6%), discussing accommodations (63.3%-98.0%; +34.7%; 95% CI 28.4%-40.8%), and comfort supporting colleagues with disabilities (35.2%-97.1%; +61.9%; 95% CI 55.1%-67.6%) (all p < 0.0001). Attitudes toward physicians with disabilities were favorable at baseline and remained high (97.0% vs 99.0%; +2.0%; 95% CI -0.9% to 4.9%; p = 0.20). Respondents rated the curriculum excellent or very good (95.6%; 95% CI 91.8%-97.7%). Students agreed that the workshop would benefit future practice (99.0%; 95% CI 96.5%-99.7%) and improve patient outcomes (99.5%; 95% CI 97.2%-99.9%). Exploratory thematic analysis identified 5 themes: open communication and active listening, individualized accommodations, collaborative adaptation, structural accessibility, and the value of time in inclusive care.

DISCUSSION: The curriculum improved attitudes, comfort, and recognition of disability as both patient and physician identity. Key lessons include the value of experiential, team-based learning; explicit framing beyond deficit-based models; and clinical observation integrated with structured reflection. Future studies should examine longitudinal retention and transfer to clinical practice.

articles.title: Pain Pathophysiology and Assessment in Pediatric Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Pain is pervasive and affects upwards of 59% of critically ill children. Consequences of severe pain include worsened health related quality of life and longer lengths of stay. Evaluating pain in non-verbal critically ill children is a unique challenge due to difficulties with communication and the wide variety of developmental stages. The purpose of our review is to examine the underlying pathophysiology of pain, the current landscape in pain assessment of non-verbal critically ill children and pain assessment tools for non-verbal critically ill children. We performed literature searches from April 25, 2023 to November 20, 2025; we performed literature searches using PubMed and EMBASE with a combination of keywords that included "pain", "pathophysiology", "pediatric", "comfort-behavioral", "FLACC", "P-CPOT", "ventilated", "PICU". The pathophysiology of pain starts with inflammatory reactions at the site of injury, which are transmitted via the dorsal horn to the ascending spinothalamic tract and converge onto the brain using two separate pathways. There are three behavioral pain scales that have been validated in both ventilated and non-ventilated critically ill children: the faces, legs, activity, crying, and consolability scale; the COMFORT-Behavior scale; and the pediatric critical care pain observation tool. While pain assessments are regularly performed in PICUs worldwide, there still exist sites in which validated scales are not used, or no scales are used to evaluate pain. Pain is frequent among critically ill children, and its prompt identification can be challenging. Understanding the pathophysiology of pain and the barriers that clinicians face in identifying pain, particularly in non-verbal critically ill children, will improve the care of these patients.

articles.title: No impact of gluten-free diet on glycemia, growth, or quality of life in asymptomatic celiac disease with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Evidence is limited on longitudinal health outcomes with a gluten-free diet (GFD) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and asymptomatic celiac disease (CD) identified by screening.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the impact of the GFD on glycemic management, anthropometrics, gastrointestinal symptoms, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and nutritional intakes in patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.
