METHODS: Celiac Disease and Diabetes Longitudinal Follow-up and Evaluation Study (CD-LiFE) was a prospective follow-up study (NCT03122093) whereby 62 participants aged 8-45 years (77% adult, 23% pediatric) with T1D and screen-detected CD were evaluated annually over a 2-year study period.

RESULTS: 51.6% of participants were GFD-adherent (daily gluten intake < 10 mg) at study baseline. After 2 years, rates of GFD adherence increased (72.7%) with only 15.2% transitioning to a gluten-containing diet (GCD). No differences were seen in mean HbA1c levels between individuals on a GFD and GCD (Δ = 0.1%; 95% CI: -0.6 to 0.4; P = .613, weight (Δ = 0.2 kg/m2; 95% CI: -2.3 to 2.8; P = .848) or BMI among adults (Δ = -1.1 kg/m2; 95% CI: -0.4 to 0.6; P = .149) nor BMI Z scores among pediatric participants (Δ = 0.91; 95% CI: -0.34 to 2.16; P = .136), number of acute GI symptoms (IRR = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.6 to 1.5; P = .810) nor longitudinal differences in HRQoL with respect to generic (Δ = -0.4; 95% CI: -4.0 to 3.3; P = .840) nor diabetes-specific HRQoL (Δ = 1.5; 95% CI: -2.9 to 5.9; P = .505).

CONCLUSION: This 2-year follow-up study demonstrates adherence to a GFD does not impact glycemic control, anthropometrics, GI symptom development, or HRQoL in adult and pediatric patients with T1D and screen-detected CD.

articles.title: Turing, Hopf, and their coupling: a unified framework for neural pattern formation.
articles.abstract: The brain as a nonlinear dynamical system with intrinsic self-organization is a central tenet of modern neuroscience. However, how spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal patterns spontaneously emerge from homogeneous states remains a fundamental puzzle. This review systematically synthesizes three core mechanisms-Turing instability, Hopf bifurcation, and their coupling-within a unified nonlinear framework. The Turing mechanism breaks spatial symmetry via diffusion-driven instability, generating static patterns. Hopf bifurcation triggers temporal oscillations as eigenvalues cross the imaginary axis, explaining rhythmogenesis. Their coupling, occurring at critical points where both instabilities coincide, produces higher-order spatiotemporal structures such as spiral waves and oscillatory patterns. Mathematically unified under the spectral crossing criterion, these three mechanisms constitute a complete evolutionary continuum from spatial self-assembly to spatiotemporal self-organization. Addressing real-world challenges posed by multiscale heterogeneity, intrinsic noise, and finite network size, future research should develop a multi-agent AI-driven "digital twin testbed." This will facilitate the transition from phenomenological description to causal inference and translate dynamical theory into closed-loop regulation, personalized interventions for brain disorders, and neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Intelligent control of spreading depression in a dual-layer ring network under saturation constraints.
articles.abstract: Spreading depression (SD) is a phenomenon characterized by complete depolarization of neurons and glial cells, and is associated with various brain disorders such as migraine and stroke. The initiation and propagation of SD are regulated by multiple factors, exhibiting typical nonlinear characteristics. Pharmacological options for SD-related disorders remain limited by efficacy, tolerability, and safety concerns. This situation has motivated computational investigation of non-pharmacological, closed-loop neuromodulation strategies. Based on the Wei model and a double-layer ring network model, this paper proposes an intelligent control framework with predictive capability and saturation constraints. Firstly, a temporal convolutional network (TCN) is constructed to predict extracellular potassium concentration, which is then used to identify potential SD events. Next, a controller with saturation constraints is designed based on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network to address the identified SD. When SD is about to occur, real-time intervention is achieved through a cyclic process of prediction-identification-regulation. Simulation results show that the proposed framework can identify impending SD and suppress its initiation and propagation under bounded stimulation amplitudes. These in silico findings provide a computational basis for further study of closed-loop neuromodulation for SD-related disorders.

articles.title: A novel homozygous ITCH nonsense variant causing autoimmune disease, multisystem, with facial dysmorphism: expanding the phenotypic and geographic spectrum.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune disease, multisystem, with facial dysmorphism (ADMFD) is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder. It is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in ITCH, which encodes a ubiquitin ligase that regulates immune homeostasis. Fewer than 15 cases have been reported, all of North American or Western European origin. We describe a girl of Egyptian origin living in the United Arab Emirates. She was first evaluated at age 8 years for severe short stature, delayed puberty, and primary hypothyroidism. Glucagon stimulation testing excluded growth hormone deficiency. At age 15 years, a 145-gene panel identified a novel homozygous ITCH nonsense variant (c.2119C>T; p.Arg707*), supporting a molecular diagnosis of ADMFD. At age 16 years, she presented with diabetic ketoacidosis. Glutamic acid decarboxylase and insulin autoantibodies were positive, confirming autoimmune type 1 diabetes mellitus. Hemoglobin A1c improved from 13.0% (119 mmol/mol) to 6.1% (43 mmol/mol). Thyroid ultrasound confirmed Hashimoto thyroiditis. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed pituitary enlargement and an enlarging cystic pineal lesion. This case extends the ethnic and clinical spectrum of ADMFD to an endocrine-dominant phenotype without hepatic or gastrointestinal involvement. The pituitary and pineal findings have not been described in ADMFD and need characterization. Hepatic and gastrointestinal surveillance remains recommended.

articles.title: Use of osilodrostat in life-threatening ectopic Cushing syndrome secondary to neuroendocrine tumor.
articles.abstract: Ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) syndrome is a rare, severe form of endogenous Cushing syndrome requiring rapid cortisol reduction; experience with osilodrostat in critically ill patients remains limited. A 41-year-old woman with a prior supraglottic neuroendocrine tumor (NET) presented with rapidly progressive proximal weakness, severe hypokalemia, hypertension, and delirium. Adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism was confirmed, with a 12 × 10 × 14-cm abdominal mass showing somatostatin receptor uptake as the probable ectopic source. She required intensive care, intubation, and intravenous etomidate, but developed vasoplegic shock and multiorgan failure despite cortisol reduction. Etomidate was replaced by oral osilodrostat, which rapidly achieved stable serum cortisol over 4 weeks. Open left hepatectomy confirmed a well-differentiated ACTH-positive NET, with postoperative biochemical remission and marked neurological recovery. This case highlights osilodrostat as an effective, safe, and less labor-intensive alternative to parenteral steroidogenesis inhibition in severe ectopic Cushing syndrome, enabling stabilization before definitive surgery.

articles.title: Successful hypertension control in 17-hydroxylase deficiency using crinecerfont.
articles.abstract: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency (17OHD) is a rare form of CAH characterized by cortisol deficiency, impaired sex steroid production, and excess deoxycorticosterone (DOC), resulting in low-renin hypertension and hypokalemia. Management typically relies on glucocorticoid therapy to suppress adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-driven steroidogenesis, but adequate disease control may require supraphysiologic glucocorticoid doses and intensive antihypertensive treatment. Crinecerfont, a corticotropin-releasing factor type 1 (CRF1) receptor antagonist approved for classic CAH, has not previously been reported in 17OHD. We describe a 23-year-old woman with 46,XY karyotype and classic 17OHD with severe persistent hypertension despite high-dose glucocorticoids, spironolactone, and multiple antihypertensive agents. Despite treatment escalation, DOC and pregnenolone levels remained elevated and blood pressure remained poorly controlled. Following initiation of crinecerfont 100 mg twice daily, blood pressure improved to 120-130/80-90 mmHg, plasma renin activity increased, and DOC and pregnenolone concentrations normalized without further glucocorticoid escalation. Clinical and biochemical improvements were sustained during 12 months of follow-up. This case represents the first reported use of crinecerfont in 17OHD and suggests that CRF1 receptor antagonism may offer a novel therapeutic option for refractory hypertension driven by ACTH-dependent mineralocorticoid excess.

articles.title: Thyroid storm induced by palpation thyroiditis after subtotal parathyroidectomy for lithium-induced hyperparathyroidism.
articles.abstract: Palpation thyroiditis is an inflammatory condition of the thyroid gland that may occur following mechanical manipulation, particularly during parathyroid surgery. While postoperative biochemical thyrotoxicosis is relatively common, most patients remain asymptomatic, and severe presentations such as thyroid storm are rare. We report a 52-year-old man with primary hyperparathyroidism, likely lithium-induced, who underwent subtotal parathyroidectomy. His immediate postoperative course was uneventful; however, on postoperative day 3, he developed anterior neck swelling, followed by systemic symptoms including tachycardia, tremor, and fatigue by postoperative day 5. Biochemical findings confirmed severe thyrotoxicosis, and imaging demonstrated inflammatory swelling and edema around the thyroid without abscess formation. Initial management with propranolol and antibiotics resulted in transient clinical improvement. On postoperative day 9, the patient deteriorated with confusion, pyrexia, and worsening tachycardia, necessitating intensive care unit admission, where a diagnosis of thyroid storm was established. Management included intubation, carbimazole, propranolol, hydrocortisone, and cholestyramine, with discontinuation of lithium therapy. Thyroid function normalized within weeks, with sustained euthyroidism at 1-year follow-up. This case highlights thyroid storm as a rare but serious complication of palpation thyroiditis following parathyroid surgery and emphasizes the importance of early recognition and appropriate supportive management.

articles.title: Association between a nurse-led advocacy model and treatment adherence among patients with pulmonary Tuberculosis: a non-randomized controlled trial in Zhejiang Province, China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic barriers and patient-centered monitoring deficits often undermine tuberculosis (TB) treatment adherence in urban environments, escalating the risk of clinical attrition and multidrug resistance. This study evaluated the association between an integrated Nurse-Led Advocacy Model (NLAM) and therapeutic adherence among patients with pulmonary TB within Zhejiang Province, China.

METHODS: A non-randomized controlled trial was conducted across municipal clinics in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, between August 17, 2023, to August 1, 2025. Following propensity score matching via a 1:1 nearest-neighbor algorithm to eliminate baseline imbalances, 300 patients were evaluated: 152 in the NLAM cohort (received structured, face-to-face advocacy sessions spanning intensive and continuation phases with digital adherence technology (DAT) consisting of an electronic smart pill box and the WeChat-TB mini-program interface and 148 in the routine clinical care (RCC cohort; received standard institutional treatment monitoring).

RESULTS: Baseline demographic profiles and clinical characteristics were highly balanced between groups (p > 0.05). The NLAM cohort exhibited significantly higher medication adherence across both drug-susceptible (mean ± SD: 94.5% ± 2.6% vs. 82.8% ± 2.9%; p < 0.001) and multidrug-resistant strains (90.9% ± 2.1% vs. 72.3% ± 2.1%; p < 0.001) compared to the RCC group. Longitudinal survival analysis showed a significantly lower rate of cumulative clinical attrition under the advocacy framework (5.3% [8/152] vs. 14.9% [22/148] loss to follow-up events; Relative Risk = 0.35, 95% Confidence Interval: 0.16-0.77; Log-rank p < 0.001). Patient-perceived nursing support based on the Nursing Advocacy Scale was remarkably higher in the NLAM cohort (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Structured nurse-led advocacy framework coupled with smart-box digital monitoring is strongly associated with optimized medication adherence, heightened patient-perceived support, and minimized clinical attrition.

articles.title: Association between obstructive sleep apnea and severe exertional dyspnea in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exertional dyspnea is a common and disabling symptom of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The severity of dyspnea may not correspond closely to spirometric impairment. In patients with COPD and coexisting obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), recurrent nocturnal desaturation may represent an additional sleep-related feature relevant to severe exertional dyspnea.

METHODS: We included 758 clinically stable patients with COPD. Severe exertional dyspnea was defined as a modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale (mMRC) score ≥3. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the associations of the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation index (ODI), and percentage of sleep time with oxygen saturation below 90% (T90) with severe exertional dyspnea.

RESULTS: Participants were predominantly male (92.2%), with a median age of 67.0 years. Severe exertional dyspnea was present in 199 patients (26.3%). After adjusting for confounders, ODI ≥15 was significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.14-2.51, p = 0.009). In contrast, neither AHI ≥15 nor T90 ≥ 10% showed a statistically significant association. In continuous analyses, log(ODI + 1) remained significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.03-1.57, p = 0.025), whereas log(AHI + 1) and log(T90 + 1) were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Nocturnal ODI was independently associated with severe exertional dyspnea, whereas AHI and T90 were not. The more consistent association for ODI suggests that recurrent nocturnal oxygen desaturations may provide clinically relevant information about the OSA-related component of symptom burden beyond respiratory-event frequency or cumulative nocturnal hypoxemia.

articles.title: Failed-repair proximal tubular epithelial cells in the transition from acute kidney injury to chronic kidney disease: mechanisms, identification, and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) increases the risk of chronic kidney disease, even after apparent recovery of kidney function. Incomplete proximal tubular repair provides a cellular basis for this discrepancy. Failed-repair proximal tubular epithelial cells (FR-PTECs) retain impaired differentiation and inflammatory or profibrotic activity during recovery, forming a persistent epithelial subset within the broader spectrum of maladaptive repair. This review examines their conceptual definition, mechanisms, identification, and therapeutic implications. Single-cell, multiomic, and spatial studies characterize divergent repair trajectories and interactions between abnormal epithelia, immune cells, and stromal cells. Metabolic dysfunction, chromatin remodeling, cell-cycle arrest, and senescence can sustain these responses, but are not universal criteria for identifying FR-PTECs. Experimental studies support functional contributions to fibrosis, whereas human evidence predominantly establishes tissue phenotypes and associations rather than a causal post-AKI trajectory. Tissue assessment provides direct phenotypic evidence; fluid biomarkers offer complementary information about injury, recovery, and prognosis without specifically measuring FR-PTEC burden. Potential interventions are considered according to preservation of adaptive repair, restoration of epithelial function, and selective suppression or clearance of pathological cells. This therapeutic framework remains hypothesis-generating. Translation requires reproducible classification and longitudinal evidence linking epithelial states to kidney outcomes and treatment response.

articles.title: Wearable acoustic cardiography for detection of left ventricular and valvular dysfunction: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative cardiac evaluation based on history and physical examination is subjective, risking delayed diagnosis or excessive echocardiography. Acoustic cardiography (ACG) synchronizes ECG and heart sound analysis for rapid point-of-care cardiac screening. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of wearable ACG for left ventricular dysfunction, significant valvular dysfunction, and the consistency of ACG-aided preoperative risk assessment with expert consensus.

METHODS: This prospective single-center study enrolled consecutive patients undergoing major elective non-cardiac surgery. Echocardiography served as the reference standard; the primary endpoint was LVEF <40%.

RESULTS: Among 262 patients, ACG showed excellent performance for LVEF <40% (AUC=0.979, sensitivity 93.3%, specificity 96.4%). It achieved substantial agreement with echocardiography for significant valvular dysfunction (κ=0.69). Adding ACG improved consistency with expert consensus versus physical examination alone (κ=0.71 vs 0.55).

CONCLUSIONS: Wearable ACG provides high accuracy for preoperative screening of systolic and valvular dysfunction. It facilitates targeted echocardiography referral. Further trials are needed to verify its impact on referral decisions and perioperative outcomes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2300073695.

articles.title: Fever-induced OR560 promotes antibacterial immunity through macrophage pseudopod formation and phagocytosis.
articles.abstract: Fever is a conserved physiological response to pathogen infection. However, how fever promotes host defense remains poorly understood. Here we find that fever empowers antibacterial immunity by inducing olfactory receptor 560 (OR560) to promote macrophage phagocytosis. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we discovered that OR560 is indispensable for macrophage phagocytosis. Febrile temperature drives the serum response factor-dependent OR560 induction in macrophages to boost phagocytosis. OR560 responds to bacteria-derived peptides and plays an essential role in mediating pseudopod formation-a key step required for target uptake. Modulation of body temperature in mice showed that the immune-amplifying effect of fever depends predominantly on OR560. We further demonstrated that the genetic ablation of either Olfr560 or serum response factor (Srf) in mice not only abolished fever-potentiated macrophage phagocytosis but also led to catastrophic defects in bacterial clearance and increased mortality upon infections. Thus, our work reveals that OR560 is a pivotal regulator of fever-enhanced antibacterial phagocytosis and integrates both pathogen-derived and febrile signals to ensure a robust response to infection.

articles.title: Viral persistence and post-acute outcomes following high-consequence negative-sense RNA virus infections.
articles.abstract: High-consequence viral pathogens, including filoviruses, arenaviruses, bunyaviruses, and henipaviruses, can cause severe acute disease with high case-fatality rates. Although survivors occur in the absence of specific therapies, outcomes may be improved through early diagnosis, supportive care, and, for select pathogens, licensed or investigational countermeasures. The increasing number of survivors has focused attention on post-acute consequences of infection. Viral RNA, viral antigen, and infectious virus have been detected after recovery in selected body fluids and tissues, raising questions regarding transmission risk, reservoirs, and persistence. Survivors may also experience diverse long-term sequelae affecting neurological, ocular, auditory, musculoskeletal, cardiopulmonary, and general health. In some cases, late-onset disease or relapse has been reported months to years after recovery. Here, we review evidence for persistence of high-consequence negative-sense RNA viruses, summarize sequelae, examine late syndromes, and highlight research priorities needed to improve survivor care and preparedness.

articles.title: Fungal pathogen Metschnikowia bicuspidata exploits exosomal miRNA as a cross-kingdom effector to suppress innate immunity in the crustacean host Eriocheir sinensis.
articles.abstract: Fungal pathogens have evolved sophisticated strategies to modulate host immunity and promote infection, yet the role of exosome-like vesicle (ELV) as mediators of small RNA delivery in fungal-animal interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we report that the pathogenic yeast Metschnikowia bicuspidata secretes ELVs enriched in microRNAs that function as cross-kingdom regulators of host innate immunity in the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis). High-throughput sequencing identified a repertoire of fungal-derived exosomal microRNAs with predicted targets in multiple host immune pathways, suggesting coordinated immune modulation. Among these, a novel microRNA, miR-23-3p was highly enriched and selectively delivered into host cells during infection. Functional analyses demonstrated that miR-23-3p directly targets the p38 MAPK gene, a conserved signaling hub in innate immunity, leading to suppression of downstream immune responses, including antimicrobial peptide production, reactive oxygen species generation, and phenoloxidase activity. Consequently, p38 suppression enhanced fungal survival in the hemolymph and increased host mortality during infection. Mechanistically, inhibition of p38 attenuated activating transcription factor 2 (ATF2) activity, leading to reduced expression of dual oxidase 2-like (Duox2L) and diminished ROS production. Given the central role of p38 MAPK in immune regulation across diverse species, our findings suggest that targeting conserved immune signaling pathways via exosomal microRNAs may represent a broadly utilized virulence strategy among fungal pathogens. This study provides new insights into cross-kingdom RNA-based immune modulation and expands our understanding of fungal pathogenicity in crustacean hosts.

articles.title: Comparison of acute kidney injury after robot-assisted versus laparoscopic partial nephrectomy in high-risk patients: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) compared with laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN) in patients with limited renal reserve remains uncertain. We compared early AKI and six-month renal outcomes between approaches in high-risk patients.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients with solitary kidney, documented CKD, or preoperative estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 who underwent laparoscopic or robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy between October 2015 and December 2023. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) adjusted for measured baseline differences. The primary outcome was creatinine-defined AKI within 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included AKI stage, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, length of stay, non-AKI complications, and 6-month renal function postoperatively. Sensitivity analyses restricted the cohort to 2021-2023 or applied overlap weighting.

RESULTS: Among 227 patients, 76 underwent robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy and 151 underwent laparoscopic partial nephrectomy. After IPTW, 24-hour AKI occurred in 32.4% versus 26.9% (odds ratio [OR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68-2.49; p = 0.425). AKI stage (common OR 1.27, 95% CI 0.70-2.31; p = 0.435) and ICU admission (20.0% vs 18.1%; p = 0.740) were similar. Operative duration was longer with RAPN (median difference 20.9 min; p < 0.001), whereas clamp time and blood loss were comparable. Postoperative length of stay was 4 versus 5 days (p = 0.058). Six-month eGFR was lower after RAPN (45.9 vs 51.0 mL/min/1.73 m2; median difference -5.1, 95% CI -9.5 to -0.7; p = 0.022), but percentage eGFR decline did not differ (p = 0.299). A > 20% decline occurred in 19.3% versus 9.3% (OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.00-5.45; p = 0.050). The primary AKI finding was consistent in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: In high-risk patients, robotic-assisted partial nephrectomy was not associated with a lower incidence or severity of 24-hour postoperative creatinine-defined AKI compared with LPN. Six-month renal findings were exploratory and warrant confirmation.

articles.title: Prolonged Cholestasis as an Initial Presentation of Miliary Tuberculosis in a Pediatric Patient.
articles.abstract: Miliary tuberculosis is a severe form of tuberculosis resulting from hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and may cause respiratory failure and multiorgan involvement in infants. Hepatic involvement is uncommon and may present as prolonged cholestasis and granulomatous hepatitis, making the diagnosis particularly challenging. We report an infant with miliary tuberculosis presenting with infantile cholestasis and acute respiratory failure. A 2-month-old infant presented with persistent cholestasis developed at 6 weeks of age and acute respiratory failure requiring noninvasive mechanical ventilation. Initial evaluation, including intraoperative cholangiography, excluded biliary atresia, and an extensive infectious, metabolic, autoimmune, immunologic, and genetic evaluation did not identify an alternative cause. Chest computed tomography demonstrated bilateral ground-glass opacities and peripheral micronodules in a miliary pattern. Liver biopsy showed granulomatous hepatitis with focal central necrosis and multinucleated giant cells. The diagnosis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis was confirmed by sputum polymerase chain reaction and acid-fast bacilli culture. A four-drug anti-tuberculosis regimen led to complete clinical, radiological, and biochemical resolution, with full recovery by 4 months of age. Miliary tuberculosis should be considered in infants presenting with severe respiratory failure, prolonged neonatal cholestasis, and granulomatous hepatitis, particularly in endemic regions. Early recognition of miliary pulmonary patterns on imaging and prompt initiation of targeted anti-tuberculosis therapy is critical to improve outcomes and ensure a favorable prognosis.

articles.title: A Rare Post-Hair Transplant Complication With Complete Recovery.
articles.abstract: Postoperative complications following hair transplantation are generally mild and self-limited; however, severe infectious or inflammatory reactions involving the periorbital or cervicofacial regions are exceedingly rare yet potentially vision- or life-threatening. Early recognition and prompt multidisciplinary management are essential, as delayed intervention may result in rapid soft-tissue progression, necrosis, and systemic instability. A 34-year-old man developed rapidly progressive cervicofacial edema 48 h after an uncomplicated hair transplantation procedure. The patient had no history of prior cranial surgery, trauma, or implanted prosthetic material. The swelling originated in the recipient area and rapidly extended to the forehead and bilateral periorbital regions, accompanied by severe pain, fever, hypotension, and hemodynamic instability. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated markedly elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 193 mg/L (reference < 5 mg/L), procalcitonin 51.43 ng/mL (reference < 0.05 ng/mL), lactate 9.68 mmol/L (reference 0.5-2.2 mmol/L)) with progressive leukopenia. Despite empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics, intensive care support, and multidisciplinary management, the patient's condition deteriorated, with worsening edema, hemorrhagic-purulent bullae, bilateral pleural effusions, and atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. Subsequent periorbital skin necrosis required surgical debridement. Later during hospitalization, neck soft-tissue involvement with multiple small fluid collections emerged. Gradual improvement followed escalation of antimicrobial therapy and corticosteroid administration; however, residual frontal muscle akinesia and right facial nerve paresis persisted. The patient eventually stabilized on long-term azathioprine therapy and achieved full clinical recovery. This case underscores that rapidly progressive cervicofacial edema, periorbital involvement, frontal muscle akinesia, and right facial nerve paresis after hair transplantation, although rare, may indicate a fulminant infectious or inflammatory process requiring urgent, multidisciplinary management. Early recognition, timely therapeutic escalation, and close monitoring are critical to preventing irreversible tissue damage and systemic complications. Increased awareness of such severe postoperative reactions can enhance clinical vigilance and improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Early deep infection after operatively managed low-velocity tibial gunshot fractures is associated with older age, temporary external fixation, and longer time to definitive fixation.
articles.journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to determine postoperative infection rates and identify factors associated with deep infection in low-velocity tibial gunshot wound (GSW) fractures managed operatively.

DESIGN: This is a retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: The setting includes a Level 1 urban trauma center.

PATIENTS/PARTICIPANTS: The participants in this study are adult patients with operatively managed tibial fractures resulting from low-velocity GSWs treated between 2015 and 2024. Inclusion required operative fixation, 48 hours of postoperative intravenous antibiotics, and a minimum of 3 months of follow-up. A total of 113 patients with 116 tibial fractures met the inclusion criteria.

INTERVENTION: Intervention included operative fixation of tibial GSW fractures with a uniform 48-hour postoperative intravenous antibiotic regimen.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was deep infection, defined as infection requiring operative debridement, intravenous antibiotics, or positive deep tissue or hardware-associated cultures.

RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 33.9 ± 13.0 years, and 84.5% were male. Deep infection occurred in 13 patients (11.2%). Patients who developed deep infection were older (P = 0.046) and experienced longer intervals from injury to definitive fixation (P = 0.008). Temporary external fixation was strongly associated with deep infection (odds ratio 9.81, 95% confidence interval 2.06-46.66; P = 0.002). Temporary external fixation was associated with a longer overall time from injury to definitive fixation (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In operatively managed tibial GSW fractures treated with a standardized 48-hour antibiotic regimen, increasing age, temporary external fixation, and a longer interval from injury to definitive fixation were associated with increased risk of infection. These findings may help identify higher-risk patients and inform future strategies to reduce infection after ballistic tibial fractures.

articles.title: A Phase 1, Dose Escalation Study of Lenalidomide and Ibrutinib for Relapsed/Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: BTK inhibitors have transformed the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), but strategies to deepen and prolong response are needed. Lenalidomide is active in CLL/SLL through a non-overlapping mechanism but is limited by toxicity. We evaluated lenalidomide combined with ibrutinib in relapsed/refractory (R/R) CLL/SLL.

METHODS: In this multicenter, phase 1, 3+3 dose-escalation study, patients with R/R CLL/SLL after ≥ 1 prior therapy received a 28-day ibrutinib run-in (420 mg daily), then added lenalidomide with intra-patient escalation to a cohort-assigned maximum of 2.5, 5, 7.5, or 10 mg daily. Lenalidomide was stopped after 12 cycles; ibrutinib continued until progression or intolerance. The primary endpoint was safety, tolerability, and maximum tolerated dose (MTD).

RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients were enrolled. The MTD of lenalidomide was 5 mg daily. Dose interruptions or reductions occurred in 85% of patients; 7 (26%) and 5 (19%) discontinued for toxicity and progression, respectively. Significant cardiac toxicity occurred in 26%, including heart failure and ventricular arrhythmia (2 patients [7%] each). The overall response rate was 88% (13% complete response). After a median follow-up of 50.4 months, median progression-free survival was 69.5 months (95% CI 53.4-NE).

CONCLUSION: Lenalidomide plus ibrutinib is effective in R/R CLL/SLL but carries an unexpectedly high risk of cardiac toxicity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01886859.

articles.title: First-Attempt Video Laryngoscopic Intubation in an Adult With Down Syndrome and Severe Tracheal Compression From a Giant Retrosternal Goiter.
articles.abstract: Giant retrosternal goiters can cause severe tracheal compression and pose substantial challenges for airway management and surgical resection. These challenges may be further increased in adults with Down syndrome (DS), in whom craniofacial abnormalities, macroglossia, obesity, limited neck mobility, and potential cervical spine abnormalities may contribute to difficult airway management. We report the perioperative management of a 29-year-old woman with DS and a giant multinodular retrosternal goiter causing marked rightward tracheal deviation and critical tracheal narrowing to approximately 7 mm, requiring combined cervical resection and median sternotomy. Preoperative assessment identified multiple predictors of difficult mask ventilation and tracheal intubation, while severe intellectual disability made awake airway management impractical. A multidisciplinary airway and surgical strategy were therefore developed, incorporating optimized positioning and preoxygenation, video laryngoscopy as the planned primary intubation technique, flexible bronchoscopy for confirmation and rescue, and predefined escalation to surgical airway and extracorporeal support if conventional airway management failed. Following controlled intravenous induction, tracheal intubation was achieved on the first attempt with a 6.0-mm endotracheal tube without hypoxemia or hemodynamic instability. Total thyroidectomy and median sternotomy were completed uneventfully. After an adequate cuff-leak test and confirmation of full neuromuscular recovery, the patient was extubated in the operating room and received postoperative bilevel positive airway pressure and overnight intensive care monitoring. No respiratory or other major postoperative complications occurred, and she was discharged home on postoperative day 5. This case illustrates the individualized integration of established difficult-airway principles when DS coexists with severe mechanical tracheal compression from a giant retrosternal goiter. Successful management depended not on a single airway technique, but on careful preoperative anatomical and functional assessment, selection of a feasible primary approach, optimized oxygenation, and an immediately executable multidisciplinary rescue pathway.

articles.title: Emergency Physician-Performed Point-of-Care Ultrasound Identified Left Atrial Myxoma in Acute Cerebellar Infarction.
articles.abstract: Cardiac myxoma is a rare but potentially curable cause of cardioembolic stroke. Early identification of a potential cardiac embolic source may be challenging when neurological symptoms predominate during the initial emergency department evaluation. A 72-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with acute-onset dizziness and vomiting. Although her National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 0, she was unable to walk independently. Electrocardiography demonstrated newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation. Because a cardioembolic mechanism was considered, the emergency physician performed bedside cardiac point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), which revealed a highly mobile left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum. POCUS was performed 28 min after arrival, before brain magnetic resonance imaging, which demonstrated multiple acute cerebellar infarctions without large-vessel occlusion. Intravenous alteplase was not administered despite presentation within the therapeutic time window. Anticoagulation with intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated. Surgical resection was postponed after hemorrhagic transformation of the cerebellar infarction was detected on hospital day 14. The patient underwent complete tumor resection on hospital day 41, and histopathological examination confirmed cardiac myxoma. She was discharged on hospital day 54 with a favorable outcome. This case illustrates the potential value of emergency physician-performed cardiac POCUS for early identification of structural cardiac abnormalities during the initial evaluation of selected patients with suspected cardioembolic stroke.

articles.title: Twenty-Three Years of Survival Observed in a Diabetic Woman Receiving Extended-Hours Hemodialysis (18-25 Hours per Week) With a Liberalized Diet.
articles.abstract: Patients with diabetes undergoing hemodialysis are known to develop numerous complications and have significantly higher mortality risk compared with patients without diabetes. Improving glycemic control is expected to improve the prognosis of patients with diabetes undergoing hemodialysis. However, dietary restrictions imposed for dialysis management and blood glucose control cause malnutrition, leading to an increased risk of protein-energy wasting (PEW), which complicates blood glucose control. Conventional hemodialysis is performed three times a week for 4 h. In contrast, our clinic provides extended-hours hemodialysis with a liberalized diet, 3-4 times a week for 6-8 h, to control hypertension and prevent malnutrition. This report describes a patient who initiated renal replacement therapy (RRT) for diabetic nephropathy and, despite multiple complications after transferring to our clinic, maintained extended-hours hemodialysis with a liberalized diet for 23 years. In this case, monotherapy with α-glucosidase inhibitors maintained glycemic control, with an average glycated albumin level of 18.0±1.7%. After the patient transferred to our clinic, her body mass index (BMI) and muscle mass increased. However, severe vascular calcification was already present shortly after transfer, resulting in two severe diabetic vascular complications caused by vascular calcification: ischemic heart disease and below-knee amputation. BMI temporarily decreased at the time of each event, but subsequently trended upward again. Left ventricular ejection fraction remained within the normal range at 62-72%, and the patient maintained independence in daily life after below-knee amputation, albeit with wheelchair use. The changes in muscle mass and prognosis in this case likely reflect multiple factors, including adequate dialysis dosage and high health literacy, during extended-hours hemodialysis with a liberalized diet. These observations offer insights into diabetic patients on hemodialysis but do not establish causality.

articles.title: Potential Association Between Antibiotics and Atrial Fibrillation: A Review of Current Evidence and Mechanistic Insights.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic-associated cardiotoxicity has traditionally been discussed in relation to QT prolongation and torsade de pointes. A possible association between antibiotic exposure and atrial fibrillation (AF) has also been reported, but infection itself is an established AF trigger. This review distinguishes observational epidemiology, pharmacovigilance analyses, clinical case reports, and experimental studies when considering antibiotic classes and proposed mechanisms. Pharmacovigilance findings include AF reporting associations for macrolides, whereas much of the cardiovascular evidence for fluoroquinolones concerns QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias. AF-specific clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Proposed pathways include electrolyte disturbances, autonomic effects, drug interactions, inflammatory or allergic reactions, myocardial injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and gut dysbiosis. These pathways provide biological plausibility but do not demonstrate that antibiotic exposure causes clinically relevant atrial changes or AF. FAERS and VigiBase can identify potential safety signals but cannot independently establish incidence or causality. Confounding by infection type and severity, patient susceptibility, and concomitant treatments limits interpretation of clinical associations. The qualitative AF relevance categories summarize the available support for a potential association and do not quantify clinical risk or formally grade evidence certainty. Overall, the proposed associations remain hypothesis-generating. Appropriately controlled studies are needed to distinguish potential antibiotic effects from infection-related AF and to determine their clinical relevance.

articles.title: Perioperative Management of a Breastfed Child Whose Mother Was Receiving Injectable Semaglutide: A Case Report Outlining Use of Gastric Point-of-Care Ultrasound.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), including semaglutide, are increasingly used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus and for weight management. Although generally effective, specific end-organ effects, including delayed gastric emptying, may impact the perioperative care of patients receiving these agents. Given these concerns, guidelines have been suggested for the perioperative care of patients receiving GLP-1 RAs. However, these recommendations do not specifically address the increasingly encountered scenario in which a breastfeeding mother is taking a GLP-1 RA and the breastfed infant or young child is presenting for anesthetic care. We present a 15-month-old breastfed child who presented for surgery and whose mother was receiving once-weekly injectable semaglutide. Given limited evidence-based medicine to guide perioperative care in this clinical scenario, preoperative gastric point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) was used to evaluate gastric volume before induction of anesthesia. Perioperative care of breastfed children of mothers receiving GLP-1 RAs is discussed, the role of gastric POCUS is presented, and options for perioperative care are reviewed.

articles.title: Relationship Between Estrogen-Induced BRCA2 and Development of Gastric Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fourth most common malignancy, affecting one in 11 men (9.1%) and one in 23 women (4.38%). Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and smoking are the primary risk factors for GC. Individuals who have multiple other family members with GC are also at higher risk owing to lifestyle and genetic factors. H. pylori-eradicating medications can reduce the risk of disease. The incidence of GC increases after 50 years of age, particularly among men; however, the reason for the differing incidence rates between the sexes remains unclear.

METHODS: To clarify the reasons for sex differences in GC incidence rates from a molecular pathological perspective, we utilized cancer genome profiling (CGP) and information on BRCA2 expression levels obtained by immunohistochemistry and the number of GC cases in the family.

RESULTS: We investigated the incidence of GC in families with hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) and found it to be 4.2-fold higher than that in non-HBOC families. In families with versus without HBOC, men accounted for 74.57% and 53.67% of all GC cases, respectively, indicating that men are more likely to develop GC in the former group. Furthermore, estrogen stimulation induced breast cancer type 2 (BRCA2) expression in genetically modified mice as well as in cultured cells, and low-grade atypical cells were observed in the gastric mucosal tissues of female mice that underwent ovarian resection. Additional research experiment revealed that stimulation by the female hormone estrogen induces the expression of BRCA2, which suppresses the development of GC. Clinical studies have also shown that patients with GC who have high BRCA2 expression exhibit longer survival rates than those in whom BRCA2 expression is low.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the data suggest that the higher mortality rate of GC in men than in women may be due to a protective effect of BRCA2.

articles.title: Impact of Center Volume on Access to Pancreas Transplantation and Waiting List Mortality: A 25-y Eurotransplant Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreas transplantation remains among the few treatments able to restore sustained insulin independence in selected patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus, yet annual transplant numbers have declined across the Eurotransplant region. Previous work has linked center volume to posttransplant graft and patient survival, but its influence on access to transplantation and waiting list mortality remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 6672 patients listed for vascularized pancreas transplantation within Eurotransplant between 2000 and 2024. Centers were classified each year by tertile of annual transplant volume into low-, medium-, and high-volume categories. Cumulative incidence functions for transplantation and waiting list mortality were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen estimator. Cause-specific time-varying Cox proportional hazards models were fitted, adjusting for recipient age, sex, blood group, country, registration year, and waiting list size.

RESULTS: Overall, 4410 patients (66.1%) received a transplant and 655 (9.8%) died on the waiting list. Compared with low-volume centers, listing at medium-volume (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.27) and high-volume centers (HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.16-1.45) was independently associated with a higher probability of transplantation. Waiting list mortality was also lower at medium-volume (HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.53-0.92) and high-volume centers (HR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.90).

CONCLUSIONS: Within Eurotransplant, patients listed at low-volume pancreas transplant centers face a dual disadvantage of reduced access to transplantation and higher waiting list mortality, with implications for allocation policy, center designation, and patient referral.

articles.title: Cuproptosis in kidney diseases: Mechanisms, pathophysiology, and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Cuproptosis is a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by copper binding to lipoylated mitochondrial proteins, protein aggregation, loss of iron-sulfur cluster proteins, and proteotoxic stress. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of cuproptosis, its involvement in acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), diabetic nephropathy (DN), and renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and the therapeutic implications of its modulation. Experimental studies implicate cuproptosis in tubular epithelial injury, podocyte dysfunction, and renal damage associated with metabolic, ischemic, and inflammatory stress. In clear cell RCC, altered expression of cuproptosis-related genes is associated with tumor behavior, prognosis, and the immune microenvironment, while experimental induction of copper-dependent cell death provides a rationale for therapeutic investigation. These findings support a disease-dependent approach: suppressing cuproptosis to protect non-malignant renal tissue and inducing it to target susceptible cancer cells. Copper chelators, copper ionophores, and interventions targeting pathway regulators are being investigated within this framework. However, much of the evidence derives from computational analyses and preclinical models, and gene-expression signatures alone do not establish active cuproptosis. Clinical translation requires functional validation, reliable biomarkers, and strategies that achieve tissue selectivity while preserving essential copper homeostasis. Cuproptosis therefore provides a mechanistic framework for investigating renal injury and cancer, with therapeutic application dependent on establishing efficacy and safety in the relevant disease context.

articles.title: In-hospital outcomes associated with renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, Beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in acute decompensated heart failure: Analysis by chronic kidney disease status and heart failure subtypes.
articles.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between early inpatient neurohormonal antagonist prescriptions and outcomes in acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) remain incompletely characterized across kidney function and heart failure subtypes.

METHODS: In 2208 ADHF admissions, adjusted logistic regression assessed ACE inhibitor/angiotensin receptor blocker (ACEi/ARB), beta-blocker, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) prescriptions during the first seven days in relation to worsening renal function (WRF), mortality, and their composite, stratified by CKD and ejection fraction. Sensitivity analyses examined a day-7 landmark cohort and pre-admission medication history.

RESULTS: ACEi/ARB prescriptions were associated with lower adjusted odds of WRF (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.70, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.57-0.87) and in-hospital mortality (aOR 0.54, 95% CI 0.34-0.86); MRA showed similar associations, whereas beta-blockers showed none. Significant estimates were observed in HFrEF (WRF aOR 0.61 for ACEi/ARB and 0.53 for MRA) but generally not in LVEF >40%, and CKD status did not modify these associations (all P for interaction >0.05). In a day-7 landmark analysis excluding early WRF, first-onset WRF associations were attenuated and no longer significant overall but persisted in HFrEF. New ACEi/ARB and MRA users had lower WRF odds than never users but did not differ from continuing users; continuing beta-blocker users had higher WRF odds than new users.

CONCLUSION: In this ADHF cohort, ACEi/ARB and MRA use was associated with lower odds of WRF, but associations weakened after accounting for onset timing and remained significant only in HFrEF. These observational findings do not establish treatment benefit.

articles.title: Why emerging infectious diseases are becoming more complex in the twenty-first century.
articles.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases in the twenty-first century arise within rapidly changing biological, ecological, environmental, social, and health care systems. Recent outbreaks and antimicrobial resistance show that infectious disease threats can no longer be understood through pathogen-centered models alone. This review examines why infectious diseases are becoming more complex, with emphasis on zoonotic spillover, environmental change, climate-sensitive transmission, globalization, antimicrobial resistance, viral evolution, surveillance, and preparedness. Infectious disease complexity reflects interactions among microbial adaptation, reservoir ecology, host susceptibility, human-animal contact, land-use change, climate pressure, urbanization, mobility, health care exposure, and unequal public health capacity. Case examples including Ebola disease, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), highly pathogenic avian influenza, Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS), coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), Nipah virus disease, and mpox show that containment depends on transmission biology, exposure setting, timing of infectiousness, and health system readiness. Antimicrobial resistance adds a slower but persistent crisis because resistant organisms, resistance genes, antimicrobial residues, and vulnerable hosts circulate across hospitals, communities, food systems, wastewater, and environmental reservoirs. Preparedness should move upstream of the first recognized human case. Future strategies should make ecological prevention measurable, study reservoir-host dynamics, anticipate pathogen adaptation, reduce exposure at spillover interfaces, detect silent human infection earlier, and respond rapidly through coordinated investigation. Infectious disease control in the twenty-first century will require integrated systems that connect ecological prevention, molecular insight, surveillance, health care resilience, public trust, equity, and sustained global cooperation.

articles.title: Impact of glycemic status on coronary lesion characteristics in patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to determine if higher blood sugar, even within the prediabetes range, affects coronary lesion characteristics.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Symptomatic patients with confirmed CAD on CCTA were stratified into three different groups based on their glycated-hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels: 1) Euglycemia, HbA1c below 5.7% (HbA1c < 39 mmol/mol) 2) Prediabetes, HbA1c-levels between 5.7% and 6.4% (HbA1c = 39-46 mmol/mol) 3) Diabetes, HbA1c-levels ≥6.5% (HbA1c ≥ 48 mmol/mol). A plaque analysis of culprit lesions on CCTA using a dedicated plaque analysis software was performed and findings between the three different groups were compared.

RESULTS: Overall 184 patients and 247 coronary lesions were analyzed. Coronary lesion length was significantly greater in prediabetic [(29.5 mm (12.7-50-4) versus 24.8 mm (11.4-51.1), p = 0.025)] and diabetic individuals [(30.1 mm (16.7-50.2) versus 24.8 mm (11.4-51.1), p = 0.005)] compared to those with normal HbA1c levels. In terms of plaque composition and volume, diabetic individuals demonstrated a significantly higher amount of total lipid-rich plaque volume [(62.5 mm3 (38.1-93.7) versus 41.9 mm3 (22.4-66.7), p < 0.001] and total fibrotic plaque volume [55.7 mm3 (37.1-92.2) versus 29.3 mm3 (16.9-61.2), p = 0.004] compared to euglycemic patients. In multivariable adjusted logistic regression, there was a significant association between both prediabetes and diabetes and predominantly non-calcified plaques (odds ratio [OR] 2.124 [95% CI (1.016-4.437), p = 0.045 and OR 2.505 (1.029-6.098), p = 0.043].

CONCLUSION: Poor glycemic status is associated with a higher prevalence of predominantly noncalcified plaques in symptomatic individuals. When compared to euglycemic individuals, prediabetic individuals demonstrate an extended coronary lesion length similar to diabetics. These factors may play a role in the poorer clinical outcomes even observed in patients with borderline diabetes.

articles.title: Assessment of safety and effectiveness of continuous intravenous labetalol infusion for blood pressure control in patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: a STROBE-compliant observational study.
articles.journal: Current therapeutic research, clinical and experimental
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current evidence on continuous labetalol infusion for blood pressure (BP) control in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH) is limited with unclear information on higher doses.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of continuous labetalol in SICH patients.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-arm observational study involving SICH patients who received continuous labetalol infusion to achieve and maintain target BP (<140/90 mmHg). Effective outcomes included BP control, the time required to achieve the target BP, BP variability, and hematoma expansion. Safety outcomes included adverse event (AE) rates and predictive factors. Subgroup analyses were performed by categorizing patients into low (≤300 mg) and high (>300 mg) cumulative dose groups within 24 hours.

RESULTS: A total of 84 patients were available for analysis. The median time to reach target BP was 2.0 hours (interquartile range, IQR: 0.5-3.3 hours), and the median percentage of time at target BP was 53% (IQR: 35-66%). The BP profile suggested stable BP control over 24 hours. Hematoma expansion was observed in 8.3% of patients. During continuous labetalol infusion, 42 AEs were reported in 19 patients, with bradycardia being the most common (22.6%). However, no resuscitation was required. The incidence of bradycardia or hypotension appeared to be comparable between the low and high cumulative dose groups. Predictive factors for AEs included baseline systolic BP (SBP), baseline heart rate (HR), and diabetes, all having an inverse relationship with the probability of AEs.

CONCLUSION: Continuous labetalol infusion provides effective and sustained BP control in SICH, with an acceptable safety profile at cumulative doses exceeding 300 mg. Lower baseline SBP and HR were associated with a higher risk of AEs and may help identify patients requiring closer monitoring.The study was registered with the Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20240423003) and can be accessed at https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org/show/TCTR20240423003.

articles.title: Ocular Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) provide substantial glycemic and cardiometabolic benefits, but concerns regarding diabetic retinopathy (DR) progression and nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) have raised questions about their ocular safety. This review critically evaluates current evidence and its clinical implications.

METHODS: A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was conducted from inception through July 2026. Evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, meta-analyses, pharmacovigilance investigations, clinical guidelines, and regulatory documents was narratively synthesized.

RESULTS: In SUSTAIN-6, semaglutide increased DR complications compared with placebo (3.0% vs. 1.8%; hazard ratio 1.76, 95% confidence interval 1.11-2.78), predominantly among patients with pre-existing retinopathy and substantial early glycemic improvement. However, subsequent trials and meta-analyses did not establish a consistent class-wide increase in retinopathy risk. Early worsening appears more closely associated with rapid glycemic reduction than with established direct retinal toxicity. Observational and pharmacovigilance studies have identified a potential association between GLP-1 RAs and NAION, although conflicting findings, limited event numbers, and residual confounding preclude definitive causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence favors individualized ocular risk assessment and targeted ophthalmologic surveillance rather than routine avoidance of GLP-1 RAs. Patients with established retinopathy warrant particular attention during treatment initiation. Prospective studies incorporating standardized ophthalmologic outcomes are essential to clarify unresolved safety signals and optimize clinical monitoring.

articles.title: Differential associations of contralesional and ipsilesional brain functional connectivity with lower-limb impairment after stroke.
articles.abstract: Stroke may induce distinct plastic structural changes within the ipsilesional and contralesional hemispheres of the brain, leading to interhemispheric imbalances in cortical connectivity. Maximum joint range of motion (ROMmax) impairments may also occur in the paretic limb, contributing to increased interlimb asymmetry and impaired gait. This study examined the influence of ipsilesional and contralesional brain functional connectivity on hip flexion ROMmax interlimb asymmetry and walking performance in stroke survivors. Eighteen individuals with chronic stroke (57.5 ± 14.8 years; 26.7 ± 22.2 months post-stroke) were assessed for functional connectivity of the ipsilesional and contralesional general hemispheres and specific primary motor cortex (M1) areas of the brain with resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). Participants were also assessed for hip flexion active ROMmax of the paretic and non-paretic limbs and 10-m walk test, and ROMmax interlimb asymmetry was further calculated. Relationships between changes in these variables were examined by Pearson product-moment (r) and regression analyses. Hip flexion ROMmax interlimb asymmetry was significantly associated with contralesional functional connectivity in both general (r = 0.53) and M1-specific (r = 0.48) regions of the brain (P < 0.05). Walking performance was only associated with contralesional M1 connectivity (r = 0.51; P < 0.05). Contralesional hemisphere connectivity explained 28% of the variance in ROMmax asymmetry, while contralesional M1 connectivity explained 26% of the variance in walking time. No significant relationships were found for brain connectivity within the ipsilesional hemisphere. Greater brain functional connectivity in contralesional cortical regions is associated with increased hip ROMmax asymmetry and impaired walking performance in stroke survivors, highlighting the role of contralesional networks in post-stroke motor impairment.

articles.title: Polydopamine-coated liposomes for oral delivery of tirzepatide: Overcoming gastrointestinal barriers to improve therapeutic efficacy.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide (TZP), the first dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, offers substantial therapeutic benefits for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) but remains confined to subcutaneous injection. While oral delivery of peptide therapeutics improves patient compliance, it is severely hampered by enzymatic degradation and mucosal barriers in the gastrointestinal tract. Liposomes, as biocompatible nanocarriers, can protect encapsulated drugs, enhance intestinal stability, and enable controlled release. Herein, TZP-loaded liposomes (TZP-Lip) were prepared via reverse-phase evaporation and further coated with polydopamine (PDA) to obtain TZP-Lip@PDA for enhanced oral delivery. TZP-Lip@PDA exhibited an encapsulation efficiency of 95.02 ± 1.14%, a particle size of 145.9 ± 1.49 nm, and preservation of the secondary structure of TZP. The PDA coating functioned as a physical diffusion barrier that conferred sustained-release behavior in simulated gastrointestinal fluids, while enhancing mucus penetration and promoting cellular uptake in Caco-2 cells. Pharmacokinetic studies showed that oral TZP-Lip@PDA achieved measurable plasma exposure, whereas oral free TZP remained below the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ, 5 ng/mL). Despite a tenfold higher dose (8.8 vs 0.88 mg/kg), oral TZP-Lip@PDA achieved a Cmax approximately 50% of that observed after subcutaneous administration of free TZP, within the 12-h sampling window, indicating substantial progress but also the remaining quantitative gap between the two routes. In T2DM rats, oral TZP-Lip@PDA (8.8 mg/kg) significantly enhanced the integrated hypoglycemic response during the 12-h observation period compared with oral free TZP and TZP-Lip. In summary, TZP-Lip@PDA enhances the oral delivery of TZP by sustaining drug release, enhancing mucus penetration and promoting cellular uptake, which offers a potential strategy for peptide and protein oral delivery.

articles.title: Optimal temperature windows of mild hyperthermia in tissue regeneration: from bone to skin and beyond.
articles.journal: International journal of hyperthermia : the official journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mild hyperthermia (MHT) has emerged as a promising biophysical approach for promoting tissue repair and regeneration. Controlled, sub-ablative heating can stimulate regenerative cellular responses while preserving tissue viability. However, the optimal thermal conditions vary across tissues and remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the regenerative effects of MHT across bone, skin and wound tissue, skeletal muscle, cardiovascular tissue, peripheral nerves, and neural cell models. Particular emphasis is placed on tissue-specific temperature windows, underlying biological mechanisms, heat-delivery technologies, and clinical translation.

RESULTS: MHT supports tissue regeneration and repair-related responses through coordinated regulation of heat-shock responses, immune polarization, angiogenesis, cellular metabolism, progenitor-cell activity, and pro-regenerative signaling pathways. Evidence from bone, skin, and skeletal muscle models demonstrates enhanced osteogenesis, wound repair, myogenic differentiation, vascularization, and functional recovery. Cardiovascular and neural studies further suggest that controlled heating can support repair by improving cell survival, reducing oxidative and inflammatory injury, and creating a microenvironment favorable for recovery. The principal 39-42 °C range provides a practical framework for regenerative MHT, although effective conditions depend on tissue type, exposure duration, treatment frequency, perfusion, heating modality, and the regenerative endpoint assessed. Advances in targeted heat-delivery, real-time thermometry, and regenerative biomaterials are expanding the potential for precise, tissue-adapted treatment.

CONCLUSION: MHT represents a versatile and promising adjunct to tissue regeneration. Establishing tissue-specific temperature-time protocols and integrating precise thermal control with regenerative technologies may enable its translation into individualized therapies for diverse injuries.

articles.title: Direct visualization endoscopic retrograde appendicitis therapy for recurrent appendicitis with fecaliths and pinworm infection.
Health-Related Quality of Life Across Neurologic Conditions: A Cross-Sectional Cohort Study Using Real-World Patient-Reported Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Health-related quality of life (HRQOL) is an important outcome within value-based care for patients with neurologic conditions. The American Academy of Neurology recommends the use of Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Global Health as a patient-reported outcome performance measure to assess stability or improvement over 1 year. However, interpretation of this measure requires an understanding of HRQOL across neurologic populations. Our study leveraged real-world data collected through the electronic health record to characterize differences in HRQOL across common neurologic conditions.

METHODS: This is a cross-sectional study of adult patients with 1 of 10 conditions (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis [ALS], back pain, brain tumor, dementia, major depression, epilepsy, migraine, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson disease, and stroke) who completed patient-reported outcomes as standard care between October 2015 and March 2023 at a large Neurologic Institute. Patients completed PROMIS-GH, from which physical and mental summary scores (Global Mental Health [GMH], Global Physical Health [GPH]) were calculated, PHQ-9 depression screen, and condition-specific measures. EQ-5D utility index was estimated from PROMIS-GH. These were summarized across conditions after adjustment for demographics, clinical characteristics, and self-reported condition-specific severity.

RESULTS: There were 133,636 patients included in this analysis (mean age 51.5 [SD ± 18] years, 64% female, 81% White race). Overall adjusted average scores for GPH, GMH, PHQ-9, and EQ-5D were 42.7 ± 5.0, 43.6 ± 5.0, 7.9 ± 3.7, and 0.68 ± 0.11, respectively. Scores were significantly different across condition, with GPH ranging from 39.6 ± 5.5 for back pain to 45.9 ± 3.9 for brain tumor. Patients with brain tumor, back pain, stroke, ALS, and multiple sclerosis had more favorable GMH and PHQ-9 scores, while patients with depression, epilepsy, and dementia had the most affected GMH and PHQ-9 scores. Patients with back pain and headache had the lowest EQ-5D scores (0.63 ± 0.13 and 0.67 ± 0.09), while those with brain tumor had the highest (0.77 ± 0.08).

DISCUSSION: This study provides condition-specific and severity-specific benchmarks for PROMIS-GH and related HRQOL measures that can support interpretation of patient-reported outcomes across neurologic populations. These data inform clinical care, quality measurement, research, and the implementation of the AAN-recommended performance measure.

articles.title: Glove stewardship framework for implementing WHO/CDC guidelines in the post-COVID era: A call for action.
articles.abstract: Basic infection prevention and control practices start with hand hygiene, which remains the cornerstone of infection prevention. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered conventional infection prevention behaviors and practices. Despite the return to prepandemic infection control measures, a persistent gap remains between evidence-based recommendations and clinical practice, characterized by inappropriate or excessive use of gloves. Excessive or unnecessary glove use is associated with reduced hand hygiene adherence, increased cross-contamination, heightened risk of hospital-acquired infections, and substantial financial and environmental burdens. To address these challenges, the authors propose a Glove Stewardship Framework (GSF) designed to promote risk-based glove decision-making, reinforce the central role of hand hygiene, reduce cross-contamination, and mitigate environmental harm. Modeled after antibiotic stewardship programs, the GSF emphasizes leadership commitment, accountability, education, targeted interventions, monitoring, and ethical stewardship. This article discusses a comprehensive, nursing-centered framework that operationalizes World Health Organization and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention glove-use recommendations within postpandemic clinical practice and education. By advancing a culture of conscious glove use grounded in evidence and supported by leadership, the GSF aims to strengthen infection prevention, professional accountability, and sustainability across health care systems.

articles.title: Pitfalls and pearls of geriatric trauma care.
articles.abstract: Geriatric trauma represents a growing public health concern as the population of adults aged 65 years and older continues to expand. Traumatic injury remains the fifth leading cause of death in this age group and is associated with significantly higher morbidity, mortality, and health care costs compared with younger trauma populations. Geriatric physiologic changes, comorbid disease burden, polypharmacy, and altered pharmacokinetics complicate the assessment and management of injured older adults and contribute to frequent undertriage and delayed recognition of life-threatening injury. Low-energy mechanisms, particularly ground-level falls, account for the majority of injuries in this population yet often result in disproportionately severe outcomes. Cognitive impairment, anticoagulant use, frailty, and limited physiologic reserve further increase vulnerability following trauma.This article examines the epidemiology and pathophysiology of geriatric trauma, highlighting common pitfalls in care, including medication-related complications, underrecognition of shock, delirium, elder abuse, and mental health disorders. Evidence-based clinical pearls are presented to guide assessment, resuscitation, and disposition decisions, with emphasis on adjustment for age for trauma activation criteria, early imaging, delirium screening, and interdisciplinary care. Current recommendations from the American College of Surgeons are discussed, including geriatric-specific trauma activation thresholds, frailty assessment, and use of structured screening tools such as the Confusion Assessment Method. The Geriatric 5Ms framework is introduced as a patient-centered approach to clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Outcomes among Pregnant Women with Measles and Their Infants in the United States - Preliminary Analysis, 2025-2026.
articles.abstract: AbstractMeasles virus infection during pregnancy can result in severe maternal illness, adverse pregnancy and infant outcomes, and neonatal complications, including congenital measles. During multiple large outbreaks from January 1, 2025, to September 28, 2026, a total of 112 cases of confirmed measles during pregnancy and 13 cases of congenital measles were reported to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; complications included maternal pneumonia, preterm delivery, and neonatal complications. Almost all pregnant women with measles (98%) had not received measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination before pregnancy or had unknown vaccination status. MMR vaccination before pregnancy and high community MMR vaccination coverage are important to prevent measles and related complications.

articles.title: Stepping up liver care: Rethinking alcohol treatment in chronic liver disease.
A Meta-Research Review of Statistical Practices for Image-Reliant AI Tools Predicting Lung Cancer Outcomes.
articles.abstract: AbstractAI models using medical images are increasingly proposed to support clinical decision-making in lung cancer, motivating assessment of their methodological rigor and transparency. To assess how these models are developed, evaluated, and reported, and to identify gaps in best statistical practices, we conducted a cross-sectional meta-research review of OpenAlex-indexed studies (January 1, 2023, to June 30, 2025) that developed image-based AI tools for lung cancer risk prediction, detection, or prognosis. Thirty-six studies met our inclusion criteria. Convolutional neural networks were used in most studies (27 studies, 75%), and area under the curve (AUC) was the most frequently reported evaluation metric (29 studies, 81%). Although 23 studies (64%) reported some form of uncertainty quantification, most were limited to presenting confidence intervals for global performance metrics (e.g., AUC, sensitivity, and accuracy) rather than individual prediction- or risk-level uncertainty. Common limitations included limited external test set use (14 studies, 39%), insufficient subgroup analyses (10 studies, 28%), and limited adherence to established prediction-model reporting guidelines. Overall, future research should prioritize standardized reporting, use of external test sets, and model performance assessment across clinically relevant subpopulations. The coexistence of increasingly powerful AI-based prediction models with inconsistent study design, evaluation, and reporting practices emphasizes the urgent need to implement more rigorous and transparent methodological standards in this field. (Funded by Yale School of Public Health.).

articles.title: Heart rate variability and calcium economy in sarcoidosis: the role of parathyroid hormone.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcoidosis (SA) dysregulates calcium metabolism, causing relatively suppressed/low normal parathyroid hormone (PTH). Autonomic dysfunction, assessed by heart rate variability (HRV), occurs in SA-related cardiac/neurological involvement. Their relationship in SA remains uncharacterized.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 373 SA patients, having 24-h HRV and calcium measurements. Spearman correlations were computed for 11 HRV indices against 5 calcium parameters (PTH, serum calcium, urinary calcium, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (1,25(OH)2D), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D)). Multivariable linear regression models were constructed, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), cardiac involvement, corticosteroid use, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus.

RESULTS: The short-term fractal scaling exponent of detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA1) (r = -0.202, p = 0.0001, q = 0.005, n = 370), low-frequency (LF) power (r = -0.165, q = 0.027) and the LF-to-high-frequency ratio (LF/HF) (r = -0.140, q = 0.042) were inversely correlated with PTH. DFA2, the long-term fractal scaling exponent, was positively correlated with PTH (r = +0.147, q = 0.032). Urinary calcium was positively correlated with LF power, LF/HF, DFA1, and mean heart rate (HR) (r ≈ 0.23-0.24, all q < 0.05). SD2, a Poincaré-plot index of longer-term HRV, was positively associated with 25(OH)D (r = 0.166, q = 0.027). In multivariable analysis, DFA1 was independently predicted by age, sex, cardiac involvement, and diabetes mellitus. The PTH-DFA1 correlation was numerically larger without than with cardiac involvement (r = -0.228 vs -0.078), but formal tests did not establish a difference (interaction p = 0.608; Fisher's z p = 0.224). Between corticosteroid users and non-users (r = -0.407 vs -0.155), the interaction was nominally significant (p = 0.035), but Fisher's z test was not (p = 0.062). Subgroup analyses are exploratory.

CONCLUSIONS: PTH/urinary calcium associate with fractal and sympathovagal HRV indices in SA. These exploratory findings suggest modest calcium-autonomic associations warranting prospective study.

articles.title: Vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults: prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with certain chronic medical conditions, and immunocompromised patients. RSV can result in acute and longer-term cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity, and declines in physical functioning and quality of life.

AREAS COVERED: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. Robust clinical trial data showed an acceptable safety profile and demonstrated efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in RSV-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)/asthma exacerbations. These findings are reinforced by real-world evidence showing effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations, COPD/asthma exacerbations, and cardiovascular events.

EXPERT OPINION: This emerging evidence supports a broader role of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 beyond preventing RSV-LRTD alone to preserve cardiovascular and respiratory health. RSV vaccination should be considered within an integrated routine care and preventive management strategy for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions, alongside other adult immunizations and health interventions. Addressing implementation barriers for adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and emphasizing its role in maintaining health and independence will be critical to enable widespread uptake and help protect patient health.

articles.title: Analysis of a recent human parvovirus B19 outbreak using a new genomic surveillance system.
articles.abstract: Human parvovirus B19 is the causative agent of various clinical diseases like erythema infectiosum, transient aplastic crisis, fetal hydrops, reactive arthritis, and rarely potentially fatal organ diseases.
