RECENT FINDINGS: This review focuses on the intersections between chronic lung disease and otolaryngology practice, with a particular emphasis on bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), asthma, diffuse lung disease (DLD), and suppurative lung disease. Newer therapies have been recently approved, that have continued to change disease progression and prognosis.

SUMMARY: Chronic lung diseases (CLD) represent a significant source of morbidity across all age groups, with profound implications for both lower and upper airway health. By enhancing awareness of these intersections, ENT surgeons can better support this complex and vulnerable patient population.

articles.title: A plasma proteomic frailty signature for cardiovascular risk stratification: A multi-cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty predicts adverse health outcomes, but its relationship with cardiovascular disease (CVD) requires further validation across diverse populations. The value of a circulating protein signature for cardiovascular risk assessment remains uncertain.

METHODS: We examined frailty-CVD associations in the XiDu2017 cohort (n = 4323) and UK Biobank (UKB; n = 84,276) using logistic and Cox regression, respectively. XiDu longitudinal analyses included 844 participants without baseline CVD. In the UKB proteomic subset, a 20-protein frailty (PF) score was compared with clinical frailty and a model of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: Each higher frailty category was associated with prevalent CVD in XiDu (adjusted odds ratio, 1.120; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.004-1.251). In UKB, frail participants had a higher CVD hazard than robust participants (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.28-1.48). For heart failure, the 5-year area under the curve (AUC) was 0.756 for PF and 0.595 for clinical frailty. Adding PF to conventional risk factors increased the optimism-corrected heart failure AUC by 0.113 (95% CI, 0.077-0.142).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical frailty was associated with cardiovascular outcomes in both cohorts. PF showed incremental discrimination for selected outcomes, particularly heart failure. External validation and evaluation of clinical utility are needed before clinical application.

articles.title: Adiposity and glycemic patterns among adults meeting measured cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic stage 1 criteria: a multicohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline defines cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) stage 1 by excess or dysfunctional adiposity. Whether adiposity and glycemic patterns distinguish subsequent risk is uncertain.

METHODS: Adults aged 45-79 years meeting measured stage 1 criteria were studied in CHARLS and CHNS. Four patterns combined body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, and prediabetes. Modified Poisson models estimated risk ratios (RRs). Progression and hypertension models used censoring weights; cumulative self-reported cardiovascular disease (CVD) models used baseline-covariate imputation. The nonglycemic composite was a key secondary outcome. NHANES assessed reclassification with ancestry-appropriate thresholds and age-sex standardization. Chinese cohorts lacked albuminuria and subclinical CVD assessment.

RESULTS: In CHARLS (model n = 965), adiposity plus prediabetes was associated with metabolic progression versus prediabetes only (RR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.18-1.61). Corresponding RRs were 1.45 (1.21-1.74) for nonglycemic progression and 1.55 (1.21-1.98) for CHNS hypertension. Among 1824 participants, concordant BMI and waist adiposity was associated with cumulative reported CVD through 2020 (RR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.23-2.71). CVD associations attenuated in complete-case models and after additional adjustment for metabolic measures. Standardized NHANES reclassification ranged from 0.8% to 9.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Adiposity and glycemic patterns identified prognostic heterogeneity among adults meeting measured CKM stage 1 criteria, supporting joint assessment of these features.

articles.title: Twenty-five-year imaging follow-up of an untreated giant Spetzler-Martin grade V Brain arteriovenous malformation associated with cerebral infarction and epilepsy.
articles.abstract: Brain arteriovenous malformations (BAVMs) are typically associated with intracranial hemorrhage, whereas ischemic stroke associated with a high-grade BAVM is an exceptionally rare complication. We present the 25-year long-term imaging follow-up of a 39-year-old male with a giant Spetzler-Martin grade V BAVM. Initially diagnosed at age 14 via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) due to a visual deficit, the complex lesion was managed conservatively owing to prohibitive procedural risks. Twenty-five years later, the patient presented with acute left limb weakness and recurrent adult-onset epilepsy. Current diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) mapping demonstrated chronic ischemic changes in the bilateral frontal lobes and a new acute-to-subacute infarction in the left parietal lobe. Concurrent MRA and MRI demonstrated a massive 13.5 × 6.3 cm nidus with prominent vascular flow voids and deep venous involvement. The patient received supportive medical management and antiseizure therapy. Motor function showed near-complete recovery at 3 months, although recurrent minor seizures persisted during longer-term follow-up. This 25-year imaging follow-up documents the long-term imaging follow-up of a giant, untreated Spetzler-Martin grade V BAVM and documents the occurrence of delayed ischemic complications during long-term follow-up of a giant BAVM. In extreme-risk, unruptured cases, conservative management with imaging surveillance is a carefully considered option, though it carries ongoing long-term risks.

articles.title: Assessment of Medication Regimen Complexity and Adherence in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Patients at a Tertiary Care Teaching Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Medication regimen complexity and poor adherence are major barriers to optimal management, yet limited evidence exists in Nepal. This study aimed to assess medication regimen complexity and adherence among COPD patients attending a tertiary care hospital in Nepal.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2023 to May 2024 at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Nepal. A total of 174 COPD patients aged ≥40 years were enrolled using convenience sampling. Medication regimen complexity was assessed using the validated 65-item Medication Regimen Complexity Index (MRCI), and adherence was evaluated with the Nepali version of the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Pearson's chi-square test and binary logistic regression were performed at a 5% level of significance to examine factors associated with medication nonadherence.

RESULTS: Of the total, 46.6% demonstrated suboptimal adherence, strongly associated with smoking (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: 7.5; 95% CI: 2.82-19.90; p < 0.001) and alcohol use (aOR: 3.66; 95% CI: 1.578-8.49; p = 0.003). COPD regimens exhibited higher complexity (mean MRCI: 10.296 ± 5.4) than non-COPD medications (3.66 ± 3.478). High COPD MRCI (aOR: 25.8; 95% CI: 14.7-38.5; p = 0.03) and high patient-level MRCI (aOR: 15.6; 95% CI: 6.7-33.9; p < 0.001) were significant predictors of nonadherence.

CONCLUSION: COPD-specific regimens were found to be more complex, and higher regimen complexity together with lifestyle factors, such as smoking and alcohol consumption, were strong determinants of nonadherence. Simplifying regimens through fixed-dose combinations, pharmacist-led interventions, and behavioral counseling may improve medication adherence and treatment outcomes in COPD patients.

articles.title: Association Between Periodontitis and Ischemic Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease (IHD) is a leading cause of global mortality. This study examined the association between periodontitis severity, graded by clinical attachment loss (CAL), and IHD in a representative sample of US adults.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2014 cycle, including a full-mouth periodontal examination, of participants aged ≥30 years with complete periodontal and IHD data (n = 2807; weighted n ≈ 122,396,066). Periodontal status was classified by maximum interdental CAL, using the severity thresholds of the 2018 classification of periodontal diseases: no-or-initial-attachment loss (CAL ≤2 mm; reference), Stage II periodontitis (CAL 3-4 mm), and Stage III/IV periodontitis (CAL ≥5 mm). IHD was defined as a composite of self-reported coronary heart disease, angina, or heart attack. Weighted prevalence of IHD was computed for each periodontal group, and survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for IHD, adjusting sequentially for demographic characteristics (age, sex, race/ethnicity, and family income), smoking, diabetes, hypertension, and other cardiovascular risk factors.

RESULTS: The weighted prevalence of IHD was 5.71% overall and increased across periodontal groups: 2.45% (no-or-initial-attachment loss), 4.66% (Stage II), and 8.82% (Stage III/IV) (p = 0.0004). In unadjusted models, Stage III/IV periodontitis was associated with higher odds of IHD than no-or-initial-attachment-loss (OR 3.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33-11.07; p = 0.003). After full adjustment, the association was attenuated, but the point estimate remained elevated (OR 1.47; 95% CI 0.40-5.39; p = 0.05). Older age, current smoking, diabetes, hypertension, and self-reported bone loss were independent predictors of IHD.

CONCLUSION: In this nationally representative study, Stage III/IV periodontitis was associated with a higher prevalence of IHD. Although the association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment, the findings suggest a potential link, possibly mediated by shared risk factors and inflammatory pathways.

articles.title: Ambient Air Pollution and Kawasaki Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) is a childhood vasculitis with a multifactorial etiology involving genetic susceptibility and environmental influences. Ambient air pollution has been proposed as a potential environmental trigger, but epidemiological findings have been inconsistent across pollutants, populations, and exposure periods. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the association between ambient air pollution and KD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from database inception through December 29, 2024, for observational studies evaluating associations between ambient air pollutants and KD. Multivariable-adjusted estimates were preferentially used for quantitative synthesis. Hazard ratios and odds ratios were interpreted as relative risks, and estimates were standardized to a 10 µg/m3 increase in pollutant concentration where applicable. Random-effects models were used to obtain pooled relative risks, with heterogeneity assessed using I 2 statistics.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The studies included diverse epidemiological designs and were predominantly conducted in Asian populations, with additional studies from North America and Italy. Across the quantitative synthesis, no statistically significant association was observed between a standardized 10 µg/m3 increase in individual pollutants and KD occurrence. The pooled relative risks were 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.985-1.016) for PM2.5, 1.00 (95% CI, 0.983-1.022) for PM10, 1.008 (95% CI, 0.966-1.051) for SO2, 0.99 (95% CI, 0.989-1.009) for NO2, and 1.013 (95% CI, 0.981-1.046) for O3 and CO. For PM2.5, between-study heterogeneity was moderate (I 2 = 43.8%), whereas Egger's test showed no evidence of significant publication bias (p = 0.2703).

CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant overall association between ambient air pollution and KD. However, associations may vary by pollutant, exposure timing, geographical setting, and meteorological conditions. Future studies should use standardized exposure windows and account for key meteorological factors to clarify these potential context-specific associations.

articles.title: Service Availability and Readiness for Essential Health Services in Somalia: A Narrative Review of Facility Evidence and Health-System Priorities.
articles.abstract: Essential health services are central to universal health coverage; however, nominal service availability does not necessarily indicate that facilities are ready to deliver care safely, continuously and equitably. In Somalia, evidence on service availability and readiness remains dispersed across facility assessments, policy documents, programme reports and peer-reviewed studies, limiting its use for planning and equitable resource allocation. This narrative review synthesizes Somalia-specific evidence on service availability, facility readiness, readiness-related delivery constraints and health-system priorities for strengthening essential health services. Evidence was classified as direct facility-readiness measures, readiness-related delivery-system indicators or coverage, programme-performance and outcome indicators to distinguish structural readiness from indirect signals of delivery-system performance. Available evidence suggests important readiness gaps across emergency and critical care, surgical services, maternal and newborn health, immunization, nutrition, communicable diseases and selected non-communicable disease services. These gaps are reinforced by donor-dependent and geographically uneven financing, fragile supply chains, workforce shortages and maldistribution, weak referral and emergency transport systems, fragmented public, private, NGO and humanitarian service delivery, and limited routine use of facility-assessment data. Rural, displaced, nomadic, pastoralist and conflict-affected populations experience substantial access barriers. Institutionalizing readiness monitoring and linking facility-assessment evidence to planning, budgeting, supervision, supply allocation, donor coordination and accountability could help Somalia move from nominal service availability toward effective, continuous and equitable essential health-service coverage.

articles.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Thyroid Dysfunction Among Clinical Populations in Bangladesh: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Thyroid dysfunction (TD) is a significant endocrine burden with profound implications for systemic health; however, consolidated epidemiological data within the clinical landscape of Bangladesh remain sparse. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence and identify clinical factors associated with TD among Bangladeshi clinical populations using data published between 2010 and 2025. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and PROSPERO registration (CRD42025116168), six electronic databases were searched without language restrictions. Data from clinical populations (aged ≥12 years) were synthesized using a random-effects model. Subgroup analysis and univariable random-effects meta-regression were employed to explore drivers of heterogeneity, whereas publication bias was assessed via Peters' regression test. The pooled prevalence of TD was 23.72% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 17.90-30.72) across clinically heterogeneous populations, with hypothyroidism identified as the predominant abnormality (20.55%) over hyperthyroidism (4.93%). Meta-regression identified clinical profile as the factor most strongly associated with heterogeneity, revealing that patients with metabolic-inflammatory disorders (e.g., diabetes, metabolic syndrome) exhibited a markedly higher prevalence (34.77%) than endocrine-reproductive groups (19.14%). Furthermore, comprehensive biochemical assessments (thyroid-stimulating hormone [TSH] with free hormones) yielded higher prevalence estimates (28.31%) than limited TSH-only testing (18.31%). Peters' regression test showed no significant asymmetry (p = 0.384), though this should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies (k = 8). These results underscore a critical "dual burden" of endocrine and systemic disease in Bangladesh. The high prevalence within metabolic high-risk groups necessitates the integration of routine, comprehensive thyroid screening into standard clinical management protocols to optimize endocrine care and mitigate long-term systemic complications.

articles.title: Spatial and Sociodemographic Distribution of Predicted 10-Year Cardiovascular Disease Risk Among Hypertensive Adults in Bangladesh: Evidence From BDHS 2022.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major public health problem in Bangladesh, especially among adults with hypertension, yet the sociodemographic patterning, wealth-related inequities, and spatial distribution of their predicted CVD risk are poorly understood. Using the 2022 Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey (2544 adults aged ≥18 years; 1412 in the propensity score-matched sample), we estimated predicted (not overserved) 10-year CVD risk among adults with hypertension and examined its sociodemographic correlates, wealth-based inequalities, and geographical clustering. Risk was categorized as low, medium, or high, using a matrix adapted from the World Health Organization/International Society of Hypertension (WHO/ISH) approach, which requires no cholesterol data, and combines hypertension grade, age, sex, recent tobacco use (within 30 min), obesity, and diabetes. Analyses included descriptive and bivariate tests, ordered logistic regression, propensity score matching to assess covariate imbalance across wealth groups, and Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi* spatial analyses. Overall, 44.7% had low, 18.7% medium, and 36.6% high predicted risk. Older age, female sex, overweight/obesity, recent tobacco use, and higher household wealth were associated with higher predicted risk, although some associations partly reflect the classification rules rather than true differences in risk. In the matched sample, nonpoor participants were slightly more likely than poor participants to have elevated predicted risk (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 1.25; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-1.57), with a stronger association among those with secondary or higher education (AOR: 1.97; 95% CI: 1.09-3.56). Excluding adults under 35 years left most associations and the wealth-education interaction unchanged but altered the education and age effects. Spatial autocorrelation was significant (Global Moran's I = 0.133, p = 0.027), with hotspots in Comilla, Dhaka, Narayanganj, and Narsingdi. These findings concern predicted risk rather than observed cardiovascular events and may support integrating absolute CVD risk assessment into primary care and geographically targeted prevention for hypertensive adults in Bangladesh.

articles.title: Trends in acute myocardial infarction mortality with diabetes mellitus as a contributing cause of death in the United States, 1999-2025, with forecasts through 2030 and exploratory projections for 2031-2040.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major risk factor for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with increased mortality. Despite substantial advances in the management of both conditions, the population-level mortality burden involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate national trends and disparities in mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025 using CDC WONDER data, forecasts were generated through 2030, with exploratory projections extending through 2040, stratified by DM type, age, sex, and race and ethnicity.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of U.S. national mortality data from 1999 to 2025 was conducted to identify deaths among adults aged ≥ 25 years in which AMI; ICD-10 code I21 was the underlying cause and DM; ICD-10 codes E10-E14 was a contributing cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and crude mortality rates (CMRs) were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using joinpoint regression to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Time-series methods were used to forecast mortality through 2030, with exploratory projections through 2040 .

RESULTS: Trend analyses were conducted using observed mortality data from 1999 to 2025, whereas projections extended from 2026 to 2040. A total of 762,802 deaths were attributed to AMI, with DM documented as a contributing cause, among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2025. Overall mortality significantly declined (AAMR: 18.9 to 9.16; AAPC: -3.05; 95% CI: -3.3 to -2.9; P < 0.001). Males showed higher AAMRs (23.32 in 1999 to 12.72 in 2025) when compared to females (15.74 to 6.2). Older adults aged ≥ 65 years carried the greatest mortality burden, with CMR decreasing from 72.9 in 1999 to 32.4 in 2025. NH Blacks had the highest AAMR (29.95 to 12.68). Forecasts projected a decline in overall AAMR from 8.17 in 2026 to 6.72 in 2030. Exploratory projections suggested a further decline to 3.08 by 2040, although substantial uncertainty surrounded these long-term estimates. The AAMR for deaths involving AMI as the underlying cause and T2DM as a contributing cause increased from 3.34 in 1999 to 4.15 in 2025, whereas the corresponding AAMR for T1DM decreased from 1.90 to 0.23.

CONCLUSION: Mortality involving AMI as the underlying cause and DM as a contributing cause has significantly declined and is projected to continue declining through 2040. Disparities among males, NH Blacks and older adults require refined strategies to improve outcomes.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02124-x.

articles.title: Cold-Inducible RNA-Binding Protein Alleviates Hypertensive Renal Injury Through the KEAP1-NRF2 Pathway.
articles.abstract: Angiotensin II (Ang II) plays crucial roles in renal dysfunction, fibrotic changes, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. CIRBP, a cold-inducible RNA-binding protein, functions to maintain cellular homeostasis. However, its role in renal damage elicited by Ang II remains unclear. Here, we investigated the mechanisms through which Cirbp overexpression alleviates renal damage caused by Ang II, and Cirbp deletion induces basal renal injury. Transcriptomic analysis identified the involvement of Cirbp in hypertension-related renal injury. Across the animal and cell models, Cirbp overexpression attenuated Ang II-induced renal dysfunction, fibrosis, apoptosis, and inflammation, whereas Cirbp deficiency aggravated basal injury and increased renal susceptibility to injury. CIRBP activated the KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway to mitigate redox stress. This renoprotective effect was reversed following the application of the NRF2 inhibitor ML385, but was resumed by the NRF2 agonist RA839. Together, CIRBP modulates redox imbalance during Ang II-mediated renal damage through KEAP1-NRF2 signaling.

articles.title: Cardiovascular diseases and guideline-directed medical therapy in low socio-economic status patients: A single center experience.
articles.journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with a low socio-economic status (SES) exhibit high cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) and a high burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but they are under-recognized in clinical practice. In this study, we explored CVRFs and CVD in low-SES patients, and estimated the guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) prevalence for each CVD.

METHODS: Consecutive individuals with low-SES who attended the primary care and cardiology clinics within a single charitable medical center between 2024 and 2025 were retrospectively recruited. Data on SES, symptoms, CVRFs, CVDs, and treatment strategies were collected and analyzed descriptively. GDMT comprised class I medications reported by patients and documented in their medical records at the time of data collection for each CVD.

RESULTS: Among the 2374 patients, the mean age was 58.7 ± 6 years (57.2% females). Common CVRFs included hypertension (39.5%), diabetes (28.6%), and hyperlipidemia (27.4%). Common CVDs included coronary artery disease (CAD) (12.4%), heart failure (HF) (6%), and atrial fibrillation (AF) (1.7%) (mean ages: 55.79, 63.12, and 62.4 years, respectively). CAD patients had a high prevalence of acute coronary syndrome (74.2%), with most managed noninvasively (87%), but 38.5% received GDMT. HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) exceeded HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) (63.6% vs. 32.8%). Prevalent HF causes included CAD, hypertension, and valvular disease (33.6%, 27.3%, and 26.6%, respectively). GDMT rates for HFrEF and HFpEF were 18.7% and 34%, respectively. The mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 3.5 for AF patients, with 42.8% on GDMT (78% on warfarin).

CONCLUSIONS: Low-SES patients had a high prevalence of CVRF, where CAD, HF, and AF were most common. The patients were relatively young and managed conservatively, but GDMT rates were low. These findings may guide policymakers to improve cardiovascular care in low-SES individuals.

articles.title: Stem cells for hepatic regeneration: Evaluating mechanisms, sources, and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract: Despite rapid advances in regenerative medicine, the clinical translation of stem cell-based therapies for end-stage liver disease remains limited. These approaches seek to promote hepatic repair through cell replacement, paracrine signaling, and immunomodulation, but differ substantially in their mechanisms, functional capabilities, and translational readiness. The distinctive contribution of this review is a mechanism-based and translation-oriented framework that links the biological properties of different stem-cell sources to the requirements for clinical application. We critically compare mesenchymal stem cells, embryonic stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells, hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, and liver-resident progenitors according to their predominant regenerative mechanisms, differentiation capacity, immunogenicity, safety, manufacturing feasibility, and clinical evidence. Particular attention is given to distinguishing direct hepatocyte replacement from paracrine support and stimulation of endogenous repair, while separating preclinical findings from evidence obtained in human studies. We also examine MSC-derived extracellular vesicles as an emerging cell-free approach and assess how organoid-based differentiation, three-dimensional encapsulation, and scalable bioreactor systems may address limitations in hepatocyte maturation and functional stability. Importantly, hepatocyte-marker expression is distinguished from mature metabolic function when evaluating the therapeutic potential of stem-cell-derived hepatic cells. By integrating these biological and engineering considerations with product heterogeneity, tumorigenic risk, manufacturing reproducibility, and the need for validated, mechanism-linked potency assays, this review identifies the principal barriers to clinical translation. Rather than providing a descriptive catalog of therapeutic platforms, it offers a comparative framework for evaluating how regenerative mechanisms, functional maturity, and manufacturing constraints shape the clinical readiness of stem cell-based strategies for hepatic regeneration.

articles.title: A rare neurovascular complication of Lemierre syndrome: Skull base pachymeningitis and reversible inflammatory stenosis of the petrous-cavernous internal carotid artery.
articles.abstract: Lemierre syndrome is a septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein that follows an oropharyngeal infection, most often caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum. Its intracranial complications are predominantly venous; arterial involvement is uncommon and its nature is rarely characterized on imaging. We report the case of a 22-year-old woman admitted with fever, headache, left cervical pain and vomiting 1 week after an acute pharyngitis treated with azithromycin. Blood cultures grew F necrophorum, and contrast-enhanced cervical computed tomography showed thrombosis of the left internal jugular vein extending to the jugular bulb. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) on day 3 showed skull base pachymeningitis with patent dural sinuses. On day 7, the patient developed raised intracranial pressure and diplopia. Time-of-flight angiography showed segmental narrowing of the petrous and cavernous segments of the left internal carotid artery, and contrast-enhanced black-blood 3D T1-weighted fast spin-echo images showed circumferential thickening and enhancement of its wall, absent before contrast and on the contralateral side, consistent with an inflammatory arteritis contiguous to the infected jugular foramen; the dural sinuses remained patent. Treatment combined 21 days of intravenous antibiotic therapy active against anaerobes, therapeutic anticoagulation and acetazolamide. On day 15, MRI with the same sequences showed resolution of the mural enhancement, a normal arterial caliber, regression of the pachymeningitis and partial regression of the jugular thrombosis, and the patient had fully recovered by day 28. This case illustrates how vessel wall MRI, even with a routine sequence interpreted against internal controls, can characterize arterial involvement in Lemierre syndrome and document its reversibility.

articles.title: Multi-Analytical Characterization and Taxonomic Distinction of Australian Plant Exudates.
articles.abstract: Plant exudates have been used worldwide for millennia in broad applications due to their unique physicochemical properties. Indigenous Australians have used exudates in long-standing cultural and technical practices, including hafting adhesives and paint binders. Chemical characterization and botanical identification can provide important insight into the origin, properties, and usage of exudate materials from the archaeological past to the present. However, Australian exudates and cultural heritage materials have been far less examined compared to European, Asian, and North African counterparts. Here, we report combined Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, X-ray Raman scattering (XRS) spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, and pyrolysis gas chromatography mass spectrometry (py-GC-MS) analyses for atomic- to molecular-level characterization of over 20 genera of Australian exudates. This research contributes to fundamental understanding of the chemistry of exudates that drives their usage as natural binders. Integration of all four techniques and multivariate statistics reveals chemical differences at both the genus and species level. We establish correlations between taxonomic groupings and chemical composition to identify key features for distinction of exudates. Our multi-analytical approach provides new insight into the unique chemistry of less well-studied Australian exudates, with impact on the characterization of exudates in important cultural and archaeological materials worldwide.

articles.title: Immunogenicity of the 9-Valent Human Papillomavirus Vaccine in Occupationally-Exposed Adults.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection and has a well-established role in the pathogenesis of recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC). HPV DNA is detectable in surgical smoke, and case reports have linked occupational exposure to laryngeal papillomatosis in healthcare workers. In 2026 a joint European Laryngological Society/Union of European Phoniatricians Delphi consensus agreed that occupational exposure is plausible and that vaccination should be offered to workers at risk, but stronger recommendations were not issued due to absence of transmission and immunogenicity data. Immunogenicity data in adults over 26-particularly men-remain minimal in the literature.

METHODS: In a single-center prospective study, 9-valent HPV vaccine naïve operating room staff and surgeons within otolaryngology, general surgery, urology, and obstetrics-gynecology aged 27-69 were recruited to receive the standard three-dose 9-valent vaccine. Antibody titers for HPV 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58 were measured at baseline (Month 0) and after the completion of their vaccine series (Month 7).

RESULTS: Of 33 enrolled adults, 21 completed the study (18 male, 3 female; mean age 36 years, range 27-61; 4 aged > 45 years). At Month 7, all 21 seroconverted for all nine types of HPV (100% seroconversion).

CONCLUSION: The 9-valent HPV vaccine produced 100% seroconversion in a predominantly older, male, occupationally-exposed cohort that has been under-represented in prior research. This data suggests that offering vaccination to at-risk workers, addressing the immunogenicity gap identified by the ELS/UEP consensus.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 3.

articles.title: Impact of BMI on Ramadan fasting in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus: Insights from the DaR Global Surveys 2020-2022.
articles.journal: Journal of Taibah University Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fasting during the holy month of Ramadan is a central religious practice for Muslims worldwide, including individuals living with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Managing diabetes during prolonged fasting presents significant clinical challenges, particularly balancing glycemic control and preventing complications such as hypoglycemia. The body mass index (BMI) is a widely used surrogate marker for metabolic status and may significantly influence the physiological response and tolerance to fasting in individuals with T2DM. However, data are limited regarding the relationship between BMI and fasting experiences among diabetic individuals in diverse Muslim-majority populations. This study used data from the Diabetes and Ramadan (DaR) Global Survey, conducted via SurveyMonkey, to examine the associations between BMI and fasting-related outcomes among adults with T2DM in Muslim-majority countries. The findings may support more personalized risk stratification and clinical guidance for safe fasting practices in this population.

METHODS: Using a specifically designed SurveyMonkey questionnaire, Muslim individuals with T2DM were surveyed in several countries in different geographical regions and stratified by BMI. Basic demographic, clinical, and fasting-related data were collected and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics to explore differences between subgroups.

RESULTS: Among 6530 participants, 42.4% were overweight and 37.7% were obese, and obesity was more prevalent in females and the Gulf region. Individuals with obesity were younger and had a slightly longer duration of diabetes. Glycemic control (mean HbA1c ∼ 8.2-8.4%) was similar among BMI groups. Obesity was associated with higher systolic blood pressure, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and microalbuminuria. Pharmacologic management patterns varied little, although use of GLP-1 receptor agonists was greater among individuals with obesity, and Ramadan fasting intentions and practices remained consistent across BMI groups. Self-reported hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia rates were comparable, although overweight participants had higher rates of emergency visits (p = 0.01). Most participants received Ramadan-specific diabetes education, but self-monitoring of blood glucose adherence varied.

CONCLUSION: Individuals with T2DM in all BMI categories were able to fast safely during Ramadan, with no significant differences in fasting behavior or adverse events. Despite a higher burden of cardiometabolic comorbidities among obese participants, glycemic control and complication rates during fasting were comparable. These findings highlight the importance of structured education and individualized care for supporting safe fasting among people with diabetes, regardless of BMI.

articles.title: Regional and national variation in donor and recipient characteristics, transplant practice, and outcomes after liver transplantation (the IMPROVEMENT collaborative): a multicentre cohort study.
authors: de Fatima Santana Ferreira Boin I
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outcome variability in liver transplantation remains globally driven by differences in donor-recipient characteristics and in risk-mitigation strategies. Prediction models lack geographic balance and fail to account for current disease classification and advanced organ preservation methods. The IMPROVEMENT study (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05289609) aimed to characterise the donor-recipient risks and to develop and validate global prognostic algorithms (mortality and complication rate).

METHODS: This non-competitive, international, cohort study involved 61 centres across Europe, Asia, North and South America, Oceania. Centres provided 83 balanced data series. 5218 patients were enroled in retrospective (2017-2019) and/or prospective (2022-2023) cohorts to avoid COVID-19 confounding. A four-step analytical hierarchy process (world maps, radar graphs, donor versus recipient risk plot, and mixed-effects generalised models) enables visualisation of risk propensity, namely, "aggressiveness", and risk-mitigation balance, namely "coverage adequacy". Outcome measures were 90-, 365-, and 730-day mortality and high complication rates.

FINDINGS: Overall survival rates at 90 days, 1 year and 5 years were 93, 90 and 80, respectively. Predictors of mortality included recipient age, CAD, pre-operative complex portal thrombosis, preoperative ventilatory life support, MASLD, MELD 3.0 > 30, packed red blood transfusions (PRBC), and cold ischaemia time ≥360 min. The high complication rate resulted dependent from preoperative ventilatory life support, complex portal thrombosis, TIPS and PRBC. Notably, donor factors had a low impact on outcomes, reflecting successful donor-recipient matching and new graft perfusion modalities. Transplant at high-volume centres (>65 transplants/year) was a significant protective factor (mortality and complication rates). C-statistics of 90-day mortality and high complication rate models were 0.78 and 0.77, respectively.

INTERPRETATION: The IMPROVEMENT study shows that, unlike before, recipient and system-level factors now appear to account for the largest proportion of outcome variability. Implementing risk-mitigation strategies can offset high-risk profiles. These findings provide a robust framework for equitable health resource allocation and clinical decision-making worldwide.

FUNDING: Italian Ministry of Health #RF-2021-12372422 grant.

articles.title: Health-care burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in European tertiary-care outpatient clinics (CONSTANS): a prospective multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite modeling-based epidemiological studies of MASLD, precise estimates of the prevalence and health-care resource utilization in outpatient clinical practice are unknown. We assessed, in a real-life setting, the prevalence of suspected/confirmed MASLD and described health-care resource utilization.

METHODS: A prospective, observational study of patients attending the outpatient hepato-gastroenterology clinics of eight European tertiary care centers during three months. Follow-up data of patients with suspected/confirmed MASLD were recorded 12 months after the screening visit: final diagnosis, disease stage, diagnostic work-up and the use of health-care resources.

FINDINGS: 5240 outpatients from Germany, France, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Spain and Slovakia were screened. The main reasons for visit were: chronic viral hepatitis, 33.4% (1749/5240), miscellaneous hepatobiliary conditions including neoplasms, 32.9% (1725/5240) and known/suspected MASLD, 24.7% (1293/5240) (pooled prevalence of 26.1% (95% CI: 19.1-34.7)). 1134 suspected/confirmed MASLD patients were included, the diagnosis was confirmed in 80.2% (909/1134). Significant fibrosis was documented in 22.7% (257/1134) and cirrhosis (including burn-out MASLD) in 21.3% (241/1134). Procedures performed differed between countries, overall 66.4% (753/1134) had imaging studies, 65.3% (740/1134) non-invasive fibrosis tests, 20.4% (231/1134) liver biopsy, while referral for further cardiometabolic assessment or therapy was minimal (144/1134, 15.8%). The cost of all procedures and visits was in the range of that recommended for exploring hepatitis C before treatment, although highly variable between countries.

INTERPRETATION: MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment.

FUNDING: IMI2-Grant Agreement 777377-LITMUS.

articles.title: Development and External Validation of an Updated Nomogram Including Both MRI and Local PSMA PET/CT Information for the Prediction of Side-specific Extraprostatic Extension in Patients Treated with Radical Prostatectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The predictive value of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for extraprostatic extension (EPE) in prostate cancer remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We assessed whether adding PSMA PET/CT to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and clinical factors improves side-specific EPE prediction.

METHODS: Patients undergoing PSMA PET/CT and MRI before radical prostatectomy were analysed retrospectively. The endpoint was side-specific EPE (≥pT3a). Predictors were selected by backward elimination, and the final nomogram was fitted using generalised estimating equations to account for clustering of lobes within patients. Discrimination, calibration, and net benefit were assessed, with external validation in an independent single-centre cohort.

RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Development and validation cohorts included 801 and 287 lobes. The final model comprised prostate-specific antigen density (odds ratio [OR] 1.54 [95% confidence interval {CI} 0.94-2.50]; biopsy International Society of Urological Pathologists grade group (2 vs benign/1: OR 2.01 [95% CI 1.27-3.19]; 3 vs benign/1: OR 3.82 [95% CI 2.30-6.35]; 4 vs benign/1: OR 2.50 [95% CI 1.54-4.08]; 5 vs benign/1: OR 4.05 [95% CI 2.18-7.53]), MRI T-stage (organ-confined with a lesion [OC] vs organ-confined with no lesion [NL]: OR 1.31 [95% CI 0.86-1.99]; EPE vs NL: OR 4.11 [95% CI 2.56-6.60]), PSMA T-stage (OC vs NL: OR 1.67 [95% CI 1.07-2.61]; EPE vs NL: OR 2.59 [95% CI 1.49-4.49]), PSMAtotal (OR 1.72 [95% CI 1.33-2.23]). In development, the PSMA-MRI nomogram showed superior discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.80 vs 0.71, p < 0.001). On validation, the updated model demonstrated discrimination comparable to the reference model (AUC 0.85 vs 0.86, p = 0.9), with minor risk overestimation and similar net clinical benefit. Limitations include a relatively small validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: The PSMA-MRI nomogram appeared to outperform the MRI-only model in development, but this was not confirmed in validation, indicating limited, context-dependent incremental value.

articles.title: Erratum to "Regulatory roles and translational potential of the Kruppel-like factor family in liver disease" [iLIVER 5 (2026) 100252].

articles.title: Effectiveness of incretin receptor agonists compared to metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy: a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Lipodystrophy syndromes are rare disorders of abnormal fat distribution and metabolic disease. The only approved therapy for generalized lipodystrophy is recombinant leptin (metreleptin), which is not approved for partial lipodystrophy. Recent data suggest efficacy of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) dual agonists (collectively referred to as incretins) to treat complications of lipodystrophy.

OBJECTIVE: To compare metabolic outcomes of incretin therapies vs metreleptin in partial lipodystrophy.

DESIGN: Retrospective review of patients who received metreleptin as part of a clinical trial and incretins during routine care under a natural history study.

SETTING: NIH Clinical Center.

PATIENTS: Twelve female patients with partial lipodystrophy, aged 16-85 years. All but 1 patient had diabetes.

INTERVENTION: Eleven patients with partial lipodystrophy were treated with metreleptin (mean duration 104 ± 38 months) before switching to incretin therapy (duration 32 ± 13 months). A twelfth patient took metreleptin and an incretin concurrently.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Outcome measures included hemoglobin A1c, insulin dose, Matsuda index, insulinogenic index, disposition index, fasting glucose and insulin, homeostatic model of beta cell function (HOMA-B), homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), weight, lipids, liver elastography, and liver steatosis.

RESULTS: Hemoglobin A1c was significantly lower during incretin vs metreleptin treatment (mean difference -1.1 ± 0.4%, range -4.75% to -0.1%, P = .005), associated with modest weight reduction (mean difference -1.5 ± 3.9 kg, range -10.4 to 3 kg, P = .046). Most other metabolic parameters did not differ significantly between treatment periods.

CONCLUSION: In patients with partial lipodystrophy, incretins may provide better diabetes control than metreleptin, with comparable control of other metabolic parameters.

articles.title: Subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by a paradoxical septic embolism from pacemaker lead infection: A case report.
articles.abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage resulting from a paradoxical septic embolism associated with right-sided cardiac infection has not been previously reported. An 85-year-old woman with a history of aortic valve replacement and right ventricular pacemaker implantation 7 years earlier presented with sudden-onset left upper limb weakness and a small subarachnoid hemorrhage over the right frontal convexity. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a small aneurysm in the distal right middle cerebral artery. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed vegetation on the right ventricular pacemaker lead, and blood cultures showed growth of Listeria monocytogenes. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale without evidence of infection in the left cardiac chambers or bioprosthetic aortic valve. The patient was diagnosed with subarachnoid hemorrhage due to the rupture of an infectious intracranial aneurysm, presumably caused by a paradoxical septic embolism originating from the pacemaker lead vegetation. After antibiotic therapy, follow-up transthoracic echocardiography revealed complete resolution of the lead vegetation. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of subarachnoid hemorrhage resulting from a presumed paradoxical septic embolism associated with a pacemaker lead infection.

articles.title: Long non-coding RNAs in monocyte/macrophage-mediated immune dysregulation and organ injury in sepsis: mechanistic insights and therapeutic potential.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction characterized by a dysregulated host response that oscillates between hyperinflammation and immunosuppression. Monocytes and macrophages are pivotal players in the immunopathogenesis of sepsis, driving both the initial cytokine storm and the subsequent state of immunosuppression. There remains an urgent need for new therapeutic approaches that effectively target monocytes and macrophages. As some of the most promising targets for RNA therapeutics (RNATx), which regulate molecular networks in a cell type-restricted manner, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as critical regulators of monocyte and macrophage functions, influencing their polarization and alterations during sepsis. This review systematically synthesizes current knowledge on how lncRNAs regulate the two immune states of sepsis-hyperinflammation and immunosuppression-in these monocytes and macrophages. We also examine the organ-specific effects of lncRNA-mediated macrophage dysfunction in sepsis-induced lung, liver, kidney, cardiac, and brain injury. By clarifying the molecular mechanisms of lncRNA action, we discuss their potential as therapeutic targets, providing insight into novel precision medicine strategies for sepsis management.

articles.title: Helicobacter pylori, Betel Quid Chewing, and Endoscopic Pathology in Dyspeptic Patients: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and betel quid (BQ) chewing are both highly prevalent in South Asia and are independently implicated in upper gastrointestinal mucosal injury, yet their joint contribution to endoscopic pathology in dyspeptic patients is poorly characterised. We aimed to describe the exposure profile of dyspeptic patients with and without endoscopic pathology, quantify the individual and joint associations of H. pylori and BQ use with pathology and explore trends with BQ exposure.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional analytical study, 211 consecutive dyspeptic patients attending a tertiary gastroenterology department were classified as having endoscopic pathology (Group A, n = 141) or a normal endoscopic examination (Group B, n = 70). H. pylori status, BQ exposure (including a cumulative 'BQ-Quid-Years' index), and body mass index (BMI) were recorded, and multivariable logistic regression, additive-interaction analysis and dose-response modelling were performed.

RESULTS: Group A patients were older (median 40 vs. 31 years, p = 0.009) and more often male (58.2% vs. 41.4%, p = 0.039) than Group B. Pathology prevalence rose stepwise from 52.2% in patients negative for both H. pylori and BQ use to 72.5% in patients positive for both (trend p = 0.076). The relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) showed no clear evidence of departure from additivity (-0.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] -1.14 to 0.39), although the wide interval does not exclude synergistic or sub-additive effects. After multivariable adjustment, male sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.01, 95% CI 1.50-6.04, p = 0.002) and, more modestly, age (aOR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.05, p = 0.039) were independently associated with pathology; H. pylori (aOR 1.38, p = 0.353) and BQ use (aOR 1.66, p = 0.219) showed positive but non-significant associations.

CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was the most robust, independently associated correlate of endoscopic pathology in dyspeptic patients, and age showed a more modest, independent association.

articles.title: Serial metabolic profiling and liver transplantation in concurrent maple syrup urine disease and type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Maple syrup urine disease (MSUD) and type 1 diabetes (T1D) require careful attention to dietary composition and predispose to ketoacidosis. The co-occurrence of these metabolic disorders therefore compounds these challenges. Here, we present a 29-year-old man with prenatally diagnosed MSUD and childhood-onset T1D who, despite extreme metabolic vulnerability, did well until his mid-20s, when he was admitted to the hospital 8 times for metabolic decompensation, with the latter 7 times occurring within a 12-month period. Most laboratory evaluations were suggestive of MSUD crisis rather than diabetic ketoacidosis. Ultimately, the patient underwent liver transplantation for definitive treatment of MSUD. The case illustrates the complexity of comanaging T1D with an inborn error of metabolism requiring dietary modification that challenges glycemic management.

articles.title: Delayed recognition of primary thyroid lymphoma with progressive thyroid enlargement and cardiopulmonary symptoms.
articles.abstract: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare thyroid malignancy that may present with respiratory symptoms overlapping with cardiopulmonary disease, contributing to delayed diagnosis. We report a 78-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic thyroiditis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, and prior lung cancer whose worsening dyspnea was repeatedly attributed to underlying cardiopulmonary conditions. She subsequently developed dysphonia and dysphagia with a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass requiring tracheostomy for airway protection. Prior computed tomography imaging obtained during multiple evaluations for cardiopulmonary symptoms incidentally demonstrated subtle thyroid enlargement with progressive interval growth on retrospective review. Core biopsy confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, and staging established stage IIIE disease. Given her age and comorbidities, a dose-reduced regimen of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was initiated. Despite treatment, her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she died shortly thereafter. This case underscores how overlapping comorbidities can obscure PTL presentation until advanced airway compromise develops. In patients with persistent respiratory symptoms despite appropriate cardiopulmonary management, careful review of prior imaging is critical because subtle thyroid enlargement may otherwise be overlooked.

articles.title: Rethinking hypertension in the brain: from blood pressure control to temporal blood pressure stability-a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporal blood pressure variability (BPV) may contribute to cerebrovascular injury beyond mean blood pressure (BP), yet the mechanisms linking antihypertensive treatment patterns to temporal BP instability remain incompletely understood. This scoping review synthesised evidence linking treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants of BP control, temporal BPV, and cerebrovascular vulnerability.

METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched for studies evaluating antihypertensive medication adherence, pharmacodynamic persistence, BPV, and cerebrovascular outcomes. Data were charted using a standardised form and synthesised narratively according to predefined thematic domains.

RESULTS: The available evidence suggests that inconsistent antihypertensive exposure and reduced pharmacodynamic persistence may contribute to increased temporal BPV. Generally BP fluctuations are associated with cerebral small vessel disease, white matter injury, vascular cognitive impairment, and other manifestations of cerebrovascular vulnerability independent of mean BP. This review investigates the relationship between treatment instability, pharmacodynamic determinants, and temporal BPV and proposes a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework to facilitate future individualised risk stratification and guide prospective investigation.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports expanding hypertension management beyond achieving mean BP targets to include optimisation of temporal BP stability. Recognising treatment persistence and pharmacodynamic coverage as determinants of BP stability provides a clinically relevant framework for improving cerebrovascular protection and individualised risk assessment. These findings support consideration of temporal BP stability as a potential complementary dimension of hypertension management for preventing chronic cerebrovascular injury and vascular cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Functional involvement of AMPK in Lumpy skin disease virus replication and associated cellular stress responses.
articles.abstract: Lumpy skin disease virus (LSDV) infection induces extensive cellular stress responses and metabolic reprogramming in host cells. However, the regulatory mechanisms linking these changes to viral replication remain unclear. In this study, MAC-T cells were used as an in vitro infection model to investigate LSDV-induced cellular stress responses and their impact on viral replication. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that LSDV infection activated pathways associated with energy stress, oxidative stress, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, suggesting disruption of cellular energy homeostasis and redox balance. Transmission electron microscopy further demonstrated mitochondrial structural damage in infected cells. Subsequent analyses showed that the ATP/AMP ratio and lactate metabolism decreased during infection, accompanied by elevated mitochondrial calcium levels and excessive reactive oxygen species accumulation. Mechanistically, LSDV infection activated the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4-CHOP and IRE1α-JNK-BECN1 pathways, indicating induction of ER stress-related signaling. Given the role of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) as a central metabolic stress sensor, we further examined its function during LSDV infection. LSDV infection enhanced AMPK activation, as evidenced by increased phosphorylation of Thr172. Inhibition of energy stress, oxidative stress, or ER stress reduced AMPK phosphorylation to varying degrees, suggesting that multiple stress responses collectively contribute to AMPK activation. Furthermore, AMPK inhibition impaired LSDV replication, while downstream analysis revealed that AMPK activation promotes autophagosome formation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that LSDV-induced cellular stress responses activate AMPK signaling to facilitate viral replication, providing new insights into host metabolic regulation and identifying AMPK as a potential antiviral target.

articles.title: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy-related physiologic and metabolic changes influence drug exposure and response. Yet therapeutic decisions often lack individualized biologic guidance. Obstetric pharmacometabolomics uses endogenous metabolic signatures to investigate and potentially predict and monitor drug response in pregnancy.

AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception through October 12, 2026, using terms related to metabolomics, pharmacometabolomics, medication exposure, treatment response, maternal-placental-fetal metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and obstetric medications. Human pregnancy studies, longitudinal investigations, drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistic preclinical studies were prioritized. This review examines pregnancy-specific metabolic adaptations, analytical approaches, and potential applications involving aspirin, antihypertensives, antidiabetic therapies, antiretrovirals, antimicrobials, corticosteroids, and psychiatric medications. It also considers pharmacometabolic approaches to preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, fetal growth disorders, obesity, and HIV-associated pregnancy.

EXPERT OPINION: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics offers a promising framework for individualized therapeutics, but clinical implementation requires longitudinal studies, standardized biospecimen collection, rigorous exposure assessment, validated biomarkers, and diverse populations. Integration with pharmacogenomics, pharmacomicrobiomics, pharmacoproteomics, and model-informed drug development can improve therapeutic precision, provided that clinical utility is demonstrated.

articles.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome modulates HPV genotype-specific clearance/persistence: role of bacterial dysbiosis in cervical carcinogenesis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study focuses on the distinct epidemiological features of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes in Asian populations: HPV52/56/58 show uniquely high prevalence and strong correlation with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, but their detection rates drop sharply in invasive cervical cancer, a pattern clearly different from the persistent dominance of HPV16/18 throughout malignant progression.

METHODS: To further elucidate the potential host-microbe interactions underlying these epidemiological observations, we integrated a 16S rRNA-sequenced cross-sectional discovery cohort and an independent longitudinal validation cohort from a Chinese population, with strict experimental quality control throughout the workflow.

RESULT: The preliminary analytical results demonstrate that a Lactobacillus-dominant cervicovaginal microbiome (CVM) is significantly and positively associated with HPV viral clearance, while enriched abundance of Gardnerella, Saccharofermentans and Atopobium exhibits a robust correlation with persistent HPV52/56/58 infection. Three undercharacterized microbial taxa-Chryseobacterium, Sphingobacterium and Enhydrobacter are closely linked to sustained HPV16/18 prevalence across advanced disease stages, and show negative correlation with the above obligate anaerobes, which aligns with the sharp decline of HPV52/56/58 in tumor tissues. A hormone-linked Chryseobacterium enrichment were also identified, a taxon with previously reported progesterone-degrading functional properties.

CONCLUSION: While further longitudinal studies are required to establish causal relationships, our results indicate that CVM dysbiosis may modulate the natural history of these high-burden HPV genotypes, and provide a foundational rationale for subsequent development of genotype-specific, microbiota-targeted cervical disease intervention strategies.

articles.title: Emodin ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy by regulating mitochondrial dynamics of fission and fusion and ferroptosis through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway.
articles.abstract: Emodin, a natural anthraquinone with known antioxidant properties, has not been fully investigated in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), a condition marked by oxidative stress, ferroptosis and metabolic disturbance, and lacking specific therapies. A DCM model was induced by streptozotocin and a high‑fat diet. Cardiac function after emodin treatment was assessed via echocardiography, while myocardial injury, fibrosis and myocardial iron concentration were evaluated histologically. Mitochondrial fission‑fusion dynamics were examined using transmission electron microscopy and confocal imaging. In vitro functional rescue experiments using Ferrostatin‑1 and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) knockdown via small interfering RNA or AAV9 was performed to determine its role in emodin‑regulated ferroptosis, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dynamics and Nrf2 signaling. Emodin improved left ventricular systolic function, attenuated metabolic disorders, reduced myocardial iron concentration and fibrosis, and suppressed excessive mitochondrial fission and lipid peroxidation in DCM mice. These effects were largely reversed by AHR knockdown. Mechanistically, emodin promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation and upregulated antioxidant molecules, while AHR silencing abrogated these protective effects, thereby exacerbating ferroptosis and mitochondrial dynamic imbalance. In conclusion, emodin protects against high glucose‑induced cardiac injury and improves mitochondrial function by limiting ferroptosis and restoring mitochondrial fission‑fusion homeostasis, effects that are mediated through the AHR‑Nrf2 pathway. These findings suggest emodin and the AHR‑Nrf2 axis as potential therapeutic targets for DCM.

articles.title: Elabela in pregnancy: Physiology, associated disorders and translational perspectives (Review).
articles.abstract: Elabela (ELA) has emerged as a critical regulator of reproductive success, signaling through the cognate apelin receptor (APJ) (encoded by the APLNR gene) to orchestrate embryonic development and placental function. The present narrative review summarizes evidence spanning from molecular mechanisms to clinical phenotypes, evaluating the role of ELA in both physiological pregnancy and major complications, including preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction and gestational diabetes, as well as emerging associations with placental disorders and early pregnancy loss. The present review addresses three key challenges: i) The receptor paradox in APJ‑low or APJ‑negative contexts; ii) inconsistencies among clinical ELA measurements; and iii) the need to distinguish direct ELA evidence from inference drawn from apelin studies. Current findings position ELA as a candidate biomarker and experimental therapeutic target; however, its clinical utility remains unproven due to pre‑analytical variability across sample types (plasma vs. serum), inconsistencies between detection platforms (ELISA vs. immunohistochemistry), and biological heterogeneity across specific disease subtypes (such as preeclampsia and heart failure). Future work should focus on defining receptor‑ and isoform‑specific signaling, standardizing ELA measurement and establishing pharmacokinetics, dose‑response relationships, delivery strategies and maternal‑fetal safety.

articles.title: Roles of TRIM proteins in cardiovascular diseases: From pathogenesis to therapeutic targeting (Review).
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are driven by sustained mechanical stress, metabolic derangement, inflammation and oxidative injury, which progressively disrupt cellular homeostasis within the heart and vasculature. Although current therapeutic strategies have substantially improved clinical outcomes, most interventions primarily target downstream pathological manifestations rather than upstream regulatory mechanisms that determine stress adaptation and tissue remodeling. Tripartite motif (TRIM) proteins constitute a large family of E3 ubiquitin ligases characterized by a highly conserved RBCC domain architecture and diversified C‑terminal regions. By catalyzing distinct ubiquitin chain topologies and functioning as molecular scaffolds, TRIM proteins broadly regulate protein turnover, inflammatory signaling, metabolic adaptation and cell fate determination. Emerging evidence identifies TRIM proteins as context‑dependent regulators whose biological effects are shaped by cell type, disease stage and microenvironmental conditions. Multiple TRIM family members have been linked to a wide spectrum of cardiovascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, vascular calcification, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic cardiomyopathy. At the cellular level, TRIM proteins influence disease initiation and progression by modulating endothelial dysfunction, vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic remodeling, cardiomyocyte survival and metabolic homeostasis, fibroblast activation and immune‑inflammatory responses. The present review summarized the biochemical characteristics and cell‑specific functions of TRIM proteins and delineates their mechanistic roles in cardiovascular pathogenesis. In addition, it discussed their emerging potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, highlighting both translational opportunities and context‑dependent challenges.

articles.title: Macrophage polarization reprogramming by resveratrol: A novel mechanism for protecting the intestinal mucosal barrier in sepsis (Review).
articles.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by a life‑threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. A key clinical feature of sepsis is disruption of the intestinal mucosal barrier, which not only increases intestinal permeability but also facilitates the translocation of bacteria and toxins, thereby exacerbating systemic inflammatory responses. M1/M2 macrophage polarization imbalance as an important contributor to sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal injury. M1 macrophages promote tissue damage primarily through proinflammatory mechanisms during sepsis, whereas M2 macrophages contribute to tissue repair and inflammation resolution through anti‑inflammatory responses. However, dysregulated M1/M2 macrophage polarization during sepsis may aggravate intestinal inflammation and impair barrier function. Resveratrol, a natural plant compound, has demonstrated anti‑inflammatory, antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties and has been reported to alleviate various pathological conditions, including sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal barrier dysfunction. Resveratrol may mitigate the inflammatory environment in sepsis and promote intestinal mucosal barrier repair through modulation of macrophage polarization. However, most current evidence is derived from experimental studies and further investigation is required to clarify its clinical applicability. The present review aimed to comprehensively examine the mechanisms underlying sepsis‑induced intestinal mucosal barrier damage and its association with M1/M2 macrophage polarization and to explore the potential role of resveratrol in regulating macrophage polarization and alleviating sepsis‑associated intestinal injury. By synthesizing current research, the present review identified critical gaps in knowledge and discusses future directions for understanding the role of resveratrol‑mediated immunomodulation in sepsis‑associated intestinal barrier dysfunction.

articles.title: Fatty acid‑binding proteins at the inflammation‑cancer interface: Isoform‑specific metabolic‑immune mechanisms and therapeutic implications (Review).
articles.abstract: Fatty acid‑binding proteins (FABPs) comprise ten mammalian isoforms (FABP1‑FABP9 and FABP12), each a small intracellular lipid chaperone traditionally viewed as a mediator of fatty acid uptake, trafficking and metabolic partitioning. Evidence from metabolic disease, immunology and oncology indicates that selected FABP isoforms also regulate inflammatory signaling, immune‑cell metabolism and tumor‑stromal crosstalk. Prior reviews have mainly emphasized single isoforms of FABPs or single disease categories. The present narrative review organized FABP biology as a context‑specific evidence map across the inflammation‑cancer interface, in which each principal claim is reported together with the experimental system, with the outcome and limits of extrapolation described. The main mechanistic focus was FABP4, FABP5 and FABP7. The structural determinants of isoform specificity, ligand routing to nuclear receptors and the non‑classical secretion of FABP4 as a circulating adipokine were summarized. The evidence supports a model in which FABPs may contribute to, rather than fully explain, the progression from metabolic stress to chronic low‑grade inflammation, premalignant remodeling and the establishment of the tumor microenvironment. In the present model, FABP4 links adipocytes, macrophages, endothelial cells and tumor cells through fatty acid shuttling and inflammasome/cytokine signaling; FABP5 connects retinoic acid and peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor β/δ signaling with tumor‑cell growth and T helper/regulatory T‑cell balance; and FABP7 regulates neural‑lineage tumor plasticity through ligand‑dependent retinoid X receptor α signaling. In addition, translational evidence was stratified into clinically observed biomarkers, preclinical therapeutic targets and conceptual future technologies. Particular attention was paid to biomarker confounding by obesity, diabetes, age and sex, and to the therapeutic paradox in which FABP5 inhibition may suppress T helper 17 cell‑driven inflammation while enhancing regulatory T‑cell‑mediated immunosuppression in cancer. This synthesis provides a restrained conceptual framework for stage‑, isoform‑ and cell‑type‑specific FABP research.

articles.title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
articles.abstract: Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers. In vitro, small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

articles.title: Development of an accurate CRISPR/Cas13 diagnostic system for Wuchereria bancrofti.
articles.abstract: Disease surveillance is critical for WHO's Global Programme to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis (LF), but current field-ready diagnostics exhibit insufficient sensitivity and/or specificity in low-endemic settings. We aim to develop an ultra-sensitive and field-friendly CRISPR/Cas13-based SHERLOCK (Specific High-sensitivity Enzymatic Reporter unLOCKing) tool for point-of-care detection of Wuchereria bancrofti infection. The SHERLOCK assay, combining recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with CRISPR/Cas13a detection, was performed in two-step and one-pot formats, with sensitivity compared to qPCR (the emerging gold standard). The W. bancrofti SHERLOCK assays achieved a detection limit of 0.1 fg/μL gBlock DNA and showed no cross-reaction with five other filarial species. Assays were validated using 149 pooled mosquito and 185 human blood samples from Samoa, which were previously tested for LF antigen using WHO-recommended Filariasis Test Strips (FTS) and microscopically examined for microfilariae (Mf). For both mosquito and human samples, the two-step SHERLOCK assay reached 100% sensitivity and specificity, while one-pot SHERLOCK showed 94.0-96.4% sensitivity and 100% specificity. To improve the field deployability of the assay, we also used lyophilized one-pot SHERLOCK master mix and assessed its thermostability after storage at 25, 4, and -20°C. The lyophilized one-pot SHERLOCK mix maintained a detection limit of 10 fg/μL W. bancrofti gBlock after 10 days at 25°C, indicating reduced reliance on cold-chain for reagent storage and transport. However, when testing human blood samples with lyophilized SHERLOCK, reduced sensitivity (59.7%) was observed. This CRISPR-based platform offers a promising field-ready next-generation approach to LF diagnostics, potentially addressing current limitations, enhancing surveillance, and elimination efforts.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange improves survival in alcohol-related acute-on-chronic liver failure: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is associated with high short-term mortality and limited therapeutic options. Therapeutic plasma exchange (PLEX) may improve outcomes by removing inflammatory mediators, but randomized evidence in ACLF is limited. This study evaluated the efficacy of PLEX in alcohol-related ACLF (A-ACLF).

METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 100 patients with A-ACLF were randomized (1 : 1) to PLEX plus standard medical therapy (SMT) or SMT alone. PLEX was performed for up to three sessions. Coprimary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and 30-day survival. Secondary outcomes included hospital stay, ventilator requirement, and longitudinal changes in disease severity scores and laboratory parameters.

RESULTS: All 100 patients (PLEX n = 50; SMT n = 50) completed follow-up. In-hospital mortality was lower with PLEX [24 vs. 52%; P = 0.007], with an absolute risk reduction of 28% (number needed to treat: 3.6). Thirty-day survival was higher with PLEX (72 vs. 36%; P < 0.001), with an adjusted hazard ratio for mortality of 0.43 (P = 0.003). Significant improvements were observed in the model for end-stage liver disease sodium, Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver ACLF Research Consortium, and Child-Turcotte-Pugh scores, and in international normalized ratio, creatinine, lactate, ammonia, and von Willebrand factor (all P < 0.001 for interaction). Hospital stay was shorter with PLEX (19 vs. 24 days; P = 0.023). No major PLEX-related adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSION: PLEX improves short-term survival and disease severity in A-ACLF and may be a valuable therapeutic option where transplantation is limited.

articles.title: Real-World Treatment Patterns, Tolerability, and Outcomes Among Patients With CLL/SLL Treated With First-Line Ibrutinib, Acalabrutinib, or Zanubrutinib in the US Community Oncology Setting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Covalent Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (cBTKis) are standard first-line (1L) therapies for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)/small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL). In clinical trials, second-generation (2G) cBTKis demonstrated better tolerability than ibrutinib, particularly regarding cardiotoxicity; however, real-world evidence on their use, discontinuation, and tolerability remains limited. This study examined treatment patterns and outcomes of cBTKis in the US community oncology setting.

METHODS: CLL/SLL patients who initiated 1L therapy between November 21, 2019 and July 31, 2023 were identified from electronic health records. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated time to treatment discontinuation (TTD), time to next treatment or death (TTNT-D), real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS), and overall survival (OS). Adverse events (AEs) were reported as proportions and incidence rates. Cox proportional hazards models assessed factors associated with TTD. Correlations between rwPFS and OS were evaluated with Kendall's tau.

RESULTS: Among 584 patients, 384 initiated ibrutinib, 150 acalabrutinib, and 50 zanubrutinib. Median follow-up durations were 35.6, 42.3, and 16.1 months, respectively. Overall, 51.2% discontinued 1L therapy by 24 months and 65.9% by end of follow-up, most commonly due to AEs (38.4%).
