Electrochemical sensing has attracted considerable attention as a rapid, low-cost, and point-of-care approach for pathogen detection and infection monitoring. Among these sensing platforms, carbonaceous materials occupy a central role owing to their favorable electrochemical properties, including wide potential windows, facile electron-transfer kinetics, tunable surface chemistry, biocompatibility, and low-cost fabrication. This review critically examines recent advances in carbonaceous electrochemical sensors for infectious disease diagnostics, focusing on carbon films, carbon fibers, graphene and graphene derivatives, carbon nanotubes, fullerenes, graphene quantum dots, and nanodiamonds. We discuss how the structural and electronic characteristics of each material influence sensing performance, recognition element immobilization, signal transduction, and analytical figures of merit. Particular emphasis is placed on electrochemical strategies for the detection of whole pathogens, nucleic acids, proteins, and infection-associated metabolites, as well as emerging applications in continuous monitoring of microbial metabolite production, biofilm development, and antimicrobial efficacy. Carbonaceous materials enable sensitive detection across many sensor designs, but the analytical performance depends strongly on the material properties, electrode architecture, surface modification, and recognition strategy used. Translation to clinical use is limited less by sensitivity than by performance in complex samples, where biofouling, poor stability, and limited reproducibility have rarely been addressed through validation. By comparing the advantages and limitations specific to each material class, this review aims to inform the rational design of future electrochemical platforms for infectious disease diagnosis and monitoring.

articles.title: Authors' Response: Rapidly Improving Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: A Biological Phenotype or a Care-Dependent Clinical Trajectory.
Trend analysis from 1990 to 2020 reveals a decline in hepatocellular carcinoma in Osaka, Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. In Japan, the historically high HCC burden has been largely driven by hepatitis virus infection, although metabolic and lifestyle-related risk factors have become increasingly prevalent. This study describes long-term trends in HCC incidence in Osaka Prefecture from 1990 to 2020.

METHODS: Population-based data from the Osaka Cancer Registry were used to identify newly diagnosed HCC cases, defined as International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition, topography code C22.0 with morphology codes 8170-8175 and behavior code 3. Sex-specific and age-standardized incidence rates were calculated using the World Health Organization 2000-2025 world standard population. Age-specific rates were estimated for individuals aged 50-79 years, and temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression.

RESULTS: From 1990 to 2020, 99,889 HCC patients were registered, of whom 70,962 (71.04%) were men and 28,927 (28.96%) were women. The age-standardized incidence rate declined from 45.77 to 14.56 per 100,000 persons in men and from 10.87 to 3.90 per 100,000 persons in women. Joinpoint analysis showed significant declines from 1997 onward in men and from 2000 onward in women. Age-specific incidence rates among individuals aged 50-79 years showed overall declines in both sexes, although the timing and magnitude varied by age and sex.

CONCLUSIONS: Age-standardized HCC incidence rates in Osaka Prefecture declined substantially from 1990 to 2020 in both sexes, with distinct temporal patterns by age and sex. These findings provide a basis for understanding long-term changes in HCC incidence and informing prevention strategies.

articles.title: Age, Steatotic Liver Disease, Cardiometabolic Risks and Alcohol on Cardiorenal Outcomes and Mortality: Chinese Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is increasingly diagnosed in younger adults, yet whether its long-term risk profiles differ by age remains poorly defined.

METHODS: Within the prospective Kailuan cohort, 34,988 participants with incident SLD were identified and matched (up to 1:4) with the non-SLD controls. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), while eXtreme Gradient Boosting with SHapley Additive exPlanations quantified the relative importance of SLD, cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs), and alcohol on chronic kidney disease (CKD), cardiovascular disease (CVD), and mortality across age groups.

RESULTS: After a median follow-up of >10 years, the HRs for the associations between SLD and CKD (HR: 1.44, 95% CI: 1.22-1.70), CVD (1.65, 1.23-2.23), and mortality (1.46, 1.05-2.03) were significantly stronger in the early-onset (≤40 years) group than in late-onset (>40 years) group (all P for interaction <0.05). Alcohol-related subtypes exhibited a positive dose-response for CKD only in the early-onset group. SHAP analysis within models restricted to the predefined domains (SLD, CMRFs and alcohol) suggested that SLD had relatively high predictive importance for adverse outcomes in early-onset group, whereas the predictive importance of CMRFs predominated in late-onset group.

CONCLUSIONS: Age significantly modifies the associations of SLD, CMRFs, and alcohol with clinical outcomes. The relative impact of SLD on cardiorenal risk is most pronounced in early adulthood, supporting the potential value of age-tailored risk assessment, though interventional validation is needed.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Liver Disease: From Biological Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Sex differences in liver disease are evident in epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical outcomes, although their magnitude and direction vary according to etiology, age, reproductive stage, exposure, and region. Men bear a higher global burden of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whereas primary biliary cholangitis and autoimmune hepatitis predominantly affect women. These patterns reflect the interplay of hormonal, genetic, immunological, metabolic, behavioral, and social determinants. Women generally exhibit stronger innate and adaptive immune responses, which may promote viral clearance but also contribute to autoimmune susceptibility. Experimental studies have identified estrogen receptor, androgen receptor, and sex-chromosome-related pathways that may influence steatosis, fibrosis, and hepatocarcinogenesis. However, many proposed mechanisms remain incompletely validated in humans. Sex also influences pharmacokinetics and access to liver transplantation, whereas evidence for sex-specific differences in treatment efficacy, particularly in immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy for HCC, remains inconclusive. This review synthesizes evidence across major liver diseases with explicit evidence labels, separates biological sex from gender-related factors, and concludes that sex currently informs risk assessment, surveillance, and equitable care rather than sex-specific treatment.

articles.title: The association of childhood maltreatment, depression, and their combination with adiposity and dyslipidemia: an individual participant data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While childhood maltreatment and depression are recognized risk factors for poor metabolic health, the extent to which these individually or in combination with each other contribute to metabolic risk remains unknown. Therefore, we investigated adiposity and dyslipidemia across four groups: adults with neither a history of childhood maltreatment nor depression (controls), with childhood maltreatment, with depression, or with both.

METHODS: We conducted an individual participant data meta-analysis using 11 cohort studies. Childhood maltreatment was assessed with reports of physical, emotional, and/or sexual abuse. Depression was established with clinical interviews or validated symptom scales. Adiposity was assessed with body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) and dyslipidemia with circulating triglycerides and low-density/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (LDL-c/HDL-c).

RESULTS: In the pooled sample (N = 167,332), 6% had childhood maltreatment, 21% depression, and 6% both. Compared to controls, participants with maltreatment had slightly higher adiposity (dBMI=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.10], p=.012; dWHR=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.12], p=.030) but similar lipid levels (dtriglycerides=0.01 [95%CI, ‒0.03-0.04], p=.751; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.01 [95%CI, ‒0.03-0.06], p=.560). Those with depression had higher adiposity (dBMI=0.06 [95%CI, 0.01-0.12], p=.030; dWHR=0.12 [95%CI, 0.08-0.16], p<.001) and dyslipidemia (dtriglycerides=0.08 [95%CI, 0.04-0.12], p<.001; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.13 [95%CI, 0.07-0.18], p<.001). Participants with both maltreatment and depression had the highest adiposity (dBMI=0.17 [95%CI, 0.04-0.30], p=.010; dWHR=0.16 [95%CI, 0.07-0.24], p<.001) and dyslipidemia (dtriglycerides=0.14 [95%CI, 0.11-0.16], p<.001; dLDL-c/HDL-c=0.18 [95%CI, 0.12-0.23], p<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Childhood maltreatment and depression are associated with unfavorable metabolic health, with the largest dysregulations found when maltreatment and depression co-occur. Mechanisms of metabolic dysregulation in maltreatment and/or depression should be better understood to prevent progression to metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Photoinactivation of SARS-CoV-2 spike protein by functionalized peptide.
articles.abstract: For the inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, which is an attractive target for the treatment of COVID-19, the S-RBD (spike protein receptor-binding domain)-binding peptide was functionalized with an on/off switchable photooxygenation catalyst. This peptide induced the oxygenation of the S-RBD under near-infrared irradiation, resulting in the inactivation of the S-RBD and subsequent inhibition of viral infection.

articles.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction at the crossroads of liver disease and depression: Focus on the liver-brain axis.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction may provide a biological link between liver disease and major depressive disorder (MDD), two conditions that frequently coexist. In chronic liver disease, changes in energy metabolism, redox balance, Ca2+ homeostasis, and mitochondrial quality control promote metabolic stress, inflammation, and tissue injury. Studies of MDD report related mitochondrial changes that affect neuronal activity, neuroinflammation, and synaptic function. The liver and brain also exchange metabolic and inflammatory signals through the circulation, autonomic nerves, and the gut. Recent studies have identified hepatic acetate metabolism, complement component 3, lipocalin 2, and hepatic clearance of neuroactive microbial metabolites as components of this communication. Vagal and sympathetic pathways provide additional routes, while liver injury can also alter mitochondrial function in the brain. In this review, we integrate clinical and experimental evidence to examine how these processes may contribute to the comorbidity of liver disease and depression. We also discuss the limits of current evidence and consider how spatial and single-cell profiling, brain bioenergetic imaging, and liver-directed interventions can test the proposed mechanisms. Together, current evidence supports mitochondrial dysfunction as a plausible and testable link between hepatic and neural pathology and provides a framework for studying liver disease and depression comorbidity.

articles.title: Association between remitted major depressive disorder and subsequent risk of cognitive deficit and neurocognitive disorders - A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: In late life, a major depressive episode (MDE) is often a prodrome for dementia. Several studies have also shown that even an MDE in full remission is a risk factor for dementia, including when the MDE occurred years earlier. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the extent to which a diagnosis of remitted major depressive disorder (rMDD) is associated with cognitive deficits or a diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia in late life. We searched PubMed, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception through May 2, 2026 for peer-reviewed publications that examined cognitive performance or a diagnosis of MCI or dementia in older adults with rMDD. We narratively synthesized and meta-analyzed findings; 50 publications were included reporting on 28 separate studies with nonoverlapping participant groups (6,512 participants with rMDD and 60,493 healthy controls [HCs]). Of 24 studies assessing cognitive performance, 19 (79.2%) supported that rMDD is associated with cognitive deficits in late life. Of six studies assessing diagnoses with rates reported in both groups, three (50.0%) supported that rMDD increases the risk of MCI or dementia. All 24 studies assessing cognitive performance were meta-analyzed; while there was significant heterogeneity among the studies, individuals with rMDD demonstrated significantly worse performance than HCs for global cognition and each of the seven cognitive domains analyzed. Overall, our results strongly support that rMDD is associated with cognitive deficits in late life. Older adults with a history of rMDD require individualized risk assessment for cognitive decline.

articles.title: Outcomes of Intramedullary Fibular Strut Grafting Combined With Locking Plate Fixation for Aseptic Distal Tibial Nonunion.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Aseptic distal-third tibial diaphyseal nonunion after failed intramedullary nailing remains challenging because of inadequate distal fixation and mechanical instability. This study evaluated revision surgery using an intramedullary nonvascularized autologous fibular strut graft combined with an anterolateral locking plate. MATERIAL AND METHODS This retrospective case series included patients who underwent revision surgery for aseptic distal-third tibial diaphyseal nonunion between January 2020 and December 2024. Inclusion criteria were symptomatic nonunion after primary intramedullary nailing, a Radiographic Union Scale for Tibial fractures (RUST) score of 10 or lower, and a minimum postoperative follow-up of 9 months. Patients with infection, pathological fractures, or incomplete follow-up were excluded. Revision consisted of debridement, intramedullary placement of a nonvascularized autologous fibular strut graft, and anterolateral locking plate fixation. The primary outcome was fracture union based on clinical and radiographic criteria. RESULTS Eleven patients (9 men, 2 women; mean age, 50.9 years) were included. Four had atrophic and 7 had hypertrophic nonunion. Mean follow-up was 16 months (range, 9-27 months). Union was achieved in 10 patients (90.9%). The only failure occurred in a patient with atrophic nonunion, with no evidence of union after 11 months. No microbiological evidence of infection was detected during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS This revision technique achieved a high union rate in patients with aseptic distal-third tibial diaphyseal nonunion after failed intramedullary nailing. It may be particularly useful when exchange nailing alone is unlikely to provide adequate distal stability. Larger comparative studies are warranted.

articles.title: Pembrolizumab-Induced Pneumonitis in Esophageal Cancer: Three Clinical Scenarios and a Management Framework.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Pembrolizumab prolongs survival in advanced esophageal cancer but carries a risk of checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP), a rare and potentially fatal immune-related adverse event. Real-world management of CIP is particularly complex in developing countries, where endemic tuberculosis and limited access to advanced diagnostic tools for infection create substantial diagnostic uncertainty, especially in patients with pre-existing pulmonary comorbidities. CASE REPORT We report 3 cases of stage IV esophageal squamous cell carcinoma that developed pembrolizumab-related CIP with distinct clinical trajectories. Case 1 was a 51-year-old man with multiple metastases, grade 3 steroid-refractory CIP, rapid disease progression, transitioned to best supportive care. Case 2 was a 72-year-old man with COPD and cisplatin-induced renal failure and CIP difficult to distinguish from acute exacerbation, who fully recovered with corticosteroids, but pembrolizumab was permanently discontinued due to high recurrence risk. Case 3 was a 61-year-old previously healthy man, grade 2 CIP after 6 cycles, with complete recovery, and successful pembrolizumab rechallenge without relapse. CONCLUSIONS Three clinical scenarios provide a practical framework for managing checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP): (1) palliation for severe, steroid-refractory CIP accompanied by oncological progression; (2) permanent discontinuation for steroid-responsive CIP in patients with high-risk baseline features; and (3) safe rechallenge for mild CIP following complete resolution. Key decision determinants include CIP severity, steroid responsiveness, underlying lung function, and anticipated therapeutic benefit. Empiric antibiotics should be individualized. This is a hypothesis-generating single-institution observation, not a validated management guideline.

articles.title: Early Outcomes of 2-Port Totally Endoscopic Mitral Valve Repair with Artificial Chordae for Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the early outcomes of 2-port, nonrobotic, totally endoscopic mitral valve repair using artificial chordae in patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 84 selected patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation who underwent 2-port, nonrobotic, totally endoscopic mitral valve repair between July 2023 and June 2026. All patients received artificial chordae and ring annuloplasty. The primary outcomes were early mortality, mitral valve reoperation, and recurrent moderate or greater mitral regurgitation during follow-up.

RESULTS: No patient died early, underwent conversion to sternotomy, or required mitral valve reoperation. Mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 156.1±44.0 and 111.9±34.8 minutes, respectively, and the mean main skin incision length was 2.9±0.3 cm. During a mean follow-up of 12.1±9.0 months, no patient died or underwent mitral valve reoperation. Freedom from recurrent moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 98.5%±1.5% at 6 months, 96.7%±2.3% at 1 year, and 87.9%±6.3% at 2 years. Only 4 patients remained at risk at 24 months, limiting precision of the 2-year estimate.

CONCLUSION: Two-port, nonrobotic, totally endoscopic mitral valve repair using artificial chordae was feasible in selected patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation and yielded favorable early clinical and echocardiographic outcomes. Longer and more complete follow-up is needed to establish durability.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of experimental chromogenic medium for Streptococcus agalactiae subclinical mastitis detection in dairy cows.
articles.abstract: This research paper had the objective of evaluating the accuracy of an experimental chromogenic medium for detection of Streptococcus agalactiae intramammary infection, using quarter and composite milk samples. Four herds were visited once to collect milk samples from all lactating cows (N = 117). Quarter and composite samples were plated on the chromogenic medium (index test). Simultaneously, quarter samples were plated on blood agar, and the catalase-negative cocci isolates were further speciated by MALDI-TOF MS (reference standard). Three thresholds were used to estimate the chromogenic medium's accuracy parameters. The coefficient of agreement between observers was 0.71 for the final diagnosis of S. agalactiae, and 0.88 for determining colony colours. For quarter milk samples, sensitivity ranged from 44.35% to 87.54%, depending on the threshold. The specificity was 97.81% to 93.55%. The positive predictive value was 80.68% to 83.60%. The negative predictive value was 87.62% to 98.87%. For composite milk samples, there was little difference in accuracy compared to quarter milk samples. Accuracy was highly variable among farms. Regardless of the threshold used, the observed proportion of false-negative results may not be acceptable in S. agalactiae eradication programmes. The variability in accuracy among farms should be further studied under field conditions.

articles.title: Should an infected preauricular sinus be excised during active infection? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of laryngology and otology

articles.title: Impact of chronic subclinical mastitis on milk production, risk of clinical mastitis and involuntary removal from the herd: a risk-set case-control study.
articles.abstract: The objectives of this study were: 1) to evaluate the impact of chronic subclinical mastitis (SCM) on milk production, risk of clinical mastitis (CM) and culling, 2) to identify cow factors associated with chronic SCM and 3) to describe characteristics of SCM, such as aetiology. Cows from six dairies were enrolled. The case group (GCA; N = 36) included cows with chronic SCM (started lactation with somatic cell count (SCC) <200,000 cells/ml and experienced SCC ≥200,000 cells/ml in two consecutive months). The control group (GCO; N = 64) included cows with SCC <200,000 cells/ml prior to inclusion. Milk culturing was performed from GCA at inclusion and a month thereafter. At inclusion, the following evaluations were performed: teat-end hyperkeratosis, udder position in relation to the hock, teat length, teat shape, and body condition score. Outcomes were monthly Dairy Herd Improvement Association milk production and SCC, risk of CM and risk of culling, from inclusion to the end of lactation. Milk production after inclusion was greater in GCO (25.70 ± 3.22) than in GCA (21.94 ± 3.28 kg/cow/day). The cumulative incidence of CM during the study period was 52.78% (19/36) and 20.31% (13/64) in GCA and GCO, respectively. Regardless of parity, the hazard of CM was 3.29 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.48-7.33) times greater in GCA than in GCO. The culling rate was 22.22% (8/36) and 7.81% (5/64) in GCA and GCO cows, respectively. Among multiparous cows only, the hazard of culling was 4.04 (95% CI: 1.73-9.47) times greater in GCA than in GCO, while there was no culling in GCA primiparous cows. Among all evaluations performed, parity was the only factor associated with chronic SCM. The odds of chronic SCM were 4.65 (95% CI = 1.91-11.36) times greater for multiparous than primiparous cows. Results of this study can be used to estimate financial losses in future studies and support on-farm decisions.

articles.title: GenErlangFit: a tool for estimating empirical waiting-time distributions to inform compartmental epidemic models.
articles.abstract: In standard compartmental models of infectious diseases, assumptions about the duration of time spent in each state (e.g., latent period, infectious period) significantly influence model outcomes and interpretation. When represented deterministically as systems of ordinary differential equations or stochastically as Markov chains, these models often assume constant transition rates between states, which implies an exponential distribution of "waiting times" in each state. However, this assumption is not consistent with available data for many diseases. An alternative that remains analytically or computationally tractable is to model each state as a series of multiple identical substates, which results in a gamma (Erlang) distributed overall duration of time spent in each disease state (known as the "linear chain trick"). While well-known, few studies have presented formal methods for determining the optimal number of substates or extended this approach to encode a wider variety of distributions by including non-identical substates. Here we introduce GenErlangFit, an open-source R package and Shiny web application for fitting Erlang and related distributions to empirical waiting-time data. It combines maximum likelihood parameter estimation with parametric bootstrap hypothesis testing to prioritize the simplest model structures that produce waiting times consistent with observed data. To improve flexibility, we incorporate the Erlang-Exponential model, an extension of the standard Erlang distribution that adds a final exponentially-distributed stage with a unique transition rate, allowing better approximation of empirical distributions with varying skewness and tail behavior. The web application provides an accessible interface for modelers to fit empirical data and build parsimonious, data-driven compartmental models.

articles.title: Familial erythrocytosis, differential diagnosis and clinical impact.
articles.abstract: Erythrocytosis (EC) may occur as a compensatory response to pathological or non-pathological situations in secondary settings, or instead it can be found as a primary event in either clonal or non-clonal diseases. The aim of this paper is to enumerate and describe the different types of EC, with a special focus on familial EC. Polycythemia Vera (PV) represents the most common cause of acquired primary EC. PV causes a reduced quality of life because of the burden of systemic symptoms, a reduced life expectancy versus the global population. Cause of death is equally divided into thrombosis and clonal evolution. Non-neoplastic EC must be distinguished into hereditary and acquired EC. Primary hereditary EC can be determined by activating mutations occurring on the erythropoietin receptor, Src Homology 2-B adaptor protein 3 or Janus activated kinase-2 gene sequences. Secondary hereditary EC may originate from mutations occurring on the HGB chain genes or on bisphosphoglycerate-mutase gene. Acquired ECs are compensation events mostly due to pulmonary diseases, uncompensated cardiac abnormalities, adverse drug events. Thresholds indicating a higher thrombotic risk are not known in congenital erythrocytosis and are commonly borrowed from PV or non-clonal non-hereditary acquired EC. No specific recommendations exist for prophylaxis and treatment in familial EC. New diagnostic technologies should be used to afford a genetic diagnosis for familial EC, and consensus recommendations, if not evidence-based, should be given to assure optimal diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

articles.title: Biomarker Consistency and Clinical Utility of the TyG-Bilirubin Model for Drug-Eluting Stent Restenosis.
articles.abstract: The combined use of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and total bilirubin offers a potentially accessible approach to predicting drug-eluting stent in-stent restenosis (DES-ISR). This correspondence discusses several considerations regarding the interpretation and clinical applicability of a recently published prediction model. Discrepancies between the reported total bilirubin concentrations and the sums of direct and indirect bilirubin fractions warrant clarification, particularly given the central role of bilirubin in the proposed equation. Furthermore, angiographically detected restenosis should be distinguished from clinically significant restenosis requiring revascularization. Although the TyG-bilirubin model demonstrated moderate discrimination during internal validation, its incremental predictive value beyond conventional clinical risk factors requires careful interpretation. Further clarification of model calibration, validation procedures, and clinical net benefit at relevant decision thresholds would strengthen the evidence supporting its application. Addressing these issues may facilitate the translation of biomarker-based risk stratification into clinical decision-making after percutaneous coronary intervention.

articles.title: Isotopic red cell mass measurement: usefulness in 2026 for the diagnostic work-up of erythrocytosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The study aimed to evaluate the role of red blood cells (RBC) isotopic mass measurement as second step in the diagnostic work-up of erythrocytosis in patients with negative initial investigations (blood gas analysis, erythropoietin [EPO] level, JAK2V617F mutation).

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 93 patients who underwent RBC isotopic measurement between January 2010 and December 2022 at a tertiary care university hospital. Analysable data were available for 25 patients, of whom 20 met haemoglobin/haematocrit diagnostic thresholds for erythrocytosis and had a triple-negative initial work-up consisting of following laboratory parameters: p50/COHb, EPO levels, and JAK2V617F mutation. All patients underwent RBC isotopic measurement, with positive results defined by an increase of ≥ 25% in measured RBC volume compared to theoretical values.

RESULTS: Among triple-negative patients (n = 20), seven (35%) presented with a positive isotopic measurement indicative of increased RBC mass. Identified causes of absolute erythrocytosis included chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, obstructive sleep apnoea, cyanotic heart disease, and neoplastic processes. Notably, 13 (65%) patients had normal RBC mass measurements, with only one patient eventually diagnosed with polycythaemia vera confirmed by bone marrow biopsy. This false negative result was caused by an undeclared therapeutic phlebotomy performed just before RBC mass analysis. As expected in relative erythrocytosis, additional investigations in the other 12 cases with a negative isotopic analysis did not yield useful diagnostic findings.

CONCLUSION: Our data suggests that RBC isotopic mass measurement is a useful investigation in patients with erythrocytosis whose initial work-up does not provide diagnostic clues for either polycythaemia vera or a secondary absolute erythrocytosis. In our hands, a negative RBC isotopic measurement, along with a triple-negative initial work-up (p50/COHb, EPO level, JAK2V617F mutation) ruled out myeloproliferative neoplasia and secondary forms of absolute erythrocytosis. By utilizing RBC isotopic measurement as a second step in the evaluation of patients with erythrocytosis, unnecessary investigations can be avoided, leading to cost-effective diagnostic work-up.

articles.title: Serum Magnesium in Relation to Insulin Resistance and Atherogenic Lipid Indices in Hyperlipidemic Patients: A Retrospective Study Highlighting Confounding by Statin Indication.
articles.abstract: Hypomagnesemia has been linked to insulin resistance and dyslipidemia in a variety of populations, but findings remain inconsistent, and evidence in statin-treated, hyperlipidemic groups is still limited. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 97 euthyroid, hyperlipidemic outpatients (57 normoglycemic, 40 prediabetic) at a tertiary endocrinology clinic, examining serum magnesium in relation to the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and several atherogenic lipid indices. Rather than showing the expected association, magnesium had no significant relationship with HOMA-IR or with any of the atherogenic indices (atherogenic index of plasma, triglyceride/HDL ratio, LDL/HDL ratio, atherogenic coefficient) across correlation, multivariable regression, and quartile-based sensitivity analyses; nearly all magnesium levels fell within the normal range, limiting sensitivity to detect an association and precluding any distinction between chronic and acute hypomagnesemia. An exploratory interaction between magnesium and statin use was observed, with lower magnesium tracking prediabetic status only among statin-treated patients (p = 0.018), a finding that needs verification in larger groups with data on statin duration. Statin use was far more common in prediabetic patients (62.5% versus 24.6%, p < 0.001), and accounting for this imbalance-a secondary methodological finding-revealed an independent association between prediabetes and higher HOMA-IR, lower HDL, and higher uric acid, not evident in the unadjusted comparisons. The results suggest that the expected magnesium-insulin resistance relationship may not hold in a hyperlipidemic, statin-treated, and narrowly normomagnesemic population, and demonstrate how unequal treatment exposure can bias the evaluation of metabolic risk in similar groups.

articles.title: Personalized photobiomodulation for TMD-related pain: an evidence mapping review of individual determinants of dosimetry.
articles.abstract: Photobiomodulation (PBM) is widely used for pain management in temporomandibular disorders (TMD), yet the extent to which individual anatomical, physiological, or psychosocial factors influence dosimetric decisions remains unclear. This evidence mapping review aimed to characterize how individual patient-level determinants have been considered in PBM dosimetry in studies of TMD-related pain. This evidence mapping review systematically searched PubMed, MEDLINE, LILACS, the Cochrane Library, and EMBASE, SCOPUS and ClinicalTrials.gov for studies published between 2010 and July 2026, with additional citation searching. Eligible designs included randomized controlled trials, clinical protocols, and systematic or narrative reviews addressing PBM for TMD-related pain in relation to individual-level characteristics (e.g., age, sex, BMI, skin phototype, tissue thickness, and psychosocial variables). PRISMA 2020 was retained as the primary reporting framework, and reporting was additionally cross-checked against applicable PRISMA-ScR items. Methodological appraisal was performed using JBI tools and ROBIS, when applicable. The search identified 387 records, including 329 from electronic databases and 58 from ClinicalTrials.gov; citation searching identified no additional records. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria: five randomized controlled trials, one narrative review, one systematic review, and one clinical trial protocol. Across the five randomized controlled trials, sample sizes ranged from 44 to 147 randomized participants, with 293 participants included in the final analyses across studies. PBM protocols varied substantially in dosimetric parameters and treatment schedules. Pain outcomes showed different statistical patterns across trials; three randomized controlled trials did not demonstrate significant between-group differences in pain outcomes, whereas Aisaiti et al. reported a significant between-group effect for TMJ arthralgia but not for masseter myalgia. Among the randomized controlled trials, TMD subtype was examined as a potential response modifier, psychosocial variables were assessed without being used to modify dosimetry, and pain-point localization was used for individualized treatment targeting. Separately, one clinical trial protocol proposed individualized dosimetry based on BMI, skin phototype, and tissue thickness. In conclusion, current PBM research for TMD-related pain relies predominantly on predefined, non-individualized protocols and shows limited incorporation of individual patient-level determinants into dosimetric decision-making. Evidence regarding individualized PBM dosimetry remains preliminary: only one clinical trial protocol proposed a formal individualized dosimetric model, and no completed clinical trial directly compared individualized dosimetric adjustment with predefined protocols. Current evidence is therefore insufficient to determine whether individualized dosimetric approaches provide clinically meaningful advantages. Future well-designed clinical studies should directly evaluate whether systematic incorporation of patient-level determinants into PBM dosimetry improves clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Fractional CO₂ laser for eyelid and periorbital wrinkles and laxity: short- and long-term clinical results using a standardized protocol.
articles.abstract: Eyelid and periorbital rejuvenation is a common aesthetic concern. This study aimed to describe an original and detailed fractional CO₂ laser protocol and evaluate its efficacy and safety for skin tightening and wrinkle reduction in the upper and lower eyelids and periorbital region, with 12-month follow-up. A single-arm, evaluator-blinded clinical trial was conducted in 27 patients presenting with eyelid and periorbital laxity and wrinkles. All patients underwent a single session of fractional CO₂ laser treatment. Clinical outcomes were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months using two study-specific grading scales evaluated by two independent expert assessors, along with patient-reported outcomes. Significant reductions were observed in eyelid and periorbital laxity (p < 0.0001) and in fine lines and wrinkle depth (p < 0.0001). At 3 months, 74% of patients achieved good overall improvement (50-75% correction; p < 0.0001). Improvements were maintained over time with minor variations, including a peak effect at 6 months followed by a slight decline at 12 months. At 12 months, 70% of patients reported being satisfied or very satisfied. No unexpected adverse events or complications were observed. The protocol described appears to be a safe and potentially effective approach for eyelid and periorbital rejuvenation, associated with improvements in skin tightening and wrinkle reduction, with high patient satisfaction and results generally maintained over at least a 12-month follow-up. Registry trial code: E43597637. Trial registration number: IMV/AlcoleaJM/03/04/2022. Data of registration: 2022/06/07.

articles.title: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in stage IV non-small cell lung cancer undergoing immune checkpoint blockade: Comparison to [18F]FDG PET/CT and role in response evaluation and prognosis.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT and [18F]FDG PET/CT in patients with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to explore the potential of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters in evaluating treatment response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), as well as the association between total lesion (TL) FAPI and progression-free survival (PFS).

METHODS: Twenty patients with stage IV NSCLC were prospectively included in this exploratory study. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT was performed at baseline and repeated after six weeks of ICB therapy. Baseline lesion uptake (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and target-to-background ratio (TBR)) were compared with previously performed [18F]FDG PET/CT. Baseline values and early changes in [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-derived parameters (ΔTLFAPI and primary tumour ΔSUVmax) were related to treatment response and evaluated in relation to PFS.

RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT demonstrated a higher TBR than [18F]FDG PET/CT (all lesions analysed together: median TBR 7.34 vs. 5.05; p < 0.01), while SUVmax values did not differ significantly (median 9.42 vs. 9.13; p = 0.06). Early treatment responders showed marked reductions in TLFAPI whereas non-responders showed a median increase (median change - 50.41% vs. +10.11%; p = 0.01). Above-median baseline TLFAPI was associated with shorter PFS (HR 3.33, 95% CI 1.01-10.96; p = 0.048).

CONCLUSION: [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT confirmed its potential role in lesion detection. This exploratory study showed that early changes in TLFAPI might be associated with treatment response of ICB, and that baseline TLFAPI might be associated with PFS. Future studies on the role of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT in guiding ICB therapy would be of great interest.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Data to Care: Practical Considerations for Health Departments.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Data to care is a public health strategy to improve care engagement among people with HIV (PWH). Health departments face common barriers to the success of data to care programs, particularly the relatively low accuracy of surveillance data for identifying and contacting out-of-care PWH. We conducted a systematic review focused on practical approaches for health departments to more effectively reach out-of-care PWH.

RECENT FINDINGS: Across 31 publications describing data to care programs using public health surveillance data, a median of 20.2% (IQR 10.7-36.3%) of investigated cases led to a PWH who was confirmed to be out of care. Programs that incorporated other data sources, such as HIV clinic records, more efficiently identified out-of-care PWH. Supplementing surveillance-based data to care efforts with additional data sources like clinical records or real-time alerts at points of clinical contact can improve the efficiency of finding PWH who are truly out of care.

articles.title: Effects of different doses of high-power laser therapy combined with conventional physiotherapy in patients with nonspecific neck pain: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Nonspecific neck pain is a prevalent musculoskeletal condition that commonly results in persistent pain, functional impairment, and restricted cervical range of motion. High-Power Laser Therapy (HPLT) has gained attention as a complementary intervention in physiotherapy for managing this condition. However, evidence comparing the clinical effectiveness of different HPLT dosage protocols remains limited, highlighting the need for further investigation. This study investigated the clinical effectiveness of two different HPLT doses, each delivered in conjunction with a conventional physiotherapy program, by assessing their impact on pain intensity, neck-related functional disability, and cervical range of motion (ROM) in patients with nonspecific neck pain. A randomized controlled trial was conducted on 52 participants randomly assigned to a low-dose HPLT group (n = 26) or a high-dose HPLT group (n = 26). Both groups received HPLT combined with conventional physiotherapy for the study duration. Pain intensity was measured using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), neck-related disability using the Neck Disability Index (NDI), and cervical ROM (flexion, extension, side-bending, and rotation) using the OB Goniometer. The primary analysis was performed using a Gaussian generalized estimating equation (GEE) model including group, time, and the group × time interaction, with participant as the clustering variable. Between-group differences in change were reported with 95% confidence intervals and Cohen's *d*, with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment for multiple outcomes. A baseline-adjusted ANCOVA model was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Fifty-two participants were analysed (26 per group). Both groups improved from pre- to post-treatment; however, the high-dose group demonstrated significantly greater improvements across all outcomes, as indicated by significant group × time interactions (all false-discovery-rate-adjusted *q* < 0.001). The between-group differences in change favoured the high-dose group, with large effect sizes for pain intensity (Cohen's *d* = -3.21), neck disability (- 3.04), cervical flexion (*d* = 1.50), extension (1.64), left lateral flexion (1.70), right lateral flexion (1.15), left rotation (2.04), and right rotation (1.44). These findings remained consistent in the baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Cohen's d values represent standardized between-group differences in pre-to-post change Both HPLT dose protocols combined with conventional physiotherapy improved pain, neck-related disability, and cervical ROM in patients with nonspecific neck pain. The higher-dose protocol produced significantly greater short-term improvements than the lower-dose protocol. However, the absence of an exercise-only or sham-laser control group prevented determination of the independent contribution of HPLT to the observed improvements.

articles.title: Selective Pharyngeal Timing Changes Following a Serial 40-Bolus Swallowing Protocol in Adults with Acute Stroke.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether a serial 40-bolus swallowing protocol designed to increase swallowing demand was associated with changes in the timing of swallowing events and to explore potential mechanisms beyond peripheral neuromuscular origins.

DESIGN: Pre-post within-subject repeated-measures design.

SETTING: General acute-care hospital and designated stroke center.

PARTICIPANTS: Sixty-three adults with acute stroke and videofluoroscopically confirmed dysphagia.

INTERVENTIONS: The protocol comprised recorded initial and final 1-mL thin-liquid barium swallows and 38 intervening trials consisting of clinically indicated boluses and supplemental self-paced moderately thick juice swallows as needed.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Oral transit time, pharyngeal transit time, pharyngeal delay time, and durations of laryngeal vestibule closure, cricopharyngeal opening, and laryngeal elevation.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed in three measures. Pharyngeal transit time was longer during the final swallow (initial: M = 2.44, SD = 3.58; final: M = 4.87, SD = 8.61), t(58) = - 2.04, p = .046. Similarly, pharyngeal delay time was prolonged (initial: M = 1.81, SD = 3.53; final: M = 4.04, SD = 7.91), t(58) = - 2.01, p = .049. Additionally, cricopharyngeal opening duration was longer (initial: M = 0.35, SD = 0.14; final: M = 0.38, SD = 0.15), t(59) = - 2.26, p = .028. Wilcoxon tests corroborated all three findings.

CONCLUSIONS: The selective pattern of changes suggests that peripheral neuromuscular mechanisms alone may not fully explain the observed swallowing alterations. Rather, central neural mechanisms may contribute to swallowing changes associated with increased demand in adults with acute stroke.

articles.title: Comparison of 0.5 mg and 1.0 mg alteplase for catheter-based thrombolytic evacuation of intracerebral hemorrhage.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although catheter-based minimally invasive evacuation with alteplase has been investigated for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), the optimal intraparenchymal alteplase dose remains uncertain. We compared hematoma evacuation, procedural outcomes, and short-term neurological outcomes between 0.5 mg and 1.0 mg alteplase regimens administered every 8 hours.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 27 patients with spontaneous supratentorial ICH treated with navigation-guided catheter placement and intrahematoma alteplase irrigation (0.5 mg, n=14; 1.0 mg, n=13). Serial computed tomography assessed residual hematoma volume and percentage reduction. Alteplase administrations, catheter indwelling duration, and changes in Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores were compared.

RESULTS: Residual hematoma volumes did not differ significantly between groups at 24, 48, 72, or 96 hours. At 24 hours, median hematoma volume reductions were 35.5% and 44.2%, respectively (P=0.198). Final volume reductions were 74.5% and 73.0% (P=0.344). Alteplase administrations (9.2±2.8 vs. 9.2±3.8, P=0.990) and catheter indwelling duration (77.1±31.8 vs. 79.4±30.0 hours, P=0.621) did not differ significantly. Between-group changes in GCS and NIHSS scores were also nonsignificant.

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant differences in hematoma evacuation, procedural outcomes, or short-term neurological outcomes were detected between the two regimens in this small retrospective cohort. These exploratory findings require validation in larger prospective studies to determine the optimal alteplase dose for catheter-based evacuation of spontaneous ICH.

articles.title: Temporal patterns of soil microorganisms near buried corpses and the development of a model for estimating postmortem interval.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accurately determining the postmortem interval is a critical challenge in forensic practice. As soil serves as a key environmental medium for cadaver decomposition, its microbial communities may carry time-specific information. This study investigates the temporal succession patterns of soil microorganisms surrounding buried cadavers and explores the feasibility of translating these patterns into a quantitative predictive model.

METHODS: A soil burial model using rat carcasses was established, with sampling conducted at 12 time points between 0 and 60 days. After extracting soil microbial DNA, Illumina MiSeq sequencing was performed. Community composition analysis, alpha diversity calculations, NMDS analysis, and LEfSe-based differential species screening were employed to reveal microbial succession patterns; A feature embedding strategy was employed for dimensionality reduction, combined with a random forest regression algorithm, to construct a PMI prediction model across seven taxonomic levels from phylum to OTU. Model performance was evaluated using R2, MAE, RMSE, and Pearson correlation coefficients.

RESULTS: The soil microbial community exhibited significant phasic succession over time following death; alpha diversity and richness indices peaked at 6 days PMI and then continued to decline; NMDS analysis confirmed a three-phase succession pattern in community structure; LEfSe identified 30 time-dependent differentially expressed taxonomic units (candidate microbial biomarkers).

CONCLUSION: The soil microbial community beneath a buried body exhibits a regular temporal succession pattern and can serve as a biological indicator for estimating PMI. The order-level predictive model, constructed based on 16 S rRNA sequencing and the Random Forest algorithm, demonstrated high goodness of fit and predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.9370, MAE = 4.05 days, RMSE = 4.98 days, r = 0.9687), providing a reliable microbiome-based technical approach for forensic time-of-death estimation within the 0-60-day PMI window.

articles.title: Postmortem histopathology of the heart in right dominant arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM-R) - a systematic literature review.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM), particularly its classical right-dominant form historically termed arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), is a rare but important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD) in young adults, posing significant challenges in forensic practice. Postmortem diagnosis relies primarily on careful macroscopic and histopathological examination, as clinical or genetic information is often unavailable. This review of published autopsy cases highlights fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricular myocardium as the most consistent histological finding, while macroscopic features such as ventricular wall thinning, dilation, or fatty infiltration were less consistently reported. Considerable variability exists in tissue sampling strategies, staining methods and criteria applied for diagnosis. Postmortem genetic testing is rarely performed due to logistical and financial constraints. These limitations complicate the establishment of standardized diagnostic thresholds and may affect forensic determinations of cause of death. Nonetheless, systematic histopathological evaluation remains essential for identifying ACM-R and can guide targeted molecular analyses in selected cases. The findings emphasize the need for standardized protocols for tissue sampling and histological assessment, ideally supported by multicenter reference collections. Such measures would improve diagnostic reliability, reproducibility, and forensic robustness in the postmortem identification of ACM/ACM-R.

articles.title: Immediate blood‑mediated inflammatory reaction in islet transplantation: evidence and consequences for short‑term graft function.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: The instant blood‑mediated inflammatory reaction (IBMIR) is a major cause of early islet loss in intraportal islet transplantation. However, direct clinical evidence for the IBMIR in human recipients remains scarce, and its relationship with short‑term graft function has not been systematically evaluated. This study aimed to characterise the IBMIR in clinical islet transplantation and assess its association with graft function.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 27 patients with diabetes who underwent 34 allogeneic islet transplant procedures were enrolled. Serial blood samples were collected pre‑transplant and at 2 h and 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 days post‑transplant to measure coagulation, complement component, platelet, cytokine and lymphocyte parameters. Short‑term graft function was assessed by the BETA-2 score at 1 month, with a score ≥17.4 indicating good function. LASSO regression with bootstrap stability assessment (500 iterations) and Firth penalised logistic regression were used to identify independent predictors.

RESULTS: Rapid coagulation activation and platelet consumption occurred immediately after islet infusion, accompanied by transient elevations of IL-6, TNF-α, IL-10 and IFN-γ, while complement component activation was modest. Profound lymphocyte depletion was observed but was attributed to induction immunosuppression. Good graft function was achieved in 13 out of 34 procedures (38.2%). Independent predictors included pre‑transplant platelet count (OR 0.982, p=0.044), T cell count (OR 0.997, p=0.038), proportion of B cells (OR 0.828, p=0.018), post‑transplant B cell count (OR 0.949, p=0.002), IL-4 (OR 1.680, p=0.038) and fibrin degradation products (FDP) (OR 0.946, p=0.045). The AUCs of the receiver operating characteristic curve (95% CI) for predicting good graft function were 0.842 (0.697, 0.988) for post‑transplant B cell count, 0.782 (0.602, 0.962) for pre‑transplant proportion of B cells, 0.753 (0.581, 0.924) for pre‑transplant T cell count, 0.703 (0.521, 0.886) for platelet count, 0.694 (0.504, 0.884) for post‑transplant IL-4, and 0.668 (0.482, 0.855) for FDP.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: This study provides comprehensive clinical evidence that the IBMIR occurs in human islet transplantation, and that the severity of IBMIR‑related responses is associated with short‑term graft function. Integrated monitoring of coagulation, inflammatory and immune parameters may assist in both prognostic assessment and clinical decision‑making, guiding peri‑transplant management and early intervention to improve graft outcomes.

articles.title: BTB and CNC homology 1 deficiency mitigated ischemia/reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury in a glutaredoxin-2-dependent manner.
articles.abstract: The BTB and CNC homology 1 (Bach1) suppresses the transcription of antioxidant genes through binding to antioxidant response elements in the promoter regions. Glutaredoxin-2 (Grx2) is essential for maintaining mitochondrial function under oxidative stress conditions. This study investigates the hypothesis that Bach1 exacerbates ischemia/reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) through inhibiting Grx2 expression. Wild-type C57BL/6 J and Bach1 knockout (Bach1-/-) mice were employed to establish acute renal I/R injury models. An in vitro hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model was constructed using HK-2 cells. HK-2 cells were transfected with Bach1 siRNA, Grx2 siRNA, and Grx2 overexpression plasmid. Dual-luciferase reporter assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirmed the regulatory relationship between Bach1 and Grx2. Furthermore, the effects of the Bach1 inhibitor HPPE on renal ischemia-reperfusion injury were investigated. Grx2 was significantly downregulated while Bach1 was predominantly upregulated in the kidneys of I/R-induced AKI mice, patients with acute tubular necrosis, and H/R-injured HK-2 cells. Grx2 overexpression mitigated mitochondrial oxidative stress and restored mitochondrial function. luciferase reporter assays and electrophoretic mobility shift assays confirmed that Bach1 acts as a transcription factor that directly interacts with the GLRX2 promoter. Bach1 deletion upregulated Grx2 expression both in vivo and in vitro, leading to improvements in mitochondrial dysfunction and renal proximal tubule injury. Furthermore, HPPE, a Bach1 inhibitor, enhanced Grx2 expression in H/R-injured HK-2 cells, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and renal proximal tubule injury. Bach1 deficiency attenuates I/R-induced AKI via a Grx2-dependent mechanism. Therefore, targeting Bach1 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for mitigating ischemia/reperfusion-induced AKI. KEY MESSAGES: Bach1 induces oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in renal ischemia/reperfusion injury. Bach 1 deficiency mitigated renal ischemia/reperfusion injury via upregulating glutaredoxin-2. Targeting Bach1 may be a promising intervention strategy for renal ischemia/reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Preoperative Sepsis Severity and Outcomes After Appendectomy for Complicated Appendicitis in Children: A NSQIP-P Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complicated appendicitis in children is associated with substantial morbidity, but outcomes remain heterogeneous. We evaluated whether preoperative sepsis severity is associated with postoperative outcomes after appendectomy for complicated appendicitis.

METHODS: The 2016-2022 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program-Pediatric database was queried for patients younger than 18 years undergoing appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Patients were stratified as no sepsis, systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS), sepsis, or septic shock within 72 hours of surgery. The primary outcome was 30-day composite postoperative morbidity. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between sepsis severity and morbidity.

RESULTS: Among 34,436 children, 27.6% had no sepsis, 8.7% had SIRS, 63.4% had sepsis, and 0.3% had septic shock. Composite morbidity occurred in 11.1%, 11%, 17.5%, and 43.1%, respectively (P<.001). Organ-space surgical site infection, unplanned reoperation, postoperative percutaneous drainage, and hospital length of stay were greatest with sepsis and septic shock. Three patients with septic shock died (2.9%; P<.001). On multivariable analysis, sepsis (aOR 1.64, 95% CI 1.53-1.77; P<.001) and septic shock (aOR 2.78, 95% CI 1.67-4.62; P<.001) were associated with increased postoperative morbidity after adjustment for demographic and clinical covariates.

CONCLUSIONS: Increasing preoperative sepsis severity is associated with worse outcomes after appendectomy for complicated appendicitis in children and may inform risk stratification, perioperative planning, and postoperative surveillance before operative findings are available to treating clinicians.

TYPE OF STUDY: Retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: WHO 2024 altitude-adjusted first-trimester hemoglobin and gestational diabetes mellitus: a two-center case-control study in Peru.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between 2024 World Health Organization (WHO) altitude-adjusted first-trimester hemoglobin concentration and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) in women receiving care at two Peruvian centers located at markedly different elevations.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, unmatched case-control study of singleton pregnancy episodes managed between 2018 and 2024 at referral hospitals in Cajamarca (2,750 m) and Trujillo (34 m). First-trimester hemoglobin was adjusted for altitude according to WHO 2024 recommendations. Associations with GDM were estimated using unconditional logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors, adjusting for maternal age, body mass index category, recorded parity, educational level, and study site. Because case and control sampling fractions differed between centers, the study-site coefficient was treated as a design adjustment rather than an etiologic association.

RESULTS: The analysis included 318 pregnancy episodes, comprising 126 GDM cases and 192 controls. Each 1 g/dL increase in altitude-adjusted hemoglobin was associated with higher odds of GDM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.17, 95 % confidence interval [CI] 1.64-2.87; p<0.001). An altitude-adjusted hemoglobin concentration ≥13 g/dL was associated with substantially higher odds of GDM (aOR 5.29, 95 % CI 3.03-9.22; p<0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of nonlinearity (p=0.556), and there was no evidence of effect modification by study site (p for interaction=0.962).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher WHO 2024 altitude-adjusted first-trimester hemoglobin was independently associated with subsequent GDM across both study settings. These findings support altitude-adjusted early-pregnancy hemoglobin as a potentially informative risk marker, but not as a diagnostic or screening threshold.

articles.title: Flavonoids in the Prevention and Treatment of Liver Diseases: Research Progress and Future Perspectives.
articles.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
articles.abstract: The liver is a central metabolic organ essential for maintaining physiological homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely associated with the development and progression of various chronic diseases. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) have become major causes of chronic liver injury worldwide, posing a substantial public health burden. Flavonoids are naturally occurring polyphenolic compounds widely distributed in plants. Representative flavonoids, including quercetin, epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), luteolin, naringenin, and puerarin, exhibit diverse biological activities, such as anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metabolic regulatory effects, highlighting their therapeutic potential in liver diseases. This review systematically summarizes the preventive and therapeutic roles of flavonoids in MASLD and ALD, with particular emphasis on their underlying molecular mechanisms. Current evidence indicates that flavonoids protect against liver injury by regulating glucose and lipid metabolism, alleviating oxidative stress and inflammation, modulating the gut microbiota and maintaining gut-liver axis homeostasis, thereby reducing hepatic lipid accumulation and hepatocellular injury and ultimately attenuating disease progression. We also discuss the major challenges limiting their clinical application, including low bioavailability, interindividual variability, insufficient long-term safety data, limited large-scale clinical evidence, and potential drug interactions. Future research should focus on structural optimization, advanced drug delivery systems, combination therapies, and microbiota-based personalized interventions. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive mechanistic framework for the hepatoprotective effects of flavonoids and offers a theoretical basis for their development as promising therapeutic agents and nutritional interventions for liver diseases.

articles.title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics.
articles.abstract: Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype-specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

articles.title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

articles.title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss.
articles.abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic's fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave-mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

articles.title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and Gdf15 knockout (Gdf15-/-) mice are partially protected from CKD-induced anorexia and weight loss despite worsening renal function and inflammation. GDF15 receptor Gfral knockout (Gfral-/-) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed Gdf15-/- and Gfral-/- mice exhibited phenotypic and molecular divergence. Pair feeding in Gdf15-/- mice reverses loss-of-GDF15's effect on body weight but does not restore renal functions. In contrast, pair feeding in Gfral-/- mice reverses loss-of-GFRAL's effect on both body weight and renal function. Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

articles.title: rTMS attenuates microglial phagocytosis and promotes neurorepair in a photothrombotic stroke mouse model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on functional recovery in photothrombotic (PT) stroke mice and whether rTMS promotes neurorepair by modulating microglial phagocytosis.

METHODS: Eight-week-old male C57BL/6J mice were used to establish a focal stroke model via photothrombosis (PT group). The Sham group and PT + rTMS group were included. rTMS was initiated 24 h after modeling. Neurological deficits were assessed. Microglial activation, synaptic phagocytosis, neuronal injury and the levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) were evaluated. Differentially expressed proteins and core regulatory pathways were analyzed.

RESULTS: rTMS treatment significantly increased body weight, prolonged the latency to fall and shortened the balance beam crossing time, reduced foot faults, and improved the discrimination index in PT mice. rTMS reduced the number of Iba1-positive microglia and CD68-positive cells, attenuated microglial synaptic phagocytosis and alleviated neuronal loss and apoptosis. rTMS significantly decreased the levels of TNF-α, IL-6 and IL-1β in the brain. A total of 416 differentially expressed proteins were identified between the PT and PT + rTMS groups. The differentially expressed proteins were significantly enriched in microglial phagocytosis pathways and related signaling pathways.

CONCLUSIONS: rTMS significantly ameliorates neurological deficits and cognitive impairment in PT stroke mice. The underlying mechanism may involve the inhibition of excessive microglial activation, attenuation of microglia-mediated synaptic phagocytosis and alleviation of neuroinflammation. Proteomic analysis reveals that rTMS modulates the expression of proteins associated with microglial phagocytosis-related signaling pathways, which may contribute to the observed post-stroke neurorepair effects.

articles.title: Long-term stability of cellular-resolution brain-computer interface recordings after stroke.
articles.abstract: Objective.Implantable brain-computer interfaces (iBCIs) with single-neuron resolution are showing great promise for restoring mobility and communication in individuals with spinal cord injury or motor neuron disease. Stroke is the most common cause of acquired brain injury and a major contributor to long-term disability, making chronic stroke a highly relevant indication for iBCIs. However, whether stable intracortical recordings can be obtained from the structurally lesioned human brain is unknown.Approach.We report recordings from four 64-channel microelectrode arrays implanted in a participant with chronic aphasia after a large left-hemispheric stroke. The arrays targeted right-hemispheric frontoparietal regions homotopic to the damaged left-hemispheric language network.Main results.Across 111 sessions spanning 1240 days, unit yield and signal quality remained stable. Waveform-based tracking reliably identified individual units across sessions, including across extended recording gaps. Short- and long-term unit stability was comparable to previous reports from iBCI participants without structural brain lesions, and tracked units showed consistent spiking properties across sessions.Significance.Our findings provide the first evidence that single-neuron recordings can remain stable over the long term following a large hemispheric stroke involving substantial cortical and subcortical injury. They establish the feasibility of chronic, cellular-resolution iBCIs after stroke and support the development of neurorestorative applications for deficits caused by structural brain injury.

articles.title: A conditional diffusion synthesis of DWI and ADC maps for early stroke support.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. Effective treatment is associated with fast and effective lesion quantification from image observations. non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is the common first imaging to discard other neurological conditions, but it has limited sensitivity for detecting early ischemic changes. In addition, Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) studies are considered the gold standard for early lesion characterization through diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) sequences and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps. Nonetheless, the analysis from MRI images is delayed, restricted for some patient conditions, and typically limited because of accessibility constraints. Although recent approaches have addressed these limitations by synthesizing DW-MRI from NCCT, they often fail to reproduce ischemic lesions. Moreover, their performance is usually reported with whole-image metrics, which can overestimate image quality. This work explores the capability of conditional diffusion models to synthesize DWI sequences and ADC maps from NCCT to support care protocols in early stroke scenarios. In particular, we explore both a direct synthesis from NCCT to ADC and a conditional cascade configuration. In the cascade, the NCCT is used as a conditioning input to generate synthetic DWI findings. Then, the corresponding ADC maps are generated from the synthetic DWI. The conditional diffusion models outperformed the U-Net, Pix2Pix and CycleGAN baselines in the brain region, reaching an SSIM of 0.53 for DWI and up to 0.36 for ADC. Direct diffusion achieved a higher global ADC fidelity than cascade diffusion (SSIM 0.87 vs 0.83), whereas cascade diffusion obtained a lower ADC error within the lesion (MAE 0.19 vs 0.22).

articles.title: Monte Carlo simulation of a neuroimaging acquisition with MAPSSIC, aβ+sensitive intracerebral microprobe for awake and freely moving rats.
articles.abstract: Objective.Establishing robust correlations between molecular neuroimaging and behavioral studies is essential in preclinical research to advance our understanding of brain function and to critically assess the translational relevance of animal models in drug development. Achieving this goal, however, requires imaging animals while they are awake and freely moving-an ongoing challenge, as most preclinical imaging techniques rely on anesthesia.Approach.To overcome the limitations imposed by anesthesia, the MAPSSIC project aims to develop a novel implantable pixelated probe based on monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS), designed for use in awake, freely moving rats. By virtue of its direct implantation within the targeted brain regions, the MAPSSIC probe enables the local detection of short-rangeparticles emitted by radiotracers, in contrast to conventional micro-PET systems that rely on detecting coincident annihilation-rays. In this study, we present Monte Carlo simulations of a typicalin vivobrain imaging experiment using [C]Raclopride, a commonly employed-emitting radiotracer, to evaluate the probe's performance.Main results.Results show that over 93% of detected events originate from particles emitted within the first 2 mm surrounding the probe while also allowing to quantify variations of 5%-30% of the non-displaceable binding potential (BP) with discrepancy of less than 4% compared to micro-PET.Significance.This Monte Carlo study demonstrates the device's ability to capture small variations of BPbased on spatially localized information, validating its suitability for quantitative kinetic analysis in brain structures such as the striatum.

articles.title: Large-Field Single-Cell Morphodynamic Scattering Imaging Enables Rapid, Heterogeneity-Resolved Phenotypic Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing.
articles.abstract: Timely antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) is essential for the management of bloodstream infections, yet conventional phenotypic AST relies primarily on bulk bacterial growth, requiring prolonged incubation and masking clinically relevant population heterogeneity. Here, we present a morphology-based AST approach that quantifies time-resolved responses of individual bacteria as an alternative phenotypic measure of antimicrobial susceptibility. Large-field, label-free scattering imaging enables parallel monitoring of thousands of bacteria, while deep learning-assisted segmentation provides quantitative extraction of integrated scattering intensity and image-derived geometric features during β-lactam antibiotic exposure. This high-throughput single-cell analysis preserves population heterogeneity and supports measurements across clinically relevant samples. Distinct antibiotic-dependent morphodynamic trajectories emerged within 60 min, enabling rapid susceptibility determination while retaining information beyond binary growth inhibition.
