These single-cell response profiles further enabled preliminary minimum inhibitory concentration determination, evaluation of responses to antibiotic combinations, and quantification of resistant subpopulations in a defined susceptible-resistant mixture. Direct analysis of ten clinical positive blood culture samples tested against five antibiotics achieved 96.7% categorical agreement with the clinical reference method, with an estimated post-positivity workflow time of approximately 95 min. These findings establish time-resolved single-cell morphology as an informative phenotypic measure for rapid AST that preserves drug-dependent response patterns and bacterial population heterogeneity.

articles.title: Quantum Sensing Technologies for Ultrasensitive Biomarker Detection in Biomedical Diagnostics from Fundamental Principles to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Quantum sensing technologies offer unprecedented detection sensitivities down to single-molecule, attomolar detection limits and thus are emerging as transformative tools for ultra-sensitive biomarker detection in biomedical diagnostics. This comprehensive review synthesizes insights from over 380 plus studies to provide recent advances in quantum sensor platforms, examining the fundamental quantum mechanical principles that enable enhanced sensitivity, and surveys a diverse range of quantum sensing technologies along with their applications across the biomedical field. Specifically, nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, quantum dots, superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), and other quantum sensing modalities applied to biomarker detection for cancer diagnostics, cardiovascular disease, neurological disorders, and infectious disease detection are reviewed. Further, the key technical challenges that hurdle their clinical translation are critically evaluated. The review results demonstrate that quantum-enhanced biosensors have achieved detection limits of the order of magnitude below conventional methods. Intrinsic to their capabilities, several quantum sensing platforms have progressed to clinical testing and early commercialization efforts. Specifically, for point-of-care diagnosis, early disease detection, and personalized medicine.

articles.title: Texturing Behavior-Empowered PANI-Wrapping C-Fe2O3 Hierarchical Microarchitectures for Wearable Ammonia and Pressure Sensing.
articles.abstract: Simultaneously monitoring ammonia (NH3) leakage and human motion is desirable for safeguarding astronauts' safety in spacecraft equipped with NH3-driven propulsion, in which stable and selective NH3 sensing combined with reliable pressure detection is highly required. However, little is reported on a sensing material that synergistically presents the required NH3 and pressure sensing. Here, wearable NH3 and pressure sensing has been developed using PANI-wrapping carbon-intermixed Fe2O3 hierarchical microarchitectures (PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs), which have been synthesized by employing fern-shaped C-Fe2O3 HMAs with trunk/branches as structural precursors, followed by conformal PANI-wrapping. Beneficially, PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs present a wide detection range of 0.1 ppm-10 v/v%, 167-day-long stability and high selectivity toward NH3. Further, a pressure sensor prototype has been constructed by laminating PET tapes onto the HMAs-integrated flexible electrode, revealing an excellent pressure-dependent response and machine-learning-assisted human-motion recognition. Such superior dual sensing is attributed to the texturing behavior, in which conformal texturing of PANI along the hierarchical surface of C-Fe2O3 HMAs establishes heterojunctions with a built-in electric field to amplify resistance modulation, while fern-shaped HMAs with trunk/branches provide abundant active interfaces and electron transport pathways. Practically, a wearable dual-sensing device that integrates flexible NH3 and pressure sensor prototypes has been built with reliable dual-sensing responses.

articles.title: Activating Zn Sites of Au/ZnO Nanocages via Au Clusters Enables Highly Sensitive Acetone Detection for Diabetes Screening.
articles.abstract: Although acetone in exhaled breath is a reliable biomarker for diabetes mellitus, its trace-level detection under high-humidity conditions remains challenging for early noninvasive diagnosis. In this study, Au-loaded ZnO nanocages derived from ZIF-8 were synthesized. The 0.4 wt % Au/ZnO-based sensor exhibits an ultrahigh response of 260.6 toward 40 ppm acetone, a theoretical detection limit as low as 0.468 ppb, fast response/recovery (2/116 s), excellent selectivity, and long-term stability. Moreover, it successfully distinguishes simulated exhaled breath of healthy individuals from that of diabetic patients under 90% RH. Theoretical calculations reveal that Au clusters activate neighboring Zn sites through electronic transfer, enhancing the chemical adsorption capacity of Zn sites for acetone molecules-a mechanism that goes beyond the conventional view of increased adsorbed oxygen. These findings provide new insights into the activation of active sites by noble metal loading and offer a promising strategy for designing highly sensitive and humidity-resistant acetone sensors toward noninvasive diabetes screening.

articles.title: Nanobody-Based Lateral Flow Assays: Applications, Innovations, Challenges, and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Nanobody-based lateral flow assays (LFAs) are an emerging class of point-of-care diagnostics that combine enhanced thermal stability, target affinity comparable to or in some cases exceeding that of conventional antibodies, and low-cost recombinant production of nanobodies with the versatility of conventional antibody-based detection formats. This review examines recent progress in nanobody engineering, assay architecture, and signal amplification strategies that improve analytical sensitivity, specificity, and multiplexing potential. Despite these advances, several technical and translational challenges persist, including broad analyte compatibility, difficulties in optimal nanobody pair selection, scalability of expression systems, and the need for robust and reproducible conjugation chemistries. The growing integration of computational modeling and AI-driven nanobody design has accelerated the discovery and optimization pipelines, yet standardized frameworks for validation and benchmarking remain scarce. Addressing these limitations will be important for the further clinical translation and commercial deployment of nanobody-based LFAs across diverse applications in infectious disease diagnostics, food safety testing, and environmental monitoring.

articles.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
articles.abstract: Rapid, portable detection of multiple nucleic acid targets is essential for infectious disease surveillance and precision oncology. CRISPR-based diagnostics have set a high bar for sensitivity and single-base specificity, yet their reliance on collateral nuclease activity complicates multiplexing, integration with amplification, and point-of-care deployment. Here, we present TIMBER (templated incision mediated by endonucleases of repair), a non-CRISPR platform that achieves comparable performance without nonspecific nuclease activity. TIMBER uses a repair endonuclease to cleave probes containing abasic sites only when they are hybridized to a matched target. The system exhibits strong specificity, enabling single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination. TIMBER provides an analytical limit of detection of 12 pM without preamplification or one copy per μL (1.6 aM) with preamplification through RT-PCR or RT-LAMP, with results observable by visual fluorescence or on lateral flow. We deploy TIMBER to detect SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and further demonstrate multiplex detection of four targets, enabling identification of EGFR mutations in lung cancer samples. This approach offers a flexible, rapid, and low-instrument-ready solution for diverse nucleic acid diagnostics, from viral detection to cancer genotyping.

articles.title: Clinical Practice Guideline: The Diagnosis, Treatment, and Follow-Up Management of Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) is a life-threatening thrombotic microangiopathy. The global incidence of immune-mediated TTP (iTTP) is 1-6 cases per million people per year. The new (S3-level) clinical practice guideline is the first in the German-speaking world to compile evidence- and consensus-based recommendations on the diagnosis, treatment, follow-up management, and care of patients with immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (iTTP) and congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (cTTP).

METHODS: This clinical practice guideline was developed under the aegis of the Society for Thrombosis and Hemostatsis Research (Gesellschaft für Thrombose- und Hämostaseforschung, GTH) according to the criteria for S3-level guidelines issued by the Association of the Scientific Medical Societies in Germany (Arbeitsgemeinschaft der Wissenschaftlichen Medizinischen Fachgesellschaften, AWMF). It is based on information from publications retrieved through systematic literature searches and a structured assessment of the evidence using the GRADE scheme (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation), with a formal consensus process.

RESULTS: Early diagnosis of TTP is essential. Measurement of ADAMTS13 activity is the diagnostic gold standard. In case of clinical suspicion of acute iTTP, treatment with plasma exchange, corticosteroids, and caplacizumab should be initiated at once. In a randomized trial with an active control group, plasma exchange lowered mortality at the end of the first treatment cycle from 15.7% to 3.9%. In a cohort study, standard treatment with plasma exchange, corticosteroids, caplacizumab, and rituximab was associated with a mortality of 2.2%, compared to 12.2% in a historical control cohort. Further management consists of regular clinical follow-up, ADAMTS13 monitoring, and the detection and treatment of late sequelae. For pregnancy in female TTP patients, monitoring and recurrence prophylaxis are recommended.

CONCLUSION: The purpose of the clinical practice guideline is to improve the acute care and interdisciplinary management of TTP. Further research is needed on the use of recombinant ADAMTS13 and on the definition of uTTP (TTP in the absence of causative antibodies or genetic mutations).

articles.title: From Answers to Agents: What Must Change Before Generative and Agentic AI Becomes Clinical Infrastructure in Hematology?
articles.journal: Turkish journal of haematology : official journal of Turkish Society of Haematology
articles.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence in hematology is entering a new phase. The prevailing question of whether large language models are accurate enough for clinical decision support is being overtaken by a more difficult challenge as systems shift from answering questions to acting: extracting structured cases, routing them, classifying variants, and grounding recommendations in guidelines and case memory. In 2026, a hematology agent achieved roughly 83% concordance with tumor-board decisions in a prospective silent trial with hallucinations in 0.3% of cases, suggesting that for well-structured tasks the binding constraint is shifting from accuracy to governability. Moving from experimental support to reliable infrastructure requires four changes: validating trajectories rather than answers, allocating autonomy inversely to case complexity, treating deployed models as regulated instruments under continuous surveillance, and engineering against automation bias, with data-privacy and consent safeguards throughout. For hematologists, this reframes AI adoption as a governance and human-factors program rather than a search for a better model.

articles.title: When Thrombosis and Hemorrhage Coexist: A Case of Pediatric Septic Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of haematology : official journal of Turkish Society of Haematology

articles.title: Field-Deployable Paper-Based Detection of Vibrio vulnificus via Mechanically Automated Sequential RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a.
articles.abstract: Vibrio vulnificus (V. vulnificus) is a highly virulent marine pathogen that causes severe infections, including sepsis and necrotizing fasciitis, with high fatality rates in susceptible individuals. Rapid and sensitive on-site detection is therefore essential, yet existing methods often depend on laboratory-based equipment and trained personnel, limiting field applicability. Here, we present an automated, paper-based RPA/CRISPR-Cas12a diagnostic platform that integrates a microfluidic paper pad with a spiral-spring-driven mechanical actuator. The device enables sequential execution of recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), CRISPR-Cas12a-mediated detection, and lateral flow assay (LFA) readout through a single user-initiated winding step, without the need for external power or instrumentation. The multistep process was achieved through automatic reconfiguration of the paper pads, enabling pipette-free transfer of RPA amplicons from the paper-based RPA pad to the paper-based CRISPR pad, followed by transfer of the reporter probes to the LFA strip. The paper-based system is preloaded with lyophilized reagents and designed to autonomously control fluid flow and reaction timing. Targeting the vvhA gene specific to V. vulnificus, the platform achieved a limit of detection of 1 colony-forming unit per reaction (CFU/reaction) in pure cultures. This sensitivity was consistently reproduced in gill swab samples from oysters exposed to artificially contaminated seawater at 20 CFU/mL, confirming that reliable detection was achievable in oyster gill swabs under these conditions. Overall, this work establishes a fully mechanical, instrument-free RPA/CRISPR-based diagnostic system for V. vulnificus, offering a rapid, portable, and highly sensitive approach for point-of-care testing and food safety applications.

articles.title: Persistent Apical Periodontitis Associated with Extraradicular Calculus-Like Deposits Involving an Adjacent Vital Tooth: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Extraradicular calculus-like deposits are uncommon in post-treatment apical periodontitis and difficult to characterise before surgery. A 26-year-old man presented with a persistent sinus tract related to tooth 21 despite root canal treatment and retreatment. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) showed a defect extending to the palatal/distal root surface of tooth 22, which responded normally to cold and electric pulp sensibility testing; small plaque-like/punctate radiopaque foci were closely adherent to that root surface. Tooth 22 underwent root canal treatment after caries removal because apical resection was anticipated. Microsurgical exploration revealed hard dark-grey deposits on the apical surface of tooth 21 and more extensively on tooth 22. The deposits and granulation tissue were removed, root-end resection and retrograde filling were performed and histology showed chronic inflammatory tissue. Tooth 23 remained pulp-responsive throughout follow-up. At 21 months, the sinus tract had resolved and radiographic bone fill was evident. Because no microbiological or compositional analysis was performed, the deposits' origin and causal role cannot be established. This case documents an uncommon association between persistent apical periodontitis and extraradicular calculus-like deposits involving the root surface of an adjacent tooth with preserved preoperative pulp sensibility and illustrates the value of CBCT and microsurgical inspection.

articles.title: Intercellular crosstalk and functional heterogeneity of hepatic stellate cells: A translational framework for chronic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver diseases are a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with hepatic fibrosis representing the common pathological pathway that can lead to cirrhosis, portal hypertension and hepatocellular carcinoma. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are the principal source of myofibroblasts during liver fibrogenesis and have therefore emerged as central therapeutic targets. However, recent advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial omics and lineage-tracing approaches have fundamentally revised the traditional view of HSC activation as a uniform process. Instead, HSCs comprise a spectrum of phenotypically and functionally distinct states that dynamically evolve in response to chronic liver injury and differ in their contributions to extracellular matrix deposition, inflammation, immune regulation, vascular remodelling and tissue repair. During disease progression, HSCs integrate biochemical, metabolic and biomechanical cues derived from injured hepatocytes, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, immune cells and the extracellular matrix, while simultaneously reshaping the hepatic microenvironment through reciprocal intercellular communication mediated by soluble factors, extracellular vesicles, direct cell-cell interactions and matrix-derived signals. This bidirectional crosstalk underlies both fibrosis progression and its potential regression, highlighting HSC plasticity as a defining feature of chronic liver disease. In this review, we discuss the emerging concepts of HSC phenotypic heterogeneity and intercellular communication, summarizing the molecular mechanisms that govern HSC state transitions and their interactions within the hepatic niche. Finally, we examine how these discoveries are transforming current approaches to precision anti-fibrotic therapies, providing a translational framework for the treatment of chronic liver diseases.

articles.title: Comparative effects of metformin, semaglutide and tirzepatide on oxidative stress, thiol-disulfide homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Oxidative stress, impaired thiol-disulfide (DIS) homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage contribute to vascular complications in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We compared redox-related biomarker changes among patients receiving metformin, semaglutide, or tirzepatide and examined associations between thiol-DIS homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: 141 participants with T2DM were categorised according to prescribed glucose-lowering management and followed for 3 months. Anthropometric measures, glycaemic indices, oxidative stress markers, thiol-DIS homeostasis parameters and serum 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) were assessed at baseline and follow-up. Correlation analyses examined associations with changes in 8-OHdG, and multivariable regression assessed the independent association between changes in native thiol (NT) and 8-OHdG.

KEY RESULTS: Improvements in weight, glycaemic control and insulin resistance were observed in all active treatment groups. Greater improvements in redox status and thiol-DIS homeostasis were observed in the semaglutide and tirzepatide groups than in the metformin group. Oxidative DNA damage decreased during follow-up in all active treatment groups, with the greatest reductions observed in the semaglutide and tirzepatide groups. Changes in NT showed the strongest association with oxidative DNA damage and remained independently associated after adjustment for selected covariates.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Metformin, semaglutide and tirzepatide treatment was associated with improvements in redox status, thiol-DIS homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage, with greater changes in the semaglutide and tirzepatide groups. NT may have the potential as a biomarker of treatment response and support an association between changes in thiol-DIS homeostasis and oxidative DNA damage during contemporary antidiabetic therapy.

articles.title: Contrast-Enhanced Dual-Energy CT for Differentiating Paragangliomas From Other Neck Masses: A Quantitative Diagnostic Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: To assess the diagnostic utility of contrast-enhanced dual-energy CT (DECT) in differentiating paragangliomas from other neck masses by evaluating the diagnostic performance of individual quantitative spectral parameters.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this institutional ethics committee-approved ambispective study, 62 patients with suspected neck masses were included, yielding 70 lesions. All lesions underwent contrast-enhanced DECT. Quantitative analysis included iodine, calcium, hydroxyapatite, and uric acid concentrations, lesion attenuation, and lesion location. The reference standard was histopathology or DOTANOC PET/CT findings, depending on clinical feasibility. The diagnostic performance of individual quantitative DECT parameters was assessed separately using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Paragangliomas showed significantly higher iodine and hydroxyapatite concentrations but lower mean contrast-enhanced attenuation than nonparaganglioma neck masses (p ≤ 0.001). An iodine concentration threshold ≥ 3.9 mg/mL achieved 93% sensitivity and 76% specificity, while a uric acid concentration threshold ≤ 928 mg/cm3 achieved 96% specificity. ROC-derived thresholds were identified and evaluated separately for the individual quantitative DECT parameters.

CONCLUSION: Contrast-enhanced DECT demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for differentiating paragangliomas from the heterogeneous group of nonparaganglioma neck masses included in this study, with iodine concentration showing the strongest individual discriminatory performance. These individual quantitative DECT parameters may aid preoperative lesion characterization; however, further validation in larger independent cohorts is required.

articles.title: Detection of Wolbachia (Rickettsiales: Anaplasmataceae) strain in Aedes albopictus (Diptera: Culicidae) from diverse breeding habitats in Sarawak, Malaysian Borneo: First report on baseline data for dengue vector control strategies.
articles.abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health issue in Malaysia, and Sarawak reports an increasing number of cases each year. Wolbachia (Rickettsiales: Anaplasmataceae), an endosymbiotic bacterium naturally found in some insect populations, offers a new method for controlling dengue vectors by releasing Wolbachia-infected Aedes mosquitoes. However, there is currently a scarcity of baseline data on natural Wolbachia infection status in mosquito populations from Sarawak. A cross-sectional study was conducted from March to May 2025 across 21 locations within a higher education institution campus in Sarawak. Mosquito larvae and pupae were collected from active breeding sites, reared to adulthood and identified morphologically using taxonomic keys. Wolbachia detection was performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) targeting the Wolbachia surface protein (wsp) gene for strains A and B. Additionally, the dengue virus was detected by reverse-transcriptase PCR (RT-PCR). A total of 277 mosquito larvae and pupae were collected from 32 active breeding sites. Fifteen different breeding habitat types were identified, with tires (28.9%) and discarded containers (23.5%) being the most common. Morphological identification of 119 successfully emerged adults revealed that 93.3% (n = 111) were Aedes albopictus and 6.7% (n = 8) were Culex quinquefasciatus. No Aedes aegypti was recorded. Clear water (59.4%) was the predominant water quality at breeding sites, followed by turbid (34.4%) and polluted (6.3%). Wolbachia screening of 14 pooled A. albopictus samples showed an overall pool positivity rate of 42.9% (6/14 pools). As exact pool sizes were not recorded, this value could not be converted to individual-level prevalence and should be interpreted as an upper bound. A single infection with the Wolbachia strain B was detected in two pools, while superinfection with both strains A and B was observed in four pools. No single Wolbachia A infection was detected. Likewise, all samples tested negative for the dengue virus.This study provides the first baseline data on natural Wolbachia infection in A. albopictus populations from Sarawak. The presence of both single and superinfections suggests the potential for utilizing Wolbachia-based vector control strategies in the region. These findings will inform future planning for the release of Wolbachia-infected Aedes mosquitoes as part of integrated dengue control programs in Sarawak.

articles.title: Association of Feeding Therapy Timing and Frequency With Time to Independent Oral Feeding in Infants With Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize feeding therapy utilization and delivery patterns and examine associations of therapy dose (timing and frequency) with time to independent oral feeding in infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE).

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of infants with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia and discharged feeding independently by mouth from two Level IV neonatal intensive care unit (NICUs) between 2017 and 2024. Multivariable linear regression assessed associations of therapy timing and frequency with time to independent oral feeding, adjusting for encephalopathy severity, abnormality on brain magnetic resonance imaging, and intubation days.

RESULTS: Among 358 infants, 326 (91%) received feeding therapy. Therapy was initiated a median of 1.5 d after therapeutic hypothermia and was delivered at a median of 3.5 sessions per week. Each day of delayed initiation was associated with a 0.5 d longer time to independent oral feeding (95% CI 0.3-0.7), and each additional weekly session with a 1 d shorter time to independent oral feeding (95% CI: -1.5 to -0.5).

CONCLUSION: Earlier initiation and greater frequency of feeding therapy were associated with faster attainment of independent oral feeding. Therapy timing and frequency may represent potentially modifiable aspects of NICU care that warrant prospective investigation.

articles.title: Microneedle array safety: a review of skin irritation, infection risk, and repeated application.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The local skin safety of microneedles (MNs) for drug and vaccine delivery depends on product design, formulation, actual skin exposure, and conditions of use. This review covers four types: solid pretreatment, coated, dissolving, and hydrogel-forming MNs.

AREAS COVERED: Targeted PubMed searches covered database inception through 3 November 2026; official regulatory guidance was also examined. The review distinguishes irritation, vaccine reactogenicity, hypersensitivity, sensitization, and infection, and discusses skin barrier recovery, mechanical integrity, material and formulation exposure, and microbial control. Selected human studies are summarized by design, exposure, follow-up, safety findings, and limitations. Repeated application and self-administration are also considered.

EXPERT OPINION: Most local reactions in the reviewed clinical studies were mild or moderate, but severe reactions, discontinuations, and prolonged pigmentation changes were also reported. Safety assessment should consider severity, duration, recovery, and the ability to continue use. Evidence on rare infections, sensitization, and long-term repeated use remains limited. Observed tolerability should therefore be interpreted within the products and conditions studied. We propose prioritizing evidence that links actual exposure to skin reactions and supports the microbiological quality of the finished product. Low bioburden does not replace required sterility.

articles.title: Incident or Worsening Diabetes With Abiraterone Versus Enzalutamide in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Abiraterone and enzalutamide are frequently used to treat metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), yet their comparative safety is incompletely understood. We sought to determine whether abiraterone is associated with an increased risk of incident diabetes or progression of diabetes severity in older US adults with mCRPC. Using the SEER-Medicare database, we designed an active-comparator, new user study comparing sustained use of abiraterone versus enzalutamide. We established two cohorts at baseline: one free of diabetes and one with prevalent diabetes. A marginal structural model was implemented to account for time-varying confounding. Two-year risks of incident diabetes and increase in the adapted diabetes complications severity index (aDSCI) were estimated. The cohort without diabetes at baseline consisted of 2,321 abiraterone and 1,369 enzalutamide initiators. The cohort with baseline diabetes consisted of 749 abiraterone and 569 enzalutamide initiators. The cumulative incidence of diabetes was 11.9 and 7.8 percentage points for the continuous abiraterone use and enzalutamide use strategies, respectively (risk difference (RD) = 4.1; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.2, 7.0). The cumulative incidence of a worsening aDCSI score was 23.1 and 19.0 percentage points for the continuous abiraterone use and enzalutamide use strategies, respectively (RD = 4.1; 95% CI: -1.7, 9.8). Abiraterone is associated with increased risk of new-onset diabetes among men with mCRPC, compared with enzalutamide. Among those with prevalent diabetes, progression in diabetes severity may be greater with abiraterone, though findings were less precise. The safety profiles of androgen receptor pathway inhibitors warrant consideration when individualizing treatment.

articles.title: A minimal physical model of adhesion-dependent protrusion explains confined haptotaxis and oscillatory cell migration.
articles.abstract: Haptotaxis is the directed migration of cells along gradients of substrate adhesion, and is an important guidance mechanism in biology. Recent experiments on fibronectin-patterned tracks show that cells typically migrate toward higher adhesion, then oscillate around the adhesion maximum, with substantial variability in speed and cell length. To explain these cellular shape and migration dynamics we present a minimal model for confined haptotaxis, built around one key physical ingredient: local adhesion strength directly enhances the recruitment of protrusive actin polymerization activity at the cell edge. This coupling creates a front-rear difference in protrusive activity, biasing the cell towards polarization in the direction of the higher adhesion. Quantitative comparison with experiment shows strong agreement at multiple levels: cell population-level directionality statistics and position-dependent changes in cell length and velocity. At the single-cell level, the model reproduces the full diversity of experimentally observed trajectories, including haptotactic bias and its dependence on adhesion-gradient strength, initial position, length and speed variations, myosin II inhibition, and migration on inverted adhesion gradients. Variability in experimental trajectories and migration speed is explained by differences in intrinsic actin polymerization activity and stochastic fluctuations, accounting for the full spectrum of observed migration patterns. Together, our results identify adhesion-dependent amplification of protrusive activity as a minimal and sufficient physical mechanism for understanding haptotaxis.

articles.title: Pregnancies among adolescents and young women on dolutegravir vs. standard-of-care in the ODYSSEY trial and effects of the dolutegravir neural tube defect safety alert.
articles.abstract: ODYSSEY evaluated dolutegravir(DTG)-based antiretroviral therapy (ART) vs. standard-of-care (SOC) in children and adolescents starting first- or second-line ART. During the trial, the World Health Organization issued a safety alert regarding an increased neural-tube defect risk with DTG use in pregnancy. We describe contraceptive use and pregnancies in 278 female ODYSSEY participants aged ≥13 years. Over 3 years post-alert, contraceptive use was similar on DTG and SOC, while the pregnancy rate on DTG was marginally lower (IRR = 0.67,95%CI:0.35-1.27; p = 0.22) and 6 females switched off DTG during pregnancy. There were 82 pregnancies (48 on DTG, 34 on SOC) in 62 females (median age at first pregnancy 18.5 years). Closest viral load before/at pregnancy was <200 copies/mL for 43/55(78%) pregnancies; virological suppression was generally sustained on the same ART through pregnancy (15/19(79%) on DTG, 11/17(65%) on SOC); three participants who switched to DTG in pregnancy remained suppressed, while 2/4 participants who switched off DTG experienced virological rebound. Pregnancy outcomes - 52 live births, 2 stillbirths, 25 spontaneous/induced abortions, 1 ectopic pregnancy - were similar on DTG and SOC. No congenital abnormalities were reported. One infant acquired HIV. Findings support continued use of dolutegravir in adolescents and highlight issues around management of a safety alert affecting pregnancy. Abbreviations: ART: Antiretroviral therapy; DTG: dolutegravir; HIV: human immunodeficiency virus; IUD: intrauterine device; LMIC: low- and middle-income countries; NTD: neural-tube defect; ODYSSEY: a randomised trial of dolutegravir-based antiretroviral therapy vs. standard of care in children with HIV infection starting first-line or switching to second-line ART (PENTA 20); SAE: serious adverse event; SOC: standard of care; SSA: sub-Saharan Africa; VL: viral load; WHO: World Health Organization.

articles.title: Social support and resilience as key determinants of PrEP linkage among adults who inject drugs in rural Appalachian Kentucky.
articles.abstract: People who inject drugs are at high risk for HIV infection and have low Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake. Several complex, multi-level PrEP linkage barriers among vulnerable PWID occur at the individual, interpersonal, and structural levels. However, social support and resilience have been shown to help mitigate these barriers for PWID, yet remain largely underexplored. This paper examined determinants of PrEP linkage among PWID residing in rural Appalachian Kentucky. We enrolled 80 participants from two purposively selected syringe service program sites that serve PWID in counties that rank among the top ten most vulnerable to HIV in the nation. Results from our multivariable logistic regression revealed a significant association between PrEP linkage and emotional support (aOR = 1.96, CI = 1.06;3.62), as well as self-efficacy (aOR = 2.39, CI = 1.12;5.10), an important domain of resilience. Findings suggest that emotional support (e.g., from peer support specialists, community health workers, and other harm reduction providers) and self-efficacy may influence PrEP linkage among PWID. This highlights the importance of integrating PrEP services within syringe service programs. Such integration can create an environment that fosters self-efficacy, resilience, and social support for PWID by offering accessible services, peer navigation, and stigma-free care.

articles.title: Outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy through midline catheters: A single-site experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: For selected patients, the midline catheter is a feasible and safe administration route for outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT). However, there is limited information on the safety of administering specific medications though midline catheters.

METHODS: We retrospectively collected clinical data on patients receiving midline catheters for OPAT after implementation of an institutional guideline on safe antimicrobial administration through midline catheters. Primary outcome was any major device complication, including catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) and catheter-related thrombosis (CRT). Secondary outcomes were any minor device complication (e.g., catheter dislodgement, catheter occlusion, infiltration, leaking at catheter insertion site, or superficial venous thrombosis [SVT]) and device failure, defined as premature midline catheter removal due to any device complication. Findings were summarized using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Between July 2021 and November 2023, 131 patients with a median age of 64 years (IQR, 48-73 years) received midline catheters for OPAT. Urinary tract infection (49.6%) was the most common indication, followed by skin and soft tissue infection (15.3%) and pneumonia (7.6%). Ertapenem (42.7%) and ceftriaxone (17.6%) were the most common antimicrobials administered. The median duration of OPAT was 11 days (IQR, 8-12 days), with 20 (15.3%) patients receiving treatment for >14 days. There were no CRBSI events, and 2 (1.5%) patients experienced CRT. Minor device complications and device failure were common as they occurred in 17 (13%) and 11 (8.4%) patients, respectively.

CONCLUSION: We found a low risk of major device complications when peripherally compatible OPAT were delivered through midline catheters.

articles.title: The "push-pause" flushing technique in small-bore neonatal catheters: A fluid dynamics analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter flushing efficiency depends heavily on flow dynamics, as wall shear stress drives deposit removal. The "push-pause" (pulsatile) flushing technique is recommended for the maintenance of vascular access devices (VADs), based on its proposed ability to improve intraluminal clearance through the generation of turbulent flow. However, the hydrodynamic mechanisms underlying this technique remain incompletely characterized, particularly in small-bore neonatal catheters. This study evaluated the theoretical velocity and pressure requirements to generate a steady turbulent flow within neonatal catheters using an idealized fluid-dynamics model.

METHODS: Mathematical modeling was applied to polyurethane (PUR) catheters typically used in neonatology, with outer diameters ranging from 1 to 3.5 Fr, internal diameters from 0.17 to 0.80 mm, and lengths from 15 to 40 cm. The Reynolds number (Re) was used to determine the critical velocity (vcrit) corresponding to the onset of transitional flow (Re = 2300) and fully turbulent flow (Re = 4000). The corresponding pressure drops (ΔP) were estimated using the Darcy-Weisbach equation and the Blasius friction factor (λ), assuming 0.9% normal saline at 25°C.

RESULTS: At Re = 2300, calculated critical velocities ranged from 2.59 to 12.17 m/s, with ΔP ranging from 0.77 to 59.94 bar. At Re = 4000, calculated velocities ranged from 4.50 to 21.17 m/s, with ΔP ranging from 2.02 to 157.88 bar. The pressure drop in the catheter is directly proportional to its length but inversely proportional to the cube of its internal diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: In this idealized fluid-dynamics model, the velocity and pressure requirements for reaching conventional Reynolds-number thresholds are highly dependent upon the geometry of the catheter under investigation. These effects are particularly evident in 1 Fr and 2 Fr catheters, where the ΔP are substantially higher. Our results suggest that any potential benefit of the "push-pause" flushing technique in small-bore neonatal catheters would need to rely on hydrodynamic mechanisms other than fully developed turbulence. Further experimental studies of its transient hydrodynamic effects are needed to define safe device-tailored flushing practices.

articles.title: Acute human immunodeficiency virus infection and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.
Gut microbiota and metabolic regulation in pregnancy-related disorders.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in maintaining host metabolic homeostasis through, but not limited to, the production of a wide array of bioactive metabolites. Pregnancy is accompanied by profound physiological and metabolic adaptations, paralleled by dynamic remodeling of the gut microbial ecosystem. While these alterations are often adaptive, persistent imbalance can disrupt key metabolic pathways and contribute to the development of major pregnancy-related disorders. This review focuses on the metabolic crosstalk between the host and gut microbiota during pregnancy. We highlight how dysregulation of microbiota-derived metabolites may contribute to the pathogenesis of common metabolic gestational complications, including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy. Finally, we propose a unifying metabolite-centered framework linking pregnancy-associated gut dysbiosis to disease-specific metabolic axes, with implications for early prediction and precision intervention.

articles.title: Prevalence of Complementary and Alternative Therapies in Respiratory Tract Infections in Children and Parental Attitudes.
articles.journal: Journal of transcultural nursing : official journal of the Transcultural Nursing Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) use in children with respiratory tract infections and to evaluate parents' attitudes toward these treatments.

METHODS: This descriptive and cross-sectional study was conducted in the pediatrics clinic of a university hospital. The sample consisted of the parents of 155 children.

RESULTS: It was determined that 94.8% of the parents used CAM methods and 92.1% preferred these methods before drug treatment. The mean total score on the Traditional and Complementary Medicine Attitude Scale was 119.47 ± 22.13. The CAM methods most frequently used by parents were herbal products, steam inhalation, saline nasal irrigation, honey, and traditional practices.

DISCUSSION: These findings underscore the importance of routinely assessing parents' CAM use during health care encounters, addressing potential safety concerns, promoting safe and appropriate CAM use, and providing parents with evidence-based, culturally sensitive counseling.

articles.title: Multiple Revision Surgery and Postoperative Recurrence in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is associated with frequent postoperative recurrence, often requiring revision surgery. Whether previous revision surgeries independently increase the risk of subsequent recurrence remains unclear. We therefore evaluated the association between revision history and postoperative recurrence in CRSwNP.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 571 CRSwNP patients who underwent endoscopic sinus surgery and completed 24-month follow-up. Patients were stratified into primary surgery (n = 418), single revision (n = 105), and multiple revision (n = 48) groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models assessed the association between revision history and recurrence.

RESULTS: Patients with a history of multiple revisions had a significantly higher postoperative recurrence rate than those undergoing primary surgery. Compared with the nonrecurrence group, recurrent patients were older, had a higher body mass index, and more frequently had allergic rhinitis, asthma, and a smoking history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, multiple revision surgery remained independently associated with an increased risk of postoperative recurrence, whereas a single revision was not. After full adjustment, multiple revision surgery exhibited the independent association with an increased risk of recurrence (HR = 1.926, p = 0.003). Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed significantly lower recurrence-free survival in patients with multiple prior revisions throughout the 24-month follow-up.

CONCLUSION: A history of multiple revision surgeries is independently associated with postoperative recurrence in CRSwNP. Patients with multiple surgeries should be recognized as a distinct high-risk population requiring individualized postoperative management beyond repeated surgical intervention.

articles.title: Mitochondrial dynamics regulation in neurogenesis during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke ranks among the leading causes of death and disability worldwide. Vascular recanalization after stroke can trigger cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury(CIRI), which disturbs mitochondrial homeostasis and blunts endogenous neurogenesis, limiting brain functional recovery. Although mitochondrial dynamics govern neural stem cell fate under physiological conditions, how this machinery reshapes neurogenesis specifically in the pathological context of CIRI remains incompletely synthesized.

OBJECTIVE: This review focuses on the mechanistic links between mitochondrial dynamics disturbance, impaired energy metabolism, and defective endogenous neurogenesis under CIRI, as well as therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics to restore neurogenesis after reperfusion insult.

METHODS: Relevant literature on neurogenesis, energy metabolism, and mitochondrial dynamics was reviewed to elucidate their roles in CIRI. Additionally, experimental data on mitochondrial dynamics-related proteins regulating neurogenesis were examined, with special attention to findings obtained from cerebral ischemia-reperfusion experimental models.

RESULTS: Therapeutic approaches promoting endogenous neurogenesis represent a novel strategy for treating ischemic-induced neural injury. Neurogenesis is closely linked to mitochondrial energy metabolism. In CIRI, reperfusion stress disrupts the balance of mitochondrial fission-fusion, which further impairs metabolic reprogramming required for neural stem cell activation, proliferation and neuronal survival. Direct in-vivo evidence connecting mitochondrial dynamics remodeling to neurogenesis in CIRI is still limited. Targeting mitochondrial dynamics to rescue energy homeostasis may serve as a means to revive endogenous neurogenesis post-CIRI.

CONCLUSION: Energy metabolism and pathological changes following cerebral ischemia-reperfusion are closely associated with mitochondrial dynamics. Modulating mitochondrial dynamics holds potential to rescue metabolic disturbance and restore neurogenesis after CIRI.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation Without Prior Major Bleeding.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

articles.title: Identifying Habit Cues to Prevent Falls: Secondary Analysis From Falls After Stroke Trial.
articles.abstract: Habit formation principles may be important in enabling fall-prevention behaviours for stroke survivors. Secondary analysis of data from FAST (Falls After Stroke Trial) examined the extent to which lifestyle-integrated functional exercises (LiFE) to reduce falls are done habitually over time and what cues prompt people to implement them. Participants were ≥50 years, ≤5 years post-stroke, and in Australia. Interventions were conducted at home. Habit strength measured by the Self-Report Behavioural Automaticity Scale. Habit automaticity scores increased significantly at 12 months for routine activities (M = 3 to M = 3.9, n = 116, p < .001), though they dropped slightly but significantly for challenging activities (M = 2.39 to M = 2.15, n = 66, p = .03). The most common cue responses that prompted or a LiFE exercise were Situational - doing something in a specific context or Object/Place - seeing a specific object/place. In this high-risk post-stroke population, the habit formation of LiFE delivery may be key to adopting and maintaining exercise embedded in occupation.

articles.title: Effect of Dental Loupes on Students' Fine Motor Skills and Working Posture.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the effect of dental loupes on the working posture and fine motor skills of dental students under simulated conditions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a randomized crossover study involving 33 dental students. The response variables were the neck angular deviation, working distance and fine motor skills. The independent variable was the magnification system (unaided vision, 2.5× Galilean loupes, 3.0× Galilean loupes and 3.0× ergonomic loupes). Participants were randomly assigned to two groups. During the first session, Group I performed a manual dexterity task under unaided vision, whereas Group II completed three dexterity tasks using the three loupe systems tested. The conditions were reversed after 1 week. Posture was recorded using photographs during the performance of the fine motor skills test. Neck angular deviation was analyzed using the Software for Postural Assessment. The working distance was measured using the Measure app, and fine motor skills were assessed using the Dental Manual Dexterity Assessment. Descriptive statistics, one-factor repeated measures analysis of variance (rANOVA) and Bonferroni's post hoc test were performed (α = 0.05).

RESULTS: The ergonomic loupes were associated with a greater working distance (p < 0.001) and reduced neck angular deviation (p < 0.001), but they did not significantly influence fine motor skills (p = 0.211).

CONCLUSION: The use of ergonomic loupes was associated with improvements in the working posture of dental students under simulated conditions, particularly by increasing working distance and reducing neck angular deviation. No statistically significant differences in fine motor skills were observed under the conditions tested.

articles.title: Evaluation and Management of Iron Disorders: Consensus Guidance From the National Classical Hematology Consortium.
articles.abstract: Disorders of iron homeostasis, including iron deficiency and iron overload, are among the most common conditions in classical hematology, yet management varies widely across specialties. The National Classical Hematology Consortium (NCHC) developed consensus-based guidance for the evaluation and management of iron disorders in adult and pediatric patients through iterative literature review and expert consensus. We present a structured, algorithmic framework covering laboratory evaluation, diagnosis of iron deficiency and hyperferritinemia, genetic testing, MRI-based iron quantification, iron supplementation, infusion reaction management, phlebotomy, and chelation. Our framework also highlights updates in the management of iron deficiency, including the addition of a black box warning to the intravenous iron formulation ferric carboxymaltose highlighting the risk of severe and prolonged hypophosphatemia. This guidance aims to standardize care and improve outcomes across diverse clinical settings.

articles.title: Development, expert consensus, and pilot feasibility of a school-integrated telehealth model for childhood epilepsy care in India.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop, validate through expert consensus, and pilot-test the feasibility of Tele-ESSI (Tele-School Health-led Epilepsy Smart Schools in India), a school-integrated telehealth intervention for childhood epilepsy in resource-limited settings.

METHODS: A multi-phase, mixed-methods intervention development study was conducted across three geographically diverse districts in India. Phase 1 comprised a stakeholder needs assessment through structured workshops, focus group discussions (FGDs), and semi-structured interviews. Phase 2 involved participatory co-design and intervention development, followed by Phase 3, which involved expert validation using a two-round modified Delphi process (consensus threshold: ≥80% agreement; interquartile range ≤1.0). Phase 4 comprised pilot feasibility testing in five purposively selected schools (n = 30 teachers). Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, and qualitative data underwent thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Three stakeholder workshops (n = 364 participants), FGDs, and in-depth interviews identified system-level gaps in epilepsy literacy, seizure first-aid capacity, and school-healthcare coordination. The resulting Tele-ESSI model integrated three core components: (1) telephonic clinical decision support, (2) structured capacity building, and (3) a multilingual digital integration platform. Fourteen experts completed the modified Delphi process, achieving ≥80% consensus across all domains (mean ratings 8.3-8.8/9). Pilot testing demonstrated high feasibility (4.62 ± 0.30), acceptability (4.44 ± 0.33), usability (4.52 ± 0.38), perceived effectiveness (4.38 ± 0.43), and satisfaction (4.13 ± 0.57). FRAME-guided refinements improved training clarity and digital accessibility.

SIGNIFICANCE: Schools remain underutilized platforms for epilepsy care in low- and middle-income countries, where fragmented health-education coordination contributes to delayed management, stigma, and educational disruption. Tele-ESSI is a stakeholder-informed, consensus-validated, and pilot-tested model that addresses these system-level gaps through integrated clinical support and capacity building within the school setting. Findings support progression to a large-scale effectiveness trial. If effective, the model offers a replicable, scalable, intersectoral framework adaptable to comparable resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Aortic arch reconstruction using a fan-shaped autologous pulmonary artery patch: a report of two cases.
articles.journal: General thoracic and cardiovascular surgery cases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous pulmonary artery tissue has recently been reported as a useful reconstructive material for aortic arch repair in infants with arch hypoplasia. We describe two infants with coarctation of the aorta associated with marked aortic arch hypoplasia who underwent aortic arch reconstruction using a fan-shaped autologous pulmonary artery patch.

CASE PRESENTATION: Two infants with coarctation of the aorta and a hypoplastic aortic arch underwent surgical repair. Case 1 was a 2-month-old girl weighing 4.7 kg with coarctation of the aorta, aortic arch hypoplasia, and a ventricular septal defect who presented with ductal shock. Case 2 was a 20-day-old boy weighing 2.9 kg with prenatally diagnosed coarctation of the aorta, arch hypoplasia, a ventricular septal defect, and a large patent ductus arteriosus. In both patients, the anterior wall of the main pulmonary artery was harvested and fashioned into a fan-shaped patch. The patch was tailored using preoperative computed tomography measurements, including the circumference of the descending aorta, to obtain a gradual transition in arch caliber. Ventricular septal defect closure was performed in Case 1, whereas pulmonary artery banding was performed in Case 2. The postoperative course was uneventful in both cases. Early postoperative computed tomography demonstrated satisfactory arch morphology without airway compression. Furthermore, at the latest follow-up, there was no clinically significant obstruction of the reconstructed arch based on upper- and lower-extremity blood pressure measurements and transthoracic echocardiography, although mild residual flow acceleration was observed in Case 2.

CONCLUSIONS: Aortic arch reconstruction using a fan-shaped autologous pulmonary artery patch is technically feasible in selected infants with coarctation of the aorta associated with marked arch hypoplasia. This technique enables patient-specific geometric augmentation of the aortic arch with satisfactory early postoperative results. Long-term follow-up is required to evaluate durability and late outcomes.

articles.title: Cannabis use among psychiatric in-patients: Prevalence, clinical characteristics and hospital outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Cannabis use is common among people receiving psychiatric care and may be associated with more complex clinical presentations and inpatient trajectories, but its prevalence and association with hospitalization outcomes remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of documented cannabis use during psychiatric hospitalizations and to explore associated socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study analyzing routinely collected data from the electronic health records of patients admitted between 2019 and 2024. Descriptive statistics and multivariable analyses were conducted to examine associations of cannabis use with length of stay, seclusion and restraint.

SETTING: Psychiatric inpatient units of the Groupe Hospitalier Universitaire (GHU) Paris Psychiatrie et Neurosciences hospital group, a network of public psychiatric hospitals in Paris, France.

PARTICIPANTS: 32 429 hospital stays corresponding to 17 040 individual adult patients. The median age was 40 years (interquartile range 28-54) and 45.4% were female.

MEASUREMENTS: Documented cannabis use was the main exposure, identified through multiple complementary sources: a positive urine toxicology result, presence of a cannabis-related diagnosis in structured clinical data and a natural language processing keyword search algorithm applied to free clinical notes. Outcomes were length of stay, seclusion and restraint. Covariates included socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics such as age, sex, diagnostic category, comorbidities, housing status and legal admission status.

RESULTS: Cannabis use was documented in 25.0% of patients, and an overall increase was observed over the study period despite year-to-year fluctuations. Compared with individuals without documented use, those with identified use were more often male, younger and had higher rates of psychotic disorders and comorbidity. In multivariable models, the association between documented cannabis use and length of stay varied according to legal admission status, whereas no interaction with legal admission status was observed for seclusion or restraint. Cannabis use was associated with longer length of stay, with adjusted ratios of mean length of stay of 1.22 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.16-1.27] for voluntary admissions, 1.23 (95% CI = 1.17-1.29) for involuntary admissions under a civil procedure, 1.39 (95% CI = 1.28-1.50) for state-ordered admissions and 1.64 (95% CI = 1.24-2.16) for incarcerated and forensic patients. Documented cannabis use was also associated with higher odds of seclusion [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.73, 95% CI = 1.56-1.91] and restraint (aOR = 1.88, 95% CI = 1.48-2.37).

SUMMARY: Cannabis use appears to occur in about a quarter of psychiatric inpatients in Paris, France, and prevalence is rising; it appears to be associated with longer (vs. shorter) hospitalizations and higher odds of coercive interventions (vs. no coercive interventions) during the stay.

articles.title: Considerations in the association between red blood cell transfusion and infection after trauma.
Infective endocarditis with multifocal embolic strokes in the presence of a patent foramen ovale: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report a complicated and rare case of multiple-territory cerebral infarctions secondary to native aortic valve infective endocarditis caused by coagulase-positive Staphylococcus aureus species in a patient with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus. This case is interesting because of the atypical presentation with initial urinary tract infection, subtle neurological deficits, and delayed pulmonary findings, which emphasizes the diagnostic challenge of endocarditis in patients with multiple comorbidities. In addition, identifying potential contributors, including a patent foramen ovale and atrial septal aneurysm, to embolic events adds novelty, highlighting the importance of careful cardiovascular evaluation in unexplained strokes.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 54-year-old Arab male with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes mellitus who initially presented with urinary and respiratory tract infections, ketosis, and rising inflammatory marker levels. The patient was first diagnosed with a urinary tract infection due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Despite appropriate antibiotics, the patient remained febrile and developed right upper limb weakness, which was initially attributed to a longstanding problem. Neurological evaluation revealed a subacute left occipital infarction with multiple additional infarcts on CT. Blood cultures revealed Staphylococcus aureus. The initial HRCT chest was normal, but repeat imaging revealed bilateral patchy ground-glass opacities and consolidations. MRI of the brain revealed multiple acute and subacute infarcts, some with hemorrhagic transformation, in the occipital, frontal, parietal, and cerebellar regions. An investigation for the cardiac source revealed a patent foramen ovale on transthoracic echocardiography. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a type 2L atrial septal aneurysm with large mobile vegetations on the native aortic valve, which was consistent with infective endocarditis. Despite ongoing antibiotics and escalation of care at a tertiary hospital, the patient's condition worsened, with acute severe aortic regurgitation and multiorgan failure, and he unfortunately passed away.

CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity and severe clinical course of valve infective endocarditis presenting with multiple cerebral infarctions. This finding underscores the importance of early consideration of endocarditis in patients with unexplained strokes, especially in the context of systemic infections and cardiovascular anomalies, such as PFO or atrial septal aneurysm. Early identification of such atypical presentations can improve timely diagnosis, intervention, and patient outcomes.

articles.title: Swedish Dental Hygienists' Experiences of Two Evidence-Based Concepts in Non-Surgical Treatment of Patients With Periodontitis-A Questionnaire Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare Swedish dental hygienists (DHs) experiences of two different non-surgical treatment protocols directed to patients with periodontitis in general dentistry.

METHODS: The study included DHs who participated in a clinical trial comparing two evidence-based protocols for non-surgical periodontal treatment; Conventional non-surgical therapy (CNST) often comprising several sessions with integrated patient education and instrumentation versus a full-mouth protocol, called Guided periodontal infection control (GPIC), with initial focus on patient education followed by a single session of ultrasonic instrumentation. A questionnaire on DHs' experiences of the treatment protocols was distributed when their patients reached 6-months evaluation. Data were processed with descriptive and non-parametric statistics.

RESULTS: DHs in the GPIC group devoted more time to educational/behavioural measures before instrumentation than DHs in CNST. DHs' ratings of patients' pain/discomfort during instrumentation showed a more varied picture in both a positive and negative direction in GPIC than CNST; however, the median ratings were similar across groups. No differences were observed between the treatment groups regarding DHs' experiences of stress/physical discomfort related to treatment. About 50% of DHs in both groups found it difficult to justify the time and cost of educational and behavioural measures in therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: The GPIC concept encouraged DHs to devote more time to patient education before instrumentation than CNST. No prominent differences were observed between treatment groups regarding DHs' ratings of patient discomfort during therapy or DHs' perceived stress/discomfort related to therapy. Regardless of treatment approach, DHs may find it difficult to justify the cost of patient education.

articles.title: Signaling pathways and targeted therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common and lethal malignancies, representing a major global health concern. Viral hepatitis, metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD)-related hepatitis, and alcoholic hepatitis are three critical precursor lesions that can progress to HCC. Owing to its insidious onset, HCC is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage, where surgical intervention is no longer feasible. This underscores the pivotal role of systemic therapies, including targeted therapy, in improving patient outcomes. Over the past decade, the first-line systemic treatment landscape for advanced HCC has progressed from a single approved tyrosine-kinase inhibitor (sorafenib) to a range of targeted agents and, more recently, targeted-immunotherapy combinations. In randomized phase III trials, first-line combination regimens such as atezolizumab plus bevacizumab have improved median overall survival to 19.2 months versus 13.4 months with sorafenib (HR = 0.66, 95%CI: 0.52-0.85), extending survival beyond the range historically achieved with single-agent targeted therapy. The evolution from initial single-agent targeted therapy to current targeted-immunotherapy combinations reflects the ever-evolving therapeutic strategies and deepened understanding of HCC pathogenesis. Further investigation into the signaling pathways and molecular targets of HCC is crucial for advancing precision medicine in this malignancy. Herein, we comprehensively review the tumor microenvironment (TME), key signaling pathways, and approved targeted-immunotherapy regimens for HCC, including agents approved by the US FDA and, where FDA approval is absent, by other regulators such as China's NMPA (sintilimab plus IBI305, camrelizumab plus apatinib, and the LEAP-012 regimen). We also discuss early-phase clinical trials of promising agents, drug resistance and safety concerns in targeted-immunotherapy, as well as future research directions.

articles.title: Human mesenchymal stromal cells for Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease 1A treatment: a Phase 1 clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1 A (CMT1A) is the most common inherited peripheral neuropathy, with no effective treatments available. Based on previous preclinical findings, this open-label Phase 1 study aimed to evaluate the short-term safety, tolerability, and exploratory efficacy of allogeneic Wharton's jelly-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (WJ-MSCs) in patients with CMT1A.

RESULTS: Nine patients with CMT1A received a single intravenous administration of WJ-MSCs at either 5 × 10⁵ cells/kg (low-dose, n = 3) or 2.5 × 10⁶ cells/kg (high-dose, n = 6). No dose-limiting toxicities or serious adverse events were observed during the 16-week follow-up. A total of four adverse events were reported-one in the low-dose cohort and three in high-dose cohort-including injection-site erythema and headache. All events were mild, transient, and assessed as either unrelated or unlikely to be related to WJ-MSCs. No clinically meaningful abnormalities were identified. Exploratory clinical outcome measures showed numerical changes at Week 16, with a reduction in CMTNSv2 in the high-dose group; however, the study was not powered to assess efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: This Phase 1 clinical trial supports the short-term safety and tolerability of single intravenous administration of WJ-MSCs in patients with CMT1A. This study represents the first clinical evaluation of systemic WJ-MSC therapy in patients with CMT1A and provides a safety foundation for subsequent larger, controlled studies with longer follow-up.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05333406, Registered 06 January 2022, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05333406 .

articles.title: Agreement between AI-based automated and expert-defined manual whole-body tumor volume assessment in [¹⁸F]FDG-PET/CT of NSCLC patients.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Whole-body tumor burden is an emerging biomarker for disease assessment and response monitoring in PET/CT, and automated approaches may enable standardized, observer-independent quantification. Automated and expert-defined tumor volumes differ in their delineation, and their agreement remains unclear. This method-comparison study evaluated the agreement between threshold-based AI volumetric PET metrics and expert-defined manual whole-body tumor volumes at baseline and during treatment.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, [¹⁸F]FDG-PET/CT examinations from 118 patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC were analyzed, comprising 118 baseline and 278 follow-up examinations (n = 396). Manual whole-body tumor segmentation was compared with automated metrics (TMTV41%, TMTVSUV4) from CE-marked software. Agreement was assessed using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), Bland-Altman analysis, coverage probability within predefined relative limits, agreement on the presence of measurable tumor burden, and agreement in the change from baseline. All follow-up examinations were included in a secondary analysis accounting for repeated examinations within patients.

RESULTS: At baseline, CCC was 0.94 (95% CI 0.74-0.95) for TMTVSUV4 and 0.81 (0.35-0.86) for TMTV41%, with wide and asymmetric intervals. Concordance was lower at the first follow-up (0.74 and 0.40) and across all follow-up examinations (0.59 and 0.40). On the ratio scale, automated measurements deviated at the first follow-up, with geometric mean ratios of 1.46 (95% CI 1.19-1.79) for TMTV41% and 0.37 (0.29-0.48) for TMTVSUV4. Coverage probability within ± 20% of the manual reference was 26.3% for both metrics at baseline and 11.1% and 13.7% at the first follow-up. TMTVSUV4 returned a volume of zero in 28 of 278 follow-up examinations in which the expert reference remained positive. Agreement in the relative change from baseline was low (CCC 0.08 for TMTV41% and 0.44 for TMTVSUV4), and agreement in exploratory response categories defined by a ± 30% change in tumor volume was only fair (Cohen's κ 0.32 and 0.35).

CONCLUSION: Automated threshold-based PET volumetry reflects overall tumor burden but is not interchangeable with anatomically guided expert delineation. Agreement is lower during treatment and is only fair when the change from baseline is classified into response categories, supporting the use of AI-based volumetry as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for expert assessment.

articles.title: Correction: Comment - Louis XIV's terminal illness clinical chronology favors necrotizing soft-tissue infection.
Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus and depression at 5 years postpartum.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with a higher risk of maternal depression across the first postpartum year. However, whether this association persists remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the links between GDM and depressive symptoms at 5 years postpartum. We used data from 384 participants from the prospective pre-birth Gen3G cohort (Canada). We defined GDM according to international diagnostic criteria, based on a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test in the second trimester of pregnancy. We assessed glucose/insulin values as additional predictors. Among 384 participants, 38 had GDM in the second trimester of pregnancy. At 5 years, participants self-reported depressive symptoms using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale. Regression analyses examined associations between GDM and metabolic markers and depressive symptoms adjusting for demographic/lifestyle factors. We did not find evidence of associations between GDM and depressive symptoms at 5 years postpartum, albeit limited by our number of GDM cases.

articles.title: Histologic Ductules in Preauricular Cysts and Sinuses: A Possible Framework for Lesion Recurrence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Preauricular cysts and sinuses are common congenital anomalies that may recur after excision, which has traditionally been attributed to incomplete removal of the primary tract. However, microscopic epithelial remnants, similar to those described in thyroglossal duct cysts and branchial cleft anomalies, may also contribute to persistent disease. This study evaluated the histologic architecture of preauricular cysts in pediatric patients to determine whether microscopic epithelial ductules are present beyond the dominant lesion, offering a possible explanation for recurrence.

METHODS: Pediatric patients undergoing surgical excision of preauricular cysts at a tertiary care pediatric hospital between October 10, 2025 and April 10, 2026 were prospectively reviewed. Clinical data including demographics, infection history, and histopathologic findings were recorded. Specimens were oriented intraoperatively, inked at defined margins, and examined microscopically for epithelial ductules separate from the dominant cyst or tract, including their presence at excision margins.

RESULTS: Twenty patients (8 males, 12 females; median age 4 years 6 months, range 8 months-14 years 3 months) met inclusion criteria. Five had bilateral lesions, yielding 25 excised preauricular cysts and/or sinuses. Microscopic epithelial ductules separate from the dominant lesion were identified in 10 of 25 specimens (40%), five of which had ductules at the surgical margins.

CONCLUSION: Microscopic epithelial ductules may be present in a subset of preauricular cysts and sinuses, suggesting their histologic architecture can extend beyond the dominant tract and potentially contribute to recurrence after excision. These findings support careful, wide excision with attention to specimen orientation.

articles.title: One Distance, Two Measures: Rethinking the Sylvian Fissure and Insula in Fetal Congenital Heart Disease.
Cilostazol for Secondary Prevention of Stroke and Cognitive Decline: An Updated Systematic Review.
articles.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cilostazol may benefit secondary stroke prevention and cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). Evidence for its role in preventing recurrent stroke and cognitive decline, particularly after lacunar stroke, remains limited although evolving.

AIM: We updated a previous systematic review to evaluate cilostazol effects on long-term outcomes after stroke or cognitive decline.

SUMMARY OF REVIEW: The protocol was registered on PROSPERO and conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. We searched MEDLINE and EMBASE from January 2019 to August 2026 for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of cilostazol, alone or with other antiplatelets, in adults with stroke, SVD, or cognitive impairment. We cross-checked prior searches (1990 - 2019) and manually checked additional relevant sources. Meta-analyses and sensitivity analyses were performed where possible with data from the previous review. Twenty-one publications were identified since 2019, including 14 new RCTs, which synthesised with 20 previous trials, gave 34 RCTs overall (n=16,740). Cilostazol reduced recurrent ischemic stroke (OR 0.75 [95% CI 0.65-0.87]), hemorrhagic stroke (OR 0.46 [0.33-0.66]), all stroke (OR 0.68 [0.59-0.77]), major cardiovascular event (OR 0.71 [0.61-0.82]), dependency (OR 0.86 [0.73-0.99]) and depression (OR 0.33 [0.20-0.53]), with a non-significant trend towards improved mood scores. The reduction in ischemic stroke was most consistently observed in chronic-phase long-term trials and those with ≥40% lacunar stroke, although the associations in meta-regression were weak and further attenuated after adjustment for comparator antiplatelet regimens. Trials reporting cognitive function were sparse and methodologically inconsistent, without clear effects on cognitive scores. Cilostazol increased headache, palpitations, diarrhoea, dizziness, and tachycardia or arrhythmia.

CONCLUSIONS: Cilostazol appears effective and safe for long-term secondary stroke prevention, including after lacunar stroke, while its effects on cognition and mood require confirmation in further randomised trials.

articles.title: Initial oxidation and surface modification of polyethylene by the Bacillus cereus BR6119-derived recombinant cytochrome P450.
articles.abstract: Plastics are widely used because of their durability; however, their increasing production has caused serious environmental pollution. Additionally, microplastics and leached additives pose potential risks to human health. Therefore, microorganism- and enzyme-based initial oxidation and surface modification has emerged as a promising eco-friendly alternative for plastic waste treatment. In this study, we assessed the depolymerizing potential of polyethylene-a representative recalcitrant polymer-using Bacillus cereus BR6119 isolated from a plastic landfill site and recombinant cytochrome P450 enzyme cloned from this strain. The isolated strain grew in minimal medium with polyethylene as the sole carbon source for 6 weeks and field emission scanning electron microscopy revealed physical damage to the polyethylene surface. In addition, fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy revealed an increase in hydroxyl, alkene, and ester functional groups-indicating initial oxidation and surface modification of the polymer chains. B. cereus BR6119-derived cytochrome P450 gene was inserted into the pET-21a (+) expression vector and overexpressed in Escherichia coli. The resulting crude enzyme containing the B. cereus BR6119-derived recombinant cytochrome P450 induced structural alterations in polyethylene for 5 days. These results demonstrate that enzyme-based initial oxidation and surface modification can serve as a faster plastic depolymerization strategy than that of cell-based approach. This study suggests the potential for developing bacteria- or enzyme-assisted biological treatment technologies for plastic waste management.

articles.title: Intraoperative Augmented Reality Visualization During Lymph Node Dissection in Cutaneous Malignancies: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete lymph node dissection (CLND) in selected patients with cutaneous malignancies presents anatomical challenges, and current imaging offers limited intraoperative guidance. This pilot study assessed the feasibility of intraoperative augmented reality (AR) visualization of patient-specific, fludeoxyglucose-18 positron emission tomography (FDG-PET/CT) derived three-dimensional (3D) model at predefined stages during CLND.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this prospective pilot study, 16 consecutive patients undergoing CLND for cutaneous malignancies were enrolled. Preoperative FDG-PET/CT datasets were segmented to generate patient-specific 3D model, projected via an AR headset at predefined stages before and during surgery.

RESULTS: The median age was 71 years (range 33-79 years); 11 patients had melanoma (68.8%), 4 had Merkel cell carcinoma (25.0%), and 1 had squamous cell carcinoma (6.3%). Eight patients (50%) had received neoadjuvant systemic therapy. Dissection sites included superficial groin (9, 56.3%), deep groin (4, 25.0%), axilla (2, 12.5%), and combined (1, 6.3%). The median largest nodal size on imaging was 32 mm (range 13-65 mm). AR projection was successfully completed in all 16 patients across all predefined surgical stages, with no technical failures or AR-related complications. Mean operative time was 106.2 min (SD ±38.4). Postoperative complications occurred in seven patients (43.8%), consistent with expected rates, including wound infection in six (37.5%) and collection requiring drainage in one (6.3%).
