CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative AR visualization of patient-specific, FDG-PET/CT-derived 3D models was technically feasible at predefined stages of CLND for cutaneous malignancies. Further studies should assess registration accuracy, workflow, and clinical utility.

articles.title: Bayesian Two-Stage Estimation of Dose-Response Relationships in Hybrid Decentralized Trials with Preplanned Dose Titrations.
articles.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating long-term dose effects in early-phase decentralized longitudinal clinical trials, where dose titrations are preplanned to enhance patient tolerability and adherence. In such decentralized settings, outcome data are collected both onsite (e.g., from clinical trial sites) and remotely (e.g., from home), thereby increasing patient centricity and convenience. However, remote data collection may introduce measurement bias and increased variability, posing challenges for estimation accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose an efficient and robust Bayesian two-stage estimation procedure that decouples the flexible longitudinal modeling of mixed onsite and remote data and titration dynamics (stage 1) from the final parametric estimation of the long-term dose-response curve (stage 2). To enable adaptive integration of onsite and remote data, a horseshoe prior is incorporated to model potential bias arising from remote measurements. Extensive simulation and sensitivity studies demonstrate that the proposed method achieves efficient and robust estimation of long-term dose-response relationships across a wide range of decentralized trial scenarios.

articles.title: Age-related impairment of oncogenic surveillance promotes liver tumor initiation.
articles.abstract: Aging is a major risk factor for liver cancer, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, using a mouse model in which hepatocytes express oncogenic NRASG12V, we found that clearance of oncogene-induced senescent (OIS) cells was delayed in aged versus young mice, followed by tumor development exclusively in aged mice. Oncogenic injury rapidly induced Spp1+ macrophage accumulation in aged livers, impairing OIS cell clearance and sustaining inflammation permissive to malignant transformation. The resulting tumors resembled human steatotic hepatocellular carcinoma and lacked the NRASG12V mutation. Consistently, SPP1+ macrophages were more abundant in human livers from older versus younger individuals with cirrhosis and liver cancer. Depletion of Spp1+ macrophages or intermittent senolysis using dasatinib plus quercetin (D+Q) partially restored OIS cell clearance, alleviated inflammation and reduced tumor incidence in aged mice. Our findings identify impaired OIS surveillance as a driver of tumor development during aging and highlight Spp1+ macrophages as a target to reduce age-associated liver cancer risk.

articles.title: [Evaluation of the practice development within advanced nursing practice in the intensive care unit].
articles.abstract: Since 2022, academically qualified nurses have been systematically integrated into direct patient care at Klinikum Oldenburg. This article describes the further development of the academic skill-grade mix, the roles of nursing experts, Advanced Practice Nurses and nursing science, and its implementation in intensive care. In 2026, an exploratory online survey assessed perceptions of the academic roles among 25 academically qualified nurses and 63 clinical staff members. Knowledge transfer, accessibility as a professional resource and practice development activities were predominantly perceived positively. At the same time, areas for further development were identified regarding role clarity and team participation. The findings suggest that sustainable implementation of academic nursing roles should be understood as an ongoing organisational development process.

articles.title: Myosynangiosis in pediatric moyamoya arteriopathy: a comparative case series.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Moyamoya arteriopathy (MM) is a progressive arteriopathy of the terminal intracranial internal carotid arteries. While pial synangiosis is a common indirect revascularization technique in pediatric patients, there are scenarios where a donor vessel is not available, necessitating consideration of other techniques, such as placement of muscle (myosynangiosis). Although data on this approach is limited, we present our experience to better inform decision-making.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center review of pediatric patients with MM who underwent surgical revascularization with myosynangiosis from 2014 to 2024. All patients underwent either myosynangiosis exclusively (either unilateral or bilateral) or myosynangiosis on one hemisphere and pial synangiosis on the contralateral hemisphere. We obtained patient demographics, etiology of MM, and preoperative Suzuki grade. Postoperatively, the patients were assessed for their rate of perioperative ischemic stroke and long-term outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 26 pediatric patients (49 hemispheres) were identified with a mean age at presentation and mean follow-up of 10 years (range 1-20) and 2 years (0.5-9), respectively. Per hemisphere, 32 and 17 hemispheres were treated with myosynangiosis and pial synangiosis, respectively. Regarding 41 hemispheres that underwent postoperative analysis, no pial synangiosis hemispheres (0/15, 0%) and two myosynangiosis hemispheres (2/26, 8%) developed strokes during the long-term follow-up period. Moreover, there was no statistical significance between the two techniques in terms of Suzuki grade, etiology of MM, and rate of postoperative stroke.

CONCLUSION: Pial synangiosis remains a safe and effective revascularization technique for MM. When an adequate donor vessel is absent, myosynangiosis offers comparable stroke protection but does have a trend toward more postoperative strokes. Overall, our findings suggest that myosynangiosis is a durable, effective treatment for MM when pial synangiosis is not an option.

articles.title: Beyond treatment timing: modeling the screening-to-care pathway for screening-detected hypertension.
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension

articles.title: Multidisciplinary consensus on ampullary carcinoma: evidence-based clinical recommendations from ENS-CCA.
articles.abstract: Ampullary carcinoma, a malignant tumour that originates in the ampulla of Vater, is a rare disease, under-represented in cancer registries and clinical trials. Owing to its intrinsic anatomical complexity, the ampulla of Vater displays substantial tissue heterogeneity, which makes ampullary carcinoma pathological diagnosis challenging, with special relevance for determining if the tissue origin is intestinal or pancreatobiliary. These features of ampullary carcinoma, together with its low incidence, explain the lack of an international consensus on standard of care management. This expert Consensus Statement, endorsed by the European Network for the Study of Cholangiocarcinoma (ENS-CCA) and the European Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) Action Precision-Biliary Tract Cancer (BTC) Network, aims to establish evidence-based guidelines to help the oncology community provide a decision-making framework for patients with ampullary carcinoma. A group of multidisciplinary experts from 12 countries performed an in-depth review of the epidemiology, diagnosis, molecular landscape and management of ampullary carcinoma, detailing unmet needs, and proposed a strategic plan with future directions based on agreed expert recommendations on each topic.

articles.title: Paediatric metabolic syndrome criteria as predictors of early adult metabolic syndrome: findings from the EPITeen cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several definitions of metabolic syndrome (MetS) are used in paediatric populations. This study investigates the predictive capacity of five MetS definitions at age 13 for identifying MetS at age 27 and explores whether adding non-classic variables improves prediction.

METHODS: Participants from the EPITeen cohort (n = 815) with valid data on MetS components at ages 13 and 27 were included. At age 13, MetS was defined using Cook, Ferranti, Ford, Agudelo, and International Diabetes Federation (IDF) criteria, and at age 27 using the Alberti consensus. Predictive capacity was estimated using the area under the ROC curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Performance metrics such as sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, accuracy, and likelihood ratios were calculated. Non-classic variables were added to the criterion with a higher AUC.

RESULTS: At age 13, MetS prevalence ranged from 0.9% (IDF) to 12.5% (Ferranti), and at age 27 it was 3.4%. Ferranti definition had the highest AUC (0.696; 95% CI 0.609-0.784), although not significantly higher than the other criteria. Ferranti was also the least conservative criterion, classifying substantially more adolescents as having MetS (77.4%) but with lower specificity, accuracy, and likelihood ratios than the other criteria. LDL-C was the only non-classic variable that showed a significant improvement in Ferranti's AUC (0.765; 95% CI 0.683-0.846).

CONCLUSIONS: Paediatric MetS definitions showed limited ability to predict MetS in early adulthood. Ferranti definition with LDL-C demonstrated the best predictive capacity and, due to its performance metrics, can support targeted preventive public health strategies throughout the life course.

articles.title: Epigenetic enzymes in autism spectrum disorder: a brain imaging study.
articles.abstract: Genetics, environmental factors and epigenetic processes contribute to the etiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Epigenetic alterations that have been reported in ASD through human postmortem work include alterations in histone acetylation and density of histone deacetylases (HDACs), which are epigenetic enzymes that decrease histone acetylation and repress gene transcription. Histone deacetylases are altered in autism-relevant animal models and treatments targeting HDACs result in symptom rescue in these models. Here, we used positron emission tomography (PET) with the radiotracer [11C]Martinostat to measure HDACs in vivo in the brain. Twenty-one autistic adults and 23 non-autistic neurotypical adults (NT) completed a [11C]Martinostat PET-magnetic resonance imaging brain scan. Region of interest analysis showed that [11C]Martinostat uptake was lower in the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) in autistic adults compared to NT. Exploratory whole brain voxelwise analysis showed lower [11C]Martinostat uptake in the insula, hippocampus, and superior temporal gyrus in the right hemisphere, and the orbitofrontal cortex bilaterally in autistic adults compared to NT. No regions showed higher [11C]Martinostat uptake in autistic adults compared to NT. These findings provide evidence for lower in vivo HDAC levels (as measured by [11C]Martinostat uptake) in ASD in brain areas involved in socio-emotional processing and implicate HDACs in ASD, which may lead to future therapeutic investigations.

articles.title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia.
articles.abstract: Urban mobility is central to economic activity, social inclusion and access to services. COVID-19 caused disruptions to mobility globally, yet its long-term impacts in Latin America remain poorly understood. Using  > 170 million anonymised and aggregated location records from Meta-Facebook users in Argentina, Chile and Colombia (April 2020-May 2022), we examine changes in overall mobility volume relative to pre-pandemic baselines across socioeconomic and rural-urban gradients. Two years after the pandemic onset, mobility in the highest-density urban cores remained  ~ 25-50% below baseline across the three countries, while the top 33% most affluent communities had not returned to baseline. These differences are explained by the scale of the initial mobility shock rather than by subsequent recovery rates. Our findings reveal how a global shock can entrench disparities in human mobility, with implications for urban resilience and planning in unequal nations. Our study underscores the need for proactive policies to prevent long-lasting mobility inequalities.

articles.title: Letter: Prediction Timing and Comparative Performance of the HALP Score for Postoperative Atrial Fibrillation After Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery.
Pharmacogenomic Testing in Pediatric Medicine: A Literature-Based Overview of Implementation Programs.
articles.abstract: Clinical implementation of pharmacogenomics (PGx) can optimize drug response and minimize adverse drug reactions. However, barriers exist toward implementation in clinical practice, particularly in pediatrics, where robust evidence is limited. A comprehensive literature search across three databases identified studies reporting current PGx implementation in pediatric care. Studies were independently assessed by two individuals, and inclusion required active or near-future PGx implementation in pediatrics. The search identified 46 articles describing 45 institutes with documented pediatric PGx implementation, most based in China (n = 15), the United States (n = 13), Canada (n = 3), and Europe (n = 3). PGx testing was mainly used in oncology (15.5%), neurology (14.7%), and hematology (11.6%). The most frequently tested genes were TPMT (56%), CYP2C19 (56%), CYP3A5 (50%), CYP2D6 (47%), and CYP2C9 (47%). Over 140 drugs were included in PGx testing in pediatrics, of which 31 drugs were tested for at ≥5 institutes. The top drugs were mercaptopurine, azathioprine, and thioguanine. Notably, these PGx targets cluster in pediatric hemato-oncology, where they contribute to optimization of anticancer treatment, supportive care, and may be used to reduce direct and late treatment-related adverse effects. Successful implementation programs often started by establishing a PGx project team, increasing awareness of possible clinical implications, developing standard operating procedures, integrating PGx results into the electronic health record with clinical decision support, and educating physicians and patients. To improve the use of PGx in pediatric care, more clinical studies in pediatric populations are needed to improve generalizability and geographic representativeness of evidence and to support integration into clinical protocols.

articles.title: (Meth)acrylate Allergy in the Era of Nail Cosmetics and Medical Devices: Limitations of HEMA and Optimization of Patch Testing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: (Meth)acrylate allergy is increasingly caused by modern exposures such as nail cosmetics and diabetes-related medical devices. The performance of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) as a screening allergen and the optimal composition of patch test series remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate patch test results to a (meth)acrylate series, assess the performance of HEMA, analyze co-reactivity patterns, and optimize allergen panels.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted in 955 patients patch tested with a (meth)acrylate series between 2015 and 2025. Frequencies of positive reactions, clinical relevance, causative products, co-reactivity and diagnostic yield of individual allergens were analyzed.

RESULTS: Of 955 patients, 176 (18.4%) had ≥ 1 positive reaction. Nail cosmetics (47%) and diabetes devices (15%) were the main sources. HEMA identified 61% of sensitized patients; 39% would have been missed if tested alone, including 32% of clinically relevant cases. Sensitivity varied by exposure, performing well in nail cosmetics (94%) but poorly in diabetes devices (12%) and other categories. Strong clustering and co-reactivity were observed. Complete detection was achieved with 13 haptens, while 6 and 8 identified 90% and 95% of cases.

CONCLUSIONS: HEMA is not sufficient as a universal screening allergen. Testing can be optimized by tailored, exposure-based allergen panels.

articles.title: Precise Fluorination Amplifies the Theranostic Potential of FAP-Targeting Cyclic Peptide-Based Radioligands: From Preclinical Discovery to Clinical Validation.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeting radiopharmaceuticals have emerged as promising imaging agents for stromal-rich malignancies; however, their therapeutic potential remains limited by insufficient cellular internalization, leading to suboptimal intratumoral uptake and retention. Leveraging fluorine's "magic" effects on potency, permeability, and pharmacokinetics, we developed FAP-targeting cyclic peptide radioligands with enhanced in vivo tumor retention and improved pharmacokinetics via structure-guided residue fluorination. Screening 18 rationally designed FAP-2286 derivatives yielded three lead fluorinated analogs. Preclinical studies showed that fluorination patterns strongly influenced in vivo behavior; structure-activity relationship analyses linked these effects to lipophilicity, metabolic stability, cellular uptake, and FAP-binding affinity. Second-round PEGylation and N-terminal modification of six peptides further improved tumor retention and reduced non-target accumulation, identifying [68Ga]Ga-HKF-020 as the optimal clinical candidate. In a first-in-human study of 20 volunteers, exploratory subgroup analyses showed higher uptake of [68Ga]Ga-HKF-020 in metabolically active lesions, together with lower uptake in selected non-target organs, compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286. Therapeutically, [177Lu]Lu-HKF-020 and [177Lu]Lu-HKF-024 produced pronounced tumor growth inhibition without evident treatment-related toxicity. Thus, this study establishes fluorination as a robust and facile strategy for optimizing the theranostic potential of FAP-targeting cyclic peptide radioligands, providing a broadly applicable chemical approach to enhance the pharmacological properties of diverse peptide radioligands.

articles.title: An FGFR2-Targeted PET/NIR-II Dual-Modal Probe for Metastatic Lymph Node Detection and Intraoperative Guidance in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Accurate identification of metastatic lymph nodes (LNs) remains a major challenge in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) surgery. Single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunohistochemistry reveal enrichment of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) in metastatic LNs, providing a clinically informed target for molecular imaging. Guided by this finding, an FGFR2-targeted dual-modality probe, 18F-NOTA-(ICG)-DcP5, is engineered by integrating the cyclic peptide DcP5, indocyanine green (ICG), and a NOTA radiolabeling module within a unified molecular construct. The probe enables complementary positron emission tomography (PET) and second near-infrared-window (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging across whole-body and local operative settings, while competitive blocking supports an FGFR2-dependent targeting component. Across subcutaneous and orthotopic ESCC models, a proof-of-concept lymph node dissemination model, and metastatic LN-derived patient-derived xenografts, the imaging strategy supports lesion detection, lymph-node discrimination, and NIR-II-guided intraoperative localization. The probe achieves a NIR-II tumor-to-background ratio of 3.64 ± 0.23, exceeding clinical ICG (1.39 ± 0.20) by 162%. A rapid ex vivo incubation protocol further distinguishes metastatic from non-metastatic LNs in freshly resected human surgical specimens using histopathology as the reference standard (AUC = 0.9167). By bridging clinically informed target discovery with multimodal image-guided intervention, this work advances a precision strategy for selective lymph -node management in ESCC.

articles.title: A Methodological and Interpretive Framework to Strengthen Scientific Rigor in Plant Virus Seed Transmission Research: A Case Study of Begomoviruses.
articles.abstract: Interpreting evidence on seed transmission of plant viruses remains challenging because studies often differ in the strength of biological evidence and the context in which that evidence is generated. As a result, findings may be over- or under-interpreted, resulting in inconsistent terminology and making comparisons across studies difficult. A review of 22 recent begomovirus seed transmission studies revealed substantial methodological variation, including differences in seed source, mother-plant infection method, seed handling, grow-out assay design and scale, timing of progeny plant evaluation and testing, and the extent of confirmation of virus viability or infectivity in progeny plants. To address these issues, we introduce the Rigor and Relevance Pyramid as an interpretive framework for research on seed transmission of plant viruses. The Pyramid separates two independent but related dimensions of inference: the strength of biological evidence and the relevance of the experimental context. The evidence/rigor axis distinguishes seed association, putative progeny plant infection, and biologically confirmed seed-to-progeny transmission, whereas the epidemiological relevance axis distinguishes proof-of-concept, controlled validation, and natural or epidemiological contexts. This approach helps clarify what type of conclusions a given study can reasonably support and promotes more consistent use of terms such as "seed-associated," "seed-borne," and "seed-transmitted." Practical experimental considerations are also outlined to help align study design with the intended level of inference. By linking evidentiary strength to study context, the framework improves interpretation and consistency among studies and provides a clearer basis for interpretation in pest risk assessment and seed health management.

articles.title: Hyperglycaemia-Associated Neutrophil Dysregulation Links SIRT1 Suppression to NET-Mediated Kidney and Vascular Injury.
articles.abstract: Long-term complications of diabetes mellitus include diabetic kidney disease and cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms linking these comorbidities remain incompletely understood. Here, TMLE analyses in human cohorts with cardiovascular disease revealed that increasing glucose levels were associated with neutrophilia, systemic inflammation, vascular and renal injury, supporting a role for neutrophils in hyperglycaemia-associated end-organ damage. In hyperglycaemic Apoe- / - mice with pre-existing atherosclerosis, hyperglycaemia was accompanied by increased neutrophil production, accelerated bone marrow egress, prolonged circulating lifespan, and enhanced neutrophil infiltration into the kidney and atherosclerotic plaques, alongside tissue injury and atherosclerosis progression. Mechanistically, hyperglycaemia was associated with reduced neutrophil sirtuin 1 activity and increased neutrophil extracellular trap formation. Pharmacological activation of sirtuin 1 reduced neutrophil extracellular trap formation and attenuated renal injury, vascular inflammation, and atherosclerotic plaque progression in vivo. Together, these findings support a neutrophil-associated mechanism linking hyperglycaemia to cardiovascular and renal complications in the context of pre-existing cardiovascular disease and highlight SIRT1 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy to mitigate hyperglycaemia-associated renal and cardiovascular complications.

articles.title: Key Factors Influencing Emergence of Anguina funesta from Annual Ryegrass Seed Galls.
articles.abstract: Anguina funesta is a regulated seed gall nematode infecting cool-season annual ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum) in Oregon's Willamette Valley, where much of the world's grass seed is produced. Because detection of this quarantine pest in seed lots results in rejection at international ports, Oregon seed growers need management strategies that reduce A. funesta infection in production fields. To best employ effective management strategies, an understanding of the biological and environmental factors triggering second-stage juvenile (J2) emergence is needed to exploit the most vulnerable life stage of this nematode. Therefore, in this study, we investigated how abiotic factors (temperature and moisture) and biotic factors (presence of maternal floral bracts and root exudates) influence J2 emergence in the Oregon seed production system. Removal of maternal floral bracts from galls resulted in the fastest emergence at 4°C, with time to 50% emergence (T50) at 15.8 to 26.1 days. Conversely, intact galls exhibited peak emergence velocity at 10°C (T50 = 30.8 to 31.4 days), demonstrating a structural 'thermal decoupling' mechanism where gall tissue degradation regulates nematode emergence. Furthermore, intact galls on a wetted soil substrate at 10°C exhibited prolonged T50 of 40.7 to 74.8 days (P < 0.0001), identifying a significant hydrological barrier to emergence. Finally, root exudates and timing impacted emergence velocity (P < 0.01) where exudates from non-hosts accelerated emergence compared to the water control, and Week 1 and Week 3 exudates driving slower emergence thresholds than Week 2 exudates. These findings will support predictively timed management strategies and future epidemiological studies.

articles.title: Enterovirus 71 Infection Orchestrates One-Carbon Metabolism and S-Adenosylmethionine Generation to Drive Inflammation-Related Chromatin Methylation.
articles.abstract: S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) is the major methyl donor for histone, DNA, and RNA methylation, thereby linking cellular metabolism to chromatin state and gene transcription. However, how enterovirus 71 (EV71) infection regulates SAM generation and how SAM-dependent methylation contributes to host gene regulation remain unclear. Here, we show that EV71 infection enhances glucose-, serine-, and methionine-derived metabolic inputs into the methionine cycle and promotes SAM generation through de novo ATP synthesis. Mechanistically, EV71 2Apro cleaves ubiquitin-protein ligase E3 component n-recognin 4 (UBR4), thereby reducing UBR4-mediated MAT2A ubiquitination and stabilizing MAT2A to support SAM production. We further show that EV71 3Cpro promotes SETD2-dependent trimethylation of histone H3 at lysine 36 (H3K36me3), which is associated with DNMT3B enrichment and gene-body DNA methylation at inflammatory and cell-death-associated genes. In parallel, EV71 3Dpol interacts with METTL14, a core component of the m6A methyltransferase complex, and contributes to m6A deposition on host transcripts. Disrupting the 2Apro/UBR4, 3Cpro/SETD2, 3Cpro/DNMT3B, or 3Dpol/METTL14 interactions using designed cell-penetrating peptides reduced EV71-induced methylation changes, viral replication, inflammatory responses, and tissue injury. Together, our findings reveal a metabolic-epigenetic regulatory axis by which EV71 rewires one-carbon metabolism and SAM availability to promote methylation-dependent host gene expression and inflammatory pathogenesis.

articles.title: The Dual GCGR/GLP-1R Agonist Survodutide Demonstrates Multiple Cardiometabolic Benefits in a Free Choice Diet-Induced Obese Hamster Model.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Survodutide, a glucagon/GLP-1 receptor dual agonist, is currently being investigated in Phase 3 clinical trials in people living with obesity and metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Here we explored whether survodutide provides cardiometabolic benefits in the golden Syrian hamster, a preclinical model with a human-like lipoprotein metabolism.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Lean or free choice diet-induced obese (DIO) hamsters were treated subcutaneously once daily for up to 7 weeks with vehicle or survodutide at various doses (3-30 nmol/kg) to evaluate the cardiometabolic benefits.

RESULTS: In DIO hamsters, survodutide dose-dependently reduced plasma amino acid levels and decreased body weight, with reduction in high fat/cholesterol diet and 10% fructose water intakes. In lean hamsters with free access to water or alcohol, survodutide also reduced alcohol intake significantly. In DIO hamsters treated with survodutide at 20 nmol/kg, the weight lowering effect of survodutide reduced the proportion of fat mass and increased the proportion of lean mass and significantly reduced the HOMA-IR index of insulin resistance, peri-pancreatic and peri-renal fat mass and intra-muscular fat content. Survodutide significantly reduced total cholesterol levels including LDL-cholesterol and strongly lowered fasting plasma triglycerides. Additionally, survodutide treatment was associated with lower heart and left ventricle weight (both p < 0.001 vs. vehicle), and lower E/A ratio as measured by echocardiography (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Survodutide demonstrated multiple cardiometabolic benefits in hamsters. Our preclinical data further emphasize the potential of survodutide for the treatment of obesity and related comorbidities.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of Automated Insulin Delivery in Young People With Type 1 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate changes in glycaemic and psychosocial outcomes among young people with Type 1 diabetes after AID initiation in real-world settings.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library (1 January 2016 to 4 June 2026) for prospective real-world studies involving young people (≤ 21 years) initiating AID. Primary outcomes were TIR and HbA1c. Three-level random-effects models were used, complemented by prespecified subgroup, sensitivity and multivariable meta-regression analyses. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using ROBINS-I and GRADE.

RESULTS: Forty-three prospective studies involving 3668 participants were included. After AID initiation, TIR increased by 11.54 percentage points (95% CI 9.60-13.49) and HbA1c decreased by 0.64 percentage points (95% CI -0.84 to -0.44), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 95.8% and 97.0%, respectively) and prediction intervals included the null value. Longer follow-up was associated with smaller improvements in TIR and smaller reductions in TAR across studies, whereas no statistically significant association was observed for TBR. Studies with higher mean baseline HbA1c reported greater improvements in TIR and TAR, but not TBR. Hypoglycaemia Fear Survey (HFS) scores decreased in both patients and caregivers, and caregiver-reported Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) scores also decreased; evidence for improvements in patient-reported PAID scores was limited. The certainty of evidence was low for the primary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: AID initiation was followed by improved glycaemic outcomes and reduced hypoglycaemia fear and caregiver-reported distress. However, substantial heterogeneity and low-certainty evidence warrant cautious interpretation. Controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework (OSF), https://osf.io/uw8mp/.

articles.title: Effect of Oral Deglusterol on Fasting Glucose and Insulin Resistance in Adults With Prediabetes: A Randomised, Double-Blind and Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of Deglusterol, a synthetic peptide, for improving fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and metabolic parameters in adults with prediabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 adults with prediabetes at four Indian sites were assigned 1:1 to oral Deglusterol (30 mg twice daily; 60 mg/day) or placebo for 28 days. The primary endpoint was change in FPG. Secondary endpoints included fasting plasma insulin (FPI), HbA1c, C-peptide, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), HOMA-β, quantitative insulin sensitivity check index (QUICKI), lipids, blood pressure and body composition. Efficacy was analysed in the modified intention-to-treat population by analysis of covariance.

RESULTS: At Day 28, Deglusterol significantly reduced baseline-adjusted FPG versus placebo (least-squares mean difference: -9.24 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval: -16.39 to -2.09; p = 0.035). In exploratory analyses, between-group differences favoured Deglusterol for FPI (-18.58 μIU/mL; p = 0.009), C-peptide (-2.06 ng/mL; p = 0.019), HOMA-IR (-0.96; p = 0.027) and QUICKI (+0.03; p = 0.009), whereas HbA1c, body weight and body fat mass did not differ significantly. Three Deglusterol-treated participants (8.6%) had mild-to-moderate treatment-emergent adverse events, none serious.

CONCLUSIONS: Deglusterol for 28 days was associated with greater FPG reduction versus placebo in adults with prediabetes, alongside favourable exploratory between-group differences in insulin-related markers, supporting its further evaluation as a peptide-based approach to early glycaemic management. Larger, longer trials are required to assess effects on HbA1c and durability of efficacy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials Registry-India, CTRI/2023/01/048723.

articles.title: External Validation of Diabetes Risk Prediction Models in Women With a History of Gestational Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The aim of the study was to externally validate diabetes risk prediction models in women with a history of gestational diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Discrimination was evaluated with the Harrell's C-index. Calibration was evaluated by comparing predicted risks against observed risks.

RESULTS: Among the 1180 participants, 104 cases of incident diabetes were identified during a median follow-up of 8.1 years. Harrell's C-index was 0.819 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.864) for the model proposed by Belsti et al., 0.788 (95% CI 0.740-0.836) for the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Diabetes Risk Model, 0.773 (95% CI 0.723-0.824) for the Framingham Diabetes Risk Model (FDRM), 0.770 (95% CI 0.722-0.818) for the Man model, 0.736 (95% CI 0.685-0.788) for the Ignell model, 0.707 (95% CI 0.653-0.761) for the Li model, 0.706 (95% CI 0.654-0.758) for the Köhler model, 0.702 (95% CI 0.650-0.754) for the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score, 0.689 (95% CI 0.636-0.742) for the American Diabetes Association Diabetes Risk Test and 0.665 (95% CI 0.607-0.723) for the Parkhi model. The Belsti model, ARIC model and FDRM showed good calibration after in-cohort recalibration for 5- and 10-year incident diabetes. The sensitivity of the median score of the Belsti model was 93% (95% CI 83%-100%) for incident diabetes at Year 5.

CONCLUSIONS: Among women with prior gestational diabetes, the Belsti et al. model demonstrated good discrimination for predicting incident diabetes and may help guide screening frequency. The ARIC model and the FDRM are simple, valid tools for diabetes risk prediction in this population.

articles.title: Association of fibrosis-4 index with cardio-cerebro-renal morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes beyond liver diseases.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study hypothesized that the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index could serve as a simple marker for risk stratification of multiple organ outcomes, including cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal diseases, beyond liver disease in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: Patients with T2DM who had sufficient data to calculate FIB-4 within one year before or after diagnosis were identified from a multi-hospital system in Taiwan between January 2008 and December 2023. Outcomes included the incidence of and mortality from cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal diseases. Adjusted incidence rate ratios (aIRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using Poisson regression. Adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: Among 54,651 patients (379,481 person-years), risks generally increased across FIB-4 categories. Compared with the low FIB-4 group (<1.3), the intermediate (1.30-2.67) and high (>2.67) FIB-4 groups had higher risks of incident cardiovascular disease (aIRR: 1.34, 95%CI: 1.22-1.46 and aIRR: 1.94, 95%CI: 1.74-2.17, respectively) and cardiovascular mortality (aHR: 1.27, 95%CI: 1.08-1.49 and aHR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.46-2.14, respectively). Higher FIB-4 levels were also associated with incident renal disease (aIRR: 1.18; 95%CI: 1.07-1.30 and aIRR: 1.25, 95%CI: 1.10-1.41, respectively), but not significantly with renal disease-related mortality (aHR: 1.01, 95%CI: 0.76-1.33 and aHR: 1.35, 95%CI: 0.96-1.89, respectively). Associations with incident cerebrovascular disease (aIRR: 1.05, 95%CI: 0.93-1.19 and aIRR: 1.13, 95%CI: 0.96-1.33, respectively) and cerebrovascular mortality (aHR: 0.98, 95%CI: 0.75-1.29 and aHR: 1.20, 95%CI: 0.86-1.68, respectively) were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Beyond liver disease, the FIB-4 index may serve as a simple clinical marker for stratifying the risks of cardiovascular disease incidence and mortality, and incident renal disease, in patients with T2DM.

articles.title: [A hypoxemic pneumonia cluster caused by Histoplasma capsulatum in Guadeloupe].
articles.abstract: We report on a cluster of four patients admitted to the University Hospital of Guadeloupe due to acute hypoxemic respiratory distress associated with a diffuse interstitial syndrome. Two patients required intensive care due to clinical severity, while the remaining two were hospitalized in the pulmonology ward. Clinical interviews revealed shared recent exposure: participation in a group activity involving the cleaning of an abandoned cabin. Pulmonary mycological investigations confirmed infection with Histoplasma capsulatum. In one patient, the diagnosis was established through an H. capsulatum PCR performed on bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. An environmental investigation conducted inside the cabin identified as the exposure site detected the fungus, thereby corroborating the link between the event and the cluster. While the patients with hypoxemia achieved favorable outcomes under combined antifungal therapy and corticosteroids, the non-hypoxemic patients responded satisfactorily to antifungal therapy alone. These four cases were part of a larger group of eighteen potentially exposed individuals, fourteen of whom underwent systematic clinical evaluation. This cluster highlights (a) the diagnostic challenges posed by histoplasmosis in areas of low endemicity and (b) the variability of its clinical presentation. The clinical case underscores the value of sensitive diagnostic tools, particularly PCR, with regard to severe acute presentations. Lastly, this report lays emphasis on the importance of environmental investigations in view of identifying sources of exposure, guiding clinical assessment, and preventing further cases.

articles.title: [Chronic bronchiolitis? How about pulmonary nocardiosis?].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The term bronchiolitis refers to inflammation of the bronchioles, the distal ends of the airway. In adults, involvement may result from a wide range of underlying pathologies. According to some studies, its etiology remains unknown in 31% of cases, and involvement is referred to as idiopathic or cryptogenic. To our knowledge, nocardiosis has not previously been reported as a cause of chronic bronchiolitis. With this in mind, we report a clinical case confirming the existence of nocardiosis bronchiolitis, which had previously been described, and suggesting the existence of nocardiosis bronchiolitis as a chronic disease.

OBSERVATION: This clinical case is the first description of chronic nocardiosis bronchiolitis treated by antibiotics (sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim) over a period of six months. The clinical and radiological course was favorable, with improved symptomatology, expected resolution of recent cavitary lesion and, most notably, regression of diffuse micronodular involvement that had been followed for more than seven years, with no known explanatory factor other than nocardiosis treatment.

CONCLUSION: The above-mentioned clinical course is suggestive of chronic nocardiosis bronchiolitis, a hypothesis that will require confirmation in further studies or clinical case reports. In case of idiopathic bronchiolitis, however, screening for nocardiosis by bronchoalveolar lavage can already be recommended.

articles.title: Phosphate Additives in Ultra-Processed Foods: Greater Intake, Distribution, and Bioavailability, With Hidden Risks to Kidney Health.
articles.abstract: Scientific interest in phosphate-containing food additives (Pi-additives) stems from their relevance to dietary management of chronic kidney disease, whereas public concerns are centered on excess phosphate intake associated with their largely unrestricted use in the industrial processing of widely consumed foods and beverages and a potential link to premature mortality. This perspective examines how Western diets have transitioned toward ultra-processed foods and beverages, which now account for 60%-70% of calorie intake, and how this shift has been linked to the rise in noncommunicable diseases-notably chronic kidney disease-and mortality and to substantial increases in Pi-additive intake, contributing to excessive phosphorus consumption. We describe the broad range of inorganic and organic Pi-additives and their regulation by the European Union and US Food and Drug Administration, their technical functions that promote extensive use in food processing, and differences in phosphate absorption. Survey intake limitations and inadequate nutrient databases hinder determination of needed individual intake exposure estimates of Pi-additives critical to determining safe use and causal associations of high Pi-additive ultra-processed food intake with kidney disease risk. Together, these intake needs and Pi-additive features provide the basis for exploring mechanisms underlying the toxic effects of Pi-additives on kidney health and related chronic diseases.

articles.title: Association Between Mental Health Disorders and Non-dispensed Prescriptions Among Adults With Chronic Diseases: A Nationwide Register-Based Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Medication non-adherence is a major challenge in the management of chronic diseases. Mental health disorders commonly co-occur with somatic conditions and may impair patients' ability to initiate and manage their pharmacological treatment. The aim of this study is to examine the association between mental health disorders and primary non-adherence to medication in chronic diseases.

METHODS: We used comprehensive nationwide register data from Finland on outpatient prescriptions, patient characteristics, and taxable income in 2021. The study population comprised individuals using medications for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, or asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Primary non-adherence was defined based on prescriptions that had not been dispensed by a community pharmacy within the 2-year validity period of the prescription. Those with mental health disorders were matched 1:1 with controls without mental health disorders using propensity score matching based on age, sex, income level, and measures of disease severity and comorbidities. Linear probability model was used to estimate the adjusted difference in the probability of having at least one non-dispensed prescription.

FINDINGS: Among the 695,628 matched individuals, those with mental health disorders had a higher prevalence of primary non-adherence to medications for chronic diseases compared to those without mental health disorders. After adjustment, those with mental health disorders were associated with a 0.7 percentage point (p < 0.001) increase in the probability of having at least one non-dispensed prescription compared to those without.

IMPLICATIONS: Mental health disorders were associated with a higher probability of primary non‑adherence to medications for chronic diseases. Although the adjusted difference was small (0.7 percentage points), the findings suggest that treatment initiation among individuals with co-occurring mental and somatic conditions may warrant attention at the population level.

articles.title: Primate area FST: a nexus for synthesizing a world in motion.
articles.abstract: Encoding the content of the dynamic, three-dimensional (3D) world is an overarching function of the visual system. Research on the middle temporal area (MT) has been instrumental in establishing the neural basis of two-dimensional velocity and depth computations in primates. In this review, we explore how the fundus of the superior temporal sulcus (FST), an area downstream of MT, may contribute to the construction of behaviorally relevant representations of where objects are headed, what shape they have, and why they move. We survey structural and functional evidence from macaques and humans that implicates FST in this complex synthesis. Based on the collective evidence, we propose that FST supports the perception of a cohesive 3D world by bridging the dorsal 'where', ventral 'what', and more recently posited lateral 'social' visual pathways.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in primary care: prevalence and risk factor insights.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains underdiagnosed, especially in primary care (PC), where most at-risk patients present themselves.

METHODS: A cross-sectional prospectively recruited cohort study was conducted in Belgian PC. The prevalence of fibrosis and steatosis was evaluated using Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography (VCTE) and Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAPTM). Non-invasive tests (NITs) (Fibrosis 4-index (FIB-4), Forns Index (FI), NAFLD Fibrosis Score (NFS), Fatty Liver Index (FLI), and Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI)) were calculated. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify risk factors for steatosis and fibrosis.

RESULTS: The prevalence of MASLD was 60.6% (n = 348/574) (≥248 dB/m combined with cardiometabolic criteria), with 9.9% and 2.6% showing significant (≥8 kPa) and advanced fibrosis (>12 kPa). NITs yielded prevalence estimates for advanced fibrosis: FIB-4 (4.4%), FI (5.1%), and NFS (7.7%). Steatosis was detected in 61.5%, 50.1%, and 62.6% of the cohort using CAPTM, FLI, and HSI. Higher BMI was associated with steatosis (OR 1.25, p < 0.001) and fibrosis (OR 1.12, p < 0.001). Male sex was a risk factor for both (p < 0.05). Elevated triglycerides and GGT were linked to steatosis, T2DM and high AST to fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: MASLD affects over 60% of our PC cohort, and 12% needs further fibrosis assessment. These findings show the potential utility of NITs in identifying and referring at-risk individuals in PC.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT04647409.

articles.title: The effect of wearing a sleep cap on the sleep and physiological variables of infants hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit: A randomized controlled experimental study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the effect of a specially designed sleep cap on the sleep and physiological variables of infants hospitalized in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).

METHODS: This randomized controlled experimental study included 53 infants (Intervention group: 26, Control group: 27) born after 32 weeks of gestation between September 2020 and March 2021. Infants in the intervention group wore a sleep cap developed by the investigator during sleep, while infants in the control group did not. Video recordings were taken over three consecutive days (7:00 PM and 7:00 AM) and evaluated by the investigator and an independent expert. Variables evaluated included sleep duration, number of awakenings, and physiological parameters. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square test, t-test, Mann-Whitney U test, Friedman test, Wilcoxon test, and repeated measures ANOVA.

RESULTS: On the third follow-up day, a statistically significant increase in sleep duration was observed in the intervention group compared to the control group (p = 0.006). Although there was no significant difference in the total number of awakenings, a significant decrease in awakenings was detected, especially in premature infants (p = 0.016). In addition, significantly higher oxygen saturation levels were observed in the intervention group on the second follow-up day (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The use of the developed sleep cap increased sleep duration, reduced awakenings, and improved oxygen saturation levels in infants in the NICU.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: The use of a sleep cap may be recommended to improve sleep quality in infants hospitalized in the NICU.

CLINICAL TRIALS ID: The research protocol was registered in the Clinical Trials with the NCT07423962.

articles.title: Psychometric evaluation of the DiKA-T1D-v2: An educational assessment tool to support personalised diabetes education in adolescents and young adults with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To update and psychometrically evaluate the Knowledge About Type 1 Diabetes (DiKA-T1D), an educational assessment tool designed to identify individual knowledge gaps and support personalised diabetes education in adolescents and young adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D).

METHODS: A methodological study was conducted with 115 adolescents and young adults with T1D attending two Portuguese diabetes outpatient clinics. The original DiKA-T1D was revised to reflect advances in diabetes technology and current self-management recommendations. Content validity was assessed through expert review and feedback from young people with T1D. Psychometric evaluation included item difficulty and discrimination, internal consistency, and confirmatory factor analysis.

RESULTS: The Knowledge About Type 1 Diabetes, version 2 (DiKA-T1D-v2) demonstrated satisfactory content validity and incorporated clinically relevant knowledge domains, including contemporary diabetes technologies and self-management. Item difficulty and discrimination varied substantially across the instrument, indicating differentiated performance across knowledge areas. Internal consistency was modest (KR-20 = 0.51). Confirmatory factor analysis provided limited support for a homogeneous latent structure, indicating substantial heterogeneity across knowledge domains. These findings support interpreting the DiKA-T1D-v2 primarily as a clinically oriented educational assessment rather than as a homogeneous psychometric scale.

CONCLUSION: The DiKA-T1D-v2 provides an updated assessment of diabetes knowledge that may support paediatric nursing practice by helping identify individual knowledge gaps, tailor educational interventions, and monitor learning over time. Further validation in larger and more diverse populations is needed to strengthen evidence regarding its measurement properties and clinical utility.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: The DiKA-T1D-v2 may support paediatric nurses in identifying individual knowledge gaps and tailoring diabetes education to the needs of adolescents and young adults.

articles.title: Reply to Letter to the Editor regarding: "Papillary Muscle VT and Recurrence After Ablation: Interpreting Procedural and Structural Complexity".
Cardiovascular Risk Associated With Psychostimulant Therapy in Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
AIM: We aimed to evaluate the cardiovascular safety of psychostimulant medications for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), review current screening guidelines, and propose a novel clinical evaluation framework to specifically guide prescribing clinicians and cardiologists.

METHOD: We conducted a International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews-registered systematic review of peer-reviewed literature, meta-analyses, and clinical guidelines. Electronic searches were performed in MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO, and Cochrane CENTRAL (January 2005 to October 2025), alongside major guideline repositories.

RESULTS: Data was synthesised from 52 studies and six medical society guidelines. Although psychostimulants cause modest increases in baseline heart rate and systolic blood pressure, contemporary data demonstrates no significant increase in the relative risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, or sudden cardiac death in healthy populations. However, the risk profile in older adults and those with cardiovascular comorbidities remains uncertain, with a small number of studies showing potential risk. Current guidelines recommend baseline history and physical examination but advise against broad-based electrocardiogram (ECG) screening or routine cardiology referrals without clinical red flags. However, these guidelines are outdated and predominantly focused on a paediatric population. They under-recognise potential risk for older and comorbid patients. To address this gap, we propose a novel, evidence-graded clinical evaluation framework comprising clear baseline assessments, and explicit red flags warranting an ECG or cardiology opinion. This framework incorporates age- and risk-stratified referral pathways and introduces specific age thresholds (routine referral for asymptomatic patients aged >65 years, and consideration for those aged 50-65 years). In addition, there is an emphasis on an individualised approach to managing complex comorbidities that balances cardiovascular risk against the morbidity of untreated ADHD.

CONCLUSIONS: Psychostimulants are safe in young, healthy populations, but potential risks for older patients and those with pre-existing cardiovascular comorbidities require careful clinical consideration.

articles.title: Haptoglobin Phenotype and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The haptoglobin (Hp) 2-2 phenotype, due to its poor antioxidant profile, has been postulated to be associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), especially in those with diabetes. However, there are conflicting results in the literature.

METHOD: A systematic review of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) was performed to identify studies that reported CVD outcomes among people with different Hp phenotypes (PROSPERO registration: CRD42024617869). Meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model to determine the relative risk (RR) of CVD outcomes in people with the Hp 2-2 versus non-Hp 2-2 phenotype.

RESULTS: A total of 792 studies were screened. For any CVD, 38 studies were included (n=69,824 participants). Hp 2-2 phenotype was not associated with a higher risk of CVD (RR [95% confidence interval (CI)] 1.01 [0.98-1.05]; p=0.46, I2=37.1%). No significant association was found for myocardial infarction (n=13 studies), stroke (n=7), CVD mortality (n=7), peripheral artery disease (n=2), atrial fibrillation (n=2), or heart failure (n=2). For coronary artery disease/coronary heart disease (CAD/CHD) (n=21), a borderline significant association was observed (p=0.049), especially in the diabetes subgroup (n=13; RR [95% CI] 1.14 [1.01-1.29]; p=0.041); however, Egger's test suggested potential publication bias.

CONCLUSION: Our results suggest the Hp phenotype alone may be of limited clinical prognostic value for CVD risk. However, it does not preclude the possibility that treatment effects may differ by Hp phenotype. Further studies are needed to elucidate the impact of Hp levels and whether CVD treatment outcomes differ by Hp phenotype.

articles.title: Reply to Letter to the Editor "Papillary muscles and Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia" regarding: "Papillary Muscle-Originated Ventricular Tachycardia in Advanced Heart Failure: The Role of RAAS and Sympathetic Activation on Substrate Formation".
Papillary Muscle-Originated Ventricular Tachycardia in Advanced Heart Failure: The Role of RAAS and Sympathetic Activation on Substrate Formation.
Cardiovascular Complications of Methamphetamine Use: An Australian Perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Methamphetamine use is increasing in Australia and internationally, with cardiovascular disease emerging as a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Despite growing recognition of methamphetamine-associated cardiovascular disease, dedicated Australian clinical guidelines remain lacking.

METHOD: A narrative review was performed with literature published between 2000 and 2025. Evidence relating to methamphetamine-associated coronary artery disease, pulmonary hypertension, cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, and management was synthesised with emphasis on the Australian context.

RESULTS: Methamphetamine contributes substantially to healthcare utilisation and cardiovascular morbidity in Australia. Chronic exposure is associated with accelerated coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, pulmonary arterial hypertension, cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Methamphetamine-associated cardiomyopathy frequently presents with severe heart failure in younger patients, although partial reversibility may occur with abstinence. Managing methamphetamine-associated cardiovascular disease is complicated by psychosocial instability, relapse risk, and uncertainty regarding eligibility for advanced heart failure therapies. Australian literature also highlights fragmented care pathways and limited integration between cardiology, addiction medicine, and mental health services.

CONCLUSIONS: Major evidence gaps remain regarding methamphetamine-associated cardiovascular disease epidemiology, advanced therapies, long-term outcomes, and optimal integrated care pathways in Australia. National multidisciplinary guidelines and prospective Australian registries are urgently needed.

articles.title: Prognostic value of early renal recovery after cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) is common and strongly associated with adverse outcomes. Whether the timing of renal recovery adds prognostic information beyond AKI severity remains uncertain. We examined the association between renal recovery status after CSA-AKI and long-term mortality.

METHODS: In a retrospective cohort from a nationally representative US electronic health record platform (2016-25), we identified adults who developed CSA-AKI within 7 days of coronary artery bypass grafting, valve surgery, or thoracic aortic surgery. The primary exposure was renal recovery status at 7 (early recovery) and 90 days (transition to chronic kidney disease [CKD]) after CSA-AKI onset. Full renal recovery was defined as a return of serum creatinine to <1.5× baseline and <26 μM above baseline, without dialysis. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations between non-recovery and the primary outcome of all-cause mortality, adjusting for AKI stage and prespecified covariates.

RESULTS: From 539 658 patients, 111 232 (20.6%) developed CSA-AKI (mean age 68 yr; range 19-94; 28% female). In the early-recovery analysis, 90 029 of 111 232 patients (80.9%) recovered within 7 days; in the CKD-transition analysis, 94 064 of 100 916 (93.2%) recovered within 90 days. Both early non-recovery (adjusted hazard ratio 1.20; 95% CI 1.15-1.25; P<0.001) and transition to CKD by day 90 (adjusted hazard ratio 1.12; 95% CI 1.04-1.20; P=0.002) were independently associated with higher mortality. Our findings were consistent across AKI stages.

CONCLUSIONS: Both delayed renal recovery and transition to CKD after CSA-AKI are associated with higher long-term all-cause mortality that is independent of CSA-AKI severity.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Retatrutide in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes, Overweight or Obesity: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity are major global health challenges, and substantial weight loss alongside effective glycaemic control remains an unmet therapeutic need. Retatrutide, a novel once-weekly unimolecular triple agonist of the GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, may provide greater weight reduction and metabolic benefits than currently available therapies. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of retatrutide in adults with T2DM, overweight or obesity.

METHODS: Electronic databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing retatrutide with placebo in adults with T2DM, overweight or obesity. Random effect models were used to pool continuous outcomes as mean differences (MDs) and binary outcomes as risk ratios (RRs), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-based subgroup analyses were performed. The primary outcome was absolute change in body weight.

RESULTS: Five RCTs including 2323 participants were included. Retatrutide significantly reduced body weight (MD, -10.77 kg; 95% CI, -14.56 to -6.98), HbA1c (MD, -1.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.17 to -0.89) and waist circumference (MD, -8.20 cm; 95% CI, -10.28 to -6.11). Retatrutide increased the risks of nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea and constipation, whereas serious adverse events were comparable with placebo.

CONCLUSION: Retatrutide substantially improves weight and glycaemic outcomes but increases gastrointestinal adverse events. Further large-scale trials are needed to establish its long-term efficacy, safety and cardiovascular effects.

articles.title: YTHDF1 Promotes PCV2 Replication by Recognizing the M6A Modification at Site A508 of the Cap mRNA.
articles.abstract: Porcine circovirus type 2 (PCV2) is the smallest known mammalian virus and is distributed worldwide, causing substantial economic losses to the swine industry. N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant internal mRNA modification, has a pivotal role in the viral life cycle. The m6A reader protein YTHDF1 enhances the stability and translation of m6A-modified transcripts. Here, we show that YTHDF1 interacts with m6A-modified PCV2 Cap mRNA, thereby enhancing Cap mRNA stability and promoting PCV2 replication. This interaction and the consequent stabilization depend on the m6A-recognition capability of YTHDF1. Mechanistically, YTHDF1 recognizes the m6A-modified site (A508) on PCV2 Cap mRNA to enhance its stabilization. Accordingly, a rescued PCV2, PCV2A508T, exhibited attenuated replication compared with wild-type PCV2 (PCV2WT); notably, YTHDF1 failed to enhance the replication or stabilization of the PCV2A508T. In vivo, YTHDF1 deficiency reduced PCV2 viral loads and alleviated pathological lesions in the lungs, spleens, and kidneys of infected mice. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical role of m6A modification in PCV2 replication and suggest that targeting the YTHDF1-m6A axis may provide a novel therapeutic strategy against PCV2 infection.

articles.title: The Next Postcode Lottery in Type 1 Diabetes: Echoes of the Past and Future Direction.
Efficacy and Safety of Qiliqiangxin in Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction With and Without Diabetes: A Post Hoc Analysis of the QUEST Trial.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate the prognostic significance of diabetes and the efficacy and safety of Qiliqiangxin (QLQX) according to diabetes status in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) in the QUEST trial.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This post hoc analysis included patients with New York Heart Association Class II-IV and left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%, randomized to QLQX or placebo plus standard therapy. The primary outcome was first HF hospitalization or cardiovascular (CV) death; the key secondary outcome was total HF hospitalizations and CV death.

RESULTS: Among 3110 patients, 877 (28.2%) had diabetes. After multivariable adjustment, diabetes was associated with higher risks of the primary outcome (hazard ratio [HR] 1.18; 95% CI 1.01-1.39; p = 0.040) and key secondary outcome (rate ratio [RR] 1.22; 95% CI 1.03-1.45; p = 0.024). QLQX reduced the primary outcome in patients with diabetes (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.51-0.89; p = 0.006) and without diabetes (HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.70-0.97; p = 0.023), with no significant interaction by diabetes status (p for interaction = 0.355). Secondary outcomes showed similar findings. Effects on N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, estimated glomerular filtration rate and blood pressure were consistent across subgroups. QLQX was well tolerated, with no significant treatment-by-diabetes interaction for adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: In this post hoc analysis of the QUEST trial, diabetes was associated with worse clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF. QLQX reduced HF hospitalization or CV death in patients with and without diabetes, with no significant treatment-effect heterogeneity.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Unique Identifier: ChiCTR1900021929. http://www.chictr.org.cn.

articles.title: Association Between FLAIR Vascular Hyperintensities and Angiographic Collateral Status in Acute MCA Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The clinical significance of Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (FLAIR) vascular hyperintensities (FVHs) in acute ischemic stroke remains debated, particularly regarding their relationship with leptomeningeal collateral circulation. We aimed to assess the association between FVHs on baseline MRI and angiographic collateral status evaluated by digital subtraction angiography (DSA) in patients with middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusion.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including patients treated between 2010 to 2018 for an acute ischemic stroke due to isolated M1 MCA occlusion from two cohorts. All patients underwent baseline MRI with FLAIR sequences and pre-treatment DSA. FVHs were assessed using two approaches: a topographic score (FVH-ASPECTS) and a semi-quantitative score based on the number of axial FLAIR slices showing at least one FVH (FVH-slices). Collateral status was graded using the ASITN/SIR scale and dichotomized as poor (grades 0-2) or good (grades 3-4). Associations were evaluated using Spearman correlation, nonparametric tests, and logistic regression. Technical sensitivity analyses accounted for slice thickness and interslice spacing. Interreader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients.

RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were included. FVH-slices showed moderate-to-good interreader agreement (ICC = 0.77), whereas FVH-ASPECTS had lower reproducibility (ICC = 0.34). FVH-slices was weakly correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.27, P = .053) and was higher in patients with good collaterals (P = .021). In univariable logistic regression, each 1-point increase was associated with higher odds of good collateral status (OR = 1.30; 95% CI, 1.00-1.70), but this association was attenuated after accounting for acquisition parameters. FVH-ASPECTS correlated with the full ASITN/SIR scale (ρ = 0.30, P = .029) but was not significantly associated with dichotomized collateral status. Neither FVH score nor ASITN/SIR grade was associated with 3-month functional outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: FVH-slices was more reproducible than FVH-ASPECTS and showed a weak positive association with angiographic collateral status. However, attenuation after technical adjustment and the limited sample size indicate that these exploratory findings require prospective validation.

articles.title: Foveal Avascular Zone Alterations and Associated Biochemical Markers in Children With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate foveal avascular zone (FAZ) alterations among children with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) without diabetic retinopathy (DR) and associations between circulating biochemical markers and FAZ alterations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 50 children with T1DM without DR and 63 healthy controls for baseline analysis. FAZ area was measured using optical coherence tomography angiography, and longitudinal analyses were performed among participants with follow-up data. Baseline FAZ differences between groups were assessed. Among children with T1DM, multivariable linear regression evaluated associations between biochemical markers and baseline FAZ area and the percentage increase in FAZ area over 2 years. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed for markers associated with FAZ enlargement to assess their discriminatory ability for greater FAZ enlargement.

RESULTS: Compared with healthy controls, children with T1DM without DR exhibited larger baseline FAZ areas. During follow-up, FAZ area remained stable in healthy controls, whereas T1DM children showed FAZ enlargement at 1 and 2 years. Higher glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), blood glucose, aspartate aminotransferase and lactate dehydrogenase levels were associated with larger baseline FAZ areas. After multiple-comparison adjustment, only HbA1c remained significantly associated with baseline FAZ area. Higher baseline HbA1c level was also associated with a greater 2-year percentage increase in FAZ area. ROC analysis showed the potential discriminatory ability of HbA1c for greater FAZ enlargement.

CONCLUSIONS: Subclinical macular microvascular alterations may occur in children with T1DM before clinically detectable DR. Long-term glycaemic exposure may represent a key factor associated with early macular microvascular changes in T1DM children.

articles.title: Changes in Biological Age Acceleration and Risk of Incident Diabetes: Results From Three Large Cohort Studies.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the associations of baseline and longitudinal changes in biological age acceleration with incident diabetes in three large prospective cohorts.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multi-cohort study included 474 109 participants from the Kailuan and Dongfeng-Tongji cohorts in China and the UK Biobank. Biological age was estimated using PhenoAge and Klemera-Doubal Method (KDM) age, both derived from nine routinely measured clinical indicators. Biological age acceleration was defined as the residual from regressing biological age on chronological age within each cohort, separately at baseline and the first follow-up. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were applied to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the associations of baseline biological age acceleration and its longitudinal changes (persistent accelerated ageing, delayed accelerated ageing, recovery from accelerated ageing and stable non-accelerated ageing) with the risk of diabetes. Results from the three cohorts were pooled using meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with non-accelerated ageing, baseline accelerated ageing was associated with a higher risk of diabetes (PhenoAge: pooled HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.21-1.48; KDM age: pooled HR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.34-1.92). In analyses of longitudinal changes, compared with participants with persistent accelerated ageing, those with delayed or recovered accelerated ageing had 21%-34% lower risks of diabetes (pooled HR ranges: PhenoAge, 0.72-0.79; KDM age, 0.66-0.67). Participants who consistently maintained non-accelerated ageing had the lowest risk of diabetes (PhenoAge: pooled HR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.54-0.61; KDM age: pooled HR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.38-0.61).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that biological age acceleration and its changes are associated with diabetes risks.

Genome-Wide Association Study Identifies Novel Loci Exhibiting Additive Resistance to Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus in Soft Winter Wheat.
articles.abstract: In the Great Plains, wheat streak mosaic virus (WSMV) contributes to yearly yield losses, which has led to the development of resistant hard winter wheat varieties. However, resistance to WSMV in soft winter wheat (SWW) varieties, primarily grown in eastern North America, has not been well researched. We conducted a screening of 281 SWW commercial and experimental lines against WSMV infection in a controlled growth chamber environment. Plants were inoculated at 15-days post-planting and symptom phenotyping was conducted 14 and 28 days post-inoculation using a 0-4 phenotypic scale developed for this screening. Phenotypes obtained from the screening were used in a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify genomic regions influencing the phenotypic response of SWW to WSMV infection. The mean phenotypic value across genotypes was 1.0, while the highest phenotypic value was 2.1 and the lowest was 0. Two SWW genomic regions were identified as associated with WSMV resistance on chromosomes 2D and 7B. Soft winter wheat lines with one or both regions had a reduction in WSMV symptoms, indicating that both regions moderately reduced WSMV symptoms. When examined in tandem the effects of the QTLs were found to be additive. This study provides a critical first step in identifying WSMV resistance in SWW lines and a foundation for developing resistant varieties to better serve growers' needs in Eastern North America.

articles.title: Ileal duplication cyst presenting with right iliac fossa tenderness.
Patch Testing for Implanted Cardiac Device-Related Delayed Hypersensitivity Reactions: Practical Considerations.
articles.abstract: Hypersensitivity reactions to cardiac implantable electronic devices, including pacemakers, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and structural cardiac devices, are rare but clinically significant complications. Diagnosis can be challenging because these devices contain numerous potential allergens, clinical presentations are variable and may mimic infection, and standard testing approaches are limited. Potential allergens include metals and other device components, as well as other components, including topical cutaneous adhesives, suture material, anesthetics, and antibiotic envelopes. Pre-implantation testing is not routinely recommended; however, may be considered in certain cases. Post-implantation testing should be considered in patients with persistent cutaneous or systemic symptoms after excluding other potential causes, particularly infection. We summarize potential allergens associated with cardiac device implantation procedures, discuss indications and special considerations for patch testing, and provide a practical, device-specific approach to patch testing in this setting. Recognition of relevant exposures and accurate interpretation of patch test results may facilitate diagnosis and guide management in patients with suspected cardiac device hypersensitivity.

articles.title: Evaluation of Reticulocyte Channel on Sysmex XN-10 for Resolving Cold Agglutination in Samples With High Prevalence of Thalassemic Hemoglobinopathies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cold agglutinins interfere with automated complete blood count analysis by causing red cell aggregation and spurious erythrocyte indices. This study evaluated the Sysmex XN-10 reticulocyte channel for resolving cold agglutination and assessed the performance of delta RBC and delta MCHC in a population with a high prevalence of thalassemia and hemoglobinopathies (TH).

METHODS: Twenty healthy controls, 29 TH samples, and 126 consecutive specimens with MCHC > 38.5 g/dL were studied. Optical parameters obtained in the preincubation reticulocyte channel were compared with conventional impedance parameters after incubation at 37°C. Agreement, correlation, and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Optical and impedance parameters showed strong agreement in healthy and TH cohorts. Of 126 high-MCHC specimens, 122 showed cold agglutination on smear; 84 had quantifiable preincubation values, and 72 normalized after incubation and were included for quantitative comparison. Preincubation optical parameters showed strong concordance with postincubation impedance values. Twelve samples with persistent postwarming abnormalities appeared better resolved in the reticulocyte channel. Delta RBC % ((RBC-O - RBC-I)/RBC-I × 100) was highly sensitive for cold agglutination, with 100% sensitivity at a threshold of > 5%, while specificity decreased in TH-prevalent cohorts. Delta MCHC % ((cMCHC - MCHC)/MCHC × 100) showed excellent discriminatory performance, with an optimal cut-off of < -7.7% yielding 98.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

CONCLUSION: The Sysmex XN-10 reticulocyte channel provides a reliable approach for resolving cold agglutination-related interference in complete blood count analysis. In TH-prevalent settings, sequential use of delta RBC and delta MCHC potentially improves discrimination and facilitates more efficient release of reliable hematology results.

articles.title: Impact of artificial intelligence-driven risk prediction scores on decision-making in heart failure in the hospital: study protocol for a vignette study across nine international hospitals.
INTERACT: understanding inclusivity in oncology clinical trials using a data-driven approach - protocol for a retrospective observational study and service evaluation.
Sputum bacteria and antibiotic resistance in adults hospitalised with asthma: a 27-year longitudinal analysis.
Occurrence and associated factors of lupus nephritis, advanced chronic kidney disease, avascular necrosis and mortality in systemic lupus erythematosus in a contemporary Japanese SLE cohort.
Engineering live biotherapeutic products (eLBPs): modularization and systematic building strategies.
articles.abstract: The continued advancement of synthetic biology and related technologies has reinvigorated traditional probiotic therapies. Researchers can customize the bacterial chassis to construct eLBPs on demand. These can perform a variety of functions, including sensing and processing of disease signals, in situ production or targeted delivery of drugs, and long-term treatment of chronic diseases. The performance of these functions depends on the precise cooperation between the modules and the rational design of the genetic circuit. However, the mechanisms of some microbial-host interactions remain unclear, and modular design approaches are lacking. These problems have largely hindered the further development of eLBPs. Here, we review the current state of development of eLBPs and the problems encountered, followed by possible solutions and potential future research directions. The engineering components in eLBPs are categorized as: sensor module, signal processing module, delivery module, containment module, and colonization module. The modular construction strategy can facilitate the design of eLBPs and expedite their deployment in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. Finally, we describe the design process of eLBPs based on modularization strategies, discuss the differences between this approach and the traditional drug development process, and provide an outlook on the future development and potential problems associated with this technology.

articles.title: The impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 therapy on transfusion medicine: Possible implications for blood donors and recipients-A narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (RAs) are among the fastest adopted drugs today, with tens of millions of users expected within 5 years.
