Beyond established metabolic benefits, emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1 therapy modestly reduces haemoglobin and iron stores while lowering cardiovascular and other chronic disease burdens. This review explores potential implications for transfusion medicine, affecting both blood supply and demand.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review of peer-reviewed literature included a retrospective cohort study of 700 patients receiving GLP-1 RAs and an American Society of Hematology (ASH) clinical commentary, alongside market-projection data identified through targeted searches of GLP-1 pharmacology, haematological effects, donor eligibility and chronic disease outcomes. Claude Sonnet 5 was used solely for editorial refinement and data synthesis under human oversight.

RESULTS: GLP-1 therapy is associated with a small but statistically significant haemoglobin decline (0.2 g/dL), with approximately 1 in 12 treated patients developing anaemia and reduced ferritin in at-risk subgroups. Conversely, GLP-1 therapy reduces major adverse cardiovascular events, with preliminary evidence suggesting potential benefits in haematological malignancy progression. An estimated 25-40 million people globally may use GLP-1 therapy by 2029-2030, potentially influencing donor haemoglobin distributions and transfusion demand.

CONCLUSION: The scale of GLP-1 adoption warrants proactive attention from blood services. Recording GLP-1 use in donor questionnaires, monitoring donor haemoglobin trends and incorporating changing chronic disease burdens into demand forecasting may be beneficial. Prospective transfusion medicine-specific research is needed to quantify these effects.

articles.title: Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection Repair: Time to Train the Team.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Training in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair is traditionally acquired at consultant stage. Advanced aortic fellowships, such as that at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital (UK), allow safe training to occur at an earlier stage. This retrospective cohort study describes the structure and core competencies of this training model and reports comparative outcomes for trainee-led versus consultant-led ATAAD repair.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of all ATAAD cases repaired at Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital, over a 5-year contemporary period, between October 2018 and September 2023. The prespecified primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were in-hospital mortality, stroke, reexploration for bleeding, and length of stay. Perioperative care was regulated through Standard Operating Policies and custom and practice agreements within teams. In addition, we report the elective and urgent aortic surgery caseload over the same period for context.

RESULTS: A total of 128 cases of ATAAD repair were performed in this period by consultants (70) and by trainees (58). These procedures took place alongside 1,025 elective and urgent major aortic cases, of which 113 were trainee-led. There was appropriate case selection in ATAAD with bias in favor of the consultant group being populated with a higher proportion of patients in a preoperative renal failure state (6 vs. 0) and requiring total arch reconstruction with frozen elephant trunk (17 vs. 7).

CONCLUSION: Within this specialist high-volume aortic unit, structured fellowship training was associated with perioperative outcomes for trainee-led ATAAD repair that were comparable to consultant-led repair, despite trainees performing a less complex case mix. We conclude that, within such a unit, training in ATAAD is achievable in the context of (1) an elective aortic practice, (2) appropriate case selection, (3) standardized surgical techniques in ATAAD, and (4) standardized perioperative operating policies, underpinned by a supportive, invested training culture across all teams.

articles.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps in Ischemic Stroke: From Thrombus Architecture to Therapeutic Targeting.
articles.abstract: Background Despite major advances in reperfusion therapy, a substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke fail to achieve successful reperfusion or meaningful functional recovery. Increasing evidence suggests that thrombus composition plays a critical role in determining response to both thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), extracellular networks of DNA, histones, and neutrophil-derived proteins, have emerged as key mediators of immunothrombosis and contributors to treatment resistance. Review Summary NETs are consistently identified within thrombi retrieved during mechanical thrombectomy, where they localize predominantly to platelet- and von Willebrand factor-rich regions of the thrombus shell. Experimental and clinical evidence indicates that NETs contribute to fibrinolytic resistance through multiple complementary mechanisms, including reduced clot permeability, persistence of a plasmin-resistant chromatin scaffold, sequestration of fibrinolytic proteins, and accumulation of endogenous fibrinolysis inhibitors. Beyond their role in thrombolysis resistance, NETs influence thrombus architecture and mechanical properties, potentially contributing to thrombectomy complexity and reduced first-pass reperfusion. NET burden has been associated with stroke severity, poorer functional outcomes, and adverse reperfusion profiles. Emerging therapeutic strategies targeting NETs, particularly DNase I, have progressed from translational studies to early-phase clinical trials, providing the first evidence that NET-directed interventions may be feasible in acute ischemic stroke. Conclusions NETs represent a mechanistically important component of stroke thrombus biology and a promising therapeutic target. Growing translational and clinical evidence supports further evaluation of NET-targeted therapies as adjuncts to current reperfusion strategies. Future studies incorporating biomarker-guided patient selection and tissue-level reperfusion endpoints will be essential to determine their clinical utility.

articles.title: Heparin Versus Saline for Locking Central Venous Access Devices in Pediatric Oncology: Results of a Multicenter Survey by the German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term central venous access devices are essential for the treatment of children and adolescents with malignancies. As uniform evidence-based standards for their maintenance are lacking, practices vary among pediatric oncology centers within the German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology network. The aim of this survey was to assess current central venous access device maintenance practices within centers of the German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional survey, 76 German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology centers in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland were asked about central venous access device maintenance, locking solutions, flushing intervals and techniques, and surveillance of catheter-associated complications. Data were analyzed descriptively at the institutional level.

RESULTS: Forty-eight centers were included (63.2%). Heparin was used as a locking solution for Broviac/Hickman catheters in 56.3% and for ports in 52.1% of centers, whereas 0.9% saline was used in 41.7 and 43.8%, respectively. Broviac/Hickman catheters were predominantly flushed weekly (87.5%), while port flushing intervals varied. Push-pause flushing was used by 60.4% of centers. Almost all centers had a standard operating procedure (97.9%), but only 41.7% systematically monitored catheter-associated bloodstream infections and thrombosis.

DISCUSSION: Compared with the 2013 German Society for Pediatric Oncology and Hematology survey, in which approximately 90% of centers used heparin locking, heparin is now used considerably less frequently. Substantial interinstitutional heterogeneity persists.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the need for harmonized, evidence-based recommendations and standardized prospective surveillance of central venous access device-associated complications.

articles.title: The Rare Wrong Turn: Hybrid Management of Iatrogenic Vertebral Artery Injury During Internal Jugular Central Venous Catheter Placement.
articles.abstract: BackgroundCentral venous catheter (CVC) insertion into the internal jugular vein (IJV) is a routine procedure, yet it carries a small but significant risk of arterial injury. While accidental arterial puncture occurs in 3.0%-9.4% of cases, inadvertent arterial cannulation is rare. Iatrogenic vertebral artery (VA) injury is exceptionally rare due to its protected anatomical position in the neck, but it carries a high risk of stroke and is difficult to manage with manual compression.Case DescriptionAn 89-year-old female required emergent IJV CVC placement following a cardiac arrest attributed to profound hypovolaemia. Computed tomography angiography suggested subclavian artery cannulation, however dynamic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) revealed a more complex trajectory: the CVC had penetrated the IJV and the adjacent VA, terminating in the subclavian artery. Removal of the catheter resulted in an immediate active contrast extravasation on DSA.ManagementDue to haemodynamic instability and a lack of onsite neurointerventional services, a hybrid management strategy was employed. A covered stent was deployed in the subclavian artery to seal the VA origin, followed by manual compression under fluoroscopic guidance to control retrograde flow from the distal VA.ConclusionThis case highlights that profound hypovolaemia can increase the risk of "through-and-through" venous punctures, leading to rare arterial injuries. In resource-limited settings where neurointerventional services were unavailable, a combination of proximal stenting and prolonged manual compression achieved haemostasis in this specific clinical setting.

articles.title: Kidney Failure Risk Equation for Vascular Access Planning: A Practical Framework for Vascular Surgeons.
articles.abstract: The timing and selection of vascular access (VA) in patients with chronic kidney disease are key determinants of hemodialysis outcomes. Conventional referral strategies based solely on estimated glomerular filtration rate may lead to premature or delayed arteriovenous fistula creation, resulting in unnecessary procedures or initiation of dialysis with a catheter. The Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE), which incorporates demographic and biochemical variables, provides a more individualized prediction of kidney failure risk within 2- and 5-year intervals. This review summarizes global validation studies of the KFRE, examines proposed risk thresholds for timely VA referral, and outlines a practical algorithm for incorporating the KFRE into multidisciplinary VA planning. From a vascular surgeon's perspective, the KFRE may serve not only as a referral tool but also as a decision-support framework for reassessing the appropriateness and timing of access creation after nephrology referral. In particular, the KFRE-based risk estimates should be interpreted alongside patient-specific factors, including age, frailty, comorbidities, life expectancy, vascular anatomy, dialysis modality preference, and transplant plans. This review also discusses competing-risk considerations, current limitations, and future directions for integrating the KFRE into routine clinical workflows.

articles.title: Social Risks and Health-related Quality of Life in Women Who Have Experienced Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between social risk factors (housing instability and food insecurity) and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in a sample of women with a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional survey data on women aged 18 years and older from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (2014, 2015, and 2017) were analyzed. GDM was defined by self-reported diagnosis of diabetes only during pregnancy. Social risk factors were defined by self-reported experiences of housing instability and food insecurity within the previous year. Linear regression models were run to evaluate the association between social risks and HRQoL outcomes, controlling for sociodemographic variables and comorbidity confounders. Interaction terms between each social risk factor and race/ethnicity were tested for each outcome but were not significant; thus, the analyses were not stratified.

RESULTS: Among the total study sample (weighted N = 3,080,442) of adult women with a history of GDM, 36.6 and 44.0% reported experiences of food insecurity and housing instability, respectively. Among women with a history of GDM, housing instability, and food insecurity were associated with reduced self-rated general health status (- 0.19; 95% CI: - 0.38, - 0.004 and - 0.27; 95% CI: - 0.47, - 0.08, respectively) in models adjusted for sociodemographic variables and comorbidities.

CONCLUSION: Results indicate significant relationships between social risk factors and self-rated general health status. We found no relationship by race/ethnicity. These results underscore the need for continued interventions to address social risks to improve the health and well-being of women with complicated pregnancies.

KEY POINTS: · Social risks worsen health after GDM.. · Housing and food needs affect self-related health.. · Systems-level action needed to improve outcomes..

articles.title: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Therapy Delivery for Infants with Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: Factors Associated with Receipt, Timing, and Frequency.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objectives of this study are to characterize neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) therapy delivery among infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE); identify infant characteristics associated with feeding and developmental therapy receipt, timing, and frequency; and evaluate differences in therapy delivery between sites.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of infants with HIE treated with therapeutic hypothermia and admitted to two Level IV NICUs between 2017 and 2024. Multivariable regression models evaluated factors associated with therapy receipt, timing, and frequency after adjustment for infant clinical characteristics, sociodemographic factors, and site.

RESULTS: Among 379 infants, 367 (97%) received at least one NICU therapy session during hospitalization, including 348 (92%) who received feeding therapy and 320 (84%) who received developmental therapy. Developmental therapy receipt differed substantially between sites (98 vs. 70%). In multivariable analyses, site was associated with receipt (adjusted odds ratio: 0.06, p < 0.01), initiation (adjusted time ratio [aTR]: 1.22, p < 0.01), and frequency (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR]: 0.62, p < 0.01) of developmental therapy, even after adjustment for infant clinical and sociodemographic factors. Longer duration of ventilator support was associated with later initiation of both feeding (aTR: 1.03, p < 0.01) and developmental therapy (aTR: 1.02, p < 0.01). Higher birth gestational age was associated with greater developmental therapy frequency (aIRR: 1.08, p < 0.01), whereas longer duration of ventilator support was associated with lower feeding (aIRR: 0.99, p = 0.01) and developmental therapy frequency (aIRR: 0.99, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: NICU therapy was common among infants with HIE, but developmental therapy delivery varied substantially between sites independent of measured infant characteristics. These findings highlight opportunities to standardize therapy referral and delivery across NICUs.

KEY POINTS: · Most infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy received NICU therapy.. · Nearly all infants received feeding therapy.. · Developmental therapy varied between sites.. · Standardization of therapy referrals may improve care delivery..

articles.title: Oxysterol-Mediated Nuclear Receptor Signaling in Metabolic and Cardiometabolic Diseases: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Therapy.
articles.abstract: This review synthesizes current evidence on oxysterol-mediated nuclear receptor signaling in metabolic and cardiometabolic disorders, with particular emphasis on liver X receptors (LXRs), Farnesoid X receptor (FXR), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), and selected steroid hormone receptors. It examines the contribution of oxysterol dysregulation to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, while critically evaluating the limitations of proposed oxysterol biomarkers. Therapeutic strategies are discussed according to their principal mechanisms, distinguishing interventions that influence cholesterol and oxysterol metabolism from agents that act through downstream nuclear receptors or other metabolic pathways. These include experimental LXR and FXR modulators, PPAR-directed agents, and thyroid hormone receptor-β (THR-β) agonism with resmetirom, whose clinical effects are mediated predominantly through hepatic THR-β-dependent regulation of lipid metabolism. Overall, this analysis identifies downstream receptors and metabolic enzymes as more manageable pharmacological intervention targets while highlighting the mechanistic significance of oxysterol nuclear receptor interactions.

articles.title: Outcomes for Open, Endovascular, and Hybrid Treatment for Non-A Non-B Aortic Dissections: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes of open (conventional arch repair, frozen elephant trunk), endovascular based treatment, hybrid, and conservative management for non-A non-B aortic dissection.

DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE and Embase from inception to 9 September 2025, with a supplementary search for conservatively managed cohorts.

REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions of non-randomised observational studies, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO CRD42024534559). English language cohort studies and case series of ≥ 15 adult patients with non-A non-B dissection reporting predefined outcomes were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale). Proportions were pooled separately within each modality (random effects, logit transformation). No between modality comparison was made. Sensitivity analyses comprised leave one out, influence diagnostics, and a generalised linear mixed model. Certainty was rated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies comprising 1 062 patients (mean age 55 years, 82% men) were included; 1 019 contributed to the pooled estimates. Pooled in hospital mortality was 4.6% (95% CI 2.2 - 9.6) after endovascular based treatment, 5.5% (2.6 - 11.3) after frozen elephant trunk, 7.8% (4.2 - 14.3) after hybrid repair, and 11.1% (4.0 - 27.1) with conservative management, with widely overlapping confidence intervals. Stroke ranged from 3.9% after endovascular based treatment to 9.7% with conservative management. Over 12 - 60 months mean follow up, cumulative mortality after discharge ranged from 3.1% (frozen elephant trunk) to 15.0% (conservative management), with 33.4% crossover to intervention. Retrograde type A dissection followed only stent graft based strategies (endovascular based treatment 3.4%); endoleak affected 15.7% of endovascular based treatment and 13.4% of hybrid patients. Certainty was very low overall.

CONCLUSION: In this synthesis, in hospital mortality was below 10% after endovascular based treatment, frozen elephant trunk and hybrid repair, each with a distinct complication profile relevant to treatment selection. These single arm proportions derive from populations selected by anatomy and operative fitness and are of very low certainty, and do not support estimation of comparative treatment effects.

articles.title: Environmental Stress and Metabolic Reprogramming: Mechanistic Links to Endocrine and Metabolic Disease.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: The global burden of metabolic and endocrine disorders continues to rise, and conventional risk factors alone do not fully explain this trend. Increasing evidence implicates environmental stressors, including persistent organic pollutants, plasticizers, heavy metals, air pollution, and mycotoxins, in metabolic disease. This review examines metabolic reprogramming as a mechanistic link between environmental exposure and endocrine dysfunction. Environmental stressors perturb mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis, fatty-acid oxidation, lipogenesis, autophagy, and redox homeostasis, affecting pancreatic β-cells, hepatocytes, adipocytes, and steroidogenic tissues. Metabolic intermediates may couple these disturbances to epigenetic regulation, including histone acetylation, lactylation, and DNA methylation, thereby stabilizing maladaptive metabolic states. Cross-organ communication through adipose-liver-muscle, gut-brain, gut-kidney, and heart-immune axes may amplify local perturbations into systemic endocrine, cardiovascular, renal, reproductive, and metabolic dysfunction. We propose a two-phase model in which sub-lethal metabolic reprogramming precedes overt disease, with redox imbalance, metabolic-epigenetic coupling, and positive feedback loops driving progression. Emerging interventions targeting redox balance, mitochondrial function, metabolic pathways, and the microbiome are also evaluated, although exposure-specific clinical evidence remains limited. This framework positions metabolic reprogramming as a tractable mechanistic target and highlights priorities for mixture toxicology, metabolomics, stable-isotope tracing, single-cell approaches, gene-environment interactions, and early biomarker development.

articles.title: Gestational PET-NP exposure induces placental injury and fetal growth restriction with a PPARα-associated transcriptional response.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: The placental toxicity of polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastics (PET-NPs) during pregnancy remains poorly understood. Pregnant mice were orally exposed to 20-nm PET-NPs at 10 mg/kg/day from gestational day 3.5 to 17.5. PET-NP-associated fluorescence was detected in placental tissues, accompanied by placental injury, reduced fetal weight and crown-rump length, increased embryo mortality, and decreased fetal number. Placental RNA sequencing identified 1,532 differentially expressed genes. Enrichment analyses revealed suppression of proliferation-related transcriptional programs and positive enrichment of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signaling gene set. Network toxicology analysis also identified PPAR signaling and prioritized Ppara as a candidate for further investigation. PET-NP exposure increased placental expression of Ppara, Rxra, Acox1, Cd36, Acadm, and Pdk4. GW6471 treatment attenuated these transcriptional changes, alleviated placental injury, and improved fetal growth and embryo survival. Immunofluorescence staining further showed enhanced PPARα signals in CK7-positive trophoblast regions. In vitro, HTR8/SVneo trophoblasts internalized PET-NPs and subsequently exhibited impaired proliferation and migration, which were partially restored by GW6471. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the placental and developmental toxicity of gestational PET-NP exposure and support the potential involvement of a PPARα-associated response in the observed toxicity.

articles.title: Blood urea nitrogen and 30-day mortality in Sepsis with malignancy: A retrospective cohort study with point-of-care translational validation.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood urea nitrogen (BUN) reflects renal function, perfusion, and catabolic status, but its association with short-term mortality and point-of-care measurability in sepsis with malignancy remains unclear. We evaluated early ICU BUN in relation to 30-day mortality and assessed a portable BUN test strip.

METHODS: We analyzed 4189 adults with sepsis and malignancy from MIMIC-IV v2.2. Cox regression and nonlinear analyses assessed first-day ICU BUN and 30-day mortality. Separately, 165 clinical samples were measured using a paper-based photochemical BUN strip and Cobas 8000. Agreement was evaluated by Deming regression, Lin's concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), Bland-Altman analysis, and categorical agreement.

RESULTS: Thirty-day mortality was 31.6% (1323/4189). After full adjustment, each 10 mg/dL increase in BUN was associated with a 4% higher mortality risk. The association was nonlinear (P < 0.001), increasing below 45.03 mg/dL (HR per 10 mg/dL, 1.244; 95% CI, 1.147-1.350) and plateauing thereafter. The test strip showed strong agreement with Cobas 8000 (Deming regression: y = 0.991× - 0.103; r = 0.993), with a mean bias of -0.51 mg/dL and 95% limits of agreement of -7.57 to 6.55 mg/dL. Four-category agreement was 89.1% (weighted κ = 0.911). For BUN ≥40 mg/dL, sensitivity and specificity were 97.0% and 99.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Early ICU BUN was independently associated with 30-day mortality in sepsis with malignancy. The portable BUN test strip showed strong agreement with Cobas 8000 and reliable high-BUN classification, supporting rapid point-of-care measurement.

articles.title: Drp1-mediated Mitochondrial Fission in the Wasp Sting-induced Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.journal: Toxicon : official journal of the International Society on Toxinology
articles.abstract: The effect and mechanism of dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1) during acute kidney injury (AKI) triggered by wasp stings were investigated using an established animal model. Wasp sting increased the p-Drp1S616 and decreased p-Drp1S637 in the kidney. Drp1 inhibition improved mitochondrial fission, mitochondrial dysfunction, stimulator of interferon genes expression, programmed cell death (apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis), and renal dysfunction. Our findings revealed the important role of Drp1-mediated mitochondrial fission in wasp sting-induced AKI.

articles.title: An optimised cryopreservation method for Mycoplasma genitalium.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma genitalium is extremely fastidious, compromising viability during storage (cryopreservation). We show that supplementing culture media with 10% sucrose provides superior cryoprotection during storage at -80 °C and in liquid nitrogen. This simple optimisation provides a foundation for standardised biobanking and will support future research into this clinically important pathogen.

articles.title: A simplified nitrocellulose disc-based colloidal gold immunoassay for preliminary detection of Mycoplasma synoviae antibodies.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma synoviae is an important poultry pathogen routinely diagnosed using ELISA. To overcome some limitations, we developed a nitrocellulose (NC) membrane disc-based immunoassay for detecting antibodies against M. synoviae. Colloidal gold-conjugated antigen was used as the signaling probe. In positive sera, target antibodies bind to the NC disc, and the gold-antigen probe is captured. After removing the NC discs, a decrease in OD530 was observed. The assay was evaluated using chicken, immunized rabbit, and pre-immunized rabbit sera, and different serum diluents were compared. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility of assay for detecting antibodies against M. synoviae.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness and safety of appropriately reduced-dose DOAC compared with standard-dose DOAC in reducing combined coronary and cerebral events among atrial fibrillation or flutter patients with non-recent percutaneous coronary intervention: a propensity-matched real-world cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal long-term antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL) after remote percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) requires balancing thromboembolic and bleeding risks. Comparative outcomes of appropriately reduced-dose versus standard-dose direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To compare ischemic and bleeding outcomes between appropriately reduced-dose and standard-dose DOAC therapy in patients with AF/AFL and non-recent PCI (>12 months).

METHODS: Using the TriNetX network, we performed a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study of adults with AF/AFL, prior PCI >12 months, and DOAC therapy. Patients with indications requiring warfarin were excluded. Patients receiving reduced-dose DOAC met guideline-recommended dose reduction criteria based on age, body weight, serum creatinine and creatinine clearance specified in pivotal DOAC studies. They were matched 1:1 to standard-dose DOAC recipients. Co-primary outcomes were net clinical outcomes (any ischemic or bleeding event), composite ischemic events (myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or systemic embolism), and composite bleeding events (gastrointestinal bleeding or nontraumatic intracranial hemorrhage).

RESULTS: After matching, 3276 patients (1638/group) were included. Reduced-dose DOAC was associated with similar risks of net clinical outcome (HR 1.011, 95% CI 0.772-1.324; p = 0.156), composite ischemic events (HR 0.970, 95% CI 0.728-1.293; p = 0.415), composite bleeding events (HR 1.146, 95% CI 0.888-1.479; p = 0.254), and all individual ischemic and bleeding endpoints (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AF/AFL and remote PCI, appropriately reduced-dose DOAC demonstrated effectiveness and safety comparable to standard-dose DOAC, supporting guideline-directed dose reduction in eligible patients.

articles.title: Head-to-head comparison of multimodal models incorporating clinical, imaging, and epicardial adipose tissue radiomics for predicting the 3-year MACEs in patients with stable angina.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with stable angina pectoris (SAP), the prognostic value of a multimodal model combining conventional coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) parameters and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) radiomics for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) has not been systematically compared.

METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 153 patients with SAP who underwent CCTA. The cohort was randomly split into training (n = 107) and test (n = 46) sets. The composite MACE endpoints included cardiac death, myocardial infarction, hospitalization for acute heart failure, and revascularization (none occurred). Clinical and imaging features were selected using univariate/multivariate logistic regression models, and EAT radiomic features were reduced via Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Logistic regression with L2 regularization was used to construct five models: clinical, imaging, radiomics, clinical-imaging, and full (clinical-imaging-radiomics) models. Performance was assessed by calculating the area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: The clinical-imaging model achieved a test AUC of 0.897 (95% CI 0.800-0.995), outperforming the clinical (0.812, 0.677-0.948) and radiomics-only (0.836, 0.722-0.950) models. The full model had a test AUC of 0.895 (0.798-0.993), not significantly different (P = 0.265). All models showed good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow, all P > 0.05). Decision curve analysis showed net benefit across risk thresholds 0.1-0.8, with the clinical-imaging model being the most practical.

CONCLUSIONS: A routine clinical-imaging model provided excellent 3-year MACE prediction (test AUC 0.897), with no incremental benefit from EAT radiomics. The clinical-imaging model is simple, low-cost, and ready for integration into routine CCTA-based risk stratification.

articles.title: Imported Melioidosis in Japan: Clinical Spectrum, Diagnostic Delays, Misidentification, and Laboratory Biosafety Risks.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Melioidosis, caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, is potentially fatal but rare in Japan. In non-endemic areas, detection and management are complicated by under-recognition, heterogeneous clinical presentation, delayed diagnosis, and misidentification.

METHODS: We reviewed patients diagnosed with melioidosis at Saitama Medical Center, Saitama Medical University, from 2017 to 2025 and searched PubMed and Ichushi-Web for cases reported in Japan from 1990 to 2025. We extracted epidemiological, clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data from all included cases.

RESULTS: A total of 23 cases were included in the overall analysis, comprising 21 cases identified through the literature review and two institutional cases. All patients were male, with reported ages ranging from the 30s to 75 years, and diabetes mellitus was the predominant comorbidity. Clinical presentations ranged from acute disease to prolonged or relapsing courses and included pneumonia, abscesses, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, infectious aneurysm, and lymphadenitis. Specific environmental exposures were often undocumented. The interval from symptom onset to microbiological diagnosis ranged from two days to approximately 22 months, and effective antimicrobial therapy was substantially delayed in some cases. Four patients experienced relapse, generally after insufficient treatment or inadequate eradication therapy. Misidentification or incomplete species-level identification occurred in five cases, particularly with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest under-recognition of melioidosis in Japan, substantial diagnostic errors, and a risk of unrecognized laboratory exposure. Detailed travel and exposure histories, prompt effective therapy, adequate eradication therapy, careful interpretation of microbiological results, and clinician-laboratory communication are essential.

articles.title: Salmonella enterica Calvarial Osteomyelitis With Pachymeningeal Involvement During Everolimus Therapy: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Everolimus is used for advanced malignancies and after solid organ transplantation. Infection is a recognized adverse effect. Salmonella osteomyelitis of the calvarium is rare. We report calvarial osteomyelitis with adjacent pachymeningeal involvement in a patient receiving long-term everolimus for metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 57-year-old man developed high fever and watery diarrhea after two years of everolimus therapy. A tender swelling appeared over the scalp vertex two to three weeks after the diarrhea began and enlarged over the next several days. He had generalized tonic-clonic seizures shortly before readmission. Salmonella enterica was isolated from two sets of peripheral blood cultures and from the drained abscess; serotyping was not performed. Magnetic resonance imaging showed acute calvarial osteomyelitis with an intraosseous collection, a subgaleal abscess and enhancement of the adjacent dura. Everolimus was withheld. The patient underwent drainage and surgical debridement of the infected bone and adjacent dura and received intravenous ceftriaxone for 21 days. Follow-up imaging at three months showed resolution of the abscess and dural enhancement. Everolimus was restarted, and there was no relapse during six months of follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Calvarial osteomyelitis should be considered when focal scalp swelling follows a febrile diarrheal illness in a patient receiving everolimus. A normal absolute lymphocyte count and the absence of corticosteroid treatment do not exclude a serious bacterial infection during prolonged mTOR inhibition. The case does not show that everolimus caused the infection, and the short antibiotic course should not be generalized.

articles.title: Advancing the field of TAVR: expanding indications and emerging technologies.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) was first developed for patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) at prohibitive risk for surgery. Over the past two decades, the continuous evolution in device technologies, procedural techniques and operator experience, has dramatically improved the safety and efficacy of TAVR, fuelling its expansion to newer patient cohorts. Current guideline recommendations now advocate for TAVR in younger, low surgical-risk patients. Accumulating evidence highlighting the impact of adverse cardiac remodelling and cardiac fibrosis in patients with severe AS, has prompted earlier treatment in patients with asymptomatic severe or moderate aortic stenosis. As more patients are treated earlier and at a younger age, the goals of TAVR now shift beyond the acute procedural result, towards ensuring the implanted prosthesis is optimized for longer-term valve performance and clinical outcomes. Procedural techniques to optimize stent frame expansion together with novel stent frame and leaflet design technologies are being developed to optimize long-term valve durability. Despite this, the need for re-interventions or redo-TAVR procedures is expected to increase. The challenges faced in planning and executing these complex procedures is being met with developments in pre-procedural imaging and simulation technologies, together with the development of leaflet modification techniques, designed to overcome coronary challenges. Further development of dedicated devices for cerebral embolic protection, calcium modification for transfemoral access and treatment of severe pure native aortic regurgitation, also continue to expand the applicability for TAVR. In this review, we summarise the evidence in these contemporary patient populations, as well as the procedural techniques and technologies that continue to advance the frontiers of TAVR.

articles.title: Revisiting calcium plaque modification in contemporary times: Drill, shock, cut or none of the above?
articles.abstract: Coronary artery calcification remains a major challenge in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), impairing lesion crossability and device delivery, increasing procedural complications, and predisposing to stent underexpansion, a key determinant of in-stent restenosis, stent thrombosis, and target-lesion failure. Because angiography detects only about half of coronary calcium, intravascular imaging has become central to identifying lesions that require advanced preparation and to confirming adequate modification before stent implantation. The contemporary toolbox includes devices with fundamentally different mechanisms of action: non-compliant, cutting, scoring, and super-high-pressure balloons; intravascular lithotripsy, with several novel platforms now emerging; rotational and orbital atherectomy; and excimer laser coronary atherectomy. Recent randomized trials have largely shown comparable imaging and procedural outcomes across strategies, and no device has demonstrated superiority for clinical endpoints. This review summarizes the mechanisms, technical considerations, indications, limitations, and comparative evidence for each technology. We propose a practical, imaging-guided algorithm, integrating randomized evidence and expert opinion, built on four questions: Can the lesion be crossed? What are the calcium severity and phenotype? Is the lesion adequately prepared for stenting? Is the stent adequately expanded? Device selection should be individualized according to calcium phenotype, patient and lesion characteristics, operator expertise, and cost, with non-compliant balloons remaining the cornerstone of initial lesion preparation. Ultimately, the goal is not maximal calcium modification but adequate lesion preparation and optimal stent expansion, with minimal procedural risk and cost.

articles.title: The predictive value of baseline retinal FAZ area and FAZ roundness index, measured by OCTA, on the vision improvement after 6 months anti-VEGF therapy for neovascular AMD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To preliminarily investigate the predictive value of foveal avascular zone (FAZ) morphological parameters measured by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) for visual prognosis at 6 months after anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) treatment in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

METHODS: This single-center, prospective cohort study enrolled 98 treatment-naïve patients with monocular nAMD. Baseline OCTA was performed to measure the FAZ area and circularity index, and patients were followed for 6 months. The primary outcome was the change in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) from baseline (ΔBCVA). Univariate and multivariate linear regression were used to construct a prediction model, with internal validation performed using Bootstrap and a nomogram.

RESULTS: The multivariate linear regression model was statistically significant (P < 0.001, adjusted R² = 0.305). After adjusting for age, baseline BCVA, and number of injections, older age (P < 0.001), larger FAZ area (P = 0.006), and lower FAZ circularity index (P = 0.027) were independent risk factors for lower ΔBCVA. Sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Bootstrap internal validation showed an optimism-corrected R² of 0.264, with a mean absolute calibrated error of 1.336. Among secondary outcomes, the decrease in central retinal thickness (CRT) change (ΔCRT) was significantly greater in good responders than in poor responders (P = 0.003), while no significant between-group differences were found in intraretinal fluid (IRF) resolution or ellipsoid zone (EZ) integrity (both P > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: A larger baseline FAZ area and a lower circularity index were independently associated with a poorer visual prognosis at 6 months after anti-VEGF treatment in patients with nAMD. The nomogram based on FAZ morphological parameters demonstrated some predictive potential in internal validation; however, external validation is warranted.

articles.title: A randomized controlled trial of rotational thromboelastometry-guided blood component transfusion for difficult-to-treat variceal bleeding in ACLF.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Difficult-to-treat acute variceal bleeding (AVB) in acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) may require substantial red blood cell transfusions and coagulation-directed blood components (CDBCs), including fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, and platelets, thereby predisposing to transfusion-related adverse events (TAEs). We assessed rebleeding, mortality, and CDBC requirements with rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM)-guided versus standard coagulation test (SCT)-guided transfusion strategies.

METHODS: In this single-centre, randomised controlled trial, patients with ACLF and difficult-to-treat AVB were assigned (1:1) to ROTEM-guided or SCT-guided CDBC transfusion. The primary endpoint was first rebleeding by Day 42. Other endpoints included CDBC requirements, TAEs, and survival.

RESULTS: Of 1,341 patients screened between November 2021 and January 2026, 766 had well-controlled bleeding and 313 were ineligible; 262 were randomised (ROTEM, n=132; SCT, n=130). Mean age was 45.1±11.6 years, MELD-Na 24.2±9.7, 64.5% had alcohol-associated ACLF, and 73% presented with shock. Bleeding sources were esophageal varices (85.9%) and gastric varices (14.1%); 113 patients had multiple bleeding sites, 112 had active spurting, and 37 had failure of endoscopic bleeding control, with 17 TIPS and 20 Danis-Ella stents insertions. First rebleeding by Day-42 occurred in 12.9% with ROTEM versus 13.9% with SCT (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.0 percentage points [pp]; 95% CI: -9.2 to 7.3). All-cause mortality through the end of study was 31.1% versus 38.5%, respectively (ARD, -7.4 pp; 95% CI: -18.6 to 4.1). CDBCs were not required in 75.8% versus 52.3% (ARD, +23.5 pp; 95% CI:11.9 to 34.2). TAEs occurred in 6.8% versus 14.6% (ARD, -7.8 pp; 95% CI:-15.6 to -0.2).

CONCLUSIONS: ROTEM guidance reduced coagulation-directed blood component administration and TAEs compared with SCTs without compromising rebleeding or survival, supporting a restrictive approach in ACLF with difficult-to-treat AVB.

(GOODHEART-ACLF TRIAL) REGISTRATION: NCT05124041.

articles.title: Molecular Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Influenza in Hospitalized Adults with Pulmonary Conditions in North India: A Prospective Single-Centre Study.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus and influenza cause respiratory illness among adults with pulmonary conditions, but Indian data remains limited. We enrolled 110 hospitalized adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, or acute respiratory distress syndrome from July 2024 to June 2025. Multiplex real-time RT-PCR detected RSV or influenza in 22 (20.0%) patients: RSV 6 (27.3%), Influenza B 9 (40.9%), A(H3N2) 4 (18.2%), and A(H1N1)pdm09 3 (13.6%). Eleven of 22 detected infections (50.0%) occurred during January-March 2025. Among virus-positive patients, ICU admission, invasive mechanical ventilation, and mortality occurred in 81.8%, 63.6%, and 22.7%, respectively.

articles.title: Developing lifelong care and training systems for adult congenital heart disease in Japan.
articles.abstract: The increasing number of patients with adult congenital heart disease (ACHD) has created a need for healthcare systems that provide continuous care across the lifespan. Adults with repaired complex lesions require assessment of residual abnormalities, late complications, and the consequences of historical surgical techniques, while aging introduces acquired cardiovascular disease and other comorbidities. In Japan, these changing needs have encouraged the development of ACHD specialist training and regional clinical networks. This narrative review examines the evolution of Japanese care and training systems, with particular emphasis on the participation of adult cardiologists, collaboration with pediatric cardiologists and congenital cardiac surgeons, and multidisciplinary support. A sustainable model connects comprehensive specialist centers with affiliated institutions, local cardiology services, and primary care, with responsibilities determined by underlying heart conditions, physiological status, and anticipated treatment needs. Transition should prepare patients for self-management and establish continuity with the receiving adult service. Specialist education must combine congenital anatomy and surgical history with the management of adult cardiovascular and extracardiac disorders. Dedicated nurses, echocardiographers, hepatologists, obstetricians, and other professionals are essential to this approach. Recent Japanese initiatives include an official ACHD specialist certification system and collaboration among societies to address Fontan-associated liver disease. Remaining priorities include reliable epidemiological surveillance, equitable access, protected training opportunities, and reimbursement that supports coordination and multidisciplinary care. Japan's experience illustrates how service development and workforce education can be integrated to support lifelong care, although the effects of these initiatives on continuity, clinical outcomes, and patient burden require further evaluation.

articles.title: Efficacy Comparison of Acupuncture, Electroacupuncture and Transcutaneous Acupoint Electrical Stimulation as Adjunctive Interventions for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Network Meta‑Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acupuncture, electroacupuncture and transcutaneous acupoint electrical stimulation (Acu‑TENS) are frequently utilized as adjuvant interventions for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Although multiple randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have investigated the clinical benefits of acupoint‑stimulation therapies, comprehensive quantitative head‑to‑head comparisons of their efficacy and safety are scarce. This network meta‑analysis (NMA) sought to systematically compare clinical outcomes of the three acupoint‑stimulation modalities as add‑on interventions to usual care among patients with COPD.

METHODS: We performed this network meta‑analysis following PRISMA‑NMA reporting guidelines. Comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed and Cochrane Library from database inception to 20 September 2026. Eligible RCTs investigating acupuncture, electroacupuncture or Acu‑TENS for COPD were included. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction; Cohen's κ‑statistic was calculated to evaluate inter‑rater agreement for study eligibility and phase classification. Risk‑of‑bias assessment was conducted using the RoB 2 tool for randomized trials. Primary outcomes covered pulmonary function indicators, and secondary outcomes included exercise tolerance, symptom scales, inflammatory biomarkers and safety indicators. All analyses were performed under the consistency assumption for star‑shaped evidence networks without closed loops, where formal incoherence assessment was not feasible. All comparative estimates between active acupoint‑stimulation interventions were derived exclusively from indirect comparisons, which rely heavily on the transitivity assumption. Leave‑one‑out sensitivity analysis was implemented to test the robustness of treatment rankings derived from the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Post‑hoc exploratory subgroup analyses stratified by COPD disease phase and intervention duration were conducted. SUCRA values represent relative ranking probability and do not inherently denote clinically meaningful superiority. Confidence in evidence was appraised using the CINeMA framework. Comparison‑adjusted funnel plots were generated for outcomes with sufficient available data.

RESULTS: A total of 40 RCTs involving 2591 COPD participants and 14 clinical endpoints were included. All evidence networks were star‑shaped without closed loops; comparisons between different active acupoint‑stimulation modalities relied entirely on indirect evidence under an untested consistency assumption. For pulmonary function, relative to usual care (UC), Acu‑TENS combined with usual care (TEAS_UC) showed a statistically significant improvement in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁) (WMD 0.41L, 95%CI 0.06‑0.76L), and acupuncture combined with usual care (ACU_UC) also statistically significant improved FEV₁ (WMD 0.31L, 95%CI 0.18‑0.44L). For exercise tolerance, ACU_UC produced a statistically significant increase in 6‑minute‑walk distance (6MWD) versus UC (WMD 73.62m, 95%CI 42.26‑104.98m). For respiratory symptoms, TEAS_UC yielded a statistically significant reduction in COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score (WMD -6.28, 95%CI -9.47 to -3.09) compared with UC. SUCRA‑based relative probability rankings suggested differential performance across endpoints, yet several rankings shifted after excluding individual studies, indicating limited stability. Most pairwise comparisons yielded low or very‑low confidence evidence according to CINeMA assessments. Safety data were sparse across included trials, with no documented serious adverse events or adverse‑event‑related treatment withdrawals.

CONCLUSIONS: Three acupoint‑stimulation therapies as add‑on to usual care exhibited variable patterns of benefit across COPD‑related endpoints. TEAS_UC showed favourable pooled estimates for pulmonary‑function indices, dyspnoea‑related outcomes, and inflammatory biomarkers including interleukin‑6 and tumour necrosis factor‑α. ACU_UC appeared promising for exercise tolerance, forced vital capacity, health‑related quality‑of‑life, and safety outcomes. Electroacupuncture combined with usual care (EA_UC) yielded suggestive benefits for overall respiratory‑symptom‑scale score. These findings originate primarily from indirect comparisons within star‑shaped networks, and are constrained by low‑to‑very‑low evidence certainty, unstable treatment rankings, incomplete safety reporting, and moderate‑to‑high risk of violations to the transitivity assumption. SUCRA‑derived relative rankings should be interpreted cautiously and cannot establish definitive clinical superiority for any individual intervention. Further high‑quality multicentre randomised controlled trials are needed to validate the present results.

articles.title: Research Advances in Diabetic Keratopathy.
articles.abstract: We systematically synthesize recent advances (primarily January, 2020, to June, 2026, with additional references from other years as appropriate) in the pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic techniques, and treatment strategies for diabetic keratopathy. Emphasizing the importance of early identification and targeted intervention, we propose a novel systematic framework integrating the "mechanism-phenotype-therapy" continuum. Diabetes mellitus damages corneal nerves, endothelial cells, and epithelium through multiple complex mechanisms, leading to corneal hypoesthesia, delayed epithelial healing, and reduced transparency. Advances in diagnostic technologies, particularly in vivo confocal microscopy, have enabled quantitative assessment of corneal nerve morphology, establishing it as a sensitive biomarker for diabetic peripheral neuropathy. Current therapeutic approaches, however, remain largely limited to symptomatic management, despite the regulatory approval of mechanism-based therapies such as cenegermin (EMA 2017; FDA 2018) for neurotrophic keratitis. Emerging strategies targeting neuroprotection, immunomodulation, metabolic pathways, and regenerative medicine show considerable promise. We critically appraise the evidence base, identifying consensus, controversies, and knowledge gaps that require future investigation. Therefore, diabetic keratopathy management requires a multifaceted approach encompassing early diagnosis, mechanistic elucidation, and personalized treatments. Future research should focus on deciphering underlying molecular pathways, particularly neuro-immune crosstalk, and translating these findings into precise diagnostic tools and effective multi-targeted therapies to improve corneal health in diabetic patients.

articles.title: Shared Decision-Making in Elective Spine Surgery: Surveying Discordance between Patients and Surgeons.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: In elective spine surgery, clinical scenarios frequently arise where decisions about operative management rely on surgeon judgment and patient preferences, particularly when clinical evidence is equivocal.

PURPOSE: We aimed to investigate how surgeons and patients prioritize risk-benefit assessments, guideline adherence, and patient autonomy when deciding whether to proceed with surgery in ambiguous cases.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional, vignette-based survey study.

PATIENT SAMPLE: 41 adult patients evaluated for degenerative spine conditions at a tertiary academic spine clinic, and 34 practicing spine surgeons recruited from institutional and national spine surgery organizations.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Self-report measures: Using a five-point Likert scale, respondents rated their willingness to proceed with surgery, perceived surgical risks and potential benefits, reliance on clinical practice guidelines, and the importance assigned to patient preferences/autonomy.

METHODS: Five vignettes representing common ambiguous clinical dilemmas in elective spine surgery were developed and administered via a REDCap survey. Descriptive statistics, nonparametric group comparisons (Wilcoxon rank-sum tests), and mixed-effects linear regression models were used to analyze and compare response distributions between the two cohorts.

RESULTS: Overall willingness to proceed with surgery did not significantly differ between surgeons and patients (β = -0.008, p = 0.95). However, surgeons gave significantly higher ratings to operative risks (β=0.49, 95% CI=[0.27,0.71], p<0.001) and benefits (β=0.25 [0.03,0.48], p=0.029). Conversely, surgeons placed significantly lower importance on patient autonomy (β=-1.03 [-1.24,-0.83], p<0.001) and clinical guideline adherence (β=-1.00 [-1.21,-0.78], p<0.001) compared to patients. Exploratory analyses indicated that spine surgeons at academic hospitals or who are earlier in their careers rated clinical guidelines higher than their peers, while surgeons with higher surgical volumes rated patient autonomy lower (p<0.05). Patients with a history of spine surgery rated anticipated benefits lower and clinical guidelines higher than patients without prior spine surgery (p<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In ambiguous elective spine surgery scenarios, patients and surgeons differed in their evaluations of risks, benefits, patient preferences, and clinical guidelines. Recognizing these distinctions is a critical step toward improving clinical communication to develop a more ethically coherent shared decision-making framework for elective spine surgery.

articles.title: Social Determinants of Health and Short- and Long-Term Outcomes After Anterior and Lateral Lumbar Interbody Fusion.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Social determinants of health (SDoH) independently predict worse outcomes after lumbar fusion, but existing evidence derives almost entirely from posterior or mixed-approach cohorts and rarely accounts for the surgical construct. Anterior and lateral lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF, LLIF, OLIF), with their distinct fusion biology and morbidity profiles, have not been isolated.

PURPOSE: To examine the association between SDoH burden and short- and long-term anterior and lateral lumbar interbody fusion outcomes while holding the fusion construct constant.

STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network, a federated platform aggregating de-identified electronic health record data from healthcare organizations in the United States (TriNetX US Collaborative Network; data accessed September 27, 2026).

PATIENT SAMPLE: Adults undergoing anterior and lateral lumbar interbody fusion (CPT 22558/22585), divided by the presence (All-SDoH) or absence (No-SDoH) of coded Z55-Z65 diagnoses. Cohorts were matched 1:1 on demographics, comorbidities, behavioral-health covariates, and the specific surgical construct. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to L5-S1 procedures (the level least accessible to lateral transpsoas approaches) to model a strictly anterior lumbar interbody fusion cohort and, for pseudarthrosis, to only patients with postoperative lumbar CT or MRI to add as control for healthcare utilization.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Physiologic and functional measures, including emergency department (ED) visit, readmission, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, surgical site infection, and sepsis at 3 months; and ED visit, readmission, mortality, pseudarthrosis (primary outcome), hardware-related complication (diagnosis code), and revision surgery (procedure code) at 1 and 2 years.

METHODS: Short- (3-month) and long-term (1- and 2-year) outcomes were compared between propensity matched cohorts using odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals, with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction across all outcome-timepoint comparisons.

RESULTS: Matching yielded 854 pairs at 3 months, 823 at 1 year, and 739 at 2 years, with all covariates well balanced (standardized mean differences <0.1). At 3 months, only ED utilization differed (12.9% vs. 9.3%; OR 1.45; p=0.017), whereas perioperative medical complications did not. ED utilization remained elevated at 1 and 2 years, and readmission was elevated at 2 years. Two-year pseudarthrosis was higher in the All-SDoH cohort (15.4% vs. 9.3%; OR 1.77; p<0.001; FDR-adjusted p=0.003), as was revision surgery (7.0% vs. 4.1%; OR 1.79; p=0.012), whereas coded hardware complication was only marginally higher (7.8% vs. 5.3%; OR 1.53; p=0.046). The pseudarthrosis association persisted among patients with postoperative lumbar CT or MRI (2-year 14.2% vs. 9.2%; OR 1.63; p=0.028) and was directionally consistent in an L5-S1-only cohort (411 pairs; 13.4% vs. 9.0%; OR 1.56; p=0.046). Mortality did not differ.

CONCLUSIONS: Among propensity-matched anterior and lateral lumbar interbody fusion patients with comparable constructs, documented high SDoH burden was associated with greater ED utilization, readmission, pseudarthrosis, and revision surgery, without differences in perioperative morbidity or mortality. These associations persisted in L5-S1 and imaging-restricted sensitivity analyses, suggesting that the relationship between social disadvantage and fusion outcomes reported in posterior cohorts may extend to anterior and lateral interbody fusion. Whether addressing social needs improves outcomes requires prospective study.

articles.title: Response to the Letter on "Discharge Albuminuria in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Interpretation".
Dinitroaniline Herbicides Function as Novel Inhibitors of Human and Rodent 11β-Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase 2.
articles.abstract: The widespread use of herbicides in the agriculture raises significant concerns regarding their endocrine-disrupting effects. This study investigated the inhibitory potential of 19 herbicides (in 9 subclasses) against 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 2 (11β-HSD2) in human and rat orthologs. Screening revealed that herbicides in the dinitroaniline subclass exhibited marked inhibitory activity, among them, oryzalin was the strongest inhibitor (IC50 = 39.67 ± 0.93 μM for human and 38.52 ± 0.36 μM for rat), followed by prodiamine, profluraline, ethalfluralin, benfluralin and isopropalin. Surface Plasmon Resonance analysis confirmed direct binding of oryzalin and isopropalin to human 11β-HSD2 (KD = 48.6 μM and 77.3 μM, respectively) and demonstrated attenuation of NAD+ binding. Enzyme kinetics established a mixed/noncompetitive inhibition mechanism for these dinitroaniline herbicides. In primary human placental cell and BeWo cell models, these compounds significantly suppressed cortisol metabolism at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR/3D-QSAR) analyses identified molecular hydrogen bond and topological polar surface area as critical determinants of potency. Molecular docking corroborated these findings, revealing stable binding of the inhibitors within the NAD+-binding pocket. ADMET prediction provided insights into their metabolic stability and toxicokinetic properties. Network toxicology analysis points to glucocorticoid metabolism inhibition with apparent mineralocorticoid excess. This provides compelling evidence that dinitroaniline-class herbicides are direct inhibitors of 11β-HSD2, identifying a novel molecular mechanism by which these chemicals may disrupt glucocorticoid signaling and potentially impact fetal programming and hypertension.

articles.title: β-Blocker Use and Descending Thoracic Aortic Remodeling after Extensive Repair for Type A Aortic Dissection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Descending thoracic aorta (DTA) remodeling is a major determinant of late outcomes after extensive aortic arch repair for type A aortic dissection. This study evaluated the association between postoperative β-blocker use and long-term DTA remodeling after extensive repair.

METHODS: From 2010 to 2019, 1,147 patients with type A aortic dissection who underwent extensive aortic arch repair were categorized into β-blocker (n=777) and non-β-blocker (n=370) groups. The main outcomes were overall survival, DTA dilation, and false lumen thrombosis. The additional outcome was DTA reintervention or rupture.

RESULTS: The median follow-up was 64.0 months. β-Blocker use was not significantly associated with all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.50-1.26; P=0.32). β-Blocker use was associated with a slower increase in the DTA diameter at the diaphragmatic (β±standard error, -0.47±0.18; P=0.012) and celiac (β±standard error, -0.35±0.168; P=0.038) levels. At the pulmonary artery bifurcation level, a greater reduction in the aortic diameter was observed in the β-blocker group, although the difference was not significant (β±standard error, -0.242±0.123; P=0.051). β-Blocker use was associated with higher rates of complete false lumen thrombosis in stent-covered (hazard ratio, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.06-1.39; P=0.005) and stent-uncovered (hazard ratio, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.22-1.83; P<0.001) DTA segments. The cumulative incidence of DTA reintervention or rupture did not differ significantly between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.47-1.22; P=0.25).

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational study, postoperative β-blocker use was associated with slower aortic dilation at the diaphragmatic and celiac levels and higher rates of complete false lumen thrombosis in stent-covered and stent-uncovered DTA segments.

articles.title: Personalized Xenogeneic Arterial Grafts Support Long-Term Functional Vascular Integration.
articles.abstract: The clinical need for small-diameter vascular grafts remains unmet due to limited availability of autologous vessels and poor long-term performance of synthetic alternatives. Here, we present a personalized tissue engineering strategy enabling the use of xenogeneic arterial matrices for long-term vascular reconstruction. Decellularized arterial scaffolds derived from sheep, pig and cow were reconditioned with autologous blood to generate personalized tissue-engineered arteries (P-TEAs), which were implanted as carotid interposition grafts in sheep and evaluated for up to 12 months. At the study endpoint, all grafts in animals completing the study were patent, including one graft that required reintervention to restore blood flow. No thrombosis, stenosis, aneurysm formation, or calcification was observed at the study endpoint. Longitudinal imaging demonstrated stable luminal geometry, while histological and ultrastructural analyses demonstrated preservation of extracellular matrix architecture, extensive recellularization, luminal endothelial coverage and tissue vascularization. Endothelial coverage was observed in the single graft examined at one month. Biomechanical assessment indicated that P-TEAs exhibited an estimated burst pressure within the supraphysiological range and increased stiffness relative to native arteries, consistent with adaptive matrix remodelling while maintaining functional integrity. Transcriptomic profiling further indicated that graft displayed transcriptional similarity to native arteries, consistent with vascular phenotype. Importantly, xenogeneic grafts showed no sustained activation of the circulating T-cell subsets examined, suggesting a limited systemic T-cell response within the parameters assessed. Collectively, these findings support the potential of personalized xenogeneic vascular grafts to achieve long-term patency and constructive tissue remodelling. This approach provides a scalable and clinically translatable strategy to overcome donor tissue limitations and represents a significant advance towards an off-the-shelf vascular scaffold followed by recipient-specific graft manufacturing. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: The long-term remodelling of decellularized biomaterials into functional living tissues remains a central challenge in regenerative medicine. This study demonstrates that decellularized xenogeneic arterial extracellular matrix can be personalized by autologous blood reconditioning to generate vascular grafts that achieve stable function for at least 12 months in a large-animal model. The grafts underwent extensive luminal endothelial coverage, revascularization and cellular repopulation while preserving extracellular matrix architecture, developing favourable biomechanical properties, exhibiting transcriptional similarities to native arteries at the 12-month endpoint, and avoiding sustained systemic immune activation. Beyond validating a clinically translatable vascular graft, this work provides comprehensive evidence of long-term biomaterial remodelling and host integration, offering insights that are broadly relevant for the development of regenerative biomaterials and decellularized tissue scaffolds.

articles.title: EMPODERA Intervention for Spanish-speaking Latino Caregivers of Critically Ill Oncology Patients: Cultural Adaptation Process.
articles.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Surrogate decision-makers of critically ill patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) often experience extreme psychological distress. For Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers, additional socioeconomic and healthcare challenges frequently compound their emotional suffering.

OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to address the unique needs of Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers.

METHODS: Mixed-methods, approach to adapt the EMPOWER intervention to EMPODERA, guided by ecological validity and cultural adaptation process models. Spanish-speaking Latino caregivers of ICU patients (n=11), Latino critical care providers (n=7), and mental health providers who treat Latino caregivers (n=5) from one ICU at a comprehensive cancer center in New York City and professional networks across the U.S. and Latin America were recruited. The EMPOWER intervention (Enhancing & Mobilizing the POtential for Wellness & Emotional Resilience) is an ultra-brief intervention originally designed to improve coping and reduce distress in English-speaking surrogates.

RESULTS: Analysis of the quantitative and qualitative findings suggest several adaptations including: (1) reduce stigma of assistance for mental health and provide educational materials promoting psychosocial care, (2) offer a resource booklet to address caregivers' social needs, (3) mitigate literacy issues using simple language and visual aids, and (4) include culturally-syntonic metaphors that resonate more effectively with the target audience.

CONCLUSION: Our findings highlighted the significance of making key adaptations of EMPOWER. Feedback suggested the importance of clarifying definitions of concepts, using clear language, and incorporating values to align with Latino cultural values. Key informants also recommended supplementing the intervention with psychoeducational resources to address mental health stigma. Future research is needed to evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of EMPOWER for Latino caregivers.

articles.title: Every-Other-Day Fasting Ameliorates Diet-Induced Fatty Liver Disease with Associated Changes in Gut Microbiota and Bile Acid Profiles.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely associated with unhealthy dietary patterns and characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation and impaired glucose homeostasis. Although every-other-day fasting (EODF) has emerged as a promising temporal dietary strategy, the nutritional mechanisms underlying its protective effects against MASLD remain unclear. Here, C57BL/6J mice were assigned to four dietary regimens: control diet, control diet with EODF, high-fat/high-sugar (HFHS) diet, and HFHS with EODF. EODF significantly reduced body weight and fat mass, improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, and alleviated hepatic steatosis in HFHS-fed mice. These benefits were accompanied by increased microbial diversity and partial restoration of the HFHS-disrupted gut microbiota. Integrated microbiome-bile acid profiling identified Lactobacillus as an EODF-responsive genus linked to improved metabolic phenotypes and glycocholic acid (GCA)-related bile acid alterations. EODF was associated with increased Lactobacillus abundance and compartment-specific changes in GCA levels, with lower fecal levels and higher circulating and hepatic levels. Oral GCA supplementation reproduced key EODF benefits, including reduced adiposity and hepatic triglyceride accumulation, and improved glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity. Hepatic metabolomics revealed increased carnitine-related metabolites and remodeling of glutathione and branched-chain amino acid metabolism, providing potential mechanistic insights into GCA-associated metabolic remodeling related to fatty acid utilization and redox homeostasis. These findings indicate that EODF improves HFHS-induced MASLD with associated changes in the gut microbiota-bile acid axis, identifying GCA-related changes as a potential metabolic link connecting dietary timing with liver health.

articles.title: A Novel Scoring System for Systematic Assessment of Functional Studies of KCNQ1 Variants.
articles.journal: The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD
articles.abstract: Until recently, functional characterization has remained underutilized in the classification of variants in the KCNQ1 gene due to application at only the supporting level of evidence (PS3_Supporting or BS3_Supporting). The Potassium Channel Arrhythmia Variant Curation Expert Panel (VCEP) has addressed this by introducing a framework based on the most advanced methodologies currently available to guide the evaluation of functional evidence for PS3 or BS3 at enhanced strength. The development of a point-scoring system that rewards independent evidence from diverse assays reduces uncertainty in the evaluation of functional studies for KCNQ1 and other ion channel genes, providing a more reliable framework for variant interpretation.

articles.title: Delayed oxygen saturation recovery after the 6-minute walk test: Prognostic implications for COPD patients.
articles.abstract:
RESEARCH QUESTION: The 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is a fundamental instrument in the clinical management of COPD patients, yet the prognostic value of specific physiological parameters during the recovery phase remains underexplored. This study aimed to determine whether the recovery time of oxygen saturation (SpO2-RT) following a 6MWT is associated with long-term prognosis (death and hospitalizations) in a cohort of patients with COPD.

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: In this prospective observational cohort, 512 consecutive patients were recruited through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service and underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry, and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a ≥3% decrease in SpO2 from baseline during the 6MWT; SpO2-RT was the time from test completion until SpO2 returned to baseline.

RESULTS: Of the 512 enrolled patients 25% were female. Those who experienced oxygen desaturation during the 6MWT exhibited significantly worse pulmonary function (FEV1%, RV%, IC/TLC and DLCO%) (p <.0001), higher fibrinogen levels (p =.01), lower quadriceps strength (p =.02), reduced PA (p <.0001), and a shorter distance walked (p <.0001). Within the desaturation sub-cohort, differences were analysed based on a SpO2-RT cut-off ≥ 80 seconds. Patients with a prolonged SpO2-RT exhibited more severe pulmonary function impairment (p values ranging from .02 to <.0001), significantly lower PA (p =.001), and shorter distance 6MWT (p <.0001). During the 3-year follow-up increased SpO2-RT was associated with increased mortality (p =.03) and hospitalizations (p =.0003). In the adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO2-RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalization (p = .02) and mortality (p =.04).

INTERPRETATION: A prolonged SpO2-RT ≥ 80 identifies a COPD phenotype characterized by diminished respiratory reserve and an increased risk of subsequent exacerbation-related hospitalizations and all-cause mortality. SpO2-RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.

articles.title: Comorbidities associated with respiratory syncytial virus hospitalization in young and old adults: a detailed population-based case-control study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Older and comorbid individuals are at risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. Comorbidity-specific associations with RSV hospitalization are insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort and case-control study of adults hospitalized for laboratory-verified RSV infection 2021-2023 at three Swedish centers, and age-matched population controls. We compared individual associations with hospitalization for several comorbidities and age groups, as well as associations with death or severe disease among hospitalized cases.

RESULTS: We identified 355 patients hospitalized with RSV and 3550 controls. Asthma (OR 3.2, 95% CI 2.4-4.2), COPD (OR 4.6, 95% CI 3.4-6.2), atrial fibrillation (OR 4.2, 95% CI 3.2-5.5), heart failure (OR 4.3, 95% CI 3.2-5.8), and chronic kidney disease (OR 3.5, 95% CI 2.5-4.8) were strongly associated with hospitalization. We observed even stronger associations for neurological disease, hematologic malignancy, and organ transplantation with approximately six- to eightfold higher ORs. The associations were stronger among younger individuals for heart failure, chronic kidney disease, cancer, and immunosuppression. COPD and solid cancer were associated with 30-day mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with chronic cardiopulmonary, renal and neurologic disease, hematologic malignancy, or a history of transplantation had high ORs for RSV-associated hospitalization. COPD and cancer patients had risk of a poor outcome.

articles.title: Higher Shifting Ability Is Associated with Reduced Threat-Safety Differentiation During Fear Generalization.
articles.abstract: Adaptive fear generalization is beneficial to help individuals efficiently cope with novel situations with potential threats based on previous knowledge in complex environments, while overgeneralization may lead to unnecessary fear responses to safe stimuli, increasing the susceptibility of some anxiety disorders. Previous studies have shown that the three core components of executive function - shifting, updating, and inhibition play an important role in fear processing. However, it remains unclear whether subcomponents of executive function modulate fear generalization or not. To fill this gap, a total of 80 participants were recruited to complete executive function and fear generalization tasks in this study. Specifically, the participants underwent three tasks assessing the three components of executive function, including shifting, updating, and inhibition. Subsequently, all participants completed fear learning and generalization tasks, and recorded their shock expectancy ratings, skin conductance response (SCR), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals in the prefrontal region.
