We found that participants with high shifting ability showed reduced threat-safety differentiation and increased shock expectancy ratings to generalization stimuli(GS). During fear generalization, higher shifting ability was associated with lower oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO) responses in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. In contrast, updating and inhibition showed no comparable significant associations with behavioral fear generalization. Together, these findings highlight the distinct association of shifting ability with fear generalization behavior, accompanied by a localized prefrontal hemodynamic response.

articles.title: Ischemic Stroke Risk in Women with Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Regression Analysis of Temporal Trends.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Female sex has historically been associated with increased ischemic stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), but recent studies suggest that this association has weakened over time, with inconsistent findings.

OBJECTIVE: To assess temporal trends in female sex-associated stroke risk in patients with AF using meta-regression.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science were searched for studies reporting adjusted estimates of sex differences in stroke risk among patients with AF. Random-effects meta-regression was performed using restricted maximum likelihood, with calendar time modeled linearly and using natural cubic splines to assess nonlinearity. Leave-one-study-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 47 studies comprising 85 effect estimates and 5,114,440 patients (46.0% women) were included. Female sex-associated stroke risk declined significantly over time (β = -0.0091 per year; 95% confidence interval, -0.0145 to -0.0036; P = .001), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I2 = 86.8%). The nonlinear model provided a better fit than the linear model (P = .022) and explained 15.3% of between-study heterogeneity. In the most recent observation periods, no statistically significant sex difference in stroke risk was observed. The declining trend remained significant in all leave-one-study-out analyses.

CONCLUSION: The excess stroke risk associated with female sex in patients with AF has declined over time and was no longer statistically significant in the most contemporary observation periods. These findings support reconsideration of the role of female sex in contemporary stroke risk stratification.

articles.title: One Puncture, One Catheter: Upper-Extremity Venous Access With Robotic Magnetic Navigation for Right Atrial Ablation in Adults With Congenital or Complex Cardiac Anatomy.
Voltage-gated sodium channels Nav1.6-Nav1.9 in autonomic control: Evidence and pharmacological implications.
articles.abstract: Voltage-gated Na+ (Nav) channels are major determinants of neuronal excitability and important pharmacological targets, yet their isoform-specific contributions to autonomic nervous system signaling remain incompletely defined. Here, we evaluate evidence for Nav1.6-Nav1.9 in autonomic-relevant neuronal pathways and examine the implications for Nav channel-targeted pharmacology. Direct functional evidence varies substantially among isoforms. Nav1.6 is implicated mainly in rostral ventrolateral medullary sympathoexcitation in models of stress-induced hypertension. Evidence is strongest for Nav1.7 in postganglionic sympathetic and airway parasympathetic transmission; Nav1.8 in intracardiac ganglion neurons and a genetically defined sudomotor pathway, with additional anatomical or pathway-level evidence in vagal and stellate ganglion preparations; and Nav1.9 in visceral afferents and enteric neurons, where persistent subthreshold current regulates neuronal gain. These assignments are neither anatomically exclusive nor fixed: neuronal identity, co-expressed conductances, subcellular localization, physiological state, and drug exposure can alter the functional consequences of engaging a given isoform. As isoform-selective compounds advance, autonomic effects may therefore represent pathway-consistent target engagement rather than nonspecific intolerance and, depending on the pathway and disease state, may constitute a safety consideration, a therapeutic opportunity, or both. Integrating autonomic physiology with isoform selectivity, state dependence, and physiologically relevant challenge should improve interpretation and development of Nav channel-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy with delivery at 24-27 weeks' gestation: risk factors and adverse maternal outcomes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early-onset hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) prior to 34 weeks are associated with significant morbidity and mortality for pregnant patients and their neonates, but HDP with delivery prior to 28 weeks is less well characterized.

OBJECTIVE: We sought to identify risk factors and quantify maternal morbidity and mortality for HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks' gestation.

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study used United States births within the Premier Healthcare database between October 2015 and December 2020. Included individuals were 12-55 years old, with birth at 24 weeks' gestation or later. HDP was categorized by gestational age at delivery (24-27, 28-33, 34-36, and ≥37 completed weeks' gestation). We assessed maternal demographic data, clinical characteristics, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including mortality, severe maternal morbidity (SMM), intensive care unit (ICU) admission and readmission. Multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between candidate risk factors and HDP stratified by gestational age at delivery; results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Multivariable logistic regression estimated the association of each gestational-age subgroup of HDP with adverse pregnancy outcomes. Separate models were built using distinct reference groups including 1) no HDP and 2) HDP at or beyond 37 weeks' gestation.

RESULTS: Of 4,666,784 births, 546,962 (11.7%) had an HDP. Of those with HDP, 5,797 (1.1%, 0.1% of all births) delivered at 24-27 weeks, 35,237 (6.4%, 0.8% of all births) delivered at 28-33 weeks, and 413,657 (75.6%, 8.9% of all births) delivered after 37 weeks. Risk factors common across gestational age subtypes of HDP included chronic hypertension, chronic kidney disease, pregestational diabetes, pre-existing cardiac disease, body mass index (BMI) ≥40 kg/m2, use of assisted reproductive technology, and age ≥40 years. Risk factors most associated with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks were chronic hypertension (aOR 11.45, 95%CI 10.85-12.08), chronic kidney disease (aOR 4.88, 95%CI 4.24-5.62), and antiphospholipid antibody syndrome [APLS] (aOR 4.51, 95%CI 3.46-5.87). Multiple pregnancy and pregestational diabetes were most associated with HDP with delivery at 28-33 weeks (aOR 7.48, 95%CI 7.27-7.69 and aOR 3.06, 95%CI 2.95-3.17). BMI ≥40 kg/m2 was most associated with HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks (aOR 2.33, 95%CI 2.29-2.36). HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks had the highest rate of SMM (616 per 10,000 births [95%CI 556-681] vs 26/10,000 [95%CI 25-26] and 77/10,000 [95%CI 74-80] among those with no HDP and HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks, respectively). The odds of SMM and ICU admission were highest among those with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks. Maternal mortality was rare, but occurred most frequently in those with HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks (121 per 100,000 births [95%CI 49-249] vs 5/100,000 [95%CI 4-5] and 7/100,000 [95%CI 5-10] among those with no HDP and HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: HDP with delivery at 24 to 27 weeks' gestation occurred in 0.1% of all pregnancies and was associated with disproportionately high SMM compared to HDP with delivery at ≥37 weeks. Risk factors for HDP with delivery at 24-27 weeks may differ from those for HDP with delivery later in gestation, particularly HDP at term.

articles.title: Urinary extracellular vesicle microRNA profile in dogs with visceral leishmaniasis: differential expression and exploratory associations with renal Doppler indices and proteinuria.
articles.abstract: Canine visceral leishmaniasis (CVL) is a systemic zoonosis caused by Leishmania infantum, for which dogs are the main urban reservoir. Infected dogs may present non-specific clinical signs and, in advanced cases, die of chronic kidney disease. This study evaluated urinary microRNAs (miRNAs) as candidate biomarkers of renal injury in naturally infected dogs. Fifteen dogs were included: five healthy controls and ten untreated dogs at the moderate stage of disease according to the LeishVet guidelines. All dogs underwent clinical and laboratory assessment, renal Doppler ultrasonography, and serological and molecular diagnosis of CVL. The CVL group showed typical clinical signs, including onychogryphosis, lymphadenomegaly, and cutaneous lesions, as well as laboratory abnormalities such as hyperglobulinemia. Ultrasonography revealed increased renal echogenicity and an elevated peak systolic velocity in the left kidney. Urinary extracellular vesicles were isolated for RNA extraction and miRNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), followed by bioinformatic analysis. Twenty-one differentially expressed miRNAs were identified, including three with previously described physiological renal expression: miR-486 and miR-378 (up-regulated) and cfa-let-7f (down-regulated). The differentially expressed miRNAs were correlated with renal Doppler indices and the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPC). Pearson correlation analyses were performed in the infected group, without correction for multiple comparisons. These exploratory analyses identified six statistically significant associations involving five miRNAs: miR-222 was negatively correlated with the resistive index (RI) of both kidneys; miR-95 was negatively correlated with the RI of the left kidney; miR-221 was negatively correlated with the RI of the right kidney; cfa-let-7a-2 was positively correlated with the RI of the left kidney; and cfa-let-7g was negatively correlated with UPC. These findings suggest that the altered urinary miRNA profile may reflect molecular processes associated with renal alterations in dogs with CVL. Urinary miRNAs may therefore be promising candidates for further investigation as minimally invasive biomarkers of renal involvement in canine visceral leishmaniasis.

articles.title: Engineering microneedle-based transdermal insulin delivery systems for diabetes mellitus: from material design to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Microneedle (MN)-based transdermal delivery has emerged as a promising strategy to address the limitations of conventional insulin administration while overcoming the barrier function of the stratum corneum. This review critically examines insulin-loaded MN systems, including solid, coated, hollow, dissolving, and hydrogel-forming MNs, with emphasis on the relationships among material selection, MN architecture, insulin formulation and stability, fabrication, mechanical and insertion performance, drug release, and therapeutic outcomes. Natural and synthetic polymers, biodegradable and bioresponsive materials, and formulation strategies for preserving insulin structural integrity and biological activity are discussed together with major fabrication technologies and critical quality attributes. Preclinical evidence from in vitro, ex vivo, and diabetic animal studies is evaluated alongside pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics performance and the available clinical evidence. Next-generation smart MNs, including glucose oxidase- and phenylboronic acid-based glucose-responsive systems and related hypoxia-, pH-, and enzyme-responsive approaches, are also discussed for glucose-regulated and closed-loop insulin delivery. Comparison with established insulin-delivery technologies highlights both the potential advantages and remaining translational challenges of MN systems. Future integration with continuous glucose sensing, digital health technologies, personalized medicine, sustainable materials, and scalable manufacturing may further support the development of insulin MNs as next-generation technologies for diabetes management.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Clinical Features of Eosinophilic Esophagitis: Analysis Using over 300 Million Medical Records in the Cosmos Database.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic allergic disease of the esophagus with increasing prevalence.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize EoE epidemiology and clinical features in the largest U.S. cohort to date.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the Epic Cosmos database (1990-2024), comprising >300 million deidentified patients, for prevalence, incidence, geographic distribution, comorbidities, and treatment patterns of EoE as identified by diagnostic code.

RESULTS: Of 300,278,878 patients, 508,739 had EoE by diagnostic code. Prevalence and incidence increased by 7.1 and 2-fold, respectively. EoE prevalence was highest in northern states (i.e., New Hampshire 0.31%). There was a bimodal distribution of peak incidence in the second decade followed by the fifth decade of life. There was an overall higher proportion of males (59%), although this predominance decreased with increasing age (2.7 ratio of male to female for <10 years of age compared to 1.5 for 20-29 years of age). EoE diagnosis was strongly associated with the presence of comorbid allergies including food allergy, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis and asthma (OR 63.4), food allergy (OR 16.1), and gastrointestinal diseases such as celiac disease (OR 11.5). Amongst food allergies defined by diagnostic codes, wheat showed the strongest association (OR 54.0). Proton pump inhibitors were the most common treatment (83.4%, n=424,084), followed by topical steroids (30.5%, n=155,211), and dupilumab (7.6%, n=38,648).

CONCLUSION: EoE prevalence is rising in the U.S. with regional variation and strong associations with atopic and gastrointestinal comorbidities. These findings provide updated epidemiologic and clinical insights and highlight evolving treatment trends.

articles.title: Liver Biochemical and Clinical Outcomes After IL-23 Pathway Therapy in IBD Patients With Mild Baseline Liver Test Abnormalities: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The significance of mild baseline liver test abnormalities in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) receiving IL-23 pathway therapy is uncertain. We compared subsequent recorded outcomes between patients with mild abnormalities and those with a normal baseline liver panel.

METHODS: Retrospective 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort study in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults with Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis and a record of ustekinumab, risankizumab, guselkumab, or mirikizumab were classified by ALT, AST, total ALP, and total bilirubin in the preceding six months. Outcomes were assessed over days 1-730. Matching included demographic, liver-disease, metabolic, medication, prior-biologic, and biomarker variables. Liver diagnoses were not clinically adjudicated.

RESULTS: After matching, 7,022 patients per group were analyzed. ALT ≥99 U/L occurred in 7.163% versus 3.048% (HR 2.406, 95% CI 2.050-2.823), AST ≥111 U/L in 3.745% versus 1.908% (HR 1.978, 1.606-2.435), total ALP ≥209 U/L in 5.938% versus 1.595% (HR 3.823, 3.103-4.710), and total bilirubin ≥2.5 mg/dL in 2.820% versus 1.097% (HR 2.588, 1.989-3.367). New fatty liver (HR 2.065, 1.717-2.483), new cirrhosis (HR 1.756, 1.173-2.629), and all-cause death (HR 1.567, 1.196-2.054) were also more frequent. Acute liver failure counts were too small to report.

CONCLUSIONS: Mild baseline liver test abnormalities were associated with more subsequent recorded liver test elevations, fatty liver, cirrhosis, and death. These associations may reflect underlying liver disease and closer surveillance; they do not establish drug-induced liver injury or the liver safety of IL-23 pathway therapy.

articles.title: Association between allergic diseases and future risk of endometriosis: A population-based cohort study.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic disease of extrauterine endometrial-like tissue. Multimorbidity of endometriosis and allergic diseases is well-established, though it remains unclear whether allergic disease is a prospective risk marker for endometriosis and whether diagnosis by adolescence has implications for endometriosis risk.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between allergic disease, including timing of diagnosis, and future risk of endometriosis.

METHODS: This population-based study used linked health administrative databases for all hospital-born females in Ontario, Canada between 1988-1998 (N = 525,326), followed to death, loss of public health insurance, or December 2023. Allergic diseases were asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis measured as time-varying exposures. Cox proportional hazards models were used to compare endometriosis risk from the 10th birthday onward between females diagnosed versus never diagnosed with allergic disease across the life course (median follow-up 19.7 years), controlling for birth and demographic characteristics, primary care continuity, and comorbidities.

RESULTS: Incidence of endometriosis was 10.5/10,000 person-years in females with allergic disease and 6.4/10,000 person-years in females without allergic disease. There was a positive association between allergic disease, particularly asthma, and risk of endometriosis for which the magnitude was inversely associated with age at allergic disease diagnosis; the aHR were 1.51 (95% CI 1.29-1.77), 1.35 (95% CI 1.26-1.45), and 1.21 (95% CI 1.13-1.29) for allergic disease diagnosed by age 10, at age 20, and at age 30 years, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Females with allergic disease, especially a diagnosis of asthma before age 20 years, may have elevated risk of endometriosis.

articles.title: Sex and Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting Outcome.
articles.abstract: Whether female sex independently influences short-term prognosis after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) or primarily reflects differences in baseline risk and surgical complexity remains controversial. We aimed to examine if sex is independently associated with in-hospital outcomes after CABG. This is an observational study of consecutive adults undergoing CABG between 2011 and 2024. The primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE). We analyzed 2,101 patients (21.5% women). Women were older than men (68.9±10.6 vs 66.2±10.3 years, p<0.001) and more frequently underwent combined valve/CABG surgery (43.7% vs 24.9%, p<0.001), but had less left ventricular systolic dysfunction (43.9% vs. 50.9%, P=0.04), and lower rates of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (10.6% vs 15.8%, p=0.007). Women had higher rates of in-hospital mortality (9.1% vs 4.5%, p<0.001) and MACCE (13.0% vs 7.5%, p <0.001). However, after multivariable adjustment (including age, renal function, preoperative hemoglobin, body surface area, ventricular function, urgency, and surgical complexity) female sex was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.84 - 2.17, p=0.21) nor MACCE (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 0.84 - 1.82, p=0.27). Propensity score matching and inverse probability weighting were consistent with no significant association between female sex and prognosis. In conclusion, compared to men, women that undergo CABG had a different baseline risk profile and more frequent combined procedures. However, after adjusting for baseline characteristics and procedural factors, the associations between sex and outcomes were no longer statistically significant.

articles.title: Association of the Cholesterol-High-Density Lipoprotein-Glucose Index With Depressive Symptoms and Their Longitudinal Trajectories Among Stroke Survivors: Analyses of NHANES and CHARLS.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depressive symptoms can complicate stroke recovery. The association between the cholesterol-high-density lipoprotein-glucose (CHG) index and depressive symptoms among stroke survivors is unclear. We examined prevalent symptoms and symptom trajectories in two datasets.

METHODS: Analyses included 448 stroke survivors from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and 215 from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). NHANES analyses used survey-weighted logistic regression and restricted cubic splines. In CHARLS, baseline CHG in 2011 was examined in relation to depressive symptom trajectories assessed in 2013, 2015, and 2018 using multinomial logistic regression, spline comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and 500 participant-level bootstrap resamples with trajectory assignments held fixed.

RESULTS: In NHANES, 80 participants met the PHQ-9 cutoff for depressive symptoms; the adjusted odds ratio per one-unit increase in CHG was 2.39 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.86-6.64; P = 0.093). Spline analyses suggested a possible nonlinear pattern (overall P = 0.038, P for nonlinearity = 0.033), with wide confidence intervals at the extremes of the CHG distribution.In CHARLS, three depressive symptom trajectories were identified: Low stable (n = 128), Increasing (n = 55), and Decreasing (n = 32).In the three-class analysis, the likelihood-ratio test (P = 0.019) and AIC favored the spline model. BIC favored the linear model. The fully adjusted linear estimate for the Decreasing versus Low stable trajectory was imprecise (relative risk ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.27-1.47). With trajectory assignments held fixed, the median bootstrap P value for nonlinearity was 0.0045, and 419 of 500 resamples (83.8%) yielded P < 0.05. The E-value for the point estimate was 1.17.

CONCLUSIONS: In NHANES, cross-sectional spline analyses suggested an approximately U-shaped association between CHG and prevalent depressive symptoms among stroke survivors. In the exploratory three-class CHARLS model, lower and higher baseline CHG levels corresponded to higher predicted probabilities of the Decreasing and Increasing trajectories, respectively, and the probability of the Low stable trajectory peaked at intermediate CHG levels.These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger, independent cohorts of stroke survivors.

articles.title: Risk Factors and Predictive Models for Gastrostomy Tube Placement After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastrostomy tube (G-tube) placement is considered post-stroke when oral intake cannot meet nutrition, hydration, or medication needs. Associated factors are heterogeneous and may reflect both patient impairment and institutional practice.

AIMS: Identify factors associated with G-tube placement and descriptively summarize published prediction models.

SUMMARY OF REVIEW: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Cochrane through October 1, 2025, and reference lists were searched through December 20, 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool, and eligible odds ratios (OR) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Of 1,131 records, 25 studies were included; 12 were eligible for meta-analysis and nine contributed estimates. Seven studies evaluated seven prediction models. Across studies, 89 factors were identified, and risk of bias was often moderate or high. Higher National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was associated with placement (k=4; OR per point 1.090 [95% CI 1.085-1.095]), but one administrative study contributed 98.5% of the weight. Excluding it yielded OR 1.081 [95% CI, 1.041-1.122]. Male sex (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.13-1.29) and Black, Hispanic, and Asian/Pacific Islander race/ethnicity compared with White (ORs 1.42-1.75) were associated with higher odds of G-tube placement. Conversely, private insurance compared with Medicare was associated with lower odds of placement (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.79-0.93). Heterogeneity varied across comparisons (I²=0%-90.6%). Model outcomes and performance reporting varied, limiting comparisons; none incorporated imaging-based swallowing physiology.

CONCLUSIONS: G-tube placement is multifactorial, and existing evidence primarily reflects observed placement rather than physiologically confirmed swallowing impairment that is sufficiently severe to warrant prolonged enteral feeding. Heterogeneity and frequent moderate-to-high risk of bias limit interpretation. Prospective studies should evaluate whether externally validated, imaging-informed models improve prediction of ongoing feeding needs.

articles.title: Discordance between cystatin C- and creatinine-based estimated GFR levels is associated with a poor prognosis in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus and preserved creatinine-based estimated GFR.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We investigated whether difference between estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFRdiff) calculated from cystatin C (eGFRcys) and from creatinine (eGFRcr) influences the prognosis of people with type 2 diabetes and eGFRcr ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.

METHODS: A total of 518 people with type 2 diabetes and eGFRcr ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 were enrolled in a long-term observational study. eGFRdiff was calculated as eGFRcys minus eGFRcr. The primary endpoint was the incidence of renal and cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: During the 15-year median follow-up period, 200 primary endpoints occurred. The adjusted hazard ratio of the primary endpoint was 1.53 (95 % CI: 1.05-2.23) in the low subgroup (eGFRdiff < -15) and 0.69 (95 % CI: 0.42-1.12) in the high subgroup (15 < eGFRdiff), as compared to the middle subgroup (-15 ≤ eGFRdiff ≤ 15). This association was observed only in individuals with normoalbuminuria, but not in those with albuminuria. eGFRdiff was negatively correlated with age and positively correlated with 24-hour urinary creatinine excretion and estimated protein intake.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater negative eGFRdiff, which may be attributed to ageing and low muscle mass, was associated with the poor prognosis in people with type 2 diabetes and preserved eGFRcr, particularly in those with normoalbuminuria.

articles.title: Adverse social determinants of health and their association with mortality in early-onset type 2 diabetes: A nationally representative survey with linked mortality data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adverse social determinants of health (SDoH) relate more strongly to mortality in early- versus late-onset type 2 diabetes, and whether depression mediates this, is unclear.

METHODS: We analysed 6,083 adults with type 2 diabetes (999 early-onset; 5,084 late-onset) from NHANES 1999-2018, followed for mortality to 2019. Eight SDoH subdomains formed a 0-8 score. Survey-weighted logistic and Cox models examined associations and effect modification by onset group; counterfactual mediation (B = 300) estimated mediation by depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥ 5) in 2005-2018.

RESULTS: Each additional SDoH point was associated with higher odds of having early-onset rather than late-onset diabetes (OR 1.09, 95 % CI 1.03-1.16). Adjusted mortality was higher for early-onset than late-onset diabetes (HR 2.42, 1.84-3.18; crude estimate reversed). Per SDoH point, mortality rose 43 % in early-onset (1.43, 1.30-1.57) versus 21 % in late-onset disease (1.21, 1.16-1.27); per SDoH category, the ratio of HRs was 1.35 (1.11-1.65, P = 0.004). Depression mediated 13.8 % and 6.4 %; between-group difference was not significant (dIE 0.035, P = 0.071).

CONCLUSIONS: The SDoH-mortality association was steeper in early-onset diabetes; depression accounted for only a modest, within-group share. Social risk screening is warranted; depression may represent a modifiable intermediate target on the pathway from social disadvantage to premature death.

articles.title: Fibrosis severity and age-adjusted FIB-4 performance in a multicenter Brazilian biopsy-proven MASLD cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent in Latin America. Contemporary biopsy-based data on fibrosis severity in Brazil are limited. We evaluated fibrosis severity and the diagnostic performance of FIB-4 in a multicenter Brazilian cohort with biopsy-proven MASLD.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 2,335 MASLD patients with available liver biopsy from 11 tertiary centers in three Brazilian regions. Fibrosis stage, factors associated with advanced fibrosis (≥F3), and FIB-4 performance were evaluated. Because one Southern center predominantly enrolled candidates for bariatric surgery, analyses were repeated after excluding this center.

RESULTS: Mean age was 49.1±14.4 years; 50.3% men. Advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis were present in 14.3%, and 4.6%, respectively. After exclusion of the Southern bariatric-surgery center regional differences in fibrosis firstly observed were no longer significant. In the primary multivariable analysis, older age and geographic region were associated with advanced fibrosis, whereas T2DM showed an unexpected inverse association; these associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant in the sensitivity analysis. FIB-4 was available in 1,853 patients, with an AUROC of 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.83) for advanced fibrosis. The AUROC was 0.72 (95% CI 0.65-0.79) in patients >65 years. Optimized cutoffs were 0.98 for patients ≤65 years and 1.78 for those >65 years.

CONCLUSIONS: This large biopsy-proven Brazilian MASLD cohort showed a substantial proportion of clinically significant and advanced fibrosis, while most patients had F0-F1 fibrosis. Regional comparisons were strongly influenced by center-specific case mix. FIB-4 showed good overall accuracy, although age-specific cutoffs may improve risk stratification.

articles.title: ASA use in pregnancy and risk of venous thromboembolism: population-based propensity score-weighted study.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pregnancy and the postpartum period heighten the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether low-dose ASA prevents VTE in pregnancy is unknown.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether low-dose ASA is associated with a lower risk of VTE during pregnancy and postpartum.

METHODS: A population-based retrospective cohort study in Ontario, Canada, 2018-2021. Included were women aged 16-55 years with a livebirth or stillbirth. Excluded were those with VTE pre-pregnancy or up to 16 weeks. The exposure was low-dose ASA initiated at 12-16 completed weeks vs. no ASA use. ASA was typically continued to 35 completed weeks. The primary outcome was any objectively diagnosed VTE between 17 weeks' gestation and up to 42 days postpartum discharge. Cause-specific hazard models compared ASA use vs. non-use, weighted by propensity-based overlap weights.

RESULTS: There were 13 382 pregnancies with low-dose ASA exposure, and 280 162 without ASA exposure. After a median (IQR) duration of follow-up of 189 (182 to 196) and 196 (189 to 203) days, respectively, VTE occurred among 72 women in the ASA group (weighted incidence rate 2.8 per 100 000 person-days), and 989 women in the comparison group (2.2 per 100 000 person-days) - a weighted HR of 1.26 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.62). The corresponding weighted HR for pulmonary embolism was 1.11 (95% CI 0.73 to 1.70), and for DVT 1.33 (95% CI 0.98 to 1.80).

CONCLUSION: In this observational study, documented low-dose ASA prophylaxis was not associated with a lower observed risk of VTE. Residual confounding by indication, including from unavailable prior-pregnancy history, cannot be excluded.

articles.title: JHRS2026 in Kyoto: Building the Future of Arrhythmia Care Together.
Factor XI/XIa Inhibitors as Novel Anticoagulants for the Treatment of Splanchnic Vein Thrombosis in Cirrhosis: Is It Time to Move Forward?
Determinants and Clinical Impact of Medication Non-Adherence in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adherence to guideline-recommended medical therapy reduces the risk of major adverse limb events (MALE) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with lower extremity peripheral artery disease (LE-PAD), yet adherence remains low. This study aimed to prospectively identify determinants of therapeutic non-adherence among unselected patients with LE-PAD seen in routine practice.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre, prospective study of consecutive patients with symptomatic LE-PAD seen at Amiens-Picardie University Hospital between June and December 2025. Adherence was assessed at inclusion using the self-administered Girerd questionnaire (good, moderate, or poor adherence) and re-assessed at 3 months. Determinants of non-adherence were identified using ordinal logistic regression. Associations with MALE (Firth's penalized logistic regression adjusted for a priori confounders) and MACE (Fisher's exact test) were assessed at 3 months, and at 6 months as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Of 174 patients included, 171 completed the Girerd questionnaire and were analysed (median age 69 years, 73.7% male): 31.0% had good adherence, 40.4% moderate, and 28.7% poor adherence. Diabetes (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.35, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.26-4.38) and obesity (aOR 2.24, 95% CI 1.06-4.74) were independently associated with poorer adherence, whereas regular alcohol use was associated with better adherence (aOR 0.19, 95% CI 0.07-0.55). Poor adherence increased from 28.7% to 40.0% at 3 months (p=0.009). At 3 months, all 5 MACE occurred in poorly adherent patients (10.9% vs. 0%, p=0.002), and poor adherence was non-significantly associated with MALE (aOR 2.26, 95% CI 0.73-7.71); at 6 months, this association was significant (aOR 4.14, 95% CI 1.47-12.9).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, unselected LE-PAD population, diabetes and obesity were independent determinants of poor therapeutic adherence, which was associated with early cardiovascular events and with limb events at 6 months. These findings identify a distinct high-risk patient profile that could be screened at first consultation to guide individualized adherence-support interventions.

articles.title: True Lumen Guided Stent Sizing Predicts Distal Aortic Remodeling After ATAAD Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Descending thoracic aorta (DTA) remodeling is a critical determinant of long-term survival after acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair. Despite the widespread use of the frozen elephant trunk (FET) technique, quantitative evidence for stent graft sizing based on true lumen (TL) dimensions remains scarce. This study investigated whether the difference between the stent and true lumen diameters (Δ) serves as a reliable predictor of late DTA remodeling.

METHODS: 147 ATAAD patients (2018-2022) were analyzed. Preoperative CTA was used to measure true lumen diameter (TL), false lumen diameter (FL) or total aortic diameters at the proximal landing zone. The parameter Δ was defined as the implanted stent graft diameter minus the preoperative TL diameter. Late DTA remodeling was defined by a >20% increase in TL proportion, FL thrombosis, and the absence of significant enlargement of the total aortic diameter. Multivariable logistic regression and ROC analysis were employed to evaluate the predictive value of Δ and identify an optimal clinical threshold.

RESULTS: ΔWas independently associated with late DTA remodeling (adjusted OR 1.163 per 1-mm increase; P = 0.010). ROC analysis identified 9 mm as the optimal cutoff. Patients with Δ > 9 mm had higher remodeling rates than those with Δ ≤ 9 mm (90.6% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.031). Subgroup analyses showed a generally consistent direction of association across stent-graft sizes, although statistical significance varied among subgroups. This finding was confirmed in an external validation cohort of 42 subsequent patients treated at our center.

CONCLUSIONS: A Δ threshold > 9 mm was associated with a higher likelihood of favorable late distal aortic remodeling after FET, providing a simple, evidence-based benchmark for preoperative planning.

articles.title: Strain-Dependent Modulation of Akt Pathway in Streptozotocin-Induced Diabetes: A Comparative Study in BALB/c and C57BL/6 Mice.
articles.abstract: Divergent genetic backgrounds influence susceptibility to experimental diabetes, with C57BL/6 mice generally exhibiting greater sensitivity to Streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetes than BALB/c mice. However, the molecular basis underlying these strain-dependent responses remains incompletely understood. This study investigated strain-specific metabolic and Akt signalling responses to STZ-induced diabetes in vivo. Male C57BL/6 and BALB/c mice received a single intraperitoneal injection of STZ (150 mg/kg). Diabetes progression was assessed by fasting blood glucose (FBG), glucose and insulin tolerance tests (GTT and ITT), fasting serum insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and % of β-cell function. Pancreatic insulin content, serum biochemical markers, lipid profiles, and tissue histology were evaluated. Insulin-signalling-related gene expression was assessed by RT-qPCR, while total Akt protein and insulin-stimulated Akt phosphorylation were measured in skeletal muscle. C57BL/6 mice demonstrated an approximately threefold greater susceptibility to diabetes, characterized by exacerbated hyperglycaemia, impaired glucose tolerance, decreased pancreatic insulin content, and disruption of normal islet architecture. In contrast, BALB/c mice retained comparatively higher pancreatic insulin content but showed features suggestive of altered insulin responsiveness, including reduced skeletal muscle Irs1 expression. Diabetic C57BL/6 mice exhibited increased skeletal muscle Akt mRNA and total Akt protein abundance, accompanied by markedly reduced insulin-stimulated p-Akt/total Akt ratio, whereas diabetic BALB/c mice showed reduced total Akt protein but a comparatively preserved Akt phosphorylation response. Overall, STZ induced distinct strain-dependent metabolic responses. C57BL/6 mice displayed features consistent with a more T1DM-like profile, whereas BALB/c mice showed features suggestive of altered insulin responsiveness. These findings suggest that functional Akt activation, rather than Akt abundance alone, may be associated with the divergent metabolic responses to STZ between these strains.

articles.title: METTL3-Mediated m6A Methylation of Malat1 is Associated With Macrophage Polarization and Sepsis-Associated Acute Lung Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The present investigation explores the association of methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3)-the catalytic component responsible for depositing N6-methyladenosine (m6A) marks-with the pathogenesis of acute lung injury (ALI) within septic contexts. We aim to investigate its relationship with Malat1 m6A modification, the Malat1/mmu-miR-129-5p/Pax6-Zeb2 competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network, and macrophage polarization, along with the underlying molecular mechanisms in an experimental model.

METHODS: An endotoxin-induced ALI model, a classic experimental paradigm for sepsis-associated ALI, was generated in vivo by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) into specific pathogen-free C57BL/6 mice. Prior to model establishment, mice received intravenous injections of Mettl3-silencing lentivirus for intervention. The degree of lung injury, inflammatory cytokine levels, expression of core molecules, and Malat1 m6A methylation levels were assessed. In vitro, an inflammatory model was created by stimulating RAW264.7 macrophages with LPS. Molecular interactions and regulatory functions were examined.

RESULTS: LPS-induced ALI model mice exhibited significant upregulation of Mettl3, Malat1, Pax6, and Zeb2 transcripts in lung tissue, alongside notable downregulation of mmu-miR-129-5p. Malat1 m6A methylation levels were also significantly increased. These changes were tightly linked to pro-inflammatory M1 phenotypic polarization of macrophages and lung tissue damage (all P < 0.001). Silencing Mettl3 significantly reduced Malat1 m6A methylation levels, reversed the aberrant expression of the downstream regulatory axis, inhibited pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, and alleviated local and systemic inflammation, pulmonary edema, and lung injury (all P < 0.001). Mechanistic studies indicated that Malat1 acts as a molecular sponge for mmu-miR-129-5p, a microRNA that directly interacts with the Pax6 3'UTR, thereby regulating PAX6 and ZEB2 protein expression in a ceRNA-dependent manner (all P < 0.001). Rescue experiments suggested that the Malat1/mmu-miR-129-5p axis, along with downstream PAX6-ZEB2 signaling, is involved in the regulatory effect of METTL3 on macrophage phenotypic differentiation and the associated inflammatory processes within the LPS-induced inflammatory model.

CONCLUSION: METTL3 is aberrantly overexpressed in the LPS-induced model of sepsis-associated ALI. This elevation is closely associated with METTL3-dependent m6A methylation of Malat1, which in turn is associated with its subsequent upregulation. Mettl3-dependent m6A modification of Malat1 is associated with dysregulation of the Malat1/mmu-miR-129-5p/Pax6-Zeb2 ceRNA network and may contribute to the pathogenesis of sepsis-associated pulmonary injury, a mechanism closely linked to pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization. These findings provide a novel potential epigenetic target and experimental basis for the prevention and treatment of sepsis-associated ALI.

articles.title: Fluctuations in international normalized ratio during co-administration of tirzepatide and warfarin within a left ventricular assist device population: Two case reports.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide is a GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist that can improve glycemic control in patients with diabetes and promote weight loss in obesity, but its effect on medications requiring therapeutic drug monitoring, such as warfarin, has not been fully evaluated.

OBJECTIVES: Limited studies examine INR fluctuations using pharmacokinetic models or in vivo INR values in patients concomitantly taking tirzepatide and warfarin, though case reports suggest potential indirect impact on INR trends. Further evidence of the drug interaction between glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) agonists and warfarin is necessary.

CASE SUMMARY: The use of the GLP-1/GIP agonist tirzepatide is increasing due to its robust efficacy in weight loss and cardiometabolic risk reduction. However, drug interactions resulting from its pharmacologic effects have not been thoroughly evaluated. Warfarin is an anticoagulant with a narrow therapeutic index that requires therapeutic drug monitoring. While warfarin prescribing has decreased due to increased affordability of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), it is the most efficacious oral option for anticoagulation for certain populations, including those with left ventricular assist devices (LVAD). This manuscript describes two cases of LVAD patients enrolled in a pharmacist-run anticoagulation clinic who required significant warfarin dose adjustments after tirzepatide initiation. In tandem with the INR challenges coinciding with tirzepatide dose titrations and desired weight loss, these cases highlight real-world issues that impact patient care and warfarin management, including therapy lapses due to prior authorization requirements, antibiotic drug interactions commonly used to treat LVAD driveline infection, and fluctuating dietary vitamin K intake due to drastic appetite suppression with tirzepatide.

PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: The INR fluctuations in both cases can be attributed to several pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic mechanisms at play during concomitant administration of tirzepatide and warfarin, including delayed gastric emptying, plasma protein displacement, appetite suppression, and weight loss. These case reports provide insight into the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic interactions between tirzepatide and warfarin, which required significant dose reductions, as well as attention to external factors like drug shortages and concomitant antibiotic therapy, to maintain therapeutic INR.

articles.title: SMYD2-mediated STAT3 activation promotes GSDME-dependent pyroptosis and fibrosis in cisplatin-induced chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Cisplatin is a cornerstone chemotherapeutic agent for solid malignancies but is limited by dose-dependent nephrotoxicity. GSDME-dependent pyroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) has emerged as a critical driver of subsequent chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although protein methylation within RTECs is implicated in cisplatin-induced renal injury, the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain largely undefined. Here, we established a murine model of cisplatin-induced CKD via repeated low-dose injections and performed in vitro experiments in HK-2 cells. Pharmacological inhibitors (Stattic for STAT3; LLY507 for SMYD2), tubular epithelial cell Smyd2 conditional knockout, and siRNA-mediated knockdown or plasmid-based overexpression were employed to dissect the SMYD2-STAT3-GSDME regulatory axis. Cisplatin concurrently upregulated SMYD2 protein expression and STAT3 tyrosine 705 phosphorylation in RTECs both in vivo and in vitro. STAT3 phosphorylation directly promoted GSDME expression and pyroptosis, whereas its inhibition by stattic significantly ameliorated renal fibrosis. Notably, SMYD2 ablation-whether by LLY507 or genetic knockout-markedly reduced STAT3 phosphorylation and GSDME-dependent pyroptosis, while SMYD2 overexpression exerted opposite effects. Mechanistically, SMYD2 promoted STAT3 Y705 phosphorylation in a K685-dependent manner, enhancing nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity, and this was associated with increased GSDME expression, thereby accelerating pyroptosis and fibrotic progression in CKD. Collectively, these findings establish the SMYD2-STAT3-GSDME axis as a novel mediator of cisplatin-induced CKD and identify SMYD2 as a promising therapeutic target for preventing this debilitating complication.

articles.title: Joint associations of EAT-Lancet diet adherence and ambient air-pollution mixtures with respiratory disease risk: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Whether sustainable dietary patterns and real-world multipollutant exposure are jointly associated with respiratory disease risk remains unclear. We prospectively analysed 64,212 UK Biobank participants with assessment-centre Oxford WebQ data as the primary dietary analysis cohort, with additional analyses incorporating participants with at least one or at least two valid dietary assessments. Adherence to the EAT-Lancet diet was derived from 24-h dietary recall data. For each outcome, an air-pollution mixture score (APS) integrating PM2.5, PM10, PMcoarse, NO2 and NOx was constructed by applying weights estimated from covariate-adjusted weighted quantile sum regression in the corresponding eligible UK Biobank pollution cohort to the dietary analysis cohorts. Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations with incident overall respiratory disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Each 1-SD higher APS was associated with higher risks of overall respiratory disease (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.10) and COPD (HR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.15), but not asthma. Each 1-point higher EAT-Lancet score was associated with lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-0.98) and COPD (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.97), but not asthma. Compared with participants with low EAT-Lancet adherence and high APS, those with high adherence and low APS had lower risks of overall respiratory disease (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.66-0.82), COPD (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.54-0.74), and asthma (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.68-0.95). Formal interaction tests were not statistically significant in the primary analysis, although COPD interaction estimates were consistently positive across dietary analyses, with the strongest evidence among participants with at least one valid dietary assessment (RERI 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.37). Higher EAT-Lancet adherence and lower multipollutant exposure were jointly associated with lower respiratory disease risks, particularly COPD, suggesting that sustainable dietary patterns may complement population-level air-quality policies.

articles.title: Association of BMI with type 2 biomarkers, asthma burden, and severe asthma attack risk: an analysis of control groups of the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis.
authors: Oxford Asthma Attack Risk Scale Meta-analysis (ORACLE2) Consortium
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related asthma is frequently described as a type 2-low phenotype, but data on type 2 biomarker distributions across BMI and their relationship with asthma attack risk are scarce. We aimed to examine the distribution of type 2 biomarkers across BMI categories in adolescents and adults with asthma and to investigate how BMI relates to risk of severe attacks.

METHODS: We analysed data from the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis of control groups of 22 randomised placebo-controlled asthma trials, previously identified through a systematic review of MEDLINE from Jan 1, 1993, to April 1, 2021. We estimated annualised severe asthma attack rate ratios using negative binomial models, adjusted for sex, age, blood eosinophil count (BEC), fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), percent predicted forced expiratory volume in 1 s (ppFEV1), percent predicted forced vital capacity, treatment step, previous severe attacks, and trial.

FINDINGS: In the ORACLE2 patient-level meta-analysis (n=6513), 2393 (37%) of 6513 participants with asthma had overweight (BMI 25 kg/m2 to <30 kg/m2) and 2723 (42%) had obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2). Those with obesity had highest symptom burden, lowest baseline ppFEV1, and were most frequently on Global Initiative for Asthma step 5 treatment. Although the proportion of patients with dual type 2-high biomarkers (BEC ≥0·3 × 109 cells per L and FeNO ≥35 parts per billion) was lower in the obese versus normal BMI group (15% vs 26%; p<0·0001), the proportion of type 2-low asthma (BEC <0·15 × 109 cells per L and FeNO <20 ppb) was higher (18% vs 13%; p<0·0001), indicating that 82% of asthma patients with obesity still have some degree of type 2 inflammation. Compared with normal BMI, severe obesity (BMI ≥40 kg/m2) was associated with a significantly higher asthma attack risk (adjusted rate ratio 1·57, 95% CI 1·06-2·33).

INTERPRETATION: Most patients with obesity-related asthma have evidence of type 2 inflammation despite a modest shift towards type 2-low disease. High BMI is associated with increased asthma burden and attack risk. These findings support a multidimensional view of obesity-associated asthma, in which type 2 inflammation frequently coexists with obesity-related mechanisms that independently contribute to disease burden and asthma attack risk.

FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research, Oxford Biomedical Research Centre, Association Pulmonaire du Québec, Fonds de Recherche du Québec-Santé, Academy of Medical Sciences, and Ghent University Special Research Fund.

articles.title: Multi-biomarker risk score for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis based on serum proteins by the Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium (PROLIFIC): a risk score development and validation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite decades of research, clinicians still do not have approved prognostic biomarkers that can help predict how quickly idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) will progress in individual patients. The Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium (PROLIFIC) was formed to develop well-qualified assays suitable for use as prognostic biomarkers within the context of clinical trials for IPF.

METHODS: For this risk score development and validation study, assays were developed for 12 peripheral blood biomarkers discovered in previous studies, representing epithelial damage (CYFRA 21-1, SP-D, CA-125, CA-19-9, and KL-6), fibrosis (MMP-7, TNC, and POSTN), inflammation (CCL18, CXCL13, and sICAM-1), and thrombosis (PAI-1), and used for IPF patient baseline serum measurements within the derivation dataset (Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation [PFF] Patient Registry; n=657) and the validation dataset (placebo groups of the ISABELA studies; n=229). The PFF Patient Registry enrolled patients in the USA (start date March 29, 2016; data cutoff Nov 30, 2022). ISABELA 1 (NCT03711162) enrolled patients in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, Chile, Czechia, Denmark, Germany, Greece, Japan, Peru, Spain, Taiwan, Türkiye, the UK, and the USA (start date Nov 28, 2018; completed March 30, 2021). ISABELA 2 (NCT03733444) enrolled patients in Argentina, Canada, France, Germany, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Poland, South Africa, South Korea, and the USA (start date Nov 5, 2018; completed March 30, 2021). Single and multi-marker statistical analyses were performed for transplant-free survival and forced vital capacity (FVC) decline at 1 year, adjusting for sex, age, BMI, antifibrotic medication, smoking pack-years, percent predicted FVC (ppFVC), and percent predicted diffusion capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide. Penalised logistic regression was used to select prognostic biomarkers using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator method, and the resulting model was used to derive a multi-marker risk score. The performance of the PROLIFIC risk score was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and by the sensitivity and specificity of the Youden Index.

FINDINGS: In 657 participants in the PFF Patient Registry IPF derivation cohort, the mean age was 70·69 years (SD 8·08), 168 (26%) were female, 489 (74%) were male, 617 (94%) were White, ten (2%) were Black, 14 (2%) were Asian, and 16 (2%) were other race. A 10% or higher absolute decline of ppFVC within 1 year occurred in 20 (3%) of 657 patients. Overall longitudinal FVC decline was significantly associated with baseline MMP-7, SP-D, KL-6, PAI-1, CA19-9, CYFRA 21-1, CXCL13, and sICAM-1. Death (62 [9%] of 657 patients) or lung transplant (37 [6%] of 657 patients) within 1 year was significantly associated with baseline SP-D, sICAM-1, TNC, and KL-6. A multi-marker prognostic model or PROLIFIC risk score for the composite outcome of death, lung transplant, or at least 10% absolute decline in ppFVC at 1 year was associated with baseline SP-D, CXCL13, sICAM-1, TNC, and CA-125 (derivation area under the curve [AUC] 0·809 [95% CI 0·763-0·855]; Youden Index sensitivity 0·643 and specificity 0·847). In 229 participants in the ISABELA study validation cohort, the mean age was 70·08 years (SD 6·79), 36 (16%) were female, 193 (84%) were male, 168 (73%) were White, one (<1%) was Black, 53 (23%) were Asian, and 7 (3%) were other race. A 10% or higher absolute decline of ppFVC occurred in 31 (14%) of 229 patients, death in six (3%) of 229 patients, and lung transplant in zero patients within 1 year. The performance of the PROLIFIC risk score was tested in this validation cohort (AUC 0·711 [95% CI 0·614-0·808]; Youden Index sensitivity 0·820 and specificity 0·430).

INTERPRETATION: A multi-marker algorithm confirmed the important serum proteins consistent with findings from previous analyses and yielded a patient-level prognostic risk score for transplant-free survival and FVC decline in IPF. The PROLIFIC risk score has been accepted into the US Food and Drug Administration Biomarker Qualification Program as a prognostic biomarker in patients with IPF to identify patients who are more likely to have clinical events or disease progression within 1 year and to be used as a stratification factor or as an eligibility criterion in clinical trials.

FUNDING: The Prognostic Lung Fibrosis Consortium.

articles.title: Obesity and asthma: rethinking the type 2 immune landscape.
Kinetics of myxovirus resistance protein A in adults with influenza and SARS-CoV-2 infection in the outpatient setting: a prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory viral infections have few virus-specific biomarkers, with current monitoring relying on subjective symptoms and non-specific biomarkers (procalcitonin and C-reactive protein). Myxovirus resistance protein A (MxA), a virus-specific biomarker, has shown rapid induction (1-2 h) and a moderate half-life (approximately 2·3 days) in experimental studies, but its protein-level kinetics remain poorly characterised in individuals with naturally acquired respiratory viral infections. We investigated MxA temporal kinetics in these patients, evaluated its potential as a biomarker for monitoring infection resolution, and assessed antiviral treatment efficacy in individuals with influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infection.

METHODS: This single-centre, prospective cohort study enrolled adult outpatients (aged ≥18 years) with acute respiratory viral infections from the outpatient clinic at China-Japan Friendship Hospital in Beijing between Dec 11, 2023, and March 14, 2024, with 2-3 follow-up visits within 14 days. Patients were included if they presented with at least two respiratory symptoms with a symptom duration of seven days or less. Exclusion criteria included interferon therapy within 30 days, major surgery, myocardial infarction or stroke, substantial trauma or burns, vaccination within 30 days, or unavailable study samples. Viral pathogens included influenza, SARS-CoV-2, rhinovirus, human coronaviruses, respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and enterovirus. Peripheral blood samples were collected, and MxA levels were measured quantitatively using a fluorescence immunochromatography assay. Symptom severity, virological data, and antiviral treatment regimens were documented. Generalised estimating equation (GEE) models were used to assess the dynamic relationships between MxA levels, viral reads measured by multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing (mp-tNGS), and symptom severity, and the effects of antiviral treatments on MxA trajectories.

FINDINGS: A total of 201 outpatients with respiratory viral infections (59 influenza A, 43 influenza B, 78 SARS-CoV-2, 21 other viruses) with a median age of 34 years (41 for SARS-CoV-2) were included in this study. MxA levels were high on the day of symptom onset (median 116·0 ng/mL; IQR 84·7-166·0), peaked around day 2, and gradually decreased, falling below 50 ng/mL by day 10. SARS-CoV-2 showed significantly faster MxA decline than did influenza (p<0·0001). Multivariable GEE models showed that longitudinal changes in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS correlated positively and significantly with MxA levels (estimate=18·0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 10·4-25·7; p<0·0001). MxA correlated with mean total symptom scores (estimate=0·0029; 95% CI, 0·0018-0·0041; p<0·0001) and systemic symptom scores (estimate=0·0045; 95% CI, 0·0029-0·0060; p<0·0001), with strongest associations in the early infection phase. MxA levels also correlated positively with the mean respiratory symptom scores (estimate=0·0023; 95% CI, 0·0009-0·0038; p=0·0015). In individuals with influenza B, MxA levels declined significantly faster when treated with baloxavir compared with oseltamivir (estimate=-10·8; 95% CI, -17·1 to -4·5; p=0·0008). This faster decline trend aligned with changes observed in viral reads measured by mp-tNGS and clinical symptom improvement. In individuals with SARS-CoV-2, those receiving no antiviral therapy showed significantly slower MxA decline (p=0·022). Among patients with lower respiratory viral infections who experienced fever within 48 h of blood sampling (n=48), higher baseline MxA independently associated with increased in-hospital mortality (odds ratio 1·004; 95% CI, 1·001-1·008).

INTERPRETATION: Our findings indicate that temporal changes in MxA levels correlate closely with viral load and symptom severity, suggesting that MxA could serve as a potential biomarker for monitoring infection resolution in respiratory viral infections. MxA decline is slower than viral load clearance (days 7-8), which may partially reflect its half-life; MxA levels generally fell below 50 ng/mL by day 10 after symptom onset, supporting its potential utility for monitoring infection resolution. Combining MxA with viral load testing provides a more comprehensive disease assessment. Additionally, MxA could help to guide antiviral management, although further validation is required. Limitations include small subgroup sample sizes, variable enrolment timing, low participant retention, and exclusion of immunosuppressed patients.

FUNDING: Beijing Research Ward Excellence Program, Department of Emergency Response, National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, China-Japan Friendship Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, National Natural Science Foundation of China, Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases-National Science and Technology Major Project, Zybio, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences (CAMS) Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences, and New Cornerstone Science Foundation. Materials for MxA measurements were provided by Zybio.

articles.title: Lactate infusion as therapeutic strategy in critically ill patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: RESuscitation of Critically ill patients Using hypErtonic LACtate (RESCUE-LAC) Collaborators
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Administering lactate to critically ill patients or patients undergoing major surgery may improve hemodynamics, reduce intracranial pressure and decrease fluid requirements. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to analyze whether these beneficial effects also translate into mortality reduction.

METHODS: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing lactate infusion against any control in adult patients having critical illness or undergoing major surgery. Primary outcome was mortality at the last reported follow-up. Data on other clinical outcomes (length of stay, survival with good neurological outcome, adverse events), and hemodynamic data (heart rate, blood pressure, cardiac output, fluid balance) were also extracted.

RESULTS: A total of ten RCTs with a total of 763 patients were included. All studies investigated hypertonic sodium lactate (HSL), compared against isotonic or hypertonic fluids. Investigated settings included acute cardiovascular care (cardiac and aortic surgery, acute heart failure), severe burn injury and traumatic brain injury. Mortality was similar in all settings but has to be taken as hypothesis generating due to the very low number of trials. We found no difference in other secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypertonic sodium lactate did not demonstrate a mortality difference, but administering HSL appeared to be safe, as no adverse events were reported. Overall, our findings have to be considered hypothesis-generating rather than practice changing due to the very small sample size and different populations.

STUDY REGISTRATION: International prospective register of systematic reviews, PROSPERO registration no. CRD420251124739.

articles.title: Global variability in ICU sedation practices: Does it matter?
articles.abstract: Sedative and opioid infusions are commonly administered to promote patient comfort and safety, and to facilitate mechanical ventilation of adult patients in the intensive care unit (ICU). Sedation guidelines promote use of the ABCDEF bundle that incorporates an analgesia-first approach, maintains light sedation through protocolization and/or spontaneous awakening trials, avoids benzodiazepines and promotes use of dexmedetomidine (vs. propofol) for patients at high risk for delirium or who are failing spontaneous breathing trials due to agitation. This narrative review identifies substantial variability in the use of the ABCDEF bundle, and the guideline-recommended sedation practices embedded in it, between different ICU populations, ICUs within and across health systems, and between different countries and regions. The application of the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) explains factors influencing this variability including the sedation intervention itself, external influences on the ICU, organization of the ICU, clinician knowledge and experience, and activities needed to sustain change. Strategies to address barriers for implementing evidence-based ICU sedation management and reduce identified global variability are proposed to improve the outcomes of mechanically ventilated adults admitted to the ICU.

articles.title: Feeling Lost: Family perceptions of gaps in bereavement care following a child's sudden and unexpected death in the PICU.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A minority of families experience the death of a child in a Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) setting from unexpected causes, such as sepsis, or trauma. For these families, the sudden shock of their child's death can increase the likelihood of complex grief responses, such as post-traumatic stress and prolonged grief disorder. However, systematic bereavement follow-up services to support their grief are currently lacking.

AIM: To understand family perspectives on gaps in bereavement support to inform the development of a PICU bereavement service.

METHODS: A single site qualitative study was conducted following a constructivist approach, underpinned by meaning reconstruction theory. Adult relatives of children who had died unexpectedly in the PICU in the past five years participated in semi-structured focus groups and interviews. Data analysis followed a thematic approach.

FINDINGS: Fifteen participants (four fathers, 10 mothers and one close family friend) participated in two focus groups and two interviews. Six themes were developed around a central concept of feeling lost: 1) harmful communication, 2) unresolved grief roadblocks, 3) searching and finding nothing, 4) coronial complexities, 5) financial burden, and 6) caregivers needing care.

CONCLUSION: Families felt lost following their child's unexpected death, and bereavement care was fragmented, difficult to find and often unsuitable. Further research and service improvements are needed to better support all family members after the unexpected death of a child in a PICU.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Clinicians should establish trusting relationships with families before initiating bereavement contact, and ensure communication is agreed upon. Families may benefit from alternatives to medical bereavement meetings held in hospital to unpack their questions and concerns. Clinicians should provide practical guidance on navigating available grief supports, considering all family members' needs while acknowledging financial constraints. Many families find the coronial process challenging and require ongoing support.

articles.title: What nurses should not do when managing the PiCCO haemodynamic monitoring system in critically ill adults: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map the errors that critical care nurses should avoid when managing the 5 PiCCO system in critically ill adults, trace each error to its supporting sources and classify the type of evidence behind it.

METHODOLOGY: Scoping review (Arksey and O'Malley; Levac et al.) reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Records from PubMed (without nursing or age filters, validated against six known sources), Scopus, CINAHL, Cuiden, Dialnet, ENFISPO and SciELO were screened 10 independently by two reviewers; manufacturer documentation was searched, and sources from an earlier search phase were re-assessed. Each item was classified by evidence type.

RESULTS: Fifty-eight sources were included: 20 retained from the earlier search phase, 36 from the database searches, one manufacturer document and one nursing article found on a journal website. Thirty-one "Not-to-Do" items were mapped across seven competency domains; 15 configuration and calibration account for 12 items, and two items rest only on indirect evidence. Recalibration should follow clinical need or change in the pulse contour signal rather than a fixed interval.

CONCLUSIONS: The largest share of the mapped items concerns configuration and calibration, upstream of parameter interpretation; how often these errors occur in practice is unknown. 20.

articles.title: From Plasma to Plaque: Pathway-Anchored Proteomics and the Search for Coronary Subphenotypes.
Renal Response to a Dual Vasopressin Antagonist in Acute Heart Failure: Post-Hoc Analysis From AVANTI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The dual vasopressin 1a/2 receptor antagonist pecavaptan improved congestion on the short term, but the effect was not maintained at 30 days in patients hospitalized with heart failure (HF). Little is known about the renal effects of vasopressin antagonists in patients with HF.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to investigate the effects of pecavaptan related to kidney function.

METHODS: The AVANTI trial randomized hospitalized HF patients with residual congestion to 30 mg pecavaptan or placebo adjunctive to standard of care. Changes in kidney function and treatment response according to estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 438 patients (baseline eGFR 53 mL/min/1.73 m2 [IQR: 42-68]), pecavaptan relative to placebo decreased eGFR (difference in change -3.67 mL/min/1.73 m2 [95% CI: -6.38 to -0.96]; P = 0.008) and increased urine albumin-creatinine ratio (log-transformed difference 0.47 [95% CI: 0.12-0.83]; P = 0.009) from baseline to day 30. In contrast, treatment with pecavaptan relative to placebo showed a trend towards reduction in blood urea nitrogen (BUN) (log-transformed difference -0.07 [95% CI: -0.15 to 0.01]; P = 0.079) at day 30. Baseline kidney function did not modify the treatment effect of pecavaptan on weight loss at day 7 and 30 (P interaction = 0.694 and 0.778).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized with HF, pecavaptan relative to placebo decreased eGFR, increased urine albumin-creatinine ratio, and showed a trend toward reduction in BUN. Baseline kidney function did not modify the effect of pecavaptan on weight loss. While the decline in eGFR and BUN likely reflect reversible hemodynamic and direct drug-mediated effects, respectively, further research is needed to establish the renal safety of dual vasopressin receptor antagonists in HF patients. (A Trial to Study BAY1753011 in Patients With Congestive Heart Failure [AVANTI]; NCT03901729).

articles.title: Forging the Interventional Heart Failure Specialist: A JACC: Advances Expert Panel.
articles.abstract: Interventional heart failure (IHF) integrates advanced heart failure management with catheter-based procedural expertise to address clinical scenarios that neither interventional cardiology nor advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology can optimally manage alone. Despite growing clinical need, no standardized training pathway, competency framework, or workforce infrastructure exists. This Expert Panel proposes a comprehensive framework comprising: a core-and-track taxonomy defining 5 universal competency clusters and 5 procedural track domains; 13 clinical activities structured using entrustable professional activity methodology as pathway-agnostic training endpoints; multiple training pathways evaluated against shared competency benchmarks; and implementation guidance including a three-phase pilot-to-accreditation strategy, consortium models, hybrid compensation structures, and a minimum viable registry to generate comparative effectiveness evidence. Realization requires multisociety consensus, pilot program data, and collective commitment to building the training and evidence infrastructure needed to advance interventional heart failure toward recognized subspecialty status.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Adiposity-related evidence for APOA2, FTO, and MC4R: a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of recent human studies (2019-2025)" [Diabetes & Metab Syndr: Clinic Res Revs 20(9) (2026) 103498].
Impact of Atrial Fibrillation on the Association Between Shock Index and Trauma Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Trauma remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with hemorrhagic shock as the most common cause of preventable traumatic death. Shock Index (SI) (heart rate/systolic blood pressure) is a clinical marker of hemodynamic instability associated with an increased risk of massive transfusion, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and mortality. However, SI interpretation may be confounded in patients with atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter ( collectively, AF), whose baseline tachycardia can distort SI values independent of true hemodynamic compromise.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included adult trauma patients (≥18 y) admitted to a level I trauma center between January 2020 and October 2025. We excluded patients with missing discharge status or vital signs. We determined AF status from admission documentation and prior medical history. Collected variables included age, sex, injury mechanism, Injury Severity Score, and admission SI. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital and ICU length of stay (LOS). Group comparisons used chi-square and Student's t-tests. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors independently associated with mortality; linear regression examined associations between AF, SI, and resource utilization, adjusting for age, sex, Injury Severity Score, mechanism, and SI category.

RESULTS: Among 14,553 trauma patients, 1012 (7%) had AF. AF patients were older (median 77 versus 46 y), more often females (48.9% versus 36.2%), and predominantly sustained blunt trauma via ground-level falls (78.1% versus 26.9%; all P < 0.001). AF was not independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.03, 95% confidence interval 0.68-1.57; P = 0.882). SI ≥ 1.30 remained independently associated with mortality in AF patients (adjusted odds ratio 3.73, 95% confidence interval 1.16-11.97; P = 0.027). AF was independently associated with longer hospital LOS (+1.91 d) and ICU LOS (+1.14 d; both P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite underlying rhythm irregularity, elevated SI remained independently associated with mortality in AF trauma patients. SI can still be used as a diagnostic data point in clinical decision-making for these complex patients.

articles.title: Pemafibrate attenuates hepatic lipid droplet accumulation through peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα)-mediated activation of ketogenesis.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is an increasing global health burden, yet pharmacological therapies addressing its metabolic basis remain limited. Here, we show that pemafibrate, a selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-α (PPARα) modulator, attenuates histologically assessed hepatic lipid droplet accumulation in a mouse model of MASLD induced by obesity and hypertension. This reduction in hepatic lipid droplet accumulation was accompanied by enhanced hepatic ketogenesis and was attenuated in hepatocyte-specific Hmgcs2-deficient (Hmgcs2ΔHep) mice. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that pemafibrate upregulates genes involved in fatty acid metabolism, oxidative phosphorylation, and ketogenesis. Notably, these responses appear to involve hepatocyte-autonomous mechanisms and pemafibrate-induced upregulation of Hmgcs2. Collectively, our findings identify hepatic ketogenesis as an important downstream mediator of pemafibrate action in MASLD and provide mechanistic insight into how pemafibrate modulates hepatic lipid droplet accumulation and metabolic pathways in MASLD. These results highlight ketone body metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic liver disease.

articles.title: Incremental value of [18F]FDG PET/CT for [177Lu]Lu-PSMA therapy selection in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: We assessed how discordance definition, clinical selection, and denominator construction affect estimates of the additional information provided by [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT before therapy with [177Lu]Lu-labeled ligands targeting prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA). Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science were searched through 13 July 2026. Thirty-two reports were retained. Revision-stage analyses separated protocol-screening exclusions, clinical-referral discordance, imaging-phenotyping cohorts, and retrospective classification of treated patients. Exploratory binomial-logit-normal models used adaptive integration and profile-likelihood confidence intervals, with alternative-model and leave-one-out checks. Adjusted survival associations were analyzed separately from treatment-predictive effects. Discordance-attributed screen failures were 0/18, 8/75 and 51/291 in three protocol-screening cohorts; their exploratory summary was 12.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.6%-23.0%). Three clinical-referral cohorts reported 16/89, 56/298 and 29/70, while a separate imaging-phenotyping cohort reported 45/98. Reconstructed trial-screening denominators yielded an exploratory additional-exclusion estimate of 14.4% (95% CI 1.8%-25.4%). A VISION-like referral reread identified additional discordance in 3/71 patients. Retrospective treated-cohort classifications of 3/26 and 24/75 were not interpreted as prospectively observed exclusions. Three heterogeneous adjusted survival estimates showed an adverse association (exploratory hazard ratio 3.81, 95% CI 1.03-14.02), but differed in exposure and adjustment. Dual-tracer findings identify heterogeneous disease and adverse prognosis, but current evidence does not validate either universal or risk-adapted FDG screening, or demonstrate that excluding discordant patients from radioligand therapy improves outcomes.

articles.title: Acute inflammatory responses to hyperinsulinemia, hypoglycemia, and hyperglycemia in individuals with and without type 2 diabetes: a clamp-based proteomic study.
articles.abstract: Obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic low-grade inflammation are intricately linked, yet whether inflammatory responses to acute metabolic perturbations differ in T2D remains incompletely characterized.
