We investigated broad inflammatory responses to hyperinsulinemia, hypoglycemia, and hyperglycemia under clamp conditions in eleven individuals with T2D and eleven controls (CON), well balanced by age, sex and BMI, using a 92-plex proximity extension assay. In both groups, hyperinsulinemia, hypoglycemia, and hyperglycemia led to a predominant suppression of circulating inflammatory markers, with reductions observed in 4, 12, and 26 of 71 fully evaluable proteins, respectively. By contrast, FGF-21 and IL-6 increased similarly in the hypo- and hyperglycemic conditions. Inflammatory responses to hyperinsulinemia and hypoglycemia were largely similar between groups. However, during hyperglycemia, suppression of inflammatory markers was generally attenuated in T2D compared with CON, with group differences observed for 6 of 71 markers including SIRT2, STAMBP, and TNFSF14, none of which survived multiplicity correction. Adjusted analyses suggested that this attenuated immunosuppression was explained by lower achieved insulin levels in T2D, with a lesser contribution from sympathetic dominance of the autonomic nervous system. These findings suggest that the anti-inflammatory actions of insulin dominate the acute inflammatory response to metabolic perturbations across the glycemic range within the investigated time frames. The attenuation of this response in T2D, partly attributable to relative beta-cell failure, may result in an excess proinflammatory burden during everyday postprandial glucose excursions, potentially contributing to vascular complications and supporting a therapeutic target for treatments that restore prandial insulin action.

articles.title: Detector-side neural timing calibration for TOF-PET from coincidence supervision.
articles.abstract: Machine-learning methods can model non-linear event-dependent timing effects in time-of-flight positron emission tomography (TOF-PET), but calibration measurements naturally provide timing supervision only at the coincidence-level rather than for individual detector interactions. We investigate whether coincidence measurements can be used to learn reusable detector-side timing calibration functions without individually labelled interaction times.Approach: A shared detector-conditioned neural network independently processes each single-event readout and predicts a detector-side timing correction and variance contribution. During training, two detector-side timing estimates are differenced and compared with the geometrically expected time difference obtained from point-source coincidence measurements. We evaluate the method on three heterogeneous PET systems against conventional time-skew and time-walk calibration and matched direct coincidence-level neural models.Main results: Under a common energy-window setting, the proposed model reduced coincidence timing resolution from 321.7 to 263.0ps, 462.4 to 431.7ps, and 417.0 to 382.0ps relative to charge-based time-walk correction on the three systems. In detector-pair holdout experiments, detector-side models achieved comparable or slightly better timing performance than direct coincidence-level neural models while retaining independently applicable singles-level outputs. The learned calibration generalized to unseen source positions and detector pairs, enabled recombination of independently trained scanner components after scalar timing-reference alignment, provided event-wise coincidence-timing uncertainty stratification in both full-ring systems, and remained compatible with low-precision inference after quantization-aware training.Significance: Coincidence supervision enables reusable detector-side timing corrections that improve CTR without single-event timing labels. This preserves a singles-level calibration interface while enabling machine-learning-based nonlinear timing correction, modular scanner calibration, and event-specific coincidence-timing uncertainty estimates.

articles.title: PRISM: a physics-informed spatiotemporal convolutional network for interaction localisation in continuous annular nanocomposite PET scintillators.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Continuous annular positron emission tomography (PET) detectors moulded from nanocomposite scintillators such as LaF 3 :Ce in polystyrene could substantially reduce fabrication cost relative to discrete-crystal arrays, but strong optical (Rayleigh) scattering and coincidence label ambiguity make recovery of the first point of interaction (FPoI) a severely ill-posed inverse problem. We investigated whether embedding scanner topology and coincidence physics into the network itself renders it tractable.

APPROACH: PRISM (Physics-informed Regression of Interactions in Scintillating Monoliths) is a spatiotemporal convolutional network that treats dual-surface photodetector readout as a short burst of time-binned cylindrical intensity maps (five 10 ns frames). It applies circular padding azimuthally to respect cylindrical topology, injects positional and radial depth-ratio channels, and is trained with a virtual cylinder-aware loss combining permutation-invariant coincidence regression with boundary constraints and a polar-weighted auxiliary term. A LaF 3 :Ce/polystyrene scanner (42.9 mm mean radial thickness, 296 mm axial field of view) was modelled in OpenGATE; 8 587 880 18 F decays yielded 735 230 labelled bursts.

MAIN RESULTS: On a held-out set, PRISM achieved a median three-dimensional FPoI error of 8.26 mm (mean 10.33 mm; 90th percentile 19.4 mm), a threefold reduction relative to physics-agnostic backbones under an identical input representation (ResNet-18: 25.61 mm median), with fewer trainable parameters. Restricting evaluation to the inner half of the annulus reduced the median to 6.67 mm.

SIGNIFICANCE: Embedding cylindrical continuity and coincidence-permutation invariance materially improves localisation in strongly scattering monolithic annular detectors, supporting the feasibility of low-cost continuous-shell nanocomposite PET.

articles.title: Implementing Digital Mental Health Interventions for Children and Young People in Emergency Care Settings: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency departments play a central role in crisis management for children and young people's (CYP) mental health. These settings face significant challenges in delivering effective support, such as shortages of mental health specialists, long waiting times, and overcrowding. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) may have the potential to expand access to care, bridge service gaps, and alleviate pressure on emergency settings for CYP experiencing mental health crises.

OBJECTIVE: This review systematically reviews the current evidence for the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness of DMHIs for CYP in emergency care settings.

METHODS: We conducted database searches using APA PsycInfo, Embase, MEDLINE, and Web of Science from January 2015 to September 2025. We included quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods studies that related to the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness of DMHIs in acute settings. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility were added as post hoc outcomes for this secondary review after implementation-related evidence was identified in the original search. DMHIs included telepsychiatry, phone calls, SMS text messaging, and computerized interventions. In addition to studies reporting data from CYP under the age of 25 years, we included those evaluating data from caregivers and care providers. All selected studies were assessed for quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.

RESULTS: Overall, 6778 articles were retrieved from the database searches, of which 13 articles met the inclusion criteria. In total, data from 1495 patients, of whom 1048 received a DMHI, 413 caregivers, and 250 care providers were included across studies, excluding 1 study that did not report the sample size for care providers. Mental health presentations included depressive symptoms, violent behaviors, suicidal ideation and attempts, intoxication, and multiple mental health conditions. DMHIs were broadly acceptable, particularly for interventions such as telepsychiatry and structured follow-up phone calls. Feasibility, appropriateness, and cost-effectiveness outcomes were more varied. These were affected by the specific intervention design, emergency care context, and user characteristics. CYP valued computerized interventions that incorporated age-appropriate design and language; telepsychiatry, phone calls, and automated SMS text messaging interventions that enabled continued support and connectedness with health care professionals; and interventions delivered at appropriate intervals. Conversely, health care providers raised concerns about increasing workloads for interventions that required specialist facilitation. Electronic cognitive behavioral therapy was viewed as more appropriate for CYP with prior therapy experience, and SMS text messaging intervention outcomes were limited in CYP with histories of behavioral violence.

CONCLUSIONS: DMHIs show promise in supporting the mental health care needs of CYP in emergency care settings. CYP, caregivers, and care providers demonstrated a willingness to use these tools, but careful consideration is needed to improve the appropriateness and feasibility of these interventions. More diverse studies are needed to explore these findings in different contexts and to address existing shortcomings to support the implementation of DMHIs.

articles.title: Generative AI Chatbot Responses to Suicide and Self-Harm: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A growing number of US adults and youth confide in generative AI chatbots for mental health support, including disclosure of suicide and self-harm risk. While chatbot response quality, safety, and effectiveness could impact population-level suicide and self-harm rates, there are no systematic reviews of this burgeoning literature.

OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review of studies evaluating generative AI chatbot responses to disclosure of suicide and self-harm risk.

METHODS: We followed PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 and PRISMA-S (PRISMA literature search extension) guidelines and preregistered the protocol on the Open Science Framework. We included English-language, peer-reviewed publications and preprints from 2020 to 2025 that empirically evaluated generative AI conversational responses to suicidal ideation, suicidal or nonsuicidal self-harm, or suicide-planning content. Eligible designs included audits, chatbot development, and adversarial "jailbreaking" studies. We excluded nongenerative systems, clinician-training tools, and prediction-only models. The final database searches were run from December 18 to 23, 2025 (PubMed, Embase, APA PsycINFO, IEEE Xplore, arXiv, and OSF Preprints). On July 26, 2026, publication status was rechecked to update preprint vs published classification. After deduplication, titles/abstracts and full texts were independently screened by 2 reviewers, with discrepancies resolved by consensus. Methodological quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018. We conducted a narrative synthesis across 7 safety domains and 5 AI classifications (proprietary, open-weight, companions, clinical, and study-specific).

RESULTS: Of 1042 deduplicated records, 126 full texts were reviewed, and 29 were included (16 published; 13 preprints). Most studies evaluated suicidal content only (21/29). Twenty were solely audit studies, 2 chatbot development, and 1 jailbreaking. The rest combined approaches. Most used synthetic, single-turn prompts; only 6 used multiturn conversations. Most studies evaluated ≥2 of our 5 AI classifications (17/29). Proprietary models were included most frequently (23/29). When compared, proprietary models (eg, ChatGPT and Claude) tended to provide higher-quality responses than open-weight models (eg, Llama and DeepSeek) and many companions (eg, Replika and Character.AI); however, this trend weakened with sensitivity analysis. Chatbots generally performed well on emotional support, but responses were often generic and lacked context. Chatbots rarely assessed suicide or self-harm risk and performed most poorly when disclosure was ambiguous or moderate. Responses were inconsistent, often requiring multiple turns before referral to crisis resources or human support. Overtly harmful responses were rare under standard conditions but common under jailbreaking.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence is limited by the proportion of preprints, variable quality, synthetic single-turn prompts, small samples, heterogeneous outcomes, and rapid model versioning. Nonetheless, current chatbots tend to provide validation but struggle to escalate care, assess risk, and resist jailbreaking. Research is needed on stakeholder perspectives and on the short- and long-term clinical impact of chatbot responses using follow-up assessments in real-world or clinical settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: OSF Registries osf.io/7fz95; https://osf.io/7fz95.

articles.title: Accuracy of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Assessment by Noncardiologists E-Point Septal Separation and Teichholz Methods: Simulation-Based Pre-Post Training Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) enables rapid bedside estimation of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) in the emergency department. Among quantitative methods, E-point septal separation (EPSS) and Teichholz-derived calculations are commonly used; however, their comparative accuracy when performed by noncardiologist clinicians remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the accuracy and efficiency of EPSS and Teichholz-based methods for LVEF assessment by emergency department physicians, using the Simpson biplane method as the reference standard.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective pre-post interventional study using standardized patients (SPs) at a university simulation training unit (March 2025). Following prerecorded lectures and demonstration videos, emergency department physicians (n=26) measured LVEF using three bedside methods-EPSS, Teichholz long-axis, and Teichholz short-axis-before and after a focused hands-on training session including supervised image acquisition and guided LVEF measurement. Five SPs with cardiologist-confirmed LVEF values ranging from 16% to 73% were used across the study assessments. The primary outcome was the absolute difference between participant-measured and reference LVEF. Secondary outcomes included time-to-completion and participant-reported confidence for each method.

RESULTS: Before training, EPSS demonstrated a significantly lower absolute error (median 5 percentage points, IQR 3-13) compared with Teichholz long-axis (17 percentage points, IQR 9-27) and Teichholz short-axis (13 percentage points, IQR 4-24) methods (P=.009). EPSS also required less time (median 73 seconds, IQR 53-121) than Teichholz long-axis (150 seconds, IQR 103-200) and Teichholz short-axis (100 seconds, IQR 67-184) (P=.02). After training, no statistically significant difference in absolute LVEF error was detected among methods in the preserved-LVEF assessment (P=.93). In the posttraining reduced-LVEF assessment, no statistically significant difference in absolute LVEF error was detected among methods in the SP with an LVEF of 48% (P=.48). In contrast, in the single SP with an LVEF of 16%, absolute LVEF error differed significantly among methods (P=.008), with greater error for EPSS (median 30.5 percentage points) than for Teichholz long-axis (11 percentage points) and Teichholz short-axis (8 percentage points). EPSS remained the fastest technique in preserved (62 seconds; P<.001) and reduced LVEF cases (79 seconds; P<.001). Confidence scores improved across all methods, with EPSS demonstrating the highest median posttraining confidence (P=.01). Greater variability in EPSS measurements was observed in reduced LVEF, with a mean bias of -16 (SD 23) percentage points and wide 95% limits of agreement from -61.1 to 29.1.

CONCLUSIONS: Following focused ultrasound training, no statistically significant difference in absolute LVEF error was detected among methods in the preserved-LVEF assessment or in the SP with an LVEF of 48%. However, EPSS demonstrated greater error than both Teichholz methods in the single SP with an LVEF of 16%, a case-specific finding that should be considered hypothesis-generating. EPSS required less time to perform and was associated with higher learner confidence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20250123008; https://tinyurl.com/3kphcru3.

articles.title: Integrating Multidimensional Clinical Data to Develop a Visual Nomogram for Individualized Prediction of Postinfectious Bone Loss in Patients With Spinal Infection: Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postinfectious bone loss can lead to spinal instability and severe neurological complications, with potentially devastating outcomes. However, prognostic models to support individualized risk assessment remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and internally validate a visual nomogram integrating multimodal clinical data to estimate postinfectious bone loss risk in patients with spinal infection and inform individualized monitoring strategies.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used consecutive sampling at Shandong Public Health Clinical Center. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were extracted from medical records. Eligible patients had confirmed spinal infection, a baseline vertebral bone destruction height ratio less than one-third, and complete baseline and follow-up data. Postinfectious bone loss was defined as a height ratio greater than or equal to one-third on computed tomography 12 months after baseline. Predictors were selected from 31 baseline variables using univariable logistic regression followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to construct the nomogram. Internal validation used 500 bootstrap resamples, repeating all predictor selection and model-fitting steps. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve analysis.

RESULTS: Postinfectious bone loss occurred in 48.9% (109/223, 95% CI 42.4%-55.4%) of patients. The nomogram combined infection characteristics (multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and infected spinal segment), skeletal status (osteoporosis), and laboratory markers (interleukin-6, albumin, and plasma fibrinogen) to estimate individual risk. In the multivariable model, the odds ratios (ORs) were 2.718 (95% CI 0.993-7.444; P=.05) for multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and 7.345 (95% CI 2.757-19.570; P<.001) for osteoporosis. Relative to cervical infection, ORs were 14.041 (95% CI 1.079-182.662; P=.04) for thoracic, 28.876 (95% CI 2.648-314.895; P=.006) for lumbar, and 12.604 (95% CI 0.436-364.075; P=.14) for thoracolumbar infection. Per unit increase, ORs were 1.004 (95% CI 0.996-1.012; P=.30) for interleukin-6 (pg/mL), 3.673 (95% CI 2.410-5.598; P<.001) for plasma fibrinogen (g/L), and 0.834 (95% CI 0.749-0.929; P=.001) for albumin (g/L). Discrimination remained high after optimism correction, with an AUC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.919-0.972), compared with an apparent AUC of 0.954 (95% CI 0.931-0.978). Calibration assessment yielded an intercept of 0.00 (95% CI -0.43 to 0.43) and a slope of 1.00 (95% CI 0.75-1.25), while the Brier score was 0.096 (95% CI 0.064-0.118), indicating close agreement between predicted and observed risks and low overall prediction error.

CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a visual nomogram integrating baseline clinical characteristics, imaging features, and laboratory parameters to predict postinfectious bone loss in patients with spinal infection. Extending previous association studies to individualized risk prediction, the model showed good discrimination and calibration in internal validation. This approach may help identify high-risk patients and inform closer monitoring and timely reassessment before further structural deterioration and neurological complications.

articles.title: Developing a Digital Intervention to Support Parents of Young People Who Self-Harm: A Person-Based Approach Informed by Systematic Review and Qualitative Research.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-harm among children and young people (CYP) is a major public health concern and is associated with increased risk of suicide and ongoing mental health difficulties. Parents frequently play a central role in supporting a young person who self-harms; yet, many report experiencing intense emotional distress, uncertainty, and isolation. Despite this, few interventions have been developed specifically to support parents' own well-being. Existing interventions typically involve parents as part of treatments targeting the young person rather than addressing parents' emotional needs directly.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a digital intervention designed to support the well-being of parents of CYP who self-harm using a Person-Based Approach.

METHODS: Intervention development followed the stages of the Person-Based Approach. Evidence gathering included using an existing systematic review of parents' experiences and development-stage findings from a systematic review of interventions containing components aimed at improving parental well-being in the context of youth self-harm. Qualitative data were collected through interviews, focus groups, and co-design workshops with parents, young people, clinicians, and third-sector professionals to understand user needs and preferences. These findings informed the development of guiding principles and a theory of change. Intervention content was then developed iteratively with input from a parent advisory group. A small alpha test was conducted to identify actionable problems with content, presentation, navigation, emotional burden, and engagement to inform further optimization only.

RESULTS: The systematic review identified few interventions that explicitly targeted parental well-being, with substantial variation in content, delivery, and evaluation. Qualitative findings highlighted parents' needs for support in managing emotional distress, understanding self-harm, responding to their child, and reducing isolation. These insights informed the development of a modular digital intervention including psychoeducation, strategies for managing parental distress, communication guidance, and reflective activities to support well-being. Formative alpha testing generated follow-up feedback from 7 of 12 enrolled parents; 5 provided no follow-up, leaving sustained engagement uncertain. Feedback from completers identified priorities for optimization, particularly around goal-setting content, crisis information, and login burden. Five of the 12 enrolled participants did not provide follow-up data, and reasons for noncompletion were unknown.

CONCLUSIONS: This study describes the development of a digital intervention to support the well-being of parents of CYP who self-harm. Grounded in systematic review evidence, qualitative research, and formative user testing, the intervention addresses an important gap in available support for families affected by youth self-harm. Actionable priorities for further development were identified, with further work needed to establish feasibility and effectiveness.

articles.title: HIV-Related Stigma and Associated Factors Among Rural Older Men in Sichuan Province, China: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing burden of HIV among older adults in China underscores the importance of understanding HIV-related stigma in aging populations. Rural older men may be particularly affected because of limited HIV-related knowledge and educational exposure. However, evidence regarding HIV-related stigma and its associated factors in this population remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess HIV-related stigma among rural older men in Sichuan Province, China, and examine its associations with HIV-related knowledge, educational attainment, economic conditions, and previous exposure to HIV-related education.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Sichuan Province from October 2024 to June 2025. A multistage sampling approach combining random selection of geographic units with convenience recruitment of individual participants at the final stage was used. A total of 526 rural men aged 50 years or older were included in the final analysis. Data were collected through face-to-face administration of structured questionnaires assessing sociodemographic characteristics, HIV-related training, HIV-related knowledge, and HIV-related stigma. Pearson correlation analysis and multivariable logistic regression were used to examine factors associated with HIV-related stigma.

RESULTS: Only 13.3% (70/526) of participants met the criterion for adequate HIV-related knowledge. The mean overall HIV-related stigma score was 3.25 (SD 0.53), with fear of infection being the highest-scoring dimension. HIV-related knowledge scores were negatively correlated with overall HIV-related stigma scores (r=-0.323; P<.001). In multivariable logistic regression, an educational attainment of primary education or below (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.743, 95% CI 1.052-2.888), a monthly income less than 1000 CNY (1 CNY=US $0.15, as of November 9, 2026; aOR 2.936, 95% CI 1.005-8.581), no participation in HIV-related training (aOR 5.267, 95% CI 2.649-10.475), and inadequate HIV-related knowledge (aOR 2.796, 95% CI 1.567-4.990) were independently associated with higher HIV-related stigma.

CONCLUSIONS: Rural older men in Sichuan demonstrated low HIV-related knowledge and substantial HIV-related stigma, particularly fear of infection. Lower educational attainment, lower income, lack of HIV-related training, and inadequate HIV-related knowledge were independently associated with higher stigma. These findings support the need for accessible and culturally appropriate interventions that correct misconceptions about HIV transmission, address fear and social distance toward people living with HIV, and provide up-to-date information on HIV treatment, particularly for rural older men with fewer educational and economic resources.

articles.title: Probable Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Pneumonitis After Combined Ipilimumab-Nivolumab Therapy in a Child: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a rare, life-threatening immune-related adverse event with limited pediatric experience.

OBSERVATIONS: A 16-year-old boy with achondroplasia and renal cell carcinoma developed hypoxemic respiratory failure 4 days after the second ipilimumab-nivolumab cycle and 4 hours after appendectomy. Chest computed tomography showed ground-glass opacities and consolidations. Alternative etiologies were investigated but not supported, although postoperative lung injury and infection could not be excluded. Probable CIP was considered. Intravenous methylprednisolone (2 mg/kg/d) was followed by rapid clinical and radiologic improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: CIP should be considered in postoperative respiratory failure after immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure.

articles.title: Gestational age at diagnosis as a system-derived latency marker rather than a causal mediator in mediation analyses of prenatal decision-making in congenital heart disease.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

articles.title: Early Identification of Patients at Risk of Low Physical Activity After Minor Ischemic Stroke Using Simple Clinical Indicators.
articles.abstract: PurposePhysical activity is associated with stroke recurrence and functional decline; therefore, early identification of patients at risk of reduced physical activity is clinically important. We aimed to examine whether simple clinical indicators obtained during acute hospitalization can identify patients at risk of low physical activity 3 months after discharge following minor ischemic stroke. We conducted a secondary analysis of data from two prospective observational studies that included 134 patients with first-ever minor ischemic stroke. The primary outcome was low daily step count (< 6,025 steps/day) at 3 months after discharge, measured using a triaxial accelerometer.Major FindingsAmong the 134 participants, 73 (54.5%) had a low step count. A shorter 6-min walk distance (odds ratio [OR] 0.992, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.987-0.997; p = 0.002) and nondrinking status (drinker vs. nondrinker: OR 0.342, 95% CI 0.150-0.782; p = 0.011) were independently associated with a low step count. The multivariable logistic regression model demonstrated moderate discrimination (apparent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.763, 95% CI 0.682-0.845), with an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.712 after bootstrap validation.ConclusionSimple clinical indicators obtained during acute hospitalization may help to identify patients at risk of low physical activity after discharge following minor ischemic stroke. However, the model requires further validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Imaging-Based AI vs Radiologists for Preoperative Lymph Node Metastasis in Esophageal Cancer: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging-based AI technologies, particularly deep learning and radiomics, offer a novel approach to improving the accuracy of lymph node metastasis (LNM) diagnosis.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of imaging-based AI models compared with radiologists in detecting preoperative LNM in esophageal cancer (EC).

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted across 5 databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and IEEE Xplore) up to August 19, 2026. Eligible studies assessed imaging-based AI for preoperative LNM detection in EC (pathology reference standard). The protocol was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD420251169109). The PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool with AI) tool was used for quality assessment. Bivariate random-effects models were used to calculate pooled sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (DOR), and area under the curve (AUC); between-study heterogeneity was described using τ² and I² (interpreted descriptively rather than categorically); homogeneity of study effects was tested with the Q statistic, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) were derived for all pooled estimates. Head-to-head comparisons used a random-effects meta-analysis of within-study paired differences (restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment).

RESULTS: A total of 18 studies were included. Across the 17 internal validation sets (2485 participants), AI models demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 0.77 (95% CI 0.73-0.81; 95% PI 0.62-0.87), specificity of 0.79 (95% CI 0.73-0.84; 95% PI 0.48-0.94), a DOR of 12.88 (95% CI 9.57-17.33; 95% PI 4.5-37.0), and an AUC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.81-0.86; 95% PI 0.80-0.86). In the 10 head-to-head studies, AI showed higher sensitivity than radiologists (a paired difference of +0.27, 95% CI 0.11-0.37; 95% PI -0.26 to 0.45; P=.006) and higher discrimination (DOR ratio 4.65, 95% CI 2.53-8.56; 95% PI 0.97-22.42; P<.001), whereas specificity did not differ (+0.06, 95% CI -0.08 to 0.16; 95% PI -0.39 to 0.26; P=.30). Pooled arm-specific AUCs were 0.86 (95% CI 0.82-0.89; 95% PI 0.79-0.91) for AI and 0.67 (95% CI 0.59-0.75; 95% PI 0.44-0.84) for radiologists. In 4 external validation studies, pooled sensitivity was 0.66 (95% CI 0.46-0.81; 95% PI 0.31-0.90), specificity was 0.85 (95% CI 0.75-0.91; 95% PI 0.63-0.94), and the DOR was 10.42 (95% CI 3.50-31.01; 95% PI 0.6-142.0). These estimates remain subject to substantial heterogeneity and design-related bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Imaging-based AI models demonstrated promising pooled diagnostic performance for preoperative LNM detection in EC. By pairing AI with radiologists' performance in the same cohorts, reporting PIs alongside CIs, and separating internal from external validation, this review provides a more realistic assessment than previous average-effect estimates. In predominantly retrospective and heterogeneous cohorts, AI had higher pooled sensitivity and discrimination than radiologists, whereas specificity did not differ; the selective extraction of the model with the highest AUC and very low certainty of evidence precludes conclusions about clinical superiority. These findings support AI as a decision-support tool, warranting prospective, multicenter external validation and prespecified human-AI comparisons rather than replacing radiologists.

articles.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity.
articles.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)-mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

articles.title: Exercise-Mimetic Irisin Nanoplatforms Orchestrate Mitochondrial Integrity and Neuroinflammatory Modulation in Cerebral Ischemic-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, constrained by the narrow therapeutic windows and limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability of neuroprotective agents. Mitochondrial dysfunction and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) are recognized as central pathological drivers of ischemic injury. While exerciese-induced neuroprotection provides promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by difficulties in standardizing exercise regimens and adapting them for patients with mobility impairments. Here, we report a bioinspired nanoplatform that integrates an exercise-mimetic strategy with precision mitochondrial protection to promote neuronal repair. The nanoplatform integrates Angiopep-2-mediated BBB penetration and a phenylboronate-modified multifunctional architecture, enabling lesion-specific cargo release and efficient ROS scavenging within ischemic neurons. In a murine model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), Ang-PPPC@irisin markedly restored mitochondrial integrity and attenuated neuroinflammation through regulation of the UCP2 pathway and enhanced ROS clearance, leading to a significant reduction of cerebral infarct volume. Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing revealed anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective transcriptional programs. Notably, this strategy extended the therapeutic window beyond 4.5 h limit of thrombolytic therapies, highlighting its clinical potential. Our findings establish an exercise-inspired therapeutic strategy that combines BBB-penetrating delivery with mitochondria precision medicine, offering a translatable strategy for advancing stroke rehabilitation and broadening the scope of exercise-based interventions.

articles.title: Umbilical cord blood culture for the diagnosis of early onset neonatal sepsis: A retrospective study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe diagnosis of early onset sepsis (EOS) depends on the isolation of a pathogen from blood or cerebral spinal fluid. While the technique for collecting umbilical cord blood culture (UCBC) is simpler than newborn blood culture (NBC), evaluation of this practice has not been undertaken at our local neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).ObjectiveTo determine the diagnostic accuracy of UCBC versus NBC for the diagnosis of EOS in neonates.MethodsWe retrospectively collected data between April 1, 2021 and October 31, 2024 for infants admitted to the NICU at risk for EOS. Paired NBC and UCBC collected within 2 hours of each other and prior to the start of antibiotics were included. Clinical outcomes, blood culture results and antibiotic usage were collected. Sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios (LRs), and positive (PPV) and negative predictive values (NPV) were calculated to evaluate accuracy. The association between culture contamination and vaginal delivery was assessed by logistic regression.ResultsOf the 773 newborns at risk for EOS, 256 had paired cultures with a mean (standard deviation) gestation and birth weight of 34.2 (3.5) weeks and 2329 (803) grams, respectively. Sensitivity and specificity of UCBC was 75.0% (95% CI 40.9-92.9%), 92.7% (95% CI 88.9-95.4%), respectively. Eighteen UCBC cases (7.0%) were considered contaminated. Vaginal delivery conferred a higher risk of contamination (p = 0.02).ConclusionsWhile the specificity of UCBC is high, reduction in UCBC contaminants is a priority. Furthermore, calculating reliable estimates of diagnostic accuracy will required multicentre studies given the low incidence of EOS.

articles.title: Inhibition of H2S Production Reduces Portal Pressure and Attenuates Liver Fibrosis in Bile Duct-Ligated Rats.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a gaseous signalling molecule with vasodilatory properties and regulates inflammation and fibrosis in the liver.

METHODS: Rats with bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced liver disease were treated with propargylglycine (PAG; 30 mg/kg via intragastric gavage), a selective inhibitor of cystathionine γ-lyase, the main source of H2S in the cardiovascular system and liver, or vehicle. PAG treatment was initiated at day 5 after BDL to evaluate its effects on the progression of liver fibrosis and portal hypertension.

RESULTS: In BDL rats, PAG significantly reduced portal pressure (PP) (10.4 ± 2.7 mm Hg versus 16.0 ± 3.9 mm Hg, p < 0.05) without affecting systemic pressure. In mesenteric arteries mounted on a wire myograph, no differences were observed in responses to acetylcholine and H2S donor sodium hydrosulfide between treated and untreated BDL rats. In the liver, PAG treatment significantly reduced the expression of IL-6, TGF-β, and collagen I and markedly attenuated hepatic fibrosis and architectural distortion. Rats treated with PAG also exhibited significantly lower alanine aminotransferase.

CONCLUSION: In BDL rats, inhibition of H2S synthesis decreases PP and attenuates liver fibrosis, suggesting that targeting H2S may represent a therapeutic strategy for portal hypertension, potentially through modulation of intrahepatic resistance.

articles.title: Vascular Ageing in Conditions Associated with Early-Onset Hypogonadism.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early-onset hypogonadism may increase the risk of early vascular ageing (EVA).

METHODS: Boys with conditions linked to intrauterine hypogonadism - Klinefelter syndrome (KS) and hypospadias - were recruited alongside healthy controls. Assessments included clinic blood pressure (BP), flow-mediated dilatation, carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), and pulse wave velocity. Fasting blood tests measured testosterone, anti-Müllerian hormone, luteinising hormone, follicle-stimulating hormone, triglycerides, glucose, and cholesterol. Oxidative stress and epigenetic markers were evaluated using total antioxidant capacity (TAOC), peroxide, oxidative stress index (OSI), 8-hydroxydeoxyguanosine (8-OHdG), thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS), glutathione, alpha klotho protein, histone H3 modification, telomerase, and DNA methyltransferase (DNMT) activity.

RESULTS: Eleven boys per group were studied (median age: 14.5 years). Systolic BP was higher in KS and hypospadias compared with controls. CIMT and pulse pressure were elevated in hypospadias versus controls. Mean arterial pressure was increased in KS. Oxidative stress markers (TBARS, TAOC, peroxide, and OSI) were higher in hypospadias. 8-OHdG was elevated in hypospadias versus controls but lower than in KS. DNMT activity was increased in both KS and hypospadias. No differences were observed in alpha klotho, histone H3 modification, or telomerase.

CONCLUSION: Adolescents with early-onset hypogonadism show evidence of EVA, with associated oxidative stress and epigenetic alterations warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Hypertension-Induced Retinal Microvascular Remodeling in Women.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet its effects on the retinal microvasculature in women, independent of pregnancy and diabetes, remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We integrated retinal imaging in female participants with structural assessments in hypertensive female mice to evaluate retinal microvascular remodeling.

RESULTS: In women, higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced retinal arteriolar area and retinal thinning, independent of BMI or glycemic status. Women over age 50 exhibited greater retinal microvascular loss, suggesting age-related susceptibility. After adjusting for age, retinal arteriolar area remained significantly associated with hypertension, whereas venular area and retinal thickness were primarily associated with age. No significant age × hypertension interactions were observed for any outcome. In parallel, hypertensive BPH/2J mice displayed retinal microvascular rarefaction and reduced pericyte coverage compared with normotensive BPN/3J controls.

CONCLUSION: Across species, hypertension induced rarefaction, arteriolar loss, and pericyte depletion, indicating impaired microvascular integrity. These findings support the utility of retinal imaging as a noninvasive biomarker of hypertensive microvascular disease in women.

articles.title: Optimized Activatable Fluorescent and Photoacoustic Imaging Platform toward Precision Detection of Multi-stage Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Molecular imaging utilizing near-infrared (NIR) window and photoacoustic (PA) imaging-which offers high sensitivity, resolution, and tissue penetration-represents a promising approach for visualizing liver diseases. However, there are rare probes for detecting multi-stage liver diseases with high sensitivity, precision, and multi-mode functionality. To address this, we present a novel "Electron Delocalization Equalization" strategy by expanding molecular conjugated system in synergy with charge neutralization to achieve a high-performance NIR/PA molecular platform N5. As a proof of concept, a "single key & dual-locked" probe named N5O was prepared. The NIR and PA signals of N5O are specifically activated by peroxynitrite (ONOO-), which serves as a universal hallmark in the microenvironments of various liver diseases. The design enables rapid response, high sensitivity, and exceptional specificity for imaging multi-stage liver conditions. The strong NIR emission allows accurate assessment of early acute liver injury and diabetic liver disease and reveals that combining hypoglycemic and antioxidant treatments can effectively reverse pathological liver conditions at intermediate stages. In liver cancer models, N5O achieves high-contrast imaging (T/N ∼ 10.7) and accurately outlines tumor margins during fluorescence/PA-guided surgery, substantially lowering postoperative recurrence. Importantly, it also sharply distinguishes human carcinoma from adjacent normal tissue (T/N ∼ 28.1), highlighting its clinical potential.

articles.title: Smart pH-Switchable Nanozyme-Hydrogel Platform with Phycocyanin-Stabilized Mn-Doped Prussian Blue for Synergistic Photothermal-Multienzyme Cascade Therapy of Infected Wounds.
articles.abstract: Infected wound healing remains a major clinical challenge due to persistent bacterial infection, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), prolonged inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration. Here, we develop a smart composite hydrogel (PPB/PB-Mn@PC) by integrating Mn-doped Prussian blue nanozymes surface-modified with phycocyanin (PB-Mn@PC) into a dynamic polyvinyl alcohol/pullulan/borax (PPB) hydrogel. The system features pH-responsive accelerated release of PB-Mn@PC in the acidic infected microenvironment, combined with excellent self-adaptive filling, self-healing, and tissue adhesion properties. The PB-Mn@PC nanozymes exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency under 808 nm laser irradiation and multienzyme-mimicking activities. Notably, their catalytic behavior dynamically switches: predominant SOD/CAT-like ROS scavenging under neutral conditions for cytoprotection, and enhanced POD-like activity under acidic conditions that supports bacterial killing without a proportional increase in freely diffusible ·OH, thereby limiting collateral oxidative burden. In vitro, the composite hydrogel demonstrates excellent biocompatibility, efficient broad-spectrum antibacterial activity (including biofilm disruption), ROS scavenging, and promotion of macrophage M2 polarization. In vivo, in S. aureus-infected full-thickness wound models, the smart hydrogel significantly reduces bacterial burden, accelerates wound closure, enhances re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and angiogenesis, while effectively suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α). This work presents a rationally designed smart hydrogel platform that integrates dynamic mechanics, intelligent microenvironment-responsive release, and synergistic photothermal-multienzyme therapy, offering a promising strategy for the efficient management of infected wounds.

articles.title: CPR outcomes in adults with Fontan physiology: Survival rates and advance care directives.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Outcomes from cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) in patients with Fontan physiology are largely unstudied, contributing to a knowledge gap that makes advance care planning challenging. The goal of our study was to describe outcomes for adult patients with Fontan physiology who received CPR.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of adult patients with Fontan physiology who had at least one outpatient visit to an adult congenital heart center between 2006 and 2021 and sustained resuscitation for in- or out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Peri-procedural cardiac arrest cases were excluded.

RESULTS: Of 46 patients across 10 centers, 22 (47.8%) had a lateral tunnel Fontan. The median age at cardiac arrest was 31 years (interquartile range: 26, 39). There were 27 (58.7%) in-hospital arrests. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved in 54.3% (95% confidence interval 40.0-68.7%). Survival to hospital discharge occurred in 43.5% (29.2-57.8%), and 34.8% (21.0-48.6%) survived to 1 year after CPR. Less advanced New York Heart Association class and cardiac arrest due to ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation were associated with increased one-year survival (p=0.02 and 0.01, respectively). Only 32.6% of patients had documented advance care planning discussions.

CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort of adults with Fontan physiology receiving CPR, over half regained spontaneous circulation; however, only 34.8% were alive 1-year post-arrest. Because fewer than one-third of patients had documented advance care planning prior to arrest, the study highlights the need for proactive counseling and individual goals-of-care discussions in patients with Fontan physiology.

articles.title: snputils: A High-Performance Python Library for Genetic Variation and Population Structure.
articles.abstract: Large-scale genomic and population-genetic datasets offer unprecedented opportunities to study population structure and uncover the genetic basis of complex traits and diseases. Existing analytical tools, however, are characterized by format incompatibilities, limited functionality, and computational inefficiencies, forcing researchers to construct pipelines chaining together fragmented command-line utilities and ad hoc scripts. These are difficult to maintain, scale, and reproduce. We present snputils, an open-source Python library for high-performance processing and analysis of genotype, ancestry, phenotype, and identity-by-descent data within a single framework suitable for biobank-scale research. snputils provides unified data containers and efficient routines for genotype quality control, filtering, merging, and computing classical population-genetic statistics, with optional ancestry-specific masking. An identity-by-descent module supports reading multiple formats, filtering, and ancestry-restricted segment trimming for relatedness and demographic inference. snputils also incorporates ancestry masking and multi-array functionalities for dimensionality reduction methods, as well as efficient implementations of admixture simulation, admixture mapping, genome-wide association testing, and advanced visualization capabilities. With support for the most commonly used file formats, snputils natively supports human and non-human diploid datasets represented in standard formats. At the same time, its modular and optimized design reduces technical overhead, facilitating reproducible workflows that accelerate discoveries in population genetics, genomic research, and precision medicine. Benchmarks show faster I/O and concordant PCA, allele-frequency statistics, and admixture mapping results relative to established reference tools, with substantial runtime reductions. snputils is available at https://github.com/AI-sandbox/snputils, with documentation and tutorials at docs.snputils.org.

articles.title: GDF-15 levels in human umbilical cord blood demonstrate sex dimorphism, and associations with fetal insulin sensitivity and lipids.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) has been implicated in regulating energy homeostasis and insulin sensitivity in rodents, and associated with diabetes in humans. Circulating GDF-15 concentrations are higher in male vs. female adults. Little is known on GDF-15 in newborns in humans. We sought to assess whether cord blood GDF-15 varies by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and sex of newborns, and characterize the associations with insulin sensitivity, growth factors and lipids in newborns.

DESIGN AND METHODS: In a study of 110 newborns of GDM and euglycemic mothers, we assessed cord blood GDF-15 in relation to insulin sensitivity and growth-related factors [glucose/insulin ratio, insulin-like growth factors (IGF-1, IGF-2), leptin, adiponectin] and lipids [total cholesterol (TC), high-density-lipoprotein (HDL) and low-density-lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, and triglycerides].

RESULTS: Cord blood GDF-15 concentrations were higher in females vs. males [median (IQR): 3.5 (3.1, 4.6) vs. 2.8 (2.2, 3.6) ng/ml, P=0.001], and in GDM vs. euglycemic pregnancies [3.6 (2.7, 5.4) vs. 3.1 (2.3, 3.7) ng/ml, P=0.036]. Adjusting for maternal and neonatal characteristics, cord blood GDF-15 concentration was positively associated with female sex (24.2% higher, P=0.008, model R2=0.35), but not with GDM (P=0.99). Cord blood GDF-15 was inversely correlated with glucose/insulin ratio (an indicator of insulin sensitivity, r=-0.27, P=0.025), and positively with IGF-2 (r=0.30, P=0.002) and triglycerides (r=0.47, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The study is the first to discover an inverse sex difference in GDF-15 concentrations in newborns from that reported in adults, and demonstrates that GDF-15 may affect insulin sensitivity and lipid metabolism in fetal life in humans.

articles.title: Transforming Tuberculosis Detection: Rapid Sensitive Isothermal Nucleic Acid Test Identifies Infection and Key Drug-Resistance Mutations in Resource-Limited Settings.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) continues to claim over a million lives annually, with multidrug-resistant strains (MDR-TB) threatening global control efforts. The existing diagnostic systems are not sufficiently portable, affordable, user-friendly, and sensitive for the rapid detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) DNA, including drug-resistance-associated mutations, under decentralized environments. Addressing this challenge, we have developed a next-generation, highly sensitive, point-of-care, rapid yet user-friendly TB diagnostic system that combines pH-based colorimetric loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) targeting dual TB-markers (IS6110 and IS1081) with a portable, AI-enabled device and smartphone-based readout. Further, a probe-free, highly sensitive fluorometric version has also been introduced. In a primary clinical evaluation study conducted with 105 samples, the test demonstrated excellent gene-specific performance achieving 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for IS6110, alongside 100% sensitivity and 70.65% specificity for IS1081. Subsequently, field deployment was carried out on 119 participants in a primary healthcare (PHC) environment, aided by minimally trained healthcare personnel, which resulted in 95.60% sensitivity and 100% specificity. The same platform architecture, without modification, extends seamlessly to drug-resistance profiling, demonstrated here as a proof-of-concept through a probe-free, allele-specific LAMP approach for the rapid and accurate detection of key mutations in MTB DNA associated with rifampicin (rpoB) and isoniazid (katG) resistance. By combining the robust LAMP-based, highly sensitive molecular assay with AI-driven portable automation in a compact, accessible format, this diagnostic system offers an affordable, highly sensitive yet user-friendly solution for community-level TB detection and drug-resistance monitoring without the need for complex infrastructure or highly trained personnel. This platform eventually has the potential to accelerate early screening, reduce transmission, and drive forward global TB elimination.

articles.title: Genome-wide mapping shows coding ITGAM variants drive a reversible interferon-suPAR axis in lupus nephritis.
articles.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a leading cause of kidney failure in systemic lupus erythematosus. Coding variants in ITGAM, encoding the myeloid integrin CD11b, are among the strongest genetic risk factors for LN, yet leave its abundance unchanged. Mapping the locus's trans-regulatory effects in blood from 31,684 individuals, the risk haplotype drove a type I interferon (IFN-I) program in myeloid cells. The locus resolved into two haplotypes, with an R77H-linked coding haplotype driving the trans program without affecting cis-abundance and a regulatory haplotype modulating abundance without any trans regulation. In paired blood and kidney from LN patients, the IFN-I and NF-κB arms were engaged and amplified in R77H carriers, and CD11b+ myeloid cells accumulated at the glomerulus and upregulated PLAUR, coupling the program to suPAR, an effector of podocyte injury. Re-engaging CD11b pharmacologically or genetically suppressed both arms and reversed established disease in LN models, and protected mice engrafted with cells from R77H-carrier patients. A Phase Ib trial is evaluating this mechanism in LN. A genome-wide scan found that this architecture, trans regulation without cis effect on variant's own gene, recurs at 80 disease-associated loci, defining a class of checkpoint variants. Together, these findings suggest that a common coding variant can drive kidney disease without changing expression and is therapeutically targetable.

articles.title: Cardiac amyloidosis: contemporary diagnosis and management with illustrative cases of ATTR and AL subtypes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) is an increasingly recognized, treatable cause of heart failure. Prompt distinction between transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and light-chain cardiac amyloidosis (AL-CA) is critical because delayed AL diagnosis can be fatal.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines epidemiology, mechanisms, multimodality imaging, diagnostic algorithms, and established and emerging therapies. Literature was identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library searches and reference screening; the original search dates require author confirmation. Emphasis is placed on immediate serum free light-chain and serum/urine immunofixation testing, nonbiopsy ATTR diagnosis in eligible patients, and TTR sequencing after ATTR confirmation. Three clinical cases illustrate diagnostic and therapeutic challenges.

EXPERT OPINION: Earlier diagnosis, urgent exclusion of AL-CA, universal TTR genetic testing, and multisystem evaluation of hereditary ATTR are essential. Multidisciplinary, phenotype-guided care and validated treatment-response measures will be increasingly important as therapies expand.

articles.title: Uromodulin T62P variant causes kidney tubular stress and injury modulated by age and polygenic risk.
articles.abstract: While ultra-rare missense variants in UMOD cause highly penetrant autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease, a more frequent UMOD T62P variant conveys intermediate risk with variable penetrance. To determine whether age or polygenic risk contributes to the variable penetrance of T62P, we combined genotype and phenotype data from 882,306 individuals across the UK Biobank (discovery cohort) and the All of Us and MyCode biobanks (validation cohorts). We also analyzed the impact of aging on uromodulin processing and cellular stress in stably transfected kidney tubular cells expressing wild-type or mutant UMOD. We compared the effects of the GPS on the risk of CKD between T62P carriers and non-carriers and tested for the GPS-by-T62P interaction. The UMOD T62P variant was reproducibly associated with higher risk of CKD, and its effect increased with age. Compared to the wild-type and canonical R185S pathogenic variant, clones of T62P-expressing cells exhibited intermediate defects in uromodulin maturation, causing endoplasmic reticulum retention and cellular stress increasing with cellular aging. We also observed significant T62P-by-GPS interaction, with T62P carriers in the top quintile of the GPS having over 5-fold higher risk of CKD compared to the population average (OR 5.17, 95%CI: 2.94-9.08, P=1.0E-08). In summary, we demonstrate that the penetrance of kidney disease in T62P carriers is strongly modified by both age and polygenic risk.

articles.title: Re: "WSOPRAS and ITEDS Consensus Statement on the Assessment and Management of Thyroid Eye Disease".
Developing an Interdisciplinary Framework for Behavioral Data Collection to Advance Coupled Behavioral-Epidemic Models: Cross-Sectional Study in 6 European Countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human behavior influences infectious disease spread and the effectiveness of public health interventions. However, behavioral dynamics are often simplified in policy-oriented epidemic models, largely owing to the scarcity of suitable empirical data.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop an interdisciplinary approach to collecting theory-grounded behavioral data on SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, capturing the complexity and temporal dynamics of preventive health behaviors while quantifying factors relevant to epidemic modeling.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey of adults in France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom from March to July 2024, using age-, sex-, education-, and region-based quotas. Guided by both the capability, opportunity, motivation-behavior model and the requirements of epidemic modeling, we combined validated instruments with modeling-oriented measures in the questionnaire. We assessed temporal changes in retrospectively reported perceived COVID-19 severity and willingness to vaccinate across 5 time points, associations between vaccination willingness, uptake, and timeliness, and differences in behavioral indicators by vaccination status. To capture interactions relevant to both disease transmission and information exchange, we measured age-specific in-person and discussion contacts. Selected measurements then informed a coupled behavioral-epidemic model to illustrate how intention-behavior gaps and changing intention shape simulated vaccination dynamics.

RESULTS: After data quality filtering, 22,228 survey responses were analyzed. Vaccination willingness correlated with uptake and timeliness, although the proportion of initially unwilling respondents who received ≥2 vaccine doses ranged from 5.7% (95% CI 3.2%-8.3%) to 17.9% (95% CI 12.8%-23.1%) across countries. Respondents with low willingness delayed vaccination by approximately 2 months compared to those with high willingness (low willingness: 5.3 months, 95% CI 5-5.8; high willingness: 3.2 months, 95% CI 3-3.4). Respondents retrospectively reported declining perceived COVID-19 severity and willingness to vaccinate over time. Behavioral differences between vaccinated and unvaccinated respondents extended across 96% of the analyzed indicators (Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, P<.001) and were largest in the motivation domain. Vaccinated respondents reported higher vaccine confidence and trust in health authorities and lower concerns about vaccine safety. Average daily discussion contacts mirrored age-specific patterns of in-person contacts, ranging from 1.4 (95% CI 1.2-1.6) to 2.9 (95% CI 2.5-3.2) among adults aged <60 years across countries, compared with 0.5 (95% CI 0.4-0.6) to 1.2 (95% CI 1-1.4) among those aged ≥60 years. In model simulations, incorporating the intention-behavior gap increased vaccination coverage, while allowing willingness to change over time slowed uptake and reduced final coverage.

CONCLUSIONS: This interdisciplinary approach provides a practical route from behavioral theory to empirical measurements that inform states, transitions, vaccination and social contact processes in behavioral-epidemic models. By providing an empirical basis for representing behavioral heterogeneity and dynamics, this study reduces reliance on simplified behavioral assumptions, supporting the development of more realistic behavioral-epidemic models and effective response strategies.

articles.title: Cilia and Nutrient Sensing.
articles.abstract: Primary cilia are solitary, membrane-bound organelles protruding from the surface of most cells in the organism. Their protein composition is strictly controlled by protein trafficking, homeostatically regulated by the transition zone, by intraflagellar transport, and by a complex called the BBSome. The precise control of protein composition in this organelle allows cells to detect hormonal, mechanical, and nutrient-derived cues and translate them into cellular responses. Among the multiple responses that a primary cilium can conduct, are metabolic responses, both at the systemic level and at the cellular level. This review examines how ciliary signaling contributes to energy homeostasis across metabolically relevant tissues such as hypothalamic neurons, as well as beta and alpha cells of the pancreas. We revise literature showing how the ciliary response can control feeding behavior, body weight and glucose metabolism. We also analyze how derangement of several of these sensory and responsive properties result in disease manifestations in syndromic ciliopathies that can include obesity and diabetes. Finally, we revise more recent literature that suggests cilia play a fundamental role in energy sensing and metabolic responses in a cell autonomous manner, that is in the way cells sense the environmental availability of nutrients and react by mounting the optimal energetic response accordingly. Multiple lines of evidence suggest that cilia can sense the availability of nutrients and energy via LKB1-AMPK-mTORC1 axis and/or the fine tuning of mitochondrial responses to nutrient availability. While this represents a rather new field of investigation, it might bring forward a novel role for cilia in sensing the environment and coordinating a cellular response.

articles.title: Antipsychotic Co-Initiation Versus Monotherapy Initiation for People with Acute/Exacerbated Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Antipsychotic co-initiation is sometimes used in schizophrenia spectrum disorders to expedite treatment response, although its use remains controversial due to mixed evidence. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the benefits and harms of antipsychotic co-initiation.

METHODS: We searched the databases MEDLINE, PsycINFO, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to 25 March, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing antipsychotic co-initiation with antipsychotic monotherapy initiation in people with acute/exacerbated schizophrenia spectrum disorders. All antipsychotic combinations were eligible. Trials were excluded if antipsychotics were initiated more than 1 week apart. Review phases were conducted in duplicate. Random-effects meta-analyses calculated standardized mean differences and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Absolute effects were estimated using mean differences and the monotherapy group event rate as the baseline risk. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: Fifteen randomized controlled trials (1937 inpatients, mean age = 32.3 ± 5.6 years, male = 61%) testing 14 antipsychotic combinations over a mean of 10 weeks (range = 1-35) were included. Compared with monotherapy initiation, antipsychotic co-initiation likely improves treatment response (RR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.11, 1.48; moderate certainty), with effects observed as early as 1 week and greater benefits among people with lower symptom severity and those receiving first-generation combinations. Antipsychotic co-initiation may slightly reduce total symptoms (standardized mean difference = - 0.35, 95% CI - 0.71, 0.00) and negative symptoms (standardized mean difference = - 0.55, 95% CI - 1.08, - 0.02; both low certainty). There was little to no evidence of benefit for other efficacy outcomes, including positive symptoms, depressive symptoms, quality of life, and global illness severity (very low to moderate certainty). Antipsychotic co-initiation may not increase adverse effects (RR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.87, 1.09), serious adverse effects (RR = 1.51, 95% CI 0.50, 4.53), or any of the specific side effects examined, including extrapyramidal symptoms, anxiety, constipation, sialorrhea, fatigue, or weight gain (all low certainty). Antipsychotic co-initiation may not affect benzodiazepine (RR = 1.05, 95% CI 0.95, 1.15) or anticholinergic co-use (RR = 0.97, 95% CI 0.76, 1.23; both low certainty). All-cause discontinuation was similar between groups (RR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.81, 1.13; moderate certainty), as were specific-cause discontinuation rates (low-to-moderate certainty). Overall, 28% of participants did not complete the trials.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with monotherapy initiation, there is moderate certainty evidence that antipsychotic co-initiation improves treatment response in acute/exacerbated schizophrenia spectrum disorders without increasing short-term discontinuation. However, its impact on other outcomes remains less certain and with effect sizes that may not be clinically relevant. Evidence certainty was frequently downgraded due to the risk of bias from missing data and imprecision, therefore, adequately powered trials with improved retention strategies are needed.

articles.title: Left pulmonary artery of ductal origin from the left carotid artery with right aortic arch.
articles.abstract: Ductal origin of the pulmonary artery (DOPA) is rare and usually involves the brachiocephalic or subclavian artery. We describe a preterm male neonate (33 weeks) with cyanosis and respiratory distress from birth. Echocardiography showed a right aortic arch with an aberrant left subclavian artery (ALSA) and a left pulmonary artery (LPA) that was not connected to the main pulmonary artery (MPA). CT angiography showed a single left-sided, duct-like vessel connecting the left common carotid artery (LCC), at the carotid bulb, to the LPA. The descending aorta was right-sided, and there was no Kommerell diverticulum, complete vascular ring, or airway or oesophageal compression. Echocardiography also showed moderate peripheral stenosis of the right pulmonary artery. Prostaglandin E1 was started and the LPA was surgically reimplanted onto the MPA. The infant was discharged on room air. To our knowledge, only a few similar cases of left DOPA arising from the carotid artery have been reported. The absence of a left brachiocephalic trunk may explain this variant. Histology of the divided vessel showed ductal tissue.

articles.title: Repeated-Sprint Training in Hypoxia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis with Exploratory Dose-Response Modeling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Repeated-sprint training in hypoxia may improve repeated-sprint performance, but the relationship between external hypoxic exposure and adaptation remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To quantify the effects of repeated-sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) on repeated-sprint performance near sea level and examine the hypoxic dose-response relationship using both frequentist and Bayesian approaches.

METHODS: Eight databases were systematically searched for randomized-controlled trials comparing RSH with matched repeated-sprint training in normoxia (RSN). Best (RSAbest) and mean (RSAmean) repeated-sprint performance were synthesized using frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses, with exploratory study-level dose-response modeling. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2), and certainty using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies met the eligibility criteria. RSH produced small effects on RSAbest (k = 16; g = 0.24, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.00 to 0.48; I2 = 16.2%) and RSAmean (k = 20; g = 0.31, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.53; I2 = 13.6%). Bayesian analyses supported these findings, with probabilities of benefit of 98.4% and 99.9%, respectively. Dose-response analyses identified no consistent linear or nonlinear association between cumulative external hypoxic exposure and either outcome, nor any consistent optimal hypoxic dose.

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis indicates that repeated-sprint training in hypoxia may produce small improvements in both best and mean repeated-sprint performance, supported by both frequentist and Bayesian analyses. Study-level analyses identified neither a consistent linear or nonlinear association between training-structured external hypoxic exposure and performance nor an optimal hypoxic dose. Future trials should standardize repeated-sprint outcomes and report continuous or high-frequency peripheral oxygen saturation alongside mechanical training output to better characterize the effective hypoxic dose. Registration PROSPERO CRD420251151108.

articles.title: Polystyrene Micro‑ and Nanoplastics in Human Blood: Detection, Protein Corona, Haematological Effects, and Coagulation Disturbances.
articles.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are widespread contaminants that can enter the human bloodstream and accumulate in tissues, where they may promote thrombosis and inflammation. This review evaluates how MNPs interact with human blood components. It focuses on polystyrene (PS), the most widely used model polymer in biological studies. PS predominates because well-defined particles are commercially available and their surface chemistry can be tuned. In this review, we critically discuss current analytical approaches for MNP detection in blood, emphasizing their limitations, persistent methodological challenges, and highlight the lack of standardized protocols, particularly for nanoscale particles. Building on evidence that MNPs can reach and persist in circulation, we further explore their interactions with the blood system at both the plasma protein and cellular levels. PS particles may adsorb plasma proteins, forming a protein corona that alters protein conformation and function. At the cellular level, PS MNPs can interact with and be internalized by blood cells, potentially inducing cytotoxic, genotoxic, and inflammatory effects. Importantly, these interactions may disrupt the coagulation cascade and contribute to both procoagulant and anticoagulant alterations. Based on accumulated experimental evidence, MNP exposure is increasingly associated with cardiovascular and haematological risks, as well as potential long-term effects such as chronic inflammation and genotoxicity. To advance the field, future studies should prioritize standardized particle characterization (including size, surface charge, and corona composition), environmentally relevant exposure levels, and reproducible preparation protocols to enable reliable risk assessment and resolve current inconsistencies in the literature.

articles.title: Unveiling the genetic architecture of primary aldosteronism: a multi-omics investigation into subtype-specific insights.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a global public health challenge, with primary aldosteronism (PA) being the most common cause of secondary hypertension. Understanding the genetic architecture of PA is crucial for identifying potential therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify genetic underpinnings associated with PA subtypes, including aldosterone-producing adenoma (APA) and bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (BAH).

METHODS: We conducted a genome-wide Mendelian randomization analysis using adrenal tissue-specific expression quantitative trait loci and hyperaldosteronism genomic data. Replication analysis was performed using a series of independent genome-wide association study datasets. Protein-protein interaction network, pathway enrichment analysis, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data, and Bayesian colocalization analysis were employed to validate and prioritize candidate genes.

RESULTS: A total of 168 genes were identified as having causal relationships with PA subtypes. Pathway enrichment analysis highlighted aldosterone synthesis and lipid metabolism as key pathways. FBN2 emerged as the most significant gene associated with APA, showing enriched expression in aldosterone-producing cells and correlating with KCNJ5 gene expression. RXFP2 was identified as a robust candidate gene for BAH, with evidence of shared causal variants.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study provided novel insights into the genetic inferences of PA subtypes, implicating FBN2 as a potential contributor to APA, and RXFP2 as a key contributor to BAH, respectively. Further experimental and clinical validations are required.

articles.title: Olfactory and cognitive performance decrease in type 2 diabetes: insights from a Mexican exploratory cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Impaired olfactory function has been associated with mild cognitive impairment in individuals with type 2 diabetes. This disease represents a major public health problem in developing countries, where studies addressing olfactory function are scarce. This study aimed to determine the relationship between olfactory and cognitive performance in Mexican adults with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional study included individuals aged 20 to 65 years. Participants were categorized into two groups: patients diagnosed with type 2 diabetes (T2D group, n = 29) and healthy controls (control group, n = 39). Olfactory function (threshold, discrimination, and identification) was evaluated using a custom version of the Snap & Sniff test to obtain the TDI score, and cognition was evaluated using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). The main outcomes were TDI and MoCA scores, which were compared in the full sample and after restricting the sample by age and education. ANCOVA was used to control for age and education effects.

RESULTS: TDI and MoCA scores were lower in the T2D group than in the control group; this effect persisted in the restricted sample and after controlling for age and education. In addition, TDI score and HbA1c values correlated negatively in the T2D group.

CONCLUSION: This study found reduced olfactory and cognitive performance among Mexican individuals with type 2 diabetes, suggesting an association between olfactory and cognitive function.

articles.title: Adjunctive ursodeoxycholic acid in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled open-label pilot study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adequate glycemic control remains difficult to achieve. Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) has shown potential glycemic benefits in chronic liver disease patients and anti-inflammatory effects in animal models of type 2 diabetes. This pilot study investigated the effect of UDCA as adjunctive therapy on metabolic and inflammatory biomarkers in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: Patients were randomized to control and UDCA groups. All patients received metformin 1000 mg plus vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily. The UDCA group received additional UDCA 450 mg twice daily. Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included fasting blood glucose (FBG), lipid profile, body mass index (BMI), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), high mobility group box 1 (HMGB-1), asprosin, malondialdehyde (MDA), and A-kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1). Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after three months.

RESULTS: Per-protocol analysis included forty-four patients per group. After three months, the UDCA group had significantly lower HbA1c (P = 0.001) than the control group. Among secondary outcomes, only IL-6 remained significantly lower in the UDCA group than in the control group after adjusting for multiple comparisons (P < 0.001, q = 0.017). Other secondary biomarkers did not differ significantly between groups. Biomarker findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive UDCA was associated with a possible improvement in glycemic control, while biomarker changes should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating. However, per‑protocol analysis may overestimate treatment effects, and the open‑label design and predominantly female cohort limit generalizability. These findings require confirmation in larger, intention‑to‑treat trials.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial​ was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov under identifiers NCT05902468 (registration date: 15-6-2023).

articles.title: Serum extracellular vesicle microRNA profiling: a candidate signature for pediatric MASLD and potential functional role of miR-103a-3p.
articles.abstract:
