PURPOSE: Serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived microRNAs (miRNAs) may serve as noninvasive biomarkers for pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), but their discriminatory potential and biological relevance remain to be fully clarified.

METHODS: Differentially expressed serum EV miRNAs were screened by small RNA sequencing in the discovery cohort (n = 30), and candidate miRNAs were subsequently validated by quantitative real-time PCR in children with MASLD and healthy controls within a single-center, relatively small validation cohort (final analytical dataset, n = 95). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate diagnostic performance. An ob/ob mouse model and HepG2 steatosis model were used to explore the possible functional involvement of candidate miRNAs.

RESULTS: Small RNA sequencing identified 126 differentially expressed miRNAs in serum EVs from children with MASLD. After filtering, 30 miRNAs were prioritized for downstream analysis. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the target genes of these miRNAs were mainly associated with the PI3K-AKT, Ras, and MAPK signaling pathways. qRT-PCR validation confirmed significant upregulation of miR-223-3p, miR-28-5p, miR-151a-3p, and miR-103a-3p in MASLD-derived EVs, with AUCs of 0.748, 0.608, 0.714, and 0.717, respectively. A three-miRNA panel composed of miR-223-3p, miR-103a-3p, and miR-151a-3p yielded an AUC of 0.771, with a sensitivity of 60.0% and specificity of 89.1%. A model based on clinical variables alone (BMI, insulin, ALT and AST) achieved an AUC of 0.963, and adding the three-miRNA panel did not significantly improve discrimination (AUC 0.977; P = 0.167). In ob/ob mice, miR-103a-3p and miR-151a-3p were upregulated in liver tissue, and overexpression of miR-103a-3p in oleic acid/palmitic acid-treated HepG2 cells markedly increased intracellular triglyceride accumulation and lipid droplet formation.

CONCLUSIONS: The serum EV-derived miR-223-3p/miR-103a-3p/miR-151a-3p signature represents an exploratory candidate biomarker panel for pediatric MASLD. Among these candidates, miR-103a-3p may show possible functional involvement in processes related to hepatic steatosis.

articles.title: The Hypertensive Brain under Stress: An Integrative Human Physiology Perspective.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Hypertension is a major risk factor for cerebrovascular disease, yet its impact on cerebral blood flow regulation may not be fully evident under resting conditions. This review examines cerebrovascular responses to physiological challenges in hypertensive humans.

RECENT FINDINGS: Studies using pharmacological vasodilatory stimulation, hypoxia, hypercapnia, neuronal activation, and exercise reveal alterations in cerebrovascular responsiveness despite relatively preserved resting perfusion. These abnormalities vary across stimuli and vascular territories, with some evidence suggesting greater posterior circulation vulnerability. However, responses to hypercapnia remain inconsistent, and exaggerated exercise pressor responses may impose additional cerebrovascular challenges. Preserved resting cerebral blood flow does not necessarily indicate intact cerebrovascular regulation. Evaluating responses to distinct physiological challenges may provide a more comprehensive understanding of cerebrovascular dysfunction in hypertension. Future studies should clarify regional differences, underlying mechanisms, and the influence of disease progression on these responses.

articles.title: Device - Based Autonomic Modulation in Arrhythmia and Beyond.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Autonomic imbalance contributes to the initiation and maintenance of cardiac arrhythmias and represents an emerging therapeutic target. This review summarizes the current evidence for device-based and targeted autonomic neuromodulation and evaluates its potential across arrhythmias and cardiovascular disease.

RECENT FINDINGS: Preclinical and clinical studies of vagus nerve stimulation, ganglionated plexus ablation, renal and cardiac sympathetic denervation and baroreflex activation therapy demonstrate beneficial effects on autonomic tone, electrophysiological remodeling, inflammation and arrhythmic burden. Emerging evidence also supports applications beyond arrhythmias, including heart failure and systemic inflammatory disease. Although neuromodulation shows promising therapeutic potential, clinical efficacy remains heterogeneous, with important uncertainties regarding optimal targets, stimulation parameters, patient selection, and treatment monitoring. Future research should prioritize standardized protocols, validated biomarkers, phenotype-specific strategies, and closed-loop approaches.

articles.title: From Conventional to Next-Generation Probiotics in Pregnancy: A Critical Review of Preterm Birth Prevention.
articles.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB) is a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality. Its aetiology is heterogeneous, encompassing infectious, inflammatory, vascular, cervical and iatrogenic pathways, and maternal dysbiosis is implicated in a subset of spontaneous phenotypes rather than in PTB as a whole. Probiotic modulation of the maternal microbiota has been proposed as prevention. We find a marked asymmetry in the evidence. In very low birthweight preterm infants, probiotics reduce severe necrotising enterocolitis and all-cause mortality, but this treats the consequences of prematurity and does not extrapolate to antenatal prevention. Within pregnancy, the only meta-analysis with PTB as a primary endpoint is null; the single randomised trial with obstetric outcomes missed its primary endpoint, pooled estimates for Group B Streptococcus colonisation rest on trials at predominantly unclear or high risk of bias and were not reproduced in later placebo-controlled trials, and the most favourable result comes from a single-arm study with a historical comparator. Efficacy therefore remains unproven, and no strain or formulation can be recommended outside clinical trials. Reports of a resident placental microbiome have not withstood scrutiny. Probiotic effects are strain-specific, yet several studies with obstetric endpoints do not report the organism to strain level. Safety differs fundamentally between pregnant adults and preterm infants, in whom invasive infection, product contamination and the absence of licensed products are documented concerns. Next-generation approaches remain preclinical. Progress requires adequately powered randomised trials that report full strain designations, confirm engraftment at the intended site and use clinical obstetric endpoints as primary outcomes.

articles.title: Bidirectional Signaling between Cardiomyocytes and Cardiac Fibroblasts: Revisiting RV Remodeling and Translational Therapeutic Insights.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is an incurable, progressive lung disease characterized by high pulmonary artery pressure and vascular resistance. The resulting hemodynamics lead to right ventricular (RV) hypertrophy and failure. Although vasodilating pharmacotherapies are available for the treatment of this disease, these therapies cannot fully prevent RV failure from being the leading cause of death in patients with PAH. Researchers have identified that the pathophysiology of RV remodeling and subsequent RV failure is mediated by complex cellular interactions between various cardiac cell types, including cardiomyocytes (CM), cardiac fibroblasts (CF), endothelial cells, inflammatory cells, and the many metabolic signaling pathways active in all cell types. When subjected to chronic pressure overload, CMs undergo hypertrophic growth, metabolic changes, mitochondrial dysfunction, increased oxidative stress, and calcium imbalances. These pathological changes in CM lead to the activation of CF, resulting in myofibroblast differentiation from CF and the excessive production of ECM proteins from myofibroblasts, resulting in myocardial fibrosis and ventricular stiffness. The interaction between CMs and CFs occurs via several mechanisms, including paracrine signaling, extracellular vesicles, and neurohumoral signaling pathways. These mechanisms together trigger RV, causing it to adapt to the increased afterload and undergo maladaptive remodeling and subsequent failure. Understanding the cellular mechanisms that regulate RV remodeling is important for identifying novel therapeutic targets. This review explores PAH pathophysiology, the significance of the RV in disease progression, the roles of CMs and CFs in RV remodeling, cellular mechanisms, and emerging therapeutic targets aimed at maintaining normal RV function in PAH.

articles.title: Association of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions with Diabetes Mellitus and Cardiovascular Risk Factor Burden: A Multicenter, Retrospective, Cross-sectional Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPL) are an emerging optical coherence tomography (OCT) finding that has been linked to systemic cardiovascular disease. Their relationship with cardiovascular risk factors (cvRF) remains to be established, particularly in high-risk populations.

METHODS: In this retrospective, multicenter, cross-sectional comparative study of 122 patients (61 with retinal artery occlusion, 61 controls with one to four cvRF), age- and sex-adjusted logistic regression assessed the association of cvRF with RIPL, and interaction terms tested whether associations differed between controls and cases. Discrimination of RIPL lesion count for diabetes mellitus and for two or more cvRF was assessed with receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, including likelihood ratios (LR).

RESULTS: RIPL were present in 66 of 122 patients (54.1%). After adjustment for age and sex, the number of cvRF (Nr. cvRF; OR 2.01 per additional cvRF, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.27-3.17) and diabetes mellitus (OR 3.34, 95% CI 1.43-7.79) were associated with RIPL (both q = 0.013). Associations were stable in sensitivity analyses and weaker in cases alone. No interaction test showed a difference between controls and cases, but power was limited. RIPL lesion count discriminated poorly for diabetes mellitus (area under the curve (AUC) 0.62, 95% CI 0.52-0.72; at ≥ 1 lesion LR+ 1.57, LR- 0.52) and for Nr. cvRF ≥ 2 (AUC 0.65, 95% CI 0.56-0.73; at ≥ 2 lesions LR+ 8.34, 95% CI 1.19-58.60, LR- 0.73). No evidence of an association with carotid stenosis was found.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, RIPL were associated with cardiovascular risk factor burden, an association carried mainly by diabetes mellitus. RIPL lesion count discriminated poorly, and the findings do not support its use as a stand-alone screening tool.

articles.title: Clinical utility of dual-energy CT-guided gout management: a single-centre retrospective before-and-after study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-energy CT (DECT) can visualize monosodium urate (MSU) deposition, but evidence is limited regarding potential clinical benefits of DECT beyond diagnosis in gout.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate potential clinical benefits of performing DECT beyond diagnosis in patients with gout.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective pre-/post-implementation study at the rheumatology outpatient clinic of Jeju National University Hospital, Jeju, Republic of Korea (May 2016-April 2020). DECT was introduced in May 2018. Among patients who underwent DECT, DECT positivity and disease-duration discrimination were assessed using ROC/AUC and cutoffs were explored. For prognostic comparisons, analyses were restricted to patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi at baseline and compared the DECT-performed group with the no-DECT group using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW).

RESULTS: A total of 722 patients were included (no-DECT n = 506; DECT performed n = 216). Among DECT-performed patients, 110/216 were DECT-positive (50.9%). Disease duration showed limited discrimination for DECT positivity (AUC 0.626). In prognosis analyses (n = 645), IPTW-weighted flare outcomes were similar between groups (any flare: OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.87-1.83; flare count: IRR 1.37, 95% CI 0.94-2.01), and change in serum urate did not differ (β 0.01 mg/dL, 95% CI - 0.32 to 0.34). Renal outcomes favored the DECT-performed group (ΔeGFR β 2.39 mL/min/1.73m2, 95% CI 0.27-4.51; eGFR decline ≥ 10: OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.31-0.95; CKD stage worsening: OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.90).

CONCLUSIONS: Clinically occult MSU deposition was detected by DECT in approximately half of scanned patients, and disease duration alone had limited utility for identifying DECT-positive patients. In weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with flare outcomes or serum urate change but was associated with more favorable renal outcomes. Key Points • Dual-energy CT (DECT) detected clinically occult monosodium urate deposition in approximately half of scanned gout patients (50.9%). • In IPTW-weighted analyses among patients without clinically apparent subcutaneous tophi, DECT performance was not associated with 1-year flare outcomes or serum urate change. • DECT performance was associated with more favorable 1-year renal outcomes, including greater ΔeGFR and lower risks of eGFR decline and CKD stage worsening.

articles.title: 'Tis the season: how three common respiratory viral infections affect cardiac biomarkers and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Epidemics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS‑CoV‑2) arise yearly. Individuals with co-morbidities are at higher risk for hospitalisation and a severe infection course. Along respiratory disease, acute cardiac events (ACEs) are possible, although the relative risk for the specific infection remains unclear. This study compares cardiac biomarkers as indicators of cardiac damage in hospitalized persons infected with influenza, RSV or omicron-SARS-CoV-2, and analyzes their correlation with in-hospital courses of disease.

METHODS: Retrospective comparative analysis of cardiac biomarkers (high-sensitivity-troponin-T, (hs-TNT), N-terminal-pro-hormone of brain-natriuretic-peptide (NT-proBNP) and creatinine kinase (CK)) in hospitalized individuals with influenza, RSV or omicron-SARS-CoV-2 and studied secondary outcomes such as ACEs, ICU-admission and all-cause in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Of 251 patients with influenza, 131 with RSV and 117 with omicron-SARS-CoV-2 infections, pre-existing conditions varied between cohorts, with COPD being most frequent in RSV, and diabetes and cardiovascular disease being more prevalent in omicron-SARS-CoV-2 patients. Patients with RSV had the highest hs-TnT, NT-proBNP and CRP levels, CK levels were highest in influenza. Hs-TnT was above the cut-off in 86.1% of RSV cases, 74.4% of omicron-SARS-CoV-2 and 63.4% of influenza. Risks of mortality, ICU-admission and ACEs were comparable between the cohorts. Likelihood of ICU-admission was associated with ACEs, advanced age, increased CK, hs-TnT, NT-proBNP, CRP and creatinine concentrations, respectively. Presence of cardiovascular disease, occurrence of ACEs, age, hs-TnT, NT-proBNP, and CRP were associated with higher mortality.

CONCLUSION: Hospitalized individuals with seasonal viral infections experience a high prevalence of ACEs, contributing to poor disease outcomes.

articles.title: Association of 13N-ammonia PET-derived myocardial flow reserve and rest left ventricular ejection fraction with 5-year outcomes in patients with prior coronary revascularization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography (PET)-derived myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and rest left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) are independently associated with 5-year cardiovascular outcomes after revascularization and whether adding MFR improves model fit and apparent discrimination beyond age, sex, and LVEF.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 227 patients with prior percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) undergoing rest and adenosine-stress 13N-ammonia PET. Patients with repeat revascularization within 90 days after PET were excluded. The 5-year primary endpoint was the first occurrence of cardiac death, myocardial infarction, sustained ventricular tachycardia, heart-failure hospitalization, or PCI/CABG > 90 days after PET. A prespecified Cox model included continuous MFR, rest LVEF, age, and sex. The incremental value of MFR was assessed by likelihood-ratio testing and change in apparent Harrell C-statistic. PCI-only and 90-day landmark sensitivity analyses and continuous MFR-by-LVEF interaction were tested.

RESULTS: Of 227 patients (median age, 73 years; 187 [82.4%] men), 199 (87.7%) had prior PCI. During a median 3.6-year follow-up, 55/227 (24.2%) reached the primary endpoint. Lower MFR and lower rest LVEF were independently associated with endpoint hazard (adjusted hazard ratios: 1.40 per 0.5-unit lower MFR (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.79; P = 0.009) and 1.28 per 10-percentage-point lower rest LVEF (95% CI, 1.06-1.54; P = 0.01)). Adding MFR improved model fit (P = 0.008) and apparent C-statistic (0.641 to 0.696) (difference, 0.055; 95% CI, 0.006-0.110). Associations persisted in PCI-only and 90-day landmark analyses; no continuous MFR-by-LVEF interaction was evident (P = 0.20).

CONCLUSIONS: After coronary revascularization, lower MFR and lower rest LVEF were independently associated with the 5-year composite endpoint after adjustment for age and sex. MFR improved model fit and apparent discrimination, without statistical evidence of an MFR-by-LVEF interaction.

articles.title: Frequency and longitudinal changes of incidental spinal 18F-FDG uptake in participants undergoing PET/CT cancer screening.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the frequency, anatomical distribution, and longitudinal changes of increased 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake in the spine among participants undergoing PET/CT cancer screening, and to assess its clinical significance.

METHODS: In total, 4882 participants who underwent FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) for cancer screening were included. Participants with a history of malignancy or spinal surgery were excluded. Spinal FDG uptake with a maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) ≥ 2.5 was defined as increased spinal FDG uptake. The SUVmax, spinal site, and spinal level were recorded. The frequency of increased spinal FDG uptake was analyzed according to age and sex. Among participants with increased spinal FDG uptake, the distribution of uptake was analyzed according to spinal site and level. Longitudinal changes in the SUVmax were evaluated in participants with increased spinal FDG uptake.

RESULTS: Among all 4882 participants, the frequency of spinal FDG uptake with SUVmax ≥ 2.5 increased with age. In 847 participants with increased spinal FDG uptake, the most frequent sites of increased uptake were the vertebral bodies (72.5%) and facet joints (21.3%). Vertebral-body uptake was predominantly observed at the thoracolumbar junction (T11-T12) and in the lower lumbar spine (L4-L5); facet or interspinous joint uptake was concentrated in the lower lumbar spine (L3/4-L4/5). Among the 346 participants who underwent serial FDG PET/CT examinations over a median follow-up period of 735 days, 88.7% showed a decrease in spinal FDG uptake to an SUVmax of < 2.5.

CONCLUSION: Most incidental increases in spinal FDG uptake detected during PET/CT cancer screening decreased on follow-up, suggesting that these incidental findings are usually transient and likely benign in participants without a history of malignancy or spinal surgery.

articles.title: Associations between daily step counts and postprandial glucose metrics in adults with T1D: between- and within-participant analyses under free-living conditions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the association between wearable-derived daily step counts and postprandial continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D), using both between-participant and within-participant analyses.

METHODS: Adults with T1D were recruited from two centers between November 2023 and November 2025, simultaneously wearing a CGM device and a smart wristband for 14 days under free-living conditions. Daily step counts were categorized as < 7,000, 7,000-10,000, and > 10,000 steps/day. Postprandial CGM-derived metrics included time above range (TAR), time in range (TIR), time below range (TBR), coefficient of variation (CV), standard deviation (SD), and mean glucose (MG). Associations were examined using between-participant and within-participant analyses.

RESULTS: Among 60 participants with T1D (mean age 47 ± 14 years; 58% men), between-participant analyses showed lower postprandial TBR in both the 7,000-10,000 and > 10,000 steps/day groups than in the < 7,000 steps/day group, the adjusted differences were - 3.68% points (adjusted 95% CI, -6.99 to -0.37; adjusted P = 0.025) and - 4.60% points (adjusted 95% CI, -8.16 to -1.05; adjusted P = 0.007), respectively. No between-participant differences were observed for TAR, TIR, SD, CV or MG. In within-participant analyses (11 participants), postprandial CV and SD were lowest on days with 7,000-10,000 steps. Compared with these days, days with > 10,000 steps showed higher CV (estimated difference, 3.00% points; adjusted 95% CI, 0.11 to 5.90; adjusted P = 0.040) and SD (estimated difference, 0.27 mmol/L; adjusted 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.52; adjusted P = 0.025), whereas days with < 7,000 steps showed higher SD (estimated difference, 0.26 mmol/L; adjusted 95% CI, 0.01 to 0.50; adjusted P = 0.034). CV was also higher on days with < 7,000 steps, but the difference was only nominally significant before Bonferroni adjustment (estimated difference, 2.61% points; adjusted 95% CI, -0.25 to 5.46; unadjusted P = 0.029; adjusted P = 0.086).

CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory analyses showed that higher habitual step counts were associated with lower postprandial TBR between participants, whereas the within-participant analyses suggested the lowest CV and SD on days with 7,000-10,000 steps.

articles.title: Focus on environmental pollutants and metabolic disorders as risk factors and a foundation for identifying new therapeutic targets for alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract: Given that Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative condition and the leading cause of dementia, developing a new, effective, disease-modifying and safe therapy for AD is a priority. Rather than being driven by a single causative factor, AD is currently viewed as a multifactorial disorder in which protein aggregation, dysregulated lipid metabolism, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress form a complex and interconnected pathogenic network, leading to progressive neurodegeneration. The scientific community is increasingly focusing on the pathogenesis of AD in the context of exposure to environmental pollutants and the rapid rise in the prevalence of metabolic disorders. Metabolic disorders, primarily insulin resistance and diabetes mellitus, are already identified as critical risk factors for this disease, and the mechanisms of action of antidiabetic drugs and related agents are being intensively studied for their potential application in combating AD. Regarding environmental pollutants, their impact on AD pathogenesis is only partially recognised, especially for phenols, parabens, and phthalates, as well as certain organophosphate esters, pesticides, heavy metals, suspended particulate matter, and, more recently, microplastics and nanoplastics. This review article aims to present a novel, critical analysis of the literature on AD, with a particular focus on environmental pollutants and metabolic disorders as risk factors, and to provide deeper insight into the mechanisms underlying its onset and progression, which may serve as a foundation for identifying new therapeutic targets for the treatment of this disease.

articles.title: Neuroimmune pharmacology of dextromethorphan/bupropion (Auvelity): Mechanistic insights into microglial regulation, inflammasome suppression, and therapeutic translation.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as a central pathogenic mechanism in major depressive disorder and diverse neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury, and neuropathic pain. Persistent activation of microglia and astrocytes, excessive cytokine production, inflammasome activation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity can collectively disrupt neuronal homeostasis and promote disease progression. Dextromethorphan/bupropion (Auvelity) is a fixed-dose combination that integrates N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonism, sigma-1 receptor agonism, monoaminergic modulation, and cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibition, thereby producing sustained dextromethorphan exposure and multimodal pharmacological activity. Preclinical studies of dextromethorphan and bupropion individually provide mechanistic evidence suggesting potential effects on microglial activation, Toll-like receptor 4 and nuclear factor kappa B signaling, inflammasome activity, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function. However, direct evidence demonstrating that these neuroimmune effects are produced by the fixed-dose combination remains limited. This review examines the pharmacological basis of dextromethorphan/bupropion, its potential interactions with major neuroimmune pathways, and available experimental and clinical evidence. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing direct combination evidence from component-specific findings and mechanistic extrapolation. The translational relevance of reported mechanisms is considered across major neuroinflammatory disorders, with attention to pharmacokinetic exposure, clinical evidence, biomarker assessment, and future precision neuroimmunopharmacological strategies. Overall, dextromethorphan/bupropion has established antidepressant efficacy and a biologically plausible neuroimmune profile, but combination-specific mechanistic and biomarker-driven studies are required to determine whether these pathways contribute directly to its therapeutic effects. This evidence synthesis also considers exposure-related limitations, disease-specific applicability, and the distinction between therapeutic plausibility and demonstrated neuroimmune target engagement.

articles.title: Mineralocorticoid-responsive polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion associated with voriconazole: a case report.
articles.abstract: Voriconazole (VRCZ) has been associated with renal and adrenal adverse effects, including rare cases of salt-wasting nephropathy. However, the clinical characteristics and underlying mechanisms of VRCZ-associated natriuresis remain incompletely understood.A 48-year-old male with chronic empyema and refractory pneumothorax was admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) because of worsening respiratory status. VRCZ therapy was administered from ICU day 1 through day 22. During the third week of ICU admission, his urine output progressively increased, reaching 4,000-6,000 mL/day from ICU day 23 onward. This increase was accompanied by increased urinary sodium excretion. Despite substantial urinary sodium losses and continuous fluid administration, his serum sodium concentration initially remained within the normal range. VRCZ was discontinued on ICU day 23; however, polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion persisted for several days. On ICU day 23, the active renin concentration was 2.36 pg/mL, and the aldosterone concentration was below 4.0 pg/mL. Fludrocortisone was initiated at 0.05 mg/day on ICU day 26, after which urine output gradually decreased. Fludrocortisone was discontinued on ICU day 43, and polyuria did not recur.This case suggests the presence of a mineralocorticoid-responsive state characterized by marked polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion during VRCZ therapy. Although a causal relationship between VRCZ exposure and impaired aldosterone production cannot be established, VRCZ may have contributed to reduced mineralocorticoid activity. Clinicians should consider possible mineralocorticoid dysfunction when unexplained polyuria and increased urinary sodium excretion develop during VRCZ therapy, even in the absence of overt hyponatremia.

articles.title: Prevalence and risk factors associated with bovine alphaherpesvirus 1 (BoAHV1) and bovine leukemia virus (BLV) infections in a semi-arid environment in Brazil.
articles.abstract: Dairy cattle production plays a major role in the Brazilian semi-arid region. However, the activity is characterized by low productive and reproductive efficiency. Among the agents responsible for productive and reproductive losses in cattle are bovine alphaherpesvirus 1 (BoAHV1) and bovine leukemia virus (BLV). Thus, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of and identify risk factors associated with BoAHV1 and BLV infections in two dairy basins in the semi-arid region of the state of Pernambuco, Brazil. A cross-sectional study was conducted, with serum samples collected from 522 cattle distributed across 32 dairy herds. Serological diagnosis for BoAHV1 was performed by seroneutralization (SN), and for BLV by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Risk factor analysis was carried out using univariate analysis followed by a mixed-effects regression model. The individual seroprevalence of BoAHV1 and BLV was 78.0% and 3.8%, respectively. Herd-level prevalence was 100.0% for BoAHV1 and 40.6% for BLV. Age (≥ 10 years) was identified as a risk factor for BoAHV1 infection (OR = 6.5). These findings represent the first report of BLV infection in the study region. Therefore, preventive measures are needed to limit the spread of these agents in the region and to reduce their impact on dairy production systems.

articles.title: Intracranial hemorrhage in glioblastoma: incidence, risk factors, and outcome.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The incidence, risk factors and clinical implications of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with glioblastoma have not been well studied.

METHODS: We identified patients with WHO 2021 glioblastoma in the Zurich database and explored the incidence, putative risk factors, management and outcome of ICH. ICH was verified by central MRI and imaging report review.

RESULTS: Among 387 patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2019, 40 had an ICH at diagnosis. Of these, 4 patients were on anti-platelet agents, and 2 patients were on anticoagulation. All ICH occurred in the tumor region. Patients with ICH at diagnosis were younger (p = 0.001), had less cardiac disease (p = 0.027), and had larger tumors (p = 0.020). Median survival was similar between patients with (15 months) or without (13 months) ICH at diagnosis. Among 22 patients with ICH later in the disease course, 7 patients (37%) experienced ICH prior to first progression. ICH were not intratumoral in 8 patients. Ten patients (45%) had no change in management, 7 patients (32%) were referred to palliative care. Nine patients (50%) had been pre-exposed to bevacizumab, yet, 193 patients (53%) without ICH had received bevacizumab, too. Five patients (23%) had platelet counts below 100,000/µl within 14 days prior to ICH. Median survival in the 22 patients who experienced ICH after diagnosis (17 months) was not inferior than in patients without ICH (13 months).

CONCLUSION: ICH is rare in glioblastoma. It may be related to intrinsic features of the tumor and its blood vessels, however, platelet count and blood pressure should be monitored regularly. ICH does not signify a poor outcome overall.

articles.title: Sleep in progressive supranuclear palsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of polysomnographic findings.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate polysomnographic measured sleep changes in patients with progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) compared with controls.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, All EBM databases, and Web of Science were searched. Eight studies were included in the quantitative meta-analysis, involving 183 individuals with PSP and 158 controls.

RESULTS: Meta-analyses revealed reduced sleep efficiency, total sleep time, and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep percentage, and increased wake time after sleep onset, N1 sleep percentage, REM latency, and apnea hypopnea index in PSP patients compared with controls. No significant group differences were observed in sleep latency, N2 sleep percentage, N3 sleep percentage, or arousal index.

CONCLUSIONS: Our meta-analysis found that multiple objective sleep abnormalities are present in individuals with PSP compared with controls. This suggests the potential value of polysomnography in characterizing sleep disturbances in PSP. These findings might be useful for distinguishing PSP from other neurodegenerative diseases. Future research should explore the effects of clinical characteristics (i.e., disease duration, disease severity, and comorbid sleep disorders) on sleep in PSP.

articles.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Ukraine and Neighboring Poland Before and During Russia's Full-Scale Invasion of Ukraine: A Comparative Analysis of Public Surveillance Data, 2019-2025.
articles.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 brought war injuries, overcrowded hospitals and transfers of patients across borders, all of which favor the spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). National trends before and during the war have not been compared with those of a neighboring country.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study used publicly available, aggregated surveillance data on invasive isolates from the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Europe for Ukraine (2019-2023) and from the European Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network for Poland (2019-2025). Five pathogen-antibiotic combinations were compared between the pre-war (2019-2021) and war (2022-2023) periods using risk ratios (RR), a test for trend and a difference-in-differences analysis.

RESULTS: Carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae rose from 61.0% to 71.3% in Ukraine (RR 1.17, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.07-1.27) and from 12.5% to 17.5% in Poland (RR 1.41, 95% CI: 1.25-1.58). In Poland, most of the increase occurred in 2021, before the invasion. Carbapenem resistance in Acinetobacter species increased in Ukraine (74.2% to 83.0%) but not in Poland (79.1% to 78.1%; ratio of odds ratios 1.80, 95% CI: 1.17-2.77). Meanwhile, Ukrainian surveillance coverage increased from 1% to 45% of the population, and blood culture rates remained low.

CONCLUSIONS: Reported carbapenem resistance in Ukraine was very high before the full-scale war and higher during it, most clearly in Acinetobacter species. Because surveillance expanded and the COVID-19 pandemic and antibiotic use also changed over this period, these data cannot show that the war caused the increase. Stronger infection control and coordinated cross-border surveillance are needed.

articles.title: Correction: Pulmonary Vein Isolation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: What Did We Learn from the SHAM Ablation Studies?
Plasma metabolic signatures preceding incident type 2 diabetes mellitus: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to identify circulating plasma metabolic biomarkers associated with incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), construct a composite metabolic risk score (CMRS), and evaluate its incremental predictive utility beyond conventional clinical risk factors.

METHODS: A total of 224,874 diabetes-free participants from the UK Biobank were randomly allocated into a derivation cohort (70%, N = 157,411) and a locked internal validation cohort (30%, N = 67,463). A two-stage feature selection framework combining regularized Elastic Net Cox regression with age- and sex-adjusted multivariable Cox models under Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) control was applied in the derivation cohort to build the CMRS. Incremental predictive capacity was evaluated in the validation cohort by comparing a comprehensive clinical base model incorporating baseline glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and lipid profiles with and without CMRS.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 12,150 incident T2DM cases occurred. A core signature of 52 nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) metabolites was identified. In the locked internal validation cohort (N = 67,463), continuous standardized CMRS was independently associated with incident T2DM (fully adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1-standard deviation [SD] increase = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.61-1.82, P < 0.001; subdistribution HR accounting for competing mortality = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.59-1.83, P < 0.001). Segmented linear regression identified an exploratory inflection threshold along the continuous standardized score at CMRSscaled = -​1.474 (95% CI: -​1.638 to -​1.309, P < 0.001), below which approximately 7.0% of the cohort resided, with risk slopes of β1 = -0.141 below versus β2 = +0.905 above the threshold. Adding CMRS to the fully adjusted clinical base model yielded modest discriminative gains, increasing Harrell's C-index from 0.8603 (95% CI: 0.8542-0.8665) to 0.8660 (95% CI: 0.8600-0.8719; ΔC = +​0.0056, P < 0.001) and 10-year time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.878 to 0.883 (ΔAUC = +​0.005, 95% CI: 0.004-0.007, paired bootstrap P < 0.001). In 1000-iteration nested bootstrap internal validation, model optimism was negligible (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.8674). Although continuous Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI = 30.55%, 95% CI: 27.21%-33.89%, P < 0.001) and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI = 0.859%, 95% CI: 0.751%-0.967%, P < 0.001) metrics showed statistical gains, overall incremental prognostic impact was modest, accompanied by a 10-year Brier score error reduction from 0.0298 to 0.0295 (index of prediction accuracy improvement [ΔIPA] = +​0.82%).

CONCLUSIONS: The 52-metabolite CMRS is independently associated with incident T2DM and provides modest incremental predictive discrimination and precision beyond comprehensive clinical models incorporating standard glycemic and lipid measures.

articles.title: Long-term oncological outcomes, late side effects, and cosmesis of partial-breast versus whole-breast irradiation for early-stage breast cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long-term outcomes after partial-breast irradiation (PBI) versus whole-breast irradiation (WBI) for early-stage breast cancer remain uncertain. We compared long-term oncological outcomes, late effects, and cosmesis.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and CINAHL from database inception to 9 March, 2026. Eligible studies were randomised controlled trials comparing PBI with WBI after breast-conserving surgery for stage 0-II breast cancer, with at least 7 years of follow-up. The primary outcome was ipsilateral breast tumour recurrence (IBTR). Secondary outcomes were non-breast cancer mortality (NBCM), overall, disease-free and breast cancer-specific survival, locoregional recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, late effects, and cosmesis. Random-effects models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Peto odds ratios (ORs) were used for NBCM. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261334941).

RESULTS: Twelve trials including 15,670 women were included. PBI was associated with higher IBTR overall (HR 1.61, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08-2.41; p = 0.02; I2 = 71%). In the prespecified external-beam subgroup comprising three trials, the pooled HR was 1.24 (95% CI 0.89-1.73; p = 0.21; I2 = 0%), without a statistically significant difference. NBCM was lower overall with PBI (OR 0.77, 0.64-0.91; p = 0.003; I2 = 0%), but not in the external-beam subgroup (OR 0.73, 0.52-1.03; p = 0.07; I2 = 0%). Overall, disease-free, and breast cancer-specific survival were similar. Once-daily external-beam PBI and multicatheter brachytherapy showed favourable cosmesis and fewer late effects, whereas twice-daily 3D-conformal radiotherapy was associated with poorer cosmesis.

CONCLUSION: PBI should not be considered a single treatment approach. Long-term oncological and cosmetic outcomes vary across PBI techniques and fractionation schedules, highlighting the importance of technique-specific evidence. The NBCM signal remains hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Role and mechanisms of the immunoproteasome in cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract: The immunoproteasome is an inducible proteasome isoform containing β1i (LMP2/PSMB9), β2i (MECL-1/PSMB10), and β5i (LMP7/PSMB8). Experimental cardiovascular studies associate immunoproteasome-dependent changes in ATRAP, PTEN, SOCS3, and ATG5 with inflammatory signalling, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and autophagy, although selective direct cleavage of each substrate by the immunoproteasome is not fully established. The biological effects vary with disease stage, cell type, inflammatory and metabolic context, and catalytic subunit. In chronic inflammatory remodelling, increased immunoproteasome activity can enhance pathological signalling, whereas mouse myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion models identify protective functions of β2i and β5i in mitochondrial homeostasis and cell survival. In contrast, evidence from diabetic cardiomyopathy supports overall cardiac proteasome insufficiency without proving a selective β2i/β5i defect. Human cardiovascular evidence remains largely observational. Selective immunoproteasome inhibitors have not been established as cardiovascular treatments, and their safety, tissue selectivity, and optimal timing require investigation. Thus, immunoproteasome modulation should be interpreted as a context-dependent experimental strategy rather than a uniform therapeutic target.

articles.title: Functional and health-related quality-of-life outcomes following stereotactic radiotherapy for glioma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Functional preservation and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) are increasingly recognized as important treatment outcomes for patients with glioma undergoing stereotactic radiation; however, these outcomes have not been comprehensively synthesized. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating functional and HRQoL outcomes following stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) and stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) for glioma. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting standardized functional or HRQoL outcomes following SRS or SRT for newly diagnosed or recurrent glioma were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I v2. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions were performed for binary Karnofsky Performance Status outcomes (KPS), with subgroup analyses by treatment modality and disease setting. Pre- and post-treatment KPS changes were summarized descriptively. Nineteen studies comprising 21 study arms met inclusion criteria. KPS was the predominant functional outcome measure, while multidimensional HRQoL instruments were infrequently and inconsistently reported. The pooled proportion of preserved functional status was 86.4% (95% CI, 71.4-94.2%) following SRS and 57.7% (95% CI, 32.3-79.6%) following SRT, with a significant between-group difference (p > 0.05). Functional decline was more common among recurrent than newly diagnosed cohorts (29.0% vs. 15.8%, p > 0.001). Descriptive analyses demonstrated stable or slightly improved KPS in newly diagnosed cohorts but greater declines among recurrent cohorts. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated persistent functional preservation following SRS after restriction to recurrent and high-grade cohorts. Stereotactic radiation was associated with preservation of functional status in most patients with glioma. Although SRS demonstrated greater functional preservation than SRT, important differences in patient selection warrant cautious interpretation. Standardized, longitudinal HRQoL assessment remains a major unmet need and should be incorporated into future prospective studies evaluating stereotactic radiation for glioma.

articles.title: Acute healthcare utilization among children potentially eligible for pediatric palliative care throughout the disease trajectory: a nationwide population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pediatric palliative care (PPC) aims to improve the quality of life of children with life-limiting or life-threatening conditions through early integration alongside disease-directed treatment. However, many eligible children remain under-recognized and underserved. We aimed to characterize acute healthcare utilization among children with life-limiting chronic conditions in Israel from diagnosis to death, with emphasis on the final year of life, and to compare utilization across age groups and geographic regions. This retrospective population-based cohort study used electronic medical records from Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest health maintenance organization. Children aged 0-18 years diagnosed with life-limiting or life-threatening chronic conditions between 2000 and 2025 were included. Healthcare utilization throughout follow-up was analyzed. The cohort included 83,419 children (59.2% male; mean age at diagnosis 5.9 ± 5.9 years), of whom 3267 (3.9%) died during follow-up. During the final year of life, 43.5% had ≥ 5 hospitalizations (mean 6.3 ± 7.7), 52.7% were admitted to the intensive care unit, and 16.0% had ≥ 5 emergency department visits. Community specialist consultations (49.1% with 5 or more) and X-ray imaging (40.4% with 5 or more) were frequent during the final year of life. In contrast, access to palliative care was minimal, with 95.7% of children who died receiving no palliative consultation and only 0.2% receiving hospice referral or pain consultation. Healthcare utilization differed significantly by age group and geographic region (both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Children with life-limiting conditions experience intensive acute healthcare utilization, particularly near the end of life, alongside extremely limited access to pediatric palliative care. These findings, aggregated across the 2000 to 2025 study period, do not capture temporal trends but rather highlight a persistent gap and support expansion of pediatric palliative care services.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children with life-limiting conditions have intense healthcare use near the end of life, and specialist pediatric palliative care is associated with less intensive acute care.

WHAT IS NEW: • In a nationwide Israeli cohort of 83,419 children, acute care was high across the whole disease course, yet >95% of those who died received no palliative consultation, a gap persisting under universal coverage.

articles.title: Features of cold adaptation in membrane proteins from psychrophilic bacteria: a gram-stratified comparative analysis across thermal niches.
articles.abstract: Membrane proteins must function within lipid bilayers whose physical properties vary with growth temperature, yet whether cold adaptation leaves detectable signatures in membrane protein sequences and structures beyond lipid remodeling remains unclear. Here we compare primary (17,431 proteins, 162 references) and tertiary structural properties derived from AlphaFold models (6,782 structures) across psychrophilic, mesophilic, and thermophilic bacteria spanning both Gram-negative and Gram-positive lineages. Using reference-anchored statistics to control for family composition effects, we find that the properties of transmembrane (TM) helix-helix length, aggregate hydropathy, packing density (PD), and relative solvent accessibility-show only modest thermal-group differences. In contrast, extra-membrane loop regions of Gram-negative multi-pass proteins reveal reproducible psychrophile-associated compositional shifts: increased Ile, Ser, Thr, Lys, and Asp; decreased Ala, Arg, Pro, and Leu. These patterns are mirrored by opposite shifts in thermophilic proteins, creating temperature-dependent gradients for key residues. Ser + Thr fraction emerges as the single most robust physicochemical signature at the primary sequence level, significant across both TM and non-TM regions. Tertiary structure analyses reveal increased kinks and interhelical H-bonds per helix in psychrophilic 12 TM proteins, in parallel with decreased PD and altered solvent accessibility contrast, suggesting subtle structural loosening. Critically, all trends are Gram-dependent: Gram-positive organisms show weaker and sometimes opposite patterns, suggesting that envelope architecture shapes the accessible design space for thermal adaptation. Taken together, the results in this study suggest that cold adaptation of bacterial membrane proteins proceeds primarily through non-TM loops and loop-region compositional adjustments alongside lipid-mediated homeoviscous adaptation, while TM helix cores remain constrained by hydrophobic matching requirements between helix and bilayer.

articles.title: From heat summation to climate adaptation: lessons from 75 years of the Winkler Index for agroclimatic metric design.
articles.abstract: Agroclimatic indices are foundational tools for matching crop cultivars to suitable climates, yet the accelerating pace of climate change is exposing the limits of indices built on mean conditions. The Winkler Index (WI) is a regional categorization system based on heat summation informed by wines made from grapes throughout California in the 1940s to 1960s, and it remains one of the most widely used agroclimatic indices in viticulture. This systematic review characterizes the main uses, themes, and contexts of the WI across 679 publications from 61 countries over 75 years, to identify broadly transferable principles for agroclimatic index design. The successes stem from its ability to predict a highly nuanced outcome-cultivar suitability and wine quality-from a simple, communicable metric. Its documented limitations, including a single thermal metric, fixed calendar thresholds, inability to capture extremes, variability, or evaporative demand, and coarse spatial resolution, mirror the limitations of analogous indices across cropping systems. As climate change intensifies the mismatch between mean-condition indices and increasingly volatile growing environments, the WI's trajectory offers a template for the next generation of bioclimatic indices across agricultural systems.

articles.title: Liver-brain axis: mechanisms, translational discoveries and therapies.
articles.abstract: The liver-brain axis, which refers to a dynamic, bidirectional crosstalk orchestrated through metabolic, immune, hormonal, and neural pathways, plays a pivotal role in modulating numerous physiological processes and is increasingly implicated in the pathogenesis of both hepatic and neurological diseases. Here, we review the mechanisms governing liver-brain communication, with particular emphasis on genetic, metabolic, and immunological interdependencies. We examine hepatic encephalopathy as an established neurological complication of liver disease, critically assess reported associations with neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric conditions, and review hepatic and systemic changes observed in neurological disorders. We highlight recent translational discoveries and therapeutic interventions targeting the liver-brain axis, including bile acid modulation, microbiota-derived signaling, and metabolic reprogramming. Special focus is given to energy expenditure, lipid and glucose homeostasis, and bile acid metabolism as central mediators of this systemic communication. The emerging insights into the liver-brain axis offer promising avenues for integrated treatment strategies.

articles.title: Medical and surgical complication rates following conversion total hip arthroplasty for intertrochanteric femur fractures: a propensity-matched analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intertrochanteric (IT) femur fractures are often managed with internal fixation, but subsequent complications may necessitate conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA). Comparative outcomes remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We identified patients undergoing THA from January 2014 through September 2023 in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Conversion THA followed prior IT fracture fixation; primary THA included all indications; and fracture THA was the index procedure for an acute IT fracture. We analyzed two comparisons: conversion THA (n = 1,790) versus primary THA (n = 209,902), and conversion THA (n = 1,732) versus fracture THA (n = 887). Following 1:1 propensity score matching, 1,788 and 883 pairs, respectively, were identified. Medical complications at 90 days, transfusion within 7 days, and surgical complications at 2 years were assessed.

RESULTS: Compared with primary THA, conversion THA was associated with higher odds of anemia (odds ratio [OR] 2.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.22-3.17), periprosthetic fracture (OR 5.02, 95% CI 3.47-7.28), and periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; OR 4.73, 95% CI 3.22-6.94). Compared with fracture THA, conversion THA was associated with lower odds of respiratory failure (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96) and urinary tract infection (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.94), and higher odds of periprosthetic fracture (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.23-2.60) and PJI (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.70-4.82).

CONCLUSION: Conversion THA was associated with higher odds of most measured complications than primary THA and higher odds of periprosthetic fracture and PJI than fracture THA. These findings suggest that the complexity of conversion procedures underscores the need for careful perioperative optimization, and support consideration of arthroplasty for selected IT fractures. Residual confounding and the exclusion of patients with successful fixation preclude conclusions about the superiority of arthroplasty over initial fixation. Future studies should directly compare arthroplasty with initial fixation to guide treatment selection.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III Therapeutic Study.

articles.title: Hepatic stellate cell-derived TGFα drives CCN2-dependent liver fibrosis via the EGFR-JNK/c-Jun signaling pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver fibrosis is a major cause of liver-associated morbidity and mortality, yet effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) are central fibrogenic effector cells. Transforming growth factor-α (TGFα), an EGF receptor (EGFR) ligand, participates in tissue remodeling, but its role in HSC activation and liver fibrogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated whether HSC-derived TGFα promotes liver fibrosis and explored the underlying mechanism.

METHODS: Publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets (GSE137720 and GSE171904) were analyzed to assess TGFα expression in HSCs following carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced liver injury. CCl4-treated mice were used to validate TGFα expression by immunofluorescence staining, RT-qPCR and western blotting (n = 6 per group). TGFβ-stimulated LX2 cells were used to mimic a profibrogenic microenvironment, and gain- and loss-of-function assays were performed to examine HSC activation, proliferation and migration.

RESULTS: TGFα expression was markedly upregulated in HSCs in fibrotic mouse livers and in TGFβ-stimulated LX2 cells. TGFα overexpression promoted HSC activation, as evidenced by increased expression levels of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), collagen, type I, alpha 1 (COL1A1) and collagen, type III, alpha 1 (COL3A1), alongside enhanced cell proliferation and migration. Conversely, knocking down TGFα led to the suppression of these fibrogenic responses. Mechanistically, TGFα activated EGFR-JNK/c-Jun signaling and upregulated cellular communication network factor 2 (CCN2). EGFR knockdown abolished JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation, reduced CCN2 expression and impaired HSC activation.

CONCLUSIONS: HSC‑derived TGFα functions as an upstream driver of CCN2‑dependent liver fibrosis via EGFR‑JNK/c‑Jun signaling, highlighting TGFα as a potential therapeutic target for antifibrotic intervention in chronic liver disease.

articles.title: The surgical management of spigelian hernias: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spigelian hernias (SH) account for 0.12% to 2% of abdominal hernias. They are rare lateral ventral hernias caused by a defect in the transversus abdominis aponeurosis, most commonly at the intersection of the linea semilunaris and arcuate line. We aimed to assess patient characteristics, surgical management, and postoperative outcomes after SH repair.

METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane, EMBASE, Web of Science, and LILACS were systematically searched without date or language restrictions for studies of patients undergoing SH repair. Two authors independently performed screening and data collection. Outcomes included operative time, hospital length of stay (LOS), seroma, hematoma, and surgical site infection (SSI). RStudio was used for statistical analysis.

RESULTS: The search identified 3,892 records, of which five studies met eligibility criteria. These included four retrospective and one prospective cohort spanning 2000-2020. Among 185 patients, 112 (60%) were female and 73 (40%) male. Laparoscopic repair was performed in 144 patients (77.8%), open repair in 38 (20%), and robotic repair in 3 (1.6%). Forty-two patients (22.7%) underwent emergent repair due to bowel incarceration, while 143 (77.3%) underwent elective repair. Pooled hematoma, seroma, and SSI rates were 4.49% (95% CI 1.69-11.37), 12.44% (95% CI 4.98-27.7), and 5% (95% CI 2.26-10.7), respectively. Mean operative time was 57.7 min (95% CI 38.2-87), and mean hospital LOS was 1 day (95% CI 0.5-1.9).

CONCLUSIONS: SH are rare abdominal wall hernias with female predominance in this pooled cohort. Overall, 22.7% required emergent repair due to incarceration. SSI and hematoma rates were low, hospital LOS was short, and seroma was the most frequently reported postoperative complication. Larger studies with standardized long-term follow-up are needed to better characterize outcomes after SH repair.

articles.title: Dual anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibody-positivity in suspected immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy: a case-based review.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by severe proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase (CK). IMNM is generally classified as anti-signal recognition particle (SRP)-positive, anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR)-positive, or seronegative. Concurrent anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR positivity is exceedingly uncommon, and its clinical significance remains uncertain. A 63-year-old man with prior statin exposure presented with progressive proximal lower-extremity weakness and rhabdomyolysis (CK > 12,000 U/L). MRI demonstrated bilateral symmetric muscle edema and post-contrast enhancement consistent with inflammatory myopathy. Although CK initially declined with intravenous fluids and statin discontinuation, weakness persisted and marked CK elevation recurred. Five days later, he was readmitted and diagnosed with sigmoid adenocarcinoma with nodal metastases. Serologic testing was positive for both anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibodies, supporting a presumptive clinical diagnosis of IMNM; muscle biopsy and EMG were not performed. Immunosuppression was initially deferred because of active infection and postoperative instability related to newly diagnosed malignancy. Following clinical stabilization, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) was administered over two days, followed shortly thereafter by methylprednisolone. Gradual functional improvement was observed, and the patient was discharged on a tapering glucocorticoid regimen with planned monthly IVIG. A structured literature search identified six publications describing 11 reported cases of dual anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP antibody positivity, although potential overlap among retrospective cohorts precluded determination of the exact number of unique individuals. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with this rare serologic profile. Persistent or recurrent proximal weakness and marked CK elevation despite statin withdrawal should prompt consideration of IMNM. Treatment may require individualization when infection, malignancy, or other comorbidities limit conventional immunosuppression. The clinical significance and potential malignancy associations of dual seropositivity remain uncertain and warrant further study.

articles.title: Caregiving experiences of family caregivers of patients with a urostomy after radical cystectomy for bladder cancer: a meta-synthesis of qualitative studies.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore the caregiving experiences of family caregivers of patients with urinary stomas.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in seven English databases (PubMed, Embase, ProQuest, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CINAHL, and EBSCO) and three Chinese databases (CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP) to identify qualitative studies exploring the caregiving experiences of family caregivers of patients with urinary stomas from database inception to April 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. The findings were synthesized using the JBI meta-aggregation approach and reported in accordance with the Enhancing Transparency in Reporting Qualitative Syntheses (ENTREQ) guidelines.

RESULTS: A total of 11 studies were included. Thirty-two findings were aggregated into eight categories, leading to three synthesized findings: the accumulation of multidimensional burdens from initial postoperative shock to long-term caregiving exhaustion; family caregivers' supportive care needs and experiences with external support; and personal growth and life reconstruction through active adaptation to the caregiving role.

CONCLUSIONS: Family caregivers of patients with urinary stomas experience persistent multidimensional burdens, ranging from initial postoperative shock to long-term caregiving exhaustion, and report unmet needs for professional, social, and family support. Nevertheless, some family caregivers demonstrate personal growth and life reconstruction through active adaptation to the caregiving role. Multidimensional support strategies integrating professional, family, and community resources should be developed to address caregivers' unmet needs, alleviate caregiving burdens, and support their adaptation to caregiving roles.

articles.title: Pediatric versus adult moyamoya disease and syndrome: Hypertension, syndromic risk, and in-hospital outcomes in a national inpatient analysis of an estimated 69,000 hospitalizations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moyamoya disease (MMD) demonstrates age-dependent phenotypes, but national comparative outcome data remain limited. We compared comorbidities, treatment use, and predictors of adverse in-hospital outcomes between pediatric and adult MMD. The National Inpatient Sample (NIS) cannot differentiate idiopathic MMD from moyamoya syndrome, and sickle cell-related moyamoya cannot be isolated in this dataset; "MMD" here therefore denotes the combined cohort.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional analysis of the NIS (2003-2020). Applying HCUP discharge weights, 13,853 unweighted moyamoya-coded discharges represented approximately 69,000 hospitalizations. Hospitalizations were stratified into pediatric (≤ 18 years) and adult cohorts. Outcomes were ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), and in-hospital mortality, ascertained from discharge-record codes. Weighted multivariable logistic regression adjusted for comorbidities, race or ethnicity, payer, income quartile and tobacco use, with design-based variance in which sampling strata recovered from the discharge weights served as primary sampling units.

RESULTS: Adults accounted for 80.9% of hospitalizations and children for 19.1%. Adults had higher rates of ischemic stroke (25.0% vs. 15.9%), hemorrhagic stroke (6.9% vs. 2.9%), SAH (5.6% vs. 1.4%), and mortality (2.4% vs. 0.9%) (all p < 0.001). Pediatric age was associated with lower odds of mortality (aOR 0.37, 95% CI 0.24-0.58), hemorrhagic stroke (aOR 0.42, 0.33-0.52), and SAH (aOR 0.26, 0.19-0.37), with no difference in ischemic stroke (aOR 0.96, 0.83-1.11). Hypertension was associated with all four outcomes (aOR 1.60 to 2.21) and carried the largest comorbidity estimate for each cerebrovascular outcome; for mortality the largest was myocardial infarction (aOR 2.19, 1.31-3.68). Bypass was associated with lower odds of mortality (aOR 0.41, 0.23-0.72), hemorrhagic stroke (aOR 0.50, 0.37-0.68), and SAH (aOR 0.53, 0.37-0.75), but not ischemic stroke (aOR 0.98, 0.84-1.16). Down syndrome was associated with ischemic stroke (aOR 1.84, 1.42-2.37); its association with mortality did not reach significance (aOR 1.89, 0.98-3.64).

CONCLUSION: Hypertension was the comorbidity most consistently associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes. Bypass was associated with lower odds of hemorrhagic events and mortality, but patients selected for surgery differ systematically from those managed conservatively, so the direction of any true effect cannot be determined. All reported outcomes are discharge record-level coded associations, not proven causal effects, and because the NIS carries no present-on-admission indicator they cannot separate disease present at admission from in-hospital complications. Prospective confirmation is required.

articles.title: Effects of waiting-room-initiated music on self-reported dental anxiety, physiological responses, and cortisol-oxytocin relationship during restorative dental treatment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This randomized controlled clinical study evaluated the effects of waiting-room music on self-reported dental anxiety, physiological responses, salivary cortisol and oxytocin, and their associations during restorative treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety healthy adults with moderate dental anxiety (MDAS 10-18) were randomized into control, waiting-room music (BM), and music continued throughout treatment (FM) groups (n = 30). MDAS was assessed before and after treatment. Physiological parameters were recorded at four time points, and salivary hormones at three time points.

RESULTS: MDAS scores decreased significantly after treatment in all groups (p < 0.001), without significant group or interaction effects. Oxygen saturation (p = 0.002) and body temperature (p = 0.025) differed among groups. Both blood pressures changed over time, with a significant systolic group × time interaction (p = 0.001). Hormonal levels showed no significant between-group differences. However, significant positive cortisol-oxytocin correlations were observed in the FM group, whereas significant negative correlations were found in the Control group.

CONCLUSIONS: Music initiated in the dental waiting room did not provide an additional reduction in self-reported dental anxiety and showed limited effects on physiological parameters. However, exploratory correlation analyses revealed positive cortisol-oxytocin correlations in the FM group, where music continued throughout treatment, and negative correlations in the Control group. These should be interpreted cautiously, as pre-existing cortisol-oxytocin associations at baseline (T0) may have influenced the results. The findings require further investigation to clarify their biological and clinical significance.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Music initiated in the dental waiting room and continued throughout restorative treatment may serve as a simple, non-invasive supportive intervention. Although its benefits on self-reported dental anxiety and physiological anxiety parameters were not demonstrated, the observed cortisol-oxytocin correlation patterns warrant further investigation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07274501. This study was registered at www.
