articles.title: Identifying GAN mutations in three families with giant axonal neuropathy: a clinical study and literature review.
articles.abstract: Giant Axonal Neuropathy (GAN) is a very rare autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disease caused by mutations in the GAN gene encoding gigaxonin protein. Mutation in the GAN gene causes dysfunction in gigaxonin protein leading to abnormal accumulation of neurofilaments causing sensory and motor dysfunctions. The present article highlights the clinical profile, electrophysiology, and genetics of six patients belonging to three unrelated Indian families having Giant Axonal Neuropathy. These cases had an average age of onset of 5.17 years with symptoms such as progressive gait disturbance, distal muscle weakness, and recurrent falls. Prominent clinical features included nystagmus, foot deformities. Kinky hair, which is a characteristic finding was absent in all of our patients. Neurophysiologically, these patients showed signs of severe sensory and motor axonal polyneuropathy with significant reduction in mean CMAP amplitude (1.48mV) and motor nerve conduction velocity (37.17m/s). MRI scan showed typical neuroimaging findings of symmetrical diffuse deep white matter hyperintensity with sparing of the U-fibers along with severe cervical cord atrophy. Genetically, we reported three homozygous variants such as novel missense mutation (p.Tyr347Cys) in Family 1, novel 3' splice site proximal mutation (c.1237-3 C > G) in Family 2, and large (~ 76.37 KB) deletion of GAN and BCO1 in Family 3. The identification of these novel mutations expands the known genetic spectrum of GAN. Early diagnosis through integrated neuroimaging and genetic testing is crucial for effective clinical management and genetic counseling to prevent recurrence in affected families.

articles.title: Endobronchial Ultrasound-Guided Transbronchial Needle Aspiration and Transbronchial Biopsy for Peripheral Pulmonary Lesions in Patients with Interstitial Lung Disease: A Phase Ⅱ Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The addition of radial endobronchial ultrasound (r-EBUS)-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (TBNA) to transbronchial biopsy (TBB) may improve the relationship between the r-EBUS probe and target lesion, helping overcome the limited efficacy of TBB alone. However, the efficacy and safety of this sequential procedure for peripheral pulmonary lesions (PPLs) in patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unknown. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance and safety of r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB for PPLs in patients with ILD.

METHODS: In a single-center, single-arm, phase Ⅱ trial, patients with PPLs and concomitant ILD were prospectively enrolled to undergo r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB under virtual bronchoscopy navigation and fluoroscopy. The primary endpoint was the diagnostic yield for PPLs. Secondary outcomes included improvement in r-EBUS findings, procedural time, and safety.

RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were analyzed, excluding one patient who was found to have an endobronchial lesion during bronchoscopy. The median maximum lesion diameter on computed tomography was 22.3 mm (range: 11.2-70.3 mm). The diagnostic yield for PPLs in patients with ILD was 78.7% (37/47 patients, lower 95% confidence interval: 66.6%, P < 0.001). Improvement in r-EBUS findings during TBNA/TBB procedures was observed in 70.8% (17/24 patients, 95% confidence interval: 48.9-87.4%). The median procedural time was approximately 50 min. Pneumothorax occurred in two patients, one of whom required thoracic drainage.

CONCLUSION: This phase II study suggested that sequential r-EBUS-guided TBNA followed by TBB might be a useful diagnostic approach for PPLs in patients with ILD, with no serious adverse events observed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: jRCT1042230076.

articles.title: 3D-CT-guided patient-specific instrumentation versus conventional implants for traumatic malunited distal radius corrective osteotomies: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Corrective osteotomy for traumatic malunited distal radius fractures has traditionally relied on conventional pre-contoured plates. Patient-specific instrumentation (PSI) with three-dimensional (3D) CT-guided planning offers theoretical advantages through individualised design and improved anatomical fit, but comparative clinical evidence remains limited. We aimed to evaluate functional outcomes and complications following patient-specific versus conventional implants for distal radius corrective osteotomy.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, including MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and CINAHL databases for studies published up to September 2025. Clinical studies directly comparing PSI with conventional implants, and single-arm PSI studies, were included. Meta-analyses were performed when two or more studies reported identical outcome measures, using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool (RoB-1).

RESULTS: Eighteen studies (15 single-arm PSI, three comparative) with 321 patients (282 PSI, 39 conventional) were included; mean follow-up was 14.4 ± 5.5 months and mean age 46.8 ± 7.3 years. For radiological parameters, volar tilt showed a pooled mean difference (MD) of - 8.87° (95% CI - 11.42 to - 6.32; I2 = 0.0%) favouring less volar tilt with PSI; radial inclination showed a pooled MD of - 0.89° (95% CI - 4.19 to 2.41; I² = 0.0%); and ulnar variance a pooled MD of 1.19 mm (95% CI - 0.40 to 2.78; I² =265.9%). Flexion-extension improved by 26.63°, with a final pooled arc of 134.69° (95% CI 117.73 to 154.08). Pronation-supination improved by 23.33°, with a final arc of 159.71° (95% CI 153.83 to 165.81). The pooled complication rate was 4% (95% CI 1% to 7%) and the revision risk ratio was 0.60 (95% CI 0.27 to 1.35; I2 = 0.0%) for PSI.

CONCLUSION: There was a promising trend towards fewer complications and revision surgery with PSI. Both techniques achieved acceptable radiological restoration, with PSI conferring a modest advantage in ulnar variance but resulting in slight under-correction of volar tilt. Functional outcomes and range of motion improved to a clinically meaningful degree with both approaches, though this was accompanied by substantial heterogeneity between studies. High-quality randomised controlled trials are required to confirm these findings and to justify the additional costs associated with PSI technology.

articles.title: Trends in inpatient surgical treatment of multifragmentary proximal radius fractures in Germany, 2010-2024: a nationwide analysis of procedure statistics.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Operative treatment of proximal radius fractures is reported to have increased, but it is unclear how much of the increase reflects demographic change and whether the balance between osteosynthesis and arthroplasty has shifted. We describe inpatient operative treatment of proximal radius fractures coded as multifragmentary in Germany, 2010-2024, and how coding, denominators and care setting affect its interpretation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: DRG procedure statistics of the Federal Statistical Office identified osteosynthesis of multifragmentary articular fractures of the proximal radius (OPS 5-794.*4) and radial head arthroplasty (OPS 5-824.3). Rates were modelled with quasi-Poisson, the arthroplasty proportion with quasi-binomial regression; Kitagawa decomposition separated demographic change. Sub-period analyses, alternative denominators and a coding-drift indicator were added.

RESULTS: Procedures rose from 5,351 to 7,163 (+ 33.9%), mainly before 2020 (rate ratio 1.026 per year, 95% CI 1.017-1.035); demographic change explained 6-13%. The share of multifragmentary codes among open reductions rose from 64.1% to 70.0%. The proportion of arthroplasty rose from 13.8% to 16.8% between 2010 and 2013, stayed at 15.6-17.3% until 2022 without a trend (odds ratio 0.994 per year, 95% CI 0.986-1.002) and reached 19.9% in 2024, probably inflated by a shift of osteosynthesis to the outpatient sector.

CONCLUSIONS: The data do not show a steady shift from osteosynthesis towards arthroplasty. Code counts depend on coding, denominators and care setting; without indication, fracture classification and outcome, the statistics cannot show whether treatment decisions changed.

articles.title: Surgical anatomy of the hypoglossal canal - systematic review with meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hypoglossal canal (HC) is a vital conduit for the hypoglossal nerve (CN XII) and venous structures. Variations in its morphology, particularly bony septations, can complicate skull-base surgeries such as transcondylar or far-lateral approaches. This study aims to provide a meta-analysis of HC prevalence, morphometry, and surgical landmarks.

MATERIALS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through December 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Pooled prevalence and mean dimensions were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses explored the impact of sex, side, nationality, and study type. Leave-one-out analysis was performed to evaluate the source of heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Thirty-three studies involving 10,132 skulls were included. The pooled prevalence of a typical (non-septated) HC was 60.39% (95% CI: 46.67-73.34). Variations occurred in nearly 40% of cases, including incomplete (18.85%) and complete (17.74%) septations. A significant discrepancy was found between study types: cadaveric studies reported a complete septation prevalence of 35.39%, while imaging studies detected only 9.03% (p = 0.0070). Morphometric analysis established the HC is located within a mean distance of 10.0-10.8 mm (95% CI: 9.12-12.11) from the posterior and anterior margins of the occipital condyle. No significant differences were observed based on sex or laterality. Substantial heterogeneity and potential publication bias through asymmetry test was detected.

CONCLUSIONS: Structural variations of the HC are frequent developmental variants rather than rare anomalies. The significant under-detection of septations by imaging suggests that standard preoperative CT may overlook complex neural or venous partitioning. A 10 mm distance from the condylar margins may serve as a practical anatomical reference for individual preoperative assessment to avoid iatrogenic injury to CN XII during condylar drilling.

articles.title: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens following total hip arthroplasty due to acetabular screw penetration of the external iliac vein: a case report and review of the literature.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Phlegmasia cerulea dolens (PCD) is a rare, life-threatening complication of total hip arthroplasty (THA). We report a fatal case caused by acetabular screw penetration of the external iliac vein (EIV), and review the literature on this complication.

METHODS: We describe the presentation, diagnostic findings, and management of a single case. We compare it with previously published reports of EIV injury and PCD following THA.

RESULTS: A 61-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes developed PCD approximately 24 h after left THA. She presented with hemodynamic instability, severe lactic acidosis, and a cold, cyanotic, pulseless left leg. Preoperative CT showed partial occlusion of the left EIV next to an acetabular screw. At surgery, the screw had penetrated and torqued into the EIV. Emergency open thrombectomy, laparotomy for proximal vascular control, EIV resection with polytetrafluoroethylene graft reconstruction, and fasciotomy were performed. Despite transient improvement, she developed progressive rhabdomyolysis, disseminated intravascular coagulopathy, and refractory multiorgan failure. She died on postoperative day 7. This course is most consistent with systemic reperfusion injury after prolonged venous ischemia.

CONCLUSION: EIV injury after THA can present as venous occlusion and PCD rather than intraoperative hemorrhage, delaying recognition. Iliac vein occlusion next to an acetabular screw on CT should raise suspicion of screw penetration. Prolonged ischemia may carry a high risk of fatal reperfusion syndrome after revascularization. Primary amputation deserves earlier and more explicit consideration in this setting. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of THA-related PCD from Vietnam.

articles.title: Impact of slit versus non-slit mesh on recurrence after inguinal hernia repair: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inguinal hernia repair is among the most frequently performed operations worldwide, and durable mesh-based repair is the standard of care. During laparo-endoscopic repair, surgeons choose between slit and non-slit mesh to accommodate the cord structures, yet the optimal configuration remains uncertain. We aimed to determine whether slit mesh, compared with non-slit mesh, reduces recurrence without increasing chronic groin pain or mesh-related complications.

METHODS: We searched Embase, PubMed and Scopus for comparative studies of slit versus non-slit mesh in adults undergoing inguinal hernia repair. Randomised controlled trials and prospective or retrospective comparative cohorts were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB-2 and the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, with certainty rated using GRADE. Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as odds ratios (OR) and continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD), using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation as the primary analysis. Sensitivity analyses used the DerSimonian-Laird and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) estimators, the latter recommended when few studies contribute to an outcome. Recurrence was also analysed by study design, by leave-one-out analysis and using adjusted effect estimates where available. Heterogeneity was quantified with the I2 statistic.

RESULTS: Six comparative studies were included: one quasi-randomised trial and five retrospective cohorts. The trial reported no recurrence in either arm, so five studies (3,825 hernias or patients) contributed to the pooled recurrence estimate. In the primary REML analysis, slit mesh was associated with lower recurrence (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.91; P = 0.028; I2 = 33.5%). This finding was not robust. With the HKSJ adjustment the interval was 0.14 to 1.32 (P = 0.105), and the 95% prediction interval was 0.06 to 3.11. Omitting Chue et al. (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.39) or Zarras et al. (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.16 to 1.46) removed statistical significance. The association was confined to these two propensity-adjusted or matched cohorts, which had the shortest follow-up (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.67), and was absent in the three unadjusted cohorts (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.10 to 3.08). Chronic pain (5 studies; OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.96 to 2.10; P = 0.080), operative time and length of stay did not differ significantly. Certainty of evidence was very low for all outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of slit mesh on recurrence compared with non-slit mesh. The point estimate favoured slit mesh, but the association depends on two observational cohorts with short follow-up and does not persist under HKSJ estimation. Its plausible range is compatible with both a substantial reduction and an increase in recurrence. The evidence is also very uncertain about the effect of slit mesh on chronic pain, and a modest increase in chronic pain cannot be excluded. This evidence does not support overturning existing international guideline caution against routine mesh slitting. Adequately powered randomised data with standardised slit technique and longer follow-up are needed before either configuration can be recommended over the other.

articles.title: Echocardiography in ARDS: beyond imaging, toward bedside decision-making.
Same-day, one-bag rapid desensitization for pertuzumab hypersensitivity: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pertuzumab is a cornerstone of HER2-positive breast cancer therapy but can elicit hypersensitivity reactions (HSRs) that jeopardize optimal oncologic care. Rapid drug desensitization (RDD) enables safe re-exposure when no equivalent alternatives exist. We report a two-patient case series using a same-day, one-bag, 10-step RDD protocol after severe immediate HSRs to pertuzumab.

CASE PRESENTATION: Two female patients with triple-positive breast cancer developed immediate HSRs during pertuzumab administration. Both had received premedication with dexamethasone, ondansetron, and chloropyramine. They were both managed per anaphylaxis guidelines and, upon stabilization, underwent same-day one-bag, 10-step RDD under continuous monitoring. Case 1: A 40-year-old woman initially developed dyspnea, wheezing, and chest tightness during her first pertuzumab infusion. These symptoms resolved spontaneously and were initially attributed to her underlying pulmonary disease and pleural effusion. Four weeks later, during a conventional full-dose re-exposure, she developed generalized urticaria, labial and lingual angioedema, hypoxemia (SpO₂ 89%), and hypotension (80/60 mmHg) after receiving approximately 140 mg of pertuzumab. The reaction was treated with intramuscular epinephrine and intravenous saline. Same-day RDD was subsequently completed without breakthrough reactions. Case 2: A 39-year-old woman developed facial flushing, fever, headache, dyspnea, chest tightness, a choking sensation, hypoxemia (SpO₂ 90%), hypertension (150/90 mmHg), and lower back pain 16 min into her third pertuzumab infusion, after receiving approximately 112 mg. She received intramuscular epinephrine, supplemental oxygen, and intravenous saline. Same-day RDD was successfully performed. The same protocol was subsequently repeated during cycles 4, 5, and 6 without breakthrough reactions.

CONCLUSIONS: These cases describe the use of a single-bag, 10-step RDD protocol for pertuzumab after severe immediate HSRs. Although the experience is limited to two patients, successful administration of the prescribed dose was achieved in both cases. Further studies are needed to evaluate the reproducibility, safety, and potential advantages of this simplified approach.

articles.title: [18F]FDG‑PET/CT screening in infective endocarditis detects both symptomatic and asymptomatic extracardiac lesions of clinical relevance.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Extracardiac complications (ECC) influence prognosis and management in infective endocarditis (IE) substantially. Although [18F]FDG-PET/CT is recommended for symptomatic patients, the value in unselected IE populations remains uncertain.

METHODS: Retrospective multicenter study evaluating consecutive patients with suspected or definite IE undergoing [18F]FDG-PET/CT screening in the Region of Southern Denmark (January-August 2025). Extracardiac findings were registered per-lesion. Clinical impact was defined as any downstream consequence attributable to a [18F]FDG-PET/CT-detected lesion, irrespective of the clinical relevance. Significant clinical impact required a clinically relevant lesion affecting patient management.

RESULTS: Extracardiac lesions were detected in 120/152 patients with clinical impact in 61 and significant clinical impact in 34 (39 lesions), corresponding to a number needed to screen of 4-5. Of the 39 lesions with significant clinical impact, 18 were symptomatic and 21 asymptomatic, including malignancies, visceral septic embolism, and drainable foci. Vertebral infection was suspected in 15 patients and confirmed in 13; only 2 lacked prescan back pain, indicating that [18F]FDG-PET/CT rarely identifies asymptomatic spondylodiscitis. In contrast, among 15 patients infected with gut-associated streptococci, [18F]FDG-PET/CT revealed colonic foci in 8 asymptomatic cases, all leading to polypectomy, thereby removing a lesion that may have been relevant to the pathogenesis of IE.

CONCLUSION: Systematic [18F]FDG-PET/CT screening generated substantial subsequent diagnostic workload with limited clinical value, as lesions affecting patient management were detected in only a minority. Half of these occurred in patients without prescan symptoms, thereby raising the possibility that [18F]FDG-PET/CT may have a role in specific asymptomatic subgroups beyond the guideline‑recommended symptom‑driven application.

articles.title: Glymphatic dysfunction links neuropsychiatric symptoms to cognitive decline via neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPSs) are prevalent in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the mechanistic link to glymphatic dysfunction remains unclear.

METHODS: In this multi-cohort study (Chinese discovery cohort, n = 212; Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative [ADNI; n = 446]), NPSs were assessed via the Neuropsychiatric Inventory Questionnaire (NPI-Q) and categorized into hyperactivity, psychosis, affective, and apathy subsyndromes. The diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index was used as a noninvasive imaging proxy related to glymphatic function. Cross-sectional associations of NPSs with ALPS-index, cognition, brain structures, and positron emission tomography (PET) measures (ADNI only) were examined. In ADNI, longitudinal trajectories were evaluated by NPSs-ALPS phenotypes, followed by exploratory survival analyses of cognitive progression and amyloid conversion. Mediation analyses examined whether ALPS-index and neurodegeneration mediated the NPSs-cognition association. A multivariable Cox nomogram incorporating NPI-Q score, ALPS-index, APOE ε4 status, and demographics was developed and internally validated for cognitive progression.

RESULTS: NPSs, particularly apathy subsyndrome, were associated with lower ALPS-index, poorer cognition, and brain atrophy across cohorts. In ADNI, NPSs were additionally associated with AD-related PET pathology. Lower ALPS-index and brain atrophy/PET pathology, individually or jointly, mediated the NPSs-cognition association. Longitudinally, the NPSs + Low_ALPS phenotype showed greater cognitive and neuroimaging deterioration and higher risks of cognitive progression (HR = 2.63) and amyloid conversion (HR = 6.17) than the non-NPSs + High_ALPS phenotype. Similar patterns were observed for Apathy-ALPS phenotypes. The nomogram showed acceptable discrimination for cognitive progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower ALPS-index values, reflecting altered glymphatic function, may link NPSs with cognitive decline through neurodegenerative changes in AD. Integrating NPSs with the ALPS-index could provide complementary information for characterizing disease progression and risk stratification.

articles.title: Combined high-intensity interval training and propionate supplementation attenuate ventricular remodeling and cognitive decline in a rat model of heart failure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Heart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by progressive ventricular remodeling, chronic inflammation, and functional decline, often accompanied by cognitive deficits. Although pharmacological therapies improve symptoms, residual morbidity persists, highlighting the need for effective non‑pharmacological strategies. High‑intensity interval training (HIIT(and gut microbiota metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids, may benefit cardiac and cognitive outcomes, but their combined effects in HF are unclear.

METHODS: Forty male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to control, HF, HF + Propionate (1000 mg/kg orally), HF + HIIT, and HF + HIIT + Propionate groups. HF was induced via subcutaneous isoproterenol injections (130 mg/kg over four days). A 6-week low-volume HIIT program (three sessions per week) after HF confirmation. Cardiac structure and function were evaluated by echocardiography. Systemic inflammation and cardiac stress markers (TNF-α, IL-10, CRP, and BNP), myocardial fibrosis, and spatial memory were assessed.

RESULTS: HF induced marked ventricular dysfunction, elevated BNP and CRP levels, increased myocardial fibrosis, and impaired spatial memory. Both HIIT and propionate independently reduced systemic inflammation and myocardial collagen deposition compared with HF. The combined intervention produced greater improvements in ejection fraction and fractional shortening, increased IL-10, and reduced TNF-α. Preservation of spatial memory was observed only in the combined group (p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: The combination of propionate supplementation and low-volume HIIT effectively improves ventricular remodeling, reduces inflammation and fibrosis, and attenuates cognitive impairment in rats with heart failure.

articles.title: [Clinical guideline on synovialectomy : The role of synovialectomy in inflammatory rheumatic diseases and specific synovial pathologies].
articles.abstract: Modern basic drug therapies have fundamentally revolutionised the treatment of inflammatory rheumatic diseases. However, treatment-resistant inflammation in individual joints-so-called 'rebellious joints'-is often overlooked. This article highlights the indispensable role of synovialectomy as a targeted local therapy for preventing irreversible joint destruction. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, the key steps in step-by-step diagnosis, histopathological confirmation using the synovitis score, and interdisciplinary perioperative management are presented in a practical manner. Furthermore, using specific indications as examples, the article clarifies when and how local intervention ensures joint preservation. It offers sound guidance for the tailored care of your rheumatology patients at the interface between rheumatology, orthopaedics and trauma surgery.

articles.title: VEGFR-2 missense variants as modulators of cancer therapeutic response: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Missense variants of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) may impact the efficacy of VEGFR-2 inhibitors due to structural alterations at drug target site. These variants may also influence the efficacy of non-VEGFR-2 inhibitors by impacting the angiogenesis initiation, downstream signalling of VEGFR-2, metabolism, alternate signalling pathways, and the immune microenvironment. This review aims to systematically analyse the translational bridge between VEGFR-2 missense variants and therapeutic response in different cancer types.

METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 Statement guidelines and systematically identified 29 peer reviewed cohort studies, clinical trials, case reports, case series, and preclinical experimental studies published from January, 2015 to August, 2025.

RESULTS: The VEGFR-2 variants Q472H, T771R, R1032Q, and V297I were among the most frequently reported variants in different types of cancer. Variant Q472H showed variable associations with therapeutic response, with some studies reporting better response to VEGFR-2 inhibitors, whereas others reported poor response or treatment resistance to vandetanib and sunitinib. Variant R1032Q was found in patients responding better to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and pazopanib. VEGFR-2 T771R was reported to be associated with poor therapeutic response.

CONCLUSION: The selected studies suggest some benefits in therapeutic response for VEGFR-2 inhibitors and tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), but poor response to chemotherapeutic agents in presence of the missense variants across different cancer types. However, as these observations originated from a limited set of studies with heterogenous methodologies, the identified variant-treatment associations should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require validation through well-designed prospective clinical studies and larger cohorts.

articles.title: Dose-Response and Temporal Patterns of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Idiopathic Overactive Bladder: A Model-Based Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: OnabotulinumtoxinA is effective for idiopathic overactive bladder (OAB), but its dose-time benefit-risk profile is uncertain. We characterised dose-dependent efficacy and safety over time.

METHODS: PROSPERO-registered (CRD420261471347), this review searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the CENTRAL through 6 August 2026, for randomised controlled trials of fixed-dose onabotulinumtoxinA (50-300 U) versus placebo or another dose in adults with idiopathic/non-neurogenic OAB. Efficacy used Bayesian joint dose-response/time-course model-based network meta-analysis; cumulative safety used a complementary log-log model with follow-up time offset. Risk of bias and confidence were assessed using the revised Cochrane risk of bias tool (RoB 2) and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA).

RESULTS: Sixteen trials included 2841 participants. Model-estimated 12-week mean differences for 100 U versus placebo were -1.67, -2.37, and -1.19 episodes/24 h for frequency, urgency, and urgency urinary incontinence (UUI), respectively. Benefit for frequency and urgency extended through 200 U, whereas UUI showed little additional improvement beyond 100 and 150 U. Safety models estimated increased urinary tract infection, retention, and clean intermittent catheterisation (CIC) hazards with 100-300 U versus placebo. Twelve-week CIC risk was 4.7% with 100 U and 10.4% with 200 U (hazard ratio [HR] 2.28, 95% credible interval [CrI] 1.11-5.15, 95% predictive interval (0.68-8.66)). Evidence was sparse for 300 U and active-dose comparisons; heterogeneity and bias reduced confidence in some estimates.

CONCLUSIONS: Benefits above the licensed 100-U dose were modest, particularly for urgency urinary incontinence. Their clinical importance and benefit-risk balance require confirmation in adequately powered randomised head-to-head trials.

articles.title: 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT was complemented by 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT for benign insulinoma imaging, with histopathology validation.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the role of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and the histopathology analysis in patients with suspected insulinoma.

METHODS: 100 patients with suspected insulinoma were enrolled. Diagnostic performance, semi-quantitative parameter values, and immunoreactivity score (IRS) were compared. Correlation of GLP-1R and SSTR2 IRS was analyzed with semi-quantitative parameters, maximum tumor diameter, and Ki-67 index.

RESULTS: 51 patients and 11 patients were confirmed as insulinoma with histopathology and consensus of the multidisciplinary team (MDT), respectively. The combination of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT achieved superior diagnostic performance, reducing false-negative results compared to single-tracer PET/CT. The dual-tracer PET/CT demonstrated higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value (NPV) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 (NPV, p < 0.05) and 68Ga-DOTATATE (all p < 0.001). In G1 lesions, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed significantly higher SUVmax (49.55 ± 37.69 vs. 22.46 ± 14.38, p = 0.035) and TBR (12.38 ± 6.55 vs. 6.71 ± 4.59, p = 0.029) than 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT. These results were in accordance with elevated SSTR2 IRS compared with GLP-1R IRS (8.60 ± 1.92 vs. 6.01 ± 1.87, p = 0.002). In G2 lesions, SUVmax, TBR, and GLP-1R IRS were slightly higher on 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT (p > 0.05). SSTR2 IRS was positively associated with maximum tumor diameter (r = 0.358, p = 0.025) and negatively associated with the Ki-67 index (r = -0.547, p < 0.001). SUVmax and TBR of 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 and 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT showed positive correlations with their corresponding IRS (all p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT is recommended as the first-line functional imaging modality for patients with suspected insulinoma. When 68Ga-NOTA-Exendin-4 PET/CT shows negative results, 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT serves a complementary role. These were in accordance with the different expression of GLP-1R and SSTR2 between G1 and G2 insulinomas.

articles.title: Clinic vs. Screen: Comparing Fully In-Person to Virtual-Plus-In-Person Cardiac Fitness and Rehabilitation Programs for Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fitness and rehabilitation programs offer meaningful benefits for individuals with congenital heart disease (CHD), and newer delivery models include hybrid formats combining virtual and in-person training. Our program added a hybrid option that started in 2021. We hypothesized that the convenience of hybrid delivery would improve program adherence and patient satisfaction while remaining safe and effective compared with in-person training alone. In this retrospective cohort study of 158 participants with CHD between 2017 and 2025 (70 in-person only, 88 hybrid), groups were similar at baseline, including distance traveled, except for baseline percent predicted peak oxygen consumption (pppVO2) (p = 0.001) and FORCE risk category, as expected (p = 0.003). Both groups improved in pppVO2, strength, and flexibility, and no major adverse events occurred across a total of 2,018 in-person and 761 virtual sessions. Mindset improved among hybrid but not in-person participants. There were no significant between-group differences for physical fitness or mindset outcomes after adjustment for FORCE level, baseline pppVO2, and era effect (2017-2020 vs. 2021-2025). Contrary to our hypothesis, adherence (median 19 vs. 16 sessions, p = 0.12) and satisfaction were similar, and hybrid participants who rated both formats preferred their in-person sessions over their virtual (p < 0.001). Thus, both delivery models were associated with meaningful improvements without major adverse events, and hybrid delivery was associated with improvements comparable to fully in-person programming. The preference for in-person sessions suggests that direct social connection is valued. As the field moves toward technology-enabled delivery, these findings support flexible models that integrate virtual training while preserving in-person connection.

articles.title: SGLT2i Use and Safety in Congenital Heart Disease: An Analysis of the ACTION Heart Failure Registry.
articles.abstract: Based on favorable data in the adult population, sodium-glucose cotransport-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been introduced in children with heart failure (HF) including those with congenital heart disease (CHD). We sought to determine the pattern and safety of SGLT2i in children with HF due to CHD (CHD-HF) using the ACTION HF registry. We queried the ACTION HF registry for patients ≤ 18 years with CHD who were started on an SGLT2i between (7/6/2020-1/15/2025). Demographics, clinical characteristics, adverse events (AEs), and discontinuation rates were collected and analyzed. Of 365 patients started on SGLT2i, 28.5% (n = 104/365) had CHD [61.5%, (n = 64/104) univentricular and 38.5% (n = 40/104) biventricular]. The median age was 11.1 years (IQR 6.2-14.4). At the time of initiation, 49% (51/104) had at least moderate-to-severely depressed systolic function and 26% (27/104) had HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Follow-up data were available for 75 patients at a median of 163 days (IQR 76.0 -325.5). In follow-up, 6% (n = 5/75) had discontinued the SGLT2i due to AEs. In total, 14.7% (n = 11/75) had an AE, the most common being urinary tract infection (UTI); 5% and acute kidney injury (AKI); 5% while 1 patient developed ketosis (1.3%). Most patients were alive and remained on treatment (72%, n = 54/75) with 8 patients having ≥ 1 admission for HF management, 2 progressing to ventricular assisted device (VAD), 9 transplanted and 1 death. SGLT2i appear to be well tolerated in children with CHD-HF with low discontinuation and AE rates. Further follow-up is needed to evaluate long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Pediatric CT-Based Coronary Artery Z-Score: Development of Normative Reference Models and Comparison with Echocardiography-Based Methods.
articles.abstract: Pediatric cardiac computed tomography (CT) is increasingly used to identify and monitor coronary artery lesions caused by Kawasaki disease. This study was aimed to develop a CT-based normative coronary artery Z-score method derived from normal pediatric coronary arteries and to compare the Z-scores between the CT- and echocardiography-based methods. A total of 298 children (age range, 1 month - 18 years) with no or trivial cardiovascular disease who underwent ECG-synchronized dual-source cardiac CT were included. Coronary artery diameters were measured in six segments: the left main, proximal and distal left anterior descending, left circumflex, and proximal and distal right coronary arteries. Using the measured coronary artery diameter and body surface area for each segment, Z-scores for normal pediatric coronary arteries were estimated using the lambda-mu-sigma method. The Z-scores using CT-based method were correlated and compared with those using echocardiography-based methods. The CT-based coronary artery Z-score method was developed using the square root model for all six segments, with corresponding Z-score curves generated. The CT- and echocardiography-based methods demonstrated high correlations (R = 0.90 to 0.99; p < 0.001). Echocardiography-based methods frequently produced higher or lower Z-scores, compared with the CT-based values. Bland-Altman plots illustrated the estimated bias from - 0.6 to 0.1 and the 95% limits of agreement ranging from - 0.2 ~ 0.5 to -1.0 ~ 0.8. The CT-based method demonstrated moderate-to-good agreements with echocardiography-based methods (k = 0.427 and 0.640, P < 0.001). This study provides CT-specific coronary artery Z-score models for proximal and distal coronary segments across a broad pediatric age range. The systematic differences and incomplete agreement between CT-based and echocardiography-based Z-scores indicate that echocardiographic reference equations should not be applied interchangeably to CT measurements.

articles.title: Validation of Pre-Operative Proteinuria for Post Cardiac Surgery Acute Kidney Injury Prediction in Infants.
articles.abstract: To validate a clinical prediction model for acute kidney injury (AKI) in infants undergoing cardiac surgery by integrating pre- and post-operative urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) with established clinical variables, including age, sex, prior cardiac surgeries, surgical type, RACHS-1 score, cardiopulmonary bypass time, and baseline kidney function. It was a prospective observational study done in a cardiothoracic unit of a tertiary care hospital in India. Infants aged 1 month to 1 year under cardiopulmonary bypass. Exclusion criteria included neonates, children > 1 year, pre-existing kidney dysfunction, structural renal abnormalities, prior kidney transplant, and incomplete data. Patients were followed through hospital discharge (up to 11 days). AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria. Urine ACR was measured at 6 h post-operatively and daily for two days. Among 66 infants, AKI occurred in 45.5% (n = 30). The pre-operative clinical model demonstrated an AUC of 0.838 (95% CI, 0.732-0.944). Adding pre-operative ACR improved the AUC to 0.925 (95% CI, 0.864-0.986), with a sensitivity of 80.0%, specificity of 94.4%, positive predictive value of 92.1%, and negative predictive value of 85.0%. Adding first post-operative ACR did not further improve model discrimination. The final eight-variable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram to estimate an individual infant's probability of postoperative AKI. Integration of albuminuria with clinical parameters improves prediction of cardiac surgery-associated AKI in infants. This combined model and accompanying nomogram provide a practical approach for early risk stratification and may be particularly valuable in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: The epigenetic control on the inflammatory profiles in leprosy: insights of the miRNA let-7a-5p in TLR4 signaling.
articles.abstract: Leprosy is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae, still affecting many individuals despite progress in controlling its transmission. The disease presents a spectrum of immune responses, from the resistant Th1 form (tuberculoid - TT) to the susceptible Th2 form (lepromatous - LL). Gene expression regulation plays a critical role in these immune responses, with microRNAs (miRNAs) acting as key post-transcriptional modulators in physiological and pathological processes. This study investigates the role of miRNA let-7a-5p in the control of TLR4 pathway signaling and correlates its function with clinical outcomes in leprosy. In silico enrichment analysis of previous miRNAs differential expression profiles, in TT and LL leprosy patients, identified pathways involved in pathogen recognition, such as miRNA let-7a-5p targeting the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4). Considering its potential regulatory role, we characterized the function of let-7a-5p in modulating TLR4 expression and downstream signaling, reducing CXCL1 production. These findings demonstrate that let-7a-5p modulates the TLR4-mediated inflammatory response and suggest its involvement in the immune regulation underlying the clinical spectrum of leprosy.

articles.title: Clitoral transmucosal oxygen tension as a novel marker of coronary artery disease and the vascular component of female sexual dysfunction in postmenopausal women with type 2 diabetes: a pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women with diabetes, yet female-specific vascular markers remain poorly defined. Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is heterogeneous and influenced by multiple nonvascular factors, which may limit the specificity of questionnaire-based assessment for cardiovascular risk stratification. We investigated whether clitoral transmucosal oxygen tension (TmPO2), an objective measure of clitoral tissue perfusion, is associated with coronary artery disease (CAD) and female sexual function in postmenopausal women with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional pilot study, we consecutively enrolled 33 postmenopausal women aged at least 55 years with angiographically documented CAD and 32 matched diabetic women without known CAD. Female sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI). TmPO2 was measured noninvasively at the clitoral mucosal surface. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and multivariable logistic regression were performed.

RESULTS: Women with CAD had significantly lower TmPO2 than women without CAD (22.5 ± 12.1 vs. 38.5 ± 16.3 mmHg, p < 0.001). ROC analysis identified 26 mmHg as the optimal cutoff for CAD discrimination, with 69.7% sensitivity, 81.2% specificity, and an area under the curve of 0.793. TmPO2 < 26 mmHg remained independently associated with CAD after adjustment for age, diabetes duration, BMI, HbA1c, smoking, microalbuminuria, uric acid, and C-peptide (OR 12.51, 95% CI 2.89-54.06, p < 0.001). TmPO2 correlated with FSFI total score and with domains most plausibly related to genital hemodynamics.

CONCLUSION: In postmenopausal women with type 2 diabetes, reduced TmPO2 was associated with CAD and with the vascular component of female sexual function. As a pilot study, these findings suggest that TmPO2 may represent a novel, noninvasive marker of FSD that better reflects cardiovascular risk than symptom-based questionnaires.

articles.title: Trends in serum total testosterone among U.S. adult men: an analysis of NHANES 2011-2016 and 2021-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Population studies have suggested secular declines in serum testosterone, but whether these declines persisted into recent years is uncertain.

PURPOSE: To compare serum total testosterone and the prevalence of testosterone < 300 ng/dL among U.S. adult men in 2011-2016 and 2021-2023.

METHODS: We analyzed 4,419 men aged ≥ 20 years examined in the morning session of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011-2012, 2013-2014, 2015-2016 and August 2021-August 2023. Total testosterone was measured by isotope-dilution liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, with published calibration applied to 2011-2012. Survey-weighted linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, body mass index (BMI), race and ethnicity, education, insurance, smoking, alcohol use, diabetes and high cholesterol. Pairwise cycle comparisons used Bonferroni correction.

RESULTS: Adjusted mean total testosterone was 451.9, 432.4, 449.5 and 477.6 ng/dL across the four cycles (overall p = 0.002). Compared with pooled 2011-2016, mean total testosterone was 32.9 ng/dL higher in 2021-2023 (95% CI 12.5-53.3; p = 0.002). Compared with 2015-2016, the difference increase was 28.1 ng/dL (95% CI 3.1-53.1; Bonferroni p = 0.17). Adjusted prevalence of testosterone < 300 ng/dL ranged from 17.2% to 19.5% and did not differ across cycles (p = 0.90). Inverse probability weighting for missing covariates gave a similar estimate (32.9 ng/dL), while age-only adjustment gave 25.1 ng/dL (95% CI - 1.6 to 51.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Serum total testosterone among U.S. men was not lower in 2021-2023 than in 2011-2016; adjusted means were modestly higher, although the difference from 2015 to 2016 alone was not significant after correction. The cross-sectional design, absence of 2017-2020 data and unascertained testosterone therapy in 2021-2023 preclude causal interpretation. Continued population surveillance and longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether the higher contemporary mean testosterone level persists and to clarify its contributing factors and its clinical significance.

articles.title: Optimization and Characterization of Vibrio-Derived Postbiotic Against Vibrio alginolyticus and Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
articles.abstract: Vibriosis is a major infectious disease affecting aquaculture, caused by Vibrio species such as Vibrio alginolyticus (VA) and Vibrio parahaemolyticus (VP), with widespread antibiotic resistance (AMR) in Vibrio spp. Postbiotics, primarily composed of fatty acids and bacteriocins, offer a sustainable alternative. This study aimed to optimize culture conditions for Vibrio-derived postbiotics rather than from lactic acid bacteria with targeted anti-Vibrio activity and identify their active components. Central Composite Design (CCD) was applied to optimize postbiotic production by manipulating candidate species (VA or VP), temperature (25-45 °C) and salinity (1.5-9.0%). Cell-free supernatants (CFS) were prepared, and anti-Vibrio activity was assessed. Fatty acid, bacteriocin-like inhibitory substance, and hydrogen peroxide-dependent activity were evaluated via pH adjustment, protease, and catalase treatments, respectively. Organic acids and fatty acids were extracted with ethyl acetate and analyzed using GC-MS, while MIC assays confirmed antibacterial activity. Optimal postbiotic production was achieved using VA at 36 °C and 1.5% salinity, yielding CFS that inhibited VA growth by 23.3%. Fatty acid-dependent inhibition contributed 18%, hydrogen peroxide ~ 7.8%, while bacteriocin-like activity was negligible (~ 1.4%). GC-MS identified oleic acid (40%) and tridecanoic acid (25%) as the major components. Both compounds exhibited moderate antibacterial activity with MICs of 500 µg/mL against VA and VP. CCD successfully optimized Vibrio postbiotic production, yielding oleic acid and tridecanoic acid as the major components. These Vibrio-derived postbiotics show potential as targeted, eco-friendly alternatives to antibiotics for sustainable vibriosis management and AMR mitigation in aquaculture.

articles.title: Anatomical adjuncts during minimally invasive repair of large indirect and inguinoscrotal hernias: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Large indirect and inguinoscrotal hernias combine an enlarged lateral defect with a residual distal sac that may contribute to clinically apparent postoperative seroma. Several anatomical adjuncts have been described, including true myofascial closure, calibrated ring constriction, distal-sac narrowing and percutaneous canal semi-closure. We evaluated the comparative evidence for these strategies while distinguishing their different anatomical targets.

METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched on 29 July 2026, supplemented by SinoMed searching and backward and forward citation chasing. Comparative studies of adults undergoing minimally invasive mesh repair for large indirect, inguinoscrotal or European Hernia Society L3 hernias were eligible. Randomised and observational studies were analysed separately, and true myofascial closure was analysed separately from the other anatomical adjuncts. Random-effects models used the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence using GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine comparative studies were included (five randomised, four retrospective; 1246 participants/repairs), six evaluating true myofascial closure. At approximately 7 days, study-defined seroma occurred in 75/414 (18%) participants after true myofascial closure compared with 153/457 (34%) without closure, corresponding to approximately half the relative risk and about 15 fewer seromas per 100 participants at the observed event rates (RR 0.50, 95% CI 0.29-0.87). The randomised trials showed a similar direction of effect, although uncertainty was wide because only two trials contributed. At approximately 1 month, the estimate pooled across all four true myofascial closure studies was imprecise (RR 0.36, 95% CI 0.13-1.00). Operative time was longer with true myofascial closure by a pooled mean of 5.62 min (95% CI 0.47-10.78), but heterogeneity was very high (I² = 90%). In a sensitivity analysis excluding one trial with reconstructed dispersion data, the difference was 3.81 min (95% CI 0.25-7.37). Recurrence occurred in 0/604 intervention-arm and 9/642 control participants, but sparse events and short follow-up precluded a reliable effect estimate.

CONCLUSION: True myofascial closure of the deep inguinal ring is a promising adjunct: low-certainty evidence suggests that it may reduce clinically apparent early seroma. Recurrence benefit and long-term neurological, cord and testicular safety remain uncertain, and the highly heterogeneous operative-time estimate is not generally applicable. Current evidence does not support routine use or establish superiority of one anatomical strategy.

articles.title: Conditional survival reveals a prognostic crossover by molecular subtype, but not by anatomic stage, in female breast cancer: a population-based SEER study, 2010-2022.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diagnosis-anchored survival statistics do not describe prognosis for patients who have already survived several years. We compared how the prognostic weight of molecular subtype and AJCC anatomic stage evolves over survivorship time within a single population-based cohort.

METHODS: Using the SEER 17-registry database, we identified 612,926 women with invasive breast cancer diagnosed 2010-2022. Five-year conditional overall and breast cancer-specific survival (OS, BCSS), CS(5|x), was estimated by the landmark Kaplan-Meier method by AJCC stage and molecular subtype. Interval-specific Cox models (0-2, 2-5, 5-8, > 8 years) and flexible parametric models with time-varying coefficients estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs). Crossover points were interpolated on a 3-month landmark grid with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: TNBC's BCSS aHR relative to HR+/HER2 - fell from 3.27 (0-2 years) to 1.66 (2-5 years), 0.74 (5-8 years), and 0.49 (> 8 years), falling below 1 approximately 6 years after diagnosis in flexible parametric models. Conditional survival crossed at approximately 3.7 years already survived for OS (95% CI 3.5-3.9) and 4.5 years for BCSS (4.2-4.7), with similar estimates in patients diagnosed 2010-2012 only and with competing-risk estimation. Stage IV vs. Stage I's aHR also declined (30.3 to 13.6), but no stage contrast crossed within 8 years.

CONCLUSION: Among women surviving several years after diagnosis, the excess mortality associated with TNBC and HR-/HER2 + disease disappears and then reverses relative to HR+/HER2 - disease, whereas differences between AJCC stages narrow without reversing within the available follow-up. These mortality-based estimates can inform prognostic counseling; they do not by themselves support changes to surveillance.

articles.title: Spatial Epidemiology of Breast Cancer Screening Uptake in India: Patterns, Clusters, Determinants and Decomposition.
articles.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer prevalence is rising steadily in India. Despite this, rural women are less likely to undergo regular breast cancer screening compared to their urban counterparts, and this disparity has not been extensively explored. The present study aims to assess the prevalence of breast cancer screening, identify its determinants, examine spatial variations, and analyze rural-urban differences among women aged 30-49 years at both national and sub-national levels.

METHODS: We used data from the 5th round of the National Family Health Survey in India (NFHS-5). We examined how breast cancer screening coverage varied across sociodemographic groups. We made LISA maps showing where similar patterns of screening coverage occurred, and we also recorded the Moran's I statistic to measure spatial clustering. We used Stata 17 to run a multivariable logistic regression to identify the most important factors. We also conducted a multivariate decomposition analysis to understand the causes of differences in screening coverage.

RESULTS: The national coverage of breast cancer screening is only 0.87%. Multivariable logistic regression showed that higher odds of breast cancer screening were associated with older age, education, being a Christian woman, the richest wealth quintile, and age of first intercourse. Across all regions, rural-urban disparities are evident, with higher breast cancer screening coverage in urban areas (1.27%) than in rural areas (0.67%). Decomposition analysis showed that disparities in uptake of breast cancer screening are due to residential region, education, exposure to media, number of children, smoking, diabetes, and alcohol use.

CONCLUSIONS: Disparities in screening are evident, necessitating sustainable region-specific targeted interventions that raise awareness, and adopting best practices from southern India in other regions is essential.

articles.title: SOS: Surgeon Outside Surgery. A cross-sectional survey on work-life balance and surgical career sustainability among general surgeons.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Work-life balance (WLB) and career sustainability are important concerns in surgical practice. This study explored perceived WLB and associated demographic and occupational characteristics among general surgeons.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, international, online survey conducted between March and June 2026, which was created by general surgeons, distributed through surgical societies and professional social media sites. In total, 484 general surgeons with at least five years of experience were recruited for data analysis via descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 484 general surgeons were included in the final analysis. Only 33.3% of respondents reported an adequate work life balance, while 52.7% experienced work-related exhaustion. More than half of the participants worked over 50 hours per week (53.1%), slept less than 6 hours per night(51.4%), and were dissatisfied with their salary (53.7%). Furthermore, 49.2% had considered leaving surgery because of lifestyle-related reasons, whereas only 23.8%Powered by Editorial Manager® and ProduXion Manager® from Aries Systems Corporation considered their current surgical career sustainable.

CONCLUSION: This study revealed serious concerns within the surgeon community regarding their well-being and career sustainability. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the cross sectional design, the predominance of Italian participants, and the use of a non validated survey instrument. Even though no causal relationship can be made, there is an important point raised that needs to be further explored.

articles.title: Outcome following damage control surgery at two tertiary academic hospitals in Pretoria, South Africa.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Damage Control Surgery (DCS) is a critical intervention for patients with abdominal trauma and physiological compromise. The purpose of the study was to assess the outcomes of patients who underwent DCS for abdominal trauma and identify factors associated with 30-day mortality at two tertiary academic hospitals in Pretoria, South Africa.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study reviewed adult trauma patients (≥ 18 years) who underwent DCS over five years. Data collected included demographics, mechanism of injury, comorbidities, physiological parameters, organ injuries, operative details, complications, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 114 patients were included, predominantly men (96.49%), with a median age of 32 years. Penetrating trauma accounted for 66.67%. Temporary abdominal closure was used in 97.37% of patients. The majority of patients underwent one (46.49%) or two (39.47%) relook laparotomies. Complications after definitive surgery occurred in 57.89%. The median hospital stay was 15 days. The 30-day mortality rate was 14.9%. The univariate analysis showed COVID-19 infection (p = 0.021), systolic blood pressure (p = 0.011), Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) (p = 0.000), and the number of laparotomies (p = 0.009), were predictors of mortality. In the multivariate analysis, COVID-19 infection (p = 0.002) and GCS (p = 0.048) were associated with mortality.

CONCLUSION: The leading mechanisms necessitating DCS were penetrating injuries. Postoperative complications were notable. Hypotension, reduced GCS score, COVID-19 infection and multiple laparotomies were associated with mortality. A reduced GCS score and COVID-19 infection were associated as independent predictors of mortality; however, the latter should be interpreted with caution due to the limited number of cases. These findings highlight the importance of early assessment and risk stratification in patients undergoing DCS.

articles.title: Silent guests of the thorax: a surgical perspective on intrathoracic neurogenic tumors.
articles.abstract: Intrathoracic neurogenic tumors (INTs) are neoplasms arising from neurogenic structures in the mediastinum, such as nerve sheath, ganglion, and paraganglion cells. This retrospective study (January 2020-December 2025) evaluated the clinical management, preferred surgical approaches, postoperative morbidity, and recurrence status of patients operated on for INTs at our institution. After ethical approval, data on demographics, imaging (CT, MRI, 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose [18 F-FDG] PET/CT), and surgical approach (video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery [VATS], thoracotomy, endobronchial argon plasma coagulation [APC]) were recorded. Histopathological evaluations were performed by experienced pathologists, and postoperative follow-up included clinical and radiological assessments at specific intervals. Twenty consecutive surgical patients were analyzed (13 [65%] females), and most (60%) were asymptomatic. Histopathology showed 18 (90%) benign and 2 (10%) malignant tumors, with schwannoma (75%) being the most frequent subtype. Mean SUVmax was 5.02 in malignant and 3.10 in benign cases. Surgery was performed by VATS in 55%, thoracotomy in 35%, and endobronchial APC in 10% of patients. Complications occurred in 2 (10%) patients. No recurrence was observed during a mean follow-up of 21.4 months (range, 2-62 months; 27.5 months for malignant and 20.7 months for benign cases); however, given the short follow-up duration in several patients, late recurrence cannot be definitively excluded. In our experience, preoperative biopsy rarely altered management, although larger studies are needed before definitive recommendations on its routine use can be made. Direct surgical resection remains the gold-standard approach for both definitive diagnosis and treatment. Given the rare variants and atypical localizations (e.g., intrapulmonary, endobronchial) in our series, a personalized surgical strategy tailored to tumor localization and patient-specific factors is essential for optimizing clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Higher ERAS compliance is associated with shorter hospital stay and lower ICU utilization in a resource-limited healthcare system - a prospective colorectal cohort study.
articles.abstract: ​Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways integrate evidence-based perioperative care to improve recovery after colorectal surgery. Although a compliance threshold of 70-75% has been proposed, outcomes at higher adherence levels remain incompletely characterized, particularly in resource-limited healthcare systems. We aimed to evaluate the achievable compliance and its association with postoperative outcomes in such a setting.This prospective single-center cohort included patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery between 2022 and 2024. Compliance with 20 ERAS elements was assessed in six groups (≤ 75% and 5-percentage-point bands up to 100%). Outcomes included hospital length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU) utilization, morbidity, readmission, and mortality. Unadjusted analyses were supplemented by exploratory multivariable models.Among 338 patients, mean compliance was 89.3%; median LOS was 6 days (interquartile range 5-7). ICU admission occurred in 23.7%, total morbidity in 28.1%, and early morbidity in 16.9%. Higher compliance correlated with shorter LOS (R = - 0.36), lower ICU admission (R = - 0.30), and fewer early complications (R = - 0.19; all p < 0.001). After adjustment, each 5-percentage-point increase in compliance was associated with a 4.8% relative reduction in geometric mean LOS (p = 0.0023) and approximately 5.4 h shorter ICU stay among admitted patients (p = 0.0039). Late complications and readmission showed no statistically significant unadjusted compliance association.High ERAS compliance was achievable in a resource-limited healthcare system. Across the examined compliance groups up to 100%, higher adherence was associated with shorter hospitalization and ICU duration. Morbidity findings were less consistent and did not show uniform additional benefit.

articles.title: Comparison between stapled and handsewn anastomoses in emergency intestinal surgery in elderly patients. A retrospective multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence comparing stapled and handsewn anastomoses in emergency intestinal surgery remains uncertain.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort included 756 patients aged > 60 years undergoing emergency ileo-ileal or ileo-colic anastomosis during 2005-2022. Primary outcomes were anastomotic leakage and bleeding. Secondary outcomes included surgical site infection (SSI), reintervention, major complications and length of stay. Binary outcomes were compared using two-sided Fisher's exact tests; multivariable logistic regression was exploratory.

RESULTS: Stapled and handsewn anastomoses were performed in 333 and 423 patients, respectively. Leakage occurred in 1.2% versus 2.6% (p = 0.198), and bleeding in 3.9% versus 6.4% (p = 0.143). Unadjusted rates of SSI (8.1% versus 12.8%; p = 0.044), reintervention (3.9% versus 7.8%; p = 0.031), and Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ III complications (9.3% versus 20.3%; p < 0.001) were lower in the stapled group. Median length of stay was 10 versus 12.5 days (p = 0.131). Handsewn anastomosis was associated with SSI in exploratory multivariable analysis (adjusted odds ratio 2.34, 95% confidence interval 1.09-5.03; p = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant differences in leakage or bleeding were detected, but few events limited precision. Associations with secondary outcomes cannot establish causal effects because of surgeon-directed technique selection and unmeasured confounding. Findings are hypothesis-generating; technique selection should remain individualized.

articles.title: Review no. 4: clinical research using proteinuria as an outcome: concepts, definitions, and practical considerations.
articles.abstract: Proteinuria is a central biomarker in nephrology and is widely used as an outcome measure in clinical trials and observational studies. Across diverse kidney diseases, reductions in urinary protein excretion are strongly associated with improved long-term kidney outcomes, and proteinuria-based endpoints are increasingly incorporated into contemporary clinical trial design and regulatory evaluation. However, multiple statistical approaches are available for analyzing proteinuria, and the choice of method substantially influences clinical interpretation, statistical power, and regulatory acceptability. In this review, we provide a practical, methodologically focused overview of statistical strategies for handling proteinuria outcomes in clinical research. We describe three major analytic frameworks: treatment of proteinuria as a continuous variable, dichotomization using clinically meaningful thresholds, and longitudinal modeling of repeated measurements. Analyses treating proteinuria as a continuous outcome commonly use general linear models with log-transformed proteinuria ratios, preserving statistical information and improving statistical efficiency, whereas dichotomous endpoints enhance interpretability yet reduce statistical power and depend on threshold selection. Longitudinal models, including mixed-effects approaches, can incorporate repeated measurements over time and account for within-subject correlation. These approaches also align with modern estimand-based regulatory expectations for handling missing data and intercurrent events. Practical considerations for study design, endpoint selection, and regulatory alignment are summarized to guide investigators in choosing appropriate analytic strategies. By integrating statistical rigor with clinical interpretability, optimized handling of proteinuria outcomes can enhance trial efficiency, improve reproducibility, and strengthen the translation of biomarker-based findings into meaningful kidney disease therapies.

articles.title: Trends and causes of death among patients with polycystic kidney disease undergoing dialysis in Japan, 2010-2024: an analysis of a nationwide dialysis registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is the fourth leading cause of kidney failure worldwide. However, long-term trends in the number and causes of death among dialysis patients with PKD remain unclear.

METHODS: This nationwide registry-based study used Japanese Society for Dialysis Therapy Web-based Analysis of Dialysis Data Archives data from 2010 to 2024. Crude mortality risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for each cause of death by comparing patients with and without PKD, both overall and stratified by sex.

RESULTS: Annual dialysis populations ranged from 9,039 to 12,488 in the PKD group and from 280,410 to 324,454 in the non-PKD group. Overall, 10,308 patients with PKD and 465,423 without PKD died. In both groups, the proportion of deaths among older patients increased over time. Heart failure-related deaths decreased, whereas infection-related deaths increased. Compared with patients without PKD, those with PKD had a consistently lower annual risk of all-cause mortality (RR, 0.62; 95%CI 0.61-0.63) and lower cause-specific mortality risks. SAH was the only cause of death showing a trend toward higher mortality risk in patients with versus without PKD (RR, 1.17; 95%CI 0.97-1.40). In sex-stratified analyses, SAH-related mortality did not differ significantly between patients with and without PKD among men, whereas it was significantly higher in patients with PKD among women (RR, 1.96; 95%CI 1.53-2.50).

CONCLUSIONS: SAH remained a frequent cause of death, particularly among women, suggesting persistent cerebrovascular vulnerability after dialysis initiation and underscoring the need for cerebrovascular risk assessment and surveillance.

articles.title: Associations between gestational diabetes susceptibility variants and pregnancy outcomes across glucose-metabolism phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore the association of genetic variants for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) with adverse pregnancy outcomes in pregnant Chinese women with different abnormal glucose metabolism.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort-based secondary analysis included 439 controls and 452 women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM; impaired fasting glucose [IFG], n = 115; impaired glucose tolerance [IGT], n = 337). Logistic regression analyses evaluated the relationships between four GDM-susceptibility single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and adverse pregnancy outcomes, including assessment of SNP-by-phenotype interactions.

RESULTS: In controls, MTNR1B rs10830963 was associated with higher odds of pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH; adjusted odds ratio (OR) 2.358, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.036-5.367), intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (3.239, 1.084-9.681), and cesarean delivery (1.363, 1.014-1.831), while C2CD4A/B rs7172432 was associated with higher odds of macrosomia (2.023, 1.024-3.996). In the IFG group, rs10830963 was associated with lower odds of large for gestational age (LGA; 0.341, 0.163-0.714), C2CD4A/B rs7172432 with higher odds of LGA (1.952, 1.031-3.696) and macrosomia (3.021, 1.055-8.648), and CMIP rs16955379 with lower odds of PIH (0.133, 0.030-0.589). In the IGT group, rs16955379 was associated with higher odds of PIH (3.143, 1.199-8.238). SNP-by-glucose-metabolism phenotype interactions were observed for CMIP rs16955379 with PIH (P = 0.008) and preterm delivery (P = 0.045), and MTNR1B rs10830963 with LGA (P = 0.039).

CONCLUSION: Given the modest subgroup sizes and single-center design, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory. They suggest that associations between selected GDM-susceptibility SNPs and adverse pregnancy outcomes appeared to differ by OGTT-defined glucose-metabolism phenotypes but require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: A phase 1 study of LY3214996 (temuterkib), an ERK1/2 inhibitor, administered alone or in combination with other agents for advanced and/or metastatic cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: LY3214996, a potent and selective ERK1/2 kinase inhibitor, demonstrated preclinical tumor growth inhibition and regression in cancers with RAS/MAPK pathway mutations and was evaluated in patients with advanced/metastatic tumors.

METHODS: This multicenter, nonrandomized, open-label phase I study included dose-escalation and dose-expansion phases for patients with advanced/metastatic tumors. The primary endpoint was the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of oral LY3214996 as monotherapy and in combination. Safety, tolerability, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and drug-drug interactions (DDIs) were also assessed.

RESULTS: The RP2D for LY3214996 monotherapy was 400 mg QD, and the RP2D for LY3214996 in combination with abemaciclib was 200 mg QD. Dose-limiting toxicities from the dose-escalation cohorts included dehydration, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, macro-papular rash, and elevated creatinine. Among 210 patients treated with LY3214996 (monotherapy or in combination), 91.0% experienced ≥ 1 treatment-related adverse event (TRAE) and 33.8% experienced ≥ 1 grade 3 TRAE, with diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, and nausea most commonly reported. Nine deaths (4.3%) occurred during therapy. No complete responses were observed; 4 (1.9%) patients achieved a partial response. LY3214996 exposure increased with increasing doses ranging from 25 to 800 mg, reaching maximum observed concentrations 1-2 h postdose, and a mean elimination half-life of 3-5 h. LY3214996 exposure decreased when coadministered with encorafenib; no other DDIs were observed. Decreases in phosphorylated p90RSK were observed across all dose levels; however, these decreases were not associated with response.

CONCLUSIONS: LY3214996, administered as monotherapy or in combination, demonstrated modest antitumor activity and a tolerable safety profile in patients with advanced/metastatic solid tumors.

GOV TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT02857270.

articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: Effects of tomatine on the production of testosterone in rat Leydig cells.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tomatine exhibits antimicrobial properties against certain classes of microbes. In addition, tomatine inhibits the growth of androgen-dependent prostate cancer LNCaP cells. However, the mechanism of action of tomatine in reproductive endocrinology remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: In this study, we investigated the acute effects of tomatine on testosterone secretion both in vitro and in vivo in male rats.

METHODS: Testosterone levels in medium and plasma samples were measured using radioimmunoassay.

RESULTS: In vitro results revealed that basal testosterone release was not altered by treatment with tomatine at concentrations ranging from 10⁻9 to 10⁻6 M. However, cotreatment with tomatine for 1 h significantly inhibited testosterone release stimulated by human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), 25-OH-cholesterol, forskolin, or androstenedione. By contrast, A23187-evoked testosterone release was not affected. In vivo experiments, blood samples were collected from rats at various time intervals following intravenous injection of hCG. Plasma testosterone levels were significantly lower in the tomatine-pretreated rats than in the control rats. Similarly, testosterone levels were lower in the rats injected subcutaneously with tomatine once daily for 7 days compared with the controls. These findings indicate that short-term tomatine treatment inhibits hCG-evoked testosterone production.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that tomatine inhibits steroidogenesis of testosterone in Leydig cells, suggesting a potential regulatory role of tomatine in reproductive endocrinology. These results provide a novel perspective for further investigation of the effect of tomatine on reproductive hormone regulation.

CLINICAL TRIAL: Not applicable.

articles.title: Significant postoperative weight loss in patients on glucagon-like peptide-1 agents is associated with increased instability risk after shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Use of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonists has increased substantially for weight loss and metabolic disease management. Significant postoperative weight loss following total shoulder arthroplasty may alter soft tissue tension, joint stability, and periarticular biomechanics. However, the relationship between GLP-1-associated weight loss and implant-related complications remains poorly defined. This study evaluated whether GLP-1 users with substantial postoperative weight loss have higher two-year implant complication rates compared with those with minimal weight change.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using a multi-institutional electronic medical record network. Adult GLP-1 users undergoing primary shoulder arthroplasty with at least two years of follow-up and documented pre- and postoperative BMI were included. Patients were stratified by postoperative BMI change into <10% and ≥10% loss groups. A subgroup analysis was performed for reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA). Propensity score matching was used to balance demographics and comorbidities. Two-year implant complications were compared using odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: After matching, 2127 patients were included, of whom 368 (17.3%) experienced ≥10% BMI loss. In the overall cohort, substantial weight loss was associated with a higher risk of implant dislocation (5.4% vs. 2.8%; OR 1.96; 95% CI 1.13-3.29; p = 0.011). In the rTSA subgroup, ≥10% BMI loss was similarly associated with increased dislocation risk (5.7% vs. 2.7%; OR 2.17; 95% CI 1.01-4.40; p = 0.034). No other implant-related complications differed significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: Among GLP-1 users, postoperative BMI loss ≥10% is associated with increased risk of dislocation following shoulder arthroplasty, particularly in rTSA. These findings suggest substantial weight loss may impact soft tissue balance and implant stability and should be considered in perioperative counseling and postoperative monitoring.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Protective effects of PACAP38 eye drops treatment on the vertical information processing pathway in type 2 diabetic retinopathy.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetic retinopathy (T2DR) is increasingly recognized as a neurodegenerative disease characterized by early neuronal and glial alterations in addition to microvascular damage. Pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) has emerged as a promising neuroprotective agent. The present study investigated the protective effects of PACAP38 eye drops treatment in a rat model of T2DR, with a particular focus on retinal neuronal populations and synaptic integrity. Type 2 diabetes was induced by a combination of a high-fat diet and two low-dose intraperitoneal streptozotocin injections (30 mg kg-1, one week apart). Retinal morphology and cellular integrity were assessed using immunohistochemistry. Diabetes induced marked disruption of the outer limiting membrane, increased Müller cell gliosis, and pronounced degeneration of photoreceptors, synaptic structures, interneurons, and ganglion cells. Significant reductions were observed in the number of cone photoreceptor cell bodies, ribbon synapse-associated CTBP2 fluorescence, bipolar and rod bipolar cell populations, and in the number of Brn3a-positive ganglion cells. In contrast, horizontal cells showed relative resistance to diabetic injury. PACAP38 treatment markedly attenuated diabetes-induced retinal damage. PACAP38 preserved tight junction organization, reduced glial activation, significantly protected cone photoreceptors and their synaptic terminals, and maintained populations of bipolar, rod bipolar, and ganglion cells. Although rod photoreceptor loss and ribbon synapse alterations were only partially improved, overall retinal organization and neuronal survival were substantially preserved in PACAP38-treated diabetic animals.
