These findings demonstrate that topical PACAP38 administration exerts broad neuroprotective effects across multiple retinal layers and may support the preservation of vertical signal transmission in T2DR, highlighting its therapeutic potential in diabetic retinal neurodegeneration. Retinal function was not assessed in the present study; the conclusions presented here are therefore based on structural and marker-based evidence.

articles.title: Functional outcome after surgical excision of neurogenic heterotopic ossification around the hip.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurogenic heterotopic ossification (NHO) involves abnormal bone formation in soft tissues following neurological injuries such as spinal cord injury or head injury. When affecting the hip, it can severely impair hip movement and mobility in patients.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the functional outcomes after surgical excision of neurogenic HO around the hip.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of 12 patients who underwent excision of the HO around the hip for neurological causes between June 2019 and July 2024 was conducted. The patients were contacted on the telephone and asked specific questions. Functional results were assessed using the Hip Outcome Score - Activities of Daily Living (HOS-ADL) and Non-Arthritic Hip Score (NAHS). Pain was recorded using a numerical rating scale (NRS) ranging from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst pain) in increasing intensity as described by the patients. For mobility, a 4-point scale was used: (1) Bedridden; (2) Ambulatory but dependent on caregivers; (3) Ambulatory but cane-assisted; and (4) Unassisted ambulatory. Non-parametric tests were used. Scores are presented as median (IQR). The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for comparison.

RESULTS: The median age was 29 years. The median duration of disease before surgery was 20.5 months, and the median follow-up duration was 31 months. Functional assessment scores showed significant improvement. The median HOS-ADL score (maximum score = 68) improved from 7.5 (IQR: 5-8) to 51 (IQR: 10-63) (p = 0.002), while the non-arthritic hip score (maximum score = 80) improved from 15.5 (IQR: 11-17.5) to 50 (IQR: 13-63) (p = 0.002) after excision of HO. The median 4-point mobility score improved from 2 (IQR: 2-2) to 4 (IQR: 2.5-4) (p = 0.002), and the median NRS pain score improved from 3 (IQR: 2-3) to 0 (IQR: 0-2.5) (p = 0.006) after surgery.

CONCLUSION: Surgical removal of neurogenic HO around the hip can lead to improved pain, mobility, and daily functioning in most cases. As their mobility status improves, they become independent in their activities of daily living. However, recurrence and postoperative deep infection were associated with poor outcomes.

articles.title: Carotid plaque inflammation on [18F]FDG PET/MR provides incremental prognostic information beyond Plaque-RADS and luminal stenosis in medically treated atherosclerosis.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether carotid plaque inflammation quantified by [18F]FDG PET/MR-derived target-to-background ratio (TBR) provides incremental prognostic information beyond luminal stenosis and MRI-based Carotid Plaque-RADS for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events in medically treated carotid atherosclerosis.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 151 patients with carotid atherosclerosis receiving medical therapy who underwent baseline [18F]FDG PET/MR. SUVmax, TBR, Plaque-RADS, and stenosis severity were assessed with readers blinded to outcomes. The primary endpoint was three-point MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal ischaemic stroke. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using Cox regression, time-dependent ROC analysis, bootstrap-validated Harrell C-index, AIC, likelihood ratio testing, and continuous net reclassification improvement.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 36 months (IQR 32-41 months), 21 patients (13.9%) experienced three-point MACE. After adjustment for age, sex, and C-reactive protein, TBR (HR 5.10, 95% CI 3.22-8.07), SUVmax (HR 4.03, 2.21-7.35), stenosis severity (HR 8.54, 3.84-18.97), and Plaque-RADS (HR 4.19, 1.73-10.15) were each associated with MACE. Addition of TBR to a structural model comprising stenosis and Plaque-RADS yielded the highest discrimination (apparent C-index 0.911; optimism-corrected 0.906) and lowest AIC (147.49). TBR showed higher 36-month discrimination than SUVmax (AUC 0.94 vs. 0.80).

CONCLUSION: In medically treated patients with carotid atherosclerosis, [18F]FDG PET/MR-derived TBR was associated with three-point MACE and provided incremental prognostic information beyond MRI-based Plaque-RADS and luminal stenosis.

articles.title: [Systematics of locally applied anti-infective agents in wound treatment: active substances, properties and indications : Position paper of the Working Group on Hygiene and Microbiology of the Chronic Wounds Initiative, ICW].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute and chronic wounds represent a frequent medical challenge in which local anti-infective treatment plays a key role in wound cleansing and infection control. Despite existing guidelines, there is uncertainty in the clinical practice regarding the selection and indication-based use of wound irrigation solutions and antiseptics.

OBJECTIVE: This position paper aims to provide a structured systematization of local antimicrobial agents and practical guidance for their differentiated application.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: The position paper describes the definitions and distinctions of antiseptics, antimicrobial agents and wound irrigation solutions. Active substance classes, products, mechanisms of action, concentration-dependent effects, excipients and retentivity are narratively appraised using regulatory information, clinical studies and systematic reviews as well as translational or in vitro data and consensus-based recommendations. Specific wound scenarios and special patient groups are additionally addressed.

RESULTS: Comparative clinical evidence for individual substances and products is heterogeneous and often limited. Evidence-based statements, experimental findings and expert consensus are therefore transparently differentiated. In addition to common pitfalls and negative recommendations, the paper addresses efficacy profiles, retentivity, specific wound scenarios and application restrictions. Antiseptics should be used for a defined indication and duration and de-escalated once the treatment goal has been achieved.

CONCLUSION: This position paper provides a practical, evidence-informed decision aid. Where robust clinical data with good evidence are lacking, recommendations are explicitly identified as consensus based. Product-specific summaries of product characteristics and instructions for use remain decisive for individual application.

articles.title: Reduced versus standard activity regimens in [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer: efficacy and toxicity profiling.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Lutetium-177 ([177Lu]Lu)-Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) using reduced vs. standard activity regimens.

METHODS: In this exploratory retrospective single-center study, 55 patients scheduled for a reduced activity regimen of 6 GBq [177Lu]Lu-PSMA per cycle were compared with 55 receiving standard activity (7.4 GBq per cycle). Efficacy was assessed by Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) changes after two cycles using Prostate Cancer Clinical Working Group version 3 (PCWG3), progression-free (PFS), and overall survival (OS). We also stratified patients into low- vs. high-PSMA-tumor volume (TV) groups determined by baseline PSMA PET/CT. Toxicity was assessed by evaluating laboratory changes from baseline to nadir, along with Common Terminology Criteria of Adverse Events (AE) 5.0.

RESULTS: Reduced activity RPT was effective with a median PSA change of -32% (Interquartile range, -78 to 42%) after two cycles. 25 patients (45%) achieved partial response (stable disease: 14 (25%); progressive disease: 16 (29%)). PSA change (P = 0.961), PCWG3 response distributions (P ≥ 0.219), PFS (P = 0.449) and OS (P = 0.096) were similar in both activity groups. For the reduced activity regimen, we observed significant increase in creatinine (+ 5%) and declines in hemoglobin (-13%), white blood cell counts (-24%) and platelets (-26%; P ≤ 0.001). Those differences, however, were comparable relative to the standard activity group (P ≥ 0.135). In a similar manner, number of renal and hematologic grade 3 AE were identical in both cohorts (six, each).

CONCLUSION: In this preliminary, retrospective proof-of-concept analysis, reduced-activity [177Lu]Lu-PSMA RPT was associated with encouraging efficacy and safety outcomes compared with standard-activity treatment. These hypothesis-generating findings may provide a preliminary rationale for future prospective studies evaluating the clinical utility of individualized activity regimens in PSMA RPT.

articles.title: Progressive cutaneous nocardiosis due to Nocardia brasiliensis: A case report.
articles.abstract: Primary cutaneous nocardiosis has a nonspecific presentation and may be mistaken for common bacterial or deep fungal infections. We describe a 59-year-old man with untreated chronic hepatitis C whose HbA1c was in the diabetic range and who developed a painful purulent forearm lesion after minor trauma while cleaning an abandoned building. The patient was managed as an outpatient. The infection progressed despite initial debridement and a 10-day course of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate, requiring repeat surgical debridement. Culture findings raised suspicion of Nocardia, and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry identified Nocardia brasiliensis. Broth microdilution demonstrated susceptibility to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, amoxicillin-clavulanate, ceftriaxone, amikacin, and linezolid, but resistance to imipenem, ciprofloxacin, and clarithromycin. Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 160/800 mg every 12 h was prescribed for a planned three-month course. The patient reported clinical improvement approximately six weeks after treatment initiation. This case emphasizes appropriate sampling, species-level identification, isolate-specific susceptibility testing, and surgical source control in progressive cutaneous nocardiosis.

articles.title: Microbial barrier integrity of 3-way-stopcocks following disinfection with and without mechanical challenge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The study assessed the microbial barrier integrity of 3-way stopcocks exposed to various disinfecting agents in terms of stress cracks with potential relevance for infection prevention and control.

METHODS: Four different 3-way stopcocks were filled with medium containing each more than 100,000 colony-forming units of Staphylococcus epidermidis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli and Candida albicans, with subsequent exposure to four different disinfecting agents for 6 and 24 h as well as for 28 days, exceeding realistic real-word exposure times. Mechanical challenge was simulated by repeated docking of syringes, combined with 24 h disinfection turns. After the disinfection terms, lacking bacterial growth from closed 3-way stopcocks as well as positive growth from the bacterial suspension inside was confirmed in brain heart infusion broth.

RESULTS: Absence of bacterial growth from closed 3-way stopcocks and remaining vitality of the bacteria in the suspension within the stopcocks could be confirmed in all instances.

CONCLUSIONS: The 3-way stopcocks showed a robust barrier microbial integrity against long-term disinfection without and with combined mechanical challenging. The results suggest that infection prevention and control risks due to stress cracks caused by disinfection of 3-way stopcocks seems to be negligible and that their disinfection is safe to be performed.

articles.title: Effect of short-course oral dexamethasone on acute phase response following intravenous zoledronate infusion: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Zoledronate (ZA) is a potent aminobisphosphonate used in osteoporosis treatment. A common side effect is the acute-phase response (APR), which occurs in nearly 40-50% of individuals who receive the fi rst dose.

PURPOSE: This open-label randomized trial evaluated the efficacy of short-course oral dexamethasone in reducing APR following the first ZA infusion.

METHODS: Participants with osteoporosis (n = 51) were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either intravenous ZA plus oral dexamethasone 4 mg on the day of infusion (D0) and two subsequent days (D1 and D2; intervention arm) or intravenous ZA alone (control arm). Oral temperature was measured by a digital thermometer at baseline, three times daily on D0-D2, and on the morning of D3. The primary outcome was the change in temperature from baseline over 3 days, estimated using a linear mixed-effects model.

RESULTS: Fifty participants (62% diabetes; intervention, n = 26, and control, n = 24) were included in the analysis. The between-group difference in temperature change from baseline, averaged across all post-infusion timepoints, was 0.35 °C (95% CI: 0.19 to 0.51; p < 0.001), favoring the intervention group. The intervention effect was most marked on the evening of D1 (0.99 °C [95% CI: 0.71 to 1.27]; p < 0.001). Incident fever (temperature ≥37.8 °C) occurred in 26.9% of participants in the intervention group, compared with 66.7% in the control group (p = 0.01; NNT: 2.5). Rescue paracetamol was needed more frequently in the control group (79.2% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.022).

CONCLUSION: Our findings support the use of a 3-day course of oral dexamethasone to reduce post-infusion fever in first-time ZA users.

CTRI REGISTRATION NO: CTRI/2025/01/079301.

articles.title: Examining the relationship between objective and patient-reported physical function in adults with cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer and its therapies negatively impact physical function (PF), which is commonly captured using patient-reported PF measures. Though important, patient-report PF tools may fail to capture important aspects of objectively measured PF, limiting their ability to provide a comprehensive assessment of PF.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare patient-reported (PROMIS-Physical Function Computer Adaptive Test, PROMIS PF) and objective (Bellarmine Norton Assessment Tool, BNAT) measures of PF in adults with a history of cancer.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included a referred and volunteer sample of 94 adults with a history of cancer (91.5% women, 60.1 ± 10.8 years) who completed the BNAT and the PROMIS PF. The BNAT includes the 2-minute step test (MST), 30-second sit-to-stand (STS), 30-second arm curl, and timed-up-and-go (TUG), with total scores calculated from the sum of subscale scores. Pearson's correlations, variance (r2), and descriptive statistics were used to evaluate the relationships between BNAT and PROMIS scores.

RESULTS: Weak correlations were observed between PROMIS PF total scores and BNAT total scores (r = 0.313, p = 0.002) and between the PROMIS PF and BNAT raw scores, including STS (r = 0.362, p = 0.001), arm curl (r = 0.320, p = 0.002), and TUG (r = -0.319, p = 0.002). Variance explained ranged from 3.3%-13.1%, suggesting limited overlap between subjective and objective measures.

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that patient-reported and performance-based assessments of PF are generally weakly associated in adults with a history of cancer. These findings highlight the potential value of incorporating both approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of PF in clinical and research settings.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT06039488.

articles.title: Life-Threatening Retroperitoneal Hematoma After Radial PCI: A Rare Case of Spontaneous Lumbar Artery Bleeding.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous retroperitoneal hematoma is a rare, life-threatening complication of antithrombotic therapy, seldom considered after radial percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old man underwent radial PCI of the right coronary artery 3 days after streptokinase for inferior myocardial infarction on dual antiplatelet therapy and enoxaparin. Twelve hours later, he developed abdominal pain and hypotension, with hemoglobin falling from 11.6 to 6 g/dL. Computed tomography showed a large left retroperitoneal hematoma with active extravasation, and angiography localized bleeding to the left third lumbar artery, which was successfully embolized. Recovery was complicated by acute renal failure requiring dialysis; the hematoma resolved on follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Layered fibrinolytic, antiplatelet, and anticoagulant exposure can cause spontaneous non-access-site bleeding even after radial access, where retroperitoneal hemorrhage is rarely suspected.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Radial access does not eliminate major bleeding risk. Unexplained hypotension after PCI should prompt early imaging to exclude retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

articles.title: When Unloading Backfires: Intra-Aortic Balloon Pumping and Dynamic LVOT Obstruction in Takotsubo Syndrome.
Time-Evolving In Situ Coronary Thrombosis During Durable LVAD Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction during durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support is usually attributed to pump thromboembolism or anticoagulation failure; in situ coronary thrombosis arising from local vascular pathology is rarely recognized.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with pre-implant angiography confirming patent coronary arteries developed acute left anterior descending artery occlusion during long-term continuous-flow LVAD support. Intravascular ultrasound showed mural-adherent thrombus at the coronary bifurcation with negative remodeling and intact distal architecture, distinguishing in situ thrombosis from embolic occlusion. Aspiration thrombectomy without stenting restored normal flow.

DISCUSSION: Nonpulsatile hemodynamics, endothelial dysfunction, and recurrent bacteremia likely converged to produce coronary thrombosis independent of conventional embolic mechanisms, a scenario infrequently described in the LVAD literature and relevant to clinicians evaluating unexplained myocardial infarction in this population.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In situ coronary thrombosis is an underrecognized, mechanistically distinct cause of myocardial infarction during LVAD support. Serial coronary imaging with intravascular ultrasound aids diagnosis and can guide thrombus-directed therapy without unnecessary stenting.

articles.title: ST-elevation myocardial infarction in Europe (2022-24): the EuroHeart Acute Coronary Syndromes-Percutaneous Coronary Interventions Programme.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The European Unified Registries on Heart Care Evaluation And Randomized Trials (EuroHeart) collaboration of national registries evaluates contemporary care of common cardiovascular diseases in Europe. This report summarizes care of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) across 13 countries using EuroHeart Acute Coronary Syndromes-Percutaneous Coronary Interventions registry data.

METHODS: Aggregated data were analysed from national registries in the EuroHeart Acute Coronary Syndromes-Percutaneous Coronary Interventions registry collaboration, expanding from six countries in 2022 to 13 in 2024. Baseline characteristics, acute reperfusion, discharge medications, and in-hospital outcomes were collected for STEMI admissions. Key quality indicators were evaluated.

RESULTS: In total, 146 958 STEMI admissions were collected between 2022 and 2024. Mean age across all countries was 65.4 years (lowest and highest individual country mean: 62.0; 69.3); 27.9% were female (18.2; 36.2), 37.8% current smoker (22.4; 58.7), 58.2% had hypertension (42.9; 76.2), 22.5% diabetes (12.8; 35.2), and 8.9% prior heart failure (3.0; 31.2). The proportion of patients reperfused was high [95.0% (90.6; 100)], with radial artery access in 87.6% (73.2; 95.1). Only 63.9% (34.3; 95.5) received reperfusion within 90 min of diagnostic ECG, with large variability between countries. Prescriptions at discharge were high for aspirin [90.3% (83.2; 98.5)], P2Y12 inhibitors [95.1% (92.0; 100.0)], and statins [93.2% (86.5; 97.1)], but lower for ezetimibe [23.4% (12.9; 34.2)] and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors [32.7% (16.7; 42.3)]. In-hospital mortality was 6.4% (1.6; 9.5).

CONCLUSIONS: The EuroHeart Acute Coronary Syndromes-Percutaneous Coronary Interventions registry provides continuous monitoring of standards of care for patients with STEMI. While quality of care is high overall, opportunities for improvement remain in modifiable risk factors, timing of invasive procedures, intensity of antiplatelet treatments, as well as lipid-lowering and heart failure medications at discharge.

articles.title: Current evidence and future directions of factor XI inhibition in cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract: Factor XI (FXI) inhibition has emerged as a promising antithrombotic strategy aimed at reducing thrombosis while preserving hemostasis. Its development has been supported by the dissociation between FXI-mediated thrombus propagation and physiological coagulation, as well as by early phase II studies that characterized target inhibition, dose response, and preliminary bleeding and efficacy signals across cardiovascular settings. However, phase III data have shown that clinical benefit is not uniform. In atrial fibrillation, OCEANIC-AF was stopped early because asundexian 50 mg once daily provided less protection against stroke or systemic embolism than apixaban, despite lower bleeding. Conversely, OCEANIC-STROKE demonstrated that asundexian reduced recurrent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke without increasing major bleeding. In acute coronary syndromes, the neutral PACIFIC-AMI results and the discontinuation of LIBREXIA-ACS for futility suggest limited incremental efficacy when activated factor XI (FXIa) inhibition is added to contemporary antiplatelet therapy. Evidence in orthopedic thromboprophylaxis, cancer-associated thrombosis, and end-stage renal disease remains promising but incomplete. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov, focusing on phase II and III clinical studies of FXI/FXIa inhibition. This review summarizes the clinical evidence for FXI/FXIa inhibitors and discusses how future use will depend on matching the appropriate agent, dose, comparator, and patient population.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Combined Supine-Prone Quantitative Myocardial Perfusion SPECT for Detecting Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease: A Patient- and Vessel-Territory-Based Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess and compare the diagnostic performance of supine-only, prone-only, and software-derived combined supine-prone quantitative myocardial perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) for identifying obstructive coronary artery disease in male patients.

METHOD: This retrospective, single-center diagnostic accuracy study evaluated men who underwent a one-day stress-rest myocardial perfusion SPECT protocol with technetium-99m (Tc-99m) sestamibi, had both supine and prone stress and rest acquisitions, and subsequently underwent invasive coronary angiography within 3 months. Total perfusion deficit (TPD), summed stress score (SSS), summed rest score (SRS), summed difference score (SDS), and vessel-territory measurements were recorded from the supine, prone, and combined datasets. Obstructive coronary artery disease was defined as stenosis of at least 50% in the left main coronary artery or at least 70% in the left anterior descending artery (LAD), left circumflex artery (LCx), or right coronary artery (RCA).

RESULTS: Combined stress TPD demonstrated the greatest patient-level discriminatory ability (area under the curve [AUC], 0.892; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.846-0.938). The corresponding AUCs for supine and prone stress TPD were 0.798 and 0.868, respectively. The AUC gain for combined versus supine stress TPD was 0.094 (95% CI, 0.048-0.140; P < 0.001), whereas the gain for combined versus prone stress TPD was 0.024 (95% CI, -0.008 to 0.056; P = 0.142). For supine stress TPD, the optimal cutoff was 6.20, yielding 77.0% sensitivity, 73.7% specificity, and 74.5% accuracy. For combined stress TPD, the optimal cutoff was 4.10, yielding 88.5% sensitivity, 84.4% specificity, and 85.4% accuracy.

CONCLUSION: In male patients undergoing a complete stress-rest examination, software-derived combined supine-prone quantitative myocardial perfusion SPECT (MPS) improved specificity and overall diagnostic accuracy compared with supine-only assessment by reducing false-positive findings caused by inferior and inferolateral attenuation. Combined positioning should be viewed as an adjunct to, rather than a substitute for, paired stress-rest assessment and physician visual interpretation.

articles.title: Pyrolysis of Hexamethyldisiloxane.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. A
articles.abstract: The pyrolysis of hexamethyldisiloxane (HMDSO) was studied behind reflected shock waves (1400-1500 K, 0.28-12.0 atm) with molecular beam sampling and time-of-flight mass spectrometric (TOF-MS) detection. The higher-pressure experiments used tunable synchrotron vacuum ultraviolet (SVUV) photoionization while the lower-pressure experiments employed electron-impact ionization. The results yielded complementary time-resolved information about the species formed during HMDSO pyrolysis, allowing improved understanding of the dominant reaction pathways. Additional SVUV-TOF-MS experiments, without time resolution and using a SiC microreactor (290 and 1273 K), yielded higher resolution photoionization mass spectra and improved signal-to-noise for small but important mass spectral features. The observed pyrolysis products included H2, SiC, methane, acetylene, ethylene, trimethylsilanol and several silicon-containing molecules and radicals smaller than HMDSO. H2 and SiC were observed for the first time during HMDSO pyrolysis. Almost negligible peaks were observed for species larger than HMDSO indicating that growth pathways analogous to polyaromatic hydrocarbon formation were unfavorable in the shock tube and microreactor experiments. This is contrary to literature studies at lower temperatures and longer residence times. The experimental work was complemented by a theoretical study of the initiation pathways in HMDSO pyrolysis. Over the range of conditions studied here, the dominant dissociation channel (∼95%) is Si-C bond fission to make CH3 radicals. Minor initiation reactions include a molecular channel yielding 2-silaisobutene + trimethylsilanol and C-H bond fission yielding H + (CH3)3SiOSi(CH3)2CH2. Pressure falloff in these unimolecular initiation reactions was negligible at T < 1500 K but persists at higher temperatures, even in this large molecule. Mass spectral features consistent with tetramethylsilane and trimethylsilanol were observed, but not their more reactive coproducts. The present experimental and theoretical studies provide considerable insights into the initial pyrolysis mechanism of an important silica nanoparticle precursor and provide a new foundation for extrapolation to other fully methylated siloxanes.

articles.title: Composition-Dependent Phase Partitioning and Nanoscale Mixing in Rapidly Condensed U/Al and U/Al/Fe Vapors.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. A
articles.abstract: Rapid cooling of multicomponent vapors produces oxide particles through coupled oxidation, nucleation, condensation, and aggregation occurring on millisecond time scales. In uranium-bearing systems, these pathways remain poorly understood when redox-active and refractory elements condense together. Here, we isolate the effect of initial composition by comparing binary uranium/aluminum (U/Al) and ternary uranium/aluminum/iron (U/Al/Fe) vapors condensed under a fixed temperature profile in a plasma flow reactor (PFR). Oxygen for oxide formation was supplied through the aqueous nitrate precursors introduced into the argon plasma. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), electron diffraction, elemental mapping, and image-based particle statistics were used to relate particle morphology, crystal structure, elemental partitioning, and projected particle size. Binary U/Al condensates formed predominantly α-UO3 and η-Al2O3 as small, weakly aggregated particles. Increasing Fe relative to Al shifted the condensates toward larger aggregates containing UO2, η-Al2O3, Fe3O4, and mixed U-Fe oxides. Correlated high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) measurements show that U and Fe are spatially associated within particle aggregates, including mixed U-Fe oxide crystallites, whereas Al preferentially partitions into spatially distinct crystalline and amorphous Al-rich regions. These results demonstrate that initial composition controls both phase selection and nanoscale chemical partitioning during rapid condensation, providing particle-scale constraints for models of nonequilibrium multicomponent oxide formation.

articles.title: Influenza-specific Plasmablast Responses Elicited by Vaccination of Infants and Toddlers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infants and young children are at higher risk for severe outcomes from seasonal influenza, including hospitalization and death. The original exposure to influenza antigens through vaccination or infection in infants and young children may shape B cell responses that occur following subsequent exposures to influenza. Here we examined influenza-specific plasmablast responses in a longitudinal birth cohort to define the magnitude of responses occurring in childhood, beginning with the very first antigen exposure.

METHODS: Infants were enrolled in a community-based birth cohort in the US and were followed longitudinally, with weekly sampling of nasal secretions for virus detection and recording of respiratory symptoms. PBMCs were collected following influenza vaccination and/or infection to define the frequency of total and influenza-specific antibody secreting cells (ASC) using a multiplex fluorescent ELISpot assay. A subset of participants were selected for further analysis to quantify influenza-specific antibody titers by ELISA and HAI.

RESULTS: Plasmablast responses to an initial 2-dose series given to infants and toddlers were comparable in magnitude to the response seen following influenza infection in antigen-naïve children, while levels following the 3rd vaccination were similar to adult responses. Influenza-specific IgG responses in early childhood correlated with the magnitude of influenza-specific IgG plasmablast responses. Potentially protective HAI titers ( ≥ 40) were generally achieved following the 3rd vaccine dose.

CONCLUSIONS: These results support the use of a 2-dose initial vaccine series in infants and young children and demonstrate that robust influenza-specific plasmablast responses and antibody titers consistent with protection are achieved following the 3rd vaccine dose.

articles.title: Electrophysiology Highlights from the ESC Congress 2026: new hope on the boulevard of broken dreams.
[Anasarca, serositis, and lymphadenopathy - symptoms suggestive of idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease].
articles.abstract: Idiopathic multicentric Castleman disease (iMCD) is a rare, potentially life-threatening lymphoproliferative disorder associated with systemic inflammation and dysregulated IL-6 signalling. We describe a 64-year-old woman with rapidly progressive fever, anasarca and serositis. Infection, autoimmune disease and malignancy were not demonstrated. PET-CT showed generalized hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy, and excisional lymph node biopsy showed histopathological features consistent with Castleman disease. After exclusion of HHV-8 infection and POEMS syndrome, iMCD-NOS was diagnosed. Siltuximab and corticosteroids led to rapid clinical and biochemical improvement. The combination of anasarca, serositis, and generalized lymphadenopathy should prompt early excisional biopsy, and haematology referral, as timely diagnosis enables targeted IL-6-directed therapy.

articles.title: Expert Consensus on Pediatric and Primary Care Practitioner Management of Atopic Dermatitis in Children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common, chronic, recurring, inflammatory skin disease that commonly affects children. Pediatricians and primary care providers (PCPs) serve as the frontline clinicians for children with AD. The purpose of this expert consensus panel was to review the published literature on pediatric AD and develop best practice recommendations for pediatric primary care.

METHODS: A panel of experts in pediatric atopic dermatitis, including dermatologists and allergists, was selected and clinical issues delineated. A comprehensive literature search was completed using a combination of keywords "atopic dermatitis," "pediatric," "diagnosis," "treatment," and "primary care." Articles were reviewed and consensus statements generated. A modified Delphi process was used to assess, edit, and approve or reject each statement, and a strength of recommendation was assigned.

RESULTS: The literature search produced 60 articles. Screening resulted in 22 articles that met criteria. The panel unanimously voted to adopt 10 consensus statements and recommendations: five with strength "A," two with strength "B," and three with strength "C." Management suggestions include severity assessment of AD, assessing impact of poorly controlled AD on multiple life dimensions, appropriate use of topical steroid and nonsteroidal agents, considerations for referral to specialists, and practitioner awareness of FDA approved targeted topical and systemic therapies including advanced biologic and other systemic agents.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric primary care serves a crucial role in the management of AD. Early and accurate diagnosis, evaluation of quality of life (QoL), knowledge of the proper use of topical corticosteroids, understanding the length of an appropriate trial of topical therapies, identification of patients requiring escalation to systemic treatment, and timely referral to specialists are essential for comprehensive care.

articles.title: Determining the optimal treatment strategies of IDH1 inhibitors in patients with R/R mIDH1 AML: a United States Delphi consensus.
articles.abstract: There is a need for recommendations about the optimal isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) inhibitor treatment strategy within the relapsed/refractory (R/R) IDH1 mutation (mIDH1) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) treatment paradigm. This study aimed to develop consensus-based recommendations for treatment of R/R mIDH1 AML. A panel of 17 clinicians (including a three-person steering committee) with expertise in the treatment of patients with R/R mIDH1 AML participated in this Delphi panel. Two rounds of electronic surveys were distributed allowing anonymous completion of both open-ended scoping questions and Likert-scale based consensus statements. Panelists agreed that the IDH1 inhibitors ivosidenib and olutasidenib demonstrate clinical efficacy with adequate tolerability in patients with R/R mIDH1 AML. When selecting preferred initial treatments, consensus established that (1) olutasidenib is the preferred option for R/R mIDH1 AML patients previously exposed to a venetoclax-based treatment regimen and (2) venetoclax-based treatment is preferred for patients with prior exposure to an ivosidenib-based treatment.

articles.title: Association of Robotic Pancreaticoduodenectomy With Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism: A Propensity Score-Matched National Analysis.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the association between robotic pancreaticoduodenectomy (RPD) and postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) compared with open pancreaticoduodenectomy (OPD).MethodsAdults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy in the ACS NSQIP pancreatic-targeted database (2022-2024) were identified. RPD patients were matched 1:1 to OPD patients by propensity score, including a modified fistula risk score (mFRS). Matched comparisons used paired methods (exact McNemar test, conditional odds ratios). A primary multivariable model was restricted to operative approach and baseline characteristics, and a sensitivity analysis excluded the transfusion component of the mFRS.ResultsOf 11 223 patients, 1361 (12.1%) underwent RPD, and all were matched (n = 2722). VTE occurred in 4.8% of patients after RPD and 2.6% after OPD (paired risk difference 2.2 percentage points, 95% CI 0.8-3.6; conditional OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.24-2.85; P = .003). The difference was driven predominantly by pulmonary embolism (2.3% vs 0.9%; P = .004) rather than deep vein thrombosis (2.9% vs 1.9%; P = .10). In the primary multivariable model, robotic approach (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.24-2.86) and obesity (OR 2.19, 95% CI 1.44-3.32) were associated with VTE; the estimate for robotic approach was similar without transfusion (OR 1.84, 95% CI 1.22-2.79). Overall, 36% of VTE events were diagnosed after discharge.ConclusionsIn contemporary national data, RPD was associated with a higher rate of postoperative VTE than OPD, predominantly pulmonary embolism. These observational, hypothesis-generating findings do not establish the benefit of any new prophylaxis strategy; prospective studies of risk-stratified extended thromboprophylaxis are warranted.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics, Mechanisms, and Management of Gore Cardioform Device-Related Thrombosis: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Device-related thrombosis (DRT) is a rare but potentially serious complication following transcatheter closure of patent foramen ovale (PFO) and atrial septal defect (ASD). Although the Gore Cardioform family of septal occluders is increasingly used in contemporary structural heart interventions, evidence regarding associated thrombotic complications remains limited and fragmented. In this narrative review, we systematically summarize the available literature on DRT associated with Gore Cardioform devices, including randomized clinical trials, observational studies, and published case reports. The overall incidence appears low; however, reported cases highlight a heterogeneous clinical presentation, ranging from incidental imaging findings to systemic embolic events. Thrombus formation most commonly occurs within the early post-implantation period, although late events have also been described. Potential mechanisms are multifactorial and include incomplete endothelialization, flow disturbances related to device design, and patient-specific prothrombotic conditions. Identified risk factors include hypercoagulable states, atrial arrhythmias, inadequate antithrombotic therapy or poor adherence, large defect size, and device-related factors affecting septal apposition. Current management strategies are largely empirical and typically involve systemic anticoagulation, with most cases resolving without the need for invasive intervention. In selected high-risk or refractory cases, thrombolysis or surgical removal may be required. Given the absence of device-specific guidelines, we propose a practical, clinically oriented framework for the prevention, detection, and management of suspected DRT in patients undergoing PFO or ASD closure with Gore Cardioform devices.

articles.title: Automated corticospinal tract shape measures and functional recovery after stroke: an exploratory study in patients receiving rTMS-based rehabilitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper limb motor recovery after stroke remains challenging to predict solely based on clinical measures. The role of corticospinal tract (CST) shape in functional recovery following stroke is not well understood.

OBJECTIVE: We examined the associations between automated CST shape measures and changes in functional independence and upper limb motor function in stroke patients receiving repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS)-based rehabilitation.

METHODS: This study included 42 stroke patients. The modified Barthel Index (MBI) and Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity motor score (FMU-M) were employed to evaluate motor impairment before and after rTMS-based rehabilitation. Relative CST shape metrics were calculated as the ratio of the ipsilesional to contralesional values using automated tractography. Univariate and multivariate analyses were used to identify the associations between shape metrics, clinical variables, and motor improvement.

RESULTS: Automated tractography was unsuccessful in three patients. MBI improvement was significantly associated with elongation (r = -0.41, p = 0.01) and number of tracts (r = 0.39, p = 0.01), whereas FMU-M improvement was related to trunk volume (r = 0.36, p = 0.02). In the multivariable stepwise analysis, relative elongation (p = 0.04), age (p < 0.01), and onset-to-diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) interval (p = 0.02) were associated with MBI improvement. The selected model yielded a prediction R2 of 0.46. For FMU-M improvement, relative trunk volume was not selected.

CONCLUSIONS: Along with clinical variables, relative CST elongation derived from automated tractography showed an exploratory association with improvement in functional independence in patients receiving rTMS-based rehabilitation.

articles.title: Mapping the Developmental Landscape of Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes and Cardiac Organoids Relative to Native Heart Tissue.
articles.abstract: The development of physiologically relevant human cardiac models is essential for drug discovery and disease modeling; however, achieving the transcriptomic and metabolic maturity of adult human tissue remains a challenge. In this study, we performed a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic comparison of in vitro-induced pluripotent stem cell cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) in 2D cultures, 3D cardiac organoids, and native fetal and adult human cardiac tissue. CMs from both 2D and organoid cultures were immature compared to adult CMs. 3D organoids exhibit a more complex cellular architecture comprising multiple cardiac cell types, and they possess a unique proliferative fibroblast population that is not represented in the adult or fetal heart. Organoids also showed immaturity in non-CMs as well as CM cell types. Both iPSC-CMs and cardiac organoids were metabolically immature with enhanced expression of both glycolytic and reduced fatty acid oxidation genes. However, maturation was not a binary state, as the in vitro CMs were distinct from fetal CMs, and had transcriptionally advanced calcium handling and electrophysiology, but immature metabolism and stress responses. When assessed versus adult heart tissues they were also distinct. Our work provides a molecular roadmap of the gaps between in vitro models and the native adult heart, highlighting areas for future improvement in in vitro CMs.

articles.title: Telehealth for hypertension: A network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTelehealth interventions for blood pressure (BP) monitoring and counselling are increasingly used to support follow-up care and long-term management in hypertension (HT). However, the comparative effectiveness of different telehealth feature combinations remains unclear.MethodsWe conducted a network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating telehealth monitoring interventions in adults with HT. Interventions were classified into four core digital health features: tracking (T), notify (N), remote (R) and educate (E). Intervention combinations included T, N, R, E, TN, TR, TE, NE, TNR, TNE, TRE, NRE and TNRE. Standard care (SC) served as the reference comparator. The primary outcome was controlled BP. Secondary outcomes were medication adherence and changes in systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP (DBP).ResultsForty RCTs involving 11,644 patients were included. Interventions incorporating more telehealth features were more effective than SC. For BP control, TNRE showed the highest odds of achieving control (OR 2.97, 95%CI 1.77-4.98), followed by TRE (OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.05-6.94). For medication adherence, only TNE showed a numerically greater effect, although the difference was not statistically significant, versus SC (SMD 3.36, 95%CI -0.43 to 7.15). For SBP, TNRE (MD -3.69 mmHg, 95%CI -7.00 to -0.38) and TNE (MD -3.83 mmHg, 95%CI -6.84 to -0.81) were associated with significant reductions versus SC. For DBP, only TNRE showed a significant reduction (MD -3.02 mmHg, 95%CI -5.30 to -0.74).ConclusionMulti-component telehealth interventions were associated with better BP outcomes than simpler approaches or SC. More integrated telehealth models may therefore offer greater benefit for HT follow-up.

articles.title: Clinical Impact of Routine Duffy Antigen Testing in Children With Low Absolute Neutrophil Counts.
articles.abstract: Duffy-null-associated neutrophil count (DANC) is a common physiological explanation for an isolated low absolute neutrophil count but frequently remains unrecognized, resulting in prolonged specialist follow-up and repeated investigations. We conducted a single-center prospective-retrospective cohort study evaluating the clinical impact of routine Duffy antigen testing in children referred for neutropenia at a tertiary pediatric immune-hematology clinic. Among 141 children undergoing Duffy phenotyping, 107 (75.9%) were Duffy-null; six were excluded because baseline immune-hematological abnormalities required continued specialist evaluation. Among 101 children with isolated DANC, routine testing was associated with shorter time to diagnostic resolution (median 0 vs. 43 months), fewer outpatient visits (1 vs. 7), and lower mean cumulative healthcare costs (€317 vs. €1007 per patient) compared with historical evaluation. Advanced imaging, genetic testing, and bone marrow examinations were performed only in the historical cohort. Routine Duffy phenotyping, integrated with clinical assessment and baseline immune-hematological evaluation, enabled earlier diagnostic resolution and reduced specialist surveillance and healthcare utilization in children with isolated DANC.

articles.title: From GLP-1 Receptor Agonism to Multi-Receptor Targeting in Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists are established kidney-protective therapy in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease, and co-agonists and multi-agonists that also target the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon receptors are advancing. Most reviews address these agents as a single class. This narrative review examines the three receptors separately, distinguishing the renal efficacy of a molecule from the causal contribution attributable to each of its receptor targets, and addresses three questions. First, what is known about the renal actions of each receptor: GLP-1 receptor agonism is the only receptor profile for which a drug (semaglutide) has shown kidney benefit in a dedicated outcome trial (FLOW), although the receptor-specific mechanism in humans is not established, as natriuresis is acute, not sustained, and hemodynamic effects are context-dependent; no GIP receptor-specific renal signature has been established in humans; and glucagon receptor signaling appears bidirectional, with potentially protective tubular actions coexisting with a risk of hyperfiltration. Second, whether co-agonists and multi-agonists provide kidney benefit beyond GLP-1 receptor agonism alone: tirzepatide consistently reduces albuminuria and was associated with fewer major kidney events than dulaglutide in an exploratory analysis of SURPASS-CVOT, driven largely by new-onset macroalbuminuria, and glucagon-containing agents show early albuminuria signals, but no design isolates a receptor-specific contribution and none has been tested in a dedicated kidney outcome trial. Third, how kidney function should be assessed during pharmacological weight loss, when changes in muscle and fat mass may bias creatinine- and cystatin C-based estimates. We propose a receptor-based hierarchy of evidence as a hypothesis-generating framework and identify the trials and kidney metrics needed to test it.

articles.title: Mapping the Right Atrial Ganglionated Plexuses Using the Novel Tau20-RETROmapping System.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexuses (ET-GPs) from the intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system are proposed upstream drivers of atrial fibrillation (AF). The investigational Tau20-RETROmapping system (TauRhythm Therapies, UK) was developed to identify ET-GPs and was used to characterize their distribution in the right atrium (RA) of patients undergoing repeat AF ablation.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the anatomical distribution and nature of RA-GP sites using the Tau20-RETROmapping system.

METHODS: Patients undergoing re-do AF ablation were recruited. The Tau20-RETROmapping system was used to map RA ET-GP sites by delivering synchronized high-frequency stimulation (HFS; 50 mA, 40 Hz, 80 ms, up to 15 trains) via a contact-force-sensing ablation catheter. If sinus rhythm could not be maintained, AV-dissociating-GP (AVD-GP) sites were identified using continuous HFS (50 mA, 20 Hz, 10 s). All test sites were annotated on a 3D electroanatomic map.

RESULTS: 54 patients underwent RA-GP mapping (63 ± 8 yrs, 67% male, paroxysmal AF: 35%) with 72 ± 16 GP sites tested to identify 9.7 ± 3.2 GPs. Mapping strategies included ET-GP only (29 patients), mixed ET-GP/AVD-GP (20), and AVD-GP only (5). ET-GPs clustered at the inferior right free wall, right atrial appendage (RAA)-superior vena cava (SVC) junction, RAA-RA interface, anterolateral wall, and posterior intra-atrial septum. Few GP sites were identified on the posterior wall, and none on the cavotricuspid isthmus. AVD-GPs were almost exclusively septal. Notable responses included SVC-induced ectopy, AF initiation, and pulmonary vein ectopy during RA stimulation.

CONCLUSION: The novel Tau20-RETROmapping system enables systematic RA ET-GP mapping. Distinct GP clustering patterns and observed electrophysiological phenomena may enhance understanding of AF mechanisms, particularly non-pulmonary vein triggers.

articles.title: Predicting metal toxicity from bioaccumulated concentrations in Gammarus fossarum - Part 1: Describing the effects of nine trace metal elements on survival kinetics of females and embryos using the GUTS model.
articles.abstract: Once introduced into freshwater ecosystems, trace metal elements (TMEs) can induce a wide range of sub-lethal and lethal effects across taxa, ultimately compromising ecosystem health and biodiversity. Traditional environmental risk assessments rely on static dose-response models, which fail to capture the temporal dynamics of effects. Mechanistic toxicokinetic-toxicodynamic models, as General Unified Threshold models of Survival (GUTS), provide a more realistic framework by linking external concentration of contaminant to lethal effects under time-variable conditions. In this study, GUTS-RED models were applied to assess the toxicity of nine TMEs (As, Cd, Cr, Co, Cu, Pb, Ni, Ag, and Zn) for the freshwater amphipod Gammarus fossarum, a European sentinel species widely used in ecotoxicology. Individuals were exposed for 21 days to concentration gradients of each metal, and mortality was recorded for adult females and embryos. GUTS models fitted to such survival kinetics gave estimate of key toxicity parameters such as the killing rate, the No Effect Concentration or the 21 days 50% Lethal Concentration for each stage and each TME. By comparing both ontogenetic stages, this work provides novel insights in life-stage-specific sensitivity to metal exposure and bridges mechanistic modelling and empirical ecotoxicology, offering a refined and ecologically relevant framework for assessing metal-related risks in freshwater ecosystems. Furthermore, a complementary assessment of toxicity based on internalized and bioavailable fractions of contamination will be presented in a companion study, thereby improving the accuracy and ecological realism of toxicity predictions for the interpretation of French biomonitoring data.

articles.title: Middle Ear Rhabdomyosarcoma: An Updated Survival Analysis From the Children's Oncology Group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Middle ear rhabdomyosarcoma (ME-RMS) is often locally advanced at diagnosis with extension occurring through the tympanic membrane, intracranially, or laterally in front of or under the ear but rarely metastasizes distantly. We describe the presentation and outcomes of patients with ME-RMS treated on recent Children's Oncology Group (COG) clinical trials.

PROCEDURE: Patients with ME-RMS enrolled on COG studies for newly diagnosed RMS from 1997 to 2022 were included. Demographic information, tumor characteristics, and survival information were analyzed using descriptive and survival statistics.

RESULTS: Fifty-one patients with ME-RMS were identified. The majority (68.6%) were male and under 10 years old (98%). Tumor histology was most commonly embryonal (47.1%) or botryoid (37.3%). The majority (76.5%) had tumors ≤5 cm. Lymph node involvement was identified in 27.5%. Most tumors were classified as COG Stage 2 (54.9%) or 3 (39.2%), with the vast majority Intergroup Rhabdomyosarcoma Study (IRS) Group III (92.2%). Most (96.1%) received radiation therapy for local control. The 4-year event-free survival (EFS) was 72.6% (95% CI 59.8-85.3) and overall survival (OS) 76.2% (95% CI 63.8-88.7) for the entire cohort. There was no difference in EFS or OS related to tumor size, COG stage, or clinical group. Patients treated on study D9803 had a numerically higher, but not statistically significant 4-year EFS (81.5%, 95% CI 66.8-96.1) and OS (85.2%, 95% CI 71.5-98.9) compared with ARST0531 and ARST1431, which had a combined 4-year EFS (60.9%, 95% CI 37.3-84.5) and OS (64.5%, 95% CI 40.6-88.3).

CONCLUSIONS: ME-RMS is a rare, locally aggressive tumor that predominantly affects young children. Outcomes remain suboptimal without demonstrated improvement over the 25-year period of this study. Although survival did not significantly differ across treatment protocols, the observed numerically lower survival with reduced cyclophosphamide exposure on more recent trials supports further evaluation of treatment intensity in this population.

articles.title: One-Stop Catheter Ablation Combined With "Kissing" Left Atrial Appendage Closure in a Patient With Dextrocardia and Atrial Fibrillation: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: One-stop catheter ablation (CA) combined with left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (LAAC) is widely used in patients with atrial fibrillation (AFib); however, it is extremely challenging to perform catheter-based procedures in rare cases of AFib with dextrocardia and complex LAA anatomy. Such cases may require precise occlusion strategies, such as dual-device "Kissing LAAC." However, to our knowledge, no cases of one-stop CA combined with Kissing LAAC in patients with AFib, dextrocardia, and complex LAA anatomy have been reported. A 67-year-old woman with persistent AFib and dextrocardia was found on preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to have a complex bilobed LAA with a shared orifice diameter of approximately 26 mm and shared depth of approximately 12 mm. Therefore, single-device closure was considered unlikely to achieve effective occlusion. A one-stop CA combined with LAAC procedure was planned. After CA, intraoperative multi-projection digital subtraction angiography (DSA) was used to determine the deployment angle, evaluate the superior and inferior lobes, and guide device selection. Two 20-mm WATCHMAN FLX devices were implanted under DSA guidance, and the procedure was completed without immediate complications. At the 3-month follow-up, the patient maintained sinus rhythm, and CTA showed stable device position without device-related thrombus. However, a residual shunt of 2.92 mm was observed on 3-month CTA. This case suggests that one-stop CA combined with Kissing LAAC may be technically feasible in a highly selected patient with AFib, dextrocardia, and complex bilobed LAA anatomy, and it may provide a valuable clinical reference for similar cases.

articles.title: Systemic therapies and cardiovascular events in older adults with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
articles.journal: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psoriatic disease is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Shared inflammatory pathways may allow systemic therapies to influence cardiovascular outcomes; however, evidence in older adults remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: To estimate the association between systemic therapy classes and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in older adults with psoriatic disease.

METHODS: We conducted a population-based cohort study using linked administrative health data from Ontario, Canada. We identified adults aged ≥66 years with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis who newly initiated systemic therapy between April 2007-March 2022. Time-varying exposure classes were methotrexate, other older medications, anti-TNF, anti-IL17, anti-IL12 or 23 biologics and tofacitinib. MACE, the primary outcome, included coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular events, heart failure and peripheral arterial disease. Using Andersen-Gill recurrent-event models, we estimated adjusted rate ratios, comparing current use of each medication class with non-use of that class.

RESULTS: Among 8967 older adults, 51.3% were female and the median age at treatment initiation was 71 years (interquartile range [IQR], 68-76). Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years (IQR, 2.8-8.5), participants contributed 53,378 person-years, during which 2942 recurrent MACE occurred. In fully adjusted analyses, compared with the respective medication class non-use, methotrexate use was significantly associated with lower MACE rates (rate ratio [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.71-0.92), as was anti-TNF biologic use (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.62-0.98). Estimates for anti-IL12 or 23 (RR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.68-1.08) and anti-IL17 biologics (RR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.57-1.06) were directionally consistent with anti-TNF biologics but imprecise, reflecting limited power. Other older systemic medications (RR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.87-1.19) and tofacitinib (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.28-1.68) showed no clear evidence of association.

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with psoriatic disease, methotrexate and anti-TNF biologics were associated with lower MACE rates. Estimates for newer biologics were directionally consistent but imprecise, supporting further longitudinal cardiovascular safety evaluation in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Assessment of knowledge, attitude, and practice towards cardiology pharmacy among pharmacists and physicians at pediatric oncology setting.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionCardiology pharmacist provides patient care, optimizes cardiovascular medication therapy, minimizes drug interactions, and helps in savings cost and time. This study assessed pharmacists' and physicians' knowledge, attitudes, and practice toward cardiology pharmacy service at a pediatric oncology hospital.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional study utilizing an anonymous and voluntary survey was conducted targeting pharmacists and physicians.ResultsA total of 125 respondents participated, including 87 pharmacists and 38 physicians. Both groups demonstrated low knowledge scores (median: 2 out of 8), with no statistically significant difference between them. Knowledge deficiencies were evident regarding the management of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT). Most participants (92.8%) recognized the positive impact of cardiology pharmacy services on drug efficacy and toxicity reduction. Both groups acknowledged the role of cardiology pharmacist in assisting cardiologists with setting treatment plans, minimizing errors, and monitoring drug therapy. A higher proportion of pharmacists than physicians considered drug therapy monitoring as their responsibility (83.9% vs. 65.8%; P = 0.00836). Pharmacists were also more likely than physicians to consider patient counselling their responsibility (95.4% vs. 65.8%; P < 0.001). Drug dosage and interaction inquiries were the most frequently reported reasons for communication with cardiology pharmacist.ConclusionThis study highlighted the value of cardiology pharmacy services in pediatric oncology settings while emphasizing the need to strengthen healthcare professionals' knowledge of cardio-oncology. Continuous education and training programs are recommended to fill this knowledge gap. These findings emphasize strengthening multidisciplinary teamwork and collaboration to support patient care and the effective delivery of cardiology pharmacy services.

articles.title: PET imaging for cardiac sarcoidosis: a prospective comparison of 64Cu-DOTATATE and 18F-FDG.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diagnosing cardiac sarcoidosis with 18F-FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is complicated by high physiological myocardial 18F-FDG uptake. We conducted a prospective clinical trial to assess the value of 64Cu-DOTATATE-a preparation-free alternative to 18F-FDG-in cardiac sarcoidosis.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We included 66 patients ≥ 18 years: 22 with suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, 22 with previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis; and 22 controls without known inflammatory heart disease. Patients with suspected and previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis underwent 18F-FDG and 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT; controls underwent 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT. Two expert nuclear medicine physicians performed blinded scan readings. Median age was 55.2 years (82% men) in suspected cardiac sarcoidosis; 57.4 years (91% men) in previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis; and 57.2 years (82% men) in controls. Median scan interval was 9 days (IQR 6-18). In suspected cardiac sarcoidosis, scan interpretation (active vs. no active cardiac sarcoidosis) was concordant in 20/22 patients (91%), showing substantial agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.70). In previously diagnosed cardiac sarcoidosis, scan interpretation was concordant in 20/22 patients (91%), showing almost perfect agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.82). No controls had ⁶⁴Cu-DOTATATE uptake suggestive of active cardiac sarcoidosis. In patients with suspect foci on both scans (n = 13), myocardial-to-background ratio was 3.28 (IQR 2.81-5.13) for 18F-FDG and 2.63 (IQR 2.11-3.46) for 64Cu-DOTATATE (P = 0.24). Inter-observer agreement was high (Cohen's kappa = 1.00 for 18F-FDG and 0.84 for 64Cu-DOTATATE).

CONCLUSION: 18F-FDG and 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT showed high scan interpretation agreement and strong inter-observer agreement. Unlike 18F-FDG, 64Cu-DOTATATE requires no patient preparation. Our findings support a potential clinical value of 64Cu-DOTATATE PET/CT in cardiac sarcoidosis.

articles.title: PCR-Based Detection of Adenoviral DNA and Infection Control Interventions for Epidemic Keratoconjunctivitis in an Ophthalmology Clinic.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adenoviral conjunctivitis is a highly contagious ocular infection and may be associated with environmental contamination in ophthalmology clinics. This study aimed to detect adenovirus DNA by real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) in clinical and environmental samples and to evaluate whether a multimodal infection control intervention reduced adenoviral DNA detection.

METHODS: This prospective before-after study was conducted in the ophthalmology outpatient clinic of a university hospital in Kocaeli, Türkiye. A total of 40 samples from patients and 70 samples from environmental surfaces were collected during the pre-intervention (Group 1) and post-intervention (Group 2) periods. The intervention consisted of hand hygiene training, surface disinfection using a 200 ppm chlorine dioxide-based agent, and one month of active observation. Adenovirus DNA was detected by real-time PCR, with a cycle threshold value < 38 considered positive.

RESULTS: No demographic differences were detected between Group 1 and Group 2 (p > .05). Overall adenovirus PCR positivity decreased significantly after the intervention, from 36.4% to 7.3% (p = .001). Significant reductions were observed in both patient samples (55% to 10%; p = .007) and environmental samples (25.7% to 5.7%; p = .049). Before the intervention, adenoviral DNA contamination was most frequently detected on applanation tonometer tips (3/7, 42.9%) and slit-lamp biomicroscopes (3/10, 30%). Epiphora was independently associated with PCR positivity (aOR: 10.077; 95% CI: 1.096-92.617; p = .041).

CONCLUSION: Adenoviral DNA was detectable in both patient and environmental samples even during the non-epidemic period (July-September). A bundled infection control intervention was associated with a significant reduction in adenoviral DNA detection. However, because PCR detects viral DNA rather than viable viruses, genotyping was not performed to establish the relatedness of patient- and surface-derived viruses, and the intervention components were applied simultaneously, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of reduced contamination rather than a confirmed reduction in viral viability or transmission.

articles.title: Predictors of Hypomagnesemia Among Hospitalized Patients: A Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum electrolyte monitoring is critical for identifying clinical deterioration in inpatient settings. Clinical and advanced practice nurses rely on laboratory trends to validate physical assessments, implement interventions, and advocate for changes to the treatment plan. Although magnesium plays a key role in potassium and calcium homeostasis, it is not evaluated as routinely as these electrolytes, and data on hypomagnesemia in U.S. hospitals remain limited.

PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine the frequency and clinical predictors of hypomagnesemia among hospitalized patients.

METHODS: An exploratory, descriptive, correlational design was used to examine electronic health record data from 2019 through 2022. Univariate analysis was used to determine the frequency of hypomagnesemia within the dataset and logistic regression models identified patient-level predictors.

RESULTS: Of 93,507 medical records retrieved, 61,043 (65.3%) had a serum magnesium level documented either 30 days prior to admission or during hospitalization, and of these, 17,713 (29%) met the criteria for hypomagnesemia. Hypomagnesemia was significantly associated with hypokalemia and hypocalcemia. Key predictors of hypomagnesemia included use of antidiabetics, anti-ulcer medications, or antidepressants, and history of endocrine disorders, diabetes, digestive disorders, mental health conditions, or abdominal surgery. Although most diuretics were associated with hypomagnesemia, loop diuretics were found to have a protective effect, as was an age older than 80 years.

CONCLUSION: Hypomagnesemia affects a large percentage of hospitalized patients and strongly correlates with other electrolyte imbalances. Understanding these high-risk profiles enables nurses to anticipate possible deficiencies, advocate for targeted screening and additional treatment, and prevent rapid clinical declines in their patients.

articles.title: Metabolic health in children and adults with congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Suboptimal treatment of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) could result in elevated blood pressure and other symptoms of metabolic syndrome, but this has not been systematically investigated in young patients in Sweden. The objective of this study is to investigate whether young patients with CAH in Sweden have elevated blood pressure, dyslipidemia or effects on glucose homeostasis.

METHODS: The present study assessed ambulatory blood pressure, lipid profiles and glucose homeostasis in 52 patients with salt-wasting, simple virilizing and non-classic CAH (27 <18 years) and 96 age- and sex- matched apparently healthy controls (34 <18 years). Group differences between patients and controls were assessed using linear models. Correlations between genotype group (based on the severity of the allele carrying the mildest CYP21A2 variant), blood pressure, and metabolic parameters were assessed by Spearman correlation adjusted for age, sex, and BMI.

RESULTS: Blood pressure was not affected in adult patients. In children with CAH, a more severe CYP21A2 genotype was associated with higher systolic day pressure, and higher mean arterial pressure (MAP) values, while the mean group values remained around the population norm. Metabolic profiles in blood showed effects on glucose homeostasis, lower kidney filtration rates and higher blood lipids in both children and adults with CAH. These effects correlated with a more severe CYP21A2 genotype. In children it also correlated with a higher glucocorticoid replacement dose.

CONCLUSION: Blood pressure is overall well managed in young patients with CAH in Sweden, but the metabolic outcome needs to be carefully monitored in children.

articles.title: Birthweight, adipokines, and clinical characteristics in new-onset type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low birthweight increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk and severity, and is associated with altered plasma adipokines including leptin, adiponectin, and resistin in people without diabetes. We hypothesized that birthweight is associated with adipokine perturbations contributing to greater disease severity at T2D-onset.

METHODS: Fasting plasma adiponectin (n=7540), leptin (n=7429), and resistin (n=7518) levels were measured in individuals with newly diagnosed T2D using the MESO Quickplex SQ 120 multiplex platform. Linear and log-binomial/robust Poisson regression analyses were applied for associations between midwife-recorded birthweight and adipokine levels adjusted for sex, age, T2D-polygenic risk score, and BMI. Associations between adipokines and clinical characteristics were assessed using similar models additionally adjusted for birthweight.

RESULTS: Birthweight was not associated with adipokine levels. However, each 1000g lower birthweight was associated with a 15.2% (95% CI: 11.7, 18.6) higher plasma leptin level only after adjusting for BMI. A 20% higher adiponectin level was associated with later T2D-onset (+1.3 years), lower BMI (-0.30 kg/m2), lower CRP (-6.0%), and higher HOMA2-S (+5.5%). In contrast, higher leptin and resistin levels were associated with higher BMI (+0.58 vs +0.27 kg/m2) and CRP (+6.0% vs +12.4%), and lower HOMA2-S (-3.6% vs -2.0%), respectively. All adipokines were associated with differential use of glucose-, blood pressure-, and lipid-lowering medications.

CONCLUSION: Low birthweight was associated with higher plasma leptin only after BMI adjustment, and not with adiponectin or resistin levels in individuals with newly diagnosed T2D. Associations between adipokines and distinct clinical characteristics at T2D-onset may predominantly be explained by factors other than birthweight.

articles.title: Hyperuricemia is associated with exposure to periodontitis and its potential role in the periodontal-renal association: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the association between the severity of periodontitis and hyperuricemia, as well as the role of hyperuricemia in the association between periodontitis and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR).

METHODS: A cross-sectional data set of 10,158 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2009-2014 was analyzed. The association between stages III-IV periodontitis (exposure) and hyperuricemia (primary outcome) was assessed by multivariable logistic regression. The relationships among periodontitis, hyperuricemia, and eGFR were evaluated by mediation analyses and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.

RESULTS: Of the participants, 19.0% were diagnosed with hyperuricemia, which was more commonly found in individuals with periodontitis at stages III-IV versus stages I-II (22.3% vs. 17.5%, P < 0.001). After adjustments, individuals with stages III-IV periodontitis had 1.202 times the odds of having hyperuricemia (odds ratio [OR] = 1.202, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.039 to 1.390, P = 0.015) than those with stages I-II periodontitis. Mediation analyses suggested that the association between stages III-IV periodontitis and severely impaired kidney filtration function (eGFR at stages G3b-G5) was explained by 18.4% for hyperuricemia. Incorporating stages III-IV periodontitis into ROC models significantly enhanced hyperuricemia's discriminative performance for eGFR impairment, particularly in females (area under curve [AUC] > 0.8). Sensitivity analyses confirmed these findings.

CONCLUSION: Periodontitis is associated with an increased prevalence of hyperuricemia, and hyperuricemia appears to be a contributing factor in the relationship between periodontitis and severely impaired kidney filtration function.

articles.title: Interpreting cerebral 18F-FDG hypometabolism in Alzheimer's disease: A multidomain framework for supply, transformation, demand, and clearance.
articles.abstract: Cerebral glucose hypometabolism measured by 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET) is a reproducible feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the signal does not directly quantify mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation or adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production. The measured 18F-FDG signal reflects tracer delivery, membrane transport, phosphorylation, cellular activity, and tissue composition, so reduced 18F-FDG uptake cannot be attributed to impaired oxidative phosphorylation alone. To organize these interacting influences, this narrative review considers four functional domains: Supply (perfusion and glucose transporter-mediated transport), Transformation (hexokinase-dependent phosphorylation and redox-sensitive metabolic regulation), Demand (synaptic activity and neuron-glia metabolic coupling), and Clearance (glymphatic exchange and interstitial solute homeostasis). This framework is used as an interpretive structure rather than as a new disease mechanism. We compare the strength of evidence across these domains and outline testable predictions for longitudinal imaging studies, experimental models, and cell-resolved analyses. The framework is illustrated using neuron-glia metabolic coupling, context-dependent metabolic adaptation, and provisional clearance-related interactions, with the AD-cancer comparison used as a contextual example rather than a mechanistic analogy. This approach may help distinguish alternative mechanisms underlying cerebral hypometabolism and inform biomarker design and translational studies.

articles.title: Citrus flavonoids in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD): mechanisms and clinical evidence.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), previously termed non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), is strongly linked to excess energy intake, obesity, insulin resistance and cardiometabolic dysfunction. Oranges, grapefruit, mandarins and lemons, together with the peel and pulp left from juice processing, are the main dietary sources of flavonoids studied as candidate adjuncts in this setting. This review evaluates hesperidin/hesperetin, naringin/naringenin, nobiletin, tangeretin and selected emerging citrus flavonoids across mechanistic, preclinical and human evidence. In cell and animal models these compounds reduce de novo lipogenesis, increase fatty acid oxidation, improve insulin signalling, activate antioxidant defences, suppress inflammatory and profibrotic pathways, and restore mitochondrial quality control and gut-liver axis signalling. The translational strength of this evidence is limited by heterogeneous disease models, designs in which treatment begins before disease is established, doses that exceed plausible human exposure, and incomplete pathway validation. Human evidence comes mainly from small, short-duration studies of hesperidin and naringenin, with lifestyle co-interventions and surrogate outcomes; no trial has shown histological improvement in MASH or fibrosis. Bioavailability depends on glycoside conversion, gut microbial metabolism, conjugation, food matrix and formulation, and citrus-drug interactions have to be considered for each compound and product. Citrus flavonoids are therefore still at an investigational stage. Standardised preparations, physiologically relevant exposure, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic linkage and adequately powered trials with clinically meaningful liver endpoints are needed.

articles.title: The SUFU/AUA Guideline on Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Office-Based Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery (URPS) Procedures.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this guideline is to balance responsible antibiotic stewardship with the need to minimize the risk of serious post-procedure infectious complications, including urosepsis and surgical site infection.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: An evidence-based methodologist conducted a comprehensive, systematic literature search from January 1996 through July 2025 using Ovid in MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. The outcome of interest was defined as confirmed post-procedural urinary tract or surgical site.

RESULTS: Full-text review was performed on 556 studies; 34 were included in the evidence base. This guideline produced 30 statements (9 are evidence-based recommendations, 2 are clinical principles, and 20 are expert opinions).

CONCLUSION: Both the individual's and the procedure's characteristics were considered when attributing risk of serious post-procedure infectious complications and when formulating recommendations for the use of periprocedural antibiotic prophylaxis.
