Low-risk procedures were defined as those that do not involve violation of the urothelium (e.g., catheter exchange, bladder instillation, diagnostic cystoscopy, percutaneous needle placement) and can generally rely on appropriate surgical site preparation and clean/sterile technique, with antibiotic prophylaxis generally unnecessary in most individuals. Increasing invasiveness, with violation of the urothelium or repeated instrumentation, was associated with an increased risk of post-procedure infectious complications, especially in patients at elevated risk for urosepsis (i.e., poor clearance of potential pathogens) or with a positive urinalysis (i.e., potential untreated bacteriuria). Avoiding unnecessary routine antibiotic prophylaxis for office-based urogynecology procedures, in favor of selective use in elevated-risk populations, may entail tolerating a small risk of symptomatic infection to reduce the burden of multidrug-resistant bacteria.

articles.title: Fibrinogen Replacement in Liver Transplantation: A Clinical Review of Fibrinogen Concentrate Versus Cryoprecipitate for Hemostatic Management.
articles.abstract: Coagulopathy and massive bleeding remain major challenges in liver transplantation (LT), often requiring aggressive transfusion support and targeted correction of hypofibrinogenemia. Cryoprecipitate has historically been the primary fibrinogen replacement therapy in LT; however, fibrinogen concentrate (FC) is increasingly used due to advantages in standardization, viral inactivation, rapid reconstitution, and reduced colloidal transfusion volume. Despite adoption across trauma, cardiac surgery, and perioperative hemostasis programs, the evidence base specific to LT remains limited and largely observational. This narrative review analyzes current data on fibrinogen biology in end-stage liver disease (ESLD), contrasts the pharmacologic and operational properties of cryoprecipitate and FC, evaluates LT-specific studies and registry data, and extrapolates evidence from other surgical populations. The review emphasizes potential benefits of FC (predictable dosing, rapid availability, and possibly improved clot firmness) as well as emerging concerns regarding graft thrombosis. Recommendations emphasize individualized, viscoelastic-guided therapy rather than protocolized fixed dosing; however, significant evidence gaps remain and require randomized trials powered for bleeding, thrombotic, and graft-related outcomes.

articles.title: Acute Pulmonary Embolism in the ICU: A Twelve-Year Analysis of 195 392 Hospitalizations Across United States Health Systems.
articles.abstract: ImportanceThe intensive care unit (ICU) burden of acute pulmonary embolism (PE) in the United States, and the extent to which social vulnerability shapes outcomes at the critical care level, remain incompletely characterized in the contemporary treatment era.ObjectiveTo evaluate the epidemiology, treatment, and outcomes of acute PE in adults admitted to United States ICUs, with a focus on socioeconomic vulnerability.DesignRetrospective cohort study over 48 calendar quarters (January 2014 to December 2025).SettingUnited States ICUs within the Epic Cosmos electronic health record database.Participants195 392 hospitalizations of 189 663 unique adults admitted to an ICU with a principal billing diagnosis of acute PE.InterventionsNone.Measurements and Main OutcomesThe incidence of ICU hospitalization for acute PE rose from 6.40 to 10.52 per 1000 ICU admissions, an increase of 0.34 per 1000 per year (95% CI 0.31 to 0.37; Poisson rate ratio 1.037 per year). All cause in-hospital mortality was 8.9%; annual mortality declined from 10.5% (2014) to 8.3% (2019), peaked at 9.7% during the pandemic (2021), and settled at 8.5% to 9.0% without returning to the 2019 nadir. The share of hospitalizations with a simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index of 0 was stable at 15.3% to 18.5%, vasopressor use rose from 11.9% to 20.8%, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy rose from 2.6% (2016) to 31.2% (2025) of hospitalizations. Mortality rose across Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) quartiles from 8.5% (Quartile 1, least vulnerable) to 10.7% (Quartile 4, most vulnerable); after adjustment for severity, comorbidity, race, rurality, and time, the Quartile 4 odds ratio was 1.24 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.33; c statistic 0.717), robust across four alternative SVI constructions (1.21 to 1.28) and to state level clustering, with an E value of 1.79. Anticoagulation practice transformed, with direct oral anticoagulant use rising from 17.7% to 74.3% and warfarin falling from 60.1% to 4.1%.ConclusionsAcross twelve years, the ICU burden of acute PE grew substantially, in parallel with the adoption of catheter based reperfusion and without growth in the share of lowest risk admissions, and greater socioeconomic vulnerability was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

articles.title: Association of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Arterial Coupling With Short-Term Prognosis in Patients With Sepsis: A Bedside Echocardiography-Based Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the prognostic value of tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion/pulmonary artery systolic pressure (TAPSE/PASP), a noninvasive marker of right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling, for 28-day and 90-day mortality in sepsis.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included adults with sepsis who underwent bedside echocardiography within 24 h of ICU admission. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression assessed associations between TAPSE/PASP and mortality. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap internal validation, and decision curve analysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed 90-day survival.ResultsAmong 360 patients, 107 (29.7%) died within 28 days. TAPSE/PASP was lower in non-survivors than survivors [0.40 (0.33-0.50) versus 0.60 (0.49-0.77) mm/mm Hg; P < 0.001]. After adjustment for age, sex, SOFA score, lactate, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, and NT-proBNP, each 0.1 mm/mm Hg increase in TAPSE/PASP was associated with lower odds of 28-day mortality (OR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.61-0.93; P = 0.012). TAPSE/PASP alone had an AUC of 0.799 (95% CI: 0.751-0.848), with an optimal cutoff of approximately 0.466 mm/mm Hg. Adding TAPSE/PASP to the clinical model increased the AUC from 0.846 to 0.854 (DeLong P = 0.234); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.842. Higher TAPSE/PASP was associated with a lower 90-day mortality hazard (HR = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.71-0.96; P = 0.013). Patients with TAPSE/PASP ≤0.40 mm/mm Hg had lower 90-day survival.ConclusionLower TAPSE/PASP was associated with higher 28-day mortality and a higher 90-day mortality hazard in sepsis. Its addition did not significantly improve clinical-model discrimination. Prospective multicenter validation is needed.

articles.title: Screening Whole-Body MRI in Cancer Predisposition Syndromes: Imaging Strategies, Diagnostic Yield, and Clinical Impact.
articles.abstract: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI) has become an important surveillance tool in selected cancer predisposition syndromes because it enables multiorgan evaluation without ionizing radiation. This review summarizes current technical considerations for screening WB-MRI, including syndrome-adapted anatomic coverage, scanner platform selection, core sequences, diffusion-weighted imaging, contrast use, pediatric workflow, interpretation, postprocessing, and the selective role of hybrid PET/MRI. The strongest evidence supports WB-MRI for Li-Fraumeni syndrome, in which surveillance beginning in infancy can detect presymptomatic malignancies and improve outcomes. WB-MRI also has an established role in constitutional mismatch repair deficiency and an evolving genotype-specific role in hereditary paraganglioma-pheochromocytoma syndromes. In hereditary retinoblastoma and other emerging syndromes, its use remains more selective. Across syndromes, WB-MRI performs best for bone, marrow, and soft-tissue lesions but is less effective for some mucosal, glandular, and very small pulmonary lesions. False-positive and incidental findings remain important limitations and may lead to additional imaging or biopsy. Overall, WB-MRI is most valuable within a risk-adapted, multidisciplinary surveillance strategy and, when indicated, combined with targeted organ-specific imaging.

articles.title: Navigating heart failure self-care in a resource-limited setting through indigenous knowledge, cultural practice and family support.
Atypical Lymphoid Proliferation: A Challenging Diagnostic Category With Borderline Characteristics and Variable Biological Potential.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Atypical lymphoid proliferation (AtLP) is a descriptive hematopathology diagnosis used when a lymphoid infiltrate shows abnormalities beyond ordinary reactive hyperplasia but lacks sufficient morphologic, immunophenotypic, molecular, or clinical evidence to define a lymphoma. This category matters clinically because many benign, borderline, immune-dysregulated, infectious, therapy-associated, and early neoplastic processes converge at the reactive-malignant interface.

OBJECTIVE: This review summarizes contemporary concepts in AtLP, emphasizing diagnostic boundaries, lymphoma mimics, ancillary testing, reporting language, and risk-based follow-up within the Fifth edition of the World Health Organization Classification of Haematolymphoid Tumours (WHO-HAEM5) and International Consensus Classification (ICC) framework.

DESIGN: We prepared a narrative synthesis from open-access hematology and hematopathology literature, WHO-HAEM5 and ICC-related publications, NCBI Bookshelf resources, American Society of Hematology educational material, and recent reports on AtLP and several Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated, immunodeficiency-associated, mucosal, autoimmune, and therapy-associated lymphoid proliferations.

RESULTS: AtLP is not a single disease entity but a provisional diagnostic category that requires integration of tissue architecture, cytology, lineage, immunophenotype, clonality, viral studies, genetics, clinical distribution, host immune status, medication exposure, and longitudinal behavior. Major mimics include reactive follicular hyperplasia, infectious mononucleosis, EBV-positive lymphoproliferative disorders, marginal zone lymphoma mimics, classic Hodgkin lymphoma mimics, T follicular helper (TFH)-derived lymphomas, Castleman disease, immunoglobulin G4 (IgG4)-related lymphadenopathy, Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, Rosai-Dorfman disease, sarcoidosis, dermatopathic lymphadenopathy, posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorders, and drug-related lymphadenopathies.

CONCLUSIONS: We suggest using AtLP sparingly and transparently. It is most useful when it conveys residual diagnostic uncertainty, defines the main differential diagnosis, documents limitations of sampling or ancillary studies, and recommends appropriate correlation, surveillance, expert review, or repeat biopsy rather than premature reassurance or overtreatment.

articles.title: Hyaluronic acid and other adherence compounds in embryo transfer media for assisted reproductive technologies.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Successful implantation of the embryo into the endometrial lining is a key step in in vitro fertilisation (IVF). Adherence compounds such as hyaluronic acid (HA) and fibrin sealant are sometimes added to the embryo transfer medium to increase the likelihood of embryo implantation and pregnancy. This is the third update of a Cochrane review first published in the Cochrane Library in 2010.

OBJECTIVES: To determine whether adding adherence compounds to embryo transfer media improves pregnancy outcomes, including live birth, and decreases miscarriage, in women undergoing assisted reproduction.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Trials Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO on 20 May 2025 for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that examined the effects of adherence compounds in embryo transfer media on pregnancy outcomes. We communicated with experts in the field and checked reference lists of relevant studies.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included only truly randomised trials that compared embryo transfer media containing functional concentrations of adherence compounds (high HA: 0.5 mg/mL) to media with no or low HA (≤ 0.25 mg/mL). We applied the Trustworthiness in RAndomised Controlled Trials (TRACT) checklist to all included studies from the 2020 review and this update. We included only studies free of serious trustworthiness concerns.

OUTCOMES: Critical review outcomes were live birth and miscarriage. Important outcomes were clinical pregnancy, multiple pregnancies, ectopic outcomes, congenital anomalies, and adverse events.

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane risk of bias tool (RoB 1).

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible and calculated pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a fixed-effect model. We performed statistical analysis according to Cochrane guidelines. We corresponded with study authors as required. We summarised results narratively where necessary. We assessed evidence certainty using GRADE.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of 13 studies with 4931 participants. Twelve studies with 4720 participants compared high-concentration HA to no or low-concentration HA. One study with 211 participants compared fibrin sealant to no fibrin sealant.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: High-concentration versus low-concentration or no hyaluronic acid Low-certainty evidence suggests that adding high HA to transfer media may slightly increase the chance of live birth (RR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.19; I² = 41%; 7 studies, 3775 participants). If the chances of live birth with no or low HA are 35%, adding high-concentration HA may increase live birth from between 35% to 42%. However, the observed effect was not robust to any of the planned sensitivity analyses, suggesting that high-concentration HA may not have meaningful effects on live birth. Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that adding high HA to transfer media probably makes little to no difference to the chance of miscarriage (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.21; I² = 0%; 8 studies, 3205 participants). This suggests that if the risk of miscarriage with no or low HA is 8%, then adding high HA to transfer media the risk of miscarriage is between 6% and 9%. Low-certainty evidence suggests that adding high HA to transfer media may slightly increase the chance of clinical pregnancy (RR 1.12, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.19; I² = 18%; 11 studies, 3989 participants). If the baseline chance of pregnancy with no or low HA is 42%, the addition of high HA to transfer media may increase clinical pregnancy from 43% to 50%. Low-certainty evidence suggests that adding high HA to transfer media may increase multiple pregnancies (RR 1.51, 95% CI 1.29 to 1.78; I² = 25%; 8 studies, 3621 participants). If the baseline chance of multiple pregnancies with no or low HA is 10%, the addition of HA may increase the chance from 13% to 18%. However, the effect observed may be attributed to a policy of transferring multiple embryos per treatment cycle. No studies reported on total adverse events. Many studies were associated with unclear or high risk of bias, particularly for selective reporting and other bias. Consequently, we downgraded the certainty of the evidence once or twice for risk of bias. We also downgraded the outcome 'multiple pregnancy' for indirectness because the included studies used multiple embryo transfer policies. RCTs on other potential adherence compounds are currently limited.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Low-certainty evidence shows that the addition of high HA to embryo transfer media may slightly increase live birth. However, the observed effect was not robust to any of the planned sensitivity analyses, suggesting that high HA may not have meaningful effects on live birth. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that adding high HA to embryo transfer media probably results in little to no difference in miscarriage. Low-certainty evidence shows that the addition of high HA to embryo transfer media may slightly increase clinical pregnancy. If the chance of clinical pregnancy with no or low HA is 42%, the addition of high HA may increase clinical pregnancy from 43% to 50%. This observed effect held under both a random-effects and fixed-effect model. Low-certainty evidence also shows that the addition of high HA to embryo transfer media may increase multiple pregnancies. If the chance of multiple pregnancies with no or low HA is 10%, the addition of high HA may increase multiple pregnancies from 13% to 18%. Although this is likely explained by increased implantation under multiple embryo transfer policies, rather than a direct effect of HA on monozygotic twinning. Further reporting and research on the impacts of high HA in transfer media for single embryo transfer protocols, and on adverse events and congenital abnormalities, is needed. RCTs on other potential adherence compounds are currently limited.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: 2020 version: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007421.pub4 2014 version: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007421.pub3 2010 version: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007421.pub2 Protocol: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007421.

articles.title: Exploring the proteomic landscape of enamel beyond molar incisor hypomineralization opacities: An LC-MS study.
articles.abstract: It remains unclear if proteomic alterations in molar incisor hypomineralization (MIH) extend beyond opaque enamel (OE). This study compared the protein composition of demarcated MIH opacities and adjacent, unaffected enamel. Opaque MIH enamel (OE), enamel beyond the opacity borders (BOE), and healthy enamel (HE) were analyzed by LC-MS. Teeth from children with MIH (n = 7) and controls (n = 4) were microdissected by region and processed individually. Differential abundance was assessed using paired statistics for OE versus BOE and unpaired tests for OE versus HE. OE differed from BOE (166 proteins) and HE (103 proteins), whereas no proteins differed between BOE and HE. Of the proteins differing in OE, 82 were shared between the OE-BOE and OE-HE comparisons (79.6% of OE-HE; 49.4% of OE-BOE). OE showed higher protein abundance, enriched in plasma and immune-related proteins, apolipoproteins, serpins, and collagen chains, with relative reductions in several keratins. Recurrently altered proteins included serum albumin, antithrombin-III, alpha-1-antitrypsin, collagen alpha-1-chain, collagen alpha-2(I)-chain, and ameloblastin. Principal component analysis separated OE from BOE and HE, whereas BOE largely overlapped with HE. MIH-associated proteomic alterations on the occlusal surface appear confined to OE, whereas unaffected enamel beyond opacities is proteomically similar to HE.

articles.title: Benefit of carotid ultrasound in patients with inflammatory joint diseases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Patients with inflammatory joint diseases (IJDs) are at increased risk of cardiovascular (CV) disease. The aim of this study was to explore the relationship between CV risk factors and the presence of carotid plaques (CPs) across age groups, to identify IJD patients who would benefit from carotid ultrasound as part of CV risk assessments.

METHOD: The study comprised IJD patients aged 25-85 years who were referred for CV risk evaluations between 2008 and 2024. To focus on CV reclassification potential, patients with known prior CV disease or those otherwise classified as very high CV risk were excluded. CV risk factors included smoking, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and family history of premature CV disease. Patients were categorized by the number of risk factors (0 to ≥ 4) and age groups.

RESULTS: The analysis included 1397 IJD patients not classified as very high CV risk. Dyslipidaemia, smoking, obesity, and hypertension were the most prevalent CV risk factors, affecting 40% or more of the cohort. The prevalence of CP increased with age, with two-thirds of older adults exhibiting CP, regardless of CV risk factors. In younger and middle-aged adults, CP prevalence rose with the number of CV risk factors.

CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate a substantial burden of subclinical carotid plaque in IJD. They support targeted carotid ultrasound for CV risk reclassification in older patients and in younger or middle-aged individuals with conventional risk factors.

articles.title: Infectious Keratitis Associated with Endophthalmitis: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review examines commonly reported exposures, etiologies, and outcomes of patients with infectious keratitis (IK) progressing to endophthalmitis.

METHODS: Six databases were searched for studies from inception until 11/16/25. Randomized controlled trials, cohort and case control studies, cross-sectional studies, and case series published in English were included. Study selection and data extraction were conducted independently by two reviewers; study quality was assessed using JBI Critical Appraisal tools. Data from included studies were synthesized descriptively.

RESULTS: Of 7,172 studies identified, 93 met inclusion criteria. Most studies met more than 70% of JBI appraisal criteria for each study type. The most common reported exposures for IK-associated endophthalmitis included prior ocular surgery (29.6%), steroid use (13.4%), and diabetes mellitus (8.6%). The most frequently identified pathogens were Pseudomonas (19%), Fusarium (12%), and Staphylococcus (10%). Among patients with reported visual outcomes, 69.3% had final visual acuity <20/400 and 36% of patients underwent enucleation or evisceration.

CONCLUSION: Endophthalmitis secondary to IK is associated with poor visual outcomes.

articles.title: Brucellosis Presenting as Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis in Children: Two Cases and a Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Brucellosis, the most common zoonotic infection worldwide, can involve almost any organ system. Cutaneous manifestations are uncommon (~6%), and vasculitic presentations are rare. Two pediatric cases of Brucella-associated leukocytoclastic vasculitis presenting as acute hemorrhagic edema of infancy and IgA vasculitis are reported, together with a review of the pediatric literature highlighting the clinical spectrum and possible pathogenetic mechanisms of this rare association.

articles.title: Association Between Fluid Balance Trajectory and Mortality in Patients with Sepsis-Induced Myocardial Injury: A MIMIC-IV Database Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with sepsis-induced myocardial injury (SIMI) frequently face complex challenges in fluid management. The fluid balance trajectory, a key indicator of dynamic fluid changes, remains unclear in its association with the prognosis of SIMI patients.

OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between fluid balance trajectory and mortality in patients with SIMI.

METHODS: Data were sourced from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC) database. A group-based multi-trajectory model (GBMT) was applied to identify subgroups of SIMI patients with distinct fluid balance trajectories. The association between different fluid balance trajectories and 7-day mortality was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression models. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to verify the robustness of the results. The incremental prognostic value of fluid balance trajectory for mortality prediction was also investigated.

RESULTS: A total of 988 patients with SIMI were enrolled, and four distinct trajectories were identified via GBMT. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed significant differences in 7-day survival probabilities across fluid balance trajectory groups (P-Log-rank=0.038). Cox regression analysis demonstrated that, in the fully adjusted model, patients in Class 4 (stable low positive balance) (hazard ratio=3.279, 95% confidence interval: 1.668-6.448, P<0.001) had a higher risk of 7-day mortality compared with Class 1 (rapid decline), while no significant differences were observed in Class 2 (ultra-rapid decline) (P=0.052) and Class 3 (gradual decline) (P=0.073). No subgroups with interaction effects were identified (P interaction>0.05). Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Adding fluid balance trajectory to baseline Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score improved discrimination for 7-day mortality (increase in the area under the curve=0.045; DeLong P=0.017).

CONCLUSION: Persistent low-level positive fluid balance is associated with increased mortality in patients with SIMI. The study may provide a scientific reference for mortality risk stratification and clinical fluid management in SIMI patients.

articles.title: Neurocognitive Performance in Middle-Aged Adults With and Without HIV Infection in Côte d'Ivoire (VIRAGE).
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A decline in neurocognitive and physical functioning is common among people living with HIV (PLWH) as they age. In many resource-limited countries, screening for neurocognitive impairment (NCI) remains challenging and available data are scarce. This study aimed to assess the cognitive performance of PLWH followed in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire, and to examine the association between NCI and HIV factors, functional abilities and physical capacities.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 298 PLWH and 199 HIV-uninfected individuals (median age 51 years, female: 69%) participated in neurocognitive tests assessing verbal fluency, memory, processing speed, attention, executive functioning and motor speed. Tests for physical performance included the 6-min walk test, the five-times sit-to-stand test and grip strength. HIV factors included nadir CD4, antiretroviral duration, treatment failure and toxicity. Functional ability was assessed through the Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) and the WHODAS-2 questionnaires. The global neurocognitive score (GNS) and global deficit score (GDS), summarizing participants' overall functioning, were computed after transformation of the neurocognitive raw scores into regression-based z-scores relative to the performance of the HIV-negative group. These global scores were used to assess the associations between NCI and the HIV factors, physical capacities and functional abilities.

RESULTS: In adjusted analysis, PLWH achieved poorer scores than controls on the forward digit span test (padj = 0.0008), colour trail tests 1 (padj = 0.04) and 2 (padj = 0.001) and pegboard test (padj = 0.00002). The median GNS was -0.12 (Interquartile Range [IQR]: -0.51 to 0.19). The median GDS was 0.17 (IQR: 0-0.43), which translates into one in five PLWH having a GDS suggesting NCI. GNS and GDS were not associated with HIV-related factors or functional ability. Grip strength was consistently associated with the global scores (p < 0.05) but not the other physical tests.

CONCLUSION: Grip strength warrants further investigation as a potential screening tool for NCI among these middle-aged PLWH.

articles.title: Shared decision-making and withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment in an open paediatric cardiac ICU: a case report.
articles.abstract: A one-year-old boy with pulmonary atresia and intact ventricular septum sustained devastating hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury after in-hospital cardiac arrest. Brain death was not formally determined, and he remained legally alive. After staged shared decision-making and ethics committee review, mechanical ventilation was withdrawn with family-centred preparation, illustrating that such discussions were feasible in an open paediatric cardiac ICU.

articles.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of 68Ga-Labeled BCMA-Targeting Nanobodies for PET Imaging of Multiple Myeloma.
articles.abstract: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a critical biomarker for multiple myeloma (MM). In this study, three 68Ga-labeled BCMA-targeting nanobodies (C02, C06, and C07) were developed and evaluated. Protein-based binding assays showed apparent nanomolar affinities, with dissociation constants of 58 ± 7 nM, 87 ± 9 nM, and 33 ± 3 nM, respectively. Their BCMA specificities were confirmed by the high BCMA-positive H929 cell uptakes (6.08 ± 0.73%, 4.59 ± 0.45%, and 4.05 ± 0.29% at 0.5 h, respectively) and significant inhibition (82%, 88%, and 66%, respectively) by the unlabeled nanobodies. [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-BCMA-C07 exhibited the most favorable profile in microPET/CT imaging, with tumor uptake of 3.26 ± 0.19% ID/g, renal uptake of 13.61 ± 1.90% ID/g, and tumor-to-muscle ratio of 7.46 ± 2.82 at 0.5 h post-injection (p.i.). These findings support [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-BCMA-C07 as a promising BCMA-targeted PET radiotracer with potential for further clinical translation.

articles.title: Narrow-Spectrum Oxadiazole Antibacterials that Target Cell-Wall Septation in Clostridioides difficile and Spare the Gut Microbiota.
articles.abstract: Recurrence of infection is a challenge in treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI), observed in 25% of patients. The first-line antibiotics disturb the gut microbiota, exacerbating the already disrupted commensal gut homeostasis and allow for C. difficile colonization. Narrow-spectrum antibiotics are critical for selective targeting of C. difficile while preserving beneficial gut flora, thereby mitigating recurrence. Our study investigates a novel class of highly selective, nitroimidazole-based oxadiazole antibacterials. We detail the chemical basis for their exceptional selectivity against C. difficile over commensal bacteria and elucidate their mechanism of action. Oxadiazole 2 inhibits penicillin-binding proteins 1 and 3 involved in septal peptidoglycan biosynthesis during vegetative cell division. We further demonstrate by whole-genome sequencing that treatment of mice with oxadiazole 2 does not disrupt the gut microflora and confers an impediment to colonization by C. difficile. This work is foundational for development of a new generation of narrow-spectrum therapeutics to combat CDI.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and Preclinical Evaluation of [18F]FPON, a First-In-Class PET Tracer Targeting Proliferating Cell Nuclear Antigen for Glioblastoma Imaging.
articles.abstract: Proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) is a central regulator of glioma stem cell maintenance and therapy resistance, yet no noninvasive method exists to visualize its expression in vivo. We developed [18F]FPON, a first-in-class small-molecule PET tracer targeting PCNA, derived from the clinical inhibitor AOH1996. FPON binds recombinant PCNA with a Kd of 900.8 ± 131.2 nM, comparable to AOH1996. [18F]FPON is synthesized in one step with a decay-corrected radiochemical yield of 11.43 ± 4.03% (n = 6) and >95% radiochemical purity, readily crosses the blood-brain barrier, and remains >87% intact in brain at 60 min post-injection. In orthotopic U87 glioma xenografts, [18F]FPON exhibits specific tumor uptake (SUVr = 2.58 ± 0.38 vs contralateral brain), which is significantly reduced by AOH1996 (SUVr = 1.62 ± 0.24, p < 0.01). These results establish [18F]FPON as a promising PET tracer for noninvasive imaging of PCNA and support its potential use as a companion diagnostic for PCNA-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Selective Fluorination Affords Hydrophilic Synthetic Glycoconjugates Stable In Vivo.
articles.abstract: Therapeutics based on native carbohydrates such as lactose often suffer from short circulation half-lives in vivo due to their rapid clearance from the bloodstream by hepatic C-type lectin receptors, which limits their therapeutic efficacy. A common counter-strategy is to develop structurally distinct glycomimetics by introducing aromatic substituents. However, these modifications often increase hydrophobicity and, in multivalent conjugates, may promote nanoaggregation in the bloodstream, adversely affecting their pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties. In our conceptually distinct approach, strategic fluorine substitution in the native carbohydrate scaffold modulates pharmacokinetics while preserving high water solubility and bioavailability. The prepared highly water-soluble multivalent glycopolymers fluorinated at the 3'- and 4'-positions based on a biocompatible polyoxazoline scaffold exhibited circulation times comparable to the unmodified macromolecular carrier and substantially longer than native lactose-terminated analogues. We establish site-selective carbohydrate fluorination as a broadly applicable platform to improve the pharmacokinetic properties of soluble glycan-based therapeutics, useful for targeting biomedically important lectins, such as β-galactoside-binding galectins.

articles.title: Discovery of XT1061, a HBV Capsid Assembly Modulator, as a Promising Therapeutic Candidate for Clinical Treatment of HBV Infection.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) persists as a major unresolved infectious disease. Patients typically require lifelong administration of nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) or interferons but seldom achieve functional cure. Recent studies indicate that HBV core assembly modulators (CAMs), when combined with NAs and interferons, can more effectively reduce HBsAg in plasma, thereby facilitating functional cure. In this research, we discovered compound 39 (designated XT1061) through structural optimization of previously reported GLP-26, which exhibited potent anti-HBV activity in vitro (EC50 = 1.0 ± 0.1 nM). In the murine AAV/HBV model, XT1061 induced rapid reduction of HBV DNA and sustained viral DNA clearance throughout treatment. Notably, Combination therapy of XT1061 with pradefovir mesylate (PDV) exhibited significantly enhanced efficacy compared with monotherapy. Further preclinical evaluation and Phase I clinical trials (NCT06280534) confirmed that XT1061 possesses favorable drug-like properties and low safety risks. Collectively, XT1061 represents a promising anti-HBV therapeutic candidate, providing a viable strategy for the clinical management of chronic HBV infection.

articles.title: 18F-Labeled 7-Azaindole-Based Radioligands for Imaging Colony-Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor in Glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: A series of 7-azaindole-based compounds were designed and synthesized as novel colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) ligands. Four potent ligands (IC50 < 40 nM) were radiolabeled with fluorine-18 via the 5-fluoroethoxy substituent on the 7-azaindole ring and evaluated comprehensively in rodents and U87MG glioma models. Among them, [18F]PLX6 (IC50 = 12.3 nM) showed modest brain uptake and rapid clearance in rats. Micro-PET/CT imaging resulted in clear visualization of both subcutaneous and intracranial orthotopic U87MG gliomas. Treatment with PLX3397 or PLX5622 significantly reduced tumor uptake, indicating specific binding of [18F]PLX6 to CSF1R. Ex vivo autoradiography at 30 min postinjection (p.i.) confirmed high tumor-to-brain ratio (10.14 ± 1.52) and specific binding of [18F]PLX6 to CSF1R. Metabolic analysis showed that intact [18F]PLX6 was the predominant radioactive species in tumors at 30 min p.i. These results support further evaluation of [18F]PLX6 as a promising PET imaging agent for noninvasive visualization of CSF1R expression in glioblastoma.

articles.title: Discrete prognostic Implications of the prognostic nutritional index in surgically treated locally advanced tongue cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced tongue cancer is associated with malnutrition. This study evaluated the prognostic significance of the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and sarcopenia in surgically treated locally advanced tongue cancer.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To investigate associations among PNI, NLR, sarcopenia, and survival outcomes.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Patients with pathologic T3-T4 tongue squamous cell carcinoma who underwent curative surgery between 2010 and 2022 were retrospectively reviewed. Preoperative PNI and NLR were calculated from laboratory data. Sarcopenia was assessed using skeletal muscle index at the C3 level on CT or PET/CT. Overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 152 patients, low PNI (HR, 1.789; 95% CI, 1.417-2.692; p = 0.010) and high NLR (HR, 1.558; 95% CI, 1.067-2.010; p = 0.047) were associated with worse OS. Sarcopenia was not significantly associated with OS or DFS. Among patients with sarcopenia, low PNI (HR, 2.918; 95% CI, 1.194-7.134; p = 0.019) and high NLR (HR, 2.107; 95% CI, 1.094-4.470; p = 0.047) were associated with poorer OS. NLR negatively correlated with survival duration (ρ = -0.209; p = 0.011).

CONCLUSION AND SIGNIFICANCE: PNI and NLR may be useful prognostic biomarkers, particularly in sarcopenic patients.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes for cardiovascular disease prevention in mixed adult populations: an overview of reviews.
articles.abstract: Potassium-containing low-sodium salt substitutes (LSSS) replace part of sodium chloride with potassium chloride to lower sodium intake and increase potassium intake. Yet, the review literature is overlapping and methodologically heterogeneous. This overview of reviews assessed the efficacy, safety, and evidence quality of potassium-containing LSSS for blood pressure, cardiovascular outcomes, and adverse events. Following a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420261294404), we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Global Health (EBSCO) and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception to 6 March 2026. Eleven reviews met eligibility. Methodological confidence (AMSTAR 2) was high in one, moderate in three, low in five, and critically low in two, and primary-study overlap was very high. With LSSS, 24-h urinary sodium was lower by 9.41-35.82 mmol/d and 24-h urinary potassium was higher by 7.19-17.22 mmol/d. Review-level pooled estimates favoured potassium-containing LSSS for systolic (mean difference -4.00 to -8.87 mmHg) and diastolic blood pressure (-1.42 to -4.04 mmHg). Later reviews also reported lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.88-0.89), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.72-0.87), composite cardiovascular events, and selected stroke outcomes. However, these clinical-outcome estimates drew heavily on overlapping primary studies, particularly the Salt Substitute and Stroke Study, and are less independently replicated than the blood-pressure evidence. Serum potassium changed minimally (-0.02 to 0.18 mmol/L), with no clear excess of hyperkalaemia or serious adverse events reported. LSSS consistently lowered blood pressure; cardiovascular-event and mortality benefits remain promising but less certain. Trials outside East Asia with clearer formulation reporting and stronger safety data in higher-risk populations are needed.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rb1 attenuates adriamycin-induced cardiotoxic dysfunction in rats with changes in myocardial AMPK activity and CaV1.2 phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: This study examined whether ginsenoside Rb1 (Gs-Rb1) attenuated systolic dysfunction in adriamycin (Adr)-treated rats and whether this response was accompanied by changes in serum NT-proBNP, myocardial AMPK activity, and Ser1928-phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2. Fifty male Wistar rats were assigned to five groups: control, HF, Gs-Rb1, AraA, and AraA + Gs-Rb1. Echocardiography assessed cardiac function. Serum NT-proBNP was measured by ELISA, AMPK activity was determined enzymatically, and total LTCC and phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2 were assessed by western blotting. Correlation and multivariable regression analyses examined associations between myocardial readouts and systolic function. Compared with HF rats, Gs-Rb1-treated rats showed higher LVEF, stroke volume, and cardiac output, together with lower serum NT-proBNP. Gs-Rb1 also increased myocardial AMPK activity, Ser1928-phosphorylated LTCC/CaV1.2 abundance, and the pLTCC/tLTCC ratio, whereas total LTCC abundance did not differ among groups. AraA attenuated these changes. The pLTCC/tLTCC ratio was positively correlated with LVEF and myocardial AMPK activity and negatively correlated with serum NT-proBNP. In multivariable regression, AMPK activity and NT-proBNP remained independently associated with LVEF, whereas pLTCC/tLTCC did not. Overall, Gs-Rb1 attenuated Adr-induced cardiac dysfunction in rats. Functional improvement was accompanied by lower serum NT-proBNP, higher myocardial AMPK activity and increased LTCC/CaV1.2 phosphorylation, supporting pharmacological involvement of AMPK-associated signaling in this model.

articles.title: Seizure burden and continuity of care among children with epilepsy during Sudan's armed conflict: A multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We examined how Sudan's armed conflict changed seizure burden and continuity of care for children on established treatment, and whether the disruptions families described were patterned by conflict exposure or household economic position.

METHODS: Between 26 April and 23 September 2024, clinicians interviewed caregivers of children aged 2-18 years whose epilepsy had been diagnosed before April 2023, recruited from an online pediatric neurology tele-clinic and two eastern teaching hospitals. Care and seizure burden before the war were compared with those at interview using exact McNemar tests. Outcomes were compared between conflict-affected and relatively spared states using prevalence ratios, with Benjamini-Hochberg control of the false discovery rate, and four prespecified multivariable models.

RESULTS: Of 176 interviews, 153 children were analyzed (60.1% male). Follow-up had become irregular for 87 of 152 (57.2%), treatment had been interrupted at least once for 80 of 153 (52.3%), and 66 (43.1%) had lost contact with their physician. The proportion having two or more seizures a month rose from 25.5% to 32.9% (18 deteriorated, 7 improved; exact McNemar p = 0.04). Fifty-six children (36.6%) had a seizure lasting more than 5 min; 34 (60.7%) reached an emergency department immediately and 30 (53.6%) obtained rescue medication. Prolonged seizures (52.1% vs. 28.8%; adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 1.74, 95% CI 1.16-2.63) and irregular follow-up (72.3% vs. 51.0%; aPR 1.45, 95% CI 1.11-1.88) were more frequent in conflict-affected states, but neither unadjusted difference remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons (smallest q = 0.12). Interruption of therapy was determined mainly by household income (lowest two bands, aOR 2.98, 95% CI 1.47-6.04) rather than geography.

SIGNIFICANCE: Epilepsy care in Sudan has been disrupted along the whole pathway and in every region studied. Cost, not distance from the front line, was the dominant barrier to uninterrupted treatment.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Sudan has been at war since April 2023, and we interviewed the families of 153 children who already had epilepsy when the war began. More than half had missed their regular clinic visits, and more than half had run out of their seizure medicine at least once, most often because the family could not afford it. Children living in the states where fighting was taking place were more likely to have long seizures and to miss follow-up, though these differences were not statistically conclusive. Making seizure medicines free would help these children more than any other single measure.

articles.title: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases 2024 single topic symposium proceedings part 1: State of the field.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract: Since the first North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (EGIDs) single-topic symposium (STS) in 2006, the field has advanced dramatically, culminating in the first Food and Drug Administration-approved therapy for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in 2022. The 2024 STS, EGID Xcelerating Care, Research and Innovation in an Evolving Landscape (EXCEL), convened experts to review state-of-the-art science, clinical practice, and emerging innovations in pediatric EGIDs. This report (Part 1-EoE) highlights progress in understanding EoE pathogenesis, evolving therapeutic paradigms, and advances in disease monitoring. Landmark discoveries have redefined EoE as a chronic, immune-mediated epithelial disorder driven by genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures, challenging the historical focus on eosinophils as primary effectors. Therapeutic updates include step-up dietary elimination strategies, optimized use of proton pump inhibitors and swallowed topical corticosteroids, and the integration of biologics such as dupilumab, now approved for children as young as 1 year. Ongoing research targeting type 2 cytokines, mast cells, and epithelial barrier dysfunction may further transform management across the lifespan. Innovations in disease assessment, including the Index of Severity for Eosinophilic Esophagitis, endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe, minimally invasive esophageal string and Cytosponge tests, and unsedated transnasal endoscopy, promise to enhance precision care while reducing procedural burden. The EXCEL symposium also launched the SPARK! (Supportive Platform for Advancing Research and Knowledge) module, fostering collaboration and mentorship among early-career investigators. Together, these advances mark a new era in EoE research, diagnosis, and treatment, emphasizing individualized, multidisciplinary, and lifespan-oriented care.

articles.title: Nutritional Management in Children and Adolescents with Diabetes.
articles.abstract: The International Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Diabetes (ISPAD) guidelines represent a rich repository that serves as the only comprehensive set of clinical recommendations for children, adolescents, and young adults living with diabetes worldwide. This chapter is an update of the 2022 ISPAD nutritional guidelines, focused on diabetes-specific nutrition education for children and adolescents living with early-stage Type 1 Diabetes, Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) and Type 2 Diabetes (T2D). New or substantially updated areas include nutritional recommendations for early-stage T1D, dietary interventions for automated insulin delivery systems, weight management in T1D, management of disordered eating in diabetes and dietary management of T2D.

articles.title: Alternate Healthy Eating Index and Risk of Overall and Cause-Specific Mortality among Cancer Survivors: Insights from the NHANES Database.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI) was initially developed to evaluate dietary patterns in relation to chronic diseases. Existing studies have established a link between higher AHEI scores and a lower risk of cancer in the general population. However, the association between AHEI and survival outcomes among cancer patients requires further investigation.

METHODS: This study included 3,483 U.S. adult cancer survivors with complete dietary data,from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2003-2018. A modified AHEI (0-100 points) was calculated via the 'dietaryindex' R package. Restricted cubic spline and Kaplan-Meier plots were used to investigate the dose-response relationships and survival probabilities. Weighted multivariable Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were applied to evaluate the associations between AHEI and mortality risk.

RESULTS: 1,061 deaths (21.8% weighted percentage) occurred over a median surveillance period of 86.50 months, including 230 cardiovascular and 338 cancer deaths. A higher AHEI was correlated with a lower risk of overall mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]: 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98; p=0.04). However, no significant correlation was observed for cardiovascular or cancer-specific mortality after full adjustment. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested potential variations in the association by age, smoking status, and diabetes.

CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to the AHEI was modestly associated with lower overall mortality among U.S. adult cancer survivors, but not with cause-specific mortality.

articles.title: Eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases 2024 single topic symposium proceedings part 2: State of the field.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract: While advances in the management of eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) have transformed clinical practice, eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases beyond the esophagus (non-EoE EGIDs, including eosinophilic gastritis [EoG], enteritis [EoN], and colitis [EoC]) remain incompletely defined and understudied. The 2024 North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) EGID single-topic symposium (STS), EGID Xcelerating Care, Research and Innovation in an Evolving Landscape (EXCEL), Part 2-non-EoE EGIDs, highlighted emerging efforts to standardize nomenclature, diagnostic thresholds, and treatment strategies for this heterogeneous group of disorders. Histopathologic consensus criteria now distinguish disease by gastrointestinal (GI) segment, underscoring the need for site-specific biopsy sampling and recognition of additional features such as eosinophilic cryptitis, glandulitis, and submucosal involvement. Transcriptomic analyses reveal distinct molecular signatures among EoG, EoN, and EoC, suggesting variable type 2 inflammatory and non-type 2 mechanisms across the GI tract. Systemic corticosteroids are effective but limited by toxicity; dietary interventions and topical corticosteroids show inconsistent benefit; and early biologic trials targeting interleukin-4 receptor α (IL-4Rα), interleukin-5 (IL-5), and Siglec-8 demonstrate histologic improvement with variable symptom response. Advances in artificial intelligence offer promise for automating histologic assessment and integrating clinical, endoscopic, and molecular data, while health equity, patient-reported outcomes, mental health support, multidisciplinary collaboration, and seamless transition to adult care emerge as central to lifelong disease management. Through initiatives such as SPARK! (Supportive Platform for Advancing Research and Knowledge), NASPGHAN aims to accelerate discovery and mentorship in non-EoE EGIDs, catalyzing progress comparable to that achieved in EoE over the past two decades.

articles.title: Neutrophil Extracellular Traps at the Intersection of Cancer and Sepsis: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Cancer and sepsis are two leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Advances in oncologic treatments have increased survival rates for a variety of cancers, but they have also increased the number of patients with severe immune dysfunction. Consequently, infections that might otherwise stay localized can quickly progress to sepsis. There is an additional connection between sepsis and cancer. Dysregulated inflammatory signaling, metabolic reprogramming, endothelial damage, and disruptions in coagulation pathways represent a complex, interconnected array of immunological processes involved in both conditions. The host must simultaneously manage infection and respond to tumor-driven immune modulation, contributing to a precarious immunological balance. Consequently, compared with non-oncologic populations, cancer patients who develop sepsis often exhibit severe immune dysfunction and greater vulnerability to secondary infections. The innate immune system is essential to this complex biological environment. Neutrophils are crucial early host defense effector cells that contribute to pathogen clearance through several mechanisms. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), which are extracellular networks of chromatin fibers decorated with antimicrobial proteins capable of capturing and neutralizing pathogens, have been identified as a crucial mediator connecting infection, inflammation, and thrombosis. Excessive or unchecked NET formation can have adverse effects. Growing evidence indicates that NETs play a role in immunothrombotic phenomena, organ dysfunction, and microvascular injury during sepsis. Additionally, NETs have been increasingly linked to tumor biology, where they may aid immune escape, stimulate tumor growth, and promote metastatic spread. Understanding the dual role of NETs at the nexus of infection and cancer is essential. This narrative review analyzes available data on neutrophils and NETs in cancer patients with sepsis, highlighting emerging mechanisms and potential therapeutic implications.

articles.title: "Submaximal" stenting - A strategy for rescue therapy in large vessel occlusion (LVO) acute ischemic stroke secondary to intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD): A single-center case series.
articles.journal: Interventional neuroradiology : journal of peritherapeutic neuroradiology, surgical procedures and related neurosciences
articles.abstract: BackgroundIntracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) is a leading cause of acute ischemic stroke (IS). When endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) fails due to underlying ICAD-related large vessel occlusion (LVO), rescue stenting becomes necessary. We describe and report outcomes for "submaximal" stenting-deliberate balloon-mounted stent deployment at subnominal pressures (typically 6-7 atmospheres)-to minimize vessel wall trauma during emergency revascularization.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated patients undergoing "submaximal" acute rescue stenting with Resolute OnyxTM and Onyx FrontierTM drug-eluting stents (DES) (Medtronic) from January 2020 to July 2025. Primary outcomes were technical success-patency without adjacent vessel occlusion-and procedural safety, defined as absence of intraprocedural vessel rupture. Secondary outcomes included in-stent thrombosis, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), and functional status (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS]) at discharge and follow-up.ResultsAmong 37 patients (median age 59.0 years [IQR 56.0-73.0]; 67.6% male; 78.4% Black) who underwent acute rescue stenting after failed thrombectomy, all had severe (70%-99%) stenosis. The most treated vessels were M1 MCA (37.8%), basilar artery (27.0%), and intracranial ICA (16.2%). All interventions achieved technical success with immediate postprocedural vessel patency. No intra-operative bleeding events occurred. sICH occurred in 8.1% and in-stent thrombosis in 16.2%. Median hospital stay was 10.0 days (IQR 6.0-14.0) and median clinical follow-up 156.0 days (approximately 5.2 months). Median discharge NIHSS was 11.0 (IQR 2.3-14.8) and mRS 4.0 (IQR 2.0-5.0).Conclusions"Submaximal" stenting-deliberate under-expansion at subnominal pressures-with Resolute Onyx™ and Onyx Frontier™ DES appears technically feasible and safe as an acute rescue strategy for patients with ICAD-LVO stroke refractory to EVT. This approach warrants further investigation in larger-scale studies.

articles.title: AB070597 Attenuates Renal Fibrosis and Reduces Circulating Indoxyl Sulfate in Adenine-Induced Renal Failure Mice.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterized by progressive renal fibrosis, to which uremic toxins such as indoxyl sulfate (IS) contribute. However, the mechanisms linking uremic toxin accumulation to coagulation-related and profibrotic signaling remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the effects of the amino acid and dipeptide complex AB070597 in an adenine-induced renal failure mouse model. AB070597 was administered orally twice daily for 6 weeks, beginning concurrently with adenine feeding. Renal injury was assessed using blood urea nitrogen, plasma creatinine, and cystatin C levels. Plasma and urinary IS concentrations, renal F3(tissue factor) mRNA expression, fibrin(ogen) immunoreactivity, TGF-β-Smad signaling, and fibrosis-related markers were evaluated. AB070597 administration was associated with lower plasma creatinine, cystatin C, and IS concentrations in adenine-fed mice. Urinary IS-to-creatinine ratios and renal expression of Cyp1a1 did not differ significantly between the RF and RF+AB groups. In contrast, AB070597 significantly reduced renal F3 mRNA expression and fibrin(ogen) immunoreactivity. AB070597 also decreased Smad2/3 phosphorylation and the expression of profibrotic genes, including Serpine1 and Ctgf. Histological analyses demonstrated reduced collagen IV-positive areas, accompanied by decreased Col4a1 expression and attenuation of renal fibrosis. These findings demonstrate that AB070597 attenuates the development of renal injury and fibrosis in adenine-induced renal failure. Its protective effects are associated with reduced renal F3 expression, fibrin(ogen) immunoreactivity, and TGF-β-Smad signaling, suggesting that modulation of coagulation-related and profibrotic pathway probably contribute to its effects.

articles.title: Responsiveness to Change and Minimal Clinically Important Difference of the AusTOMs-OT for Outpatients With Arthritis.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of occupational therapy. Revue canadienne d'ergotherapie
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo build evidence on the effectiveness of occupational therapy interventions for people with arthritis, client data must be collected using outcome measures that are responsive to measure change, with known minimal clinically important difference (MCID).PurposeTo review the responsiveness and MCID of a selection of Australian Therapy Outcome Measures for Occupational Therapy (AusTOMs-OT) scales, as a global measure to capture outcomes for people with arthritis.MethodInternal responsiveness was determined using the Effect Size II: standardized response means (SRMs) approach, and the MCIDs were calculated using the SRMs method and a distribution-based approach.ResultsThe responsiveness of the selected AusTOMs-OT scales was confirmed with a large (>0.8) effect. MCID was calculated at half a point, and 95% of clients achieved or exceeded this threshold.ConclusionFew comprehensive outcome measures exist for use with people who have arthritis that are responsive to change and have known MCID. Selected AusTOMs-OT scales may be used clinically to demonstrate statistically robust, clinically relevant change and in intervention effectiveness research.

articles.title: The Cardiac SERCA pump Improves Peripheral Glucose Transport Through a Protein Disulfide Isomerase-Dependent Pathway during Diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Calcium handling has emerged as an important regulator of metabolic function, yet the role of cardiac calcium cycling in systemic glucose homeostasis remains unclear. We hypothesized that cardiac-specific overexpression of the sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca⁲⁺-ATPase (SERCA) pump improves whole-body glucose regulation by restoring glucose transport in peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues under diabetic condition. Transgenic (TG) mice with cardiac-specific SERCA overexpression and wild-type (WT) mice were made type 1 diabetic (Dx). Glucose transporters (GLUT) trafficking was assessed using a biotinylated photolabeling assay. To explore potential cardiac-derived mediators, we performed quantitative proteomic analysis of cardiac tissue of WT and TG mice. Diabetic WT mice exhibited a significant reduction in cell-surface GLUT4 content in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, which was rescued in Dx TG mice (p<0.05). Using SignalP and TargetP tools, we further determined that 16 and 32 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) in ventricles and atria of TG mice (vs. WT), respectively, were potentially secreted. We further demonstrated a substantial increase in the expression of prolyl-4-hydroxylase beta polypeptide (P4Hb), also known as protein disulfide isomerase A1 (PDIA1), in the ventricle of healthy and diabetic TG mice (by 1822% and 1355%, p<0.001 and p=0.008, respectively). We further demonstrated an increased P4Hb level in the serum of diabetic TG mice (p=0.01). Furthermore, incubation with recombinant human P4Hb increased glucose uptake by 33% in vitro (p=0.03). These findings suggest that, under diabetic condition, cardiac SERCA overexpression partially restored glucose transport in peripheral tissues through cardiokines, such as PDIA1/P4Hb. Insights gained from this study could lead to the discovery of novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for diabetic patients.

articles.title: Referral for knee pain and gait training leads to multiple sclerosis diagnosis: a case report.
articles.journal: The Journal of manual & manipulative therapy
articles.abstract: Physical therapists frequently receive referrals to evaluate patients with suspected mechanical knee pain and associated gait dysfunction. However, atypical examination findings may indicate alternative or coexisting etiologies. This case report describes the physical therapist's clinical reasoning and management of a 28-year-old male referred for gait training and chronic left knee pain. While focused musculoskeletal examination findings correlated with the patient's knee pain, this diagnosis did not explain recurrent falls and gait abnormalities, including wide base of support, increased left hip flexion, and forceful foot contact. Neurological examination revealed abnormal upper motor neuron findings, prompting referral for neurological workup. Imaging revealed lesions in the brain and cervical and thoracic spine that were consistent with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. Neurology initiated disease-specific management, including pharmacological infusions and neurological physical therapy. Knee pain resolved after five physical therapy visits, whereas gait and balance deficits persisted and required neurological rehabilitation. The divergent course was consistent with two coexisting contributors rather than a single misattributed diagnosis. This case demonstrates that testing whether a confirmed mechanical diagnosis accounts for all findings reduces premature diagnostic closure, even when the examination provides a plausible mechanical explanation for part of the presentation.

articles.title: Comparison of arteriovenous fistula cannulation strategies based on current evidence: A systematic review of complication risks associated with the rope ladder, area, and buttonhole techniques.
articles.abstract: This study systematically evaluated differences in short- and long-term complication risks associated with different puncture techniques (rope‑ladder, area, and buttonhole methods) for arteriovenous fistulas in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database from inception to January 1, 2026. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment, followed by a meta‑analysis using Python software. A total of 21 randomized controlled trials involving 2169 patients were included. Regarding short‑term complications, no statistically significant differences in infection risk were observed between the rope‑ladder or area method and the buttonhole method; however, both the rope‑ladder and area methods were associated with a significantly higher risk of bleeding compared with the buttonhole method (both p < 0.01). For long‑term complications, both the rope‑ladder and area methods showed significantly increased risks of aneurysm formation and fistula thrombotic occlusion relative to the buttonhole method; the area method was also associated with a significantly higher risk of fistula stenosis. In terms of functional outcomes, the rope‑ladder method had a lower one‑time cannulation success rate than the buttonhole method at the patient level, whereas considerable heterogeneity was observed across studies regarding one‑time success rates at the puncture‑event level. Available evidence suggests that the buttonhole method may offer potential advantages in reducing bleeding, aneurysm, and fistula thrombotic occlusion, with no significant difference in infection risk compared with the other methods. Current evidence indicates that different arteriovenous fistula puncture techniques are associated with varying complication risks in maintenance hemodialysis patients. An individualized puncture strategy, guided by patient vascular characteristics, center expertise, and the limitations of existing evidence, along with standardized pre‑ and post‑puncture assessment and systematic nursing care, may help reduce the incidence of related complications.

articles.title: Clinical guideline highlights for the hospitalist: Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines for the Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock in Children 2026.
Myocardial Scar-Detected Cardiac Magnetic Resonance on Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The implantation of conduction system pacing (CSP), in particular left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), involves deep septal lead deployment 1.5 cm distal to the His bundle to achieve subendocardial capture of the left bundle branch; hence, myocardial scar is theoretically a critical determinant of both procedural success and subsequent CRT response. This review aimed to evaluate the impact of myocardial scar assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance late gadolinium enhancement (CMR-LGE) on LBBAP outcomes.

METHODS: Three electronic databases (Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect) were searched for eligible studies from database inception until June, 12 2026. When at least two studies reported comparable quantitative outcomes, random-effects meta-analysis was performed using RStudio.

RESULTS: Eight studies (n = 581 patients) met the eligibility criteria. Qualitatively, the presence of myocardial scar attenuates lead placement and electrical resynchronization, with smaller reductions in left ventricular activation and dyssynchrony, wider paced QRS duration, and more loss of conduction-system capture. Higher scar burden was associated with attenuated reverse remodeling (LVEF improvement, LVESV reduction, and LVEDD reduction). Higher scar burden was also associated with a higher risk of heart failure hospitalization, ventricular arrhythmia, and all-cause mortality. Quantitatively, CRT responders had lower baseline global LGE burden (MD -6.27%; 95% CI -10.84 to -1.70; p = 0.0072) and septal LGE burden (MD -7.94%; 95% CI -11.87 to -4.00; p < 0.0001) than non-responders.

CONCLUSION: Myocardial scar may determine LBBAP outcomes, with the septal scar emerging as the most consistent predictor of worse outcomes. This qualitative early analysis supports pre-procedural LGE-CMR in selected LBBAP patients.

articles.title: Epicardial adipose tissue induces endothelial dysfunction via Activin A-mediated endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and mitochondrial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) exhibit elevated risks of endothelial dysfunction, though the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. As a unique visceral adipose tissue, epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) may play a crucial role in regulating endothelial function and is significantly thickened in AF patients. However, the mechanism by which EAT influences endothelial dysfunction in AF patients has not been elucidated. In this study, we found that human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with EAT-conditioned medium exhibited significantly elevated endothelial injury markers and increased expression of Activin A. Suppressing Activin A expression using shRNA partially alleviated endothelial dysfunction. Transcriptome sequencing analysis revealed that, compared to HUVECs treated with subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT)-conditioned medium, differentially expressed genes in HUVECs treated with EAT-conditioned medium were mainly enriched in pathways related to endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and mitochondrial biogenesis and bioenergetics. Further investigation demonstrated that EAT-conditioned medium suppressed the expression of endothelial markers (VE-cadherin and CD31) in HUVECs while increasing the expression of mesenchymal markers (α-SMA and vimentin) and initiating the EndMT process by activating Smad2/3 binding to SNAIL. Additionally, the Seahorse assay showed that mitochondrial respiration was significantly inhibited in EAT-treated HUVECs, accompanied by impaired mitochondrial biogenesis pathways and upregulated oxidative stress. While suppressing Activin A expression using shRNA effectively ameliorated the detrimental effects of EAT on EndMT and mitochondrial function in HUVECs. Therefore, targeted inhibition of Activin A in endothelial cells may be a potential strategy for alleviating EAT-mediated endothelial dysfunction in AF patients.

articles.title: Lipid-lowering treatment following acute coronary syndrome: real-world LDL-cholesterol target attainment and implications of restricted formulary access.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following acute coronary syndrome (ACS), European guidelines recommend LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L and ≥50% reduction from baseline, with early treatment intensification when statin monotherapy is unlikely to achieve these targets.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate longitudinal lipid changes and LDL-C target attainment post-ACS and explore implications of restricted formulary access to ezetimibe within publicly funded healthcare.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre longitudinal observational cohort study included patients with ACS undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting and attending cardiac rehabilitation. Lipids were assessed at coronary intervention (T1), following atorvastatin 80 mg (T2), rosuvastatin monotherapy (T3), and 4-6 months after adding ezetimibe 10 mg (T4). Primary outcomes were LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L and ≥50% reduction from baseline. Longitudinal changes were evaluated using Friedman and prespecified consecutive stage Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment.

RESULTS: Among 90 patients, 80 (88.9%) were male, 64 (71.1%) presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and 76 (84.4%) underwent PCI. LDL-C decreased significantly (Friedman χ²(3) = 135.56; p < 0.001), with significant reductions between consecutive stages after adjustment. The T2-T3 reduction was substantially smaller than T3-T4. No patient achieved LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L at T2 or T3. At T4, 36.5% achieved this target, 54.9% with paired baseline measurements achieved ≥50% reduction, and 26.8% achieved both criteria. Total cholesterol changed significantly (p < 0.001), whereas HDL-C (p = 0.153) and triglycerides (p = 0.282) did not.

CONCLUSIONS: Sequential high-intensity statin monotherapy was insufficient to achieve LDL-C targets. The largest additional reduction followed ezetimibe addition, highlighting opportunities for earlier reassessment and guideline-directed treatment intensification. Restricted formulary access may influence treatment pathways, although causality cannot be established.

articles.title: Ketamine to treat depression and the wish to hasten death in advanced cancer patients: The KODIAC pilot study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate ketamine inpatients with advanced cancer, major depressive disorder (MDD) and wish to hasten death (WTHD).

METHODS: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NCT04471818) in patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Participants received standard antidepressant therapy and were randomized to ketamine or placebo. After 2 double-blind infusions, allocation was opened, and control patients could cross over to ketamine. The primary outcome was change in MDD according to the Mexican Brief Edinburgh Depression Scale (BEDS-Mx); WTHD was assessed with the Schedule of Attitudes Towards Hastened Death (SAHD-Mx).

RESULTS: A total of 19 participants (12 in the ketamine group, 7 in the placebo group) and 12 participants (8 in the ketamine group, 4 in the placebo group) were included in the intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) populations, respectively. Results showed a decrease in BEDS-Mx and SAHD-Mx scores among ITT patients treated with ketamine vs. placebo (from 13.6 to 4.6 vs. 13.3 to 11.7 [p=0.0018]; from 4.0 to 0.5 vs. 3.7 to 3.6 [p=0.0093] across visit 1-4) and in the PP population (13.9 at baseline to 4.4 by the fourth study visit vs. from 13.8 to 12.7 [p=0.0001]; 3.7 at baseline to 0.2 by the fourth study visit vs. from 3.0 to 4.2 by the final visit [p=0.00001]). There were no serious adverse events reported.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: Ketamine is a safe and effective rapid-onset intervention that improves depressive symptoms and decreases WTHD in advanced cancer.

articles.title: PCSK9 and PCSK9 inhibitors in pregnancy: what do we know?
articles.abstract: Some lipid changes during pregnancy are physiological. Specifically, normal pregnancy raises maternal cholesterol, triglyceride, LDL- and HDL-cholesterol (LDL-C and HDL-C, respectively) levels in order to allow the placenta to absorb these lipoproteins and promote fetal and maternal health. However, pre-existing and pregnancy-related dyslipidemia can be associated with clinical complications, thus worsening the mother's and fetus's health. Accordingly, pathologic dyslipidemia is linked to gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, preterm birth, large-for-gestational-age infants, hyperviscosity syndrome, and macrosomia. In addition, pregnancy-related dyslipidemia increases the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Therefore, optimizing maternal and fetal health requires effective management measures, including dietary adjustments and, in certain situations, pharmaceutical interventions. Pregnancy-associated dyslipidemia offers distinct treatment concerns due to its implications on mother and fetal health. Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) modulates LDL receptors on hepatocytes, making them less available for LDL particle removal from circulation. Several lines of research have consistently demonstrated that PCSK9 activity affects LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk; therefore, PCSK9 inhibitors have been developed and approved worldwide as an effective LDL-C-lowering therapy in different clinical settings. In significant clinical studies, monoclonal PCSK9 antibodies significantly reduced plasma LDL-C levels and cardiovascular event rates. However, the impact of these drugs in pregnancy has not been exactly demonstrated. This review discusses the role of PCSK9 and PCSK9 inhibitors in pregnancy-associated dyslipidemia.

articles.title: Sustained use of the integrated palliative care outcome scale in specialized palliative care 5 years after implementation: Findings from patient records and the experiences of staff and patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The Integrated Patient care Outcome Scale (IPOS) is validated for use in palliative care to assess patients' symptoms and care needs. Despite proven benefits, the implementation of systematic assessments in palliative care has been slow. The aim was to assess how IPOS use has been sustained in clinical practice 5 years after implementation, using data from patient records and experiences of staff and patients in specialized palliative care.

METHODS: In study both quantitative and qualitative approaches were used. In specialized palliative care, patient records (n = 100) were reviewed, staff (n = 49) and patients (n = 7) participated in semi-structured interviews. Median age among staff was 46 years, the majority were registered nurses; patients had a median age of 75 years. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze patient records and qualitative content analysis to analyze interviews.

RESULTS: According to patient records, IPOS was used in 37% of patients, of which 3% during the last week of life. The interviews showed that staff and patients experienced that IPOS ensures that the patient's voice is heard and symptoms are detected; it facilitates meaningful conversations with patients, which guide care planning. However, barriers were, lack of guidelines on IPOS use, difficulties in implementing IPOS, and how to use IPOS during end-of-life care.

SIGNIFICANCE OF RESULTS: The results highlight the potential benefits of using IPOS in everyday care for both patients and staff through ensuring that the patient's voice is heard, facilitating conversations, and supporting care planning. However, clear routines for its use are needed.

articles.title: Multisystemic aspects of Duchenne muscular dystrophy: The proteomics perspective.
articles.abstract: Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy are muscle wasting disorders that are caused by abnormalities in the DMD gene resulting in altered expression patterns of tissue-specific dystrophin protein isoforms. The X-linked disease is primarily characterized by contractile weakness of voluntary muscles, but also affects the heart, smooth muscles and the nervous systems. The pathobiochemical aspects of dystrophinopathy have been well documented regarding neuromuscular, neurological, cardio-respiratory and orthopaedic alterations, but not the effects of organ-organ communication. More recent analyses of dystrophic animal models have revealed additional body-wide changes in the immune response, endocrine system and energy metabolism in dystrophinopathy, and organ-specific effects in the kidneys, liver and spleen. In the field of neuromuscular disease, clinical proteomics is now established as a key technique for systematic biomarker discovery, mostly in association with easily accessible biological fluids. As a complementary approach, tissue proteomics has been employed to both identify novel disease markers and increase our pathophysiological understanding of cellular disease mechanisms. In analogy to the vast proteomic knowledge of muscle-related changes in Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy, this article attempts to fill the knowledge gap between the primary abnormality in the DMD gene and the underlying proteome-wide changes of non-neuromuscular aspects of dystrophinopathy. The main aim of this review is to summarize the complexity of multisystemic changes in muscular dystrophy. However, it is important to stress that most current proteomic datasets are limited to animal models, highlighting the need for independent replication and validation in human studies to establish their reproducibility and potential clinical relevance.

articles.title: Evaluating Antenatal Counselling Outcomes at 22-24 Weeks' Gestation After Lowered Resuscitation Thresholds for Neonates: Experience From a Victorian Tertiary Perinatal Centre Cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate trends in decision making and pregnancy outcomes following antenatal counselling of women at risk of preterm birth between 22 and 24 weeks' gestation at the Royal Women's Hospital, following the implementation of the 2020 Safer Care Victoria guideline which lowered the threshold to consider resuscitation from 23 to 22 weeks.

METHODS: In this retrospective audit, we reviewed 194 antenatal consultations conducted from January 2021 to December 2024.
