articles.title: Kidney Involvement in Familial Hypercholesterolemia: From Renovascular Disease to Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is an inherited lipid disorder characterized by sustained exposure to elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and markedly increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Although FH has traditionally been regarded primarily as a coronary and systemic vascular disease, renal involvement may represent an under-recognized component of its clinical spectrum. Patients with FH may exhibit an increased prevalence of renovascular disease, renal arteriosclerotic lesions, reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), albuminuria, and chronic kidney disease (CKD). These manifestations may reflect various but interconnected mechanisms, including macrovascular atherosclerosis, endothelial dysfunction, hypertension, altered lipoprotein metabolism, elevated lipoprotein(a), and cumulative vascular injury. Importantly, CKD in FH appears to identify a subgroup of patients with particularly high cardiovascular vulnerability, acting as a prognostic amplifier beyond traditional lipid parameters. A kidney-oriented assessment in FH should include evaluation of eGFR, albuminuria, blood pressure phenotype, lipoprotein(a), and clinical suspicion of renovascular disease. Renovascular imaging should not be performed indiscriminately, but may be considered in selected patients with early-onset or resistant hypertension, unexplained kidney function decline, asymmetric kidney size, recurrent pulmonary edema, or diffuse atherosclerotic disease. Therefore, in this review, we focused on kidney involvement in FH patients both as a target organ and as a cardiovascular risk enhancer in this lipid disorder, along with the current management guidelines for FH and CKD.

articles.title: When is a PVI "successful"? Characterising OCEAN/ALONE-AF Enrolment Criteria with Continuous Rhythm Monitoring.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The OCEAN/ALONE-AF trials demonstrated low stroke risk in patients deemed AF-free 12 months post-ablation using intermittent Holter monitoring. Whether these patients had true AF freedom or had undetected AF remains unknown. We characterised the rhythm phenotype selected by this enrolment strategy.

METHODS: SINGLE-SHOT CHAMPION and COMPARE-CRYO are randomised trials in paroxysmal AF patients undergoing ablation, with implantable cardiac monitors (ICM) used for continuous rhythm monitoring. This post-hoc analysis included patients with no clinical atrial tachyarrhythmia (ATA) recurrence within 12 months and CHA2DS2-VA ≥1. Monte Carlo simulations (n=5,000) using individual-level ICM data replicated the OCEAN/ALONE-AF eligibility criteria (two simulated 48-hour Holter). Misclassification rates and ATA burden were quantified.

RESULTS: Of 411 patients, 232 were eligible (172 cryoballoon ablation, 60 pulsed-field ablation). Simulated intermittent Holter monitoring classified as ATA-free 223 patients (96.1%; 95% simulation interval [SI] 94.4-97.8%); however, 67 patients (30.0% 95% SI 28.8-31.3%) had ATA on ICM. Among these 223 patients, ATA burden was very low (<0.1%) in 20.6%, low (0.1-1.0%) in 8.7%, and moderate (>1.0%) in 0.7%. In an exploratory analysis, misclassification was numerically higher in patients with CHA2DS2-VA≥3 (33.4% vs. 27.4%). Findings were robust across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one-third of patients deemed ATA-free by OCEAN/ALONE-AF criteria had undetected ATA recurrence on ICM, with very low ATA burden (<0.1%). These findings suggest that the low stroke rates in OCEAN/ALONE-AF may reflect successful arrhythmia burden suppression rather than complete arrhythmia eradication, with intermittent Holter monitoring serving as a pragmatic surrogate for a low-burden state.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary exercise rehabilitation program for patients with stage 3-4 chronic kidney disease in China: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a global health concern, and patients with CKD often exhibit low levels of physical activity, which decline further as renal function worsens. International clinical practice guidelines for CKD emphasize that a multidisciplinary approach to managing chronic diseases can enhance patient outcomes. Exercise rehabilitation, as a secondary preventive measure, supports CKD management, yet its multidisciplinary implementation in China remains in its early stages.

METHODS: A single-center, randomized controlled trial was conducted at the Nephrology Department of a tertiary affiliated hospital, spanning from May 2022 to March 2023. A total of 109 patients with stage 3-4 CKD were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the intervention group (n=54) or the control group (n=55), based on the order of their outpatient visits. Both groups received standard nephrology treatment and care. Additionally, the intervention group participated in a 12-week exercise rehabilitation program, incorporating multidisciplinary management within an outpatient setting. This program involved individual assessments, group health education, personalized counseling, and follow-up. The primary outcome measures, assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks, encompassed changes in handgrip strength, kidney function, nutritional status, self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life.

RESULTS: The intervention group exhibited improvements in grip strength from baseline to week 12, compared to the control group (7.281 kg [95% CI: 4.117 to 10.445], P<0.001). Compared with the control group, the intervention group showed reductions in BMI from baseline to week 12 (-2.561 kg/m2 [95% CI: -3.389 to -1.732]). Favorable changes in serum albumin, self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life were sustained in the intervention group at week 6 and week 12, whereas the beneficial effect on eGFR was sustained only at week 12. No significant group-by-time interaction differences were observed in haemoglobin between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: The 12-week multidisciplinary exercise rehabilitation management program has been shown to significantly improve physical function, kidney function, nutritional status, self-efficacy, and health-related quality of life in patients with stage 3-4 chronic kidney disease in China, supporting its clinical implementation and dissemination.

articles.title: Assessment and management of hypoglycemia in children and adolescents with diabetes.
articles.abstract: Hypoglycemia remains the most frequent acute complication of insulin therapy in children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes (T1D). It poses a constant perceived threat, making the minimization of hypoglycemia a central objective of diabetes management. This chapter builds on the 2022 ISPAD guidelines, synthesizing current evidence on the definition, incidence, symptoms, management, sequelae, and risk factors of hypoglycemia in individuals with T1D and insulin therapy across the pediatric age range. Its insights may also be relevant to insulin treatment in other related conditions. An important theme is the impact of diabetes technology on reducing time in hypoglycemia. The chapter provides revised hypoglycemia management using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) and automated insulin delivery (AID) where they are accessible, while the burden persists in resource-limited settings. Updates include glucose thresholds for active management and carbohydrate dosing for children using AID, newer glucagon formulations for treatment, contemporary data on the neurocognitive, psychosocial, cardiovascular and mortality consequences of hypoglycemia, and an expanded framework for risk assessment, including CGM-derived metrics, to guide hypoglycemia prevention. The recommendations given in this chapter emphasize individualized prevention, timely treatment, structured education, and equitable access to CGM and AID to further reduce the burden and consequences of hypoglycemia in children and adolescents with T1D.

articles.title: Effects of Transurethral Thulium Laser Enucleation of the Prostate on Postoperative Erectile Function and Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Patients With Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND This prospective randomized study examined whether transurethral thulium laser enucleation of the prostate (THuLEP) provides greater early improvement in lower urinary tract symptoms than transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) and compared secondary perioperative and functional outcomes in patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 104 patients with BPH treated from January 2021 to June 2023 were randomly assigned to TURP (n=52) or THuLEP (n=52). Primary outcome was 1-month postoperative between-group difference in International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS). Secondary outcomes included perioperative parameters, quality of life (QOL), International Index of Erectile Function-5 (IIEF-5), maximum urine flow rate (Qmax), postvoid residual volume (PVR), and 30-day complications. Sex hormone levels and inflammatory biomarkers interleukin-4 (IL-4) and IL-17 were evaluated as exploratory correlates of early postoperative status. RESULTS At 1 month, the primary endpoint favored THuLEP: mean IPSS was 5.35 ± 0.54 in the THuLEP group and 7.65±0.78 in the TURP group (unadjusted mean difference [THuLEP minus TURP], -2.30; 95% CI, -2.56 to -2.04; adjusted ß=-1.24; 95% CI, -1.68 to -0.80; P<0.01). Secondary analyses showed lower blood loss, shorter catheterization duration and hospital stay, higher 1-month IIEF-5 and Qmax, lower PVR and QOL, and fewer 30-day complications with THuLEP. Exploratory biomarker analyses showed 1-month between-group differences in E2, T, T/E2, IL-4, and IL-17. These early postoperative comparisons do not establish medium- or long-term superiority. CONCLUSIONS THuLEP produced a greater reduction in LUTS at 1 month than TURP for the prespecified primary endpoint. Several secondary perioperative and functional outcomes also favored THuLEP. Sexual-function and biomarker findings remain preliminary, requiring longer follow-up and external confirmation.

articles.title: Worsening Hypertensive Control as a Clue to High-Grade Brachiocephalic and Subclavian Artery Stenosis in Primary Care: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Upper-extremity peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a less common manifestation of peripheral arterial disease than lower-extremity PAD. Many patients with upper-extremity PAD remain asymptomatic until significant arterial stenosis develops, leading to the manifestation of limb ischemia. Measuring bilateral arm blood pressure can detect an inter-arm blood pressure difference and lead to early diagnosis and management. This report describes the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with uncontrolled hypertension and was found to have unequal upper-limb blood pressure measurements due to high-grade brachiocephalic and subclavian artery stenosis. CASE REPORT We present the case of a 67-year-old man who attended a primary care clinic for hypertension follow-up. He experienced worsening of his previously controlled hypertension over 3 months, without claudication or neurological symptoms. Physical examination identified a significant inter-arm blood pressure discrepancy and diminished pulses in the affected limb. Computed tomography angiography confirmed high-grade stenosis over the right brachiocephalic artery and subclavian artery. He was subsequently referred to the vascular team and managed with medical therapy and regular surveillance. At 1-year follow-up, he remained asymptomatic with no reported complications. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the importance of considering upper-extremity PAD in patients with uncontrolled hypertension detected during a routine primary care follow-up. Early diagnosis and optimal medical therapy are crucial for achieving favorable outcomes and preventing complications by reducing cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Clinicopathologic Features of Hepatic Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis.
articles.journal: The American journal of surgical pathology
articles.abstract: Hepatic Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is rare and, in adults, poorly characterized, largely because most prior series ascertained cases on the basis of clinically evident liver disease in the setting of multisystem LCH (MS-LCH). We assembled a cohort defined solely by histologically confirmed hepatic LCH, irrespective of extrahepatic disease, comprising 18 adults and 8 children (2000 to 2022). Among the adults (mean age: 51.6 y; 9 men, 9 women), half had isolated liver-limited single-system LCH (SS-LCH) and MS-LCH, respectively. Two distinct morphologic patterns emerged. Discrete mass-forming lesions (11/18; 61%) were typically incidental and liver-confined (SS-LCH); architecturally preserved and associated with normal-to-mildly-elevated liver enzymes, they showed readily identifiable Langerhans cells and favorable course without transplantation or LCH-related death. In contrast, disseminated portal infiltration (7/18; 39%) was strongly associated with MS-LCH and presented with cholestasis, bile duct injury/loss, ductular reaction, and advanced fibrosis or biliary-type cirrhosis, mimicking cholestatic disorders; Langerhans cells were often sparse or obscured, requiring immunohistochemistry for detection. This pattern carried substantial morbidity: 4 patients underwent transplantation and 3 died of LCH. Morphologic pattern discriminated clinical presentation, biochemical abnormalities, and outcome more sharply than disease extent did (SS-LCH vs. MS-LCH). All 8 pediatric patients had MS-LCH with disseminated portal infiltration and advanced fibrosis that resembled the adult disseminated pattern but achieved favorable outcomes following early, frequent liver transplantation. These findings define the clinicopathologic spectrum of hepatic LCH across age groups and indicate that recognizing these 2 patterns and their diagnostic pitfalls can improve risk stratification, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and guide management.

articles.title: Alcohol consumption prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection and Long COVID: A retrospective analysis by alcoholic beverage type and intake level.
articles.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is a post-acute condition persisting after a SARS-CoV-2 infection. Evidence on alcohol consumption in LC is limited. This study evaluated the association between pre-infection alcohol consumption and LC by intake level and beverage type. This retrospective case-control study (May 2022-June 2025) included 340 adults with confirmed COVID-19. LC was defined based on the World Health Organization's definition using questionnaire data. Alcohol consumption was quantified as grams of ethanol/day. Beverage-specific analyses were performed. Multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Of the 340 participants, 202 (59.4%) met the definition of LC. Compared with abstainers, moderate (OR = 0.44; 95% CI: 0.23-0.82) and high alcohol consumption (OR = 0.35; 95% CI: 0.12-0.99) were inversely associated with LC in the fully adjusted model. Each additional gram of ethanol/day was associated with lower odds of LC (OR = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.90-0.99). Beer and liquor consumption showed inverse associations, although the liquor estimate was based on few exposed LC cases. Pre-infection alcohol consumption was inversely associated with LC, including moderate and high intake categories, but these observational findings do not establish a causal or protective effect. Further studies are needed.

articles.title: Impact of single-ventricle heart disease on ethnically diverse families.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Care for patients with single-ventricle heart disease requires lifelong, multidisciplinary management; however, its impact on caregivers' socio-economic and psychological well-being remains inadequately explored.

METHODS: We conducted a survey of caregivers of patients with single-ventricle heart disease who presented to our tertiary centre from November 2024 to November 2025, collecting anonymous responses on the self-reported social, economic, and psychological impact of the disease on families.

RESULTS: A total of 104 caregivers completed the survey (response rate > 96%). Most respondents were of non-White ethnicity (64%), with 47% identifying as Hispanic. Approximately one-third of families lived remotely, including 60% in rural communities and nearly 20% at high elevation. One-quarter of parents reported high out-of-pocket medical expenses. Hispanic parents more frequently reported income loss due to reduced work hours compared with White parents (58% vs 35%, p = 0.03). Self-reported mental health disease burden was high amongst caregivers (40%), siblings (30%), and spouses (15%), regardless of ethnicity or educational level. Survey identified several actionable items such as topics that were not adequately discussed during peri-natal counselling, including high medical cost of disease (65%), caregiver burnout (75%), and anticipated mental health disorders in children (56%).

CONCLUSION: Single-ventricle heart disease imposes substantial social, financial, and self-reported psychological burdens on families. These findings highlight opportunities to improve anticipatory guidance and counselling at diagnosis. Expanding cost-effective, multidisciplinary care models, including comprehensive Fontan programs, may help mitigate these challenges. As advances in care improve survival, greater attention to caregivers and family well-being remains essential.

articles.title: The Impact of Stigma and Discrimination on Youth Living with Type 2 Diabetes: A Mixed-Methods Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stigma is associated with suboptimal diabetes outcomes in adults, yet it remains underexplored in youth with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We evaluated the relationship between stigma and clinical and psychosocial outcomes in youth with T2D and explored their experiences of stigma and discrimination at different social-ecological levels.

METHODS: Twenty-nine youth living with T2D for ≥6 months and 24 parents participated in a mixed-methods pilot study with surveys and semi-structured interviews conducted in English or Spanish. Surveys included validated measures assessing global health and quality of life (QOL), depression, perceived discrimination, sociodemographic factors, and T2D-related stigma. Clinical data were abstracted from medical records. Quantitative data were analyzed via descriptive statistics and Spearman correlations (ρ). Qualitative data exploring experiences of stigma and discrimination were coded via inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Stigma experiences were common, with 93% of youth and 54% of parents reporting at least one stigma experience, most frequently related to blame and judgment. Stigma was significantly associated with discrimination (ρ=0.635, p<0.001), depression (ρ=0.410, p=0.027), and reduced quality of life (ρ=-0.625, p=0.010), but not with HbA1c or BMI. Regression analyses confirmed stigma is strongly associated with discrimination (R²=.297, p=0.002). Qualitative interviews showed that youth experienced T2D-related stigma at multiple levels, from internalized guilt and shame to family burden, peer exclusion, and unfair treatment in healthcare settings. Participants also described how diabetes stigma intersects with immigration status to amplify discrimination experiences.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes-related stigma is commonly experienced among youth living with T2D and is associated with discrimination and worse psychosocial outcomes. These findings underscore the need to address stigma as a critical component of comprehensive diabetes care across multiple social-ecological levels.

articles.title: Fontan patients with systemic left ventricle have superior response to 6-month exercise program over patients with right ventricle.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In Fontan patients, transpulmonary flow depends on systemic venous pressure, pulmonary vascular resistance, and ventricle preload. Reduction in cardiopulmonary function is common in Fontan patients. Exercise is considered a promising self-care method to harden particularly lower limbs for supporting transpulmonary flow. We studied whether a 6-month exercise program improves cardiopulmonary function in Fontan patients and if the response is dependent on ventricular morphology.

METHODS: Forty-one paediatric stable Fontan patients with right (RV n = 29) and left (LV n = 12) dominant ventricle morphology were included. Patients with RV were further divided into antegrade (RV-A) and retrograde (RV-R) coronary flow groups. Before the individualised self-guided training, the test subjects were inquired for exercise habits followed by cardiopulmonary exercise testing, body composition, and muscular fitness. Repeat testing was done in 31 patients that completed the exercise prescription. Differences between groups were tested using one-way analysis of variance; within-group changes were analysed using paired t-tests.

RESULTS: Thirty-one patients (LV n = 11, RV-A n = 12, RV-R n = 8) completed the exercise intervention without complications. In comparison to RV patients, those with LV had superior baseline peak VO₂ (p = 0.046) and its improvement by intervention (p = 0.009). RV-R subgroup demonstrated a reduction in the VE/VCO₂ slope, indicating improved ventilation-perfusion matching. Pulmonary function remained unchanged. Muscular fitness improved across all groups.

CONCLUSION: A home-based 6-month exercise program was safe and functional. Patients with systemic LV demonstrated superior improvements in cardiopulmonary fitness. Patients with hypoplastic left heart (RV morphology) improved ventilatory efficiency only. Differences in coronary perfusion may affect exercise response in hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

articles.title: Utility of dobutamine stress testing during routine catheterisation in Fontan patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fontan patients remain at risk for late complications mainly due to high venous pressure, requiring periodic haemodynamic evaluation. Dobutamine stress testing can assess the cardiovascular reserve; however, catheterisation data during dobutamine stress testing are limited in Fontan patients. This study examined whether haemodynamic responses to dobutamine stress testing differ between those who had experienced major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) by the last follow-up and those without MACE.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective case-control study included post-Fontan patients who underwent diagnostic catheterisation with dobutamine stress testing from 2000 to 2023. Patients were divided into a MACE group (n = 14) and a non-major adverse cardiovascular events group (non-MACE) (n = 39) based on the presence or absence of MACE by the last follow-up. Patients' clinical data were compared between two groups.

RESULTS: The median age at catheterisation was 29 years in the MACE group and 18 years in the non-MACE group (p = 0.027). Brain natriuretic protein levels were significantly higher in the MACE group (40.5 vs. 12.0 pg/mL, p = 0.004). The pulmonary vascular resistance index at baseline was higher (1.6 vs. 1.2 WU•m2, p = 0.037) in the MACE group. During dobutamine stress testing, the MACE group demonstrated lower aortic systolic pressure (117 vs. 126 mmHg, p = 0.006) and systemic vascular resistance index (19.9 vs. 25.8 WU•m2, p = 0.028) compared with the non-MACE group. In multivariable analysis, the MACE group was characterised by reduced systemic vascular resistance index during dobutamine stress testing and increased brain natriuretic protein.

CONCLUSIONS: Dobutamine stress testing may provide a novel haemodynamic marker for identifying Fontan patients at risk of MACE by revealing differences in systemic vascular responses that are not apparent at rest, although its prognostic value requires further prospective validation. (249 words).

articles.title: The art of fetal congenital cardiac counselling: a narrative review for fetal cardiology practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in fetal echocardiography have significantly improved prenatal detection of CHD, facilitating early diagnosis, optimised perinatal planning, and improved neonatal outcomes. However, a prenatal diagnosis of CHD can impose a substantial psychological and emotional burden on expectant parents, highlighting the importance of effective and compassionate fetal cardiac counselling.

OBJECTIVE: To review contemporary principles and approaches to fetal cardiac counselling following a prenatal diagnosis of CHD, with particular emphasis on empathetic communication, parental autonomy, shared decision-making, and psychosocial support.

METHODS: This narrative review draws on contemporary clinical literature, professional guidelines, and established principles of patient-centred communication to examine key components of effective fetal cardiac counselling and identify practical strategies for supporting families throughout the prenatal and postnatal journey.

RESULTS: Effective fetal cardiac counselling extends beyond the accurate communication of anatomical findings, prognosis, and treatment options. It requires an individualised, structured, and empathetic approach that acknowledges parental emotional responses, addresses uncertainty, and facilitates informed decision-making. Clear communication, realistic prognostic discussions, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuity of care are central to establishing trust and supporting families. Integrating psychological support and revisiting information over successive consultations may further enhance parental understanding, preparedness, and confidence.

CONCLUSIONS: Compassionate communication is a fundamental component of high-quality fetal cardiac care. Combining clinical expertise with empathy, honesty, shared decision-making, and longitudinal psychosocial support can help families navigate the complexities of prenatal CHD diagnosis. Embedding these principles into routine fetal cardiology practice is essential to delivering holistic, family-centred care.

articles.title: Association of the Family Nutrition and Physical Activity Environment with CVD Risk Factors among Kuwaiti Schoolchildren.
articles.abstract: Childhood obesity and its associated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk are increasing globally, yet limited research has examined the role of family lifestyle environments in Middle Eastern populations. Kuwaiti children have been shown to have elevated CVD risk. To examine the association of the family nutrition and physical activity environment (FNPA) with CVD risk factors among Kuwaiti schoolchildren. FNPA environments were assessed using a validated parent-reported questionnaire in 356 Kuwaiti schoolchildren (mean age 10.4 ± 0.4 years; 52% girls) in a cross-sectional study. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, and lipid profiles were obtained using standardized procedures. Logistic regression analyses examined associations between FNPA score groups and CVD risk factors, with models adjusted for sex and, where applicable, BMI. FNPA scores were significantly lower among girls than boys (p < 0.05). High FNPA scores (>53) were associated with lower odds of obesity (OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.43-0.78; p < 0.001). High FNPA scores were also associated with lower odds of at-risk HDL cholesterol (OR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.28-0.76), low HDL cholesterol (OR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25-0.85), elevated TC/HDL ratio (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24-0.74), and at-risk triglycerides (OR = 0.57, 95% CI: 0.34-0.96) after adjustment for sex and BMI (all p < 0.05). Lower FNPA scores were associated with higher odds of multiple CVD risk factors among Kuwaiti schoolchildren. These findings highlight the family nutrition and physical activity environment as an important context for early CVD risk, although the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

articles.title: Low-Cost Visual Art in Stroke Neurorehabilitation: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Each stroke survivor's path to recovery is highly individualized, often needing support and collaboration from an interdisciplinary team of experts. This scoping review aims to explore how low-cost visual art is used as an intervention in stroke neurorehabilitation beyond traditional therapy alone.

DESIGN: Medline, CINAHL, Embase, Scopus, PubMed, and DOAJ databases were searched using keywords: art, art communication, art therapy, stroke, and neuroplasticity. Titles and abstracts were screened by one reviewer; full texts by two reviewers, with conflicts resolved by a third. 42 papers were included and mapped across three themes: communication, stroke therapy, and neuroplasticity.

RESULTS: Visual art supported self-expression and patient-clinician communication, particularly for patients with language or visuospatial deficits, while art-based assessments were used to identify cognitive-perceptual impairments. Low-cost therapeutic interventions, including drawing, painting, and other group art programs, were associated with improvements in quality of life, mood, self-efficacy, social connectedness, and fine motor or speech outcomes. However, visual arts-based research directly linking to neuroplastic changes remains limited.

CONCLUSION: Visual art can be applied as low-cost and accessible interventions, although further research on the relationship between visual art, neuroplasticity, and clinical implementation is needed.

articles.title: Virtual Reality and Body Weight-Supported Treadmill Training in Gait and Balance Rehabilitation After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on the effects of Virtual Reality (VR) and Body Weight-Supported Treadmill Training (BWSTT) on gait and balance after stroke.

DESIGN: This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, Supplemental Digital Content 2, https://links.lww.com/PHM/D94. PubMed, SciELO, PEDro, LILACS, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to May 2026 for RCTs of VR and/or BWSTT after stroke. Methodological quality was assessed with the PEDro scale and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Evidence on gait and balance outcomes was qualitatively synthesized across VR and BWSTT trials because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Fifteen RCTs (900 individuals) were included: six on VR and nine on BWSTT. VR studies reported improvements in gait velocity, cadence, adaptability, community ambulation, and balance, whereas BWSTT studies reported improvements in gait performance, postural control, functional mobility, walking endurance, and symmetry. Several studies reported effects comparable to conventional rehabilitation. PEDro scores ranged from 6-8, and certainty of evidence from low to moderate.

CONCLUSION: Both interventions may represent adjuncts to conventional rehabilitation for improving gait and balance after stroke. Although they may contribute through therapeutic mechanisms, direct comparisons remain limited. Low to moderate certainty of evidence highlights the need for RCTs using standardized protocols.

articles.title: Reducing the burden of cervical cancer in Zambia in the next 40 years: impact of enhanced screening efforts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Zambia bears one of the world's highest cervical cancer burdens, driven by high human papillomavirus (HPV) prevalence, gaps in vaccination and screening, and the intersecting human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) epidemic.

METHODS: In this study we assess the potential impact of scaling up HPV screening alongside vaccination efforts, based on a community outreach plan designed by ICAP Columbia and Zambia's Ministry of Health. The plan targets Zambia's rural communities and promotes self-collection of samples, on-site HPV testing, and same-day treatment when eligible, with referral to hub sites for severe cases. To estimate the expanded screening's impact, we developed an individual-based model capturing HPV transmission through age-structured sexual partnership, and subsequent progression from infection to cervical lesions and cervical cancer. The model was calibrated to Zambia's demographic profile, 2022 HPV prevalence, 2020 cervical cancer incidence. We compared five 40-year scenarios: no intervention, vaccination only (girls 9-14 years); vaccination plus visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA)-based screening targeted towards women living with HIV, and scenarios extending screening to all women ( ~ 200,000 vs ~400,000 tests/year with 5% annual increase). Outcomes were cervical cancer incidence, percent reduction across intervention scenarios, and cumulative cases averted. Uncertainty was quantified via repeated stochastic simulations with bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs). Sensitivity analyses examined alternative HIV incidence trajectories and reduced screening accessibility.

RESULTS: By 2060, HPV vaccination alone reduces cervical cancer incidence by 47% (95% CI: 39%-55%) compared to current rates but has limited effect in the first 20 years. Adding population screening accelerates impact: under ~400,000 tests/year, incidence falls 64% (95% CI: 56%-70%) by year 20 and 97% (95% CI: 96%-98%) by year 40, averting ~35,000 cases by 2040 and ~183,000 by 2060 and reaching the World Health Organization elimination threshold by 2060. Exploratory analyses suggest additional long-term benefit from vaccinating boys, especially when vaccination coverage is suboptimal.

CONCLUSIONS: In Zambia, vaccination alone will not meaningfully reduce cervical cancer burden in the near term, and pairing vaccination with a community-based HPV-screening/treatment could prevent tens of thousands of cancer cases within two decades and place elimination within reach.

articles.title: Mapping the use of LEGO® serious play® in health professions education: a scoping review of educational outcomes and applications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The LEGO® Serious Play® (LSP) method has been developed as an innovative pedagogical strategy in higher education, particularly in health professions education, where its use has been associated with active learning, reflection, and engagement. However, gaps remain in the understanding of how it has been applied and of its main educational outcomes. This review aimed to map the use of LSP in health professions education, identifying its applications, contexts, and outcomes.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, with searches performed in electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and Google Scholar. Studies addressing the use of LSP in health-related higher education were independently selected by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer when consensus could not be reached. Data were extracted and analysed using descriptive and thematic approaches.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included: six qualitative studies (66.7%), two quantitative studies (22.2%), and one experience report (11.1%). The studies were conducted across different contexts in health professions education. The thematic analysis identified five main categories: (1) promotion of engagement and active learning; (2) development of critical-reflective thinking; (3) construction of professional identity and socio-emotional competencies; (4) mediation of sociocultural processes; and (5) interprofessional collaboration. Overall, the studies reported perceived educational benefits of LSP, particularly in student engagement, depth of reflection, and collaborative learning.

CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review suggests that LEGO® Serious Play® has been used in health professions education as a pedagogical strategy associated with student engagement, reflection, professional identity development, socio-emotional competencies, and interprofessional collaboration. Although the current evidence base is heterogeneous and predominantly qualitative, its applicability is shown across different contexts, interprofessional settings, and educational environments. Future research should consider comparative and longitudinal designs, report implementation fidelity more clearly, and examine whether reported educational benefits are sustained beyond the immediate novelty of the intervention.

articles.title: Autosomal dominant inherited retinal dystrophies in Japan: clinical characteristics, genetics, and implications for precision medicine.
authors: IRD Genomic Research Promotion Taskforce of the Japanese Retina and Vitreous Society
articles.abstract: Autosomal dominant inherited retinal dystrophies (AD-IRDs) constitute a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of disorders in Japan, including retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and the disease category of "macular dystrophies" caused by numerous pathogenic variants across more than 25 genes. Although AD-IRDs represent a smaller proportion of IRDs when compared with autosomal recessive or X-linked forms, their clinical significance is substantial owing to high variable penetrance, marked intrafamilial variability, and the frequent presence of late-onset or mild phenotypes that remain underdiagnosed.The introduction of next-generation sequencing (NGS) enabled multigene testing and improved diagnostic yields in RP cohorts, with subsequent advances increasing detection rates to approximately 45%, particularly for AD-IRDs. More recently, IRD-specific variant interpretation frameworks have further enhanced diagnostic accuracy and nationwide genomic integration.These advances have clarified the genetic spectrum of AD-IRDs in Japan, with recurrent pathogenic variants in hotspots identified in RHO, RP1, RP1L1, PRPH2, and GUCY2D as major contributors. In parallel, deep phenotyping using multimodal retinal imaging, electrophysiology, and refined genotype-phenotype correlation analyses has revealed population-specific variant distributions associated with characteristic clinical patterns in Japanese cohorts. In addition, emerging therapeutic approaches have now been developed, including gene editing, allele-specific suppression, antisense oligonucleotides, RNA editing, and regenerative cell transplantation strategies.This review summarizes the large-scale cohort studies, molecular functions, phenotypes, and ethnic characteristics of Japanese AD-IRDs and discusses future directions toward precision medicine.

articles.title: Surveillance of selected infectious agents in captive felids from Polish zoological gardens - preliminary study.
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases threaten the health and welfare of captive nondomestic felids, yet data on the occurrence of infectious agents in zoological collections remain limited. The aim of this study was to investigate the exposure to selected feline viral pathogens together with Toxoplasma gondii in captive white lion, Amur (Siberian) tiger, white Bengal tiger, Eurasian lynx, cheetah, and sand cat maintained in two Polish zoological gardens using molecular and serological methods. Serum samples and nasal swabs were collected for analysis. Serological testing was performed for feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV), feline leukemia virus (FeLV), and T. gondii, while real-time PCR assays were used to detect feline calicivirus (FCV), feline herpesvirus type 1 (FHV-1), feline leukemia virus (FeLV), and feline coronavirus (FCoV). Nasal swabs were also used for conventional bacteriological examinations. Feline calicivirus RNA was detected in nasal swabs from one white lion and white Bengal tiger, whereas all tested animals were negative for FHV-1, FCoV, and FeLV by real-time PCR. Serological analysis revealed: (i) no evidence of FIV infection; (ii) antibodies against T. gondii in two animals; and (iii) FeLV seropositivity in one white lion despite a negative PCR result. Staphylococcus aureus and Acinetobacter beijerinckii were detected in the sample of white Bengal tiger, as well as Staphylococcus haemolyticus and Psychrobacter maritimus cultured in the sample of white lion. These isolates were distinguished by their low resistance to antimicrobials: : ampicillin, amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, cephalothin, tetracycline and oxytetracycline (A. beijerinckii), clindamycin (S. aureus), as well as streptomycin (P. maritimus). These findings contribute to knowledge of infectious diseases in zoo-housed felids in Central Europe and highlight integrated molecular and serological surveillance for health monitoring and disease management in zoological collections.

articles.title: Adipose Tissue Dysfunction as a Failure of Energy Buffering: A Unifying Framework for Metabolic Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Common metabolic disorders are usually defined by organ-specific abnormalities or diagnostic thresholds, despite substantial overlap in their underlying physiology. This review develops a capacity-based framework in which adipose tissue is considered the principal long-term buffer for sustained energy surplus, and metabolic dysfunction is interpreted in relation to the balance between nutrient surplus and remaining adipose buffering reserve. We distinguish current substrate load from remaining adipose buffering reserve and propose how this distinction might be tested.

RECENT FINDINGS: Established concepts including adipose expandability, adiposopathy, lipotoxicity, and personal fat thresholds, together with recent capacity-based models, emphasise that metabolic risk depends on adipose tissue function rather than its size alone. We integrate these observations into a proposed temporal sequence in which constrained adipose reserve is accompanied by compensatory insulin dynamics, followed by declining adipose lipid containment and impaired suppression of lipolysis. With persistent nutrient surplus, maladaptive remodelling and adipocyte stress may lead to adipocyte death and crown-like structure formation. If adipocyte replacement is insufficient, surviving adipocytes may face greater lipid-storage demands, potentially accelerating dysfunction and promoting ectopic lipid deposition. This framework links tissue-specific insulin dynamics, structural adipose tissue injury, ectopic lipid exposure, and threshold-defined disease expression within a shared sequence of declining metabolic resilience. It further distinguishes reduction of current substrate load from restoration of buffering reserve, providing a potential explanation for metabolic heterogeneity, incomplete reversibility, and vulnerability to relapse after apparent clinical improvement. The proposed sequence of events and the role of remaining reserve in relapse require longitudinal validation.

articles.title: Triad-Based Synergistic Framework for Accelerating Chronic Wound Repair: Combinative Mechanistic Approaches through Integrating Biometal Nanoparticles, Biopolymers, and Phytoconstituents.
articles.abstract: Biometal nanoparticle (BNP)-integrated bioactive compounds are promising for chronic wound healing due to their increased surface area, antimicrobial and redox activity. Mechanisms of three BNPs - Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), and Silver (Ag) across healing stages are reviewed. Despite their clinical use, limitations like poor stability and uncontrolled ion release reduce their efficacy. To overcome these limitations, BNPs are considered in combination with bioactive components - biopolymers and phytoconstituents as a Triad based system, in which the three components do not merely form additive functions but rather perform complementary function. BNPs contribute antimicrobial and redox activity, biopolymers regulate material stability along with leveraging controlled ion delivery whereas phytoconstituent modulate oxidative stress, tissue repair and inflammation. Keen emphasis is placed on the dynamic integration of these components into mechanism through two interconnected axes of chronic wound healing- Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) dependent infection control and growth factor upregulation for tissue regeneration. Four ROS-mediated BNP-driven antibacterial pathways were discussed; although BNP-driven antibacterial activity is known, its use via these specific mechanisms remains untapped in wounds. Intrinsic growth factor upregulation by the triads was reviewed, supporting enhanced repair. The triad composite is thus proposed not simply as a three-component composite, but as a mechanistic bridge that links antimicrobial activity, redox regulation, inflammatory control and growth-factor-mediated healing to address the multifactorial infection-prone wounds. A framework for eco-friendly, multifunctional dressings is provided, and future directions, including smart nanoplatforms and AI-assisted design, are outlined for next-generation wound care.

articles.title: Microplastic contamination of Schizothorax eurystomus (Kessler, 1872) in the Karadarya River (Uzbekistan).
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are considered an increasingly hazardous pollutant in freshwater ecosystems due to their trophic transfer and ecological risks. This study investigated the MPs contamination, shape, size, colour and polymer composition of MPs in fish samples of the widely distributed species Schizothorax eurystomus from the Karadarya watershed, the main river of the Fergana Valley, during 2023-2024. The 36 samples were collected from areas with three anthropogenic impact zones. MPs were extracted by alkaline digestion and density-based separation. Morphological classification, Raman spectroscopy, and statistical analysis methods were applied. MPs were primarily detected in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) and the gills; The overall MP burden was similar in both organs, with a median of 0 particles/individual in the GIT (mean 1.75 ± 4.72 SD; range 0-28) and a median of 1 in the gills (mean 1.64 ± 2.13 SD; range 0-9); the difference was not statistically significant (Mann-Whitney U = 535.5; p = 0.18). Despite comparable abundances, the two organs differed in particle morphology, with fibers predominating in the gills (94.9% of particles). Pearson and Spearman correlations showed a strong correlation between body length and mass (r = 0.89; rs = 0.94; p < 0.001), whereas in the gills a weak positive association with age was observed (rs = 0.34; n = 36; p = 0.044), …and no association with age was found in the GIT (rs = 0.12; p = 0.473). Raman spectroscopy verified the polymeric constituents to be PET, PEVA, PES blends, PPSU, PMP blends, and PE polymers. Sulfone-based polymers were more frequent in the gills, while PET were most frequent in the GIT. This pattern is consistent with gill contamination occurring mainly through filtration, whereas GIT contamination results from ingestion. The results demonstrate the ecological relevance of MP contamination in Central Asian freshwater systems and the need for continued environmental monitoring of riverine MP pollution.

articles.title: Kennedy disease mimicking idiopathic inflammatory myopathy: a 9-year diagnostic delay and case-based review.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIMs) are frequently considered in patients with proximal weakness and hyperCKemia, but inherited neuromuscular disorders may produce the same initial phenotype. We describe a 56-year-old male technician with 9 years of progressive myalgia, proximal weakness and creatine kinase (CK) elevation who had been treated as having inflammatory myopathy. Although CK decreased during glucocorticoid and leflunomide therapy, muscle strength, walking capacity and bulbar function did not improve in parallel. Reassessment identified long-standing tremor, tongue fasciculations, muscle atrophy and reduced lower-limb reflexes. Myositis serology was negative, thigh magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse atrophy and fatty replacement without conspicuous active oedema and nerve conduction studies demonstrated reduced or absent sensory nerve action potentials with largely preserved motor conduction velocities. Needle electromyography showed widespread chronic neurogenic abnormalities. Quadriceps biopsy showed advanced chronic, non-specific changes; immunohistochemistry demonstrated only sparse CD68-positive macrophages, no definite CD4-, CD8- or CD20-positive lymphocytic infiltrates, no increased sarcolemmal major histocompatibility complex class I expression and no remarkable C5b-9 deposition. Molecular genetic testing by Sanger sequencing identified 45 CAG repeats in exon 1 of the androgen receptor (AR) gene, confirming Kennedy disease (KD). A focused narrative review identified four relevant reports: three describing KD initially classified as polymyositis and one describing true antisynthetase syndrome coexisting with KD. The present case highlights biochemical-functional discordance as a practical trigger for diagnostic reassessment. In presumed IIM, falling CK without parallel improvement in strength, gait or bulbar function should prompt neurological examination, electrodiagnostic testing and, when clinically indicated, targeted genetic analysis.

articles.title: Resistant and Refractory Migraine: Updated Consensus Definitions and Management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Resistant and refractory migraine are high burden migraine disease states that persist despite evidence-based preventive treatment. This review summarizes the 2025 international consensus definitions, presents a structured clinical reassessment before classification, and reviews management strategies and evidence gaps.

RECENT FINDINGS: Under the consensus definition, resistant migraine requires that at least three preventive categories have been addressed, including at least one due to inadequate efficacy. Refractory migraine requires that all evidence-based categories have been addressed. Among these, onabotulinumtoxinA, a calcitonin gene-related peptide pathway inhibitor, and at least two additional categories must have been ineffective despite adequate trials. Other categories may be considered addressed because of intolerance or an absolute contraindication. Both definitions require two of three disease burden criteria: disability, at least eight monthly migraine days, or daily headache between migraine attacks. It also defines probable refractory and treatment-responsive migraine. Before classification, clinicians should confirm the phenotype and baseline state, reconsider secondary headache and comorbidity contributions, audit preventive trials, and optimize acute and bridge treatment. Most treatment evidence predates the consensus definitions or uses less stringent criteria. For resistant migraine, management should prioritize completion of remaining evidence-based preventive categories. Refractory migraine may require re-evaluation of prior trials, within-category switching, rational combination therapy, individualized time-limited off-label trials, investigational options, behavioral treatment, and multidisciplinary care. These definitions remain consensus-derived and are not included in the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Prospective studies using these criteria are needed for validation and to define epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, biomarkers, and treatment response.

articles.title: Serial [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/MRI during teprotumumab therapy in thyroid eye disease.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: A hypothesis-generating integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics nominates SPP1-CD44 innate-adaptive crosstalk in ocular hypertension.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation accompanies retinal ganglion cell (RGC) loss in glaucoma, but the immune states elicited by intraocular pressure (IOP) elevation and the crosstalk among them remain incompletely characterized. We performed a hypothesis-generating re-analysis integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomes from four public cohorts. Among 30,063 CD45 + immune cells from the microbead ocular hypertension (OHT) model (GSE293358), the retinal homeostatic-microglia compartment was relatively depleted under OHT. In contrast, MHCII+ macrophage/APC and lymphocyte compartments, including γδ T, NK, and T cells, were relatively expanded, whereas DAM-like microglia showed a non-significant upward trend. These changes reflect composition within the CD45 + fraction and should not be interpreted as absolute changes in cell number. Diffusion pseudotime organized microglia along an inferred homeostatic→DAM→interferon/MHCII transcriptional continuum, with module scores showing directional concordance in an independent bulk time-course cohort (retina DAM Δ=+1.00, nominal p = 0.044; two pooled libraries per group, exploratory). In sorted Müller glia, expression of the microglia-restraining ligand Cx3cl1 was markedly reduced (log2FC = - 5.30; nominal p = 0.010, with no gene passing FDR correction in this n = 3-per-group cohort). Cell-cell communication inference further predicted an OHT-associated SPP1→CD44 ligand-receptor interaction from activated myeloid cells to lymphocytes. Together, these findings nominate candidate hypotheses involving immune-state reorganization and ligand-receptor signaling in OHT; we present them as parallel, compartmentalized responses and do not claim a validated causal cascade. Exploratory Mendelian randomization and compound-reversal analyses (Figs. S1 and S2 in Online Resource 1) did not provide definitive causal or therapeutic evidence. All proposed mechanisms are inferred from transcriptomic data and require protein-level, spatial, and functional validation.

articles.title: Loss of nuclear YAP1 expression in autopsy myocardium across selected fatal congenital heart disease phenotypes.
articles.journal: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
articles.abstract: Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1), a key effector of Hippo signalling, regulates cardiomyocyte proliferation and cardiac growth. Its expression pattern in human congenital heart disease (CHD) myocardium from fetal to postnatal stages remains incompletely characterized. This study evaluated nuclear and cytoplasmic active YAP1 expression in ventricular myocardium from fatal CHD cases and non-CHD controls. We retrospectively reviewed 76 autopsy cases with CHD from a tertiary centre and performed immunohistochemistry using an antibody specific for active (non-phosphorylated) YAP1 on ventricular myocardium from selected subgroups, including hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), hypoplastic right heart syndrome (HRHS), transposition of the great arteries (TGA), and heterotaxy syndrome, together with 14 non-CHD controls. High quality tissue samples were available from 26 CHD cases and 14 non-CHD controls. Nuclear YAP1 staining was semiquantitatively scored and dichotomized as preserved expression versus complete loss. The results show the YAP1 staining became more focal and weaker with increasing age, but no complete loss of nuclear YAP1 expression was observed in control cases. Complete loss of YAP1 expression was observed more frequently in HLHS, HRHS, and TGA. In age-adjusted analyses with Holm correction, HLHS remained the most consistent association with complete nuclear YAP1 loss. In conclusion, loss of cardiomyocyte active YAP1 immunoreactivity was identified in selected fatal congenital heart disease phenotypes. These results highlight altered myocardial active YAP1 expression and provide a basis for investigating its role in ventricular development and responses to abnormal cardiac haemodynamics.

articles.title: FAP-targeted 211At radiotherapy remodels the tumor microenvironment and is associated with enhanced anti-PD-L1 efficacy.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)‑positive cancer‑associated fibroblasts contribute to immune exclusion and resistance to checkpoint blockade in the tumor microenvironment (TME). This study evaluated whether 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr, a FAP‑targeted alpha‑emitting radiopharmaceutical, could remodel the TME and enhance responsiveness to PD-L1 blockade.

METHODS: Given the complex and immune-excluded microenvironment of lung cancer, we analyzed public datasets to define the clinical and immune context of FAP in this malignancy. 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr was synthesized and characterized for radiochemical purity, stability, FAP‑specific uptake, DNA damage, and PD‑L1 induction. Biodistribution, PET/CT imaging, therapeutic efficacy, histology, immune remodeling, and systemic cytokine profiles (MSD platform) were assessed in LLC/3T3‑FAP tumor‑bearing mice treated with saline, 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr, TPP-1 (a PD-L1-blocking peptide), or combination.

RESULTS: FAP was enriched in stromal regions and correlated with advanced stage, reduced CD8⁺ T‑cell infiltration, and immunosuppressive signatures. 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr showed > 95% radiochemical purity, FAP‑dependent uptake, induced γ‑H2AX foci, and upregulated PD‑L1 in vitro. Tumor uptake peaked at 5.63 ± 0.72%ID/g (1 h) and remained 4.53 ± 2.13%ID/g at 24 h. Combination therapy exhibited the most potent tumor growth inhibition, reduced 18F‑FDG uptake, increased PD-L1-specific 68​Ga-TPP-1 uptake, decreased proliferation and angiogenesis, and enhanced CD8⁺ T‑cell infiltration and granzyme B expression. At the immunological level, MSD‑based cytokine analysis revealed that combination therapy induced more extensive alterations in systemic immune modulation than either monotherapy, whereas 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr alone shifted the profile toward pro‑inflammation. No overt organ histopathology or sustained body-weight loss was observed during the assessment period (8 days), while treatment-associated haematological changes (reduced WBC and RBC counts) were detected.

CONCLUSION: In the engineered LLC/3T3-FAP model, 211At-FAP-2286-Tyr selectively targets FAP-rich tumor stroma, induces DNA damage and adaptive PD-L1 upregulation, and is associated with a shift of the immune-excluded TME toward a state that is more responsive to PD-L1 blockade. These findings suggest that FAP-targeted alpha radiotherapy may be a promising strategy for TME remodeling and immunotherapy sensitization in preclinical NSCLC models, and support further investigation toward clinical translation in more physiologically relevant systems.

articles.title: Correction: Influences of an NR1I2 polymorphism on heterogeneous antiplatelet reactivity responses to clopidogrel and clinical outcomes in acute ischemic stroke patients.
[Emphasizing multidisciplinary collaborative management of severe intra-abdominal infection].
articles.journal: Zhonghua wai ke za zhi [Chinese journal of surgery]
articles.abstract: Severe intra-abdominal infection (SIAI) is a common critical condition in general surgery and can rapidly progress to sepsis, septic shock, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome. With advances in the management of sepsis and critical care medicine, the management of SIAI has gradually evolved from a surgical approach centered primarily on source control to an integrated strategy combining source control with organ support, reflecting the close interdisciplinary integration of surgery and critical care medicine. The management of SIAI requires close collaboration between general surgeons and intensivists across multiple aspects of care, including early assessment, source control, fluid management, organ support, and antimicrobial therapy. Establishing joint surgical-ICU assessment, stage-based collaborative management, and multidisciplinary team collaboration may help achieve a dynamic balance between source control and organ protection. The development of the acute care surgery model has further promoted the integration of surgical and critical care management. This article reviews the pathophysiological characteristics of SIAI and its interdisciplinary nature involving surgery and critical care medicine, focusing on the coordination of source control and organ support, stage-based surgical-ICU management, multidisciplinary team collaboration, and integrated management within the acute care surgery framework, and discusses the construction and future development of a multidisciplinary collaborative management model for SIAI.

articles.title: Association Between Social Isolation and Stroke Risk among Survivors Following the Great East Japan Earthquake: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence linking social isolation (SI) with incident stroke remains limited, especially regarding post-disaster populations and potential sex-based differences. We examined sex-based differences in the association between SI and incident stroke among Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) survivors.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 27,379 GEJE survivors. SI was assessed at baseline using the Lubben Social Network Scale. Incident stroke (ischemic and hemorrhagic) was identified using the population-based Iwate Stroke Registry. Three sequential, sex-stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for age, BMI, systolic blood pressure, HbA1c, LDL, HDL, estimated glomerular filtration rate, drinking and smoking status, exercise habit, marital status, living arrangement, educational attainment, employment status, psychological distress (K6), and housing damage.

RESULTS: 208 men and 156 women developed stroke during follow-up (mean follow-up: 5.99 years). SI was significantly associated with an increased risk of stroke in men (HR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.06-1.92), but not in women (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.62-1.40; p for interaction = 0.005). The association was observed mainly for ischemic stroke in men (HR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.07-2.12). Subgroup analyses by housing damage showed a stronger association among men without direct housing damage than among men with housing damage (adjusted HR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.02-1.90 vs. 1.19; 95% CI, 0.68-1.91).

CONCLUSIONS: In post-disaster populations, SI is significantly associated with incident stroke in men but not women. Socially isolated men in disaster-affected areas represent a priority group for public health interventions to reduce stroke risk.

articles.title: Current Status and Future Prospects of Catheter Ablation for Brugada Syndrome.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: Brugada syndrome is a type of arrhythmia with a highly hereditary tendency with characteristic electrocardiographic findings that is associated with lethal arrhythmias. An implantable cardioverter defibrillator is recommended to avoid cardiac sudden death, because medical therapy cannot completely suppress the occurrence of ventricular fibrillation (VF). Meanwhile, ablation for Brugada syndrome has been reported to prevent VF. The targets of ablation are the triggers of premature ventricular contraction that induce VF, and the substrate of the epicardium in the right ventricular outflow tract where VF may develop and be maintained. After substrate ablation, the characteristic electrocardiogram in Brugada syndrome normalizes, and VF is prevented in many patients. Based on the characteristics of the abnormal delayed potentials observed in the epicardial arrhythmogenic substrate, the target of ablation, although depolarization abnormalities are considered a possible mechanism underlying Brugada syndrome, it appears that repolarization abnormalities are also involved.

articles.title: Impact of Body Mass Index on Recurrence After Catheter Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation in Patients With Left Atrial Low-Voltage Areas　- Prespecified Subanalysis of the SUPPRESS-AF Trial.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-voltage area ablation (LVA-ABL) is used for substrate modification in persistent atrial fibrillation (AF), but whether its benefit varies by body mass index (BMI) is uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This prespecified subanalysis of the multicenter randomized SUPPRESS-AF trial included patients with persistent AF undergoing initial catheter ablation. After pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), patients with low-voltage areas (LVAs; bipolar voltage <0.5 mV) totaling ≥5 cm2were randomized to adjunctive LVA-ABL or PVI alone. Overall, 341 patients were stratified by BMI quartile (Q1, 14.1-20.8 kg/m2; Q2, 20.9-23.3 kg/m2; Q3, 23.4-26.0 kg/m2; Q4, 26.1-37.9 kg/m2). The primary endpoint was AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) recurrence after a 3-month blanking period without antiarrhythmic drugs through 12 months. Overall AF/AT recurrence did not differ by BMI quartile (log-rank P=0.97). In BMI-stratified analyses, adjunctive LVA-ABL was associated with lower recurrence than PVI alone in Q2 (28.6% vs. 53.5%; log-rank P=0.020; adjusted hazard ratio 0.47; 95% confidence interval 0.22-0.95), whereas no clear benefit was observed in Q1, Q3, or Q4. The treatment-by-BMI interaction was not statistically significant (P=0.089).

CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive LVA-ABL did not demonstrate a statistically significant treatment-by-BMI interaction. Although recurrence was lower in the BMI Q2, this subgroup finding should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis generating. Further studies are warranted to determine whether substrate burden can refine substrate definition and lesion targeting.

articles.title: Concurrent Emphysematous Cystitis and Rectal Pneumatosis with Sepsis.
Switching from Febuxostat to Dotinurad in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease and Hyperuricemia: A Single-center, Non-randomized Study.
articles.abstract: Objective　This study aimed to evaluate switching from febuxostat to dotinurad, which increases the fractional excretion of uric acid (FEUA), in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and hyperuricemia (HUA).Methods　Sixty patients with CKD and HUA who received febuxostat first underwent a 3-month observation period, followed by a 3-month intervention period, during which treatment was switched from febuxostat to dotinurad. The primary outcomes were changes from baseline to 3 months after switching in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated from serum creatinine (eGFRcreat) and cystatin C (eGFRcys), as well as the serum uric acid (UA) levels.Patients　The main inclusion criteria for enrollment were patients with CKD stage G2-G4 who received febuxostat for HUA.Results　During the observation period, the mean eGFRcreat decreased significantly. The baseline eGFRcreat (mL/min/1.73 m2) was 36.0±15.2, and the serum urate level (mg/dL) was 5.5±1.2. During the intervention period, eGFRcreat increased in contrast to the significant decline observed in eGFRcys. After 3 months of switching to dotinurad, the mean serum UA levels increased significantly from 5.5±1.2 to 6.1±1.4 mg/dL, despite a significant elevation in FEUA.Conclusions　Switching from febuxostat to dotinurad resulted in discrepant changes in eGFRcreat and eGFRcys, suggesting that the renal function should be assessed carefully after switching. Additionally, the risk of elevated serum UA levels should be considered when switching from febuxostat to dotinurad in patients with CKD.

articles.title: Early Oxygenation Response Predicts Short-Term Mortality in an Acute Exacerbation of Interstitial Lung Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Objective　An acute exacerbation of interstitial lung disease (AE-ILD) is a life-threatening condition associated with high short-term mortality. Although corticosteroids are widely used, the clinical outcomes vary considerably, and early prognostic indicators in heterogeneous real-world populations remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early changes in the oxygenation status after treatment initiation and short-term mortality in patients with AE-ILD.Methods　This retrospective cohort study included patients with AE-ILD requiring oxygen therapy and receiving high-dose corticosteroids (≥1 mg/kg prednisolone equivalent) between January 2012 and January 2024. The oxygenation response was assessed on days 3-5 after treatment initiation based on changes in oxygen requirement and intensity of oxygen-delivery support; patients were classified as responders or non-responders. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. A multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors.Patients　Sixty-eight patients (29 responders and 39 non-responders).Results　The 30-day mortality rate was 29.4% (20/68). In a sensitivity analysis of patients assessed on day 3, responders had a significantly lower 30-day mortality than nonresponders [9.1% (2/22) vs. 50.0% (13/26), p = 0.004]. Overall, 28 patients (41.2%) died during follow-up, including eight of 29 responders (27.6%) and 20 of 39 nonresponders (51.3%). Responders had a significantly better overall survival than nonresponders (median survival: not reached vs. 107 days; log-rank p = 0.014). In the multivariate analysis, early oxygenation response was independently associated with lower 30-day mortality (OR, 0.050; 95% CI, 0.010-0.266; p < 0.001), and severe respiratory failure was associated with a higher mortality (OR, 8.518; 95% CI, 1.903-38.132; p = 0.005).Conclusion　An early improvement in the oxygenation status after treatment initiation was independently associated with lower short-term mortality in patients with AE-ILD. This simple and practical measure, assessed within 3-5 days of treatment initiation, may help identify patients at higher risk and support early clinical decision-making in heterogeneous real-world populations.

articles.title: Sleep Quality in Hospitalized Patients with Chronic Liver Disease: A Retrospective Study with an Exploratory Analysis of Covert Hepatic Encephalopathy.
articles.abstract: Objective　Sleep-related disturbances are an important comorbidity of chronic liver disease (CLD) but are not routinely assessed in clinical practice. We evaluated sleep quality using the Japanese version of the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and explored its association with covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE).Methods　This retrospective, single-center study enrolled hospitalized patients with CLD who completed the PSQI upon admission. Poor sleep quality was defined as a PSQI global score ≥6. Factors associated with poor sleep quality were evaluated using logistic regression analysis. CHE was assessed in a subcohort of patients who completed a neuropsychological test (NPT) battery.Results　Among the 180 enrolled patients (median age, 68 years; 65.0% men), the median PSQI global score was 5 (interquartile range, 3-8), and 88 (48.9%) reported poor sleep quality. In a multivariate analysis, medication use for pruritus (odds ratio [OR], 5.24) and a SARC-F score of ≥4 (OR, 3.19) were independently associated with PSQI ≥6. The NPT-assessed subcohort comprised 41 patients (CHE, 24; non-CHE, 17). PSQI global scores were higher in the CHE group than in the non-CHE group (Hodges-Lehmann estimate [CHE - non-CHE], 3.0; p=0.013). Component-level analyses indicated a shift toward higher scores for PSQI component 5 (sleep disturbances) in the CHE group. CHE remained associated with PSQI ≥6 after multivariate adjustment in the subcohort (OR, 8.00).Conclusions　Poor sleep quality was common among hospitalized patients with CLD and associated with medication use for pruritus and SARC-F ≥4. An exploratory analysis suggested an association between the CHE classification and poor sleep quality.

articles.title: A Case Report of Follicular Lymphoma with Concurrent Membranoproliferative Glomerulonephritis.
articles.abstract: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) associated with non-Hodgkin lymphoma has been frequently reported; however, its association with follicular lymphoma (FL) is rare. A man in his late 70's presented with hypertension, edema, and weight gain. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a mesenteric mass. A biopsy confirmed FL, and a renal biopsy showed type I MPGN. After two cycles of G-CHOP therapy, the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio markedly decreased, and a complete response was achieved.

articles.title: Infective Endocarditis Diagnosed by 2023 Duke-ISCVID Criteria with Negative Blood Culture and 18F-FDG PET/CT Findings.
articles.abstract: A 69-year-old man was admitted to our hospital with a fever suggestive of infective endocarditis. His medical history included mitral valve replacement and tricuspid valve repair. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography revealed no definite vegetations, and 18Fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18FDG-PET/CT) showed no abnormal cardiac uptake. His blood culture results were negative. Finally, the patient was diagnosed with Bartonella-associated infective endocarditis, with markedly elevated IgG titers against Bartonella henselae (≥1: 1,024). Bartonella endocarditis should be considered in patients with negative blood culture and 18FDG-PET/CT findings.

articles.title: The "Udon Noodles Sign": A Potential Complementary Tool for Estimating the Last Known Well Time.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: To guide tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) therapy in acute ischemic stroke with an unknown onset time, the last known well (LKW) time and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) mismatch on MRI are commonly used, although their diagnostic accuracy remains suboptimal. We investigated whether abdominal CT findings of "udon" noodles could estimate the last meal time (LMT), exploring its potential as a complementary chronological tool when the LKW time is uncertain.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 102 patients with documented udon ingestion time and available abdominal CT data. The "udon noodles sign" was defined as the presence of high-density noodle-like structures in the stomach. Gastric Hounsfield Unit (HU) values were measured and correlated with the time elapsed since ingestion.

RESULTS: The "udon noodles sign" was positive in 64 cases (62.7%). A significant negative correlation was observed between gastric HU values and elapsed time (r = -0.626, p < 0.0001). A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis for predicting a 4.5-hour window for tPA yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.82. A cutoff value of 123.0 HU provided a sensitivity of 53.1% and a specificity of 96.9%.

CONCLUSION: A CT-based analysis of gastric udon noodles may be effective in estimating the time from the last meal. Given its high specificity, the "udon noodles sign" with HU values of ≥ 123.0 could serve as a complementary tool for indirectly estimating the LKW time.

articles.title: Blood-Pressure-Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum.
authors: Blood Pressure Lowering Treatment Trialists’ Collaboration
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear.

METHODS: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, <4%; highest decile, >27%).

RESULTS: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points), and the number needed to treat to prevent one major cardiovascular event over 5 years was lower in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (38 vs. 255). The incidence of a cardiovascular or hemodynamic event was 12.0 per 1000 person-years in the intervention group and 6.5 per 1000 person-years in the comparator group; the incidence of an adverse renal event was 3.3 and 2.2 per 1000 person-years, respectively; and the incidence of a neurovestibular or fall-associated event was 19.1 and 16.6 per 1000 person-years. The relative increase in the risk of each safety-outcome event with antihypertensive treatment as compared with placebo or usual care did not appear to vary across deciles.

CONCLUSIONS: Blood-pressure lowering was associated with a decreased risk of major cardiovascular events across the risk spectrum, including a predicted 5-year risk below 4%. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; PROSPERO registry number, CRD42018099283.).

articles.title: Differences Between Urban and Rural Counties in Pregnancy-Related Deaths - United States, 2015-2024.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: Residents of rural communities face multiple health challenges, including higher pregnancy-related mortality (the death of a woman during or within 1 year of the end of pregnancy from any cause related to or aggravated by pregnancy); however, causes of pregnancy-related mortality by urban-rural classification are not well described. To better understand differences in pregnancy-related mortality by urban-rural classification levels, CDC analyzed data from 7,357 pregnancy-related deaths that occurred during 2015-2024 from CDC's Pregnancy Mortality Surveillance System. The numbers of pregnancy-related deaths per 100,000 live births, or pregnancy-related mortality ratios (PRMRs), were examined across six urban-rural classifications based on the National Center for Health Statistics' urban-rural classification scheme, and by race and ethnicity, age, and underlying cause of death.
