Although most deaths occurred among women living in urban counties, PRMRs were highest among those living in rural counties across age categories, most racial and ethnic groups, and cause-of-death categories. Cardiovascular conditions (including cardiomyopathy) and infection or sepsis were the most frequent causes of pregnancy-related mortality across all urban-rural classifications. These findings highlight potential needs to improve access to primary, obstetric, and specialty care in rural communities.

articles.title: T Cell Interactions with Fibroblastic Reticular Cells in Infection and Cancer.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Secondary lymphoid organs coordinate interactions between T cells and antigen-presenting cells that enables the initiation  of immune responses. Within the T cell zone, fibroblastic stroma constructs a three-dimensional cellular and extracellular matrix network that provides essential structural, biochemical, and mechanical support for T cells and dendritic cells. Through the provision of specialised signals, this fibroblastic network engages with immune cells and fine-tunes immune activity at homeostasis and during antiviral and anticancer immune responses. Beyond regulating immune activation, fibroblasts are critical for restoring tissue organisation following inflammation, ensuring that lymphoid organs remain poised for subsequent immune responses. In this chapter, we explore the mechanisms through which T cell zone fibroblasts orchestrate immune control in health and disease.

articles.title: Specialized Pro-resolving Mediators in Airway Inflammation and Chronic Lung Disease: Cellular Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Chronic lung diseases can arise from repetitive inflammatory insults that become excessive or lead to exhaustion of counter-regulatory mechanisms with resultant dysregulated inflammation. In health, resolution mechanisms are active in the lung and participate in control of immune responses and maintaining lung homeostasis. Resolution of airway inflammation is a coordinated multicellular process driven, in part, by specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs), including lipoxins, resolvins, protectins, and maresins. These mediators engage G-protein-coupled receptors to limit leukocyte recruitment, promote efferocytosis, reprogram immune cell phenotypes, and stimulate epithelial restitution and barrier repair, while preserving host defense. In health, lipid mediator class switching ensures timely transition from pro-inflammatory eicosanoids to pro-resolving SPMs. In chronic lung diseases, such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, these pathways can become uncoupled due to defects in SPM biosynthesis, SPM receptor signaling, or the cellular execution of resolution programs. This chapter reviews mechanistic and translational insights into cellular-resolution programs across the immune, epithelial, and neural components of the lung and highlights potential associations between defects in these resolution mechanisms and airway diseases. Recent advances in our understanding of resolution mediators and mechanisms in the lung present opportunities to leverage endogenous resolution pathways as a potential new therapeutic framework for chronic lung disease modification.

articles.title: Intraoperative Diastolic Blood Pressure Variability and Myocardial Injury in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between intraoperative blood pressure variability and postoperative myocardial injury (PMI) after endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is unknown.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled AIS patients who underwent EVT between June 28th, 2016, and January 11th, 2021. PMI was assessed using cardiac troponin I measurement. Intraoperative diastolic blood pressure (DBP) variability was assessed using the coefficient of variation (CV). A population-level CV threshold was derived from the inflection point of the logistic regression curve. The primary outcome was PMI during hospitalization. To establish the association between DBP variability and PMI, multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for possible confounders.

RESULTS: During the study period, 469 AIS patients were included. The median age was 63 years, and 142 (30.3%) were women. A total of 84 (17.9%) patients experienced PMI. An intraoperative diastolic CV of 16% was estimated as the threshold. After adjusting for confounders, with every 1% increase in diastolic CV above 16%, there was a 17% increase in the odds of experiencing PMI (OR=1.17; 95% CI: 1.09-1.27; P≤0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DBP variability is associated with PMI in AIS patients undergoing EVT. Future randomized clinical trials should evaluate whether stabilizing diastolic perfusion pressure reduces the incidence of PMI.

articles.title: Sign convention and internal consistency in fetal strain analysis.
Multiple hypertension-mediated organ damage: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Subclinical morpho-functional alterations affecting the heart, brain, kidneys, retina, aorta, and peripheral vasculature induced by chronic hypertension are defined by current guidelines as hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD). Several lines of evidence indicate that these alterations carry adverse prognostic significance across all blood pressure (BP) categories, regardless of traditional cardiovascular (CV) risk factors.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review provides an overview of the pathophysiological background and prevalence of HMOD at cardiac, vascular, renal, retinal and cerebral sites, as well as the clinical relevance of multiple HMOD and the limitations of CV risk stratification based on a single HMOD marker. Relevant literature was identified through a narrative search of PubMed/MEDLINE, OVID, and the Cochrane Library, last updated in June 2026, with no predefined restriction on publication date. Particular emphasis is placed on the coexistence and clustering of HMOD across different organs and on the potential value of a multiorgan assessment.

EXPERT OPINION: As damage in one organ cannot be reliably inferred from the assessment of another, a comprehensive yet patient-tailored evaluation of cardiac and extracardiac HMOD may improve CV risk stratification and guide clinical management in patients with hypertension.

articles.title: Cerebral actinomycosis in pediatrics: Brain abscesses caused by Schaalia georgiae.
articles.abstract: Actinomycosis is a rare bacterial infection caused by Gram-positive bacilli of the order Actinomycetales, which are commensals of the oral cavity. Involvement of the central nervous system is exceptional and is usually associated with hematogenous spread from a dental focus. We report a case of cerebral actinomycosis in an immunocompetent pediatric patient following a tooth extraction. We present a 14-year-old female patient with partially corrected congenital heart disease who developed multiple brain abscesses from which Schaalia georgiae was isolated. Surgical drainage and intravenous antibiotic therapy were administered for six weeks, followed by a prescription for long-term oral doxycycline and outpatient follow-up. The nonspecific clinical presentation, polymicrobial nature, and difficulty isolating the organism make diagnosis challenging. This case highlights the importance of considering actinomycosis in the differential diagnosis of pediatric brain abscesses and of a timely medical-surgical approach to improve clinical outcomes and reduce sequelae.

articles.title: Diverging mortality trajectories of tobacco-documented pulmonary hypertension, COPD, and lung cancer in the United States, 2018-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) mortality may not have followed recent improvements in tobacco-related diseases. We compared PH mortality with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer and assessed whether divergence was specific to deaths with documented tobacco use.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) WONDER mortality data for US residents aged ≥25 years. PH required I27.0 or I27.2 as the underlying cause; COPD and lung cancer formed the benchmark. Age-adjusted mortality-rate ratios for 2018-2024 were modeled using inverse-variance weighting, restricted maximum likelihood, and Knapp-Hartung inference. A post hoc analysis removed the tobacco-documentation requirement.

RESULTS: Among tobacco-documented deaths, PH mortality showed no clear linear change (annual percent change, 0.50%; 95% confidence interval (CI), -1.55% to 2.59%), whereas benchmark mortality declined (-4.83%; 95% CI, -5.51% to -4.15%). The PH-to-benchmark rate ratio increased 5.59% annually (ratio of annual rate ratios, 1.056; 95% CI, 1.035-1.078; p = 0.001). The unrestricted estimate was nearly identical (1.056; 95% CI, 1.032-1.080).

CONCLUSIONS: Recent PH mortality diverged from improving COPD and lung-cancer mortality. Because the unrestricted comparison yielded a nearly identical estimate, the divergence cannot be considered tobacco-specific. Death certificates cannot establish smoking exposure, PH phenotype, or causality.

articles.title: Bacterial neonatal conjunctivitis in a neonatal intensive care unit: incidence, aetiology, predictors, and antimicrobial resistance.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the incidence, aetiology, risk factors, and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of pathogens associated with NC in a Brazilian NICU.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included neonates admitted to a NICU between January 2015 and June 2022. The research team conducted daily surveillance through systematic medical record reviews using standardized data collection forms and case definitions based on National Healthcare Safety Network criteria.

RESULTS: Among 1,013 neonates, 12.3% developed bacterial conjunctivitis, with onset occurring at a median of 14 days of life (IQR: 9-19). Multivariable analysis identified prior peripherally inserted central catheter use and prolonged NICU stay as significant predictors of NC. Of the 140 bacterial isolates, 62.1% were Gram-positive bacteria (GPB), predominantly Staphylococcus epidermidis (43.7%), whereas 37.9% were Gram-negative bacteria (GNB), mainly Serratia marcescens (24.5%). Oxacillin resistance was detected in 64.6% of GPB, while multidrug resistance was identified in 5.7% of GNB. Ciprofloxacin eye drops showed high in vitro activity against the tested pathogens and were the most frequently used treatment. Neonates with conjunctivitis had a longer median hospital stay than those without conjunctivitis (30 vs. 9 days).

CONCLUSIONS: Bacterial conjunctivitis was common among neonates admitted to the NICU and was predominantly associated with GPB, including oxacillin-resistant isolates. Ciprofloxacin showed high in vitro activity against the tested pathogens. Strengthening infection prevention and control measures and surveillance may help reduce the burden of neonatal conjunctivitis.

articles.title: Positive serum Herpes simplex virus type 1 IgM antibodies are associated with increased risk of post-stroke cognitive impairment after acute ischemic stroke: a prospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) frequently disables survivors of ischemic stroke. Whether herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) reactivation contributes is unknown.

METHODS: In a prospective single-center cohort (2021-2024), 212 consecutive patients with first-ever acute ischemic stroke had admission serum HSV-1-IgM measured within 48 h. PSCI was Montreal Cognitive Assessment < 22 at 12 months (6-month interim assessment). COVID-19 exposure was recorded for all enrollees (91.5% prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, 96.7% spike-IgG positive). Analysis used multivariable logistic regression, Spearman correlation, ROC and bootstrap validation. .

RESULTS: Twelve-month PSCI occurred in 32.5% (69/212), more often with HSV-1-IgM positivity (51.8% vs 25.6%, p < 0.001). HSV-1-IgM positivity was independently associated with PSCI (adjusted OR 2.85, 95% CI 1.29-6.26, p = 0.009), consistently at 6 months and after adjustment for homocysteine and inflammatory markers (OR 2.62, 95% CI 1.06-6.48). HSV-2 seropositivity was 20.3%, with a borderline association with PSCI (p = 0.068) not surviving multiple-comparison correction. HSV-1-IgM predicted PSCI (AUC 0.788, 95% CI 0.727-0.846; Youden cutoff 0.73 PEIU/mL, 78.3% sensitivity, 69.9% specificity).      .

CONCLUSIONS: Recent HSV-1 reactivation is independently associated with 12-month PSCI. Serum HSV-1-IgM is a candidate risk-stratification biomarker, but the cutoff requires external validation.

articles.title: JAK/STAT signaling in allergic airway inflammation: from effector cytokines to pathogenic immune memory and disease-modifying therapy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Allergic airway inflammation is defined by a persistent immune memory but is usually treated as acute and reversible inflammation. Glucocorticoids and biologics control symptoms well, yet relapse follows withdrawal, indicating that current therapy suppresses effector cytokines without removing the memory that re-initiates disease. Most pro-allergic cytokines signal through the shared Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) pathway.

AREAS COVERED: Based on PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library searches from inception to 2026, we describe the signaling modules and networks that generate acute inflammation, then examine a less discussed second output in which the same pathway is proposed to establish and preserve pathogenic memory through local IgE class switching by lung-resident memory B cells, tissue-resident memory T cells, and the breakdown of regulatory B cell tolerance. Strategies are judged by whether they modify disease rather than only control symptoms.

EXPERT OPINION: Inhaled JAK inhibitors have not yet demonstrated airway target engagement in humans; trials should report local p-STAT6 inhibition rather than exhaled nitric oxide alone. Disease modification should be defined by relapse-free interval after withdrawal, not by symptom scores during treatment, with circulating type 2 memory B cells as the most tractable candidate readout.

articles.title: Erratum to "A Glass Half-Full: Physical Activity Discussions Between Health Care Professionals and Patients With Atrial Fibrillation" Canadian Journal of Cardiology Volume 42, Issue 11, November 2026, Pages 2732-2743. DOI: 10.1016/j.cjca.2026.04.007.
Infant mortality due to congenital heart disease in Brazil: a nationwide study of regional inequality and diagnostic imprecision, 2010-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of congenital anomaly-related deaths. In Brazil, a country marked by heterogeneous access to specialized care, mortality due to CHD may reflect disease severity and regional differences in diagnosis, screening, and treatment.

METHODS: The authors characterized temporal trends, regional and federative-unit patterns of CHD-related infant mortality in Brazil from 2010 to 2024 using data from the Mortality Information System (SIM) and Live Birth Information System (SINASC). The primary case definition was restricted to ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Temporal trends were evaluated via Prais-Winsten regression and linear regression with Newey-West standard errors to calculate the Annual Percent Change (APC) and 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, Brazil recorded 45,543 CHD deaths in children under one year (108.3 deaths per 100,000 live births). The Central-West and the Southeast had the highest and the lowest regional rates (125.70 and 104.38 per 100,000). National mortality notification increased (APC was 0.623%; 95% CI: 0.201 - 1.047; p = 0.012), with significant increases in the North (APC, 2.363%; p < 0.001) and Northeast (APC, 0.994%; p = 0.007), while other regions remained stationary. Over half of the deaths occurred in the neonatal period (52.8%).

CONCLUSION: Infant mortality notification due to CHD in Brazil increased from 2010 to 2024, showing marked regional inequalities. Rising trends in the North and Northeast and the high proportion of post-neonatal deaths suggest that delayed diagnosis, referral limitations, continuity-of-care gaps, and diagnostic imprecision in death certification influence preventable mortality.

articles.title: Developmental hemostasis and coagulation disorders in neonates and infants: diagnostic challenges and modern clinical management.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To provide an updated overview of developmental hemostasis, diagnostic methodologies, hereditary and acquired coagulation diseases, and novel laboratory instruments pertinent to neonatal and infant care.

SOURCES: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar. The review included relevant original studies, reviews, guidelines, and consensus statements on developmental hemostasis, neonatal coagulation abnormalities, thrombosis, and laboratory diagnostics.

SUMMARY OF THE FINDINGS: Coagulation factors, natural anticoagulants, fibrinolysis, platelet function, and fibrin structure change with gestational and postnatal age. Prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen, platelet count, and D-dimer therefore require age- and assay-appropriate interpretation. The review distinguished inherited bleeding disorders from acquired coagulopathies, including disseminated intravascular coagulation, vitamin K deficiency bleeding, and sepsis-associated coagulopathy. It also discussed neonatal thrombosis and the complementary roles of thromboelastography, rotational thromboelastometry, and thrombin-generation testing.

CONCLUSIONS: Accurate recognition of coagulation abnormalities in neonates depends on understanding developmental hemostasis and using age-appropriate laboratory reference ranges. Clinical findings should be interpreted together with conventional coagulation tests and, where appropriate, newer diagnostic methods.

articles.title: Rapid Determination of multi-VOCs in breath using Vernier quantum-cascade laser spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: We present a fully integrated, portable spectrometer based on Vernier-tuned quantum-cascade laser (QCL), developed for real-time measurement of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath. A dedicated overflow-based breath-inlet interface provides stable and reproducible sampling by minimizing gas-exchange delays and preventing water condensation, while enabling automated segmentation of diagnostically relevant phases of individual exhalations either through flow- or CO2-triggering. To address quantification in congested mid-infrared spectra, we developed an automated sliding-window selection algorithm based on a hierarchical search strategy. The algorithm identifies narrow spectral regions with high specificity for a target analyte and low contributions from spectral interferences, thereby reducing dependence on subjective spectral-window selection and enabling robust and reproducible procedure for quantification. The analytical workflow was validated through controlled spiking experiments with limits of quantification ranging from 6-200 ppb for the VOCs investigated. Real-time breath measurements in individual volunteers are presented as proof-of-concept demonstrations of the platform's ability to monitor different breath VOCs and their temporal dynamics in complex gas matrices. The measurements include a biphasic postprandial methanol response following fruit consumption and prolonged washout of the asthma-inhaler propellant 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a). The high temporal resolution additionally resolves intra-breath VOC profiles, providing information on differences in the temporal behavior of endogenous and exogenously induced contributions. Overall, the combination of Vernier-QCL spectroscopy with automated spectral-window selection and controlled breath sampling provides a compact and robust approach to time-resolved multi-VOC quantification in human breath and establishes a basis for further development toward clinical breath-research applications.

articles.title: Modeling of novel converging beam radiotherapy system in Geant4 Monte Carlo simulation.
articles.abstract: Purpose. A Geant4-based model was created to simulate radiation transport within a novel radiotherapy system developed by Convergent Radiotherapy and Radiosurgery (Convergent RnR; Haifa, Israel). This treatment device incorporates a Bragg-diffraction x-ray lens to focus x-rays from a conventional x-ray tube towards a small but finite focal spot with quasi-monoenergetic photons.Methods.The simulation model included an x-ray tube and a CRnR focusing lens consisting of single-crystal aluminum tiles. To validate the Geant4 model of this device, transverse and longitudinal in-air and in-water dose distributions from the converging beam field were calculated and compared to radiochromic film measurements.Results.The implemented Monte Carlo (MC) simulation model predicted a mean photon energy of 53.96 keV and showed agreement within 0.5% when compared with the SpekPy calculation. Both the simulation and experiment produced an attenuation characteristics of 3.2 mm Al. In-water tissue maximum ratios showed percentage differences ⩽3% at depths of 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70 mm. Exceptions were observed at 80, and 85 mm, likely due to reduced film statistics, local dose variations, and positioning uncertainty. A gamma analysis of in-water scanning dose distributions demonstrated a >96% pass rate for the 2%/2 mm criterion and >99% for the 3%/3 mm criterion across all focal depths.Conclusions.In this study, CRnR's converging beam radiotherapy system was implemented in Geant4 to demonstrate the device operation and characterize its physical and dosimetric outputs. The MC simulation implemented in this work successfully demonstrated converging dose distributions with Bragg-diffraction physics, which were in good agreement with radiochromic film measurements. This simulation model may be used to further refine the converging beam system design for clinical implementation, including validation of the treatment planning system.

articles.title: Computational fluid dynamics analysis of percutaneous left ventricular assist device support modes on ventricular hemodynamics and hemocompatibility.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous left ventricular assist devices (PLVADs) provide cardiac support in heart failure, yet the hemodynamic effects of varying support levels and the balance between ventricular unloading and blood trauma remain unclear. This study employed numerical simulations to analyze a PLVAD-supported left ventricle under three pump speeds: low, high, and normal control. Analysis encompassed both conventional hemodynamic parameters (e.g. TAWSS, oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT)) and validated mathematical model. Results showed that PLVAD support enlarged the vortex core and increased vorticity in the left ventricle, while reducing them at the aortic outlet. It effectively lowered ventricular wall pressure-achieving unloading-but also decreased aortic outlet WSS. Furthermore, PLVAD elevated OSI and endothelial cell activation potential while reducing TAWSS and RRT, effects that intensified at higher speeds. Increased speed also raised non-physiological scalar shear stress (SSS) and platelet activation, significantly increasing the hemolysis index in the rotational domain and elevating blood damage risk in the ventricular chamber compared to normal physiology. In conclusion, while PLVAD effectively unloads the ventricle, it impairs flow pulsatility and hemocompatibility. Controlling high-speed-induced SSS and platelet activation is critical to mitigate hemolysis. Monitoring hemocompatibility indicators-especially in the apical and aortic outlet regions-is essential due to their link with thrombosis and adverse events.

articles.title: Multiple Chemical Class-Based Potent VEGFR2 Inhibitors as Anticancer Therapeutics: Structure-Activity Relationship and Chemicobiological Interactions Studies.
articles.abstract: Angiogenesis regulation is associated with disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, atherosclerosis, and cancer. Tumor development and metastasis are directly affected by tumor angiogenesis. In addition to tumor cells, host cells produce pro- and anti-angiogenic molecules that regulate tumor angiogenesis. VEGFs and their receptor, VEGFR2 (KDR), strongly influence angiogenesis. When activated, KDR undergoes autophosphorylation, which ultimately promotes endothelial cell proliferation, tumor angiogenesis, tumor growth, and metastasis. Overexpression of VEGFR2 has been observed in various cancer types, including hepatocellular carcinoma, renal carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer. Researchers have developed several VEGFR2 inhibitors over the past few decades. This review examines the structure-activity relationships (SARs) of several recently developed chemical classes, including chalcones, quinazolines, pyridines, pyrimidines, thiadiazoles, indazoles, triazoles, quinoxalines, and pyrazoles, as VEGFR2 inhibitors, with an emphasis on anticancer activity. We also analyze the chemico-biological interaction profiles of several small-molecule VEGFR2 inhibitors. This review article provides an overview of the latest advances in medicinal chemistry approaches to VEGFR2 inhibitors.

articles.title: Space-by-time semi-NMF: a decomposition approach for single-trial neural decoding.
articles.abstract: Objective.The activity of populations of sensory neurons is assumed to encode stimulus information across both spatial and temporal dimensions, reflecting differences in tuning across neurons and variations in their responses over time. With the rapid expansion of simultaneously recorded neural populations in electrophysiological experiments, there is an increasing demand for analytical frameworks capable of compactly capturing this multidimensional sensory information within single-trial population activity, particularly under conditions of high baseline activity.Approach.To address this, we developed a novel analytical method that decomposes neural activity into spatial firing patterns (co-firing neuron ensembles), temporal firing patterns (temporal dynamics of these groups of neurons), and trial-dependent activation coefficients (strength of recruitment of such firing patterns on each trial). This method extends the space-by-time nonnegative matrix factorization (SbT-NMF), a tensor decomposition that imposes nonnegativity constraints on all factorized matrices and is suitable for inherently nonnegative data such as neural activity by relaxing the nonnegativity constraint on one matrix. This modification enables the application of an important baseline correction, which involves subtracting prestimulus activity from the data. As a result, the input may contain negative values, reflecting deviations from baseline and thereby reducing the influence of ongoing activity before the stimulus.Main results.We applied this refined method to primary visual cortex data from the Allen Brain Institute and found that SbT-semi NMF (660.7%) achieved a 32% relative increase in stimulus decoding performance over the original SbT-NMF (501.4%).Significance.These findings highlight the importance of accounting for baseline correction to achieve compact and linearly decodable low-dimensional representation of neural population dynamics in our proposed frameworks.

articles.title: Principal component analysis in analytical chemistry: finding patterns in complex data.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Modern analytical instruments routinely generate datasets with hundreds or thousands of measured variables per sample, far too many to examine by eye or with simple univariate statistics. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is the most widely used method for making sense of such data. It reduces a complex, high-dimensional dataset to a small number of new summary variables, called principal components, which capture the most important patterns of variation. These can be plotted and inspected visually, allowing the analyst to spot clusters of similar samples, detect outliers and identify which measured variables are driving the differences between groups. This Technical Brief explains what PCA is, how it works, the contexts in which it is most useful, and what software is available to carry it out.

articles.title: Dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman immunoassay for simultaneous determination of atrial-fibrillation-associated NT-proBNP and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I in artificial serum.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation is associated with myocardial wall stress and low-grade injury, yet parallel measurement of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) generally requires separate immunoassays. We developed a single-chamber, dual-channel surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) immunoassay that combines antibody-functionalised magnetic capture beads with Au@Ag nanotags encoded by 4-mercaptobenzonitrile at 2227 cm-1 and 4-mercaptobenzoic acid at 1077 cm-1. A 9 × 9 full-factorial calibration design spanning 0-10 000 pg per mL NT-proBNP and 0-500 pg per mL hs-cTnI was executed across three independently prepared tag lots. Ten spatial spectra were aggregated at the sample level, preprocessed and quantified by a batch-grouped partial least-squares model. Limits of detection were 6.30 pg mL-1 for NT-proBNP and 0.46 pg mL-1 for hs-cTnI; corresponding limits of quantification were 18.7 and 1.35 pg mL-1. Across matrix lots and concentration levels, recoveries were 93.1-107.8% and total coefficients of variation were 4.8-9.4%. Thirty-six independently prepared, blinded artificial-serum specimens representing four dual-biomarker phenotypes were compared with electrochemiluminescence and chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassays. Under an equal-error-variance assumption, Deming slopes were 0.963 and 1.012, concordance correlation coefficients were 0.9951 and 0.9930, and concentration-quadrant agreement was 35/36. Grouped validation and specimen-level comparison assessed the dual readout without treating spatial spectra as independent replicates. This architecture provides a controlled route to simultaneous cardiac-biomarker measurement in artificial serum.

articles.title: Magnetic bead-assisted DSN/CRISPR-Cas12a fluorescence biosensor for sensitive and specific detection of miRNA-122.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: MicroRNA-122 (miR-122) is a liver-enriched miRNA closely associated with hepatic disorders, making its sensitive detection crucial for liver disease-related biomarker analysis. Herein, we report a magnetic bead-assisted duplex-specific nuclease (DSN) cleavage strategy coupled with CRISPR/Cas12a fluorescence biosensing for sensitive miR-122 detection. A biotinylated DNA probe containing both a miR-122 recognition region and a Cas12a activator region was immobilized on streptavidin-modified magnetic beads. Upon target hybridization, DSN selectively cleaved the RNA/DNA duplex, releasing the DNA activator while enabling miR-122 recycling. After magnetic separation, the released activator triggered Cas12a-mediated trans-cleavage of a fluorophore-quencher-labeled ssDNA reporter, generating a fluorescence turn-on signal. Under optimized conditions, the biosensor showed a linear response from 100 fM to 10 nM, with a detection limit of 85 fM. The assay exhibited high specificity against mismatched sequences and other miRNAs, and achieved satisfactory recoveries (93.0-95.3%, RSD < 8%) in 10% human serum. This magnetic bead-assisted DSN/CRISPR-Cas12a fluorescence biosensor provides a simple, sensitive, and specific platform for miR-122 detection, holding promise for liver disease-related diagnostic applications.

articles.title: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of microplastics in chicken based on portable near-infrared spectroscopy and interpretable machine learning.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Portable near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with interpretable machine learning was employed for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of polypropylene (PP), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) in chicken. A total of 244 samples were prepared, including pure chicken and PP-, PVC-, and PET-spiked chicken (61 samples per type, mass fractions: 0.01-0.8%). NIR spectra were acquired over 900-1700 nm. After optimal preprocessing and outlier removal via Monte Carlo cross-validation (MCCV), competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) was selected over the successive projections algorithm (SPA) for characteristic wavelength extraction prior to modeling. For qualitative analysis, a data-driven soft independent modeling of class analogy (DD-SIMCA) model was constructed, achieving sensitivities of 85.71-92.86% and specificities of 82.93-100%. For quantitative analysis, the optimal model varied with microplastic (MP) type: CARS-SVR (support vector regression) for PET (Rp2 = 0.8923, RPD = 3.0468); CARS-ElasticNet for PP (Rp2 = 0.8267, RPD = 2.4022), and CARS-PLS (partial least squares) for PVC (Rp2 = 0.8969, RPD = 3.0397). SHAP-based interpretability analysis was further employed to quantify each wavelength's spectral contribution and identify MP-specific absorption bands. This study innovatively integrates portable NIR spectroscopy with SHAP-based interpretable machine learning for MP detection in chicken and demonstrates the potential of this strategy for rapid on-site screening of MP contamination in poultry products.

articles.title: Silencing FGL2 alleviates rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury by activating the Nrf2 signaling to suppress ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury (RM-AKI) is a primary complication of rhabdomyolysis with increasing incidence and poor prognosis. Emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of RM-AKI. Fibrinogen-like protein 2 (FGL2) has been reported as a contributor to RM-AKI, yet its potential role in ferroptosis regulation and the precise mechanisms remain elusive. We found that FGL2 expression was increased in kidney tissues from glycerol (Gly)-induced mice and in myoglobin (Myo)-stimulated HK-2 cells. In vivo, FGL2 knockout attenuated Gly-mediated renal dysfunction, ferroptosis, and inflammation. In vitro, FGL2 knockdown enhanced cell viability, suppressed ferroptosis (reduced ROS, lipid peroxidation, MDA, and Fe2+; increased GSH, GPX4, and xCT), and diminished TNF-α and IL-1β release in Myo-treated HK-2 cells, whereas FGL2 overexpression produced the opposite effects. Notably, the detrimental effects of FGL2 overexpression were specifically reversed by the ferroptosis inhibitor Fer-1, confirming ferroptosis as the primary downstream pathway. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays revealed a direct physical interaction between FGL2 and Keap1. FGL2 knockdown decreased Keap1 protein levels and inhibited Nrf2 ubiquitination, thereby increasing Nrf2 expression and its nuclear accumulation and activating Nrf2 signaling in Myo-treated HK-2 cells. Moreover, Nrf2 inhibition or knockdown abolished the protective effects of FGL2 knockdown, while Nrf2 overexpression counteracted FGL2 overexpression-induced injury exacerbation. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that FGL2 interacts with Keap1 to promote Nrf2 ubiquitination, thereby suppressing Nrf2 signaling and driving ferroptosis and inflammation in RM-AKI, suggesting that targeting FGL2 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for this disease.

articles.title: Developmental sleep during lethargus is associated with metabolic homeostasis and heritable adaptive responses to infection in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.abstract: Sleep is a fundamental physiological state essential for metabolic and neuronal homeostasis; however, its contribution to lipid and energy metabolism during development remains incompletely understood. Here, we used Caenorhabditis elegans to investigate the metabolic significance of Developmentally Timed Sleep (DTS). Lethargus-associated DTS was mechanically disrupted using 1 kHz piezoelectric buzzer-induced mechanical stimulation, followed by behavioural, physiological, metabolic and molecular analyses. DTS disruption was associated with reduced behavioural quiescence, altered sleep-associated gene expression, reduced survival and elevated oxidative stress. Notably, disruption during the L4-young adult lethargus window was associated with increased feeding and markedly enhanced lipid accumulation, accompanied by upregulation of the lipid metabolic regulators fat-6, nhr-64 and nhr-80. Despite increased lipid storage, levels of the triglyceride lipase ATGL were elevated, suggesting enhanced lipid mobilization concurrent with persistent lipid accumulation. This metabolic phenotype was accompanied by reduced mitochondrial activity, decreased intracellular ATP, downregulation of atp-3 and activation of AMPK-mediated energy sensing, suggesting energetic stress and potentially inefficient downstream utilization of mobilized lipids. DTS disruption was additionally associated with increased acy-1 and crh-1 expression and enhanced CREB phosphorylation, indicating altered cAMP-CREB-associated neuronal signalling. Furthermore, disruption of DTS in offspring of Salmonella Typhi-infected parents was associated with reduction in their ability to generate heritable adaptive resistance and altered daf-16, sgk-1 and skn-1 mRNA expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that developmental sleep may play a role in lipid storage, mobilization, mitochondrial bioenergetics and cellular energy sensing, with potential consequences for neuronal and adaptive stress responses.

articles.title: Stabilizing the plaque: does intensive medical treatment modify coronary atherosclerosis in women with INOCA?
Decoding the cellular and paracrine landscape of epicardial adipose tissue-myocardial crosstalk in coronary artery disease.
Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.

METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

articles.title: tsRNAs in HCC: Biology, liquid biopsy and therapy.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, and there is an urgent need for non-invasive diagnostic tools and effective treatments. Transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are a novel class of small non-coding RNAs generated by site-specific cleavage of transfer RNAs. This review summarizes the biogenesis, classification and biological functions of tsRNAs, focusing on their roles in HCC. tsRNAs contribute to multiple cancer hallmarks, including proliferation, resistance to apoptosis, immune modulation, angiogenesis, metastasis, and metabolic reprogramming, through the regulation of signaling pathways, epigenetic control, and translational regulation. Because tsRNAs are highly stable in body fluids, they represent promising liquid biopsy markers. Several specific tsRNAs have shown excellent diagnostic performance, with area under the curve (AUC) values above 0.84 and improved sensitivity when combined with conventional markers such as alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Preclinical evidence using antagomirs or agomirs to target oncogenic or tumor-suppressive tsRNAs has demonstrated encouraging anti-tumor effects in HCC models. tsRNAs are emerging as valuable diagnostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for HCC. Clinical translation still faces challenges including low delivery efficiency, off-target effects, and a lack of standardized protocols. Future efforts should focus on unified nomenclature, standardized detection methods, and combination strategies with immunotherapy and targeted therapy to advance precision hepatology.

articles.title: Unequal survival after ischaemic heart disease in Eastern Europe: a sex-specific GBD 2023 analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sex disparities in ischaemic heart disease (IHD) outcomes are well documented in Western Europe but remain poorly characterized across Eastern Europe a region marked by substantial mortality inequalities. We aimed to determine whether population-level case fatality among individuals living with IHD differed by sex in Eastern Europe and to identify modifiable risk factors associated with disparities.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed sex-specific estimates from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study for seven Eastern European countries. Age-standardized IHD mortality and prevalence rates were combined to derive mortality-to-prevalence ratios (MPRs) as a measure of population-level case fatality. Risk factor-attributable mortality was similarly normalized to prevalence. Estonia, which had the lowest MPRs (men 3.00%; women 1.77%), served as the benchmark for Z-score analyses (|Z| ≥ 1.96 = P < 0.05). In 2011 women in five of six countries had higher MPRs than Estonian women (Z = 2.25-4.35), whereas men showed excess MPRs in only 3 countries (Z = 2.29-3.18). By 2023 all six countries showed higher female MPRs than Estonia (Z = 3.27-5.14). In men excess MPRs persisted in Latvia the Russian Federation and Ukraine (Z = 2.48-3.16) and emerged in Belarus (Z = 4.79) but remained non-significant in Lithuania and the Republic of Moldova. Female-specific benchmark signals were observed for high fasting plasma glucose in Belarus and the Republic of Moldova, and for high systolic blood pressure in Lithuania, the Republic of Moldova, and the Russian Federation.

CONCLUSIONS: Pronounced sex disparities in IHD population-level case fatality persist across Eastern Europe. Lithuania and the Republic of Moldova showed the most consistent female disadvantage. Excess female population-level case fatality was most consistently associated with key modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Nutritional interventions' impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings.
articles.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

articles.title: Improved plaque composition from intensive medical treatment in women with angina and non-obstructive coronary disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Among women with suspected ischaemia and non-obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA), the temporal effect of combination intensive medical treatment (IMT) with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors or receptor blockers, statins, and aspirin on coronary plaque composition is not known. This prospective ancillary study examined changes in atherosclerotic plaque volumes and composition (percentage of total plaque volume) over time between IMT and usual care (UC).

METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants from the randomized WARRIOR trial with the presence of plaque on their first coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) were enrolled for a follow-up CCTA at least 2 years after randomization. Volumes and volumetric composition (percentage of total plaque volume) of non-calcified plaque (NCP), low-density NCP (LD-NCP, defined as NCP <30 HU), and calcified plaque (CP) were quantified over the coronary tree in the serial scans.Participants (n = 186) completed both scans with good image quality (94 IMT arm and 92 UC arm). Overall mean age was 61.0 years (SD ±10.9), and there were no statistically significant differences in baseline risk factors, plaque volumes, or statin treatment between the arms.There was a greater bi-annualized increase in CP volume [ΔCP volume (mm3)] in the IMT arm, 6.2 (SD ±15.5) compared to the UC arm, 3.9 (SD ±16.0), P = 0.013, and a consistent greater reduction in NCP composition [ΔNCP composition (%)] in the IMT arm, -3.9 (SD ±7.7) compared to the UC arm, -1.5 (SD ±5.8), P = 0.003, with no increase in total plaque volume.

CONCLUSION: In women with suspected INOCA, IMT reduces NCP volumetric composition to a greater extent than UC and may promote plaque stabilization.

articles.title: Growth hormone and ageing cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: The age-related decline in growth hormone (GH) secretion, termed the somatopause, parallels the structural and functional deterioration of the ageing heart. How this endocrine withdrawal translates into myocardial failure at the molecular level remains incompletely mapped. GH/insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) signalling acts via phosphoinositide 3-kinase/Akt/mechanistic target of rapamycin and Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase/c-Myc cascades on four processes central to cardiac ageing: Akt-dependent nuclear retention of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), established primarily in non-cardiomyocyte models; peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator 1α (PGC-1α)-driven mitochondrial biogenesis; suppression of the p53/p16INK4a senescence programme; and metabolic-epigenetic regulation of cell-cycle competence via α-ketoglutarate/lysine demethylase 5 and Jumonji domain-containing protein 3 chromatin gating. In mouse cardiomyocytes, positive transcription elongation factor b is rate limiting for Myc-driven proliferation, plausibly explaining why adult cardiomyocytes retain latent cell-cycle machinery yet rarely divide. A candidate GH-releasing hormone receptor-hypoxia-inducible factor 1α axis, supported by a single recent experimental study, is examined as an emerging hypothesis for cell-type-selective cardioprotection independent of systemic GH. We integrate these strands along a single tractable axis: IGF-1/Akt/TERT/p53/PGC-1α with metabolic-epigenetic modulation. The 2025 Marra trial (NCT03775993; 64 randomized, 45 completers; surrogate and functional endpoints not powered for clinical events) reports that physiological GH restoration improves peak VO2 (+3.1 vs. -1.8 mL/kg/min, P < 0.01), New York Heart Association class, and quality of life in heart failure (HF) with confirmed GH deficiency. A meta-analysis of 25 studies quantifies the U-shaped IGF-1-HF relationship, with the HF vs. control IGF-1 difference derived from six of those studies. Plasma proteomic organ-ageing signatures show accelerated cardiac ageing is associated with 2.5-fold heart-failure risk. We present a hypothesis-generating framework identifying GH/IGF-1 axis restoration as a candidate determinant of heart-failure progression, warranting event-driven confirmation.

articles.title: Beyond the vessel wall: single-cell dissection of epicardial fat-myocardial crosstalk in coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) has emerged as an active regulator of cardiovascular disease, yet the cellular and molecular features of myocardial-associated EAT (mEAT) in coronary artery disease (CAD) remain incompletely defined.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of mEAT from patients with CAD (n = 9), nonCAD cardiovascular surgery patients (n = 9), and forensic controls without cardiac disease (n = 2), integrated with histology, CT-based EAT volume assessment, matched right atrial myocardium analysis, and functional in vitro assays. mEAT contained diverse adipocyte, stromal, immune, and vascular cell populations. In CAD, we identified two disease-enriched inflammatory cell states, inflammatory adipogenic cells (IAC) and inflammatory stromal cells (ISC), characterized by immune activation, stress-response signalling, extracellular matrix remodelling, and impaired adipogenic features. Histological analyses confirmed enlarged adipocytes, increased fibrosis, and higher abundance of IAC/ISC-associated markers in CAD-mEAT. Exploratory integration with CT imaging suggested a possible association between increased EAT volume and enrichment of inflammatory cell states. Comparative analyses with published adipose and cardiac single-cell datasets indicated that IAC and ISC share features with previously described inflammatory adipocyte and stromal populations, while displaying a distinct marker combination enriched in CAD-associated mEAT.Cell-cell communication analyses identified THBS1-CD36 and SEMA4A/SEMA3C-NRP1/PLXNA signalling as predicted CAD-associated communication axes involving inflammatory mEAT populations and myocardial cell types. Conditioned medium from CAD-mEAT-derived adipocytes/IAC altered contractile properties of human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte (CM) microtissues, while simultaneously impairing endothelial tube formation and migration. Recombinant THBS1 and SEMA3C partially recapitulated selected effects, whereas combined CD36 and NRP1 blockade partially attenuated endothelial and CM responses.

CONCLUSION: Together, these data provide a high-resolution map of CAD-associated mEAT remodelling and identify IAC and ISC as inflammatory cell states linked to altered adipose-vascular and adipose-myocardial signalling. These findings support the concept that cellular and molecular features of mEAT may complement imaging-based EAT assessment and inform future studies on CAD-associated adipose tissue inflammation.

articles.title: Placental growth factor in pulmonary hypertension: addressing the angiogenesis paradox via immune remodelling.
JAK3 regulates PIP5K expression and promotes PIP2 generation and Ca2+-driven platelet activation in arterial thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Phospholipase C evoked increases in intracellular Ca2+ levels are a prerequisite for platelet activation and subsequent thrombosis. The protein tyrosine kinase Janus kinase 3 regulates phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate levels in platelets, thereby significantly mediating activation-dependent platelet function and arterial thrombosis.

articles.title: Spatial heterogeneity of APD under long QT conditions: characterization and relationship to sinus activation sequence.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Enhanced spatial variation in ventricular action potential duration (APD) is known to contribute to arrhythmia development under long QT conditions, although the causes of APD variation are unclear. Specifically, between-individual variation in the locations of pro-arrhythmic long APD islands and associated repolarization gradients is difficult to explain in the context of established regional variation in electrophysiology. This study aimed to explore the mechanisms underlying the spatial heterogeneity of ventricular APD under baseline and long QT conditions.

METHODS AND RESULTS: New Zealand White rabbit hearts (n = 26) were Langendorff-perfused with oxygenated Tyrode's solution and loaded with blebbistatin and FluoVolt. Optical mapping of transmembrane voltage from the anterior epicardial surface of the right (RV) and left ventricles (LV) during sinus rhythm revealed a strong inverse relationship between activation time and APD90 in all hearts (linear regression slope: -0.85 ± 0.17, r2: 0.60 ± 0.12, P < 0.0001), despite considerable between-heart variation in the activation sequence. Lengthening of the pacing cycle length (350-1000 ms) and dofetilide-induced IKr blockade each induced greater AP prolongation in ventricular sites with earlier sinus activation, contributing to increased spatial heterogeneity of APD90. Optical measurement of APD90 from cardiomyocytes isolated after optical mapping of the intact heart indicated that myocytes from ventricular sites with earlier sinus activation had longer intrinsic APD90. Isolated RV myocytes also exhibited shorter average APD90 than LV myocytes. Measurement of the mRNA levels of 22 genes encoding cardiac ion channel, transporter and regulatory proteins demonstrated that ventricular sites with distinct sinus activation times exhibit different gene expression profiles. With increasing sinus activation time, the mRNA levels of Scn5a and most repolarization genes decreased while that of Kcnip2 increased.

CONCLUSION: Ventricular sites with distinct sinus activation times exhibit different electrophysiological properties which contribute to enhanced spatial heterogeneity of APD under long QT conditions.

articles.title: DNMT3A-driven clonal haematopoiesis induces semaphorin 4A-dependent endothelial activation in heart failure.
Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Intermediate-High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether catheter-directed thrombolysis improves clinical outcomes in patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, as compared with anticoagulation alone, is uncertain.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we randomly assigned patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism (defined by hemodynamic stability, a simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index score of ≥1, and right ventricular dysfunction plus an elevated level of cardiac troponin or natriuretic peptide) in a 1:1 ratio to receive catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy (thrombolysis group) or anticoagulation therapy alone (standard-care group). The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, recurrence of pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included clinically relevant bleeding as defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium, major bleeding as defined in the Global Use of Strategies to Open Occluded Coronary Arteries guidelines, and intracranial hemorrhage.

RESULTS: A total of 558 patients underwent randomization; 280 were assigned to the thrombolysis group, and 278 to the standard-care group. The median age was 64 years, and 40.9% were female. A primary-outcome event occurred in 2 patients (0.7%) in the thrombolysis group and in 19 patients (6.8%) in the standard-care group (relative risk, 0.10; 95% confidence interval, 0.02 to 0.44; P<0.001); this difference was driven mainly by the lower incidence of cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse in the thrombolysis group. By day 7, clinically relevant bleeding had occurred in 13 patients (4.6%) in the thrombolysis group and in 14 patients (5.0%) in the standard-care group (P = 0.85); major bleeding in 4 (1.4%) and 6 (2.2%), respectively (P = 0.54); and intracranial hemorrhage in 2 (0.7%) and none. One patient in the thrombolysis group died within 30 days, and 4 patients in the standard-care group died within 7 days.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism, catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy led to a lower risk of death from any cause, recurrent pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization than anticoagulation therapy alone. (Funded by the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic and others; PRAGUE-26 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05493163; EudraCT number, 2022-002218-18; European Union Clinical Trials number, 2024-516144-25-00.).

articles.title: Eplontersen for Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening disease caused by deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR). Eplontersen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces the production of hepatic TTR. The effect of eplontersen on ATTR-CM is unclear.

METHODS: In this phase 3, international, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with ATTR-CM to receive subcutaneous eplontersen (45 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 140 weeks, in addition to standard treatment. The primary end point was a cumulative composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular clinical events up to week 140. The effect of death from noncardiovascular causes on the primary analysis was assessed with a cumulative composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events up to week 140.

RESULTS: A total of 1432 patients underwent randomization and received at least one dose of the assigned intervention (715 patients in the eplontersen group and 717 in the placebo group). The mean age of the patients was 76.4 years, and 90.6% were men. A total of 381 primary end-point events occurred in 210 patients (29.4%) receiving eplontersen, and 392 events occurred in 231 patients (32.2%) receiving placebo (rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.09; P = 0.28). Death from cardiovascular causes, as a component of the primary end point, occurred in 74 patients in the eplontersen group and in 70 in the placebo group; there were 307 cardiovascular clinical events in the eplontersen group and 322 in the placebo group. The rate ratio for the composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.71 to 1.04). Serious adverse events occurred in 413 patients (57.8%) in the eplontersen group and in 426 (59.4%) in the placebo group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with ATTR-CM, eplontersen therapy did not lead to a lower risk of a composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular events than placebo up to 140 weeks. (Funded by Ionis Pharmaceuticals and AstraZeneca; CARDIO-TTRansform ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04136171.).

articles.title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone enhances platelet activation and arterial thrombosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), elevated in conditions like subclinical hypothyroidism, has been clinically linked to a higher risk of morbidity and mortality in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). Here, we aim to investigate the effects of TSH on CAD-associated platelet activation and arterial thrombosis, along with the underlying mechanisms.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Clinical studies demonstrated that higher TSH levels are associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in CAD patients. In vitro human and mouse platelet function studies found that TSH potentiates agonist-induced platelet aggregation, dense granule adenosine triphosphate release, integrin alpha-IIb beta-3 activation, P-selectin release from α-granules, platelet spreading, and clot retraction. Furthermore, in vivo animal studies demonstrated that TSH enhances thrombosis, whole blood thrombus formation, and middle cerebral artery occlusion-induced brain injury. Mechanistic studies revealed that platelets express the TSH receptor (TSHR). TSH binds to platelet TSHR and activates both the Gs/cAMP/PKA and Gq/Ca2+/PKC/MAPK signalling pathways. Activation of the Gq pathway is more pronounced than that of the Gs pathway, thereby potentiating platelet activation. Finally, our in vivo work showed that TSH aggravates microvascular obstruction and promotes myocardial infarction expansion in a mouse myocardial ischaemia/reperfusion injury model.

CONCLUSION: TSH augments platelet activation and in vivo thrombus formation through engagement of platelet TSHR, subsequently activating downstream signalling cascades involving Gs/cAMP/PKA and Gq/Ca2+/PKC/MAPK pathways.

articles.title: Talquetamab in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: 3-year follow-up of the phase 1/2 MonumenTAL-1 study.
articles.abstract: Talquetamab is the first and only approved bispecific antibody targeting G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D for the treatment of relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma based on results from the phase 1/2 MonumenTAL-1 study. Here, we report efficacy and ongoing safety from MonumenTAL-1 with 3 years of follow-up. Patients naïve to T-cell redirection therapy (TCR) received talquetamab 0.4 mg/kg weekly (n = 143) or 0.8 mg/kg every other week (n = 154); a separate cohort received prior TCR (n = 78; either of the 2 talquetamab doses). Median follow-up was 38, 31, and 30 months in the 3 cohorts, respectively, as of September 2024. Overall response rate was 67% to 74%, and complete response or better rate was 33% to 42%. Median progression-free survival was 7.5, 11.2, and 7.7 months, and median overall survival (OS) was 34.0 months, not reached, and 28.3 months (36-month OS rates, 49.3%, 60.8%, and 44.6%), in the 3 cohorts, respectively. The most common adverse events (AEs) were cytokine release syndrome (73%-79%; grade 3/4, 0.6%-2.1%), taste changes (72%-76%), and infections (61%-78%; grade 3/4, 21%-26%). Ataxia/balance disorders occurred in 5.3% of patients (no grade 4/5 events). Dose reduction and discontinuation rates due to AEs remained low; no patients died of talquetamab-related AEs. With 3 years of follow-up, talquetamab continued to demonstrate high rates of deep and durable responses. The long-term safety profile was comparable with previous results and continued to show lower risk of high-grade infections relative to approved B-cell maturation antigen-targeting bispecific antibodies. This study was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03399799 (phase 1) and NCT04634552 (phase 2).

articles.title: Placental growth factor promotes endothelial activation and inflammatory remodelling in pulmonary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder marked by pulmonary vascular remodelling and vessel loss, paradoxically occurring despite high vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signalling. While VEGF/VEGF receptor (VEGFR) pathways are implicated in disease pathogenesis, their role in endothelial and immune cell crosstalk remains poorly understood. Placental growth factor (PlGF), a VEGF family member that selectively binds VEGFR-1, exerts pro-inflammatory effects in other pathological contexts, but its contribution to PAH pathophysiology is unclear. This study explored the contribution of PlGF to endothelial activation and immune-mediated vascular remodelling in PAH.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Serum levels of PlGF, VEGF-A, soluble VEGFR-1 (sVEGFR-1), and soluble VEGFR-2 (sVEGFR-2) were measured in 80 treatment-naïve PAH patients from the EFORT cohort and in healthy controls. Their association with survival was then assessed. VEGFR-1 expression was evaluated in human PAH lung tissue. The functional role of PlGF was investigated in Plgf-/- rats exposed to chronic hypoxia or monocrotaline, and in mechanistic studies using primary human pulmonary endothelial cells and monocyte-derived macrophages.Circulating PlGF and sVEGFR-1 were elevated in PAH and associated with worse survival. VEGFR-1 expression was increased in PAH lung endothelium. Genetic deletion of Plgf protected rats from experimental pulmonary hypertension, leading to reduced pulmonary pressures, right ventricular hypertrophy, and vascular remodelling. PlGF deficiency reduced endothelial intercellular adhesion molecule (ICAM)-1/vascular cell adhesion molecule (VCAM)-1 expression, macrophage infiltration, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production (CCL5/RANTES, osteoprotegerin, and LIX/CXCL5). In vitro, PlGF induced endothelial adhesion molecule expression and promoted macrophage polarization towards a pro-remodelling M2-like phenotype.

CONCLUSION: PlGF is upregulated in PAH, its concentration predicts adverse outcomes, and it actively drives vascular remodelling by coupling endothelial activation to immune dysregulation. These findings establish PlGF as both a prognostic biomarker and a promising therapeutic target for PAH.

articles.title: [Homans' sign : useful or obsolete ?].
articles.abstract: Homans' sign is still occasionally documented when deep vein thrombosis is suspected, despite poor diagnostic performance. A hospitalised patient with a negative Homans' sign but marked calf asymmetry; in whom venous ultrasonography confirmed deep vein thrombosis is reported. This case illustrates that Homans' sign should neither confirm nor exclude deep vein thrombosis. Assessment should rely on overall clinical probability and appropriate diagnostic testing.

articles.title: Barriers and facilitators to health behavior change: perspectives of individuals with serious mental illness in health-promoting interventions - a systematic review of qualitative evidence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical health-promoting interventions for individuals with serious mental illness (SMI) have been shown to be clinically effective in improving health outcomes, yet often fall short in meeting participants' needs, as reflected in high dropout rates. However, studies indicate that individuals with SMI want to improve their physical health. To address this need, a detailed understanding of the barriers to and facilitators of health behavior change for individuals with SMI participating in health-promoting interventions is crucial.

METHODS: To identify barriers to and facilitators of health behavior change for individuals with SMI in health promoting interventions, a systematic review of qualitative evidence was conducted. Medline, PsycINFO, CINHAL, and SSCI databases were searched for qualitative studies reporting perspectives on health behavior changes among individuals with SMI (18 +) who participated in health-promoting interventions. Health-promoting interventions were defined as those that included at least two aspects of physical health (such as diet and physical activity). The Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) tool was utilized to assess the quality of the studies. Data were extracted, thematically analyzed, and mapped to the capability, opportunity and motivation for behavior change (COM-B) model.

RESULTS: A total of 4242 references were identified and 27 studies, including 547 individuals with SMI, met the eligibility criteria. The synthesis and interpretation of the findings were informed by the COM-B model. Individuals with SMI reported physical and psychological capabilities that led to improvements in physical and mental health as a result of participating in a health-promoting intervention. Physical and social opportunities, such as clear and coherent intervention content or support from trained professionals, were identified as facilitators of behavior change. Additionaly motivation played a crucial role in sustaining health behavior changes among individuals with SMI.

CONCLUSION: This review identifies key factors shaping health behavior change among individuals with SMI, emphasizing that change often depends more on external opportunities than on individual motivation alone. These findings highlight the importance of accessible, inclusive, and socially supportive interventions, and contribute to the development of integrated, person-centered frameworks for research and practice.

articles.title: Association of electronic versus paper-based documentation with completeness of prehospital emergency physician reports in suspected acute coronary syndrome: a retrospective cohort analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete prehospital documentation supports safe handover, continuity of care, quality assurance, and secondary data use in emergency medical services. This study examined the association between documentation format and record completeness in a physician-staffed prehospital cohort of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS), with particular attention to information relevant to hospital handover.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 2,787 prehospital emergency physician reports for suspected ACS, recorded in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, between 1 January 2014 and 31 December 2018. Six records with implausible dates were excluded before primary analysis. The final analytic cohort therefore comprised 2,781 reports: 2,120 from paper-based documentation (PBD) and 661 from electronic-based documentation (EBD). The primary endpoint was complete documentation of a predefined record set comprising hospital destination, prehospital length of stay, initial and handover systolic and diastolic blood pressure, initial and handover peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2), documentation of a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), and a numeric pain score (NRS). A sensitivity analysis repeated the endpoint without the NRS. Completeness rates were compared using chi-square tests, and adjusted associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression including age, sex, calendar year, and ACS subtype.

RESULTS: Overall record completeness was higher in the EBD group than in the PBD group (90.9% vs. 48.2%; p < 0.001), an absolute difference of 42.7% points. The largest between-group differences involved handover blood pressures, handover SpO2, prehospital length of stay, and 12-lead ECG documentation. In the adjusted model, EBD remained associated with higher odds of a complete record (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 10.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 7.58-14.48; p < 0.001). When the NRS was excluded from the endpoint, completeness remained higher in the EBD group (94.9% vs. 75.6%; aOR 4.40, 95% CI 3.44-5.62; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Electronic documentation was associated with more complete prehospital emergency physician reports in suspected ACS, particularly for handover-relevant variables. However, documentation modality was structurally confounded with treatment site, precluding isolation of an independent technology effect. As this study assessed a process metric rather than clinical outcomes, prospective multicentre studies should determine whether structured electronic documentation improves handover quality, workflow reliability, treatment timeliness, guideline adherence, and patient-centred outcomes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS00036944 (MONAH1 study).

articles.title: Out of hospital cardiac arrest following low voltage electrical injury with complete neurological recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low voltage electrical injuries are generally associated with minimal or no external burns but may cause severe injury, fatal cardiac arrhythmias and respiratory arrest depending on length of exposure, size of individual, environmental humidity and the cross-sectional area in contact with electrical source. Complete neurological recovery after prolonged resuscitation is uncommon.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of 22 years old male who sustained low voltage electrical injury culminating in out of hospital cardiac arrest. He brought to the emergency department within 10 min after the incident. With initial rhythm of asystole. High quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation started immediately according to advanced cardiac life support guideline; the rhythm converted from asystole to ventricular fibrillation after third cycle of resuscitation requiring three defibrillation attempts. Return of spontaneous circulation was achieved at the end of eighth cycle of resuscitation. Subsequently the patient admitted to intensive care unit and post cardiac arrest care were continued which includes mechanical ventilatory support, hemodynamic support, seizure management, fever prevention. The patient showed progressive neurological improvement and discharged home after three days of stay in intensive care unit with complete neurological recovery.

CONCLUSION: This case shows the critical importance of immediate transport to the hospital, early high-quality CPR and comprehensive post cardiac arrest care for patient survival.

articles.title: Risk factors for liver cirrhosis in patients with overlapping SLE and primary biliary cholangitis: a retrospective study.
Data-Driven Methods Supporting Mental Health and Well-Being Service Delivery: Umbrella Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health and well-being services generate substantial operational and client-level data. Review-level evidence on how data-driven methods support service delivery remains fragmented across technologies and settings.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize review-level evidence on data-driven methods relevant to mental health and well-being service delivery, including business intelligence (BI), data visualization, and machine learning (ML), and identify applications, implementation challenges, and evidence gaps.

METHODS: We conducted an umbrella review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020. The original searches of Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and PsycINFO were completed on January 27, 2026. During revision, supplementary PubMed and Embase searches were conducted on September 22, 2026. For both supplementary databases, the search was restricted at the database-search stage to publications from 2021 to the current date and to review/systematic review records; eligibility screening then retained the original January 27, 2026, evidence cutoff. All records were independently screened by 2 reviewers using Covidence (Veritas Health Innovation); the reviewer pair differed between the original and supplementary search phases. Eight structured reviews were critically appraised using the JBI checklist and synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Eight structured reviews were included (3 systematic reviews, 4 scoping reviews, and 1 umbrella review). Seven reviews contributed primary study or source-level evidence, while one umbrella review synthesized 44 reviews. The retrieved evidence was dominated by AI and ML, including conversational agents, natural language processing, and clinical decision support, whereas dedicated BI and operational data visualization syntheses were sparse. Two reviews directly addressed mental health service delivery, 4 were adjacent or partially direct, and 2 were indirect but relevant. Only one review focused specifically on mental health helplines. Service-level benefits were reported more consistently than sustained clinical benefits, although the evidence remained heterogeneous and partly indirect. Safety and implementation concerns included symptom worsening, bias, hallucination, privacy, trust, integration barriers, and inequitable access.

CONCLUSIONS: Review-level evidence relevant to mental health and well-being services is uneven and concentrated on AI/ML. Because the search required all 3 concept blocks, BI- and visualization-focused reviews may have been under-retrieved. BI and operational data visualization, helpline-specific implementation, long-term effectiveness, safety, and equity require more direct and prospective evaluation before findings can be generalized across service settings.

articles.title: Predicting Rheumatoid Arthritis Flares Using Wearable Device Data: Deep Learning Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) flares are common and unpredictable. Current monitoring relies on episodic clinical visits and laboratory testing, thereby limiting the ability to anticipate disease worsening. Wearable devices may support continuous remote monitoring, but models must account for missing real-world data, heterogeneous consumer devices, and the distinction between symptomatic disease activity and systemic inflammation.

OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning (DL) time-series models using wearable-derived physiological data to predict symptomatic and inflammatory RA flares up to 28 days in advance.

METHODS: In a prospective cohort study, adults with RA used a smartwatch (Apple Watch; Apple Inc), a wearable fitness tracker (Fitbit; Google LLC), or a smart ring (Oura Ring; Oura Health Oy). Daily wearable-derived heart rate, heart rate variability, and step-count were harmonized across devices and linked with smartphone-based patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and available C-reactive protein results. Symptomatic flares were defined using longitudinal RAPID3 (Routine Assessment of Patient Index Data 3) scores, and inflammatory flares were defined using a prespecified C-reactive protein threshold.
