Classical machine learning and DL models were trained to predict daily flare vs remission status at 0-, 7-, 14-, 21-, and 28-day horizons. Model evaluation used a temporally ordered 70/30 within-participant train-test split. Performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROCAUC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and participant-level sensitivity. This prediction-model analysis was not prospectively registered.

RESULTS: Forty-nine participants contributed 5624 days of overlapping wearable and clinical data. Participants used Apple Watch (n=31), Fitbit (n=15), or Oura Ring (n=3). DL models outperformed machine learning models using imputed wearable data, with average ROCAUC improvements of 5.3% for symptomatic flares and 18.4% for inflammatory flares, and AUPRC improvements of 9.3% and 44.1%, respectively. For 7-day-ahead prediction, transformer models incorporating wearable-derived physiology and demographic features achieved ROCAUCs of 0.95 for both symptomatic and inflammatory flares, with AUPRCs of 0.92 and 0.91, respectively. Adding daily PRO improved participant-level sensitivity for inflammatory flare prediction from 0.67 to 0.87. Performance remained stable across prediction horizons for up to 4 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Wearable-derived physiological signals analyzed with DL may support personalized forecasting of symptomatic and inflammatory RA flare states weeks in advance. By integrating passive digital biomarkers with PROs, this approach offers a scalable framework for proactive RA monitoring that could help identify disease exacerbations earlier than episodic clinical assessment alone. Further validation in larger, more diverse cohorts and prospective studies is needed to determine whether wearable-guided forecasting improves clinical decision-making, timely intervention, and long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Associations of systemic conditions and antiresorptive medication exposure with peri-implant outcomes: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate associations of selected systemic conditions and antiresorptive exposure with peri-implant outcomes, separating disease associations from treatment response, biomarkers and medication safety.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CENTRAL were searched to 12 July 2026. We synthesised clinical evidence in adults with dental implants narratively by exposure, comparison, and outcome, with design-appropriate appraisal and target-specific GRADE assessment.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261435202.

RESULTS: The reported synthesis comprised 38 studies; one contributed to both osteoporosis and antiresorptive categories. Of 244 reports sought, 170 (69.7%) were not retrieved. Diabetes findings varied across glycaemic, smoking and clinical settings. Some obesity and antiresorptive comparisons reported less favourable outcomes, with confounding and imprecision limiting interpretation. The adjusted antiresorptive-peri-implantitis OR was 3.91 (95% CI 1.29-11.9) in one study. Evidence for cardiovascular, rheumatoid, skeletal and neurological conditions was limited. Eight selected comparative targets had very low certainty. Uncontrolled retention, biomarkers and selected osteonecrosis cases did not establish disease incidence.

CONCLUSIONS: Restrictive searching, retrieval loss and inconsistent exclusion decisions limit completeness and confidence. The evidence cannot establish equivalence to healthy populations, uniform safety or diagnosis-wide contraindications. Osteoporosis and antiresorptive exposure require separate interpretation. No external funding was reported.

articles.title: Atrial Leadless Pacing in Combination with Existing ICD Systems in Long QT Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Long QT syndrome is an inherited or acquired condition characterized by prolonged ventricular repolarization and is characterized by a propensity for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. Management often incorporates beta blockers, which have the greatest effect on reducing arrhythmic risk, and implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD) implantation. Subcutaneous ICDs provide effective defibrillation therapy while avoiding intravascular leads and are an attractive option for patients at high risk of infection or thrombosis, or for younger patients to reduce intravascular lead dwell time. Subcutaneous ICDs provide defibrillation therapy but do not offer pacing and antitachycardia pacing. Leadless pacemakers are often favored for similar reasons, and combined use with ICDs introduces challenges, including device interaction. We report 2 cases of interaction between ICD sensing and atrial leadless pacemakers in long QT syndrome, including a case of S-ICD oversensing, not yet described in the literature, and a comparative case in a transvenous system.

articles.title: TAVR in Membranous Septal Aneurysm: Procedural Strategy and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Membranous septal aneurysm (MSA) is a rare abnormality that can complicate transcatheter aortic valve replacement because of a nonuniform and partially unsupported landing zone.

CASE SUMMARY: An 81-year-old woman with heart failure and severe aortic stenosis was found to have a membranous septal aneurysm on multimodality imaging. Cardiac computed tomography demonstrated an elliptical annulus (area 581 mm2; perimeter 89 mm). After heart team evaluation, transcatheter aortic valve replacement was performed using a 35-mm self-expanding Navitor valve. The valve was successfully deployed after 1 recapture, achieving stable positioning with mild paravalvular leak. The patient developed complete heart block requiring permanent pacemaker implantation, with otherwise favorable recovery and improved ventricular function on follow-up.

DISCUSSION: MSA poses a risk of anchoring instability rather than rupture alone. Careful sizing and optimal implantation depth are key to optimizing outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement in MSA is feasible when stability is prioritized through tailored sizing and carefully selected implant strategy.

articles.title: Ventricular Septal Pseudoaneurysm After Inferior Myocardial Infarction: Multistage Interventional Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular septal pseudoaneurysm is a rare, life-threatening mechanical complication of acute myocardial infarction, arising from blood dissecting within the necrotic septum to form a false lumen.

CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man developed a postinfarction ventricular septal pseudoaneurysm with a "single-inlet, dual-outlet" morphology 5 days after primary percutaneous coronary intervention for inferior-wall infarction. A staged transcatheter strategy-occluding the larger outlet first, then the inlet 5 months later-achieved progressive hemodynamic improvement and favorable 18-month outcomes.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights an underrecognized, high-risk entity and shows that anatomy-tailored staged closure is a viable alternative to high-risk surgery when single-stage repair is infeasible.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Suspect postinfarction septal dissection in recurrent heart failure or new murmurs after myocardial infarction; imaging is key. In complex pseudoaneurysms, a staged outlet-first then inlet closure strategy yields favorable long-term results.

articles.title: Retrograde Mitral Paravalvular Leak Closure Through a Mechanical Aortic Prosthesis After Failed Antegrade Access.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral paravalvular leak can cause heart failure and hemolysis after valve replacement. Transcatheter closure is an option when repeat surgery carries high risk.

CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old woman with mechanical valves in both the aortic and mitral positions had a symptomatic, approximately 5-mm posterior mitral leak. We first attempted transseptal closure but could not cross the defect. We then passed through the central orifice of her bileaflet mechanical aortic valve and crossed the leak from the ventricular side. An 8-mm Amplatzer Vascular Plug II was deployed through a 5-F delivery system. Valve function was preserved, and follow-up imaging showed no significant residual leak.

DISCUSSION: The position and small size of the leak, the bileaflet aortic prosthesis, and the low-profile delivery system made this route feasible in this patient.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Retrograde access may be useful after failed antegrade crossing, even in the presence of a mechanical aortic valve.

articles.title: Ruptured Tricuspid Hydatid Cyst Causing Nonthrombotic Pulmonary Embolism and Right Ventricular Failure Requiring VA-ECMO.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac echinococcosis is rare, and tricuspid valve involvement is exceptionally uncommon. Ruptured right-sided cysts can mimic acute pulmonary embolism, delaying diagnosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old Yemeni man presented with acute dyspnea, fever, and collapse. Imaging demonstrated bilateral pulmonary artery filling defects with right ventricular strain and a large mobile tricuspid valve mass. Refractory hypoxemia and obstructive shock developed despite maximal medical therapy, prompting venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a heterogeneous cystic lesion and a patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting. Emergent surgery revealed a ruptured tricuspid leaflet hydatid cyst; histopathology and serology confirmed Echinococcus.

DISCUSSION: Not all pulmonary artery filling defects are thrombotic. This case demonstrates nonthrombotic pulmonary embolism from ruptured cardiac hydatid cyst and the role of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a bridge to diagnosis and surgical management in acute right ventricular failure from obstructive intracardiac pathology.

articles.title: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation: Long-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) is diagnosed in survivors of sudden cardiac arrest when no underlying cause is identified. Predicting prognosis in patients with IVF remains challenging. In this case series, we describe 3 patients with IVF to explore the clinical course of IVF.

CASE SUMMARY: Patient 1 experienced multiple recurrences within the first years following the index event. Patient 2 remained free of arrhythmic events over 30 years and ultimately chose implantable cardioverter-defibrillator explantation. Patient 3 initially appeared to follow a similarly benign course, but experienced a late recurrence 23 years after the index event.

DISCUSSION: We illustrated the course of IVF, ranging from decades without events to frequent recurrences, even after decades without events. Distinct subgroups may exist; however, further research is necessary to identify them.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: These cases show the heterogeneity and unpredictability of long-term outcomes in patients with IVF. In the absence of reliable predictors, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator therapy remains essential in patients with IVF.

articles.title: A Digital Health Communication Intervention to Reduce Nicotine and Tobacco Use Among Young Adults (Our Health Matters): Protocol for a Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual use of nicotine vapes and combustible cigarettes is high among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ+) young adults (YAs). Culturally targeted health communications interventions delivered via mobile multimedia messaging (ie, MMS) may support engagement and influence behavior, but optimal message framing and intervention feasibility are underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: This protocol describes the rationale and design of a pilot randomized controlled trial (RCT) examining the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effectiveness of an MMS-delivered, culturally targeted health communications intervention to reduce dual use among LGBTQ+ YAs and inform a phase III trial.

METHODS: This study describes a 3-arm, parallel-group RCT. Participants (target: n=300; n=240 after 20% expected attrition) were US adults, aged 18-35 years old, self-identified as LGBTQ+, were fluent in English, reported ever use of nicotine vapes and combustible cigarettes, and current use of at least one product, owned a US carrier mobile phone with MMS capability, and had internet or Zoom (Zoom Communications) access. Participants were randomized to standard risk (messages emphasizing harms of both products), comparative risk (messages contrasting cigarette harms relative to vapes), or sun safety control conditions. They received condition-specific communications three times weekly for 6 weeks, plus weekly engagement prompts. We conducted baseline, 6-week, and 12-week surveys assessing nicotine and tobacco use, and behavioral antecedents. We randomly selected 40 participants for postintervention interviews at 6 weeks. Feasibility (recruitment, retention, and engagement) and acceptability of the intervention are primary outcomes. The primary exploratory effectiveness outcome is smoking and vaping cessation at 12 weeks. To evaluate feasibility and scalability, we will calculate basic descriptive analyses for comparison with prespecified thresholds. We will apply generalized linear models (GLMs; identity link) for acceptability outcomes at 6 weeks (message and effects perceptions, relevance, and reactance) and estimate preliminary descriptive effect sizes for the exploratory cessation outcome using relative risk. Qualitative data will contextualize quantitative outcomes. Exploratory analyses include GLMs (logit link) for 12-week smoking cessation. With 240 completers, the trial would have ~95% power to detect a 17-percentage point difference in quit rates between an experimental arm and control (assuming 8% control quit rate; Bonferroni corrected α=.025).

RESULTS: The parent study, which included formative research, was funded by the National Cancer Institute in August 2021. Data collection occurred between September 2024 and February 2026. Of 295 eligible individuals, 292 were enrolled and randomized to standard risk (n=99), comparative risk (n=98), and sun safety control (n=95) arms. At baseline, participants were mostly aged 26-35 years (n=165, 56.5%), cisgender female (n=128, 43.8%), and bisexual+ (n=157, 53.8%). Data analyses began in March 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol describes an MMS-delivered, culturally targeted health communications intervention to reduce tobacco use among LGBTQ+ YAs who smoke and vape. Findings will provide critical data to inform a phase 3 RCT.

articles.title: Effects of Milk or Yogurt Supplementation on Bone Health, Body Composition, and Gut Microbiota in Canadian Young Adults: Protocol for a Three-Arm Parallel-Group Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is a major global public health concern. Optimizing peak bone mass during young adulthood is the main preventive strategy for reducing fracture risk later in life. Dairy foods, such as milk, provide nutrients, including calcium and protein, that support bone health, while fermented dairy foods, including yogurt, may confer additional benefits through potential modulation of the gut microbiome. However, the long-term comparative effects of milk and/or yogurt supplementation compared with no dairy supplementation on bone health, body composition, and the gut microbiome in Canadian young adults remain unknown.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effects of 2-year supplementation with fermented (yogurt) and nonfermented (milk) dairy products, compared to a habitual diet, on femoral neck bone mineral density (BMD) in Canadian adults aged 19 to 30 years, and to directly compare the effects of milk versus yogurt supplementation. The secondary objectives include assessing changes in BMD at skeletal sites, including the total hip, lumbar spine, and whole body, as well as body composition, hormonal factors, bone turnover markers, and gut microbiota composition and diversity following the intervention.

METHODS: The Fermented-Non-Fermented-Dairy trial is a 2-year, prospective, randomized, 3-arm, parallel-group controlled trial. Eligible healthy adults (N=120) aged 19 to 30 years living in Saskatoon, Canada, with calcium intake of <800 mg per day were randomized to one of three arms: (1) milk (375 mL) with habitual diet, (2) yogurt (350 g) with habitual diet, or (3) control (habitual diet). Data are collected at 5 time points: baseline and months 6, 12, 18, and 24. The primary outcome is the femoral neck BMD change. The secondary outcomes include BMD at other skeletal sites (total hip, lumbar spine, and whole body), bone mineral content (total hip, femoral neck, lumbar spine, and whole body), bone structure and geometry, biochemical markers of bone turnover (osteocalcin, bone-specific alkaline phosphatase, C-terminal telopeptide of type 1 collagen, transforming growth factor [TGF]-β1, TGF-β2, TGF-β3, and TGF-β receptor II), bone-related hormonal markers (parathyroid hormone, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and serum and salivary insulin-like growth factor 1), anthropometrics, body composition (total fat and lean mass), and gut microbiota.

RESULTS: Recruitment was conducted between July 2024 and July 2025, with an allocation ratio of 1:1:1 for the 3 study arms. Currently, month 12 follow-ups are ongoing. Month 24 assessments will take place from November 2026 to July 2027, followed by data analysis and dissemination of findings.

CONCLUSIONS: This study uses a robust methodology and multidimensional outcome assessment to evaluate the effects of dairy supplementation on skeletal and metabolic health in young adults. The findings will contribute to evidence on dairy-based nutritional strategies to optimize long-term bone health in Canadian young adults.

articles.title: Failing Fontan Circulation Bridged to Heart Transplantation With a Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump.
articles.abstract: An 18-year-old male patient with Fontan circulation was admitted to our institution with progressive cardiac decompensation. Because of his severely impaired systolic function, he had previously been listed for heart transplantation. Following admission, he rapidly developed cardiogenic shock, necessitating cardiopulmonary resuscitation and intubation. After implantation of a microaxial flow pump through the right subclavian artery, hemodynamics and respiration stabilized quickly; notably, the patient was extubated on the first postoperative day. Sixteen days thereafter, heart transplantation was performed successfully. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patients with a failing systemic ventricle in Fontan circulation can be successfully bridged to heart transplant by insertion of a microaxial flow pump.

articles.title: Two Decades on a Pump: What the Longest LVAD Survivor Teaches Us.
Complex Calcified Aortic Segments: What Is the Best Approach?
Novel Heterozygous NEXN Variant (c.1015del; p.Glu339Lysfs⁎14) Leading to Severe Infantile Dilated Cardiomyopathy Requiring Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathogenic NEXN variants are a rare cause of dilated cardiomyopathy. Heterozygous variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic range, including infantile presentations that typically recover, whereas transplant-requiring infantile disease has been reported only with biallelic genotypes or alongside a second cardiomyopathy gene variant.

CASE SUMMARY: We present a 21-year-old male who underwent orthotopic heart transplantation at 6 months of age for severe infantile dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous frameshift variant in NEXN (c.1015del; p.Glu339Lysfs⁎14), absent from population databases and classified as pathogenic.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first monoallelic NEXN variant reported as the sole candidate genotype in infantile-onset end-stage DCM requiring transplantation. Reported monoallelic disease runs from spontaneous recovery to transplantation, and variant position does not predict severity, so a further factor is likely to be involved.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Monoallelic NEXN loss of function can cause end-stage infantile DCM. Reported outcomes in children run from spontaneous recovery to transplantation. Retrospective genetic testing of adults transplanted in childhood can establish a molecular diagnosis 2 decades later and redirect screening for their relatives.

articles.title: Reply: Emergency TAVR in Critical Aortic Stenosis: Stabilize First or Treat the Cause?
A Roadmap Through Uncertainty: Cardiac CT From Diagnosis to Mitral Valve-in-Valve Planning.
Global Multidisciplinary Cardiometabolic Care Delivery: Outcomes From UNITE.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiometabolic disease, including cardiovascular disease driven by obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and renal dysfunction, is a major and growing global health burden, affecting an estimated 1.54 billion adults. From 2000 to 2023, prevalence more than doubled in both sexes, with wide variation across age, socioeconomic, and geographic groups.

RATIONALE: The UNITE pilot initiative (Revolutionizing the Delivery of Care in CV Disease and T2DM) aimed to close gaps in the delivery of guideline-directed medical therapy for at-risk patients with T2DM by implementing a multidisciplinary, team-based model focused on longitudinal risk factor optimization rather than individual therapies.

PROJECT SUMMARY: UNITE was implemented across 4 sites in the United States and Argentina, spanning diverse health care settings. Sites received structured design support and ongoing virtual expert guidance, covering referrals, workflows, scheduling, and data collection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Focused cardiometabolic clinics improved care coordination, therapy optimization, and patient engagement across diverse health care settings. Successful implementation was characterized by longitudinal follow-up, multidisciplinary coordination, and consistent use of guideline-directed medical therapy rather than specific health system structures.

articles.title: Emergency TAVR in Critical Aortic Stenosis: Stabilize First or Treat the Cause?
Beyond Closing the Hole: Device-Defect Geometry in Edge-to-Edge Repair of Mitral Leaflet Perforation.
ECPR-to-Heart Transplant in a Young Woman With PPA2-Associated Metabolic Cardiomyopathy Presenting as Inferolateral STEMI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder associated with rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Heightened sensitivity to alcohol has been reported in some affected individuals. Heart transplantation in affected patients is rarely reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 21-year-old woman with no prior history presented with chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, and vomiting after alcohol intake. Electrocardiogram showed inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation. She developed pulseless electrical activity arrest en route to coronary angiography and underwent extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Coronary angiography was normal. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction <20%). Despite Impella 5.5 support, no recovery occurred. Whole-genome sequencing identified pathogenic and likely pathogenic PPA2 variants, confirming PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy. She underwent successful orthotopic heart transplantation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights fulminant cardiogenic shock due to PPA2-related cardiomyopathy. Rapid genomic sequencing established the diagnosis when angiography and endomyocardial biopsy were unrevealing, informed prognosis, and enabled genetic counseling and cascade family testing.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: PPA2 cardiomyopathy should be suspected in young patients with arrest, severe ventricular dysfunction, and normal coronaries. Rapid genomic sequencing can be diagnostic and guide management.

articles.title: Mitral TEER in Advanced Heart Failure: Navigating the Gray Zone.
Beyond Aneurysm Size: Lifelong Thrombotic Risk in Adult Kawasaki Disease.
Beyond the Lumen: Toward Imaging-Guided Management of High-Risk Plaques.
Coronary Bioadaptation in the Young: Moving Beyond Permanent Caging.
Papillary Fibroelastoma in Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Papillary fibroelastomas (PFEs), benign valvular cardiac tumors, are uncommonly reported in transplant recipients, with management complicated by comorbidities.

CASE SUMMARY: Five patients (ages 27-77 years) underwent heart transplantation, with complicated post-transplant courses, and were maintained chronically on immunosuppression. Surveillance echocardiography identified valvular PFEs, 0.4 to 0.6 cm in size, with timing varying from intraoperative imaging (donor hearts) to 10 years post-transplant.

DISCUSSION: The majority of PFEs were clinically silent, small, relatively stable, and, given elevated operative risk, were managed conservatively with continued surveillance. KRAS mutations, reported in ∼33% of PFEs, suggest a neoplastic origin, though the synergistic impact of immunosuppression in PFE growth and proliferation in transplant recipients is unknown. Lack of large databases for PFEs in transplant recipients limits direct comparison with nontransplant patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: These cases underscore the value of surveillance imaging and need for balancing surgical risk in management. Prolonged follow-up is needed to clarify natural history and optimal management.

articles.title: Prevalence and Factors Associated With Late Initiation of Antenatal Care Among Women Attending the University Clinics of Kamina: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early initiation of antenatal care (ANC) is a key strategy for reducing maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality. It enables timely detection and management of pregnancy-related complications, identification of high-risk pregnancies, and appropriate referral. Despite its proven benefits, late initiation of ANC remains common in low-resource settings.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of late initiation of ANC and identify its associated factors among women attending their first ANC visit at the University Clinics of Kamina, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

METHODS: We conducted an analytical cross-sectional study from December 1, 2024, to August 30, 2025, at the University Clinics of Kamina. Consecutive sampling of all eligible women attending their first ANC visit during the study period was performed. The study included 203 women who were pregnant. Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a structured questionnaire administered electronically through KoBoCollect and were complemented by information extracted from ANC cards. Late initiation of ANC was defined as the first antenatal consultation occurring after 16 weeks of amenorrhea, in accordance with national standards. Data were analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics (version 23). Logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with late initiation. Variables with P<.20 in bivariate analysis were included in the multivariable model. Descriptive statistics were used to estimate prevalence and summarize participant characteristics. No a priori sample size or statistical power calculation was undertaken; the sample consisted of all eligible women who attended their first ANC visit during the study period and consented to participate. Supply-side characteristics of ANC services were not comprehensively assessed.

RESULTS: The prevalence of late ANC initiation (after 16 weeks of amenorrhea) was 63.5% (95% CI 56.9%-70.1%). After multivariable adjustment, the following factors were independently associated with late ANC initiation: extreme maternal age (<20 years or >35 years; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.74, 95% CI 1.07-13.06), low partner educational level (aOR 3.16, 95% CI 1.13-8.80), age of the youngest child (≤2 years; aOR 4.47, 95% CI 1.94-10.29), and unintended pregnancy (aOR 2.46, 95% CI 1.05-5.76). The model demonstrated good discriminatory ability, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 79.4% (95% CI 0.716-0.873).

CONCLUSIONS: Late initiation of ANC was highly prevalent among women attending the University Clinics of Kamina and may adversely affect maternal and perinatal outcomes. The observed associations suggest that interventions should prioritize adolescents and older women, strengthen the involvement of male partners, and improve access to family planning and early pregnancy detection strategies. These findings should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional, single-facility design.

articles.title: National trends in elderly chronic obstructive pulmonary disease burden (2010-2021) in India and subnational disparities among older adults: a Global Burden of Disease secondary analysis.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a critical public health challenge and a leading non-communicable disease globally. In India, it represents a primary driver of morbidity and mortality among older adults, that is, aggravated by population aging, tobacco smoking, and high air pollution exposure. The national trends among the elderly and subnational data focusing specifically on geographic variations remain limited. This study aims to evaluate national longitudinal trends in the COPD burden among individuals aged 60 years and older from 2010 to 2021, while contextualizing these patterns against subnational disparities among older adults across Indian states. A secondary data analysis was conducted utilizing the Global Burden of Disease 2010-2021 database. The target population included Indian adults aged ≥ 60 years for national longitudinal trends and for the cross-sectional state-level mapping. Key indicators evaluated included prevalence (PR), incidence, mortality (MR), and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Temporal trend shifts and critical inflection joinpoints over the 11-year period were evaluated via joinpoint regression models utilizing permutation tests. National Joinpoint models for the elderly revealed a steady decline in MR from 2010 to 2019 (decreasing from approximately 643 to 575 per 100,000), followed by an accelerated drop between 2019 and 2020 before stabilizing near 488 per 100,000 in 2021. National elderly DALY rates closely mirrored this downward mortality trajectory. Conversely, the prevalence in elderly (PR) increased from 15,170.94 per 100,000 in 2010 to 15,398.74 per 100,000 in 2015, reaching 15,642.10 per 100,000 by 2021. Subnational cross-sectional mapping highlighted stark regional inequities. State-wise elderly (≥60 years) prevalence varied from 12,986.76 per 100,000 in Goa to 18,680.00 per 100,000 in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. This was led by the northern and northwestern regions, including Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Delhi. The highly populous states like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, however, demonstrated a substantial disability (DALY) burden. While declining national mortality and DALY rates reflect notable progress in elderly clinical management, the rising longitudinal prevalence underscores an expanding pool of surviving patients requiring sustained care. Marked regional disparities persist across the country's elderly (≥60 years) population. This demands immediate prioritization of the high-risk states and regions. Public health strategies must transition toward region-specific interventions, promote clean domestic energy initiatives in rural areas, and enhance the primary care screening capacities.

articles.title: Accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation alter the surface chemistry, morphology and charge properties of PET microplastic fibres.
articles.abstract: Microplastic fibres released from synthetic textiles are a major source of plastic contamination in wastewater treatment systems and agricultural soils receiving biosolids. Understanding how these fibres transform during environmental ageing is important for evaluating their environmental fate and potential interactions with co-occurring contaminants. This study investigated the physicochemical transformation of cryomilled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastic fibres (MPFs) subjected to accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation using multiple analytical techniques. The fibres exhibited dimensions (183 ± 159 µm length; 20.6 ± 3.6 µm width) comparable to those reported for textile-derived microplastic fibres. Both ageing processes induced substantial changes in fibre properties, including increased surface roughness, cracking and fragmentation, a four-fold increase in surface area (0.045 ± 0.005-0.187 ± 0.004 m2 g-1), reduced thermal stability, and changes in PET surface chemistry consistent with oxidative modification. Changes in surface charge were also observed, with the point of zero charge (pHPZC) decreasing from 5.02 to 3.03, indicating increased surface acidity following degradation. These transformations suggest that PET MPFs subjected to accelerated weathering and oxidative degradation may exhibit different environmental behaviour from pristine fibres due to changes in surface morphology, chemistry and charge. The results highlight the importance of considering degraded induced physicochemical changes when evaluating the potential environmental behaviour of PET MPFs and provide a basis for future investigations of their environmental fate and interactions with co-occurring contaminants.

articles.title: Effect of a Prandial Insulin Dose Reduction on Glycemia During Postprandial Aerobic Exercise in Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes Using an Automated Insulin Delivery System. A Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of a 25% prandial insulin dose reduction on continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived time in range (TIR; 70-180 mg/dL) before aerobic cycling exercise in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes (T1D) using an automated insulin delivery (AID) system.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Sixteen participants (9 female; age 12.9 ± 3.1 years; body mass index 20.4 ± 3.1 kg/m2; HbA1c 52.3 ± 10.3 mmol/mol, 6.9 ± 0.9%) completed two heavy-intensity, constant load aerobic cycling sessions with a maximum duration of 60 min. One hundred and twenty minutes beforehand, participants activated Ease-off mode and adjusted the Personal Glucose Target to 150 mg/dL. Sixty minutes thereafter, a standardized carbohydrate drink (0.75 g/kg body mass) was consumed together with either a full prandial insulin dose (FPD, 100%) or a 25% reduced prandial insulin dose (RPD, 75% of FPD) in randomized order. Capillary blood glucose (BG), sensor glucose (SG), and AID were assessed around the sessions. The primary outcome, exercise TIR during FPD and RPD, as well as all other export-derived CGM metrics and AID were analyzed using a mixed-effects analysis with "bolus condition" (FPD and RPD) and "time interval" as within-subject factors.

RESULTS: At exercise onset, BG levels were significantly higher with RPD compared with FPD (211 ± 50 mg/dL vs. 180 ± 53 mg/dL; P = 0.03). CGM-derived exercise TIR did not differ between FPD and RPD (58 ± 41% vs. 52 ± 34%; P = 0.99). Exercise time above range (>180 mg/dL) was 42 ± 41% in FPD and 48 ± 37% in RPD (P = 0.99). Time below range (TBR) was 0% in both arms during exercise, as exercise was stopped at 90 mg/dL reflecting the protocol safety threshold rather than an absence of hypoglycemic risk. Mean exercise duration was significantly longer in RPD than in FPD (37.1 ± 17.5 vs. 30.1 ± 14.8 min; P = 0.03), and safety-related exercise cessations were significantly more frequent in FPD than in RPD (10 vs. 4, P = 0.03). No between-condition differences in glycemia or AID were observed during the nocturnal postexercise or 24-h periods (both P > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: A 25% prandial insulin dose reduction prior to postprandial aerobic exercise did not improve CGM-derived TIR in children and adolescents with T1D using the mylife CamAPS FX system and yielded higher preexercise glucose, although participants exercised longer and reached glucose-related stopping thresholds less often. Because sessions were stopped at a BG of 90 mg/dL (still within the target range), the scope for detecting during-exercise differences was constrained; within these limits, our data do not support routine prandial insulin dose reduction in this setting.

articles.title: Associations Between Matsuda Index and Islet Autoantibody Profiles in Relatives of Individuals with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Insulin sensitivity has been proposed as a modifier of type 1 diabetes risk. We investigated whether insulin sensitivity, assessed by the Matsuda Index, is associated with islet autoantibody (IAb) positivity in relatives of individuals with type 1 diabetes.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed five islet IAbs (glutamic acid decarboxylase [GAD], insulinoma-associated antigen 2 [IA-2], MIAA, islet cell antibody [ICA], and zinc transporter 8 [ZnT8]) in IAb-positive relatives enrolled in the TrialNet Pathway to Prevention study (n = 7137). Logistic regression models assessed associations between individual IAb specificities and multiple-IAb positivity (≥2 specificities) and a Matsuda Index at or above the cohort median, before and after adjustment for beta cell secretory function (Index60 or area under the curve C-peptide-to-glucose ratio [AUC ratio]) and age. Linear regression compared continuous Matsuda values by single versus multiple positivity and by disease stage.

RESULTS: In unadjusted models, IA-2, MIAA, ZnT8, ICA, and ≥2 IAb positivity were associated with higher odds of Matsuda Index ≥6.52 (odds ratios [ORs] 1.235-1.627 for individual IAbs; OR: 1.347 for ≥2 IAbs; all P ≤ 0.0003). After adjustment for age and Index60, associations reversed for IA-2, ZnT8, ICA, and multiple-IAb positivity, while an inverse association emerged for GAD (ORs 0.627-0.802 for individual specificities; OR: 0.666 for multiple positivity; all P ≤ 0.0002). AUC ratio-adjusted models yielded similar findings; MIAA was not significantly associated in either adjusted model. Continuous analyses showed lower adjusted Matsuda values in multiple- versus single-IAb-positive participants (mean differences -0.959 and -1.321 with Index60 and AUC ratio adjustment, respectively). Stage 2 participants had lower Matsuda values than Stage 1 participants before and after adjustment (all P < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATIONS: Multiple-IAb positivity and several individual specificities were associated with lower Matsuda values after adjustment for age and either metabolic index. These conditional, cross-sectional associations do not establish causality or temporal direction. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their biological significance.

articles.title: Use of 3D Intracardiac Echocardiography for Concomitant Ablation of Atrial Fibrillation and Left Atrial Appendage Closure: A Step by Step Guide.
articles.abstract: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) has traditionally played a secondary role in atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC), with transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) remaining the standard for appendage imaging. The rise of pulsed field ablation (PFA) has increased interest in adjunctive tools for real-time contact assessment, while trials such as OPTION have highlighted the clinical rationale for combining AF ablation with LAAC in a single procedure. This article describes a step-by-step procedural workflow for concomitant ablation and LAAC using 4D ICE to guide transseptal access, PFA catheter contact, and LAAC device sizing and deployment. Practical troubleshooting strategies for septal crossing and appendage visualization are also discussed.

articles.title: Impact of Real-Time Tissue Proximity Indicator Visualization and Pulsed Field Tag Coloring on Lesion Delivery and Procedural Workflow During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation Using the VARIPULSE Catheter.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The updated VARIPULSE™ software (V8.1.1.944) introduces a real-time tissue proximity indicator, enhanced VISITAG™ differentiation of complete versus incomplete applications, and grid-based color coding for lesion assessment during pulsed field ablation (PFA). Its impact on procedural workflow and lesion delivery remains insufficiently defined.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We compared 55 pulmonary vein isolation procedures performed with the updated software and 91 procedures performed with the previous version (V8.1.0.325) in 146 consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation. The updated software was associated with a higher number of PFA applications per procedure (19.76 ± 4.10 vs. 17.74 ± 3.90; p < 0.001), with more applications across all pulmonary veins, without increases in fluoroscopy time, radiation dose, or procedure duration (54.06 ± 14.99 vs. 56.64 ± 17.23 min; p = 0.046). Procedure time decreased further after an initial learning curve of 30 cases. First-pass isolation of all pulmonary veins was achieved in 83.6% versus 78.0% of procedures (p = 0.41).

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest modified, proximity-guided lesion delivery without a relevant workflow penalty.

articles.title: RNA interference and antisense strategies for chronic hepatitis B: mechanisms, clinical advances, and pathways toward functional cure.
articles.abstract: Current Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) therapies, nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon (IFN), suppress viral replication but cannot eliminate covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) or integrated HBV DNA, leaving CHB a global health threat. High antigen levels cause profound immune exhaustion, so agents must silence viral transcripts while restoring antiviral immunity. This review summarizes RNA interference (RNAi) platforms as emerging therapies. Preclinical and phase I-II data show that GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs (xalnesiran, imdusiran, elebsiran, daplusiran/tomligisiran, RBD-1016) reduce HBsAg by 1-2 log IU/mL, often for months after treatment. By targeting transcripts from both cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, they offer a mechanistic advantage over current antivirals. Combinations with capsid assembly modulators, pegylated IFN, therapeutic vaccines, or antisense drugs yield additive or synergistic declines in antigen, supporting RNAi as a backbone for curative multidrug regimens. Despite promising safety and efficacy, obstacles remain: HBsAg plateaus, incomplete immune restoration, delivery challenges in advanced liver disease, and lack of biomarkers for patient selection. Nevertheless, RNAi therapies represent a paradigm-shifting strategy that could move CHB care toward a finite, immune-driven functional cure. A literature search was conducted using Google Scholar for articles on RNAi and antisense strategies for CHB (1985-2026).

articles.title: A new prognostic stratification model for follicular lymphoma in the rituximab era.
articles.abstract: Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index (FLIPI) is a common prognostic stratification tool for follicular lymphoma (FL). High total metabolic tumour volume (TMTV) has been identified as an independent predictor of outcomes, but few studies have quantified the relative contributions of FLIPI and TMTV. A new prognostic model integrating FLIPI with baseline TMTV (cut-off = 510 cm3) was developed as FLIPI-M. Overall, 300 patients with FL grades 1-3A were included, including a development cohort (n = 155) and an independent validation cohort (n = 145). At a median follow-up of 85.3 months in the development cohort, median progression-free survival (PFS) was 94.1 months and median overall survival was not reached. The 7-year PFS rates were 65.56%, 56.59% and 11.36% in the low-, intermediate- and high-risk FLIPI-M groups respectively (p < 0.001). TMTV provided additional prognostic value beyond the FLIPI and improved conventional FLIPI risk stratification among patients with FLIPI scores of 2-3, and identified a high-risk subgroup with a particularly poor median PFS of 1.56 years. This discrimination was validated externally. FLIPI-M is a potentially useful prognostic tool for FL, particularly for identifying high-risk patients in the rituximab era.

articles.title: Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Versus Conservative Management in Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection With Acute Coronary Occlusion: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is predominantly managed conservatively, with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) reserved for selected high-risk presentations. The benefit of PCI in SCAD presenting with acute coronary occlusion (ACO), the most severe SCAD phenotype, remains unclear.

AIMS: This study aimed to determine the association between PCI at index angiography and clinical outcomes in patients with SCAD and ACO. Additional objectives were to assess whether PCI was associated with improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and determine whether the effect of PCI on clinical outcomes varies by lesion location, time to angiography and indications for PCI.

METHODS: Patients with core-laboratory adjudicated SCAD and ACO (Thrombolysis In Myocardial Infarction 0-1 flow) were identified from the ANZ-SCAD registry, a multicentre Australian and New Zealand cohort. Patients undergoing PCI were propensity-matched to conservatively managed patients using ST-elevation myocardial infarction presentation, out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, and dissection location. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE); secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and heterogeneity of treatment effect by lesion location, time to angiography, and number of indications for PCI.

RESULTS: Of 846 patients with confirmed SCAD, 211 (25%) had ACO; 88 were successfully propensity matched (44 PCI, 44 conservative). Median symptom-to-angiography time was 8 (IQR 3-33) hours with 55.3% (42/76) within 12 h. Despite matching for baseline and angiographic characteristics, patients undergoing PCI had significantly more recognized indications for intervention (mean 2.68 vs. 1.02, p < 0.001) and shorter times to angiography (5.0 h vs. 13.3 h). PCI success (TIMI 2-3 flow restoration) was achieved in 61.4% and complications in 36.4%. There was no significant difference between PCI and conservative management for in-hospital MACE (9.1% vs. 4.5%, p = 0.7), long-term MACE (median follow-up 24 months, 14% vs. 9.1%, p = 0.5), or LVEF > 40% (79% vs. 77%, p = 0.9). These findings were consistent across lesion location, symptom-to-angiography time, and number of PCI indications.

CONCLUSION: In this propensity-matched analysis of SCAD with acute coronary occlusion, PCI was not associated with improved in-hospital or long-term MACE, or LVEF, compared to conservative management. These findings may reflect prolonged ischemic times, technical challenges of PCI in SCAD as well as residual confounding by indication. Larger prospective studies are needed to identify which patients with ACO-SCAD, if any, derive meaningful benefit from timely revascularisation.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of the Interaction Between Sarcopenia and Aortic Stenosis Hemodynamic Phenotypes.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hemodynamic phenotype of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with the long-term outcomes following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Furthermore, sarcopenia has been associated with poor outcomes after TAVI. How the hemodynamic phenotype of severe AS relates to the presence of sarcopenia and how the interaction between both factors relates to all-cause mortality after TAVI have not been evaluated.

AIMS: The present study investigated how the combination of sarcopenia and the hemodynamic phenotypes of AS impacts long-term outcomes in patients undergoing TAVI.

METHODS: In this single-center, retrospective study, a cohort of consecutive patients with severe AS who underwent TAVI between 2010 and 2024 with available computed tomography data to analyze the presence of sarcopenia was evaluated. Severe AS was classified into four hemodynamic subtypes according to mean transvalvular gradient, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and stroke volume index (SVi). Sarcopenia was defined by sex-specific cut-offs of psoas muscle area at the L4 level on computed tomography. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Four hundred and seven patients (median age 82 years [78-85 years] and 38% male) were analyzed. Normal flow-high gradient was the most frequent severe AS hemodynamic phenotype (74%), followed by classical low flow-low gradient (13%), paradoxical low flow-low gradient (7%), and 6% had normal flow-low gradient. Sarcopenia was present in 42% of the patients, and it was more common among patients with classical low flow-low gradient severe AS (76%). The interaction between sarcopenia and paradoxical low flow-low gradient severe AS was independently associated with all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 2.82; confidence interval 95% 2.54-3.14; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The presence of sarcopenia is not uncommon among patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI and significantly affects outcomes in patients with paradoxical low flow-low gradient severe AS.

articles.title: Global stroke risk factors: differences between high-income and low- and middle-income countries.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the global epidemiology, pathophysiology, and risk factors for stroke, with a specific focus on disparities between high-income countries (HICs) and low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), and to identify key drivers of the differential burden.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesized data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study 2021, the World Stroke Organization (WSO) Global Stroke Fact Sheet 2025, and other major population-based studies, meta-analyses, and guidelines. Countries were classified according to World Bank income groups. We compared stroke incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), subtype distribution, the prevalence and control of modifiable and non-modifiable risk factors, and the availability of stroke services between HICs and LMICs.

RESULTS: Stroke is the second leading cause of death among non-communicable diseases and a major cause of disability, with over 160 million DALYs lost annually. A disproportionate burden falls on LMICs, which account for 87.2% of stroke deaths and 89.4% of DALYs. Ischemic stroke accounts for about 65% of incident strokes globally (74.9% in HICs vs 63.4% in LMICs), whereas intracerebral hemorrhage accounts for 31.1% of strokes in LMICs vs 17.8% in HICs; hemorrhagic stroke is associated with higher mortality. High systolic blood pressure is the dominant modifiable risk factor, contributing to approximately 57% of stroke DALYs. Risk factor control and access to care diverge markedly by income setting: only about one in five people with hypertension worldwide have it controlled, and 28% of low-income countries report general availability of all WHO-recommended antihypertensive medicines versus 93% of high-income countries; more than 4 in 10 adults with diabetes are undiagnosed; ambient particulate matter and household air pollution account for 16.6% and 11.2% of stroke DALYs, respectively; and stroke units are available in 91% of high-income versus 18% of low-income countries.

DISCUSSION: HICs have achieved substantial reductions in stroke incidence and mortality through robust prevention strategies and advanced healthcare infrastructure. In contrast, LMICs continue to struggle with limited healthcare access, insufficient stroke registries, and the rising adoption of unhealthy Western diets. These profound regional disparities underscore the urgent need for targeted, resource-appropriate prevention strategies. Addressing these inequalities requires a multi-faceted approach, including strengthening primary care, implementing public health campaigns, and establishing reliable stroke surveillance systems in LMICs.

articles.title: Effect of Back Support on Vital Signs and Comfort After Transfemoral Angiography.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The transfemoral approach for coronary angiography may cause changes in vital signs, pain, and reduced comfort due to prolonged immobilization. This study investigated the effect of back support on vital signs and comfort after coronary angiography.

METHODS: This randomized experimental study was conducted in the coronary intensive care unit of a public hospital with a total of 75 patients (experimental group: 37; control group: 38). After transfemoral angiography, back support was applied to the experimental group, whereas standard care was provided to the control group. Data were collected using the Patient Information Form, Vital Signs Monitoring Chart, Visual Analog Scale, and Immobilization Comfort Scale. Data analysis included descriptive statistics and two-way mixed ANOVA.

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the experimental group demonstrated higher peripheral oxygen saturation values (F = 6.624; p = 0.012; η2 = 0.083) and lower respiratory rate values (F = 17.432; p < 0.001; η2 = 0.193). Pain intensity in the experimental group was statistically significantly lower than that in the control group (F = 64.089; p < 0.001; η2 = 0.46). Comfort levels assessed after the procedure were statistically significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (t = 10.247; p < 0.001; η2 = 0.59).

CONCLUSIONS: The use of back support after transfemoral angiography was found to be effective in reducing respiratory rate, pain, and increasing peripheral oxygen saturation and comfort levels. In coronary ICUs, back support should be considered not only as a comfort measure but also as a supportive intervention that may contribute to improved oxygenation and patient comfort.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT: 06643182.

articles.title: Comparative Outcomes of Robotic-Assisted Versus Manual Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Using a Four-Channel Robotic Platform.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted PCI (R-PCI) reduces operator radiation and physical workload. Existing platforms operate a single guidewire at a time, and comparative data on R-PCI in situations that require a second wire for side-branch protection are lacking.

AIMS: We evaluated the feasibility and safety of R-PCI using a four-channel platform, compared with manual PCI (M-PCI), in elective single-vessel PCI.

METHODS: In this single-center pilot study, 40 patients were enrolled (M-PCI, n = 30; R-PCI, n = 10). The four-channel architecture enabled remote dual-wire side-branch protection in 3 of the 10 R-PCI cases. Procedure time, operator and patient radiation, contrast volume, NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX), and CK-MB and troponin-I at 6 and 12 h were recorded. Pre-specified per-minute rates were calculated. Groups were compared with the Mann-Whitney U test.

RESULTS: Technical and clinical success were 100%, with no conversion to manual operation and no device-related adverse events. R-PCI procedures were longer than M-PCI (33.3 ± 11.4 vs. 26.0 ± 15.1 min; p = 0.027). Operator radiation outside the lead apron was 92% lower with R-PCI (p < 0.001). Cumulative patient radiation and contrast did not differ significantly, but per-minute rates were lower for contrast (-43%; p < 0.001), DAP (-35%; p = 0.002), and air kerma (-42%; p < 0.001). Operator workload (NASA-TLX) was 68% lower (p = 0.002). Post-procedural CK-MB was lower at 6 and 12 h (p = 0.049 and 0.044), and troponin-I followed the same direction without reaching significance.

CONCLUSIONS: R-PCI with a four-channel platform was feasible and safe, with lower operator radiation, lower workload, and lower per-minute patient exposure, and allowed remote dual-wire side-branch protection.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06735716 (LNR-AVIARMX2-I02). Registered prior to first patient enrollment.

articles.title: Machine Learning Versus Clinical Risk Scores for Predicting Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury After Coronary Angiography or Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Risk stratification for contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) before coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) may inform procedural planning and preventive management. Machine-learning (ML) models frequently report higher discrimination than established clinical scores, but whether this represents genuine incremental value or unequal comparator specification is unclear. Seven databases were searched until June 20, 2026 for studies evaluating ML and a traditional CA-AKI score in identical patients. The primary outcome was the within-study difference in C-statistic (ΔC), pooled by random-effects meta-analysis with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and stratified by validation level and comparator construction. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed with PROBAST + AI and GRADE. Eleven studies (65,045 patients, 4670 events) were eligible; 10 were meta-analyzed. Pooled ΔC for each study was 0.154 (95% CI, 0.114-0.195; I2 = 87.4%), every study favoring ML. In seven studies that also refitted a logistic regression in-cohort, ΔC was 0.157 against the frozen score and 0.120 (95% CI, 0.040-0.200) against the regression. With each study's median-ranked algorithm, ΔC was 0.112 (95% CI, 0.044-0.179). One comparison was external; calibration was seldom reported and eight of 11 studies were at high risk of bias. ML models consistently out-discriminated established CA-AKI risk scores, but less so against an in-cohort refitted regression or without best-model selection. With little external validation and limited reporting of calibration or clinical utility, current evidence does not support replacing established clinical scores with ML models in routine coronary angiography or PCI practice.

articles.title: Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Understanding the Drivers and Reviewing the Current Landscape.
articles.abstract: Despite a decrease in colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence over the past decade there has been a steady increase in CRC among adults under 50 years. This entity is considered distinct from late-onset CRC and is termed as early-onset CRC (EOCRC). EOCRC is now the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in that age group. About two-thirds of EOCRC cases are sporadic and are not associated with a genetic or heritable cancer syndrome. There has been a worldwide effort to understand the molecular pathogenesis, risk factors, and drivers of sporadic EOCRC over the past few years in an attempt to direct prevention and management strategies. These drivers range from lifestyle-related habits (smoking, alcohol, diet, and sedentary lifestyle) and metabolic disorders (obesity and diabetes), dysbiosis and the microbiome, environmental toxin exposures, and early life exposures like childhood obesity, antibiotic exposure, and early microbiome development. Understanding the clinical behaviors of EOCRC distinct from late-onset CRC, as well as the current screening recommendations may provide opportunities for early detection and inform future practices. The objective of this review article is to identify, categorize, and summarize the current available data on the emerging drivers of EOCRC and understand the current landscape of the disease.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Pulsus Alternans: A Hemodynamic Harbinger of Right Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) pulsus alternans is a rare hemodynamic finding in patients with advanced heart failure. While pulsus alternans is classically associated with left ventricular failure, its appearance in the right ventricle carries distinct prognostic and management implications. We present the case of a 66-year-old patient with end-stage heart failure who exhibited RV pulsus alternans during right heart catheterization. This finding served as a harbinger of clinical deterioration and suggested a poor prognosis for isolated left ventricular mechanical circulatory support. Recognition of this sign is vital for clinicians to guide appropriate decision-making regarding advanced mechanical circulatory support and transplantation.

articles.title: External validation and component analysis of the urea-hemoglobin-lactate composite for 30-day mortality in upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Laboratory composites for upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB) often lack external validation. We evaluated the transportability and component contribution of (urea/hemoglobin) × lactate (UHL) for 30-day mortality.

METHODS: Two retrospective cohorts included 503 hospitalized patients undergoing endoscopy in Van, Türkiye, and an independent Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) cohort. Discrimination, laboratory-component contribution, and calibration of a fixed UHL-age-sex model were assessed.

RESULTS: Mortality was 7.0% (35/503) in Van. Of 1,608 eligible MIMIC-IV patients, 835 (51.9%) had early lactate testing; 819 had complete UHL components (63 deaths; 7.7%). Mortality was 7.8% among tested versus 2.6% among untested patients. UHL area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) decreased from 0.881 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.838-0.922) in Van to 0.722 (95% CI, 0.649-0.786) in external complete cases. UHL did not outperform urea × lactate in Van (ΔAUC, 0.004; 95% CI, -0.028 to 0.036; p = .810) or MIMIC-IV (ΔAUC, 0.008; 95% CI, -0.010 to 0.027; p = .378). Adjusted odds ratios per doubling of UHL were 2.72 (95% CI, 1.96-3.77) and 1.66 (95% CI, 1.40-1.96), respectively. Hemoglobin was nonsignificant in the external free-component model (odds ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.41-1.30; p = .283). The fixed model had an external AUC of 0.732 (95% CI, 0.661-0.799) and calibration slope of 0.468 (95% CI, 0.327-0.609).

CONCLUSIONS: In external complete cases selected by early lactate testing, UHL remained prognostic without significantly outperforming urea × lactate. Its incremental clinical utility beyond established UGIB scores remains unknown.

articles.title: A Seven-Parameter Leukocyte Cell Population Data Model for Differentiating Pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia From Infectious Mononucleosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and infectious mononucleosis (IM) can produce overlapping symptoms, atypical lymphoid cells, and abnormal hematology-analyzer flags. A complete blood count-derived model could help prioritize urgent smear review.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 702 development and 200 temporal-validation records. Complete-case analyses included 543 and 195 records, respectively. The seven-variable logistic model was reconstructed from development data and applied to validation without refitting, using the retained probability cutoff of 0.328. Revision analyses included nonparametric comparisons, paired DeLong testing, calibration, and post hoc age sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: The model retained WNR-X, WPC-X, NE-WX, NE-WY, LY-WY, LY-WZ, and MO-WX; p(IM) < 0.328 indicated ALL. Development AUC was 0.976 (sensitivity 90.6%; specificity 96.7%). Validation AUC was 0.970, sensitivity 87.4%, specificity 94.6%, and accuracy 90.8%. The model outperformed NE-WY, the best individual parameter (DeLong p < 0.001). Validation calibration yielded a Brier score of 0.064, slope of 0.816, and Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.022.

CONCLUSION: The seven-parameter CPD model showed excellent discrimination, but imperfect calibration and lower sensitivity in children younger than 5 years support conservative use as a laboratory-triage adjunct. It cannot replace morphology, immunophenotyping, or EBV testing and requires prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Programmable nanomedicine for precision metabolic reprogramming: Integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and RNA therapeutics in diabetes.
articles.abstract: The diabetes mellitus is a complex metabolic disorder involving dynamic interactions between various genetic, epigenetic, immunometabolic, environmental factors leading to the disruption of metabolic homeostasis in the system. The main treatments for conventional management are glycemic control, and target only the hallmark of disease, but not underlying molecular networks. The advent of multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), RNA therapeutics, and nanomedicine, has sparked an era of precision metabolic interventions against the gene circuits driving disease. In this review, the authors outline the development of smart nanovectors as platforms for gene silencing and gene programming of pro-diabetic genes selectively. Target discovery via AI principles, Omics approach for the identification of diabetogenic networks, next generation RNA therapeutic modalities, intelligent responsive Nanovectors, tissue-specific metabolic reprogramming, and autonomous therapeutic systems are discussed. Moreover, the role of digital twins, biosensor feedback loops, synthetic biology and closed-loop therapeutic architectures as the building blocks of precision medicine are explored. In combination, these emerging technologies create a flipping paradigm for adaptive metabolic reprogramming and could faster bring about sustainable therapies for disease modification and functional remission of diabetes.

articles.title: Development of a Novel Virtual-Reality System for at-Home Training to Promote Functional Use of Impaired Arm of Stroke Survivors via Movement Amplification.
articles.abstract: Stroke survivors often avoid using their more-impaired arm, leading to long-term functional decline. To address this problem, we developed a home-based virtual-reality (VR) system designed to incentivize impaired-limb use. The system incorporates subject-specific movement amplification, increasing displayed virtual arm/hand range of motion (ROM) based on each individual's impairment patterns. Small voluntary movements are amplified within VR games to produce functionally meaningful actions that simulate everyday tasks. Game difficulty and amplification levels were progressively adjusted as performance improves, promoting continued challenge and confidence. Feasibility was evaluated in 12 chronic stroke survivors. Out of 12, 10 completed the 6-week semi-supervised home training (17% attrition), with 5 classified as compliant (play time ≥1.2 hours/week) and 5 as noncompliant (play time <1.2 hours/week). Participants demonstrated high engagement, with in-game use of the more-impaired arm far exceeding chance level (50%) in both compliant (90.8%) and noncompliant subgroups (73.2%). Improvements in motor impairments, assessed by Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA), were positively correlated with compliance (i.e., play time: r = 0.66; P = 0.05). The Compliant group showed a mean FMA improvement of 3.2 points (Cohen's dav = 0.48), and of 5.7 points (dav = 0.77) for those without pain complications (n = 3). Participants without pain complications also reported reductions in symptoms (r = -0.80) and social limitations (r = -0.73). These findings demonstrated the feasibility of a semi-supervised, home-based VR intervention that promotes impaired arm use after stroke, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and absence of control group.

articles.title: The HIV Care Continuum of Transgender People in a Specialized Consultation Center in Barcelona, Spain: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Transgender people with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) face multiple health challenges, from sociodemographic disparities to gaps in clinical care. This study aimed to describe the characteristics and HIV care continuum in transgender people with HIV in Barcelona, Spain, and to identify issues hindering care. We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational cohort study including transgender people with HIV receiving care at Hospital Clínic de Barcelona between March 2019 and February 2020. Among 193 participants (mean age 37 years, standard deviation 9), 98% (189/193) were transgender women, 88% (168/190) were born in Latin America, and 88% (147/167) reported a history of sex work. At the first clinic visit, 76% (147/193) had detectable HIV viral load, including 39% (27/70) of antiretroviral treatment (ART)-experienced individuals, compared with 16% (31/193) at the last clinic visit. Forty-six percent (88/193) had CD4 counts <350 cells/mm³ at their first clinic visit. Overall, 75% (145/193) missed at least one scheduled visit during the preceding year, 7% (13/191) had discontinued ART, 49% (90/184) had been hospitalized, and 16% (30/193) had experienced an acquired immunodeficiency syndrome-defining opportunistic infection. Gender-affirming hormone therapy was reported by 47% (83/177), while 19% (37/191) received endocrinology follow-up. Recreational drug use was reported by 56% (98/176). Recreational drug use and hospital admissions were associated with missed visits in the multivariable analysis. Transgender people with HIV in Barcelona showed multiple vulnerabilities and gaps across the HIV care continuum, including missed visits, detectable viremia, and limited access to supervised gender-affirming care. These findings support the need for multidisciplinary approaches to improve care.

articles.title: Prophylactic Fasciocutaneous Advancement in Geriatric Ankle Fractures: A Comparative Study of Wound Complications.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ankle fractures in elderly patients are common and carry substantial soft tissue risks. This study evaluated the clinical association of a prophylactic, tension-free fasciocutaneous advancement (FA) technique vs conventional closure on surgical wound outcomes.

METHODS: This comparative cohort study analyzed 180 geriatric patients (age ≥ 60 years) undergoing open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) for closed, unstable ankle fractures using lateral plating protocols; high-risk profiles with pre-existing necrosis, open fractures, or active infection were excluded. Group A (n = 60; retrospective cohort) underwent prophylactic FA maneuver with regular closure, whereas group B (n = 120; concurrent and historical control cohort) received conventional closure alone. The primary outcome was total surgical wound complications, assessed until wound closure or resolution. Demographic analysis, matching between groups, and wound complications using Fisher exact test and χ2. Stata V.14 was used for data analysis. Sample size was estimated to be 120 patients, with 80% power and α = 0.05.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, including age, sex, and comorbidities, showed no significant difference detectable with the numbers available between groups. The total incidence of surgical wound complications was significantly lower in the intervention cohort (group A: 6.7% [4/60]) compared to the conventional closure group (group B: 23.3% [28/120]; P = .0065) despite a higher proportion of fracture-dislocations in group A (P = .029). In univariate analysis, prophylactic FA was associated with a 77% reduction in the crude odds of surgical wound complications (OR = 0.23, 95% CI 0.08-0.70; P = .010). Multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, diabetes, smoking, and fracture-dislocation supported this association (adjusted OR = 0.20, 95% CI 0.06-0.63; P = .006). Only fracture-dislocation drove a 13% change in the adjusted estimate and was itself independently associated with wound complications (adjusted OR = 2.32, 95% CI 1.03-5.24; P = .042); the rest were not confounders.

CONCLUSION: In geriatric patients undergoing plate fixation for unstable ankle fractures, prophylactic fasciocutaneous advancement was significantly associated with fewer total surgical wound complications than conventional closure. Given the retrospective, non-randomized design, prospective confirmation is warranted; nonetheless, this simple, reproducible adjunct shows clinical utility in closed fractures managed with standardized lateral plating protocols.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Impact of Cardiac CT-Defined True Septal Right Ventricular Lead Position on Electrical and Structural Remodeling After Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy With Defibrillator Implantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The impact of true right ventricular (RV) septal lead positioning on response to cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) remains controversial. We investigated the association between cardiac computed tomography (CT)-defined RV defibrillator lead position and CRT response.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 105 patients who underwent CRT-defibrillator (CRT-D) implantation and post-implantation cardiac CT to assess RV lead position. All patients had documented biventricular pacing ≥ 90% at 6 months. Based on CT findings, patients were classified into a true septal RV lead group (n = 56) and a non-septal group (n = 49). Changes in QRS duration and echocardiographic parameters at 6 months and long-term clinical outcomes were compared between the groups. CRT response was defined as a ≥ 15% reduction in left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV) at 6 months.

RESULTS: Post-implantation QRS duration was significantly shorter in the septal group than in the non-septal group (136.2 ± 15.8 vs. 157.4 ± 21.8 ms, p < 0.001). At 6 months, the septal group showed greater improvements in left ventricular ejection fraction (Δ8.4 ± 9.7% vs. 3.8 ± 8.5%, p = 0.011) and LVESV (Δ-31.8 ± 39.2 vs. -11.9 ± 39.1 mL, p = 0.013), with a higher CRT response rate (73.2% vs. 42.9%, p = 0.003). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that true septal RV lead positioning was independently associated with CRT response (odds ratio, 3.33; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-9.78; p = 0.029). No significant between-group differences were observed in mortality or heart failure hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac CT-defined true septal RV lead positioning was associated with greater electrical resynchronization and enhanced LV reverse remodeling after CRT-D implantation. Anatomical RV lead position may represent an important modifiable determinant of CRT response.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Linear Ablation for Peri-Mitral Annular Atrial Flutter Using the Pentaspline Pulse Field Ablation Catheter.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite widespread use of the pentaspline pulse field ablation (PFA) catheter to treat atrial fibrillation, there is limited data supporting its feasibility, safety, and effectiveness in creating linear lesions to treat peri-mitral atrial flutter (AFL).

OBJECTIVE: To assess the safety and efficacy of using the pentaspline PFA catheter to treat peri-mitral AFL.

METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective review of consecutive patients receiving catheter ablation using the pentaspline PFA catheter to treat peri-mitral macroreentrant AFL.

RESULTS: A total of 80 patients underwent catheter ablation for clinical peri-mitral AFL. Ablation was guided by electroanatomic mapping in all patients. AFL was treated with a lateral mitral line in 38 patients (47.5%), an anteroseptal mitral line in 31 patients (38.8%), a septal mitral line in 6 patients (7.5%), and an anterolateral mitral line in 5 patients (6.3%). Acute procedural success was achieved in 70 patients (87.5%) using the pentaspline catheter; the remaining 10 patients (12.5%) required additional radiofrequency ablation to achieve procedural success. Acute complications occurred in 4 (5.0%) patients: 2 (2.5%) patients sustained electrical isolation of the left atrial appendage, 1 (1.3%) had transient hematuria, and 1 (1.3%) had pericarditis. After a median follow-up of 322 days (IQR 192-432), 42 patients (52.5%) had recurrent AFL. Of these patients, 26 patients underwent a repeat ablation procedure-all demonstrated electrical breakthrough across the prior mitral line.

CONCLUSIONS: While the pentaspline catheter can achieve acute procedural success when treating peri-mitral AFL with linear ablation of the mitral annulus, the long-term efficacy of this treatment strategy is modest.

articles.title: Cumulative microvascular disease burden is associated with lower-limb amputation in patients attending a high-risk diabetes foot clinic.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is high prevalence of micro and macrovascular complications of diabetes in people attending high-risk diabetes foot clinic.

AIM: To evaluate whether the complication composite score of microvascular and macrovascular complications is associated with lower-limb amputation (LLA) among patients attending a high-risk diabetes foot clinic.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective clinical audit of 124 patients managed at the Townsville University Hospital high-risk foot clinic. The primary outcome was documented LLA. The microvascular complication composite score was defined as the number of retinopathy, neuropathy and nephropathy/albuminuria complications present (score 0-3). The macrovascular complication composite score was defined as the number of ischaemic heart disease, stroke and peripheral vascular disease complications present (score 0-3). Baseline characteristics were compared by amputation status. Logistic regression model examined the independent association of vascular complication composite scores with amputation.

RESULTS: Among 124 patients, 44 (35.4%) had undergone LLA. Retinopathy (72.7% vs 37.5%, P < 0.001), neuropathy (90.9% vs 75.0%, P = 0.035), obesity (72.7% vs 56.2%, P = 0.083) and dyslipidaemia (93.2% vs 80.0%, P = 0.068) were more common in the amputation group. The mean microvascular complication composite score was higher in patients with amputation than in those without amputation (2.2 vs 1.6, P < 0.001). In the main adjusted model, each additional microvascular complication was associated with higher odds of amputation (OR: 2.31, 95% CI: 1.31-4.10, P = 0.004), whereas the macrovascular complication composite score was not independently associated with amputation after adjustment (OR: 1.59, 95% CI: 0.88-2.88, P = 0.125).

CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk foot clinic audit, microvascular complication composite score was strongly and independently associated with LLA.
