A simple microvascular burden load derived from routine clinical data may help identify patients who warrant intensified multidisciplinary foot protection, vascular assessment and secondary prevention strategies.

articles.title: Whole Blood versus Balanced Component Therapy in Trauma Resuscitation: Physiological Changes Within the First 4 Hours after Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uncontrolled hemorrhage remains the leading cause of potentially preventable death after traumatic injury, particularly within the first hours following trauma. Whole blood (WB) transfusion has regained widespread acceptance in trauma resuscitation, with prior studies demonstrating its feasibility and safety compared with balanced component therapy (BCT). However, few studies have specifically evaluated the early physiological effects of WB during the critical first hours after injury using injury-anchored laboratory assessments. This study compared WB and BCT regarding early physiological recovery within the first 4 hours after injury, with secondary assessments of hematological parameters and in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 234 trauma patients who underwent massive transfusion within the first four hours after injury at a tertiary trauma center between 2016 and 2025. Patients received either WB or BCT administered in a 1:1:1 ratio of packed red blood cells, plasma, and platelets. Baseline laboratory values were obtained within 1 hour of injury and repeated at 4 hours. Changes in metabolic (lactate), coagulation (INR), and acid-base (base excess) parameters were analyzed using analysis of covariance models.

RESULTS: WB did not demonstrate superiority over BCT regarding early physiological recovery within 4 hours post-injury. Adjusted analyses showed no significant differences in lactate, base excess, or coagulation trajectories between the groups. Rates of early physiological deterioration were also comparable. However, WB was associated with significantly higher hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelet levels at 4 hours. In multivariable analysis, transfusion strategy was not independently associated with in-hospital mortality, whereas age, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and Injury Severity Score were independent predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: WB resuscitation did not demonstrate superior early physiological recovery compared with BCT but was associated with better preservation of hematological parameters. These findings support WB as a potentially viable and operationally practical alternative to BCT during early trauma resuscitation.

articles.title: Optical coherence tomography usage for optimization, prevention and management of percutaneous coronary intervention failure.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a cornerstone of coronary artery disease management, yet procedural failure remains a significant clinical problem. The potential clinical consequences of PCI failure are restenosis and stent thrombosis, which could arise through several mechanisms.

AREAS COVERED: This review was based on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, from database inception through October 2026, using the terms 'optical coherence tomography,' 'stent failure,' 'in-stent restenosis,' 'stent thrombosis,' 'PCI,' and 'PCI failure.' The review summarizes current evidence on OCT-guided index PCI and complex lesion subsets such as bifurcations, left main disease, and calcified lesions. We also discuss OCT's imaging capabilities, its ability to detect both mechanical and biological causes of PCI failure, and its role in guiding targeted corrective interventions.

EXPERT OPINION: OCT has become an important tool for guiding PCI. OCT also provides unique mechanistic insights into the mechanisms underlying PCI failure, allowing mechanism-specific interventions. Despite current limitations, including cost and accessibility, integrating OCT into routine practice optimizes procedural results and may reduce adverse cardiovascular events. Future developments and standardized OCT-guided protocols are likely to enhance the prevention and management of PCI failure over the next few years.

articles.title: Emergent antioxidant therapies for COPD management.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a main cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and its management continues to be challenging because of its marked biological and clinical heterogeneity. Among the many mechanisms involved in COPD, oxidative stress has emerged as one of the central drivers of disease progression by disrupting redox homeostasis and promoting inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and tissue injury. At a molecular level, excessive production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species overwhelms endogenous antioxidant defenses, leading to oxidative damage of lipids, proteins, and DNA, while also altering redox-sensitive signaling pathways.

AREA COVERED: In this review, we provide an overview of oxidative stress in COPD, covering its biochemical basis, cellular and molecular mechanisms, endogenous antioxidant defenses, oxidative stress biomarkers, and their clinical relevance. We also discuss current antioxidant therapies and emerging mechanism-based therapeutics, including nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor2 (Nrf2) activation, mitochondrial-targeted antioxidants, ferroptosis inhibition, inflammasome modulation, and interleukin (IL)-targeted therapies.

EXPERT OPINION: Although Interleukin-33 (IL-33) -targeted therapies are currently the most clinically advanced, mitochondria-targeted therapies may ultimately represent the most promising strategy for disease modification because they address multiple interconnected mechanisms underlying COPD progression.

articles.title: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Attitudes, Self-Efficacy, and Prescription Practices Among Physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil: Insights for Optimizing PrEP Service Delivery.
articles.abstract: Brazil is well-known for its longstanding public policies for HIV prevention; however, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) uptake remains suboptimal in the country. Expanding PrEP uptake depends on physicians' attitudes, prescription self-efficacy, and practices. Thus, our study investigated the prevalence of positive attitudes toward PrEP, prescription self-efficacy, and PrEP prescription practices, as well as the factors associated with these outcomes among physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil. A self-administered cross-sectional survey was conducted online among 283 physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil, between July 2024 and January 2025. We used bivariate and multivariable logistic regression to examine associations between sociodemographic and other characteristics and the outcome variables (i.e., attitudes, self-efficacy, and prescription practices), with multiple imputations for missing data. Participants' mean age was 33.6 years (standard deviation = 4.7 years). Most participants were White (82.5%) and female (69.8%), and only 15.2% specialized in infectious diseases. Most (87.7%) participants held positive attitudes toward PrEP, while less than one-third (31.3%) reported high prescription self-efficacy, and only 21.5% had prescribed PrEP. Participants with an Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Queer, or Other (LGBQ+) sexual orientation were more likely to have positive attitudes toward PrEP [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 10.08, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.83-55.53], high PrEP prescription self-efficacy (aOR: 9.89, 95% CI: 4.66-21.00), and a past prescription for PrEP (aOR: 4.08, 95% CI: 1.66-10.02). In addition, infectious disease specialists were more likely to have high PrEP prescription self-efficacy (aOR: 108.51, 95% CI: 28.23-417.01) and a past PrEP prescription (aOR: 48.85, 95% CI: 18.62-128.10). Conversely, participants assigned male at birth were less likely to have positive attitudes toward PrEP (aOR: 0.34, 95% CI: 0.14-0.83). Physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil, held positive attitudes toward PrEP but exhibited low self-efficacy and low prescription rates. Our results emphasize the need for tailored training programs to enhance prescription self-efficacy and increase PrEP prescribing among noninfectious disease specialists and primary care physicians in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

articles.title: Reframing Person-Centred Care as a Safety Critical Practice in the Digital Era-A Discursive Paper.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This discursive paper argues that person-centred fundamental care is not separate from, or secondary to, safety-critical care; it is a safety-critical nursing practice.

DESIGN: A discursive paper.

DATA SOURCES: The Fundamental of Care Framework was used as a conceptual lens to purposively identify relevant conceptual and empirical literature for discussion. PubMed and CINAHL databases were searched for papers and supplemented by citation searching and reference list checking. Sources were interpreted iteratively in relation to the nurse-patient relationship, the integration of physical, psychosocial and relational care needs and the context in which care is delivered. Similarities, differences and tensions were compared to develop a transparent, conceptually informed argument rather than a comprehensive evidence synthesis.

DISCUSSION: Three connected areas: fundamental care as skilled and safety-critical nursing practice; the capacity of digital technology to support or disrupt fundamental care; and the implications for nursing education, leadership, policy and healthcare systems. Considered through the lens of the Fundamentals of Care Framework, digital technologies may strengthen safety when they support relational engagement, integrated care and professional judgement, but may undermine it when they redirect attention towards documentation, alerts and task completion.

CONCLUSION: Digital technologies offer important opportunities to support nursing care, but their contribution to safety depends on how they are designed, implemented and used. Applying the Fundamentals of Care Framework demonstrates that technology should support the nurse-patient relationship, the integration of physical, psychosocial and relational care needs and the context required for safe care. Recognising person-centred fundamental care as skilled and safety-critical is therefore essential to ensure that digital innovation strengthens rather than displaces relational engagement, professional judgement and integrated care.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND PATIENT CARE: Person-centred fundamental care should be recognised as skilled, safety-critical nursing practice. Nurses, educators, leaders and policymakers should ensure that digital systems support the nurse-patient relationship, integrate care needs and facilitate the organisational conditions required for safe care. Further research should examine how different technologies and clinical contexts affect nurses' relational, observational and interpretive work, particularly for patients at greater risk of missed care.

IMPACT: The Fundamentals of Care Framework was used to examine how digital technologies may enable or disrupt the relational, integrated and contextual dimensions of fundamental care. It demonstrates that technology should be evaluated not only by its efficiency or capacity to record activity, but by whether it supports the nursing practices through which risks are recognised, care needs are integrated and harm is prevented. The paper identifies implications for nursing education, leadership, policy, research and digital system design.

PATIENT AND PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: There was no patient or public contribution to this discursive paper.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance, Image Quality and Radiation Dose of Ultra-Low Dose Chest CT Compared With Chest Radiography for Latent Tuberculosis Screening: Influence of Image Reconstruction Techniques.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) affects over one quarter of the global population and poses a significant risk of reactivation in immunocompromised patients. Accurate radiological assessment is essential before initiating immunosuppressive therapies. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance, image quality, and radiation dose of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) compared with chest radiography (CXR) for detecting radiological features of LTBI.

METHODS: In this prospective single-centre study, adults undergoing LTBI screening prior to immunosuppressive therapy underwent standard CXR and ULDCT. Subjective image quality was independently assessed by two radiologists who were blinded to the outcomes, while objective image quality assessment was performed by a single radiologist. LTBI-related findings were recorded. Statistical analyses included interobserver agreement, paired modality comparison, and radiation dose assessment.

RESULTS: Thirty-four participants (BMI 28.6 ± 6.9 kg/m2) were included. The mean ± SD effective dose for ULDCT was 0.13 ± 0.02 mSv in comparison to 0.10 ± 0.07 mSv for the CXR. ULDCT detected granulomas in 12 patients (16 lesions); CXR detected none of the CT-confirmed granulomas; maximum intensity projections identified additional lesions. CXR sensitivity for granuloma detection was 0% (95% CI: 0%-26.5%) when CT was used as the reference. ULDCT also identified pulmonary nodules, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, calcified nodes, and incidental findings not visible on CXR, including features suspicious for active tuberculosis in two cases.

CONCLUSION: The results indicate that ULDCT is superior to CXR for detecting calcified granulomas and other LTBI-related thoracic findings at comparable radiation doses.

articles.title: Clinical and procedural characteristics and six-month cardiovascular outcomes of patients undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: comparison of acute and chronic coronary syndromes in a tertiary care centre.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the rising burden of coronary artery disease in India, real-world data on PCI patient characteristics and procedural practices remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics of patients undergoing PCI and to assess 6-month cardiovascular outcomes at a tertiary care centre.

METHODS: This single-centre observational cohort study included 264 patients undergoing PCI. Demographic, clinical, angiographic, procedural, and 6-month follow-up data were collected using structured case record forms and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: The mean age was 58.49 ± 9.97 years, and 76.5% of patients were male. Overall, 61.0% were overweight or obese according to Asian BMI criteria, and 54.5% had preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥55%). Urgent or emergent PCI accounted for 84.5% of procedures. The left anterior descending artery was most frequently treated (34.8%), Type C lesions predominated (52.7%), and radial access was used in 85.2% of cases. Single-, double-, and triple-vessel disease occurred in 39.8%, 35.2%, and 25.0% of patients, respectively. Triple-vessel disease was more prevalent among patients aged ≥60 years than younger patients (31.8% vs. 18.5%; p = 0.042). Multivariable logistic regression identified age ≥60 years and prior PCI as independently associated with triple-vessel disease. Higher LVEF was associated with lower CAD severity in ordinal logistic regression (OR = 0.978, 95% CI = 0.958-0.997; p = 0.027). Six-month MACE occurred in 42 patients (15.9%) and was associated with smoking/tobacco use and other social habits in unadjusted analyses.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world cohort, patients were predominantly middle-aged males with a high burden of overweight/obesity and acute coronary syndromes. Increasing age (≥60 years), prior PCI, and lower LVEF were associated with more extensive coronary artery disease, particularly triple-vessel disease. MACE occurred in 15.9% of patients and was associated with smoking/tobacco use and other social habits.

articles.title: Speak up now: Preventing infection and building a safety culture in NICUs in Somalia's war-affected and fragile health system.
articles.journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition

articles.title: Correction: Feco-prevalence and risk factors of Helicobacter pylori infection among adults with dyspepsia in Mogadishu, Somalia: a cross-sectional study.
Development and validation of a risk nomogram for predicting post-RFA recurrence in HCC patients: a five year follow up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Currently, there are existing predictive models for post Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) recurrence in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients; however, these models commonly suffer from small sample sizes, lack external validation in most cases, and some require additional assessments or tests for predictive factors. This imposes financial and psychological burdens on patients, rendering the generalizability in clinical settings.

METHODS: We utilized multiple imputation with random forest to fill missing data, followed by employing subjective expertise in conjunction with Lasso regression to select the optimal predictive factors. Eventually, the predictive factors were categorized into different types, and distinct predictive models were constructed. We assessed model performance in both the training and validation sets using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, Decision curve analysis (DCA) curves, calibration curves, and other evaluation metrics such as sensitivity to select the optimal predictive model.

RESULTS: A total of 762 HCC patients aged between 17 and 91 years were enrolled. The ROC curve showed that the model combining AFP with treatment factors and tumor factors exhibited the best performance in both the training set (0.818 [0.636, 1]) and validation set (0717 [0.636, 1]). This model demonstrated well-calibrated predicted recurrence-free survival (RFS) at 6, 12, and 18 months. Decision curve analysis indicated a good net benefit of this prediction model across a reasonable range of threshold probabilities, and it achieved respective C-indexes of 0.795 (0.473, 0.961) in the training set and 0.594 (0.423, 0.791) in the validation set. Other evaluation metrics for this predictive model all suggest that the final predictive model has good model predictive performance.

CONCLUSIONS: This study, by incorporating a larger sample size and including more easily detectable variables, constructed post-RFA recurrence predictive models that performed well in both the training and validation sets. This enhances the operationality and generalizability of the predictive models in practical settings.

articles.title: Preventing congenital syphilis: a review of maternal screening.
articles.abstract: Congenital syphilis remains one of the most preventable causes of stillbirth, neonatal mortality, and infant morbidity worldwide. Despite inexpensive diagnostic tests and effective treatment, surveillance indicates a resurgence of maternal and congenital syphilis. Untreated maternal infection can result in miscarriage, stillbirth, prematurity, neonatal death, or severe congenital disease. In 2022, the World Health Organization estimated 700,000 congenital syphilis cases worldwide, resulting in nearly 390,000 adverse pregnancy outcomes, including fetal and neonatal deaths and infants born with clinical disease. Implementation failures across the prevention cascade continue to undermine global elimination efforts. Surveillance data demonstrate concerning increases in high-income countries, including the United States, Canada, and Australia, while substantial disparities persist among Indigenous and marginalised populations. Congenital syphilis prevention relies on timely antenatal screening, early diagnosis, and prompt treatment with benzathine penicillin. However, prevention failures, including limited access to antenatal care, missed screening opportunities, delayed treatment, and inadequate partner management, continue to drive transmission despite the availability of diagnostics and treatment. The COVID-19 pandemic further exposed vulnerabilities in maternal health services, widening existing prevention gaps and weakening surveillance systems. Conversely, successful elimination initiatives demonstrate that congenital syphilis is preventable when screening, treatment, surveillance, and health-system implementation are effectively integrated. Strengthening antenatal screening programmes, expanding access to rapid point-of-care diagnostics, implementing repeat screening where appropriate, and reinforcing integrated surveillance systems should therefore remain global priorities. Ultimately, eliminating congenital syphilis is not a technological but an implementation challenge requiring sustained political commitment, equitable access to maternal healthcare, and coordinated public health action.

articles.title: Histone lactylation: unveiling the epigenetic key to neurological disorders.
articles.abstract: The recognition of histone lactylation (Kla) as a lactate-associated epigenetic change has dramatically altered our understanding of lactate and has moved beyond its long-standing characterization as a metabolic waste product. Histone lactylation dynamically regulates gene transcription in response to metabolic changes in the microenvironment by bridging cellular metabolism and chromatin remodelling. It is particularly crucial for the central nervous system (CNS), which has a high energy demand and complex cellular composition. Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that the Kla is involved in the pathogenesis of diverse neurological disorders. This review synthesizes evidence that microglial H4K12la drives a self-amplifying glycolytic feedback loop via PKM2 while H3K18la activates age-dependent NF-κB-mediated paracrine signaling in Alzheimer's disease. H3K9la and Dld-K127 lactylation reprogram microglial and metabolic states to accelerate dopaminergic neurodegeneration in individuals with Parkinson's disease. These compounds play biphasic roles in promoting acute neuroinflammation but conferring delayed neuroprotection in individuals with ischaemic stroke. H3K18la mediates microglial neuroprotection whereas neuronal H3K14la triggers ferroptosis in response to intracerebral haemorrhage. H3K9la-dependent LUC7L2-MLH1 signalling underlies chemoresistance and stemness maintenance. We further elucidate the molecular machinery of histone lactylation, its physiological functions in CNS homeostasis and the cell-type-specific pathological mechanisms underlying its dysregulation. We highlight the therapeutic advantages of targeting site-specific and cell-type-specific histone lactylation to interrupt pathogenic feedback loops and promote translational applications.

articles.title: Clinical management of cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in the North Denmark Region: a descriptive study of practice patterns in the past decade.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a common complication in patients with cancer. Contemporary clinical characteristics and management in Denmark, including uptake of DOACs and planned treatment duration, remains unexplored. Anticoagulants for patients with cancer in Denmark are not traceable in nationwide prescription registries. We aimed to describe characteristics and routine clinical management of cancer-associated VTE at a Danish university hospital prior to (2017-2021) and after (2023-2025) the nationwide recommendation of DOACs as first-line treatment.

METHODS: Manual electronic record review of patients with imaging-confirmed cancer-associated VTE in a hospital discharge registry. Information about clinical characteristics (e.g., VTE type, incidental vs. non-incidental VTE) and clinical management (e.g. choice of anticoagulant, planned treatment duration) in each time-period was recorded.

RESULTS: Overall, we included 414 patients with confirmed cancer-associated VTE, of which 37% had haematological cancer. All patients were treated with anticoagulation, including the 12% with incidental VTE. An increase in the use of DOACs after the new recommendation was evident, rising from 33.0% to 72.5%, with broadly similar uptake in haematology and oncology. DOACs were used in accordance with guidelines with respect to renal function and platelet count. Planned treatment duration ranged from three months to lifelong but remained unspecified in 1/3 of contemporary cases.

CONCLUSIONS: All patients with cancer-associated VTE, both symptomatic and incidental, were treated with anticoagulation. A substantial increase in the use of DOACs over time was evident. Planned treatment duration was variable and remained unspecified in approximately 1/3 of VTE cases.

articles.title: Association between body mass index and neuropeptides in the microvascular function: the role of migraine.
articles.journal: The journal of headache and pain
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Both migraine and obesity are associated with major cardiovascular disease, and obesity shows a bidirectional relationship with migraine. As both are linked to microvascular alterations, we examined the association between BMI and microvascular function and whether this association differed by migraine status.

METHODS: We performed post hoc analyses in a cohort including middle-aged women with presumed elevated cardiovascular risk (either due to a medical history of polycystic ovary syndrome or ischemic stroke). Dermal blood flow (DBF) was measured using a forearm model to quantify neuropeptide activity as a marker of microvascular function. Measurements were performed under control conditions and after local application of lidocaine/prilocaine cream (EMLA®), which inhibits axon-reflex-mediated neuropeptide release. Linear regression analyses were conducted for the area under the curve (AUC) of overall DBF responses under control conditions and the ratio of EMLA to the control condition. The AUCs under control and EMLA conditions, as well as BMI, were natural log-transformed. Models were adjusted for alcohol use, physical activity, smoking, and postmenopausal state. Estimates (β) with heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors (HC3 SEs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Interactions with migraine status were tested using the pooled Wald test.

RESULTS: Of 132 women (mean 51.2 years, SD = 4.3), 125 had complete BMI and microvascular data, including 58 (46.4%) with migraine. Overall, BMI was not associated with higher responses under control conditions (adjusted β = 0.32, HC3 SE = 0.22; 95% CI -0.12‒0.75), in women without migraine (adjusted β = 0.39, HC3 SE = 0.33; 95% CI -0.25‒1.03), nor in women with migraine (adjusted β = 0.27, HC3 SE = 0.34; 95% CI -0.39‒0.93), Pinteraction=0.73. Under EMLA conditions, we observed no significant association between BMI and neuropeptide-mediated response in the total population (adjusted β = -0.40, HC3 SE = 0.21; 95% CI -0.82‒0.02) or in women with migraine (adjusted β = 0.11, HC3 SE = 0.27; 95% CI -0.43‒0.64). However, a higher BMI was significantly associated with lower responses in women without migraine (adjusted β = -0.76, HC3 SE = 0.29; 95% CI -1.33‒-0.18), Pinteraction=0.045.

CONCLUSIONS: Migraine may modify associations between BMI and microvascular function. The absence of an association between BMI and higher neuropeptide activity in individuals with migraine may point to distinct pathophysiological mechanisms in this group, warranting further research.

articles.title: Trust and Behavioural Intention to Use Artificial Intelligence Among ICU Nurses: An Empirical Structural Equation Modelling Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: AI-assisted systems in intensive care units face a major bottleneck because nurses lack trust and willingness to use them, limiting clinical impact. This study examined ICU nurses' trust and acceptance of AI using an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology model.

METHODS: A multicentre cross-sectional study was conducted via an online survey. Structural equation modelling was performed using SPSS AMOS for data analysis. The study adhered to the STROBE checklist for observational research reporting.

RESULTS: From June to July 2025, ICU nurses participated in this study. Intention to use AI was moderately high. The model was rigorously tested and validated with data, confirming credibility and reliability. Cognitive trust significantly increased intention, and affective trust did so significantly but more weakly. Performance expectancy had no significant direct effect on intention or trust. Effort expectancy did not directly affect intention, but indirectly promoted adoption by strengthening cognitive and affective trust. Social influence directly boosted intention and acted indirectly through trust. Perceived risk did not directly lower intention, but indirectly hindered adoption by reducing both types of trust.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Understanding the mechanisms by which critical care nurses utilise artificial intelligence in the ICU can help promote the adoption of AI in intensive care units.

CONCLUSIONS: This study clearly shows trust is the key determinant of whether ICU nurses use AI. Belief in AI performance increases intention only when nurses trust the system. Colleague and leader support is the strongest route to build trust, whereas perceived risk erodes trust and discourages use. These results shift attention from utility to trust. We recommend a trust-first strategy for critical care: before deployment, ensure reliability, communicate risks transparently and have trusted experts demonstrate value, enabling safe, effective nurse-AI collaboration.

REPORTING METHOD: Authors adhered to the STROBE checklist for cross-sectional studies.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTIONS: This study did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct, or reporting.

articles.title: Effects of Ischemic Preconditioning on Post-exercise Injury Biomarkers, DOMS, and Endothelial Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute exercise, particularly at high intensity, confers physiological benefits but may also cause tissue injury. The protective effects of ischemic preconditioning (IPC) in clinical medicine have been demonstrated in some studies. This systematic review evaluated whether IPC applied before exercise can attenuate exercise-induced injury markers, muscle soreness, and endothelial dysfunction.

METHODS: Five databases were searched for peer-reviewed English-language studies published up to 29 June 2025. Three reviewers independently screened records using participants, intervention, control, outcome, study (PICOS) criteria for eligibility and assessed the risk of bias using Cochrane Risk of bias (RoB) 2 and Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Multilevel meta-analyses with cluster-robust variance adjustments were used to compare IPC with control conditions, with pooled effects reported as effect sizes (ES). Publication bias was evaluated using Egger's test. Evidence certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: A total of 13 studies (3 RCTs randomized controlled trials, 9 crossover, and 1 cross-sectional) with 263 participants (243 male, 20 female) were included. IPC significantly reduced delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) overall (ES = - 0.92, 95% CI - 1.83, - 0.01, p = 0.049), but only when applied locally (LIPC, ES = - 1.16, 95% CI - 1.82, - 0.50, p < 0.01) at 24 h (ES = - 1.04, p = 0.048) and 48 h (ES = - 1.16, p = 0.03) post-exercise. A favorable pooled effect on flow-mediated dilation was observed across heterogeneous protocols involving acute remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC), an acute comparison of LIPC with RIPC, and repeated LIPC (ES = 0.98, 95% CI 0.11-1.84, p = 0.03). No significant effects were observed for total creatine kinase (total CK, ES = - 0.38, 95% CI - 1.26, 0.50, p = 0.32) or cardiac troponin following RIPC (ES = 0.08, 95% CI - 1.79, 1.96, p = 0.86). No significant improvements in total CK were observed for acute or repeated IPC, LIPC, or RIPC (p > 0.05). Meta-regression identified recovery time as a significant moderator for cardiac troponin T (β = 0.02, p = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis is the first to systematically find that the protective effects of IPC can extend to certain exercise-induced injuries. Pre-exercise LIPC attenuated DOMS for up to 48 h, especially after high-intensity eccentric exercise, and may provide some protection against exercise-induced endothelial dysfunction. IPC did not significantly attenuate exercise-induced increases in injury biomarkers, although protective effects may emerge at later timepoints. Overall, IPC shows potential as a protective strategy against exercise-induced injury in sports medicine. However, the magnitude of its effects, optimal protocols, and the reliability of chronic application require confirmation in larger, higher-quality studies.

articles.title: Sudden cardiac death prevention in contemporary cardiovascular care: the role of the wearable cardioverter-defibrillator and coordinated reassessment.
articles.abstract: Successful cardiovascular treatment does not necessarily eliminate sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. After myocardial infarction, newly diagnosed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, or some other potentially high-risk conditions, clinicians must decide how to protect patients while treatment is optimized and the need for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) is reassessed.This review examines the evidence for the wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and its relevance to contemporary cardiovascular care. Randomized and observational studies inform patient selection, sustained wear, and reassessment, but appropriate device interventions should be distinguished from demonstrated mortality benefit. Contemporary medical therapy can reduce SCD risk and improve ventricular function, although optimization takes time and residual risk remains. Catheter ablation may address ventricular arrhythmia burden and residual substrate but does not replace an indicated ICD. Japanese studies suggest that some eligible patients may not receive a discussion regarding device-based protection.We propose protected risk reassessment: temporary protection when appropriate, treatment optimization, and a planned decision about subsequent device therapy. An identified SCD prevention doctor or team should coordinate this pathway. The role is defined primarily by commitment to prevention and responsibility for continuity of care, supported by ongoing education and access to specialist expertise, rather than by subspecialty or affiliation alone.The aim is to connect risk recognition with an informed treatment plan and ensure that each patient reaches reassessment. Substrate-directed ventricular tachycardia treatment, risk markers beyond LVEF, and questions after structural interventions provide additional context, but do not substitute for appropriate device protection. The optimal duration of temporary protection remains a research priority.Graphical Abstract Cardiovascular treatment may improve symptoms and hemodynamics without eliminating residual arrhythmic risk. Temporary protection with a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD), optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), assessment of the arrhythmogenic substrate, and ventricular arrhythmia treatment may inform individualized reassessment. Subsequent ICD decisions require risk assessment, patient preferences, and planned follow-up. The proposed SCD prevention doctor/team coordinates this process; the framework does not itself establish additional device indications or outcome benefits.

articles.title: Electrolyte deficiencies in adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit: a narrative review.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are ubiquitous in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). We sought to conduct a narrative review of hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypophosphatemia, and hypokalemia in critical care.

SOURCE: We searched Ovid MEDLINE®, Embase®, Cochrane CENTRAL, and reference lists for information relevant to the physiology, epidemiology, and treatment of electrolyte deficiencies in adults with critical illness. We also looked for information about financial costs and environmental impact of treatment.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Electrolyte deficiencies are common in patients admitted to the ICU, with prevalences of 55-88% for hypocalcemia, 27-66% for hypomagnesemia, 15-53% for hypophosphatemia, and 17-50% for hypokalemia. Neuromuscular and cardiovascular symptoms are common to all four deficiencies, and the benefits and harms of routine or protocolized treatment are uncertain. Calcium replacement is potentially fraught, with possible harm in cardiac arrest data, lack of any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) investigating replacement, and difficulties diagnosing deficiency outside of ionized calcium measurement. Prophylactic magnesium administration may prevent postoperative atrial fibrillation in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, but whether protocolized replacement reduces atrial fibrillation or mortality in patients with critical illness without cardiac problems is uncertain. Phosphate replacement may be relevant to ventilator weaning and ICU-acquired weakness, owing to its physiologic role in cellular energy and available clinical data. Potassium replacement has been investigated in large observational studies and an RCT, indicating that higher thresholds are not superior to lower ones. Enteral replacement is associated with lower costs and less environmental impact compared with the intravenous route.

CONCLUSIONS: Electrolyte deficiencies and their treatment are common in adult patients admitted to the ICU. The impact of particular thresholds and dosing strategies for treatment on patient outcomes, resource use, and the environment remain important areas for future research.

articles.title: Emodin Attenuates Lipid Accumulation by Regulating Iron Homeostasis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
articles.abstract: Abnormal lipid metabolism is a vital factor in the development of several chronic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, which are increasingly related to disruption in lipid and iron metabolism. Emodin (EM), an active anthraquinone derivative from Rheum palmatum, has shown promise in regulating lipid metabolism. However, its molecular mechanisms are still unclear. In this study, Saccharomyces cerevisiae treated with oleic acid (OA) was used as a cellular model of lipid accumulation to investigate the molecular mechanism by which emodin reduces lipid accumulation. Using Oil Red O staining, thin-layer chromatography, and microscopy, EM significantly reduced OA-induced lipid accumulation in yeast cells. Meanwhile, ICP-AES showed increased intracellular iron levels in OA-treated cells, whereas emodin treatment reduced these levels. Exogenous ferrous ions promoted yeast lipid accumulation and attenuated EM's lipid-lowering effect by elevating intracellular iron levels. In contrast, deferoxamine DFO, an iron chelator, simulated a low-iron environment, reversed this effect, and enhanced EM's lipid-lowering effect. Moreover, EM appeared to interact with Fe²⁺, resulting in formation of an insoluble complex under the experimental conditions. We then analyzed overlapping targets, lipid accumulation, and iron homeostasis using bioinformatics. Expression of key regulatory genes (FUS3, KSS1, HOG1, PKC1, and CMD1) increased with iron but decreased with emodin. In conclusion, our results suggest that emodin reduces lipid accumulation by modulating iron homeostasis and signaling pathways involved in iron-related lipid biosynthesis.

articles.title: Barriers to Bridges: Leveraging a Multidisciplinary Collaborative Care Model to Innovate Recruitment to Retention Pathways in School Mental Health.
articles.journal: The journal of behavioral health services & research
articles.abstract: Behavioral health workforce shortages limit efforts to address the growing youth mental health crisis, particularly in rural and underserved communities. The Multidisciplinary Pathways to Recruit, Train, and Retain School Mental Health Providers in Iowa (MPath) project was developed to address these shortages through a multidisciplinary workforce development model grounded in the Collaborative Care framework. This paper describes the MPath model and presents findings from a 4-year mixed-methods program evaluation. Data sources include administrative records, participant surveys, professional development evaluations, post-graduation surveys, and exit interviews from 48 scholars enrolled across three cohorts, with 21 graduates, 20 active scholars, and 7 withdrawals. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, with qualitative data analyzed through iterative coding and constant comparison. Findings indicate high levels of scholar satisfaction, particularly regarding financial support, mentoring, professional development, and practicum experiences. More than 90% of scholars reported that the program prepared them for their future careers, and professional development activities were associated with perceived gains in behavioral health knowledge and skills. Approximately 71% of graduates were employed at graduation, and most are working in positions aligned with their training and serving high-need schools or communities. Qualitative findings highlighted the importance of tuition assistance, multidisciplinary collaboration, and experiential learning. Results underscore the influence of broader policy and funding environments on workforce development efforts. Implications are discussed for strengthening behavioral health workforce pipelines through ecosystem-level investments in scholars, supervisors, partnerships, and training infrastructure.

articles.title: Association of Early Autonomic Dysfunction with Cerebral and Systemic Hemodynamics in Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Autonomic dysfunction is prevalent after severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) and associated with poor outcomes. Heart rate variability (HRV) reflects the dynamic balance between sympathetic and parasympathetic autonomic activity and can be readily examined using bedside cardiac waveforms. The relationship between autonomic dysfunction and cerebral perfusion is underexplored. We aimed to characterize the relationship between early autonomic dysfunction and cerebral and systemic hemodynamics after sTBI.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients enrolled in the BOOST-3 clinical trial with available cardiac and intracranial pressure (ICP) waveform data. Time-varying standard deviation of normal-normal intervals (SDNN) at 5-min resolution over the first 24 h postinjury was calculated. Cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) was calculated from dynamic ICP and mean arterial blood pressure (MAP) measurements. The association between time-varying SDNN, cerebral hemodynamics, and systemic hemodynamics was examined with moving correlation analysis and time-lagged linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Among 341 patients, the mean (SD) age was 41.8 (17.0) years, and 273 (80.1%) patients were male. Median (IQR) initial Glasgow Coma Scale score was 6 (4-7). On moving correlation analysis, lower SDNN correlated with lower CPP (peak r = 0.52 at 119 h postinjury, p < 0.001) over the first 5 days postinjury. In time-lagged models, lower SDNN was associated with lower MAP (peak standardized β = 0.019, p < 0.001) and lower CPP (peak standardized β = 0.025, p < 0.001) intermittently over 12 lag hours.

CONCLUSIONS: Early autonomic dysfunction after sTBI is associated with intermittently lower MAP and lower CPP in the subsequent 12 h. These results link early postinjury autonomic activity to altered hemodynamics and support further investigation of HRV in this population.

articles.title: Racialized Economic Polarization and Disparities in Diabetes Outcomes among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in North Carolina.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract: Black-White disparities in type 2 diabetes outcomes are stark, particularly in North Carolina, and reflect persistent inequities shaped by neighborhood conditions. One critical aspect of these conditions is the racialized distribution of economic resources. Racialized economic polarization captures the extent to which residents of a geographic area are concentrated at the extremes of racialized and socioeconomic deprivation and privilege and may represent an important upstream determinant of diabetes disparities. Yet, evidence linking racialized economic polarization to diabetes outcomes, particularly among patients already diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, remains sparse. We combined electronic health record data (2018-2022) from UNC Health and census tract data from the 2015-2019​American Community Survey 5-year estimates to (1) assess the relationship between racialized economic polarization and diabetes outcomes-including mean glycated hemoglobin (A1c), A1c variability, and dichotomized versions of each to represent high risk-among Black and White patients with type 2 diabetes​, and (2) determine whether these relationships vary by race. Results from ​linear regression and linear probability models​​ indicated that for White patients, living in census tracts with higher concentrations of high-income, White residents was associated with lower mean levels of A1c and A1c variability, as well as lower probabilities of high A1c and high A1c variability. Among Black patients, these associations were weaker and the association with A1c variability was ​​not statistically significant​. Findings underscore the importance of addressing upstream determinants of diabetes disparities and highlight the need for policies aimed at equitably distributing resources and expanding access to health-promoting opportunities in historically marginalized communities.

articles.title: Fosb mediates inflammation-related tubular senescence and maladaptive repair to drive the AKI-to-CKD transition.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common clinical disorder that often progresses to chronic kidney disease (CKD), driven by persistent inflammation and maladaptive repair. However, the specific mechanisms by which inflammation-driven tubular senescence mediates the AKI-to-CKD transition remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate the role of Fosb in inflammation-driven tubular senescence and the AKI-to-CKD transition.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We examined Fosb expression in renal tubules from AKI patients and multiple mouse models of AKI. Fosb-/- knockout mice were generated to evaluate its effects on primary cultured renal tubular epithelial cells (RTECs) dysfunction, cellular senescence and renal interstitial fibrosis. Furthermore, we elucidated the mechanism by which Fosb drives chronic progression of AKI both in vivo and in vitro.

RESULTS: ScRNA-seq revealed that Fosb is selectively enriched in the late stage of AKI and closely correlated with tubulointerstitial fibrosis. Fosb deficiency improved animal survival, alleviated renal damage, attenuated inflammation, tubular senescence, and fibrotic remodeling. Mechanistically, Fosb drives senescence and fibrosis by upregulating RNA-binding motif protein 11 (RBM11) and promoting its cytoplasmic redistribution in sepsis-induced RTECs. Cytoplasmic RBM11 binds to and inhibits protein phosphatase 2 A (PP2A), leading to dephosphorylation damage of Drp1-Ser637, which in turn induces mitochondrial dysfunction and renal tubular cell senescence, promoting the chronic progression of AKI. The pharmacological activation of PP2A by FTY720 effectively reversed RBM11 induced mitochondrial damage and cellular senescence.

CONCLUSION: The Fosb-RBM11-PP2A-Drp1 axis drives inflammation-related maladaptive repair and chronic progression after AKI, representing a promising target to block the AKI-to-CKD transition.

articles.title: FMF-TrackR: real-time digital monitoring of attack triggers in children with Familial Mediterranean Fever.
articles.abstract: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) attacks may be influenced by environmental and physiological factors, but evidence on potential triggers is largely retrospective. We aimed to prospectively characterize FMF attacks and their temporal relationship with patient-attributed potential triggers using a real-time digital monitoring platform. Children aged 8-18 years with FMF were prospectively followed from October 2025 to May 2026 using FMF-TrackR, a web-based platform combining weekly assessments with event-based real-time attack reporting. Attack characteristics, potential triggers, and infection onset were recorded contemporaneously. Eighty-five children were followed for 2620 person-weeks; 96.4% of scheduled weekly entries were completed. Forty-nine patients (57.6%) reported 79 attacks, corresponding to 3.02 attacks per 100 person-weeks. Median attack duration was 2.0 days (IQR 2.0-3.0). A potential trigger was reported in 46 attacks (58.2%). Infection was the most frequent trigger (24.1%), followed by psychological stress (17.7%). Infectious symptoms preceded attack onset by a median of 2.0 days (IQR 2.0-3.0). Arthralgia was more frequent in infection-attributed than stress-attributed attacks (57.9% vs. 28.6%, p = 0.048). All six hospital presentations occurred during infection-attributed attacks. Conclusions: Real-time digital monitoring enabled prospective, event-level characterization of FMF attacks and patient-attributed potential triggers with high completion rates. Infection and psychological stress were the most frequently reported triggers. The close temporal relationship between infection onset and FMF attacks highlights the value of contemporaneous monitoring for capturing transient exposures and attack patterns in pediatric FMF.

articles.title: Zinc Transporter Expression Diverges Between Blood and Airway Cells in Feedlot Steers with Bovine Respiratory Disease.
articles.abstract: Bovine respiratory disease (BRD) is a major welfare and economic concern in cattle. Zinc (Zn) is essential for immune function and is redistributed among tissues during infection as part of the acute phase response, yet how this is coordinated at the level of the Zn transport machinery in cattle is poorly understood. The objective was to characterize expression of Zn transporters (ZIP and ZnT families) and metallothioneins (MT) in whole blood (WB), nasopharyngeal swab cells (NPS), and bronchoalveolar lavage cells (BAL) during an experimental viral-bacterial co-infection, and whether expression was associated with disease severity. A secondary objective evaluated intranasal (IN) Zn and vitamin A (VA) treatments. Forty-eight Angus-cross steers were assigned to four IN treatments (n = 12/group): control, IN VA, IN Zn, or IN VA + Zn. Steers were inoculated with BRSV on d 0, treated on d4, and inoculated with Mannheimia haemolytica on d 5. WB and NPS were collected on d 0, 5, and 7, and BAL on d 0 and 7. Infection drove compartment-specific remodeling. In WB, several ZIP importers were downregulated on d 5 following BRSV infection while ZnT1, ZnT5, MT1A, and MTF-1 were upregulated (P ≤ 0.03). In contrast, NPS cells broadly upregulated ZIP importers, ZnT5, ZnT7, ZnT9, and MT by d 5 (P < 0.0001), and BAL cells showed broad upregulation of Zn import and export machinery by d 7 (P ≤ 0.02). IN Zn increased MT1A and MT2A expression in NPS on d 5, with treatment effects largely confined to the nasopharyngeal compartment. Expression in WB and NPS correlated with clinical score even under mild disease conditions. These findings indicate that nutritional immunity during BRD involves coordinated Zn transporter remodeling across multiple compartments, and that transporter expression in accessible sample types may reflect disease burden in cattle.

articles.title: Opportunistic identification of metabolic syndrome using abdominal CT-derived body composition: a comparative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the performance of abdominal CT-based body composition indices, novel simplified indices, traditional measures, and laboratory findings in identifying metabolic syndrome (MetS) under a definition that excludes waist circumference (WC).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-center study enrolled 3089 adults between January 2020 and June 2025. Patients were classified into MetS and metabolically healthy groups according to the Guideline for the Prevention and Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes in China (2020 edition). Deep learning tools (TotalSegmentator and BOA) were used to quantify adipose tissue, skeletal muscle, and bone at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) level. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were compared using DeLong tests. Subgroup analyses were performed by gender and BMI categories.

RESULTS: In total, 3089 patients (median age 63 years [Q1-Q3, 55-71], 1481 men) were evaluated. Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) area at the L3 level had the highest AUC (0.723), outperforming WC (0.689) and BMI (0.605) (all p < 0.001). Its performance was comparable to a multivariable model (AUC 0.723 vs. 0.728, p = 0.067). In subgroup analyses, the VAT area achieved the highest AUC in the normal-weight group (0.745), the obese group (0.680), the male group (0.686), and the female group (0.722). Inflammatory markers, muscle, and bone had lower AUCs (0.55-0.63).

CONCLUSIONS: The VAT area is the individual index with the highest discriminatory performance among those evaluated for identifying MetS, comparable to that of complex models. It may be measured opportunistically on routine abdominal CT, and may offer adjunctive value for normal-weight individuals.

KEY POINTS: Question The value of quantitative body composition analysis in identifying metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains to be further clarified. Findings Under a waist circumference-free MetS definition, L3 visceral adipose tissue area outperformed novel simplified indices, traditional anthropometric measures, and laboratory biomarkers in total and subgroups. Critical relevance statement Routine abdominal CT can opportunistically measure visceral adipose tissue area at L3 as an adjunctive risk marker, and may aid in identifying MetS in normal-weight individuals, thereby providing guidance for lifestyle interventions.

articles.title: Rewilding the lung: environmental exposures recalibrate pulmonary immunity and respiratory mechanics with implications for allergy and asthma research.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract: For decades, immunologists have relied on specific pathogen-free (SPF) laboratory mice to study immune function, yet these models often lack environmental exposures that shape human immunity. The impact of such environmental factors on pulmonary immunity and respiratory mechanics remains underexplored. Here we discuss recent work by Bouali and colleagues where indoor rewilding of laboratory mice introduced ecological complexity, leading to expanded pulmonary immune cell populations and altered respiratory mechanics without lung injury. These findings reveal that pulmonary immunity is highly adaptable and continuously influenced by environmental experience. This environmental calibration enhances the physiological relevance of preclinical allergy and asthma models by better reflecting the immune diversity and heterogeneity observed in human disease, thereby offering new insights into disease susceptibility and therapeutic responses.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in PM2.5-associated pulmonary inflammation: a critical appraisal of mechanistic and causal evidence.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PM2.5 exposure is consistently associated with respiratory inflammation, and experimental studies increasingly implicate ferroptosis. However, lipid-peroxidation markers and protection by broad-spectrum antioxidants do not establish that ferroptotic cell death drives inflammation.

OBJECTIVE: To appraise the evidence that ferroptosis causally contributes to PM2.5-associated pulmonary disease.

APPROACH: This critical review appraised respiratory studies identified through literature searches initially conducted in Europe PMC and OpenAlex up to 26 September 2026, with supplementary database searching during revision. Particular attention was given to exposure design, intervention specificity, functional outcomes, cell type, and human evidence. Because study selection was performed by a single reviewer without independent duplicate screening, eligible studies may have been missed and eligibility decisions may have been subject to selection bias. The findings therefore represent a critical appraisal of the examined literature rather than an exhaustive systematic synthesis.

FINDINGS: It is well established that PM2.5 exposure elicits iron- and lipid-peroxidation-related responses in airway cells, and ferroptosis-directed inhibitors and selected genetic perturbations attenuate both lipid injury and airway phenotypes in allergic-airway and acute-injury models. The evidence is weaker and partly conflicting where protection is achieved with Nrf2 activators and other multipotent interventions, which cannot isolate ferroptosis from parallel antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.

THREE GAPS PREDOMINATE: Three gaps predominate: whole-lung measurements obscure cell-specific mechanisms; bolus instillation and high in vitro doses limit exposure translation; and human findings remain largely associative. Asthma, fibrosis, and combined-pollutant experiments address distinct questions and cannot support a single pooled effect.

CONCLUSION: Ferroptosis is a plausible contributor to PM2.5-related pulmonary inflammation, but its necessity and clinical importance remain incompletely established. Factorial rescue studies, orthogonal cell-restricted genetic tests, realistic aerosol exposure, and prospective human validation would provide more decisive evidence.

articles.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

articles.title: Ebola virus-based antibody products cross-neutralize 2026 Bundibugyo virus glycoprotein.
articles.abstract: The ongoing 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) disease has highlighted the urgent need for therapeutic countermeasures. Whether Ebola virus (EBOV)-induced antibodies can cross-neutralize contemporary BDBVs is unclear. Here we test a diverse panel of EBOV-derived polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies, including plasma from humans after EBOV infection and horse plasma and mice serum immunized with available EBOV immunogens, against vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudotypes presenting BDBV-2026 glycoprotein (GP). We find that all antibodies retain cross-neutralizing activity against BDBV-2026 glycoprotein. These findings identify existing Ebola virus-derived antibody preparations as candidates for rapid evaluation.

articles.title: Epithelial cell adhesion molecule on alveolar macrophages promotes the clearance of pulmonary bacterial infections.
articles.abstract: Alveolar macrophages (AMs) serve as a critical first line of defence against respiratory pathogens and ensure lung function during both infection and steady-state conditions. They express several surface markers, including epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM, also known as CD326), whose role remains unclear. Here we show that EpCAM is a distinct surface marker of fetal-derived AMs, distinguishing them from other tissue-resident macrophages. Although it is dispensable for their homeostatic function, it contributes to efficient uptake and timely clearance of respiratory bacterial pathogens including Streptococcus pneumoniae and Legionella pneumophila. During influenza infection, EpCAM is rapidly downregulated in AMs via TNF-mediated NF-κB signalling, and the Epcam locus undergoes sustained chromatin repression and epigenetic remodelling. Its downregulation persists after viral clearance, and AMs from virus-infected mice show significantly reduced bacterial uptake. This suggests that viral infection reprogrammes AMs, contributing to increased susceptibility to secondary bacterial infection. These findings uncover a previously unknown role for EpCAM and highlight its potential impact on AM phenotypic plasticity.

articles.title: Deep learning-based retinal biomarker for cardiovascular risk capturing the microvascular-macrovascular continuum in type 2 diabetes: a multi-cohort external validation study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes elevate CVD risk, but no biomarker has yet captured this microvascular-macrovascular continuum. We evaluated whether a deep learning-derived retinal biomarker (the Dr Noon CVD score) reflects increasing macrovascular risk alongside microvascular burden.

METHODS: Participants from the Hanyang dataset (N=301) were stratified into three groups according to microvascular burden: no diabetic retinopathy or renal involvement, diabetic retinopathy without renal involvement, and both diabetic retinopathy and renal involvement. Associations between the retinal biomarker and microvascular burden were assessed using multivariable linear regression with adjustment for conventional risk factors and either the pooled cohort equations (PCE) score or the PREVENT scores (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular disease EVENTs). Additional subgroup analyses further stratified participants according to the severity of retinopathy and renal involvement, and external validation was also performed in two longitudinal cohorts, the Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disease Etiology Research Center-High Risk cohort (CMERC-HI; N=270) and a UK Biobank cohort (N=2655).

RESULTS: The retinal biomarker increased stepwise with greater microvascular burden in the Hanyang dataset (3.79 points per group; 95% CI 2.55, 5.03), corresponding to an effect size that is comparable to approximately 10 years of ageing. This gradient remained robust after adjustment for the PCE or PREVENT scores, and was replicated in severity-based subgroup analyses (β=1.80 per group; 95% CI 1.34, 2.25). These graded increases in the retinal biomarker across microvascular complication groups were replicated in external cohorts (CMERC-HI, β=3.67; 95% CI 2.43, 4.91; UK Biobank, β=1.58; 95% CI 1.06, 2.11), in parallel with stepwise increases in cardiovascular event incidence across microvascular burden groups (CMERC-HI: 1.1, 8.4 and 25.1 per 1000 person-years, respectively; UK Biobank: 7.3, 9.0 and 21.8 per 1000 person-years, respectively). In survival analyses, the retinal biomarker remained independently associated with incident cardiovascular events (CMERC-HI: HR per 1 SD=1.76; 95% CI 1.06, 2.93; UK Biobank: HR per 1 SD=1.35; 95% CI 1.14, 1.61), and addition of the retinal biomarker to the model attenuated the HRs associated with microvascular complication groups by approximately 17-37%.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: The retinal biomarker reflected increasing macrovascular risk with microvascular burden, offering the possibility of independent risk stratification beyond that captured by conventional scores, and supporting its potential for use in integrated vascular assessments in diabetes care.

articles.title: Point-of-care ketone patterns and monitoring practices in youth with type 1 diabetes using dapagliflozin as adjunct-to-insulin therapy as part of the ATTEMPT study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: We aimed to describe elevated ketone events (EKEs; temporally related clusters of β-hydroxybutyrate ≥0.6 mmol/l) in the Adolescent Type 1 Diabetes Treatment with SGLT2i for Hyperglycemia and Hyperfiltration Trial, evaluating adjunct-to-insulin use of dapagliflozin (5 mg/day for 16 weeks) vs placebo.

METHODS: During the trial, participants received education regarding use of the STOP DKA Protocol, a diabetic ketoacidosis risk mitigation strategy, and instruction to monitor ketones during illness and at-risk situations. As part of this secondary analysis, relative frequency and severity of EKEs, associated blood glucose levels and participants' monitoring practices were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 2906 unique point-of-care ketone readings, 93.4% were non-elevated. Observation of 146 EKEs revealed more events in participants receiving dapagliflozin compared with placebo (101 vs 45; p<0.001; n=48 in each group). This difference was driven by moderate EKEs (0.6-1.4 mmol/l), with only one case of diabetic ketoacidosis seen in the dapagliflozin group. Associated blood glucose levels were lower with dapagliflozin than with placebo (8.3 mmol/l vs 18.3 mmol/l; p<0.001). Ketone monitoring frequency was similar between groups (p=0.106). Repeat ketone checks were observed in 63.0% of EKEs.

CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Adjunctive low-dose dapagliflozin was largely associated with normal ketone levels and few EKEs. Events occurred in both study arms, with a greater frequency, but not increased severity, in the dapagliflozin arm. Participants demonstrated consistent repeat ketone checking and only one diabetic ketoacidosis event occurred, suggesting structured mitigation tools may help prevent progression to diabetic ketoacidosis. These findings underscore the importance of monitoring ketone trends per a risk mitigation protocol in enabling the safe use of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors in youth with type 1 diabetes.

articles.title: Dengue has exploded globally with shocking speed.
Metabolic memory in adipose tissue.
articles.abstract: Long-term studies of diabetes complications established the concept of metabolic memory and inspired a broader search for forms of biological memory across metabolically active tissues. Here, we propose that adipose tissue serves as a tissue-level hub of metabolic memory, retaining molecular and cellular imprints of past physiological states that shape future responses. We discuss evidence that cold exposure and thermogenic remodelling prime adipose tissue for enhanced adaptation to subsequent challenges, and examine the emerging concept of obesity memory, including whether adipose tissue preserves a record of prior obesity after weight loss and whether this memory can be erased over time. Finally, we consider the clinical implications of this framework for childhood obesity and the growing population of patients cycling on and off incretin-based therapies, highlighting key opportunities for mechanistic and translational discovery.

articles.title: Dual HSP90/HDAC6 inhibition remodels the tumor microenvironment to enhance cancer immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: Tumor microenvironment (TME) arises from dynamic and reciprocal interactions between cancer cells and stromal components such as immune cells, fibroblasts, and tumor vasculature, thereby generating extensive intratumoral heterogeneity that underlies resistance to many anticancer therapies. Addressing this complexity requires strategies that move beyond single-target interventions to engage hub proteins coordinating multiple malignant pathways at integrated regulatory nodes. Here, we developed PSY-3-11, a rationally designed dual inhibitor of heat shock protein 90 and histone deacetylase 6, and validated its coordinated antitumor activities. PSY-3-11 induced multifaceted remodeling across TME compartments by suppressing pathological angiogenesis, promoting vascular normalization, reducing epithelial-mesenchymal transition and PD-L1 expression, and reprogramming immunosuppressive myeloid populations toward an M1-like phenotype. In syngeneic tumor models, it markedly enhanced CD8⁺ T cell infiltration, activation, and cytotoxic readiness. Moreover, when combined with CTLA-4 blockade, PSY-3-11 produced robust and durable antitumor responses without increasing systemic toxicity, including in immunologically "cold" tumors that typically fail to respond to checkpoint inhibitors. Collectively, PSY-3-11 represents a promising immunomodulatory therapeutic candidate capable of reconditioning the heterogeneous TME and overcoming intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy. Its mechanism and favorable safety profile support its use as a combination-ready adjuvant to potentiate a range of cancer immunotherapies, including checkpoint inhibitors and adoptive cell therapies.

articles.title: Examining the impact of genome-wide findings for tobacco use through GWAS-impact analysis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) transformed our understanding of complex trait genetics by identifying thousands of disease-associated variants. A tobacco use GWAS by Liu and colleagues, published in 2019, represents a landmark achievement in addiction genetics, identifying 406 loci associated with tobacco use behaviors. Despite widespread citation, the research impact and translational applications of these findings remain uncharacterized.

METHODS: We conducted a 'GWAS-impact analysis', systematically searching PubMed and Web of Science for studies citing Liu et al. 10 through June 2023. Studies were included if they utilized tobacco use summary statistics in follow-up analyses. Two reviewers independently screened articles and extracted data on phenotypes, analytical methods, and clinical applications. We used ADHD as a case study to illustrate how different analytical approaches can be applied to investigate a single phenotype relationship.

RESULTS: We identified 345 studies investigating tobacco use in relation to 1857 phenotypes across diverse health domains. General substance use (n = 203), Interventions on whole body (n = 124; an ICHI chapter that includes BMI and other anthropometric measurements), and Mental, behavioral or neurodevelopmental disorders (n = 100) dominated the research landscape. Mendelian randomization was the predominant analytical approach ( ~ 72% of studies), followed by polygenic score analyses and genetic correlation methods. Only three studies examined clinical applications. Version reporting was often inconsistent. Of the 345 included studies, 134 (38.8%) could not be classified by which version of the summary statistics they used, and only 22 (6.4%) reported using the version computed without UK Biobank participants.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings map research uptake while exposing a persistent translational gap, indicating the need for standardized phenotyping, triangulated causal inference, and evaluations establishing whether tobacco genetics adds clinical value beyond existing risk assessment.

articles.title: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus.
articles.abstract: Since early 2024, highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus (clade 2.3.4.4b) has caused outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle, infecting other mammals including humans. Here, we evaluate the protective efficacy of two commercially available seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 isolate, A/Texas/37/2024, in influenza-naïve female ferrets. All unvaccinated ferrets develop severe disease and succumb to infection or meet humane euthanasia criteria. Immunisation with an inactivated influenza vaccine reduces viral titres in multiple respiratory and extrapulmonary tissues and delays disease progression but does not prevent fatal outcomes. By contrast, five of six ferrets immunised with a live attenuated influenza vaccine survive challenge and show more effective control of viral replication in the nasal mucosa. Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract.

articles.title: Predictive uncertainty representations in clinical AI shape physicians' advice uptake, accuracy, and trust.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Machine-learning-based clinical decision support is entering routine care, but its value depends on whether clinicians can judge when to follow its advice and when to override it. Evidence suggests this judgment is often poorly calibrated in both directions. Whether displaying a model's predictive uncertainty helps physicians integrate advice more selectively is unclear.

METHODS: In a preregistered, randomized vignette experiment, 227 physicians produced 1,802 sepsis risk assessments. Physicians gave an initial risk estimate, saw advice from a machine-learning system, and revised their estimate. They were randomized to see a risk score alone, or the score together with one of two visual representations of predictive uncertainty: icon arrays with uncertainty bands, or quantile dotplots. Outcomes were advice uptake, accuracy of the revised risk estimate, and trust.

RESULTS: Here we show that both uncertainty representations increase advice uptake relative to the risk score alone, by 23% and 21%, and that the gap between correct and incorrect advice is descriptively about twice as large. Uptake of incorrect advice is not reliably reduced. Both formats improve the accuracy of revised risk estimates, with the larger effect for quantile dotplots, but only icon arrays increase trust. Physicians describe uncertainty as actionable only where they can tell why it is elevated.

CONCLUSIONS: Displaying predictive uncertainty changes how physicians integrate machine-learning advice, but the representation format determines whether the benefit appears mainly as accuracy or trust. The effect is partial: uncertainty representations support recognizing reliable advice more than rejecting unreliable advice.

articles.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes.
authors: Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank Study Group
articles.abstract: Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort (N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) (N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, Plog-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, plog-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c (pAUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant (p = 0.035) and age-related (p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

articles.title: Age at Migration and Health Shock Resilience.
articles.abstract: Using comprehensive data on the Swedish population, we document that massive age-specific immigrant-native hospitalization gaps during the COVID-19 pandemic were strongly related to host-country exposure during childhood. Exploiting variation between siblings, we test and systematically rule out several potential explanations for the role of host-country exposure: it is not attributable to (i) shared family characteristics (e.g., genetics), (ii) birthplace-specific factors, (iii) known pre-existing medical risk factors, (iv) social or economic segregation, or (v) differences in vaccination behavior.
