articles.title: External Validation of the COLOFIT Colorectal Cancer Risk Prediction Model Across a Whole English Health System: A Cohort Study of 137,149 Symptomatic Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Faecal immunochemical testing (FIT) triages suspected colorectal cancer in English primary care, but fewer than 5% of patients with a positive test have cancer. COLOFIT combines FIT with age, sex, platelet count and mean corpuscular volume to estimate one-year cancer risk, but has been externally validated only in single NHS trusts.

AIMS: To externally validate COLOFIT across a whole English health system and estimate its effect on urgent referrals and cancer detection.

METHODS: We linked all primary care FIT requests in South Yorkshire and Bassetlaw (2022-2024) to full blood counts from five laboratory systems and colorectal cancer diagnoses within 1 year. The published COLOFIT equation, without recalibration, was compared with FIT thresholds of 10 and 20 μg/g, including decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: COLOFIT was calculable for 137,149 of 151,429 requests (90.6%); 1253 patients (0.9%) had colorectal cancer. COLOFIT discriminated better than FIT alone (c-statistic 0.90 vs. 0.88; p < 0.0001) but over-predicted risk (observed-to-expected ratio 0.78), reflecting lower baseline incidence (calibration slope 0.95). A 1% COLOFIT threshold would have avoided 5462 urgent referrals (18.7%; 95% confidence interval 18.3%-19.2%), with 27 additional cancers (95% confidence interval 16-39) not urgently referral over 3 years (approximately 200 referrals avoided per additional cancer). COLOFIT had greater net benefit than FIT at all threshold probabilities (0.1%-5%).

CONCLUSIONS: COLOFIT was calculable from routine data for 9 in 10 patients and would reduce urgent referrals by almost one-fifth, at a small, quantified cost in cancers requiring safety-netting. Findings support national adoption with routine outcome monitoring.

articles.title: A glutathione/cellulase dual-stimuli responsive dual-fungicide nanoplatform enables synergistic inhibition of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum and boosts rapeseed defense.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sclerotinia stem rot, caused by Sclerotinia sclerotiorum, threatens global rapeseed production. Increasing fungicide use accelerates pathogen resistance, necessitating combinations of fungicides with distinct modes of action. Stimuli-responsive nano-formulations co-delivering dual agrochemicals offer a transformative strategy for disease management. Here, we engineered a glutathione (GSH)/cellulase dual-stimuli-responsive nano-formulation, Azo/Bos@DMSNs-EMC, co-encapsulating azoxystrobin (Azo) and boscalid (Bos) for precision control of S. sclerotiorum.

RESULTS: The delivery platform utilizes epichlorohydrin-crosslinked carboxymethyl cellulose (EMC)-coated dendritic mesoporous silica nanoparticles, achieving a total drug loading of 15.13%. Under simulated infection conditions (1 mg mL-1 GSH + 0.2 mg mL-1 cellulase), the system exhibited remarkable enzyme-triggered release, discharging 90.5% of Azo and 91.9% of Bos within 72 h. Bioassay results demonstrated that the dual-loaded nanoformulation exhibited a significant synergistic effect. In pot trials, Azo/Bos@DMSNs-EMC maintained 53.6% therapeutic efficacy at 14 days post-treatment, significantly outperforming the commercial suspension concentrate (24.1%). The formulation enhanced plant disease resistance by upregulating defense-related enzymes (SOD, PPO, POD, PAL, GST) and key resistance genes (BnaGSTU5, BnaGSTU25, BnaGSTZ1, BnaPAL1, and BnaSOD3). Furthermore, the nanocarrier exhibited 2.37-fold lower acute toxicity to earthworms than conventional formulations, indicating improved safety for non-target organisms.

CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that Azo/Bos@DMSNs-EMC, a dual-stimuli-responsive and dual-loaded pesticide delivery system, not only enables targeted pesticide release within plant tissues and enhances pathogen suppression via fungicide synergism, but also effectively induces and activates endogenous defense enzymes in rapeseed. This technology provides a novel strategy for the eco-friendly control of rapeseed sclerotinia stem rot. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Assessing the methodological quality of meta-analyses of exercise interventions for gestational diabetes: Application of the AMSTAR 2 tool.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIM: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a common pregnancy complication that increases maternal and fetal health risks and substantially elevates the likelihood of developing type 2 diabetes postpartum. Effective, evidence-based management is crucial. This study aimed to assess the methodological quality of meta-analyses on exercise interventions for women with GDM using the AMSTAR 2 tool and identify factors influencing research quality.

METHODS: Relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses were systematically identified through PubMed and Web of Science, and seven were included after rigorous screening. Methodological quality was assessed with AMSTAR 2, while differences by the characteristics of the included reviews were analysed using normality testing, independent-samples t-tests and Mann-Whitney U tests. Inter-rater reliability was calculated with Cohen's Kappa coefficient.

RESULTS: All seven included systematic reviews and meta-analyses were rated 'Critically Low' in methodological quality. For critical items 4 and 7, 71.4% and 57.1% of reviews, respectively, were rated 'Partial Yes'; none received a 'Yes' rating for either item. Comparative analysis showed no statistically significant differences in quality scores based on publication year, number of authors, study duration, research focus or number of included studies. However, funding status showed a statistically significant association with quality scores (t = 2.988, p = 0.031).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that the overall methodological quality of meta-analyses on exercise interventions for GDM remains low, underscoring the need for standardised guidelines that incorporate AMSTAR 2-based methodological evaluation. Until more methodologically rigorous systematic reviews become available, clinicians should interpret the current meta-analytic evidence with caution, and clinical practice guidelines should consider both intervention effectiveness and the methodological quality of the supporting evidence.

articles.title: [Diabetic striatopathy revealed by the rapid correction of severe hyperglycemia: Case report and literature analysis].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetic striatopathy (DS) is a rare and poorly understood neurometabolic complication of poorly controlled diabetes mellitus, whose pathogenesis remains poorly understood.

CASE STUDY: A 53-year-old patient with no prior medical history was hospitalized for polyuria-polydipsia, which led to the discovery of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c]: 14.4%) without ketosis. After four weeks of insulin therapy, which rapidly corrected the HbA1c (7.4%), involuntary movements of hemi-chorea/ballism of right limbs and face developed. Brain MRI showed bilateral thalamic, external capsules, and left subthalamic nucleus hyperintensities.

CONCLUSION: Rapid correction of hyperglycemia is a possible fourth etiological and pathophysiological factor-and a diagnostic feature-that has been rarely reported in cases of SD.

articles.title: A Japanese adolescent case of Chung-Jansen syndrome with obesity, diabetes mellitus and a rare missense variant of PHIP p.(Phe17Cys).
articles.abstract: We report on a 13-year-old girl who presented with intellectual disabilities, behavioral abnormalities, dysmorphic features, obesity and diabetes mellitus. Whole-exome sequencing identified a rare PHIP variant (NM_017934.7: c.50T > G p.(Phe17Cys)) in the patient, corresponding to the diagnosis of Chung-Jansen syndrome. At age 16, oral aripiprazole treatment was initiated because behavioral problems and anxiety aggravated. Subsequently, chronic hyperglycemia and obesity worsened. At age 18, hemoglobin A1c and body mass index increased to 9.4% and 33 kg/m2. The initiation of subcutaneous insulin and tirzepatide therapy successfully improved her glycemic control. This is the first report to describe the detailed clinical phenotype of the PHIP p.(Phe17Cys) variant, providing valuable insight into pathogenicity despite its previous registration in ClinVar and gnomAD.

articles.title: Extrahepatic malignancies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: from epidemiologic association to risk prediction and screening.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has been associated with an increased risk of extrahepatic malignancies, although these associations vary across cancer sites and populations. Given the high prevalence of MASLD and its close relationship with established cancer risk factors, epidemiological associations alone are insufficient to inform screening decisions. The key clinical question is whether information obtained during routine MASLD assessment can improve cancer-specific risk prediction to guide clinical management. In this Review, we examine the evidence for risk stratification beyond established cancer risk factors, focusing on fibrosis severity, metabolic phenotype, genetic susceptibility, and routinely available non-invasive tests. Although the fibrosis-4 index and selected MASLD phenotypes have been associated with incident malignancy, most studies rely on composite cancer outcomes, with limited evidence for site-specific discrimination, calibration, incremental predictive value, or external validation. Associations between liver stiffness and extrahepatic cancer have also been inconsistent, leaving the independent contribution of fibrosis severity to extrahepatic cancer risk uncertain. No MASLD-related measure provides validated cancer-specific absolute-risk estimates sufficient to justify modifying established screening strategies. Colorectal cancer represents a promising setting for evaluating risk-adapted approaches. Future research should prioritize cancer-specific prediction models, establish clinically actionable absolute-risk thresholds, and determine whether incorporating MASLD-related measures into screening decisions improves clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The exposome in myositis: environmental triggers and disease modulation.
articles.abstract: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are heterogeneous autoimmune diseases in which environmental and iatrogenic exposures may influence susceptibility, phenotype and disease course. The exposome framework extends beyond isolated triggers by integrating general external, specific external and internal exposures across the life course and their interaction with host genetics. We review evidence for ultraviolet and geoclimatic factors, inhalational and occupational exposures, infections and SARS-CoV-2, drugs, microbiome and metabolic factors, lifestyle, reproductive and early-life exposures, and gene-environment interactions. The strongest exposure-autoimmunity models are statin-associated anti-HMGCR immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myositis; ultraviolet radiation and smoking show phenotype-specific epidemiological signals, whereas evidence for the internal exposome remains largely associative. Emphasis is placed on causal inference, reverse causation and the distinction between temporal signals and population-level risk, as well as on the difference between causal confidence and clinical actionability, from which practice points and a research agenda are derived.

articles.title: The effects of brief motivational interviewing by general practitioners for patients with type 2 diabetes: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brief motivational interviewing (brief MI) is a patient-centered approach designed for use within time-limited primary care consultations to support behavior change and diabetes self-management. General practitioners (GPs) play a central role in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) management; however, evidence regarding the effectiveness of brief MI delivered by GPs remains unclear. This systematic review evaluated the effectiveness of brief MI delivered by GPs for adults with T2DM in primary care settings.

METHODS: A systematic search of Scopus, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, Ovid, PubMed, Wiley Online Library, Google Scholar, and Consensus was conducted from database inception to March 2026. Randomized and non-randomized studies evaluating brief MI training or implementation by GPs for adults with T2DM were included. Outcomes included GP-related outcomes (knowledge, confidence, counseling behavior, and adherence to MI techniques) and patient-related outcomes (glycemic control, cardiovascular risk factors, behavioral outcomes, and psychosocial outcomes). Study quality was assessed using the Jadad scale and Joanna Briggs Institute tools.

RESULTS: Five studies involving 338 GPs, 1409 patients with T2DM, and 190 healthcare facilities met the inclusion criteria; four were randomized controlled trials and one was a non-randomized trial. Brief MI training ranged from a 4-hour workshop with web-based modules to 1.5-day and 3-day training programs, with follow-up ranging from 3 to 12 months. Brief MI training generally improved GPs' knowledge, confidence, and patient-centered practices. Among studies assessing patient outcomes, two reported significant short-term improvements in HbA1c associated with brief MI, whereas a one-year study found improvements in metabolic status in both intervention and control groups without an additional overall benefit of brief MI. Improvements were also reported in selected outcomes, including blood pressure, lipid profiles, body weight, patient motivation, and understanding of diabetes management; however, these effects were inconsistent across studies. Evidence regarding sustained behavioral change, medication adherence, and long-term metabolic outcomes remained limited.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence regarding brief MI delivered by GPs for patients with T2DM remains limited and inconclusive. Brief MI may improve GP practices and provide modest short-term benefits in patient motivation and selected cardiometabolic outcomes; however, evidence for sustained long-term effectiveness remains insufficient. Larger pragmatic primary care trials with standardized brief MI training, implementation-fidelity assessment, and longer follow-up are needed to determine its clinical effectiveness and sustainability in routine diabetes care.

articles.title: Prevalence and outcomes of bloodstream infections caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria in the emergency department: results from a prospective multicentre study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are a major cause of sepsis and septic shock cases presenting to the Emergency Department (ED). The aim of the present study was to determine the prevalence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) among patients presenting to the ED with BSI, to identify factors associated, and describe their impact on clinical outcomes.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted an observational prospective multicentre study, involving 7 centres, including all adult patients admitted between January 2025 and October 2025 with a confirmed BSI. Primary outcome was to determine the prevalence of BSIs caused by MDROs and the factors associated with MDROs BSI.

RESULTS: We included 210 patients with a confirmed BSI: the origin of BSI was the urinary tract in 44.3% of subjects; Gram-negative bacteria accounted for 68.6% of cases, mainly Enterobacterales (60.9%). A MDRO was isolated in 56 (29.2%) of the 192 patients with available susceptibility data. The presence of a urinary catheter was the only independent predictor of MDRO BSI (OR 3.423, 95% CI 1.522-7.695; p = 0.003). Overall, 28-day and 7-day mortality and clinical response rate were 34.2%, 10.3% and 46.1%, respectively. A higher baseline SOFA score was independently associated with 28-day mortality (OR 1.379, 95% CI 1.009-1.885; p = 0.044), whereas infectious disease consultation resulted as a protective factor (OR 0.137, 95% CI 0.021-0.901; p = 0.039).

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of BSIs diagnosed in the ED were caused by MDROs. Knowledge of local resistance epidemiology and early identification of patients at increased risk of MDRO infections are essential to optimize empirical antibiotic therapy and improve clinical outcomes.

The Prognostic Value of PSMA-total Tumor Volume for Overall Survival in mHSPC: Exploratory Evaluation Within the ENZAMET Trial and PROMISE Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ChemoHormonal Therapy Versus Androgen Ablation Randomized Trial for Extensive Disease in Prostate Cancer (CHAARTED) risk stratification is an important risk stratification tool in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC). However, clinicians are increasingly using prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET)/computed tomography (CT).

OBJECTIVE: Here, the prognostic value of PSMA-total tumor volume (PSMA-TTV) for overall survival (OS) in a developmental cohort from the Enzalutamide in First-Line Androgen Deprivation Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer (ENZAMET) trial with validation in the larger Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) Registry was evaluated.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants who underwent PSMA-PET/CT before enrolment in the prospective phase 3 ENZAMET trial (development cohort) or were classified as having mHSPC in the ongoing international PROMISE Registry (validation cohort) were included, and PSMA-TTV was derived using a semiautomated method. In the ENZAMET dataset, the association of PSMA-TTV categories with time to progression and OS in addition to CHAARTED groups by conventional imaging, was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests. ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV categories were tested in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and log-rank tests and Cox regression analyses.

RESULTS AND LIMITATIONS: Overall, 100 patients from ENZAMET and 993 patients from the PROMISE Registry were analyzed. The upper ENZAMET-derived PSMA-TTV category was ≥72 ml. In patients with CHAARTED criteria low-volume disease, 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml versus <72 ml was 36% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 16-83) versus 71% (60-85; p = 0.019) in survival curves; 5-yr OS for PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml was not associated with shorter OS in the ENZAMET subgroup (50% [32-78] vs 73% [63-85]; p = 0.063) but in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup (33% [27-40] vs 78% [75-81]; p < 0.001). The hazard ratio for upper PSMA-TTV category ≥72 ml was 6.8 (95% CI = 5.3-8.7) in the PROMISE mHSPC subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: PSMA-TTV ≥72 ml from an ENZAMET cohort is prognostic for OS in the PROMISE mHSPC cohort. Further validation of PSMA-TTV as a prognostic biomarker with potential to be a predictive marker to identify patients for intensification is warranted.

The role of microRNAs, miR-30d and miR-126 in the progression of obesity to type 2 diabetes: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obesity represents the first stage of the metabolic continuum leading to insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes (T2D), and a variable risk of vascular complications. In this context, microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as biomarkers reflecting early metabolic alterations. Among them, miR-30d and miR-126 have been extensively studied; however, their behavior across metabolic progression remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically analyze the available evidence on the expression of miR-30d and miR-126 in adults with overweight, obesity, prediabetes, and T2D, and to evaluate their potential utility as biomarkers of metabolic progression.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Original studies in adults (≥18 years) evaluating the expression of miR-30d and/or miR-126 in serum or plasma within the target populations were included. Searches were performed in PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Wiley Online Library for studies published between 2010 and 2025.

RESULTS: Thirty-one studies involving a total of 3917 participants were included. miR-30d exhibited heterogeneous expression in prediabetes and a consistent tendency toward upregulation in T2D, particularly in the presence of microvascular complications, demonstrating discriminatory capacity. In contrast, miR-126 showed early deregulation, with reduced expression in T2D and in patients with vascular complications, and demonstrated diagnostic utility that increased when combined with clinical variables.

CONCLUSIONS: miR-30d and miR-126 display distinct expression patterns across the metabolic continuum. While miR-30d is associated with disease progression and severity in advanced T2D, miR-126 emerges as an early marker of endothelial dysfunction. Their combined assessment may provide complementary value for metabolic risk stratification.

articles.title: Sensor-detected hypoglycaemia in type 1 diabetes: An outcome-specific narrative review of counterregulation, severe hypoglycaemia, chronic complications and quality of life.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has made visible large numbers of hypoglycaemic episodes that people with type 1 diabetes (T1D) do not perceive, and the clinical significance of this sensor-detected hypoglycaemia (SDH) remains contested. We examine whether SDH is clinically meaningful, arguing that its significance is outcome-dependent.

METHODS: We narratively synthesised evidence on the association between SDH and four outcomes-glucose counterregulation, severe hypoglycaemia, chronic complications, and quality of life-in adults with T1D, focusing on time below range and the Glycemia Risk Index (GRI) identified by searching MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library.

RESULTS: For counterregulation, SDH is consequential: real-world time below 3.0 mmol/L is independently associated with an attenuated adrenaline response to subsequent hypoglycaemia. For severe hypoglycaemia, SDH carries genuine but conditional predictive value, informative mainly when combined with awareness status and the depth and variability of exposure. For chronic complications, composite metrics such as the GRI are associated with albuminuria, retinopathy, and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy, but wherever the index has been decomposed, the driver is its hyperglycaemia rather than hypoglycaemia component. For quality of life, unperceived SDH has not been shown to independently impair daily functioning, which is associated instead with person-reported hypoglycaemia.

CONCLUSIONS: SDH should be interpreted alongside hypoglycaemia awareness and the person's lived experience rather than in isolation, and recorded separately from person-reported hypoglycaemia in both clinical practice and trials.

articles.title: High-risk diabetes: Psychiatric diagnoses in a cohort with recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Diabetic ketoacidosis is linked to poorer mental health, chronic hyperglycaemia and early complications including mortality. We describe the complex psychiatric presentations of people with recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis undergoing specialist assessment.

METHODS: This cohort study examined diabetic ketoacidosis admissions in adults with type 1 diabetes between January 2020 and June 2025. Recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis was defined as at least two recorded admissions during this period. Psychiatric diagnoses were recorded following comprehensive specialist assessment.

RESULTS: Among 750 adults experiencing 1501 diabetic ketoacidosis episodes, 263 had recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis, accounting for 1015 episodes (67.6%). Of these, 90 (34.2%) underwent psychiatric assessment. Their median age was 28 years (IQR: 22-40), 54 (60.0%) were female and mean HbA1c was 102 mmol/mol (11.5%). Psychiatric diagnoses were identified in 84 (93.3%), including personality disorder in 57 (63.3%) and depressive disorders in 49 (54.4%). Of those with personality disorder, 48 (84.2%) had no such diagnosis documented at referral. Housing insecurity affected 20 (22.2%), and 64 (71.1%) were not in employment or education.

CONCLUSION: Psychiatric diagnoses, particularly personality disorder and depression, were common in this assessed population. Psychiatric treatment embedded within diabetes services (diabetes psychiatry) warrants prospective evaluation to establish its effectiveness in improving clinical outcomes and reducing admissions.

articles.title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)-mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium-doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice-induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce3+/Ce4+ ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20-fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate (para-nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N-terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD-NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This pan-PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle-mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

Causal effects of extreme climate hazards on antimicrobial resistance across One Health reservoirs: protocol for a scoping review and evidence gap map.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Extreme climate events are increasing in frequency and intensity, with potential consequences for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) across One Health reservoirs. However, the evidence base remains fragmented, and the capacity of existing studies to support causal inference has not been systematically assessed. This scoping review aims to map evidence linking extreme climate hazards to AMR outcomes across human, animal and environmental reservoirs; assess causal inference potential of identified studies and identify critical evidence gaps.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: 10 bibliographic databases are being searched for studies published from January 2000 to August 2026, with final updates and supplementary searches planned for November 2026. Searches began in December 2025; screening of records retrieved to date is complete, but data extraction and causal inference assessment have not started. Two reviewers (CH and TPN), with SL adjudicating disagreements, will independently extract data and assess studies of six extreme climate hazard categories across human, animal and environmental reservoirs. An eight-criterion causal inference potential framework will provide criterion profiles and descriptive scores from 0 to 16; its unvalidated weighting and classification thresholds will be examined in sensitivity analyses. Inter-rater agreement will be reported before consensus. A 6×8 evidence gap map will summarise study coverage, with separate sub-reservoir and outcome domain displays for antimicrobial use, phenotypic resistance and genotypic resistance. Harvest plots and narrative synthesis will preserve these distinctions. The review is expected to be completed in February 2027.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This scoping review will analyse existing published data; therefore, ethical approval is not required. The completed review will be submitted for publication in a peer-reviewed open access journal. The evidence gap map, harvest plots and underlying dataset will be made publicly available through an open data repository. Findings will be disseminated through scientific conferences and briefing materials for relevant international initiatives.

articles.title: The development of a core outcome set of relationships and sex education for and with students with intellectual disability: a Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish adult stakeholder consensus on the importance of outcomes of Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) for students with intellectual disability to be included in a core outcome set (COS).

DESIGN: A two-round online Delphi survey.

PARTICIPANTS: Adult stakeholders: parents of children with intellectual disability aged 5–25 years; teachers; researchers in the field of sexuality and relationships of people with intellectual disability; policy makers and people from third sector organisations involved in developing or campaigning for policies for people with intellectual disability.

METHODS: A comprehensive list of outcomes generated in a previous stage of this COS development was presented in the two-round online Delphi survey. Adult stakeholders rated the importance of outcomes for students with intellectual disabilities in primary and secondary education. Students’ views were incorporated in the survey and outcome rating.

RESULTS: 92 participants completed both rounds of the survey. 18 outcomes reached the consensus threshold as being the most important and were included in the COS of RSE for students with intellectual disability in primary education. 31 outcomes reached consensus as the most important and were included in the COS of RSE for secondary school students with intellectual disability. Outcomes related to the human body and development; emotions and feelings; healthy relationships and associated social skills; sex and sexuality; keeping safe; consent; self-esteem; and human rights.

CONCLUSIONS: The COS provides a complete set of outcomes of RSE for students with intellectual disability in primary and secondary education to be used by researchers in future RSE evaluations as well as by policy makers to underpin the policy. The use of the COS will provide a significant first step towards harmonising RSE outcome measurement, development of effective RSE, improving its delivery and sustainability for this population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: The study was registered in the COMET database prospectively (https://www.comet-initiative.org/Studies/Details/1787).

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of nutritional, exercise and combined interventions for sarcopenia-related outcomes in older adults with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sarcopenia-related decline in muscle strength, mass and physical performance is common and clinically important in older adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Nutritional, exercise and combined interventions may improve these outcomes but their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. Existing evidence syntheses have largely focused on individual intervention types, haemodialysis populations or broader populations without CKD-specific comparisons. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) will address these gaps by comparing nutritional, exercise and combined interventions in older adults with CKD.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Randomised controlled trials evaluating nutritional, exercise or combined interventions in predominantly older adults with CKD will be identified through comprehensive searches of seven electronic databases: PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) and Wanfang Data, as well as other relevant sources. The primary outcomes will comprise three domains: muscle strength, muscle mass and physical performance, with handgrip strength, appendicular skeletal muscle mass/mass index and gait speed prioritised, respectively. Risk of bias will be assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Pairwise meta-analyses and frequentist random-effects NMA will be performed where clinically and methodologically appropriate. Separate networks will be constructed for each outcome domain. Transitivity, heterogeneity and network inconsistency will be assessed, and potential effect modifiers, including CKD and dialysis characteristics, baseline sarcopenia risk, intervention duration, nutritional dose and exercise intensity, will be explored where sufficient data are available. Treatment rankings will be assessed using P-scores alongside effect estimates and their uncertainty. Certainty of evidence will be evaluated using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA).

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval is not required for this study, as it will use data from previously published literature. The results of this systematic review will be disseminated through presentations at national and/or international conferences and publication in a peer-reviewed journal.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261499848.

articles.title: Physiology-based versus guideline-based interpretation of intrapartum cardiotocograph in nulliparous women in term labour at baseline and longitudinally in the prediction of early neonatal outcome: study protocol for a prospective observational study with randomisation of interpretation methods (the 'PHYSGUIDE' study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Current clinical guidelines for intrapartum fetal heart rate (FHR) monitoring (1) do not systematically exclude antenatal injuries or the baby’s ability to tolerate labour, thereby risking further injury; (2) do not acknowledge appropriate fetal adaptation to non-asphyxiating acute bradycardia or tachycardia leading to unwarranted operative deliveries; (3) are based on classification of deviations from predefined baseline FHR, variability and decelerations to estimate the risk of intrapartum hypoxia, while the healthy fetus deploys changes in the same FHR features to adapt appropriately to hypoxia, making the distinction between the hypoxic and the non-hypoxic fetus challenging, resulting in unnecessary operative delivery and lack of recognition of the decompensating fetus; and (4) are silent on best practice for the management of intrapartum factors, which may interfere with fetal adaptation to intrapartum stressors such as fever, meconium, chorioamnionitis/fetal inflammation and the synergistic interaction between hypoxia and inflammation. We developed an algorithm for intrapartum FHR interpretation as part of service development, widely termed ‘physiology-based guidelines’, based on (1) establishing normal fetal behaviour in early labour, (2) fetal cardiovascular responses to intrapartum stressors and the development of progressive fetal compromise and noted lower than UK national averages for low Apgar score at 5 min, neonatal encephalopathy and emergency caesarean section (Em Cs) in a single tertiary unit in London. However, there are no clinical trials or prospective studies comparing the sensitivity and specificity of ‘physiology-based guidelines’ to established practice guidelines such as the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics 2015 guidelines for intrapartum FHR interpretation for neonatal and maternal outcomes, and the recent promotion of widespread use of the ‘physiology-based guidelines’ in a so-called ‘consensus expert opinion’ lacks evidence.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This is a prospective observational study comparing ‘physiology-based’ interpretation of intrapartum cardiotocography (CTG) to ‘guidelines-based’ interpretation in 2500 nulliparous women in term labour in the prediction of composite neonatal outcome, including 5-minute Apgar score <7, neonatal acidosis (pH <7.05 and base excess <−12 mmol/L), antenatal brain injury, admission to neonatal intensive care unit, neonatal encephalopathy, need for therapeutic hypothermia, neonatal sepsis, meconium aspiration syndrome, hypotonia, hypoglycaemia, feto-maternal haemorrhage, perinatal stroke and intrapartum or neonatal death <28 days. A secondary aim is to compare the incidence of Em Cs and instrumental vaginal delivery for fetal compromise between the two methods of interpretation. The study does not compare participants but the accuracy of two methods of interpretation of the same CTG from each woman in predicting a selection of perinatal outcomes, that is, 2500 comparisons in a total of 5000 CTG interpretations. There are no baseline differences. Based on experience and previous research, we estimated that about 3% of labours are complicated by acute FHR bradycardia and considered pathological, requiring intervention based on current guidance for intrapartum CTG interpretation. We expect that ‘physiology-based’ interpretation could reduce this proportion to 1%. Based on these assumptions, 2500 paired observations will allow more than 90% power to detect a McNemar’s OR of ≥3, including Bonferroni correction for multiple testing with components of the primary outcome and allowance for 20% sample loss.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: The study was granted ethical approval by the Padua Regional Ethics Committee, code number CET-ACEV: 6259/AT/25, and accepted or reviewed by the local ethics committee of the participating centres. The results of the study will be disseminated at national and international conferences and published in peer-reviewed journals.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ISRCTN59827903.

articles.title: Optimising the prevention, detection and management of diabetes distress in adults with type 1 diabetes: D-stress feasibility study protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes distress describes the psychological and emotional burden of living with diabetes and is associated with reduced self-management and adverse diabetes outcomes. Clinical guidelines recommend routine assessment and management of diabetes distress, but this is not always implemented. Therefore, there is a need to develop approaches to deliver emotional health support in routine clinical care more effectively. We describe here the protocol for a study to (i) assess the feasibility of implementation of the D-stress pathway, comprising enhanced usual care (EUC) and an online, group-based, psychological diabetes distress reduction intervention called REDUCE, (ii) evaluate the feasibility of the study protocol, (iii) detect a signal of change in diabetes distress score and interstitial glucose time in range and (iv) refine initial programme theories of how both interventions (EUC and REDUCE) work, for whom and under what circumstances.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This feasibility study includes a multicentre trial within a cohort design where sites have a staggered exposure to the interventions alongside a realist process evaluation. Four UK National Health Service (NHS) diabetes services will recruit 80 adults with type 1 diabetes (≥1 year) using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) (≥3 months). All participants will receive EUC and provide monthly data over 7 months on diabetes distress (measured by the Type 1 Diabetes Distress Assessment System) and interstitial glucose measured by using CGM. Participants with elevated diabetes distress will be offered the 6-week, group-based, online REDUCE intervention plus EUC, compared with EUC alone. Up to 20 participants with type 1 diabetes, 10 family members/friends, 16 healthcare professionals delivering EUC and five REDUCE facilitators will be interviewed to explore their experience of receiving training and delivering the D-stress pathway. Up to 20 EUC consultations and REDUCE sessions will be observed. Feasibility will be assessed against prespecified progression criteria and analysed descriptively using summary statistics. Primary outcomes include baseline level of diabetes distress, recruitment rate, intervention uptake and data completeness, which will be analysed descriptively. Qualitative data will be analysed using framework analysis guided by realist programme theories developed for this study.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval was granted by NHS Research Ethics Committee (REC) (Bromley REC: 25/LO/0469) and the Health Research Authority. All participants will provide informed consent. Findings will be disseminated via publication in peer-reviewed journals, conferences, presentations and with relevant diabetes charitable organisations and networks, including Diabetes UK and the PsychoSocial Aspects of Diabetes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT07193446.

articles.title: Development and analysis protocol for ORCHARD-Stroke: a multimodal cohort study of infection, systemic inflammation and poststroke dementia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cognitive impairment and dementia affect approximately one-third of stroke survivors. Established risk factors, including age, stroke severity and pre-existing cerebrovascular disease, account for only part of the variance, and potentially modifiable contributors remain poorly characterised. In non-stroke populations, infection is associated with increased dementia risk, particularly vascular dementia, and risk may be greatest in patients with underlying cerebral small vessel disease (SVD). Infection complicates around one-third of acute strokes and SVD is prevalent in this population. However, few studies have examined infection and poststroke dementia, and the potential modifying effects of acute inflammation and SVD burden are unknown. Oxford and Reading Cognitive Comorbidity, Frailty and Ageing Research Database-Stroke (ORCHARD-Stroke) aims to address these gaps using large-scale multimodal routinely acquired data comprising hospital electronic health records (EHRs) with linked mental health records, Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme (SSNAP) data and brain imaging, allowing detailed phenotyping of acute stroke at scale together with infection, inflammatory biomarkers and cognitive outcomes.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: ORCHARD-Stroke is an observational cohort study using routinely acquired EHR and audit data. All primary acute stroke admissions will be extracted from the EHRs of Oxford University Hospitals National Health Service Foundation Trust and Royal Berkshire National Health Service Foundation Trust from January 2017 to December 2030 (n≥10 000). Eligible patients will have a primary International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision diagnosis of ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage. Subarachnoid haemorrhage is excluded. EHR data will be linked to SSNAP for stroke severity and subtype, and to regional mental health records for cognitive outcomes. Routinely acquired brain imaging will be obtained with automated quantification of SVD and atrophy, and acute ischaemic lesion extent from existing e-Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score (e-ASPECTS) outputs. The primary exposure is in-hospital infection, classified by site, severity and number. The primary outcome is incident poststroke dementia, after exclusion of prestroke dementia, analysed using Fine and Gray competing risks regression with death as the competing event and adjusted for prespecified covariates including demographics, stroke severity, SVD burden, comorbidity and frailty. Effect modification by SVD burden will be tested using a formal interaction term, and analyses stratified by stroke subtype and by presence or absence of moderate-to-severe SVD. Secondary analyses will examine inflammatory biomarkers (acute phase proteins, blood count indices, composite inflammatory indices) with and without co-occurring infection, and outcomes including cognitive decline and dementia subtype.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: ORCHARD-Stroke operates under the Oxford and Reading Cognitive Combordity, Frailty, and Ageing Research Database-Electronic Patient Records (ORCHARD-EPR) ethics approval granted by the South Central Oxford C Research Ethics Committee (REC reference: 23/SC/0258). Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publication and presentations at national and international stroke and dementia conferences.

articles.title: Beta-blockers in combination with chemotherapy and breast cancer survival: protocol of an emulated target trial in Norway leveraging both prevalent users and non-users at time zero.
Monitoring of Metabolic Diseases Risk Factors in Tehran (MMRT).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), especially metabolic diseases, pose an increasing public health challenge in low and middle-income countries like Iran. Understanding their prevalence, incidence and risk factors is essential for effective prevention. The Monitoring of Metabolic Diseases Risk Factors in Tehran (MMRT) study was launched to examine NCDs and their risk factors in a large urban population in Iran.

PARTICIPANTS: The MMRT is a prospective cohort study initiated in 2017, enrolling 7836 participants aged 20–70 from northwest Tehran, Iran. Baseline data were collected through questionnaires, physical exams, imaging such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and liver elastography and biochemical tests. These data provided essential information about their demographics, lifestyles, medical histories and other biomarkers. Participants underwent annual phone follow-ups for NCD incidence. Of the 7836 enrolled participants, 7600 completed a comprehensive 5-year re-evaluation using the same assessments as in the baseline phase.

FINDINGS TO DATE: Among the 7600 participants who completed the 5-year reassessment, the mean baseline age was 42.7±10.0 years and 3436 (45.2%) were men. At baseline, the prevalence of metabolic syndrome was 36.8%, hypertension 22.4%, diabetes 9.5%, metabolic (dysfunction)-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) 16.4% and cardiovascular disease 10.3%. Five-year cumulative incidence (per 1000 participants) was 285.2 for metabolic syndrome, 145.1 for diabetes, 92.5 for MASLD, 48.8 for hypertension, 39.5 for cardiovascular disease and 23.8 for myocardial infarction. Increasing age and higher body mass index were significantly associated with incident diabetes and MASLD, while male sex was associated with incident cardiovascular disease and myocardial infarction. Higher physical activity and greater wealth index were inversely associated with multiple outcomes.

FUTURE PLANS: MMRT will continue annual follow-up and periodic in-person re-evaluations to characterise long-term trends in NCD incidence. Its comprehensive data collection and prospective design help understand disease trends, risk factors and the implementation of public health strategies.

articles.title: Epidemiology of new and new persistent antipsychotic use after admission to internal medicine: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the epidemiology of new and new persistent use of antipsychotic medications following admission to internal medicine services and identify patient-related and admission-related variables associated with usage patterns of antipsychotic medications.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using data from the Internal Medicine Database that captures all admissions between 2010 and 2020.

SETTING: Landspítali—The National University Hospital of Iceland.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 75 484 admissions to internal medicine services, specialist secondary healthcare excluding mental health services, for patients 18 years and older surviving 90 days postdischarge. Among these, 64 906 admissions were not dispensed an antipsychotic prescription in the year prior to admission and were eligible for analysis for new antipsychotic use. Patients were classified according to antipsychotic dispensation patterns prior to and following admission into patients with preadmission use (dispensed ≥1 prescription in year preceding admission), patients with new non-persistent use (dispensed ≥1 prescription within 90 days of discharge but none between 90 and 180 days after discharge), patients with new persistent use (dispensed ≥1 prescription within 90 days of discharge and ≥1 prescription between 90 and 180 days after discharge) and patients with no use (no medication dispensed within 90 days after discharge).

OUTCOMES: The primary outcome was the incidence of new and new persistent antipsychotic use after admission to internal medicine at Landspítali. Secondary outcomes were patient and hospitalisation variables associated with new and new persistent antipsychotic use.

RESULTS: Of 75 484 admissions, 14.0% were dispensed a prescription for antipsychotic use in the preceding year. Among the 64 906 patients without use prior to admission, 3.4% initiated new use of antipsychotic medications in the 90 days following discharge, and of those, 57.1% developed new persistent use. The most commonly dispensed antipsychotic prescription was quetiapine. New antipsychotic use was more likely in patients with a higher frailty risk index classification and for patients with diagnoses of dementia, delirium, substance abuse, schizophrenia, mood and anxiety disorders. New antipsychotic use was more common in prolonged hospital stays and admission to geriatric, neurology, oncology, palliative care subspecialties and in admissions including rehabilitation, intensive care and with discharged to geriatric rehabilitation. Older age, increased comorbidity, prolonged hospital stays and admission to geriatric subspecialties were associated with new persistent antipsychotic use.

CONCLUSIONS: Although only a small proportion of patients admitted to the internal medicine wards at Landspítali initiate antipsychotic treatment, more than half of those with new use develop new persistent use. Older age, comorbidity, prolonged hospitalisation and geriatric admissions were associated with new persistent antipsychotic use.

articles.title: Triple Antibiotic Prophylaxis and Revision Risk in Adult Spinal Deformity Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection and wound complications remain major sources of morbidity after multilevel fusion for adult spinal deformity. Whether adding an aminoglycoside (gentamicin or tobramycin) to vancomycin-cefepime prophylaxis improves outcomes is unclear.

METHODS: Retrospective review of 264 patients undergoing multilevel adult spinal deformity fusion receiving postoperative prophylaxis with vancomycin-cefepime, with or without an aminoglycoside. The primary outcome was a composite of major wound complications (surgical site infection, dehiscence, seroma, abscess, or osteomyelitis). The secondary outcome was revision surgery. Propensity score matching (1:1, caliper 0.2 SD) on age, diabetes, prior wound infection, prior spine surgeries ≥2, hardware failure, and pelvic fixation yielded 174 matched patients (87 per group). Multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

RESULTS: Major wound complications did not differ between groups in unmatched (16.7% vs 22.5%, P = 0.329) or matched cohorts (16.1% vs 20.7%, P = 0.557). Revision surgery was less frequent with aminoglycoside addition in the unmatched cohort (17.5% vs 30.8%, P = 0.024; aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.21-0.76, P = 0.005) with a consistent but nonsignificant trend in the matched cohort (21.8% vs 34.5%, P = 0.092; aOR 0.52, 95% CI 0.26-1.04, P = 0.066). Absolute risk reduction for revision surgery was 12.6%.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding aminoglycoside to vancomycin-cefepime was not associated with reduced overall wound complications but was consistently associated with lower revision surgery rates. These findings suggest possible benefit specific to deep infection risk, warranting prospective confirmation with nephrotoxicity assessment.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: In multilevel adult spinal deformity fusion, adding an aminoglycoside to vancomycin-cefepime prophylaxis was associated with lower revision surgery rates but not fewer overall wound complications. This supports a prospective trial of selective use in patients at high risk for deep infection with renal safety monitoring.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Preoperative Prediction Model for Pain-Function Discordance Among Pain Responders After Percutaneous Vertebroplasty for Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize pain-function discordance among patients who achieve clinically meaningful pain relief after percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP) for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) and to develop and internally validate a preoperative model for this conditional recovery pattern.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with OVCFs treated with PVP between June 2022 and June 2025. Pain and disability were assessed using the visual analog scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) at baseline and 3 months. Clinically meaningful improvement was defined as a relative VAS reduction of ≥ 39% and ODI reduction of ≥ 35%. Among patients meeting the pain-response criterion, pain-function discordance was defined as VAS improvement ≥ 39% with ODI improvement < 35%. A prespecified logistic regression model included age, body mass index (BMI), pre-fracture walking impairment, and MRI-derived paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration. Performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, Brier score, decision curve analysis, and 1000-bootstrap internal validation. LASSO and an absolute-MIC sensitivity analysis were performed as secondary analyses.

RESULTS: Of 450 pain responders, 71 (15.8%) had pain-function discordance. Older age (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.70 per 5 years, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.36-2.14), higher BMI (OR 1.16 per 1 kg/m2, 95% CI 1.07-1.26), pre-fracture walking impairment (OR 4.33, 95% CI 2.40-7.83), and greater paraspinal muscle fatty infiltration (OR 1.57 per 10 percentage points, 95% CI 1.24-1.99) were independently associated with discordance (all p < 0.001). The apparent AUC was 0.808 (95% CI 0.754-0.855) and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.797; the optimism-corrected Brier score was 0.114 and the calibration slope was 0.949. LASSO at λ1se retained the same four predictors, and associations were directionally consistent in the absolute-MIC sensitivity analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in six patients with meaningful pain relief after PVP did not meet the prespecified threshold for relative functional improvement and experienced substantial residual disability. A four-variable preoperative model showed good internal discrimination and satisfactory calibration for this conditional recovery pattern. The model estimates the risk of functional discordance among pain responders and requires external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Low-dose polymyxin B combined with ginsenoside Rg1 synergistically attenuates Escherichia coli-induced sepsis in rabbits.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Gram-negative bacterial sepsis remains a therapeutic challenge, as antibiotics can trigger endotoxin release and worsen inflammation. Polymyxin B (PMB) neutralizes endotoxin but is dose-limited by toxicity. This study investigated whether ginsenoside Rg1, a Toll-like receptor 4 signaling inhibitor, synergizes with low-dose PMB in an Escherichia coli (E.Coli)-induced rabbit sepsis model. Rabbits received either saline without E.Coli challenge, E.Coli inoculation alone, or E.Coli inoculation followed by Rg1, PMB, or their combination. Sepsis was induced by subcutaneous E.Coli challenge, and treatments were administered intravenously immediately thereafter. Bacterial burden, endotoxin, temperature, leukocytes, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and intestinal histopathology were assessed over 48 hr. The Rg1-PMB combination produced sustained reductions in bacteremia, endotoxin, fever, neutrophilia, and cytokine levels, whereas PMB alone cleared bacteria and endotoxin but failed to suppress leukocyte elevation or cytokine production. Histologically, the combination preserved intestinal villi, tight junctions, and mitochondria, while PMB alone offered only partial protection. These findings demonstrate that Rg1 extends the therapeutic window of low-dose PMB by providing sustained anti-inflammatory and organ-protective effects beyond the bactericidal and endotoxin-neutralizing actions of PMB. This dual-target strategy may represent a promising toxicity-sparing approach for the management of Gram-negative sepsis.

Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring.

DESIGN: Nationwide population based cohort study.

SETTING: Danish national registers.

PARTICIPANTS: 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Metabolic disorders in offspring, including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and overweight or obesity, were identified from hospital and prescription records. Offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during spermatogenesis (three months before pregnancy) were compared with those of fathers who did not take antidepressants during this period and fathers who used antidepressants only during pregnancy to further account for underlying paternal mental health conditions. Associations between paternal antidepressant use and metabolic disorders, collectively and individually, were estimated as propensity score weighted hazard ratios using Cox regression.

RESULTS: 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders.

CONCLUSIONS: The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.

articles.title: Unexpected left atrial mass after cardiac surgery.
Nurses' Dysphagia Screening for Acute Stroke Patients Within 24 h and Associated Factors: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess dysphagia screening practice among nurses caring for acute stroke patients within 24 h of admission and associated factors.

DESIGN: Institution-based cross-sectional design.

METHOD: A study was conducted across five hospitals. Of the 422 nurses sampled, 417 completed the study (98.8% response rate) and researchers triangulated with 130 patient charts. We used descriptive statistics, chi-square tests and multivariate logistic regression to analyse factors associated with screening practice.

RESULTS: Among participating nurses, most were male, held a bachelor's degree, and had less than 5 years of work experience. Fewer than half (41.5%) of nurses reported screening within 24 h. Only 11% of them adhered to a formal screening protocol. Triangulated chart reviews confirmed that less than one-third of stroke patients received any dysphagia assessment. A multivariate logistic regression model revealed that prior training, knowledge, working unit, and the availability of institutional guidelines were associated with screening practice.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of standardised, nurse-led dysphagia screening is low. Addressing system-level barriers, deploying targeted training and implementing institutional guidelines could improve screening compliance.

IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSES AND/OR PATIENTS: Nurse managers and policymakers should prioritise structured, bedside dysphagia screening training and enforce clinical protocols to bridge the gap between guidelines and practice, ultimately reducing post-stroke aspiration pneumonia and other complications.

IMPACT: Lack of standardised protocols, validated screening tools and structured nurse training contributes to inadequate screening, significantly heightening the risk of aspiration pneumonia. Strengthening these screening practices directly benefits stroke survivors through early risk identification, while offering evidence to inform nurses and policymakers in resource-limited settings.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient involvement. Nurses (n = 417) were interviewed, and 130 stroke patient charts were reviewed.

articles.title: Photographic Documentation Standards for Facial Plastic Surgery: An International Modified Delphi Consensus.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Aims and Backgrounds. Published before-and-after photography is a central component of outcome reporting in facial plastic and reconstructive surgery, yet no enforced, specialty-wide standard exists. This study presents an expert consensus-derived standard.

HISTORICAL ASPECTS: Historically, journal photography requirements have addressed equipment, lighting, positioning and reproduction ratios without producing a standard.

TECHNIQUES: Of 21 facial plastic surgeons invited, 16 agreed to participate in a four-round modified Delphi study. Rounds 1 to 3 rated statements on a five-point Likert scale with aggregate feedback returned between rounds; consensus required a median ≥4 (agreement) or ≤2 (disagreement), with an interquartile range (IQR) of 1 or less. Round 4 was a ratification vote requiring 70% acceptance, with re-rating of statements lacking consensus in consecutive rounds. Current and Future Development. Sixteen panelists ultimately responded and 6 completed Round 4. Of 225 statements rated, 126 were ratified, 15 failed ratification, and 84 did not advance to the vote. Ratified statements carried a median rating of 5.0 and a median ratification vote of 100%.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The panel produced a ratified photographic standard spanning general image features and eight procedure categories, intended for adoption into journal author instructions.

articles.title: Impact of Hydrocortisone on Left Ventricular Mass and Function in Extremely Preterm Infants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Our primary objective was to determine if hydrocortisone (HC) administration in extremely preterm intubated neonates is associated with an increase in the left ventricular mass index (LVMI) at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age (PMA). The secondary objective was to compare the incidence of pulmonary hypertension at 36 weeks' PMA in infants receiving HC versus placebo.

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective observational study of a subset of infants in the Neonatal Research Network randomized controlled trial (RCT) "Hydrocortisone to Improve Survival without Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia." Infants eligible for the RCT were < 30 weeks' gestation without major congenital anomaly, 14 to 28 days postnatal age, intubated, and had received ≥ 7 days of invasive mechanical ventilation. Infants were randomized to a 10-day tapering course of HC or placebo. The effect of HC on LVMI on echocardiogram at 36 weeks' PMA was evaluated using linear regression adjusted for the trial stratification factors (center and gestational age strata).

RESULTS: Among 128 infants (61 HC, 67 placebo), body surface area (BSA)-indexed LVMI was lower among patients in the HC group (49.3 vs. 53.1 g/m2, p = 0.04). However, height-indexed LVMI, left ventricular hypertrophy, systolic function, and the systolic-to-diastolic duration ratio did not differ significantly. Pulmonary hypertension occurred in 8.2% of infants in the HC group, as compared with 13.4% in the placebo group (p = 0.17).

CONCLUSION: Among preterm intubated infants, a 10-day tapering course of HC was associated with lower BSA-indexed LVMI at 36 weeks' PMA, but other measures of cardiac structure and function showed no consistent differences. Pulmonary hypertension was numerically less frequent in the HC group, but the difference was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Clinical trial registration does not apply to this study. The primary trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT01353313.

articles.title: The Athlete's Heart Beyond 50: Cardiac Remodeling and Arrhythmic Features.
articles.abstract: While cardiovascular adaptations to intensive exercise are well established in younger athletes, how these adaptations persist and evolve with age remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated cardiovascular remodeling and its clinical correlates associated with competitive exercise in older adults. We studied 478 participants (61.9±8 y; range 50-90), including 303 master athletes, 99 recreationally active participants, and 76 sedentary participants. All underwent clinical evaluation, electrocardiography, exercise testing, and transthoracic echocardiography. Master athletes showed greater left ventricular dimensions and volumes, higher septal e', lower E/e', lower resting heart rates, and superior exercise capacity compared with sedentary participants, whereas recreationally active participants showed intermediate characteristics. Master athletes also had a lower prevalence of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, symptoms, and medication use. Exercise-induced ventricular ectopic beats were more frequent among master athletes than sedentary participants. In multivariable analysis, higher maximum workload (odds ratio, 3.74; 95% confidence interval, 2.38-5.86; p<0.001), lower E/e' (odds ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-0.99; p=0.039), and exercise-induced ventricular ectopic beats (odds ratio, 1.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.04-2.80; p=0.022) were independently associated with master athlete status, whereas hypertension was inversely associated (odds ratio, 0.53; 95% confidence interval, 0.31-0.90; p=0.019). In older adults, long-term competitive exercise was associated with superior exercise capacity and favorable cardiac remodeling, but also with greater exercise-induced ventricular ectopy, supporting cardiovascular screening and longitudinal surveillance.

articles.title: Single port robotic kidney-pancreas transplantation with ipsilateral graft placement: initial feasibility report.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Simultaneous kidney-pancreas transplantation is the most definitive treatment for type 1 diabetes with end-stage renal manifestations. While most kidney-pancreas transplants are performed via open approaches, select groups have begun performing multiport robotic transplants with and without hand assistance. Here we describe our techniques of fully robotic kidney/pancreas transplantation. We trace our evolution from multiport robotics with contralateral graft placement to single-port, ipsilateral implantation through a 5cm incision, preserving the contralateral vessels for a future transplant. Of six robotic kidney/pancreas transplants, our mean operative time was 5 hours, 56 minutes (range 5:26-6:45) with mean kidney and pancreas vascular anastomotic times of 31 and 40 minutes (range 26-36, 27-45 minutes). Three single-port cases averaged 5 hours, 49 minutes (range 5:33-6:12) with kidney and pancreas vascular anastomotic times of 31 and 39 minutes (range 26-35, 27-45 minutes). All recipients experienced immediate graft function and were discharged after a median of 3.5 hospital days. At 30 days, all patients had functioning allografts and did not require reintervention related to their transplant organs. We believe this could indicate a technical advancement in kidney/pancreas transplantation, justifying further study of robotic techniques.

articles.title: Protocol for a randomized controlled trial in home health care assessing the efficacy of a virtual health coaching intervention promoting self-care of informal caregivers of patients with heart failure and cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Informal caregivers often prioritize the health needs of patients over their own self-care, leading to poor mental health. Few rigorously designed trials have tested interventions targeting mental health in caregivers of patients with heart failure and cognitive impairment, particularly in home health care settings. Interventions that improve caregiver well-being may also influence patient outcomes through dyadic mechanisms, but this hypothesis has been insufficiently examined in randomized trials.

METHODS: This article describes the protocol for a Stage II, randomized controlled trial evaluating the efficacy of a virtual health coaching intervention (Virtual Caregiver Coach for You [ViCCY]) compared to usual care. We will enroll 256 informal caregivers of adults with HF and mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment receiving home health care, along with a subsample of 60 patients. Caregivers will be randomized 1:1 to ViCCY or usual care using stratified permuted block randomization. ViCCY consists of 10 individualized virtual coaching sessions delivered over six months. The primary outcome is caregiver mental health measured by the SF-36 at six months. Secondary caregiver outcomes include self-care, stress, coping, and caregiver burden. Patient outcomes include mental health, depression, anxiety, somatic HF symptoms (e.g., shortness of breath). Mixed-effects regression models will be used to evaluate intervention effects and explore dyadic mechanisms (i.e., dyadic relationship strain).

DISCUSSION: This trial addresses an important gap in caregiver intervention research by targeting caregivers of patients with heart failure and cognitive impairment in home health care. The findings will inform the design of scalable, theory-based caregiver interventions and future pragmatic trials.

articles.title: Commentary: An updated sample protocol for provision of mifepristone and misoprostol in early pregnancy without pre-treatment ultrasonography.
articles.abstract: Provision of medication abortion without pre-treatment ultrasonography, especially via telehealth, has rapidly expanded since 2020, and a large body of research indicates this care model is safe and effective. However, evidence indicates that 40-60% of individuals seeking care who are eligible for treatment may be mischaracterized as ineligible under current protocols, largely due to the criteria intended to identify people with ectopic pregnancy. In particular, symptoms of pain and bleeding are common during pregnancy and have low positive predictive value to identify ectopic pregnancy. These symptoms are also common among people experiencing early pregnancy loss who may seek medication management. In this paper, we propose a revised protocol for providing mifepristone and misoprostol without pre-treatment ultrasonography to people desiring abortion or management of pregnancy loss in early pregnancy, including those with ectopic pregnancy symptoms or risk factors who are otherwise clinically stable. The protocol centers shared decision-making to evaluate a patient while simultaneously providing abortion care when the likelihood of ectopic pregnancy is elevated. Patients with symptoms of ruptured ectopic pregnancy, hemorrhage, or sepsis are directed to immediate in-person evaluation. IMPLICATIONS: We expect the proposed protocol will safely increase the proportion of people eligible for mifepristone and misoprostol without ultrasonography. Research should document outcomes of the protocol as it is incorporated into services.

articles.title: Prevalence and Prognostic Impact of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction in Patients with Secondary Tricuspid Regurgitation: A Clinical and Probability-Based Assessment.
articles.abstract: Secondary tricuspid regurgitation (sTR) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) often coexist due to shared risk factors and pathophysiological mechanisms; however, the prevalence, recognition, and prognostic impact of HFpEF in patients with significant sTR remain unclear. We sought to evaluate HFpEF prevalence and its association with all-cause mortality in this population. We retrospectively studied patients at Mayo Clinic (2005-2016) with ≥moderate-severe sTR, LVEF >50%, and no significant left-sided valvular disease. HFpEF probability was estimated using the H₂FPEF score (≥6 defined high probability), along with Framingham Heart criteria (FHC) and ICD-9/10 codes for diastolic heart failure. All-cause mortality was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression, restricted to patients who survived ≥1 year after the index echocardiogram. Among 1,735 patients (age 73±14 years; 64% female), an H₂FPEF score ≥6 was present in 904 (52%). Of these, 567 (63%) fulfilled FHC, but only 154 (17%) had a corresponding ICD diagnosis of diastolic heart failure. Patients with H₂FPEF ≥6 had worse survival compared with those with lower scores, irrespective of FHC status (reference: H₂FPEF <6): H₂FPEF ≥6 without FHC fulfillment (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.14-1.57) and H₂FPEF ≥6 with FHC fulfillment (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.16-1.57). In conclusion, in patients with significant sTR, a high clinical probability of HFpEF is comment but frequently under-recognized and under-documented. High HFpEF probability by clinical scores is associated with increased mortality. These data call for more systematic application of clinical assessment, structured probability scoring, and hemodynamic evaluation to identify HFpEF among patients with sTR.

articles.title: Relationship between Coronary Artery Calcification and Plaque Vulnerability: Women versus Men.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coronary artery calcium score (CACS) is a validated marker of coronary atherosclerotic burden and a strong predictor of adverse cardiovascular events. Recently, we reported that CACS 0, compared with CACS ≥1, was associated with lower plaque vulnerability assessed by optical coherence tomography (OCT). However, whether this relationship differs between women and men is unexplored.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the relationship between CACS and OCT-derived vulnerable features, stratified by sex.

METHODS: This is a sex-stratified substudy of our previously reported cohort. Patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent cardiac computed tomography and OCT of the target vessel before percutaneous coronary intervention were divided into four CACS groups (0, 1-99, 100-399, and ≥400).

RESULTS: A total of 479 patients and 1038 lesions (227 in 108 women and 811 in 371 men) were analyzed. CACS 0 was associated with a lower prevalence of thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA) in men, but not in women (p for interaction<0.001), irrespective of clinical presentation and lesion location (target vs. non-target). In contrast, in women with CACS 0, macrophage accumulation was less frequent (p for interaction=0.015), but plaque erosion was more frequent, compared to CACS≥1 (42.9% vs 4.6%, p<0.001), a pattern not observed in men (p for interaction=0.011).

CONCLUSIONS: In men with CAD, CACS 0 was associated with a lower prevalence of TCFA. In women, CACS 0 was associated with a lower prevalence of macrophage accumulation and a greater prevalence of plaque erosion. These findings support sex-specific interpretation of CACS in predicting plaque vulnerability.

articles.title: Targeting the TXNIP-NLRP3 redox Interface: Protein-Protein interaction pharmacology in pyroptosis and cardioinflammation.
articles.abstract: Association between thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) and NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) is widely cited as a redox-sensitive checkpoint linking oxidative and metabolic stress to cardiovascular inflammation, and is increasingly described as a protein-protein interaction drug target. Rather than surveying NLRP3 biology or cataloging inflammasome inhibitors, which recent comprehensive reviews already cover, this critical review addresses a methodological problem: almost every study invoked in support of this target measures something other than the interaction itself. Expression changes, genetic depletion, antioxidant treatment and downstream cytokine or pyroptosis readouts are each compatible with reduced TXNIP-NLRP3 association arising indirectly, through altered TXNIP abundance, localization or redox state, or through conformational inhibition of NLRP3. As its central contribution, this article sets out an explicit five-tier validation framework defining what must be shown to justify an interaction-selective claim, and applies it to the literature. On this basis, proposed contact residues remain untested hypotheses derived from docking of partner-stripped templates; the strongest cardiovascular data establish TXNIP-dependent signaling in cardiac microvascular endothelium rather than interface dependence; and the two reported interaction-disrupting compounds, PSSM1443 and phenethyl isothiocyanate, reach only the lower tiers, with binding site, affinity and selectivity unresolved. Conflicting findings in endotoxic shock and metabolic liver disease indicate that even the direction of the interaction's functional effect is model-specific. The review concludes by specifying the assay cascade, counter-screens and rescue experiments needed to move from pathway association to interface validation, and the comparative studies against conventional NLRP3 inhibition without which a therapeutic advantage cannot be claimed.

articles.title: Development and translational validation of a novel mouse model for cat allergic rhinitis.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: About 30% of the North American population are affected by seasonal or perennial rhinitis. Allergens from cats are common triggers of allergic rhinitis. Importantly, cat allergic rhinitis (cat-AR) is a major risk factor for more severe allergic diseases, including asthma.
