Current therapies rarely achieve full symptom control and development of novel therapeutics is constrained by lack of physiologically relevant preclinical models.

OBJECTIVE: Establishment of a clinically-informed mouse model of cat allergic rhinitis.

METHODS: Controlled human exposure was performed using airborne natural cat dander (CD) in a validated environmental exposure facility. Symptom scores, immune cells, IgE, and cytokine concentrations were captured. In mice, we established a 14-day intermittent intranasal sensitization and challenge protocol using the same CD allergens. Clinical signs in mice were objectively quantified using AI-based video detection. Cellular changes in the nose were assessed with level-specific, spatial resolution. Lastly, systemic sensitization was confirmed through serum IgE and intradermal ear challenges.

RESULTS: Following CD exposure, cat-allergic participants displayed increased nasal symptoms and eosinophil influx in the nose. CD-sensitized mice recapitulated key clinical features following CD challenge, including increased nasal rubbing, elevated nasal immune cell infiltration, and systemic sensitization. Spatial analysis revealed marked regional differences in immune cell infiltration within the turbinate mucosa and olfactory regions of the nasal cavity.

CONCLUSIONS: This novel mouse model provides a translationally valuable platform for investigating local and systemic mechanisms of cat-AR. It will serve for mechanistic and therapeutic evaluations with the goal of improving clinical translation and therapeutic precision.

articles.title: Adipocyte lipolysis associates with long-term development of hyperlipidaemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adipocyte functions (cellularity, lipid breakdown and synthesis) associate with simultaneous presence of elevated circulating lipid levels. This study examined if such features also relate to future development of hyperlipidaemia.

METHODS: Between 1988-2016 we investigated 1004 Swedish individuals with biochemical/anthropometric examinations, a health questionnaire, and abdominal subcutaneous adipocyte size, basal and stimulated lipolysis (triglyceride breakdown), and adipose insulin resistance (Adipo-IR, fasting serum levels of insulin times fatty acids). All individuals were contacted again 2018-22 for a repeated health survey (17 years in mean observation time). A response was obtained from 280 participants, whereof 210 individuals did not haveout hyperlipidaemia at baseline and follow-up and 44 developed a hyperlipidaemia diagnosis at follow-up. These groups were compared by unpaired t-test and logistic regression, while considering the influence of relevant co-factors.

RESULTS: Of all functional features, only the basal (spontaneous) adipocyte lipolysis rate (log10 µmoles of glycerol release per number of adipocytes) independently associated with development of hyperlipidaemia over time. The basal lipolysis rate was about 45 % increased (p = 0.0002) in those developing hyperlipidaemia. This relationship with hyperlipidaemia development was independent of sex, age, body mass index, initial lipid levels, waist-to-hip ratio, bariatric surgery, observation time, insulin resistance, body weight changes over time , smoking, physical activity or simultaneous presence of type 2 diabetes.

CONCLUSION: The basal rate of fat cell lipolysis associates with future development of hyperlipidaemia even following adjustment for pertinent co-factors.

articles.title: HELZ2 knockdown alleviates hepatic steatosis and reduces inflammatory responses in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) involves hepatic steatosis, metabolic dysfunction and inflammation. HELZ2 has been linked to hepatic lipid metabolism and immune transcription, but its role in MAFLD remains unclear.

METHODS: Peripheral-blood whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed in eight patients with MAFLD and eight healthy controls. Candidate genes were examined by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. We studied HELZ2 in HFD-fed mice via AAV8-mediated knockdown and in a public human liver RNA-sequencing cohort.

RESULTS: HELZ2 was nominally upregulated in the discovery cohort but lost significance after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (log2FC = 0.677; nominal P = 0.00475; adjusted P = 0.999). It had the highest discovery-cohort AUC (0.922) and was the only prioritized gene significantly increased in validation. Peripheral-blood HELZ2 strongly correlated with clinical parameters of MAFLD, including BMI, liver enzymes, and lipid profiles. In an independent liver cohort (GSE135251), HELZ2 expression was higher in the fatty liver disease group (median ratio, 1.42; two-sided Wilcoxon P = 0.000709). HFD feeding increased hepatic HELZ2 expression, TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, circulating cytokines, and CD86/iNOS, while reducing Arg1/CD206. HELZ2 knockdown reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, steatosis, and serum ALT/AST, with minimal body-weight effects, and reversed the pathway-associated readouts, circulating cytokines, and tissue-marker changes.

CONCLUSIONS: HELZ2 is associated with MAFLD, and its knockdown alleviated hepatic steatosis and liver injury in HFD-fed mice. These improvements were accompanied by reduced inflammatory responses and TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB-associated signaling, together with altered M1/M2-associated tissue-marker expression. The findings do not establish a direct HELZ2-TLR interaction or macrophage-specific polarization effects; the underlying molecular mechanism remains unresolved.

articles.title: Serum per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance concentrations across chronic kidney disease stages and albuminuria categories.
articles.abstract: This study investigated serum concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and their associations with kidney function in 474 patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) across five stages, recruited at Kaohsiung Medical University from August 2016 to January 2017. The purpose was to clarify the relationships of PFAS concentrations with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), key markers of kidney health. Serum concentrations of seven PFAS compounds were measured using ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Linear regression and natural cubic spline models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, UACR, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and coronary artery disease as appropriate. PFAS distributions differed across CKD stages for six of the seven compounds, but stage-specific medians followed compound-specific, non-monotonic patterns rather than a progressive increase with CKD severity. PFAS concentrations were also lower in participants with macroalbuminuria. In the fully adjusted linear model, higher eGFR was positively associated with T-PFOS, PFOA, PFDA, PFUnDA, and PFNA after false-discovery-rate correction. After correction for multiple testing, eGFR-UACR interactions were supported for T-PFOS, PFOA, PFUnDA, and PFNA. Spline tests supported nonlinearity for PFOA, PFDA, and PFNA after correction for multiple testing. These cross-sectional findings emphasize that serum PFAS concentrations in CKD should be interpreted in relation to both kidney function and albuminuria.

articles.title: Early breast cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
authors: ESMO Guidelines Committee. Electronic address: clinicalguidelines@esmo.org
articles.journal: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and causation: from prediction to causal inference in biomedical research.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To distinguish what dental artificial intelligence (AI) models demonstrate from what their findings are claimed to mean, and to offer a framework for matching each claim to the evidence required to support it.

OVERVIEW: AI studies in dentistry report sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve: measures of agreement between model outputs and a reference standard. Yet verbs such as predict, detect, identify, and explain are used interchangeably, and outputs are often read as identifying modifiable causes or as evidence of clinical benefit. Using the causal hierarchy of association, intervention, and counterfactual reasoning, this review separates description, prediction, causal effects of interventions, and individual counterfactuals. Directed acyclic graphs illustrate how confounding by indication can make an effective treatment appear harmful in a predictive model. The review summarizes the identification conditions that causal claims require (exchangeability, positivity, consistency) and where AI can legitimately contribute: measurement, nuisance-function estimation, heterogeneous treatment effects, and hypothesis-generating causal discovery. Model-explanation methods describe how a fitted model behaves, not how patients would respond to intervention. A published caries-detection model illustrates the evidence needed to move from diagnostic accuracy to claims about clinician decisions and patient outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Most AI models developed for prediction operate at the association level. Model complexity and dataset size cannot substitute for a defined intervention, an appropriate design, and defensible identification assumptions.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Dental AI accuracy studies show agreement with a reference standard, not that using the tool improves decisions or patient outcomes. Such claims require comparative evaluation of AI-assisted care.

articles.title: ECM1: From Structural Protein to Disease Modulator-A Potential Therapeutic Target and Biomarker in Human Diseases.
articles.abstract: The multifunctional glycoprotein extracellular matrix protein 1 (ECM1) is essential for immune homeostasis, organ development, angiogenesis, and skin integrity. Dysregulation of ECM1 is closely associated with various human diseases. In skin disorders such as lichen sclerosus and lipoid proteinosis, ECM1 autoantibodies or ECM1 gene mutations disrupt collagen homeostasis and extracellular matrix interactions. In malignant tumors, elevated ECM1 expression promotes tumor growth, invasion, metastasis, therapy resistance, and microenvironment remodeling via activation of ERK, PI3K/AKT, and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, correlating with poor prognosis. ECM1 exerts bidirectional immunomodulatory effects in autoimmune diseases. In inflammatory bowel disease, it drives pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization through the GM-CSF/STAT5 pathway, whereas in central nervous system autoimmunity, it exerts protective effects by inhibiting Th17 differentiation. Notably, ECM1 shows tissue-specific dual roles in fibrotic diseases: it aggravates renal fibrosis but protects against liver fibrosis. As a secreted protein detectable in blood and urine, ECM1 is emerging as a promising non-invasive biomarker. ECM1 has been proposed as a potential urinary biomarker for chronic kidney disease. Furthermore, ECM1-targeted therapeutic strategies, including gene therapy, monoclonal antibodies, and small-molecule drugs, have shown efficacy in multiple disease models. Collectively, ECM1 links extracellular matrix homeostasis to disease progression and holds promise as a diagnostic and therapeutic target.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of variable perioperative antiplatelet regimens in patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current SVS recommendations for perioperative antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy (CEA) are limited. In acutely symptomatic patients, dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) is recommended for secondary stroke prevention. In asymptomatic patients, there are no clear recommendations, though single antiplatelet therapy with aspirin (ASA) is commonly used. We examined the efficacy and safety of various perioperative antiplatelet regimens in patients who underwent CEA in the VQI.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all patients who underwent CEA in VQI from January 2003 to September 2024. We stratified patients based on their pre-operative antiplatelet regimen: No-antiplatelet, ASA-only, Clopidogrel-only, DAPT (ASA/Clopidogrel), and Alternative-DAPT (ASA/Alternative P2Y12 Inhibitors). We created propensity scores for each treatment regimen and assessed in-hospital stroke/death and bleeding complications using inverse probability of treatment weighted log binomial regression, with ASA-only as the reference group and adjusting for intraoperative protamine use and drain placement. We also assessed outcomes stratified by preoperative symptom status.

RESULTS: Of 195,619 CEA patients: 53% received ASA-only, 11% No-antiplatelet, 6% Clopidogrel-only, 30% DAPT, and 1% Alternative-DAPT. The corresponding unadjusted rates of in-hospital stroke/death were 1.3%, 1.7%, 1.2%, 1.2%, and 1.6%. After adjustment, compared with ASA-only, in-hospital stroke/death was lower with Clopidogrel-only (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.97) and DAPT (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.72-0.87). In symptomatic patients (26% of the cohort), there was a trend towards lower in-hospital stroke/death with DAPT (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.00). In asymptomatic patients, in-hospital stroke/death was lower with Clopidogrel-only (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52-0.90) and DAPT (RR 0.73, 95% CI 0.64-0.83). Bleeding complications were higher with DAPT (RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.35-1.66) and trended toward higher with Clopidogrel-only (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.00-1.48) but were similar across other regimens.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with ASA-monotherapy, Clopidogrel-monotherapy and DAPT were associated with lower rates of in-hospital stroke/death after CEA driven by lower rates of stroke, albeit with higher rates of bleeding complications, particularly with DAPT. These findings highlight Clopidogrel-monotherapy as a potential alternative to DAPT for patients undergoing CEA, with similar efficacy and more acceptable bleeding risk. Analyses in patients on alternative P2Y12 inhibitors were limited by sample size; however, analyses with a larger cohort will be valuable in the future. Overall, our findings emphasize a potential role for clopidogrel-monotherapy in stroke prevention among patients undergoing CEA and highlight the importance of individualized risk assessment.

articles.title: Beyond injury grade: Anatomic location and outcomes after endovascular repair of blunt thoracic aortic injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Contemporary risk stratification for blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) has largely emphasized injury grade, whereas the prognostic importance of injury location remains poorly defined. More proximal injuries may require complex arch reconstruction and management of the supra-aortic branches, potentially increasing procedural risk. We evaluated the association between anatomic aortic injury zone and perioperative and long-term outcomes after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR).

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing TEVAR for BTAI in the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative from 2013 through April 1, 2026. Patients were classified according to the proximal extent of the aortic injury as proximal (zones 0-2), isthmic (zone 3), or distal (zones 4-5). Multinomial propensity scores incorporating pretreatment demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and injury-severity variables were used to generate stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights. Weighted logistic regression with center-clustered standard errors evaluated perioperative outcomes. Cox regression evaluated all-cause mortality, and Fine-Gray regression evaluated aorta- or branch-related reintervention with death treated as a competing event. Zone 3 served as the reference group.

RESULTS: Among 2,693 patients, 551 (20.5%) had proximal injuries, 1,772 (65.8%) had zone 3 injuries, and 370 (13.7%) had distal injuries. Injury-grade distributions did not differ significantly among groups. After weighting, proximal injury was associated with greater in-hospital mortality compared with zone 3 injury (11.0% vs. 8.5%; odds ratio [OR], 1.33; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.76; P=0.046) and greater 30-day aortic reintervention (2.2% vs. 0.8%; OR, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.30-6.92; P=0.010). Stroke and spinal cord ischemia did not differ significantly. Proximal injury was also associated with a greater cumulative incidence of aortic reintervention (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.94; 95% CI, 1.06-3.53; P=0.031), although its association with all-cause mortality during follow-up did not reach statistical significance (hazard ratio, 1.28; 95% CI, 0.99-1.65; P=0.060). Distal injury was not associated with increased perioperative or long-term adverse outcomes compared with zone 3 injury.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TEVAR for BTAI, proximal injury location was associated with greater in-hospital mortality and aortic reintervention despite similar injury-grade distributions. Anatomic injury zone may complement injury grade when assessing procedural risk and planning postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Left Prefrontal-Centered Network Modulation During Cognitive-Motor Dual-Task Cycling After Stroke: An fNIRS Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare prefrontal and motor cortical activation and functional connectivity (FC) between single-task and cognitive-motor dual-task cycling after stroke as the primary outcomes, and to examine associations of task-related neural changes with task performance and clinical function as secondary analyses. The relationship between resting-state FC and task-related FC changes was examined exploratorily.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center, within-subject study included 42 clinically stable patients with stroke. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) was recorded during rest, single-task cycling, and dual-task cycling with serial subtraction by 7. Recordings covered four bilateral prefrontal and motor regions of interest. General linear model-derived β values quantified cortical activation; Pearson correlations quantified intra- and inter-regional FC. Paired tests compared task conditions. Spearman correlations examined associations with cognitive accuracy, motor dual-task cost, lower-limb motor function, global cognition, and gait speed. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate(FDR).

RESULTS: Compared with single-task cycling, dual-task cycling increased left prefrontal β values (mean difference, 0.0426; 95% CI, 0.0274-0.0621; P_FDR<0.001). FC increased for left-right prefrontal and left prefrontal-bilateral motor connections (mean differences, 0.0534-0.1092; P_FDR≤0.033). Resting-state FC was not associated with task-related FC changes. Left prefrontal activation changes correlated with cognitive accuracy (P_FDR<0.001), left motor activation changes with lower-limb motor function (P_FDR=0.037), and right prefrontal-left motor FC changes with global cognition (P_FDR=0.037). No FDR-significant associations were found with motor dual-task cost or gait speed.

CONCLUSION: Dual-task cycling after stroke was characterized by a greater left prefrontal HbO-derived hemodynamic response and stronger left prefrontal-centered HbO-based connectivity. These task-related hemodynamic changes may reflect cognitive-motor resource recruitment and individual functional differences.

articles.title: The microbiota-gut-brain axis in ischemic stroke recovery: Mechanistic insights, evidence gaps, and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis has been implicated in outcome after ischemic stroke, but acute neuroprotection, later functional status, and recovery trajectories are distinct endpoints. This narrative review examines immune and metabolic mechanisms against that distinction. Experimental studies establish that sympathetic activation can initiate intestinal epithelial and mucus-barrier injury, while microbiota perturbation can alter gut-associated lymphocyte responses and their trafficking to the injured brain or meninges. Metabolite studies differ in pathway and cell-type specificity: indole-3-propionic acid has microglia-targeted triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 evidence, indole-lactic acid has conflicting effects, and butyrate-associated interleukin-22 signaling leaves cellular sources unresolved. Human observational evidence mainly concerns later disability and cognitive impairment. Small probiotic trials report functional or cognitive signals, but mixed stroke populations, co-interventions, short follow-up, and unproven microbial mediation constrain interpretation. We assess recovery relevance separately from causal design and reporting limitations. Post-stroke experimental interventions with repeated behavioral assessments exist, but early treatment can combine tissue preservation with subsequent recovery. Clinical signals justify confirmatory studies rather than routine microbiota-directed treatment. Nutritional standardization and longitudinal biomarker validation are immediate priorities; defined interventions need reproducible exposure, safety, and rehabilitation-integrated testing. A bidirectional framework explains the evidence without equating mechanistic plausibility or preliminary clinical benefit with demonstrated neural repair.

articles.title: Precision in detecting ocular hypotensive effects of topical medications, laser trabeculoplasty, and trabecular meshwork bypass stent implantation surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the precision in calculating intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction following laser trabeculoplasty (SLT), trabecular meshwork bypass stenting (Hydrus), or prostaglandin analog (PGA) initiation using individual pre- and post-intervention measurements.

DESIGN: Longitudinal multi-site observational study.

SUBJECTS: Patients with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension treated with SLT, Hydrus, or PGA who underwent home IOP monitoring for 1 week before and after treatment as part of their routine care.

METHODS: Subjects used a rebound home tonometer to obtain multiple daily measurements. The average of all IOP measurements before and after treatment was used to calculate the "best available estimate" (BAE) of change in IOP. Individual or matched pairs and triplets of IOP values in each period were sampled in a bootstrap fashion to determine the precision of IOP comparisons, defined as being within 2mmHg of the BAE. Linear mixed-effects modeling (LMM) and multivariable linear regression (MLR) were used to account for the inclusion of both eyes.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Fraction of IOP change measurements within 2mmHg of the BAE.

RESULTS: 66 subjects (125 eyes) successfully recorded multiple daily IOP measurements before and after SLT, Hydrus, and PGA, with a mean change in IOP of in 1.7 mmHg (SE 0.32), 2.1 mmHg (0.38), and 2.2 mmHg (0.40), respectively. About 54% of IOP comparisons before and after treatment were within 2 mmHg of the BAE, with no significant differences across interventions (Dirichlet mixed-effects model). Accounting for diurnal variation improved precision: comparing only paired PM IOP values, clinic hour IOP values, or IOP values within two hours of each other increased this percentage to 56.7%, 57.0%, and 60.0%, respectively (p<0.005). Comparing the average of 2 or 3 IOP measurements before and after the interventions increased the precision to 69.6% and 83.7%, respectively (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Single IOP comparisons identify the change in IOP only slightly more than half the time. Results were similar regardless of IOP lowering intervention. Measuring IOP at similar times of day or taking multiple measurements before and after treatment improves precision. Home tonometry may be beneficial in assessing effectiveness of glaucoma therapy.

articles.title: IRAG1 is a smooth muscle cell-enriched coronary artery disease candidate gene regulated by SRF/MYOCD.
articles.abstract: Inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor-associated cGMP kinase substrate 1 (IRAG1) is a well-established regulator of intracellular Ca2+ signaling and smooth muscle cell (SMC) relaxation, yet its relevance to vascular disease and transcriptional regulation remain poorly understood. Here, we identified IRAG1 as a candidate effector gene at a coronary artery disease (CAD) susceptibility locus by integrating GWAS, eQTL and scATAC-seq datasets. Multiple variants linked to the CAD index variant rs11042937 were associated with IRAG1 expression in human aortic tissues, including a variant rs7482037 located within a vascular SMC (VSMC)-selective regulatory element linked to IRAG1 by peak-to-gene analysis. IRAG1 was enriched in arterial tissues and contractile VSMCs but downregulated in human atherosclerotic plaques and phenotypically modulated VSMCs. Cholesterol loading and inflammatory stimulation similarly reduced IRAG1 expression in cultured VSMCs. Mechanistically, myocardin (MYOCD), a master regulator of the contractile VSMC phenotype through its interaction with serum response factor (SRF), robustly induced IRAG1 expression. Luciferase reporter assays further demonstrated that three evolutionarily conserved promoter CArG elements mediate MYOCD-dependent transcriptional activation. Functionally, IRAG1 knockdown in human coronary artery SMCs induced inflammatory and proliferative transcriptional programs, and significantly enhanced VSMC proliferation under both basal and PDGF-BB-stimulated conditions. Together, these findings identify IRAG1 as a SMC-enriched candidate CAD effector gene and extend the functional scope of the SRF/MYOCD transcriptional program to include an additional regulator of intracellular Ca2+ signaling and VSMC relaxation. IRAG1 may contribute to maintaining VSMC homeostasis and represents a potential therapeutic target for future investigation in atherosclerotic disease.

articles.title: Productive Failure-Based Teaching for Uncertainty Management in Cerebrovascular Decision-Making: A Nonrandomized Mixed-Methods Study.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Managing uncertainty is central to cerebrovascular practice. We compared short-term outcomes of productive failure and direct instruction in neurology residents.

METHODS: This single-center, nonrandomized controlled pretest-posttest mixed-methods study allocated 62 residents; 60 were analyzed (30 per group) after one per group was excluded for incomplete baseline questionnaires. Each curriculum comprised five 90-minute sessions over 9 elapsed calendar days. Assessments occurred within 7 days before the first session and within 7 days after the final session. Mean pre-post intervals were 17.4 days for productive failure and 18.0 days for control. Uncertainty tolerance was the primary outcome; secondary outcomes were critical thinking disposition, simulated decision quality, and decision time. Analysis of covariance adjusted for corresponding baseline scores. Focus groups and reflective journals explored productive failure participants' experiences.

RESULTS: Adjusted productive failure-minus-control differences were 5.32 for uncertainty tolerance (95% confidence interval 1.92-8.72; P = 0.003), 16.27 for critical thinking disposition (5.53-27.01; P = 0.004), 9.21 for decision quality (5.12-13.31; P < 0.001), and 0.100 minutes for decision time (-0.059-0.259; P = 0.215). Qualitative themes concerned initial struggle, structured debriefing, and a shift toward ambiguity management.

CONCLUSIONS: Productive failure was associated with higher short-term uncertainty tolerance, critical thinking disposition, and simulated decision quality. The nonrandomized design limits causal inference; these assessments do not establish durable change or knowledge retention.

articles.title: Timing of DOAC initiation after ischaemic stroke with atrial fibrillation: a UK survey of changes in opinion and practice.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Several recent clinical trials have reported that early direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) initiation following acute ischaemic stroke and atrial fibrillation is safe and non-inferior to delayed DOAC initiation. This study aims to explore whether these findings are associated with changes in clinical practice.

METHODS: An online survey was sent to UK based clinicians via national organisations in 2025. Responders were asked to select what day following acute ischaemic stroke they would initiate anticoagulation in three case vignettes of differing stroke severity. Responses were compared to a survey conducted in 2018, prior to the publication of the trials TIMING, ELAN, START and OPTIMAS. Median values and interquartile ranges for the day in which responders would initiate anticoagulation were generated for each vignette and compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. Questions surrounding confidence in early DOAC initiation and whether clinical practice has changed following the OPTIMAS trial were asked.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven people responded to the 2025 survey. In mild stroke the median day of DOAC initiation was day 1 (IQR 1-3); in moderate stroke day 3 (IQR 2-5) and in severe stroke day 7 (IQR 4-14). This was significantly lower in all three vignettes compared to the 2018 survey, with the differences in median between surveys being 2 days in mild stroke (p <0.001), 4 days in moderate stroke (p <0.001) and 7 days in severe stroke (p <0.001). 98.5% (n=65) of responders felt very or somewhat confident in early DOAC initiation and 86.3% (n=57) reported a change in their clinical practice.

CONCLUSION: In this online survey, following the publication of several trials including OPTIMAS, UK-based clinicians demonstrate and report greater confidence in the early initiation of DOACs following acute ischaemic stroke. Over 85% of respondents reported a change in clinical practice, suggesting that trial data can rapidly influence patient care.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights Into Exercise-Driven Stroke Rehabilitation for Post-Stroke Behavioral and Functional Recovery: Integrating Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract: Objective To systematically elucidate the underlying mechanisms by which exercise facilitates functional recovery after stroke, and to provide evidence-based perspectives on optimal exercise prescription for stroke rehabilitation.Methods This review synthesizes findings from both preclinical and clinical studies investigating the effects of exercise on post-stroke recovery. Mechanistic evidence was drawn from animal models and cellular experiments, while clinical evidence was derived from trials employing aerobic, resistance, balance, and robotic-assisted training, with outcomes measured using biomarkers including BDNF, IGF-1, VEGF, and inflammatory cytokines.Results Exercise promotes stroke recovery through four interconnected mechanistic pathways: (1) repairing mitochondrial function via regulation of fission and autophagy; (2) reducing neuroinflammation and inhibiting pyroptosis; (3) enhancing neuroplasticity through dendritic remodeling and synaptic repair; and (4) stimulating angiogenesis by upregulating VEGF and eNOS to restore cerebral perfusion. Clinical studies corroborate these findings, demonstrating that various exercise modalities significantly improve gait, muscle strength, mood, and cognitive function, with biomarker changes correlating with functional gains.Conclusion Exercise exerts multi-target, multi-pathway synergistic effects that constitute a robust biological basis for stroke rehabilitation. However, optimal parameters regarding exercise intensity and timing remain to be standardized. Future research should prioritize individualized exercise prescription to maximize therapeutic benefits and facilitate widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Heparin-Based Prophylaxis Is Not Associated With Lower Venous Thromboembolism Risk After Elective Single-Level Lumbar Fusion: An Electronic Health Record Analysis of 144,752 Patients.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is an uncommon but serious complication of spine surgery. The benefits of chemoprophylaxis remain uncertain given concerns regarding postoperative bleeding.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the associations between heparin-based prophylaxis, VTE incidence, and bleeding-associated outcomes after elective single-level lumbar fusion.

STUDY DESIGN/SETTING: Retrospective cohort study using Epic Cosmos, a national electronic health record database.

PATIENT SAMPLE: Adults undergoing elective single-level lumbar fusion between 2016 and 2025 were categorized as receiving no prophylaxis, early prophylaxis (postoperative day [POD] 0-2), or delayed prophylaxis (POD 3-5) with prophylactic-dose unfractionated or low-molecular-weight heparin.

OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was 90-day VTE. Secondary outcomes included 90-day transfusion, spinal irrigation and debridement (I&D), and hemorrhagic stroke.

METHODS: Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models accounting for clinical and operative characteristics and comorbidities were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: Among 144,752 eligible patients, 107,528 (74.3%) received no prophylaxis, 34,859 (24.1%) early prophylaxis, and 2,365 (1.6%) delayed prophylaxis. Prophylactic anticoagulation was not associated with reduced 90-day VTE (early vs. none: HR 1.08, 95% CI [0.95, 1.23], p = 0.470; delayed vs. none: HR 1.21 [0.86, 1.70], p = 0.266). Early prophylaxis was associated with higher hazards of transfusion (HR 1.70 [1.54, 1.88], p < 0.001), I&D (HR 1.50 [1.26, 1.79], p < 0.001) and hemorrhagic stroke (HR 1.84 [1.17, 2.90], p = 0.018). Delayed prophylaxis was not associated with transfusion (HR 1.28 [0.96, 1.70], p = 0.095) but was associated with higher hazards of I&D (HR 2.33 [1.60, 3.41], p < 0.001) and hemorrhagic stroke (HR 2.83 [1.11, 7.21], p = 0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: Heparin-based prophylaxis was not associated with a lower VTE risk but was associated with a higher risk for bleeding-related events. These findings raise questions regarding the utility of universal heparin-based prophylaxis in this population and should be weighed alongside individual thromboembolic and bleeding risks.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III.

articles.title: Clinical practice guidelines from the Societat Catalana d'Anestesiologia, Reanimació i Terapèutica del Dolor (SCARTD) for the comprehensive management of the difficult airway in obstetric patients.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
articles.abstract: The Airway Division of the Societat Catalana d'Anestesiologia, Reanimació i Terapèutica del Dolor (SCARTD) has drawn up these clinical guidelines for the comprehensive management of the difficult airway in obstetric patients. The aim of this document is to update the available evidence and current recommendations to include the scientific evidence published since the previous version. To draw up these guidelines, the main international guidelines on airway management in obstetrics were identified and examined, and those with the highest methodological quality were selected using the AGREE II instrument, and a systematic review of the literature published between 2012 and 2025 was performed. When evidence was absent, limited, indirect, or of low quality, recommendations were established through a Delphi consensus process involving experts in the field. The guideline addresses key aspects of airway assessment, preparation, and management in pregnant women, including advance airway planning, optimization of interdisciplinary communication, and the role of clinical simulation as a strategy to improve patient safety. This document provides updated and practical recommendations for the management of the difficult airway in obstetric patients, with the aim of enhancing maternal safety and optimizing clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Digital Health and the Next Decade of Electrophysiology.
Epigenetic Aging and Severity of Nocturnal Intermittent Hypoxia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal intermittent hypoxia (IH) is a hallmark feature of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and contributes to oxidative stress and inflammation, which in turn may accelerate biological aging. Epigenetic clocks can estimate biological age from DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Is greater severity of IH associated with increased biological aging?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We studied adults referred for suspected OSA in a multisite sleep and circadian research network, a cross-sectional observational cohort (2016-2021). IH severity was assessed using the 4% oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from home sleep apnea testing or in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG). DNAm from peripheral blood leukocytes was assayed using Illumina EPIC arrays. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) and pace of aging were calculated using multiple DNAm clocks. Linear regression models were adjusted for leukocyte composition, age, sex, ethnicity, BMI, smoking, site, alcohol, diabetes, and hypertension. A false discovery rate of 0.05 was used.

RESULTS: A total of 1364 participants were included (median age, 56 yrs; median ODI, 16/h; median BMI, 32 kg/m2; 57% male). Higher ODI was associated with EAA for PhenoAge (β = 0.028, adjusted P = .0048) and with pace of aging (DunedinPACE, β = 0.0005, adjusted P =.0012). No significant associations were observed for first-generation clocks.

INTERPRETATION: Greater IH severity, as assessed by ODI, was independently associated with increased biological aging as measured by PhenoAge and DunedinPACE clocks. These findings support a link between OSA and biological aging, raising the possibility of using epigenetic age measures as biomarkers of OSA-related morbidity.

articles.title: DHEA-S in Pulmonary Hypertension: Insights from PVDOMICS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH.

RESULTS: DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p<0.01 for all). Associations between DHEA-S levels and PH severity metrics appeared most prominent in females with Group 1 PH. A doubling of DHEA-S was associated with a 2.8 mmHg (95% CI 1.6-4.1) lower mean pulmonary artery pressure, 3.2% (95% CI 2.0-4.4%) higher RV ejection fraction, and 22m (95% CI 11-33) farther 6MWD (all p<0.01). Higher DHEA-S associated with better RV function, but not pulmonary hemodynamics or 6MWD in females with Group 2 PH and males with Group 3 PH. In Group 1 PH, associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity appeared stronger in post-menopausal compared with premenopausal females.

INTERPRETATION: Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.

articles.title: Novel Combined Heart-Liver Transplantation Strategy in Fontan-Associated Heart and Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT) in patients with failing Fontan physiology remains challenging due to patients' extensive surgical histories, complex anatomy, significant collateral vessel burden, and often advanced multiorgan dysfunction. We describe a comprehensive, protocolized surgical strategy to optimize outcomes in this population.

METHODS: In December 2023, we implemented a standardized CHLT approach for patients with Fontan-associated heart and liver disease. Key elements include 1) a multidisciplinary selection process; 2) routine utilization of ex vivo perfusion for both cardiac and hepatic allograft preservation; 3) dual attending case coverage; 4) staged implantation with routine extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) support following heart implantation; and 5) continued hemodynamic optimization during hepatic implantation. We review outcomes of 12 consecutive CHLT procedures performed using this strategy.

RESULTS: Mean age at CHLT was 31.2 years (standard deviation 12.2, range 14-50); 75% were male. All had single-ventricle physiology after Fontan palliation and biopsy-proven cirrhosis. Most grafts (83%) were from donation-after-brain-death donors. Median ex vivo perfusion times were 225 and 609 minutes for heart and liver grafts, respectively. Preemptive VA-ECMO was used in all cases, with more than half decannulated intraoperatively. One early death occurred in a highly sensitized patient; all others remain free from stroke, renal failure, and cardiac rejection. One-year survival was 92%.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured, protocolized CHLT strategy can achieve favorable early outcomes in carefully selected patients with Fontan-associated heart and liver disease.

articles.title: Impact of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist Treatment on Post-Operative Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated cardiovascular benefits with anti-inflammatory and anti-arrhythmic properties. This study aimed to evaluate the association of GLP-1 use with postoperative atrial fibrillation and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery from 2010 to 2025. Patients were stratified into GLP-1 users and non-users. Patients with a history of atrial fibrillation (AF), concurrent MAZE procedure, and prior cardioversions or ablations were excluded. The primary outcome was incidence of new onset postoperative AF within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included AF-related readmissions and all-cause mortality. Multivariable adjusted regression models were used to compare POAF incidence and time-to-event secondary outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 8,672 patients were included. The 411 GLP-1 users were younger with higher BMI and HbA1c and were more likely to have diabetes compared to non-users (all p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, GLP-1 users demonstrated a significantly lower incidence of postoperative AF compared to non-users (29.0% vs. 34.6%, RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.99, p=0.038). AF-related readmission in GLP-1 users were 1.2% at 1 year and 3.5% at 5 years, compared to 2.9% and 6.5% in non-users, respectively (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.30-1.13, p=0.111). One- and five-year mortality was similar between groups (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67-1.25, p=0.561).

CONCLUSIONS: In this large real-world cohort, GLP-1 agonist use was associated with significant reduction of new onset postoperative AF and trended towards lower AF related readmissions. These findings support further investigation of GLP-1s in perioperative cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Risk Model for Long-Term Mortality after Esophageal Cancer Resection - Analysis from the STS General Thoracic Surgery Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are no reliable risk models for predicting long-term survival after esophagectomy for esophageal cancer. We aimed to address this gap by developing and validating an all-cause mortality risk model to predict long-term survival probabilities in esophagectomy patients.

METHODS: Adult patients undergoing esophagectomy for esophageal cancer in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (2012-2023; 280 hospitals) were studied. Vital status was determined by linkage to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Death Index and/or Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services inpatient data. Risk model to estimate survival probability was developed using stratified multivariable Cox regression. Discrimination was assessed using bootstrap-adjusted concordance index and time-dependent ROC. Calibration was evaluated by comparing observed to predicted survival probabilities. Generalizability was evaluated by internal-external repeated cross-validation.

RESULTS: 16,056 esophageal cancer patients were included. Median follow-up was 5.4 years, with mean age of 65.7 years (SD=9.2). Five-year survival for pathologic stages I-IV were 62.0%, 45.9%, 31.1% and 23.7%, respectively. Most patients (76.8%) received neoadjuvant therapy with 19.0% pathological complete response (pCR) overall. Patients with pCR demonstrated higher 5-year overall survival (61.8% vs 40.6%). Bootstrap adjusted C-index was 0.68 (95%CI=0.67-0.68); incorporating postoperative complications into the model increased C-index to 0.70.

CONCLUSIONS: A 10-year risk prediction model for all-cause mortality was developed using national-scale, real-world clinical data linked to long-term vital status data. This model showed excellent performance with accurate prediction of observed survival patterns in all patients, across all risk score groups, and for all pathologic stages and neoadjuvant treatment.

articles.title: Psychological distress and cardiovascular reactivity: Two dimensions of stress-related risk.
After CARDIO-TTRansform: Rethinking disease-modifying therapy in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
Evolution of cardiovascular risk scores in type 2 diabetes: Insights from the USA, the UK, and China.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), and cardiovascular risk scores increasingly inform preventive strategies and treatment decisions. However, these scores have been developed across diverse populations, regions, and time periods using heterogeneous methodological approaches, raising questions about their comparability, transportability, and applicability in diabetes care. We provide an up-to-date synthesis of cardiovascular risk scores relevant to T2D in the USA, the UK, and China, drawing on reviews, guideline documents, and targeted literature searches across these settings and relevant regional or global contexts. Models were compared across 20 methodological and implementation domains. A total of 56 cardiovascular risk score entries were identified, including 31 classified as general-population models and 25 as T2D-specific models. These models differed substantially in derivation populations, predictor composition, outcome definitions, prediction horizons, validation patterns, and implementation characteristics, while T2D-specific models more frequently included diabetes-related predictors such as glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), diabetes duration, albuminuria, and renal function. Descriptive evidence based largely on indirect cross-study comparisons did not establish a consistent performance advantage for either category. Marked regional variation may reflect differences in epidemiology, healthcare systems, data infrastructure, and guideline traditions, which could influence model development, recalibration, and clinical use. Cardiovascular risk prediction has gradually moved towards larger datasets, richer predictor information, broader cardiovascular outcomes, greater emphasis on validation, and more accessible implementation formats. Overall, cardiovascular risk scores in T2D show substantial heterogeneity, and no single model is optimal across all settings. Selection of cardiovascular risk scores in T2D patients should place emphasis on population-specific validation, calibration, alignment of the predicted outcome and prediction horizon with the clinical decision, predictor availability, and implementation feasibility, rather than model category alone. Local recalibration and periodic performance reassessment may be particularly relevant when absolute risk estimates inform threshold-based preventive treatment decisions. (300 /300 words).

articles.title: Risk of Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack After Pulsed Field Ablation Compared with Thermal Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether pulsed field ablation (PFA) carries a cerebrovascular risk different from that of thermal ablation has been questioned since an adjudicated cohort reported a higher 30-day incidence of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) with PFA. Previous meta-analyses addressed this question only as a secondary outcome, with pooling methods poorly suited to rare events.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the incidence of stroke or TIA after PFA and thermal ablation for atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase and the Cochrane Library through September 2026 for studies comparing PFA with thermal ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF). The primary endpoint was the composite of stroke or TIA within 30 days; secondary endpoints were stroke and TIA within 30 days, and all endpoints over the full follow-up. Effects were pooled as random-effects Peto odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies comprising 21,915 patients were included. Within 30 days, stroke or TIA occurred in 24 of 6,688 patients after PFA and in 17 of 10,973 after thermal ablation (OR 2.18; 95% CI 1.13-4.22; I2 = 0%). In paroxysmal AF, the estimate was in the same direction but not significant (OR 2.76; 95% CI 0.85-8.93). Stroke (OR 1.43; 95% CI 0.36-5.73) and TIA (OR 2.09; 95% CI 0.37-11.67) did not differ, nor did any endpoint over the full follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: PFA was associated with an approximately 2-fold higher incidence of stroke or TIA within 30 days than thermal ablation. This result should be considered hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies with systematic neurological assessment are warranted.

articles.title: Body Mass Index and Perioperative Complications Following Acetabular Fracture Fixation: A Single-Centre Analysis of 421 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to answer the following questions: (1) Do obese patients presenting with acetabular fractures have different fracture characteristics and injury findings at presentation compared with normal-weight and overweight patients? (2) Is elevated BMI associated with perioperative complications following acetabular fracture fixation, after controlling for fracture-related characteristics?

HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that elevated BMI would be associated with distinct fracture characteristics at presentation and with an increased risk of perioperative complications following acetabular fracture fixation.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed of 421 patients who underwent operative fixation of an acetabular fracture at our institution with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Patients were stratified into three BMI groups: normal (BMI ≤ 25, Group 1, n = 231; N), overweight (BMI > 25 AND < 30, Group 2, n = 133; OW), and obese (BMI ≥ 30, Group 3, n = 57; OB).

RESULTS: The three BMI groups differed significantly in sex distribution (p = 0.048), and prevalence of diabetes (p = 0.049). Posterior wall involvement (N 44.2%, OW 40.2%, OB 68.4%; p = 0.001), the distribution of fracture patterns (p = 0.001), dislocation (31.9%, 24.2%, 47.4%; p = 0.007), femoral head lesions (6.2%, 9.8%, 19.3%; p = 0.009) and loose bodies (30.5%, 22.1%, 43.9%; p = 0.010) differed across the three groups. Perioperative complications occurred in 6.5% (N), 7.5% (OW) and 17.5% (OB) of patients (p = 0.024). On exploratory binary logistic regression, BMI was associated with perioperative complications (OR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.02-1.19, p = 0.01), with each 1-unit increase in BMI associated with a 10% increase in the odds of complications.

DISCUSSION: In this large single-center study of operatively treated acetabular fractures, fracture presentation differed across BMI groups, with difference in the rates of posterior-type fractures, posterior wall involvement, hip dislocation, femoral head lesions and loose bodies. Elevated BMI was associated with perioperative complications following acetabular fracture fixation, even after controlling for these fracture-related characteristics.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III; retrospective prognostic comparative study.

articles.title: Validation and Establishment of the Contrast Volume Prediction Model: For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR (the FORE-EVAR calculator).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a preventable complication associated with iodinated contrast volume during endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR). We previously published a prediction model "For Optimizing Renal Efficiency in EVAR" (FORE-EVAR) which utilizes 13 patient-specific variables to generate a recommended contrast-volume threshold to prevent CA-AKI after EVAR. This study evaluates FORE-EVAR against machine-learning models and establishes FORE-EVAR's user-interface for general use.

METHODS: Eight machine-learning algorithms were applied to a 49,417-patient Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) EVAR cohort (2003-July 2024). Following comparison of FORE-EVAR with machine-learning models, an updated VQI EVAR dataset (August 2024-October 2025) of 7,112 new patients was used for temporal validation.

RESULTS: Using split-sample approach (80% training; 20% validation) of the 49,417-patient dataset, FORE-EVAR demonstrated a strong AUC=0.753 (comparable to machine-learning models [range=0.712-0.759]) with similar performance across other predictive metrics. Importantly, FORE-EVAR requires input of 13 patient variables which is significantly less than the 50+ variables required by machine-learning models. The comparable prediction metrics and simplicity of variables support FORE-EVAR as a practical candidate for clinical implementation. Temporal validation with the 7,112-patient dataset showed AUC=0.706, emphasizing FORE-EVAR's predictability across cohorts. FORE-EVAR's user-interface provides three personalized outputs: CA-AKI risk category (Low, Moderate, High, or Very High); a recommended contrast volume threshold; and predicted CA-AKI risk at fixed volumes of 50mL and 100mL for procedural guidance.

CONCLUSIONS: FORE-EVAR is a validated prediction tool which provides valuable patient-specific contrast-volume recommendations. Prospective studies are needed to evaluate FORE-EVAR's impact on intraoperative contrast volume and incidence of CA-AKI.

articles.title: Early Clinical Outcomes and Midterm Symptom Response After Hybrid Repair of Symptomatic Aberrant Subclavian Artery and Kommerell Diverticulum: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe early morbidity and mortality and midterm symptom response after hybrid repair of symptomatic aberrant subclavian artery with Kommerell diverticulum.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center series at Ankara City Hospital included 11 symptomatic adults who underwent hybrid repair. Demographic characteristics, arch laterality, presenting symptoms, operative information, perioperative events, and follow-up symptom assessments were reviewed. Analyses were descriptive.

RESULTS: Patients were aged 45-61 years; seven were male. Technical success was reported in all 11 patients (100%). Three patients had a right-sided and eight a left-sided aortic arch. Dysphagia occurred in eight patients (72.7%), chest pain or pressure in six (54.5%), and dyspnea in four (36.4%). Early mortality was 1/11 (9.1%). One patient developed delayed paraplegia after central debranching and TEVAR and subsequently died from pneumonia-associated sepsis. Stroke and an access complication occurred in another patient after central debranching and zone 0 TEVAR. Hospital stay among the 10 survivors was 6.7 ± 2.3 days. Mean reported follow-up was 32.6 ± 9.7 months. Among 10 assessed patients, five (50.0%) had complete relief, three (30.0%) partial relief, and two (20.0%) no change. Quantitative diverticular remodeling and systematic cohort-wide branch-patency data were unavailable.

CONCLUSION: Symptom improvement after hybrid repair was reported in most assessed patients, but complete relief occurred in half of those assessed. The early death and neurological morbidity underline the risks of repair. These findings support individualized counseling and structured follow-up but do not establish long-term durability.

articles.title: Utility of preoperative vein mapping in the detection of venous disease prior to infrainguinal arterial bypass.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Great saphenous vein (GSV) is the preferred bypass graft conduit for treatment of infrainguinal peripheral arterial disease. Duplex ultrasound vein mapping can assess GSV quality during preoperative planning, including the presence of thrombus or thrombophlebitis. The objective of this study was to identify the proportion of patients with these findings on preoperative mapping and, secondarily, to evaluate vein diameter.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-institution study of patients with peripheral arterial disease undergoing outpatient vein mapping from March 2013-December 2021 preparatory to infrainguinal bypass. We recorded the presence of superficial vein thrombosis (SVT), ipsilateral deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and GSV diameter.

RESULTS: A total of 191 patients met inclusion criteria. Previously undiagnosed SVT was found in 13.2% and DVT in 11.7% of all veins evaluated. Of the DVTs, 55.0% were found in the tibial or peroneal veins, 20.0% in the femoral-popliteal veins, and 15.0% in both sets of segments. No significant differences in demographics or comorbidities were identified in patients with and without SVT. Approximately half (51.5%) had GSV that was ≥2.5mm throughout the thigh and calf, and only one-third (32.7%) had GSV ≥2.5mm without SVT or ipsilateral DVT.

CONCLUSION: An appreciable portion of patients were found to have previously undiagnosed SVT and DVT. These findings highlight the importance of vein mapping to guide the decision to use GSV as an infrainguinal bypass conduit, assist in deciding which segments are appropriate for use, and avoid unnecessary dissection.

articles.title: Prevalence and Impact of Different Patterns of Left Ventricular Remodeling on Chronic Severe Aortic Regurgitation Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic aortic regurgitation (AR) leads to increased left ventricular (LV) preload and afterload, most commonly manifesting as eccentric hypertrophy, although other remodeling patterns may occur. This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of different patterns of LV remodeling in patients with chronic severe AR and to evaluate their associations with all-cause mortality and symptoms.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 1,009 patients with ≥moderate-severe chronic AR identified by echocardiography. LV geometry was classified as normal, concentric remodeling, concentric hypertrophy, or eccentric hypertrophy based on relative wall thickness and LV mass index; concentric remodeling and hypertrophy were combined because of small sample size. Associations with outcomes were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Eccentric hypertrophy was the most prevalent pattern (65%), followed by concentric remodeling/hypertrophy (17%) and normal geometry (18%). Concentric remodeling/hypertrophy was more common in older patients with systemic hypertension and chronic kidney disease and was associated with less severe AR. This remodeling pattern was associated with increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 2.17; 95% confidence interval, 1.34-3.52; p <0.001) after adjustment for age, sex, NYHA functional class, AR severity, and the Charlson Comorbidity Index, whereas no mortality difference was observed between eccentric hypertrophy and normal geometry. LV remodeling patterns were not associated with symptom status in multivariable analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: In severe AR, concentric remodeling/hypertrophy and normal geometry are present in a substantial proportion of patients. Concentric remodeling/hypertrophy is associated with increased all-cause mortality, whereas LV remodeling patterns are not associated with symptoms.

articles.title: Adverse perinatal outcomes associated with increasing birthweight among U.S. births complicated by diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Macrosomia is increasing in prevalence globally and is more common among pregnancies complicated by diabetes. There are limited data regarding the risks with increasing degrees of birthweight above 4,000 grams among births complicated by diabetes.

OBJECTIVE: We sought to evaluate the association between increasing birthweight above 4,000 grams and adverse outcomes among births complicated by diabetes, stratified by diabetes type (preexisting and gestational diabetes).

STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study of singleton, non-anomalous, U.S. live births to persons with diabetes between 37- and 42-weeks' gestation from years 2012 to 2021 utilizing data from the National Center for Health Statistics. Births of infants weighing at least 3000 grams were included and stratified into four increasing weight categories: 4,000-4,499 grams, 4,500-4,999 grams and ≥5,000 grams with 3,000-3,999 grams serving as the reference group. Maternal outcomes included mode of delivery, obstetric anal sphincter injuries, gestational hypertension, eclampsia, admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), and need for blood transfusion. Neonatal outcomes included Apgar score <7 at 5 minutes, neonatal ICU admission, assisted ventilation, seizures, and infant death. Chi-squared and multivariable Poisson regression analyses were performed for statistical comparisons and presented as adjusted incidence risk ratios (aRR).

RESULTS: There were 1,736,509 births included in this analysis. Higher birthweights were associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Births of infants in all birthweight groups ≥4,000 grams were associated with higher risk of delivery via operative vaginal or cesarean, maternal blood transfusion, Apgar score <7 at 5 minutes, NICU admission, neonatal assisted ventilation, neonatal seizures and infant death. Newborns ≥5,000 grams had the highest rates of adverse neonatal outcomes, including Apgar score <7 at 5 minutes (aRR 3.23, 95% CI 2.94-3.54), NICU admission (aRR 4.15, 95% CI 4.03-4.27), assisted ventilation (aRR 3.15, 95% CI 2.99-3.31), neonatal seizures (aRR 4.08, 95% CI 2.41-6.90) and infant death (aRR 2.91, 95% CI 1.98-4.29). When stratified by diabetes type, similar effect sizes were seen, although the adjusted risk of adverse outcomes was generally higher for those with gestational diabetes.

CONCLUSIONS: Birthweights ≥4,000 grams were associated with increasingly higher risk of adverse outcomes among births complicated by diabetes. Future studies focused on targeted prenatal interventions to reduce risk for macrosomia as well as improve postnatal transitions are needed.

articles.title: Preoperative azithromycin use in cesarean deliveries complicated by suspected intraamniotic infection.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A prior randomized clinical trial demonstrated the benefit of adjunctive azithromycin for labored cesareans in reducing postpartum infections and neonatal morbidity but excluded patients with intraamniotic infection (IAI). IAI is an independent risk factor for postpartum infectious morbidity and neonatal morbidity. The role of azithromycin in cesareans complicated by IAI remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the impact of preoperative azithromycin use on postpartum infectious complications and neonatal morbidity in patients who underwent cesarean deliveries complicated by suspected IAI (sIAI).

STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing cesarean deliveries complicated by sIAI, and their corresponding singletons, in a single healthcare system between April 1, 2013 and December 13, 2023. Patients were excluded if they were missing delivery admission data, antibiotic data, or lacked a clinical diagnosis of sIAI. All singleton neonates were included. Clinical diagnosis of sIAI was based on standard guidelines. Exposure of interest was preoperative azithromycin. The primary outcome in this study was a postpartum infectious morbidity composite including surgical site infection (SSI), endometritis, pelvic abscess, pneumonia, or sepsis within 42 days of delivery. Secondary maternal outcomes included components of the composite, readmission, and adverse reactions to azithromycin. A planned secondary analysis was performed assessing neonatal morbidity. The primary outcome for this analysis was a neonatal morbidity composite during the delivery admission, which included suspected or confirmed sepsis, respiratory distress syndrome, necrotizing enterocolitis, periventricular leukomalacia, intraventricular hemorrhage, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and death. Secondary outcomes for the neonates included components of the composite, admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), and NICU length of stay. Data were analyzed with bivariate statistics and regression models to control for confounders and practice changes over the study period.

RESULTS: Of the 985 delivering patients who met inclusion criteria, 666 (67.6%) received preoperative azithromycin. Differences in patient age, race, penicillin allergy frequency, and tobacco use were seen between patients who received azithromycin and those who did not. Preoperative azithromycin use was associated with different rates of intrapartum IAI treatment, vaginal preparation use, preoperative cefazolin prophylaxis, postpartum antibiotic receipt, and estimated blood loss at delivery. After controlling for confounding variables, azithromycin use was associated with markedly lower odds of the maternal composite outcome (aOR: 0.58; 95% CI:0.35, 0.96) and SSI (aOR: 0.48; 95% CI:0.25, 0.92). Preoperative azithromycin was also associated with reduced odds of the neonatal composite outcome (aOR: 0.36, 95% CI: 0.23, 0.57), suspected sepsis (aOR: 0.29, 95% CI: 0.18, 0.47) and NICU admission (aOR: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.33, 0.72).

CONCLUSION: Azithromycin use as antibiotic prophylaxis in cesarean deliveries complicated by sIAI was associated with lower rates of postpartum infectious complications within 42 days postpartum and neonatal morbidity during the delivery admission.

articles.title: Reverse peritoneal autodialysis: pseudo-AKI after prostatectomy.
The gut-lung-brain axis in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke disrupts intestinal homeostasis and pulmonary host defense, but a continuous microbiota-mediated pathway to secondary brain injury remains unproven. This narrative review evaluates gut-brain, gut-lung, and lung-brain interactions, distinguishing experimental evidence, clinical associations, and findings from other disease models. Experimental studies support intestinal microbial and immune contributions to stroke outcomes, barrier dysfunction, and dissemination of selected gut-associated bacteria. However, intestinal expansion is not necessarily required for pulmonary colonization, and microbial origin does not establish transmission routes. Aspiration, hematogenous or lymphatic dissemination, and impaired pulmonary clearance require separate investigation. Pneumonia is associated with poorer neurological outcomes, but microbiome-specific causation remains unestablished. Pulmonary microbiota-dependent immune and neural mechanisms identified in autoimmune and migraine models provide mechanistic precedents, yet their relevance to ischemic stroke remains uncertain. The gut-lung-brain axis therefore represents an evidence-informed framework rather than a proven self-sustaining causal cycle. Establishing microbial sources, transmission routes, and pulmonary mediation of brain injury is essential to identify actionable peripheral mechanisms influencing stroke injury and recovery.

articles.title: Insomnia reorganizes large-scale functional connectivity abnormalities in depression: Evidence from functional gradients and neurotransmitter mapping.
articles.abstract: Sleep disorders are one of the most prevalent and clinically important features of depression, yet their impact on the large-scale organization of brain functional abnormalities remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether insomnia reshapes whole-brain resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) abnormalities in depression and alter their hierarchical and neurochemical organization. Resting-state fMRI data were acquired from depressed patients with (INS, n = 32) and without insomnia symptoms (NINS, n = 24), and healthy controls (HC, n = 45). Network-based statistics (NBS) was used to identify altered RSFC subnetworks. We then examined the hierarchical distribution of network abnormalities using the principal functional gradient, assessed clinical relevance, and evaluated their spatial correspondence with neurotransmitter atlas. Results showed that the INS group exhibited more widespread functional connectivity impairments, primarily concentrated in the visual and sensorimotor networks. Moreover, these abnormal connections showed a hierarchical distribution pattern along the principal functional gradient, with lower-level sensory systems more affected than higher-level cognitive networks. Significant differences in node degree were observed in the visual network, and functional connectivity within this network was associated with anxiety scores in the INS group. Spatial similarity analyses revealed overlapping but distinct neurotransmitter profiles across groups, with shared correlations for mGluR5 and stronger μ-opioid-related associations in the INS group. These findings suggest that insomnia symptoms in depression are associated not simply with more severe dysfunction, but with a reorganization of large-scale functional abnormalities toward lower-order sensory systems, characterized by a gradient-dependent connectivity distribution and altered associations with specific neurotransmitter systems, particularly μ-opioid receptors.

articles.title: A Multicenter Randomized Open-Label Trial of On-Demand Direct Oral Anticoagulant Cessation in Colonoscopic Polypectomy (The MADOWAZU Trial).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Guidelines recommend preprocedural interruption of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), but it requires strict adherence and may lead to unnecessary anticoagulant interruption in patients without polypectomy. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficiency of "on-demand" DOAC cessation after polypectomy compared with "scheduled" cessation before colonoscopy for all patients.

METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial conducted at 33 hospitals in Japan compared a "scheduled" preprocedural DOAC cessation strategy for all patients with an "on-demand" strategy of continuing DOACs until the day of colonoscopy, followed by DOAC cessation after polypectomy if performed. The primary endpoint was polypectomy-related clinically significant bleeding, with a noninferiority margin of -5%.

RESULTS: Among 314 patients receiving DOACs who underwent colonoscopic polypectomy ("Scheduled" group, n=159, "On-demand" group, n=155), polypectomy-related clinically significant bleeding occurred in 7 patients (4.4%) in the "Scheduled" group and 5 patients (3.2%) in the "On-demand" group (risk difference, 1.2%; 90% CI, -2.4% to 4.7%), showing noninferiority. Intraprocedural controllable bleeding was more frequent in the "On-demand" group (Scheduled 3.4% vs. On-demand 7.0%; P = 0.0037). Periprocedural DOAC exposure was higher in the "On-demand" group than in the "Scheduled" group among patients without polypectomy. No thromboembolic events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In this open-label, multicenter, randomized trial, "on-demand" DOAC cessation after polypectomy was noninferior to "scheduled" preprocedural cessation regarding postpolypectomy bleeding, with fewer missed DOAC doses in patients without polypectomy but modestly more controllable intraprocedural bleeding, and may offer a practical alternative. University Hospital Medical Information Network (UMIN) Clinical Trials Registry, UMIN000039418.

articles.title: Triamcinolone Acetonide for Upper Eyelid Retraction in Thyroid Eye Disease: A Systematic Review and Single-Arm Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Upper eyelid retraction is the most frequent sign of thyroid eye disease, yet surgical correction is deferred until the disease is quiescent, and systemic corticosteroids and targeted biologics carry appreciable toxicity and cost. We searched 4 databases to April, 2026, and pooled 12 studies (540 patients, 741 analytical units) evaluating local periocular triamcinolone acetonide injection, extracting only the triamcinolone arm of comparative trials. Injection lowered margin reflex distance-1 by a mean of 1.78 mm (95% CI, 1.20 to 2.35 mm) and produced clinical improvement in 87.0% of treated units (95% CI, 80.0% to 93.0%). Clinical activity score and proptosis did not change significantly. Transient ocular hypertension occurred in 4.0% and post-injection ptosis in 0.6% (95% CI, 0.2% to 2.0% by generalized linear mixed model). Certainty of evidence was very low to low throughout because all data derive from uncontrolled single-arm cohorts. Local triamcinolone injection is an inexpensive, accessible option for eyelid retraction during active disease, although controlled trials are lacking.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes of anti-type 2 biologic therapies in eosinophilic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis of adjudicated cardiovascular events in phase 3 randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are followed by a marked and sustained increase in cardiovascular risk, and anti-type 2 biologics reduce exacerbations in eosinophilic COPD. Whether these agents modify cardiovascular outcomes is unknown.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched to 31 October 2026 for phase 3, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of anti-type 2 biologics in eosinophilic COPD. The primary outcome was independently adjudicated 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Data were pooled with the fixed-effect Peto method. Trial sequential analysis (TSA) was performed to assess the conclusiveness of the available evidence and estimate the sample size needed to detect a treatment effect, assuming a two-sided α of 5% and 80% power.

RESULTS: Seven trials met the eligibility criteria. Three (BOREAS, NOTUS and MATINEE; 2676 patients; 45 events) reported adjudicated MACE, whereas adjudicated MACE from GALATHEA and TERRANOVA were not reported. Biologic therapy was associated with a numerical but non-significant reduction in MACE (Peto odds ratio [OR] 0.66, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.37-1.19; p = 0.17; I2 = 0%; very low certainty). Estimates were OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.20-1.03) with interleukin (IL)-4/IL-13 blockade by dupilumab and OR 0.99 (95% CI 0.43-2.32) with IL-5 blockade by mepolizumab, with no evidence of a difference between molecular targets (test for subgroup differences, p = 0.19). The accrued information (2676 patients) was 24% of the required information size (10,959 patients).

CONCLUSIONS: Current phase 3 evidence does not establish a cardiovascular effect of anti-type 2 biologics in eosinophilic COPD. Standardized cardiovascular-risk assessment and prospectively adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes are needed in future biologic trials.

articles.title: Comment on "Management of portal vein thrombosis in cirrhosis: Risks, treatments, and outcomes of a retrospective multicenter study with over 10 years of follow-up".
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology

articles.title: ATP7B-Hepatic Stellate Cell Axis in Wilson Disease: From copper-induced hepatocyte injury to fibrosis and cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wilson disease results from pathogenic ATP7B variants that impair copper loading into ceruloplasmin and hepatobiliary copper excretion. Hepatic copper accumulation causes hepatocyte injury, inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, but the mechanisms linking copper stress to persistent fibrogenesis remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE: This critical review evaluates the ATP7B-hepatocyte-immune-hepatic stellate cell (HSC) axis as an integrative framework, distinguishing mechanisms directly demonstrated in Wilson disease from evidence derived from ATP7B-specific, copper-toxicity, and fibrosis models.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Human Wilson disease evidence supports copper retention, mitochondrial and proteostatic injury, inflammation, matrix remodelling, and fibrosis. Wilson disease-specific experimental studies further implicate hepatocyte TGF-β1, N2 neutrophil programming, Nrf2-SULT1E1-LXR dysregulation, NF-κB-associated inflammation, prion-protein-mediated copper uptake, and microtubule remodelling. Indirect evidence suggests roles for direct copper effects on HSCs, mitochondrial DAMP signalling, inflammasome activation, and extracellular-vesicle communication. However, Wilson-specific evidence remains limited for YAP/TAZ, Wnt signalling, ferroptosis, cuproptosis, hepatocyte extracellular-vesicle cargo, and a direct ATP7B-to-HSC relay.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports a multicellular ATP7B-copper-hepatocyte-immune-HSC framework rather than a single linear ATP7B-HSC pathway. Therapeutic strategies should be stage-matched, combining restoration of copper homeostasis with control of persistent hepatocyte injury, immune activation, HSC activity, and matrix remodelling.

articles.title: Futile Recanalization and Tissue-Level Reperfusion Failure after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Bibliometric Analysis from 2008 to 2026.
articles.abstract:
