OBJECTIVE: Futile recanalization remains a major barrier to the clinical effectiveness of endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), affecting approximately half of patients who achieve successful angiographic recanalization. This study mapped the global research landscape, collaborative networks, thematic structure, and emerging topics in this field.

METHODS: English-language publications classified as Article in the Web of Science Core Collection and meeting the predefined original-research eligibility criteria were identified for the period from January 1, 2008, to June 22, 2026. Bibliometric and visualization analyses were performed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R-bibliometrix.

RESULTS: A total of 249 articles from 92 journals were included, peaking at 53 publications in 2025. China led in corresponding author output; Australia and Switzerland achieved the highest average citations. Capital Medical University contributed the most articles (n = 106). Keyword co-occurrence analysis identified four thematic clusters: microvascular pathophysiology, imaging-based patient selection, clinical outcome prediction, and reperfusion injury. Keyword burst analysis suggested an increasing emphasis on tissue-level perfusion, large-vessel occlusion, and the no-reflow phenomenon during 2025-2026.

CONCLUSION: The literature increasingly emphasizes the distinction between macrovascular recanalization and tissue-level reperfusion, together with imaging-based risk stratification and potentially modifiable metabolic and inflammatory factors. These findings identify areas requiring further mechanistic investigation, external validation of predictive models, and prospective clinical evaluation.

articles.title: Surgical decompression of Atlantostyloid Jugular Compression.
articles.abstract: Atlantostyloid jugular compression syndrome is an increasingly recognized cause of venopathic intracranial hypertension. It presents an anatomic target for surgical intervention. The presentation includes visual disturbance, headache and sometimes nausea and vomiting. Diagnosis requires careful clinical evaluation and radiographic identification of the compression.

articles.title: Multivariate genome-wide association study of cardiometabolic diseases reveals shared genetic architecture and enhances risk prediction through integrated polygenic and proteomic risk scores.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiometabolic diseases (CMD) are interconnected, but their shared and domain-specific genetic architecture and the value of integrating genetic and proteomic information for risk prediction remain unclear.

METHODS: We applied LD score regression, factor analyses, and genomic structural equation modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics for seven CMD components in European-ancestry cohorts. We performed multivariate genome-wide association analysis, functional annotation, tissue and cell-type enrichment, gene prioritization, and pathway analysis. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) were evaluated in 310,708 UK Biobank participants, and proteomic risk scores (ProRS) were developed and tested in a proteomics subset of 33,253 participants.

RESULTS: A hierarchical model identified cardiac (coronary artery disease and heart failure), vascular (stroke and hypertension), and metabolic (body mass index, type 2 diabetes, and triglyceride-to-HDL cholesterol ratio) factors underlying a higher-order CMD factor. We identified 328 independent CMD-associated variants, including 15 novel variants, and prioritized 297 high-confidence CMD genes. Heritability was enriched in brain regions, adipose tissue, and gastrointestinal mucosa. Participants in the highest versus lowest CMD-PRS decile had 2.82-fold higher CMD risk. ProRS outperformed PRS for CMD prediction (AUC, 0.740 versus 0.681), while the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.741. Participants with high PRS and high ProRS had the greatest risk (HR, 2.51; 95% CI, 2.29-2.75).

CONCLUSION: CMD reflects shared genetic liability with distinguishable cardiac, vascular, and metabolic components. Plasma proteomics adds predictive information to inherited risk and may improve risk stratification, although external validation and a parsimonious protein panel are required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Residual Calcium Density Reflects Plaque Vulnerability and Cerebrovascular Event Risk in Symptomatic Carotid Disease.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The relationship between carotid calcification characteristics and plaque vulnerability or rupture risk remains controversial. This study investigated whether quantitative computed tomography angiography (CTA) metrics of carotid calcification (calcium score, volume, density, and residual [volume normalised] calcium density) are associated with plaque vulnerability, symptomatic status, and recurrent ipsilateral ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) in patients with carotid artery disease ipsilateral to cerebrovascular symptoms.

METHODS: Patients with recent TIA or ischaemic stroke and ipsilateral ≥ 2 mm carotid plaque with < 70% stenosis underwent baseline CTA and magnetic resonance imaging. Calcifications on CTA (≥ 130 HU) were segmented, yielding calcium score, volume, and density. As volume and density are strongly correlated, volume normalised residual calcium density was calculated as standardised residuals from a density-volume regression model. Associations with vulnerable plaque features (intraplaque haemorrhage, thin or ruptured fibrous cap, lipid rich necrotic core, and ulceration), symptomatic side, and recurrent ipsilateral TIA or ischaemic stroke were assessed using logistic, conditional logistic, and Cox regression models.

RESULTS: Among 193 patients (mean age 67.8 ± 8.5 years, 74.6% men), 26 had recurrent ipsilateral TIA (n = 14) or ischaemic stroke (n = 12), over median five year follow up. Lower calcium density and residual calcium density were independently associated with vulnerable plaque features (odds ratios [ORs] 0.40 - 0.60). Residual calcium density was independently associated with symptomatic side (OR 0.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.47 - 0.88) and recurrent TIA or ischaemic stroke (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.29 - 0.95).

CONCLUSION: Residual calcium density is an independent marker of carotid plaque vulnerability and ipsilateral ischaemic stroke and TIA risk in patients with carotid artery disease ipsilateral to cerebrovascular symptoms.

articles.title: Discharge Albuminuria in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Interpretation.
External evaluation of serum osmolality equations in critical care: transportability and formula-dependent classification in MIMIC-IV and eICU.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum osmolality equations are used in acute care, but their individual errors and dependence on the provenance of the reference result can limit interpretation in critical illness.

OBJECTIVES: We tested whether the Calderón B equation improves serum osmolality estimation in critically ill adults and how formula choice affects concentration classification.

METHODS: We analysed adult MIMIC-IV and eICU hospitalizations with complete chemistry at the first osmolality record within seven ICU days. The simple, Khajuria-Krahn, and Calderón B equations were compared without refitting using error, calibration, and classification. A previously fixed screening rule (Khajuria-Krahn ≥295 mOsm/kg for reference >300 mOsm/kg) was assessed descriptively in overlapping records. Confidence intervals used patient clusters in MIMIC-IV and hospital clusters in eICU.

RESULTS: The analysis included 3905 MIMIC-IV and 3286 eICU hospitalizations. MIMIC-IV MAEs were 7.00, 6.73, and 8.66 mOsm/kg for the simple, Khajuria-Krahn, and Calderón B equations; Calderón B exceeded Khajuria-Krahn by 1.92 mOsm/kg (95% CI 1.80-2.05). Corresponding eICU MAEs were 9.20, 8.92, and 10.35 mOsm/kg; the difference was 1.43 (0.75-2.07). Excluding seven hospitals with formula-like patterns reversed the eICU comparison with the simple equation but not with Khajuria-Krahn. In the formula-pattern-excluded eICU high-glucose subset, Calderón B reduced low-side classification at 320 mOsm/kg while increasing high-side classification. Fixed-rule sensitivity was 90.6% in MIMIC-IV and 89.3% in eICU; specificity was 73.8% and 72.4%.

CONCLUSIONS: Calderón B showed no transportable MAE advantage over Khajuria-Krahn. In the formula-pattern-excluded eICU high-glucose subset, formula choice changed classification direction, and hospital-level formula-like patterns materially affected eICU comparisons.

articles.title: A Novel Clinic Model: Embedding Palliative Care for Patients with Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: . Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) have high symptom burden and may lack the opportunity to express care preferences and engage in advance care planning (ACP). Embedding palliative care (PC) in kidney clinic may fulfill this unmet need.

MEASURES: . We developed and piloted screening criteria for older patients who may benefit from PC referral. Of those screened, we measured demographics, symptom management, ACP, dialysis discussions, healthcare utilization, and deaths.

INTERVENTION: . In this pilot, screening criteria identified older CKD patients with potentially unmet PC needs, and nephrologists were prompted to refer patients to PC. If referred, a PC appointment was scheduled adjacent to a kidney clinic visit.

OUTCOMES: . Of patients seen in the pilot embedded clinic, 100% reviewed ACP, 90% discussed symptoms, and 75% had dialysis discussions.

CONCLUSIONS/LESSONS LEARNED: . Embedding PC in kidney clinic for patients with advanced CKD with screening criteria is a feasible ambulatory model of care.

articles.title: Self-Care Practices in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Qualitative Study to Inform the Development of a Digital Behavioral Intervention.
articles.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus is a pregnancy complication that requires quick behavioral adaptation to maintain glycemic control. Interventions often target predefined behaviors, yet self-care practices remain mostly undescribed, and there is little connection to behavior theories. This study aimed to characterize how pregnant women with gestational diabetes enact self-care and discuss how practices can inform the development of a digital behavioral intervention. We interviewed 25 women living in Portugal with current or past gestational diabetes, recruited from hospitals and from the community. Interviews were semi-structured and focused on self-care practices, learning processes, and healthcare experiences. Sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically, informed by the Matarese et al. (2018) self-care model. The practices identified were organized into three categories: self-awareness, self-monitoring, and self-management. Self-awareness involved searching for information online, consulting healthcare professionals, and analyzing blood glucose levels. Self-monitoring included preparing for blood glucose measurement, as well as systematically registering the glycemia values and related events. Self-management encompassed changes in eating habits, such as strict meal scheduling, fractionated eating with snacks, food substitutions, label reading, and home cooking; and incorporated physical activity strategies, including walking after meals, strength training, and stretching exercises. Findings highlight that effective, long-term behavior change interventions should move beyond prescriptive advice to address underlying behavioral determinants and support women's lived practices. To that end, integrating behavior techniques of education, training, and enablement can better support women's needs, enhance adherence, reduce the burden of self-management, and ultimately improve health outcomes.

articles.title: Development and External Validation of a First-Trimester Prediction Model for Fetal Growth Restriction Using Fully Automated Placental Ultrasound: A Prospective Multicentre Observational Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and externally validate a first-trimester model for fetal growth restriction (FGR) using established risk factors alongside novel placental biomarkers.

DESIGN: Two prospective cohort studies: one for model development and one for geographically and temporally distinct external validation.

SETTING: A specialist fetal medicine centre (London) and a routine NHS ultrasound department (Oxford), UK.

POPULATION: Women attending routine first-trimester combined screening at 11+2-14+1 weeks of gestation.

METHODS: Alongside routine antenatal care, an additional first trimester three-dimensional placental scan with power Doppler was performed. The OxNNet Toolkit Placenta automatically derived placental volume and perfusion biomarkers (single vessel fractional moving blood volume), combined with established risk factors in a competing-risks (Fine-Gray) model. Development-cohort coefficients were applied unchanged on external validation.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Composite FGR (birthweight < 3rd centile, < 10th centile with abnormal fetal Doppler or < 10th centile with neonatal unit admission); discrimination (area under the curve, AUC) and detection rate at matched false-positive rates.

RESULTS: Of 6196 pregnancies (3083 [49.8%] nulliparous), 383 (6.2%) developed composite FGR. Placental volume was among the strongest predictors, second only to ethnicity. On external validation the AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.71-0.79). At the 34% false-positive rate of the existing UK risk-assessment approach, the model detected 70.1% (95% CI 62.1-78.6) of composite FGR cases, compared with 48% detection by the existing approach in the OxPLUS cohort. Performance was maintained in nulliparous women (AUC 0.71 [0.66-0.77]).

CONCLUSIONS: Novel placental biomarkers contribute significantly to predictive performance, and the model performed well on internal and external validation and outperformed the existing UK risk-assessment approach. Performance was maintained in nulliparous women, who are particularly disadvantaged by current FGR risk prediction. The model could either substantially improve detection at a similar surveillance burden or reduce surveillance referrals while maintaining improved detection; prospective implementation and health-economic evaluation will determine the optimal operating threshold.

articles.title: Effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes and their association with weight loss: a substudy of the randomised, double-masked, parallel-group, phase 3a REDEFINE 2 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, demonstrated substantial weight loss versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes in REDEFINE 2. We aimed to evaluate glycaemic outcomes in a subgroup of participants who underwent continuous glucose monitoring (CGM).

METHODS: REDEFINE 2 was a global 68-week, double-masked, parallel-group phase 3a trial that included 1206 adults from 12 countries with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes who were randomly assigned (3:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg or placebo. Participants were assigned treatment using a centralised web-based system. Participants, investigators, site staff, and the sponsor were masked to group allocation throughout the trial. A subgroup of 199 participants from 35 US sites (including university hospitals, health-care centres, research centres, and other centres) were equipped with a CGM device (Dexcom G6 Pro) for double-masked measurements from week -3 to 0, week 20 to 24, and week 64 to 68. Prespecified secondary endpoints included change in time in range (TIR; 3·9-10·0 mmol/L) and change in time in tight range (TITR; 3·9-7·8 mmol/L) for CagriSema versus placebo. REDEFINE 2 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05394519, and is completed.

FINDINGS: Between Feb 1 and Aug 11, 2023, 199 participants were enrolled in the CGM subgroup (149 in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and 50 in the placebo group) and had their CGM data analysed. The mean age of participants in the CGM subgroup was 60·4 years (SD 11·3), 106 (53%) of the 199 participants were female, 93 (47%) were male, and 160 (80%) were White. Compared with placebo, participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group had a significant increase from baseline to week 68 in mean percentage of TIR (45·9 percentage points [SE 1·2] vs 3·0 percentage points [5·7]; estimated treatment difference [ETD] 42·9 percentage points [95% CI 30·7-55·0]; p<0·0001) and mean percentage of TITR (50·4 percentage points [2·2] vs 2·8 percentage points [2·7]; ETD 47·7 percentage points [95% CI 40·7-54·7]; p<0·0001) using the trial product estimand. The overall observed mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 was -16·7% (SD 7·9) for the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and -1·8% (4·5) for the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 144 (97%) of 149 participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and in 42 (84%) of 50 participants in the placebo group, and were predominantly mild or moderate in severity.

INTERPRETATION: In this hypothesis-generating analysis, CGM-based assessments provided evidence of an effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes in people living with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the potential use of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg for improving glucose control in people living with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.

FUNDING: Novo Nordisk.

articles.title: Correction to Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2026; published online Nov 14. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2213-8587(26)00275-5.
Glycaemic outcomes with CagriSema in type 2 diabetes: relationship to weight loss.
The global hypertension care cascade in May Measurement Month 2023: a cross-sectional opportunistic blood pressure screening campaign.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Raised blood pressure is the leading contributor to global morbidity and mortality. May Measurement Month is an annual global blood pressure screening campaign aimed at raising hypertension awareness. In this study we present the results of the 2023 campaign.

METHODS: In this multinational, cross-sectional blood pressure screening survey, volunteers aged 18 years and older were opportunistically recruited using convenience sampling. Recruitment took place between May 1 and July 31, 2023, at screening sites (eg, hospitals, community centres, etc) across 70 countries. Participants completed three sitting blood pressure measurements and a questionnaire on demographic, clinical, and lifestyle information all on the day of recruitment. Raised blood pressure was defined as systolic blood pressure of 140 mm Hg or more or diastolic blood pressure of 90 mm Hg or more or both (ie, from an average of the mean of the second and third of three readings). Hypertension was defined as raised blood pressure, taking blood pressure-lowering medication, or a combination of the two. The main outcome was to describe the hypertension care cascade at the global and regional level and by sex.

FINDINGS: Of 673 304 participants screened (mean age 47·5 years [SD 17·3]; 362 116 [54·2%] were female and 306 241 [45·5%] were male), 547 584 (81·3%) were from lower-income or middle-income countries and 95 920 (14·2%) had never previously had their blood pressure measured. Of 258 802 participants with hypertension (121 168 [39·6%] were male and 135 242 [37·3%] were female), 163 295 (63·1%) were aware, 156 218 (60·4%) were being treated, 89 530 (34·6%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg, and 40 748 (15·7%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 130/80 mm Hg. Awareness, treatment, and control rates were all higher among females than males. Of 156 218 taking blood pressure-lowering medication, 89 530 (57·3%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg and 40 748 (26·1%) to lower than 130/80 mm Hg, with 67 062 (51·6%) using monotherapy. 169 272 participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension (25·1% of those surveyed; 65·4% of participants with hypertension). 128 448 (44·8%) of those with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or higher, 35 482 (68·8%) with a history of diabetes, 5041 (68·8%) with kidney failure, and 7141 (76·2%) of those with heart failure had hypertension.

INTERPRETATION: One-quarter of participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension, reflecting the high global burden and low rates of awareness. Opportunistic May Measurement Month screening provides a low-cost, scalable route to increase awareness and detection of raised blood pressure.

FUNDING: Servier, Omron, and Medtronic.

articles.title: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries: diagnostic pathways and stratified treatment.
articles.abstract: Myocardial injury with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), formerly known as myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries, challenges the long-standing assumption that myocardial infarction is synonymous with obstructive coronary artery disease. Rather than a paradox, MINOCA reflects the limitations of angiography-centred paradigms and the complexity of contemporary cardiovascular pathophysiology. Consistent with this updated definition, this Review approaches MINOCA as a working diagnosis that encompasses diverse mechanisms, including plaque disruption, coronary vasomotor dysfunction, microvascular disease, and non-coronary conditions. We propose a pragmatic, mechanism-oriented framework for selecting and sequencing complementary investigations, highlighting how intracoronary imaging, cardiac magnetic resonance, and coronary functional testing can be integrated according to the clinical scenario to refine diagnosis, while balancing diagnostic yield with procedural risk and resource availability. We discuss the implications for management, emphasising that treatment should be guided by underlying pathophysiology rather than a uniform approach derived from obstructive myocardial infarction. Emerging evidence supports the implementation of a stratified therapy to improve patient-centred outcomes. Finally, we discuss research priorities for improving mechanism-specific diagnosis and treatment, arguing that MINOCA represents both a conceptual advance and a transitional step toward a mechanism-based taxonomy of myocardial injury and infarction.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is not associated with risk of incident inflammatory bowel disease in U.S. adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Some observational studies have linked higher dietary sugar intake to increased risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), though few studies have evaluated diabetes and IBD risk. Here, we examined the relationship between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and incident IBD.

METHODS: We utilized data comprising 225 328 U.S. adults (mean baseline age 46 years) from the prospective Nurses' Health Study (1986-2020), Nurses' Health Study II (1991-2021), and Health Professionals Follow-Up Study (1986-2020). We excluded those with IBD at baseline and type 1 diabetes mellitus. We confirmed T2DM via validated questionnaires and IBD through medical record review. Using Cox proportional hazards models, we estimated hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC) according to diagnosis of T2DM, adjusting for confounders. We also examined hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and metformin use and IBD risk.

RESULTS: We documented 391 CD and 510 UC cases over 6 171 602 person-years of follow-up. T2DM was not associated with risk of CD (P = .28) or UC (P = .79). Compared with participants without T2DM, those with T2DM had an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.75 (95% CI, 0.44-1.27) for CD and 1.06 (95% CI, 0.69-1.62) for UC. In participants with available HbA1c (n = 5900), there was no association between having at least prediabetes (HbA1c  ≥5.7) and risk IBD (all P ≥ .32). Metformin use was also not associated with IBD risk (all P ≥ .15).

CONCLUSIONS: T2DM was not associated with incident CD or UC, indicating that IBD risk is not influenced by insulin resistance. Other potential mechanisms to explain the increased risk of IBD seen with dietary sugar intake should be the focus of future study.

articles.title: Restoring neuronal CD47 alleviates microglia dependent synaptic loss and memory decline in diet-induced obesity mice.
articles.abstract: Healthy synapses are protected from elimination by inhibitory "don't-eat-me" signals, but how these checkpoints fail during metabolic disease is unknown. Here, we demonstrate that diet-induced obesity triggers cognitive decline by dismantling this crucial neuroimmune safeguard. A high-fat diet rapidly induces neuronal insulin resistance in the hippocampus, suppressing neural activity and causing a selective loss of synaptic CD47, a key "don't-eat-me" molecule. This breach in the CD47-SIRPα checkpoint unleashes microglia to excessively prune synapses, causing synaptic attrition and memory impairment. While loss of CD47 accelerates this pathology, restoring its expression in hippocampal neurons provides a robust rescue, halting over-pruning and preserving cognitive function even under continuous metabolic stress. Our work elucidates a hierarchical mechanism where early metabolic dysfunction disarms a synaptic self-defense system, initiating microglia-driven neurodegeneration. We thus identify the neuronal CD47-SIRPα axis as a critical, druggable target to intercept cognitive decline in obesity and diabetes.

articles.title: Sonication improves microbiological yield in prosthetic joint infections: contributions of rapid sample processing and culture methods.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prosthetic Joint Infections (PJIs) are major arthroplasty complications associated with high morbidity and healthcare costs. Conventional culture methods have limited sensitivity, particularly in biofilm-related or antibiotic-exposed infections. The study aimed to compare the microbiological yield of sonication with conventional culture methods in PJIs and to consider rapid sample processing as a potential factor contributing to the observed culture yield.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study included 25 patients who underwent two-stage PJI revision from March 2018 to March 2020 at Manisa Celal Bayar University Hospital. Intraoperative samples ‒ including periprosthetic tissue, synovial fluid, and explanted prostheses ‒ were processed using both standard culture and sonication methods. Samples were transported and processed rapidly (within approximately one hour) to preserve microbial viability. Isolates were identified using automated systems, and antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted according to EUCAST criteria. Data were analyzed using SPSS v20.0.

RESULTS: Among 25 patients, 18 were women (72%) and 7 were men (28%) with a mean age of 69.4 ± 7.0 years; hypertension (64%) and diabetes mellitus (36%) were the most frequent comorbidities. Sonication broth cultures showed the highest overall positivity rate (96%), compared with sonication solid cultures (48%), synovial fluid cultures (50% among patients with available samples), and periprosthetic tissue cultures (40%). This high microbiological yield may be associated not only with biofilm disruption but also with rapid sample transport and processing. The most frequent pathogens were Staphylococcus epidermidis (33.3%) and Staphylococcus aureus (25%).

CONCLUSION: Sonication substantially improved microbiological yield compared with conventional culture methods. Rapid sample transport and processing may have contributed to the high microbiological yield observed in this study, although the independent effect of processing time could not be isolated.

articles.title: Assessment of artificial intelligence chatbot responses for gynecologic cancer management.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the quality and accuracy of common large language model chatbots in answering physician-level gynecologic oncology management questions.

METHODS: Three common chatbots (Microsoft CoPilot GPT 5.1, Chat GPT 5.0 Basic, and OpenEvidence 2026) were used. Twenty different gynecology oncology management questions were entered identically into each chatbot. Responses were blinded and randomly assigned and reviewed by attending physicians. They were assessed for accuracy and completeness (0 = not accurate or complete, 1 = accurate, 2 = accurate and complete). Each response was assessed for quality with the DISCERN instrument, and for understandability and actionability by patients, using the patient education materials assessment tool (PEMAT). Readability statistics were collected for each response to include: Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level Score, passive sentence percentage, and word count. Descriptive statistics and linear mixed-effects models were used to compare chatbot performance metrics.

RESULTS: OpenEvidence was the most accurate and complete (1.45), followed by ChatGPT (1.22) and CoPilot (0.98, p = 0.028). OpenEvidence had the highest DISCERN score, followed by CoPilot and ChatGPT (50.7, 41.0, 40.08, p < 0.001). ChatGPT had the highest PEMAT score, followed by CoPilot and OpenEvidence (82.2%, 81.3%, 66.5%, p < 0.001). Reading ease was highest with CoPilot (16.6, p < 0.001). OpenEvidence had the highest Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score (17.9, p < 0.001). With a one-way ANOVA comparison by question type, there was no significant difference in accuracy between the chatbot responses.

CONCLUSION: For use by gynecologic oncologists, OpenEvidence was the most accurate and complete chatbot. Further studies are needed to continue to evaluate large language models as they improve and integrate into clinical practices.

articles.title: Autologous plasma-based therapies: mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational applications.
articles.abstract: Autologous plasma-based therapies have emerged as an expanding domain within hematology, transfusion medicine, and regenerative therapeutics. These interventions, including platelet-rich plasma, platelet lysate, and plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (exosomes), leverage biologically active components of a patient's own blood to promote tissue repair and modulate inflammation. Platelets serve as reservoirs of growth factors and cytokines, while plasma-derived extracellular vesicles act as intercellular signaling mediators capable of influencing gene expression and immune responses. This review provides a comprehensive evaluation of the mechanistic rationale, clinical applications, safety profile, and regulatory considerations surrounding these autologous biologics. Evidence from randomized trials and meta-analyses supports the efficacy of platelet-rich plasma in selected musculoskeletal conditions, particularly knee osteoarthritis, while platelet lysate has demonstrated promise in ocular surface disease, wound healing, and degenerative joint disorders. Plasma-derived exosomes represent a rapidly evolving frontier, with encouraging early-phase data but a need for rigorous clinical standardization and controlled trials remain necessary. Although these therapies are generally well tolerated due to their autologous origin, heterogeneity in preparation methods and limited regulatory harmonization remain significant challenges. As the boundaries between classical transfusion practices and advanced biologic therapies continue to expand, autologous plasma-derived interventions exemplify a translational bridge between hemotherapy and regenerative medicine. Continued standardization, high-quality clinical trials, and regulatory oversight are essential to define their role within evidence-based clinical practice.

articles.title: Feature Importance Unreliability in Supervised Models for Hypertension Risk Factor Identification: An Empirical and Theoretical Critique.
Microtubule Detyrosination Contributes to Altered Nuclear Mechanotransduction and Signaling in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction and is accompanied by extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, including increased desmin, tubulin, and detyrosinated tubulin levels, which we previously showed contribute to impaired relaxation. Because microtubules connect to the nucleus via the Linker of Nucleoskeleton and Cytoskeleton complex, we investigated whether cytoskeletal remodeling alters nuclear morphology, mechanics, and hypertrophy-associated signaling. Using electron microscopy and immunofluorescence in cardiac septal tissue from patients with obstructive HCM and nonfailing donors, and immunofluorescence and live-cell imaging in septal tissue from wild-type and homozygous HCM-associated Mybpc3 c.2373InsG mice, we found that nuclei were enlarged and highly invaginated, with restricted nuclear deformation during contraction, indicating altered mechanotransduction. These changes were associated with increased Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) nuclear localization and increased expression of YAP1 target and hypertrophic genes. Inhibiting microtubule detyrosination reduced nuclear abnormalities, restored nuclear deformation, and tended to decrease YAP1 nuclear translocation, identifying nuclear mechanotransduction as a potential therapeutic target in HCM.

articles.title: Heterogeneous patterns and predictors of advance care planning engagement among intensive care nurses: A multicentre latent profile analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify distinct profiles of advance care planning (ACP) engagement among intensive care unit (ICU) nurses and examine factors associated with profile membership.

METHODS: A multicentre cross-sectional survey was conducted among ICU nurses in tertiary hospitals in China. ACP-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices were assessed using the Chinese version of the Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices regarding Advance Care Planning scale. Latent profile analysis was used to identify distinct engagement profiles, followed by multinomial logistic regression to examine factors associated with profile membership.

RESULTS: Among 955 ICU nurses, three ACP engagement profiles were identified: Low Engagement (65.9%), Knowledge Dominant but Practice-Inactive (10.7%), and Positive Attitude with Knowledge Deficit (23.5%). Compared with the Low Engagement Profile, nurses with an undergraduate education were more likely to belong to the Positive Attitude and Practice with Knowledge Deficit Profile (aOR = 1.626, 95% CI:1.008 to 2.622, P = 0.046). More frequent care of end-stage patients was associated with higher odds of membership in the Knowledge Dominant but Practice-Inactive profile (aOR = 1.831, 95% CI:1.543 to 2.172, P < 0.001), whereas general clinical experience showed no significant association with profile membership.

CONCLUSIONS: ACP engagement among ICU nurses was heterogeneous, with most nurses showing low engagement. Addressing specific knowledge deficits regarding advance directives, POLST, and surrogate decision-makers is essential. The identified profiles suggest that ACP education may need to be differentiated according to nurses specific knowledge, attitudinal, and practice needs, and that supervised clinical practice may be a potential component of future interventions.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: These profiles may potentially inform how critical care educators tailor training to specific knowledge and practice gaps. Future longitudinal or interventional studies are needed to determine whether such tailored approaches could strengthen nurses' capacity to engage patients in ACP.

articles.title: Shear-controlled separation of PET/HDPE blend wastes for high-purity PET recovery in mechanical recycling.
articles.abstract: The mechanical recycling of post-consumer mixed plastics is hindered by their unknown composition and by quality deterioration arising from the immiscibility of the constituent polymers, which form microstructure during melt processing, limiting effective fractionation. In this study, we present a shear- and composition-controlled separation strategy for poly(ethylene terephthalate)/high-density polyethylene (PET/HDPE) blends by coupling controlled melt processing with simple density-driven physical fractionation. Rheological, thermal, and microscopic analyses revealed that low-shear processing (5 s⁻1) promoted phase segregation and enhanced separation efficiency, whereas high-shear processing (115 s⁻1) generated finely dispersed morphologies that restricted density-driven fractionation. At 5 s⁻1, the 70/30 wt% PET/HDPE blend achieved 93.0% PET recovery and an overall separation efficiency of 83.7%. For the more challenging 50/50 wt% blend, a 5 min coalescence treatment increased PET recovery from 51.8% to 77.0%. At a constant shear rate, increasing the content of higher-viscosity HDPE generally reduced PET recovery, whereas shifting the composition toward higher PET ratios significantly enhanced separation efficiency through the formation of larger HDPE domains within the lower-viscosity PET matrix. In addition, an empirical predictive framework combining bulk melt rheology with DSC-derived phase purity enabled the estimation of unknown PET/HDPE compositions with an average error of 4.0%, outperforming the rheology-only and FTIR-based models. Overall, this work demonstrates that controlling shear conditions and blend composition can markedly improve the separability of melt-processed PET/HDPE blends, providing a simple and practical route for recovering polymer-rich streams from mixed plastic waste.

articles.title: Association between the cardiometabolic index and the risk of incident diabetes among elderly Chinese adults with hypertension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between baseline cardiometabolic index (CMI) and incident diabetes among older Chinese adults with hypertension.

DESIGN: Longitudinal cohort study. SITE: Xinzheng, Henan Province, China.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 19,466 adults aged ≥60 years with hypertension and without diabetes at baseline in 2018, followed through annual health examinations from 2019 to 2023.

METHODS: Cox proportional hazards regression was applied to examine the association between baseline CMI and incident diabetes, with hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) calculated. Nonlinear dose-response patterns were evaluated using restricted cubic spline (RCS) functions. Additional stratified subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were performed to determine the robustness of the observed associations.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 4.87 years, 3345 participants (17.18%) developed diabetes. Compared with the lowest CMI quartile, the highest quartile had a 48% higher adjusted diabetes hazard (HR=1.48; 95% CI: 1.34-1.64). Each standard deviation increase in CMI was associated with an 11% higher diabetes hazard (HR=1.11; 95% CI: 1.08-1.15). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a nonlinear association (P for overall association<0.001; P for nonlinearity<0.001). Findings were consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline CMI was associated with increased incident diabetes risk among older Chinese adults with hypertension. CMI may be a candidate marker for diabetes risk assessment, but external validation and comparison with established risk prediction tools are required before routine clinical use.

articles.title: [Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and personal accomplishment among family physicians in Castilla y León, Spain: a cross-sectional study].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dimensions of the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey for Medical Personnel (MBI-HSS [MP]), their historical categories, and sociodemographic and occupational associations among family physicians in Castilla y León, Spain.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study using a web-based survey.

SETTING: Primary care in the public health system of Castilla y León, Spain.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 422 family physicians recruited through convenience and snowball sampling between April and July 2026.

MAIN MEASUREMENTS: Continuous MBI-HSS (MP) scores were the primary outcomes; historical categories were secondary non-diagnostic descriptions. We estimated descriptive statistics, internal consistency, and linear regressions with heteroskedasticity-consistent type 3 (HC3) standard errors and Benjamini-Hochberg correction.

RESULTS: Mean scores were 29.81 (95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 28.45-31.16) for emotional exhaustion, 9.03 (95% CI: 8.36-9.70) for depersonalization, and 35.23 (95% CI: 34.47-35.99) for personal accomplishment. Adverse categories were 57.1% for high emotional exhaustion, 38.6% for high depersonalization, and 37.9% for low personal accomplishment. Cronbach's alpha ranged from 0.806 to 0.943. Men had lower emotional exhaustion than women (β=-4.66; q=0.044); participants aged ≥60 years had lower emotional exhaustion (β=-6.96; q=0.044) and depersonalization (β=-3.63; q=0.022) than those aged<40 years.

CONCLUSIONS: High emotional exhaustion and relevant proportions of high depersonalization and low personal accomplishment were observed. Sex, age, or experience were associated with selected dimensions, whereas occupational signals were less robust. The findings support multidimensional assessment without inferring causality or regional prevalence.

articles.title: Impact of preoperative GLP-1 agonist use on patient-reported outcomes in obese patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty: a propensity score match analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity has traditionally been associated with increased perioperative risk in patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), originally developed for diabetes management, have recently emerged as an effective strategy for weight loss. Although recent literature has suggested that GLP-1 RA use may reduce postoperative complications following TKA, their impact on patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) remains unclear.

METHODS: A retrospective review of an institutional database identified 11,025 consecutive patients who underwent primary TKA. After exclusion, a 1:3 propensity score-matched analysis was performed to balance baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, yielding 146 obese patients who used preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonists and 438 matched non-users. Evaluated PROMs included SF-10a, PROMIS Global Mental and Physical, and KOOS-PS. Clinically meaningful improvement was assessed using the Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID). Secondary outcomes included 90-day and one- and two-year complications.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences between GLP-1 RA users and non-users in preoperative or postoperative PROM scores, delta scores, or the proportion of patients achieving MCID improvement across SF-10a, PROMIS Global Mental, PROMIS Global Physical, or KOOS-PS (P > 0.05 for all). Rates of 90-day medical complications, including pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, and surgical site infection, were similar between groups (P > 0.05 for all). Additionally, there were no differences in one- or two-year surgical complications, including periprosthetic joint infection, revision TKA, dislocation, loosening, or periprosthetic fracture (P > 0.05 for all).

CONCLUSION: Among obese patients undergoing TKA, preoperative GLP-1 RA use was not associated with differences in patient-reported outcomes or complication rates at short- to mid-term follow-up. These findings suggest that GLP-1 RA therapy alone does not yield clinically meaningful improvements in postoperative functional recovery.

articles.title: From Stroke Prevention to Occupational Safety: Antiplatelet Withdrawal After PFO Closure in Professional Divers.
Associations of Physical Activity With Aortic Structure and Hemodynamics in the UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intense physical training is associated with cardiac remodeling, but the relationship between habitual exercise and aortic phenotypes in the general population remains poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated associations between physical activity and aortic size and function in a large population-based cohort.

METHODS: We analyzed 13,289 UK Biobank participants without hypertension who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance and wrist accelerometry. Ascending and descending aortic area, diameter, and distensibility were modeled against device-measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), mean acceleration, and self-reported MVPA. Sex-stratified generalized linear models were adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, medications, laboratory values, vitals, and accelerometer wear. Stroke volume index and systolic blood pressure were evaluated as candidate mediators.

RESULTS: Higher MVPA was associated with larger ascending and descending aortic dimensions in both sexes (P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each additional 60 minutes per day corresponded to 0.37 mm (95% CI: 0.25-0.49) and 0.39 mm (95% CI: 0.25-0.53) larger ascending aortic diameter in women and men, respectively, and 0.28 mm larger descending aortic diameter in both women and men. Distensibility was preserved across all segments. Higher mean acceleration and self-reported MVPA were associated with greater aortic distensibility in men. Stroke volume index accounted for 42% to 60% of the MVPA-aortic area association. Systolic blood pressure was not a mediator.

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults without hypertension, MVPA was associated with larger aortic dimensions without impaired distensibility, partially mediated by greater stroke volume. These associations suggest physical activity-related aortic dilation may be distinct from vasculopathy-driven aortic enlargement. Longitudinal prospective studies incorporating exercise data are warranted to validate these findings.

articles.title: Multimodal Approach for Predicting Outcome After Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source.
Reply: From Stroke Prevention to Occupational Safety: Antiplatelet Withdrawal After PFO Closure in Professional Divers.
Accuracy of a 3-Lead Smartwatch Electrocardiogram for Detecting Ischemic Electrocardiographic Changes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely diagnosis of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is critical, but delays in obtaining an electrocardiogram (ECG) remain a challenge. Smartwatches may enable rapid, out-of-hospital assessment.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine the diagnostic accuracy of a simplified 3-lead smartwatch ECG (I, III, and V2) for detecting ischemic ECG changes, using the standard 12-lead ECG as the reference standard.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter study, patients with suspected ACS underwent both a standard 12-lead ECG (reference standard) and a 3-lead (I, III, and V2) smartwatch ECG. The primary endpoint was diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of the smartwatch ECG for detecting ischemic ECG changes by fully blinded interpretation. Key secondary endpoints included accuracy by ACS subtype, intermethod agreement, and quantitative ST-segment correlation.

RESULTS: A total of 309 participants were enrolled (120 ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI], 120 non-STEMI, and 69 controls). The smartwatch ECG showed a sensitivity of 93.2% (95% CI: 89.2%-96.0%) and specificity of 95.9% (95% CI: 88.5%-99.1%) for ischemic ECG changes vs the reference 12-lead ECG (κ = 0.84). Performance was high for both STEMI (sensitivity, 88.9%) and non-STEMI (sensitivity, 97.4%; enriched by inclusion criteria requiring overt ischemic ECG changes). The intraclass correlation coefficient for ST-segment elevation was 0.851 (95% CI: 0.777-0.900).

CONCLUSIONS: A simplified 3-lead smartwatch ECG provides reliable, quantitatively accurate data for identifying ischemic ECG changes. This technology may empower patients to seek care sooner, addressing patient-related delay, the dominant component of total ischemic time.

articles.title: Characterizing sarcopenic obesity in Spanish older adults: an ESPEN-EASO consensus-based approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism and the European Association for the Study of Obesity (ESPEN-EASO) consensus provides diagnostic criteria for sarcopenic obesity. Although sarcopenia is common in older adults, the prevalence and characteristics of sarcopenic obesity remain insufficiently described. This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of sarcopenic obesity in older adults and its distribution by age, sex, and living setting, as well as to examine the impact of sarcopenic obesity, sarcopenia, and obesity on functional, cognitive, emotional, and quality-of-life variables.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted. A total of 300 older adults living in the community (n = 168) or residents in long-term care facilities (n = 132) were recruited using a convenience sampling approach. To define those with sarcopenic obesity, sarcopenia, obesity or no condition, the assessments included anthropometric, physical, functional and clinical measurements.

RESULTS: 73.6% of the sample screened positively for sarcopenic obesity, and 22.3% were diagnosed with sarcopenic obesity. The highest percentage of sarcopenic obesity was found in older adults aged ≥85 group (48.4% of them), women (28% of them), and older adults living in long-term care facilities (40.9% of them). A total of 158 older adults (52.7%) had one of the three conditions or a concomitant situation, and 16% had all the three conditions. The group with only sarcopenic obesity had a lower gait speed and cognitive status than those with only obesity (p < 0.001 for both), but a higher gait speed than those with only sarcopenia (p < 0.001). These results should be interpretated with caution due to the single-province recruitment.

CONCLUSION: Nearly a quarter of our sample was affected by sarcopenic obesity, with most being older adults ≥85 years old, women, and lived in long-term care facilities. Sarcopenic obesity tends to be concomitant with either sarcopenia or obesity. Sarcopenia is the condition that mostly affects gait speed, followed by sarcopenic obesity. Future studies should incorporate more comprehensive muscle measures including neuromuscular function, muscle fat infiltration, and alternative body composition indices to improve diagnostic precision and enhance the understanding of sarcopenic obesity.

articles.title: Analysis of trends in economic costs, average weights and length of stay for vascular surgery in Spain: Results of the Spanish national registry over an 8-year period (2016-2023) and future plan.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This research aims to help policymakers and healthcare providers estimate the expected long-term costs of treating chronic vascular diseases.

OBJECTIVE: To identify trends in the costs, average lengths of stay, and average hospital stays for Angiology, Vascular, and Endovascular Surgery (AVES) services in Spain.

METHODS: A population-based longitudinal study analyzing annual data on contacts, costs (APR-DRG), average lengths of stay, and average hospital weights for AVES services between 2016 and 2023, published by the Spanish Registry of Specialized Care-Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD). Age- and sex-adjusted annual linear trends were estimated using linear regression models.

RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2023, the average cost of AVES increased from €4200.44 to €5217.79. An age- and sex-adjusted annual increase of €170.95 was estimated (p<0.001; 95% CI: 115.01-226.89). The mean cost was €2271.30 lower in women (p<0.001) and €2588.40 higher in patients over 65 years of age (p<0.001). By diagnosis, significant increases were observed in most groups, except for chronic arterial ischemia, pelvic varices, and superficial venous thrombosis. A notable increase of €929.65/year was seen in aortic aneurysms and dissections. The mean length of stay (8.87 days) increased by 0.14 days/year (p=0.036), being shorter in women and longer in patients ≥65 years of age. The mean weight remained stable.

CONCLUSIONS: AVES costs are steadily increasing, particularly for aortic aneurysms and dissections. Weight and contacts remain stable, with a slight increase in average length of stay. This increase could be related to greater complexity of care.

articles.title: Perceptions of pediatric intensive care unit professionals regarding palliative and end-of-life care.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Supporting children/families with life-limiting illnesses is a common reality in paediatric intensive care units (PICU). This approach requires a high level of competence in decision-making and care planning. The coexistence of intensive care and palliative and end-of-life care and the capacity of the teams managing it needs to be explored to identify areas for improvement.

OBJECTIVE: To explore healthcare professionals' perceptions of their experience of supporting children and families from a palliative and end-of-life care perspective in a PICU.

METHODOLOGY: A qualitative study was conducted in a PICU at a high-complexity hospital (first reflective cycle of a participatory action research study). The population consisted of all healthcare professionals in the unit. Purposive sampling was carried out, seeking maximum heterogeneity in relation to experiential variables. Three discussion groups were held (average duration 115min). Thirty-seven professionals participated (55% nurses, 24% paediatricians and 21% nursing assistants). A thematic analysis of the discourse was carried out.

RESULTS: The experience of working with critically ill children was described as difficult but emotionally and intellectually rewarding. The professionals referred to death as taboo and expressed the need to normalise it and reconceptualise the process of dying. They considered that the experience of accompanying the patient depends on each case, as 'not all deaths are the same'. They felt that the palliative care approach almost always 'comes too late'. In their discourse, they identified strengths and weaknesses as a team, as well as organisational and structural opportunities and barriers that condition the approach to palliative care and end-of-life care for children and families.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: The experience of caring for a critically ill child and their family is complex. Conducting a reflective analysis of the situation from the perspective of the professionals themselves allows for the development of strategies to improve the palliative and end-of-life approach that guarantee excellent care.

articles.title: Analysis of patient safety culture in an intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Studying the characteristics and level of development of a healthcare organization's safety culture is a necessary management strategy and constitutes the starting point for understanding and subsequently transforming it. Our main objective was to evaluate the patient safety culture in the intensive care unit of our hospital and identify existing strengths and weaknesses in order to detect potential areas for improvement and implement the necessary strategies.

METHOD: Descriptive, cross-sectional observational study. Sociodemographic and occupational variables were collected along with the validated and Spanish-translated Hospital Patient Safety Survey. The survey consists of 12 dimensions, with 3 groups of questions, rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Responses were classified as positive, neutral, or negative. Student's t-test, chi-square test, and ANOVA were used for bivariate analysis, with P < .05.

RESULTS: Sixty-five questionnaires were obtained (98.48% response rate). The mean score for the safety culture perceived by nursing professionals was 7.62 ± 1.44. Fourteen professionals (21.4%) reported an adverse event in the last year, and 46 (70.8%) had recently received patient safety training. The dimensions with the highest scores were "Organizational Learning/Continuous Improvement'' and ``Teamwork in the Unit/Service", with 67.2 and 71.9 points, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Nursing professionals perceive a positive safety culture in the intensive care unit, with particular strength in the areas of organisational learning/continuous improvement and teamwork. Furthermore, a higher perception of patient safety and a higher rate of adverse event reporting than previously documented have been observed.

articles.title: Spectral analysis of dynamic long-axial-field-of-view PET studies: a flexible framework for whole-body multi-organ kinetic quantification.
articles.abstract: Although long-axial-field-of-view (LAFOV) PET systems are increasingly installed worldwide, quantitative analysis of dynamic LAFOV PET remains largely based on compartmental models or graphical methods. This study systematically evaluates and adapts spectral analysis (SA) as a flexible, data-driven framework for multi-organ kinetic quantification. Approach.SA represents the tissue impulse response function as a non-negative combination of exponential components without requiring a predefined compartmental structure. Four implementations were investigated: standard SA, SA with tracer arrival delay correction (SA*), spectral analysis with iterative filter (SAIF), and SAIF with delay correction (SAIF*). The methods were evaluated at both volume of interest (VOI) and voxel levels using dynamic 18F-FDG PET/CT data from 24 cancer patients, including 40 tumor lesions. Main results. Delay correction improved early-phase time activity curve (TAC) fitting and reduced Akaike information criterion (AIC) values across most organs. SA* achieved comparable or better fitting performance than two-tissue compartmental model with delay correction (2C*) in several regions without requiring a predefined compartmental structure. Kinetic parameter estimates showed the highest consistency for Ki, while K1, VT, and vascular contributions exhibited greater method-dependent variability. The resulting spectra revealed distinct kinetic patterns across normal organs and individual tumors. At the voxel level, SA* generated acceptable parametric images without iterative filtering, while SAIF* provided additional signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvements, particularly in some tumor regions.Significance. This first systematic evaluation demonstrates the potential of SA for multi-organ kinetic quantification with dynamic LAFOV PET. Its flexible kinetic representation may be particularly valuable for investigating novel diagnostic and theranostic radiotracers whose whole-body kinetic behavior is not yet fully characterized.

articles.title: Triglyceride-glucose combined with obesity indices and cardiovascular disease risk in cancer survivors: A UK Biobank cohort study with threshold identification.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors face elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, yet practical markers for identifying high-risk survivors are limited. The triglyceride‑glucose (TyG) index and its derivatives combining TyG with body mass index (TyG-BMI), waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), or waist circumference (TyG-WC) have been validated in general populations, but their comparative performance and threshold effects in cancer survivors remain unexplored. We evaluated all four indices for incident CVD, coronary artery disease (CAD), stroke, and atrial fibrillation (AF), and identified risk thresholds.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 24,763 cancer survivors from the UK Biobank without pre‑existing CVD. All four indices were calculated at baseline. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CVD as a composite of CAD, stroke, and AF, and for each component separately. Restricted cubic splines characterized nonlinear dose‑response relationships and threshold effects. Subgroup analyses were performed by cancer type and lifestyle factors.

RESULTS: During a median 15.9‑year follow‑up, 4590 CVD events occurred. Per‑standard deviation increases in TyG, TyG‑BMI, TyG‑WHtR, and TyG‑WC were associated with 6% (HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09), 14% (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.17), 14% (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.10-1.18), and 16% (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.12-1.20) higher CVD risk, respectively. Associations with CAD were similar (per-SD HRs 1.14-1.21), with none for stroke. TyG‑BMI and TyG-WHtR showed nonlinear associations with CVD, with risk accelerating beyond inflection points of 261.54 and 5.59, respectively. Associations were strongest in breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers, whereas no association was observed in hematologic malignancies. For AF, the three obesity-combined indices were positively associated, whereas TyG alone exhibited a J‑shaped relationship.

CONCLUSIONS: The obesity-combined indices, particularly those incorporating BMI and waist-to-height ratio, are independently associated with higher CVD and CAD risk. Thresholds of TyG‑BMI > 261.54 and TyG‑WHtR > 5.59 may help identify high‑risk survivors.

articles.title: Sex-specific mechanisms in pulmonary arterial hypertension: Integrating evidence from rodent models, genetics, and hormonal biology.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a disease of the pulmonary vasculature leading to increased vascular resistance and right ventricular failure. Despite advances in understanding of its pathomechanism, the influence of sex on the development of PAH remains incompletely understood. Thus, this review aimed to summarise the current understanding of the mechanisms underlying PAH in women and men and to identify sex-related mechanisms influencing this disease, considering the available evidence from experimental models. Available studies suggest that the protective effect observed in females (in experimental models) is likely linked to the action of estrogens. Estrogen metabolism, particularly changes in the relative proportions of its metabolites, may contribute to sex-related differences, although it is unlikely to explain them fully. A shift in estrogen metabolism has been observed towards metabolites with potent mitogenic and remodeling effects (16α-hydroxyestrone) at the expense of protective metabolites (such as 2-methoxyestradiol). Furthermore, genetic factors may shape the sex differences observed in PAH development. In addition to the well-documented influence of mutations in the bone morphogenetic protein receptor type 2 gene, which may partly explain the differing severity of the disease in males and females, attention is also being drawn to other molecular pathways associated, among other things, with the activity of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 and B-cell lymphoma transcription factors and disturbances in estrogen receptor alpha-dependent signaling. The data presented confirm the existence of sex dimorphism in PAH and point to the potential for personalized treatment strategies.

articles.title: Microglial progranulin suppresses post-ischemic tauopathy through lysosomal regulation.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major long-term consequence of ischemic stroke. Although microglial dysfunction has been implicated in chronic neurodegeneration, the mechanisms linking microglia to post-ischemic tau pathology remain unknown. We investigated whether microglial progranulin-dependent lysosomal pathways regulate post-ischemic tau homeostasis and cognitive decline. We used rat and progranulin (Grn)-knockout mouse models of middle cerebral artery occlusion with reperfusion. Phosphorylated tau accumulation was assessed. Microglia were depleted using the colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor inhibitor PLX3397. Proteomic analyses were performed. Recombinant progranulin was administered intravenously in blinded validation experiments. Ischemic stroke induced progressive accumulation of phosphorylated tau in both neurons and microglia, whereas β-amyloid deposition was not detected. Tau burden correlated with cognitive impairment, and exogenous tau exacerbated both tau accumulation and cognitive decline. Only pre-ischemic microglial depletion accelerated tau accumulation (P = 0.041) and cognitive decline (P = 0.020), whereas delayed depletion had no effect, indicating a temporally restricted protective role of microglia. Proteomic analyses identified progranulin as a prominently downregulated protein following microglial depletion. Progranulin deficiency increased tau accumulation and reduced lysosomal marker expression, whereas recombinant progranulin reduced tau levels and improved cognitive function (P < 0.001 and P < 0.05, respectively). In conclusion, microglia exert a temporally restricted protective role by maintaining post-ischemic tau homeostasis through progranulin-dependent lysosomal function. These findings identify the microglial progranulin-lysosomal pathway as a potential therapeutic target for PSCI.

articles.title: Building a Career in Hemostasis and Thrombosis.
Activation of platelets by thrombopoietin triggers fatal thrombosis in mouse models of myeloproliferative neoplasms.
articles.abstract: Thrombosis is a frequent complication in patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) and is responsible for high morbidity and mortality. The driver gene mutations that cause MPN are associated with increased risk of thrombosis, but the mechanisms how they mediate a pro-thrombotic state are not completely understood. Previous studies on MPN mouse models expressing JAK2-V617F have reported an elevated risk of both thrombosis and bleeding. Here we report on the unexpected finding that mouse models of MPN with thrombocytosis expressing JAK2-V617F or CALRdel52 suffered fatal disseminated thrombosis upon injection with thrombopoietin (TPO). Mice with platelet counts >4x1012/L died within 5-20 minutes after TPO injection and exhibited severe lung thrombosis, whereas the majority of mice with platelets <4x1012/L survived and exhibited a lower degree of lung thrombosis. Platelet factor 4 (PF4) concentration in plasma of JAK2-V617F mutant mice increased after TPO injection, consistent with PF4 release from alpha granules during platelet activation. Pretreatment of JAK2-V617F mice with the anti-aggregating agents aspirin and clopidogrel strongly reduced the number of lung thrombi and prevented lethality after TPO injection, indicating that platelets play a central role in this process. Pretreatment of JAK2-V617F mice with the JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib or with the MEK inhibitor trametinib significantly reduced the number of lung thrombi after TPO injection, but had only minor effect on survival. Although TPO-receptor agonists are not used in the treatment of MPN, our findings suggest that elevated TPO levels, e.g. occurring during acute infection or inflammation, may contribute to the pathophysiology of thrombosis in MPN.

articles.title: Adipocyte endothelin B receptor knockout improves dyslipidemia in high fat diet fed obese mice.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: Obesity is characterized by impaired adipose tissue lipid metabolism and elevated endothelin-1 (ET-1). We have shown that ET-1 promotes adipocyte dysfunction via the ETB receptor. However, the mechanisms by which ETB signaling regulates lipid metabolism remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that adipocyte ETB receptor activation causes dyslipidemia in diet induced obese mice. Therefore, adipocyte-specific ETB receptor knockout (adETBKO) and ETB receptor overexpression (adETBOX) mice and littermate controls were fed normal (NMD) or high-fat diet (HFD) for 10 weeks. HFD induced marked dyslipidemia in control mice with increased plasma cholesterol, LDL, NEFA, triglycerides and reduced HDL. Increased cholesterol, LDL, and NEFA were attenuated in adETBKO mice whereas adETBOX did not significantly alter these parameters. Further,we found HFD suppressed Fasn expression and upregulated Plin2 in both visceral and subcutaneous adipose, whereas suppression of Lpl expression was observed in visceral adipose. Changes in lipid metabolism genes were attenuated in adETBKO mice. Consistent with this, RNA-seq analysis demonstrated significant differences in genes for lipid oxidation pathways in visceral adipose tissue of HFD-fed controls vs. NMD which was attenuated in adETBKO mice. Collectively, these data identify adipocyte ETB signaling as a key regulator of visceral adipose lipid handling and a contributor to obesity-associated dyslipidemia.

articles.title: TSG-01 in the treatment of chronic heart failure in patients with coronary artery disease: A prospective clinical phase IIa trial.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of physiology and pharmacology
articles.abstract: TSG-01, a novel agent dominated by secondary ginsenosides, may benefit chronic heart failure (CHF), yet its efficacy and safety in CHF patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) remain unclear. This phase IIa trial enrolled 85 CAD patients with NYHA III CHF (40-75 years), randomized to high-dose TSG-01 (n=29), low-dose TSG-01 (n=28), or placebo (n=28) for 12 weeks. Outcomes were evaluated in the intention-to-treat cohort (ITT, n=85) and an exploratory digoxin-free cohort (n=59). No significant between-group difference was found for the NYHA-based efficacy endpoint. In the ITT cohort, only low-dose TSG-01 significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) versus placebo; in the digoxin-free cohort, both doses yielded significant LVEF improvement. Diseases occurring the infectious and infective system, gastrointestinal system and the blood and lymphatic system are the common adverse events, with no significant difference between the 3 groups. Together, this study demonstrates that TSG-01 is well tolerated with similar adverse event profiles across groups, and confers potential cardiac benefits in digoxin-free patients, warranting further confirmatory studies. Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov, no. NCT04515290.

articles.title: Efficacy of Bovine Lactoferrin in Chronic Hepatitis C: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Biochemistry and cell biology = Biochimie et biologie cellulaire
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Bovine lactoferrin (bLF), a glycoprotein with antiviral and immunomodulatory properties, has been investigated as a potential therapeutic agent. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of bLF on virologic and biochemical outcomes in patients with chronic HCV infection. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through November 5, 2024 (CRD42024621752). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing bLF with placebo or no treatment. Pooled analyses used a random-effects inverse-variance model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², with exploratory subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Five randomized controlled trials were included, four contributing to quantitative analyses. No statistically significant differences were observed for virologic response (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.74-1.36; I² = 31%), biochemical response (RR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.71-1.53; I² = 0%), or sustained virologic response (RR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.63-1.76; I² = 0%). Subgroup analyses and meta-regression identified no significant sources of heterogeneity. The available randomized evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit of bLF on virologic or biochemical responses. Further studies using contemporary treatment strategies and mechanistic endpoints are warranted.

articles.title: Cognitive and Mood Symptoms Associated with Unemployment in Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether subjective and objective cognitive function, mood, and fatigue are associated with unemployment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC).

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 66 individuals with PASC (meanage=46.35) completed self-report measures of fatigue, depression, anxiety, and subjective cognitive decline, and neuropsychological testing. Participants had COVID-19 ≥ 2 months prior, brain fog, at least two other persistent symptoms with no major or unstable neurological or psychiatric disorder, and were not hospitalized during infection. Analysis of covariance was conducted, controlling for demographics, mood, and fatigue.

RESULTS: Unemployed participants (29%) reported greater perceived executive dysfunction since COVID-19 and exhibited poorer performance on measures of immediate memory and working memory compared to employed participants.

CONCLUSIONS: Unemployed individuals with PASC demonstrate greater cognitive difficulties, highlighting the need for optimized symptom management in this population.

articles.title: Applying Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing to Quantify the Cost of Rescue Transesophageal Echocardiography: An Emergency Diagnostic Service.
Interaction-Rich Odorant Receptor Neighborhoods and Olfaction-Dependent Subsocial Behavior in a Parasitoid Wasp.
articles.abstract: Insect social behaviors are closely linked to olfaction; yet the genomic mechanisms shaping chemoreceptor expansion and behavior remain poorly understood. The subsocial ectoparasitoid wasp Sclerodermus guani relies on olfaction to coordinate host-seeking, reproduction, and maternal care, providing a tractable system to investigate these relationships. Here, we present a chromosome-level genome assembly for S. guani and integrate chromatin conformation, transcriptomics, electrophysiology, and functional genetics to examine the organization and behavioral significance of odorant receptors (ORs). We identify 148 ORs marked by tandem expansion and sex-biased antennal expression. These ORs preferentially occupy interaction-rich topologically associating domains characterized by elevated interaction frequency, identifying a distinctive higher-order genomic context for this expanded sensory receptor family. To functionally characterize this structurally organized receptor family, we generated a heritable null mutation in the OR co-receptor (Orco). Orco mutants displayed severe impairments in host-seeking, mating, oviposition, and maternal care. Strikingly, mutants frequently laid eggs on conspecific larvae, indicating a loss of kin recognition and raising the possibility that OR-mediated olfaction contributes to parasitism and maternal care in this lineage. Together, these findings suggest that genome architecture may bias chemosensory gene diversification and that OR signaling is necessary for coordinated subsocial behavior in S. guani.

articles.title: A Swarm-Intelligent Dual-Layer Differential Privacy Framework for Reliable Distributed Learning.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural networks and learning systems
articles.abstract: Data privacy protection is a critical challenge in distributed machine learning. Differential privacy (DP) provides provable privacy guarantees for models by injecting strictly controlled noise. However, existing solutions either merely apply noise perturbation to the data or model at the individual level, failing to defend against population-level inference based on statistical analysis. Alternatively, they focus exclusively on protecting single high-order statistics, which neither covers other key distribution characteristics nor avoids disrupting the inherent data structure. Inspired by the dual-layer collaborative decision-making of scout bees in the hive selection behavior of the bee colony, we propose a bionic dual-layer protection framework, which is a Hive-like bionic system that provides a protective Guard for the support vector machine (SVM), named HiveGuard-SVM. Such a framework abstracts data distribution at the population level while implementing noise protection at the individual level, preventing attackers from inferring the data distribution or reverse-engineering original data from local parameters. Theoretical analysis shows that the framework satisfies strict $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ -DP while maintaining the model generalization performance. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets demonstrate that HiveGuard-SVM outperforms several existing state-of-the-art methods.

articles.title: Evaluation of the ACS Trauma Quality Improvement Program benchmark for intracranial pressure monitoring across trauma centers.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI), intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring detects and directs management for intracranial hypertension. ICP monitoring is recommended for sTBI patients and is included as a benchmarked quality metric by the American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Programs (ACS-TQIP), which reports annual ICP monitor usage across all participating trauma centers. We evaluated whether greater institutional ICP utilization was associated with lower center-level mortality.

METHODS: For this retrospective observational study, adult patients aged 18 years and older meeting the ACS-TQIP definition of sTBI admitted to Level I or II trauma centers from 2013 to 2023 were identified. Patient data were aggregated by trauma center and calendar year to mirror the ACS-TQIP benchmarking framework. Annual institutional ICP monitor utilization and in-hospital mortality rates were calculated for each center-year combination. Multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models evaluated whether centers with higher ICP monitor utilization had lower mortality after adjusting for patient demographics, injury severity, neurological status, operative intervention, injury mechanism, and hospital length of stay.

RESULTS: Among 191,686 sTBI patients, 29,224 (15.2%) underwent ICP monitoring. ICP monitor utilization ranged from 11% to 21% during the study period with a notable increase in 2017, whereas overall mortality remained largely unchanged. Year-specific analyses demonstrated a protective association between greater ICP monitor utilization and mortality in 2015 and an association with increased mortality in 2023. After adjustment for differences in patient and institutional characteristics, higher institutional ICP monitor utilization was not associated with lower center-level mortality (odds ratio=0.99, 95% CI=0.97-1.00; P=0.128).

CONCLUSIONS: Using over a decade of TQIP data, greater institutional ICP monitor utilization was not associated with lower mortality across ACS-TQIP centers. These findings suggest that greater institutional adoption of ICP monitoring alone may not improve center-level outcomes and support periodic reassessment of ICP monitoring as a benchmarked ACS-TQIP quality metric.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, prognostic & epidemiological.
