articles.title: Reduced microbial touch transmission by engineering the microtopography of medical glove surfaces.
articles.abstract: Touch transmission of pathogens is a major contributor to the spread of infectious disease within hospitals as health care workers interact with patients and the environment. Reducing microbial transmission by touch contact can reduce rates of health care-associated infections. We modified commercial medical gloves with superhydrophobic (Cassie-Baxter) microtopographies to test rates of microbial attachment and transmission through touch contact with contaminated fomite surfaces. Molded post and groove topographies with critical dimensions between 2.5 and 15 micrometers were evaluated through compressive touch experiments with six clinically relevant microbial species (Candida albicans, Enterococcus faecium, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus epidermidis). After compressive contact (1- to 9-newton force), results showed an average reduction of 1.65 log (97.8%) in cells transferred to post or straight-walled groove-modified gloves compared with unmodified gloves, for all species (P < 0.0001). For sequential touch transmission to multiple surfaces, there was a 1.8 to 2.0 log (98.4 to 99%) reduction in S. aureus and K. pneumoniae transferred to modified gloves compared with controls. Transfer efficiencies fell from 43.6 ± 12.2% to 1.79 ± 0.70% (P10) and 1.75 ± 0.48% (SW15) for S. aureus (P < 0.001), with comparable reductions for K. pneumoniae. Touch transmission from dry biofilms and hospital bedrail surfaces was similarly reduced. The mechanisms underlying this nonspecific microbial repellency were reduction in physical transfer of contaminated fluids and limited surface area for microbial attachment. These reductions in microbial attachment and transfer for topography-modified gloves may contribute to reducing pathogen transmission within hospitals.

articles.title: Elevated G-CSF concentrations promote both neutrophilic and type 2 inflammation to drive lung pathology during asthma exacerbations.
articles.abstract: Acute exacerbations of asthma, frequently triggered by respiratory viral infection, account for a substantial proportion of asthma-related morbidity, mortality, and health care expenditure. It is anticipated that augmented type 2 and neutrophilic inflammatory responses coordinate to drive lung pathology, but the mechanisms underlying virus-induced exacerbations remain poorly defined. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) is classically recognized for its capacity to potentiate neutrophilic responses, although evidence suggests that it can also enhance type 2 inflammation in specific settings. We hypothesized that virus-induced elevation in pulmonary G-CSF could enhance both neutrophilic and type 2 immune responses and associated pathologies during asthma exacerbations. In a human experimental rhinovirus (RV) infection model, we demonstrated that virus challenge specifically increased airway G-CSF levels in patients with asthma but not healthy individuals. Elevated G-CSF correlated with heightened neutrophilic and type 2 inflammation and with adverse clinical outcomes. In addition, increased G-CSF concentrations were associated with heightened airway virus titers and greater upstream induction of the IL-1β/IL-23-IL-17A axis. These findings were recapitulated in a mouse ovalbumin (OVA)-RV model of asthma exacerbation. Subsequent targeting of G-CSF at the time of virus challenge in OVA-RV mice reduced both neutrophilic and type 2 inflammation, lung damage, epithelial remodeling, and airway hyperresponsiveness. Reciprocal administration of recombinant G-CSF, in place of RV, to OVA-treated mice was sufficient to augment neutrophilic and type 2 inflammation. These studies provide mechanistic insight into the inflammatory pathways underlying acute asthma exacerbations and highlight G-CSF as a potential therapeutic target to ameliorate pathology in this setting.

articles.title: Biological augmentation of electronic health records through estimation of patient proteomes.
articles.abstract: High-dimensional proteomic profiling can improve clinical risk prediction and provide insight into disease biology, but routine acquisition of omic data at population scale remains impractical. We developed Real-world AI-based Biomarker Inference Technology (RABIT), a machine learning framework that biologically augments electronic health records (EHRs) by projecting longitudinal clinical histories into a high-dimensional proteomic representation space learned from paired EHR and plasma proteomics. RABIT was trained using patients with paired EHRs and measured plasma proteomics and externally validated in an independent cohort with paired data. RABIT profiles showed broad concordance with measured protein expression and more closely resembled measured proteomics than their input EHR. Incorporating these biologically augmented representations improved 5-year disease onset prediction across 14 conditions (n = 449,223; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 33.7%) and generalized to an external cohort (n = 1,038,419; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 70.3%). RABIT profiles reproduced clinically meaningful organ-specific biological changes in response to aging and further outperformed models built from comprehensive established clinical predictors in prediction of chronic kidney disease progression, major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Last, RABIT enabled biological signatures derived from small discovery cohorts to be extended to population-scale clinical datasets, generating clinically relevant hypotheses linking cytomegalovirus-associated immune states to variation in brain tumor outcomes. Together, these results demonstrate that biological augmentation of EHRs can enable molecularly informed clinical prediction and hypothesis generation at population scale.

articles.title: MnCO3-Ag Heterojunction Sonosensitizer for Enhanced Sonodynamic Therapy and Silver Ion Release against Implant-Associated Bacterial Infection.
articles.abstract: Implant-associated infections caused by biofilm-forming pathogens remain a major clinical challenge. Sonodynamic therapy (SDT) represents a promising non-antibiotic antibacterial strategy. However, its therapeutic efficacy is often limited by the low reactive oxygen species (ROS) yield and poor biodegradability of the sonosensitizers. Herein, we developed MnCO3-Ag nanoparticles (Mn-Ag NPs) as a biodegradable Schottky heterojunction sonosensitizer for the treatment of implant infections associated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). The Mn-Ag heterointerface promotes charge separation under ultrasound (US) irradiation and enables efficient generation of multiple ROS. Meanwhile, ROS generated under US irradiation promotes the oxidative release of Ag+ from the Ag phase, enabling a cascade sonodynamic/ion-release antibacterial mechanism that couples ROS-mediated damage with Ag+-mediated bactericidal activity. In vitro antibacterial experiments showed that Mn-Ag NPs reduced the number of viable MRSA by 2.5 log (99.7%) in 96-well plates. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Mn-Ag NPs under US induced oxidative stress in MRSA and disrupted biosynthesis, DNA-binding processes, and metabolic regulation. In a murine implant-associated infection model, Mn-Ag NPs reduced viable MRSA by 2.6 log (99.7%) under US irradiation, alleviated tissue inflammation, and promoted tissue recovery. In addition, Mn-Ag NPs gradually degraded in the acidic infected microenvironment. This work highlights a biodegradable Schottky heterojunction strategy for enhancing charge separation and ROS generation, thereby enabling synergistic sonodynamic/Ag+-mediated antibacterial therapy against biofilm infections.

articles.title: When Does Fluid Intake Become a Meaningful Exposure in Heart Failure? Lessons from FRESH-UP.
The Sec61-EMC complex promotes biosynthesis of the SARS-CoV-2 non-structural proteins.
articles.abstract: The genomic RNA of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the global COVID-19 pandemic, encodes polyproteins pp1a and pp1ab which contain 16 non-structural proteins (NSPs) that support critical steps in infection. Despite this, how the polyproteins are synthesized and membrane-inserted in the host cell is unclear. Here we demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 exploits the Sec61-endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane complex (EMC) translation machinery to promote biosynthesis of the virus polyproteins, leading to successful replication and infection. The Sec61-EMC complex engages NSP3-the first transmembrane (TM) protein in pp1a/pp1ab-during active translation. Strikingly, of the four TM segments in NSP3, a marginally hydrophobic domain between TM3 and TM4 is required for EMC-binding and confers EMC-dependent expression. Our results reveal an ER-dependent mechanism for translation of the SARS-CoV-2 NSPs during virus infection, providing insights that should lead to new anti-SARS-CoV-2 therapeutic approaches.

articles.title: Viral envelope protein engagement of host integrin signaling for intestinal peritrophic matrix disruption.
articles.abstract: The intestinal peritrophic matrix (PM) is a chitin-rich barrier that protects arthropods from enteric pathogens, but how crustacean viruses alter this structure during infection remains poorly understood. In the giant freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii, Decapod iridescent virus 1 (DIV1) infection coincides with progressive changes in PM architecture and permeability. Starved prawns exhibited PM impairment, higher viral DNA loads, and greater mortality than fed controls. Starvation-induced immunosuppression may also have contributed to these poorer outcomes following DIV1 challenge. Similarly, knockdown of chitin synthase 2 (MrCHS2) decreased PM-associated chitin, compromised barrier function, and elevated early intestinal viral signals, supporting a protective role for the PM without isolating PM-specific effects. In protein-interaction assays, the Kazal-type serine protease inhibitor MrSPINK5 associated with MrCHS2. Silencing MrSPINK5 partially preserved PM chitin content and barrier integrity while improving survival during DIV1 infection. Exposure to recombinant viral envelope protein 168L induced MrSPINK5 transcription, and heterologous co-immunoprecipitation assays supported an interaction between 168L and host integrin β (MrITGβ). During intact DIV1 infection, MrITGβ knockdown and pharmacological inhibitors linked integrin-associated signaling to MrSPINK5 induction; however, barrier integrity and survival were assessed solely under MrITGβ knockdown and not in the inhibitor experiments. Together, these findings link DIV1 infection to changes in peritrophic matrix structure and permeability and identify MrSPINK5 as a contributor to barrier impairment. The observed association between viral 168L and MrITGβ, together with the signaling responses detected during infection, provides a basis for further investigation into how viral and host factors contribute to barrier dysfunction.

articles.title: Risk of severe dengue in immunocompromised adults in Thailand: A multi-centre retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Case reports suggest severe outcomes in immunocompromised patients, but large cohort comparisons are lacking. We compared dengue outcomes between immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients.

METHODS: A retrospective multicenter cohort study of patients with laboratory-confirmed dengue infection between January 2023 and June 2024 was conducted. People living with HIV (PLWH) with CD4 < 350 cells/µL, recipients of solid organ transplantation, hematopoietic stem cell transplant within 2 years, active malignancy, splenectomy or asplenia, and conditions requiring immunosuppressive agents were classified as immunocompromised. Severe dengue based on WHO 2009 criteria, hospitalization, length of stay, and 30-day mortality were primary outcomes.

FINDINGS: A total of 894 dengue patients were included, including 59 were immunocompromised. Immunocompromised patients were older (median [interquartile range] age 47.0 [30.0-59.0] vs 33.5 [26.0-49.0] years) and had greater comorbidity burden (Charlson index 1 [0-3] vs 0 [0-1]). Clinical presentation was similar, although absence of fever was more common (10.2% vs 1.1%). Laboratory findings were comparable at presentation, but immunocompromised patients had lower nadir platelet counts and prolonged thrombocytopenia. Severe dengue was more frequent in immunocompromised patients (22% vs 4.9%), with higher hospitalization rates, longer stays, and mortality. In multivariable analysis, immunocompromised status (OR 3.43, 95% CI 1.61-7.31) and comorbidity index (OR 1.33, 95% CI 1.16-1.52) were independently associated with severe dengue.

INTERPRETATION: This study adds to the current evidence of higher risk of severe dengue outcome in immunocompromised highlighting the need for improved strategies for prevention and treatment in this patient population.

articles.title: Ex Vivo Modeling of Pneumocystis murina Infection Using Precision-Cut Lung Slices to Evaluate Drug Susceptibility and Host Immune Responses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocystis cannot be cultured, hindering drug development. Munyonho et al. recently described the use of precision-cut lung slices (PCLS) to study P. murina by inoculating uninfected lung slices in short term cultures with P. murina. Herein, we report a new ex vivo PCLS approach leveraging heavily infected lung to preserve the infected microenvironment and enable assessment of antifungals and host responses.

METHODS: PCLS were prepared from heavily infected mouse lungs with PCP. Grocott methenamine silver (GMS) and fluorescent confocal microscopy were used to demonstrate P. murina and lung structures. Infected PCLS slices were incubated for 3 days with pentamidine, ISFP10, or the anti-inflammatory agent ALW-II-41-27 that inhibits EphA2. Viability of PCLS was assessed with Resazurin and qPCR for epithelial markers podoplanin (Pdpn) and surfactant protein C (Sftpc). Pneumocystis numbers were determined with qPCR.

RESULTS: GMS staining and fluorescent confocal microscopy showed abundant P. murina organisms within the PCLS, closely modeling in vivo characteristics of PCP. Infected PCLS slices were incubated for 3 days with the test agents. Resazurin and qPCR for Pdpn and Sftpc confirmed viability of P. murina-infected PCLS throughout. Both pentamidine-treated and ISPF10-treated PCLS exhibited a significant reduction in organisms. Lastly, we performed PCLS using CD4+-depleted PCP-infected EphA2-/- and wild-type mice, followed by treatment with ALW-II-41-27. EphA2 inhibition, either through genetic deletion or pharmacologic intervention, significantly reduced IL-6 release by infected PCLS.

CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a heavily infected ex vivo PCLS model of PCP enabling concurrent evaluation of anti-Pneumocystis therapy and host immune responses.

articles.title: Nasal breathing impairment as a determinant of sleep quality: subjective symptoms and MRI-based findings from the Hamburg City health study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To examine the association between subjective and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)-based nasal breathing impairment (NBI) and sleep quality within a population-based cohort from the Hamburg City Health Study (HCHS).

METHODOLOGY: 746 HCHS-participants completed nasal-breathing questionnaires and underwent 3-T neuro-MRI. Subjective NBI was identified by self-reported breathing difficulty or nasal discharge and quantified by NOSE-D score. Objective NBI was defined by the presence of septal deviation (SD), radiological sinus disease (RSD; via Lund-Mackay Score), nasal polyposis, concha bullosa, septal spur, and the minimal cross-sectional area (mCSA) of the isthmus nasi. Sleep quality endpoints comprised fatigue, difficulty falling or staying asleep and daytime sleepiness (via Epworth-Sleepiness-Scale). Non-parametric statistics and binary logistic regression were applied.

RESULTS: Subjective and objective NBI correlated significantly. Participants with subjective NBI showed greater anterior and superior SD, a higher prevalence of polyposis, and smaller bilateral mCSA. Subjective NBI related weakly to higher fatigue and greater difficulty initiating sleep but not to ESS scores. Objective MRI-based variables did not correlate with sleep quality.

CONCLUSIONS: Subjective NBI, but not objective MRI-derived abnormalities, is weakly associated with impaired sleep quality. Anatomical narrowing contributes to perceived obstruction, yet psychosocial and neurophysiological factors could mediate the relationship between nasal airflow sensation and sleep quality.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and cardio-oncology: a paradigm shift in cancer therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), associated with mutations in genes such as DNMT3A, TET2, JAK2, and splicing factors, may contribute to cardiovascular injury in patients with cancer beyond treatment-related cardiotoxicity.

MAIN FINDINGS: Traditional cardiooncology surveillance relies on left ventricular ejection fraction, global longitudinal strain, and cardiac biomarkers, which may not fully capture early cardiovascular risk. Incorporating high-sensitivity troponin monitoring and variant allele frequency assessment could improve early risk identification, although these approaches require further clinical validation. Such strategies may support personalized cardioprotection and continuity of cancer treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the potential shift from a drug-centred to a host-centred model of cardiotoxicity, emphasizing CHIP-associated inflammation and individualized cardiovascular monitoring during cancer therapy.

articles.title: Atraumatic esophageal rupture.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Association of Nurse Practitioners
articles.abstract: Boerhaave syndrome is the atraumatic rupture of the esophagus and has a very low incidence of approximately 3.1 per 1,000,000 per year. Although the mortality ranges from 10% to 50%, with the morbidity and mortality increasing as the time to diagnosis and intervention increases. This is clinically significant because patients frequently present 24 hours or more after the incident. As time elapses, complications related to the perforation such as chemical mediastinitis, pneumothorax, and sepsis increase exponentially, making early recognition very important. This case study is the presentation of a patient presenting to the emergency department after an atraumatic esophageal rupture from choking on a hot dog. Readers will learn the history, pathophysiology, anatomy, workup, differential diagnosis, and treatment associated with atraumatic esophageal rupture.

articles.title: Lactobacillus-derived threonine mediates the protective effect of piceatannol against endometritis.
articles.abstract: Bacterial endometritis reflects a convergence of persistent infection, barrier failure, and excessive inflammation, yet how the gut microbiota influences these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that piceatannol (PIC) alleviates Escherichia coli-induced endometritis through a microbiota-dependent mechanism that limits uterine injury and preserves epithelial barrier function. PIC reshaped the gut microbial community, with Lactobacillus emerging as a prominent responsive taxon, and supplementation with Lactobacillus vaginalis reproduced much of the protective phenotype. We next found that PIC and L. vaginalis converged on a common metabolic change: increased L-threonine in the intestine and circulation, with elevated levels also detected in the uterus. Increasing L-threonine was sufficient to reduce uterine injury, bacterial burden, inflammation, and barrier disruption. In endometrial epithelial cells, L-threonine increased SHMT1 abundance and methylation potential and was associated with KMT5C-dependent H4K20me3 remodeling at inflammatory loci. Disruption of SHMT1 or KMT5C weakened these protective responses. Together, these findings connect PIC-associated gut microbial remodeling with L-threonine-dependent metabolic and epigenetic regulation of uterine inflammation.

articles.title: Trends in Self-Reported Vision Difficulty and Eye Care Utilization Among Adults With Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Adults with diabetes are at high risk for diabetic eye diseases and recommended to receive regular screening.

OBJECTIVE: To examine national trends in prevalence of vision difficulty and eye care utilization among US adults with diabetes from 1997 to 2024.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cross-sectional trend analysis of National Health Interview Survey data from US adults aged 18 years or older with diabetes.

EXPOSURES: Age, sex, race and ethnicity, education, seeing an eye care practitioner in the past year, current insulin use, diabetes type, time since diabetes diagnoses, and health insurance coverage.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes examined were self-reported vision loss and eye care utilization. Based on the survey questions assessing vision loss, it was not possible to determine whether reported vision loss was central, peripheral, or both, or whether it was specific to 1 eye or both. Analyses examined annual prevalence and trends from 1997 to 2018 and 2019 to 2024.

RESULTS: The full sample included 74 719 individuals. Prevalence of vision difficulty declined between 1997 (23.8%) and 2006 (17.1%; average percent change [APC], -3.4%; 95% CI, -8.8% to -1.6%), followed by no change through 2024. Prevalence of eye care utilization increased only between 2014 (50.3%) and 2018 (55.3%; APC, 3.0%; 95% CI, 0.1% to 8.4%).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Over nearly 3 decades in the US, prevalence of vision difficulty among adults with diabetes initially declined and then plateaued, and prevalence of eye care utilization increased modestly. Findings highlight opportunities to support vision health in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Ethnic Disparities in CKD Recognition, Treatment, and Outcomes Among Arab and Jewish Adults in Israel.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: Ethnic disparities in chronic kidney disease (CKD) may persist within universal health-care systems. We examined CKD recognition, treatment patterns, and long-term outcomes among Arab and Jewish adults with laboratory-defined CKD. We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using Clalit Health Services electronic health records. Adults with laboratory-defined CKD between 2000 and 2023 were included. The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause mortality or kidney replacement therapy (KRT); principal secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality and KRT analyzed separately. Additional outcomes included cardiovascular events, and >50% eGFR decline; annualized eGFR slope was evaluated descriptively. Adjusted models included diabetes as a covariate, with complementary joint ethnicity-diabetes models and propensity score matching. Among 549,291 adults, 77,174 (14%) were of Arab ethnicity and 472,117 (86%) were of Jewish ethnicity. Arab participants were younger (62±14 versus 72±12 years), more frequently had diabetes (74% versus 52%), and were less likely to have documented CKD (35% versus 46%). Although the crude primary outcome was less frequent among Arab participants (25% versus 44%), kidney-specific outcomes were less favorable, including more frequent KRT (4.8% versus 3.3%) and >50% eGFR decline (25% versus 20%). Annualized eGFR slope was modestly more negative among Arab participants. After adjustment, Jewish ethnicity was associated with lower hazards of the primary composite outcome (HR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.77-0.79), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.79-0.82), and KRT (cause-specific HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.85-0.92), and lower odds of >50% eGFR decline (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.87-0.91). Arab participants with diabetes had the highest adjusted risk; findings were consistent after matching. Arab adults with laboratory-defined CKD had lower disease recognition and less favorable adjusted mortality and kidney outcomes. Diabetes contributed importantly to risk but did not fully account for these disparities, supporting systematic CKD recognition and targeted strategies to improve equitable care.

articles.title: The Intrarenal See-Saw: Differentiating the Hemodynamic and Electrolyte Effects of Glucagon and Glucagon-Like-Peptide-1 Receptor Therapies.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: The management of metabolic disease is undergoing a paradigm shift with the transition from single-agent glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) to novel dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor co-agonists. While GLP-1RAs offer established, weight-independent cardiorenal protection, the intentional therapeutic agonism of glucagon, a hormone historically targeted for suppression, introduces profound and largely unexamined physiological shifts. This review clarifies the distinct, often opposing, mechanisms of these hormones, focusing specifically on their divergent roles in kidney hemodynamics and tubular solute handling. Evolutionarily, glucagon defends against starvation by driving hepatic gluconeogenesis and ureagenesis, but its kidney hemodynamic effects are highly context-dependent. Experimental models suggest glucagon may trigger tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF)-mediated glomerular hyperfiltration via proximal Na+/amino acid co-transport after a protein meal, and via direct thick ascending limb (TAL) stimulation during fasting, though long-term human data remain limited. In contrast, GLP-1 coordinates the fed state, inducing proximal natriuresis via Na+/H+ exchanger 3 (NHE3) inhibition while concurrently acting as a kidney vasodilator, effectively uncoupling distal sodium delivery from tubuloglomerular feedback. The advent of dual co-agonists exploits the "glucagon paradox", harnessing glucagon's potent thermogenic and hepatic lipid-oxidizing properties while neutralizing its hyperglycemic risk via simultaneous GLP-1 agonism. However, the kidney implications of chronic pharmacological glucagon exposure remain poorly defined. We explore the theoretical risks of competing hemodynamic forces, the potential microvascular benefits of rapid hepatic steatosis resolution, and the hypothesized alterations in distal tubular electrolyte transport. Furthermore, we highlight how concurrent sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibition might offer complementary protection, proposing its potential role as a theoretical hemodynamic buffer against glucagon-induced hyperfiltration. As dual incretin/glucagon therapies enter clinical practice, nephrologists must proactively investigate these mechanisms to anticipate complex electrolyte challenges and harness the full renoprotective potential of next-generation metabolic pharmacology.

articles.title: Low Oral Antibiotic Efficacy for Persistent Odontogenic Sinusitis Following Dental Extraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While odontogenic sinusitis (ODS) caused by infectious dental pathologies can resolve following definitive dental treatment like dental extraction, many patients experience persistent ODS. In patients with persistent ODS following dental extraction, oral antibiotic efficacy remains incompletely studied. This study evaluated antibiotic success in treating persistent ODS following extraction.

METHODS: A multicenter prospective cohort study was conducted over 2 years with adults whose ODS persisted for more than 2 months following dental extraction. ODS was caused by either endodontic infection or extraction. At first rhinologic visits, symptoms and durations, 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22), computed tomography (CT), and middle meatal endoscopy findings were recorded. Patients were then prescribed 14 days of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. Clinical outcomes were reassessed roughly 2 months later. If purulence resolved at second visits, they were seen 2-3 months later. If purulence persisted at second visits, or recurred at third visits, endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) was offered, and patients were followed for disease resolution.

RESULTS: Of 40 patients, median age was 58.5 years, and 60% were male. Patients had a median 1.0 antibiotic course prior to first visits (14.0 total days/patient). After amoxicillin-clavulanate courses following first rhinologic visits, 57.5% reported transient improvement, but 92.5% were symptomatic at second visits, with symptom recurrence at a median of 7.0 days. Ultimately, 12.5% achieved resolution following antibiotics alone. Of the 35 unresolved patients, 28 underwent ESS, and 96.4% resolved after primary ESS alone.

CONCLUSION: Persistent ODS after extraction rarely resolved after oral amoxicillin-clavulanate, generally following a prior oral antibiotic course. Considering the high success rate of ESS in these patients, earlier ESS should be considered rather than repeated antibiotics.

articles.title: Deceased Burn Patients as Organ Donors: Post-Transplant Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: There were 105,459 patients on the transplant waiting list in the United States in 2025. Only 48,149 (~46%) patients received a transplant during 2024. A high demand coupled with a low supply of organs leaves many transplant recipients perpetually on the waiting list. Literature review reveals a small number of studies on organ donation in deceased burn patients. Burn patients with unsurvivable injuries are prone to have multi-system organ failure and sepsis, leading to them often being overlooked for potential organ donation due concern for organ viability. A review of available records from the University of Kansas Medical Center (KUMC), an American Burn Association (ABA) verified center, between 2023 and 2024 yielded 3 deceased burn patients who were evaluated for potential organ donation. A descriptive review of the characteristics of these cases was undertaken. Of the 3 burn patients declared brain dead or switched to Comfort Measure Only (CMO) care and referred for potential organ donation, 3 underwent organ retrieval with 2 having organs subsequently transplanted to recipients. When death is the expected outcome for a burn-injured patient, it is not always top-of-mind for caregivers or family members to consider potential organ donation. Nonetheless, all members of the burn care team should be reminded to consider the possibility of organ donation.

articles.title: Cell death and growth dynamics shape DNA-replication-based estimates of microbial growth.
articles.abstract: A widely used approach for estimating bacterial growth rates is the origin-to-terminus ratio, or peak-to-trough ratio (PTR), which estimates DNA replication activity from origin and terminus copy numbers. Although PTR is theoretically related to bacterial growth rate, it is often compared with, or used to reason about, changes in population size, which reflect the balance between cell division and loss. These quantities may therefore diverge when cell death is appreciable. Here, we used stochastic, cell-based modelling and controlled laboratory experiments to examine how cell death affects the relationship between PTR and changes in population size. We show that transient stress-induced mortality and heterogeneous survival can cause PTR to fail to reflect changes in population size but still reflect bacterial growth rate. We experimentally validated these predictions by exposing Escherichia coli to osmotic shock or antibiotics, and measuring change in population size and DNA replication activity. We further show that initial physiological state, lag before replication resumes, and abrupt growth arrest can alter the relationship between PTR and change in population size. In the presence of mortality, lag can make PTR more reflective of changes in population size whereas it decreases its correspondence with bacterial growth rate. Together, these results demonstrate how cell death and changes in replication dynamics can bias the interpretation of PTR-based estimates of population change under controlled laboratory conditions.

articles.title: Immune conditioning with BCG rebalances the central-peripheral neuroimmune axis after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) triggers a neuroimmune response involving central inflammation, oxidative stress, systemic immune dysregulation and behavioral impairment. Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination induces long-lasting immune reprogramming with neuroprotective potential; we investigated whether peripheral BCG pretreatment modulates the neuroinflammatory and behavioral consequences of experimental IS. Male Wistar rats, 110 days old, received a single subcutaneous dose of BCG or saline 14 days before middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Two independent cohorts were studied: in Cohort A, infarct size was quantified by TTC staining 24 h after MCAO; in Cohort B, the neurological score was recorded daily for nine days, behavior was assessed on days 10-12 and tissues were collected on day 13. BCG significantly reduced infarct area and attenuated markers of neuroinflammation and oxidative damage in cognition-related brain regions. These changes were accompanied by habituation of exploratory activity in the open field, with no significant differences in the forced swim test. At the systemic level, BCG reduced corticosterone, preserved splenic parameters and attenuated the ischemia-induced increase in circulating IFN-γ, compatible with modulation rather than suppression of peripheral immune competence. Collectively, our findings indicate that peripheral immune conditioning through BCG is associated with a reshaped host response to ischemia involving both neuroimmune and neuroendocrine compartments. Because BCG was administered before ischemia, these data characterize immune preconditioning rather than a therapeutic strategy. Targeting the central-peripheral immune axis may represent a promising strategy to mitigate neuroinflammatory damage and behavioral impairment following IS.

articles.title: Engineering Intrinsically Anti-Inflammatory Synthetic Macromolecules.
articles.abstract: Inflammation drives numerous acute and chronic diseases, yet current therapies, whether small-molecule drugs or biologics, are often limited by toxicity, poor targeting, or high cost. Synthetic macromolecules have emerged as a promising alternative. Their size enables multivalent interactions, prolonged circulation, and on-demand structural tailoring. This review focuses on synthetic macromolecules that exert intrinsic anti-inflammatory activity by virtue of their chemical structure, including covalent polymer-drug conjugates in which the polymeric component contributes essentially to the therapeutic effect, while excluding systems in which the polymer functions merely as an inert carrier. We classify these materials into four mechanistic categories spanning a spatial gradient from extracellular to intracellular, encompassing reactive species-scavenging chemistry, multivalent capture and neutralization of pro-inflammatory mediators such as cell-free DNA and histones, interfacial regulation at cell surfaces and tissue barriers, and intracellular reprogramming of inflammatory signaling pathways. For each category, we discuss the chemical design, biological rationale, and therapeutic outcomes in animal models. We then survey their applications across acute conditions (e.g., lung/liver injury, sepsis) and chronic diseases (e.g., atherosclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis). Finally, we address remaining challenges, including long-term safety, delivery efficiency, immunogenicity, and manufacturing scalability, and outline future directions such as inflammation-responsive materials and multi-target strategies.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the cornerstone of myocardial revascularization in patients with complex coronary artery disease. However, long-term outcomes are limited by graft failure, particularly with saphenous vein grafts, and recurrent ischemic events. Graft attrition follows time-dependent mechanisms, with early failure driven predominantly by platelet-mediated thrombosis and later failure mainly related to intimal hyperplasia and accelerated atherosclerosis. Antithrombotic therapy is, therefore, central to secondary prevention after CABG, but requires a time-adapted approach.

OBSERVATIONS: Lifelong aspirin remains the foundation of post-CABG antiplatelet therapy and is uniformly recommended by current guidelines, whereas the role, including the intensity and duration, of dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) remains controversial. Historically, post-CABG antithrombotic strategies have been extrapolated from percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), despite important differences in pathophysiology in ischemic recurrences and bleeding risk. As PCI paradigms have shifted toward risk-adapted and de-escalation strategies, emerging CABG-specific randomized clinical trials are now challenging the routine use of PCI-like DAPT after surgery.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This review summarizes the biological rationale for antithrombotic therapy after CABG, critically appraises contemporary randomized evidence, and proposes a risk-adapted framework integrating the pathophysiology of graft failure, clinical presentation, and bleeding susceptibility.

articles.title: Computed Tomography Imaging Markers Associated With Prognosis at 10 Years: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SCOT-HEART Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography reduces long-term myocardial infarction in patients with stable chest pain. However, the extent to which quantitative and qualitative plaque characteristics retain prognostic value over the long term remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between CT markers of coronary artery disease and 10-year outcomes.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a post hoc observational analysis of the Scottish Computed Tomography of the HEART (SCOT-HEART) randomized clinical trial, which took place at 3 centers in Scotland from November 2010 to September 2014. Participants in the SCOT-HEART trial who underwent CT were included, after excluding those with for whom CT was not available or was not of adequate quality for analysis. This analysis was conducted from November 2010 to May 2023.

EXPOSURES: Quantitative assessment (Autoplaque 2.5) included calcium score and burden in percentage of calcified, noncalcified, low-attenuation, and total plaque and right coronary artery pericoronary adipose tissue (RCA PCAT) attenuation. Obstructive disease (>70% stenosis) and adverse plaque characteristics were visually assessed.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was myocardial infarction or coronary artery disease death at 10 years.

RESULTS: Among 1769 patients (mean [SD] age, 57.6 [9.4] years; 997 [56.4%] male), a primary event occurred in 117 (6.6%) during the 10 years of follow-up. Patients with myocardial infarction or coronary artery disease death had a higher median (IQR) cardiovascular risk score (22 [15-32] vs 15 [9-23]; P < .001), calcium score (387 [59-1041] vs 15 [0-190] Agatston units; P < .001), and more had obstructive disease (59% vs 23%; P < .001). Median (IQR) total (37.7 [0-48.8] vs 48.6 [42.2-54.7]; P < .001), calcified (0.3 [0-2.5] vs 3.2 [0.9-7.9]; P < .001), noncalcified (34.5 [0-45.0] vs 42.5 [36.4-48.5]; P < .001), and low-attenuation plaque burden (3.9 [0-6.8] vs 6.3 [4.3-8.3]; P < .001) and mean (SD) RCA PCAT attenuation (-76.1 [8.2] vs -73.4 [8.7]; P = .002) were higher in patients with the primary outcome. When adjusted for cardiovascular risk score and CT scanner type, total, calcified, noncalcified, and low-attenuation plaque burdens were independently associated with the primary outcome in all patients (hazard ratio [HR] per doubling for total: 1.32; 95% CI, 1.18-1.48; P < .001; calcified: 1.65; 95% CI, 1.44-1.88; P < .001; noncalcified: 1.29; 95% CI, 1.16-1.44; P < .001; and low-attenuation plaque: 1.51; 95% CI, 1.28-1.78; P < .001), and in both male individuals (HR per doubling for total: 1.27; 95% CI, 1.10-1.46; P = .001; calcified: 1.53; 95% CI, 1.32-1.79; P < .001; noncalcified: 1.24; 95% CI, 1.08-1.42; P = .002; and low-attenuation plaque: 1.41; 95% CI, 1.15-1.73; P < .001) and female individuals (HR per doubling for total: 1.30; 95% CI, 1.07-1.57; P = .007; calcified: 1.64; 95% CI, 1.17-2.30; P = .004; noncalcified: 1.30; 95% CI, 1.07-1.57; P = .008; and low-attenuation plaque: 1.57; 95% CI, 1.15-2.13; P = .004), but RCA PCAT attenuation was not associated in male participants. Patients with a low-attenuation plaque burden greater than 4% were more likely to experience the primary event (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.69-4.20; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this post hoc analysis of a randomized clinical trial, among patients with stable chest pain, CT findings including quantitative plaque metrics were associated with outcomes up to 10 years, suggesting potential prognostic value.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01149590.

articles.title: Synaptic Vesicle Glycoprotein 2A and Excitatory-Inhibitory Balance in Psychiatric Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) is widely used as a positron emission tomography (PET) proxy of synaptic density. PET studies have consistently reported SV2A deficits across schizophrenia-related disorders. Beyond its structural role, SV2A is involved in calcium-dependent neurotransmission and may contribute to the regulation of network excitatory-inhibitory balance.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize preclinical evidence on the role of SV2A in kindling (ie, hyperexcitation) development, an experimental intervention that induces long-lasting increases in brain excitability, and to examine the associations of SV2A modulation with kindling development as a model of hyperexcitation, with implications for interpretation of SV2A PET findings in neuropsychiatric disorders.

DATA SOURCES: EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to December 30, 2025.

STUDY SELECTION: Experimental animal studies assessing SV2A expression or pharmacological or genetic modulation in kindling models. Two independent reviewers performed study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment (Systematic Review Centre for Laboratory Animal Experimentation tool).

DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: This systematic review was registered in PROSPERO and conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood estimation were conducted for seizure severity and odds of reaching kindling criteria. Heterogeneity was assessed using Q, τ2, and I2 statistics, and meta-regression analyses examined potential moderators.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Changes in SV2A expression, seizure severity, and odds of reaching kindling criteria.

RESULTS: Thirty studies were included across 3 categories: SV2A measurement (7 studies), genetic (2 studies) and pharmacological modulation (22 studies), with 1 study contributing to 2 of these categories. Kindling experiments in wild-type animals consistently reported higher hippocampal SV2A expression, primarily in GABAergic neurons. Genetic models of reduced SV2A function showed higher susceptibility to kindling. SV2A-targeting interventions were associated with significantly lower seizure severity (Hedge g = -2.16; 95% CI, -2.95 to -1.37; P < .001; I2 = 82.3%) and lower odds of reaching kindling (odds ratio, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P < .001; I2 = 0.4%).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This meta-analysis found that SV2A expression is dynamically regulated by neuronal activity and may represent a compensatory mechanism aimed at restoring synaptic homeostasis in response to repeated excitatory stimulation. These findings suggest that SV2A may index not only synaptic density but also circuit resilience, with potential relevance for neuropsychiatric disorders characterized by excitatory-inhibitory dysregulation.

articles.title: Real-world outcomes of endoscopic versus surgical resection for duodenal subepithelial lesions: defining the practical boundaries of endoscopic therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Duodenal subepithelial lesions (D-SELs) are rare and exhibit heterogeneous growth patterns, complicating treatment selection amid limited evidence. We compared endoscopic (ER) and surgical resection (SR) outcomes and identified factors associated with conversion to surgery after attempted ER.

METHODS: We retrospectively compared clinicopathological characteristics, resection and perioperative outcomes, adverse events, and follow-up between ER and SR in 133 patients with non-ampullary D-SELs treated from April 2019 to April 2024. Conversion-associated factors were assessed using univariable and parsimonious multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among the 133 patients, 101 underwent attempted ER (ESD/EFTR) and 32 underwent SR. En bloc and R0 resection rates among completed ER cases were 96.7% and 90.1%, respectively; 82/101 (81.2%) achieved R0 without conversion. Compared with SR, ER was associated with shorter procedure time (39 vs 210 min, P<0.001), hospital stay (6 vs 13 days, P<0.001), and lower post-procedure infection (1.0% vs 18.8%, P<0.001), with no significant differences in other adverse events or mid-term oncologic outcomes during follow-up. Conversion occurred in 10/101 (9.9%) attempted ER cases. Extraluminal growth (OR 24.27, 95% CI 2.38-247.21, P=0.007) and tumor size >3 cm (OR 86.70, 95% CI 7.01-1072.44, P<0.001) were independently associated with conversion.

CONCLUSION: In selected patients, ER achieved high resection success and was associated with favorable perioperative outcomes, with no recurrence or metastasis observed during follow-up. Tumor size >3 cm and extraluminal growth were independently associated with conversion, informing preoperative risk assessment and individualized treatment selection while supporting the potential role of ER in selected patients.

articles.title: Exercise Prehabilitation and Recovery After Head and Neck Cancer Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Preoperative physical activity is associated with improved postoperative outcomes in various cancer populations, but its impact for patients with head and neck cancer (HNC) remains understudied.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of an exercise prehabilitation program on postoperative mobility after HNC surgery.

DESIGN, SETTINGS, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized clinical trial conducted from January 2024 to December 2025 at a single tertiary center in Portland, Oregon, included adults undergoing HNC surgery with free flap reconstruction. Patients with planned postoperative intensive care unit stays, severe mental health conditions, serious heart or lung conditions, bony metastases, falls within the past year, cognitive impairments, or impaired mobility requiring assistive devices were excluded. Follow-up was through hospital discharge or postoperative day 14.

INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized to 2 to 5 weeks of exercise prehabilitation or control. Prehabilitation involved walking 2000 to 4000 steps per day, measured using wearable activity trackers, and strength exercises 3 times weekly.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was daily postoperative step counts. Secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, length of stay, discharge disposition, pain scores, and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality-of-Life Questionnaire, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 for depression, and program satisfaction surveys.

RESULTS: A total of 52 patients were randomized (25 control, 27 intervention); 12 discontinued after randomization, leaving 40 patients (median [IQR] age, 61 [53-68] years; 25 [63%] male) for analysis (20 per group). Twenty-five participants (63%) had oral cavity or oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Lower extremity flaps were received in 8 patients (40%) in the prehabilitation group and 12 patients (60%) in the control group (standardized mean difference [SMD], 0.41). Baseline comorbidities, cancer characteristics, sarcopenia, functional performance, and wearable activity tracker adherence were comparable. Median (IQR) preoperative step counts were similar (4950 [3330-7370] steps for prehabilitation vs 4730 [4040-6650] steps for control; SMD = 0.07). There were no differences in postoperative step counts or secondary outcomes. In an exploratory analysis, patients above the median preoperative steps (4810) demonstrated greater postoperative mobility (median [IQR] of 1150 [332-1840] steps for those above the median vs 335 [81-491] steps for those below the median; log-transformed difference, 1.39 [95% CI, 0.49-2.30]).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial demonstrate that exercise prehabilitation was feasible for patients with HNC but did not generate significant improvements in early postoperative outcomes. Future randomized clinical trials are needed to evaluate whether a higher preoperative step count is associated with greater postoperative mobility.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06079697.

Diastolic dysfunction in adults with congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract: Diastolic dysfunction is a major determinant of cardiovascular symptoms, quality of life, and overall prognosis in adults with acquired heart disease. The global burden of disease is increasing, and substantial progress has been made in developing standardized multimodality approaches for the assessment of left ventricular diastolic function. In adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) diastolic dysfunction is substantially more prevalent than in the general population; however, it remains comparatively under-investigated, under-diagnosed, and under-treated. Assessment is complicated by the marked heterogeneity of this population, including the influence of underlying anatomy, prior surgical interventions, and residual haemodynamic lesions on ventricular filling physiology. Consequently, a 'one-size-fits-all' approach or direct extrapolation of guidelines from acquired heart disease is often inappropriate. This state-of-the-art review summarized the current evidence and contemporary approaches to the assessment and management of diastolic dysfunction in ACHD, highlighting the strengths and limitations of available diagnostic modalities. In addition, lesion-specific considerations and practical diagnostic and management frameworks are proposed to evaluate and treat diastolic dysfunction across the spectrum of ACHD.

articles.title: Gestational Age and Birth Outcomes in US Freestanding Birth Centers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Gestational age is a key determinant of neonatal outcomes, yet limited research has examined its distribution and associated outcomes within freestanding birth center populations in the United States. This study aimed to describe the distribution of gestational age and evaluate its association with neonatal outcomes in a national birth center sample.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the American Association of Birth Centers Perinatal Data Registry. Gestational age was categorized into clinically relevant groups. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize gestational age distribution. Associations between gestational age and neonatal outcomes, including hospital transfer, Apgar scores, low birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, readmission, breastfeeding, and perinatal death, were assessed using χ2 tests.

RESULTS: Births in freestanding birth centers were concentrated at later gestational ages, with the highest proportion occurring at 40 weeks and fewer early-term births than observed nationally. Gestational age was significantly associated with multiple neonatal outcomes. Neonatal hospital transfer was more frequent at 36 and 37 weeks and increased again at 41 weeks compared with 39 weeks. Low 1-minute Apgar scores were more common at 40 and 41 weeks, whereas no differences were observed in 5-minute Apgar scores. Low birth weight and neonatal intensive care unit admission were most common at earlier gestational ages and least common at 39 and 40 weeks. Readmission rates were higher at 36 and 37 weeks, lowest at 40 weeks, and increased modestly at later gestational ages. Breastfeeding rates remained high across all gestational age groups, and perinatal death was rare.

DISCUSSION: Neonatal outcomes were most favorable at 39 and 40 weeks within this birth center population, with higher risk observed at earlier and later gestational ages. These findings support the importance of gestational age in risk stratification and shared decision-making for individuals planning birth center care.

articles.title: Quantitative comparison of SPECT- and PET- based methods for treatment planning and dosimetry in Y-90 radioembolisation therapy.
articles.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
articles.abstract: Quantitative post-therapy imaging is essential for verifying administered activity and assessing dose distribution following Y-90 radioembolisation. This study compared large energy acceptance window Y-90 SPECT and PET for estimating implanted activity relative to the standard SIRTEX vial calibration method and evaluated their equivalence dosimetry. The retrospective Y-90 SPECT were acquired using protocols optimised for qualitative rather than quantitative imaging. The predictive accuracy of Tc-99​m MAA SPECT and compartmental models for pre-therapy dosimetry estimation was also investigated. A cohort of 28 patients treated with Y-90 resin microspheres underwent pre-therapy Tc-99​m MAA SPECT and post-therapy Y-90 SPECT and PET. The regional doses (tumour, perfused liver, and lungs) were calculated using the local deposition model. Equivalence between methods was assessed using the two one-sided tests. The Y-90 SPECT and PET measurements of implanted activity was on average -3 % ± 12 % and -5 % ± 13 %, of the SIRTEX calculated method. Tumoural doses derived from Y-90 SPECT and PET were statistically equal and equivalent (mean difference -1 %, SD ± 14 %), and perfused liver doses were equivalent within ±5 Gy (mean difference 2 Gy, SD 13 Gy). Despite statistical equivalence, a 14-42% variability in individual measurements remained. Tc-99​m MAA SPECT-predicted tumour doses showed closer agreement with PET doses than the partition model (4% vs 6%), while perfused liver and lung predictions were comparable. Although PET remains the current clinical reference standard, Y-90 SPECT provides clinically acceptable equivalence where PET is not available while supporting post-therapy verification and retrospective dosimetric analyses.

articles.title: Acetazolamide in Decompensated Heart Failure: Current Use and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Congestion remains the principal driver of hospitalisation in decompensated heart failure, yet complete decongestion is frequently not achieved with loop diuretics alone, particularly in patients with advanced heart failure or impaired kidney function. Acetazolamide, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, reduces proximal tubular sodium and bicarbonate reabsorption, thereby enhancing downstream sodium delivery and potentially overcoming mechanisms of diuretic resistance. This review summarises contemporary evidence for acetazolamide as adjunctive therapy in decompensated heart failure, focusing on intravenous and oral formulations, renal and electrolyte safety, and practical patient selection. The ADVOR trial, which excluded patients taking sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, supports early intravenous acetazolamide added to loop diuretics to improve natriuresis, urine output and short-term decongestion, with acceptable in-hospital safety. Evidence for oral acetazolamide is less consistent, suggesting improved diuresis and natriuresis but more variable clinical decongestion, possibly due to delayed absorption. Acetazolamide is a practical add-on option for selected patients, particularly those with inadequate loop diuretic response or metabolic alkalosis.

articles.title: Reproducibility and variability of visual capillary refill time assessment by intensive care physicians: comparison with near-infrared spectroscopy and automated video analysis in a cross-sectional observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Capillary refill time (CRT) is a widely used bedside marker of peripheral perfusion in intensive care, and its clinical relevance has grown after recent randomized trials incorporated it into hemodynamic resuscitation algorithms. Reproducibility under routine conditions remains poorly characterized, and objective tools to reduce observer-dependent variability are lacking. We developed a custom Python-based software for automated colorimetric CRT analysis and compared visual assessment with this tool and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) in a controlled experimental model.

METHODS: Eight healthy adult volunteers underwent three conditions: baseline, venous congestion at 50% of diastolic blood pressure (DBP), and congestion at 75% DBP. Tissue oxygen saturation (StO₂) was recorded continuously by NIRS every 3 s. Fingertip-pulp compression videos were obtained at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 240 s. Sixteen ICU clinicians assessed 2401 coded videos in random order. The Python colorimetric tool was applied to valid recordings. Reproducibility was evaluated with variance-component models, intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), coefficients of repeatability (CR), and linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Mean visual CRT was 1.77 ± 0.65 s. No significant effects of congestion condition (F = 1.45, p = 0.23) or time (F = 1.48, p = 0.230) were detected; marginal R² was 0.04 and conditional R² was 0.44. Interobserver ICC was 0.52 (95% bootstrap CI 0.42-0.61), with a CR of 1.20 s; mean intraobserver ICC was 0.69 (range 0.42-0.84). Simulations showed ICC rising to 0.76 with three observers, 0.84 with five, and 0.92 with ten. NIRS (904 observations) detected significant condition- and time-related changes (p < 0.001); late-phase StO₂ differed by 8.46% between congestion levels, and nadir StO₂ was lower under greater congestion (p = 0.0018). Automated analysis of 53 recordings yielded a mean CRT of 3.89 ± 1.26 s, a significant congestion effect (F = 6.32, p = 0.016; marginal R² 0.12, conditional R² 0.48), and a mean between-condition difference of 0.68 s (p = 0.017).

CONCLUSIONS: Visual CRT showed moderate reproducibility and did not detect graded perfusion changes. Both NIRS and the Python-based automated software identified condition-related differences that visual assessment missed. These results call for cautious interpretation of isolated CRT when small serial changes inform clinical decisions, and support further evaluation of automated approaches in critically ill patients.

articles.title: Rethinking peripheral blood stem cell mobilization in multiple myeloma: from rescue to risk-adapted strategies.
articles.abstract: Peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) mobilization is essential for autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) in multiple myeloma. Although mobilization success traditionally relies on achieving a minimum CD34+ cell dose, clinical outcomes are influenced by apheresis procedures, remobilization, treatment delays, and patient burden. We reviewed pivotal randomized trials, prospective and real-world studies, and contemporary quadruplet induction data to evaluate the transition from rescue-based to risk-adapted PBSC mobilization. In a pivotal phase 3 trial, plerixafor plus granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) enabled 71.6% of patients to collect ≥ 6 × 106 CD34+ cells/kg within two apheresis procedures, compared with 34.4% with G-CSF plus placebo. On-demand plerixafor guided by peripheral CD34+ monitoring enabled 95% of patients to collect ≥ 2 × 106 cells/kg and rescued approximately 90% of those requiring intervention. Daratumumab-containing induction is associated with lower stem cell yields and increased plerixafor use while generally preserving ASCT feasibility. In the prospective DILEMMA study, daratumumab-treated patients had lower first-apheresis yields and greater on-demand plerixafor use than propensity-score-matched historical controls; however, all achieved ≥ 2 × 106 CD34+ cells/kg. Although the non-randomized design limits causal inference, response-guided interventions may help mitigate daratumumab-associated mobilization impairment. Motixafortide enabled 92.5% of patients to collect ≥ 6 × 106 cells/kg within two apheresis procedures and 88.8% after one procedure, compared with 26.2% and 9.5%, respectively, with placebo. These findings support proactive, risk-stratified PBSC mobilization using locally appropriate thresholds and real-world evidence from Korea to improve collection predictability and efficiency, while minimizing treatment delays and patient burden.

articles.title: A multimodal fusion model integrating two-dimensional ultrasound radiomics, deep learning features, and clinical indicators for non-invasive assessment of renal interstitial fibrosis in patients with chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF) is a common pathological pathway through which chronic kidney disease (CKD) progresses to end-stage renal disease. Percutaneous renal biopsy remains the gold standard for RIF assessment, but is invasive and unsuitable for dynamic monitoring. This study aimed to develop and validate a multimodal model integrating clinical indicators, two-dimensional ultrasound radiomics features, and deep learning features for non-invasive assessment of RIF severity in patients with CKD.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 359 CKD patients who underwent renal biopsy between January 2022 and December 2025 were consecutively enrolled and divided into a training set (n = 251) and a validation set (n = 108) at a 7:3 ratio. To mitigate batch effects from different ultrasound machines, the ComBat harmonization method was applied to the radiomics features. To prevent information leakage, all preprocessing steps (including PCA and LASSO) were strictly performed within the inner folds of the 5-fold cross-validation. Five primary models and two ablation models were constructed: Clinic, Radiomics, DL, DLR, Combined, Clinic + Radiomics, and Clinic + DL. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), continuous NRI, and IDI. Grad-CAM was used for interpretability analysis of the DL model.

RESULTS: A total of 359 patients were included, comprising 239 (66.6%) with mild RIF and 120 (33.4%) with moderate-to-severe RIF. Pathologically, membranous nephropathy (40.7%) and IgA nephropathy (33.7%) were the dominant types. In the validation set, the ablation models showed stepwise improvements over the clinical baseline (AUC = 0.839): Clinic + Radiomics achieved an AUC of 0.859, and Clinic + DL achieved an AUC of 0.862 with a high specificity of 92.5%. The full Combined model achieved the highest AUC of 0.877 (95% CI: 0.813-0.942), significantly outperforming the Radiomics, DL, and DLR models (all P < 0.05). Compared with the Clinic model, the AUC improvement of the Combined model did not reach statistical significance (P = 0.195); however, it demonstrated a meaningful improvement in overall risk discrimination (IDI = 0.173). In multivariable logistic regression, eGFR, blood_sugar, and age were independently associated with moderate-to-severe RIF.

CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal model significantly improved discrimination over single imaging and dual-modality models. While its performance was comparable to the pure clinical model in terms of AUC, the multimodal fusion provided valuable incremental value in continuous risk reclassification (IDI). Clinical indicators, particularly eGFR, remain robust and indispensable baselines for RIF assessment.

articles.title: Intravenous dapagliflozin did not induce ketogenesis or improve cardiac and skeletal muscle function in resuscitated murine sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized controlled trials have shown benefits of temporary caloric restriction in acute critical illness, attributed partially to activated ketogenesis. Ketone-ester administration has been associated with improved hemodynamics in cardiogenic-shock and heart-failure patients, and with improved skeletal muscle function in septic mice. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors improve chronic heart failure outcomes, possibly partially through enhanced ketogenesis. We hypothesized that intravenous dapagliflozin activates ketogenesis and improves cardiac and skeletal muscle function in murine sepsis, particularly during intermittent fasting.

METHODS: First, in a dose-finding study, 12 healthy catheterized mice were randomized to placebo or dapagliflozin 1 or 10 mg/kg/day for 5 days. Second, 59 septic mice were randomized to placebo or dapagliflozin 10 mg/kg/day for 3 or 5 days. Sepsis was induced by cecal ligation and puncture; mice received fluids, antibiotics, analgesics, and (from day 1) continuous parenteral nutrition (PN). Third, we randomized 18 septic mice to placebo or dapagliflozin 10 mg/kg/day for 3 days during intermittent fasting, induced by withholding PN for 9 h/day. We performed echocardiography before sacrifice on day 3; extensor digitorum longus muscle force was assessed ex vivo on day 5. Untreated mice served as healthy reference (n = 30). Glucosuria, blood glucose, plasma 3-hydroxybutyrate (3HB), and myocardial metabolic gene expression were assessed. We studied Spearman correlation between plasma 3HB and echocardiographic markers.

RESULTS: In healthy catheterized mice, both dapagliflozin doses induced glucosuria (405 [296-500] and 500 [390-500] versus 60 [47-98] mg/dL; P = 0.010 and P = 0.028) without hypoglycemia. Dapagliflozin induced glucosuria in septic mice (day 5: 376 [244-600] versus 0 [0-0] mg/dL; P < 0.001) without affecting survival. With continuous PN, dapagliflozin did not increase 3HB, nor improve cardiac or skeletal muscle function. During intermittent fasting, it lowered blood glucose (53 [41-56] versus 70 [61-78] mg/dL; P = 0.027) without increasing 3HB or improving cardiac function. Myocardial mitochondrial oxidation genes were generally suppressed by sepsis without consistent dapagliflozin effects. 3HB correlated positively with ejection fraction, stroke volume and cardiac output.

CONCLUSIONS: Dapagliflozin provoked glucosuria, but did not induce ketogenesis, nor improve cardiac or skeletal muscle function in septic mice, regardless of nutritional strategy. Future research should assess alternative strategies that enhance ketone availability.

articles.title: Evolution in management of women with Bartholin's cyst/abscess presenting to the emergency department: a comparative analysis in one Irish tertiary hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bartholin glands are bilateral mucus-secreting glands located at the posterolateral aspect of the vaginal introitus. Obstruction of the gland duct can result in formation of a Bartholin cyst, while secondary infection may lead to abscess formation. Traditionally, management has included antibiotics, incision and drainage, or marsupialisation, often requiring hospital admission or theatre access. Word catheter insertion was introduced in 2022 at Cork University Maternity Hospital as an outpatient management option. This study aimed to evaluate changes in management and clinical outcomes following its introduction.

METHODS: A retrospective comparative review was performed of all individuals presenting to the emergency department with a Bartholin cyst or abscess in 2021 and 2023. Electronic healthcare records were reviewed for demographics, presentation characteristics, treatment modality, hospital admission, complications, and follow-up arrangements. Statistical analysis was performed using chi-squared testing.

RESULTS: A total of 145 individuals were included, comprising 69 presentations in 2021 and 76 in 2023. Demographics between cohorts were comparable, with no significant differences in age distribution, co-morbidities, or BMI. Individuals presenting in 2023 were more likely to attend out-of-hours services (59.2% vs 43.0%, p = 0.049). Management strategies changed significantly following introduction of the Word catheter. In 2021, antibiotics and incision and drainage were the most common treatments, while no Word catheters were used. By 2023, Word catheter insertion became the predominant treatment modality (0% vs 46.1%, p < 0.001). Hospital admission rates decreased significantly following implementation of the Word catheter service (44.9% vs 7.9%, p < 0.001), reflecting a shift toward outpatient management. Complications were more frequently documented in 2023 (22.4% vs 5.8%, p = 0.004), likely reflecting improved follow-up and documentation. Planned follow-up arrangements also increased substantially in 2023.

CONCLUSION: Introduction of the Word catheter resulted in a significant shift toward outpatient management of Bartholin cysts and abscesses, with a marked reduction in hospital admissions. These findings are consistent with international and Irish data supporting Word catheter insertion as a safe, effective, and resource-efficient first-line treatment option. Further prospective studies are warranted to better evaluate long-term recurrence and complication rates.

articles.title: Cholesterol Screening in Youth: Rethinking the Role of Fasting.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Fasting lipid profiles have long been considered the standard for assessing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk in adults and youth. This review examines the physiologic, clinical, and public health evidence supporting a nonfasting-first approach to pediatric lipid screening, with a focus on improving early detection of familial hypercholesterolemia (FH).

RECENT FINDINGS: Nonfasting lipid profiles show minimal variation in total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), and non-HDL-C, while triglycerides (TG) rise modestly and predictably. Apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing lipoproteins, non-HDL-C, and lipoprotein(a) remain stable across feeding states. Large cohort studies demonstrate high concordance in ASCVD risk classification between fasting and nonfasting samples, with nonfasting LDL-C and non-HDL-C outperforming fasting values in predicting ASCVD events. Only a small minority of children require confirmation after fasting, typically those with moderate-to-severe hypertriglyceridemia (e.g., TG ≥ 175 mg/dL) or suspected disorders of chylomicron metabolism. Nonfasting testing improves compliance, enables same-day testing, and facilitates school-based and community screening. Nonfasting lipid testing is accurate, practical, and well-suited for universal pediatric screening. Harmonizing pediatric guidelines with adult recommendations, expanding point-of-care testing, and incorporating nonfasting measurements into clinical trials could substantially improve early detection of FH and other lipid disorders, and enhance cardiovascular prevention efforts.

articles.title: Prospective Real-World Evaluation of Clinical Remission Outcomes with Mepolizumab in Patients with Severe Asthma: The REIMAGINE Study Protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Observational studies demonstrate that approximately one third of patients receiving mepolizumab for severe asthma achieve clinical remission (no exacerbations, no oral corticosteroid [OCS] use, controlled symptoms and stabilised lung function) after 1 year of treatment. Data suggest that patients initiating treatment before irreversible airway deterioration are more likely to achieve clinical remission. The prospective REIMAGINE study will evaluate clinical remission with mepolizumab in patients with severe asthma not receiving maintenance OCS (mOCS), without severe lung function impairment, in a real-world setting.

METHODS: REIMAGINE is an international, multicentre, prospective, single-arm study of patients initiating mepolizumab who have forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) ≥ 60% predicted, ≤ 4 asthma exacerbations per year and are not receiving mOCS. The following data are being collected at baseline and at routine healthcare visits for 24 months: exacerbations; outpatient visits, emergency department visits and hospital admissions for asthma; medication use; lung function by spirometry; patient-reported outcomes, including the Asthma Control Test (ACT); and adverse events. The primary endpoint is clinical remission at 12 months using a four-component definition: no clinically significant asthma exacerbations (CSEs), no use of systemic corticosteroids for asthma, an ACT score of ≥ 20 and no clinically significant deterioration from baseline in FEV1.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: Predictors of achieving clinical remission in patients on biologic therapy include earlier treatment initiation, limited OCS use and lower lung function impairment. Initiation of biologic therapy with mepolizumab in participants of the REIMAGINE study, before disease progression, is predicted to reduce CSEs and the need for OCS, improve symptoms and maintain lung function, increasing the likelihood of achieving clinical remission.

CONCLUSIONS: REIMAGINE is the first prospective real-world study assessing the impact of mepolizumab on clinical remission, providing valuable insights into clinical remission outcomes in patients with severe asthma who initiate mepolizumab therapy before irreversible disease progression.

TRIAL REGISTRY: Trial registration number: ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06041386; GSK clinical trial registry: 219871.

articles.title: Association of the FTO rs9939609 variant with metabolic syndrome in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between FTO rs9939609 and metabolic syndrome (MetS) in adults across five genetic models.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through 8 August 2026, with broader supplementary searches on 23 September 2026. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp inference. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, multiplicity corrections, sensitivity analyses, and small-study effects were assessed.

RESULTS: Thirty-one publications comprising 32,900 participants were included; 15 contributed to meta-analysis. Each model included 11-15 independent comparisons. Nominal associations were observed for allelic (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.02-2.50), recessive (1.83, 1.04-3.21), homozygote (2.21, 1.20-4.06), and heterozygote models (1.60, 1.01-2.53), but not the dominant model (1.47, 0.99-2.18). None remained significant after Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Heterogeneity was substantial to considerable (I² = 67.1%-88.3%); all prediction intervals crossed the null. The homozygote association remained nominally significant in all 11 leave-one-out iterations but attenuated after jointly excluding Song (control-specific Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium deviation) and Gogoi-Mising (influence analysis prompted by reported whole-stratum deviation). Egger's tests detected no statistically significant small-study effects.

CONCLUSION: Evidence does not establish a conclusive association between FTO rs9939609 and MetS. Unadjusted estimates, substantial heterogeneity, prediction intervals crossing the null, and very low evidence certainty warrant interpreting these findings as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: The Use of Inverse Probability Weighting to Estimate Treatment Effects on the Non-Zero Count Outcome in Hurdle Models.
articles.journal: Prevention science : the official journal of the Society for Prevention Research
articles.abstract: In prevention research, analysts often encounter outcomes exhibiting a count distribution with excess zeros. To account for this, two-part zero-altered hurdle models are commonly employed that separately model: (1) the zero vs. non-zero part using logistic regression and (2) the count portion among the non-zeros or those "at-risk" for the outcome using count regression. In a randomized controlled trial (RCT), analyses testing the effect of the intervention on the count portion in a hurdle model are conditional on being non-zero at the post-intervention follow-up assessment. Because non-zero status is determined post-randomization, the distribution of covariates by study condition in that non-zero subpopulation may deviate from the overall sample that was randomized and, thus, the causal interpretation of the treatment effect based on randomization may no longer hold. Without accounting for potential selection effects, estimates from the count portion of the model may be biased, a critical but largely overlooked methodological issue in the evaluation of trial outcomes. To address this challenge, we propose estimating the treatment effect on the count regression portion of the model using inverse probability weighting (IPW-CR). With this approach, observations are reweighted to make the distribution of baseline covariates similar across study conditions in the non-zero subsample. Using data from an RCT of an intervention to reduce alcohol use, we demonstrate the IPW-CR approach for the hurdle model and compare the weighted results with traditional unweighted results. In this data example, the unweighted approach showed a statistically significant reduction in the non-zero count of drinks per typical week in the intervention relative to the comparison condition; however, the IPW-CR approach yielded an attenuated and statistically non-significant intervention effect. The IPW-CR approach may be a feasible and promising strategy to overcome potential selection bias when examining effects of an intervention on the count portion of a hurdle model in an RCT setting.

articles.title: Clozapine Intoxication: What Can We Learn from Case Reports? A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clozapine remains the gold standard for treatment resistant schizophrenia; however, the complex pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties makes clozapine susceptible to interactions and thus increase the risk of intoxications.

OBJECTIVE: By reviewing published case reports on acute clozapine intoxications, we aimed to identify clinical scenarios, risk factors and trajectory outcomes, to recommend potentially preventable measures.
