METHOD: We systematically searched PubMed and Embase and included all published articles describing cases with acute intoxication in adults (18-64 years) by using the ICD-10 definition of acute intoxication. Furthermore, a description of increases in clozapine dose or plasma levels should be evident (or suspected) for inclusion. Case reports were categorized exclusively in one of the following groups: 'drug-drug interactions', 'intentional overdose', 'infection/inflammation', 'smoking cessation', 'unintentional overdose' and 'other'.

RESULTS: Eighty-seven studies were included, resulting in 100 case reports. The largest group was intentional overdose with 35 cases (35.0%), followed by infection/inflammation 22 (22.0%), drug-drug interactions 18 (18.0%), other 13 (13.0%), smoking cessation 8 (8.0%) and lastly unintentional overdose 4 (4.0%). Overall, 34 cases (34.0%) required intensive care while 35 (35.0%) required medical hospitalization (non-intensive care). Two cases had a fatal outcome. Maximum survived clozapine plasma level was 9476 ng/mL and the highest survived ingested dose was 12.5 g. The most common intoxication symptoms were sedation, confusion and tachycardia.

CONCLUSIONS: The major finding of this review is that clozapine-induced intoxications can be life-threatening, illustrated by 2 fatal cases and 34 cases (34.0%) receiving treatment in an intensive care unit. This points out that clozapine intoxications should be taken seriously, and preventable measures should be taken whenever possible.

articles.title: Asthma Medication Use Among Pregnant Women in Japan: A Large-Scale Claims Database Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal asthma is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, and guideline-concordant maintenance therapy, particularly inhaled corticosteroids (ICS), is recommended throughout pregnancy. However, real-world evidence on asthma medication use among pregnant women undergoing long-term asthma management in Japan remains limited.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to describe asthma medication use among pregnant women with asthma who had a live birth, using a large-scale administrative claims database in Japan.

METHODS: We conducted a utilization study between January 2005 and July 2023 using data from the JMDC Inc. administrative claims database. Pregnancies ending in live births and linked to infants (delivery ≥ 2010) in women aged 15-49 years were identified using previously developed algorithms. Asthma was defined by ICD-10 codes J45-J46 plus long-term ICS-based management. We described the prevalence of class-specific asthma medication use across 90 days before pregnancy onset, during each trimester, and 90 days postpartum based on dispensing or claim records.

RESULTS: We identified 2452 pregnancies among 2387 women with asthma and multiple ICS-containing inhalation uses (mean maternal age [standard deviation] 34.0 [4.4] years). Among women receiving long-term asthma management, the use of any asthma medication declined from 100% in the pre-pregnancy period (by definition) to 73.8% in the first trimester, 55.8% in the second trimester, 51.1% in the third trimester, and 50.9% postpartum. Similarly, the proportion of pregnant women using ICS-containing medications declined from 100% before pregnancy to 70.9%, 52.7%, 48.1%, and 46.0% across the corresponding periods. Use of adjunctive medications (including tulobuterol patches, leukotriene receptor antagonists, sustained-release theophylline, short-acting β2-agonists, and systemic corticosteroids) was markedly lower during pregnancy than before pregnancy.

CONCLUSIONS: Asthma medication use declined from early to mid-pregnancy, whereas ICS-based therapy remained the predominant maintenance treatment throughout the perinatal period. These findings support continued guideline-concordant management during pregnancy and highlight the need for attention to unintended treatment interruption when pregnancy is recognized.

articles.title: Transportation Noise and Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This narrative review examines transportation noise as a potentially modifiable cardiovascular exposure, emphasizing endothelial dysfunction, vascular inflammation, atherosclerotic disease, and prevention.

RECENT FINDINGS: Controlled human studies demonstrate acute endothelial dysfunction after nighttime transportation noise, while animal experiments support oxidative stress and vascular inflammation. Human FDG-PET/CT findings suggest a stress-arterial inflammatory pathway but remain observational. Structural imaging has not consistently linked noise to plaque burden or calcification progression. Cohorts and meta-analyses generally associate road-traffic noise with small increases in myocardial infarction and stroke, although broader ischemic heart disease estimates are less consistent. Overlapping populations, residual confounding, and exposure error limit causal interpretation. Mitigation can reduce acoustic exposure and improve some intermediate outcomes, but prevention of myocardial infarction or stroke has not been established. Evidence is most direct for acute vascular effects and more uncertain for chronic atherogenesis. Source-level noise mitigation has demonstrated benefits in reducing acoustic exposure and may also improve sleep and reduce noise-related annoyance. Serial plaque imaging and controlled natural experiments with prespecified cardiovascular outcomes are needed to test whether noise reduction prevents atherosclerotic events.

articles.title: Correction: An explainable machine learning-based prediction model for sarcopenia in elderly Chinese people with knee osteoarthritis.
Ultrasensitive Detection of Phospholipase C Using a Smartphone-Readable Paper Sensor Enabled by Ultrafast ATRP Signal Amplification.
articles.abstract: Phospholipase C (PLC) activity is closely related to bacterial pathogenicity and infection. A portable paper-based sensor with enhanced signal amplification was developed for the sensitive determination of PLC by integrating ultrafast atom transfer radical polymerization (UATRP) with smartphone colorimetric readout. First, the phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), which serves as a specific substrate for PLC, is attached to chitosan (CS) modified filter paper (FP) through glutaraldehyde (GA). After specific hydrolysis of PE by PLC, the generated phosphate groups were captured by Zr(IV), which further enabled the immobilization of tribromoacetic acid (TBA) as a multibrominated initiator. Under visible light irradiation, UATRP of methacrolein proceeded rapidly, generating abundant aldehyde-containing polymer chains on the paper surface within 10 min. Owing to the correspondence between PE and TBA, as well as the three bromine initiation sites on each TBA molecule, this strategy afforded nearly 300-fold signal amplification. The resulting aldehyde groups reacted with Schiff reagent to produce a purple-red signal, which was quantified using a smartphone. Under the optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a linear response toward PLC over the range of 1.0 × 100 to 1.0 × 105 mU/L, with a detection limit of 0.11 mU/L (S/N = 3). The proposed sensor also showed good selectivity, satisfactory reproducibility (RSD = 3.01%), and good stability. The recoveries obtained in spiked MCF-7 cell samples ranged from 96.60% to 100.43%, indicating promising applicability in complex biological matrices. This work provides a rapid and effective UATRP signal amplification strategy for portable and sensitive PLC detection.

articles.title: Time Scale Modeling of Disease Transmission: Implications to Swine Flu Dynamics.
articles.abstract: The choice of time scale can substantially influence observations and real-time data collected during infectious disease outbreaks. Models formulated without an appropriate time scale may produce inaccurate predictions of disease dynamics, potentially leading to misguided public health policies for outbreak prevention and control. In this study, we develop explicit and implicit time-scale models on h Z  , where h denotes the model time step. Using data collected during the 2009 H1N1 influenza pandemic, we identify an appropriate time scale and demonstrate that incorporating time-scale features enhances the models' ability to capture patterns in real-time infection data. We analyze the proposed models on general time scales, derive their basic reproduction numbers, and establish corresponding stability conditions. We further introduce a linearization technique for dynamic equations on general time scales and develop a second-generation matrix approach to address analytical challenges arising from the nonrecursive structure of implicit models. Global sensitivity analysis and data fitting demonstrate that the choice of time scale substantially affects both the epidemic peak size and its timing, highlighting the importance of incorporating time-scale features into infectious disease models.

articles.title: Swimming exercise alleviates memory impairment and anxiety-like behavior in a rat model of type 2 diabetes: association with hippocampal redox status and PGC-1α, BDNF and Sigma-1 receptor mRNA expression.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is frequently accompanied by cognitive decline. We investigated how swimming exercise affects behavior, hippocampal redox status and mRNA expression of inflammatory, apoptotic, mitochondrial and neurotrophic markers, including PGC-1α, BDNF and sigma-1 receptor (Sig-1R), in high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced T2DM rats. Male Wistar rats (n = 6/group) were assigned to Control, Diabetes, Exercise and Diabetes + Exercise groups. Exercised groups swam for 4 weeks (60 min day- 1, 5 days week- 1). Behavior was evaluated with the Open Field, Elevated Plus Maze and Morris Water Maze tests. Hippocampal MDA, SOD, TOS, TAC and gene expression (RT-qPCR) were measured; data were analyzed by two-way ANOVA. Compared with controls, sedentary diabetic rats showed impaired probe-trial memory, increased anxiety-like behavior, reduced locomotion, higher hippocampal MDA and TOS, lower SOD and TAC, higher NF-κB and Bax and lower Bcl-2, PGC-1α and Sig-1R mRNA expression (P < 0.05). Exercised diabetic rats showed lower MDA, TOS, NF-κB and Bax, higher SOD, TAC, Bcl-2, PGC-1α, BDNF and Sig-1R, and better scores in several anxiety-related and probe-trial memory measures than sedentary diabetic rats (P < 0.05). However, a significant diabetes × exercise interaction showed a larger exercise effect in diabetic rats only for serum insulin, EPM arm preference, MDA, NF-κB, Bax, PGC-1α and Sig-1R; for most other parameters, including probe-trial memory, exercise effects did not differ between diabetic and non-diabetic rats. Overall, regular swimming may be a promising non-pharmacological strategy against diabetes-associated hippocampal dysfunction.

articles.title: Early-life respiratory tract infections and childhood asthma risk: causal factor, risk marker, or modifiable target for asthma prevention?
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Early-life respiratory tract infections (RTIs) have repeatedly been associated with later childhood wheeze and asthma, but the interpretation of these associations remains complex. This review summarizes associative and mechanistic evidence linking early-life RTIs with asthma development, emphasizing infection severity and burden, lung function, allergic susceptibility, and preventive opportunities. We conducted a narrative review of evidence from cohort studies, registry-based studies, meta-analyses, and mechanistic literature examining associations between early-life upper RTIs (URTI) and lower RTIs (LRTI) and childhood asthma. We additionally considered evidence on lung function, allergic susceptibility, and potential interactions between respiratory infections and allergic airway disease; i.e., the two-hit hypothesis. The evidence linking early-life RTIs to later childhood asthma is strongest for LRTIs, particularly severe, physician-attended, or hospitalized episodes, including bronchiolitis, pneumonia, RSV-associated LRTI, and rhinovirus-associated wheezing illness. These infections are consistently linked to later wheeze, asthma, asthma-related morbidity, and impaired lung function. However, early-life RTIs may both contribute to asthma pathogenesis and identify children with pre-existing susceptibility, including reduced early lung function, genetic predisposition, or altered antiviral responses. Evidence for upper RTIs is less established, but frequent respiratory infections, particularly colds, have been associated with later asthma risk. Finally, the two-hit hypothesis suggests that children with both early-life RTIs and allergic sensitization or allergic airway disease may have a particularly high risk of developing asthma.

CONCLUSION: Early-life RTIs are important markers of asthma risk, but whether they represent modifiable targets for prevention remains uncertain. Future studies should integrate infection phenotyping with lung function, immune profiling, and allergic disease assessment to clarify causality and guide targeted preventive strategies.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Early-life respiratory tract infections (RTIs), particularly severe lower RTIs and respiratory syncytial virus- or rhinovirus-associated wheezing illnesses, are linked to the development of childhood asthma. • Whether these infections cause asthma or identify susceptible children remains uncertain.

WHAT IS NEW: • This review highlights that severe and repeated infections may contribute to the development of asthma while also revealing pre-existing structural, genetic, antiviral, or allergic susceptibility. • Potential two-hit interactions between RTIs and allergic airway disease suggest that prevention research should address both infection burden and host susceptibility.

articles.title: Generation and characterization of a Golden Gate-rescued HCoV-OC43 strain with enhanced replication and neurovirulence in neonatal mice.
articles.abstract: Human coronavirus OC43 (HCoV-OC43) is a seasonal betacoronavirus with established neurotropic properties and is widely used as a model for coronavirus research under biosafety level 2 conditions. Although mouse-adapted HCoV-OC43 strains have been described, further genetic and phenotypic characterization of recombinant strains may improve their utility as research models. In this study, we generated a recombinant HCoV-OC43-P9 strain (rOC43-P9) using a Golden Gate-based reverse genetics approach and characterized its replication properties in cell culture and neonatal C57BL/6 mice. Compared with OC43-1558, rOC43-P9 generally produced higher infectious virus titers in the cell lines examined. Following intracranial inoculation, both viruses caused severe disease in neonatal mice, with no significant difference in survival between the infected groups, although higher infectious virus titers were detected in the brains of rOC43-P9-infected mice at selected time points. Following intranasal inoculation, rOC43-P9 was associated with earlier detection of infectious virus in brain tissues and more rapid disease progression than OC43-1558. Viral antigen and mild histopathological changes were also observed in lung tissues, although productive pulmonary infection was not established. These findings provide further phenotypic characterization of recombinant HCoV-OC43-P9 and support its potential utility as a research model for coronavirus-associated central nervous system infection.

articles.title: A Multicenter Survey of Palliative Care Services and Characteristics of End-of-Life Involvement Across Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Units.
authors: Collaborative Research from the Pediatric Cardiac Intensive Care Society (CoRe-PCICS) Investigators
articles.abstract: Most children with congenital and acquired heart disease who die do so in intensive care settings. Although palliative care (PC) improves pain, suffering, and quality of life for seriously ill children, its integration within pediatric heart centers remains inadequately characterized. We conducted a multicenter survey of 31 U.S. pediatric heart centers to evaluate current PC delivery, including application of PC principles; models of integration, including subspecialty team involvement; bereavement support; and education and training practices. Palliative care services and principles were widely available; however, programmatic integration was inconsistent. Respondents estimated that initial advance care planning discussions often occurred late in the disease course. Most centers (58%) reported that additional PC training occurs only when clinicians independently seek it. The most frequently cited barrier to integration was the perception that PC is reserved for end-of-life care or when curative options have been exhausted. Bereavement support also varied: 58% of centers reported hospital-level bereavement programs, whereas only 26% had bereavement needs assessment and follow-up embedded within the heart center for families of children who died in the CICU. These findings demonstrate substantial variability in PC integration and highlight the need for more systematic approaches to improve the quality of life for children with advanced heart disease and their families.

articles.title: School Readiness and Early Learning in Young Children with Critical Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract: Despite evidence for developmental problems in children with critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), we know little about their readiness to learn at early school age. The objective of this study was to examine school readiness in children with CCHD compared to a community control (CC) group. Hypotheses were that the CCHD group would have more problems in readiness than the CC group and that these problems would be associated with lower scores on achievement testing. Children (35 CCHD and 46 CC) who were originally assessed prior to school entry were reassessed at ages 5 to 7 years while in kindergarten or first grade. Readiness was measured using tests of readiness skills and caregiver ratings of developmental milestones. Achievement testing examined math, reading, and spelling skills. Analyses controlling for sex at birth and social risk examined group differences and associations of the readiness measures with achievement. The CCHD group had significant weaknesses relative to the CC group on nearly all readiness and achievement measures. Analysis controlling for the same or similar readiness measures from a previous assessment conducted prior to school entry (age 4-5 years) suggested cross-age stability in readiness problems in the CCHD group. Weaknesses in readiness were associated with lower achievement scores. The findings confirm readiness problems in children with CCHD at early school age accompanied by weaknesses in academic achievement. Results highlight areas of readiness most likely to be compromised, reveal factors related to variability in readiness, and underscore the need for developmental screening prior to or soon after school entry.

articles.title: Retinal dehydrogenase 1, a novel interacting partner to influenza A virus nucleoprotein.
articles.abstract: Influenza A virus is known to manipulate host metabolic processes. Earlier, we reported differential expression of cellular retinal dehydrogenase 1 (RALDH1) in cells expressing recombinant influenza A virus nucleoprotein. Here, the interaction of virus nucleoprotein and RALDH1, an enzyme involved in retinoic acid synthesis, was investigated. Additionally, the relationship between virus nucleoprotein and the retinoic acid inducible gene (RIG-I) and RALDH1 was also evaluated. Our study demonstrated a novel interaction between host RALDH1 and virus nucleoprotein with a correlation between RALDH1 and RIG-I expression, an antiviral host response factor. This is a preliminary report; studies are ongoing to elucidate the interplay between RALDH1 and the virus nucleoprotein in the regulation of RIG-I during infection.

articles.title: The role of Cbl-b: relationship between cancer and infectious disease.
articles.abstract: Casitas B-cell lymphoma-b protein (Cbl-b) is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that negatively regulates signaling pathways. Although it is involved in the maintenance of immune homeostasis, Cbl-b may also be exploited by tumors or pathogens, leading to immune evasion and persistent infection. In recent years, the role of Cbl-b in tumor immunotherapy has been progressively elucidated, with related Cbl-b inhibitors (such as NX-1607) advancing into clinical trials. It has also been found that Cbl-b inhibition or knockout enhances host immune responses in infection models, such as lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) and Candida albicans infection models. Consequently, Cbl-b-targeting strategies hold promise as potent adjuncts to infectious disease treatments, particularly when combined with therapeutic vaccines or other immune-enhancing therapies. Given the immunological parallels between infection and tumorigenesis, this review examines the immunoregulatory role of Cbl-b in both contexts and compares their similarities and differences. Additionally, this review summarizes currently available mainstream Cbl-b-targeting strategies to provide new insights for the application of Cbl-b in immunotherapy for infectious diseases.

articles.title: [Distal prosthetic joint replacement in periprosthetic distal femoral fractures].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of distal femur replacement is to treat a periprosthetic distal femoral fracture that can no longer be managed with plate osteosynthesis. Reasons for this can include a large bony defect or a loose prosthesis. The goal is to achieve early, pain-adapted full weight-bearing, rapid mobilization and the restoration of independence.

INDICATIONS: Distal femoral fractures with a loosened endoprosthesis (Lewis-Rorabeck type III), displaced, complex fractures with a stable prosthesis (type II), large metaphyseal or epiphyseal defect zones, failure of osteosynthesis, severe osteoporosis with anticipated loosening following osteosynthesis, geriatric patient population.

CONTRAINDICATIONS: Acute or chronic periprosthetic infection; severe medical comorbidities that preclude major surgical intervention.

SURGICAL TECHNIQUE: The procedure is performed via a medial parapatellar and/or subvastus approach. After exposure, the distal femur is resected depending on the fracture level and bone quality. The medullary canal is then prepared for cemented or cementless stems. This is followed by the modular assembly of the distal femoral prosthesis with the implantation of the tibial prosthetic components. The femoral and tibial components can then be implanted and coupled (rotational or hinged joint). Finally, the soft tissues are closed.

POSTOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT: Early mobilization with possible full weight-bearing starting on the first postoperative day. Regular wound checks; removal of the drainage tube after 24-48 h. Standardized thrombosis prophylaxis based on pre-existing conditions. Analgesia according to WHO grades I-III. Support for mobilization using forearm crutches until the second or third postoperative week.

RESULTS: In a retrospective cohort of 24 patients, the complication rate was 37.5%, with a revision rate of 29.1%. The most common complication was aseptic loosening, which occurred in 20.8% of patients. Despite the high complication rate, distal femoral replacement enables early mobilization with good functional reconstruction and represents an effective treatment option for complex fractures.

articles.title: Prediction of PD-L1 status and characterization of tumor subtype in NSCLC with static and abbreviated dynamic LAFOV [18F]FDG PET.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to assess the potential of abbreviated dynamic [18F]FDG PET imaging using a long axial field-of-view (LAFOV) scanner for non-invasive characterization of tumor subtypes and prediction of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) status in treatment-naïve patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

METHODS: 51 treatment-naïve patients with histologically confirmed NSCLC (34 adenocarcinomas [LUAD], 17 squamous cell carcinomas [LUSC]) underwent a 20-min dynamic [18F]FDG PET/CT acquisition starting 45-min post-injection on an LAFOV system. Parametric images of net influx rate (Ki) and distribution volume (DV) were reconstructed using a direct Patlak approach with patient-specific scaled population-based input functions. PD-L1 tumor proportion score was determined from one histopathologically sampled lesion per patient.

RESULTS: PD-L1 positive lesions demonstrated higher SUVmax (16.9 ± 9.6 vs. 11.6 ± 5.7; p = 0.04), Kimax (0.077 ± 0.04 vs. 0.054 ± 0.02; p = 0.03), and DVmax (428.7 ± 253.5 vs. 278.7 ± 145.2; p = 0.02) than PD-L1 negative lesions. LUSC lesions showed higher SUVmax (18.7 ± 8.5 vs. 12.9 ± 8.2; p = 0.008) and Kimax (0.08 ± 0.02 vs. 0.06 ± 0.04; p = 0.02) than LUAD lesions, whereas DVmax did not differ (p = 0.69). In the histopathology-matched LUAD analysis, apparent/optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.74/0.70 for SUVmax/Kimax, 0.71/0.67 for Kimax/DVmax, and 0.75/0.71 for SUVmax/SUVpeak, without evidence of superior discrimination by any model.

CONCLUSION: PD-L1 prediction using both static and kinetic [18F]FDG PET parameters was feasible in NSCLC, with comparable performance between SUV- and parametric-based metrics, without evidence of superior discrimination by any model. These preliminary findings require validation in larger independent cohorts. Abbreviated dynamic LAFOV PET/CT enables whole-body assessment of tumor glucose kinetics in a clinically practical protocol.

articles.title: Performance of LI-RADS to diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma in patients presenting with locally advanced liver disease on CT or MRI.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the diagnostic performance of LI-RADS version 2018 in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) presenting with locally advanced intrahepatic tumor burden on CT or MRI.

METHODS: This retrospective study included consecutive CT and MRI exams containing liver lesions from January 1, 2013-December 30, 2022, of patients at high risk for HCC. CT and MRI exams were reviewed independently by eight radiologists who assigned a LI-RADS category to the largest lesion. Pathology served as the exam-level reference standard for HCC diagnosis. Positive predictive value (PPV), sensitivity, and specificity of the LR-5 (definitely HCC) category and combined LR-5 and LR-TIV (tumor in vein) "definitely due to HCC" categories to determine HCC diagnosis were calculated.

RESULTS: In 408 patients (340 [83%] men, mean age, 66 years ± 9.6) with 472 exams, 328 (80%) patients had HCC. The PPV for LR-5 alone was 95% (95% CI: 92-99%), with high specificity of 90% (95% CI: 84-97%) and low sensitivity of 48% (95% CI: 43-54%). The PPV of the combined categories was 96% (95% CI: 93-98%), with moderate specificity of 86% (95% CI: 78-94%) and moderate sensitivity of 77% (95% CI: 73-82%). Inter-reader agreement was substantial for LR-5 alone (κ = 0.71 [95% CI: 0.57-0.84]) and moderate for the combined categories (κ = 0.58 [95% CI: 0.40-0.73]).

CONCLUSION: Findings in this selected pathology-confirmed cohort support the potential role of imaging-based diagnosis in this setting. Further research in broader, unselected clinical populations is warranted.

articles.title: Navigating equivocal PI-RADS category 3 prostate MRI with risk-based stratification.
articles.abstract: PI-RADS v2.1 category 3 on prostate MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) represents an intermediate risk category imaging phenotype rather than a uniform clinical risk category contributing to the dilemma in biopsy decision-making. Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is found in a minority of PI-RADS 3 lesions, yet interobserver agreement is moderate and benign mimics, such as stromal BPH nodules and focal prostatitis are common, so a simple binary interpretation of biopsy versus no biopsy (biopsy avoidance) is inadequate. This review proposes a two-step approach. Step 1 is to confirm that the lesion is truly PI-RADS 3 by addressing image quality (PI-QUAL v2), interpretative variability, and overcall or undercall. Step 2 is to apply clinical risk stratification, in which PSA density (PSAD), treated as a continuum rather than a single cutoff is the most validated modifier, supplemented by biopsy history, PSA kinetics, family history and lesion-level imaging features. Selected low-risk patients can safely avoid immediate biopsy under a structured safety-net surveillance pathway, whereas patients with higher post-MRI risk should undergo targeted sampling with perilesional or systematic cores as appropriate. Population-specific baseline risk, including the higher csPCa prevalence and lower MRI negative predictive value reported in Black men, may alter pathway performance, although validated race-specific thresholds remain uncertain. Emerging tools, including serum and urine biomarkers, quantitative MRI and artificial intelligence, and PSMA PET with the PRIMARY score, may refine this pathway but require different levels of validation before routine use.

articles.title: Reperfusion status and clinical outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the association between reperfusion status assessed by expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade and clinical outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery (MCA) M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patient data were pooled from five randomized controlled trials and a cohort study. Patients with MCA M2 occlusion undergoing EVT were stratified into 3 groups (eTICI 0-2a, eTICI 2b-2c, and eTICI 3). The primary effectiveness outcome was modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. Secondary effectiveness outcomes included 90-day mRS score 0-1, 0-3, and ordinal mRS score distribution. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 48 h. Multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) were performed.

RESULTS: Among 599 patients, 308 achieved eTICI 3 reperfusion. Compared with eTICI 0-2a, eTICI 3 was significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-2 in both the adjusted (aOR, 2.94; 95% CI, 1.54-5.60; p = 0.001) and the IPTW model (aOR, 3.49; 95% CI, 2.30-5.30; p < 0.001). eTICI 2b-2c was also associated with higher odds of 90-day mRS 0-2. Similar trends were observed for secondary effectiveness outcomes. After IPTW, eTICI 3 was associated with lower rates of mortality (p < 0.001) and sICH within 48 h (p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with MCA M2 occlusion undergoing EVT, eTICI 3 reperfusion was associated with better functional outcomes. However, the safety of achieving eTICI 3 reperfusion in this population needs further validation.

KEY POINTS: Question How is the degree of reperfusion achieved after endovascular treatment associated with 90-day functional outcomes in patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion? Findings In 599 patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion, eTICI 3 was associated with functional independence, whereas associations with mortality and intracranial hemorrhage were less consistent across analytical models. Clinical relevance Among patients with middle cerebral artery M2 occlusion undergoing endovascular treatment, eTICI 3 reperfusion was associated with better functional outcome. The association may inform postprocedural assessment, but the benefit of an additional attempt to achieve eTICI 3 reperfusion needs further study.

articles.title: A plaque heterogeneity score derived from high-resolution vessel wall imaging for identifying stroke-associated vulnerable carotid plaques.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To quantitatively characterize plaque heterogeneity using high-resolution vessel wall imaging (HR-VWI) and to investigate the value of this heterogeneity marker in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques associated with stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 423 carotid plaques in 341 patients from three medical centers between June 2018 and June 2024 using contrast-enhanced T1-weighted HR-VWI. Plaque voxels were clustered via a Gaussian mixture model, and the spatial distribution patterns of subregions were integrated to compute the plaque heterogeneity score (PHS). A multivariable discriminative model was developed to identify stroke-associated plaques. An age-stratified analysis was further performed to assess the consistency of model performance across age subgroups.

RESULTS: Plaques from Center 1 were divided into training (n = 168) and internal validation (n = 72) sets, while Centers 2 (n = 73) and 3 (n = 110) served as external validation cohorts. The integrated model (graphically represented as a nomogram) demonstrated excellent discriminative performance across all datasets, with areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.849-0.865. The model maintained robust discriminative accuracy across age subgroups, with a maximum intergroup AUC difference of 0.041. PHS showed significant incremental discriminative ability (ΔAUC: 0.080-0.112; IDI: 0.089-0.138; all p < 0.05) beyond conventional vulnerability and burden assessments. In external validation set 1, adding PHS to Plaque-RADS improved discrimination (ΔAUC: 0.134; IDI: 0.143; both p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The PHS effectively quantifies carotid plaque heterogeneity and provides significant incremental value for identifying stroke-associated plaques when integrated with conventional metrics. This interpretable framework holds promise for future clinical translation.

KEY POINTS: Question Current identification of stroke-associated carotid plaques relies on qualitative plaque assessment, which is operator-dependent and lacks quantitative measures of plaque heterogeneity. Findings The plaque heterogeneity score independently identified stroke-associated carotid plaques; combined with conventional metrics, it achieved areas under the curve of 0.849-0.865 across multicenter cohorts. Clinical relevance Integrating the plaque heterogeneity score with conventional assessment improves identification of stroke-associated vulnerable carotid plaques, supporting individualized risk stratification and timely preventive decisions in patients with carotid atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Serum lipid profile and obstetric outcome in women infected with HIV on antiretroviral therapy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) is known to alter lipid metabolism but effectively reduce the risk of mother-to-child transmission. As HIV infection and pregnancy itself lead to an increase in serum lipid levels, pregnant women receiving ART drugs are at risk for dyslipidemia and consequently may face short- and long-term health issues. This study aims at assessing the influence of ART, in particular tenofovir disoproxil (TDF), on maternal lipid concentrations and related obstetric outcome.

METHODS: This is a retrospective, exploratory real-world data analysis of pregnancies in women with HIV infection treated at the study center between 2005 and 2024. Serum concentrations of total cholesterol (TC), triglycerides (TG), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) were collected at five timepoints (preconception; first, second, third trimesters; postpartum) and compared to reference ranges of healthy pregnant women.

RESULTS: 144 pregnancies of 93 women were included. In 66.0% of pregnancies (n = 95), women received ART containing TDF, and in 24.3% (n = 35) non-TDF drugs (missing data 9.7%, n = 14). Serum lipid levels increased throughout pregnancy but stayed within reference ranges. TC, TG and LDL levels were lower than the corresponding values reported for healthy pregnant women in an external reference cohort. Compared to non-TDF-based ART, TDF-based ART was associated with lower TC (beta [95% CI] = - 0.28 [ - 0.54 to - 0.02], p = 0.036; 127 pregnancies) and HDL (beta [95% CI] = - 0.15 [ - 0.28 to - 0.02], p = 0.024; 97 pregnancies) levels. For TG (beta [95% CI] = - 0.13 [ - 0.33 to 0.08], p = 0.229; 128 pregnancies) and LDL (beta [95% CI] = - 0.09 [ - 0.37 to 0.19], p = 0.518; 97 pregnancies), no statistically significant associations were observed. After adjustment for calendar period (2005-2011 vs. 2012-2024), TDF-based ART remained associated with lower HDL levels (beta [95% CI] = - 0.14 [- 0.27 to - 0.01], p = 0.032; 97 pregnancies), whereas the association with TC was attenuated and no longer statistically significant. No associations with birthweight and gestational age at childbirth were detected.

CONCLUSION: TDF-based ART was associated with lower HDL levels compared to non-TDF therapy, without an observed effect on pregnancy outcome. Further analyses are required to evaluate the association of ART and maternal and offspring long-term cardiovascular health.

articles.title: Outpatient anti-seizure medication tapering following status epilepticus: Clinical predictors and seizure outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Management of anti-seizure medications (ASMs) after hospitalization for status epilepticus (SE) is poorly defined, particularly regarding outpatient tapering. We aimed to identify factors associated with ASM tapering and compare seizure recurrence between early and late taper strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study of adults hospitalized for SE between 2011 and 2021 with at least 1 year of outpatient follow-up. Statistical analyses included Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable logistic regression to evaluate factors associated with ASM tapering within 1-2 years and seizure recurrence.

RESULTS: Among 282 patients (mean age 55 ± 18 years; 47% female), 37.9% underwent outpatient ASM tapering, of whom 83.7% remained seizure-free for at least 6 months. Early tapering (≤1 year) was associated with higher seizure recurrence compared with late tapering (>1 year) (28.2% vs. 2.7%, p < 0.001). None of eight patients tapered after 2 years experienced recurrence within 6 months. Nonconvulsive SE (odds ratio [OR] 2.21 [1.28-3.84], p = 0.005) and acute symptomatic SE (OR 1.79 [1.01-3.16], p = 0.045) were independently associated with tapering. Most patients who tapered (73.8%) had short SE duration (≤1 day). Acute symptomatic SE was associated with lower 6-months seizure recurrence Odds, approaching significance (adjusted OR 0.27 [0.07-1.03], p = 0.055). Longer SE duration (6-10 days vs. <1 day) was associated with higher odds of recurrence in univariable but not multivariable analysis. SE etiology, number of prehospital ASMs, comorbidities, and outpatient EEG completion were not associated with tapering or recurrence.

SIGNIFICANCE: Despite a relatively low seizure recurrence rate, fewer than 40% of patients underwent ASM tapering. These findings suggest supervised tapering may be reasonable beginning 1 year after SE, particularly in patients with shorter SE duration. Prospective studies are needed to refine tapering strategies.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We reviewed 10 years of medical records from 282 adults hospitalized with status epilepticus to examine when anti-seizure medications were reduced and whether seizures returned. Fewer than 40% had their medications tapered, and most remained seizure-free for at least 6 months. Seizures were more likely to return when medications were reduced within 1 year of hospitalization and less likely following status epilepticus caused by an identifiable trigger, such as a stroke, infection, metabolic disturbance, or missed medication. These findings may help clinicians and patients make more informed decisions about whether and when to reduce anti-seizure medications after status epilepticus.

articles.title: High-PEEP ventilation is associated with pulmonary injury, inflammatory changes, and hippocampal cellular alterations after experimental ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) frequently require mechanical ventilation during intensive care. Although experimental evidence suggests that injurious ventilation may amplify neuroinflammation, the effects of different ventilatory strategies on blood-brain barrier (BBB)-related molecular markers and glial responses after AIS remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that increasing levels of positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) would modulate cerebral inflammation after AIS and would be associated with BBB alterations, glial remodeling, and hippocampal injury.

METHODS: Twenty-four male Wistar rats were subjected to focal AIS induced by thermocoagulation of pial vessels. After 24 h, the animals were mechanically ventilated for 2 h as follows: tidal volume, 6 mL/kg; FiO2, 0.25 at different PEEP levels (3 cmH2O, 9 cmH2O, or 11 cmH2O). Arterial blood gases, mean arterial pressure (MAP) and lung mechanics were assessed at baseline and at the end of ventilation. Plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, lungs, and brains were collected for molecular, histologic, and immunohistochemical analyses.

RESULTS: MAP did not differ among groups throughout the experiment. PEEP 11 cmH₂O resulted in higher transpulmonary peak and plateau pressures than the lower-PEEP groups and in higher transpulmonary driving pressure, particularly compared with PEEP 3 cmH₂O. Higher PEEP was associated with increased pulmonary inflammation, endothelial injury markers, and alveolar heterogeneity. In plasma, circulating interleukin (IL)-1β (p = 0.014) and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α (p = 0.011) were higher in the PEEP 11 cmH2O group compared with PEEP 3 cmH2O group. In the brain, high PEEP increased cerebral IL-1β and TNF-α, reduced ZO-1 expression, and lowered hippocampal neuronal density. Morphometric analysis further demonstrated astrocytic and microglial remodeling within the hippocampus. MAP did not associate with cerebral biomarkers, while PEEP showed a positive correlation with cerebral TNF-α expression (r = 0.56, p = 0.02).

CONCLUSION: High-PEEP ventilation intensified pulmonary and cerebral inflammatory responses after experimental AIS and was associated with reduced expression of a key BBB junctional protein, glial remodeling, and reduced hippocampal NeuN-positive neuronal density.

articles.title: Thrombosis in cardio-oncology: different studies, a common call for individualised care.
Interpreting elevated cerebrospinal fluid erythritol: biomarker, mediator, or both?
articles.abstract: We comment on the recent Mendelian randomization study by Wei et al., which reported an association between genetically proxied cerebrospinal fluid erythritol and unfavorable ischemic stroke prognosis. We highlight that erythritol originates not only from dietary intake but also from endogenous production via the pentose phosphate pathway, complicating the interpretation of cerebrospinal fluid erythritol levels. We further discuss emerging mechanistic evidence linking erythritol to platelet activation and endothelial dysfunction and propose that erythritol may represent a biomarker of metabolic stress, a mediator of vascular injury, or both. Clarifying these mechanisms may improve the interpretation of metabolomic findings in cerebrovascular disease and guide future mechanistic and clinical investigations.

articles.title: Dual Functional Cure in HBV/HIV-1 Co-infection: A Narrative Review for Critical Appraisal of Current Evidence and Conceptual Framework.
articles.abstract: The syndemic of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) affects millions of people worldwide. Each virus exacerbates the pathogenesis of the other, leading to accelerated liver disease and increased mortality. While combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) suppresses both viruses, it rarely achieves a functional cure, which is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance for HBV and durable cART-free remission for HIV-1, due to persistent viral reservoirs (covalently closed circular DNA for HBV and integrated proviral DNA for HIV-1). Recent parallel advances in HBV and HIV-1 cure research have generated considerable interest in a "dual functional cure". In this review, we critically evaluate whether current evidence supports such a concept. We first summarize the epidemiology of HBV/HIV-1 coinfection, and then outline coinfection‑specific barriers and opportunities that distinguish a dual cure from a simple superposition of two single‑disease strategies. Next, we compare major cure strategies (interferon‑based, immune checkpoint blockade, Toll‑like receptor agonists, broadly neutralizing antibodies, gene editing, and latency targeting) in terms of evidence level in monoinfection versus coinfection, safety concerns, and translational barriers. Finally, we propose a sequential, personalized framework as a hypothesis‑generating tool, emphasizing that most steps remain extrapolations requiring dedicated coinfection trials. We conclude by defining actionable research priorities, including patient selection criteria, end point choices, and management of hepatitis flares.

articles.title: Real-World Maribavir Treatment Patterns and Effectiveness in Refractory Cytomegalovirus After Transplantation: Findings from the US CMV OMNI-PLATFORM Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Here, results from the real-world cytomegalovirus (CMV) OMNI-PLATFORM study that assessed treatment patterns and outcomes with maribavir and other anti-CMV treatments for post-transplant CMV infections across a US population are presented.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study used a novel approach to assess electronic medical records and clinical notes from solid organ transplant (SOT) and hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients across four US transplant centers (November 2021-June 2025). Eligible patients had a diagnosis of CMV infection post-transplant and received anti-CMV treatment. Patients were followed from 3 months prior to transplant until the end of the study period. All anti-CMV treatments were characterized as lines of treatment (LOTs). Primary outcomes were treatment success (composite outcome reflecting real-world testing and treatment patterns) and maintenance of treatment success (no re-initiation of anti-CMV treatment for 4 weeks after treatment success). Treatment and switching patterns were also assessed.

RESULTS: The overall cohort included 1299 patients (91.4% SOT, 8.6% HCT). Most SOT recipients had undergone kidney transplant (57.8%). The mean age of patients was 52.9 years, 40.3% were female, and the median (interquartile range) time from transplant to CMV infection was 108.0 (37.0-200.0) days. The most frequently reported first-line (LOT 1) monotherapy was valganciclovir (1044/1291 [80.9%]). Most treatment switches to maribavir in LOT 2 were observed after intolerance to previous anti-CMV treatment (41/46 [89.1%]). In a subanalysis of 130 instances of maribavir use across all LOTs in SOT recipients aged ≥ 12 years, 98 (75.4%) instances met the composite definition of treatment success and 83/98 (84.7%) had maintenance of treatment success.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-transplant CMV treatment patterns are complex and often involve switching treatments due to refractoriness and/or intolerance to prior treatments. Maribavir demonstrated high treatment success in a subgroup of SOT recipients, supporting its effectiveness in routine clinical practice and informing real-world CMV treatment strategies.

articles.title: The Safety and Efficacy of Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir/Voxilaprevir in Patients with Chronic Hepatitis C who Failed Prior Directly Acting Antivirals: A Nationwide Multicenter Study in Taiwan.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Although direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) achieve high cure rates in patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, a subset of patients fail first-line DAA therapy. This post-authorization study aimed to evaluate the real-world safety and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir (SOF/VEL/VOX) in a DAA-experienced population.

METHODS: A total of 116 DAA-experienced patients who received 12 weeks of SOF/VEL/VOX between 2021 and 2024 were enrolled retrospectively and prospectively from 15 sites in Taiwan. The primary objective was to assess safety, including adverse events (AEs), serious adverse events (SAEs), adverse drug reactions (ADRs), serious adverse drug reactions (SADRs), and drug-induced liver injury (DILI); the secondary objective was the sustained virological response (SVR12).

RESULTS: Of the 116 patients (Full Analysis Set), the most common prior DAA failures were glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (31.9%) and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (29.3%). The SVR12 rate was 98.1% (105/107) in the modified full analysis set, with 100% efficacy observed in subgroups with cirrhosis, HBV/HCV coinfection, HIV/HCV coinfection, and those with a history of liver transplantation. Regarding safety, 44.8% of patients experienced at least one AE, although 97.5% of these events were nonserious. The incidence rate of any AE was 2.0 events per person-year (95% confidence interval: 1.5-2.7). The most common AEs included gastrointestinal disorders (28.4%) and infections (12.1%). No cases of DILI, hyperbilirubinemia, SADRs, or treatment-related SAEs occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: Twelve weeks of SOF/VEL/VOX is highly effective and well-tolerated as retreatment for chronic hepatitis C after prior DAA failure, with no new safety concerns identified.

articles.title: Rapid Molecular Diagnostics and the "Cost of Wait": An Expert Opinion on Clinical Excellence and Economic Sustainability in the Era of Rising Antimicrobial Resistance.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) was associated with an estimated 4.71 million deaths in 2021, and direct healthcare costs attributable to AMR are projected to reach US$159 billion/year by 2050. Reliance on culture-based diagnostics, which require 48-72 h for pathogen identification and susceptibility testing, contributes to a "cost of wait", characterized by prolonged empirical broad-spectrum therapy and potentially worse outcomes.

METHODS: This expert opinion is based on four interactive in-person sessions of the 6th Middle East, North Africa, and Commonwealth of Independent States (MENA/CIS) Xpert Champions' Club (2025), in which infectious disease specialists, clinical microbiologists, and health economists from six Gulf Cooperation Council countries discussed the clinical, economic, and policy role of rapid molecular diagnostics (RMD), with emphasis on the Gulf region. Session transcripts were analyzed thematically, and the panel's perspectives were contextualized with literature identified through a targeted search.

RESULTS: The panel considered the integration of RMD with antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs) a clinical priority. Meta-analyses in bloodstream infection suggest that this combination is associated with lower mortality and shorter time to optimal therapy, whereas RMD without stewardship show little survival benefit. Economic evaluations, largely model-based and conducted outside the region, suggest that RMD combined with ASPs is likely to be cost-effective, although results depend on test volume and setting. RMD complement rather than replace culture and phenotypic susceptibility testing and are limited by panel coverage, specimen quality, and the inability to distinguish colonization from infection. The panel identified settings in which RMD are most likely to add value: time-critical inpatient care, admission screening for multidrug-resistant organisms, intrapartum testing of women with unknown group B Streptococcus (GBS) status, and initial testing for tuberculosis (TB), within a One Health policy framework.

CONCLUSIONS: When targeted to appropriate settings and embedded in stewardship, RMD may improve clinical outcomes and support value-based healthcare in the Gulf region. Region-specific studies of clinical impact and cost-effectiveness are needed.

articles.title: Examining the Feasibility of a Co-designed Digital Health Platform for Preventing Stroke.
articles.abstract: The Love Your Brain (LYB) digital health platform was developed to improve the knowledge of stroke risk factors and promote healthy behaviors to prevent stroke. We aimed to examine the feasibility and exploratory outcomes of the LYB digital health platform. A mixed methods feasibility evaluation was conducted. Individuals aged ≥ 18 years, with internet access and no history of stroke, were recruited through StrokeSafe programs across Australia. Participants were randomized (1:1:1) to a massive open online course (MOOC), a text message, or control, with stratification by age and sex. Primary outcomes included feasibility of trial procedures (recruitment, retention and data completeness), intervention fidelity, engagement, and acceptability of the digital platform. Exploratory outcomes comprised stroke knowledge and self-reported healthy behaviors assessed at baseline and 12-week follow-up. Qualitative data were obtained from interviews with purposively selected participants from each arm (n = 3), StrokeSafe presenters (n = 5), and free-text responses (n = 42) from the satisfaction survey. Quantitative descriptive statistics and qualitative thematic analysis were integrated using a weaving approach and presented visually through joint display tables. Between April and July 2024, 53 individuals were screened, of whom 43 (81.1%) were eligible and 31 (72.1% of eligible individuals) were randomized, representing 20.7% of the planned sample size. Retention at 12 weeks was 77.4% (24/31), with data completeness ranging from 71.0% to 77.4% across outcome measures. In the MOOC group, 6/9 (66.7%) participants initiated the intervention, of whom four completed all required modules (44.4% of those allocated to the MOOC group). Engagement with the MOOC was limited, with 71.4% of participants reporting that they stopped engaging with the course at some point during the intervention period. In the text message group, 247 SMS were sent as scheduled, with no delivery failures or opt-outs. Acceptability was generally positive overall, although responses were mixed among MOOC participants. Exploratory analyses suggested improvements in stroke knowledge among participants with follow-up data. Qualitative findings indicated that the trial procedures were straightforward; however, barriers to recruitment through StrokeSafe presentations were identified, including time limitations, recruitment materials that lacked emotional appeal, and challenges associated with digital enrollment, providing potential explanations for the recruitment shortfall. This feasibility study identified strengths and challenges in implementing the LYB digital health platform. Findings support refinement of recruitment procedures, participant engagement strategies, and intervention delivery processes before progression to a larger trial.Trial registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry: ACTRN12624000540516.

articles.title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Bacteroides fragilis Cell-Free Supernatants Favor Apoptosis with Limited Necrosis in A549 Lung Cancer Cells.
articles.abstract: Bacterial cells and their secreted products can influence inflammatory signaling and cellular fate in cancer cells. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Bacteroides fragilis bacterial suspensions and their cell-free supernatants (CFSs) in A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Treatment conditions-bacterial suspensions at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 20 or CFSs at a final concentration of 50% (v/v)-were selected using the MTT reduction assay as a measure of cellular metabolic activity. Cytokine and Toll-like receptor/IKK-associated gene expression was assessed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction after 24 and 48 h, alongside NOS2 and ARG1, which encode enzymes involved in nitric oxide synthesis from L-arginine and an alternative route of L-arginine utilization, respectively. Phosphorylated nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) p65 abundance relative to β-actin was measured by Western blotting. Extracellular nitrite levels and apoptosis/necrosis were evaluated using the Griess assay and Annexin V-fluorescein isothiocyanate/propidium iodide flow cytometry, respectively. All assays were performed in three independent experiments. Responses depended on bacterial species, treatment form, and exposure duration. L. plantarum bacterial treatment showed comparatively stronger early attenuation of pro-inflammatory gene expression. Mixed CFSs shifted from early inflammatory and regulatory transcription toward reduced IL6, TNF, and CXCL8 expression after 48 h. Bacterial suspensions reduced the phosphorylated NF-κB p65/β-actin ratio, with the greatest reduction following mixed bacterial treatment, whereas B. fragilis CFS produced the strongest reduction among the CFSs. Changes in NOS2 and ARG1 expression were not consistently paralleled by extracellular nitrite levels. Among the evaluated treatments, mixed CFSs produced the lowest proportion of viable cells (68%) and the highest proportions of early (20%) and late apoptotic /secondary necrotic cells (8%), while necrosis remained minimal (1%). Overall, the mixed CFSs elicited predominantly apoptotic cell death with limited necrosis in A549 cells under the conditions tested. Their effects on pro-inflammatory gene expression were time-dependent, with lower IL6, TNF, and CXCL8 expression than either individual CFS at 48 h.

articles.title: Development and validation of a multimodal prediction model incorporating ultrasound-based deep learning and novel serum biomarkers for ovarian tumor diagnosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ovarian tumors are the most prevalent tumor types in the female reproductive system, with ovarian cancer being a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women. Ultrasound and serological tests are commonly used for detecting ovarian tumors in clinical diagnosis. The aims of this study were to utilize deep learning (DL) to extract features from ultrasound (US) images of ovarian tumors and establish an auxiliary diagnosis model based on these images. Additionally, proteomic analysis of the serum from different patient groups was conducted to identify new molecular markers. The combination of serum molecular markers and the DL diagnosis model based on US images was used to construct a new diagnosis and differential diagnosis system for ovarian tumors, providing novel approaches for the early screening and follow-up monitoring of ovarian tumors.

METHODS: The imaging cohort included 916 patients (679 development and 237 test patients; 1319 ultrasound images obtained by transabdominal and transvaginal scanning). A separate cohort of 66 patients underwent targeted serum ELISA and multimodal assessment. Five independently seeded patient-level random training/test partitions were used for internal evaluation. The binary task included 53 benign or malignant patients, and the three-class task included all 66 patients.

RESULTS: In the imaging study, the reported image-based test-set class-specific accuracies were 89.4%, 89.8%, and 91.3% for benign, borderline, and malignant tumors, respectively. In the serum cohort, five random held-out tests yielded binary mean patient-level accuracy of 66.2% ± 3.5% for DL and 83.1% ± 7.5% for clinical data + DL + LRRFIP1. Three-class mean accuracy was 62.1% ± 5.6% for DL and 66.5% ± 7.5% for the all-marker model. A separate patient-level ROC analysis gave binary AUC 0.883 (95% CI 0.783 to 0.964) for LRRFIP1 fusion and three-class macro-AUC 0.744 (0.655 to 0.831) for all-marker fusion. The accuracy and ROC analyses are reported separately. Recorded ROMA and IOTA decisions provided clinical-reference context for the binary task.

CONCLUSION: The multimodal approach showed a higher binary held-out accuracy for LRRFIP1 fusion than for DL alone within the serum cohort. The smaller three-class accuracy difference was not accompanied by a macro-AUC improvement. These internal findings warrant confirmation in larger paired cohorts.

articles.title: Cardiotoxicity Associated with Gynecologic Malignancy Treatment.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review explores the complex relationship between the treatment of gynecologic malignancies and cardiovascular (CV) disease. Special attention is paid to shared risk factors, treatment-related cardiotoxicity, and strategies for mitigating cardiovascular risk.

RECENT FINDINGS: Uterine cancer has surpassed ovarian cancer as the most lethal gynecologic malignancy in the United States. Endometrial cancer mortality has increased 3% annually. A 2.7 fold increase in myocardial infarction and stroke incidence has been described among gynecologic cancer survivors compared to women without a history of cancer. Emerging strategies to mitigate the development of cardiotoxicity include pegylated liposomal doxorubicin, dexrazoxane, prophalactic neurohormonal therapies, and statins. Gynecologic cancer patients require comprehensive risk assessment and monitoring throughout all stages of cancer treatment. Identifying high risk attributes, actively managing risk factors, employing cardioprotective pharmarcotherapies, and performing ongoing surveillance are discussed.

articles.title: Obesity, type 2 diabetes, and erectile dysfunction: pathophysiology and emerging therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is highly prevalent in men with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and should be regarded as a multifactorial cardiometabolic condition rather than an isolated sexual symptom. In this setting, ED arises from the convergence of endothelial dysfunction, impaired nitric oxide signaling, insulin resistance, chronic low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, visceral adiposity, autonomic neuropathy, and functional hypogonadism, with psychosocial factors further modulating disease burden and treatment response. Beyond its impact on quality of life, ED may also act as an early marker of systemic vascular disease and increased cardiovascular risk, particularly in metabolically unhealthy men. This review summarizes the epidemiology, pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical evaluation, and therapeutic management of ED in the context of obesity and T2DM. A central theme is that ED in these patients should be approached within a broader metabolic and cardiovascular framework, including assessment of glycemic control, visceral adiposity, hormonal status, and global cardiovascular risk. First-line treatment remains centered on lifestyle intervention and phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors, while second-line therapies, penile prosthesis, and testosterone replacement retain an important role in selected patients. Particular attention is given to disease-modifying metabolic strategies. Weight loss, especially when accompanied by improvement in insulin sensitivity, glycemic control, and androgen balance, is consistently associated with better erectile outcomes, with bariatric surgery providing the strongest proof of concept. Emerging evidence suggests that incretin-based therapies and other glucose-lowering agents may influence erectile function beyond glycemic control alone, although available data remain heterogeneous and sometimes conflicting. Overall, ED in obesity and T2DM requires a phenotype-driven, multidisciplinary approach integrating sexual medicine, diabetology, endocrinology, obesity care, and cardiovascular risk stratification.

articles.title: Interpreting miR-18a-5p in Chronic Heart Failure: Biomarker Reliability and Endothelial Remodeling.
Long-term renal outcomes and systemic complications in chronic hypoparathyroidism under conventional therapy: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term clinical outcomes and systemic complications in patients with chronic hypoparathyroidism (HP) managed with conventional therapy at tertiary endocrinology centers.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included patients followed at four referral centers in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (2018-2021). Demographic, clinical, laboratory, therapeutic, and complication data were evaluated. Data are presented as n (%) or median (p25-p75).

RESULTS: Of 113 participants (93.8% women; median age 46 years [37-56]; median disease duration 7.5 years [4-15]), HP was postsurgical in 93.8%, most often for nontoxic multinodular goiter (63.8%). Conventional therapy improved serum calcium and reduced phosphate (both p < 0.001). Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) declined over follow-up (93.1 vs. 81.1 mL/min/1.73 m²; p < 0.001), with chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in 32.3%. Advanced CKD stages were associated with systemic arterial hypertension (SAH) and diabetes mellitus (DM) (p < 0.001 and p = 0.001). Participants with CKD progression were older (62 vs. 57 years; p = 0.036) and had longer disease duration (12 vs. 7 years; p = 0.025) than non-progressors; osteopenia was also more prevalent among them (24.1% vs. 5.0%; p = 0.018).

CONCLUSION: Although conventional therapy promotes adequate metabolic control, clinically relevant complications persist, most notably progressive renal decline affecting nearly one-third of the cohort. CKD progression was associated with older age, longer disease duration, and a higher burden of SAH and DM, indicating a multifactorial process rather than a single cause. These findings underscore the need for rigorous long-term monitoring of renal and cardiometabolic risk in chronic HP, and for prospective, adjusted studies to clarify the specific contribution of the disease and its treatment.

articles.title: Consensus on procedural steps and end-product definition for robotic distal and total gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy: the MASTER-D2 Delphi study.
authors: International Gastric Cancer Association Robotic Gastrectomy Working Group
articles.journal: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to investigate consensus among experts in robotic gastric cancer surgery on the procedural steps of robotic distal and total gastrectomy (DG, TG) and the anatomical end-points of D2 lymphadenectomy.

BACKGROUND: Variability in intraoperative performance during gastric cancer surgery impacts immediate postoperative and long-term oncological outcomes. There is no consensus on the procedural steps and anatomical end-points for robotic gastrectomy.

METHODS: A modified Delphi was conducted with 15 expert surgeons from Europe, Asia and North America. Items were generated via hierarchical task analysis, rated through two anonymous online rounds, and finalised at an in-person meeting. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement. Internal consistency, inter-rater agreement, and stability were assessed.

RESULTS: Of 19 invited experts, 15 (79%) completed Rounds 1 and 2, and 13 (86.7%) attended Round 3. Consensus was achieved on 85 statements: 62 of 67 items for DG, 57 of 65 for TG, and 14 items defining the anatomical boundaries and post-dissection end-product of a D2 lymphadenectomy. Ten items did not reach consensus. Inter-rater agreement improved between the online rounds.

CONCLUSION: Consensus was reached on the procedural steps of robotic DG and TG and the anatomical end-points of D2 lymphadenectomy, defining the content to be scored in each phase by a future surgical quality assurance tool. These 85 statements provide the content evidence for MASTER-D2. Evidence of reliability, and of relations to surgeon experience and patient outcomes, will be gathered through video-based testing in future studies.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Disease in Hidradenitis Suppurativa.
articles.abstract: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition in which follicular occlusion and rupture trigger the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and IL-17. Growing evidence suggests that unregulated inflammation may contribute to cardiometabolic disease, which occurs at elevated frequency in HS patient populations, though the nature and directionality of these associations remain incompletely understood. This review synthesizes epidemiologic, pathophysiologic, and clinical evidence to provide an updated assessment of the relationship between HS and cardiometabolic disease. A comprehensive review of the literature was conducted using PubMed and Embase through October 2026. Search terms included hidradenitis suppurativa or acne inversa in combination with conditions such as hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, dyslipidemia, metabolic syndrome, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and cardiovascular disease. Evidence from multiple longitudinal studies suggests that HS may precede the development of hypertension, dyslipidemia, and T2DM, whereas obesity shows potential evidence for a true bidirectional relationship. Mechanistically, chronically elevated cytokine levels might contribute to cardiometabolic disease through impaired insulin signaling, endothelial dysfunction, and hepatic lipid accumulation. Conversely, cardiometabolic disease may amplify systemic inflammation, thereby lowering the threshold for follicular rupture and promoting HS progression. These overlapping inflammatory pathways have therapeutic implications, and early evidence has shown that HS-targeted biologics may be associated with reduced cardiometabolic risk, while cardiometabolic agents have shown some benefit in HS disease activity. Yet, multiple extrinsic factors and environmental influences, including social and structural determinants of health, independently shape risk for both conditions, and may confound currently observed associations. In summary, current evidence suggests a complex, bidirectional relationship between HS and cardiometabolic disease that may be driven by shared inflammatory pathways. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating cardiometabolic risk assessment into routine HS care and underscore the high need for well-designed, prospective studies to strengthen our understanding of disease risk and progression to better address clinical management.

articles.title: Small nerve fibre involvement in youth with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Peripheral diabetic neuropathy is frequently subclinical in youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D), and early nerve-fibre involvement may escape symptom-based assessment. We investigated early large- and small-fibre involvement using clinical evaluation, nerve conduction studies (NCS), quantitative sensory testing (QST), and skin-biopsy-derived intraepidermal nerve fibre density (IENFD).

METHODS: Fifty-nine participants were studied: 41 youth with T1D (mean ± SE age 16.71 ± 0.57 years; diabetes duration 5.91 ± 0.57 years) and 18 age- and sex-matched controls. All underwent neurological examination, QST, and distal-leg skin biopsy; NCS were performed in T1D participants. Small-fibre neuropathy (SFN) was classified using Besta criteria as a provisional research framework, with an operational Toronto-adapted classification used as a complementary exploratory analysis.

RESULTS: NCS was abnormal in two T1D participants. In the primary comparison with 18 unrelated controls, IENFD was lower in participants with T1D (10.76 ± 3.42 vs. 13.23 ± 2.76 fibres/mm; P = 0.008), although the difference was no longer statistically significant in a sensitivity analysis including all 25 biopsied controls (P = 0.098). Participants with reduced IENFD were older, taller, and had impaired lower-limb cold detection thresholds (CDT) (27.10 vs. 28.58 °C; P = 0.019), without significant heat detection thresholds (HDT) differences. IENFD was positively associated with lower-limb CDT (r = 0.366; P = 0.019), but not with diabetes duration or HbA1c. Sixteen of 41 participants (39.0%) fulfilled the provisional Besta-based classification compatible with SFN: 11 with clinical findings plus objective abnormalities and five with concordant QST and IENFD abnormalities without clinical findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Early small-fibre involvement was identified in this cohort, with 16 of 41 youth with T1D (39.0%) fulfilling the provisional Besta-based classification compatible with SFN. Reduced distal-leg IENFD and impaired cold perception supported complementary structural and functional abnormalities. Longitudinal studies are needed to define their prognostic significance.

articles.title: Association between cumulative Chinese visceral adiposity index and glycemic outcomes among Chinese adults with baseline prediabetes: a two-cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the association between the cumulative Chinese visceral adiposity index (CumCVAI) and glycemic transitions among adults with prediabetes.

METHODS: We conducted a dual-cohort study of adults with prediabetes from the Gannan cohort and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The two cohorts were analyzed independently. CumCVAI was calculated from two CVAI measurements. Multinomial logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), and subgroup analyses were performed, with persistent prediabetes as the reference outcome, to assess associations between CumCVAI and glycemic outcomes after adjustment for potential confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 442 participants from the Gannan cohort (2-year follow-up) and 3,115 participants from CHARLS (4-year follow-up) were included. In the Gannan cohort, 7.0% progressed to diabetes and 56.6% reverted to normoglycemia, compared with 15.5% and 23.2%, respectively, in CHARLS. In fully adjusted models, each 100-CVAI-year increase in CumCVAI was associated with a lower likelihood of glycemic reversion in both cohorts (Gannan: RRR = 0.54, 95% CI: 0.37-0.78; CHARLS: RRR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.84-0.95). For progression to diabetes, the association was statistically significant in CHARLS (RRR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.19-1.38), but not in Gannan (RRR = 1.30, 95% CI: 0.68-2.48). The RCS analyses showed no significant evidence of non-linearity for either glycemic outcome in either cohort.

CONCLUSION: CumCVAI was associated with glycemic outcomes among Chinese adults with prediabetes. However, because the second CVAI measurement and glycemic outcomes were assessed concurrently, their temporal sequence could not be determined. Larger studies with subsequent glycemic assessments are needed.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Preoperative Sarcopenia and Outcomes after Laparoscopic and Robotic Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preoperative sarcopenia has been increasingly noted as a predictor for outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. However, its impact among patients undergoing minimally invasive CRC resection remains unknown. This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the relation between preoperative sarcopenia and short-term outcomes after minimally invasive (MIS) CRC surgery.

METHODS: This review followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search through different databases was performed to identify studies assessing adult patients with CRC who underwent minimally invasive colorectal resection. Eligible studies assessed preoperative sarcopenia using objective measures and included a non-sarcopenic comparator group. Pooled odds ratios and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals were estimated; we also used the I² statistic for evaluating heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Eleven studies including 2,453 patients were included, of whom 855 were sarcopenic, and 1,598 were non-sarcopenic. Preoperative sarcopenia showed a higher risk estimate for overall postoperative complications, although the confidence interval crossed the null value (OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.99-3.74; I²=70.1%). A similar pattern was observed for severe complications (OR 1.92, 95% CI 0.80-4.61; I²=63.1%). For surgical site infection, the pooled estimate favored higher odds among patients with preoperative sarcopenia, but the association was not statistically significant under the prespecified random-effects model (OR 1.95, 95% CI 0.70-5.44; I²=61.6%). Anastomotic leakage was not significantly associated with preoperative sarcopenia under the prespecified random-effects model (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.57-2.51; I²=24.8%).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative sarcopenia, as defined in the included studies, may be associated with adverse short-term outcomes after minimally invasive colorectal cancer surgery. However, the evidence was characterized by substantial heterogeneity, unadjusted estimates, heterogeneous sarcopenia definitions, and very low certainty, limiting conclusions regarding an independent prognostic effect.

articles.title: Acrylamide and Endocrine-Metabolic Disruption: Evidence from Human and Animal Studies - A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: This review compiles and analyzes the scientific evidence of the effects of acrylamide on the endocrine system in animals and humans. We review the potential pathways of exposure, metabolism, mechanisms of action, and metabolic implications.

RECENT FINDINGS: Acrylamide affects the endocrine and reproductive systems and is correlated with changes in sex hormones, puberty and menopause. In addition, maternal acrylamide exposure can affect the endocrine and metabolic features of offspring. Therefore, direct or indirect acrylamide exposure can interfere with sex hormones, thyroid function and glycemic homeostasis, with potential implications for infertility, thyroid tumors and the development of metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes and obesity. Acrylamide, a toxic compound present in many foods, affects redox balance and cellular processes, such as signaling pathways, and induces neurotoxicity, reproductive toxicity and genotoxic effects. These effects are associated with oxidative stress, DNA damage and protein dysfunction, and affect physiological systems, such as the endocrine system.

articles.title: Pituitary-gonadal hormone profiles in maintenance dialysis: dialysis modality and factors associated with low testosterone in men.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare pituitary-gonadal hormone profiles between patients receiving maintenance dialysis and age- and sex-comparable individuals without chronic kidney disease (CKD), evaluate differences according to dialysis modality, and examine factors associated with low testosterone in male dialysis patients.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional comparative study included 111 dialysis patients and 74 controls. Pituitary-gonadal hormone profiles were compared between dialysis patients and controls and between hemodialysis (HD) and peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients. In men, low testosterone was defined as total testosterone <3 ng/mL confirmed on two separate morning measurements. Factors associated with low testosterone were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression with bootstrap confidence intervals.
