RESULTS: Dialysis patients had higher prolactin concentrations than controls, while gonadotropin concentrations were higher in both men and postmenopausal women. Male dialysis patients also had lower total testosterone concentrations. Testosterone levels were similar between HD and PD patients. Prolactin concentrations were higher in PD patients, and estradiol concentrations were higher in both men and postmenopausal women receiving PD than in those receiving HD. Low testosterone was present in 32 of 58 male dialysis patients (55.2%). In the multivariable model including age, diabetes mellitus, and prolactin, higher prolactin concentrations were independently associated with greater odds of low testosterone (OR 1.151, bootstrap 95% CI 1.084-1.347; p = 0.004), whereas diabetes mellitus and age were not significantly associated with the outcome.

CONCLUSION: Maintenance dialysis is associated with alterations in pituitary-gonadal hormone profiles. Although testosterone concentrations were similar between dialysis modalities, higher prolactin concentrations were associated with low testosterone in male dialysis patients.

articles.title: Individuals Treated for Hypertension: Long-Term Cardiovascular Complications and Mortality in Accordance with Age.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertension increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality, but age-specific complications among medically treated patients are undetermined.

AIM: To investigate the complication risks by age among patients medically treated for hypertension and the background population.

METHODS: This Danish nationwide population-based cohort study included patients treated for hypertension with a minimum of two medications and referents by exposure density matching based on sex, birth year, and index date. Absolute risks and hazard ratios were stratified by age groups and estimated using competing-risks survival analyses and Cox proportional hazards regression models, respectively. Additionally, the persons' expected life years were assessed.

RESULTS: The study included 711,352 patients with hypertension and 2,845,408 referents (median age, 62.0 years, 53.9% women). The median duration of follow-up was 11.3 years. Compared with matched referents, the hazard ratios were higher among younger than among older patients with hypertension. Compared with matched referents, the hazard ratios were higher among younger than among older patients with hypertension. For individuals aged ≤ 40 and > 80 years, respectively, the hazard ratios were: heart failure, 4.62 (95% CI, 4.13-5.17) and 1.17 (95% CI, 1.14-1.21); ischaemic heart disease, 3.02 (95% CI, 2.84-3.21) and 1.25 (95% CI, 1.22-1.29); stroke, 2.95 (95% CI, 2.71-3.21) and 1.02 (95% CI, 0.99-1.05); atrial fibrillation, 2.80 (95% CI, 2.54-3.07) and 1.17 (95% CI, 1.15-1.20); and all-cause mortality, 2.64 (95% CI, 2.46-2.83) and 0.87 (95% CI, 0.86-0.88). The expected mean loss of life years among patients compared with referents ranged from 2.1 years (95% CI, 2.1-2.2) at ≤ 40 years to 0.14 years (95% CI, 0.10-0.16) at ≤ 80 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with referents, individuals medically treated for hypertension at particularly younger ages have higher risks of long-term cardiovascular complications. The findings emphasise the importance of early cardiovascular prevention among patients with hypertension.

articles.title: The Growing Burden of Hypertension Management in Very Old Adults.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Demographic trends suggest a remarkable increase of the very elderly population in the next decades. Hypertension is among the most common chronic conditions in older adults. Outcome evidence to guide safe and effective hypertension management in adults aged ≥ 80 years remains limited.Indeed, very old and frail adults have historically been under-represented in randomized trials.Subsequent epidemiologic analyses and trials established benefits of treatment in selected older adults, while leaving uncertainty for those with substantial frailty.In the present viewpoint we analyze the available evidence supporting control of blood pressure and effective and safe treatment of hypertension in selected very old adults, underlying the need of targets and drug regimens tailored to frailty, orthostatic symptoms and comorbidity with the aim to preserve cognition, function, and quality of life.

articles.title: Longitudinal Blood Pressure Trends Among Transgender Individuals Receiving Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: It is unknown how receipt of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) may impact a patient's blood pressure (BP).

AIM: To characterize the association of initiating GAHT on longitudinal BP readings and hypertension management in transgender individuals.

METHODS: We performed a single center analysis of transgender individuals receiving GAHT between January 2013 and December 2022. The subjects were assigned to transgender women or transgender men cohorts and then into cohorts by BP values, aligning with the 2017 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association BP guideline definitions. A linear mixed effect model was fitted for each cohort to determine change in BP over five years on GAHT, adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of 862 transgender women and 891 transgender men, with a prevalence of hypertension (HTN) before GAHT of 42% and 33%, respectively. Transgender men and women with normal or elevated systolic BP (SBP) had a rise in SBP of 3 mmHg on GAHT. There was a decrease of 6.9 mmHg for transgender men with stage 2 HTN. Transgender women and men with baseline HTN had a reduction in diastolic BP (DBP) by 4 mmHg on GAHT.

CONCLUSIONS: Observed BP changes following GAHT initiation were modest and varied according to baseline BP category. Among participants with baseline hypertension, no worsening of blood pressure was observed during follow-up.

articles.title: Updates in Diagnosis and Treatment of ATTR Cardiac Amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes the contemporary epidemiology, diagnostic approaches, screening strategies, and therapies for transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM), with emphasis on evolving diagnostic paradigms and emerging therapeutic targets.

RECENT FINDINGS: ATTR-CM is an under recognized yet treatable infiltrative cardiomyopathy with meaningful prevalence among patients with HFpEF, aortic stenosis, and select orthopedic conditions. Despite advances in noninvasive diagnosis and broader screening efforts, unacceptable delays in diagnosis remain rampant and continue to be an impediment to effective treatment. The expanding availability of disease-specific therapies, alongside a robust therapeutic pipeline, has heightened the clinical importance of earlier identification and intervention to improve outcomes. ATTR-CM is an increasingly recognized contributor to heart failure-related morbidity and mortality. Advances in screening, diagnosis, and disease-modifying therapies have begun to shift its disease course, underscoring the importance of timely detection and management.

articles.title: Radiogenomic profile of PIK3CA mutation in lung cancer: PET/CT findings, co-mutation patterns, and exploratory survival associations.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) constitutes the vast majority of lung cancers and exhibits significant genetic heterogeneity. The PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway is important in tumor development and metabolism. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between PIK3CA mutation status and clinical features, PET/CT metabolic parameters, co-mutation profiles, and exploratory survival associations in NSCLC patients from a radiogenomic perspective.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 162 NSCLC patients who underwent both Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) and 18 F-FDG PET/CT imaging between 2019 and 2025. Clinical, histopathological, and PET/CT parameters [mean standardized uptake value (SUVmean), peak SUV (SUVpeak), maximum SUV (SUVmax), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), and total lesion glycolysis (TLG)] were recorded. The relationships between PIK3CA mutation status, concomitant gene mutations, and PET/CT metabolic parameters were evaluated. Overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and the log-rank test. In addition, a Cox proportional hazards sensitivity analysis adjusting for age, sex, histological subtype, TNM stage, and performance status was performed in patients with available staging data.

RESULTS: PIK3CA mutations were detected in 29% of patients. PIK3CA-positivity was significantly associated with smoking status and squamous cell carcinoma histology (p = 0.002, p < 0.001, respectively). ROC analysis demonstrated modest discriminatory performance for SUVmax and limited discriminatory performance for SUVpeak in distinguishing PIK3CA mutation status (p < 0.001 and p = 0.011, respectively). Co-mutation analysis revealed significant associations of PIK3CA mutations with TP53 (p < 0.001) and NF1 (p = 0.046) alterations, whereas no significant associations were observed with KRAS or EGFR mutations. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in overall survival according to PIK3CA mutation status (log-rank p = 0.993). Consistently, PIK3CA mutation status was not significantly associated with overall survival in the Cox sensitivity analysis adjusted for age, sex, histological subtype, TNM stage, and performance status (HR = 0.86, 95% CI: 0.55-1.33; p = 0.499). In an exploratory analysis restricted to PIK3CA-mutated patients, concurrent KRAS mutation was associated with shorter overall survival (log-rank p = 0.002); however, this subgroup finding should be interpreted cautiously because of the small number of KRAS co-mutated cases.

CONCLUSIONS: PIK3CA-mutated NSCLC tumors showed higher metabolic activity, particularly higher SUVmax values, than PIK3CA-wild-type tumors. However, SUVmax demonstrated only modest discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.703), with substantial overlap between mutation groups. These findings support an association between PIK3CA mutation status and tumor glucose metabolism rather than a clinically applicable imaging-based prediction model. FDG PET/CT cannot substitute for molecular testing, and the present study does not establish a role for PET/CT parameters in treatment selection. Further prospective and externally validated studies incorporating standardized treatment, staging, and follow-up data are required to determine the clinical relevance of these radiogenomic and survival associations.

articles.title: Interchangeability of PSMA PET Tracers and Theranostic Target Efficacy in Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Three prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography (PET) tracers hold FDA approval, and the theranostic agent, 177Lu-PSMA-617, given with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) is now indicated for PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive disease, in addition to its use in metastatic castration-resistant disease. Our aim is to summarize the PSMA PET tracers in clinical use and their cross validity for 177Lu-PSMA-617 target efficacy.

RECENT FINDINGS: Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat, and F-18 flotufolastat differ marginally in half-life, production, and urinary excretion, but none have shown diagnostic superiority. Pivotal trials, including VISION, PSMAfore, and PSMAddition determined eligibility with centrally read Ga-68 PSMA-11. American Society of Clinical Oncology guidance nevertheless accepts any of the three PSMA PET tracers for candidacy, and the 177Lu-PSMA-617 product label concurs. The rationale is physiologic and consensus-based: VISION defined positivity relative to liver uptake, and joint European American nuclear medicine guidance applies this rule to all tracers. Additionally, tumor/liver and tumor/salivary gland ratios are scanner-independent surrogates, supporting this cross validity. Quantitative predictors of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response and overall survival were derived using Ga-68 PSMA-11, but emerging fluorine-18 data are supportive, though there's a lack of standardization. The approved tracers appear cross-valid for liver-referenced eligibility and quantitative metrics predicting treatment response, but the strongest evidence remains tied to Ga-68 PSMA-11. Tracer interchangeability rests on consensus, rather than companion-diagnostic trials. Future randomized intra-patient comparison could potentially establish whether tracer choice alters eligibility or predicts benefit, and whether thresholds are tracer specific.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and bone fragility: pathophysiological links between liver and skeletal metabolism.
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) pose substantial global health burdens. Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and microarchitectural deterioration, leading to increased fracture risk, whereas MASLD encompasses a spectrum ranging from simple steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The prevalence of both conditions has risen markedly, in parallel with the global increase in obesity, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Emerging evidence suggests a potential pathophysiological link between MASLD and osteoporosis, highlighting the existence of a liver-bone axis. Shared mechanisms, including chronic low-grade inflammation, insulin resistance, adipokine imbalance, oxidative stress, vitamin D deficiency, and alterations in cytokine and osteokine signaling, may contribute to bone loss in patients with MASLD (Fig. 1). In particular, pro-inflammatory mediators and molecular pathways implicated in MASLD progression may disrupt the balance between bone formation and resorption, thereby promoting skeletal fragility. Several observational studies and meta-analyses have reported an association between MASLD and adverse skeletal outcomes, including higher odds of osteoporosis or osteoporotic fractures (OR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.31), increased risks of osteoporosis (RR = 1.28, 95% CI 1.08-1.52) and fractures (RR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.00-1.37), as well as lower BMD; however, findings are not entirely consistent across populations and disease stages. Herein, we aim to summarize current evidence regarding the association between MASLD and osteoporosis and to explore the underlying pathogenetic mechanisms linking these two conditions. A better understanding of the liver-bone crosstalk may facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals and support the development of integrated therapeutic strategies targeting both hepatic and skeletal health.

articles.title: Serum 25(OH)D, albumin-corrected calcium, and diabetic retinopathy in type 2 diabetes: distinct dose-response patterns in a cold-region cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Calcium and vitamin D have both been associated with diabetic retinopathy (DR), but whether they exhibit similar or distinct dose-response relationships with DR remains unclear. This study investigated the associations of albumin-corrected calcium and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] with DR in patients with type 2 diabetes from northern China.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study including 976 patients with type 2 diabetes was conducted between 2019 and 2024. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the associations of albumin-corrected calcium and 25(OH)D with DR, with eGFR and HbA1c included as covariates. Restricted cubic spline(RCS) analyses were used to characterize dose-response relationships, and stratified and sensitivity analyses were performed by renal function.

RESULTS: Patients with DR had higher albumin-corrected calcium levels and lower 25(OH)D concentrations than those without DR. After adjustment for potential confounders, albumin-corrected calcium was positively associated with DR, whereas 25(OH)D was inversely associated with DR. RCS analyses revealed distinct dose-response patterns. Albumin-corrected calcium showed a significant nonlinear association with the presence of DR, with the odds increasing markedly above 2.110 mmol/L, whereas 25(OH)D demonstrated an approximately linear inverse association.

CONCLUSIONS: Albumin-corrected calcium and 25(OH)D were independently associated with DR in patients with type 2 diabetes. The distinct dose-response patterns observed for calcium and vitamin D suggest that they may have different roles in the metabolic processes associated with DR.

articles.title: Analysis of PFNA closed reduction and internal fixation combined with extracorporeal shock wave therapy for intertrochanteric femoral fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the therapeutic value of combining closed reduction and internal fixation with a proximal femoral nail anti-rotation (PFNA) system and extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) in patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures (IFF).

METHODS: This study was a randomized controlled trial. Sixty patients with IFF were randomized into two groups. The control group (n = 30) underwent PFNA fixation, while the intervention group (n = 30) received PFNA fixation plus ESWT. The primary outcomes were fracture healing time and time to full weight-bearing. Secondary outcomes included Harris hip score (HHS), visual analogue scale (VAS) score, hip joint range of motion (ROM), radiographic parameters [quality of fracture reduction, tip-apex distance (TAD), and neck-shaft angle], 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) score, and complication incidence.

RESULTS: The intervention group demonstrated shorter times to full weight-bearing and fracture healing than the control group (both P < 0.001). Compared with preoperative values, HHS scores increased at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively in both groups, with higher scores in the intervention group (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004, respectively). Compared with preoperative values, VAS scores decreased at 1, 3, and 6 months in both groups, with lower scores in the intervention group (all P < 0.001). At 6 months postoperatively, hip range of motion (flexion, extension, adduction, abduction, internal and external rotation) increased in both groups and was greater in the intervention group (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, P = 0.003, P < 0.001, P = 0.002, and P = 0.006, respectively). No significant differences were observed between the two groups in quality of fracture reduction, TAD, or neck-shaft angle (P = 0.361, P = 0.503, and P = 0.517, respectively). At 6 months, PF, RP, BP, GH, VT, SF, RE, and MH scores increased in both groups and were higher in the intervention group (P < 0.001, P = 0.002, P < 0.001, P = 0.002, P = 0.001, P < 0.001, P = 0.007, and P < 0.001, respectively). The complication rates were 3.33% (1/30) and 10.00% (3/30) in the intervention and control groups, respectively, with no statistically significant difference (P = 0.612).

CONCLUSION: PFNA fixation combined with ESWT may improve short-term efficacy within 6 months postoperatively for IFF.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: ChiCTR2300021245.

articles.title: Trauma & Stroke: Cerebrovascular Complications in Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for cerebrovascular complications that contribute to mortality and long-term disability. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and management of cerebrovascular complications after TBI, including post-traumatic cerebral infarction, blunt cerebrovascular injury, post-traumatic vasospasm, delayed cerebral ischemia, and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies have improved understanding of the roles of endothelial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, coagulopathy, and impaired cerebral autoregulation in the pathogenesis of cerebrovascular injury after TBI. Contemporary trauma and stroke guidelines increasingly support systematic vascular imaging, multidisciplinary decision-making, and individualized antithrombotic strategies. Early identification of cerebrovascular complications requires serial neurological assessments, targeted vascular imaging, and physiologic monitoring. Management should be guided by the specific vascular phenotype while balancing ischemic and hemorrhagic risks. Future prospective studies are needed to standardize diagnostic criteria, refine surveillance strategies, and optimize mechanism-specific therapies.

articles.title: Autochthonous Weissella cibaria paraprobiotics modulate inflammatory responses induced by heat-inactivated Aeromonas hydrophila in tambaqui.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of dietary supplementation with Weissella cibaria paraprobiotics (strains M14, I10, or their combination/MIX) for 60 days on growth performance, intestinal morphology, and immunoinflammatory responses in juvenile tambaqui (Colossoma macropomum). Heat treatment at 70 °C for 10 min resulted in no detectable bacterial growth under the culture conditions tested, while preserving gross cellular morphology. In contrast, exposure to 100 °C for 10 min caused evident morphological alterations, including increased surface roughness and visible surface disruption. Following the experimental induction of coelomitis using heat-inactivated Aeromonas hydrophila, paraprobiotic supplementation modulated innate immune and hematological responses. Increased serum lysozyme activity was observed in the M14 and MIX treatments, whereas myeloperoxidase (MPO) activity was higher in the I10 and MIX treatments. All supplemented groups exhibited reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which may reflect modulation of inflammatory responses or reduced phagocyte activation. Hematological alterations included changes in circulating leukocyte and thrombocyte profiles, with treatment-specific responses. The MIX treatment was associated with lower hepatic histopathological scores. Before the inflammatory challenge, the I10 treatment showed increased total leukocyte and thrombocyte counts, while neutrophilia and lymphopenia were observed in the supplemented groups. Furthermore, fish supplemented with I10 exhibited lower proximal intestinal mucosal fold height and width. No significant differences in zootechnical performance were observed among treatments. Overall, the findings suggest that heat-inactivated W. cibaria modulated innate immune and hematological responses 12 h after coelomitis induction in juvenile tambaqui. Future studies should investigate different doses of each strain in the formulation, evaluate inflammatory responses at multiple time points, and assess protection against bacterial infection through challenges with live bacteria.

articles.title: Extreme temperatures and allergies and asthma.
articles.abstract: As climate change increases the frequency of prolonged periods of unusually high or low temperatures (heat waves and cold spells) are likely to remain a major contributor to preventable morbidity for allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis, asthma, atopic and contact dermatitis, food and insect sting allergy. We discuss here the impact of heat waves and cold spells through the lens of the new classification for hypersensitivity reactions centered on disease endotypes, offering potential targeted solutions to increase individual resilience to the environmental stressors based on their mechanisms of actions. The effects of extreme temperatures are counteracted through an adaptive process called allostasis. Allostasis begins with immune maturation in early life, with effective management of human resilience against environmental stressors relying on diet, microbiome, and epithelial barrier as essential foundations These protective mechanisms may become inadequate with accelerated climate change. The resulting dysregulated resilient response can cause a variety of immune-mediated conditions such as allergies, asthma, autoimmune diseases, and cancers, with asthma and allergies being the earliest indicators of the environmental driven imbalance in the lifetime of an individual. This review also details the clinical consequences of extreme temperatures on allergies and asthma and demonstrates how healthcare professionals can drive the change for mitigating their impact by educating patients on extreme temperature-related health risks and providing adaptive guidance.

articles.title: Segmental microbiological findings at ventriculoperitoneal shunt explantation: a descriptive pilot series with emphasis on wound dehiscence.
articles.abstract: Most ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunt infections are acquired at implantation; a proportion present with dehiscence of the overlying wound, and component-level culture findings in this presentation remain poorly characterised. We describe a six-site sampling protocol applied at shunt explantation in a cohort dominated by this presentation. Six adults undergoing complete VP shunt removal for suspected infection (2023-2025) were included: four with scalp wound dehiscence, one with meningitis and one with early malfunction. Specimens comprised ventricular CSF, ventricular catheter tip, burr-hole deflector, valve, distal-catheter luminal fluid and terminal peritoneal catheter. The deflector and valve were sonicated, catheter segments rolled and cultures interpreted qualitatively. Among four patients with dehiscence, S. aureus was recovered in all. Positive cultures were limited to proximal specimens in three, and ventricular CSF cultures were negative in two, each with only one positive proximal hardware component. In the meningitis patient, CSF and three hardware components, including the distal catheter, were positive, whereas the deflector and distal-catheter fluid cultures were negative. The patient explanted within 24 h yielded two different commensals on proximal hardware but was not considered to have established shunt infection. Site comparisons were confounded by differing culture methods. Six-site sampling was completed in all six patients. This preliminary descriptive series documents component-level microbiological findings in patients presenting with wound dehiscence but cannot establish an infection route, diagnostic superiority or an expected anatomical distribution. Larger studies using uniform quantitative processing are required.

articles.title: The median suboccipital craniotomy in the semi-sitting position: Surgical technique, outcomes, complication avoidance, and prevention of venous air embolism.
articles.abstract: The semi-sitting position provides gravity-assisted exposure of the posterior fossa and posterior tentorial space but carries position-specific risks, chiefly venous air embolism (VAE). This study describes a standardized protocol for the median suboccipital craniotomy in the semi-sitting position, with a emphasis on avoiding complications, and reports its outcomes over 15 years. A prospectively maintained database of 147 consecutive patients who underwent median suboccipital craniotomy in the semi-sitting position by the same surgical team at a tertiary center from 2005 to 2020 was retrospectively reviewed. Lesions were stratified by targe location, and perioperative complications, including VAE detected by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), were analyzed descriptively. Of 147 patients (82 female; age range 5-82 years), 95 (64.6%) had posterior fossa tumors and 52 (35.4%) had vascular lesions; 12 (8.2%) had lesions of the posterior incisural space or tentorial surface requiring a supracerebellar trajectory. TEE-detected VAE occurred in 38 patients (25.9%), all managed intraoperatively without cardiorespiratory compromise or paradoxical embolism. All bone flaps were replaced. Complications occurred in 10 patients (6.8%): superficial wound infection (2.7%) and transient hydrocephalus (4.1%); there were no pseudomeningoceles and no 30-day mortality. The median suboccipital craniotomy in the semi-sitting position, performed by an experienced team under a multimodal VAE prevention protocol, was associated with a low complication rate. The stepwise checklist presented here may help teams using this position anticipate and avoid its specific complications, particularly for lesions of the posterior incisural space.

articles.title: Sonic Hedgehog Signaling as a Multicellular Target in Neuroinflammation Following Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
articles.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, neuroinflammation plays a pivotal role in both secondary brain injury and subsequent repair and remodeling. Its dynamic evolution is collectively regulated by cell type, temporal window, and the local microenvironment. As a critical regulatory axis governing development and tissue homeostasis, the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling pathway is activated in various cell types post-stroke, participating in inflammatory responses and the remodeling of the neurovascular unit. However, the different roles of Shh pathway across distinct stages and cell types often lead to seemingly contradictory research findings. This article systematically reviews the regulatory mechanisms of the Shh pathway in inflammation related to neuronal survival, microglial polarization, reactive astrocyte proliferation, and blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity at different stages of ischemic stroke. At the neuronal level, Shh may inhibit inflammation initiation by indirectly reducing damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) release. At the microglia/macrophage level, Shh affects their inflammatory program and repair function, driving a shift from the traditional M1/M2 dichotomy to a multi-state spectrum. At the astrocyte level, impaired Shh exacerbates BBB destruction during the acute phase, whereas activated Shh promotes BBB repair and regulates glial scar properties during the repair phase. At the BBB level, Shh limits the entry of circulating immune cells into the central nervous system (CNS) through a three-layered mechanism involving structure, function, and cellular spectrum. Based on the above, this review aims to explore the potential and challenges of Shh pathway as a therapeutic target for neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke, while considering the inflammatory-related consequences within the stroke stage-cell type-inflammatory state framework.

articles.title: Rapid screening and identification of epigallocatechin-3-gallate and quercetin derived from traditional Chinese medicine as inhibitors of pan-orthopoxviruses : Quercetin and EGCG against orthopoxviruses.
articles.abstract: Poxviruses are major zoonotic pathogens. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has been used for antiviral treatment; however, data on the efficacy of TCM against poxviruses remain limited. Therefore, this study assessed the antiviral activity of 15 active ingredients derived from TCM against orthopoxviruses. The cytotoxic concentration 50 (CC50) was determined using Vero cells. Subsequent screening was performed to select compounds with potential antiviral activity in vitro using vaccinia virus expressing green fluorescent protein (VTT-EGFP) as a model. (-)-Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), NK007, quercetin, emetine, and pyrvinium pamoate demonstrated notable anti-orthopoxvirus activity in Vero cells. The EC50 value of quercetin and EGCG were 3.04-8.00 µM and 39.39-60.55 µM, respectively by qPCR and 1.24-2.53 µM and 44.76-66.36 µM by Plaque assay in Vero cells infected with orthopoxviruses (VTT-EGFP, ectromelia virus, and monkeypox virus), respectively. Quercetin primarily targeted the post-entry phase, whereas EGCG affected the viral entry phase. Quercetin and EGCG suppressed the transcription of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1 and IL-6, and when combined with the antiviral drug cidofovir (CDV), exerted a synergistic antiviral effects against VTT-EGFP. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance analyses revealed the EGCG-binding affinity and conserved interactions with VACV A27L and D8L proteins. Quercetin and EGCG effectively inhibited viral replication and suppressed the expression of inflammatory cytokines in Vero cells infected with orthopoxvirus. Furthermore, EGCG exhibited binding affinity and conserved interactions with VACV A27L and D8L proteins in vitro. These findings will facilitate the development of therapeutic agents that act against monkeypox as well as infection with other orthopoxviruses.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Risk Associated with Hormonal Therapy in Prostate Cancer: A Cardio-Oncology Approach to Treatment Selection.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the cardiovascular risk of contemporary hormonal therapy for prostate cancer, focusing on androgen deprivation therapy, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists and antagonists, and androgen receptor pathway inhibitors. It also considers how baseline cardiovascular assessment may guide treatment selection and monitoring.

RECENT FINDINGS: Men with prostate cancer often have cardiovascular comorbidities and multiple cardiovascular risk factors. Androgen deprivation therapy may promote adverse metabolic, vascular, and electrophysiological effects, particularly in patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease. Pooled analyses often favor gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonists over agonists in patients with established cardiovascular disease, although randomized evidence remains inconclusive. Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors increase the risk of hypertension and other cardiovascular events, but their toxicity profiles differ. Cardiovascular phenotype and treatment-specific toxicity should inform individualized therapy when oncological efficacy is comparable. Cardiovascular risk-factor optimization, tailored monitoring, and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology care are essential. Prospective trials with adjudicated cardiovascular endpoints are needed to define the comparative cardiovascular safety of individual hormonal therapies.

articles.title: [Vasoplegia-A problem that can be rationally treated and perhaps may be avoided, at least in some patients!].

[Practical guidance on ethics in outpatient intensive care for adults : Consensus paper by the sections on ethics, disorders of consciousness and coma, studies and standards in neuromedicine, and early rehabilitation in intensive care of the German Interdisciplinary Association for Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine (DIVI)].
articles.abstract: Thanks to advances in intensive care medicine, an increasing number of patients are surviving the acute phase of a critical illness - often with considerable uncertainty regarding their prognosis. It is therefore necessary to make prognoses and to define treatment goals and limits as part of a shared decision-making process whilst patients are still receiving intensive care. Failure to do so risks a 'treatment automatism', which shifts decisions on limiting treatment to secondary areas such as outpatient intensive care. There, there is often a continuing need for intensive care management and unresolved ethical conflicts, which contribute to prolonged inappropriate or excessive care. Particular areas of tension arise between prolonging life and quality of life, and between autonomy and care. This article highlights key ethical issues in outpatient intensive care for adults, clarifies them from a normative perspective and bundles them into practical recommendations.

articles.title: Ketamine administration for acute severe agitation in a pediatric emergency department: prevalence and clinical profile-a 6-year retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Ketamine is widely used in pediatric emergency departments (ED) for procedural sedation, but evidence regarding its use for acute severe agitation in adolescents remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of ketamine administration for acute agitation in a tertiary pediatric ED over 6 years and describe patient characteristics and outcomes. This observational retrospective study was conducted at the pediatric ED of a tertiary-level university teaching hospital, IRCCS Burlo Garofolo, Trieste, Italy, from January 2020 to December 2025. Electronic medical records of patients aged 0-17 years receiving ketamine were analyzed. Trends in ED visits, agitation crises, and ketamine utilization were evaluated. Clinical features, dosing, adverse events, and ED outcomes were summarized for patients receiving ketamine for severe agitation. Among 139,295 ED visits, 1803 (1.3%) were for acute agitation. Overall, 622 ketamine doses were administered to 558 patients. Agitation control accounted for 8.7% of doses (n = 54). The prevalence of ketamine use for agitation control rose from 0% to 7.49%. These 54 doses were given across 26 episodes in 22 patients (median age 16 years, IQR 15-17; 63.6% male). Agitation stemmed mainly from behavioral crises (42.3%). Ketamine was delivered intravenously in 65.4% of episodes and intramuscularly in 23.1%. Adverse events were rare. Post-treatment, 50% of patients were discharged from the ED, 26.9% were admitted to intensive care.

CONCLUSION: This study showed that the use of ketamine for severe agitation progressively increased over the study period, while describing a series of pediatric patients treated with ketamine for severe agitation control.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric emergency settings have reported a substantial increase in visits for behavioral and psychiatric problems, including episodes of psychomotor agitation as well as aggressiveness. • Evidence regarding the efficacy of ketamine in controlling acute, severe agitation in adolescent populations remains scarce.

WHAT IS NEW: • Agitation control emerged as the second most frequent indication for ketamine administration in a tertiary pediatric emergency department, driven by a progressive increase in its utilization over the 6-year study period. • Agitation control was successfully achieved with a single ketamine dose in 84.6% of cases.

articles.title: Temporal changes in FAPI uptake in subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progression: implications for preclinical FAP-targeted imaging and therapy.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Subcutaneous U87MG xenografts are widely employed for the evaluation of FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals, despite limited insight into the regulation of FAP expression. In this study, we investigated the temporal changes of FAP using longitudinal PET/CT imaging, biodistribution studies, autoradiography, immunohistochemistry, in vitro co-cultures, pharmacological and theranostic interventions.

METHODS: Subcutaneous U87MG xenografts were longitudinally imaged using [68Ga]Ga-DATA5m.SA.FAPI and [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 PET/CT. Ex vivo biodistribution, autoradiography, and species-specific immunohistochemistry were performed across tumor development. Soluble FAP (sFAP) levels were quantified in plasma and conditioned media. Paracrine U87MG-fibroblast communication was investigated in normal and cancer-associated fibroblasts (NF and CAF) co-cultures with or without galunisertib or UAMC1110. The potential involvement of TGF-β signaling was examined in vivo using galunisertib, and exploratory radionuclide therapy was performed using [177Lu]Lu-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2.

RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 PET uptake increased from day 7 to 15 (3.2 ± 0.2 to 9.1 ± 0.9%ID/mL) followed by a decline at day 21 (6.7 ± 1.8%ID/mL). Ex vivo biodistribution supported this increase (13.5 ± 2.5 to 27.8 ± 1.3%IA/g) but showed only a modest decline by day 21 (24.3 ± 1.8%IA/g). Descriptive immunohistochemical analyses showed an apparent increase in human and murine FAP staining across the examined tumor specimens at early and intermediate time points. Galunisertib-treated mice showed numerically lower radiotracer uptake at day 15 (7.5 ± 1.6 vs. 10.5 ± 1.3%ID/mL) (p = 0.0652). In vitro, U87MG-fibroblast interactions induced fibroblast activation, with a 6-fold increase in FAP expression, up to 900-fold IL-6 upregulation and increased sFAP release (472 ± 149 pg/mL), while galunisertib treatment reduced these responses. Radionuclide therapy reduced tumor growth but did not abolish [68Ga]Ga-DOTAGA.Glu.(FAPI)2 uptake at day 29.

CONCLUSION: FAPI uptake varies as subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progress, and complementary biological analyses provide additional context for interpreting these changes. These results highlight the importance of tumor stage and biological context when evaluating FAP-targeted radiopharmaceuticals in this preclinical model.

articles.title: Preoperative imaging for localising hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands in primary hyperparathyroidism: An umbrella review.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands enables minimally invasive parathyroidectomy (MIP) in primary hyperparathyroidism (pHPT). This umbrella review summarises more than a decade of meta-analytic evidence on preoperative localisation imaging.

METHODS: Twenty-eight systematic reviews (published 2012-2025) were identified through a PubMed search and assessed within a predefined inclusion period (2011-2026). The analysis covered ultrasonography (US), [99mTc]Tc-methoxyisobutylisonitrile ([99mTc]Tc-MIBI) scintigraphy with single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT), four-dimensional CT (4D-CT), and [11C]methionine and [18F]fluorocholine positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT). Pooled sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and detection rate (DR) were extracted, using histopathology and, where available, postoperative biochemical cure as reference standard.

RESULTS: Pooled sensitivity/specificity was 80%/77% for US and 84%/87% for [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy. Detection rates were 84-88% for SPECT/CT, 74% for SPECT alone, and 70% for planar scintigraphy. Multiphase CT achieved 73% per-quadrant and 81% per-side sensitivity; after negative or inconclusive scintigraphy, 4D-CT reached 71% sensitivity and 81% PPV. [11C]methionine PET/CT sensitivities ranged from 77 to 86%. Radiolabelled choline ([11C]choline and [18F]fluorocholine) PET performed best (pooled sensitivity 95%, PPV 97%, DR 91%). [18F]fluorocholine outperformed [99mTc]Tc-MIBI scintigraphy (96% vs. 54% per patient), [11C]methionine (92% vs. 80% per lesion, indirect comparison) and 4D-CT (92% vs. 85% per patient). In the largest choline meta-analysis (1,716 patients), pooled sensitivity was 93.8% and the surgical cure rate 92.8%.

CONCLUSION: Among currently available techniques, [18F]fluorocholine PET/CT provides the highest diagnostic accuracy for preoperative localisation of hyperfunctioning parathyroid glands. It consistently surpasses conventional scintigraphy and 4D-CT in sensitivity while entailing lower radiation exposure.

articles.title: Fragility-associated nonunion represents a distinct biological phenotype compared with trauma-associated nonunion: a retrospective cohort study of 213 consecutive cases.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Long bone nonunion is conventionally treated as a uniform disease entity. We hypothesized that nonunion arises through distinct biological pathways, with a fragility-associated phenotype driven by systemic biological vulnerability differing fundamentally from a trauma-associated phenotype driven by local soft tissue compromise and infection.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of 213 consecutive long bone nonunions treated at a Level 1 trauma center (2007-2018). Patients were classified as fragility-associated (age ≥ 65 years and/or documented osteoporosis; n = 51, 23.9%) or non-fragility/trauma-associated (n = 162, 76.1%). Groups were compared regarding demographics, comorbidity profiles, fracture characteristics, infection rates, operative burden, laboratory parameters, and treatment strategies. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to evaluate independent predictors of septic nonunion and high revision burden.

RESULTS: The fragility phenotype was characterized by significantly higher comorbidity burden (3.2 ± 1.6 vs. 1.8 ± 1.6; p < 0.001), cardiovascular disease (90.2% vs. 41.4%; p < 0.001), renal insufficiency (25.5% vs. 3.7%; p < 0.001), elevated CRP (median 11.5 vs. 4.0 mg/L; p = 0.012), and higher ASA classification (ASA ≥ III: 39.2% vs. 19.1%; p = 0.006). The trauma-associated phenotype showed higher rates of open fractures (25.3% vs. 13.7%), polytrauma (27.8% vs. 9.8%; p = 0.014), and nicotine use (47.5% vs. 11.8%; p < 0.001). On multivariate analysis, fragility was not an independent predictor of septic nonunion (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.44-2.61; p = 0.886) or high revision burden (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.28-2.75; p = 0.829), while open fracture (OR 3.34, 95% CI 1.40-7.99; p = 0.007) and septic nonunion (OR 25.17, 95% CI 9.14-69.29; p < 0.001) were the dominant risk factors.

CONCLUSION: Fragility-associated and trauma-associated nonunions represent distinct clinical phenotypes. The fragility phenotype is driven by systemic biological vulnerability but does not confer increased infection or reconstructive burden. These findings support phenotype-specific approaches to nonunion prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Clinical value of 18F-FDG-PET/CT-detected immune-related adverse events in oncological immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: A systematic review.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs), including subclinical inflammatory toxicities detectable by 18F-FDG PET/CT. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the organ distribution, diagnostic utility, and prognostic significance of PET-detected irAEs (PET-irAEs) in patients with cancer.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science and Embase was conducted through September 2026. Studies reporting on PET-detected irAEs and clinical outcomes in human participants treated with ICIs were included. Data were summarized via narrative synthesis. No formal meta-analysis was performed; organ-site events were aggregated descriptively by cancer type.

RESULTS: PET-irAEs displayed cancer-specific organ profiles: bladder cancer showed thyroid (34%) and gastrointestinal (28.3%) enrichment; non-small-cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) was characterized by gastrointestinal (50%) and pulmonary (19.5%) involvement and melanoma exhibited a heterogeneous multisystem distribution. Evidence regarding the predictive and prognostic significance of PET-irAEs remains inconsistent. Although several studies have demonstrated associations between PET-irAEs and favorable treatment responses or survival outcomes, others have reported no statistically significant relationships. Interpretation of the available evidence is limited by small sample sizes, the lack of adjusted analyses, and susceptibility to selection bias, residual confounding, and time-dependent bias.

CONCLUSION: 18F-FDG PET/CT shows promise as an important tool for the early detection and monitoring of immune-related toxicities. However, the utility of PET-irAEs as imaging biomarkers for predicting treatment response and prognosis requires further validation in large-scale prospective studies.

articles.title: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade is associated with preserved carotid ultrastructure and reduced oxidative stress and apoptotic markers in renovascular hypertension.
authors: de Carvalho Dos Santos Cunha RL
articles.abstract: Persistent activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) in renovascular hypertension (RH) promotes oxidative stress (OS), apoptosis, and vascular remodeling, thereby contributing to the progression of arterial damage. We investigated whether treatment with losartan, enalapril, or spironolactone attenuated RH-induced changes in oxidative stress, apoptotic markers, RAAS components, and vascular ultrastructure. Male Wistar rats were induced to RH by clipping the left renal artery (2-kidney-1-clip, 2K1C) and received losartan (10 mg/kg/day), enalapril (10 mg/kg/day), spironolactone (25 mg/kg/day), or vehicle for 4 weeks by oral gavage. We quantified Bax, Bcl-2, cytochrome c, gp91phox, and GPX-1 by immunohistochemistry, measured systolic blood pressure (SBP) by tail-cuff plethysmography and plasma aldosterone by ELISA, evaluated carotid artery ultrastructure using transmission electron microscopy, and assessed the classical local RAAS pathway with RT-qPCR. All treatments reduced SBP and the immunostaining of gp91phox, BAX, BCL-2, and cytochrome c, whereas the BAX/BCL-2 ratio did not differ among groups. Only enalapril reduced plasma aldosterone and increased GPX-1 expression. Untreated 2K1C rats showed lower carotid Ace mRNA than SHAM rats, and enalapril increased Ace, At1ra, and At1rb mRNA. Qualitative ultrastructural analysis showed that smooth muscle cells kept a contractile profile in the treated groups, similar to that of the SHAM group. Losartan, enalapril, and spironolactone were associated with lower SBP, reduced markers of OS and of the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway, and preserved carotid ultrastructure in 2K1C rats. Enalapril was the only treatment that also lowered aldosterone and increased GPX-1. The absence of increased local RAAS gene expression in the untreated carotid arteries of 2K1C animals suggests a predominant role of systemic RAAS activation in vascular injury.

articles.title: Angiotensin II and high salt alter the endothelin-1/eNOS axis in human endothelial cells and young mice: attenuation during concurrent losartan treatment.
articles.abstract: Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) measurements require interpretation alongside vascular function when assessing experimental endothelial dysfunction. To characterize ET-1/eNOS-associated molecular and vascular changes during angiotensin II (Ang II) or high-salt challenge and identify the endpoints attenuated during concurrent losartan treatment. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) received Ang II (1 μM) or additional NaCl (40 mM) for 24 h, with or without losartan (1 μM). Eight-week-old male C57BL/6JGpt mice underwent four-week Ang II or high-salt challenges with or without concurrent losartan (n = 6 per group). Blood pressure, ET-1, aortic transcripts, immunoreactivity and aortic-ring relaxation were assessed. In HUVECs, both challenges increased EDN1 expression and ET-1 secretion and reduced NOS3 expression. Losartan attenuated Ang II-associated EDN1 and NOS3 changes (both P < 0.01), whereas the ET-1 secretion comparison was not significant. All three high-salt/losartan comparisons were also not significant. In mice, both challenges increased systolic blood pressure and plasma ET-1 and impaired acetylcholine-induced relaxation, while sodium nitroprusside responses were preserved. Concurrent losartan attenuated the blood-pressure and functional changes. Ang II and high salt produced ET-1/eNOS-associated molecular changes in HUVECs and vascular abnormalities in young adult mice. Losartan attenuated selected molecular and functional abnormalities. These findings support interpreting molecular and vascular-function endpoints together when assessing experimentally induced endothelial dysfunction.

articles.title: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated depletion of LncRNA PVT-1 mitigates YAP/TAZ-TEAD1 signalling and maladaptive repair in a cellular model of AKI-to-CKD transition.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) progressing to chronic kidney disease (CKD) is often caused due to sustained tubular injury, inflammation, maladaptive repair, and other universal molecular mechanisms. Long non-coding RNAs (LncRNAs) serve as molecular bridges that stabilize these processes along the AKI-to-CKD continuum. The LncRNA plasmacytoma variant translocation 1 (PVT-1) has emerged as a key regulator of inflammatory and fibrotic signalling in various kidney diseases. Its involvement in modulating Hippo-YAP/TAZ signalling through diverse molecular pathways has been reported; however, its role in renal disease, particularly in the AKI-to-CKD transition, remains incompletely understood. Previous transcriptomic analyses conducted by our lab identified PVT-1 to be dysregulated during the AKI-to-CKD transition, prompting an investigation of its functional role. Here, we combined systems biology, structural modelling, and a CRISPR/Cas9-mediated PVT-1 editing in rat tubular epithelial cells (NRK-52E) to define its contribution to tubular injury. The RNAfold and catRAPID databases identified a 122-nucleotide region of LncRNA PVT-1 with high predicted binding affinity for YAP1, and HDOCK-based macromolecular docking yielded a favourable predicted complex. CRISPR/Cas9-based editing in NRK-52E cells (a polyclonal, partially edited population with residual PVT-1 transcript) resulted in substantial PVT-1 depletion, as confirmed by qRT-PCR, T7EI assay, and FISH. The exposure to rh-TGF-β1 (an in-vitro surrogate model mimicking the AKI-to-CKD transition) upregulated PVT-1 levels, increased superoxide generation, suppressed Hippo regulators, and promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition and pathological ECM deposition; PVT-1 depletion attenuated these effects, with changes in related indicators consistent with restored Hippo signalling, preserving epithelial markers, and decreasing collagen and fibronectin accumulation. Altogether, this in-vitro study demonstrates that LncRNA PVT-1 contributes to the regulation of the Hippo-YAP/TAZ signalling during renal fibrosis, supporting the PVT-1-Hippo axis as a candidate targetable node in the AKI-to-CKD progression.

articles.title: Zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis and septic shock: a double-blind randomized trial.
articles.abstract: Sepsis and septic shock remain major causes of morbidity and mortality in intensive care units (ICUs). Zinc deficiency is common in critically ill patients and may contribute to immune dysregulation, inflammation, and organ dysfunction. However, evidence regarding zinc supplementation in sepsis remains limited. This study aims to evaluate the clinical effects of early oral zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations. In this prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 60 adults with Sepsis-3 sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations were randomized (1:1) to receive oral zinc sulfate (50 mg elemental zinc daily) or matching placebo until ICU discharge or death. The primary outcome was total hospital length of stay (LOS). Secondary outcomes included in-hospital mortality, ICU LOS, vasopressor duration, acute kidney injury, need for renal replacement therapy, duration of invasive mechanical ventilation, inflammatory biomarkers, and serial Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores. Analyses were performed on an intention-to-treat basis, including competing-risk analyses accounting for in-hospital death. Overall mortality was 23.3% in the zinc group and 36.7% in the placebo group (risk ratio 0.64; 95% CI 0.29-1.42; p = 0.260). Total hospital LOS was shorter with zinc supplementation (median [IQR] 9.0 [7.75-12.5] vs 14.0 [10.0-16.25] days; p = 0.006), including among patients with septic shock (10.0 [8.0-11.5] vs 15.0 [11.0-20.0] days; p = 0.004). ICU LOS did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.304). Competing-risk analyses accounting for in-hospital death and baseline prognostic factors did not demonstrate an independent association between zinc supplementation and earlier discharge alive. No consistent treatment-related improvements were observed in mortality, organ dysfunction, inflammatory biomarkers, or other secondary outcomes. Early oral zinc supplementation in adults with sepsis or septic shock and low serum zinc concentrations was associated with shorter unadjusted hospital LOS; however, this association was not confirmed in adjusted competing-risk analyses. Zinc supplementation did not significantly improve mortality or other major clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicenter randomized trials. Trial registration: Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT), IRCT20210519051348N2, prospectively registered on February 3, 2025.

articles.title: Shigella's c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases modulate biofilm and virulence phenotypes.
articles.abstract: To establish infection and cause disease, the intracellular pathogen Shigella must successfully navigate a series of host defenses and distinct microenvironments within the human body. One way Shigella navigates these environments is by using the secondary messenger c-di-GMP, which regulates many different bacterial behaviors. C-di-GMP is synthesized by diguanylate cyclases and broken down by c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases (PDEs). In this study, we investigated how Shigella flexneri's c-di-GMP-specific PDEs impact c-di-GMP turnover and subsequently biofilm and virulence phenotypes. We knocked out each of S. flexneri's six c-di-GMP-specific PDEs to determine how these PDEs impact biofilm, virulence, and c-di-GMP levels within the bacterial cell. We found that these PDEs negatively regulate c-di-GMP levels while modulating S. flexneri's virulence and biofilm behavior. We also noted that altering the expression of these S. flexneri PDEs changes bacterial cell size. Transcriptome analysis revealed that a S. flexneri ΔpdeB strain differentially expresses many genes, including increased expression of virulence genes ipgD and ipgE, and reduced expression of genes associated with lipid metabolism. We confirmed that a S. flexneri ΔpdeB strain has reduced levels of C19 fatty acid methyl ester. This study highlights the complexities of c-di-GMP signaling in regulating numerous Shigella pathways.IMPORTANCEShigella, an intracellular human pathogen and the causative agent of dysentery, infects hundreds of millions of people worldwide each year. The rapid rise of antibiotic-resistant Shigella strains underscores the urgent need to better understand its physiology and identify new therapeutic targets. In this study, we investigated how Shigella c-di-GMP-specific phosphodiesterases regulate c-di-GMP levels and associated bacterial phenotypes. We found that altering the expression of enzymes involved in c-di-GMP degradation significantly impacts Shigella biofilm formation, host cell invasion, and the composition of the bacterial cell membrane.

articles.title: Interim residual metabolic burden complements categorical PET assessment in a real-world cohort of PD-1-treated classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Immune-related response patterns may complicate interim FDG PET assessment in Hodgkin lymphoma (HL). We evaluated whether quantitative residual metabolic burden adds prognostic information beyond Lugano/LYRIC-based assessment during PD-1-based therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center landmark study included 63 patients with HL who underwent baseline and interim FDG PET/CT during PD-1-based therapy. Interim PET was categorized using a Lugano/LYRIC-based three-level classification. Interim total lesion glycolysis (TLG) was designated as the principal residual-burden metric, with interim metabolic tumor volume (MTV) evaluated as a closely related alternative volumetric measure. Landmark progression-free survival (PFS) was calculated from the interim PET date. Associations were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox models, incremental model performance, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Fifteen PFS events occurred during a median follow-up of 34.2 months. Categorical Lugano/LYRIC assessment, Deauville grouping, and percentage change in SUVmax were not statistically associated with PFS. Higher log-transformed interim TLG (HR per 1-SD increase, 1.97; 95% CI, 1.10-3.55; P = 0.023) and interim MTV (HR, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.14-3.04; P = 0.013) were associated with higher PFS event hazards. Among 54 patients without definite progression, PFS events occurred in 8 of 25 patients with high interim TLG and 3 of 29 with low interim TLG. Models incorporating quantitative residual burden yielded higher apparent and optimism-corrected C-index point estimates than categorical assessment alone, but internal performance estimates remained variable.

CONCLUSION: Higher interim residual FDG-avid burden was associated with less favorable PFS and may complement categorical response assessment, particularly by revealing prognostic heterogeneity among patients without definite progression. The observed improvement in discrimination was exploratory and requires prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Breaking the mold: the unique features of mycobacterial biofilms.
articles.abstract: Biofilms are microbial communities found ubiquitously in natural and built environments. Biofilm formation increases bacterial resistance to physical displacement and stressors. During infection, biofilm formation can grant bacteria elevated recalcitrance to antibiotics, complicating treatment options. These features have driven numerous studies aimed at elucidating the mechanisms underlying biofilm formation and dispersal, and accordingly, how these processes can be controlled. The bulk of biofilm research efforts have been concentrated on two pathogen-rich bacterial phyla, Pseudomonadota (synonym Proteobacteria; containing most Gram-negative pathogens) and Bacillota (synonym Firmicutes; containing most Gram-positive pathogens). As such, a common practice for researchers interested in biofilm formation in a Gram-negative bacterial species is to first identify parallel genes, adhesins, or regulatory systems in well-studied genera, including Pseudomonas and Escherichia. Similarly, if studying biofilm formation in a Gram-positive species, the large amount of work done in Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, and Bacillus can fuel inspiration. Like a microbe in rich broth, researchers working with one of those representative genera find themselves happily awash in a treasure trove of biofilm-relevant literature. Although Actinomycetota (synonym Actinobacteria) houses numerous notorious human pathogens, and despite many of those pathogens demonstrating biofilm formation during infection, there have been comparatively few studies dedicated to elucidating biofilm formation in this phylum. Here, we summarize the circumstances contributing to this deficit, review the current biofilm literature for the Actinomycetota genus Mycobacterium, and examine the conserved and unique features of mycobacterial biofilm formation relative to the more well-studied bacterial phyla.

articles.title: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India.
articles.abstract: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic.

articles.title: Cancer mortality among disaggregated Hispanic/Latino populations in the United States, 2003-2023.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: National statistics aggregate Hispanic/Latino individuals, potentially masking differences in health outcomes. We compared age-adjusted cancer mortality rates and trends across US Hispanic/Latino populations disaggregated by origin.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the National Cancer Institute mortality database with detailed Hispanic/Latino origin (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, and other Hispanic/Latino) for all states and DC (2003-2023). Age-adjusted cancer mortality rates and average annual percent changes were calculated for all cancers combined and selected cancers, by Hispanic/Latino origin, sex and age.

RESULTS: Overall, 744,540 cancer deaths were reported among Mexican (n=399,956), Puerto Rican (n=88,107), Cuban (n=67,582), and other Hispanic/Latino (n=188,895) individuals. Among men, increasing mortality was concentrated among those aged ≥65 years, including cancers of the liver (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Other), brain (Cuban, Other), and oral (Other); and colorectal among those aged <50 years (Other). Among women, increasing mortality was also concentrated in the oldest group (≥65 years), including cancers of the endometrium (all groups), liver (Mexican, Puerto Rican, Other), pancreas (Puerto Rican, Cuban, Other), brain (Mexican, Other), breast (Other), and lung (Cuban). Among women aged 50-64 years, increasing mortality trends were observed for endometrium (Mexican, Other), pancreas (Other), liver (Other), and brain (Other). Among women aged <50 years, increasing mortality rates were observed for endometrium (Mexican, Other), colorectal (Mexican, Other), stomach (Other), and cervix (Other).

CONCLUSIONS: Cancer mortality differed by origin among US Hispanic/Latino populations.

IMPACT: Cancer control efforts must consider these differences, which may reflect variations in exposures to infectious agents, health behaviors, and care across the cancer control continuum.

articles.title: Public Reporting of Vascular Quality Initiative Participation Among Vascular Surgery Training Programs: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Website Disclosure.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) promotes nationwide quality improvement and outcome benchmarking in vascular surgery. This study evaluated the extent to which accredited vascular surgery training programs in the United States publicly advertise participation in the VQI or other quality metrics on institutional websites.MethodsThis descriptive, cross-sectional study used quantitative content analysis. All Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)-accredited vascular surgery programs were identified, and VQI participation was obtained from the Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) website. Program websites were systematically reviewed between December 2023 and January 2024 for mention of VQI participation, VQI star rating, or other quality metrics. VQI registry involvement was then compared between programs that mentioned participation and those that did not. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics.ResultsOf 119 programs, 105 (88.2%) participated in the VQI. Only 34 (32.4%) publicly mentioned participation, and 14 (13.3%) reported their star rating. Among participating programs, mention rates were higher in integrated-only (6/10, 60.0%) and dual-pathway (29/54, 53.7%) compared with fellowship-only programs (13/41, 31.7%). Programs that mentioned participation demonstrated greater involvement across all VQI registries. Over half of all programs (57.1%) reported other quality metrics, including the U.S. News & World Report rankings and the Intersocietal Accreditation Commission (IAC).ConclusionsAlthough VQI participation is nearly universal, public disclosure remains limited compared with other quality measures. Programs that do report participation demonstrate greater VQI registry involvement.

articles.title: Pseudolymphomatous Cutaneous Angiosarcoma of the Scalp: A Clinicopathological Diagnostic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Pseudolymphomatous cutaneous angiosarcoma (cAS) is a rare variant of cAS characterized by a dense lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate that can obscure the underlying malignant endothelial proliferation, mimicking inflammatory dermatoses or cutaneous lymphoid neoplasms, creating a major diagnostic pitfall. We describe a new case and review the existing literature on this rare entity.A 71-year-old man presented with a scaly pruritic eruption that progressed to extensive adherent necrotic plaques with secondary infection. Histological examination revealed a diffuse dermal neoplasm with irregular anastomosing vascular channels accompanied by a dense lymphocytic infiltrate. The diffuse strong expression of endothelial markers (including erythroblast transformation-specific-related gene (ERG)) by the atypical endothelial cells, along with the morphology, confirmed the diagnosis of pseudolymphomatous cAS. The tumor later metastasized to the breast, and the patient died 11 months after the initial diagnosis.This case underscores the significant clinical and histological diagnostic challenges posed by pseudolymphomatous cAS. It also emphasized that despite its clinically deceptive appearance, this variant may follow an aggressive clinical course with metastatic spread and disease-related death. Recognition of this rare variant requires a high index of suspicion, careful clinicopathologic correlation, and awareness of immunohistochemical pitfalls and limitations.

articles.title: Clinical Features and Outcomes of Adenovirus Infections in Critically Ill Patients: A Retrospective Multicenter Case-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Human adenovirus (HAdV) infection can lead to severe organ involvement in the ICU, particularly among immunocompromised patients. In this study of ICU patients with HAdV infection, we aimed to 1) determine the prevalence of HAdV disease, 2) identify risk factors for HAdV disease, and 3) evaluate its association with ICU mortality.

DESIGN: Retrospective, multicenter, and propensity score case-matched study.

SETTING: Eight ICUs in France.

PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients admitted between January 2011 and January 2024 with at least one positive HAdV polymerase chain reaction result from any biological sample were included. HAdV infections were classified as either localized infections or systemic HAdV disease.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 169 patients were analyzed, including 115 patients (68%) classified as localized HAdV infection and 54 patients (32%) as HAdV disease. Hematologic malignancies were significantly more frequent in patients with HAdV disease (74% vs. 37%; p < 0.001). Twenty-three patients (43%) with HAdV disease received allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Pneumonia was the main end-organ manifestation (n = 36/54; 67%). By multivariate analysis, allogeneic HSCT (odds ratio [OR], 3.04) and corticosteroid therapy (OR, 2.89) were independently associated with HAdV disease. ICU mortality was 45% (n = 76). By multivariate analysis, HAdV disease (OR, 3.15), performance status greater than or equal to 2 (OR, 3.35), and Sequential Organ Failure Assessment scores at admission (OR, 1.17 per point) were independently associated with ICU mortality. Mortality remained significantly higher in the HAdV disease group (OR, 10.50) compared with matched ICU patients without HAdV infection.

CONCLUSIONS: HAdV disease occurred in approximately one-third of ICU patients with HAdV infection, predominantly among those with hematologic malignancies or corticosteroid therapy, and was independently associated with mortality.

articles.title: Point-of-Care HbA1c Screening in Dental Settings: Elevated HbA1c and Patient-Reported Prior Glycemic Concerns.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate point-of-care hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) screening yield in dental settings and characterize gaps in patient-reported prior glycemic concern and primary care engagement.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 904 adults. Primary care engagement and prior glycemic concerns were assessed via a pre-visit survey. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression characterized screening yield and factors associated with no reported prior glycemic concern.

RESULTS: 27.3% of patients had elevated HbA1c (≥ 5.7%), including 7.0% in the diabetes range (≥ 6.5%). Among 247 patients with elevated HbA1c, 60.7% reported no prior glycemic concern, rising to 70.1% among those in the prediabetes range. Overall, 31.5% were not engaged with primary care. Those not engaged with primary care had 4.25-fold higher adjusted odds of reporting no prior glycemic concern.

CONCLUSIONS: Dental-based HbA1c screening may complement primary care by identifying elevated HbA1c among patients with and without regular primary care engagement.

articles.title: Recurrent In-Stent Restenosis With Localized Coronary PET Uptake: An Etiologic Challenge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent in-stent restenosis (ISR) may involve localized inflammatory remodeling. Molecular imaging can provide additional information during etiologic assessment.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe 2 patients with ISR in whom multimodality assessment raised the possibility of localized coronary inflammatory remodeling. The first patient had multiple episodes of left anterior descending artery ISR despite repeated drug-coated balloon angioplasty. Fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) showed mild coronary uptake in case 1, who received prednisone after repeat coronary intervention. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET/CT showed mild coronary uptake in case 2, who had autoimmune serological abnormalities. She received prednisone and hydroxychloroquine, followed by planned coronary recanalization with stent implantation 2 months later. Neither had recurrent angina during 18- and 15-month follow-up, respectively.

CONCLUSION: In ISR, coronary tracer uptake on fluorodeoxyglucose- or fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-PET/CT may prompt consideration of a possible inflammatory remodeling process after major mechanical and conventional clinical causes have been assessed.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Recurrent in-stent restenosis warrants a systematic reassessment of mechanical and biological contributors, including possible inflammatory remodeling, to inform subsequent treatment. In selected patients, PET/CT may complement structural assessment and, when interpreted alongside clinical findings, inform individualized multidisciplinary management.

articles.title: Diffuse Lipomatous Infiltration of the Interventricular Septum Presenting as an Incidental Cardiac Lesion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diffuse lipomatous infiltration of the interventricular septum is a rare entity that may mimic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, infiltrative cardiomyopathy, or malignant cardiac pathology, with its natural history and clinical significance remaining incompletely understood.

CASE SUMMARY: A 62-year-old man underwent investigation of an incidental interventricular septal lesion identified on echocardiography. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography demonstrated a poorly circumscribed infiltrative fat-containing lesion, and endomyocardial biopsy and negative mouse double minute 2 fluorescence in situ hybridization supported benign lipomatous infiltration. Two-year follow-up demonstrated sustained clinical and imaging stability.

DISCUSSION: This case provides histopathological, molecular, and longitudinal characterization of a rare form of myocardial lipomatous infiltration.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging are essential for characterizing fat-containing cardiac lesions due to their distinct attenuation and chemical properties. Fat-containing interventricular septal lesions should not be assumed benign when lesion morphology or distribution is atypical, and histopathological and molecular assessment may be required to guide diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Characteristics and Long-Term Outcomes of Patients With History of Malignancy Undergoing Heart Transplantation.
Inflammation-Driven Osteoclast Activity in Charcot Foot: Evidence from Blood and Bone Biomarkers.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: Osteolysis mediated through inflammation and activation of the receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (RANKL)-osteoprotegerin (OPG) pathway has been proposed as a key initiating mechanism of Charcot neuro-osteoarthropathy (CN). The aim of this cross-sectional study was to compare plasma levels and bone tissue expression of RANKL, OPG, and TNF-α among four groups: people with CN, people with diabetes mellitus (DM) and diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN), people with DM without DPN, and healthy individuals. Overall, 59 participants were included: 24 with CN, 10 with DM and DPN, 11 with DM without DPN, and 14 healthy controls. Plasma levels of soluble RANKL (sRANKL), OPG, TNF-α, interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (BALP) were measured. Bone specimens from 38 participants were analyzed by histology and immunohistochemistry to assess RANKL, OPG, and TNF-α expression. CN patients had higher plasma levels of sRANKL [149.5 (114.8, 213.1) versus 75.4 (58.8, 143.8) pmol/L, P = .027], OPG [425.6 (330.1, 568.1) versus 299.6 (199.7, 356.7) pg/mL, P = .005], and TNF-α [3.7 (2.7, 5.3) versus 2.5 (1.6, 2.8) pg/mL, P = .001] compared with patients with DM without DPN. IL-6 levels were higher in CN than in healthy controls [5.91 (0.04, 17.51) versus 0 (0, 0.83) pg/mL; P = .003], as were BALP levels [26.5 (0, 65.5) versus 0 (0, 0) ng/mL; P = .003], whereas IL-1β levels did not differ among groups (P = .362). Bone analysis showed higher expression of RANKL [6.0 (4.0, 8.3) versus 2.0 (2.0, 2.0) and 1.0 (1.0, 1.0)], OPG [6.0 (6.0, 9.0) versus 4.0 (2.0, 4.0) and 1.0 (1.0, 1.0)], and TNF-α [4.0 (3.5, 6.8) versus 2.0 (1.0, 2.0) and 1.0 (1.0, 1.0)] in CN patients compared to those with DM without DPN and healthy controls. These findings support upregulation of inflammatory and osteoclast-regulating pathways in CN, highlighting inflammation-driven bone resorption and DPN-related osteoclast dysregulation.
