articles.title: Long-term recreational soccer participation and 10-year changes in cardiac structure and function in middle-aged women with hypertension.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular risk increases across middle age in women, but the association between sustained recreational soccer participation and long-term cardiac remodelling is unclear. We investigated 10-year changes in echocardiographic measures of cardiac structure and function in middle-aged women with mild-to-moderate hypertension originally randomized to recreational soccer or non-exercise control. The exercise group continued organized recreational soccer participation, completing 1.6 (SD 0.6) sessions/week across the 10-year follow-up. At 10 years, 11 exercisers and 10 controls completed transthoracic echocardiography. Outcomes were analysed using constrained linear mixed-effects models. Left ventricular mass decreased in controls (-12.28 g; 95% CI -23.94 to -0.63; P = 0.0398) but did not change detectably in exercisers (7.39 g; 95% CI -3.81 to 18.59; P = 0.183), yielding a between-group difference in change of 19.67 g (95% CI 4.09 to 35.26; P = 0.0161). The corresponding indexed difference was 11.55 g/m2 (95% CI 2.52 to 20.58; P = 0.0151). Right ventricular internal diameter increased less in exercisers than controls (between-group difference, -0.56 cm; 95% CI -0.87 to -0.25; P = 0.00150). Confidence intervals for diastolic function, tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and left atrial size spanned zero. Long-term recreational soccer participation was associated with differences in selected 10-year cardiac structural changes, but these small exploratory analyses do not establish beneficial remodelling.

articles.title: Incessant Fascicular Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation After MitraClip Procedure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a case of a 52-year-old man with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and advanced renal failure, who presented with electrical storm 4 months after concomitant MitraClip and TriClip procedure for severe functional mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Electrocardiography showed VT with right bundle branch block morphology and superior axis. The VT was refractory to antiarrhythmic drugs and cardioversion despite sedation and hemodynamic support. An emergent electrophysiological study was consistent with fascicular reentry originating from the left posterior fascicle, arising on a background of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy with left ventricular scar. Catheter ablation targeting the left posterior fascicle rendered the VT non-inducible. During one year of device-monitored follow-up, no recurrent ventricular tachycardia (VT) was documented.

articles.title: Association Between Initial Mechanical Power and 28-Day Mortality in Invasively Ventilated Patients: a Retrospective Cohort Study in a Mixed Latin American ICU.
articles.abstract: Background and AimsMechanical power integrates multiple ventilatory variables into a single measure of energy transferred to the respiratory system and has been associated with mortality in critically ill patients. However, evidence from Latin America remains scarce, and no previous large cohort from the region has directly compared mechanical power with driving pressure. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between initial mechanical power and 28-day mortality, and to compare its prognostic performance with driving pressure in a mixed intensive care unit in Latin America.Patients and MethodsA retrospective cohort study included adult patients who required invasive mechanical ventilation for at least 24 h between January and December 2024 in a tertiary care teaching hospital. Mechanical power was calculated from first-24-h ventilatory parameters obtained during controlled ventilation. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. Discriminative performance was assessed with ROC analysis, survival with Kaplan-Meier curves, and independent associations with Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, APACHE II, and SOFA scores.ResultsA total of 496 patients were included; 28-day mortality was 28.4%. Mechanical power was significantly higher in non-survivors than in survivors (18.84 [13.21-23.53] vs 13.93 [10.73-18.06] J/min; P < .001). Discriminative performance was moderate (AUC 0.67; 95% CI 0.62-0.73) and higher than that of driving pressure (AUC 0.61; DeLong P = .025). Patients with mechanical power ≥17 J/min had lower survival (Log-rank P < .001). In the joint Cox model, mechanical power remained independently associated with mortality (HR 1.03; 95% CI 1.02-1.05), whereas driving pressure did not.ConclusionsInitial mechanical power was independently associated with 28-day mortality and provided modest incremental prognostic information compared with driving pressure in this Latin American cohort. These findings are exploratory and require external validation in larger multicenter studies.

articles.title: Pasteurella multocida bacteraemia presenting as septic shock with extensive chest wall cellulitis following a cat bite: A case report.

articles.title: Current rehabilitation approaches in ALS/MND and use of digital health technology; an international survey of occupational therapists and physiotherapists.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Occupational Therapists (OTs) and Physiotherapists (PTs) provide rehabilitation at all stages of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)/motor neurone disease (MND), but research is limited on current rehabilitation practice. In particular, little is known about digital health technology use, which is increasingly available in healthcare. This international online survey investigated current rehabilitation practices and digital health technology use among OTs and PTs.

METHODS: A 46-question survey consisting of open- and closed-ended questions targeted OTs and PTs through professional bodies, special interest groups, and social media. Questions explored symptom management, treatment strategies, and digital health technology use in ALS/MND. Quantitative data were analyzed primarily using descriptive statistics, while open-ended questions were qualitatively analyzed using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: There were 240 responses from 16 countries (OTs = 85; PTs = 155). Respondents worked in ALS/MND for a median of 8 years (IQR 11). Fatigue (61.3%) and spasticity (45%) were the top symptoms often/always managed by respondents. OTs more frequently managed cognition, with PTs more frequently managing cough and secretions, pain, and prescribed exercise (stretches, strengthening, and aerobic). The majority (89%, n = 213) screened for falls. Only a minority (27%, n = 65) used digital health technology in ALS/MND.

CONCLUSION: This survey investigated the current rehabilitation approaches and digital health technology use among OTs and PTs in ALS/MND. The survey confirmed the diverse and varied roles of OTs and PTs, with overlap in fatigue and spasticity management. Digital health technology use was low among OTs and PTs. These findings can inform future research into rehabilitation practices among OTs and PTs and digital health technologies development in ALS/MND.

articles.title: Vaccination, inflammation, and atrial fibrillation: expanding the boundaries of cardiovascular prevention.
Conduction Across the Donor-Recipient Anastomosis as a Substrate for Atrial Arrhythmia After Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Late atrial arrhythmia after heart transplantation is usually attributed to rejection, and the donor-recipient anastomosis is assumed to isolate the native pulmonary venous cuff. We mapped it in three recipients treated with pulsed field ablation. In the first, native posterior wall electrograms cycled at half the tachycardia cycle length and conducted intermittently to the donor atrium until anastomotic ablation isolated them. The second had septal reentry despite a durable anastomosis; the third had reconnection of previously isolated pulmonary veins. Rejection was excluded in all. Although limited to three patients, these findings support mapping the anastomosis before attributing arrhythmia to rejection.

articles.title: Presumed Leflunomide-Induced Lung Injury in a Dog.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe a clinical case of presumed drug-induced lung disease (DILD) caused by leflunomide, including a clinical case summary and a discussion of current veterinary and translational understandings of the diagnostic and therapeutic approach to DILD and the possible relationship between leflunomide use and interstitial lung disease in a dog.

CASE SUMMARY: A 1-year-old intact male mixed-breed dog with a history of steroid-responsive meningitis-arteritis managed on prednisone, leflunomide, and cyclosporine was presented for a 2-day history of coughing, vomiting, lethargy, and anorexia. Thoracic radiographs showed an interstitial pulmonary pattern, while computed tomography showed diffuse pulmonary infiltrates and severe tracheobronchial lymphadenomegaly. Diagnostic testing including fungal serology and airway cytology/culture effectively ruled out infectious etiologies. Because the patient responded completely to a cessation of leflunomide therapy and anti-inflammatory doses of corticosteroids, we suspect these signs were the result of DILD as has been reported with leflunomide use in people.

NEW OR UNIQUE INFORMATION PROVIDED: This is the first report of leflunomide-induced lung disease in veterinary medicine. Clinicians should be aware of the adverse drug event and use caution when considering this medication in patients with preexisting pulmonary disease.

articles.title: Leadless Pacemaker AVEIR VR: Performance of the Rate-Responsive Sensor During Exercise.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To date, no published data have evaluated the exercise performance of the AVEIR VR leadless pacemaker.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to assess, during bicycle ergometer exercise testing, the relationship between the intrinsic sinus heart rate and the ventricular rate delivered by the AVEIR VR pacemaker. Patients with atrial fibrillation or those unable to perform exercise testing were excluded.

METHODS: Patients underwent a bicycle ergometer exercise test using a workload protocol normalized to body weight (W/kg) according to their level of physical activity (sedentary or active). Simultaneous device interrogation was performed throughout the test. Intrinsic sinus heart rate and paced heart rate (or the projected paced heart rate in non-pacemaker-dependent patients) were recorded. Sensor latency was defined as the time required to achieve a 10-beats/min increase in paced heart rate above baseline.

RESULTS: Between January and October 2025, 13 patients were included (69.9 ± 12.7 years; 23% women). Five patients were physically active, and eight patients were pacemaker-dependent. The mean sensor latency was 3.5 min in pacemaker-dependent patients and 2.7 min in non-pacemaker-dependent patients. Rate-response gain required adjustment in 38.5% of patients following exercise testing. Base rate and/or the maximum heart rate response were modified in 76.9% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Exercise testing in patients implanted with an AVEIR VR leadless pacemaker demonstrated an overall appropriate rate-response, although with a non-negligible sensor latency. A substantial proportion of patients required post-exercise optimization of rate-response programming, highlighting the value of exercise-guided device programming to improve physiological chronotropic adaptation.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Multielectrode Mapping Catheter Designs in Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-density (HD) electroanatomical mapping is routinely used for scar-related ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. The performance of multielectrode mapping catheters with different array designs has not been directly compared.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the procedural performance of two different multielectrode mapping catheter designs-a flexible spline catheter (SC) and a fixed paddle catheter (PC) in scar-related VT ablation.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 104 consecutive patients who underwent left ventricular scar-related VT ablation (SC, n = 44; PC, n = 60). The primary endpoint was acute procedural success, defined as non-inducibility of the clinical VT after ablation. Secondary endpoints included procedural efficiency, VT inducibility, VT morphology burden, and procedural and in-hospital adverse events.

RESULTS: Acute procedural success was achieved in 95.5% of SC and 98.3% of PC procedures (p = 0.57). Procedure duration, LV mapping time, mapping point count, fluoroscopy time, and adverse-event rates were comparable between groups. Overall VT inducibility (mechanical or programmed induction) was similar (81.8% vs. 76.7%; p = 0.63); however, ≥3 distinct inducible VT morphologies were significantly more frequent with the spline catheter than with the paddle catheter (38.6% vs. 11.7%; p = 0.002). During follow-up, rates of VT recurrence (34.5% vs. 20.0%; p = 0.19) and repeat ablation (13.8% vs. 7.3%; p = 0.44) did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Both catheter designs achieved comparable acute procedural success, procedural efficiency, and safety in scar-related VT ablation. Procedures with the spline catheter were associated with a higher inducible VT morphology burden; this hypothesis-generating finding, which may partly reflect differences in substrate location, warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: 2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, in collaboration with the European Renal Association (ERA).

articles.title: Learning points for nephrologists from the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, developed in collaboration with the ERA.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract: The brand new '2026 ESC Guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease, developed in collaboration with the ERA' are the first European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines to consider management of both cardiovascular disease (CVD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD), and are unique in their breadth and depth of considerations on the topic. Updated ESC methodology is employed to assess the levels of evidence that support 165 formally structured recommendation statements. These are accompanied by practical treatment algorithms. A key objective was to encourage screening for CKD and basic management of risk of CVD and kidney failure by all clinicians who encounter patients with CKD, with the aim of reducing global disease burden. The full version of the guidelines is reproduced in Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation, and this accompanying report is a synopsis of key learning points for the nephrology community. We particularly highlight when the presence of CKD modifies standard approaches to CVD management. Special consideration is given to practical pre-transplant CVD assessment and avoidance of contrast-induced acute kidney injury without delaying procedures or interventions. The guidance should assist in planning health services to ensure this high-risk patient group with CVD and CKD are managed effectively without prejudice or delay despite potential complexities of co-existent CKD. This synopsis also highlights areas of contention where better evidence is needed and includes a comparison of key points between the 2026 ESC Guidelines and the KDIGO (Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes) 2024 guideline for the evaluation and management of CKD.

articles.title: Assessment of Medical Urgency for Heart Transplant in Patients With Cardiac Amyloidosis and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Using a Continuous Risk Score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current 6-status US heart allocation system uses a treatment-based framework for heart transplantation listing, with status 1 representing the highest urgency. However, this system may inadequately risk-stratify patients with restrictive cardiomyopathy, specifically cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), for whom many high-intensity medical and device-based therapies are less effective.

METHODS: We identified all adult heart transplantation candidates listed between 2019 and 2024 using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. We determined the medical urgency of candidates with CA and HCM using the validated 50-point US-Candidate Risk Score, which incorporates laboratory data and use of mechanical circulatory support.

RESULTS: The study cohort included 26 545 candidates (median age, 56 years; 74% male), of whom 534 were diagnosed with CA (2.0%) and 860 with HCM (3.2%). Overall, patients with CA had significantly higher overall median UC-CRS scores compared with those with HCM and other diagnoses (36, 26, 30; P<0.01), and across statuses 1 to 4. A higher proportion of patients with CA were categorized as high risk (CRS >40) compared with other diagnoses (33% versus 27%; P<0.01), while patients with HCM had the lowest proportion of high-risk scores (22%). Status 2 was the most common status at transplant across all groups, with exceptions at status 2 most frequently used among patients with CA and HCM compared with all others (58%, 70%, 46%; P<0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with CA have higher medical acuity by US-Candidate Risk Score than is reflected in the current 6-status system. Both CA and HCM rely heavily on exceptions to achieve transplantation, highlighting the need for a continuous risk-based allocation model.

articles.title: Weekly Journal Scan: Is aficamten meeting expectations in symptomatic non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?
Desmoplakin Deficiency Disrupts Mechanotransduction and Calcium Homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by progressive myocardial dysfunction and life-threatening arrhythmias. Pathogenic variants in DSP, encoding the desmosomal protein desmoplakin, are among the leading causes of ACM. Although desmosomal disruption is central to disease initiation, the mechanisms linking DSP (desmoplakin) deficiency to arrhythmogenesis and adverse cardiac remodeling remain poorly defined. We investigated the molecular basis of DSP deficiency-mediated ACM and evaluated mechanism-based therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: DSP-deficient mice and human iPSC-based engineered heart tissues were established to evaluate arrhythmogenic phenotypes. YAP1 (yes-associated protein 1)-overexpression and Myo5a (myosin Va) depletion models were generated in vivo and in vitro to validate potential mechanistic links between DSP deficiency and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Mitochondrial reactive oxygen species scavenger MitoTEMPO, adeno-associated virus-mediated CaMKII inhibition using AIP, and genetic introduction of the ryanodine receptor 2-S2814A variant were used to verify mechanism-based therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial dysfunction and CaMKII-dependent calcium dysregulation.

RESULTS: DSP deficiency in vivo and in vitro leads to cytoskeletal disorganization, impaired YAP1-TEAD1 transcriptional activity, and suppressed expression of the mitochondria-skeleton tethering protein Myo5a. These structural and transcriptional alterations are accompanied by mitochondrial impairment, reduced contractile force, and calcium-handling abnormalities in cardiomyocytes. At the tissue and organ levels, these cellular defects increase signal-transduction heterogeneity, ultimately resulting in ventricular arrhythmias. Phenotypic rescue was achieved through multiple interventions: restoring YAP1 signaling, scavenging mitochondrial reactive oxygen species with MitoTEMPO, AAV-mediated CaMKII inhibition with AIP, and genetic introduction of the ryanodine receptor 2-S2814A variant in DSP-deficient iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. All these approaches successfully improved mitochondrial function, restored contractile capability, and alleviated arrhythmia phenotypes in cells, engineered tissues, and mice.

CONCLUSIONS: DSP deficiency drives ACM through a novel mechanotransduction-mitochondrial-calcium signaling axis. These findings elucidate the functional network linking myocardial structure, mitochondrial-calcium homeostasis, and arrhythmic phenotypes, providing potential therapeutic targets for ACM.

articles.title: Time-to-Control: A Missing Dimension of Hypertension Quality.
Effects of Remote Monitoring of Tachy-Devices: A Systematic Review and Component Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote monitoring (RM) is a multicomponent intervention that includes scheduled interrogation and automated alerts in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillators (CRT-Ds); however, the prognostic contribution of its individual components remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the effects of RM components on the prognosis of patients with ICDs or CRT-Ds.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and major clinical trial registries. Randomized controlled trials assessing RM in patients with ICDs or CRT-Ds were included. The primary outcome was hospitalization due to cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or device-related complications. The secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and unscheduled outpatient visits. The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Data were synthesized using random-effects pairwise meta-analysis, random-effects network meta-analysis (NMA), and additive component NMA (CNMA).

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies with 11,502 patients were included. Pairwise meta-analysis showed that RM-based follow-up reduced heart failure hospitalizations compared to in-person follow-up (risk ratio [RR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.74-0.98). NMA indicated that a configuration combining scheduled remote interrogations (≥1 month), automated alerts, and in-person visits (<12 months) was associated with lower cardiovascular mortality than in-person visits (<12 months) (RR 0.43, 95% CI 0.21-0.86). CNMA found no consistent independent associations between the RM components and outcomes.

CONCLUSION: RM reduced heart failure hospitalization, but no individual component showed consistent effects, suggesting that outcomes may depend on the overall configuration rather than isolated components.

articles.title: Catheter Ablation Outcomes in Patients With Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation and Resolved Atrial Thrombus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although anticoagulation therapy can achieve thrombus resolution in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), ablation outcomes in this population remain poorly defined. We compared ablation outcomes between patients with NVAF and resolved atrial thrombus and those without a thrombus history.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled consecutive NVAF patients undergoing initial catheter ablation. Group A (patients with documented atrial thrombus that had resolved prior to ablation) was enrolled between August 2019 and December 2022; Group B (patients without a history of atrial thrombus) was enrolled between July 2022 and December 2022. The primary endpoint was atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence within 12 months, defined as any atrial tachyarrhythmia lasting ≥30 s beyond the 3-month blanking period.

RESULTS: In total, 21 patients in Group A and 291 patients in Group B were analyzed. Compared to patients in Group B, patients in Group A were younger (60.0 [57.0-66.0] years vs. 67.0 [60.0-71.0] years, p = 0.011) and exhibited higher prevalence of non-paroxysmal AF (81.0% vs. 52.6%, p = 0.012), heart failure (28.6% vs. 6.5%, p = 0.001), vascular disease (28.6% vs. 5.5%, p < 0.001), and elevated B-type natriuretic peptide levels (95.2% vs. 59.8%, p = 0.001). Group A demonstrated significantly higher atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence (HR 2.41, 95% CI 1.27-4.55; p = 0.007) and had a higher prevalence of low-voltage areas (LVAs) (66.7% vs 35.1%, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Patients with NVAF and resolved atrial thrombus had a significantly higher atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after catheter ablation, likely reflecting more advanced atrial substrate remodeling, as indicated by the higher prevalence of LVAs.

articles.title: Aging with congenital heart disease: when acquired risk amplifies a congenital substrate.
Weekly Journal Scan: The anticoagulation dilemma in intermediate-risk atrial fibrillation.
Reshaping lead-leaflet interaction: annuloplasty-enabled TEER for complex CIED-related tricuspid regurgitation.
Macrophage CD40 signalling inhibition improves cardiac function after myocardial infarction by limiting fibroblast activation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a dynamic immune response transitioning through inflammatory, reparative, and fibrotic phases. While CD40L-CD40 signalling is central to immune activation, its role in macrophage-driven fibrosis post-MI remains poorly understood.

METHODS: Plasma soluble (s)CD40L was determined in patients with ST-segment elevation MI (STEMI; n = 360). Left ventricular (LV) function was quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) at 5 days and 6 months post-MI. In a murine model of reperfused MI, CD40-TRAF6 signalling was inhibited using TRAF-STOP. LV function was assessed by echocardiography. Cardiac fibrosis was analysed histologically and by qPCR. Cardiac cells were profiled by scRNA-/CITE-seq, flow cytometry, and spatial transcriptomics. Predicted key cell-cell interactions were recapitulated in vitro.

RESULTS: In STEMI patients, sCD40L peaked 5 days post-admission and was associated with scar size, LV remodelling, and re-hospitalization at 6 months. In mice, a CD40+SPP1+ macrophage population with pro-fibrotic marker expression (e.g. Fn1, Nampt, Spp1) emerged transiently at Day 5 post-MI and co-localized with activated fibroblasts. TRAF-STOP treatment initiated 5 days post-MI reduced CD40+SPP1+ macrophage abundance, attenuated fibrotic gene expression, limited scar formation, and improved LV function. In co-culture experiments, TRAF-STOP ameliorated pro-fibrotic macrophage signalling and macrophage-mediated fibroblast activation.

CONCLUSIONS: In STEMI patients, elevated plasma sCD40L at Day 5 post-MI is associated with larger scar size, impaired LV function, adverse remodelling, and an increased rate of re-hospitalization at 6 months. Mechanistically, this is driven by a transient CD40+SPP1+ macrophage population emerging during the reparative phase of MI that is targetable by CD40-TRAF6 inhibition to limit fibrosis and preserve LV function.

articles.title: Diagnostic and prognostic performance of CT pulmonary vascular density in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
articles.journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease that eventually increases pulmonary vascular resistance and leads to right heart failure. Although right heart catheterization remains essential for definitive diagnosis, quantitative information obtained from routinely performed chest computed tomography (CT) may provide complementary noninvasive assessment. We investigated whether CT-derived pulmonary vascular density is associated with the presence and severity of PAH and with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Patients undergoing standard workup for suspected PAH were recruited. Pulmonary vascular density was quantified as the percentage of lung area occupied by small pulmonary vessels with a cross-sectional area <5 mm² (%CSA<5), measured at standardized upper-, middle-, and lower-lung levels. Associations with PAH, pulmonary hemodynamics, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and all-cause mortality were evaluated.

RESULTS: A total of 116 patients were enrolled (median age 57.2 years; 74.1% women), of whom 49 (42.0%) had PAH. Baseline characteristics including NT-proBNP level and tricuspid regurgitation velocity on transthoracic echocardiography were similar between those with and without PAH. Lower pulmonary vascular density, particularly middle-lung %CSA<5, was associated with higher mean pulmonary artery pressure (ρ = -0.197, p = 0.036) and higher NT-proBNP level (ρ = -0.367, p < 0.001). Middle lung %CSA<5 was also associated with the presence of PAH (odds ratio per 1% increase, 0.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.02-0.71). During follow-up, 18 patients died. The discriminative ability of CT-derived vascular density for mortality was modest and comparable to conventional echocardiographic measures (C-statistics = 0.536 versus 0.639). Adding CT-derived vascular density to NT-proBNP improved risk reclassification.

CONCLUSION: Reduced small pulmonary vessel density on chest CT was associated with PAH and greater hemodynamic severity. Quantitative assessment of pulmonary vascular density may provide complementary structural information from CT examinations already obtained during the evaluation of suspected PAH. Further studies are required to determine whether this imaging marker improves diagnosis or risk stratification beyond established clinical assessments.

articles.title: Menstrual health, genitourinary symptoms, and health-seeking behaviour among Santhal tribal women in rural Paschim Bardhaman, West Bengal, India.
articles.abstract: Menstrual health is shaped by socioeconomic conditions, sociocultural norms, and access to appropriate healthcare services. This study assessed menstrual-health practices, self-reported reproductive and genitourinary symptoms, culture-confirmed urinary tract infection, and healthcare-seeking behaviour among Santhal women in rural Paschim Bardhaman, West Bengal, India. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted during 2023-2024 among 180 Santhal women aged 15-49 years in three villages of Faridpur-Durgapur Community Development Block, Paschim Bardhaman district. Participants were recruited through complete enumeration. Structured face-to-face interviews assessed menstrual-health practices, knowledge, restrictions, symptoms, and healthcare-seeking behaviour. Urine samples were collected from 34 participants who underwent culture testing. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and logistic regression. Sixty percent of participants used old clothes, often washed without soap and dried indoors. Among the 34 participants who provided urine samples for culture, 27 (79.4%) had significant bacteriuria; culture positivity was observed in 20 of 22 symptomatic participants and 7 of 12 asymptomatic participants. Illiteracy (adjusted OR [aOR] = 2.35; 95% CI: 1.13-4.65) and lower socioeconomic status (aOR = 2.17; 95% CI: 0.78-3.38) were associated with higher odds of reported reproductive/genitourinary morbidity. Nearly one-third of symptomatic women did not seek professional healthcare, while some relied on self-treatment or local healers. Among women in this study population, unsafe menstruation-management practices, limited menstrual-health knowledge, and incomplete institutional care-seeking were common. Lower literacy and socioeconomic disadvantage were associated with higher reported morbidity.

articles.title: Oral Health-Related Quality of Life and Chronic Disease Trajectories in Occupational Therapy Health Management.
articles.abstract: Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) may be relevant to chronic disease management, yet longitudinal evidence on domain-specific associations with disease accumulation remains limited. This study examined chronic disease trajectories and time-varying associations of OHRQoL dimensions in community-dwelling middle-aged and older adults. Using 2018, 2020, and 2022 Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA) data, latent growth modeling (LGM) was conducted in 5,733 participants. Chronic disease count increased over time with significant individual variability. Physical function was associated with chronic disease count in 2020 and 2022, pain/discomfort in 2022, and psychosocial function in 2020. These findings suggest that multidimensional oral health assessment may help occupational therapists identify health-management needs related to eating, symptom and medication management, and social participation, supporting oral health integration within the Health Management domain of the Occupational Therapy Practice Framework-Fourth Edition (OTPF-4).

articles.title: Building and Sustaining the Disease Intervention Workforce: A Rapid Scoping Review-Informed Framework.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The disease intervention (DI) workforce is essential for preventing and controlling infectious diseases, yet variability in roles and training hampers workforce stability and effectiveness. Certification may help standardize competencies, but its implementation requires understanding workforce barriers, benefits, and feasible solutions. This project aimed to identify factors that influence DI workforce certification and develop a framework to inform certification pathways.

METHODS: We conducted a rapid scoping review following an a priori protocol and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. We searched PubMed, MEDLINE Complete, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and Google Scholar for US-based sources published during 2014-2025. Two independent reviewers screened records and extracted data using pilot-tested tools; disagreements were resolved through consensus, with a third reviewer consulted as needed. We inductively coded benefits, barriers, and solutions; mapped them to Public Health Accreditation Board certification objectives; and refined themes by consensus into a multidomain framework.

RESULTS: Thirty-five sources met the inclusion criteria. Analysis identified benefits (n = 37), barriers (n = 40), and solutions (n = 27) distributed across organizational, workforce, and community domains. Benefits aligned with standardized competencies, stronger career pathways, and enhanced service capacity. Barriers included workforce shortages, limited training infrastructure, inconsistent expectations, and challenges in meeting broad community needs. Solutions emphasized academic-practice partnerships, regionally adaptable training, employer support, and strategies to improve workforce stability and preparedness.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight multiple determinants that may shape DI workforce certification. The resulting framework offers an initial structure for guiding certification standards and strategies to strengthen and sustain a DI workforce that is prepared for current and future infectious disease threats.

articles.title: Functional single ventricle with Scimitar syndrome diagnosed prenatally using fetal MRI.
articles.abstract: Scimitar syndrome is a type of partial anomalous pulmonary venous return. When isolated, its prognosis is not poor. However, when combined with a functional single ventricle, the prognosis is extremely poor. Furthermore, prenatal diagnosis of Scimitar syndrome by fetal echocardiography is challenging, and most cases are diagnosed after birth. A case of Scimitar syndrome that was diagnosed prenatally using fetal MRI performed to evaluate a hypoplastic right lung in a fetus with a functional single ventricle is presented.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Protein Quality Control as a Hierarchical Defense System in Health and Disease.
articles.abstract: Mitochondria sustain energy production, metabolism and cellular stress responses, yet their function depends on the continuous delivery and maintenance of many proteins. Most mitochondrial proteins are made outside the organelle and must enter the correct compartment, fold and assemble before becoming functional. Defects at any of these steps can threaten both mitochondrial and cellular health. This Review organizes mitochondrial protein quality control (MpQC) into four interconnected functional tiers: (1) monitoring proteins before and during mitochondrial import; (2) folding and removal of damaged proteins inside mitochondria; (3) remodeling and selective recycling of mitochondrial components or entire organelles; and (4) communication of mitochondrial stress to broader cellular response pathways. These tiers interact rather than forming a fixed sequence, and their effects depend on stress intensity, duration and tissue context. We distinguish established pathways from emerging or debated mechanisms and examine how initially protective responses may become harmful under persistent stress. Finally, we consider their relevance to ageing, neurodegeneration and metabolic disease, and highlight unresolved questions for future research.

articles.title: Primary Neurolymphomatosis with Multiple Neural and Systemic Lesions Depicted by Digital 18F-FDG-PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Primary neurolymphomatosis (NL) is a rare manifestation of malignant lymphoma defined by neural involvement present at diagnosis. The increasing use of magnetic resonance imaging and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has improved recognition of NL. We report a case of a 73-year-old Japanese man with histologically confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, whose pretreatment 18F-FDG-PET/CT showed multiple lesions in cranial, spinal, and peripheral nerves, as well as systemic involvement (including lymph nodes, adrenal glands, testes, the right knee joint, and lower-limb bones), thus demonstrating both neural and widespread extranodal disease.

articles.title: Feasibility, Renal Safety, and Clinical Outcomes of Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Very Elderly Patients: A Retrospective Comparison With Intravascular Ultrasound.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution intracoronary imaging that can improve the outcomes of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, OCT requires contrast media, raising concerns regarding renal safety in very elderly patients.

AIMS: This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, renal safety, and clinical outcomes of OCT-guided PCI compared with intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided PCI in very elderly patients.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients aged ≥ 85 years who underwent elective PCI at a single center (April 2019-May 2025). Procedures were divided into OCT-guided and IVUS-guided PCI groups. The primary endpoints were procedural success, procedural complications, contrast volume, and kidney injury. The secondary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after discharge.

RESULTS: Ninety-four PCI procedures were analyzed (OCT, n = 38; IVUS, n = 56). The mean age was 88.0 ± 2.6 years, and baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 46.0 ± 15.1 mL/min/1.73 m2. Before adjustment, contrast volume was higher in the OCT group than in the IVUS group (p = 0.027); however, OCT use was not independently associated with contrast volume after adjustment (p = 0.37). OCT use was not significantly associated with the eGFR change ratio (p = 0.48), procedural complications (p = 0.33), or post-discharge MACE (p = 0.93). Baseline eGFR was significantly associated with the eGFR change ratio (p = 0.015) and post-discharge MACE (p = 0.049).

CONCLUSIONS: OCT-guided PCI was feasible in very elderly patients and was not associated with worse renal or clinical outcomes than IVUS-guided PCI when careful contrast management was applied.

articles.title: HspBp1 Promotes Tau Pathology and Cognitive Impairments by Inhibiting STUB1(CHIP)-Mediated Tau Ubiquitination.
articles.abstract: Tau pathology is a core neuropathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD), increasing evidence indicates that disruption of protein quality control contributes to Tau accumulation. However, the upstream modulators that impair Tau clearance are poorly defined. Heat shock protein 70-binding protein 1 (HspBp1), a co-chaperone of the E3 ubiquitin ligase STUB1 (CHIP), has been implicated in proteostasis regulation, but its role in Tau pathology remains unknown. We found that HspBp1 was selectively expressed in hippocampal neurons and markedly upregulated in the hippocampus of aged AD mice. Neuron-specific overexpression of HspBp1 exacerbated Tau and Tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic and dendritic degeneration and cognitive impairments, whereas HspBp1 downregulation significantly attenuated Tau-induced neuropathology and cognitive deficits. Mechanistically, HspBp1 reduced STUB1 levels and disrupted STUB1-Tau interactions, leading to decreased Tau ubiquitination and impaired proteasomal degradation. Consequently, Tau accumulated and underwent pathological hyperphosphorylation. Importantly, restoration of STUB1 expression largely abolished HspBp1-induced Tau accumulation, synaptic dysfunction and cognitive deficits. Meanwhile, upregulation of STUB1 improves Tau pathology and cognitive impairments in P301S mice. These findings support HspBp1 as an age-associated modulator that promotes Tau pathology by suppressing STUB1-mediated Tau ubiquitination and degradation. Targeting the HspBp1-STUB1 axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.

articles.title: From Emerging Vectors to Missed Fevers: Why Fragile Health Systems Need Integrated Fever-Vector Preparedness.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract: Climate change, urbanization, population mobility, and expanding mosquito vectors are reshaping infectious-disease risks in fragile health systems, where surveillance, diagnosis, and response often remain fragmented. This Policy Analysis argues that preparedness should move beyond isolated pathogen- or vector-specific programs toward an integrated fever-vector model. Undifferentiated fever should serve as the clinical entry point linking environmental intelligence, entomological surveillance, sentinel fever surveillance, tiered laboratory testing, and public health response. Such integration could improve recognition of arboviral infections overlooked in malaria-centered systems, support earlier outbreak detection, and guide targeted vector control and diagnostic preparedness. Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa illustrate the urgency of this shift because climate shocks, displacement, weak laboratory systems, and emerging urban vector-borne risks increasingly converge. The priority is not a more technologically complex system, but a connected and sustainable preparedness architecture capable of linking emerging vectors with febrile illnesses presenting in routine care.

articles.title: Clarifying Equivocal 99mTc-Sestamibi Scintigraphy: 18F-fluorocholine PET/CT and PET/MRI Co-Registration Unveil Parathyroid Adenoma and Skull Brown Tumor in Suspected MEN-1.
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 50-year-old woman with a history of acromegaly who was evaluated for persistent hypercalcemia and elevated parathyroid hormone levels. Previous examinations, such as neck ultrasound and parathyroid scintigraphy with technetium-99m-sestamibi, were not conclusive for adenoma. 18F-fluorocholine (18F-CH) positron emission tomography (PET)/computed tomography showed focal pathological uptake in the retrothyroid region compatible with parathyroid adenoma and intense uptake at the level of the cranial vault in the occipital region. PET/magnetic resonance imaging co-registration also demonstrated 18F-CH accumulation in the known pituitary microadenoma and in the occipital lesion. The bone lesion, initially considered an angioma, was reinterpreted as a brown tumor and was subsequently confirmed histologically. This case highlights the role of 18F-CH PET in the localization of occult parathyroid adenomas and in the correct interpretation of bone lesions in a possible context of multiple endocrine neoplasia.

articles.title: Inguinal Hernia Sac Implantation on 18F-FDG PET/CT in Uterine Serous Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: A 62-year-old woman underwent whole-body 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) for staging. Imaging demonstrated an intensely 18F-FDG avid uterine mass measuring 130×120×100 mm, periuterine and interaortocaval metastatic lymph nodes, and an abdominal extra-pelvic peritoneal implant establishing FIGO 2023 stage IVB disease. In addition, a 33×27 mm 18F-FDG-avid lesion was identified within the left inguinal hernia sac, compatible with an unusual localization of peritoneal dissemination. This case illustrates the value of 18F-FDG PET/CT in demonstrating atypical metastatic sites and mapping the extent of disease through whole-body imaging.

articles.title: Interval Progression Before 177Lu-PSMA Mimicking Treatment Failure on Interim PSMA PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Interpretation of follow-up prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) during lutetium-177-labeled PSMA (177Lu-PSMA) radioligand therapy (RLT) may be misleading if rapid disease progression occurs between baseline PSMA PET/CT and initiation of RLT. A 78-year-old man with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer underwent baseline gallium-68-PSMA PET/CT to assess eligibility for 177Lu-PSMA-RLT and was deemed eligible. Interim PSMA PET/CT after 2 cycles showed multiple new lesions and an increased total tumor burden, suggesting progressive disease. However, these lesions were already visible on post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT)/CT after cycle 1, indicating interval progression between baseline PSMA PET/CT and initiation of 177Lu-PSMA-RLT rather than treatment failure. In rapidly progressive disease, cycle-1 post-therapy SPECT/CT may provide a true imaging baseline for response assessment.

articles.title: Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma with Tumour Thrombus Extending Into the Superior Vena Cava Demonstrated by Multimodality Imaging.
articles.abstract: Macroscopic venous tumor thrombus is an uncommon manifestation of differentiated thyroid carcinoma and is more frequently associated with follicular thyroid carcinoma than papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). We report a 45-year-old woman with PTC comprising follicular (80%) and solid (20%) subtypes, extensive vascular invasion, and tumour thrombus extending from the right internal jugular vein into the superior vena cava (SVC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) delineated the intravascular extent. Following total thyroidectomy and thrombus resection, three iodine-131 treatments totalling 16.65 GBq were administered over 22 months. Serial post-therapy imaging demonstrated persistent iodine-avid pulmonary, left acetabular, and intravascular disease, while stimulated thyroglobulin increased from 150,002 to 232,920 ng/mL. Subsequent 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/CT showed thyroid bed recurrence, pulmonary and skeletal metastases, and prominent 18F-FDG uptake within the SVC tumour thrombus. These findings confirmed viable intravascular tumour and demonstrated phenotypic heterogeneity, raising concern for evolution toward radioiodine-refractory disease and supporting referral for multidisciplinary assessment of systemic therapy.

articles.title: The Prognostic Value of 18F-FDG PET/CT Parameters in Mantle Cell Lymphoma: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is an aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma for which accurate early prognostication is crucial. This study primarily investigated the potential of quantitative metabolic parameters derived from baseline and interim 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) scans to independently predict treatment response and survival outcomes in patients with MCL.

METHODS: A total of 48 newly diagnosed MCL patients were retrospectively enrolled in a cohort; of these, 32 patients had interim PET/CT scans analyzed. Semi-quantitative parameters, including standardized uptake value (SUV) and its normalizations, alongside quantitative volumetric parameters such as total body metabolic tumor volume (tMTV) and total body total lesion glycolysis (tTLG), were measured. Independent prognostic factors were determined by Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: A strong reduction in SUV, tTLG, and tMTV values between baseline and interim PET/CT verified a significant metabolic response to treatment. Interim volumetric parameters, specifically tTLG and tMTV, demonstrated superior performance in predicting treatment response. Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified tMTV and SUV normalized to body surface area (SUVbsa) as independent prognostic factors for progression-free survival (PFS). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that high baseline SUVbsa and high interim SUV values were strongly associated with poor survival outcomes. Overall survival was not independently associated with any PET/CT parameter in the multivariate model.

CONCLUSION: In MCL patients, baseline SUVbsa and quantitative parameters derived from interim PET/CT are powerful and independent biomarkers for PFS. These data can improve prognostic stratification and guide risk-adapted therapies by enabling the early identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: A Silent Traveler: 18F-FDG-negative Intravascular Leiomyomatosis with Intracardiac Extension.
articles.abstract: Intravascular leiomyomatosis (IVL) is a rare entity, which may present with leiomyomas. IVL is characterized by intravascular proliferation of smooth muscle cells. It may develop independently or originate from uterine leiomyoma and extend into the adjacent pelvic veins with possible extension into the inferior vena cava and beyond. It may or may not be symptomatic and often is an incidental finding on radiological imaging. To evaluate its extent, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) play an important role. We illustrate an interesting case in which non avid pelvic masses with filling defect in pelvic veins extending into the inferior vena cava and right atrium was detected on oncological 18F-FDG PET/CT acquired for known right parotid gland mucoepidermoid carcinoma. Later, post surgical histopathology revealed leiomyomas and IVL.

articles.title: An Incidental Case of Inflammatory Myopathy Detected During Oncologic 18F-FDG PET/CT Imaging.
articles.abstract: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) is widely used in oncologic imaging; however, unexpected skeletal muscle uptake on oncologic 18F-FDG PET/CT is a relatively frequent incidental finding, with a substantial proportion attributable to benign inflammatory conditions. Inflammatory myopathies may demonstrate increased FDG uptake through mechanisms similar to those in malignancy and may mimic metastatic disease, posing a diagnostic challenge in oncologic imaging. In this case, we aimed to demonstrate incidental 18F-FDG uptake related to inflammatory myopathy detected on oncologic 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging.

articles.title: Post-cardiac Injury Syndrome as a Cause of False-positive 18F-FDG PET/CT for Infection.
articles.abstract: Post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) is an autoimmune inflammatory condition that may occur weeks after cardiac surgery and can closely mimic infection on 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT). We report the case of a 53-year-old woman who presented six weeks after aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic graft implantation, with persistent chest pain, fever, and elevated inflammatory markers, raising the suspicion of infective endocarditis. Whole-body PET demonstrated intense, heterogeneous 18F-FDG uptake along the sternotomy site and the ascending aortic graft, findings typically suggestive of infection, whereas no abnormal uptake was observed at the prosthetic valve. Despite these imaging findings, repeated blood cultures and surgical site samples remained negative. A diagnosis of Dressler syndrome, a form of PCIS, was ultimately established. Treatment with high-dose aspirin led to rapid clinical and biological improvement. This case points to a significant diagnostic pitfall in 18F-FDG PET/CT in the postoperative setting and underscores the importance of integrating imaging findings with clinical and microbiological data to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary antibiotic therapy.

articles.title: Spatial trends in multiple micronutrient supplementation effects on low birth weight and infant wasting in rural Bangladesh: a secondary geospatial analysis of the JiVitA-3 randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine spatial patterns in low birth weight (LBW) and infant wasting across the JiVitA-3 study area and assess whether the effects of antenatal multiple micronutrient supplementation (MMS) vary along the same geographic gradients as socio-economic status and dietary diversity.

DESIGN: We conducted a secondary analysis of the JiVitA-3 cluster randomised trial comparing MMS to iron-folic acid (IFA). Outcomes included LBW (<2500 g) and thin mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) at birth (<9 cm), 1 month (<11 cm) and 3, 6 and 12 months (<11·5 cm). Spatial intensity surfaces of LBW and thin MUAC relative to normal values were estimated. Generalised estimating equation Poisson regression models assessed MMS v. IFA effects, adjusting for socio-economic status, maternal dietary diversity, education, parity, BMI and gestational age. Geographic effect modification by longitude was evaluated using natural cubic splines. Modeled relative risks were smoothed and mapped.

SETTING: Rural northwest Bangladesh.

PARTICIPANTS: 21 975 singleton live births within geolocated households.

RESULTS: LBW and infant wasting exhibited a clear east-west gradient, with higher risk in the more rural east. MMS reduced risk of LBW (RR 0·86, 95 % CI: 0·83, 0·90) and thin MUAC at birth (RR 0·90, 0·84-0·97), 1 month (RR 0·89, 0·86-0·92) and 3 months (RR 0·86, 0·80-0·94), but not at 6 or 12 months. Spatial effect modification was present for LBW (Wald interaction coefficient p value <0·001) and thin birth MUAC (p = 0·016). Outcomes and modelled relative risks had visually concordant spatial patterning.

CONCLUSIONS: While LBW and infant wasting varied geographically, the protective effect of MMS was uniform across space, supporting universal distribution. Additional interventions are needed beyond infancy.

articles.title: Coexistence of Granulomatous Inflammation and Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Diagnostic Pitfall in 18F-FDG PET/CT.
18F-FDG-avid Lytic Mandibular Metastasis Mimicking Dental Pathology in a Case Diagnosed with Esophageal Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophageal adenocarcinoma is an aggressive malignancy that frequently metastasizes to lymph nodes, the liver, lungs, and adrenal glands. Mandibular metastasis is rare and can clinically mimic dental infections. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography imaging showed intense 18F-FDG uptake in a lytic mandibular lesion initially interpreted as dental pathology. Follow-up imaging revealed that it was part of systemic metastatic bone disease, supported by concomitant iliac bone involvement. This case report serves as a diagnostic reminder that mandibular lesions showing 18F-FDG uptake in oncology patients should prompt careful hybrid imaging evaluation rather than being reflexively attributed to dental pathology.

articles.title: Additive Value of Whole-body CT in Patients Imaged with PET/CT for Solitary Pulmonary Nodules.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In routine positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging of solitary pulmonary nodules (SPNs), CT acquisition is typically performed from the vertex to the mid-thigh. The administered 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) dose is adjusted according to patient weight and is independent of the scanned body region; however, radiation exposure from the CT component increases with scan length. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the clinical value of extrathoracic CT imaging in patients undergoing PET/CT for SPN characterization and to quantify the potential reduction in radiation dose when CT is limited to the thorax.

METHODS: A total of 154 patients who underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT for the evaluation of SPNs between 2009 and 2011 were retrospectively analyzed. None of the patients had a prior diagnosis of malignancy or had received chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Incidental extrathoracic CT findings were classified as major, moderate, or minor according to their clinical significance. CT radiation dose was estimated using dose-length product (DLP) values. PET findings, incidental CT findings, radiation dose, and acquisition times were evaluated.

RESULTS: Extrathoracic CT findings were detected in 61 patients (39%), with a total of 86 incidental lesions. However, only 3 patients (2%) had major extrathoracic findings requiring urgent clinical intervention. Two of these were osteolytic bone lesions that were 18F-FDG avid and potantially detectable on whole-body PET. Extrathoracic 18F-FDG uptake was observed in 10 patients (6.5%). The mean DLP was 458.3±70.5 mGy cm for whole-body CT and 130.8±9.1 mGy cm for thorax-only CT, corresponding to a 3.5-fold higher CT radiation dose (p<0.01). A PET-based protocol, however, prolongs acquisition time by approximately 6 minutes.

CONCLUSION: In SPN PET/CT evaluation, routine body CT does does not provide clinically significant additional information in most patients but substantially increases radiation exposure. Performing thoracic CT following whole-body PET, with additional targeted CT only when extrathoracic PET abnormalities are detected, may reduce radiation exposure while preserving the diagnostic information provided by CT of the thorax. However, such an approach prolongs acquisition time and increases workload.

articles.title: Shiitake Mushroom Extract (AHCC®): Enhancing Clearance of HPV Infection with Clinical Evidence.
articles.abstract: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection underlies a wide spectrum of anogenital disease, including genital warts, intraepithelial neoplasia, and HPV-related malignancy. Although prophylactic vaccination is highly effective, it does not provide therapeutic benefit for established infection, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies that enhance host antiviral immunity. Active Hexose Correlated Compound (AHCC®), a standardized extract derived from Lentinula edodes mycelia, has demonstrated immunomodulatory and immunoenhancing effects through regulation of cytokine signalling and activation of natural killer and T-cell responses. Pilot clinical studies and subsequent randomized clinical investigations in women with persistent high-risk HPV infection have shown significantly higher viral clearance rates with AHCC® compared with placebo, accompanied by normalization of immune biomarkers. In patients treated for condyloma acuminata, AHCC® supplementation has been associated with reduced recurrence. Although clinical data in men are lacking, the shared immunopathogenesis of cervical and penile HPV infection supports a plausible role for AHCC® in male genital disease, including genital warts and penile intraepithelial neoplasia. AHCC® therefore represents a promising, safe immunomodulatory adjunct in HPV-related dermatoses that warrants further investigation in male cohorts.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of HER2-ICI Combination Therapy in Solid Tumours: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combining human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted agents with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is an emerging treatment strategy for solid tumours. However, the pooled efficacy and safety profiles of HER2-ICI combination therapy and HER2-targeted monotherapy remain uncertain.

METHODS: Four databases were searched from inception to June 3, 2025. We screened randomised controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomised trials (non-RCTs) and single-arm studies using HER2-ICI combination therapy or HER2-targeted monotherapy. The population comprised patients with solid tumours.

RESULTS: We analyzed 40 studies with 4,670 patients. The pooled CR estimates were 9.1% for combination therapy and 3.3% for monotherapy (p = 0.049), whereas the pooled ORR and DCR estimates were similar. The pooled mPFS estimates were 5.22 months for combination therapy and 6.86 months for monotherapy. The pooled mOS data were unavailable for combination therapy, whereas the pooled mOS estimate for monotherapy was 18.64 months (I2 = 93.9%). The pooled estimates of grade 5 TRAEs were 3.6% for combination therapy and 1.2% for monotherapy (p = 0.021), and the corresponding TRSAE estimates were 23.3% and 13.5%, respectively (p = 0.018). The pooled estimates of dose reduction due to TRAEs were 10.0% and 22.7%, respectively (p = 0.025).

CONCLUSIONS: HER2-ICI combination therapy showed a higher pooled CR estimate and higher pooled estimates of selected serious safety outcomes, but an mPFS or mOS advantage could not be established. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of comparative superiority.

articles.title: Epidemiology and Mechanisms of Gastric Cancer in Cold Regions: Multifactorial Interactions and Region-Specific Biomarkers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUD: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a leading global malignancy with distinct epidemiological patterns across geographical zones.

METHODS: This review comprehensively analyzed the epidemiological patterns, biomarker profiles, and molecular mechanisms of GC in cold regions, offering an innovative perspective on the interplay between environmental, genetic, and microbiological factors.

RESULTS: Cold geographic zones, including high-latitude and high-altitude areas, exhibit a disproportionately high GC incidence attributable to chronic cold exposure, high-salt dietary habits, vitamin D deficiency, and high prevalence of Helicobacter pylori infection with enhanced virulence genotypes such as CagA+ /VacA+ /OipA+. The study identifies and categorizes novel region-specific biomarkers - including virulence factors, epigenetic regulators (e.g. CDH1, methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR), miR-21), and metabolic markers like short chain fatty acids (SCFAs) - and delineates their roles in dysregulating key pathways including Wnt/β-catenin signalling and hypoxia-induced angiogenesis. A significant contribution lies in establishing a multifactorial mechanistic framework that links cold climate stressors with gastric carcinogenesis through immune modulation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota alterations.

CONCLUSIONS: These insights facilitate the development of targeted prevention protocols and climate-adapted therapeutic interventions for high-risk populations in cold regions.

articles.title: The Emerging Role of PPM1A and PPM1B in Regulating Cell Death and Their Implications for Disease Therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protein kinases and phosphatases stringently regulate phosphorylation and dephosphorylation to coordinate this vital cell process. While protein kinases add phosphate groups to proteins, protein phosphatases remove them by hydrolysis, acting as complementary regulators in cellular signalling. Protein phosphorylation and dephosphorylation are important for regulating protein function and programmed cell death pathways. Protein phosphatase, Mg2+/Mn2+-dependent, 1A (PPM1A) and protein phosphatase, Mg2+/Mn2+-dependent, 1B (PPM1B) are metal-dependent serine/threonine phosphatases that dephosphorylate substrates to regulate many biological processes and diseases.

METHODS: This review summarises recent studies investigating the roles of PPM1A and PPM1B in cell death pathways and their implications across various diseases, as well as current advances in the development of specific inhibitors and activators targeting these phosphatases.

RESULTS: PPM1A and PPM1B are implicated in multiple cellular death pathways, including apoptosis, autophagy, necroptosis and PANoptosis. They are also associated with various diseases, including infectious, neurodegenerative and malignant diseases. Furthermore, specific inhibitors and activators targeting PPM1A and PPM1B have been investigated, highlighting their potential as therapeutic targets.

CONCLUSIONS: PPM1A and PPM1B play important roles in regulating cellular death pathways and disease-associated processes. A better understanding of their biological functions and the development of specific modulators may provide valuable insights into potential therapeutic strategies for diverse pathological conditions.

articles.title: Association of Urine Specific Gravity With Hemoglobin Concentration in Chronic Kidney Disease, Independent of eGFR and Proteinuria.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 10% of the global population. Current staging relies on glomerular markers (estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] and proteinuria), which may not fully capture kidney dysfunction. Urine specific gravity (SG) is a functional marker of urinary concentrating ability that may provide complementary information. We evaluated whether lower urine SG is independently associated with lower hemoglobin concentration after adjustment for eGFR, proteinuria, and other clinical covariates. MATERIAL AND METHODS This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1064 patients with CKD not receiving dialysis with paired morning urine SG and hemoglobin levels within 7 days at a tertiary center in Warsaw, Poland (2019-2025). Patients on dialysis, with transplantation, or active malignancy were excluded. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin <13.0 g/dL for men and <12.0 g/dL for women. Multivariable linear regression assessed the SG-hemoglobin association, adjusting for eGFR, age, sex, diabetes, heart failure, acute kidney injury, and dipstick proteinuria. RESULTS Urine SG was independently associated with hemoglobin (ß=0.607 g/dL per 0.010-unit increase; 95% CI, 0.396-0.817; P<0.001), with a graded association across groups (P for trend <0.001). In advanced CKD (eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m²), median hemoglobin concentration was 13.0 g/dL in the high-SG group and 11.9 g/dL in the low-SG group (Hodges-Lehmann location shift, 0.9 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.3-1.6; P=0.008). Results remained robust in sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS Higher urine SG was independently associated with higher hemoglobin in non-dialysis CKD. This cross-sectional association does not establish causality or support using SG alone for anemia assessment or treatment decisions. Prospective validation is needed.

articles.title: Invasive Fungal Rhinosinusitis in Gaza: 3 Cases From Nasser Medical Complex.
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal rhinosinusitis is a rapidly progressive, life-threatening infection that requires immediate intervention. In this case series, we describe 3 patients with suspected invasive fungal rhinosinusitis who were managed at Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Yunis, Palestine, between February and May 2026. All patients underwent multidisciplinary management and, when applicable, surgical debridement. Two of the 3 patients died, while the surviving patient had persistent facial nerve paralysis.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Outpouchings.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular outpouchings are being increasingly detected by imaging modalities. Diverse anatomical and pathological entities may manifest as a left ventricular outpouching filled with contrast material or blood on imaging studies. These outpouchings frequently display similarities and are often unfamiliar to radiologists and clinicians, leading to difficulty upon identification. Many outpouchings can be accurately identified or excluded during standard imaging, while others may require further evaluation by electrocardiographically gated contrast-enhanced computed tomography or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging for a definitive diagnosis. Distinguishing between these entities is essential for efficient management, as their outcomes differ markedly.

articles.title: Prevalence and clinical significance associated with different morphologies of left ventricular wall thickening.
articles.abstract:
INTRO: As recognition of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with milder phenotypes presenting later in life increases, differentiation from age-related sigmoid septal remodeling becomes increasingly important." This study seeks to describe the prevalence and clinical associations of basal septal hypertrophy and compare its clinical profile with other patterns of left ventricular wall thickening.

METHODS: From 2012 to 2019, this study identified 4,622 initial echocardiograms with normal left ventricular systolic function without significant aortic or mitral dysfunction. Wall morphology was divided into 4 groups: normal septal and posterior wall thickness (n=3,126, 67.6%), thickened septal and posterior wall (concentric thickening; n=1,010, 21.9%), basal septum 12-15 mm with normal posterior wall (basal septal hypertrophy, n=423, 9.2%), and basal septum > 15 mm with normal posterior wall (n=58, 1.2%). Univariate and multivariate regressions models were created to describe the relationship between wall morphology with hypertension and heart failure. Further, stratified analyses were used to describe the relationship of age with wall morphology. Models were adjusted for baseline demographics and clinical covariates.

RESULTS: The study participants were 22% Black, 53% female with a mean age of 55.8 ± 16.6 years. Clinically, 12.9% and 59.6% were diagnosed with heart failure and hypertension, respectively. Prevalence of both concentric thickening and increased basal septal thickness increased with age (see figure 1). Relative to normal thickness, all forms of thickening were associated with coronary disease, heart failure, and hypertension (all: p<0.001), but only concentric thickening was associated with diabetes mellitus (p<0.001). In multivariate analyses, all forms of thickening were associated with hypertension, but only concentric thickening was independently associated with heart failure (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Basal septal hypertrophy and concentric thickening were both associated with advancing age and hypertension. Only concentric thickening remained associated with heart failure after multivariable adjustment. These findings describe differing clinical profiles among wall-thickening phenotypes but should not be interpreted as evidence of causality. Further studies are needed to guide clinicians in differentiating pressure overload-related BSH from other distinct clinical phenotypes.

articles.title: Molecular characterisation of norovirus GII.4 Sydney [P16] among children with acute gastroenteritis in Sabah of Malaysian Borneo.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Norovirus (NoV) is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE), especially in children under 5 years old, with significant morbidity in middle-income countries like Malaysia. This study aimed to detect and characterise the NoV among children with acute gastroenteritis in 2019 to 2020.

METHODOLOGY: Stool samples from 124 children with watery diarrhoea were extracted and analysed using RT-PCR, nucleotide sequencing, and phylogenetic analyses.

RESULTS: NoV was detected in 27/124 (21.8%) samples, with GII (81.5%) being the predominant genogroup, followed by GI (18.5%). Phylogenetic analysis revealed GII.4[P16] as the most common strain, followed by GII.6[P7]. GII.4 Sydney 2012 strains showed high nucleotide identity to the reference strains from different geographical regions. GII.6 strains showed limited changes compared to earlier studies but warrant attention due to their increasing global presence. Children aged 0-23 months had higher odds (6.7 times) of NoV infection, likely due to behavioural factors and lack of immunity.

CONCLUSION: This study observed an increase in NoV proportion from 17.7% in 2018-2019 to 21.8% in 2019-2020 and changes in predominant genotypes. These findings emphasise the importance of continuous surveillance to track NoV genetic diversity and guide vaccine development, particularly in middle-income countries with high AGE morbidity but low mortality. Future studies should focus on broader geographic coverage and longer surveillance periods to better understand NoV epidemiology in Malaysia.

articles.title: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy and the development of heart failure in patients with liver cirrhosis: from hyperdynamic circulation to impaired cardiac reserve.
articles.abstract: Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM) is a syndrome comprising functional, structural, electrophysiological, and molecular cardiac abnormalities that develop in the setting of liver cirrhosis in the absence of another primary cardiac disorder sufficient to explain the observed phenotype. Myocardial dysfunction may remain clinically silent at rest, as reduced afterload and hyperdynamic circulation can preserve or even increase left ventricular ejection fraction. Progressive portal hypertension and splanchnic vasodilatation, together with neurohormonal activation, chronic inflammation, and disruption of the gut-liver-heart axis, contribute to adverse myocardial remodelling and impaired cardiac function. These mechanisms are associated with impaired relaxation, attenuated chronotropic and inotropic responses, and progressive exhaustion of cardiac reserve. Clinically, this continuum may evolve from subclinical diastolic dysfunction and reduced global longitudinal strain to overt heart failure, most commonly presenting as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or high-output heart failure. In advanced cases, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and right ventricular failure may develop. Haemodynamic stress during infection, bleeding, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement, and liver transplantation is of particular clinical relevance. This review discusses the mechanisms underlying the development of heart failure, contemporary diagnostic criteria for CCM, the role of cardiac reserve assessment, biomarkers, and cardiac magnetic resonance, as well as therapeutic implications.The potential contribution of hypergammaglobulinaemia to myocardial injury remains speculative, and a causal relationship has not been established.

articles.title: Robot-assisted kidney autotransplantation across indications and platforms: a systematic review and sparse-event meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: We assessed reported safety and clinical outcomes of robot-assisted kidney autotransplantation across indications, techniques and potentially overlapping reports. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and ScienceDirect were searched through 22 August 2026. Primary human reports with robotic nephrectomy or implantation were eligible. Joanna Briggs Institute checklists assessed methodological limitations. Indication-specific findings were described separately. Series with at least five procedures and no identified overlap entered exploratory logistic-normal binomial models with profile-likelihood 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Eligibility and synthesis changes were post hoc. Twenty-three reports represented 17 putative report families; the exact number of unique patients could not be established. Two reports were not retrieved. Five series (125 patients) contributed primary data. Pooled proportions were 33.1% for any postoperative complication (95% CI 18.6-49.0%), 11.2% for major complications (5.5-21.1%), 3.2% for graft nonfunction or loss (0.8-7.3%) and 1.2% for conversion (< 0.1-5.0%; one event/86 patients; four reporting series). These estimates describe the included case mix, not a common risk across indications or techniques. Mortality reporting was incomplete. Symptom outcomes were heterogeneous, with persistent or worsened pain in some patients. Certainty in the pooled frequencies was very low. Published experience demonstrates technical feasibility in selected patients, with substantial uncertainty about safety and clinical benefit. Technical graft success does not establish symptom relief or comparative effectiveness. Standardized prospective data are needed. Registration: PROSPERO CRD42024610953.

articles.title: Optimizing task-oriented training with non-invasive brain stimulation after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate comparator-specific effects of non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) combined with task-oriented training (TOT) on upper-limb motor function, functional task performance, and activities of daily living after stroke, and to explore potential treatment modifiers.

METHODS: Eight English- and Chinese-language databases were searched through March 2025. Fourteen randomized controlled trials were included. Sham-controlled class A comparisons constituted the primary analysis, while comparisons with TOT alone, NIBS alone, and conventional rehabilitation were analyzed separately as secondary analyses. Random-effects models were used, with shared groups apportioned within each analysis. An active-versus-active treatment-timing comparison was excluded from efficacy pooling.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies involving 1,029 participants were included in the review. Sham-controlled analyses favored combined treatment for FMA-assessed motor function (SMD = 0.77, 95% CI 0.46-1.07; four studies), but not for functional task performance (SMD = 0.28, 95% CI -0.10-0.66; four studies) .The overall MBI synthesis favored combined treatment （MD = 9.35, 95% CI 6.26-12.44; five studies）. Secondary comparisons favored combined treatment for motor function and daily living, whereas functional task performance estimates varied by comparator. Exploratory subgroup findings may be confounded by comparator differences. These findings do not establish a synergistic effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Sham-controlled evidence supports an added effect of NIBS on FMA-assessed motor function during TOT, but stimulation-specific benefits for functional task performance and daily living remain uncertain. Larger sham-controlled trials with matched rehabilitation doses are needed to clarify clinical benefits and optimal treatment parameters.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420250649176.

articles.title: Cystic clear cell thymoma in a cat: clinical, imaging, anatomopathological and immunohistochemical findings.
articles.abstract: Thymomas are uncommon thymic epithelial neoplasms in cats and may present uncommon histological variants, such as cystic clear cell thymoma.
