The aim of this case report was to describe the clinical, imaging, anatomopathological, and immunohistochemical findings of a cystic clear cell thymoma in a four-year-old mixed-breed female cat presented with anorexia and progressive dyspnea. Imaging examinations revealed a large heterogeneous mediastinal mass with cystic components, accompanied by pleural effusion and pulmonary compression. Ultrasound-guided cytology was inconclusive. Despite intensive supportive care, the patient died due to respiratory failure. Necropsy revealed a large mediastinal mass occupying approximately 70-80% of the thoracic cavity, accompanied by compressive pulmonary atelectasis and hydrothorax. Histologically, the neoplasm was predominantly composed of carbohydrate-rich clear epithelial cells accompanied by cystic structures, scattered mature lymphocytes and rare Hassall's corpuscles. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong nuclear expression of p40, p63 and CKAE1/AE3 in the neoplastic cells, whereas CD3 labeling was restricted to non-neoplastic lymphocytes, supporting the diagnosis of cystic clear cell thymoma. This report expands the current knowledge of this rare tumor variant in cats and highlights the importance of imaging examinations, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry for establishing a definitive diagnosis.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Essential Trace Elements and Telomere Maintenance: A Review on Selenium, Zinc, Copper, and Iron.
articles.abstract: Telomeres play an important role in health, aging, and longevity. Telomere length is influenced by several factors, including telomerase activity and diet. Trace elements are micronutrients that exist in very small quantities in the human body and that are primarily obtained through diet. They are classified into essential and non-essential trace elements. Because of their roles in numerous biological processes and their ability to modify telomerase activity, essential trace elements have been proposed to modulate telomere length. This review synthesizes the existing literature on the relationship between telomere biology (telomere length and telomerase activity) and four essential trace elements (selenium, zinc, copper and iron). The relationship between the mentioned trace elements' status and telomere dynamics appears to be affected by numerous factors. Thus, further research is needed where all relevant factors are taken into account. Moreover, because of the observational nature of the evidence and the limited scope of interventional and Mendelian randomization studies, causal inference is constrained. That is why it cannot be definitively determined whether dysregulation of the discussed trace elements drives telomere attrition or vice versa. A hypothesis of a vicious self-amplifying cycle, in which mitochondrial decline and oxidative stress take part, is proposed in this review. The presence of such a cycle, if proven, would have consequent research and clinical implications. Therefore, combined interventions addressing oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, trace element status, and telomere dynamics at the same time would represent a more comprehensive approach worth investigating.

articles.title: Radiomics and deep learning in locally advanced rectal cancer: linking imaging biology to response-adapted treatment.
articles.abstract: Neoadjuvant treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer produces a wide range of tumor responses, and total neoadjuvant therapy and watch-and-wait strategies have made response assessment a central task for radiologists. Morphological MRI criteria detect complete responders with limited sensitivity because fibrosis, edema, and small foci of residual tumor can overlap after treatment. Radiomics and deep learning extract quantitative features beyond qualitative visual assessment. This narrative review examines their biological correlates and reported performance along the treatment pathway. We discuss tumor cellularity, fibrosis, spatial heterogeneity, segmentation, feature extraction, multimodal fusion, baseline prediction, longitudinal assessment, restaging, and recurrence risk. Previously published meta-analyses report summary areas under the curve of approximately 0.85 for MRI-based prediction of pathological complete response; these estimates were not pooled in this review and reflect heterogeneous imaging time points, response definitions, and validation methods. Representative studies are critically appraised using domains drawn from radiomics quality and prediction-model reporting frameworks. Most evidence remains retrospective, and external performance is variable. Imaging heterogeneity, post-treatment segmentation, limited numbers of complete responders, and inconsistent reference standards restrict applicability. Models trained on conventional chemoradiotherapy require evaluation in total neoadjuvant therapy and immunotherapy cohorts, while watch-and-wait models require sustained clinical complete response and local regrowth endpoints. Prospective observational validation should be distinguished from evaluation of model-guided care. Radiomics and deep learning remain investigational decision-support tools whose translation requires independent validation, calibrated risk estimates, workflow integration, and prospective evidence of clinical benefit.

articles.title: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in indeterminate renal masses and advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: clinical utility and management impact in a real-world cohort.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab is a PET radiotracer targeting carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX), a biomarker highly expressed in clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). Following the high diagnostic accuracy demonstrated in the phase III ZIRCON trial, this study evaluated the real-world clinical performance and management impact of [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT in patients with indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Within an early access program, patients with renal lesions of uncertain origin underwent [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT for noninvasive lesion characterization, while patients with advanced ccRCC were imaged for postoperative assessment, recurrence evaluation, or metastatic restaging. Following intravenous administration of 37 MBq (± 10%) [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab, PET/CT was performed on day 5 post-injection. Findings were correlated with histopathology where available, and their impact on clinical management was assessed retrospectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients (22 men, 6 women; mean age, 71 ± 9 years) were included: 18 with indeterminate renal masses (Group A) and 10 undergoing postoperative, metastatic, or restaging evaluation (Group B). In Group A, PET/CT demonstrated CAIX-positive findings in 10/18 patients (56%) and CAIX-negative findings in 7/18 (39%); one patient showed heterogeneous tracer uptake. Histopathological confirmation was available in 11/18 patients (61%). Within this verified subset, patient-level PET/CT findings were concordant with histopathology, with all CAIX-positive patients (6/6) confirmed as ccRCC and all CAIX-negative patients (5/5) confirmed as non-ccRCC or benign. At the lesion level, however, concordance was incomplete in one patient: four CAIX-avid lesions were identified, two of which were confirmed as ccRCC, while the remaining two corresponded to an angiomyolipoma and normal renal parenchyma. PET/CT findings were associated with a subsequent change in the documented management plan in 11/18 patients (61%; 95% CI, 35.7-82.7%). In the exploratory Group B cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT demonstrated the presence or absence of detectable CAIX-avid findings and contributed to therapeutic and surveillance decisions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab PET/CT showed concordance with histopathology in the limited verified subset and was associated with changes in clinical management, supporting further prospective evaluation in indeterminate renal masses and advanced ccRCC.

articles.title: Dual-tracer ¹⁸F-FDG and ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac spindle cell sarcoma.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract: A 33-year-old woman presented with long-standing abdominal distension and unexplained ascites. Serum CA125 levels were significantly elevated. Abdominal CT revealed a cystic lesion in the left adnexal region with massive ascites. To determine the etiology, 18F-FDG PET/CT was performed after fasting for at least 6 h. The adnexal lesion showed no appreciable FDG uptake, favoring a benign cystic lesion. Unexpectedly,​ heterogeneous hypermetabolism was found along the right heart border. Because the interpretation of cardiac FDG findings may be confounded by physiological or nonspecific myocardial uptake, ¹⁸F-FAPI PET/CT was subsequently performed for further characterization, which revealed a more extensive and conspicuous tracer uptake within the cardiac lesion than FDG PET/CT, more clearly delineating its extent. The patient subsequently underwent partial surgical resection of the cardiac mass with biopsy. Histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular findings supported the diagnosis of cardiac spindle cell sarcoma with partial myofibroblastic differentiation. This case reports a rare primary cardiac spindle cell sarcoma and highlights the complementary value of FDG and FAPI PET/CT in evaluating primary cardiac malignancies. It also underscores the importance of multimodal imaging in guiding differential diagnosis and clinical management.

articles.title: PET/CT radiomics integrating tumour and whole-body composition enhances prognostic prediction in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a multicentre study.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate an integrated PET/CT‑based radiomic model that combines tumour characteristics and whole‑body composition features for predicting progression‑free survival (PFS) in patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).

METHODS: This multicentre retrospective study included 477 patients with pathologically confirmed ESCC who underwent pretreatment [¹⁸F]FDG‑PET/CT. Patients were allocated to training (n = 294), internal validation (n = 74), and external validation (n = 109) cohorts. Primary tumours and whole‑body composition components, including skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose tissue, visceral adipose tissue, intermuscular adipose tissue and spine, were automatically segmented on PET/CT images. Radiomic features were extracted from both tumour and body‑composition regions. Feature selection and model development were performed using machine learning approaches. A composite clinical-tumour-body composition model was constructed and compared with clinical and tumour‑radiomic models.

RESULTS: The integrated model showed superior prognostic performance over individual models, achieving C‑indices of 0.802 (95% CI: 0.770-0.832), 0.716 (95% CI: 0.639-0.797), and 0.732 (95% CI: 0.660-0.796) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. The corresponding AUCs for 3‑year PFS prediction were 0.895 (95% CI: 0.858-0.930), 0.831 (95% CI: 0.727-0.923), and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.639-0.895). The model stratified patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups, with significantly different PFS between the two strata across all cohorts (log‑rank P < 0.05). Decision curve analysis supported the clinical utility of the integrated model.

CONCLUSIONS: A PET/CT‑based radiomic model integrating clinical, tumour, and whole‑body composition features provides robust, externally validated postoperative prognostic stratification for ESCC. This approach may facilitate individualised risk assessment and inform treatment decision‑making.

articles.title: Forensic dating of thrombi in pulmonary embolism: neutrophil-to-macrophage ratio and bi-exponential modelling in an autopsy series.
articles.abstract: Thrombus dating is a relevant issue in forensic pathology, particularly in fatal pulmonary embolism (PE), where chronological assessment may contribute to the reconstruction of thromboembolic events and their medico-legal interpretation. This study aimed to investigate thrombus chronology in fatal PE by applying a quantitative neutrophil-to-macrophage (N/M) ratio model integrated with histological and immunohistochemical analysis. Twenty-six autopsy cases in which PE was certified as the cause of death were examined. Overall, 81 thrombi were analysed, including 67 pulmonary thrombi and 14 extrapulmonary venous thrombi. To assess temporal variability within thrombi, multiple anatomically distinct portions were sampled, resulting in the analysis of 162 histological samples. Thrombus age was estimated using a bi-exponential Levenberg-Marquardt N/M ratio model interpreted together with ancillary histological and immunohistochemical markers of thrombus organization. Estimated thrombus age ranged from less than 1 h to more than 10 days. Histological evidence of organization was predominantly observed in samples estimated to be older than 5 days. Several pulmonary thrombi exhibited complex internal stratification, with mural, central, and distal portions displaying substantially different estimated ages. Comparison between pulmonary and extrapulmonary venous thrombi revealed substantial temporal overlap, with no consistent chronological sequence identifiable across cases. In this autopsy series, thrombi of different estimated ages frequently coexisted, consistent with a multistage thromboembolic process. Application of the quantitative N/M ratio model provided a reproducible framework for early thrombus dating. These findings support the value of integrated thrombus analysis for forensic reconstruction and medico-legal evaluation of fatal PE.

articles.title: A multidimensional approach to CAR T cell therapy: basic research, clinical evidence, and future development.
articles.abstract: Further progress in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy will require linking insights into cellular biology with treatment delivery. This issue of Progress in Hematology addresses T-cell exhaustion, new CAR-based therapies for hematological malignancies, real-world evidence supporting sustainable care, and applications in autoimmune diseases as an emerging field. Together, these reviews examine how cellular function, target selection, manufacturing, treatment delays, and long-term follow-up influence therapeutic benefit. Defining disease-specific treatment goals and the required depth and duration of cellular activity, while connecting biological insights with clinical and operational evidence, will help guide the development of safe and sustainable CAR T cell therapy.

articles.title: Consciousness, complexity, and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Consciousness remains one of science's most challenging problems because it cannot be exhaustively characterized as a single function, computation, or behavior; it also refers to the presence and organization of subjective experience. This position paper integrates clinical neurology, neurophysiology, psychiatry, psychoanalysis, embodied cognition, moral neuroscience, theoretical physics, philosophy of mind, and neurotechnology. We argue that, despite major advances in identifying neural correlates, computational models, and behavioral markers, contemporary consciousness research has not resolved the explanatory gap between objective description and subjective experience. We propose that claims about consciousness at neurophysiological, embodied, cognitive, social, and ontological levels should be coordinated through explicit cross-level constraints rather than merged into a single unitary theory. These domains have different evidential roles and are not all constituents of consciousness. Perturbational measures of cortical complexity, including the Perturbational Complexity Index (PCI) and its state-transition variant (PCIst), support assessment of preserved conscious capacity in studied human populations. They do not independently determine a clinical diagnosis or phenomenal content. Evidence from aphasia, sleep, anesthesia, and disorders of consciousness also demonstrates dissociations among language, wakefulness, behavioral responsiveness, and conscious experience. Perspectives from embodied simulation, mind-object identity, quantum information, and the philosophy of physics are treated here as heuristic stress tests rather than as mechanistic accounts; they keep open foundational questions concerning subjectivity, representation, and the role of the observer. We advocate constrained pluralism, a methodological framework in which consciousness is conceptualized as an integrated, embodied, relational, and temporally extended process. Such an approach provides a coherent foundation for future research while strengthening the dialogue between neuroscience, clinical practice, philosophy, and neuroethics.

articles.title: MoCA deficits and white matter in Huntington's disease.
articles.abstract: This study explored the relationship between the Montreal Cognitive Assessment's (MoCA) subdomains and white matter changes in Huntington's disease (HD). Fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) were measured using Diffusion Tensor Imaging (DTI) in 22 early-stage symptomatic HD patients and 20 healthy controls. Tract-Based Spatial Statistics was used to compare the two groups and to correlate patients' FA and MD values with their performance on MoCA subdomains. Among all MoCA subdomains, only visuospatial performance was associated with white matter integrity in the corpus callosum, corona radiata, and superior longitudinal fasciculus, supporting the utility of identifying regional imaging correlates of specific cognitive performance through the combination of DTI analysis and brief screening tools in early-stage patients.

articles.title: Development and preclinical evaluation of CP021, a CD38-targeted cyclic peptide radiotheranostic platform for multiple myeloma.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract: Small and disseminated lesions within the bone marrow remain challenging to detect and eradicate in multiple myeloma (MM), highlighting the need for targeted approaches capable of both sensitive imaging and localized radiation delivery. CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells and represents an established target in MM, but CD38-directed radiopharmaceuticals with rapid tumor targeting and favorable pharmacokinetics remain limited. Here, we developed CP021, a high-affinity CD38-targeting cyclic peptide, and evaluated [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 for PET imaging, together with [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 and [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 for targeted radionuclide therapy in preclinical MM models.MethodsDOTA-CP021 was labeled with ⁶⁸Ga or ¹⁷⁷Lu and DOTAM-CP021 with ²¹²Pb. Radiochemical properties, PET imaging, biodistribution, pharmacokinetics, dosimetry, therapeutic efficacy, and safety were evaluated in MM xenograft models.ResultsAll radioconjugates showed > 95% radiochemical purity and good stability. [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-DOTA-CP021 demonstrated CD38-dependent tumor uptake; at 60 min, uptake in CD38-high MOLP-8 xenografts was 12.35 ± 1.37%ID/g, 1.8- and 3.1-fold higher than in MM.1 S and U266B1 tumors, respectively. [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-DOTA-CP021 produced activity-dependent tumor growth inhibition and prolonged survival. Repeated [²¹²Pb]Pb-DOTAM-CP021 further improved tumor control, extending median survival to 36.5 and 47 days at cumulative activities of 0.555 and 1.11 MBq, respectively, versus 16 days with PBS (P < 0.001). No overt treatment-related toxicity was observed.ConclusionCP021 provides a versatile CD38-targeted radiotheranostic platform combining rapid molecular imaging with β- and α-particle therapy. Its performance across radionuclides supports further development for detecting and treating CD38-positive MM lesions.

articles.title: RheumBench: A Specialist-Validated Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Rheumatology.
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for clinical decision support, yet scalable and specialty-specific methods for evaluating their performance and safety remain limited. We developed RheumBench, the first rubric-based LLM benchmark in rheumatology, providing a specialist-validated framework for open-ended evaluation. We evaluated ten systems, comprising three frontier proprietary general-purpose LLMs, one frontier open-weight general-purpose LLM, and six clinical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, including two certified medical products and one rheumatology-specific RAG system. RheumBench comprised 100 clinical cases (70 diagnostic and 30 diverse clinical management) and 1,020 case-specific rubric criteria independently reviewed and weighted for clinical appropriateness and potential harm by two board-certified rheumatologists. Systems were evaluated for answer quality, prompt sensitivity, potential harm, diagnostic accuracy, and system confidence. Responses were scored by a three LLM judge panel, yielding 50,553 rubric-level LLM evaluations, with high agreement with rheumatologist consensus (Cohen's κ = 0.91). Overall system performance (0-100%) varied substantially, with a maximum RheumBench score of 54.0% (Claude Fable 5), and frontier general-purpose LLMs generally outperformed clinical RAG systems, including certified Prof. Valmed and DR.INFO. Management case performance varied widely, with thorough prompting improving mean management scores in 9 of 10 systems and yielding a peak score of 72.9% with GPT-5.6 Sol. Potentially severe errors occurred with all systems and were predominantly omission errors. In predominantly rare-disease cases, top-1 accuracy reached 57.1% (GPT-5.6 Sol) and top-3 67.1% (Claude Fable 5). Self-reported system confidence was generally high and diagnostic calibration analyses showed systematic overconfidence for all systems, with the lowest Brier score of 0.203 (Claude Fable 5). RheumBench identified substantial differences that were not explained by clinical specialization or medical product certification. These findings highlight limitations of current LLM-based clinical decision support, and underscore the need for human oversight. Further studies are needed to assess human-LLM interaction and effects on clinical outcomes.

articles.title: ACC hyperactivity and synaptic remodeling underlie sensory hypersensitivity in Adnp-haploinsufficient mice.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic variants in the transcriptional regulator ADNP cause a frequent autism syndrome marked by pronounced tactile and pain hypersensitivity, yet the responsible cortical circuits are poorly defined. Here we show that Adnp-haploinsufficient (Adnp-HT) mice exhibit mechanical and thermal hypersensitivity together with enhanced shock-related defensive responding. Caudal conditional Adnp deletion did not reproduce these phenotypes, arguing against a dominant peripheral or spinal contribution. c-Fos mapping and ultrahigh-field fMRI revealed stimulus-evoked hyperresponsiveness across a distributed sensory-affective network that included the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and recordings from naive mice identified increased intrinsic excitability and altered synaptic transmission in ACC pyramidal neurons. Global chemogenetic inhibition of ACC excitatory neurons only partially normalized mechanical and paw-heat hypersensitivity but increased shock-related freezing, whereas inhibition of electric-foot-shock-activated (FosTRAP2) ACC ensembles normalized mechanical and paw-heat responses and attenuated baseline and early shock-related freezing. Multiomic profiling, MERFISH, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing converged on synaptic and ion-channel programs in layer 2/3 and layer 5 excitatory neurons. These results identify the ACC as a major, but not exclusive, cortical contributor within a broader network and support cell-type- and ensemble-resolved approaches to ADNP-linked sensory abnormalities.

articles.title: First-in-human multiplexed PET demonstrated with two oncological indications: [18F]FDG/[68Ga]DOTATOC in neuroendocrine tumor and [18F]FDG/[18F]FCH in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: Postoperative dual-time-point [18F]Fluorocholine PET imaging in suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma: comparison with [11C]Methionine PET/MRI.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Detecting residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) by MRI is challenging due to post-surgical or post-radiotherapy tissue remodeling. While [11C]Methionine ([11C]MET) PET demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for RPA, its use is limited to centers with an on-site cyclotron. [18F]Fluorocholine ([18F]FCH) PET, which has shown incidental uptake in pituitary adenomas, may offer a viable alternative. This study compared dual-phase [18F]FCH with [11C]MET PET imaging for localizing suspected residual or recurrent pituitary adenoma (RPA) and characterizing uptake differences between suspected RPA and pituitary gland remnant (PGR) after surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 23 patients addressed during the follow-up of an ablated pituitary adenoma (n = 23). The presence of suspected RPA was determined by multidisciplinary consensus integrating postoperative metabolic imaging, serial MRI follow-up, and biochemical data. Two patients underwent reoperation, in whom histopathological confirmation was available. All patients underwent a standard [11C]MET PET/MRI acquisition (mean activity = 397 ± 51 MBq) and subsequently a 20-min dynamic [18F]FCH PET/MRI acquisition, followed by an additional late static [18F]FCH PET/CT acquisition performed at 40-55 min post-FCH injection (mean activity = 334 ± 77 MBq). RPA and PGR uptake were compared visually and quantitatively using maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) for both tracers.

RESULTS: All lesions suspected of representing RPA were visually detected on both early and late [18F]FCH images. In suspected RPA, [18F]FCH uptake was comparable to [11C]MET uptake, with mean SUVmax values of 6.2 ± 2.3 for early (3-20 min post-injection) [18F]FCH PET, 5.1 ± 2.3 for late [18F]FCH PET, and 5.5 ± 1.9 for [11C]MET (p = 0.11 and 0.51, respectively). Both suspected RPA and PGR showed decreasing [18F]FCH uptake over time, with a significantly greater decline in PGR (early PET SUVmax: 5.7 ± 1.5; late PET SUVmax: 3.7 ± 1.1; time-by-region interaction, p < 0.0001). Accordingly, the RPA/PGR SUVmax ratio was significantly lower on early [18F]FCH images than on late [18F]FCH images (p = 0.0014) and [11C]MET images (p < 0.001), whereas it did not differ significantly between late [18F]FCH and [11C]MET images (p > 0.5).

CONCLUSION: [18F]FCH PET/MRI demonstrated uptake in lesions suspected of representing RPA, with uptake levels comparable to those observed with [11C]MET PET/MRI. The greater decline in PGR uptake on delayed imaging improved the quantitative RPA/PGR contrast, supporting dual-time-point [18F]FCH PET/MRI as a promising approach for postoperative tissue discrimination. These exploratory findings require prospective validation using an independent reference standard.

articles.title: Nutritional interventions in neonatal sepsis prevention & treatment.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly among preterm infants with profound immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal immaturity. Optimizing nutrition represents a promising yet complex strategy to support immune function, preserve gut integrity, and improve outcomes in this high-risk population. This narrative review explores the interplay between neonatal sepsis, inflammation, and nutrition, with a focus on the roles of human milk, parenteral nutrition, and selected nutritional interventions, including lactoferrin, probiotics, long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamin D, and iron. Overall, while nutrition is fundamental to neonatal resilience against infection, no single nutrient intervention has been shown to reliably prevent or treat neonatal sepsis. Future research should prioritize precision nutrition approaches, mechanistic studies linking nutrition to immune and metabolic pathways, and well-designed clinical trials to inform individualized nutritional care and improve both short- and long-term outcomes of vulnerable neonates. IMPACT: Optimizing nutrition is essential in the acute management of neonatal sepsis. Future advances in nutraceuticals and ensuring adequate nutrition for infants will have a major impact on sepsis mortality and neurodevelopmental outcomes. There is scope for nutritional optimization to improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and pulmonary outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity and mortality in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), yet preventive strategies remain limited. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have metabolic and anti-inflammatory effects, but their association with respiratory outcomes in RA is unknown. Using electronic health record data from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of adults with RA and type 2 diabetes mellitus who initiated GLP-1-based therapy or a DPP-4 inhibitor between January 1, 2016, and January 1, 2025. Primary coded outcomes were incident coded diagnoses of interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary hypertension (PH) over 3 years, with secondary outcomes including coded bronchiectasis, hospitalization, respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and all-cause mortality. Time-to-event analyses used Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. After matching, 1,656 patients were included in each cohort. Incident ILD occurred in 42 GLP-1RA users versus 54 DPP-4i users with no significant difference (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.57-1.29, p = 0.46). GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly reduced pulmonary hypertension (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.33-0.68, p < 0.001), mechanical ventilation (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.35-0.89, p = 0.013), respiratory failure (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58-0.96, p = 0.023), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.48-1.00, p = 0.047). No significant differences were observed for bronchiectasis or hospitalization. In patients with RA and T2DM, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risk of pulmonary hypertension, but not incident ILD, compared with DPP-4i use. Additional reductions in respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, and mortality warrant further prospective evaluation of GLP-1RAs in RA-related pulmonary disease.K.

articles.title: An upregulated Ano9 variant causes multiple renal defects and chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: A recent genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis identified ANO9 (anoctamin 9; TMEM16J) as a candidate gene involved in chronic kidney disease (CKD). ANO9 belongs to the anoctamin family of proteins, which function as ion channels and phospholipid scramblases. To investigate the role of ANO9 in kidney function, we analyzed Ano9-knockout (KO) mice and knockin mice expressing the CKD-associated human variant ANO9-T604A (murine Ano9-T595A). Enhanced expression of Ano9-T595A mRNA was observed, resulting in enhanced ANO9 protein abundance at the renal brush border. Elevated ANO9 expression was also observed in adenine-induced kidney injury and in human diabetic and IgA nephropathy, suggesting a contribution of ANO9 to CKD pathogenesis. Ano9-T595A mice developed renal inflammation characterized by increased expression of IL-1, IL-6, CXCL1, TGF-β1, α-SMA, and CLCA1, accompanied by T-cell infiltration. Interstitial fibrosis, and a modest rise in serum creatinine paralleled these changes. Enhanced apoptosis and compensatory cell proliferation, as well as proteinuria and reduced expression of the tubular endocytic receptors megalin and cubilin, together with other transport proteins were present in animals expressing Ano9-T595A. In addition, renal epithelial cells from Ano9-T595A mice exhibited impaired intracellular Ca2⁺ signaling, which may also contribute to disease development. Our findings suggest that dysregulated ANO9 expression and/or defective endosomal sorting caused by the Ano9-T595A variant promotes renal injury and dysfunction. This study identifies ANO9 as an important regulator of kidney homeostasis and provides a mechanistic explanation for the increased susceptibility to CKD in individuals carrying the ANO9-T604A variant.

articles.title: [18F]DPA714 PET reveals occult glial activation and tracks disease severity in MOGAD: a prospective study.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is a heterogeneous neuroinflammatory disorder. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity. Translocator protein (TSPO) is a sensitive biomarker of glial activation that can be imaged non-invasively using PET. We aimed to characterize intracranial inflammatory patterns across MOGAD phenotypes using [18F]DPA714 PET/MRI.

METHODS: In this prospective study, 32 MOGAD patients and 10 age/sex-matched healthy controls underwent [18F]DPA714 PET/MRI and comprehensive clinical assessment. All participants were confirmed as high-affinity binders for the TSPO radioligand (rs6971 genotyping) and provided written informed consent. Standardized uptake value ratios (SUVR) were quantified; PET‑positivity was defined as SUVR > control Mean SUVR + 2 SD.

RESULTS: [18F]DPA714 PET showed significantly higher detection rate than MRI (27/32, 84.38% vs. 16/32, 50.00%; P = 0.007). [18F]DPA714 uptake correlated with mRS and CASE scores at baseline (both P < 0.01), and changes in SUVR correlated with changes in both scores over follow-up (n = 20; P < 0.05 and P < 0.01, respectively). Patients with seizures, sensory disturbances, or cognitive decline showed higher SUVR in corresponding brain regions. Three PET-based subtypes were identified-cortical-predominant, thalamic/limbic system-predominant, and brainstem/cerebellar-predominant, which exhibited distinct clinical and laboratory features. Patients who achieved clinical improvement had higher baseline abnormal [18F]DPA714 uptake intensity and greater post‑treatment SUVR reduction (both P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this single-center exploratory study, [18F]DPA714 PET demonstrated a significantly higher positive detection rate than conventional MRI and correlates with disease severity, supporting its potential as a promising imaging biomarker for MOGAD assessment, precise classification and management.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05293405 https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05293405) registered 24 March 2022 first participant enrolled 14 December 2021 retrospectively registered.

articles.title: NR1I2 rs3732356 polymorphism and anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury in eastern Chinese patients: A preliminary study.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Genetic factors may underlie anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ATLI), the most common and severe adverse reaction in tuberculosis treatment. We aimed to assess whether the risk of ATLI might be influenced by nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group I member 2 (NR1I2) gene polymorphisms.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A 1:4 individual matched case-control study was performed using 224 ATLI cases and 896 controls. Five single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the NR1I2 gene were analyzed. A multiple conditional logistic regression model was used to estimate the association between genotypes and ATLI risk by the odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with liver disease history and smoking as covariates. Interaction and age-stratified analyses were conducted to investigate gene-age interactions in ATLI risk and genetic associations with ATLI across age groups.

RESULTS: No significant associations between the five NR1I2 SNPs and ATLI were observed in the overall analysis. Statistically significant interactions were absent on either the multiplicative or additive scale. In exploratory subgroup analyses, rs3732356 was associated with lower ATLI risk in patients aged under 60 years in the dominant model (OR = 0.540, 95%CI: 0.312-0.933, p = 0.027) and additive model (OR = 0.607, 95%CI: 0.390-0.946, p = 0.027). Peak total bilirubin (TBil) was significantly higher in patients with TG genotype of rs3732356 than in those with TT or GG (16.8 μmol/L vs. 14.3 μmol/L vs. 12.5 μmol/L, respectively, p = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: Despite a preliminary age-stratified signal for rs3732356, we found no overall association and no significant effect modification by age, which warrants validation in larger studies.

articles.title: Where rivers are roads: challenges for cardiovascular prevention in the Amazon. How Brazil's floating primary healthcare units are bringing care to remote river communities.
The reduced hospital costs of periprosthetic joint infection patients with successful initial treatment : two-year estimations using activity-based costing.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to 1) estimate the two-year hospital costs of treating periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) patients by outcomes of treatment success or treatment failure; 2) compare costs between patients with treatment success or treatment failure, stratified by PJI presentation and initial treatment type; and 3) estimate the cost burden for the study cohort and the projected Australian PJI cost burden of PJI patients by treatment success outcomes.

METHODS: A total of 212 hip and 287 knee patients from the Prosthetic joint Infection in Australia and New Zealand Observational (PIANO) study were included. Patients were grouped by treatment success outcomes, treatment type, and timing of PJI presentation (early acute, late acute, or chronic) at two-year follow-up. Hospital costs were calculated using activity-based costing.

RESULTS: For hips, the mean cost of 67 patients with treatment failure was AUD $85,179 (SD 72,030), which was 1.44-fold higher than of 145 successfully treated patients ($59,234 (SD 45,581)). Of successfully treated hip patients, those who underwent additional surgeries ($70,257 (SD 38,481)) had 1.25-fold higher mean costs than patients with successful initial treatment ($56,238 (SD 42,929)). For knees, the mean cost of 133 patients with treatment failure ($89,073 (SD 64,707)) was 1.72-fold higher than 154 patients with successful treatment ($51,785 (SD 31,449)). Of successfully treated knee patients, those who underwent additional surgery ($85,326 (SD 44,885)) had 1.88-fold higher mean costs than patients with successful initial treatment ($45,284 (SD 23,286)). Treatment failure outcomes for patients initially treated with two-stage revision total hip arthroplasty, two-stage revision total knee arthroplasty, single-stage revision total knee arthroplasty, and extensive knee debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) cost 1.78, 1.94, 1.74, and 1.79-fold higher, respectively, compared with successfully treated patients with the same initial treatment (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: At two-year follow-up, PJI patients with successful initial treatment had reduced hospital costs, highlighting the importance of strategies that aim to 'get it right the first time'. Patients with treatment failure account for approximately $131 million (51%) of the estimated $254 million annual Australian burden of hip and knee PJI.

articles.title: Serum procalcitonin in the assessment of febrile neutropenia in hematological patients.
articles.abstract: This review focuses on recent literature of the use of procalcitonin (PCT) to assess infection severity and prognosis in hematological patients with chemotherapy-induced febrile neutropenia (FN). A substantial proportion of patients with hematological malignancies receive intensive chemotherapy, which often leads to neutropenia, associated with infectious complications, and prolonged use of antibiotics. Antimicrobial resistance is a growing problem with far-reaching consequences, and hematological patients undergoing chemotherapy are at a particularly high risk. Observational studies indicate that PCT concentration 0.1-0.5 μg/L suggests localized infection; systemic infection is unlikely when PCT <0.1 μg/L, and likely when PCT ≥2 μg/L. In sepsis studies utilizing PCT-guided therapy, the threshold values used at the initiation of treatment range from 0.10 to 0.5 μg/L. The commonly used criteria for discontinuation include 50 % reduction from the previous value, 65 % decrease within three days, or ≥80-90 % decrease from the peak value. Of note, these cut-offs are based on early clinical studies and do not consider variable analysis methods available. When these thresholds are applied to sepsis patients, the duration of treatment is typically reduced by approximately two days. Some studies have reported reduction in antibiotic-related adverse effects and antimicrobial resistance, and even a decrease in mortality. Further experience and data are needed regarding PCT-guided management in hematological patients with chemotherapy-induced FN. Findings of observational studies largely support the utility of PCT measurements in chemotherapy-induced FN, but there is a paucity of interventional studies evaluating the use of PCT algorithms in FN patients and the results are inconsistent.

articles.title: Ambient environmental risk factors for asthma incidence across the lifecourse: what is left to learn?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The impacts of the ambient environment on asthma have been a topic of extensive research. However, most of this work has explored associations among individuals with asthma on outcomes such as symptoms, hospitalizations and asthma control. This review will focus on the state of the evidence on asthma onset and the ambient environment, highlighting the gaps in the field.

AREAS COVERED: This review of articles in English in PubMed published before 10/31/2026 will cover the state of the evidence on impacts of several groups of ambient environmental exposures (air pollution and traffic exposures, climate‑related factors, ultraviolet radiation, and greenness) on onset of asthma in children and adults.

EXPERT OPINION: Compared to the vast literature on the impacts of the ambient environment on individuals, especially children, with asthma, there is far less evidence on the role of the ambient environment as a primary risk factor. Additionally, the literature is dominated by single-exposure studies. Given more recent emphasis in the field on the exposome, or all exposures experienced across the lifecourse, we are likely at a key turning point in the field where the evidence base could and should be built quickly to fill these gaps.

articles.title: Pediatric reference interval for serum soluble prion protein using the Canadian laboratory initiative on pediatric reference intervals (CALIPER) cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish pediatric reference intervals (RIs) for serum soluble cellular prion protein (PrPc) and to explore potential age- and sex-related differences.

METHODS: The study was conducted within the Canadian Laboratory Initiative on Pediatric Reference Intervals (CALIPER) cohort. Blood samples were collected from healthy children and the adolescents aged 1-18 years at the Hospital for Sick Children (Toronto, ON, Canada) from a multiethnic population following informed parental consent. Participant eligibility was determined using standardized health questionnaires and predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. A total of 125 serum samples were aliquoted and transferred to the University of Saskatchewan for quantification of serum cellular prion protein (PrPc) using a modified enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Pediatric RIs were established according to Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) C28-A3 guidelines using non-parametric and robust statistical methods to estimate the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles and their corresponding 90 % confidence intervals.

RESULTS: The overall pediatric RI for serum soluble PrPc was 1.37 (1.18-1.48) to 4.21 (3.88-4.48) ng/mL. Sex-stratified analysis using the robust method produced RIs of 0.91 (0.64-1.19) to 4.29 (3.98-4.59) ng/mL for males and 1.13 (0.92-1.36) to 4.17 (3.89-4.40) ng/mL for females. No significant differences in mean PrPc concentrations were observed between males and females, and no significant correlation between PrPc concentration and age was detected.

CONCLUSIONS: We established pediatric RIs for serum soluble PrPc for the first time and provided baseline values that may support the interpretation of laboratory measurements of PrPc as a potential biomarker in pediatric populations.

articles.title: Integrating miRNA bioinformatics and nanotechnology for precision diagnosis and therapy in hypertension.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypertension is a leading contributor to cardiovascular and renal morbidity worldwide, and its management remains largely empirical. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate pathways central to blood-pressure homeostasis and are stable in the circulation, positioning them as candidate noninvasive biomarkers and therapeutic targets for precision antihypertensive strategies.

AREAS COVERED: This review examines circulating miRNA signatures reported in hypertensive patients, including miR-21, miR-145, miR-122 and miR-155, and their association with target-organ damage. Discrepancies between cohorts are appraised in relation to sample matrix, comorbidities, detection platform and normalization, and the pre-analytical standardization required for reproducible measurement. Mechanistic roles in renin-angiotensin-aldosterone signaling, renal sodium handling, endothelial function and oxidative stress are discussed, with bioinformatics and machine-learning pipelines for biomarker discovery, their validation requirements, and preclinical nanocarrier platforms providing proof of concept for miRNA delivery without established clinical efficacy or safety.

EXPERT OPINION: miRNA-guided diagnosis and therapy in hypertension remains preclinical; no miRNA nanomedicine has entered hypertension-focused clinical trials. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized sampling and normalization, externally validated multi-cohort machine-learning signatures, and nanocarriers with demonstrated cytosolic delivery and acceptable repeated-dose safety. Stepwise integration of these strands offers the most realistic route to translation.

articles.title: Pharmacotherapy options for managing hepatitis B in children: an update.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may face decades of infection before developing advanced liver disease. Pediatric management remains challenging because of age-dependent treatment eligibility, limited long-term evidence, and uncertainty regarding functional cure.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines treatment indications, international guidelines, and the efficacy and safety of interferon-based therapy and nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in children and adolescents. International guidelines were prioritized, supplemented by PubMed and Cochrane Library searches through September 2026 without a lower publication-date limit. We discuss treatment withdrawal, developmental safety, immunosuppression, special populations and transition to adult care. Emerging therapies are assessed with particular attention to the limits of applying adult results to children.

EXPERT OPINION: In our view, earlier treatment deserves further studies, but younger age alone is insufficient grounds for intervention. Favorable responses in selected childhood cohorts do not establish benefits from treating all children with high viremia. Bepirovirsen offers potential for finite therapy by reducing HBV transcripts, yet adult efficacy cannot establish pediatric benefit. Over the next five years, adolescent trials should assess sustained HBsAg loss after treatment withdrawal and acceptable safety. Until then, effective NA suppression remains a clinically valuable option, even when cure is not achieved.

articles.title: Health Care Team Awareness, Knowledge, and Perceptions of Neonatal Delirium: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Neonatal delirium is increasingly recognized as an important neuropsychiatric condition in critically ill infants, yet awareness and understanding among health care providers remain limited. Underdiagnosis may contribute to prolonged hospitalization, increased morbidity, and adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. This study assessed health care team members' awareness, perceptions, and knowledge of neonatal delirium across a large children's hospital and affiliated neonatal care locations.

STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to multidisciplinary neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) team members within a quaternary academic children's health system and affiliated sites. The survey included demographic items, multiple-choice questions, Likert-scale statements, and open-ended responses. Descriptive statistics summarized quantitative data, and content categorization was applied to open-ended responses.

RESULTS: A total of 117 respondents completed the survey, representing nursing, advanced practice providers, physicians, respiratory therapists, rehabilitation therapists, and pharmacy. Nearly half of respondents had never heard the term neonatal delirium. Among those familiar with the condition, definitions most commonly referenced agitation, altered consciousness, and sleep-wake disturbance. Ninety percent of respondents agreed that newborn infants can experience delirium, while only 60% indicated that delirium can also occur in preterm infants. Sixty percent indicated that delirium is assessable in infants, and 73% reported previously caring for an infant with suspected delirium. Respondents identified multiple barriers to screening and management, including limited awareness, lack of content expertise, and concerns about medication safety.

CONCLUSION: Awareness and understanding of neonatal delirium vary considerably among NICU providers, with notable educational and structural barriers to consistent recognition and management. These findings support the need for foundational education, multidisciplinary training, and continued research to inform development of effective strategies for assessing and managing neonatal delirium in neonatal care settings.

KEY POINTS: · NICU providers show wide gaps in awareness of neonatal delirium.. · Barriers include limited knowledge and inconsistent recognition.. · Findings support education and standardized delirium screening and management protocols..

articles.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on mitochondrial unfolded protein response-associated proteins in the colon tissue of mice with functional constipation].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To observe the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) at "Tianshu" (ST25) and "Shangjuxu" (ST37) acupoints on the expressions of mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) - related proteins in the colon tissue of functional constipation (FC) model mice, so as to explore its potential mechanisms underlying improvement of FC.

METHODS: Eighteen male C57BL/6J mice were randomly divided into 3 groups:normal control (NC), FC model (M), and EA (n=6 per group). The FC model was established by gavage of loperamide suspension (1 mg/mL, 0.1 mL/10 g), twice daily for 14 d. The EA group received alternating unilateral EA stimulation of ST25 and ST37(3 Hz/15 Hz, an electric current intensity being able to induce slight tremor of the mouse's limbs) for 20 min, once daily, 5 d a week for 2 weeks. The mice in the NC and M groups underwent equivalent restraint. Gastrointestinal transit function was assessed by measuring the first blue stool discharge time, 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, and intestinal propulsion rate. Histopathological changes of the colon tissue were examined by H.E. staining, and the mitochondrial ultrastructure of colonic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) was observed by using a transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) and the mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) levels were assayed using flow cytometry, and the mitochondrial ATP content in the colon tissue was measured using colorimetric assay. The immunohistochemistry stain was employed to detect the expressions of key UPRmt markers heat shock protein-60 (HSP60) and LON protease 1 (LONP1) in the colon tissue.

RESULTS: Compared with the NC group, the M group exhibited a significant increase in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a considerable reduction in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP level, ATP content, and the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). Following EA intervention, compared to the M group, the EA group showed a marked decrease in the first blue stool discharge time and average immunofluorescence intensity of mtROS (P<0.01), and a notable increase in the 6-hour fecal pellet count, stool character score, rate of water content, small intestine propulsion rate, MMP, ATP content, and the expression of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins in the colon tissue (P<0.01, P<0.05). The results of ultrastructure showed that the mitochondria of SMCs in the colon tissue was significantly swollen, with membrane damage and severe cristae rupture in the M group, while in the EA group, the mitochondrial swelling was mild, with significant improvement in the membrane and cristae integrity of the SMCs.

CONCLUSIONS: EA at ST25 and ST37 can effectively ameliorate gastrointestinal dysfunction and restore mitochondrial integrity in colonic SMCs of FC mice, which may be associated with its functions in up-regulating the expressions of HSP60 and LONP1 proteins to activate UPRmt.

articles.title: [Research on the underlying mechanisms of electroacupuncture in improving colonic dysmotility in ulcerative colitis mice based on cyclic nucleotide-gated cation channels].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To study the mechanism of electroacupuncture (EA) of "Shangjuxu"(ST37) underlying improvement of colonic dysmotility in ulcerative colitis (UC) mice through regulating hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated cation channel 2 (HCN2).

METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice were randomized into control, model and EA groups, with 8 mice in each group. The UC model was established by giving 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) to the mice. EA (2 Hz/100 Hz, 0.9 mA) was applied at bilateral ST37 for 20 min, once a day for 7 d. The body weight, stool appearance and bloody stool conditions were recorded and the disease activity index (DAI) score was determined. The morphological changes of the colonic tissue were observed after H.E. staining. The changes of colonic motility before and after EA intervention were assessed by using in vivo and in vitro electrophysiological methods. The colonic transit time (glass bead method) and intestinal propulsion rate (ink mark method) were calculated. The positive expression of colonic HCN2, 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT), tryptophan hydroxylase 1 (TPH1), and serotonin transporter (SERT) were detected by immunofluorescence staining. The expression levels of TPH1 and SERT mRNAs and proteins were detected using real-time quantitative PCR and Western blot separately. The Vil1MerCreMerHCN2fl/fl mice were randomly divided into a control group and an induction group, with 8 mice in each group. The Vil1MerCreMerHCN2fl/fl mice were specifically conditionally knocked out the HCN2 gene in the intestinal epithelium. The mice in the induction group were injected with 5 mg/mL tamoxifen. ELISA was used to detect the contents of 5-HT and cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) in the serum. The RIN-14B cells were divided into a normal group and a transfection group. The transfection group was knocked down the expression of HCN2 in the RIN-14B cells. ELISA was used to detect the contents of 5-HT and cAMP in the cell supernatants. Real-time quantitative PCR was used to detect the mRNA expressions of HCN2 and TPH1 in the RIN-14B cells.

RESULTS: In contrast to the control group, the model group showed a significant decrease in the body weight and a notable increase in the DAI score and histopathological score (all P<0.001). In vivo and in vitro electrophysiology showed that DSS mice had significant colonic motility dysfunction, decreased frequency, amplitude, and the area under the curve (AUC) of colonic pressure curves (all P<0.001). Colonic transit time was strikingly prolonged while propulsion rate was significantly lower in DSS mice (all P<0.001). Expression of colonic HCN2, co-localized with 5-HT, were markedly increased (P<0.001), along with elevated expression of 5-HT, TPH1 and SERT (all P<0.001). All the increase and decrease of the indexes mentioned above were reversed by EA ( P<0.001, P<0.01, P<0.05). Conditional deletion of HCN2 in the intestinal epithelium markedly reduced the serum contents of 5-HT and cAMP ( P<0.001). Knockdown of HCN2 in RIN-14B cells reduced the expression levels of HCN2and TPH1 mRNAs (P<0.001), along with a significant decrease of the contents of 5-HT and cAMP in the cell supernatant (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: EA at ST37 can improve colonic dysmotility in UC mice by modulating the expression of HCN2 in enterochromaffin cells and regulating the release of 5-HT.

articles.title: [Effects of electroacupuncture on apoptosis and inflammation in rats with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease based on integrated stress responses].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To observe the effect of electroacupuncture on rats with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), so as to explore its potential mechanisms.

METHODS: Thirty SD rats were randomly divided into a control group, a model group, and an electroacupuncture group, with 10 rats in each group. The COPD model was established by combining lipopolysaccharide instillation with smoke exposure. Following successful modeling, the electroacupuncture group received bilateral electroacupuncture at the "Feishu"(BL23) and "Zusanli"(ST36) points (dense-disperse wave, 4 Hz/20 Hz, 1-3 mA), once daily, 20 min/session, for 2 consecutive weeks. General conditions of rats in each group were compared before and after intervention. Post-intervention, histopathological changes in lung tissue were observed via HE staining. Serum levels of interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and IL-1β were measured by ELISA. TUNEL staining was used to detect apoptosis in lung tissue, and the apoptosis index was calculated. The protein and mRNA expressions of protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase (PERK), eukaryotic initiation factor 2α (eIF2α), activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4), C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP), B-cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2), and Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax) in lung tissue were detected by Western blot and real-time quantative PCR respectively.

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, rats in the model group exhibited poorer general condition after intervention, with significant pathological damage in lung tissue;serum IL-6, TNF-α and IL-1β levels and the apoptosis index in lung tissue were significantly increased (P<0.01), and serum IL-10 level was decreased (P<0.01). The protein and mRNA expressions of PERK, eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP and Bax in lung tissue were increased (P<0.01, P<0.05), while Bcl-2 protein and mRNA expressions were decreased (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, rats in the electroacupuncture group showed improved general condition and reduced pathological damage in lung tissue;serum IL-6, TNF-α and IL-1β levels and apoptosis index were decreased (P<0.05, P<0.01), and serum IL-10 level was increased (P<0.01). The protein and mRNA expressions of PERK, eIF2α, ATF4, CHOP and Bax in lung tissue were decreased (P<0.05), and Bcl-2 protein and mRNA expressions were increased (P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Electroacupuncture ameliorates lung injury in COPD rats, potentially by inhibiting the PERK/eIF2α/ATF4/CHOP cascade of the integrated stress response pathway, thereby reducing apoptosis and inflammation.

articles.title: [Electroacupuncture inhibits astrocyte activation and alleviates neuroinflammation in rats with ischemic stroke based on JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effect of electroacupuncture (EA) intervention on neuroinflammatory response in rats with ischemic stroke by modulating astrocyte activation, based on the Janus kinase 2(JAK2)/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3(STAT3) signaling pathway.

METHODS: Forty-five male SD rats were randomly selected as the sham operation group. The ischemic stroke model was established by occlusion of the middle cerebral artery by referring to the modified Zea Longa's suture-occlusion method. Ninety successfully modeled rats were randomly assigned to model group and EA group which were further divided into subgroups based on the intervention time points (1, 3 and 7 d). For rats of the EA group, EA (2 Hz/10 Hz, 1.5 mA) was applied to "Baihui" (GV20) and "Dazhui" (GV14) for 20 min (starting from 2 h post-modeling), once daily for 1, 3 or 7 d. The modified neurological severity score (mNSS) was used to assess neurological deficits, and 2, 3, 5-Triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining was employed to measure the cerebral infarction volume. Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining was used to observe histopathological changes in the ischemic cortex. The protein expression levels of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), JAK2, STAT3, phosphorylated-JAK2 (p-JAK2), p-STAT3, complement component 3 (C3), and S100 calcium-binding protein A10 (S100A10) in the ischemic brain tissue were detected using Western blot. The contents of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and IL-6 in the ischemic brain tissue were determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The mRNA expression levels of GFAP, JAK2, and STAT3 in the ischemic brain tissue were detected by using quantitative real-time PCR. The double-staining immunofluorescence intensity of GFAP and STAT3 of the ischemic brain tissue was determined using immunofluorescence staining.

RESULTS: Compared with the sham operation group, the model group showed a significant increase in cerebral infarction volume (P<0.01), and mNSS, protein expression levels of GFAP, JAK2, STAT3, p-JAK2, p-STAT3, and C3, contents of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and mRNA expression levels of GFAP, JAK2 and STAT3 at the 1st, 3rd and 7th day (P<0.01), and the immunofluorescence intensity of GFAP and STAT3 co-staining (P<0.01), and a significant reduction in the expression of S100A10 at the 1st, 3rd and 7th day (P<0.01). The ischemic cortex exhibited severe neuronal structural damage, characterized by obvious nuclear pyknosis, cellular swelling and rupture, disordered axonal arrangement and vacuolar changes. After EA intervention, all the increased and decreased levels of the indexes mentioned above were reversed (P<0.05, P<0.01), including obvious improvement of morphology of neurons in the ischemic cortex, characterized by more regular cell arrangement and clearer cellular nucleus. Compared with the group receiving EA for 1 d, the group with 7 d of EA treatment exhibited lower protein expression levels of GFAP, C3 and S100A10 as well as decreased contents of TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6 (P<0.01), while the group receiving EA for 3 d showed up-regulated S100A10 protein expression (P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: EA can improve neurological deficits and reduce cerebral ischemic volume in ischemic stroke rats, which may be related to its functions in inhibiting the activation of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, mitigating neuroinflammation response mediated by excessive astrocyte activation, and the effects are time-dependent.

articles.title: [Mechanism of acupuncture improving thrombolysis safety in ischemic stroke based on necroptosis mediated by RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL signaling pathway].
articles.journal: Zhen ci yan jiu = Acupuncture research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To observe the effect of acupuncture on inhibiting necroptosis mediated by the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/receptor-interacting protein kinase 3 (RIPK3)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling pathway in rat model of ischemic stroke, so as to reveal the mechanism underlying the improvement of ultra-time-window thrombolysis safety by acupuncture.

METHODS: Ninety-nine male successful modeling SD rats were randomly divided into the model, 6 h thrombolysis, and acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis groups, with 33 rats in each group. In addition, 33 SD rats were randomly selected as the sham-operation group. Except for the sham-operation group, rats in the other groups were subjected to the autologous thromboembolism method to establish the ischemic stroke model. Rats in the 6 h thrombolysis group were treated with intravenous thrombolysis using recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) at 6 h after the successful modeling. Rats in the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group were additionally treated with acupuncture at bilateral "Neiguan" (PC6) and "Shuigou" (GV26) for 20 min after the thrombolysis. Neurological function was evaluated by Bederson score. The cerebral infarction volume was measured by 2, 3, 5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was detected by Evans blue permeability assay. Brain water content was measured by the volume specific gravity method. Hemoglobin concentration was detected by spectrophotometry. The protein expressions of RIPK1, RIPK3, and p-MLKL were detected by Western blot. The mRNA expressions of RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL were detected by real-time PCR. The co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells was detected by double immunofluorescence staining.

RESULTS: After modeling, the cerebral blood flow of rats significantly decreased, and the neurobehavioral scores increased (P<0.01). At 24 h after successful modeling, compared with the sham-operation group, the model group had a significant increase in neurobehavioral scores, percentage of infarct volume, and BBB permeability (P<0.01), as well as an elevation in the protein expression level of RIPK1 (P<0.05) , the mRNA expression levels of RIPK1, RIPK3, and MLKL in the ischemic penumbra (IP, P<0.01, P<0.05), and increased percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP(P<0.01). Following intervention and compared with the model group, the 6 h thrombolysis group had a further increase in BBB permeability, brain water content, and cerebral hemoglobin concentration (P<0.01, P<0.05);elevated protein expression levels of RIPK3 and p-MLKL in the IP (P<0.05);increased mRNA expression levels of RIPK3 and MLKL in the IP (P<0.05);and an increased percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP (P<0.01). Compared with the model group, the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group showed decreased neurobehavioral scores, percentage of infarct volume, BBB permeability, and brain water content (P<0.01, P<0.05);decreased protein and mRNA expression levels of RIPK1 in the IP (P<0.05);and a reduced percentage of co-localization of p-MLKL and endothelial cells in the IP (P<0.05). Compared with the 6 h thrombolysis group, the acupuncture+6 h thrombolysis group demonstrated a significant decrease in all the aforementioned indicators (P<0.01, P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Timely intervention with acupuncture can improve neurological function, reduce cerebral infarct volume, lower BBB permeability, and decrease the incidence of thrombolytic complications in rats with ischemic stroke after thrombolysis, thereby improving the safety of thrombolysis. Its mechanism may be related to the inhibition of endothelial cell necroptosis mediated by the RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL signaling pathway.

articles.title: Expedited partner therapy uptake and STI clearance among cisgender women in a prospective study in Kenya.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We examined factors associated with expedited partner therapy (EPT) uptake and clearance of Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and/or Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) among women taking HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in Kenya.

METHODS: We conducted a nested analysis of cisgender women enrolled in the dPEP Kenya Study (N=449) who tested positive for CT and/or NG during quarterly testing over one year. Following each positive test, participants received treatment, were offered optional EPT, and returned for a test of cure 2-4 weeks later. Baseline characteristics were compared between participants with and without EPT uptake using chi-square tests. Generalized estimating equation models assessed visit-level correlates of EPT uptake and test-of-cure outcomes while accounting for repeated infections over time.

RESULTS: Among 140 participants with CT or NG infection at 209 study visits, 75% (n=105) accepted EPT at least once. Women who accepted EPT were more likely to have an independent income (61.9% p=0.018) and report recent transactional sex (54.3%, p=0.032). At the visit level, having a primary sex partner was positively associated with EPT uptake (OR=2.17, 95% CI=1.01-4.65, p=0.047). Intimate partner violence was associated with lower EPT uptake in multivariable analysis (OR=0.23, 95% CI=0.06-0.95, p=0.042). EPT uptake was not significantly associated with a negative test-of-cure result (OR=2.42, 95% CI=0.89-6.56, p=0.082).

CONCLUSIONS: EPT uptake was high among women taking PrEP in Kenya. While partner and relationship factors influenced uptake, EPT was not significantly associated with STI clearance at test of cure.

articles.title: Self-administered therapies in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria: balancing quality of life with clinically relevant risks.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Complement inhibitors have transformed outcomes in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), with intravenous (IV) C5 inhibitors resulting in sustained hemolysis control, reduced thrombotic risk, and improved survival. Ongoing IV infusions, however, can be burdensome for some patients, and terminal complement blockade can result in clinically significant extravascular hemolysis (EVH) in a subset of patients. Four new self-administered agents, pegcetacoplan, iptacopan, crovalimab, and danicopan, have expanded the therapeutic landscape in PNH.

AREAS COVERED: This review draws on pivotal trial data, patient-reported outcome analyses, and real-world evidence to examine the current clinical role of each agent. We searched PubMed and Google Scholar with no date range limitations, supplemented by hematology conference abstracts and regulatory documents. We weigh patient-centered benefits against clinically relevant risks, including adherence, infection risk, breakthrough hemolysis, and limited pregnancy data. We offer a practical framework for approaching self-administered therapies in PNH.

EXPERT OPINION: Self-administered therapies expand options for individualized PNH care, but greater autonomy shifts responsibility for adherence and complication recognition onto patients, underscoring the continued need for structured education, patient support programs, and specialist oversight. Longer-term real-world data, particularly on adherence, breakthrough hemolysis, and pregnancy, are needed to guide patient selection and further support use of these agents.

articles.title: A chromone-based Schiff base derivative for the Cd2+-promoted detection of l-proline: validated by DFT, test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, cellular imaging, and real/herbal water recovery analysis.
articles.abstract: l-proline is a vital stress marker in plants and an indicator of food quality and clinical diagnosis. In this work, we applied a simple chromone-based Schiff base derivative, (E)-3-(((3-mercapto-5-phenyl-4H-1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)imino)methyl)-4H-chromen-4-one (CT), for the Cd2+-complex-promoted detection of l-proline in acetonitrile. Within 10 minutes of incubation, the CT-Cd2+ complex exhibited a strong PL "Turn-On" response in the presence of l-proline among the amino acids, which remained stable between pH 3 and 8. The Job's plot and 1H NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance)-based titration studies confirmed the 1 : 1 stoichiometry of CT + Cd2+ to l-proline. Between 0.1 µM and 300 µM, the PL linear dynamic range of CT + Cd2+ to l-proline was observed, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 141 nM and an association constant (K a) of 4.25 × 103 M-1 using the Benesi-Hildebrand plot. The mode of binding and the possible photoinduced electron transfer/fluorescence resonance energy transfer (PET/FRET) mechanism are defined by FTIR spectroscopy, 1H NMR, HR mass spectrometry, and density functional theory (DFT) studies. l-proline sensing by the Cd2+ complex-promoted technique is corroborated using a test strip, cotton swab, fish tissue, and A549/MCF-7 cellular imaging. l-proline recovery from tap water and herbal water extracts (including Astragalus root (AA), Hedysari root (NAAI), and Coastal Glehnia root (SGC)) ranged from 89.89% to 113.98%. This unique design drives future innovation for l-proline monitoring in biological and environmental samples.

articles.title: Corrigendum to 'Ex vivo modelling reveals low levels of CKS1 inhibition boost haematopoiesis via AKT/Foxo1 signalling' Experimental Hematology 146C 2026 104768.
Scale-Dependent Friction in Rough SiO2/Single-Crystal MoS2 Contacts.
articles.abstract: The scale limits of superlubricity in realistic multiasperity contacts remain poorly understood. Although lateral atomic-force cancellation in incommensurate or disordered interfaces can generate low friction, how experimentally accessible contact size, local stress state, and load distribution regulate this scale-dependent behavior remains unclear. Here, we investigate the scale-dependent shear strength of SiO2 glass sphere/single-crystal MoS2 contacts with different sphere radii using atomic force microscopy and a custom microtribometer across extended load ranges. By combining power spectral density-based random rough surface generation with boundary element method simulations, we evaluate a dimensionless contact-scale parameter ai/bcore,i defined by the ratio between contact-patch radius and a characteristic elastic core width in rough multiasperity interfaces. The results show that the effective shear strength decreases continuously with increasing real contact area at small-to-intermediate contact scales, consistent with enhanced statistical cancellation of lateral atomic forces expected for disordered interfaces. As contact scale further increases, this reduction is progressively suppressed as the maximum scale parameter (ai/bcore,i)max approaches unity and an increasing fraction of the load is carried by contact patches satisfying ai/bcore,i > 1. The R = 2.5 mm probe condition exhibits a higher effective shear strength and a broader simulated contact-pressure distribution than the smaller-probe conditions. However, because sphere radius and the measured roughness spectrum were not independently varied, these differences cannot be attributed uniquely to sphere curvature. Instead, they reflect the combined influence of probe geometry, roughness statistics, and the resulting multiasperity contact state. Our results establish a multiscale framework linking atomic-force cancellation, finite contact-size effects, and rough-contact statistics, revealing how structural superlubricity gradually loses its scale invariance in realistic multiasperity interfaces.

articles.title: Astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles deliver Serpina3k to attenuate cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by restraining neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To determine whether astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) deliver Serpina3k to recipient neural cells and protect against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI).

METHODS: A mouse transient middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion model was combined with pharmacological inhibition of sEV release, astrocyte-targeted Serpina3k knockdown and intrathecal delivery of astrocyte-derived sEVs. Brain sEV cargo was profiled by label-free proteomics and Transwell co-cultures were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Neurological outcomes, infarct volume, apoptosis and inflammatory mediators were assessed, and Serpina3k-interacting proteins were identified by co-immunoprecipitation.

RESULTS: Blocking sEV release aggravated neurological deficits, neuronal apoptosis and inflammation. Brain-derived sEVs increased after ischemia-reperfusion and protected neurons against oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation. Serpina3k was enriched in ischemia-derived sEVs and localized predominantly to astrocytes; astrocytic Serpina3k knockdown reduced sEV-associated Serpina3k and worsened deficits, whereas Serpina3k-deficient sEVs increased neuronal apoptosis, microglial IL-1beta and IL-18 release, infarct volume and Caspase-6/NLRP3 signalling. Serpina3k co-immunoprecipitated with Caspase-6 and Omi/HtrA2. In vivo, Serpina3k-deficient astrocytic sEVs were associated with larger infarct volume, increased Omi/HtrA2 expression and reduced HAX-1 expression.

CONCLUSION: Astrocyte-derived sEV-associated Serpina3k is an endogenous protective cargo that limits cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by restraining microglial inflammatory activation and neuronal apoptosis.

articles.title: A consensus spinal cord cell-type atlas across mouse, macaque, and human.
articles.abstract: The spinal cord contains cell types critical for motor, sensory, and autonomic function, many of which are implicated in neurological disease and injury. Yet no shared molecular framework links human spinal cord cell types to the animal models used to study them. Here, we present a cross-species atlas integrating single-nucleus gene expression, chromatin accessibility, and spatial transcriptomics from over one million nuclei spanning cervical to sacral segments in human, macaque, and mouse. Consensus clustering resolves 111 cell type groups replicable across all three species, whose spatial distributions map spinal laminae and nuclei, including Clarke's column.
