Identity and laminar organization are highly conserved, yet abundance and expression are allometrically scaled, with the dorsal horn being the principal site of divergence, concentrated in neurotransmitter receptor genes and including a primate-specific glycine receptor subunit switch. Sequence models uncover a conserved transcription factor grammar and nominate motifs underlying enhancer-adeno-associated virus (AAV) access to a divergent dorsal horn population.

articles.title: Forward stroke volume and ejection fraction estimation in mitral regurgitation: a computational hemodynamic approach.
articles.abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is a common valvular heart disease in which conventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) can be misleading, as they do not distinguish between effective forward flow and regurgitant volume. This limitation may result in underestimation of the true hemodynamic burden of the disease. In this study, we develop a computational framework based on a closed-loop lumped-parameter cardiovascular model to evaluate forward cardiac function in MR. The model incorporates a regurgitant pathway across the mitral valve together with flow calculations at the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), allowing estimation of forward stroke volume (FSV) and forward ejection fraction (FEF). The model was first assessed against published physiological reference values and then used to simulate different levels of mitral leakage. As simulated regurgitant fraction increased from 0% to 58.30%, FSV decreased from 65.35 to 51.37 ml and FEF from 60.22% to 35.21%, while LVEF increased from 60.17% to 84.40%. These results illustrate how increased LVEF can coexist with reduced forward output in modeled MR. Overall, the proposed approach provides a physiologically interpretable and computationally efficient tool for analyzing MR hemodynamics. The framework provides a research tool for investigating MR hemodynamics and comparing conventional and forward-flow-based measures. Further validation using patient-specific clinical data is required before it can be considered for clinical application.

articles.title: Endothelial Contributions to Venous Thrombus Resolution.
articles.abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is an obstructive vascular condition with an incidence of approximately 1 in 1,000 adults per year. Complications of DVT include post-thrombotic syndrome, which is debilitating and painful, and pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Current treatments for DVT are associated with increased risks of bleeding, infection, or re-thrombosis, and failure to accelerate natural venous thrombus resolution. Venous thrombus resolution occurs through a process of organization that involves thrombus retraction away from the vein, fibrinolysis of the thrombus, and the formation of vascular channels within and around the thrombus. Endothelial cell (EC)-lined vascular channels are present in rodent and human resolving thrombi. Rodent models of DVT show that thrombus neovascularization occurs as early as 3 to 4 days after thrombus induction and increases progressively thereafter throughout thrombus resolution. The extent to which thrombus neovascularization contributes to its resolution, as well as the source of the ECs that vascularize the resolving thrombus, is unclear. Circumstantial evidence suggests that neovascularization is driven by resident ECs that ingress into the resolving thrombus, while circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) promote neovascularization in a paracrine manner. Resident ECs and EPCs also contribute to thrombus fibrinolysis. The aim of this review is to describe the role of ECs and EPCs in DVT resolution, and the potential of promoting thrombus endothelialization and vascularization for the treatment of DVT. We will also outline knowledge gaps in the understanding of endothelial contributions to DVT resolution. The promotion of EC-mediated thrombus resolution represents a novel therapeutic strategy for DVT.

articles.title: A Keratin and Polyacrylamide Dual Network Hydrogel Based on Dynamic Coordination between Polydopamine and Mg2+ for Infected Wound Repair.
articles.abstract: Exogenous bacterial infection severely impairs skin wound repair and creates a complex therapeutic challenge that requires simultaneous infection control, oxidative stress regulation, and tissue regeneration. In this study, a PAM/HK/PDANP-Mg2+ multifunctional hydrogel (HPPM) was developed as a cascade therapeutic dressing for infected wounds. In this system, polyacrylamide (PAM) provided a flexible covalently cross-linked framework. Hydrolyzed keratin (HK) offered bioactive and cytocompatible interfaces. Polydopamine nanoparticles (PDANPs) endowed the hydrogel with adhesiveness, photothermal antibacterial activity, and radical scavenging capacity. Coordination between Mg2+ and PDA, together with intermolecular hydrogen bonding, contributed to reversible physical cross-linking within the PAM framework. The optimized HPPM (0.012) hydrogel exhibited a porous structure, high swelling ratio (∼1277%), strong adhesion properties (31.00 kPa), and large tensile elongation (∼560%). Under 808 nm near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, HPPM achieved mild photothermal heating and over 99% antibacterial efficiency against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus). It also showed favorable antioxidant activity, cytocompatibility, and pro-migratory effects. In an S. aureus-infected rat wound model, HPPM (0.012) + NIR accelerated wound closure, reduced inflammation, enhanced collagen deposition and re-epithelialization, and regulated IL-10/TNF-α expression. These results suggest that HPPM promotes infected wound healing through dynamic coordination-driven cascade remodeling of the infected wound microenvironment.

articles.title: Epoxy-Functionalized Polysilsesquioxane Coatings for Rear-Side Impact Protection of Thin Functional Ceramics.
articles.abstract: High-performance protective coatings capable of preventing catastrophic impact fracture of thin brittle inorganic substrates are urgently demanded for next-generation 5G/6G consumer electronics; however rational design strategies that simultaneously retain pristine surface aesthetics and achieve prominent shock resistance are still lacking. Herein, a rigid epoxy-functionalized polysilsesquioxane hybrid resin is synthesized, followed by cross-linking with various amine curing agents through a high-efficiency synchronous thermal-moisture dual-curing route. The optimized EGSI coating crosslinked by isophorone diamine (IPDA) achieves a pencil scratch hardness of 9H and a nanoindentation modulus of 2.66 GPa. Viscoelastic characterization confirms a distinctive filler-free self-reinforcement effect originating from the siloxane skeleton; the glass transition becomes indistinct, and the optimized coating preserved ∼40% of its initial glassy storage modulus, corresponding to a remarkably high rubbery plateau modulus of ∼750 MPa up to 300 °C. Ball-drop impact tests support the effectiveness of the proposed rigid backing structural constraint mechanism. When coated on the rear face of 300 μm structural ceramic sheets, the EGSI layer elevates the maximum crack-free nominal drop energy to 63.9 mJ, representing a 233% enhancement compared with bare ceramics. Different from conventional front-side energy-absorbing coatings, this noninvasive rear-side reinforcement scheme avoids damaging the decorative exterior of ceramic components and enables low-cost upgrading of ordinary sintered ceramics to high shock-resistant grade. This study establishes a design approach for the tested systems and coating configuration optimization methodology for reinforcing brittle substrates, showing great application prospects in smartphone ceramic back covers, ultrathin glass panels, and other electronic protective components.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning reveals topological control of vacancy energetics in 2D carbon.
articles.abstract: Vacancy defects strongly influence the structural and energetic behavior of two-dimensional carbon materials, yet their energetic description remains challenging due to the interplay between local reconstruction and network topology. In this work, we combine atomistic simulations, topological descriptors, and machine learning to investigate vacancy energetics in graphene and phagraphene. A dataset of defective structures was generated across vacancy concentrations from 2% to 24% and characterized using physically grounded descriptors, including ring statistics. Increasing vacancy concentration induces a progressive reorganization of the carbon network, with a reduction of hexagonal rings and the emergence of non-hexagonal motifs. This effect is more pronounced in graphene, while phagraphene exhibits a more distributed response due to its intrinsic topological diversity. Machine learning models achieve high predictive accuracy, with graphene displaying a structured and near-linear descriptor-energy relationship, whereas phagraphene requires more flexible models. SHAP analysis identifies the vacancy count as the dominant contributor to the predictions, with ring-based topology acting as a secondary but systematic correction. A reduced model based on nvac and the topological descriptor (R5 - R6) captures the main energetic trends, and the comparison between graphene and phagraphene shows that the weight of this topological correction depends strongly on the underlying lattice. These results establish a direct link between topology, structural disorder, and vacancy energetics in two-dimensional carbon systems.

articles.title: LSEC-derived CXCL9 orchestrates immune recruitment and hepatocyte reprogramming in liver fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver injury involves complex intercellular communication, yet the contribution of non-classical immune cell populations remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC)-derived CXCL9 as a pivotal regulator of hepatocyte reprogramming and fibrogenesis in chronic liver injury. Through the integration of bulk transcriptomic profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in vitro hepatocyte assays, we demonstrate that CXCL9 is robustly upregulated in LSECs, rather than Kupffer cells or hepatic stellate cells, following toxic liver injury. KEGG enrichment analysis reveals significant activation of the chemokine signaling pathway (NES = 1.75, P .adj = 1.9 × 10 -4 ), and functional experiments show that exogenous CXCL9 potently induces both regenerative gene ( Hbegf) and pro-inflammatory gene expressions ( Ccl2 , Cxcl2 , Il6 , and Tnf ) in primary hepatocytes ( P  < 0.0001-0.01). Gain- and loss-of-function co-culture models further confirm that LSEC-derived CXCL9 is both necessary and sufficient for hepatocyte inflammatory activation and regenerative responses, predominantly via CXCR3 signaling. These findings reveal an underappreciated LSEC-CXCL9-CXCR3 axis as a driver of maladaptive parenchymal reprogramming and fibrogenesis, expanding the paradigm of hepatic chemokine biology and highlighting a novel therapeutic target for chronic liver disease.

articles.title: Myocardial Bridge in High School Athlete With Exertional Symptoms: Innocent Bystander or Major Player?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial bridge (MB) is largely considered a benign condition, though it may lead to myocardial ischemia because of coronary vessel compression. It is a known cause of sudden cardiac arrest/death in young athletes.

CASE SUMMARY: A 16-year-old boy athlete with asthma presented with exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and tachycardia following 3-mile races. Echocardiography showed a small atrial septal defect and normal coronary artery origins. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated a left anterior descending MB. Stress cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging showed no inducible perfusion defects. Cardiac catheterization for intracoronary flow assessment demonstrated compromised coronary flow distal to the MB, with compression on intravascular ultrasound. Surgical unroofing of the MB allowed a safe return to competition.

DISCUSSION: Exhaustive workup and invasive assessment of intracoronary flow are invaluable to determine significant compression of a MB causing ischemia in athletes with exertional symptoms.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Exertional symptoms in athletes should be considered for advanced imaging to exclude significant lesions that compromise coronary flow.

articles.title: Puerarin preserves microglial homeostasis and protects against acute cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating autophagy and oxidative stress through Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microglial oxidative stress and dysregulated autophagy contribute to secondary neuronal injury following ischemic stroke. Puerarin (PUE), a bioactive isoflavone with established antioxidative and neuroprotective properties, may protect against cerebral ischemia by modulating microglial dysfunction; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: The neuroprotective effects of PUE were investigated in a rat transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) model and in BV2 microglia subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Microglial phenotypic alterations, oxidative stress, and autophagic activity were evaluated using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), ultrastructural, biochemical, and fluorescence-based analyzes. Data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics, pharmacological gain- and loss-of-function approaches, and adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9)-mediated Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) knockdown were employed to define the role of Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK2/STAT3) signaling. Microglia-mediated neuroprotection was further assessed using an HT22 neuron-microglia co-culture system.

RESULTS: PUE reshaped the microglial landscape by preserving the homeostatic microglial phenotype while suppressing ischemia-induced pathological activation. PUE reduced intracellular and mitochondrial ROS production, restored redox homeostasis, suppressed excessive autophagosome formation, and downregulated the autophagy-related proteins 3/5/12 (ATG3/5/12). Mechanistically, these protective effects were mediated through inhibition of JAK2/STAT3 signaling. Genetic silencing of JAK2 recapitulated the effects of PUE, whereas pharmacological activation of JAK2/STAT3 largely abolished its antioxidative, anti-autophagic, and neuroprotective activities. Furthermore, conditioned media from PUE-treated microglia significantly alleviated neuronal injury in HT22 cells, supporting a microglia-mediated paracrine mechanism of neuroprotection.

CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings identify JAK2/STAT3-dependent regulation of the oxidative stress-autophagy axis as a critical mechanism underlying microglial homeostasis after acute cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) and establish PUE as a promising therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Multiscale and cross-organ antidiabetic effects of Ajuga decumbens and harpagide: Integrating hepatic metabolism, immune regulation, and gut microbiota.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a complex metabolic disorder involving dysregulated glucose homeostasis and interconnected disturbances across multiple organs. Plant-derived bioactive compounds represent promising candidates for metabolic regulation. Although Ajuga decumbens exhibits anti-inflammatory and lipid-modulating activities, its antidiabetic potential and underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized, particularly from a multiscale and cross-organ perspective.

PURPOSE: This exploratory study aimed to evaluate the antidiabetic activities of A. decumbens extracts, identify candidate bioactive constituents, and investigate their potential mechanisms within an integrated multiscale framework.

METHODS: An integrated experimental strategy combining in vivo, in vitro, in silico, and omics-based approaches was employed. High-fat diet (HFD)-fed diabetic mice were used to evaluate acute and long-term metabolic effects. α-amylase inhibition assays were performed to investigate potential effects on carbohydrate digestion. Phytochemical profiling, quantitative chromatography, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to identify and characterize candidate bioactive constituents. Transcriptomic analysis and 16S rRNA gene sequencing were used to explore hepatic molecular responses and gut microbial alterations. Integrated correlation network analysis was subsequently performed to examine associations among metabolic phenotypes, hepatic gluconeogenic signaling, immune polarization, and gut microbiota.

RESULTS: Ajuga decumbens leaf extract (ALE) reduced postprandial blood glucose by 27.77% following an acute starch challenge and inhibited α-amylase activity (IC₅₀ = 47.39 ± 8.84 μg/ml). Harpagide (HPG), identified as a quantitatively prominent bioactive constituent, also exhibited α-amylase inhibitory activity (IC₅₀ = 8.01 ± 1.48 μg/ml) and reduced postprandial glucose by 25.99%. Four weeks of treatment improved glycemic regulation, lipid metabolism, and insulin resistance-related indices while attenuating diabetes-associated histopathological abnormalities. Mechanistic investigations indicated that ALE and HPG modulated hepatic gluconeogenesis-associated signaling through the Akt/FoxO1 pathway and altered macrophage polarization-related markers. Both treatments were also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, including the relative abundances of an uncultured taxon within Desulfobacterota, Colidextribacter, and the Eubacterium xylanophilum group. Integrated correlation analysis further revealed two partially differentiated association networks linking hepatic gluconeogenic regulation, immune polarization, gut microbial composition and diversity, and metabolic phenotypes.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide integrated evidence supporting the antidiabetic potential of A. decumbens leaf extract and HPG through multiple biological processes involving intestinal α-amylase inhibition, hepatic gluconeogenic regulation, immune modulation, and gut microbial alterations. The identification of distinct cross-scale association patterns provides a systematic framework for investigating their metabolic effects and supports further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation of ALE and HPG as plant-derived candidates for T2DM management.

articles.title: Catastrophic Multivessel Coronary Thrombosis After Discontinuation of Antithrombotic Therapy in Adult-Onset Kawasaki Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kawasaki disease (KD) diagnosis in adulthood is often delayed and can lead to severe coronary sequelae.

CASE SUMMARY: A 23-year-old man who first developed clinical manifestations of KD at age 18 years developed a medium-sized coronary artery aneurysm because of delayed initial treatment. Antithrombotic therapy, including warfarin, was prescribed but later discontinued during follow-up. At age 23 years, he presented with acute myocardial infarction complicated by lethal ventricular arrhythmias requiring mechanical circulatory support. Emergency coronary angiography revealed concurrent thrombotic occlusions of the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries. Emergent percutaneous coronary intervention of both vessels restored coronary flow, resulting in favorable neurologic and clinical recovery.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights that interruption of antithrombotic therapy in patients with KD-related coronary aneurysms may precipitate catastrophic multivessel thrombosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patients with persistent KD-related coronary artery aneurysms require follow-up and antithrombotic therapy tailored to thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Very Late Complete Heart Block After Cardiac Transplantation Presenting as Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complete atrioventricular (AV) block is an uncommon late complication after heart transplantation; in the denervated allograft, which depends on rate for output, it may present as heart failure rather than syncope.

CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old man developed complete AV block 22 years after biatrial transplantation, presenting with acute decompensated heart failure and preserved ejection fraction. Serial electrocardiograms over 5 years documented stepwise progression to complete AV block. After conventional septal fixation repeatedly failed, left bundle branch area pacing was delivered via the atrial port with a right ventricular backup lead on the ventricular port; symptoms and function improved at 6 months.

DISCUSSION: Very late allograft conduction disease is rarely documented longitudinally and is easily misattributed to rejection; physiological conduction system pacing was feasible despite failed conventional fixation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider conduction disease in long-term transplant recipients presenting with heart failure, and use serial electrocardiographic surveillance to detect its gradual evolution.

articles.title: Demographic variation of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus among Round Gobies in the St. Lawrence River.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We investigated the demographic dynamics of viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV) infections in wild Round Goby Neogobius melanostomus from the nearshore habitats of the upper St. Lawrence River from 2018 to 2022. We examined viral prevalence and titers between Round Goby sexes and age-classes to identify how demography correlates with prevalence and amplification of this pathogen within this host species.

METHODS: Reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction was used to detect and quantify viral N-gene genetic material in pooled organ (i.e., liver, kidney, spleen) and brain tissues of wild Round Gobies that were collected from the upper St. Lawrence River. Age and sex were assigned to each individual to elucidate how patterns of infection prevalence and amplification vary depending on demography within this host species.

RESULT: Viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus was detected by reverse-transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction in 49.62% of the sampled Round Gobies, with significant variation in prevalence and titers observed across demographic groups. Sex-based VHSV prevalence was 15.87% in females and 55.95% in males, and infected fish of both sexes contained similar median viral titers. Age-based prevalence increased with age, ranging from 14.29% in age-1 fish to 68.35% in age-4 fish, whereas viral titers were highest in age-2 fish and decreased with age thereafter.

CONCLUSION: Round Gobies exhibit a high prevalence (49.62%) of VHSV infections. However, the pathogen is distributed unevenly among demographics within this species. Both sex and age interact with the infection status of an individual.

articles.title: Tangeretin alleviates airway hyperresponsiveness through epithelial prostaglandin E2 signaling.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) is driven by airway inflammation together with disrupted epithelial-smooth muscle signaling. Current therapies mainly target inflammation or directly relax airway smooth muscle (ASM), whereas strategies aimed at restoring endogenous epithelial control of ASM tone remain incompletely explored. Using target prediction and screening, we identified tangeretin as a candidate modulator of airway epithelial cells (AECs) that may regulate neighboring ASM function.

PURPOSE: To determine whether tangeretin modulates epithelial-smooth muscle crosstalk, elucidate the underlying mechanism and evaluate its therapeutic effect in AHR.

STUDY DESIGN: Ex vivo functional assays, primary cell experiments and a murine asthma model were combined for investigation.

METHODS: A network pharmacology approach was used to predict candidate targets, which were then evaluated by pharmacological validation and molecular docking. Contractile tension recordings were performed in isolated mouse tracheal rings with intact or denuded epithelium. Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) release from primary mouse AECs was quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Whole-cell currents were recorded by patch clamp technique. ASM membrane potential was assessed using DiBAC4(3)-based fluorescence imaging. An ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma model was established to evaluate the effects of nebulized tangeretin on AHR and lung function. AHR was assessed by whole-body plethysmography as methacholine-induced enhanced pause (Penh) and lung function was evaluated by forced expiratory manoeuvres.

RESULTS: Tangeretin induced concentration-dependent relaxation of mouse tracheal rings in an epithelium-dependent manner. Cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition attenuated tangeretin-evoked relaxation. Molecular docking suggested relatively modest predicted non-covalent interactions between tangeretin and COX-1/2, consistent with increased PGE2 release from primary AECs. Antagonism of E-type prostanoid receptor 2 (EP2) or EP4 receptors, or inhibition of the large conductance Ca2+-activated K+ channel (BKCa), significantly reduced tangeretin-induced relaxation. Patch clamp recordings further verified that PGE2 markedly enhanced outward currents in ASM cells, which were inhibited by the selective BKCa blocker iberiotoxin. Supernatant from tangeretin-treated AECs triggered ASM membrane hyperpolarization, while L-type voltage-dependent Ca2+ channel (VDCC) blockade attenuated the relaxation elicited by tangeretin. Tangeretin also retained partial relaxant activity under high-K+ depolarizing conditions. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, nebulized tangeretin reduced methacholine-induced increases in the Penh index and improved FEV100/FVC, with effects similar to salbutamol. However, COX inhibition diminished the bronchodilatory effects of tangeretin. Moreover, nebulized tangeretin ameliorated OVA-induced type 2 inflammation.

CONCLUSION: Tangeretin may promote COX-dependent PGE2 production in AECs, which engages an EP receptor-BKCa-VDCC suppression cascade to reduce ASM contractility and AHR. These findings identify an epithelium-driven mechanism underlying tangeretin-induced ASM relaxation and provide a rationale for further investigating its therapeutic potential in asthma.

articles.title: Diagnosis of Chagas disease using tensor Tucker-compressed ECG scalograms.
articles.abstract: Objective. As modest illness-related patterns are dispersed throughout the temporal, spectral, and inter-lead dimensions of the electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, automated diagnosis of Chagas disease from ECG recordings remains difficult. To address this challenge, this study develops a tensor-based representation framework that preserves the multidimensional characteristics of ECG scalograms while learning low-dimensional projection subspaces using Tucker decomposition.Approach. The proposed framework integrates multi-domain feature extraction, tensor-based representation learning, dimensionality reduction, and ensemble classification for automated Chagas disease detection from 12-lead ECG recordings. It extracts five categories of features: (a) scalogram from specific ECG leads; (b) scalogram features from beat-aligned averaged ECG segments; (c) heart rate variability-based statistics; (d) statistical features from every ECG lead; and (e) patient information (weight, age, and sex). The continuous wavelet Transform for time-frequency feature extraction is used to create scalograms, which allow for the capture of multi-scale frequency patterns and local transients linked to the course of the disease. A 3D tensor representation that maintains spatial, temporal, and frequency linkages was created by assembling the scalogram-based features. Optimal partial Tucker tensor decomposition was used to reduce dimensionality. For improved classification performance, the resulting core tensor was flattened, merged with the remaining features (b to e), and then subjected to Fisher score-based feature selection. A RUSBoost classifier was employed for binary classification of 12-lead ECG recordings into Chagas and other classes, while addressing class imbalance through random under-sampling.Main results. The proposed framework was evaluated on the hidden PhysioNet/CinC 2025 Challenge test set through a follow-up Challenge submission under the team nameSpectra, achieving an accuracy of, an1-Chagas score of, an AUPRC of, an AUROC of, and an overall Challenge Score of, indicating good generalization to previously unseen ECG recordings.Significance. This work introduces a projection-based tensor representation learning strategy for ECG analysis that transforms high-dimensional scalogram based features into compact latent features while retaining clinically relevant temporal, spectral, and inter-lead information. The proposed framework can facilitate reliable automated Chagas disease screening from routine ECG recordings for earlier clinical intervention.

articles.title: Restoring Coronary Vasomotion in Pediatric Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy: A Bioadaptor-Based Interventional Strategy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous coronary interventions in cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) remain challenging. In CAV, diffuse neointimal proliferation contributes to progressive allograft dysfunction and increased mortality. Although second-generation drug-eluting stents are widely utilized, permanent vessel caging may limit adaptive remodeling, resulting in target lesion failure. Drug-eluting coronary bioadaptors have been designed to provide vessel support while enabling restoration of physiological vasomotion.

CASE SUMMARY: We report the case of a 15-year-old male patient with CAV, 4 years after heart transplantation. A DynamX drug-eluting coronary bioadaptor was successfully implanted in the circumflex artery. At 20-month follow-up, coronary angiography and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated preserved vessel patency and compliance, with no evidence of target lesion failure.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the feasibility of bioadaptor-based percutaneous coronary interventions in a pediatric heart transplant recipient with CAV and supports further evaluation of this technology in patients with complex coronary lesions.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Bioadaptors may provide acute vessel support while allowing dynamic vessel motion after uncaging in CAV.

articles.title: Microenvironment-adaptive nanozyme biomaterials for diabetic wound regeneration: materials chemistry, catalytic networks and tissue-specific delivery.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are sustained by a dynamically coupled microenvironment characterised by hyperglycaemia, oxidative stress, hypoxia, persistent infection and defective inflammatory resolution. Importantly, these abnormalities are not only therapeutic targets but also chemical boundary conditions that determine nanozyme catalysis by regulating substrate availability, electron transfer, active-site accessibility and mass transport. This review therefore moves beyond the conventional classification of nanozymes according to material type or nominal enzyme-like activity and establishes a structure-microenvironment-catalysis-delivery-regeneration framework for diabetic wound therapy. We critically analyse how metal valence, defect chemistry, coordination environments, heterointerfacial charge transfer, pore architecture and surface biointerfaces determine catalytic behaviour under wound-relevant conditions. Superoxide dismutase (SOD)-, catalase (CAT)-, peroxidase (POD)-, oxidase (OXD)- and glucose oxidase (GOx)-like activities are interpreted as an interconnected reaction network involving substrate generation and competition, oxygen consumption and production, and stage-dependent changes in the balance between antibacterial oxidation and regenerative redox regulation. Delivery matrices are considered integral components of the catalytic system because they regulate nanozyme retention, substrate transport and active-site exposure. Diabetes-associated oral wounds are further discussed as a tissue-specific stress test characterised by salivary clearance, polymicrobial biofilms, mechanical disturbance and coupled soft-hard tissue regeneration. Finally, priorities for wound-relevant catalytic benchmarking, mechanistic attribution, biosafety, manufacturing reproducibility and clinical translation are proposed.

articles.title: Isoliquiritigenin attenuates doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative damage through the Piezo1/Ca²⁺/Pdk4 signaling axis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Doxorubicin (DOX) is widely employed as an antineoplastic agent in clinical settings, yet its therapeutic utility is constrained by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, partly resulting from oxidative injury to cardiomyocytes and impairment of mitochondrial function. Hence, there is an urgent imperative to develop cardioprotective strategies targeting oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. Previous studies have suggested that isoliquiritigenin (Iso) confers protection against DOX-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC); however, the exact molecular mechanisms governing its pharmacological activity have yet to be elucidated.

PURPOSE: The objective of this study was to further explore the cardioprotective effects conferred by isoliquiritigenin (Iso) and to clarify the potential molecular mechanisms involved.

METHODS /STUDY DESIGNS: Oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, myocardial injury, and intracellular calcium levels were examined in cardiomyocytes. In addition, mechanistic investigations were conducted using cardiomyocyte-specific Piezo1-knockdown mice generated by AAV9, along with EGTA treatment for calcium depletion, Piezo1 knockdown, and Pdk4 overexpression in cardiomyocytes.

RESULTS: Treatment with Iso was found to significantly attenuate DOX-induced myocardial injury, histopathological damage, and apoptosis of cardiomyocytes in vivo. Moreover, in vitro experiments corroborated that Iso effectively rescued H9c2 cells and NMCMs from DOX-induced cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, and apoptosis. Further investigations revealed that isoliquiritigenin (Iso) preserved mitochondrial function through suppression of oxidative stress damage and restoration of the equilibrium between mitochondrial fusion and fission. The underlying mechanism revealed that Iso exerts its effects by targeting the Piezo1 mechanosensitive channel and subsequently modulating Pdk4 via Ca²⁺ signaling.

CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings suggest that the cardioprotective efficacy of Iso against DOX-induced cardiotoxicity is mediated by the Piezo1-Ca²⁺-Pdk4 signaling pathway, which operates to attenuate oxidative insults, preserve mitochondrial integrity, and reduce apoptotic loss of cardiac myocytes.

articles.title: Ginsenoside Rg6 ameliorates COPD by targeting RAGE to suppress MAPK/NF-κB signaling, thereby preserving alveolar barrier integrity and attenuating EMT.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is pathologically characterized by progressive alveolar epithelial barrier disruption, a pathological process primarily driven by chronic cigarette smoke exposure. While Ginsenoside Rg6 (Rg6) has shown therapeutic promise in pulmonary injury models, its direct molecular targets and the precise mechanisms by which it preserves barrier integrity remain unclear.

PURPOSE: This study investigates whether Rg6 mitigates COPD by directly targeting the RAGE receptor, thereby suppressing the downstream signaling axes concurrently preserve alveolar barrier integrity and attenuate epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT).

METHODS: The therapeutic efficacy of Rg6 was evaluated in CSE-challenged MLE-12 alveolar epithelial cells and an LPS/CS-driven mouse COPD model. Transcriptomic profiling was utilized to identify upstream regulatory nodes. Direct Rg6-RAGE engagement was rigorously validated via molecular docking, MD simulations, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), DARTS, and CETSA. The functional dependency of Rg6's protective effects on RAGE was dissected using siRNA knockdown in vitro and AAV-shRAGE delivery in vivo.

RESULTS: Oral Rg6 significantly ameliorated pulmonary function decline, emphysema, and the inflammatory microenvironment in COPD mice, achieving efficacy comparable to dexamethasone. Crucially, Rg6 effectively preserved alveolar barrier integrity, restored tight junctions, and attenuated EMT-associated phenotypic shifts. Transcriptomic profiling identified the AGE-RAGE axis as the central upstream hub governing this structural protection. Comprehensive biophysical assays confirmed that Rg6 directly binds to and thermodynamically stabilizes the RAGE protein pocket. Mechanistically, Rg6 suppressed RAGE-mediated hyperactivation of the MAPK (p38, JNK) and NF-κB (p65) cascades, which serve as the central drivers for tight junction disassembly and EMT in epithelial cells. Furthermore, RAGE ablation in vitro and in vivo demonstrated that Rg6's capacity to preserve epithelial architecture is primarily RAGE-dependent.

CONCLUSIONS: Rg6 directly targets alveolar RAGE to inhibit the RAGE-MAPK/NF-κB signaling cascade. By suppressing this axis, Rg6 concurrently preserves alveolar barrier integrity and attenuates EMT-like transitions, actively restoring alveolar structural homeostasis and positioning it as a promising therapeutic candidate for COPD.

articles.title: Atractylenolide III alleviates MASLD by inhibiting lipid synthesis and apoptosis via PTEN.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as a major global health issue. This study aims to investigate the ameliorative effects of atractylenolide III (ATL III) on MASLD and its underlying molecular mechanisms, thereby providing theoretical basis and experimental support for the development of therapeutic drugs for MASLD.

METHODS: A high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mouse model and a combination of oleic acid and palmitic acid (PO)-induced lipid deposition model in AML-12 hepatocytes were established. The therapeutic effects of ATL III on hepatic lipid accumulation, injury, and inflammation were evaluated using biochemical assays, histopathological staining, immunofluorescence, Western blot (WB), and quantitative real-time PCR. Transcriptome sequencing was performed to screen for key targets, and molecular docking together with cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) were used to validate the potential binding between ATL III and the target protein. The findings were further verified using a liver-specific Pten knockdown mouse model.

RESULTS: In vivo experiments showed that ATL III significantly ameliorated hepatic lipid accumulation, injury, and inflammatory response in HFD feeding mice. In vitro experiments demonstrated that ATL III effectively reduced lipid accumulation in PO-induced AML-12 cells without affecting cell viability. Transcriptome sequencing and KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that the differentially expressed genes regulated by ATL III were enriched in the phosphatidylinositol 3‑kinase (PI3K)/serine/threonine protein kinase B (AKT), fatty acid metabolism, and apoptosis pathways. Further studies showed that ATL III engaged PTEN in a cellular context and upregulated its expression, thereby inhibiting excessive AKT activation. WB analysis confirmed that ATL III regulated lipid synthesis and apoptosis-related proteins via the PTEN/AKT axis. Notably, liver‑specific knockdown of Pten significantly attenuated the ameliorative effects of ATL III on the expression of the above molecules, as well as on liver injury and lipid accumulation.

CONCLUSIONS: ATL III ameliorates hepatic steatosis, injury, and inflammation in HFD-induced MASLD mice. Mechanistically, ATL III upregulates PTEN expression and suppresses excessive AKT activation, thereby reducing hepatic lipid synthesis and hepatocyte apoptosis. Liver-specific knockdown of Pten attenuates the protective effects of ATL III, confirming that PTEN is functionally required for its beneficial actions. These findings suggest that ATL III represents a potential therapeutic candidate for MASLD by acting through the PTEN/AKT pathway.

articles.title: Hydrogel-extracellular vesicle platforms: orchestrating the osteogenic microenvironment for cell-free bone regeneration.
articles.abstract: Bone defects remain difficult to treat because impaired vascularization, inflammation, infection and metabolic dysfunction limit endogenous repair. Unencapsulated extracellular vesicles (EVs) may also be rapidly cleared from defect sites. Hydrogel-EV systems combine vesicle bioactivity with local retention, controlled release and structural support, offering a cell-free strategy for bone regeneration. This review summarizes EV sources, separation, characterization and cargo, and outlines the endosomal biogenesis of exosomes. We examine EV-mediated regulation of osteogenesis, angiogenesis, immunity and osteoclast-mediated resorption. Hydrogel materials, EV-loading approaches, passive and stimuli-responsive release, and methods for evaluating EVs within hydrogels are discussed. Applications in uncomplicated, infected and diabetes-associated bone defects are compared according to their pathological microenvironments. Translational barriers include heterogeneous EV preparations, inconsistent separation and dosing standards, inadequate mechanical performance, and mismatched hydrogel degradation and bone-healing kinetics. Insufficient biodistribution and long-term safety data further limit clinical translation. This review provides a framework for developing hydrogel-EV platforms for bone regeneration.

articles.title: Qishen Yangxin Granule ameliorates cardiac function and ventricular remodeling in dilated cardiomyopathy by attenuating inflammation and myocardial fibrosis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Qishen Yangxin Granule (QSYX), a clinically utilized traditional Chinese medicinal formula, has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for cardiovascular diseases. However, its cardioprotective mechanism in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains incompletely defined.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of QSYX against DCM and the associated anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic mechanisms.

METHODS: Cardioprotective effects of QSYX were assessed both in vivo using a doxorubicin-induced DCM rat model and in vitro using rat cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with lipopolysaccharide. Evaluations included cardiac function, histopathological analysis, levels of inflammatory factors, and myocardial fibrosis markers. Single-cell RNA sequencing was employed to explore the potential mechanism of QSYX-mediated improvement in cardiac structure and function. Modulation of the toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway was examined via western blot, immunohistochemistry, confocal laser scanning microscope, and real-time reverse transcription-PCR. The specific p38 MAPK agonist LY188011 was used to verify the dependence of QSYX effect on the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

RESULTS: QSYX administration improved cardiac function in DCM rats, accompanied by significant attenuation of cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, apoptosis, inflammatory cell infiltration, and collagen deposition. Comparable protective effects were observed in lipopolysaccharide-treated cardiac fibroblasts. Mechanistically, QSYX suppressed lipopolysaccharide-induced upregulation of TLR4, p38 MAPK, and NF-κB p65 and downregulated the expression of inflammatory factors and myocardial fibrosis markers. Furthermore, intervention with LY188011 confirmed that the cardioprotective effects of QSYX are mediated through suppression of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

CONCLUSION: QSYX attenuates myocardial inflammation and fibrosis primarily through inhibition of the TLR4/p38 MAPK/NF-κB signaling pathway, thereby exerting cardioprotective effects against DCM-induced cardiac injury.

articles.title: A multifunctional Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide hydrogel loaded with propolis extract to promote oral mucosal repair.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract: Oral ulcer is a prevalent mucosal injury characterized by bacterial infection, oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation, while current therapies remain insufficient to comprehensively regulate the complex healing process. Herein, we developed a multifunctional bioactive hydrogel (DH@Pro) by incorporating propolis extract into a dynamic polysaccharide network composed of Dendrobium officinale polysaccharide and phenylboronic acid-grafted hyaluronic acid HA-PBA. The DH@Pro hydrogel exhibited excellent antioxidant, immunomodulatory, regenerative properties and promoted angiogenesis. In vivo studies using rat oral ulcer models demonstrated that DH@Pro exerted distinct effects throughout different healing phases to achieve comprehensive oral ulcer repair. Furthermore, its therapeutic efficacy in a full-thickness skin wound model highlighted its broader regenerative potential. This study presents a natural polysaccharide-based hydrogel strategy that integrates infection control, inflammation regulation, and regeneration promotion for comprehensive oral ulcer repair.

articles.title: Herbal bioactive compounds modulating ferroptosis and pyroptosis in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury: a systematic review of molecular basis, proposed crosstalk, and translational challenges.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI) remains a major cause of neonatal mortality and disability despite therapeutic hypothermia. Ferroptosis and pyroptosis are implicated in HIBI.

PURPOSE: To critically evaluate herbal bioactive compounds modulating ferroptosis- and pyroptosis-associated injury in neonatal HIBI.

STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review conducted and reported following PRISMA 2020.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through September 2026. Eligible studies used in vivo neonatal HIBI models, tested chemically defined plant-derived compounds, reported ferroptosis-related markers or evidence of pyroptotic execution beyond inflammasome activation, and assessed neuroprotective outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE.

RESULTS: Of 1441 records, 17 studies investigating 16 compounds met eligibility criteria. Nine examined ferroptosis and eight examined pyroptosis; glycyrrhizin was the only compound studied across both pathways, in separate studies. Included compounds spanned diverse structural classes and botanical sources. Studies reported reduced pathway-associated markers and improved brain-injury outcomes, but in vivo pathway dependency was demonstrated for only four compounds. No included study reported both ferroptosis-specific and pyroptosis-specific markers in the same neonatal HIBI model. Several risk-of-bias domains were predominantly rated unclear.

CONCLUSION: Preclinical studies suggest that herbal bioactives can modulate ferroptosis- and pyroptosis-associated processes in neonatal HIBI and warrant further evaluation as multi-target candidates. However, no study tested whether a single compound modulates both pathways within the same model. Future studies should apply pathway-specific manipulation alongside assessment of the second pathway in the same model and address developmental-stage specificity, therapeutic timing, model variability, brain availability, formulation barriers, and other pharmacological considerations.

articles.title: Adjunctive fucoidan, fucoxanthin, and l-carnitine mitigate albuminuria and preserve eGFR over a 12-week treatment period in diabetic kidney disease: A translational study and proof-of-concept randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Standard therapies for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) reduce albuminuria but trigger an acute eGFR decline, limiting clinical initiation. We evaluated whether a standardized marine formula comprising oligo-fucoidan, fucoxanthin, and l-carnitine (FFL) provides potential renoprotective effects with stable renal function.

METHODS: Preclinically, diabetic CKD mice received FFL for 8 weeks. Clinically, a 12-week randomized trial evaluated adjunctive FFL in DKD patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors (100%) and ACEIs/ARBs (85.5%). Efficacy was analyzed using baseline-adjusted robust ANCOVA (per-protocol, n = 55) and validated under intention-to-treat (ITT, n = 63) sensitivity analysis with Baseline Observation Carried Forward imputation.

RESULTS: Preclinically, FFL significantly attenuated renal dysfunction, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and inflammation. Clinically, baseline-adjusted robust ANCOVA showed that adjunctive FFL achieved a highly significant, adjusted 39.40% greater reduction in UACR compared to control (Geometric Mean Ratio [GMR] = 0.60; 95% CI: 0.40-0.90; p = 0.01), which was validated under ITT-ANCOVA sensitivity analysis (adjusted 32.18% greater UACR reduction; GMR = 0.67; 95% CI: 0.48-0.93; p = 0.01). Crucially, eGFR remained stable and preserved over 12 weeks (PP adjusted GMR = 1.01, p = 0.74; ITT adjusted GMR = 1.01, p = 0.78). FFL also significantly lowered baseline-adjusted LDL (GMR = 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95; p < 0.01) with a baseline-dependent response maximizing at a 24.28% reduction in patients with baseline dyslipidemia (p < 0.01), while displaying preliminary, exploratory glycemic signals. No serious adverse events or significant potassium elevations occurred.

CONCLUSION: Standardized marine FFL is a safe, well-tolerated adjunctive therapy that reduces albuminuria and dyslipidemia while preserving stable renal hemodynamics over 12 weeks.

articles.title: Macaque Area LIP Reflects Confidence-Dependent Changes in Decision Policy.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The process of forming a decision gives rise to an estimate of its quality or likelihood of success. This graded sense of confidence is important for guiding subsequent decisions, but a neural mechanism linking subjective confidence to formation of the next decision has not been identified. We trained two male rhesus macaques to report a perceptual choice and simultaneous confidence judgment in a reaction-time (RT) motion discrimination task. Monkeys were more likely to repeat a rewarded choice when they reported low confidence on the previous trial and showed greater changes in RT after a surprising outcome (low-confidence correct or high-confidence error). Neural activity in the lateral intraparietal area (LIP) encoded the previous trial's choice and confidence more strongly after a low-confidence correct trial, and the strength of history encoding was correlated with a trial-by-trial estimate of choice bias. Ramping dynamics of the decoded decision variable also depended systematically on the conjunction of confidence and reward on the previous trial, in a manner that reflected individual differences between animals. The findings suggest that LIP not only reflects the formation of the current decision but could participate in confidence-guided learning via adjustments of the subsequent decision process.

articles.title: Temporal Trends, Underuse, and Multilevel Factors Associated With Maximum-Dose Statin Therapy in Acute and Chronic Coronary Syndromes　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Study.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-intensity or maximally tolerated statin therapy has robust evidence for secondary prevention in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), and is strongly recommended in international guidelines. However, comprehensive real-world data on its use and associated factors remain limited.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Using data from the JROAD-DPC database (2017-2022), we analyzed ACS and CCS patients who underwent revascularization and were discharged alive. We assessed temporal trends in lipid-lowering therapy and examined associated factors, including patient demographics, comorbidities, treatment strategies, and hospital structural characteristics, using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression models. Among 358,570 patients with ACS and 392,821 with CCS, the use of maximum-dose statins increased from 8.6% in 2017 to 34.1% in 2022 in ACS and from 7.8% to 19.1% in CCS, but remained suboptimal. After multivariable adjustment, older age, underweight status, and coronary artery bypass grafting were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins in ACS. In CCS, older age, underweight status, and higher comorbidity burden were associated with lower use of maximum-dose statins. Hospital structural factors, including a higher number of cardiologists, were also associated with a greater use of maximum-dose statins.

CONCLUSIONS: Maximum-dose statin use among ACS and CCS patients remains suboptimal in Japan. Multilevel factors contribute to this evidence-practice gap, underscoring the need for comprehensive interventions at multiple levels to reduce disparities in care delivery.

articles.title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm2[GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.

articles.title: Renal Denervation to Enable Kidney Transplant Listing in Resistant Hypertension Patient on Hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is often poorly controlled in patients with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and evidence for renal denervation in this population remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 38-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis because of thrombotic microangiopathy who developed refractory hypertension with recurrent hypertensive emergencies despite 6 antihypertensive agents and aggressive ultrafiltration, precluding kidney transplant listing. After a thorough secondary hypertension work-up, he underwent off-label catheter-based bilateral renal denervation, after which his blood pressure improved substantially, hypertensive emergencies ceased, and he was subsequently added to the transplant waitlist.

CONCLUSION: Renal denervation may serve as adjunctive therapy to help dialysis patients with resistant hypertension reach transplant candidacy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Understand the limitations of pharmacologic and dialytic therapy for blood pressure control in dialysis-dependent patients. Appreciate how refractory hypertension may serve as a barrier to kidney transplant listing and how renal denervation may address it.

articles.title: 3,4-dehydro-3‑hydroxy-α-lapachone, a novel naphthoquinone, ameliorates hepatic fibrosis by targeting the guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(i) subunit alpha-2/peroxiredoxin 1 signaling axis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic fibrosis progresses to irreversible cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma without timely clinical intervention. Despite substantial clinical burden, no targeted therapies are currently approved specifically for hepatic fibrosis across the broad spectrum of chronic liver diseases, leaving a critical unmet need. Verbena officinalis L. has long been used in traditional medicine for hepatobiliary disorders, yet its active constituents, molecular targets, and mechanisms of antifibrotic action remain largely uncharacterized.

PURPOSE: This study was designed to identify novel anti-hepatic fibrosis components of Verbena officinalis and elucidate their underlying mechanisms of action.

METHODS: Therapeutic efficacy was assessed in bile duct ligation and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis mouse models. Bioactivity-guided fractionation coupled with high-content screening was applied to isolate active metabolites. Drug affinity responsive target stability identified candidate targets; direct binding was validated via surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assay, and molecular docking. Mechanisms were confirmed through integrated molecular and functional studies.

RESULTS: The ethyl acetate fraction exhibited the most potent anti-hepatic fibrotic activity, from which thirty-four metabolites, including two previously undescribed naphthoquinones (1 and 2) and one new dammarane-type triterpenoid (16), were isolated. Compound 1, identified as 3,4-dehydro-3‑hydroxy-α-lapachone (DH), demonstrated robust anti-fibrotic efficacy. Notably, DH at 10 mg/kg achieved in vivo efficacy comparable to the clinical agent pirfenidone at 200 mg/kg under the tested experimental conditions. Mechanistically, DH directly binds guanine nucleotide-binding protein G(i) subunit alpha-2 (GNAI2) at residues Phe171 and Leu250, suppressing the GNAI2-peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1) signaling axis to attenuate fibrogenesis. GNAI2 is consistently associated with fibrotic progression across multiple disease contexts and acts as an important functional mediator of hepatic stellate cell activation and hepatic fibrosis.

CONCLUSION: This work establishes DH as an anti-fibrotic agent with a rigorously validated protein target and binding mechanism, addressing a longstanding translational gap in phytochemical research. DH acts primarily through GNAI2-PRDX1 pathway inhibition. We acknowledge that DH possesses well-described redox-active properties and may therefore engage additional intracellular targets; accordingly, the GNAI2-PRDX1 axis represents the primary validated mediator rather than the exclusive mechanism of action. These findings establish GNAI2 as a novel therapeutic target and identify DH as a promising lead compound for the development of novel anti-fibrotic agents.

articles.title: A small molecule utilizes both antivirulence and host-directed mechanisms to combat bacterial infection.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance is progressively undermining the efficacy of conventional antibiotics, and intracellular infections caused by Salmonella typhimurium (ST) remain difficult to eradicate, underscoring the need for alternative therapeutic strategies.

PURPOSE: To identify natural small molecules possessing both antivirulence and host-directed activities against ST infection, and further characterize their mechanisms of action.

METHODS: A dual-screening strategy was employed to identify compounds that inhibit both ST invasion and intracellular replication. RNA sequencing, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, western blot analysis, β-galactosidase reporter assay, scanning electron microscopy, and flow cytometry were performed to investigate the mode of action of the active compound. A murine enterocolitis model was established to evaluate its therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: Ferulic acid (FA) emerged as a dual-acting inhibitor. FA suppressed SPI-4 promoter PsiiA activity, reduced SPI-4 transcription and SiiE secretion, and impaired SiiE-dependent adhesion, thereby limiting bacterial invasion. In parallel, FA suppressed macrophage STAT3 phosphorylation and enhanced NRF2 signaling, leading to reduced intracellular ferrous iron and ferroptosis, which in turn restricted intracellular bacterial replication. Furthermore, FA treatment alleviated ST-induced enterocolitis in mice.

CONCLUSIONS: FA protects against ST infection by attenuating bacterial virulence and modulating host iron homeostasis. These findings support its potential as a combined antivirulence and host-directed therapeutic candidate.

articles.title: PCCT and IVUS-NIRS for High-Risk Plaque Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk coronary plaque may be underrecognized in patients with atypical symptoms and negative biomarkers. Advanced coronary imaging can add anatomical and prognostic information.

CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman presented with acute chest pain, mild ischemic electrocardiographic changes, and negative high-sensitivity troponin. Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) showed a predominantly noncalcified, lipid-rich-appearing plaque in the left anterior descending artery despite a low risk profile. Angiography confirmed significant stenosis, and intravascular ultrasound with near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) demonstrated a high-risk plaque phenotype with maximum lipid core burden index over 4 mm of 347. Percutaneous coronary intervention used distal drug-coated balloon treatment and proximal-to-mid drug-eluting stent implantation. Postprocedural imaging confirmed adequate stent expansion and lower NIRS lipid signal.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the complementary role of PCCT and intravascular imaging for identifying and managing vulnerable coronary plaque.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: PCCT for noninvasive plaque characterization and intravascular ultrasound-NIRS for intraprocedural guidance provide a complementary strategy for personalized management of vulnerable coronary plaque.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Diabetes Status on Outcomes After Physiology-Guided Revascularization　- Insights From the J-PRIDE Registry.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of diabetes status on outcomes after physiology-guided revascularization remains unclear. This study evaluated clinical outcomes in patients with insulin-treated diabetes (ITD), non-ITD (NITD), and without diabetes after physiology-guided revascularization.

METHODS AND RESULTS: From the J-PRIDE registry, 3,140 patients were categorized into non-diabetes (n=1,797), NITD (n=1,133), and ITD (n=210) groups. The primary endpoint was the 1-year incidence of target vessel failure (TVF), a composite of cardiac death, target vessel-related myocardial infarction, and clinically driven target vessel revascularization. The 1-year TVF rate was significantly higher in the ITD and NITD groups than in the non-diabetes group (6.1% and 4.1% vs. 2.0%, respectively), with adjusted hazard ratios for the ITD and NTD groups of 2.14 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-4.19; P=0.027) and 1.63 (95 CI 1.02-2.61; P=0.041), respectively. The non-hyperemic pressure ratio cut-off predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) ≤0.80 was lower in the ITD than NITD and non-diabetes groups (0.87 vs. 0.89 and 0.90, respectively). The ITD group had the highest risk of TVF across all FFR values, followed by the NITD and non-diabetes groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with ITD and NITD exhibit worse clinical outcomes than those without diabetes. Notably, patients with ITD remained at elevated risk across the entire FFR spectrum, suggesting that physiological severity alone may not fully capture their residual cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Determinants and Clinical Impact of Direct Stenting in Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction　- An ATLAS-OCT Substudy.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct stenting (DS) is a simplified strategy for primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI); however, its role in the era of advanced intravascular imaging remains incompletely defined. We aimed to identify determinants of DS use and its impact on procedural efficiency and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-defined stent implantation quality in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

METHODS AND RESULTS: The ATLAS-OCT trial was a prospective multicenter nationwide study mandating OCT guidance in Japan. In this subanalysis, clinical characteristics, angiographic and OCT findings, procedural metrics, and clinical outcomes were compared between patients undergoing DS and those treated with balloon predilatation. Among 436 patients, DS was performed in 32.1% (n=140), with marked interinstitutional variability (0-68.3%; P<0.01), suggesting a strong influence of operator preference. DS use was not associated with angiographic features or OCT-defined culprit plaque morphology. DS significantly reduced contrast volume and procedure time. Post-PCI OCT showed a trend towards a larger minimum stent area and greater stent expansion index with DS. These benefits were not associated with in-hospital or 1-year outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary OCT-guided primary PCI for STEMI, DS appears to be driven primarily by operator preference rather than lesion characteristics. In this study, DS was associated with improved procedural efficiency without significantly compromising OCT-assessed stent implantation quality or mid-term clinical safety.

articles.title: Bayesian Real-Time Decision Support for Strategy Optimization in Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusion (CTO) is often prolonged, underscoring the need for timely strategy selection. Although several preprocedural scoring systems exist, they offer limited guidance regarding intraprocedural dynamics. This study aimed to develop a framework that updates success probabilities to support optimal strategy transitions during the procedure.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Two endpoints were defined: (1) successful crossing using antegrade wire escalation (AWE); and (2) time-constrained success using either AWE (<15 min) or advanced techniques (<60 min, intravascular ultrasound [IVUS] guided or retrograde). Preprocedural complexity scores (J-CTO, PROGRESS-CTO, CT-RECTOR) and procedural responses were sequentially incorporated into a Bayesian model to update real-time success probabilities. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation compared the procedural efficiency of advanced techniques. With an initial success probability of 50%, previous failure reduced the likelihood of AWE success to 26.5% and the time-based endpoint to 40.8%. Failure with intermediate-tip-load wires (~3 g) further decreased success probabilities to 6.1% for AWE and 30.5% for the time-based endpoint. When advanced strategies were required, IVUS-guided approaches showed a trend towards higher estimated procedural efficiency (76.6%) under feasibility-constrained conditions (mean difference: 3.0%; 95% credible interval: -5.6%, 11.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: A real-time Bayesian framework enables dynamic adaptation during CTO PCI and may help identify scenarios where earlier transition to advanced techniques is warranted based on evolving procedural information.

articles.title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste.
articles.abstract: Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800-5050 nm and width: 780-970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst's analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

articles.title: Wide Dynamic Range of Contrast-Encoding in Neural Responses in Macaque V1.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: The dynamic range of contrast-encoding in the early visual system has been investigated at both single-neuron and population levels in animals using oriented stimuli such as gratings and Gabor patches. However, contrast-encoding of unoriented stimuli such as Gaussians has been less explored, even though such stimuli can evoke a large population response. In studies that employ Gaussians, contrast response functions of neurons and neural populations in the primary visual cortex are typically characterized across a limited range of Weber contrasts up to 100%, which may not adequately reflect the statistics of contrast in natural scenes. Indeed, our preliminary analysis shows that locations with center-surround contrasts far exceeding the level comparable to a Gaussian stimulus of 100% Weber contrast are ubiquitous in natural scenes. Thus, our current understanding of contrast-encoding remains incomplete in the context of natural environments. Here, we measured spiking activities of individual neurons using electrophysiology and population responses using widefield calcium imaging in V1 of fixating male macaques (Macaca mulatta), while Gaussian stimuli were presented over a wide range of Weber contrasts, up to 900%. Both the average spiking response and the average population response continued to increase robustly above 100% Weber contrast. Only a small minority of neurons saturated below 100% Weber contrast. These results demonstrate that the dynamic range of contrast-encoding in V1 is broader than previously assumed and aligns more closely with the statistics of contrast in natural scenes.

articles.title: High Lipoprotein(a) Is a Predictor of Adverse Events and Heart Failure in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is a well-established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but its prognostic role after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. This study investigated the association between Lp(a) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), in patients with AMI.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 1,235 patients with AMI from the NARA-MI registry who underwent emergency percutaneous coronary intervention and had serum Lp(a) measured at admission. Based on receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, patients were categorized into high (≥24 mg/dL) and low (<24 mg/dL) Lp(a) groups. The primary endpoint was MACE, defined as all-cause death, recurrent AMI, HF hospitalization, or unplanned coronary revascularization. During a median follow-up of 3.6 years, 497 MACE events occurred. The incidence of MACE (48.0% vs. 38.3%; P=0.004) and HF hospitalization (9.3% vs. 5.0%; P=0.008) was significantly higher in the high Lp(a) group. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, high-Lp(a) independently predicted MACE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-1.73; P=0.001) and HF hospitalization (HR 1.87; 95% CI 1.15-3.04; P=0.016). Among patients with HF, 39.7% were classified as HFpEF.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) is independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes after AMI, particularly HF. Measurement of Lp(a) may improve risk stratification after AMI and help identify patients at high risk of developing HF, including HFpEF.

articles.title: Pathogenic Variants in NKX2-5 Associated With Familial Atrial Septal Defect and Conduction System Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most atrial septal defects (ASDs) occur sporadically, but familial cases can occur and carry a 10% risk of transmission to offspring.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 3-generation family with autosomal dominant secundum ASD and conduction system disease related to a novel NKX2-5 variant (c.300del; p.Asp101Thrfs∗75). The index patient, a 58-year-old woman with prior ASD repair and mitral valve replacement, presented with chronotropic incompetence, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and prolonged pauses, leading to pacemaker implantation. Her mother had an ASD, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The proband's daughter also had an ASD. Genetic testing revealed a novel NKX2-5 pathogenic variant in all 3 patients.

REVIEW SUMMARY: The combination of an ASD and conduction system disease represents the most common phenotype in patients with pathogenic NKX2-5 variants.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: A thorough family history and genetic testing are needed when evaluating patients with ASD and concurrent conduction system abnormalities.

articles.title: Validation of an Electronic Health Record Model for Unplanned Readmission in Patients With Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk scores aim to predict 30-day heart failure (HF) readmissions.

PROJECT RATIONALE: Current models, including Epic's Risk of Unplanned Readmission for a 30-Day Event, demonstrate modest to moderate discriminatory ability (area under the curve: 0.59-0.72).

PROJECT SUMMARY: The goals of this study were to create an electronic health record (EHR)-automatable 30-day HF readmission risk calculator; to test the accuracy of Epic's model to predict 30-day HF readmission risk; and to compare the 2 models. To derive our EHR-automatable model using machine learning, we first performed a systematic review of 30-day HF risk prediction models. We then compared the predictive capabilities of the Epic model with our model. The Epic model had a C-statistic of 0.74, and the derived EHR risk score had a C-statistic of 0.76 (P = 0.41), suggesting comparable performance.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Risk scores are fundamental for personalization of care to accelerate resources for those who need them most. Although both models had moderate discrimination in predicting 30-day HF readmission, the independently derived model provides a platform for future enhancement, such as the inclusion of electrocardiogram-based artificial intelligence diagnostics.

articles.title: First-in-Human Permanent Totally Leadless Left Ventricular Septal Endocardial Pacing With Atrioventricular Synchrony.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless cardiac resynchronization combining WiSE system ultrasound-mediated left ventricular pacing with leadless right ventricular pacing has been reported. However, atrioventricular-sequential left ventricular pacing triggered by atrial leadless pacing impulse without right ventricular pacing has not been reported.

FIRST-IN-HUMAN/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: An 86-year-old man with complete heart block and cardiomyopathy received a dual-chamber leadless pacemaker (AVEIR DR) with WiSE left ventricular endocardial electrode on the septal wall. A novel "sync-to-pace" delay configuration enabled the atrial pacing impulse to trigger left ventricular stimulation, achieving a QRS duration of 142 ms.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates proof of concept for a fully leadless atrioventricular-synchronized system capable of delivering left ventricular septal endocardial pacing without right ventricular pacing dependency, offering a physiological pacing strategy for selected patients.

NOVELTY: First-in-human demonstration of an ultrasound-mediated left ventricular endocardial electrode triggered by an atrial leadless pacing impulse to deliver atrioventricular-sequential left ventricular septal stimulation without right ventricular pacing.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This novel totally leadless architecture is a proof of concept for a more physiological pacing option for pacing-dependent patients while avoiding transvenous lead-related complications.

articles.title: Late Progressive Multivalvular Regurgitation After Heart Transplantation With Preserved Graft Function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Late clinical decline after heart transplantation is commonly attributed to rejection, cardiac allograft vasculopathy, or ventricular dysfunction. Progressive structural valvular disease is less frequently emphasized when graft systolic function is preserved.
