CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman underwent orthotopic heart transplantation at age 13 for familial restrictive cardiomyopathy. Nearly 10 years later, she developed progressive exertional fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and dizziness despite preserved graft systolic function and no significant cardiac allograft vasculopathy. Serial imaging demonstrated severe mitral regurgitation, moderate to severe aortic regurgitation, and moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation. She underwent redo sternotomy with bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement and tricuspid repair, with preserved ventricular function and clinical recovery at early follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights progressive multivalvular disease as an important valve-level cause of late clinical decline after heart transplantation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider structural valvular disease in symptomatic long-term heart transplant recipients with preserved graft function.

articles.title: Argatroban Anticoagulation for Transcarotid TAVR Under Conscious Sedation in a Patient With Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe argatroban anticoagulation in a patient with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve replacement under conscious sedation.

KEY STEPS: Vitamin K antagonist therapy was discontinued and intravenous argatroban initiated, with anti-factor IIa monitoring. Procedural anticoagulation consisted of an argatroban bolus followed by continuous infusion guided by activated clotting time. An ultrasound-guided intermediate cervical plexus block with remifentanil sedation maintained consciousness for neurological assessment. Argatroban was resumed postoperatively before transition to vitamin K antagonist therapy.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Surgical carotid access under argatroban requires careful balancing of thrombotic and bleeding risks. Maintaining consciousness for neurological monitoring adds an anesthetic challenge, requiring adequate anesthesia for carotid exposure while avoiding excessive sedation; an intermediate cervical plexus block may cause dysphagia.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Integrating argatroban anticoagulation with locoregional anesthesia may address the competing requirements of surgical carotid access and continuous neurological monitoring in patients with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia undergoing transcarotid transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Advanced Heart Failure and Ventricular Dysfunction: An Evolving Heart Team Strategy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction and mitral regurgitation are underrepresented in pivotal transcatheter edge-to-edge repair trials and are often ineligible for transplantation or LV assist devices, leaving limited options when guideline-directed medical therapy fails.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe 6 patients aged 38 to 82 years with LV ejection fraction 10% to 20% and severe (4+) to torrential (5+) mitral regurgitation, 4 patients presenting in or near cardiogenic shock requiring inotropic, vasopressor, or intra-aortic balloon pump support. All underwent transcatheter edge-to-edge repair as our multidisciplinary heart team strategy evolved.

DISCUSSION: With increasing experience, the heart team incorporated individualized pharmacologic or temporary mechanical support, preprocedural hemodynamic optimization, and anatomy-driven device selection. One patient initially referred for palliative care was subsequently reassessed and treated. This series illustrates how iterative multidisciplinary learning may expand transcatheter edge-to-edge repair candidacy in carefully selected, high-risk patients with advanced heart failure and profound ventricular dysfunction and limited therapeutic alternatives.

articles.title: Severe Bioprosthetic Mitral Valve Dysfunction: Multimodality Imaging Identifies Structural Valve Degeneration and Guides Valve-in-Valve TMVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe bioprosthetic valve dysfunction presents a diagnostic challenge because distinguishing reversible leaflet thrombosis from structural valve degeneration may not be possible using echocardiography alone.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with end-stage renal disease, previous bioprosthetic mitral and aortic valve replacement, and prior valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement presented with heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Multimodality imaging demonstrated severe bioprosthetic mitral valve dysfunction with restricted leaflet motion, raising suspicion for leaflet thrombosis. Empiric intravenous unfractionated heparin was commenced while cardiac computed tomography was arranged. Computed tomography excluded hypoattenuated leaflet thickening and demonstrated severe leaflet calcification, confirming structural valve degeneration. After heart team discussion, transseptal valve-in-valve mitral replacement resulted in rapid hemodynamic and clinical recovery.

DISCUSSION: Serial multimodality imaging guided escalation from anticoagulation to definitive valve intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent prosthetic valve dysfunction after anticoagulation should prompt reassessment for structural valve degeneration. Transseptal valve-in-valve transcatheter mitral valve replacement is an effective treatment for selected high-surgical-risk patients.

articles.title: Valve-in-Root TAVI vs Redo Surgery in a Young Adult With Failed Bioprosthesis.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC OF CONTROVERSY: Whether valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) or redo surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) is preferred for structural valve degeneration of a Freestyle stentless aortic root in a young adult, and whether a Ross procedure at index surgery would have better served lifetime management.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with a failed stentless aortic root (implanted at age 20 for bicuspid aortic valve regurgitation) presented with severe bioprosthetic regurgitation and ventricular dilatation. Transfemoral ViV TAVI with a 29-mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 Ultra Resilia was performed successfully.

PRO VIEWPOINT: ViV TAVI avoids redo sternotomy, preserves future options, and aligns with patient preference to avoid anticoagulation.

CON VIEWPOINT: Redo SAVR with a mechanical valve-and a Ross procedure at the index operation-may offer superior lifetime sequencing, avoiding constraints of successive transcatheter implants.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Lifetime planning must begin at the index operation; both ViV TAVI and redo SAVR require heart team deliberation with explicit consideration of all future interventions.

articles.title: Iliofemoral Venous Stenosis Complicating Large-Bore Access for Balloon Mitral Valvotomy, Unmasking Incidental May-Thurner Anatomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-bore transvenous access for balloon mitral valvotomy (BMV) can be complicated by unrecognized iliofemoral venous disease, occasionally unmasking a congenital variant.

CASE SUMMARY: A 51-year-old woman with rheumatic mitral stenosis and NYHA functional class III-IV dyspnea, on acenocoumarol for atrial fibrillation, was scheduled for BMV. After right femoral venous access and transseptal puncture, hardware >8-F could not be advanced; venography showed a tight, recoiling right external iliac vein stenosis, not responding to intravenous nitroglycerine, treated with angioplasty and stenting, and BMV was deferred. Computed tomography venogram 14 days later confirmed stent patency and incidentally revealed left common iliac vein compression by the right common iliac artery, consistent with asymptomatic May-Thurner anatomy rather than syndrome. Acenocoumarol was continued after stenting, held 3 days before reattempt, and BMV was then completed successfully via the same route.

DISCUSSION: Comprehensive venous evaluation during difficult large-bore access can uncover clinically silent iliocaval anatomic variants and guide individualized, staged management.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into the therapeutic effects of Mongolian medicine Eligengurigumu-7 against non-alcoholic fatty liver disease via the PPAR signalling pathway.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)， is characterised by a complex, multi-stage pathogenesis and progression and imposes a substantial economic burden on global public health. Thus, an urgent need exists to improve the understanding of NAFLD-related hepatic disease progression and identify effective therapeutic strategies. Eligengurigumu-7 (GRGM-7) is a common treatment prescription for liver diseases in Mongolian medicine. However, its pharmacodynamics and mechanism of action remain largely unclear.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the hepatoprotective efficacy of GRGM-7 against NAFLD, identify its bioactive constituents absorbed into the bloodstream, and elucidate its key molecular targets and underlying regulatory pathways.

METHODS: The key differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and pathways during the progression of NAFLD-related hepatic diseases were identified through bioinformatics analysis and immunofluorescence validation of clinical samples. NAFLD mouse models induced with either a high-fat diet (HFD) or a methionine- and choline-deficient diet (MCD) were established. The therapeutic effects of GRGM-7 against NAFLD were evaluated in these models by comparing the physiological, biochemical, and pathological indicators of the control groups, model groups, and each dose treatment group. Through RNA-sequencing and non-targeted metabolomics analysis and the combined analysis of multi-source datasets, the key pharmacodynamic targets, regulatory function directions, and regulatory pathways of GRGM-7 involved in improving NAFLD were identified and verified through reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blotting (WB) experiments. The chemical components of GRGM-7 were identified using ultra performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS), and the compounds absorbed into the bloodstream (CABs) were identified and analysed based on the principles of serum pharmacochemistry. CABs were quantitatively analysed in the original herbal formulation through high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and molecular docking was used to analyse the interaction between the CABs and active targets. The hepatoprotective effects of CABs and GRGM-7, as well as their effects on the targets were confirmed in an in vitro NAFLD model of oleic acid-induced AML-12 cells. Additionally, PPARγ and ACLY were subjected to siRNA-mediated silencing, and fenofibrate was used as a pharmacological agonist of PPARα to further functionally validate the involvement of the PPAR signaling pathway and ACLY in the effects of GRGM-7.

RESULTS: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) signalling was a crucial pathway involved in NAFLD-related hepatic disease progression. GRGM-7 administration ameliorated MCD- and HFD-induced NAFLD in mice and protected the liver by regulating the PPAR signalling pathway, promoting fatty acid metabolism, and maintaining liver lipid homeostasis. ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) served as a key candidate target associated with the progression of NAFLD and therapeutic action of GRGM-7. GRGM-7 contained several chemical components that were absorbed into the bloodstream. Among these CABs, cosmosiin exhibited a high affinity for key DEGs and crucial targets within signalling pathways. Moreover, cosmosiin showed a favourable hepatoprotective effect on the NAFLD cell model induced in vitro. GRGM-7 exhibited the strongest hepatoprotective effect in vitro, accompanied by modulation of the PPAR signalling pathway. Silencing of ACLY or PPARγ alleviated metabolic abnormalities, whereas subsequent GRGM-7 treatment produced further improvements. Fenofibrate treatment similarly ameliorated the OA-induced metabolic abnormalities, whereas combined treatment with fenofibrate and GRGM-7 further enhanced these effects, supporting the involvement of the PPAR signalling pathway and ACLY in the metabolic effects of GRGM-7.

CONCLUSION: PPAR signalling was the key pathway involved in the progression of NAFLD-related hepatic diseases, and ACLY was one of the key potential targets. GRGM-7 regulated the PPAR signalling pathway by modulating fatty acid metabolism, thereby exerting a hepatoprotective effect. These findings highlight the potential utility of GRGM-7 as a therapeutic agent for NAFLD.

articles.title: Direct SVC Access for Valve Replacement With Percutaneous Venotomy Suture System Hemostasis: A Way In.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult patients with congenital heart disease often have limited vascular access due to previous procedures and anatomic variations.

CASE SUMMARY: This case describes how a percutaneously placed venotomy suture system allowed for direct percutaneous superior vena cava access for delivery sheath insertion for transcatheter pulmonary valve replacement. This system allowed for a novel access approach and the achievement of hemostasis in an otherwise noncompressible site.

DISCUSSION: The availability of percutaneously placed venotomy suture placement systems allows for a more daring approach to noncompressible sites within the mediastinum and has the potential to be applied to allow large-bore closed chest access to other mediastinal structures.

articles.title: FOLFOX-Associated Ventricular Fibrillation Arrest in a Patient With Colon Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity is uncommon but may cause life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man with stage IIIB colon cancer developed chest discomfort and out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest approximately 72 hours after his first folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil (5-FU), and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) cycle. Electrocardiography showed anterior ST-segment elevations, but coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive left and right coronary arteries. Echocardiography showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 30%, which improved to approximately 50% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging without myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement. FOLFOX was discontinued, guideline-directed medical therapy was initiated, and an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for secondary prevention.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights a rare, severe presentation of fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity after the first treatment cycle despite no prior cardiac history.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ventricular fibrillation may occur early during FOLFOX therapy. Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management are essential.

articles.title: Therapeutic efficacy and dosing regimen evidence synthesis of Ursolic Acid for liver injury: A preclinical systematic review with machine learning.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ursolic acid (UA), a pentacyclic triterpene, shows hepatoprotective efficacy and favorable safety in various animal models of liver injury. However, robust preclinical evidence remains scarce.

PURPOSE: To synthesize the preclinical evidence for UA and explore how UA dose and treatment duration are associated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT) improvement in animal models of liver injury.

STUDY DESIGN: This preclinical systematic review integrating meta-analysis and machine learning followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA).

METHODS: Relevant preclinical studies through April 11, 2026 were systematically retrieved from PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, OVID, CNKI and Wanfang. Machine learning analyses were used to identify factors associated with ALT improvement, particularly human equivalent dose (HED) and treatment duration.

RESULTS: Forty-seven articles were included in this analysis. UA markedly improved histopathological parameters, liver function, biochemical parameters, serum lipid levels, oxidative stress indicators, and inflammatory markers in liver injury animal models. Random forest was selected as the final predictive model. The analysis further identified model administration route, treatment duration, HED, and time of administration as key determinants for the improvement rate of ALT. An exploratory HED range of approximately 5-7 mg/kg was associated with greater predicted ALT improvement.

CONCLUSION: The study indicates that UA exerts hepatoprotective effects in animal models of liver injury. Potential mechanisms include modulation of the gut-liver axis, attenuation of hepatic and systemic oxidative stress, and suppression of inflammation and fibrosis. Given the exploratory nature of these preclinical findings, the translational potential of UA warrants further rigorous validation.

articles.title: Antitumor potential of medicinal plants from the Brazilian Cerrado: a systematic review of experimental studies.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Brazilian Cerrado harbors 12,180 cataloged angiosperm species; 7395 (60.7%) are endemic to Brazil, and its flora has been used in traditional medicine for generations. Regardless, the antitumor potential of these species has been investigated in a fragmented manner.

PURPOSE: To compile and analyze experimental evidence on the antitumor effects of preparations derived from Cerrado plant species in vitro and in vivo models.

METHODS: Searches were conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Scopus, without date restrictions and limited to publications in English. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using an adapted risk-of-bias assessment tool.

RESULTS: Sixty-two studies were included; 55 employed in vitro models and 12 employed in vivo models, five of which combined both approaches. The studies encompassed a broad range of malignancies, including melanoma, leukemias, glioblastoma, and breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers, and evaluated crude extracts, fractions, and isolated compounds from >40 species. The most frequently documented antitumor effects were cell viability reduction, apoptosis induction via the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, cell cycle arrest, and matrix metalloproteinase inhibition. Annona crassiflora, Campomanesia adamantium, Stryphnodendron adstringens, and Tapirira guianensis were each reported in three or more independent studies (most frequently investigated species). Relevant methodological limitations, including a widespread absence of tumor selectivity data, pharmacokinetic profiles, and experimental blinding, were revealed. No clinical trials evaluating Cerrado plant species as oncological interventions were identified.

CONCLUSION: The Cerrado flora represents a relevant source of compounds with preclinical antitumor activity, but essential translational data remain absent.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO database (CRD420261372222). Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261372222.

articles.title: Aspirin eugenol ester attenuates alcoholic liver injury via the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway-mediated ferroptosis suppression.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcoholic liver injury (ALI) is a prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and represents a major public health burden. Previous pharmacological and pharmacodynamic studies have indicated that aspirin eugenol ester (AEE) exerts multiple pharmacological activities, including protective effects against non-alcoholic fatty liver disease. However, whether AEE can ameliorate ALI and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

PURPOSE: This study sought to explore the protective effects of AEE on ALI and to delineate the associated molecular mechanisms.

METHODS: This study investigated the protective effects of AEE against ALI using both in vitro and in vivo models, with a particular focus on elucidating its molecular mechanisms.

RESULTS: In cellular models, AEE significantly alleviated ethanol- and erastin-induced cytotoxicity and morphological damage, while markedly reversing abnormalities in superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, Fe2+ accumulation, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, 4-Hydroxynonenal levels and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, AEE attenuated ethanol-induced ferroptosis by activating the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 antioxidant axis. This result was validated in primary mouse hepatocytes. In animal models, AEE markedly improved alcohol-induced metabolic disturbances, including dyslipidemia, glucose disorders, and hepatic steatosis, while restoring hepatic redox homeostasis and ethanol metabolism through upregulation of alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) and suppression of CYP2E1. Consistently, AEE enhanced NRF2 signaling and ferroptosis resistance in liver tissues, as evidenced by increased expression of SLC7A11, GPX4, ferritin, and HO-1, along with reduced expression of BAP1, Keap1 and P53.

CONCLUSIONS: AEE exerts a potent protective effect against ALI by attenuating ethanol-induced ferroptosis via activation of the NRF2/SLC7A11/GPX4 signaling pathway, thereby improving hepatic metabolic homeostasis.

articles.title: Diabetic cataract at type 1 diabetes onset: frequency and characteristics.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric diabetic cataract is a rare acute complication of diabetes mellitus and may result in permanent visual impairment. Reported prevalences range from 0.25 % to 3.4 %, while data from Germany remain limited. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and clinical characteristics of cataract in children with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes at a German tertiary medical center.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated children and adolescents admitted to the Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, University Medical Center Ulm, with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes between January 2008 and February 2024 who underwent ophthalmologic screening at the Department of Ophthalmology of the same center. A final cohort of 141 patients was analyzed.

RESULTS: Cataract was diagnosed in 6 of 141 patients, corresponding to 4.3 % of the ophthalmologically examined cohort. The median age of patients with cataract was 12.4 years. Mean HbA1c was significantly higher in patients with cataract than in those without cataract (15.8 % vs. 12.4 %; p<0.05). Visual acuity was significantly lower in patients with cataract than in those without cataract (0.19 vs. 0.03 logMAR; p<0.05). The predominant morphology was snowflake-like posterior subcapsular cataract. Retinal findings were normal in all patients, irrespective of cataract status.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center cohort of screened children with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes, cataract was detected more frequently in our ophthalmologically examined cohort than previously reported. Pediatric diabetic cataract may be underdiagnosed at diabetes onset. Initial ophthalmologic evaluation in children and adolescents with new-onset type 1 diabetes should, therefore, include slit-lamp examination, especially in patients with visual symptoms or markers of prolonged hyperglycemia.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair of Mitral Valve Leaflet Perforation Guided by 3D Multiplanar Reconstruction Imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve leaflet perforation is generally considered unsuitable anatomy for transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER), with published experience largely limited to bailout treatment of iatrogenic perforations.

CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man with severe symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR) was referred for TEER. Intraprocedural transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) unexpectedly revealed a large posterior mitral leaflet perforation. Guided by 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging, 2 XTW MitraClip devices were deployed on both sides of the perforation, effectively "sandwiching" the defect between the clips and reducing MR from severe to mild.

DISCUSSION: This case supports the feasibility of MitraClip as a primary treatment for mitral leaflet perforation in carefully selected patients. TEE with 3D multiplanar reconstruction imaging enabled accurate anatomic characterization and facilitated precise device positioning, resulting in an excellent procedural outcome.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Mitral valve leaflet perforation may be amenable to TEER in select cases. 3D TEE imaging is critical for procedural planning and helps to facilitate precise device positioning.

articles.title: Refractory Ventricular Tachycardia-Induced Severe Cardiomyopathy in a Child: Successful Radiofrequency Ablation With ECMO Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular tachycardia (VT)-induced cardiac dysfunction is a recognized but uncommon cause of cardiomyopathy in children.

CASE SUMMARY: A 7-year-old girl presented with severely depressed left ventricular function and incessant VT that was refractory to multiple antiarrhythmics and attempted cardioversions. Because of hemodynamic instability, the patient required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support and ultimately radiofrequency ablation of a focal VT that was localized to the right midventricular septum near the moderator band. The patient had a subsequent return of normal biventricular function.

DISCUSSION: Focal VT causing severe dysfunction, unresponsive to both medical therapy and cardioversion, originating from the moderator band of the right ventricle, requiring ECMO support and radiofrequency ablation is extremely rare in the pediatric population, with few reports in the literature.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: High-risk radiofrequency ablation of unusual focal VT originating from the right ventricular midventricular septum during ECMO may be accomplished with excellent clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The Longest Documented LVAD Survival: 22 Years of Durable Mechanical Circulatory Support.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Durable mechanical circulatory support has allowed patients prolonged survival with mitigation of myriad complications. As survivorship extends beyond a decade, driveline integrity and device management present complex clinical challenges.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a 73-year-old man who, to our knowledge, had the longest period of durable mechanical support at 22 years and 10 months across 3 ventricular assist devices.

DISCUSSION: Advancements in left ventricular assist device technology have continued to improve patient outcomes and can sustain meaningful quality of life over 2 decades in carefully selected patients with the support of a multidisciplinary team.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Well-selected patients can be supported with durable mechanical support for over 2 decades with the guidance of a multidisciplinary team. Evaluation of driveline malfunctions in collaboration with the manufacturer is critical for timely intervention.

articles.title: Polypharmacological targeting of atopic dermatitis by natural products: A mechanism-driven systematic review.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atopic dermatitis (AD) involves interconnected disturbances in epidermal barrier function, immune regulation, microbial homeostasis, and neuroimmune itch. Natural products influence several of these processes, but their mechanistic and clinical evidence remains fragmented.

PURPOSE: To assess natural product-based interventions for AD within a polypharmacological framework and identify priorities for clinical translation.

STUDY DESIGN: Mechanism-driven systematic review with qualitative narrative synthesis.

METHODS: PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to March 2026. Eligible studies evaluated isolated natural compounds, characterized extracts or formulations, natural lipids, or microbe-derived interventions in patients with AD or validated experimental models. Evidence was synthesized by chemotype, pathological axis, molecular target or pathway, study design, and translational relevance.

RESULTS: A total of 156 original studies were retained. Reported effects clustered around epidermal differentiation and lipid homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, host-microbial interactions, and pruriceptive pathways. Preclinical studies provided mechanistic evidence for barrier-restorative, immunomodulatory, microbiome-related, and antipruritic effects involving multiple pathways. Clinical studies reported improvements in disease severity, barrier-related measures, pruritus, and quality of life, although findings varied across interventions and study designs. Direct target engagement, exposure-response relationships, and contributions of individual constituents in multicomponent preparations remained incompletely resolved.

CONCLUSION: Natural products provide a pharmacologically diverse basis for intervention across interconnected AD pathways. Current evidence supports therapeutic potential and multitarget activity, although polypharmacological synergy, comparative efficacy, and long-term safety require further validation. Clinical translation requires reproducible product characterization, direct mechanistic validation, pharmacokinetic assessment, human-relevant models, and well-designed clinical studies.

articles.title: Multi-omics integrated analysis reveals the therapeutic mechanism of 919 formula in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and is driven by metabolic stress-induced inflammation. Emerging evidence implicates cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells as key contributors to the progression of MASLD. However, therapeutic strategies specifically targeting pathogenic CD8⁺ T cell responses in MASLD are still scarce. The clinical efficacy of the 919 formula in MASLD has been demonstrated, yet its cellular targets and molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: Single-cell transcriptomics profiled peripheral blood immune composition in 919 formula treated MASLD patients, and UPLC-QE-MS characterized bioactive constituents of the 919 formula. Efficacy and immune mechanisms were tested in HFD/MCD mouse models (AST/ALT and histology) and CD8⁺ T cell adoptive transfer. CD8⁺ T cells treated with control or 919 formula-containing serum were analyzed by flow cytometry, Seahorse assays, transcriptomics, immunoblotting, and molecular docking.

RESULTS: Single-cell transcriptomic profiling showed that 919 formula treatment was associated with a selective reduction in circulating CD8⁺ GZMB⁺ T cells and an attenuation of CD8⁺ T-cell activation in patients with MASLD. In both HFD- and MCD-induced mouse models, the 919 formula markedly alleviated hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, which was accompanied by a decreased proportion of CD8⁺ GZMB⁺ T cells, reflecting reduced CD8⁺ T-cell activation. Furthermore, adoptive transfer experiments demonstrated that CD8⁺ T cells treated with 919 formula-containing serum were sufficient to confer protection against MCD-induced liver injury. Mechanistically, 919 formula treatment was associated with reduced PKM2-dependent glycolysis and STAT5 phosphorylation in CD8⁺ T cells, while pharmacological activation of PKM2 partially reversed these effects. Finally, Schizandrin C was identified as a representative bioactive component of the 919 formula. Molecular docking and SPR analyses supported its direct interaction with PKM2, while functional assays demonstrated its capacity to suppress CD8⁺ T-cell activation.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings suggest that the 919 formula alleviates MASLD, at least in part, by attenuating pathological CD8⁺ T-cell activation and cytotoxicity, with PKM2-STAT5 signaling potentially contributing to this effect. Schizandrin C may contribute to the therapeutic effects of the 919 formula, although the overall efficacy of this complex herbal formulation is likely to involve coordinated actions of multiple bioactive constituents.

articles.title: Cinnamaldehyde protects against early diabetic retinopathy: an integrative In vivo and computational study.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision impairment, and current treatments are limited to advanced stages. Cinnamaldehyde (CA), the primary bioactive constituent of cinnamon, has demonstrated anti-apoptotic and anti-diabetic properties, but its role and mechanism in early DR remain unexplored. This study investigated whether CA protects against early DR and whether the effect is associated with phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (AKT) pathway activation.

PURPOSE: This study investigated whether CA exerts anti‑apoptotic effects in early DR and whether these effects are associated with PI3K/AKT pathway phosphorylation. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET prediction were employed as hypothesis‑generating and supportive computational tools to predict potential key targets, validate binding stability, and assess drug‑likeness.

METHODS: Diabetes was induced in rats by streptozotocin. After 8 weeks of hyperglycemia, diabetic rats received daily oral CA (100 mg/kg) or vehicle until week 20. Retinal morphology and apoptosis were assessed by H&E and TUNEL staining. Expression of PI3K/AKT pathway components and apoptosis‑related markers was analyzed by immunohistochemistry, RT‑qPCR and Western blot. Network pharmacology was used to predict CA targets and DR‑related genes, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment. Molecular docking was performed on 10 targets (Bcl‑2, Bax, XIAP, CASP3, IL6, ERBB2, TNF‑α, EGFR, BDNF, AKT2), with subsequent 100‑ns molecular dynamics simulations and MM‑GBSA binding free energy calculations for four key targets (ERBB2, AKT2, Bcl‑2, TNF‑α). ADMET properties were predicted using ADMETlab 3.0.

RESULTS: CA did not lower blood glucose or prevent weight loss in diabetic rats (p > 0.05 vs. diabetic controls). However, CA was associated with ameliorated retinal histological changes and a reduction in TUNEL-positive cells in the ganglion cell layer (from 37.33 ± 7.09% to 18.67 ± 2.25%, p < 0.05). CA treatment was associated with upregulation of Bcl-2 and XIAP and downregulation of Bax and Caspase-3 at both protein and mRNA levels (all p < 0.05), and with increased PI3K/AKT phosphorylation (p < 0.05) without altering total PI3K or AKT. Re-analysis of animal-level densitometry showed that p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT in the D group were 27.1% and 32.5% of N levels, respectively, and that CA treatment increased these ratios to 213.5% and 227.2% of D levels. Network pharmacology predicted 77 common targets between CA and DR, with PI3K‑AKT among the top enriched pathways. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding of CA to ERBB2 (-6.275 kcal/mol), AKT2 (-5.678 kcal/mol), EGFR (-5.712 kcal/mol), TNF‑α (-5.560 kcal/mol), and Bcl‑2 (-5.503 kcal/mol). Single-trajectory 100-ns MD simulations were consistent with retention of CA in the AKT2 and ERBB2 binding pockets, with protein-aligned ligand displacements of ∼4-5 Å, whereas the ligand left its initial binding site in the Bcl-2 and TNF-α trajectories. ADMET prediction was consistent with favorable oral bioavailability, Caco-2 permeability, and predicted BBB permeability, but does not establish blood-retinal barrier penetration.

CONCLUSION: CA treatment was associated with amelioration of retinal histological changes and a reduction in TUNEL-positive cells in the GCL under persistent hyperglycemia, without a detected improvement in fasting glucose. The observed changes were associated with PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and modulation of apoptotic regulators. Computational analyses provide exploratory, hypothesis-generating evidence. The correlational nature of the PI3K/AKT findings, the absence of causal pathway intervention, and the exploratory nature of the computational predictions should be considered when interpreting these results.

articles.title: Natural products as modulators of cuproptosis: A systematic review of mechanisms, therapeutic potential, and future directions.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cuproptosis is a copper ion-dependent form of regulated cell death discovered in 2022. Its mechanism lies in the binding of copper to acylated proteins in the tricarboxylic acid cycle, thereby triggering proteotoxic stress. Natural products, with their structural diversity and good biocompatibility, are gradually becoming regulators of cuproptosis.

PURPOSE: To systematically clarify the mechanisms by which natural products regulate cuproptosis, identify its core targets, and evaluate its therapeutic potential, with a particular focus on cancer therapy and neurodegenerative diseases.

METHODS: Literature from PubMed and CNKI up to August 1, 2026 was retrieved using keywords including "cuproptosis", "copper ionophore", and "natural product", etc.; studies on natural product intervention in cuproptosis in tumors, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular diseases were screened and included, and the molecular mechanisms, regulatory modes, and therapeutic prospects were comprehensively analyzed.

RESULTS: The core cuproptosis axis involves FDX1-mediated reduction of Cu2+ to Cu+, binding of Cu+ to lipoylated DLAT, and mitochondrial dysfunction. This axis is tightly controlled by copper homeostasis proteins (SLC31A1, ATP7A/B). Natural products bifunctionally modulate cuproptosis. Specifically, they induce tumor cell cuproptosis by elevating intracellular copper or disrupting copper metabolism, and protect normal cells via copper chelation or FDX1 inhibition. Such strategies benefit tumor drug resistance reversal and neuroprotection in neurodegenerative diseases, but their development is restricted by unclear mechanisms, poor druggability and insufficient clinical translation.

CONCLUSION: Natural products are versatile modulators of cuproptosis with dual utility as probes and lead compounds. Future work should identify direct targets, improve druggability, and enable clinical translation.

articles.title: Selective Hemostasis in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot With an Absent Left Pulmonary Artery: The Bleeding Lifeline.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hemoptysis after repair of tetralogy of Fallot is uncommon and should prompt evaluation for residual pulmonary arterial lesions, infection, and systemic-to-pulmonary collaterals.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old woman with repaired tetralogy-type anatomy and an absent left pulmonary artery presented 5 months after intracardiac repair with hemoptysis. Postoperative computed tomographic angiography showed an absent/nonvisualized left pulmonary artery, a small focal hemorrhagic opacity in the left lower lung, and systemic collateral supply from the descending thoracic aorta and left inferior phrenic artery. Selective inferior phrenic angiography demonstrated hypertrophied feeders to the left lower lung with abnormal parenchymal blush. Superselective coil embolization of the culprit feeder achieved flow stasis and reduced blush; other collaterals were preserved to avoid pulmonary infarction.

DISCUSSION: In unilateral absence of a pulmonary artery, collaterals may be both the bleeding source and the lung's functional blood supply.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Management should target the culprit bleeding feeder rather than obliterating all collaterals.

articles.title: Timing of intraventricular hemorrhage in preterm infants less than 32 weeks of gestational age.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) remains a major challenge in preterm infants, with its exact timing and periods of greatest risk still debated. This study aims to describe the timing, incidence, severity, and risk factors for IVH in preterm infants born before 32 weeks' gestation.

METHODS: A prospective observational study of 182 preterm infants (<32 weeks) was conducted in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit. Standardized cranial ultrasounds were performed at 0-6, 6-24, 24-48, and 48-96 h post-birth and graded via Papile criteria. Maternal and neonatal associations with IVH were analyzed.

RESULTS: IVH incidence was 17 % (31/182), predominantly mild (80.7 %), while severe cases comprised 19.4 %. Almost half of the events (45 %) occurred within the first 6 h, followed by a second peak between days 2 and 4. While univariate analysis linked several immaturity and illness markers to IVH, multivariate models identified invasive ventilation as the sole independent predictor (adjusted OR 3.99, p=0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: IVH in very preterm infants occurs predominantly in the first hours after birth, with a subsequent risk window between 2 and 4 days. Invasive ventilation is the strongest independent risk factor, emphasizing the need for protective respiratory care. Early and ongoing ultrasound screening remains essential for timely diagnosis.

articles.title: Autoimmune adrenalitis in adolescents in Germany: a series of 4 cases.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This case report summarises clinical findings in four adolescents (aged 14-17 years) diagnosed with autoimmune adrenalitis at a German University Children's Hospital between 2019 and 2025.

CASE PRESENTATION: Clinical presentation varied and included fatigue, arterial hypotension, depressive symptoms, hyperpigmentation of the skin, and in one case acute kidney failure associated with acute viral infection. All patients showed hyponatraemia, reduced cortisol levels in serum and elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone concentrations at diagnosis. Autoimmune adrenalitis was confirmed in all patients by the presence of autoantibodies against the adrenal cortex. Interestingly, three of the four cases were diagnosed within a period of only 18 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Our case series of autoimmune adrenalitis may suggest a potential increase  in the annual incidence among adolescents. The clinical diversity of symptoms at diagnosis ranging from depression to acute kidney failure was striking. Since delayed diagnosis may lead to life-threatening complications, awareness of clinical variability is essential for physicians to achieve timely diagnosis. Cortisol levels should be routinely measured in patients with unclear fatigue and hyponatraemia.

articles.title: Taurocholic acid attenuates hepatic inflammation in MASH and modulates the PPARγ/NF-κB axis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a progressive form of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, is characterized by hepatocellular injury, inflammation, and varying degrees of fibrosis. Nevertheless, effective pharmacological treatments remain limited. Bile acids act as important signaling molecules, and disruption of bile acid homeostasis has been implicated in MASH pathogenesis. Here, we investigated whether the endogenous taurine-conjugated bile acid taurocholic acid (TCA) modulates hepatic inflammation in MASH. Network pharmacology identified 42 shared targets between TCA and MASH, including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ), mitogen-activated protein kinase 14, mitogen-activated protein kinase 8, prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2, nitric oxide synthase 3, with enrichment in peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling and inflammation-related pathways. Molecular docking further suggested potential interactions between TCA and the bile acid receptors farnesoid X receptor and G protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1. In a mouse model of MASH, TCA ameliorated hepatic steatosis and inflammatory cell infiltration; reduced serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase activities; decreased hepatic inducible nitric oxide synthase, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin-1β levels; increased PPARγ abundance; and suppressed nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) activation. Consistently, in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, TCA reduced the production of pro-inflammatory mediators, increased PPARγ expression, and suppressed NF-κB activation. These effects were markedly attenuated by the selective PPARγ antagonist GW9662. Collectively, these findings suggest that TCA attenuates hepatic inflammation in MASH, at least in part through modulation of the PPARγ/NF-κB signaling axis. These results provide a mechanistic rationale for further investigating bile acid-based strategies targeting inflammatory pathways in MASH.

articles.title: Sodium butyrate combined with ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains attenuates alcoholic liver disease by restoring gut-liver homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and intestinal barrier dysfunction, while limited effective pharmacological interventions remain currently available. This study investigated the protective effects of sodium butyrate (NaB), alone and in combination with newly isolated ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains on ALD, and examined the contribution of the gut microbiota. After 6 weeks of NaB intervention, associated indicators including liver injury, lipid metabolism, inflammatory mediators, alcohol-metabolizing enzyme activities, histopathology, intestinal barrier markers, and serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were assessed. 16S rRNA gene sequencing and antibiotic (ABX) pretreatment were used to evaluate microbiota involvement. In parallel, bacterial strains were isolated from long-term alcohol consumers without clinically apparent liver injury, and screened for ethanol-stress tolerance, ethanol-metabolizing capacity, and NaB-responsive growth, ultimately five strains (ML, MN, T2, T23, and TF) were firstly selected as the probiotic candidates for single or comined with NaB to evaluate in mice with ALD. As a result, NaB reduced indices of liver injury, dyslipidemia, inflammation, histopathological damage, and circulating LPS, while improving ADH/ALDH activity and ZO-1/Occludin expression. These effects were partially dependent on modulating gut microbiota. The five strains showed ethanol-metabolizing potential and NaB-responsive growth, and each strain improved several indices of alcohol-associated liver injury. Across multiple gut-liver axis endpoints, combination treatment generally provided enhanced protection than either intervention alone. Herein, a novel type of human-derived probiotic Lactobacillus strain, alone or combined with the postbiotic butyrate, effectively alleviated disease outcomes, highlighting its potential as a novel probiotic-postbiotic combination therapy.

articles.title: Qishen granule improves myocardial fibrosis in heart failure via Piezo1/Calpain2/LAMP1/CTSS in CCR2+ macrophages.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial fibrosis represents a common terminal pathological pathway in heart failure (HF), and currently, there is a lack of therapies specifically targeting the core pathological mechanisms of myocardial fibrosis, namely persistent inflammation and excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. In the present study, our aim was to evaluate the effectiveness of the herbal formulation Qishen Granule (QSG) against myocardial fibrosis.

METHODS: A model of HF with myocardial fibrosis was established by performing left anterior descending artery (LAD) ligation in mice. After three weeks of QSG treatment, cardiac function, fibrosis, and cardiac conduction were evaluated. We identified potential targets through network pharmacology and RNA sequencing analysis. The targeted effects of QSG were further validated using flow cytometry, Western blot, quantitative real-time PCR, and immunofluorescence techniques.

RESULTS: QSG can improve the heart function of HF mice, reduce myocardial inflammation and fibrosis, and effectively enhance cardiac conduction function. Its core mechanism lies in regulating the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 and the calcium-dependent cysteine protease 2 (Calpain2) activation cascade, thereby blocking lysosome-associated membrane protein 1 (LAMP1) hydrolysis and cathepsin S (CTSS) release while reducing ECM deposition. In CCR2+ macrophages, QSG inhibits calcium influx by reducing Piezo1 expression, thereby suppressing myofibroblast activation. Knockdown of Piezo1 partially abrogates QSG's antifibrotic effects, confirming Piezo1 as an essential target for QSG's protective actions.

CONCLUSIONS: QSG reduces ECM deposition by targeting and inhibiting the Piezo1/Calpain2/LAMP1/CTSS signal axis in CCR2+ macrophages, thus improving myocardial fibrosis. This study provides a novel therapeutic strategy for HF-associated myocardial fibrosis by leveraging mechanosensitive signaling pathways.

articles.title: Tirzepatide attenuates cardiac microvascular injury and ferroptosis-related lipid peroxidation in diabetic mice: endothelial responses in the context of partial PRKN silencing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic metabolic stress damages the cardiac microvasculature. We evaluated tirzepatide-associated cardiac and endothelial effects, including endpoint patterns after partial silencing of parkin RBR E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (PRKN) and lipidated microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B-II) accumulation during lysosomal blockade.

METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice received a normal diet, a high-fat diet (HFD), or HFD/streptozotocin (STZ); HFD and HFD/STZ cohorts received tirzepatide or vehicle for 8 weeks. Metabolic, cardiac, microvascular, lipid-peroxidation, iron, and protein endpoints were assessed; ultrastructure was evaluated descriptively. Human cardiac microvascular endothelial cells (HCMECs) underwent high glucose/palmitic acid (HG/PA), PRKN-silencing, and bafilomycin A1 (BafA1) experiments.

RESULTS: In HFD/STZ mice, tirzepatide improved selected glycemic and lipid measures and attenuated ventricular dilation, systolic dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, and microvascular injury. Myocardial 4-hydroxynonenal, malondialdehyde, and ferrous iron were lower, and mitochondrial quality-control and ferroptosis-related protein profiles shifted toward control levels. In HG/PA-exposed HCMECs, tirzepatide increased the JC-1 aggregate/monomer ratio, decreased 4-hydroxynonenal and acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4, and increased glutathione peroxidase 4 and ferritin heavy chain 1. Among tirzepatide-treated cultures, endpoints were less favorable with partial PRKN silencing than with control small interfering RNA, although treatment-associated differences remained within the PRKN-silenced background. BafA1 increased LC3B-II in control and HG/PA + tirzepatide cultures; the increase under HG/PA alone was not significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide was associated with less cardiac microvascular injury and ferroptosis-related lipid peroxidation. PRKN-silencing status was associated with endothelial endpoint patterns after tirzepatide treatment; effect modification and requirement were not established. Receptor dependence, mitophagic flux, and independence from systemic metabolic improvement remain unresolved.

articles.title: Notoginsenoside R1 attenuates post-ischemic pyroptosis: a novel CKLF1-endoplasmic reticulum stress pathway-mediated mechanism.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke induces neuronal pyroptosis driven by excessive endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, which exacerbates secondary brain injury. Notoginsenoside R1 (NGR1) has demonstrated neuroprotective properties; however, whether its mechanism involves the modulation of chemokine-like factor 1 (CKLF1)-mediated ER stress remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to determine whether NGR1 regulates CKLF1 to suppress the CCR5/ER stress/NLRP3 axis and thereby attenuate neuronal pyroptosis following ischemic injury.

METHODS: In vivo experiments were performed using a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), while in vitro studies employed oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) in PC12 cells and primary neurons. CKLF1-knockout rats, the CKLF1 agonist C27, and pharmacological inhibitors (TAK-799, 4-PBA, and MCC950) were utilized to dissect the pathway. Pyroptosis was assessed via lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release, TUNEL staining, immunofluorescence, Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, and immunoblotting of NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-N. Molecular interactions were examined using co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA).

RESULTS: NGR1 significantly reduced infarct volume, cerebral edema, and neurological deficits in MCAO rats, effects that were abolished in CKLF1-knockout animals. In OGD-treated PC12 cells, NGR1 improved viability, decreased LDH release, and reduced the proportion of Annexin V/PI-positive cells. Similarly, in OGD-treated primary neurons, NGR1 diminished TUNEL-positive cells and reduced immunofluorescence intensity of pyroptotic markers. In both cellular models, NGR1 downregulated NLRP3, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-N expression. Co-IP confirmed interactions between CKLF1 and both NLRP3 and CCR5. C27-induced CKLF1 activation promoted ER stress and pyroptosis, both of which were blocked by TAK-799. 4-PBA suppressed NLRP3 activation, whereas MCC950 did not affect ER stress, confirming that ER stress acts upstream of NLRP3 inflammasome activation. DARTS and CETSA verified direct binding of NGR1 to CKLF1.

CONCLUSION: NGR1 directly binds CKLF1, thereby suppressing the CCR5/ER stress/NLRP3 cascade and attenuating neuronal pyroptosis. These findings establish a mechanistic framework supporting the therapeutic potential of NGR1 in ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Targeting renal lipotoxicity with natural products in chronic kidney disease: mechanisms, molecular targets, and translational prospects.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal lipotoxicity is increasingly recognized as a metabolic driver of chronic kidney disease (CKD), linking excessive lipid delivery, impaired fatty acid oxidation, defective cholesterol handling, and insufficient lysosomal clearance to inflammation, ferroptosis, and fibrosis.

PURPOSE: This review evaluates evidence on the effects of natural products on impaired renal lipid handling and downstream pathways of lipotoxic injury in CKD.

STUDY DESIGN: A structured, mechanism-oriented narrative review.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection were searched for experimental, translational, and clinical studies related to CKD, renal lipotoxicity, lipid metabolism, organelle stress, and natural products or phytochemicals. Database searching was complemented by reference-list screening, citation tracking, and targeted searches for relevant mechanistic and translational evidence. Evidence was synthesized narratively and evaluated according to mechanistic directness and translational relevance.

RESULTS: Renal lipotoxicity is best understood as an imbalance among lipid uptake, synthesis, fatty acid oxidation, cholesterol efflux, and autophagic-lysosomal clearance rather than lipid accumulation alone. Natural products have been reported to modulate these processes and downstream inflammatory, ferroptotic, and fibrotic responses. However, most intervention studies were preclinical, concentrated in diabetic kidney disease models, and based on renal lipid burden or pathway-associated markers rather than direct measurements of lipid flux.

CONCLUSION: Natural products provide useful pharmacological probes and candidate leads for renal lipotoxicity, but translation requires chemically defined preparations, reproducible exposure, renal target engagement, mechanism-matched pharmacodynamic biomarkers, dose-response data, and CKD-relevant safety assessment.

articles.title: Physcion attenuates renal fibrosis by disrupting PKM2-FAK1 interaction and suppressing the FAK1/ERK signaling axis.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal fibrosis (RF) is the final common pathway of chronic kidney disease with limited therapeutic options. Pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) is upregulated in fibrotic kidneys and promotes pro-fibrotic signaling. Physcion (PHY), a natural anthraquinone, exerts organ-protective effects, but its direct targets and systemic mechanisms in RF remain unclear.

PURPOSE: This study aims to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which PHY alleviates RF, and to identify its direct targets and downstream signaling pathways.

METHODS: TGF-β1-induced HK-2 cells and unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) mice were used. The PKM2-FAK1 interaction was identified by Lip-MS, IP-MS, Co-IP, and molecular docking. The PHY binding site on PKM2 was determined via site-directed mutagenesis, and AAV-mediated knockdown was used to confirm PKM2 dependency in vivo. Multi-omics with canonical correlation analysis (CCA) and clinical RF specimens were also analyzed.

RESULTS: PHY alleviated RF in UUO mice with reduced fibrotic lesions and improved renal function. Mechanistically, PHY directly binds PKM2 at the F26 residue, and disrupts the PKM2-FAK1 physical interaction. Consequently, PHY inhibited FAK1/ERK1/2 phosphorylation and reduced pro-fibrotic markers, effects abrogated by PKM2/FAK1 knockdown and the F26A mutation. AAV-mediated PKM2 knockdown eliminated PHY's renoprotective effect. Additionally, PHY remodeled gut microbiota and altered metabolic profiles in UUO mice. Clinically, serum PKM2 activity was elevated in CKD patients and correlated with renal dysfunction markers.

CONCLUSION: This research identifies that PHY targets the PKM2-F26 residue, disrupts PKM2-FAK1 interaction, thereby inhibiting the FAK1/ERK pathway. Meanwhile, PHY synergistically modulates the gut-kidney metabolic axis, providing a promising therapeutic candidate and new target for RF.

articles.title: Dihydromyricetin attenuates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury associated with modulation of sirtuin 1-forkhead box O3 signaling and mitophagy.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke remains associated with substantial neurological disability, and effective strategies for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) are limited. Dihydromyricetin (DHM) has shown neuroprotective properties in experimental neurological disorders, but its effects and associated molecular mechanisms in CIRI remain incompletely understood. This study therefore evaluated the protective effects of DHM pretreatment and examined the signaling events associated with these effects in experimental CIRI.

METHODS: A mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion followed by reperfusion and an HT-22 cell model of oxygen-glucose deprivation followed by reoxygenation were used to evaluate the effects of DHM. In vivo outcomes included infarct volume, histopathological injury, neurological deficits, and recognition memory. In vitro outcomes included cell viability, lactate dehydrogenase release, apoptosis, oxidative stress, adenosine triphosphate content, and mitochondrial morphology. Network pharmacology was used to nominate candidate regulatory targets. Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and deacetylase activity, forkhead box O3 (FOXO3) acetylation and subcellular localization, and mitophagy-related changes were assessed by immunoblotting, nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, immunofluorescence, and co-immunoprecipitation. The selective SIRT1 inhibitor EX527 and small interfering RNA-mediated SIRT1 knockdown were used to examine SIRT1 involvement, whereas bafilomycin A1 and Parkin knockdown were used to assess mitophagic flux and the functional contribution of Parkin. A cellular thermal shift assay was used to test whether DHM produced a detectable change in SIRT1 thermal stability.

RESULTS: DHM pretreatment reduced infarct volume, improved neurological scores and recognition memory, and ameliorated histopathological injury in mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. In HT-22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation, DHM improved cell viability and adenosine triphosphate content, reduced oxidative stress and apoptosis, and preserved mitochondrial morphology. These effects were accompanied by increased SIRT1 expression and deacetylase activity, reduced FOXO3 acetylation, increased nuclear FOXO3, and changes in phosphatase and tensin homolog-induced kinase 1/Parkin and mitophagy-related markers consistent with enhanced mitophagic flux. EX527 and SIRT1 knockdown attenuated several molecular and protective effects of DHM, and Parkin knockdown weakened DHM-associated improvements in cellular outcomes. The cellular thermal shift assay did not detect a DHM-induced shift in SIRT1 thermal stability.

CONCLUSION: In the tested experimental models, DHM attenuated experimental CIRI, and these effects were associated with increased SIRT1 activity, FOXO3 deacetylation and nuclear accumulation, and Parkin-mediated mitophagy. Post-ischemic treatment studies and direct molecular validation are required to establish therapeutic relevance and the precise causal relationships among these events.

articles.title: Microbiome-guided prioritization of Corynebacterium striatum in diabetic foot ulcers and preclinical evaluation of tanshinone IIA.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are characterized by impaired healing and infection, but microbial signatures linked to glycemic status and their therapeutic relevance remain unclear.

PURPOSE: To identify DFU taxa associated with glycemic status and test whether microbiome-guided prioritization can inform evaluation of Tanshinone IIA (Tan IIA).

STUDY DESIGN: Clinical metagenomic discovery followed by in vitro functional and multi-omics analyses, biophysical studies, and in vivo evaluation.

METHODS: Wound samples from 54 DFU patients underwent HbA1c-stratified shotgun metagenomics. A prioritized patient-derived Corynebacterium striatum isolate was assessed for Tan IIA antibacterial and antibiofilm activity, multi-omics responses, and candidate-protein binding. Topical Tan IIA was tested in non-inoculated and C. striatum-inoculated diabetic wounds.

RESULTS: C. striatum was enriched in higher-HbA1c wounds and positively associated with continuous HbA1c (β = 0.422, 95% CI 0.095-0.748; P = 0.011; q = 0.064). Tan IIA inhibited the isolate (MIC = 64 μ g/ml), reduced biofilm biomass, and induced stress, redox, cell-envelope, and metabolic responses. SPR supported binding to MurD and TrxB. On day 14, wound closure was significantly greater in inoculated wounds (93.40% vs. 78.80%; adjusted P = 0.0187). In inoculated wounds, Tan IIA reduced EUB338-positive bacterial signal and viable counts versus vehicle (8.587 vs. 8.847 log10 CFU/g; adjusted P =  0.0480).

CONCLUSION: HbA1c-stratified metagenomics prioritized C. striatum as a glycemic-status-associated candidate. These findings support microbiome-guided preclinical evaluation of plant-derived Tan IIA as a topical candidate for infected DFUs.

articles.title: The Long Memory of the Biatrial Anastomosis: Late Atrial Thrombosis After Heart Transplantation.
Coronary Venous Disease: An Overlooked Cause of Heart Failure.
Plastic stent-based management versus metal stent exposure for lifelong biliary drainage in unresectable malignant hilar biliary obstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are widely used for malignant hilar biliary obstruction (MHBO), but whether they improve long-term drainage over plastic stents is uncertain. As chemotherapy prolongs survival, biliary drainage must be sustained across the remaining disease course. We compared intended lifelong biliary drainage failure (LDF) between plastic stent-based management and SEMS exposure using a causal inference framework.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 608 consecutive patients who underwent initial endoscopic drainage for unresectable MHBO at 22 Japanese tertiary centers between January 2020 and March 2024. SEMS use was modeled as a time-varying, irreversible exposure. A marginal structural model with stabilized inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights was used to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for LDF, defined as the point at which drainage could no longer be maintained by any endoscopic, endoscopic ultrasound-guided, or percutaneous approach.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 184 days, 130 patients (21.4%) had LDF and 384 (63.2%) died. SEMS exposure was associated with higher odds of LDF (adjusted OR 1.87, 95%CI 1.28-2.73; P = 0.001), consistent across sensitivity analyses (OR range, 1.75-2.53). The association strengthened from 1.79 at 90 days to 2.93 at 450 days. Cumulative costs were higher in an exploratory analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: SEMS exposure was associated with higher odds of LDF and higher costs than plastic stent-based management. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and prospective studies are needed to determine whether routine first-line SEMS use should be reconsidered when biliary drainage is intended to last across the remaining disease course.

articles.title: Modified citrus pectin orchestrates hepatic redox homeostasis through an Alistipes dispar-nicotinamide-sirtuin 1 axis to mitigate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified citrus pectin (MCP) is a bioactive functional component with potential metabolic benefits, but its therapeutic mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remain unclear.

PURPOSE: To determine whether MCP alleviates MASLD through gut microbiota remodelling and to identify the key microbial and metabolic mediators involved.

STUDY DESIGN: MASLD mouse models, multi-omics analyses, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), bacterial supplementation, and pharmacological inhibition were integrated to establish microbiota-metabolite-host causality.

METHODS: MCP efficacy was evaluated by assessing hepatic steatosis, inflammation, oxidative stress, and lipid metabolism. Metagenomics and metabolomics were used to identify MCP-responsive microbes and metabolites. FMT, administration of live or heat-killed Alistipes dispar, validation in db/db mice, and SIRT1 knockdown and inhibition with EX-527 were performed to verify causality and mechanism.

RESULTS: MCP markedly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Metagenomics identified enrichment of A. dispar as a key microbial signature associated with MCP efficacy. Live, but not heat-killed, A. dispar reproduced the protective effects of MCP and improved metabolic abnormalities in db/db mice. Mechanistically, MCP promoted A. dispar proliferation and increased nicotinamide levels, activating hepatic nicotinamide salvage and the SIRT1/PGC-1α/PPARα/CPT1A axis to enhance fatty acid oxidation. This response also suppressed COX-2/HMGB1-mediated inflammation and activated Nrf2/HO-1 antioxidant defence. EX-527 abolished the beneficial effects of MCP and A. dispar.

CONCLUSION: MCP alleviates MASLD through an A. dispar-nicotinamide-SIRT1 axis that restores metabolic, inflammatory, and redox homeostasis.

articles.title: Diagnostic significance of histopathological assessment of villous extracellular matrix in normal and pathological placentas.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The extracellular matrix of chorionic villi is an important factor ensuring the structural and functional viability of the placenta. The aim of the study was to compare the collagen-elastic frame of different types of chorionic villi in normal and pathological pregnancy in the I-III trimesters.

METHODS: We compared placentas of the I, II and III trimesters in pathological pregnancies associated with (1) fetal and placental malformations/genetic aberrations/dysgenesis, as well as (2) chronic fetoplacental hypoxia/asphyxia with the group of placentas from uncomplicated pregnancies of the appropriate gestational period. The study was performed by light microscopy on sections stained by Weigert (elastic fibers), Masson's trichrome (type I collagen) and Gomori's silver staining (type III collagen).

RESULTS: Physiological pregnancies showed stage-specific remodeling of the collagen-elastic frame. The dominance of the reticular organization of the stroma decreased as the villi matured. At the same time, the proportion of collagen fibrillar structures increased and was accompanied by the relative decrease in the number of subtrophoblastic elastic fibers in the distal, mainly terminal villi. The persistence of diffuse fibrillar and elastic stromal patterns in the terminal villi of full-term placentas was observed with delayed maturation of the villi and diabetes-associated changes in the placenta. Peripheral granular pattern of elastic fiber distribution in aberrant hydropic and dysmorphic villi was detected in fetal and placental malformations, genetic abnormalities, and dysgenesis. A diffuse homogeneous type I collagen pattern was associated with impaired fetoplacental unit formation and hypoxic damage.

CONCLUSIONS: Placentas of the I-III trimester with disorders of the formation of the fetoplacental unit, dysmetabolic conditions and hypoxic damage demonstrate patterns of remodeling of the collagen-elastic framework of chorionic villi, which differ from normal placentas of the corresponding gestational age.

articles.title: Longitudinal immune signatures in influenza A patients administered Lianhua Qingwen capsules.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: LHQW, a traditional Chinese medicine formulation, had been reported to accelerate symptom recovery in patients with influenza A virus (IAV) infection, yet the underlying immunological mechanisms remained largely unexplored.

METHODS: We integrated 41-plex CyTOF, RNA-seq, and Olink to characterize longitudinal peripheral immune signatures in IAV-infected patients receiving LHQW, and validated key findings using in vitro functional assays with active components and an in vivo IAV mouse model.

RESULTS: IAV infection induced broad perturbations across innate and adaptive immunity. LHQW treatment was associated with functional tuning across immune compartments, including enhanced monocyte activation with increased CD25 and CD40, and augmented CD8+ T-cell activation accompanied by attenuation of inhibitory checkpoints including PD-1 and CD39 across multiple CD8+ T-cell subsets. Intercorrelation analyses further suggested a temporal shift from a partially activated yet inhibition-leaning state on day 3 toward a more coordinated pattern of myeloid-lymphoid activation by day 7. Consistent with these clinical immune signatures, salidroside, an active component of LHQW, increased the frequency of CD40+ non-classical monocytes, whereas kaempferol reduced the frequencies of PD-1+ and CD39+ cells within CD8+ T cells in vitro. In a mouse model of IAV infection, high‑dose LHQW recapitulated key aspects of this immunomodulatory pattern and reduced pulmonary viral RNA loads.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings revealed time-dependent peripheral immune remodeling associated with LHQW treatment during recovery from IAV infection.

articles.title: PDCD4-driven steatosis via the HNF4A/GK axis is attenuated by the natural compound isosinensetin.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Programmed cell death factor 4 (PDCD4) has been implicated in various metabolic disorders. However, its role and underlying mechanisms in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) have not been fully elucidated.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to define the role of PDCD4 in hepatic steatosis and identify potential therapeutic strategies targeting its downstream metabolic pathway.

METHODS: RNA sequencing was performed on liver tissues from wild-type and PDCD4-knockout mice to identify dysregulated metabolic pathways and candidate downstream genes. The PDCD4-HNF4A-GK regulatory pathway was investigated using genetic, histological, biochemical, and molecular analyses in mouse models and hepatocytes. Virtual screening and molecular docking were used to identify candidate GK-targeting compounds.

RESULTS: Hepatocyte-specific PDCD4 deletion increased hepatic GK expression and aggravated lipid accumulation. GK knockout markedly attenuated PDCD4 deficiency-induced lipid accumulation in hepatocytes. Mechanistically, PDCD4 suppressed HNF4A translation, thereby limiting HNF4A-dependent GK transcription. Virtual screening identified isosinensetin as a candidate GK inhibitor. Isosinensetin inhibited GK activity and reduced lipid accumulation in hepatocytes and CDAHFD-fed mice.

CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that GK may warrant further investigation for ameliorating hepatic steatosis, and provide preliminary evidence for the PDCD4-HNF4A-GK axis in the regulation of hepatic triglyceride metabolism. Further studies are required to establish the relevance of this axis to the full spectrum of MASLD pathology.

articles.title: Post-stroke neuroplasticity: Spatiotemporal multicellular networks and traditional Chinese medicine interventions.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke remains a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. Although reperfusion therapy has improved clinical outcomes in the acute phase, long-term functional recovery remains limited. Neuroplasticity, a fundamental basis for functional recovery, is increasingly recognized as a multicellular interactive process rather than a neuron-centric phenomenon. In this context, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and phytomedicine may provide unique therapeutic value because of their multi-component, multi-target, and network-level regulatory properties.

PURPOSE: This review aims to summarize the multicellular interaction networks involved in post-stroke neuroplasticity and elucidate their spatiotemporal regulatory mechanisms in neural repair, with particular attention to the potential role of TCM-based network modulation.

STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review.

METHODS: Relevant studies on neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocyte lineage cells, peripheral immune cells, inflammatory mediators, phytomedicinal compounds, TCM formulas, and neuroplasticity after stroke were narratively reviewed and synthesized to construct an integrated framework of multicellular interaction networks.

RESULTS: Following stroke, neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocyte lineage cells, and peripheral immune cells form dynamic multicellular interaction networks that reshape the inflammatory microenvironment through cytokines, neurotrophic factors, extracellular vesicles, and other signaling mediators. These networks regulate post-stroke neuroplasticity in a stage-dependent and region-specific manner. Temporally, neuroplasticity evolves from acute injury-dominant inflammatory activation to subacute repair initiation and later network reorganization. Spatially, the infarct core, ischemic penumbra, and distant brain regions exhibit distinct inflammatory states, cellular responses, repair potential, and therapeutic priorities. Importantly, gray matter synaptic remodeling and white matter repair follow asynchronous trajectories, suggesting that post-stroke neural repair requires temporally and spatially matched interventions. Within this framework, TCM may act as multi-component and multi-target network modulators capable of simultaneously regulating neuroinflammation, glial responses, synaptic remodeling, and white matter repair. Accordingly, precision repair strategies should be designed as stage-specific and region-specific interventions targeting multicellular interaction networks rather than as uniform therapeutic approaches.

CONCLUSION: Multicellular interaction networks play a central role in regulating post-stroke neuroplasticity. Understanding their spatiotemporal characteristics may facilitate the development of stage-specific, region-specific, and individualized neural repair strategies for stroke treatment. TCM-guided multi-target modulation represents a promising strategy aligned with this network-level repair framework, although further mechanistic and clinical validation is still needed.

articles.title: Camellia nitidissima Chi flower extract ameliorates alcoholic liver disease by reshaping bile acid homeostasis and intestinal barrier function.
articles.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bile acid (BA) dyshomeostasis and intestinal barrier dysfunction are critical drivers of alcoholic liver disease (ALD), for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Although Camellia nitidissima Chi flower possesses anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and microbiota-modulatory properties, its role in ALD remains unclear.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of C. nitidissima Chi flower extract (CNFE) against ALD and elucidate its effects on BA homeostasis and intestinal barrier integrity.

METHODS: Bioactive constituents were identified using serum pharmacochemistry. CNFE efficacy was evaluated in an ethanol-escalated ALD mouse model. 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics, and molecular biology assays were used to investigate the effects of CNFE on the enterohepatic circulation of BAs and intestinal barrier integrity. Farnesoid X receptor (FXR) involvement was validated through molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, microscale thermophoresis, and in vivo FXR-specific interventions.

RESULTS: CNFE effectively ameliorated hepatic injury, systemic inflammation, and intestinal barrier damage in ALD mice. Mechanistically, CNFE reshaped BA homeostasis by suppressing hepatic synthesis, enhancing biliary efflux, reducing ileal reabsorption, and promoting fecal BA excretion, partly through FXR activation. Concurrently, CNFE-driven gut microbiota remodeling increased short-chain fatty acid production and reinforced intestinal barrier integrity.
