Despite this, most PAD patients do not receive dietary counselling, and few clinical studies have directly evaluated nutritional interventions in PAD populations. Given its low cost, safety, and potential for meaningful impact, dietary modification represents an underused but promising strategy in PAD prevention and treatment. Future research should prioritize PAD-specific dietary intervention trials and strategies for integrating nutrition into vascular care pathways.

articles.title: Peripheral vs. central arterial stiffness and cardiovascular events in older adults: the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV) is a representative measure of central arterial stiffness and an independent predictor of cardiovascular disease (CVD). Femoral-ankle pulse wave velocity (faPWV) represents peripheral arterial stiffness, but its association with CVD has not been specifically investigated.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 3402 Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities participants without prior coronary heart disease (CHD), heart failure (HF), or stroke at Visit 5 (2011-13) [mean age 74.8 (4.9) years, 36.1% male, 22.0% Black]. Femoral-ankle pulse wave velocity and cfPWV were measured by Omron VP-1000 Plus. The primary outcome was CVD (CHD, HF, and stroke). We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. During a median 9.0-year follow-up, 607 CVD events occurred. Overall, faPWV showed an inverse association with CVD, with hazard ratio (HR) for top vs. bottom quartile of 0.80 (95% confidence interval, 0.64-1.01) and p-for-trend of 0.017 in Model 1 (demographically adjusted) and HR of 0.86 (0.68-1.09) and p-for-trend of 0.096 in Model 2 (further adjusted for CVD risk factors). In contrast, cfPWV was positively associated with CVD in both models [HR for top vs. bottom quartile, 1.22 (0.95-1.56); p-for-trend = 0.043 in Model 2]. The ratio of cfPWV to faPWV ('cf-fa ratio') showed a stronger association with CVD [HR, 1.37 (1.07-1.74); p-for-trend = 0.005] than cfPWV. Examining CVD subtypes, the only significant contrast in Model 2 was cf-fa ratio and HF.

CONCLUSION: Femoral-ankle pulse wave velocity showed a borderline significant inverse association with CVD, and cf-fa ratio appeared more strongly associated with CVD than cfPWV. Our findings indicate distinct prognostic implications of central vs. peripheral arterial stiffness and support cf-fa ratio as an alternative measure for CVD risk assessment.

articles.title: The association between small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and peripheral artery disease: a large-scale cohort study and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: High levels of small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL) cholesterol are associated with an increased risk of ischaemic heart disease and stroke; however, data on peripheral artery disease are sparse and results inconclusive. We tested the hypothesis that higher levels of sdLDL cholesterol are associated with an increased risk of peripheral artery disease.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 31 036 individuals free of lipid-lowering therapy, ischaemic heart disease, and ischaemic stroke with measurements of sdLDL cholesterol at study entry in 2013-17. During a median follow-up of 6.2 years, 155 were diagnosed with peripheral artery disease. The association was confirmed using the Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) ≤ 0.9 as an endpoint. Furthermore, a meta-analysis of current and previous studies was conducted in 46 748 individuals including 660 peripheral artery disease cases. Finally, as a comparison across different vascular beds, risk estimates for myocardial infarction and ischaemic stroke were calculated. In multivariable adjusted models per 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) higher sdLDL cholesterol, the hazard ratio for peripheral artery disease was 2.06 [95% confidence interval (95% CI): 1.45-2.92] while the odds ratio for ABI ≤0.9 was 1.53 (1.08-2.15). Fixed and random effect meta-analysis risk estimates for peripheral artery disease did not differ and was 1.62 (1.27-2.06) for the highest vs. the lowest quartile of sdLDL cholesterol. For the 91st-100th vs. the 1st-50th percentiles of sdLDL cholesterol, we found hazard ratios of 2.59 (1.55-4.33) for peripheral artery disease, 2.18 (1.58-3.02) for myocardial infarction, and 1.84 (1.37-2.48) for ischaemic stroke.

CONCLUSION: Higher levels of sdLDL cholesterol were robustly associated with increased risk of peripheral artery disease in the present study and in a meta-analysis.

articles.title: Treatment outcomes among obese and non-obese women at high-risk of gestational diabetes: secondary analysis of the CDC4G clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We examined whether the association between treatment and adverse pregnancy outcomes among high-risk women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) differed by maternal obesity status.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of The Changing Diagnostic Criteria for Gestational Diabetes (CDC4G) trial, a prospective, unblinded, stepped-wedge cluster randomised clinical trial evaluating the implementation of the WHO-2013 GDM diagnostic criteria among women screened based on risk factors. The trial was conducted in 2018 with follow-up to August 2019. We included women whose GDM diagnosis based on a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test was discordant between the Swedish-GDM criteria (fasting plasma glucose ≥ 7.0 mmol/L and/or a region-specific 2-hour plasma glucose threshold ranging from 8.9 to < 11.1 mmol/L) and the modified WHO-2013 criteria (fasting plasma glucose ≥ 5.1 mmol/L and/or 2-hour plasma glucose ≥ 8.5 mmol/L). The 1-hour plasma glucose criterion could not be evaluated because these measurements were unavailable before implementation of the WHO-2013 criteria. Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m² and non-obesity as BMI 18.5-29.9 kg/m². The primary outcome was large-for-gestational-age neonate (LGA), defined as birthweight > 90th percentile by Swedish reference standards. Multilevel Poisson and multinomial regression models adjusted for baseline characteristics were used.

RESULTS: Among 2069 women with discordant classification by diagnostic criteria, 917 (55.9% with obesity) were undiagnosed and untreated, and 1152 (46.3% with obesity) were diagnosed and treated. In multivariable models, treatment did not reduce the risk of LGA among women with obesity (relative risk (RR) 0.94, 95% CI 0.81-1.08) but reduced risk among women without obesity (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.54-0.88), interaction P < .01.

CONCLUSIONS: Among high-risk women, implementing the WHO-2013 GDM diagnostic criteria was associated with a reduced risk of LGA among women without obesity, but not among women with obesity, partly reflecting the baseline lower risk of LGA among treated women with obesity than untreated women without obesity. Interpretation is limited by the absence of data on glycaemic control during pregnancy. Further research should evaluate how maternal characteristics modify treatment effectiveness to optimise management strategies for women with GDM.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN41918550. https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN41918550 .

articles.title: Experimental variables determine inflammatory phenotype and steroid responsiveness in murine asthma models.
articles.abstract: Murine models of allergic asthma are widely used to investigate disease mechanisms and evaluate therapeutic interventions. However, the extent to which experimental variables influence disease severity, immune phenotypes, and therapeutic responsiveness remains unclear. Models of ovalbumin-induced allergic asthma were established using different mouse strains (C57BL/6 and BALB/c), sensitization adjuvants (aluminum hydroxide and complete Freund's adjuvant), and anesthetic agents (tribromoethanol and isoflurane). Disease severity and inflammatory phenotype were assessed using histological analyses, antibody production, inflammatory cell infiltration, cytokine production, and responsiveness to dexamethasone treatment. C57BL/6 and BALB/c mice developed comparable airway inflammation but displayed distinct immune phenotypes. BALB/c mice exhibited enhanced eosinophilic inflammation and stronger Th2-associated responses, whereas C57BL/6 mice showed relatively increased neutrophilic inflammation. Comparison of the two adjuvant protocols revealed distinct inflammatory and immunological profiles. The Alum-based protocol was associated with predominantly eosinophilic and Th2-skewed responses, whereas the CFA-based protocol exhibited a milder mixed inflammatory profile with a relatively greater neutrophil contribution. In a murine model of asthma induced by ovalbumin and lipopolysaccharide administration, tribromoethanol and isoflurane anesthesia resulted in mixed eosinophilic-neutrophilic inflammation, with greater histological inflammation and interferon-γ-associated responses observed under tribromoethanol anesthesia. Thus, inflammatory and immunological outcomes vary across the experimental conditions examined, while dexamethasone responses differ between groups within the strain- and sensitization/challenge-protocol comparisons. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate experimental conditions and improving the reproducibility and translational relevance of preclinical asthma studies.

articles.title: Cold Agglutinin Disease-Keeping a Cool Head in Diagnosis and Management.
articles.journal: British journal of hospital medicine (London, England : 2005)
articles.abstract: Cold agglutinin disease (CAD) is a rare autoimmune haemolytic anaemia characterised by autoantibodies, known as cold agglutinins (CA), to erythrocyte antigens that react at low temperatures. CA, which are typically of immunoglobulin M (IgM) isotype, often bind to erythrocytes at acral sites of the circulation. This results in red cell agglutination and activation of the complement cascade. These lead to the clinical manifestations of cold-induced circulatory symptoms and chronic haemolysis, which can decompensate during intercurrent febrile illness or surgery. A heightened risk of thrombosis may be seen in active CAD. The underlying pathophysiology of CAD is driven by a small clonal B-cell population in the bone marrow, but the diagnosis requires the exclusion of an overt malignancy, infection, or autoimmune disorder that can be associated with a secondary cold agglutinin syndrome. The workup of CAD is multimodal, incorporating serological (often requiring meticulous temperature-controlled handling), radiographic, and histological investigations. The mainstay of CAD management is cold avoidance, and treatment is indicated in patients with symptomatic disease. In the emergency setting, rescue therapies such as complement inhibitors can be considered alongside warmed blood transfusions. Targeting the pathologic B-cell clone is the primary therapeutic strategy; however, head-to-head randomised controlled trials comparing different approaches are lacking. Given its rarity, CAD can present with diagnostic and therapeutic challenges to clinicians across a range of environments. Involvement of a multidisciplinary team of healthcare professionals incorporating haematologists, histopathologists and the transfusion laboratory is crucial in optimising the care of patients with this condition.

articles.title: An Update on Early Versus Delayed Oral Anticoagulation and Risks of Ischemic Stroke or Intracranial Hemorrhage After Cardioembolic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of anticoagulant therapy initiation in patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation remains unclear. Current guidelines are inconsistent, and emerging evidence suggests a possible benefit of early initiation of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). This study aimed to define the time frames used in the literature and to systematically review and meta-analyze the risks of recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients receiving early versus delayed oral anticoagulants (OACs) initiation.

METHODS: The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024528109). Relevant studies were searched using PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and OpenGrey. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions tool for observational studies and the Cochrane Risk-of-bias Tool 2.0 for randomized-controlled trials. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted, and the results were presented as forest plots. Publication bias was assessed using funnel plots.

RESULTS: Ten studies met the inclusion criteria. In the included studies, early OAC initiation was defined as treatment initiation within 3-6 days after acute ischemic stroke related to atrial fibrillation. There were no significant differences in early and delayed OACs for RIS or ICH (RIS: odds ratio (OR) = 0.81; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.61-1.10; I 2 = 33%; ICH: OR = 0.81; 95% CI: 0.57-1.15; I 2 = 0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Early OAC use, defined as initiation within 3-6 days after acute ischemic stroke, was not associated with an increased risk of RIS or ICH in patients with cardioembolic stroke. These results provide a practical definition of early anticoagulation in the existing literature and may support more consistent interpretation of current guideline recommendations.

articles.title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Generated Virtual Hypertension Patients as Proxies for Real Patient Perspectives: Comparative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating virtual patients for health care applications. However, whether LLM-generated virtual patients can reproduce patient-reported priority rankings remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: We evaluated whether LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients could approximate real patient-reported perspectives, and whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improved alignment with patient-reported priority rankings.

METHODS: A total of 20 patients from multiple regions completed structured questionnaires ranking priorities across 7 domains related to AI-assisted hypertension management. A total of 8 LLMs were evaluated under 3 simulation conditions: unconstrained generation, patient-specific simulation, and RAG-enhanced simulation. For unconstrained generation, each model produced 20 virtual patient profiles, each constructed by grouping baseline variables into the study categories and selecting the most frequent category across 10 repeated generations. For patient-specific baseline and RAG-enhanced simulations, each model generated 10 complete questionnaire responses per participant and condition; the modal complete 4-item ranking within each domain was selected as the final ranking. Model-generated rankings were compared with patient-reported rankings using total accuracy, top-1 accuracy, and full accuracy. In addition, 5 hypertension clinicians independently inferred patient-priority rankings while blinded to both real patient responses and LLM outputs, providing a human reference benchmark.

RESULTS: Aggregated unconstrained virtual patient profiles varied across models, with 45%-55% having college-level education, and 75%-95% using antihypertensive medication. In patient-specific baseline simulations, total accuracy ranged from 46.3% to 71.4%. RAG improved all 3 accuracy metrics across the eight models, increasing mean total accuracy from 62.8% to 76.6%, top-1 accuracy from 51.6% to 72.9%, and full accuracy from 22.2% to 49.4% (all P<.001). The largest mean domain-level gains occurred in safety escalation awareness and emotional support and reassurance. Qwen-RAG achieved the highest total accuracy (86.1%) and full accuracy (64.3%). In descriptive comparisons, its corresponding values exceeded those of the clinician consensus (72.5% and 45.0%), while top-1 accuracy was numerically similar (80.7% vs 80.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: LLM-generated virtual hypertension patients can moderately approximate real patient perspectives, but unconstrained aggregated profiles differed demographically, behaviorally, and clinically from the enrolled reference cohort under the study conditions. RAG substantially improves concordance between virtual patient rankings and patient-reported priorities and may provide a scalable methodological approach for incorporating patient-perspective proxies into digital health research contexts.

articles.title: Music in the cath lab: from playlist to proof.
The copper-based carbon dot nanozyme catalytic engineering for achieving the balance regulation of ROS/RNS in the vascular pathological microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Rapid re-endothelialization of stent surfaces is critical to reduce late stent thrombosis and restenosis. Supplementation with endogenous gaseous signaling molecules, e.g., NO, holds promise to selectively inhibit SMC proliferation while supporting EC growth, accelerating vascular repair. However, the regulatory efficacy of these gasotransmitters is challenged by the complex pathological microenvironment induced by stent implantation, including oxidative stress, reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts, inflammation, and coagulation cascades. Herein, we propose a surface catalytic engineering strategy based on a Cu-doped carbon dots (Cu/C-dots) nanozyme-modified stent surface. By introducing multifunctional Cu/C-dots, we mimic the catalytic activities of natural enzymes such as superoxide dismutase (SOD) and peroxidase (POD) to scavenge ROS, while simultaneously exploiting Cu sites to catalyze NO release from endogenous NO donors. Our results demonstrate that the cooperative catalytic system formed by Cu and carbon dots efficiently eliminates ROS and effectively alleviates local oxidative stress and acute inflammatory responses at the lesion site. Notably, this approach prevents the formation of peroxynitrite (ONOO-), a toxic byproduct arising from the reaction between NO and ROS, thereby maximizing the vasoregulatory functions of NO. Consequently, the coating significantly reduces platelet adhesion, activation, and thrombus formation, and selectively modulates SMC behavior. Compared with bare metal stents, the coated stents markedly accelerate endothelial regeneration and effectively suppress neointimal hyperplasia. Collectively, this strategy offers substantial advantages in promoting rapid endothelialization, inhibiting neointima formation, and restoring vascular homeostasis. This surface multi-catalytic engineering approach may provide a novel solution to address the limitations of current vascular stents.

articles.title: Tamibarotene attenuates sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy via a CD36-dependent macrophage efferocytic and anti-inflammatory programme.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SCM) is a leading cause of sepsis mortality, driven by impaired macrophage efferocytosis and hyperinflammation. We tested whether tamibarotene confers SCM protection via CD36-mediated macrophage efferocytosis.

METHODS: A non-contact Transwell co-culture of RAW264.7 macrophages and HL-1 cardiomyocytes recapitulated the SCM microenvironment in vitro. CD36, efferocytic receptors (CX3CR1, MERTK, TIM4), polarization markers (iNOS, CD206, CD163), oxidative stress, and apoptosis were quantified by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence. Complementary in vivo studies used a murine SCM model with AAV9-mediated CD36 modulation to validate mechanistic findings.

RESULTS: In vitro, tamibarotene upregulated CD36 in LPS-stimulated macrophages, increased efferocytic receptor expression, promoted M2 polarization (elevated CD206/CD163, reduced iNOS), and attenuated ROS accumulation, mitochondrial injury, and apoptosis (downregulated Bax/cleaved caspase-3, upregulated Bcl-2). CD36 knockdown reversed these benefits and abolished tamibarotene's efficacy. In vivo, AAV9-mediated CD36 overexpression restored myocardial antioxidant enzymes (SOD, GSH-PX), reduced lipid peroxidation (MDA), and lowered circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines (hs-CRP, IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), while upregulating efferocytic and anti-apoptotic proteins and downregulating pro-apoptotic mediators. CD36 knockdown exacerbated myocardial injury and systemic inflammation.

CONCLUSIONS: CD36 is a critical regulator of macrophage efferocytosis and polarization. Tamibarotene upregulates CD36 to enhance efferocytic capacity and M2 polarization, suppress oxidative stress and inflammation, and reduce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, conferring SCM protection. The CD36-efferocytosis axis represents a novel therapeutic target for SCM immunotherapy.

articles.title: Mitophagy receptor OPTN alleviates renal fibrosis via ubiquitinated TOMM22.
articles.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of damaged mitochondria, is crucial for maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis. Its dysregulation is implicated in various diseases and pathological conditions, including renal fibrosis. Although PRKN (Parkin) and OPTN (optineurin) are known regulators of mitophagy, with PRKN ubiquitinating outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) proteins and OPTN recruiting autophagic machinery, the molecular intermediates coordinating their functions remain unclear. Here, we identify TOMM22, a core mitochondrial outer membrane protein, as a potential molecular link between PRKN-mediated ubiquitination and OPTN recognition during mitophagy-associated responses. We demonstrate that TOMM22 is ubiquitinated by PRKN primarily at Lys76 with Lys63-linked polyubiquitin chains, and recognized by the ubiquitin-binding domain of OPTN. Furthermore, given the high mitochondrial abundance in renal tubules and the emerging role of mitophagy dysfunction in renal fibrosis, we investigated the in vivo effects of modulating this pathway. We found that impairment of the PRKN-TOMM22-OPTN axis-mediated mitophagy was associated with mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and fibrosis progression. Conversely, overexpression of PRKN or TOMM22 was associated with improved mitochondrial function and reduced renal fibrosis in vivo. Clinically, OPTN, PRKN and TOMM22 expression levels were lower in kidney tissues from patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) than in those from patients with minimal change disease (MCD). Our findings provide insights into the regulation of mitochondrial quality control and suggest a potential role for the PRKN-TOMM22-OPTN axis in renal fibrosis.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias: A Systematic Review and Dual-Framework (Frequentist and Bayesian) Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is being applied to ventricular arrhythmias, but human evidence remains limited to small, single-arm studies. We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, major conference archives, and reference lists through March 1, 2026, for human studies of catheter-based PFA for ventricular tachycardia (VT) or premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) enrolling at least 5 patients. We pooled study-defined acute procedural success with two complementary analyses of the same data: a frequentist random-effects model and a Bayesian binomial-logit hierarchical model that expresses the same evidence as posterior probabilities. Seven unique studies (274 patients enrolled; 12 study arms, 270 arm-level patients) were included. Pooled acute success was 84.3% (95% confidence interval 77.7-89.2%) across 6 VT arms (n = 173) and 86.6% (80.6-91.0%) across 6 PVC arms (n = 97); the posterior probability that the pooled parameter success exceeds 80% was 97.1% for VT and 96.7% for PVCs. Major complications occurred in 5.8% (3.5-9.4%; 7 studies). Coronary spasm was the principal PFA-specific event; no study performed late angiography or intravascular imaging, and phrenic nerve and esophageal outcomes were largely not assessed. One study measured hemolysis systematically. Recurrence during available follow-up (3.3-9.6 months per study) was 36% for VT across 5 arms and 22% for PVCs. These findings support acute procedural feasibility. Durability, safety, and comparative effectiveness remain uncertain and require standardized prospective assessment.

articles.title: Racial Disparities in Lupus Nephritis: A Nationwide Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical rheumatology : practical reports on rheumatic & musculoskeletal diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lupus nephritis (LN) disproportionately affects racial minorities and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality.

OBJECTIVE: National-level data on racial disparities in LN remains limited and our study aims to highlight key racial disparities and predictors of inpatient mortality in LN.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study.

SETTING: Discharge-level data from US hospitalizations included in National Inpatient Sample database.

PARTICIPANTS: Adult hospitalizations with a primary/secondary diagnosis of LN were included from National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2019 using ICD-10 codes and divided into African Americans (AA) or Hispanics versus other races.

INTERVENTION: Not applicable. This was an observational analysis.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Several variables, including demographics, outcomes, and health care burden were compared. Multivariate logistic regression was conducted for predictors of mortality. p value of ≤0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: Among 104, 865 adult LN hospitalizations, 66.3% were AA or Hispanics. Compared with other races, this group were more often females (85.5% vs. 79.9%), younger (38.4 vs. 45.6 y), from lowest-income quartile (45.8% vs. 23.6%), and had Medicaid (30.6% vs. 19.4%). They also had higher rates of acute kidney injury/chronic kidney disease (AKI/CKD) (82.5% vs. 79.1%), ESRD (44.6% vs. 33.9%), and leaving against medical advice (3.0% vs. 1.7%), but lower rates of renal transplant (4.3% vs. 5.2%), transfers to skilled nursing facilities (8.7% vs. 13.3%), and mortality (1.7% vs. 2.6%). Significant mortality predictors included: age, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), Medicaid, small bed size, sepsis, pulmonary embolism/deep vein thrombosis (PE/DVT), and CKD. (All p≤0.05 unless specified).

LIMITATIONS: Review of medical data from an administrative database involved reliance on diagnostic coding, limited detailed clinical information, and residual confounding.

CONCLUSION: African Americans and Hispanics represented two-thirds of LN hospitalizations and had distinct demographic profiles, reflecting greater socioeconomic disadvantage and renal disease burden. Mortality was influenced by age, comorbidity burden, Medicaid status, hospital size, sepsis, PE/DVT, and CKD highlighting key factors influencing potential disparities.

articles.title: Supervision Consultation as an Organizational Resource to Buffer Occupational Burnout: Proposal of a Longitudinal Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occupational burnout is a widespread challenge in contemporary workplaces and is associated with reduced employee well-being, productivity, and organizational sustainability. Although resource-based models emphasize the protective role of personal and job resources, organizational-level interventions targeting burnout remain underexamined. Professional supervision represents a potentially scalable organizational resource that may buffer burnout through the enhancement of personal resources such as occupational self-efficacy, work engagement, and job satisfaction.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this research proposal is to describe a planned study evaluating whether sustained supervision consultation-delivered face-to-face or online-may buffer occupational burnout indirectly by strengthening key personal resources across diverse occupational groups.

METHODS: This research proposal describes a planned longitudinal randomized controlled trial with three parallel arms: (1) face-to-face supervision consultation, (2) online supervision consultation, and (3) a waitlist control condition. Structural equation modeling using random-intercept cross-lagged panel models will be used to examine mediation processes over time. Approximately 300 participants from multiple occupational sectors will be recruited. Assessments will be conducted at baseline (T1), 3 months (T2), and 6 months (T3). The proposed intervention consists of 12 biweekly 90-minute group supervision consultation sessions delivered over a 6-month period. Burnout will be measured primarily using the Burnout Assessment Tool (BAT) and supplemented with the Link Burnout Questionnaire (LBQ) to enable comparison across competing conceptualizations. Occupational self-efficacy, work engagement, and job satisfaction will be examined as mediating personal resources. Data will be analyzed using longitudinal structural equation modeling, including mediation and multigroup analyses.

RESULTS: As of February 2026, the study protocol has been finalized, but participant recruitment and data collection had not yet commenced. Preparatory work was supported by an internal seed grant awarded in June 2021 under the University of Gdańsk UGrants-first Programme. No data analysis had been conducted. The proposed study remains in the planning stage and will be implemented following ethics approval, trial registration, and acquisition of the necessary resources. Findings from the completed study will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications.

CONCLUSIONS: This research proposal describes a planned study evaluating supervision consultation as a preventive organizational intervention for burnout. The study aims to contribute to theory-driven, resource-based approaches to occupational well-being and to inform the development of future organizational interventions.

articles.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Community-Based Interventions for the Prevention and Control of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Pakistan: Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-based interventions (CBIs) are a promising strategy for preventing and controlling noncommunicable diseases, including type 2 diabetes mellitus. However, the success of such interventions depends on cultural and contextual factors that influence community mobilization and participation.

OBJECTIVE: This qualitative study aimed to investigate the barriers and facilitators to CBIs for the prevention and control of type 2 diabetes in rural and urban Pakistan.

METHODS: We conducted a multisite qualitative study involving 37 in-depth interviews and 12 focus group discussions with community members with known and unknown type 2 diabetes status, their caregivers, community elders, and health care providers. Data were collected from approximately 50 participants in rural and urban areas of Pakistan and were analyzed using the framework approach.

RESULTS: Three overarching themes emerged-familiarity with CBIs, barriers to implementation, and facilitators to implementation-mapped across the socioecological model. Participants displayed limited yet varied understanding of CBIs, with rural participants often equating them to research activities, while urban participants linked them to health education and moral responsibility. Barriers included low awareness, misconceptions, gender and cultural constraints, logistical challenges, economic hardship, and security concerns. Facilitators encompassed engagement with community leaders, gender-sensitive approaches, incentives, accessible venues, mass mobilization, religious spaces, and involvement of local health care workers for intervention delivery. Rural-urban contrasts highlighted the influence of social cohesion, prior exposure, and structural factors on CBI uptake.

CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights that CBIs for diabetes prevention and control in Pakistan require contextually tailored, culturally sensitive, and gender-responsive approaches. Rural-urban contrasts underscore the role of social cohesion, prior exposure, and structural factors in shaping engagement. Integrating these insights can guide the design and implementation of scalable, sustainable CBIs aimed at tackling diabetes across diverse Pakistani communities.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Digital Mental Health Interventions in Community-Based Care: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental health conditions are a leading cause of disability and economic burden worldwide. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) may widen access, but economic evidence from community mental health settings, including low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), has not been synthesized by perspective, time horizon, and comparator type.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the cost-effectiveness of DMHIs delivered in community mental health settings.

METHODS: This systematic review followed the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines and was registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO CRD420251141326). PubMed, Scopus, the Directory of Open Access Journals, and the Cochrane Library were searched for economic evaluations published from January 2010 to June 2025 involving adolescents (aged 10 years and older) through older adults with mental disorders. Two reviewers independently screened studies, and the quality was appraised using the Consensus on Health Economic Criteria (CHEC) list. Costs were standardized to 2025 US $, and findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Of 2478 records identified, 20 economic evaluations were included: 16 randomized controlled trials, 3 decision-analytic models, and 1 uncontrolled single-arm study, conducted in high-income countries and LMICs (Kenya, Lebanon, China, and Southeast Europe). Depression (n=11, 55%) and anxiety (n=7, 35%) were the most frequent targets. Of 20 studies, 10 (50%) used a health care payer perspective only, 1 (5%) study used a societal perspective only, and 9 (45%) used both perspectives; time horizons ranged from 2 weeks to 10 years. Thirteen (65%) studies were cost-effective at the willingness-to-pay thresholds applied, and 4 (20%) were not; 3 (15%) did not state a threshold. Among the 16 studies reporting quality-adjusted life years, 4 (25%) were dominant (less costly and more effective), 11 (69%) were more costly and more effective, and 1 (6%) was less costly and less effective. The BlueIce smartphone app for self-harm and the NIDUS-Family (New Interventions for Independence in Dementia Studies) dementia intervention were dominant, whereas a societal perspective made some interventions cost-saving, such as Step-by-Step in Lebanon. Interventions that were not cost-effective included those evaluated in Germany, the United States, and Southeast Europe, and 1 psychosis trial with a high incremental cost-effectiveness ratio. Methodological quality was high in 15 (75%) studies, moderate in 4 (20%), and low in 1 (5%).

CONCLUSIONS: DMHIs in community settings can offer good value for money, particularly guided internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy for depression and anxiety, and may be cost-saving from a societal perspective. The evidence is limited by short time horizons (often 12 months or less), waitlist and usual care comparators, and heterogeneous outcome measures. Future evaluations should use longer follow-ups, active comparators, and a common utility measure, ideally the EQ-5D questionnaire.

articles.title: Structural validity and exploratory model refinement of HLS-EU-Q16 in patients with recent stroke or transient ischemic attack: a Rasch analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Experiencing a stroke is a sudden, life-changing event, leading to long-lasting needs for care, support and rehabilitation, even for stroke survivors with less severe disability. Patients with stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA) need the ability to navigate healthcare systems and understand and apply health information. This highlights the importance of assessing health literacy in this population with adequate instruments. The aim of this study was to investigate the structural validity of the 16-item European Health Literacy Survey Questionnaire (HLS-EU-Q16) in individuals with recent stroke or TIA.

METHODOLOGY: Patients with recent stroke or TIA, referred to home-based rehabilitation, completed the HLS-EU-Q16, which assesses perceived abilities to access, understand, appraise and apply health information. Each item has four response categories (very easy to very difficult). The four-category item responses were evaluated using a Rasch rating scale model. Analyses included category functioning, local independence, dimensionality, item and person fit, separation and reliability, and differential item functioning (DIF).

RESULTS: A total of 156 patients with recent stroke or TIA (73.6 years, 75 women) were included. The modified Rankin scale indicated that the majority experienced mild to moderate disability. ​Rating scale functioning was satisfactory. However, the original model exhibited local dependence, underfitting and overfitting items, and indications of multidimensionality (1st contrast eigenvalue = 2.39). An exploratory process of item removal and reanalysis resulted in a 12-item model. Retained items demonstrated local independence and acceptable fit. The model explained 55.1% and the 1st contrast eigenvalue was 1.95. Nine participants (5.8%) demonstrated person misfit. Person separation index was 2.66 with reliability of 0.88, indicating ability to distinguish between approximately three levels of health literacy. Two items demonstrated meaningful DIF by sex, showing higher difficulty among men.

CONCLUSIONS: In this sample, a 12-item model demonstrated better fit to the Rasch model than the original HLS-EU-Q16. The findings suggest that this shorter model may reduce respondent burden when assessing health literacy in individuals with recent stroke or TIA. However, these results need to be interpreted with caution due to the modest sample size. Therefore, the modelś validity needs to be evaluated in independent and more diverse stroke samples.

articles.title: Evaluating Human and AI-Based Triage Performance in the Emergency Department: Real-World Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergency departments (EDs) depend on rapid, reliable triage for patient safety and flow. The Manchester Triage System (MTS) is widely implemented but exhibits known interrater variability. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential decision-support tools for triage and early assessment, yet real-world comparative evaluations remain scarce.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare clinician and LLM performance on ED triage accuracy, specialty assignment, diagnostic recommendations, and admission prediction in a real-world cohort.

METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study, 305 walk-in ED encounters at a German tertiary-care hospital were analyzed. A nurse performed real-time MTS-assessment and initial specialty assignment at presentation. Each anonymized case was independently evaluated by 4 physicians and 12 LLMs from 4 providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Mistral). Triage agreement was assessed against 2 reference standards: a consensus human label (ground-truth 1 [GT1]) and real-time nurse-assigned MTS-triage (ground-truth 2 [GT2]). For human raters, a leave-one-out variant of GT1 (LOO-GT1) assessed incorporation bias. The primary statistic was quadratic-weighted Cohen κ (unweighted κ reported alongside). Secondary outcomes were directional triage errors (over- or undertriage, |Δ|≤1), specialty top-1 accuracy, per-case precision, recall, F1-score of recommended diagnostics, and admission prediction (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]).

RESULTS: Median age was 45 (IQR 31-62) years; 188 (61.6%) patients were male; admission rate was 20.1% (56/278). Against GT1, human-rater (physicians and nurse) accuracy ranged 0.59-0.83 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.60-0.88; unweighted κ 0.35-0.74), and LLM accuracy 0.35-0.70 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.46-0.72; unweighted κ 0.11-0.53). Under LOO-GT1, human-rater weighted κ fell to 0.48-0.81. Only 1 clinician (Doctor 1, weighted κ 0.81) retained agreement clearly above any LLM, while 3 LLMs (Gemini-3.5-flash=0.72, GPT-5.5=0.69, and GPT-5=0.66) exceeded the LOO-corrected agreement of the remaining 4 human raters. One-off agreement exceeded 86% for all raters and models. Vs GT1, overtriage ranged 6%-56% and undertriage 6%-36%. Vs GT2, corresponding ranges were 11%-62% and 5%-30%. Against the study specialty reference, physician specialty-assignment accuracy ranged 0.88-0.93 and LLM accuracy 0.62-0.80. Against the operational triage-pathway specialty assignment, the corresponding ranges were 0.81-0.82 and 0.57-0.75. Model diagnostic recommendation F1-scores ranged 0.55-0.69. Admission prediction demonstrated high sensitivity (0.73-0.95) and NPV (0.90-0.96), but modest PPV (0.25-0.41).

CONCLUSIONS: In a real-world ED cohort, 1 clinician (Doctor 1, a specialist physician) had the highest urgency agreement point estimate under both GT1 and LOO-GT1. Under LOO-GT1, 3 contemporary LLMs reached agreement that exceeded that of the other 4 clinicians. For specialty assignment, all clinicians remained clearly ahead of the best LLM. LLMs showed strong sensitivity and high NPV for admission prediction, but modest PPV precludes autonomous use. Because both reference standards are empirical rather than outcome-anchored gold standards, findings represent agreement against expert consensus and routine practice rather than an absolute correctness benchmark, and support a complementary, human-in-the-loop role for LLM-based decision-support in ED triage and early assessment.

articles.title: Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy as the Initial Presentation of Sato-Variant Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome in a Child.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sato variant of cyclic vomiting syndrome (CVS) is characterized by hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis hyperactivation with episodic catecholamine surges, hypertension, and lethargy. Catecholamine-mediated cardiovascular complications have not been characterized in this population.

CASE SUMMARY: A 6-year-old girl presented with cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction 11%). Cardiac biomarkers were markedly elevated. Ventricular function recovered within 2 weeks, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed no late gadolinium enhancement, excluding myocarditis. The presentation was consistent with stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy. She was subsequently diagnosed with the Sato variant of CVS after developing recurrent stereotypical vomiting episodes complicated by hypertensive crises (systolic pressures >200 mm Hg). Management with propranolol prophylaxis and on-demand antihypertensives preserved cardiac function over nearly 2 years of follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This is the first report of stress cardiomyopathy complicating Sato-variant CVS without an arrhythmogenic substrate, demonstrating that episodic catecholamine surges in this subtype can produce life-threatening cardiac complications in children.

articles.title: Aortic Root Replacement and LVAD in Valvular Heart Disease: Bridge to Recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: End-stage valvular heart disease with severe myocardial fibrosis is traditionally managed with heart transplantation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 31-year-old man with bicuspid aortic valve, severe regurgitation, ejection fraction of 16%, and extensive fibrosis (extracellular volume, 39.1%) underwent a Bio-Bentall procedure with left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. After 27 months of support with optimized guideline-directed medical therapy, ejection fraction recovered to 66%, permitting minimally invasive device explantation. Paired histopathology demonstrated collagen volume fraction regression from 40.26% to 0.65%.

DISCUSSION: This case challenges the dogma that severe fibrosis precludes myocardial recovery. The outcome likely reflects synergistic effects of volume overload correction, sustained mechanical unloading, and aggressive neurohormonal blockade. However, bridge to recovery remains uncommon, requires long-term commitment, and is not reproducible in all comparable patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Combined Bio-Bentall and LVAD implantation may achieve bridge to recovery in carefully selected young patients with end-stage valvular disease, but patient selection remains critical and outcomes are not guaranteed.

articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

articles.title: Effect of Aficamten vs Metoprolol on Cardiac Biomarkers in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) may change with therapy.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to examine biomarker responses to aficamten vs metoprolol monotherapy in patients with oHCM in the randomized MAPLE-HCM (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM) trial and assess if changes parallel treatment effects.

METHODS: Differences in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) from baseline to end of therapy were compared by treatment.

RESULTS: Participants receiving aficamten (n = 88) or metoprolol (n = 87) were generally well matched for baseline characteristics. After 24 weeks, geometric mean NT-proBNP decreased by 73% with aficamten but increased by 42% with metoprolol (treatment effect -81% [-85% to -76%]; P < 0.001). Mean hs-cTnI decreased by 43% with aficamten and by 17% with metoprolol (treatment effect -28% [-41% to -13%]; P = 0.001); both biomarkers reverted to baseline after washout. Regardless of treatment, the correlation between changes in biomarkers was significant for NT-proBNP and peak oxygen uptake (-0.42; P < 0.001) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) (-0.26; P < 0.001) and between changes in hs-cTnI and KCCQ-CSS (-1.9; P = 0.013) but not peak oxygen uptake (-0.11; P = 0.22). When considering treatment, there were significant correlations between improvements in NT-proBNP and Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract gradient (LVOT-G) (r = +0.25; P = 0.02) and the ratio between early transmitral filling and early diastolic tissue Doppler velocity (r = +0.50; P = 0.001) with aficamten. Correlations between improvements in hs-cTnI and Valsalva LVOT-G (r = +0.17; P = 0.03) and maximal left ventricular wall thickness (r = +0.25; P = 0.001) were observed with aficamten.

CONCLUSIONS: Aficamten treatment resulted in lower NT-proBNP and hs-cTnI vs metoprolol. Reduction in NT-proBNP correlated with improved exercise capacity, LVOT-G, and health status. These results provide mechanistic insights regarding the benefit of aficamten over metoprolol in MAPLE-HCM. (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM [MAPLE-HCM]; NCT05767346).

articles.title: Genetic and Clinical Predictors of Myocardial Recovery in Biopsy-Proven Pediatric Myocarditis Requiring Ventricular Assist Device.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial recovery with ventricular assist device (VAD) support is a rare but favorable outcome.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to identify genetic and clinical determinants of myocardial recovery in pediatric patients with myocarditis requiring VAD support.

METHODS: This multicenter study included 86 pediatric patients with biopsy-proven myocarditis on VAD support from MYKKE (Myocarditis Registry for Children and Adolescents). A subcohort (n = 57) underwent next-generation sequencing of cardiomyopathy-associated genes. Patients were stratified by outcome (recovery vs nonrecovery). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) model and logistic regression were applied to identify clinical variables of recovery. Gene burden and rare variant enrichment analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Recovery occurred in 37% (32/86) of patients. Cardiomyopathy-associated variants were enriched in the cohort compared with population control subjects (P < 0.001). Likely pathogenic/pathogenic (LP/P) cardiomyopathy-associated variants were more common in the nonrecovery group (P = 0.045). Gene burden analyses implicated TNNI3 (cardiac troponin I), BAG3 (BAG cochaperone 3), and LMNA (lamin A/C) in nonrecovery. Patients with findings of chronic myocarditis on biopsy more often carried LP/P variants or high-probability variants of uncertain significance compared with patients with acute myocarditis (P = 0.027). The LASSO-derived model showed good discrimination for recovery (area under the curve: 0.90; 95% CI: 0.83-0.98), identifying 11 variables. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, young age, female sex, and acute myocarditis on biopsy were significantly associated with recovery. Genetic variants provided independent negative predictive value for recovery beyond the LASSO-derived model (LP/P: P = 0.065; LP/P/high-probability variants of uncertain significance: P = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric myocarditis, myocardial recovery is associated with absence of cardiomyopathy-associated genetic variants, severe inflammation, and young age. Incorporating genetic analyses into the diagnostic workflow may improve identification of recovery candidates and guide personalized treatment strategies.

articles.title: AGA Clinical Practice Update on Endoscopic Management of Zenker's Diverticulum and Cricopharyngeal Bar: Commentary.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) Institute Clinical Practice Update is to review the available evidence supporting endoscopic treatment of Zenker's diverticulum and cricopharyngeal bar and examine various approaches for therapy.

METHODS: This Clinical Practice Update was commissioned and approved by the AGA Institute Clinical Practice Updates Committee and the AGA Governing Board to provide timely guidance on a topic of high clinical importance to the AGA membership and underwent internal peer review by the Clinical Practice Updates Committee and external peer review through the standard procedures of Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. This expert commentary incorporates important published studies in this field and reflects the experiences of the authors, who are interventional endoscopists with expertise in third-space endoscopy and endoscopic therapies for Zenker's diverticulum.

articles.title: From Training to Implementation: Building a Network of Pediatric Readiness Improvement and Simulation Mentors (PRISMs).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric emergency care coordinators (PECCs) are a crucial component in achieving high Pediatric Readiness Scores, but most community emergency departments struggle to adopt and sustain the role. We hypothesized that a structured PECC mentorship model would expand capacity to establish, train, and support PECCs.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study involved the training, implementation, and evaluation of Pediatric Readiness Improvement and Simulation Mentors (PRISMs) to support PECC implementation in community emergency departments across Texas and Michigan. PRISMs included experienced nurse PECCs recruited through regional nursing networks. With support from the study team, PRISMs guided PECCs in community emergency departments through pediatric readiness improvement using simulation as a key tool. Mixed-methods surveys combined with PRISM activity logs were used to capture the success and perception of the program.

RESULTS: In total, 37 PRISMs were hired (Texas: 31; Michigan: 6). PRISM training sessions were well-received and resulted in significant gains in self-efficacy. PRISMs engaged 262 community emergency departments, resulting in 515 simulations with 4025 total learners. PECC progression data were provided for 183 community emergency departments where 58.5% were beginning in this role, and only 4.9% had reached independence. Support from the study team and bi-weekly check-in meetings were reported as the most valuable aspects of the program.

DISCUSSION: PRISMs were successful in the initial engagement and education of PECCs, but few successfully mentored PECCs to independence within 1 year. The reported importance of study-team support and program meetings highlights the ability of a strong community of practice to support PECC implementation.

articles.title: 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: pilot study with fibroblast profiling.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is overexpressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), driving an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We report a prospective study integrating ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT with ex vivo CAF subset profiling in treatment-naïve NSCLC.

METHODS: 15 patients underwent 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT alongside standard-of-care imaging (Cohort 1: five surgical candidates; Cohort 2: ten advanced-disease patients). Standardised uptake values (SUV) were derived from primary tumour, lymph nodes, mediastinal blood pool (MBP), background lung and metastatic deposits. Plasma collagen remodelling biomarkers (PRO-C3, C3M, C3F, PRO-C11) were measured in 13 patients. Fresh tumour and adjacent non-cancerous lung tissue were samples following surgical resection (n = 5) to allow for CAF subset identification by flow cytometry.

RESULTS: 68Ga-FAPI PET demonstrated avid uptake in all primary tumours (SUVmax 3.97-14.01; mean 9.67 ± 2.84) with low background lung signal (SUVmean mean 0.68 ± 0.28; range 0.30-1.27), yielding good tumour-to-background ratios (TBR mean 16.88 ± 9.85; range 8.07-40). Compared with 18F-FDG PET-CT, 68Ga-FAPI upstaged two patients (previously undetected bone and retro-orbital metastases), but demonstrated discordant (negative 68Ga-FAPI) nodal signal in two further patients. Plasma collagen biomarkers were measurable but did not correlate significantly with 68Ga-FAPI SUV (Spearman r ≤ 0.44 for all markers). FAP high CAF subsets (S1 + S5) were higher in tumour compared with matched normal lung and CAF S5 correlates with SUVmax (r = 0.90, p = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: 68Ga-FAPI PET-CT is feasible and well-tolerated in NSCLC, provides complementary staging information to FDG PET-CT, and reflects tumour FAP biology as evidenced by ex vivo CAF subset enrichment.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET-CT provides complementary staging information to ¹⁸F-FDG PET-CT in treatment-naïve NSCLC and is shown to reflect intratumoral FAP biology directly. This prospective pilot study provides preliminary evidence that ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-46 PET-CT may act as a non-invasive marker of the fibroblast-rich tumour microenvironment in NSCLC, which requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Dairy-derived bioactive peptides in the regulation of obesity and type 2 diabetes: engineered production strategies, mechanisms and translational challenges.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in food science and nutrition
articles.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes are interrelated metabolic disorders and pose growing socioeconomic and clinical burdens. Although current pharmacotherapies, such as metformin and orlistat, are widely used, their long-term effectiveness may be constrained by side effects, poor compliance, and incomplete glycemic control in some patients. Hence, interest in food-derived peptides as sustainable dietary interventions for metabolic health has increased. Casein and whey proteins can generate peptides with potential anti-obesity and anti-diabetic activities by modulating digestive enzymes, incretin signaling, insulin sensitivity, and inflammation. However, evidence is predominantly from in vitro and animal studies, with limited human validation. Their clinical translation is further limited by bitterness, gastrointestinal instability, low bioavailability, and batch-to-batch variability. This review summarizes recent advances in peptide production, including fermentation, enzymatic hydrolysis, and synergistic production, and highlights mechanistic and translational challenges. The integration of AI and machine learning with advanced fermentation and enzymatic hydrolysis has, been reported to increase peptide yield and diversity. Engineering solutions, such as peptide self-assembly, nanoliposomes, nanofibers, and double-emulsion microencapsulation, may enhance peptide stability and delivery. Future research should prioritize AI-driven peptide discovery and improved delivery systems to enhance gastrointestinal stability and bioavailability, alongside rigorous standardized clinical trials to facilitate clinical translation of dairy-derived peptides.

articles.title: Vasopressin Versus Norepinephrine in Septic Shock: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials Focusing on Vasopressor Timing.
articles.abstract: Background and aimsThe optimal choice and timing of vasopressor therapy in septic shock remain uncertain. While norepinephrine is recommended as first-line treatment, vasopressin may offer potential benefits, particularly regarding renal outcomes. We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of vasopressin versus norepinephrine, with a focus on timing of initiation.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing vasopressin and norepinephrine in adult patients with septic shock. The primary outcome was short-term mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT), ICU length of stay, and serious adverse events. Random-effects models were used for the primary analyses, except for RRT, for which a fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel model was used because of concerns regarding small-study effects. Prespecified subgroup analyses evaluated initial randomized vasopressin strategy versus second-line vasopressin.ResultsSix randomized controlled trials including 1580 patients were analyzed. There was no significant difference in short-term mortality between vasopressin and norepinephrine (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.86-1.11; I2=0%). Vasopressin was associated with a significantly lower requirement for RRT (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.97; p = 0.016). No significant differences were observed in ICU length of stay (MD -0.18 days, 95% CI -2.30 to 1.94; I2=85.9%) or serious adverse events (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.76-1.50; I2=0%). Subgroup analysis showed a greater reduction in RRT with an initial randomized vasopressin strategy (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.50-0.84) than with second-line vasopressin (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.81-1.15), with a significant subgroup interaction (p = 0.014).ConclusionsVasopressin was associated with a reduced requirement for renal replacement therapy in patients with septic shock. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested a greater benefit with an initial vasopressin strategy compared with second-line vasopressin. No significant differences were observed in mortality, ICU length of stay, or serious adverse events.

articles.title: Association Between Hospital Performance and Care Delivery for out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract: IntroductionOut-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a leading cause of death worldwide, with substantial variation in survival between hospitals. Differences in post-arrest hospital care may explain this variation. We used a US national claims database to evaluate the association between increasing hospital performance and provision of care interventions.MethodsWe retrospectively studied the 2020-2022 National Emergency Department Sample database. OHCAs were defined by emergency department visits with: (1) an ICD-10 cardiac arrest diagnosis; or, (2) procedure codes for cardiopulmonary resuscitation. We included adult (age >18) patients with an associated hospitalization, excluding ED visits with a disposition of death. The main outcome was provision of hospital care interventions. Hospital performance quartiles were primarily defined by each hospital's proportion of OHCA patients surviving to hospital discharge. Using ordinal logistic regression, we evaluated the association between increasing hospital performance quartile and care intervention, accounting for patient demographics and year of cardiac arrest.ResultsAmong 192,207 patients treated at 1565 hospitals, survival to discharge was higher at top-quartile hospitals than bottom-quartile hospitals (46.0% vs 24.4%). Interventional cardiac procedures were associated with increasing hospital performance (left heart catheterization-aOR 2.0[1.8-2.1]; percutaneous coronary intervention-aOR 1.9[1.8-2.0]; ventricular assist device-aOR 1.8[1.7-2.0]; automatic implantable cardioverter defibrillator-aOR 2.2[2.1-2.4]; extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-aOR 3.3[2.4-4.5]; coronary artery bypass graft-aOR 2.4[2.1-2.7]). Arterial line placement (aOR 1.2[1.04-1.4]) and therapeutic hypothermia (aOR 1.5[1.1-2.3]) were also associated with increasing hospital performance quartile. Other interventions were not associated or were inversely associated with hospital performance: echocardiography, body imaging, head imaging, electroencephalogram, central lines, do not resuscitate orders.ConclusionInterventional cardiac procedures were consistently associated with increasing hospital performance quartile; arterial line placement and therapeutic hypothermia were associated only in our primary analysis. Diagnostic and neuroprognostication procedures were not associated with, or were inversely associated with, increasing hospital performance.

articles.title: Your network is your net worth: Membership in professional organizations helps innovate and saves lives.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract: Professional networking and active participation within organizations such as the ASPEN are critical drivers of clinical innovation and lifesaving patient care. This presidential address describes how human connection and peer-to-peer knowledge sharing bridge critical gaps in medical literature, directly accelerating the translation of bench research into bedside solutions. Drawing on a multi-decade career in nutrition support pharmacy at Boston Children's Hospital, ASPEN president Kathleen Gura shares three pivotal clinical scenarios that illustrate the power of the ASPEN network. Advancement of Lipid Emulsions: An international connection led to the first compassionate use of an intravenous fish oil lipid emulsion to treat essential fatty acid deficiency. This spark ignited 20 years of collaborative animal and clinical research, ultimately securing FDA approval for treating intestinal failure-associated liver disease. Global Health: Using ASPEN's drug shortage guidelines allowed an interdisciplinary team to resolve a critical pediatric multivitamin shortage in Vietnam as part of an educational effort leading to the advancement of nutritional care nationwide and ultimately the establishment of the Vietnamese Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (VietSPAN). Catheter Lock Solutions: Peer collaboration helped identify alternative catheter lock solutions to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs). When domestic regulatory shifts caused severe ethanol shortages, efforts were made to import 4% tetrasodium EDTA lock solutions under FDA compassionate use guidelines. These experiences demonstrate that solving complex clinical nutrition challenges requires a collaborative community. This address challenges the next generation of clinicians to actively engage, share unpublished insights, and utilize the collective expertise of the ASPEN infrastructure to optimize specialized patient care.

articles.title: Population Access to Medicare-Eligible MRI and PET 1 Year After Australia's 2025 Licensing Reform: A National Analysis With a Scenario for the 2027 Licence Removal.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Australia's Medicare MRI funding moved from machine-level licensing to practice-based eligibility on 1 July 2025, with licensing removal flagged for 2027. We measured access to Medicare-eligible MRI and PET approximately 1 year later and modelled what the 2027 removal could add through existing private MRI units.

METHODS: National cross-sectional geospatial study. All Commonwealth-registered Medicare-eligible MRI (420) and PET (139) practices (July 2026) were mapped and every address independently re-checked (81 corrected). Traffic-free drive times were computed on the national road network from the population-weighted centre of Australia's 60,453 smallest census areas (population 27,613,654). Access was stratified by jurisdiction, remoteness, Modified Monash town size and socioeconomic disadvantage, using adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs).

RESULTS: Nationally, 89.3% of Australians lived within a 30-min drive of Medicare-eligible MRI (94.9% within 60 min) and 88.8% within 60 min of PET (94.5% within 120 min). Thirty-minute MRI access fell from 93.0% in large rural towns to 35.4% in medium rural towns and 0.9% in very remote communities. Disadvantage showed a modest adjusted gradient (30-min MRI access 88.2% in the most disadvantaged decile vs. 93.1% in the least; PR per decile 1.005, 95% CI 1.002-1.008). If all 116 existing private MRI sites became eligible, 30-min coverage would rise by 0.3 percentage points, with essentially no change at 60 min.

CONCLUSION: One year post-reform, geographic access is high overall but ends abruptly beyond large rural towns; existing-unit eligibility would shift only a small, cut-off-sensitive fringe, while remote access needs both new scanners and sufficient regional workforce capacity to operate them.

articles.title: Accuracy and Treatment Experience of a Next-Generation Continuous Glucose Monitoring System in Children With Diabetes: A Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
AIM OF STUDY: To assess the diagnostic accuracy between the next-generation, factory-calibrated continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system and self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) measurements, and to evaluate user experience with the system in Saudi children with diabetes.

METHODS: We performed a diagnostic accuracy study of the next-generation Synchronized Artificial Intelligence System CGM system (Syai) more than 60 days. Sixty children aged 0 to 18 years with diabetes requiring insulin treatment wore the sensor on the upper arm, abdomen, thigh, or buttock for up to 14 days, followed by rotation to another site. Sensor performance was tested against SMBG. We reported the mean absolute relative difference (MARD) between CGM and SMBG measurement pairs, the proportion of CGM values meeting the 15/15, 20/20, and 30/30 agreement criteria.

RESULTS: The mean age of the children was 9.0 ± 4.4 years, and 30 (50.0%) were men. The average diabetes duration was 2.7 ± 2.8 years, mean hemoglobin A1c was 9.1 ± 1.8%, and time in range (70-180 mg/dL) was 50.5 ± 19.6%. A total of 238 sensors were worn for 60 days, providing 2364 paired CGM-SMBG measurements for agreement analysis from 52 participants, including 1480 pairs from the upper arm, 585 from the abdomen, and 299 from the buttock/thigh. The overall pair-weighted MARD was 11.74% (participant-cluster bootstrap 95% CI, 10.79%-13.05%). The overall 15/15, 20/20, and 30/30 agreement rates were 76.44%, 86.29%, and 94.92%, respectively. No serious adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSION: The Syai CGM system showed good accuracy with SMBG and a favorable user experience in this pediatric cohort.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) Clinical Trials Registry, http://www.sfda.gov.sa/en/node/3549755.

articles.title: Identifying subgroups of unmet needs in hospitalized stroke patients: A latent profile analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the latent profiles of unmet needs among stroke patients and examine characteristic differences across profiles. A total of 494 stroke patients were recruited through convenience sampling between May and October, 2023. The patients' unmet needs were assessed using the Chinese version of the Longer-term Unmet Needs after Stroke monitoring tool, which covers informational, physical, psychological, and social needs. Three distinct profiles emerged: low needs group, high information-focused needs group, and high functional and psychosocial needs group. Patients with lower incomes were more likely to belong to the low needs group than the high functional and psychosocial needs group. Those with greater functional disability, more severe depressive symptoms, and lower quality of life were more likely to be classified into the high functional and psychosocial needs group than the low needs group. These findings highlight the importance of stratified, evidence-based interventions tailored to different patient profiles.

articles.title: Parvalbumin Is Associated with Periodontitis-Abetted Tubular Injury in Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is a major form of chronic kidney disease caused by long-term diabetes, and it is characterized by progressive injury of glomerular and tubular compartments driven by metabolic and inflammatory stress. While clinical and epidemiologic studies have linked periodontitis with worse renal outcomes in diabetes, the molecular mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly defined. In this study, we examined whether ligature-induced periodontitis (LIP) can aggravate tubular injury in type 2 diabetic KK-Ay mice, and we explored the possible contributing factor and its related molecular mechanism in the progression of tubular injury. In KK-Ay mice, LIP exacerbated renal dysfunction, as indicated by increased expression of the tubular injury marker lipocalin 2, more pronounced interstitial fibrosis, increased macrophage infiltration, and disturbances in systemic electrolyte balance. Transcriptomic profiling of renal tubular fractions showed that LIP induced distinct gene expression changes in diabetic kidneys, with enrichment of pathways related to ion transport, calcium signaling, MAPK signaling, and diabetic metabolism. Among the most strongly upregulated genes, a calcium-binding protein parvalbumin (PVALB) was found to be a possible candidate mediator in tubular injury under diabetes. Immunofluorescent staining revealed that LIP enhanced PVALB expression mainly in the distal convoluted tubule in KK-Ay mice. In macrophage models (J774A.1 and THP-1), recombinant PVALB robustly induced IL-1β expression and secretion, particularly under hyperglycemic conditions. Mechanistically, PVALB activated NF-κB and p38 MAPK signaling via TLR2 and/or TLR4, leading to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, caspase-1 cleavage, and IL-1β maturation in J774A.1. Pharmacologic inhibition of caspase-1 significantly attenuated IL-1β secretion from J774A.1 and THP-1. These findings suggest that periodontitis aggravates tubular injury in diabetic nephropathy, and they identify PVALB as a potential mediator linking distal tubular injury to macrophage inflammasome activation.

articles.title: Antitumor Activity of CD54-Targeting Antibody-Drug Conjugates in Preclinical Models of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated malignancy with limited treatment options, particularly in advanced stages. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy, but the identification of optimal, highly expressed tumor-specific membrane targets for NPC remains a critical challenge. Through integrative multi-omics analysis, we identified CD54 as a candidate ADC target, validated its overexpression in NPC tissues and cell lines, and synthesized two CD54-directed ADCs (CD54-DXd and CD54-MMAE) to evaluate their therapeutic potential using in vitro assays and in vivo xenograft models. CD54 was consistently overexpressed in the NPC datasets and tissues examined, which was associated with advanced TNM stage, higher EBV DNA load, and poorer overall survival. Its expression was upregulated following EBV infection in vitro. Both CD54-ADCs exhibited potent and specific cytotoxicity against NPC cells in vitro and induced significant tumor regression in mouse models, with a favorable safety profile. In conclusion, these findings nominate CD54 as a compelling therapeutic target for NPC, supporting the further development of CD54-directed ADCs.

articles.title: Cath Lab Mortality Evaluation: A Methodical Approach in Accordance With Contemporary Best Practices at the World's Largest PCI Center.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Morbidity and Mortality Conferences (MMCs) are essential for enhancing quality in cardiac catheterization laboratories, yet their translation into actionable improvements is often limited. We share our experience with a system-based quality improvement (QI) initiative at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD) in Karachi, Pakistan, the world's largest primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) center, aimed at enhancing the quality of cath lab operations and patient care for high-risk South Asian patients with acute coronary syndrome.

METHODS: From October 2022 to September 2023, a structured MMC-QI framework was implemented to review all 463 cath lab mortalities (from 9265 primary PCIs and 2769 early invasive PCIs). Weekly multidisciplinary reviews by a cardiologist-led committee evaluated patient characteristics, procedural deficiencies, and system delays using standardized forms. Findings were categorized (e.g., technical errors, system inefficiencies) and informed targeted QI interventions, such as streamlined emergency department (ED) triage and enhanced PCI protocols. Descriptive statistics and subgroup analyses (age, gender) were conducted, with door-to-balloon (DTB) times compared pre- and post-intervention.

RESULTS: Of 463 mortalities (5.4% rate), 64.1% were male (mean age 61.8 ± 10.9 years), 76% had cardiogenic shock, and 87.5% died within 48 h. Key issues included suboptimal stenting (29%), no-reflow/slow-flow complications (22.5%), and inadequate technical approaches (13.2%). Unexpected mortalities (43%) were more common in females (p = 0.039), with higher diagnostic inadequacies (p < 0.001). QI interventions reduced technical issues (23% to 4.3%), procedural complications (33% to 15%), inadequate stenting (40% to 22%), and ED delays (33% to 18%). Median DTB time improved from 115 to 95 min (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Our experience with an MMC-QI framework demonstrates significant improvements in procedural quality, system efficiency, and care delivery in a high-volume PCI center. While mortality rates remained stable, this system-based approach offers a scalable model for high-burden settings, with potential for broader application pending further evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Insights Into Transplant Immunology and Syphilis Biology: A Single-Center Retrospective Study on the Follow-Up of Organ Recipients From Donors With Reactive Syphilis Serology.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Donor screening for syphilis and, if reactive, administration of therapy to solid organ transplant recipients is widely recommended and practiced. There is little evidence available on donor-derived syphilis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study. Solid organ transplant recipients of donors with reactive syphilis serology were monitored at post-transplant Months 3 and 6. Association between recipient CLIA reactivity and transplant-related variables was explored.

RESULTS: Between January 2020 and May 2024, organs from 31 syphilis-reactive donors were transplanted. Seventeen (27%) of 62 solid organ transplant recipients became CLIA reactive at post-transplant Month 3. Reactivity was independently associated with liver transplant and higher donor rapid plasma reagin (RPR) titer.

CONCLUSION: Asymptomatic CLIA reactivity is common after solid organ transplant from donors with reactive syphilis serology, particularly in liver recipients. Non-treponemal test reactivity was uncommon. The transmissibility of syphilis through organ transplant requires further elucidation.

articles.title: [Clinical utility of a two-step strategy combining the DiabetesLiver score and vibration-controlled transient elastography for liver fibrosis screening in community-dwelling patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Nanjing].
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical utility of a two-step strategy combining the DiabetesLiver score (DLS) and vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) for liver fibrosis screening in community-dwelling patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Nanjing. Methods: This prospective study enrolled 1 158 T2DM patients from 8 community health centers in Nanjing (Maigaoqiao, Xinjiekou, Taishan, Mufushan, Banqiao, Dingshan, Yuejianglou, and Lanyuan) between June and October 2025. Patients with DLS>3.99 were defined as high-risk for liver fibrosis and recommended for referral to a tertiary hospital for VCTE; those with DLS≤3.99 were permitted to undergo VCTE voluntarily.Patients were staged according to VCTE-derived liver stiffness measurement (VCTE-LSM): VCTE-LSM≤8.0 kPa indicates no or mild liver fibrosis (stage F0-F1); VCTE-LSM>8.0 kPa indicates clinically significant liver fibrosis (stage≥F2); VCTE-LSM>10.0 kPa indicates advanced liver fibrosis (stage≥F3); VCTE-LSM>15.0 kPa indicates liver cirrhosis (stage F4). The primary endpoint was the relative miss rate of the fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) among patients identified as high-risk for liver fibrosis by DLS and confirmed as≥F2 by VCTE. Results: A total of 1 158 T2DM patients were enrolled, of whom 147 were assessed as high-risk for liver fibrosis by DLS. Ultimately, 91 patients completed VCTE, including 83 DLS-assessed high-risk patients and 8 non-high-risk volunteers. VCTE findings showed that 57 patients were classified as stage F0-F1, and 34 patients as≥stage F2. Among the 34 patients confirmed to have≥F2 fibrosis by VCTE, 32(94.1%, 32/34) were identified as high-risk individuals for liver fibrosis according to DLS assessment. The 3 patients with VCTE-indicated F4 underwent further magnetic resonance elastography, all of which suggested cirrhosis. Among the 32 DLS high-risk patients with VCTE-confirmed≥F2, the miss rate with FIB-4 screening was 25.0% (8/32). Conclusions: Among community-dwelling patients with T2DM in Nanjing, DLS can be used for liver fibrosis risk stratification and to guide high-risk individuals to undergo further VCTE. The proportion of VCTE-confirmed≥F2 fibrosis among DLS high-risk patients was relatively high, whereas FIB-4 missed 25.0% of cases in this population, suggesting that the two-step strategy combining DLS and VCTE has potential for community-based liver fibrosis screening.

articles.title: [Regional brain iron deposition and its correlation to cognitive function in mild cognitive impairment according to amyloid-β status].
