articles.abstract: Objective: To compare the spatial distribution of brain iron deposition between amyloid-β-positive (Aβ+) and Aβ-negative (Aβ-) patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) using quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) and Aβ positron emission tomography (PET), and to examine the relationship between iron deposition and cognitive function. Methods: This retrospective study included 40 patients with MCI who attended the memory clinic at Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, between January and August 2024 and were enrolled in the Shanghai Memory Study cohort. Patients were classified as Aβ+(n=19) or Aβ-(n=21) based on visual assessment of Aβ PET images. All patients underwent QSM, Aβ positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI), and neuropsychological assessments. Regional QSM susceptibility values were compared between the 2 groups using independent-samples t tests or Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Partial Spearman correlation analysis was used to assess associations between QSM susceptibility values and Aβ PET standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR). Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and years of education were used to examine the associations between temporal lobe susceptibility values and cognitive function in each Aβ group. Analysis of the area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of logistic regression models and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to assess the discriminative performance and net benefit, respectively, of inferior temporal gyrus QSM, Aβ PET SUVR, and their combination for identifying Aβ+MCI. Results: Temporal lobe QSM susceptibility values were higher in the Aβ+group than in the Aβ-group [(0.15±1.23) ppb vs (-0.91±1.26) ppb, P=0.010]. Significant between-group differences were observed in the inferior temporal gyrus [(0.42±2.05) ppb vs (-1.62±1.68) ppb, P=0.001] and transverse temporal gyrus [(11.74±3.44) ppb vs (9.07±3.62) ppb, P=0.022]. QSM susceptibility values in the temporal lobe overall (ρpartial=0.44, P=0.006) and inferior temporal gyrus (ρpartial=0.40, P=0.013) were positively correlated with Aβ SUVR. In the Aβ+group, higher inferior temporal gyrus susceptibility values were associated with lower Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores (β=-1.03, PFDR=0.046) and lower scores for attention (β=-0.33, PFDR=0.044), language (β=-0.83, PFDR=0.013), and visuospatial function (β=-1.03, PFDR=0.046). These associations were not statistically significant in the Aβ-group. The areas under the AUC for inferior temporal gyrus QSM, Aβ SUVR, and the combined model were 0.782, 0.902, and 0.912, respectively. DCA showed that the Aβ PET SUVR model and the combined model provided greater net benefit than the QSM model across most threshold probabilities. Conclusions: Patients with Aβ+MCI had greater temporal lobe iron deposition than those with Aβ-MCI. Temporal lobe iron deposition was positively associated with Aβ burden. Among patients with Aβ+MCI, greater inferior temporal gyrus iron deposition was associated with poorer cognitive function.

articles.title: [Current status of diabetic foot care in China: a multicenter cross-sectional study based on real-world data from a diabetic foot specialty alliance].
authors: Yangtze River Delta Integrated Diabetic Foot Specialty Alliance
articles.abstract: Objective: To characterize diabetes-related foot care in China using multicenter real-world data from the Yangtze River Delta Integrated Diabetic Foot Specialty Alliance. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using hospitals as the units of analysis. All alliance member hospitals that met the eligibility criteria and completed data submission were included. Data for 2024 were collected using a standardized, structured questionnaire developed by the alliance. The questionnaire covered outpatient and inpatient care for diabetes and diabetic foot disease, including visit and admission volumes, mean cost per admission, mean length of stay, major amputation counts, and in-hospital mortality, as well as the availability of surgery-related resources. Hospitals were categorized by tier (tertiary, secondary, or primary) and geographical location. Patterns of care were compared across hospital tiers and regions. Multivariable linear regression was used to examine associations of resource availability with clinical outcomes and healthcare resource utilization. Results: A total of 453 hospitals across 14 provincial-level administrative regions in China were included. Tertiary hospitals accounted for the largest proportion (216/453, 47.68%), followed by secondary (130/453, 28.70%) and primary hospitals (107/453, 23.62%). Of these, 76 (16.78%) were located in northern China and 377 (83.22%) in southern China. Endocrinology was the lead department for diabetic foot care in 314 hospitals (69.32%). Participating hospitals reported 9.673 8 million outpatient visits and 1.202 1 million inpatient admissions for diabetes, with total medical expenditure of CNY 10.008 1 billion. Diabetic foot disease accounted for a small proportion of diabetes-related outpatient visits (1.31%, 0.127 0 million/9.673 8 million) and inpatient admissions (3.29%, 0.039 6 million/1.202 1 million), but a larger proportion of medical expenditure (7.13%, CNY 713.1 million/CNY 10 008.1 million) and inpatient days (5.30%, 0.486 6 million/9.174 4 million). This pattern was more pronounced among the 216 tertiary hospitals, where the hospital-level proportions of diabetes-related expenditure and inpatient days attributable to diabetic foot disease averaged 21.32%±0.43% and 13.66%±0.29%, respectively. The major amputation rate and in-hospital mortality rate were 2.5% (993/39 340) and 0.2% (76/39 340), respectively.For both diabetes and diabetic foot disease, outpatient visit volume, inpatient admission volume, and mean cost per admission were highest at tertiary hospitals, followed by secondary and primary hospitals (all P<0.05). For diabetes care, inpatient admission volume was higher in northern hospitals, whereas mean cost per admission was higher in southern hospitals. For diabetic foot care, inpatient admission volume, major amputation rates, and in-hospital mortality rates were higher in northern hospitals (all P<0.05). The availability of surgery-related resources, including digital subtraction angiography, magnetic resonance imaging, interventional operating rooms, and intensive care units, was not significantly associated with major amputation or in-hospital mortality rates but was positively associated with hospitalization costs and length of stay (all P<0.05). Conclusions: Diabetes and diabetic foot care involve substantial medical expenditure. Care volume, costs, and surgery-related resource availability vary markedly across hospital tiers. Regional differences are also evident in inpatient admission volume, major amputation rates, and in-hospital mortality rates.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of nocturnal enuresis in children in primary medical and health institutions (2026 edition)].
authors: Pediatric Urodynamics and Pelvic Floor Group, Pediatric Surgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Association
Greater Bay Area Society of Pediatric Urology and Continence
articles.abstract: Nocturnal enuresis is a common paediatric disorder that seriously impairs children's physical and mental health as well as the quality of family life. Primary medical and health institutions undertake core responsibilities including early screening and identification, initial standardized treatment, long-term continuous follow-up and tiered referral for childhood nocturnal enuresis, serving as a key frontline for the full-cycle prevention and management of this condition. To further standardize the diagnostic and therapeutic workflows and chronic disease management system of childhood nocturnal enuresis in primary-care settings across China, the Pediatric Urodynamics and Pelvic Floor Group, Pediatric Surgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Association together with the Greater Bay Area Society of Pediatric Urology and Continence (GBASPUC), convened experts in relevant disciplines. On the basis of the latest domestic and international evidence-based medical data, and considering the current status of primary-care resources and clinical characteristics in China, the experts systematically addressed core issues such as the scope of primary-care-oriented nocturnal enuresis management, early identification and classification, essential assessment items and minimum examination standards, initial therapeutic regimens for monosymptomatic and non-monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis, management of comorbidities, reassessment of treatment response, criteria for tiered referral, long-term follow-up strategies and a three-level prevention framework. Nine expert recommendations were finally formulated, aiming to provide reference for primary-care practitioners to implement standardized and practical diagnosis, treatment and full-cycle management of childhood nocturnal enuresis.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on blood pressure and vascular assessment and multidisciplinary management of adult Takayasu arteritis (2026 edition)].
authors: Rheumatology Branch of Chinese Women′s Medical Association
Rheumatism Committee of Chinese Association of Integrative Medicine
Rheumatology Branch of Shanghai Medical Association
articles.abstract: Takayasu arteritis-related hypertension (TARH) is common and often refractory, leading to severe target organ damage involving the heart, brain, kidneys, and major vessels, which significantly impacts patient prognosis and is a major cause of death in patients with Takayasu arteritis. However, there is currently no unified consensus on systematic evaluation and standardized management in clinical practice. To address this, the Zhongshan Hospital of Fudan University took the lead, in collaboration with the Rheumatology Branch of Chinese Women's Medical Association, Rheumatism Committee of Chinese Association of Integrative Medicine, Rheumatology Branch of Shanghai Medical Association, and multidisciplinary experts from across China. On the basis of the "Chinese multidisciplinary recommendations on the diagnosis and treatment of Takayasu's arteritis-related hypertension" published in 2021, this consensus has been updated to address key issues in TARH, including epidemiology, definition, early identification and comprehensive assessment of high-risk populations, antihypertensive drug therapy, and revascularization, with 16 core clinical questions identified. Through evidence retrieval and multiple rounds of discussion and voting, 28 recommendations have been formulated. This consensus aims to standardize clinical decision-making in TARH, improve blood pressure control rates, reduce target organ damage, and improve the long-term prognosis of Chinese TARH patients.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on imaging diagnosis of comorbid pulmonary tuberculosis and lung cancer (2026 edition)].
authors: Radiology Professional Committee on Infection and Inflammation of the Chinese Research Hospital Association
Beijing Image Diagnosis and Treatment Technology Innovation Alliance
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis and lung cancer are major global health threats. China faces the dual burden of a prevalent tuberculosis epidemic and high incidence of lung cancer. These two diseases exhibit complex mutual reinforcement relationships, with both demonstrating high prevalence rates and clinical complexity in practice. Due to the similar clinical symptoms and easily confused imaging manifestations, diagnosis and treatment decision-making become more challenging. There is an urgent need for standardized imaging diagnostic consensus to guide clinical practice. To address this, Radiology Professional Committee on Infection and Inflammatory of the Chinese Research Hospital Association and the Beijing Image Diagnosis and Treatment Technology Innovation Alliance organized multidisciplinary experts to develop the Expert consensus on imaging diagnosis of comorbid pulmonary tuberculosis and lung cancer (2026 edition), which outlines 11 recommended guidelines. The consensus emphasizes the central role of integrated diagnosis combining clinical data, imaging findings, etiology, and pathology, recommends low-dose spiral CT for lung cancer screening in tuberculosis patients, and preliminarily defines the value and application scenarios of multimodal imaging (CT, MRI, PET-CT) and artificial intelligence in coexisting disease diagnosis, aiming to enhance the level of imaging diagnosis for tuberculosis-lung cancer comorbidity in clinical practice.

articles.title: [Guidelines for gender-affirming hormone therapy in adults (2026 edition)].
authors: Gonadology Group, Endocrine and Metabolism Branch, Chinese Medical Doctor Association
articles.abstract: Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) involves the use of exogenous medications to modify sex hormone levels in patients with disorders of sex development (DSD) or gender incongruence (GI), aligning them with the individual's psychological gender identity and promoting the development of sex characteristics. Properly administered GAHT helps the patients achieve or approach physical and psychological congruence, improve self-acceptance, and enhance mental health and quality of life. With the accumulation of clinical experience in China in the past decade, GAHT protocols have been gradually developed to better suit China's national conditions. The Gonadology Group, Endocrine and Metabolism Branch of Chinese Medical Doctor Association invited multidisciplinary experts, including endocrinology, gynecology, urology, plastic surgery, reproductive medicine, psychiatry and medical ethics into a guideline development panel. Based on the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE), the guidelines have been developed around the basic requirements, medication protocols, safety, and ethical considerations of GAHT in adults with DSD or GI. Using the modified Delphi method and incorporating input from patient representatives, the expert panel issued 20 recommendations for 11 key clinical questions. This guideline aims to standardize GAHT practices in China and provide clinical guidance to improve the physical and mental health of adults with DSD or GI.

articles.title: [Twenty years of continuous glucose monitoring research: from technological breakthrough to conceptual innovation].
articles.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) is a transformative and innovative technology that has shifted glucose monitoring from single-point measurements to continuous, dynamic, and visualized assessment. Over the past two decades, CGM has evolved from retrospective monitoring to real-time and intermittently scanned systems and subsequently to integration with automated insulin delivery systems. In parallel, a dynamic glucose assessment framework centered on time in range (TIR) has gradually been established. This CGM-centered framework has reshaped the paradigm of glycemic management. Meanwhile, the application of CGM is expanding beyond the assessment of glycemic control to the identification of risks of long-term adverse outcomes and the characterization of digital metabolic phenotypes, with the potential to support precision interventions for diabetes. This article reviews the evolution of CGM technology and its assessment framework, discusses its clinical applications in diabetes, pregnancy, inpatient care, and special populations, and examines current challenges, including technical standardization, insufficient evidence regarding long-term outcomes, and the underutilization of high-dimensional data. Future directions, including extended-wear and noninvasive sensors, multimodal monitoring, and artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine, are also discussed. The future value of CGM lies not simply in generating more data, but in translating continuous glucose data into clinically meaningful information that can improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: [Epidemiology and complications of type 1 diabetes mellitus in China: current status, challenges and future perspectives for prevention and management].
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by a low population-level incidence coexisting with a substantial absolute disease burden in China. Recent estimates indicate that China ranks third globally in the number of individuals living with T1DM. This article reviews the current epidemiology of T1DM and its complications in China, discusses existing challenges, and explores future prevention and cotrol strategies, with the aim of improving T1DM management and patient outcomes. Key features include a high proportion of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) at diagnosis among children and adolescents; a large proportion of adult-onset cases among newly diagnosed patients; a heavy burden of chronic complications in hospitalized patients; and increasingly recognized psychosocial impairment, together with rising health economic costs. Compared with European and North American countries, China still has substantial gaps in T1DM research, including long-term patient registries, complication follow-up cohorts, prognosis improvement for adult-onset patients, real-world evidence generation, and health economic evaluation. Future T1DM prevention and control strategies in China should move beyond insulin monotherapy toward an integrated approach encompassing early screening of high-risk populations, precision stratification, systematic management, comprehensive complication prevention, and whole-lifecycle care, to reduce acute complications, improve long-term prognosis, and alleviate the overall disease burden.

articles.title: Molecular diagnostic testing variation and outcomes in pediatric complicated pneumonia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Staphylococcus aureus is estimated to cause <10% of pediatric complicated community-acquired pneumonia (cCAP) cases, yet >70% receive empiric methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA)-directed antibiotics. Molecular diagnostic testing (MDT) improves pathogen detection compared with culture; however, its impact on antibiotic stewardship and outcomes remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To (1) describe national variation in MDT use among children hospitalized with cCAP and (2) compare length of stay (LOS), MRSA-directed antibiotic exposure, and costs across testing strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of children 2 months to 18 years of age hospitalized with cCAP (2021-2024) using the Pediatric Health Information System database. MDT was classified as broad-array (multiplex polymerase chain reaction [PCR] or sequencing-based modalities) or single-target (PCR assays for Streptococcus pneumoniae or Staphylococcus aureus). Because culture use was nearly universal, hospitals were grouped by high versus low broad-array and single-target MDT use, generating four groups via K-means clustering. Generalized estimating equations assessed associations between testing group and outcomes, adjusting for payor, intensive care unit admission, and illness severity.

RESULTS: Among 2994 hospitalizations at 43 hospitals, 98.5% had blood or pleural cultures, 26.2% broad-array MDT, and 44.2% single-target MDT. MRSA-directed antibiotic use ranged from 67% to 93% across the four groups. Compared with hospitals with low broad-array/low single-target MDT, those with low broad-array/high single-target MDT use had lower MRSA-directed antibiotic exposure (risk ratio [RR]: 0.34, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.17-0.67; p = .002). LOS and costs did not differ among groups.

CONCLUSION: Low broad-array/high single-target MDT use was associated with reduced MRSA-directed antibiotic exposure without differences in LOS or costs. Prospective studies should evaluate MDT-guided antibiotic optimization.

articles.title: Chronic Total Occlusions and Their Relationship With Ventricular Function and Arrhythmia.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Chronic total occlusions (CTOs) are common and have an estimated prevalence of 20% in patients with coronary artery disease. Their presence has been associated with worse outcomes in both stable coronary artery disease and acute coronary syndromes, including a higher incidence of ventricular arrhythmias and impaired left ventricular function. A bidirectional relationship exists between left ventricular impairment and ventricular arrhythmias: left ventricular impairment increases the risk of ventricular arrhythmias, and ventricular arrhythmias can further depress left ventricular function. Despite these relationships, there has been minimal evidence demonstrating a clear prognostic benefit of revascularization, and current guidelines recommend revascularization of CTOs primarily for refractory angina. This review aims to describe the relationship between CTOs, ventricular arrhythmias, and left ventricular function and evaluate the current evidence on whether revascularization can reduce ventricular arrhythmia risk or improve left ventricular function.

articles.title: Reconsidering Cementum Biology: A Continuum Framework for Updated Understanding of Cementum Formation and Function.
articles.abstract: Cementum is essential for tooth attachment to periodontal ligament and bone, and the formation of new cementum is required for tissue regeneration after destruction by periodontitis. Despite its central role in oral health, cementum biology is relatively undefined compared with other mineralized tissues. For decades, cementum biology has been informed by its classification into subtypes, which are based on differences in cellularity and the presence and orientation of intrinsic collagen fibers. But the fixed traits implied by these classifications are now being challenged by new molecular, developmental, and pathological data. Proteomic analyses indicate extensive overlap in the protein repertoires of cementum and bone, suggesting limited molecular distinction across cementum subtypes. Developmental studies show that cementoblast activity can adapt to mechanical loading, suggesting that the form and function of cementum are not fixed but sensitive to environmental stimuli. In animal models, cementogenesis is suppressed by infection, inflammation, and metabolic stress. These processes can be reversed by restoring physiological regulation of inorganic pyrophosphate and tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase or by rescuing the function of sirtuin 3 or the transcription factor CXXC-type zinc finger protein 5. Arising from these data on how cementum metabolism is regulated by inflammatory signaling and by interactions between immune and progenitor cells, we propose a "continuum framework." In this proposal, the structural characteristics of cementum emerge from context- and environment-dependent regulatory influences rather than from predetermined subtypes that are fixed at early stages of root and cementum development. This proposal reconsiders cementum biology based on a continuum framework that complements existing classifications and could suggest new perspectives to resolve questions in cementum regulation, which is critically important for periodontal repair and regeneration.

articles.title: Association of outpatient waiting time with pain intensity and coping strategies in patients with nonspecific chronic low back pain scheduled for physiotherapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Waiting time in an outpatient clinic is an essential component of health care. However, there is limited evidence on the association of outpatient waiting time (OWT) with pain intensity and coping strategies in patients with nonspecific chronic low back pain (NSCLBP) scheduled for physiotherapy.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association of OWT with pain intensity and coping strategies of catastrophizing, diverting attention, reinterpretation, and cognitive coping in patients with NSCLBP.

METHODS: The study was a prospective observational design that consecutively recruited 60 patients (30 males, 30 females) with NSCLBP at a teaching hospital. Patients' sociodemographic and physical characteristics were collected. OWT during patients' second physiotherapy treatment visit was measured with a digital stopwatch from arrival to before treatment. Patients' pain intensities were assessed on arrival, before, and after treatment using a visual analog scale, while coping strategies were assessed on arrival and after treatment using the Coping Strategies Questionnaire-24. Patient satisfaction was assessed using a 0-100 scale. Data were summarized with descriptive statistics and analyzed with multiple regression, Spearman's correlation, Wilcoxon test and chi-square with significance at p < .05.

RESULTS: Patients' catastrophizing on arrival (β = -0.69, p < .001) and marital status (β = 0.23, p = .009) were associated with OWT. OWT negatively correlated with catastrophizing on arrival (ρ=-0.78, p < .001). Although pain intensity increased significantly (p < .001) before treatment (5.82 ± 1.35 to 6.34 ± 1.42), it decreased after treatment (2.98 ± 1.56). Catastrophizing, reinterpretation, and cognitive coping increased significantly (p < .05) after treatment. A significant association (χ2 = 9.11, p = .028) was found between OWT and patient satisfaction with treatment.

CONCLUSION: Patients' catastrophizing on arrival and marital status are associated with OWT. While catastrophizing on arrival negatively associates with OWT, marital status positively associates with OWT. Although pain intensity increases during OWT, multimodal physiotherapy intervention is likely to improve pain intensity, catastrophizing, and reinterpretation in patients with NSCLBP. These findings highlight the importance of minimizing delays in outpatient physiotherapy visits.

articles.title: Second-to-Third-Trimester Progression of Fetal Urinary Tract Dilation and Childhood Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To identify sonographic predictors of chronic kidney disease (CKD) at ages 1, 3 and 5 years in children with mild second-trimester urinary tract dilation (UTD) that progressed to severe third-trimester dilation.

METHOD: Retrospective cohort study at a tertiary fetal CAKUT (congenital anomaly of the kidney and urinary tract) clinic; prenatal data from January 2015 to September 2020, with follow-up through May 2026. Ninety-four fetuses were analyzed. CKD was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min/1.73 m2 confirmed ≥ 3 months apart from age 1 year. K1 denoted the more affected kidney (wider anterior-posterior renal pelvic diameter), and K2 the contralateral kidney. Predictors were identified using Firth-penalized logistic regression with leave-one-out cross-validation.

RESULTS: CKD developed in 15 of 94 children (16%) followed for a median of 8.7 years (IQR 7.4-10.2); all were male with bilateral involvement. Within the bilateral subgroup (n = 38), parenchymal abnormality of the less-affected kidney (K2) and bladder abnormality were the two independent predictors of CKD on Firth multivariable regression (K2 parenchymal OR 7.48, 95% CI 1.13-49.35; bladder OR 9.60, 95% CI 1.49-61.68), achieving an apparent AUC of 0.872 and a leave-one-out cross-validated AUC of 0.806.

CONCLUSION: Fetuses with mild second-trimester UTD that progress to severe third-trimester UTD carry a clinically significant risk of early-childhood CKD. Third-trimester findings of the less-affected kidney may support prenatal risk stratification, pending external validation in an independent cohort.

articles.title: Phenotyping of cardiac pathologies in Afro-caribbeans: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) claims 18.6 million lives annually worldwide. Caribbean nations are particularly vulnerable to CVDs, as by Western standards they are largely comprised of racial/ethnic minorities and classified as Low-and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs); with race/ethnicity and socioeconomics affecting health outcomes. Cardiac pathology phenotypes (morphologic descriptions) can guide targeted diagnostics and therapeutics, yet despite this, there exists paucity of literature on Afro-Caribbean cardiac pathologies. This scoping review mapped existing cardiac pathology phenotyping literature across thirteen predominantly Black Caribbean nations and the diaspora; summarizing existing data, identifying gaps and setting the stage to prioritize future CVD cohort studies to reduce Afro-Caribbean under representation in the medical literature.

METHODS: This review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Four academic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Bireme - Latin America and the Caribbean Literature on Health Sciences), and Google Scholar were queried with predefined search terms to obtain articles in English between 1990 - 2025, with Afro-Caribbeans from 13 nations or diaspora (United States of America (USA), Europe or Canada), with cardiac pathology phenotyping data derived from ECG, imaging or autopsy.

RESULTS: Forty studies featuring 17 cardiac foci across 9 countries were identified with the United Kingdom (UK) having the most (13). Seventeen were cross-sectional, 9 prospective cohorts, 6 retrospective cohorts, 5 retrospective case series, 1 prospective case series, and 2 case-control studies. Foci included left ventricular structure/function (9), heart failure (6), peripartum cardiomyopathy (4), ischemic heart disease (4), transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (3), valvulopathies (2), cardiorenal disorders (2), and miscellaneous (10). Sample sizes ranged from N = 15 to 5329, with N ≥ 100 in 22 of the 40 studies. Phenotyping utilized echocardiography (31), ECG (13), stress echocardiography (1), CT angiography (1), coronary angiography (2), cardiac MRI (1), and transesophageal echocardiography (2).

CONCLUSIONS: A review of literature on cardiac pathology phenotypes in Afro-Caribbean populations was performed, demonstrating paucity of large, prospective studies and use of advanced imaging, resulting in scarcity of data. Future work should prioritize multicenter cohorts, standardized multimodal imaging, and longitudinal follow-up to describe phenotypes and regional epidemiology and potentially guide resource allocation.

articles.title: Cardiac troponin I removal during continuous renal replacement therapy: a potential role for membrane adsorption.
Subcutaneous versus intravenous insulin in managing patients with cardiogenic shock: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stress hyperglycemia is common in cardiogenic shock (CS) and has been consistently linked to adverse outcomes, yet how it should be treated remains unsettled. Current guidance favors intravenous insulin in hemodynamically unstable patients because subcutaneous absorption becomes unpredictable under hypoperfusion, but this recommendation rests largely on pharmacokinetic reasoning rather than on outcome data. Whether the choice of route translates into a prognostic difference in CS is therefore unknown. We compared 30-day, 90-day, and 360-day all-cause mortality between patients with CS initially managed with subcutaneous versus intravenous insulin.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV (version 3.0; 2008-2022). Patients with CS were identified by ICD-9 code 785.51 and ICD-10 code R57.0; we excluded those younger than 18 years or receiving no insulin. The exposure was the initial route of insulin administration, and endpoints were all-cause mortality at 30, 90, and 360 days. The primary analysis used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models, with 1:1 propensity score matching (caliper 0.05) and inverse probability of treatment weighting performed as complementary analyses using different strategies to address confounding. Because treatment was allocated by clinical judgment rather than randomization, we calculated E-values to gauge robustness to unmeasured confounding and repeated the analysis in a 24-h landmark cohort to address immortal time bias, complemented by subgroup, sensitivity, and mediation analyses.

RESULTS: Of 1,782 eligible patients with CS, 1,147 received subcutaneous insulin and 635 received intravenous insulin; mortality reached 42.3% at 30 days, 49.3% at 90 days, and 56.3% at 360 days. Patients in the intravenous group died less often throughout follow-up (35.1% vs. 46.2%, 39.8% vs. 54.5%, and 44.3% vs. 63.0%; all p < 0.001). In the primary multivariable Cox analysis, the association persisted after full adjustment (hazard ratios [HRs] 0.719, 0.700, and 0.659), and complementary propensity score matching (0.749, 0.714, 0.672) and inverse probability of treatment weighting (0.789, 0.760, 0.706) yielded consistent estimates, as did landmark restriction (0.684, 0.655, 0.624). E-values of 2.13, 2.21, and 2.40 for the point estimates, and 1.61, 1.72, and 1.93 for the confidence limits closest to the null, indicated moderate robustness, and no prespecified subgroup showed effect modification; benefit was greatest when insulin was started within 3 h of admission or continued beyond 1 day. Mechanistically, the intravenous group had higher glucose before treatment yet lower post-treatment mean glucose, maximum glucose, and glycemic variability, and mean glucose mediated 24.1%, 16.0%, and 11.0% of the association. This glycemic advantage came at a cost, however, as intravenous insulin was associated with more hypoglycemia after adjustment (odds ratio [OR] 1.623) and after matching (OR 1.609).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with CS, initial intravenous insulin administration was associated with lower mortality at 30, 90, and 360 days but with a higher risk of hypoglycemia. Because clinicians, rather than a protocol, selected the route, and because data on insulin dose and glycemic targets were unavailable, confounding by indication cannot be excluded despite E-value and landmark analyses. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish the superiority of either route.

articles.title: Hsp20-Promoted Protective Protein Aggregation Drives Stress Tolerance Heterogeneity in Bacteria.
articles.abstract: Phenotypic heterogeneity in stress tolerance among isogenic bacterial cells fundamentally impacts the efficiency and robustness of microbial bioprocesses while fostering persistent infections, yet its underlying regulatory mechanisms remain elusive. Here, by integrating single-cell RNA-sequencing with microfluidic time-lapse tracking, we discovered small heat shock protein Hsp20 as a central regulator of acid-tolerance heterogeneity. Strikingly, contrary to its canonical role as a holdase to prevent protein aggregation, Hsp20 actively promotes the formation of protective protein aggregates that sequester transcription and metabolic proteins to inactivate gene transcription and metabolism. Hsp20-promoted aggregates drive cells into varying depths of dormancy, regulating the trade-off between stress tolerance and post-stress recovery of single cells. Hsp20 enhances cellular tolerance at the expense of recovery capacity, an aspect that has rarely been systematically reported. Moreover, Hsp20-regulated protection extends broadly to heat, oxidative, and bile salt stresses, revealing a generalizable strategy for stress adaptation. Our work broadens the roles of small heat shock proteins in cytoplasmic protective aggregation during the microbial stress response and provides a mechanistic link between transcriptional noise and phenotypic heterogeneity. It offers a new theoretical basis for understanding the survival strategies of prokaryotes and for precision control in microbial industry and epidemic control.

articles.title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Head and Neck Cancer: Integrated Evidence From TCGA Genomic Analysis and a US Multicenter Database Study.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a risk factor for head and neck cancer (HNC), but the effects of antidiabetic drugs on this risk are unclear. We evaluated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) using the TriNetX US electronic health record database, while investigating the molecular role of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) in HNC. Adults ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed T2DM (2012-2024) were studied retrospectively. Among > 250 million records, 105,605 GLP-1RA users were propensity-score matched 1:1 with 105,605 nonusers. Over a median 5-year follow-up, GLP-1RA use was associated with significantly lower risks of incident HNC (HR: 0.723; 95% CI: 0.617-0.848) and all-cause mortality (HR: 0.737; 95% CI: 0.715-0.759). Results remained consistent across sex, age, obesity, smoking, alcohol use, GLP-1RA type, and further sensitivity analyses. Molecular analyses showed that higher GLP1R expression was associated with better overall survival in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (TCGA-HNSC). GLP1R expression progressively decreased from normal to tumor and metastatic tissues, correlated with oncogenic mutation status, and was inversely associated with cell-cycle programs. In an independent multi-institutional biobank (Tri-VGH Biobank), GLP1R expression was significantly lower in tumor than matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (27 pairs), findings confirmed by tumor immunofluorescence. Overall, these epidemiological and molecular findings support a potential protective role of GLP-1RA/GLP1R signaling in HNC.

articles.title: Co-exposure to tobacco smoke and ambient air pollution in relation to asthma exacerbations: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tobacco smoke (TS) exposure and ambient air pollution are important triggers of asthma exacerbations, but their combined effects remain poorly understood. We investigated whether co-exposure to TS and ambient air pollutants was associated with asthma exacerbations in the U.S.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 5,780 participants aged ≥ 3 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005-2006. Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and ozone (O3) exposures were estimated using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Community Multiscale Air Quality modeling system. Serum cotinine was used as a biomarker of TS exposure. Asthma exacerbations were assessed by self-reports of asthma-related emergency care visits in the previous 12 months. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine associations between asthma exacerbations and co-exposures to the air pollutants and to assess additive interactions.

RESULTS: Among participants with current asthma (8.9%), 17.7% reported asthma-related emergency care visits. Co-exposure to TS and elevated ambient NO2 levels was associated with higher odds of asthma emergency care visits [odds ratio (OR) = 2.78, 95% CI:1.11-6.92] but only among children. Although no additive interactions were identified for PM2.5 or O3, TS and elevated PM2.5 co-exposure was associated with asthma visits among children (OR = 2.92, 95% CI:1.13-7.56).

CONCLUSIONS: Co-exposure to TS and ambient air pollution (elevated NO2, PM2.5) was associated with asthma-related emergency care visits among U.S. children. These findings underscore the importance of reducing both TS and ambient air pollution exposures to reduce the burden of asthma, especially in children.

articles.title: Reconsidering futility after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
Pediatric Lemierre's syndrome caused by Streptococcus intermedius: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lemierre's syndrome is a rare but life-threatening condition classically caused by Fusobacterium necrophorum. Although members of the Streptococcus anginosus group have been reported as uncommon pathogens, this is, to our knowledge, the first reported pediatric case of Lemierre's syndrome caused by Streptococcus intermedius. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges associated with an atypical microbiologic etiology.

CASE PRESENTATION: A previously healthy 12-year-old male presented to the emergency department with 8 days of fever, headache, and right-sided neck pain following recent travel. On arrival, he was tachycardic and ill-appearing with meningismus, prompting evaluation for meningitis. Computed tomography (CT) of the neck revealed a non-occlusive thrombus of the right internal jugular vein, while a subsequent lumbar puncture was unremarkable. Further evaluation with chest CT demonstrated multiple pulmonary nodules, including a cavitary lesion. Blood cultures grew S. intermedius. The constellation of internal jugular vein thrombosis, septic pulmonary emboli, and bacteremia established the diagnosis of Lemierre's syndrome. The patient was treated with intravenous antibiotics followed by oral therapy without anticoagulation, resulting in clinical and radiographic improvement, normalization of inflammatory markers, and resolution of the internal jugular vein thrombus.

CONCLUSIONS: This report expands the recognized microbiologic spectrum of pediatric Lemierre's syndrome by identifying S. intermedius as a causative pathogen in what may be the first reported pediatric case. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for Lemierre's syndrome in children presenting with persistent fever and unilateral neck pain, even in the absence of ongoing pharyngitis, as early imaging, blood cultures, and prompt targeted antimicrobial therapy are critical for favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Five-Year Survival and Its Determinants Among Women With Breast Cancer in the Algerian Wilaya of Batna: A Population-Based Cancer Registry Study.
articles.abstract: In Algeria, 5-year survival for breast cancer (BC) has improved over the past three decades, but drivers of the remaining survival deficits need to be assessed. Within the population-based cancer registry of Batna, northeastern Algeria, we assessed survival (overall and net) and its determinants among women diagnosed with BC during 2010-2012. Vital status was retrospectively ascertained through hospital and civil registration data, as well as telephone calls, whilst sociodemographic and clinical data were extracted from medical records. In total, 366 women were included; mean ± SD age at diagnosis was 48 ± 12 years. Clinical-epidemiologic data were available for 302 (83%). After 5 years, 68/366 (19%) women had died, 278 (76%) were alive, and 20 (5%) were lost to follow-up, rendering 5-year overall survival of 81% (95% CI: 76, 85) and net survival of 84% (80, 88). After mutual adjustment, TNM Stage III/IV (n = 169/284, 60%) accounted for 55% of deaths, while suboptimal treatment (no surgery, 24%, or no chemotherapy, 4%, or no radiotherapy, 31%) accounted for an additional 22%. Diabetes was also associated with higher mortality, based on a small sample. These findings indicate relatively high five-year survival after BC diagnosis; nevertheless, survival gains through earlier BC detection and improving access to comprehensive BC treatment could further reduce deaths in this setting.

articles.title: A Photoelectrically Activated Neural Stem Cell Matrix for Nerve Repair.
articles.abstract: Stem cell therapy for nerve injury requires a local environment that supports cell delivery and regulates neurotrophic output. An injectable PN-junction-based biomimetic neural matrix (PNBM) integrates silicon PN-junction microfragments and neural stem cells within a thermoresponsive hyaluronic acid-methylcellulose-laminin hydrogel. Under 635 nm illumination, the microfragments generate reproducible photovoltages and amplify intracellular calcium responses. Compared with light alone, PN-junction photoactivation reduces first-spike latency by 91% and increases firing frequency 3.45-fold. Transcriptomic analysis identifies  phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) pathway enrichment, while protein assays demonstrate increased secretion of nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, and glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor. In noncontact cocultures, photoactivated PNBM increases process extension and burst frequency in HT22 hippocampal cells and promotes Schwann cell alignment and myelin basic protein expression. In rats with optic nerve crush, treatment preserves retinal structure, reduces the astroglial lesion response, and improves visual evoked potentials. In sciatic nerve crush, it improves locomotor performance, motor electrophysiology, axon-myelin organization, and gastrocnemius preservation. PNBM couples semiconductor photoactivation to enhanced stem cell trophic output and provides a locally delivered bioelectronic matrix for central and peripheral nerve repair.

articles.title: Event Analysis after Caries Arrest with Silver Diamine Fluoride in Adults.
articles.abstract: The objectives of this retrospective analysis of longitudinal clinical treatment records from the US Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) were to determine whether teeth treated with silver diamine fluoride (SDF) to arrest a cavitated or noncavitated carious lesion required subsequent caries-related extraction/root canal therapy or direct/indirect restoration and whether 2 or more applications of SDF were more effective than 1 application. Inclusion criteria were Veterans eligible for continuing/comprehensive dental care, with at least 1 tooth treated with SDF (CDT code = D1354), a minimum 1-y follow-up time following index SDF, and were VA dental service patients for at least 1 y prior to index SDF. Multiple applications of SDF on a tooth and multiple teeth per veteran were included. Demographic covariates were age, sex, race, and ethnicity. Medical covariates included medical complexity/illness burden, prescription medication burden, and use of medications with strong anticholinergic properties. Dental covariates were the dentist's clinical assessment of xerostomia, receipt of in-office applied fluoride, and count of caries-related restorations in the year prior to index SDF treatment. Cox proportional hazards-based regression models for repeated data on teeth clustered within patients were used to allow for inclusion of time-dependent cumulative SDF treatments and to identify factors predictive of time to failure and estimate their associations with the outcomes. The analyses included 66,199 SDF-treated teeth in 20,833 Veterans. Most teeth (69%) received 1 SDF application, 19% received 2 SDF applications, and 12% received 3+ SDF applications. For teeth with multiple applications, the median time between applications was 180 d. Seventy-five percent of teeth survived (mean follow-up = 3 y); 7% failed due to caries-related extraction/root canal therapy (mean follow-up = 1.5 y) and 18% due to direct/indirect restoration (mean follow-up = 1 y). Multiple SDF applications versus 1 application decreased the hazard by 90% for extraction/root canal therapy and 98% for direct/indirect restoration, demonstrating clinically meaningful caries arrest in adults.

articles.title: Emerging pharmacological therapies for hereditary hemochromatosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hereditary hemochromatosis (HH) is a genetic disorder characterised by excessive intestinal iron absorption, progressive iron accumulation and organ damage, including cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Therapeutic phlebotomy remains the mainstay of treatment, effectively removing excess stored iron and helping prevent progression of liver disease. However, its effects on symptoms and extrahepatic manifestations remain incompletely established. This review examines advances in understanding the hepcidin-ferroportin axis and their implications for novel pharmacological therapies for HH.

METHODS: This narrative review discusses the molecular mechanisms underlying HH and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the hepcidin-ferroportin axis.

RESULTS: Since the identification of the HFE gene in 1996, advances in understanding mammalian iron metabolism have clarified the role of disrupted hepcidin-ferroportin signalling in HH. These discoveries have identified therapeutic targets, including hepcidin replacement, TMPRSS6 inhibition and ferroportin inhibition. Therapies targeting these pathways offer potential approaches to addressing the underlying dysregulation of intestinal iron absorption.

CONCLUSION: Improved understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying HH has enabled the development of novel approaches to managing iron overload. Further clinical evaluation is required to establish their long-term efficacy, safety and role alongside therapeutic phlebotomy.

articles.title: Anesthetic considerations for obstetric patients with an implanted spinal cord stimulator.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of anaesthesia = Journal canadien d'anesthesie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Implantable spinal cord stimulators (SCSs) for the treatment of refractory neuropathic pain are becoming increasingly common in patients presenting for surgery, and their presence has important implications for anesthetic care. This is particularly relevant in obstetric anesthesia, where neuraxial techniques are routinely employed for labour analgesia and anesthesia for Cesarean delivery. In this Continuing Professional Development module, we synthesize the available case experience from the literature and provide practical recommendations to guide anesthesiologists in the perioperative management of obstetric patients with an SCS.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Numerous case reports describe the safe use of both epidural and spinal anesthetic techniques in obstetric patients with an SCS. All obstetric patients with an SCS should undergo antenatal consultation with an anesthesiologist and neuromodulation specialist (usually a pain medicine physician or neurosurgeon) responsible for managing the device. Preprocedural planning, including review of relevant imaging and a focused physical examination, is essential to minimize the risk of device damage. Ultrasound can be used to assist the provider in identifying a safe neuraxial access point and may also help to improve first-pass success. The literature suggests that prior implantation of SCS components within the epidural space may be associated with a higher risk of SCS lead movement, potential for infection, and inadequate epidural labour analgesia and surgical anesthesia. In contrast, the success of spinal anesthesia for Cesarean delivery appears largely unaffected by the presence of neurostimulation leads. In patients undergoing Cesarean delivery, management considerations include temporary device inactivation, minimizing the use of monopolar cautery, and being familiar with the course of the device's leads from the impulse generator to the stimulating electrode to avoid inadvertent surgical damage.

CONCLUSIONS: Neuraxial anesthesia is feasible and generally safe for obstetric patients with an SCS but requires careful planning and awareness of unique risks. Antenatal anesthesiology and neuromodulation consultation, imaging review, ultrasound guidance, and patient counselling can help optimize outcomes and minimize complications.

articles.title: Epidemiological and genetic investigation of a Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia outbreak in kidney transplant recipients: consistent with patient-patient and healthcare-associated transmission.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PjP) is a severe opportunistic infection in transplant recipients. Increasing evidence supports interhuman transmission, particularly in healthcare settings.

METHODS: We investigated a cluster of PjP cases among kidney transplant recipients at the outpatient clinic of a Swiss tertiary hospital between September 2024 and June 2025. Clinical, radiological, microbiological, and epidemiological data were collected. Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) was performed on available respiratory samples. Overlaps in patient visits were analyzed to reconstruct potential transmission events. Environmental and ventilation characteristics were also assessed.

RESULTS: Seven patients were identified, accounting for 7.5% (7/94) of the kidney transplant recipient cohort. All presented with exertional dyspnea and oxygen desaturation; five had dry cough, and four reported weight loss and subfebrile states. Chest computed tomography (CT) showed bilateral ground-glass opacities with lobular sparing. All cases were microbiologically confirmed by bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL). MLST was available in four patients and showed an identical P. jirovecii genotype in all four. Reconstruction of clinic attendance revealed repeated same-day overlaps among affected patients in shared clinical areas. The shared waiting area had an airflow of 100 m3/h, corresponding to 3.08 air changes per hour, and its windows could not be opened. Following implementation of combined preventive measures, no additional PjP cases were identified through October 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support possible airborne transmission of P. jirovecii in an outpatient setting and highlight the critical role of environmental and organizational factors in outbreak dynamics.

articles.title: Flow-mediated dilation and carotid intima-media thickness in primary hyperparathyroidism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) and cardiovascular (CV) risk remains unclear. Endothelial dysfunction and arterial wall thickening are early markers of CV risk. We performed a systematic review to evaluate (a) the association between PHPT and these vascular parameters, assessed by flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT), and (b) the impact of parathyroidectomy on these outcomes.

METHODS: Studies assessing FMD and/or cIMT in PHPT were retrieved from Embase and MEDLINE up to November 2025 (PROSPERO: CRD420251076642). Risk of bias was evaluated using Cochrane criteria. Mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed with the I² statistic. Analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.4.1.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine observational studies (1,152 PHPT patients and 1,773 healthy controls) were included. PHPT patients had significantly lower FMD (MD -6.44, 95% CI: -9.80, -3.08; P = 0.0002; I2 = 98%) and higher cIMT (MD 0.07, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.11; P < 0.0001; I2 = 86%) than controls. Following parathyroidectomy, FMD improved (MD 5.88, 95% CI: 1.77, 9.99; P = 0.005; I2 = 97%), reaching values comparable with controls (MD -1.27, 95% CI: -3.48, 0.94; P = 0.26; I2 = 69%); cIMT decreased (MD -0.05, 95% CI: -0.08, -0.02; P = 0.004; I2 = 71%), with values not different from controls (MD 0.01, 95% CI: -0.02, 0.03; P = 0.62; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: PHPT is associated with endothelial dysfunction and arterial wall thickening, suggesting increased CV risk. FMD and cIMT significantly improve after parathyroidectomy.

articles.title: Long-term metabolic and biochemical outcomes of pasireotide LAR in resistant acromegaly.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pasireotide long‑acting release (PAS‑LAR) is a second‑generation somatostatin receptor ligand approved for patients with acromegaly resistant/intolerant to first‑generation analogues or combination medical therapy. Real‑world evidence on its metabolic impact and tumour response remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long‑term efficacy, metabolic safety, and tumour effects of PAS‑LAR in a real‑life cohort of acromegalic patients.

METHODS: This was a single-centre, retrospective observational study conducted at a tertiary endocrine centre in Romania. Thirty acromegalic patients previously treated with first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands (fg-SRLs) ± pegvisomant ± cabergoline were switched to PAS-LAR ± cabergoline. Data were collected at baseline, after 3- and 6-months of PAS-LAR treatment, and at the last available visit (median 36.5 months).

RESULTS: Thirty patients (66.7% female; mean age 44.4 ± 12.0 years) were treated with PAS-LAR for a mean duration of 44.4 ± 31.2 months. IGF-1 xULN decreased from 1.64 ± 0.79 at baseline to 0.99 ± 0.44 at the last visit (p < 0.0001), with strict disease control (IGF-1 xULN ≤ 1.0) achieved in 60.0% of patients. Acceptable biochemical control (IGF-1 < 1.3 xULN) increased from 26.7% to 76.7% (p < 0.001). Random GH decreased from 4.26 ± 5.38 to 1.58 ± 1.43 ng/mL (p < 0.001). Median HbA1c increased from 5.65% (IQR 5.50-5.90) to 6.20% (IQR 6.03-6.88; p < 0.001). New-onset diabetes occurred in 9/24 (37.5%) patients without diabetes at baseline. At the last evaluation, HbA1c was ≥ 7.0% in 6 patients (20.0%). In exploratory analyses, higher diagnostic IGF-1 xULN correlated with greater increases in FPG (rho = 0.562, p = 0.001) and HbA1c (rho = 0.555, p = 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Exploratory analyses suggested that higher IGF-1 levels at diagnosis may be associated with greater glycemic deterioration during follow-up. This potential association requires confirmation in larger cohorts. Hyperglycemic events are frequent but largely manageable with standard antidiabetic therapy. Lipid parameters remain stable or improve slightly. Early glucose monitoring should be standard during PAS‑LAR therapy.

articles.title: Conservative management of piriformis syndrome: a systematic review of rehabilitation approaches and clinical outcomes.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To synthesize available evidence on the effectiveness of conservative rehabilitation strategies for piriformis syndrome, emphasizing pain reduction and functional improvement.

METHODS: Conducted per PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251154880), this review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and PEDro for studies published between January 2015 and 2026. Eligible designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized studies and case reports on rehabilitation interventions. Risk of bias and methodological quality were assessed using Cochrane RoB2, ROBINS-I, and the Downs and Black checklist. Evidence certainty was evaluated via the GRADE framework in accordance with SWiM guidelines. Due to heterogeneity, data were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Forty-two studies (1,971 participants) met the inclusion criteria. Multimodal rehabilitation programs generally yielded better outcomes than single-modality approaches. Manual therapies, specifically myofascial release and muscle energy techniques, were more effective than stretching alone for pain and functional recovery. Exercises emphasizing hip abductor and extensor strengthening were crucial for successful management. In refractory cases, adjuncts like extracorporeal shockwave therapy, ultrasound-guided dry needling, and botulinum toxin injections provided potential benefits for sustained pain reduction. However, overall evidence strength remained limited due to small, heterogeneous studies with high or unclear risk of bias.

CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports an active, multimodal rehabilitation approach for piriformis syndrome, prioritizing targeted manual therapy and strengthening exercises. While promising, the evidence base is limited by methodological shortcomings. High-quality, adequately powered RCTs with standardized protocols are required to establish definitive clinical recommendations.

articles.title: Phage SSB-bound ssDNA triggers allosteric activation of the bacterial defense system PD-T7-3.
articles.abstract: To survive persistent viral predation, bacteria deploy diverse abortive infection (Abi) systems that trigger cell death to halt phage propagation. Many such systems rely on toxic HEPN-domain endoribonucleases that must be strictly restrained during homeostasis. However, the mechanisms ensuring their latent autoinhibition and precise activation remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize PD-T7-3, an Abi system that comprises a single polypeptide with an N-terminal HEPN domain and a C-terminal sensory domain. Ultrastructural analyses show that PD-T7-3 forms a latent dodecameric complex, autoinhibited by an intrinsic hairpin loop that occludes the RNase active site. Unexpectedly, activation is triggered by single-stranded DNA acting as an allosteric ligand, which strictly requires potentiation by the phage-encoded single-stranded DNA-binding (SSB) protein T7 Gp2.5. This mechanism is insulated against host interference, as the host SSB protein fails to trigger nuclease activation. Our findings reveal a prokaryotic immune strategy that exploits viral replication machinery to license toxic effector RNases, establishing a distinct regulatory mechanism for self-versus-nonself discrimination.

articles.title: Left atrial appendage occlusion versus DOACs in atrial fibrillation: beyond device versus drug.
articles.abstract: Recent randomized trials have broadened interest in left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. Their interpretation requires attention to differences in patient populations, medical comparators, outcome definitions, and noninferiority margins. This commentary examines PRAGUE-17, OPTION, CHAMPION-AF, and CLOSURE-AF alongside recent meta-analyses to inform patient selection and shared decision-making. Reductions in nonprocedural bleeding reported in several trials must be weighed against procedural complications, post-implant treatment requirements, and uncertainty about ischemic stroke protection. CHAMPION-AF highlights the distinction between composite noninferiority and individual component outcomes, particularly when observed event rates are substantially lower than anticipated. CLOSURE-AF's failure to establish noninferiority cautions against assuming that high bleeding risk alone identifies patients who benefit from implantation. DOACs remain central to stroke prevention in eligible patients, while LAAO provides an alternative for selected patients with contraindications to long-term anticoagulation or recurrent major bleeding despite optimization. Selection should incorporate procedural risk, life expectancy, tolerance of post-implant antithrombotic therapy, follow-up capacity, and informed patient preferences. Proposed patient profiles require validation, and comparative economic value remains uncertain. Future research should prioritize transparent component reporting, clinically justified noninferiority margins, and identification of patients most likely to benefit. Clinical decisions should match patients to complete treatment pathways through shared decision-making.

articles.title: Indobufen in OPTION and INSURE: does background P2Y12 inhibition explain the difference?
articles.abstract: The graphic proposes that partial COX-1 inhibition by indobufen is sufficient with P2Y12 blockade but insufficient without it. In OPTION, 4,551 patients undergoing elective PCI received indobufen on top of clopidogrel. The net endpoint was 4.47% versus 6.11%, driven by less bleeding. In INSURE, 5,438 patients with acute ischemic stroke received indobufen alone. Recurrent stroke was 7.9% versus 6.4%, and indobufen failed to meet non-inferiority at 90 days.

articles.title: Construction of murine atrial thrombosis models.
articles.abstract: To establish and characterize a murine model of atrial thrombosis induced by electrical stimulation (ES). Twenty-one male C57BL/6J mice (20-30 weeks old, body weight ≥ 25 g) underwent thoracotomy. The exteriorized atrium was subjected to ES via a sheathed needle inserted 2-4 mm into the atrial cavity. Gradient stimulation parameters (5 mA or 10 mA; 1-2 min duration) were tested (n = 5 in each group), with a sham group for comparison (n = 3) and a pre-treated anticoagulation group with enoxaparin (n = 3). Transthoracic echocardiography, gross anatomical examination, Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E), and Martius-Scarlett-Blue (MSB) staining, were applied to evaluate thrombus formation. CD31 immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to assess alterations of the atrial endocardial endothelium. These mice were used to assess short-term (≤ 1 h) model success rate. An additional 30 mice were used to assess long-term (1-7 days post-ES) model success rates of LA and RA (n = 15 in each group ). ES reliably induced intra-atrial thrombus formation. The short-term thrombus-formation success rate reached 10% for both the left atrium (LA) and right atrium (RA). The long-term success rate was 26.7% for LA thrombosis and 86.7% for RA thrombosis. Pre-treatment with enoxaparin effectively suppressed thrombus generation. CD31 expression in the atrial endocardium was higher in ES‑stimulated mice relative to control mice. Direct intracavitary ES produces a reproducible mouse atrial-thrombosis model with distinct LA and RA long-term outcomes. This model supports mechanistic investigation and therapeutic testing for atrial-thrombosis-related diseases.

articles.title: The distal landing zone and technical success of chronic total occlusion PCI: determinants and complexity-score performance in a multicenter gulf registry.
articles.abstract: Technical success is required for any clinical benefit from percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) of a chronic total occlusion (CTO). CTO complexity scores were developed in different populations and for different procedural endpoints, and their performance in Gulf practice is not well defined. We evaluated the pre-procedural determinants of CTO PCI success, with particular attention to the distal landing zone, and compared three established complexity scores in the same cohort. We analyzed 420 patients undergoing CTO PCI in the multicenter Gulf CTO registry (seven tertiary centers in four countries, 2021-2023). The primary outcome was technical success, defined as TIMI grade 3 flow with < 30% residual stenosis; procedural success was the co-primary outcome. J-CTO, PROGRESS-CTO, and a registry-based reconstruction of RECHARGE were evaluated against technical success and compared with DeLong's test for correlated receiver operating characteristic curves. Because J-CTO was originally developed for guidewire crossing within 30 min, this comparison addresses discrimination for technical success rather than performance against each score's original endpoint. Technical success was achieved in 327 of 420 patients (77.9%), and procedural success in 314 (74.8%). Four lesion characteristics were independently associated with technical success: a good distal landing zone (odds ratio [OR] 5.14, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.88-9.17), blunt (OR 0.35, 0.18-0.67) and ambiguous (OR 0.25, 0.13-0.50) proximal cap morphology relative to a tapered cap, any calcification (OR 0.47, 0.28-0.81), and moderate-to-severe tortuosity (OR 0.32, 0.13-0.83). No baseline clinical characteristic was independently associated with success. For prediction of technical success in this cohort, the registry-based RECHARGE reconstruction had a C-statistic of 0.708 (95% CI 0.647-0.768), compared with 0.657 (0.595-0.719) for J-CTO and 0.553 (0.484-0.623) for PROGRESS-CTO. Re-weighting the five J-CTO components did not improve optimism-corrected discrimination (0.662 to 0.644); adding a good distal landing zone increased it to 0.715. In this multicenter Gulf cohort, CTO PCI success was driven primarily by lesion anatomy, with distal landing-zone quality showing the strongest association. A score containing a distal-vessel component showed greater discrimination for technical success in this dataset, but the three scores were developed for different endpoints, and the RECHARGE variable was reconstructed retrospectively. The clinically important finding is therefore not that one score is intrinsically superior, but that systematic pre-procedural assessment of the distal vessel appears to add meaningful information beyond conventional lesion-complexity features.

articles.title: scBiopsy-seq as a highly sensitive platform for temporal single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis.
articles.abstract: The development of temporal single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) assays enables systematic investigation of the effects of various types of perturbations in a time course with single-cell resolution. However, the existing temporal scRNA-seq technologies have certain limitations in reliability, detection efficacy and detection diversity. Here we develop the scBiopsy-seq assay, which combines synergistic electroosmosis and electrophoresis for efficient RNA extraction and digital microfluidics with a hydrophobic interface for high-performance sample processing. scBiopsy-seq can detect over 10,000 genes per extraction of cytoplasm with a ~96% success rate. scBiopsy-seq can perform sequential extraction of the cytoplasm from the same cell multiple times, enabling the association of a cell's phenotypic responses with its transcriptional dynamics. We used scBiopsy-seq to analyze response dynamics to virus infection or transcriptional suppression at single-cell resolution. scBiopsy-seq, which generates data with similar quality to that of scRNA-seq, will dramatically expand the application of temporal scRNA-seq toward a broader spectrum of biological research.

articles.title: Hospital-Based Doula Programs in the United States: A National Environmental Scan of Program Availability and Characteristics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the prevalence and structure of hospital-based doula programs in the United States.

STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We conducted a national environmental scan of United States hospitals offering labor and delivery services. Doula program characteristics including model type, eligibility, and cost were summarized using descriptive statistics.

DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: Hospital lists were compiled from state health department records and cross-referenced with a national Medicaid-participating hospital registry. Of 2470 hospitals identified, websites were searched using hospital names and the term "doula" and manually reviewed. Hospitals mentioning doula services (n = 244) comprised the analytic sample.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: 9.9% of hospitals (244/2470) mentioned a doula program. Prevalence was highest in the Northeast (19.5%) and West (15.0%), and lowest in the Midwest (7.4%) and South (3.2%). Five program models were identified: Affiliated Doula Programs, Hospital-Employed Programs, Community-Based Organization (CBO) Partnerships, Volunteer Programs, and Research Initiatives. Affiliated doula networks (33.6%) and hospital-employed doulas (25.4%) were most common. Eligibility criteria included insurance status, income, race, or clinical risk. Forty-six percent were free; cost was unclear for 45%. Most hospital websites (66.5%) did not mention doulas.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospital-based doula programs are uncommon and vary widely. Limited website information may hinder patient awareness and access, particularly among those who could benefit most.

articles.title: Post-translational modification networks in ischemia-reperfusion injury: from molecular crosstalk to precision intervention.
articles.journal: Apoptosis : an international journal on programmed cell death
articles.abstract: Ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a severe pathological consequence triggered by events such as myocardial infarction and stroke, frequently resulting in multiple organ dysfunction and systemic inflammatory response. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) have recently attracted increasing attention as pivotal regulators of the cellular response to IRI. This review elucidates the dual roles of PTMs in this pathological process. Specifically, well-characterized modifications, including phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitination, critically mediate cellular damage by promoting cell death, exacerbating inflammatory responses, and impairing mitochondrial function. Conversely, PTMs also exert protective effects by modulating autophagic activity, enhancing anti-oxidative stress capacities, and facilitating tissue repair mechanisms. Building upon these mechanistic insights, this review further explores the potential clinical applications of PTM-targeted modulators and individualized therapeutic strategies within the context of precision medicine. Despite these advances, challenges remain. The complex crosstalk among different PTMs remains largely uncharacterized, and developing regulators with precise target specificity presents significant technical hurdles. Moreover, the inherent heterogeneity among patients underscores the critical need for individualized therapeutic approaches to ensure safe and effective clinical translation. Collectively, PTMs do not function as isolated modification events but rather constitute a spatiotemporally dynamic regulatory network whose dual (damaging versus protective) roles are determined by modification type, specific site, temporal window, and organ context; a systematic understanding of this network will establish a solid theoretical basis for the precise intervention of IRI, ultimately bridging the gap between fundamental discoveries and clinical applications.

articles.title: Predicting Energy Expenditure and Metabolic Tolerance for Medical Nutrition Therapy in Neurocritical Care: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical nutrition therapy (MNT) is a key determinant of outcome in critically ill patients, as both underfeeding and overfeeding are associated with unfavorable outcome. Optimal energy provision should consider both resting energy expenditure (REE) and the extent of catabolism to match the exogenous energy delivery to the patient's net demand and thereby maintain metabolic tolerance. Hence, we aimed to evaluate (1) the accuracy of predictive equations (PEs), (2) metabolic tolerance, and (3) REE in patients with acute brain injury.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, single-center observational cohort study including mechanically ventilated neurocritical care patients with an expected intensive care unit stay of ≥ 10 days. REE was measured repeatedly using indirect calorimetry (IC) at predefined time points (days 0-10) and compared with commonly used PEs. Metabolic intolerance was defined as hypophosphatemia (< 0.65 mmol/L) and/or insulin requirement > 1 U/h. Multivariable mixed-effects models were used to identify predictors of metabolic intolerance and intraindividual REE variability.

RESULTS: A total of 52 patients with 317 IC measurements were included. The Harris-Benedict formula showed the highest agreement among all tested equations, yet only 59% of estimates fell within 85-115% of measured REE. In patients with obesity (body mass index > 30 kg/m2), PEs showed clinically relevant bias (> 200 kcal). Metabolic intolerance occurred in 32% of observations and was independently associated with higher body temperature and higher proportions of administered relative to prescribed calories, while female sex was associated with lower risk. In mixed-effects models, resolving organ dysfunction disease severity was associated with greater REE variability (β = -44.1; 95% confidence interval, - 75.7 to - 12.6; p < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: In neurocritical care patients, REE is highly dynamic and cannot be reliably estimated using PE, supporting the use of IC for energy assessment. Changes in disease severity may serve as a pragmatic trigger for reassessment. Overfeeding, male sex, and higher body temperature were associated with metabolic intolerance, underscoring the importance of precise energy assessment. Future studies should evaluate IC-guided, metabolic-tolerance-directed nutritional strategies to improve clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Implant survival and the impact of inflammatory arthritis on revision risk following primary total knee arthroplasty: an 11-year single-center analysis.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate implant survival following primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) over an 11-year period at a tertiary referral centre in the eastern Black Sea region of Türkiye, and to identify independent risk factors for revision, with particular attention to inflammatory arthritis (IA).

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 3,364 patients who underwent primary TKA between 2015 and 2025 were identified from institutional records. The primary outcome was all-cause revision. Implant survival was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared between groups with the log-rank test. Deaths (n = 83) were treated as competing events; cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator, and multivariable cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were fitted using four prespecified covariates (age, sex, IA, and diabetes mellitus). Firth penalized-likelihood regression was used as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: The median follow-up was 3.8 years, and 44 patients (1.31%) underwent revision. Kaplan-Meier institutional revision-free survival was 99.7%, 98.4%, and 97.6% at 1, 5, and 10 years, respectively. Patients with IA had significantly lower survival than those with osteoarthritis (10-year survival 91.7% vs. 97.7%; log-rank p = 0.012). IA was associated with an increased risk of revision in the cause-specific Cox model (hazard ratio 3.25, 95% CI 1.16-9.10; p = 0.025), with concordant estimates from the Fine-Gray and Firth models; this association, however, rested on four events and was statistically fragile (fragility index 1). On chart review, revisions in the IA group were predominantly attributable to aseptic loosening (three of four). Age, sex, and diabetes mellitus were not independently associated with revision.

CONCLUSION: Over an 11-year calendar period with a median individual follow-up of 3.8 years, institutional revision-free survival was high (97.6% at 10 years). Inflammatory arthritis was associated with a higher revision risk, driven predominantly by aseptic loosening; given the small number of events, this should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating signal. Preoperative rheumatological optimisation may represent a modifiable pathway warranting prospective study.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III (retrospective prognostic cohort study).

articles.title: Anti-obesity medications in people with kidney disease: a review.
articles.abstract: Obesity accelerates progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), worsens cardiovascular risk and limits access to kidney transplantation. This narrative review summarises current evidence for anti-obesity medications in CKD. Traditional therapies provide modest weight loss and carry safety limitations, whereas incretin-based agents, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide, achieve substantial weight reduction with emerging renal benefits. Evidence remains limited in advanced CKD and dialysis populations.

articles.title: Progressive SLAMF7 downregulation is associated with terminal CD8 T-cell exhaustion and aggressive disease in renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: T-cell exhaustion is a dysfunctional state under persistent antigenic stimulation in chronic viral infections and tumors. Although immune checkpoint blockade can reinvigorate exhausted T cells, responses remain limited, emphasizing the need to better understand exhaustion.
