SLAMF7 is an immune-regulatory receptor, but its regulatory and functional role during CD8 + T-cell exhaustion remains unclear. Here, we reported that SLAMF7 was absent in naïve mouse and human CD8 T cells but was induced upon in vitro activation. Following acute lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, all effector and memory subsets expressed SLAMF7, with higher levels in more differentiated cytolytic populations. Under persistent antigenic stimulation, including chronic LCMV infection, murine tumor models, human renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and non-small cell lung cancer, SLAMF7 was highly expressed in progenitor and transitory exhausted subsets but downregulated in PD-1hi terminally exhausted cells. This downregulation coincided with increased inhibitory receptor and TOX expression, attenuated cytotoxic and polyfunctional responses, and progressive epigenetic remodeling toward terminal exhaustion-associated chromatin programs. Furthermore, SLAMF7 deficiency impaired CD8 + T-cell expansion and antitumor activity. Across models, SLAMF7 downregulation was more closely associated with prolonged antigen exposure than with antigen burden. In RCC patients, SLAMF7-based stratification revealed distinct immunological states: SLAMF7-HI tumors retained progenitor-like CD8 T cells with preserved effector function, whereas SLAMF7-DN tumors were enriched for terminally exhausted cells and associated with high nuclear grade. Collectively, these findings identify SLAMF7 downregulation as a marker of terminal CD8 T-cell exhaustion and suggest its potential as a biomarker of immune competence and disease severity.

articles.title: Mechanisms of kidney protection by semaglutide in type 2 diabetes and CKD.
Advances in GLP-2 research: mechanisms and therapeutic applications.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide 2 (GLP-2) is a proglucagon-derived peptide that is co-secreted with GLP-1 from intestinal endocrine L cells. The best-characterized actions of GLP-2 are its trophic and anti-inflammatory effects within the gastrointestinal tract. A GLP-2 analogue, teduglutide, has been utilized for the treatment of short bowel syndrome for over a decade, yet the actions and therapeutic potential of GLP-2 beyond the gut remain underexplored. GLP-2 exerts cardioprotective, hepatoprotective and immunomodulatory effects in preclinical studies, and circulating levels of GLP-2 correlate with the extent of tissue injury and sepsis in humans. GLP-2 also reduces gallbladder emptying and inhibits bone resorption. The actions of GLP-2 are transduced through a single GLP-2 receptor, which is expressed both within and external to the gut, including in the central nervous system, where its activation is associated with improved glucose homeostasis, attenuation of obesity-associated neuroinflammation and neuroprotection. In this Review, we highlight advances in our understanding of the effects of GLP-2 within and beyond the gut, highlighting the translational relevance of potential new indications and innovations in GLP-2 therapeutics, while discussing limitations and gaps in the existing data.

articles.title: Optimal blood pressure levels for preventing bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation aged under 75 years receiving anticoagulant therapy stratified by concomitant antiplatelet therapy: a large-scale real-world data study (F-CREATE project).
articles.journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract: Using a large-scale, real-world database from Japan, this study stratified atrial fibrillation (AF) patients receiving anticoagulation therapy by the use of concomitant antiplatelet agents to determine the optimal blood pressure (BP) levels for minimizing bleeding risk. This Japanese retrospective cohort study utilized linked administrative claims and health checkup records from multiple insurance societies. Among the 4039 anticoagulated patients with AF aged under 75 years included in the analysis, 3267 received single antithrombotic therapy (SAT: anticoagulant only), while 772 received dual antithrombotic therapy (DAT: anticoagulant + one or more antiplatelet agents). BP was classified into normal/high normal BP (<130/80 mmHg), elevated BP (130-139/80-89 mmHg), and grades I/II/III hypertension (≥140/90 mmHg). Co-primary outcomes were intracranial bleeding and extracranial bleeding. During a mean follow-up period of 3.03 years, 23 intracranial and 114 extracranial bleeding events were observed among patients receiving SAT. During a mean follow-up period of 3.02 years, 10 intracranial and 38 extracranial bleeding events were observed among patients receiving DAT. The incidence rates of intracranial bleeding (per 100 person-years) were highest among patients with grades I/II/III hypertension receiving DAT (1.07%), followed by patients with grades I/II/III hypertension receiving SAT (0.39%). The incidence rates were lowest among patients with normal/high normal BP receiving SAT (0.10%) and DAT (0.08%). Extracranial bleeding showed no clear association with BP levels in patients receiving either SAT or DAT. In this real-world study of patients with AF aged under 75 years receiving anticoagulation therapy, the optimal BP for minimizing intracranial bleeding was <130/80 mmHg, regardless of concomitant antiplatelet use.

articles.title: Highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic and polygenic diseases from spent medium.
articles.abstract: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases.

articles.title: Chronological Clinicopathological Evolution of Acquired Idiopathic Generalized Anhidrosis Following COVID-19 With Concurrent Diffuse Alopecia and Erythroderma.
articles.abstract: Acquired idiopathic generalized anhidrosis (AIGA) is a rare disorder characterized by generalized thermoregulatory sweating impairment without an identifiable cause. In Japan, it is designated as an intractable disease. We report the case of a 50-year-old man who developed generalized erythroderma followed by diffuse alopecia and complete (100%) generalized anhidrosis after COVID-19 infection. Despite treatment with corticosteroid pulse therapy and cyclosporine, the anhidrosis remained refractory and persisted during a 2-year follow-up period, whereas alopecia and erythroderma gradually improved. Sequential skin biopsies were performed at three distinct time points: before clinically recognized anhidrosis, during the established anhidrotic stage, and at the 2-year follow-up. The findings revealed a dynamic pathological progression in the sweat duct and secretory coil. Before clinically recognized anhidrosis, there was marked lymphocytic infiltration, predominantly involving the sweat ducts rather than the secretory coils, accompanied by intraepithelial lymphocyte infiltration and ductal epithelial cell apoptosis. In the established anhidrotic stage, marked secretory coil atrophy with collapse of the normal bilayered secretory architecture was observed. Outer secretory cells (clear cells) and inner secretory cells (dark cells) were almost completely lost. At the 2-year follow-up, inflammatory cell infiltration had largely subsided, whereas abnormalities of the bilayered secretory architecture persisted and marked sweat duct loss was evident. The concurrent development of AIGA and erythroderma following COVID-19 infection suggests a common IFN-driven mechanism involving adnexal immune dysregulation. The chronological clinicopathological observations in the present case provide valuable longitudinal insights into the structural changes of the eccrine apparatus in this case of AIGA.

articles.title: Clinically significant cytomegalovirus infection under letermovir prophylaxis: Treatment response, survival and increased risk of EBV reactivation and PTLD.
Health economics of teleneurological consultations connecting patients and their physicians with neurologists in Germany.
articles.abstract: IntroductionTeleconsultations promise to enhance access to and quality of healthcare. This study evaluated costs, cost-effectiveness, and cost-utility of video-teleconsultations in the stepped-wedge cluster-randomized NeTKoH trial that connected patients and their primary care physicians in rural areas in northeastern Germany with neurologists.MethodsData on costs and hospitalization were obtained from participating statutory health insurances using claims data. Quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) were computed from patient responses to EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level questionnaires, at enrolment and 3-month follow-up, while waiting times for neurologist examinations were derived from follow-up responses and teleconsultation logs.ResultsData from 372 patients were analyzed: The intervention led to reduced costs, -209 EUR (95% confidence interval [-1350; 767]), shorter lengths of stay for hospitalized patients, -4.45 days [-15.17; 4.40], shorter waiting times for an initial assessment by a neurologist, -39.59 days [-49.66; -29.37] (-5.34 EUR/day [-35.24; 20.09]), no change in QALYs, 0.00 years [-0.01; 0.01], but a statistically significantly lower proportion of cases triaged to continued care in the primary care setting, -0.20 [-0.31; -0.08], and a higher proportion of hospitalized patients, 0.05 [-0.02; 0.11].DiscussionTeleconsultations were cost-effective with respect to waiting times for an initial contact with a neurologist and hospital lengths of stay.

articles.title: [Unilateral parotid involvement revealing Sjögren's disease: Between inflammation and lymphoma].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sjögren's disease is a systemic autoimmune disease in which parotid involvement is typically bilateral and symmetrical. Unilateral parotid enlargement is an unusual presentation that should raise suspicion of a lymphomatous complication.

OBSERVATION: We report the case of a 75-year-old woman with a history of Hodgkin lymphoma in complete remission who presented with sicca symptoms associated with painful right parotid swelling. Ultrasonography showed heterogeneous parotid echotexture with ill-defined hypoechoic areas, without a focal mass or lymphadenopathy. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a "salt-and-pepper" appearance and microcystic changes, without a discrete mass or diffusion restriction. 18F-FDG positron emission tomography (PET/CT) showed no pathological parotid uptake. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of Sjögren's disease.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of an integrated clinical, biological, and imaging approach to differentiate inflammatory parotid involvement from lymphomatous complications, while PET/CT should be reserved for cases with persistent suspicion of lymphoma.

articles.title: [Cardiovascular preventive recommendations. PAPPS 2026 thematic updates].
articles.abstract: The recommendations of the semFYC's Program for Preventive Activities and Health Promotion (PAPPS) for the prevention of vascular diseases (VD) are presented. New in this edition are new sections such as obesity, chronic kidney disease and metabolic hepatic steatosis, as well as a 'Don't Do' section in the different pathologies treated. The sections have been updated: Epidemiological review, where the current morbidity and mortality of CVD in Spain and its evolution as well as the main risk factors are described; Vascular risk (VR) and recommendations for the calculation of CV risk; Main risk factors such as arterial hypertension, dyslipidemia and diabetes mellitus, describing the method for their diagnosis, therapeutic objectives and recommendations for lifestyle measures and pharmacological treatment; Indications for antiplatelet therapy, and recommendations for screening of atrial fibrillation, and Recommendations for management of chronic conditions. The quality of testing and the strength of the recommendation are included in the main recommendations. A new feature in this edition is the inclusion of age and gender perspectives.

articles.title: Sleep and mental health outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy: A matched cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare sleep quality, mental health symptoms, and PASC outcomes among pregnant and non-pregnant participants with and without prior COVID-19 infection.

METHODS: A matched cross-sectional study design was undertaken, comparing four groups: 1) Not Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; 2) Not Pregnant, prior COVID-19; 3) Pregnant, no prior COVID-19; and 4) Pregnant and prior COVID-19.

RESULTS: A total of 1,868 women were included in the analysis (934 pregnant and 934 not pregnant). Among participants with prior COVID-19, those who were pregnant had significantly more comorbidities, and higher hospitalization rates, compared to those not pregnant with prior COVID-19. Overall, prior COVID-19 infection was consistently associated with poorer sleep quality and more sleep disturbances, regardless of pregnancy status. In addition, participants who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 were more likely to report a shorter sleep duration of <5 and <6 hours per night, compared with those not pregnant with no prior COVID-19. Adjusted analyses showed pregnant participants with prior COVID-19 had worse sleep quality and more frequent sleep problems than non-pregnant participants without prior COVID-19. Furthermore, those who were pregnant with prior COVID-19 had a 1.76 to 2.69 times increased odds of developing PASC symptoms, compared to those not pregnant. These high rates of persistent PASC symptoms reported at 3 and 6 months, indicating more prolonged or delayed symptom expression. They also experienced worse mental health outcomes, with the prevalence ratio of having depression and anxiety symptoms occurring 1.89 and 1.72 times higher, respectively, among pregnant individuals with a history of COVID-19.

CONCLUSION: Prior COVID-19 infection should be considered when assessing sleep and mental health in pregnancy due to its association with long-term PASC symptoms. Tailored post-COVID care, maternal health policies, and vaccination should be prioritized.

articles.title: Best of Times, Worst of Times: State Economic Conditions and Medicare Imaging Composition Across Two Macroeconomic Episodes.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study investigates the determinants of imaging utilization across two distinct macroeconomic disruptions by comparing the elective musculoskeletal (MSK) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-to-urgent computed tomography (CT) ratio during the Great Recession recovery and the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: State-level utilization data for elective MSK MRI and urgent CT codes were obtained from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners by Geography and Service Public Use Files (2013-2023), state annual unemployment rates from the Bureau of Labor Statistics Local Area Unemployment Statistics program, and diagnostic radiologist density per 100,000 population from a published aggregation of the National Provider Identifier registry. Associations between changes in the elective-to-urgent imaging ratio and state unemployment were evaluated across both periods. Multivariable linear regression assessed the contributions of unemployment change and diagnostic radiologist density.

RESULTS: During the Great Recession recovery, larger declines in unemployment were associated with greater increases in the elective-to-urgent imaging ratio (r = -0.36, p = 0.010). Each 1% decrease in unemployment corresponded to approximately 8 additional elective MSK MRI examinations per 1000 urgent CT examinations (β = -7.85, 95% CI -13.76--1.94). No such association was observed during the COVID-19 period (r = 0.07, p = 0.61). In multivariable analysis, unemployment change predicted imaging composition during the recession recovery, whereas diagnostic radiologist density approached significance as a negative predictor during COVID-19 (β = -3.05, p = 0.05). On cross-sectional analysis, elective-to-urgent imaging ratio varied 2.4-fold across states, remained stable over time (r = 0.80-0.88), and was inversely associated with radiologist density (r = -0.32--0.44).

CONCLUSION: Imaging composition reflected demand-side economic recovery after the Great Recession but was more closely associated with supply-side constraints during the COVID-19 pandemic, suggesting that the effects of macroeconomic conditions on imaging utilization depend on the nature of the underlying shock.

articles.title: Quantitative Ultrasound-Based Machine Learning Versus the FAST Score for Identifying At-Risk MASH: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Since pharmacological therapies were approved for noncirrhotic adults with at-risk metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), identifying this population noninvasively has become urgent. We therefore developed machine learning (ML) models using quantitative ultrasound (QUS) parameters and serum AST, and compared them with the FibroScan-AST (FAST) score.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 418 patients with biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), 138 with at-risk MASH. Five ML models were developed using four QUS parameters obtained from a general-purpose ultrasound system (LOGIQ E10, GE HealthCare) (ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter, integrated backscatter coefficient [IBSC], signal-to-noise ratio, and two-dimensional shear wave elastography), together with serum AST. Performance was assessed by nested cross-validation (CV) and compared with the FAST score using the DeLong test and Brier scores. A sensitivity analysis excluded patients with F4 fibrosis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantified feature contributions.

RESULTS: All five ML models outperformed the FAST score (cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [CV-AUROC], 0.739 [95% CI: 0.690-0.789]; p < 0.05). Ensemble achieved the highest CV-AUROC (0.834 [0.795-0.873]), and the lowest Brier score (0.152). Results were similar after excluding F4 fibrosis (Ensemble, 0.827; FAST, 0.729; p = 0.001). SHAP identified IBSC as the most influential followed by two-dimensional shear wave elastography and AST.

CONCLUSION: ML models integrating QUS parameters and AST outperformed the FAST score in identifying at-risk MASH in this single-center cohort, with Ensemble showing the best discrimination.

articles.title: Predictive value of different obesity indicators for non-alcoholic fatty Liver disease.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Our objective is to understand the prevalence of no alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in a community population in Luzhou City and the predictive value of different obesity indicators for NAFLD.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 432 participants from a community health service center in Luzhou City, selected randomly between January 1st and March 1st, 2024, were divided into the NAFLD group and the non-NAFLD group. Differences in lipid accumulation index (LAP), visceral fat index (VAI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), weight-adjusted waist circumference index (WWI), and related biochemical indicators were compared between the two groups. LAP, VAI, WHtR, and WWI were divided into four groups (P1-P4, I1-I4, R1-R4, W1-W4) based on quartile levels. The distribution of NAFLD among the groups was compared, and Cramér's V coefficient was used to represent the correlation. Logistic regression and ROC curve analysis were used to explore the predictive value of these obesity indicators for NAFLD, with stratified analysis conducted by age.

RESULTS: The prevalence of NAFLD was 43.75%. Among them, the prevalence rates for men and women were 44.2% and 43.5% respectively. There were significant differences between NAFLD patients and non-NAFLD patients in terms of age, hypertension, diabetes, cerebral infarction, etc. The levels of waist circumference (WC), WWI, WHtR, LAP, VAI, weight, BMI, ALT, uric acid (UA), and triglyceride (TG) in the NAFLD group were all higher than those in the non-NAFLD group, while the level of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDLC) in the NAFLD group was significantly lower than that in the non-NAFLD group. NAFLD was positively correlated with the levels of LAP, VAI, WHtR and WWI (Cramer's V values were 0.457, 0.329, 0.391 and 0.214, respectively). Logistic regression showed that all obesity indicators were significantly associated with the risk of NAFLD (all p < 0.05). The ROC curve analysis indicated that all obesity indicators can predict the risk of NAFLD (AUC >0.5). Among them, LAP had the best predictive value (AUC = 0.762). In different age groups, the predictive ability of VAI in the 20-49 age group was higher than that in the 70-80 age group (0.829 VS 0.635,p = 0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of NAFLD among the physical examination population in a certain community of Luzhou City is relatively high, and the levels of LAP,VAI, WWI and WHtR are positively correlated with the risk of NAFLD. These obesity indicators all have good predictive value for the occurrence of NAFLD across different age groups.

articles.title: Steatotic liver disease management in low- and middle-income countries.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract: Steatotic liver disease (SLD), especially metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), is globally the most frequent cause of chronic liver disease. Its already high prevalence continues to increase across all regions. However, low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) inadequately address SLD. Guidance increasingly emphasizes the role of non-invasive diagnostics, multidisciplinary management and access to approved pharmacotherapies, however these recommendations often compete with other pressing health priorities in many LMICs. This review examines the current evidence on epidemiology, clinical challenges, and health-system gaps affecting SLD care in LMICs and proposes context-appropriate models to improve prevention, early detection, and long-term management. We summarize regional patterns across the Middle East and North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America, highlighting substantial variability in burden and risk profiles. Persistent barriers, including low public and provider awareness, limited availability of non-invasive tests, inconsistent screening practices, shortages in primary-care and hepatology capacity, and high out-of-pocket costs, contribute to delayed diagnosis and limited access to pharmacotherapy, bariatric surgery, and liver transplantation. Policy constraints and fragmented care further impede guideline-recommended pathways. SLD research from LMICs remains scarce, and populations from these regions are markedly underrepresented in clinical trials, restricting the applicability of emerging therapies. Integrating SLD into existing non-communicable disease and chronic care platforms offers a practical route for scaling-up risk stratification and monitoring. This review outlines feasible, cost-conscious strategies that align with local realities and support more equitable models of care, with the goal of improving outcomes and reducing the growing burden of SLD in LMICs.

articles.title: Functional Neuroimaging in Tinnitus: Review of Recent Advances.
articles.abstract: Chronic subjective tinnitus, the perception of sound without an external source, is highly prevalent, clinically heterogeneous, and lacks a cure and objective diagnostic tests. This review examines how functional neuroimaging is closing that gap. Hemodynamic (functional MRI [fMRI], functional near-infrared spectroscopy, PET) and electrophysiological (electroencephalography, magnetoencephalography) modalities redefine tinnitus as a brain-network disorder involving auditory, limbic, and cognitive systems. Altered default mode network connectivity, auditory-limbic hyperconnectivity, and reduced thalamocortical inhibition are emerging as candidate biomarkers that track severity and may help stratify patients. These findings increasingly guide therapies such as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and real-time fMRI neurofeedback.

articles.title: Pulsatile Tinnitus: Diagnostic Evaluation, Otologic Management, and When to Refer.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile tinnitus is a symptom with heterogeneous causes spanning the temporal bone and the head and neck vasculature, and patients often receive divergent recommendations from different specialties. This review presents a mechanism-based approach for the otologist, built on how flow sound is generated and transmitted to the inner ear. Bedside maneuvers, audiometry, and targeted imaging distinguish venous, arterial, arteriovenous, neoplastic, middle-inner ear junction, and central causes. Transmastoid resurfacing treats sigmoid sinus wall anomalies, whereas dural arteriovenous fistula and pulsatile tinnitus with idiopathic intracranial hypertension require prompt neurointerventional or neuro-ophthalmologic referral.

articles.title: Targeting the calcium-sensing receptor, CaSR, for prophylaxis of pollution-driven obstructive airways disease: a proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urban particulate matter (PM) is a major pollutant driving obstructive airways disease. We hypothesised that this reflects activation of the Calcium-Sensing Receptor (CaSR) on airways cells by metal cations in PM.

METHODS: We examined (i) the metal cation content of PM; (ii) the temporal relationship between PM exposure and asthma exacerbation in human populations, assessed using a retrospective, observational, population-based cohort study; (iii) CaSR activation by PM in transfected HEK293 cells; (iv) human lung CaSR immunoreactivity; (v) PM induction of pro-inflammatory mediators in primary human airways cells and dendritic cell maturation; (vi) the therapeutic efficacy of a topically applied CaSR negative allosteric modulator (NAM) in a murine surrogate of obstructive airways disease.

FINDINGS: PM contained multiple cationic CaSR activators. In human populations, asthma exacerbation correlated with exposure to calcium ions within ambient PM. PM activated the CaSR in HEK293 cells. Airways epithelial and innate pro-inflammatory cells intensely expressed the CaSR. PM exposure elevated expression of mRNA encoding alarmins and pro-inflammatory mediators by bronchial epithelial cells and dendritic cell maturation, effects all significantly abrogated by NAMs. In the murine surrogate, a topically applied CaSR NAM significantly abrogated IL-33-driven lung inflammation and remodelling in vivo.

INTERPRETATION: PM-induced airways inflammation is at least partly driven by CaSR activation. Prophylactic, topical therapy with CaSR NAMs may arrest progression of airways obstruction in severe asthma and COPD.

FUNDING: Marie Curie ITN, KESSII European Social Fund, NHMRC of Australia, NIHR Health Protection Research Unit, Inman Charitable Trust, Shandong Province "Double-Hundred Talent Plan" Teams, GOA BOF, HEAL Network, Medical Research Future Fund, University of Technology Sydney, MRC, NIHR Oxford BRC, NERC.

articles.title: Spasmodic Dysphonia and Muscle Tension Dysphonia: A Review of Neuroimaging and Neurophysiological Evidence.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Spasmodic dysphonia (SD), or laryngeal dystonia (LD), and muscle tension dysphonia (MTD) are clinically overlapping voice disorders with different positions in current pathophysiological models. This review synthesizes multimodal neuroimaging and neurophysiological evidence on their central mechanisms, compares the implicated neural systems, and assesses whether such measures can aid future differential diagnosis.

METHODS: A structured search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Europe PMC, and Google Scholar (final search, March 29, 2026), limited to English-language publications from January 2000 through March 2026 and supplemented by reference-list screening and forward citation tracking. Evidence was synthesized across task-based and resting-state fMRI, structural MRI and morphometry, diffusion tensor and kurtosis imaging, PET, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), and magnetoencephalography. Studies were appraised qualitatively for design, sample size, diagnostic phenotype, comparator groups, treatment or botulinum toxin washout status, findings, and limitations.

RESULTS: The SD/LD literature provided relatively consistent evidence of abnormalities across distributed voice-control networks involving cortical, subcortical, cerebellar, and brainstem systems, recurring in primary sensorimotor cortex, supplementary and premotor regions, inferior frontal and parietal cortices, insula, putamen, thalamus, cerebellum, and their white-matter connections. Some abnormalities persisted outside phonation or before movement onset, supporting a trait-like component; TMS showed impaired cortical inhibition and a shortened cortical silent period (CSP) in SD/LD. The MTD evidence base remained limited, comprising one case-control task-fMRI study of ten women, one single-patient pre-/post-treatment fMRI study, and one TMS study with an MTD comparator. These findings suggested possible central involvement but did not establish a causal mechanism, a stable MTD-specific network, or the contributions of compensation, state-dependent effects, and phonatory effort; comparable CSP shortening was not reported in MTD.

CONCLUSIONS: SD/LD is best understood as a distributed disorder of central voice-control networks, whereas MTD appears to be a hyperfunctional voice disorder with plausible but incompletely characterized central influences. Unequal evidence volume should not be read as established biological divergence, and the "neurological" versus "non-neurological" distinction remains provisional. Imaging and physiological measures are not yet validated biomarkers, and CSP is only a candidate marker pending replication and validation. Larger, clinically stratified, harmonized multimodal head-to-head studies are needed, potentially integrating neural, physiological, acoustic, and clinical measures for reliable differential diagnosis.

articles.title: Association between affective temperament and anxiety in takotsubo syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Takotsubo syndrome (TK) is a reversible stress cardiomyopathy with clinical symptoms similar to ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) but without significant coronary lesions on coronary angiography. In more than two thirds of cases, TK occurs after physical or emotional stress, positive or negative. The aim of this study was to assess if affective temperaments and psychiatric disorders differed in patients with TK syndrome in comparison with STEMI patients. Affective temperaments are considered as the biologically stable part of emotional reactivity.

METHODS: In a non-interventional case-control study, 38 patients who had a TK and 76 patients who had a STEMI were assessed respectively using the TEMPS-A scale, the Burns anxiety inventory, and the MINI scale to compare presentations of the five affective temperaments, anxiety and psychiatric comorbidities. The two population groups were similar on age, sex and date of cardiac event.

RESULTS: All temperament scores were significantly higher in the TK group in comparison to the STEMI control group, except for irritable temperament. Anxiety was significantly higher in the TK group (mean [standard deviation]=19.08 [15.76]) compared to the control group (5.25 [8.44]; p <0.001). Anxiety disorders were significantly more frequent in the TK group in comparison to the control group.

CONCLUSION: The results suggest that affective temperaments may be stress vulnerability markers. Further study could lead to improved assessment of cardiovascular risk and management of patients with TK syndrome.

articles.title: Distinct yet complementary roles of temporal and spectral predictions in auditory detection.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Predictive processing enables the brain to anticipate both when and what sensory events will occur. Although temporal and spectral predictions are both known to facilitate perception, their functional contributions and interaction remain poorly understood, particularly in uncertain listening conditions where predictions must be inferred from implicit statistical regularities rather than explicit cues or rhythms. Here, we orthogonalized temporal and spectral predictability in a non-rhythmic auditory detection task and used a signal-detection framework to dissociate perceptual and decisional processes in humans of either sex. Temporal predictions primarily increased response readiness: predictable target timing led to faster responses and more hits but also more false alarms, reflecting a liberal shift in response bias. Spectral predictions, in contrast, selectively enhanced perceptual sensitivity without a comparable speeding of responses. Crucially, despite their distinct behavioral effects, temporal and spectral predictions interacted synergistically, such that perceptual sensitivity was greatest when both sound timing and frequency were predictable, consistent with a spectrotemporal filter mechanism. Furthermore, temporal and spectral variability were encoded differently: performance adapted strongly to the distribution of foreperiod durations but remained largely stable across the spectral distribution, suggesting that the brain exploits temporal and spectral statistics in distinct ways when forming predictions under uncertainty. Together, these findings demonstrate that temporal and spectral predictions make complementary contributions to auditory decision-making, interact synergistically to improve perceptual sensitivity, and rely on distinct encoding strategies for temporal and spectral variability.Significance statement In everyday listening, the brain must predict both when relevant sounds will occur and what they will sound like. Although temporal ("when") and spectral ("what") predictions are both known to support perception, their distinct functions and possible synergies are not well understood. Here, using a non-rhythmic auditory detection task and a signal-detection framework, we show that temporal predictions mainly increase response readiness, whereas spectral predictions selectively enhance perceptual sensitivity. When both are available, they interact synergistically to maximize sensitivity. These findings reveal that temporal and spectral predictions make complementary contributions to auditory decision-making and show how the brain combines multiple predictive dimensions to improve perception under uncertainty.

Abnormalities in blood tests for monitoring long-term conditions: a matched retrospective cohort study using routinely collected primary care data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is unclear which blood tests should be included in routine monitoring for people with hypertension (HTN), type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and chronic kidney disease stage 3 (CKD3). We identified uncertainty around monitoring sodium and potassium in HTN, T2DM and CKD3; haemoglobin in T2DM; and thyroid function in CKD3.

AIM: To determine whether abnormalities of sodium, potassium, haemoglobin and TSH are more common in patients with these long-term conditions (LTCs) than in matched people without them.

DESIGN & SETTING: Matched retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: UK general practices contributing to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD).

METHOD: We identified people diagnosed with HTN, T2DM or CKD3 between 01/01/2012 and 31/12/2019 and 1:1 age-, sex- and practice-matched controls without these LTCs. Cox regression was used to analyse time to first abnormal blood test, first clinically significant abnormal result, and hypothyroidism diagnosis. To account for bias from higher testing in people with LTCs, analyses were restricted to those with at least one blood test and adjusted for annual testing frequency.

RESULTS: The numbers of people with HTN, T2DM and CKD3, and matched controls, were 83,563, 25 820 and 18,012, respectively. All LTCs were associated with an increased risk of an abnormal blood test result (hazard ratios [HR]>1). After adjustment for testing frequency, age and sex, only clinically significant potassium abnormalities in CKD remained more frequent than in matched controls (HR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2 to 2.1).

CONCLUSIONS: After accounting for testing frequency, the rate of clinically significant test abnormalities was similar in both groups.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk factors, endotypes of chest pain and the effect of functional coronary angiography.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether patients with suspected angina and no obstructive coronary artery disease (ANOCA) have similar cardiovascular risk profiles across clinical endotypes and whether endotype-informed management improves cardiovascular risk factor control.

DESIGN: CorCTCA (NCT03477890) was a prospective, multicentre, randomised controlled trial to identify coronary endotypes (non-cardiac chest pain, obstructive coronary artery disease, microvascular angina, vasospastic angina, mixed disease). Participants were randomised to disclosure or non-disclosure of coronary function results to the treating physician.

SETTING: Outpatients undergoing computerised tomography coronary angiography.

PARTICIPANTS: Participants identified with unobstructed coronary arteries underwent invasive coronary function testing (fractional flow reserve, bolus thermodilution acetylcholine provocation).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Baseline cardiovascular risk factors, preventive therapies and changes in risk factors during follow-up were evaluated.

RESULTS: Among 250 participants enrolled (mean age 55.9 years; 62.4% women), 19 (7.6%) had obstructive (FFR≤0.80) and 231 (92.4%) non-obstructive coronary disease. The estimated duration of symptoms prior to enrolment was 18.0 (9.0, 36.0) months. Coronary endotype groups included obstructive CAD (n=19), microvascular (n=127), vasospastic (n=27), mixed (microvascular and vasospastic) (n=17) angina and non-cardiac chest pain (n=60). Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes and obesity (48.4% obese) were common and similarly distributed across coronary endotypes. Of 244 with completed questionnaires, 179 (73.4%) reported inactive or minimally active lifestyles. LDL cholesterol was measured at baseline in 247/250 participants, of whom 179 (90.3%) had LDL-c exceeding 1.4 mmol/L. The proportion of participants with elevated LDL cholesterol was similar across coronary endotypes (p=0.206). Endotype-informed management reduced systolic blood pressure at 12 months (−5.59 mm Hg; 95% CI −10.99 to −0.19; p=0.044); however, standard care pathways exhibited no significant improvements in physical activity, C-reactive protein, lipid profile or resting heart rate optimisation.

CONCLUSIONS: Uncontrolled cardiovascular risk factors were highly prevalent irrespective of coronary endotype. Risk factor modification of this patient population should be encouraged in clinical practice.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03477890.

Association between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and risk of non-ischaemic cardiovascular disease: nationwide, register based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the associations between hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (pre-eclampsia and gestational hypertension) and the postpartum risk of non-ischaemic cardiovascular disease.

DESIGN: Nationwide, register based cohort study.

SETTING: Four Danish national registers (Civil Registration System, National Patient Register, Medical Birth Register, and Danish National Prescription Register), 1 January 1978 to 31 December 2022.

PARTICIPANTS: 1 314 888 women with at least one live birth or stillbirth at or after 20 weeks' gestation in 1978-2022 and with no known history of circulatory or chronic kidney disease before their first pregnancy.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Diagnosis of any non-ischaemic cardiovascular disease (ie, pulmonary heart disease, left sided valvular disease, conduction disorders, cardiac arrest, arrhythmias, heart failure, cerebral haemorrhage, aneurysm or dissection, arterial thromboembolism, and venous thromboembolism).

RESULTS: The cohort was followed for 28 460 581 person years (median follow-up 20 years, interquartile range 10-32 years). Women with gestational hypertension or pre-eclampsia were 35% (hazard ratio 1.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.29 to 1.42) and 39% (hazard ratio 1.39, 1.35 to 1.43) more likely, respectively, than women without hypertensive disorders of pregnancy to develop non-ischaemic cardiovascular disease and had increased rates of 10 disease subtypes. Gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia were both most strongly associated with heart failure (gestational hypertension: hazard ratio 1.88, 95% CI 1.57 to 2.26; pre-eclampsia: hazard ratio 1.96, 1.76 to 2.18). Some associations varied by subtype; for example, gestational hypertension was more strongly associated with cerebral haemorrhage than pre-eclampsia (hazard ratio 1.70, 95% CI 1.45 to 1.98 v 1.30, 1.17 to 1.44; P=0.005) whereas the reverse was true for venous thromboembolism (hazard ratio 1.17, 1.04 to 1.31 v 1.41, 1.33 to 1.50; P=0.003). Associations were not influenced by age or time since birth but seemed to be partially mediated by hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: A history of pre-eclampsia or gestational hypertension was associated with many non-ischaemic cardiovascular diseases, suggesting both shared and disorder-specific underlying mechanisms. The findings suggest a need to broaden clinical awareness of the potential comorbidities after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy to include non-ischaemic cardiovascular disease.

Biologicals in Allergy: Immunological Consequences With Oncologic Implications-An EAACI BIOLAO Task Force Joint Position Paper of the AllergoOncology and Biologicals Working Groups.
articles.abstract: Biological therapies targeting Type 2 inflammation have transformed the management of severe allergic diseases, including asthma, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, atopic dermatitis, and chronic spontaneous urticaria. As the use of these agents continues to expand, questions arise regarding their potential long-term effects on immune homeostasis, including possible consequences on tumor immune surveillance and cancer biology. In this joint position paper of the Task Force BIOLAO of the EAACI AllergoOncology Working Group and the EAACI Biologicals Working Group, we review the current evidence on the pro- and anti-tumorigenic implications of biologicals used in the treatment of allergic diseases. We summarize in vitro and in vivo mechanisms of action findings on the immunological pathways targeted by these agents and we discuss how modulation of IgE-, IL-5, IL-4/IL-13-, TSLP-, and IL-31-related networks may influence tumor biology. We also review available clinical evidence regarding cancer incidence and malignancy risk in allergic patients receiving biologicals. Current clinical data do not indicate a consistent increase in malignancy risk associated with approved allergy biologicals, although long-term and cancer-specific data remain limited. This position paper aims to support researchers in interpreting the interface between allergy and oncology and to define AllergoOncology priorities for future translational and clinical research.

articles.title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates and Oral Toxicities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are an emerging and promising class of anticancer therapeutics. This retrospective study aimed to characterize the oral toxicities associated with ADC treatment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was conducted using de-identified clinical data from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) PatientExploreR database through 2024. A total of 13 ADCs were included in the analysis. Demographic characteristics, cancer diagnoses, treatment data, and oral toxicity data were retrieved for all eligible patients.

STATISTICAL ANALYSIS: Descriptive statistics summarized demographic characteristics, smoking status, oral toxicity prevalence, and median time to onset. Associations between oral toxicity categories and sex, race, and smoking status were assessed using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact tests.

RESULTS: A total of 1144 patients who received ADC therapy were included in the study, including 59.7% females, 15.9% males, and 24.0% unknown. Oral toxicities were recorded in 13.7% of patients, with mucosal lesions being the most prevalent (10.5%), followed by dry mouth (2.3%) and orofacial neuropathies (1.0%). A Pearson's chi-square test demonstrated a significant association between sex at birth and oral toxicity category (p = 0.023). The frequency of oral mucosal lesions varied significantly across the ADCs (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test with Monte Carlo simulation, 100 000 replicates; p < 0.0001). The frequency of dry mouth and orofacial neuropathies did not differ significantly among the ADCs (p = 0.412 and 0.297).

CONCLUSION: Given the expanding use of ADCs in cancer therapy, characterization of their toxicity profile is essential. In this study, oral toxicities were observed in 13.7% of patients, with oral mucosal lesions being the predominant toxicity, followed by dry mouth.

articles.title: In Vitro Synergism and Preliminary In Vivo Efficacy of Florfenicol Combined with Oxytetracycline against Streptococcus agalactiae Infection in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
articles.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae is one of the most serious diseases in Nile tilapia aquaculture. The objective of this study was to evaluate the potential combinational therapy of florfenicol (FF) and oxytetracycline (OTC) against S. agalactiae strains. Checkerboard microdilution assays of FF + OTC showed that among 10 S. agalactiae isolates, 9 were synergistic and 1 was additive. In the efficacy test, Nile tilapia juveniles were divided into 6 groups (in triplicate): control, FF 10 mg/kg/day, FF 20 mg/kg/day, OTC 50 mg/kg/day, OTC 100 mg/kg/day and a combination of FF 10 + OTC 50 mg/kg/day. Each fish was injected intraperitoneally with a resistant isolate of S. agalactiae at 108 CFU and treated with antibiotics via medicated feeds twice daily for 7 days. The survival rate of the FF + OTC combination was 100%, significantly higher than the control (23.33%), low-dose OTC (43.33%) and FF groups (53.33%). The total bacterial counts in the liver of FF + OTC-treated fish were significantly lower than those of the control group (1.05 and 5.15 × 107 CFU/g, respectively). This preliminary study demonstrates that the FF + OTC combination was effective against S. agalactiae infections.

articles.title: Effects of maternal voice via affective-semantic dual pathways on emergence delirium in children under general anaesthesia: a randomised controlled trial protocol.
Prevalence and risk factors of chronic kidney disease in Chinese patients with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Experiences of peer educator dyads and nurse educators in delivering a Targeted Self-Management Intervention (TEAM) to reduce stroke burden in Uganda: a qualitative study.
Drugs to treat chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulmonary fibrosis: What we currently have and how transient receptor potential mucolipin channel modulators could change therapy.
articles.abstract: Endolysosomes harbour a diverse array of ion channels, transporters, pumps and exchangers that regulate the bidirectional flux of ions and solutes between the cytosol and the endolysosomal lumen. Among the principal families of non-selective Ca2+- and Na+-permeable cation channels localized to the endolysosomal system are the transient receptor potential mucolipin (TRPML) channels and the two-pore channels (TPCs). This review summarizes recent advances demonstrating pathophysiologically relevant roles of TRPML channels in pulmonary disease, with particular emphasis on their regulation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and the consequent effects on extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling, including collagen and elastin homeostasis. Pharmacological activation of TRPML1 has been shown to promote the release of multiple MMPs, whereas genetic ablation of TRPML1 in mice results in reduced extracellular MMP levels, increased collagen deposition and the development of a fibrotic lung phenotype. In contrast, activation of TRPML3 enhances the endocytic uptake of MMPs, specifically the macrophage elastase MMP12. Accordingly, TRPML3-deficient mice exhibit increased extracellular elastin accumulation, and an emphysema-like lung phenotype. This phenotype is further aggravated following exposure to tobacco smoke, highlighting the protective role of TRPML3 in maintaining pulmonary ECM homeostasis under physiological and pathological conditions. Collectively, these findings identify TRPML channels as key regulators of ECM turnover through their complementary roles in the secretion and uptake of MMPs. Given the limited treatment options and absence of curative therapies for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or lung fibrosis, pharmacological modulation of TRPML channel activity may offer new opportunities for treatment.

articles.title: Cross validation of Ultrasound- and Serum-Based Scores for Fibrosis Assessment after Liver Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Purpose This study aimed to conduct a comprehensive comparison of non-invasive diagnostic approaches for graft fibrosis (shear wave elastography (SWE), serum-based scores) in liver transplant (LT) recipients against transient elastography (TE). Materials & Methods In this retrospective analysis of 195 liver transplant recipients from a tertiary transplant center, an ultrasound-based technique (SWE PLUS) and serum-based scores were compared with TE. Liver stiffness > 7.5 kPa was defined as significant fibrosis. All data were collected at one visit and ultrasound measurements followed FESUMB guidelines. Statistics included correlation analysis, uni- and multivariable logistic regression and AUROC analyses. DeLong test was used to compare AUCs. Results Median time from LT were 49 months with 44 % females and a median age of 59 years. SWE PLUS showed a strong correlation with TE (rho = 0.69, p < 0.0001) and an excellent diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.901. In univariable regression analysis, the serum-based scores were associated with the presence of significant fibrosis. In multivariable analysis only SWE PLUS was an independent predictor of significant fibrosis (OR = 2.561, p < 0.001). SWE PLUS outperformed all serum-based tests for the detection of graft fibrosis (each p < 0.001). Conclusion Our results demonstrate applicability of SWE for the diagnosis of graft fibrosis in LT recipients. SWE PLUS may represent a promising alternative to TE for graft fibrosis detection. German Abstract Zielsetzung Ziel dieser Studie war ein Vergleich nicht-invasiver diagnostischer Ansätze (Scherwellenelastographie (SWE PLUS), Serumbasierte Verfahren) zur Detektion einer Transplantatfibrose bei Patienten nach Lebertransplantation (LT). Materialien & Methoden In dieser retrospektiven Analyse von 195 Lebertransplantierten wurden SWE PLUS sowie serumbasierte Scores mit transienter Elastographie verglichen. Eine Lebersteifigkeit > 7,5 kPa definierte eine signifikante Transplantatfibrose. Alle Daten wurden im Rahmen eines einzelnen Untersuchungstermins erhoben; die Ultraschallmessungen erfolgten gemäß den EFSUMB-Leitlinien. Die Analysen umfassten Korrelationsanalysen, uni- und multivariable logistische Regressionsanalysen sowie AUROC-Analysen und den Vergleich der AUROCs mittels DeLong-Test. Ergebnisse Die mediane Zeit seit LT betrug 49 Monate; 44 % waren weiblich, das mediane Alter lag bei 59 Jahren. SWE PLUS korrelierte stark mit TE (rho = 0,69; p < 0,0001) und zeigte eine AUC von 0,901. In der univariablen Regressionsanalyse waren die serumbasierten Scores mit dem Vorliegen einer signifikanten Fibrose assoziiert, jedoch war in der multivariablen Analyse lediglich SWE PLUS unabhängig mit signifikanter Transplantatfibrose assoziiert (OR = 2,561; p < 0,001). SWE PLUS zeigte sich signifikant besser in der Prädiktion der Transplantatfibrose verglichen mit allen untersuchten serumbasierten Scores (p jeweils < 0.001). Schlussfolgerung Unsere Ergebnisse zeigen die Anwendbarkeit der SWE PLUS zur Diagnose einer Transplantatfibrose bei Patienten nach LT. SWE PLUS stellt eine vielversprechende Alternative zur TE für die Detektion einer Transplantatfibrose dar.

articles.title: Infections in Immune Thrombocytopenia: Pathogenesis, Treatment-Related Risk, and Prevention.
articles.abstract: Infections are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). Although the risk of infection is generally attributed to immunosuppressive treatments, infections are also frequent in patients treated with thrombopoietin receptor agonists, suggesting that ITP, itself, may be an immunodeficient condition. In this review, we explore the pathogenesis and risk factors for infection in ITP and review data on infection risk with different treatment modalities. We conclude with recommendations on integrating infection risk in treatment decisions and mitigating infection risk in patients with ITP.

articles.title: Prioritization of Mobile Application Features for Sustained Medication Adherence.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sustained medication adherence is critical for managing chronic diseases, yet digital adherence tools often demonstrate variable long-term effectiveness. Understanding which application features most strongly drive adherence is essential for optimizing mhealth intervention design.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to prioritize feature-level satisfactions within a mobile adherence application that predict sustained medication adherence among patients with chronic diseases.

METHOD: This study was conducted among adults with diabetes, hypertension, asthma or heart failure who had low baseline adherence (Morisky Medication Adherence Scale [MMAS-8<6]. Adherence was assessed using the MMAS-8 at baseline, 3 months (early adherence) and 6 months (sustained adherence). Feature satisfaction was evaluated at 6 months using the Mobile Adherence Satisfaction Scale (MASS). Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was applied to test direct feature effects on sustained adherence, adjusting for baseline and early adherence. Combined Importance-Performance Map Analysis (cIPMA) were used to assess feature necessity, importance and performance.

RESULTS: A total of 463 participants (mean age 55.2 years, 54.2% female) were included. SEM explained 32% of the variance in sustained adherence. Early adherence exerted the strongest influence (β=0.36, P<0.001). Among features, personal health record (β=0.25, P<0.001), missed-dose reminders (β=0.29, P=0.01), refill reminders (β=0.24, P=0.03) and caregiver monitoring (β=0.17, P<0.001) were significant predictors. cIPMA highlighted personal health record (importance = 0.25, performance = 71.7), missed-dose reminders (0.29, 65.1), and refill reminders (0.24, 63.9) as most influential features, with caregiver monitoring (0.17, 50.3) showing moderate importance but lowest performance. Necessity condition analysis confirmed the personal health record as a necessary condition for high adherence (CE-FDH=71.7%, d=0.17, P=0.02).

CONCLUSION: The effect of feature-level satisfaction was heterogeneous, where personal health record, missed-dose reminders, refill reminders and caregiver monitoring emerged as key determinants of sustained adherence, indicating that reliability and informational functions should be prioritized when designing mobile adherence interventions.

articles.title: Clopidogrel Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics on Ischemic and Bleeding Risk in STEMI Patients Post-PCI: A Model-informed Dosing Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association of the model-estimated clopidogrel active metabolite (clop-AM) plasma concentrations and maximum platelet aggregation (MPA) with clinical outcomes in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

METHODS: This study enrolled 724 STEMI patients undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel 75 mg daily. A population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PPK/PD) model was used to estimate clop-AM plasma concentrations and MPA. Clinical outcomes included 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, the composite of cardiac death, recurrent myocardial infarction, unplanned revascularization, stent thrombosis, or ischemic stroke) and bleeding events (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium types ≥ 2). Cox models assess the association between clop-AM concentration and MPA with clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: PPK-estimated clop-AM exhibited a dual effect: higher clop-AM quartiles (Q3-Q4 vs. Q1) were associated with lower MACE risk (HR [95% CI]: 0.38 [0.15-0.91], 0.47 [0.21-1.06]) but higher bleeding risk (1.70 [0.69-4.21], 3.08 [1.10-8.60]). The clop-AM-MACE association was L-shaped (non-linearity P < 0.05) with a breaking point at 13.6 nM, while bleeding risk increased linearly with concentration. PPD-estimated MPA displayed inverse associations with both endpoints compared with those of clop-AM. Leveraging these findings, a PPK model-guided dosing strategy was developed. Counterfactual simulation in CYP2C19 EM demonstrated that the PPK-guided dosing (60 or 70 mg) reduced bleeding risk by 1.6% (7.0 to 5.4%) compared to the standard 75 mg without compromising MACE protection.

CONCLUSION: PPK/PD-estimated clop-AM and MPA exhibit inverse, dose-dependent associations with MACE and bleeding, validating PPK-PD linkage and justifying model-based individualized dosing post PCI.

articles.title: Effects of daily wild blueberry consumption for 12 weeks on cardiometabolic health in middle-aged/older adults with above-normal blood pressure: results from a randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence suggests wild blueberries (WBB) can improve vascular function. However, findings from randomized controlled trials are equivocal and limited, particularly among middle-aged and older adults with above-normal blood pressure (BP).

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of daily consumption of freeze-dried WBB powder on endothelial function and other cardiometabolic health parameters in middle-aged and older adults with above-normal BP.

METHODS: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm trial, 52 postmenopausal women and men aged 40-75 y with elevated BP or stage 1-hypertension were randomized to consume 22 g/d freeze-dried WBB powder or an isocaloric placebo for 12 weeks. The primary outcome, endothelial function, was assessed as the endothelial function was assessed as reactive hyperemia index (RHI). Secondary outcomes included arterial stiffness, brachial and aortic hemodynamics, circulating biomarkers of cardiometabolic health, and gut microbiota composition.

RESULTS: WBB consumption did not improve endothelial function or most cardiometabolic health parameters compared to placebo (P > 0.05). A treatment × time interaction was observed for aortic pulse pressure, which increased in WBB group relative to placebo (+3.0 mmHg; 95% CI 0.29, 5.67; P = 0.03); however, this isolated finding was not accompanied by adverse changes in other hemodynamic or arterial stiffness parameters. Several adverse within-group hemodynamic changes were observed in the placebo group but not the WBB group. Gut microbial α- and β-diversity did not change differentially between groups over time, although overall community composition differed modestly between groups. Exploratory analyses indicated baseline microbial richness was associated with improvements in endothelial function, particularly in the WBB group.

CONCLUSIONS: Consumption of 22 g/d of freeze-dried WBB powder for 12 weeks did not improve endothelial function or other cardiometabolic health parameters in the current study. Baseline gut microbiota may contribute to inter-individual variability in response, highlighting the need for larger studies incorporating precision nutrition approaches. Clinical Trial Registration number in clinicaltrials.gov: NCT04530916.

articles.title: Cat and Dog Component-Resolved Diagnostics in SPT-Negative, Whole-Extract-sIgE-Positive Patients:Complement Skin Testing and Whole-Allergen IgE:a Single-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Component-resolved diagnostics (CRD) distinguishes primary sensitization from cross-reactivity.

OBJECTIVE: To describe dog and cat CRD profiles in a U.S. referral cohort, with focus on patients with negative skin prick testing (SPT) and detectable whole-extract specific IgE (sIgE).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 432 patients who underwent cat and/or dog CRD between April 2024 and April 2025. Detectable whole-extract and component sIgE was defined as >0.10 kUA/L. CRD was performed only when whole-extract sIgE was detectable.

RESULTS: d 1 was the most common cat component (85.1%), followed by Fel d 4 (46.1%) and Fel d 7 (39.2%). Among cat SPT-negative patients, 60.9% had detectable whole-extract cat sIgE, with Fel d 1, Fel d 4, Fel d 7, and Fel d 2 being detected in 73.1%, 38.8%, 27.9%, and 19.1%, respectively. Can f 5 (54.2%) and Can f 1 (46.3%) were the predominant dog components. Among dog SPT-negative patients, 89.4% had detectable whole-extract dog sIgE, with Can f 5, Can f 1, and Can f 6 being detected in 51.1%, 36.5%, and 32.1%, respectively. In patients with negative SPT and detectable whole-extract cat and dog sIgE, concurrent sensitization to Fel d 2-Can f 3, Fel d 7-Can f 1, and Fel d 4-Can f 6 was observed in less than a third of patients and most individuals also had detectable sIgE to additional components.

CONCLUSION: Cat and dog CRD describe molecular patterns beyond whole-extract testing. Prospective studies correlating component-specific sensitization with clinical and therapeutic outcomes are needed to guide CRD use in cat/dog allergy management.

articles.title: Age-dependent decoupling of body mass index from obesity-related complications under the 2025 clinical obesity definition.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology Commission defined clinical obesity as excess adiposity (Step 1) accompanied by obesity-related organ dysfunction or limitation of daily activities (Step 2). Whether body mass index (BMI) identifies adults with obesity-related complications equally well across age groups remains unclear in East Asian populations, where metabolic complications often occur at lower BMI.

METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from 31,830 adults in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) 2019-2024. Fourteen obesity-related complications were operationalized from the Lancet Commission criteria and the guidelines of the Korean Society for the Study of Obesity (KSSO). Obesity was defined as BMI ≥25 kg/m2 (KSSO), and Step 1 combined this threshold with waist-based criteria. The primary endpoint for diagnostic accuracy was obesity-related multimorbidity (≥2 complications); ≥1 complication, the Commission's Step 2 rule, was analyzed in parallel. Discrimination of BMI, waist circumference (WC) and waist-to-height ratio (WHtR) was evaluated in four age groups (19-34, 35-49, 50-64 and ≥ 65 years). All estimates incorporated survey strata, primary sampling units (PSU) and pooled examination weights, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) derived via PSU-cluster bootstrapping.

FINDINGS: The weighted prevalence of clinical obesity among Korean adults was 37.7% (95% CI 37.1-38.5). The area under the ROC curve (AUC) of BMI for obesity-related multimorbidity declined from 0.786 (0.766-0.806) among adults aged 19-34 years to 0.636 (0.623-0.649) among those aged ≥65 years. Among adults aged ≥65 years with KSSO-normal BMI (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), 86.7% had at least one obesity-related complication. BMI ≥25 kg/m2 identified 71% of adults with multimorbidity aged 19-34 years but only 41% of those aged ≥65 years. WC and WHtR discriminated better than BMI among adults aged ≥65 years (AUC 0.659 and 0.668), although their discrimination also declined with age.

INTERPRETATION: Clinical obesity affects more than one-third of Korean adults. BMI discriminates obesity-related complications well in young adults (19-34 years) but poorly in older adults (≥65 years). From middle age (35-64 years) onwards, BMI-based screening should be complemented by waist-based measures and direct assessment of obesity-related complications.

articles.title: Evaluation of Bioelectric Impedance analysis in a cohort of non-invasive Ventilated patients with Acute Respiratory failure: The NIVAR Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Bioimpedance (BIA) parameters, such as phase angle (PhA), could assess body composition and tissue integrity (e.g., muscle mass status) in critically ill. Respiratory muscular dysfunction may lead to failure of non-invasive ventilation (NIV), defined as the need for endotracheal intubation (ETI). Thus, we aimed to evaluate the association of BIA parameters with NIV failure and hospital mortality.

DESIGN: Single centre prospective observational cohort study. Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06996197).

PATIENTS: Patients with AHRF with COVID-19 who required NIV support and ICU admission.

INTERVENTIONS: A BIA assessment was performed within the first 24 hours after NIV onset.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Patient characteristics, severity scores, NIV settings, BIA parameters and outcomes were recorded. Cox-hazard multivariate analysis was used to assess the association between BIA parameters and NIV failure. Seventy-four patients were included, 58 (78.4%) men, with a median age of 63.5 (53-71) years. The mean BMI was 30±6 kg·m-2. Forty-three patients (58.1%) required ETI after initiating NIV support, with a median length of 4 (3-6) days from the NIV onset to ETI. After adjusting for potential covariates, higher PhA was associated with a trend towards lower rates of NIV failure (HR: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.29-1.00; P=0.05) and lower hospital mortality (Hazard Ratio: 0.43; 95% CI: 0.24-0.76; P=0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: We found that body composition measured by BIA parameters may be associated with lower mortality and a trend towards lower NIV failure.

articles.title: Association between systemic immune-inflammation index and three-year visual decline in patients with diabetic retinopathy: A real-world longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of visual impairment in diabetes. The association between systemic inflammation and subsequent visual outcomes in patients with established DR remains unclear. We investigated the association between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and visual decline using real-world longitudinal data.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with DR receiving ophthalmic care at Peking University Third Hospital. SII was calculated from neutrophil, platelet, and lymphocyte counts. The primary outcome was visual decline, defined as an increase in logMAR best-corrected visual acuity of ≥0.2 during up to 3 years of follow-up. Multivariable Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 1,725 eyes from 914 patients, 748 experienced visual decline. Higher SII was associated with a higher hazard of visual decline after multivariable adjustment (HR per 100-unit increase, 1.033; 95 % CI, 1.012-1.055; P = 0.003). No significant nonlinearity or subgroup interactions were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline SII was associated with increased risk of 3-year visual decline in patients with DR, supporting its potential relevance for visual prognosis.

articles.title: Immune-mediated diseases, plasma proteomic signatures, and risk of incident type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate associations of time-updated immune-mediated diseases and cumulative disease burden with incident type 2 diabetes and identify plasma proteins associated with both conditions.

METHODS: We included 461,575 UK Biobank participants without recorded or self-reported diabetes at baseline. Twenty-six immune-mediated diseases were modeled as time-updated exposures with a 365-day lag for incident disease. Cox models assessed disease status, burden, and duration. Sensitivity analyses considered baseline glycemia and class-specific medication use. Among 43,609 participants with Olink data, multistage proteomic analyses and LASSO Cox regression prioritized candidate proteins.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 21,183 participants developed type 2 diabetes. Any time-updated immune-mediated disease was associated with higher risk (HR 1.45, 95 % CI 1.40-1.51). HRs were 1.42 (1.37-1.47) for one disease and 1.65 (1.53-1.79) for at least two diseases (P for trend < 0.001). Associations persisted after biochemical exclusions (HR 1.52 (1.47-1.58)) and medication adjustment (1.44 (1.39-1.50)). Proteomic analyses identified 308 concordant candidates; coefficient ranking after LASSO prioritized HGF, PRAP1, IL18R1, INHBC, and LEP.

CONCLUSIONS: Time-updated immune-mediated disease and greater disease burden were associated with higher subsequent type 2 diabetes risk. Proteomic findings highlighted candidate immune-metabolic pathways warranting further validation.

articles.title: IgG reactivity with Strongyloides venezuelensis surface antigens: Potential diagnostic target in immunocompromised patients.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Strongyloidiasis remains a major diagnostic challenge, particularly in immunocompromised individuals, in whom the infection may progress to severe and potentially fatal forms. In line with the recommendations of the World Health Organization's recommendations emphasizing the need for sensitive and specific diagnostic methods, this study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the cuticle extract of Strongyloides venezuelensis infective larvae (iL3) for the detection of IgG antibodies in serum samples from immunocompromised individuals.

METHODS: The S. venezuelensis iL3 cuticular extract was prepared using the cationic detergent CTAB (iL3-CTAB). A panel of 44 serum samples from immunocompromised patients was analyzed by ELISA and Western blotting.

RESULTS: ELISA reactivity ranged from 0.084 to 2.347, with higher absorbance values observed in patients with S. stercoralis infection compared to uninfected controls. Using a cut-off of 0.185, 63.6% (14/22) of infected individuals were identified as positive, while all uninfected controls (100%, 22/22) were classified as negative. Western blotting revealed six band ranges of immunodominant protein fractions ranging from 15 to 163 kDa. Notably, the 30-39 kDa protein fraction was recognized in all infected individuals (100%, 22/22), and only 22.7% (5/22) of controls.

CONCLUSION: These results highlight the diagnostic potential of the S. venezuelensis iL3-CTAB cuticular extract and support its use as a promising antigenic source for the immunodiagnosis of strongyloidiasis, particularly by Western blotting, in immunocompromised patients.

articles.title: Ischemic Stroke Guidelines in Latin America: A Systematic AGREE II Appraisal.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in Latin America, yet the methodological rigor and standardization of regional clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) remain inconsistent. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the quality and the diagnostic and pharmacological treatment recommendations of ischemic stroke CPGs across the region.

METHODS: Systematic literature review and guideline appraisal. Six evidence-based ischemic stroke CPGs developed by scientific societies or recognized public health entities in Latin America, selected from 2,339 identified records. The primary outcome was the methodological quality of the CPGs, independently evaluated using the AGREE II instrument. The secondary outcome was the alignment of their recommendations against the Canadian Stroke Best Practice Recommendations (CSBPR), which served as the highest-quality reference standard.

RESULTS: The analyzed CPGs originated from Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, and Peru. Three CPGs (Colombia, Mexico, and Peru) were strongly recommended (scoring ≥60% in ≥4 AGREE II domains), and three (Brazil, Chile, and Cuba) were not recommended. The highest-rated domain was "clarity of presentation" (median: 83%), and the lowest was "applicability" (median: 33%). Critical therapeutic gaps were identified: no Latin American CPG included a target door-to-needle time of ≤30 minutes for intravenous thrombolysis, none mentioned tenecteplase, and notable discrepancies existed regarding endovascular thrombectomy care.

CONCLUSIONS: Latin American ischemic stroke CPGs show significant heterogeneity in methodological rigor and adherence to international evidence. Addressing critical gaps in acute management recommendations, particularly concerning rapid thrombolysis and thrombectomy, is vital to optimize regional stroke care.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42024506861.

articles.title: Patients Meeting CHOICE-2 Criteria and Coded Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis in a United States Thrombectomy Sample: Identification Using Administrative Proxies.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) after successful thrombectomy is supported by emerging randomized controlled trial evidence. We used claims data from before publication of Chemical Optimization of Cerebral Embolectomy 2 (CHOICE-2) to identify how many patients met selected CHOICE-2 criteria and received coded IAT in a United States thrombectomy sample.

METHODS: We studied a single-vendor United States claims sample from January 2020 through June 2025. Administrative proxies for selected CHOICE-2 criteria were applied sequentially. Sensitivity analyses varied encounter definitions, claim type, and the same-encounter intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) exclusion. Coded IAT frequency was reported using a Wilson 95% confidence interval (CI).

RESULTS: Among 1,477 patients with acute ischemic stroke and thrombectomy, 953 (64.5%) met the selected CHOICE-2 criteria. Omitting the ICH exclusion increased this number to 1,154 (78.1%). IAT was coded in 15/953 patients (1.57%; 95% CI, 0.96%-2.58%). Across sensitivity analyses, coded IAT frequency ranged from 1.30% to 1.57%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-vendor United States claims sample, 64.5% met the selected CHOICE-2 criteria and 1.57% had an IAT code before CHOICE-2 publication. The data should be interpreted with an understanding of limitations posed by use of administrative proxies in our analysis.

articles.title: Left ventricular mass and allometrically scaled dimensions in athletic Quarter Horses: Preliminary echocardiographic reference values for Vaquejada athletes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Echocardiographic data for Quarter Horses competing in Vaquejada remain limited.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize differences in left ventricular mass (LVM), geometry, and resting systolic indices between athletic and non-trained Quarter Horses and describe preliminary echocardiographic reference values.

METHODS: Fifty Vaquejada athletes and 15 contemporaneous controls underwent echocardiography. LVM was estimated from linear dimensions and indexed to body surface area. Analyses included Welch tests, regression adjusted for age and body weight, and empirical percentiles. Interobserver agreement was assessed in 15 athletes.

RESULTS: Athletes were older and heavier. LVM was 3004.64 ± 582.95 versus 1921.13 ± 134.16 g (+56.4%), and indexed LVM was 493.91 ± 92.45 versus 333.23 ± 23.23 g/m² (+48.2%; both P < 0.001). The adjusted LVM difference was +624.43 g (95% confidence interval 398.99-849.87; P < 0.001). Athletes had larger ventricular internal diameters (12.25 versus 9.48 cm), lower relative wall thickness (0.371 versus 0.471), and lower fractional shortening (35.66 versus 41.46%) and ejection fraction (61.97 versus 69.97%; all P < 0.001). Unscaled wall-thickness measures did not differ significantly. The LVM intraclass correlation coefficient was 0.9998.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater estimated LVM and a distinct ventricular geometric pattern characterized Vaquejada athletes after adjustment for age and weight. Preliminary echocardiographic reference values provide population-specific descriptive data requiring validation. Cross-sectional findings do not establish physiological adaptation or exclude occult disease.

articles.title: Evaluation of the Suture Length-to-Wound Length Ratio as a Risk Factor for Surgical Site Infection after Exploratory Laparotomy in Horses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical site infection (SSI) is a common complication of exploratory laparotomy in horses. The suture length-to-wound length (SL:WL) ratio (suture length divided by wound length) indicates closure quality in human surgery, where a ratio of at least 4:1 reduces incisional hernia, but its relevance to SSI in horses is unknown.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To determine whether the SL:WL ratio is associated with SSI after exploratory laparotomy in horses.
