METHODS: Retrospective study of 76 horses that underwent exploratory laparotomy for colic and survived at least 15 days. SSI was defined as purulent or persistent serous/serosanguineous incisional drainage within 15 days. The SL:WL ratio was analysed as a continuous variable and in four categories (≤5, >5 and <6, ≥6 and <7, ≥7). Variables with univariable likelihood-ratio test P < 0.20 were considered for multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of the 76 horses, 20 (26.3%) developed SSI. The median SL:WL ratio was 5.98 (range 3.26-10.9). The ratio was not associated with SSI in univariable analysis (odds ratio [OR] 1.12 per unit, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.76-1.63) or after adjustment for pyrexia (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.81-1.78). SSI occurred in 23.1%, 28.0%, 14.3% and 41.2% of horses across the four categories (P = 0.302). Pyrexia before the clinical diagnosis of SSI was associated with SSI (adjusted OR 3.21, 95% CI 1.06-9.66).

CONCLUSION: In these 76 horses, the SL:WL ratio was not associated with SSI, either as a continuous variable or across categories, whereas pyrexia preceding the clinical diagnosis of SSI was.

articles.title: From PET bottle to microbial stress: In vitro effect of microplastics and Nanoplastics mix on Escherichia coli and environmental Bacteria.
articles.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs) are biologically active environmental particles, yet bacterial responses to aged, heterogeneous particles remain poorly understood. We examined artificially aged polyethylene terephthalate micro- and nanoplastics (PET-MNPs; 75, 150, and 300 mg/L) using Gram-positive and Gram-negative freshwater and marine bacteria, with Escherichia coli as a reference. Apparent growth responses depended strongly on cultivation format: 24-well plates provided the greatest discrimination for E. coli, Vibrio natriegens, and Bacillus mycoides, whereas the more oxygen-dependent species showed format-specific responses. Confocal imaging revealed species-specific cell-particle associations; however, fluorescence-based viability and oxidative-stress readouts were confounded by PET-MNP binding and particle-mediated dye activation, preventing straightforward quantitative interpretation. Proteomics identified species-specific changes associated with iron and metal homeostasis, cell-envelope remodeling, proteostasis, and RNA regulation, including increased abundance of selected secreted proteins. Together, our findings show that aged PET-MNPs act as biologically active interfaces, alter bacterial physiology in a species-dependent manner, and pose a complication for standard optical and fluorescence-based toxicity assays, which must be supplemented with complementary analyses.

articles.title: Variceal Embolization Combined With Partial Splenic Embolization for Recurrent Variceal Bleeding in Cavernous Transformation of the Portal Vein: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of variceal embolization (VE) combined with partial splenic embolization (PSE) for recurrent variceal bleeding in patients with cavernous transformation of the portal vein (CTPV) who were not candidates for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS).

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with CTPV and recurrent gastroesophageal variceal bleeding who underwent VE plus PSE between January 2020 and August 2024. The primary effectiveness endpoint was variceal rebleeding. Secondary endpoints included non-variceal rebleeding, new or worsening ascites, overt hepatic encephalopathy, changes in liver function, and survival time. Safety was assessed by procedure-related complications. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to evaluate variceal rebleeding and survival.

RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included, all had noncirrhotic CTPV (100%). Median follow-up was 825 days. Ten patients (43.5%) presented with acute bleeding; bleeding was controlled in all (immediate hemostasis rate, 100%). During follow-up, 11 patients (47.8%) experienced variceal rebleeding, with a median time to rebleeding of 217 days. New or worsening ascites occurred in 2 patients (8.7%). Two patients (8.7%) died. Liver function remained stable, with a significant increase in albumin levels at 1 year (P = .032). No major procedure-related complications were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: VE combined with PSE was feasible and demonstrated an acceptable safety profile in patients with CTPV and recurrent variceal bleeding who were not candidates for TIPS, and it may represent a treatment option in selected high-risk patients.

articles.title: Microscopic and molecular detection of blood pathogens in reptiles from South Carolina (USA).
articles.abstract: Reptiles host a wide diversity of vector-borne blood pathogens. South Carolina (SC), USA, remains understudied despite its high herpetofaunal diversity. The aim of this study was to detect the diversity, prevalence, and parasitemia of some blood pathogens in reptiles from 11 localities in SC. A total of 305 individuals representing 19 snake species (N = 164), 11 lizard species (N = 136), and 3 turtle species (N = 5) were sampled between February and July 2020. Blood smears prepared from live reptiles were examined microscopically for the presence of apicomplexans. Molecular analyses (PCR and sequencing) were performed on available blood samples from live reptiles and blood-rich organs collected from fresh road-killed individuals to detect haemogregarines, members of the family Anaplasmataceae, Rickettsia spp., and Borrelia miyamotoi. Microscopy revealed haemogregarine infections in 21.5% of examined individuals, with the highest prevalence in snakes (37.8%) and turtles (40%). PCR detected DNA from apicomplexans identified as Hepatozoon sp. and Haemogregarina sp. in 29.3% of the samples. In addition, 2% of the animals tested were positive for the presence of Anaplasmataceae including Candidatus Allocryptoplasma californiense. No sample tested positive for Rickettsia spp. or B. miyamotoi. Parasitemia varied widely among hosts (3.21-3504.85 parasites per 10,000 erythrocytes), and statistical analyses confirmed significant differences among reptile species and sampling locations. Phylogenetic analysis placed the detected haemogregarines within known clades of Hepatozoon and Haemogregarina. These results provide the first comprehensive survey of blood pathogens, including parasites, in reptiles from SC and highlight substantial variation in infection patterns among taxa and localities.

articles.title: Complementarity-determining regions 1, 2, and 3 are essential for the neutralizing activity of the monoclonal antibody HN1D4-4D9 targeting the hemagglutinin-neuraminidase protein of the Peste des Petits Ruminants virus.
articles.abstract: Peste des Petits Ruminants virus (PPRV) causes a highly contagious and often fatal disease in small ruminants, leading to substantial economic losses. The hemagglutinin-neuraminidase (HN) glycoprotein, a critical surface antigen of PPRV, is the primary target for neutralizing antibodies. In a previous study, we characterized a novel monoclonal antibody (mAb), designated HN1D4-4D9, which neutralizes PPRV by blocking viral adsorption and interfering with receptor interactions. This study aimed to identify the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) in the mAb HN1D4-4D9 that are essential for its neutralizing activity. The variable heavy (VH) and variable light (VL) chain sequences of HN1D4-4D9 were determined for the first time using HybSeq HT next-generation sequencing. The most abundant VH and VL sequences were synthesized and recombinantly expressed. Western blot analysis showed that deletion of any one of CDR1, CDR2, or CDR3 in either the heavy or light chain completely abolished antigen-antibody binding, indicating that the sequence integrity of all six CDRs is required for recognition of the antigen. Crucially, functional evaluation demonstrated that the synthetically recombinant HN1D4-4D9 mAb retained potent neutralizing activity against early PPRV infection in vitro. Co-expression of the VH and VL domains of this recombinant mAb inhibited the early stages of PPRV infection by blocking viral adsorption. Together, the sequencing and functional characterization of HN1D4-4D9 enhanced our understanding of the molecular determinants governing its neutralizing activity. These findings provide critical insights for the rational design of CDR-based peptide inhibitors or recombinant antibody therapeutics against PPRV infection.

articles.title: A candidate IMS framework for local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb in sepsis.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhubarb has traditionally been used to clear heat and remove toxins, dispel blood stasis, and promote blood circulation. Its traditional oral use and bowel-purging properties provide ethnopharmacological clues for exploring links of local-systemic regulation in sepsis.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To examine candidate intermediate substances (IMS) in local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb and representative anthraquinones, and propose a testable framework from an indirect pharmacology perspective.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this narrative review, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Google Scholar were searched through October 12, 2026. Evidence on emodin, rhein, aloe-emodin and chrysophanol was synthesized alongside traditional use, pharmacokinetics, safety and clinical findings. IMS links were appraised by mechanistic support; exploratory protein-protein interaction network analysis and molecular docking were performed.

RESULTS: Preclinical studies showed modulation of inflammation, immunity, oxidative stress and coagulation alongside reduced injury across multiple organs. Within the IMS framework, soluble mediators and immune cells represent candidate signal-transmitting links, whereas barrier integrity and microbial ecology regulate conditions for generating and propagating injurious stimuli. Exploratory network analysis prioritized candidates including AKT1, while docking suggested potential anthraquinone-protein interactions.

CONCLUSIONS: The candidate IMS framework offers a testable explanation for local-systemic links underlying multiorgan protection by rhubarb and its representative anthraquinones in sepsis. Translation requires standardized formulations, exposure characterization, functional mediator validation and clinical evaluation of benefit and safety alongside standard care.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Ca2+-redox signaling in procoagulant platelets: An emerging target for safer antithrombotic therapy.
articles.abstract: Procoagulant platelets (PPs) represent a specialized platelet subpopulation characterized by sustained cytosolic calcium (Ca2+) elevation and phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization, providing a catalytic surface that amplifies thrombin generation and thrombus formation. Emerging evidence identifies mitochondrial Ca2+ handling as a central regulator of this phenotype, linking intracellular Ca2+ dynamics with mitochondrial dysfunction and procoagulant activity. In this review, we integrate current knowledge on the mechanisms governing PPs formation, with particular emphasis on Ca2+ signaling pathways. We describe how Ca2+ release from the dense tubular system (DTS), together with store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE), drives mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake through the mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU). Mitochondrial Ca2+ overload promotes mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, leading to supramaximal cytosolic Ca2+ signals that trigger TMEM16F-mediated PS exposure and the commitment to a procoagulant state. Importantly, we highlight mitochondrial pathways-including Ca2+ signaling, reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and bioenergetic regulation-as promising therapeutic targets to selectively modulate platelet function. We further review pharmacological strategies targeting these pathways, including mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and mPTP regulation, mitochondrial redox signaling, and metabolic and bioenergetic remodeling, emphasizing the functional crosstalk among these processes. Special attention is given to mitochondria-targeted drug delivery systems based on lipophilic phosphonium cations (TPP+), which enable accumulation of bioactive compounds within platelet mitochondria. Finally, we present derivatives aimed at modulating mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and preventing PPs formation. Mitochondrial modulation attenuates experimental thrombosis while preserving hemostatic endpoints in preclinical models, although PPs also contribute to hemostasis; whether this therapeutic window exists in humans remains to be established.

articles.title: Heat Shock Proteins in Parkinson's Disease: A Dynamic Continuum from Neuroprotection to Pathology.
articles.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common neurodegenerative disorder, is pathologically defined by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) and the abnormal aggregation of α-synuclein (α-syn) into Lewy bodies, which spread from the nigrostriatal system to the olfactory bulb, lower brainstem, limbic regions, and ultimately the cerebral cortex. Heat shock proteins (HSPs) are a group of essential molecular chaperones maintaining proteostasis in this disease. However, their roles are far more complicated than previous researchers considered. This is not a simple dichotomy. We argue that HSPs are neither intrinsically protective nor pathogenic; instead, they exist on a dynamic continuum shaped by disease stage, ATP supply, and the integrity of the co-chaperone network. We propose that HSPs' functional shifts in PD may be stage-dependent: HSC70/HSP70-mediated compensatory clearance predominates in early phases, clearing misfolded/aggregated α-synuclein by inhibiting aggregation and promoting degradation to maintain protein homeostasis. In later stages of the disease, PD pathology leads to ATP depletion and co-chaperone network imbalance, shifting HSPs' function toward HSP90-driven pathogenic mechanisms. This framework moves HSPs from a binary classification to a dynamic, stage-sensitive model, with direct implications for trial design and therapeutic timing. However, a systematic overview dynamic role for HSPs remains lacking. Here, we synthesize evidence on both the protective and pathogenic roles of HSPs in PD, providing proposed ideas for a theoretical foundation for developing rational, HSP-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Modelling glucagon secretion in pancreatic α-cells from diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Impaired glucagon regulation is a major contributor to the altered glucose homeostasis observed in type 2 diabetes. Although diabetic α-cells exhibit profound changes in glucagon secretion and Ca2+ activity, the mechanisms linking altered intracellular dynamics to abnormal hormone release remain poorly understood. In this work we combine quantitative analysis of experimental Ca2+ recordings from control and diabetic (db/db) mice with a mathematical model of α-cell secretion to investigate the origin of dysregulated glucagon release. Signal-processing tools tailored to the heterogeneous, non-stationary nature of α-cell activity are used to extract per-cell descriptors of Ca2+ oscillations (frequency, amplitude, threshold crossings, cubic excursion), which feed a six-state ordinary-differential-equation model of regulated granule trafficking and exocytosis calibrated against experimental secretion data. Increased α-cell mass and glucagon content explain db/db hypersecretion at low glucose; high glucose additionally requires faster effective fusion and priming. A global variance-based (Sobol') sensitivity analysis then quantifies the contribution of the model parameters and initial conditions to the cumulative secretion. Under the biologically-defensible assumption of unchanged Ca2+-sensor kinetics, the two parameters with the largest total-order effect are the maximal fusion rate and the total granule count. The model predicts a redistribution of granules towards the primed and readily releasable pools in diabetic α-cells at high glucose, providing a mechanistic explanation for sustained hyperglucagonemia. The study illustrates how kinetic modelling combined with variance-based sensitivity analysis can turn single-cell measurements into mechanistic insight, an approach transferable to other hormone-releasing cell systems.

articles.title: Beyond longevity: Cardiovascular prevention and healthy brain aging.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular prevention has extended life expectancy, and the question now is whether the added years are accompanied by preserved cognition and independence. This review asks what cardiologists can do for brain health today, on what evidence and for whom. We keep apart three brain health outcomes that are often treated as one, namely cognitive test performance, incident mild cognitive impairment or dementia, and years lived with preserved cognition, and we separate observational associations from randomized evidence. We also review vascular-neurodegenerative interactions and life-course risk-factor management. The 2024 Lancet Commission estimate that approximately 45% of dementia is attributable to 14 modifiable factors is a modelled population attributable fraction, not a measured treatment effect. Among interventions on these factors, blood-pressure lowering has the strongest randomized evidence, mainly for mild cognitive impairment, with some evidence for dementia, whereas signals for other cardiovascular drug classes remain unconfirmed. Multidomain programs improve cognitive test scores modestly, but several trials were neutral. Emerging tools improve prediction but have not been shown to improve preventive management in asymptomatic patients. Anti-amyloid therapies for Alzheimer's disease challenge antithrombotic and blood-pressure decisions traditionally located within the cardiologist's remit, under regulatory conditions that differ by region. We close with ten practical proposals classified by type of supporting evidence, including cognitive assessment whenever the result would change care, a checklist for cardiology input before anti-amyloid therapy, and a minimum set of cognitive outcomes for cardiovascular trials. We argue, as a synthesis rather than a proven effect of every cardiovascular intervention, that cardiovascular prevention is already, in part, dementia prevention, and that cognitively healthy life-years should be measured as one of its outcomes.

articles.title: Spinal Shock and the Bulbocavernosus Reflex: A Systematic Review of an Untested Clinical Rule.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Standard teaching holds that acute spinal cord injury (SCI) may produce a flaccid, areflexic state termed spinal shock, that the bulbocavernosus reflex (BCR) is typically lost and returns as that state resolves, and that classification and prognostication should await its return.

PURPOSE: This review tested each component against clinical data.

STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review with educational-resource analysis.

PATIENT SAMPLE: Twenty-seven studies of spinal shock and sacral reflexes after SCI.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Five prespecified questions on spinal shock definition, acute flaccid paralysis, initial BCR absence, BCR return, and prognosis.

METHODS: MEDLINE and Embase were searched through August 2026. Data were extracted and risk of bias was assessed in duplicate, and certainty was rated with GRADE.

RESULTS: Three of 20 studies fully documented flaccidity with depressed tendon reflexes, but global areflexia was uncommon. The BCR was frequently present during clinically defined spinal shock and after complete injury, so its absence did not define that state. It was absent in some neurologically intact adults and changed state without documented neurological change, and its reproducibility as a marker was not established. Initial BCR status showed no association with neurological recovery in three studies at high risk of bias. No study documented BCR return at resolution of flaccid paralysis. Neurological prognostic evidence was of very low certainty.

CONCLUSIONS: The teaching that BCR absence defines spinal shock is not supported, and deferring classification and prognostication until BCR return is untested. Such a rule, propagated through surgical training, shapes examination, counseling, and bedside decisions.

articles.title: Impact of Complete Resident Absence on Perioperative Outcomes in Spine Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using the 2024 South Korean Medical Crisis as a Natural Experiment.
articles.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND CONTEXT: Resident physicians have key intraoperative and perioperative roles in academic spine surgery. How spine surgery outcomes change when all residents are absent at the same time is not known.

PURPOSE: To determine whether complete resident absence is associated with differences in perioperative outcomes of spine surgery after adjustment for confounders, and whether any association differs by surgical complexity.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study using the 2024 South Korean resident walkout, a mass resignation of resident physicians, as a natural experiment.

PATIENT SAMPLE: We included 258 consecutive patients who underwent elective thoracolumbar or lumbar spine surgery by one attending surgeon at a single tertiary academic center. Patients were treated in a with-resident period (December 2022-February 2024; n = 129) or a without-resident period (March 2024-August 2025; n = 129). Surgical complexity was graded as Grade 1, discectomy; Grade 2, 1-2 level posterior instrumented fusion, predominantly posterior lumbar interbody fusion; or Grade 3, ≥3-level fusion, corpectomy, or revision fusion.

OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were operative time, estimated blood loss (EBL), and postoperative hospital stay. Secondary outcomes were a composite complication endpoint (dural tear, transfusion, surgical site infection, reoperation, or intensive care unit admission), its individual components, 30-day readmission, and in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: Groups were compared without adjustment and with multivariable regression. Sensitivity analyses used propensity score weighting, calendar-matched windows, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class strata, and procedure restriction. This study received no funding, and the authors report no study-specific conflicts of interest.

RESULTS: After adjustment for confounders, complete resident absence was not associated with significant differences in operative time (β = +6.3 min; 95% CI, -8.0 to 20.7; p = 0.386), EBL (β = +27.0 mL; 95% CI, -68.4 to 122.3; p = 0.578), hospital stay (β = +1.6 days; 95% CI, -2.1 to 5.4; p = 0.394), or composite complications (odds ratio, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.50-1.93; p = 0.967). No sensitivity analysis showed a significant difference. ASA class 3 patients made up 46.5% of the with-resident group and 25.6% of the without-resident group. The surgeon's operative volume declined by 30% over calendar-matched 12-month windows. No resident-by-complexity interaction was significant. In exploratory stratified comparisons, hospital stay among Grade 1 patients was longer without residents (Hodges-Lehmann median difference, 1.0 day; 95% CI, 0.0-2.0; p = 0.020). Among Grade 3 patients, dural tear occurred in 0% with residents and 8.7% without residents (p = 0.121).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-surgeon cohort, complete resident absence was not associated with statistically significant differences in short-term perioperative outcomes. However, surgery during the walkout was concentrated in lower-risk patients, volume declined, and confidence intervals were wide. These findings therefore do not show that outcomes were unaffected. The stratum-specific findings are exploratory and need confirmation in adequately powered multicenter studies.

articles.title: Consensus document on best practices in paediatric anaesthesia in Spain.
articles.journal: Revista espanola de anestesiologia y reanimacion
articles.abstract: Pediatric anaesthesia is associated with a higher risk of critical adverse events, especially in children under 3 years of age and in patients with comorbidities. En Spain persiste variabilidad en la formación de los equipos, la disponibilidad de recursos y los circuitos asistenciales, lo que condiciona inequidades de seguridad y calidad. El objetivo de este documento es sintetizar recomendaciones de buenas prácticas dirigidas a garantizar una atención anestesiológica pediátrica segura, homogénea y de calidad. Las recomendaciones fueron elaboradas por un grupo de expertos de la sección pediátrica de la SEDAR mediante revisión narrativa de la evidencia y consenso, y posteriormente ratificadas por la junta directiva de la SEDAR. Se establecen criterios de selección de pacientes y de adecuación del centro según la edad, la complejidad y el estado ASA, estándares de competencias profesionales, requisitos mínimos de dotación y recursos materiales y recomendaciones específicas para quirófano, áreas alejadas de quirófano, URPA y unidades de críticos.

articles.title: Beyond Amyloid in Alzheimer's Disease: A Multiscale Evidence-Based Review of Pathogenesis, Biomarkers, and Emerging Therapeutics.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterised neuropathologically by amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation, phosphorylated-tau neurofibrillary tangles, synaptic dysfunction, and neuronal loss. However, the temporal and causal relationships underlying disease initiation, progression, and clinical heterogeneity remain incompletely resolved. Increasing evidence supports a multiscale model in which amyloid-tau pathology intersects with genetic susceptibility, epigenetic regulation, impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial and metabolic stress, neuroimmune activation, vascular dysfunction, and declining neural resilience. Familial variants in APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 directly perturb amyloid processing, whereas APOE ε4, TREM2, and polygenic variation influence lipid metabolism, protein clearance, vascular integrity, and glial responses. DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, and non-coding RNAs may further shape neuronal and immune states, although their directionality and causal significance remain incompletely established. Similarly, microbial and environmental exposures have been associated with inflammatory and proteostatic alterations, but definitive evidence for causation in sporadic AD is lacking. This review integrates genetic, epigenetic, proteostatic, metabolic, neuroimmune, vascular, and environmental mechanisms across disease stages and cellular compartments. We critically evaluate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma biomarkers, amyloid/tau PET, multimodal imaging, extracellular vesicles, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approaches for diagnosis, prognosis, stratification, and therapeutic prioritisation. Therapeutic evidence is stratified from established symptomatic treatments and approved anti-amyloid antibodies to investigational tau-, immune-, epigenetic-, RNA-, microbiome-, stem-cell-, neuromodulatory-, and nanoparticle-based strategies. By distinguishing causal human evidence from observational, experimental, and computational findings, this synthesis identifies priorities for biomarker-guided, stage-specific, and mechanism-informed interventions while avoiding premature inference of causality or clinical benefit.

articles.title: Outcomes of Surgery After Neoadjuvant Chemoimmunotherapy in Selected N3 Stage III Non-small cell lung cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the conversion of unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to resectable status is a growing area of research, few studies have delineated the prognosis of clinical N3 patients undergoing surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. This retrospective study compared the outcomes of stage III patients with NSCLC at clinical N3 who successfully underwent surgical resection after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy with those of stage III N0-2 patients who received the same treatment followed by surgery in a matched cohort.

METHODS: Drawing from a database of patients with NSCLC at Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital (2019-2023), we identified individuals with clinical Stage III (N3) disease, as well as those with Stage III (N0-2) disease, who underwent surgical resection following neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. For these patients, after completion of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, mandatory re-biopsy of the originally involved N3 stations (via EBUS-TBNA or supraclavicular puncture) was required to confirm pathological negativity before surgical resection was subsequently performed only for cases validated as resectable by a multi-disciplinary team assessment. We utilized 3:1 propensity score matching to adjust for baseline imbalances between the study cohorts. The primary outcome was Disease-Free Survival (DFS).

RESULTS: In the matched cohort, 57 patients with clinical Stage III (N3) NSCLC and 171 paired patients with clinical Stage III (N0-2) analysis showed that the objective response rate (ORR) was 62.2% in the N3 cohort and 69.1% in the N0-2 cohort. Additionally, the 3-year DFS rates were 67.2% vs 73.3% (hazard ratio = 1.37; 95% confidence interval = 0.76-2.49, P= .29). Further subgroup analysis revealed that the DFS rates of 22 patients with Biopsy-confirmed cN3 disease and 35 patients with PET/CT-confirmed cN3 disease were similar, and the 3-year DFS rates were 59.3% vs 72.2% (hazard ratio = 1.43; 95% confidence interval = 0.56-3.64, P = .45). Multivariate analysis suggested that pathological complete response (pCR) was an independent predictor of DFS prolongation in the N3 cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: For carefully selected patients with stage III (N3) NSCLC who achieve downstaging and undergo surgery after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, postoperative DFS is comparable to that of N0-2 patients, supporting surgical intervention as a component of multimodal therapy in this specific subset of patients who achieve surgical conversion.

articles.title: Exploratory evaluation of treponemal IgA enzyme immunoassays with commercial antigens for serological diagnosis and post-treatment follow-up of syphilis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The laboratory diagnosis of syphilis relies on serological detection of treponemal and non-treponemal IgG and IgM antibodies. Limited evidence suggests the potential of IgA as a marker of infection. We exploratory evaluated the treponemal IgA response using two enzyme immunoassays (EIAs) and assessed its value during first infections, reinfections, and post-treatment follow-up.

METHODS: A panel of 253 sera from 85 syphilis episodes (41 first infections, 44 reinfections) and 50 non-syphilitic controls was analysed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of two IgA EIAs adapted from commercially available IgM assay kits from Dia.Pro (Italy) and Euroimmun (Germany).

RESULTS: Overall sensitivity was 96.5-100%, while specificity was 98% for both assays. In reinfections, patients with secondary syphilis showed a ≥2-fold increase in IgA optical density (OD) values, whereas only a minority of patients in primary or latent stages met this criterion. For treatment monitoring, IgA levels declined consistently after treatment, with most patients achieving a ≥50% reduction in OD within 6-12 months.

CONCLUSIONS: Treponemal IgA assays combine characteristics of non-treponemal and treponemal tests, suggesting potential for both syphilis detection and treatment monitoring. Larger longitudinal studies are required to validate their potential in diagnosing reinfection and integration into syphilis diagnostic algorithms.

articles.title: Complete HIV-1 Seroreversion After Advanced HIV Infection Diagnosed in Adolescence: A Case Report.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: Decreased or lost serologic reactivity to human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) has been described primarily when antiretroviral therapy (ART) is initiated during acute infection. Complete seroreversion after presentation with advanced disease and a fully developed confirmatory serologic response is exceptional. A 16-year-old male was admitted in May 2021 with weight loss, progressive neurocognitive impairment, and pneumonia. Two specimens were reactive by immunoassay, and Western blot confirmed antibodies to gp160, gp41, p55, p24/p25, and p18/p17. The baseline viral load was 2,654,451 copies/mL, and the CD4+ T-cell count was 38 cells/µL. ART with dolutegravir/abacavir/lamivudine was initiated, with rapid virologic suppression and immunologic recovery. In August 2023, two independent specimens were nonreactive on repeat serologic testing and negative by Western blot, while plasma HIV-1 RNA remained suppressed. LTR amplification followed by Sanger sequencing yielded a sequence matching HIV-1 sequences (identity, 92.93-93.94%; E = 2 × 10⁻²⁹ to 2 × 10⁻³⁰), providing molecular evidence compatible with cell-associated HIV-1 genetic material. The CCR5 genotype was wild-type/wild-type, and neither HLA-B*27 nor HLA-B*57 was identified. Through February 2026, plasma RNA remained undetectable during ART; through March 2026, serology remained negative. Negative serology did not invalidate the diagnosis, which was supported by high-level viremia, advanced immunodeficiency, and a positive Western blot, and it should not prompt withdrawal of the established diagnosis or discontinuation of ART outside an ethical and closely monitored protocol. CCR5/HLA did not in itself explain the seroreversion, underscoring the importance of interpreting discordant results in their clinical context.

articles.title: Factors associated with progression of hepatic steatosis, progression of liver fibrosis, and de novo MASLD in people with HIV: a 5-year transient elastography cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in people with HIV (PWH), yet its long-term progression is poorly characterized. We examined the 5-year cumulative incidence of hepatic steatosis progression, liver fibrosis progression, and de novo MASLD in PWH, and the factors associated with each outcome.

METHODS: In a retrospectively constructed cohort with prospective follow-up, 361 PWH underwent baseline transient elastography (December 2019-April 2020), of whom 315 completed reassessment by February 2026. Outcomes were assessed by controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement. We estimated cumulative incidences and used multivariable modified Poisson regression with robust variance, adjusted for age and follow-up duration, to identify factors associated with each outcome, applying Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction within outcomes.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 67.3 months, steatosis progressed in 83 of 273 eligible participants (30.4%), fibrosis in 47 of 278 (16.9%), and de novo MASLD developed in 65 of 193 (33.7%). Greater relative weight gain was associated with all three outcomes (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] per 10-percentage-point increase: 1.27 for steatosis progression, 1.20 for fibrosis progression, and 1.35 for de novo MASLD; all FDR-adjusted P < 0.001). Baseline MASLD was associated with liver fibrosis progression (aRR 3.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.61-5.69), whereas its association with hepatic steatosis progression was imprecise (1.72, 0.87-3.37). Type 2 diabetes (2.51, 1.52-4.14) and longer time since HIV diagnosis (1.06 per year, 1.02-1.10) were also associated with fibrosis progression. Higher baseline CAP was associated with de novo MASLD (1.26 per 10 dB/m, 1.12-1.42). Baseline integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) use was not clearly associated with any outcome (aRR for de novo MASLD 1.01, 0.59-1.72).

CONCLUSIONS: In PWH, baseline MASLD, type 2 diabetes, and longer time since HIV diagnosis were associated with liver fibrosis progression. Greater relative weight gain was consistently associated with de novo MASLD and progression of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, highlighting the clinical relevance of weight monitoring and management.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06940375.

articles.title: Global Research Trends at the Intersection of Macular Degeneration and Refractive Error: A Bibliometric and Visual Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the publication patterns, collaborative networks, and thematic developments at the intersection of macular degeneration and refractive error using a bibliometric analysis.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A comprehensive search of the Web of Science Core Collection (SCI-Expanded and SSCI) was conducted from 1 January 2004 to 31 December 2024. The search combined keywords for macular degeneration (e.g., "AMD," "choroidal neovascularization") and refractive error (e.g., "myopia," "hypermetropia"). After screening, 1,716 peer-reviewed English-language publications were included. CiteSpace (v6.3.R3) and VOSviewer (v1.6.20) were used for collaboration networks, co-citation maps, and keyword co-occurrence analysis. Microsoft Excel supported descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 1,716 publications were included. Publication output increased markedly after 2016 and peaked in 2024. China contributed the most publications, while the United States showed the highest citation count and total link strength. Jost B. Jonas and Kyoko Ohno-Matsui were the most productive authors. Keyword analysis showed growing interest in artificial intelligence, deep learning, and myopia control alongside established treatment and imaging topics. Citation-based comparisons for recent years should be interpreted cautiously because these publications have had shorter citation windows.

CONCLUSIONS: Macular degeneration and refractive error research has grown substantially over the past two decades. China leads in output, while the United States leads in citation impact and collaboration strength. This gap suggests that publication volume does not always translate into research influence. Artificial intelligence has emerged as a rising direction. These findings may help researchers identify collaboration opportunities and future priorities.

articles.title: Photodynamic Therapy for Anti-infection in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Review of Clinical Evidence and Practical Challenges.
articles.abstract: Infected diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) carry high infection and amputation risks, and conventional therapies are increasingly limited by antibiotic resistance and biofilms. This review evaluated the clinical efficacy and safety of antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) as an adjunctive treatment for infected DFUs and mapped barriers to translation. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through January 2025 for clinical studies of aPDT in infected DFUs. Seventeen eligible studies were included, comprising randomized controlled trials (RCTs), non-randomized controlled studies, case series, and case reports. Data on protocols, outcomes, and safety were extracted and synthesized narratively; risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. aPDT consistently reduced microbial burden, with a dose-dependent reduction of up to -2.94 log10 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL (p < 0.001), and promoted wound closure. One controlled study reported lower amputation rates with aPDT than with control (5.6% vs. 100%; p = 0.002). Adverse events were mainly transient local pain or burning. However, evidence certainty was low to very low because of high risk of bias, heterogeneous photosensitizers/light doses/treatment schedules, small samples, and short follow-up. Key translational barriers include non-standardized protocols, wound hypoxia, exudate, limited light penetration, and weak health-economic data. Although promising, aPDT is not yet ready for routine adoption. Priority should be given to protocol harmonization, biomarker-guided patient selection, and large pragmatic trials. This review maps the evidence and proposes a tiered research roadmap.

articles.title: Trends in Atrial Fibrillation and Atrial Flutter Management in Reproductive-Age Women: GWTG-AFib Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The occurrence of cardiac arrhythmias in reproductive-aged women has increased in the United States. Management remains challenging due to limited guideline evidence and the maternal/fetal risks associated with many anti-arrhythmia therapies.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize prescription patterns and management trends in the treatment of atrial arrhythmias in reproductive-aged women over the past decade.

METHODS: The Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)-Atrial Fibrillation registry was queried between 2013 and 2024, and all women of reproductive-age (≤50 years) hospitalized with atrial fibrillation (AFib) or flutter (AFL) were included. Medications were classified into low risk, conflicted, and avoided/contraindicated during pregnancy. Discharge prescribing patterns of the most used anticoagulants, antiarrhythmic agents, and rate control medications were analyzed. Temporal trends were assessed using the Cochrane-Armitage test, and group comparisons were performed using Chi-square analysis.

RESULTS: Among 3,755 hospitalizations for AFib or AFL in reproductive-aged women between 2013 and 2024, 2,732 (72.8%) were discharged on an anticoagulant, while 1,380 (36.8%) received an antiarrhythmic medication. Overall, 75.3% of encounters were discharged on medications generally classified as avoided/contraindicated during pregnancy, with a significant upward trend in the use of such medications over the study period (p<0.05), largely driven by increased anticoagulant use. New-onset AFib accounted for 651 hospitalizations (20.5%), with rhythm-control strategies used more frequently than rate control in this subgroup (62%).

CONCLUSION: The frequent and increasing use of medications with potential pregnancy-related concerns highlights the need for reproductive-specific guidance that integrates arrhythmia management with reproductive planning and medication safety.

articles.title: Comparison of Pulsed Field Ablation Technologies for Atrial Fibrillation Ablation: a Systematic Review and Pairwise Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Commercial pulsed field ablation (PFA) platforms differ in catheter geometry, mapping integration, irrigation, and energy-delivery strategy.

OBJECTIVE: To compare FARAPULSE, VARIPULSE, PulseSelect, Affera/Sphere-9, and Volt across procedural, biological, safety, and efficacy outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through October 8, 2026. Separate random-effects pairwise meta-analyses were performed for each direct device comparison. Exploratory analyses examined lesion strategy, publication year, electroanatomic mapping, and intracardiac echocardiography.

RESULTS: Forty-six observational reports representing 43 studies were included. VARIPULSE workflows used less fluoroscopy than FARAPULSE (MD -13.54 minutes; 95% CI -18.89 to -8.19) and PulseSelect (MD -11.45; 95% CI -16.96 to -5.94), while Affera/Sphere-9 used less than FARAPULSE (MD -7.20; 95% CI -10.27 to -4.14). Affera/Sphere-9 showed less haptoglobin depletion than FARAPULSE, PulseSelect, and VARIPULSE; Volt showed less than FARAPULSE. No platform consistently shortened procedure time or differed clearly in overall complications or acute kidney injury. Comparative durability remained limited outside FARAPULSE and PulseSelect.

CONCLUSION: The platforms showed distinct workflow and biomarker profiles without one uniformly superior system. VARIPULSE and Affera/Sphere-9 workflows used less fluoroscopy in available direct comparisons, and Affera/Sphere-9 and Volt showed less haptoglobin depletion in selected comparisons. These biomarker findings did not establish a renal or hard clinical advantage. Comparative durability remains uncertain.

articles.title: Electrocardiographic imaging of ventricular activation and repolarization in PLN- and PKP2-cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 12-lead electrocardiograms, though commonly used in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy diagnosis, lack spatial detail. Electrocardiographic imaging (ECGI) offers a comprehensive assessment of cardiac electrical activity and may better detect electrical abnormalities to identify individuals at risk of disease expression.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize activation and repolarization in Plakophilin-2 (PKP2) and Phospholamban (PLN) pathogenic variant carriers compared to controls.

METHODS: ECGI was used to estimate cardiac activation and repolarization in controls and PKP2-/PLN-carriers. Patterns most frequently observed in controls subjects were classified as normal activation/repolarization; distinct patterns as delayed right/left ventricular (RV/LV) activation/repolarization.

RESULTS: 131 subjects (40 [27;54] years, 55% female) were included: 20 controls and 111 variant carriers with absent or variable phenotypes (54 PKP2, 57 PLN). Ventricular arrhythmias occurred more frequently in PKP2-carriers with delayed RV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (85% vs 21%, P<0.001), and more often in PLN-carriers with delayed LV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (38% vs 0%, P=0.003). T-wave inversions (TWI) in V1-V3 were more often observed in PKP2-carriers with delayed RV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (77% vs 0%, P<0.001), and TWI in V4-V6 were more common in PLN-carriers with delayed LV repolarization compared to normal repolarization (50% vs 4%, P=0.001). Delayed repolarization was also identified in 31% of pre-symptomatic PLN-carriers. Delayed activation was not associated with a more severe phenotype.

CONCLUSION: Delayed repolarization was associated with more severe phenotypic disease expression. As delayed RV/LV repolarization was also identified in a subset of pre-symptomatic variant carriers, ECGI may aid early risk stratification of pathogenic variant carriers.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation in elderly patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data regarding the safety and clinical efficacy of pulsed field ablation (PFA) for atrial fibrillation (AF) in older patients are limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and impact on healthcare utilization of PFA for AF in patients aged ≥75 years.

METHODS: This sub-study of the multicenter SENTINEL registry included consecutive patients undergoing first-time AF ablation with a pentaspline PFA system across 13 centers in Australia and New Zealand. Outcomes were compared among patients aged <65 years, 65-74 years, and ≥75 years. Primary endpoints were major procedural complications and healthcare utilization (composite of unplanned rehospitalization for atrial arrhythmia, cardioversion and repeat catheter ablation).

RESULTS: Of 1,611 patients, 769 (48%) were aged <65 years, 573 (36%) aged 65-74 years and 269 (17%) aged ≥75 years. Patients aged ≥75 years had greater comorbidity burden, and higher prevalence of non-paroxysmal AF and left atrial dilatation. Major procedural complications were uncommon and similar across age groups (0.9%, 0.2% and 0.7%, respectively; p=0.48). Over a median follow-up of 426 days, healthcare utilization (10.8%, 12.0% and 10.0%; p=0.61) and arrhythmia recurrence (17.2%, 19.5% and 19.3%; p=0.39) were comparable across age groups. Age ≥75 years was not independently associated with healthcare utilization or arrhythmia recurrence after multivariable adjustment and propensity score matching.

CONCLUSION: In this large multicenter study, low procedural complication rates and comparable clinical outcomes were observed across age groups following PFA for AF, supporting individualized selection of patients for AF ablation rather than categorical exclusion based on age alone.

articles.title: Hyperactivation of p53 and pRb is a potential therapeutic option in HPV driven cancers.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most frequently acquired sexually transmitted infection. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of HPV mainly contribute to the development of cancerous lesions by dysregulating the host p53 and pRb tumour suppressor pathways, respectively. Although prophylactic vaccines are available for HPV infection, they are ineffective for established HPV infections. Despite significant advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapies, recurrent, metastatic, and treatment-resistant HPV-associated cancers continue to present substantial clinical challenges, highlighting the urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies.As the E6 and E7 viral oncoproteins are key drivers of HPV-positive cancer pathogenesis, targeting these proteins represents a rational approach for developing new therapies. Gene therapy is currently studied extensively as a potential strategy for cancer regression. RNA interference technology and CRISPR approaches are highly effective in downregulating the expression of viral oncoproteins. In most cancer types, tumour suppressor proteins are frequently mutated; however, in HPV-induced cancers, they typically remain wild type. Hence, increasing the bioavailability of tumour suppressor proteins is a therapeutic option. CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) is a CRISPR system variant in which catalytically inactive Cas9 (dcas9) is fused with a transcriptional activator to induce gene expression. Unlike CRISPR, CRISPRa increases the expression of the targeted gene without genomic modifications. Although there are few strategies available to increase the expression of tumour suppressor proteins, CRISPRa has gained a major focus as an effective and promising strategy. There is potential to develop CRISPRa as a future therapeutic intervention to treat HPV induced cancers combined with other treatment modalities.

articles.title: Interpretable MEG decoding of perceived speech: Source-space patterns and the stimulus features that drive retrieval.
articles.abstract: Short segments of perceived speech can be retrieved from non-invasive magnetoencephalographic (MEG) recordings by a deep network trained with a CLIP-style objective against wav2vec 2.0 audio embeddings (Défossez et al., 2023; Baevski et al., 2020; Radford et al., 2021). Such studies do not convert their weights into the notions used in classical electrophysiology. Although the spatial filters in the front end of Défossez et al. (2023) could in principle be mapped to source topographies, the dynamic properties of those sources remain out of reach. Which properties of the speech stream contribute to the decoding is equally unclear. Here we scrutinize a decoder with a physiologically motivated, factorized spatial-temporal front end that permits joint interpretation of learned spatial topographies and temporal patterns in relation to the MEG forward model. Building on the framework of Petrosyan et al. (2021, 2022), we replace the 2D Fourier spatial attention of Défossez et al. (2023) with a layer parameterized by spherical harmonics (Sivakumar et al., 2016), reduce the subject-specific representation from 270 to K=25 branches, and add trainable temporal filters so that each branch has an explicit learned spatial filter and temporal response. Ocular and cardiac components are removed before training, since either could supply stimulus-locked information that would otherwise be mistaken for cortical. On the cleaned MEG-MASC dataset (Gwilliams et al., 2023) the model reaches 39.75±0.34% Top-1 accuracy among 1005 candidates across six model initializations (mean ± SD), with approximately 20× fewer trainable parameters in the decoder. Its learned spatial patterns can be mapped through a cortical inverse model (Petrosyan et al., 2021; Haufe et al., 2014), yielding approximate source-magnitude projections with recurrent bilateral structure over lateral cortex, concentrated around temporal and adjacent peri-Sylvian regions. Paired MEG occlusion, replacing feature-marked speech segments with matched donors from feature-present and feature-absent intervals, shows significant positive effects for 15 of 19 tested stimulus features, the largest effects being silence, sound intensity, vowels and acoustic onsets. Intriguingly, the randomly ordered word lists behave oppositely: replacing word-list MEG with MEG recorded during coherent narrative improves retrieval relative to word-list donor MEG. The wav2vec target can be reduced to about twelve learned feature dimensions with only a small reduction in retrieval accuracy, whereas strong temporal compression causes a clear performance loss. Decoders with physiologically interpretable spatial-temporal front ends can thus serve as knowledge-discovery tools: their learned weights can be converted into source-space and temporal patterns, while input interventions reveal what the decision rule relies on.

articles.title: SUMOylation in adipose tissue formation and plasticity: SUMOylation supports adipocyte homeostasis.
articles.abstract: The inability of the adipose tissue to properly handle release and storage of fatty acids increases the risk of metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer, indicating a need to strengthen knowledge about the biologic functions of adipose tissue in mediating physiological processes and disease development. This review investigates the contribution of posttranslational modifications of target proteins by small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) peptides, the process known as SUMOylation, to adipogenesis and adipose tissue identity. SUMOylation is essential to maintain cellular homeostasis, especially through nuclear activities like transcription and epigenetic mechanisms. We propose a model depicting how the SUMOylation pathway supports adipocyte differentiation from mesenchymal stem cells into adipocytes, and thus how it contributes to adipocyte identity and fate. In addition, the model illustrates how SUMOylation regulates key adipogenic transcription factors, including CCAAT/enhancer-binding proteins (CEBPs) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARG), acting to safeguard physiologic lipid storage. Understanding SUMOylation's role in adipocyte formation, function and fate may offer novel perspectives for metabolic disease therapeutics.

articles.title: PVI Using the Fixed Loop PFA in Paroxysmal AF: One-Year Outcomes with Continuous Implantable Loop Recorder Monitoring.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is a promising non-thermal energy modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF), with favorable safety and efficacy data. However, published data rely on intermittent rhythm monitoring, which likely underestimates recurrence rates. We sought to evaluate 12-month outcomes of PVI using the PulseSelect™ system in patients with paroxysmal AF (PAF) monitored continuously with implantable loop recorders (ILRs), and to characterize the performance of a standardized "6-4" lesion delivery workflow.

METHODS: This is a single-center, prospective observational study of consecutive patients aged <75 years with symptomatic, PAF and an ILR. All ablations were performed using the PulseSelect™ catheter using a standardized workflow delivering 6 antral and 4 ostial PFA applications per pulmonary vein (PV), guided by left-sided intracardiac echocardiography. The primary endpoint was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias from 91 to 365 days post-ablation, assessed by continuous ILR.

RESULTS: Twenty-five patients (13 male, 12 females; mean age 68.3 ± 4.2 years; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.5 ± 0.6) underwent PVI between August and November 2024. Acute PVI was achieved in 100% of PVs. Median procedure and left atrial dwell times were 74 (IQR 48-82) and 44 (IQR 34-57) minutes, respectively. Mean fluoroscopy time was 3.2 ± 1.7 minutes. At 12 months, freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias off class I/III antiarrhythmic drugs was observed in 22 of 25 patients (88%).

CONCLUSIONS: In a PAF cohort with mandatory continuous rhythm monitoring, the PulseSelect™ system using a standardized workflow achieved universal acute PVI and favorable 12-month arrhythmia-free outcomes with an excellent safety profile. Continuous monitoring provides the most rigorous assessment of freedom from recurrence.

articles.title: Developing a clinical prediction model for common bile duct stones: A dual-centre NHS cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediction of common bile duct stones (CBDs) may improve the efficiency of MRCP services by reducing unnecessary scans and prioritising patients most likely to benefit. Although current guidelines provide risk-stratified pathways, uncertainty remains in selecting patients for MRCP, and a substantial proportion of scans are normal. This study aimed to identify independent clinical, biochemical and radiological predictors of CBDs.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of a consecutive 300 patients from two NHS hospitals who had MRCP to assess for CBDs. Clinical (cholangitis, pancreatitis), biochemical (initial and pre-MRCP liver function tests (LFTs), trends of LFTs) and radiological (ultrasound findings) variables were analysed. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression were used to identify significant and independent predictors. Our proposed multivariate model predicting CBDs was evaluated using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: CBDs were identified in 37% of patients. Univariate analysis identified significant predictors including age (P<0.001), pre-MRCP bilirubin (P=0.001), pre-MRCP alkaline phosphatase (P=0.003), ultrasound findings (P=0.004), and LFTs trend (P<0.001). Multivariate analysis revealed statistically independent predictors as older age (OR 1.021 per year; P=0.006), abnormal ultrasound findings (OR 1.812; P=0.026), and persistently high or rising LFTs trends (OR 2.150; P=0.027). This multivariate model demonstrated an AUC of 0.718 (95% CI: 0.660-0.776, P<0.001), indicating an acceptable diagnostic performance for CBDs. Marginal predictors included male gender (OR 1.681, P=0.081) and pre-MRCP bilirubin (OR 1.009, P=0.081).

CONCLUSION: Increasing age, abnormal ultrasound findings, and rising or persistently high LFT trends were independent predictors of CBD stones. These readily available variables may support risk assessment and prioritisation of further investigation; however, prospective validation is required before the model can be incorporated into clinical pathways.

articles.title: Looking further at 'lean' metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease - how much does weight influence outcomes?
Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and eye-related outcomes - A systematic review and meta-analysis. OphthoEvidence Report 1.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials examining the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) use across all clinical indications and ocular outcomes.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: GLP-1 RAs are widely used to manage diabetes, obesity, and other cardiometabolic conditions. However, their effects on diabetic retinopathy and other ocular outcomes remain uncertain.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to August 2025. Eligible trials compared any GLP-1 RAs with placebo, standard care or active comparator for patients with any clinical indication. Pairs of reviewers conducted study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessments independently. We performed random-effects meta-analyses and rated certainty of evidence using GRADE.

RESULTS: A total of 142 trials enrolling 172,050 participants met eligibility criteria. Moderate to high certainty evidence suggests GLP-1 RAs probably increase the risk of diabetic retinopathy (odds ratio (OR) 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.15 [1.03-1.28]), vitreous hemorrhage (OR 95% CI 1.64 [1.08-2.49]), need for retinal procedures (OR 95% CI 1.37 [1.07-1.75]), total retinal vascular disorders (OR 95% CI 1.54 [1.12-2.12]), including retinal vascular occlusion (2.33 [1.22-4.45]). High certainty evidence also showed GLP-1 RAs reduce glaucoma risk (0.58 [0.34-0.99]). Moderate certainty evidence suggests GLP-1 RAs likely have little to no effect on the risk of cataract (0.95 [0.85 - 1.06]) and retinal detachment (1.40 [0.87 - 2.27]). We are very uncertain about the effects of GLP-1 RAs on age-related macular degeneration (0.91 [0.15-5.45]) and ischemic optic neuropathy (2.19 [0.49-9.85]). Results were consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to placebo- or standard-care-controlled trials, and follow-up duration did not modify the effects for any outcome.

CONCLUSION: Moderate- to high-certainty evidence suggests that GLP-1 RAs likely result in an increase in the risk of selected retinal events, but reduce the risk of glaucoma. Given the low absolute incidence of these events, clinicians can counsel patients that the ocular risks of GLP-1 RAs are small and likely outweighed by their cardiometabolic benefits, while advising early monitoring for retinal events in those with diabetes or pre-existing retinopathy.

articles.title: Integrated Surveillance of Bloodborne Pathogen Exposure and Suboptimal Health Status for Occupational Infection Prevention Among Healthcare Workers: A Pre-Post Intervention Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bloodborne pathogen exposure (BBPE) remains a major occupational hazard among healthcare workers (HCWs). Universal precautions overlook individual susceptibility. Suboptimal health status (SHS) is linked to impaired occupational performance, yet is rarely integrated into prevention strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a pre-post intervention study among HCWs at a tertiary hospital. Baseline data were collected in July 2024 (n=2,637), followed by an 11-month integrated intervention combining training, surveillance, post-exposure management, and wellness support. Post-intervention evaluation was conducted in July 2025 (n=2,590). BBPE and SHS outcomes were compared across periods. Independent risk factors were identified for risk-stratified modelling.

RESULTS: BBPE incidence decreased from 7.02% to 3.47%. Reporting increased from 58.4% to 82.2%, while mastery of prevention knowledge improved from 23.9% to 56.7%. Male sex, physician occupation, surgical/emergency staff, lower post-exposure management compliance, and higher SHS burden were independently associated with BBPE. A risk prediction model showed moderate discrimination (AUC=0.714). A nonlinear association between SHS scores and BBPE was verified.

DISCUSSION: The prediction model combined with SHS threshold facilitates targeted stratified prevention.

CONCLUSIONS: Integration of occupational exposure surveillance with wellness assessment reduced BBPE and improved infection prevention practices. Routine SHS assessment supports stratified prevention and optimized infection control resource allocation.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbot for Viscoelastic Testing Guidelines: A Randomized Blinded Evaluation of a Guideline-Anchored Large Language Model.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viscoelastic hemostatic assays (VHAs) can provide critical timely information for hemostatic management but are challenging to apply at the bedside. Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to provide rapid guidance yet are prone to errors. We sought to improve guideline-concordance of LLM responses to clinically relevant questions about VHAs by grounding the model in a published clinical guideline.

METHODS: We conducted a randomized, blinded physician evaluation comparing responses from a base model and a retrieval augmented generation (RAG) model grounded in a VHA guideline. The primary outcome assessed model preference. Descriptive statistics were reported for domain ratings. Logistic regression was used to test the association between domains and model preference.

RESULTS: Eight physicians performed 115 blinded evaluations across 48 prompts. The RAG model was preferred in 85% of comparisons (exact binomial test, p < 0.001; 95% CI 72.2%-93.9%). Interrater agreement between the two assigned evaluators was no better than chance (Krippendorff's α = -0.075, raw interrater agreement 60%), and 40% of prompts required tiebreaker adjudication to reach this result. Mean quality ratings favored the RAG model across three domains: concision 3.92 (3.69-4.15) vs 2.78 (2.55-3.01); hallucination 3.77 (3.33-4.20) vs 2.82 (2.38-3.26); and overall quality 3.70 (3.44-3.97) vs 2.81 (2.55-3.08) for the RAG and base models, respectively. Results remained consistent in analyses excluding tiebreakers.

CONCLUSION: Guideline-anchoring led to improved physician ratings and guideline-concordance of AI responses on questions about viscoelastic testing.

articles.title: Adrenal vein thrombosis during pregnancy or the postpartum period: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adrenal vein thrombosis (AVT) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that may present as nonspecific abdominal or lower back pain during pregnancy and may be overlooked because of overlapping obstetric or gastrointestinal symptoms. AVT remains poorly characterized epidemiologically, and its management is not supported by robust evidence or consensus-based recommendations.

OBJECTIVE AND METHODS: To improve diagnosis and management, we searched the MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect and Cochrane Library databases up until October 2025 for publications on AVT in pregnancy and postpartum.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight articles reporting 73 AVT episodes in 71 patients (three retrospective studies, five case series and thirty case reports) were reviewed. Presentation was consistent but nonspecific: mainly acute abdominal (74.4%) or lower back pain (49.3%), often associated with nausea (23.3%) and vomiting (31.5%). Events occurred predominantly in the third trimester (79.6%), at a mean ± standard deviation gestational age of 31±5.7 weeks. Most cases were unilateral (63/72, 87.5%) and right-sided (48/72, 66.7%). Diagnosis relied mainly on contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (56/73, 76.7%). Imaging evidenced adrenal necrosis and hemorrhage in 88.9% and 8.3% of cases, respectively. Adrenal insufficiency requiring hydrocortisone occurred in 17.1% of cases and was mainly associated with bilateral AVT. Low-molecular-weight heparin was the preferred anticoagulant during the acute phase (81.8%), followed by a switch to an oral anticoagulant postpartum (25.7%). The median treatment duration was of 24 weeks. Opioids analgesics were required in 54.8% of cases.

CONCLUSION: This review summarizes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, management, and outcomes of AVT during pregnancy and postpartum.

articles.title: Asthma Pathogenesis: Lessons Learned from Biologics.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract: Biologic therapies have transformed severe asthma management while providing insights into the mechanisms underlying clinical disease. Inhibition of IgE, interleukin (IL)-5/IL-5R, IL4Rα (IL-4/IL-13) and thymic stomal lymphopoietin (TSLP) have established the causal contribution of type 2 (T2) inflammation to exacerbations and systemic corticosteroid dependence. In children and young people, the evidence for exacerbation reduction is more robust for targeting IgE and IL4Rα than IL5 potentially reflecting a greater contribution of allergen and IgE mediated mechanisms in early onset disease. In general, T2-directed biological therapy has a larger positive impact on the frequency of asthma attacks than lung function and day-to-day symptoms although there is some inconsistencies in the magnitude of benefit observed in different domains. This may be because biologics targeting T2 inflammation beyond IL5 exert effects upon structural cells such as goblet cell hyperplasia, mucus plugging, and mast cell-airway smooth muscle interactions translating to greater downstream effects on lung function airway hyper-responsiveness. The impact of biologics upon co-morbidities such as nasal polyposis and eczema is also molecular pathway specific, which provides insights into shared mechanisms. Conversely, targeting neutrophil chemokines, IL-17 inhibition, and IL-23 provides no clinical benefit and may cause met harm, suggesting a role for these pathways in mitigating airway microbial dysbiosis and infection. This review synthesises mechanistic and clinical evidence from successful, unsuccessful and harmful biologic interventions to develop an integrated model of asthma pathogenesis that highlights the need for earlier intervention to alter asthma's natural history and the discovery of novel interventions targeting unmet mechanisms of disease.

articles.title: Causal inference in developmental psychopathology and human neuroscience.
articles.abstract: Developmental psychopathologists and human neuroscientists seek to identify the causes and mechanisms underlying the emergence of psychopathology across development. In order to move closer to achieving this important goal, we argue that widespread adoption of methods emerging from the field of causal inference is needed. Causal inference is an interdisciplinary field that seeks to establish cause-and-effect relationships from data, whether experimental or observational. Evaluating causality in an observational setting requires invoking a set of identification assumptions: foundational conditions, often untestable from the data alone, under which a statistical estimator can be given a valid causal interpretation. Through detailing these assumptions-and their connection to core components of statistical models-in the context of the complexity inherent to doing developmental psychopathology and human neuroscience research, we give researchers the background to begin thinking through how to address causality using observational data. Finally, we detail steps for researchers to take to effectively integrate causal inference methods into their research program, from articulating their research questions, to designing studies, to effectively communicating the strengths and limitations of their results.

articles.title: Subclinical Atrial Fibrillation: Detection, Risk Stratification, and Clinical Management.
articles.abstract: Subclinical atrial fibrillation (SCAF) presents a clinical challenge in which increasingly sensitive detection has outpaced the evidence needed to guide treatment. This review integrates recent evidence on detection, thromboembolic risk, disease progression, and clinical management, with particular emphasis on studies published since 2024 and their implications for Japanese practice. Implantable monitors, patch electrocardiography, consumer wearables, and home devices broaden opportunities for detecting asymptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF), while artificial intelligence may refine selection for monitoring. However, differences in diagnostic definitions, population risk, and AF burden complicate the translation of greater diagnostic yield into stroke prevention; pooled screening evidence suggests only modest benefit. Secondary analyses of ARTESiA and NOAH-AFNET 6 have challenged reliance on episode duration alone. Recent SCAF duration and frequency were not significantly associated with thromboembolic risk in ARTESiA, and atrial high-rate episode duration did not significantly modify treatment effects in NOAH-AFNET 6. These findings do not establish a safe duration threshold. Patient characteristics and progression to clinical AF or longer episodes remain relevant to longitudinal assessment, although subgroup treatment estimates require cautious interpretation. Randomized evidence indicates that direct oral anticoagulants reduce ischemic stroke but increase major bleeding, without a demonstrated mortality benefit. Management therefore requires confirmation of the arrhythmia, individualized assessment of benefit and harm, shared decision-making, comorbidity management, and continued surveillance. European, American, and Japanese recommendations differ in terminology, duration criteria, risk scores, and recommendation strength; the Japanese device-detected AF recommendation warrants reassessment in light of contemporary randomized evidence. Trials of screening, rhythm-guided anticoagulation, rhythm control, and factor XI inhibition address important remaining uncertainties, but results from clinical AF populations will require careful evaluation before application to SCAF.

articles.title: Delayed Ambulation Is Associated With Hospitalization-Associated Disability in Older Patients With Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitalization-associated disability (HAD) frequently affects older patients with heart failure (HF), and early mobilization is recommended to mitigate functional decline. However, the relative contribution of different mobilization stages to clinical outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 495 patients aged ≥65 years hospitalized for HF and receiving physical therapy were included. Standing was defined as the achievement of upright weight-bearing posture, whereas ambulation was defined as forward walking. The primary outcome was HAD, defined as a ≥ 5-point decline in the Barthel Index at discharge compared with pre-hospital baseline. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of time to first standing and ambulation and the risk of HAD.

RESULTS: HAD occurred in 197 patients (39.8%). Time to first ambulation was independently associated with HAD [odds ratio (OR) 1.17 per day; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.29; p = 0.002], whereas time to first standing was not (OR 1.10; 95% CI 0.94-1.28; p = 0.257). In group-based analyses, delayed ambulation was associated with a higher odds of HAD irrespective of early mobilization status (early standing /early ambulation: 26.4%; early standing /delayed ambulation: OR 2.20; delayed standing /delayed ambulation: OR 2.54). These findings were consistent across sensitivity and subgroup analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Delayed ambulation, but not delayed standing alone, is independently associated with HAD in older patients with HF. Time to first ambulation may serve as a simple clinical marker for identifying patients at increased risk of functional decline during hospitalization. WHAT ARE THE CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS?

articles.title: Inflammatory status, rather than atherosclerotic burden, is associated with delayed oxygen uptake kinetics in coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic burden and inflammation are key determinants of coronary artery disease (CAD) progression, but their relative associations with functional impairment remain unclear. We investigated whether both inflammatory status and atherosclerotic burden are associated with functional capacity and oxygen uptake (VO₂) on-kinetics in obstructive CAD.

METHODS: Patients with angiographically confirmed CAD performed a six-minute walk test with portable gas analysis. VO₂ steady-state (VO₂SS) and work-corrected mean response time (wMRT) were assessed. Inflammatory markers and coronary atherosclerotic burden were analyzed. Associations were evaluated using correlation and network analysis.

RESULTS: Atherosclerotic burden was modestly associated with VO₂SS (r = -0.320; p = 0.029) and walking distance (r = -0.371; p = 0.010), but not wMRT (p > 0.05). Inflammatory markers [high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin (IL) -6, IL-8, IL-10] correlated with VO₂SS and distance (p < 0.05), while hs-CRP (p = 0.011), IL-6 (p = 0.003), and IL-8 (p < 0.01) were associated with wMRT. Network analysis identified VO₂SS and wMRT as central nodes, with IL-6 showing the highest expected influence in the exploratory network.

CONCLUSIONS: Inflammation is more closely associated with impaired functional capacity and VO₂ kinetics than atherosclerotic burden in CAD.

articles.title: Beyond BMI: The triglyceride-glucose index and incident coronary artery calcification according to obesity status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body weight is widely used as a visible proxy for metabolic health, yet insulin resistance is common in adults whose body mass index appears reassuring. We examined whether the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index, a fasting surrogate of insulin resistance, identifies adults without obesity whose risk of developing coronary artery calcification (CAC) approaches that of adults with obesity.

METHODS: We analyzed 1861 adults without diabetes, lipid-lowering therapy, or known cardiovascular disease who underwent serial cardiac computed tomography and had a baseline Agatston score of zero. The outcome was incident CAC. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by Poisson regression and stratified by obesity status, using TyG quartiles with common cohort-wide cut-offs.

RESULTS: Incident CAC occurred in 477 participants (25.6%) during 11,782 person-years. In the overall cohort, the highest TyG quartile was associated with an increased risk compared with the lowest (IRR 1.41, 95% CI 1.11-1.80). This association was confined to non-obese participants (IRR 1.76, 95% CI 1.26-2.45; p for trend = 0.003), whereas incidence rates were unchanged across quartiles among obese participants (p for trend = 0.999; p for interaction = 0.033). Non-obese participants in the highest TyG quartile had a risk comparable to that of obese participants (IRR 1.06, 95% CI 0.87-1.30).

CONCLUSIONS: A high TyG index identified non-obese adults whose risk of developing CAC was comparable to that of obese adults, whereas obese adults were at high risk irrespective of the TyG index. A normal body mass index may not indicate a low risk of developing CAC in individuals with a high TyG index.

articles.title: Head-to-head comparison of Finerenone, Eplerenone, and spironolactone in heart failure: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
