BACKGROUND: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are commonly used in the treatment of heart failure (HF). Direct comparative data examining the association of available MRAs with HF outcomes are limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using the US TriNetX federated electronic health record network (July 2021-August 2025) to compare clinical and safety outcomes associated with finerenone, eplerenone, and spironolactone in a large real-world HF cohort. Adults with HF newly initiated on spironolactone, eplerenone, or finerenone were included. One-to-one propensity score matching was performed for each pairwise comparison. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, all-cause hospitalization, and intravenous diuretic use at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the composite and acute heart failure. Safety outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI) and hyperkalemia. Subgroup analyses were performed in HF with reduced ejection fraction and preserved ejection fraction.

RESULTS: Prematched cohorts included 326,580 spironolactone, 8705 eplerenone, and 2666 finerenone patients. After matching, 8699 patients per group were included in the eplerenone-versus-spironolactone comparison and 2651 per group in the finerenone-versus-spironolactone comparison. Compared with spironolactone, eplerenone was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.91; p < 0.001), while finerenone showed a greater reduction (RR 0.59, 95% CI 0.55-0.63; p < 0.001). Finerenone was also associated with lower all-cause mortality, hospitalization, IV diuretic use, acute heart failure, AKI, and hyperkalemia versus spironolactone, and lower risk of the primary composite outcome versus eplerenone (RR 0.68, 95% CI 0.61-0.74; p < 0.001). Associations were consistent across HF phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this propensity-matched real-world analysis, finerenone was associated with lower rates of adverse clinical and safety outcomes than either steroidal MRA, while eplerenone was associated with modestly lower rates than spironolactone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and indicate the need for prospective head-to-head evaluation of MRAs in HF.

articles.title: Culprit lesion is associated with cardiac but not all-cause mortality in OHCA-complicated acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported conflicting results regarding the association between culprit lesion and mortality in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) complicated by out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Since the prognostic impact of culprit lesion location differs according to the cause of death, cause-specific analyses are essential.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 249 patients with type 1 AMI complicated by OHCA receiving percutaneous coronary intervention. Patients were classified according to culprit lesion location as left main trunk (LMT) / proximal left anterior descending artery (LAD) or other sites. The primary outcomes were 90-day all-cause, cardiac, and non-cardiac mortality. The multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was applied for all-cause mortality. Competing risk analyses using multivariable cause-specific hazard models were performed for cardiac and non-cardiac mortality.

RESULTS: Patients with LMT / proximal LAD culprit lesions more frequently presented with ST-elevation myocardial infarction and exhibited features of larger infarction, lower left ventricular ejection fraction, and more frequent use of mechanical circulatory support. All-cause mortality was comparable according to the culprit lesion [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.93-2.14]. The LMT / proximal LAD culprit lesions were independently associated with increased cardiac mortality (adjusted HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.04-2.64), whereas non-cardiac mortality was similar between the two groups (adjusted HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.31-1.81).

CONCLUSIONS: Among AMI patients complicated by OHCA, culprit lesion was not associated with non-cardiac and all-cause mortality, although the LMT / proximal LAD culprit lesions were associated with increased cardiac mortality.

articles.title: Trial-level associations of treatment-induced changes in NT-proBNP, patient-reported health status, and exercise capacity with clinical outcomes in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), patient-reported health status, and exercise capacity are commonly evaluated as measures of treatment response in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). However, it remains uncertain which treatment-induced changes show the strongest associations with treatment effects on major clinical events. We compared these associations in phase 3 ATTR-CM trials.

METHODS: We searched PubMed through September 30, 2026, for phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trials of disease-modifying ATTR-CM therapies. Random-effects meta-regression using restricted maximum likelihood assessed trial-level associations of treatment-induced changes in NT-proBNP, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OS), and 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) with treatment effects on all-cause mortality, cardiovascular (CV) death, and recurrent CV events including CV-related hospitalizations and urgent heart failure visits. The log ratio of treatment-induced relative changes in NT-proBNP and between-group differences in KCCQ-OS and 6MWD were used as covariates. Weighted R2 and p-values from weighted regression and small-sample-corrected analyses were reported.

RESULTS: Five trials involving 3,520 participants were included. All five contributed to the analysis of all-cause mortality, whereas four contributed to analyses of CV death and recurrent CV events. Treatment-induced change in NT-proBNP showed the strongest trial-level association with treatment effects on recurrent CV events (weighted R2 = 0.955; β = 1.138; weighted regression p = 0.023; small-sample-corrected p = 0.106). No other associations were statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Our trial-level meta-regression identified the strongest association between treatment-induced changes in NT-proBNP and treatment effects on recurrent CV events, but this association was not statistically significant after small-sample correction. Given the small number of trials, this finding should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The observed association should be further evaluated in updated meta-regression analyses as results from ongoing ATTR-CM trials become available.

articles.title: Walking to Work and Incident Dyslipidemia: Reduced Risk of Low High-density Lipoprotein Cholesterol.
Multi-strategy engineering boosting soluble expression of PET hydrolase in E. coli.
articles.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization offers a promising route for closed-loop recycling of post-consumer poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PC-PET), but the lack of scalable, high-yield production of PET hydrolases remains a major bottleneck. In particular, ICCG, a prominent PET hydrolase, suffers from poor soluble expression in Escherichia coli, limiting its industrial application. Here, we report a multi-strategy engineering approach that achieves record-high soluble expression of ICCG in E. coli while preserving catalytic activity and thermostability. Specifically, synergistic integration of secretion pathway engineering and solubility tags enhanced both intracellular solubility and extracellular translocation. Rational engineering of surface-exposed hydrophobic residues then yielded five single-point variants with elevated soluble expression. The combination variant M1 (A49K/P55R/A103N/A138S) afforded a 2.9-fold enhancement in soluble expression, concomitant with augmented PET depolymerization activity and uncompromised thermostability. In fed-batch fermentation, soluble production of the PET hydrolase reached 5.2 g/L, the highest reported titer for PET hydrolases to date. The crude M1 preparation efficiently depolymerized white pure polyester textile (98.9% degradation within 20 h) and black pure polyester textile (82.2% degradation within 24 h). This study provides a scalable, cost-effective manufacturing route for PET hydrolases, which is expected to expedite the industrial adoption of enzyme-based plastic recycling and thereby support the overarching goal of closed-loop PET fiber recycling.

articles.title: Integrated physiological, phenolic and histological profiling of heat-primed somatic P. radiata plants under abiotic stress.
articles.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
articles.abstract: Thermal priming during somatic embryogenesis has been proposed as a complementary mechanism associated with cellular reprogramming to enhance stress tolerance in plants. To assess the priming effect, somatic plants of Pinus radiata regenerated from heat-shock primed (PP, 60 °C) and non-primed (NP, 23 °C) proliferating embryogenic masses were subjected to drought (D), heat (H) and combined drought-heat (DH) stress and sampled at early (T1) and late (T2) exposure stages. Physiological measurements, phenolic profile characterization, histochemical and stereological analyses were used to evaluate primed plant response under abiotic stressors. D and H increased the relative abundance of phenylpropanoid-derived compounds compared with control plants, reflecting the involvement of antioxidant defense mechanisms, while combined DH did not generate a conclusive response. Thermal priming did not alter the global phenolic composition under any stress condition; however, PP plants displayed significantly lower relative abundance of compounds, mainly flavonoids, than NP under D at T2. This pattern was supported by targeted quantification of catechin and quercetin-3-O-glucopyranoside. Furthermore, the untargeted phenolic profile was negatively correlated with relative water content, which was greater in PP. Histochemical analyses detected no qualitative differences in phenolic distribution, whereas the endodermal volumetric fraction was constitutively higher and drought-stable in PP plants, contrasting with a drought-induced increase in NP plants. Overall, these findings suggest that thermal priming during somatic embryogenesis may promote stress- and time-dependent modulation of phenolic metabolism, potentially associated with improved water status and a stable endodermal structure, which may attenuate or alter the defensive adjustments to D.

articles.title: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. The antiviral activity of liraglutide was attenuated by both AMPK inhibitor Compound C and siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown, supporting the claim that AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis contributes to liraglutide's anti-ZIKV activity. Given its clinical availability, liraglutide represents a promising therapeutic option for immediate repurposing for managing patients infected with ZIKV.

articles.title: [Scientific relevance of the collected variables in the WeanNet registry: a systematic overview].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The WeanNet registry, which has existed for many years, represents one of the largest databases in the field of prolonged weaning, with over 55,000 enrolled patients to date. As part of a planned restructuring of the registry, a revision of the recorded database fields is intended. The objective of this study was to examine which of the existing variables are actually utilized in scientific publications.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted on March 15, 2026, to identify publications using data from the WeanNet registry. Subsequently, the variables reported in these articles were extracted and analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 13 publications (8 single-center, 5 multi-center) were identified. Out of the 143 collected variables, 87 (60.8%) were included in at least one analysis. The most frequently recorded data included demographics, admission and discharge dates of the weaning unit, start and end of invasive ventilation, cause of acute respiratory failure, comorbidities, and the weaning classification at the end of the inpatient stay. Notably, approximately 56 variables (39.2%) of the collected values have not yet been utilized in scientific evaluations.

CONCLUSION: The results demonstrate that the majority of the collected variables are relevant for scientific analysis. A revision of the database structure can help reduce the documentation burden, improve data quality, and further enhance the scientific utility of the registry.

articles.title: [The "Reichenhall Recommendation 2024" explained using a case report].
articles.abstract: The "Reichenhaller Empfehlung 2024" provides an updated, interdisciplinary guideline for the evaluation of occupational diseases No. 1315, 4301, and 4302, as listed in Annex 1 of the German Ordinance on Occupational Diseases (BKV). These concern obstructive airway diseases caused by isocyanates, allergenic, or irritant or toxic agents. The guideline places particular emphasis on a structured assessment of exposure, differentiated diagnostics including lung function testing and allergological tests, as well as a comprehensible causality assessment in accordance with social law requirements. The recommendation thus supports a quality-assured and consistent assessment practice within the statutory accident insurance. In the article, the application of the recommendation is demonstrated using the case of a livestock transport driver with allergic Asthma and COPD and sensitization to occupational allergens. The occupational exposure is considered a significant cause in the sense of occupational disease No. 4301. The degree of reduction in earning capacity (MdE) considers current guidelines for diagnostics and therapy options. Recommendations are also provided regarding exposure avoidance and measures for secondary and tertiary prevention.

articles.title: Alcohol, diabetes, and colorectal cancer: is there a safe sip?
articles.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute

articles.title: Brain insulin resistance in the development of obesity and type 2 diabetes: temporal trajectories in humans.
articles.abstract: Brain insulin resistance might promote dysregulated eating and impaired systemic metabolism. This Review addresses the central question of temporality-whether brain insulin resistance precedes peripheral insulin resistance. We summarise human approaches to quantify brain insulin resistance and scalable biomarkers anchored to imaging-defined phenotypes. Across the metabolic continuum, alterations appear to emerge early in hypothalamic and mesolimbic systems and are modified by sex and metabolic health. Functional neuroimaging readouts often shift after modest lifestyle or pharmacological interventions, whereas insulin-stimulated brain glucose uptake might require more sustained systemic change. Evidence of hypothalamic gliosis suggests that inflammatory responses could link metabolic stress to impaired brain insulin action. Collectively, the data are consistent with a trajectory from diet-sensitive central alterations to later bidirectional reinforcement of central and peripheral insulin resistance, accelerating progression towards metabolic disease. GLP-1 receptor agonists, GLP-1/GIP dual agonists, and emerging multi-agonists may engage overlapping circuits, raising the possibility that part of their benefit arises from restoring, bypassing, or compensating for impaired brain insulin action.

articles.title: Ringer's lactate versus saline in the fluids in septic shock (FISSH) trial: a multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite fluid therapy being a hallmark of treatment for patients with septic shock, the optimal crystalloid to use in this setting remains unclear. We aimed to compare the effect of two different, commonly used crystalloids in patients with septic shock.

METHODS: In this multicentre, blinded, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial, adults (aged ≥16 years) at 30 academic and community hospitals across Canada and Saudi Arabia who were critically ill with septic shock were randomly assigned (1:1) via a web-based randomisation system to receive Ringer's lactate or 0·9% saline for all bolus and maintenance fluid throughout their intensive care unit (ICU) stay up to day 30, stratified by hospital. Randomisation used permuted blocks of undisclosed variable sizes. We included patients who had a systolic blood pressure lower than 90 mm Hg or a mean arterial pressure of less than 65 mm Hg after 1 L bolus or a serum lactate greater than 4 mmol/L, had a clinically suspected infection, and were within 6 h of emergency department presentation or ICU consultation. We excluded patients who had new raised intracranial pressure, had acute burn injury on more than 10% of the body surface area, were already receiving chronic or acute dialysis at the time of screening, or were admitted to ICU directly from the operating room, post-anaesthetic care unit, or another hospital or health-care facility. All bedside clinicians, patients, caregivers, research staff, and biostatisticians were masked to allocation. The primary endpoint was 30-day in-hospital mortality analysed on an intention-to-treat basis. The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03677102).

FINDINGS: Between Oct 6, 2018, and Feb 1, 2026, we screened 2457 patients and randomly assigned 1113, with a further ten excluded after randomisation (557 patients in the Ringer's lactate group and 546 in the saline group). 491 (44·5%) were female and 612 (55·5%) were male, the mean baseline APACHE II score was 24·7 (SD 8·8), and patients received a mean of 5844 mL (SD 4761) of study fluid. The mean baseline serum lactate was 4·8 mmol/L (SD 3·5) and the mean serum creatinine was 176·5 μmol/L (SD 126·4). 187 (33·6%) patients died in the Ringer's lactate group 180 (33·0%) died in the saline group (relative risk 1·02 [95% CI 0·86-1·21]; p=0·80). There were no serious adverse events.

INTERPRETATION: In this trial of patients who were critically ill with septic shock, Ringer's lactate compared with saline had no effect on 30-day in-hospital mortality.

FUNDING: The Canadian Institutes of Health Research and the Physician Services Incorporated Foundation.

articles.title: Diabetes and drug-resistant tuberculosis: priorities beyond host-pathogen metabolism.
Repetitive levodopa treatment drives cell-type-specific striatal adaptations associated with progressive dyskinesia in parkinsonian mice.
articles.abstract: The use of levodopa to manage Parkinson's disease (PD) symptoms leads to levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID) and other motor fluctuations, which worsen with disease progression and repeated treatment. Aberrant activity of striatal D1- and D2-expressing medium spiny neurons (D1-/D2-MSNs) underlies LID, but the mechanisms driving its progression remain unclear. Using the 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) mouse model of PD/LID, we combined in vivo and ex vivo recordings to isolate the effect of repeated treatment in LID worsening and other changes in the motor response to levodopa. We found that LID worsening is linked to potentiation of levodopa-evoked responses in both D1-/D2-MSNs, independent of changes in dopamine release or MSN intrinsic excitability. Instead, strengthening of glutamatergic synapses onto D1-MSNs emerged as a key signature. Moreover, we found that changes in D2-MSN activity are associated with LID duration, which parallels a reduction in D2 receptor (D2R) sensitivity. These findings reveal striatal adaptations contributing to the worsening of levodopa-related complications.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Real-World Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Three single-inhaler triple therapy (SITT) formulations are available for patients with COPD who remain symptomatic or experience exacerbations. We aimed to synthesise evidence on the effectiveness and patient-centred outcomes of SITT in non-randomised observational studies.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify observational studies evaluating the effectiveness of SITT in real-world COPD populations. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to 31 March 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and pooled mean differences and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Study quality was assessed with the National Institutes of Health tool for before-after studies.

RESULTS: In 21 studies with 13,494 participants, SITT initiation was associated with improved lung function, with FEV1 increasing by 0.16 L (95% CI: 0.06-0.25) and FVC by 0.14 L (95% CI: 0.03-0.25) at 12 months compared with pre-treatment. Severe exacerbations were 55% lower (IRR 0.45; 95% CI: 0.24-0.84) and total exacerbations 58% lower (IRR 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27-0.67). Symptom burden improved (CAT -5.48 points; 95% CI: -6.86 to -4.11), as did self-reported inhaler adherence (TAI-10 +2.13 points; 95% CI: 1.11-3.15). Similar changes were observed at 1-3 months. Heterogeneity was high, and prediction intervals for most 12-month outcomes crossed the null. In exploratory subgroup analyses, improvements were larger in patients stepping up from mono- or dual therapy than in those switching from multiple-inhaler triple therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis of real-world studies suggests that SITT is associated with clinically meaningful improvements in lung function, exacerbations, symptoms, and adherence in COPD, although high heterogeneity warrants caution in generalising these findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CRD420251184078.

articles.title: Real-world comparison of SOFIA versus other aspiration catheters for first-line aspiration in the ETIS registry.
articles.journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contact aspiration has become a widely accepted first-line strategy for mechanical thrombectomy in large vessel occlusion stroke (LVOS). However, evidence directly comparing the performance of different aspiration catheters in real-world settings remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the safety and efficacy of the SOFIA aspiration catheter with other aspiration catheters used for first-line aspiration in LVOS within the ETIS registry.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of consecutive patients from the multicenter French ETIS registry who underwent endovascular treatment for LVOS using first-line contact aspiration between January 2021 and June 2024. Patients were categorized according to the use of SOFIA versus other aspiration catheters. The primary outcome was first pass effect (FPE), defined as achieving modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) 2c-3 after a single pass. Secondary angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes were assessed. Propensity score overlap weighting and multiple imputation were applied to account for prespecified confounding and missing data.

RESULTS: Among 11468 patients, 5048 underwent first-line aspiration [2865 (56.7%) received SOFIA catheters and 2183 (43.3%) other catheters]. Baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. FPE rates were comparable (42.3%vs. 43.4%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.96; 95% CI, 0.84-1.08). Secondary angiographic outcomes, procedural times, and 3-month functional outcomes (mRS 0-2: 43.0% vs. 43.6%; aOR = 0.98; 95% CI, 0.86-1.10) did not differ significantly. Procedural complications were slightly more frequent in the SOFIA group (6.8%vs. 5.3%; aOR = 1.29; 95% CI, 1.01-1.65), while symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred less often (8.9%vs. 11.3%; aOR = 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62-0.94), though both differences lost significance after correction for multiple comparisons.

CONCLUSION: In this large real-world cohort, SOFIA catheters were the most commonly used for first-line aspiration in LVOS. Their efficacy and safety were comparable to those of other aspiration catheters. Dedicated prospective studies are warranted to confirm these results.

articles.title: Carotid web as a potential etiology of intracranial large vessel occlusion in patients initially classified as embolic stroke of undetermined source: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid web has emerged as a potential embolic source in embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), but its association with intracranial large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relationship between carotid web and intracranial LVO in patients initially classified as ESUS and to characterize carotid web imaging features associated with LVO.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study, consecutive patients initially classified as anterior circulation ESUS after standardized etiologic evaluation and admitted to 3 stroke centers between January 2017 and December 2025 were included. Patients were classified as having LVO or non-LVO based on acute vascular imaging. Carotid web was primarily assessed by carotid computed tomography angiography and independently reviewed by 2 blinded neuroradiologists. Presence, laterality, and 6 quantitative morphological features were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the independent association between ipsilateral carotid web and intracranial LVO.

RESULTS: Among 705 patients initially classified as ESUS, 311 (44.1%) had intracranial LVO. Ipsilateral carotid web was more frequent in patients with LVO than in those without LVO (13.2%vs 2.0%, p < 0.001), whereas the prevalence of contralateral-only carotid web did not differ between groups. After adjustment for age, sex, and vascular risk factors, ipsilateral carotid web remained independently associated with LVO (odds ratio 7.78, 95% confidence interval 3.46 to 17.46). Among patients with ipsilateral carotid web, those with LVO had greater web length, smaller angulation, and larger sagittal web area (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients initially classified as ESUS, systematic imaging review identified a strong and independent association between ipsilateral carotid web and intracranial LVO. These findings support further investigation of carotid web morphology in etiologic evaluation.

articles.title: Luminescent labeling enables detection of PET nanoparticles in freshwater organisms.
articles.abstract: Nanoplastic detection in biological matrices is challenging because of particle size and interference from biological autofluorescence. Here, we compared ligand-free Yb3 +/Er3+-based upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) and Eu(TTA)3 as labels for aqueous nanoPET colloids and assessed their imaging performance in Raphidocelis subcapitata, Brachionus calyciflorus, and Daphnia magna. Near-infrared excitation of UCNPs produced distinguishable signals in all three species, although microscopy did not always resolve whether particles were internalized or surface-associated. Eu3+ emission was spectrally confirmed in the intestine of D. magna but was not reliably distinguished in R. subcapitata or B. calyciflorus because of autofluorescence. Neither unlabeled nor UCNPs-labeled nanoPET significantly affected the population growth rate of B. calyciflorus or the juvenile growth rate of D. magna. However, a tendency towards reduced juvenile growth was observed in D. magna exposed to nanoPET+w-UCNPs at the highest concentration (70 µg·mL⁻¹), although this decrease was not statistically significant (p = 0.09). These findings define the complementary imaging performance and current limitations of two labels in freshwater organisms.

articles.title: Brain and spinal cord chronic neuroinflammation in multiple sclerosis: a large-scale post-mortem study and longitudinal MRI cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs) represent a subset of chronic active, or mixed active/inactive, lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS). Whether chronic neuroinflammation is synchronised across the craniospinal axis and can predict spinal cord degeneration remains unknown. We aimed to evaluate the correlation of pathology, including lesion types and microglial state, between the brain and spinal cord, and to determine if brain PRL count predicts longitudinal spinal cord atrophy.

METHODS: We combined a large-scale neuropathological study with an in vivo longitudinal clinical-MRI study. Brain and spinal cord tissues from 194 MS donors (5317 samples; 8874 lesions) were analysed to correlate lesion types and microglial state across central nervous system regions. For the clinical-MRI cohort, 173 adults with MS [118 women (68%); 48 progressive; median EDSS 1.5] underwent baseline 3T brain and spinal cord MRI, with longitudinal follow-up over a median of 2.5 years. Brain PRLs were identified via susceptibility-sensitive imaging. The spinal cord cross-sectional area (SCCSA) was measured longitudinally at C2-C3, C4-C5, and T4-T9 at two time points.

FINDINGS: Large-scale post-mortem analysis revealed that intra-donor proportions of mixed active/inactive lesions in the brain were correlated with those in the spinal cord (p = 2.22e-9, r = 0.41). Microglia/macrophage activity scores (p = 4.30e-6, r = 0.32) and microglial nodules (p = 3.55e-4) were similarly synchronised. In vivo, higher baseline brain PRL counts independently predicted accelerated spinal cord atrophy at C2-C3 (β = -0.049 mm2/year, p = 0.03), resulting in an ∼9% steeper SCCSA decline per PRL. The association remained significant after adjustment for T2 lesion burden and treatment.

INTERPRETATION: Neuroinflammation is concordant between the brain and spinal cord. In vivo, brain PRLs correlate with accelerated upper cervical spinal cord atrophy, supporting its potential as an imaging biomarker of progressive spinal cord neurodegeneration.

FUNDING: Intramural Research Program at the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) of the US National Institutes of Health (NIH), the National MS Society (grant RFA-2203-39325), the European Research Council (ERC-Stg 2025-101221868) and the Stitching MS research (MS research 23-406i-basis).

articles.title: Psychosocial support after paediatric intensive care: promising evidence, persistent questions.
Complications associated with the insertion site of arterial catheters in intensive care: A propensity score-matching analysis - Letter on Narváez-Martínez et al.
Achalasia and gastroparesis: association, risk factors, and relationship with myotomy.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal surgery : official journal of the Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early studies identified gastric neuronal abnormalities and delayed gastric emptying in achalasia, yet its clinical association with gastroparesis remains poorly defined. We examined this association and compared gastroparesis-related outcomes by esophageal myotomy status and technique.

METHODS: Patients with achalasia were identified in TriNetX (2010-2024) and propensity score-matched 1:1 to nonachalasia controls. The primary outcome was newly diagnosed gastroparesis. Multivariable Cox regression identified factors that were independently associated with gastroparesis within the achalasia cohort. Separate matched analyses compared patients with and without myotomy and those who underwent laparoscopic Heller myotomy (LHM) vs peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM).

RESULTS: A total of 42,538 patients with achalasia were identified. During follow-up, gastroparesis was newly diagnosed in 2.7% of patients with achalasia vs 0.4% of matched controls (odds ratio, 6.15; 95% CI, 5.27-7.18; P <.001). Among patients with gastroparesis, achalasia was associated with more frequent pyloric dilation (8.5% vs 1.7%), pyloric intervention or gastric electrical stimulation (GES; 5.1% vs 1.6%), and feeding access placement (6.8% vs 3.1%; all P <.001). Female sex, diabetes, gastroesophageal reflux disease, chronic opioid use, cannabis use, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use were independently associated with an increased risk of gastroparesis (all P <.05), whereas prior myotomy was associated with a lower risk (hazard ratio, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.48-0.73; P <.001). In matched comparisons, myotomy was associated with fewer gastroparesis diagnoses (1.1% vs 1.7%), less prokinetic use (3.4% vs 7.6%), and fewer gastroparesis-related symptoms (8% vs 13.3%), but more pyloric intervention or GES (1.8% vs 0.6%; all P <.05). No statistically significant differences were detected between LHM and POEM.

CONCLUSION: Achalasia was associated with more frequent gastroparesis diagnoses and greater related treatment utilization. Myotomy was associated with fewer diagnoses and symptoms, despite greater use of pyloric intervention or GES. These findings support a clinical overlap between achalasia and gastroparesis and warrant prospective physiologic studies to clarify the contribution of multilevel foregut dysmotility.

articles.title: Long-term air pollution and COVID-19 severity in New York City hospitalized patients: Mediation by pre-existing atrial fibrillation and myocardial infarction.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract: Evidence links long-term air pollution to COVID-19 severity. Given ongoing COVID-19 hospitalizations, we explored how historical pollution influences COVID-19 outcomes. We examined whether pre-existing cardiovascular conditions, both major predictors of severe COVID-19 and strongly associated with pollution, mediate the relationship between historical pollution and adverse COVID-19 outcomes. We studied NYC residents hospitalized with COVID-19 (3/1/2020-2/28/2021; N = 20,118), using harmonized electronic health records. Historical exposure to particulate matter (PM2.5), black carbon (BC), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and ozone (O3) was assigned using 11-year annual averages (2009-2019) from NYC Community Air Survey ZIP Code data. Logistic regression estimated the odds of 15 cardiovascular conditions as mediators (e.g., myocardial infarction (MI), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure, hypertension). Modified Poisson regression estimated risks of adverse COVID-19 outcomes, including acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), pneumonia, ventilation, and dialysis, and Cox regression estimated hazards of fatality and discharge, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, environmental vulnerability, and exposure-mediator interaction. In the first wave (March-June 2020), historical PM2.5, BC, and NO2 increased risk of ARDS, pneumonia, and dialysis; inverse estimates found for O3. Pre-existing AF and MI accounted for the largest indirect effects of long-term PM2.5 exposure on ARDS, dialysis, ventilation, and fatality outcomes. Nearly 25% of the effect of long-term PM2.5 on ARDS, dialysis, and ventilation was mediated by AF or MI. Overall, historical pollution is linked to adverse COVID-19, with AF and MI as potential mediators. Findings encourage research on long-term pollution influencing pandemic outcomes and strategies to improve cardiovascular health in communities experiencing long-term pollution.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing quotients: Expanding the concept beyond peak  V . O 2 Q .
articles.abstract: Interpretation of cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is limited by uncertainty regarding normal standards for key exercise parameters. Previously, we demonstrated that a quotient derived from a first percentile lower boundary for peak oxygen uptake (peak  V . O 2 Q   ) was prognostically informative. We hypothesised that similar lower-bound ('first percentile') values could be derived for other clinically important CPET parameters. We undertook retrospective analysis of CPET data from two UK tertiary centres between 2012 and 2024. First percentile values were derived for peak work rate, anaerobic threshold and end-exercise O2 pulse, overall and stratified by age and sex. Quotients were calculated as the measured value divided by the first percentile value. Associations with all-cause mortality were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. Prognostic performance was compared with conventional percent predicted expressions using Harrell's C-statistics. Data from 1377 patients were included. First percentile values were 28 W for peak work rate, 6.5 mL kg- 1 min- 1 for anaerobic threshold, and 6.2 mL beat- 1 for males and 4.5 mL beat- 1 for females for O2 pulse. Lower quotient values were independently associated with increased all-cause mortality after adjustment for age, sex and body mass index, including peak work rate quotient [hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.18-1.62], anaerobic threshold quotient (HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.10-1.98) and O2 pulse quotient (HR 2.38, 95% CI 1.54-3.69). Quotient measures demonstrated superior prognostic discrimination compared with conventional percent predicted expressions. Lower-bound values for multiple CPET parameters can be derived and used to generate physiologically meaningful quotient measures associated with survival.

articles.title: Bacterial Causes and Antibiotic Susceptibility of Community-Acquired Bloodstream Infections in Children Aged 2 and Younger at a Tertiary Hospital in Ndola, Zambia.
articles.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.abstract: Bacterial bloodstream infections are common causes of acute febrile illness in children. Sepsis, a condition of global public health concern, is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Zambia. This study aimed to characterize common bacteria, associated factors, and resistance patterns of community-acquired bloodstream infections in children ages 2 years old and younger at Arthur Davison Children's Hospital. This cross-sectional study was conducted among children admitted with a temperature ≥38.0°C and clinical features of sepsis from January to June 2024. Blood cultures were incubated at 37°C; species identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing were done on positive cultures. Multivariable logistic regression was used for association of factors. Of 200 children screened, 175 had blood culture results, but 28 had contaminant cultures; 51 of 147 blood cultures (34.7%) yielded pathogenic bacterial isolates. Common pathogenic isolated bacteria were Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 14/51, 27.5%), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 11/51, 21.6%), Enterobacter spp. (n = 6/51, 11.8%), and Escherichia coli (n = 4/51, 7.8%). More than half of S. aureus (n = 6/11, 54.5%) were methicillin-resistant. Factors associated with positive blood culture result were history of breathing difficulties (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 4.19, 95% CI: 1.12-15.65) and weight-for-age Z-score ≥-2 SDs compared with <-2SD (AOR = 0.22, 95% CI: 0.07-0.70). The proportion of Gram-negative pathogenic community-acquired bloodstream infection bacteria isolated was 62.7% (n = 32/51), and at least four of seven isolated species were multidrug resistant. We recommend implementation of infection prevention measures and strengthened antimicrobial stewardship programs.

articles.title: bigrig: A range simulator for the DEC[+J] model.
articles.abstract: Quality software tools for science need to be rigorously tested and verified. However, there is a major challenge to testing software used for phylogenetics and similar analysis. As a field, we have a shortage of ground truth data which can be used for validation, resulting in a reliance on simulated data. This reliance on simulated data results in a second challenge: verifying the correctness of the tool which generates the simulated data. In historical biogeography, software to simulate data has often been implemented on an ad-hoc basis to verify specific tools, instead of releasing it as a standalone package. Here, we introduce bigrig, a simulator for the DEC[+J] model of range evolution. We show that bigrig is correct via rigorous statistical testing and validation using two completely independent simulation algorithms. We show that results between these independent implementations do not deviate by more than 0.0001 with 99.999% confidence. We also show that bigrig is extremely fast, capable of generating data for trees with tens of thousands of tips in under a second.

articles.title: Lifestyle Counseling Practices for Inpatients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Focus on Exercise and Dietary Guidance Using the 2011-2019 National Inpatient Sample.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeThe purpose of this study is to assess the practices of exercise and dietary (lifestyle) counseling among patients with T2DM in the inpatient setting in USA.DesignCross-sectional and trend analyses.SettingIn the United States, using the National Inpatient Sample data from 2011 to 2019.SampleAdult patients aged 18 years and older who were hospitalized with T2DM.MeasuresMain outcome measure is lifestyle counseling, which includes dietary and exercise counseling; defined using the International Classification of Diseases (ICD)-9 and ICD-10 codes.AnalysisDescriptive analyses were performed to examine the trends in the prevalence of diabetes followed by trends in the practice of counseling services by patients with diabetes.ResultsThe proportion of hospitalized patients with T2DM receiving counseling increased statistically from 0.36 per 100,000 hospitalizations in 2011 to 0.43 in 2019. Lifestyle counseling was highest among those aged 65 and older, non-Hispanic Whites, and those with Medicare, with decreasing trends in utilization among younger, 18-34 and 35-54 age groups, and those identifying as Hispanic.ConclusionsIncreased provision and uptake of lifestyle counseling for and among hospitalized patients with T2DM is needed to align with a health care system moving towards value-based care. Resources to increase provider knowledge and referral rates are needed to increase the uptake of lifestyle counseling.

articles.title: Vector Flow Mapping Energy Loss and Pump Flow in Left Ventricular Assist Device Patients: A Transesophageal Echocardiography Pilot Study.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support redirects intraventricular flow toward the inflow cannula. We examined whether vector flow mapping-derived energy loss (EL), a measure of viscous dissipation related to spatial velocity gradients, was associated with controller-displayed pump flow. This prospective single-center pilot enrolled 33 patients undergoing LVAD-related surgery with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography; 31 HeartMate 3 recipients were analyzable. The maximum available peak EL across three views was the primary measure. Log-transformed maximum peak EL was associated with displayed flow after adjustment for pump speed and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (B = 0.181, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.033-0.330), cannula angle (B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.052-0.356), or aortic regurgitation grade (B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.050-0.358). Among 28 complete cases, associations persisted using the mean of three view-specific peaks (B = 0.213-0.245; p = 0.007-0.019). In a 10-case interobserver reanalysis, maximum peak EL had an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.759 (95% CI: 0.294-0.934), with ratio limits of agreement of 0.56-2.41. Cannula angle and aortic regurgitation grade were not associated with EL. These preliminary findings support larger prospective studies but do not establish mechanism, measurement interchangeability, or clinical utility.

articles.title: C-reactive protein, rather than pyuria, may help differentiate asymptomatic bacteriuria from symptomatic urinary tract infection.
articles.abstract: Distinguishing asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB) from symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI) may reduce unnecessary antibiotic use. We retrospectively compared admission C-reactive protein (CRP), urinary leukocyte count, and hematologic indices in 400 consecutive episodes of significant bacteriuria in 337 adults referred to an infectious diseases service between January 2021 and June 2026. Two investigators independently applied Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) criteria to documented symptoms; bacteremia concordant with the urine isolate indicated infection. Analyses used areas under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves (AUCs), patient-level cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals (CIs), and multivariable logistic regression. ASB accounted for 154 episodes (38.5%); baseline characteristics were broadly similar between groups. All ASB episodes received antibiotics (median 11 days; 1,778 antibiotic-days); 47 of 95 with bacterial isolates (49.5%) involved resistant organisms. CRP had an AUC of 0.892 (95% CI 0.858-0.923), outperforming the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR; 0.714), procalcitonin (0.672), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII; 0.580), and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR; 0.441; all comparisons p < 0.001). Urinary leukocyte count did not discriminate (AUC 0.482; 95% CI 0.429-0.539). CRP discrimination was lower against localized than systemic UTI (AUC 0.784 vs. 0.915). Below 5 mg/L, 3 of 46 episodes were symptomatic UTI (negative predictive value [NPV] 93.5%; 95% CI 82.5-97.8%). Among modeled inflammatory markers, only CRP was independently associated with symptomatic UTI (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 8.05 per log unit). Platelet counts were higher in ASB (272 vs. 243 ×10³/µL; p = 0.003), potentially explaining weaker performance of platelet-containing indices than NLR alone. In this retrospective cohort, admission CRP showed good discrimination between episodes classified as ASB and symptomatic UTI, whereas pyuria did not. The low-CRP threshold requires prospective validation before guiding antibiotic withholding.

articles.title: Urinary incontinence and its association with clinical and respiratory characteristics in women with asthma: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: The association between asthma and urinary incontinence is investigated. In this cross-sectional, descriptive study, we aimed to determine the effects of urinary incontinence in women with asthma. Participants were evaluated using the International Urinary Incontinence Advisory Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-UI-SF), Urinary Incontinence Severity Index, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), Asthma Control Test (ACT), and COSMEDFX. The relationship between urinary incontinence and anxiety, depression was assessed using the Pearson correlation coefficient test. Multivariate linear regression analysis was used to identify specific variables independently associated with the ICIQ-UI-SF score. HADS scores were higher in women with asthmatic urinary incontinence (p = 0.034); ACT, FEV1%, FEV1/FVC, MEP scores were lower (p = 0.017,0.028,0.007,0.026). Women with asthma; age, number of births, severity of urinary incontinence, depression, severity of asthma, expiratory muscle strength, and ICIQ-UI-SF were associated with urinary incontinence. There may be a relationship between respiratory symptoms, changes in intrathoracic pressure, and urinary incontinence in women with asthma.

articles.title: Can Testimonial Learning be Considered Rational?: Revisions, Extensions, and New Insights to a Theory of Selective Trust.
articles.abstract: Numerous studies have shown that children selectively learn from others' testimony and are not indiscriminately trusting of all social interaction. Thirteen years ago, we published a paper (Sobel & Kushnir, 2013) that introduced a theory of selective trust in testimony grounded in rational learning mechanisms similar to those we developed with our mentor, Alison Gopnik, to explain children's causal reasoning and theory change. In honor of Alison receiving the Rumelhart Award, we take the opportunity to engage with our original claims, update them in light of new evidence, and propose ways to integrate the rational framework with new ideas in the field. We begin with a review of two recent meta-analyses that support the rational learning account. We then consider new data showing that testimony enhances processing of children's own observations and actions and discuss how this data might lead to extensions of our theory. We next revisit and modify our original claims about "emotional trust" and suggest that affiliative motives which conflict with truth-seeking motives may alter, or even undermine, the rational learning process. We end with new directions for selective trust research: examining developmental changes from infancy, integrating more cultural influences, and considering the role of selective trust in children's increasing interactions with AI and other technology.

articles.title: A Stage-Based Clinical Framework for Addressing Family Building Across the Cancer Survivorship Continuum.
articles.abstract: Family building is a priority for many reproductive-aged women with cancer. These patients experience higher rates of infertility and primary ovarian insufficiency and lower live birth rates than their nonaffected peers. The current health care infrastructure prioritizes fertility preservation in the peridiagnostic period, a focus well justified in its attempt to allow future posttreatment attempts at pregnancy. However, this approach risks overlooking the full longitudinal continuum of reproductive care that patients may require, particularly in the immediate- and long-term survivorship period, during which patients may re-engage with parenthood goals. In this commentary, we introduce a stage-based framework to delineate key phases across this continuum: 1) fertility preservation at diagnosis, 2) posttreatment fertility counseling and assessment, and 3) pregnancy planning. We offer opportunities to integrate obstetrician-gynecologists with subspecialist expertise across reproductive endocrinology and infertility, oncology, and maternal-fetal medicine to address gaps in care. Extending focus beyond the time of diagnosis and prioritizing coordinated stage-specific care across the survivorship period represents a necessary next step to align clinical practice with the reproductive goals of cancer survivors.

articles.title: Severe proliferative lupus nephritis in two transgender women with long-term feminizing hormone exposure.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEstrogen is implicated in the female preponderance of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), but sustained exogenous estrogen exposure in a 46,XY individual cannot be studied in a trial, and only three cases of biopsy-proven lupus nephritis have been reported in transgender women on gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT).CasesCase 1, aged 31, had begun GAHT about a decade before presentation and had a first- and second-degree family history of SLE. She had already been lost to endocrine follow-up when lupus-specific antibodies were documented at 25; the rheumatology consultation requested then did not take place, and she continued oral estradiol unassessed for 6 years. She presented with nephrotic syndrome and class IV+V nephritis (NIH activity index 20/24). After remission, an unsupervised switch from transdermal back to oral estradiol was followed within 1 month by a rise in proteinuria from 0.5 to 3.1 g/24 h, which returned to 0.65 g/24 h 3 weeks later with the prednisone taper paused and no other change in treatment. Case 2, aged 38, reported estrogen-progestogen use from the age of 18 for about 15 years, discontinued about 5 years before presentation, at doses she could not specify and with no hormone level available. She presented with oligo-anuric acute kidney injury requiring hemodialysis, polyserositis, hemolytic anemia and class IV nephritis. Microangiopathic hemolysis (schistocytes, haptoglobin ≤10 mg/dL from day 8, normal ADAMTS13 activity, platelets 144 ×109/L at onset) was treated with corticosteroids, rituximab and, from day 14, eculizumab under a working diagnosis of atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome; the biopsy, taken after treatment had begun, showed no microangiopathic lesion. She became dialysis-independent after 36 days and reached partial remission.ConclusionsTwo cases cannot establish a causal role for estrogen: in neither can cumulative exposure be quantified, in Case 2 it had ended about 5 years before onset, and in Case 1 family history, autoantibodies present 6 years before diagnosis and the absence of rheumatological assessment in that interval explain the severity at presentation at least as well. The hypothesis they raise is that gender-affirming estrogen exposure may unmask or accelerate SLE in predisposed individuals. No guideline recommends autoimmune screening before or during GAHT, and both patients had taken estrogen for years without contact with care. Recording a family history of SLE at the start of GAHT, and a low threshold for urinalysis and serology when symptoms appear, might be warranted.

articles.title: Beyond symptom reduction: The effectiveness of cognitive behavioural therapy for interpersonal problems.
articles.journal: Psychotherapy research : journal of the Society for Psychotherapy Research
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Interpersonal problems are important transdiagnostic features in the development and treatment of mental disorders. However, evidence on causal effects of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and differential treatment effects on interpersonal problems is scarce.

METHOD: We emulated two treatment arms comparing modern routine CBT (nCBT = 256) with a naturalistic waitlist control condition (nwaiting condition = 431) using observational data of outpatients with various mental disorders assessed at three measurement points: waitlist intake, pre- and post-therapy. Causal forest analysis was applied to estimate treatment effects on self-reported interpersonal problems, given observed baseline variables.

RESULTS: Analyses indicate moderate effectiveness of CBT for perceived interpersonal distress, alongside an estimated increase in self-reported dominance. No patient characteristics predicted a substantial treatment advantage of CBT over waiting.

CONCLUSION: Although the findings are subject to methodological limitations and should be interpreted cautiously, they provide preliminary evidence that CBT may be an effective and broadly applicable treatment for interpersonal problems. Future randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these results and establish causal inference.Clinical or methodological significance of this articleAlthough a few studies have established causal effects of cognitive behavioural therapy on interpersonal outcomes, comparable evidence from routine clinical practice has been lacking. This study demonstrates how novel machine learning approaches can be used to approximate treatment effects using routine outcome data, thereby providing valuable insights into effectiveness across both global and dimensional measures of interpersonal problems.

articles.title: Molecular subtyping, prognostic model construction, and immune microenvironment analysis of cervical squamous cell carcinoma based on metabolic health and disease prevention.
articles.abstract: Background: Cervical squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) development is modulated not only by HPV infection but also by host metabolic health. Purpose and method: This study characterised disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) in 241 TCGA-CESC and 300 GSE44001 patients to build a prognostic model and interpret it within a metabolic health-oriented prevention framework. Seventeen differentially expressed DRGs, enriched in glycolysis, fatty acid metabolism, and redox homeostasis, defined three metabolic-distinct molecular subtypes. Result: A six-gene DRG-score (DSTN, TLN1, MTHFD1L, MYH10, TXN, SLC7A11) and nomogram predicted prognosis effectively (C-index 0.747/0.665; 1-year AUC 0.835). High-risk tumours showed an immunosuppressed phenotype (immunotherapy response 20.0% vs. 71.9%) concordant with obesity- and diabetes-associated immune dysfunction, and reduced sensitivity to methotrexate, implicating one-carbon metabolism. Conclusion: These findings indicate that metabolic health optimisation-weight control, nutrition, physical activity, and management of diabetes and dyslipidemia-constitutes a modifiable pillar of CSCC prevention complementary to HPV vaccination and screening, warranting prospective validation with DRG-based stratification.

articles.title: IL-2Rα Overexpression Enhances CAR T-Cell Therapeutic Efficacy in B-Cell Lymphoma.
articles.abstract: Interleukin-2 (IL-2) is critical for sustaining T-cell expansion during infection and cancer. However, the α subunit of the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (IL-2Rα, also known as CD25) is only transiently expressed following activation, limiting durable cytokine responsiveness. To overcome this barrier, we engineered CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells with constitutive IL-2Rα expression and evaluated their functional fitness. CAR19-IL-2Rα T cells exhibited hypersensitive STAT5 signaling and proliferated more robustly than conventional CAR19 T cells under limiting IL-2 conditions. In long-term rechallenge assays, enforced IL-2Rα expression sustained proliferation, enhanced tumor clearance, and conferred resistance to regulatory T cell (Treg)-mediated suppression by improving competition for IL-2. In a xenograft B cell lymphoma model, CAR19-IL-2Rα T cells improved tumor control and survival without increasing circulating cytokine levels associated with cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or the expression of exhaustion-associated markers PD1 and LAG3. Transcriptomic profiling revealed strong induction of DDIT4, an mTORC1 inhibitor, following constitutive IL-2Rα expression in vivo, suggesting the activation of a feedback mechanism that limits CAR T-cell expansion. Together, these results identify IL-2Rα overexpression as an engineering strategy that enhances CAR T-cell function, improves resistance to Treg-mediated immunosuppression, and promotes durable antitumor activity. This work establishes cytokine receptor rewiring as a simple and clinically compatible approach to enhance CAR T-cell therapy in B-cell malignancies.

articles.title: Dissecting the Genetic Architecture of White Spot Resistance in Tropical Maize Reveals Novel Loci and Valuable Breeding Resources.
articles.abstract: Maize white spot (MWS) is a severe foliar disease that threatens maize production and grain quality worldwide. Understanding the genetic basis of resistance is crucial for the development of durable resistant varieties. In this study, a large multi-parent population (MPP) comprising 904 recombinant inbred lines (RILs), derived from six tropical/subtropical maize inbred lines crossed with a temperate line, was used to identify genetic variations underlying MWS resistance. Phenotypic data collected over 4 years, combined with 6,390,967 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) obtained from whole-genome resequencing, established a comprehensive framework for dissecting the genetic basis of MWS resistance using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and linkage analysis. Population structure (Q) and kinship (K) were incorporated to control for relatedness. The combined analysis identified five promising candidate genes (Zmhsftf25, Zm00001eb107230, Zmmpk8, Zmmmp86, and Zm00001eb168510), which encode heat-stress transcription factors, remorin proteins, mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs), and leucine-rich repeat (LRR) proteins involved in defense signaling and stress responses. qRT-PCR further confirmed the early induction of these genes following infection. Haplotype analysis identified superior resistance haplotypes derived from tropical parents, which can be directly utilized in marker-assisted selection (MAS) for temperate maize improvement. Additionally, a putative "membrane-to-nucleus" signaling model was proposed to elucidate the molecular mechanism underlying maize immune response to MWS. This study not only identified novel loci associated with MWS resistance but also provided valuable genetic resources and a theoretical basis for overcoming the genetic bottleneck of temperate maize through marker-assisted breeding.

articles.title: NIR-Triggered Photothermal-Gated Microneedle Patch for Stage-Responsive Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Burn Wounds.
articles.abstract: Achieving precise and effective treatment of infected burn wounds across different healing stages remains a major challenge in current wound management strategies. To address this issue, we developed a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive photothermal-gated hemin-coated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PA)/magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) microneedle patch (abbreviated as PPMH), designed to enable spatiotemporally controlled therapeutic gaseous-ionic release for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling throughout wound healing. The microneedle matrix, constructed from biocompatible polymers, integrates exudate-absorbing components at the base and hydrogen-generating magnesium silicide nanosheets (MN) at the needle tips. A hydrophobic hemin shell serves as a photothermal-responsive gate for on-demand activation. Upon insertion into the wound tissue, the microneedles effectively penetrate biological barriers and establish localized therapeutic interfaces. Upon NIR irradiation, the hemin shell undergoes rapid photothermal conversion, triggering gate opening and controlled hydrogen release within the dermal tissue. During the inflammatory phase, the released hydrogen alleviates oxidative stress and suppresses inflammation, while the photothermal effect of the outer hemin coating exerts potent antibacterial action to clear local bacterial infection. In the subsequent regeneration phase, the sustained release of Mg2+ and Si-containing species promotes angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. Collectively, this system effectively modulates the wound microenvironment in a stage-dependent manner, accelerating tissue regeneration and functional recovery. Therefore, PPMH designed in this study represents a versatile and translational platform for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling and multi-targeted treatment of complex burn wounds.

articles.title: Platelet-derived extracellular vesicles aggravate macrophagic pyroptosis in Dabie bandavirus infection.
articles.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne infectious disease causing remarkably increased morbidity and mortality in East Asia. Thrombocytopenia is a hallmark pathogenic event in SFTS, clinical feature and an independent predictor of multi-organ failure and poor clinical outcomes. Although Dabie bandavirus (DBV) can bind to and replicate within platelets, the contribution of activated platelets to SFTS pathogenesis remains elusive. Here, we identify platelet-derived extracellular vesicles induced by DBV (DPEVs) as critical mediators of immune dysregulation. DBV-activated platelets released abundant extracellular vesicles that directly induced macrophage pyroptosis and markedly amplified virus-driven inflammatory responses. Proteomic and functional analyses demonstrated that DPEVs reprogram macrophages toward a pro-inflammatory and pyroptosis-prone state. Compared with vesicles generated by physical disruption, DPEVs displayed enhanced immunostimulatory capacity, indicating stimulus-dependent functional specialization. Mechanistically, DPEVs disrupted mitochondrial integrity, promoted mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production, thereby triggering the downstream pyroptotic program. In addition, DPEVs were capable of incorporating viral components, suggesting a potential dual role in both inflammatory amplification and viral dissemination. Collectively, these findings define a previously unrecognized pathogenic axis linking platelet activation, extracellular vesicle signaling, mitochondrial injury, and macrophage pyroptosis during DBV infection. DPEVs act as a key amplifier of inflammation and provide a mechanistic link between thrombocytopenia and disease severity in SFTS, highlighting their potential value as both biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: The Aspergillus fumigatus C2-domain protein SppA is required for septal integrity and alters susceptibility to echinocandins and neutrophil killing during infection.
articles.abstract: Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen whose ability to maintain hyphal integrity and withstand host defenses is critical for virulence. Septal pores, which connect hyphal compartments, are dynamically regulated to preserve cellular integrity under stress, yet the molecular components governing this process remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify and characterize a septal pore-associated protein, SppA, and demonstrate its essential role in maintaining septal integrity in A. fumigatus. We show that expression of SppA is positively regulated by the transcription factor ZfpA and is induced in response to the cell wall-targeting antifungal caspofungin. Deletion of sppA resulted in defective septal organization and increased susceptibility to hyphal damage. The mutant exhibited heightened sensitivity to cell wall-targeting antifungal agents, indicating a role in cell wall stress tolerance. In a zebrafish model of invasive aspergillosis, loss of SppA significantly attenuated virulence which was abrogated in neutrophil-deficient zebrafish. Further, the mutant strain displayed increased susceptibility to killing by primary human neutrophils, suggesting that proper septal pore formation contributes to fungal survival during host immune attack. Together, our findings establish SppA as a critical determinant of septal integrity, antifungal tolerance, and pathogenicity in A. fumigatus, and position it as part of a ZfpA-regulated, caspofungin-responsive pathway that supports fungal survival during stress and infection.

articles.title: Nutrition-Related Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices of Oncology Nurses: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional support is an essential component of comprehensive cancer care, and oncology nurses serve as key implementers. Yet the nutrition-related knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of these nurses, as well as influencing factors, remain insufficiently explored.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate nutrition-related KAP among clinical oncology nurses, analyze the impact of demographic and organizational variables, and propose targeted management strategies.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional design was employed. Participants were oncology nurses recruited from three tertiary hospitals in China via convenience sampling. Data were collected through a self-administered structured questionnaire. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, independent samples t tests (with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons), one-way analysis of variance tests (followed by post hoc Tukey HSD [honest significant difference] tests), Spearman correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression.

RESULTS: Of the 412 eligible nurses who were invited, 362 completed the questionnaire (response rate, 87.9%). The mean total KAP score was 71.2, with mean subscale scores of 23.1 for knowledge, 23.8 for attitudes, and 24.3 for practices; these subscale means represent, retrospectively, 72%, 79%, and 64% of maximum possible totals, suggesting a relative weakness in the practices dimension. Significant positive correlations were detected between total KAP scores and number of nutrition-related trainings in the past year, possession of nutrition-related professional certification, presence of a designated clinical dietitian in the department, number of years working in oncology, research project participation, professional title, and age. Multiple linear regression revealed seven independent predictors, with an adjusted R2 of 0.468, accounting for 46.8% of the total variance: number of nutrition-related trainings in the past year (standardized β = 0.30), number of years working in oncology (standardized β = 0.25), presence of a designated clinical dietitian (standardized β = 0.22), research project participation (standardized β = 0.20), possession of nutrition-related professional certification (standardized β = 0.18), professional title (standardized β = 0.15), and age (standardized β = 0.12). Post hoc power analysis (for a regression model with 11 predictors, α = 0.05, R2 = 0.468, N = 362) indicated a power greater than 0.99.

CONCLUSIONS: The clinical oncology nurses in this study exhibited moderately high levels of nutrition-related KAP; yet a discernible knowledge-practice gap was evident. Improving the nutrition management capabilities of oncology nurses demands integrative strategies that combine ongoing individual professional development and robust institutional support. Key recommendations include implementing tiered training programs, embedding clinical dietitians in oncology care teams, promoting nurses' active research involvement, and developing specialized nutrition-related certification pathways.

articles.title: Temporal trends in gonorrhea and chlamydia infections during pregnancy: 2013-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective was to evaluate GC and CT infection prevalence and risk factors in pregnancy.

METHODS: Retrospective cross-sectional study of all pregnant patients who delivered 2013-2023 at a tertiary care center in Alabama. Primary outcome was the prevalence of composite GC and/or CT infection (GC/CT) during pregnancy; secondary outcomes included rates of individual GC or CT, coinfection, time to treatment and rate of treatment. Outcomes were compared with joinpoint regression models. A planned secondary analysis compared risk factors associated with GC/CT versus no infection over time.

RESULTS: 40,139 patients were included. 7.5% (N=3011) had composite GC/CT infection: 0.9% (N=361) GC, 5.8% (N=2309) CT, and 0.8% (N=341) both. Only CT rates statistically decreased when adjusting for changes in patient characteristics (aOR 0.98 [95%CI 0.97-0.99]). Time to treatment decreased, with indeterminate clinical impact (2013: median 5 days [interquartile range (IQR)0-10], 2023: 2 days [IQR0-4]). Rate of treatment increased through 2017 (71.7%), then declined through 2023 (61.3%). GC/CT was associated with younger age, Black race, lower body mass index, single status, singleton pregnancy, and government insurance/self-pay (all adjusted OR significant). By the end of the study, patients with GC/CT were more likely to self-identify with Hispanic ethnicity (2013:6.2% [N=20/325 (95%CI 4.0-9.3)], 2023:18.6% [N=36/194 (95%CI 13.7-24.6)]) and have private insurance (2013:5.5% [N=18/325 (95%CI 3.5-8.6)], 2023:14.9% [N=29/194 (95%CI 10.6-20.6)]) (all p-for-trend<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: We describe decreasing prevalence of CT infection in pregnancy at our center. We affirm well-established GC/CT risk factors and suggest increasing associations of private payor status and Hispanic ethnicity with GC/CT infection.

articles.title: BiLLM-DR: Bilinear LLM-Enhanced Heterogeneous Graph Learning for Drug Repositioning.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Drug repositioning seeks to identify new therapeutic indications for existing drugs, yet computational prediction remains challenging because drug-disease association networks are sparse, highly imbalanced, and frequently fail to fully exploit biomedical semantic information. We propose BiLLM-DR, a bilinear large language model (LLM)-enhanced heterogeneous graph learning framework for drug repositioning. BiLLM-DR uses a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder to derive semantic representations from relation-masked drug and disease textual profiles. These representations are refined through message passing over drug-similarity, disease-similarity, and training-only drug-disease association graphs, while a bilinear predictor models disease-specific drug compatibility for candidate prioritization. In ten-fold cross-validation, validation and test associations were excluded from graph construction, and all unknown pairs in the corresponding evaluation partitions were retained as candidate negatives. BiLLM-DR achieved AUC values of 0.9737 and 0.9669 and AUPR values of 0.7052 and 0.6273 on Cdataset and Fdataset, respectively. DropEdge-rate analyses further supported the use of DropEdge as sparse-graph regularization in this architecture. A retrospective RepoDB-based evaluation yielded AUC/AUPR values of 0.7517/0.8011 and 0.8116/0.7598 on the two datasets, respectively. An asthma case study provided additional database-based and computational evidence for selected prioritized candidates. Collectively, these results support the utility of integrating biomedical semantics, heterogeneous graph learning, and bilinear interaction modeling for drug repositioning.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Elevated Left Ventricular End-Diastolic Pressure in STEMI Patients Undergoing Primary PCI: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (LVEDP) during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) may reflect early ventricular stiffness and impaired filling after ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its prognostic value remains uncertain. MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through February 14, 2026, for studies comparing elevated versus normal or low LVEDP in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models for all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiac mortality, overall heart failure, stroke, and recurrent myocardial infarction, with subgroup analyses by follow-up duration and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty assessment. Eight studies comprising 9820 patients were included. Elevated LVEDP was significantly associated with increased all-cause mortality (RR: 1.83, 95% CI: 1.48-2.27, P < 0.001), remaining consistent across short-term (RR: 2.22 [1.64-3.00], P < 0.001), intermediate-term (RR: 2.00 [1.33-3.01], P = 0.009), and long-term (RR: 1.57 [1.24-1.98], P < 0.001) follow-up. Elevated LVEDP also predicted higher risks of cardiac mortality (RR: 2.06, 95% CI: 1.49-2.85, P < 0.001), MACE (RR: 2.31, 95% CI: 1.03-5.21, P = 0.04), and overall heart failure (RR: 1.42, 95% CI: 1.06-1.90, P = 0.02). No significant associations were observed for stroke or recurrent myocardial infarction. Evidence certainty was predominantly low or very low. In STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, elevated LVEDP indicates higher all-cause mortality, cardiac mortality, MACE, and overall heart failure, but not stroke or recurrent infarction. Standardized LVEDP thresholds are needed for clinical risk stratification.

articles.title: Opt-out syphilis screening for priority populations in a high-volume hospital emergency department, Miami, Florida, 2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital syphilis (CS) prevention requires timely diagnosis and treatment of pregnant females with syphilis. Lack of prenatal care, or medical care without syphilis screening, are common reasons pregnant females with syphilis are not diagnosed timely. To address this gap, an emergency department (ED) in Miami-Dade County, Florida implemented an opt-out syphilis screening program geared toward females of child-bearing age. We describe syphilis screening and treatment outcomes to inform CS prevention efforts.

METHODS: All syphilis tests from 2023 performed in the ED were stratified by test results. Patients with positive syphilis results were matched against Florida's sexually transmitted infection surveillance system to identify new infections. Treatment of new syphilitic infections was assessed by location, timing of treatment initiation, and treatment completion.

RESULTS: A total of 15,345 ED visits included syphilis testing; 1,194 (8%) were reactive for syphilis, and 164 new syphilitic infections were identified (1% of those tested). Among new syphilitic infections, 79% (n=129) were adequately treated (100% of pregnant females), with 51% (n=66) treated at the ED (11% empiric treatment) and 33% (n=43) treated at the local health department. Two-thirds (n=110) of new infections were among females: 13 were pregnant, 9 became pregnant within a year. All but 2 pregnancies (20 of 22) did not result in CS.

CONCLUSION: Opt-out syphilis screening geared toward females of childbearing age identified new syphilitic infections, providing timely syphilis diagnosis and treatment that prevented most CS infections. Most patients diagnosed with syphilis were successfully treated within the ED. However, collaboration with local health departments substantially increased successful treatment.

articles.title: Combined resistance and aerobic exercise in chronic kidney disease: An exploratory study of physical activity as a moderator of adaptations.
articles.abstract: Physical inactivity is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and might contribute to impaired skeletal muscle and physical function. Whether habitual physical activity (PA) influences adaptation to structured exercise in CKD remains unclear. We examined the effects of 6 weeks of combined flywheel resistance and aerobic exercise (FRE+AE) on neuromuscular and physical function and explored whether baseline self-reported PA moderated treatment response in older male Veterans with stages 3-4 CKD. Twenty-four participants were randomized to FRE+AE (n = 12) or health education (EDU; n = 12).
