Outcomes included vastus lateralis (VL MT) and rectus femoris (RF MT) muscle thickness, maximal voluntary isometric torque (MVIT), isokinetic knee-extensor power at 60° s- 1 and 180° s- 1, gait speed (GS), five-repetition sit-to-stand (STS) and timed up and go (TUG). Intervention effects were evaluated using baseline-adjusted linear regression, and baseline PA was examined as a continuous moderator. At 6 weeks, FRE+AE resulted in greater VL MT than EDU (adjusted difference, 3.31 mm; 95% confidence interval, 0.91-5.71; P = 0.010) and greater GS (0.17 m s- 1; 95% confidence interval, 0.07-0.26; P = 0.002). Treatment effects for RF MT (2.09 mm; P = 0.051) and isokinetic power at 180° s- 1 (28 W; P = 0.060) favoured FRE+AE but were not statistically significant after controlling for multiple comparisons. No clear treatment effects were observed for MVIT, power at 60° s- 1, STS or TUG. Baseline PA did not moderate treatment effects across outcomes. These findings demonstrate that short-term FRE+AE can improve VL MT and GS in older male Veterans with moderate-to-advanced CKD, whereas baseline habitual self-reported PA did not explain variation in treatment responsiveness.

articles.title: Endurance Exercise Training Before Myocardial Infarction Reduces Decline of Myocardial Function in Old Mice.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pre-infarction endurance training reduces scar formation and adverse cardiac remodeling in rodents; however, evidence is largely restricted to young animals. Whether these benefits extend to aged individuals, the population most affected by myocardial infarction (MI), remains unclear.

METHODS: We investigated the effects of 6 weeks of endurance exercise training prior to MI in aged mice (20 months). C57BL/6 mice were randomized to exercise (EX-MI, n=11; treadmill running 30 min/day, 5 days/week) or sedentary conditions (SED-MI, n=12). MI was induced by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending artery. FDG PET imaging was performed on days 5 and 7 post MI, and cardiac structure and function were evaluated by MRI at day 28. Histological analyses were performed ex vivo.

RESULTS: Exercise training resulted in smaller and thicker infarct scars compared with sedentary controls. Despite similar lef t ventricular dilation, EX-MI mice showed significantly improved systolic function, with higher ejection fraction and stroke volume. This was supported by enhanced global longitudinal and radial strain rates. Likewise, regional deformation analysis demonstrated higher circumferential and radial strain within the scar. FDG uptake was increased in the infarct region at day 7. Additionally, remote myocardium was thicker and exhibited greater radial deformation in exercised animals.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows that short time endurance exercise training in older mice prior to acute MI reduces post-MI left ventricular remodeling, scar size, and scar thinning. Myocardial contractility in both the remote and infarct areas were preserved by endurance training, potentially reflecting an enhanced compensatory capacity induced by pre-infarction exercise training.

articles.title: Bias in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency testing: observations from a real-world evidence study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) affects an estimated 80,000-100,000 individuals in the US, yet fewer than 10% of those with severe genotypes are identified. Despite guidelines recommending testing all COPD patients, real-world testing rates remain low, and the clinical features driving testing decisions-and whether they validly identify AATD-are poorly characterized. We aimed to characterize who undergoes AATD testing in COPD and whether the features driving testing align with AATD-specific risk.

METHODS: Using de-identified EHR data from the EVERSANA database (2015-2023) covering >2.8 million COPD patients, using a combination of diagnosis codes, treatments and laboratory results patients were identified as AATD-positive (n = 5962), AATD-negative (n = 36,837), or AATD-unknown/untested (n = 2,223,048). After entropy balancing, demographic, clinical, and medication characteristics were compared across groups to identify features associated with testing and assess whether those features corresponded to positive identification.

RESULTS: Only 1.7% of eligible COPD patients were tested. AATD-negative patients showed the highest prevalence of symptom-related diagnoses and COPD medication use, including shortness of breath (66% vs. 59% in positives) and albuterol use (73% vs. 64%). Emphysema-the feature most specific to AATD-was more prevalent among AATD-positive than AATD-negative patients (40% vs. 34%) and lowest among the untested (20%). Untested patients were older (53% ≥65), less symptomatic, and less intensively treated.

CONCLUSIONS: Testing decisions appear driven by general symptom burden and severity rather than AATD-specific features like emphysema, systematically overlooking older, less symptomatic patients most likely to be missed. Machine learning-assisted candidate identification, reflex testing, and clinical decision support offer promising strategies to close this gap.

articles.title: Interpreting Biomarker Dynamics After Acute Heart Failure: Lessons From PREMIER.
Right atrial reservoir strain and clinical outcomes after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical relevance of right atrial (RA) function in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) remains unclear. We investigated the association between RA reservoir strain (RASr) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing M-TEER.

METHODS: We retrospectively assessed RASr using automated two-dimensional strain analytical software in patients undergoing M-TEER. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization after M-TEER.

RESULTS: Of 298 patients undergoing M-TEER (age 78.1 ± 9.6 years; male 61.1%; and functional mitral regurgitation 64.4%), the median RASr was 19.6% (interquartile range: 10.3-32.5%). Atrial fibrillation, larger RA area, lower left atrial reservoir strain, and lower tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion or right ventricular fractional area change were correlated to lower RASr. Lower RASr was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome, independently of clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and procedural results (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.96 per 1% increase in RASr, 95% confidence interval: 0.92-0.99, p=0.031). Our maximally selected log-rank statistics showed that the optimal cut-off value of RASr to discriminate the primary outcome was 24%. Incorporating RASr into conventional clinical and echocardiographic parameters improved model fit, with a modest improvement in discrimination for clinical outcome after M-TEER.

CONCLUSION: Reduced RASr is associated with adverse clinical outcomes after M-TEER. Our findings highlight the potential importance of RASr as a component of right-sided cardiac function. The assessment of RASr may improve risk stratification in patients undergoing M-TEER.

articles.title: Protocol to combine endocrine fibroblast growth factor concentrations into a single cardiovascular risk biomarker in chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract: Here, we present a protocol to combine endocrine fibroblast growth factor (FGF) concentrations into a single variable as a biomarker of cardiovascular risk in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). We describe steps for preparing the R environment and datasets, performing factor analysis, and deriving a composite score. We then detail score clustering and comparisons across CKD stages and cardiovascular event-free survival. This approach can be applied to similar settings to characterize phenotypes and assess their relationship with clinical outcomes. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Gonzalez-Rodriguez et al.1.

articles.title: Viral and host RLR ligands and role of m5C modification in innate immune response to influenza virus.
articles.abstract: RIG-I-like receptors (RLRs) are essential for detecting RNA virus infections and initiating antiviral immune responses. This study examines the roles of RIG-I, MDA5, and LGP2 in recognizing WT influenza virus infections and their RNA ligands at the nucleotide sequence and post-transcriptional modification levels. RIG-I and MDA5 are critical for sensing influenza A (IAV) and B (IBV) viruses. RNA ligands from RIG-I and LGP2 purifications demonstrate immunostimulatory activity in type-I IFN assays. RIG-I binds the negative-sense NS segment, and both RIG-I and LGP2 target the negative-sense M segment. Negative-sense viral segments are more potent in activating type-I IFN signaling than their positive-sense counterparts, which aligns with the IC50 values of the NS and M segments binding to RIG-I. Additionally, upon infection, RIG-I recognizes RNA polymerase III transcripts with reduced 5-methylcytosine (m5C) levels. These findings underscore the importance of viral and host ligands, along with NSUN2-driven post-transcriptional modifications, in RLR-mediated anti-influenza immunity.

articles.title: Creep in Minimum Inhibitory Concentration of Commonly Used Disinfectants Against Clinical and Hospital Environmental Bacterial Isolates.
articles.abstract: Indiscriminate disinfectant use in health care settings is quietly shaping a new resistance threat. Reduced susceptibility allows hospital pathogens to persist and co-select antibiotic resistance, undermining infection control. This study focuses on the emerging and often overlooked link between disinfectant tolerance and antimicrobial resistance in bacterial isolates from clinical and hospital environments. A total of 250 clinical isolates, Escherichia coli (50), Klebsiella pneumoniae (50), Acinetobacter baumannii (50), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (50), and Staphylococcus aureus (50), along with 12 outbreak-associated K. pneumoniae and 38 environmental isolates from hospital surfaces, were included. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the modified Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method. Minimum inhibitory and bactericidal concentrations (minimum inhibitory concentration [MIC] and minimum bactericidal concentration [MBC]) of seven commonly used disinfectants (benzalkonium chloride, sodium hypochlorite, glutaraldehyde, chlorhexidine, hydrogen peroxide, phenol, and ethyl alcohol) were determined by macrobroth dilution. Polymerase chain reaction was employed for qacA/B, qacE, Class 1 and 2 integrons, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) genes (blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M), and Class B and D carbapenemase genes (blaIMP, blaVIM, blaNDM, and blaOXA-48). Statistical analysis was done using Fisher's exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Multidrug resistance was observed among the clinical isolates. Disinfectants showed variable efficacy, with chlorhexidine, benzalkonium chloride, and glutaraldehyde exhibiting elevated MICs among outbreak and environmental isolates. Environmental isolates were significantly associated with higher MICs for benzalkonium chloride and glutaraldehyde (p < 0.0001). Class 1 integrons were notably observed in K. pneumoniae (90%) and E. coli (78%). Among the total isolates, 56% were ESBL producers, while 67% harbored multiple Class B β-lactamase genes. No association was seen between MIC values of the tested disinfectants and resistance genes.

articles.title: Rising Prevalence, Distinct Demographics, and Preserved Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Mucoid Pseudomonas aeruginosa-A 9-Year Single-Center Retrospective Study (2017-2025).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mucoid phenotype of Pseudomonas aeruginosa is associated with chronic respiratory infection, biofilm formation, and antimicrobial tolerance. Its epidemiological features in general hospital populations remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: All non-duplicate P. aeruginosa clinical isolates recovered between 2017 and 2025 at a tertiary hospital in China were analyzed retrospectively. Mucoid phenotype was determined by colony morphology. Antimicrobial susceptibility was interpreted per CLSI breakpoints.

RESULTS: Among 6,949 isolates, 1,932 (27.8%) were mucoid. The mucoid proportion rose from 14.0% in 2017 to 35.2% in 2025 (p < 0.001). Mucoid isolates showed significantly lower resistance rates than non-mucoid isolates across all 12 anti-pseudomonal agents tested (mean fold difference 4.7). Carbapenem resistance was 11.3% versus 34.7% for imipenem and 5.5% versus 30.8% for meropenem. Ceftazidime-avibactam retained activity against 99.3% of mucoid isolates. Mucoid isolates were predominantly from female patients (62.7%), outpatient settings (59.7% mucoid), and respiratory specimens (98.2%), whereas intensive care units had the lowest mucoid proportions (1.3% to 5.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Mucoid P. aeruginosa in the general hospital setting represents a clinically distinct entity characterized by rising prevalence, a female-predominant outpatient demographic, and preserved antimicrobial susceptibility. Recognition of the mucoid phenotype should prompt consideration of clinical context rather than automatic concern for multidrug resistance.

articles.title: Cellular communication network factor 3 functions as an osteoanabolic hormone during pregnancy and lactation.
An Interferon/JAK1-2/MCL1/BCL2A1/BCL-XL signaling axis causes resistance to Venetoclax in human AML.
articles.abstract: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we have profiled twenty human adult acute myelogenous leukemia (AML) samples and five normal bone marrows. We found that AML with monoblastic/monocytic differentiation aberrantly expressed a mixture of inflammation-associated and interferon (IFN) inducible genes and identified IL2RA, INHBA, EREG, and BCL2A1 as IFN target genes. The monoblastic/monocytic AML cells expressed types I and II IFN transcripts, which correlated with the expression of endogenous retroelements. Prognostically, high IFN target gene expression analyzed in TCGA AML data uncovered poor 3-year patient survival rates of 5% to 14%. We treated nineteen primary human AML with IFN types I and II ex vivo and measured frequent resistance induction to Venetoclax. While the baseline expression of anti-apoptotic BCL2 family members MCL1, BCL2A1, and BCL-XL in AML cells was highly variable, IFN treatment induced the combinatorial expression of MCL1, BCL2A1, and BCL-XL. The sum of expression of the three anti-apoptotic BCL2 family members divided by BCL2 best predicted resistance to Venetoclax ex vivo and in Decitabine/Venetoclax-treated patients in vivo. The treatment of primary human AML with the Janus Kinase 1-2 inhibitors Ruxolitinib or Baricitinib reversed IFN-induced Venetoclax resistance providing rationale and translational opportunities for improvements in Venetoclax-based therapies in AML.

articles.title: ENaC cleavage at furin sites supports renal sodium conservation in male mice.
articles.abstract: Epithelial Na+ channel (ENaC) activity is stimulated by proteolysis of its α and γ subunits, which involves the pro-protein convertase furin. Our recent work showed that disruption of furin sites in either the α or γ subunit produces a mild phenotype in mice, despite in vitro evidence that furin-dependent cleavage is critical for channel activity. To compound the defect in ENaC proteolysis, we generated mice that lack furin consensus sites in both the α and γ subunits (αF2MβγFM mice). Male αF2MβγFM mice had lower body weights and higher aldosterone levels, as well as increased ENaC expression compared to wild type (WT) mice during Na+ restriction. However, total ENaC activity was similar between WT and αF2MβγFM mice, as assessed by benzamil-induced natriuresis, patch clamp recordings from renal tubules, and amiloride-sensitive currents in the distal colon. Following benzamil treatment during Na+ restriction, αF2MβγFM mice exhibited signs of volume depletion and extremely high aldosterone levels compared to WT mice despite increased ENaC expression. αF2MβγFM mice fed a control diet also had lower body weights than WT mice and displayed signs of volume depletion. These data suggest that αF2MβγFM mice have impaired channel function, with organ-level ENaC activity being preserved through aldosterone-dependent compensation.

articles.title: Circulating cellular communication network factor 3 predicts maternal skeletal recovery during lactation.
A case report of a woman with accelerated junctional rhythm as the first manifestation of cardiac amyloid light-chain amyloidosis.
articles.abstract: Cardiac amyloid light-chain amyloidosis (CALA) usually presents in a manner similar to other cardiomyopathies and conduction disorders; however, junctional rhythm has rarely been reported. We present the case of a 47-year-old woman with CALA associated with multiple myeloma and an atypical clinical presentation. Her initial manifestations included right-sided heart failure, a transient ischemic attack, and acute-on-chronic pulmonary thromboembolism. The electrocardiogram showed a persistent junctional rhythm with right bundle branch block. Imaging studies demonstrated an infiltrative cardiomyopathy. CALA was suspected based on characteristic imaging findings and elevated serum lambda light-chain levels. During hospitalization, the patient developed dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Daratumumab-based regimen (Dara-CyBorD) was initiated; however, 6 months after diagnosis, the patient died due to cardiac decompensation. This case highlights that uncommon manifestations, such as junctional rhythm and dynamic obstruction, may be part of the clinical spectrum of CALA.

articles.title: Exploring the Requirements of Clinicians for Transparent and Trustworthy Decision Support Systems in Intensive Care: Focus Group Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding how digital systems can support clinical decision-making is crucial, especially with the growing deployment of increasingly complex AI models. This complexity raises concerns about trustworthiness, affecting the safe and effective adoption of such technologies. In intensive care units (ICUs), where clinicians make high-stakes, time-sensitive decisions, decision support tools must be designed to align with clinical needs and cognitive workflows. A better understanding of decision-making processes and requirements for decision support tools is vital for providing effective solutions.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigates ICU clinicians' decision-making processes, their use of decision support systems (DSSs), and the design requirements for DSSs to ensure transparent and trustworthy recommendations.

METHODS: We conducted 2 virtual focus groups with 7 ICU clinicians from 1 hospital in September 2024. Participants included nurses, charge nurses, and medical doctors, each with at least three years of professional experience. The focus groups explored participants' perspectives on DSSs in relation to our study objectives. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied to the focus group transcripts, and analytic decisions were made inductively using open coding. Both semantic and latent coding were used. Following independent coding, a combined codebook was developed collaboratively, from which key themes and subsequent design recommendations were identified.

RESULTS: Three core themes emerged from the analysis: ICU Decision-Making Relies on a Wide Range of Factors (theme 1); Complexity of Patient State Is Challenging for Shared Decision-Making (theme 2); and Acceptability and Usability of DSSs (theme 3). Five design recommendations derived from clinical input provide insights to inform future DSSs for intensive care: provide variable levels of detail (recommendation 1); support integration into existing clinical systems (recommendation 2); present explanations with additional contextual information (recommendation 3); prompt independent thought (recommendation 4); and facilitate communication of patient state (recommendation 5).

CONCLUSIONS: DSSs have the potential to enhance ICU decision-making, but their adoption depends on alignment with clinicians' needs and workflows. To improve trust and usability, future systems must provide transparent recommendations, adapt to varying levels of patient complexity, and facilitate rather than replace human expertise. Our findings inform the development of transparent and trustworthy DSSs, which may improve their acceptance in ICU settings.

articles.title: Stakeholder Acceptance, Trust, and Implementation of AI in Oncology: Mixed Methods Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI is entering oncology workflows faster than evidence on stakeholder acceptance, trust, and sustained use. Existing syntheses rarely distinguish anticipated attitudes from actual use across oncology stakeholders.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study is to synthesize primary empirical evidence on stakeholder acceptance, trust, and implementation of AI in oncology and examine variation by stakeholder group, clinical task, AI exposure, and implementation maturity.

METHODS: We conducted a Joanna Briggs Institute-guided mixed methods systematic review with convergent integrated synthesis; the protocol was registered before formal eligibility screening. Eight databases were searched without date or language limits (August 6-9, 2026), yielding 46,206 records and 31,802 unique records. Title and abstract screening used 2 balanced primary allocations, joint bidirectional readjudication, and blinded verification of a stratified 10% (n=3182) sample. Full-text assessment, extraction, and critical appraisal were dual independent. Acceptance/Trust modes and F1-F8 coverage were independently coded across 309 studies and reconciled. Eight integrated findings were anchored to the nonadoption, abandonment, scale-up, spread, and sustainability framework; an emergent economic finding was reported separately. Adjusted stage models controlled for study design, publication format, and publication period; robustness analyses examined screening provenance and appraisal sensitivity.

RESULTS: We included 309 primary empirical studies; 187 (60.5%) were published in 2025 or 2026. Exposure ranged from hypothetical opinion to real-world implementation (n=82 studies), but only 6 described routine use. Acceptance was empirically assessed in 267 studies and Trust in 127. Relative to anticipatory stage 1, Acceptance assessment was less frequent in evaluated-interaction stage 2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.07, 95% CI 0.02-0.25; P<.001) and stages 3+4 (aOR 0.12, 95% CI 0.03-0.45; P=.001). Transparency/explainability coverage (F3) was lower in stages 3+4 (aOR 0.20, 95% CI 0.08-0.47; q<0.001). Workflow/interoperability coverage (F5) was higher and governance coverage (F7) lower in both later contrasts after false discovery rate correction. Trust declined descriptively across stages, but adjusted contrasts were nonsignificant. Eight integrated findings spanned clinical value, performance, transparency, oversight, workflow, readiness, governance, and implementation, plus an emergent stage 1 economic finding. The principal Acceptance, F3, F5, and F7 findings persisted in the 229-study original screening subset.

CONCLUSIONS: In oncology, the AI evidence profile appears to differ from anticipated use to implementation. Acceptance was empirically assessed most often before deployment; later-stage studies more often examined workflow and less often examined transparency and governance. The challenge is whether favorable attitudes and early deployment translate into calibrated, governed, and sustained routine use. An interpretive stage-specific model identifies assessment priorities across exposure and implementation contexts, but is not a validated causal or predictive model. Later-stage evaluations should retain measurement of Acceptance, trust calibration, governance, durability, and workflow outcomes.

articles.title: Urgent True-Lumen Recovery Using Tip-Detection Antegrade Dissection and Re-Entry for Ongoing Myocardial Ischemia Caused by Progressive Subintimal Space Expansion.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Progressive subintimal space expansion during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a serious complication that may compress the true lumen, impair coronary flow, and cause ongoing myocardial ischemia. Tip-detection antegrade dissection and re-entry (TD-ADR) is an intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided re-entry technique developed for chronic total occlusion (CTO) intervention; however, its role as an emergency bailout strategy during non-CTO PCI remains unclear. An 84-year-old woman underwent elective PCI for a severely stenotic, tortuous left anterior descending artery lesion. Repeated guidewire attempts resulted in progressive subintimal space expansion with true-lumen compression, coronary flow deterioration, chest pain, and ischemic ST-segment elevation. As further parallel-wire attempts were considered unlikely to restore distal true-lumen access and risked further enlarging the subintimal space, IVUS-guided TD-ADR was adopted as an emergency bailout strategy. With the AnteOwl WR IVUS catheter and a Finecross GT-supported Conquest Pro 12 ST penetration wire positioned in parallel within the subintimal space, repeated transducer sweeps enabled real-time identification of the wire tip, its direction, and the target true lumen. Re-entry was achieved with a single puncture, followed by advancement of the microcatheter into the true lumen and exchange to a soft workhorse wire. Cutting-balloon fenestration then decompressed the subintimal space, after which drug-eluting stents were implanted. Final angiography demonstrated TIMI 3 flow and a satisfactory angiographic result. Peak creatine kinase was 560 U/L, follow-up echocardiography showed no new regional wall-motion abnormalities, and the patient was discharged without complications. This case suggests that TD-ADR may represent a valuable emergency bailout strategy for urgent true-lumen recovery in selected non-CTO PCI cases complicated by progressive flow-limiting subintimal space expansion. Early recognition of failed conventional wiring and timely conversion to TD-ADR may facilitate myocardial salvage.

articles.title: From Uncrossable to Under-Expanded: A Dual Role for Excimer Laser in Complex Calcific LAD PCI.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severely calcified coronary lesions remain a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), frequently resulting in difficulty with device crossing, inadequate lesion preparation, stent delivery, and lastly stent under-expansion. Intravascular imaging provides important information regarding the extent and distribution of coronary calcium and can guide in selecting appropriate calcium modification strategy. Excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA) is an established adjunctive technique that may be useful in selected balloon-uncrossable lesions as well as in refractory stent under-expansion.

CASE SUMMARY: A 52-year-old man with diabetes mellitus and hypertension presented with chest discomfort since 1 day, with electrocardiographic changes, a significantly positive Troponin value and normal ejection fraction. In view of clinical presentation of acute coronary syndrome, a coronary angiography was done which demonstrated calcific multivessel coronary artery disease with a 95% calcific stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) artery and an 80% distal LAD stenosis. After balloon pre dilatation, saline ELCA (0.9-mm catheter; fluence 50, rate 60) facilitated IVUS crossing. A 3.0 × 38-mm drug-eluting stent was deployed in the ostioproximal LAD but remained significantly under-expanded despite high-pressure balloon dilatation. Repeat ELCA followed by further balloon dilatation resulted in good stent expansion, with a final IVUS minimum stent area of 7.2 mm2 and TIMI 3 flow without residual stenosis or complications. The patient remained well at 6-month follow-up.

articles.title: Temporal stability of the Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Specific Comorbidity Index.
articles.abstract: Nearly two decades have elapsed since the Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation-Specific Comorbidity Index (HCT-CI) was reported, during which the allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) landscape has changed drastically. We examined whether the impact of the overall HCT-CI score and its components on transplant outcomes has changed over time. Our study included 33 679 patients who underwent their first allogeneic HSCT in Japan between 2008 and 2022. We assessed temporal trends in the prognostic impact of HCT-CI and its components on 2-year non-relapse mortality (NRM) using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models including interaction terms between transplant year and each covariate. The prognostic association of the total HCT-CI score with NRM appeared largely stable across transplant years, with hazard ratios (HRs) for HCT-CI ≥3 compared with HCT-CI = 0 ranging from 1.55 to 1.73, whereas the temporal validity of individual HCT-CI components was heterogeneous. Arrhythmia, cardiac disease, diabetes mellitus and infection showed consistently elevated HRs, prior solid tumour and severe pulmonary disease showed apparent time-dependent changes in effect size, and others showed null or weak effects. These findings suggest that HCT-CI remains relevant to post-HSCT risk stratification, whereas component weighting and definitions may warrant re-evaluation.

articles.title: Identification of the Ty-bearing resistance to tomato yellow leaf curl virus in north-central China and its breakdown by southern tomato virus infection.
articles.abstract: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) seriously impacts tomato production in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. Here, we collected 214 tomato samples during 2021-2024 from a major tomato production area in north-central China, Shanxi Province, and found the occurrence of TYLCV in 7 out of 9 cities. Resistance assay revealed that five out of six commonly-planted tomato cultivars lacked Ty resistance genes and were susceptible to TYLCV infection. Genotype analysis of field samples revealed that 57 samples harbored Ty resistance genes, and 16 out of them were mixed infected by TYLCV+southern tomato virus (STV) or TYLCV+STV+other viruses. Interestingly, although STV is seed-transmitted and exhibited no obvious symptoms in tomato plants, it promoted TYLCV infection in Ty-1/Ty-1 and Ty-1/ty-1+Ty-3a/ty-3a tomato plants and induced typical TYLCV symptoms in Ty-1/Ty-1 plants. Furthermore, we identified disease resistance (R) genes responsive to TYLCV infection and uncovered the potential antiviral role of SlCIPK11 and SlSTY46. These findings revealed the lack of Ty-based resistance in tomato plants in north-central China, and the breakdown of Ty-1- and Ty-3a-mediated TYLCV resistance due to STV. In summary, the mining and pyramiding of TYLCV-resistant R genes in commercial tomato cultivars will be a promising strategy for TYLCV management in the field under mixed infection.

articles.title: Methylophiopogonanone B Alleviates Hypoxic Pulmonary Hypertension by Modulating Mitophagy via SRC.
articles.abstract: Methylophiopogonanone B (MO-B), an active homoisoflavonoid from Ophiopogon japonicus (L.f.) Ker-Gawl, has shown diverse pharmacological activities, but its role in hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (HPH) remains unclear. Here, we investigated the therapeutic effect of MO-B on HPH and the underlying mechanism. In a rat model of chronic hypoxia-induced HPH, MO-B treatment significantly improved cardiopulmonary function, as reflected by increased PAT/PET and TAPSE, reduced right ventricular hypertrophy index, and attenuation of pulmonary vascular remodeling, fibrosis, and apoptosis. MO-B also restored mitochondrial function by increasing ATP production and respiratory chain complex I/II activities, while suppressing excessive FUNDC1-related mitophagy in lung tissues. In hypoxia-exposed human pulmonary artery endothelial cells, MO-B improved cell viability, reduced migration and apoptosis, alleviated mitochondrial damage, restored mitochondrial function, and inhibited mitophagy and autophagic flux. Multi-database target prediction, molecular docking, and cellular thermal shift assay identified SRC as a potential target of MO-B. Mechanistically, MO-B increased SRC phosphorylation, and its protective effects were enhanced by the SRC agonist Tolimidone but attenuated by the SRC inhibitor PP2 or SRC knockdown. These findings suggest that MO-B ameliorates HPH, at least in part, by inhibiting excessive mitophagy through the SRC/FUNDC1 signaling pathway, highlighting MO-B as a potential therapeutic candidate for HPH.

articles.title: Multi-omics reveals the mechanism of Amorphophallus albus response to Athelia rolfsii infection.
articles.abstract: Amorphophallus albus is an economically important crop with high edible and medicinal values. However, its commercial production is severely threatened by southern blight, caused by the devastating soil-borne fungus Athelia rolfsii ( A. rolfsii), and the molecular mechanisms of underlying A. rolfsii virulence and the corresponding host defense responses remain largely unexplored. In this study, A. rolfsii ( BJ25) was isolated from diseased Amorphophallus albus petioles, and its whole genome was sequenced and assembled, with high-quality genome and a size of 69.28 Mb. Pathogenicity assays and transmission electron microscope (TEM) revealed severe ultrastructural degradation in host petiole cells, characterized by the irreversible breakdown of chloroplasts, mitochondria, and cell walls. Physiological analyses demonstrated a collapse of the host antioxidant system: while peroxidase (POD) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities exhibited a transient early elevation, catalase (CAT) activity and malondialdehyde (MDA) content increased continuously, indicating severe oxidative stress and membrane lipid peroxidation. Furthermore, combined transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed that the coordination between transcription and translation gradually intensified in Amorphophallus albus upon pathogen infection. A total of 103 co-differentially expressed target genes, including PAL1/4, CYP, PR1-2 and ABC transporter genes, were screened from pathways of phenylpropanoid-derived secondary metabolism, plant-pathogen interaction, and phytohormone signal transduction. Among the dominant TF families (AP2/ERF, WRKY, and NAC), WRKY14, WRKY40, ERF4, and NAC036 serve as hub regulators. These TFs orchestrate downstream defense pathways through promoter binding and protein-protein interactions were verified by expression profiling, cis-element characterization and PPI prediction. Collectively, these findings systematically clarify the cytological, physiological, and molecular dynamics of the Amorphophallus albus and A. rolfsii interaction, providing valuable genomic resources and theoretical foundations for breeding resistant varieties and developing targeted disease control strategies.

articles.title: Real-World Data in Economic Evaluations of Schizophrenia: A Systematic Review of Roles, Applications and Methodological Gaps.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Real-world data (RWD) are increasingly used in health economic evaluation and health technology assessment (HTA). However, there is limited understanding of how RWD are incorporated into economic evaluations of schizophrenia, a condition characterised by complex care pathways and long-term disease trajectories. This review aims to systematically examine how RWD have been incorporated into economic evaluations of schizophrenia, with particular attention to their roles, patterns of use, reporting transparency and methodological limitations.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO). MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO were searched for studies published between 2015 and 2025 reporting full economic evaluations incorporating RWD. Data were extracted on study characteristics, methodological approaches and the use of RWD across analytical domains. Findings were synthesised narratively due to heterogeneity across studies. Reporting completeness was assessed using the Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS) 2022 checklist, and the suitability of electronic health record (EHR) data was evaluated using The Professional Society for Health Economics and Outcomes Research (ISPOR) Suitability of EHR Data (SUITABILITY) Checklist.

RESULTS: In total, 30 studies were included: 15 model-based, 12 observational and three trial-based evaluations. RWD use was concentrated in clinical inputs, including event-rate parameters, as well as healthcare utilisation and costs, with limited application to health utilities and broader societal outcomes. In model-based evaluations, RWD primarily informed individual parameters rather than model structure or complete treatment pathways. Observational evaluations used patient-level RWD directly, but several had small samples, and only a minority reported formal confounding adjustment. Trial-based evaluations mainly used RWD to supplement resource-use and cost data. Reporting of data processing, missingness and validation was incomplete, limiting assessment of data suitability and analytical credibility.

CONCLUSIONS: RWD use in schizophrenia economic evaluations remains concentrated in individual inputs, with limited application to model structure and long-term care pathways, where evidence on routine practice may offer particular added value. Priorities include better aligning RWD use with decision-relevant evidence needs, strengthening analytical methods and improving reporting transparency. RWD should be used selectively, alongside complementary evidence sources, where they are fit for purpose and their likely contribution to decision-making justifies the additional resources required.

articles.title: Bistability and intermittency: linking synaptic variability and slow potassium currents to spontaneous seizures generation.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous seizures emerge from abrupt transitions between asynchronous neural activity and pathological burst synchronization. In this work, we combine 24-hour recordings from rats with spontaneous absence seizures and a conductance-based neuronal network model to investigate the mechanisms underlying these transitions. By systematically varying excitatory and inhibitory coupling, we show that the model reproduces bistable and intermittent dynamical regimes and captures the duration and variability of seizure-like events observed experimentally. The similarity between simulated and experimental seizure duration distributions is supported by Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistics. To identify dynamical signatures of the transition from physiological to pathological activity, we analyzed postsynaptic potentials and the slow potassium current using recurrence-based measures. We find that the increase in inhibition enhances postsynaptic potential variability, thereby facilitating spontaneous switching between down and up-states. At the same time, the slow potassium currents exhibit a marked reorganization of its temporal structure, indicating that intrinsic ionic dynamics are also reshaped in the intermittent regime. Together, these findings suggest that spontaneous seizure-like activity emerges from the combined action of synaptic variability and intrinsic slow-current dynamics. More broadly, our results provide a computational framework for linking recurrence-based dynamical fingerprints to biophysical mechanisms of spontaneous seizure generation.

articles.title: Fibroblast growth factor 21 mediates pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease via the NRF2/GPX4 axis.
articles.abstract: Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent metabolic disorder among pediatric populations. Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) is a key regulator of hepatic metabolism; however, the mechanisms underlying its contribution to the pathogenesis of pediatric MASLD remain unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the role of FGF21 in obesity-associated MASLD and to examine the involvement of ferroptosis in this pathological process. In a cross-sectional cohort, serum concentrations of FGF21, 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE), and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in children with obesity and biopsy-confirmed MASLD. Subsequently, a murine model of MASLD was established by high-fat diet feeding, followed by assessment of body weight, blood lipid profiles, and serum FGF21 concentrations. Hepatic lipid accumulation and histopathological changes were assessed using hematoxylin and eosin staining, Oil Red O staining, and Masson staining. Serum ferroptosis-related biomarkers, including 4-HNE, glutathione (GSH), and the GSH/ oxidized glutathione (GSSG) ratio, were quantified by ELISA, whereas hepatic ferroptotic changes were examined by transmission electron microscopy. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction demonstrated reduced messenger RNA (mRNA) expression of FGF21, NFE2L2, and GPX4, whereas immunoblotting confirmed decreased protein expression of FGF21, NRF2, and GPX4 in samples from both children with MASLD and mice with high-fat diet-induced obesity. To investigate the functional role of FGF21, lentiviral-mediated knockdown of FGF21 was performed in HepG2 cells. Silencing FGF21 restored NRF2-GPX4 signaling and markedly attenuated hepatocellular lipid accumulation, indicating that suppression of this antioxidant pathway contributes to hepatic steatosis. Collectively, these findings suggest that FGF21-mediated ferroptosis may represent a mechanistic link between obesity and pediatric MASLD and identify the FGF21/NRF2/GPX4 axis as a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: Reintervention and postoperative complication rates after cerebrospinal fluid shunting for intracranial arachnoid cysts: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Intracranial arachnoid cysts are benign collections of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that may require surgical intervention when they become symptomatic. CSF shunting is a common treatment option, but it is associated with risks of complications and the need for further interventions. Therefore, evaluating these outcomes is crucial to inform management. This review aimed to evaluate reintervention and complication rates after CSF shunting for intracranial arachnoid cysts. This systematic review follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 protocol. In February 2026, the following search terms were used: ("Arachnoid Cysts"[MeSH] OR "arachnoid cyst" OR "intracranial arachnoid cyst") AND ("Cerebrospinal Fluid Shunts"[MeSH] OR shunt OR ventriculoperitoneal shunt OR cystoperitoneal shunt), in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science databases. A random-effects model was used to pool proportions, and heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic. Five retrospective observational studies comprising 332 patients were included, of whom 91 underwent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunting. The pooled reintervention rate, analyzed in 71 patients, was 18.8% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 9.7-33.3; I² = 17.5%). The pooled prevalence of postoperative complications, assessed in 80 patients, was 20.3% (95% CI: 4.38-58.62; I² = 83.6%), indicating substantial heterogeneity. Shunt-related infection, analyzed in 57 patients, occurred in 5.47% (95% CI: 1.77-15.65; I² = 0%), with no significant heterogeneity. In leave-one-out analysis, the pooled complication estimate ranged from 11% to 32%, and excluding one study removed most of the between-study heterogeneity. All five studies were at serious risk of bias. Cerebrospinal fluid shunting for intracranial arachnoid cysts is associated with substantial rates of reintervention and clinically relevant postoperative complications. The certainty of this evidence is very low. Given the burden of long-term shunt dependency, shunting is best reserved for patients in whom other treatments are unsuitable or have failed.

articles.title: Cost Effectiveness of Sublingual Edaravone Dexborneol versus Human Urinary Kallidinogenase in Treating Acute Ischemic Stroke in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The efficacy and safety of sublingual edaravone dexborneol (ED-SL) in treating acute ischemic stroke (AIS) have been well established by clinical trials. This study aims to evaluate the cost effectiveness of ED-SL versus human urinary kallidinogenase (HUK) for the treatment of AIS in China.

METHODS: From the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system, we developed a hybrid model combining a decision tree and a Markov model to assess the cost effectiveness of ED-SL compared with HUK over a 20-year time horizon. The analysis used a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold of 1.5 times China's 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) per capita. Clinical efficacy inputs were derived from the pivotal trials for each intervention (TASTE-SL for ED-SL and RESK for HUK) and adjusted using a matching-adjusted indirect comparison (MAIC). Costs and outcomes were discounted at 4.5% annually, with a 1-year cycle length. We performed both one-way sensitivity analyses (OWSA) and probabilistic sensitivity analyses (PSA) to evaluate the robustness of the base-case results.

RESULTS: Compared with HUK, ED-SL resulted in cost savings of ¥568 and gained an additional 0.3684 quality-adjusted life years, demonstrating that treatment with ED-SL was dominant to treatment with HUK. The results were robust across both the OWSA and PSA methods.

CONCLUSIONS: ED-SL is a more cost-effective treatment for AIS patients than HUK in China.

articles.title: Impact of achieving target serum uric acid levels ≤6.0 mg/dL on renal function decline and cardiovascular events in individuals with hyperuricemia: a JMDC database study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Urate-lowering therapy (ULT) is standard hyperuricemia treatment. The effectiveness of achieving the guideline-recommended serum uric acid (sUA) target (≤6.0 mg/dL) in reducing chronic kidney disease (CKD) and cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used a Japanese claims database to determine whether achieving target sUA levels is associated with reduced adverse clinical outcomes. Individuals with baseline sUA ≥8.0 mg/dL were stratified into three groups based on status at follow-up (closest date to 365 days): ULT and sUA ≤6.0 mg/dL; ULT and sUA >6.0 mg/dL; non-ULT and sUA ≥8.0 mg/dL. We assessed annual estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope, 5-year risks of CKD, and cardiovascular composite events.

RESULTS: Among 143,244 individuals (mean age 44.6 years, 97.0% male), achieving target sUA (≤6.0 mg/dL) significantly reduced the risks of gout (adjusted hazard ratio 0.48; 95% confidence interval 0.40, 0.57) and type 2 diabetes (0.87; 0.76, 0.99) vs. the non-ULT group. Individuals not reaching target sUA despite ULT had higher risks of CKD (1.28; 1.08, 1.53) vs. the non-ULT group. Within the ULT cohort, reaching ≤6.0 mg/dL significantly lowered the risk of gout (0.59; 0.49, 0.71), CKD (0.70; 0.53, 0.94), and cardiovascular composite events (0.83; 0.70, 1.00) vs. having sUA >6.0 mg/dL. Annual eGFR slopes showed no significant intergroup differences.

CONCLUSION: Individuals with hyperuricemia achieving sUA ≤6.0 mg/dL had lower risks of CKD and cardiovascular events than those who did not. Reaching this target may provide significant clinical benefit beyond the management of gout symptoms, warranting verification in further studies.

articles.title: A capacitive field-effect sensor utilizing mbene embedded with aptamer-gold nanoparticles for label-free detection of tear TNF-α as a non-invasive diabetic retinopathy biomarker.
articles.abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR), recognized as a leading cause of irreversible blindness among adults, poses a severe threat to the visual health of over 500 million individuals with diabetes globally. Recent advancements in non-invasive biomarker detection have offered new avenues for the early diagnosis of DR. Among these biomarkers, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), a key pro-inflammatory cytokine, is regarded as an optimal biomarker for reflecting DR progression. In this study, we developed a novel composite nanomaterial, AuNPs@CrB, utilizing capacitive field-effect label-free nucleic acid detection technology. This material was employed, for the first time, to fabricate a capacitive field-effect sensor (CFS), achieving sensitive and rapid detection of TNF-α in tear fluid. The biosensor exhibited outstanding analytical performance, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 2.14 pM and a linear detection range spanning from 0.01 nM to 100 nM. Statistical analysis indicated that the biosensor possesses high specificity toward TNF-α and exhibits favorable detection performance in artificial tear samples, thereby meeting the concentration detection requirements pertinent to clinical diagnostics. Furthermore, the assay features a rapid detection time of less than one minute (with a total assay time of ~ 60 min), which significantly expedites the diagnostic turnaround process. This biosensor holds considerable potential as a novel, non-invasive tool for the early diagnosis of DR and establishes a technical foundation for the detection of additional tear-based biomarkers.

articles.title: Cognitive and neural outcomes of executive function training in healthy adults: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Cognitive training can strengthen executive functions, which are essential for adaptive behavior, yet evidence integrating cognitive and neural adaptations in healthy adults remains limited. This systematic review (PROSPERO: CRD420251107775), conducted according to PRISMA 2020, synthesized 26 publications examining executive function training and cognitive and neural outcomes in healthy adults. These comprised 24 randomized controlled trial publications and two quasi-experimental studies, representing 24 independent samples (N = 1,303; intervention = 667; control = 636). Cognitive improvements were most consistently reported for working memory and inhibitory control, although transfer varied across studies and several trials reported null findings. Neural evidence showed more consistent training-related changes in functional than structural measures, particularly involving electrophysiological dynamics and prefrontal or frontoparietal systems, whereas structural findings were more heterogeneous. Thirteen publications examined cognitive-neural associations across structural, functional, hemodynamic, metabolic, and electrophysiological measures; however, these relationships were heterogeneous and not consistently observed. Cognitive and neural changes were therefore not uniformly coupled, limiting mechanistic interpretations. Methodological constraints included small samples, short interventions, heterogeneous training and outcome measures, and limited availability of prespecified analysis plans. Overall, the evidence supports training-related cognitive and neural plasticity but indicates important limits to broad transfer and consistent brain-behavior convergence. Larger, longer, prospectively registered studies integrating cognitive and neural outcomes are needed to establish the durability, generalizability, and functional significance of these effects.

articles.title: Marginal Ulcer After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: Prevalence and Complications at Three-Month Endoscopic Evaluation in a Prospectively Followed Cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Marginal ulcer (MU) is a frequent complication of Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), with reported incidences ranging from 0.6% to 25%. It is associated with multiple risk factors, although the available evidence is heterogeneous. The aim of this study was to determine the three-month endoscopic prevalence, associated factors, and complications of MU in a contemporary cohort with protocolized endoscopic follow-up.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of a cohort of adult patients undergoing RYGB between 2022 and 2025 at a university hospital, managed with a protocolized postoperative follow-up program after preoperative evaluation by a multidisciplinary MBS team. Demographic variables, clinical risk factors, and complications were recorded. A protocolized postoperative follow-up regimen was implemented, including lansoprazole prophylaxis (30 mg/day, orally on an empty stomach) for three months. H. pylori status was assessed preoperatively by rapid urease test during preoperative endoscopy (performed in 100% of patients); all positive cases received eradication therapy prior to surgery and eradication was confirmed at the postoperative endoscopy. Postoperative analgesia included sublingual ketorolac for a maximum of three days, after which NSAIDs were discontinued. MU was confirmed by upper gastrointestinal endoscopy at the third postoperative month. All risk-factor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory; associations are reported as odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI).

RESULTS: One hundred and twenty-five patients were included, with a mean body mass index (BMI) of 41.3 kg/m² (Obesity III); 79% were female. Ninety-seven patients (78%) completed the protocolized endoscopic follow-up; 28 patients (22%) did not attend the scheduled evaluation. The three-month endoscopic prevalence of MU was 14.4% (14/97). Smoking was more frequent in patients with MU (28.6% vs. 7.2%; OR 5.13; 95% CI 1.23-21.4; p = 0.035), an exploratory association with a wide confidence interval. H. pylori infection (pre-eradication) showed no significant association with MU (OR 0.64; 95% CI 0.18-2.21; p = 0.561); the wide confidence interval precludes definitive conclusions. Complications during the follow-up of MU cases included anastomotic stricture (2/14, 14.3%) and upper gastrointestinal bleeding (1/14, 7.1%); no perforations, fistulas, or mortality were recorded.

CONCLUSION: Three-month endoscopic prevalence of MU was 14.4% in this RYGB cohort. Most lesions were asymptomatic, with symptoms arising exclusively in patients who developed complications. These findings are hypothesis-generating; prospective studies are needed to evaluate the impact of protocolized surveillance on patient outcomes.

articles.title: Zinc Protects Against Bisphenol F-Induced Renal Dysfunction via Modulation of XO/UA-Nrf2/NF-κB Signaling and Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bisphenol F (BPF), an emerging endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in renal toxicity through oxidative stress and inflammation. This study investigated the protective effects of zinc (Zn) against BPF-induced kidney damage, with emphasis on the xanthine oxidase/uric acid (XO/UA) axis, Nrf2/NF-κB signaling, and mitochondrial function.

METHODOLOGY: Male rats were assigned to control, BPF, Zn, and BPF + Zn groups. Renal function biomarkers, electrolyte balance, hematological indices, oxidative stress parameters, inflammatory mediators, and mitochondria function markers were evaluated alongside histopathological assessment.

RESULTS: BPF exposure significantly impaired renal function, evidenced by elevated creatinine, urea, lactate, and LDH, disrupted electrolyte homeostasis, and reduced erythropoietin, red blood cell count, and hemoglobin levels. These alterations were associated with increased XO/UA activity, suppressed Nrf2 signaling, enhanced NF-κB-mediated inflammation, and marked oxidative stress. Furthermore, BPF induced mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by reduced Bcl-2 expression, increased cytochrome c release, and activation of caspase - 3-mediated apoptosis, accompanied by decreased Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and Ca2⁺-ATPase activities. Notably, Zn supplementation attenuated these effects by restoring antioxidant defenses, suppressing inflammation, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and improving renal structure and function CONCLUSION: These findings highlight Zn as a potential therapeutic agent against BPF-induced nephrotoxicity via modulation of redox, inflammatory, and mitochondrial pathways.

articles.title: Observation of the efficacy of LED 830 nm near-infrared light combined with medication for erythematotelangiectatic rosacea.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of LED 830-nm near-infrared light combined with pharmacotherapy in the treatment of erythematotelangiectatic rosacea (ETR). Seventy-five patients were randomly assigned to the pharmacotherapy plus 830-nm LED phototherapy group, the pharmacotherapy plus 590-nm LED phototherapy group, or the pharmacotherapy-only group. All patients received oral hydroxychloroquine for 4 weeks and topical tacrolimus for 12 weeks. The two combination therapy groups received LED phototherapy at the designated wavelength twice weekly for 12 weeks. Improvements in facial erythema and the erythema efficacy index were compared before and after treatment. After 12 weeks of treatment, based on clinician assessment, the persistent erythema efficacy index and paroxysmal flushing efficacy index in the pharmacotherapy plus 830-nm LED phototherapy group were significantly higher than those in the pharmacotherapy plus 590-nm LED phototherapy group and the pharmacotherapy-only group (P < 0.05); the paroxysmal flushing efficacy index in the pharmacotherapy plus 590-nm LED phototherapy group was higher than that in the pharmacotherapy-only group (P < 0.05). For objective instrumental measurements, the pharmacotherapy plus 830-nm LED phototherapy group showed more marked reductions in RIR, PEA, and EI values than the pharmacotherapy plus 590-nm LED phototherapy group and the pharmacotherapy-only group (P < 0.05). Mild tanning occurred in 26.92% of patients in the pharmacotherapy plus 830-nm LED phototherapy group and 19.23% of patients in the pharmacotherapy-only group. LED 830-nm combined with pharmacotherapy showed significant advantages in improving both persistent erythema and paroxysmal flushing in ETR, with an onset of approximately 8 weeks, and was superior to 590-nm yellow light. LED 590-nm combined with pharmacotherapy showed better targeted efficacy in alleviating paroxysmal flushing. These findings suggest that phototherapy at different wavelengths has specific advantages in targeted intervention for symptoms across different pathological dimensions, providing robust evidence for individualized and precise combination therapy in clinical practice.

articles.title: NUCLEON: An Ontology of Chemical Elements and Nuclides for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Nuclear Medicine.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Radiopharmaceutical information in imaging systems is typically recorded as free text or as flat code system entries that include little or no computable information about radionuclides' physical properties. This article introduces the Nuclide and Element Ontology (NUCLEON), a machine-processable knowledge resource that represents the 118 known chemical elements and 5408 nuclides, including 2019 metastable isomers, with computable nuclear properties. The ontology declares each element and nuclide as both a class and an individual: the class structure generates a taxonomy that aligns with vocabularies of chemistry and clinical medicine, and the individual entities support quantitative assertions, such as half-life. Each of 7691 decay branches is an individual specifying its mode of decay and branching ratio; 7399 branches have an explicit link to their decay product (daughter) nuclide, derived from the decay mode rather than transcribed. Ground-state data were taken from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) LiveChart of Nuclides, isomer data from the NUBASE2020 evaluation, and the energies and yields of 3990 radiation emissions of clinically coded radionuclides and their decay chains from International Commission on Radiological Protection (ICRP) Publication 107; symbols and names were verified against standard chemical nomenclature. NUCLEON is linked to the Ontology of Chemical Elements, SNOMED Clinical Terms, and DICOM radiopharmaceutical isotope and PET radionuclide code sequences, allowing a nuclide to be resolved directly from a DICOM header. The ontology incorporates 215,862 triples across 5533 classes and 17,253 named individuals. Automated checks confirmed the arithmetic consistency of atomic, neutron, and mass numbers, and none of the derived decay products disagreed with ICRP Publication 107 or the Evaluated Nuclear Structure Data File. Element names are provided in seven languages. NUCLEON is available at https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/NUCLEON .

articles.title: Paediatric cutaneous leishmaniasis in Tunisia: clinico-epidemiological characteristics and Leishmania species identification.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Paediatric cutaneous leishmaniasis (PCL) remains a significant public health issue causing physical, psychological, and social burden worldwide. Despite the endemicity of this infection in Tunisia, PCL remains insufficiently characterized. In this context, the aim of our study was to assess the epidemiological characteristics and the clinical polymorphism of PCL and to identify the Leishmania (L.) species in the Tunisian setting. A cross-sectional study included 333 children with suspected CL and originated from endemic foci in Gafsa and Kairouan. Diagnosis was based on microscopic examination of stained tissue smears and 18 S rRNA conventional PCR for microscopy-negative samples. Clinical polymorphism was assessed among the laboratory-confirmed PCL cases, and Leishmania species was identified by PCR-RFLP of the ribosomal internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS 1) region. A total of 155 out of 333 children (46.5%) were confirmed positive including 144 cases detected by microscopy and 11 additional cases detected by PCR. Paediatric CL was significantly associated with age, with the highest proportion observed among children aged ≤ 6 years, as well as lesion location and duration. Nine clinical forms were identified. The ulcero-crusted form predominated (108/155, 69.68%), followed by ulcerated (17/155, 10.97%), papulonodular (12/155, 7.74%), and impetiginous (11/155, 7.1%) forms. Lupoid, necrotic, verrucous, sporotrichoid, and eczematous forms were uncommon. Among the 155 laboratory-confirmed PCL cases, Leishmania species was successfully identified in 120 cases (77.4%): L. major was identified in 114 of the 120 successfully typed cases (95.0%), L. infantum in 5/120 (4.16%), and L. killicki in 1/120 (0.83%). The ulcero-crusted form was the predominant presentation among infections due to L. major and L. infantum. Facial lesions appeared more frequent in L. infantum infections; however, the association between species and lesion location was not statistically significant (P = 0.165). Leishmania infantum infection was characterized by a predominance of the ulcero-crusted form (80%), followed by the ulcerated form (20%), whereas the single L. killicki case was ulcero-crusted.

CONCLUSION: Among the laboratory-confirmed PCL cases, L. major was the predominant species identified, accounting for 95.0% (114/120) of successfully typed cases. This species showed marked clinical polymorphism, although ulcero-crusted lesions were by far the most common presentation. Because atypical forms may mimic other dermatoses, a clinical assessment should be supported by parasitological and molecular confirmation whenever feasible.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • In the Tunisian setting, CL has a large clinical polymorphism among the general population. No data is available regarding the clinico-epidemiological features of CL among children.

WHAT IS NEW: • Among children clinically suspected of having CL, younger age, facial lesion location, and lesion duration of 1-3 months were associated with laboratory-confirmed CL. • Among confirmed cases, typical clinical forms predominated, particularly the ulcero-crusted form, while atypical presentations were uncommon but clinically relevant.

articles.title: Near-infrared transcranial photobiomodulation reduces cognitive deficits in rat model of Alzheimer's disease: the possible role of synaptic plasticity and neurotrophic factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, impaired synaptic function, and depletion of neurotrophic factors. Transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) has emerged as a potential non-invasive therapeutic option. We evaluated tPBM effects on cognition, hippocampal synaptic and neurotrophic proteins, long-term potentiation (LTP), and neuronal firing in an Aβ1-42-induced rat model of AD.

METHODS: Male Wistar rats were allocated to six groups: control, sham, AD, and AD+tPBM at 8, 16, or 32 J/cm². Animals received 810-nm pulsed-wave tPBM for 14 days after intracerebroventricular Aβ1-42 or vehicle injection. Behavioral outcomes used n = 8/group; electrophysiology, n = 6/group; and western blotting, n = 3/group. Outcomes included open-field, T-maze, and Barnes-maze performance, CA1 fEPSP/LTP, single-unit firing, and synaptic and neurotrophic protein expression.

RESULTS: Compared with AD, 8 J/cm² tPBM improved T-maze alternation (p = 0.0029) and Barnes-maze escape latency (p = 0.0376) and increased probe-trial target-quadrant time (p = 0.0432). Omnibus effects were large for alternation (partial η²=0.689) and target-quadrant time (partial η²=0.709). At 8 J/cm², PSD-95 (p = 0.0422), synaptophysin (p = 0.0055), Gap-43 (p = 0.0181), NGF (p = 0.0154), GDNF (p = 0.0014), and mean post-HFS fEPSP slope (p < 0.0001) increased versus AD; corresponding omnibus partial η² values were 0.715, 0.843, 0.774, 0.852, 0.874, and 0.613, respectively. Single-unit firing also increased versus AD (p = 0.0341; partial η²=0.437). The 16- and 32-J/cm² treatments were generally non-significant.

CONCLUSION: Under these conditions, 8 J/cm² was the most consistently effective tPBM fluence, attenuating Aβ-associated cognitive and synaptic deficits and enhancing hippocampal plasticity. These preclinical findings support further dose-optimized, adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Intraindividual comparison of [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET/CT for initial staging of breast cancer: Additional lesion detection and clinical impact.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET/CT for initial staging of breast cancer and assess the incremental clinical impact of FAPI findings.

METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 83 patients with newly diagnosed invasive breast cancer who underwent both examinations within 7 days before treatment. Patient- and lesion-level detection, paired SUVₘₐₓ, histology-specific FDG non-detection, stage migration, additional biopsy, treatment modification, and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated using a composite reference standard. Generalised estimating equations accounted for within-patient lesion clustering.

RESULTS: Patient-level positivity was 98.8% (82/83) for FAPI and 91.6% (76/83) for FDG (two-sided exact McNemar p = 0.031). FAPI detected 98.7% (235/238) of reference-positive lesions versus 67.2% (160/238) with FDG (p < 0.001); 76 lesions were FAPI-positive/FDG-negative and one was FDG-positive/FAPI-negative. Among 159 matched lesions, median SUVₘₐₓ was 12.10 for FAPI and 3.90 for FDG (p < 0.001). FDG non-detection was more frequent in invasive lobular carcinoma than in invasive ductal carcinoma/no special type (49.0% vs 30.1%; clustered odds ratio, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.004-4.54; p = 0.049). FAPI findings resulted in stage migration in 19.3%, additional biopsy in 18.1%, and treatment modification in 21.7% of patients. FAPI-only disease was not significantly associated with PFS (p = 0.343).

CONCLUSION: [68​Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT detected substantially more breast, nodal, and osseous lesions than [18F]FDG PET/CT and provided verified findings that altered staging and management. FAPI PET/CT may serve as a complementary initial-staging modality, particularly when FDG avidity is low; prospective multicentre validation is required.

articles.title: Single-sample-calibrated image-derived pharmacokinetics of the PD-L1-targeted tracer [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 using total-body PET: Beyond conventional venous blood sampling.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility and additional value of total-body PET image-derived pharmacokinetics over venous blood-sampling method in investigating non-tumor tissue and lesion kinetics of the PD-L1-targeted tracer [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 in patients with malignant tumors.

METHODS: Patients with solid tumors underwent a 60-min dynamic total-body PET acquisition following [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 injection, and a 20-min static scan at 120 min post-injection, accompanied by serial venous blood sampling. Systemic PK parameters were estimated via noncompartmental analysis based on time-concentration curves from venous blood sampling and image-derived venous vascular regions using a single-sample calibration, and the PK parameters obtained from the two methods were compared. To characterize kinetic parameters, time-activity curves (TACs) of non-tumor tissues and lung lesions were fitted using compartment models. Lesions' kinetic metrics and standardized uptake value (SUV) were compared after stratification by tumor proportion score (TPS; < 50% vs. ≥ 50%).

RESULTS: Image-derived maximum concentration (Cmax) was significantly higher and time to Cmax (Tmax) was significantly shorter than those obtained from venous blood sampling. No significant between-method differences were observed for the remaining PK parameters, except SVC-derived clearance (CL; 2.35 ± 0.69 vs. 2.69 ± 0.90 L/h, P = 0.016). The relative differences were within 18% for right atrium (RA) and within 19% for superior vena cava (SVC) for these parameters. Lesions with high TPS (≥ 50%) demonstrated significantly elevated K1 (0.51 ± 0.17 vs. 0.11 ± 0.09 mL/cm3/min, P = 0.009) and k2 (6.06 ± 1.76 vs. 2.19 ± 1.60 min-1, P = 0.009) compared to those with low TPS (< 50%). Additionally, dynamic [68​Ga]Ga-NOTA-SNA002 PET provided information on tracer retention in non-tumor tissues and lesions.

CONCLUSION: Total-body dynamic PET imaging with a single-sample calibration provides PK data comparable to conventional venous blood sampling while simultaneously characterizing tissue kinetic profiles throughout the body. Additionally, these kinetic parameters may offer complementary value for the stratification of lesion-level PD-L1 expression and the preliminary assessment of immunotherapy response.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This phase I clinical trial was approved by the National Medical Products Administration of China and was registered at www.chinadrugtrials.org.cn  (registry number: CTR20232251).

articles.title: Online self-management for men with uncomplicated LUTS: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of an online self-management intervention compared to usual care in men with uncomplicated LUTS over a six-month period.

METHODS: In this pragmatic, randomized controlled non-inferiority trial with online enrollment from the general population, participants were randomized (1:1) to either the online self-management intervention or usual care. Men with LUTS were recruited through social and other media. The primary outcome was the Patient Global Impression of Improvement after six months. Secondary outcomes included symptom severity (ICIQ-MLUTS), quality of life, healthcare utilization, medical consumption costs, and cost-effectiveness.

RESULTS: Due to a lower-than-anticipated inclusion rate, the trial was discontinued prematurely. Non-inferiority of the intervention could not be established. Nevertheless, more men in the intervention group reported improvement (difference 17.7%; 95% CI - 13.3% to 48.7%), and symptom severity decreased more in this group (mean difference - 1.63; 95% CI - 2.83 to - 0.42). Men in the control group used more formal care than those in the intervention group. Costs in the intervention group were lower (- €64.41; 95% CI - 155.76 to 13.17), with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of - €165 (95% CI - 717 to 70) and an incremental cost-utility ratio of - €1233 (95% CI - 35,149 to 40,198).

CONCLUSION: Non-inferiority of the intervention compared to usual care for the primary endpoint could not be demonstrated. However, the likelihood of the intervention resulting in markedly worse outcomes than usual care appears small. Cost-effectiveness results were more favorable for the intervention. Further research on the benefits and harms of the intervention is warranted.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT05356260, registered on 2022-04-08.

articles.title: Incidental joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake in oncological PET/CT: prevalence, distribution, and comparison with [¹⁸F]FDG.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize incidental joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake in oncological PET/CT, compare it with [¹⁸F]FDG, and define the prevalence and anatomical pattern of visually increased uptake.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 175 consecutive patients with solid tumors underwent [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74-PET/CT. Uptake was assessed in the acromioclavicular (AC), glenohumeral/subacromial (GH/SA), coxofemoral (CF), and sacroiliac (SI) regions. Dual-tracer [¹⁸F]FDG-PET/CT was available in 51 patients. SUVmax and target-to-background ratios (TBRs) were determined, and paired tracer comparisons were performed at the patient level.

RESULTS: Increased [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 shoulder uptake occurred in 83/175 patients (47.4%), most frequently involving the GH/SA (68/83, 81.9%) and AC (62/83, 74.7%) regions. CF and SI uptake was observed in 25.7% and 9.1%, respectively. In the dual-tracer cohort, shoulder [¹⁸F]FDG uptake occurred in 12/51 (23.5%) patients. Across evaluated joints, [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake exceeded [¹⁸F]FDG uptake (SUVmax: 6.5 ± 6.3 vs. 2.7 ± 1.5; TBR: 7.0 ± 5.9 vs. 4.6 ± 2.0; both p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSION: Joint and periarticular [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 uptake is a frequent incidental finding in oncological PET/CT, particularly in the shoulder region. The incomplete concordance between [¹⁸F]F-FAPI-74 and [¹⁸F]FDG uptake suggests potentially complementary but non-equivalent imaging information. Prospective multimodal studies are needed to clarify the underlying etiology and clinical relevance of incidental joint-associated FAPI uptake.

articles.title: Superabsorbent polymer bead ingestion in children: a systematic review of clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, treatment strategies, and factors associated with serious outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superabsorbent polymer (SAP) beads are expandable hydrogel products increasingly recognized as pediatric foreign bodies capable of causing intestinal obstruction. Although infants and young children represent most reported cases, factors associated with serious outcomes remain unclear. This systematic review evaluated clinical features, diagnostic challenges, treatment strategies, and factors associated with serious outcomes after pediatric SAP bead ingestion.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CNKI were searched from the earliest indexed records through March 2026. Pediatric case reports and case series describing SAP bead ingestion were included. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, imaging findings, anatomical involvement, interventions, and outcomes were extracted. Exploratory analyses assessed factors associated with serious outcomes.

RESULTS: The review included 58 reports describing 107 pediatric bead-related cases. The primary analysis comprised 62 known-age ingestion cases; 57/62 (91.9%) underwent at least one procedural intervention and 53/62 (85.5%) underwent surgery. Among the 62 cases, 49 (79.0%) involved children aged ≤ 18 months. Age ≤ 18 months was not associated with serious outcomes (OR 0.99, p = 1.000). Serious outcomes were associated with multiple-bead ingestion (OR 3.55, p = 0.044), multiple gastrointestinal-site involvement (OR 5.19, p = 0.007), duodenal involvement (OR 4.48, p = 0.022), and retained or missed beads documented during treatment (OR 299.67, p < 0.001). Imaging was performed in 50/62 (80.6%) cases; findings were discordant in 34/36 (94.4%) cases receiving multiple modalities. Ultrasonography had the highest positive-detection proportion (27/32, 84.4%), but an exploratory comparison did not show shorter time to intervention or fewer serious outcomes among children who underwent ultrasonography.

CONCLUSION: Published cases show that water-bead ingestion can cause intestinal obstruction requiring procedural treatment. In this selected case-report literature, young age alone was not associated with serious outcomes, whereas bead burden, anatomical extent, and retained or missed beads were associated with greater severity. These exploratory associations are vulnerable to selection bias, sparse data, and confounding and should not be interpreted as independent predictors.

articles.title: More threatening illness perceptions are associated with greater symptom burden in older adults with heart failure.
Revised Reference Intervals for Serum Free Light Chains: Implementation at the Mayo Clinic.
articles.journal: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Universal reference intervals (RIs) for serum free light chains (FLCs) were established in 2002 using nephelometric instrumentation and early-generation reagents. Since then, assay platforms have evolved, renal effects have been characterized, and lot-to-lot drift has been documented. Large population-based studies also proposed age- and kidney function-stratified RIs. We evaluated whether legacy RIs remain appropriate following transition to a turbidimetric platform with stabilized reagents and established updated RIs.

METHODS: Serum samples from 489 screened healthy adults were analyzed using the Optilite assay with stabilized κ calibrators. Samples with monoclonal proteins assayed by MASS-FIX, mass spectrometry-based monoclonal protein detection assay, were excluded. Central 99% RIs were derived using nonparametric methods. A secondary cohort of 106 individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) was analyzed to evaluate the effect of renal function. To assess clinical impact, 2025 clinical results, including >20 000 MASS-FIX-negative samples, were reclassified using legacy and revised RIs.
