RESULTS: The 2002 RIs were not verified in this contemporary cohort with 24.9% and 5.3% exceeding the historical upper limits for κFLC and κ/λ ratio, respectively. Newly established 99% RIs are 0.61 to 4.02 mg/dL for κ, 0.67 to 3.46 mg/dL for λ, and 0.57 to 2.45 for the κ/λ ratio. Lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was associated with increased FLC concentrations but smaller effects on the κ/λ ratio. Among MASS-FIX negative clinical samples, revised RIs reduced abnormal high flagging for κ/λ ratio from 17.6% to 4.1%.

CONCLUSIONS: Legacy FLC RIs do not verify due to assay updates. Nonparametric 99% RIs better reflect contemporary assay performance and substantially reduce clinically meaningful misclassification.

articles.title: Identifying candidate markers of infection progression and urinary tract deterioration in pediatric neurogenic bladder.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We performed a pilot study to evaluate whether candidate urinary biomarkers measured during routine clinical visits were associated with future urinary tract infections (UTIs) or urinary tract deterioration in children with neurogenic bladder.

METHODS: Urine was collected by catheterization from pediatric patients with neurogenic bladder at the time of routine urodynamics or kidney ultrasound in 2015-2016. Samples were separated into colonized and sterile groups based on urine culture and analyzed for antimicrobial peptides (BD-1, HIP/PAP, HD-5, LL37, NGAL) and the urothelial marker UPK3A by ELISA. Charts were reviewed up to September 2024 to determine infection progression (increased UTI frequency or UTI requiring hospitalization) or urinary tract deterioration (bladder medication changes, need for surgical intervention, progression on urodynamics or imaging).

RESULTS: A total of 86 patients were enrolled, 38 with sterile urine and 48 with colonized urine. Median follow-up time was 7.4 years (IQR 7.1-7.8 years). In the sterile cohort, elevated BD-1 was associated with subsequent infection progression (671.7 ng/mg vs. 298.2 ng/mg, p = 0.039) and urinary tract deterioration (397.2 ng/mg vs. 139.9 ng/mg, p = 0.004), while elevated UPK3A was associated with urinary tract deterioration (27.70 vs. 10.66 ng/mg, p = 0.015). No candidate biomarker in the colonized samples was associated with infection progression or urinary tract deterioration.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates the exploratory association of candidate urinary markers, specifically BD-1 and UPK3A, with infection progression and urinary tract deterioration in patients with neurogenic bladder.

articles.title: Reproductive History and Non-Incontinence Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Women: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the associations between reproductive history and non-incontinence lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) in women.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for observational studies examining parity, childbirth, delivery mode, or obstetric factors in relation to non-incontinence LUTS. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study designs, exposures, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Forty-five reports met the eligibility criteria. Several population-based studies associated parity or childbirth history with overactive bladder (OAB). Longitudinal studies suggested that multiple vaginal deliveries were associated with LUTS progression, while cesarean delivery was associated with a lower hazard of incident OAB than spontaneous vaginal delivery in one cohort. Associations between parity and individual symptoms, particularly urgency and urinary frequency, were inconsistent. Reports examining postpartum urinary retention and voiding dysfunction addressed delivery-related and obstetric factors, but heterogeneity in outcome definitions, assessment timing, and clinical settings limited comparisons. The evidence was predominantly observational, limiting causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: Reproductive history may be associated with selected non-incontinence LUTS outcomes, particularly OAB and LUTS progression. However, findings varied across symptom phenotypes and reproductive exposures. Postpartum urinary retention and voiding dysfunction should be considered separately from chronic LUTS. Further prospective studies using standardized definitions and appropriate confounder adjustment are needed.

articles.title: Bioprotective potential of Sargassum muticum extracts against Stemphylium vesicarium in tomato.
articles.abstract: Stemphylium vesicarium, the pathogen responsible for brown spot disease, poses a significant challenge to pear production and threatens a variety of crops, including onion, parsley, and sunflower. While synthetic fungicides remain the primary control method, their environmental risks, association with microbial resistance, and potential health effects underscore an urgent need for sustainable alternatives. This study explores the potential of Sargassum muticum (Yendo) Fensholt, an invasive seaweed, as a valuable source of bioactive compounds for the development of sustainable plant-protective products for controlling S. vesicarium infections. Native to East Asia and now widespread along European coastlines, S. muticum represents an abundant and underutilized biomass resource rich in minerals, phytohormones, and phenolic acids, including salicylic acid, which may contribute to the observed protective effect following extract application, making it a promising source for eco-friendly agricultural applications. The findings reported here, obtained through controlled infection assays with Solanum lycopersicum L., suggest that treatments with S. muticum extracts, particularly root irrigation and potential seed priming, may have beneficial effects on plant growth, potentially associated with milder disease symptoms. These results support the valorization of invasive seaweed biomass as a source of bio-based agricultural products and contribute to the development of environmentally friendly strategies for the sustainable management of S. vesicarium infections and other crop diseases.

articles.title: Cross-species transcriptomic integration and experimental evaluation of THC-responsive signature genes identified by consensus machine learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robust signature genes of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) exposure remain difficult to identify because gene expression responses vary across species, tissues, and experimental conditions.

OBJECTIVE: Here, we developed an integrative framework combining cross-species transcriptomics, consensus machine learning, and targeted experimental evaluation to identify recurrent THC responsive molecular signatures.

METHODS: A total of 21 public RNA-seq datasets comprising 201 samples from humans, macaques, and mice were analyzed using a standardized pipeline incorporating ortholog mapping, ComBat batch correction, and leave-one-dataset-out cross-validation. Consensus feature selection using Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Stability Selection identified 22 high-confidence candidate signature genes.

RESULTS: The ensemble classifier achieved an AUC of 0.719 and an average precision of 0.698. Functional enrichment analysis highlighted mitochondrial gene expression, mitochondrial translation, and endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein processing as major THC associated processes. RT-qPCR evaluation of eight representative candidates showed limited concordance for genes predicted to be downregulated. In contrast, upregulation-associated candidates showed substantially greater experimental concordance, with increased expression following THC treatment.

CONCLUSION: Overall, these results provide partial and direction-dependent experimental support for the prioritized candidates, with greater concordance observed among upregulation-associated genes.

articles.title: VSIG4 promotes renal cancer progression by inducing AKT-mediated epithelial-mesenchymal transition and is linked to an immunosuppressive immune microenvironment.
articles.abstract: The treatment options for metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (mccRCC) are limited, and treatment efficacy is poor. New treatment methods are urgently needed to improve the clinical outcomes of mccRCC patients. VSIG4 is an oncogene that is involved in the growth and migration of various tumours. However, the biological role of VSIG4 in renal cancer and the related mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the role of VSIG4 in the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer and the related molecular mechanisms. We used the CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE methods to calculate the proportion of infiltrating immune cells and the proportion of immune stroma in 551 clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. The R package "limma" was used to screen for differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Univariate Cox regression analysis and protein‒protein interaction (PPI) network analysis were employed to identify the core genes among the DEGs. Further analysis was conducted on the correlation between the expression of the core gene VSIG4 and immune cell infiltration as well as clinicopathological characteristics. The expression level of VSIG4 was measured using qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Lentiviral infection was used to downregulate VSIG4 expression in renal cancer cells. CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, scratch, and Transwell assays were performed to evaluate the biological function of VSIG4 in renal cancer cells. In vivo experiments in mice were carried out to explore the effects of VSIG4 inhibition on the proliferation and metastasis of renal cancer cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed that VSIG4 was highly expressed in ccRCC and that its expression level was positively correlated with tumour stage and grade. VSIG4 is a key molecule that promotes the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer. The results of patient sample verification indicated that the expression of VSIG4 in renal cancer tissues was significantly greater than that in adjacent normal tissues. Downregulation of VSIG4 inactivated the p-AKT signaling pathway, consequently impairing epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and associated migratory capacity. Moreover, it was closely related to the inhibition of PD-L1 and IL-10 and the activation of IL-2, IL-4, IFN-γ, and SHP-2 (PTPN11). VSIG4 is highly expressed in renal cancer tissues and promotes the invasion and metastasis of renal cancer cells. This effect is mediated, at least in part, through the AKT signaling pathway, which concurrently drives EMT, upregulates PD‑L1 and IL‑10, and downregulates IL‑2, IL‑4, IFN‑γ, and SHP‑2 (PTPN11).Our results collectively establish VSIG4 as a promising therapeutic target of renal cancer progression and validate its potential as a therapeutic target for ccRCC intervention.

articles.title: RCT of SBRT for oligometastatic NSCLC.
articles.abstract: We read with great interest the systematic review recently published in Clinical and Experimental Metastasis (Clin Exp Metastasis. 2026;43(6):62), which synthesized the evidence including two randomized controlled trials (RCTs).Given the central role of RCTs in establishing high-level evidence within evidence-based medicine, we write to highlight one omitted RCT as well as a recently published RCT relevant to this topic. We believe incorporating these studies complements the findings of the systematic review and provides readers with a more comprehensive overview of the current randomized evidence supporting stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) in oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

articles.title: MMC-DTA: A Multi-Modal Contrastive Learning-Based Drug-Target Affinity Prediction Model for Anti-Parasitic Drug Discovery.
articles.abstract: Parasitic diseases affect hundreds of millions of people globally, significantly contributing to high morbidity and mortality rates worldwide. However, existing drug therapies for parasitic diseases still face challenges such as drug resistance and severe side effects. Accurate prediction of drug-target affinity is vital for advancing anti-parasitic drug development. Although numerous computational methods have been proposed to explore topological and semantic information of biomolecules and integrate multi-modal data, most of them still face challenges in cross-modal information interaction, limiting their generalization capability for anti-parasitic drug discovery. To address these issues, we propose a multi-modal contrastive learning-based drug-target affinity prediction model (MMC-DTA). MMC-DTA employs a pre-training model-based multi-scale feature extraction strategy to learn the sequence and topology features of drugs and proteins, which effectively capture abundant features from the sequence and topological graph of drugs and proteins. Further, a multi-modal contrastive learning-based fusion strategy is specifically designed to effectively balance and integrate the information of the two modalities, and thereby enhance the representation of drug-target interactions. Experimental results on two public datasets and a newly collected dataset related to parasites demonstrate that MMC-DTA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in drug-target affinity prediction. Furthermore, the generalization capability of the model is validated in several realistic scenarios. Specifically, the proposed MMC-DTA demonstrates better generalization under a zero-shot scenario, and exhibits the promise to compensate for a lack of drug-parasite proteins binding affinity data for identifying anti-parasitic drugs.

articles.title: MKP-ECG: A Knowledge-Enhanced Dual-Stream Network for Robust Arrhythmia Classification with Medical Prior-Guided Multi-Loss Optimization.
articles.abstract: Accurate classification of cardiac arrhythmias from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for clinical decision-making, yet deep learning models often struggle with minority classes such as Fusion beats (F-type) owing to severe class imbalance and insufficient integration of domain knowledge. In this work, we propose Medical Knowledge Prior Network (MKP-ECG), a knowledge-enhanced dual-stream network for four-class arrhythmia classification (N, S, V, F) following the AAMI standard. The first stream employs a multi-scale CNN with residual connections and squeeze-and-excitation attention to learn data-driven representations from raw waveforms. The second stream, termed the Medical Prior Module, extracts a 34-dimensional clinical feature vector encoding morphology, rhythm, template matching, and rule-based indicators that mirror the reasoning process of cardiologists. The two streams are fused through explicit feature concatenation and a knowledge attention gate that dynamically modulates neural representations based on clinical evidence, and are jointly optimized by a composite loss function comprising two novel medical knowledge prior losses: a knowledge graph KL-divergence loss that aligns predictions with expert-defined electrophysiological priors and a clinical constraint loss that penalizes predictions contradicting established diagnostic criteria. Evaluated on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database under the inter-patient DS1/DS2 paradigm with methodologically corrected data augmentation (waveform-only SMOTE with nearest-neighbor clinical feature copying and purity-weighted contrastive loss), MKP-ECG achieves 99.14% accuracy, 92.77% Macro-F1, and 76.98% F-class F1-score with perfect F-recall, representing a 51.7% relative improvement over the knowledge-free baseline. Independent evaluation on the INCART database, where the model is trained and tested entirely within INCART using the same architecture and hyperparameters without any dataset-specific tuning, provides encouraging evidence of architectural generalizability under a record-split protocol, achieving 99.71% accuracy and 87.43% F-class F1-score.

articles.title: Complication rates and functional outcomes following endoscopic endonasal optic canal and orbital apex decompression procedures for non-traumatic optic neuropathy: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify functional outcomes and complication rates following endoscopic endonasal optic nerve decompression (EOND), a spectrum of related procedures, for non-traumatic optic neuropathy (NTON), and to identify sources of variability in the published evidence.

METHODS: Systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020. Five databases were searched to April 2025 for outcomes after endoscopic endonasal decompression of the optic canal, orbital apex or medial orbit. Proportions were pooled with a random-effects inverse-variance model on the logit scale (REML); sparse safety events with exact binomial intervals. Subgroups were defined by aetiology and surgical corridor. Risk of bias used an item-level Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence GRADE.

RESULTS: Seventeen studies (356 patients, 437 treated eyes or optic nerves) were eligible. Across 14 studies (364 analytic units), pooled improvement in visual acuity or optic nerve function was 78% (95% CI 65-87), with substantial heterogeneity (I² 78%) and a wide prediction interval (27-97%). Aetiology accounted for most of this: 95% (91-97) in dysthyroid optic neuropathy, 63% (46-77) in raised intracranial pressure and 59% (40-76) in neoplastic or compressive disease (p < 0.001), I² 0-42% within strata. Among 6 studies (135 units) with formal perimetry, visual field improvement was 77% (69-84; I² 0%). New-onset diplopia was bimodal: 25% (11-45) where orbital fat was removed versus 6% (2-14) where it was not (p = 0.016). Severe complications occurred in 5 of 311 patients (1.6%, 0.5-3.7).

CONCLUSIONS: EOND for NTON achieves visual improvement in most treated eyes with a low rate of severe morbidity, but the pooled estimate is not a single expected value: aetiology, not technique alone, dominates benefit, and diplopia risk is driven by orbital fat removal. Certainty is very low by GRADE for all endpoints except visual field improvement, which is low. Aetiology-specific reporting and standardised outcome definitions are needed.

articles.title: Comparative performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT versus contrast-enhanced CT for predicting pCR to neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced gastric cancer.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare the performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT with that of contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) in predicting pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy (NAT) in locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC).

METHODS: This post-hoc analysis of a prospective trial finally enrolled 56 patients with LAGC who completed both ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT and CE-CT at baseline and post-NAT and subsequently underwent curative gastrectomy. Pre- and post-NAT PET parameters, including SUVmax, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), FAPI-avid tumor volume (FTV), and total lesion FAP expression (TLF), were measured, and their percentage changes were calculated. PET parameters were compared, and their predictive performance for pCR was benchmarked against that of RECIST 1.1 based on CE-CT.

RESULTS: Baseline FTV and TLF, as well as all post-treatment PET parameters (SUVmax, TBR, FTV, TLF) and their corresponding percentage changes parameters from baseline, were significantly lower in the pCR group than in the non-pCR group (all P < 0.05). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified all the above as significant predictors of pCR. Compared with CE-CT assessed by RECIST 1.1, post-treatment FTV (FTV-post) and post-treatment TLF (TLF-post) showed significantly higher areas under the curve (AUCs; P = 0.010 and P = 0.036, respectively). Among all predictors, TLF-post achieved the highest discriminative ability (AUC, 0.851), with a sensitivity of 88.89%, a specificity of 74.47%, and a negative predictive value of 97.22%. In contrast, RECIST 1.1 demonstrated perfect specificity (100%) but was limited by a markedly low sensitivity (11.11%).

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to systematically compare ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT with CE-CT for predicting pCR after NAT in LAGC. The superior predictive performance of ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI-04 PET parameters over RECIST 1.1 criteria supports its role as a valuable response assessment tool, with the potential to inform treatment adaptation-particularly by identifying patients with residual disease who may benefit from timely curative-intent surgery.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov. NCT05140746. Registered 8 November 2021 retrospectively.

articles.title: Surgical resection versus biopsy in primary central nervous system lymphoma: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is usually diagnosed by stereotactic biopsy followed by high-dose methotrexate-based therapy; however, the role of upfront resection in selected patients remains debated.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis was reported according to PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from January 2001 to June 2026 for comparative studies of upfront resection versus biopsy in newly diagnosed intracranial PCNSL. Hazard ratios (HRs) for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were pooled using random-effects models. The primary analysis was restricted to biopsy-only comparative studies, while broader non-biopsy comparator studies were assessed in exploratory sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I domains and certainty of evidence with GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine studies including 1,333 patients contributed to the OS analysis and five studies including 962 patients to the PFS analysis. Resection was associated with improved OS compared with biopsy (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.95; I2 = 52.7%), but the effect was attenuated after inclusion of recent anatomically restricted and propensity-matched cohorts. The PFS association was not statistically significant (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.55-1.18; I2 = 80.3%). Evidence certainty was low for OS and very low for PFS.

CONCLUSIONS: Upfront resection may be associated with improved OS in selected PCNSL patients, but the absence of robust PFS benefit and the high risk of selection bias argue against routine cytoreductive surgery. Biopsy remains the standard approach, with resection reserved for carefully selected cases.

articles.title: Graves' disease with thyroid storm: a truly grave disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Graves' disease can be exacerbated by thyroid storm. This endocrine emergency is a very rare condition in children and adolescents, with a mortality rate of approximately 10%-30%.

PATIENT AND METHODS: Here, we report on a 12-year-old girl with known Graves' disease who presented with pneumonia and thyroid storm (tachycardia, hyperpyrexia, hepatic failure, gastrointestinal manifestations [vomiting, diarrhea], and encephalopathy). She required immediate intensive care treatment including anti-thyroid medication, β‑blocker, and steroids as well as cooling and sedation. Twelve hours after admission, the patient developed cardiovascular collapse with asystole requiring immediate resuscitation. After intensive care treatment, the patient made a full neurological recovery within 1 week without any sequelae.

CONCLUSION: Considering its substantial mortality rate, it is essential to include thyroid storm within the differential diagnosis in critically ill children and adolescents with Graves' disease.

articles.title: Effects of Closed-Loop Emotion-Adaptive Multimodal Biofeedback on Resting Autonomic Regulation and Stress in Young Adults: An Exploratory Pilot Randomized Controlled Intervention Study.
articles.abstract: Young adulthood is a critical period during which chronic stress and autonomic dysregulation are common and are associated with adverse psychological and cardiovascular outcomes. Conventional biofeedback systems often use fixed respiratory pacing, frequently at 6 breaths/min (0.10 Hz), even though cardiovascular resonance frequency varies among individuals. This exploratory pilot randomized controlled intervention study compared a closed-loop, individualized resonance-oriented multimodal biofeedback intervention with fixed 0.10-Hz paced breathing in young adults with elevated perceived stress. The adaptive system integrated multimodal physiological sensing with a previously validated facial emotion recognition module and progressively adjusted respiratory guidance toward a participant-specific rate associated with maximal heart rate variability (HRV) amplitude. Both groups completed 20-minute sessions three times weekly for four weeks. This single-blind, randomized controlled pilot trial enrolled 30 participants (18-30 years), who were randomly assigned to either an adaptive biofeedback group (n = 15) or a fixed-rate paced breathing control group (n = 15). Participants completed a structured 4-week intervention protocol. Physiological and psychometric assessments were performed at baseline and after the intervention, including heart rate variability (HRV) indices (RMSSD and SDNN), respiratory sinus arrhythmia (RSA), electrodermal activity (EDA), and Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) scores. Intervention effects were evaluated using repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) and effect size analysis. The adaptive biofeedback group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in resting autonomic physiological measures than the control group following the four-week intervention, as assessed during standardized resting recordings performed before and after the intervention period. Adaptive biofeedback increased RMSSD by 38% (p < 0.001, d = 0.85) and SDNN by 42% (p < 0.001, d = 1.25), indicating enhanced parasympathetic modulation and autonomic flexibility. A significant Group × Time interaction was observed for RSA (p < 0.001). Electrodermal activity decreased significantly, indicating reduced sympathetic arousal, while PSS-10 scores also declined significantly, reflecting lower perceived stress following the intervention. Adaptive biofeedback was associated with greater improvements in resting cardiorespiratory synchronization, autonomic coherence, and physiological stability following the intervention period. The individualized resonance-oriented closed-loop intervention was associated with greater improvements in resting autonomic measures than fixed 0.10-Hz paced breathing after four weeks. Because the intervention combined individualized resonance-oriented pacing, closed-loop adjustment, multimodal monitoring, and affective-context input, the present design cannot determine the independent contribution of each component. The findings should therefore be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating.Clinical Trial Registration CTRI/2026/04/107,535.

articles.title: Association of coronary 68Ga-DOTATATE uptake with CCTA-derived plaque burden in patients without prior cardiovascular events.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: 68Ga-DOTATATE is a positron emission tomography (PET) radiotracer with affinity for somatostatin receptor 2 on pro-inflammatory macrophages. While specific plaque features are linked to inflammatory activity and risk of rupture, the association between plaque composition and functional inflammation remains to be investigated. We aimed to investigate whether 68Ga-DOTATATE can detect plaques features associated with inflammation in asymptomatic patients, and its association with atherosclerotic plaque features.

METHODS: Forty participants without prior cardiovascular events with either no significant coronary artery disease (CAD) or extensive CAD underwent 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), and were matched 1:1 by age and sex. Coronary tracer uptake was quantified using the maximum target-to-background ratio (TBRmax), calculated by dividing coronary uptake by blood pool activity in the superior vena cava. Associations between plaque features and TBRmax were assessed on a ​per-patient and a per-​plaque level.

RESULTS: Mean age was 65 years, 85% were male. On a patient level, higher percent atheroma volume and calcified plaque volume were associated with higher TBRmax. On a plaque level, higher non-calcified and low-density plaque volumes were associated with higher TBRmax (p = 0.020 and p < 0.001), whereas, in contrast to the patient level analyses, calcified plaque volume was associated with a lower TBRmax (p = 0.019). High-risk plaques were associated with higher TBRmax (p = 0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: Coronary ⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE uptake is strongly associated with high-risk plaque features on CCTA on a plaque level. These findings support the potential of ⁶⁸Ga-DOTATATE PET and CCTA-derived parameters for identifying high-risk plaques associated with inflammation in asymptomatic patients.

articles.title: Robotic versus laparoscopic cholecystectomy and the risk of perioperative bile duct injury: a statewide inpatient analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bile duct injury (BDI) remains a rare but serious complication of cholecystectomy. Whether robotic cholecystectomy (RC) influences BDI risk compared with laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC), independent of intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) use and patient characteristics, remains incompletely defined.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective population-based analysis of adult inpatient cholecystectomy admissions in the Texas Inpatient Public Use Data File (2024). Cholecystectomy approach was classified as robotic or laparoscopic based on ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. IOC was identified using the ICD-10-PCS biliary fluoroscopy code BF11YZZ. BDI was identified using ICD-10-CM codes for direct or postprocedural BDI excluding diagnoses present on admission. Patient characteristics, comorbidities, and preoperative diagnoses were assessed descriptively. Given the rarity of events, adjusted analyses were conducted using penalized logistic regression with bootstrap confidence intervals. A secondary descriptive analysis was performed using the Texas Outpatient Public Use Data File to characterize outpatient cholecystectomy volume, IOC utilization, and index-encounter BDI incidence.

RESULTS: A total of 32,740 inpatient cholecystectomies were identified, including 21,669 laparoscopic (66.2%) and 11,071 robotic (33.8%) procedures. IOC was performed more frequently during laparoscopic cases than robotic cases (32.2% vs 12.6%). Overall, 20 BDIs occurred (0.06%). Unadjusted BDI rates were higher after LC than after RC(0.79 vs 0.27 per 1,000 cases). After adjustment for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, and preoperative diagnosis, RC was associated with lower odds of BDI compared with LC (adjusted odds ratio 0.47; 95% CI, 0.13-1.00). IOC use was not independently associated with reduced BDI risk.

CONCLUSIONS: In this statewide inpatient analysis, robotic cholecystectomy was associated with lower odds of bile duct injury recognized during the index hospitalization. This exploratory finding should not be interpreted as evidence that the robotic approach reduces overall BDI risk because injuries diagnosed after discharge were not captured, only 20 events occurred, and residual confounding and outcome misclassification remain possible.

articles.title: Comparative predictive value of modified CT-PCI and PET-PCI for surgical resectability and overall survival in pseudomyxoma peritonei.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate total and selected (regions 2 and 9-12) CT‑based and PET‑based Peritoneal Cancer Index (CT‑PCI and PET‑PCI) for predicting surgical resectability and overall survival (OS) in pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP).

METHODS: 54 patients were retrospectively enrolled. The predictive performance of total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI for surgical resectability was assessed using ROC curve analysis. OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, with comparisons stratified by CT-PCI, PET-PCI, and completeness of cytoreduction (CCR) scores. Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to identify independent prognostic factors.

RESULTS: CT-PCI demonstrated high predictive accuracy for resectability (total: 92.6%; selected: 90.7%), whereas PET-PCI showed moderate to high accuracy (total: 74.1%; selected: 88.8%). Patients with high total or selected CT-PCI or PET-PCI scores had worse OS than those with low scores (all log-rank P < 0.001). Significant OS differences were also observed between CCR subgroups: CCR 0-1 versus CCR 3 (P = 0.04), CCR 0-1 versus CCR 4 (P < 0.001), and CCR 2 versus CCR 4 (P = 0.011). Notably, OS didn't differ significantly between CCR 3 (incomplete cytoreduction) and CCR 4 (no surgery). Multivariate Cox regression identified both CT-PCI (HR = 5.589, P = 0.033) and PET-PCI (HR = 6.992, P = 0.007) as independent prognostic factors for OS.

CONCLUSION: Both total and selected CT-PCI and PET-PCI are useful for predicting resectability and OS in PMP patients. CT-PCI is more suitable for preoperative resectability assessment, whereas PET-PCI provides complementary prognostic information. Selected PCI (regions 2 and 9-12) showed predictive performance comparable to that of total PCI while requiring assessment of fewer regions.

articles.title: Development and temporal validation of a bedside score for acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia in emergency mesenteric CTA candidates: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and temporally validate a bedside risk score (BTCH-AOMI) based exclusively on pre-CTA clinical variables to predict acute occlusive mesenteric ischemia (AOMI) in emergency CTA-selected patients.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 285 adult patients (development cohort [2017-2022]: n = 187, 85 AOMI; temporal validation cohort [2023-2024]: n = 98, 42 AOMI). A 0-5-point score was constructed using four pre-CTA predictors: abdominal distension (1 point), AOMI risk conditions (1 point), peritonitis (2 points), and bedside inflammatory response (1 point). Score performance was evaluated and compared with an operationalized "pain-out-of-proportion" rule.

RESULTS: In temporal validation, the BTCH-AOMI score achieved moderate discrimination (AUC: 0.744, 95% CI: 0.651-0.834), significantly outperforming the pain-out-of-proportion rule (AUC: 0.521, 95% CI: 0.441-0.601; P = 0.002). Observed AOMI rates across validation strata (0-1, 2-3, and 4-5 points) were 25.0%, 45.5%, and 88.2%, respectively. A threshold of ≥ 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 71.4% and specificity of 64.3%; a threshold of ≥ 1 point yielded 95.2% sensitivity and 23.2% specificity.

CONCLUSIONS: The BTCH-AOMI score demonstrates moderate temporal discrimination and superior performance over traditional "pain-out-of-proportion" assessment. It is intended strictly as an adjunct for risk stratification and prioritization within emergency CTA pathways, not as a tool to exclude AOMI or replace CTA imaging.

articles.title: The prognostic value of sequential PSMA-PET/CT in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: a study of response assessment in patients receiving systemic therapy and cytoreductive prostatectomy.
articles.abstract: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) carries inferior prognosis. Although incorporating cytoreductive radical prostatectomy (cRP) into systemic therapy is safe, patient outcomes are variable. Prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA-PET/CT) demonstrates superior lesion detection compared to conventional imaging, yet its role in serial monitoring for mHSPC remains undefined. This study prospectively enrolled 48 men with PSMA-PET/CT-confirmed mHSPC to evaluate sequential imaging for response assessment and prognostication. Patients received six cycles of androgen deprivation therapy with novel hormonal agents ± docetaxel, followed by optional cRP. PSMA-PET/CT, multiparametric MRI, and PSA were obtained at baseline, post-systemic therapy, and six weeks after cRP. Blinded reviewers assessed imaging response using RECIST 1.1 and EAU/EANM criteria, while pathological response and biochemical status were independently evaluated. Following systemic therapy, both primary and metastatic lesion SUVmax decreased significantly (from 18.15 to 4.05 and 13.95 to 3.93, respectively; both P < 0.0001), while ADC values increased (0.725 to 0.955 × 10- 3 mm2/s; P < 0.0001). EAU/EANM response classifications (7 complete, 31 partial, 10 stable/progressive disease) correlated strongly with RECIST (Spearman's R = 0.79, P < 0.0001) but weakly with post-therapy PSA. Notably, PSMA identified residual disease missed by conventional imaging in nine discordant cases. Among 25 patients undergoing cRP, six (24%) achieved favorable pathological response, with significantly lower post-therapy primary SUVmax (2.400 vs. 4.800, P = 0.047). The average SUVmax of metastatic lesions after systemic therapy was a strong predictor of detectable PSA following cRP (OR = 1.640, 95%CI = 1.214-2.995, P = 0.019, AUC-ROC of 0.965). These findings underscore the value of sequential PSMA-PET/CT for monitoring therapeutic response and informing treatment decisions in mHSPC.

articles.title: [Physiotherapy in intensive care units in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland: tasks, developments, and challenges].
articles.abstract: Physiotherapy in intensive care units across the German-speaking region of Europe (Germany, Austria, and Switzerland-DACH) plays a central role in interprofessional early rehabilitation. Based on multimodal approaches and evidence-based assessments, it improves functional quality of life and reduces the incidence of post-intensive care syndrome. National and international guidelines establish early rehabilitation-ideally commencing within 72 h-as the standard of care. However, there is significant heterogeneity in physiotherapy training across these three countries. This article aims to outline the differences and similarities regarding education and the implementation of physiotherapeutic interventions in the intensive care setting.

articles.title: KOALA-FIT: Feasibility of an 8-Week Telehealth Exercise Intervention for Young Children Living with Congenital Heart Disease and Their Families.
articles.abstract: Reduced exercise capacity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Regular participation in physical activity from a young age may mitigate these effects. Despite childhood representing a critical period for establishing lifelong healthy behaviours, evidence for safe and effective exercise interventions in this age group are lacking. We evaluated the feasibility of KOALA-FIT, an 8-week family-based telehealth exercise intervention for young children living with moderate to complex CHD. A non-randomised pilot trial was conducted in children aged 5-10 years. Seventeen children from fifteen families completed baseline testing (children: mean age 7.3 ± 1.6 years; parents: mean age 40.9 ± 6.0 years). Physical activity was assessed by 7-day accelerometry in children and parents. Families participated in weekly telehealth exercise sessions delivered by an exercise physiologist, alongside home-based family activity challenges. Feasibility was evaluated across four domains (acceptability, practicality, implementation and preliminary efficacy), using quantitative and qualitative measures. Feasibility was defined as a score of > 80% in the combined feasibility questionnaires in > 50% of families. KOALA-FIT demonstrated high feasibility and acceptability, with 60% of families reporting overall feasibility scores above 80%. Program retention was high (15/17 children), with 80% of children and 60% of parents attending ≥ 75% of prescribed sessions. Children's weekday sedentary behaviour decreased following the intervention, although overall physical activity levels were unchanged. Qualitative analysis generated three themes; influences on child engagement, parental co-participation as a catalyst and logistics of telehealth. KOALA-FIT was a feasible and acceptable family-based telehealth intervention for young children with CHD who were successfully recruited. High retention, attendance, and engagement support the potential of this model to promote physical activity participation, warranting evaluation in a larger controlled trial.

articles.title: Use of the MemoSorb Bioresorbable PFO Device in an 11-Year-Old Diver with Phospholamban Mutation and Familial Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: We report biodegradable device implantation for primary prevention in an asymptomatic 11-year-old boy with a patent foramen ovale, normal biventricular function and phospholamban mutation, conferring an elevated future risk of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. He was a keen diver with ambitions to be a marine biologist. Following multidisciplinary discussion, closure of the defect was agreed using a bioresorbable device to optimize future transseptal intervention for potential cardiomyopathy. A 34 mm MemoSorb® PFO Occluder (Lepu medical Technology, Beijing, China) was positioned, complicated by complete atrioventricular block, regressing to first degree after removing the device. A 28 mm device was then successfully implanted. Intermittent 2nd degree atrioventricular block occurred post-procedurally but was successfully treated with steroids, with normal Holter ECG a few weeks later. Bubble test echocardiography was negative after 6 months. The patient was allowed to dive again. The MemoSorb ® biodegradable device can be implanted in selected cases. More studies are needed to confirm safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Climate Change and Congenital Heart Disease: Towards Climate-Informed Congenital Cardiology.
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common congenital anomaly and, as survival has improved, the priorities of congenital cardiology have expanded from anatomical correction and early survival to lifelong cardiovascular health, neurodevelopment, quality of life, and equitable access to care. Climate change introduces an additional and increasingly relevant dimension to this evolving landscape. Environmental exposures during pregnancy, including extreme heat and ambient air pollution, have been associated with selected congenital heart defects, although causal relationships remain uncertain. Across the life course, individuals with CHD may also be vulnerable to climate-related stressors through altered cardiovascular physiology, reduced physiological reserve, and dependence on specialised healthcare. At the same time, extreme weather and other climate-related disruptions may challenge the resilience of congenital cardiac services, while resource-intensive healthcare contributes to greenhouse-gas emissions. We propose climate-informed congenital cardiology, a specialty-specific, life-course framework that integrates four dimensions within congenital cardiac practice: environmental determinants of fetal cardiac development, potential climate-related vulnerability among people living with CHD, resilience of specialised congenital cardiac services, and the environmental sustainability of congenital cardiac care. Rather than positioning climate change as a new causal explanation for CHD, the framework conceptualises environmental change as a cross-cutting influence on disease development, lifelong health, healthcare delivery, and the environmental consequences of care. This integrated perspective provides an organising structure for research priorities, clinical adaptation, service planning, education, and policy.

articles.title: Fetal Ventricular Longitudinal Strain Does Not Predict Neonatal Hypoxemia in D-Transposition of the Great Arteries: A Prospective Multi-Center Study by the Fetal Heart Society Research Collaborative.
articles.abstract: Neonates with transposition of the great arteries (TGA) and intact ventricular septum (IVS) can develop life-threatening hypoxemia after birth. There are no known reliable fetal echocardiographic markers of postnatal hypoxemia. Using a large, multi-center prospectively recruited cohort, we analyzed fetal ventricular strain and its association with postnatal hypoxemia. Eighteen centers enrolled maternal-fetal dyads. Fetal ventricular longitudinal strain and strain rate measurements were obtained. The primary outcome measure was preoperative neonatal hypoxemia. The secondary outcome measure was reported need for balloon atrial septostomy (BAS). Intra- and inter-rater reliability was assessed. Fetal longitudinal strain was compared to normative data from a previously published study evaluating strain in fetuses without congenital heart disease. Longitudinal strain was performed on 79 fetuses with TGA/IVS. Of those, 29 (37%) developed postnatal hypoxemia. A BAS was performed in 45 (57%). There was no statistically significant difference in fetal longitudinal strain between those with postnatal hypoxemia and those without. Similarly, fetal longitudinal strain did not differ among those who received a BAS and those who did not. Among fetuses with TGA/IVS, while right and left ventricular longitudinal strain was similar, right ventricular free wall strain was significantly higher than left ventricular longitudinal strain. Compared to the previously published normative data, longitudinal strain for both ventricles were significantly higher in fetuses with TGA/IVS. This prospective multi-center study identified no association between fetal longitudinal strain and postnatal hypoxemia or need for BAS in neonates with TGA/IVS, highlighting the importance of delivery planning for all fetuses with TGA to include preparations for BAS.

articles.title: Prevalence, etiology, and trajectory of anemia in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Anemia is a common extraintestinal manifestation of pediatric inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet reported prevalences vary widely, partly because case definitions differ, and no pediatric pooled estimate exists. We aimed to quantify the prevalence, etiologic composition, severity, and 1-year trajectory of anemia in pediatric IBD under age/sex-specific criteria. We searched six databases from inception to 15 June 2026 for studies in patients under 18 years. The prespecified primary analysis estimated prevalence at diagnosis in representative cohorts using World Health Organization (WHO) age- and sex-specific hemoglobin thresholds; a comprehensive estimate combined all eligible cohorts regardless of definition. Proportions were pooled by random-effects generalized linear mixed models; heterogeneity was summarized by I2 and prediction intervals. Sixty-three cohorts (15,994 children) gave an overall prevalence of 61.7% (95% CI 56.4-66.7); in the 10 WHO-defined primary cohorts (2559 children), it was 60.8% (52.5-68.4, 95% prediction interval 31.9-83.6). Prevalence varied nearly 28 points on definition alone (40.5% with fixed cutoffs vs 68.9% with age-appropriate criteria). Among anemic children, iron deficiency predominated (78.0%; five cohorts, very low certainty). Prevalence was similar in Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, higher in active disease (74.8% vs 48.5%), and fell to 37.0% at 1 year.

CONCLUSION: These definition-standardized estimates quantify a burden guidelines recognize: averaged across heterogeneous settings, two-thirds of children anemic at diagnosis, mostly from iron deficiency, and more than a third at 1 year. Because the case definition, not setting, was a significant source of variation, age- and sex-specific thresholds are essential for screening, management, and comparable research.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261436312. Reported according to the PRISMA 2020 statement.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Anemia is a common extraintestinal manifestation of pediatric IBD, but reported prevalence ranges from about 40% to 80% and no pediatric-specific pooled estimate exists.

WHAT IS NEW: • This first pediatric-specific meta-analysis provides pooled, WHO age/sex-standardized reference estimates: in 63 cohorts (15,994 children), two-thirds were anemic at diagnosis and more than a third at 1 year. • The anemia case definition-not country income-was a significant, prespecified source of between-study variation; age- and sex-specific thresholds are essential for comparable estimates.

articles.title: Sonodynamic therapy for malignant brain tumors: a systematic review​ of preclinical and early clinical evidence.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma and other malignant brain tumors are difficult to treat due to the invasive behavior of the disease, resistance to conventional medicines, and the blood-brain barrier that limits delivery of therapeutics. This systematic review evaluates the potential of Sonodynamic Therapy (SDT), a non-invasive therapy that combines low-intensity ultrasound with tumor-selective sonosensitizers to produce fatal reactive oxygen species (ROS). A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Analysis of 36 qualifying studies suggested that SDT could induce tumor-specific apoptosis and necrosis with little injury to healthy brain tissue by generating reactive oxygen species (ROS) and ultrasonic cavitation. Various sonosensitizers, such as 5-aminolevulinic acid, Photofrin II, and novel nanosonosensitizers, can improve their tumor targeting and efficacy. Early-phase clinical trials, including phase 0/1, phase 1 and phase 1/2 trials, have demonstrated encouraging safety, feasibility, and preliminary biological and clinical activity in high-grade gliomas and juvenile brain tumors. Optimization of the ultrasonic parameters (frequency, intensity, pulse patterns) is critical for therapeutic outcomes. Moreover, novel combination approaches with chemotherapy, radiation, and immunotherapy may synergistically improve the anti-tumor advantages of SDT. To summarize, SDT is a novel and minimally invasive therapy that has the potential to significantly improve the outcomes of patients with malignant brain tumors by selectively targeting tumor cells. Although the clinical application is enabled by improvements in sonosensitizer design and ultrasound technology, some problems with standardization of protocols and optimization of delivery still exist. Larger clinical trials are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety and its integration with multimodal therapy may delineate future neuro-oncological treatment paradigms.

articles.title: Acute cardiac events and pneumonia are associated with the highest perioperative mortality after radical prostatectomy: analysis of reimbursement codes of > 400,000 in-hospital cases using German total population data from 2006 to 2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Our aim was to analyze the correlation between mortality and distinct postoperative complications and to assess the mortality depending on the postoperative course.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed the nationwide DRG-Database of the German Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) from 2006 to 2022 and included all cases of radical prostatectomy. Additionally, all possible codes for complications and comorbidities were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 446,636 cases of radical prostatectomy (RP) were analyzed. Overall, in-hospital mortality was stable at 0.13% (n = 577). The highest proportion of postoperative deaths on a single day occurred at the third day (n = 46), followed by the fifth (n = 34) and seventh day (n = 31). The overall rate of cases associated with potential complications was 30.4%. The highest rates were detected for codes associated with urinary tract complications (13.5%), followed by infections (11.6%), hemorrhage (11.3%), and other surgical complications (8.6%) (p < 0.05). The mortality rate (MR) for each complication category was highest for cases coded with cardiovascular (12.0%, Relative Risk (RR) 348.6) pneumonia (7.3%, RR 74.8) thromboembolic events (6.3%, RR 67.6) and cerebral complications (4.0%, RR 32.1) (p < 0.001). Single codes most highly associated with mortality were cardiac arrest (59.2%, RR 553.8), systemic thrombolysis (50.9%, RR 434.9) and severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) (47.3%, RR 378.4). Cases coded with acute hemodialysis were associated with an elevated risk of postoperative mortality (MR = 36.5%, RR 341.9). Chronic dialysis cases were more often coded with a higher MR than non-dialysis cases (MR = 4.33%, RR = 34.9).

CONCLUSION: A total of 30.4% of RP cases had at least one coded potential complication during the hospital stay. The most frequent codes for potential complications were codes associated with urinary tract-, infection-related, and hemorrhagic complications. Codes referring to potential cardiovascular and pulmonary complications were associated with the highest mortality risk. Codes for hemodialysis were also related to an increased risk of mortality.

articles.title: Antithrombotic Therapy in the First 24 Hours After Endovascular Stroke Treatment: Practice Patterns, Center Variation and Confounding in the ANGEL-ACT Registry.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To describe antithrombotic therapy in the first 24 h after endovascular treatment (EVT) and its determinants, and how far outcome comparisons depend on adjustment.

METHODS: Post hoc landmark analysis (24‑h assessment) of the prospective ANGEL-ACT registry (111 Chinese centers, 2017-2019) using mixed-effects logistic regression, sequential adjustment and quantitative bias analysis.

RESULTS: Of 1793 patients, 87 left hospital against medical advice within 24 h. Of the remaining 1706, 60.7% had antiplatelet therapy recorded by 24 h (mostly dual), 8.5% anticoagulants and 23.3% no antithrombotic agent; in atrial fibrillation, 3.4% received an oral anticoagulant and 31.7% no antithrombotic agent. Antiplatelet therapy was associated with stent placement (adjusted odds ratio 1.97, 95% CI 1.38-2.83) and inversely with symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH; 0.45, 0.28-0.72), intraprocedural complications and atrial fibrillation; the between-center median odds ratio was 2.65 (2.16-3.44). For 90-day death, standardized risk ratios were 0.60 (0.44-0.82) without and 0.69 (0.54-0.91) with adjustment for 24‑h NIHSS and sICH (E-values 2.70 and 2.26). If unmeasured, sICH could have biased the risk ratio by up to 1.52-fold, enough to explain the fully adjusted estimate (bias factor needed 1.45) but not the less adjusted one (1.66).

CONCLUSION: Antithrombotic therapy within 24 h after EVT was associated with stenting, bleeding and atrial fibrillation and varied between centers beyond measured case mix. Its association with lower mortality is likely to remain partly confounded, as confounding as strong as that observed for measured factors could account for most or all of it, and should not be read as a treatment effect.

articles.title: Whole-body metabolic network alterations and their association with cognitive performance in type 2 diabetes: an 18F-FDG PET/MR study.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) disrupts multi-organ glucose metabolism, but systemic inter-organ metabolic coordination and its relevance to cognition remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to construct whole-body metabolic covariance networks using whole-body 18F-FDG PET/MR and explore their associations with cognitive performance in T2DM.

METHODS: Twenty-nine patients with T2DM and 46 healthy controls were enrolled. Mean standardized uptake value normalized to lean body mass (SULmean) were extracted from nine cerebral subregions and nine peripheral tissue compartments to calculate whole-body metabolic covariance. These 18 regions were then aggregated into nine major nodes to construct the metabolic connectivity network. Two brain-peripheral decoupling scores were derived from Z-residual covariance features. Correlation and mediation analyses assessed associations between brain-peripheral decoupling and cognition, while four predictive models were compared for classification performance.

RESULTS: Although intra-brain metabolic correlations were numerically higher in T2DM patients than in controls across 32 of 36 region pairs, these differences did not survive FDR correction (all q > 0.05). Similarly, brain-peripheral couplings showed only nominal differences between groups and were not FDR-significant (q > 0.05). Network topology analysis indicated different descriptive hub configurations (spleen and pancreas in controls vs. subcutaneous (SAT) and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) in T2DM). Across all participants, the signed decoupling score showed a modest inverse association with MoCA scores in the pooled cohort (r = - 0.31, P = 0.007) that did not reach significance within either subgroup (T2DM: r = - 0.14, P = 0.445). Mediation analysis provided no statistical evidence that brain-peripheral decoupling mediates the association between T2DM status and cognitive outcomes. The multimodal ElasticNet model achieved the highest classification performance (AUC = 0.726, 95% CI 0.602-0.840).

CONCLUSIONS: Whole-body metabolic network analysis may provide complementary systems-level information for characterizing T2DM-related metabolic dysregulation and cognitive vulnerability.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for alcohol use disorder: mechanisms, clinical evidence and testable predictions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing condition characterized by disturbances in reward processing, stress responses, immune signaling, and metabolic regulation. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), originally developed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, have attracted attention as candidate treatments for AUD because they act on several of these interconnected pathways.

OBJECTIVES: This narrative review examines the neurobiological pathways shared by ethanol exposure and GLP-1 signaling, appraises preclinical and clinical evidence while distinguishing demonstrated effects from untested mechanisms, and derives testable predictions from a state-dependent translational model.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for literature published up to 15 July 2026 using terms related to GLP-1 receptor agonists, alcohol, reward circuitry, inflammation, metabolism, craving, and relapse; one randomized trial published after the search date was added during revision. Experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, observational investigations, and systematic reviews were synthesized narratively, and each finding was assigned a predefined evidence status (Established, Indirect, or Hypothesis).

RESULTS: In rodent and non-human primate models, the GLP-1 receptor agonists exendin-4, liraglutide, exenatide, and semaglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide reduce alcohol consumption and relapse-like behavior and attenuate alcohol-evoked mesolimbic dopamine release, although most mechanistic experiments used male animals. Anti-inflammatory and metabolic actions have been shown mainly in non-alcohol models, and a post hoc biomarker analysis of an exenatide trial was null. In randomized trials, once-weekly exenatide did not reduce heavy-drinking days (primary endpoint) over 26 weeks. Injectable semaglutide reduced laboratory alcohol self-administration in a 9-week trial in non-treatment-seeking adults and, in a 26-week trial in treatment-seeking adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe AUD, reduced the percentage of heavy-drinking days more than placebo (between-group difference - 13.7 percentage points). In an 8-week trial in treatment-seeking adults, oral semaglutide did not reduce laboratory cue-elicited craving (primary endpoint) or drinks per day but reduced heavy-drinking days. Observational studies associate GLP-1RA exposure with lower rates of AUD-related outcomes, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.

CONCLUSIONS: Preclinical evidence that GLP-1RAs reduce alcohol intake is consistent, whereas randomized evidence for semaglutide is emerging but limited to three phase 2 trials with 48-108 participants. Whether reward, inflammatory, or metabolic pathways mediate reduced drinking in humans has not been demonstrated; inflammatory and metabolic mediation, in particular, remains a hypothesis. The proposed state-dependent model yields testable predictions-reward-related change preceding weight loss, larger effects on drinking intensity than on drinking frequency, and a prespecified treatment-by-metabolic-phenotype interaction-that adequately powered multicenter trials with formal mediation analyses can confirm or refute.

articles.title: Obesity in COPD: Pathophysiological mechanisms, body phenotypes, clinical impact, and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This narrative review aimed to analyze the interaction between obesity and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). We hypothesized that obesity significantly modifies COPD pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, and prognosis, requiring an integrated management approach.

MAIN METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed, PubMed Central, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and the GOLD 2026 recommendations. Search terms included "COPD and obesity", "obesity paradox in COPD", "sarcopenia", "sarcopenic obesity", "BMI and COPD prognosis", "systemic inflammation", "metabolic syndrome", and "pulmonary rehabilitation". Relevant English-language publications, predominantly from the last 10 years, were selected based on scientific relevance.

RESULTS: Evidence indicates that obesity affects COPD through altered respiratory mechanics, increased ventilatory demand, chronic systemic inflammation, and its frequent coexistence with metabolic syndrome, diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular disease. Excess body weight increases dyspnea, reduces exercise tolerance, and worsens quality of life. Although several studies describe an obesity paradox, BMI alone inadequately reflects prognosis, emphasizing the importance of body composition assessment to identify sarcopenic obesity.

CONCLUSIONS: Obesity and COPD interact through complex pathophysiological mechanisms that influence disease severity and prognosis. Comprehensive assessment, including body composition evaluation, together with individualized interventions targeting weight management, muscle preservation, pulmonary rehabilitation, physical activity, and comorbidity control, may improve functional outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Fatal dengue cases in travellers from 1995 to 2025: A targeted review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries and territories, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported globally in 2024 alone. International travellers are at risk of infection when visiting endemic regions. While dengue in travellers is well described, dengue-related mortality in this population has not been comprehensively synthesised. We compiled and critically assessed available data on reports of fatal dengue cases among international travellers over a 30-year period.

METHODS: A targeted review was conducted to identify dengue-related fatalities in travellers from non-endemic countries acquiring infection in endemic regions between 1995 and November 2025. PubMed searches using terms related to dengue, mortality, and travel were complemented by hand-searching conference proceedings, national and international surveillance reports, publicly accessible national infectious disease databases, media reports, and anecdotal notifications. Cases were classified as confirmed or probable based on diagnostic method and/or inclusion in surveillance systems. Data were extracted, cross-referenced to avoid duplication, and analysed descriptively.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven fatal travel-related dengue cases were identified, of which 55 were classified as confirmed/probable and 12 cases had limited information. Of the 55 confirmed/probable cases, 22 reported both country of residence and acquisition, spanning 14 endemic destinations. Confirmed/probable fatal cases occurred among patients aged <1-79 years; 25.5% were female, 21.8% were male, and in 52.7% sex was not documented. Where infection status was available, most were primary infections (9/16). Reported fatal manifestations included neurological, cardiac, haemorrhagic, and hyperinflammatory complications. Diagnostic and reporting heterogeneity was substantial, and surveillance gaps were evident.

CONCLUSIONS: Dengue-related mortality among travellers is rare but likely under-recognised and underreported. Strengthened diagnostic capacity and heightened clinical awareness may support earlier recognition and management of severe cases in travellers, while harmonised international reporting systems could improve case ascertainment and contribute to future prevention strategies.

articles.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Agentic Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Infectious Disease Practice.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) discourse in infectious disease (ID) has focused on benchmarking large language model chatbots against clinicians, a useful but narrowing inquiry. Agentic AI is a different paradigm: goal-directed systems that pursue clinical objectives over time, integrating data, invoking tools, monitoring results, and adapting without repeated prompting. This Viewpoint defines the anatomy of an agent, situates it within a 3-level framework (predictive, conversational, agentic), and examines how agents could transform 6 domains of ID practice: clinical care, antimicrobial stewardship, clinical microbiology, infection prevention and control, research, and epidemiology and pandemic preparedness. Individual components have proven value; integrated systems remain untested. No validated agentic system has been deployed in clinical ID; error propagation, algorithmic bias, cost, absent validation frameworks, undefined liability, and consequences for the workforce and its training must be addressed first. The ID community has a narrow window to shape these systems before decisions are made without it.

articles.title: When Randomization Is Not an Option: Lessons in Causal Inference from Long-Term Real-World Evidence in XLH.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research

articles.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement Versus Medical Therapy for Severe Secondary Tricuspid Regurgitation: The TRIPLACE Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) carries a poor prognosis, yet comparative real-world data on transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) versus medical therapy remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes of TTVR versus medical therapy in patients with secondary TR.

METHODS: This observational study included the TRIPLACE registry (NCT06033274; TTVR cohort, N = 395, 24 centers, 2017-2025) and the Bronx-Valve Registry (NCT05453526; medical therapy cohort, N = 784, single center, 2017-2019). A 30-covariate propensity score was used for overlap weighting, targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (ATO). The primary endpoint was the 2-year composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure (HF) hospitalization.

RESULTS: TTVR achieved ≤ mild TR in 93.7% and ≤ moderate TR in 98.7%. In-hospital mortality was 0.8%. The most common 30-day adverse events were new permanent pacemaker implantation (14.8%) and severe bleeding (6.5%). Median follow-up was 363 days (Q1-Q3: 63-1,151 days). After ATO weighting, all covariates included in the propensity score model achieved exact mean balance (maximum standardized mean difference: 0.000). TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year primary endpoint (ATO-HR: 0.60 [95% CI: 0.40-0.89]; P = 0.012) and lower all-cause mortality (ATO-HR: 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38-0.99]; P = 0.044), whereas HF hospitalization did not differ significantly between groups (ATO-cause-specific HR: 0.69 [95% CI: 0.39-1.24]; P = 0.215).

CONCLUSIONS: In this observational comparison, TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year risk of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization compared with medical therapy in patients with secondary TR. These findings should be interpreted in the context of procedure-related risks and the nonrandomized study design.

REGISTRATION: (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment [TRIPLACE]; NCT06033274).

articles.title: Predictors of COVID-19 Hospitalization Costs in a Tertiary Hospital in Kuwait: Evidence From Real-World Data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: COVID-19 has imposed significant economic pressures on healthcare systems worldwide, with hospitalization costs constituting a major component. In Kuwait, previous estimates have reported average inpatient costs but lacked granularity on cost predictors across diverse patient subgroups. This study examined predictors of COVID-19 hospitalization costs and variations in costs across admission periods in 2021.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of all patients (N = 7569) admitted to Jaber Al-Ahmed Hospital, the national tertiary referral center for COVID-19 in Kuwait, in 2021. Patient-level hospitalization costs were derived using the microcosting approach reported previously elsewhere from the same cohort. Multivariable generalized linear models were used to estimate marginal cost differences, while accounting for demographic, clinical, and treatment-related characteristics. The month of admission and pandemic wave were included to assess differences in costs across admission periods in 2021.

RESULTS: Intensive care unit admission and the use of remdesivir, corticosteroids, antibiotics, and immunosuppressants were associated with significantly higher costs. Patients with cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, or cancer also incurred higher costs. COVID-19 vaccination and hypertension were associated with lower costs. South Asian and Arab patients had lower estimated costs than Kuwaiti nationals. Costs declined by 24.7% over the year and by 8.6% across pandemic waves.

CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 hospitalization costs varied substantially by patient characteristics, treatment regimens, and over time. Cost differences suggest further investigation into potential differences in disease severity, treatment pathways, and healthcare access. These findings support the need for data-informed, and equitable healthcare planning.

articles.title: Household Food Insecurity and Suspected Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in U.S. Adolescents.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease in youth and is influenced by social and environmental conditions. Food insecurity is prevalent among US adolescents and may contribute to metabolic risk, but its relationship with MASLD during adolescence is not well defined.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of adolescents aged 12-19 years using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data. Household food security was categorized using a validated US Department of Agriculture survey. Suspected MASLD was defined by elevated sex-specific alanine aminotransferase with at least one cardiometabolic risk factor. Survey-weighted logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, and race and ethnicity were used to estimate associations.

RESULTS: The analytic sample included 7,098 adolescents (mean age 15.4 years), of whom 12.1% met criteria for suspected MASLD. The prevalence of suspected MASLD increased across worsening household food security categories (10.9% in food-secure to 15.8% in low or very low food security; p for trend <0.001). In adjusted analyses, low or very low household food security was associated with higher odds of suspected MASLD compared with food-secure status (odds ratio 1.44; 95% confidence interval 1.16-1.79).

DISCUSSION: Household food insecurity is associated with higher odds of suspected MASLD among US adolescents. Food insecurity may represent a clinically relevant marker of metabolic vulnerability during adolescence and help identify youth at increased risk for MASLD.

articles.title: High-Pressure Controlled-Dissection Coronary Intervention With the Drug-Coated Balloon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary dissection after drug-coated balloon (DCB) predicts late luminal gain, but it is frequently covered with a drug-eluting stent (DES) to avoid acute vessel closure. A "dissected artery that does not occlude" may be possible with controlled dissection using the double buddy-wire cutting technique.

CASE SUMMARY: Wire cutting followed by DCB infrequently results in striking dissections. Three such cases are presented: A long spiral dissection in the right coronary artery and 2 mid left anterior descending artery dissections. Follow-up coronary angiograms revealed healed, widened coronary arteries.

DISCUSSION: In the SELUTION DeNovo study, DCB + bailout DES is 66% more likely to fail than upfront DES-by the same operators. Wire cutting produces a longitudinal dissection, instead of a circumferential dissection, which can extend as a counterflow flap, the mode of acute vessel closure.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Lesion preparation consensus for DCB tolerates a 30% residual stenosis and advises bailout stenting for significant dissections. The double buddy-wire cutting technique with high-pressure balloon dilatations may overcome these limitations.

TRIALS: GRAND-DES (Grand Drug-Eluting Stent registry), REC-CAGEFREE I, SELUTION DeNovo.

articles.title: Simultaneous Mitral and Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac amyloidosis can be accompanied by combined atrioventricular regurgitation, yet same-session transcatheter treatment of both valves in this setting remains rarely reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old man with wild-type transthyretin amyloid-associated cardiomyopathy, permanent atrial fibrillation, and progressive heart failure under transthyretin amyloidosis-specific medication presented with severe symptomatic mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Same-session transcatheter edge-to-edge repair was successfully performed using 1 device at the mitral and 2 devices at the tricuspid valve. Mitral and tricuspid regurgitation were reduced from severe to mild-moderate and from torrential to moderate, with intraprocedural final mean gradients of 3 mm Hg and 1 mm Hg, respectively.

DISCUSSION: At 1 year, the patient was in New York Heart Association functional class I and II, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide had decreased from 2,550 to 726 pg/mL.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In selected patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis with severe symptomatic bivalvular regurgitation, combined transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at both atrioventricular valves may offer an effective treatment option.

articles.title: Salinity shapes within- and between-host infection dynamics of the oyster pathogen Vibrio aestuarianus.
articles.abstract: Environmental variability plays a central role in shaping infectious disease dynamics in marine ecosystems, yet the mechanistic basis of its effects on host-pathogen interactions remains largely unresolved. Recurrent adult mortalities of the Pacific oyster (Magallana gigas) are frequently associated with Vibrio aestuarianus subsp. francensis, but the environmental drivers of outbreak dynamics remain poorly understood. Using complementary approaches spanning national surveillance, field monitoring, controlled experiments, and separate bacterial and host transcriptomic analyses, we assessed distinct aspects of the relationship between salinity and disease dynamics. Twelve years of surveillance data showed that V. aestuarianus was more frequently detected at sites classified as variable-salinity environments, while lower salinity was associated with greater oyster mortality during field monitoring in the Thau Lagoon (France). Under controlled conditions, low salinity increased oyster mortality and enhanced transmission by promoting bacterial shedding, viability and relative dominance in seawater. Transcriptomic analyses showed that low salinity induces the expression of metabolic, stress-response, and virulence-associated genes in V. aestuarianus, while high salinity primarily triggers osmotic stress adaptation. Separate transcriptomic analyses revealed that oyster haemocytes exhibited a salinity-dependent shift. Low salinity is associated with metabolically intensive processes whereas higher salinity conditions are characterized by enrichment of immune-related signalling pathways during infection. Together, these complementary datasets support salinity as an important ecological regulator of V. aestuarianus disease dynamics and identify candidate physiological processes that may contribute to the observed phenotypes. Integrating salinity into disease risk assessment may improve prediction and management of oyster mortality under increasing hydrological variability in coastal environments.

articles.title: Urinary Metabolomic Signatures in Chronic Pancreatitis: A Discovery Phase Investigation of the PROCEED Study.
authors: Consortium for the Study of Chronic Pancreatitis, Diabetes, and Pancreatic Cancer (CPDPC)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is an inflammatory disease lacking diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers. Metabolomics has been previously reported by our research group to detect differences in urinary metabolites within a small group of subjects with pancreatitis. We screened urine samples collected from subjects with CP for metabolites that may serve as biomarkers. Here we perform a discovery, pilot study using an advanced platform to investigate urinary metabolite signatures in CP.

METHODS: Urine samples from control (n = 40) and definitive CP (n = 40) PROCEED subjects were analyzed by ALEX-CIS GC-TOF Mass Spectrometry. Each urine sample was analyzed across 328 metabolites:139 named and identified; 189 un-identified. Metabolite levels were normalized to sample median metabolite abundances for further analyses.

RESULTS: Direct comparison of urinary metabolite abundances identified 21 metabolites that were differentially expressed in CP versus control groups with 6 metabolites reduced and 15 enriched in urine samples. All 21 showed good discriminatory performance (AUC range; 0.77 - 0.83) with top classifiers (AUC > 0.8) including phenoxyacetic acid, mannose, glycerol-3-galactoside (G3G), xylulose, and ribonic acid (RA). Correlation and hierarchical clustering analysis identified two distinct metabolite clusters.
