Univariate and subgroup analyses further show several metabolites are also associated with CP-related clinical factors, such as diabetes and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction (EPD), supporting a urinary metabolic signature reflective of both disease status and relevant metabolic comorbid conditions.

CONCLUSION: These data support urinary metabolomic profiling as a promising noninvasive tool for pancreatic disease detection and characterization, providing justification for more comprehensive investigation.

articles.title: Practice patterns and unmet needs in pediatric eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases in the United States.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize pediatric eosinophilic gastrointestinal disease (EGID) care practices and unmet needs in the United States.

METHODS: A Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) survey was administered to attendees of the 2024 North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition single-topic symposium.

RESULTS: The response rate was 60% (203/339). Among US attending gastroenterologists (AGs), 72% reported seeing >5 eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) patients per month, whereas 68% saw ≤5 non-EoE EGID patients per year. Improved treatment options were the leading unmet need for EoE care. AGs' rates of dupilumab use for current EoE patients: <10% (29%), 10%-25% (41%), 26%-50% (18%), and 51%-100% (6%). One-food elimination diets were used in >25% of current patients by 53% of AGs. The proportions of AGs reporting swallowed topical corticosteroid use in >25% of current EoE patients were 61%, 44%, and 62% in academic, community, and private practices, respectively; corresponding proportions for proton pump inhibitors were 39%, 56%, and 31%. Reported use of unsedated transnasal esophagoscopy and endoluminal functional lumen imaging probe was higher in academic than in community or private practices (48% vs. 0% vs. 0%, p < 0.0001; 52% vs. 6% vs. 15%, p < 0.001). Esophageal string and sponge tests were rarely used by AGs' (string = 7%; sponge = 2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Practice variation and unmet needs persist in pediatric EGID care. Use of advanced monitoring technologies was greatest among academic AGs. Further research should identify barriers to implementation.

articles.title: Evaluating Pollution Prevention Effectiveness for Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences Methods.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada's National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993-2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001-2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

articles.title: Unveiling Whole Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological Metrics.
articles.abstract: Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10-8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.

articles.title: Electronic consultations in pediatric gastroenterology: An opportunity for innovative care.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition

articles.title: Impact of autoimmune liver disease on rejection risk and outcomes after liver transplantation: a comprehensive analysis.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract: Autoimmune liver disease (AILD), including autoimmune hepatitis, primary biliary cholangitis, and primary sclerosing cholangitis, is a common indication for liver transplantation (LT). AILD has been proposed to increase T cell-mediated rejection (TCMR) risk, though published data are conflicting. Importantly, prior studies did not account for tacrolimus trough levels, a major determinant of TCMR risk. We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of adult, transplant-naive, liver-only recipients maintained on tacrolimus-based immunosuppression between 2009 and 2022. TCMR and graft failure incidence were compared between AILD and non-AILD recipients using multivariable Cox models adjusted for median tacrolimus levels and relevant clinical variables. Separate Cox models for each covariate, adjusted for tacrolimus median, evaluated risk factors for chronic rejection (CR). Among 1101 LT recipients, 143 (13.0%) had AILD. Of the 298 recipients who developed at least one episode of TCMR, 18.8% had AILD. Multivariable sensitivity analysis demonstrated higher TCMR risk among AILD recipients (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.12-2.13, p=0.01). This increased TCMR risk was further quantified using robust effect size index and found to be -0.08 (i.e., negligible to small effect). Independent predictors of CR included prior TCMR (HR 4.94, 95% CI 2.05-11.90, p<0.001), CMV mismatch (donor-positive/recipient-negative; HR 2.54, 95% CI 1.17-5.52, p=0.02), and sex mismatch (HR 2.63, 95% CI 1.22-5.68, p=0.01), whereas AILD was not associated with CR. Notably, CR, rather than TCMR or AILD, was independently associated with inferior graft survival. In conclusion, AILD is independently associated with an increase in TCMR risk after LT; however, this effect is small and does not translate into inferior graft survival. In contrast, CR is independently associated with reduced graft survival. Prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

articles.title: Microalgae-Macrophage Hybrid Exosome-like Nanovesicles for Mitophagy Restoration and Wound Regeneration in Aging.
articles.abstract: The wound healing capacity in the elderly is significantly impaired, leading to increased susceptibility to inflammation and infection, and potentially contributing to reduced lifespan. In aged wounds, dysfunctional mitophagy in senescent cells (SnCs) results in the persistent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, fostering a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that further delays tissue repair. To address this challenge, we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with hybrid exosome-like nanovesicles to enhance wound healing in aging. These hybrid nanovesicles (termed SP-M2-ENs) were generated by extrusion-mediated fusion of spirulina-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (SP-ENs) with M2 macrophage-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (M2-ENs). SP-ENs are rich in phycocyanin and exhibit strong antioxidant activity, whereas M2-ENs carry multiple anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. This synergistic combination endows the hybrid system with enhanced anti-inflammatory and regenerative capabilities. To ensure sustained release and conformability to irregular wound topographies, the hybrid nanovesicles were encapsulated within a thermosensitive hydrogel (PF-127 gel), forming the final therapeutic construct, designated SP-M2-ENs@Gel. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that SP-M2-ENs@Gel effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), promotes tissue regeneration, stimulates angiogenesis, modulates macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, and enables prolonged delivery of therapeutic agents. Specifically, SP-M2-ENs@Gel accelerates healing in aged wounds by restoring mitophagy function in senescent cells, thereby alleviating chronic inflammation. Collectively, this platform represents a promising strategy for overcoming senescence-impaired wound repair, highlighting the clinical translatability of engineered exosome-based therapies in regenerative medicine.

articles.title: Quantifying Viscoelastic Alterations in Virus-Infected Cells by Optical Tweezers.
articles.abstract: The viscoelasticity of cells is closely related to their physiological functions, influencing processes such as differentiation, proliferation, and migration. Viruses replicate by infecting host cells and can affect the cells' viscoelastic properties. However, current research mainly focuses on changes in the overall cellular viscoelasticity, while intracellular viscoelastic properties remain difficult to measure. Optical tweezers, due to their noncontact nature, offer a promising tool for measuring intracellular viscoelasticity. In this study, the viscoelastic moduli of host cells infected with three different viruses (H9N2, PRV, and HSV) were measured using the active-passive calibration method and microrheological techniques. The changes in viscoelastic moduli across different frequency ranges were systematically analyzed. The results showed that viral infection altered the viscoelastic properties of cells, with the extent of changes varying by virus type. We conclude that viral infection leads to an increase in viscous modulus and a decrease in elastic modulus of the host cell, and this is attributed to virus-induced depolymerization of the cytoskeleton, which reduces cellular elasticity and increases viscosity. These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of virus-induced alterations in cellular viscoelasticity and offer a theoretical foundation for further studies on the cellular mechanisms of viral infections.

articles.title: Janus Biofuel Cells for Electrosynergistic Enhancement of Microenvironment-Adaptive Cascade Catalysis in Infected Diabetic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: The treatment of infectious diabetic wound is greatly hampered by hyperglycemia, inflammation, and microcirculatory dysfunction. Bioelectric stimulation and nanozyme catalysis provide a potential strategy for chronic wound repair but suffer from limitations including external electric power, low activity, and competitive multienzyme reactions. Given this, we developed microenvironment-responsive Janus GOx-Au@PCH-Pt nanoparticles (NPs) as biofuel cells, integrating cascade enzymatic catalysis and self-powered electrical stimulation. The biofuel cell features hydroxylated polyaniline (PCH) NPs as conductive bridges, Pt nanoclusters as the cathode, and glucose oxidase (GOx)-grafted Au (GOx-Au) as the anode. Under infection (acidic pH), conductive PCH shuttles electrons to generate microcurrent that accelerates enzyme catalysis on both the Au anode (GOx) and Pt cathode (peroxidase, POD). The enhanced GOx-POD cascade strengthens ·OH generation, and the self-powered electric field enhances ·OH diffusion across phospholipid bilayers, achieving significant bacterial killing and biofilm dispersion. During tissue repair, neutral/alkaline conditions switch Pt nanozyme from POD to catalase (CAT) and transform PCH into a benzoquinone structure as the electron acceptor. Reversed electron flow boosts the GOx-CAT cascade catalysis on the electrodes, accelerating glucose consumption, suppressing advanced glycation end product formation, and alleviating oxidative stress, while electrical stimulation reduces hypoxia-inducible factor-1α expressions. This synergistic effect promotes collagen deposition and orderly arrangement and normalizes microenvironment with oxygen-generating, hypoglycemic, anti-inflammatory, and macrophage phenotype-shifted features, thereby accelerating wound healing. This designed nanoscale biofuel cells realize adaptive microcurrent modulation and spatiotemporal cascade catalysis, offering a minimally invasive paradigm for infected diabetic wound therapy.

articles.title: Receptor-Modular Nanocaptors for Programmable Cytokine Sequestration.
articles.abstract: Pathological cytokine networks underlie inflammatory injury and tumor-associated immunosuppression, yet most cytokine-targeted therapies rely on molecularly fixed, pathway-specific antagonists. We present a receptor-modular nanomaterial strategy for constructing modular cytokine nanocaptors (MCNs) whose sequestration profiles can be reconfigured by exchanging receptor modules. Cytokine receptor ectodomains are engineered as independently producible serum albumin fusion proteins and coassembled with poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) into compositionally defined nanoparticles. This architecture decouples cytokine-binding specificity from nanoparticle structure, enabling high-density codisplay of multiple receptor modules on single particles. Representative MCNs simultaneously sequester IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ and suppress cytokine-driven inflammatory signaling more effectively than matched soluble receptor mixtures. By altering module composition while preserving the same assembly framework, MCNs can be redirected from sequestering pro-inflammatory cytokines in sepsis, acute lung injury, and fulminant hepatitis to depleting immunosuppressive mediators in tumors. These results establish receptor-modular nanocaptors as programmable materials for disease-tailored cytokine sequestration and immune-microenvironment reconfiguration.

articles.title: Decoupling Conductivity and Interfacial State in Pristine-Like Carbon Nanotube Coatings Reveals Their Distinct Contributions to Neuronal Function.
articles.abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) combine high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and nanoscale architecture, making them promising materials for neural interfaces. However, the strong coupling between CNT morphology, electrical transport, and surface chemistry has limited identification of the material properties that directly regulate neuronal function. Here, we establish an experimental strategy to disentangle morphology-dependent network transport from interfacial wettability using pristine-like CNT coatings. Multiwalled CNTs with comparable diameters but distinct lengths were reversibly functionalized, spray-coated, and thermally defunctionalized to produce homogeneous conductive networks while recovering pristine-like electrical transport and surface chemistry. Subsequent conditioning in phosphate-buffered saline substantially reduced surface hydrophobicity without detectable alteration of the graphitic CNT framework, generating coatings with comparable interfacial wettability but distinct network morphologies. Primary spinal cord neuron-glia cultures grown on these substrates were characterized by immunocytochemistry, electrophysiology, and calcium imaging. All CNT coatings supported comparable neuroglial density and network formation, whereas PBS-conditioned coatings, characterized by a more wettable interface, consistently exhibited enhanced spontaneous bursting and calcium activity compared with their untreated coatings. Across all conditions, neuronal network activity was more consistently associated with the initial interfacial state of CNT coatings, as experimentally reflected by their wetting behavior, than with CNT length or morphology-dependent electrical transport. These findings identify the initial CNT interfacial state, with wettability serving as an experimentally accessible descriptor, as a key design parameter for CNT-based neural interfaces. Furthermore, they suggest that the initial interfacial state may influence the subsequent evolution of the biomolecular layer at the cell-facing interface, thereby contributing to the modulation of neuronal function.

articles.title: Tunable Gaussian Random Number Generator from a Nanoscopic Domain-Wall-Based Spintronic Device.
articles.abstract: Existing hardware implementations of Gaussian random number generators (RNGs) rely on large arrays of binary devices, resulting in substantial hardware footprints or sampling-time overheads. Here, we present a racetrack memory-based random number generator (RTM-RNG) that directly generates analog Gaussian random number streams from a single domain-wall-based nanoscale racetrack. A geometrically engineered racetrack tip creates a localized current-density gradient, enabling field-free stochastic domain-wall nucleation driven by nanosecond current pulses. The domain-wall nucleation probability is continuously tunable via an electrically generated Oersted field or an external magnetic field, providing direct control over the mean of the output distribution. We demonstrate more than 256 distinguishable states from a single nanoscopic RTM-RNG device, thus making a Gaussian RNG with more than 8-bit resolution possible. Compared with conventional binary random bitstreams, the RTM-RNG achieves high-quality Gaussian distributions up to 83 times faster.

articles.title: An Optoelectronic SnP2S6 Memristive Neuron for Biologically Inspired Multimodal Neuromorphic Information Processing.
articles.abstract: Neuromorphic systems capable of integrating multiple sensory modalities offer a promising route toward energy-efficient information processing that more closely emulates biological neural networks. Here, we demonstrate a multifunctional ITO/SnP2S6/Ti memristive neuron that combines reproducible volatile resistive switching and integrate-and-fire dynamics under electrical-pulse stimulation with wavelength-selective photoresponses and short-term optoelectronic synaptic plasticity. Leveraging these experimentally measured device characteristics, we construct a multimodal neuromorphic recognition framework that integrates volatile memristive neurons with programmable memristive synapses. Inspired by the parallel processing of visual features in the primate visual system, structural and color information are independently encoded and processed through separate electrical and optical pathways before being integrated for classification. Importantly, inference is implemented using experimentally measured neuronal firing statistics and programmed synaptic conductance states, rather than idealized device models, thereby establishing a direct link between device characteristics and system-level functionality. As a proof-of-concept, the framework is evaluated on a fruit-recognition task using a subset of the Fruits-360 image data set, achieving a classification accuracy of 94.9% through multimodal fusion and substantially outperforming recognition based on either modality alone. These results establish SnP2S6 memristive devices as a versatile platform for integrating electrical and optical neuronal functionalities and highlight their potential for hardware-realistic multimodal in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

articles.title: Attempts to Understand and Manipulate the Orientation and Retention of Peptides Inside Nanopores Expand the Toolbox for Nanopore-Based Proteomics.
articles.abstract: Nanopore techniques have emerged as promising tools for deciphering complex proteomics from the single-molecule level by profiling individual peptides. The entry orientation of a peptide and its subsequent retention inside the nanopore are crucial for the analytical results but remain challenging to be properly defined, which limits the sensing capability of nanopore-based proteomics technology. Here, we propose that electrically driving peptide entry into α-hemolysin nanopores against opposing electroosmotic flows is a promising platform to guide the polypeptide with a preferential orientation. α-Hemolysin mutants with opposite ion selectivity have been engineered and employed to measure peptides at pH 3.8 and at alkaline pH exceeding 10.0. The impact of peptide charge distribution on the orientation has been investigated by simulating the peptide dipole moment and electrophysiology measurements. In addition, the retention position of the peptide has been altered by introducing tryptophan residues at position 125 within the β-barrel region of α-hemolysin, which increases the sensitivity for specific peptide region and enables the detection of initially inaccessible monomethylation modifications. Thus, we present a rational framework to investigate and manipulate the orientation and dwelling position of peptides inside the α-hemolysin nanopore, which can enhance our capability to profile polypeptides by using nanopore techniques.

articles.title: Recombinant Humanized Collagen V-Engineered Implant Interfaces Drive in situ Low-Thrombogenic Vascular Repair via Selective Bioadhesion.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular implants (e.g., vascular stents, occluders) face persistent challenges of thrombosis, immune activation, and delayed endothelial healing. Moreover, functional surfaces that can synergistically balance the demands of antithrombosis and pro-endothelialization remain suboptimal. Here, we develop a genetically engineered, recombinant humanized collagen V (rhCol V) that promotes vascular endothelial cell proliferation via the αvβ3-FAK pathway and induces smooth muscle contractile transition. Proteomics indicates reduced platelet adhesion via αIIbβ3 inhibition, thereby reducing thrombogenicity. In rabbit models, rhCol V-coated stents outperformed drug-eluting stents in long-term endothelial repair and remodeling, while suppressing acute thrombosis and immune activation. This engineered biomaterial has the potential to enhance the safety and efficacy of cardiovascular implantable devices.

articles.title: Combating the Bloodstream Infection Cascade: Sequential Therapeutic Nanomaterials for Pathogen Elimination, Immunomodulation, and Organ Protection.
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are life-threatening systemic syndromes with a high mortality rate, characterized by a highly sequential pathophysiological progression. Although early antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatments have improved short-term survival rates, single-stage interventions are insufficient to reverse the high risk of long-term mortality among survivors. To address the urgent clinical need for stage-specific interventions to improve patient outcomes, nanomaterials have emerged as a highly promising platform due to their design flexibility and intelligent microenvironmental responsiveness. This Review first outlines the pathophysiological characteristics of BSIs at each stage, from the initial pathogen invasion to the final multiple-organ dysfunction, which serves as the basis for the design of nanomaterials. Then, following the progression of BSIs, the representative nanotherapeutic strategies developed in recent years for different pathological stages are systematically categorized and discussed. Finally, the review discusses the challenges confronting nanomaterials in BSI management, such as the selection of optimal treatment timing and clinical translation, and provides future perspectives on design strategies and developmental directions for nanomaterials in BSI treatment.

articles.title: Acute Kidney Injury After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: An Early-Concentrated Mortality Burden.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a recognized complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but data based on the updated Valve Academic Research Consortium-3 (VARC-3) definition remain limited. We aimed to determine the incidence of VARC-3-defined AKI, identify factors associated with its development, and characterize its prognostic significance in patients undergoing TAVI.

METHOD: We retrospectively analyzed 106 consecutive patients who underwent TAVI at a single center and had paired baseline and early postprocedural creatinine measurements. AKI was defined and staged according to VARC-3 criteria. Factors associated with AKI were assessed using univariable logistic regression; survival was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and landmark analyses.

RESULTS: AKI developed in 16 of 106 patients (15.1%). Lower baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and higher procedural contrast volume were the only variables significantly associated with AKI in univariable analysis (both p=0.007). Patients with AKI had markedly reduced survival (log-rank p=0.012). Landmark analysis demonstrated that excess mortality was concentrated within the first six months (hazard ratio [HR] 13.23, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.30-52.96, p=0.0003), with no significant association thereafter.

CONCLUSION: VARC-3-defined AKI occurred in approximately one in seven TAVI patients and was associated with substantially impaired survival. The excess mortality associated with AKI was concentrated predominantly within the first six months; among patients with AKI who died, the majority of deaths were classified as cardiovascular. These findings characterize the temporal and cause-specific pattern of AKI-associated mortality and should be interpreted as observational associations rather than evidence of a causal effect of AKI.

articles.title: Uric Acid/HDL Cholesterol Ratio and the Non-Dipping Blood Pressure Phenotype in Primary Hypertension.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We examined whether nocturnal dipping status in primary hypertension varies according to the serum uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) and evaluated the ratio's ability to distinguish patients classified as non-dippers from those classified as dippers.

METHOD: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 260 consecutive patients with primary hypertension and a finalized 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) report. Dipping status was obtained from the finalized clinical report. The UHR was calculated as serum uric acid divided by high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). Its adjusted association with non-dipping was estimated using multivariable logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses in the 182 participants with retrievable detailed ABPM data additionally adjusted for 24-hour or nighttime mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to quantify apparent in-sample discrimination.

RESULTS: There were 132 dippers (50.8%) and 128 non-dippers (49.2%). Median UHR values were 0.111 [0.104-0.118] and 0.129 [0.123-0.141], respectively (P < 0.001). In the primary model, the odds ratio (OR) for a 0.01 increase in UHR was 2.922 (95% confidence interval [CI], 2.188-3.901; P < 0.001). In the 182 patients with detailed ABPM data, the association persisted after additional adjustment for 24-hour systolic and diastolic blood pressure (OR, 2.685; 95% CI, 1.911-3.773; P < 0.001) and, separately, for nighttime systolic and diastolic blood pressure (OR, 2.622; 95% CI, 1.512-4.548; P < 0.001). The apparent area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.855 (95% CI, 0.805-0.900); the exploratory threshold of 0.122 had a sensitivity of 78.9% and a specificity of 84.8%.

CONCLUSION: A higher UHR was associated with the non-dipping phenotype, including after adjustment for ambulatory blood pressure levels. These cross-sectional findings do not establish incremental clinical utility, and the observed discrimination and threshold require independent validation.

articles.title: A visible light-responsive silver-based antibacterial hydrogel for treating pressure ulcer wounds.
articles.abstract: As a common chronic wound disease in clinical settings, pressure ulcers (PUs) are skin growth abnormalities or defects caused by persistent pressure. Pressure sores are often difficult to treat effectively because wounds often contain bacteria, which can lead to contamination and infection. Silver phosphate (Ag3PO4) has become a very promising antibacterial agent due to its unique combination of ion-mediated toxicity and visible-light absorption properties. Here, a visible-light (vis)-responsive polyvinyl alcohol/polyacrylic acid/AgI/Ag3PO4 (PVA/PAA/IP) hydrogel with antibacterial properties was constructed. The results of colony counting and bacterial live/dead staining experiments showed that the visible-light-responsive PVA/PAA/IP hydrogel had a significant antibacterial effect on Staphylococcus aureus, and the antibacterial efficiency could reach 100% in 20 min. The ion-mediated toxicity of the hydrogel was proven by measuring the release of Ag+. The ability of the PVA/PAA/IP hydrogel to promote the healing of PU wounds under visible light was verified in the skin wounds of the mouse PU model. After 10 days of treatment, the PU wounds were basically cured. Visible-light irradiation can promote the release of Ag+ and the generation of heat in the hydrogel, thereby effectively removing bacteria from the wound surface, reducing the inflammatory response and promoting the healing of PU wounds.

articles.title: Recurrent Toxin-mediated Rash Due to Streptococcus dysgalactiae subsp. equisimilis: A Case Series of Five Adults.
Protothecosis: Clinicopathological Diagnosis of a Rare Human Dermatosis.
Evolving procedural volume and indications in pediatric endoscopic ultrasound: A single-center 10-year experience.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The adoption of endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) in pediatric gastroenterology has been limited by patient size and provider training; nevertheless, its utilization has been increasing. Understanding current trends in EUS indications and procedural volume, and the impact of pursuing formal training by pediatric endoscopists, is important for positioning this technology in pediatric gastroenterology practice.

METHODS: We reviewed all cases of EUS over a 10-year period at a freestanding children's hospital. We analyzed patient and procedural characteristics with descriptive statistics and examined changes in procedural volume and indications over time using negative binomial regression.

RESULTS: A total of 154 EUS procedures (118 diagnostic [76.6%] vs. 36 therapeutic [23.4%]) were performed in 142 unique patients (median age 13.9 years (interquartile range [IQR] 10.5, 17.5; weight range 12.7-189 kg). The most common procedural indications were evaluation of a mass (n = 56, 36.4%), assessment of abnormal pancreas imaging (n = 38, 24.7%), and drainage of peripancreatic fluid collections (n = 33, 21.4%). Procedural volume and number of indications per study year increased over the study period (p < 0.001 and p = 0.01, respectively), with a significant increase in volume (168%, p < 0.01) occurring after completion of formal EUS training by one of our faculty members.

CONCLUSIONS: Our single-center review suggests EUS is an increasingly utilized diagnostic and therapeutic modality with evolving pediatric indications. Access to at least one pediatric endoscopist with formal training in EUS may increase its local utilization. Multicenter studies would be helpful to shed further light on national trends in pediatric EUS and validate these findings more broadly.

articles.title: Gastrointestinal symptom assessment tools in infants and toddlers with disorders of gut-brain interaction.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBIs), formerly referred to as functional gastrointestinal disorders, are highly prevalent in infancy and early childhood and are primarily diagnosed and monitored through symptom-based assessment. In infants and toddlers, the evaluation of gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms relies almost exclusively on caregiver-reported outcome measures, making the availability of validated questionnaires essential for both clinical practice and research. This narrative review provides an overview of the main validated GI symptom questionnaires currently used to assess DGBIs-related symptoms in infants and toddlers. A literature search was conducted using major scientific databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Database, to identify studies employing validated questionnaires or symptom scales in this age group. The use of validated questionnaires allows for standardized symptom assessment, improves comparability across studies, and supports clinical decision-making and longitudinal monitoring. However, gaps remain regarding age specificity, symptom coverage, and cross-cultural validation. A clear understanding of the available tools and their appropriate use is essential to improve diagnostic accuracy, follow-up, and research quality in infants and toddlers with DGBIs.

articles.title: Effect of Creatine Supplementation on Nutritional Status in Patients on Maintenance Hemodialysis: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of creatine supplementation on nutritional status in adult patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing hemodialysis.

DESIGN AND METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library databases on July 31, 2025. This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). Eligibility was assessed by three independent reviewers and all included studies were at high or serious risk-of-bias.

RESULTS: From 65 articles identified, seven studies were included. The results revealed some inconsistencies mainly due to the heterogeneity between the studies in terms of creatine dosage, time of intervention and characteristics of the population. Some of the included studies showed significant changes in several body composition-related characteristics (lean body mass, fat-free mass, skeletal muscle mass index, skeletal muscle mass, body fat, total body water, phase angle), biochemical parameters (creatinine and urea), and physical performance (handgrip strength, gait speed, leg extension-1 repetition maximum, Short Physical Performance Battery). There were also improvements in Malnutrition Inflammation Score and quality of life. A negative correlation was found between baseline guanidinosuccinate and inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein, α1-acid glycoprotein).

CONCLUSION: Most of the included studies reported possible signals of benefit that require confirmation in adequately powered and low-bias trials.

articles.title: Pre-Transfer CTA and Futile Transfers in the Drip-and-Ship Model: Triage Precision, Workflow Trade-offs, and a Persistent Gray Zone.
articles.abstract: Background Patients not receiving endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) after interhospital transfer in a "drip-and-ship" stroke network place a burden on the system. The impact of pre-transfer computed tomography angiography (CTA) at the primary stroke center (PSC) on transfer outcomes and workflow efficiency has not been well characterized. Methods This retrospective study enrolled 314 acute ischemic stroke patients transferred for potential EVT within the Tainan-Chiayi Stroke Network (October 2021-September 2025). Patients were stratified by CTA timing: pre-transfer (n=66) versus post-transfer (n=248). Workflow time metrics were compared. Transfers not followed by EVT were classified into three categories: potentially avoidable, physiologically unavoidable, and gray zone. Results Among transferred patients, pre-transfer CTA was associated with a higher EVT treatment yield (72.7% vs. 33.9%; P<0.001), but a longer PSC door-in-door-out time (140 vs. 88 min; P<0.001). In multivariable analysis, post-transfer CTA remained the strongest independent predictor of not undergoing EVT (aOR 5.21; 95% CI 2.83-9.60). Among transfers not followed by EVT in the post-transfer CTA group, 40.2% were classified as potentially avoidable due to the absence of an actionable occlusion. Gray zone scenarios, driven primarily by large infarct cores, intracranial atherosclerotic disease and medium vessel occlusion, constituted the dominant remaining category in both groups. Conclusion Pre-transfer CTA was associated with a higher EVT treatment yield but a longer PSC processing time. The persistent gray zone requires strategies beyond imaging alone, and the trade-off between triage precision and transfer efficiency warrants ongoing evaluation across diverse stroke network settings.

articles.title: Global Research Trends and Current Landscape of Allergen Immunotherapy for Allergic Rhinitis and Asthma: A Comprehensive Bibliometric Analysis.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergen Immunotherapy (AIT) is the only therapeutic approach that can alter the progression of immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated allergic disorders. It plays a crucial role in promoting immune tolerance and effectively managing allergic rhinitis (AR), asthma and venom hypersensitivity.

METHODS: This study conducted a systematic bibliometric analysis of global research in the field of AIT. A total of 1,718 relevant articles published from 2000 to 2025 were extracted from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC; n = 1,718) and PubMed (n = 1,586), and in-depth analyses were performed using tools including CiteSpace, VOSviewer and Charticulator.

RESULTS: Annual publication volume has shown steady growth with significant acceleration since 2014. Additionally, the United States has dominated research output, European countries have formed a strong secondary cluster, and China has shown the fastest growth since 2017, while international collaborations formed a densely connected core with sparsely linked peripheral groups. Primary research focused on the management of AR and asthma, whereas studies of food allergy and atopic dermatitis contributed relatively little within an AR/asthma-anchored corpus. The comparative effectiveness of sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) and subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) has emerged as a key focus in highly cited literature. The temporal evolution of keywords demonstrated a shift from traditional allergen extracts to molecularly characterized allergens, component-resolved diagnosis, and personalized immunotherapy approaches.

CONCLUSION: This study comprehensively delineated the knowledge framework and translational challenges in global AIT research, specifically addressing issues in the translation of scientific achievements to clinical applications. Future research should focus on developing innovative delivery systems, optimizing treatment protocols, identifying predictive biomarkers, and conducting real-world evidence studies to effectively bridge the gap between scientific advancements and clinical implementation.

articles.title: Assessment of Sleep Quality and Psychological Distress on Stroke Incidence: A Prospective Cohort Study with Inflammatory and Metabolomic Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of sleep and psychological distress in stroke is increasingly recognized. However, the joint effects of the two were unclear. Thus, this study aims to investigate the impact of sleep and psychological distress.

METHODS: 366305 participants from the UK Biobank were included. Cox proportional hazard regression models were used to assess the longitudinal associations between sleep, psychological distress and all-cause stroke (AS). The multiplication and mediation analysis were also performed to evaluate the relationship between the two exposures. Finally, we conducted mediation analyses of 177 biomarkers between sleep, psychological stress and AS to reveal the inflammatory and metabolic mechanisms.

RESULTS: After 16-year follow-up, sleep score showed a linear inverse correlation with AS (hazard ration [HR] = 0.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.94-0.98, P <0.001), whereas psychological distress showed a nonlinear positive relationship with AS (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 1.05-1.09, P <0.001). The impacts of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke were similar to AS. There was no significant interaction between sleep and psychological stress in the risk of AS, but they were mutual mediating variables. We observed that C-creative protein and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, serving as shared mediating factors for sleep and psychological stress, may be involved in the occurrence of AS.

CONCLUSION: Poor sleep and high psychological stress are independent risk factors for stroke, and both can contribute to stroke risk by exacerbating inflammatory responses and affecting lipid metabolism.

articles.title: The Lung-Brain-Immune Axis: Mechanistic Pathways Linking Pulmonary Inflammation to Neuropsychiatric and Neurological Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic respiratory diseases and neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders contribute substantially to the global disease burden but have traditionally been studied as distinct organ-system disorders. Emerging evidence supports an integrated lung-brain-immune axis through which pulmonary inflammation can alter central nervous system (CNS) function and contribute to neurological and neuropsychiatric disease.

SUMMARY: This review synthesizes preclinical and clinical literature examining the anatomical, immunological, environmental, and clinical mechanisms linking pulmonary inflammation to CNS dysfunction. Evidence was synthesized across neural and immune communication pathways, inflammatory signaling, environmental and infectious triggers, disease-specific associations, lifespan susceptibility, and translational applications. Lung-brain communication is bidirectional and occurs through vagal and autonomic neural pathways, circulating inflammatory mediators including interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, immune-cell trafficking, and disruption of the alveolar-capillary and blood-brain barriers. These processes promote microglial priming, astrocyte reactivity, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction, providing a cellular basis for cognitive and affective symptoms. Air pollution, respiratory viruses, allergens, and tobacco smoke can activate these pathways, which are implicated in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, acute respiratory distress syndrome, long COVID, and interstitial lung disease. Susceptibility varies across the lifespan, from prenatal immune activation and adolescence to immunosenescence. Emerging biomarkers, anti-inflammatory and neuromodulatory therapies, and immune-phenotype-based stratification may enable more targeted interventions.

KEY MESSAGES: The lung-brain-immune axis provides a unifying biological framework in which pulmonary inflammation can act as a modifiable driver of neuroimmune dysfunction. Mechanistically validated causal models and longitudinal human studies are needed to clarify disease-specific pathways and translate these insights into clinical practice.

articles.title: Evaluation of right ventricular function in patients with severe and very severe mitral stenosis: insights from advanced echocardiographic techniques.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right Ventricular (RV) failure has a critical role in the onset and progression of clinical symptoms and the prognosis of patients with Mitral Stenosis (MS), but the exact role, effect, and pathophysiology of RV dysfunction in MS are still controversial. In this study, we aimed to evaluate echocardiographic signs of systolic RV dysfunction using Tissue Doppler Imaging (TDI) and Velocity Vector Imaging (VVI) in subjects with severe and very severe MS.

METHODS: 46 isolated MS cases (23 severe and 23 very severe) and 23 healthy controls were enrolled in this study. RV function was assessed by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), and peak systolic velocity of the tricuspid annulus (S') using TDI, and RV free wall strain (RVFWS) employing VVI. Furthermore, these values correlations with mitral valve area (MVA) and pulmonary arterial pressure (PAP) were assessed.

RESULTS: TAPSE, FAC, S', and RVFWS values were substantially declined in MS cases compared with healthy controls. Moreover, PAP values were considerably increased in MS subjects. Additionally, S' and TAPSE values were significantly lower in very severe MS patients compared with severe patients.

CONCLUSION: RV systolic function deteriorates in patients with severe and very severe MS. It appears that the degree of the severity of MS can proportionately affect the extent of RV dysfunction and some of its echocardiographic markers such as S' and TAPSE. TDI and VVI can be used as practical early diagnostic methods for RV dysfunction in MS.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Evaluation of magnetic resonance elastography performance in the assessment of clinically significant liver fibrosis in pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) for detecting clinically significant liver fibrosis (fibrosis stage ≥2) in pediatric patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

METHODS: Cross-sectional, retrospective study of children aged 5-20 years with MASLD who underwent liver biopsy and MRE within 6 months of each other between January 1, 2010, and June 30, 2025. Data collection and chart review were conducted between August 1, 2025, and October 30, 2025. Clinically significant fibrosis was defined as Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network (NASH CRN) Stages 2-4 (F2-F4). Using multivariable logistic regression, a predictive model was developed. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and Youden's Index for optimal cutoff.

RESULTS: The study included 126 patients; 65% male, 39% Hispanic; median age 15 years, 31 (25%), with clinically significant fibrosis. Liver stiffness was higher in those with F2-F4 than those with F0-F1 (2.92 vs. 2.35 kPa; p < 0.01), with no difference in hepatic proton density fat fraction (PDFF). No liver stiffness threshold accurately indicated the presence of clinically significant fibrosis. PDFF was inversely correlated with stiffness in those with F0-F1 (p < 0.0001), but not F2-F4 (p = 0.978).

CONCLUSIONS: MRE has fair discriminatory ability for the detection of clinically significant fibrosis. Therefore, imaging should be used in conjunction with clinical, demographic, and laboratory factors to determine the need for liver histology.

articles.title: Obesity-associated changes in immune cell dynamics during alphavirus infection revealed by single-cell transcriptomic analysis.
articles.abstract: Obesity alters host immunity, resulting in worse disease outcomes following infection with various pathogens, including arthritogenic alphaviruses. However, the impact of obesity on the functional landscape of immune cells during acute arthritogenic alphavirus infection remains incompletely explored. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to dissect the blood and tissue immune responses to Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection in lean and obese mice. Footpad injection of MAYV caused significant shifts in immune cell populations and induced robust expression of interferon response and proinflammatory cytokine genes and related pathways in both blood and tissue. In MAYV-infected lean mice, single-cell analysis of the footpad response revealed a unique macrophage subset (F4/80loMHCII+) with high expression of interferon-responsive genes that was replaced by an alternative, F4/80int population in infected obese mice. Macrophages isolated from lean mice had higher levels of inflammatory gene expression. Furthermore, obese macrophages infected with MAYV and CHIKV ex vivo produce an immunoregulatory response (IL-10) compared to lean macrophages that produce a higher pro-inflammatory response (TNF). The stronger inflammatory response in lean macrophages was associated with less severe systemic disease in lean mice. These results provide evidence for the role of a unique population of macrophages that may contribute to the superior capacity of lean mice to control arthritogenic alphavirus infection.IMPORTANCEArthritogenic alphaviruses-including chikungunya, Mayaro, and Ross River viruses-cause chronic, often disabling joint and muscle disease and are expanding into new regions, yet no approved therapies target the disease process itself. Obesity is a known risk factor for more severe outcomes after infection, but the underlying immune mechanisms have been unclear. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we show that infection drives widespread interferon and inflammatory responses in blood and infected tissue and that obesity specifically alters the macrophage populations present at the infection site. Lean mice mount a highly activated, interferon-driven macrophage response linked to better control of local inflammation, while obese mice instead accumulate a related but less activated population enriched for necroptosis-associated genes and linked to greater tissue damage. These findings identify a specific macrophage subset as a likely contributor to the more severe alphavirus disease seen with obesity and a potential target for future therapies.

articles.title: Nonlinear joint associations of admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and blood urea nitrogen with in-hospital acute kidney injury in cirrhosis with acute variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common following acute variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with cirrhosis. This study assessed the nonlinear individual and joint associations of admission neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) with in-hospital AKI.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicentre retrospective cohort study included 953 patients with cirrhosis and acute variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The primary centre constituted the derivation cohort (n = 667), and the other two hospitals constituted the validation cohort (n = 286), without patient overlap between the two cohorts. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses assessed nonlinear associations in the derivation cohort, with spline specifications applied unchanged to the validation cohort. A four-group NLR-BUN matrix based on derivation cohort cutpoints was evaluated as a secondary exploratory analysis and applied unchanged to the validation cohort.

RESULTS: In-hospital AKI occurred in 168 patients (25.2%) in the derivation cohort and 71 patients (24.8%) in the validation cohort. Median time to AKI was 4 days (IQR, 3-6). Both admission NLR and BUN showed significant nonlinear associations with AKI. Jointly modelled as continuous spline terms, both retained evidence of nonlinear associations, and the RCS fitted better than the corresponding linear model (likelihood-ratio p = 0.001). Joint nonlinearity remained significant in validation (p = 0.046).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission NLR and BUN were nonlinearly associated with in-hospital AKI. The continuous joint association constituted the primary evidence, whereas the data-derived NLR-BUN matrix should be considered exploratory. The retrospective design and validation restricted to the participating centres limit the broader clinical generalizability of the findings.

articles.title: Molecular Discordance Between Primary Non-Small Cell Lung Cancers and Brain Metastases: Associations With Intracranial Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: In an era of molecular-guided systemic oncologic therapies, a proportion of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases (BMs) have demonstrated molecularly discordant profiles for anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK), epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) biomarkers compared with the primary tumor. However, its effect on outcomes remains unclear. We investigated the association between molecular discordance for these actionable markers and clinical outcomes in patients with NSCLC BM.

METHODS: We performed a single-institution retrospective analysis screening 476 patients who underwent treatment for a NSCLC BM from January 2012 to December 2025, with 40 patients having molecular profiling for the primary lung and BM lesions. Patient molecular profiles were categorized as concordant or discordant based on comparison of the ALK, EGFR, and KRAS mutational statuses at both tumor sites. Descriptive statistics, univariate comparisons, Kaplan-Meier survival, and Fine-Gray competing risk analyses were performed between the concordant and discordant cohorts. Multiple comparison using false discovery rate was performed for survival-related outcomes.

RESULTS: ALK, EGFR, or KRAS molecular discordance occurred in 32.5% (13/40) of observed cases. Although nonsignificant, the concordant cohort had a higher rate of distant brain failure (DBF) (63.0% vs 30.8%, P = .056); conversely, the discordant cohort had a higher rate of local recurrence (38.5% vs 18.5%, P = .17). The discordant cohort had a lower subdistribution hazard of DBF than the concordant cohort (subdistribution hazard ratio: 0.34, 95% CI: 0.13-0.91, P = .032). However, this significant difference did not persist after false discovery rate-adjusted analysis. Significant differences in time to intracranial progression, time to local recurrence, and overall survival were not observed between the 2 cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Molecular discordance was observed in >30% of analyzed cases, and the subdistribution hazard of DBF differed significantly between the 2 cohorts. This rate of discordance may warrant further investigation on whether increased BM profiling could help refine current approaches to NSCLC BM management.

articles.title: Sheep model of periprosthetic joint infection induced by low-dose Staphylococcus aureus in cancellous bone : a platform for translational research.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a devastating complication following joint arthroplasty surgery, associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Animal models play a critical role in advancing understanding of PJI and in evaluating therapeutic interventions. However, large-animal models that reproducibly capture cancellous bone infection relevant to hip and knee arthroplasty remain limited. This study evaluated a novel large-animal infection model in sheep.

METHODS: A skeletally mature sheep model was developed to investigate peri-implant bone pathology following Staphylococcus aureus infection. Titanium implants were inoculated with a low bacterial dose and surgically placed in cancellous bone. Animals were euthanized at seven and 21 days post-implantation. Histological, microbiological, and micro-CT (µCT) analyses were performed to assess inflammatory response, implant-associated bacterial colonization, and cancellous bone microarchitecture.

RESULTS: The model reproducibly established localized implant-associated infection without evidence of systemic bacterial dissemination. Histological analysis demonstrated increased neutrophil infiltration and fibroplasia at infected sites, most pronounced at 21 days post-implantation. Microbiological analysis demonstrated that persistent implant-associated S. aureus recovered following sonication. µCT analysis identified cancellous bone loss at infected femora at 21 days, with reductions in bone volume fraction and mean bone apparent density, consistent with early infection-associated bone remodelling.

CONCLUSION: This sheep model captures key features of early implant-associated infection relevant to PJI, including localized bacterial colonization and cancellous bone degradation, and provides a translationally relevant platform for investigating potential therapeutic interventions. The findings characterize early infection-associated bone changes and trabecular adaptation, supporting the utility of this model for evaluating diagnostic approaches and therapeutic strategies relevant to PJI.

articles.title: TMEM106B mediates ACE2-independent replication of the SARS-CoV-2 SE484D variant in airway-derived cell models.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to cause significant respiratory disease, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although ACE2 is the primary receptor for viral entry, previous studies have identified a naturally occurring, ACE2-independent entry pathway that depends on cell-surface heparan sulfates and the E484D substitution within the receptor-binding domain of Spike (S). In this study, we expand the panel of airway-derived cell lines that support ACE2-independent, S-E484D-dependent entry, and identify the host lysosomal transmembrane protein TMEM106B as the alternative receptor for infection. Specifically, we show that knockout of TMEM106B completely abolishes infection by SARS-CoV-2 SE484D in NCI-H522 and NCI-H661 cells. Ectopic expression of the luminal C-terminal domain (CTD) of TMEM106B, either alone or redirected to the plasma membrane, is sufficient to enable viral entry largely independent of cell-surface heparan sulfates in non-permissive cells. We show that S-E484D is required for TMEM106B utilization, whereas other variant of concern substitutions at S-E484 are unable to mediate entry. Fc-TMEM106B-CTD fusion protein binds to a chimeric VSV-SARS-CoV-2 SE484D with a higher affinity than WT virus and blocks infection by SARS-CoV-2 SE484D, supporting a direct interaction between S-E484D and TMEM106B-CTD. Serial passaging experiments with VSV-SARS-CoV-2 SE484D identify a V951A mutation within the heptad repeat 1 region that enhances viral spread and fusogenicity in the ACE2-independent cell models. Together, these findings demonstrate that TMEM106B is a key mediator of a naturally occurring ACE2-independent pathway in multiple airway-derived cell lines, and suggest that variation in the S protein can expand receptor usage by SARS-CoV-2.

IMPORTANCE: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to acquire mutations in the viral spike (S) protein as it circulates in humans. How these mutations influence the cell and tissue tropism of SARS-CoV-2 remains poorly understood. While ACE2 is the canonical host cell receptor for SARS-CoV-2, previous studies revealed the presence of a naturally occurring ACE2-independent entry pathway in multiple airway-derived cell lines that can be utilized only by a SARS-CoV-2 variant bearing the E484D substitution within the viral S protein. Here, we expand the airway-derived cell line models that support ACE2-independent and S-E484D-dependent entry and show that the host lysosomal transmembrane protein, TMEM106B, is an essential viral entry factor. Although the E484D substitution is currently rare in human isolates, our findings raise the possibility that even single mutations in SARS-CoV-2 S can allow the utilization of alternative entry pathways that broaden its cell and tissue tropism.

articles.title: PEDV S protein induces CMPK2 to activate cGAS-STING and NLRP3 antiviral signaling through MLS-dependent mitochondrial localization.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) poses a threat to the global swine industry, yet how PEDV-encoded proteins regulate mitochondria-associated innate antiviral immunity remains unclear. Here, we identify the PEDV spike (S) protein as an upstream inducer of cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinase 2 (CMPK2) expression. Viral protein screening and domain-mapping analyses showed that the S protein induced CMPK2 expression through type I interferon (IFN-I)-related signaling and interferon regulatory factor 1 (IRF1), while its N-terminal S1⁰ region retained the ability to induce CMPK2 expression. The antiviral function of CMPK2 required mitochondrial localization mediated by its mitochondrial localization signal (MLS). As a rate-limiting enzyme in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) synthesis, CMPK2 contributed to mtDNA homeostasis. PEDV infection induced mitochondrial dysfunction and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) accumulation. Under these conditions, CMPK2 was critical for the generation and cytosolic release of oxidized mtDNA (ox-mtDNA). Cytosolic ox-mtDNA acted as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) to activate the cGAS-STING pathway and the NLRP3 inflammasome, thereby restricting PEDV replication. Deletion of the MLS disrupted the mitochondrial localization of CMPK2, impaired its regulation of mtDNA homeostasis, and largely abolished its immunostimulatory and antiviral activities. Moreover, S protein-induced activation of cGAS-STING and the NLRP3 inflammasome was markedly attenuated in CMPK2-KO cells. Collectively, our findings reveal that the PEDV S protein engages CMPK2-dependent mitochondrial antiviral immunity and establish that MLS-mediated mitochondrial localization of CMPK2 is essential for ox-mtDNA generation, cytosolic release, and innate immune activation.

IMPORTANCE: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) causes severe diarrhea in pigs and substantial economic losses, but which viral proteins trigger protective host responses remains unclear. We show that the viral spike protein activates host defense signaling and increases the expression of cytidine/uridine monophosphate kinase 2, a mitochondrial host defense factor. This factor promotes the generation and cytosolic release of oxidized mitochondrial DNA, which activates antiviral and inflammatory defenses that limit viral replication. Its localization within mitochondria is essential for these protective effects. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized immunoregulatory role for the spike protein and show how a viral structural protein can engage mitochondrial DNA metabolism to strengthen host defense. These findings establish an MLS-dependent role for CMPK2 in mtDNA-associated antiviral immunity during PEDV infection.

articles.title: Identification of a highly conserved neutralization epitope targeting poxvirus F13/F13L homologs across seven genera of the subfamily Chordopoxvirinae, family Poxviridae.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The emergence of the human monkeypox epidemic sparked interest in the development of broadly protective pan-poxvirus vaccines that protect against all members of the Poxviridae family. Here, we describe a B-cell monoclonal antibody (mAb) raised against the lumpy skin disease virus ORF29 protein that demonstrates broad-spectrum cross-binding activity against seven genera in the Chordopoxvirinae subfamily, Poxviridae family. Subsequently, a novel continuous linear and conformational epitope has been systematically identified among poxviruses. Furthermore, alanine-scanning mutagenesis analysis confirmed that five critical amino acids (199IGGVF203) of this novel epitope were highly conserved among poxviruses. Crucially, neutralizing assays revealed that this mAb (ORF293C4-2E9) retained broad-spectrum binding and cross-neutralizing activity against capripoxvirus and orthopoxvirus infections in vitro. In vitro antibody internalization and functional assays demonstrated that full-length IgG from ORF293C4-2E9 exhibited higher neutralizing potency than that of its corresponding Fab fragment at the initial stage of viral attachment. Finally, mouse challenge experiments demonstrated that passive ORF293C4-2E9 transfer and peptide immunization provided cross-protective efficacy against ectromelia virus infection following intranasal injection in vivo. Our research provides experimental evidence for heterosubtypic immunity and demonstrates the feasibility of epitope-based approaches for developing pan-poxvirus vaccines and antiviral drugs.

IMPORTANCE: Similar to the COVID-19 pandemic, the recent global outbreak of human monkeypox highlights the critical need for vaccines and therapeutics that offer broad protection against a range of poxviruses. In this study, we comprehensively describe a monoclonal antibody derived from the lumpy skin disease virus that maintains broad cross-reactive binding and neutralizing activity against various poxviruses, including orthopoxviruses (e.g., monkeypox, vaccinia, and ectromelia) and capripoxviruses. Our study identified a highly conserved epitope within the ORF29 protein and its analogs in seven genera in the subfamily Chordopoxvirinae of the Poxviridae family. Our findings provide the first experimental evidence that heterosubtypic immunity can be achieved through epitope-targeted strategies, thereby paving the way for the development of a universally conserved epitope for a broad-spectrum poxvirus vaccine and antiviral drugs.

articles.title: Recommendations for the use of hormone and nonhormone treatment of vasomotor symptoms of menopause: Menopause Medical Eligibility Criteria (MenoMEC) based on insights from a modified Delphi panel.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop a Menopause Medical Eligibility Criteria (MenoMEC) tool to guide individualized, evidence-based care for the treatment of vasomotor symptoms due to menopause.

METHODS: We conducted a modified Delphi panel of 15 multidisciplinary experts to establish US-focused consensus recommendations for hormone and nonhormone therapy use in managing moderate-severe vasomotor symptoms, considering various comorbid conditions. An online survey assessed agreement with proposed recommendations using a nine-point Likert scale, with ≥70% agreement defining consensus. Items lacking consensus were discussed in a structured in-person meeting, leading to refined recommendations and final development of the tool.

RESULTS: Panelists affirmed hormone therapy as first-line for eligible women and nonhormone therapy for those with contraindications or who decline hormone therapy. Recommended first-line nonhormone therapy options were selective serotonin/serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, and oxybutynin, after accounting for contraindications. Neurokinin therapies (eg, fezolinetant, elinzanetant) were supported as first-line but limited by access and cost. Clonidine and most herbal/over-the-counter products were not recommended due to potential adverse effects, drug-drug interactions, or lack of evidence of benefit or harm. Specific recommendations regarding the appropriateness of therapy addressed women with cardiovascular disease, metabolic syndrome, thrombosis, liver disease, smoking, and hormone-sensitive cancers. All panelists agreed that there was an urgent need to provide structured guidance to the clinical community regarding the selection and use of hormone versus nonhormone therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: This panel provided structured, symptom-based, and comorbidity-based recommendations to optimize therapy for the management of vasomotor symptoms and supported the development of a MenoMEC guideline for use in primary care clinical settings.

articles.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea and hypertension: pathophysiological links, blood pressure phenotypes and treatment effects.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and arterial hypertension frequently coexist and are linked by recurrent nocturnal cardiovascular stress. Intermittent hypoxemia, arousals and intrathoracic pressure swings promote sympathetic activation, vascular dysfunction and abnormal blood-pressure (BP) regulation.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review integrates epidemiological, mechanistic and interventional evidence on the OSA-hypertension relationship based on a PubMed search (start until September 2026). Particular emphasis is placed on nocturnal hypertension, non-dipping, masked and resistant hypertension; the roles of intermittent hypoxemia, sympathetic overactivity, baroreflex, and endothelial dysfunction; and treatment effects of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), mandibular advancement devices and weight loss. Evidence from CPAP-withdrawal trials and recent meta-analyses is used to identify characteristics associated with a greater BP response to OSA treatment.

EXPERT OPINION: The modest average BP reduction with CPAP conceals substantial heterogeneity. Treatment effects are strongest for nocturnal BP and in patients with uncontrolled BP, severe OSA and sufficient nightly treatment exposure. Future cardiovascular OSA management should move beyond the apnea-hypopnea index toward combined characterization of nocturnal physiological stress, clinical OSA phenotype, BP phenotype, and effective treatment exposure.

articles.title: Sweet cherry (Prunus avium) fruit pomace extract attenuates Salmonella enteritidis host interactions and preserves intestinal barrier integrity.
articles.abstract: Non-typhoidal Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis (SE) remains a significant cause of global foodborne illness/disease, causing intestinal barrier disruption, mucosal inflammation, and oxidative tissue injury. This study evaluated the potential of a polyphenolic rich sweet cherry pomace extract (CPE) at sub-inhibitory concentrations of 0.5, 1, and 2 mg mL-1 in Caco-2 cells and 100, 200, and 400 µg mL-1 in Caenorhabditis elegans to mitigate SE-induced damage to the cell or to the host. In Caco-2 cells monolayers, CPE inhibited SE adhesion at all assessed concentrations and reduced cell invasion at ≥1 mg mL-1. Furthermore, CPE dose-dependently improved epithelial-barrier integrity, as indicated by increased transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) and decreased paracellular permeability by up to 72.6% at 2 mg mL-1. Gene expression analysis revealed that CPE upregulated tight junction gene expressions (Claudin-1 and ZO-1) while downregulating the host invasion-associated RhoG gene transcript. Additionally, CPE suppressed SE-induced expression of pro-inflammatory NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 genes and upregulated host antioxidant defense Nrf2-HO-1-GcLc genes transcripts. In a Caenorhabditis elegans infection model, CPE treatment significantly decreased intestinal SE colonization (achieving up to a 1.47 log10 CFUs per worm reduction at 200 µg mL-1) and extended host survival following a biphasic concentration-response pattern. These findings suggest that sweet cherry pomace extracts modulate host responses during SE infection and may contribute to improved host resilience against infection.

articles.title: A genome-wide meta-analysis identifies a sex-specific genetic effect for platelet aggregation in response to agonists.
authors: Nhlbi Trans-Omics For Precision TOPMed Consortium
articles.abstract: Sex-specific genetic effects on platelet aggregation may contribute to differences in thrombotic risk between women and men, yet the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly defined. We performed whole-genome sequencing-based genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of 19 harmonized platelet aggregation phenotypes in response to adenosine diphosphate (ADP), epinephrine (EPI), and collagen across three independent cohorts: GeneSTAR, the Framingham Heart Study (FHS) and the Old Order Amish (AMISH). Our meta-GWAS identified a cluster of low-frequency variants within a 20 kb region on chromosome 10 showing strong sex-specific associations with platelet aggregation in response to low-dose EPI. The lead variant, rs116725046, exhibited a genome-wide significant sex interaction (p = 6.7 × 10-9), with opposite phenotypic effects in women and men. Female carriers demonstrated increased platelet aggregation, whereas male carriers showed decreased aggregation, consistent across cohorts. Several variants in tight linkage disequilibrium with the lead variant yielded additional significant interaction signals for low-dose EPI. The associated variants reside within an intronic region of the long noncoding gene LINC00702, with FUMA annotations indicating regulatory chromatin states. Megakaryocyte epigenome data also indicates potential regulatory activity in platelet precursor cells in this genomic region. eQTL analyses suggested sex-differentiated genetic regulation of LINC00702 in multiple tissues, with reduced expression in male heterozygotes only. An Androgen Response Element motif was identified upstream of LINC00702, supporting a potential hormone-responsive regulatory mechanism. Together, these findings identify a novel sex-specific regulatory locus associated with platelet reactivity and highlight LINC00702 as a biologically plausible mediator of sexually dimorphic platelet responses.

articles.title: Reweighting Free Energy Profiles with Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Fast Consensus Building.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
articles.abstract: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made density functional theory (DFT)-level molecular dynamics highly affordable. However, their rapid proliferation makes it prohibitively expensive to benchmark every new model against the potential of mean force (PMF), the bridge between microscopic atomic fluctuations and macroscopic thermodynamic and kinetic observables. Reweighting the trajectory of a single "source" MLIP onto a suite of target potentials offers a cheaper route, but it is hindered by the statistical collapse of exponential free energy perturbation when the phase-space overlap between potentials is low. We show that for system sizes of practical interest, this collapse is essentially unavoidable, and we quantify it with an information-theoretic diagnostic, the reweighting entropy, that indicates when reweighting can be trusted. To sidestep the collapse, we introduce a systematic, scalable reweighting framework spanning exponential reweighting, the Gaussian approximation, and the energy-only estimator. When applied to the intramolecular radical cyclization of hexenyl (17 atoms), all three estimators perform well and reproduce the target ωB97M-V/def2-TZVP PMF. However, when extended to Li+ transport through a water-solvated zeolite (601 atoms), only the energy-only estimator recovers the PMFs of a diverse suite of MLIPs from a single source simulation by discarding the noisy entropic contribution to the free energy correction. An independent, brute-force umbrella sampling of one of the most divergent targets (MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN) for this system confirms it: beyond the shape of the PMF, both the reaction and activation free energies are recovered within chemical accuracy. The same analysis reveals that the studied MLIPs partition into two clusters, one of plain generalized gradient approximation (GGA) models (PBE, PBE-sol) and one of meta-GGA and/or dispersion-corrected models (PBE-D3, r2SCAN, r2SCAN-D4), reflecting differences in their training data and DFT reference. The resulting protocol thus offers an affordable and reliable route to cross-model consensus on materials properties, even when exact reweighting is statistically intractable.

articles.title: Prehospital Antibiotics for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: Research Summary.
Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Fluids Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Early resuscitation with intravenous fluids is recommended for patients with sepsis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the effect of liberal vs more conservative fluid resuscitation strategies in the ambulance on mortality among patients with suspected sepsis.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicenter, 2 × 2 factorial randomized clinical trial conducted by 4 paramedic services and their destination hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38.0 °C), and hypotension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] <100 mm Hg), and obtainable intravenous access. Patients were enrolled between March 23, 2020, and August 20, 2025, with last follow-up in December 2025.

INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to receive liberal fluids (up to 2 L of normal saline regardless of subsequent SBP) or usual care (fluids only when SBP <90 mm Hg and stopped when SBP ≥100 mm Hg) during prehospital care and until transfer of care in the emergency department. (Patients were additionally randomized to receive ceftriaxone vs placebo; analysis of which is reported separately.).

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was hospital mortality, defined as death prior to hospital discharge up to day 90. There were 17 secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality at 90 days, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, mechanical ventilation, vasopressor therapy, dialysis, and total fluids infused within 24 hours of hospital arrival.

RESULTS: Among 1686 randomized patients, 1669 were eligible and 1646 were included in the primary outcome analysis (830 in the liberal fluids group and 816 in the usual fluids group). The median age of patients was 76 (IQR, 63-85) years and 938 (57.0%) were male. Most patients in both groups received a fluid bolus (826/848 [97.4%] in the liberal fluids group; 700/821 [85.3%] in the usual fluids group) during transport, but patients in the liberal fluids group received a larger volume (median, 1500 mL [IQR, 1000-2000 mL]) vs 500 mL [IQR, 175-800 mL] in the usual fluids group; difference, 910.1 mL [95% CI, 857.3-962.9 mL]). Hospital mortality was 149/830 (18.0%) in the liberal fluids group and 149/816 (18.3%) in the usual fluids group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.80-1.20]; unadjusted risk difference, -0.3 [95% CI, -4.0 to 3.4]; P = .82). Among the 17 secondary outcomes, all were similar between groups. Adverse events, including pulmonary edema during transport, were infrequent in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: A more liberal fluid resuscitation strategy for the prehospital management of patients with suspected sepsis did not reduce mortality compared with more restrictive usual care.
