TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741.

articles.title: Prehospital Fluid Resuscitation for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: Research Summary.
Inhibition of HRD1 Alleviates Doxorubicin-Induced Dilated Cardiomyopathy via Regulating the Ubiquitination Degradation of COX5A.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX), a chemotherapeutic agent, can cause heart failure due to loss of cardiomyocytes through programmed cell death. Mitochondrial dysfunction and programmed cardiomyocyte death are central features of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC), yet the upstream ubiquitin-dependent mechanism linking proteostasis disturbance to mitochondrial respiratory impairment remains incompletely understood. The E3 ubiquitin ligase HMG-CoA reductase degradation protein 1 (HRD1) plays an important role in cardiac function and survival; whether HRD1 elevation contributes to DIC is unclear. This study aimed to determine whether HRD1 promotes DIC by inducing ubiquitination and degradation of cytochrome c oxidase subunit 5A (COX5A), thereby impairing mitochondrial function and aggravating cardiomyocyte death. DOX-treated C57BL/6J mice, primary cardiomyocytes and AC16 cells were used in this study. DOX increased HRD1 expression in mouse cardiac tissue and cultured cardiomyocytes. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of HRD1 attenuated DOX-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial remodelling. In vitro, HRD1 knockdown alleviated, but HRD1 overexpression aggravated DOX-induced apoptosis- and ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury. Mechanistically, HRD1 was associated with COX5A, a nuclear-encoded subunit of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV and promoted its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. The catalytically inactive HRD1-C291A mutant attenuated this effect compared with wild-type HRD1. Moreover, we also found that COX5A knockdown abolished the protective effects of HRD1 knockdown; by contrast, COX5A overexpression countered the injury associated with HRD1 overexpression. The present study demonstrates that HRD1 promotes DOX-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, cardiomyocyte death, cardiac dysfunction and myocardial remodelling by mediating COX5A ubiquitination and degradation. These findings identify the HRD1-COX5A axis as a potential therapeutic target for DOX-induced cardiac injury.

articles.title: Prehospital Antibiotics for Patients With Suspected Sepsis: The PITSTOP-Antibiotics Factorial Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Early treatment with antibiotics is considered an important intervention to reduce mortality for patients with sepsis.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the effect of earlier treatment with antibiotics in the ambulance on 90-day mortality compared with usual treatment in the emergency department.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, 2 × 2 factorial randomized, placebo-controlled trial was conducted among 4 paramedic services and their destination hospitals in Ontario, Canada. Participants were adults with suspected sepsis, defined as suspected infection, fever (≥38.0 °C), and hypotension (systolic blood pressure <100 mm Hg). Patients were enrolled between March 23, 2020, and August 20, 2025, with final follow-up in December 2025.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive 1 g of intramuscular ceftriaxone or placebo (and to receive liberal fluids vs usual fluids; reported separately) during prehospital care in the ambulance. All patients could receive open-label antibiotics in the emergency department.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was hospital mortality, defined as death prior to hospital discharge to day 90. There were 17 secondary outcomes, including all-cause mortality at 90 days, hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, use of mechanical ventilation, use of dialysis, positive culture results, and antibiotics within 24 hours of hospital arrival.

RESULTS: Among 2091 randomized patients, 2048 were eligible for the primary analysis, with 1026 randomized to receive ceftriaxone and 1022 randomized to receive placebo. The median (IQR) age of patients was 75 (62-85) years and 1162 (56.7%) were males. The mean (SD) time from paramedic arrival at patient to administration of study drug was 37 (36) minutes in the ceftriaxone group and 39 (55) minutes in the placebo group. Most patients (735 of 795 [92.5%] in the ceftriaxone group and 730 of 792 [92.2%] in placebo group) were treated with antibiotics in the hospital after a mean (SD) of 247.3 (207.7) minutes after paramedic arrival among patients in the ceftriaxone group and 252.8 (218.0) minutes among the placebo group. The rate of hospital mortality was 182 of 1009 (18.0%) in the ceftriaxone group and 186 of 1011 (18.4%) in the placebo group (risk ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.81-1.17]; P = .77). Of 17 secondary outcomes, all were similar between the groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with suspected sepsis on evaluation by paramedics, earlier treatment with antibiotics in the ambulance did not reduce mortality compared with usual care provided in the emergency department.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03068741.

articles.title: Effects of a short-term exercise program on functional capacity and perceived exertion in middle-aged adults: a pilot study.
articles.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity is a major modifiable risk factor for chronic diseases and functional decline in adulthood. Although the benefits of exercise are well established, evidence regarding the effectiveness of short-term and easily implementable exercise interventions in real-world settings remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the effects of an 8-week structured physical activity program on functional capacity and perceived exertion in middle-aged adults.

METHODS: Twelve adults aged 50-71 years participated in a quasi-experimental pre-post-intervention study. The intervention consisted of an 8-week supervised exercise program performed 2-3 times per week (45-60 min/session), including aerobic, resistance, mobility, and balance exercises. Functional capacity was assessed before and after the intervention using the Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), plank test, and Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired t-tests.

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed across all outcomes (P<0.05). The distance covered during the 6MWT increased from 459.2±15.4 m to 503.6±15.0 m (+44.4 m; +9.7%), indicating improved functional exercise capacity. Plank performance improved from 35.7±4.0 s to 49.8±4.5 s (+14.2 s; +39.7%), reflecting enhanced core muscular endurance. Perceived exertion decreased from 14.5±0.7 to 11.4±0.5, suggesting improved tolerance to physical activity following the intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: A short-term and low-complexity exercise program was associated with improvements in functional capacity and reduced perceived exertion in middle-aged adults. These findings support the effectiveness of brief and easily implementable exercise interventions for promoting functional health in real-world settings.

articles.title: [Not Available].
articles.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A woman in her eighties was repeatedly admitted to hospital with episodes of confusion.

CASE PRESENTATION: The patient had a medical history of recurrent urinary tract infections, stroke and Waldenström macroglobulinaemia. The medical work-up revealed hyperammonaemia, but no evidence of infection, cerebral ischaemia or infarction, or transformation of her Waldenström macroglobulinaemia. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) showed signs of blood shunting past the liver through the pelvic veins. There was no evidence of hepatic insufficiency on laboratory tests, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or liver biopsy.

INTERPRETATION: A portosystemic shunt was suspected to be a significant contributor to her hyperammonaemia, and she underwent surgical closure of the pelvic venous shunts. Following surgery, her ammonia levels decreased significantly, and her episodes of confusion ceased. Five years after surgery, her ammonia levels remained normal and she was no longer confused.

articles.title: Prevalence of recorded type 2 diabetes among different immigrant groups in Norway.
articles.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes varies between immigrant groups, with a high prevalence previously reported in some groups. However, there is a lack of recent research examining these differences. The aim of this study was to provide an updated overview of the variation in prevalence.

MATERIAL AND METHOD: Diagnoses recorded in the Norwegian Control and Payment of Health Reimbursements Database (KUHR) and the Norwegian Patient Registry in the period 2017-2023 were linked to data from Statistics Norway on immigrant background, country of birth and year of birth. Relative risks (RRs) with 95 % confidence intervals (CIs) for a recorded diagnosis of type 2 diabetes were estimated for different immigrant groups, using the Norwegian-born population as the reference group.

RESULTS: Overall, immigrants had a higher risk of type 2 diabetes than people born in Norway (RR 1.70, 95 % CI 1.68-1.72). The risk was substantially higher among refugees, immigrants from Africa and immigrants from Asia (RR 2.66, 3.11 and 2.91, respectively). Immigrants from North America and Oceania, and from the EU, EEA and the UK, had a lower risk (RR 0.66 and 0.68, respectively). Immigrants born in Pakistan had the highest risk (RR 5.03), followed by those born in Somalia. Immigrants born in Lithuania had the lowest risk (RR 0.32), followed by Ukraine. Relative differences between the Norwegian-born population and immigrants were greatest among women.

INTERPRETATION: There is substantial variation in the prevalence of recorded type 2 diabetes between groups based on country of birth or reason for immigration. Targeted measures aimed at specific sections of the immigrant population are needed to reduce health inequalities.

articles.title: [Not Available].
articles.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke
articles.abstract: The disease burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and harmful alcohol use is substantial and increasing. Early detection of liver fibrosis can reduce morbidity and mortality. Guidelines from European associations specialising in diabetes, obesity and liver disease therefore recommend screening high-risk groups for liver fibrosis. This clinical review summarises the evidence base for the diagnosis, management and follow-up of patients with steatotic liver disease.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Phenotypes in Children Aged 6-12 Years: A Pediatric Nephrology Research Consortium (PNRC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) enables identification of hypertension phenotypes carrying distinct cardiovascular risk profiles, yet data on phenotype distribution and cardiac outcomes in younger school-age children remain limited.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cross-sectional study conducted across 11 Pediatric Nephrology Research Consortium sites included children aged 6-12 years without chronic kidney disease who underwent ABPM and echocardiography within 3 months. Blood pressure (BP) phenotypes were classified per the 2022 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on ABPM in Children and Adolescents.

RESULTS: Of 212 children (median age 10.6 years, 45.3% female, median BMI z-score 1.56), sustained hypertension was most prevalent (39.6%), followed by white-coat hypertension (30.7%), normotension (17.0%), and masked hypertension (12.7%). Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, left ventricular mass index [LVMI] ≥95th percentile for age and sex) was identified in 49 children (23.1%), present across all phenotypes. No BP phenotype was independently associated with LVH or LVMI in adjusted (for age, sex and BMI z-score) or sensitivity models (site level clustering and device type). BMI z-score was the only independent correlate of LVH (PR 1.36, 95% CI 1.01-1.82, p = 0.04). Nocturnal hypertension was associated with higher LVMI after full adjustment (β = 2.66, 95% CI 0.10-5.21); sensitive to ABPM device type adjustment. Among children with masked hypertension, 88.9% had nocturnal hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter cohort of younger children without CKD, BP phenotype was not significantly associated with LVH; BMI z-score was the most consistent correlate of cardiac remodeling, and nocturnal hypertension showed an exploratory association with higher LVMI after BMI z-score adjustment.

articles.title: The Rate of Epidural Hematoma Following Lumbar Interlaminar Epidural Steroid Injection in 1787 Patient Encounters for Patients on Anticoagulant or Antiplatelet Medications: A Retrospective Review and Summation of Current Literature.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Report the rate of epidural hematoma (EH) following lumbar interlaminar epidural steroid injections (ILESI) in patients prescribed anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications (ACAP).

METHODS: This analysis is a retrospective cohort study in a single private multispecialty practice reviewing 1787 unique patient encounters. Main outcome measures are to follow up patients after lumbar ILESI procedure by retrospective clinical chart review, outside clinical records review, and telephone follow up of consecutive patients over 8 years. Patients are stratified by whether ACAP medication was maintained or ceased prior to lumbar ILESI procedure.

RESULTS: There were zero clinically relevant EHs (0/1787, 0%, 95% CI 0.0-0.2%). In 310 patient encounters maintained on anticoagulation (either AC only or AC in conjunction with AP), the rate of clinically relevant EH was 0/310 (0%, 95% CI 0.0-1.2%). Patients who maintained AP medication alone, the rate of clinically relevant EH was 0/649 (0%, 95% CI 0.0-0.6%). Two patients without follow up data were not included in analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the risk of EH following ILESI is low even in patients maintained on ACAP medication. At least 10 case reports of EH following lumbar ILESI have been published. Aggregating our data with other published cohorts, the rate of EH following lumbar ILESI, regardless of ACAP status, is 2/10,536 (0.02%, 95% CI 0.0-0.07%).

articles.title: Migration of a Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Stent Causing Incomplete Cardioplegic Arrest: Stent Gone Astray!
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) stenting is an established palliative option in tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) when surgical repair poses a high-risk. We report a rare, life-threatening complication in a 4-year-old child with TOF, a hypoplastic pulmonary annulus, and multiple comorbidities that precluded primary corrective surgery. RVOT stenting was therefore planned. During catheterization, the stent embolized, necessitating emergency surgical retrieval. Intraoperatively, the stent was seen lodged across the aortic valve, preventing complete leaflet coaptation, and causing the cardioplegia to leak into the left ventricle. This resulted in an incomplete cardioplegic arrest. Real-time transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) identified the mechanism of cardioplegia failure, delineated the stent position, guided its repositioning, and facilitated successful cardioplegia delivery and definitive surgical repair. This case emphasizes meticulous anatomical evaluation and highlights the indispensable role of intraoperative TEE in high-risk RVOT stenting.

articles.title: Reliability and Validity of the Modified Star Excursion Balance Test in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes is a prevalent diagnosis in the older adult population and is associated with disease-related physical deficits including loss of balance and increased risk of falls. Although a number of balance assessments have been validated in the general older adult population, a need for type 2 diabetes-specific balance measures has been identified. The purpose of this study was to investigate the test-retest reliability and validity of the Modified Star Excursion Balance Test (mSEBT) in older adults with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: Twenty-four older adults with type 2 diabetes (8 males, 16 females, mean age = 68.25 years [SD = 6.9]) were included. Participants completed the mSEBT, the Timed Up and Go (TUG), Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), and the Six-Item Activities-Specific Balance Confidence Scale (ABC-6) on 2 separate days. Scores were compared between testing days, and reliability was analyzed using the intraclass correlation coefficient and minimal detectable change (MDC95). Validity was assessed by comparing the initial scores of the mSEBT with the other outcome measures using Pearson's correlation coefficient, Spearman's rho, scatter plots, and Bland-Altman plots with 95% limits of agreement (LOA).

RESULTS: The intraclass correlation coefficient and MDC95 for the mSEBT were 0.90% (95% CI = 0.78-0.95) and 14.80%, respectively. Significant correlations (P < .05) were found between the mSEBT and all other measures of balance including the TUG (r = -0.72), SPPB (r = 0.82), and ABC-6 (rs = 0.41). Bland-Altman plots and 95% LOA using z scores suggested considerable agreement between the mSEBT versus the SPPB (95% LOA = -1.14 to 1.14) and ABC-6 (95% LOA = -1.93 to 1.93). Less agreement was found between the mSEBT and TUG (95% LOA = -3.67 to 3.67).

CONCLUSION: The findings of this study indicate that the mSEBT is a reliable and valid assessment of balance in older adults with type 2 diabetes. Further, a change of 14.80% or greater on the mSEBT in older adults with type 2 diabetes is representative of a true change in balance.

articles.title: Clinical and Financial Burden of Infectious Complication After Elective Cardiac Operation in the US.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare-acquired infections (HAI) after cardiac surgery impose substantial clinical and economic burdens. We examined factors associated with HAI and their relationship with mortality, hospital length of stay, and costs in a national cardiac surgical population.

STUDY DESIGN: Adult (≥18 years) elective hospitalizations involving coronary artery bypass grafting, valve repair or replacement, or combined procedures were identified in the 2016-2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Entropy balancing followed by regression was used to evaluate associations between HAI and clinical and economic outcomes.

RESULTS: Among an estimated 962,261 patients, 7.4% developed HAI. After risk adjustment, HAI was associated with greater mortality (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 5.11; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.82-5.42), an additional 8.54 hospital days (95% CI, 8.23-8.76), and $41,110 in increased hospitalization costs (95% CI, $39,656-$42,565). Older age (AOR, 1.01/year; 95% CI, 1.00-1.02), female sex (AOR, 1.66; 95% CI, 1.62-1.70), and low-income status (AOR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.25) were associated with HAI. Sepsis and bacteremia accounted for the greatest incremental costs per episode and largest estimated annual cost burden.

CONCLUSIONS: HAI after elective cardiac surgery is associated with markedly greater mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and substantial additional costs. These findings support prioritizing targeted infection prevention within cardiac surgical quality improvement and healthcare resource stewardship.

articles.title: Indications for medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). The 2026 ESSKA-EKA formal consensus. Part 1-Patient history and clinical principles.
articles.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This consensus followed the ESKKA formal consensus methodology and aimed to provide updated, evidence‑based and expert‑opinion recommendations defining current indications for medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). Part I focuses on patient history, demographics and clinical assessment.

METHODS: European expert surgeons and scientists were organized into a steering group (11 experts from 9 countries), a rating group (23 experts from 16 countries) and a peer-review group of representatives of the ESSKA-affiliated national societies to ensure geographic applicability and acceptance. The steering group developed 35 question-and-answer statements (20 related to Part I). The statements were graded according to the strength of scientific evidence: Grade A (high level of scientific evidence), Grade B (scientific presumption), Grade C (low level of scientific support) or Grade D (expert opinion). Following statement development, an independent rating group evaluated each recommendation according to scientific quality and clinical relevance using a 9-point Likert scale (1 = totally inappropriate and 9 = totally appropriate). Statements with a median agreement below 7 were revised, and an updated manuscript was submitted to the rating group for a second evaluation. A final combined 'face-to-face' meeting between the steering and rating groups enabled completion of the final version of the document. The final version of the manuscript was subsequently reviewed by the peer review group to produce the final consensus statement.

RESULTS: In this Part I, consensus was reached on 12 questions with strong agreement (median ≥ 7; range: 7-9), while the remaining 8 demonstrated relative agreement (median ≥ 7; range: 5-9). No statements were deemed uncertain. However, the overall quality of the supporting evidence was low, with all statements classified as Grade C or D.

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus was undertaken to provide the best available recommendations for medial UKA in patients with isolated medial compartment osteoarthritis or spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee. Current evidence supports expanded indications, as factors such as anterior cruciate ligament deficiency, younger age, higher body mass index, patellofemoral arthritis, chondrocalcinosis, rheumatoid arthritis and fixed flexion deformity are no longer considered absolute contraindications. This study's clinical relevance is to provide evidence to guide patient selection and surgical planning, and to help surgeons choose appropriate treatment options.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level I.

articles.title: Circumflex-perfused mass and mitral regurgitation after coronary bypass.
articles.abstract: BackgroundIschemic cardiomyopathy-associated mitral regurgitation (ICM-MR) may improve after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, its determinants remain unclear. We investigated left circumflex coronary artery (LCx)-perfused left ventricular (LV) mass volume and regional myocardial mechanics related to ICM-MR improvement after isolated CABG.MethodsData of 22 patients with ICM-MR who underwent isolated CABG (2016-2023) were retrospectively studied using preoperative and 1-year postoperative coronary computed tomography and echocardiography. Patients were grouped by 1-year MR change: improvement (≥1-grade reduction) and non-improvement (no change/worse). Perfused LV mass volume, regional longitudinal strain, and mitral tethering geometry were compared.ResultsAmong the 22 patients, nine (41%) exhibited MR improvement, whereas 13 (59%) did not. The change in the LCx-perfused LV mass volume was significantly greater in the improvement group than in the non-improvement group (11 [3-16] vs 0 [-6-5] mL; p = 0.049). The LCx longitudinal strain substantially improved in the improvement group (-10.3% [-11.6 to -1.4] vs +1.2% [-3.2 to +4.6]; p = 0.016). The improvement group demonstrated greater reverse remodeling: tenting height (-2.2 mm [-2.4 to -0.6] vs -0.5 mm [-0.7 to 0.2], p = 0.007), tenting area (-0.54 cm2 [-0.85 to -0.35] vs  + 0.02 cm2 [-0.07 to + 0.57], p < 0.001), and posterior leaflet tethering angle (-5° [-9 to -2] vs 1° [-2 to 4], p = 0.038).ConclusionsImprovement in ICM-MR after isolated CABG was associated with an increased LCx-perfused LV mass volume, concomitant regional functional recovery, and mitral geometry reversal, suggesting a possible role of LCx territory recovery in mitral regurgitation improvement.

articles.title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model for Early Prediction of Septic Shock in Intensive Care Unit Patients: The Incremental Value of Cardiac Output.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEarly identification of septic shock is critical for timely resuscitation, yet conventional vital signs such as blood pressure exhibit physiological lag during the compensatory phase. Whether advanced hemodynamic parameters confer incremental predictive value within machine learning (ML) early warning frameworks remains unquantified.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study used the MIMIC-IV v3.0 database. From 7384 patients with hemodynamic monitoring records, 1716 adult ICU patients contributing 16,140 hourly prediction windows were analyzed. Patients were partitioned into a development set (n = 1372) and a held-out test set (n = 344). Two nested models predicted septic shock within 6 h: a baseline model using routine variables and an enhanced model adding cardiac output (CO), cardiac index (CI), stroke volume index (SVI), and systemic vascular resistance index (SVRI). XGBoost was the primary classifier. Patient-level cross-validation and clustered bootstrap evaluated discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, while SHAP and ablation assessed feature contributions.ResultsThe enhanced model consistently outperformed the baseline across four algorithms. With XGBoost, cross-validated AUROC improved from 0.862 (95% CI 0.847-0.877) to 0.881 (0.867-0.894), a gain of 0.018 (0.010-0.027; DeLong p = 3.22 × 10-11). Sensitivity increased from 0.249 to 0.316 and F1 from 0.335 to 0.388. Held-out AUROC was 0.819 versus 0.844 (p = 2.06 × 10-6). Calibration was comparable, and the enhanced model provided greater net benefit at threshold probabilities of 0.01-0.49. SHAP ranked CO second only to lactate; removing CO reduced AUROC by 0.017 (0.008-0.024), whereas removing the derived indices had negligible effects.ConclusionsIncorporating cardiac output into routine monitoring models provides robust incremental value for early septic shock prediction. CO captures circulatory compromise masked by compensatory normotension and may support risk-stratified ICU surveillance.

articles.title: Real-Time Cumulative Fluid Balance Surveillance and Stewardship in Critical Care: From Prediction to Prevention of Fluid Overload.
articles.abstract: Fluid therapy is a crucial intervention in critical care, but the same treatment that restores perfusion during shock may become harmful when positive fluid balance persists after stabilization and contributes to organ dysfunction. A key conceptual distinction is that daily fluid balance (FB), cumulative fluid balance (CFB), and percent cumulative fluid balance (%CFB) are quantitative measurements, whereas fluid overload (FO) is a clinical state in which positive fluid balance is associated with or contributes to clinically meaningful organ dysfunction or morbidity. Building on the ADQI framework, an important bedside challenge is how to monitor the evolving CFB trajectory, identify the fluid sources driving accumulation, and recognize when a measurable positive balance has become clinically harmful FO. This review builds on the existing outcome-focused literature and offers a complementary implementation-oriented framework. We summarize the physiology of fluid equilibrium, contemporary terminology for FB, CFB, %CFB, and FO, and the bidirectional relationship between positive fluid balance, FO, and acute kidney injury (AKI). We then emphasize fluid profiling as a method to distinguish necessary resuscitation from potentially modifiable sources of fluid exposure, including maintenance fluids, medication carriers, flushes, diluents, and parenteral nutrition. Consistent with the ADQI emphasis on dynamic assessment across phases of fluid therapy, we suggest CFB monitoring as an evolving bedside signal by integrating %CFB, CFB trajectory and rate of change, daily weight, urine output, AKI stage, creatinine corrected for fluid balance, hemodynamics, respiratory status, and organ-specific tolerance. Finally, we outline a future research agenda centered on real-time electronic dashboards, prescribed CFB targets, predictive trajectory monitoring, renal angina-based risk stratification, urinary biomarkers, furosemide stress testing, pharmacy-nursing stewardship bundles, and pragmatic trials of structured de-resuscitation. The goal is to move beyond static numeric thresholds toward earlier recognition of adverse CFB trajectories and prevention of clinically harmful FO.

articles.title: Association between body mass index and perimenopause symptom burden: a cross-sectional global study using the Flo App.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between body mass index (BMI) and overall perimenopause symptom burden, measured by the total Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) score, and domain-specific psychological, somatic, and urogenital symptoms.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted through the Flo app between December 2024 and May 2025 and included 1,988 women in perimenopause aged 35 years or older. BMI was categorized into six groups from underweight to obesity class III. Total and domain-specific MRS scores were compared using ANOVA and pairwise comparisons. Multiple linear regression identified predictors of symptom burden.

RESULTS: In multivariable regression models adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, income, education, smoking, physical activity, alcohol use, and comorbididities (anxiety, depression, and diabetes), obesity classes I-III were independently associated with higher total (B=1.21-1.42, all P<0.05) and somatic (B=0.76-0.92, all P<0.001) MRS scores relative to normal weight, whereas no BMI category was independently associated with psychological or urogenital scores. Comorbid anxiety and depression emerged as the strongest independent predictors of symptom burden across all domains, followed by insufficient income, lower educational attainment, and active smoking, whereas more frequent physical activity was associated with lower symptom burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher BMI was independently associated with greater perimenopause symptom burden, particularly in the somatic domain, underscoring the multifactorial nature of symptom burden during the menopause transition.

articles.title: Concurrent association between standard lipid parameters and menopausal status in midlife Korean women: a nationwide cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Menopause is accompanied by cardiometabolic changes; however, most studies have examined lipid changes as outcomes of the menopause transition. Using a large nationwide cross-sectional dataset, we sought to characterize the concurrent association between standard lipid parameters and menopausal status-without inferring directionality-and to examine whether the magnitude of the association differs by age at menopause, with a particular focus on early menopause (EMP).

METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) health screening database, we analyzed 426,337 women aged 40-55 years with consistent menopausal status reported at both the 2011 and 2013 examinations (either premenopausal at both, or postmenopausal at both). Lipid parameters (total cholesterol [TC], low-density lipoprotein cholesterol [LDL-C], high-density lipoprotein cholesterol [HDL-C], and triglycerides [TGs]), measured at the 2013 index examination, were categorized using clinical cut-offs. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed; the previously presented unadjusted model has been removed because it is uninterpretable in the presence of substantial age-related confounding. Models were sequentially adjusted for age, socioeconomic and lifestyle factors, and reproductive factors (primary model), with a secondary model additionally including metabolic comorbidities and statin use as potential intermediate variables. Subgroup analyses compared EMP (below 45 y) versus non-EMP (45 y and above).

RESULTS: In fully adjusted analyses, higher TC, LDL-C, and TG were associated with higher odds of being postmenopausal. Compared with TC <200 mg/dL, adjusted odds ratios (ORs) were 1.24 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.21-1.26) for TC 200-239 mg/dL and 1.52 (95% CI: 1.47-1.57) for TC ≥240 mg/dL (P<0.001). Relative to LDL-C <100 mg/dL, LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL showed an OR of 1.64 (95% CI: 1.53-1.75) (P<0.001). TG ≥200 mg/dL was associated with an OR of 1.14 (95% CI: 1.09-1.18) versus TG <150 mg/dL (P<0.001). HDL-C was inversely associated; compared with HDL-C ≥60 mg/dL, HDL-C <40 mg/dL showed an OR of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82-0.90) (P<0.001). Associations were substantially stronger for EMP, including TC ≥240 mg/dL (OR=2.18, 95% CI: 1.81-2.61) and LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL (OR=2.83, 95% CI: 1.96-4.07). Estimates were highly consistent across our sequentially adjusted models (relative change in OR <2% between the primary model and the secondary model that additionally adjusted for potential intermediates), supporting the robustness of the findings to additional covariate adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Adverse lipid profiles were concurrently associated with menopausal status, with substantially more pronounced associations in EMP. Owing to the cross-sectional design, the directionality of these associations-whether menopause-driven dyslipidemia, lipid-mediated accelerated ovarian aging, or shared upstream determinants-cannot be established, and the results should be interpreted as cross-sectional correlates rather than causal effects.

articles.title: Evidence appraisal of clinical practice guidelines for managing menopausal symptoms: a systematic literature review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Symptoms associated with menopause can significantly impair quality of life. Although menopausal hormone therapy remains a well-established and highly effective intervention, a wide range of nonhormone therapies are available on and off-label as options for women in whom menopausal hormone therapy is contraindicated or not preferred. Although multiple clinical guidelines address the use of menopausal hormone therapy and nonhormone therapy for managing symptoms of menopause, the consistency of the recommendations and the robustness of the supporting evidence remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: Evaluate current United States menopause treatment guidelines in the context of emerging therapies (menopausal hormone therapy and nonhormone therapy) and evolving clinical practice.

EVIDENCE REVIEW: We systematically searched PubMed and EMBASE for United States menopause treatment guidelines published between 2014 and 2024. We included clinical practice guidelines and consensus statements, excluding those limited to surgically induced menopause. We extracted data using the Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcomes, Recommendation framework and assessed guideline quality.

FINDINGS: Of 655 records screened, 13 met the inclusion criteria from organizations including the American Association of Clinical Endocrinology, The Menopause Society, and the Endocrine Society. Guidelines evaluated menopausal hormone therapy for managing vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome, premature ovarian insufficiency, hypoactive sexual desire disorder, sleep disturbances, and depression, contingent on individual risk profiles. Nonhormone therapies, including selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, gabapentin, and fezolinetant, were supported by moderate to high-quality evidence. Most guidelines advise against over-the-counter or alternative treatments due to limited data. No guideline provided decision-support tools or therapeutic sequencing algorithms for nonhormone therapy selection. Seven guidelines were of moderate quality, four low-moderate, and two low quality with none rated high quality, primarily due to gaps in stakeholder involvement and applicability.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This review highlights variable quality and consistency in United States clinical recommendations for vasomotor symptoms. Future guidelines should incorporate structured decision frameworks to guide therapy selection based on contraindications, patient preferences, and risk profiles.

articles.title: Trained Innate Immunity in Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Chronicity: Hematopoietic Memory and Failure of Inflammation Resolution.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: Diabetes-related foot ulcers remain prone to non-healing and recurrence despite appropriate vascular, surgical, antimicrobial, and off-loading care. We evaluated whether trained innate immunity provides a coherent explanation for this chronicity and defined priorities for clinical translation. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through August 5, 2026, for literature on trained immunity, diabetes, hematopoiesis, diabetic wounds, neutrophil extracellular traps, macrophages, efferocytosis, biofilm, epigenetics, immunometabolism, and inflammation resolution. Primary mechanistic studies, human translational studies, clinical guidance, and authoritative reviews were prioritized and classified as direct wound evidence, systemic contextual evidence, or hypothesis-level inference. Diabetes can produce persistent metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in hematopoietic progenitors and descendant myeloid cells. In diabetic wounds, excessive NETosis, macrophage dysfunction, impaired apoptotic-cell clearance, and recurrent microbial or damage signals can reinforce inflammation and disrupt vascular, stromal, and epithelial repair. Direct evidence supports components of this model, but the complete longitudinal bone-marrow-to-wound pathway has not been demonstrated in humans. Trained immunity should therefore be treated as a falsifiable mechanism of treatment resistance and recurrence, not as a clinical diagnosis. Clinically, this framework supports phase-aware biomarker sampling and confines immune-directed adjuncts to adequately perfused, source-controlled ulcers. Longitudinal cohorts with functional rest-and-rechallenge assays, lineage-aware epigenetic measurements, and rigorous adjustment for perfusion, infection, and off-loading are needed.

articles.title: Impact of early tocilizumab administration on cytokine release syndrome from multiple myeloma bispecific antibodies.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionRecent guidelines support first-line use of tocilizumab for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) associated with bispecific antibodies for multiple myeloma. Uniquely, our institution utilizes additional prophylactic dexamethasone the day after bispecific antibody administration. This study contributes to the available evidence to determine optimal first-line CRS management while considering this differing prophylaxis strategy. The primary objective was to describe the impact of early tocilizumab on the incidence of CRS refractory to initial treatment.MethodsThis was a retrospective single-center observational study. Adults aged 18 years or older with multiple myeloma who received elranatamab, talquetamab, or teclistamab, between December 1, 2022, and December 31, 2025, and had documented CRS were included. Descriptive statistics were used to report outcomes.ResultsTwenty-two patients, over 26 hospital admissions were included. Most patients received talquetamab (46%), while elranatamab and teclistamab each accounted for 27%. Initial CRS management included dexamethasone alone in ten patients, tocilizumab alone in seven, both agents in five, and neither treatment in four. Three patients experienced CRS that was refractory to initial treatment, and all instances of refractory CRS occurred in patients initially treated with dexamethasone alone. Recurrent CRS occurred in four patients.ConclusionBoth refractory and recurrent CRS were numerically lower in the tocilizumab alone group. Length of stay was similar among groups. These findings suggest that using tocilizumab for initial CRS management may reduce refractory and recurrent cytokine release syndrome with minimal impact on length of stay.

articles.title: Increased Task Precision Demands Disproportionately Reduce Paretic Arm Choice After Right-Hemisphere Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with right cerebrovascular accidents (RCVAs) use their contralesional paretic arm less than those with left cerebrovascular accidents (LCVAs). However, the contribution of task precision demands to this disparity remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To examine effects of arm choice and performance under increased task precision demands in RCVA compared to LCVA and their relation to daily paretic arm use.

METHODS: Eighteen individuals with chronic unilateral stroke (8 LCVA and 10 RCVA) with similar motor impairment and 9 age-matched neurotypical controls performed a planar reaching task, choosing either arm to reach randomly presented targets. Target size was manipulated to test whether movement precision demands influenced arm choice. Paretic arm use in daily life was measured with bilateral accelerometers over 5 consecutive days. Reaction time to left and right targets was recorded to examine lateralized attention effects on paretic arm performance. Lease absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used to identify whether measures of motor and attentional capacity predicted paretic arm use.

RESULTS: The RCVA group showed significantly fewer paretic arm reaches and more nonparetic arm midline crosses than controls. Target size influenced paretic arm choice in RCVA, but not in LCVA and controls. Both motor performance and attention measures predicted paretic arm choice. Finally, arm choice during small target conditions predicted daily arm use measured with accelerometry.

CONCLUSIONS: Greater task-precision demands amplify paretic arm nonuse after RCVA, suggesting that hemisphere of lesion moderates the effect of precision demand on paretic arm choice. Motor and attentional deficits, together with nonpreference-paresis concordance may contribute to heightened nonuse.

articles.title: Care-Seeking Decision Delay in Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Mixed-Methods Study at a Tertiary Hospital in Guangzhou, China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine the duration and associated factors of care-seeking decision delay in adults with acute myocardial infarction(AMI).

DESIGN: Convergent mixed-methods study.

SAMPLE: 233 adults with AMI at a tertiary hospital in Guangzhou, China; 13 participants were interviewed.

MEASUREMENTS: Care-seeking decision delay was calculated from recalled symptom-onset and decision-to-seek-care times, with >60 minutes classified as delayed care seeking. Symptom recognition-related knowledge and care-seeking concerns were assessed using the Chinese Acute Coronary Syndrome Response Index knowledge subscale and Concerns Questionnaire. Quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and content analysis, respectively, then integrated.

RESULTS: Overall, 68.7% of participants experienced care-seeking decision delay. Greater social concerns (aOR = 1.24) and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (aOR = 6.93) were associated with higher odds of delay, whereas greater concern about serious consequences (aOR = 0.69) and accompaniment by friends or colleagues at symptom onset (aOR = 0.02) were associated with lower odds. Interviews described difficulties in symptom interpretation and attribution, limited awareness of chest pain centers, and distrust of local healthcare services as perceived barriers to timely care-seeking.

CONCLUSIONS: Care-seeking decision delay was common. Public health nursing strategies addressing symptom recognition, social concerns, and emergency-care pathway awareness warrant further evaluation.

articles.title: Pneumocephalus After Positive Pressure Ventilation Without Skull Base Defect: A Diagnostic Quest.
articles.journal: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pneumocephalus typically results from craniofacial trauma, tumors, infections, or skull base defects. Acute pneumocephalus in a patient without prior neurological history or obvious skull base defects presents a diagnostic challenge.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 65-year-old male with a history of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and multiple esophageal dilations post-radiation presented with hypercapnic respiratory failure. He developed acute-onset altered mental status after initiation of Bilevel Positive Airway Pressure (BiPAP). An urgent head computed tomography (CT) scan showed pneumocephalus, and subsequent sinus CTs showed no skull base defects. Nasal endoscopy showed no obvious clear fluid drainage, and nasal secretions tested negative for beta-2 transferrin. Retrospective review of a chest CT from 3 months prior revealed a small proximal esophageal defect with prevertebral air tracking. Follow-up CT imaging confirmed air tracking along the T1 costovertebral joint, identifying an enterothecal fistula as the route for positive-pressure air entry into the spinal canal and cranial vault. The pneumocephalus resolved within 10 days with conservative measures. Although surgical obliteration of the fistula was discussed, the patient opted against surgical intervention.

CONCLUSION: Spontaneous or positive-pressure-induced pneumocephalus without a skull base defect should prompt investigation of alternative air-entry pathways, including enterothecal fistulas, particularly in patients with predisposing risk factors such as esophageal malignancy and dilations.

articles.title: Association of Cardiac Rehabilitation with Mortality after Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVI/SAVR): A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) treat severe aortic stenosis. Although cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves functional recovery, its association with mortality remains unclear. We aimed to assess this association in adults following TAVI or SAVR.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 17, 2026. We included randomized and observational studies comparing mortality after CR versus usual care following TAVI or SAVR. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Random-effects meta-analyses and exploratory meta-regressions were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 7 observational studies (n=178,525 participants) were included (six pooled; n=92,213), all focusing on all-cause mortality. Participants reported mean or median ages ranged from 67 to 83.9 years, with 37-66.7% women across studies. All studies were deemed to have a high methodological quality. Pooled results revealed that CR was associated with a lower all-cause mortality risk compared to control groups (HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.41-0.84], p=0.004; I2=95%). Sensitivity analyses yielded similar results, as did sub-analyses restricted to TAVI participants (HR 0.68 [95% CI 0.50-0.92], p=0.012). No sub-analysis could be performed for SAVR participants alone. Exploratory meta-regression analyses found no statistically significant associations between studies' characteristics (e.g., patients' age, CR duration, follow-up length) and effect estimates (all p>0.05), although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of studies.

CONCLUSION: Participation in CR after TAVI/SAVR is associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Future studies should determine whether participants' or interventions' characteristics modulate these effects.

articles.title: Sustainability in Healthcare: A Delphi Consensus Study on Practices, Barriers, and Improvement Strategies among Nurses in the United Arab Emirates.
articles.abstract: Sustainability is increasingly recognized as a priority in healthcare, yet most available evidence addresses the organizational level, with limited insight into how nurses themselves perceive sustainability in their daily practice. Identifying these perceptions is a necessary first step for planning improvement efforts, particularly in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where nurse-specific evidence remains scarce and sustainability in healthcare faces significant challenges. This study aimed to identify nurses' perspectives on current sustainability and non-sustainability-aligned practices in UAE healthcare settings, the barriers to sustainable practice, and strategies for improvement. A two-round Delphi study was conducted among nurses practicing in the UAE. In Round 1, open-ended questions identified sustainability and non-sustainability-aligned practices, barriers, and improvement suggestions, which were thematically grouped into 45 statements. In Round 2, participants rated their agreement with each statement using a five-point Likert scale, with ≥70% agreement defining consensus. In the findings, all 45 statements achieved consensus, with agreement levels ranging from 81.4% to 95.1%. Participants mostly identified sustainability with actions involving waste segregation, recycling, conservation of resources and energy, and digitalization, whether applied or not; meanwhile, excessive use of disposable items (such as gloves, syringes, infusion bags, and masks) had an agreement level of 88.2% as an unsustainable action. The highest overall agreement concerned the cost of implementing sustainable technologies as a barrier (95.1%). Suggestions for improvement that included training of employees, policy implementation, and the use of renewable sources of energy likewise garnered significant agreement (85.3%-91.2%). Findings were largely concerned with issues relating to the environment and resources, and less so with social, educational, and workforce continuity aspects of sustainability. In conclusion, sustainability among nurses working in UAE healthcare facilities is viewed mainly in terms of waste management, resource conservation, and the use of fewer disposable materials. These priorities and barriers were consensually identified by nurses and provide an initial framework for sustainability projects based on nurses' views, but sustainable development will also need to address other aspects, including workforce, social, and knowledge-based elements, in addition to environmental ones. Further research needs to explore the actual implementation of these priorities and barriers and sustainability of changes over time.

articles.title: Effects of Functional Visuo-Proprioceptive Stimulation on Upper- and Lower-Limb Motor Impairment After Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional proprioceptive stimulation (FPS), combining coordinated vibratory stimulation with synchronized visual feedback, may facilitate motor recovery after stroke; however, the effects of multi-joint visuo-proprioceptive stimulation on upper- and lower-limb impairment remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of FPS on upper- and lower-limb motor impairment in individuals with subacute stroke and examine movement-related perceptual responses.

METHODS: In this single-center, 2 × 2 crossover randomized controlled trial, 25 inpatients with subacute stroke were enrolled; 21 completed the study. Participants received upper- and lower-limb FPS in random order, with each intervention lasting 2 weeks (six 30-minute sessions) separated by a washout period. Motor impairment was assessed with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the upper extremity (FMA-UE) and Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the lower extremity (FMA-LE). After each session, participants rated movement-related perceptual responses.

RESULTS: Treatment × time interactions were significant for FMA-UE (F = 6.20; P = .015) and FMA-LE (F = 5.80; P = .019). Upper-limb FPS improved FMA-UE scores more than lower-limb FPS (7.22 vs 2.59 points). Lower-limb FPS improved FMA-LE scores more than upper-limb FPS (2.23 vs 0.70 points). Movement-related perceptual response ratings increased across sessions. No carryover effects or adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: FPS was associated with reductions in motor impairment after upper- and lower-limb stimulation in subacute stroke, with stronger evidence for effects on the upper extremity. Upper-limb gains approximated reported minimal clinically important difference ranges for the FMA-UE, suggesting potential clinical relevance. Coordinated visuo-proprioceptive stimulation may be a feasible rehabilitation adjunct that warrants further investigation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000041284.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary vascular disease, and right ventricular adaptation in transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexists with pulmonary hypertension (PH), which is associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). However, the prognostic impact of PH subtypes and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) thresholds in this setting remains insufficiently defined. We evaluated guideline-based PH classifications and their association with outcomes in a large real-world TTVI cohort.

METHODS: In an international multicenter registry, 903 patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI underwent pre-procedural right heart catheterization and were followed for up to two years. PH was defined as mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg, and PVR was stratified according to guideline thresholds. Endpoints included procedural success, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: PH was present in 88% of patients; among patients with PH, median PVR was 2.7 WU. A pre-capillary component (PVR >2 WU) was observed in 68%, including 13% with PVR >5 WU. Procedural success was 81%. NYHA functional class improved significantly from baseline to follow-up irrespective of PH status or PVR. Mortality increased with PH and higher PVR. A PVR threshold of >2 WU alone did not discriminate survival, whereas PVR >5 WU identified a high-risk phenotype. An integrated classification combining PH status, PVR >5 WU, and RV-PA uncoupling (TAPSE/PASP <0.30 mm/mmHg) provided effective prognostic stratification.

CONCLUSION: High procedural success and symptomatic improvement were observed following TTVI across PH subgroups. Although infrequent among TTVI patients, a PVR >5 WU identifies a high-risk phenotype with increased mortality. Comprehensive hemodynamic profiling improves risk stratification and may support patient counselling and informed decision-making.

articles.title: Ethical Decision-Making for TAVR in Very Elderly Patients: Beyond Chronological Age Toward Meaningful Clinical Benefit.
authors: de Almeida Palma da Fonseca JH
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has emerged as a transformative therapy for severe aortic stenosis, yet its application in very elderly patients raises complex clinical and ethical challenges. Chronological age alone is an inadequate basis for treatment selection. Patients of similar age may differ substantially in frailty, functional reserve, cognitive status, comorbidity burden and projected survival. Available evidence suggests that carefully selected nonagenarians can experience acceptable survival and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life after TAVR, although outcomes remain heterogeneous and are strongly influenced by factors beyond age. This review examines ethical decision-making for TAVR in very elderly patients through a patient-centered framework integrating projected survival, frailty, functional recovery, cognition, quality of life, and individual preferences. Particular attention is given to the concept of procedural futility and to the challenges of applying these principles in resource-constrained healthcare systems. Brazil is presented as an illustrative example of broader challenges shared by many low- and middle-income countries, including disparities in access, limited availability of multidisciplinary and palliative care, family-centered decision-making, and rapidly aging populations. A shift from chronological age toward expected survival with meaningful clinical benefit may provide a more clinically relevant approach to TAVR selection in advanced age.

articles.title: ERC advanced grant: moving cardiovascular prevention upstream of conception.
From Evidence to Everyday Practice: NASN's Year of Building for School Nurses.
articles.abstract: Meeting increasingly complex student health needs requires school nurses to have access to evidence-based education, foundational preparation, and trusted professional resources. This article highlights three NASN initiatives advanced in 2026: a comprehensive national curriculum for managing type 1 diabetes, the NASN Certificate Series™: Framework Essentials for School Nurses, and the development of NORA, the NASN Online Resource Assistant. Together, these initiatives connect clinical education, specialty orientation, and resource navigation to support school nurses throughout their professional journey. The article explores how these investments contribute to NASN's broader strategic priorities and a more connected system of professional support, with the goal of strengthening school nursing practice and improving student outcomes.

articles.title: Predictors of Recovery From Aphasia After Stroke.
articles.abstract: Predicting recovery from aphasia after stroke is challenging, yet essential. Accurate prognoses would enable stroke survivors and families to establish realistic expectations and make informed decisions, allow clinicians to plan rehabilitation, and inform the development and implementation of interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on predictors of aphasia recovery, integrating diverse biological, behavioral, environmental, and temporal determinants into a unified conceptual framework organized around 3 fundamental determinants: the integrity of the language network, neuroplasticity throughout the remaining brain, and the passage of time. Lesion location and extent are powerful predictors, accounting for more than half of the variance in aphasia outcomes, but other interacting factors contribute to heterogeneous recovery trajectories, including variability in language network organization and effects of diaschisis. The capacity for neuroplasticity depends on the brain health and functionality of surviving tissue, but the realization of this potential depends critically on engagement in language use, which can be promoted by intensive speech-language therapy, social participation and supportive communication environments. Recovery follows a predictable decelerating time course, with rapid early gains driven primarily by reperfusion and resolution of dysfunction in brain regions that support language, and modest but meaningful longer-term improvements deriving from neuroplastic changes. This framework provides a practical heuristic for understanding aphasia recovery, developing clinical prediction tools, and identifying modifiable factors to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: BAT Activation and Cardiometabolic Protection: Weighing Realities of Mechanistic Studies From Epidemiological Promises.
articles.abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a thermogenic organ that, per gram, consumes glucose and lipids at high rates and secretes endocrine factors (batokines) that act on liver, muscle, and the vasculature to modulate insulin sensitivity, lipid metabolism, and hemodynamic function. These features provide several plausible routes by which its activation could improve cardiometabolic health. Large retrospective cohorts have consistently found associations between the incidental uptake of the glucose analogue [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose in BAT with lower prevalence of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, cardiovascular disease, and impaired vascular function. Cold exposure and β-adrenergic agonism remain the best-established activators of human BAT metabolism and produce measurable improvements in insulin sensitivity and lipid profiles. Nevertheless, skeletal muscle, white adipose tissue, and the cardiovascular system are coactivated by the same stimuli, rendering difficult to isolate the independent contribution of BAT. This review aims to describe the mechanistic basis, the observational and interventional human evidence, and the safety considerations relevant to BAT as a cardiometabolic target and highlight the lack of specificity in directly targeting BAT thermogenesis to decipher its clinically meaningful impact on metabolic health in humans.

articles.title: Quality of Care and Outcomes Among American Indian and Alaska Native Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: Cardiovascular Health Insights From the American Heart Association Get With The Guidelines Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: American Indian and Alaska Native (AI/AN) patients in the US face a disproportionate burden of cardiovascular disease, yet data on the quality of care and outcomes in this population are limited. Using the American Heart Association's Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease registry, we evaluated the clinical profiles and use of evidence-based therapies among AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction compared with White patients.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 1955 AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction in 45 states participating in the Get With The Guidelines-Coronary Artery Disease program from 2017 to 2022. Six performance measures were evaluated: aspirin within 24 hours, β-blocker and statin at discharge, smoking cessation counseling, ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor/ARB (angiotensin II receptor blocker) for EF ≤40%, and antiplatelet therapy at discharge. Additional metrics included door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes for ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction, cardiac rehabilitation referral, GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) use for those with obesity and diabetes, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Compared with White patients, AI/AN patients with acute myocardial infarction were younger, with a higher prevalence of diabetes, obesity, and end-stage renal disease. Overall, the utilization of evidence-based medical therapies and smoking cessation counseling was similar. However, door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes for ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction was significantly lower for AI/AN patients (65.5% versus 76.2%; P<0.0001). Cardiac rehabilitation referral was also significantly lower for AI/AN patients (69.1% versus 72.9%; P<0.01). Adjusted in-hospital mortality was higher for AI/AN patients (adjusted odds ratio, 1.27 [95% CI, 1.03-1.56]; P=0.02) when adjusted for patient characteristics, but differences were attenuated after adjustment for hospital characteristics (adjusted odds ratio, 1.13 [95% CI, 0.88-1.47]).

CONCLUSIONS: AI/AN patients received similar evidence-based therapies as White patients, but disparities remain in cardiac rehabilitation referral and timely reperfusion. Differences in in-hospital mortality may be attributed to the types of hospitals where AI/AN patients receive care, indicating the need for targeted interventions to improve cardiovascular outcomes in these communities.

articles.title: Second-Line Antihypertensive Drugs and Risk of Microvascular Complications in Patients With Hypertension and Type 2 Diabetes Receiving Renin-Angiotensin System Inhibitors: A Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: More than half of the US adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) have hypertension. Some antihypertensive drugs, particularly thiazide(-like) diuretics (TDs) and β-blockers (BBs), are associated with hyperglycemia, yet long-term impact in patients with both conditions remains limited. We evaluated microvascular complication risk across second-line antihypertensive therapies following first-line renin-angiotensin system inhibitor use.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using a 15% random sample of nationwide Medicare Fee-for-Service claims from 2011 to 2020 was conducted to emulate a target trial among adults aged 65 years or older with concomitant hypertension and T2D. Two 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons were conducted: BBs versus calcium channel blockers (CCBs) and TDs versus CCBs, with matching based on demographic characteristics, index year, comorbidities, and concomitant medications. The primary outcome was a composite of diabetic nephropathy, diabetic retinopathy, and diabetic neuropathy identified by International Classification of Diseases diagnosis codes. Patients were followed until the earliest occurrence of new-onset microvascular complication and were censored at disenrollment, death, or study end. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: A total of 27 395 patients were included. In the BBs versus CCBs and TDs versus CCBs cohorts, the mean age was 76 and 75; 40.3% and 39.1% were men, and 8.6% and 11.0% were Black patients. The incidence rates of microvascular complications were 8.89 and 8.33 per 100 person-years among BB and CCB users, respectively, and 7.85 and 7.95 per 100 person-years among TD and CCB users, respectively. Compared with CCB, BB (hazard ratio, 1.07 [95% CI, 1.00-1.14]) was associated with higher risk of microvascular complications, although the risk for TDs (hazard ratio, 0.99 [95% CI, 0.93-1.05]) was nonsignificant.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with CCBs, BBs were associated with modestly higher risk of microvascular complications, although no association was observed for TDs.

articles.title: Retrograde Approach for Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Young Patients Post-Arterial Switch Operation: A Case Series.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: We report the cases of three young patients presenting with chronic total occlusions (CTO) affecting reimplanted coronary arteries following arterial switch operation (ASO), who were treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) using the retrograde approach. Despite the unique procedural challenges posed by reimplanted coronary vessels, retrograde PCI was technically successful in all cases. This series highlights the potential role of PCI in a population traditionally managed with surgical revascularization and underscores the importance of increasing awareness of CTO PCI within pediatric and congenital cardiology teams. Finally, it raises critical considerations regarding the optimal timing of intervention, balancing procedural feasibility, growth-related anatomical challenges, and the potential consequences of long-lasting coronary occlusion.

articles.title: Greater social support is associated with less impairment in activities of daily living among older adults undergoing first percutaneous coronary intervention.
Skeletal Outcomes from Parathyroidectomy Versus Cinacalcet for Secondary Hyperparathyroidism in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Bone loss and fractures are complications of secondary hyperparathyroidism (sHPT). Parathyroidectomy (PTX) is an effective procedure that can improve skeletal outcomes. Calcimimetics therapy also improves biochemical control, but direct comparisons with PTX on bone outcomes remain limited. We conducted a meta-analysis to compare skeletal outcomes between PTX and calcimimetics.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases for randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing PTX with cinacalcet and reporting fracture or bone mineral density (BMD) outcomes up to 5 March 2026. Summary effect estimates (relative risk (RR) for fracture outcomes and standardised mean difference (SMD) for BMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated.

RESULTS: We identified 2552 records, of which eight studies (two RCTs, six observational) were included. Five studies reported fracture outcomes. Pooled analyses showed a modestly lower fracture rate with cinacalcet than with PTX (random-effects model: RR = 0.90, 95% CI 0.81-0.99; common-effects model: RR 0.9 (0.81-1.00). However, this finding was largely driven by a single study. Three studies reported BMD outcomes. There was no difference in change in lumbar spine (SMD = -0.52 [-1.34 to 0.31]) or femoral neck BMD (SMD = -0.88 [-1.86 to 0.11]) between groups.

CONCLUSION: Although pooled fracture estimates favoured cinacalcet, no definitive evidence indicated a difference in fracture risk between cinacalcet and PTX. Cinacalcet and PTX demonstrated no statistically significant differences in BMD effects in patients with sHPT. This finding should be interpreted cautiously given confounding, selection bias, and heterogeneity between studies.

articles.title: Boron-doped carbon quantum dots as a novel fluorescent nanosensor for imeglimin determination: green synthesis, analytical validation, and plasma application.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Imeglimin (IMN) is a novel oral antidiabetic drug for the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is designed to enhance glycemic control by addressing mitochondrial bioenergetics. Ongoing monitoring of its concentration in biological fluids is essential to ensure therapeutic efficacy and to prevent potential adverse effects. In this study, a novel fluorescent sensing platform was developed using carbon quantum dots (CQDs) that were doped with boron (CQDs@B) through a microwave-assisted synthesis. The method's quantum yield was 31.15%, and the fluorescence response was recorded at 445 nm after excitation at 360 nm (borate buffer pH 7.8), with minimal signal interference from other coexisting excipients and all tested drugs (except apalutamide). The system demonstrated high sensitivity with a linear range between 6.0 and 200.0 ng mL-1, and a detection limit was as low as 1.83 ng mL-1. The practical performance of the sensor was confirmed by analyzing IMN in spiked plasma samples, showcasing its potential for real-world biomedical applications. These results endorse the application of this eco-friendly nanoprobe in therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical diagnostics.

articles.title: 18F radiolabeled Tb-Gd codoped LaF3 nanoparticles as trimodal probes for PET/MRI/photoluminescence.
articles.abstract: Lanthanide fluoride nanoparticles (LnF3 NPs) are promising candidates for multimodal imaging. Here, we report the use of hybrid LnF3 nanoparticles as trimodal probes for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography (PET), and optical imaging using chromophoric antennae for their efficient photosensibilization. Hybrid GdxTbyLa1-x-yF3 nanoparticles with varying compositions were synthesised as well as their analogues doped with 18F as a radiotracer. Their structure and composition were characterized in the solid state and in aqueous solution. Their colloidal stability was also monitored, using dynamic light scattering, zeta potential measurements along with computed tomography. Their photophysical properties were investigated, as a function of Ln(III) core composition and ligand capping. A composition-dependent structural transition was observed: nanoparticles containing at least 30% La(III) adopt a hexagonal phase with spherical morphologies (20-30 nm) and show enhanced Tb(III) luminescence through antenna sensitization, whereas lower La(III) contents favour an orthorhombic phase with weaker emission. Magnetic studies showed that longitudinal relaxivity decreases as Gd(III) + Tb(III) content increases, while transverse relaxivity depends mostly on magnetic susceptibility, allowing the tuning between T1- and T2- weighted MRI contrast. Efficient 18F incorporation was achieved with radiochemical yields ranging from 67% to 86%, enabling robust PET imaging. Finally, the NP dispersions were successfully detected using MRI and PET/CT, and exhibited bright emission visible with the naked eye, demonstrating their potential as a versatile platform for next-generation multimodal contrast agents.

articles.title: Developing a Pragmatic Framework for Assessing Unexplained Falls in Older Adults: A Multidisciplinary Delphi Study.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: BackgroundFalls in older adults are a major public health concern, and their etiology may remain unclear after initial evaluation. Unexplained falls represent a clinical situation in which no clear explanation is identified following the initial assessment and may require a structured diagnostic approach.ObjectiveTo develop a multidisciplinary framework for the initial assessment of unexplained falls in older adults.MethodsA modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with nine experts in geriatrics, cardiology, neurology, ENT, and general practice. An initial list of 28 items derived from a targeted literature review was evaluated using a 5-point Likert scale. Items reaching consensus were retained, while items not reaching consensus were excluded or discussed and reformulated before re-rating.ResultsThe final consensus identified 16 key items across three domains: case history, clinical examination, and targeted investigations. Cardiovascular, neurological, vestibular, and iatrogenic factors were central to the assessment. Experts emphasized clinical reasoning and targeted investigations rather than exhaustive testing. Cardiovascular assessment, specialist referral when indicated, and medication review were considered essential components of care.

articles.title: May the haemodynamic force be with you: Promise and challenges in preclinical small rodent assessment.
Consensus-Based Diagnostic Criteria for Parsonage-Turner Syndrome/Neuralgic Amyotrophy: A Modified Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/AIMS: Parsonage-Turner syndrome (PTS), also known as neuralgic amyotrophy (NA), is an acute-onset peripheral neuropathy predominately affecting the upper extremity and causing substantial pain and disability. No formal international consensus-based diagnostic criteria exist, contributing to diagnostic delays, inconsistent terminology, and limited ability to collate and systematically analyze data. This study aimed to develop consensus-based diagnostic criteria and a diagnostic algorithm for PTS/NA.

METHODS: A modified Delphi study was conducted with an international, multidisciplinary panel of experts selected based on clinical and research experience with PTS/NA. A steering committee drafted preliminary statements informed by a literature review and panelist-derived diagnostic challenges across 9 domains. Two electronic survey rounds used Likert-scale and binary response formats, with consensus defined as ≥ 75% agreement or disagreement.

RESULTS: All 13 panelists completed both rounds (100% response rate). Of 86 items, 52 (60%) reached agreement. The panel endorsed "Parsonage-Turner syndrome" and "neuralgic amyotrophy" as interchangeable terms. Classic PTS/NA was defined by acute-onset severe pain (≥ 7/10) and severe weakness in a non-myotomal distribution. Non-classic presentations warranted confirmatory electrodiagnostic testing and/or nerve-focused imaging. Hourglass-like nerve constrictions were considered likely pathognomonic (100% agreement). If steroids were considered, early initiation was recommended in classic presentations, even before confirmatory testing.

DISCUSSION: These criteria may shorten time to diagnosis, standardize terminology, guide resource utilization, and facilitate clinical trials. Future research should prioritize validation of the criteria in patient cohorts.

articles.title: Soluble receptors for advanced glycation end products is associated with cardiac mortality among patients with stable ischemic heart disease: long-term follow-up of the LAERTES study.
articles.journal: Biomarkers : biochemical indicators of exposure, response, and susceptibility to chemicals
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It has been suggested that circulating levels of the soluble receptor for advanced glycation end products (sRAGE) is a biomarker of underlying inflammation. There is limited data regarding its prognostic value in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD). We explored the long-term prognostic value of sRAGE levels on cardiac mortality in patients with CAD.

METHODS: This is a retrospective analysis from LAERTES Study. Serum sRAGE levels were measured at baseline. sRAGE were quantified using DuoSetELISA kit. Primary endpoint was cardiac death and secondary endpoint the composite of non-fatal acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and ischemic stroke.

RESULTS: Data were obtained from 800 patients (13% female, median age 62 years, median follow-up 6 years) of whom 76 died from cardiac death, 84 experienced ACS and 12 had ischemic stroke. Patients with cardiac death were older and had more comorbidities. sRAGE levels were predictive of cardiac death and remained an independent predictor for cardiac death (HR: 1.31, 95% CI: 1.03-1.67, p = 0.027) after adjustment for traditional risk factors and left ventricular ejection fraction. sRAGE levels could not predict the secondary endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher sRAGE levels are independently associated with cardiac mortality among CAD patients.

articles.title: Self-Calibrating Fluorescence-Exclusion Microfluidic Platform for 3D Topographic Profiling of Living Cell Monolayers.
articles.abstract: Cell monolayers are active living matter whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture and mechanical remodeling regulate tissue function, yet fast and continuous topographic monitoring remains difficult. Here, we present fluorescence exclusion microscopy for monolayers (FLEXOM), a microfluidic platform combining multilayer micropillar arrays with negative-staining optics to convert wide-field images into self-calibrated 3D height maps. Geometry-anchored cavities allow in-frame self-calibration at confluence, correcting global intensity variations shared by sample and reference regions. FLEXOM enables longitudinal 3D profiling from isolated cells to confluent sheets with sub-second temporal resolution, sub-micrometer temporal height precision, and multiday biocompatibility and operational stability. FLEXOM reveals two distinct anisotropic signatures. First, monolayers show distinct cell type-dependent vertical thickness profiles despite comparable lateral footprints. Two vertical descriptors, mean height and within-cell height standard deviation, distinguish cell types more accurately than nine two-dimensional (2D) lateral descriptors.
