Second, under acute osmotic shock, diverse confluent cell monolayers exhibit geometrically anisotropic vertical-lateral remodeling. Under hypotonic stimulation, projected area changes lag behind height changes. Consistent with this lag, cyclic hypotonic-isotonic switching at 3-min intervals produces predominantly vertical remodeling with limited cycle-dependent lateral changes. Our work provides a high-resolution 3D profiling tool and a framework for axis-resolved analysis of topographic responses in active living matter.

articles.title: FOXM1-induced TRIM9 inhibits neutrophil extracellular traps formation to attenuate cerebral I/R injury via STING/AMPK axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major challenge in stroke management, with neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) playing a key role in exacerbating damage. This study aimed to elucidate the function and mechanism of FOXM1 in cerebral I/R injury.

METHODS: A mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in bEnd.3 endothelial cells were established. NETs formation was assessed by detecting MPO-DNA complexes, H3Cit, and neutrophil elastase. Inflammatory cytokines were evaluated using RT-qPCR, and protein stability was assessed by cycloheximide chase assay. Molecular interactions were examined using chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and dual luciferase reporter assay.

RESULTS: FOXM1 was downregulated following I/R. FOXM1 overexpression reduced infarct volume, edema, and NETs formation in MCAO mice. In vitro, FOXM1 upregulation attenuated endothelial injury in OGD/R-stimulated bEnd.3 cells and decreased the release of NETs markers. Mechanistically, FOXM1 directly bound to the promoter of TRIM9 and activated its transcription. TRIM9 subsequently promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of HMGB1, thereby influencing STING/AMPK signaling and reducing NETs formation. Knockdown of either TRIM9 or FOXM1 partially reversed the effects of HMGB1 depletion on NETs formation.

CONCLUSION: FOXM1 overexpression ameliorated cerebral I/R injury by enhancing TRIM9 expression, which suppressed NETs formation through HMGB1-modulated STING/AMPK signaling.

articles.title: Approaches to the Management of Splenomegaly and Hypersplenism in Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Disease: A Review and Recommendations for Surgical and Minimally Invasive Interventions.
articles.abstract: The spleen is essential for hematologic and immune homeostasis. In hemoglobinopathies such as thalassemia and sickle cell disease (SCD), splenomegaly and hypersplenism are common complications that cause cytopenias, increased transfusion requirements, and significant morbidity. This review evaluates non-pharmacological interventions for managing splenomegaly in these populations. Total splenectomy reduces transfusion needs and resolves hypersplenism but carries significant long-term risks, including overwhelming post-splenectomy infection (OPSI), thromboembolic events, and pulmonary hypertension. Partial splenectomy preserves immune function by retaining ≥25% of splenic tissue, though benefits may be temporary because of remnant regrowth. Partial splenic embolization (PSE) reduces transfusion dependence while preserving splenic immunity and is suitable for non-surgical candidates, with post-embolization syndrome and, rarely, abscess formation as complications. Splenic radiofrequency ablation (RFA) offers modest hematologic improvements and a favorable safety profile but has limited published data, particularly in SCD. Splenic irradiation (SI) is primarily palliative and lacks robust evidence in benign hemoglobinopathies. Managing splenomegaly in thalassemia and SCD requires an individualized approach. While total splenectomy provides definitive results, the high risk of long-term complications warrants careful consideration. Spleen-preserving strategies, particularly partial splenectomy and partial splenic embolization, offer a balanced approach by mitigating hypersplenism while preserving crucial immune function. Minimally invasive techniques such as RFA show promise but require further investigation. Treatment decisions should be tailored to the patient's clinical condition, disease severity, and available healthcare resources.

articles.title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology.
articles.abstract: Imperceptible skin electronic interfaces for bidirectional communication are essential for next‑generation healthcare and human-machine interfaces. The long‑standing absence of an ideal interfacing material has made it challenging to achieve high‑quality bidirectional electrophysiology without disturbing innate perception. Inspired by the human stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, we report a metallic stratum corneum (MSC): a synthetic mesohydrous gel reinforced with a silver nanowire network. MSC achieves > 106 S m-1 conductivity, dual‑mode (electronic/ionic) conduction, sub-micron thickness, and months‑long ambient stability. Its porous ultrathin architecture enables multidimensional imperceptibility (tactile, mechanical, thermal, and vapor‑permeable). MSC records electrophysiology with signal‑to‑noise ratio surpassing commercial gel electrodes, delivers efficient neuromuscular stimulation, and forms high‑resolution electrode arrays for spatiotemporal muscle mapping. By reconciling electronic performance, skin compatibility, and imperceptibility, the mesohydrous gel establishes a promising material platform for next-generation on-skin bioelectronics.

articles.title: Adrenal Vein Sampling: Impact of Intraprocedural Sedation on Cortisol Levels and the Point-Of-Care Quick Cortisol Assay Kit.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation oncology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adrenal vein sampling (AVS) is routinely performed to subtype primary aldosteronism, a common cause of secondary hypertension. Many radiologists administer intravenous sedation during lengthy AVS procedures. The aim of this retrospective study was to determine the impact of sedation on cortisol measurements in AVS.

METHODS: Adults who underwent successful AVS with intraprocedural sedation (both midazolam and fentanyl) in 2023 were included. Patients who received alternate sedation or had unsuccessful AVS were excluded. Adrenal and peripheral vein cortisol and aldosterone levels were recorded pre and post sedation, with the Selectivity index (SI) calculated. The number of adrenal vein samples with cortisol levels below 828 nmol/L (threshold for positive Point-of-care Quick-Cortisol Assay (POC-QCA)) was also recorded. Cortisol, aldosterone and selectivity index were compared using median, interquartile range and one-tail paired t-test. Fischer exact test was used to compare the number of negative POC-QCA.

RESULTS: Fifty patients (52% male, mean age 51.3) were included. Following sedation, mean adrenal vein cortisol levels decreased significantly on both the right (2325.5 to 1018.5 nmol/L; p = 0.00012) and left (1659 to 933 nmol/L; p = 0.0020). Median SI also decreased significantly on the right (10.60 to 4.99; p = 0.00041) and left (6.99 to 3.93; p = 0.0012). There was a 90% increase in adrenal vein samples below the POC-QCA threshold (p-value = 0.0038).

CONCLUSION: Intraprocedural sedation had a significant impact on adrenal vein cortisol levels, which in turn impacts the SI. Interpretation of cannulation success following intravenous sedation based on POC-QCA or laboratory-measured cortisol requires care.

articles.title: Vesicle-Surface Recognition Coupled with Graphdiyne-zyme Arrays for Marker-Independent Colorimetric Fingerprinting of Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles.
articles.abstract: Bacterial extracellular vesicles (bEVs) that encode disease-relevant molecular information are released into body fluids at early stages of infection, rendering them promising biomarkers for early diagnosis. However, the lack of universal surface markers causes limitation of conventional antibody-based strategies, severely restricting the use of bEVs for early diagnosis. Here, we report a marker-independent recognition strategy that translates the interfacial heterogeneity of bEV membranes into amplified catalytic signatures. Graphdiyne-zyme sensor arrays are designed and constructed, in which the graphdiyne spatially fixes and organizes three kinds of metal oxides to form multiple nanozymes with confined, multivalent catalytic interfaces. By coupling vesicle-surface recognition with graphdiyne-zyme arrays, the interfaces efficiently transform subtle membrane variations into distinct colorimetric fingerprints. The graphdiyne-zyme array generated distinguishable colorimetric fingerprints for bEVs from six UTI-associated bacterial species and, when integrated with an XGBoost classifier, achieved an accuracy of 96.9% in a clinical test set comprising 32 samples. This study establishes an analytical framework for the marker-independent recognition of bEVs, delivering an alternative approach to replace conventional affinity-based biosensing strategies.

articles.title: Complementary Single-Cell Microflow HILIC and Ion Pair LC-MS Reveal Bystander Metabolic Effects in a Macrophage Model of Tuberculosis.
articles.abstract: Single-cell metabolomics remains analytically challenging due to the low abundance and chemical diversity of metabolites in individual cells. We have developed complementary microflow hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) and ion pair (IP) liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) methods to expand metabolite coverage in single macrophages. Ion pair LC-MS was applied to single cells for the first time, enabling retention of highly polar and ionic metabolites that elute early under conventional reversed-phase conditions. Across Mycobacterium bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-infected, uninfected bystander, and control-unexposed THP-1 macrophages, both microflow methods detected significantly more features than a previously reported analytical-flow HILIC method. The two microflow methods provided complementary chemical space, together yielding 633 unique name-annotated metabolites with MS2 spectra. This depth enabled pathway-level interpretation at single-cell resolution, revealing infection-associated changes in purine-, arginine-, glutathione-, and one-carbon folate-associated metabolism. Metabolite-level interrogation indicated shared purine and amino acid changes in both infected and neighboring macrophages, while a potential bystander phenotype arose, characterized by elevated glycine and heterogeneous adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels. Finally, we demonstrate sequential IP and HILIC analysis of the same single cell, establishing a route toward maximal coverage from individual cells. These results position microflow HILIC and IP LC-MS as powerful, orthogonal strategies for advancing single-cell metabolomics and unveiling heterogeneity within complex biological microenvironments.

articles.title: An Asymmetric Input Precondition-Gated AND DNA Circuit for Dual-Mutation Analysis.
articles.abstract: DNA molecular logic gates typically treat multiple inputs as equal-status Boolean variables, making it difficult to handle the inherent temporal priorities and weight disparities of signals in real biological networks. Here we report a precondition-gated asymmetric AND molecular circuit that achieves logic discrimination of two unequal-weight inputs within a dual-DNAzyme cascade framework. A prerequisite input undergoes signal accumulation through autocatalytic positive feedback, and the resulting gating molecule grants detection access to the secondary input pathway via a de-inhibition mechanism, ensuring that the system responds to the secondary input only after the prerequisite condition is satisfied. A dissipative cycle embedded in the secondary pathway further endows the circuit with chemical renewability after a single response. This design extends conventional AND logic from a condition of spatial co-existence to one governed by priority. Using this circuit for the combined detection of low-prevalence amoxicillin resistance-associated mutations and high-prevalence clarithromycin resistance-associated mutations in Helicobacter pylori infection, as demonstrated in simulated clinical specimens, the system produces a positive output only when both resistance-associated mutations are present, mirroring the decision logic for dual resistance status. This precondition-gated asymmetric AND circuit provides an expandable molecular platform for advancing DNA molecular computation from static combinational logic toward dynamic logic.

articles.title: The Evolution of Craniosynostosis Surgery Research: Global Trends, Collaboration, and Emerging Themes.
articles.abstract: Craniosynostosis surgery has evolved substantially with the introduction of cranial vault remodeling, minimally invasive endoscopic techniques, distraction osteogenesis, and advanced operative planning. Prior bibliometric studies have examined craniosynostosis broadly and nonsyndromic craniosynostosis specifically, but the surgery-focused literature remains incompletely characterized. We analyzed the global literature on craniosynostosis surgery in the Web of Science Core Collection. The search, performed on June 13, 2026, yielded 2517 records. Publication output increased gradually before accelerating in the late 1990s and peaking in 2021. Research articles comprised 2128 records (84.55%). Surgery was the leading Web of Science category (n=2097), followed by clinical neurology (n=624), pediatrics (n=477), and dentistry, oral surgery and medicine (n=320). The United States contributed the most publications (n=1251), followed by Japan (n=157), England (n=153), and Germany (n=105). The University of Pennsylvania was the most productive organization in the retrieved dataset. Keyword overlay mapping highlighted craniosynostosis, distraction osteogenesis, and craniofacial surgery, with more recent average publication years for terms including craniofacial, cranial vault remodeling, and syndromic craniosynostosis. The surgery-focused craniosynostosis literature has expanded substantially and is concentrated in a limited number of countries and academic centers. Continued international collaboration and standardized outcome reporting may strengthen future research.

articles.title: High seroprevalence of anti-Toxocara IgG but no detectable association with epilepsy: a community-based case-control study in Southern Nigeria.
articles.abstract: Human toxocariasis, caused by migrating larval stages of Toxocara canis and T. cati, is a common zoonotic helminth infection worldwide and has been proposed as a contributor to epileptogenesis. This exploratory community-based case-control study assessed anti-Toxocara IgG seroprevalence (a marker of past exposure), factors associated with seropositivity, and the association between seropositivity and epilepsy in Southern Nigeria. Between September and December 2023, 23,027 residents of five communities were screened door-to-door with a validated epilepsy questionnaire. Sera from 40 neurologist-confirmed cases and 38 community controls were tested by western blot using T. canis larval excretory-secretory antigens. Of 78 participants, 68 were seropositive (87.2%; 95% CI 78.0-92.9), a figure for a selected sample, not community prevalence. Seropositivity was 85.0% (34/40) in persons with epilepsy and 89.5% (34/38) in controls (crude OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.17-2.58; p = 0.738; age-adjusted OR 1.18, 95% CI 0.26-5.45). With control seroprevalence near 90%, power was low: no significant association was detected, but one cannot be excluded. Older age (p = 0.026) and two hand-hygiene practices (p = 0.041, p = 0.013; unexpected direction) were associated with seropositivity in univariate analysis; given only ten seronegative participants and 19 uncorrected comparisons, the hygiene associations are probably spurious. Anti-cysticercal IgG (12.8%) likewise did not differ by epilepsy status. Anti-Toxocara seropositivity is near-universal in these communities, and peripheral serology has little discriminatory value for epilepsy in such settings; larger studies using neuroimaging, EEG and CNS-directed laboratory measures are needed.

articles.title: Interactions between HIV and steatotic liver disease-associated genetic variants on incident cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic liver disease due to steatotic liver disease (SLD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in people with HIV (PWH). Common single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) increase SLD risk and severity, but it remains unknown whether they have a differential effect on liver disease progression in PWH.

METHODS: Participants in the Veterans Affairs Million Veteran Program without viral hepatitis or prevalent cirrhosis were eligible. We evaluated cirrhosis incidence according to the number of SLD risk alleles in PNPLA3, MBOAT7, TM6SF2, and GCKR in PWH and people without HIV (PWoH). We estimated independent and interactive effects of HIV and each SNP on incident cirrhosis using Cox regression models.

RESULTS: Among 2,008 PWH, 61 developed cirrhosis (median follow-up 15.7 years). Among 590,764 PWoH, 17,395 developed cirrhosis (median follow-up 13.8 years). Unadjusted incidence rates of cirrhosis by number of risk alleles in PNPLA3, TM6SF2, and GCKR demonstrated dose-response relationships, while MBOAT7 exhibited a dominant effect. In adjusted models, risk allele number in PNPLA3 (HR 1.47, 95% CI 1.43-1.50), MBOAT7 (HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09), TM6SF2 (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.30-1.40), and GCKR (HR 1.07, 95% CI 1.05-1.09) was associated with incident cirrhosis. There was a positive interaction between HIV and number of risk alleles in GCKR (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.06-2.15).

CONCLUSIONS: Genetic predisposition to SLD modifies cirrhosis risk. A common variant in GCKR demonstrates differential effects on cirrhosis risk in PWH compared to PWoH. To improve liver outcomes, precision-based strategies incorporating both HIV status and genetic susceptibility require further study.

articles.title: The Great Masquerader: A Case Series Unveiling the Diverse Presentations of Abdominal Tuberculosis in a Middle Eastern Tertiary Hospital.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Abdominal tuberculosis (TB) remains a diagnostic challenge because of its diverse clinical manifestations and ability to mimic other surgical conditions. The global burden of TB, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, further compounds this diagnostic challenge. Delayed diagnosis contributes to substantial morbidity, especially in regions where TB is endemic. CASE REPORT This case series highlights 4 distinct presentations of abdominal TB, emphasizing early recognition and multidisciplinary management. The diagnosis was established or considered presumptively based on a combination of clinical assessment, radiological findings, intraoperative observations, microbiological testing, and histopathological examination. Despite standard anti-tuberculous therapy initiation in all patients, 2 experienced progressive clinical deterioration and subsequently died. The cases included: 1. Ileocecal TB causing small bowel obstruction with terminal ileal perforation in a patient previously treated with intravesical Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) therapy for bladder cancer, in whom disseminated BCG infection could not be definitively distinguished from Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. 2. Retroperitoneal TB presenting as a cystic mass initially suspected to represent an ovarian cyst or soft tissue neoplasm. 3. Peritoneal TB mimicking recurrent peritoneal metastases in a patient with a history of colorectal cancer, in whom TB polymerase chain reaction and acid-fast bacilli staining results were negative; histopathology and multidisciplinary assessment supported a presumptive diagnosis. 4. A retroperitoneal tuberculous abscess with vertebral involvement requiring percutaneous drainage and microbiological confirmation. CONCLUSIONS This case series underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for abdominal TB, particularly when clinical and radiological findings mimic malignancy. Histopathological assessment and multidisciplinary collaboration remain essential when microbiological investigations are inconclusive.

articles.title: Lee Silverman Voice Treatment-BIG Group Therapy Effects on Motor Function, Occupational Performance, Activities of Daily Living, Depression, and Quality of Life in Patients With Stroke.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND This study investigated the additional effects of Lee Silverman Voice Treatment-BIG (LSVT-BIG) group therapy when combined with conventional rehabilitation on motor function in patients with stroke. Occupational performance, activities of daily living, depression, and quality of life were secondary outcomes. MATERIAL AND METHODS Sixteen patients were randomly assigned to an experimental (n=8) or control group (n=8). Both groups received conventional occupational and physical therapy; the experimental group additionally received LSVT-BIG group therapy (60 minutes/session, 4 consecutive days/week for 4 weeks, for 16 total sessions). Assessments included the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), Manual Function Test (MFT), Korean version of the Fugl-Meyer Assessment (K-FMA), Functional Reach Test (FRT), 10-meter walk test (10MWT), Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM), Korean-Modified Barthel Index (K-MBI), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life (SS-QOL). Between-group differences in change scores were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. RESULTS Within-group analysis showed significant improvements in selected MAS subdomains, MFT, K-FMA, FRT, 10MWT, COPM, BDI, and SS-QOL; K-MBI did not improve significantly. Between-group comparisons showed significant differences in selected MAS, MFT, and K-FMA domains, 10MWT, COPM, and SS-QOL, but not FRT, K-MBI, or BDI. Analyses were exploratory and not adjusted for multiple comparisons. CONCLUSIONS The addition of group-delivered LSVT-BIG to conventional rehabilitation was associated with preliminary, domain-specific differences in selected measures of motor function, occupational performance, and quality of life in hospitalized patients with stroke. However, significant differences were not observed across all assessed outcomes. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and exploratory analyses. Larger studies with clearly prioritized primary outcomes are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Interaction of Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites With Inflammatory Markers and Cellular Rejection in Patients With Advanced Heart Failure Treated With Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Gut microbiota-derived metabolites (GMDMs) are involved in the pathophysiology of heart failure (HF) and may play an important role in patients after orthotopic heart transplantation (Htx). This study aimed to evaluate key GMDMs and their relationship with inflammation and the occurrence of acute cellular rejection (ACR) in patients undergoing Htx. MATERIAL AND METHODS This was an observational study that enrolled consecutive patients qualified for Htx between June 2022 and November 2023. The study included 15 healthy volunteers, 20 patients undergoing non-Htx cardiac surgery, and 32 consecutive patients undergoing Htx. The GMDMs trimethylamine oxide (TMAO), indoxyl sulfate, and p-cresol sulfate were evaluated in the serum before the procedure and at 1, 3, and 6 months after procedure in the study and control groups. ACR was diagnosed using endomyocardial biopsies. RESULTS The study group consisted of 32 patients qualified for Htx (78% male, 52±11 years old). Baseline levels of TMAO (0.77 [0.52-1.45] ug/mL) and p-cresol sulfate (9.90 [4.03-18.21] ug/mL) were significantly higher than in the healthy control group (0.28 [0.15-0.51] ug/mL and 4.45 [0.79-8.35] ug/mL, respectively; all P<0.05). Significant correlations were found between TMAO and endothelin (ET-1), as well as with procalcitonin, at 1 and 6 months after Htx. The study group did not show significant changes in metabolites in the follow-up period. Despite GMDMs being higher in the ACR group, the differences did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS TMAO and p-cresol sulfate were increased in patients with advanced HF. Moreover, TMAO correlated with ET-1 and procalcitonin; however, there was no association between GMDMs and ACR incidence.

articles.title: Ketogenic and low-carbohydrate diets in cardiovascular prevention: can safety and efficacy coexist?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To assess whether low-carbohydrate and ketogenic diets achieve cardiometabolic efficacy while maintaining safety. Particular attention is paid to the quantity and quality of carbohydrate restriction and their replacement foods.

RECENT FINDINGS: Randomized trials show that short-term improvements in weight and glycemia diminish with longer follow-up, and lipid effects vary with the degree and quality of carbohydrate restriction and their replacement foods. Across 174 randomized trials, triglyceride reductions were similar across moderate-carbohydrate, low-carbohydrate, and ketogenic-carbohydrate diets, whereas LDL-C increases were progressively greater with increasing degrees of carbohydrate restriction. LDL-C responses are heterogeneous, and controlled feeding studies demonstrate increases in small LDL particles and ApoB with ketogenic diets. Substituting carbohydrates with plant protein and unsaturated fats improve triglycerides while lowering LDL-C and ApoB. Prospective cohort studies associate plant-derived low-carbohydrate patterns with lower cardiovascular risk. Clinical cardiovascular-event evidence remains observational.

SUMMARY: Carbohydrate restriction may be compatible with cardiovascular health, but safety and efficacy depend on the quantity and quality of carbohydrate restriction, their replacement foods, and individual lipoprotein response. Cardiovascular outcome trials are needed to determine metabolic and lipoprotein effects of carbohydrate restriction on cardiovascular events, but practical and financial barriers to conducting such trials are prohibitive.

articles.title: Itaconate: An Emerging Metabolic Regulator Linking Immunity and Ferroptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Itaconate, generated in activated myeloid cells by aconitate decarboxylase 1 (historically termed immune-responsive gene 1), coordinates immunometabolism, redox signalling and regulated cell death. Emerging evidence links this pathway to ferroptosis; however, interpretation is complicated by the frequent conflation of endogenous itaconate with exogenously administered native itaconate and electrophilic derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate and dimethyl itaconate.

METHODS: This review critically integrates the biosynthesis, transport and intercellular signalling of itaconate with its effects on ferroptosis. Evidence is examined across solute carrier family 7 member 11-dependent cystine uptake, glutathione supply, glutathione peroxidase 4 expression, stability and catalytic activity, iron-sulfur clusters, ferritinophagy, phospholipid remodelling, mitochondrial redox signalling and selective autophagy, distinguishing cell-autonomous effects in myeloid cells from cell-nonautonomous transfer to parenchymal and tumour cells.

RESULTS: The available evidence supports a context-dependent model: itaconate-related signalling can suppress ferroptosis and limit acute tissue injury, but may also preserve immunosuppressive myeloid populations or confer ferroptosis resistance on tumours; at high pharmacological exposures, selected compounds can instead promote ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical translation requires compound-resolved terminology, validated ferroptosis endpoints, cell-specific delivery, quantitative exposure and target-engagement biomarkers and careful assessment of infection- and tumour-related risks.

articles.title: When trauma triggers a storm: a case report of refractory status dystonicus in a child.
articles.abstract: Dystonia is a movement disorder characterized by sustained or intermittent muscle contractions that cause abnormal movements or postures. Status dystonicus (SD), also known as dystonic storm, is a rare but life-threatening neurological emergency that is often refractory to treatment. We describe the case of a 5-year-and-6-month-old boy who developed SD after severe traumatic brain injury. Initial neuroimaging revealed multiple intracranial hemorrhagic lesions, including basal ganglia involvement. He subsequently developed refractory generalized dystonia with laryngeal involvement, requiring prolonged sedation, mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, and gastrostomy. Despite stepwise treatment with pharmacological agents, including trihexyphenidyl, clonazepam, clonidine, and tetrabenazine, recurrent dystonic crises occurred when sedation was tapered. A multidisciplinary approach involving pediatric neurology, intensive care, nutrition, physiotherapy, and rehabilitation supported gradual recovery. The child was discharged after 38 days while receiving antidystonia medications, which were successfully tapered within 6 months, and he ultimately regained functional independence. This case emphasizes the importance of early recognition and intensive multimodal management of SD in children, particularly after traumatic brain injury with basal ganglia involvement. Timely interventions, including ventilatory support, tracheostomy, individualized pharmacotherapy, and structured rehabilitation, may be critical for survival and long-term recovery. Because standardized treatment protocols for pediatric SD are lacking, management should be tailored through a multidisciplinary approach.

articles.title: Pediatric comminuted frontal bone and zygomaticomaxillary complex fracture with facial lacerations in a 3-year-old girl: a case report.
articles.abstract: Pediatric craniofacial fractures are uncommon, particularly those involving the frontal bone and zygomaticomaxillary complex (ZMC), owing to the relative pliability and incomplete ossification of facial bones in young children. We report the case of a 3-year-old girl who sustained a comminuted frontal bone fracture and a ZMC fracture following a high-velocity road traffic accident. The patient presented with extensive facial lacerations, exposed bone, and multiple displaced fractures. Computed tomography confirmed a comminuted fracture of the frontal bone involving the anterior table and supraorbital rim, along with fractures of the zygomatic arch, infraorbital rim, and anterior maxillary wall. Definitive surgical management was performed within 48 hours of injury and consisted of open reduction and internal fixation using titanium mesh and low-profile miniplates through the existing lacerations. Serial neurological assessments demonstrated intact infraorbital and facial nerve function. The patient was followed for 1 year, after which the mesh was electively removed. No signs of infection, fibrosis, or abnormal bone development were observed. This case highlights that, in selected pediatric patients with severely comminuted craniofacial fractures, early diagnosis and temporary rigid fixation using titanium mesh, combined with planned elective removal, can provide stable reconstruction while minimizing potential growth disturbance and optimizing long-term functional and aesthetic outcomes.

articles.title: The electrochemical physiology of organelles.
articles.abstract: Membrane-bound organelles maintain distinct chemical environments that are essential for their specialized functions. Yet, while organelle morphology, protein composition and dynamics have been extensively characterized, very little was known about their lumenal microenvironment prior to work from our laboratory. Here, we chart the development of a chemical imaging approach that enabled the measurement of ions, reactive species and membrane potential within native organelles in living cells and organisms. These measurements reveal that organelles maintain characteristic ionic and electrical states, that populations of even a specific type of organelle can be chemically heterogeneous, and that lumenal ion levels change during organelle maturation or physiological events. Beyond simply defining the ionic milieu of organelle lumens, quantitative ion imaging revealed new ion transport mechanisms, demonstrated that cell surface ion channels are active in organelles, mapped reactive-species production at subcellular spatial resolution and linked organelle physiology to disease states and cellular behavior. Together, these findings reveal that organelles have electroal behaviour because they harbor transmembrane ion gradients, ion transporting proteins, and membrane potential. We discuss how this emerging view may illuminate inside-out signaling across organelle membranes and outline the technological advances required to move from static chemical maps toward real-time, single-organelle physiology in living systems.

articles.title: Pulsed Field Ablation Versus Thermal Ablation for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials With Reconstructed Time-to-Event Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) creates myocardial lesions with brief, nonthermal electrical pulses. We synthesized randomized comparisons of PFA with radiofrequency and cryoballoon ablation for pulmonary vein isolation in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through October 13, 2026. We included randomized trials enrolling adults with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and comparing PFA with thermal ablation. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios and mean differences. Leave-one-out and Baujat analyses examined sensitivity and heterogeneity. Time-to-event data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves. Four randomized trials, reported in 6 publications, enrolled 1396 participants. For 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia, the 4-trial analysis (n=1392) found no significant difference (risk ratio 1.04, 95% confidence interval, 0.92-1.17; P=0.374; I2=3.6%). Reconstructed data comprised 1368 participants and 423 recurrences. Estimated 12-month freedom from recurrence was 70.6% with PFA and 66.7% with thermal ablation (log-rank p=0.097; hazard ratio 0.84, 95% confidence interval, 0.70-1.02). Procedure time was numerically lower with PFA, but the pooled result was nonsignificant and heterogeneous. Fluoroscopy time did not differ significantly; left atrial dwell time was shorter with substantial heterogeneity. No safety outcome differed significantly, and no atrioesophageal fistulas were reported. Randomized evidence indicates similar short-term efficacy for PFA and thermal ablation. The reconstructed survival analysis favored PFA numerically but did not establish a difference.

articles.title: Otitic Hydrocephalus Revisited: Mastoiditis-associated Cerebral Sinovenous Thrombosis Masquerading as Pseudotumor Cerebri in 2 Children.
Addressing Pediatric Behavioral and Mental Health Concerns by Integrating Community Health Workers in a Primary Care Clinic: An Analysis of Goals and Progression toward Completion.
articles.journal: The Journal of ambulatory care management
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Community health workers (CHWs) demonstrate great promise in addressing inequities in access to child behavioral health services. We sought to understand the workflow of CHWs integrated into a pediatric primary care clinic by describing and quantifying the behavioral health service goals identified by families and examining the time it took CHWs to complete steps toward goals.

METHODS: Participants (N = 257) were families at an urban federally qualified health center who identified primary and secondary goals to address pediatric behavioral and mental health concerns with their CHWs. Information on goals and CHWs' workflows was extracted from electronic medical records. Steps towards goal completion were identified for each primary goal, in addition to a "target step," defined as the final step within the CHW's control. Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests were used to examine goal frequency and demographic differences in goals. Time to target step completion was described using medians and interquartile ranges.

RESULTS: The most common primary goals were attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder evaluation and treatment; autism evaluation; community-based behavioral health supportive services; and special education evaluations. Variations in the time to target step and completion were seen across goals, although there were uniformly substantial delays between target and goal completion steps.

CONCLUSIONS: This study is one of the first quantitative descriptions of the role CHWs play in addressing common child behavioral needs in pediatric primary care settings. Understanding the range of behavioral issues CHWs were involved in and the challenges they faced can provide valuable information for pediatric practices that are looking to engage CHWs to expand their behavioral capacity.

articles.title: Gaps in Insurance Coverage and Preventive Care Attendance Among Nonelderly Adults With Diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of ambulatory care management
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether past-year gaps in insurance coverage and year-round uninsurance were associated with lower attendance at preventive visits over the past year among nonelderly adults with diabetes.

METHODS: Using nationally representative data from the National Health Interview Survey (2020-2023), our analysis included all nonelderly adults (18-64 years) with a self-report of a diabetes diagnosis. Multivariable regression was employed to assess associations between health insurance coverage (continuous private, continuous public, coverage gap, or year-round uninsured) and receiving general preventive care visits or glycated hemoglobin (A1C) testing in the past year.

RESULTS: Our analytic sample had 4506 nonelderly adults with type I or II diabetes. The weighted analysis estimated that 58% were continuously insured by private insurance, 31% by public, 6% experienced a coverage gap, and 5% were continuously uninsured; 79% received preventive care visits while 94% received A1C testing. Compared with respondents with continuous private insurance, respondents who experienced a coverage gap had a decreased probability of preventive care visits (adjusted marginal effect: -0.09; 95% CI: -0.16, -0.01; p = .014), with the lowest probability among those who were continuously uninsured (adjusted marginal effect: -0.26; 95% CI: -0.35, -0.18; p < 0.001). Preventive care attendance did not vary between respondents with continuous public and private coverage. Similar patterns were observed for receipt of A1C testing.

CONCLUSIONS AND ACTION STEPS: Stable health insurance is essential for nonelderly adults with diabetes to regularly receive preventive and diabetes-related care. Policies aimed at reducing coverage gaps may improve chronic disease management.

articles.title: Monitoring of regional ventilation and ventilator-induced lung injury in pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (MoVe lupARDS): a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients suffering from a neonatal or paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (nARDS/pARDS) are faced with high rates of morbidity and mortality despite advances in lung-protective ventilation. Prolonged invasive mechanical ventilation (MV) bears the risk of ventilator-induced lung injury, making a personalized ventilator management essential. Positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) is a key driver for balancing between alveolar lung collapse, recruitment, and overdistension, but optimal individualized bedside adjustment of PEEP remains challenging. Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is a non-invasive, radiation-free bedside monitoring technique that allows real-time assessment of regional ventilation distribution and may support individualized PEEP titration. Data from adult ARDS populations illustrates that an EIT-guided and individualized PEEP strategy might improve morbidity and mortality in these patients. Evidence for this approach in nARDS/pARDS remains limited.

METHODS: The MoVe lupARDS is a prospective, single-center, randomized controlled superiority trial with a parallel-group design and a 1:1 allocation ratio. A total of 120 neonates, infants, and children with mild to severe nARDS/pARDS requiring prolonged invasive MV for more than 24 h will be eligible for study inclusion. Patients will be randomly allocated to either receive an individualized EIT-guided PEEP approach (intervention) or to receive a clinically guided PEEP strategy (control) according to in-hospital standards. Additional monitoring includes a daily echocardiography assessment, lung ultrasound score, and proteomics as well as biomarker profiling from blood and lung aspirates. The primary endpoint is ventilator-free days at day 28 (VFD-28). Secondary endpoints are as follows: duration of MV, VFD-14, duration of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, extubation failure, and in-hospital mortality.

DISCUSSION: This MoVe lupARDS study aims to determine whether an individualized EIT-guided PEEP improves clinical outcomes and reduces ventilator-induced lung injury in nARDS/pARDS. The results may provide important evidence for a personalized strategy for optimizing lung-protective ventilation and improving bedside longitudinal lung monitoring in this vulnerable patient population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Registry, DRKS00035447. Registered on 23 December 2024. https://drks.de/register/de/trial/DRKS00035447/preview .

articles.title: Environmental influences and implementation effectiveness of community-based hypertension management: a five-year natural experiment in Southwest China.
articles.journal: International journal for equity in health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension management poses significant challenges in regions experiencing rapid urbanization, particularly where healthcare resources vary substantially across urban and rural areas. Luzhou City's community-based hypertension management program, initiated in 2014 and gradually expanded city-wide, provides valuable insights into implementing chronic disease management in diverse socioeconomic settings. This study evaluates the program's effectiveness through a five-year natural experiment, examining detection rates, implementation patterns, and environmental and socioeconomic influences.

METHODS: We analyzed health examination data from seven districts and counties of Luzhou City (2019-2023), encompassing 122 townships and streets. Environmental data, including air pollutants, vegetation coverage, and meteorological parameters, were obtained from the Weijing Remote Sensing platform and National Tibetan Plateau Data Center. Spatial autocorrelation analysis and Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling were employed to assess program implementation patterns and environmental and socioeconomic influences on detection rates. Regular calibration of equipment and standardized training of healthcare providers ensured data quality.

RESULTS: City-wide hypertension detection rates increased from 21.60% in 2019 to 29.27% in 2023, with notable regional variations. Less economically developed counties demonstrated exceptional improvements, with Gulin and Luxian achieving the highest annual improvement rates (Estimated Annual Percentage Change [EAPC]: 10.57% and 10.22%, respectively). Middle-aged adults (45-49 years) showed the most substantial improvement (EAPC: 14.45%). Bayesian spatiotemporal modeling identified significant environmental and socioeconomic correlates: average temperature showed the strongest environmental association (RR = 1.0506 per 1 °C, 95% CrI: 1.0186-1.0850), followed by O₃ concentration (RR = 1.0224 per 1 µg/m³, 95% CrI: 1.0158-1.0314). GDP and urbanization rate were negatively associated with detection rates, while hospital bed density showed a positive association (RR = 1.0314 per 1 bed/1,000 population, 95% CrI: 1.0155-1.0521). Spatial analysis revealed persistent clustering patterns (Moran's I: 0.1889-0.2655, P < 0.05), indicating structural influences on program effectiveness.

CONCLUSIONS: The successful implementation of community-based hypertension management in resource-limited settings demonstrates the feasibility of reducing healthcare disparities through systematic approaches. The varying effectiveness across regions and age groups, coupled with significant environmental influences, indicates the importance of context-sensitive implementation strategies. These findings provide valuable guidance for chronic disease management in developing regions, emphasizing the potential for achieving health equity through well-structured community health programs.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Vertical Evacuation During a Flood Disaster at an Elderly Care Facility in Fukushima: Experience From Typhoon Yun-yeung (2023).
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract: Flooding disasters increasingly threaten residents of long-term care facilities, where external evacuation may pose substantial risks. During Typhoon Yun-yeung in September 2023, record-breaking rainfall caused severe flooding in Iwaki City, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan. Naraha Tokiwaen Geriatric Health Services Facility, located in a designated flood hazard zone, conducted an internal vertical evacuation after surrounding roads became impassable. Thirty-eight ground-floor residents, with a mean age of 85 years and mostly requiring moderate to full care, were relocated to the second floor using elevators within approximately 30 minutes. Despite concurrent COVID-19 cases on the upper floor, zoning and infection-control measures were implemented, and no injuries, acute medical deterioration, or secondary infections occurred. This case suggests that rapid vertical evacuation may represent a feasible risk-reduction strategy for frail residents during flood disasters when supported by prior preparedness, hazard-based planning, and coordinated staff response.

articles.title: Protocol-Aware Secondary Analysis of Archived NWB Current-Clamp Recordings: Feature Reportability, Stability, and Reproducibility.
articles.abstract: Reuse of archived electrophysiology data requires more than successful file parsing: measurements must also be supported by the protocol and acquisition structure from which they are derived. We developed a protocol-aware workflow for reproducible secondary analysis of intracellular current-clamp recordings stored in Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) format. The workflow performs exact acquisition-stimulus sweep pairing, technical-integrity quality control, protocol-family stratification, feature-specific computability and reportability assessment, sensitivity analysis, acquisition-sufficiency testing, and family-versus-pooled benchmarking while retaining data and code provenance. We evaluated the workflow on 177 independently identified marmoset cortical cells from DANDI:001776. All 9,651 candidate voltage-current records were exactly paired and passed the technical gates; 5,447 quality-controlled LongPulse sweeps formed 350 protocol families, of which 291 (83.1%) supported at least one primary-reportable feature. Endpoint reportability ranged from 48.9% to 63.7%. Passive cohort estimates were robust to tested analysis settings, whereas adaptation was more definition-sensitive and firing-rate-current slopes required broader current-level support. In multi-family cells, family-specific firing-rate-current slopes differed by more than 20% from pooled estimates in approximately 37% of eligible cells. These results show that NWB standardization alone does not establish analytical comparability. Explicit protocol context, reportability states, acquisition-sufficiency diagnostics, and provenance provide a reusable basis for auditable analysis and downstream computational modelling.

articles.title: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis: Current Therapeutic Limitations and a Critical Appraisal of Nanotechnology-based Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is a neglected parasitic skin infection transmitted by sand flies to humans and remains a major public health challenge in endemic regions with increasing spread into newly affected and previously non-endemic areas. The disease is characterized by disfiguring dermal lesions that can result in prolonged physical, psychological, and socioeconomic impacts. Despite its substantial global burden, therapeutic management of CL remains challenging owing to the absence of effective vaccines, inadequate efficacy and toxicity of currently used drugs, and emergence of drug-resistant Leishmania species. Conventional treatments, including pentavalent antimonials, amphotericin B (AMB), and miltefosine are associated with significant cost, safety, and compliance constraints, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies. This critical review provides an integrated overview of epidemiology, and immunological aspects of CL while highlighting the risk factors contributing to CL spread, such as climate change and political instability. It further critically assesses current treatment strategies and their constraints, underlining the urgent need for safer and more effective alternatives. In this context, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have been introduced as a rational formulation approach to overcome the biopharmaceutical and pharmacokinetic challenges associated with current and emerging antileishmanial agents. Nano formulations such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles and metallic nanostructures have revealed promising preclinical results for CL. This review investigates the potential of nano-based formulations to guide and support the future development of enhanced treatment strategies for CL. Despite advancements in nanotechnology research, translational obstacles persist, including scalability, cost-efficiency and regulatory approval. Nevertheless, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems represent a promising approach to improve the efficacy, targeting and safety profile of antileishmanial therapies, although further translational and clinical studies are required before their widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Anticoagulation for Atrial Fibrillation after Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Systematic Review and Frequentist-Bayesian Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation is a leading cause of ischemic stroke, and oral anticoagulation is commonly used for stroke prevention. However, the use of oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage presents a therapeutic dilemma due to the increased risk of recurrent bleeding. This study aims to update the evidence on the efficacy and safety of oral anticoagulation in this high-risk population.

METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, and Embase, from inception to 30 April 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing the initiation of oral anticoagulation with no anticoagulation in adults with atrial fibrillation after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Frequentist, Bayesian, and trial sequential analyses were used. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events.

RESULTS: A total of five randomized controlled trials were included, comprising 733 participants. Frequentist meta-analysis showed that oral anticoagulation was associated with a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with no anticoagulation [risk ratio (RR) 0.59; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.37-0.94; I2= 24%]. Bayesian meta-analysis generally favored oral anticoagulation across a range of prior distributions and heterogeneity assumptions, with a probability of RR < 0.8 exceeding 90% in six of ten scenarios.

CONCLUSIONS: Starting oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation after intracerebral hemorrhage was associated with a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events compared with no anticoagulation.

articles.title: Intracranial Pressure Waveform Response to Hypertonic Saline Bolus in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to identify features of intracranial compliance (ICC) reflected in intracranial pressure (ICP) waveform morphology following bolus of 20% hypertonic saline (HTS) to manage intracranial hypertension.

METHODS: ICP was monitored during 89 HTS injections in ten patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) and high intracranial hypertension. Pulse amplitude (AMP), P2/P1 ratio, pulse shape index (PSI), and normalized time to peak (TTP) were retrospectively analyzed over 3h including pre-, during, and postinjection interval. Trajectories of mean ICP and ICC surrogates were characterized using linear mixed models to assess individual contributions to the response following HTS injection.

RESULTS: HTS injections induced transient decreases in all variables as follows: ICP [15.6 mmHg, 95% confidence interval (CI; 10.8, 20.3mmHg)], AMP [5.6 (3.5, 7.6mmHg)], P2/P1 [0.49 (0.32, 0.66)], PSI [0.65 (0.43, 0.87)], and TTP [0.054 (0.03, 0.07)]. Baseline P2/P1, TTP, and PSI showed predominantly between-patient variability [variance partition coefficient (VPC) = 0.56, 0.67, and 0.67, respectively], whereas baseline ICP and AMP showed greater within-patient variability (VPC = 0.18 and 0.24). Response-related features were also predominantly characterized by within-patient variability, with VPCs ranging from 0.20 to 0.27 for maximum decrease and from 0.13 to 0.23 for AAC. In random-intercept models, higher baseline ICP was associated with larger reductions in AMP (β = 0.13, p < 10-4), PSI (β = 0.02, p = 10-4), and TTP (β = 0.001, p = 0.034) following HTS administration, whereas baseline morphology metrics did not significantly improve the prediction of ICP reduction after adjustment for baseline ICP. When ICP nadir was modeled directly instead of the baseline-dependent change score, neither baseline ICP nor baseline morphology was significantly associated with ICP nadir. Adjustment for end-tidal CO2 (EtCO2) and prior osmotherapy did not materially alter these association patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: ICP waveform morphology, as assessed by P2/P1, PSI, and TTP, is influenced by changes in intracranial pressure but also retains substantial patient-specific variability. In contrast, AMP is primarily driven by changes in intracranial pressure.

articles.title: One Anastomosis Gastric Bypass (OAGB) vs Sleeve Gastrectomy (SG) in Patients with Obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m²: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² presents unique clinical challenges, often requiring highly effective metabolic and bariatric interventions to achieve substantial weight reduction and obesity-associated medical conditions remission. Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) remains the most frequently performed procedure globally due to its technical simplicity and favorable short-term safety. However, long-term concerns regarding recurrent weight gain (RWG) and suboptimal clinical response (SoCR) in patients with higher baseline BMIs persist. One anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) has emerged as a powerful alternative, combining both restrictive and intestinal-rerouting mechanisms to optimize metabolic outcomes. Despite its growing popularity, head-to-head evidence directly comparing the long-term efficacy, safety profiles, and complication rates of OAGB versus SG specifically within patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m² demographic remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the mid-term efficacy, safety profile, and resolution of metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions between one anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB) and sleeve gastrectomy (SG) in patients with BMI ≥ 50 kg/m².

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) and observational cohorts. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane through January 2026. Primary endpoint was total weight loss (%TWL). Secondary endpoints were remission of type 2 diabetes (T2D), hypertension remission, and rate of reoperation. Data was pooled using RevMan 5.4, evaluating Risk Ratios (RR) for dichotomous variables and Mean Differences (MD) for continuous variables, with 95% Confidence Intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Eleven studies encompassing a total of 2,539 patients were included in the final review. The pooled analysis demonstrated that OAGB yielded a statistically significant superior Total Weight Loss compared to SG (MD = 9.56; 95% CI [9.01, 10.11]; p < 0.00001). Conversely, there was no statistically significant difference between the two techniques regarding T2DM remission (RR = 1.08; 95% CI [0.97, 1.20]; p = 0.16) or hypertension remission (RR = 1.20; 95% CI [0.98, 1.45]; p = 0.07). Additionally, the reoperation rates were comparable between the OAGB and SG groups (RR = 1.13; 95% CI [0.40, 3.20]; p = 0.82).

CONCLUSION: In patients with obesity and BMI ≥ 50 kg/m², OAGB provides significantly greater total weight loss compared to SG. Both procedures demonstrate comparable safety profiles and similar effectiveness in the remission of major metabolic obesity-associated medical conditions. OAGB is a highly effective and safe alternative for managing obesity.

articles.title: Buyuan decoction attenuates COPD-associated skeletal muscle atrophy: insights from network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vivo validation.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia, a clinical syndrome defined by reduced muscle strength and mass, frequently complicates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and impairs physical performance. Buyuan Decoction (BYD) has shown protective effects against COPD-associated skeletal muscle atrophy, but its mechanisms beyond previously reported oxidative-stress regulation remain incompletely understood. We integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vivo experiments to explore the mechanisms of BYD against COPD-associated skeletal muscle atrophy. A rat COPD model was induced by cigarette smoke and LPS. Muscle function and molecular changes were evaluated by grip strength, muscle weight, histopathology, and biochemical assays. Network pharmacology indicated 121 overlapping targets between BYD-related targets and a sarcopenia-related target set used for disease-target retrieval, with enrichment in inflammation, metabolism, hypoxia, and apoptosis pathways. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding affinities, with the quercetin-SIRT1 complex exhibiting the lowest binding energy. In vivo, BYD improved grip strength and muscle mass, attenuated lung and muscle histopathology, reduced TNF-α and IL-6 levels, increased SOD activity and ATP content, reduced STAT3 phosphorylation at Tyr705, downregulated MuRF1 expression, and increased the expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, OPA1, and HDAC2. These changes were accompanied by concordant mRNA levels and enhanced SIRT1 deacetylase activity. Collectively, these findings suggest that BYD may protect against COPD-associated skeletal muscle atrophy, an effect associated with changes in SIRT1/PGC-1α-related mitochondrial regulatory markers and STAT3-related inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: Aging-Related Stroke Disability: The Mediating Role of Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Aging and inflammation constitute significant risk factors for poor functional outcomes and recurrent stroke following ischemic stroke. Although aging is associated with heightened inflammatory responses, no prior study has quantified the extent to which inflammation mediates aging-related functional impairment and stroke recurrence. We included patients from the Third China National Stroke Registry with measurements of six inflammatory biomarkers (interleukin-1 receptor antagonist, interleukin-6 [IL-6], high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [hsCRP], lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 activity and mass, and chitinase-3-like protein 1 [CHI3L1, YKL-40]). We evaluated associations between age and these biomarkers. Mediation analyses were conducted to assess whether inflammatory biomarkers mediated the association between aging and 90-day functional disability and stroke recurrence. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the mediation effects. Among 10,349 eligible patients, age was most strongly associated with IL-6, hsCRP, and YKL-40. Mediation analyses revealed that IL-6 (percentage mediated [PM] = 15.3%), hsCRP (PM = 9.7%), and YKL-40 (PM = 11.4%) partially mediated the aging-functional outcome relationship, but not stroke recurrence. Sensitivity analyses showed consistent results. Inflammation, reflected by IL-6, hsCRP, and YKL-40, partially mediates the effect of aging on functional disability after ischemic stroke or TIA, but not on stroke recurrence. These findings highlight inflammatory pathways as potential targets for improving outcomes in elderly stroke patients.

articles.title: Temporal changes in chelonid alphaherpesvirus 5 (Scutavirus chelonidalpha5) infection among marine turtles at Mabul Island, Sabah, Malaysian Borneo.
articles.abstract: Fibropapillomatosis (FP) is a debilitating tumour formation affecting marine turtles worldwide and is strongly associated with chelonid alphaherpesvirus 5 (ChHV5; Scutavirus chelonidalpha5). Long-term surveillance is important to evaluate temporal changes in ChHV5 detection and FP occurrence. This study aims to assess ChHV5 infection in marine turtles of Mabul Island, representing the third surveillance period following previous investigations in 2015-2016 and 2019. Field sampling was conducted in May 2022, and the tissue samples were screened via PCR-based assays targeting four ChHV5 regions (UL18, UL22, UL27, and UL30). DNA sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were performed to verify and characterise the ChHV5 isolate obtained in this study. Of 118 marine turtles sampled (108 green and 10 hawksbill turtles), nine green turtles were PCR-positive for ChHV5, representing 8.3% of the sampled green turtles. This was significantly lower than in 2019 (42.9%; P < 0.001) but did not differ significantly from the baseline in 2015-2016 (7.8%; P = 1.000). Eight of the nine ChHV5-positive turtles were clinically healthy, indicating viral DNA detection despite the absence of FP. Partial UL30 sequences (Mabul isolates) clustered with isolates from diverse geographical regions. These findings demonstrate substantial temporal variation in ChHV5 infection and support continued surveillance to better understand ChHV5 infection dynamics in marine turtles.

articles.title: Estimating exposure thresholds for robotic surgical skill decay: a systematic review and quantitative threshold synthesis.
articles.abstract: The duration of reduced robotic operative exposure associated with deterioration in technical performance, and the minimum recent case frequency needed to preserve performance, remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus through October 3, 2026. Eligible studies assessed robotic operators after proficiency, training, or established practice in relation to exposure gaps or recent case frequency. Study quality was appraised using MERSQI. Technical-quality (T_skill*) and efficiency (T_eff*) vulnerability thresholds were estimated using separate Bayesian interval-censored models. Twenty-four reports representing 22 study clusters were included (median standardized MERSQI, 11.8/18). In the primary analyses, the exploratory cross-study posterior median vulnerability thresholds were 41.6 days for technical quality (95% credible interval [CrI], 9.0-143.5) and 48.9 days for efficiency (95% CrI, 9.4-192.9). Model-implied probabilities of threshold onset by 90 days were 73.2% and 66.4%, respectively. Broad sensitivity analyses incorporating retention-favorable evidence shifted the medians to 110.8 and 89.4 days. A pooled recent-volume threshold was not identifiable; fewer than two versus at least two robotic cases monthly represented only an exploratory boundary. Measurable robotic performance vulnerability may emerge within weeks of reduced exposure, but timing varies substantially and broader retention-inclusive sensitivity analyses yield later estimates. No universal minimum-volume or credentialing cutoff is supported.

articles.title: Differential metabolic impacts of a modified traditional Japanese diet and the DPP-4 inhibitor alogliptin on uric acid dynamics in drug-naïve subjects with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Uric acid (UA) is traditionally regarded as a metabolic risk marker; however, its dynamic behavior during glucose-lowering therapy remains incompletely understood. We investigated the effects of a modified Japanese diet for diabetes (MJDD) and the DPP-4 inhibitor alogliptin on UA dynamics in subjects with early-stage T2DM. In this non-randomized, prospective observational study, drug-naïve patients received MJDD (n = 58) or alogliptin (n = 52) monotherapy for 3 months. Changes (Δ) in serum UA were analyzed in relation to glycemic control, insulin resistance, adipo-IR, and beta-cell function. Both interventions significantly reduced FBG and HbA1c while paradoxically increasing serum UA and HOMA-B. Baseline UA was the primary determinant of ΔUA in both cohorts. MJDD significantly reduced BMI, insulin, FFA, HOMA-R, and adipo-IR, with effects most pronounced in subjects with baseline BMI ≥ 25. In contrast, alogliptin selectively reduced adipo-IR in leaner subjects (BMI < 25). Across both treatments, ΔUA correlated positively with ΔHOMA-B and inversely with ΔHbA1c. Notably, during MJDD, ΔUA showed a paradoxical negative correlation with ΔBMI and ΔFBG, and a positive correlation with ΔFFA. Subjects exhibiting the greatest UA increases demonstrated the most marked improvements in HOMA-B and, with MJDD, the greatest weight loss. These findings indicate that MJDD and alogliptin exert distinct metabolic effects in early T2DM, yet both link rising UA to enhanced HOMA-B, suggesting that UA may serve as a dynamic pharmacometabolic biomarker reflecting therapy-specific metabolic changes.

articles.title: RSV prevention after nirsevimab: what Europe has learned-and what it has not.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Europe moved within two seasons from selective respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prophylaxis for a small high-risk group to population-based strategies capable of protecting most infants. We aimed to examine the European experience with RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction, and identify key lessons regarding implementation, programme performance, comparative evaluation, and remaining evidence gaps. Studies evaluating RSV prevention after nirsevimab introduction in Europe were searched. Evidence was mapped according to implementation strategies, effectiveness outcomes, healthcare impact, safety, resistance, and emerging research questions. Real-world studies from Europe consistently reported considerable reductions in RSV hospitalisation and intensive-care admission following nirsevimab implementation. Heterogeneity in programme design and delivery suggests that product effectiveness is only one determinant of impact: programme characteristics like administration timing, catch-up strategies, coverage, maternity-versus-community delivery, and the age distribution of baseline burden influence observed outcomes. Second-season evidence distinguishes limited residual individual protection from a persisting cumulative two-season benefit. Maternal RSVpreF vaccination is highly effective when administered sufficiently before delivery, although cross-strategy comparisons remain vulnerable to timing and selection bias. Safety findings remain reassuring; resistance-associated substitutions are detectable but have not undermined population-level effectiveness. The recent introduction of clesrovimab further expands preventive options.

CONCLUSION: Europe has answered whether universal infant RSV prevention can reduce severe disease burden but not yet standardised how programmes are compared. The next phase should move from product advocacy to programme science: one primary strategy for most infants, explicit rescue indications, linked immunisation-outcome-genomic surveillance, common estimands and transparent measurement of equity and opportunity cost.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Long-acting monoclonal antibodies and maternal RSVpreF vaccination prevent severe RSV disease in early infancy.

WHAT IS NEW: • The European lesson is not a universal product ranking: delivery architecture, catch-up and the interval between maternal vaccination and birth determine population impact. • Second-season policy requires estimand discipline: limited residual effectiveness can coexist with substantial cumulative two-season benefit and no rebound.

articles.title: Farklı lingual tutma malzemelerinin diş eti sağlığı üzerindeki etkilerinin değerlendirilmesi.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Maintaining post-orthodontic stability is critical to prevent relapse, with fixed lingual retainers (LR) considered the clinical gold standard. However, these appliances create mechanical barriers that facilitate plaque and calculus accumulation, potentially compromising long-term periodontal health. This study aimed to prospectively evaluate and compare the 12-month effects of four different LR materials on plaque retention, gingival health, and calculus formation.

METHODS: A total of 140 participants (95 females, 45 males; mean age 15.9 ± 1.2 years) were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 35): Group 1 (G1) (0.0175-inch 7-strand stainless steel), Group 2 (G2) (0.022 × 0.016-inch 8-strand dead-soft wire), Group 3 (G3) (0.038 × 0.016-inch prefabricated Ortho FlexTech), and Group 4 (G4) (fiber-reinforced composite). Periodontal parameters including Plaque Index (PI), Gingival Index (GI), and Dental Calculus Index (DCI) were recorded at baseline (T1), 3 (T2), 6 (T3), 9 (T4), and 12 months (T5) by a single calibrated examiner (ICC > 0.80). Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA and repeated measures analysis of variance (p < 0.05).

RESULTS: All groups exhibited a statistically significant intra-group increase in PI, GI, and DCI scores over the 12-month follow-up (p < 0.05). While inter-group comparisons revealed no significant differences for PI (p > 0.05), Group 3 showed significantly higher GI scores at T3 compared to Group 1, and Group 2 reached the highest GI values at T4 (p < 0.05). Notably, Group 3 (prefabricated wire) demonstrated significantly higher DCI values than Groups 1 and 4 at the T4 and T5 time points (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: The four fixed LR types showed generally comparable periodontal outcomes over the 12-month follow-up period. No significant long-term differences were observed among the retainer types in terms of PI and GI. However, the prefabricated stainless steel retainer (G3) demonstrated significantly greater dental calculus accumulation than Groups 1 and 4 at the later follow-up time points. These findings suggest that retainer design and structural characteristics may influence calculus accumulation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The findings indicate that all fixed lingual retainers require regular periodontal monitoring; however, prefabricated and larger-diameter designs may be associated with greater calculus accumulation. Material selection should therefore be combined with individualized oral hygiene instruction and regular professional maintenance.

articles.title: Non-fatal assaults with glass objects: a retrospective forensic analysis of 70 cases.
articles.abstract: Glass objects are readily available in settings associated with interpersonal violence and may cause blunt, sharp, or combined injuries depending on the mechanism of use and glass fragmentation. This retrospective study analyzed 70 non-fatal assaults with glass objects evaluated at a single forensic medicine department between 2014 and 2025. The study focused on assault circumstances, object type, mechanism of injury, fragmentation, wound morphology, anatomical distribution, and injury severity. Injured persons and assailants were predominantly male. Assaults most often occurred in pubs, bars, and restaurants, and alcohol involvement was frequently recorded. Contact assaults with held glass objects were more common than assaults with thrown objects, and repeated assault with a glass object was documented in approximately one fifth of cases. Glass fragmentation occurred in most cases, but did not necessarily result in sharp injuries; blunt injuries were also observed after breakage. Conversely, intact glass objects caused only blunt injuries, usually one and never more than two lacerations. Severe injuries were less common but included fractures of the head, face, and dentoalveolar region, open-globe injuries, vascular neck injury with hypovolemic shock, and facial nerve injury. The most clinically significant consequences were associated with the sharp action of glass fragments, particularly in the periocular and neck regions. These findings highlight the importance of reconstructing the assault mechanism, including object type, repeated action, fragmentation, and secondary action of glass fragments.

articles.title: A tiered postmortem work-up for suspected Kounis syndrome: proposal derived from a systematic review of 47 fatal autopsied cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kounis syndrome, the concurrence of acute coronary syndrome with mast-cell- and platelet-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, is increasingly recognised clinically but remains poorly standardised at autopsy.

METHODS: We performed a PROSPERO-registered systematic review compliant with PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched, complemented by citation chasing, an eosinophilic-coronary-disease sensitivity search and hand-searching. Eligible records described fatal autopsied Kounis-spectrum cases, including allergic myocardial infarction and eosinophilic coronary periarteritis/arteritis. The fatal case was the unit of analysis; postmortem biochemistry, mast-cell histology and immunohistochemistry, toxicology and diagnostic certainty were extracted.

RESULTS: Thirty-six records contributed 47 unique fatal autopsied cases from 17 countries (1969-2025). Postmortem tryptase was measured in 6/47 cases (12.8%), histamine in 1/47 (2.1%) and immunoglobulin E in 1/47 (2.1%); any mast-cell-specific tissue method was used in 11/47 (23.4%). Thirty-six cases were type I/type I-like, eight type II/II-like and three type III. Biochemical testing clustered in iatrogenic/periprocedural and type II cases, whereas anti-tryptase immunohistochemistry clustered in the eosinophilic-coronary-periarteritis literature, documenting a dissociation between tissue and biochemical methods. The finding held among definite/probable (tryptase 3/31) and methodologically stronger cases (2/19), and was attenuated, not reversed, among thirteen cases explicitly diagnosed as Kounis syndrome or allergic coronary disease by their authors (3/13).

CONCLUSION: Reports of fatal autopsied Kounis cases rarely document biochemical testing for mast-cell activation. We propose, for prospective validation, a tiered, indication-driven minimum postmortem work-up, modelled on the multimodal Cianci et al. [52] case, for sudden deaths in which Kounis syndrome enters the differential diagnosis.

articles.title: Minimally invasive and nephron-sparing surgery for renal cancer: a nationwide analysis of 228,185 nephrectomies in Germany, 2011-2024.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Nephron-sparing and minimally invasive surgery are recommended for localised renal cell carcinoma, but the evidence comes from expert centres. We examined whether their advantages hold in routine care and whether access is equitable.

METHODS: We analysed all 228,185 adult nephrectomies for renal cancer in the German hospital census, 2011-2024. Outcomes were in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE-RN), acute kidney injury, dialysis and length of stay. Access was compared by mixed-effects logistic regression with random hospital intercepts, procedure type by inverse probability of treatment weighting.

RESULTS: The minimally invasive share rose from 19.7% to 59.4%, robot assistance from 9.7% to 79.4% of those, and partial nephrectomy overtook radical in 2017, reaching 62.5%. Adjusted odds were lower with minimally invasive access for death (odds ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.42-0.56), MACCE-RN (0.56) and acute kidney injury (0.57), with a 21% shorter stay, and lower still with robot assistance than laparoscopy for acute kidney injury (0.46 vs. 0.72) and dialysis (0.67 vs. 0.92). Partial nephrectomy was associated with lower odds of death (0.61) and dialysis (0.41), without a shift towards patients with greater comorbidity. Minimally invasive surgery had ever been performed in 17.9% of the smallest and 95.9% of the largest centres.

CONCLUSION: Both approaches became predominant and in routine care were associated with the advantages reported from expert centres. These are observational associations, not evidence of intrinsic superiority: administrative data carry no tumour stage and no follow-up beyond discharge. Adoption depended on hospital volume, not patient characteristics.

articles.title: Perioperative morbidity and surgical outcomes of robot-assisted versus open radical cystectomy in obese patients (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: We compared short-term surgical morbidity and recovery between robot-assisted radical cystectomy (RARC) and open radical cystectomy (ORC) in bladder cancer patients with a body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30 kg/m². Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261489060), five databases were searched through October 15, 2026. Study quality, risk of bias, and evidence certainty were rated via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), ROBINS-I, and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). Random- and fixed-effect models generated summary odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and weighted mean differences (WMDs). Four retrospective cohorts (NOS 8-9; n = 3,127: 723 RARC, 2,404 ORC) were included. In the broad four-study composite analysis, overall major morbidity did not differ significantly (12.9% vs. 17.6%; OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.38-1.18, p = 0.164; I² = 54.1%). However, in a harmonized analysis restricted to clinical registries recording unplanned surgical reoperation (Clavien-Dindo ≥ IIIb; k = 3, n = 2,006), RARC was associated with fewer reoperations (3.7% vs. 6.6%; OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.29-0.81, p = 0.005; I² = 0.0%), including across peer-reviewed cohorts alone (k = 2, OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.26-0.85, p = 0.012).
