Across two-study syntheses heavily weighted toward a single propensity-matched registry, RARC showed lower absolute rates and odds of transfusion (10.7% vs. 37.2%; OR 0.20, p < 0.001), wound infection (5.8% vs. 18.0%; OR 0.29, p < 0.001), and readmission (15.1% vs. 22.5%; OR 0.61, p < 0.001), plus shorter hospitalization (WMD - 3.47 days, p < 0.001). Pulmonary morbidity (3.9% vs. 4.7%; OR 0.73, 95% CI 0.39-1.39, p = 0.341), total complications (p = 0.402), and operative time (p = 0.607) were inconclusive. While four-study composite major morbidity was non-significant, RARC is observationally associated with fewer unplanned reoperations, transfusions, and wound infections in selected obese candidates (low-to-very-low GRADE certainty).

articles.title: Innate and adaptive immunity in diseases of dogs and cats associated with Candida spp., Malassezia spp. and Cryptococcus spp.: a critical review.
articles.abstract: The interactions between hosts and Malassezia spp., Candida spp., and Cryptococcus spp. can cause infections in dogs and cats and are associated with colonisation, overgrowth, hypersensitivity reactions, and localised or invasive disease. This review examines the roles and importance of innate and adaptive immunity in infections caused by these fungi. Focusing mostly on canine and feline literature, experimental literature was considered when lacking. In Malassezia-associated disease, serum antibody concentrations have not consistently reflected clinical activity, while experimental studies indicate that fungal control and inflammatory damage are not necessarily coupled. In candidiasis, the importance of epithelial immunity, neutrophils, and other phagocytes varies by site of infection, and most mechanistic data are derived from C. albicans. In cryptococcosis, experiments show that phagocytes suppress fungal proliferation and provide an intracellular niche for them. The role of each mechanism depends on infection site and clinical form of the disease. There is limited literature on veterinary immunotherapy, including allergen-specific immunotherapy for hypersensitivity to Malassezia spp. Vaccine-, cytokine-, and immune-checkpoint-based therapies have mostly been tested experimentally. In animal infections, especially in dogs and cats, correlations have been reported for the mechanisms discussed. One of the biggest gaps in the literature is the lack of studies linking these mechanisms to disease course, recurrence, fungal clearance, and treatment efficacy.

articles.title: Prognostic factors and prognostic models for recovery and treatment response in patients with painful cervical radiculopathy: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to critically appraise (1) prognostic factors and models for recovery, and (2) prognostic factors and models for conservative treatment response in patients with painful cervical radiculopathy.

METHOD: MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, and Web of Science were searched. Two independent reviewers screened abstracts and full-text articles and extracted data independently. Data extraction was performed using the Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews checklist. The Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) and the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment (PROBAST) were used to assess risk of bias. Strength-of-evidence summaries were created in GRADEpro, using prognostic factors and models as outcome variables and evaluating the consistency of the research findings.

RESULTS: The systematic search retrieved 8,661 records, and seven studies met the selection criteria. Four studies examined prognostic factors: two for recovery and two for response to conservative treatment. Two studies assessed prognostic models predicting recovery after conservative treatment, and one study assessed a prognostic model for treatment response to neural tissue management. All prognostic factors studies were rated high risk and had very low certainty of evidence. The type of health insurance might be a prognostic factor for workdays lost. Differentiating soft disc herniation from osteophytes did not show clear prognostic value. A C2-C7 Cobb angle > 7.7° might be associated with a more favourable outcome after conservative treatment. The presence of Modic changes might be associated with a favourable short-term response to cervical thrust manipulation. Of the three prognostic model studies, one was rated as low risk of bias and two as high risk of bias. In total, five prognostic models were identified. Three predicted 12-month recovery outcomes (AUCs 0.75-0.79), one predicted 28-day treatment success (likelihood ratio 8.3, 95% CI 1.9-63.9), and one predicted response to neural tissue management, with a nomogram score ≥ 89 indicating a 90% probability of improvement (95% CI 56-98). The certainty of evidence was low to moderate. Only one prognostic model study was internally validated, and none of the included models were externally validated.

CONCLUSION: Evidence on prognostic factors and models in painful cervical radiculopathy remains limited and of very low to moderate-certainty. As none of the prognostic models were externally validated, their implementation in clinical practice cannot be supported. External validation studies are needed.

articles.title: Guanylate-binding protein 5 at the crossroads of infection, sterile immunity, and malignancy.
articles.abstract: Guanylate-binding protein 5 (GBP5) is a vertebrate-specific paralog that retains the highly conserved dynamin-like GTPase fold but has undergone rapid sequence evolution. While sharing a conserved structural core that is recruited to damaged membranes, GBP5 has adapted to function as a context-dependent signaling node in mammalian immunity. During specific intracellular infection, GBP5 provides vital defense by scaffolding the cytosolic NLRP3 inflammasome and contributes to protective pyroptosis. Yet, in sterile pathologies, GBP5 has been proposed to interact with the STAT1 transcription factor and promote an M1-polarized macrophage state, although this model awaits independent replication. Within tumors, this dual-signaling hub, integrating cytosolic inflammasome and nuclear STAT1 signaling, acts as a context-dependent molecular switch, driving either immune evasion via PD-L1 upregulation or anti-tumor immunity. Ultimately, resolving the energetic basis of GBP5's GTPase cycle, namely how nucleotide binding and hydrolysis control its conformational dynamics and interactions, remains a key unresolved question for therapeutically uncoupling its pathological roles in sterile inflammation and tumor immune evasion from antimicrobial defense.

articles.title: Bioelectric signalling: mechanisms, biological functions, diseases, diagnosis and therapy.
articles.abstract: Bioelectric signalling arises from the coordinated activity of ion channels, transporters, exchangers, and pumps, which establish the membrane potential and ionic gradients, generate endogenous electric fields, and support intercellular bioelectric coupling. These occur in both excitable and non-excitable tissues, where they interact with biochemical, mechanical, metabolic, and transcriptional networks. Excitable tissues serve as established model systems linking ion transport to rapid bioelectric activity and organ function. This review focuses primarily on the less extensively characterised roles of persistent and spatially organised bioelectric states in non-excitable and weakly excitable tissues. Evidence from the fields of development, regeneration, wound repair, immunity, and tissue remodelling suggests that bioelectric states may function as instructive signals, modulators of signalling responsiveness, permissive physiological conditions, or integrated indicators of cell and tissue state. This functional classification provides a framework for interpreting bioelectric alterations associated with cancer, fibrosis, chronic inflammation, metabolic disease, and neurological and cardiovascular disorders. We examine how membrane voltage, calcium signalling, endogenous electric fields, and gap junctional coupling interact with canonical pathways and tissue architecture. Experimental criteria are proposed to distinguish regulatory mechanisms from adaptive or secondary changes. The development of bioelectric diagnostics is evaluated in relation to analytical validity, biological interpretation, clinical validity, and clinical utility, together with therapeutic strategies based on ion channel modulation, electrical stimulation, conductive biomaterials, and bioelectronic interfaces. Integrating quantitative measurements, controlled perturbations, and computational modelling could help define when bioelectric states offer mechanistic leverage, predictive information, or clinically actionable targets.

articles.title: Locoregional administration of bispecific CAR-T cells targeting CD44 and CD133 in recurrent high-grade glioma: a first-in-human investigator-initiated trial.
articles.abstract: Grade IV glioma remains highly lethal, and effective therapies for recurrent disease remain limited. Glioma stem cells (GSCs) contribute to therapeutic resistance and tumor recurrence, providing a rationale for GSC-targeted immunotherapy. We conducted a single-center, single-arm investigator-initiated trial evaluating locoregional administration of CD44/CD133 bispecific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells incorporating a truncated interleukin-7 receptor α (IL-7Rα) intracellular domain in ten adults with recurrent grade IV glioma. Treatment was well tolerated, with no dose-limiting toxicities or Grade ≥2 cytokine release syndrome. Adverse events were predominantly mild and transient, and no patient required IL-6 or IL-1 blockade. CAR-T cell leakage into peripheral blood remained minimal, whereas cerebrospinal fluid cytokine elevations were modest following infusion. Three patients achieved partial responses. The median overall survival after the first CAR-T cell infusion was 465 days. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing and proteomic analyses suggested patient stratification in macrophage-associated signatures, particularly in interferon signaling and antigen-presentation programs, which were associated with distinct clinical outcomes independently of IDH mutation status in this cohort. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of repeated locoregional administration of GSC-targeting IL-7Rα-armored bispecific CAR-T cells. Exploratory immune profiling further identified inter-patient heterogeneity in macrophage-associated immune programs, which warrants validation in larger prospective studies. (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05577091, NMPA No. CXSL2500032).

articles.title: Healthy Work Environments-2025: A National Status Report.
articles.journal: American journal of critical care : an official publication, American Association of Critical-Care Nurses
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The health of nurse work environments has long been linked to critical patient and nurse outcomes. The American Association of Critical-Care Nurses (AACN) has surveyed nurses about their work environments since 2006; the 2021 survey documented deterioration across all 6 healthy work environment standards during COVID-19.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the state of nurse work environments in 2025, assess progress in implementing the 6 AACN healthy work environment standards, and examine associations between work environment and key nurse outcomes.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was administered to US registered nurses in 2025 through AACN membership and partners. The survey included items mapped to each healthy work environment standard, the Maslach Burnout Inventory emotional exhaustion subscale, and modules on workplace violence and staffing. Multivariable regression examined associations between work environment and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 11 957 respondents, intent to leave employer within 12 months was substantially lower than in 2021 (17.5% vs 35.8%), and 77.5% of respondents reported job satisfaction. However, 38.0% met criteria for high emotional exhaustion, 70.1% reported patient emotional abuse, and 52.6% reported physical violence. Implementation of the healthy work environment standards improved markedly since 2021, with most respondents reporting that their units were "well on the way" or "fully implemented" for each standard, compared with 29% in 2021, although gaps persisted in decision-making training (43.7% disagreed that all team members receive ongoing training), authentic leadership accountability, and staffing governance.

CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 survey signals meaningful post-pandemic stabilization in retention and implementation of healthy work environment standards, but endemic workplace violence, burnout, and gaps in staffing governance and leadership accountability demand continued attention.

articles.title: Radiographic vertebral heart size in clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: Vertebral heart size (VHS) is a widely used radiographic method for evaluating cardiac size in dogs, and breed-related variation has been reported. However, breed-specific VHS data for Shiba Inu dogs have not previously been reported. This retrospective study evaluated VHS in 42 clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs with no evidence of cardiac disease based on physical examination, thoracic radiography, and echocardiography. VHS was measured using right lateral thoracic radiographs. The mean ± standard deviation VHS was 9.62 ± 0.35 vertebrae. These findings provide baseline radiographic data for clinically healthy Shiba Inu dogs.

articles.title: Lower Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index Independently Predicts Periprosthetic Joint Infection in Elderly Patients After Primary Total Joint Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether low geriatric nutritional risk index (GNRI) affects risk of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains unclear. The present study explored this question among elderly undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA).

METHODS: This retrospective study included 5,157 patients aged 65 years or older who underwent primary total knee or hip arthroplasty (TKA/THA). The associations between preoperative GNRI and PJI were examined with Firth penalized logistic regression. The GNRI was analyzed as a continuous, binary, and quartile-based variable. Discrimination of GNRI, ratio of albumin to fibrinogen (AFR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI) was assessed with receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis and compared with the DeLong test. Incremental predictive value beyond a baseline clinical model, restricted cubic spline analysis, and calibration assessment were also performed.

RESULTS: Postoperative PJI occurred in 46 of 5,157 patients (0.9%). The absolute PJI rate was 4.39% among patients who had GNRI less than 98 and 0.30% among those who had GNRI ≥ 98. In the fully adjusted model, each 1-unit decrease in GNRI was associated with increased odds of PJI (OR [odds ratio], 1.23; 95% CI [confidence interval], 1.16 to 1.31; P < 0.001), and GNRI less than 98 was associated with higher odds of PJI (OR, 6.73; 95% CI, 2.97 to 18.60; P < 0.001). The GNRI had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.843, compared with 0.753 for AFR and 0.646 for PNI. After bootstrap internal validation, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.835 for the baseline clinical model and 0.903 after the addition of GNRI. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis demonstrated an inverse association between GNRI and PJI risk, and calibration was acceptable.

CONCLUSION: Low preoperative GNRI is independently associated with PJI after primary TJA in elderly patients. In this cohort, GNRI showed a higher observed AUC than the other nutritional indices evaluated, supporting its potential utility for preoperative risk assessment.

articles.title: Correction: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme Inhibitors or Angiotensin-Receptor Blockers for Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
Progress in Reducing the Black-White Mortality Gap From 1993 to 2023 in the United States: An Analysis of the National Mortality Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reducing racial mortality disparities remains a central goal of U.S. health policy, and progress varies by cause of death.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify cause-specific contributions to changes in excess mortality rate (EMR) among Black versus White populations.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional temporal analyses.

SETTING: Mortality data.

PARTICIPANTS: Non-Hispanic Black and non-Hispanic White decedents stratified by sex and age at death (<20, <65, or ≥65 years).

MEASUREMENTS: EMRs among Black versus White populations in 1993 and 2023 for all-cause and 24 causes of death, calculated as differences in age-standardized mortality rates, and changes in EMRs, calculated by subtracting the 2023 EMR from the 1993 EMR with cause-specific contribution to all-cause EMR reduction, expressed as a percentage.

RESULTS: In 2023, all-cause EMR for Black versus White persons decreased by 56% (288.5 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for males and by 68% (175.8 deaths per 100 000 person-years) for females compared with 1993. Among males, reductions were predominantly driven by cancer (38.2% [95% CI, 36.4% to 40.0%]), HIV (17.5% [CI, 17.0% to 18.1%]), and heart disease (12.3% [CI, 10.2% to 14.4%]); among females, primary drivers were heart disease (31.9% [CI, 29.8% to 34.0%]), cancer (13.0% [CI, 11.3% to 14.8%]), and HIV (7.9% [CI, 7.5% to 8.3%]). Further gains were limited by lower progress or worsening disparities in maternal death; nephritis and accidents and adverse effects in both sexes; and homicide and legal intervention, diabetes, hypertension without heart disease, and cerebrovascular diseases (≥65 years) in males. Over time, cancer fell from the leading contributor to sixth among males and from second to fifth among females, whereas HIV declined from fourth or fifth to tenth in both sexes as contributors to the Black-White mortality gap.

LIMITATION: The analysis compared 1993 and 2023, although peak EMR years varied by cause of death, and alternative periods could yield different cause-specific contributions.

CONCLUSION: Reductions in EMR among Black versus White populations were driven by improvements in mortality from major causes. Shifting drivers of the racial mortality gap highlight priorities for further progress.

PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: American Cancer Society and Research Ireland.

articles.title: Sotatercept in Action: Rethinking Right Ventricular Physiology?
Letter by Zhu et al Regarding Article, "Oxidized Phospholipids, Lipoprotein(a), and Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome".
Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure-Volume Loop Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading.

METHODS: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure-volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography).

RESULTS: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34-67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0-65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0-42.0] mm Hg; P<0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P<0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183-242] to 160 [IQR, 129-204] mL; P<0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6-56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2-44.4] g; P<0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P=0.002). Ventricular-arterial coupling (end-systolic/arterial elastance) improved although load-independent contractility decreased alongside the decrease in effective arterial elastance. By contrast, nonresponders demonstrated a clinical-hemodynamic disconnect. Despite persistently elevated RV afterload and unchanged end-systolic/arterial elastance, a significant reduction in RV mass (56.1 [IQR, 45.9-81.0] to 46.4 [IQR, 35.9-59.4] g; P=0.003) was observed, accompanied by a significant decrease in B-type natriuretic peptide levels, whereas 6-minute walk distance did not change significantly (+15 m [95% CI, -12 to 42]; P=0.23); the difference in 6-minute walk distance change between groups did not reach significance (P=0.10). Reduction in RV mass and chamber size was observed in the absence of pulmonary vascular unloading among hemodynamic nonresponders to sotatercept in 2 independent cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

articles.title: Response by Tsimikas et al to Letter Regarding Article, "Oxidized Phospholipids, Lipoprotein(a), and Cardiovascular Outcomes After Acute Coronary Syndrome".
Predicting the Release and Continuation of Physical Restraints for Hospitalized Patients: A Decision Tree Model.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To identify factors associated with the continuation and release of physical restraints (PRs) among hospitalized patients and develop a simple prediction model that is clinically applicable.

METHOD: Participants included 492 patients who were physically restrained upon hospital admission. A decision tree analysis was performed using the continuation or release of PR at discharge as the outcome and age, level of care required, cognitive impairments, Functional Independence Measure (FIM), and Nichijo-seikatsu Kino Hyokahyo (NSKH [Activities of Daily Living Functional Assessment Scale]) at admission as independent variables.

RESULTS: A decision tree was created using the total score and memory item of FIM and communication item of NSKH as predictor variables. The re-substitution accuracy of the created decision tree was 78.9%, and that for 10-fold cross-validation was 75.4%.

CONCLUSION: The created decision tree was considered a useful objective indicator for predicting the continuation or release of PRs in hospitalized patients.

articles.title: Caregiver Use and Interest of Supportive Resources.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore caregiver knowledge of, access to, and use of supportive resources, as well as advertising preferences.

METHOD: Participants were recruited through a national caregiver e-newsletter, local organizations, and an online platform. A total of 263 responses were analyzed in the current cross-sectional study using descriptive statistics and chi-squared tests.

RESULTS: Transportation was the most frequently used resource (46%) and respite care was the least used (28%). Of those who never used certain services, more than one half indicated some interest in future use. The top three preferred sources for receiving information about resources were social media, health care providers, and word of mouth.

CONCLUSION: Various supportive programs can help alleviate stress and fatigue associated with caregiving. Despite available resources, caregivers face barriers that may limit use, and some resources may be preferred over others. Organizations supporting caregivers can improve awareness by targeting social media and partnering with health care professionals to reach those most interested.

articles.title: Platelet activation in chemotherapy: from mechanistic deciphering to precision intervention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis are clinical paradoxes; patients may have both life-threatening bleeding and thrombotic events simultaneously. Here, we summarize recent advances elucidating this contradiction and introduce a framework for mechanism-guided precision management.

RECENT FINDINGS: Chemotherapies often induce a platelet hyper-reactive/procoagulant state despite numerical reduction. Based on the latest evidence, we propose a four-tier classification of chemotherapy-induced platelet activation: Type I directly binds to platelet receptors (e.g. doxorubicin-CLEC-2), triggers inside-out signaling, induces thrombosis and platelet clearance; Type II is caused by GSDME-mediated pyroptosis (e.g. cisplatin); Type III (cyclophosphamide, 5-fluorouracil) damages the endothelium and thus recruits and activates platelets; and Type IV (paclitaxel, methotrexate) has dual effects, contextually promoting or suppressing the procoagulant/aggregatory phenotype. Notably, immunotherapies (e.g. immune-checkpoint inhibitors) may also increase cardiovascular risk through platelet activation. New diagnostic biomarkers, including platelet activation markers (e.g., P-selectin, phosphatidylserine exposure, desialylation), glycocalicin for GPIbα shedding and GSDME-N for pyroptosis, will potentially shift platelet monitoring from rudimentary counting to a dynamic functional assessment of pivotal biomarkers.

SUMMARY: Recent findings provide a molecular basis for mechanism-directed thromboprophylaxis and the development of targeted adjunctive therapies in the chemotherapy setting, thus advancing precision oncology medicine that retains antitumor effects and restores platelet functional homeostasis.

articles.title: Circulating fatty acid-binding protein 4 and metabolic syndrome in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hormone molecular biology and clinical investigation
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Circulating fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) reflects adipose-tissue dysfunction and metabolic inflammation, but its association with metabolic syndrome remains uncertain. We quantified differences in circulating FABP4 between adults with and without metabolic syndrome and evaluated its diagnostic relevance.

CONTENT: PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were initially searched from inception through 1 May 2026 and updated on 17 September 2026. Peer-reviewed adult studies reporting serum or plasma FABP4 in relation to formally defined metabolic syndrome were eligible. Standardized mean differences were calculated as Hedges g and pooled using a restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects model with Hartung-Knapp inference. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, influence analyses, sensitivity analyses, and small-study effects were evaluated.

SUMMARY: Thirty-one publications were included. The primary meta-analysis comprised 15 effects and 2,702 participants. FABP4 was higher in metabolic syndrome (Hedges g=0.803, 95 % CI 0.606-1.001), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=75.9 %; τ2=0.0927) and a 95 % prediction interval of 0.116-1.490. Prespecified sensitivity and leave-one-out analyses were directionally consistent. The adjusted Begg-Mazumdar test (p=0.1142) and Pustejovsky-Rodgers SMD-specific regression (p=0.3533) were not statistically significant but did not exclude publication bias. Diagnostic AUCs ranged from 0.56 to 0.918.

OUTLOOK: Circulating FABP4 is elevated in metabolic syndrome and represents a promising adipokine biomarker linking adipose dysfunction with systemic metabolic disease. However, heterogeneity and limited standardized diagnostic evidence preclude its use as a universal stand-alone diagnostic test.

articles.title: Treatment adherence and clinical response in adolescents with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) commonly manifests during adolescence and requires sustained treatment. This study aimed to evaluate treatment initiation, adherence, and clinical response to different therapeutic modalities in adolescents with PMOS.

METHODS: This observational study included 40 adolescents aged 14-18 years with PMOS who were evaluated and treated at a tertiary adolescent gynecology clinic. Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for baseline characteristics and recommended treatments, and a face-to-face questionnaire was used to assess treatment initiation, self-reported duration of uninterrupted adherence, and changes in clinical symptoms. Associations between treatment adherence, clinical response, and pediatric endocrinology consultation were evaluated.

RESULTS: Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) were the most frequently recommended treatment (75.0 %, n=30). Treatment initiation rates were 83.3 % (n=25) for COCs, 36.8 % (n=7) for weight loss interventions, 100 % (n=5) for progesterone therapy, 66.7 % (n=2) for metformin, and 42.9 % (n=3) for laser hair removal. While 20 % of participants (n=8) reported never initiating the recommended treatments, only 10 % (n=4) maintained uninterrupted treatment adherence for longer than 6 months. Regression of menstrual irregularities was reported more frequently among participants with adherence for at least 3 months than among those with shorter adherence (82.6 % vs. 52.9 %, p=0.043); corresponding rates for hirsutism regression were 54.5 % and 13.3 %, respectively (p=0.011). Pediatric endocrinology consultation was associated with adherence for at least 3 months (65.2 % vs. 23.5 %, p=0.009).

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term treatment adherence was low despite relatively high treatment initiation rates. Longer adherence was associated with greater reported improvement in menstrual irregularities and hirsutism. Multidisciplinary management may improve treatment adherence and clinical response in adolescents with PMOS.

articles.title: [Berberine targets Smurf2 to regulate the TGF-β/Smads signaling pathway and alleviate myocardial fibrosis in rats with atrial fibrillation].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To explore the therapeutic efficacy and related mechanism of berberine in treating atrial fibrillation by regulating the transforming growth factor β (TGF-β)/Smads signaling pathway. Methods: The SD rats were divided into the normal group, the model group, the low-dose berberine group, the medium-dose berberine group, the high-dose berberine group, the amiodarone group, and the SRI-011381 group (SRI-011381 is a TGF-β signaling pathway activator). The atrial fibrillation rat model was constructed by injecting acetylcholine and calcium chloride. The fibrotic model was constructed by stimulating primary atrial fibroblasts with angiotensin Ⅱ (AngⅡ). The cells were divided into the control group, the AngⅡ group, the low berberine group, the high berberine group, the berberine+si-NC group (si-NC was a negative control small interfering RNA), and the berberine+si-Smad ubiquitination regulatory factor 2 (Smurf2) group (si-Smurf2 was a small interfering RNA targeting Smurf2). The pathological changes of atrial tissue were detected by hematoxylin-eosin staining, the fibrosis of atrial tissue was examined by Masson staining, and the expression levels of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), type Ⅰ collagen, type Ⅲ collagen, Smurf2, TGF-β1, p-Smad3, p-Smad2, Smad7, and TGF-β receptor type Ⅰ (TβR-Ⅰ) were detected by Western blotting. The pull-down experiment was used to screen the target proteins related to berberine. The relevant target proteins were then subjected to KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. Molecular docking was performed using AutoDock. Results: In rats, compared with the normal group, the duration of atrial fibrillation in the model group was increased, and the pathological damage and fibrosis of the atrial tissue were aggravated (P<0.05); compared with the model group, the high-dose berberine group showed a reduction in the duration of atrial fibrillation after treatment, and the pathological damage and fibrosis of the atrial tissue were alleviated (P<0.05). The pull-down experiment identified Smurf2 as the key target for the treatment of atrial fibrillation with berberine; KEGG analysis revealed that the key pathway was the TGF-β signaling pathway; molecular docking showed that berberine had a strong binding affinity for Smurf2. In the cells, compared with the AngⅡ group, the expression levels of TGF-β1, p-Smad3, p-Smad2, TβR-Ⅰ, type Ⅰ collagen, type Ⅲ collagen, and α-SMA proteins in the the low-dose berberine group, high-dose berberine group and the berberine+si-NC group were decreased, while the expression levels of Smurf2 and Smad7 proteins were increased (P<0.05); compared with the berberine+si-NC group, the expression levels of TGF-β1, p-Smad3, p-Smad2, TβR-Ⅰ, type Ⅰ collagen, type Ⅲ collagen, and α-SMA proteins in the berberine+si-Smurf2 group were increased, while the expression levels of Smurf2 and Smad7 proteins were decreased (P<0.05). In rats, compared with the model group, the expression levels of TGF-β1, p-Smad3, p-Smad2, TβR-Ⅰ, type Ⅰ collagen, type Ⅲ collagen, and α-SMA proteins in the high-dose berberine group were decreased, while the expression level of Smad7 protein was increased (P<0.05); compared with the high-dose berberine group, the expression levels of TGF-β1, p-Smad3, p-Smad2, TβR-Ⅰ, type Ⅰ collagen, type Ⅲ collagen, and α-SMA proteins in the SRI-011381 group were increased, while the expression level of Smad7 protein was decreased (P<0.05). Conclusion: Berberine may alleviate myocardial fibrosis in atrial fibrillation rats by targeting Smurf2 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smads signaling pathway.

articles.title: [Risk factors for long-term new-onset atrial fibrillation after percutaneous intramyocardial septal radiofrequency ablation in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To explore the influencing factors of long-term new-onset atrial fibrillation (AF) after percutaneous intramyocardial septal radiofrequency ablation (PIMSRA) in patients with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM). Methods: A total of 339 HOCM patients who underwent PIMSRA at the Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Diagnosis and Treatment Center of Xijing Hospital, Air Force Medical University from October 2016 to October 2022 were retrospectively enrolled. Patients were followed up until December 31, 2024. According to whether AF occurred more than 30 days after operation, patients were divided into the AF group and the non-AF group. Clinical data were collected and compared between the two groups. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression model was used to identify independent influencing factors for long-term new-onset AF after PIMSRA. A receiver-operating characteristic curve was plotted to evaluate the predictive performance of baseline left-atrial diameter (LAD) and determine its optimal cut-off value. Kaplan-Meier survival curve was used to assess AF-free survival. Results: The included patients were aged (47±13) years, and 209 (61.7%) were male. There were 17 patients in the AF group and 322 in the non-AF group. The follow-up duration was (4.0±1.7) years, and the incidence of long-term new-onset post-procedural AF was 5.0% (17/339). Compared with the non-AF group, the AF group had older age ((56±12) years vs. (47±13) years), larger baseline LAD ((47.1±6.6) mm vs. (40.6±4.9) mm), higher E/e' ratio ((20.4±5.4) vs. (17.3±5.9)), greater premature atrial contraction burden (0.26% (0.09%, 0.39%) vs. 0.02% (0, 0.07%)), and higher provoked left ventricular outflow-tract pressure gradient ((151.6±41.2) mmHg vs. (125.2±44.0) mmHg, 1 mmHg=0.133 kPa) (all P<0.05). At the final follow-up, post-operative LAD improved compared with baseline in both groups (AF group: (43.5±6.7) mm vs. (47.1±6.6) mm, P=0.031; non-AF group: (36.4±4.4) mm vs. (40.6±4.9) mm, P<0.001). Post-operative LAD remained larger in the AF group than in the non-AF group ((43.5±6.7) mm vs. (36.4±4.4) mm, P<0.001). Multivariate Cox regression demonstrated that baseline LAD (per 1-SD increase, HR=1.171, 95%CI 1.053-1.302, P=0.004) was an independent influencing factor for long-term new-onset AF after PIMSRA. Receiver-operating characteristic curve analysis showed that the optimal cut-off value of baseline LAD was 43.5 mm, yielding an area under the curve of 0.79 (95%CI 0.69-0.90, P<0.001), with a sensitivity of 71% and specificity of 75%. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that the 1-, 3- and 5-year AF-free survival rates were 98.5%, 96.2% and 94.0%, respectively. Conclusion: Baseline LAD is an independent influencing factor for long-term new-onset AF after PIMSRA in HOCM patients. It can assist clinicians in early identification of high-risk individuals and formulation of individualized follow-up strategies.

articles.title: [Association between sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors and mortality in cancer patients with coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes].
articles.journal: Zhonghua xin xue guan bing za zhi
articles.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the association between sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) use and risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and cancer mortality in cancer patients with coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes. Methods: This is a multicenter, retrospective cohort study. The study included adult patients diagnosed with cancer and concomitant coronary artery disease and type2 diabetes at 82 hospitals in Tianjin between August 2017 and July 2025. Patients were grouped according to SGLT2i use after cancer diagnosis and matched in a 1∶1 ratio using propensity score matching. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included cardiovascular and cancer mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between SGLT2i use and outcomes. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to age, sex, comorbidities (hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease), and medication use (metformin and insulin). Restricted mean survival time (RMST) analysis was performed to quantify the survival benefits associated with SGLT2i. Results: A total of 18 383 patients, aged 70 (64, 76) years were included, and 9 408 (51.2%) were males. The SGLT2i group comprised 6 537 patients, and the non-SGLT2i group comprised 11 846 patients. After propensity score matching, each group comprised 4 784 patients. During a median follow-up of 995 days, 1 642 deaths (17.2%) were recorded. Multivariable Cox regression showed that SGLT2i use was associated with significantly lower risks of all-cause mortality (HR=0.398, 95%CI 0.357-0.444, P<0.01), cardiovascular mortality (HR=0.502, 95%CI 0.418-0.603, P<0.01), and cancer mortality (HR=0.263, 95%CI 0.209-0.330, P<0.01). Subgroup analyses showed that the association between SGLT2i use and reduced risk of all-cause mortality was stronger among patients younger than 65 years and those without hypertension or heart failure (all P for interaction<0.05). The RMST for all-cause mortality was significantly longer in the SGLT2i group than in the non-SGLT2i group over a 60-month horizon (RMST difference: 7.02 months, 95%CI 6.24-7.80, P<0.01; RMST ratio: 1.15, 95%CI 1.13-1.17, P<0.01). Conclusion: In patients with cancer and comorbid coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes, SGLT2i use is significantly associated with reduced risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and cancer mortality.

articles.title: Incremental associations of pharmacological components in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We conducted a component network meta-analysis (CNMA) of phase 3/4 randomized trials to evaluate incremental effects of pharmacological therapies in heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFmrEF/HFpEF; LVEF >40%).

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through 1 August 2025 (updated 30 March 2026). We performed an additive CNMA evaluating cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) and assessed certainty of evidence.

RESULTS: Twenty-four trials and five secondary reports were included. The primary network was sparse (10 trials, 12 regimens), constraining interaction detection and component stability. Incretin-based interventions (pooling semaglutide and tirzepatide, iHR 0.69, 95% CI 0.53-0.91), SGLT-2 inhibitors (0.80, 0.74-0.88), ARNis (0.82, 0.68-0.99), and MRAs (0.89, 0.81-0.98) showed significant component associations, driven principally by fewer HFHs. No drug class significantly reduced mortality. SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs remained significant across sensitivity analyses except LVEF ≥50%, with SGLT-2 inhibitors most precise. ARNi benefits lost significance under stricter background therapy thresholds (>60%) and contemporary trial restrictions. Evidence for incretins was low-certainty and sensitive to trial selection.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT-2 inhibitors and MRAs provide the most robust incremental benefit, while evidence for other drug classes remains context-dependent. These findings should guide research priorities rather than define combination regimens.

PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: http://www.crd.york.ac.uk/ PROSPERO identifier is CRD420251107058.

articles.title: Neuronal IL-34 programs microglial activity via the TGF-β-MEF2C axis to constrain neuroinflammation following brain ischemia.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Brain ischemia induces robust neuroinflammation driven by microglial activation, yet whether ischemic neurons actively reprogram microglial phenotypes to limit inflammation remains elusive. Here, we identify neuronal interleukin-34 (IL-34) as a critical immunomodulatory signal that maintains microglial homeostasis after cerebral ischemia. We demonstrate that ischemic injury augments IL-34-CSF1R signaling between neurons and microglia. Neuron-specific overexpression of Il34 (Syn1-Il34tg mice) attenuated infarct volume and neurodeficits after middle cerebral artery occlusion, whereas neuronal Il34 knockdown exacerbated brain injury. Microglial depletion abolished IL-34-mediated neuroprotection, suggesting microglia as essential effectors. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that neuronal IL-34 preserved homeostatic microglial signatures (P2ry12, Cx3cr1, Tgfbr1), while suppressing inflammatory activities (Il1b, Tnf, Cxcl2) through upregulation of the transcription factor MEF2C. Mechanistically, IL-34 activated TGF-β signaling in microglia and inhibition of TGF-β signaling abolished the protective effects of IL-34, whereas microglia-specific Mef2c overexpression rescued neuroprotection despite TGF-β blockade. Thus, ischemic neurons deploy IL-34 to orchestrate the immunoregulatory activity of microglia via the TGF-β-MEF2C axis, representing a previously unrecognized endogenous mechanism counteracting neuroinflammation. Our study reveals neuronal IL-34 as a potential therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of a transvalvular microaxial flow pump in infarct-related cardiogenic shock from the perspective of German statutory health insurance.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In infarct-related cardiogenic shock, a transvalvular microaxial flow pump reduced 180 day mortality but increased adverse events. We evaluated its cost-effectiveness for German statutory health insurance (SHI).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A cohort state-transition model compared the two strategies over a lifetime horizon: a 180 day acute phase from trial outcomes, and chronic states with or without heart failure. Costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were discounted at 3% in 2023 euros. Parameter uncertainty was assessed probabilistically and unresolved acute payments by threshold analysis.

RESULTS: The pump yielded 1.06 additional QALYs at incremental costs of €38,121 and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €36,083 per QALY. At an illustrative willingness-to-pay threshold of €50,000 per QALY, the probability of cost-effectiveness was 86%. Bleeding 21.8 versus 11.9%, limb ischemia 5.6 versus 1.1%. Due to unavailable arm-specific case-group data, the reference analysis assumed equal case-group, nursing and readmission payments between arms. Net monetary benefit remained positive when the residual acute payment difference was below €14,703.

CONCLUSIONS: Under the reference assumptions, the pump may be cost-effective for German SHI, conditional on an unresolved acute payment difference that arm-specific routine billing data could determine.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT01633502. This model-based economic analysis was not separately registered.

articles.title: Unconventional modulation of Nav1.4 by a scorpion toxin through cooperative binding to voltage sensor and the pore domain.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels are targeted by animal peptide toxins, which serve as powerful molecular probes for dissecting channel structure-function relationships and lead molecules for drug discovery. β-scorpion toxins trap voltage sensor domains to remodel Nav channel gating, yet high-resolution structural evidence defining this process remains elusive. Here, we characterize LmNaTx1, a β-scorpion toxin from Lychas mucronatus. LmNaTx1 exerts state-dependent bimodal modulation on Nav1.4: it facilitates channel activation while suppressing sodium conductance, accelerates slow-inactivation onset, and delays recovery from slow inactivation. We solved the 2.68 Å cryo-EM structure of the LmNaTx1-hNav1.4 complex, revealing that LmNaTx1 inserts into the extracellular cleft jointly formed by domain II voltage sensor (VSDII) and the extracellular loop III (ECLIII) of the pore domain. Toxin binding remodels the S3-S4II loop and displaces S0/S3II helices to trap VSDII within a pre-activated intermediate state. MD simulations recapitulate step-wise VSDII conformational transitions and demonstrate that toxin-driven rearrangements tighten the intracellular pore gate. Mutagenesis combined with electrophysiology confirm that VSDII trapping remodels the activation and inactivation gating, whereas ECLIII engagement contributes both to inhibition and activation. Subtype-specific sequence variations in the ECLIII region underlie the prominent species- and isoform-dependent activities of the toxin toward insect and mammalian Nav channels. Our study provides a structural basis for the dual-action mechanisms of β-scorpion toxins on Nav channels and presents a structural framework for understanding toxin binding, channel gating modulation, ecological adaptation, and rational drug design.

articles.title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these "vaccinal" effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell-dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our findings identify the Fc-FcγR axis as a critical determinant of the reliable induction of durable remission and provide a mechanistic framework for developing Fc-engineered bNAbs designed to enhance vaccinal immunity and advance antibody-based strategies with the potential to achieve functional cure.

articles.title: Gaplinc regulates myeloid metabolic pathways in trans in endotoxic shock.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) Gaplinc is a known regulator of the innate immune response; however, the systemic mechanisms governing its influence on survival during endotoxic shock remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Gaplinc as a dosage-dependent immune and metabolic rheostat. While Gaplinc knockout (KO) mice exhibit elevated baseline immune response genes (IRGs) and resistance to lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced shock, we demonstrate that transgenic Gaplinc overexpression produces the opposite phenotype: suppressed baseline IRGs, diminished nuclear p65, and hypersensitivity to endotoxemia. Analysis of heterozygous and rescue models reveals that Gaplinc functions in trans and is haploinsufficient, requiring strict transcript dosage to maintain wild-type immune homeostasis. To uncover the mechanistic basis of this survival advantage, we performed RNA Antisense Purification (RAP-MS) and identified the mitochondrial enzyme MCCC1 as a primary Gaplinc binding partner. Loss of Gaplinc drives systemic metabolic reprogramming, characterized by reduced mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and a protective lipidome featuring elevated lysophosphatidylcholines and diminished free fatty acids. Finally, while myeloid-specific conditional KOs confer partial protection against LPS-induced hypothermia, tissue-wide expression mapping and sex-dimorphic clinical chemistries suggest a broader, multisystemic role for the lncRNA. Collectively, these data demonstrate that Gaplinc bridges transcriptomic immune regulation with systemic lipid and metabolic output, dictating survival outcomes in systemic inflammation.

articles.title: Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia: A 10-y follow-up.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Vacant lot greening has been shown to reduce violence and crime in the short-term [C. C. Branas et al., Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 115, 2946-2951 (2018)]. We assessed the 10-y impact of a 2013 clustered randomized controlled trial (RCT) of lot greening in Philadelphia on violence and crime. We measured lot greening by treatment assignment from the original 2013 cluster RCT and a longitudinal greening score to assess the sustainability of the treatment assignment from 2012 through 2023. Our outcomes were the annual reported total crime, violent crime, and firearm violent crime per square mile at each lot. We conducted intent-to-treat and contamination-adjusted intent-to-treat analyses to estimate the local average treatment effect on relative change in crime. Lots randomized to the full greening intervention remained greener over time compared to other lots. In intent-to-treat analyses, compared to lots that received no intervention, lots that received any intervention had a 9% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.96) and a 9% decrease in violent crime (estimate = 0.91, 95%CI = 0.86, 0.97) per square mile per year. In contamination-adjusted analyses, compared to lots without sustained greening treatment, lots with sustained greening treatment had a 12% decrease in density of any crime (estimate = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.93) and an 11% decrease in density of violent crime (estimate = 0.89, 95%CI = 0.83, 0.95) per square mile per year. Even after a decade, vacant lot greening continues to prevent violence.

articles.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC-HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC-HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure-temperature (P-T) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC-HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.

articles.title: Impact pathways of a jurisdictional approach to slowing deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Governance of many of the world's largest remaining tropical forests is shared across multiple levels of government, giving subnational jurisdictions a central role in forest management. This has motivated growing interest in jurisdictional approaches (JAs) to control deforestation. For JAs to deliver on national and international conservation priorities, those priorities must be translated into incentives that reduce deforestation at the jurisdictional level. Brazil's Priority List (PL), launched in 2008, creates such incentives by identifying high-deforestation municipalities, subjecting them to intensified monitoring, enforcement, and credit restrictions, and establishing jurisdiction-wide criteria for exit that make municipalities accountable for deforestation within their borders. While prior studies show that the PL reduces deforestation, it remains unclear where these reductions occur and whether there is displacement across land tenure types or into neighboring municipalities. We assemble a municipality-level panel dataset for the Brazilian Legal Amazon (2000-2024) that combines PL designations with annual deforestation disaggregated by land tenure. Using a heterogeneity-robust difference-in-differences estimator, we estimate effects within and across municipalities. We find large and statistically significant reductions concentrated on private lands, including agrarian reform settlements and other private properties. Within listed municipalities, we find no evidence of decreased or increased clearing in Protected Areas, Indigenous Territories, or undesignated public lands. Total deforestation also declines in neighboring municipalities, with reductions concentrated on private lands. These findings are consistent with the PL translating national conservation priorities into local land-use change while limiting displacement, offering insights for the design of jurisdictional approaches aimed at forest conservation.

articles.title: Salpyran ligands at the interface of copper chemistry and biology: structure-function relationships, metal selectivity, redox control, and biological interactions.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates Salpyran, a tetradentate N3O ligand, and electronically modified derivatives. Systematic potentiometry reveals that substituent effects modestly modulate metal binding without significantly improving Cu(II)/Zn(II) selectivity. Direct comparison with trientine identifies an unexpected Fe(III) preference for Salpyran, thus limiting its application as a copper-selective chelator but provides key design principles for future structural refinement. Our data shows that. Cu(II)-Salpyran suppresses ROS generation, protects peptides from oxidation, and binds DNA non-oxidatively. Proof-of-concept 64Cu radiolabelling shows PET imaging compatibility, though Fe(III) competition requires framework refinement. Cytotoxicity studies reveal context-dependent antiproliferative activity: copper coordination enhances potency in most cancer lines but reduces it in carboplatin-resistant NSCLC models, without cross-resistance. This work establishes Salpyran as a versatile platform and provides design principles linking ligand structure, metal selectivity, redox behaviour, and biological activity.

articles.title: The potential of transcranial direct current stimulation to enhance P300-based brain-computer interface speller performance: a feasibility study.
articles.abstract: Objective.To evaluate whether anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) enhances the P300 event-related potential and whether this enhancement translates into improved target-non-target automatic classification.Approach.Ten participants without known motor impairments, neurological or psychiatric disorders completed real and sham multichannel tDCS sessions in a randomized, counterbalanced, sham-controlled, single-blind crossover design. Each session included pre- and post-stimulation brain-computer interface (BCI) runs using a P300 speller and an attention-demanding task during stimulation. P300 peak amplitudes,R2discrimination between target and non-target events, and channel-wise offline classification accuracy were computed. Fatigue was assessed at four time points. Statistical analyses assessed effects ofStimulation type(real vs sham) andTime(pre vs post) on P300-related metrics. An exploratory analysis compared good and poor baseline performers using BCI calibration data.Main results.SignificantStimulation × Timeinteractions in P300 peak amplitude were observed at P3, PO8, POz, and Oz, reflecting differential pre-to-post changes between real and sham stimulation. Channel-wise classification accuracy demonstrated a significant interaction betweenStimulationandTimeat P4, indicating a localized improvement in offline target-non-target discrimination after real stimulation. This improvement was not accompanied by improved online character-level BCI performance.Significance. Multichannel anodal tDCS over the left DLPFC produced localized neurophysiological P300 modulation in parieto-occipital regions, with a positive trend in channel-wise classification accuracy, reaching statistical significance only at P4. Together with the larger, although non-significant, gains observed in participants with low baseline performance, these findings suggest that tDCS effects may be more pronounced in this subgroup, which is relevant for future translation to clinical populations. These findings support the feasibility of using left DLPFC tDCS to modulate P300-related activity and target-non-target discriminability, while highlighting the need to better understand how localized neurophysiological changes propagate through the complete BCI decoding pipeline.

articles.title: Cytoreduction for MPN-associated splanchnic vein thrombosis.
Multivariate searchlight decoding of structural disconnection and network features for predicting post-stroke deficits.
articles.abstract: Objective.Lesion-symptom mapping and structural disconnection analyses have advanced our understanding of post-stroke deficits but remain predominantly based on forward inference, limiting identification of regions specifically predictive of behavioral impairment. We developed a multivariate voxelwise searchlight decoding framework for inverse inference integrating probabilistic structural disconnection with network-topological features.Approach.The analysis included 326 stroke patients from the GRECogVASC cohort assessed six months after stroke. For each patient, an age-specific probabilistic structural disconnection map was reconstructed using normative diffusion MRI tractography from 403 healthy controls. Within each voxel-centered searchlight, four features were extracted: disconnection probability, degree, clustering coefficient, and closeness centrality. Support vector machine classifiers were trained within deficit-specific decoding spaces using balanced bootstrap aggregation and majority voting to predict motor, executive, and processing-action-speed impairments. Statistical significance was assessed using 1000 permutations, retaining voxels that consistently performed above chance across bootstrap iterations. Decoding-derived regions were subsequently assessed for within-cohort individual-level classification.Main results.Initial validation focused on left and right motor impairments, identifying predictive regions primarily within the contralateral precentral gyrus, internal capsule, and corticospinal tract, with mean accuracy ranges of 68.7%-77.9%, 66.4%-74.6%, and 64.8%-71.8%, respectively. At the individual level, decoding-derived masks preserved overall classification performance, with accuracy improvements of up to 2.6% for individual deficits while reducing voxel dimensionality by up to 95.4%. Executive dysfunction and processing-action-speed deficits showed statistically above-chance but lower accuracies (54.5%-66.9%). Executive dysfunction involved predominantly left-lateralized frontotemporal regions, whereas processing-action-speed deficits involved distributed fronto-insular, temporal, parietal, visual-association, and commissural pathways.Significance.The multivariate searchlight decoding framework integrating structural disconnection and network topology provides an inverse-inference approach complementary to lesion- and disconnection-symptom mapping for identifying spatially specific predictive patterns after stroke. The strong motor findings provide proof-of-concept support for the approach, whereas the cognitive results support its extension to distributed behavioral domains while underscoring the need for independent replication before neuroanatomical or clinical interpretation (Clinical trial registration: NCT01339195).

articles.title: Effects of benralizumab on clinical outcomes and small airway function in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma: a real-world study.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of benralizumab in Chinese patients with severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA), focusing on small airway dysfunction.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed SEA patients treated with benralizumab for ≥6 months. Outcomes included ACQ-5 scores, blood eosinophils, IgE, FeNO, spirometry, functional electrical impedance tomography (fEIT), and adverse events. ROC curve analysis identified baseline predictors of clinical remission.

RESULTS: Among 24 patients, blood eosinophils were virtually eliminated by week 4. At 6 months, patients showed significantly reduced IgE and FeNO, alongside improved FEV1, PEF, and MEF25-75 (p < 0.05). fEIT sensitively detected regional pulmonary ventilation improvements. Overall, 79.2% of patients achieved clinical remission at 6 months. Baseline eosinophil counts were significantly higher in remitters and strongly predicted clinical remission (AUC = 0.874; optimal cutoff: 460 cells/μL). Treatment was well-tolerated, with only one mild fever reported.

CONCLUSION: Benralizumab significantly improves asthma control, global lung function, and regional small airway ventilation in Chinese SEA patients. Baseline blood eosinophils serve as a robust biomarker to predict clinical remission and guide precision patient selection.Trial registration: ChiCTR2600121928.

articles.title: Managing Abnormal Uterine Bleeding During Anticoagulant Therapy in Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulant therapies, including heparins, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) such as rivaroxaban, apixaban, and dabigatran, are crucial for the treatment and the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE). While DOACs offer improved safety profiles, their use, especially in women of reproductive age, increases the risk of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), particularly heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB). HMB, defined as blood loss exceeding 80 mL per cycle or causing significant life disruption, is associated with reduced quality of life and substantial economic costs. Women on anticoagulants report higher incidences of HMB, often requiring adjustments in therapy or additional interventions. Management strategies include referral for a gynecological consultation, adjustment of hormonal therapy and anticoagulant treatment, administration of tranexamic acid, and treatment of iron deficiency. This narrative review underscores the importance of a comprehensive, personalized approach to managing AUB in women on anticoagulants to optimize both anticoagulation effectiveness and patient quality of life.

articles.title: Intuitive knowledge of object acoustics enables perceptual separation of physical variables from impact sounds.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Upon hearing objects collide, humans can estimate physical attributes such as material and mass. Although the physics of sound generation is well established, the inverse problem that listeners solve-of inferring physical parameters from sound-remains poorly understood. Classical accounts posit the use of acoustic cues that correlate with physical variables but do not explain how humans might distinguish multiple concurrent physical causes. To study this problem, we measured impulse responses from hundreds of everyday objects, extracted their resonances, and used statistics of the resonances to build a probabilistic generative model of impact sounds. We then used the model to synthesize and manipulate stimuli for experiments measuring judgments of physical variables. Humans accurately judged object properties from collision sounds. However, when both of the colliding objects varied, performance was impaired if the distribution of object resonances deviated from those measured in real-world objects. The results suggest that humans have internalized the statistical regularities of real-world object acoustics, and use this knowledge to separate the acoustic contributions of the distinct objects in the world that give rise to sounds.

articles.title: From the Mailbox to the Microphone: The Neurology Podcast and the Evolution of Medical Education.
articles.abstract: When the Neurology® Podcast debuted in September 2007, podcasting occupied the fringes of academic medicine. Smartphones had only just emerged, and streaming audio was uncommon. Nearly 2 decades later, the Neurology Podcast stands among the longest-running physician-hosted podcasts in medicine and has fundamentally expanded how one of the world's leading neurology journals educates its readers. Although the technologies through which neurologists consume information have changed dramatically since 2007, the podcast's enduring success reflects a remarkably constant mission: to deliver practical, clinically relevant education through authentic conversation. This article traces the origins and evolution of the Neurology Podcast through archival documents, contemporaneous publications, and personal recollections from those who created it.

articles.title: Germline Genetic Variants and Epilepsy Surgery Response: Individual Participant Pooled Analysis of 272 Patients.
authors: Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) Surgery Workgroup, and the Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) Genetics Workgroup
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Genetic testing is increasingly used in presurgical evaluation, but the yield of resection and ablation across germline genetic epilepsies remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review of MEDLINE (PubMed) and Scopus and added cases from 3 institutional cohorts and the Pediatric Epilepsy Research Consortium (PERC) databases, including individuals with pathogenic/likely pathogenic germline variants besides tuberous sclerosis who underwent resection or laser ablation. Etiologies were grouped into biologically informed categories (GATORopathies, vascular, overgrowth, copy number variants (CNVs), channelopathies, synaptopathies, and other). Primary outcome was seizure freedom (Engel I) at the last follow-up. Group comparisons used Fisher exact and Kruskal-Wallis tests (α = 0.05; Bonferroni when applicable). Prespecified sensitivity analyses stratified by lesional status, excluded GATORopathies, and restricted to literature-only cases.

RESULTS: We included 224 literature cases (65 studies), 36 institutional cases, and 12 PERC cases (n = 272). The median follow-up was 24 months (interquartile range 12-48.0). Seizure freedom was achieved in vascular disorders 14/19 (73.6%), GATORopathies 79/120 (65.8%), CNVs 18/31 (58.0%), overgrowth 9/16 (56.6%), channelopathies 13/43 (30.0%), synaptopathies 4/18 (22.2%), and other 11/25 (44.0%) (overall p < 0.001). Among cases with available imaging results, 208/253 (82.2%) had epileptogenic MRI lesions, including 64% of channelopathies and 80% of the synaptopathies. In univariate contrasts (each category vs all others), odds of seizure freedom were higher for vascular disorders (2.64-fold, 95% CI 0.87-9.65) and GATORopathies (2.41-fold, 95% CI 1.44-4.09), and lower for synaptopathies (∼4.2-fold lower, OR 0.23, 95% CI 0.05-0.77) and channelopathies (∼4.5-fold lower, OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09-0.48). Direction and magnitude were consistent across prespecified sensitivity analyses (lesional only, literature only, exclusion of GATORopathies).

DISCUSSION: Resective surgeries can be effective in germline genetic epilepsies, but outcomes vary by pathway. Disorders with discrete, lesional substrates (GATORopathies, vascular) show the highest likelihood of seizure freedom, whereas channelopathies and synaptopathies, despite the presence of MRI lesions, have substantially lower yields even in lesional cases. Prospective, genotype-aware surgical registries with standardized reporting (EEG, imaging, and pathology) and time-to-event outcomes are needed to refine the selection of surgical candidates and quantify seizure and non-seizure-related outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination.

RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%).

DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).
