The dual primary endpoints were a composite of coronary heart disease death, MI, ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven arterial revascularization (4-point [4-P] MACE) and 3-point (3-P) MACE (not including ischemia-driven arterial revascularization). In this prespecified analysis, all dual primary endpoint events (first and subsequent) were analyzed using negative binomial regression models.

RESULTS: Among 12,257 patients followed for a median of 4.6 years, there were 1,654 first 4-P MACE and 1,107 subsequent events (67% more) for 2,761 total events. There were 779 first 3-P MACE and 146 subsequent events (19% more) for 925 total events. Evolocumab reduced the rate of first 4-P MACE by 19% (HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.73-0.89; P < 0.0001), was associated with a reduction of subsequent events by 25% (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.61-0.91), and reduced total events by 20% (IRR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.71-0.90; P = 0.0002). Likewise for 3-P MACE, evolocumab reduced the rate of first events by 25% (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.65-0.86; P < 0.0001), was associated with a reduction of subsequent events by 37% (IRR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.42-0.94) and reduced total events by 27% (IRR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.63-0.86; P = 0.0001). Based on annualized incidence rate differences over the full follow-up period, evolocumab was projected to prevent 31 first and 24 subsequent 4-P MACE, for 55 total events per 1,000 patients over 5 years (95% CI: for the total-event difference: 36-74). The corresponding estimates for 3-P MACE were 20 first and 5 subsequent events, for 25 total events per 1,000 patients over 5 years (95% CI: for the total event difference: 15-37). Results were consistent across key subgroups, including by statin intensity and presence of qualifying atherosclerosis.

CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of patients experiencing a cardiovascular event had more than 1 event. The addition of evolocumab reduced the total number of MACE, providing support for the role of intensive low-density lipoprotein cholesterol lowering to prevent first and subsequent MACE in patients at high cardiovascular risk and no prior MI or stroke. (Effect of Evolocumab in Patients at High Cardiovascular Risk Without Prior Myocardial Infarction or Stroke [VESALIUS-CV]; NCT03872401).

articles.title: Low Ventricular Chamber Stiffness Identifies a High-Risk Eccentric Remodeling Phenotype in the Fontan Circulation: A FORCE Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rising end-diastolic pressure in patients with a Fontan circulation has led to the hypothesis that circulatory failure is driven by progressive ventricular stiffening. However, end-diastolic pressure is influenced by loading conditions and extracardiac constraint and may not accurately reflect chamber stiffness. We aimed to characterize ventricular chamber stiffness using the end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship and examine its clinical and prognostic significance in patients with a Fontan circulation.

METHODS: In the FORCE registry (Fontan Outcomes Registry Using Clinical Examinations), chamber stiffness was quantified with the exponential coefficient β derived from single-beat end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship reconstruction using paired catheterization and cardiovascular magnetic resonance data. The β values were standardized as body surface area- and sex-based Z scores and related to clinical characteristics, ventricular remodeling, and a composite adverse outcome (death, transplantation listing, sustained atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, protein-losing enteropathy, or plastic bronchitis).

RESULTS: Among 814 patients (median age, 14.7 years), median β was 0.034 mL-1 (0.025-0.046). Lower β Z score was associated with dominant right ventricle, eccentric remodeling with reduced ejection fraction, increased collateral flow and intracardiac recirculation, greater symptom burden, and higher arrhythmia prevalence, despite similar filling pressures. Over a median follow-up of 2.7 years (0.9-6.1 years), lower β Z score independently predicted adverse outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.30 per 1-SD decrease [95% CI 1.04-1.61]). A β Z score <-0.71, β<0.025 mL-1, or body surface area-indexed end-diastolic volume >103 mL/m2 showed similarly modest discrimination for adverse outcomes overall (area under the curve, 0.59), with greater discrimination in dominant right ventricles.

CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, lower rather than higher chamber stiffness was associated with adverse Fontan outcomes, identifying a high-compliance phenotype characterized by ventricular dilation and eccentric remodeling. These findings suggest that, in the contemporary FORCE cohort, Fontan failure might be more closely associated with this remodeling phenotype than with progressive stiffening.

articles.title: May the FORCE Be With You: Focusing on Ventricular Compliance in Fontan Failure.
Impact of cytoreductive therapy in myeloproliferative neoplasm-associated splanchnic vein thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN) are at risk of splanchnic vein thrombosis (SVT). Previous studies have failed to demonstrate a benefit of hydroxyurea therapy in preventing recurrent thrombosis after SVT, but they are limited by small sample sizes and inability to account for starting, stopping, or switching of cytoreductive therapies. To better assess the impact of cytoreductive therapy on thrombosis recurrence, we performed a retrospective cohort study of patients with MPN-SVT from the international GASTRO-MPN consortium, treating cytoreductive therapy as a time-dependent covariate. We identified 757 patients, of whom 43% were treated with cytoreductive therapy. During a median follow-up of 7.4 years, 256 patients (34%) had thrombosis recurrence; 145 (19%) had SVT extension/recurrence/transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt thrombosis, and 138 (18%) had a thrombosis recurrence outside the splanchnic bed (74% were venous). In addition, 262 patients (35%) experienced clinically relevant bleeding and 170 (22%) died. After adjusting for age, sex, previous thrombosis, timing of MPN diagnosis relative to SVT, anticoagulation initiation within 30 days of SVT diagnosis, MPN type, JAK2 status, other cancers and cirrhosis, cytoreductive therapy was associated with a decreased risk of recurrent thrombosis (hazard ratio [HR], 0.67; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.50-0.89; P = .01). This was driven by a lower risk of SVT extension/recurrence (HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.42-0.90; P = .01) but not by extra-splanchnic thrombosis recurrence (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.72-1.30; P = .82). In a subgroup of patients without erythrocytosis/thrombocytosis at initial SVT (n = 275), cytoreductive therapy was associated with an HR of 0.65 (95% CI, 0.40-1.07; P = .09) for recurrent thrombosis. These data support the use of cytoreductive therapy for patients with MPN-SVT to prevent recurrent thrombosis, particularly SVT extension/recurrence.

articles.title: Outcomes after 7/8 and <7/8 mismatched unrelated donor PBSC transplantation with PTCy: results from the ACCESS trial.
articles.abstract: The ACCESS trial is a prospective, multicenter phase 2 trial evaluating peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) transplantation using 4/8 to 7/8 HLA-mismatched unrelated donors (MMUD) with posttransplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy), tacrolimus, and mycophenolate. Adults undergoing first hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) with myeloablative conditioning or reduced-intensity conditioning (RIC)/nonmyeloablative conditioning (NMA) were enrolled. This expanded analysis includes all enrolled adult PBSC HCT recipients, including the protocol-specified RIC/NMA cohort expansion, to improve precision of outcome estimates and provide descriptive analyses by HLA-match level. Among 268 adults, 183 received 7/8 and 85 received <7/8 MMUD grafts; 82.4% of the <7/8 cohort received 6/8 MMUD grafts. Median follow-up among survivors was 11.9 months. At 1 year, overall survival was 78.6% (95% confidence interval [CI], 71.9-83.9) in the 7/8 cohort and 85.6% (95% CI, 76.0-91.5) in the <7/8 cohort. One-year relapse, nonrelapse mortality, and graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)-free relapse-free survival were 17.1%, 13.7%, and 51.1% vs 22.8%, 8.4%, and 54.6%, in the 7/8 and <7/8 cohorts, respectively. The cumulative incidence of grade II to IV and grade III to IV acute GVHD by day 100 was 36.6% and 7.7% in the 7/8 cohort vs 28.3% and 5.9% in the <7/8 cohort. Moderate-to-severe chronic GVHD at 1 year was 11.3% vs 7.7% in the 7/8 and <7/8 cohorts, respectively. Among adult ACCESS trial participants treated on a uniform young-donor PBSC/PTCy platform, short-term outcomes with predominantly 6/8 MMUD transplantation were encouraging. Because donor match level was not prospectively assigned and between-group comparisons were exploratory, these findings are descriptive and should not be interpreted as establishing equivalence with 7/8 MMUD transplantation. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT04904588.

articles.title: Safety of proton pump inhibitors: an overview of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
A phase 2a randomized study to evaluate sapablursen in patients with non-transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia intermedia.
articles.abstract: Non-transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia intermedia (NTDT) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder characterized by decreased β-globin production in erythroid cells resulting from mutations in the β-globin gene that is not treated with transfusion. NTDT is further characterized by a relative excess of α-globin, which drives ineffective erythropoiesis resulting in increased iron absorption and ultimately iron overload. Sapablursen is an antisense oligonucleotide that reduces the production of transmembrane protease serine 6 (TMPRSS6) and increases hepcidin production. This phase 2a study evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of sapablursen in patients with NTDT. Eligible patients had a clinical diagnosis of NTDT with genotypic confirmation of β-globin gene mutations. Twenty-nine patients with NTDT were treated with sapablursen at doses ranging from 30 to 160 mg once every 4 weeks for up to 2 years. Sapablursen was generally safe and well tolerated. The study did not meet its primary or secondary end points of increased blood hemoglobin or reduced liver iron content (LIC). In earlier studies, including a phase 1 trial in healthy volunteers and a phase 2 trial in patients with polycythemia vera, sapablursen produced dose-dependent increases in serum hepcidin levels. However, in patients with NTDT, similar doses and exposures did not lead to consistent dose-dependent increases in serum hepcidin. LIC and serum erythroferrone were elevated at baseline and throughout the current study. These 2 factors may prevent the elevation of serum hepcidin via the TMPRSS6 pathway. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04059406.

articles.title: Early Hemodynamic Safety of Simultaneous Initiation of Finerenone and Empagliflozin in Chronic Kidney Disease and Type 2 Diabetes: The CONFIDENCE Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Clinical use of clinician-initiated cystatin C testing in assessing renal function in a subset of patients taking tenofovir disoproxil/emtricitabine as HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis: a retrospective chart review.
Infraposition, Esthetics, Survival, and Complications of Implant-Supported Crowns in the Anterior Maxilla: A Retrospective Study with 11 to 21 Years of Follow-up.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To elucidate the long-term esthetic qualities, clinical outcomes, and patient satisfaction with implant-supported single crowns (ISSCs) to replace missing teeth in the anterior maxilla.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Of 172 patients provided with ISSCs, 107 patients with 133 single crowns accepted participation in a follow-up study after 11 to 21 years. Esthetics were assessed using the Pink Esthetic Score (PES), the White Esthetic Score (WES), and the California Dental Association (CDA) index. Patients completed questionnaires on esthetics, function, complications, and health. Most patients were enrolled in planned follow-up visits according to the clinic's routine. Photographs and radiographs at follow-up were compared with photos and radiographs taken at crown placement. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Fisher exact test, multiple regression, and Cohen's kappa for interrater reliability.

RESULTS: Infraposition was observed in 68% of ISSCs, but only 8% had an infraposition ≥ 1 mm. Significant differences between sexes were found in the groups without (P < .001) or with slight infraposition (0.1 to 0.5 mm) (P = .001), with men showing less infraposition. Patients with an infraposition ≥ 0.5 mm were more likely to notice this difference (P = .032). Esthetic assessments gave lower scores for color compared to shape, and color mismatch increased over time. Despite these issues, patient satisfaction remained high, with most patients unaware of positional or color differences of their ISSCs. The survival rate was 99% for implants and 92% for crowns. Bone loss was limited, with 86% of the implants having < 1.2 mm of bone loss up to 10 years later, and only 7% had a bone loss > 1.8 mm.

CONCLUSIONS: A high percentage of ISSCs placed in the anterior maxilla exhibited infraposition and an increasing color mismatch over time. Implant and crown survival were high, with few complications and a limited mean bone loss. Patient satisfaction was high despite color mismatch and infraposition.

articles.title: Vertical Bone Reconstruction with CAD/CAM Titanium Mesh: A Prospective Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the use of customized CAD/CAM titanium mesh for the treatment of Cawood and Howell Class V bone atrophy through mean vertical and horizontal bone gains and complication rates.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective clinical trial aimed to evaluate the use of CAD/CAM titanium mesh for the treatment of Class V bone atrophy (Cawood and Howell classification). All patients underwent a preoperative digital planning phase with CBCT imaging, digital intraoral scanning, and extraoral and intraoral photos. The operative phases were divided into four stages: reconstructive surgery (T1), implant surgery (T2), prosthetic phase (T3), and 1-year follow-up (T4). Study variables included (1) the mean vertical and horizontal bone gain by CBCT superposition, (2) peri-implant marginal bone loss by periapical radiographs, and (3) complications by clinical examination.

RESULTS: A total of 25 patients (9 men, 16 women; mean age: 60 ± 8.5 years) with 30 surgical sites were included. The bone defects contained spans of three to six missing teeth, resulting in a mean mesiodistal length of 29.9 ± 8.53 mm and a mean augmentation volume of 2.03 ± 0.96 cm3. Mean vertical and horizontal bone gains were 5.87 ± 1.6 mm and 5.64 ± 2.1 mm, respectively, and mean mesial and distal implant marginal bone losses were 0.61 ± 0.34 mm and 0.46 ± 0.32 mm, respectively. No intraoperative complications were observed. Healing complications included Class I membrane exposure in four patients (16%) and one case (4%) of Class III exposure with infection that required mesh removal.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of CAD/CAM-customized titanium mesh in guided bone regeneration appears to be a predictable and effective technique for managing severe alveolar ridge atrophy. This approach allows for precise, patient-specific augmentation with favorable bone gain and a manageable complication profile, thus supporting its use as a valuable tool in advanced implant therapy.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Less-Invasive vs Large Window Designs for Lateral Sinus Floor Elevation: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether lateral sinus floor elevation (LSFE) through a less-invasive window design (LIWD) can achieve (1) adequate sinus augmentation and (2) a safe procedure with reduced patient discomfort compared to a large window design (LWD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Sixty LSFEs (LIWD, n = 30; LWD, n = 30) with simultaneous implant placement were performed in a randomized controlled clinical trial on 60 subjects (75% men, mean age: 49.87 ± 6.03 years) who were followed for a mean of 30.7 ± 0.41 months. CBCT was used to measure augmented bone height (primary outcome variable) and augmented bone length (secondary outcome variable) preoperatively and 6 months postoperatively to determine the adequacy of the augmentation. Perioperative complications were assessed to determine LIWD safety. The patient's postoperative quality of life (PPQOL) was also measured. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, t tests, and correlation analyses conducted with both Pearson and Spearman methods, with a significance level set at P < .05.

RESULTS: The mean window sizes for the LIWD and LWD groups were 21.7 ± 3.3 mm2 and 58.7 ± 12.0 mm2, respectively, which was statistically significant (P < .001). The augmented bone height and length showed no significant difference between the groups (P = .824, P = .591, respectively). Also, there was no correlation between window size and augmented bone height (r = 0.006, P = .96) or length (r = 0.063, P = .632). Membrane perforation rates and surgical time showed similar results in both groups. The PPQOL measures revealed less discomfort (P < .0001) in the LIWD group.

CONCLUSIONS: The LIWD provides a feasible, efficient, and safe approach for LSFE, with adequate sinus augmentation. Reducing the window size does not increase surgical risks or duration, and LIWD produced significantly less discomfort.

articles.title: The Influence of Systemic Factors on Postoperative Complications and Osseointegration of Zygomatic Implants: A Retrospective Study with up to 5 Years of Follow-up.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To retrospectively evaluate the influence of systemic factors on postoperative complications and osseo-integration of zygomatic implants over a follow-up of up to 5 years and to investigate whether implant surface characteristics affect the incidence of complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed clinical records of patients who received zygomatic implants at a private clinic between 2009 and 2021. Eligible cases included those with complete records and adequate follow-up, while incomplete or interrupted treatments were excluded. All patients were treated using the zygoma anatomy-guided approach (ZAGA) after computed tomography planning, with implant surface types classified into three groups: (1) full-body threaded machined, (2) full-body threaded treated, and (3) polished body with apical and cervical threads treated. Patients were followed up at 6 months, 1 to 4 years, and 5 years or more. The primary outcome was the association of systemic conditions and postoperative complications (implant loss, oroantral communication, sinusitis, cysts, and infections). Secondary outcomes included the associations between implant surface type, number of implants (two or four), and complication rates. Descriptive statistics, Fisher exact test, and Pearson's test were used, with significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: Among 1,026 patients who underwent dental implant surgery, 241 received zygomatic implants, with 195 included in the final analysis after follow-up review. The overall success and survival rates were 95.38% and 95.90%, respectively. Most patients (91.3%) experienced no complications, while 8.7% reported adverse events, primarily implant loss, oroantral communication, sinusitis, or cyst formation. Statistical analysis showed no significant association between systemic conditions, implant macrogeometry, or number of implants (two vs four) and the occurrence of complications (P > .45). Complications were more frequently observed in the medium-term follow-up period (12 to 48 months). These findings suggest that zygomatic implants demonstrate high survival and success rates regardless of systemic status, implant design, or implant number, although complications may arise, predominantly in the medium-term period.

CONCLUSIONS: Although patients with systemic conditions exhibited a higher incidence of complications, these differences were not statistically significant. Therefore, systemic conditions did not increase the risk of postoperative complications or implant loss in this sample. I.

articles.title: Is Alveolar Ridge Preservation Necessary in Molar Sites? A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate whether alveolar ridge preservation (ARP) in molar sites, compared to spontaneous healing (SH), adequately preserves ridge dimensions to facilitate successful implant placement while reducing the need for additional bone augmentation procedures such as guided bone regeneration (GBR) or sinus floor augmentation (SFA). The benefit of ARP in reducing the need for additional bone augmentation procedures to facilitate implant placement has been demonstrated, particularly in single-rooted tooth sites. However, its efficacy in molar sites remains unclear.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A literature search was conducted using four electronic databases. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), controlled clinical trials (CCTs), and cohort studies involving adult patients undergoing molar tooth/teeth extraction planned for implant placement and with a minimum follow-up of 3 months were included. Data on horizontal and vertical ridge dimension changes, need for GBR or SFA for implant placement, and other implant-related outcomes were collected.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included: eight RCTs, two CCTs, three prospective cohort studies, and one retrospective cohort study. A total of 571 sites were analyzed, with the number of sites in individual studies ranging from 20 to 80. In periodontally sound sockets, the ridge width reduction was less in the ARP groups (range: -1.02 ± 0.88 mm to -2.73 ± 1.68 mm) than in the SH groups (range: -2.36 ± 0.91 mm to -4.44 ± 3.71 mm). A similar trend was noted for ridge height reduction, irrespective of the condition of the extraction socket. Moreover, ARP reduced the need for advanced grafting procedures (20.8% for ARP groups vs 47.7% for SH groups), including GBR, SFA, and SFA via the lateral window approach.

CONCLUSIONS: Within the limits of this review, it can be concluded that ARP in molar sites can limit postextraction alveolar bone resorption and reduce the need for additional bone augmentation procedures as well as the likelihood of requiring SFA via the lateral window approach in maxillary posterior sites.

articles.title: Effect of the Two-Piece Abutment Concept and Abutment Disconnection/Reconnection on Marginal Bone Level Changes: A Split-Mouth Randomized, Parallel-Designed, 36-Month Follow-up, Preliminary Clinical Study.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To conduct a comparative evaluation of the clinical and radiographic findings of definitive two-piece abutments placed at stage-two surgery following submerged healing and definitive abutments used in standard prosthetic treatments.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The study was designed as a prospective, split-mouth, randomized, parallel-designed, blinded clinical trial. The study comprised two groups: a test group and a control group. The test group received a two-piece abutment, while the control group received a standardized healing abutment. The study analyzed a total of 10 patients and 20 implants. Clinical and radiographic measurements were obtained at baseline (T0) and at follow-ups of 6 months (T1), 12 months (T2), and 36 months (T3). Radiographic measurements were calculated on standardized periapical radiographs to determine marginal bone level changes (ΔMBL) at different time points, emergence angles, and emergence profiles mesially and distally.

RESULTS: A significant difference was found between the groups in mesial, distal, and mean ΔMBL at T0-T1 and distal and mean ΔMBL at T0-T3 values (P < .05 for both). Emergence angle values were found to be below 30 degrees both mesially and distally in both groups (P > .05). A statistically significant correlation was found between healing/definitive abutment disconnection/reconnection and distal ΔMBL at T0-T3 (P < .05).

CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of the study-including a small sample size and the study design minimizing confounding factors-it was concluded that two-piece definitive abutment application may have significant effects in terms of reducing ΔMBL in both the short and long term. However, further studies with a larger sample size are needed.

articles.title: Prediction Models for Frailty in People Living with HIV: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is increasingly prevalent among people living with HIV, who experience earlier onset and a higher burden of frailty than the general population. Prediction models that identify people living with HIV at risk of future frailty could enable timely, targeted intervention. However, the evidence on prediction models developed specifically for frailty in people living with HIV has not yet been systematically evaluated.

OBJECTIVE: This review aims to systematically identify and critically appraise multivariable prediction models for the future occurrence of frailty in people living with HIV and to assess and summarize their methodological quality and predictive performance.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, and Chinese databases (SinoMed, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP) from inception to July 24, 2026. Studies that developed or validated any multivariable statistical or machine-learning prediction model for frailty in people living with HIV were eligible. Title and abstract screening, full-text evaluation, data extraction (Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies [CHARMS]), and risk-of-bias and applicability assessment (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool [PROBAST]) were conducted independently in duplicate.

RESULTS: The search identified 2523 records (initial search: 2205; updated search: 318); 137 full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and only 1 study met all inclusion criteria. Frail RISC-HIV (Frailty Risk in the Short-Term for Care of People with HIV) was developed in the Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems (CNICS) cohort (n=4680; training n=3170; validation n=1510) using Bayesian model averaging and LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) regression combined with Cox proportional-hazards models to predict incident frailty within 2 years. The model comprised 8 predictors (baseline frailty score, depressive symptomatology [Patient Health Questionnaire-7], prescribed antidepressants, current illicit opioid use, current marijuana use, current antiretroviral therapy, age, and sex) and achieved acceptable discrimination in the validation set (Harrell C=0.76, 95% CI 0.73-0.79), with a sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 61% at a 5% risk threshold; calibration under-predicted the observed risk (predicted 7.9% vs observed 14.7% in the validation set). PROBAST assessment rated the study at high overall risk of bias, driven primarily by the analysis domain. To our knowledge, no external validation of the model was identified, and TRIPOD (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis) reporting was incomplete. Quantitative synthesis was not feasible.

CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base for frailty prediction in people living with HIV currently comprises a single, internally validated model that has not yet been externally validated. This critical evidence gap underscores an urgent need for further model development and rigorous external validation in diverse settings, with standardized frailty definitions and reporting in accordance with TRIPOD.

articles.title: Beyond Calcium: CT Phenotyping of Fibrocalcific Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract: Aortic stenosis is characterized by progressive fibrocalcific remodeling driven by inflammation, fibrosis, and calcification. Although echocardiography and noncontrast computed tomographic calcium scoring (aortic valve calcium score) remain the clinical standards for hemodynamic and structural assessment, computed tomographic angiography, already routinely performed for transcatheter aortic valve replacement planning, provides complementary tissue-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific valve remodeling. Artificial intelligence is increasingly being applied to facilitate the quantitative assessment of fibrocalcific burden and periaortic adipose tissue inflammation. This review examines emerging applications of computed tomographic angiography for fibrocalcific tissue characterization, inflammatory phenotyping, and artificial intelligence-enabled risk assessment in aortic stenosis and discusses their potential role in complementing conventional hemodynamic assessment.

articles.title: Fluid resuscitation in pediatric septic shock-Insights and reflections from the PRoMPT BOLUS Trial.
Mediterranean Diet vs. DASH Diet in Long-Term Blood Pressure Control and Cardiovascular Risk Reduction in Adults With Hypertension: A Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a highly prevalent modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, chronic kidney disease, and premature mortality. This review compares the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension diet and the Mediterranean diet for hypertension management in middle-aged and older adults. A targeted PubMed search was conducted to identify randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses published within the past five years evaluating either dietary pattern for blood pressure control, cardiometabolic outcomes, adherence, and clinical practicality. Foundational studies were included for historical and definitional context. The DASH diet demonstrated the strongest and most consistent blood pressure reduction, supported by structured sodium targets and nutrient composition emphasizing fruits, vegetables, low-fat dairy, whole grains, lean proteins, nuts, and legumes. The Mediterranean diet showed more modest average blood pressure effects but broader cardiometabolic benefits, particularly for lipid profile and long-term cardiovascular risk. Direct head-to-head evidence remains limited to one randomized controlled trial. Current evidence supports both diets as first-line dietary strategies for hypertension management. Because either healthy, plant-forward pattern may provide meaningful benefit, diet selection should be individualized according to blood pressure goals, cardiometabolic risk, patient preference, cultural context, and anticipated adherence.

articles.title: Optimising ethnic diversity in post intensive care rehabilitation research: Strategies used in the iRehab trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Greater ethnic diversity within clinical trials supports more equitable and generalisable findings. However, rehabilitation trials often overlook participant ethnic diversity. This study assessed ethnic diversity and representation within the iRehab trial and described strategies used to optimise ethnic diversity.

METHODS: Ethnicity data from screening logs were reviewed monthly and compared to UK census data. Recruitment sites were reviewed to ensure geographic spread. Also, participants in the iRehab intervention group self-reported their ethnicity for comparison with screening logs. An annual workshop was delivered to discuss recruitment tips for optimising ethnic diversity, with three selected sites sharing more comprehensive experiences.

RESULTS: Participants identifying as White were overrepresented when compared to UK census data; this reduced slightly across the trial lifetime. Geographic spread of iRehab trial sites was wide, supporting inclusive recruitment. No differences existed between participant- and site-identified ethnicity. Sites agreed that translation of all patient-facing trial materials would be inefficient, but the trial poster should be translated into five prevalent languages. Further discussions: (1) re-affirmed the need to use varied communication strategies to reach potential participants (e-mail, WhatsApp, family involvement); (2) create a trial video with an accompanying transcript; (3) meet regularly to share recruitment strategies.

CONCLUSION: The iRehab trial embedded opportunities to optimise ethnic diversity with modest improvements in representativeness, exhibiting similar levels of ethnic diversity as per the clinical population. Achieving representativeness that is similar to the clinical ICU population necessitates collaboration with stakeholders. Future studies should test effectiveness of strategies to enhance representativeness of underserved populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN11266403.

articles.title: Safety and Cost-Benefit of Simultaneous Bilateral Carotid Angioplasty and Stenting in a Lower-middle-income Country: A Single-centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Internal carotid artery stenosis accounts for 15%-20% of transient ischaemic attacks and ischaemic strokes. In lower-middle-income countries (LMICs), simultaneous bilateral carotid artery stenting (CAS) may be a cost-effective alternative to staged procedures.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the safety, cost-effectiveness and 30-day outcomes of simultaneous bilateral CAS at a single centre in Kolkata, India.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 35 patients. Procedures were performed by three operators with varying experience (senior: >12 years; juniors: 3 years). Embolic protection devices were not used, to minimise costs. Outcomes were monitored through discharge and a mandatory 30-day follow-up.

RESULTS: The 30-day mortality, stroke and myocardial infarction rates were 0%. Post-procedural complications occurred in 11.4% of cases and were managed successfully. The simultaneous approach yielded a 51.1% cost reduction compared with projected staged costs.

CONCLUSION: Simultaneous bilateral CAS is a safe, cost-effective strategy in LMIC settings when performed by experienced neuro-interventionalists, with a stable safety profile through 30 days post-procedure.

articles.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Dynamics Study of Gegen-Huangqi Herb Pair against Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatohepatitis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, hepatocellular injury, and progressive fibrosis. Gegen-Huangqi herb pair (GHHP) is used in traditional Chinese medicine for metabolic disorders, but its candidate constituents and potential molecular interactions in MASH remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: Candidate constituents and predicted targets of GHHP were retrieved from BATMAN-TCM using a score cutoff >=20 and an adjusted P value <=0.05. MASH-associated targets were obtained from GeneCards and the Genetic Association Database (GAD), followed by network and enrichment analyses. Ten networkranked candidate compounds and 22 candidate targets were evaluated by molecular docking. Representative protein-ligand complexes were further analyzed by 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations using GROMACS 2022.03, and MM/GBSA binding free energies were calculated from frames sampled throughout the entire 100-ns trajectories.

RESULTS: Forty-five herb-compound records were retrieved for GHHP, corresponding to 749 predicted targets. Intersection analysis identified 112 GHHP-MASH candidate targets, including 31 high-confidence targets shared by GHHP, GeneCards, and GAD. Network analysis identified 10 top-ranked compounds for docking. Enrichment analysis implicated inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including IL-17, HIF-1, FoxO, TNF, AMPK, mTOR, MAPK, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease pathways. Docking predicted favorable interactions for several compound-target pairs, including coumestrol-PRKAB1 (-10.1 kcal/mol), coumestrol-SIRT1 (-10.0 kcal/mol), sophoradiol-GPBAR1 (-10.4 kcal/mol), and sophoradiol-CXCR4 (-10.4 kcal/mol). Five representative complexes were evaluated by MD and MM/GBSA; predicted binding free energies were -25.78, -16.00, -35.13, -28.38, and -5.84 kcal/mol for SIRT1-coumestrol, GPBAR1-Robustadial A, GPBAR1- Sophoradiol, CXCR4-Sophoradiol, and CXCR4-gamma-sitosterol, respectively.

DISCUSSION: The integrated analysis linked GHHP constituents with MASH-related metabolic and inflammatory networks and revealed distinct structural and energetic profiles among selected protein-ligand complexes. PRKAB1, SIRT1, GPBAR1, CXCR4, and several AMPK-, TNF-, and mTOR-related pathways emerged as prominent components of the predicted interaction network.

CONCLUSION: These findings delineate a multi-component, multi-target molecular interaction landscape for GHHP in MASH and identify several compound-target pairs with favorable docking and free-energy profiles.

articles.title: A dual-task prediction model for industrial equipment based on prior knowledge-enhanced shared features and dual-path gated recurrent units.
articles.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction and health state (HS) assessment are core tasks in industrial prognostics and health management. Most existing data-driven methods treat them as independent tasks, ignoring their inherent correlation and task specificity. A dual-task model based on prior knowledge-enhanced shared features and dual-path gated recurrent units (DP-GRU) is proposed. First, task-specific prior knowledge enhances shared spatio-temporal feature adaptability. Then, a dual-task output module is designed for task specificity. For RUL prediction, HS information adaptively evaluates RUL feature importance under different HSs, and DP-GRU boosts long-term memory for non-stationary data. For HS assessment, Additive Margin Softmax loss improves classification robustness. Finally, homoscedastic uncertainty optimizes dual-task loss weights. Three-case experiments verify its superiority over benchmarks and provide support for full-life-cycle equipment health management.

articles.title: Cardiomyocyte-derived circulating extracellular vesicles enable a non-invasive liquid biopsy of human myocardium.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive interrogation of difficult-to-sample tissues remains a central challenge in human health. Here, we identify and characterize cardiomyocyte-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs; "cardiovesicles") as a liquid interface to the myocardium. Integrating induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes, genetic models, and multi-omics, we identify two cardiomyocyte-enriched surface markers (POPDC2 and CHRNE), enabling antibody-based cardiovesicle immunocapture from human plasma. Cardiovesicles are enriched for cardiomyocyte transcripts, exhibiting disease-specific transcriptional signatures in heart failure and myocardial infarction. Paired human myocardial tissue-plasma analyses demonstrate cardiac enrichment (versus bulk EVs) and concordance with myocardial single-nucleus transcriptional profiles. In patients undergoing cardiopulmonary bypass, cardiovesicles capture rapid, dynamic transcriptional changes that parallel cardiomyocyte (not fibroblast, endothelial, and myeloid) responses to ischemic stress. Functional genomics implicates cardiovesicle transcripts in cardiomyocyte cell-specific cardiovascular disease liability in large human populations. Cardiovesicles may capture dynamic cardiomyocyte states in humans that reflect genetic disease liability, supporting an EV-based approach to non-invasive liquid biopsy of the myocardium.

articles.title: Female homicides in Liguria, Italy: A 30-year retrospective forensic study (1995-2025).
articles.journal: Journal of forensic and legal medicine
articles.abstract: Female homicide is an important epidemiological and medico-legal issue characterized by heterogeneous circumstances, relationship dynamics, and injury patterns. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiological, relational, circumstantial, and autopsy features of female homicide cases examined at the Institute of Legal Medicine of the University of Genoa. A retrospective study was conducted on female homicide cases examined at autopsy between January 1, 1995, and December 31, 2025. Demographic, relational, circumstantial, and autopsy data were collected and analyzed using descriptive statistics. Forty cases were identified. The mean age of the victims was 53.65 years (range, 10-94). In 22 cases (55%), the perpetrator was a current or former intimate partner. Most homicides occurred in domestic settings (75%). Sharp or penetrating instruments were used in 16 cases (40%), firearms in 11 (27.5%), and blunt-force mechanisms in seven (17.5%). The most frequent causes of death were sharp-force injuries (40%), gunshot injuries (27.5%), and blunt-force injuries (15%). The head was involved in 18 cases (45%), while the face, neck, and upper limbs were each involved in 17 cases (42.5%). The perpetrator's refusal to accept the victim's decision to end the relationship was documented in 10 cases (25%). The findings highlight the importance of integrating relational and circumstantial evidence with autopsy findings to achieve a comprehensive medico-legal assessment of female homicides. Systematic autopsy documentation and collaboration among forensic pathologists, law enforcement agencies, and healthcare and social services may contribute to a better understanding of the circumstances associated with these deaths and support the development of preventive strategies.

articles.title: Discovery of a potent multitarget coumarin derivative via α-amylase inhibition: synthesis, structural optimization, and comprehensive in vivo evaluation in STZ-induced diabetic rats.
articles.abstract: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) combines chronic hyperglycemia with oxidative damage, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction and progressive organ injury, calling for multifunctional agents. We designed, synthesized and characterized sixteen novel coumarin-based hydrazide derivatives (4a-9c). Their in vitro α-amylase inhibitory activity was evaluated, and a structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis was performed. Among the synthesized compounds, derivative 8b exhibited the highest α-amylase inhibitory potency, with an IC50 value of 56.3 μM, exceeding that of the reference inhibitor acarbose (IC50 = 74.6 μM). Compound 8b was selected for further in vivo evaluation in streptozotocin (STZ) induced diabetic rats. For a month, oral treatment of 5 mg/kg/day dramatically improved dyslipidemia and decreased fasting blood glucose, hepatic and renal dysfunction, oxidative stress, proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6), and endothelial dysfunction biomarkers (sICAM-1 and sVCAM-1). Histopathological examination of liver and pancreatic tissues further supported the ability of compound 8b to protect against diabetic-induced tissue injury. Collectively, our in vivo findings demonstrate the multimodal therapeutic benefits of compound 8b in restoring systemic homeostasis in STZ-induced diabetic rats. To further elucidate its molecular mechanism, molecular docking studies were performed using human pancreatic α-amylase (PDB ID: 1B2Y). A validated cross-docking protocol demonstrated a predicted favorable binding affinity of compound 8b within both the catalytic and substrate-recognition subsite of the enzyme, which is consistent with our experimental SAR findings. DFT indicated electronic properties favoring efficient non-covalent enzyme binding with moderate reactivity. Together, our synthetic, biological, histopathological and computational findings identify 8b as a promising multifunctional antidiabetic lead warranting further pharmacological study.

articles.title: Molecular fingerprint insights into microplastic‑derived dissolved organic matter mediating phosphate immobilization on microplastic‑goethite complexes.
articles.abstract: Microplastic‑derived dissolved organic matter (MP‑DOM) is pervasive in aquatic systems, yet its polymer‑specific controls on nutrient cycling remain poorly understood. This study investigated orthophosphate adsorption on pre-synthesized MP-goethite complexes in the presence of MP-DOM leached from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polylactic acid (PLA). Batch experiments showed that MP-DOM competed with orthophosphate for goethite adsorption sites, with PET-DOM exerting a stronger inhibitory effect (60.0% adsorption reduction) than PLA-DOM (57.1%). Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry results revealed preferential depletion of lignin-, protein-, and lipid-like molecular formulas, reflecting distinct compositional traits: PET-DOM is enriched in carboxyl-rich protein and lipid components, whereas PLA-DOM is dominated by tannin-like and condensed aromatic constituents. Mechanistic fraction‑based tests confirmed that DOM components enriched in oxygen‑containing groups, potentially including carboxyl‑ and phenolic‑hydroxyl‑related structures, may exhibit stronger competitive effects for phosphate adsorption on goethite. Beyond site competition, MP-DOM reduces surface Fe(III) and induces goethite amorphization, with more significant mineral alteration under PET-DOM exposure. This study provides molecular‑level insights into how MP‑DOM alters phosphate retention in the sediments, highlighting that polymer‑driven MP‑DOM effects should be considered when assessing internal phosphorus loading in MP‑polluted aquatic systems.

articles.title: Strategies for Portal Vein Anastomosis in Pediatric Liver Transplantation: Hemodynamic Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pediatric liver transplantation is the optimal treatment for children with end-stage liver disease. However, using adult donor livers often leads to portal vein size mismatch, increasing anastomotic risks. Hemodynamic assessment is crucial for surgical success.

METHODS: Numerical simulations using non-Newtonian fluid models were performed to compare normal portal vein anatomy, three hypoplastic models, and five anastomotic types. Key parameters included flow distribution, velocity, pressure, and wall shear stress (WSS). Simulated flow rates were validated against published clinical data.

RESULTS: Stenosis increased flow velocity and pressure. The 50% stenosis model reached a WSS of 35 Pa-three times the normal value-with high stress zones near the bifurcation. Certain anastomotic techniques improved hemodynamic performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Confluence and interposition graft anastomoses most closely restored normal hemodynamics. Optimal reconstruction requires not only sufficient diameter but also geometric continuity, axial alignment, and attention to bifurcation walls to avoid complications. Clinical validation with intraoperative flow probes and postoperative ultrasound is needed. Additional simulations augmented inflow conditions (simulating collateral ligation) demonstrate that increased inflow elevates WSS by 28%-35% at the bifurcation outer wall in geometrically suboptimal anastomoses, supporting the selective use of augmentation maneuvers.

articles.title: Derepression of Gene Expression Underlies HDAC Inhibitor-Mediated Reversal of Diastolic Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Diastolic dysfunction contributes to the pathogenesis of heart failure (HF) and various other cardiac conditions. Inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs) prevents and reverses diastolic dysfunction in multiple preclinical models. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms by which HDAC inhibitors improve cardiac relaxation remain poorly defined. Here, using single-cell RNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, and cell-based assays, we demonstrate that broad gene repression in cardiac non-myocytes is a central mechanism underpinning diastolic dysfunction and HF. HDAC inhibition remodels chromatin architecture and derepresses critical transcriptional programs in multiple cardiac cell types, offering a multifaceted therapeutic strategy for heart diseases characterized by impaired diastolic function.

articles.title: Inverse gas chromatographic characterization of black benzoin as a bio-based stationary phase: Surface energetics, acid-base modeling, and isomer selectivity.
articles.abstract: Inverse gas chromatography (IGC) under low-probe-loading conditions intended to approximate infinite dilution was employed to investigate the surface thermodynamics, Lewis acid-base interactions, and chromatographic selectivity of black benzoin (BB), a natural balsamic resin. The dispersive component of surface free energy (γSD) was determined over 303.2-328.2 K using the Dorris-Gray, Schultz, and Hamieh thermal methods. Surface Lewis acid-base characteristics were evaluated using the classical Gutmann graphical approach and generalized Hamieh models (2-P, 3-P, 4.2-P, 4.3-P, and 5-P). Model performance was assessed using regression statistics, information criteria, and leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Chromatographic selectivity was investigated for structural and positional isomers of butyl acetates, butyl alcohols, amyl alcohols, and xylenes. The dispersive surface energy decreased with increasing temperature for all three methods, although its absolute magnitude depended on the calculation approach. The Gutmann analysis yielded KA= 0.0619, KD= 0.0470, and KD/KA= 0.759, indicating amphoteric Lewis acid-base characteristics with moderately predominant acidity. Among the generalized Hamieh formulations, the 5-P model provided the best in-sample fit (uncentered R² = 0.9964; RMSE = 0.2238 kJ mol⁻¹), whereas the 4.3-P model exhibited the lowest LOOCV RMSE (0.4958 kJ mol⁻¹), marginally lower than that of the 5-P model (0.4991 kJ mol⁻¹). The sensitivity of higher-order regression coefficients highlighted the importance of cautious physicochemical interpretation. Selectivity factors exceeded unity for all investigated isomer pairs, reaching a maximum of 9.66 for n‑butyl alcohol/tert‑butyl alcohol at 333.2 K. These findings demonstrate the potential of BB for chromatographic discrimination of structurally related compounds and emphasize the importance of balancing model fit, complexity, and interpretability when characterizing surface acid-base interactions.

articles.title: Are Higher NT-proBNP Thresholds for Atrial Fibrillation Necessary in Trials of HFrEF?
Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment: The DIG-Mod HF Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The DIG-Mod HF trial is the first trial to evaluate the mechanistic effects of low-dose digoxin on myocardial work and functional exercise capacity in patients with heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction receiving contemporary guideline-recommended medical therapy (GRMT). Although a recent meta-analysis demonstrated clinical benefit of cardiac glycosides in addition to contemporary GRMT, the mechanistic basis for this effect remains unexplored.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to investigate whether low-dose digoxin improves myocardial work and functional exercise capacity when added to optimized GRMT.

METHODS: An open-label, randomized crossover trial enrolled 50 patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction on maximally tolerated GRMT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to digoxin 0.125 mg/day plus standard of care or standard of care alone, each for 24 weeks, for a total study duration of 48 weeks. Co-primary endpoints were within-patient changes in peak oxygen consumption (Vo2) and left ventricular global work index.

RESULTS: The study population was highly optimized, with 88% in NYHA functional class II on near-universal quadruple GRMT. Digoxin did not significantly improve peak Vo2 (mean difference: -0.08 mL/kg/min; 95% CI: -1.64 to 1.47 mL/kg/min; P = 0.914). Global work index improved significantly (mean difference: 157.8 mm Hg%; 95% CI: 12.2-303.4 mm Hg%; P = 0.034). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12 score also improved during the digoxin period. The composite safety endpoint did not differ significantly between arms (P = 0.089).

CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose digoxin significantly improved myocardial work without improving peak Vo2. Demonstrating these effects in a clinically stable, well-treated population is consistent with an independent pharmacologic effect of digoxin in addition to modern guideline-directed therapy. (Effects of Digoxin in Modern Heart Failure Treatment [DIG-Mod HF]; EU Clinical Trials Register Number: 2024-513448-26-00).

articles.title: Colchicine for Acute Kidney Injury Prevention? The Jury Is Out.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: Primary Mönckeberg Medial Sclerosis: 30-Year Follow-Up and Whole-Genome Sequencing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mönckeberg medial sclerosis (MMS) usually accompanies diabetes mellitus or chronic kidney disease and carries a high cardiovascular risk; primary forms are rare and genetically uncharacterized.

CASE SUMMARY: In 1996, advanced MMS was found incidentally in a 46-year-old man without procalcific risk factors. At 30-year follow-up, he remained asymptomatic. Color-coded duplex ultrasonography and photon-counting detector computed tomography (PCD-CT) showed severe medial calcification from the abdominal aorta to the below-the-knee arteries without hemodynamically relevant stenosis, and arterial stiffness was increased. Whole-genome sequencing found no rare variant in 6 calcification genes; a coronary calcification polygenic score was at the 98.8th percentile.

DISCUSSION: Primary MMS may follow a benign course distinct from secondary forms, possibly reflecting a different pathogenesis. A negative targeted genome analysis does not exclude a genetic cause.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Medial calcification without diabetes or kidney disease can remain clinically silent for decades. Family segregation and cohort studies are required to define its genetic basis.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation, Atrial Flutter, and Orthodromic Atrioventricular Re-Entrant Tachycardia With a Concealed Left-Sided Accessory Pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accessory pathway (AP)-mediated tachycardias are a common cause of supraventricular tachycardia; however, their relationship with atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL) is often under-recognized.

CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old man presented with recurrent narrow-complex tachycardia, AF, and typical AFL occurring in close temporal proximity. An electrophysiology study demonstrated inducible orthodromic atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia with eccentric retrograde atrial activation, consistent with a concealed left inferoposterior AP. The pathway was successfully ablated. At 9-month follow-up, there was no recurrence of AF, AFL, or supraventricular tachycardia.

DISCUSSION: Prior studies suggest APs may facilitate atrial arrhythmogenesis. This case highlights the interplay between atrioventricular re-entrant tachycardia and atrial arrhythmias and the importance of recognizing multiple mechanisms in a single patient.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Concealed APs may trigger AF and AFL. Targeted ablation can eliminate multiple arrhythmias.

articles.title: Ipsilateral Retrograde Approach Via CC-0 Septal-to-Septal Invisible Collateral for Uncrossable LAD Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrograde percutaneous coronary intervention for non-chronic total occlusion lesions via angiographically invisible septal collateral channels remains technically challenging.

CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old man with recurrent unstable angina after a recent inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction presented with a tortuous, severe stenosis of the mid-left anterior descending artery. Antegrade wiring of the lesion failed despite multiple guidewires with microcatheter support. No angiographically visible collateral channels (CCs) were identified from either the contralateral or ipsilateral circulation; nevertheless, ipsilateral retrograde surfing through an invisible CC-0 collateral successfully crossed from the proximal to the distal septal branches using a Fielder XT-A guidewire, and revascularization was completed successfully.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case demonstrates that angiographically invisible septal CCs can be traversable, and that a retrograde approach through such channels can effectively revascularize an otherwise uncrossable lesion.

articles.title: Wearable Tissue Oximetry in Cardiogenic Shock: Microcirculatory Deterioration Preceding Macrohemodynamic Collapse.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock can progress rapidly, even when conventional macrohemodynamic vital signs remain stable. Continuous, noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring is uncommon but could provide early signals of impending decompensation.

FIH/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY: The authors report near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography monitoring with the investigational NIRSense Envello Core wearable device. The patient was a 66-year-old man with complex valvular disease and combined pre/post capillary pulmonary hypertension, who rapidly deteriorated and died despite intensive care unit management.

DISCUSSION: Chest-derived tissue oxygen saturation and perfusion index appeared to signal deterioration ∼4 hours before clinically recognized collapse, and correlated strongly with central venous pressure (r = -0.95; perfusion index) and systolic pulmonary artery pressure (r = 0.87; tissue oxygen saturation).

NOVELTY: To our knowledge, this is the first continuous microcirculatory characterization of the transition to terminal cardiogenic shock using a wearable near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography device.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring may detect hemodynamic collapse before conventional vital signs, identifying a potential window for earlier intervention.

articles.title: Dual-Chamber Leadless Pacemaker Implantation in Dextrocardia With Situs Inversus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dextrocardia with situs inversus presents unique anatomical challenges for cardiac device implantation. AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation has not previously been reported in this setting.

CASE SUMMARY: An 84-year-old man with dextrocardia and situs inversus underwent AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation for symptomatic bradycardia. Preprocedural 3-dimensional computed tomography merged with intraprocedural fluoroscopy, together with right atrial contrast angiography and fluoroscopic guidance, facilitated successful implantation of both devices. The procedure was completed without complications, and the subsequent clinical course was uneventful.

DISCUSSION: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported experience of AVEIR DR dual-chamber leadless pacemaker system implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus totalis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Careful preprocedural anatomical planning, catheter manipulation adapted to mirror-image anatomy, and a systematic implantation strategy enabled successful dual-chamber leadless pacemaker implantation in a patient with dextrocardia and situs inversus.

articles.title: Higher Quality Temperature Control Is Associated With Improved Outcomes Following Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Multicenter Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: Hypothermic temperature control has not consistently demonstrated a neuroprotective effect, resulting in heterogeneity of use in clinical practice. We evaluated temperature control quality across 4 institutions and its association with clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of institutional registry data collected between 2021 and 2024 in survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) with Glasgow Coma Scale Motor score less than 6 from 4 academic centers with established cardiac arrest programs. Eligible patients included those 18 years of age or older, treated with hypothermic temperature control (33-36°C) using a feedback-controlled device, and admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU). A temperature control quality score (0-6) was assigned for each patient. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge. The secondary outcome was good neurologic outcome at hospital discharge, defined as a Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) score of 1-2. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions quantified the relationship between quality of temperature control, as an ordinal variable, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 356 included patients, most were male (N=224, 62.9%) with mean (standard deviation [SD]) age 58.1 (15.2) years. Most suffered a nonshockable arrest (N=262, 73.6%) and did not receive layperson CPR (N=225, 63.2%). Median [IQR] Pittsburgh Cardiac Arrest Category score was 4 [3,4], mean (SD) lactate 9.1 (4.1) mmol/L, and pH 7.09 (0.17). Median [IQR] preinduction time was 2.3 [1.5 to 3.5] hours and 150 (42.1%) were treated with early neuromuscular blockade. Adjusting for confounders in the multivariable model, an increase of one-point in the temperature control quality score was associated with improved survival at hospital discharge (odds ratio [OR] 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07 to 1.64). A one-point increase in the quality score also resulted in a shift towards lower (improved) CPC score (OR 1.28; 95% CI, 0.05 to 1.55). The direction of effect was consistent across all centers.

CONCLUSION: In unresponsive survivors of OHCA, an increase in temperature control quality was associated with improved survival and better neurologic outcome; however, confounding by site, injury severity, or perceived prognosis is possible. Lack of temperature control parameter standardization may influence efficacy and practice variability within pragmatic-design clinical trials possibly contributed to neutral trial results. Prospective trials evaluating the importance of temperature control quality and the population most likely to benefit from hypothermic temperature control are essential.

articles.title: State-Level Trends in Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock Management Bundle (SEP-1) Compliance and Sepsis Mortality in the United States.
Von willebrand factor antigen identifies liver-related risk across surgical treatment pathways in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment selection between resection and transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) considers tumor characteristics and liver function, but may incompletely capture underlying hepatic risk. We assessed the prognostic value of von Willebrand factor antigen (vWF-Ag) across these treatment pathways.

METHODS: We studied 345 patients with HCC undergoing resection (n=105) or listed for transplantation (n=240) at two centers. vWF-Ag was measured before resection or at listing. Outcomes included survival, recurrence, and waitlist dropout, with the latter assessed using competing-risk methods. Analyses included cohort-specific vWF-Ag strata, continuous and spline models, adjustment for MELD, up-to-seven sum, and log10(AFP), and treatment interactions.

RESULTS: Overall survival was comparable between strategies when measured from listing or surgery, while recurrence was more frequent after resection (HR 10.0). After resection, rising vWF-Ag was independently associated with higher mortality (adjusted HR 1.042 per 10%) and recurrence (adjusted HR 1.046). At listing, vWF-Ag above 413% was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of dropout (41.6% vs. 25.2% at 24 months), driven by clinical deterioration or death rather than tumor progression, independently of MELD. After transplantation, vWF-Ag did not stratify survival or recurrence, and the vWF-Ag by treatment interaction was significant for mortality and recurrence (all p≤0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: In HCC patients, vWF-Ag was associated with adverse outcomes after resection and non-oncological waitlist dropout, but not post-transplant outcomes. This differential association supports the hypothesis that vWF-Ag captures risk linked to the underlying hepatic disease that persists after resection but is attenuated following transplantation. vWF-Ag may complement conventional selection criteria by identifying patients with technically resectable HCC whose prognosis remains compromised by underlying liver disease, supporting prospective evaluation of its role in selecting between resection and transplantation.

articles.title: Developing a Structured Toolkit to Address Delays in Time to Surgery for Low-energy Hip Fracture Patients: The Surgical Wait Time for Fracture Treatment (SWIFT) Initiative.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed surgery (>24 to 48 hours) for hip fracture patients is associated with higher morbidity, mortality, and cost, but determinants of delay vary by setting. Improvement strategies must align with specific barriers. This study aimed to identify determinants affecting time to surgery (TTS) and develop a tailored resource to guide health systems in selecting interventions to improve TTS.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were completed with key stakeholders using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and Theoretical Domains Framework. Transcripts were analyzed to identify determinants affecting TTS, which were organized into themes and matched to tailored strategies using the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC) tool to create an improvement matrix. The quality improvement team tracked quarterly TTS within 24 hours for patients with and without echocardiograms, and performance was calculated using running weighted averages.

RESULTS: Seventeen stakeholders from orthopedics, internal medicine, anesthesiology, emergency medicine, cardiology, and nursing were interviewed. Thematic analysis identified 7 major contributors to delayed TTS: patient health, care coordination, prioritization, improvement climate, availability, incentive structures, and empowerment. Our analysis generated 23 sub-themes and 66 codes. A total of 39 site-specific barriers were matched to 17 ERIC strategies spanning interactive assistance, tailoring to context, stakeholder interrelationships, training/education, clinician support, financial strategies, and infrastructure changes. Before implementation, 62% of patients underwent surgery within 24 hours, including 23% of those requiring an echocardiogram. After implementation, 74.1% of patients had surgery within 24 hours, including 35.8% requiring echocardiograms.

CONCLUSION: An improvement strategy matrix improved TTS for hip fracture patients within one health system. This process may be used by other health systems to identify and address determinants of delays.

articles.title: Adjunctive Fibular Shortening Osteotomy During Total Ankle Arthroplasty for Severe Varus Ankle Osteoarthritis: A Retrospective Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe varus ankle osteoarthritis can make total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) technically difficult because residual coronal malalignment, lateral gutter impingement, and unstable talar reduction may persist despite standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. This study describes early clinical and radiographic outcomes after adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy in a highly selected subgroup of patients undergoing TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 4 patients who underwent adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy during TAA after standard intraoperative balancing failed to restore stable talar reduction and adequate lateral clearance. These cases were identified from 320 TAAs performed over a 10-year period. Radiographic assessment included talocrural angle difference relative to the contralateral ankle and fibular length discrepancy. Clinical assessments included the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score and 36-item Short Form (SF-36) survey. Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: All 4 ankles had severe varus deformity >30° and preoperative talocrural angle difference >7° compared with the contra-lateral ankle. Mean fibular shortening was 8.2 ± 0.9 mm. Mean talocrural angle difference improved from 9.2° ± 1.3° preoperatively to 0.6° ± 0.3° postoperatively. Fibular union occurred in all cases at a mean of approximately 20 weeks. The mean AOFAS ankle-hindfoot score improved from 38.8 ± 3.0 to 54.2 ± 1.7, and the mean SF-36 score improved from 26.5 ± 1.9 to 42.2 ± 3.1. No fixation failure or recurrent gross instability was observed during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy may be considered as a selective intraoperative balancing option during TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis when residual lateral impingement and instability persist after standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. Larger studies with validated patient-reported outcomes and longer follow-up are required to define its indications and durability.

articles.title: A Pilot MDR-Based Study of MTHFR rs1801133 Distribution and Exploratory Interaction Patterns in Ischemic Stroke Patients from Northeast India.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Ischemic stroke (IS) is one of the main causes of death worldwide, impacted by hereditary, lifestyle, and environmental factors. The MTHFR rs1801133 (C677T) is widely studied in relation to IS. This pilot study examined the distribution of MTHFR rs1801133 among patients with IS from Southern Assam and explored the relationship between genetic and demographic variables.

METHODS: Fifty IS patients were enrolled in the study. The MTHFR rs1801133 was analyzed by polymerase chain reaction and Sanger sequencing. Multifactor dimensionality reduction (MDR) was performed as an exploratory within-case analysis.

RESULTS: Thirteen patients (26%) had the heterozygous CT genotype, while 37 (74%) had the CC genotype; no TT genotype was observed. MDR identified the combination of rs1801133-age-smoking [testing balanced accuracy (TBA) = 0.8207, cross-validation consistency (CVC) = 9/10] and age-smoking (TBA = 0.9457, CVC = 10/10) as prominent interaction models. Additional sequence variants were also detected.

CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the MTHFR rs1801133 distribution and exploratory interaction patterns by MDR among IS patients from Southern Assam.

articles.title: Advocating for a Structured Stroke Training Program for Non-Specialized Physicians - Insights from the Nepal Stroke Project.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract: Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) face major challenges in delivering quality stroke care, largely due to a shortage of neurologists. The Nepal Stroke Project (NSP) has provided stroke training for physicians and nurses over the past four years. This qualitative study explored barriers, facilitators, and unmet needs to improve program effectiveness and sustainability. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight healthcare professionals involved in NSP and analyzed using Kuckartz's qualitative content analysis. Thematic saturation was reached within the purposively selected sample. Participants valued online lectures and on-site workshops but emphasized the need for greater frequency and broader reach. A structured blended learning approach, certification, and prioritization of non-specialist physicians were highlighted as key priorities. Telemedicine and task-shifting to mid-level providers represent important complementary strategies. A structured, scalable training program with certification and equitable access may help address workforce gaps and inform similar initiatives in other LMICs.

articles.title: Function-integrated injectable poly(methyl methacrylate) bone cement engineered with silver-templated mesoporous calcium-silicate nanoparticles via a chitosan-glycerophosphate hydrogel.
articles.abstract: Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement remains a mainstay of bone reconstruction, yet its high polymerization exotherm, mismatched stiffness, bioinertness and lack of antibacterial activity can lead to thermal injury, stress shielding and post-operative infection. Here we report a single-phase strategy that addresses these limitations together. Mesoporous calcium-silicate nanoparticles (MCSNs) and silver-templated MCSNs (Ag-MCSNs) were dispersed in a thermosensitive chitosan-glycerophosphate (CS-GP) hydrogel and blended with PMMA to prepare three modified cements. The hydrogel phase lowered the peak polymerization temperature from ∼77 °C to below 40 °C, extended the working time beyond 20 min and created interconnected pores throughout the PMMA matrix with a dominant pore diameter of ∼79 µm. The modified cements exhibited an elastic modulus of 140-170 MPa and a compressive yield strength of 7-10 MPa, closely matching cancellous bone, and these properties were retained after 28 days of immersion in simulated body fluid. The MCSN-containing cements additionally promoted apatite deposition, with cumulative calcium uptake reaching 2.8-3.3 mmol L-1 at day 28. Antibacterial testing against E. coli and S. aureus showed that only the Ag-MCSN cement produced clear inhibition zones, disrupted bacterial membranes on contact, and significantly reduced the number of recoverable colonies (p < 0.05) without compromising cytocompatibility. A single Ag-MCSN phase can therefore endow PMMA cement with combined bioactivity and antibacterial activity while improving its thermal and mechanical performance, a combination that holds promise for infection-resistant bone reconstruction.

articles.title: 18F-labelled nitrogen mustard-based alkylating anticancer agents. Synthesis of the boronate precursors followed by copper-mediated radiofluorination.
articles.abstract: Synthesis of 18F-radiotracers of melphalan and an analouge of the peptide-drug conjugate melflufen is reported. The tracers were obtained by copper-mediated radiofluorination from organoboronate precursors. The new fluorine-18 species were applied for in vitro PET studies.

articles.title: Differential co-localization analysis of multi-sample and multi-condition experiments with spatialFDA.
articles.abstract: Advances in spatial omics data generation have led to an explosion in new datasets that record the spatial location of transcripts and proteins. However, challenges remain in the analysis of spatial omics data. One important analysis is differential cellular co-localization (CCoL): the quantification of the clustering, or spacing, of one or more cell types across multiple conditions. Our framework spatialFDA combines methodology from spatial statistics with functional data analysis to accurately quantify and test for differences between conditions in CCoL across spatial scales. Using two simulation studies, we show that spatialFDA performs well in controlled settings. Furthermore, spatialFDA recovers known biological processes in type-1 diabetes and adds insights about the CCoL strength in space. spatialFDA is readily available as an open-source Bioconductor R package.

articles.title: Subtype-specific metabolic remodeling and cellular tropism drive the hyperpathogenicity of influenza A(H3N2).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In seasonal influenza epidemics, the H3N2 subtype typically causes a heavier disease burden than H1N1; however, the host metabolic basis underlying its hyperpathogenicity remains incompletely elucidated.

METHODS: Using a laboratory-generated mouse-adapted H3N2 strain (H3N2-P7) and an H1N1 murine infection model, this study systematically compared the disease dynamics and metabolic profiles of H3N2 and H1N1 infections to unveil the molecular mechanisms driving their differential pathogenicity.

RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that H3N2 and H1N1 exhibited similar viral replication levels in the lungs and induced comparable body weight loss. Pathological analyses revealed that, compared to H1N1, H3N2 displayed a stronger tropism for tracheal ciliated cells and induced more severe vascular endothelial damage. Furthermore, the two viral subtypes triggered distinct metabolic remodeling, H1N1 infection was characterized by a specific enrichment in tryptophan metabolism, whereas H3N2 infection resulted in severe dysregulation of histidine and α-linolenic acid metabolism. The differential viral cell tropism and subtype-specific metabolic remodeling may collectively contribute to the hyperpathogenicity of H3N2.

CONCLUSIONS: This study not only uncovers the molecular fingerprints of H3N2 hyperpathogenicity but also provides a vital theoretical foundation for the development of subtype-specific prognostic biomarkers and host metabolism-targeted precision therapies for severe influenza.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Anti-Müllerian Hormone for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2023 international evidence-based guideline for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) conditionally recommended serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) as an alternative to ultrasound for diagnosing polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM) in adults, marking a significant shift in diagnostic practice. However, the diagnostic accuracy of AMH remains debated, particularly regarding its utility as a standalone test, its application across diverse populations, and its use in adolescents.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Major electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, were searched for diagnostic accuracy studies published until November 2024, and studies evaluating serum AMH against the Rotterdam criteria for PCOS or ultrasound-defined PCOM were included. A bivariate random-effects model was used to pool sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for three key questions: AMH for 1) PCOS diagnosis in adults, 2) PCOM diagnosis in adults, and 3) PCOS diagnosis in adolescents. The Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2 tool was used to assess the risk of bias.

RESULTS: For adult PCOS diagnosis, 83 studies (n = 33,376) were included, yielding a pooled sensitivity of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.78-0.83) and a specificity of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.86-0.91). For adult PCOM diagnosis, six studies (n = 11,436) provided a pooled sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.70-0.86) and a specificity of 0.88 (95% CI, 0.77-0.94). In contrast, the analysis for adolescent PCOS (11 studies, n = 1,090) revealed a significantly lower accuracy, with a pooled sensitivity of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.58-0.73) and a specificity of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.71-0.83). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across all analyses.
