CONCLUSION: The current, updated meta-analysis confirms that serum AMH is a highly specific and moderately sensitive biomarker for diagnosing PCOM and PCOS in adults, supporting its role as an adjunctive diagnostic tool. However, its utility as a standalone test is limited by significant heterogeneity; in addition, its diagnostic performance is further limited in adolescents, providing evidence against its use in such population. Future efforts must focus on the international standardization of AMH assays and the development of population-specific reference values to enhance its clinical utility.

articles.title: Neobladder Impact on Liver Function: A Nationwide Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radical cystectomy (RC) with urinary diversion alters gastrointestinal and metabolic physiology. Orthotopic neobladders (NBs) have traditionally been viewed with caution in patients with hepatic concerns owing to potential reabsorption of urinary solutes. This study aimed to investigate the long-term risks of de novo liver disease, hypertension (HTN), and diabetes mellitus (DM) after RC, challenging the prevailing assumption of hepatic toxicity from NB diversion.

METHODS: This retrospective nationwide cohort study used data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database (2010-2023). Patients without preoperative liver disease, HTN, or DM were included. Primary endpoints were the incidence of liver disease, HTN, and DM. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) balanced covariates in NB and ileal conduit (IC) groups. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: In the IPTW-adjusted cohort (n = 22,144), NB was associated with a 29% lower risk of de novo liver disease compared with IC (HR, 0.71; 95% confidence interval, 0.59-0.84; P < 0.001). Patients with NB also demonstrated a lower incidence of liver cirrhosis (2.04% vs. 2.63%; P = 0.003). In the open-surgery subgroup, NB was associated with reduced risks of HTN (HR 0.92; P < 0.001) and DM (HR, 0.94; P = 0.028). Limitations include the retrospective design and use of administrative codes as diagnoses.

CONCLUSION: Contrary to long-standing concerns regarding urea reabsorption, NB diversion was associated with a lower incidence of de novo liver disease and better metabolic preservation than IC diversion.

articles.title: Plasma Corticosteroid-Binding Globulin Decreases in Decompensated Cirrhosis but Does Not Correlate With Total Cortisol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adrenal insufficiency is prevalent in cirrhosis, but plasma cortisol is considered an unreliable biomarker due to potential corticosteroid-binding globulin (CBG) depletion. Our previous study demonstrated normal plasma CBG concentrations in Child-Pugh A cirrhosis. We aimed to determine plasma CBG concentrations in Child-Pugh B and C patients and assess correlation with basal and stimulated cortisol.

METHODS: Plasma CBG, cosyntropin test results and hepatic function markers were obtained in 68 adult patients with Child-Pugh B-C cirrhosis from the University of Virginia Medical Centre. Data from healthy controls (n = 100) and Child-Pugh A cirrhosis patients (n = 15) from the Royal Adelaide Hospital were used for extended analysis. Plasma CBG was correlated with cirrhosis severity and cosyntropin test results.

RESULTS: Plasma CBG concentrations were 27% lower in Child-Pugh B patients (335.9 [IQR: 228.1-418.4] nmol/L, p < 0.001) and 40% lower in Child-Pugh C patients (274.7 [IQR: 199.0-301.9] nmol/L, p < 0.001) compared to Child-Pugh A patients, who were similar to controls (457.1 [IQR: 430.9-506.5] vs. 439.5 [IQR: 398.6-516.5] nmol/L, p = 0.30). There was a negative correlation between plasma CBG and MELD (ρ = -0.502, p < 0.001), MELD-Na (ρ = -0.509, p < 0.001), and Child-Pugh Scores (ρ = -0.495, p < 0.001). In Child-Pugh B-C patients, there was no correlation between plasma CBG and baseline cortisol (ρ = -0.042, p = 0.74), nor cosyntropin-stimulated cortisol (ρ = +0.039, p = 0.75).

CONCLUSION: Plasma CBG is reduced in Child-Pugh B-C cirrhosis but does not correlate with basal or cosyntropin-stimulated cortisol. This raises further questions about the effect of CBG on altered total cortisol levels in cirrhosis and the value of adjusting existing diagnostic thresholds for adrenal function solely based on CBG concentrations.

articles.title: Complementary Metabolic Effects of Exercise and GLP-1-Based Pharmacotherapy in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Multilevel Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To assess exercise added to glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based pharmacotherapy and pharmacotherapy added to care incorporating exercise or physical-activity advice in Type 2 diabetes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Five databases were searched through 6 October 2026. Two- and three-level random-effects models included selective GLP-1 receptor agonists and tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/GLP-1 receptor agonist. Bias and certainty were assessed. Adherence and harms were summarised.

RESULTS: Of 16 732 records, 24 reports represented 23 independent studies. Exercise addition reduced glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c; mean difference -1.39 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI] -2.34 to -0.44), fasting glucose (-1.29 mmol/L), 2-h glucose (-1.30 mmol/L), total cholesterol (-0.55 mmol/L) and triglycerides (-0.42 mmol/L). Drug addition reduced HbA1c (-1.25 points; 95% CI -1.65 to -0.85), fasting glucose (-2.05 mmol/L), percentage weight change (-7.30 points), waist (-4.93 cm) and systolic pressure (-3.69 mmHg); body mass index and several lipids also improved, while inflammation remained uncertain. Nominal interactions suggested larger HbA1c differences at baseline HbA1c ≥ 8% (-1.70 vs. -0.88 points; p = 0.018), greater waist reductions in longer studies (-6.50 vs. -3.14 cm; p = 0.0079) and fasting-glucose differences by prescribed activity (p = 0.003), although high-volume evidence was sparse. None survived multiplicity adjustment (minimum q = 0.184); these findings generate hypotheses, not optimal dosing rules. Exercise adherence was seldom quantified; gastrointestinal events and discontinuations were higher in some drug arms.

CONCLUSIONS: These results support integrating feasible exercise with indicated GLP-1-based therapy to address glycaemia and broader cardiometabolic targets. Delivery, body composition and tolerability require monitoring; optimal dosing and synergy remain unproven.

articles.title: Implications of Food Ultra-Processing on Liver Health Considering Plant Origin Foods: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: We aimed to investigate whether levels of industrial processing modify the association between plant-sourced foods intake and risks of MASLD and liver cirrhosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cohort study included 185 965 UK Biobank participants. Metabolomic signatures capturing individual metabolic responses to plant-sourced foods consumption (% of total grams) were constructed using elastic-net regression. Cox proportional hazards regression and mediation analyses were used to explore potential associations and mechanisms.

RESULTS: Every 10-percentage-point increment in plant-sourced non-ultra-processed foods (UPF) consumption was associated with 14% and 12% lower risk of MASLD (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.83-0.89) and liver cirrhosis (0.84-0.94). Conversely, plant-sourced UPF consumption was associated with elevated risk of MASLD (1.14-1.23) and liver cirrhosis (1.10-1.24). Specific metabolomic signatures linked to plant-sourced non-UPF (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.71-0.85) and UPF (HR: 1.21-1.29) showed similar associations with both liver diseases and accounted for 17%-32% of the associations. Replacing 10% of total food weight from plant-sourced UPF with an equivalent proportion of plant-sourced non-UPF was associated with reduced risk of MASLD (HR: 0.84, 95% CI: 0.81-0.88) and liver cirrhosis (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.91).

CONCLUSIONS: Plant-sourced non-UPF intake was associated with reduced risks of MASLD and liver cirrhosis, whereas plant-sourced UPF intake was associated with higher risks. Our findings underscore the importance of considering the degree of food processing, even in plant-sourced foods, to prevent the development of liver diseases. The constructed metabolomic signatures may provide insight into biological pathways linking dietary processing with liver disease risk.

articles.title: Estimated Glucose Disposal Rate, Genetic Susceptibility and Risks of Incident and Recurrent Coronary Artery Disease: Evidence From the UK Biobank Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Insulin resistance (IR) and genetic susceptibility are risk factors for coronary artery disease (CAD). The estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) is a surrogate marker of IR. This study aimed to examine their joint effects, interaction and predictive ability for CAD incidence and recurrence.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: 460 859 participants were included from the UK Biobank study: 445 281 without CAD for incident CAD analyses and 15 578 with CAD for recurrent CAD analyses. eGDR was derived from waist circumference, hypertension status and glycosylated haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). Genetic susceptibility was assessed by the polygenic risk score (PRS) for CAD. Multivariable Cox models estimated the hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence interval (CI). Predictive ability was assessed by the C-index.

RESULTS: The median follow-up period was 13.8 years. Compared with the lowest eGDR quartile and medium/high PRS, the highest eGDR quartile with low PRS had the lowest risks of incident CAD (HR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.23-0.27) and recurrent CAD (HR = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.62-0.73). Interactions between eGDR and PRS were significant for incident CAD (p < 0.001) but not significant for recurrent CAD (p = 0.052). The addition of eGDR and PRS into conventional risk factors significantly improved the predictive ability for incident CAD (△C index = 0.017, 95% CI: 0.016-0.019) and recurrent CAD (△C index = 0.005, 95% CI: 0.003-0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Both eGDR and CAD-PRS are needed to predict incident and recurrent CAD. High levels of eGDR with low CAD-PRS are associated with lower incident and recurrent CAD risk. eGDR and CAD-PRS improve the predictive ability for incident and recurrent CAD.

articles.title: Interdisciplinary regenerative management of a radicular cyst associated with a cemental tear and external inflammatory resorption: A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cemental tears are rare clinical entities where a portion of the cementum detaches from the root surface, often leading to localized periodontal or periapical destruction. They are frequently misdiagnosed as vertical root fractures or primary endodontic lesions. This case reports on the successful interdisciplinary management of a radicular cyst associated with a cemental tear and external inflammatory resorption (EIR).

METHODS: A 63-year-old female presented with a sinus tract and radiographic evidence of apical and lateral radiolucency involving teeth #9 and #10. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) identified a cemental tear and an unobturated lateral canal on the necrotic tooth #9, and EIR with a periapical/periodontal abscess on tooth #10, which had been previously root canal treated. Tooth #9 received initial nonsurgical root canal therapy, while tooth #10 received nonsurgical retreatment; both were followed by a combined surgical approach involving apicoectomy of both teeth, removal of the cemental tear, and periodontal regeneration using enamel matrix derivative, platelet-rich fibrin, and bone allograft.

RESULTS: Histopathologic analysis confirmed a radicular cyst. The cemental tear and lateral canal on tooth #9 were confirmed intraoperatively under the surgical microscope. At 2-week, 4-week (suture removal), 2-month, and 6-month follow-up, including CBCT re-evaluation, the patient exhibited favorable soft-tissue healing and resolution of clinical symptoms.

CONCLUSION: A coordinated endodontic‒periodontal microsurgical approach utilizing advanced regenerative biomaterials achieved favorable short-term clinical and radiographic healing of a complex lesion involving a cemental tear, lateral canal, EIR, and radicular cyst, allowing preservation of both teeth. Longer follow-up is needed to confirm the durability of these results.

KEY POINTS: Cemental tears and lateral canals are easily overlooked on two-dimensional radiographs and can mimic vertical root fractures or routine endodontic‒periodontal lesions; cone-beam computed tomography combined with direct microsurgical inspection improves diagnostic accuracy. A coordinated, single-stage endodontic‒periodontal surgical approach-combining apicoectomy, cemental tear removal, and regenerative therapy (enamel matrix derivative, platelet-rich fibrin, and bone allograft)-can achieve favorable short-term healing and avoid extraction, even in teeth with combined periapical and periodontal involvement. Histopathologic confirmation remains essential for definitive diagnosis of radicular cysts and for verifying suspected cemental tear fragments; longer-term follow-up is needed to confirm the durability of regenerative outcomes.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: A small piece of the outer covering of a tooth root, called cementum, can sometimes separate from the tooth. This is called a cemental tear, and it is easy to miss because it can look like a cracked tooth or a common gum infection on X-rays. In this case, a 63-year-old woman had ongoing infection near her upper front teeth. Detailed three-dimensional imaging (a type of dental computed tomography scan) revealed a cemental tear on one tooth and slow, ongoing damage to the root surface of a neighboring tooth, along with a fluid-filled cyst at the site. A dental specialist team performed root canal treatment, then surgically removed the damaged piece of tooth root and used tissue-healing materials, including a gel derived from tooth-forming proteins and a concentrate made from the patient's own blood, to help the bone and gum tissue heal. Six months later, healing looked favorable both clinically and on imaging, and the patient's teeth were saved rather than removed. This case shows how combining advanced imaging with a coordinated effort between root canal and gum specialists can help save teeth that might otherwise need extraction, though longer follow-up is needed to confirm the healing lasts.

articles.title: Partial Splenic Artery Embolization as a Bridging Strategy for Coronary Revascularization in Non-ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction Complicated by Thrombocytopenia Due to Hypersplenism: A Case Report and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Managing acute coronary syndrome in patients with severe thrombocytopenia remains a major clinical challenge. The high risk of bleeding often contraindicates dual antiplatelet therapy and invasive procedures, creating a dilemma for clinicians when urgent revascularization is required. A 74-year-old male with a history of colorectal carcinoma and splenic vein thrombosis presented with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Laboratory evaluation revealed severe, refractory thrombocytopenia (36,000/μL) due to hypersplenism. Given the high surgical and bleeding risk, partial splenic artery embolization (PSE) was performed as a bridging therapy. Platelet counts increased to 131,000/μL within 5 days enabling safe percutaneous coronary intervention for a critical 90% stenosis in the left anterior descending artery. The patient was discharged without periprocedural or early postprocedural complications and with normalized platelet counts. PSE represents an effective, minimally invasive bridging strategy to safely increase platelet counts in high-risk patients with NSTEMI complicated by hypersplenism-related thrombocytopenia, thereby enabling timely and safer coronary revascularization.

articles.title: Environmental Factors Display Multiple Associations with West Nile Virus Risk Modeling in Kansas.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: West Nile virus (WNV) persists as a significant vector-borne disease in the United States, yet risk prediction frameworks vary widely across the Midwest and often rely on sparse case data or limited mosquito surveillance. These challenges are amplified by the asymptomatic nature of WNV infection. Incorporating publicly available environmental and landscape variables-such as temperature, precipitation, drought indices, and land cover-may offer a more robust and scalable foundation for regional WNV risk assessment.

METHODS: Seven years of human and equine WNV case data were integrated with Culex mosquito surveillance records, county-level land cover, and weekly temperature, precipitation, and drought indices for the state of Kansas. Mosquito abundance from 26 unique trapping sites was assessed using annual regression models, and case occurrence was evaluated using zero-inflated negative binomial models. Site-level trend assessments examined ecological patterns in relation to precipitation, drought, and habitat composition.

RESULTS: Lagged temperature and drought severity were the most stable environmental indicators of case occurrence, supported by trend-level contrasts between drought and nondrought seasons. Landscape composition shaped mosquito responses to precipitation and moisture availability. Although Culex abundance showed a significant monotonic association with WNV cases at a 3-week lag, regression models did not detect a linear relationship.

CONCLUSION: Publicly available, routinely updated, and geographically resolved environmental indicators can support a scalable WNV risk assessment framework. This study represents the first integration of these environmental, landscape, and surveillance factors for Kansas and provides a foundation for future work incorporating viral testing of mosquito pools, finer-scale land use data, and more consistent trap placement to strengthen predictive capacity.

articles.title: Outcomes of respiratory failure and support in children with cancer from resource-variable hospitals.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Studies suggest noninvasive respiratory support (NRS) prior to intubation is associated with poor outcomes in children with cancer, but those treated successfully with NRS alone typically have higher survival.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between NRS and outcomes among children with cancer and acute respiratory failure in resource-variable hospitals.

METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter quality improvement registry among hospitals providing childhood cancer care in Latin America and Spain. Clinical deterioration events (CDE) were counted if respiratory support was used, and CDE mortality was the primary outcome. Mixed methods and logistic regression were used to assess associations with mortality.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: 2446 CDEs were included, occurring among 1996 individual patients from 82 hospitals in 20 countries. Respiratory support included invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) alone (63.9%), n = 1564, NRS alone (20.3%, n = 496) and NRS prior to intubation (15.8%, n = 386). Overall CDE mortality was 47.7%, with the highest mortality in the NRS prior to IMV group (63.5%). Compared to NRS alone, both NRS prior to intubation (OR = 27.0, 95%CI:17.7-41.0, p < 0.001) and IMV alone (OR = 19.7, 95%CI:13.5-28.7, p < 0.001) had increased odds of CDE mortality. Among CDEs requiring IMV and controlling for center variability, NRS prior to IMV was associated with CDE mortality (aOR: 1.53, 95%CI:1.17-2.00, p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: In these resource-variable setting, NRS prior to intubation was associated with higher mortality. While there is a subgroup of children who benefit from NRS, use of this modality in patients with multi-organ dysfunction and for prolonged duration without improvement should be reconsidered.

articles.title: Conduction System Pacing With DF-1 ICD Systems Using a Medtronic 3830 Lead: A Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) who require ventricular pacing are at risk for pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) from chronic right ventricular (RV) pacing. Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), offers more physiologic ventricular activation, but integration with ICD therapy remains challenging. The DF-1 ICD connector standard provides an opportunity to incorporate a separate CSP lead while maintaining high-voltage ICD therapy. We evaluated the feasibility of an alternative ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead connected to a dual-chamber ICD generator.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of 17 consecutive patients who underwent this configuration at a single center between October 2022 and August 2025. For subgroup analyses, patients were stratified by baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) as LVEF ≤ 50% (n = 9) or LVEF > 50% (n = 8). QRS duration, LVEF, left ventricular end-systolic dimension (LVESD), tricuspid regurgitation (TR) severity, and device outcomes were assessed during follow-up.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 15.0 months (IQR 6.2-19.2). The Medtronic 3830 lead was successfully implanted in all 17 patients, with confirmed LBBAP in 16 patients (94.1%) and deep septal pacing without definitive left bundle branch capture in one patient. No CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure were required. Among patients with paired measurements, LVEF increased from 41.6% ± 15.0% to 45.9% ± 14.1%, although the change was not statistically significant (p = 0.169), while LVESD decreased from 4.33 ± 0.72 cm to 3.89 ± 0.79 cm (p = 0.022). In paired subgroup analyses, patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated an increase in LVEF from 31.9% ± 6.2% to 40.1% ± 14.3% (p = 0.053) and a decrease in LVESD from 4.62 ± 0.65 cm to 4.11 ± 0.71 cm (p = 0.048), whereas patients with baseline LVEF >50% demonstrated no significant change in either measure. QRS duration did not change significantly in either subgroup. Overall TR severity did not change significantly (Bhapkar p = 0.337), although 5 of 12 patients with paired imaging experienced at least a one-grade increase in TR severity and no patient developed new severe TR. Two patients (11.8%) died during follow-up, with neither death attributed to the device configuration.

CONCLUSION: An ICD configuration using a DF-1 defibrillation lead paired with a Medtronic 3830 CSP lead on a dual-chamber generator was technically feasible, with successful 3830 lead implantation in all patients, confirmed LBBAP in 94.1%, and no CSP lead revisions for mechanical or electrical failure during intermediate-term follow-up. Patients with baseline LVEF ≤50% demonstrated numerical improvement in LVEF and a reduction in LVESD, while ventricular function remained stable in those with LVEF >50%. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective comparative studies.

articles.title: Independent Predictors of In-Hospital Mortality in Surgically Treated Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infections: A 6-Year Experience from a Jordanian Tertiary Center.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infections (NSTI) is a life-threatening infection of the subcutaneous tissue and fascia, and it is considered a surgical emergency with high mortality rates. There is a lack of recent studies on this topic in Jordan and in the region. This study aims to identify any factors associated with a higher mortality rate in patients with NSTI who underwent surgical management.

METHODS: This is a single-center retrospective cohort study conducted on all patients with NSTI who underwent surgical management at Jordan University Hospital from 2019 to 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, laboratory results, cultures, and postoperative outcomes, with the primary outcome being in-hospital mortality. Any patient with incomplete data was excluded.

RESULTS: A total of 53 patients were enrolled in this study, with a mortality rate of 17.0%. Thirty-two (60.4%) of the included patients were males, with a mean age of 59.6. The most common comorbidity among enrolled patients was found to be diabetes mellitus (71.7%), but it was found to have no association with mortality. Septic shock (p < 0.01) and decreased level of consciousness (p < 0.01) were the 2 strongest predictors of in-hospital mortality in this cohort.

CONCLUSION: Multiple factors were associated with mortality in patients with NSTI, with the strongest predictors being sepsis and decreased level of consciousness. Further clinical studies are needed to assess these factors to improve the management of NSTI and decrease its mortality.

articles.title: NR6A1 Drives Cardiac Remodeling by Transcriptionally Activating the Mineralocorticoid Receptor.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) and mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2) signaling is a central driver of pathologic cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF). The transcriptional regulation of NR3C2 and the amplification of RAAS-driven cardiac remodeling remain poorly understood.

METHODS: Transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing data, along with HF samples from humans and mice, were used for gene expression analysis. Cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgenic (Nr6a1-cTG) and knockout (Nr6a1-cKO) mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction to evaluate cardiac remodeling and dysfunction. Adeno-associated virus 9-shNr3c2 was used to test whether Nr3c2 contributes to remodeling driven by Nr6a1 overexpression. Primary mouse cardiomyocytes were used for in vitro analysis. RNA sequencing, Western blot, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and luciferase assays were performed for the mechanism analysis.

RESULTS: NR6A1 (nuclear receptor subfamily 6, group A, member 1) expression was increased in the heart tissue from human and mouse failing hearts. Activation of NR6A1 contributed to the hypertrophic growth of cardiomyocytes in vitro. In mice, a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 transgene aggravated left ventricular dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis after transverse aortic constriction, whereas a cardiomyocyte-specific Nr6a1 knockout protected the heart from failure and remodeling. Transcriptome analysis of NR6A1 downstream transcriptional targets revealed that Nr3c2 is a prominent RAAS-related downstream target in both hearts and cardiomyocytes. The transcription cofactor NR6A1 directly bound the Nr3c2 promoter, increased promoter activity, and enhanced Nr3c2 transcription in cardiomyocytes. Nr3c2 silencing attenuated NR6A1-associated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and reduced cardiac dysfunction and hypertrophy in Nr6a1-cTG mice after transverse aortic constriction. Analysis of the upstream regulation of NR6A1 in HF stress revealed that HF-related angiotensin II/AT1R signaling promoted NR6A1 expression and its downstream transcriptional and functional events in a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-dependent manner.

CONCLUSIONS: RAAS (angiotensin II) increases the orphan receptor NR6A1, which transcriptionally activates MR/NR3C2 signaling and aggravates RAAS-associated pathologic remodeling under HF stress. This regulatory network represents an undefined feed-forward amplification mechanism linking angiotensin II signaling to MR/NR3C2 activation and may be a therapeutic target for HF with persistent MR activation.

articles.title: VAD Wean Recovery Network: Long-Term Outcomes of LVAD Weaning for Myocardial Recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial recovery facilitated by the combination of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and guideline-directed medical therapy can lead to sufficient myocardial improvement. This in turn may allow LVAD weaning in appropriately selected patients with chronic advanced heart failure. However, sufficient data on the long-term outcomes of this therapeutic strategy are lacking, thereby hindering widespread adoption of LVAD weaning. We present the primary results from the VAD Wean Myocardial Recovery International Network examining long-term outcomes after LVAD weaning for myocardial recovery.

METHODS: We studied 603 patients with chronic advanced heart failure from 60 international centers who underwent LVAD weaning. Preimplantation, LVAD cardiac recovery assessment, and postweaning patient characteristics and outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was event-free survival (free of heart transplantation or re-LVAD) in the weaned-for-recovery cohort.

RESULTS: The LVAD-weaned cohort had a mean age of 42±15 years; 33% were female; and 9.4% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At LVAD implantation, 88% had Intermacs (Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support) profiles 1 to 3, and 41.6% required temporary mechanical circulatory support. Median LVAD support duration was 440 days (interquartile range, 261-770) before weaning. At the time of weaning, median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% (interquartile range, 45%-57.5%), and left ventricular internal diastolic diameter was 48 mm (interquartile range, 43-53 mm). One-year survival after weaning was 91%, with 2.3% requiring re-LVAD and 3.7% requiring heart transplantation. In a secondary exploratory matched analysis against LVAD bridge-to-transplantation recipients from the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation registry, long-term survival was similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: This international, multicenter analysis suggests that in patients with chronic advanced heart failure achieving myocardial recovery with LVAD support, device weaning yields excellent long-term outcomes. These findings may help address the underuse of LVADs as a bridge-to-recovery strategy in select patients.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) improves symptoms and health status at 1 year in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, but its association with clinical events during longer follow-up remains uncertain.

METHODS: This secondary analysis reports extended follow-up of TRI-FR (URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811), a prospectively registered, multicenter randomized trial comparing T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) with OMT alone in patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation. In total, 300 patients were randomized (152 to T-TEER plus OMT and 148 to OMT alone). Prespecified analyses included time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid surgery, or cardiovascular death using cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards models and recurrent HFH using the Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying model. A 12-month landmark analysis included patients alive and under follow-up at 12 months.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 30.8 months (75th percentile, 41.0; maximum, 56.4), 101 HFHs (17 fatal), 5 additional cardiovascular deaths, and 11 tricuspid surgeries were recorded. Among 81 patients with a first composite event, T-TEER plus OMT reduced the risk versus OMT alone (hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.36-0.88]; P=0.0109). Cardiovascular death or tricuspid surgery did not differ significantly (hazard ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.33-1.71]; P=0.4911). T-TEER plus OMT reduced recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.32-0.84]; P=0.0073). In the 12-month landmark cohort (n=276), T-TEER plus OMT was associated with lower risks of a first composite event (hazard ratio, 0.40 [95% CI, 0.23-0.70]; log-rank P=0.0009) and recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.44 [95% CI, 0.23-0.83]; P=0.0120). Severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation at the last core laboratory assessment was present in 6.77% with T-TEER plus OMT and 53.5% with OMT alone (P<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation, T-TEER plus OMT reduced first composite events and recurrent HFH compared with OMT alone during extended follow-up. These associations persisted among patients alive and under follow-up at the 12-month landmark.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811.

articles.title: Rare Case of Cushing's Syndrome in Infants With Reversible Myocardial Hypertrophy.
articles.abstract: The occurrence of isolated Cushing's syndrome in early infant adrenal cortical tumors is very rare. Cushing's syndrome with left ventricular hypertrophy is considered a risk factor for the development of myocardial ischemia and heart failure. We report a 5-month-old boy with Cushing's syndrome caused by adrenal cortical tumor, who presented with reversible myocardial hypertrophy and subclinical systolic dysfunction detected by left ventricular global longitudinal strain.

articles.title: Predictive Value of the SMART-COP Scoring System for Prognosis and Severity in Paediatric Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of Systolic blood pressure, Multilobar involvement, Albumin, Respiratory rate, Tachycardia, Confusion, Oxygenation, pH (SMART-COP) score in predicting short-term outcomes for children diagnosed with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled children from 3 months to 18 years old who had CAP and were admitted to a tertiary paediatric emergency department between 1 October 2023, and 1 March 2025, excluding those hospitalized within the preceding 14 days. SMART-COP was calculated at the time of presentation. The outcomes of the study were hospitalization, admission to the paediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and the necessity for advanced respiratory support or vasopressor therapy.

RESULTS: Among 1003 patients, 561 (55.9%) had a paediatric ward admission, 37 (3.7%) had a PICU admission and 19 (1.9%) required advanced respiratory or vasopressor support. The median SMART-COP score was 2 (0-9). Scores were higher in children with a paediatric ward admission than in those without a ward admission (3 vs. 1, p < 0.001), and in children admitted to the PICU than in those not admitted to the PICU (5 vs. 2, p < 0.001). Area under the curve values were 0.875 for hospital ward admission (cutoff ≥ 2; sensitivity 0.857; specificity 0.808), 0.915 for PICU admission (cutoff ≥ 4; sensitivity 0.946; specificity 0.811) and 0.929 for advanced support (cutoff ≥ 4; sensitivity 0.947; specificity 0.797).

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-centre study, SMART-COP showed good discrimination for the evaluated short-term outcomes. These findings support further prospective validation but do not establish the score as a routine paediatric triage tool.

articles.title: Harnessing Unconventional T Cell Populations With Biomaterial-Based Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Unconventional T cells (UTCs) including γδ T cells, mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and natural killer T cells have gained increased attention as potential alternatives to conventional adoptive T cell therapies due to their rapid effector function, resistance to immune escape, and allogeneic compatibility. Recent clinical trials, however, have failed to match the efficacy of preclinical studies due to challenges in maintaining and targeting balanced UTC activation in situ. UTCs are activated by disease-associated lipids or small-molecule metabolites which are highly efficacious yet rapidly cleared. Systemically administering activating quantities of these moieties can result in UTC anergy and off-target toxicity. Furthermore, effective UTC activation requires uptake and presentation of these activating ligands by antigen-presenting cells within diseased tissues to ensure spatially precise immune engagement. Biomaterial-mediated drug delivery can offer solutions to maintain and localize delivery of UTC-activating antigens to specific cells (UTCs, antigen presenting cells) and tissues (secondary lymphoid organs, tumor sites). Herein, we describe the activation mechanisms and effector functions of UTCs and detail recent advances in biomaterial-based drug delivery solutions that utilize in situ activation of UTCs to treat cancer and infectious disease. We also identify opportunities for biomaterial technologies to further explore and expand upon existing UTC-harnessing therapies.

articles.title: Decision-Making About Timing of Birth for Women With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore how women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and clinicians navigate decision-making about timing of birth amid limited evidence supporting induction of labour (IOL).

DESIGN: Qualitative descriptive study.

SETTING: Two metropolitan tertiary hospitals and one regional hospital in South Australia.

POPULATION OR SAMPLE: Women with recent experience of GDM and clinicians providing antenatal care to women with GDM.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews and focus groups were conducted with women and clinicians. Data analysed using reflexive thematic analysis informed by an interpretivist approach.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Experiences, perceptions, and information needs related to decision-making regarding the timing of birth for women with GDM.

RESULTS: Four themes illustrated how IOL was frequently positioned as the default pathway following a GDM diagnosis. Women described reduced confidence in bodily autonomy and an increased sense of responsibility for foetal safety, often perceiving induction as the safest option. Clinicians described balancing perceptions of risk, guideline interpretation, and service pressures while framing IOL as the anticipated pathway. Fragmented care and inconsistent communication limited opportunities for shared decision-making.

CONCLUSIONS: Decision-making about timing of birth for women with GDM appeared influenced by risk framing, institutional practices, and uncertainty within the evidence base. Despite limited evidence supporting routine induction, IOL was often normalised in clinical care. Greater emphasis on consistent information, balanced risk communication, and engagement with women's values and preferences may strengthen woman-centred shared decision-making.

articles.title: Improving Oxygen Extraction Fraction (OEF) Mapping From Integrated Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping and Quantitative Blood Oxygen Level Dependent Imaging (QSM+qBOLD, or QQ) by Learning Temporal Signal Evolution.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To improve deep learning-based QSM+qBOLD (QQ) oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) mapping by explicitly learning the temporal evolution of the multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) magnitude signal, whose decay encodes the tissue oxygenation that QQ-based OEF mapping depends on.

METHODS: 3D multi-echo gradient echo images were acquired in 34 ischemic stroke patients with arterial spin labeling (ASL) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). We developed QQ-S, a deep learning method that estimates OEF by inverting the QQ model. QQ-S extends QQ-NET by adding convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM) modules to the encoder to process the mGRE echoes sequentially. To isolate the effect of this architectural change, both networks were trained with the same simulated data and training scheme including the loss function. OEF maps from QQ-S and QQ-NET were compared in simulation and ischemic stroke patients.

RESULTS: In simulation, QQ-S provided more accurate OEF than QQ-NET, with lower mean absolute error (MAE) against the simulation ground truth: 3.43% vs. 5.03% in normal-appearing tissue and 4.88% vs. 10.60% in low-OEF lesions. In subacute stroke patients, where no ground truth is available, the lesion-to-contralateral OEF ratio was significantly lower with QQ-S than with QQ-NET (0.71 ± 0.26 vs. 0.81 ± 0.24; p < 0.001), suggesting more sensitive detection of lesion OEF, consistent with PET reports in the subacute phase. OEF in acute lesions and normal-appearing tissue was comparable between methods.

CONCLUSION: By explicitly learning inter-echo signal evolution with ConvLSTM, QQ-S improves OEF accuracy over QQ-NET, offering a promising tool for assessing tissue viability from conventional mGRE data.

articles.title: An exploratory baseline workflow for integrating Alzheimer's disease GWAS and entorhinal cortex expression data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrating genome-wide association study (GWAS) results with tissue gene expression is a common route to candidate genes in complex disease, but simple integration strategies are rarely tested against chance. This study presents a transparent, reproducible workflow that combines GWAS summary statistics with post-mortem brain expression data and evaluates the resulting overlap with explicit null models.

METHODS: Genome-wide significant variants from a GWAS of 455,258 individuals (GRCh37) were mapped to genes by positional proximity (Ensembl GRCh37; distance 0 inside a gene, otherwise nearest gene within 50 kb), giving 128 genes. Entorhinal cortex expression from GSE131617 (13 Braak stage 0 controls, 19 Braak stage V-VI cases; 22,011 probes) was compared with an empirical-Bayes moderated linear model adjusted for sex. Probes were mapped to validated gene symbols (14,172 genes tested). The overlap of the two gene lists was assessed with a hypergeometric test on the tested-gene background and a sex-stratified permutation test, and complemented by six sensitivity analyses, a threshold-free test, and ranked gene-set analysis.

RESULTS: No probe passed Benjamini-Hochberg correction (smallest adjusted p = 0.075). At an exploratory threshold (p < 0.05), 1458 probes (945 genes) were selected. Three genes overlapped the GWAS gene set (AGFG2, PVRL2, SLC24A4), close to the 4.0 expected by chance (hypergeometric p = 0.77; permutation p = 0.37). The result was similar without sex adjustment (five genes, p = 0.32), after excluding the APOE region, and with protein-coding genes only. GWAS genes were not shifted toward lower expression p values (p = 0.24). The three genes lie in three distinct chromosomal regions. Ranked gene-set analysis of the full results indicated lower expression in AD of gene sets for oxidative phosphorylation, ribosome, and synaptic vesicle cycle (false discovery rates 0.011, 0.013, and 0.040).

CONCLUSIONS: The overlap between GWAS-implicated genes and expression changes was not greater than expected by chance, so the three genes are exploratory candidates and not evidence of convergence. The workflow, with built-in coordinate checks and null-model testing, is released as a reproducible baseline for larger cohorts and for comparison with more formal integration methods.

articles.title: Polyamine-related transcriptomic alterations and differential co-expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyamine metabolism is implicated in cancers, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, comprehensive analyses investigating patient-disjoint pairwise co-expression changes, uncertainty estimates, and outcome-independent expression scores remain limited.

METHODS: Using transcriptomic and clinical data from TCGA-LIHC (n = 365 tumours, n = 50 adjacent non-tumour samples) and an external dataset (GSE76427, 115 tumours), we assessed differential expression, pairwise differential co-expression via Spearman correlation differences (Δρ) with bootstrap confidence intervals, and module scores in the context of overall survival.

RESULTS: There were 11 upregulated and 13 downregulated polyamine-related genes in HCC from differential expression analysis. Co-expression analysis demonstrates significant correlation changes in some gene pairs, with changes enriched among curated functional relationships (permutation p = 0.025). In univariable analyses, Core Synthesis had the highest hazard ratio (HR per SD = 1.56) among all module scores, and the strongest statistical significance (q = 1.69 × 10⁻6, p = 1.69 × 10⁻7), while Coordination Deviation had a hazard ratio below 1.0 (HR per SD = 0.84, q = 0.049, p = 0.029). For individual genes, SMS (HR = 1.46, q = 1.29 × 10⁻4), AMD1 (HR = 1.46, q = 7.14 × 10⁻4), and SMOX (HR = 1.44, q = 0.001) showed strong associations. After adjusting for age, sex, stage, grade, AFP, cirrhosis status, and treatment, Core Synthesis, Activation Burden, Synthesis Support, SMS, AMD1, SMOX, and OAZ2 remained significant. By adding Core Synthesis to a clinical baseline, there was an increase in cross-validation scores (mean out-of-fold C-index 0.665 vs. 0.608). Furthermore, external validation demonstrated the same sign of correlation change in 75% of the differential co-expression pairs (such as SAT1-SMS and OAZ2-ODC1), though prognostic performance was not significant in the smaller external dataset.

CONCLUSION: This study investigates polyamine-related transcriptional changes and co-expression remodelling in HCC. Specific burden scores and expression signatures show associations with clinical outcomes and with the sign of correlation change. These findings are hypothesis-generating and further validation will strengthen the results.

articles.title: Self-assembled ferritin nanovaccine displaying Giardia duodenalis macrophage migration inhibitory factor elicits protective immunity against giardiasis.
articles.abstract: Giardia duodenalis is a globally distributed zoonotic intestinal protozoan that infects humans and a wide range of animals, causing giardiasis characterized by diarrhea, malabsorption, growth retardation, and substantial economic losses in the livestock industry. Despite the availability of antiparasitic drugs, reinfection remains common, and the absence of effective vaccines continues to hinder sustainable control of giardiasis. Furthermore, the relatively poor immunogenicity of conventional subunit vaccines has limited the development of effective anti-Giardia immunization strategies. In this study, we developed a self-assembled ferritin nanoparticle vaccine targeting Giardia duodenalis macrophage migration inhibitory factor (GdMIF) using the SpyTag/SpyCatcher conjugation system. GdMIF was covalently displayed on the surface of ferritin nanocages to construct the SpyCatcher-ferritin nanoparticle displaying macrophage migration inhibitory factor (SF-MIF) nanovaccine. Physicochemical analyses confirmed successful nanoparticle assembly with favorable stability and prolonged antigen retention in vivo. Immunization with SF-MIF elicited significantly stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than the soluble antigen, as evidenced by enhanced antigen-specific antibody production, elevated immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) and IgG2a levels, increased secretion of interleukin 4 (IL-4), and augmented splenic lymphocyte proliferation. In addition, SF-MIF promoted the differentiation of plasma cells, memory-associated B cells, and effector memory T cells. In the Mongolian gerbil challenge model, SF-MIF conferred significant protection against G. duodenalis infection, markedly reducing both trophozoite burden and cyst shedding while exhibiting a favorable safety profile. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SF-MIF is a promising vaccine candidate against giardiasis and highlight the potential of self-assembled ferritin nanoparticles as an effective platform for developing vaccines against intestinal protozoan parasites.

articles.title: Risk factors and efficacy comparison of different treatment methods for cervical spondylotic myelopathy complicated with traumatic central cord syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aimed to analyze the independent risk factors for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) patients with traumatic central cord syndrome (TCCS). In addition, the short-term and medium-term efficacy of conservative treatment and surgical treatment on patients' neurological function and imaging were compared.

METHODS: Total of 182 patients with CSM admitted in our hospital during January 2016 to December 2021 were chosen as the study subjects. They were divided into a complicated group (with TCCS) and a non-complicated group (without TCCS). Influencing factors were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A nomogram prediction model was constructed based on these factors. Patients with TCCS were divided into a conservative group (n = 30) and a surgical group (n = 38) according to the actual treatment received. Changes in the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure III (SCIM-III) score, modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score, and imaging parameters were compared between the two groups before treatment and at 3 and 6 months after treatment. Subgroup analyses were also performed according to ASIA grade, surgical timing, and surgical approach. Complications and the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) were assessed.

RESULTS: Age, positive pathological signs, hand intrinsic muscle score, intramedullary high signal (IMHS) length, degree of spinal cord compression, and degree of spinal canal stenosis were all associated with CSM complicated by TCCS (P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age (OR = 2.264), high IMHS length (OR = 2.532), high degree of spinal cord compression (OR = 3.438), and high degree of spinal canal stenosis (OR = 3.900) were independent risk factors for CSM complicated by TCCS. And high hand intrinsic muscle score (OR = 0.430) was an independent protective factor (all P < 0.05). A nomogram prediction model was constructed based on the above five factors. At 3 months after treatment, the improvements in ASIA sensory and motor scores, SCIM-III score, mJOA score, intervertebral space height, and cervical lordosis angle in the surgical group were significantly greater than those in the conservative group (all P < 0.05), and the differences reached the MCID threshold. At 6 months after treatment, no significant differences were observed in any indicators between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Subgroup analysis by ASIA grade showed that in the B/C grade subgroup, the improvement in ASIA motor score at 3 months was greater in the surgical group than in the conservative group (P = 0.038). No significant differences in neurological improvement were found between the surgical timing subgroups or between the surgical approach subgroups. There was no significant difference in the incidence of complications between the two groups (P > 0.05), and no severe complications were observed in either group.

CONCLUSION: Advanced age, low hand intrinsic muscle score, high IMHS length, high degree of spinal cord compression, and high degree of spinal canal stenosis are independent risk factors for CSM complicated by TCCS. The nomogram provides a visual tool for clinical risk screening. Surgical treatment can significantly promote early (3-month) recovery of neurological function and imaging structure compared with conservative treatment, offering a distinct advantage in accelerating rehabilitation. However, the efficacy of the two treatment modalities converges at 6 months.

articles.title: Multiscan 3D ultrasound stitching for large-volume abdominal imaging: a phantom and prospective feasibility study in healthy volunteers and selected patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional abdominal ultrasound is limited by operator-dependent acquisition, non-standardized documentation, and a restricted field of view. Tomographic three-dimensional ultrasound combined with multiscan stitching may overcome some of these limitations by generating structured reviewable large-volume datasets that allow retrospective multiplanar review. This pilot study evaluated the technical feasibility of magnetically tracked multiscan three-dimensional ultrasound (3DUS) stitching for large-volume abdominal imaging.

METHODS: A multiscan stitching algorithm was first assessed qualitatively under controlled conditions using standardized ultrasound phantoms to evaluate volume reconstruction, seam continuity, and artifact formation. The method was then prospectively applied in 22 healthy volunteers and 22 patients with focal or chronic parenchymal liver disease in a single-centre observational within-participant comparison. Conventional ultrasound served as the clinical comparator for image quality and completeness of organ depiction, paired ordinal comparisons were exploratory and post hoc. Additional phantom and proof-of-concept torso examinations were unscored.

RESULTS: In phantom experiments, adjacent three-dimensional ultrasound volumes could be merged with visually preserved margin continuity under standardized acquisition conditions and sufficient nominal overlap. In healthy volunteers, stitched Scan 3 yielded a median image-quality score of 3 (IQR 2-3) versus 4 (4-4) for conventional ultrasound and a median organ-coverage score of 20 (18-20.75) versus 27 (26-27.75), respectively (both Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). In patients, non-stitched Scan 6 yielded an image-quality score of 4 (3-4) versus 3.5 (3-4, adjusted P = 0.289), whereas organ coverage remained lower at 17 (16.25-17) versus 27 (24.25-27, adjusted P < 0.001). Focal lesions and features of chronic liver disease were visible in reconstructed datasets, but diagnostic accuracy was not assessed. Stitching-related artifacts, respiratory motion, transducer pressure, and tracking-related limitations were identified as relevant technical challenges.

CONCLUSION: Multiscan tomographic three-dimensional ultrasound enabled large-volume abdominal ultrasound recording, with at least one analysable 3DUS dataset obtained for each of the 44 enrolled participants under favourable examination conditions. The stored datasets allowed retrospective multiplanar review, however, the fixed-reader design did not establish examiner independence or interobserver reliability. The findings remain exploratory and system-specific. Quantitative validation of geometric accuracy, diagnostic performance, reproducibility, and robustness in larger and more heterogeneous patient cohorts is required before broader clinical implementation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The non-interventional study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016736) on 27 May 2019, before the first participant was enrolled on 28 May 2019. The registry planned 50 participants, whereas 44 participants were included in the present analysis.

articles.title: Unlocking the power of citizen data in addressing infectious diseases.
articles.abstract: Citizen data is data produced with the involvement of individuals and communities, from deciding what and how to measure through to how results are used. In pandemic and epidemic intelligence, it can expand the range of information available by adding observations, local knowledge and lived experience that routine surveillance does not capture. However, its routine integration into public health surveillance and decision-making remains limited by concerns about data quality, representativeness, ethics, governance, trust, sustainability and compatibility with official information systems. This report summarises two linked WHO Innovation Forum sessions that brought together experts from public health, citizen science, research, national statistics, international organisations and civil society. Participants examined how citizen data can contribute to different stages of pandemic and epidemic intelligence and discussed the conditions required for meaningful and sustainable participation. The sessions highlighted the need to define the purpose and intended use of citizen data from the outset, design activities with participating communities and recognise citizens as partners rather than solely as data providers. Inclusive participation, clear feedback to contributors, transparent methods, appropriate data protection and links with existing surveillance and statistical systems were identified as essential. Long-term use also requires institutional ownership, adequate resources, suitable skills and continued engagement with communities. When these conditions are met, citizen data can help address information gaps, represent community realities and support more timely and locally relevant public health decisions.

articles.title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Imaging Integration for Individualized Transseptal Puncture Planning During Atrial Fibrillation Ablation.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Transseptal puncture (TSP) is a critical step during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, and accurate anatomical understanding of the interatrial septum is essential for individualized procedural planning. Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) provides real-time visualization of septal anatomy but is limited by its two-dimensional representation and operator dependence. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted multimodal imaging framework integrating preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) with intraoperative ICE to provide patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) anatomical guidance for TSP planning. This single-center study enrolled 700 patients undergoing AF ablation. An AI framework was developed using data from 500 patients to perform automated segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and CTA-ICE multimodal image integration. The framework was evaluated in an independent temporal validation cohort of 200 patients. The primary outcome was the influence of AI-assisted anatomical information on individualized TSP planning, assessed by changes in puncture strategy following AI-assisted assessment. Secondary outcomes included decision confidence, planning time, interreader agreement, and procedural feasibility. The AI framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient of 0.854 for automated anatomical segmentation and a Dice coefficient of 0.862 for 3D left atrial reconstruction. In the temporal validation cohort, at least one AI-recommended adjustment was incorporated into the final TSP strategy in 68 patients (34.0%). The recommendations addressed involved three key components of TSP planning: puncture site category in 52 patients (26.0%), puncture direction in 61 patients (30.5%), and puncture trajectory or angle in 74 patients (37.0%). AI-assisted assessment increased decision confidence (4.3 ± 0.6 vs. 3.4 ± 0.8, p < 0.001), reduced planning time (28.7 ± 10.3 vs. 42.5 ± 15.2 s, p < 0.001), and improved interreader agreement for anatomical assessment. In the temporal validation cohort, acute successful TSP was achieved in 196 patients (98.0%), with a mean transseptal time of 6.8-2.5 min and an overall complication rate of 3.0%. AI-assisted integration of preprocedural CTA with intraoperative ICE provides patient-specific 3D anatomical information that supports individualized TSP planning. The proposed framework demonstrated feasibility and compatibility with anatomical assessment and procedural planning, hopefully contributing to improve procedural or clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Renal Safety of Antistaphylococcal Penicillins Versus Cefazolin in Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia: A Causal Machine Learning Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare short-term renal safety of antistaphylococcal penicillins (ASP; nafcillin or oxacillin) versus cefazolin in adults with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteremia and explore heterogeneity of renal harm.

METHODS: We emulated a target trial using a retrospective new-user, active-comparator cohort from MIMIC-IV v3.1. The primary outcome was 7-day acute kidney injury (AKI) by creatinine-based KDIGO criteria. Five causal machine-learning models were compared in a derivation set (70%); the selected model was evaluated in a held-out test set (30%).

RESULTS: Among 2,223 screened patients, 445 were analyzed (138 ASP; 307 cefazolin). Crude AKI occurred in 48.6% with ASP and 33.4% with cefazolin. The primary held-out doubly robust average treatment effect was 0.153 (95% CI, - 0.183 to 0.416). The secondary full-cohort estimate was 0.160 (95% CI, 0.069 to 0.267). Predicted individualized treatment effects were positive across all patients, indicating variation in magnitude rather than direction of renal harm.

CONCLUSIONS: ASP showed a consistent signal of higher short-term AKI risk than cefazolin, although the primary held-out estimate was imprecise. No subgroup with a predicted renal safety advantage for ASP was identified.

articles.title: Discordance Between Guidelines and Practice in ICP Monitoring in Traumatic Brain Injury: Insights from the CENTER-TBI Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVE: Intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring is important in selected patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI). This study aims to quantify variability in ICP monitoring practices across European trauma centres, to analyse associations with patient and imaging characteristics and to explore concordance between the practice of ICP monitoring and guideline recommendations.

METHODS: In the Collaborative European Neurotrauma Effectiveness Research in Traumatic Brain Injury (CENTER-TBI) database, we assessed concordance between ICP monitoring and guideline recommendations, defined by a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score ≤ 8 and a positive computed tomography (CT) scan (Marshall score > 1) on presentation. To determine between-centre differences, the case-mix-adjusted percentage of ICP placements and duration of monitoring per centre were determined in the mixed-effects logistic regression model. To determine patient and imaging characteristics associated with the insertion of an ICP monitor, a mixed-effects logistic regression model was performed.

RESULTS: Among 2138 patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU), 921 patients (43%) received an ICP device. Among 900 patients meeting guideline recommendations for ICP monitoring, 571 (64%) received an ICP monitor. There were large between-centre variations in ICP-monitor placements and the duration of ICP monitoring [median odds ratio (MOR) 2.5, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.1-2.8 and MOR 3.2, 95% CI 2.4-3.8, respectively]. Factors associated with ICP monitoring were a lower GCS score on admission [odds ratio (OR) 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-0.9], at least one pupil that was unreactive to light (OR 1.6, 95% CI 1.1-2.5) and the presence of CT abnormalities (i.e. contusion: OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.9-3.2).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a detailed patient-level description of ICP monitoring decision-making. ICP monitoring decisions frequently extended beyond guideline criteria and were influenced by neurological, radiological and treatment-related considerations. The observed variation may reflect both differences in practice and limitations of existing guideline frameworks. These findings provide a foundation for future efforts aimed at developing ICP monitoring recommendations that are more closely aligned with real-world expert decision-making.

articles.title: Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: Revisiting the Curing Coma® Campaign COME TOGETHER Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Curing Coma Campaign (CCC) initiated a survey to assess global practices in coma management but lacked of sufficient data from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). A follow-up survey in India provided regional insights, which cannot be generalized to all LMICs. The aim of this study was to conduct a dedicated survey across various LMICs to understand local practices and challenges in the care of comatose patients.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional online survey of 163 healthcare professionals from 32 LMICs, categorized into six geographical regions following the World Bank classification. The survey, an adaptation of the original COME TOGETHER questionnaire, covered coma definition, etiology, diagnostic tools, management, and prognostication.

RESULTS: The majority of respondents were from South Asia (41.1%). Most worked in urban areas (96%), in government teaching hospitals (64%). There was substantial agreement on three cardinal features of coma: a Glascow Coma Scale (GCS) ≤ 8, absence of wakefulness, and failure to respond purposefully to stimuli. Traumatic brain injury (TBI) was the most common etiology (45%). GCS was the most frequently used assessment tool (96%). Most respondents reported no formal policy for the withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies (63%), and ethicists were rarely involved in such discussions (70%). The majority (76%) of respondents reported no patient follow-up after intensive care unit (ICU) discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: This survey highlights significant variability and critical gaps in coma management across LMICs. The findings underscore the need for standardized protocols, targeted training for healthcare professionals, and international collaboration to improve patient outcomes in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Red blood cell distribution width as a predictor of JAK2 mutation in erythrocytosis.
articles.abstract: Erythrocytosis is a common clinical finding, and accurate diagnosis of polycythemia vera (PV) requires JAK2 mutation testing. However, complete blood count (CBC) parameters may help estimate JAK2 mutation positivity during initial evaluation. We conducted a multicenter, retrospective study comprising three cohorts of patients with erythrocytosis: a training cohort (n = 212), validation cohort (n = 27), and test cohort (n = 160). Multivariable logistic regression and decision tree analysis were performed to identify predictive parameters and develop prediction models. Three independent predictors of JAK2 mutation status were identified: red cell distribution width coefficient of variation (RDW-CV, OR: 3.07), neutrophil ratio (OR: 1.27), and platelet count (OR: 1.04). Two prediction patterns were developed in the training cohort: a low-probability pattern for JAK2 mutation-positivity (platelet count < 424 × 109/L and RDW-CV < 14.8%) and a high-probability pattern for JAK2 mutation-positivity (platelet count ≥ 235 × 109/L and RDW-CV ≥ 15.5%). The validation and test cohorts demonstrated consistent performance. We developed a simple, widely available CBC-based prediction model that showed higher discriminatory performance than the conventional erythropoietin-based approach and may support the diagnostic evaluation of erythrocytosis.

articles.title: Psoriasis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Risk Estimation and Shared Care.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a systemic immune-mediated inflammatory disease associated with increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, including coronary artery disease. This review summarizes epidemiological and genetic evidence linking psoriasis, severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis to coronary outcomes, and distinguishes disease phenotype, current severity, disease duration and cumulative inflammatory burden as related but separate contributors to cardiovascular risk. We outline shared immune, lipid and metabolic pathways that promote endothelial dysfunction, plaque inflammation and atherothrombosis, and review vascular imaging approaches that characterize non-calcified plaque, total plaque burden, adverse plaque features, pericoronary inflammation and coronary microvascular dysfunction. Evidence relevant to cardiovascular risk modification is reviewed, including systemic psoriasis therapies, lipid lowering, incretin-based and other cardiometabolic agents, and anti-inflammatory strategies established in coronary disease. We propose a graded risk framework in which phenotype, severity, duration, adequacy of disease control, conventional cardiovascular risk factors and evidence of subclinical atherosclerosis inform interpretation of calculated risk. We also set out an operational shared-care pathway that assigns responsibility for screening, risk assessment, preventive therapy, monitoring and referral across dermatology, primary care and cardiology. Practical statements are labeled according to the strength of supporting evidence. Until definitive cardiovascular outcome trials in psoriatic disease are available, aggressive management of conventional risk factors alongside optimal inflammatory control remains the most defensible approach to reducing cardiovascular burden.

articles.title: Clarifying Analysis Methods in a TrinetX Study of GLP-1RA Use in Patients with Opioid Use Disorder and Diabetes.
Resident and Faculty Perspectives on Team-Based Learning in Internal Medicine Residency: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Team-based learning (TBL) is an active learning strategy associated with increased engagement and knowledge retention in undergraduate medical education. However, adoption in graduate medical education (GME) has been limited. It is unclear why this is the case.

OBJECTIVE: To explore resident and faculty perspectives on barriers to and strategies for implementing TBL in an internal medicine residency program.

DESIGN: Qualitative study nested within a prospective mixed-methods educational intervention.

PARTICIPANTS: Internal medicine residents and faculty at a mid-sized academic medical center in the Pacific Northwest.

INTERVENTIONS: Nine infectious disease-focused TBL sessions delivered during noon conferences over 5 weeks. Faculty received structured training and coaching in TBL session design and facilitation.

APPROACH: Following completion of the intervention, residents and faculty participated in semi-structured focus groups. Audio-recorded sessions were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis with constant comparison by two independent coders. Discrepancies were resolved through consensus.

KEY RESULTS: Analyses identified three primary domains: perceived learning, group dynamics, and time investment/restrictions. Residents described greater engagement, motivation, and perceived knowledge retention with TBL compared to traditional lectures, attributing these benefits to concise, clinically relevant pre-work and active, case-based discussions. Small-group formats promoted psychological safety and enriched discussion among learners at different training levels. Faculty observed increased resident engagement but described challenges related to time-intensive preparation, uncertainty about learning outcomes, and adapting to a new teaching modality. Structural barriers included inconsistent attendance due to clinical responsibilities, resistance to peer evaluation, and logistical constraints such as room layout and limited protected time.

CONCLUSIONS: Residents and faculty identified both benefits and challenges to implementing TBL in GME. Successful integration may require deliberate resident orientation, faculty development and coaching, and practical adaptations to session design, scheduling, and learning environments. These findings can inform residency programs seeking to incorporate active learning strategies into existing curricula.

articles.title: Financial and Opportunity Costs of In-person Interviews for Complex General Surgical Oncology Fellowship.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The application process for a complex general surgical oncology (CGSO) fellowship relies heavily on in-person interviews. Applicants incur significant financial and logistical costs, which have not been formally assessed.

METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of the 2025 CGSO applicant cohort was conducted. The survey tool assessed preferences regarding in-person versus virtual interviews as well as overall financial and opportunity costs incurred via the in-person interview process. Financial toxicity was evaluated using a modified 9-item FACIT-COST tool. Participants were recruited via direct outreach. Survey results were analyzed using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Of 87 subjects contacted, 36 (41.4%) participated in the survey. The applicants applied to a median of 31.5 programs, ultimately attending 13 interviews. The median total cost incurred by the applicants was $7736. Transportation ($3850) and lodging ($2000) represented the largest expenses. The applicants estimated per-interview costs of $850 when travel to a different city was required. More than half of the applicants (55.6%) had to use savings or retirement funds, estimating a mean 21.4% reduction in savings. The median modified FACIT-COST score was 25.7, indicating incurred financial toxicity. The applicants missed a median of 18 clinical days. The majority (88.9%, n = 32) of the participants reported a preference for in-person over virtual interviews.

CONCLUSION: Applicants for a CGSO fellowship personally incur significant financial and logistical costs through the process of interviews. Despite these costs, most applicants prefer in-person over virtual interviews. These findings highlight a need to explore novel strategies to reduce the financial and logistical burden on applicants while maintaining the benefits of in-person interactions.

articles.title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Model to Predict Skip Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skip lymph node metastasis (SLNM) poses major diagnostic challenges for papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and existing prediction models rely merely on clinicopathological data and have limited predictive efficacy. This research constructed an interpretable machine learning prediction model integrating clinicopathological features and peripheral blood immune-inflammatory markers, aiming to realize personalized SLNM risk assessment and guide clinical treatment decision-making for patients with PTC.

METHODS: Retrospective data from 1004 patients with PTC from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang were collected. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression filtered predictive variables, and seven supervised machine learning models were built to predict SLNM. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated via area under the curve (AUC), decision-curve analysis, and multiple auxiliary metrics, and the optimal algorithm was screened out. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis interpreted feature contribution.

RESULTS: Among all 1004 enrolled subjects, 193 (19.2%) presented with SLNM. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis retained two immune-inflammatory markers-platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and systemic immune-inflammation index-alongside five ultrasound-based clinical predictors: age, maximum tumor diameter, lesion site, multifocality and extrathyroidal extension. Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) outperformed all other tested algorithms, with an AUC of 0.970 in the training cohort and an AUC of 0.897 in the internal validation cohort. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis further assigned quantified importance weights to each predictor variable.

CONCLUSIONS: This study first integrated systemic immune-inflammatory biomarkers and clinicopathological indicators into an interpretable machine learning system then developed an open-access online prediction calculator. The model significantly improves SLNM predictive accuracy, providing quantitative evidence for individualized risk stratification and therapeutic management of PTC.

articles.title: Maribavir versus investigator-assigned therapy for treatment of refractory CMV infection: subgroup analysis of hematopoietic cell transplant recipients from a phase 3 study.
articles.abstract: Refractory cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection management is a therapeutic challenge following hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT). In the phase 3, randomized, open-label, multicenter, SOLSTICE trial (NCT02931539), transplant recipients with refractory/resistant CMV infection were randomized 2:1 to maribavir 400 mg twice daily or investigator-assigned treatment (IAT; valganciclovir/ganciclovir, foscarnet, or cidofovir) for 8 weeks. Post hoc subanalyses involving the HCT subgroup assessed the association of patient baseline characteristics with viremia clearance at Week 8 (primary endpoint) and maintenance of viremia clearance/symptom control (key secondary endpoint). These primary and key secondary endpoints were achieved in significantly more patients in the maribavir (n = 93) vs IAT (n = 48) arms (55.9% vs 20.8%; adjusted difference: 36.1%; 95% CI: 20.9-51.4; P < 0.001, and 26.9% vs 8.3%; adjusted difference: 19.8%; 95% CI: 8.1-31.4; P < 0.001, respectively). The significantly higher proportion of maribavir-treated patients (vs IAT) achieving viremia clearance was retained irrespective of preparative conditioning regimen used, baseline graft-versus-host disease or systemic corticosteroid use, or CMV mutations. Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia was numerically less frequently reported with maribavir vs ganciclovir/valganciclovir (12.2% vs 33.3%, respectively). These results highlight the benefits of maribavir vs IAT in HCT recipients with refractory CMV infection/disease, including improved CMV viremia clearance/symptom control and numerically lower neutropenia.

articles.title: Author Correction: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
Comparison of mold-based, handmade, and prefabricated articulating cement spacers in two-stage revision total knee arthroplasty for periprosthetic joint infection: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is a devastating complication most commonly managed with two-stage revision. Articulating antibiotic-loaded cement spacers may be prepared using handmade, mold-based, or prefabricated techniques; however, high-quality comparative evidence is limited, and the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Musculoskeletal Infection identified this as a knowledge gap. We aimed to compare a mold-based technique that uses a dedicated reusable sterile mold prepared from previously explanted components, used solely as a back-table molding tool and never reimplanted into the joint, with conventional handmade and commercially available prefabricated spacers.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 75 patients undergoing two-stage revision TKA for PJI (June 2019-August 2025), grouped by spacer technique: mold-based (n = 18), handmade (n = 36), and prefabricated (n = 21). PJI was diagnosed per the 2018 ICM criteria. The primary outcome was final range of motion (ROM). Secondary outcomes were KSS, WOMAC, Oxford Knee Score, infection eradication, complications, and per-patient cost. Groups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis and chi-square/Fisher tests with Bonferroni post-hoc correction.

RESULTS: Baseline demographics and infection markers were comparable across groups.
