Final ROM tended to be highest in the mold group (105.8° ± 13.6°) compared with the handmade (99.3° ± 11.7°) and prefabricated (103.1° ± 11.1°) groups, without reaching statistical significance (p = 0.227). No significant differences were observed in KSS-Knee, KSS-Function, WOMAC, or Oxford scores. Infection eradication rates were 94.4% (mold), 94.4% (handmade), and 90.5% (prefabricated) (p = 0.826). Spacer-related complications occurred in 11.1%, 30.6%, and 14.3%, respectively (p = 0.168), with all spacer fractures (n = 4) confined to the handmade group. In our institutional setting, the direct material cost of the mold-based construct was approximately 46% of the prefabricated spacer construct cost (approximately 54% lower).

CONCLUSIONS: The mold-based technique using explanted components yielded clinical outcomes that did not differ significantly from those of handmade and prefabricated spacers, with a lower direct material cost than the prefabricated spacer, and may represent a practical lower-cost alternative to prefabricated spacers in resource-limited settings. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III-retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Epigenetic clocks and adverse childhood experiences: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Epigenetic clocks predict biological age from DNA methylation patterns, providing insight into cellular aging. Different clocks capture distinct aspects of aging, and their relevance to research areas may vary - including early-life stress (ELS) and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). This meta-analysis evaluates which clocks are most associated to biological consequences of ELS and ACEs. A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251047805) to identify studies assessing associations between ACEs or ELS and epigenetic age acceleration (EAA). Eligible human studies used validated ACE or ELS measures and reported DNA methylation-based age from peripheral tissues. Data were extracted and pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models to generate beta coefficients and 95% confidence intervals (RevMan 5.4). Seventeen studies (n = 10,940) met inclusion criteria and used 8 epigenetic clocks: Horvath's, Hannum's, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, DunedinPoAm, Skin & Blood and PedBE. Amongst these, GrimAge and DunedinPACE demonstrated the strongest, most consistent associations with total ACE counts and subdomains including abuse (total, physical, sexual), neglect (total), and household dysfunction (total, socioeconomic impact). Only DunedinPACE demonstrated robust associations across strata, with significant age differences and no sex effects. This meta-analysis highlights variability in how clocks capture the biological imprint of early adversity. Later-generation clocks like GrimAge and DunedinPACE, integrating physiological and mortality-related methylation signatures, show the most consistent with cumulative effects of ELS and ACEs. These findings emphasise the need for careful clock selection and rigorous study design in stress-biology research, with implications for identifying individuals at risk for EAA and stress-related disorders.

articles.title: Molecular PET imaging of cellular senescence: from current tracers to emerging biomarker-driven strategies.
articles.abstract: Cellular senescence is a dynamic and multifaceted biological process that contributes to aging and a wide spectrum of age-related diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders. Despite increasing recognition of its pathological significance, the ability to quantify senescence noninvasively in vivo remains a major limitation, particularly for longitudinal studies and therapeutic evaluation. Positron emission tomography (PET) offers a powerful platform to address this gap by enabling quantitative imaging of molecular processes in living systems. Recent advances have led to the development of PET radiotracers targeting senescence-associated features, including lysosomal β-galactosidase activity, cell-surface markers (uPAR), and intracellular accumulation products (lipofuscin). These first-generation approaches have established proof-of-concept for imaging senescence biology; however, they primarily reflect downstream hallmarks and have been largely evaluated in non-central nervous system (CNS) models, while their ability to quantify senescent-cell burden in naturally aged tissues and the CNS remains insufficiently established. Emerging evidence motivates the study of biomarker-driven and pathway-oriented imaging strategies that may provide complementary information about senescence-associated molecular mechanisms without necessarily offering greater biological specificity. Advances in senescence biology, including curated gene sets and insights from senotherapeutic interventions, provide a framework for identifying imaging targets based on mechanistic relevance, disease association, and ligandability. Target classes spanning nuclear architecture, epigenetic regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and DNA damage signaling represent promising avenues for next-generation tracer development. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current PET tracers for cellular senescence, discusses challenges associated with CNS translation, and proposes a biomarker-driven framework for next-generation tracer development. We further introduce a comparative target-assessment framework and a stepwise validation roadmap addressing biological specificity, quantitative clinical qualification, and multimodal biomarker integration. Together, these considerations establish a framework for developing and interpreting PET biomarkers for mechanistic studies and evaluation of senescence-targeted interventions.

articles.title: Comment on: infection rates in primary inflatable penile prosthesis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of antibiotic-coated versus non-coated devices.
Markers of Blood-Brain Barrier Integrity and Neurodegeneration Across Alzheimer's and Non-Alzheimer Neurodegenerative Diseases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dysfunction of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is increasingly recognized as an early feature of Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, the relationship between BBB integrity, glial activation, and neuronal injury is not fully understood, particularly in non-Alzheimer's disorders such as frontotemporal dementia (NADD/FTD). This exploratory study investigated the relationships between BBB integrity, astroglial activation, and neuronal and tau-related injury in AD, NDD/FTD, and cognitively healthy controls (HCs).

METHODS: Of the 105 individuals who were screened, the final analytic cohort, which was characterized using PET and CSF, comprised 63 participants. These included 34 individuals with AD, 16 HCs, and 13 participants with NADD/FTD. BBB integrity was assessed using platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ), CSF fibrinogen, and the CSF/serum albumin ratio (QAlb). Plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) were assessed as markers of astroglial activation, axonal injury and tau pathology, respectively. Exploratory statistical analyses were adjusted for age and sex.

RESULTS: Markers of BBB integrity did not significantly distinguish between the diagnostic groups (all p > 0.05). Significant associations were observed across the full cohort between CSF fibrinogen and CSF total tau and QAlb, and between plasma GFAP, NfL, and pTau217 (r = 0.65-0.70, all p < 0.001 for GFAP). In exploratory mediation analyses, neither tested model showed a significant indirect effect. No comparable amyloid-related mediation effects were observed. Exploratory mediation analyses involving other markers of BBB dysfunction likewise showed no significant indirect effects.

CONCLUSION: BBB-related markers did not demonstrate consistent associations with astroglial activation and neuronal injury across diagnostic groups within this cross-sectional cohort. While these findings do not exclude a role for BBB alterations in neurodegenerative processes, they do suggest that their biological significance and potential relevance across disease stages remain unclear. Further research is required in the form of larger longitudinal studies to investigate these relationships.

articles.title: Assessing patient acceptability of type 2 diabetes risk-assessment in UK high-street dental practices: a reflexive thematic analysis of 15 interviews.
articles.abstract: Aims This qualitative study explored patient perception and experience of type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk-assessment delivered within National Health Service dental practices.Methods Fifteen adults who had completed a T2D risk-assessment participated in semi-structured interviews, analysed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis.Results Participants supported the concept of opportunistic diabetes risk-assessment in dental settings, describing the process as convenient, acceptable and reassuring, particularly because it offered a single-visit workflow and immediate results. Trust in familiar dental staff contributed to perceptions of legitimacy and comfort. Many participants valued receiving a tangible HbA1c number and expressed a desire for a plain-language printed explanation outlining the meaning of the result and recommended next steps. Preferences for follow-up strongly favoured a dual-communication approach: automatic general practitioner (GP) notification complemented by a patient-held copy to ensure understanding and encourage action. Participants agreed that strong integration with GP pathways was essential. Some also highlighted equity considerations, including the deterrent effect of patient fees and the need to ensure that screening does not compromise access to routine dental care.Conclusions Overall, dental practices were seen as a credible, convenient and potentially impactful setting for early identification of T2D risk, provided pathways remain patient-centred, well-explained and integrated with broader primary care systems.

articles.title: Periodontitis management and surgical site infection risk in mandibular fracture treatment.
articles.abstract: Aims To assess whether peri-operative periodontal treatment and oral health management in patients presenting with fractured mandibles is associated with a reduction in surgical site infections (SSIs).Methods This was a before-after service evaluation of all patients presenting to the Royal London Hospital Major Trauma Centre with fractured mandibles between January 2021 and January 2023, following the integration of a specialist periodontist and Doctorate of Clinical Dentistry hygiene and therapy students into the outpatient trauma multidisciplinary team. Data were gathered from electronic patient records and radiographic assessments, and compared with a previously published cohort from the same unit (Janaphan et al., 2022; n = 305, 2017-2020). Chi-square analysis and logistic regression with odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals were used.Results A total of 128 patients met the inclusion criteria. SSI occurred in 16 patients (12.5%) in the intervention cohort, compared with 70/305 (22.95%) in the historical cohort (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.27-0.87; p = 0.014). Stage III and Stage IV periodontal disease was present in 24.2% of the intervention cohort, a higher proportion than in the historical cohort (17.0%). No statistically significant association between severe periodontitis and SSI was identified within the intervention cohort.Conclusions In this before-after service evaluation, the introduction of peri-operative periodontal care and oral health management was associated with a lower SSI rate compared with a historical cohort from the same unit. Causation cannot be inferred from this design. These findings are hypothesis-generating and provide a rationale for a prospective controlled study with multivariable adjustment and standardised intervention documentation.

articles.title: A Differentially Methylated Region in the TNXB Gene is Associated with Relapse Activity in Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: The mechanisms driving heterogeneity in disease activity in relapsing-remitting Multiple Sclerosis (RRMS) are incompletely understood. Changes in DNA methylation, at the intersection between genetic background and environment, are crucial for MS pathogenesis, but their role in disease activity is incompletely understood. We herein investigated DNA methylation signatures of relapse in peripheral immune cells of RRMS patients. We profiled the peripheral immune methylome of 236 untreated RRMS patients from two centres using Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC BeadChips. Differential methylation analysis compared patients who relapsed (as per McDonald criteria) in the year preceding sampling (n = 160), versus patients who did not (n = 76). Regression models and causal inference testing (CIT) were used to elucidate causality between DNA methylation, genetic variation, and disease activity. One differentially methylated region (DMR), comprising 5 CpG sites, was hypomethylated in relapsed patients, and mapped within an enhancer of TNXB in the HLA class III region. We found methylation levels in this region to be extensively modulated by proximal genetic variation, particularly by variants known to influence MS risk in a large-scale GWAS. Through CIT, we observed that for 2 Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) methylation levels in the TNXB DMR acted as mediator of the genetic impact on disease activity. Furthermore, we found a correlation between methylation levels within the DMR, SNPs and TNXB gene expression in the immune cells from MS patients. DNA methylation within TNXB influences gene expression and may mediate relapse activity in RRMS. These findings highlight HLA class III regulatory mechanisms as key contributors to relapse biology.

articles.title: Prioritizing the next decade of research in bat infectious disease (batID).
articles.abstract: Bats are widely studied as asymptomatic hosts of viruses that cause high case fatality rates in humans. Though prior research into bat infections has been traditionally virus-focused, there is growing interest to more holistically understand bat-microbe relationships. In July 2025 the fourth International Symposium on the Infectious Diseases of Bats ('BatID 2025') convened, synthesizing the current state of bat-microbe research from within-host to population-level processes. Here, we outline five questions that emerged from this meeting as priority future directions. We share this review with the aim of stimulating future research, emphasizing the need for data sharing and interdisciplinary collaboration.

articles.title: In vivo evaluation of hepatotoxicity following 35-day repeated oral exposure to perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) in male Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) is a persistent contaminant that bioaccumulates through the food chain, posing severe human health risks including endocrine disruption and systemic metabolic disorders. However, the specific molecular thresholds and mechanisms underlying its 35-day repeated-dose hepatotoxicity remain poorly defined. To mimic human exposure and reflect conditions potentially associated with long-term PFNA bioaccumulation, male Wistar rats were exposed to PFNA via drinking water at doses of 0, 0.05, 0.5, and 2 mg/kg body weight/day for 35 days. Post-exposure analyses included blood biochemical and endocrine parameters, liver histopathology, hepatic lipid accumulation and quantification of oxidative stress markers, xenobiotic metabolism, activities of antioxidant defense enzymes, mitochondrial complexes I/II activity, and key gene expression related to antioxidant defenses, CYP450s and lipogenesis. PFNA induced progressive, dose-dependent liver damage, macrovesicular toxicant-associated fatty liver disease (TAFLD), and elevated oxidative stress. Xenobiotic detoxification was impaired, evidenced by reduced 7-ethoxycoumarin O-deethylase activity and CYP2C11 downregulation. Notably, the liver displayed a clear dose-dependent bioenergetic threshold: low and intermediate doses (0.05 and 0.5 mg/kg/day) activated adaptive defenses, increasing mitochondrial Complex II activity to sustain energy demands. Conversely, the 2 mg/kg/day dose triggered a severe bioenergetic collapse and metabolic exhaustion, overwhelming late compensatory responses including PPARα activation, lipogenic FAS suppression, and peak catalase activity. In conclusion, 35-day repeated oral PFNA exposure induces a dose-dependent shift from adaptive energetic defense to comprehensive hepatic metabolic collapse, providing critical insights into the toxicological risk assessment of bioaccumulative perfluoroalkyl substances.

articles.title: Clinical, microbiological, and outcome profiles of liver abscess: a multicentre study in Bogotá, Colombia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver abscess remains associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, while data from Latin America are limited. This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics, microbiological findings, antimicrobial resistance patterns, management strategies, and outcomes of liver abscess in tertiary-care centres in Colombia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective multicentre observational study including adult patients with confirmed pyogenic or amoebic liver abscess treated at four tertiary hospitals in Bogotá, Colombia, between 2015 and 2024. Demographic, clinical, imaging, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data were extracted from electronic medical records using a standardised REDCap form.

RESULTS: 253 patients were included (median age 56 years; 64.4% male). Multiple abscesses were identified in 29.3% of patients (median 1 abscess per patient, IQR 1-2), with a median maximum diameter of 6 cm (interquartile range [IQR] 4-9). Abscess cultures were positive in 69.0% and blood cultures in 42.4%. Escherichia coli (34.5%) and Klebsiella spp. (28.3%) were the most frequently isolated pathogens. Extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL) production, AmpC expression, and carbapenem resistance were detected, particularly among E. coli and Klebsiella spp. Percutaneous drainage was performed in 75.9% of patients. The median hospital stay was 12 days (IQR 7-20), 17.8% required intensive care unit admission, and in-hospital mortality was 5.3%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicentre cohort of liver abscess patients from Colombia, pyogenic abscesses predominated, with a substantial burden of antimicrobial resistance among Enterobacterales. These findings emphasise the importance of local microbiological surveillance to guide empirical therapy and reinforce antimicrobial stewardship and early drainage strategies in middle-income settings.

articles.title: Hydrated Proton-Lattice Synergy-Mediated Super-Nernstian pH Sensing in H0.95MoO3 for Translational Biofluid Monitoring and In Vivo Pathological Tracking.
articles.abstract: Maintaining pH homeostasis in biofluids is critical for normal physiological function, with even minor deviations (±0.1-0.2 pH units) serving as early biomarkers for various pathologies such as diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and wound infection. Current clinical pH monitoring relies heavily on ex vivo sampling and benchtop analysis, suffering from sampling randomness, analytical delays, and the inability to capture dynamic physiological pH fluctuations. Here, we develop a flexible biosensing system based on metalloid H0.95MoO3 nanobelts fabricated by modulating selective hydronium intercalation. This system resolves the long-standing trade-off between full physiological pH range coverage (1-11) and high precision in narrow sub-ranges, achieving super-Nernstian sensitivity (66.69 mV/pH), rapid response (3-4 s), and robust anti-interference capability against biological interferents. Moreover, it also features tunable lifespan via tailored encapsulation to adapt to diverse clinical scenarios and inherent biocompatibility for seamless in vitro/in vivo deployment. Multi-scale characterizations and theoretical analyses clarify the underlying proton-electron coupled sensing mechanism, supported by a surface site-binding model explaining the super-Nernstian sensitivity. Integrated with wireless Bluetooth transmission, the system enables in situ real-time and high-precision monitoring of saliva, sweat, diabetic wound exudate, gastric fluid, and interstitial fluid pH, providing a versatile tool for advancing precision medicine and smart diagnostics.

articles.title: Supramolecular Assemblies of Dendritic Polycarboxylates With Distinct Morphologies for Antiviral Inhibition.
articles.abstract: Viruses remain a global health threat, highlighting the need for broad-spectrum antivirals as shown during the COVID-19 pandemic. Self-assembled amphiphilic nanomaterials represent an important inhibitor class, due to their ability to inhibit viruses in a non-virus-specific manner. Herein, we functionalized a polymeric backbone, hyperbranched polyglycerol (hPG) and a perfect dendritic polyglycerol (dPG) based on a 1,3,5-tris(bromomethyl)benzene (TBMB) core with mercaptoundecanoic acid (MUA) into two different amphiphilic systems and evaluated both materials with respect to their morphology and virus-inhibiting properties against Herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) and influenza A virus (IAV). Structural analysis reveals distinct self-assembled morphologies, with hPG-MUA and dPG-MUA forming flexible sheet-like structures and nanospheres, respectively. HSV-1 plaque reduction and IAV pre-infection inhibition assays reveal half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50 values) of 2 µg/mL for each assay for hPG-MUA, while dPG-MUA exhibits negligible or no inhibition. These differences in inhibition highlight the critical role of the morphological structure of the self-assembled supramolecular structures. When specific virus-ligand interactions are absent, virus inhibition seems to be strongly influenced by the self-assembled structure and electrostatic interactions.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Alcohol Use in Cirrhosis: A Prospective PEth-Based U.S. Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Alcohol use is a modifiable driver of adverse outcomes in cirrhosis, yet its ascertainment across etiologies remains incompletely defined. We evaluated alcohol use in a prospectively recruited well-characterized cohort of adults with cirrhosis using structured self-report instruments and phosphatidylethanol (PEth).

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled adults with cirrhosis residing in Southern California. Participants underwent standardized research visits, laboratory testing, vibration-controlled transient elastography, magnetic resonance imaging and elastography, validated alcohol-use questionnaires, and PEth. Alcohol use was defined as any self-reported alcohol intake in the last year or a positive PEth. The primary outcome of this study was the prevalence of overt and occult use in participants with cirrhosis.

RESULTS: Among 275 participants with cirrhosis (56.8% women, median age of 60 [52-68] years), the most common etiologies were MASLD (38.6%), ALD (27.6%), hepatitis C (11.6%), and MetALD (1.8%). The prevalence of alcohol use based on self-report was 63.9%, while 13.8% had a PEth ≥ 10 ng/mL. Alcohol intake was frequent not only in MetALD (100%) and ALD (90.8%), but also in hepatitis C (62.5%), cryptogenic disease (54.2%), and MASLD (50%). The prevalence of occult alcohol intake identified by PEth reached 11% in ALD, 6% in hepatitis C, 5% in MASLD, and 7% in other causes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this well-characterized cohort, alcohol use was common across etiologies of cirrhosis. These findings support PEth-based monitoring in cirrhosis, particularly when alcohol exposure may affect diagnosis, counselling, transplant candidacy, or trial eligibility.

articles.title: Oxygen Facilitated Aqueous Photomediated-RAFT Polymerization: Just Add Salt.
articles.abstract: In this work, we report the first example of a novel oxygen-facilitated photoinitiation system by employing a combination of riboflavin 5'-monophosphate sodium salt (Vitamin B2) and disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na2HPO4) for conducting reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization. Under blue LED irradiation (λ = 451 nm) and an oxygen atmosphere, the bioactive form of riboflavin, flavin mononucleotide, in the presence of first Na2HPO4 and then extended to other salts, was able to initiate the controlled RAFT polymerization of N,N-dimethylacrylamide. The resulting polymer was found to also possess excellent chain fidelity after chain extension via characterization by gel permeation chromatography. These photopolymerizations were found to only proceed to high conversion in the presence of both oxygen and salt. Exploiting the oxygen-facilitated and aqueous nature of our system, we could achieve microliter-scale polymerization in mammalian cell culture medium in the presence of live cells.

articles.title: Hepatic manifestations of Pica syndrome: multicenter study.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract: Pica syndrome, characterized by the persistent ingestion of non-nutritive substances, may be associated with systemic complications, including hepatic involvement. Therefore, we aimed to investigate its hepatic manifestations in a Moroccan cohort. To this end, a prospective multicenter study was conducted from 2021 to 2024 across four healthcare centers, and clinical, biological, imaging, and liver elastography data were collected. Liver fibrosis was assessed using FibroScan® and classified according to METAVIR-equivalent stages. Among 12,520 individuals who consulted, 174 who met the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fourth Edition criteria for Pica syndrome were identified, with a prevalence of 13‰. The median patient age was 46 (range: 37-59) years, with a slight male predominance (sex ratio = 1.18). The most commonly ingested substances were clay (56%), coal (32%), paper (12%), and sand (8%). The main symptoms were abdominal discomfort (68%) and asthenia (24%). Sideropenic anemia was present in 64% of patients, and ferritin levels were low in 72%. The median liver stiffness was 5.7 (range: 4.3-8.1) kPa. Fibrosis staging showed stages F0-F1, F2, F3, and F4 in 68.4%, 14.4%, 1.7%, and 15.5% of the patients. Chronic hepatitis B virus infection was the most frequent associated etiology (47.7%). Fibrosis severity was significantly associated with liver disease etiology (p < 0.001) but not with sex or anthropometric parameters. Multivariable analysis showed that hepatitis B virus infection was independently associated with lower odds of advanced fibrosis (odds ratio = 0.16, 95% confidence interval: 0.04-0.61; p = 0.008). Pica syndrome showed heterogeneous hepatic manifestations, while liver fibrosis severity appeared to be mainly related to the underlying liver disease etiology.

articles.title: Predictive performance of the CRP-to-albumin ratio compared with MELD 3.0 and FIB-4 for long-term mortality in HCV-related cirrhosis: a 13-year follow-up study.
articles.journal: Arab journal of gastroenterology : the official publication of the Pan-Arab Association of Gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: We compared the 13-year prognostic value of the C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) with MELD 3.0 and FIB-4 in hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related cirrhosis.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 86 patients followed between 2012 and 2025. Baseline scores were assessed using ROC analysis, Kaplan-Meier methods, multivariable logistic regression for mortality status, and Cox regression for time to death.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 64 patients (74.4%) died. Non-survivors had higher CAR (4.79 vs 1.21; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (13.00 vs 9.50; p = 0.031), and FIB-4 (6.70 vs 5.00; p = 0.049). CAR had the highest numerical AUROC (0.765; 95% CI 0.66-0.85) compared with MELD 3.0 (0.654) and FIB-4 (0.641), without significant differences on DeLong testing (p = 0.18 and p = 0.14). At the CAR cutoff of 6.77, specificity and positive predictive value were 100%, but sensitivity was 40.6% and negative predictive value was 36.7%. CAR was associated with mortality status in multivariable logistic regression (OR 1.21; 95% CI 1.08-1.36; p = 0.001), but not independently with time to death in adjusted Cox regression. MELD 3.0 (HR 1.12; 95% CI 1.05-1.19; p < 0.001) and age were associated with the hazard of death. Patients subsequently receiving antiviral therapy had lower baseline CAR than untreated patients (2.14 vs 6.56; p = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: CAR may complement established prognostic scores, but its discrimination was not statistically superior. The CAR cutoff requires external validation given its low sensitivity and negative predictive value. The association between baseline CAR and subsequent antiviral treatment status should not be interpreted as a treatment effect.

articles.title: Evaluation of Publicly Available Online Information on Triggers of Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIM: Many individuals seek online information about myocardial infarction (MI) for convenience and accessibility. However, the quality and completeness of information on MI acute risk factors, also known as triggers, remain unclear, limiting its value as a patient education resource. This study aimed to assess the content and presentation of publicly available websites addressing MI triggers.

METHOD: A systematic web-based search using Google identified publicly accessible websites on MI triggers. The first 10 relevant results for each search term were assessed using the Quality Component Scoring System and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-P). Website content was systematically analysed for the presence and quality of information.

RESULTS: Seventeen (17) websites were included. Most focussed on chronic risk factors, while triggers were largely under-represented. Overall website quality was low, with deficiencies in authorship transparency, citation practices, and evidence-based guidance. The PEMAT-P evaluation showed that understandability was generally adequate and clear, whereas actionability was consistently low, with limited actionable guidance. Only two websites explicitly used the term 'trigger' and addressed MI triggers, identifying five known triggers: physical exertion (n=2), anger (n=2), respiratory infection (n=1), meteorological stress (n=1), and overeating (n=1). Most websites (n=16, 94%) did not quantify MI risk following trigger exposure, and none addressed hazard periods or temporal patterns. Prevention strategies focussed mainly on chronic risk factors, with little guidance specifically targeting MI triggers.

CONCLUSIONS: Online information on MI triggers remains sparse and of limited quality, providing few actionable resources for patient education. Trigger-related information is rarely identifiable unless users search explicitly for a specific trigger, which limits its visibility in routine patient education resources and may reduce public recognition of acute risks, delaying timely preventive action. Improving the clarity and actionability of online resources can empower patients and facilitate targeted interventions to reduce MI risk and improve cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: The Australian Cardiovascular Risk Calculator and Atherosclerotic Vascular Disease Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Australian cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk calculator (AUS-CVD-RC) was developed to improve CVD risk prediction in Australians, and launched in 2023. We tested the validity of the AUS-CVD-RC with long-term atherosclerotic vascular disease (ASVD) risk in a cohort of community-dwelling older women.

METHODS: The study included 905 older women (70 to <80 years of age) from Western Australia recruited in 1998 (baseline). Women with chronic kidney disease and prevalent ASVD were excluded. AUS-CVD-RC were calculated at baseline and grouped into low (<5%), moderate (5% to <10%) and high (≥10%) risk. Atherosclerotic events, comprising hospitalisations and/or deaths, over 5, 10, and 14.5 years were obtained from linked health records.

RESULTS: Over 5 years, 9.3% of women experienced an ASVD-related event, increasing to 21.1% and 37.0% at 10 years and 14.5 years, respectively. Compared to women with low risk, those with moderate (hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.32-6.32) and high risk (HR 6.34 95% CI 2.64-15.23) had greater hazards for an ASVD-related event over 5 years. Similar associations were observed at 10 and 14.5-years. Unadjusted event rates (%) over 5 years by AUS-CVD-RC risk groups were: low 7.4 (95% CI 3.0-15.3); moderate 20.3 (95% CI 15.5-26.2); and high risk 42.7 (95% CI 25.3-67.4). Despite this, the predictive utility for AUS-CVD-RC and ASVD events over these three different follow-up periods had an area under the curve of <0.70.

CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrate the AUS-CVD-RC identifies community-dwelling older women with a higher risk of ASVD, a population where risk prediction remains challenging. Future research should explore if the inclusion of women-specific factors may improve prognostic performance.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Hypertonic saline and high-dose furosemide in very elderly patients hospitalized for acute heart failure: A real-world cohort study" [European Journal of Internal Medicine (2026) 107201].
Hypothalamic orexin input to the medial amygdala promotes arousal from anaesthesia and modulates exploratory behaviour.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emergence from general anaesthesia is often accompanied by agitation, suggesting that recovery of consciousness can engage neural circuits that regulate arousal and behavioural responsiveness. The amygdala influences social, defensive, and exploratory behaviours, but whether orexinergic input to the amygdala regulates anaesthetic state transitions together with behavioural responses remains unclear.

METHODS: In male orexin-Cre mice, we combined viral tracing, electrophysiology, and RNAscope to define a lateral hypothalamic orexin (LHAOx) projection to the medial amygdala (MeA). Optogenetics, electroencephalography, electromyography, and fibre photometry were used to test how this circuit regulates arousal from isoflurane anaesthesia, as well as exploratory and place-preference behaviour.

RESULTS: LHAOx neurones densely innervated the MeA, where orexin receptor 2 was more abundant than orexin receptor 1 (P<0.0001). Optogenetic activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection promoted arousal from 0.75 vol% isoflurane sedation (P<0.0001), delayed induction by 3 vol% isoflurane as measured by loss of the righting reflex (P=0.0074), and accelerated emergence from 2 vol% isoflurane as measured by return of the righting reflex (P=0.0098). In behavioural assays, activation of this projection suppressed open-field exploration, increased real-time place preference, and did not produce conditioned place preference. Activation of the LHAOx→MeA projection was accompanied by increased activity in MeA vesicular GABA transporter (MeAvGAT)-expressing neurones. Direct activation of MeAvGAT neurones replicated the arousal-promoting and reduced exploratory behaviour, whereas silencing their synaptic output eliminated the induction-delaying effect and shifted the real-time preference.

CONCLUSIONS: The LHAOx projection to the MeA promotes anaesthetic arousal and acutely suppresses exploratory behaviour in male mice, with MeAvGAT serving as a key downstream target.

articles.title: Improving Prenatal Coarctation of the Aorta Screening With Dynamic Routing Knowledge Distillation and Capsule Networks: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Coarctation of the aorta (CoA) is one of the most common congenital heart defects, yet prenatal diagnosis remains difficult because of its variable and subtle anatomical presentation. To address this challenge, we developed KDCoANet, a dynamic routing knowledge distillation framework designed to identify fetuses with suspected CoA from fetal echocardiography.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective analysis of 576 video segments from 377 pregnancies. In the first stage, a high-capacity teacher model learned rich feature representations. In the second stage, we compared three training strategies for lightweight student models (FastViT, ShuffleNet, and SqueezeNet): a general group, traditional knowledge distillation, and a proposed dynamic routing distillation strategy with capsule networks (DR+Caps) to align high-order feature distributions between teacher and student models. Performance was compared with that of the general group using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: KDCoANet achieved an AUC of 0.937 in the validation dataset and 0.888 in the multicenter dataset, with sensitivities of 0.909 and 0.800, specificities of 0.800 and 0.827, and F1 scores of 0.847 and 0.800, respectively. The proposed method also produced statistically significant AUC improvements over both the general group and traditional distillation (p < 0.05). DR+Caps increased specificity and reduced the false-positive rate among prenatally suspected cases, which is clinically important in prenatal CoA screening.

CONCLUSION: KDCoANet improves diagnostic accuracy through dynamic routing distillation and capsule network-based feature alignment. The dynamic routing strategy substantially improves the alignment of high-order feature distributions between teacher and student models, resulting in better performance than traditional distillation methods. Its lightweight design enables rapid deployment in fetal echocardiography, with the potential to improve detection rates and reduce missed diagnoses.

articles.title: Real-Time Prediction of Cardiac Parameters Using Livestream Transthoracic Echocardiography Images: A Feasibility Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to develop a workflow for acquiring and analyzing livestream echocardiography images from a GE HealthCare Vivid E95 system, a real-time artificial intelligence (AI)-based automatic left ventricle segmentation, and cardiac parameter prediction. The system provides automated echocardiography image analysis independent of electrocardiogram signals.

METHODS: A software pipeline was developed to acquire and analyze livestream echocardiography images from the ultrasound system. A UNet neural network model was trained using publicly available datasets (CAMUS, EchoNet-Dynamic) and an in-house dataset (Physical Activity and Fitness in Childhood Cancer Survivors). AI models were trained using these three datasets and three loss functions, with each model evaluated independently on all three test datasets. The model with the highest Dice score on the test datasets was selected and used to process livestream echocardiography images throughout the entire cardiac cycle. The resulting segmentation masks were used to compute the cardiac parameters.

RESULTS: The offline-trained UNet models achieved an average Dice score of 0.9509. The livestream echocardiography image prediction showed average ejection fractions of 48%, 48% and 56%, corresponding to the Simpson's single-plane, area-length and Bullet methods, respectively. In contrast, EchoPAC (the GE HealthCare software tool to compute cardiac parameters) showed an average ejection fraction of 55% in nine volunteers with no known cardiac diseases.

CONCLUSION: This study shows the feasibility of AI-assisted echocardiographic image analysis based on livestream echocardiography. However, the accuracy of the obtained cardiac parameters needs improvement to align with clinical standards.

articles.title: Contemporary Penile Cancer Guidelines Compared: Pathology, Initial Staging, Primary Tumour Management, and Models of Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Penile cancer is a rare malignancy for which high-level evidence is limited, and clinical management relies heavily on guideline recommendations informed by expert consensus. The European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO-EURACAN), the European Association of Urology jointly with the American Society of Clinical Oncology (EAU-ASCO), and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) have each issued disease-specific guidelines based on the available literature and expert opinion. This review aims to compare the most recent iterations of these three guidelines, focusing on similarities and differences in pathological assessment, diagnostic evaluation and staging, management of the primary tumour, patient involvement, and centralisation.

METHODS: A narrative comparative review was conducted of the ESMO-EURACAN Clinical Practice Guideline (2024), the EAU-ASCO guideline (2026), and the NCCN guideline (2026). Recommendations were compared across pathological assessment, diagnostic evaluation and staging, management of the primary tumour, patient involvement, and centralisation.

KEY FINDINGS AND LIMITATIONS: The three guidelines are broadly concordant in pathological assessment, staging, and management of the primary tumour. Nuanced divergences lie at decision thresholds. Where surgical nodal staging is indicated, both European guidelines prefer dynamic sentinel node biopsy, whereas NCCN prefers inguinal lymphadenectomy; for pT1a G2 disease, NCCN recommends surveillance alone. NCCN alone stratifies T1 disease by substage and offers no organ-sparing surgery for T2 disease, unlike ESMO-EURACAN and EAU-ASCO. The most distinct differences lie in patient-centredness and centralisation. EAU-ASCO included the most patient advocates in its development, embeds patient-centred care from the first consultation through follow-up, and alone strongly recommends referring all patients to high-volume expert centres. Limitations include the noninterchangeable evidence grading systems and the scarcity of high-level evidence, with most recommendations resting on retrospective data and expert opinion.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: The three guidelines agree in principle, and their differences largely reflect how expert panels have interpreted a common but limited evidence base. The most distinct differences lie in patient-centredness and centralisation, where EAU-ASCO is the most comprehensive, involving patient advocates in its development and strongly recommending referral to high-volume expert centres. Recognising where a patient's management would change with the guideline applied can support clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Twice-yearly depemokimab demonstrates efficacy in patients with type 2 asthma in Asia: SWIFT-1/-2 subpopulation analyses.
articles.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depemokimab is the first ultra-long-acting biologic, with enhanced interleukin-5 binding affinity, high potency, and an extended half-life, enabling twice-yearly dosing in patients with asthma. Pre-specified analyses of the SWIFT-1/-2 studies assessed efficacy and safety in Asia, including China and Japan subpopulations.

METHODS: Patients with type 2 asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype were randomised 2:1 (depemokimab 100 mg subcutaneously/placebo) every 26 weeks, plus standard of care, over 52 weeks.

PRIMARY ENDPOINT: annualised exacerbation rate. Secondary endpoints: change from baseline to Week 52 in St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) total score, Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 (ACQ-5) score, and pre-bronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). Efficacy and safety were analysed in China/Japan subpopulations and a pooled Asia subgroup.

RESULTS: Overall, 130 patients were enrolled from Asia (58 from China; 59 from Japan). Depemokimab reduced exacerbation rates versus placebo in China (85% [95% CI: 67, 93]) and in Japan (51% [-7, 78]), with greater reductions observed in Asia (65% [40, 79]) than in the global population (54% [41, 64). Mean treatment differences (95% CI) in SGRQ total score, ACQ-5 score, and pre-bronchodilator FEV1 change from baseline at Week 52 (depemokimab vs placebo) in China were -9·57 (-19·49, 0·36), -0·28 (-0·79, 0·28), and 0·007 (-0·156, 0·169), respectively, and in Japan were -8·30 (-17·39, 0·79), -0·28 (-0·80, 0·24), and 0·101 (-0·120, 0·323), respectively. Adverse event reporting in China and Japan was consistent with the global population.

CONCLUSIONS: Depemokimab demonstrates consistent efficacy in reducing exacerbations in patients from Asia with type 2 asthma.

Effect of tailored music therapy on post-procedural systolic blood pressure during invasive coronary angiography: the MUS.E I randomised clinical trial.
Discordant serology and nucleic acid testing results in blood donor screening: Causes, resolution pathways and operational implications-A narrative review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Combined serological and nucleic acid testing (NAT) has narrowed the infectious window period for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), yet the two still disagree on a small fraction of donations. This narrative review aimed to identify the causes of serology-NAT discordance, describe the laboratory approaches used to investigate it, highlight heterogeneous practice and propose evidence-graded resolution pathways.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE literature published between January 2000 and August 2026 was reviewed with US, European, UK, World Health Organization (WHO) and International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT) regulatory and professional guidance. Causes of discordance were classified as temporal marker discordance, biological discordance, analytical false reactivity, analytical false negativity or pre-analytical error and mapped by virus and, for HBV, by reactive marker to investigation and donor-management steps.

RESULTS: Serology-reactive/NAT-nonreactive results usually reflect analytical false reactivity or resolved infection. HBV is the main exception: the meaning depends on whether hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), total antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) or immunoglobulin M (IgM) anti-HBc is reactive, and low-level or intermittent viraemia may escape minipool NAT. NAT-reactive/serology-nonreactive results mostly represent window-period infection, and their interpretation depends on NAT format, discriminatory testing, repeatability and access to confirmatory testing. Donor re-entry rules differ substantially between jurisdictions.

CONCLUSION: We provide general and virus-specific algorithms, with HBV structured by reactive marker, in which each step is labelled as a regulatory requirement, professional guidance, common practice or the authors' proposal. Establishments can adapt these pathways to local regulation and confirmatory capacity to reduce missed infections and unnecessary donor loss.

articles.title: Association of Estimated Insulin Sensitivity With Cardiovascular Disease in Individuals Without Diabetes: Use of Traditional and Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The predictive role of the Estimated Insulin Sensitivity (e-IS) index, serving as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mechanisms remains underexplored in nondiabetic populations. We aimed to evaluate the association of e-IS with CVD incidence and its predictive utility for CVD risk.

METHODS: We analyzed a national prospective cohort of participants without CVD or diabetes at baseline from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study and an external validation cohort from the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University. We used Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines to explore relations. Mediation analyses were performed to explore whether inflammation and kidney disease mediated the relation between e-IS and CVD outcomes. In addition, we used machine learning to develop an e-IS-based CVD prediction model, which underwent external validation.

RESULTS: A total of 1,083 incident CVD cases occurred. Lower e-IS levels were associated with greater CVD risk, with no evidence of a nonlinear association based on restricted cubic splines. Mediation analysis revealed that high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate accounted for 3.06% and 5.47% of the association with CVD, respectively. Integrating e-IS into a basic model significantly improved the concordance statistic for CVD (0.708 vs 0.684) and yielded robust net reclassification (net reclassification improvement, 0.318; P < .001). The machine learning model achieved area under the curve values of 0.738 for CVD, 0.754 for heart disease, and 0.719 for stroke, respectively, with consistent external validation.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that e-IS might be an independent predictor of CVD in nondiabetic populations, mediated in part by high-sensitivity C-reactive protein and estimated glomerular filtration rate. Incorporating e-IS into risk models might enhance prediction accuracy and support personalized risk stratification.Abstract available in: يبرع (Arabic); हिन्दी (Chinese); Francais (French); Deutsch (German); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesian (Indonesian); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese); Español (Spanish).

articles.title: Telehealth Use by Ethnicity and Language Across Levels of Neighborhood Internet Access: Assessment of Community Health Center Patients With Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary care delivery via telehealth has become increasingly common for diabetes care. Lack of equitable internet access, especially for video-based encounters, is a barrier to virtual care and affects Latino patients more than non-Hispanic White patients. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association between telehealth use and patient ethnicity and language and to determine whether neighborhood-level internet access moderates these associations.

METHODS: We used health record data from a national network of community health centers from 929 clinics in 30 US states. This retrospective open cohort included English-preferring Latino patients, Spanish-preferring Latino patients, and non-Hispanic White patients with type 2 diabetes who were receiving care from 2020 to 2024. Using negative binomial regression, we examined adjusted rates of total telehealth encounters, audio-only encounters, and video encounters by ethnicity/language and community-level internet access.

RESULTS: Among 123,541 patients with diabetes, non-Hispanic White patients consistently had the greatest telehealth rates (greatest total telehealth encounter rate: 7.52/year for those with high internet access), and Spanish-preferring Latino patients had the lowest rates (lowest total telehealth encounter rate: 5.06/year for those with low access). Overall, those with high internet access had more total telehealth use than those with low access. Rates of audio-only and video visits were greater for those with high vs low internet access.

CONCLUSIONS: This study showed a lower rate of telehealth delivery in community health centers for Latino patients compared with non-Hispanic White patients, especially for Spanish-preferring Latino patients with lower internet access. This information can be used by clinics to tailor virtual care more equitably.

articles.title: Development of a Clinician-Level Measure of Comprehensiveness and Its Associations With Primary Care Quality.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to develop a novel digital quality measure of comprehensiveness for primary care clinicians and to evaluate its association with care quality.

METHODS: We developed a clinician-level comprehensiveness measure based on the range of services provided using existing literature, the American Board of Family Medicine certification scope of practice surveys, and a technical expert panel. We applied the measure to electronic health record data from more than 1,000 primary care practices in the Primary Care Information Management and Evaluation Registry in 2018-2019. We used descriptive analyses to assess variation in clinician comprehensiveness scores, and bivariate and multivariate linear regression models to test associations with quality of care.

RESULTS: The 2,117 primary care clinicians studied had a mean comprehensiveness score of 0.51 on a scale from 0 to 1, with higher scores denoting provision of a greater range of services. Higher scores were associated with better quality of care, particularly with respect to cancer and depression screenings and diabetes care. When scores were converted to a 100-point scale, a 10-point increase in score was associated with a 3.3-percentage point (5.2%), 2.1-percentage point (4.8%), and 2.8-percentage point (4.2%) increase in breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening rate, respectively, and a 5.1-percentage point (14.3%) increase in depression screening. Increasing scores were similarly associated with improved quality of diabetes care, but no associations were found with body mass index screening or hypertension control.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this study align with those of prior studies of primary care comprehensiveness measures and outcomes. Using expert input and empirical testing, we developed an easily implementable quality measure that meets digital measurement requirements and that is associated with improved quality of clinical care, supporting its integration into performance reporting and value-based payment models.Abstract available in: يبرع (Arabic); हिन्दी (Chinese); Francais (French); Deutsch (German); हिन्दी (Hindi); Indonesian (Indonesian); (Japanese); Portugues (Portuguese); Español (Spanish).

articles.title: Aligned Evidence, Aligned Guidance: 2026-2027 Respiratory Virus Immunization Recommendations from The AAFP, AAP, ACOG, AND IDSA.
articles.abstract: Disruption of the federal vaccine advisory process prompted a coordinated, society-led approach to respiratory virus immunization guidance for the 2026-2027 season. The Vaccine Integrity Project (VIP) at the University of Minnesota Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy, in collaboration with the American Medical Association and with coordination support from the Council of Medical Specialty Societies, completed systematic reviews of influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization. Across 299 studies, the reviews confirmed protection against hospitalization and death and identified no new safety concerns in comparative studies. On September 2, 2026, the American Academy of Family Physicians (AAFP), American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Infectious Diseases Society of America issued aligned recommendations informed by this evidence. This report explains the shared evidence base, summarizes recommendations by age and population, describes the AAFP review and adoption process, and directs primary care clinicians to implementation and patient resources.

articles.title: Pre-Pregnancy and Contraceptive Care Experiences Among Black and Latina Women With Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Previous research has shown unmet needs for family planning care for individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and hypertension, both of which disproportionately impact non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic individuals. This study aimed to explore and describe experiences of pre-pregnancy and contraceptive counseling and care among reproductive-aged Black and Latina patients with T2D or hypertension or both.

METHODS: We purposively sampled 32 non-pregnant Black or Latina patients from Federally Qualified Health Centers who had T2D or hypertension or both. We conducted semistructured interviews, asking participants about experiences receiving pre-pregnancy and contraceptive care and about family planning goals and desires. We analyzed data using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Participants reported receiving limited information from clinicians about the potential impact of T2D or hypertension on pregnancy. However, many parous participants learned about these impacts through their experiences with pregnancy complications. Many participants described feeling pressured by clinicians to use contraception. Participants with hypertension also encountered challenges obtaining their desired contraceptive methods due to their condition. We found that the presence of a strong patient-clinician relationship can positively influence patients' receptivity to clinician-initiated conversations about family planning goals.

CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates a need to develop patient-centered approaches that address information needs and recognize the complexity of pre-pregnancy and contraceptive care in the context of T2D and hypertension. Additionally, greater attention to the unique challenges that Black and Latina women face in their health care must be considered.

articles.title: The Mediating Effect of Quality of Care on the Association Between Interprofessional Primary Care Teams and Health Service Use.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In this study, we evaluated the impact of patient attachment to a family physician practicing in an interprofessional primary care team (IPCT) on health service use, and the mediating effect of quality of care.

METHODS: This retrospective study used the Care Trajectories-Enriched Data (TorSaDE) cohort linking survey data and health administrative data from Quebec. Exposure was attachment to a family physician practicing in an IPCT (vs not practicing in an IPCT). Outcomes were nonurgent emergency department (ED) visits, total ED visits, and hospitalizations. Mediators were timely access, access to routine care, and coordination. Causal mediation analysis decomposed the total effect of IPCTs on the outcomes into 4 effects: controlled direct effect (due to neither mediation nor interaction), reference interaction (due to interaction only), mediated interaction (due to both mediation and interaction), and pure indirect effect (due to mediation only).

RESULTS: Our study cohort included 5,480 patient participants, 75% of whom were attached to a family physician practicing in an IPCT. The total effect of IPCTs on health service use was not statistically significant irrespective of the mediator examined. When timely access was the mediator, however, the mediated interaction was associated with a significant 7% reduction in nonurgent ED visits (P <.05) and a significant 8% reduction in total ED visits (P <.05). In contrast, access to routine care and coordinated care did not significantly mediate the association between having a family physician practicing in an IPCT and health service use.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, attachment to a family physician practicing in an IPCT was not significantly associated with health service use outcomes. Timely access may function as a key condition for improving the impact of IPCTs on health service use.

Evaluating Bepirovirsen: a first-in-class treatment option for chronic hepatitis B.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Over the last decade, the therapeutic paradigm of Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) has progressively shifted from lifelong viral suppression toward the ambitious goal of a functional cure, defined by sustained HBsAg clearance with durable control of viral replication after treatment discontinuation. Bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide directed against all HBV messenger RNAs, represents one of the most promising agents for functional cure. The phase 3 B-Well reported functional cure rates approaching 20%, rising to 27% in patients with lower baseline HBsAg levels.

AREA COVERED: In this review, we summarize the biological rationale, clinical evidence, and future perspectives of bepirovirsen, highlighting how emerging finite duration therapies could redefine treatment endpoints and move the field beyond viral suppression toward a realistic prospect of functional cure for patients living with CHB.

EXPERT OPINION: the therapeutic landscape of CHB is shifting from lifelong viral suppression toward functional cure as a realistic and clinically meaningful endpoint. Bepirovirsen may reduce the need for indefinite treatment and monitoring, lower healthcare costs, improve patients' quality of life, and decrease the social and psychological burden associated with chronic HBV infection.

Transcatheter Valve Repair of Tricuspid Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the TriCLASP Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is a viable option for patients with ≥severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR).

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate 2-year outcomes with the PASCAL transcatheter valve repair system from the TriCLASP European, single-arm, postmarket clinical follow-up study, including outcomes stratified by baseline TR severity.

METHODS: The TriCLASP study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair with the PASCAL system. TR reduction and clinical, functional, and quality of life outcomes were assessed at 2 years. Outcomes were also assessed by baseline TR severity (≤moderate vs ≥severe TR).

RESULTS: In 300 enrolled patients, mean age was 80.1 years, 52.0% were women, and 75.8% had ≥severe TR. Significant and sustained TR reduction was observed from baseline to 2 years, with ≤moderate TR achieved in 81.3% (P < 0.001). The 2-year Kaplan-Meier estimates for survival and freedom from heart failure hospitalization (HFH) were 77.5% ± 2.6% and 71.9% ± 2.8%, respectively, with a 71.4% decrease in annualized HFH rate (P < 0.001). Patients experienced significant improvements in functional capacity and quality of life at 2 years (NYHA functional class I/II: 73.2%; 6-minute walk distance: +26.6 m; Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score: +7.3 points; all P < 0.001). Outcomes were similar in patients stratified by baseline ≤moderate and ≥severe TR, including significant TR reduction and meaningful clinical, functional, and quality-of-life improvements.

CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes from the TriCLASP study confirm durable safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system at 2 years in a postmarket setting. Results demonstrated significant and sustained TR reduction, favorable survival, reduced HFH, and clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and quality of life, which were consistent across patients with moderate and severe TR.

articles.title: Low-Dose Ticagrelor Without Aspirin in Diabetes: Reassuring Pharmacodynamics, Open Clinical Questions.
Pharmacodynamic Effects of Different Ticagrelor Dosing Regimens With and Without Aspirin in Patients With Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy with ticagrelor is efficacious for secondary prevention in coronary artery disease (CAD) patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), there are limited data on its pharmacodynamic (PD) effects and the impact of drug dosing.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the PD effects of ticagrelor monotherapy at a 60-mg dosing regimen and how this compares with ticagrelor- and clopidogrel-based dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT).

METHODS: OPTIMUS-7 (Optimizing Antiplatelet Therapy in Diabetes Mellitus-7) is a randomized PD study in CAD patients with DM (n = 81). After a 7-day run-in with DAPT using aspirin (81 mg once daily) plus ticagrelor (90 mg twice daily), followed by ticagrelor 90 mg monotherapy for 10 days, patients were randomized to: 1) ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy; 2) aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg; or 3) aspirin plus clopidogrel 75 mg. PD assessments included VerifyNow P2Y12 reaction units (PRU), whole-blood vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein, and light transmittance aggregometry. The primary endpoint was noninferiority of ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy vs aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg on trough levels of PRU after 10 days (noninferiority margin 45 PRU). Markers of thromboxane-mediated platelet reactivity and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity were also assessed.

RESULTS: Ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy led to similar PRU levels compared with aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg (47 PRU [95% CI: 24-69 PRU] vs 40 PRU [95% CI: 18-61 PRU]; mean difference 7 PRU; 95% CI: -23 to 38 PRU), meeting the noninferiority primary endpoint. Clopidogrel-based DAPT showed higher PRU than both ticagrelor dosing regimens. Light transmittance aggregometry and whole-blood vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein showed parallel findings. Markers of thromboxane-mediated platelet reactivity and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity were increased with ticagrelor monotherapy compared with DAPT.

CONCLUSIONS: In CAD patients with DM, ticagrelor 60 mg monotherapy achieved similar P2Y12 inhibition compared with aspirin plus ticagrelor 60 mg and greater inhibition than clopidogrel-based DAPT. Ticagrelor monotherapy showed increased thromboxane-mediated aggregation and total platelet-mediated global thrombogenicity compared with DAPT regimens. (Ticagrelor With and Without Aspirin in Patients With Diabetes Mellitus [OPTIMUS-7]; NCT04484259).

articles.title: Treating the Bleeding Source Before PCI Does Not Reset Bleeding Risk.
Impact of Targeted Bleeding Source Treatment on Recurrent Bleeding Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether targeted treatment (TT) to potentially cure the cause of bleeding before percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is effective in preventing recurrent bleeding or death after PCI is unknown.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to assess whether TT affects recurrent bleeding or survival after PCI.

METHODS: We included patients from the Cardiobase Bern PCI registry with Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) 2 to 4 bleeding before index PCI. TT was defined as surgical, interventional, or medical therapy targeted to cure the cause of prior bleeding. The primary endpoint was recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding at the identical location; secondary endpoints were any BARC 2 to 5 bleeding and mortality throughout 1 year (median: 390 days [Q1-Q3: 371-430 days]) after PCI. We report inverse probability weight-adjusted hazard ratios (IPW-HRs) with TT as dependent variable, and as covariates we report the Academic Research Consortium for High Bleeding Risk variables associated with ≥4% 1-year BARC 3 to 5 bleeding, antithrombotic treatment, and bleeding location.

RESULTS: Of 19,352 patients, 847 (4.4%) had prior bleeding, 358 of 847 (42.3%) with and 489 of 847 (57.7%) without TT. Recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding at the identical location occurred in 8.9% (32/358) with TT vs 5.1% (25/489) without TT (IPW-HR: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.10-3.19; P = 0.020). There were no differences in any recurrent BARC 2 to 5 bleeding (TT 14.5% [52/358] vs no TT of 10.6% [52/489]; IPW-HR: 1.41; 95% CI: 0.95-2.08; P = 0.087) or mortality (TT 14.0% [50/358] vs no TT 12.3% [60/489]; IPW-HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 0.79-1.70; P = 0.455).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with prior bleeding before PCI, despite TT of the bleeding source, the risk of recurrent bleeding remained significantly higher at the identical location when compared with patients without TT, without a reduction in any recurrent bleeding or mortality after PCI. (CARDIOBASE Bern PCI Registry; NCT02241291).

articles.title: A Journey of Risk Scores for Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Guidance.
Predicting Ischemic and Bleeding Risk in Patients on DAPT After PCI: A Machine Learning Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary stenting prevents ischemic complications but increases bleeding risk. Individualized assessment of these combined risks may inform treatment strategies.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a machine learning algorithm for clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with potential to support clinical decisions around antiplatelet therapy.

METHODS: Data from 11 clinical trials encompassing 19,106 patients who underwent PCI with everolimus-eluting stents were randomly split 3:1 to train and validate 2 separate machine learning algorithms for ischemic (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or stent thrombosis) and bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5) risk prediction at 1 year. The Boruta algorithm was used to select the top 11 variables (providing >80% of predictive information) for final model development. An independent cohort of 10,696 patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary-care center (Mount Sinai Hospital) was used for external validation.

RESULTS: There were 594 (4.1%) ischemic and 448 (3.1%) bleeding events in the training data set. Random survival forest was selected as the best-performing model (mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.76 for ischemic events and 0.81 for bleeding). Internal and external validation yielded a mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.72 and 0.70 for ischemic events and 0.72 and 0.71 for bleeding, respectively. The 2 models met the prespecified performance goal in both validation cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: A machine learning-based tool exhibited good discriminative ability for the prediction of ischemic and bleeding events at 1 year post-PCI and warrants prospective evaluation in clinical decisions surrounding antithrombotic therapies.

articles.title: Excimer Laser Coronary Atherectomy in Contemporary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Position Statement.
articles.abstract: Excimer laser coronary atherectomy (ELCA) was introduced over 4 decades ago for the modification and debulking of coronary atherosclerotic plaque. However, the adoption of ELCA has remained low, in part because of misperceptions around and limited understanding of its mechanism of action, the disappointing early experience with the device, and limited awareness of the significant body of safety and efficacy data generated after optimization of catheter design and procedural methods. The introduction of other techniques, such as rotational atherectomy, orbital atherectomy, and lately, intravascular lithotripsy, has further contributed to uncertainty regarding the optimal placement and value of ELCA within the percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) algorithm. This document clarifies the value and role of ELCA in contemporary PCI, with new insights on its mechanism of action as well as recommendations for settings and protocols for use to help cardiologists achieve successful procedural and clinical outcomes. ELCA is a valuable tool for uncrossable and undilatable thrombotic and stent-related lesions. Lesion composition, settings, and lasing medium affect the magnitude of ELCA's photoablative effects. This study contains recommendations for ELCA setup, settings, and protocols.

articles.title: Conflict and complexity in diabetes care: a qualitative exploration of barriers to goal setting in rural Australian general practice.
Cohort profile: Ifakara Heart and Lung Clinic cohort for patients with non-communicable heart and lung diseases in rural Tanzania.
Co-design of an eye-tracking communication tool and a feasibility randomised controlled trial in conscious non-verbal ICU patients in Shanghai, China: protocol for a two-phase mixed-methods study.
Targeting estrogen receptor signalling for the management of insulin resistance: From hormones to herbal modulators.
articles.abstract: Estrogen exerts a critical influence on metabolic health by modulating insulin signalling pathways via its receptors (ERα, ERβ and the G protein-coupled oestrogen receptor [GPER]). Estrogen decline, as seen postmenopausally or in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is strongly associated with insulin resistance and the pathogenesis of Type 2 diabetes. The beneficial metabolic actions of estrogen, including enhanced insulin sensitivity, are mediated through mechanisms such as AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation, promotion of GLUT4 translocation, and suppression of inflammatory pathways. Conversely, decreased estrogen levels contribute to adipose tissue accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and exacerbated insulin resistance. Current pharmacological interventions, including hormone replacement therapy (HRT) and selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs), can ameliorate insulin resistance but are accompanied by ongoing debate concerning their cardiovascular safety and oncological risk. These risks highlights the need for more targeted therapeutic strategies. Emerging agents, such as ERβ-selective agonists and GPER activators, alongside the refined application of herbal phytoestrogens, offer promising avenues to develop tissue- and receptor-specific modulators. Consequently, future pharmacological development needs to focus on harnessing these selective estrogenic pathways to achieve optimal metabolic benefits, whilst minimising off-target effects, so paving the way for precision medicine in the management of metabolic disease.

articles.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis in a returning traveller: the risk of anchoring on exposure history.
Mesh in the midst of infection: reconstruction of extensive Fournier's and Meleney's gangrene with bowel evisceration using negative-pressure wound therapy and polypropylene scaffold.
Neurosarcoidosis presenting with central diabetes insipidus and unilateral vocal fold paresis.
Cutaneous phaeohyphomycosis caused by Phaeoacremonium alvesii in a dog.
articles.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
articles.abstract: An 11-year-old intact male Italian Greyhound receiving cyclosporine and prednisolone for thrombocytopenia developed multiple nodules on the right forelimb. Cytology revealed numerous branching fungal hyphae, and histopathology demonstrated pyogranulomatous dermatitis with intralesional hyphae. Fungal culture and internal transcribed spacer sequencing identified Phaeoacremonium alvesii. Among the antifungal agents tested, posaconazole showed the lowest minimum inhibitory concentration (0.06 mg/L). Clinical resolution was achieved with oral posaconazole treatment for 6 months and withdrawal of prednisolone. This appears to represent the first report of canine phaeohyphomycosis caused by P. alvesii. Opportunistic fungal infection should be considered in dogs receiving long-term immunosuppressive therapy that develop cutaneous nodules.

articles.title: 2026 consensus on the management of Cushing's disease: a collaborative statement from the Korean Endocrine Society and Japan Endocrine Society.
authors: Committee of Clinical Practice Guideline of Korean Endocrine Society
Korean Neuroendocrine Study Group of Korean Endocrine Society
articles.abstract: The primary treatment goal of Cushing's disease (CD) is sustained normalization of hypercortisolism as well as relief of tumor mass effects, to reduce morbidity and mortality and improve long-term quality of life. Korea and Japan share broadly similar therapeutic principles for CD; however, real-world management differs because of country-specific healthcare systems, regulatory environments, and medication availability. Building on the previously published Korean Endocrine Society (KES)-Japan Endocrine Society (JES) diagnostic consensus, a joint multidisciplinary working group developed an expert consensus focused on the treatment and management of CD. Surgical intervention for pituitary tumors, primarily via a transsphenoidal approach, remains the first-line treatment when feasible. Subsequent treatment should be individualized according to disease and tumor characteristics, severity of hypercortisolism, associated comorbidities, and regional availability of therapeutic options. Medical treatment is recommended for patients with persistent or recurrent disease after surgery, for those who are not candidates for surgery or who decline surgical intervention, and as bridging therapy in severe cases requiring urgent control of hypercortisolemia or when definitive treatment is delayed. Pituitary tumor-directed agents and adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors constitute key pharmacologic options, but the available agents and reimbursement status differ between Korea and Japan. Radiation therapy is considered when surgery is not feasible or when control is not achieved with surgery and/or medical therapy, and bilateral adrenalectomy may be reserved for highly selected refractory cases. This consensus statement provides harmonized, practice-oriented recommendations while acknowledging current evidence gaps and the need for further collaborative research to inform CD management in East Asian populations.

articles.title: Waist circumference predicts incident hepatic steatosis and progression in people with HIV: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Steatotic liver disease is a cause of growing concern in people with HIV (PWH). Longitudinal studies on unselected PWH are lacking. This study aimed to describe the dynamics of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in PWH, identify risk factors for steatosis progression and evaluate blood-based non-invasive scores and anthropometric measures for predicting incident steatosis.

METHODS: In this single-centre longitudinal cohort of PWH from Copenhagen, Denmark, hepatic steatosis and fibrosis were assessed by transient elastography at baseline and a 2-year follow-up. Risk factors were evaluated using ordinal logistic regression. The predictive performance of a panel of measures was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.

RESULTS: Of 513 cohort participants, 413 attended the follow-up. Steatosis prevalence increased from 32.4% to 37.0%. Steatosis developed in 22.9% of participants without steatosis and resolved in 33.6% with steatosis. Fibrosis prevalence decreased from 4.4% to 2.9%. Baseline waist circumference (aOR per 5 cm: 1.65, 95% CI [1.44-1.89]) and increase (aOR per 5%: 2.0, 95% CI [1.58-2.54]) were associated with higher steatosis grade at follow-up, whereas hip circumference increase was not. Statin initiation was associated with lower steatosis grade at follow-up (aOR: 0.42, 95% CI [0.17-0.97]), but the association did not persist across sensitivity analyses. Waist circumference performed comparably to blood-based scores in predicting hepatic steatosis.

CONCLUSION: Hepatic steatosis was highly dynamic over the 2-year follow-up. Steatosis progression and development were linked to waist circumference. These findings suggest that waist circumference monitoring could play a role in hepatic steatosis management in PWH.

articles.title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex.
articles.abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1-3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown.
