Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

articles.title: [The Future of Thoracic Surgery. First Position Paper from the Working Group on "Sustainability in Thoracic Surgery"].
articles.abstract: The healthcare sector is a major contributor to the climate crisis and, at the same time, faces increasing health risks due to climate change. This position paper from the Working Group on "Sustainability in Thoracic Surgery" demonstrates how thoracic surgery departments can reduce emissions, strengthen resilience, and improve the quality of care through capital and non-capital investments. Capital-intensive measures are planned by technical and operational management, as part of a structured climate protection management system, and include measures for energy efficiency, the use of renewable energy, sustainable mobility, and others. Non-investment measures focus on behavioural changes: energy-efficient ventilation/heating, shutting down air conditioning systems in the OR at night, optimising the patient's journey, strict indications for energy-intensive diagnostics, resource-efficient surgical processes, waste prevention and separation, and pilot projects for recycling contaminated single-use products. Dietary strategies (plant-based, regional, seasonal, organic) also reduce Scope 3 emissions and improve clinical outcomes. Economical use of oxygen, drastic reduction of volatile anaesthetics and anaesthetic gas recycling, as well as climate-conscious prescription of inhaled medications play an important role in pulmonology and thoracic surgery. The ERAS approach-which aims to reduce length of stay, resource consumption, complications, and the need for intensive care-is also a sustainable, cross-disciplinary strategy. This paper provides practical tools, governance recommendations, and examples to transform thoracic surgery in a sustainable, evidence-based, and cost-effective manner.

articles.title: Malaria and the Coagulation System: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Malaria is a major global infectious disease, with Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) accounting for most severe and fatal cases. Severe malaria is also a disorder of the microvasculature in which parasite sequestration, endothelial activation, platelet responses, and coagulation pathways interact. During the erythrocytic stage, infected red blood cells express P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1, enabling cytoadherence to endothelial receptors such as CD36, ICAM-1, thrombomodulin, and the endothelial protein C receptor. This promotes microvascular sequestration, tissue hypoxia, and organ dysfunction, including cerebral and placental malaria. Endothelial activation is accompanied by marked release of von Willebrand factor and relative deficiency of ADAMTS13 activity, leading to accumulation of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers that support platelet adhesion, infected erythrocyte bridging, and microvascular obstruction. Platelets have context-dependent roles: they contribute to thrombocytopenia, vascular plugging, and cerebral pathology, but may also mediate antiparasitic immunity through platelet factor 4-dependent parasite killing. More recently, anti-platelet factor 4/polyanion antibodies and antiphospholipid antibodies have been implicated in malaria-associated platelet activation, anemia, and potentially microthrombosis. Tissue factor expression by endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, and infected placental tissue further links inflammation to fibrin deposition and severe organ manifestations. Clinically, this manifests as thrombocytopenia, prolonged coagulation profiles, and potential disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Because routine adjunctive anticoagulation is not recommended, management remains strictly focused on rapid antiparasitic therapy and supportive care. This review summarizes current concepts of hemostatic dysfunction in malaria and highlights unresolved questions regarding targeted modulation of coagulation pathways.

articles.title: Trends in Hospitalisation for Pulmonary Embolism in Germany: Analysis of the German DRG-Statistics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We analysed time trends in hospitalisation rates for pulmonary embolism (PE) in Germany between 2005 and 2023.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Detailed lists of hospitalisations with the primary diagnosis of PE were provided by the Federal Statistical Office. PE were separated into severe PE with acute cor pulmonale (ICD code I26.0) and non-severe PE without (I26.9).

RESULTS: Age-standardised hospitalisation rates per 100,000 inhabitants rose from 55 in 2005 to 69 (+25.5%) in 2023. This increase occurred primarily between 2005 and 2013. In the following years from 2014 to 2023, age-standardised hospitalisation rates declined among women and remained constant among men. Age-standardised hospitalisation rates for PE with acute cor pulmonale slightly decreased with 22 in 2005 and 20 in 2023. Hospitalisation rates for those with non-severe PE increased form 32 in 2005 to 50 in 2023. In the 45-64 age group, there was a continuous increase in cases with PE with acute cor pulmonale, from 14 in 2005 to 19 (+35.7%) in 2023. Among people 65 years and older, it remained constant from 2005 to 2008, followed by a steady decline from 71 in 2009 to 57 (-19.7%) in 2023.

CONCLUSION: Analysis of hospitalisation rates due to PE in Germany presented here shows varying trends over time regarding gender, age and time periods. There was a steady increase in hospitalisation rates due to PE through 2013 and a plateau afterwards. Most striking are the steady increase in PE with acute cor pulmonale in the 45-64 age group and the decline in such PEs in the age group 65 years and older between 2008 and 2023.

articles.title: Artepillin C Positively Regulates the Expression of Regulatory Molecules by Monocytic Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells and Reduces Lung Inflammation in Experimental Asthma.
articles.abstract: Artepillin C (ArtC), the major compound of green propolis, has anti-inflammatory and pro-apoptotic properties. We previously showed that ArtC reduces lung inflammation in ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma model by inducing monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (M-MDSC); however, the underlying suppressive mechanisms remain unknown. Here, we show these mechanisms and determine whether ArtC directly affects eosinophil survival in experimental asthma. M-MDSC differentiation and activation were assessed in vitro after ArtC treatment by kinetic analysis of immunosuppressive molecules and co-culture assays measuring CD4+ T cell proliferation. The effect of ArtC on eosinophil apoptosis was also examined in vitro. In vivo, OVA-exposed mice were treated with ArtC and evaluated for lung inflammation, mucus production, eosinophil influx, M-MDSC frequency, expression of suppressive molecules by lung M-MDSC, and apoptotic eosinophils. Our results show that ArtC induced M-MDSC differentiation and activation, with increase in PD-L1 (Programmed cell Death Ligand 1), PD-L2, IDO (Indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase), and Arg1 (Arginase 1) expression and consequent suppression of CD4+ T cell proliferation. Moreover, ArtC induced eosinophil apoptosis. In vivo, ArtC-treated OVA-exposed mice showed reduced lung inflammation, mucus production, and eosinophil influx, and increased lung M-MDSC frequency, without differences in suppressor molecule expressions or apoptotic eosinophil numbers. ArtC positively regulates the expression of multiple suppressor molecules in M-MDSC in a time-dependent manner and is pro-apoptotic to eosinophils, a readout of allergic asthma, representing a potential therapeutic approach to reduce asthmatic lung inflammation.

articles.title: Telomere Biology, Vascular Aging, and Hypertension: Mechanistic Pathways, Cellular Senescence, and Cardiovascular Risk.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a major global health challenge and a leading risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. Beyond established hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory mechanisms, biological aging processes may contribute to vascular dysfunction and cardiovascular risk. Telomeres are specialized DNA-protein structures that protect chromosome ends and maintain genomic stability. Although progressive telomere shortening has been associated with cellular senescence, oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, telomere dysfunction may also occur independently of substantial changes in mean telomere length, including through telomere uncapping, oxidative DNA damage, replication-associated lesions, and impaired shelterin-mediated protection. This narrative review examines the relationship between telomere biology, vascular aging, and hypertension, integrating epidemiological, genetic, and experimental evidence. Particular attention is given to DNA damage response pathways, mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, endothelial impairment, and vascular remodeling. Human studies frequently report associations between shorter leukocyte telomere length and hypertension; however, findings from genetic studies are not uniform, and some Mendelian randomization analyses suggest that genetically determined longer telomere length may be associated with higher blood pressure or selected cardiometabolic traits. Moreover, leukocyte telomere length does not necessarily reflect telomere integrity in vascular tissues. Nutritional, environmental, and pharmacological factors that may influence telomere biology are also discussed, distinguishing observational associations from experimental and clinical evidence. Overall, current findings support a potential relationship between telomere dysfunction and vascular aging, but do not establish whether telomere alterations are independent causal determinants of hypertension, consequences of chronic vascular stress, or markers of shared biological processes. Further longitudinal, tissue-specific, and mechanistic studies are required to clarify these relationships and determine the clinical utility of telomere-related biomarkers.

articles.title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.

articles.title: Ventricular Septal Pulsed Field Ablation: Noninvasive, Longitudinal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Lesion Structure and Function in a Preclinical Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging myocardial ablation strategy, but lesion evolution and noninvasive assessment in ventricular myocardium remain incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate interventricular septal (IVS) PFA in a preclinical swine model and assess the feasibility of serial cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) for lesion characterization.

METHODS: Eight swine were allocated to acute and chronic cohorts. PFA was delivered to the IVS using a variable-loop circular catheter (VLCC). Multimodality assessments included electroanatomic mapping, serial CMR, echocardiography and pathology. Pathological lesion-depth measurements were obtained at terminal timepoints, whereas serial CMR enabled within-animal longitudinal assessment. CMR-pathology correspondence was evaluated using anatomically matched slices.

RESULTS: Serial CMR showed reductions in late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-derived lesion mass and volume by Day 21, with stabilization thereafter. Among 37 matched CMR-pathology slices from five animals, CMR-LGE-derived lesion-depth measurements showed positive association with pathology-derived measurements (Pearson's r = 0.77), moderate reliability (ICC = 0.74), and a mean difference of 0.03 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -1.15 to 1.21 mm. Both methods showed decreased chronic lesion depths, consistent with lesion maturation and fibrotic remodeling. Transient reductions in left ventricular ejection fraction and regional septal mechanics were observed after PFA, followed by partial recovery.

CONCLUSION: Ventricular septal PFA produced well-demarcated lesions that evolved into chronic fibrotic scars. Serial CMR enabled noninvasive assessment of lesion localization, depth, and temporal evolution, with lesion-depth measurements showing correspondence with anatomically matched pathological measurements, supporting the feasibility of CMR for longitudinal assessment after ventricular PFA.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and progression of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is associated with incident atrial fibrillation (AF). However, its relationship with AF progression remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether CHIP is associated with AF progression.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients with paroxysmal AF who underwent deep targeted sequencing for CHIP mutations between April 2021 and December 2022. Variant allele fraction (VAF) ≥2.0% defined CHIP. The primary endpoint was documented AF progression, defined as either (1) AF documented on at least two separate 12-lead ECGs obtained >1 week apart, or (2) 100% AF burden on extended ECG monitoring. We assessed the association between CHIP and AF progression using Cox proportional hazards regression. In patients with available left atrial (LA) electroanatomical mapping, we compared low-voltage areas (LVA) by clonal hematopoiesis (CH) status (VAF ≥1.0% cutoff).

RESULTS: Among the 310 patients (mean age 65.7±5.7 years), CHIP was present in 64 patients (20.6%). Over a mean follow-up of 2.6±1.0 years, documented AF progression occurred in 10/64 (15.6%) patients with CHIP and 15/246 (6.1%) without CHIP. CHIP was independently associated with AF progression [adjusted hazard ratio 3.38, 95% CI 1.45-7.85; P = 0.005]. In an exploratory mapping subgroup, extensive LVA (≥10.0%) was more frequent in CH [24.4% vs 9.5%; unadjusted OR 3.10, 95% CI 1.10-8.71] and numerically higher at the VAF ≥2.0% cutoff.

CONCLUSION: In patients with paroxysmal AF, CHIP was associated with a 3.4-fold higher risk of documented AF progression. Exploratory mapping findings suggest a possible association between CH and advanced atrial substrate, warranting further validation.

articles.title: Connect Proctoring: A Novel Educational Model for Training in Interventional Cardiology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural outcomes, and educational value of Connect Proctoring - a structured remote training framework combining theoretical education with real-time audiovisual supervision of live chronic total occlusion (CTO) percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) procedures.

BACKGROUND: Operator training in CTO PCI represents one of the most demanding learning pathways in interventional cardiology. The continuous development of new devices and techniques requires fast and efficient methods of learning and expertise maintenance.

METHODS: Prospective evaluation of CTO cases performed by operators interested in learning advanced techniques for CTO. Four interventional cardiologists performed 12 CTO PCI procedures in total (3 consecutive interventions per trainee) as primary operators under real-time remote supervision by one external expert proctor. The trainee theoretical knowledge was assessed before and after the programme in all four trainees, followed by a structured surveys.

RESULTS: Trainee theoretical knowledge improved by a mean of 23 percentage points (51% to 75%; range +20 to +28 points), with improvement observed in all 4 trainees. The overall trainee survey mean was 4.5/5.0; the clinical decision-making domain scored 4.9/5.0. Proctors agreed 3 cases are insufficient for independent CTO PCI (mean 1.7/5.0) but sufficient to improve parallel wiring competency (3.3/5.0). Technical success was 92 % (11/12). Mean Japanese Multicenter CTO Registry score was 1.9 ± 0.7; 83% moderate-to-severe calcification. True vessel perforation requiring treatment occurred in 2 cases (17%), both managed successfully without tamponade or mortality; 2 further cases showed minor contrast staining requiring no treatment. Local expert intervention was required for retrograde manoeuvres (3/4 retrograde cases), 2 antegrade dissection and re-entry (ADR) steps, and 1 delayed tamponade after distal vessel perforation requiring coil embolisation.

IN CONCLUSIONS: Connect Proctoring could be considered a promising educational method that when applied within a structured framework, supports the operators in the adoption of a new CTO PCI devices and techniques. A complete complications- management training must be fulfilled before any remote-only application. Multicentre prospective validation is required before broader implementation.

articles.title: Comparing the Risk of Intracranial Hemorrhage with Direct Oral Anticoagulants vs. Low Molecular Weight Heparin in Patients with Cancer-Associated Thromboembolism and Brain Metastases.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The management of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with cancer and brain metastases is complicated by the dual risk of thrombosis and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). The comparative safety of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) versus the standard of care, low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), remains uncertain in this high-risk population.

METHODS: In this retrospective TriNetX cohort study (2014-2024), adults with solid tumors, brain metastases and VTE within six months of brain metastasis diagnosis who initiated therapeutic-dose DOACs were compared with LMWH initiators after 1:1 propensity score matching. ICH at 12 months was the primary outcome and the only comparison tested formally. All-cause mortality and medically attended bleeding, ascertained from diagnosis codes, and all subgroup and sensitivity analyses are descriptive. Criteria and code lists appear in the Supplemental Material.

RESULTS: Matched cohorts included 4,252 patients each. The 12-month Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence of ICH was 9.0% (95% CI 8.1-10.1) with DOACs versus 10.5% (95% CI 9.4-11.6) with LMWH (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.72-0.98, p=0.03). Medically attended bleeding occurred in 19.5% versus 21.9% (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.77-0.96) and mortality in 48.3% versus 54.5% (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.77-0.87). ICH estimates favored DOACs in all five cancer subgroups and when restricted to newly diagnosed brain metastases (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.74-1.01).

CONCLUSIONS: DOAC initiation was not associated with a higher risk of ICH or of medically attended bleeding than LMWH, and the observed incidence of both was lower with DOACs. These findings suggest DOACs are a viable anticoagulation option in this population, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: On the Origin of Bilirubin: The Bilirubin Fuel-Switch Hypothesis and Hepatic Metabolic Flexibility.
articles.abstract: Bilirubin has traditionally been regarded as a metabolic waste product of heme catabolism, destined for hepatic processing and excretion. However, emerging evidence suggests that bilirubin also acts as a bioactive molecule that modulates various metabolic pathways. A significant, often underappreciated, observation is that fasting rapidly elevates unconjugated bilirubin in the bloodstream within hours of nutrient deprivation. This finding implicates conserved mechanisms linking bilirubin metabolism to energy homeostasis. Moreover, fasting promotes lipolysis in adipose tissue, hepatic fatty acid oxidation, ketone body synthesis, and PPARα activation. Recent research shows that bilirubin can directly activate PPARα, establishing a mechanistic link between fasting-induced hyperbilirubinemia and adaptive metabolic responses. This comprehensive review of clinical, experimental, and mechanistic data supports the hypothesis that increased bilirubin levels during fasting signal enhanced lipid oxidation, ketone production, mitochondrial function, and hormonal regulation during periods of nutrient scarcity. Elevated bilirubin levels may stem from reduced hepatic conjugation, increased free fatty acid release, altered enterohepatic circulation, and increased bilirubin synthesis. Evidence from individuals carrying Gilbert syndrome-associated UGT1A1 variants, animal models, and bilirubin-based therapeutic interventions indicates that bilirubin confers protective effects against adiposity, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and insulin resistance. The proposed Bilirubin Fuel-Switch Hypothesis posits that fasting-induced increases in bilirubin act as a metabolic signal, shifting metabolism from carbohydrate dependence to fatty acid oxidation and ketogenesis by amplifying PPARα-dependent transcriptional programs. This framework positions bilirubin as a fasting-responsive metabolic ligand that interlinks heme catabolism with fuel selection and adaptive energy regulation.

articles.title: [CMV Testing in Amniotic Fluid: Trends from 2015 to 2025 at a multidisciplinary prenatal diagnostic center].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To study trends in the number and indications for CMV testing of amniotic fluid, and pregnancy outcomes in cases of positive results.

METHODS: Patients who underwent CMV PCR testing of amniotic fluid at a Level 3 maternity hospital from 2015 to 2025. Annual trends in the number of PCR tests, indications, positive result rates, and pregnancy outcomes.

RESULTS: 1,096 cases were included. The number of CMV PCR tests on amniotic fluid increased by 12.4% per year. Over the period, the rates of testing for maternal primary infection and for ultrasound abnormalities increased by 20% and decreased by 20.8% per year, respectively. The rate of estimated fetal weight below the 3rd percentile did not change significantly, while the rate of head circumference below the 3rd percentile increased. Over 11 years, 57 patients tested positive for CMV PCR, with a stable annual rate showing no significant variation before or after 2020. Among these patients, the live birth rate has been higher since 2020 (55,6%) than before 2019 (23,8%, p = 0,028).

CONCLUSION: We observed an increase in the number of CMV PCR tests performed, particularly for maternal primary infection. This can be explained by the discovery of the efficacy of prophylactic valacyclovir, which has led to the implementation of systematic screening. The change in the fetal growth curve in 2022 could explain the increase in our rate of small head circumference measurements. No measurable impact of the COVID-19 pandemic was observed in this cohort.

articles.title: Innovations in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract: Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) can provide rapid hemodynamic stabilization in cardiogenic shock (CS), creating a bridge to myocardial recovery, durable MCS or heart transplantation. Contemporary platforms remain constrained by risk of vascular and hemocompatability-related adverse events, restricted patient mobility and support duration. These limitations have become increasingly relevant as tMCS use expands beyond acute myocardial infarction-related CS to the highly heterogeneous heart failure-related and postcardiotomy shock states. Next generation tMCS technologies seek to address these issues through lower-profile access, improved hemocompatibility, dedicated right- and biventricular support, extended support duration with greater support capabilities, enhanced patient mobility, and integrated physiologic monitoring. This State-of-the-Art Review examines the design rationale, technological maturity, and emerging clinical evidence for these platforms, while highlighting clinical, data-related, engineering and regulatory gaps in the field. Ultimately, the challenge for next-generation tMCS is not simply to deliver greater flow, but to provide appropriate, phenotype-directed circulatory support while minimizing the biological, vascular, and operational costs.

articles.title: Ex Situ Echocardiography During Normothermic Perfusion: Serial Physiologic Full Cardiac-Output Assessments for Transplant Suitability.
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical normothermic ex situ donor-heart perfusion (NEHP) uses retrograde aortic infusion which prevents hemodynamic assessment. We sought to optimize and validate guideline-directed ex situ echocardiography (ESE) for assessment of transplant suitability using a novel full-cardiac output (FCO) circuit.

METHODS: Following transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), porcine hearts were procured and maintained on NEHP for 24 hours. At hours 1, 12, and 24, maintenance NEHP was transitioned to low-preload working-heart mode (LPWH). Although not physiologic, LPWH ensured optimal coronary perfusion and allowed ESE. Hearts were transitioned to physiologic FCO mode and ESE was repeated. NEHP was returned to maintenance. LPWH-ESE and FCO-ESE parameters were compared to determine their ability to stratify function.

RESULTS: Forty-two echocardiograms (6 TTE, 36 ESE) were performed (n=6; 55±8 kg; female 50%; hearts 311±40gm). When compared to FCO-ESE, LPWH-ESE at hour 1 underestimated function (cardiac output (CO) 0.78±0.38 vs 3.26±1.70L/min, p=0.012; cardiac index (CI) 0.0024±0.0010 vs 0.0102±0.0048L/m/gm, p=0.009; stroke volume (SV) 8.0±3.5 vs 30.0±8.2mL, p=0.001; stroke work (SW) 279±102 vs 1683±1134mL/mmHg, p=0.026) and correlation was poor (R2 0.22-0.36). FCO-ESE successfully stratified function between hours 1 and 12 (LVEF 54.6±13.0 vs 33.6±6.0%, p=0.011; CO 3.26±1.70 vs 1.37±0.86L/min, p=0.003; CI 0.0102±0.0048 vs 0.0053±0.0027L/m/gm, p=0.016; SV 30.0±8.2 vs 15.3±6.6mL, p=0.001; SW 1683±1134 vs 686±472mL/mmHg, p=0.029), hours 12 and 24 (LVEF 33.6±6.0 vs 53.0±8.2%, p=0.036, and hours 1 and 24 (SV 30.0±8.2 vs 23.1±6.6mL, p=0.032). LPWH-ESE could not.

CONCLUSION: Physiologic FCO guideline-directed ESE should facilitate determination of transplant suitability in currently discarded donor hearts and thereby increase the number available for transplantation.

SOCIAL MEDIA: Guideline-directed Ex Situ Echocardiography during physiologic full cardiac output normothermic ex situ perfusion can reproducibly assess donor heart suitability for transplantation #EchoFirst @ASE360 @DHDrake.

articles.title: Association of time-updated diabetes and cardiovascular disease with mortality in the Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study.
articles.abstract: In this 2-decade, time-updated analysis of more than 10,000 Middle-Eastern people, diabetes conferred a risk comparable to established CVD for cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular mortality, whereas their coexistence conferred substantially higher risk only for the former.

articles.title: Association of blood eosinophil counts with prevalent metabolic disorders and incident type 2 diabetes by atopic status.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine the association between peripheral blood eosinophil counts and common metabolic abnormalities and to evaluate their ability to predict incident type 2 diabetes in adults with and without atopy.

METHODS: This cross-sectional and longitudinal cohort study included a randomly selected sample from a single Spanish municipality (n = 1516; 55.3% women; median age, 52 years [range, 18-91 years]). Body mass index, glycated hemoglobin, insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, prediabetes, and diabetes were assessed. Blood eosinophil counts were measured in 1504 participants. Atopic status was determined by skin prick testing. Participants were followed for a median of 11.5 years to ascertain incident type 2 diabetes.

RESULTS: In the cross-sectional analysis, eosinophil count was positively and significantly associated with obesity, metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and diabetes. These associations remained significant after adjusting for confounders and were more evident among non-atopic individuals. In the longitudinal analysis, baseline eosinophilia (>500/mm3) was associated with an increased risk of incident type 2 diabetes in non-atopic individuals. However, this association was attenuated after adjusting for confounders.

CONCLUSIONS: Common metabolic disorders are associated with higher blood eosinophil counts, particularly among non-atopic adults. The association of peripheral blood eosinophilia with the long-term risk of type 2 diabetes warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Impact of lifetime vascular complication history on cardiorespiratory fitness in older adults with type 1 diabetes: the epidemiology of diabetes interventions and complications (EDIC) study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify multi-system determinants of cardiorespiratory fitness in adults with long-standing type 1 diabetes (T1D) and assess associations with physical function and quality of life.

METHODS: We performed symptom-limited cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) in 664 participants in the Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications (EDIC) study (age 64 ± 6 years; T1D duration 43 ± 5 years; 45 % women) in 2023-2025. We assessed associations of fitness and exercise responses with antecedent and concurrent phenotypes and diabetes complications over ≈40 years.

RESULTS: Average VO2peak was 20.1 ± 6.0 ml/kg/min, with approximately one-third of participants having a VO2peak below thresholds for functional independence (<18 ml/kg/min). Beyond glycemia and CVD, renal dysfunction was strongly associated with lower VO2peak, anaerobic threshold, and delayed VO2 recovery. Associations of nephropathy measures with VO2peak were comparable to those of cardiovascular complications. VO2peak declined progressively with increasing complication burden, from 22.7 ± 6.5 ml/kg/min among participants without complications to 17.5 ± 4.7 ml/kg/min among those with complications in every system. Physical function and quality of life were also strongly associated with VO2peak.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular complications, particularly renal dysfunction, are associated with reduced cardiorespiratory fitness in long-standing T1D. Addressing multi-system complications may help preserve functional capacity with aging.

articles.title: Can artificial intelligence identify women at high risk of gestational diabetes before Pregnancy? A Population-Based study of 32 million pregnancies.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Identifying women at elevated risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) before conception could create opportunities for earlier prevention. This study aimed to evaluate whether artificial intelligence (AI) models using routinely available, non-laboratory preconception characteristics can stratify GDM risk in a subsequent pregnancy and identify women who may benefit from earlier assessment.

METHODS: This retrospective population-based study included 32,035,576 singleton live-birth pregnancies from U.S. National Center for Health Statistics data (2016-2024). Thirty-two predictors were evaluated using TabM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and logistic regression. Models were developed on 2016-2022 data, tuned and calibrated in separate 2023 subsets, and temporally tested in 2024. Performance evaluation included discrimination, calibration, risk stratification, and subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Overall, 2,372,108 pregnancies (7.40%) involved GDM; prevalence increased from 5.93% in 2016 to 8.53% in 2024. In the 2024 test cohort (n = 3,464,173), TabM achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.7119 (95% CI 0.7109-0.7128) and PR-AUC of 0.1913; XGBoost and CatBoost performed similarly. Calibration was strong. The calibration-defined highest-risk 5% had an observed GDM risk of 26.31%, capturing 15.98% of cases; the highest-risk 20% captured 45.16%.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconception characteristics yielded moderate discrimination but identified substantially elevated GDM-risk strata, supporting further evaluation of targeted preventive counseling and early metabolic assessment alongside routine pregnancy screening.

articles.title: Early Perioperative Outcomes of Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty in Octogenarians Versus Younger Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is increasingly performed at both extremes of age, yet early complications have rarely been compared between the youngest and the oldest candidates. This study compared 90-day complication rates after UKA between patients younger than 60 years and patients 80 years or older.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included all UKAs performed between 2015 and 2025: 73 patients (86 knees) younger than 60 years and 98 patients (111 knees) 80 years or older. Major complications comprised deep infection, early revision, pulmonary embolism, cardiovascular events, stroke, and death; all other complications were minor. Active range of motion, hospital-stay data, and operative time were also compared.

RESULTS: Rates of major complications (three [3.5%] versus six [5.4%]; P = 0.73) and minor complications (six [7.0%] versus nine [8.1%]; P = 1.00), active range of motion (112.7 ± 10.6 versus 114.6 ± 9.0°; P = 0.30), and lengths of stay (3.0 ± 1.5 versus 3.0 ± 1.8 days; P = 0.39) were comparable in younger and older patients. Younger patients were less often transferred to a rehabilitation facility (22.1 versus 36.9%; P = 0.03) and had a longer operative time (77.3 ± 30.2 versus 65.4 ± 17.7 minutes; P = 0.01). There were no pulmonary embolisms, cardiovascular events, or deaths.

CONCLUSION: Early complication rates after UKA were comparable in patients 80 years or older and in those younger than 60 years, despite a higher comorbidity burden in the older group. When the indication is appropriate, age alone should not preclude UKA.

articles.title: Employing Microelectrode Arrays and Optogenetics to Interrogate Neural Networks in Neurodegenerative Disease Organoid Models.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction or loss and are traditionally mechanistically studied in vivo by applying a variety of non-human model systems. Human stem cell-derived 2D and 3D neuronal cultures and organoids are emerging as valuable complementary systems for in vitro modeling of human disease-relevant processes at molecular, cellular and network-levels as they increasingly offer more detailed, physiologically relevant context. The ability to genetically manipulate and rapidly scale these platforms for high-throughput analysis and drug screening makes them a vital component for advancing new therapeutic interventions. Perhaps the greatest accelerators of these neural stem cell technologies are functional interrogation tools such as microelectrode arrays (MEAs), optical electrophysiology, and optogenetic stimulation, which are transforming how neuronal activity is measured and manipulated in vitro. This review explores how emerging tools for measuring connectivity, excitability, and synaptic dynamics are integrated into high temporal and spatial-resolution studies to connect molecular pathology to systems-level behavior and drive therapeutic discovery in neurodegenerative disease.

articles.title: Evidence and Consensus Based Imaging Guidelines in Ocular Syphilis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 21.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop imaging and consensus-based guidelines for the application of multimodal imaging in the diagnosis and management of ocular syphilis.

DESIGN: Consensus agreement guided by evidence-based literature and expert committee deliberation using nominal group technique (NGT).

PARTICIPANTS: International uveitis specialists and retina specialists participating in the Multimodal Imaging in Uveitis (MUV) taskforce.

METHODS: A subcommittee of experts formed by the MUV reviewed published literature on imaging in ocular syphilis and collected multimodal imaging datasets of serology-confirmed cases based on the Standardized Uveitis Nomenclature (SUN) criteria. Three clinical phenotypes of posterior uveitis were included: acute syphilitic posterior placoid chorioretinitis (ASPPC), syphilitic multifocal retinitis, and syphilitic necrotizing retinitis. Imaging modalities included color fundus photograph (CFP), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Through structured NGT sessions, the committee developed consensus-based descriptors of active and inactive syphilitic retinitis and imaging features associated with disease activity. The imaging guidelines were reviewed and voted upon by the full MUV taskforce.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Identification of globally acceptable multimodal imaging features of syphilitic retinitis; identification of modality-specific features of disease activity; consensus on the preferred imaging modalities for diagnosis and monitoring of disease activity and resolution.

RESULTS: The experts agreed that CFP, OCT and FAF were the most important diagnostic and follow-up imaging modalities for documenting pattern, extent, and borders of syphilitic lesions across all three disease phenotypes. CFP was helpful in identifying the characteristic morphological appearance of ASPPC, multifocal and necrotizing retinitis. In ASPPC, OCT demonstrates features of granular hyper-reflectivity of the retinal pigment epithelium with small nodular elevations, and a disrupted ellipsoid zone. FAF revealed more extensive hypo and hyper-autofluorescent areas of involvement than were clinically apparent on CFP, and these alterations regressed following initiation of treatment. FFA, ICGA and OCTA have limited role in diagnosing or assessing disease activity for all three phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: The MUV imaging guidelines for ocular syphilis extend existing diagnostic frameworks by systematically integrating multimodal imaging features for identification of specific phenotypes and for disease monitoring. CFP, FAF and OCT are important for detecting and monitoring of ASPPC, syphilitic multifocal retinitis, and syphilitic necrotizing retinitis.

articles.title: Dorsal Raphe Serotonergic Neurons at the Metabolic-Cognitive Interface: Converging Mechanisms, Causal Gaps, and Testable Predictions for Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Impairment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DACI) is clinically heterogeneous, yet the neural mechanism linking metabolic disturbance to selective cognitive-circuit dysfunction remains unresolved. We evaluated whether dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic neurons could form a metabolic-cognitive interface.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase and Scopus were searched from inception to 2 August 2026. We synthesised 62 full-text-verified original studies, assessing serotonergic identity, raphe source, projection specificity, transmitter/receptor mediation, causal directness and translational relevance.

RESULTS: DRN serotonergic populations are molecularly, physiologically and projectionally heterogeneous and integrate metabolic signals through afferents, GABAergic/glutamatergic circuitry and 5-HT1A feedback. Insulin has the strongest cell-defined support; evidence for leptin, GLP-1, ghrelin and orexin differs in causal resolution. Diabetes-associated changes in tissue 5-HT, SERT, receptor availability, evoked release and DRN excitability vary by region, stage, sex and model. DRN serotonergic pathways modulate hippocampal and prefrontal computations in non-diabetic models, but a complete diabetes-specific pathway from defined DRN remodelling to projection-selective dysfunction and cognition remains unproven.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports biological plausibility, not causal continuity. Three falsifiable predictions follow: (1) diabetes differentially alters metabolic responsiveness across molecularly and projection-defined DRN serotonergic populations; (2) abnormal responses to defined metabolic challenges precede persistent target-field serotonergic dysfunction and cognitive deficits; and (3) restoring state- and task-matched 5-HT dynamics in a verified diabetes-impaired DRN projection improves the relevant cognitive outcome without being explained by glycaemic, locomotor or affective changes. The framework guides mechanism-informed study design and exploratory biomarker evaluation, not validated diagnosis or DRN-targeted treatment.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy Patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prevalence of retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) in patients with central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) and to identify factors associated with their presence.

DESIGN: Observational cross-sectional study.

METHODS: Two hundred forty-five patients aged 18-60 years with active CSCR and 63 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were included. RIPLs were identified using high-resolution structural optical coherence tomography (OCT) and corresponding en face OCT projections. A RIPL was defined by focal inner nuclear layer thinning with corresponding outer plexiform layer elevation and topographic perivascular correspondence on en face OCT. The presence of at least one lesion in either eye classified a participant as RIPL-positive. Demographic, systemic, clinical, and imaging characteristics were analyzed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: RIPLs were identified in 85 of 245 patients with CSCR (34.7%) compared with 7 of 63 healthy controls (11.1%, P < 0.001). Bilateral RIPLs were present in 35 CSCR patients (14.3%) and 2 controls (3.2%, P = 0.028). CSCR patients with RIPLs were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had lower central retinal and subfoveal choroidal thicknesses than those without RIPLs (P < 0.05). Hypertension showed the strongest association with RIPLs presence in univariable analysis (OR 3.37, 95% CI, 1.74-6.54, P < 0.001) and remained the only independent factor in multivariable analysis (OR 2.66, 95% CI, 1.20-5.87, P = 0.016). Notably, among patients without diagnosed hypertension, RIPLs prevalence remained significantly higher than in controls (24.1% vs. 11.1%, P = 0.035).

CONCLUSION: RIPLs are highly prevalent in patients with CSCR, potentially reflecting an increased burden of cardiovascular risk factors in this cohort. This finding warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Blood pressure changes throughout pregnancy as predictors of preeclampsia: a prospective cohort study of low-risk nulliparous individuals.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
articles.abstract: Among 835 nulliparous patients who were seen once at each trimester, systolic, diastolic and mean arterial blood pressure (MAP), measured twice on both arms using an automated device after >5 minutes of rest, were stronger predictors of preeclampsia than clinical factors (P < 0.01). At 30-34 weeks, a MAP above 90 mmHg or an increase in MAP of more than 10 mmHg (compared to 11-14 weeks) could have predicted 67% (20/30) of preeclampsia cases, including all (7/7) deliveries with preeclampsia between 32 and 37 weeks. Measuring blood pressure using an automated device and following a rigorous protocol is highly effective to predict preeclampsia at each trimester of pregnancy.

articles.title: Mixed Tocotrienols in Noncirrhotic Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease- A Multicentre Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective and safe therapies for noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether oral mixed tocotrienols supplementation reduces liver fat content in adults with noncirrhotic MASLD.

METHODS: Multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial conducted between January 2021 and August 2023 at two public hospitals and three primary care clinics in Malaysia. Adults with metabolic risk factors and imaging-confirmed hepatic steatosis were enrolled. Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either mixed tocotrienols, 200mg twice daily (n=89) vs matching placebo (n=81) for 12 months. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants achieving a ≥30% relative reduction in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (PDFF) at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included changes in mean volume liver fat fraction and metabolic biomarkers.

RESULTS: All the 170 were included in the primary analysis (mean [SD] age, 46 [11] years; 60% male). At 12 months, 20 out of 89 patients (22.5%) in the tocotrienols group and 11 out of 81 patients (13.6%) in the placebo group achieved a ≥30% reduction in PDFF (relative risk [RR], 1.30; 95%CI, 0.95-1.77; P=0.134). The mean PDFF decreased modestly with tocotrienols compared with placebo (between-group difference, -3.05%; 95%CI, -5.40% to -0.18%; P=0.036). Metabolic markers and adverse events were similar between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Oral mixed tocotrienols supplementation did not achieve the ≥30% relative reduction in liver fat fraction in adults with noncirrhotic MASLD. However, the observed modest reductions in mean MRI-based measures were exploratory, requiring further evaluation in a larger trial.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04704063 CLINICAL TRIAL NO: T3-NAFL-01-2019 CLINICALTRIALS.GOV: NCT04704063.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of initiating nifedipine versus labetalol in early gestation for chronic hypertension in pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Following the Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP) trial, clinical guidelines were changed to recommend pharmacologic treatment of both mild and severe chronic hypertension during pregnancy. However, uncertainty remains regarding the comparative safety and effectiveness of commonly used first-line agents, nifedipine and labetalol. Evidence from randomized trials is limited, and ongoing trials may have restricted generalizability to real-world populations. Prior observational studies have largely restricted analyses to pregnancies ending in delivery, potentially introducing selection bias and precluding evaluation of miscarriage, an important but understudied outcome. Robust real-world evidence that captures the full spectrum of pregnancy outcomes is therefore needed to inform clinical decision-making.

OBJECTIVES: We conducted a target trial emulation to compare nifedipine versus labetalol initiation before 23 weeks' gestation for risk of pregnancy loss (miscarriage or stillbirth) and preterm birth (<37 weeks) among a cohort of pregnancies with observed (e.g., live birth, spontaneous abortion) and unobserved (i.e., lost to follow-up) outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: We used a novel algorithm to identify pregnancies in the Merative MarketScan Commercial Claims and Encounters Database with estimated last menstrual periods between July 1, 2016 and February 1, 2022. We included those with a new nifedipine or labetalol fill before 23 weeks' gestation. We estimated risks, risk differences (RDs) per 100 pregnancies, and risk ratios (RRs) among nifedipine versus labetalol initiators using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator to account for confounding, informative censoring, and competing risks. We also conducted a post hoc analysis to estimate the comparative effect of nifedipine versus labetalol on risk of preeclampsia. We considered multiple sensitivity analyses to evaluate the robustness of our primary results to assumptions regarding informative censoring, gestational age misestimation, residual confounding, outcome misclassification, target population misspecification, and measurement error in censoring dates.

RESULTS: We identified 987 nifedipine and 4,570 labetalol initiators during the study period; 22.2% of nifedipine and 10.0% of labetalol initiators filled a prescription for a different antihypertensive over follow-up. The weighted risk of pregnancy loss was 7.0% among nifedipine and 6.0% among labetalol initiators (RD=1.1 [-0.7, 2.8]; RR=1.18 [0.87, 1.59]). Weighted risks of preterm birth were 29.4% versus 22.2%, respectively (RD=7.2 [3.9, 10.5], RR=1.32 [1.13, 1.55]). In post hoc analyses, the weighted risks of preeclampsia were 38.6% versus 33.9%, respectively (RD=4.7 [0.7, 8.7], RR=1.14 [1.01, 1.28]). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared to labetalol initiators, nifedipine initiators experienced an increased risk of preterm birth but not pregnancy loss. The elevated risk of preterm birth may be explained by an increased risk of preeclampsia among nifedipine initiators, resulting in medically indicated preterm birth. These findings may reflect differences in adherence, patient characteristics, or clinical context in real-world practice and should be interpreted alongside existing trial evidence supporting the use of either medication.

articles.title: Association between the platelet to lymphocyte ratio and the clinical outcome of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinical outcomes in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using appropriate tools, and pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects model with sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Ten studies involving patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage were included. The meta-analysis showed that a higher platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio was associated with an increased likelihood of poor functional outcome. In contrast, no clear association was observed between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and delayed cerebral ischemia in the pooled analysis. The odds ratios for pneumonia and deep vein thrombosis each came from a single independent study rather than from pooled meta-analytic analyses; these unpooled estimates therefore remain exploratory and should not be interpreted as combined effect sizes. Substantial heterogeneity was present across analyses, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the results for functional outcome and delayed cerebral ischemia were not entirely stable. The available evidence is limited by the small number of studies, heterogeneity in threshold values and outcome definitions, and geographic concentration of the included populations. In conclusion, the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio may serve as a readily available prognostic marker in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, but current evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Further large, well-designed multinational studies are needed to establish optimal thresholds and to clarify its incremental value in prognostic assessment.

articles.title: Comparison of anti-hyperuricemic activity of berberine and metformin: Insight from de novo purine biosynthesis and purine metabolism and intestinal microbiome.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence has shown that the worldwide epidemic of metabolic disease including hyperuricemia (HUA) correlates with an elevation in serum uric acid (UA) as well as a marked increase in total fructose intake. Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex (PC) is a traditional medicinal material used to treat metabolic diseases including gout and HUA. Berberine (BBR), the main component of PC, possesses anti-HUA and anti-gout effects. Metformin is widely used for the treatment of metabolic syndrome. However, their effect on HUA induced by high-fructose remained unexplored. The present work endeavored to explore the anti-HUA potential of BBR and metformin on high-fructose-induced hyperuricemic rats focusing on intestinal microbiota, de novo purine biosynthesis (DNPB) of endogenous purine, purine cycle and metabolism and intestinal microbiota. Results indicated that BBR and metformin remarkably decreased the high levels of UA, creatinine, and urea induced by a long-term high-fructose diet. BBR and metformin activated the expression of ketohexokinase (KHK) and suppressed the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) to regulate fructose metabolism. Following that, BBR and metformin suppressed the activated DNPB induced by high-fructose, through which a great number of purine synthesis was inhibited. Besides, BBR promoted the purine salvage pathway (PSP) and suppressed the expression of xanthine oxidase (XOD) to inhibit the purine metabolism, resulting in the increase of inosine and decrease of IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, and accelerating the purine cycle. Metformin decreased the levels of inosine, IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, inhibiting purine cycle and metabolism. Additionally, BBR and metformin favorably modulated the species of gut microbiota, regulated intestinal purine absorption and excretion, decreased the intestinal purine contents and increased the fecal uricase and allantoinase concentration to recover UA catabolism. Our study revealed that BBR and metformin had outstanding anti-HUA effect, which was intimately associated with suppression of PPP, DNPB and XOD in the liver and modulation of the intestinal microbiota. BBR and metformin deserved to provide a preclinical basis for further investigation for the treatment of HUA.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Use and Risk of Liver Disease Progression and Decompensation in Metabolic Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Clinics and research in hepatology and gastroenterology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) are major contributors to cirrhosis. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated benefits in obesity and type 2 diabetes and may reduce liver disease progression. This study evaluated the association between GLP-1 RA use and liver disease progression in patients with metabolic liver disease.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with obesity or type 2 diabetes and a diagnosis of MASLD or MASH treated at a single academic center from 2017 to 2024. Patients were stratified by GLP-1 RA exposure. Outcomes included progression to cirrhosis and hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis. Multivariable analyses adjusted for age, sex, race, rurality, and comorbidity burden.

RESULTS: A total of 2,851 patients were included, of whom 852 received GLP-1 RAs and 1,999 did not. GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower rates of progression to cirrhosis and hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis. Progression to cirrhosis occurred in 216 GLP-1 RA users (25.4%, 95% CI: [22.5%, 28.4%]) and 588 non-users (29.4%, 95% CI: [27.5%, 31.5%]). Hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis occurred in 44 GLP-1 RA users (5.2%, 95% CI: [3.9%, 6.9%]) and 218 non-users (10.9%, 95% CI: [9.6%, 12.3%]). In adjusted analyses, GLP-1 RA use remained independently associated with a reduced risk of hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis (OR 0.54, 95% CI: [0.38-0.76], p=0.0004). A propensity score-weighted sensitivity analysis yielded a similar estimate (OR = 0.56, 95% CI: [0.39, 0.81], p=0.0022). Rural patients experienced higher rates of disease progression, although the association between GLP-1 RA use and improved outcomes was observed across geographic groups.

CONCLUSION: GLP-1 RA use was associated with reduced progression of metabolic liver disease and lower rates of hospitalization for decompensated cirrhosis. Further prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Sotatercept Improves AI Detected Electrocardiographic Signature of Pulmonary Hypertension.
Pulmonary Function Estimation from Opportunistic Chest CT Using a Hybrid Image-plus-Quantitative-Feature Deep Learning Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 80% or FVC < 80% predicted) was assessed with sensitivity, specificity and AUROC, and agreement with the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC).

RESULTS: The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV1/FVC < 0.70; CCC 0.62) and in a low-FVC, preserved-ratio pattern (CCC 0.70-0.78).

INTERPRETATION: The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: COPDGene, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT00608764.

articles.title: A real-world study of predictive factors of pulmonary rehabilitation in patients with severe COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Uptake of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in COPD patients is low. This study evaluated the use of PR in patients with severe COPD and identified predictive factors of participation in a PR program.

METHODS: A post hoc analysis of data from a large cohort of patients with severe COPD (FEV1< 50% predicted) included in a cross-sectional multicenter study conducted in Spain. The characteristics of patients referred to PR were compared to those of non-participants in a PR program. Variables independently associated with referral PR program were evaluated using bivariate analysis and a logistic regression model.

RESULTS: Of the total 4800 patients, 2080 (43%) were receiving non-pharmacological treatment, with 482 (23%) of them enrolled in a PR program. The uptake rate of PR was 10%. COPD-related variables significantly associated with referral to PR included poor COPD control, two or more exacerbations in the past year, degree of dyspnea, and degree of airflow impairment. Education and psychological support, nutritional treatment, tobacco cessation support, CPAP, home oxygen therapy, and domiciliary assisted ventilation were significantly associated with referral to PR. Other significant variables: ex-smoking condition, good/moderate adherence to inhaled therapy, living in an urban/semiurban area, and receiving specialized care by a pulmonologist.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world study of severe COPD patients, the uptake of PR was only 10%. Educational and psychological support together with nutritional treatment and smoking cessation support should be emphasized as these factors were significant predictors of PR. Overall, PR is underutilized and concentrated in patients with more severe airflow impairment.

articles.title: Recurrent enteral feeding intolerance and in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients: a time-updated analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between time-updated enteral feeding intolerance (EFI) states and in-hospital mortality in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed adults receiving mechanical ventilation who remained in the ICU for at least 3 days. EFI was assessed daily during Nutrition Days 1-7. Patients initially contributed person-time to the no-EFI state, entered the first-EFI state on the first qualifying EFI day, and entered the recurrent-EFI state on the second qualifying day. In-hospital death was the event, and alive discharge was censored. The primary Cox model adjusted for age, sex, APACHE II score, and septic shock, included an APACHE II score-by-log(time + 1) interaction, was stratified by baseline AKI, and used patient-level cluster-robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Among 447 patients, 132 died in hospital. By final cumulative status, 248 (55.5%) had no EFI, 68 (15.2%) had single-day EFI, and 131 (29.3%) had recurrent EFI. In the time-updated Model A, no independent association was observed between the first-EFI state and in-hospital mortality (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 0.66-1.90). The recurrent-EFI state was associated with higher mortality than the no-EFI state (aHR 2.30, 95% CI 1.55-3.43) and the first-EFI state (aHR 2.06, 95% CI 1.20-3.54). One-day-lag analysis retained the recurrent-versus-no-EFI association, whereas the recurrent-versus-first-EFI contrast was nonsignificant.

CONCLUSION: The recurrent-EFI state was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, although its contrast with first EFI was sensitive to exposure timing. Recurrent EFI may serve as a longitudinal marker for clinical reassessment, although residual confounding and the composite EFI definition preclude causal interpretation.

articles.title: Early phosphate repletion and ventilator-free days in hypophosphatemic critical illness: a target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypophosphatemia is common in critical illness, but whether prompt phosphate repletion improves patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of phosphate repletion within 12 hours of incident hypophosphatemia on 28-day ventilator-free days.

METHODS: In this target trial emulation using MIMIC-IV 3.0, adults during their first ICU stay with an initial serum phosphate concentration <2.5 mg/dL within 48 hours of ICU admission were eligible. Treatment strategies were repletion within 12 hours versus no repletion within that grace period, with follow-up beginning at the 12-hour landmark. Stabilized inverse probability weighting was used to estimate average treatment effects on the primary outcome of 28-day ventilator-free days.

RESULTS: Among 14,823 eligible patients, 6,995 received early repletion and 7,828 did not. Weighted covariate balance was adequate, with a maximum absolute standardized mean difference of 0.059. Early phosphate repletion did not improve 28-day ventilator-free days (MD -0.12 days, 95% CI -0.43 to 0.18, p = 0.424), ICU-free days, mortality, or renal replacement therapy. Among patients with repeat phosphate measurements, early repletion was associated with higher odds of phosphate normalization (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.24-1.50) and hyperphosphatemia (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.76).

CONCLUSION: In this target trial emulation of critically ill adults, early phosphate repletion promoted biochemical normalization without improving patient-centered outcomes, suggesting selective rather than routine early repletion.

articles.title: Arrhythmia-specific timing of first detection during extended textile ECG monitoring: a recording-level cumulative incidence analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extended ambulatory electrocardiographic monitoring improves detection of intermittent arrhythmias, but real-world recordings often have variable duration, and conventional diagnostic-yield curves may not account for censoring.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 9629 anonymized ambulatory ECG recordings of at least 24 h acquired in routine clinical practice between 2018 and 2024. Endpoints were first ECG-defined detection of atrial fibrillation (AF) burden ≤1% and ≤ 10%, non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (nsVT), pauses >3 s, bradycardia <40 beats/min for ≥60 s, and premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden >10%. Arrhythmias were algorithm-flagged and staff-verified. Kaplan-Meier estimates were used to derive day-30-normalized cumulative incidence functions (CIF*).

RESULTS: Arrhythmias of interest were detected in 3611 recordings (37.5%). Median observed monitoring duration was 15.4 days (interquartile range 8.2-28.2). At day 14, CIF* was 65.8% for AF burden ≤1%, 71.0% for AF burden ≤10%, and 71.1% for nsVT, indicating continued first detections during days 14-30. In contrast, PVC burden >10% accumulated early, with CIF* of 59.6% at 24 h and 71.5% at 5 days.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large recording-level cohort, first ECG-defined detection timing differed by arrhythmia target. Low-burden AF and nsVT continued to accrue after day 14, whereas frequent PVC burden was usually identified earlier. These findings support target-specific monitoring strategies, while clinical actionability could not be assessed in this anonymized variable-duration dataset.

articles.title: PECAM-1 as an endothelial gateway for vascular-targeted drug delivery: structural basis, mechanotransduction, and translational opportunities.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule-1 (PECAM-1/CD31) is a junctional adhesion and signaling receptor that is abundant on vascular endothelium and is also expressed on platelets and several leukocyte populations. It regulates leukocyte transendothelial migration, endothelial barrier function, mechanotransduction, platelet inhibitory signaling, and angiogenesis. Its abundant luminal expression and accessibility from the bloodstream have also made PECAM-1 an attractive target for vascular drug delivery and biomaterial engineering. This Review examines the structural features, extracellular interactions, and intracellular signaling mechanisms that determine PECAM-1 targetability. We further discuss its roles in vascular inflammation, atherosclerosis, ischemic injury, thrombosis, hematologic disorders, and cancer, distinguishing receptor blockade or activation from PECAM-1 targeted cargo delivery. Particular attention is given to delivery design, including epitope selection, ligand format, multivalency, carrier properties, intracellular trafficking, luminal anchoring, and cargo-specific requirements. We also evaluate translational factors that may determine targeting performance, including administration route, pharmacokinetics, species differences, disease-associated changes in the vascular microenvironment, manufacturing reproducibility, and patient variability. Together, current evidence supports PECAM-1 as a functional vascular receptor, an endothelial delivery address, and a bioactive interface for vascular devices, while emphasizing that successful translation requires careful matching of target biology, delivery design, therapeutic cargo, and disease context.

articles.title: Immune alterations in recent-onset psychosis: a combined analysis using cerebrospinal fluid samples and [18F]DPA-714 imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune dysfunction is hypothesised to underlie psychotic disorders. To test this, we assessed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytokine levels and their relationship with symptoms and a brain imaging marker of 18-kDa translocator protein (TSPO), a protein highly expressed by microglia in neuroinflammatory conditions.

METHODS: A case-control study was performed including patients with schizophrenia or related psychotic disorders with <5 years of illness duration and psychotic symptoms despite antipsychotic treatment, and matched healthy volunteers. All participants received clinical interviews and lumbar punctures, with 84% also receiving [18F]DPA-714 positron emission tomography (PET) scans to quantify relative cortical grey matter TSPO levels. CSF levels of IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, TNF-α were measured.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients and 25 healthy controls participated. Patients had significantly higher CSF levels of TNF-α (p < 0.001), IL-8 (p = 0.015), IL-10 (p = 0.032), and IL-13 (p = 0.002) relative to controls with moderate to large effect sizes. There were no significant correlations between symptom measures and CSF cytokine levels after correcting for multiple comparisons (all p > 0.05). Furthermore, CSF cytokine levels were not associated with PET TSPO levels in cortical grey matter regions (all p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Early course schizophrenia is associated with generalised dysregulation of CSF cytokines, consistent with immune dysregulation in psychosis. The lack of association with PET TSPO levels suggests this is unlikely to be related to microglial changes.

CLINICALTRIALS: gov: NCT03093064.

articles.title: The Effect of Albumin in Decompensated Cirrhosis Depends on the Indication: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Intravenous albumin is widely used in decompensated cirrhosis, but its efficacy across clinical indications remains inconsistent. Therefore, we evaluated the effect of albumin on mortality, major complications, and safety separately for each indication.

METHODS: We searched PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science from inception to December 2025. Primary analyses included only randomized trials in which albumin was the randomized contrast; within each indication, comparisons with standard care or placebo were analyzed separately from comparisons with an alternative plasma expander. Non-randomized studies were analyzed separately. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) were calculated.

RESULTS: Thirty-two studies were included (27 randomized); 22 randomized trials with 3,582 participants reported mortality. Albumin reduced mortality in spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP; 2 trials; RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.26-0.77) and hepatic encephalopathy (3 trials; 0.54; 0.35-0.83), but not in large-volume paracentesis (8 trials; 0.86; 0.65-1.13), long-term administration for ascites (3 trials; 0.93; 0.72-1.19), or infection other than SBP (5 trials; 0.97; 0.83-1.12); the test for differences between indications was significant (P=0.003). Findings were similar in a single trial of hospitalized patients. After paracentesis, albumin reduced paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction (0.46; 0.35-0.61), hyponatremia (0.47; 0.31-0.72), and acute kidney injury (0.63; 0.43-0.93); in SBP it reduced renal impairment (0.28; 0.15-0.51). Pulmonary complications were more frequent with albumin (5 trials; 2.66; 1.62-4.39). The secondary estimate combining indications was 0.89 (0.78-1.01; 95% prediction interval, 0.64-1.22).

CONCLUSIONS: The effect of albumin in decompensated cirrhosis is indication-specific, with a survival benefit demonstrated only in SBP and hepatic encephalopathy and more frequent pulmonary complications across indications, supporting indication-based use with monitoring for fluid overload.

articles.title: Therapeutic effects of low-frequency renal nerve neuromodulation in a preclinical model of obesity-induced hypertension.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated hypertension is increasingly prevalent and often resistant to pharmacological treatment. The renal nerve is a promising target for neuromodulation due to its critical role in blood pressure (BP) regulation. This study investigated the efficacy and physiological impact of low-frequency renal nerve stimulation (RNS) in Zucker fatty rats (ZFRs), a preclinical model of obesity-induced hypertension. Thirteen anesthetized male ZFRs underwent surgical implantation of bipolar stimulating electrodes on the left renal nerve. RNS was applied at 2.5 Hz and 5.0 Hz (0.5 mA, 0.5 ms, 30 s) while continuously recording mean arterial pressure (MAP), heart rate (HR), hindquarter flow (HQF), and ipsilateral and contralateral renal cortical perfusion (RCP). Hindquarter resistance (HQR) and renal cortical resistance (RCR) were calculated from MAP and corresponding flow values. Baseline MAP was 115 ± 5 mmHg. RNS at both frequencies produced immediate reductions in MAP (2.5 Hz: 29 ± 6 mmHg; 5.0 Hz: 30 ± 6 mmHg) without significant changes in HR. Both frequencies similarly increased HQF, with a corresponding decrease in HQR. Ipsilateral RCP was reduced at both frequencies, with a greater decrease observed at 5.0 Hz. RCR was reduced to a similar extent on both sides at both frequencies, with contralateral RCP significantly reduced only at 2.5 Hz. Low-frequency RNS effectively lowers BP in ZFRs possibly via reflex-mediated vasodilation. Reductions in renal vascular resistance despite reduced flow likely reflect compensatory renal vasodilation. Importantly, the 2.5 Hz protocol achieved similar BP-lowering effects with a smaller impact on renal perfusion, supporting its potential as a safer neuromodulatory strategy in obesity-related hypertension.

articles.title: ICU Admission and Mortality in Thyroid Storm and Impending Thyroid Storm: A 15-Year Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the demographics, clinical features, and outcomes of patients with thyroid storm and impending thyroid storm at a single center, as well as identify features associated with severe disease and mortality. We also compared clinical characteristics and outcomes between patients with impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients age 18 years or older with a clinical diagnosis of thyroid storm or impending thyroid storm at two affiliated tertiary academic hospitals between 2006 and 2021. The primary outcome was characteristics associated with a composite outcome of ICU admission or death.

RESULTS: Among 106 patients, atrial fibrillation (OR 4.09; 95% CI 1.21 to 13.85; p=.02) and acute respiratory failure (OR 22.18; 95% CI 2.29 to 215.19; p=.008) were significantly associated with ICU admission or death. Fever (p=.02) and acute respiratory failure (p=.03) differed significantly between the impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm groups.

CONCLUSION: This cohort is among the largest single-center studies of thyroid storm reported in the United States. Atrial fibrillation and acute respiratory failure were significantly associated with ICU admission or death. Acute respiratory failure also differed significantly between impending thyroid storm and thyroid storm groups, suggesting that pulmonary complications, although not included in existing diagnostic criteria, may indicate more severe disease and poorer outcomes.

articles.title: Health literacy as a determinant of cardiovascular health and outcomes.
articles.abstract: Despite remarkable advances in cardiovascular prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, substantial gaps persist between evidence-based recommendations and real-world clinical outcomes. Health literacy is an important, yet frequently overlooked and potentially modifiable, determinant of cardiovascular health.
