Limited health literacy contributes to suboptimal risk-factor control, reduced treatment adherence, delayed recognition of cardiovascular symptoms, and adverse clinical outcomes. There is a need to move beyond the traditional view of health literacy as an individual patient characteristic. Healthcare professionals and healthcare systems need to make cardiovascular information easily accessible, understandable, and actionable. Health literacy has the potential to reduce cardiovascular inequalities and can help address the challenges posed by digital healthcare and misinformation. Practical strategies are highlighted for integrating health-literacy principles into routine cardiovascular care. Health literacy should be regarded not merely as a patient education initiative, but as an actionable component of cardiovascular care quality, with the potential to improve treatment adherence, risk-factor control, and ultimately cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Causes of overall mortality among patients with invasive cutaneous melanoma ≤1.0 mm in Breslow thickness: A SEER analysis.

articles.title: Effects of long-term polyethylene terephthalate microplastic exposure on anaerobic digestion: microbial community and antibiotic resistance dynamics.
articles.abstract: Microplastics are increasingly introduced into anaerobic digestion (AD) systems, yet their long-term effects on microbial succession and antibiotic resistance dynamics remain unclear. Here, a 120-day semicontinuous AD experiment investigated the effects of polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) on digestion performance, microbial communities, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and quorum sensing (QS)-related genes. By day 120, PET-MPs increased cumulative methane yield by 13% and enhanced volatile solids removal after an initial adaptation period. Microbial community succession was characterized by a shift from communities enriched in Bacillota and Bacteroidota toward those with higher relative abundances of Pseudomonadota and Actinomycetota. A total of 971 ARG subtypes and 649 MGE subtypes were detected. ARG and MGE richness decreased by 9.3-9.8% and 21.3-23.6%, respectively, during long-term operation, accompanied by increased evenness, while multidrug resistance became more prominent during late-stage operation. Microbial β-diversity was strongly correlated with ARG β-diversity (R2 = 0.95, p < 0.01) and MGE β-diversity (R2 = 0.93, p < 0.01). PET-MPs exposure was also associated with transient changes in QS-related genes and altered bacterial-ARG-QS associations. Overall, long-term PET-MPs exposure was associated with coordinated restructuring of microbial communities, ARGs, and MGEs, highlighting microbial community succession as an important ecological context for resistome and mobilome dynamics during prolonged microplastic exposure.

articles.title: Comparing NfL, GFAP and total tau in tear fluid and plasma from participants with Huntington's disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Huntington's disease (HD) is a neurodegenerative disorder for which reliable biomarkers are increasingly important to monitor disease progression and treatment response. Although biomarkers can be measured in cerebrospinal fluid and blood, tear fluid may provide an additional non-invasive matrix suitable for repeated sampling. This study investigated the feasibility of measuring neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and total tau (t-tau) in tear fluid and explored their relationship with corresponding plasma concentrations and HD disease progression.

METHODS: Tear fluid and plasma samples were obtained from 73 participants, including manifest HD participants (n = 18), premanifest HD participants (n = 23), and controls (n = 32). Tear fluid was collected using Schirmer's strips. NfL,GFAP and t-tau concentrations were quantified using the S-PLEX Neurology Panel 1 Human electrochemiluminescence immunoassay.

RESULTS: Detectability of all biomarkers in tear fluid was high, with GFAP and t-tau detectable in all samples (100%) and NfL in most samples (range 87% in premanifest to 100% in manifest participants). Tear fluid biomarker concentrations did not differ significantly between groups and showed generally limited discriminatory performance. Plasma NfL was significantly elevated in manifest HD compared with premanifest HD and controls and showed good-to-excellent discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.895 and 0.923, respectively). Across groups, plasma NfL and GFAP concentrations were higher than in tear fluid, whereas t-tau concentrations were substantially higher in tear fluid. These differences were confirmed in participants with paired tear fluid and plasma samples (n = 53; all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: NfL, GFAP, and t-tau were highly detectable in tear fluid, but showed limited ability to distinguish between HD disease groups. Further research is required to determine the clinical utility of tear fluid biomarkers in HD monitoring.

articles.title: An Adverse Outcome Pathway-Based Hierarchical Ensemble Framework for Mechanistic Hazard Identification of Drug-Induced Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Drug-induced heart failure arises through multiple molecular initiating events and key events that conventional single-endpoint approaches cannot capture. We developed a four-tier adverse outcome pathway (AOP)-based hierarchical ensemble framework encoding the AOP 558 causal chain-phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D) inhibition, cAMP elevation and calcium dysregulation, and heart failure-into tier-specific prediction models. Hierarchical here refers to the AOP tier structure (MIE-KE1-KE2-AO), not cross-tier stacking. By integrating multi-source public databases, four molecular fingerprints, and six algorithms, the tier-specific consensus models achieved AUC values of 0.920-0.990 in internal validation. External validation on the FDA DICTrank reference list yielded an AUC of 0.667 (vs. 0.5), an accuracy of 75.9% (below the 84.0% majority-class baseline), and a sensitivity of 26.5% (9/34). SHAP analysis identified tier-specific structural features associated with PDE4D binding, cAMP signaling, and calcium homeostasis. This framework supports tier-level mechanistic hazard characterization of drug-induced heart failure.

articles.title: Chimeric antigen receptor-modified regulatory T cells: A new frontier for precision immunotherapy in autoimmune diseases.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases arise from a disruption of immune tolerance, leading to the persistent and pathological activation of autoreactive T and B cells. Although therapies based on regulatory T cells (Tregs) hold great promise for restoring immune homeostasis, their clinical application has been limited by insufficient antigen specificity and the risk of broad-spectrum immunosuppression. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) engineering has emerged as a powerful strategy to overcome these limitations, enabling Tregs to acquire antigen-specific recognition capabilities and perform targeted suppression independent of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) restriction. This article reviews research progress on CAR-Tregs in autoimmune diseases, analyzing their structural design, the role of gene editing in enhancing stability and persistence, and the molecular mechanisms of immunosuppression. Additionally, this review summarizes preclinical evidence from models of type 1 diabetes, multiple sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease, highlighting the potential of this approach to alter disease progression. Furthermore, the current status of early-phase clinical trials in the fields of transplantation and autoimmune diseases is examined, with a focus on safety and feasibility data. Finally, barriers to clinical translation, such as phenotypic instability and challenges in large-scale production ，are identified, and future directions including modular CARs, universal products, in vivo engineering, and combination therapies are proposed. Overall, this review underscores the transformative potential of CAR-Tregs as a precision immunotherapy for autoimmune diseases, while emphasizing that clinical evidence remains at an early stage.

articles.title: Evaluating the Feasibility of Cultural Dance as an Integrative Therapeutic Movement Intervention for Parkinson's Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the feasibility of hula, Hawai'i's indigenous dance, as a dance-based therapeutic intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD).

BACKGROUND: Therapeutic dance programs have demonstrated physical and psychosocial benefits for individuals with PD. Hula has been studied as an intervention for chronic conditions such as hypertension and cardiovascular disease, however, its feasibility for PD has not been explored. This study evaluated hula as a therapeutic dance intervention for people with PD.

METHODS: A three-month hula program was developed using patient and public involvement, with guidance from Hawaiian cultural experts, in collaboration with Dance for PD®. A kumu hula (hula educator) translated this feedback into a curriculum and led weekly one-hour classes. People with PD were recruited through clinical and community outreach. Primary outcomes assessed feasibility through practicality, safety, and qualitative feedback. Secondary outcomes included pre-and post-intervention measures of the 39-item Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire (PDQ-39) and Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale-Part III (UPDRS-III).

RESULTS: Eighteen participants enrolled, and 11 completed the intervention. Mean attendance was 77.6%. One adverse event occurred, unrelated to class activities and without significant complication. PDQ-39 scores showed minimal change, while average UPDRS-III scores decreased by 4.18 points. Qualitative interviews suggested improvements in mood, motivation, social connectedness, and self-confidence. Participants described hula as cognitively engaging, as it integrates choreography with storytelling, illustrating historical and poetic references in traditional Hawaiian songs and chants.

CONCLUSION: Hula was feasible, safe, and well-received as a culturally grounded therapeutic dance intervention for individuals with PD, supporting further investigation in larger controlled studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06543810.

articles.title: Tuina for post‑stroke depression: a pilot randomized controlled trial of clinical effects and exploratory mechanisms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Accumulating evidence suggests that Tuina therapy(TT) may ameliorate post‑stroke depression (PSD) through modulation of the hypothalamic‑pituitary‑adrenal (HPA) axis and inflammatory responses, though its principal therapeutic mechanism remains unconfirmed. This pilot mechanistic trial aimed to investigate whether Tuina affects HPA‑axis hormones and inflammatory cytokines in patients with PSD, and to explore whether cortisol reduction mediates the observed antidepressant effect.

METHODS: In this 2‑week, randomized, assessor‑blind, active‑controlled trial, 42 patients with PSD were assigned to receive Tuina (n=21) or cognitive behavioral therapy(CBT) (n=21). The primary outcome was change in 17‑item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD‑17). Secondary outcomes included Modified Barthel Index (MBI), Fugl‑Meyer Assessment (FMA), Mini‑Mental State Examination (MMSE), and serum biomarkers (adrenocorticotropic hormone, cortisol, and inflammatory cytokines). Data were analyzed by intention‑to‑treat using non‑parametric tests and bootstrap mediation analysis.

RESULTS: Both groups improved significantly in HAMD‑17 and MBI (p<0.01). The TT group showed greater HAMD‑17 reduction (median Δ: -5.00 vs. -4.00; p<0.001) and greater reductions in ACTH (p=0.023) and cortisol (p=0.021) than the CBT group. No significant between‑group differences were observed for FMA, MMSE, or any inflammatory cytokine. Cortisol reduction mediated 19.4% of the HAMD‑17 improvement (indirect effect: 0.2867, 95% CI: 0.0337‑0.5975).

CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot mechanistic trial, Tuina produced significant downregulation of HPA axis activity, with cortisol partially mediating antidepressant effects. Direct systemic anti‑inflammatory effects were not observed. These findings suggest that HPA axis regulation is a key pathway contributing to the antidepressant effects of Tuina.

TRIALREGISTRATION: China Clinical Trial Registry Identifier ChiCTR2400085211.

articles.title: Celastrol partially restores Prodh expression in oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-injured astrocytes: A candidate mechanism relevant to ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke (IS) is an acute cerebrovascular disease caused by obstruction of the cerebral arteries, which deprives brain tissue of oxygen and glucose. This deprivation perturbs endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis and activates the unfolded protein response (UPR). When ER stress (ERS) is severe or sustained, the UPR can no longer restore homeostasis and cell injury ensues. Celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpene compound derived from Tripterygium wilfordii, a medicinal plant used in traditional Chinese medicine, alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by regulating astrocyte function. However, whether celastrol can treat IS by relieving ERS remains unclear.

METHOD: Bulk transcriptomic (GSE202659) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; GSE233812) datasets were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis, functional enrichment analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, random-forest, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were used to identify candidate gene of celastrol in IS. scRNA-seq analysis was then applied to examine the cell-type distribution of these genes and the biological functions of the astrocytes in which they act.

RESULTS: Integrated analysis suggested that Prodh is a candidate ERS-related gene predominantly expressed in astrocytes. In cultured astrocytes subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), Prodh mRNA was downregulated, and celastrol treatment partially restored its expression; this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability in the CCK-8 assay. In addition, scRNA-seq analysis revealed that Prodh expression decreased at days 1 and 3 after IS and increased by day 7.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify Prodh as a candidate gene in astrocytes after ischemic stroke. Celastrol partially restored Prodh expression in OGD/R-injured astrocytes, and this restoration was accompanied by improved cell viability , which supports further investigation into the functional significance of this restoration.

articles.title: Identifying Undiagnosed Diabetes and Mortality Risk in Hypertensive Patients: Development and Web Deployment of a Clinical Screening Tool.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension substantially increases diabetes risk, yet routine screening with fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) may miss early cases. This study evaluated the additional diagnostic and prognostic value of oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) in hypertensive patients. A predictive model was also developed to identify high-risk individuals for targeted OGTT screening.

METHODS: A cross‑sectional analysis with linked mortality data was conducted using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 2005‑2016). A two-stage screening (FPG/HbA1c, then OGTT) was applied. The association between isolated OGTT positivity (2-h PG ≥11.1 mmol/L with normal FPG/HbA1c) and all-cause mortality was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. A nomogram for predicting isolated OGTT positivity was developed, internally validated, and benchmarked against machine learning algorithms. An interactive online calculator was deployed.

RESULTS: Among initially screen-negative hypertensive patients, OGTT identified previously undiagnosed diabetes in 5.81%, a rate 4-fold higher than in non-hypertensives (P<0.001). Isolated OGTT positivity was independently associated with a 48% increased risk of all-cause mortality​ (HR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.06-2.06). The prediction nomogram, which incorporates four routine variables (age, FPG, HbA1c, and the triglyceride-glucose index [TyG]), demonstrated strong discrimination, with a C-index of 0.798 in internal validation. It performed comparably to four machine learning algorithms while offering superior clinical interpretability. A web-based calculator was also provided for implementation.

CONCLUSION: In hypertensive patients with normal FPG/HbA1c, supplementary OGTT identifies a substantial burden of undiagnosed diabetes that is linked to increased mortality. The nomogram (using age, FPG, HbA1c, and TyG) enables clinicians to selectively target OGTT to high-risk individuals, potentially improving risk-stratified screening.

articles.title: Effect of a Nurse-Led Intervention on Self-Management and Pregnancy Outcomes in Women With Gestational Diabetes.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of an interaction model of client health behavior (IMCHB)-based nursing intervention on self-management ability, glycemic control, and maternal and neonatal outcomes in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial.

SETTING: Obstetric and endocrinology outpatient clinics at a tertiary general hospital in Dalian, China.

PARTICIPANTS: Women with GDM (N = 69).

METHODS: The control group and the intervention group received routine outpatient care, and the intervention group also received a 4-week IMCHB-based nursing intervention. We assessed the ability to self-manage with the GDM self-management questionnaire; glycemic control, via fasting, 1-hour post-load, and 2-hour post-load plasma glucose levels from a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test; and maternal and neonatal outcomes based on data abstracted from medical records.

RESULTS: At postintervention, the intervention group had higher total self-management ability scores than the control group (mean difference = 11.76, 95% confidence interval (CI) [9.30, 14.23], p < .001) and lower fasting, 1-hour post-load, and 2-hour post-load plasma glucose (mean differences = -0.48, -0.74, and -0.91 mmol/L, respectively; all ps < .001). Macrosomia was less frequent in the intervention group (3.2% vs. 23.7%; odds ratio = 0.11, 95% CI [0.01, 0.90], p = .019). No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in preterm birth, cesarean birth, premature rupture of membranes, or neonatal hypoglycemia.

CONCLUSIONS: The IMCHB-based intervention was associated with better self-management ability and glycemic control and a lower incidence of macrosomia. Larger trials are needed to confirm its effects on maternal and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Early-life factors associated with eosinophilic esophagitis in Brazilian children: an exploratory case-control study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the clinical, endoscopic, and histologic features of pediatric eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) and explore associations between early-life exposures and EoE in a South American pediatric population.

METHODS: A retrospective, exploratory case-control study evaluated Brazilian children with EoE and controls without esophageal eosinophilia at a tertiary referral center (2016-2021). Crude and sex- and age-adjusted odds ratios (aORs; Firth regression) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated, followed by a hierarchical multivariable model.

RESULTS: The authors analyzed 116 patients with EoE (median age, 65 months; 69.0% male) and 72 controls. Vomiting was the most frequent symptom. Endoscopic findings included edema, furrows, and exudates, although 13.8% had a normal esophagus. After adjustment, atopic comorbidity (aOR, 4.47; 95% CI, 2.32-8.83), prematurity (4.98; 1.81-16.87), neonatal intensive care unit admission (2.76; 1.17-7.22), and antibiotics in infancy (2.02; 1.09-3.80) were associated with higher odds of EoE, whereas exclusive breastfeeding for ≥ 6 months (0.50; 0.26-0.92) and furry pets (0.44; 0.23-0.83) were associated with lower odds. In the multivariable model, male sex (2.99; 1.51-6.03), prematurity (4.65; 1.60-16.56), and atopic comorbidity (3.61; 1.72-7.80) remained significant.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides new evidence on early-life factors associated with pediatric EoE in South America, an underrepresented region. Male sex, prematurity, and atopic comorbidity were consistently associated with EoE, whereas associations with neonatal intensive care unit admission, early-life antibiotics and acid suppression, exclusive breastfeeding, and furry pets were attenuated in multivariable or sensitivity analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Prelimbic neurons represent diverse danger-modulated behaviors and veridical threat probability structure.
articles.abstract: Prelimbic cortex activity is known to promote fear expression, yet its specific representational function within the fear circuit remains unclear. We recorded prelimbic single-unit activity in rats undergoing probabilistic fear discrimination and identified three complementary levels of representation. Prelimbic neurons represented diverse danger-modulated behaviors, not just freezing, such that the initiation and cessation of five behaviors could be accurately decoded from ensemble firing. Behavioral representations were embedded within a veridical representation of the environmental threat structure, in which the majority of prelimbic neurons tuned cue firing to learned threat probability-regardless of behavior coding. This threat probability representation supported precise decoding of learned cue identity and partial decoding of threat cue timing, both of which were degraded when discriminative responding was poor. Prelimbic outcome firing was dominated by inhibition to predicted shock. Together, these results reveal that prelimbic cortex firing is organized around threat at multiple levels, from rich representations of danger-modulated behavior to veridical probabilistic threat predictions and predictive outcome signals.

articles.title: ACAD10 encodes two orphan enzymes in the ether lipid biosynthetic and salvage pathways.
articles.abstract: Ether lipids play critical roles in membrane dynamics, antioxidant defense, and signaling. They comprise ∼20% of mammalian phospholipids, and disruptions in their metabolism cause severe genetic disorders and are associated with neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases. Ether lipids are synthesized de novo from glycolytic intermediates or salvaged from the diet. While the products of these pathways are known, several key enzymes remain unidentified, including the 1-O-alkylglycerol kinase and the 1-O-alkyl-2-acetyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate phosphatase. Here, we show that acyl-CoA dehydrogenase member 10 (ACAD10) catalyzes the phosphorylation of 1-O-alkylglycerols and the dephosphorylation of 1-O-alkyl-2-acetyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate. Worms and mice lacking ACAD10 have reduced ether lipid levels and cannot salvage dietary alkylglycerols. Furthermore, individuals from the Akimel O'odham (Pima) tribe carrying ACAD10 polymorphisms show decreased plasma ether lipid levels. Collectively, our findings resolve two long-standing gaps in ether lipid biochemistry and reveal a mechanistic link between ether lipid metabolism and a population-associated risk factor for type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Neural correlates of facial recognition in a social wasp.
articles.abstract: In humans and other primates, faces are special visual objects that are encoded by circuits selective to faces. If specialized circuits are the most efficient way to encode and discriminate among similar-looking objects of high relevance, then we expect that analogous circuits should evolve in other taxa with specialized visual individual recognition abilities. Thus, we surveyed the neural responses to visual objects across the brain of a wasp that has independently evolved specialized facial recognition, Polistes fuscatus. We found a localized population of neurons analogous to face cells, which we term "wasp cells," that selectively fire to front-facing wasp images. Some of these wasp cells encode information about facial patterns, which possibly underlie the unique visual recognition abilities of these wasps. These findings demonstrate high-level feature-selective tuning in an invertebrate and suggest that specialized circuits are an adaptive feature for nervous systems requiring complex visual recognition.

articles.title: Phase angle and Liver Frailty Index predict post-transplant home discharge in ambulatory patients with cirrhosis.
articles.journal: Liver transplantation : official publication of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the International Liver Transplantation Society

articles.title: Cell Therapy and Immune Regulation in HFpEF.
Automated EHR-based frailty index for predicting serious adverse events in older hematology inpatients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Older patients with hematological disorders often face abrupt clinical deterioration. For nursing staff, early risk identification is crucial for preventive care. This study aimed to develop and validate an automated Electronic Health Record-based Frailty Index (EFI) to predict serious adverse events (SAEs) and support clinical nursing decision-making.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,139 older inpatients (≥65 years) admitted to a hematology ward between 2019 and 2025. An EFI was constructed using six automated dimensions from EHRs. The composite SAE included mortality, Intensive Care Unit (ICU) transfer, severe clinical deterioration, and fall events. Model performance was assessed using Cox regression, C-index, and calibration plots.

RESULTS: Among 1,139 patients, 86 (7.55%) experienced SAEs. The leading events were severe clinical deterioration (47.7%) and mortality (31.4%), with falls accounting for 11.6% of SAEs. Multivariable Cox regression showed the EFI was a potent independent predictor (HR 1.66, 95% CI 1.33-2.06, P < 0.001). The model showed strong discriminative ability (AUC 0.771, 95% CI 0.714-0.828) and excellent calibration with a high degree of fit between predicted and observed risks. Kaplan-Meier analysis confirmed significantly lower SAE-free survival in patients with higher EFI scores (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The automated EFI is a reliable and highly calibrated tool for identifying high-risk older hematology patients. Its use allows nurses to move from reactive to proactive care, particularly in preventing clinical deterioration and falls.

articles.title: Alignment to the Mexican Dietary Guidelines 2023 and its Association with Nutritional Status and Cardiometabolic Indicators in Mexican Women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult women have the highest prevalence of obesity in Mexico. However, previous studies found no significant associations between dietary quality scores based on the 2015 Mexican Dietary Guidelines and health outcomes in Mexican women.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate alignment with the Mexican Healthy and Sustainable Dietary Guidelines (GASS, by its acronym in Spanish) 2023 among Mexican women of childbearing age and analyze its association with nutritional status and cardiometabolic indicators.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, observational study was conducted using a subsample of 3,612 non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 20-49 years from the National Health and Nutrition Survey 2018-19, with anthropometric, biochemical and dietary information. Multiple logistic regression models estimated associations between GASSMx-2023 scores and binary health outcomes, while multinomial logistic regression was used for outcomes with more than two categories.

RESULTS: Overall alignment with GASS was low. Moderate alignment was associated with lower relative risk ratios (RRR) of obesity measured by body mass index, and lower odds of abdominal obesity, arterial hypertension and dyslipidemias among women aged 20-39 years. Lower RRR of prediabetes and diabetes and lower odds of hypertriglyceridemia were also observed in women aged 30-39 years. In contrast, among women aged 40-49 years, high alignment was associated with higher RRR of diabetes and higher odds of low HDL cholesterol.

CONCLUSION: The association between GASS alignment and health outcomes differed by age, with more favorable associations among women aged 20-39 years and some unfavorable associations among women aged 40-49 years. The GASSMx-2023 index may be useful tool for evaluating and monitoring interventions promoting GASS recommendations.

articles.title: A pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem couples malignant stress and inflammatory myeloid remodeling across adenocarcinomas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis and tumor immune remodeling may converge through hypoxia, myeloid inflammation, neutrophil extracellular traps, platelet engagement, and endothelial dysfunction. We investigated whether they define a conserved, transcriptomically measurable tumor state.

METHODS: We integrated a lung adenocarcinoma extracellular-vesicle RNA dataset with three venous thromboembolism cohorts to derive five immunothrombotic modules. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from lung (LUAD), pancreatic (PAAD), and gastric adenocarcinoma (STAD) were analyzed. We defined the pseudo-ischemic tumor ecosystem (PTES) as a transcriptomically defined molecular state reflecting coordinated malignant-cell stress and inflammatory-myeloid activity, rather than direct evidence of tissue ischemia or a diagnosis of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism. A tissue-resolved Core PTES, calculated as the mean of standardized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs, was evaluated in 37 single-cell samples and 1107 TCGA tumors. Associations with immune states, Hallmark pathways, inferred cell-cell communication, and overall survival were assessed. The primary survival analysis used continuous Core PTES per one-standard-deviation increase, with high-versus-low PTES analyzed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Direct analysis showed the strongest effects for malignant stress (Hedges' g = 1.116), NET-like activity (g = 1.477), and endothelial activation (g = 1.288). Single-cell analysis retained 143,101 cells and localized malignant-stress and inflammatory-myeloid programs to their respective compartments. In TCGA, high Core PTES most strongly separated the inflammatory program (median difference = 1.134; rank-biserial r = 0.735). Cross-cancer GSEA identified recurrent proliferative, inflammatory, metabolic, and hypoxic programs, including E2F targets, G2M checkpoint, TNF-NF-κB, IL6-JAK-STAT3, glycolysis, and hypoxia. Inferred SPP1-CD44 and SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 interactions were detected across all three cancers. In multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and stage, each one-standard-deviation increase in Core PTES was associated with poorer overall survival in LUAD (HR = 1.205, 95% CI 1.045-1.389) and PAAD (HR = 1.458, 95% CI 1.138-1.868), but not STAD (HR = 0.912, 95% CI 0.755-1.103); the cancer-stratified pooled HR was 1.168 (95% CI 1.060-1.288). High-versus-low sensitivity analyses showed the same cancer-specific pattern.

CONCLUSION: PTES captures a conserved pseudo-ischemic ecosystem linking malignant stress with inflammatory-myeloid remodeling. It is a hypothesis-generating, transcriptomically defined ecosystem measure rather than evidence of literal tissue ischemia, a diagnostic measure of cancer-associated thrombosis or venous thromboembolism, or a validated prognostic biomarker. Prospective clinical phenotyping and functional validation are required.

articles.title: Headache in juvenile idiopathic arthritis: more common and phenotypically different than expected.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Headache is among the most common neurological complaints in childhood and can substantially impair quality of life. Although children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) experience chronic inflammation and recurrent pain, the prevalence and phenotype of primary headache in this population remain insufficiently studied.

METHODS: This cross-sectional case-control study was conducted in a tertiary pediatric rheumatology clinic between October and December 2025. A total of 109 children with JIA and 125 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) were included. Headache was assessed by structured questionnaire and neurological examination, and all diagnoses were established by a pediatric neurologist according to the International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex, family history of migraine, perceived sleep insufficiency and body mass index.

RESULTS: Primary headache was more frequent in children with JIA than in HCs (37.6% vs. 17.6%, p < 0.001). The excess was confined to tension-type headache (TTH; 22.9% vs. 4.8%, p < 0.001), whereas migraine was equally frequent (14.7% vs. 12.8%, p = 0.71). After adjustment, JIA remained associated with TTH (odds ratio [OR] 6.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.62-18.39) but not with migraine (OR 1.81, 95% CI 0.79-4.13). Conversely, family history of migraine (OR 2.35, 95% CI 1.06-5.19) and perceived sleep insufficiency (OR 3.99, 95% CI 1.76-9.02) were associated with migraine but not TTH. No disease-related or treatment-related variable was associated with headache.

CONCLUSION: Children with JIA show a selective excess of TTH rather than a uniform increase in primary headache, while established risk factors track with migraine. Systematic headache enquiry may improve recognition of this underrecognized comorbidity.

articles.title: Early defibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A systematic synthesis of the time-dependent decline of shockable rhythms.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on how shockable rhythms decline over time in adult out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) and to examine how defibrillation timing relates to rhythm deterioration and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Electronic databases were searched for studies reporting initial rhythm distribution and time-to-defibrillation or untreated arrest duration in adult OHCA. Observational cohorts, registry-based studies, physiological waveform analyses, and randomized trials were included. Data were extracted on rhythm prevalence, time-related measures, defibrillation success, and clinical outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies published between 1990 and 2025 were included, encompassing more than 262,700 OHCA cases. Among unselected cohorts, the median prevalence of initial shockable rhythms was 33.5% (IQR 22.6-42.8%). Across study designs, increasing time-to-defibrillation was consistently associated with decreasing shockable rhythm prevalence and progressive transition to non-shockable rhythms. Physiological and AED waveform analyses demonstrated progressive deterioration of ventricular fibrillation with increasing untreated duration. Early defibrillation was associated with higher defibrillation success, increased return of spontaneous circulation, and improved survival outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Shockable rhythms decline progressively with increasing untreated arrest duration, reflecting time-dependent electrical deterioration from ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia to non-shockable rhythms. These findings support the concept of a limited early shockable window in cardiac arrest and reinforce the critical importance of minimizing time-to-defibrillation across emergency response systems to improve survival in OHCA.

articles.title: Ceftriaxone Compared to Aminoglycoside-based Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Type III Open Fractures.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Open fractures are associated with substantial complications including osteomyelitis, loss of limb function, and amputation. The optimal prophylactic antibiotic regimen to prevent infections in patients with type III open fractures, which are associated with the greatest risk of complications, remains unclear. The aim of this study was to compare the efficacy and safety of ceftriaxone to aminoglycoside-based regimens.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study of adult patients with type III open fractures admitted between October 2017 and October 2021. Patients were enrolled in the study if they received either ceftriaxone or cefazolin plus an aminoglycoside for antibiotic prophylaxis. The primary outcome analyzed was the incidence of surgical site infections (SSIs) according to CDC definitions. Safety outcomes evaluated included the incidence of acute kidney injury.

RESULTS: There were 156 patients included in the analysis with 34 patients receiving ceftriaxone and 122 patients receiving cefazolin plus an aminoglycoside. The incidence of SSI was similar between patients that received ceftriaxone and cefazolin/aminoglycoside (12% versus 17%, P = 0.60). There were no differences in the incidence of acute kidney injury between groups (P = 0.74).

CONCLUSIONS: Ceftriaxone appears to have similar effectiveness preventing SSI compared to cefazolin plus an aminoglycoside in patients with type III open fractures. Monotherapy with ceftriaxone in adult patients with type III open fractures may provide a therapeutic option with greater ease of dosing with similar effectiveness to guideline recommended aminoglycoside-based therapy.

articles.title: From pin factory to Panchakarma: A neo-Smithian division of intelligence for AI-enabled Ayurveda.
articles.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
articles.abstract: Ayurveda and contemporary artificial intelligence face an inverse paradox. Ayurveda has accumulated several thousand years of individualised clinical observation but remains underrepresented in the global evidence base, because it is repeatedly evaluated using a testing architecture designed for single-molecule interventions and ill-suited to individualised, integrated care. Contemporary artificial intelligence (AI), by contrast, has frameworks for extracting structure from observation but lacks domain-specific clinical data in traditional medicine. This paper argues that the two are complementary: AI applied to terminology mapping, retrospective cohort analysis from electronic medical records, signal detection in routine clinical data, and evidence synthesis across classical and contemporary sources changes the economics of evidence generation enough to make it feasible. The argument is developed through a neo-Smithian division-of-intelligence framework, adapted from earlier work, that allocates clinical tasks across AI-first, hybrid, and human-first categories on grounds respecting both the structure of Ayurvedic practice and the comparative advantages of contemporary AI. A three-layer operational architecture, comprising a data foundation, analytics pipelines, and multi-audience delivery, is set out and tested against two contrasting clinical cases, type-2 diabetes and supportive cancer care, before being mapped onto India's regulatory framework for Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani (ASU) products. The distributional question is then addressed, six risks are named, legal implications are set out, and a phased five-year roadmap closes the argument. The technology, the regulation, and the international policy environment are now sufficient; what remains is the institutional and methodological work to carry the framework into practice.

articles.title: The bidirectional relationship between pain and kidney function in sickle cell disease.
articles.abstract: Pain and kidney disease are among the most disabling complications of sickle cell disease (SCD), but their relationship remains incompletely defined. Recurrent vaso-occlusion, haemolysis, inflammation, dehydration, and hospitalisation can increase both pain burden and susceptibility to acute kidney injury (AKI). Opioids and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are essential components of pain treatment, yet observational associations between analgesic exposure and kidney outcomes are vulnerable to confounding by pain severity, vaso-occlusive burden, and health-care utilisation. Preclinical studies nevertheless identify plausible mechanisms through which opioids may affect podocyte calcium signalling, oxidative stress, inflammatory pathways, and mast-cell degranulation, whereas NSAIDs can impair prostaglandin-dependent renal haemodynamics. Conversely, kidney injury may contribute to pain amplification through increased generation or impaired clearance of cytokines, damage-associated molecular patterns, vasoactive peptides, arachidonic acid metabolites, neurotrophins, and free haem. Evidence for several of these renal-nociceptive links in people with SCD remains indirect. In this Review, we critically evaluate human, translational, and experimental evidence for a bidirectional pain, analgesic exposure and kidney injury framework, distinguish association from causation, and identify priorities for kidney-conscious analgesia and prospective studies integrating renal biomarkers with longitudinal pain phenotyping.

articles.title: Influence of salinity changes on biological traits, oxidative stress, antioxidant defense system, and expression of heat shock protein (hsp) genes in the brine shrimp Artemia franciscana.
articles.abstract: Salinity is a critical environmental factor that exerts direct influence on aquatic invertebrates. To investigate the impacts of salinity stress, we evaluated the biological traits (body size and hatching rate), intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, antioxidant enzymatic activities (superoxide dismutase [SOD], glutathione S-transferase [GST], and catalase [CAT]), and mRNA expression levels of heat shock protein (hsp) in brine shrimp Artemia franciscana. A. franciscana cultured at low salinity exhibited a significantly larger body size than the control. Hatching rate significantly decreased at 0, 15, and 75 psu (P < 0.05). However, marked differences were not observed in the other salinity groups (25-65 psu). ROS levels and antioxidant enzyme activities are modulated by salinity shifts, resulting in a salinity-induced oxidative stress response (25, 45, and 55 psu) and an antioxidant defense system. Additionally, the upregulated mRNA expression of hsp70 and hsp90 across different salinities over 24 h indicated their potential as molecular biomarkers of salinity stress. Overall, our results demonstrate that salinity shifts affect body size and hatching rate, and induce oxidative stress along with cellular defense mechanisms in A. franciscana.

articles.title: Association of ambient particulate matter and neighborhood walkability with risk of asthma in Ningbo, China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a prevalent respiratory disorder worldwide. Ambient particulate matter (PM) and neighborhood walkability may both influence asthma development, yet their joint effects remain unclear. This study investigated the independent and combined effects of PM exposure and walkability on asthma onset.

METHODS: We prospectively followed 26,926 adults from the Yinzhou Cohort in Ningbo, China. Incident asthma was identified through the Yinzhou Health Information System (YHIS). PM exposure was estimated from satellite-derived data, whereas neighborhood walkability was evaluated using Walk Score. Cox proportional hazards models were applied to assess the associations with asthma incidence. Additive and multiplicative interactions were examined, and the Cumulative Risk Index (CRI) was used to evaluate joint effects.

RESULTS: Over 152,748 person-years of follow-up, 1032 asthma cases occurred. In single-exposure models, PM1, PM2.5, PM10, and PM2.5 components (NO3-, NH4+, and SO42-) were related to increased asthma risk, with the hazard ratios (HR) per interquartile range (IQR) increase ranging from 1.09 (95% CI: 1.00-1.20) to 1.30 (95% CI: 1.19-1.43). Conversely, an IQR increase in neighborhood walkability was associated with an 11% lower asthma risk (HR = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.82-0.96). In two-exposure models, these associations were attenuated. Additive interaction between PM1 and walkability was observed. Each IQR increase in PM1 combined with an IQR decrease in walkability corresponded to a joint hazard ratio (JHR) of 1.39 (95% CI: 1.22-1.58).

CONCLUSIONS: Long-term PM exposure increased asthma risk, whereas greater neighborhood walkability was protective. Asthma prevention strategies should consider both air pollution and built environment.

articles.title: Dose-dependent maternal LV systolic compromise in hypertensive pregnancy: Novel predictors and cumulative remodelling from recurrent exposure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterise severity-graded cardiac compromise, dose-response trends, multivariable predictors, and the cumulative cardiac impact of recurrent hypertensive exposure in an Indian tertiary-care cohort with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP).

STUDY DESIGN: Prospective observational study, AIIMS Bhopal (February 2021-August 2022).

STUDY GROUP: 100 HDP women (gestational HTN 37, pre-eclampsia 46, chronic HTN 12, superimposed PE 5); Comparison: 50 normotensive term women. Transthoracic Doppler echocardiography (Philips EPIQ 7C); HDP per ACOG; diastolic dysfunction (DD) per ASE/EACVI 2016.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: DD prevalence (primary); LVEF, concentric LVH, structural and Doppler parameters; Jonckheere-Terpstra trend, Cochran-Armitage, multivariable regression with VIF, and ROC analyses.

RESULTS: LVEF was lower in HDP (p < 0.001; d = -0.60), with monotonic dose-response (p = 0.002) and independent multivariable effect (β = -5.19; p < 0.001). DD prevalence was 4% vs 2% (OR 1.85; p = 0.67) - underpowered (post-hoc power 0.12). Concentric LVH was confined to the Study Group (5%; chronic HTN 25%, superimposed PE 20%). Prior HDP history predicted cumulative remodelling: DD 17.4% vs 0.8% (p = 0.002); concentric LVH 17.4% vs 0.8% (p = 0.009); any cardiac abnormality 21.7% vs 3.1% (p = 0.007). LV wall thickness predicted LVH as determined by RWT (AUC 0.929; cutoff >9.5 mm).

CONCLUSIONS: HDP produces severity-graded subclinical systolic compromise in the index pregnancy; cumulative structural remodelling concentrates in women with prior HDP, chronic HTN, and early-onset disease, supporting targeted echocardiographic surveillance.

articles.title: Association of pre-pregnancy obesity with residual preeclampsia risk among high-risk women receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major cause of maternal and neonatal morbidity. This study aimed to determine whether pre-pregnancy obesity was associated with residual PE risk among high-risk women receiving low-dose aspirin (LDA) prophylaxis.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study screened 482 women with pre-pregnancy obesity. Of these, 100 women classified as high risk by the Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) model constituted the study group. Using 1:2 propensity score matching based on maternal age, parity, and first-trimester mean arterial pressure, 200 LDA-treated high-risk women with a normal pre-pregnancy BMI were selected as controls. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the associations of pre-pregnancy obesity and other clinical factors with PE.

RESULTS: Among 11,395 deliveries, 482 occurred in women with pre-pregnancy obesity (prevalence, 4.23%). In the obesity group, the crude incidence of PE was 26.0% (26/100), with 8.0% (8/100) being preterm PE. In the normal-BMI control group, the incidence was significantly lower at 13.0% (26/200), with 6.0% (12/200) being preterm PE. Multivariate analysis identified chronic hypertension (aOR = 4.79, 95% CI 2.06-11.11) and gestational weight gain (GWG) (aOR = 1.09 per kg, 95% CI 1.02-1.16) as significant independent predictors of PE. The adjusted association between pre-pregnancy obesity and PE did not reach conventional statistical significance (aOR = 2.04, 95% CI 0.98-4.17; P = 0.053).

CONCLUSIONS: Among high-risk women receiving LDA prophylaxis, those with pre-pregnancy obesity had a higher crude incidence of PE than normal-BMI controls, although the adjusted association did not reach conventional statistical significance. Greater GWG was independently associated with PE risk and may contribute to the residual risk observed in this population. These findings support incorporating gestational weight counselling and management into comprehensive care alongside indicated pharmacological prophylaxis.

articles.title: Association Between Cardiorespiratory Coupling and Exercise Capacity in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the association between cardiorespiratory coupling (CRC) and exercise capacity, estimated via peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak), in patients with chronic heart failure (CHF).

APPROACH: Twenty-five CHF patients underwent VO2peak assessment during cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Electrocardiogram and respiratory flow (R) were recorded during spontaneous breathing before (PRE) and after (POST) CPET. Time- and frequency-domain heart period (HP) variability indexes were calculated. Bivariate CRC indexes were computed in high frequency (HF, from 0.15 to 0.4 Hz) band, such as the transfer function gain and phase from R to HP variability, squared coherence between HP variability and R in the HF band [K2HP‒R(HF)], and causal squared coherence from R to HP and vice versa. Correlation analysis of VO2peak with HP variability and CRC indexes in PRE and with their POST-to-PRE variations was performed in the overall cohort and in subgroups with preserved ejection fraction (pEF) and reduced ejection fraction (rEF).

MAIN RESULTS: No significant association of HP variability and CRC markers with VO2peak was found in PRE. In contrast, over the entire CHF group the POST-to-PRE variation of K2HP‒R(HF) showed a significant positive correlation with VO2peak, thus indicating that reactivity in recovering CRC after intense physical exercise is linked to exercise capacity. This association remained significant when considering exclusively pEF patients. Causal CRC indexes failed in this regard.

SIGNIFICANCE: These findings suggest that K2HP‒R(HF) represents a candidate marker to estimate exercise capacity in CHF deserving further examination over larger databases.

articles.title: [Critical reflection on the article «Pharmacological treatment of type2 diabetes mellitus»].
Post-traumatic growth of children and their caregivers after discharge from the pediatric intensive care unit: A multi-center, longitudinal, qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore how children and their primary caregivers co-construct post-traumatic growth (PTG) through everyday interactions after being discharged from the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and to examine the dynamic evolution of this process within the context of the Chinese family culture.

METHODS: This study adopted a longitudinal qualitative research design. Semi-structured interviews were conducted from March 2024 to December 2025, with 24 child-caregiver dyads discharged from four PICUs in Sichuan Province, China, at 1, 3, and 6 months after discharge. Data were analyzed using directed content analysis, incorporating deductive coding, inductive open coding, and longitudinal comparative analysis.

RESULTS: This study included 24 child-caregiver dyads. The children were aged 8-17 years and had undergone invasive procedures or life-sustaining treatment; caregivers were the children's primary caregivers. A total of 144 interview transcripts were collected, from which three themes and nine subthemes were identified. PTG after PICU discharge was revealed to be a relational and dynamically evolving process. Through jointly coping with physical vulnerability, caregiving uncertainty, and changes in family relationships, children and caregivers gradually moved from intense fear and loss of control toward negotiating caregiving boundaries, restoring daily life, and reinterpreting the illness experience, family relationships, and future expectations.

CONCLUSION: PTG after PICU discharge is a dynamic relational process jointly negotiated and reconstructed by children and caregivers through ongoing interactions.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Clinical practice should consider promoting PTG after PICU discharge as an important goal of family-centered continuity of care. Healthcare professionals should attend to the psychosocial needs of both children and caregivers, supporting them in rebuilding a sense of safety, restoring daily life, and promoting collective family adaptation.

articles.title: Implementation of nurse-led frontal electroencephalography for early neurological assessment in patients after cardiac arrest: the FRONT study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is a valuable tool for neurological prognostication after cardiac arrest. However, registration is often delayed by time-consuming electrode placement and limited availability of EEG technicians.

AIM: This study investigated the implementation of a frontal EEG (fEEG) configuration using 6 self-adhesive electrodes by nurses within 3 h of Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission in patients after cardiac arrest.

DESIGN AND METHODS: The FRONT study followed a type 3 hybrid design. Nurses were trained to start an fEEG through a theoretical and practical session and were supported by a Step-by-Step interactive guide. Knowledge, attitude, and practice surveys were completed by nurses at baseline and after each fEEG application. Correct and timely application was measured prospectively in 60 patients.

RESULTS: At baseline, the survey response rate was 46% (49/107); after application, it was 68% (41/60). Most nurses (84%) reported having sufficient knowledge of fEEG electrode placement and monitoring. The interactive guide was frequently used (98%) during fEEG initiation; the median application time was 20 min [IQR: 15-25]. All nurses found early fEEG monitoring meaningful; perception improved since implementation (3.98 ± 0.78 vs 4.54 ± 0.51, p < 0.001). During the implementation, an fEEG was applied in 88% of patients (53/60), including 73% (44/60) within 3 h. Electrode placement was confirmed as correct by EEG technicians in all evaluated patients.

CONCLUSIONS: ICU nurses were able to apply fEEG monitoring with high levels of adoption, acceptability and fidelity following a short, multifaceted training program combined with an interactive guide. Further research is needed to clarify the interpretability, diagnostic performance, prognostic value, and clinical utility of nurse-led fEEG monitoring in post-resuscitation care.

IMPLICATION FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Early bedside EEG assessment by trained ICU nurses may facilitate timely neurological evaluation in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Fertility-sparing treatment in uterine cancer: Oncological, reproductive and neonatal outcomes from a Nationwide PremEnCa cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The incidence of endometrial cancer (EC), including premenopausal, is increasing which highlights the need for long-term follow-up in fertility-sparing treatments (FST). This nationwide study's aim is to investigate FST in uterine cancer focusing on EC with oncological, reproductive, neonatal outcomes and sociodemographic features.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This nationwide population-based study identified women aged ≤45 years diagnosed with uterine cancer during 2010-2021, using Swedish national registries and medical records. Due to limited cohort size, descriptive statistics was used.

RESULTS: Among 436 women ≤45 years with EC, 25/219 (11.4%) with stage IA endometrioid EC underwent FST. Complete response (CR) was verified in 18/25 (72.0%) after median of 8.8 (range 2.6-17.2) months. During follow-up (median 91.9; 57-180 months) 6/18 (33.3%) recurred after median 8.8 (range 6.2-20.2) months. In the FST group, 68% had BMI <30 and 76% post-secondary education, versus the hysterectomy group where 40.6% had BMI <30 and 48.1% post-secondary education. The live birth rate following EC was 10/18(55%), Among uterine sarcoma, 1/3 who attempted FST remained recurrence-free and gave birth. 10/11 neonates were born ≥37 + 0 weeks gestation, 2/11 were underweight. No reported congenital anomalies.

CONCLUSIONS: The CR of FST in EC exceeded 70% however 1/3 of responders experienced a recurrence, Importantly, the long-term oncological outcome was not compromised. The majority of women receiving FST were non-obese and had post-secondary education. Fertility-sparing attempts in sarcoma was rare, with isolated successful cases. The live birth rate following EC diagnosis was 55%, most born at term without growth restriction or congenital anomalies.

articles.title: Metabolic pathways involved in autoimmune diseases.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are associated with cellular metabolic reprogramming. Disruptions to key metabolic pathways - including glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, amino acid degradation, and fatty acid oxidation - affect immune cell activation, promote pathogenic Th1/Th17 responses, destabilize regulatory T cells, support autoreactive B cells, and influence macrophage polarization. Mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, mTOR activation, lipid and sphingolipid remodeling, and gut microbiota metabolites link environmental and genetic factors to failures in self-tolerance. Each disease has distinct metabolic traits. For rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, multiple sclerosis, and type 1 diabetes, we trace the sequence of pathways, immunological effects, and phenotypes; explain why shared pathways differ in the synovium, kidney, central nervous system, and pancreatic islets; and describe the evidence that distinguishes causal mechanisms from plausible ones, along with potential biomarker signatures, none of which has yet been validated. Metabolic reprogramming primarily amplifies diseases rather than initiating them.

articles.title: Haemodynamic, functional and biomarker responses in obese patients undergoing pulmonary endarterectomy: a comparative cohort study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is common in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), but comparative data on haemodynamic recovery, biomarker kinetics and functional outcomes after pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remain limited.

OBJECTIVES: To compare haemodynamic, biomarker, functional and perioperative outcomes by obesity status after PEA.

METHODS: Single-centre cohort of 202 consecutive patients undergoing PEA for CTEPH (January 2015-February 2024), stratified by BMI (obese ≥30 kg/m², n = 62; non-obese, n = 140). Serial biomarkers were analysed using log-transformed linear mixed-effects models (LMM; group × time interaction as primary test, Bonferroni-corrected contrasts). Haemodynamics were compared by ANCOVA adjusted for baseline, cardiac index using BSA (Mosteller), and NYHA class by exact test and adjusted logistic regression.

RESULTS: The LMM group × time interaction was significant only for CK-MB [F(4; 669.3)=2.67; p = 0.031]; the single Bonferroni-significant contrast was at ∼24 h (geometric mean 42.2vs 29.3 ng/mL; p = 0.012). Troponin [F(4; 538.4)=1.69; p = 0.151] and CPK [F(4; 685.9)=1.13; p = 0.341] interactions were not significant. Postoperative cardiac index (2.70 vs 2.74 L/min/m²; p = 0.77) and ANCOVA-adjusted ΔPVR (p = 0.39) did not differ. Postoperative NYHA class I was less frequent in obese patients (47.8%vs 70.8%; adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.21-0.99). Cumulative mortality at 30 days was 9.7% in obese and 11.4% in non-obese patients (p = 0.81).

CONCLUSION: In this single-centre observational cohort, obesity was not associated with significant differences in postoperative haemodynamics, length of stay or short-term mortality, although estimates were imprecise. Obese patients less often achieved NYHA class I. These hypothesis-generating findings do not support excluding patients from PEA evaluation on the basis of BMI alone.

articles.title: Beyond PREVENT-HF: Assessing the Added Value of NT-proBNP and Imaging for Prediction of Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk prediction models for incident heart failure (HF) may enable targeted primary prevention. The American Heart Association developed the PREVENT (Predicting Risk of CVD EVENTs) equations for incident HF (PREVENT-HF).

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to externally validate PREVENT-HF in a European community-based population and assess the incremental value of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and imaging biomarkers.

METHODS: PREVENT-HF was externally validated and recalibrated in 428,084 participants from UK Biobank. Calibration, discrimination, and net clinical benefit were assessed within a competing risks framework. The incremental predictive value of NT-proBNP (N = 43,329) and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived variables (N = 58,360) was evaluated in dedicated subcohorts.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 14.1 years, 10,296 participants (2.4%) developed incident HF. PREVENT-HF substantially overpredicted HF risk (observed-to-expected ratio: 0.40), though discrimination was good (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.742). Net clinical benefit was observed only under simulated higher-incidence scenarios. NT-proBNP was strongly and independently predictive of incident HF after adjustment for PREVENT-HF (subdistribution HR: 1.61; 95% CI: 1.52-1.70), significantly improving discrimination (change in area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.038) and net clinical benefit across all incidence scenarios. Body surface area-indexed left atrial volume, indexed left ventricular mass, left ventricular ejection fraction, and global longitudinal strain were independently predictive of HF after adjustment for PREVENT-HF. After additional adjustment for NT-proBNP, only indexed left atrial volume and left ventricular ejection fraction remained independently predictive.

CONCLUSIONS: PREVENT-HF requires recalibration for European populations and generates net clinical benefit only in higher-risk populations. NT-proBNP significantly augments PREVENT-HF and should be incorporated as a continuous predictor. Imaging-derived variables provide modest further prognostic information, which may support staged screening approaches.

articles.title: Advancing professional role through a specialized Master's: Impact on MRI radiographers' skills, confidence, and career development.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Technological advancements in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) have increased the complexity of clinical practice, placing greater demands on the knowledge and professional competence of MRI radiographers. Traditional experiential training models may no longer be sufficient, highlighting the need for postgraduate education. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term outcomes of a specialised postgraduate MRI Master's programme in Italy.

METHODS: An observational cross-sectional study was conducted by sending a 26-item questionnaire to all radiographers who had completed the Master's programme over the past 13 years. The survey assessed programme evaluation, learning outcomes, and career impact. Descriptive statistics were calculated, and group comparisons were performed using Student's t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests with a Holm-Bonferroni correction (p < 0.05).

RESULTS: A total of 160 radiographers participated (56.7% response-rate). High satisfaction was reported, with Likert mean scores consistently above 4.5 across domains including teaching quality, theoretical content, and organisation. After completing the Master's programme, 21% of participants reported a salary increase and 23% a change in professional role. The qualification was a preferential or mandatory requirement in 35% of cases. No significant differences were found between in-person and blended delivery cohorts or based on prior MRI experience.

CONCLUSION: Specialized postgraduate MRI education is associated with improved technical competence and tangible career advancement. These findings support the value of structured academic training in addressing the increasing complexity of MRI practice. Investment in postgraduate MRI education can enhance workforce competence, support career progression, and foster the development of advanced knowledge and specialised skills among radiographers.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: MRI scans are becoming more complex, and radiographers may need advanced education to keep up with new technology and clinical demands. This study surveyed radiographers who completed a postgraduate MRI programme in Italy about its effect on their work and careers. This study found that participants reported improved skills, high satisfaction with the programme, and benefits such as career progression and salary increases for some graduates. This matters because specialised education can help build a skilled workforce and support better MRI services for patients.

articles.title: Clinical Free-Text Retrieval Across an Acute Physiological Derangement Composite in Intensive Care Unit Discharge Summaries: Stratified Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retrieval over clinical free text underpins record search, cohort identification, and retrieval-augmented language systems. Performance is usually summarized by a single corpus-level mean, which can obscure systematic heterogeneity across patients.

OBJECTIVE: This study tests whether known-item retrieval performance varies across an early acute physiological derangement composite measured independently of the text, whether it reproduces under a validated severity-of-illness score, and whether it is robust to alternative outcome, retrieval, and explanatory specifications.

METHODS: We linked 4078 MIMIC-IV (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV) discharge summaries to an adult medical intensive care unit (ICU) cohort and built a pooled, length-matched index of 2956 documents drawn equally from 4 strata of a prespecified composite of early acute physiological derangement, comprising vital signs and Glasgow Coma Scale, mechanical ventilation, and age. A held-out 2-sentence passage had to retrieve its originating summary after removal. Eight contrastively trained dense retrievers, 5 masked language model controls, and BM25 were evaluated. Reciprocal rank at 10 (RR@10) was regressed on exposure stratum with patient-clustered SEs and Holm correction. The analysis was repeated under the Oxford Acute Severity of Illness Score (OASIS), a validated first-day score. Additional analyses examined categorical exposure shape, untruncated target rank, hit@10 (hit at 10), lexical representation, query characteristics, age removal, organ dysfunction, and measured covariates.

RESULTS: Mean RR@10 across dense retrievers fell from 0.127 to 0.080 between the lowest and highest composite stratum (-0.047; mean relative decline 37.2%), with Holm-significant negative slopes in all 8; a pooled model gave -0.0145 per stratum (95% CI -0.0207 to -0.0082; P<.001; 23,648 observations). Under OASIS, it fell from 0.127 to 0.078 (-0.049; mean relative decline 38.7%); again, 8 of 8 were Holm-significant. The geometric mean rank of the correct document worsened by a factor of 1.17 per stratum under the composite and 1.24 under OASIS, 8 of 8 significant. BM25 also deteriorated, although from a higher baseline. It persisted across alternative query, indexing, rank, and hit@10 specifications; joint covariate adjustment attenuated the mean coefficient by 21.6%. Removing age attenuated but did not eliminate the pattern: all 8 retained negative slopes, the mean decline fell to 29.7%, and 3 of 8 remained Holm-significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical free-text retrievability declined systematically with worsening early acute physiological derangement. The association held under an externally defined and validated severity-of-illness score as well as the study-specific composite and in lexical as well as dense retrieval. Corpus-level averages can therefore conceal clinically ordered heterogeneity, and clinical retrieval systems should be evaluated across patient strata rather than overall performance alone.

articles.title: A Digital Respiratory Ecosystem for People Living With Asthma: Mixed Methods Pilot Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital health technologies (DHTs) offer potential to improve asthma management and treatment concordance with international clinical practice guidelines.

OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to develop the Breathe Digital Ecosystem (Breathe DE) and evaluate its usability, acceptability, feasibility, and preliminary effects on asthma symptoms and control, medication adherence, medication administration technique, and health status.

METHODS: Breathe DE was co-designed from January 2021 to September 2022. Modified from a former model, it was built on a single smartphone app with Bluetooth-enabled hardware components (Medical International Research spirometer and FindAir ONE smart inhaler cap). Breathe DE supports diagnostics, inhaler adherence and technique, short-acting beta-agonist (SABA) rescue inhaler overuse, environmental trigger avoidance, self-management action plan, and spirometry. A prospective observational mixed methods pilot study to evaluate Breathe DE was conducted in Southwestern Ontario from September 2022 to March 2023. A convenience sample of participants was recruited from primary care, and the study duration was 12 weeks (90 days). Participants were adults diagnosed with asthma, using a daily maintenance inhaler (Enerzair/Atectura) and an as-needed SABA rescue inhaler. Quantitative summary statistics and graphical presentation of longitudinal app interactions, inhaler technique assessment, medication adherence, asthma control, and health status were used to describe participant engagement with Breathe DE. Semistructured exit interviews were analyzed using combined deductive and inductive codebook thematic analysis to assess perceived usefulness, acceptability, and feasibility.

RESULTS: Of the 21 participants enrolled in the study, 17 completed the exit interview at week 12. The study population was predominantly female (18/21, 86%) and younger than 65 years of age (16/21, 76%). Engagement with the app was variable and waned over follow-up. Per-participant median frequencies of app interaction were 35 (IQR 26-71) days, daily medication logging was 21 (IQR 12-49), rescue inhaler use was 4 (IQR 0-15) doses, and spirometry was performed a median of 6 (IQR 2-24) times. Longitudinally, asthma control (symptoms, SABA use, and Asthma Control Questionnaire), health status indicators (mini Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire), and medication adherence indicated possible improvement in participants with complete data. Overall, participants felt that Breathe DE could be useful for symptom management and improving medication adherence. Acceptability as a tool for self-management was dependent on the participant's degree of asthma control and self-management abilities. Feasibility was impeded by some technological issues and physical barriers.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed one mobile health platform combining all major guideline-directed best practices for successful asthma management. Breathe DE created a comprehensive viewing portal into the day-to-day experience of asthma. Integration of the data types highlighted an opportunity for DHTs as a tool prescribed by the health care practitioner to facilitate partnership with the patient, giving valuable and comprehensive insights to inform individualized optimal asthma management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05594654; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05594654.

articles.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Effects of a Web-Based Premature Birth Prevention Self-Management Education Program for Women of Childbearing Age: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial With a Nested Qualitative Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature birth remains a leading cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet few interventions target women of childbearing age before pregnancy. Digital health interventions using interactive webtoon storytelling may enhance engagement and promote preconception health behaviors, but evidence regarding their feasibility and preliminary effectiveness remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot study evaluates the feasibility and preliminary effects of an interactive webtoon-based educational website for preventing premature birth among women of childbearing age.

METHODS: This explanatory sequential mixed methods pilot study used a stratified randomized controlled design, with a nested qualitative evaluation of the webtoon arm. Forty-seven eligible women of childbearing age, recruited via social media and online communities, were randomized to either an interactive webtoon-based educational website or a text-based educational website with identical content. Both groups accessed a self-guided web-based program. Outcomes were assessed online at baseline, immediately postintervention, and at the 4-week follow-up using a per-protocol approach. Primary quantitative outcomes included the Self-Management Self-Efficacy for Premature Birth Prevention (SMSE-PBP) and Health Belief Model for Premature Birth Prevention (HBM-PBP) scores. Feasibility outcomes included the intervention completion rate, 8-item Client Satisfaction Questionnaire, and Website Quality Evaluation. Sequential qualitative data were gathered through in-depth interviews with participants in the webtoon arm to explore user experience, perceived utility, and areas for improvement.

RESULTS: A total of 34 participants completed the study (uptake rate, 19/24, 79%; completion rate, 14/19, 74%). High satisfaction and usability supported the feasibility of the intervention. Generalized estimating equations revealed no significant group-by-time interaction effects for SMSE-PBP (time 1: P=.47; time 2: P=.35) or any HBM-PBP subdomains (perceived susceptibility, time 1: P=.53; time 2: P=.64; perceived severity, time 1: P=.76; time 2: P=.96; perceived benefits, time 1: P=.30; time 2: P=.67; and perceived barriers, time 1: P=.23; time 2: P=.44). However, significant main effects of time were observed for SMSE-PBP (time 1: P=.006; time 2: P<.001) and 3 HBM-PBP subdomains-perceived susceptibility (time 1: P<.001; time 2: P<.001), perceived benefits (time 1: P=.02; time 2: P=.001), and perceived barriers (time 2: P=.003)-indicating overall longitudinal improvements across both groups. Qualitative insights, obtained sequentially, highlighted heightened awareness of premature birth prevention, an enhanced understanding of the appropriate timing of preventive behaviors, and a broader range of behaviors considered important for premature birth prevention.

CONCLUSIONS: The webtoon-based educational website was feasible and acceptable to women of childbearing age. Both programs showed improvements over time in self-management self-efficacy and health beliefs related to premature birth prevention. This pilot study did not detect a clear advantage of the webtoon-based format over the text-based format, possibly because of the short intervention period. Nevertheless, the demonstrated feasibility and acceptability, together with qualitative findings from the webtoon arm, support further refinement of the program and its evaluation in a fully powered randomized controlled trial.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service KCT0008824; https://tinyurl.com/bdhv9cud.

articles.title: Developmental Analysis of Drawing Sequences: How Young Children and Adults Organize Object Parts in Line Drawing.
articles.abstract: The drawing process (how we draw), together with its outcome (what we draw), provides valuable insights into the cognitive mechanisms and motor control underlying symbolic representation. To depict developmental changes in the drawing process, this study examined the drawing sequences of Thai-speaking adults and 4- to 5-year-olds during an object-copying task. After segmenting the drawing process into discrete strokes and annotating each stroke with its corresponding object part, we extracted patterns distinguishing adults' and children's drawing sequences. Results indicated that when drawing a quadrilateral part that forms the overall structure of an object (e.g., a chair's backrest), Thai adults complete it with multiple strokes, while children typically use one stroke. Moreover, when drawing objects with hierarchical structures (e.g., a tournament), most adults group parts belonging to the same hierarchical level, while young children tend to draw parts in physical proximity sequentially. This study proposes a method for analyzing developmental changes in drawing sequences and highlights key questions for future developmental research on drawing, object recognition, and symbolic representation.

articles.title: Occurrence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus infecting field tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) in Hawaii.
articles.abstract: In this short communication, we describe the occurrence of the emerging tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV, Tobamovirus fructirugosum) in Hawaii. Disease and pathogen surveys conducted across the state focusing primarily on field tomato production reveal the presence of ToBRFV in multiple islands, and consistent detection of the virus for several years at the same field suggests it can persist in the field. To our knowledge, this is not only the first report of ToBRFV in Hawaii, but also the first official report of its presence in commercial field for tomato production in the U.S. Analysis of Sanger sequencing data reveal a high identity (>99.4%) between the detected virus isolates and ToBRFV genome sequences reported in the database. Considering the devastating impact of the virus on tomato production, we will work with growers to identify the source of the virus infection and develop practical management strategies to mitigate its impact.

articles.title: Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling.

PURPOSE: To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling.

STUDY TYPE: Prospective.

POPULATION: Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF.
