FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences.

ASSESSMENT: MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant.

RESULTS: Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm2) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm2) were significantly decreased. LAVmax was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301).

DATA CONCLUSION: PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling.

EVIDENCE LEVEL: 2.

TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 4.

articles.title: Family Resilience and Dyadic Health Outcomes in Heart Failure: An Integrative Review of Pathways and Underlying Mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) affects more than 64 million people worldwide and places substantial physical, emotional, and financial burdens on patients and family caregivers. Although family resilience is a crucial protective factor in chronic illness, evidence concerning its role in HF dyads remains fragmented because quantitative and qualitative findings have not been sufficiently integrated across populations and study designs. This integrative review synthesized evidence on family resilience in HF patient-caregiver dyads, examined its mechanisms and asymmetric effects, and identified implications for practice and research. A systematic search of 13 databases was conducted from inception to February 15, 2026. Of 677 records identified, 34 studies met the inclusion criteria. Design-appropriate tools were used for quality appraisal, and thematic synthesis was guided by the Walsh Family Resilience Framework. Family resilience operated through three core dimensions: belief systems, organizational patterns, and communication processes. Its protective effects were mediated by mutuality, resilience, and self-efficacy and moderated by factors including disease stage and gender. Dyadic care and management patterns ranged from patient-oriented and caregiver-oriented approaches to collaborative and complementary approaches. Four intervention strategies were identified: assessment and stratification, dyadic interaction and caregiver empowerment, multi-target integration, and strengths-based care. These findings support the development of family-centered care programs to improve continuity of care, quality of life, and health outcomes in HF dyads. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to further examine the dynamic nature of family resilience.

articles.title: Lung cancer multi-subtype classification via soft-voting ensemble architecture.
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is a highly heterogeneous malignant tumour, and accurate classification of its subtypes is relevant to personalized treatment planning. However, overlapping imaging appearances and severe class imbalance make multi-subtype classification challenging. To address this problem, we propose a soft-voting ensemble of EfficientNet-B3, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and DenseNet-121. The three independently optimized backbones were selected for their complementary architectural characteristics and the framework does not explicitly disentangle or fuse their feature representations. Instead, it averages their class-probability outputs at inference. Experiments on a public dataset containing 18,500 CT-PET images show that the ensemble achieves an accuracy of 0.9865 and an F1 score of 0.9865. The class-wise recalls for adenocarcinoma, large cell carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma are 99.55%, 100.00%, 96.17%, and 98.20%, respectively. These retrospective image-level results support further investigation of the framework as a potential radiologist-assistance tool.

articles.title: Optical Coherence Tomography can identify Non-Ischemic Lesions that have a Benign Outcome from those with High-Risk of Future Events. Insights from a Patient Level Pooled Analysis of COMBINE (OCT-FFR) and PECTUS-Obs Prospective Natural History Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether all lipid-rich plaques (LRP) or only thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFA) are at risk for future events, remains unclear.

METHODS: Individual patient data from two prospective studies, the COMBINE FFR-OCT and PECTUS-obs trials, performed respectively in a diabetes mellitus (DM) and myocardial infraction, (MI) patients, were pooled. Patients carrying ≥1 fractional-flow reserve (FFR) negative, optical coherence tomography (OCT) -assessed, lesions (target lesions) were divided in two groups. The first group represented patients with non-LRP and the second those with LRP. The second group was further divided in LRP-TCFAs and LRP thick-cap fibroatheromas (ThCFAs). Patients with plaque rupture or erosion were further excluded from the Non-LPR and ThCFA groups. The primary endpoint was target-lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction and target-lesion revascularization at 2 years.

RESULTS: Pooling of the two trials resulted in 722 patients carrying non-destabilized, ≥1 FFR-negative, OCT assessed lesions, of which 165 (22.8%) had non-LRP while 557 (77.2%) had LRP. In the LPR group, 224 patients (40.2%) had TCFA morphology. The primary endpoint was 29(5.2%) vs 4(2.4%) (HR 2.21, CI: (0.78-6.28), p= 0.14) in the LRP versus non-LRP groups. However, within LRP groups TCFAs were associated with a significantly higher primary endpoint rate than ThCFAs; 20 (8.9%) vs 9 (2.7%), (HR 3.22, CI: 1.46-7,11, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: At 2 years only TCFAs were associated with a high rate of TLF while the remaining non-ischemic LRP and non-LRP plaques had a very benign outcome under optimal statin-based medical treatment.

articles.title: Interpreting the Magnitude of Benefit in Transcatheter Tricuspid Repair: Population, Endpoints and Crossover.
Dapagliflozin and Right Ventricular Function in Chronic Heart Failure: Discrepancies in the Reported Data.
The protein phosphatase 2A catalytic subunit Pph22 partners with Tap42 and Rrd2 to control viability and virulence in Cryptococcus neoformans.
articles.abstract: Protein phosphatase 2A regulates eukaryotic signaling, but the function of its associated regulators remains poorly understood in the human fungal pathogen Cryptococcus neoformans. Here, we used affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry and identified 81 candidate proteins associated with the catalytic subunit Pph22, including the scaffold subunit Tpd3, the regulator Tap42, and the protein phosphatase methylesterase 1. Conditional-expression and meiotic spore analyses supported an essential role for TAP42 in viability. We identified CNAG_05505 as the Rrd2 ortholog and detected an interaction between Rrd2 and Pph22 in a yeast two-hybrid assay. Deletion of RRD2 impaired thermotolerance, altered responses to multiple stresses and antifungal agents, reduced melanin and capsule production, delayed sexual development, and inhibited titan cell formation. Mutants also displayed altered cell wall staining and reduced expression of genes involved in chitin synthesis and deacetylation. RRD2 deletion increased basal Hog1 phosphorylation, whereas PPH22 overexpression reduced it. Double-mutant analysis revealed phenotype-dependent genetic interactions between RRD2 and HOG1. Although RRD2 deletion did not significantly alter overall survival in the Drosophila infection assay, it markedly attenuated virulence in mice: all mutant-infected mice survived the 70-day observation period, and fungal burdens were reduced across multiple organs at 21 days post-infection. These findings distinguish the essential contribution of Tap42 from the broad roles of Rrd2 in stress adaptation, morphogenesis, cell surface organization, and mammalian virulence, extending the functional analysis of the cryptococcal protein phosphatase 2A regulatory network.

articles.title: The 1.5-Stage Exchange for the Management of Periprosthetic Joint Infection Following Total Knee Arthroplasty: Clarification of Terminology, Review of Clinical Outcomes, and Surgical Technique.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract: ➢ A 1.5-stage approach is distinct from single-stage and 2-stage strategies for managing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI).➢ The following criteria define 1.5-stage constructs: the use of an articulating construct for the management of PJI, implantation with the intent of optimizing durability and function, and implantation without a definitive plan for a subsequent second stage.➢ The intent of a 1.5-stage approach is to balance the need for effective infection control and durable function against the operative burden of staged interventions, while facilitating future surgery if clinically indicated.➢ Because a 1.5-stage approach seeks to preserve metaphyseal and diaphyseal bone stock by forgoing the use of osseointegrated metaphyseal fixation and diaphyseal stems, revision following a 1.5-stage exchange may be less morbid than revision following traditional single- and 2-stage protocols, particularly if reinfection occurs.➢ Future research is required to standardize surgical techniques and to delineate which patients benefit the most from a 1.5-stage strategy.

articles.title: Worse Than Just the Sum of Its Parts: Polymicrobial Infection Demonstrates Synergistic Biofilm Formation and Bone Loss: A Murine Model of Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) remains a leading cause of implant failure, with high treatment failure and mortality rates. Polymicrobial PJIs, particularly those involving Staphylococcus aureus (SA) and Candida albicans (CA), may be more common and difficult to eradicate than previously recognized. These coinfections are associated with enhanced biofilm formation, antimicrobial resistance, and worse clinical outcomes, but their in vivo impact remains poorly understood.

METHODS: We compared SA, CA, and SA + CA cocultures for biofilm formation on titanium, colony-forming units (CFUs), architecture as seen with scanning electron microscopy, and antimicrobial resistance. We then adapted a chronic murine PJI model in C57BL/6J mice to quantify longitudinal SA bioluminescence, end-point SA and CA CFUs, and femoral metadiaphyseal expansion by micro-computed tomography.

RESULTS: CA coculture increased SA CFUs compared with SA monomicrobial infection and produced complex biofilm architecture on titanium. Co-biofilms showed increased resistance to vancomycin and amphotericin B. Coinfected mice had greater SA bioluminescence, 100-fold higher end-point implant CFUs of SA, and greater femoral metadiaphyseal expansion than mice with SA monomicrobial infection, without increased CA burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with SA monomicrobial infection, SA-CA coinfection enhanced SA biofilm formation, antimicrobial tolerance in vitro, and femoral remodeling in vivo, supporting a more severe bacterial-fungal periprosthetic joint infection phenotype.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Polymicrobial PJI involving SA and CA may represent a distinct phenotype characterized by enhanced SA biofilm formation and femoral remodeling, supporting further study of improved diagnostics and targeted anti-biofilm strategies.

articles.title: AlphaFold models of host-pathogen interactions elucidate the prevalence and structural modes of molecular mimicry.
articles.abstract: Pathogens exploit host cellular machinery through protein-protein interactions (PPIs), often using molecular mimicry to hijack host cellular processes. While there have been thousands of host-pathogen PPIs determined to date, the lack of structural information for these impedes the study of the prevalence of molecular mimicry and convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. To address this, we benchmarked AlphaFold2 and 3 for prediction of structures of host-pathogen interactions observing that accurate models can be retrieved when ranking by modelling confidence, despite an overall low performance. We predicted structures for 6,782 pathogen-human PPIs yielding 803 models of higher confidence. Most pathogen proteins interacting with a common human protein are predicted to do so via the same interface, suggesting a high degree of convergent evolution of protein interaction interfaces. When comparing structural models from host-pathogen and host-host interactions, we observe that a majority of pathogen proteins are predicted to target existing human PPI interfaces. We categorized instances of mimicry into different modes, occurring at different frequencies: 1) via the same domain family (least common); 2) via a similar structural motif; and 3) via a similar linear peptide (most common). We selected examples of linear peptide interactions for binding assay testing, confirming 8 out of 12 predicted interfaces, including 3 viral linear peptide interactions. This validates AlphaFold's ability to model some host-pathogen interactions and the mechanisms underlying molecular mimicry. This work showcases the value of large-scale structural modelling to study convergent evolution of host-pathogen interactions and how molecular mimicry may contribute to infection or host defense.

articles.title: Calcium Overload, an Underrecognized Cause of Persistent Hypercalcemia in Young Children with Trisomy 21: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calcium overload in trisomy 21 is a rare and underrecognized cause of persistent hypercalcemia in infants and young children with Down syndrome. This systematic review aimed to characterize its clinical presentation, biochemical features, nutritional patterns, and treatment outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed and BASE were systematically searched for publications available up to August 2025, supplemented by searches in TRIP Database, Semantic Scholar, CORE Database, and Google Scholar. Reports describing persistent hypercalcemia in children with trisomy 21 without an identified alternative cause were eligible. Clinical, biochemical, nutritional, and treatment-related data were synthesized descriptively.

RESULTS: Twelve previously published cases met the inclusion criteria. The median age was 24.3 months (range, 10-48 months). Failure to thrive was reported in 11/12 patients (91.7%) and recurrent vomiting in 6/12 (50%). The characteristic biochemical pattern comprised PTH-independent hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and impaired renal function. Nephrocalcinosis was documented in all cases, including one diagnosed postmortem. Among the 10 patients with available nutritional information, 8 (80%) had a daily calcium intake exceeding the recommended allowance for their age, and almost all were predominantly fed infant formula or cow's milk. Conventional treatment measures did not achieve sustained normocalcemia in the reported cases, whereas all patients showed a marked reduction in serum calcium following initiation of a calcium-restricted diet. Available follow-up indicated generally stable calcium homeostasis, although renal impairment persisted in all patients, for whom follow-up laboratory studies on kidney function were available.

CONCLUSION: The systematic review identified exclusive milk feeding as the uniform feature associated with PTH-independent hypercalcemia in children with Down Syndrome. The universal presence of nephrocalcinosis and failure to thrive at diagnosis across all reported cases indicates significant diagnostic delay, likely due to limited clinical awareness and biochemical testing. Early recognition and intervention are critical to prevent long-term complications such as chronic kidney disease. To increase awareness among health care professionals, calcium overload merits inclusion as a rare complication to clinical guidance for young children with trisomy 21.

articles.title: The Chlamydia trachomatis secreted effector CebN targets nucleoporins and Rae1 to antagonize STAT1 nuclear localization.
articles.abstract: To usurp host defenses and establish a replicative niche, obligate intracellular pathogens are tasked with remodeling the host cell using a discrete repertoire of effector proteins. For Chlamydia trachomatis (C.t.), the identification of secreted proteins and their host targets, as well as the elucidation of their functions, has been particularly challenging given the inherent obstacles in applying genetics to an obligate intravacuolar pathogen. Using affinity purification-mass spectrometry, we defined host interaction partners for 21 secreted effector proteins, providing the first comprehensive type III secretion system (T3SS) effector-host interactome generated in the context of infection. Here we elucidate the function of CebN (CT584). We show that the C-terminus of CebN binds multiple nucleoporins and Rae1, host factors previously associated with viral immune evasion. Remarkably, we show that CebN localizes to the nuclear envelope not only in infected cells but also in uninfected bystander cells. Using C.t. mutants in which CebN is depleted as well as transfected CebN, we demonstrate that CebN is both necessary and sufficient to perturb STAT1 nuclear localization. Furthermore, the CebN mutants exhibit reduced intracellular replication and smaller inclusions, demonstrating a critical role for CebN in C.t. intracellular survival. Together, these findings expand our understanding of chlamydia effector biology and highlight bacterial strategies for manipulating host defenses at the nuclear pore.

articles.title: Depression, diabetes, hypertension and the risk of incident dementia: a 3-million-person multicenter cohort study using Italian administrative health data.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To address dementia as a major public health challenge, we evaluated the impact of hypertension, diabetes, depression, and their interactions on dementia onset using an Italian common data model.

METHODS: A cohort of over 3 million individuals aged 50 years or older, initially free from dementia, depression, diabetes and hypertension, was followed across five Italian regions and cities (2011-2022). All pathological conditions were identified from algorithms applied to administrative health data. Time-dependent exposures were analyzed using competing risks regression, adjusted for confounders, with mortality as a competing event, and pooled via meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Of the total cohort, 33% lived in Latium, 29% in Piedmont, 27% in Tuscany, 6% in Bologna and 4% in Trapani. The five cohorts showed similar mean age (63-65 years) and a slight predominance of women (52-55%). Dementia risk was strongly associated with depression (sub-hazard ratio [SHR]=4.55; 95% CI: 3.22-6.42), followed by diabetes (SHR=1.33; 1.08-1.63) and hypertension (SHR=1.11; 0.95-1.29). No significant exposure interactions were observed. A 3-year lag sensitivity analysis confirmed these associations with attenuated effect sizes.

DISCUSSION: Depression showed the strongest association with dementia onset. These findings highlight the crucial need for early interventions on psychiatric and metabolic risk factors and support the use of common data models for multi-regional epidemiological research.

articles.title: Heterotopic ossification: a comprehensive narrative review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, prevention, and emerging therapies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterotopic ossification is the formation of mature bone in extraskeletal soft tissues after trauma, orthopaedic surgery, burns, or neurological injury.

REVIEW FINDINGS: Pathogenesis involves mesenchymal stem cell differentiation driven by bone morphogenetic protein, transforming growth factor beta, Wnt/beta-catenin, and hypoxia-inducible factor signalling within an inflammatory microenvironment. Ultrasound detects the zone phenomenon approximately two weeks before radiography; magnetic resonance imaging shows striate and checkerboard patterns in pre-calcification lesions. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and low-dose radiation remain effective prophylactic strategies. Physiotherapy is central to conservative management, and extracorporeal shock wave therapy may benefit traumatic cases. Excision is reserved for symptomatic lesions causing significant functional limitation, pain, or neurovascular compromise, ideally after maturation to reduce recurrence, although earlier intervention may be feasible in selected athletes.

CONCLUSION: Palovarotene is the first disease-modifying treatment approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. An individualised, multidisciplinary approach is essential; biomarker research and targeted pharmacotherapy remain priorities.

articles.title: Tiny liver fluke, big impact: Global prevalence of Dicrocoelium dendriticum in ruminants revealed by 60 years of data (1966-2025): A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dicrocoelium dendriticum is a foodborne trematode causing dicrocoeliasis in domestic ruminants worldwide. While typically subclinical, chronic infection leads to hepatobiliary pathology, reduced productivity, and substantial economic losses through liver condemnation. Despite numerous regional reports, a comprehensive global synthesis of its prevalence remains limited.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420250652985). Literature searches across five databases (1966-2025) identified observational studies reporting the prevalence of D. dendriticum in ruminants. Data were synthesized using a random-effects model to calculate pooled prevalence and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed via Cochran's Q and I2, while publication bias was evaluated using Egger's regression test.

RESULTS: From 4,203 records, 115 articles comprising 194 datasets and over 49 million ruminants were included. The global pooled prevalence was 9.07% (95% CI: 8.61-9.81%) with extremely high heterogeneity (I2 = 100%, P < 0.001). By host, the highest prevalence was in cattle (14.12%), followed by sheep (10.91%). Infection was higher in females (58.85%) than in males (41.14%) and peaked in summer (25.14%). Geographically, Africa reported the highest prevalence (17.90%) and Asia the lowest (4.29%). Temporal analysis indicated a declining trend from 22.12% (1966-2000) to 8.03% (2021-2025). Evidence of publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: D. dendriticum remains widely distributed with a moderate global prevalence, varying by region, season, and host species. High heterogeneity and evidence of publication bias necessitate cautious interpretation. These findings underscore the need for standardized diagnostic protocols and region-specific control strategies.

articles.title: Protein and Energy Intake and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Acute Kidney Injury during Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Secondary Analysis of a Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence on nutritional support's impact on outcomes in critically ill AKI patients receiving CRRT is limited. We evaluated associations between delivered energy/protein intake and mortality in this population.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital (March 2024-November 2025, NCT06254703), including critically ill adults with AKI on CRRT. Daily protein and calorie delivery were calculated from enteral, parenteral, and non-nutritional sources (glucose-containing solutions, propofol, citrate). Effluent urea nitrogen was measured daily to calculate normalized protein catabolic rate (nPCR). Outcomes included 28- and 90-day mortality, dialysis independence, renal recovery at days 28/90, and RRT-free days at day 28.

RESULTS: Among 100 patients (median age 66 [IQR 51-77], 58% male, 54% 28-day mortality), non-survivors received less energy (15.8 vs 24.8 kcal/kg/day, p=0.001) and protein (0 vs 0.72 g/kg/day, p=0.002) than survivors. A J-shaped association linked protein intake to 28-day mortality: the lowest quartile (<0.09 g/kg/day) had markedly higher mortality (adjusted HR 8.63, 95% CI 3.75-19.8, p<0.001) after adjusting for sex and modified NUTRIC score. This quartile also showed the lowest dialysis independence and renal recovery rates at day 28 and fewest RRT-free days versus higher-intake quartiles. Total protein intake weakly correlated with nPCR (r=0.15, p=0.003) but not with BUN-to-creatinine ratio (r=0.09, p=0.07).

CONCLUSION: In this hypothesis-generating analysis of critically ill AKI patients on CRRT, inadequate protein and energy delivery was associated with higher mortality, and lower protein intake with worse kidney outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of nutritional support during the first week after CRRT initiation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06254703.

articles.title: Deep Learning-Derived Cardioembolism Probability from Diffusion-Weighted Imaging Predicts Occult Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Multicentre Validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification remains the dominant framework for ischaemic stroke aetiology, yet inter-observer agreement rarely exceeds κ 0.6. Deep learning algorithms trained on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) have shown retrospective promise, but prospective multicentre validation is lacking.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective diagnostic accuracy study across nine stroke centres in Korea. Consecutive patients with acute ischaemic stroke who underwent DWI within seven days of onset were enrolled between May and September 2023. A commercially deployed convolutional neural network classified each case into four modified TOAST categories (large-artery atherosclerosis [LAA], small-vessel occlusion [SVO], cardioembolism [CE], and other/undetermined) and generated a continuous CE probability score. The reference standard was site-specific expert adjudication based on the complete diagnostic workup.

RESULTS: Among 617 patients (mean age 68.9 years, 62.2% male), overall agreement was 75.7% (Cohen's κ 0.643, 95% CI 0.594-0.691). CE sensitivity reached 95.5% and SVO sensitivity 90.6%. Among 426 patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF), the CE probability score predicted newly detected AF with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.722 (95% CI 0.634-0.806). The highest-risk quintile showed an AF rate of 17.1% (number needed to screen [NNS] 5.9) versus 4.9% (NNS 20.2) in the remaining quintiles.

CONCLUSIONS: A DWI-based deep learning algorithm achieved substantial agreement with expert stroke neurologists for stroke classification. The CE probability score predicted occult AF from a single DWI sequence. This exploratory finding warrants confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Ivermectin inhibits intestinal extracellular vesicle release and alters immune-related protein cargo in Ascaris suum.
articles.abstract: Ivermectin is an important broad-spectrum anthelmintic used to treat nematode parasites including gastro-intestinal infections of humans and animals. The mode of action for ivermectin is understood to involve activation of inhibitory glutamate-gated chloride channels (GluCls). Ivermectin has also been reported to inhibit the release of extracellular vesicles (EVs). We found that EVs are released from the whole intestine of the gastro-intestinal parasite, Ascaris suum. Proteomic analysis identified 1,574 proteins within these intestinal EVs, including 100 nematode proteins with putative immune-associated functions based on homology to proteins involved in host immune processes and 140 proteins with predicted digestive functions. Ivermectin changed the abundance of the immune-associated cargo of intestinal EVs, p < 0.001. Comparative analysis following ivermectin exposure revealed 38 candidate proteins that were differentially abundant including 11 putative immune-related proteins (e.g., transthyretin-like proteins, a small heat-shock antigen, a phospholipase A2, and the NF-κB subunit p105). The ivermectin inhibition of intestinal EV release was concentration-dependent with an IC50 of 64 nM. We also identified the expression of GluCl subunit receptor genes in the Ascaris intestine. The potent inhibitory effect of ivermectin on the release of these EVs from the nematode intestine, the accompanying changes in the immune-related cargo and the expression of GluCl channel subunits, shed further light on the site and mechanisms of action of this important anthelmintic.

articles.title: Transient intracellular survival of Leptospira spp. within free-living amoebae.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic disease caused by pathogenic Leptospira spp., which persist in soil and water environments for extended periods of time. The mechanisms enabling this environmental survival remain elusive. Free-living amoebae (FLA) are widespread protozoa that act as reservoirs or "Trojan horses" for numerous bacterial pathogens, protecting them from stress and contributing to their persistence. Whether pathogenic Leptospira exploit similar interactions with FLA has not been resolved.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: Using live confocal microscopy, flow cytometry, and gentamicin protection assays, we investigated the interactions between pathogenic (Leptospira interrogans) and saprophytic (Leptospira biflexa) leptospires with three FLA species: Acanthamoeba castellanii, Dictyostelium discoideum, and Hartmannella vermiformis. While rapid internalization was observed, entry was only partially dependent on actin-driven processes and was enhanced by the presence of live bacteria. Following internalization, bacteria persisted for at least 48h as indicated by colony-forming assays. However, no evidence of intracellular replication was detected. The number of fluorescently labeled leptospires progressively declined over time, providing further evidence of leptospires survival without multiplication. Finally, analysis of environmental soils in New Caledonia showed co-occurrence of FLA and Leptospira. Soil-derived FLA also internalized pathogenic Leptospira in vitro, showing that these interactions extend to natural isolates.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Our results demonstrate that free-living amoebae internalize both pathogenic and saprophytic leptospires and that a fraction of internalized bacteria remains viable. These findings establish transient intracellular survival of Leptospira within FLA that may contribute to the ecological maintenance of Leptospira. These findings pinpoint FLA as potential components of the environmental phase of Leptospira that could play a role in shaping leptospires survival strategies relevant for transmission and host infection.

articles.title: Estimation of annual exposures and antibody kinetics against norovirus GII.4 variants from English serology data, 2007-2012.
articles.abstract: Norovirus in humans is highly contagious, causing diarrhoea and vomiting, and is especially common in young children. Winter incidence varies annually, and previous research indicates that the change of dominant norovirus variant is followed by high incidence, but having a clear mechanism to explain this observation could support better prediction of epidemics. Here we analyse unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade data from 656 children in England collected via opportunistic sampling between 2007-2012 using a mathematical model of multi-variant antibody kinetics to infer metrics such as annual attack rates and age-specific infection rates. Analysis reveals that overall infection rates with norovirus GII.4 were 205 infections per 1000 person-years (posterior median; 95% credible intervals: 191-210) with a range across years of 36-486 infections per 1000 person-years (range of posterior medians). Infection rates were lowest in children aged under 1 year at 161 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 121-210) and highest in children aged 5 years and older, at 250 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 213-289). The annual attack rate was highest in 2002, coincident with transition of the dominant variant to Farmington Hills, and frequently observed with emergence of new variants, but not always. Parameter estimates indicate moderate evidence for the immune imprinting hypothesis: a stronger antibody response to variants encountered earliest in life. Infection rates estimated here are higher than incidence reported within similar settings based on disease only and is consistent with considerable asymptomatic infection. The combined use of multi-variant antibody data and a mathematical model provide key insights on the natural history of norovirus variants which can inform epidemic planning.

articles.title: Simultaneous clavicle and rib fracture fixation in patients with severe chest wall injuries is associated with improved outcomes: A pilot study.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Simultaneous clavicle open reduction and internal fixation (Clavicle-ORIF) with surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRFs) is an understudied but potentially beneficial strategy. We compared outcomes between patients undergoing simultaneous Clavicle-ORIF with SSRF (Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF) and those undergoing SSRF alone (SSRF-Alone) for severe chest wall injury in a pilot study to determine if there is a benefit for further research on this approach.

METHODS: A prospective, 2016-2025 IRB-approved database of adults undergoing SSRF at a Chest Wall Injury Collaborative Center was queried for patients with displaced clavicle fractures. Patients undergoing Clavicle-ORIF simultaneously with SSRF were compared with patients with displaced clavicle fractures for a retrospective cohort. Outcomes were daily morphine milligram equivalents, mechanical ventilation, intensive care unit days, and hospital length of stay.

RESULTS: Of 60 consecutive patients with displaced clavicle fractures, 52 (86.7%) had complete data, of whom 17.3% underwent simultaneous Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF. The groups were similar in age (52 vs. 57 y) and injury severity (New Injury Severity Score 22 vs. 27; RibScore 4 vs. 3). Mortality was low, with 2 deaths, both in SSRF-Alone. Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF was associated with significantly fewer intensive care unit days (2 [1-3] vs. 5 [3-11], p=0.005) and less mechanical ventilation requirement (0% vs. 42%, p=0.02). Median and maximum daily morphine milligram equivalents were lower but not statistically different for Clavicle-ORIF+SSRF (38 [30-59] vs. 62 [30-83], p=0.25; and 67 [45-155] vs. 112 [61-140], p=0.61).

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study demonstrated that in patients with combined rib and clavicle fractures undergoing SSRF, simultaneous clavicle fixation has the potential to improve outcomes. The study was limited by a small sample size, but it justifies further research on the benefits of simultaneous clavicle fixation with SSRF. (J Trauma Acute Care Surg. 2026;00: 000-000 Copyright © 2026 Wolters Kluwer Health, LLC. All rights reserved.).

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Pilot Retrospective Cohort; Level III.

articles.title: Global, regional, and national burden of stroke and its pathological subtypes attributable to non-optimal temperatures, 1990 - 2021: A systematic analysis from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021 with future projections to 2036.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-optimal temperatures are significant environmental drivers of stroke. This study comprehensively evaluated the global, regional, and national burden of stroke and its pathological subtypes (ischemic, IS; hemorrhagic, HS) attributable to non-optimal temperatures from 1990 to 2021, and projected its future trajectory.

METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease 2021 study, we analyzed age-standardized mortality (ASMR) and DALY rates (ASDR) for temperature-attributable stroke across 204 countries/territories. Das Gupta decomposition quantified contributions of population aging, growth, and epidemiological changes. Age-Period-Cohort (APC) modeling disentangled longitudinal trends, and Bayesian APC and ARIMA models projected burdens to 2036.

RESULTS: From 1990-2021, the global stroke burden shifted from cold- to heat-dominance. Cold-related ASMR declined significantly, while heat-related metrics increased, especially in low/low-middle SDI regions. An "aging paradox" was observed in high-SDI regions, where aging offset epidemiological gains. IS exhibited a higher temperature-attributable age-standardized mortality rate, whereas HS accounted for a higher temperature-attributable DALY rate. Cold-attributable stroke burden was higher among females, while heat-attributable burden was higher among males at the population level. A strong cohort effect revealed lower attributable risk in younger birth cohorts, likely reflecting broad improvements in living conditions, public health, and healthcare accessibility over time. Projections to 2036 suggest an overall declining burden, but heat-related ischemic stroke risk remains a persistent challenge.

CONCLUSIONS: Our empirical findings demonstrate a shifting global stroke landscape characterized by declining cold-attributable burden alongside an escalating heat-attributable risk profile, heavily modulated by population aging and regional development levels. While this study directly identifies the demographic and geographical targets of thermal stroke vulnerability, the broader climate adaptation and precision public health strategies discussed represent evidence-informed recommendations derived from external literature, highlighting the critical need for future interventional studies to evaluate these targeted policies.

articles.title: Automated action potential parameter analysis for reproducible electrophysiological measurements in neurons.
articles.abstract: Quantitative analysis of action potential (AP) waveforms is central to studies of neuronal excitability, ion channel function, disease mechanisms and pharmacological modulation. However, AP analysis is still often performed using partially manual workflows or proprietary software environments that can constrain the amount of information extracted from APs and limit reproducibility, transparency and throughput. Here, we present a freely available, open-source software tool for extracting AP parameters, developed for use with the OriginLab software package Origin/OriginPro. APpar detects APs from membrane voltage recordings using a user-defined derivative criterion and calculates a comprehensive set of excitability parameters, including resting membrane potential, voltage threshold, overshoot, afterhyperpolarization (AHP), AP amplitude, rise and decay time, AP duration, AP half-width, AP width at 0 mV, AP area above voltage threshold, dV/dtmax, dV/dtmin and interspike interval for the respective AP. Because AP threshold is a particularly sensitive and method-dependent measurement, APpar includes a TRUE-threshold validation algorithm. After the initial forward dV/dt threshold crossing is identified, the software finds AP overshoot, searches backward to the closest preceding local dV/dt maximum, then searches backward to the user-defined dV/dt crossing and recalculates AP parameters from this validated threshold point. We validated APpar using APs from dorsal root ganglion neuron current-clamp recordings, including copied identical APs, current-evoked repetitive firing and long-duration spontaneous firing. The software produced stable measurements from identical copied APs and extracted dynamic changes in AP parameters across repetitive and spontaneous firing sequences. APpar provides a transparent, customizable and Origin-compatible framework for reproducible AP analysis in neuronal electrophysiology. KEY POINTS: Action potential (AP) waveforms contain important information about neuronal excitability and function of the underlying ion channels, but their analysis is often performed using partially manual, labour-intensive workflows, constraining the amount of information extracted from each AP, which can limit reproducibility and throughput. Measurements such as AP threshold, amplitude and duration depend strongly on how threshold is defined, creating variability between studies and laboratories. We developed APpar, a freely available open-source software tool that automatically detects APs and extracts a comprehensive set of waveform and excitability parameters within the widely used Origin/OriginPro environment. APpar incorporates a novel TRUE-threshold (Temporally Reversed Unsupervised Extraction of the Threshold) validation algorithm that improves the consistency of derivative-based threshold detection while preserving user control over physiologically meaningful analysis settings. Validation using dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron recordings showed that APpar provides stable measurements and enables efficient analysis of single AP, repetitive and spontaneous firing, supporting reproducible studies of neuronal excitability and ion channel function.

articles.title: DEL-1 deficiency exacerbates inflammation-driven cardiac dysfunction during angiotensin II-induced hypertension.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is associated with inflammatory activation in the heart that contributes to cardiac remodelling and functional impairment, yet the mechanisms that regulate these cardiac inflammatory responses remain incompletely understood. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) is a secreted immunomodulatory glycoprotein that regulates leukocyte recruitment and inflammation resolution; however, its constitutive role in cardiac inflammation and remodelling during hypertension has not been defined. Here, we investigated the function of DEL-1 during angiotensin II (ANGII)-induced hypertension using Del1-deficient mice. Echocardiographic analysis revealed a distinct temporal pattern of cardiac remodelling during ANGII infusion. Del1KO mice developed early systolic dysfunction accompanied by diastolic alterations three days after ANGII infusion, whereas wild-type (WT) littermates maintained preserved systolic performance at this stage. Importantly, these functional differences occurred in the absence of differences in arterial pressure, suggesting a blood pressure independent mechanism. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated markedly enhanced recruitment of neutrophils and inflammatory Ly6Chi monocytes into Del1KO hearts during the early phase of hypertension, indicating amplified inflammatory activation. This was accompanied by activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment, characterized by an early expansion of long-term haematopoietic stem cells, followed by a transient increase in haematopoietic progenitor populations during the intermediate phase of hypertension. During later stages of hypertension, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice but was accompanied by exaggerated hypertrophic remodelling and increased cardiac fibrosis. Together, these findings identify DEL-1 as an endogenous regulator that restrains early cardiac inflammation at the onset of hypertension and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during prolonged hypertensive stress. KEY POINTS: Hypertension is associated with cardiac inflammation and remodelling, but endogenous mechanisms that restrain early inflammatory cardiac injury remain incompletely defined. Developmental endothelial locus-1 (DEL-1) deficiency caused early systolic dysfunction and diastolic alterations during angiotensin II-induced hypertension, despite no early difference in arterial blood pressure. Loss of DEL-1 amplified early recruitment of neutrophils and Ly6Chi inflammatory monocytes to the heart and was associated with activation of the bone marrow haematopoietic compartment. At later stages, systolic function partially recovered in Del1KO mice, but this was accompanied by exaggerated fibrotic remodelling and increased profibrotic gene expression. These findings identify endogenous DEL-1 as a protective regulator that limits early inflammatory cardiac injury and supports balanced cardiac adaptation during hypertensive stress.

articles.title: A Case of Recurrent Microsporidial Keratoconjunctivitis Related to Asymptomatic Parrots Exposure.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To report the first documented case of recurrent microsporidial keratoconjunctivitis (MKC) associated with asymptomatic pet parrot exposure.

METHODS: Single case report.

RESULTS: A 46-year-old healthy woman presented with recurrent unilateral MKC. Corneal scraping cytology demonstrated microsporidia, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of corneal tissue was positive for Encephalitozoon hellem. The patient also had exposure to asymptomatic pet parrots. Although the condition initially improved with topical therapy, it subsequently recurred while the original topical regimen was still being continued. The patient initially declined parrot isolation and source-control measures and agreed to them only after the third PCR test of parrot feces became positive for E. hellem. Resolution without recurrence was achieved only after parrot isolation and environmental decontamination were implemented.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first reported case worldwide of recurrent MKC related to asymptomatic pet parrots. Unlike previously reported parrot-associated cases, serial fecal PCR testing was performed in the asymptomatic parrots in this study, and fecal PCR results ultimately became positive for microsporidia. These findings suggest that asymptomatic parrots may represent overlooked pathogen carriers and may shed microsporidia intermittently in feces. Accordingly, the diagnosis and management of parrots should not be overlooked during treatment of MKC. Importantly, this report is also the first to establish and apply a source-control strategy incorporating parrot isolation and environmental decontamination, and clearly defined topical ocular and systemic medications are provided as a practical reference for clinical management.

articles.title: Effects of Visual Feedback-Based Closed-Loop Dynamic Rehabilitation Training on Post-Stroke Gait Muscle Synergy and Entropy Features.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: Visual feedback-based closed-loop dynamic balance training (VFCBT) has been clinically shown to significantly enhance the effects of conventional rehabilitation training (CRT) on post-stroke gait recovery, but its effects on gait muscle characteristics are unclear. This study enrolled 46 patients with stroke, of whom 25 underwent CRT incorporating VFCBT, and 21 performed CRT alone. All patients completed four weeks of rehabilitation, with gait kinematics and surface electromyography from four bilateral lower-limb muscle pairs recorded simultaneously before and after training. To investigate muscle characteristics in greater detail, the full gait cycle and its four subphases were analysed as five gait phases. Muscle synergy, fuzzy approximate entropy (fApEn), and transfer entropy (TE) quantified muscle activity across phases. Results showed VFCBT and CRT increased muscle synergy number and sparsity, with greater increases after VFCBT in most phases. Across gait phases, seven VFCBT-specific and three CRT-specific population-level synergy patterns were identified, with dominant muscle in the limb preparing for or undergoing swing and the supporting limb, respectively. Affected-side muscles' fApEn increased after VFCBT but decreased after CRT in the unaffected-side swing phase (P < 0.05), indicating that VFCBT significantly enhanced muscle activation complexity. In the same phase, TE differed significantly between groups mainly in one direction within affected-side muscle pairs (P < 0.05), increasing after VFCBT but changing little after CRT, reflecting significant and selective enhancement of intermuscular information transfer by VFCBT. To our knowledge, this study provides novel evidence on VFCBT's effects on poststroke gait muscle characteristics, offering new insights into neuromuscular mechanisms underlying VFCBT-related gait improvement and informing targeted rehabilitation.

articles.title: Dynamics of parasitemia, symptoms and biomarkers during growth phase in malaria volunteer infection studies: implications for the development of highly sensitive Rapid Diagnostic Tests.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid diagnostic tests for malaria are based on two predominant biomarkers: Plasmodium falciparum histidine rich protein 2 (PfHRP2) and Plasmodium lactate dehydrogenase, the latter of which may be either genus specific (PanLDH) or Plasmodium vivax specific (PvLDH). However, these tests have reduced sensitivity at low parasitemia, and their relationship to early clinical symptoms is poorly understood.

METHODS: Using longitudinal data from 24 participants from two volunteer infection studies, one P. vivax (n=8) and one P. falciparum (n=16), we characterised the relationship between parasitemia measured by qPCR and levels of PfHRP2, PfLDH, and PvLDH in early symptomatic malaria infection prior to treatment.

RESULTS: Symptoms attributed to malaria were observed in 87.5% of P. vivax and 43.8% of P. falciparum participants prior to treatment. In P. vivax infections, symptoms first presented between 6.1 - 8.8 days post-inoculation at parasitemias of 0.403 - 27.264 parasites/µL and PvLDH levels of 0.090 - 3.374 pg/µL. While in P. falciparum infections, symptoms first presented between 3.1 - 9 days post-inoculation at 0.012 - 184.891 parasites/µL with PfHRP2 levels of 0.004 - 7.144 pg/µL.

DISCUSSION: These results indicate that symptoms considered compatible with P. vivax and P. falciparum malaria can occur in malaria-naïve adults at parasite and biomarker concentrations below published analytical detection limits of currently available RDTs. This highlights the importance of the sensitivity of diagnostic tests for the early detection of malaria, especially in low-transmission settings.

articles.title: Exploring bacteria-phage interplay: A protocol for identifying and analyzing RNA-RNA interactions.
articles.abstract: Regulatory small RNAs play crucial roles in bacteriophage (phage)-host interactions. Here, we present a protocol for capturing in-vivo RNA-RNA interactions during phage infection using RNA interaction by ligation and sequencing (RIL-seq), along with downstream data analysis pipelines. We describe steps for phage infection, UV cross-linking, cell lysis, Hfq co-immunoprecipitation, RNA ligation, and library preparation. We then detail a computational pipeline to analyze and visualize the results. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Silverman et al.1.

articles.title: A caspase-recruitment domain checkpoint for the non-canonical inflammasome.
articles.abstract: The human cysteine proteases caspase-4 and caspase-5, as well as murine caspase-11, sense intracellular lipopolysaccharide from cytosol-invading Gram-negative bacteria. The caspase recruitment domain (CARD) of these caspases directly binds to LPS, resulting in caspase oligomerization and activation, which is also referred to as assembly and activation of the non-canonical inflammasome. Consequently, proteolytic maturation of an unconstrained membrane pore-forming gasdermin D domain causes membrane rupture and pyroptotic cell death, which contributes to the pathogenesis of sepsis. However, regulatory mechanisms that control cell death and could prevent sepsis are still largely elusive. Here we show that all three members of the human CARD-only protein (COP) family, CARD16, CARD17, and CARD18, associate with these caspases, sequester LPS away from caspases, and interfere with the critical caspase oligomerization step. Hence, COPs impair caspase activation, pyroptosis, and thereby the host responses to Gram-negative bacteria escaping the phagosome and prevent LPS-mediated excessive inflammation in mice.

articles.title: Angiogenic factors and fetal Doppler for predicting adverse perinatal outcome in late-onset small fetuses with and those without pre-eclampsia.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the predictive performance of angiogenic factors and fetal Doppler, alone and in combination, for composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) in late-onset small-for-gestational age (SGA) and fetal growth restriction (FGR), in both cases with and those without pre-eclampsia (PE), to determine whether these markers predict adverse outcomes beyond their established association with PE. As a secondary objective, we evaluated their performance for predicting subsequent PE.

METHODS: This was a retrospective observational cohort study conducted at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, Spain, between January 2016 and January 2022. The study population comprised singleton pregnancies with an estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile, diagnosed with late-onset fetal smallness between 32 + 0 and 37 + 6 weeks' gestation, with available fetal Doppler ultrasound data and angiogenic factor measurements obtained at diagnosis. Placental growth factor (PlGF), soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1) and fetal Doppler indices were measured at initial assessment. CAPO was defined as the presence of at least one of the following: 5-min Apgar score < 7, umbilical cord arterial pH < 7.0, neonatal intensive care unit admission > 48 h, stillbirth, neonatal death, respiratory distress syndrome, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, neonatal sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis, Stage-III-IV retinopathy of prematurity, Grade-III-IV intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular leukomalacia or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Predictive performance for CAPO was assessed using receiver-operating-characteristics (ROC)-curve analysis and area under the ROC curve (AUC) comparisons for fetal Doppler and angiogenic factors, alone and in combination, within logistic regression models. Prediction of subsequent PE after enrolment and before delivery was evaluated similarly as a prespecified secondary analysis. Sensitivity, false-positive rate, positive predictive value and negative predictive value were calculated. All analyses were stratified according to PE development at any time before delivery.

RESULTS: Overall, 754 pregnancies with late-onset fetal smallness were included. PE was present at diagnosis in 21/754 (2.8%) cases and developed later in 23 (3.1%) cases. CAPO occurred in 84 (11.1%) cases. In the overall cohort, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio showed the highest predictive performance for CAPO (AUC, 0.791 (95% CI, 0.721-0.861)), outperforming fetal Doppler alone (AUC, 0.649 (95% CI, 0.566-0.732); P = 0.005). This was not significantly different from the performance of PlGF alone (AUC, 0.784 (95% CI, 0.711-0.856); P = 0.810). In pregnancies without PE, the predictive performance of individual angiogenic markers alone was lower compared with that in the overall cohort, and performance was similar across markers, with no significant differences between the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, PlGF and fetal Doppler, alone or in combination. In pregnancies with PE at any time, the predictive performance of all markers was not significantly different from that observed in the overall cohort, and all markers showed comparable predictive performance for CAPO, with no clear superiority. In the prespecified secondary analysis for prediction of subsequent PE, the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio alone was the single marker that achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC, 0.884 (95% CI, 0.807-0.960)), outperforming both PlGF alone and fetal Doppler alone. Combining fetal Doppler with angiogenic factors reduced false-positive rates but did not improve sensitivity.

CONCLUSION: This study confirms the predictive value of angiogenic factors, particularly the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio, for identifying CAPO and subsequent PE in late-onset SGA/FGR. Compared with the overall cohort, the predictive performance of PlGF and the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio was significantly lower in pregnancies without PE, whereas no significant difference was observed for fetal Doppler. Nevertheless, in pregnancies without PE, angiogenic markers showed predictive performance comparable to that of fetal Doppler. These findings suggest that angiogenic factors reflect underlying placental insufficiency rather than PE alone, supporting their integration into the clinical assessment of late-onset SGA/FGR in both pregnancies with and those without PE. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: "I don't let my mental illness define me": Mental health identity among marginalized young adults with serious mental illness.
articles.abstract: Illness identity has been studied for decades. Acceptance of a mental illness is an emerging concept associated with positive outcomes; however, it has been less explored in relation to illness identity. This study used a concurrent mixed methods design to explore acceptance, illness identity, and recovery outcomes among marginalized young adults living with serious mental illness. Data include in-depth, qualitative semistructured interviews and quantitative measures, which were collected at the baseline assessment of a larger National Institute of Mental Health-funded randomized trial. Qualitative inquiry was informed by grounded theory; data were coded by multiple analysts using open coding, sensitizing concepts, and constant comparison (N = 59). Analysts enhanced rigor and reduced bias by engaging in reflexive discussions. Analysts created a joint display (Guetterman et al., 2015) integrating data to understand acceptance, along with stigma and mental health literacy. Finally, analysts explored quantitative differences in outcomes by acceptance levels. Six themes emerged: (a) continuum of acceptance, (b) acceptance "takes time" and is ever-changing, (c) acceptance can be motivated by others, (d) acceptance as a pathway to coping, (e) mental health literacy as it relates to acceptance, and (f) stigma as it relates to acceptance. Four acceptance groups were identified: (a) "high acceptance," (b) "moderate acceptance," (c) "low acceptance," and (d) no acceptance. Finally, bivariate statistics indicated that those categorized high/moderate reported higher scores on hope, t(57) = -2.48, p < .05, and treatment engagement, t(57) = -1.89, p < .10, when compared to those categorized low/no. There were no differences on clinical symptoms. Implications are discussed. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Summit on Genetics in Kidney Health: A United States Perspective.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: Genetic testing and genomics are now essential components of precision kidney care, with the potential to inform diagnosis, management, family planning, and transplant decisions. Expansion of genetic testing is increasingly feasible with continuing improvements in diagnostic yield and variant interpretation as well as declining costs. The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Genetics in Kidney Health Summit convened experts in nephrology, genetics, genetic counseling, and related disciplines, together with patients and caregivers, to identify strategies for incorporating genetic testing more fully into kidney care in the United States. Patients and caregivers described genetic testing as a possible means of obtaining clarity about the cause of disease, even when treatment options are limited, and of informing reproductive decisions and cascade testing in at-risk relatives. Reflecting these perspectives, summit participants discussed a shift from criteria-based selection toward a more inclusive testing strategy, reframing the question "who should be tested?" to "who should not be tested?" To avoid exclusion of patients who could benefit from genetic testing, testing strategies should be broad and inclusive, potentially approaching universal testing within key clinical contexts, such as early-onset disease, atypical clinical features, family history of CKD, CKD of unexplained cause, or the presence of extrarenal manifestations. To address the current shortage of experts in nephrogenetics and genetic counselors, collaboration of major American nephrology and genetics organizations is needed to enhance kidney genetics training for both trainees and practicing clinicians. Centers of excellence, which at minimum should include a nephrologist with demonstrated expertise in genetic kidney diseases, at least one genetic counselor, and access to accredited laboratories and bioinformatics, can provide guidance to community nephrologists through telemedicine, virtual case discussions, and shared protocols.

articles.title: Community-based HIV prevention among men who have sex with men (MSM) in China: challenges and lessons from international experience.
articles.abstract: In China, men who have sex with men (MSM) represent a key population increasingly affected by HIV, despite the country's low overall infection rate. More than four decades after the first reported cases of AIDS, and the global response has made remarkable advances in treatment and prevention. This paper examines the functioning of community-based HIV prevention strategies in China and compares them with successful models from Spain and Latin America. Drawing on published studies, government reports, and real-world cases, which identifies major challenges, including social stigma, low motivation for testing, privacy concerns, and limited services in rural areas. These issues affect how MSM access HIV-related support. The study also also highlights effective practices from other countries, such as peer-based education, free and private testing, and collaborations with general practitioners,which could enhance current efforts in China. The findings suggest that China should strengthen community-based outreach, improve public health integration, and more support for reducing discrimination. Such measures could increase testing rates, improve treatment follow-up, and encourage more open engagement with health services among MSM. The review may also benefit other countries facing cultural and structural barriers in HIV prevention for sexual minority groups.

articles.title: Sexual health norms on HIV and STI testing among youth experiencing homelessness in seven U.S. cities: an egocentric network analysis.
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional secondary analysis examined associations between sexual health norms within social networks of youth experiencing homelessness (YEH) and recent HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing. Egocentric social network data from the Homeless Youth Risk and Resilience Survey (2016-2017; N = 1,426) across seven U.S. cities were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Network norms included descriptive, injunctive, and communication norms across five relationship types: family, home-based peers, street-based peers, intimate partners, and service providers. HIV testing norms were associated with higher odds of HIV testing among family (AOR = 2.01, 95% CI: 1.48-2.74, p < .001), home-based peers (AOR = 2.32, 95% CI: 1.48-3.63, p < .001), street-based peers (AOR = 2.37, 95% CI: 1.57-3.58, p < .001), and intimate partners (AOR = 2.17, 95% CI: 1.55-3.04, p < .001). Intimate partner STI testing norms were associated with higher odds of STI testing (AOR = 2.37, 95% CI: 1.70-3.32, p < .001). Communication norms across multiple relationship types were also associated with testing. Female and transgender/non-binary youth had higher odds of testing than male youth. Findings highlight social network norms as potential intervention targets to improve HIV and STI testing among YEH.

articles.title: Predictive Modeling of Sarcopenia Using Machine Learning: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is an age-related syndrome characterized by muscle loss and functional decline, increasing fall risks. Early identification is crucial, yet convenient and accurate screening tools remain limited in routine practice. Machine learning (ML) models show promise for early sarcopenia detection, but their diagnostic performance and methodological quality have not been systematically quantified.

OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic performance of ML models for sarcopenia prediction, compare performance across ML algorithms, and identify key sources of heterogeneity and methodological limitations.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to April 15, 2026. Eligible studies developed or validated at least one ML model for sarcopenia and provided sufficient data to reconstruct a 2×2 contingency table. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool) developed by Moons et al. The primary analysis used a bivariate random‑effects (Reitsma) model to jointly synthesize sensitivity and specificity. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values were pooled using a univariate random‑effects model with the Hartung‑Knapp‑Sidik‑Jonkman (HKSJ) method, and 95% prediction intervals (PIs) were estimated. A secondary analysis incorporated all models using cluster-robust variance estimation (RVE). Subgroup analyses and meta‑regression explored heterogeneity. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: Twenty studies (20 prespecified index models) were included. The pooled AUROC was 0.89 (95% CI 0.82-0.93; 95% PI 0.54-0.98), with pooled sensitivity of 0.77 (95% CI 0.68-0.83; 95% PI 0.37-0.95) and specificity of 0.88 (95% CI 0.83-0.91; 95% PI 0.62-0.97). Gradient boosting had the highest pooled AUROC (0.92), but CIs overlapped across algorithms. Externally validated models had a pooled AUROC of 0.85, lower than that of internal ones (0.91). The secondary analysis of all 115 models yielded consistent results. Meta‑regression identified no significant covariates. PROBAST assessment revealed that half of the studies were at high risk of bias.

CONCLUSIONS: This review provides the first quantitative synthesis of ML‑based sarcopenia prediction models, with several innovations: (1) it provides algorithm‑stratified pooled estimates of diagnostic accuracy, (2) it formally quantifies performance across algorithms and addresses the unit‑of‑analysis issue through a 2‑tier approach, and (3) it quantifies the performance gap between externally and internally validated models. By identifying specific weaknesses-insufficient external validation, poor calibration reporting, and high risk of bias-this review offers a roadmap for improving future studies. Practically, these models may serve as cost‑effective prescreening tools. However, GRADE certainty was very low, with substantial heterogeneity, insufficient external validation, and high risk of bias, indicating that current models are not yet ready for routine deployment. Future research should prioritize rigorous external validation, transparent reporting, calibration assessment, and clinically implementable design.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251267598; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251267598.

articles.title: Questionnaire Survey on Fear-Related Behavior of Dogs and Evacuation Status of Dog Owners During the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake in Japan.
articles.journal: Journal of applied animal welfare science : JAAWS
articles.abstract: Natural disasters pose substantial challenges for the safety and welfare of companion animals and their owners. Information on pet behavior and evacuation during natural disasters is limited. We investigated fear-related behaviors in dogs and evacuation patterns of dog owners during the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake in Japan. A questionnaire survey was conducted among owners who experienced the quake. Items included dog profiles, post-quake behavior, and evacuation patterns. Data from 232 owners who were near their dogs within 1 hour after the tremor were analyzed; 96 dogs (41.4%) exhibited fear-related behaviors. The dogs' fear-related behaviors were significantly associated with their general anxiety traits and the level of fear experienced by their owners. Among the 86 evacuees, 74 evacuated with their dogs. Designated evacuation sites were the most common (58.1%). Forty-five owners stayed in vehicles, while 25 used facilities (14 separated from dogs). At evacuation sites, 24 dogs (32.4%) exhibited fear-related behaviors, and 16 (21.6%) showed problem behaviors, including barking and/or aggression. These findings provide valuable insights for improving disaster preparedness, ensuring the welfare of dogs and their owners during natural disasters.

articles.title: Large Language Models for Electronic Health Records in Emergency Department (ED) and ED-Adjacent Emergency Care-Technical Strategies, Clinical Tasks, and Workflow Integration: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in clinical text processing, but their role in emergency departments (EDs) and ED-adjacent emergency care remains unclear because ED electronic health records (EHRs) are heterogeneous, time-critical, and safety-sensitive.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to synthesize peer-reviewed evidence on LLM applications to real-world ED EHR data and ED-adjacent emergency care data, focusing on clinical tasks, technical strategies, evaluation practices, and workflow integration.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses)-guided systematic review of PubMed and Web of Science (January 1, 2022, to November 14, 2025). We included peer-reviewed English-language studies applying LLM strategies to ED and ED-adjacent EHR data. We extracted dataset characteristics, model families, task formulations (classification, summarization, and information extraction), adaptation strategies (prompting, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and agentic/hybrid workflows), evaluation metrics, and ED workflow phase. Two reviewers also independently completed a design-matched methodological quality and risk-of-bias appraisal.

RESULTS: Thirty-one studies met our inclusion criteria. Many relied on single-center datasets (n=12), relatively small sample sizes (<10,000 encounters; n=20), and English-language unstructured text alone or mixed EHR inputs combining text with structured or semistructured fields. Prompt engineering was the dominant adaptation strategy (n=27), while fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation, and hybrid/agentic pipelines were less common. Postencounter studies frequently demonstrated task-specific retrospective technical feasibility, while triage, diagnostic-support, and disposition studies evaluated heterogeneous tasks and outcomes; these nonequivalent measures were not compared as indicators of workflow maturity. Workflow-phase assignment did not imply real-time integration, particularly when model inputs were available only after the relevant clinical decision point. Overall, 22 (71%) studies were classified as technical-performance-only evaluations; clinical utility was empirically assessed in only 3 (9.7%) studies, and prospective deployment in 4 (12.9%). No study directly measured patient outcomes or downstream patient-safety outcomes attributable to LLM use.

CONCLUSIONS: Current LLM applications across ED and ED-adjacent emergency care primarily function as documentation, surveillance, and auditing assistants rather than autonomous decision engines. Progress toward safe, deployable systems will require larger multicenter datasets, external and prospective validation, safety- and fairness-centered evaluation, and governance mechanisms that support responsible clinical integration. However, most evidence remains technical or retrospective, while prospective workflow integration, empirically demonstrated clinical utility, patient safety, and patient benefit remain insufficiently evaluated.

articles.title: Association of a frailty index based on routine laboratory tests with health-related quality of life in acute ischemic stroke patients: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with adverse outcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS), but its association with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remains unclear. The frailty index based on laboratory tests (FI-Lab), derived from routinely available laboratory parameters, offers an objective measure of frailty.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the associations between FI-Lab scores and HRQoL at 3 and 12 months after AIS.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 10,626 patients with first-ever AIS from the Third China National Stroke Registry. FI-Lab scores were calculated at admission and analyzed both continuously and by quartiles. HRQoL was assessed using the 3-level EuroQol five dimensions (EQ-5D-3L) index at 3 and 12 months. Multivariable linear and logistic regression analyses were used to examine the associations between FI-Lab and HRQoL.

RESULTS: HRQoL data were available for 10,415 patients at 3 months and 10,121 patients at 12 months. After multivariable adjustment, each 0.2-unit increase in FI-Lab was associated with a lower EQ-5D-3L index at both 3 months (β = -0.020, p < 0.001) and 12 months (β = -0.017, p < 0.001). Compared with the lowest FI-Lab quartile, the highest quartile was associated with lower EQ-5D-3L index at both 3 months (β = -0.041, p < 0.001) and 12 months (β = -0.036, p < 0.001). Higher FI-Lab levels were also associated with greater odds of problems with mobility, self-care, usual activities, and pain/discomfort at both follow-ups (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher FI-Lab scores were associated with poorer HRQoL at both 3 and 12 months after AIS.

articles.title: SATAY-based chemogenomic screening uncovers antifungal resistance mechanisms and key determinants of ATI-2307 and chitosan sensitivity.
articles.abstract: Multidrug-resistant fungal pathogens are a serious threat to public health and global food security. Mitigation requires the discovery of antifungal compounds with novel modes of action along with a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing antifungal resistance. Here, we apply saturated transposon analysis in yeast (SATAY), a powerful transposon sequencing method in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, to uncover loss- and gain-of-function mutations conferring resistance to 20 different antifungal compounds. These screens identify a diverse array of novel resistance mechanisms and multiple modes of action. SATAY is performed in drug-sensitive strains to generate chemogenomic profiles for compounds that lack activity against conventional laboratory strains. This study therefore provides a significant resource for exploring cellular responses to chemical stresses. We discover that the natural antifungal chitosan electrostatically interacts with cell wall mannosylphosphate and that the transporter Hol1 concentrates the novel antifungal ATI-2307 within yeast. This latter finding presents an avenue for drug design initiatives but also unveils a straightforward evolutionary path to ATI-2307 resistance with minimal fitness cost.

articles.title: Association between Candidozyma auris candiduria and subsequent candidemia in colonized critically ill patients: a nine-year cohort study.
articles.abstract: Urinary isolation of Candidozyma auris in colonized critically ill patients is common, but its clinical significance remains poorly defined. We conducted a retrospective cohort study between May 2016 and December 2025 at a 900-bed tertiary hospital in Valencia, Spain, with endemic clade III C. auris. Patients aged 14 years or older with C. auris colonization and at least one urine culture were included. Candiduria was modeled as a time-varying exposure in cause-specific Cox models. The primary outcome was subsequent C. auris candidemia; secondary outcomes were the determinants of candiduria, urinary clearance and management. Of 513 patients, 126 (25%) developed candiduria and 94 (18.3%) candidemia. Candiduria was independently associated with subsequent candidemia (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-2.58; P = .036), as was the Candida score (adjusted HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.72-2.56; P < .001); the candiduria estimate was attenuated when candidemia within 72 hours was excluded (HR, 1.50; 95% CI, 0.95-2.36). Female sex and the Candida score were independently associated with candiduria. Among patients with candiduria, 32 (25%) progressed to candidemia after a median of 9 days; neither antifungal therapy nor urinary catheter removal or exchange, modeled as time-dependent exposures, was associated with a lower risk. Urinary clearance was documented in 29 of 115 patients with follow-up cultures (25.2%), falling to 17.4% when two consecutive negative cultures were required. C. auris candiduria identified colonized intensive care unit patients at higher risk of candidemia, but the observational design precludes causal inference and prospective confirmation is required.

articles.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined as left ventricular hypertrophy of greater than 15 mm in any part of the left ventricular wall in the absence of valvular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, or other chronic conditions causing severe left ventricular hypertrophy such as uncontrolled hypertension or cardiac amyloidosis. Most people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a normal lifespan; however, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with a 0.8% annual incidence of sudden cardiac death.

OBSERVATIONS: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy affects an estimated 0.2% of people worldwide (including more than 600 000 people in the US) and is typically diagnosed with echocardiography.
