Approximately 35% to 40% of patients report effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Approximately 30% to 40% of people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy have a pathogenic gene variant that encodes for cardiac sarcomere proteins (predominantly myosin binding protein C, myosin heavy chain, and troponin). Other patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may have a polygenic predisposition and/or nongenetic risk factors. The sarcomeric gene variants cause hypercontractility and delayed relaxation of the cardiac sarcomere, which characterizes the underlying pathophysiologic problem in people with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Approximately 60% to 70% of patients have obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction due to basal septal hypertrophy. The remainder do not have outflow tract obstruction and, therefore, have nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy should participate in regular low- to moderate-intensity physical activity (such as brisk walking, jogging) as part of a healthy lifestyle. Medical therapies such as β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) and nondihydropyridine-class calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil or diltiazem) are first-line medical therapy for patients with symptoms due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. If first-line therapies do not relieve symptoms, alternative treatments include disopyramide, which improves symptoms in approximately 60% of patients, cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten or aficamten), which improve symptoms in approximately 70% to 80% of patients, or procedures to thin the septal wall of the left ventricle, including percutaneous alcohol septal ablation, which improves symptoms in approximately 75% to 80% of patients, or surgical septal myectomy, which improves symptoms in approximately 90% to 95% of patients. Guidelines recommend that first-degree relatives of patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy undergo screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with genetic testing or echocardiography.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is caused by a monogenetic pathogenic variant in approximately 30% to 40% of patients and can cause effort-related dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, or lightheadedness. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is associated with an incidence of sudden cardiac death of 0.8% per year. First-line therapies for symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy are β-blockers (eg, metoprolol, bisoprolol, nadolol) or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (eg, verapamil, diltiazem).

articles.title: Reconceptualizing COPD-Progress, Challenges, and the Path Forward.
Population-Based Evaluation of a Multidimensional Diagnostic Schema for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: A multidimensional chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) diagnostic schema incorporating imaging and clinical features beyond airflow obstruction has been proposed. However, its implications for prevalence, case composition, and prognostic stratification in the general population remain unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the population-level classification and prognostic implications of a multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema with those of the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) definition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study used the Swedish Cardiopulmonary Bioimage Study, conducted at 6 Swedish university hospitals 2013-2018 to compare diagnostic definitions in the full cohort and in a symptom-restricted subgroup approximating routine clinical practice, with mortality follow-up through September 30, 2024. Randomly sampled adults aged 50 to 64 years with complete classification data, including postbronchodilator spirometry and chest computed tomography assessment of emphysema and bronchial wall thickening were included.

EXPOSURE: Classification according to the multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema and an operationalized GOLD definition.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: COPD prevalence, case composition, and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 29 281 participants (15011 females [51.3%]; mean [SD] age, 57.5 [4.3] years) were included; 1347 participants (4.6%) met multidimensional COPD criteria. In analyses restricted to 6016 symptomatic individuals, prevalence was similar under the multidimensional and GOLD definitions (909 [15.1%] vs 853 [14.2%]), but case composition differed. Approximately one-third of patients with multidimensional COPD (281 of 909 [30.9%]) did not meet the GOLD criteria. Across the full cohort, 438 individuals (32.5% of multidimensional COPD cases) were asymptomatic and would be unlikely to undergo diagnostic evaluation in routine symptom-driven care. During follow-up, 634 deaths occurred. Among symptomatic participants, adjusted mortality risk was increased in multidimensional-only cases (hazard ratio [HR], 2.58; 95% CI, 1.66-4.01) and those meeting both definitions (HR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.59-3.04), but not in patients with GOLD-only COPD (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.44-2.00).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this population-based cohort study, COPD prevalence was similar with a multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema to that obtained using GOLD criteria, but case composition differed substantially. The multidimensional schema identified increased mortality risk among individuals not captured by GOLD, suggesting improved prognostic stratification, while the identification of many asymptomatic cases highlights an existing detection gap in current symptom-driven care pathways.

articles.title: Long-Term Nonmalignant Chronic Health Conditions in Childhood, Adolescent, and Young Adult Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma Survivors and the Impact of Radioactive Iodine Therapy: Evidence from Real-World Data.
articles.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) is the most common endocrine malignancy in children, adolescents, and young adults (CAYA) with survival exceeding 98%. Real-world data on long-term nonmalignant chronic health conditions (CHCs) remain scarce.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize long-term nonmalignant CHCs in CAYA DTC survivors relative to cancer-free controls and explore associations with radioactive iodine (RAI) exposure.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Clalit Health Services electronic health records (Israel, 1982-2022) comparing 5267 DTC survivors (diagnosed at age < 40) with 21,062 matched cancer-free controls. Incident CHCs occurring ≥2 years post-DTC diagnosis/index-date were assessed across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, pulmonary, skeletal, autoimmune/rheumatologic, and emotional domains and were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RAI subgroup analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 14.7 years (interquartile range 8.8-23.2), the risk of developing ≥1 CHC did not differ significantly between DTC survivors and cancer-free controls (54.4% vs. 52.0%; HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.00-1.11; p = 0.066). Survivors were more likely to experience multimorbidity (≥2 CHCs 35.7% vs. 32.0%) and had higher risks of several specific organ-system conditions: osteoporosis (HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.14-1.56), chronic kidney disease (HR 1.61; 95% CI: 1.32-1.96), gastroesophageal disorders (HR 1.35; 95% CI: 1.26-1.45), dyslipidemia (HR 1.23; 95% CI: 1.16-1.32), and hypertension (HR 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Pulmonary, cardiovascular, autoimmune, hepatic, and clinically diagnosed emotional disorders did not differ significantly between groups. Exploratory analyses revealed a dose-dependent RAI risk gradient (1 course: HR 1.20; 95% CI: 1.06-1.35; ≥2 courses: HR 1.33; 95% CI: 1.16-1.52).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite excellent overall survival, CAYA DTC survivors face a modest overall increase in CHC risk alongside notably greater multisystem morbidity. RAI-associated risk trends are exploratory and need further research. These findings support risk-adapted therapy and structured long-term survivorship monitoring.

articles.title: Characterization and heterologous expression of surface polysaccharides from pathogenic Enterococcus cecorum.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic variants of the chicken gastrointestinal bacterium Enterococcus cecorum are of growing concern due to their ability to cause vertebral osteomyelitis, such as enterococcal spondylitis or "kinky back," when the bacteria infect the free thoracic vertebrae of broilers. Due to the elimination of prophylactic antibiotic feed treatment that was previously used to manage the disease, there is now a need to develop other strategies for preventing pathogenic E. cecorum infections. In this work, we describe the structural characterization of two antigenic targets, a capsular polysaccharide and a rhamnopolysaccharide. Highly conserved biosynthetic gene clusters encoding enzymes for both structures have previously been identified in pathogenic E. cecorum. We show that these polysaccharides, when present on the surface of either the native or a heterologous host, induce an immune response in broilers. Furthermore, antibodies present in those sera cross-react with different E. cecorum strains and can induce killing of the pathogen in opsonophagocytosis assays. The characterization and heterologous expression of highly immunodominant cell wall polysaccharides that are conserved across many pathogenic strains is an important step toward the development of a potential glycoconjugate vaccine against E. cecorum.IMPORTANCEEnterococcus cecorum is a bacterium normally found in the gut of healthy chickens. However, pathogenic varieties of E. cecorum expressing surface capsular polysaccharides can cause skeletal deformations in the bird if the infection becomes systemic. This leads to severe morbidity and mortality in chickens raised for meat production and to significant financial losses for poultry producers. These infections were once managed by the inclusion of antibiotics in chicken feed; but this practice has been discontinued due to concern over antibiotic resistance development. We have identified polysaccharides that are conserved on the surface of many pathogenic E. cecorum that induce protective cross-reactive immune responses in chickens when the polysaccharides are expressed on a benign bacterial carrier. As an alternative to antibiotics, this is an important first step toward the development of a vaccine that specifically targets many pathogenic E. cecorum isolates and may help to reduce financial losses while improving animal welfare.

articles.title: Postherpetic Neuralgia.
Post Vaccination Tubercular Abscess in Thigh - Was it a Vaccine-Induced or Naturally Acquired Infection?
Reducing Hypothermia Among Intramural Vaginally Born Preterm Neonates Admitted in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at a Tertiary Care Centre Using Quality Improvement Approach: Authors' Reply-2.
Efficacy of novel compression gloves and stockings for prevention oxaliplatin induced peripheral neuropathy, the randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the Egyptian National Cancer Institute
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Given that oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (OIPN) is a common and dose-limiting toxicity in colorectal cancer and that effective preventive strategies remain limited, this study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of compression therapy for the prevention of OIPN.

METHODS: We conducted a randomized controlled trial in patients with stage III colorectal cancer receiving oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy, comparing pressure-controlled compression gloves and stockings during oxaliplatin infusion with usual care. The primary outcome was the incidence of grade ≥ 2 oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy (OIPN) assessed using NCI-CTCAE. Secondary outcomes included patient-reported neuropathy (EORTC QLQ-CIPN20), neuropathic pain (DN4), autonomic symptoms (Thai COMPASS-31), pain intensity (Wong-Baker Faces Pain Scale), and quantitative sensory testing. Longitudinal outcomes were analysed using mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Twenty-five patients (17 compression, 8 control) were included in the final analysis. The incidence of grade ≥ 2 OIPN did not differ significantly between groups (17.6% vs. 25.0%, p = 1.00). However, the compression group demonstrated a significantly smaller increase in total CIPN20 scores compared with controls (median change 3.51 vs. 7.96; p = 0.04). Significant intervention-by-time interactions were observed for overall, sensory, and motor CIPN20 scores, as well as DN4 scores, indicating slower symptom progression with compression therapy. No significant differences were observed in autonomic symptoms, quantitative sensory testing, or pain intensity. There were no device-related adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Compression therapy did not significantly reduce clinician-graded OIPN but was associated with a trend toward slower progression of patient-reported neuropathy and neuropathic pain, supporting further evaluation in larger trials. (Thai Clinical Trials Registry: TCTR20221107006; registered 7 November 2022).

articles.title: Plasma proteins associated with maladaptive kidney cell states and kidney function: a single-cell-informed Mendelian randomisation study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess genetic associations with kidney function for plasma proteins linked to maladaptive kidney cell states.

METHODS: We combined donor-paired single-nucleus RNA sequencing (304,989 nuclei from 80 donors) with plasma cis-protein quantitative trait loci to define candidates across four cell states. Cis-Mendelian randomisation (MR) tested creatinine-based estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in approximately 1.2 million participants. Follow-up used CKDGen and FinnGen kidney outcomes. We performed single-signal colocalisation and a multi-signal sensitivity analysis for six prioritised candidates.

RESULTS: Of 259 candidates, 228 yielded an eGFR MR estimate and 17 met the discovery false discovery rate threshold. We found no evidence of enrichment of significant MR associations amongst candidates (odds ratio 0.66, 95% confidence interval 0.37-1.11). In the matched Olink analysis, 80.8% of candidates and 69.7% of other proteins were higher at lower eGFR (odds ratio 1.82, P = 0.0038). Six candidates met the original prioritisation criteria. Only TFPI showed directionally concordant nominal associations in FinnGen, for renal failure and diabetic nephropathy. SORT1 had the strongest shared-variant evidence with eGFR (single-signal posterior probability 0.924 at the primary prior).

CONCLUSION: Single-nucleus expression and cis-MR identified a subset of candidates for follow-up, with differing support across loci and kidney outcomes. Tissue expression contextualises the plasma associations. Cellular origin and the effects of therapeutic modulation require direct evaluation.

articles.title: Concomitant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis in TAVR candidates: phenotype, in-hospital outcomes, and CT-derived extracellular volume in an Iranian cohort.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis (AS) and transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) coexist in older patients, but optimal screening for occult ATTR-CA in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) candidates remains uncertain. This study characterized the phenotype of TAVR candidates, examined factors associated with in-hospital outcomes, and assessed whether cardiac computed tomography (CT)-derived extracellular volume (ECV) contributes to ATTR-CA detection.

METHODS: Prospective single-center cohort of 70 consecutive patients aged 60 years or older with severe AS referred for TAVR assessment between June and December 2023. All patients underwent technetium-99 m pyrophosphate (99mTc-PYP) scintigraphy and CT-derived ECV, with CT-ECV positivity defined as ECV 30% or greater. Outcomes were ascertained during the index hospitalization: mortality, acute kidney injury (AKI), length of stay, and permanent pacemaker implantation.

RESULTS: Mean age was 75.0 ± 8.4 years and 38 patients (54.3%) were men. In-hospital mortality occurred in 2 patients (2.9%), AKI in 14 (20.0%), and permanent pacemaker implantation in 15 (21.4%); median hospital stay was 6 days. PYP-positive ATTR-CA was identified in 4 patients (5.7%). CT-ECV positivity was present in 8 patients (11.4%), including 3 of the 4 PYP-positive cases. Against PYP positivity, CT-ECV showed a sensitivity of 75.0% (95% CI, 19.4-99.4), specificity of 92.4% (83.2-97.5), positive predictive value of 37.5% (8.5-75.5), and negative predictive value of 98.4% (91.3-100.0).

CONCLUSION: Against PYP scintigraphy, CT-ECV showed high specificity and negative predictive value with low positive predictive value, but these estimates rest on four PYP-positive patients and are exploratory. One PYP-positive patient had an ECV below the threshold, so a negative result cannot exclude ATTR-CA. These data support the feasibility of deriving ECV from an acquisition already performed for procedural planning; clinical usefulness as a screening strategy remains to be established.

articles.title: Chlorhexidine mouthwash for oral hygiene maintenance in orthodontic patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fixed orthodontic appliances create plaque-retentive environments that complicate oral hygiene maintenance. Chlorhexidine (CHX) mouthwash is widely used as an adjunctive antimicrobial agent, but its efficacy across different concentrations in orthodontic populations requires updated synthesis. Thus we conducted our review to fill this gap by assessing CHX mouthwash in orthodontic patients.

METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) assessing CHX mouthwash in patients undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment in four databases to May 9, 2026. Outcomes included plaque index, gingival index, bleeding percentage, bleeding severity, and probing pocket depth. A random-effects model was used in R software.

RESULTS: We ultimately had twenty-one RCTs comprising 904 patients that were included. For 0.2% CHX, significant reductions were observed for plaque index (mean difference - 0.68, 95% CI - 0.99 to - 0.38) and gingival index (MD - 0.69, 95% CI - 0.96 to - 0.42). For 0.12% CHX, reductions were smaller and with borderline significance for either outcome. Bleeding severity improved with CHX in both concentrations, while bleeding percentage and probing pocket depth showed no reliable benefit. Heterogeneity was substantial for most outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: CHX mouthwash, particularly at 0.2% concentration, provides short-term adjunctive benefits for plaque control and gingival inflammation in orthodontic patients. However, high heterogeneity and potential adverse effects support selective, time-limited use rather than routine prescription.

articles.title: Household-Level Effectiveness of Cypermethrin-Imidacloprid Combination Treatment for Cimex hemipterus Control: A Randomized Field Trial in Tehran, Iran.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bed bug (Cimex hemipterus) infestations are an increasing urban public health concern because they adversely affect skin health, sleep, psychological well-being, quality of life, and impose considerable economic costs on affected households. Despite the widespread use of pyrethroid insecticides, increasing resistance has reduced treatment effectiveness, and evidence from randomized household-based field trials evaluating alternative insecticide regimens remains limited. This study compared the effectiveness of cypermethrin monotherapy with a cypermethrin-imidacloprid combination for controlling household C. hemipterus infestations.

METHODS: We conducted a randomized household-level field study in Tehran, Iran, in which 600 households with confirmed C. hemipterus infestation were allocated equally to cypermethrin monotherapy or cypermethrin plus imidacloprid. Households were inspected on Days 1, 3, 7, 10, 14, and 30. The primary outcome was the absence of live bed bugs detected by visual inspection at Day 30. Sequencing of a subset of baseline specimens was performed to identify species and VGSC variants previously associated with pyrethroid resistance.

RESULTS: All 600 households had a recorded Day-30 assessment. No live bed bugs were detected in 294/300 (98.0%) households receiving cypermethrin plus imidacloprid compared with 111/300 (37.0%) receiving cypermethrin alone (adjusted relative risk, 2.56; 95% CI 2.25-2.92; P < 0.001). Higher baseline infestation burden was associated with a lower probability of Day-30 absence of detectable live bed bugs. Molecular analysis of 75 reported specimens identified resistance-associated VGSC variants L1014F and M918I, without establishing phenotypic resistance.

CONCLUSIONS: In this randomized household field study, the cypermethrin-imidacloprid regimen resulted in a substantially higher proportion of households with no visually detectable live bed bugs at Day 30 than cypermethrin monotherapy. However, the findings are limited to short-term entomological outcomes under the investigated field conditions. The study does not establish sustained eradication, insecticide synergy, phenotypic resistance, or a causal contribution of VGSC variants to treatment failure. Further studies incorporating longer follow-up, verified insecticide application records, and phenotypic susceptibility testing are warranted.

articles.title: Standardized framework for periprosthetic DXA in hip and knee arthroplasty: multisociety RAND/UCLA consensus recommendations.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Variability in periprosthetic DXA limits reproducibility and clinical translation. This multisociety RAND/UCLA consensus provides a standardized framework for ppDXA acquisition, analysis, ROI definition, longitudinal LSC-based interpretation, and structured reporting for hip and knee arthroplasty. The framework supports auditable measurement and reporting, does not advocate universal routine ppDXA screening, and is not intended to establish outcome-validated periprosthetic BMD thresholds.

PURPOSE: Periprosthetic dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (ppDXA) is increasingly used to measure areal bone mineral density (BMD) around hip and knee implants and to characterize longitudinal changes associated with periprosthetic bone remodeling. However, variability in acquisition, analysis, region-of-interest (ROI) definition, metal-artifact handling, and reporting limits reproducibility and hinders clinical and research implementation. This multisociety consensus aimed to develop a standardized methodological framework for ppDXA acquisition, analysis, reporting, and longitudinal interpretation in hip and knee arthroplasty.

METHODS: A multinational collaboration of scientific societies from Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, and Spain convened a 21-member multidisciplinary panel with expertise in orthopedic surgery, clinical densitometry, medical physics, bone biology, epidemiology, biostatistics, and consensus methodology. A targeted evidence review and narrative synthesis informed candidate statements on the ppDXA workflow. Statements were rated, discussed, and refined using the modified RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Recommendations with high agreement were organized into six conceptual domains: quality assurance and precision; patient preparation and positioning; scan acquisition; ROI definition and analysis; longitudinal assessment; and reporting and clinical contextualization.

RESULTS: The consensus establishes minimum and optimal standards for site-level quality assurance, implant documentation, joint-specific positioning, scan parameters, metal-removal settings, implant-anchored ROI schemes, ROI-specific precision assessment, least significant change (LSC)-based longitudinal interpretation, structured reporting, and clinical contextualization. A Minimum Dataset for Reporting and practical ROI templates are provided. An exploratory therapy-aware Green-Amber-Red interpretive framework is proposed to support structured contextual interpretation and prospective evaluation of periprosthetic BMD trajectories, in conjunction with technical validity, clinical findings, imaging, systemic bone health, and treatment context.

CONCLUSIONS: These multisociety RAND/UCLA consensus recommendations provide a standardized framework to reduce avoidable technical variability, improve reproducibility, and support auditable use of ppDXA in research and selected clinical workflows. It does not advocate universal routine ppDXA screening for all patients undergoing hip or knee arthroplasty and is intended to standardize measurement and reporting rather than to establish outcome-validated diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic periprosthetic BMD thresholds.

articles.title: The economic burden of fragility: a value-based analysis of hip fracture care and the impact of fracture liaison service in the Egyptian healthcare system.
authors: Egyptian Academy of Bone and Muscle
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: With Egypt's aging population, the long-term costs of elderly hip fractures are soaring. Research shows that specialized prevention programs easily pay for themselves by stopping repeat fractures. Adopting this preventative care model will protect national healthcare budgets while keeping Egyptian seniors independent.

BACKGROUND: As Egypt's population ages, osteoporotic hip fractures have become a primary driver of geriatric morbidity and healthcare expenditure. Despite the clinical success of surgical intervention, the long-term economic "tail" of these fractures-often extending far beyond the initial hospitalization-remains poorly quantified within the national healthcare framework.

OBJECTIVES: This systematic review explores the economic implications of hip fractures in Egypt, focusing on the 12-month "continuum of care" costs and evaluating the cost-effectiveness of Fracture Liaison Services (FLS) in reducing secondary fracture rates and systemic financial strain.

METHODS: A health-economic analysis was conducted comparing the standard of care with an FLS-guided model. Data included direct surgical costs, perioperative complication expenses, and 12-month post-acute resource utilization (rehabilitation, readmissions, and pharmacotherapy).

RESULTS: Analysis reveals that the surgical act constitutes only a fraction of the total economic burden. The 12-month continuum of care cost is significantly higher due to the "revolving door" of complications and secondary fractures. Implementation of an FLS proved highly cost-effective, with the cost of a dedicated coordinator being offset by the prevention of just 2-3 hip fractures annually. Furthermore, FLS-guided care significantly closed the "treatment gap," improving adherence to bone-protecting therapies.

CONCLUSION: Addressing the "Silo" problem in Egyptian healthcare budgeting is essential. Transitioning to a value-based model-supported by the Universal Health Insurance (UHI) and mandatory FLS accreditation-is an economic imperative. Investing in secondary prevention not only preserves the functional independence of Egyptian seniors but also ensures the long-term financial sustainability of the national healthcare system.

articles.title: Differential Association Patterns of Dietary Heme, Nonheme, and Total Iron with Diseases.
articles.abstract: Dietary iron can be regarded as a double-edged sword and has multiple implications for health. The published evidence regarding the association between dietary iron intake and diseases is inconsistent and nonheme iron is understudied. We aimed to systematically examine the associations of dietary heme, nonheme, and total iron intakes with diseases. Dietary iron intake was assessed in the UK Biobank using repeated 24-hour dietary recalls. Cross-sectional phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analyses were conducted to examine the associations of dietary heme iron, nonheme iron, and total iron intakes with 735 outcomes. For associations reaching the Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold, prospective associations with incident disease were subsequently evaluated using multivariable-adjusted Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models. Among 118,945 participants with a median follow-up of 12.7 years, prospective associations were identified between dietary heme iron intake and 18 disease outcomes, nonheme iron intake and 17 disease outcomes, and total iron intake and 14 disease outcomes, with findings generally consistent across sensitivity analyses. Heme and nonheme iron showed largely distinct disease-association patterns, with iron deficiency anemia being the only shared disease outcome identified in the primary analyses. Dose-response analyses further suggested the presence of nonlinear relationships in ~ 60% of the identified associations. Body mass index modified the associations of dietary iron intake with anemia, chronic kidney disease and functional digestive disorders. Dietary heme iron, nonheme iron, and total iron intakes showed distinct patterns of linear and nonlinear associations across diseases, with several associations showing potential effect-measure modification by BMI.

articles.title: Dark Cerebellum on Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Maps-an Early Indicator of Fulminant Cerebellitis.
articles.abstract: Fulminant cerebellitis is an essential cause of acute severe encephalopathy with raised intracranial pressure in an otherwise healthy child. If the diagnosis is delayed or missed, this can be fatal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain helps in early diagnosis. Although signal changes on T2 and fluid attenuation and inversion recovery sequences in fulminant cerebellitis have been described, findings on diffusion-weighted imaging and apparent diffusion coefficient maps have been rarely reported in the literature. While the diffusion weighted image shows a bright signal, the apparent diffusion coefficient map shows a dark cerebellum. There can be brainstem compression and cerebellar tonsillar herniation. Here we report a previously healthy eleven-year-old adolescent boy who presented with an acute onset of coma in the setting of an upper respiratory tract infection and had a dark cerebellum on apparent deficient coefficient maps of MRI brain that prompted early treatment with resultant good outcome.

articles.title: Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw in Male Patients Receiving Antiresorptive Therapies: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a potentially severe complication of antiresorptive therapy, but its epidemiology in male patients remains poorly characterized because most evidence derives from mixed-sex or predominantly female populations. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated MRONJ prevalence in antiresorptive-treated men and evaluated differences by clinical setting and treatment class.

RECENT FINDINGS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science through May 31, 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261433511). Forty-six studies involving 506,678 male patients were included, with 44 datasets contributing to the quantitative synthesis. The pooled MRONJ prevalence was 7.0% (95% CI 4.6-10.5%), with extreme heterogeneity (I² = 99.2%) and a wide prediction interval (0.5-54.9%). Prevalence was substantially higher in oncologic than osteoporotic populations (7.2% vs. 0.4%; p < 0.0001). Prostate cancer cohorts showed a numerically higher prevalence than other oncologic cohorts (13.8% vs. 7.4%), although the difference was not significant. No significant difference was observed between intravenous bisphosphonates and denosumab (14.2% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.19). Cumulative exposure and oral inflammatory burden were associated with MRONJ, whereas structured preventive dental care appeared protective. MRONJ prevalence in men is clinically relevant but highly context-dependent. Oncologic populations show substantially higher prevalence than osteoporotic populations, whereas current evidence does not demonstrate a significant difference between denosumab and intravenous bisphosphonates. MRONJ risk should therefore be interpreted according to treatment indication, cumulative exposure, and clinical setting rather than through a single global estimate. Standardized definitions and male-specific reporting are needed to improve risk stratification.

articles.title: Hematologic and biological contour of Barela dromedary she-camels in relation to pregnancy reared under pastoral conditions.
articles.abstract: This pilot study was conducted to compare hematological and biochemical parameters of pregnant and non-pregnant Barela she-camels under pastoral conditions in Thal desert. A total of 30 she-camels were selected, 15 pregnant (early to mid-gestation, non-lactating) and 15 non-pregnant (mid-lactation). Both groups were kept under same extensive management and were comparable for age, parity, body weight and body condition score. Blood samples were analyzed for hematological and biochemical parameters. Data were checked for normality and compared by independent t-test. Results are presented as mean ± SD with mean difference, 95% confidence interval, Cohen's d for effect size and Holm-adjusted P-values. Pregnant she-camels had significantly lower red blood cells (Holm P < 0.001) and higher white blood cells (Holm P = 0.033) with large to very large effect sizes, while hemoglobin and packed cell volume were lower with borderline significance after Holm correction (both Holm P = 0.074). Cholesterol and total protein showed increase in pregnancy in unadjusted test but were non-significant after Holm correction. Glucose, triglycerides, urea and creatinine did not differ between groups. The results indicate that pregnancy in Barela she-camels affects hematology and protein metabolism even under pastoral conditions. Due to small sample size (n = 15 per group) and lack of prior breed-specific data, this study should be considered as a pilot. Findings were discussed in relation to published studies and provide baseline data for future work on Barela camels.

articles.title: Recent-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: What to Do for Maximum Impact a Matter of Time, Choices and Real-world Challenges.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The aim of this narrative review is to provide a practical and current perspective on how care for recent onset atrial fibrillation (AF) can be optimized, taking into account both the principles of AF care described in current guidelines and barriers in clinical practice. Within this framework, the latest evidence on anticoagulation, long-term rate versus rhythm control and comorbidities management is presented. Areas of clinical uncertainty are illustrated to help both cardiologists and emergency medicine physicians navigate new-onset AF.

RECENT FINDINGS: Early rhythm control can improve AF outcomes among recent onset AF patients, with catheter ablation emerging as a disease-modifying strategy, leading to improved long-term outcomes and a lower rate of arrhythmia recurrences compared with antiarrhythmic drugs. Early rhythm control, together with structured risk factors modification and oral anticoagulation can strongly influence the course of AF and are particularly effective in the early stages of AF. Patient education, starting from the Emergency Department is pivotal in shaping the future trajectory of AF patients.

articles.title: Carfilzomib-associated glomerular microangiopathy presenting with progressive albumin-predominant proteinuria.
articles.abstract: Carfilzomib-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication that is typically recognized based on acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia, and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia. However, glomerular microangiopathy (GMA) without overt systemic manifestations may be underrecognized and difficult to diagnose clinically. We report a biopsy-proven case of carfilzomib-associated GMA presenting as albumin-predominant proteinuria without an increase in M-protein or overt systemic TMA. A man in his 70 s with multiple myeloma achieved a very good partial response after treatment with daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone and was subsequently switched to daratumumab, carfilzomib, and dexamethasone because of cerebral infarction. During carfilzomib therapy, myeloma remained well controlled and renal function remained stable, but progressive albumin-predominant proteinuria developed without an increase in M-protein. Kidney biopsy demonstrated focal and segmental glomerular endothelial injury with minimal podocyte involvement, consistent with GMA. Proteinuria improved after carfilzomib withdrawal, increased again following dose-reduced rechallenge, and improved again after discontinuation, strongly supporting a causal relationship. This case suggests that progressive albumin-predominant proteinuria without an increase in M-protein may warrant suspicion of carfilzomib-associated glomerular injury, even without clear evidence of systemic TMA. This hypothesis-generating observation supports consideration of kidney biopsy in patients with otherwise unexplained proteinuria during carfilzomib therapy.

articles.title: Outcomes of surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation in adults with congenital heart disease.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 42 patients (mean age, 58.5 ± 14.3 years) who underwent the maze procedure or pulmonary vein isolation concomitantly with intracardiac surgery between September 2003 and November 2022. None of the patients underwent surgery primarily for arrhythmia management.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients underwent the modified Cox maze procedure; two patients additionally underwent a combination of right atrial maze and pulmonary vein isolation, one patient underwent right atrial maze alone, and ten patients underwent pulmonary vein isolation alone. Over a mean follow-up of 39 ± 34.9 months, late mortality occurred in five patients, including two cardiac deaths. Recurrent atrial fibrillation was observed in 11 patients. Atrial fibrillation recurrence-free rates were 85.4%, 81.9%, and 75.6% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. During follow-up, one patient experienced an ischemic stroke, and three patients required implantation of a new pacemaker. Exploratory analysis suggested that advanced age at the time of surgery was associated with atrial fibrillation recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant surgical ablation for atrial fibrillation was suggested as a safe and effective treatment in adults with congenital heart disease. Earlier intervention, conducted before advanced age, may be associated with improved long-term rhythm outcomes.

articles.title: Large-for-gestational-age neonates: Associated risks and perinatal adverse outcomes in a cohort of low-risk nulliparous pregnant women.
authors: Preterm SAMBA and MAES‐I Study Group
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Large-for-gestational-age (LGA) neonates represent a public health challenge associated with severe perinatal morbidity. However, evidence focusing exclusively on healthy, low-risk nulliparous populations remains limited. We aimed to investigate maternal risk factors and adverse perinatal outcomes associated with LGA in two multicenter Brazilian cohorts.

METHODS: This secondary analysis included 1343 low-risk nulliparous women enrolled at mid-pregnancy from the prospective Preterm SAMBA and MAES-I cohorts. Neonates were categorized into LGA (>90th centile, n = 161) and adequate-for-gestational-age (AGA, n = 1182). Bivariate and multivariate Poisson regression models (adjusted risk ratios [aRR], 95% confidence interval [CI]) evaluated independent predictors of LGA and a composite of any adverse perinatal outcome (APO).

RESULTS: LGA prevalence was 10.5%. Multivariate analysis identified gestational diabetes (GDM) as the sole independent maternal risk factor for LGA (aRR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.68). Classical predictors like pre-pregnancy obesity were not significantly associated with LGA. LGA neonates faced higher rates of cesarean section delivery (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.14-3.12) and complication rates, such as preterm birth (<33 weeks), neonatal sepsis, intraventricular hemorrhage, need for mechanical ventilation, neonatal near miss, and longer hospital and NICU stays. LGA remained a robust independent predictor of composite APO (aRR 1.47, 95% CI 1.21-2.10), as did non-white status, bleeding in the first half of pregnancy, and hypertensive disorder.

CONCLUSIONS: Even in low-risk obstetric populations where classical metabolic risks are attenuated, excessive fetal growth is associated with severe perinatal morbidity. LGA also predicted adverse outcomes, reinforcing the potential benefit of systematic antenatal surveillance.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor regarding "The Impact of BMI on the Effect of Biologic Agents for Severe Asthma".
A Response to: Letter to the Editor Regarding "The Impact of BMI on the Effect of Biologic Agents for Severe Asthma".
Diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America.
articles.abstract: Neurological diseases in cattle are among the most important diagnostic challenges in veterinary practice and diagnostic laboratories. In South America, surveillance systems and diagnostic networks have progressively expanded the recognition of diseases causing nervous signs in cattle, yet available information remains fragmented across countries. This review integrates current knowledge on the main diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America, with emphasis on their clinical presentation, etiopathogenesis, pathology, and diagnostic relevance, and includes brief information on treatment, control, and prevention. For practical purposes, bovine neurologic disorders are organized according to their etiologic origin into infectious, parasitic, toxic, metabolic, neoplastic, and genetic or congenital. Among infectious conditions, rabies remains the most important viral encephalitis in the region, while bovine herpesviral meningoencephalitis, malignant catarrhal fever, listeriosis, thrombotic meningoencephalitis, and suppurative bacterial infections are also relevant differential diagnoses. Parasitic disorders such as cerebral babesiosis, Trypanosoma vivax infection, nervous coccidiosis, neosporosis, coenurosis, and amoebic meningoencephalitis are less frequent but regionally significant. Toxic and metabolic causes are highly diverse and include plant and fungal intoxications, pesticide and lead poisoning, polioencephalomalacia, hypomagnesemia, vitamin A deficiency, ketosis/fatty liver syndrome, and hypocalcemia. Less common but clinically important conditions include nervous system neoplasms and congenital or hereditary disorders. A single integrated table summarizes, for each condition, the etiologic agent, geographic distribution, affected age group and neurolocalization, main neurological syndrome, principal lesions, field diagnostic aids, samples for laboratory confirmation, laboratory diagnostic methods, and the available treatment and control measures. This review highlights the wide etiologic spectrum of bovine diseases causing nervous signs in South America and emphasizes the importance of a systematic diagnostic approach integrating epidemiology, clinical neurology, gross pathology, histopathology, and targeted ancillary tests. A better understanding of these conditions should improve differential diagnosis, therapeutic decision-making, surveillance, and preventive strategies in cattle production systems across the region.

articles.title: Monocyte distribution width as a first-line test for sepsis screening: a strategy to guide procalcitonin testing.
Management of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Italian Internal Medicine Units: a Survey from the SIMI Working Group on Hepatic Steatosis.
authors: SIMI Working Group on Hepatic Steatosis

articles.title: Ranavirus is not Detected in Amphibians from Northern, Central, and Southern Mexico.
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases threaten global biodiversity. In amphibians, the ranavirosis caused by Ranavirus (Rv) leads to severe disease and mass mortality events worldwide. In Mexico, Rv was recently found in captive bullfrogs; however, its presence in wild populations has not been detected. We sampled 207 individuals from 68 species across northern, central, and southern Mexico in regions with different amphibian diversities. None of the sampled individuals tested positive for Rv or showed clinical symptoms. This assessment of Rv in wild Mexican amphibians finds no signs of infection. Ongoing surveillance is vital to detect emerging pathogens and safeguard biodiversity-rich amphibian communities.

articles.title: Ecotoxicological risk and matrix-specific exposure of pharmaceutically active compounds in the Ankobra River, Ghana: evidence from paired water-sediment monitoring.
articles.abstract: Pharmaceutically active compounds (PhACs) are bioactive contaminants whose ecological significance depends on toxicological potency and the exposure compartment encountered by aquatic organisms. Thirty-five PhACs selected to span nine therapeutic/functional groups and contrasting physicochemical behaviours represented in African pharmaceutical monitoring literature were investigated. Paired surface water and surficial sediment samples were analysed at 20 stations along the Ankobra River, Ghana. Occurrence statistics, reproducible water sediment exposure categories, exploratory spatial analyses, and water phase risk quotients (RQs) were used for screening level prioritisation. Thirty-one compounds were detected in at least one matrix. Water was dominated by acetaminophen, ibuprofen, tramadol, atenolol, atorvastatin, diclofenac, chloramphenicol and furosemide; acetaminophen reached 2547.67 ng/L. Sediment provided additional occurrence evidence, particularly for erythromycin, josamycin, tylosin A and glibenclamide, and station-level water and sediment burdens were only weakly to moderately correlated. Formal RQs were calculated only from quantified water concentrations. Of 15 compounds with both quantified water concentrations and suitable toxicity benchmarks, 13 were in the study-specific low risk screening band, fenofibrate was moderate (maximum RQ = 0.21), and tramadol was high (maximum RQ = 2.71). Lower river stations showed co-occurrence of elevated water phase RQs and sediment associated residues, identifying priorities for follow-up rather than cumulative mixture risk. Sediment data were not converted to RQs because sediment-specific benchmarks, porewater, total organic carbon, grain size and benthic toxicity data were unavailable. The study's contribution is not the paired-matrix concept itself but demonstrating how sediment occurrence data alter ecotoxicological prioritisation in a tropical West African river relative to water only monitoring.

articles.title: Correction: Association of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy with changes in eGFR slope and home blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Roxadustat promotes recovery from rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury through modulation of tubular repair dynamics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) caused by rhabdomyolysis is characterized by severe renal tubular damage. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)- 1α is upregulated in proximal tubular epithelial cells (PTECs) and is a key player in tubular repair. Roxadustat protects renal tubules in experimental AKI, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of roxadustat on tubular injury and repair dynamics in a glycerol-induced rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI mouse model.

METHODS: A glycerol-induced rhabdomyolysis-associated AKI mouse model was established with or without roxadustat pretreatment. Renal function, tubular injury, and repair markers were evaluated in vivo, and the effects of roxadustat on Sox9 expression and injury-associated responses were examined in RPTEC/TERT1 cells.

RESULTS: Roxadustat administration significantly improved renal function and attenuated tubular damage 48 h after AKI induction. Consistently, renal neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin expression was markedly reduced by roxadustat pretreatment at 48 h. At 18 h after AKI induction, renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and Sox9 expression were comparable between the AKI and roxadustat-treated AKI groups, whereas Sox9 expression remained elevated in the AKI group but was significantly reduced in the roxadustat-treated group at 48 h. The proliferating cell nuclear antigen showed a temporal expression pattern similar to that of Sox9. Roxadustat alleviated myoglobin- or ischemia-reperfusion-induced tubular cell injury and induced Sox9 expression in vitro.

CONCLUSION: Roxadustat promotes recovery from rhabdomyolysis-induced AKI, potentially by modulating the temporal dynamics of SOX9-associated tubular repair.

articles.title: Ultrasonography-based assessment of kidney volume in healthy Japanese children: a body size-normalized descriptive framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney size is closely associated with function, and ultrasonography is widely used to assess kidney morphology. Although reference values for kidney length are established, kidney volume may provide a more comprehensive assessment, particularly in growing children with variable kidney shapes. However, no framework exists to determine appropriate kidney volume for body size in children.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled children under 18 with normal kidney function who underwent ultrasonography and blood testing. Kidney volume was calculated assuming an ellipsoidal shape. Associations between total kidney volume and anthropometric parameters were examined using simple linear regression and exploratory multivariable analyses, and an exploratory descriptive framework was examined for clinical interpretation.

RESULTS: Thirty-one children (median age, 12.0 years) were included. Among anthropometric indices, body surface area (BSA) best fit total kidney volume. Owing to collinearity among anthropometric variables, BSA was selected as the representative index, and total kidney volume was normalized accordingly. Following normalization, age showed a weak positive association with total kidney volume normalized to BSA, although the association was not statistically significant (adjusted R2 = 0.0285, p = 0.18). An exploratory age-related trend was observed after normalization by BSA; however, given the limited explanatory value and lack of statistical significance, no age-based equation is presented.

CONCLUSIONS: This study proposes a pragmatic ultrasonography-based framework for interpreting kidney volume normalized to body size in Japanese children, rather than establishing a definitive model. Although limited by sample size, this approach may facilitate clinically interpretable assessment of kidney volume in routine nephrology practice.

articles.title: Comment on: Association of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor therapy with changes in eGFR slope and home blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease.
Effects of dotinurad on renal outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease and hyperuricemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of dotinurad on kidney outcomes in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and hyperuricemia.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception to July 30, 2026. Clinical studies of dotinurad in patients with CKD and hyperuricemia were included. Meta-analysis was performed using the meta package in R version 4.4.0. Pooled effect estimates were calculated using random-effects models. The primary outcomes were estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), eGFR slope, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), and urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Serum uric acid (SUA) was assessed as a secondary outcome. Sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings.

RESULTS: Twelve studies were included, of which 10 provided data for quantitative synthesis. Absolute eGFR did not change significantly after dotinurad treatment (MD, - 0.23 mL/min/1.73 m²; 95% CI, - 3.68 to 3.22; P = 0.877). Improvements in eGFR slope were reported in some studies, but differences in outcome definitions and estimation methods precluded quantitative pooling. UACR decreased significantly (MD, - 107.47 mg/gCr; 95% CI, - 183.88 to - 31.05; P = 0.021), whereas UPCR did not change significantly. SUA decreased by 1.77 mg/dL (95% CI, - 2.54 to - 1.01; P < 0.001). Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled estimates.

CONCLUSION: Dotinurad was associated with a reduction in UACR but no significant change in absolute eGFR. Although some studies reported favorable changes in eGFR slope, the available evidence does not establish that dotinurad slows CKD progression. Further studies are needed to determine whether these findings translate into sustained kidney benefits.

articles.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury and subsequent renal functional outcomes after partial nephrectomy: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To assess associations between postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) and renal outcomes after partial nephrectomy and determine whether available evidence separates acute injury from surgical nephron loss.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through 21 September 2026 for English-language full-text reports involving adults and renal outcomes assessed ≥ 3 months after surgery. Evidence was grouped by exposure, outcome, follow-up, and adjustment status. QUIPS and prognostic-factor GRADE informed appraisal. Heterogeneous estimates were not pooled for the primary synthesis.

RESULTS: Twenty-five reports were included: 21 principally addressing AKI/recovery and four evaluating Spectrum Score. Outcome-specific multivariable estimates for conventional AKI included an OR of 2.39 (95% CI 1.60-3.57) for CKD development/progression at median 137.5 weeks and an HR of 4.48 (95% CI 3.37-5.95) for CKD upstaging over 3 years. Adjustment for baseline kidney disease and preserved parenchyma was incomplete. Associations of mass-adjusted AKI with further decline from a postoperative baseline were inconsistent. Spectrum studies mainly assessed volume-normalized ipsilateral recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence cannot establish whether acute injury independently predicts long-term renal outcomes beyond the functional consequences of parenchymal resection. Conventional AKI associations may reflect both processes.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261508850.

articles.title: Effects of switching from conventional renin-angiotensin system inhibitors to angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor on renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease: a retrospective exploratory analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor (ARNI) is widely used in the management of heart failure and provides well-established clinical benefits. However, its effects on renal function in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain unclear.

METHODS: This study included 107 patients with CKD who were switched from renin-angiotensin system (RAS) inhibitors to an ARNI. Annualized changes in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over approximately 6 months before and 12 months after switching to an ARNI (ΔeGFR), as well as changes in urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) and blood pressure, were evaluated.

RESULTS: ARNI treatment was not associated with significant changes in ΔeGFR or UPCR (ΔeGFR: - 3.7 ± 10.4 mL/min/1.73 m2/year vs. - 1.1 ± 5.3 mL/min/1.73 m2/year, P = 0.07; UPCR: 0.70 g/gCr [0.17-1.73] vs. 0.41 g/gCr [0.18-1.62], P = 0.11). In contrast, both systolic and diastolic blood pressures decreased significantly following the switch to an ARNI. The effects on eGFR and systolic blood pressure were consistent regardless of baseline renal function, degree of proteinuria, or underlying kidney disease.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, neither ΔeGFR nor proteinuria changed significantly over the 12-month follow-up period following the switch from RAS inhibitors to an ARNI. In contrast, substantial reductions in blood pressure were observed across different levels of baseline renal function. However, the small sample size may have limited the statistical power to detect significant effects of ARNI on renal function, raising the possibility of a type II error. Further studies with larger sample sizes are warranted.

articles.title: Determinants of patients' trust in their usual nephrologists during renal replacement therapy selection: a nationwide multicenter cross-sectional study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient trust in physicians is an essential component of treatment decision-making. However, factors associated with trust and its impact on renal replacement therapy (RRT) modality selection remain unclear. We examined the determinants of patients' trust in their usual nephrologist and its association with dialysis modality selection in Japan.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of patients requiring RRT (n = 429). Trust was assessed using the Wake Forest Physician Trust Scale (WFPTS). Multivariable linear regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with trust. The association between trust and selection of peritoneal dialysis (PD) versus hemodialysis (HD) was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: Repeated RRT outpatient visits were significantly associated with higher trust scores (standardized β = 0.108). However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for follow-up duration, suggesting that longitudinal continuity of care may underlie the observed relationship. WFPTS scores did not differ significantly between the PD and HD groups (p = 0.200), and trust was not independently associated with PD selection (odds ratio, 1.004; 95% confidence interval, 0.988-1.021).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients' trust in their usual nephrologist was associated with repeated clinical encounters and may be primarily shaped by continuity and duration of care. However, trust was not independently associated with dialysis modality selection, suggesting that clinical and social factors may play a more prominent role in decision-making. Alternatively, trust may facilitate a patient-centered decision-making process in which either modality is selected according to individual preferences.

articles.title: Hematological and serum biochemical profiles of extensively managed Barela dromedary camels (Camelus dromedarius) in Pakistan.
articles.abstract: The camel is very important livestock specie of the arid, semi-arid and desert areas and serves substantially for the livelihood of pastorals. Barela is very important breed of dromedary camel which is famous for its milk production ability not only within the country but also for export. However, locally derived hematological and biochemical reference values under Pakistani pastoral conditions remain limited. This study aimed to set a baseline health profile for clinically healthy dromedary camels. A trial was performed to investigate hematological and biological parameters of Barela camels including about 30 animals as group-1 (n = 15) of non-rutting males and group-2 (n = 15) of non-pregnant she-camels reared under pastoral conditions at Thal desert, Punjab. The camels were used to feed crop residues and grazing/browsing for about 6-8 h with twice a day watering facility. Pastorals dewormed their animals by using injection ivermectin at the rate 1 ml per 50 kg of body weight for the control of internal parasites while spray by ecofleece solution at the rate 1 cc per liter of water for external parasites. The blood sampling was practiced by jugular puncture and the samples were analyzed for hemoglobin, red and white blood cells, packed cell volume, sugar concentrations, cholesterol, triglycerides, total protein, urea and creatinine levels. The hemoglobin level was found to be 14.86 ± 0.76 and 13.78 ± 0.96 g/dl (p = 0.0020) in group 1 & 2, respectively. The RBCs level was varied significantly between groups (p = 0.0013) and WBCs level was varied non-significantly between groups (p = 0.0512), while PCV percentage was found to be varied significantly as 38.96 ± 2.64 and 36.68 ± 2.34 in group 1 & 2, respectively (p = 0.0185). In biological parameters, the sugar concentration was estimated as 136.12 ± 6.46 and 138.66 ± 5.98 mg/dl in group 1 & 2, respectively (p = 0.2733). The levels of triglycerides, total proteins, urea and creatinine were varied non-significantly between groups while cholesterol varied significantly (p = 0.0257) as 59.62 ± 2.64 and 57.12 ± 3.14 mg/dl in group 1 & 2, respectively. The results will be a good addition to the camel science repository for this breed in particular and other camel breeds in general. It will be very useful for further relevant studies of camel hematology and biochemistry, and to set the baseline reference values. These baseline values are specific to the study population, management, and season and should be interpreted as preliminary.

articles.title: A gene-identifier mapping error produced an apparent HDAC-inhibitor repurposing signal in STAT3-mutant T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia: a corrected connectivity map reanalysis.
articles.abstract: Patients with STAT3-mutant T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia (T-LGLL) who fail first-line immunosuppression have no accepted standard of care, and transcriptome-based drug repurposing has been proposed as a way to nominate candidates. We previously reported that histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition emerged as a convergent repurposing strategy in this subgroup. That conclusion does not hold. This paper reports the error that produced it and what a corrected analysis shows. We re-executed our Connectivity Map analysis of CD8 + STAT3-mutant versus STAT3-wild-type T-LGL cells (GSE228868) and audited every step. We then ran four further queries against the identical Touchstone reference: an unchanged repeat of the original, a corrected-gene-list query, a decomposition query restricted to the genes common to both, and six queries using random gene sets matched in size. Leave-one-out resampling and formal mechanism-class enrichment tests were applied throughout. Fifteen of the 48 Entrez identifiers submitted to the Connectivity Map corresponded to no gene in our 73-gene signature, because the pipeline assigned gene symbols to Ensembl identifiers incorrectly. The affected genes lie on different chromosomes from the intended ones. The original query reproduces bit for bit, so the gene list is the only variable. With the corrected list, HDAC inhibitors fall from seven of the top fifteen compounds to two, vorinostat moves from tau - 85.2 to -72.0, belinostat from - 79.7 to -60.6 and HDAC5 knockdown from - 99.7 to -2.2. A query using only the genuine shared genes already abolishes the result, which locates its origin in the erroneous identifiers. No finding survives leave-one-out resampling. Random gene sets of the same size produce a median of 18 compounds and 37.5 knockdowns beyond tau - 90, against 2 and 14 for the corrected signature, and two of six random sets placed nine HDAC inhibitors in their top fifteen compounds. There is no transcriptome-based evidence from this dataset supporting HDAC-inhibitor repurposing in STAT3-mutant T-LGLL. A single mis-mapping step produced a coherent, mechanistically plausible and apparently highly significant class-level result. At the gene-set sizes typical of rare-disease signatures, an extreme connectivity score and the enrichment statistics computed from it do not distinguish signal from noise. We set out the checks that would have caught this.

articles.title: CAR T-cell Therapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Matching Target, Product and Treatment Context.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy can induce remission in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but responses remain inconsistent and prolonged cytopenia is common. Target expression on normal myeloid cells, heterogeneous leukemia clones, variable product fitness and subsequent transplantation jointly determine clinical outcomes. This narrative review evaluates AML CAR T-cell studies through a target-product-clinical-context framework. For each strategy, we consider malignant and normal-cell antigen distribution, receptor sensitivity, duration and control of cellular exposure, and the intended treatment role. Early clinical cohorts show remission signals with several targets, including CLL-1/CLEC12A, but studies differ in constructs, populations and post-infusion treatment. A 38-patient CLL-1 cohort reported a 73.68% objective response rate and 12.17-month median overall survival; a separate 12-patient CLL-1 study found only one morphologic leukemia-free response. These findings caution against inferring clinical activity from antigen identity alone. We outline measurements that could distinguish insufficient exposure, antigen escape and target-mediated marrow injury. Quantitative antigen thresholds and the benefit of planned transplantation remain to be tested prospectively. Clinical development should assess leukemia control together with hematopoietic recovery, infection and outcomes after subsequent therapy.

articles.title: Blood Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury and Cardiometabolic Disease in Korean and U.S. Adults: Population-Specific Associations with Hypertension and Cross-Nationally Consistent Inverse Associations with Diabetes.
articles.abstract: We harmonized nationally representative data on 18,871 Korean adults (KNHANES; 9 survey cycles, 2005-2017) and 16,159 U.S. adults (NHANES 2007-2012) and related blood lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), and mercury (Hg), individually and as mixtures, to hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, and cardiovascular disease, with prospective mortality added in the U.S. cohort. In design-based survey-weighted logistic models, positive associations with hypertension were confined to Korea (Pb 1.15, Cd 1.18, and Hg 1.07 per doubling), whereas in the United States neither Pb (OR 1.03) nor Cd (OR 1.05) was associated with hypertension. Hg showed divergent directions (OR 1.07 in Korea versus 0.96 in the U.S.). Inverse associations with diabetes were directionally consistent across populations (Pb: OR 0.80 in Korea and 0.66 in the U.S.). Nine associations survived false-discovery-rate control across the 24 primary tests: Pb, Cd, and Hg with hypertension, Pb with diabetes, and Cd with dyslipidemia in Korea; and Pb, Cd, and Hg with diabetes and Hg with dyslipidemia in the U.S. The inverse direction of the diabetes associations is most plausibly explained by reverse causation rather than a protective effect. Nonlinearity was significant in only 5 of 18 dose-response panels. Stratification on fish/seafood consumption did not explain the divergent mercury findings: interaction tests were not significant for any outcome (P 0.40-0.87), and seafood-related confounding remains one plausible but unproven explanation. Quantile g-computation showed a positive joint effect on hypertension in Korea (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.12-1.28) but a null joint effect in the U.S. (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.91-1.06). In prospective linkage to national death records through 2019 (14,468 adults, 1,957 deaths), Cd predicted all-cause mortality (HR 1.21 per doubling, 95% CI 1.14-1.29) and Pb was associated with mortality (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.01-1.16). Hg was inversely associated (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.82-0.90), a pattern consistent with confounding by seafood-related factors. Metal-cardiometabolic associations are only partly transportable across exposure environments and should be reported per population and per outcome.

articles.title: Bone mass, trabecular bone score, and fracture risk in transgender individuals under gender-affirming hormone therapy.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) may influence bone health in transgender individuals, but its effects on bone microarchitecture and fracture risk remain unclear. Bone mineral density (BMD) remained stable, with a slight decrease in trabecular bone score (TBS) in transgender women, suggesting low fracture risk and supporting clinical management.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate changes in BMD and TBS in transgender individuals undergoing GAHT and to estimate fracture risk using the fracture risk assessment tool (FRAX).

METHODS: Retrospective longitudinal study (2014-2024) conducted at the Transdisciplinary Gender Identity Program and Division of Endocrinology, Hospital de Clínicas de Porto Alegre, Brazil. A total of 111 transgender women and 43 transgender men underwent two dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) assessments during follow-up, receiving GAHT.

RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 33 (19-40) months, transgender women exhibited a modest but significant decline in TBS (1.458 ± 0.102 vs. 1.442 ± 0.104; p =0.030). Those in the highest estradiol tertile had higher lumbar spine and total femur BMD than those in lower tertiles (p =0.001), without differences in TBS. Median TBS-adjusted 10-year fracture risk was 5.4% (3.8-7.0) for major osteoporotic fractures and 0.2% (0.1-1.3) for hip fractures. Among transgender men, after a median follow-up of 27 (20-47) months, no significant changes in TBS or BMD were observed, and fracture risk remained low.

CONCLUSIONS: GAHT was associated with stable BMD in both groups. Transgender women showed a modest decline in TBS, suggesting potential microarchitectural changes despite preserved BMD. Fracture risk remained low in individuals aged ≥ 40 years in both groups.

articles.title: Patient-specific implants in mandibular and temporomandibular surgery: a systematic review of current clinical evidence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate clinical evidence on patient-specific implants (PSIs) in mandibular and temporomandibular surgery, stratified by indication, biomaterials, outcomes, and complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were searched up to January 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD42024580864). Two independent reviewers conducted study selection, data extraction, and Joanna Briggs Institute risk-of-bias assessment. Given substantial heterogeneity, a stratified narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: Eighty-three studies involving 790 patients were included (40 case reports, 35 case series, 7 observational cohorts, and 1 randomized controlled trial). Segmental, pathological, and traumatic mandibular reconstructions (34 studies) predominantly used load-bearing titanium implants, with complications including soft-tissue dehiscence, plate exposure, and hardware removal. TMJ reconstruction (27 studies; 187 patients, including combined defects) primarily involved hybrid prostheses and generally improved maximum mouth opening, although transient facial nerve weakness was reported. Orthognathic procedures (5 studies; 193 patients) used titanium fixation systems, demonstrating acceptable skeletal transfer accuracy but occasional fit discrepancies; superiority over conventional miniplates remained unproven. Aesthetic contouring and chin augmentation (17 studies; over 200 patients) mainly employed porous polyethylene or polyetheretherketone (PEEK) implants, with high patient satisfaction and predominantly transient complications.

CONCLUSIONS: The clinical performance, material selection, and complication profiles of mandibular PSIs vary by indication. PSIs have reconstructive applications in complex mandibular defects and TMJ replacement; however, their superiority over conventional fixation in elective orthognathic surgery remains unestablished.

articles.title: Developing an integrated breeding objective for Kajli sheep by combining productivity, welfare, farmer preferences, and market signals for sustainable breed improvement.
articles.abstract: In a smallholder production system, it is essential to develop an integrated breeding objective to sustainably improve indigenous small ruminant breeds. The study was conducted to develop an integrated breeding objective for Kajli sheep by incorporating productivity, welfare indicators, farmer preferences, and market signals. In the study, Five hundred Kajli sheep farmers were interviewed. Data were analyzed using R statistical software, applying descriptive statistics, composite index construction, ranking of breeding objective functions, principal component analysis(PCA), correlation analysis, and sensitivity analysis. The majority of the farmers were male, landless, and had livestock as a major occupation. Mean birth weight, weaning weight, 6-months weight, and 12-months weight were 3.0, 14.8, 26.8, and 45.0 kg, respectively, and adult males had higher body weight than females. Breeding males had a higher market price than other animals in the flock. The preweaning mortality was 21%, and the adult mortality was 14%. Heat stress and high feeding costs were welfare-related constraints, and disease resistance was the most preferred breeding trait. The Breeding Objective Function (BOF) values were mostly concentrated between 0.20 and 0.45, and PCA showed that about 59.6% variation was explained by the first two principal components. A weak to moderate correlation was observed among productivity, farmer preference, economic, and welfare indices. A stable BOF ranking across alternative weighting scenarios was confirmed through sensitivity analysis. Overall, the proposed integrated breeding objective provides a practical foundation for developing a participatory, welfare-sensitive, and market-responsive Kajli sheep improvement programme.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical applications in diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical decision-making.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects approximately 50 million people worldwide, with disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries where access to specialized care remains limited. Despite advances in neuroimaging and electrophysiology, accurate diagnosis, etiological classification, and timely identification of surgical candidates remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising tool to integrate multimodal data and support clinical decision-making across the epilepsy care continuum.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically assess and meta-analytically quantify the evidence on AI applications for diagnosis, etiological classification, outcome prediction, surgical candidate selection, and workflow optimization in epilepsy.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, with protocol registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251117939). Searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, and SciELO for studies published between January 2014 and March 2026. Eligible studies included original research in human subjects with epilepsy applying AI or machine learning models and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric with internal or external validation. Study quality was assessed using PROBAST. Pooled estimates of Area Under the Curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were derived using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models across four clinical task groups: diagnosis, classification, outcome prediction, and surgical referral.

RESULTS: From 423 identified records, 102 studies met inclusion criteria. Research output increased markedly after 2018, peaking in 2021 and 2024, with geographic concentration in China (n = 31) and the United States (n = 11). Electroencephalography and MRI were the dominant input modalities, and Support Vector Machines (n = 41) and Convolutional Neural Networks (n = 22) were the most frequently employed algorithms. Most studies relied exclusively on internal validation, and external validation remained scarce across all domains. PROBAST assessment revealed high risk of bias in the majority of studies, particularly in the participant and analysis domains. Meta-analysis demonstrated strong discriminative performance across all groups: the classification group achieved the highest pooled AUC (0.929; 95% CI: 0.837-0.971), followed by diagnosis (0.899; 95% CI: 0.859-0.929), surgical referral (0.895; 95% CI: 0.870-0.916), and outcome prediction (0.807; 95% CI: 0.740-0.861). Sensitivity was highest in the diagnosis group (0.885; 95% CI: 0.840-0.918) and lowest in surgical referral (0.729; 95% CI: 0.681-0.771), a clinically relevant asymmetry given the high cost of missing true surgical candidates in drug-resistant epilepsy. Substantial variability was observed across studies, reflecting differences in data modalities, AI architectures, and sample sizes, and indicating that pooled estimates should be interpreted with caution rather than as fixed, generalizable performance figures.

CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates robust and clinically meaningful performance across the spectrum of epilepsy care, particularly for diagnosis and surgical planning. However, uniformly high between-study heterogeneity, predominant reliance on internal validation, variable study quality, and underrepresentation of low- and middle-income country contexts limit the generalizability of current evidence and hinder clinical translation. Prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and context-adapted implementation strategies are essential to realize the full clinical potential that this body of evidence consistently demonstrates.

articles.title: Network toxicology and single-cell transcriptomics identify acrylamide- and glycidamide-related candidate biomarkers in diabetic ulcers.
articles.abstract: Diabetic ulcers (DU) are severe complications of diabetes, and environmental contaminants such as acrylamide (AA) and its metabolite glycidamide (GA) have been associated with metabolic disturbances relevant to diabetes. In this study, public transcriptomic datasets, network toxicology, protein interaction analysis, and machine learning were integrated to identify plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers overlapping with predicted AA or GA targets. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and single-cell RNA sequencing were further applied to characterize their biological roles and cellular distribution. Eight candidate genes were identified from the intersection of differentially expressed genes and predicted toxicant targets, and PNP and CTSB were ultimately identified as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers. These genes were associated with proteasome function, DNA damage and repair, immune dysregulation, and altered cell communication.
