Single-cell analysis highlighted macrophages and T cells as major cell populations with dynamic plausible candidate biomarker expression. ELISA in streptozotocin induced diabetic ulcer mice further confirmed significantly increased CTSB and PNP protein levels, providing preliminary protein-level support for their association with DU. However, the overlap of PNP and CTSB with predicted AA/GA targets represents hypothesis-generating computational evidence only and does not establish that AA/GA exposure modulates these genes in vivo. These findings support PNP and CTSB as plausible candidate DU-associated biomarkers, while the predicted AA/GA-related associations require direct exposure-based experimental validation.

articles.title: Bacterial brain abscess during pregnancy: A systematic review of maternal-fetal outcomes of neurosurgical and medical management.
articles.abstract: Bacterial brain abscess is rare during pregnancy, and evidence guiding management is sparse. This systematic review described maternal neurological status at presentation and follow-up and summarized maternal, obstetric, neonatal, antimicrobial, and surgical safety outcomes. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from 1 January 1990 to 5 August 2025. Eligible case reports and case series described pregnant adults with bacterial brain abscess managed by craniotomy, stereotactic aspiration, and/or medical therapy; immunocompromised patients and non-bacterial etiologies were excluded. Two reviewers independently assessed articles; risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute case report tool. Given clinical heterogeneity, data were summarized descriptively without formal certainty assessment. The review was pre-registered (Open Science Framework, doi: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/NU2MP) and unfunded. 18 studies reported 18 patients: 16 case reports, and two case series contributing one patient each. Median maternal age was 26.0 years (IQR 25.0-32.0; n = 17), and median gestational age at presentation was 25.0 weeks (IQR 13.0-33.7; n = 17). Ten patients underwent craniotomy (55.6%), four stereotactic aspiration (22.2%), and four medical management alone (22.2%). Neurological deficits occurred in 10/17 cases (58.8%); all 15 evaluable cases had mass effect. Neurological status improved by follow-up in 13/18 patients, although status at delivery and 30-90 days after intervention was inconsistently reported. Outcomes included one maternal death (n = 1/17), five preterm births (n = 5/12), fetal growth restriction in one twin pregnancy (n = 1/18), two pregnancy losses (n = 2/18), neonatal death (n = 1/11), and three NICU admissions (n = 3/18). Organisms were identified in 11 cases; Streptococcus spp. were most common (n = 3/11). Median antimicrobial duration was 42.0 days (IQR, 38.5-59.5). Neurological improvement was common, but serious maternal and perinatal outcomes occurred. Case-based evidence, sparse reporting, and probable selection and reporting biases limit inference. Findings support individualized multidisciplinary management but do not establish a preferred surgical approach.

articles.title: Pathological [18F]fluorodeprenyl-D2 PET findings may precede clinical relapse in LGI1 encephalitis.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: Quantitative pulmonary [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in a prospective proof-of-concept PET/CT study.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic lung disease with variable clinical trajectories and treatment responses. CT depicts structural abnormalities but may not identify biologically abnormal lung. We evaluated pulmonary uptake of the hypoxia-sensitive tracer [¹⁸F]fluoromisonidazole ([¹⁸F]FMISO) in IPF and its cross-sectional associations with CT measurements and pulmonary function.

METHODS: In this prospective proof-of-concept study with cross-sectional analyses, 10 participants with IPF and 10 age-matched healthy controls underwent [¹⁸F]FMISO PET/CT at 2 h and 4 h after injection. Whole-lung and CT-defined regional mean standardized uptake values (SUVmean) were measured. Post hoc sensitivity analyses were applied using CT-derived non-air-fraction correction to whole-lung SUVmean and to compartments below ​-400 HU and below ​-700 HU in both groups. Group comparisons accounted for independent and paired measurements. Pearson or Spearman coefficients correlations were used. Holm adjustment was applied within defined comparison families.

RESULTS: Twenty male participants were included. At 4 h, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean was higher in IPF than in healthy controls (0.521 ± 0.114 vs. 0.344 ± 0.050, adjusted p = 0.0028). After non-air-fraction correction, the difference persisted (mean difference: 0.158, pointwise 95% CI: 0.074-0.242, adjusted p = 0.0042). Corrected regional SUVmean at 4 h was also higher in IPF below -400 HU (1.721 ± 0.251 vs. 1.375 ± 0.220, adjusted p = 0.0215), with a consistent finding below ​-700 HU (adjusted p = 0.0054). Corrected mean comparisons at 2 h were non-significant with Welch's t tests. Within IPF, uncorrected whole-lung SUVmean at 4 h strongly correlated with mean lung attenuation (r = 0.812, adjusted p = 0.0172) and percent-predicted TLC (r = -0.794, adjusted p = 0.0244).

CONCLUSION: Higher [¹⁸F]FMISO uptake in IPF persisted at 4 h after estimated non-air-fraction correction in whole-lung and lower-attenuation regional measurements. Longitudinal validation of this potential imaging biomarker as a surrogate of hypoxia-specific trapping is required.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05331729. First submitted 4 April 2022 first posted 18 April 2022.

articles.title: Multimodal PET/MR imaging in Alzheimer's disease: A comparative study of structural, metabolic, synaptic and perfusion measures.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Structural MRI and 18F-FDG PET are clinically established imaging biomarkers of neuronal injury in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Synaptic density PET (SV2A), arterial spin labelling (ASL, perfusion), and cortical thickness (CTh) can offer additional information, but have not been compared within the same patients. We performed a head-to-head evaluation of these imaging measures for detecting neurodegeneration, discriminating AD from healthy volunteers (HV) and examining their associations with cognition.

METHODS: Thirty-six biomarker-confirmed AD patients (71 ± 9 y/o; M/F 17/19) underwent 18F-FDG, 18F-SynVesT-1 PET/MR and neuropsychological evaluation. Patients were classified as MCI-stage (CDR = 0.5, n = 22) or dementia-stage (CDR > 0.5, n = 14). Image processing and analysis was performed in CAT12.9 with partial volume correction for PET. PET and ASL measures were normalized to the whole cerebellum. Classification performance was evaluated with partial least squares discriminant analysis and Firth logistic regression under repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: In the MCI-stage, reductions were mainly found in the temporal cortex. In the dementia-stage, reductions for the 5 imaging measures extended to the temporoparietal, precuneal and frontal cortices. 18F-FDG PET, assessed against a separate HV cohort, showed large reductions (Cohen's d up to -2.5) and excellent discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.94). Among the cortical measures evaluated against the same HV, cortical thickness showed the largest reductions (d up to -1.6). Cortical thickness, 18F-SynVesT-1 and volumetry provided similar discriminatory performance (AUC 0.81-0.86). ASL did not show detectable reductions in MCI and had a lower AUC (0.72). Global cognition was associated with widespread atrophy, cortical thinning, and 18F-FDG hypometabolism, whereas domain-specific cognitive measures showed more localized regional associations. 18F-SynVesT-1 and ASL demonstrated weaker and less consistent correlations.

CONCLUSION: Multimodal PET and MRI measures showed overlapping yet distinct spatial patterns of neurodegeneration. In MCI, structural, metabolic and synaptic abnormalities were found, whereas perfusion deficits only significantly emerged in dementia-stage AD. Structural and functional measures differentially relate to global and domain-specific cognitive decline. The study was registered on clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05384353) as of 20 May 2022.

articles.title: Comparative validation of five early trauma scores for 24-hour in-hospital mortality in traumatic brain injury.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early risk stratification after traumatic brain injury (TBI) is crucial to guide monitoring, escalation of care, and interfacility transfer within the first hours. Bedside scores, including the "Revised Trauma Score (RTS)," "Glasgow Coma Scale, Age, and Systolic Blood Pressure score (GAP)," "modified Rapid Emergency Medicine Score (mREMS)," "Mechanism, Glasgow Coma Scale, Age, and Arterial Pressure score (MGAP)," and "Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS)," are simple and widely available. Prior studies often use mixed trauma cohorts, later endpoints, and provide limited evaluation of calibration or threshold-level clinical utility. TBI-specific head-to-head evidence is therefore needed. The five scores summarize different clinical domains. RTS incorporates the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and respiratory rate; GAP incorporates GCS, age, and SBP; mREMS incorporates age, heart rate, respiratory rate, SBP, peripheral oxygen saturation, and GCS; MGAP incorporates injury mechanism, GCS, age, and arterial pressure; and MEWS incorporates routinely measured physiologic and neurologic variables, including blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, and level of consciousness. Diastolic blood pressure is not a component of any of the five scores evaluated in this study. The component structure and clinical domains of each score are summarized in Supplementary Table S1.

METHODS: This study analyzed consecutive traumatic brain injury admissions in 2024 at a tertiary medical center in Nantong, China (n = 2,287; 24-hour mortality 7.3%). The five bedside scores were recalibrated with a single logistic equation. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), the Brier score, and calibration intercept and slope, while clinical utility was evaluated as net benefit per 100 patients at 10% and 20% thresholds. All estimates were reported with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) from 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and precision-recall curves were referenced to the cohort prevalence.

RESULTS: RTS and GAP showed the strongest discrimination, with mREMS close.

AUROC: RTS 0.874 (95% CI 0.841-0.903), GAP 0.863 (0.831-0.898), mREMS 0.856 (0.826-0.883); MGAP and MEWS were lower (0.632, 0.606). AUPRCs were 0.465 (0.381-0.531) for RTS, 0.382 (0.308-0.453) for GAP, and 0.370 (0.280-0.424) for mREMS (MGAP 0.154 (0.112-0.199); MEWS 0.129 (0.098-0.159)). Brier scores were 0.050, 0.053, and 0.055 for RTS, GAP, and mREMS, respectively. After simple logistic recalibration, calibration intercepts were near 0 and slopes near 1, with observed-vs-predicted curves close to the 45° line across deciles. At 10% and 20% thresholds, RTS and GAP achieved the highest net benefit and more favorable trade-offs per 100 patients; mREMS was intermediate.

CONCLUSION: RTS and GAP showed the best balance of discrimination, calibration, and net benefit at 10% and 20% thresholds; mREMS was comparable after simple recalibration. These findings support prioritizing RTS and GAP for early TBI risk stratification.

articles.title: Cutaneous and systemic manifestations of propylthiouracil-induced mpo-anca associated vasculitis: a case-based systematic review.
articles.abstract: Propylthiouracil (PTU) is a well-established cause of drug-induced antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), but cutaneous-limited presentations or isolated cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis (CSVV) require careful diagnostic evaluation. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with Graves' disease treated with PTU for two years who presented with painful necrotic cutaneous ulcers involving the extremities, gluteal region, and earlobes (sparing auricular cartilage), accompanied by elevated MPO-ANCA titers and biopsy-proven leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Evaluation did not identify evidence of systemic vasculitis, infection, cryoglobulinemia, or an underlying malignancy. Prompt discontinuation of PTU resulted in progressive clinical remission within two months. A comprehensive systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify all relevant published cases of PTU-induced MPO-ANCA-associated vasculitis with cutaneous manifestations. Eligibility screening and data extraction were performed following standard methodological criteria to synthesize clinical characteristics, management strategies, and patient outcomes.Synthesis of the literature confirmed a female predilection (93.3%), frequent MPO-ANCA/p-ANCA predominance, and variable exposure latencies ranging from 2 weeks to 11 years. Multi-organ involvement was common across the cohort, including renal manifestations, pulmonary complications, and musculoskeletal symptoms, alongside a subset presenting with strictly cutaneous-limited disease. Favorable outcomes were observed following PTU withdrawal and corticosteroids where indicated. PTU-induced MPO-ANCA-associated CSVV is an important diagnostic consideration. An accurate diagnosis relies on clinical, histopathological, and temporal data rather than ANCA positivity alone, and early drug cessation typically ensures a favorable prognosis.

articles.title: Group-level metabolic network organization differentiates real from ipsilateral sham acupuncture after stroke using interhemispheric metabolic ratios: a longitudinal FDG-PET study in rats.
articles.abstract: Acupuncture for stroke recovery remains controversial regarding whether stimulation at prescribed acupoints produces effects beyond sham stimulation. Here, we examined this question using a randomized three-arm longitudinal study of 200 adult female rats with right-hemisphere ischemic stroke induced by middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Rats were assigned to blank control, sham acupuncture, or real acupuncture groups and followed using serial fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) imaging and semi-quantitative behavioral assessment over a 10-day post-treatment window. Sham acupuncture was delivered at ipsilateral non-acupoints located 5 mm from the corresponding midline acupoints and was therefore treated as a potentially non-inert needling control. We used longitudinal right-over-left metabolic ratios to characterize interhemispheric metabolic imbalance and estimated metabolic connectivity from temporal correlations of regional metabolic trajectories. Behavioral scores improved in both real and sham acupuncture groups relative to blank control, but did not statistically distinguish real from sham acupuncture. In contrast, two restricted focal group-level network endpoints showed lower within-network metabolic coupling in real acupuncture than sham acupuncture within the sensorimotor network (SMN) and default mode network (DMN). Exploratory analyses using alternative dependence metrics, conservative DMN definitions, and SMN modularity showed generally consistent but non-confirmatory patterns, whereas rat-level network analyses were weaker and more variable. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the magnitude and statistical support of the RA-SA differences depended on the metabolic representation and treatment of shared temporal variation. Accordingly, the principal findings should be interpreted as group-level differences in R/L-ratio-based interhemispheric metabolic organization rather than as normalization-invariant connectivity differences. These findings provide preclinical, hypothesis-generating evidence that real and sham acupuncture were associated with different post-stroke metabolic network organization under this representation, but do not establish acupuncture efficacy, biomarker validity, or a direct mechanism of action. Future studies incorporating both sexes, healthy controls, longer follow-up, multimodal validation, and stronger subject-level behavior-network linkage are needed.

articles.title: [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT extends the vascular mapping of polyarteritis nodosa beyond [¹⁸F]FDG.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: Long-term neurocognitive outcomes in survivors of childhood retinoblastoma: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Retinoblastoma (RB) is the most common intraocular malignancy in children, and survivors may experience long-term ophthalmic and systemic morbidity. This review evaluates neurocognitive outcomes in paediatric RB survivors. A systematic search identified studies of individuals diagnosed with RB at ≤ 18 years. Eligible exposures included enucleation, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and repeated general anaesthesia. Outcomes included standardised measures of intelligence, memory, attention, processing speed, executive function, fine motor skills, adaptive behaviour, developmental status, and educational and psychosocial outcomes reported with a cognitive measure. Eligible studies were observational cohort or cross-sectional studies with ≥ 2 years' follow-up, published in English. Of 1108 identified papers, six met inclusion criteria. RB survivors demonstrated difficulties in some neurocognitive domains and subgroups, including intelligence, verbal memory, adaptive behaviour, academic performance, and cognitive screening, although mean scores were within normal ranges in several cohorts. Higher radiation dose was associated with poorer verbal memory in a small subgroup of bilateral survivors, while adaptive functioning was particularly impaired in survivors with 13q deletion syndrome. Adaptive behaviour declined early but improved by age 10. Given the small evidence base, certainty was low to very low using a GRADE-informed approach.

CONCLUSION: Findings support ongoing neurocognitive monitoring and early intervention for paediatric RB survivors. However, prospective, multicentre research is needed to clarify the contributions of RB, treatment exposures, and socioeconomic factors to long-term neurocognitive outcomes.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Retinoblastoma survivors face long-term ophthalmic and systemic morbidity from treatment. • Chemotherapy and radiation therapy are linked to neurocognitive deficits in paediatric oncology populations.

WHAT IS NEW: • Limited observational evidence suggests systemic chemotherapy may be associated with greater school difficulties and need for individualised education programmes. • In one study, socioeconomic status and cumulative anaesthesia exposure were associated with cognitive screening performance, whereas retinoblastoma diagnosis and treatment were not independently associated after adjustment.

articles.title: Single arm, Multicenter Phase II Study Investigating the Efficacy and Safety of a Novel Therapeutic Scheme in Patients with Unresectable Cholangiocarcinoma; Radioembolization in Combination with CisGem and Durvalumab (MEDI4736) PM-CARE.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive malignancy associated with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT), also known as transarterial radioembolization (TARE), may improve locoregional tumor control and enhance antitumor immune response, increasing the efficacy of systemic treatment. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of upfront TARE followed by cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab in treatment-naïve patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA.

PROTOCOL: PM-CARE is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm phase II study. Treatment-naïve eligible patients with upfront unresectable liver-predominant iCCA preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A), Eastern Cooperative Oncology performance status 0-1. Following angiographic mapping and technetium-99 m macroaggregated albumin (99mTc-MAA) simulation, participants undergo personalized dosimetry-guided SIRT. Systemic treatment with cisplatin, gemcitabine and durvalumab will start 21 days after TARE and administered for six cycles. Co-primary endpoints are overall response rate (ORR) at 6 months according to modified Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (mRECIST) and safety. Secondary endpoints include ORR on target lesion and overall by RECIST 1.1, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality-of-life. Tissue and blood-based biomarkers including tumor mutational burden, circulating tumor DNA, immune profiling and cytokine characterization will be explored.

STATISTICS: A sample size of 22 achieves 90.9% power to detect a difference of 0.30 in response rate using a one-sided exact test with a significance level of 0.05 at the primary endpoint. The drop-out inflated enrollment sample size is 28 participants.

DISCUSSION: This study will provide prospective efficacy and safety data of upfront TARE combined with current first-line chemoimmunotherapy in patients with unresectable liver-predominant iCCA.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: Clinical Trials.gov NCT06375915.

articles.title: Subphenotyping and precision medicine approaches to ARDS.
articles.abstract: Sixty years after its initial description, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains defined by bilateral radiographic opacities and impaired oxygenation rather than by its underlying biology. This syndromic definition encompasses considerable clinical and biological heterogeneity, which may contribute to the ineffectiveness of pharmacotherapy trials to date. Subphenotyping aims to address this heterogeneity by identifying more homogeneous patient groups that differ in prognosis and/or treatment response. In this narrative review, framed by the research questions outlined in the 2023 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines, we synthesize current approaches to ARDS subphenotyping across complementary domains: clinical (etiology, rapidly improving ARDS), physiological (gas exchange, recruitability, elastance, and ventilatory ratio), morphological (focal versus non-focal radiological patterns), and biological (individual injury biomarkers and the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory subphenotypes). We examine their pathobiological basis, temporal dynamics, and retrospective evidence for heterogeneity of treatment effect, and consider how parsimonious biomarker panels, machine-learning classifiers, and adaptive basket trial designs may support clinical implementation. Prospective validation across diverse populations, including resource-limited settings, remains a key priority.

articles.title: An overlooked cause of refractory shock after liver transplantation.
Financing and Organization of Long-Term Care for Older People in Need of Care: Insights from Poland.
articles.abstract: This study examined preferences for financing and organizing long-term care in Poland. A nationwide quota-stratified survey of 2,001 adults (2024) used descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, and adjusted ordinal logistic regression. State financing was supported by 85.2%; 43.0% endorsed individual financial preparation, 41.8% expressed willingness to leave employment for family care, and 43.4% preferred residential care if care-dependent. Political views were associated with all four outcomes, while sociodemographic characteristics and religiosity showed outcome-specific associations. Findings suggest considering a mixed long-term care system combining public financing, individual preparation, family support, community services, and residential care.

articles.title: Guanxinning tablet attenuates carotid artery stenosis in Tibetan minipigs induced by a high-fat diet.
articles.abstract: Carotid artery stenosis (CAS), a progressive narrowing of the carotid artery primarily driven by atherosclerosis, is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke. Guanxinning tablet (GXN), a well-established traditional Chinese medicine formula, is widely used in cardiovascular diseases; however, its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms against CAS remain largely unexplored. This study aims to investigate the effects of GXN on CAS and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. An accelerated CAS model was established using a high-fat diet (HFD) combined with left common carotid artery balloon injury in Tibetan miniature pigs. After 10 weeks of GXN administration, we evaluated systemic blood lipid profiles, carotid plaque burden via ultrasonography and arteriography, and serum biomarkers reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial injury. Comprehensive histopathological examinations (including H&E, Oil Red O, Masson's trichrome, EVG, and immunohistochemical stainings) of carotid tissues were subsequently performed. The results demonstrated that GXN significantly reduced cholesterol levels, attenuated carotid plaque area, and mitigated the severity of atherosclerotic lesions. Furthermore, GXN decreased lipid deposition and collagen accumulation while inhibiting vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) migration and intimal hyperplasia. Mechanistically, GXN suppressed oxidative stress and downregulated the expression of NF-κB, MMP-9, ICAM-1, and intimal α-SMA, thereby alleviating the inflammatory response and contributing to plaque stabilization. In summary, GXN ameliorates CAS by improving lipid metabolism, suppressing oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and inhibiting VSMC proliferation and neointimal hyperplasia, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic agent for CAS.

articles.title: Decreased Preoperative Left Atrial Function and Synchrony in Patients with Postoperative Dysfunction After Ventricular Septal Defect Repair.
articles.abstract: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) repair is the most common type of congenital heart surgery, yet little is known about left atrial (LA) mechanics before and after repair. We sought to characterize changes in LA size and function following VSD repair and evaluate whether preoperative LA mechanics are associated with postoperative left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. We hypothesized that LA mechanics worsen immediately after VSD repair and abnormal preoperative LA mechanics are associated with more severe postoperative LV dysfunction. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study in children with isolated, moderate or larger VSDs with preoperative LV ejection fraction (EF) > 50%, who underwent surgical repair between June 2012 to April 2023. LA and LV volumes were measured. LA and LV strain and synchrony were assessed using speckle-tracking echocardiography (TomTec Arena). Three primary endpoints included LA opposing wall delay, LA dyssynchrony index, and LA global longitudinal strain (GLS). All other LA and LV measures were secondary and considered exploratory and hypothesis generating. 175 patients were included. Postoperative LV dysfunction (EF ≤ 50%) occurred in 71 patients (41%), including 24 patients (14%) with EF ≤ 40% defined as severe postoperative dysfunction. After surgery, LA volume, EF, regional strain, global longitudinal strain, and synchrony all decreased. Among patients with postoperative EF ≤ 40%, preoperative LA volumes and dyssynchrony were increased, and pre and postoperative LA strain were decreased. VSD repair is associated with an immediate impairment of LA mechanics, including a reduction in LA size, ejection fraction, strain, and synchrony. These changes in the primary endpoints were robust to correction for multiple comparisons. Patients who developed severe postoperative LV dysfunction also had significantly lower postoperative LA strain. Preoperative LA dyssynchrony and reduced preoperative LA reservoir function were associated with severe postoperative LV dysfunction on adjusted analysis but did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons, therefore should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in a larger, prospective designed cohort.

articles.title: The cost of digitoxin unavailability in Germany: modelled clinical and economic consequences in heart failure.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Digitoxin reduced all-cause death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure in symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction in the published DIGIT-HF trial. Germany's only marketed oral digitoxin product became unavailable on 1 July 2026, with resupply expected after 212 days. We estimated its clinical and economic consequences.

METHODS: A counterfactual decision-analytic model combined published aggregate DIGIT-HF event rates, German diagnosis-related group costs, statutory tariffs, acquisition costs and quality-adjusted life-year estimates to compare uninterrupted supply with a 212-day interruption. Outcomes were clinical events, expenditure and net monetary benefit, extrapolated nationally under two population scenarios, with deterministic and exploratory Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Per 1000 eligible patients, uninterrupted supply corresponded to 16.8 fewer primary composite events and, estimated separately, 9.9 fewer heart failure hospitalisations. Nationally, the interruption corresponded to approximately 1700 to 3000 additional primary composite events and 1000 to 1800 heart failure hospitalisations. The net change in hospital and drug acquisition expenditure was small, as avoided digitoxin purchases largely offset additional hospital costs. At €20,000 per quality-adjusted life-year, maintained availability yielded a trial-aligned national net monetary benefit of €13.2 to €22.8 million, versus annual digitoxin expenditure of €6.7 to €11.6 million.

CONCLUSIONS: A 212-day digitoxin supply interruption may result in approximately 1700 to 3000 additional primary composite events and may forgo an estimated €13.2 to €22.8 million in net monetary benefit, while producing only a small change in hospital and drug acquisition expenditure. Thus, reliable supply of low-cost cardiovascular medicines is clinically and economically relevant.

articles.title: Changes in muscle sympathetic nerve activity following SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in patients with chronic heart failure.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors improve outcomes in heart failure (HF), but their effects on sympathetic nervous system activity in humans remain incompletely characterized. We investigated longitudinal changes in directly measured muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) after SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in patients with chronic HF.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-arm longitudinal study, 70 patients with stable chronic HF across the spectrum of left ventricular ejection fraction underwent baseline assessment including microneurography, echocardiography, laboratory testing, NYHA assessment, and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) evaluation. Follow-up assessments were available in variable numbers depending on the respective parameter; paired MSNA measurements were available in 45 patients. Mean follow-up was 8.2 ± 6.3 months. MSNA was quantified using event-count measures expressed as events per minute and events per 100 heartbeats.

RESULTS: Paired MSNA measurements were available in 45 patients. Median MSNA event count per minute decreased from 107.6 [68.6-126.5] to 64.5 [44.5-76.2] events/min (Hodges-Lehmann change - 34.80, 95% CI - 44.04 to - 26.59; p < 0.001), and MSNA event count per 100 heartbeats decreased from 75.8 [53.4-97.8] to 46.2 [31.6-62.6] events/100 heartbeats (change - 27.63, 95% CI - 33.30 to - 21.91; p < 0.001). LVEF increased by 6.03 percentage points (p < 0.001), NT-proBNP decreased (p = 0.001), NYHA class improved (p < 0.001), and KCCQ Overall Summary Score increased by 19.76 points (p < 0.001). Changes in MSNA were not significantly associated with changes in LVEF, NT-proBNP, NYHA class, or KCCQ score.

CONCLUSION: SGLT-2 inhibitor initiation in chronic HF was followed by a marked reduction in directly measured MSNA and concurrent improvement in cardiac and clinical parameters. Controlled mechanistic studies are required to determine whether these changes are directly attributable to SGLT-2 inhibition.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of CRP/PCT discordance for differentiating infectious and non-infectious inflammation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT) are widely used biomarkers for the assessment of suspected infection. While their individual diagnostic value has been well described, the clinical utility of combining both markers remains insufficiently explored. CRP/PCT discordance, such as elevated CRP with low PCT, may provide additional diagnostic context and help characterize heterogeneous infectious and non-infectious inflammatory states.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 418 adult patients admitted to a tertiary care Chest Pain Unit underwent simultaneous CRP and PCT measurements. Infection status was independently adjudicated based on clinical and microbiological data. Diagnostic performance of both biomarkers individually and in combination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. A multiplicative CRP × PCT score was developed to assess their combined diagnostic value.

RESULTS: In the study population, 137 patients (32.8%) were classified as having clinically adjudicated infection. Both CRP and PCT were independently associated with infection (both p < 0.0001). CRP demonstrated high diagnostic performance (AUC 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96), while PCT yielded an AUC of 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.93). The CRP × PCT score achieved the highest AUC (0.96, 95% CI 0.95-0.98), corresponding to a modest absolute improvement over CRP alone (ΔAUC 0.02). At the optimized cutoffs of CRP ≥ 20 mg/L and PCT ≥ 0.07 ng/mL, sensitivities were 85% for both biomarkers, with specificities of 88% and 79%, respectively. Among patients with elevated CRP, infection was substantially more frequent when PCT was also elevated (84.9%) than when PCT remained low (51.6%). However, low PCT did not exclude infection.

CONCLUSIONS: CRP demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for infection in this Chest Pain Unit cohort, and combining CRP with PCT yielded a modest incremental improvement in overall discrimination. In patients with elevated CRP, PCT provides additional information on the likelihood of infection, but low PCT should not be used to rule out infection. Prospective external validation is required to determine the clinical utility of these findings.

articles.title: Effects of Semaglutide and Dapagliflozin on Natriuretic Peptides in Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Comparative Study.
Filgotinib Safety Profile: A Pharmacovigilance Study Using Data from the VigiBase and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although filgotinib was approved in Europe and Japan, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) withheld approval owing to concerns about testicular toxicity. To address this gap, we conducted a pharmacovigilance study of filgotinib-related adverse drug reactions (ADRs).

METHODS: This study evaluated the safety profile of filgotinib using data from the VigiBase and FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) databases from the first quarter (Q1) of 2017 to Q1 2025. Signal detection involved calculating four disproportionality measures: the proportional reporting ratio (PRR), reporting odds ratio (ROR), information component (IC), and empirical Bayes geometric mean (EBGM), using predefined quantitative thresholds. Signals were refined using OpenVigil 2.1 to account for concomitant medications. The signals were ordered according to their IC025 values rather than PRR value.

RESULTS: Analysis of VigiBase data (2207 reports) revealed a predominance of ADRs among female patients (74.8%) and individuals aged 45-64 years (38.1%). Notably, 95% of reports originated in Europe. Strong disproportionate reporting signals were identified for lower respiratory tract infection (PRR = 20.5 [χ2 = 1002.3], lower bound [LB] ROR = 16, IC025 = 3.7, EBGM05 = 15.6) and hypercholesterolemia (PRR = 29.8 [χ2 = 611.9], LB ROR = 19.8, IC025 = 3.5, EBGM05 = 19.5). Time-to-onset analysis revealed diverse onset times (median, 1 month), with most ADRs assessed as possibly related to filgotinib. In FAERS (190 reports), disproportionate reporting signals were observed for epididymitis (PRR = 1060.3 [χ2 = 8350.6], LB ROR = 544.1, IC025 = 2.9, EBGM05 = 512.0) and sleep apnea syndrome (PRR = 62.7 [χ2 = 486.0], LB ROR = 32.3, IC025 = 2.6, EBGM05 = 30.8).

CONCLUSIONS: This pharmacovigilance study identified several disproportionality signals, including epididymitis, sleep apnea syndrome, infections, and metabolic abnormalities, warranting continued clinical vigilance and further investigation of the safety profile of filgotinib.

articles.title: A cluster of presumed sterile endophthalmitis after intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg injections administered on a single treatment day: a single-center observational study.
articles.journal: Journal of ophthalmic inflammation and infection
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 8 mg formulation of aflibercept may permit treatment intervals of up to 16 weeks in treatment-naïve neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME) after three initial monthly injections, depending on treatment response. Although pivotal trials reported low rates of intraocular inflammation (IOI), post-marketing sterile inflammatory events have been described. We aimed to characterize the presentation, management, and visual outcomes of a cluster of presumed sterile endophthalmitis following vial-drawn intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg administered on a single treatment day at a tertiary center.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included six consecutive patients who received intravitreal aflibercept 8 mg from single-use vials on April 25, 2024. Serial examinations included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure, slit-lamp biomicroscopy, and optical coherence tomography. Fluorescein angiography and vitreous microbiological testing were performed where clinically indicated. Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: Five of six patients (83%) developed presumed sterile endophthalmitis within 2-4 days (mean 3.0 ± 0.7 days), presenting with visual deterioration, floaters, anterior chamber inflammation, and vitritis; one patient developed hypopyon. The patient with hypopyon underwent emergency pars plana vitrectomy on April 28, 2024, and the other four patients were hospitalized on April 29, 2024, because infectious endophthalmitis could not initially be excluded. Mean BCVA worsened from 0.44 ± 0.21 logMAR at baseline to 1.32 ± 0.92 logMAR at diagnosis. All five received systemic corticosteroids and empirical topical and intravenous antibiotic treatment; Patient 5 received an intensified topical antibiotic regimen rather than the five-times-daily moxifloxacin used in Patients 1-4. Vitreous cultures from the single vitrectomized patient were negative. At approximately one year, mean BCVA was 0.40 ± 0.21 logMAR. There were no comparable inflammatory events after other anti-VEGF agents administered during the index session.

CONCLUSIONS: The five cases of presumed sterile endophthalmitis clustered after aflibercept 8 mg injections administered on April 25, 2024. No specific cause could be established because individual vial batch numbers were not recorded and microbiological testing was limited to the single vitrectomized patient. Clinicians should promptly assess post-injection inflammation, empirically address possible infection when indicated, and report suspected adverse events to pharmacovigilance systems.

articles.title: A case of inferior vena cava syndrome caused by rapid enlargement of an infected giant hepatic cyst.
articles.abstract: An 85-year-old man was admitted to our hospital with high-grade fever, chills, and impaired consciousness. Laboratory investigations revealed elevated levels of inflammatory markers, thrombocytopenia, coagulation disorders, and liver and renal dysfunction. An abdominal CT scan revealed multiple hepatic cysts and abscesses. The patient was diagnosed with sepsis and multiple organ failure secondary to a hepatic abscess. Although the inflammatory response and overall condition initially improved with intensive treatment, the inflammatory response subsequently increased again. The patient developed renal failure, liver dysfunction, marked weight gain, and worsening edema predominantly in the lower body. A subsequent abdominal CT scan revealed an increase in ascites and enlargement of the largest cyst in the right lobe of the liver, which had grown from 13 to 20 cm within three weeks, resulting in compression of the inferior vena cava (IVC) and the right atrium. The diagnosis was IVC syndrome (IVCS) secondary to an enlarged infected hepatic cyst, and percutaneous cyst drainage was performed. Following drainage, renal failure, liver dysfunction, and lower body edema improved markedly. Given the rarity of IVCS and the causes of secondary conditions, it was deemed imperative to expedite the diagnosis and treatment of the underlying disease.

articles.title: Liver Stiffness Measurements are Associated with Adverse Cardiovascular and Liver-Related Outcomes in Patients with MASLD: A Retrospective Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), severe fibrosis is associated with poorer clinical outcomes; however, the prognostic significance of moderate fibrosis is not well established. Moreover, the relationship between disease severity-assessed by liver stiffness measurements (LSM) categories or biopsy-confirmed fibrosis stages-and cardiovascular (CV) outcomes, remains limited. This study estimated the risk of CV and liver outcomes in patients with MASLD stratified by magnetic resonance elastography-determined LSM category (normal [< 3.1 kPa], moderate [3.1-4.4 kPa], severe [> 4.4 kPa]) and in patients with MASH stratified by biopsy-confirmed fibrosis stages (F0-F4).

METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study used Mayo Clinic Enterprise electronic health records (01/01/2005-03/31/2024) to compare the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) in patients with MASLD (n = 3092) or MASH (n = 4458) stratified by baseline disease severity.

RESULTS: Patients with MASLD and moderate LSM were at higher risk (hazard ratio; 95% CI) of all MALO and nonfatal ischemic stroke (1.94; 1.15-3.27; P < 0.05), CV-related death (2.84; 1.52-5.29; P < 0.01), and 3-point MACE, a composite of ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and CV-related death (1.43; 1.10-1.86; P < 0.01), compared with patients with normal LSM. Compared with patients with MASH and F0-F1, patients with F2 were at higher risk for cirrhosis (1.40; 1.00-1.96; P < 0.05) and cirrhosis-related complications (1.37; 1.03-1.82; P < 0.05) and patients with F3 were at higher risk for cirrhosis (2.54; 1.86-3.47; P < 0.01), cirrhosis-related complications (1.70; 1.28-2.26; P < 0.01), hepatocellular carcinoma (4.56; 1.84-11.32; P < 0.01) and liver transplantation (5.52; 1.42-21.37; P < 0.05). Patients in the most severe disease cohorts (i.e., severe LSM or F4) experienced elevated risk of nearly all MACE and MALO outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with MASLD and moderate LSM or MASH and F2-F3 at baseline had an elevated risk for clinical outcomes compared with patients with normal LSM or mild-to-no fibrosis, respectively.

articles.title: Late first and early second trimester fetal lung volumes assessed by MRI: normative measurements from 12 weeks to 19 weeks of gestation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reference values and validated measurement of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based total fetal lung volume (TFLV) in the late first and early second trimester are limited. Commonly used Meyers and Rypens prediction models were developed using later gestational ages and may not apply to pregnancies imaged at 12-19 weeks.

OBJECTIVE: To determine weekly reference values for TFLV between 12-week and 19-week gestation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective study of fetal MRI examinations from 2009 to 2023. Of 311 examinations identified, 128 fetuses met inclusion criteria after exclusions for motion/technical limitations and conditions affecting lung development. Two radiologists manually segmented fetal lungs in two planes to obtain TFLV. Week-specific summary statistics and regression modeling were used to derive reference values and a predictive formula. Observed TFLV was compared with values predicted by the Meyers and Rypens models using t tests. Equivalence testing assessed one-plane versus two-plane average measurements, and interobserver/intraobserver agreement was evaluated using concordance correlation coefficients (CCC).

RESULTS: Mean TFLV increased nonlinearly from 12 weeks to 19 weeks; the best-fit formula was TFLV (mL)=0.000001810×(gestational age in weeks)5.196. Meyers and Rypens models significantly overestimated observed means at all gestational weeks (all P<0.001). One-plane and two-plane average measurements were equivalent (TOST P<0.001), and TFLV did not differ significantly by imaging plane. Agreement was high (interobserver CCC 0.96; intraobserver CCC 0.95).

CONCLUSION: Fetal MRI TFLV measurement in the late first and early second trimester is reproducible using either a one-plane approach or the average of two planes. Observed TFLV values at 12-19 weeks were significantly lower than those predicted by commonly used later-gestation models (Meyers and Rypens). These early-gestation reference values may be used cautiously in selected clinical settings, with prospective validation in independent cohorts warranted.

articles.title: Short-term adherence to eyelid hygiene after verbal, written, or visual education in patients with meibomian gland dysfunction: a prospective, parallel-group, randomized comparative study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare short-term adherence to eyelid hygiene after verbal, written, or visual patient education in patients with meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD).

METHODS: In this prospective, parallel-group, randomized comparative study, 114 patients with MGD were randomized to verbal instruction alone, verbal instruction plus a written information sheet, or verbal instruction plus an illustrated step-by-step guide for a home eyelid-hygiene regimen. The primary outcome was self-reported full adherence at four weeks; secondary outcomes were changes in the Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), fluorescein tear-film break-up time (FBUT), meibomian-gland scores, and Schirmer I test.

RESULTS: Of 114 participants, 107 (93.9%) completed follow-up. Full adherence was reported by 81/107 (75.7%): 21/35 (60.0%) in the verbal, 29/36 (80.6%) in the written, and 31/36 (86.1%) in the visual group (p = 0.026). Adherence was significantly higher in the visual than in the verbal group (risk difference 26.1%, 95% CI 6.3-45.9%; adjusted p = 0.039; adjusted OR 3.96, 95% CI 1.20-13.05), whereas the written-versus-verbal difference was not significant (risk difference 20.6%, 95% CI - 0.2 to 41.3%; adjusted p = 0.17). OSDI improved in all groups (overall - 13.8 points, 95% CI - 16.2 to - 11.4) without a between-group difference. FBUT and meibum expressibility improved more in the visual group than in both other groups (baseline-adjusted p ≤ 0.024); other clinical outcomes did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Supplementing verbal counselling with an illustrated step-by-step guide was associated with higher short-term adherence to eyelid hygiene and greater improvement in tear-film stability and meibum expressibility; a text-only sheet showed a smaller, non-significant effect. The short follow-up and self-reported outcome limit conclusions about long-term adherence.

articles.title: A Retrospective study of ¹⁸F-FDG PET/CT for predicting immunochemotherapy response and differentiating tumor residue in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the predictive and diagnostic value of baseline and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT metabolic and structural features in distinguishing true residual tumor from immune-related inflammation in LA-NPC.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective analysis enrolled 95 consecutive stage III-IVA LA-NPC patients receiving first-line neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. All underwent pre- and post-treatment 18F-FDG PET/CT measuring metabolic parameters and structural features (extranodal extension [ENE]). Depth of metabolic response (DMR) was the primary endpoint; biopsy histopathology (n = 22) acted as gold standard. Multivariable regression, Spearman correlation, ROC-AUC with bootstrap validation, and sensitivity analyses were applied.

RESULTS: Baseline SUVmax (OR = 1.146 [95% CI: 1.051, 1.250]; P = 0.002) and ENE (OR = 0.171 [95% CI: 0.054, 0.544]; P = 0.003) independently predicted poor and strong DMR, respectively. Patients with baseline ENE showed higher post-treatment EBV DNA non-clearance rates (34.1% vs. 9.8%; P = 0.008). In the biopsy subgroup with discordant biochemical-imaging status, true residue had higher baseline primary tumor TLG (P = 0.048) and ENE prevalence (80.0% vs. 16.7%; P = 0.028) than inflammation. A post-treatment nodal-dominant pattern (Post-T/N ratio ≤ 0.9) was associated with a lower rate of pathologically confirmed primary-tumour residue than a primary-dominant pattern (11.1% vs. 46.2%), negatively correlating with peak CRP (rho = -0.523, P = 0.012), indicating that nodal-dominant uptake accompanied a more intense systemic inflammatory response rather than residual disease.

CONCLUSION: In LA-NPC, baseline SUVmax and ENE independently predict neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy response. Combining baseline metabolic and nodal structural features distinguishes true residual disease from immune-related inflammation.

articles.title: [Medical care of nontraumatic patients in the resuscitation room].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Standardized resuscitation room algorithms exist for major trauma, but systematic pathways for nontraumatic emergencies have historically been lacking.

OBJECTIVE: Systematic presentation of epidemiological data and consensus-based quality criteria for nontraumatic resuscitation room management.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Evaluation of recent epidemiological studies (OBSERvE, OBSERvE-DUS, monocentric and multicentric cohorts) and analysis of the recommendations of the DGINA white paper.

RESULTS: Nontraumatic emergencies constitute up to 66.6% of all resuscitation room treatments. This older, comorbid population shows a 30-day mortality of up to 36.3%. The DGINA white paper provides a consensus-based framework for structural, technical, and staff qualifications. Due to high diagnostic heterogeneity and frequent secondary specialty shifts (17.0% to 29.5%), interdisciplinary emergency medicine expertise is essential.

CONCLUSION: Resuscitation room care requires overcoming monodisciplinary approaches. Clinical emergency medicine acts as a coordinating specialty to optimize diagnostic pathways and interface management. Establishing a national registry is necessary for quality assurance.

articles.title: [When a "minor" injury isn't so minor after all].
Effect of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy on Spinal Fusion Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spinal fusion remains the benchmark procedure for degenerative spine disease, but outcomes are frequently limited by complications such as pseudarthrosis and revision surgery. With the rise in glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use for diabetes and weight management, interest has grown in their effects on bone metabolism and fusion healing. This study evaluated the association between GLP-1 RA therapy and outcomes after spinal fusion, including pseudarthrosis, revision surgery, perioperative complications, and length of stay.

METHODS: A systematic review of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Library was conducted to identify adults undergoing cervical or lumbar fusion through September 2025. Data on study design, GLP-1 exposure, spinal region, and outcomes were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted for pseudarthrosis outcomes.

RESULTS: Twelve retrospective cohort studies and two reviews were included. All cohort studies carried at least moderate risk of bias, with three judged at serious risk; none achieved a low ROBINS-I rating. GRADE certainty was low for pseudarthrosis and length of stay and very low for revision surgery, infection, and other complications. Most studies reported reduced pseudarthrosis and shorter length of stay among GLP-1 users, particularly in lumbar cohorts, whereas posterior cervical and TLIF cohorts demonstrated more variable outcomes. Meta-analysis of six studies suggested a possible association between GLP-1 use and lower pseudarthrosis at 1-year follow-up (OR 0.62), driven primarily by lumbar fusion cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative GLP-1 RA exposure may be associated with lower pseudarthrosis rates and shorter hospitalization among adults undergoing lumbar fusion. However, evidence is limited to retrospective studies with moderate-to-serious risk of bias, heterogeneous procedures, inconsistent fusion definitions, and limited drug-exposure data. Cervical fusion cohort findings were inconsistent. These results should be considered hypothesis generating and require prospective validation with standardized radiographic fusion criteria to inform perioperative management.

articles.title: Comparison of [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE and [18F]MFBG PET/CT in SDHD-associated paraganglioma: Identifying multifocal disease and localizing the secretory lesion.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging

articles.title: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes map onto distinct cholinergic and serotonergic territories in autoimmune encephalitis.
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) shows a longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET signature: acute hypermetabolism in limbic-striatal-thalamic regions and hypometabolism in posterior associative cortex, both partially reversible under immunotherapy. Whether these patterns show spatial correspondence with specific neuromodulatory systems is unknown.

METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis included twenty-two AE patients from a previously published longitudinal cohort (Cerne et al. 2025) who underwent [¹⁸F]FDG PET at clinical baseline (BS) and follow-up (FU). Using JuSpace (option 6), atlas-regional BS-FU difference maps were correlated (Spearman) with 15 normative PET/SPECT maps of multiple neurotransmitter systems. Participant-level Spearman coefficients were Fisher-z transformed. Group inference used paired BS/FU label permutations, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across all 15 maps. Spatial co-localization was interpreted as overlap in regional involvement, not as directionality of transmitter signaling. Age-adjusted regression models tested associations between individual JuSpace coefficients and clinical outcomes at BS and FU.

RESULTS: Longitudinal metabolic change showed positive spatial associations with VAChT (Fisher z = 0.164; ρ = 0.185; q = 0.023) and α4β2 (z = 0.133; ρ = 0.127; q = 0.004), and a negative association with 5-HT2A (z = - 0.108; ρ=-0.093; q = 0.014). The cholinergic alignment matches the previously described hypermetabolic limbic-striatal circuit, whereas the 5-HT2A alignment situates reversible posterior hypometabolism within serotonin-enriched association cortex. No exploratory clinical association survived multiplicity correction.

CONCLUSION: Longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET differences showed significant spatial correspondence with distinct neuromodulatory territories. Embedding longitudinal [¹⁸F]FDG PET changes into a normative receptor space provides a systems-level neurochemical framework and generates testable hypotheses on how cholinergic subcortico-limbic and 5-HT2A-enriched posterior association territories relate to acute disease expression and recovery.

articles.title: Long-term progression of disease activity, organ damage, and symptom burden in Sjögren's disease: results from a prospective multicentre cohort.
authors: On behalf SJÖGRENSER PROS Group, part of the Spanish Society of Rheumatology Systemic Autoimmune Diseases Study Group (EASSER)
articles.abstract: To identify clinical and serological factors associated with progression of systemic activity, cumulative organ damage, and symptom burden in Sjögren's disease (SjD). We conducted a prospective multicenter study including 314 patients fulfilling the 2002 AECG classification criteria. After 9.5 years of follow up, progression was assessed across three domains: systemic activity (ESSDAI ≤4 to ≥5), organ damage (increase ≥1 point in SSDDI), and change in symptom burden (ESSPRI ≤4 to>4). Baseline variables were analyzed using bivariate tests and multivariable logistic regression. Among patients with low baseline systemic activity (ESSDAI ≤4), 55 of 213 (25.8%) had moderate-high activity (ESSDAI ≥5) at follow-up. In multivariable analysis, lymphadenopathy (OR 3.4, 95% CI 1.3-8.9), low C4 levels (OR 2.7, 95% CI 1.1-6.9), fibromyalgia (OR 5.4, 95% CI 2.3-12.4), and cataracts (OR 3.6, 95% CI 1.1-12.3) were independently associated with activity progression. Cumulative organ damage progressed in 63 patients (20.1%) and was independently associated with renal involvement (OR 3.2, 95% CI 1.2-8.2) and dyslipidemia (OR 2.2, 95% CI 1.1-4.5). In an exploratory analysis, 14 of 19 patients (73.7%) with baseline ESSPRI ≤4 had ESSPRI >4 at follow-up; no multivariable analysis was performed due to the small sample size. Systemic activity and cumulative damage increased in a substantial proportion of patients with SjD. Activity progression was independently associated with lymphadenopathy, C4 hypocomplementemia, fibromyalgia, and cataracts, while damage accrual was independently associated with renal involvement and dyslipidemia. These findings highlight the differential evolution of systemic activity, organ damage, and symptom burden, supporting their complementary assessment during long-term follow-up.

articles.title: When does personalization matter? An evidence-to-action beyond smart devices demonstrating the added clinical value of personalization in precision MedTech.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Precision medicine (PM) seeks to improve prevention, diagnosis, and treatment by incorporating biologic, clinical, environmental, and behavioral variation rather than relying exclusively on population averages. Medical technology (MedTech) provides a practical interface through which this approach can be translated into continuous sensing, decision support, and individualized intervention. We use the term personalized/precision medical devices (PMDs) for a conceptual class of devices that combine person-specific inputs with analytics and device-level configuration or adaptation. PMDs overlap with smart devices, connected health, and digital therapeutics, but are distinguished by their explicit coupling of individualized data to clinically meaningful device behavior.

METHODS: This perspective uses a structured narrative literature approach. The literature survey was extended through targeted searches of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and major regulatory/standards sources for publications addressing precision or personalized medicine, biosensing, wearable and implantable devices, point-of-care diagnostics, automated drug delivery, digital therapeutics, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Medical Things (IoMT), interoperability, regulation, cybersecurity, and health equity [Oct. 2025-Oct. 2026]. Preference was given to peer-reviewed clinical studies, systematic reviews, authoritative regulatory guidance, and international standards. Evidence was synthesized narratively around a device lifecycle framework linking individual profile, sensing, data infrastructure, analytics, actuation, clinical workflow, evidence generation, and governance.

RESULTS: Clinical evidence demonstrates that some components of the PMD concept are already established. In a randomized trial, automated insulin delivery increased time in the target glucose range by 14% points versus sensor-augmented pump therapy at 24 weeks. Remote pulmonary-artery pressure monitoring reduced heart-failure hospitalization by 28% in a prespecified analysis of patients with reduced ejection fraction. In the Apple Heart Study, 419,297 participants were enrolled; 0.52% received an irregular-pulse notification, and atrial fibrillation was identified in 34% of participants who returned an analyzable electrocardiographic patch. Digital therapeutics and adaptive neurostimulation further illustrate how software and implantable systems can individualize treatment, although clinical generalizability and long-term evidence remain uneven.

CONCLUSIONS: PMDs should be viewed as an engineering and clinical integration paradigm, not as a new regulatory category. Their value depends less on novelty of individual components than on reliable linkage among person-specific data, clinically validated algorithms, device actuation, and longitudinal feedback. Translation therefore requires evidence generation, interoperability, cybersecurity, lifecycle regulation, accountable AI, and equity-by-design. The next phase of precision MedTech will be defined by selective deployment of these capabilities where individualized sensing and adaptation demonstrably improve clinical outcomes or care efficiency.

articles.title: Molecular Determinants of Contaminant Association with PET Nanoplastics Revealed by Atomistic Simulations.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: Chemical contaminants associated with nanoplastics can form environmentally pervasive, persistent complexes with potentially toxic effects. Yet, determining which contaminants are most likely to associate with nanoplastics and which molecular determinants govern this phenomenon remains challenging. Here, we used molecular dynamics (MD) to screen and compare the surface association of small-molecule contaminants with polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic particles (PET-NPPs). Toward this aim, we developed an automated, open-source MD screening pipeline that requires only a SMILES string as input. By systematically analyzing 203 environmentally relevant contaminants in complex with a PET-NPP model, we observed widespread surface association governed by a specific set of physicochemical descriptors. Contaminant net charge defined the primary interaction regime. Among neutral contaminants, association increased strongly with molecular size at lower molecular weights. Among compounds of comparable size, the strongest binders were consistent with geometric complementarity with the PET surface, involving aromatic anchoring and, in some cases, conformational adaptability. Together, these results identify model-specific molecular determinants of contaminant association with PET-NPPs, providing a framework that enables rapid, internally consistent prioritization of contaminants for targeted experimental and mechanistic follow-up.

articles.title: Large-Scale and Systematic Prediction of ADMET Properties through Heterogeneous Network and Kernel-Based Deep Learning.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: Accurately predicting absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties remains a major challenge in accelerating drug discovery, especially for underexplored natural products (NPs). Herein, we present a unified multitask learning framework that integrated heterogeneous network (HN) embeddings and a modified kernel-based deep neural network (DNN) to simultaneously predict all ADMET properties. Our model named as hdADMET captures complex molecular interactions through HNs that incorporated compound-drug relationships, experimental validated ADMET features, and the interrelationships among ADMET properties to transform the embedding representations into a kernel-based DNN for boosting the learning ability of the prediction model. Hold-out cross-validation on benchmark data sets, including ChEMBL, BindingDB, CTRPandGDSC, and NPASS, demonstrated improved and robust accuracy through data integration. Compared with the state-of-the-art multitask models, the hdADMET model achieved competitive performance with a significantly lower computational cost. Its practical utility was further demonstrated by accurately predicting the ADMET profiles of newly identified NPs mined from the literature studies. The promising candidate with high anticancer activity, low toxicity, and favorable metabolic properties was identified for further experimental validation. The hdADMET model offered an alternative way to prioritize leading compounds for clinical translation through HN embeddings and deep learning.

articles.title: Membrane Lipid Composition and Asymmetry Modulate Translocation Versus Leakage of the Model Amphipathic Peptide MAP.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) can enable intracellular access while avoiding cytotoxicity, yet their behavior is highly sensitive to membrane composition. Here we show that lipid composition and leaflet asymmetry act as a switch that determines whether the amphipathic CPP MAP undergoes nondisruptive translocation or stabilizes membrane pores that drive leakage. Using high-field computational electrophysiology (CompEL) simulations in membranes of increasing physiological relevance, we show that electrically induced membrane defects allow the insertion of MAP peptides. We find symmetric anionic bilayers favor MAP insertion coupled to transmembrane pore stabilization in POPC/POPG membranes, reproducing progressive dye release in liposome leakage assays. Incorporation of cholesterol reduces the number of inserted peptides and conducts to faster leakage kinetics in cholesterol-containing vesicles. In contrast, a minimal asymmetric membrane model (POPC extracellular leaflet; POPC/POPS intracellular leaflet) supports MAP translocation without sustained membrane disruption. This delivery-relevant mechanism is supported by efficient MAP internalization in HEK293 cells while maintaining high viability. Polarized ATR-FTIR provides structural context, indicating predominantly membrane-associated α-helical conformations across lipid compositions. Together, these results establish lipid asymmetry and composition as actionable biointerface parameters that tune CPP function between translocation and leakage and demonstrate an experimentally benchmarked framework for predicting membrane outcomes across complex lipid environments.

articles.title: An Integrated Ligand- and Structure-Based Virtual Screening and Experimental Strategy for the Prediction of Chemically Diverse GLP-1R Agonists.
articles.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
articles.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) plays a central role in metabolic regulation and is a major therapeutic target for obesity and diabetes. Peptide agonists, like semaglutide, targeting GLP-1R, remain among the most effective regulators of glucose metabolism and appetite. Nonetheless, recent reports of weight regain after treatment discontinuation sustain the interest in expanding the chemical diversity of GLP-1R ligands through drug discovery strategies. However, the structural complexity and conformational plasticity of class B1 G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) make conventional single-method virtual screening approaches prone to bias and limited chemotype recovery. Using an integrated ligand- and structure-based virtual screening pipeline, combining complementary ligand-based descriptors, multifingerprint similarity, electrostatic similarity, pharmacophore modeling, and multiconformation docking under a consensus-driven selection strategy, we identified three chemically distinct GLP-1R agonists comprising one nonpeptidic molecule (GQB47810), and two peptides (neuromedin C and DPDPE). Among them, DPDPE showed the greatest effectiveness, reaching nearly 100% of the maximal GLP-1 response, although with lower potency (EC50 = 4.3 μM). Further in vitro characterization confirmed that DPDPE behaved as a full agonist and exhibited dual agonistic activity at GLP-1R and at the glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GIPR, EC50 = 4.3 μM). Site-directed mutagenesis of the predicted binding site, with cell-surface expression measured for every mutant, and whole-cell competition binding against 125I-GLP-1 are consistent with direct engagement of the receptor. These findings establish a consensus-driven computational framework for chemotype-diverse agonist discovery at conformationally flexible GPCR targets and reveal a pentapeptide with GLP-1-like efficacy as a promising lead for next-generation small peptide therapeutics.

articles.title: Enrollment in Unified Diabetes Care and Longitudinal Glycemic and Kidney Biomarkers: A Sequential Target Trial Emulation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of enrollment in Unified Diabetes Care (UDC), an integrated digital care program, on care delivery, glycemic control, and longitudinal kidney biomarkers in type 2 diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Using records from one tertiary diabetes center in China, we emulated monthly sequential target trials from 2016 to 2024. Each month, first UDC enrollment was compared with continued active specialist usual care among adults with type 2 diabetes, recent HbA1c, and active specialist contact. Eligibility was fixed at time zero regardless of later outcome availability. Overlap weighting and outcome models addressed measured baseline differences and differential follow-up measurement.

RESULTS: A total of 33,845 patients contributed 38,796 emulated trial entries: monthly instances in which an eligible patient was assigned to first UDC enrollment or usual care. At 12 months, UDC was associated with lower HbA1c (difference -0.23 percentage points [-2.5 mmol/mol], 95% CI -0.29 to -0.18 [-3.2 to -2.0 mmol/mol]), greater HbA1c target attainment (+7.56 percentage points, 95% CI 5.47-9.65), and more regular follow-up (+6.39 percentage points). Relative differences in 1 + urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) were -16.2% at 6 months and -19.7% at 12 months; both remained significant after false discovery rate control. The exploratory 12-month estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) difference was +0.56 mL/min/1.73 m2; main trajectory analyses showed later separation, while effect magnitude and precision varied across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: UDC enrollment was associated with more continuous monitoring, sustained glycemic improvement, and lower UACR at 6 and 12 months. Small favorable eGFR differences emerged later, with their magnitude and precision varying across analytical specifications.

articles.title: Kidney Effect of Tirzepatide in Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the effect of tirzepatide on kidney parameters in youth-onset type 2 diabetes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this SURPASS-PEDS analysis, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and albuminuria were assessed in 99 participants (aged 10 to <18 years) treated with tirzepatide or placebo.

RESULTS: At baseline, 18% of participants exhibited hyperfiltration (mean eGFR 142 vs. 104 mL/min/1.73 m2 in normofiltration), and 26% had a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g. Tirzepatide (pooled) reduced eGFR, with more than twofold greater reductions in participants with baseline hyperfiltration versus normofiltration at week 30 (-20.2 vs. -8.4 mL/min/1.73 m2; both P < 0.05 vs. placebo). The proportion of participants with hyperfiltration decreased with tirzepatide and increased with placebo (P < 0.05 for pooled tirzepatide vs. placebo). At week 30, fewer participants had albuminuria across all treatment groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Tirzepatide decreased eGFR in youth with type 2 diabetes and normal to elevated eGFR, an effect primarily ascribed to the attenuation of glomerular hyperfiltration.

articles.title: One or 2 Veins in Head and Neck Free Flaps: A First-Principles Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether a head and neck free flap should drain through 1 or 2 veins remains unresolved. A second vein lowers outflow resistance and provides a backup, but it also slows flow in each vein.

METHODS: A first-principles model combined Poiseuille flow, wall shear rate, and a common-cause (beta-factor) reliability term. One parameter was fitted to published intraoperative venous velocities, and the model was then tested against independent flow, reexploration, meta-analytic, and radial forearm flap data.

RESULTS: Venous outflow accounted for about 25% of flap resistance. A second vein raised flap flow by about 15% and reduced per-vein velocity and venous pressure head to 57% of single-vein values. The relative risk of thrombotic flap loss with 2 veins reduced to RR ≈ βk, where β is the fraction of venous failures affecting both veins at once and k is the change in per-vein hazard; a second vein is harmful only when k exceeds about 1/β. Pooled data limited k to about 1.5. As predicted, dual anastomoses into separate superficial and deep systems reduced venous insufficiency in radial forearm flaps (0.7% versus 7.5% with 1 vein), whereas dual anastomoses within one system did not (11.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: The benefit of a second vein depends mainly on whether it can fail independently of the first. In the neck, a second vein from a separate venous system, drained into a separate recipient such as the external jugular system, should protect more than a second vena comitans joined to the same internal jugular trunk.

articles.title: Predictors of outcomes of endoscopic sinus surgery for CRSwNP: a systematic review of the literature.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has a wide spectrum of severity and varying impact on quality of life. Endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) is effective for symptom relief and modifying the natural history of the disease in most patients. Although there have been numerous attempts to ascertain factors predicting outcomes after ESS, there is no universally accepted model for identifying those at risk that can be applied in clinical practice.

METHODOLOGY: This systematic review aimed to identify potential pre-, peri- and post-operative factors predicting poor outcomes after ESS.

RESULTS: A total of 152 studies were identified for inclusion, revealing a number of factors well predicting poor outcomes: asthma, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug-exacerbated respiratory disease, previous surgery (time from last surgery, involvement of frontal sinus, number of surgeries), severity and duration of symptoms pre-operatively, high pre-operative Lund-Mackay score and high tissue eosinophil counts. Some evidence was also found for allergy, surgical related factors and lack of post-operative use of corticosteroids, high ethmoid-to-maxillary opacification ratios at computed tomography scan, high Lund-Kennedy endoscopic score, osteitis and interleukin-5 as biomarkers.

CONCLUSIONS: This review may assist clinicians in identifying patients at higher risk of poor outcomes after ESS, contributing to more precise and personalised medical care.

articles.title: Paradoxical psoriasis under TNF blockade in rheumatology practice: real-world burden and clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paradoxical psoriasis/pustulosis during tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) therapy may complicate immune-mediated rheumatic disease management. We evaluated its frequency, phenotype, management, and outcomes.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Records of adults receiving TNFi between 2014 and 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Authorization-derived person-time included post-event exposure. Aggregate Poisson regression included sex, diagnosis, and TNFi, with Holm correction for diagnosis and treatment comparisons.

RESULTS: Among 3,070 adults contributing 7,689.99 person-years, paradoxical psoriasis/pustulosis was documented in 60 patients (1.954%). The exposure-adjusted event rate was 0.780 per 100 person-years (95% confidence interval, 0.595-1.004). Palmoplantar involvement occurred in 91.7%, a pustular/pustulosis component in 51.7%, and complete remission in 83.3%. Median latency was 22 months; treatment was switched in 70.0%. The global diagnosis comparison was significant (p = 0.029), but the axial spondyloarthritis/ankylosing spondylitis-rheumatoid arthritis contrast was not after Holm correction (p = 0.066). The global TNFi comparison was non-significant (p = 0.145), as was the corrected infliximab-etanercept contrast (p = 0.064).

CONCLUSIONS: Paradoxical psoriasis/pustulosis was uncommon and predominantly palmoplantar. Diagnosis-specific and treatment-specific findings remain hypothesis-generating. Post-event exposure and residual confounding limit interpretation.

articles.title: Pumpless extracorporeal lung assist device in the management of idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension - implantation, weaning and explantation in a bridge-to-decision concept.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Via a primary sternotomy approach, cardiopulmonary bypass is established in a standard fashion including a separate vent in the main pulmonary artery. The outlet cannula, an angled Berlin Heart EXCOR cannula, is implanted into the body of the small, underfilled, left atrium using felt-supported single sutures. The inlet cannula, a 12 mm Berlin Heart graft adapter cannula connected to a 12 mm Terumo prosthesis and draining deoxygenated blood from the main pulmonary artery, is tunnelled through the epigastric skin and subsequently anastomosed with the main pulmonary artery. A low-resistance oxygenator (QUADROX, Maquet) is used for paracorporeal lung assist.
