articles.title: Multiplexed tear diagnostic intelligence at the point of care: toward clinically informative biomarker panels.
articles.abstract: Tear fluid is emerging as an attractive route to rapid and non-invasive diagnostics, yet its clinical translation remains constrained by microliter sample volumes, low biomarker abundance, strong preanalytical variability, and the limited interpretability of single-analyte readouts. Here, we propose that tear diagnostics should evolve from single-analyte sensing toward multiplexed tear diagnostic intelligence: the integrated extraction and interpretation of complementary molecular signals from minimal tear samples at the point of care. This work discusses why multiplexing is not merely an analytical upgrade, but a key enabling strategy for making tear testing informative, reliable, and clinically actionable. We outline the requirements for integrating rational biomarker panels with low-volume POC technologies, emphasizing biological relevance, analytical compatibility, parsimony, validation, and interpretable outputs. Hyperglycemia-related ocular disorders and infection/inflammation-related conditions are used as representative scenarios to illustrate how disease-oriented panels could transform tear diagnostics from single-biomarker sensing into a high-content, non-invasive platform for decentralized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Identifying phage host receptors using TraDIS.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The growing antimicrobial resistance crisis has sparked renewed interest in using bacteriophage (phage) as a treatment for antibiotic-resistant infections. Phage are viruses that infect and often kill bacteria and have served as key models for many molecular biology studies. There are many complex phage-bacterial interactions that dictate the success or failure of the phage life cycle, but many of these are not well understood or characterized. These include the specific interactions to recognize a bacterium during the infection process, bacterial phage defense mechanisms, and metabolic pathways that are key to phage replication. In this study, a novel Escherichia coli phage, Arnold, is characterized, and the genome sequence is reported. We then use transposon-directed insertion-site sequencing to screen a library of E. coli mutants to identify over 200 genes involved in Arnold phage infection or in phage resistance. Using this approach, we identified both an outer membrane protein (BtuB, vitamin B12 transporter) and an inner membrane protein (SdaC, serine/proton symporter) that are essential for phage infection; deletions in these genes were shown to provide immunity to infection by this phage. Understanding the genetic basis of phage infection and phage resistance should allow us to select or design phage to target specific bacterial pathogens in the future.

IMPORTANCE: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat to modern health, and new solutions are needed to fight multi-drug resistant infections. One promising solution are bacteriophages, viruses that naturally infect and kill bacteria. Phage infection is very strain specific, governed by the interaction of phage proteins with a cell surface receptor. In order to understand the rules that govern which phage can infect which bacteria, we need to identify these interacting partners. We report the genome of a phage infecting Escherichia coli and use transposon insertion sequencing to identify genes involved in phage infection, including what we propose are the cell surface receptors required for infection. This knowledge is essential for understanding and potentially engineering targeted phage treatments against specific bacterial pathogens.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence and enhanced recovery after surgery: from protocol-driven pathways to adaptive perioperative care systems (cognitive ERAS).
articles.abstract: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) programs have transformed perioperative care through standardized, evidence-based pathways, improving outcomes across surgical specialties. However, increasing patient complexity and heterogeneity expose important limitations of protocol-driven approaches, which often fail to capture dynamic physiological variability and individualized recovery trajectories. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a pathway to overcome these constraints by integrating longitudinal perioperative data and generating individualized risk predictions. However, prediction alone is insufficient for clinically meaningful personalization, which requires causal reasoning to estimate which interventions are most likely to improve outcomes for specific patients and at different stages of recovery. In this context, ERAS may evolve toward a data-informed, adaptive care system that integrates prediction, causal inference, and supervised workflow coordination. Emerging agentic AI systems may further extend ERAS beyond passive decision support toward structured care orchestration within defined clinical governance boundaries. This review examines how different AI methodologies, including supervised learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, generative models, and causal inference, can be aligned with ERAS objectives across the perioperative continuum. We also critically evaluate current evidence and key barriers to implementation. Looking forward, the convergence of AI, digital health technologies, and continuous patient monitoring may enable the emergence of cognitive ERAS, a data-driven perioperative care model that integrates prediction, causal estimation, and continuous learning to deliver personalized and dynamically adaptive recovery pathways.

articles.title: Adjunctive benefits of host modulation to non-surgical periodontal therapy: A systematic review, meta-analysis, meta-regression, and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjunctive systemic host-modulation therapy (HMT) to non-surgical periodontal therapy has promising clinical benefit. This systematic review evaluated its effect in improving periodontal clinical outcomes versus controls.

METHODS: A systematic electronic search was conducted in five databases up to April 2025 to identify eligible randomized clinical trials (RCTs) with ≥3-month follow-up. The primary outcome was probing pocket depth (PPD). Secondary outcomes were clinical attachment level (CAL) and bleeding on probing (BoP). Random-effects meta-analysis, network meta-analysis, and mixed-effects linear regression models were employed. Risk of bias was evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool. GRADE was used to assess the certainty of evidence.

RESULTS: Among 85 included RCTs, meta-analysis across 64 RCTs comprised systemically healthy and medically compromised patients. Significant PPD (low-moderate certainty) and CAL (low-high certainty) improvements were observed with systemic sub-antimicrobial-dose doxycycline (SDD) (PPD: -0.44 mm [95% confidence interval {CI}: -0.48, -0.40], p < 0.0001; CAL: -0.73 mm [95% CI: -1.04, -0.42], p < 0.0001) and omega-3 (PPD: -0.78 mm [95% CI: -1.45, -0.11], p = 0.0232; CAL: -1.06 mm [95% CI: -1.89, -0.23], p = 0.0124) when administered in healthy patients for ≥6 months. However, non-significant changes were observed in diabetics. Network meta-analysis ranked SDD first in PPD reduction at 3-month (3.00 mm [95% CI: 2.54, 3.47]) and 6-month (3.01 mm [95% CI: 2.37, 3.66]) follow-ups. Omega-3+low-dose aspirin, probiotics, bisphosphonates, and dietary interventions were not supported by evidence.

CONCLUSIONS: Although currently available evidence is inconsistent, SDD or omega-3 may complement NSPT when systemically administered for ≥6 months in healthy patients but not in diabetics.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: CRD420250652488.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Treating periodontitis with non-surgical periodontal therapy is effective, but some patients may benefit from additional treatments that help control the body's inflammatory response. This systematic review analyzed 85 randomized clinical trials to determine whether systemic host modulation therapies improve treatment outcomes. Among the available therapies, sub-antimicrobial-dose doxycycline and omega-3 fatty acids, when used for at least 6 months, provided additional improvements in pocket depth reduction and clinical attachment gain in systemically healthy patients. Similar benefits were not observed in patients with diabetes. Overall, the evidence suggests that these therapies may be useful adjuncts to conventional periodontal treatment in selected healthy patients, although further high-quality studies are needed to confirm their long-term effectiveness and identify which patients benefit the most.

articles.title: Preventive therapy for tuberculosis infection: are we making progress?
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) prevents progression from Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection to disease; however, its impact is limited by incomplete coverage, diagnostic uncertainty, toxicity, drug-drug interactions, and losses along the entire prevention cascade.

AREAS COVERED: This review critically examines the evolving concept of tuberculosis infection, concentrating on current and future regimens for presumed drug-susceptible infection. It assesses shorter rifamycin-based regimens in terms of efficacy, safety, completion, and clinical limitations, and discusses recent evidence supporting six months of levofloxacin for contacts exposed to multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis. Ongoing trials of ultra-short and novel regimens, including bedaquiline- and delamanid-based approaches are also reviewed across key populations.

EXPERT OPINION: Although TPT has progressed substantially, shorter regimens alone will not overcome the main barriers to tuberculosis prevention. The next phase should focus on precision prevention by integrating predictive host biomarkers with clinical, epidemiological, radiological, and source-case drug-susceptibility data. This next phase will require integration with public health services globally. Patient-centered delivery, stronger linkage to care, and regimens suitable for children, pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, and contacts of fluoroquinolone-resistant tuberculosis will be essential to achieve equitable population-level impact.

articles.title: Prevalence of Extragenital Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis Among Persons Assigned Female Sex at Birth in Seattle, WA.
articles.abstract: We quantified the prevalence of gonorrhea and chlamydia among ciswomen at a low-barrier clinic in Seattle, WA, that used opt-out extragenital screening over a two-year period. Approximately one quarter (23.5%) of chlamydia and one third (32.1%) of gonorrhea cases were isolated to rectal and/or oropharyngeal sites, without concurrent urogenital infection.

articles.title: Fast microwave catalytic synthesis of bis-hydroxyethyl terephthalate from plastic waste utilizing ultrathin 2D nanosheets.
articles.abstract: Microwave catalytic synthesis of bis-hydroxyethyl terephthalate (BHET) from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) offers a promising approach for plastic waste recycling. Here, we employed ultrathin nanosheets as an ideal model to study this reaction. As an example, we synthesized MnO2 nanosheets that facilitated the microwave catalytic conversion of 1 g of PET into BHET, achieving nearly 100% conversion and a roughly 82% yield of BHET within just two minutes. Importantly, 1 g of real-world PET sourced from bottles can also achieve a similar conversion result. We tentatively propose that hot-electron migration and transient Mn3+ spin-state modulation may influence the electronic environment of surface Mn centers, potentially facilitating PET glycolysis. This work offers a promising materials design strategy for the microwave-catalytic glycolysis of PET, with potential implications for sustainable plastic recycling.

articles.title: The hidden cost of seizure suppression: Understanding neurological outcome in refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus.
articles.abstract: Refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus are usually treated with continuous intravenous anesthetic drugs to achieve seizure suppression, often for days or weeks. This strategy is supported by a compelling biological rationale; prolonged seizures can promote excitotoxicity, neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and neuronal injury. Yet direct evidence that deeper or longer anesthetic coma improves long-term neurological outcome remains limited. A recurrent clinical problem is that patients who receive the most aggressive treatment are also those with the longest, most severe, and most treatment-resistant forms of status epilepticus, often in the context of high-risk underlying etiologies. Clinical complexity, seizure activity, and treatment exposure therefore become tightly intertwined. This article argues that neurological outcome after refractory and superrefractory status epilepticus should be interpreted through the interaction of three domains: the underlying disease, the epileptic process, and the burden imposed by treatment. This perspective may help explain why survivors with different etiologies, including cryptogenic new onset refractory status epilepticus, febrile infection-related epilepsy syndrome, autoimmune encephalitis, developmental and epileptic encephalopathies, metabolic disorders, and acute symptomatic conditions, may converge toward a shared long-term phenotype characterized by cognitive impairment, functional disability, persistent epilepsy, and cerebral atrophy. Current evidence does not allow the relative contribution of these domains to be quantified in individual patients. It does, however, challenge a purely seizure-centered interpretation of outcome and supports a therapeutic aim of timely seizure control with the lowest cumulative anesthetic exposure required to achieve and maintain it. Future studies should model disease, seizure, and treatment burden together using longitudinal and time-dependent variables.

articles.title: Benefits of Intracystic Bleomycin for Symptomatic Recurrent Rathke Cleft Cyst: An Institutional Update.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: The management of recurrent Rathke cleft cysts (RCC) poses a unique clinical challenge. The mainstay of treatment is reoperation with cyst drainage; however, there is limited evidence evaluating adjuvant pharmaceutical therapy in this patient population. Several studies, including a 2019 study by Ung et al at our institution, suggest a potential benefit of the use of intracystic bleomycin in recurrent RCC. The intracystic application of bleomycin is known to be beneficial in the treatment of cystic craniopharyngioma, however, its role in the treatment of recurrent Rathke cleft cyst remains unclear. To evaluate long-term outcomes of recurrent RCC treated with intracystic bleomycin, building on a 2019 study by our institution which reported no short-term follow-up recurrence.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of patients with RCC who underwent surgical resection with intracystic bleomycin between January 2011 and December 2023 by a single surgeon. This study updates our 2019 study which reported no recurrence in 6 patients who received intracystic bleomycin for recurrent RCC. Patient symptom ratings were collected preoperatively and postoperatively.

RESULTS: Of 125 patients with a history of surgery for RCC, 29 (23%) experienced radiographic recurrence. Subsequently, 24 of these patients underwent reresection with 20 of these patients receiving intracystic bleomycin at the time of secondary resection. To date, only 2 bleomycin-treated patients experienced recurrence (10%) with a median follow-up of 28.4 [4.0-54.4] months. Compared with historical data which show a 26.2% recurrence rate after secondary resection without adjuvant therapy, our bleomycin-treated cohort demonstrated a lower recurrence rate.

CONCLUSION: The use of intracystic bleomycin seems to be a safe and potentially effective treatment option in patients with recurrent RCC.

articles.title: KvrA promotes pulmonary persistence and systemic dissemination of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) poses a severe threat to human health, with KvrA, a member of the SlyA family of MarR-type transcriptional regulators, previously shown to contribute to capsule production, hypermucoviscosity formation, and virulence in Klebsiella pneumoniae. However, whether KvrA coordinates additional surface-associated pathways during infection remains incompletely understood. This study systematically investigated the role of KvrA in the survival, dissemination, and colonization of hvKp through in vitro and in vivo experiments. We found that knocking out kvrA in K. pneumoniae KPPR1 resulted in a capsular-deficient phenotype in bacterial colonies. KvrA was confirmed to positively regulate the expression of capsular polysaccharide (CPS)-associated genes, thereby promoting the synthesis of CPS. The ΔkvrA mutant displayed reduced survival rate when exposed to human serum, and the amount of its biofilm formation also decreased. Furthermore, in vitro, macrophages significantly phagocytosed more ΔkvrA mutant than wild type, indicating that KvrA contributes to phagocytic resistance of hvKp. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that KvrA regulates additional surface-associated pathways, including lipopolysaccharide (LPS) biosynthesis and type 3 fimbria-associated biofilm formation. A murine pneumonia infection model revealed that the ΔkvrA mutant exhibited higher bacterial clearance in the lung, liver, and spleen compared with the wild-type strain, indicating that KvrA contributes to in vivo survival, dissemination, and colonization of hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp). Histopathological observations further corroborated the contribution of KvrA to hvKp pathogenicity in mice. Collectively, our findings extend previous studies by demonstrating that KvrA not only regulates capsule-associated virulence traits but also coordinates additional surface-associated pathways, including LPS biosynthesis and type 3 fimbria/biofilm-related processes, contributing to pulmonary persistence and systemic dissemination of hvKp.IMPORTANCEKlebsiella pneumoniae is an opportunistic pathogen that has emerged as a significant causative agent for both community-acquired and nosocomial infections. The emergence of highly virulent and multidrug-resistant strains of K. pneumoniae poses a substantial threat to public health. The gene kvrA plays a pivotal role in the colonization and pathogenicity of K. pneumoniae. Understanding the regulatory mechanisms of KvrA in K. pneumoniae provides a theoretical basis for identifying novel genetic targets to control K. pneumoniae infections, which may facilitate the development of therapeutic agents.

articles.title: Evaluation of [18F]Fluciclatide PET/CT for αvβ3 Integrin-Related Imaging In a Preclinical Model of Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Synovial angiogenesis and integrin-mediated tissue remodeling are important components of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathology. αvβ3 integrin, expressed by activated endothelial and synovial cells, represents a molecular imaging target in arthritic joint disease. In this study, we evaluated the uptake characteristics of [18F]Fluciclatide, a radiolabeled cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartic acid (RGD) peptide primarily targeting αvβ3 integrin in the antigen-induced arthritis (AIA) rat model. AIA was induced in male Wistar rats by intra-articular antigen injection. αvβ3 integrin expression in knee joints was assessed by immunohistochemistry. Ex vivo biodistribution and dynamic positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging were performed after intravenous [18F]Fluciclatide administration. The effect of excess Cilengitide, an RGD-integrin antagonist, on tracer distribution was evaluated to assess αvβ3-directed tracer binding. Arthritic knee sections showed increased αvβ3 immunoreactivity compared with contralateral control and healthy knees. Ex vivo biodistribution showed higher tracer uptake in arthritic than in control knees at 30 minutes post-injection (0.29 ± 0.01 vs. 0.18 ± 0.01 %ID/g, p < 0.05). Dynamic PET/CT similarly demonstrated higher plateaued tracer accumulation in arthritic joints than contralateral controls, with 2.5-fold higher SUVmean values (1.86 ± 0.13 vs. 0.75 ± 0.06). Cilengitide reduced tracer uptake in several RGD-integrin-rich peripheral tissues and increased blood activity, while arthritic-knee uptake remained similar. Arthritic joint-to-blood ratios decreased after blockade from 2.47 ± 0.10 to 0.87 ± 0.08, corresponding to a ∼65% reduction (p < 0.05). Overall, [18F]Fluciclatide PET/CT visualized increased arthritis-associated tracer uptake in AIA rat joints and supports further evaluation of this tracer for αvβ3 integrin-related imaging in experimental arthritis.

articles.title: Targeting PI3K signalling for broad inhibition of β-Coronavirus infection.
articles.abstract: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) signalling pathway plays a central role in regulating key cellular processes such as survival, metabolism, and immune responses. Aberrant activation of this pathway is associated with tumorigenesis, and several PI3K inhibitors have been developed as anticancer agents. Emerging evidence suggests that viruses, including β-coronaviruses, have evolved mechanisms to exploit host PI3K signalling for their replication and immune evasion. In this study, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of a panel of PI3K inhibitors against β-coronaviruses, including murine hepatitis virus (MHV), human OC43 (HuCoV-OC43) and four major SARS-CoV-2 variants using both cell line and organoid models. Our findings reveal that these compounds exhibit low micromolar potency in inhibiting viral replication. Notably, the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor C20 (PWT33597) demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against multiple β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, MHV, and HuCoV-OC43, in conventional cell lines and in air-liquid interface (ALI)-cultured, differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cells. Given that cytokine storm is a major contributor to SARS-CoV-2-related multi-organ failure and mortality, we further explored the impact of PI3K inhibition on host inflammatory responses. We found that MHV infection markedly increased cytokine expression in RAW264.7 macrophages. Interestingly, treatment with C20 further amplified cytokine production, suggesting complex immunomodulatory effects that may not be universally beneficial. Together, our findings indicate that PI3K inhibitors such as C20 exhibit promising broad-spectrum antiviral activity. Although their immunomodulatory effects, such as enhanced cytokine production, warrant further investigation, these compounds may offer a dual opportunity to fine-tune both antiviral and host immune responses with appropriate therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: CMV-driven IFNγ-mediated sensitization of AML cells renders them preferentially susceptible to NKG2Cpos NK cell killing.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection represents a significant risk factor for transplant recipients, including patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). Interestingly, several studies have reported an association between early CMV reactivation and a reduced risk of leukemia relapse, particularly in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Given that CMV profoundly shapes the natural killer (NK) cell compartment, a contribution of CMV-primed NK cells to this effect has been proposed. To explore this mechanism, we analyzed the relationship between NK cell functionality and CMV reactivation in the context of AML. Consistent with the observations in peripheral blood, CMV-seropositive HSCT recipients displayed expanded NKG2Cpos NK cell populations within the bone marrow, characterized by high Granzyme B expression. CMV replication was associated with elevated plasma IFNγ levels, which in vitro rendered AML cells more susceptible to apoptosis when co-cultured with peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Importantly, IFNγ treatment modulated NK cell responses by inducing a variety of NK cell ligands, including HLA-E on primary bone marrow-derived blasts, and AML cell lines. In line with this, the activation of CMV-associated NKG2Cpos NK cells was enhanced upon stimulation with IFNγ-pretreated AML cells. In summary, our findings demonstrate that CMV replication induces a transient increase in IFNγ levels that influences both AML and NK cells, ultimately enhancing AML cell susceptibility to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity, thereby suggesting a role for the NKG2C-HLA-E axis.IMPORTANCEPrevious studies suggested that CMV reactivation after HSCT may reduce leukemia relapse in AML patients, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here, we show that CMV replication induces IFNγ release, which sensitizes AML cells to NK cell-mediated killing. This effect involves upregulation of HLA-E on AML cells and activation of expanded NKG2Cpos NK cells within the bone marrow. Our findings uncover a novel IFNγ-dependent link between CMV replication and enhanced NK cell cytotoxicity in AML, suggesting that combining IFNγ treatment with NK cell-based immunotherapy or NKG2A blockade could reduce post-HSCT relapse, even in CMV-negative patients.

articles.title: Age-stratified functional outcomes after microsurgical vestibular schwannoma resection in 180 adults: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The objective of this paper was to evaluate age-stratified functional outcomes after microsurgical resection of sporadic vestibular schwannoma (VS) and to assess the association of age with facial nerve and hearing outcomes within a function-preserving strategy.

METHODS: We analyzed 180 adults who underwent microsurgical VS resection at a single center and summarized outcomes in four prespecified age groups (younger adults, 18-39 years; middle-aged adults, 40-59 years; early older adults, 60-69 years; and older adults, ≥70 years). Primary endpoints were favorable facial nerve function (House-Brackmann [HB] I-II) and serviceable hearing (Gardner-Robertson [GR] I-II) among hearing-preservation candidates (preoperative GR I-II), both assessed at 2-year follow-up. Age was modeled as a continuous predictor using restricted cubic splines adjusted for Hannover tumor extension classification, side, preoperative function, symptom duration and extent of resection. A prespecified sensitivity contrast compared patients aged <60 versus ≥60 years. Secondary outcomes included Karnofsky Performance Status, complications and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay.

RESULTS: Two-year HB I-II rates were 95% (38/40), 98.6% (69/70), 88.4% (38/43), and 92.6% (25/27) across the four age groups (overall 94.5%). Among hearing-preservation candidates, serviceable hearing at 2 years was 36.8% (7/19), 45.5% (15/33), 55.6% (10/18) and 50% (4/8), respectively (overall 46.2%). Continuous-age models showed no statistically significant overall or non-linear age effect for either endpoint after adjustment. In the prespecified <60 versus ≥60 sensitivity analysis, patients aged ≥60 years had lower adjusted odds of HB I-II (OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.01-0.56; P=0.0129), whereas the hearing contrast was not significant (OR 1.68, 95% CI 0.45-6.27; P=0.4427). ICU length of stay was longer in the ≥70 group.

CONCLUSIONS: Among carefully selected surgical candidates, age alone should not preclude microsurgical resection of VS when surgery is indicated. Within a function-preserving paradigm, 2-year facial nerve outcomes remained high across age groups and serviceable hearing was achievable in appropriately selected candidates.

articles.title: Multidimensional Predictors of Post-Traumatic Stress in Relatives of Critically Ill Patients.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Relatives of critically ill patients frequently develop post-traumatic stress symptoms. Few studies have evaluated both psychological and ICU-related risk factors.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to identify factors associated with post-traumatic stress symptom severity and probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in ICU relatives.

METHODS: In this prospective multicentre cohort study (FAME), we enrolled consecutive adults on mechanical ventilation for ≥48 h in 60 ICUs in France (15 December 2022-30 January 2024); for each patient, we enrolled one relative. The relatives completed validated instruments during the ICU stay and follow-up interviews at three and six months. The primary outcome was higher PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 [PCL-5] at 3 months. Associations were sought using multivariable logistic regression for PCL-5 scores ≥31 and multivariable linear regression for three-month PCL-5 scores.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 1346 relatives, 936 (69·5%) completed PCL-5 at 3-month: 106 (11·3%) had probable PTSD and 358 (38·2%) clinically relevant post-traumatic stress symptoms. Factors associated with higher PCL-5 scores included pre-existing characteristics (social exclusion, living alone, perceived disability, and history of psychological trauma), early symptoms (anxiety, peritraumatic dissociation, and insomnia), and greater severity in the patients (vasopressor use and end-of-life decisions). Lower PCL-5 scores were associated with male sex and specific physician communication behaviours.

CONCLUSION: Post-traumatic stress symptoms were common, and approximately one in nine relatives had probable PTSD at three months. Knowledge of early psychological markers may help identify relatives at risk, while improved communication practices may decrease the risk.

articles.title: Pet keeping and perceived pet support show context-dependent associations with well-being during COVID-19.
articles.abstract: Companion animals were widely perceived as important sources of emotional support during the COVID-19 pandemic, yet studies examining the relationship between pet keeping and well-being reported mixed findings. One possible explanation is that subjective perceptions of pet-related support do not necessarily correspond to broader well-being outcomes and may depend on contextual and demographic factors. We analyzed data from a 3-measurement longitudinal survey conducted in Hungary during 2020 (N = 5,129; 3,479; 2,883 across measurement occasions). Mental well-being, COVID-related worries, and perceived pet-related support were assessed using validated scales and principal component analyses. Generalized linear models examined (1) associations between pet keeping and well-being, (2) factors related to perceived pet support, and (3) the relationship between perceived support and well-being across demographic and contextual conditions. Analyses were conducted separately for measurement occasion and pet species. Pet keeping was not consistently associated with greater well-being. A negative association emerged, but only in the third measurement occasion and disappeared after controlling for demographic composition, particularly age and household composition. COVID-related pet support was highly stable across measurement occasions and strongly overlapped with more general perceptions of pet support. Perceived support from dogs was highest, followed by support from cats and other pet species. At the same time, the association between COVID-related pet support and well-being was weak and strongly context-dependent. Individuals experiencing greater stress, financial strain, or life disruption were more likely to report stronger support from their pets despite lower well-being, suggesting that perceived pet support may partly reflect coping-related processes rather than direct well-being benefits. Overall, the findings suggest that companion animals may serve as psychologically meaningful sources of comfort during stressful periods without necessarily producing measurable improvements in global well-being. The results highlight a potential distinction between perceived support and well-being outcomes and may help explain why people consistently describe companion animals as highly beneficial despite mixed evidence for a general "pet effect."

articles.title: Initial Exercise Guidance for Children and Adolescents during and beyond Cancer Treatment: ACSM Expert Consensus Statement - Corrigendum.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

articles.title: Pan-cancer ctDNA panel and PET/CT in predicting true disease status after curative-intent treatment of head and neck cancer: a preliminary study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Early detection of minimal residual disease is essential in managing head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has been the standard imaging modality. Liquid biopsy (LB) of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has been introduced as a complementary method to enhance its diagnostic performance. The study aimed to investigate the performance of a pan-cancer ctDNA panel in conjunction with conventional PET/CT in the treatment response assessment. Patient/material and methods: Thirty-four patients with newly diagnosed HNSCC were prospectively enrolled, and 17 patients completed the study protocol. All patients underwent standard [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging and a single timepoint LB 3 months after completion of definitive oncological treatment. A commercially available pan-cancer assay was utilized for ctDNA detection and tissue genomic analysis. Statistical assessments were performed separately for pathogenic variants of ctDNA detected concordantly in tissue and LB and for all detected pathogenic variants of ctDNA.

RESULTS: The combination of ctDNA detection of concordant variants and PET/CT imaging contributed to the highest diagnostic accuracy in predicting true disease status. Sensitivity was highest for the combination of ctDNA detection of all variants and PET/CT imaging. Recurrence-free and overall survival were higher in patients having a negative LB in assessments of concordant variants when compared to those with a positive LB (p < 0.001 for both).

INTERPRETATION: A single-timepoint ctDNA detection with pan-cancer assay combined with PET/CT appears as a promising method for predicting true disease status in HNSCC. Our findings are presented as hypothesis generating due to the limited sample size.

articles.title: Summer ambient ozone and acute cardiovascular events in a changing climate: a population-based study of 8 million adults in eastern Poland.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ground-level ozone (O₃) is an underrecognized cardiovascular pollutant, but its acute effects and potential effect modification by heatwaves remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to assess same-day and lagged associations between summer O₃ exposure and cardiovascular mortality as well as the incidence of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included a population of 8 057 347 residents in 655 municipalities in eastern Poland during the summers of 2011-2020. Linked clinical records were consolidated into episodes and aggregated to 799 034 municipality-days. The 3 outcomes were modeled separately using random-effects negative binomial panel regression. Risk ratios (RRs) were estimated per 19.05 µg/m³ (interquartile range) increase in O₃, with adjustment for temporal and meteorological factors, including the Excess Heat Factor.

RESULTS: Over the 10 study summers, 112 907 cardiovascular deaths, 18 947 STEMI events, and 22 871 NSTEMI events were recorded; the mean (SD) ages were 78.8 (12.2), 67.4 (12.5), and 70.1 (11.9) years, respectively. Mean temperature and heatwave exposure increased over the study period. O₃ was associated with cardiovascular mortality (RR, 1.036; 95% CI, 1.026-1.046) and STEMI (RR, 1.035; 95% CI, 1.011-1.060), but not NSTEMI (RR, 0.997; 95% CI, 0.976-1.019). The association with cardiovascular mortality persisted after adjustment for fine particulate matter or nitrogen dioxide. The association with STEMI was attenuated after adjustment for fine particulate matter but persisted after adjustment for nitrogen dioxide. The association between O₃ and cardiovascular mortality was stronger during heatwaves (ratio of RRs, 1.035; 95% CI, 1.009-1.063).

CONCLUSIONS: Summer O₃ represents an underrecognized, climate-sensitive cardiovascular hazard associated with cardiovascular mortality and STEMI. The stronger association between O₃ and cardiovascular mortality during heatwaves highlights the potential importance of considering O₃ and extreme heat jointly in cardiovascular prevention and public health strategies.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life in patients with COPD in Türkiye: a meta-analysis of SGRQ scores and study-level correlates.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) reduces health-related quality of life (HRQoL), but estimates for Türkiye are lacking. We estimated St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) scores and explored study-level characteristics associated with differences between studies.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and TR Dizin were searched from inception to 14 September 2026. Studies of patients with COPD in Türkiye reported baseline SGRQ means and SDs were included. Means were pooled with random-effects models and 95% prediction intervals. Subgroup, moderator, and sensitivity analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: Fifty-four studies (4,561 participants) were included. The mean SGRQ total score was 51.22 (95% CI 48.09 to 54.35). Activity scored highest (62.31), then symptoms (55.59) and impacts (41.04). Heterogeneity was very high (I2 96.4% to 97.4%). Studies with mean FEV1 < 50% predicted, 6-minute walk distance <350 m, anxiety or depression scores ≥8, or BMI <25 kg/m2 reported higher scores; 16 of 32 subgroup comparisons remained significant after adjustment. In the moderator analysis, after adjustment for multiple testing, lower FEV1 and walk distance and higher anxiety scores remained associated with higher total scores, but the association with depression scores did not. Age, disease duration, and smoking weren't associated with scores.

CONCLUSION: SGRQ scores indicate considerable HRQoL impairment in COPD in Türkiye, most marked in the activity. Heterogeneity is very large, so the means are descriptive. Associations with airflow limitation, exercise capacity, and anxiety are study-level, exploratory, and don't establish patient-level determinants.

articles.title: Efficacy of an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system combined with habituation training in refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate an automated vestibular function diagnosis and treatment system (SRM-IV system) combined with habituation training in patients with refractory benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV).

METHODS: Clinical data were collected from 81 patients with refractory BPPV from December, 2023 to December, 2024. Thirty-eight received SRM-IV repositioning plus habituation training (intervention), and 43 received SRM-IV alone (control). Training was remotely supervised for three months. Follow-up was at six months.

RESULTS: Residual vertigo duration was shorter in the intervention group (6.7 ± 1.4 vs. 8.9 ± 1.6 days, p < 0.001), and the Dizziness Handicap Inventory score reduction was greater (54.5 ± 12.0 vs. 42.7 ± 11.6, p < 0.001); both were confirmed after adjustment for baseline scores (analysis of covariance, p < 0.001). Recurrence did not differ significantly between groups (28.9% vs. 34.9%, p = 0.64). Hypertension independently predicted recurrence (OR 3.65, 95% CI 1.21 to 11.05, p = 0.022). After excluding hypertensive patients, recurrence was lower in the intervention group (10.7% vs. 33.3%, p = 0.04).

CONCLUSION: Combined habituation training shortened residual vertigo and improved dizziness-related disability in refractory BPPV. The recurrence benefit became evident after excluding patients with hypertension. Blood pressure control may warrant attention in this population.

articles.title: When Immunodeficiency and Autoimmunity Collide: Baricitinib for Alopecia Areata in RNU4ATAC-Opathy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: RNU4ATAC-opathy comprises a spectrum of rare disorders caused by pathogenic variants affecting the minor spliceosome and is associated with growth restriction, skeletal dysplasia, hearing impairment, and immunodeficiency. Autoimmune manifestations are increasingly recognised but remain poorly characterised, and JAK inhibition has not previously been reported in this condition. Given the underlying immunodeficiency, it poses a unique dilemma when autoimmune manifestations arise, since immunomodulatory treatments carry increased infection risk in an already immunocompromised host.

METHOD: We describe a 9-year-old male with genetically confirmed RNU4ATAC-opathy who developed alopecia areata universalis and was treated with the JAK inhibitor baricitinib.

RESULTS: A 9-year-old boy with compound heterozygous pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants (n.13C>T and n.117A>G) had a complex phenotype including growth restriction, atopic dermatitis, epiphyseal dysplasia, bronchiectasis, and humoral immunodeficiency. In 2026, he presented with rapidly progressive alopecia areata, ultimately resulting in alopecia totalis, with complete loss of scalp hair, eyebrows, and eyelashes. Following multidisciplinary discussion, baricitinib was commenced at 4 mg daily. At just 8 weeks of treatment, there was marked regrowth of scalp hair with minimal activity seen on trichoscopy, and regrowth of eyebrows and eyelashes. Concurrent improvement in eczema was also observed, with an Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) of 0 at 8 weeks of therapy. Therapy was well tolerated without opportunistic infection, significant laboratory abnormalities, or treatment-limiting adverse effects. An infective exacerbation of bronchiectasis occurred shortly after treatment initiation; however, it responded to escalation of antimicrobial therapy without requiring cessation of baricitinib.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates successful treatment of alopecia areata universalis with baricitinib in a child with RNU4ATAC-opathy and hypogammaglobulinaemia. JAK inhibition may represent a promising therapeutic option for alopecia areata among patients with RNU4ATAC-related spliceosomeopathies and highlights the emerging role of immune dysregulation within this group of inborn errors of immunity.

articles.title: Prevalence of Antibiotic Allergy in Patients with Inborn Errors of Immunity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with inborn errors of immunity (IEI) are frequently exposed to antibiotics due to increased susceptibility to infection. Published data regarding rates of medication allergy in IEI are conflicting and may report higher rates of antibiotic allergy compared to the general population. However, many reported antibiotic allergies are not formally evaluated, leading to unnecessary avoidance of first-line antimicrobial therapy. Accurate identification of true antibiotic allergy is therefore important, as inappropriate allergy labels may contribute to the use of broader-spectrum antibiotics, increased antimicrobial resistance, higher healthcare costs, and suboptimal patient outcomes.

METHOD: This study will be conducted at Westmead Hospital, where patients with confirmed IEI currently receiving immunoglobulin replacement therapy will be reviewed to identify documented medication allergy labels, including implicated medications, reaction characteristics, and results of antibiotic testing performed. Results will be described, and statistical analysis will be used to determine the prevalence and characteristics of medication allergy in this population.

CONCLUSION: The findings of this project will help determine the prevalence of medication allergy within our cohort of patients and contribute to the currently limited body of knowledge regarding medication allergy in patients with IEI. The results may also help identify the need for larger collaborative studies involving other immunology units and support future research into antibiotic allergy assessment and de-labelling strategies aimed at improving antimicrobial stewardship and expanding safe treatment options for this patient population.

articles.title: A Rare Autoantibody with Catastrophic Consequences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5)-positive dermatomyositis is an uncommon inflammatory myopathy associated with minimal muscle involvement, rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease, and high mortality (1). We describe a severe case with rapidly progressive multisystem involvement requiring aggressive multimodal immunosuppression.

METHOD: A clinical case presentation with targeted literature review.

RESULTS: A previously well 40-year-old woman from Kenya presented with several weeks of cough, fatigue, weight loss, and progressive rash. Examination demonstrated heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, and severe digital pulp ischaemia with evolving dry gangrene. Laboratory testing showed anti-MDA5 and anti-Ro52 antibodies, elevated creatine kinase and transaminases, and thrombocytopenia. Magnetic resonance imaging of the thighs demonstrated bilateral symmetrical myositis, while chest imaging showed basal ground-glass pulmonary changes. Her course was complicated by spontaneous bilateral psoas muscle haematomas causing left femoral nerve palsy, recurrent seizures requiring intensive care admission, and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Her treatment included high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, rituximab, and tofacitinib, with subsequent escalation to cyclophosphamide and plasma exchange. Following prolonged inpatient care, she survived the acute illness and underwent rehabilitation with gradual improvement in left lower limb strength.

CONCLUSION: MDA5-positive dermatomyositis can follow a catastrophic course with rare multisystem complications. In severe or refractory disease, rapid recognition and early aggressive multimodal immunosuppression are critical to maximising the chance of meaningful recovery.

articles.title: JAK Inhibition in Refractory Ocular Surface Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic ocular inflammation following Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) is a rare but devastating condition that can lead to progressive cicatrisation, corneal failure, and irreversible visual loss despite intensive immunosuppression. Increasing evidence suggests that persistent immune dysregulation, rather than residual structural damage alone, contributes to ongoing ocular surface inflammation in severe disease. We describe a young woman with refractory ocular SJS requiring escalation to JAK inhibition after failure of conventional and biologic steroid-sparing therapy.

METHOD: A 22-year-old woman developed severe mucocutaneous SJS of uncertain trigger, with differential diagnoses including oral contraceptive-associated SJS and Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection. Her disease course was complicated by bilateral ocular involvement with progressive right-sided scarring and persistent inflammatory keratoconjunctivitis affecting the left eye. She also developed small airways disease with ground-glass changes on high-resolution computed tomography consistent with SJS-associated bronchiolitis.

RESULTS: Despite prolonged corticosteroid therapy, topical and oral calcineurin inhibition, intravenous Ig (IVIG), and high-dose mycophenolate mofetil, significant ocular inflammation persisted. Steroid-related complications included intractable glaucoma requiring tube surgery, further complicated by post-operative pseudomonal keratitis, as well as steroid-induced osteopenia. Etanercept partially improved her ocular inflammation and facilitated corticosteroid tapering; however, ongoing moderate chronic inflammation continued to prevent corneal graft surgery due to concerns about viability, delaying visual rehabilitation. Given refractory disease despite combined conventional and biologic immunosuppression, treatment was escalated to tofacitinib, which finally allowed tapering of oral prednisolone.

CONCLUSION: We describe the first reported case of severe ocular SJS responding to JAK inhibition, highlighting a promising new therapeutic approach for this potentially devastating condition.

articles.title: Give It a Shot: Design and Implementation of an In-Clinic Vaccination Program Addressing Gaps in Vaccination Uptake in Immunocompromised Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunosuppression risk management strategies in the real world often fail to adequately meet opportunities for the prevention of vaccine-preventable disease. To remedy this, the Department of Immunology at Concord Hospital collaborated with the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) Public Health Unit to develop the Vaccination@Concord initiative in immunology clinics. The goal is to immunise National Immunisation Program (NIP)-eligible immunocompromised patients at the time of clinic review. We present a review of the uptake of this program so far.

METHOD: A multistep process was conceived: first, current vaccination status was determined from the Australian Immunisation Registry (AIR) for clinic patients. Second, a personalised gap analysis was developed by integrating immune status, vaccination status, and NIP qualification criteria. Third, physician recommendations were made to the patient, followed by formal consent. Fourth, vaccines were provided in clinic. Fifth, a database was developed to support process improvement and document uptake and reasons for vaccine refusal. Mpox vaccination was not included. This is a Quality Improvement initiative.

RESULTS: Between January and June 2026, n = 75 (49% female) patients received 111 vaccines in clinic. Causes of underlying immunocompromise include human immunodeficiency virus infection (42.6%), primary immunodeficiency (28%), secondary immunodeficiencies from non-B cell-depleting immunosuppression (22.6%), and B cell depletion therapy (9.3%). The majority of patients (57%) received more than one vaccine at the same clinic visit. Shingrix was the most frequently administered vaccine. COVID was the most refused vaccine. Patterns of vaccine uptake and refusal will be presented.

CONCLUSION: We have established that in-clinic vaccination is feasible and well received. Individual vaccines encounter more refusal than others. Further directions for the program will look at increasing the repertoire of available vaccines, expanding the initiative into more services and clinics, and addressing reasons for refusal.

articles.title: Treat the Antibody or Treat the Pathway? A Case of Complement-Mediated Thrombotic Microangiopathy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome (aHUS) is a complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy associated with dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway. A small subset of patients has been identified with homozygous deletions of complement factor H-related proteins (CFHR1 and CFHR3) with anti-factor H autoantibodies, creating a unique overlap between genetic susceptibility and acquired autoimmunity.

METHOD: We describe a child with deletion of complement factor H-related proteins and autoantibody-positive haemolytic uraemic syndrome (DEAP-HUS) and review the challenges of long-term management.

RESULTS: A previously well 10-year-old boy presented with severe thrombotic microangiopathy following an infectious illness. He developed haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, and evidence of alternative complement pathway activation. ADAMTS13 activity was normal, and Shiga toxin testing was negative. Anti-factor H autoantibodies were strongly positive, and subsequent genetic testing identified homozygous deletions of CFHR1 and CFHR3. Treatment with eculizumab resulted in rapid resolution of thrombotic microangiopathy and recovery of renal function. He was subsequently transitioned to ravulizumab. Although short-term mycophenolate mofetil was administered, anti-factor H autoantibody titres remained persistently elevated. Nearly two years following diagnosis, he remains clinically well with normal renal function, normal blood counts, and no evidence of relapse despite several intercurrent infections.

CONCLUSION: The diagnostic pathway in DEAP-HUS is increasingly well recognised; however, optimal long-term management remains uncertain. Persistent anti-factor H autoantibodies despite complete clinical remission raise important questions regarding the role of ongoing complement blockade, immunosuppression, treatment withdrawal, and relapse risk. This case highlights the intersection of complement genetics and autoimmunity and illustrates the challenges of balancing treatment burden, long-term safety, and preservation of renal function in a rare complement-mediated disorder.

articles.title: Mannose-Binding Lectin Deficiency Presenting with Recurrent Encapsulated Bacterial Infections: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mannose-binding lectin (MBL) deficiency is a common innate immune defect associated with increased susceptibility to encapsulated bacterial infections, particularly in childhood. Although often asymptomatic in adults, a subset experiences recurrent respiratory infections requiring investigation for underlying immunodeficiency. This case describes an adult male with recurrent lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) and confirmed MBL deficiency, highlighting the importance of recognising innate immune defects in patients with persistent bacterial infections.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 43-year-old male, born in the UK, with a history of asthma, eczema, and allergic rhinitis, reported recurrent LRTIs since early childhood, including multiple hospital admissions. He received repeated courses of oral antibiotics over two years. Documented pathogens included Haemophilus influenzae (×2), Moraxella catarrhalis, and Streptococcus pneumoniae. He also experienced recurrent oral HSV. There was no history of meningitis, encephalitis, invasive fungal or viral infections, chronic diarrhoea, weight loss, or abscesses. Family history was notable for recurrent LRTIs in his father and two sons.

INVESTIGATIONS: Immunoglobulins showed elevated IgG (19.20 g/L) and IgE (939 kIU/L) with normal IgA and IgM. Lymphocyte subsets were within reference ranges. Complement (C3, C4, and CH50), neutrophil function, coeliac serology, and peripheral smear were normal. CT imaging demonstrated diffuse bronchial wall thickening and small nonspecific pulmonary nodules. Pneumococcal IgG response was adequate. Initial genetic testing did not identify pathogenic variants. MBL level was <56 ng/mL, and further genetic analysis confirmed MBL2 variants Gly54Asp and Arg52Cys.

MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOMES: The patient was vaccinated and commenced on prophylactic antibiotics, with subsequent clinical stability.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights MBL deficiency as an important consideration in adults with recurrent encapsulated bacterial infections, particularly when accompanied by a supportive family history. Early recognition enables targeted preventive strategies and improved long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Steroid-Responsive Lymphocytic Interstitial Pneumonitis Revealing T Cell-Dominant Chronic Active Epstein-Barr Virus Disease.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus (CAEBV) is a rare and under-recognised lymphoproliferative disorder characterised by persistent infectious mononucleosis-like symptoms, systemic organ involvement, and significant morbidity and mortality. It predominantly affects individuals of East Asian ancestry and is driven by clonal expansion of EBV-infected T or natural killer (NK) cells. Delayed recognition is common, and without definitive treatment, prognosis is poor.

CASE HISTORY: We present a case of a 14-year-old Chinese boy with a 4-year history of recurrent respiratory illnesses, intermittent cytopaenias, variable hepatosplenomegaly, and persistent EBV viraemia (1.3-2.2 × 104 copies/mL), with a previous episode of likely EBV-associated neuroinflammation. The diagnostic sentinel presentation was with fevers, cough, respiratory distress, and hypoxia. Imaging demonstrated diffuse bilateral airspace changes, and subsequent bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was complicated by pulmonary haemorrhage; however, cytology showed marked eosinophilia. Lung biopsy demonstrated EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER)-positive lymphocytic interstitial pneumonitis, with concurrent EBV viraemia confirming active EBV-associated disease. Treatment with intravenous corticosteroids resulted in rapid clinical, radiological, and biochemical improvement. Review of prior investigations identified detectable EBV viraemia dating back to 2023. Despite discharge on oral corticosteroids, positron emission tomography (PET) imaging demonstrated persistent FDG-avid nodularity and ongoing active disease within the bilateral lower lobes. Ultrasound-guided lymph node biopsy subsequently confirmed CAEBV with predominant T cell involvement and no evidence of lymphoma. Trio whole-exome sequencing with an immunological disorders gene panel identified no variants of clinical significance.

MANAGEMENT: Given his ongoing progression of pulmonary disease, treatment was subsequently intensified with further pulse intravenous steroids and cyclosporin. With worsening illness, T cell-dominant CAEBV, and the absence of an identifiable immunodeficiency amenable to targeted therapy, he was initiated on cytoreductive chemotherapy with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone (CHOP) as a bridge to definitive haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), the only recognised curative intervention for CAEBV.

articles.title: Nutrition Issues in Children Living with Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) are genetic conditions that impair immune function, increasing susceptibility to infection, risk of severe illness, and impact on quality of life. Nutrition plays a critical role in supporting immune function; however, little research has explored nutrition-related complications in IEI using a qualitative approach. This study is the first qualitative study to investigate a wide range of nutrition-related issues and nutrition care in paediatric IEI across multiple diagnoses in Australia.

METHOD: An online survey and qualitative interviews were undertaken to explore nutrition-related issues and nutrition care for individuals with clinically diagnosed IEI. Parents/carers of infants/children (≤10 years) were recruited through social media and patient support networks. Survey data were analysed descriptively; interview data were examined using thematic analysis.

RESULTS: Thirteen parents completed the survey; five parents participated in interviews. Most children (n = 11) were diagnosed before age 2, with severe combined immunodeficiency the most common condition. Qualitative findings identified multiple nutrition-related issues, including early breastfeeding cessation, faltering growth, gastrointestinal disturbances, feeding difficulties, poor appetite, and the need for nutritional support. Interviews highlighted inconsistencies and gaps in the provision of nutrition care.

CONCLUSION: Nutrition-related issues in IEI are varied, multifactorial, and often complex. Findings highlight the need to recognise nutrition as a core component of IEI management. Developing standardised nutrition guidelines is essential to address current inconsistencies in care and support long-term health and wellbeing for people with IEI and their families.

articles.title: JAK Inhibition in Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome: A Case Series from Sydney Children's Hospital.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Febrile Infection-Related Epilepsy Syndrome (FIRES) is a subcategory of New-Onset Refractory Status Epilepticus (NORSE) occurring in previously healthy individuals following a mild febrile illness. FIRES is a challenging paediatric condition with a mortality of 12% and permanent neurocognitive deficits in up to 90% of survivors. Pathogenesis appears to involve innate immune dysregulation, and first-line immunotherapy (intravenous immunoglobulin [IVIG], corticosteroids) is ineffective in most cases. A number of second-line cytokine-directed therapies have been trialled in individual case reports and short case series, but with similarly unencouraging outcomes.

METHOD: We describe three paediatric patients managed at Sydney Children's Hospital between 2024 and 2026 in whom baricitinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor, was incorporated into the immunotherapy regimen for FIRES.

RESULTS: Patient 1 was a 13-year-old girl diagnosed with FIRES with refractory status epilepticus. After 2 months of uncontrolled seizures with profound functional decline and brain atrophy, baricitinib was added to her treatment regimen. While she eventually succumbed to her illness, the introduction of JAK inhibition was accompanied by electroencephalogram (EEG) normalisation within two weeks. Patient 2, a 15-year-old girl, presented following a post-appendicectomy febrile illness. She developed refractory status epilepticus with negative autoimmune and paraneoplastic workup and markedly elevated neopterin (347 nmol/L; normal range [NR] = 0 - 30). Treatment with IVIG, methylprednisolone, and plasma exchange (PLEX) followed by baricitinib and anakinra achieved seizure control over a period of weeks. Intermittent focal seizures and encephalopathic EEG changes persist, but with return to premorbid function and return to school. Patient 3 is a 16-year-old girl who presented in March 2026 with febrile encephalopathy and escalating seizures. Following intubation, multi-agent antiepileptic therapy, and immunosuppression, including baricitinib, anakinra, and IVIG, she was extubated after 2 weeks with subsequent functional recovery, returning to school with mild residual cognitive and emotional changes.

CONCLUSION: This case series adds to the limited evidence supporting early and aggressive JAK inhibition in paediatric FIRES. The addition of baricitinib appears to offer clinically meaningful seizure reduction and EEG improvement when used alongside cytokine-directed therapy.

articles.title: Antibody Responses and Immune Memory Formation After COVID-19 Vaccination in Patients with Primary Immunodeficiency.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Primary immunodeficient (PID) patients may have poor vaccination responses and high susceptibility to severe infections, including COVID-19. Our objective was to evaluate the SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG, memory B cells (Bmem), and memory T cells (Tmem) following COVID-19 vaccination to ascertain whether third-dose COVID-19 vaccination is effective in generating immune memory in PID patients.

DESIGN AND METHOD: 25 PID patients and 29 healthy controls were sampled one month after doses two and three of the COVID-19 vaccination. Serum neutralising antibody (NAb) titres were determined in live virus assays. Using recombinant spike receptor-binding domains (RBD), we analysed plasma IgG by ELISA and Bmem by flow cytometry directed against ancestral and Omicron variants. Using overlapping peptide pools for the ancestral spike protein, we analysed activation-induced marker expression on the surface of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.

RESULTS: Regardless of mRNA or adenoviral vector vaccine priming, ancestral RBD-specific IgG levels and Nab titres were significantly lower in PID patients than controls after both doses, with minimal boosting at dose 3. Ancestral RBD-specific IgG and Nab cross-recognition of Omicron BA.5 were lower in patients than controls after both doses, with boosting evident at dose 3 in both cohorts. Despite normal total Bmem numbers, patients had fewer ancestral RBD-specific Bmem and reduced cross-recognition of both Omicron BA.2 and BA.5. Patients had increased frequencies of RBD-specific Bmem expressing CD71, and lower frequencies of IgG- and IgA-expressing RBD-specific Bmem. Total and spike-specific CD8+ Tmem were lower in patients than controls after both doses, with significant boosting upon dose 3. Spike-specific CD4+ Tmem of patients expressed lower CD69 expression and contained lower frequencies of IFNγ+TNFα+ cells than controls. Compared to patients who had seroconverted at dose 3, those patients lacking a NAb response exhibited a lower number of spike-specific CD4+ Tmem and RBD-specific Bmem, whilst numbers of spike-specific CD8+ Tmem were similar between both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, a large fraction of adult PID patients have an impaired vaccine response to COVID-19. Most patients demonstrate an intact spike-specific CD4+ and/or CD8+ Tmem response, whereas antibody, NAb, and Bmem responses are frequently reduced. Therefore, measurement of cellular responses may better reflect immune competence and is likely scalable for routine evaluation of responses to vaccination and infection. Furthermore, unlike antibody and NAb measurement, quantification of Tmem and Bmem responses is unaffected by receipt of immunoglobulin replacement therapy.

articles.title: XEMBIFY Real-World Evaluation of Utilization Patterns, Patient-Reported Outcomes, and Value Within the Connex Patient Support Program: The XPERIENCE Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Primary and secondary immunodeficiencies (PID and SID) and immune-mediated conditions such as chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP) are associated with long-term healthcare needs and reduced quality of life. These patients receive treatment with immunoglobulins, either as replacement therapy or for immunomodulation. Subcutaneous immunoglobulin (SCIg) has been demonstrated to be as effective as intravenous immunoglobulin, enabling flexible administration; however, real-world evidence on treatment utilization, tolerability, and patient experience in Australia remains limited. The XPERIENCE study aims to characterize real-world utilization patterns of Xembify (SCIg 20%), patient-reported outcomes, and healthcare resource utilization within the CONNEX Patient Support Program (PSP).

METHOD: This is a multicentre, single-arm, observational study conducted in Australian public tertiary hospitals. Paediatric and adult patients (≥2 years) receiving Xembify as part of routine clinical care, as defined by the National Blood Authority (confirmed diagnosis of PID, SID, CIDP), with stable doses for ≥3 months, and within the CONNEX PSP will be enrolled. Patients will be followed for 12 months with scheduled assessments at baseline and quarterly visits (Figure 1). The primary objective is to describe treatment utilization patterns, including dosing and administration parameters. Secondary objectives include evaluation of patient-reported outcomes (Life Quality Index [LQI], EQ-5D-5L, and Work Productivity and Activity Impairment [WPAI]), infection burden, safety and tolerability, and healthcare resource utilization. Data will be collected from medical records, patient infusion diaries, and standardized questionnaires.

RESULTS: 100 patients are expected to be enrolled over a 6-month recruitment period. Analyses will be descriptive and conducted for the overall population. Subject to patient numbers, analyses will be stratified by indication and age group.

CONCLUSION: The XPERIENCE study will generate real-world evidence on Xembify, including treatment utilization, patient-reported outcomes, and healthcare resource utilization to support optimization of immunoglobulin delivery and SCIg strategies, informing patient-centred care and healthcare resource planning. Figure 1. XPERIENCE study design.

articles.title: When Interleukin-1 Blockade Is Not Equal: Differential Response to Anakinra and Canakinumab in NLRP1-Associated Autoinflammation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: NLRP1-associated autoinflammation with arthritis and dyskeratosis (NAIAD) is a rare inflammasomopathy characterised by excessive interleukin-1 (IL-1) signalling, systemic inflammation, arthritis, dyskeratotic skin lesions, and growth impairment. Experience with targeted biologic therapy remains limited.

METHOD: We describe a child with genetically confirmed NAIAD who demonstrated differential responses to IL-1-targeted therapies.

RESULTS: A 9-year-old boy with a de novo pathogenic NLRP1 variant presented with severe immune dysregulation characterised by recurrent fevers, inflammatory arthritis, hepatosplenomegaly, dyskeratotic skin disease, inflammatory keratitis, growth failure, and persistently elevated inflammatory markers. Initial treatment with sirolimus was limited by pancytopenia and inadequate disease control. High-dose anakinra (>6 mg/kg/day) resulted in partial clinical improvement, particularly of arthritis and systemic inflammation; however, serum amyloid A remained elevated and significant disease manifestations persisted. To improve disease control, adjunctive baricitinib was introduced but was subsequently ceased following worsening cytopenias and a significant primary Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection requiring hospitalisation. Given ongoing inflammation and concerns regarding long-term risk of amyloidosis, canakinumab was approved and commenced at 4 mg/kg every four weeks. Following transition, the patient demonstrated complete normalisation of inflammatory markers and serum amyloid A concentrations (<5 mg/L) for the first time. Clinically, appetite improved, hepatosplenomegaly reduced, arthritis remained controlled, and catch-up growth was observed. Treatment burden was substantially reduced through replacement of daily injections with monthly therapy.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates successful treatment of NLRP1-associated autoinflammation with canakinumab following incomplete response to high-dose anakinra and toxicity associated with adjunctive JAK inhibition. The marked biochemical and clinical response supports a central role for IL-1β in NLRP1-mediated disease and suggests that direct cytokine neutralisation may offer advantages over receptor blockade in selected inflammasomopathies. Further experience is required to determine whether this observation is generalisable to other patients with NAIAD.

articles.title: Infectious Disease Physicians' Attitudes Towards Immunology Training and Co-Management of Immunodeficiency.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inborn errors of immunity, though rare individually, are common overall and often go undiagnosed. The COVID-19 pandemic renewed public and professional interest in immunology. Recurrent infections are the commonest presentation, suggesting that infectious disease physicians (IDPs) are frequently involved in managing these patients. Despite this need, Singapore's Specialist Accreditation Board lists 36 specialties and 10 subspecialties but does not include clinical immunology, potentially highlighting an underrecognized, unmet clinical need in Singapore.

METHOD: This study involves a 14-question online survey of IDPs from a single healthcare cluster in Singapore, exploring their exposure to clinical immunology during their training, as well as their perceptions of the potential role and value of clinical immunologists in patient care.

RESULTS: A response rate of 27/40 (67.5%) was achieved. All respondents acknowledged the importance of formal immunology training in the management of complex immune-related infections. The majority (22/27, 81.5%) see relevance in the incorporation of clinical immunology in senior residency training. While most respondents agreed that their training adequately covered secondary immunodeficiency (SID), this was less so for primary immunodeficiency (PID). The top 3 situations where IDPs most value clinical immunology input include management of recurrent or unusual infections, suspected PID, and interpretation of immunological tests. The majority of respondents felt that there is a gap in immunology expertise in their current practice setting and that access to this would improve patient outcomes. Most IDPs prefer to have the option to either discuss cases (40.7%) or co-manage (55.6%) patients with suspected PID; however, as case complexity increases, there is a stronger preference for shared, joint management (66.7%) rather than discussion alone (29.6%).

CONCLUSION: IDPs recognize and value the importance of clinical immunology training and expertise in their practice. Greater efforts are needed to acknowledge and strengthen the role of clinical immunology within Singapore's healthcare system.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 Infection Unmasking Thymoma-Associated Immunodeficiency.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Good's syndrome (GS) is characterised by the presence of thymoma with hypogammaglobinaemia.

METHOD: We describe a case of thymoma-associated immunodeficiency diagnosed following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

RESULT: A 73-year-old male initially presented to the emergency department with SARS-CoV-2 infection and small-volume haemoptysis on day 6 of illness. Despite receiving three doses of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 mRNA vaccine, the anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike protein IgG antibody test was negative. He did not require oxygen supplementation and received 3 days of i.v. remdesivir. He was discharged well on day 13 of illness. He re-presented to the emergency department on day 19 of illness with acutely worsening shortness of breath and desaturation at home. Despite receiving 14 days of i.v. baricitinib, he continued to deteriorate and was subsequently transferred to the intensive care unit for worsening type 1 respiratory failure despite prone positioning. After a trial of high-flow nasal cannulation, the patient was subsequently intubated.Serum gamma globulin levels were checked in view of persistently negative anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike and nucleocapsid protein IgG antibodies, which showed low serum IgG and IgA levels. Plasma cytomegalovirus PCR and serum galactomannan antigen tests were also positive. Mucus from the endotracheal tube and subsequently bronchoalveolar lavage grew Klebsiella pneumoniae and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia. Computed tomography of the thorax incidentally revealed a 3.3-cm by 2.1-cm anterior mediastinal mass, consistent with a thymoma. Despite appropriate treatment with targeted antimicrobials and antivirals, and i.v. immunoglobulin therapy, the patient developed a new nosocomial infection and died on day 54 of illness.

CONCLUSION: Our patient presented with GS late in life, with hypogammaglobulinaemia, poor COVID-19 vaccine responses, and a thymoma. He ultimately succumbed to multiple opportunistic and viral infections despite appropriate treatment.

articles.title: Caught in the Autoimmune Crossfire.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Drug-induced lupus and vasculitis may occur independently or as overlapping syndromes, with numerous implicated drugs. Anti-histone antibodies assist in differentiating these entities from their idiopathic counterparts (1). We present a case of a man in his 80s with drug-induced lupus and vasculitis, complicated by treatment-resistant hypertension and thrombocytopenia.

METHOD: Case presentation featuring clinical progress, investigations, and targeted literature review.

RESULTS: The patient presented with progressive breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain, and fevers without an identifiable infective focus. CT chest revealed bilateral lower lobe ground-glass changes and pleural effusions. He subsequently developed lower limb purpura and bicytopenia (Hb 81 g/L, platelets 109 × 109/L). C-reactive protein (CRP) was 146 mg/L. Acute renal impairment was also evident with Cr 209 uM and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 25 mL/min/1.73 m2, alongside microscopic haematuria (<20% dysmorphic red cells) and proteinuria. Serology showed >1:160 perinuclear anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (pANCA) with anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) and anti-PR3 antibody levels of >222 IU/L and 20 IU/L, respectively. A 1:2,560 homogeneous ANA was detected with elevated anti-double-stranded DNA (108 IU/mL) and anti-histone (9.7 U) antibodies, along with a low C4 0.13 g/L level. Serology was negative for anti-phospholipid and anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibodies. Cryoglobulins were absent. Renal biopsy showed pauci-immune glomerulonephritis with secondary tubular and interstitial damage. A fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) scan excluded large-vessel vasculitis and malignancy. A novel finding of myocarditis was identified on echocardiogram and confirmed on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The most likely culprit, hydralazine, was ceased. Modifications were made to his antihypertensive regimen, with a decision to continue methyldopa, although blood pressure control remained suboptimal. He was pulsed with intravenous methylprednisolone followed by a tapering course of prednisolone and induction doses of rituximab. Disease activity markers, including anti-histone antibody levels, improved, and he remains in remission on maintenance rituximab.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights overlapping hydralazine-induced lupus and ANCA-associated vasculitis. Anti-histone antibody levels were a useful adjunct to monitor disease activity and exclude methyldopa as the primary inciting agent. Treatment with rituximab was shown to be effective.

articles.title: Persistent Profound Isolated T Cell Lymphopenia in a 74-Year-Old Man with Disseminated Mycobacterium bovis Infection.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: T cell depletion is a recognised phenomenon in tuberculosis, including in HIV-negative patients, and is thought to result from lymphocyte sequestration, chronic immune activation, and impaired lymphopoiesis (1, 2, 3). While these abnormalities are typically reversible with treatment, severe mycobacterial infection may also unmask an underlying immunodeficiency (1, 2, 4). We report a patient with persistent profound isolated T cell lymphopenia despite successful treatment of disseminated Mycobacterium bovis infection.

METHOD: Case report with literature review.

RESULTS: A 74-year-old Caucasian Australian man presented with disseminated M. bovis infection involving lymph nodes, lungs, left adrenal gland, and right hip capsule. The presumed source was reactivation of latent childhood infection acquired through consumption of unpasteurised dairy products. He reported several years of constitutional symptoms preceding diagnosis. Historical pathology demonstrated a progressive decline in absolute lymphocyte count coinciding with the onset of symptoms. There was no history of recurrent, severe, opportunistic, or atypical infections, and no prior immunosuppressive therapy. Flow cytometry demonstrated profound isolated T cell lymphopenia with preservation of B cell and natural killer (NK) cell populations. CD4 count was 19 cells/µL (0.02 × 109/L) and CD8 count was 0.02 × 109/L at diagnosis. Full blood count was otherwise unremarkable, and immunoglobulin levels were normal. HIV and human T lymphotropic virus (HTLV) serology were negative, anti-interferon gamma autoantibodies were not detected, and QuantiFERON Gold demonstrated a preserved mitogen response.
