Potassium testing was conducted using a whole blood and serum chemistry analyzers. The hemolysis index (HI) was spectrophotometrically measured and available on 12 of the 14 hemolyzed serum samples.

RESULTS: The median time between the initial blood draw at ED presentation to the initiation of insulin was statistically higher (p<0.05) at 135 min for the hypokalemic group than for the eukalemic or hyperkaleic groups (91 and 89 min respectively). For the 14 patient encounters demonstrating hemolysis, there was also a delay in the median time to receive insulin at 129 min (p=0.058 and p<0.022) for eukalemic and hyperkalemic groups, respectively). Repeat blood collection for retesting caused some of this delay. Using the free hemoglobin concentration, an estimated corrected potassium level was made on the 12 patient encounters using published formulae.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypokalemia and the presence of hemolysis results in a delay in insulin treatment. Reporting a corrected potassium level may lead to earlier administration of insulin.

articles.title: First-in-Man Use of the Tau20-RETROmapping System to Identify and Guide Ablation of Ectopy-Triggering Ganglionated Plexuses During Sinus Rhythm as Nonpulmonary Vein Drivers of Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary vein (PV) isolation is ineffective in a proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). The Tau20-RETROmapping system was developed to help identify non-PV drivers of AF. We tested the feasibility of using the system to guide ablation of non-PV drivers during sinus rhythm.

METHODS: This was a prospective feasibility study of only non-PV ablation in patients with symptomatic AF. The Tau20-RETROmapping system was used to identify ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus (ET-GP) in the left atrium with synchronized high-frequency stimulation (50 mA, 40 Hz, 80 ms, 15 trains) during sinus rhythm. ET-GP sites were ablated with radiofrequency lesions until they were nonfunctional. Triggered atrial tachycardias were also mapped and ablated. Patients were followed for 12 months with scheduled Holter monitoring and patient-activated ECG recordings. The primary end point was atrial arrhythmia lasting ≥30 seconds after a 90-day blanking period.

RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were recruited: 8 patients with AF despite durably isolated PVs and 15 undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF. On average, 85±15 sites were tested in patients with isolated PVs (2.5±0.9 previous AF ablations, 61±9 years, LVEF 58±5%, LAd 41±2 mm), identifying 11.8±3.8 ET-GPs. Four of the eight patients also had ablation of triggered atrial tachycardias. Of the 15 patients undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF (duration 2.8±1.1 years, continuous AF ≥6 months in 80%, 64±7 years, LAd 43±2 mm), 10 completed a full left atrial ET-GP map of 102±37 tested sites. identifying 14±4.5 ET-GP sites. After a mean follow-up of 12 months and cessation of antiarrhythmic agents, arrhythmia-free survival was 63% in patients with durably isolated veins and 60% in those undergoing a first procedure for persistent AF.

CONCLUSIONS: The Tau20-RETROmapping system can identify and guide ablation of high-frequency stimulation-provoked ectopy-triggering ganglionated plexus during sinus rhythm as potential non-PV drivers of AF. This feasibility study shows promising outcomes that need exploration in larger randomized controlled studies.

articles.title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided or Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided PCI for In-Stent Restenosis Lesions: Insights From the OCTIVUS Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) remains a significant challenge despite advances in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) technology. Although intravascular imaging improves procedural optimization, direct comparative data between optical coherence tomography (OCT) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for ISR treatment remain limited.

METHODS: This study was a prespecified analysis of ISR lesions from the OCTIVUS trial (Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Versus Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention). The primary outcome was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel-related myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization. Crude and adjusted analyses using inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting and overlap propensity score weighting were performed.

RESULTS: Among the 2008 patients enrolled in the OCTIVUS trial, 164 (8.2%) underwent intravascular imaging-guided PCI for ISR lesions; 86 (52.4%) underwent OCT-guided PCI and 78 (47.6%) underwent IVUS-guided PCI. At a median follow-up of 1.8 years, the incidence of target-vessel failure was significantly lower in the OCT-guided group than in the IVUS-guided group (10.5% versus 29.5%; hazard ratio, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.16-0.74]; P=0.007). The lower incidence of target-vessel failure with OCT was consistent in adjusted analyses using inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (hazard ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.69]; P=0.004) and overlap propensity score weighting (hazard ratio, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.14-0.70]; P=0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: For the treatment of ISR lesions, OCT-guided PCI was associated with a lower risk of target-vessel failure than IVUS-guided PCI. However, given the exploratory nature of this analysis, these findings should not be considered clinically directive and warrant further investigation.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT03394079.

articles.title: Waste Not, Want Not: Making Echocardiography Work in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
Advanced Design Strategies of Natural Drug Molecule-Based Hydrogels for Diabetic Wound Healing: A Review.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds are a common and serious chronic complication of diabetes. They are characterized by persistent hyperglycemia, excessive oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, microcirculatory dysfunction, infection, impaired angiogenesis, and defective tissue remodeling. Current clinical treatments, such as debridement, infection control, offloading, and moisture regulation, only partially correct these pathological changes. Hydrogels loaded with natural bioactive compounds have therefore attracted increasing attention because they combine the advantages of a moist, biocompatible matrix with the multitarget biological activities of natural molecules. This review focuses on four major classes of natural bioactive compounds used in hydrogel systems for diabetic wounds: polyphenols, alkaloids, volatile oils, and polysaccharides. Beyond a descriptive summary of reported systems, this review analyzes how the chemical properties of each class determine the suitable loading and crosslinking strategies, and how these material design choices influence drug release, mechanical properties, and therapeutic outcomes. Representative hydrogel systems are compared in terms of drug loading, release behavior, mechanical performance, and biological effects, with emphasis on which systems are more suitable for different stages of diabetic wound repair. The review also discusses key challenges in clinical translation, including product standardization, controlled release, long-term safety, and limitations of current preclinical models. The heterogeneity of diabetic wounds and the potential for adaptive or personalized hydrogel systems are also considered. Overall, this review aims to provide a practical basis for selecting and designing natural medicine-based hydrogels according to the dominant pathological features and healing stage of diabetic wounds.

articles.title: Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias Performed With ECMO Support: A 10-Year Institutional Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability due to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) represent an extremely high-risk but understudied population. We aimed to evaluate the intraprocedural stability, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and long-term outcomes in patients undergoing ECMO-supported VA ablation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients undergoing 64 catheter ablations of VAs with ECMO support (2016-2025). Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression.

RESULTS: The median age of the patients was 62 years, and 70% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At ECMO initiation, 40 patients (70%) presented with cardiogenic shock and 43 (75%) with electrical storm. ECMO provided robust stability; minimum mean arterial pressure was similar between ventricular and nonventricular tachycardia (55 versus 60 mm Hg; P=0.124). In-hospital mortality was 42% (24/57 [95% CI, 30%-55%]). Multivariable analysis identified age (odds ratio [OR], 1.18 per year [95% CI, 1.05-1.38]; P=0.004), ischemic cardiomyopathy (OR, 24.3 [95% CI, 2.3-700.57]; P=0.005), chronic kidney disease (OR, 9.76 [95% CI, 1.89-73.26]; P=0.006), and New York Heart Association class III or IV (OR, 12.72 [95% CI, 1.86-158.46]; P=0.008) as mortality predictors, whereas VA elimination was an independent protector against in-hospital death (OR, 0.12 [95% CI, 0.01-0.77]; P=0.025). In patients presenting with electrical storm (n=43), VA elimination (n=33) was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality than VA recurrence (n=10; 27% versus 80%; P=0.007). Among survivors (n=33), 3-year survival was 78.0%, with low rates of cardiac death (3%, 1/33) during follow-up (11 [3-38] months).

CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-supported VA ablation is feasible and provides procedural stability. Although survival is limited by baseline reserve, VA elimination is associated with improved in-hospital outcomes, serving as a bridge to recovery or clinical decision.

articles.title: Twenty-One Years of Bariatric Surgery in Benin Republic: Evolution of Techniques and Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery was introduced in the Republic of Benin in 2005, yet, as in many sub-Saharan African countries, it has remained almost entirely undocumented.

OBJECTIVE: To describe how bariatric surgical techniques and their outcomes have evolved in Benin over a 21-year-period.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study including all patients who underwent bariatric surgery between January 1, 2005, and January 31, 2026, at two hospitals in Cotonou, Benin.

RESULTS: A total of 111 patients were included (mean age, 43.3 years; women, 85.6%; mean body mass index, 43.2 kg/m2). The procedures performed were laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (50.5%), adjustable gastric banding (37.8%), open sleeve gastrectomy (10.8%), and gastric bipartition (.9%). Gastric banding was discontinued in 2011, and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy has been the standard procedure since 2012. Excess weight loss at 48 months was 50% after sleeve gastrectomy versus 21% after gastric banding. At 48 months, sleep apnea, hypertension, and diabetes persisted in 8%, 11%, and 12% of patients after sleeve gastrectomy, compared with 35%, 36%, and 40% after gastric banding. Morbidity and mortality rates were 6.3% and 1.8%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery in Benin has successfully shifted to a minimally invasive approach, but its volume remains very low.

articles.title: Forecasting the Burden and Cost of Stroke in the United States: Projections by Sociodemographic Groups Through 2050: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Stroke Council; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Clinical Cardiology; Council on Hypertension; Council on Quality of Care and Outcomes Research; and Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Given expected increases in stroke burden in the United States through 2050, forecasts of the burden by age, sex, race, ethnicity, education level, income level, and health insurance status are needed.

METHODS: We used National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (January 2015-March 2020) and Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (2015-2019) data to estimate recent trends in stroke prevalence and costs, then projected prevalence and costs through 2050 accounting for population sociodemographic changes. We also projected prevalence by age, sex, race, and ethnicity strata.

RESULTS: We estimate that stroke will affect >9.0 million of ≈148 million men (6.1%) and >10.4 million of ≈154 million women (6.7%) by 2050. Prevalence will be highest among Black, American Indian/Alaska Native, and multiracial adults, reaching 25% to 30% among those >80 years of age, compared with 16% among White adults of the same age. The largest relative increases will occur among Hispanic and Asian Americans, with a 2- to 6-fold increase in absolute case numbers, depending on age. Prevalence will remain high among people with lower levels of education or income and those without health insurance; however, absolute numbers will roughly double, and costs will increase 5- to 8-fold among high school and college graduates and middle- and high-income earners. Adjusted for inflation, annual stroke care costs will quintuple to $142 billion among people 45 to 64 years of age. Young adults 20 to 44 years of age and Hispanic, American Indian/Alaska Native, and multiracial populations will experience cost increases >1000%.

CONCLUSIONS: The alarming rise in stroke burden projected by 2050 is expected to affect sociodemographic groups unequally. Programs and policies to prevent and treat stroke across age groups, mitigate widening healthcare disparities, and reduce costs are urgently needed.

articles.title: CACNA2D2 Regulates Mitochondrial Function to Attenuate Fibrosis and Atrial Fibrillation via the cGAS-STING Pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is thought to be driven by atrial fibrosis. A previous study has identified the expression of calcium voltage-gated channel auxiliary subunit alpha2delta2 (CACNA2D2) is significantly downregulated in patients with AF, but its functional role remains unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed CACNA2D2 expression levels using public databases and clinical samples. Fibroblast-specific Cacna2d2 knockout and overexpression models were established to assess its role in atrial fibrosis through in vivo electrophysiological recordings, histopathologic analysis, in vitro mitochondrial function assays, and biochemical studies. We also evaluated the role of Cacna2d2 in doxorubicin/myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis models.

RESULTS: We observed α2δ2 (encoded by CACNA2D2) expression was significantly reduced in patients with AF and Ang II (angiotensin II)-induced AF mouse models. Fibroblast-specific knockout of Cacna2d2 exacerbated Ang II-induced atrial fibrosis, increasing AF susceptibility and duration, whereas overexpression reversed these effects. In cardiac fibroblasts, Cacna2d2 overexpression blocked induction of ACTA2 (α-SMA) and COL1A1 (Col1). Mechanistically, Cacna2d2 localized to mitochondria when overexpressed in fibroblasts, blocked TGF-β (transforming growth factor-beta)-induced reactive oxygen species production and inhibit the leakage of mitochondrial DNA through the BAX/BAK channel, suppressing the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway. Notably, exogenous supplementation of Cacna2d2-overexpressing mitochondria significantly suppressed TGF-β-induced α-SMA and Col1 expression in fibroblasts. Cacna2d2 knockdown increased mortality and α-SMA expression, aggravating cardiac fibrosis in doxorubicin-treated mice, whereas its overexpression attenuated myocardial infarction-induced cardiac fibrosis and carbon tetrachloride-induced hepatic fibrosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrates that Cacna2d2 exerts antifibrotic effects by preserving mitochondrial function and preventing mitochondrial DNA-cGAS-STING pathway activation, identifying Cacna2d2 as a promising novel target for fibrotic diseases, including AF.

articles.title: Machine Learning Applied to Patient-Reported Outcomes and Passive Physiologic Sensor Data for Classification of Low Disease Activity in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated machine learning (ML) models using remotely collected patient-reported outcomes (ePROs) and wearable biosensor data to classify low disease activity (LDA) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) following treatment initiation.

METHODS: RA patients with moderate-to-high disease activity (Clinical Disease Activity Index [CDAI]>10) initiating adalimumab or upadacitinib were enrolled from 28 U.S. rheumatology clinics and followed for approximately 3-6 months. AI models used baseline clinical variables and longitudinal daily and weekly ePROs, including PROMIS measures, RADAI-5, patient global assessment, and daily pain and fatigue numeric rating scale items; a subset contributed wearable data. ML models were trained to classify follow-up LDA (~12 weeks; CDAI≤10). Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), area under the precision-recall curve (AUCPR), and F1-based metrics, including positive predictive value-constrained F1.

RESULTS: Among 150 participants with ePRO data, including 96 with wearable data, ePRO-based models achieved AUROCs of 0.745-0.857. Performance improved from 1- to 2-ePRO configurations, with limited gains from 2 to 3. The best weekly 2-ePRO generalized linear model rivaled more complex AI methods, with an AUROC of 0.843 and AUCPR 0.886. Reduced-Frequency data collection preserved predictive performance. Inclusion of wearable data did not improve performance in AI models and often resulted in lower discrimination, with wearable-only models demonstrating lower overall performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal ePRO-based ML models can classify follow-up LDA in RA using parsimonious, low-burden data collection strategies. Wearable data did not provide meaningful incremental value beyond ePROs, supporting the use of ePROs alone for routine remote monitoring of treatment response.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Smartwatch Irregular Rhythm Notification: Findings From the Apple Heart Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smartwatch irregular rhythm notifications (IRNs) can identify atrial fibrillation. IRNs' association with broader cardiovascular outcomes is unclear. We evaluated whether receipt of an IRN in the AHS (Apple Heart Study) was associated with subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events.

METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of the AHS, a prospective trial in the United States. Participants were enrolled via an iPhone app from 2017 to 2018; those who completed the end-of-study survey were included. The exposure was IRN receipt. Outcomes were self-reported new heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, and a composite of these events (major adverse cardiovascular events). Multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models included age, sex, heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, prior stroke/transient ischemic attack/systemic embolism, and vascular disease.

RESULTS: Among 293 944 participants who completed follow-up, 929 (0.32% [95% CI, 0.30%-0.34%]) received an IRN. Participants with an IRN were older, more often male, and had a greater burden of cardiovascular risk factors. At the end-of-study survey, completed 5 to 14 months after enrollment, IRN receipt was associated with higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure (odds ratio, 5.43 [95% CI, 3.09-9.57]), stroke/transient ischemic attack (odds ratio, 3.51 [1.91-6.45]), pulmonary embolism (odds ratio, 4.43 [1.92-10.20]), and major adverse cardiovascular events (odds ratio, 4.01 [2.80-5.73]). Among participants with an IRN but without atrial fibrillation, IRN receipt remained associated with statistically significantly higher adjusted odds of self-reported heart failure and major adverse cardiovascular events.

CONCLUSIONS: Receipt of a smartwatch IRN was associated with higher odds of subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events beyond atrial fibrillation. These findings suggest that IRNs may identify individuals at elevated short-term cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Opportunistic Central Nervous System Infections and Graft Outcomes in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opportunistic central nervous system (CNS) infections represent a source of morbidity and mortality among solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients. Clinicians must balance effective pathogen-directed treatment against risks of allograft rejection versus progression of infection. In this study, we defined the epidemiology and outcomes of CNS infections, including their impact on graft survival.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of SOT recipients evaluated at a transplant center between 2021 and 2024. All SOT recipients who underwent lumbar puncture and/or brain MRI were screened for CNS infection. Demographic and clinical data were extracted through medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 1206 SOT recipients who underwent transplantation and subsequent evaluation with LP/brain MRI, 52 (4.3%) patients met criteria for CNS infection. The cohort comprised 24 kidney (46.2%), 11 liver (21.2%), 11 lung (21.2%), 5 heart (9.6%), and one kidney-pancreas transplant recipient (1.9%). Median interval from transplantation to CNS infection was 19.5 months (range 0-334). Viral pathogens were the most common category(48.1%), while Cryptococcus (n = 8, 15.4%), and Aspergillus (n = 7, 13.5%) were the most frequently identified individual pathogens. Management frequently required modification of immunosuppressive therapy (n = 51, 98.1%). During follow-up, six patients (11.5%) developed allograft rejection within six months of CNS infection, while five (9.6%) experienced graft failure.

CONCLUSIONS: Allograft rejection and graft failure occurred in a substantial minority of patients. Given the high rate of immunosuppression adjustment, these findings highlight needs for multidisciplinary management strategies and evidence-based frameworks to guide medication modification during CNS infections.

articles.title: Clinical translation of viral targeting of the endothelium in pulmonary vascular diseases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary vascular diseases are characterized by endothelial dysfunction and progressive vascular remodeling. Most pulmonary vascular diseases, such as pulmonary hypertension, are rare but fatal. Although current therapies improve hemodynamics and clinical outcomes, they do not consistently restore endothelial homeostasis or reverse vascular remodeling, highlighting the potential of gene therapy as a disease-modifying strategy.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines the pulmonary vascular endothelium as a therapeutic target and discusses its heterogeneity, disease-dependent targetability, and its interactions with the other components of the vascular wall. We review adeno-associated viral, adenoviral, lentiviral and bocaviral vectors, including capsid/envelope engineering, receptor-mediated targeting, transcriptional and post-transcriptional restriction, and delivery routes. Therapeutic strategies such as gene replacement, transcription-factor delivery, and gene suppression are discussed, with particular emphasis on BMPR2. Translational barriers including viral vector immunity, species-dependent tropism, biodistribution, durability, controllability, manufacturing, and patient selection are also considered.

EXPERT OPINION: Pulmonary endothelial gene therapy represents a highly promising but clinically immature approach. Progress will depend on vectors that achieve selective transduction of pulmonary endothelial cells while minimizing off-target accumulation. Improved preclinical models including large animals or human tissue may guide vector development. Novel targeted vectors will enable effective gene transfer, thereby reducing dose and vector-based immunotoxicity.

articles.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Outcomes in a 15-Year Single-Center Cohort.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a frequent and potentially severe complication after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). We describe outcomes in a 15-year single-center cohort.

METHODS: All allo-HCT recipients with PCR-confirmed RSV infection at Karolinska University Hospital (January 2010-April 2024) were analyzed retrospectively. Outcomes were evaluated by time from HCT; ribavirin analyses were restricted to patients with upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) at presentation, at risk of progression to lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI).

RESULTS: Among 102 patients, 44 (43%) were diagnosed more than 1 year after HCT. Overall, 28 (27%) developed LRTI, including eight who progressed from URTI. RSV-associated mortality was 2/102 (2.0%); ICU admission occurred in 6/102 (5.9%). Progression from URTI to LRTI was more frequent when RSV was diagnosed within 30 days of HCT than later (4/11 [36%] vs. 4/71 [5.6%]; p = 0.010). Of 43 patients given ribavirin (predominantly oral), 31 were treated at the URTI stage; 5/31 (16%) progressed after initiation versus 2/51 (3.9%) untreated (p = 0.098). CRP was higher in LRTI than in URTI alone (median 50 vs. 17 mg/L; p = 0.011), but bacterial co-infection was also more frequent (32% vs. 14%; p = 0.045).

CONCLUSION: RSV-associated mortality after allo-HCT was low, but morbidity was prolonged, particularly early after transplantation. Findings should be interpreted cautiously given the late occurrence of RSV in many patients and differences in diagnostics and transplant practice compared with historical cohorts. This retrospective study did not show a protective effect of oral ribavirin. Prospective studies of prevention and treatment, including RSV vaccination, are warranted.

articles.title: Interosseous membrane stimulation for neuropathic and musculoskeletal pain in Veterans: real-world clinical outcomes from a retrospective case review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe patients receiving interosseous membrane stimulation (IMS) and evaluate changes in pain outcomes in a Veteran clinical cohort.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational case series.

SETTING: Veterans Health Administration neurology clinic.

METHODS: Clinical records were reviewed for Veterans treated with IMS between August 2024-April 2025. Demographic and clinical characteristics were summarized. Pain intensity was assessed using a 0-10 Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) before and after treatment sessions. Paired t-tests evaluated pre-post changes; Cohen's d effect sizes were calculated. Secondary analyses examined the proportion of sessions achieving a minimally clinically important difference (≥2-point NPRS reduction). Results: Twenty-eight patients (5 female; median age [IQR], 73 [15] years) contributed 43 sessions with paired NPRS data. Fourteen patients received multiple IMS treatments (range, 2-8 sessions). Mean NPRS scores decreased from 5.6 pre-treatment to 0.6 post-treatment, representing a mean reduction of 5.0 points (p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.8). Clinically meaningful improvement (≥2 points) was observed in 95.3% of analyzed treatment sessions (41/43 sessions). Exploratory analyses of longitudinal data (n = 9) showed no significant differences between the first and last sessions.

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial immediate pain reduction with IMS was observed and may offer an accessible nonpharmacologic intervention for neuropathic and musculoskeletal pain.

articles.title: Isolated Liver and Combined Liver-Pancreas Transplantation in Cystic Fibrosis: An Australia and New Zealand Expert Consensus Statement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: There are challenges around how transplant listing criteria, timing, waitlist management and graft selection might effectively meet the needs of people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) and advanced liver disease. A committee was assembled to formulate an approach for isolated liver transplant (LT) and combined liver-pancreas transplant (LPT) in this population.

METHODS: Twenty-two adult and paediatric transplant surgeons, hepatologists, gastroenterologists, pulmonologists, nephrologists and a transplant clinical nurse consultant devised questions regarding pre- and post-transplant management, including indications, contraindications and timing of LT and LPT in pwCF. PubMed literature search was performed for each question. Recommendations were voted on using the Delphi process, with ≥ 70% agreement to approve recommendations.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine questions were evaluated, of which 21 recommendations were approved. Broad consensus was that pwCF should receive priority on LT waiting lists because of the multi-system nature of CF (16/22, 73%). Prioritisation determined by consensus from the transplanting unit was considered the fairest approach (19/22, 86%). The committee recommended that combined LPT be considered in all patients with CF-related diabetes evaluated for LT (19/22, 86%). Recommended indications for LT included hepatic synthetic dysfunction and advanced portal hypertension (20/22, 91%); while uncontrolled systemic infection (21/22, 95%), poor lung function [FEV1 < 40%] (17/22, 77%) and severe portopulmonary hypertension (16/22, 73%) were proposed as contraindications. Poor treatment adherence or psychosocial concerns were considered relative contraindications (17/22, 77%). Quality of life should be factored in when considering LT (21/22, 95%). Portosystemic shunt placement may bridge patients with intractable variceal bleeding to LT (20/22, 91%). Aggressive pre-transplant nutritional optimisation (22/22, 100%), individualised perioperative antimicrobial prophylaxis (21/22, 95%) and postoperative renal-sparing immunosuppression protocol for all (18/22, 82%) were recommended.

CONCLUSIONS: These consensus recommendations provide criteria outlining indications, contraindications and timing for LT and LPT as well as CF-specific transplant considerations in Australia and New Zealand. They are intended to be paired with published guidelines to reduce practice variability and improve care.

articles.title: Rethinking chronic wound healing biomaterials toward integrated therapeutic platforms.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds such as diabetic ulcers and pressure sores are governed by a self-perpetuating pathological cycle of persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, bacterial infection and biofilm formation, and impaired angiogenesis. Conventional dressings, designed mainly for physical protection and exudate management, cannot sense or respond to this evolving microenvironment, and single-function biomaterials address only isolated aspects of the problem. Wound care is now moving toward platforms that couple real-time sensing of pH, reactive oxygen species, and inflammatory biomarkers with spatiotemporally controlled antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and regenerative activity. This perspective examines this shift through three converging classes of multifunctional biomaterials: theranostic systems that pair diagnosis with therapy, theragenerative systems that combine antimicrobial or anti-inflammatory action with tissue regeneration, and regenostic systems that adjust regenerative output to real-time physiological feedback. We discuss representative material designs for each class and argue that their convergence into a single total platform, capable of continuous monitoring, on-demand intervention and layer-specific tissue regeneration, marks the next stage of wound care. We also consider key barriers to clinical translation, including mechanical robustness under strain, long-term sensor stability, scalable fabrication, and the regulatory complexity of devices that function simultaneously as biomaterials, electronics, and drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The left atrial stiffness index (LASI), calculated as mitral E/e' divided by LA reservoir strain, reflects atrial myopathy and elevated filling pressure but has been studied mainly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We examined whether LASI predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and adds to established risk factors, across HF phenotypes in acute heart failure (AHF).

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 3,133 patients with AHF from the multicenter STRATS-AHF registry, classified by LVEF into HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF. During a median follow-up of 32.5 months, 616 (19.7%) had HF admissions, and 1,281 (40.9%) died. After adjustment, each doubling of LASI was associated with mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.19), as was LASI above the exploratory cutoff of 1.0 (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46). The association was similar across phenotypes (P for interaction = 0.65) and extended to HF hospitalization and the composite of death or HF hospitalization. LASI added modestly to established predictors; after adjustment for NT-proBNP, its association was not significant in patients with a measured value (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97-1.10) but persisted after multiple imputation in the whole cohort (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.15).

CONCLUSION: In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

articles.title: Dual Pathway Modulation with SGLT2 Inhibitors and Aldosterone Synthase Inhibitors in Cardio-Kidney Disease: Rationale and Trial Design of the EASi Program.
articles.abstract: Cardio-kidney diseases share interconnected pathophysiology where renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) overactivation drives pathologic hemodynamic, neurohormonal, inflammatory, and fibrotic changes leading to progressive cardiac and kidney dysfunction. Current RAAS-modulating therapies are limited by residual RAAS risk and aldosterone breakthrough despite angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy, incomplete blockade of aldosterone with mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) antagonists, hyperkalemia, and suboptimal implementation. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors (ASi) act upstream of the MR to lower aldosterone production, modulating both MR-dependent and MR-independent aldosterone effects without competing for receptor occupancy. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) reduce adverse cardiovascular and kidney events through cellular, hemodynamic and metabolic effects. The complementary mechanisms of SGLT2i/ASi (SASi) may provide improved cardio-kidney protection. The EASi program will determine whether SASi therapy, added to background guideline-directed therapy including an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI as appropriate, can improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes beyond SGLT2 inhibitor monotherapy. EASi-PROTKT (∼11,800 participants) evaluates prevention of incident heart failure events or cardiovascular death in patients with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and established cardiovascular disease. EASi-HF Preserved (∼6,000) and EASi-HF Reduced (∼4,200) evaluate cardiovascular death and first heart failure events across the LVEF spectrum. EASi-KIDNEY (∼11,000) evaluates kidney disease progression and cardiovascular endpoints in chronic kidney disease patients with and without type 2 diabetes. EASi-SYNC (∼500) is a Phase 2 trial comparing SASi versus staggered initiation of SGLT2i and ASi in patients with CKD. Together, these trials will enroll >33,000 participants and test whether SASi can redefine standard of care across the cardio-kidney disease spectrum.

articles.title: Home Infusion Short Course Remdesivir for Solid Organ Transplant Patients With COVID-19.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Solid organ transplant recipients (SOTR) are at high risk for severe COVID-19. The preferred oral antiviral, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, has significant drug-drug interactions, while remdesivir is only available intravenously (IV). In this study, we examined the feasibility, outcomes, and cost of short-course remdesivir home infusion for SOTR with COVID-19.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective chart review at a tertiary, urban academic center. We evaluated SOTR diagnosed with COVID-19 who were referred to receive home remdesivir from December 2022 to May 2024. The patients included in the study would have otherwise been admitted for inpatient infusion of IV remdesivir. Analyses included descriptive statistics of study participants' demographics and outcomes. Costs of average hospital length of stay in Washington DC, were compared to those of home infusion.

RESULTS: The study included 144 SOTR patients. The median age was 58 years, with a median duration of 3 days of COVID symptoms prior to administration of therapy. A total of 110 patients received IV remdesivir at home. Hospitalization occurred in 2.73% of patients treated with remdesivir, all for non-COVID-related reasons. The average cost of home administration for 3 days was $4279, compared to 3 days of hospitalization in DC ($12 204), with an estimated avoided inpatient administration cost of $871 750.

CONCLUSION: SOTR patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 who received home infusion remdesivir had low hospitalization and mortality rates. Most patients tolerated home IV therapy with minimal adverse events. Home infusion of remdesivir is an innovative delivery method and may reduce the cost of healthcare.

articles.title: Timing of Total Hip Arthroplasty and Lumbar Spinal Fusion in Patients With Hip and Spine Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Background ContextHip-spine syndrome involves concurrent hip and lumbar spine degeneration, often leading to overlapping symptoms that complicate management. The optimal surgical sequence between lumbar spine fusion (LSF) and total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains unclear.PurposeTo evaluate the existing literature comparing surgical sequencing strategies and determine whether THA or LSF should be performed first in patients with hip-spine syndrome.Study Design/SettingSystematic review and meta-analysis were conducted per PRISMA 2020 guidelines.MethodsPubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched to gather studies directly comparing the surgical sequencing of THA and LSF in patients with hip-spine syndrome who have undergone both procedures. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool. Where appropriate, risk ratios were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals.ResultsAfter screening 971 records, 19 studies were included. Five studies contributed to the principal dislocation synthesis, which showed no statistically significant association with surgical sequence (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.48-1.72; P = .692; I2 = 11.6%). Replacing Welling with Bala shifted the estimate towards higher risk after LSF-first sequencing (RR 2.21, 95% CI 0.98-5.00), but the confidence interval included no association. Several large cohorts outside the principal synthesis reported higher dislocation risk following spine-first surgery. Evidence for infection, loosening, revision and functional outcomes was limited by differences in populations, definitions and follow-up.ConclusionsThe evidence does not establish a preferred surgical sequence for THA and LSF. The periprosthetic fracture association derives from a single administrative cohort (Bala et al) and may reflect differences in bone quality, osteoporosis, frailty, or coding inaccuracies. Unequal post-THA observation periods in this cohort also limit interpretation of the fracture findings and dislocation sensitivity analysis. Heterogeneous fusion constructs, inconsistently reported sacral or pelvic involvement, and residual confounding further limit certainty. Surgical sequencing should remain individualized pending higher-quality evidence.

articles.title: Quantum dot-based nanotherapeutics for advanced wound healing: mechanisms, challenges, and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a biological process involving cellular and molecular events that restore tissue integrity and function. Conventional wound management strategies face limitations such as infection, delayed healing, prolonged inflammation, oxidative stress, and inadequate tissue regeneration, particularly in chronic and drug-resistant wounds. Quantum dots (QDs) have emerged as nanotherapeutic platforms owing to their tunable optical, electronic properties, antimicrobial activity and enabling drug delivery. A literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published from 2004 to 2026, using keywords related to quantum dots, nanotherapeutics, wound healing, tissue regeneration, signaling pathways, and theranostic applications. This review discusses carbon quantum dots (CQDs), graphene quantum dots (GQDs), zinc oxide quantum dots (ZnO QDs), silver quantum dots (Ag QDs), cadmium-based QDs, and doped or hybrid QDs, with emphasis on functions. QDs demonstrate antibacterial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, pro-angiogenic, and regenerative activities through modulation of PI3K/Akt, MAPK/ERK, TGF-β/Smad, NF-κB, Nrf2/Keap1, HIF-1α/VEGF, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Their incorporation into hydrogels, nanofibres, microneedles, and polymeric scaffolds enables controlled delivery, photodynamic or photothermal antibacterial activity, and fluorescence-based wound monitoring. Overall, QD-based nanotherapeutics represent a multifunctional approach to wound management, but safety evaluation and translational studies are required to establish clinical applicability.

articles.title: Impact of a sepsis clinical decision support system and workflow on sepsis-associated mortality or hospice discharge: A multihospital quasi-experimental study from 2018 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical decision support (CDS) tools may enhance sepsis care delivery by streamlining recognition, reducing workflow-related delays, and facilitating timely treatment initiation.

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the impact of the sepsis navigation tool (SNT), a CDS-driven quality improvement initiative, on all-cause in-hospital mortality or hospice discharge and adherence to key sepsis care processes.

METHODS: This retrospective, quasi-experimental study utilized electronic health record data from 631,620 adult acute care hospitalizations discharged from 10 hospitals within a large health system between 2018 and 2024. The SNT provided an optimized interface displaying sepsis metrics, a real-time sepsis timer, and shortcuts to sepsis documentation and order sets. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, piecewise linear regression models, and multivariable logistic regression models.

RESULTS: Sepsis was present in 50,911 (8.1%) hospitalizations. Following SNT implementation, mortality/hospice rates declined among sepsis (18.8%-16.3%; p < .001) and septic shock (40.0%-36.4%; p < .001) hospitalizations. Monthly mortality/hospice trends improved among sepsis hospitalizations (adjusted slope difference: 0.217%; p < .001) but not non-sepsis hospitalizations (adjusted slope difference: 0.014%; p = .207). Compared with pre-intervention, the post-intervention period had lower odds of mortality/hospice for sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.69-0.77) and septic shock (aOR=0.73; 95% CI = 0.68-0.79) hospitalizations, respectively. Intensive care unit admission rates, order set utilization, hospital length of stay, blood culture collection timing, and antibiotic administration timing also improved in sepsis hospitalizations.

CONCLUSIONS: This multihospital study demonstrated improvements in sepsis outcomes and care process measures following SNT implementation. Continued evaluation and optimization of sepsis CDS and artificial intelligence tools will be critical to further improving sepsis care.

articles.title: Global reporting of Brugada syndrome in VigiBase®: A disproportionality analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brugada syndrome (BrS) represents a rare but potentially malignant cardiac channelopathy, which may be precipitated by drugs, although data mainly derive from case reports/series.

OBJECTIVE: To describe the global reporting of BrS with drugs, including co-occurrence patterns, and identify novel potential associations.

METHODS: We used VigiBase® to perform descriptive and disproportionality analyses. The reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian information component (IC) with relevant 95% confidence/credibility intervals (95% CI) were used as disproportionality measures to identify signals of disproportionate reporting (SDR). We performed a network analysis to assess the co-occurrence patterns of related medications based on Jaccard similarity.

RESULTS: We included 544 deduplicated cases of BrS (94.7% serious events, 30.9% females, median time to onset of 30 days, 40.8% physician-reported, 63% from North America), with bupropion (n = 50), nortriptyline (n = 40) and flecainide (n = 34) as most frequently reported suspected drugs. Among 39 drugs with at least four reports, 32 emerged with an SDR, of which 17 were not listed in the BrS website (http://www.brugadadrugs.org), such as clozapine and loperamide (often overdosed). The co-occurrence network included 17 medications, regardless of the labelled role (suspected, interacting or concomitant), with a total of 12 potential co-occurrences; fentanyl exhibited the highest closeness centrality (1.0), whereas the strongest co-occurrence was reported between bupropion and nortriptyline (Jaccard similarity of 0.31).

CONCLUSIONS: Notwithstanding limitations related to pharmacovigilance and the complex BrS pathophysiology, we identified 32 medications with over-reporting of BrS, including 17 drugs not listed in the BrS website as well as clusters in affective disorders and anaesthesia.

articles.title: Exogenous β-glucan activates systemic acquired resistance (SAR) conferring dual resistance to SRBSDV and Sogatella furcifera in rice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rice is one of the most important staple crops, feeding more than half of the global population. Southern rice black-streaked dwarf virus (SRBSDV), which is persistently transmitted by the white-backed planthopper (WBPH, Sogatella furcifera), poses a serious threat to rice production. β-Glucan is a potent plant immune elicitor that induces systemic acquired resistance (SAR). However, the specific signaling pathways through which exogenous β-glucan regulates rice resistance against SRBSDV infection and WBPH infestation remains unclear.

RESULTS: Exogenous β-glucan enhanced photosynthetic capacity and antioxidant defense in healthy rice plants, and reduced the SRBSDV transmission rate and transmission load by WBPH. In SRBSDV-infected rice, β-glucan reduced SRBSDV accumulation and alleviated physiological damage. Exogenous β-glucan promoted mixed-linkage β-glucan (MLG) production and induced cell-wall remodeling by up-regulating OsCslF6, manifested as increased lignin content, thickened sclerenchyma cell walls, and a broadened mechanical-tissue zone. These were accompanied by immune modulation including up-regulated expression of callose-biosynthesis-related genes as well as activation of the salicylic acid (SA) pathway and defense pathways. In vector-insect-related bioassays, β-glucan treatment altered the feeding behavior and virus acquisition amount of WBPH, inhibited its oviposition, and shortened its lifespan.

CONCLUSION: Exogenous β-glucan promote MLG production to induce physical reinforcement of cell walls, accompanied by activation of SA-mediated immune responses, thereby enhancing rice resistance against WBPH and SRBSDV. This study reveals a novel β-glucan-induced defense mechanism in rice and provides a promising biological control strategy for the sustainable management of planthopper-transmitted viral diseases. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Disparities by insurance type across pediatric readmission/emergency revisit measures: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: National quality programs do not address disparities in pediatric readmissions, though equity is a key domain of healthcare quality. Across 15 pediatric readmission and readmission/emergency revisit (henceforth "revisit") measures, we illustrated an approach to detecting disparities by insurance type and identified the proportion of hospitals meeting a standard for high performance.

METHODS: Cross-sectional study of 75 U.S. children's hospitals in the 2023 Pediatric Inpatient Essentials administrative database. We characterized differences in readmission/revisit rates between Medicaid- and commercially insured patients across 15 all-condition and condition-specific measures. We defined disparities at the population- (aggregate sample) and hospital-level, as an absolute rate difference (ARD) <-1% between commercially- and Medicaid-insured visits. We defined hospital-level high performance as: (a) high quality (i.e., lower/better than population median); and (b) low disparities, (i.e., ARD < measure-specific cutoff).

RESULTS: At the population-level, overall readmission rates ranged between 3.1% (30-day asthma readmissions) to 14.8% (30-day all-condition revisits). For 14/15 measures, rates were higher (worse) for patients with Medicaid compared to commercial insurance. Five candidate disparities measures met our definition for population- and hospital-level disparities: (1) adjusted 30-day readmissions, (2) 14-day revisits, (3) 30-day revisits, (4) 30-day pneumonia readmissions, and (5) 30-day diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) readmissions. DKA had the highest hospital-level disparities (median hospital-level ARD: 3.5%). The 14-day revisit measure had the highest proportion of high-performing hospitals (10/54).

CONCLUSIONS: Medicaid-insured children had substantially higher readmission/revisit rates than commercially insured children across multiple measures. All-condition measures and the DKA readmission measure are potentially high-yield targets for disparities-focused quality improvement efforts.

articles.title: Surgical Treatment of Superior Mesenteric Arteriovenous Fistula after an Unsuccessful Endovascular Approach: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: A superior mesenteric arteriovenous fistula (SMAVF) is an uncommon connection between the superior mesenteric artery and vein, usually secondary to surgery or trauma. Manifestations range from abdominal pain to portal hypertension. Although endovascular management is often preferred, surgery may be required in complex cases. We report the case of a 40-year-old male with a history of two laparotomies who presented with an acute abdomen. Computed tomography revealed aneurysmal venous dilation, and arteriography confirmed an SMAVF. After an unsuccessful attempt at endovascular coil embolization due to the high-flow shunt, the fistula was successfully closed by surgical ligation. Open surgery remains a definitive and effective option when an endovascular approach is unsuccessful, unavailable, or unsuitable.

articles.title: LYN restricts the replication of influenza A virus through mediating autophagic degradation of viral nucleoprotein.
articles.abstract: The continuous evolution of influenza A virus (IAV) necessitates the exploration of host-based antiviral strategies. Our previously published study demonstrated that the tyrosine kinase LYN (LYN proto-oncogene, Src family tyrosine kinase) is a novel anti-influenza factor through directly phosphorylating the IAV nucleoprotein (NP). However, more potential antiviral functions of LYN remained unclear. Here, we reveal a kinase activity-independent mechanism by which LYN restricted IAV replication. LYN functioned as a scaffold, recruiting the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM28 (tripartite motif containing 28) to catalyze K48-linked ubiquitination of IAV-NP at lysine 470. The ubiquitination of NP enhanced the interaction with selective autophagy receptor NBR1 (NBR1 autophagy cargo receptor), leading to NP degradation via the macroautophagy/autophagy pathway. The NPK470R mutation abrogated the LYN-mediated degradation of NP and significantly promoted IAV replication. Collectively, our findings uncovered that LYN employs a two-pronged strategy to suppress IAV infection and is a promising target for anti-influenza drug development.Abbreviation: 3-MA: 3-methyladenine; ACTB: actin beta; ANOVA: analysis of variance; ATG7: autophagy related 7; CALCOCO2/NDP52: calcium binding and coiled-coil domain 2; CHX: cycloheximide; co-IP: co-immunoprecipitation; DUb: deubiquitinase; E3: E3 ubiquitin ligase; EID50: 50% egg infective dose; GFP: green fluorescent protein; GST: glutathione S-transferase; HA: hemagglutinin; HECTD1: HECT domain E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1; HERC2: HECT and RLD domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 2; HIV-1: human immunodeficiency virus type 1; HRP: horseradish peroxidase; HUWE1: HECT, UBA and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1; IAV: influenza A virus; IgG: immunoglobulin G; LYN: LYN proto-oncogene, Src family tyrosine kinase; MOI: multiplicity of infection; NBR1: NBR1 autophagy cargo receptor; NEDD4L: NEDD4 like E3 ubiquitin protein ligase; NP: nucleoprotein; NP-40: Nonidet P-40; OPTN: optineurin; PA: polymerase acidic protein; PB1: polymerase basic 1; PB2: polymerase basic 2; PBS: phosphate-buffered saline; RIPK3: receptor interacting serine/threonine kinase 3; RNF40: ring finger protein 40; SD: standard deviation; SQSTM1/p62: sequestosome 1; STUB1: STIP1 homology and U-box containing protein 1; TNF: tumor necrosis factor; TOLLIP: toll interacting protein; TRIM27: tripartite motif containing 27; TRIM28: tripartite motif containing 28; Ub: ubiquitin; UBE3C: ubiquitin protein ligase E3C; Vec: empty vector; vRNP: viral ribonucleoprotein; XIAP: X-linked inhibitor of apoptosis; ZNF598: zinc finger protein 598.

articles.title: Reduced papillary muscle uptake on stress 13N-ammonia PET is associated with higher myocardial flow reserve and may reflect relative tracer distribution.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Reduced papillary muscle tracer uptake on stress 13N-ammonia myocardial perfusion PET is common, but its physiological basis remains unclear. We investigated the association between papillary muscle uptake patterns and quantitative myocardial perfusion parameters.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 63 patients with known or suspected ischemic heart disease (mean age: 74 ± 10 years; 45 men) who underwent rest-stress 13N-ammonia PET. Patients were classified into fixed and reduced papillary muscle uptake groups by visual assessment. Global, remote, and papillary muscle-adjacent myocardial blood flow (MBF) and myocardial flow reserve (MFR) were compared between the groups. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between reduced papillary muscle uptake and remote MFR after adjustment for left ventricular (LV) geometry and function.

RESULTS: Reduced papillary muscle uptake was associated with higher global and remote MFR and higher remote stress MBF. Remote MFR showed the most pronounced group difference (2.00 ± 0.34 vs. 1.71 ± 0.57; P < 0.001). Papillary muscle-adjacent stress MBF and MFR were significantly higher in the reduced papillary muscle uptake group. In multivariable analyses, the association between higher remote MFR and reduced papillary muscle uptake remained positive after separate adjustment for left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume, and left ventricular ejection fraction and remained significant after adjustment for LVEDV.

CONCLUSION: Reduced papillary muscle uptake during stress on 13N-ammonia PET was associated with higher remote and papillary muscle-adjacent MFR. These findings support relative tracer distribution during hyperemia as a plausible explanation, and LV geometry and function may also contribute.

articles.title: Meeting Report: Interoperability of Diabetes Device Data into the Electronic Health Record.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract: Diabetes Technology Society hosted the Interoperability of Diabetes Device Data into the Electronic Health Record (EHR) meeting on June 4 to 5, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. Meeting topics included (1) the importance of interoperability of diabetes devices, (2) security and privacy for diabetes devices and enterprise information systems, (3) computerized insulin delivery in the hospital, (4) current and emerging wearable devices for diabetes, (5) the benefits of a diabetes management platform from pediatric endocrinologist, adult endocrinologist, and educator/practice management perspectives, (6) billing for remote continuous glucose monitor data interpretation, (7) a clinician panel discussion on the advantages and disadvantages of current EHR interoperability, and (8) the future of interoperability.

articles.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in the Global Lung Cancer Burden from GLOBOCAN 2024: Early- versus Late-Onset Cumulative Risks by Sex, Health-System Gradients, and Earlier Temporal Trends Across 186 Countries.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of global cancer mortality, with marked variation across levels of human development. Whether socioeconomic and health system associations differ between early-onset and late-onset disease remains unclear.

AIMS: To quantify socioeconomic inequalities in the cumulative risks of lung cancer incidence and mortality for early-onset (< 50 years) and late-onset (≥ 50 years) disease by sex; assess whether differences in longevity are associated with late-onset human development index (HDI) gradients; and examine associations with universal health coverage (UHC) and temporal trends in countries with available registry or vital statistics series.

STUDY DESIGN: Ecological analysis of cross-sectional Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 estimates from 186 countries and earlier temporal series from Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Plus (CI5plus; incidence, 2003-2017) and the WHO Mortality Database (mortality, 2003-2019).

METHODS: We used GLOBOCAN 2024 estimates to derive early- and late-onset cumulative risks by sex, with late-onset risks conditional on survival to age 50. Socioeconomic inequalities were summarized using the slope index of inequality (SII) and concentration index. We compared observed late-onset risks with regression-based counterfactuals that held remaining life expectancy at age 50 (e50) constant, performed an additive Oaxaca-Kitagawa decomposition of country-mean HDI contrasts, and examined correlations between outcomes and the UHC service coverage index. Temporal trends were estimated as annual percent changes (APCs) using single log-linear models of CI5plus incidence data (2003-2017) and WHO Mortality Database series (2003-2019).

RESULTS: Late-onset cumulative incidence far exceeded early-onset incidence (males, 5.18% vs. 0.13%; females, 3.12% vs. 0.13%). HDI associations were stronger for late-onset than early-onset incidence (males, ρ = 0.81 vs. 0.48; females, ρ = 0.80 vs. 0.60). The male SII for incidence was 7.17 for late-onset disease versus 0.11 for early-onset disease. The sex gap widened with HDI, mainly after age 50. In comparisons of country means between very high and low HDI groups, rate-related endowments exceeded e50 endowments under all reference coefficient choices examined. Higher UHC scores were associated with lower mortality-to-incidence ratios and higher cumulative risks, particularly for late-onset disease. In the monitored series for 2003-2017 (incidence) and 2003-2019 (mortality), late-onset female rates more often increased (median APCs, +2.11% and +1.37%, respectively), whereas early-onset rates and late-onset male rates more often declined.

CONCLUSION: Socioeconomic inequalities in lung cancer cumulative risk were steeper for late-onset than early-onset disease, particularly on absolute scales, and sex gaps were largest after midlife. Relative inequality measures showed a smaller contrast between early- and late-onset disease. In descriptive comparisons across HDI groups, rate-related differences exceeded longevity-related differences under all reference coefficient choices examined. During 2003-2017 (incidence) and 2003-2019 (mortality), increases were observed most consistently among females with late-onset disease. Global descriptions of lung cancer burden should distinguish by age at onset and sex.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of silver nitrate application versus marsupialization for bartholin gland cysts and abscesses: A multicenter retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare 6 month recurrence and selected clinical outcomes after marsupialization and silver nitrate application in women treated for symptomatic Bartholin gland cysts or abscesses.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included women treated between September 2022 and September 2025. Only patients with complete 6 month follow-up data were included in the final analysis. The primary outcome was recurrence of cyst or abscess within 6 months. Secondary outcomes included procedure duration, anesthesia type, early postoperative findings, return to daily activity, epithelial healing time, visible scar formation, dyspareunia among sexually active women, persistent or recurrent vulvar pain, need for repeat intervention, late secondary infection, and readmission. Recurrence was additionally evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing and univariable Cox regression, and multivariable logistic regression was used for recurrence and visible scar formation.

RESULTS: Three hundred forty-two patients were analyzed, including 189 in the marsupialization group and 153 in the silver nitrate group. Recurrence within 6 months occurred in 29/189 patients (15.3%) after marsupialization and 19/153 patients (12.4%) after silver nitrate application, with no statistically significant difference [relative risk (RR) 0.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.47-1.39; p=0.439]. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant difference in 6 month recurrence-free survival (84.7% vs. 87.6%; log-rank p=0.426; hazard ratio 0.79, 95% CI 0.44-1.41), and the adjusted treatment effect remained non-significant [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.81, 95% CI 0.42-1.55; p=0.521]. Silver nitrate application was associated with shorter procedure duration (12.7±5.6 vs. 20.4±6.9 minutes; mean difference -7.70 minutes, 95% CI -9.03 to -6.37; p<0.001), a 1-day shorter median time to return to daily activity, and shorter epithelial healing time (15.3±5.9 vs. 17.2±6.2 days; mean difference -1.90 days, 95% CI -3.19 to -0.61; p=0.004). Visible scar formation was less frequently documented after silver nitrate application (8.5% vs. 17.5%; RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.27-0.89; p=0.016) and remained lower after adjustment (aOR 0.43, 95% CI 0.22-0.86; p=0.017), although this secondary finding was exploratory. Chemical mucosal irritation or superficial burn occurred only in the silver nitrate group (10/153, 6.5%; 95% CI 3.2-11.7). Dyspareunia, persistent vulvar pain, repeat intervention, late infection, and readmission showed no statistically significant between-group differences.

CONCLUSION: Silver nitrate application and marsupialization showed no statistically significant difference in 6 month recurrence. Silver nitrate was associated with shorter procedure duration and modestly shorter recovery measures; the lower documented scar rate should be interpreted as exploratory, but local chemical irritation remains a relevant limitation.

articles.title: Adalimumab associated subacute thyroiditis in a patient with ankylosing spondylitis: A rare clinical entity.
articles.journal: The International journal of risk & safety in medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundSubacute thyroiditis is a self-limiting granulomatous inflammatory disorder, most commonly precipitated by viral infection. Thyroiditis associated with adalimumab (Tumor necrosis factor alpha inhibitor) is rare, with limited case reports to date.Case ReportOur case describes a 40-year-old man with long-standing ankylosing spondylitis on adalimumab for 7 years, who presented with a month-long history of intermittent fever, neck pain and markedly elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate). Biochemical thyrotoxicosis with diffusely reduced technetium-99m pertechnetate uptake on thyroid scan supported the diagnosis of subacute thyroiditis. An extensive evaluation excluded infectious and other autoimmune etiologies. Adalimumab therapy was suspected to be the likely precipitating factor. Prompt withdrawal of adalimumab and initiation of systemic corticosteroid therapy resulted in rapid clinical and biochemical resolution. The Naranjo adverse drug reaction probability score of 7 further supported a probable causal association.ConclusionThis case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for possibilities of biologic associated thyroiditis in patients receiving TNF-α inhibitors and presenting with fever of unknown origin.

articles.title: [Endoscopic ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors].
articles.abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (EUS-RFA) is an emerging minimally invasive treatment for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, particularly insulinomas. Traditionally, insulinomas are managed surgically, often requiring major pancreatic resections associated with significant morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and the risk of long-term complications including pancreatic insufficiency and diabetes. We report the initial clinical experience with EUS-RFA at a tertiary center in Sweden, including three patients with symptomatic insulinomas. All patients underwent successful EUS-RFA with short procedure times, minimal postoperative care and no major complications. Hypoglycemic symptoms resolved in all cases, and follow-up imaging showed no residual tumor activity. These findings align with emerging international data suggesting that EUS-RFA is a safe and effective alternative to surgery for selected patients with low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. The technique may reduce the need for extensive surgery and the associated healthcare burden, while improving patient quality of life. Although further prospective and randomized studies are needed to establish long-term outcomes and optimal patient selection, EUS-RFA has the potential to represent a paradigm shift in the management of insulinomas and other selected pancreatic lesions.

articles.title: Beyond Depression - The Moderating Roles of Somatic Symptoms and Interpersonal Difficulties in Adolescent Suicidal Ideation.
articles.abstract: Background: Depression is a central risk factor for adolescent suicidal ideation (SI), yet depressive symptoms alone do not fully explain why some adolescents develop suicidal thoughts. Somatic symptoms and interpersonal difficulties may mark forms of distress that heighten vulnerability to SI. Aims: This study examined whether somatization and interpersonal difficulties are associated with adolescent SI beyond depression, and whether they moderate the association between depression and SI. Method: Data were drawn from 8,052 adolescents attending vocational high schools in Israel. Participants completed adapted Brief Symptom Inventory subscales assessing depression, somatization, and interpersonal difficulties, along with selected Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale items assessing SI. Alcohol use, drug use, and truancy were also assessed. Analyses included descriptive statistics, hierarchical logistic regression, and moderation models using Hayes' PROCESS macro. Results: Overall, 9.7% of adolescents endorsed SI. Depression was the strongest predictor of SI, while somatization and interpersonal difficulties also made independent contributions after accounting for demographic and behavioral risk factors. Separate moderation models showed that both somatization and interpersonal difficulties strengthened the association between depression and SI, with the depression-SI link becoming stronger at higher levels of each moderator. In the full simultaneous regression model, these effects showed a more complex pattern, suggesting that moderation should be interpreted in relation to the analytic model. Limitations: The cross-sectional design, self-report measures, gender imbalance, adapted BSI subscales, selected C-SSRS items, and lack of direct trauma-related measures should be considered. Conclusion: Findings suggest that adolescent SI is shaped not only by depressive symptoms but also by somatic and interpersonal expressions of distress. School-based assessment may benefit from attending to somatic complaints and relational difficulties alongside depression.

articles.title: Structural insights into three key platelet receptors for the discovery and development of anti-thrombotic therapies: PAR-1, αIIbβ3, and GPVI.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide and is strongly driven by thrombosis, which underlies events including stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and deep vein thrombosis. Platelets are anucleate cell fragments produced by megakaryocytes that are essential for haemostasis but also make major contributions to pathological thrombosis. Although platelet receptors are major targets for antithrombotic therapy, current agents remain limited by bleeding risk, and no new antiplatelet drug has been approved since Cangrelor in 2015. The present review focuses on three structurally and mechanistically distinct platelet receptors with major relevance to drug discovery: PAR1, integrin αIIbβ3, and glycoprotein VI. These receptors represent key nodes spanning the G protein-coupled receptor, integrin, and immunoglobulin superfamily classes, and recent structural studies have clarified their activation mechanisms and drug-binding modes. I highlight how these insights have informed current inhibitors and are guiding the development of safer next-generation antithrombotic therapies. Finally, advancements in studying protein structure and their future impacts on drug design and optimisation are discussed.

articles.journal: The Korean journal of internal medicine

articles.title: 2026 Consensus on the Management of Cushing's Disease: A Collaborative Statement from the Korean Endocrine Society and Japan Endocrine Society.
authors: Committee of Clinical Practice Guidelines of Korean Endocrine Society
Korean Neuroendocrine Study Group of Korean Endocrine Society
articles.abstract: The primary treatment goal of Cushing's disease (CD) is sustained normalization of hypercortisolism as well as relief of tumor mass effects, to reduce morbidity and mortality and improve long-term quality of life. Korea and Japan share broadly similar therapeutic principles for CD; however, real-world management differs because of country-specific healthcare systems, regulatory environments, and medication availability. Building on the previously published Korean Endocrine Society (KES)-Japan Endocrine Society (JES) diagnostic consensus, a joint multidisciplinary working group developed an expert consensus focused on the treatment and management of CD. Surgical intervention for pituitary tumors, primarily via a transsphenoidal approach, remains the first-line treatment when feasible. Subsequent treatment should be individualized according to disease and tumor characteristics, severity of hypercortisolism, associated comorbidities, and regional availability of therapeutic options. Medical treatment is recommended for patients with persistent or recurrent disease after surgery, for those who are not candidates for surgery or who decline surgical intervention, and as bridging therapy in severe cases requiring urgent control of hypercortisolemia or when definitive treatment is delayed. Pituitary tumor-directed agents and adrenal steroidogenesis inhibitors constitute key pharmacologic options, but the available agents and reimbursement status differ between Korea and Japan. Radiation therapy is considered when surgery is not feasible or when control is not achieved with surgery and/or medical therapy, and bilateral adrenalectomy may be reserved for highly selected refractory cases. This consensus statement provides harmonized, practice-oriented recommendations while acknowledging current evidence gaps and the need for further collaborative research to inform CD management in East Asian populations.

articles.title: Extreme Hypereosinophilia Revealing Disseminated Strongyloidiasis in a Critically Ill Patient.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Extreme hypereosinophilia is an uncommon but clinically important laboratory finding that may indicate serious underlying disease. In tropical regions, parasitic infections, particularly Strongyloides stercoralis, should be considered. However, the diagnosis may be overlooked in critically ill patients with multiple concurrent infections. Because disseminated strongyloidiasis carries high mortality when diagnosis is delayed, early recognition and empirical anti-helminthic therapy are essential in endemic settings. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old Vietnamese farmer was transferred after 18 days of treatment for bacterial meningitis, intraventricular hemorrhage, Corynebacterium striatum pneumonia, and Candida auris infection. She remained critically ill and required respiratory support through a tracheostomy. Laboratory testing showed marked leukocytosis with extreme hypereosinophilia, severe anemia, profound hypoalbuminemia, acute kidney injury, electrolyte disturbances, and severe systemic inflammation. Arterial blood gas analysis confirmed hypoxemic respiratory failure. Given the extreme eosinophilia and endemic setting, disseminated strongyloidiasis was suspected, and empirical oral ivermectin was started before diagnosis. Strongyloides-specific IgG serology was positive, and Strongyloides stercoralis larvae were identified in sputum, confirming the diagnosis. The absolute eosinophil count declined from >10 000 cells/µL to 450 cells/µL by the next day, 180 cells/µL by treatment day 3, and 140 cells/µL by day 5. Her systemic condition remained stable for approximately 2 weeks; however, she subsequently developed recurrent intracranial hemorrhage and died in hospital. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights that strongyloidiasis should be considered in patients with unexplained marked eosinophilia, even when severe bacterial or fungal infections dominate the clinical presentation. In endemic regions, early clinical suspicion and timely empirical anti-helminthic therapy may be crucial to prevent potentially fatal disseminated strongyloidiasis, particularly in malnourished and medically complex patients.

articles.title: Evaluation of Rehabilitation Outcomes Following Therapy With the Luna EMG Diagnostic and Rehabilitation Robot for the Upper Limb and Hand in Individuals in the Chronic Post-Stroke Phase.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND This study compared a rehabilitation program using Luna EMG biofeedback with conventional physiotherapy in patients in the chronic phase after stroke, focusing on hand motor function, upper limb proprioception, and functional ability. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 124 post-stroke patients aged 45-75 years were randomly assigned to a test group (n=63) or control group (n=61). Both groups completed a 3-week rehabilitation program. The control group received conventional physiotherapy, while the test group received Luna EMG biofeedback training for the same total therapy time. Outcomes included upper limb proprioception, Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), Barthel Index, Box and Blocks Test, and Frenchay scale. RESULTS Both groups showed significant post-intervention improvements (P<0.001). Compared with controls, the test group demonstrated significantly greater improvements in upper limb proprioception, FMA-UE scores, manual dexterity, and grip function (all padj<0.001; rrb=0.40-0.89). The between-group difference in Barthel Index scores was not significant after Bonferroni correction (padj=0.138), although the test group showed slightly greater improvement. CONCLUSIONS Adding Luna EMG-based biofeedback to conventional rehabilitation may provide short-term benefits in upper limb proprioception, motor function, manual dexterity, and grip function after stroke. Further studies are needed to determine long-term effects and clinically meaningful changes.

articles.title: Elevated blood pressure is independently associated with atherosclerosis in asymptomatic, low-risk individuals.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: In 2024 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines, treatment recommendations for elevated blood pressure (BP) are based primarily on SCORE2 estimated cardiovascular risk. Screening for silent atherosclerosis is recommended (class IIb) to guide treatment decisions only in individuals with an intermediate SCORE2 (5-<10%). Those with SCORE2 < 5% are not recommended for pharmacological intervention. Whether elevated BP is associated with silent atherosclerosis (a known independent predictor of mortality) in low-risk individuals (<5%) is unknown. This study aimed to evaluate atherosclerosis across BP categories in asymptomatic, low-risk individuals from the Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis (PESA) study.

METHODS AND RESULTS: PESA participants not receiving antihypertensive medications were included. Participants underwent screening of carotid and femoral atherosclerosis (3D vascular ultrasound), as well as coronary calcium scoring (CACS, by non-contrast CT) at enrollment and at 6 years follow-up. Office BP at enrollment was categorized according to the 2024 ESC guidelines as non-elevated (<120/70 mmHg), elevated (120-139/70-89 mmHg), and hypertension (≥140/90 mmHg). Global plaque volume (GPV) was defined as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden. Progression of plaque or CACS was calculated as the change between baseline and follow-up. A total of 3833 participants (45.5 ± 4.2 years, 61% male) were included. 1619 had non-elevated BP, 2041 had elevated BP, and 173 had hypertension.
