Mean SCORE2 was 2%, and 94% of the cohort had a SCORE2 < 5% (94% in those with elevated BP). Among individuals with elevated BP, 49% had peripheral atherosclerosis, and 22% had CAC. Compared with the non-elevated BP group, and after adjusting for age, sex, and other cardiovascular risk factors, elevated BP was significantly associated with higher prevalence of peripheral atherosclerosis, greater GPV, and greater atherosclerosis progression over 6 years. Similar associations were observed in the hypertension group. Within the elevated BP group, individuals at the lower end of the range (120-129/70-79 mmHg) had increased peripheral atherosclerosis but not CACS, while those at the higher end (130-139/80-89 mmHg) showed both higher prevalence of peripheral atherosclerosis and CACS.

CONCLUSION: In this low-risk, asymptomatic population, elevated BP was independently associated with greater atherosclerosis burden and progression. While peripheral atherosclerosis was higher across the entire spectrum of elevated BP, CACS was only significantly higher in individuals in the higher-end values of BP. Silent atherosclerosis determination provides complementary information to conventional risk assessment in individuals with elevated BP and a low SCORE2.

articles.title: Time to public reimbursement of new medical technologies in Australia and England: a systematic review.
articles.journal: International journal of technology assessment in health care
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to synthesize reported timelines to health technology assessment (HTA) recommendation and publicly funded reimbursement for new medical technologies in Australia and England and to identify reported determinants of delay.

METHODS: A qualitative systematic review was conducted according to a prespecified protocol. Embase, PubMed, and Scopus were searched for English-language studies published from 2015 onward, supplemented by targeted grey literature searches. Eligible studies reported extractable quantitative HTA or reimbursement timelines for new technologies (pharmaceuticals, devices, or diagnostics) funded in Australia or England. Reported time metrics were mapped to a time-event framework including registration, HTA, and publicly funded access milestones. Given substantial heterogeneity in end point definitions and reporting, synthesis was descriptive.

RESULTS: Nine studies met the inclusion criteria. All reported on pharmaceuticals and no eligible studies were identified for medical devices or diagnostics. Most studies reported timelines for England and focused on time from registration to final HTA outcome, whereas Australian evidence more clearly captured the interval between positive HTA recommendation and reimbursement. Reported time from registration to final HTA outcome ranged from 265 to 840 days depending on study scope. Reported time from registration to publicly funded access ranged from 310 to 679 days. Evidence on determinants of delay was sparse and inconsistently reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Reported timelines to HTA recommendation and public reimbursement are substantial and highly variable in Australia and England, but are measured inconsistently across the literature. Greater standardization in reporting, clearer distinction between HTA and reimbursement milestones, and dedicated research on device and diagnostic pathways are needed.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Exposure to War- and Terrorism-Themed Social Media Content and Secondary Traumatic Stress Among Nursing Students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social media brings war- and terrorism-related news, images, and videos into users' everyday lives, and some of this content can be distressing. Nursing students use social media frequently, yet little is known about the secondary traumatic stress symptoms they may experience in relation to such content.

AIMS: To examine nursing students' social media-related secondary traumatic stress scores and associated factors.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 212 nursing students at a private university in Istanbul, Türkiye, between December 2023 and June 2024. Data were collected using a 17-item Personal Information Form and the Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale for Social Media Users (STSS-SM). Descriptive statistics, t tests, one-way ANOVA, Spearman's correlation, and multiple linear regression were used (p<.05).

RESULTS: The mean STSS-SM score was 43.47±12.42. 62.3% of participants reported being emotionally or psychologically affected by war- and terrorism-related content. The multiple linear regression model was statistically significant, F(3, 208) =6.14, p<.001, and explained 8.1% of the variance in STSS-SM scores. Choosing nursing as a career at the family's request, reporting YouTube among the most frequently used platforms, and having previously been directly affected by war or terrorism were each independently associated with higher STSS-SM scores.

DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that war- and terrorism-related content encountered on social media may affect nursing students' psychological well-being. Nursing programs should therefore consider including digital media literacy in the curriculum and ensuring that students can access psychological support when needed.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes Associated With Routine Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients With Coronary Artery Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: The optimal strategy for managing concomitant coronary artery disease (CAD) in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. We performed an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative or deferred management in patients with CAD undergoing TAVI. Major electronic databases were systematically searched for eligible RCTs. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effects model, with sensitivity analyses performed to assess robustness and explore the influence of individual studies on heterogeneity. Three RCTs were included. Routine PCI was not associated with a significant reduction in mortality or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with conservative or deferred management. However, PCI was associated with significantly higher risks of major bleeding (RR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.06-2.33; P = 0.02) and any bleeding (RR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.27-2.48; P < 0.001), while urgent revascularization was less frequent with PCI. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that individual studies influenced heterogeneity for selected outcomes, although the overall findings remained broadly consistent. Among patients with CAD undergoing TAVI, this pooled analysis of the available randomized evidence shows that an unselective, routine strategy of PCI does not reduce mortality, myocardial infarction, or major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events compared with a conservative or deferred strategy, while increasing bleeding and reducing the subsequent need for urgent revascularization. Rather than indicating that coronary intervention is unnecessary, these findings clarify the precision and consistency of this tradeoff across the available trials and support a selective, individualized strategy in which PCI is reserved for clinically or physiologically significant coronary disease rather than performed routinely on the basis of angiographic appearance alone.

articles.title: The Role of Osteopontin in the Progression and Prognosis of Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD) have a high residual cardiovascular risk. Osteopontin (OPN) may be involved in CAD progression, but its prognostic value remains unclear. This meta-analysis appraised the association between circulating OPN and clinical outcomes in CAD. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were retrieved up to April 9, 2026. Cohort or cross-sectional studies were included. Random- or fixed-effects models were employed to pool hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed utilizing I2, and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis was performed. Nine prospective cohort studies (6955 CAD patients) were included. Elevated OPN levels were associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in continuous (HR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.06-1.43) and categorical analyses (HR = 1.54, 95% CI: 1.02-2.32), with substantial heterogeneity in both analyses. Continuous OPN was associated with all-cause mortality (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 1.02-1.08), while no association was observed for categorical OPN. High OPN increased risks of recurrent myocardial infarction (HR = 2.25, 95% CI: 1.44-3.51) and heart failure readmission (HR = 2.36, 95% CI: 1.65-3.39). OPN showed no significant association with cardiovascular mortality. Sensitivity analysis revealed limited stability of pooled major adverse cardiovascular events estimates for categorical OPN. In conclusion, circulating OPN may have potential value in predicting some adverse outcomes in CAD patients, and its predictive efficacy varies by outcome type and definitions of OPN. Given high heterogeneity and unstable estimates in some analyses, standardized prospective studies are needed to validate this finding.

articles.title: Prognostic Impact of Serum Magnesium Levels in Heart Failure: Updated Evidence From a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) carries high morbidity and mortality, and the prognostic role of serum magnesium remains unclear. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis assessed associations between magnesium abnormalities and outcomes in HF. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane were searched through March 2026 for observational cohorts, registries, and post hoc randomized controlled trial analyses in adults with HF. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were HF hospitalization and cardiovascular (CV) mortality. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool and the revised Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool for Randomized Trials. Twelve studies including 648,602 patients were analyzed. Hypermagnesemia was associated with higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.32-1.44; I2 = 6%), HF hospitalization (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51; I2 = 81%), and CV mortality (RR 1.41, 95% CI 1.19-1.66; I2 = 42%). Hypomagnesemia was associated with modestly higher all-cause mortality (RR 1.15, 95% CI 1.01-1.31; I2 = 70%), with no significant association with HF hospitalization or CV death. Associations were consistent across studies published before and after 2010 and between observational cohorts and post hoc trial analyses, with no significant subgroup differences. The association between hypermagnesemia and all-cause mortality was unchanged after excluding the largest study (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.25-1.53; I2 = 13%). Serum magnesium abnormalities, especially hypermagnesemia, are associated with worse outcomes in HF. Hypomagnesemia shows a smaller, less consistent association. Because hypermagnesemia may largely reflect renal dysfunction and greater disease severity, these findings represent prognostic associations rather than evidence of causality; prospective studies should determine whether monitoring or correcting magnesium abnormalities improves HF outcomes.

articles.title: Cruciate-retaining versus condylar-stabilized reconstruction strategies in robotic-arm assisted total knee arthroplasty: a prospective, double-blinded, randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Comparisons of posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) retention and sacrifice in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) derive almost entirely from manual instrumentation, in which soft-tissue balance was not quantified. We compared patient-reported outcomes after robotic-arm assisted TKA using PCL retention with a cruciate-retaining (CR) insert versus PCL sacrifice with a condylar-stabilized (CS) insert and design-specific balancing targets. Single-centre, double-blinded randomized controlled trial. 380 patients with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 osteoarthritis underwent image-based robotic-arm assisted TKA by a single surgeon using one implant system under functional alignment. Allocation was concealed until intraoperative PCL inspection; patients, the outcome assessor and the analyst were blinded to allocation. The primary outcome was the 2011 Knee Society Score (KSS) functional activity subscale at 12 months; secondary outcomes were the Oxford Knee Score (OKS), Forgotten Joint Score-12 (FJS-12), satisfaction and complications. The primary intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis used analysis of covariance with multiple imputation (1000 imputations) for 60 missing outcomes; per-protocol analysis was a sensitivity analysis. Differences were interpreted using minimal clinically important difference (MCID) benchmarks. 320 patients (160 per group) had observed follow-up; ITT included all 380 randomized patients. The adjusted CR - CS differences were 1.69 for KSS functional activity (95% confidence interval - 0.15 to 3.53, P = .071), 1.24 for OKS (95% CI 0.64 to 1.85, P < .001) and 0.82 for FJS-12 (95% CI - 0.02 to 1.65, P = .055). The primary difference was below the 4.1-point anchor-based benchmark, and its confidence interval included zero. Additional fixed flexion deformity adjustment produced a borderline KSS result. Satisfaction was concentrated at ratings 4-5; recorded per-protocol complication counts were equal. PCL retention produced small, numerically higher 12-month scores, with no clear KSS difference in the principal ITT model. The KSS inference was sensitive to additional covariate adjustment. Equivalence, equivalent safety and outcomes in an attenuated PCL were not established.Trial registration: Clinical Trials Registry - India, CTRI/2023/01/049128, registered.

articles.title: Correlation between retinal microvascular changes and pupillary autonomic function in early type 2 diabetes: a neurovascular perspective.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To simultaneously evaluate retinal microvascular integrity by optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A) and pupillary autonomic function by automated pupillometry in type 2 diabetes, and to quantify their correlations across early disease stages.

METHODS: This prospectively enrolled, single-centre, cross-sectional study included 105 participants: 35 non-diabetic controls, 35 diabetic patients without retinopathy (DM group), and 35 with mild-to-moderate non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR). All underwent Scheimpflug-based automated pupillometry (static and dynamic) and macular OCT-A (3 × 3 mm). Flow density parameters for the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexus (DCP), foveal avascular zone metrics, and foveal vessel density (FD-300) were extracted. Spearman correlations between OCT-A and pupillometry parameters were calculated across all 105 eyes, separately within each study group, and after adjustment for group membership.

RESULTS: All four dynamic pupillometry indices showed significant progressive reductions across groups (all p < 0.001), with significant differences between the DM and control groups and between the NPDR and DM groups. DCP parafoveal flow density was lower in the NPDR group than in controls (p = 0.007) and the DM group (p = 0.005); no OCT-A parameter differed significantly between the DM and control groups. DCP flow density correlated positively with maximum dilation velocity (r =  + 0.35, p = 0.001) and early re-dilation amplitude (r =  + 0.38, p < 0.001). These associations remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction and after adjustment for group membership, and were not detectable in the control group.

CONCLUSION: Dynamic pupillometry indices were altered in diabetes without retinopathy, whereas OCT-A differences were confined to NPDR. DCP flow density correlated modestly with pupillary re-dilation indices.

articles.title: Antimicrobial peptides are differentially regulated in blood and visceral adipose tissue in obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction and linked to NLRP3-related signaling.
articles.abstract: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation in which visceral adipose tissue (VAT) plays a central immunometabolic role. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) integrate host defense and inflammatory signaling, but their regulation across metabolic compartments in human obesity remains incompletely defined. We evaluated circulating AMP concentrations and gene expression levels in VAT and circulating leukocytes from 108 participants classified according to obesity and glycemic status. These analyses were complemented with mechanistic studies in human visceral adipocytes evaluating inflammatory and microbiota-related stimuli, effects of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)related modulation, and crosstalk with PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Obesity was associated with a selective circulating AMP profile characterized by higher cathelicidin, calprotectin, lipocalin-2 and neutrophil elastase together with lower α-defensin 6 and β-defensin 1. In VAT, obesity was accompanied by increased expression of several inflammatory AMP-related genes together with higher NLRP3 and NLRP6 expression and reduced DEFB1, with additional differences emerging across glycemic groups. Circulating leukocytes displayed a partially overlapping but distinct transcriptional profile, consistent with compartment-specific regulation rather than a generalized AMP response. In vitro, visceral adipocytes showed gene- and stimulus-dependent AMP responses to inflammatory and microbiota-related signals. NLRP3 silencing attenuated selected LPS-induced inflammatory and antimicrobial responses, whereas the glucose-lowering medication glibenclamide promoted complementary stimulus-dependent effects. Adipocyte-conditioned medium modified AMP expression in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Collectively, these findings identify a selective, compartment-dependent remodeling of antimicrobial pathways in obesity and obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, with NLRP3-related mechanisms emerging as a potential contributor to the regulation of selected antimicrobial responses in visceral adipocytes.

articles.title: Where do children fit in the Asian aplastic anemia consensus?
Changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year after kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract: Pre-transplant senescence biomarkers are associated with frailty in patients undergoing kidney transplantation (KT). We examined the relationship between changes in senescence biomarkers, frailty, and physical function during the first year post-KT. Plasma concentrations of senescence biomarkers, frailty (Physical Frailty Phenotype), and physical function (Short Physical Performance Battery) were simultaneously measured. Relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection operator methods were used to select variables for multivariable models. Among 188 participants, mean age was 53 ± 13 years, 62% were male, 34% had diabetes, and 30% underwent deceased donor KT. During the first year after KT, age ≥ 60 was associated with smaller reductions in GDF-15 and IL-8, whereas Black race was associated with greater reduction in RAGE. Alemtuzumab was associated with smaller reduction in IL-7 compared to other induction agents, whereas deceased donor KT was associated with greater reduction in PAI-1. On multivariable analysis, more improvement in frailty was significantly associated with reduction in uPAR concentrations (β - 0.23, 95% CI - 0.38 to - 0.08, p = 0.003). Changes in biomarker concentrations were not independently associated with changes in physical function. Whether interventions affecting the abundance or behavior of senescent cells may counter frailty in KT recipients warrants further exploration.

articles.title: Lower urinary tract events reported with GLP-1 receptor agonists: a disproportionality analysis of FAERS and Canada Vigilance.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Rapid weight loss with GLP-1 receptor agonists removes lean mass, and whether this weakens the pelvic floor and causes incontinence is under prospective study. We examined lower urinary tract event reporting and whether its patterns fit a pelvic floor or diabetic bladder explanation.

METHODS: Disproportionality analysis of FAERS with replication in Canada Vigilance, using diabetes and obesity drug comparators, adjusted reporting odds ratios (ROR), SGLT2 inhibitors as positive control and a sensitivity analysis without them, and exploratory analyses of indication, brand, dose, onset and co-reported terms.

RESULTS: The GLP-1 receptor agonist class was not disproportionately reported with lower urinary tract events in FAERS or Canada Vigilance (adjusted ROR 0.43 and 0.50). With SGLT2 inhibitor comparators, semaglutide was neutral for the composite (0.94, 95%CI 0.85-1.04), with an incontinence signal in women (1.44, 1.14-1.81). Without them, semaglutide and DPP-4 inhibitors showed excess reporting of several urinary outcomes, tirzepatide did not. Semaglutide incontinence was reported less often with obesity than diabetes use (OR 0.66, 0.34-1.28) and with Wegovy than Ozempic (0.64, 0.36-1.16), neither significant after correction, did not rise with dose, and was co-reported with urinary tract infection, other urinary symptoms and, in six reports, muscle weakness.

CONCLUSION: No class-level excess reporting was detected. Semaglutide findings depended on the comparator set, and DPP-4 inhibitors shared its incontinence signal without SGLT2 comparators. The pattern is compatible with diabetes-related urinary morbidity, but exploratory data cannot separate this from pelvic floor weakening, confounding or reporting artefacts.

articles.title: Higher Serum Dopamine is Associated with Higher CSF Aβ42/40, Lower Amyloid-PET Burden, and Better Cognitive Function Across the Alzheimer's Disease Spectrum.
articles.abstract: Dopaminergic dysfunction has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its relationship with amyloid pathology and cognitive impairment remains insufficiently understood. This study examined whether serum dopamine is associated with CSF amyloid-β 42/40 (Aβ42/40), amyloid-PET burden, and cognitive function across the clinical diagnostic groups in ADNI, and whether amyloid biomarkers show cross-sectional statistical indirect effects in the dopamine-cognition relationship. Cross-sectional data were obtained from ADNI, including 428 participants: cognitively normal (CN; n = 138), individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 206), and patients with AD dementia (n = 84). All analyses were performed with FDR correction to account for multiple comparisons. The results showed that serum dopamine decreased progressively from CN to MCI and AD dementia, whereas CSF Aβ42/40 decreased and amyloid-PET burden increased across diagnostic stages, accompanied by progressive worsening of cognitive function. In the pooled cohort and within MCI, higher serum dopamine was significantly associated with a more favorable amyloid profile, reflected by higher CSF Aβ42/40 and lower amyloid-PET burden, as well as better cognitive function. Cross-sectional indirect-effect analyses involving CSF Aβ42/40 met the reported FDR threshold in the pooled cohort and in MCI participants. In contrast, PET indirect effects did not remain significant after FDR correction. Overall, higher serum dopamine was linked to a more favorable amyloid profile and better cognitive function in the pooled cohort and within MCI. However, future longitudinal and mechanistic studies are needed to validate these findings, clarify causality, and characterize the peripheral dopamine-amyloid-cognition association. Serum dopamine is not a direct measure of central neurotransmission, and these subgroup results do not establish different effects between diagnoses.

articles.title: Predicting the need for surgery in children undergoing enema reduction for intussusception: development and internal-external validation in a 10-year cohort.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Most children with intussusception are reduced by enema, but a minority need surgery. We developed and validated a model using information available before reduction to identify these children, and examined its stability over a decade of changing technique. Retrospective cohort (2016-2025) of children aged 3 months to < 5 years with confirmed intussusception and attempted enema reduction at a children's hospital, excluding small-bowel intussusception on pre-treatment imaging. The outcome was intussusception-directed surgery during the admission. Logistic regression included age and symptom duration (restricted cubic splines), bloody stool, vomiting, lethargy, fever, diarrhoea and reduction technique (air or ultrasound-guided hydrostatic). Performance was assessed by internal-external cross-validation across five periods. Of 6854 episodes (6281 children), 399 (5.8%) underwent surgery, 377 after failed reduction. The pooled C-statistic was 0.82 (95% CI 0.78-0.85) and the pooled observed-to-expected ratio 0.98 (0.86-1.12). Bloody stool, vomiting, lethargy, fever, age and symptom duration predicted surgery; infants accounted for 69.2% of operations. Hydrostatic reduction was associated with lower odds of surgery (adjusted OR 0.59; 0.72 [95% CI 0.46-1.13] with calendar year added); a model without it tended to over-estimate risk after 2020. A four-item count (bloody stool, vomiting, lethargy, age < 1 year) separated episodes with a surgical risk of 2.1% (score 0-2; 75.4% of episodes) from those with 17.2% (score 3-4).

CONCLUSION: In one tertiary centre, bedside features separated children at higher and lower risk of surgery after attempted enema reduction; blood tests added little. As calibration changed over time, external validation and local recalibration are needed.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Most children with intussusception are reduced by enema, but a minority need surgery; many published models are small, validated by random splitting, and some combine all ages and anatomical types.

WHAT IS NEW: • In 6,854 enema reductions in children aged 3 months to 5 years, bedside features predicted surgery across five calendar periods (pooled C-statistic 0.82); a four-item count separated risks of 2.1% and 17.2%. • Without a technique term the model tended to over-estimate risk after the switch to hydrostatic reduction, an imprecise finding confounded with other changes.

articles.title: Healthcare-Associated Factors and Candidemia in Hospitalized Patients with Diabetes and Candiduria: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Candiduria is frequently identified in hospitalized patients with diabetes mellitus, but the relationship between long-term glycemic control, healthcare-associated factors, and candidemia remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association of HbA1c and healthcare-associated characteristics with candidemia among hospitalized patients with diabetes and candiduria.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 257 hospitalized adults with diabetes mellitus and candiduria between January 2021 and September 2025. Candidemia was defined as a positive blood culture for Candida identified on the same day as candiduria or subsequently during the index hospitalization. Demographic, clinical, microbiological, and healthcare-associated variables were evaluated. Given the limited number of candidemia events, Firth penalized logistic regression was performed using central venous catheter (CVC) presence at candiduria detection, hospitalization within the preceding three months, and HbA1c.

RESULTS: Candidemia was identified in 17 patients (6.6%), with a median interval of 5 days (range, 0-30 days) between candiduria and candidemia detection. CVC presence was more frequent among patients with candidemia than among those without candidemia (52.9 vs. 8.8%; p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis, CVC presence (adjusted OR 10.23, 95% CI 3.61-29.65; p < 0.001) and hospitalization within the preceding three months (adjusted OR 2.86, 95% CI 1.02-8.31; p = 0.046) were associated with candidemia, whereas HbA1c was not (adjusted OR 0.91, 95% CI 0.69-1.12; p = 0.391). Species-level concordance between urine and blood isolates was observed in 12 of 17 patients (70.6%). Patients with candidemia had longer hospital stays, while differences in ICU admission and in-hospital mortality did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized patients with diabetes and candiduria, CVC presence and recent hospitalization were associated with candidemia, whereas HbA1c was not significantly associated with candidemia. These findings highlight the importance of healthcare-associated characteristics but do not establish a urinary source of bloodstream infection. Given the limited number of candidemia cases, the findings require cautious interpretation and validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Predicting OCT-derived retinal and choroidal thickness phenotypes in adults with diabetes using a tabular foundation model integrating ocular biometry and systemic health data.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether systemic health data and ocular biometry can predict distribution-defined central macular thickness (CMT) and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT) phenotypes in adults with diabetes using a tabular foundation model.

METHODS: We analyzed Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data (2017-2021). Upper- and lower-tail CMT and SFCT phenotypes were defined using 3%, 5%, and 10% cutoffs from the 2017-2019 development cohort and evaluated in the independent 2020-2021 temporal validation cohort. Systemic-only and anatomy-aware models, incorporating axial length and anterior chamber depth, were compared. Participant-grouped cross-validation prevented fellow-eye leakage. Discrimination, calibration, and incremental performance were assessed.

RESULTS: Overall, Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN), a tabular foundation model, demonstrated stronger predictive performance than conventional machine-learning algorithms across most phenotype prediction tasks. The CMT and SFCT cohorts comprised 3,732 and 3,699 eyes, respectively. In temporal validation, anatomy-aware TabPFN achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.722 (high CMT 3%), 0.745 (low CMT 3%), 0.817 (high SFCT 3%), and 0.880 (low SFCT 3%). Adding ocular biometry significantly improved prediction of low SFCT phenotypes compared with systemic-only TabPFN (ΔAUC, 0.121-0.157; all P ≤ 0.003), but not compared with age-plus-axial-length logistic regression. Positive predictive values were low for rare phenotypes, and calibration varied across tasks.

CONCLUSIONS: Anatomy-aware TabPFN predicted extreme OCT thickness phenotypes, particularly low SFCT, but much of the gain may reflect established axial-length-related anatomy. Clinical utility for OCT triage remains unproven and requires external validation.

articles.title: Comparing Traditional and Alternative Genetic Counseling Service Delivery Models in Multidisciplinary Breast Cancer Clinics: A Survey of Patient Experience and Understanding after Genetic Testing.
articles.journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
articles.abstract: Genetic testing for hereditary breast cancer informs surgical, systemic therapy, and risk management decisions. Traditional counseling with pre- and post-test sessions by certified genetic counselors is resource intensive. Alternative models, such as pre-test education by oncology providers with post-test counseling, may expand access, but patient experience data are limited. Adults aged 18 and over with newly diagnosed breast cancer undergoing genetic testing at University of Colorado MDC clinics were enrolled in traditional or alternative pathways. All were invited to complete two surveys based on the Genomics Outcome Scale: post-MDC (1 day after visit) and post-results (1 week after disclosure). Surveys assessed comprehension, emotional response, and free-text reflections. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis were performed. Of 142 patients, 62 (44%) underwent testing; 15 completed the post-MDC survey, 10 completed both. Respondents were mostly white (93%), female (100%), and highly educated (53% with master's+). Comprehension and emotional response were similar between models; anxiety remained low in the alternative pathway. Free-text responses highlighted family, knowledge, prevention, and societal benefit. Patient understanding and emotional response were not diminished in the alternative model. These workflows may improve access and efficiency without compromising experience. Larger, diverse studies are needed to guide scalable implementation.

articles.title: Antibiotic prescriptions in children with community-acquired empyema: an Italian multicentric study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The limited evidence guiding antibiotic therapy for pediatric empyema contributes to the frequent prescription of broad-spectrum agents, often including antibiotics categorized as "Watch" or "Reserve" according to the WHO AWaRe classification. We aimed primarily to describe antibiotic prescribing patterns in a large national cohort of children hospitalized with empyema and, secondarily, to explore associations between antibiotic exposure categories and clinical outcomes. We conducted a multicenter retrospective study including children (< 18 years) admitted with pleural empyema to 19 Italian hospitals (2018-2023). Data on antibiotic regimens, duration, route of administration, and clinical outcomes were collected. Prescriptions were categorized according to the AWaRe classification. Associations between antibiotic classes and clinical outcomes were assessed using multilevel models and inverse probability weighting with regression adjustment. All 263 patients with empyema included in the study received antibiotic therapy for a median of 27 days (IQR 20-40), including 20 days (IQR 14-28) of intravenous treatment. The most frequently prescribed agents were ceftriaxone/cefotaxime (71.9%) and glycopeptides (46.8%). Only 8.7% of patients received an antibiotic with a narrow anti-pneumococcal spectrum. Meanwhile, 97.3% received at least one "Watch" antibiotic, and 33.1% received at least one "Reserve" antibiotic. Considerable heterogeneity in antibiotic regimens was observed across centers. No demographic, clinical, laboratory, or radiological variables were consistently associated with antibiotic category selection. Exploratory adjusted analyses showed no consistent association between the evaluated antibiotic exposure categories and lower probabilities of CPAP use, mechanical ventilation, or PICU admission. Several isolated associations were observed for secondary outcomes, including lower VATS use among children exposed to anti-MRSA therapy, to be interpreted cautiously.

CONCLUSION: In this large national cohort, prolonged and broad-spectrum antibiotic exposure was common and highly variable across patients and centers. Watch and Reserve antibiotics were frequently prescribed. Exploratory adjusted analyses did not identify consistent associations between broader-spectrum exposure and major respiratory or intensive-care outcomes, but causal effects cannot be inferred from these retrospective data. These findings primarily highlight substantial stewardship opportunities and support prospective studies designed to evaluate treatment strategies with explicit consideration of treatment timing and disease severity.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Pediatric Empyema is a severe complication of pneumonia. • The optimal antibiotic management of empyema remains unclear, leading historically to antibiotic overuse.

WHAT IS NEW: • In a 19-center Italian cohort, prolonged antibiotic courses and exposure to WHO Watch and Reserve antibiotics were common, with marked heterogeneity in prescribing patterns. • Exploratory adjusted analyses did not show consistent associations between broader-spectrum antibiotic exposure and major respiratory or intensive-care outcomes.

articles.title: Susceptibility to oral candidiasis in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: insights from salivary proteomics.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) are more susceptible to oral candidiasis (OC), but the underlying host factors remain unclear. This study aimed to identify diabetes-associated salivary alterations related to oral mucosal defense and OC susceptibility.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Unstimulated whole saliva from healthy controls (HC), DM, OC, and OC-DM participants (n = 15/group) was analyzed by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Diabetes-associated alterations were assessed by DM vs. HC, followed by comparison of OC-associated responses across diabetic and non-diabetic backgrounds. Candidate proteins underwent exploratory clinical correlation analysis.

RESULTS: OC-DM participants showed lower salivary flow and higher HbA1c than DM participants, whereas fungal burden did not differ significantly between OC-DM and OC groups. Proteomics identified 236 diabetes-associated proteins enriched in salivary secretion, epithelial interaction, immune regulation, and host-microbial processes. Among 311 classifiable OC-associated proteins, 73 showed larger effects in the diabetic background, 73 attenuated effects, and 165 similar effects. MB increased in OC-DM vs. DM but not in OC vs. HC and was associated with HbA1c and salivary flow. IGHA1 increased in OC vs. HC but showed a weaker response in the diabetic background.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes-associated salivary proteomic alterations indicate impaired oral mucosal resilience and altered host responses during OC, providing exploratory insights into mechanisms potentially contributing to OC susceptibility.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: OC susceptibility in patients with diabetes may involve impaired oral mucosal defense and dysregulated host responses beyond fungal burden alone. This study provides new insights into the potential mechanisms underlying OC susceptibility in diabetes.

articles.title: Osteoporosis is associated with higher five-year surgical complication rates after total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Existing retrospective studies of total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) in patients with osteoporosis are limited by short follow-up and small cohorts and may underestimate long-term complications. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the association between osteoporosis and medical and surgical complications after primary TSA.

METHODS: Of 99,028 patients who underwent primary TSA between January 2010 and April 2018, 13,138 had a preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis and 85,890 did not. Patients with osteoporosis were older, more often female, and more comorbid. Kaplan-Meier analysis compared the cumulative incidence of surgical outcomes, and multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, and Charlson Comorbidity Index compared complications.

RESULTS: Patients with osteoporosis had a higher five year risk of revision TSA (3.59% vs. 3.29%; HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.13-1.39; p < 0.001), with higher risks of periprosthetic fracture (HR: 1.26; 95% CI: 1.06-1.50; p = 0.008) and mechanical loosening (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.05-1.36; p = 0.006), and a borderline association with dislocation (HR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.00-1.26; p = 0.049). Medical complications were also increased, including deep vein thrombosis (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.10-1.31), pulmonary embolism (HR: 1.20; 95% CI: 1.09-1.33), pneumonia (HR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.06-1.21), fluid and electrolyte imbalance (HR: 1.47; 95% CI: 1.27-1.71), transfusion (HR: 1.21; 95% CI: 1.10-1.34), urinary tract infection (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and myocardial infarction (HR: 1.15; 95% CI: 1.04-1.28).

CONCLUSION: A preoperative diagnosis of osteoporosis is associated with a higher 5-year risk of revision, periprosthetic fracture, and mechanical loosening after primary TSA.

articles.title: Associations of ambulatory and office blood pressure profiles with left ventricular geometric remodeling in children with primary hypertension.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the associations of office and ambulatory blood pressure (BP) parameters with left ventricular (LV) geometry in pediatric primary hypertension. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 322 children with primary hypertension were enrolled. LV geometry was classified using LV mass index and age-adjusted relative wall thickness (RWT) into four categories: normal geometry, concentric remodeling, eccentric hypertrophy, and concentric hypertrophy. Multivariable logistic regression (adjusted for BMI Z-score) evaluated associations of office and ambulatory BP parameters, including the office - daytime BP difference, with LV geometry. Within the subgroup with abnormal RWT, concentric hypertrophy was compared with concentric remodeling, and an interaction model assessed whether the association of the difference with LV mass index differed by RWT status. Of 322 children (age 13.0 [11.0, 14.0] years; 78.3% boys), 56 had abnormal LV geometry: 31 concentric remodeling, 16 eccentric hypertrophy, and 9 concentric hypertrophy. Concentric remodeling was associated with higher ambulatory BP, particularly diastolic BP, whereas concentric hypertrophy was associated with office BP indices but no ambulatory BP measure. Among 40 children with abnormal RWT, the office - daytime BP difference was associated with concentric hypertrophy rather than concentric remodeling, and with LV mass index in children with abnormal but not normal RWT (interaction P < 0.001), also after adjustment for office BP.

CONCLUSION: In children with primary hypertension, concentric remodeling was associated with higher ambulatory BP, while concentric hypertrophy was associated with office BP and the office - daytime BP difference. Assessing the office - daytime difference alongside ambulatory BP parameters may help identify children with abnormal LV geometry.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Elevated blood pressure in childhood is linked to left ventricular hypertrophy, but studies rarely separate concentric remodeling from eccentric and concentric hypertrophy.

WHAT IS NEW: • In 322 Chinese children with hypertension, concentric remodeling was associated with ambulatory blood pressure, while concentric hypertrophy was associated with the office-daytime blood pressure difference, a measure not previously examined in relation toleft ventricular geometry in children.

articles.title: Comparison of Carlevale and Artisan lenses for secondary implantation in aphakia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Secondary intraocular lens implantation in the absence of capsular support remains a significant surgical challenge. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to compare the clinical outcomes, refractive precision, safety profile, and surgical efficiency of the retropupillary Artisan iris-claw lens and the novel Carlevale sutureless scleral-fixated lens (SSFIOL). Conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science was performed. Five retrospective comparative studies published between 2020 and 2025 were included, comprising a total of 604 eyes. Data were synthesized using a random-effects model. Results revealed no significant differences in postoperative best-corrected visual acuity, cystoid macular edema, or corneal edema. Available retrospective evidence suggests that both techniques are effective options for secondary IOL implantation in eyes lacking capsular support. The Carlevale lens was associated with lower postoperative astigmatism overall (MD =  - 0.67 D), although this effect was primarily driven by comparisons against corneal-incision cohorts and was attenuated in sensitivity analyses. Additionally, Carlevale implantation was associated with a reduced risk of hemorrhagic complications, whereas retropupillary Artisan implantation offered a shorter operative time (MD = 13.90 min). However, given the retrospective design of available studies and limited certainty of evidence, these findings should be interpreted with caution until validated by prospective long-term trials. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251250390.

articles.title: Is psychomotor retardation associated with treatment response in adults with depression? A secondary analysis of nine randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychomotor retardation is characterized by slowed motor and cognitive processes. Although associated with greater illness severity in depression, its relationship with treatment response is unclear. We examined whether psychomotor retardation is associated with treatment outcomes in depression.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of individual participant data from nine randomized controlled trials of pharmacological, psychological, and exercise-based treatments for unipolar depression in primary care (Dep-GP). Self-reported psychomotor retardation was assessed at baseline using the Revised Clinical Interview Schedule. The primary outcome was the standardized z-score of each trial's validated self-report depression measure at 3-4 months post-randomization; the secondary outcome was remission. Within-study regression models were adjusted for established prognostic factors, with secondary analyses additionally adjusting for baseline core depressive symptoms and depression severity. Effect estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Among 4,290 participants, 2,754 (64.2%) reported psychomotor retardation. Psychomotor retardation was associated with greater depression severity at follow-up (pooled z-score = 0.184, 95% CI [0.059, 0.309], p = 0.004, I2 = 68.7%) and lower odds of remission (pooled OR = 0.737, 95% CI [0.577, 0.941], p = 0.015, I2 = 57.7%), adjusting for age, sex, ethnicity, marital status, employment status and allocated treatment. Findings were robust to adjustment for baseline core depressive symptoms but not after adjustment for full baseline severity.

CONCLUSIONS: Psychomotor retardation is associated with poorer treatment outcomes in depression, though this may reflect underlying severity. Recognition of psychomotor retardation may help identify patients at risk of poorer response and inform clinical management.

articles.title: Optimizing rate control in atrial fibrillation: conduction system pacing vs biventricular pacing.
Gender Representation in Leadership of Pediatric Hospital Subspecialty Organizations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Equity in leadership of hospital-based pediatric organizations at the national level is essential to supporting a diverse workforce and patient population.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the gender representation of women on leadership committees and boards of external organizations compared with their representation in the workforce of neonatal-perinatal medicine, pediatric critical care medicine, pediatric hospital medicine, and pediatric cardiac critical care.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study of publicly available data in 2024.

MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was representation of women in external leadership of selected subspecialties. Measures included demographic and institutional variables of American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) and external leadership organizations.

RESULTS: A total of 771 individuals across 41 external organizations were included. Women constituted 54% of these ABP-certified hospital-based subspecialists and 47.7% of identified leaders (P < .05). The representation of women was 45.5% after excluding nonphysician leaders. Women represented 35% of those holding "top seats," including president, chair, editor-in-chief, or equivalent titles. Of the categories of external organizations, women were least likely to be represented as leaders of research-oriented organizations at 42.8%. We were unable to determine the candidacy or selection process for leadership for more than 70% of the organizations. Among this subset, only 42.7% of leaders were women.

CONCLUSION: Women pediatric physicians were significantly underrepresented in external leadership positions compared with the workforce in an aggregate of hospital-based subspecialties. A lack of transparency in leadership selection may contribute to gender inequities in leadership. Opportunities exist for promoting leadership that is representative of the workforce.

articles.title: Integrative Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of aging-related genes associated with stroke risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a major cerebrovascular disease, and aging is a major risk factor associated with poorer outcomes. Identifying genetic mechanisms linking aging-related processes to stroke may help prioritize relevant genes and pathways.

AIMS: To identify aging-related genes associated with stroke risk and explore their molecular and cellular context.

STUDY DESIGN: An integrated analysis combining eQTL-based Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.

METHODS: eQTL data were obtained from eQTLGen, with stroke GWAS data from FinnGen as the discovery dataset and the GWAS Catalog as the validation dataset. MR, sensitivity and colocalization analyses were used to evaluate associations between genetically predicted gene expression and stroke risk. Single-cell data (GSE174574) were analyzed using Seurat to characterize cell-type-specific expression of prioritized genes. GSEA and GSVA were used for pathway analysis, while RcisTarget, miRWalk, and DGIdb were used to explore regulatory and drug-gene interactions.

RESULTS: In 340,999 participants, 22 aging-related genes showed nominal MR associations with stroke risk. Validation in 1,039,382 participants identified LPAR3, MEOX1, VEGFA and PRKDC. Higher genetically predicted MEOX1 and VEGFA expression was associated with lower stroke risk, whereas LPAR3 and PRKDC were associated with higher risk. VEGFA showed additional support from regional colocalization analysis, whereas LPAR3 and MEOX1 were primarily supported by MR evidence. Regulatory analysis identified 51 predicted miRNAs and 53 drug-gene interaction records involving VEGFA and LPAR3.

CONCLUSION: LPAR3, MEOX1, VEGFA and PRKDC were prioritized as aging-related genes associated with stroke risk. VEGFA showed additional support from regional colocalization analysis, while LPAR3, MEOX1 and PRKDC require further functional validation.

articles.title: Nurses' Attitudes Toward ANCC NCPD Accreditation and the Association With Perceived Value, Satisfaction, Confidence, and Educational Quality.
articles.journal: Journal of continuing education in nursing
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC) Nursing Continuing Professional Development (NCPD) accreditation provides a framework for continuing education (CE) grounded in evidence-based standards. Despite widespread use of ANCC NCPD accreditation, little research has examined how nurses' attitudes toward accreditation relate to key CE outcomes. Guided by Donabedian's model, Kirkpatrick's evaluation framework, and expectancy-value theory, this study examined nurses' attitudes toward accredited CE and the association with perceived value, satisfaction, confidence, and educational quality.

METHOD: This quantitative correlational design explored relationships between attitudes toward ANCC-accredited CE and perceived value, satisfaction with CE, professional confidence, and educational quality. Licensed nurses completed a structured survey. Data analysis included descriptive statistics and Spearman correlations.

RESULTS: Nurses reported positive attitudes toward accreditation. Significant positive correlations indicated that more positive attitudes were associated with higher perceived value, greater satisfaction, increased confidence, and enhanced perceptions of educational quality.

CONCLUSION: Nurses' attitudes toward accreditation influence key CE outcomes, aligning with theoretical expectations regarding structure, learner reaction, and motivation. Accreditation has a role in supporting high-quality CE and advancing professional development.

articles.title: When Mnemonics Outlive the Evidence: Lessons From Acute Coronary Syndrome Across the Nursing Education Continuum.
articles.journal: Journal of continuing education in nursing
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical mnemonics are widely used in nursing education to simplify complex concepts and support knowledge acquisition, retention, and clinical recall. However, they may persist after the evidence that originally informed them has evolved.

METHOD: This discussion article draws on current literature, historical reflection, and more than three decades of cardiovascular teaching observations to examine the evolution and continued recognition of the acute coronary syndrome (ACS) mnemonics MONA, AMONTH, and NOAH.

RESULTS: The discussion illustrates how these mnemonics reflected different stages in ACS management and how memorable educational tools may remain embedded in nursing education and practice despite changes in clinical evidence.

CONCLUSION: Clinical mnemonics should be periodically reviewed and revised to maintain alignment with contemporary evidence. The evolution of ACS mnemonics highlights broader implications for knowledge translation, curriculum renewal, and continuing professional development across the nursing education continuum.

articles.title: A Zwitterionic Polymeric Quaternary Ammonium Microparticle (Z-pQAM) as a Candidate Wound Dressing with Simultaneous Procoagulant, Antimicrobial, and Wound-Healing Activities.
articles.abstract: Wound infection, inadequate local hemostasis, and delayed healing remain major complications following surgery and in chronic wounds. Effective wound management requires materials that simultaneously prevent infection, support hemostasis, promote tissue repair, and maintain biocompatibility. Here, we synthesized a zwitterionic polymeric quaternary ammonium microparticle (Z-pQAM) and evaluated its biocompatibility, in vitro antimicrobial and procoagulant activity, and wound-healing effects. FTIR confirmed stepwise synthesis and quaternization, and zeta potential analysis showed that Z-pQAM retains a net-negative bulk surface charge across physiological pH. In vitro degradation studies in PBS showed that Z-pQAM retained >99% of its dry mass after three weeks, indicating slow, physiologically appropriate hydrolytic degradation. Functional assays are in line with the hypothesis that its procoagulant and antibacterial activity arise from locally accessible quaternary ammonium (QA+) microdomains rather than overall surface positivity. Z-pQAM achieved >7-log10 reduction against S. aureus and E. coli, and >5-log10 reduction against MRSA at 200 mg/mL, with Live/Dead staining confirming bactericidal membrane disruption, while maintaining <0.5% hemolysis and 100% cell viability across the tested concentration range. In recalcified whole blood, Z-pQAM achieved a blood clotting index of 36.5%, comparable to a benchmark FDA-cleared hemostatic powder. In an uninfected murine full-thickness excisional wound model, topical Z-pQAM accelerated closure at day 8 without altering epidermal thickness, reduced CD45+ inflammatory infiltration by >50% at day 3, and enhanced collagen deposition by day 12. Collectively, these findings position Z-pQAM as a promising candidate for a multifunctional topical wound dressing, combining antibacterial and procoagulant activity with biocompatibility and support for wound repair.

articles.title: Heparin-Decorated Hydrogel Microspheres Enable Bioactive Islet Encapsulation and Sustained Glycemic Control in Diabetic Mice.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by immune-mediated β-cell destruction and chronic insulin deficiency. Pancreatic islet transplantation offers a promising approach to restore endogenous insulin production; however, the early post-transplantation period remains a critical barrier to successful graft function, as rapid protein adsorption, coagulation activation, and inflammatory cell recruitment at the material interface can compromise encapsulated islet viability. Here, we develop heparin-decorated hydrogel microcapsules to regulate early material-host interactions and improve the performance of islet encapsulation. Heparin was incorporated into a poly-l-lysine-modified gelatin (PLL-GEL) network through electrostatic complexation, where PLL was covalently anchored onto gelatin via transglutaminase-mediated cross-linking, and subsequently integrated with sodium alginate microcapsules fabricated by electrospraying and calcium-mediated ionic gelation. The resulting microcapsules exhibited uniform morphology, structural stability, and favorable physicochemical properties. Heparin incorporation reduced fibrinogen adsorption, prolonged coagulation times, and decreased macrophage adhesion, indicating improved early hemocompatibility and reduced material-induced cellular interactions. Furthermore, macrophages exposed to heparin-containing microcapsules showed altered immune-related transcriptional responses, suggesting regulation of early host responses. Encapsulated islets maintained high viability and glucose-responsive insulin secretion in vitro. Following intraperitoneal transplantation into diabetic mice, heparin-decorated microcapsules improved graft retention and sustained glycemic control over 30 days. Collectively, this study presents a functional material strategy for optimizing the early-stage compatibility of hydrogel microcapsules in islet transplantation.

articles.title: Chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment attenuates auditory fear conditioning in adult male rats.
articles.abstract: Noncompetitive-777-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists induce schizophrenia-like symptoms, supporting the NMDA receptor hypofunction hypothesis. Neonatal NMDA receptor blockade with MK-801 is widely used to model neurodevelopmental aspects of schizophrenia; however, its impact on cue-specific fear learning remains incompletely characterized. Male Sprague-Dawley pups received subcutaneous injections of MK-801 (0.4 mg/kg) or saline twice daily from postnatal day 7-20. In adulthood, rats underwent auditory fear conditioning (five tone-shock pairings), 4 days of extinction (45 tone-alone trials/session), a retrieval test, and a remote retrieval test. Across acquisition and all test sessions, MK-801-treated rats showed consistently lower freezing than controls. These findings suggest that chronic neonatal MK-801 treatment disrupts acquisition or expression of cue-shock associations, or both. Given the small sample size and the potential contribution of altered locomotion or shock reactivity, future work should incorporate locomotor and sensory controls.

articles.title: Family feeding environment, food insecurity, and their associations with undernutrition and overnutrition among Indonesian school-aged children.
articles.journal: International journal of adolescent medicine and health
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The double burden of malnutrition (DBM), the coexistence of stunting and overweight/obesity, has emerged as a growing concern among school-aged children in low-and middle-income countries, yet remains poorly understood. The present study aimed to examine how family feeding environments, food insecurity, and dietary behaviours are associated with undernutrition and overnutrition in an Indonesian population undergoing rapid nutrition transition.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study involved 161 children and 116 parents across three districts in South Sulawesi. Data on dietary intake, nutritional status, feeding practices, and household food insecurity were collected using structured questionnaires, FFQ, and HFIAS. Nutritional status was assessed using BMI-for-age and height-for-age z-scores. Associations were examined using descriptive statistics, correlations, and exploratory multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: Children had low fruit and vegetable (median 127 g/day) intake and high consumption of SSB and UPF (149.5 mL/day and 116 g/day, respectively). Overweight/obesity (OWOB) affected 52.2 % and stunting 29.2 %; 4.3 % had both. Parent-reported feeding practices showed a limited association with children's dietary intake. Food insecurity was prevalent (54 %). In exploratory adjusted models, moderate food insecurity (aOR=7.51; 95 % CI: 1.14-66.76) and residence in Takalar or Makassar compared with Maros were associated with higher odds of OWOB, whereas female sex was associated with lower odds. Stunting was associated with female sex (aOR=3.79; 95 % CI: 1.28-13.08) and residence in Maros, but not with food insecurity.

CONCLUSIONS: Children's diets remained poor despite generally positive parent-reported feeding practices, which may reflect broader environmental influences. The differing correlates of OWOB and stunting highlight the need for tailored, context-specific interventions aiming at improving diet quality and food environments. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies integrating dietary, environmental, and biological data. Despite generally positive feeding practices reported by parents, children's diets remained poor, which may reflect broader environmental influences.

articles.title: Osteopathic manipulative treatment in resolving post-stroke depression: a case report.
articles.abstract: Depression affects approximately one in three people following a stroke, most commonly within the first year. The current standard of care for post-stroke depression (PSD) does not differ from that of a non-stroke patient. Few studies have investigated the application of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) within psychiatric conditions; however, studies have demonstrated its potential in downregulating the body's stress response. In this case report, we explore the use of OMT as an adjunct intervention for new-onset mild depressive symptoms following a stroke. This case follows a 64-year-old woman who presented to an outpatient behavioral health clinic in October 2024 for depressed mood following a left middle cerebral artery stroke four months prior. She initiated psychotherapy and declined medication management. After four months of psychotherapy exclusively, her mood symptoms continued to worsen and her PHQ-9 was 7. In April 2025, after six months of psychotherapy, she began OMT every two weeks, for a total of three treatments, addressing somatic dysfunctions of the head, cervical spine, thoracic inlet, and associated musculature. At each session, she completed the PHQ-9 and a pre- and post-session questionnaire assessing specific mood symptoms (sleep, irritability, stress/tension, hopelessness, anxious mood, and depressed mood). At initiation of OMT, the patient's PHQ-9 score was 5, with clinician-observed emotional lability and tearfulness. Her pre-session questionnaire indicated disturbances in sleep, irritability, hopelessness, and depressed mood. Immediately following her first treatment, the patient noted absence of symptoms on post-OMT questionnaire. Following three OMT sessions, her PHQ-9 decreased to 0 and there was no self-reported anxious or depressed mood, irritability, or hopelessness. After two months without OMT, the patient's depressive symptoms and emotional lability returned. These symptoms resolved immediately following an additional OMT session. Two weeks later, her PHQ-9 was 0 and no other mood symptoms were reported. With ongoing OMT every 4-6 weeks, subsequent PHQ-9's continued to be 0. This case suggests the potential of integrating OMT in the treatment of mild PSD, with this patient experiencing initial resolution of depressive symptoms following three OMT sessions. We hope these findings encourage providers to consider OMT in management of depressive symptoms following stroke and spur further investigation of the utilization of OMT as an adjunctive treatment in PSD.

articles.title: Somatic dysfunction characterization following acute cerebrovascular disease: the SOMADC-AC study.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: No previous study has systematically quantified somatic dysfunction (SD) in patients with acute cerebrovascular disease nor determined its relationship with focal neurological impairment or quality-of-life (QoL) after stroke. A new diagnostic paradigm, the functional pathology of the musculoskeletal system (FPMSS), may improve examiner reliability to measure musculoskeletal dysfunction and be applicable in patients with cerebral ischemia. The FPMSS methodology provides a semi-quantifiable grading scale, similar to grading reflex or motor power, to measure the disproportion of available motion.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to reliably quantify SD severity in healthy participants and patients with transient ischemic attack (TIA) or acute ischemic stroke. Additionally, we examined the relationships between musculoskeletal dysfunction identified during hospitalization, focal motor deficit severity among those with stroke, and 3-month QoL outcomes after cerebral infarction.

METHODS: Healthy asymptomatic participants, patients with TIA (disease control), and those admitted for acute ischemic stroke were recruited from an academic tertiary referral center to undergo standardized musculoskeletal examinations. Participants underwent paired, blinded ratings by two independent raters on the same day. The paired ratings were performed twice in healthy participants (2 weeks apart), once in those with transient cerebral ischemia, and up to three paired instances, 48-72 h apart, for patients admitted with acute stroke. Eighty unique musculoskeletal examination tests were performed on each participant and focused on specified body regions: cervical and thoracolumbar spines, cephalic ("upper") extremities, innominates, pedal ("lower") extremities, legs, and feet. All assessments were performed by passive, specified linkage testing for available motion, and all examiners received standardized consensus training in the FPMSS model. Participants with ischemic stroke also underwent neuromotor strength testing, based on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale motor subcomponents (NIHSS-motor), at the time of each musculoskeletal assessment, and patient-reported QoL outcomes were obtained three months after discharge in those with cerebral infarction.

RESULTS: A total of 120 participants were enrolled (20 healthy controls, 20 with TIA, 80 with ischemic stroke). Fifty-eight of 120 (48.3 %) participants were female. Changes in speech or language were the most frequent presenting symptom in those with TIA (50 %), whereas weakness affected 71.3 % of the patients presenting with stroke. Nearly two-thirds of the patients with stroke had notable paralysis (e.g., NIHSS-motor≥2), and one-third of the survivors had moderate-severe disability at discharge (modified Rankin Scale [mRS]>2). Compared to healthy participants, patients with cerebral ischemia had significantly greater SD severity. Three-month health-related QoL domains correlated with motor impairment severity from stroke but not with SD burden.

CONCLUSIONS: A greater severity of SD is seen in those with acute cerebral ischemia compared to younger healthy asymptomatic participants; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution due to potential measured and unmeasured confounding. Three-month QoL is associated with acute stroke-related motor impairment but did not correlate with SD identified during hospitalization.

articles.title: MPLA preconditioning protects against lethal radiation-combined burn injury with attenuation of KC/CXCL1-associated vascular leakage in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiation-combined burn injury (RCB), defined as concurrent irradiation and burn injury, is expected to be common in radiological or nuclear mass-casualty events and can be highly lethal. The mechanisms underlying the irradiation-burn interaction remain poorly understood, particularly whether it amplifies capillary leak and inflammatory mediator responses to drive early lethality. We examined whether repeated low-dose monophosphoryl lipid A (MPLA) preconditioning modulates this response and whether KC/CXCL1 contributes to vascular leakage.

METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice underwent 6 Gy whole-body irradiation followed 1 h later by a 20% total body surface area full-thickness burn. MPLA (10 µg/mouse) or vehicle was administered intraperitoneally on days -4 and -3. We assessed 30-day survival, hemoconcentration, intravascular FITC-albumin retention, intestinal barrier endpoints, and cytokine/chemokine responses. A separate exploratory experiment evaluated pre-irradiation anti-KC/CXCL1 antibody treatment.

RESULTS: Neither injury alone was lethal, whereas vehicle-treated RCB mice had 90% mortality (9 of 10 mice). Seven of these deaths occurred at 24-48 h after RCB. MPLA preconditioning increased 30-day survival from 10% to 80% ( p = 0.0003) and eliminated deaths within 48 h. RCB induced hemoconcentration and tended to reduce FITC-albumin retention. Compared with vehicle-treated RCB mice, MPLA-preconditioned RCB mice had less hemoconcentration, significantly higher FITC-albumin retention, and lower mesenteric lymph node bacterial burden. MPLA preconditioning suppressed KC/CXCL1, which showed the largest absolute increase among measured cytokines/chemokines at 6 h. Anti-KC/CXCL1 antibody treatment significantly increased FITC-albumin retention at 6 h (p = 0.038).

CONCLUSIONS: MPLA preconditioning improved survival after RCB. It may attenuate early inflammatory and vascular abnormalities. Exploratory antibody-treatment findings suggest a possible contribution of KC/CXCL1 to early vascular albumin leakage, warranting further validation.

articles.title: A new indication for finerenone (Kerendia).
articles.journal: The Medical letter on drugs and therapeutics

articles.title: Reoviruses hijack TOLLIP-dependent selective autophagy to degrade stress granules and suppress antiviral immunity.
articles.abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are dynamic, non-membranous cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein condensates that form in response to cellular stress and viral infection. Emerging evidence indicates that SGs play critical roles in virus-host interactions, exerting both antiviral and proviral functions. Here, using grass carp reovirus (GCRV), one of the most virulent aquareoviruses, as a model, we investigated the interplay between reoviruses and SGs and defined the functional role of SGs during reovirus infection. We found that SGs were closely associated with GCRV viroplasms and functioned as platforms for antiviral signaling, thereby restricting GCRV replication. However, GCRV infection effectively inhibited SG formation by suppressing EIF2AK2/PKR (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 alpha kinase 2)-EIF2S1/eIF2α (eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2 subunit alpha) signaling and promoting the degradation of SG-associated proteins. Mechanistically, the GCRV nonstructural protein 38 (NS38) and nonstructural protein 26 (NS26) interacted with SG-associated proteins and promoted their degradation through the autophagy-lysosome pathway. We further identified the autophagy receptor TOLLIP (toll interacting protein) as a critical mediator hijacked by NS38 and NS26 to facilitate the selective degradation of SG-associated proteins. Importantly, we extended these findings to mammalian orthoreovirus (MRV), revealing that MRV also suppressed SG formation through a mechanism similar to that of GCRV. In addition, we demonstrated that SGs exerted broad-spectrum antiviral effects against diverse aquatic viruses. Collectively, our study revealed a previously unrecognized mechanism by which reoviruses exploited selective autophagy to dismantle SGs and evade host antiviral immunity, highlighting SGs as important regulators of antiviral defense and potential targets for broad-spectrum antiviral strategies.Abbreviations: 3-MA: 3-methyladenine;
