articles.title: Predictive validity of General Movements Assessment in identifying neurodevelopmental disorders.
Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-To-Edge Repair Versus Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement for Severe Symptomatic Tricuspid Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) are both approved for severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) but lack head-to-head comparison.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to compare 1-year outcomes of T-TEER vs TTVR using causal inference in a harmonized real-world cohort.

METHODS: TRIVALVE (International Multisite Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Therapies Registry) (T-TEER, n = 384) and TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment) (TTVR, n = 398) registries were harmonized (n = 782). Inverse probability weighted survival time estimated study group average treatment effect (ATE) and treated-study group average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) effects on time to all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid valve (TV) reintervention, bleeding, and their composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), balanced for 14 baseline clinical/echocardiographic covariates, were undertaken.

RESULTS: Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan-Meier estimates was 276 days (IQR: 58-365). TTVR achieved near-complete TR elimination vs persistent mild-moderate residual TR post-T-TEER [median (IQR) grade 0 (0-1) vs 2 (1-2)]. Modeling demonstrated an early all-cause mortality penalty for TTVR (ATE: -81.3 days, P = 0.002; ATET: -79 days, P = 0.003) with a corresponding overall MACE signal (ATE: -70.7 days, P = 0.001; ATET: -69.3 days, P = 0.012).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite more complete TR reduction, orthotopic TTVR may be associated with earlier all-cause mortality and MACE penalty over T-TEER. This hypothesis-generating analysis should spur further research to identify the optimal patient phenotype for T-TEER and TTVR technologies.

articles.title: Female Sex Is Associated With Increased Health Care Use and Revision Risk After Achilles Tendon Repair.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate sex-based differences in complications, health care use, and revision rates after Achilles tendon repair.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults undergoing primary Achilles tendon repair between 2015 and 2023 were identified, stratified by sex, and matched 1:1 using propensity scores. The primary outcome was revision Achilles tendon repair; secondary outcomes were postoperative complications, emergency department visits, inpatient admissions, and opioid prescriptions, assessed at 90-day and 2-year intervals. Follow-up duration was recorded for each cohort. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated, with significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: A total of 11,251 patients were identified (68.2% men, 31.8% women). The mean follow-up was 82.0 days (men) and 81.8 days (women) for the 90-day analysis and 535.5 days (men) and 569.9 days (women) for the 2-year analysis, with a median follow-up that reached the full window in each cohort. Within 90 days postoperatively, both male and female patients experienced similar rates of wound dehiscence (P = .098), infections (P = .835), and deep vein thrombosis (P = .677). Female patients had significantly more postoperative emergency department visits (7.8% vs 5.6%, OR 1.42, P = .001) and opioid prescriptions (29.4% vs 26.8%, OR 1.14, P = .025) than males. At 2 years, female patients also showed a higher rate of revision surgery (4.4% vs 3.4%, OR 1.31, P = .048).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with male patients, female patients undergoing Achilles tendon repair had significantly higher rates of health care use (emergency department visits and opioid prescriptions) within 90 days and revision surgery within 2 years postoperatively. Differences in revision were small and may not be clinically meaningful.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Open Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis Debridement Augmented by Bioinductive Collagen Implant: Indications and Surgical Technique.
articles.abstract: Lateral epicondylitis is a common cause of elbow pain that typically resolves with conservative management. For patients with persistent symptoms and failed nonoperative treatment, surgical intervention may be considered. We describe a surgical technique for open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement with augmentation using a bovine-derived bioinductive collagen implant. The procedure involves direct visualization and excision of degenerative tendon, followed by extensor carpi radialis longus tendon repair using a suture anchor. A bioinductive patch is secured over the repair using absorbable staples and suture. This technique builds on principles established in rotator cuff repair, where bioinductive implants have shown increased tendon thickness, organized tissue regeneration, and reduced retear rates. Although no studies currently assess the efficacy of collagen augmentation in lateral epicondylitis, its hypothesized benefit lies in enhancing tendon healing and promoting growth of new tissue after debridement. Contraindications include active infection and allergy to implant materials. Postoperative rehabilitation includes early range of motion and gradual strengthening. This technique provides a reproducible approach to augment open extensor carpi radialis brevis debridement and warrants further studies to evaluate the effect of bioinductive patch augmentation and outcomes in patients with recalcitrant lateral epicondylitis.

articles.title: Bisphenol A and Its Analogues in Hypertension: Molecular Mechanisms, Epigenetic Regulation, and Therapeutic Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a leading risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart failure, stroke, and peripheral artery disease, with a lifetime risk exceeding 90% among adults aged 55-65 years. Its pathophysiology involves arterial stiffness, blood pressure variability, hormonal and neuronal dysregulation, age-related renal change, and endothelial dysfunction. Environmental endocrine disruptors, notably bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogues, are widely used in plastics and epoxy resins and may contribute by interacting with estrogen receptors and disrupting hormonal homeostasis, although human clinical evidence remains limited. This narrative review synthesizes epidemiological evidence, molecular mechanisms, and emerging therapeutic strategies linking bisphenol exposure to hypertension. The literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for publications from 2000 to 2025 and appraised with reference to the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). The mechanisms considered include oxidative stress, TGF-β/SMAD and MAPK signaling, the PI3K/AKT axis, and FOXO transcription factors, together with epigenetic alterations such as DNA methylation and histone modification. Human studies are appraised separately from experimental work, and exposure relevance, administered dose, and non-monotonic dose-response relationships are addressed explicitly. Therapeutic approaches are organized as exposure reduction, treatment of established cardiovascular effects, mechanism-directed strategies, and experimental approaches including nanoparticle-mediated delivery, chronotherapy, and RNA-based therapeutics; all remain preclinical and none has been evaluated specifically in BPA-associated hypertension. Because the human evidence is predominantly cross-sectional and the mechanistic data derive largely from experimental models, the relationships described should be regarded as associations and plausible mechanisms rather than established causal pathways.

articles.title: Evaluation of post-occlusion hepatofugal blood flow on surgeon decision making during ligation of portosystemic shunts in 53 dogs.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether hepatofugal contrast flow or caudal vena cava (CdVC) contrast filling during post-occlusion intraoperative mesenteric portovenography (PO-IOMP) were associated with the degree of extrahepatic portosystemic shunt (EHPSS) ligation performed.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort study.

ANIMALS: A total of 53 dogs.

METHODS: Data were collected retrospectively for dogs that underwent suture ligation of a single EHPSS with concurrent intraoperative mesenteric portovenography (IOMP). Review of IOMP studies was performed in a blinded manner by a single author. Logistic regression was used to evaluate associations between PO-IOMP interpretations and the degree of EHPSS ligation selected by the primary surgeon. Identified associations were further investigated using a multivariable model to control for confounding variables.

RESULTS: Complete ligation was performed in 37/53 dogs (69.8%), partial ligation in 13/53 (24.5%), and no ligation in 3/53 (5.7%). Hepatofugal contrast flow during PO-IOMP was identified in 21/53 dogs (39.6%). Dogs with hepatofugal contrast flow during PO-IOMP were more likely to have undergone incomplete ligation (partial or none) when controlling for confounding variables (odds ratio [OR] 7.06, 95% CI: 1.49-33.44, p = .014). Absence of CdVC filling during PO-IOMP was identified in 11/53 dogs (20.8%). No association was identified between dogs lacking CdVC filling during PO-IOMP and incomplete EHPSS ligation (OR 1.43, 95% CI: 0.35-5.79, p = .617). Non-responsive postoperative portal hypertension was identified in 2/53 dogs (3.8%), both necessitating euthanasia.

CONCLUSION: Hepatofugal contrast flow on PO-IOMP was associated with the decision to perform incomplete EHPSS ligation.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The identification of post-occlusion hepatofugal contrast flow may aid in patient-specific EHPSS ligation decision making.

articles.title: Assessing predictive performance of four semi-mechanistic models for long-term HbA1c with dulaglutide in people with Type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) reflects the long-term glycemic control over at least 3 months in Type 2 diabetes. Predicting HbA1c using glucose data from studies of less than 3 months would be valuable. We previously evaluated four semi-mechanistic HbA1c models (ADOPT, FFH, FHH and IGRH) for their ability to predict HbA1c for the small molecule LY2409021, and the transit compartment models (FHH and IGRH) performed well. This work aims to evaluate HbA1c predictive performance of the four models for a long-acting therapeutic protein, dulaglutide.

METHODS: The models were developed using dulaglutide concentrations, glucose and HbA1c data from a 5-week Phase 1b study. Model predictive performance was assessed by comparing model-estimated and observed HbA1c values from two Phase 2 and 3 studies. There were three metrics for predictive performance: (a) mean change from baseline HbA1c (ΔHbA1c) between observed and model-predicted values; (b) mean prediction error (MPE) for bias; and (c) root mean squared error (RMSE) for precision.

RESULTS: Overall, all models predicted the mean ΔHbA1c closely, within 0.2% of the observed values for the Phases 2 and 3 studies, at Weeks 26, 36 and 52. All models exhibited little bias (absolute MPE < 0.3%) and comparable precision (RMSE = 0.385-0.507%) estimates.

CONCLUSIONS: The transit compartment models performed consistently well for dulaglutide and LY2409021, and therefore, they are preferred for describing glycaemic control for novel antidiabetic compounds with similar mechanisms of action. Fasting glucose is more convenient to measure than average glucose in the clinic setting, favouring the FHH model that utilized fasting glucose as its biomarker.

articles.title: Superior Vena Cava Compromise During Transcatheter Atrial Septal Defect Closure: A Lesson in Implantation Geometry.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Transcatheter closure procedure of multifenestrated aneurysmal atrial septal defects (ASDs) remains technically challenging: Optimal device selection and positioning should achieve complete closure of all fenestrations while accommodating the complex three-dimensional atrial septal anatomy and its relationship to adjacent cardiac structures. Because superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction is exceedingly rare, it may easily be overlooked unless caval venous inflow is systematically evaluated by transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) after device deployment following a pre-release TEE checklist. We report the case of a 5-year-old girl with a multifenestrated aneurysmal secundum ASD. A Uni-occluder was not available; therefore, a patent foramen ovale (PFO) occluder was used for defect closure, which resulted in near-complete obstruction of the SVC by the right atrial disc of the device. The complication was recognized after positioning by intraprocedural TEE, prompting device retrieval prior to release. Subsequent closure with a dedicated ASD occluder achieved complete closure of all fenestrations without compromising caval venous return. This case highlights the importance of a concept we refer to as implantation geometry: the interplay between device-specific design, the implantation site, and complex three-dimensional septal anatomy. Recognition and careful assessment of this relationship will help optimize procedural planning and improve procedural safety in selected patients with complex, multifenestrated ASDs. Comprehensive three-dimensional anatomical assessment, appropriate device selection, and systematic TEE evaluation of the cavoatrial junction before device release are essential for safe transcatheter closure of multifenestrated ASDs-even when defect sizing appears appropriate. In particular, the geometric characteristics of PFO occluders, including their relatively large right atrial disc, should be considered when assessing the risk of SVC obstruction.

articles.title: CMR Assessment of Myocardial Reperfusion Following PPCI With or Without Manual Thrombus Aspiration in STEMI With High Thrombus Burden: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains a leading cause of morbidity and sudden cardiac death worldwide. Although primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) is the guideline-recommended reperfusion strategy, lesions with a high thrombus burden remain a clinical challenge, and routine manual thrombus aspiration is no longer recommended on the basis of all-comer trials with clinical endpoints. We used cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging to evaluate myocardial reperfusion after PPCI with or without adjunctive manual thrombus aspiration in patients restricted to the highest angiographic thrombus burden.

METHODS: One hundred STEMI patients presenting within 12 h of symptom onset, all with angiographic TIMI thrombus grade V, were randomized 1:1 (computer-generated sequence, concealed allocation) to manual thrombus aspiration followed by stenting (Group A, n = 50) or conventional PCI alone (Group B, n = 50). The trial was not prospectively registered, and no a priori power calculation was performed (predefined convenience sample). Echocardiographic and CMR images were analyzed by two independent readers blinded to treatment allocation. CMR was performed at 3 months, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded to 6 months.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were similar between groups, and no patient was lost to follow-up. On unblinded angiographic assessment, Group A had higher rates of final TIMI III flow (92% vs. 68%; risk difference 24%, 95% CI 8.4-38.6; p = 0.005) and MBG III (80% vs. 60%; risk difference 20%, 95% CI 2.0-36.4; p = 0.049). Three-month CMR showed higher LVEF (48.0% vs. 35.8%; mean difference 12.2, 95% CI 9.8-14.5), smaller infarct size (17.0% vs. 29.2% of LV mass; mean difference -12.2, 95% CI - 14.5 to -9.8), and greater stroke volume index (42.0 vs. 32.2 mL/m2; mean difference 9.8, 95% CI 7.4-12.1) in Group A (all p < 0.001). At 6 months, heart failure hospitalization was less frequent in Group A (2 vs. 10 events; 4% vs. 20%; unadjusted p = 0.028; exploratory), whereas differences in recurrent MI (4% vs. 16%; p = 0.092) and CV death (2% vs. 14%; p = 0.059) were not statistically significant. No stroke occurred in either group.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small, single-center trial of STEMI with the highest angiographic thrombus burden, manual thrombus aspiration was associated with higher angiographic reperfusion rates (assessed without blinding) and, on 3-month CMR, smaller infarct size and better ventricular function; these effect sizes are large and are probably overestimated. Clinical-event differences are exploratory: heart failure hospitalization was less frequent (2 vs. 10 events; unadjusted p = 0.028), whereas recurrent MI and cardiovascular death did not differ significantly. Given the absence of trial registration and an a priori power calculation, and the lack of an early CMR scan to assess microvascular obstruction and intramyocardial hemorrhage, these hypothesis-generating findings do not challenge the recommendation against routine aspiration and require confirmation in adequately powered, preregistered multicenter trials.

articles.title: A Contemporary Analysis of Microaxial Pump-Associated Cardiac Perforation Events From the FDA MAUDE Database.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Percutaneous microaxial pumps are used in cardiogenic shock and high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but left ventricular (LV) perforation is an infrequent but serious complication. In 2023, an FDA advisory warned of increased perforation risk.

AIMS: To describe clinical setting, patterns, high-risk subgroups, and outcomes of LV perforation in real-world reports.

METHODS: We queried the FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database (2016-2024) for Impella adverse-event reports, screened narratives for perforation terms, and manually adjudicated suspected cases to confirm LV perforation and extract device, clinical setting, presentation, management, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 24,424 Impella reports, 188 involved LV perforation (0.77%). Impella CP accounted for 52.7% and Impella 5.5 for 41.5% (few with 5.0/2.5; none with RP). Annual LV perforations per 1000 reports declined from 166.7 (2016) to 5.2 (2024). Events occurred most often during cardiac surgery (27.1%), acute coronary syndrome (19.1%), or high-risk PCI (17.0%). Intraprocedural diagnosis occurred in 76.2% and was more common with 5.5 versus CP (83.3% vs. 67.7%). With intraprocedural diagnosis, mortality was 24.6% for 5.5 and 28.4% for CP, versus 66.7% for both when diagnosis was post-procedural. Pericardial effusion (34.9%) and hypotension (28.6%) were common. Repair was attempted at 72.9% and reduced mortality, particularly for CP (19.7% with repair vs. 64.7% without; p < 0.001). Overall mortality was 30.2%, without differences by sex or race.

CONCLUSIONS: LV perforation reported with Impella devices is rare but carries high mortality; earlier recognition and prompt repair are associated with improved survival.

articles.title: Changes in combustible cigarette, heated tobacco product and electronic cigarette use and cardiovascular risk among adults with type 2 diabetes: A Korean national retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) and electronic cigarettes (ECs) are increasingly used as alternatives to combustible cigarettes (CCs), but their cardiovascular implications in type 2 diabetes remain unclear. We examined the associations between changes in smoking patterns, including self-reported changes from CCs to HTPs and/or ECs between two health screenings, and subsequent cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk among smokers with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes.

DESIGN: Nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Insurance Service data. Cause-specific Cox proportional hazards regression models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with competing-risk, overlap-weighting and other sensitivity analyses.

SETTING: Republic of Korea, using biennial national health screenings 2010-2020, with follow-up through 31 December 2022.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 63 969 individuals aged ≥ 40 years who were current CC smokers within two years of a new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes between 2010 and 2016 and who completed two health examinations were included.

MEASUREMENTS: Product-use status was self-reported at two health screenings. According to status at the second screening (2019-2020), participants were categorized as successful quitters, continued CC users, exclusive HTP/EC users or concurrent users of CC and HTP/EC. The primary outcome was incident CVD, defined as hospitalization for ≥2 days due to coronary heart disease (CHD) or acute stroke (total stroke, TS).

RESULTS: Compared with continued CC use, complete quitting was associated with lower risks of CVD (aHR = 0.72; 95% CI = 0.65-0.80), CHD (aHR = 0.76; 95% CI = 0.68-0.86) and TS (aHR = 0.64; 95% CI = 0.54-0.76). Exclusive HTP/EC use (aHR = 0.83; 95% CI = 0.62-1.11) and concurrent use (aHR = 0.88; 95% CI = 0.73-1.05) were not statistically significantly associated with overall CVD risk. In exploratory analyses based on 9 events, exclusive HTP/EC use was associated with lower risk of acute stroke compared with continued CC smoking (aHR = 0.49; 95% CI = 0.25-0.94). Estimates were directionally consistent across competing-risk, overlap-weighting and alternative-definition sensitivity analyses.

SUMMARY: Among Korean smokers with type 2 diabetes, complete smoking cessation is associated with lower risks of cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease and stroke, but exclusive use of heated tobacco products and electronic cigarettes is not statistically significantly associated with overall cardiovascular disease risk and a lower risk of stroke rests on very few events. Therefore, complete smoking cessation should remain the preferred clinical recommendation for smokers with type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: External validation of the fullPIERS model for predicting adverse maternal outcomes among Swedish women with preeclampsia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Preeclampsia affects 3%-4% of all pregnancies in the Nordic countries. It is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Using risk stratification for women diagnosed with preeclampsia could potentially reduce adverse maternal outcomes. The fullPIERS model is a clinical prediction tool that has not been validated in the Nordic countries. We therefore aimed to externally validate the fullPIERS model among Swedish women with preeclampsia.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Data were obtained from two Swedish prospective cohort studies. Predictor variables were assessed within 24 h of inclusion. Outcomes were assessed at 48 h and 7 days after inclusion. The performance of the fullPIERS model was evaluated by discrimination using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and by risk stratification at prespecified risk cutoffs. Analyses were conducted with and without hematological outcomes (blood transfusion or severe thrombocytopenia).

RESULTS: In total, 617 women were enrolled between May 2019 and March 2025. Adverse maternal outcomes occurred in 34 (5.5%) women within 48 h and 68 (11.0%) within 7 days. The fullPIERS model demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting adverse maternal outcomes within 48 h (AUC 0.64; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54, 0.74) and within 7 days (AUC 0.64; 95% CI: 0.57, 0.71). When analyses were restricted to nonhematological outcomes (n = 14 for 48 h and 19 for 7 days), the AUC was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.68, 0.89) within 48 h and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.69, 0.87) within 7 days. At a low-risk threshold of < 0.01, 297 (48.1%) women were classified as low risk, of whom one developed a nonhematological adverse outcome within 48 h, corresponding to a sensitivity of 0.93 (95% CI: 0.69-0.99) and a negative predictive value of 1.00 (95% CI: 0.98-1.00).

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the fullPIERS model demonstrated poor clinical utility in identifying low-risk and high-risk individuals for adverse maternal outcomes among Swedish women with preeclampsia. When hematological outcomes were excluded, the model improved its ability to identify women without adverse maternal outcomes. The model may have clinical utility facilitating physicians in identifying those who could be managed with a lower level of surveillance.

articles.title: Anosognosia for spatial neglect behaviour after stroke: Effects of neck muscle vibration and active exploration training - a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Anosognosia for spatial neglect - the unawareness of one's own neglect-related impairments - is a frequent but understudied consequence of right-hemispheric stroke. This exploratory analysis of unpublished data from a randomized pilot trial (Stammler et al., 2026) investigated whether neck muscle vibration (NMV), a bottom-up proprioceptive intervention, improves awareness of neglect behaviour more than standard visual exploration training. Twenty patients with spatial neglect received either active NMV or placebo NMV over two weeks, both combined with computer-based cognitive training (non-neglect-specific modules or neglect-specific visual exploration training, respectively. Awareness was assessed before and after treatment using observer- and self-ratings on the Catherine Bergego Scale. In addition, we introduced the exploratory Awareness Gain Score (AGS), designed to measure awareness change independently of symptom recovery. Although both groups showed similar reductions in neglect severity, the NMV group demonstrated significantly greater awareness gains (AGS: 36% vs. 8% newly recognized persistent deficits). While the conventional Anosognosia Index did not reveal group differences in parametric analyses, non-parametric analyses supported the AGS findings. These preliminary results suggest that NMV may enhance awareness of neglect beyond its effects on symptom severity. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and validate the AGS.Trial registration: German Clinical Trials Register identifier: DRKS00032376..

articles.title: Challenges and Progresses in Deciphering Mucin-Type O-Glycoproteomics.
articles.abstract: Protein O-glycosylation is a major type of protein glycosylation extensively distributed on membrane and secretory proteins in eukaryotes. Different from N-glycosylation's central role in protein folding, O-glycosylation is widely involved in diverse biological processes including cell recognition, signal transduction, viral infection, immune regulation, etc. However, the site-specific function of O-glycosylation is much less characterized. Compared to N-glycosylation, O-glycosylation, mucin-type O-glycosylation in particular, lacks a glycosite sequence, has more diverse glycan structures, and suffers from lower site occupancy, which makes it challenging to identify biological functions of O-glycosylation from glycoproteomic analysis. This review summarizes main difficulties in characterizing mucin-type O-glycoproteomes, updates recent progress in both sample preparation strategy and mass spectrometry methods, and provides perspectives on future directions in this field.

articles.title: Thermal Dynamics as a Non-Invasive Indicator for Cycle Life Prediction of LiFePO4/Graphite Batteries Under Fast-Charging.
articles.abstract: Resistance-induced overpotential and the associated heat generation are critical factors affecting cycle life of lithium-ion batteries under fast-charging conditions. In this study, we propose a temperature-based prognostic approach for the early prediction of battery cycle life, focusing on LiFePO4/graphite cells cycled under a fixed family of multistep fast-charging protocols at 30°C. The charging process was segmented into four state-of-charge (SoC)-resolved constant-current regions (CC1-CC4). Voltage and temperature analyses revealed that the initial SoC region (CC1) is particularly sensitive to overpotential development, where a high current density is associated with a premature transition to the constant-voltage (CV) mode and intensified heat generation. At advanced stages of cycling, temperature behavior exhibited correlations with cycle life consistent with voltage responses. Based on these observations, temperature evolution during the early cycles (third to 10th) was employed to construct a cycle life prediction model. Among the CC-resolved regions, temperature-related features from CC1 and CC4 showed higher predictive relevance than those from CC2 and CC3. These results suggest that non-invasively measured surface temperature can serve as a physically meaningful indicator for early-stage cycle life prognosis under the studied fast-charging conditions. The proposed framework provides an interpretable approach for battery health monitoring and fast-charging protocol design.

articles.title: Normative Thresholds for Upper Extremity Functional Testing in Adolescent Athletes: Outcome Measures of Strength.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of functional upper extremity measures to guide rehabilitation, reduce injury risk, and inform return-to-play decision-making has increased. However, assessment of these measures has focused primarily on collegiate and adult athletes.

HYPOTHESIS: Normative thresholds would differ by dominance, with stronger values exhibited on the dominant limb.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross sectional.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

METHODS: Healthy, adolescent athletes who reported participation in either contact or overhead upper-extremity sports completed an upper extremity functional test battery administered in a randomized order. Strength measures of internal rotation (IR) and external rotation (ER) as well as the athletic shoulder (ASH) test were collected in prone using a handheld dynamometer. Descriptive statistics were calculated for all outcome measures with separate analyses for dominant (DOM) and nondominant (NON) limbs. The 15th percentile was computed and used to establish performance thresholds. Strength measures were compared between limbs using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with effect sizes calculated. Descriptive statistics were computed to compare exploratorily male versus female and sport-based performance for all strength measures.

RESULTS: A total of 156 participants (78.2% male; 60.2% contact athletes; age, 16.5 ± 1.2 years; weight, 162.8 ± 39.2 lbs) were included for analysis. Norms and percentile thresholds across tests are presented, with shoulder strength thresholds consistently greater in the DOM limb. DOM IR strength was significantly greater than NON IR strength (P = 0.002). ASH performance was greater in the DOM limb for the I position (180 degrees of shoulder abduction; P < 0.001) and Y position (135 degrees of abduction; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Performance in healthy, adolescent athletes is influenced by limb dominance and task-specificity and indicates that reliance on collegiate or adult-derived normative values may not be appropriate.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These normative thresholds provide a clinically meaningful framework to guide rehabilitation progression and evidence-based decision-making and will serve as the foundation for future work establishing whether these measures are associated with or predictive of subsequent injury.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content in Manuscripts Submitted to Annals of Neurology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Since the large language model (LLM) program Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) was introduced in November 2022, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) expanded rapidly in published writing. This has been quantified in many fields, but not in medical journals that focus on neurology and neuroscience. We sought to characterize the use of LLM in articles submitted before and after ChatGPT became available to the general public, in a neurology journal, Annals of Neurology, that covers all neurology subspecialties.

METHODS: The study evaluated manuscripts submitted on movement disorders, dementia, and vascular neurology before and after ChatGPT became available. AI content was measured with LLM-detection platforms Pangram, Originality.ai and GPTZero. Substantial AI was defined as ≥20% of content, or >50% likelihood of AI use. Manuscript type, country of author, country, Human Development Index (HDI), AI disclosure, and publication decision were compared with AI detected.

RESULTS: Of 300 papers submitted after the introduction of ChatGPT, AI was detected by Pangram in 74 (25%) and this was substantial (≥20% of content) in 32 (11%). Substantial AI was more common in brief communications than full research articles (31% vs 10%, p = 0.006) and in vascular neurology articles (17%, vascular; 8%, dementia; and 5%, movement disorders; p = 0.012). Most manuscripts analyzed were submitted by authors from China (37%) and the United States (19%) and each had 11% substantial AI use. Authors from countries with lower levels of development were more likely to use AI (median HDI 0.797, AI ≥20% vs median HDI 0.925, AI <20%, p = 0.033). No AI was found in 60 papers submitted from July 3 to September 14, 2022 (pre-ChatGPT) by any of the AI-detection platforms. Of 300 post-ChatGPT manuscripts, 24 (8%) were accepted. None with substantial AI use were accepted (p = 0.090; odds ratio [OR] = 0.000, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.000-1.068). The authors of 5 (2%) of these papers disclosed AI use, including 1 (3%) of the papers with substantial AI detected.

INTERPRETATION: The study found AI was used in writing one quarter of papers submitted to Annals of Neurology after ChatGPT was introduced, with substantial AI content in 11%. No papers with AI ≥20% of content were accepted for publication. AI-generated text was more frequent in brief communications and vascular neurology articles. Authors in countries with lower levels of development were significantly more likely to use AI. The results suggest no advantage from AI in publication success, but point to a need for greater transparency by authors about AI use. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: FoRist: Three-DoF Soft Wearable Robot for Forearm and Wrist Assistance.
articles.abstract: The growing population of elderly individuals affected by musculoskeletal and neurological diseases experiences multijoint functional impairment, and individuals with compromised forearm and wrist function can lose independence and quality of life. However, most wearable robotic devices provide assistance for a single degree of freedom (DoF) and restrict other joint movements because decoupling multijoint kinematics remains challenging. This article introduces FoRist, a lightweight three-DoF soft wearable robot designed for forearm and wrist assistance. FoRist assists wrist ulnar/radial deviation, wrist extension/flexion, and forearm pronation/supination through a spring blade-based active-passive hybrid actuation mechanism using three motors. It integrates compact rail structures, soft tension transfer mechanisms, and a flexible twisted string actuation mechanism to assist forearm-wrist motion while preserving freedom of movement in the neighboring hand and elbow joints. The local wearable structure at the wristband rail-slider engagement has a maximum thickness of 16 mm. Its personalized usability features, including bioanatomical analysis-driven customization and user-friendly donning/doffing, support application to individuals with forearm and wrist impairments. User tests with stroke survivors showed that wearing FoRist increased the achievable range of motion and output torque across the forearm and wrist movements compared with unassisted movement. In a two-participant test of a simulated food-preparation sequence involving opening a jar, scooping jam, and spreading jam on bread, FoRist assistance increased task-relevant wrist motion and was associated with lower maximum shoulder abduction. These preliminary results support FoRist's feasibility and usability in short-term laboratory use. With its compact three-DoF architecture, low distal mass, and personalized fit, FoRist offers a promising avenue for extending rehabilitation training beyond clinical settings and has the potential to enhance independence and functional performance in activities of daily living.

articles.title: Association Between Dupilumab and Risk of Cardiovascular Diseases Among US Patients With COPD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity. Although dupilumab reduces COPD exacerbations, its cardiovascular effects remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between dupilumab and cardiovascular disease risk among patients with COPD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the US TriNetX electronic health records database with a new-user design. Patients aged ≥40 years with COPD between October 1, 2024, and June 1, 2025, receiving triple inhaler therapy were included. Patients initiating dupilumab within 30 days after COPD exacerbation were compared with those receiving triple inhaler therapy. Outcomes included acute myocardial infarction (AMI), cerebral infarction, heart failure, and atrial fibrillation/flutter (AFib/AFl). Propensity score matching (1:1) was used to balance covariates. Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 72 113 patients with COPD, 1352 matched pairs were analyzed. Dupilumab was associated with increased risks of heart failure (HR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.44-2.08) and AFib/AFl (HR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.24-1.99) compared with triple inhaler therapy. No associations were observed for AMI (HR, 1.38; 95% CI, 0.92-2.06) and cerebral infarction (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.48-1.45). Associations with heart failure and AFib/AFl remained consistent across sensitivity analyses and were observed in both eosinophil subgroups.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Higher rates of heart failure and AFib/AFl were observed among dupilumab initiators than patients receiving triple inhaler therapy alone. Given the residual confounding, these findings do not establish a causal cardiovascular effect of dupilumab. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Robotic Endoscopic Off-Pump Pericardiectomy: Early and Long-Term Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To review the perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic, endoscopic, off-pump pericardiectomy for constrictive and recurrent pericarditis at a tertiary referral center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 21 consecutive patients who underwent robotic endoscopic off-pump pericardiectomy from 2013 to 2024. The mean follow-up duration was 63.7 ± 51.1 months. Survival outcomes were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods and compared using the log-rank test or Cox regression.

RESULTS: The mean patient age at the time of surgery was 58.0 ± 15.5 years. No patient required conversion to sternotomy or cardiopulmonary bypass. There was no mortality within 6 months. Mean intensive care unit and hospital lengths of stay were 1.8 ± 1.0 and 3.7 ± 1.7 days, respectively. After surgery, right atrial pressure decreased from 20.1 ± 7.7 to 9.6 ± 5.0 mm Hg (P < 0.001), and the cardiac index increased from 2.2 ± 0.5 to 3.3 ± 0.4 L/min/m2 (P < 0.001). At the current follow-up, overall mortality was 26%, with the median survival not reached. Estimated survival at 1, 5, and 10 years was 94%, 76%, and 66%, respectively. Preoperative heart failure was associated with shorter survival (P = 0.005), whereas idiopathic etiology was associated with a more favorable survival than known causes or risk factors (P = 0.045).

CONCLUSIONS: Robotic, endoscopic, off-pump pericardiectomy was feasible and showed favorable perioperative outcomes and long-term survival. In experienced programs, this approach may represent a reasonable, minimally invasive alternative for selected patients requiring pericardiectomy.

articles.title: What Is a Blast? How to Design a Representative Pre-Clinical Model.
articles.abstract: Pre-clinical blast models vary widely in their design, using diverse subjects (animals and cells), mediums (air and water), and energy sources (wires, explosives, and gas) and levels (low to very high) to study and simulate blast exposure. While these models are often described as simulating "blast" exposure, variability exists in the resulting pressure time histories, including differences in peak pressure, duration, confinement, shock source, and the presence of a negative phase. These waveform characteristics significantly influence the overall exposure experienced during a blast and, potentially, injury outcomes. The objective of the article is to define what physically constitutes a blast wave, distinguishing it from shock-dominated pressure profiles that may result from nonexplosive sources. Using this definition, existing pre-clinical blast models are evaluated with respect to their ability to reproduce blast waveforms. By analyzing these models, this article identifies key limitations and provides guidance for designing representative pre-clinical exposure models that better reproduce blast wave characteristics. Improving blast waveform fidelity is important to improve the translation of pre-clinical experimental findings to clinical blast-induced injuries.

articles.title: Mechanistic Insights into Celastrol's Anti-Inflammatory Effects: From Molecular Targets to Therapeutic Potential.
articles.abstract: Chronic inflammation is a central pathogenic driver of a wide spectrum of diseases, including autoimmune disorders, neurodegenerative conditions, cardiovascular diseases, and metabolic syndromes. Despite advances in anti-inflammatory therapeutics, limitations such as incomplete efficacy and adverse effects necessitate the discovery of novel multitarget agents. Celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpenoid quinone methide derived from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook. f. (thunder god vine), has emerged as a potent natural product with remarkable pharmacological properties. This review comprehensively analyzes the mechanism underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of celastrol, with a particular focus on the nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) and NLRP3 inflammasome axis because of their central role in mediating the therapeutic efficacy of celastrol. We highlight its ability to modulate key signaling pathways, including NF-κB inhibition, heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) disruption, NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome suppression, and the regulation of oxidative stress via the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2/heme oxygenase-1 axis. We examined the therapeutic potential of celastrol across various disease models and demonstrated its efficacy in attenuating pathologies such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), neuroinflammation, atherosclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, and obesity-related metabolic disorders. Furthermore, we address the significant pharmacokinetic challenges hindering clinical translation, such as poor water solubility and limited oral bioavailability, and discuss innovative formulation strategies, including liposomal, polymeric, and targeted nanoparticle delivery systems designed to increase efficacy and minimize toxicity. By synthesizing current knowledge on the molecular targets and therapeutic applications of celastrol, this review underscores its promise as a multitarget anti-inflammatory agent and outlines future directions for structure-activity relationship studies, combination therapies, and clinical development.

articles.title: Patterns of wear, fracture, and re-revision in ceramic-on-ceramic total hip arthroplasty: a 31-year retrieval study.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ceramic-on-ceramic (CoC) total hip arthroplasty (THA) is commonly used in younger and more active patients due to its low wear characteristics. However, ceramic fracture and wear-related complications remain important causes of revision. This retrieval study aimed to characterise failure mechanisms and associated patient and implant factors in revised CoC bearings.

METHODS: A retrospective retrieval analysis of alumina and zirconia-toughened alumina (ZTA) CoC THA bearings revised between 1989 and 2021 was performed. Retrievals were classified as non-fractured primary revisions, fractured primary revisions, or re-revisions. Macroscopic and microscopic assessment of fracture morphology and wear patterns was undertaken. Volumetric wear and radiographic component positioning were assessed in a subset. Associations between ceramic fracture and patient activity, implant characteristics, and head size were analysed using logistic regression.

RESULTS: The most common indications for revision were aseptic loosening (35.5%), pain (34.1%), ceramic fracture (17.7%), infection (13.2%), and instability (11.8%). Ceramic fracture predominantly involved the acetabular liner (34 liner fractures versus 12 femoral head fractures). Higher patient activity level was associated with increased odds of fracture (moderate activity: OR 11.8; 95% CI, 2.66-52.7; high activity: OR 5.6; 95% CI, 1.24-25.0). ZTA femoral heads (OR 0.30; 95% CI,0.13-0.66) and larger head sizes were associated with lower odds of fracture (p < 0.001). Differences in volumetric wear between materials were not significant after adjustment for time in situ. Re-revision cases demonstrated more extensive third-body wear and shorter implant survival.

CONCLUSIONS: Ceramic fracture in CoC THA most commonly involves the acetabular liner and is associated with patient activity and implant factors. Re-revision cases demonstrate substantial third-body wear and reduced implant survival.

articles.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation nursing improves outcomes in acute COPD: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the effects of nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation on exercise capacity, pulmonary function, dyspnea, and quality of life in patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD).

METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between December 2003 and December 2024. Eligible studies compared nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation with routine care.

RESULTS: Outcome measures included the 6-min walking distance (6MWD), pulmonary function (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC), modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale (mMRC), and COPD Assessment Test (CAT). Eleven RCTs involving 986 AECOPD patients were included. Compared with routine care, pulmonary rehabilitation significantly improved 6MWD (SMD = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.62-1.16, p < 0.05), FEV1/FVC (SMD = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.18-1.06, p < 0.05), mMRC score (SMD = -0.64, p < 0.05), and CAT score (SMD = -0.93, p < 0.05). No significant differences were observed in FEV1 or FVC (p > 0.05). No significant publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: Nursing-coordinated pulmonary rehabilitation effectively improves exercise capacity, dyspnea, and quality of life in AECOPD patients, supporting its integration into routine clinical nursing care.

articles.title: Patients' and nurses' experiences of relational care in COVID-free units.
articles.abstract: BackgroundDuring the COVID-19 pandemic, precautionary visitation restrictions were implemented across hospital settings, including COVID-free units, substantially altering opportunities for relatives' presence and relational care. Although necessary for infection prevention, these measures raised ethical concerns regarding emotional support, communication, and compassionate nursing care.AimTo explore patients' and nurses' experiences of relational care under precautionary visitation restrictions in COVID-free hospital units, focusing on ethical tensions, emotional burden, and the reconfiguration of care relationships.Research designQualitative study using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA).Participants and research contextBetween March and July 2021, semi-structured interviews were conducted with seven patients and nine nurses from one hospital in Northern Italy who had direct experience of hospitalization or care delivery under restrictive visitation policies. Data were analyzed following IPA principles.Ethical considerationsEthical approval was obtained from the appropriate ethics committee (IRB approval number: 37, 20/04/2020), and all participants provided recorded informed oral consent.ResultsFour interconnected themes emerged: (1) emotional suffering and relational loneliness; (2) disruption of everyday relational care; (3) erosion of relational care under restrictive conditions; and (4) reconfiguring care relationships under restriction. Patients and nurses described emotional distress, fragmented communication, reduced relatives' involvement, and changes in relational care. Nurses additionally described ethical tensions between infection-control requirements and relationally sensitive practice, as well as adaptive changes in care relationships, including greater relational responsibility, perceived patient cooperation, and increased awareness of the importance of empathy and relational care.ConclusionsPrecautionary visitation restrictions in COVID-free hospital units substantially altered the relational dimension of care, generating emotional burden and ethical challenges for both patients and nurses. Future emergency preparedness should integrate infection-control measures with strategies that safeguard relatives' involvement and preserve compassionate, relationally oriented care.

articles.title: Isoliquiritin ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy through inhibiting the TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim was to explore the function of isoliquiritin (ILQ) on diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and its potential mechanisms.

METHODS: The roles of ILQ on cardiac function and myocardial damage of DCM rats were assessed using myocardial enzymes measurement, echocardiography, HE staining, WGA staining, Masson staining and western blot. The effects of ILQ on cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammation in myocardial tissues of DCM rats were evaluated by using TUNEL and western blot. In vitro, the roles of ILQ on HG-induced H9C2 cells damage were assessed by using CCK-8, western blot and flow cytometry. The mechanisms of ILQ in DCM were explored by using network pharmacology analysis, CETSA, DARTS assay, western blot, immunofluorescence staining, CHX chase assay, ubiquitination assay and rescue experiments through TLR4 overexpression.

RESULTS: ILQ was demonstrated to improve cardiac function, and alleviate cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in DCM rats. ILQ inhibited cardiomyocyte apoptosis and alleviated inflammation in DCM rats. ILQ treatment also repressed HG-induced H9C2 cell fibrosis, apoptosis and inflammation. Mechanically, ILQ could suppress the protein expression of TLR4 in H9C2 cells via enhancing its ubiquitination. Besides, ILQ could inhibit TLR4/NF-κB signaling in both HG-induced H9C2 cells and DCM rats. The rescue experiments indicated that TLR4 overexpression reversed the effect of ILQ on HG-induced H9C2 cell damage.

CONCLUSION: ILQ might ameliorate DCM through repressing TLR4/NF-κB signaling, thus reducing myocardial fibrosis and hypertrophy, and suppressing cardiomyocyte apoptosis and inflammation.

articles.title: Three-Dimensional Leg Alignment Analysis: Do We Need a Consensus?
articles.abstract: PurposeLower-limb deformities caused by congenital conditions or unicompartmental knee osteoarthritis are commonly treated with corrective osteotomy. Accurate surgical planning depends on precise anatomical measurements, and three-dimensional (3D) alignment analysis is increasingly used. This study quantified how different landmark, axis, and coordinate system definitions influence 3D angular measurements for assessing lower-limb deformities.MethodsTwenty-four femora and tibiae from the prospective IMI-APPROACH cohort were segmented from low-dose whole-body computed tomography scans. Established definitions of coronal and sagittal planes, anatomical landmarks, and mechanical and anatomical axes were compared. Femoral and tibial deformity parameters were calculated, including the mechanical lateral distal femoral angle (mLDFA), femoral anteversion, mechanical medial proximal tibial angle (mMPTA), posterior proximal tibial angle (PPTA), and tibial torsion. Agreement between methods was evaluated using Bland-Altman analyses.ResultsVariation in coronal plane definitions had minimal influence on femoral measurements (mean 0°). In contrast, alternative landmark and axis definitions introduced systematic bias, particularly for mLDFA. For the tibia, both plane and axis definitions affected measurements, with the largest discrepancies observed for PPTA (mean 2.6°) and tibial torsion (mean 5.6°). Comparisons between whole-leg and bone-specific coordinate systems showed small differences (<1°) across all measurements.ConclusionAnatomical landmark and axis definitions are the main sources of variability in 3D lower-limb angular measurements, whereas plane definitions have limited impact. The substantial differences observed among commonly used femoral and tibial angle definitions underscore the need for standardized 3D measurement approaches in the assessment of lower-limb geometry.

articles.title: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Early Mother's Own Milk Feeding and Outcomes in Very Preterm Infants.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to improve mother's own milk (MoM) feeding in very preterm infants through quality improvement (QI) interventions.

METHODS: This single-center study compared three sequential periods among preterm infants born at <32 weeks of gestation or with a birth weight <1,500 g admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit at Korea University Anam Hospital, pre-QI (March 2020-February 2022), post-QI-1 (March 2022-February 2024), and post-QI-2 (March 2024-February 2025). Intervention included prenatal and postnatal maternal education using brochures and videos. Outcomes included MoM usage during the first 28 days, early colostrum administration (<72 hours), necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), duration of parenteral nutrition, and time to full enteral nutrition.

RESULTS: A total 137 very preterm infants (48 pre-QI, 40 post-QI-1, and 49 post-QI-2) were analyzed. MoM usage did not significantly differ between groups. However, early colostrum administration increased significantly (29.8% versus 77.5% versus 70.8%, p < 0.001). The incidence of NEC was decreased (16.7% versus 0% versus 4.1%, p = 0.005). Moreover, duration of parenteral nutrition (13-6 days) and time to full enteral feeding (10-6 days), duration of invasive ventilation (2-0 days), hospital stay (65-53 days), and postmenstrual age at discharge were decreased (39+4-37+4 weeks) (all p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: This QI initiative improved early colostrum administration and was associated with improvements in clinical outcomes, including NEC, despite no significant increase in overall MoM use.

articles.title: Characteristic and Outcomes of Patients With ST-Segment-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Who Have Nonsystem Reasons for Delay in Treatment: A Report from the American Heart Association GWTG-CAD Registry.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Timely treatment improves outcomes in ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction. The American Heart Association's GWTG (Get With The Guidelines) registry tracks treatment times and designates exceptions for patients with nonsystem reasons for delay (NSD). However, these exception practices limit our understanding of the impact of NSD on patient outcome and quality of care.

METHODS: We analyzed patients with ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary PCI in the GWTG-CAD (GWTG-Coronary Artery Disease) registry from January 2019 to December 2021. We examined characteristics and outcomes for patients with and without reported NSD, and classified NSD into critical (cardiac arrest, intubation, left ventricular support device) and noncritical categories. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between NSD and in-hospital mortality. We analyzed hospital ranking stability using all-patient rankings as reference, comparing current practice (all NSD excepted) versus an alternative approach (only critical NSD excepted).

RESULTS: Among 74 372 patients, 23.9% had reported NSD. Mortality was higher in patients with NSD (15.4% versus 2.7%, adjusted odds ratio [OR], 2.61 [95% CI, 2.41-2.83]), driven by critical NSD (adjusted OR, 4.61 [95% CI, 4.15-5.12]), though noncritical NSD also remained elevated (adjusted OR, 1.57 [95% CI, 1.42-1.73]). Compared with all-patient reference rankings, current exception practice was associated with ranking instability: only 71% (emergency medical services) and 69% (walk-in) of top-25% hospitals retained their status, with median ranking changes of 40 to 50 positions (ρ=0.77, 0.70). Rankings stabilized when only critical NSD were excepted (91% and 87% retention; ρ=0.95, 0.95).

CONCLUSIONS: NSD in ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction care is common and associated with higher mortality. Noncritical NSD exceptions are associated with hospital ranking instability, suggesting these exception criteria warrant refinement.

articles.title: Influenza hospitalisation: predisposing and preventive factors in the prognosis of severity outcomes via multistate modelling.
authors: PIDIRAC Severe Hospitalized Influenza Surveillance Network of Catalonia Working group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study applied a multistate model (MSM) to analyse the clinical course of severe hospitalised laboratory-confirmed influenza patients (SHLCI) and identify factors associated with transitions between states during hospitalisation assessing prognostic factors for severe outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from SHLCI cases reported by 14 hospitals of the Influenza Surveillance System of Catalonia (PIDIRAC) during the 2017-2018 season. Transitions were modelled as functions of covariates using separate Cox proportional hazards models. The MSM included six states: initial ward admission (1), transient states of intensive care unit (ICU) admission (2) and back-to-ward (3), and absorbing states of discharge home (4), transfer to a long-term care facility (5) and death (6), resulting in nine possible transitions. Covariates included sex, age, vaccination status, prior treatment, and Charlson index.

RESULTS: A total of 1306 SHLCI cases were included, 1208 patients directly admitted to the ward, 35.5% vaccinated, vs 18.6% in 98 directly admitted to ICU (p = 0.001). In ward and ICU admitted, risk of death was significantly lower in those with antiviral treatment at admission (HR< 0.3). Median sojourn times in ward, ICU, and back-to-ward were 7 (4-13), 6 (3-11), and 8 (4-14) days, respectively.

CONCLUSION: MSM effectively captured dynamics of SHLCI progression, identified factors associated with intermediate and final outcomes. This approach provides a more nuanced understanding of patient trajectories and can support tailored strategies to improve vaccine uptake, prevention, and management of influenza and other acute respiratory diseases among severely hospitalised patients during epidemic activity.

articles.title: Anatomic-Hemodynamic Discordance in Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis: A Clinical Challenge.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anatomic assessment using aortic valve calcification (AVC) and hemodynamic evaluation with dobutamine stress echocardiography are recommended to diagnose true severe low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (AS); however, concordance between methods is limited. The mean gradient (MG) to effective orifice area (EOA) ratio has recently been proposed for hemodynamic assessment, with ≥25 indicating severe AS. We aimed to evaluate concordance between anatomic and hemodynamic AS severity defined by AVC and MG/EOA.

METHODS: Patients with low-flow, low-gradient AS were stratified by MG/EOA (≥25 versus <25) and sex-specific AVC cutoffs into concordant severe (MG/EOA ≥25, high AVC), concordant nonsevere (MG/EOA <25, low AVC), discordant hemodynamic severe/anatomic nonsevere (MG/EOA ≥25, low AVC), and discordant anatomic severe/hemodynamic nonsevere (MG/EOA <25, high AVC).

RESULTS: Among 431 patients (mean age, 80±8 years; 36% women), median AVC was 1631 (interquartile range, 1156-2330) Agatston units in men and 1080 (interquartile range, 719-1553) Agatston units in women. Hemodynamic severe AS occurred in 289 (67%), and anatomic severe AS in 159 (37%). Concordant grading was observed in 243 (56%) patients. Among hemodynamic severe AS, 159 (55%) were anatomic nonsevere, and among anatomic severe AS, 29 (18%) were hemodynamic nonsevere. Across 25 combinations of AVC and MG/EOA thresholds, concordance ranged from 36.7% to 64.7% and remained below two thirds.

CONCLUSIONS: Concordance between AVC and MG/EOA is modest and remains limited across alternative thresholds, with most discordance due to hemodynamic severe/anatomic nonsevere AS. This may reflect limitations of current AVC cutoffs or indicate earlier disease detection by hemodynamic assessment, leaving optimal management of discordant patients uncertain.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Pharmacological Treatments for Resistant Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resistant hypertension substantially increases cardiovascular and renal risk, while evidence for emerging pharmacological therapies is rapidly evolving.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Embase from inception to January 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments for resistant hypertension. Primary outcomes were changes in office and 24-hour systolic blood pressure; secondary outcomes included office and 24-hour diastolic blood pressure and adverse events.

RESULTS: Thirty randomized controlled trials evaluating 18 agents in 10 446 participants were included. Spironolactone produced the greatest reduction in office systolic blood pressure (mean difference, -11.36 [95% CI, -14.97 to -7.74] mm Hg; high confidence), whereas baxdrostat produced the greatest reduction in 24-hour systolic blood pressure (mean difference, -15.81 [95% CI, -21.79 to -9.82] mm Hg; high confidence). Bisoprolol showed the greatest reduction in office diastolic blood pressure (mean difference, -6.24 [95% CI, -11.23 to -1.25] mm Hg; high confidence), while propranolol showed the greatest reduction in 24-hour diastolic blood pressure (mean difference, -8.90 [95% CI, -17.28 to -0.52] mm Hg; very low confidence). Lorundrostat reduced the odds of at least 1 adverse event versus placebo (odds ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.34-0.82]). Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists showed a relative advantage in systolic blood pressure control in subgroup analyses. Confidence ratings reflect individual comparisons rather than overall network stability.

CONCLUSIONS: Spironolactone remains the pharmacological therapy with the strongest evidence for resistant hypertension. Amiloride may be an alternative for patients intolerant of spironolactone, although evidence remains limited. β Blockers may be considered for predominant diastolic hypertension or sympathetic overactivity, but this should be interpreted cautiously given the low confidence in the evidence for 24-hour diastolic blood pressure. Aldosterone synthase inhibitors and endothelin receptor antagonists are additional therapeutic options.

articles.title: Cutaneous Adverse Reactions Associated with Modern Antidiabetic Therapies: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Modern antidiabetic therapies have transformed the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), while their expanding use has been accompanied by increasing recognition of cutaneous adverse reactions. This narrative review critically examines the dermatologic safety profiles of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) /GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide, with emphasis on the strength of evidence supporting individual drug-event associations. A targeted search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted through September 2026, encompassing clinical trials, observational and pharmacovigilance studies, systematic reviews, case series, and case reports. DPP-4 inhibitor-associated bullous pemphigoid (BP) represents the most consistently supported drug-disease association, with the strongest signals reported for vildagliptin and linagliptin. For SGLT2 inhibitors, genital mycotic infections are the best-established mucocutaneous adverse event, whereas most inflammatory and immune-mediated reactions remain supported by lower-level evidence. For GLP-1 RAs, injection-site reactions are the most well-characterized cutaneous adverse events, while rare hypersensitivity, inflammatory, and autoimmune eruptions have also been described. The cutaneous safety profile of tirzepatide remains comparatively less well characterized. Alopecia has emerged as a clinically relevant signal with semaglutide and tirzepatide, with recent pooled evidence supporting an association with non-scarring alopecia; however, causality and the contribution of rapid weight loss remain uncertain. Overall, the assessment of suspected drug-related dermatoses should consider the strength of evidence supporting the drug-event association, alternative causes, concomitant medications, and the clinical consequences of treatment withdrawal.

articles.title: Utility of apolipoprotein C3/A2 ratio for cardiovascular risk assessment in statin-treated patients following percutaneous coronary intervention.
articles.abstract: In secondary-prevention patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on LDL-lowering therapy, the clinical utility of apolipoproteins (Apos) for risk stratification remains unclear. This study investigated whether combined Apo A2 (associated with HDL metabolism) and Apo C3 (associated with triglyceride metabolism) evaluation predicts cardiovascular events.We analyzed 649 statin-treated patients undergoing PCI with drug-eluting stents for acute or chronic coronary syndrome (2016-2022) with measured serum Apo levels. Patients were categorized by median Apo A2 and Apo C3 levels into three groups: low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3; low-Apo A2 or high-Apo C3; and high-Apo A2 and low-Apo C3. During follow-up, 124 patients (19.1%) experienced major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). The low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3 group had the highest incidence (50.9% vs. 34.5% vs. 21.5%) and independently predicted MACE on multivariable Cox analysis (hazard ratio, 1.52; 95% confidence interval, 1.02-2.28). The Apo C3/Apo A2 ratio (cutoff = 0.414) was significantly associated with MACE, revascularization, and heart failure rehospitalization (log-rank p = 0.001, 0.006, and 0.003). Each 0.1 increase was associated with a 23% higher MACE risk.Among statin-treated post-PCI patients, concurrent low-Apo A2 and high-Apo C3 identified a high-risk subgroup for MACE. The Apo C3/Apo A2 ratio may serve as a novel marker for residual cardiovascular risk stratification beyond LDL-cholesterol.

articles.title: DCAF15-ANKIB1 E3 super-complex licenses NLRP3 inflammasome activation via KAT5 serine ubiquitination.
articles.abstract: Aberrant activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome is a key driver of inflammatory diseases such as sepsis. The acetyltransferase KAT5 acetylates NLRP3 and promotes the subsequent full activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, but the mechanism by which KAT5 exerts its acetyltransferase activity to acetylate NLRP3 is not well characterized. Here, we identify that the E3 ligase DCAF15 plays a critical role in positively regulating NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Specifically, DCAF15 deficiency significantly attenuates LPS-induced inflammatory response in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, DCAF15 interacts with the RBR-type E3 ligase ANKIB1 to form a complex, which promotes KAT5 ubiquitination in a Ser123-dependent manner. Accordingly, ANKIB1 knockdown significantly impairs NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Consequently, KAT5-S123A remarkably decreases NLRP3 acetylation levels and thereby reduces inflammatory responses in vitro and in vivo. Our study uncovers DCAF15‑ANKIB1‑mediated Ser123‑dependent KAT5 ubiquitination as regulator of NLRP3 acetylation and inflammasome activation.

articles.title: Cardiac PIEZO 1 Channels Modulate Anxiety.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conscious cardiac interoception explains the ability of some individuals to "feel" their heartbeat without taking their pulse. Subconscious cardiac interoception detects heart signals from baroreceptors without subjective awareness.

METHODS: We used photoplethysmography to determine if contrasting sensitivity of PIEZO 1 (human mechanosensitive stretch channels) mediates each form of cardiac interoception and feelings of anxiety.

RESULTS: In healthy volunteers, conscious cardiac interoception was increased with lower heart rates and greater stroke volumes but not associated with anxiety. Disruption of Piezo 1 (rodent mechanosensitive stretch channel) in cardiac sensory neurons enhanced anxiety in rodents. PIEZO 1 sensitivity correlated inversely with state anxiety scores in men and women (r=-0.6495, P=0.0004, n=25). Cold pressor test-induced changes in cardiac work were greater in subjects with lower PIEZO 1 sensitivity when compared with subjects with higher PIEZO 1 sensitivity (values expressed as median percentage increase in rate pressure product, 27.6 [interquartile range, 19.2-35.8] versus 8.4 [interquartile range 0.38-19.13], P=0.0093). Those with lower anxiety also had enhanced coefficients of variation in their instantaneous baroreceptor gain at rest (values expressed as medians, 1.417 [interquartile range 0.8482-1.585] versus 0.7518 interquartile range [0.5947-0.8226], P=0.0082).

CONCLUSIONS: We propose that a reduction in PIEZO 1 sensitivity causes errors in subconscious interoception and leads to anxiety and increased cardiac workloads. We also report testosterone, which is anxiolytic, enhanced, whereas the stress hormone corticosterone, decreased Piezo 1 gene transcription. Selectively enhancing subconscious interoception by increasing PIEZO 1 sensitivity may reduce anxiety and improve cardiovascular health outcomes.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Jailed Balloon-Proximal Optimization Technique Versus Jailed Wire Technique for Preventing Side Branch Occlusion During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention of True Non-Left Main Bifurcation Lesions: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The jailed balloon technique prevents side branch (SB) occlusion during coronary bifurcation stenting but is complex. We developed a jailed balloon-proximal optimization technique (JB-POT) to simplify jailed balloon technique and compared its efficacy and safety with conventional jailed wire technique (JWT) for non-left main bifurcation lesions.

METHODS: In this multicenter randomized controlled trial, 110 patients with true non-left main bifurcation lesions (Medina 1,0,1; 1,1,1; 0,1,1) were randomized to JB-POT (N=55) or JWT (N=55). The primary end point was SB occlusion rate after main vessel stenting/proximal optimization technique. Secondary end points included stent malapposition, target lesion failure (composite of cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction, and revascularization), stent thrombosis, procedure time, and contrast volume.

RESULTS: JB-POT significantly reduced SB occlusion (1.8% versus 20%; P=0.006), shortened procedure time (67 [53-85] versus 82 [62-99] minutes; P=0.009), and lowered contrast volume (140 [120-160] versus 160 [130-190] mL; P=0.002) versus JWT. Severe stent malapposition occurred in 5.5% (JB-POT) versus 0% (JWT) (P=0.242). Perioperative target lesion failure (P=0.475) and stent thrombosis (P=0.242) were comparable, but JB-POT showed a tendency for improved 12-month target lesion failure-free survival (P=0.023) and a nonsignificant trend toward reduced stent thrombosis (P=0.079). Multivariable analysis identified diabetes (odds ratio [OR], 7.26), SB ostial stenosis (OR, 1.09), balloon number (OR, 1.96), and diastolic blood pressure (OR, 1.07) as exploratory SB occlusion associates.

CONCLUSIONS: JB-POT significantly reduced SB occlusion, procedure time, and contrast volume versus JWT in non-left main bifurcation percutaneous coronary intervention, with comparable periprocedural safety. It represents a novel SB protection strategy, particularly beneficial in acute myocardial infarction, renal dysfunction, or consecutive bifurcation lesions.

articles.title: Neuroimaging Profiling of Residual Ischemic Risk in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation remains a clinical challenge, as traditional risk scores such as CHA2DS2-VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes, previous stroke or transient ischemic attack, vascular disease, age 65 to 74 years, and sex category) often fail to account for the mechanistic insights provided by brain imaging. We aimed to evaluate the comprehensive role of neuroimaging parameters in identifying residual RIS risk and to determine their incremental value over clinical scoring systems.

METHODS: In this nationwide, multicenter, prospective cohort study (East Asian Ischemic Stroke Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Study, Part II [EAST-AF]), we enrolled 2270 patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation from 14 stroke centers. We performed hierarchical profiling of magnetic resonance imaging parameters, including acute and chronic infarction characteristics and cerebral small vessel disease markers. Two-year cumulative incidences and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using cause-specific hazard models.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 431 days, 123 patients experienced RIS (2-year cumulative incidence, 5.6%). The 2-year cumulative incidence of RIS was significantly higher in patients with chronic nonlacunar infarction (7.3% versus 4.6%; aHR, 1.50 [95% CI, 1.01-2.23]) and lacunes (9.0% versus 4.7%; aHR, 1.91 [95% CI, 1.28-2.86]). Mechanistically, lacunes in medullary artery territories, indicative of embolic sources, significantly increased RIS risk (aHR, 2.65 [95% CI, 1.56-4.49]), whereas those in deep perforator territories did not (aHR, 1.54 [95% CI, 0.94-2.53]). Notably, adding these neuroimaging markers to the CHA2DS2-VASc score significantly improved the model's discriminative ability, increasing the C statistic from 0.53 to 0.63 (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Comprehensive neuroimaging profiling, particularly focusing on embolic-pattern markers such as chronic infarctions and medullary lacunes, is essential for identifying high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation who may require intensified secondary prevention. Our findings suggest that imaging-based risk stratification provides critical prognostic information beyond conventional clinical scores.

articles.title: Impact of Guideline-Based Indications on Outcomes in Asymptomatic Patients With Severe Aortic Stenosis: Insights From the AVATAR Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is unknown whether current class IIa recommendations correctly identify asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis who derive enhanced benefit from aortic valve replacement (AVR). We investigated whether the presence of a class IIa recommendation per European Society of Cardiology guidelines for AVR at the time of randomization affected the outcome of patients enrolled in the AVATAR (Aortic Valve Replacement Versus Conservative Treatment in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis) trial.

METHODS: The AVATAR trial population included 157 patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis who were randomized to early AVR (n=78) or conservative management (n=79). The primary outcome comprised all-cause mortality or major adverse cardiovascular events composed of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, and unplanned heart failure hospitalization, which was compared between groups using a stratified proportional hazards model.

RESULTS: Among AVATAR trial population (mean age, 67 years; 43% women), 62 patients (39.5%) had a class IIa recommendation for AVR at the time of enrollment. The primary composite outcome was more frequent in patients with a class IIa indication for AVR versus those without a guideline indication (46.8% versus 27.4%; P=0.010). In stratified analyses, the benefit of early AVR was consistent among patients with a class IIa guideline recommendation at baseline (hazard ratio [HR], 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-1.00]) and among patients without a class IIa guideline recommendation (HR, 0.29 [95% CI, 0.12-0.73]; P-interaction=0.389).

CONCLUSIONS: Asymptomatic patients with severe aortic stenosis and with a class IIa indication for AVR had worse long-term outcomes compared with patients without a class IIa indication at the time of randomization. There is no evidence that presence of a class IIa indication modified the benefit of early AVR.

articles.title: Ibn Sīnā's description of stroke (c. 1025), one thousand years ago.
articles.journal: Journal of the history of the neurosciences
articles.abstract: Medieval descriptions of stroke are routinely omitted from contemporary historical commentaries on cerebrovascular disease. With few exceptions, the current narrative of advances passes seamlessly from Greco-Roman to early modern times, with almost no consideration given to voices in the intervening centuries. But such accounts of the history of stroke medicine are at best incomplete.
