As a case in point, we revisit a millennium-old description of stroke given in Ibn Sīnā's (c. 980-1037) celebrated eleventh-century medical encyclopedia, the al-Qānūn fī al-ṭibb (Avicenna's Canon of Medicine), completed around 1025. Reexamining a rare handwritten 1276 copy of the original Arabic text, we provide the first published translation into English of the section on stroke ("al-Saktah"; السكتة) to be derived from a preprint era manuscript. Within the humoralist medical framework of his time, Ibn Sīnā provided highly accurate descriptions of the clinical signs and symptoms of stroke, noted the occurrence of ventricular hemorrhage, and explicitly stated (possibly for the first time) a vascular etiology of stroke (understood as brain dysfunction) in the form of arterial (including carotid) occlusion. Future histories of cerebrovascular disease ought to include Ibn Sīnā's significant contribution to the canon of stroke medicine.

articles.title: Visualizing Hidden Cellular Consequences of Infection by a Minimal Genome Virus.
articles.abstract: Circoviruses represent an extreme of genome compression among animal viruses and infect diverse vertebrate hosts, including humans. Porcine circovirus 2 (PCV2) combines an exceptionally compact genome, well-established pathogenicity, and routine propagation in cultured cells, making it a practical model for studying minimal-genome virus infection. Here, we engineered a compact tetracysteine (TC)-FlAsH reporter by optimizing TC placement and configuration within the PCV2 capsid. The resulting PCV2-TC remained replication competent and enabled direct visualization and longitudinal tracking of infected cells. The reporter resolved apoptosis-associated fate transitions in living cells and enabled ultrastructural analysis of reporter-positive cells. It further uncovered Annexin V and propidium iodide (PI)-defined cell states that were masked in population-level analysis. Together, this system establishes PCV2 as a tractable minimal-genome model for directly linking infection to cell fate and revealing cellular consequences otherwise obscured in bulk populations.

articles.title: Data-Driven Subtyping of Type 2 Diabetes Identifies Two Fracture-Risk Subtypes Along a Disease-Severity Continuum.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with elevated osteoporotic fracture risk, which is underestimated by the Fracture Risk Assessment Tool (FRAX). This excess risk is heterogeneous across patients. The aim of this study is to identify clinically meaningful fracture-risk subtypes in T2DM using unsupervised clustering and evaluate their risk characteristics.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort enrolled 1876 hospitalized adults with T2DM at Ruijin Hospital (2009-2013). Fracture events were verified via electronic medical records and telephone follow-up; 1730 patients completed follow-up (median 10 years). K-means clustering was conducted with nine routine clinical variables. Cluster stability was assessed by bootstrap resampling and internal training/testing validation. Association of subtypes with fracture risk was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses treating death as a competing event. FRAX 10-year MOF probabilities were calculated with and without femoral neck BMD and assessed for calibration by the expected/observed (E/O) ratio, with the 10-year competing-risk MOF cumulative incidence as the observed risk.

RESULTS: Two subtypes were identified: a low-risk subtype (n = 1085, 62.7%) and a high-risk subtype (n = 645, 37.3%). The high-risk phenotype was characterized by older age, longer diabetes duration, markedly higher prevalence of peripheral neuropathy and microvascular complications, alongside elevated risks of major osteoporotic, hip and rib fractures. Associations remained significant with death treated as a competing risk. Subtype assignments were highly stable and reproduced significant risk separation in a held-out validation set. The E/O ratio in the high-risk subtype was approximately half that of the low-risk subtype, indicating substantially greater underestimation of fracture risk by FRAX in high-risk subtype. Conventional FRAX adjustment strategies only partially alleviated calibration bias and performed suboptimally in high-risk patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Significant heterogeneity in fracture susceptibility exists among T2DM patients. The high-risk subtype defined by clustering exhibits excess fracture burden and greater FRAX miscalibration. These exploratory findings require external validation in independent cohorts to evaluate stratified risk adjustment incorporating diabetes-related complications.

articles.title: Genetics-First Multi-Omic Triangulation Prioritizes Druggable Targets for Complementary Metabolic Traits.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The genetic regulation of beta-cell function, glycaemic control and insulin action remains incompletely resolved. We sought to prioritize druggable gene-expression targets for these complementary metabolic traits.

METHODS: We integrated the Finan druggable genome with eQTLGen and performed cis-eQTL Mendelian randomization across 15 metabolic traits. Exploratory cross-axis annotation and colocalization of outcome-wise false-discovery-rate (FDR)-positive associations were conducted independently. Candidate genes were evaluated using summary-data-based MR (SMR) with heterogeneity testing across six tissues, pancreatic single-cell transcriptomics, cellular stress-expression assays, Cry2-siRNA experiments with protein-normalized insulin secretion, protein networks and pharmacological mapping. Sensitivity analyses examined multiple testing, intervention directions, colocalization priors, conditional signals and donor covariates.

RESULTS: Quality control retained 1808 genes and 35 531 gene-variant instruments. The exploratory cross-axis analysis identified 70 genes. Separately, colocalization of 1015 FDR-positive associations identified 18 genes, of which 10 had high-confidence tissue SMR support. Six were retained as core candidates: inhibition of CRY2, AGER and ITIH3 and activation of MPI, mTOR and ITGB2. Each had at least one favourable association after global Bonferroni correction, although nominal phenotype directions and colocalization-prior robustness varied. Covariate-adjusted single-cell analyses did not establish differential-expression confirmation. Stress-expression changes were compatible with five proposed intervention directions; MPI was not significant. In MIN6 cells exposed to glucolipotoxicity, Cry2-siRNA treatment was associated with higher stimulated insulin secretion (109.90 vs. 67.11 ng/μg protein; adjusted p < 0.01). Pharmacological mapping yielded no high-confidence novel disease-modifying candidate.

CONCLUSIONS: The evidence prioritizes six candidates with different strengths and limitations for metabolic-trait research. Cry2-siRNA treatment was associated with improved stimulated secretion in stressed MIN6 cells, supporting further functional investigation. These results do not establish clinical remission, tissue-specific mediation or therapeutic efficacy.

articles.title: Bimetallic Sites Cu/Co Alloy Targeting Quorum Sensing Reversing MRSA Ciprofloxacin Susceptibility.
articles.abstract: The escalating global prevalence of infections caused by resistant pathogens emerge as a critical public health crisis, especially in implants. It underscores urgent imperative to advance novel and efficacious strategies combating antimicrobial resistance. Herein, Cu-bearing cobalt-based (CoCrMo-Cu) alloys with bimetallic active sites (Cu/Co) are designed to effectively restore methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) sensitivity to ciprofloxacin, the most representative resistant antibiotic against MRSA. By combining CoCrMo-Cu with ciprofloxacin, proposing a synergistic dual-action platform addressing MRSA-infected osteomyelitis. Results show that CoCrMo-Cu exhibit anti-infection through two-stage process: disrupting biofilm, the extrinsic physical resistance barrier. Specifically, real-time bacterial motility trajectories reveal CoCrMo-Cu disrupt bacterial initial exploration behaviors, inhibiting biofilm development. Second, inhibiting intrinsic resistance barrier: efflux systems, enhancing effectiveness of antibiotics. Such comprehensive anti-infective mechanism is attributed to quorum quenching through satisfactory reactive oxygen species generation from bimetallic active sites. Eventually, MRSA resistance to ciprofloxacin is reversed and it results in an 87.5% reduction of minimum inhibitory concentration for ciprofloxacin. CoCrMo-Cu combining with ciprofloxacin significantly eradicates MRSA-infected osteomyelitis in vivo. Unlike stop-gap solutions focus on developing novel antibiotics, we prioritize restoring MRSA susceptibility to conventional antibiotics, providing a long-term strategy addressing resistant bacterial infection with enhanced sustainability.

articles.title: Body Fat Distribution and Diabetes in Young and Middle-Aged Adults: Evidence From NHANES 2011-2018.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the relationships between regional fat mass (RFM) and fat percentage (RFP) in different body areas and associations with prevalent diabetes mellitus (DM) in young and middle-aged adults, and to evaluate whether RFM-based indicators outperform traditional obesity metrics for discriminating prevalent DM.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study analysed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011-2018 (n = 10 158; aged 20-59 years). We assessed head, arm, trunk and leg fat mass and percentage measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Restricted cubic splines and multivariate logistic regression were used to examine associations with DM. Discriminative performance was compared using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Body shapes were redefined using the upper-to-lower (U/L) fat ratio ([AFM+TFM]/LFM).

RESULTS: Higher fat in the head, arms and trunk was positively associated with DM, while leg fat showed an inverse association with prevalent DM. Compared with traditional indicators, RFM demonstrated superior discrimination for prevalent DM in the 2017-2018 subsample (AUC = 0.794 vs. BMI = 0.663, WC = 0.694, WHtR = 0.706, WHR = 0.724) with consistent superiority across the full 2011-2018 sample (RFM = 0.79 vs. BMI = 0.70, WC = 0.73, WHtR = 0.73). Each 1-unit increase in the U/L fat ratio was associated with a 4.41-fold increase in the odds of DM (OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 3.63-5.83). In the unadjusted model, the predicted probability of DM was 6.9% at a U/L fat ratio of 1.7 (median) and 19.7% at 2.3. An exploratory web-based RFM probability estimator was developed to illustrate individual probability estimation.

CONCLUSIONS: Body fat distribution, particularly the U/L fat ratio and RFM-based models, shows stronger cross-sectional associations with prevalent DM than traditional obesity indicators in young and middle-aged adults. These findings support increased research emphasis on fat distribution, rather than overall obesity, in future research on fat distribution and prevalent DM.

articles.title: 3-D Ultrasound as a new indicator for Optic Nerve Sheath Volume.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Traditional 2-D ultrasonographic measurement of the optic nerve sheath diameter has been utilized to estimate intra-cranial pressure but limitations remain, underscoring the need for more advanced imaging approaches. This study aimed to use 3-D ultrasound to determine the normative range of internal optic nerve sheath volume (ONSV) in healthy adults and identify potential factors influencing ONSV.

METHODS: A total of 69 healthy participants (26 males, 43 females) were included, with 3-D ultrasound of the optic nerve sheath performed for each participant. Each observer performed ONSV measurements twice, and all measurements were independently completed by two investigators to calculate intra- and inter-observer reliabilities.

RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 47.32 ± 15.08 y (range: 19-75 y), with a mean body mass index of 23.76 ± 4.26 kg/m². The average ONSV was 0.028 ± 0.006 mm³ (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.027-0.029 mm³), with no significant difference observed between the left and right eyes (p > 0.05). Simple linear regression analysis revealed no significant correlations between ONSV and age, sex, body mass index or waistline (all p > 0.05). The intra-observer reliability was 0.939 (95% CI, 0.910-0.967, p < 0.001), with an inter-observer reliability of 0.883 (95% CI, 0.816-0.926, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: 3-D ultrasound provides a reliable, non-invasive technique to assess ONSV. The normative ONSV range established in this study offers a foundation for future clinical applications, particularly in the non-invasive monitoring of elevated intra-cranial pressure.

articles.title: Elevated ATP-Citrate Lyase Links Hyperglycemic Metabolism to Maternal Diabetes-Induced Neural Tube Defects.
articles.abstract: The pathogenesis of neural tube defects (NTDs) precipitated by maternal diabetes mellitus (DM) encompasses a cascade of intricate cellular processes, prominently featuring excessive apoptosis. The critical metabolic mediators bridging hyperglycemic metabolism to apoptotic pathways remain unidentified, particularly in human contexts. Elevated expression of ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY), a metabolic enzyme catalyzing the synthesis of acetyl-CoA from glucose, was discerned in cranial neural tube exposed to maternal diabetes. Inhibition of ACLY effectively normalized hyperglycemia-induced augmented levels of acetyl-CoA and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac). ACLY inhibitor hydroxycitric acid (HCA) mitigated the elevated acetyl-CoA and H3K27ac levels and reduced the incidence of NTDs caused by maternal diabetes. Integrated analyses of H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation (CHIP)-seq and RNA-seq data unveiled a correlation between aberrant H3K27ac occupancy and genome-wide gene dysregulation. The most upregulated gene, thioredoxin-interacting protein (Txnip) coupled with downstream phosphorylation of ASK1 and heightened apoptosis, was prominently observed in cranial neural tube with maternal diabetes, which can be attenuated by inhibition of ACLY. Corroborative evidence from human subjects with diabetes-associated NTDs substantiated this pathogenicity. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of ACLY in linking hyperglycemic metabolism to NTDs, highlighting the potential prophylactic utility of HCA supplementation in preventing maternal diabetes-induced public health issues.

articles.title: Six Years after the Storm: Drawing the First Line on COVID-19 and Parkinson's Disease.
articles.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
articles.abstract: Six years after the SARS-CoV-2 outbreak, we revisit the fear of a post-COVID parkinsonism wave, echoing encephalitis lethargica after the 1918 pandemic, through two questions. First, is the infection a risk factor for de novo Parkinson's disease (PD)? Epidemiology reveals no robust signal, yet pathological, imaging, and experimental evidence shows the virus targets the olfactory-brainstem axis, sustains neuroinflammation, promotes α-synuclein aggregation, and leaves a dopaminergic footprint. We hypothesize an inflammation-driven, rather than directly cytopathic, mechanism in vulnerable individuals, with persistent post-COVID hyposmia as a candidate risk marker. As the PD prodrome outlasts available follow-up, this question remains open. Second, does infection alter the trajectory of established PD? Motor and non-motor worsening during and shortly after COVID-19 is consistently demonstrated. However, accelerated neurodegeneration remains unproven. Neither alarm nor reassurance is warranted, but long-term, prospective, harmonized cohorts enriched for hyposmia and characterized with α-synuclein seed amplification assays, neurofilament light chain, and dopamine transporter imaging are needed. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

articles.title: Therapeutic Potential of Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation in Central Nervous System Diseases: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), a patterned repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation technique, modulates cortical excitability and induces neuroplasticity rapidly. Recently, iTBS has garnered considerable attention for its application in multiple central nervous system disorders. Its effects extend beyond local neuronal changes, propagating across synaptic plasticity, glial responses, neurovascular-immune microenvironment, subcellular homeostasis, and large-scale neural networks, though existing mechanistic evidence remains fragmented. Heterogeneous study designs, varying disease models, stimulation targets, parameters, and observation points, contribute to inconsistent findings. Most research only establishes correlations between iTBS and molecular, cellular, or network changes, failing to confirm causal sequences or cross-level relationships. This review synthesizes evidence from stroke, spinal cord injury, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and depression and anxiety-related disorders, analyzing shared and disease-specific mechanisms across biological levels. This review identifies limitations in causal evidence and dose-response characterization and proposes a multilevel framework for interpreting the reported biological effects of iTBS, with the aim of informing future clinical translation and the optimization of disease-specific stimulation strategies.

articles.title: Testosterone therapy and anabolic steroid use: why cardiovascular risk discussions must separate the two.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular discussions about testosterone often combine exposures that differ in indication, formulation, dose, duration, and concomitant drug use. Appropriately indicated testosterone replacement, prescribing without adequate diagnostic confirmation, nonprescribed testosterone, and multi-agent androgen regimens should not be treated as interchangeable. This Perspective article proposes an exposure-based framework that distinguishes therapeutic evidence from studies of nonmedical use and experimental mechanisms. Randomized trials provide reassurance about major adverse cardiovascular events within the populations and observation periods studied, but do not establish lifelong safety or equivalence across formulations. The atrial fibrillation finding in TRAVERSE requires separate consideration of its absolute and relative magnitude. Conversely, imaging and cohort studies associate nonmedical androgen use with ventricular dysfunction and cardiovascular disease, although they do not provide a direct quantitative comparison with replacement therapy. Low endogenous testosterone and metabolic disease also require balanced interpretation: association does not establish that treatment prevents cardiovascular events. More precise terminology, realistic clinical assessment, and longitudinal exposure documentation can improve both patient care and research without minimizing either inappropriate prescribing or the harms of nonmedical androgen use.

articles.title: Correction to "Small Strokes, Big Impact: Excessive Mortality After Acute Ischemic Stroke in Parkinson's Disease".
articles.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

articles.title: Balancing Trained Immunity and Tolerance: Innate Immunity Crossroads in COVID-19 Vaccination.
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has underscored the critical role of immune responses in determining disease severity, with SARS-CoV-2 infection triggering both protective and pathological reactions. While adaptive immunity (mediated by neutralizing antibodies and memory T cells) has been the primary focus of vaccination strategies, emerging evidence highlights the importance of innate immune adaptation, a spectrum of states ranging from trained immunity, in which innate immune cells undergo epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, enhancing rapid, broad-spectrum antiviral defenses, to innate immune tolerance, in which persistent stimulation renders the same cells hyporesponsive. In this review, we frame SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19 vaccination as opposing forces along this training-tolerance continuum, and we distinguish three levels of evidence: persistent epigenetic and metabolic marks, altered responses to a secondary challenge, and demonstrable effects on clinical outcomes. We discuss how pattern recognition receptors initiate antiviral responses, how metabolic reprogramming influences immune cell behavior, and how trained immunity extends beyond leukocytes to airway epithelial and endothelial cells. Trained immunity inducers, such as Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccination, show promise in preclinical studies but yield mixed clinical results, highlighting the challenges of translating innate immune modulation into therapeutic benefits. We further examine how SARS-CoV-2 itself can act as a natural inducer of trained immunity, how maladaptive resolution of this program may contribute to long COVID, and why only a subset of infected individuals develops post-acute sequelae. Finally, we consider the post-pandemic immunological landscape, including immune debt and the resurgence of unrelated infections due to reduced microbial exposure, and the lessons these hold for vaccines against future emerging respiratory viruses. Future vaccination strategies should aim to promote context-appropriate innate antiviral responses while limiting maladaptive inflammatory persistence, integrating innate immune regulation with durable adaptive protection against SARS-CoV-2 and emerging respiratory pathogens.

articles.title: TNF Inhibition Plus Corticosteroids vs Corticosteroids Alone for Epidermal Necrolysis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis are rare, life-threatening drug reactions. The randomized tumor necrosis factor inhibitor trial compared etanercept with corticosteroids rather than testing adjunctive use, leaving the add-on strategy unresolved.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the benefits and harms of adding tumor necrosis factor inhibition to systemic corticosteroids versus systemic corticosteroids alone.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched through July 18, 2026 for comparative studies. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias and certainty; random-effects meta-analysis was used when outcomes were sufficiently comparable.

RESULTS: Five reports were eligible; 4 core nonrandomized cohorts included 296 patients. Reported early disease-control landmarks were approximately 1 to 2 days earlier with adjunctive treatment but were not pooled because definitions and time origins differed. Among 109 TNF inhibitor-treated patients, 64 received adalimumab, 15 etanercept, and 30 an unreported agent and dose. Study-defined post-treatment infection occurred in 16/109 vs 57/187 patients (unadjusted risk ratio, 0.47; 95% confidence interval, 0.21-1.05). Complete-healing times were numerically earlier with adjunctive treatment in all 3 reporting core studies but were not pooled because time origins were not sufficiently aligned or reported. Severe TEN was sparsely represented, and no deaths occurred among 226 patients with reported mortality, limiting inference for high-risk disease. Ocular-specific effects and mortality were not estimable. Certainty was very low.

CONCLUSION: Earlier disease-control signals without an observed short-term infection excess support prospective evaluation of adjunctive tumor necrosis factor inhibition, but the evidence is nonrandomized, very low certainty, and vulnerable to residual confounding; complete healing, ocular benefit, and survival remain uncertain.

articles.title: Parasitic Infections as Upstream Drivers of the Gut-Kidney Axis: Dysbiosis, Uremic Toxin Generation, and Renal Injury - A Comprehensive Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The intestinal dysbiosis-renal axis works in both directions: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and acute kidney injury (AKI) lead to gut dysbiosis, loss of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and buildup of uremic toxins. This comprehensive narrative review (assessed using SANRA) inspects parasitic infections as upstream factors that disrupt the intestinal barrier and microbiota, thereby causing renal injury. To address dysbiosis-parasite-CKD interactions, therapies, and research gaps, literature from 2015-2026 was searched in Google Scholar, PubMed/MEDLINE, EKB, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. The results were divided into nine themes: Theme 1: Diverse gut dysbiosis was observed among different parasites; for example, Strongyloides stercoralis infection in CKD patients expanded Escherichia-Shigella, Actinomyces, Rothia, Aggregatibacter, and Haemophilus while depleting the SCFA-producing Anaerostipes and Coprococcus, and the expanded Escherichia-Shigella inversely correlated with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Theme 2: Parasites can disrupt the mucosal barrier of the intestine directly by downregulating tight- and adherens-junction proteins (claudin-3/4, occludin, ZO-1, E-cadherin) and inducing epithelial apoptosis, and indirectly through tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα)/interleukin (IL)-1β and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) inflammatory signaling. Theme 3: Parasitic infections can deplete SCFA-producing bacteria and increase tryptophan production; the liver converts the resulting precursors into the protein-bound uremic toxins indoxyl sulfate (IS), p-cresyl sulfate (pCS), and trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO); however, parasites' direct generation of these toxins remains uninvestigated. Theme 4: The link between environmental enteric dysfunction (EED) due to parasitic diseases and renal injury remains unidentified. Theme 5: The kinetics of immunomodulatory helminthic metabolites remain unclear: helminth-derived ES-62 showed renoprotection in lupus nephritis models, yet whether these metabolites are renoprotective or unexpectedly trigger fibrosis through transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) remains unresolved. Theme 6: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a merging point of immune pathogenesis in both parasitic diseases and renal injury; it is activated by parasite-derived pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) such as hemozoin and lipophosphoglycan; however, T. gondii suppresses NLRP3 by hindering the NF-κB pathway. Theme 7: The impact of parasitic diseases on TMAO production hasn't been tested, although elevated TMAO independently predicts rapid eGFR decline and drives tubulointerstitial fibrosis through NLRP3, PERK/Akt/mTOR, and NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) signaling. Theme 8: Albendazole, pro/synbiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and helminth metabolites may correct dysbiosis and reduce renal injury, which might make combined antiparasitic and microecological therapies a cost-effective renoprotective strategy in endemic areas. Theme 9: Research gaps on the intestinal parasites-dysbiosis-renal axis were introduced, with proposed study designs. This first comprehensive review highlights parasitic infections as upstream drivers in the intestinal-renal axis that initiate or accelerate CKD/AKI via gut barrier disruption and uremic toxin accumulation. If validated, combining antiparasitic and microecological therapies provides an affordable renoprotective strategy for endemic, low-resource settings.

articles.title: Causes of First-week Mortality in Slower- and Fast-Growing Danish Broilers.
articles.abstract: Demand for slow-growing broilers in Europe is rising due to welfare concerns about rapid growth. First-week mortality (FWM), caused by infections and non-infectious factors, affects flock health. Data on slower-growing strains regarding FWM are limited. This study described first-week causes of death in commercial Danish broilers and included secondary exploratory comparisons among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD flocks. The study involved three rotations per farm/group (36 flocks, excluding three) and examined causes of death through necropsies of 2,022 dead chicks, with bacteriological examination performed in chicks with suspected infection. Of the recorded causes of death, 47% were classified as non-infectious and 53% as infectious based on predefined diagnostic criteria; individual chicks could have more than one recorded cause. The five most common causes of FWM, listed by frequency, were sepsis, cardiovascular collapse, renal disorders, leg disorders, and navel and yolk sac infection. No statistically significant differences were detected among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD in FWM proportions (all Tukey-adjusted p ≥ 0.207), causes of death, or related lesions (all overall BH-adjusted p-values ≥ 0.085). The most common bacterial species isolated across all organs of broiler chicks were Escherichia coli (62.4%) and Enterococcus faecalis (22.8%). In conclusion, exploratory comparisons under the commercial conditions evaluated detected no statistically significant differences in first-week mortality or recorded causes of death among Rustic Gold, Ross 308-LD, and Ross 308-HD flocks.

articles.title: Clinical Efficacy of Cordycepin in Feline Upper Respiratory Infection: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Presenting predominantly with upper airway, oral, and ocular anomalies, feline upper respiratory infection (FURI) is highly pervasive among cat populations. Given its substantial morbidity and tendency to trigger severe secondary conditions like pneumonia, it persists as a formidable hurdle in feline medicine. We investigated the therapeutic impact of cordycepin, a major active component of Cordyceps militaris, on the clinical progression and physiological recovery of cats with FURI. Our data revealed that oral administration of cordycepin over 14 days significantly mitigated respiratory symptoms, reduced systemic inflammation, re-established redox equilibrium and regulated the relative abundance of various bacteria, specifically a substantial reduction in the relative abundance of Staphylococcus. Metagenomic analysis and correlation Analysis with host defense factors further highlighted that the decline in Staphylococcus was significantly associated with increased levels of host defense factors, including IgA, CAT, and GSH-Px, as well as lower clinical scores. Collectively, cordycepin confers multi-faceted protection by synergistically dampening inflammation, mitigating oxidative stress, bolstering host immunity, and modulating microbial ecosystems. These findings underscore its translational potential, positioning cordycepin as a highly viable and promising therapeutic candidate for the clinical management of feline upper respiratory infections.

articles.title: DNA barcoding and cellular senescence in atherosclerosis: Vascular smooth muscle cell lineage tracing and potential for future Senotherapeutics.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and substantial risk persists even with optimal preventive therapy. Cellular senescence is a state of growth arrest accompanied by a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and has emerged as a candidate driver of vascular disease states. Recently, vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) have moved from passive bystanders in vascular diseases, including atherosclerosis, to pivotal cells integral to many facets of plaque biology. Within the lesion microenvironment, VSMCs undergo phenotypic switching and de-differentiation into macrophage-like, osteogenic, fibromyocyte, and senescent states, frequently extinguishing canonical lineage markers. However, defining the independent contribution of senescent VSMCs is complicated by two converging problems: the absence of a universal, specific senescence marker, and the loss of identity that accompanies VSMC trans-differentiation. We argue that DNA barcoding, a high-resolution, marker-independent lineage-tracing strategy matured in hematology and oncology, can address both obstacles. Building on the established foundation of multicolor reporters, we contrast static high-diversity libraries with evolving CRISPR-Cas9 recorders and human-translatable retrospective approaches, emphasizing that barcoding reports clonal lineage and must be paired with single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to position the senescent state on a reconstructed clonal tree. We further appraise emerging senotherapeutics, whose inconsistent and occasionally harmful in vivo results reflect a failure to identify the target cell rather than a failure of pharmacology. This distinction argues for lineage-restricted targeting. Integrating clonal barcoding, spatial multi-omics, and senescence atlases may help resolve the role of VSMC senescence in atherogenesis and enable cell-state-specific therapy.

articles.title: Response to 'Methodological concerns regarding the prognostic interpretation of contralateral FDG-avid cervical lymph nodes in lateralized oral and oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma'.
articles.journal: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery

articles.title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

METHODS: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.

RESULTS: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).

CONCLUSION: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.

articles.title: Ai-enabled type 2 diabetes research: A bibliometric analysis of research trends, knowledge structure, and emerging frontiers.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly applied to type 2 diabetes (T2D) for risk prediction, complication assessment, and personalized management. However, the global development patterns and thematic evolution of AI-enabled T2D research remain unclear. This paper conducted a bibliometric analysis of 611 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection spanning the period from 2000 to 2025, using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. Publication trends, geographical contributions, citation clustering, and thematic evolution were systematically analyzed. Results showed that AI-enabled T2D research experienced three developmental stages, with rapid growth after 2018. China and the United States were the leading contributors, accounting for over 60 % of publications. Highly cited publications indicated that risk prediction has become a major research focus. Co-citation analysis revealed a progressive knowledge structure linking practical needs, methodological foundations, clinical evidence, and technological implementation. Thematic evolution demonstrated a shift from prediction-oriented applications toward deep learning, heterogeneous clinical data, biomarkers, explainable AI, and clinically oriented risk assessment. This review summarizes AI-enabled T2D research and analyzes future directions, providing references for clinical practice.

articles.title: Clinical obesity phenotypes and heterogeneity in Site-Specific cancer Risk: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The Lancet Diabetes and Endocrinology Commission framework distinguishes preclinical from clinical obesity based on obesity-related organ dysfunction and functional impairment. We aimed to identify clinical obesity phenotypes and examine their associations with overall and site-specific cancers.

METHODS: We included 322,710 UK Biobank participants enrolled in 2006-2010 and followed through December 2022. Clinical obesity was defined as excess adiposity with obesity-related organ dysfunction or functional limitations. Latent class analysis derived phenotypes, and multivariate Cox models estimated associations with overall, obesity-related, and site-specific cancers. Site-specific heterogeneity was evaluated among participants with excess adiposity using preclinical obesity as reference.

RESULTS: Clinical obesity affected 73,536 (22.8%) participants: 44,926 (13.9%) had musculoskeletal-dominant, 22,325 (6.9%) cardiometabolic-multisystem, and 6,285 (1.9%) functional limitation-dominant obesity. During 11.79 years' median follow-up, 32,040 developed cancer. Compared with no obesity, preclinical and clinical obesity phenotypes had higher overall (hazard ratios [HRs], 1.10-1.16) and obesity-related cancer risks (HRs, 1.22-1.32), highest for cardiometabolic-multisystem obesity. Among participants with excess adiposity, heterogeneity was observed for kidney, thyroid, lung, and bladder cancers, with distinct phenotype-specific associations.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical obesity phenotypes showed modest overall cancer-risk differences but marked site-specific heterogeneity, suggesting that organ dysfunction and functional limitations may distinguish cancer susceptibility beyond adiposity alone.

articles.title: Combined Neuromelanin-Sensitive and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Links Midbrain Dopaminergic Dysfunction to Connectome Architecture in First-Episode, Medication-Naïve Major Depressive Disorder.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence implicates dopaminergic dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet direct evidence of such dysfunction and of its altered coupling with the functional connectome remains limited.

METHODS: Using neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) and resting-state fMRI, we examined differences in substantia nigra/ventral tegmental area NM-MRI signal (NMSSN/VTA) between first-episode, medication-naïve MDD patients (n = 112) and healthy controls (HC; n = 230). Network-based statistics (NBS) assessed MDD-related alterations in NMSSN/VTA-functional connectivity (FC) coupling. Spatial correspondence analyses examined the spatial convergence of these coupling alterations with normative dopaminergic molecular maps and anhedonia-related connectome patterns in MDD.

RESULTS: Patients with MDD showed lower NMSSN/VTA, with more pronounced reductions in lateral and rostral regions. NBS identified a widespread component with altered NMSSN/VTA-FC coupling in MDD, characterized predominantly by higher slopes across attention, control, sensory, and medial temporal systems and lower slopes involving limbic-striatal and default-mode connections. Network-level analysis further identified a diagnosis-dependent NMSSN/VTA-striatal-limbic connectivity relationship, with lower NMSSN/VTA associated with higher FC in MDD. Spatially, these coupling alterations converged with dopaminergic molecular architecture, showing negative correspondence with normative dopaminergic receptor and transporter distributions and positive correspondence with the anticipatory-pleasure-related connectome pattern in MDD.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide in vivo evidence of midbrain dopaminergic dysfunction and widespread disruption of dopaminergic-connectome coupling in MDD, with these coupling alterations spatially converging with anhedonia-related connectome organization. Together, these findings advance our understanding of the role of dopaminergic dysfunction in the pathophysiology of MDD.

articles.title: International Nosocomial Infection Control Consortium (INICC) report of healthcare-associated infections, data summary of 44 countries for 2017-2022, Adult and Pediatric Units, Device-associated Module.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We report International Nosocomial Infection Control Consortium (INICC) data from 2017 to 2022 on 499 intensive care units (ICUs) in 44 countries across Asia, Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East.

METHODS: Prospective ICU patient data were collected via the INICC Surveillance Online System. CDC/NHSN definitions were applied to device-associated healthcare-associated infections (DA-HAIs).

RESULTS: We collected data on 274,653 patients, 1,685,152 patient-days, 794,473 central line (CL)-days, 576,956 mechanical ventilator (MV)-days, and 1,024,993 urinary catheter (UC)-days. We identified 3,001 CL-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSI), 4,623 ventilator-associated pneumonias (VAP), and 2,829 UC-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI). Combined DA-HAI rates were 3.81 per 100 patients and 6.20 per 1,000 patient-days. CLABSI occurred at 3.78 per 1,000 CL-days, VAP at 8.01 per 1,000 MV-days, and CAUTI at 2.76 per 1,000 UC-days. Resistance reached 72.9% to ceftriaxone and 58.6% to imipenem in Klebsiella pneumoniae; 75.8% to cefotaxime in Escherichia coli; 42.9% to ceftazidime and 55.1% to imipenem in Pseudomonas aeruginosa; and 88.3% to piperacillin-tazobactam and 88.5% to imipenem in Acinetobacter spp. Methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus was 45.3% and vancomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis 8.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: DA-HAI rates were 2.1 to 7.3 times CDC/NHSN pooled means, and bacterial resistance was high, supporting continued prevention.

articles.title: Type 3 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease: Linking brain insulin resistance to amyloid-β, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, and emerging biomarkers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a modifiable risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD). The term "Type 3 diabetes" has been proposed to describe brain insulin resistance and impaired insulin signaling as potential links between metabolic dysfunction and neurodegeneration.

OBJECTIVE: This review examines the relationship between brain insulin resistance, AD-related pathology, and emerging biomarkers.

METHODS: Evidence concerning insulin signaling, amyloid-β (Aβ), tau pathology, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier disruption, and biomarkers was synthesized. This review considers mechanistic findings alongside observational and interventional evidence, while recognizing that evidence strength and causal interpretation vary across study designs. Particular attention was given to Aβ, total tau, phosphorylated tau, neurofilament light chain (NfL), glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), inflammatory mediators, extracellular vesicles, and microRNAs.

RESULTS: Impaired insulin receptor substrate-1 (IRS-1)-PI3K/Akt signaling may increase glycogen synthase kinase-3β activity, impair Aβ clearance, and promote tau hyperphosphorylation. Neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, blood-brain barrier alterations, and synaptic injury may further contribute to neurodegeneration. Emerging blood-based biomarkers, including phosphorylated tau, GFAP, NfL, extracellular vesicles, and microRNAs, show potential for minimally invasive assessment of AD-related pathology and disease monitoring. However, these markers differ in their biological significance and clinical validation.

CONCLUSION: Brain insulin resistance may represent one contributing mechanism within the multifactorial pathophysiology of AD, rather than a complete explanation of the disease. Integrating metabolic and neurodegenerative biomarkers may improve understanding of disease-related processes and support risk assessment and monitoring. Further longitudinal and clinical validation is required before emerging biomarkers can be routinely implemented in practice.

articles.title: Migraine in women.
authors: Spanish Society of Neurology’s Headache Study Group (GECSEN)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Migraine is a highly prevalent and disabling neurological disorder that imposes a substantial economic burden on patients and society. Epidemiological data show a higher incidence of the disease in women after puberty that is strongly related to hormonal fluctuations. Migraine presents clinically relevant sex-related differences, with women experiencing more severe and longer-lasting attacks than men, contributing to greater disease burden. Sex-related differences in migraine disability and comorbidities have also been reported.

DEVELOPMENT: Biological, genetic, epigenetic, and psychosocial factors contribute to sex-related differences in pain mechanisms, and, consequently, to treatment response. Migraine pain mechanisms in men and women are likely different, suggesting the need to consider patient sex as a factor in the clinical and therapeutic management of migraine. Further research is needed to deepen our understanding of the impact of sex on migraine pathophysiology and treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: This literature review, conducted by the Spanish Society of Neurology's Headache Study Group, provides an overview of the role of patient sex in migraine.

articles.title: Position statement of the Spanish Society of Neurology on the current situation of interventional neuroradiology in Spain.
Physician Attire and the Patient Encounter: A Review.
articles.abstract: Surveys of patients, and the systematic reviews that collate them, report that physician attire shapes perceptions of professionalism, trust, and communication, with a consistent preference for the white coat. This review of PubMed through October 2026 sorts this literature by study design. The preference comes from cross-sectional surveys, mostly ratings of photographs, in which patients favor a white coat and rate casual dress lowest. However, in 19 studies that assigned, alternated, or randomized attire in real or simulated encounters, 17 found no difference in patient-rated satisfaction, trust, empathy, or communication; the 2 exceptions date from 2012 and 2014. Stated preferences are malleable: they follow the attire patients have just seen and shift away from coats once contamination is mentioned. In more than 20 countries the white coat leads the surveys, but the alternatives and strength of preference vary. The one consistent effect of attire is identification: in the same clothing, women physicians are more often mistaken for nurses or assistants. Attire policies are better justified by provider identification and infection control than by patient preference.

articles.title: Beyond the Latest NT-proBNP? Rethinking Longitudinal Target Attainment in Heart Failure.
Adaptive vs. Non-Adaptive Radiation Dose Escalation in Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Comparison of NRG-RTOG 0617 and 1106 Individual Patient Data.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: For patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC), NRG-RTOG 0617 found that non-adaptive radiation therapy (naRT) dose escalation to 74 Gy worsened overall survival (OS) vs. 60 Gy, while NRG-RTOG 1106 showed PET-adapted RT (aRT) dose escalation was safe. This study compares aRT vs. naRT in LA-NSCLC.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients from RTOG 0617 and 1106 randomized to dose-escalation arms with PET-based staging were included. All received thoracic radiotherapy with concurrent and consolidation carboplatin/paclitaxel without immunotherapy. Outcomes were OS, progression-free survival (PFS), cumulative incidence of local-regional progression (CILRP), and grade 3+ toxicity. Results were adjusted for baseline differences between cohorts. Cox models evaluated survival and logistic regression models evaluated toxicity outcomes.

RESULTS: Eighty-four patients received aRT and 184 received naRT (median nominal dose 71 Gy vs. 74 Gy). naRT patients had better performance status (Zubrod 0 58% vs. 44%, p=0.0390 and less Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT) (49% vs. 92%, p<0.0001). aRT had lower lung V20 (30% vs. 32%, p=0.0413), mean esophagus dose (27Gy vs. 29Gy, p=0.0017), and trend to lower heart V40 (8% vs. 10%, p=0.0907). Unweighted, aRT had a trend to higher 3-year OS (39% vs. 27%, HR=0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.01, p=0.0535) and significantly higher CILRP (36% vs. 49%, HR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43 - 0.95, p=0.0324), with similar PFS (20% vs. 21%, HR=0.95, 95% CI 0.71-1.27, p=0.7214). Weighted analyses showed similar outcomes between cohorts. aRT had lower grade 3+ esophagitis (6% vs. 22%, OR=0.24, 95% CI 0.09-0.63, p=0.0040) and similar hematologic toxicity (36% vs. 33%, OR=1.15, 95% CI 0.66-1.99, p=0.6257). Weighted models confirmed these findings and showed lower grade 3+ pneumonitis (OR=0.114, 95% CI 0.01-0.98, p=0.0478) and cardiotoxicity (OR=0.114, 95% CI 0.01-0.98, p=0.0478) for aRT.

CONCLUSION: aRT had improved CILRP and a trend to improved OS with significantly reduced toxicity and improved dosimetry vs. naRT.

articles.title: Trends and Risk Factors for Postpartum Readmission due to De Novo Endometritis: A National Historical Cohort Study.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess national temporal trends and timing of 60-day postpartum readmission for de novo endometritis from 2010 to 2022, identify patient-, delivery- and hospital-level risk factors, and determine readmission risk following term caesarean delivery categorized by labouring status.

DESIGN: Retrospective historical cohort study.

SETTING: All-payer inpatient hospitalizations using the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project Nationwide Readmissions Database (NRD) from 2010 to 2022.

POPULATION: An estimated 38.7 million delivery hospitalizations among individuals aged 15-54 years. Delivery admissions with diagnoses of sepsis/shock, chorioamnionitis, endometritis or peripartum hysterectomy were excluded to capture de novo readmissions, as were November and December deliveries due to incomplete 60-day follow-up.

METHODS: Joinpoint regression was utilized to assess temporal trends and calculate average annual percentage changes (AAPCs) across the study period and stratified by coding eras (ICD-9-CM vs. ICD-10-CM). Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated demographic, clinical, and hospital factors associated with 60-day readmission for de novo endometritis, adjusting for potential confounders. A secondary subgroup analysis among term caesarean deliveries (2016-2022) compared labouring caesarean delivery (CD-L) to non-labouring caesarean delivery (CD-NL). Sensitivity analyses evaluated cases where endometritis was the first-listed readmission diagnosis.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: 60-day postpartum readmission with a diagnosis of de novo endometritis, and 60-day readmission with de novo endometritis as the primary (first-listed) diagnosis.

RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2022, 73 664 delivery hospitalizations (0.2%) were complicated by a 60-day readmission for de novo endometritis. Readmissions decreased from 23.8 to 14.1 per 10 000 deliveries (AAPC: -5.2%, 95% CI: -6.7% to -3.7%), with the sharpest decline occurring between 2014 and 2017 (AAPC: -12.8%, 95% CI: -16.0% to -8.1%). Most readmissions occurred rapidly, with 73.0% presenting within 0-10 days post-discharge. In adjusted models, independent risk factors included younger maternal age (15-19 years: aOR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.50-1.66; 20-24 years: aOR 1.21, 95% CI: 1.17-1.26 vs. 25-29 years), primary caesarean (aOR 1.93, 95% CI: 1.87-1.99), repeat caesarean (aOR 1.24, 95% CI: 1.19-1.28), operative vaginal delivery (aOR 1.29, 95% CI: 1.21-1.36), dilation and curettage, postpartum haemorrhage, blood transfusion and immunosuppressive conditions. Among 5.8 million term caesarean deliveries, labouring caesarean was associated with 75% increased odds of de novo endometritis readmission compared to non-labouring caesarean (0.3% vs. 0.1%; aOR 1.75, 95% CI: 1.67-1.83).

CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum readmissions for de novo endometritis are uncommon, occur primarily within 10 days of hospital discharge, and have decreased substantially over the past decade. The risk is concentrated among patients experiencing substantial intrauterine manipulation, labouring caesarean delivery, haemorrhage, or operative interventions, highlighting key targets for risk-stratified surveillance and infection prevention strategies.

articles.title: Economic impact of epizootic lymphangitis in cart pulling horses in a low-income setting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epizootic lymphangitis (EL) is a contagious fungal disease threatening the health and welfare of working equids and the economic stability of dependent communities in resource-constrained settings.

OBJECTIVES: To assess owner clinical awareness regarding EL and to quantify the direct and indirect household-level financial losses attributable to the disease in an urban working carthorse population.

STUDY DESIGN: Observational cross-sectional survey.

METHODS: Structured questionnaire interviews were conducted with 285 carthorse owners in Gondar town, Ethiopia. Descriptive statistics, financial loss modelling (converted to USD at 1 USD ≈ 133.33 ETB), and multivariable logistic regression were applied to evaluate disease awareness, economic impact drivers, and socio-demographic predictors.

RESULTS: Near-universal clinical symptom recognition was observed among respondents (94.04%), yet a profound educational gap existed, with 65.85% unaware of the underlying microbial aetiology. The mean overall financial loss was $508.05 (67,739.41 ETB) per household per year. Primary financial loss drivers were equine mortality ($306.78 [40,903.85 ETB]) and forced premature culling ($175.63 [23,416.67 ETB]). Reduced draught power capacity, opportunity cost of family labour, carcass disposal, and isolation facility costs contributed $14.69 (1959.35 ETB), $4.35 (579.74 ETB), $2.61 (347.58 ETB), and $2.61 (347.58 ETB), respectively. Out-of-pocket veterinary treatment ($0.51 [68.53 ETB]) and supplementary feeding ($0.66 [87.90 ETB]) represented negligible fractions of total losses. Owners with secondary education exhibited significantly higher odds of epidemiological awareness (OR = 4.46, 95% CI: 2.27-9.45, p < 0.001).

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Nonrandomised convenience sampling across urban cart stations may introduce selection bias, while reliance on 12-month owner recall introduces potential reporting inaccuracies for minor operational expenses.

CONCLUSIONS: While clinical recognition of EL cutaneous lesions is exceptionally high, a critical knowledge deficit persists regarding its aetiology and transmission dynamics. Veterinary outreach programmes must pair clinical disease management with targeted biosecurity education to address epidemiological misconceptions and mitigate these substantial economic shocks.

articles.title: The Changing Role of Allogeneic Transplantation in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia: Referral and Timing in the Targeted Therapy Era.
articles.abstract: Allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) remains a potentially curative option for selected patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL), but carries substantial non-relapse mortality and graft-versus-host disease. Current guidelines restrict its use as targeted and cellular therapies expand. This perspective translates those recommendations into a proposed workflow that separates early referral from the decision to transplant. Double exposure to covalent BTK and BCL2 inhibitors must be distinguished from resistance to both classes. Referral is proposed at double refractoriness and at single-class resistance with adverse genetics or limited remaining options. Proceeding requires an appropriate disease indication, an objective response, acceptable estimated procedural risk and a deliverable donor strategy, considered against available alternatives and patient preferences. Progression despite bridging, uncontrolled infection or prohibitive organ or functional impairment can prevent transplantation; reversible barriers warrant reassessment. We summarise allo-HCT outcomes with explicit time horizons and non-relapse mortality, address the risk of losing eligibility during CAR T-cell sequencing and distinguish pre-transplant MRD from post-transplant immune-response monitoring. Frailty evidence outside CLL transplantation is treated as indirect. The transplant window is a clinical synthesis, not a validated score or a new indication; its purpose is to make preparation and reassessment explicit.

articles.title: Timing of first recorded non-operative hypertonic albumin doses and nearby furosemide records in adults with a positive sepsis screen: A single-centre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Japanese sepsis guidelines ask whether hypertonic albumin should maintain serum albumin at 3.0 g/dL after initial resuscitation for septic shock. We aimed to describe when, at what serum albumin and near which drugs hypertonic albumin is recorded in routine practice.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used one Japanese tertiary hospital's health and claims records of adult admissions positive on a local sepsis screen in 2018-2026. The primary outcomes were the interval from the start of the admission day to the first recorded non-operative dose, the serum albumin before it and three intravenous drugs recorded in a window from 2 h before to 12 h after each dose. Analyses were descriptive.

RESULTS: Of 4699 screen-positive admissions (4196 individuals), 836 (17.8%) received hypertonic albumin in 5518 doses. The median interval to the first dose was 107.2 h (interquartile range 58.5-229.6). Serum albumin before the first dose was below 3.0 g/dL in 673 of 705 admissions with a value (95.5%). Furosemide was recorded within that window for 2350 doses (42.6%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 39.2-46.0), noradrenaline for 1403 (25.4%, 95% CI 22.5-28.5) and hydrocortisone for 456 (8.3%, 95% CI 6.7-9.9).

CONCLUSIONS: At this hospital, the first recorded non-operative hypertonic albumin dose usually occurred days into the admission, almost always at a serum albumin below 3.0 g/dL where measured. Furosemide was often recorded near albumin doses. Whether hypertonic albumin is often given during a phase of diuretic treatment is a question for prospective assessment.

articles.title: Integrating physiology and practice in critical care: hemodynamics and ventilatory mechanics for the beginner intensivist.
articles.abstract: This educational review provides a practical and evidence-informed overview of hemodynamic and ventilatory physiology for early-career intensivists. It integrates recent trials and expert consensus to explain how macro- and microcirculatory interactions, fluid responsiveness, vasopressor use, and mechanical-ventilation principles translate into bedside decision-making. Beyond summarizing physiology, this article emphasizes clinical reasoning, controversies, and limitations of monitoring approaches, aiming to strengthen conceptual understanding and promote individualized, physiology-guided critical care. Illustrative figures and summary tables support visual learning and reinforce the link between physiological concepts and clinical application. The review also highlights emerging frontiers, including Patient Self-Inflicted Lung Injury (P-SILI), the nuanced role of the pulmonary artery catheter in selected shock states, and ongoing challenges in bedside microcirculatory monitoring, which shape individualized critical care practice.

articles.title: Circulating microRNAs and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease risk: a two-stage Mendelian randomization and colocalization study with independent replication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The causal role of circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) in COPD pathogenesis remains unclear. We used Mendelian Randomization (MR) to evaluate genetically predicted associations between plasma miRNAs and COPD risk.

METHODS: A two-stage MR framework was employed: Stage 1 (Nikpay cis/trans-mirQTLs, n = 710) for discovery and instrument-type sensitivity; Stage 2 (FHS cis-miR-eQTLs, n = 5,239) for independent replication in available candidates. Outcomes (Total, Early-onset, Later-onset COPD) were from FinnGen R12, with FDR correction per phenotype, Steiger filtering, reverse MR, and Bayesian colocalization with prior sensitivity. Exploratory target gene prediction and GEO expression assessment were also performed.

RESULTS: Of 70 miRNAs screened, 17 reached nominal significance and 3 survived phenotype-specific FDR correction, of which miR-130a-3p and miR-103a-3p (but not miR-199a-3p) remained significant under global FDR across all 210 tests. FHS replication, available for 4 of 17 candidates, supported associations for miR-130a-3p and miR-139-3p. miR-103a-3p (protective) showed consistent trans-mirQTL sensitivity but lacked FHS instruments. Colocalization supported, but did not establish, a shared signal for miR-130a-3p and Total COPD (PP.H4 = 0.939; PP.H3 = 0.012). Horizontal pleiotropy could not be excluded for the lead instrument. GEO expression differences were non-significant in both cohorts; these miRNAs are not validated biomarkers.

CONCLUSION: These findings support a potential role of circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-130a-3p, in COPD, but are hypothesis-generating: unresolved pleiotropy, negative GEO expression findings, and replication limited to 4 of 17 candidates render their clinical relevance uncertain.

articles.title: Development and performance evaluation of a prediction model for identifying high risk populations for inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Emergency Department (ED) crowding has been recognized as a major public health problem worldwide. Excessive triage will prolong patients' waiting time and increase the workload of triage nurses while inadequate triage may raise the risk of adverse medical safety events. This study aimed to identify high risk populations for inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings, construct a risk prediction model, and evaluate its predictive value.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study enrolled adult patients triaged in the ED from January to December 2024, and a total of 5321 patients were finally included. Descriptive statistics were computed, and univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Hosmer-Lemeshow test were applied, and the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of the model were calculated.

RESULTS: Night shift attendance(OR = 1.383), chief complaint of digestive system symptoms(OR = 1.707), chief complaint of trauma(OR = 2.727)，chief complaint of cardiovascular system(OR = 0.651), triage level 1(OR = 0.057), and heart rate(OR = 0.948) were influencing factors for the accuracy of initial triage among adult emergency patients. The multivariate logistic regression prediction model constructed based on these factors had an AUC of 0.723(95%CI: 0.697-0.749), with a sensitivity of 64.6% and a specificity of 70.9%.

CONCLUSIONS: The prediction model established in this study enables triage nurses to early identify high-risk populations with inaccurate initial triage in adult emergency settings.

articles.title: Different diameters of particulate matter exposure and health outcomes: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract: Airborne particulate matter (PM) is a pervasive environmental hazard, yet the comparative toxicity of different aerodynamic diameters-particularly sub-micron particles (PM1)-remains insufficiently characterized in environmental health risk assessments. To address this, we conducted an umbrella review systematically synthesizing observational meta-analyses to evaluate the dose-response associations between PM fractions (PM10, PM2.5, and PM1) and diverse health outcomes. By harmonizing effect estimates and assessing evidence quality via the GRADE framework, we observed a potential 'size effect' influencing pollutant toxicity. Our comparative analyses suggested that PM1 may be associated with relatively stronger adverse effects than larger fractions across multiple physiological domains. Notably, PM1 exposure was associated with the highest relative risks for metabolic disorders, including metabolic syndrome (RR=1.30), childhood obesity (RR=1.41), and childhood hypertension (RR=1.61), significantly outpacing the effects of PM2.5 and PM10. Furthermore, moderate-quality evidence highlighted a striking systemic vulnerability, with PM1 demonstrating a robust association with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD, RR=1.59). Similar size-dependent toxicity gradients were observed for neurodevelopmental (autism) and respiratory (asthma) outcomes. The amplified toxicity of PM1 is likely mediated by its higher alveolar deposition efficiency, larger specific surface area for toxicant adsorption, and enhanced capacity to translocate across biological barriers (e.g., air-blood barrier) to induce systemic oxidative stress. These findings highlight that current air quality regulations, which predominantly rely on PM2.5 and PM10 mass concentrations, may not fully capture the systemic and metabolic health burdens of smaller particles. Incorporating size-resolved PM1 monitoring into environmental safety frameworks could be an important step toward better estimating human health risks and developing targeted mitigation strategies.

articles.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Excessive Daytime Sleepiness in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) is a common but often overlooked condition in older adults, and it is associated with a variety of adverse outcomes. This study aimed to explore the pooled prevalence of EDS and its risk factors among older adults.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Adults aged 60 years and older in any setting.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in 8 databases, including CNKI, VIP, CBM, WanFang Data, Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and The Cochrane Library from inception to October 2025. Two researchers independently screened the literature and extracted the information. Pooled prevalence estimates and odds ratios for the prevalence of EDS in older adults and its risk factors were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models.

RESULTS: Forty-three eligible studies were included; the overall pooled prevalence of EDS in older adults was 16.9%. Subgroup analyses revealed significant variations in prevalence across geographic regions (P < .001), with the lowest rate observed in East Asia (13.0%) and the highest in Western Asia (21.8%). Furthermore, the use of different Epworth Sleepiness Scale cutoff values resulted in significant differences. Several factors were significantly associated with an increased risk of EDS, including male sex, obesity, malnutrition, urinary incontinence, and various comorbidities (eg, dementia, Parkinson's disease, cerebrovascular disease, depression, diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, insomnia, and obstructive sleep apnea). Conversely, the use of hypnotic medications may serve as a protective factor.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: EDS is common among older adults, although prevalence estimates vary across geographic regions and according to the Epworth Sleepiness Scale cutoff used. Several demographic, nutritional, and health-related factors were associated with EDS. These findings support greater clinical attention to EDS and targeted early screening, particularly among older adults with relevant comorbidities or other associated factors, to facilitate timely evaluation and appropriate intervention.

articles.title: Characterizing multiple dimensions of climate hazards for conservation planning: a case study of estuaries in the Pacific Northwest.
articles.abstract: Incorporating the complexities of climate change into conservation planning can be challenging. Globally, climate change is projected to change the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation, and change the dynamics of extreme events of many climate variables. These changes will all have compounding effects on ecosystems worldwide, affecting species distributions, population dynamics, and survival. However, most recent climate-informed conservation planning frameworks only focus on changes in mean conditions, leaving out ecologically important information about variability and extreme events. Using a case study of estuaries in the Pacific Northwest, this research seeks to answer the question "How can changes in the mean, variability, and extremes in temperature and precipitation in estuaries best be modelled and described for practical use in ecological management?" To answer this question, we used downscaled climate projection data to estimate changes in the mean and variability of temperature and precipitation. Applying extreme value theory to these projection data, we also projected changes in the magnitude of extremes in temperature and precipitation for estuaries in the region. Using descriptive statistics and open source data, our results present a novel, holistic method of understanding climate risk, including estimating extreme events, highlighting a key research gap in conservation planning. These results also highlight that trends in the mean, variability, and magnitude of climate extremes are not consistent with each other, further underscoring the importance of considering multiple dimensions of climate change together. Despite uncertainty given by climate models, the methods presented here provide a reasonable approach to plan for conservation management in the face of climate uncertainty.

articles.title: Immunogenicity and acute reactogenicity of the 9-valent HPV vaccine in Chinese females aged 16-32 years: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The nine-valent human papillomavirus (9vHPV) vaccine offers broad protection against HPV-related diseases. However, its multidimensional safety profile-integrating acute hemodynamic changes, injection-site pain, local inflammatory reactions, and vasovagal responses-remains incompletely characterized. Validated tools for individualised risk prediction are also lacking.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analysed routinely collected data from 103 females aged 16-32 years who completed the three-dose 9vHPV vaccination schedule (0-2-6 months) between January 2023 and January 2024. Participants were stratified into three age groups: 16-20 (n = 36), 21-26 (n = 33), and 27-32 years (n = 34). Immunogenicity was assessed by geometric mean titers (GMT) and seropositive rates (SPR) for all nine HPV types one month after dose three. Safety outcomes included acute hemodynamic changes (heart rate, blood pressure), injection-site pain (Visual Analog Scale), local inflammatory reactions, systemic adverse events following immunisation (AEFI), and vasovagal reactions. Multidimensional correlation analyses, K-means clustering, temporal scan statistics, and an exploratory logistic regression-based risk prediction models were applied.

RESULTS: All nine HPV types achieved SPR ≥98.1% (range 98.1-100%), with GMT ranging from 2832 to 16,875 mIU/mL. The 16-20 years group showed significantly higher GMTs than the 27-32 years group for multiple types (e.g., HPV16: +61.1%, P = 0.010). Acute hemodynamic changes included heart rate elevation in 83.5% of participants, with 98.1% normalising within 30 min. Injection-site pain peaked immediately post-vaccination (VAS 3.8 ± 2.1) and was predominantly mild to moderate (87.4%). Heart rate elevation correlated significantly with pain intensity (Spearman ρ = 0.706, P < 0.001). Vasovagal reactions occurred in 10.7% (11/103) of participants, including syncope in 1.9% (2/103), with significant temporal clustering (scan statistic λ = 968.4, P = 0.008). K-means clustering identified four distinct reactogenicity phenotypes: normal-reactive (36.9%), balanced-reactive (40.8%), high-reactive (14.6%), and vasovagal-sensitive (7.8%). The exploratory risk prediction model showed good discriminative ability (AUC = 0.913; sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 87.0%). Baseline heart rate > 85 bpm was an independent predictor of vasovagal reactions (OR = 3.20, P = 0.008), while younger age and lower BMI were significantly associated with the vasovagal-sensitive phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary retrospective cohort, the 9vHPV vaccine induced robust immunogenicity across the 16-32 years age range with no vaccine-related serious adverse events. Acute hemodynamic changes and vasovagal reactions were transient and mostly mild, and were likely influenced by procedural and autonomic factors rather than vaccine components alone. This study provides preliminary integrated evidence linking acute hemodynamic, pain, and local inflammatory responses after 9vHPV vaccination and introduces an internally validated, exploratory risk stratification tool. External validation in unselected real-world cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Surgical margins in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: A European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) multidisciplinary modified Delphi consensus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical margin assessment in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) remains poorly standardized by HPV status, subsite, and treatment context. This European Head and Neck Society (EHNS) consensus aimed to harmonize margin assessment and margin-based decisions.

METHODS: Following systematic review, 25 multidisciplinary panelists evaluated recommendations through two Delphi rounds; consensus was ≥80 % and near-consensus 70-79.9 %. Margindefinitionswerebasedonformalin-fixed,paraffin-embeddedsections,notintraoperativeor postoperativegrossingestimates.

RESULTS: Of 48 recommendations, 32 reached consensus, six near-consensus, and 10 were rejected. "Ink on tumor" defined a positive margin irrespective of HPV status (96 %). A 5-mm mucosal margin was retained for HPV-negative OPSCC (84 %), whereas 3 mm reached near-consensus for HPV-positive disease (78.3 %); smaller thresholds were unsupported. A clear margin alone should not determine adjuvant treatment (78.3 %, near-consensus). Re-resection was recommended when the margin site was identifiable and would change adjuvant management. Positive margins warranted radiotherapy in pT1-T2 HPV-positive disease without other adverse features (80 %), whereas chemoradiotherapy was recommended with high-risk features, such as pT3-T4 disease or extranodal extension (95.8 %), and in HPV-negative disease (100 %). For close margins, selective de-escalation could be considered in highly selected HPV-positive disease without high-risk features (82.6 %), whereas HPV-negative disease warranted radiotherapy, with escalation according to additional risks (91.3 %). In fit patients aged ≥70 years with positive margins, radiotherapy alone was favored for HPV-positive disease (87.5 %), while chemoradiotherapy was retained for fit patients with HPV-negative disease (95.7 %).

CONCLUSIONS: This consensus provides a multidisciplinary framework for harmonized OPSCC margin assessment and risk-adapted postoperative management across HPV status, anatomy, and treatment-related morbidity.

articles.title: Visual capture of tactile motion: Evidence from a novel mirror box illusion.
articles.abstract: To localize touch, the brain must integrate information from representations of the skin's surface (a somatotopic reference frame) with representations of the surrounding environment (an external reference frame). While vision robustly captures the perceived location of static touches, resolving crossmodal spatial conflicts for continuous, moving stimuli remains poorly understood. Across four experiments, we demonstrate a novel visual-tactile illusion: viewing a moving stroke across the hand substantially alters the perceived trajectory of a simultaneous tactile stroke on a hidden hand, shifting the percept roughly halfway toward the direction of the visual stroke. This visual capture of tactile motion occurs independently of top-down body ownership. By systematically manipulating hand posture, we found that both somatotopic and external reference frames contribute to the perceived direction of tactile motion. Rather than defaulting to a single coordinate system, the brain combines information from both representations to construct a conscious percept of tactile motion. These results extend visual capture from the location of a touch to its trajectory, and suggest that accounts built on brief, punctate stimuli may need to accommodate both continuous tactile motion and contributions from multiple spatial reference frames.

articles.title: Outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapies (OPAT): a path to eliminating healthcare-associated infections?
