Integrated Vector, Canine, and Human Evidence Reveal a Stable Dog-Maintained Cycle of Leishmania Infantum in a Historically Endemic Area From Spain.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Leishmaniosis, caused by Leishmania infantum, is a major zoonotic vector-borne disease in southern Europe. Dogs act as the primary domestic reservoir of the parasite. However, there is growing evidence that transmission cycles involving wild lagomorphs may contribute to both epidemic and endemic human cases in certain settings. Nevertheless, the ecological and epidemiological mechanisms sustaining long-term endemic transmission in stable foci remain poorly understood. This study used an integrated One Health approach combining vector, canine, and human data to investigate transmission dynamics in a long-established endemic area with low human case incidence.

METHODS: An eco-epidemiological study was conducted in Crevillente Municipality in southeast Spain, between 2021 and 2022. Sand flies were collected using CDC light traps and analysed to determine species composition, Leishmania infection by real-time PCR, parasite identification, and blood meal sources. Dogs were tested for anti-Leishmania antibodies using ELISA. Human blood donors were assessed for Leishmania infection by PCR and for anti-Leishmania antibodies and antibodies against Phlebotomus perniciosus saliva as markers of parasite and vector exposure, respectively.

RESULTS: A total of 11,375 sand flies were collected, predominantly Sergentomyia minuta and Phlebotomus perniciosus, and displayed marked seasonal and spatial variation. High Leishmania infection rates were detected in confirmed vector species, with L. infantum identified in most samples. Blood meal analysis revealed that the primary feeding sources were dogs and humans, while rabbits and hares were detected but infrequently. Canine seroprevalence was high (43%) and associated with rural exposure. In humans, infection markers were low (3% PCR, 4% serology), despite high exposure to sand fly bites (38% seroprevalence for anti-saliva antibodies).

CONCLUSIONS: The study characterizes a Mediterranean endemic focus with intense circulation of L. infantum in vectors and dogs, widespread human exposure to sand flies, but low levels of asymptomatic human infection and no reported clinical disease during the decade preceding the study. The findings support a predominantly domestic transmission, with dogs representing the main identified reservoir host and lagomorph-derived blood meals being relatively infrequent. The potential contribution of lagomorphs to local parasite circulation warrants further investigation. The detection of Leishmania DNA in non-confirmed vector species, including sequences consistent with the L. donovani/L. infantum complex, further highlights the need for continued surveillance of Leishmania diversity and transmission dynamics.

articles.title: Increased Sodium Chloride Concentration Enhances Piscirickettsia salmonis Epithelial Translocation by Modulating Immune and Osmoregulatory Gene Expression in RTgutGC Cells.
articles.abstract: Climate change is expected to increase seawater salinity, potentially altering the physiological responses of marine organisms. In salmonids, elevated salinity has been associated with outbreaks of infectious diseases; however, the mechanisms linking salinity with intestinal epithelial dysfunction and bacterial invasion remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of increased sodium chloride concentrations on the integrity of the rainbow trout intestinal epithelial cell line RTgutGC and its relationship with P. salmonis translocation. Cells cultured under control (8 g/L NaCl) or hyperosmotic conditions (16 and 20 g/L NaCl) were assessed for cytotoxicity, epithelial integrity, permeability, bacterial translocation, and gene expression. Hyperosmotic conditions significantly increased epithelial permeability and reduced barrier integrity, as evidenced by altered paracellular permeability to Dextran FITC and modulation of tight junction-related genes, including cld-3 and zo-1. Salinity also induced the expression of osmoregulatory (tsc22 and nka) and immune-related genes (il-1β and il-10), indicating activation of response to osmotic stress. Importantly, elevated salinity significantly enhanced the translocation of P. salmonis across the epithelial monolayer, whereas no bacterial translocation was detected under control conditions. Moreover, high salinity increased infection-associated cytotoxicity, mainly at 20 g/L NaCl. Together, these findings demonstrate that increased sodium chloride concentration compromises intestinal epithelial barrier function while promoting P. salmonis translocation. These results provide mechanistic evidence linking climate-driven changes in seawater salinity with increased epithelial susceptibility to bacterial pathogens and suggest that osmotic stress may represent an important environmental factor influencing the pathogenesis of piscirickettsiosis in salmonids.

articles.title: Lifestyle Factors and Cardiometabolic Diseases in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Mixed Graphical and Bayesian Network Analysis With Sex-Specific Comparison.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To examine the complex relationships between lifestyle factors and cardiometabolic diseases and to explore sex-specific network structures and dependency patterns among middle-aged and older adults.

DESIGN: This cross-sectional study used data from Wave 5 (2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.

METHODS: Lifestyle factors included physical activity, sleep duration, smoking, and alcohol consumption. Cardiometabolic diseases were identified based on self-reported physician diagnoses. Mixed graphical models and Bayesian networks were applied to investigate conditional associations, potential dependency structures, and sex differences. The study was reported according to the STROBE checklist.

RESULTS: A total of 18,548 participants were included. In the mixed graphical models, alcohol consumption and physical activity showed the highest bridge expected influence in men, whereas physical activity and smoking were the most influential bridge nodes in women. Network Comparison Tests indicated no significant sex difference in global network strength, whereas network structure differed significantly between men and women. Bayesian network analysis identified a common dependency pattern across sexes involving physical activity, dyslipidemia, and diabetes. Sex-specific dependency patterns were also observed: alcohol consumption, stroke, heart disease, and diabetes were linked in a prominent pattern among men, whereas smoking, heart disease, and stroke were linked among women. In sensitivity analyses incorporating sociodemographic covariates, lifestyle-CMD associations remained evident in the overall sample and among women, whereas the corresponding associations were no longer clearly evident in the male network.

CONCLUSION: Lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic diseases showed distinct network association patterns between men and women. However, the male-specific Bayesian network findings were sensitive to the inclusion of sociodemographic covariates and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings provide insights into the complex associations between lifestyle behaviours and cardiometabolic diseases. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to confirm effects and sex differences.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Comprehensive, person-centred lifestyle assessment is important for the prevention and management of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs). Network-based approaches may help identify complex associations between lifestyle behaviours and CMDs, providing insights for sex-sensitive behavioural assessment and risk stratification.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

articles.title: Emerging Therapeutic Strategies Targeting Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocyte Injury: Molecular Mechanisms and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is a regulated, iron-dependent form of cell death characterized by excessive lipid peroxidation resulting from disrupted iron homeostasis and impaired cellular antioxidant defenses. Increasing evidence identifies ferroptosis as a central contributor to cardiomyocyte injury in ischemia-reperfusion injury, anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity, metabolic cardiac disorders, diabetic cardiomyopathy, and heart failure. Unlike apoptosis, necroptosis, autophagic cell death, and pyroptosis, ferroptosis is driven by glutathione depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) inactivation, and uncontrolled lipid peroxide accumulation, making it a distinct and potentially reversible therapeutic target. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms regulating cardiac ferroptosis, emphasizing the roles of GPX4, Solute Carrier Family 7 Member 11 (SLC7A11), Nuclear factor Erythroid 2-related Factor 2 (NRF2), Acyl-CoA Synthetase Long-Chain Family Member 4 (ACSL4), Ferroptosis Suppressor Protein 1 (FSP1), Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase (DHODH), and ferritinophagy, together with their interactions with other regulated cell death pathways. We further discuss emerging therapeutic approaches, including natural phytochemicals, small-molecule ferroptosis inhibitors, and gene- and molecular target-based strategies, together with the cardio-oncology implications of inhibiting ferroptosis and the translational prospects offered by nanoparticle-based delivery, multi-omics integration, and artificial intelligence-assisted predictive modeling. Current translational challenges, including the absence of validated ferroptosis-specific biomarkers, limited human-relevant disease models, and interpatient heterogeneity, are critically evaluated. By integrating molecular mechanisms, therapeutic advances, and translational perspectives, this review provides an updated framework for understanding ferroptosis in cardiovascular toxicity and identifies key opportunities for developing clinically translatable ferroptosis-targeted cardioprotective strategies.

articles.title: STAP2 contributes to retinal endothelial dysfunction in diabetes through CXCR4-associated signaling revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of vision loss and is driven by diabetes-induced retinal endothelial dysfunction. However, diabetes-associated transcriptional heterogeneity within retinal endothelial cells (ECs) and its molecular regulators remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Retinal ECs were re-analyzed from a previously published single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of db/db and db/m mouse retinas. STAP2 expression was evaluated in db/db and streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic mouse retinas, human proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) tissue, and human retinal microvascular endothelial cells (HRMECs). Gain- and loss-of-function studies assessed endothelial proliferation, migration, angiogenic activity, retinal capillary degeneration, and vascular leakage. Transcriptomic profiling was used to identify downstream mediators.

RESULTS: Three transcriptionally defined endothelial subclusters were identified, with EC3 predominantly represented in the diabetic group and showing relatively higher expression of signal-transducing adaptor protein 2 (STAP2). STAP2 was increased in diabetic retinas and high-glucose-treated HRMECs. STAP2 knockdown suppressed HRMEC proliferation, migration, and early tube formation in vitro and reduced acellular capillary formation and Evans blue extravasation in vivo, whereas STAP2 overexpression promoted these responses. Transcriptomic analysis identified C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4 (CXCR4) as a candidate downstream mediator, and CXCR4 silencing attenuated STAP2-induced endothelial responses.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify STAP2 as a previously unrecognized regulator associated with diabetic retinal endothelial dysfunction and reveal CXCR4-associated signaling as a potential mechanism involved in STAP2-mediated endothelial responses. This study provides new insights into endothelial regulation during diabetic vascular injury.

articles.title: [Acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation].
articles.abstract: Nearly half of patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation have concomitant significant coronary artery disease. In patients with severe aortic stenosis and coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease, several issues remain controversial, including the optimal diagnostic evaluation, the choice of treatment strategy (surgical, percutaneous, or conservative), the indication for and extent of coronary revascularization, and, if percutaneous coronary intervention is performed, its optimal timing. After transcatheter aortic valve implantation, selective coronary cannulation may be challenging in a subset of patients, an issue of increasing clinical relevance as accumulating evidence in recent years has progressively expanded transcatheter aortic valve implantation indications to patients with longer anticipated survival. Although the likelihood of requiring invasive coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention after transcatheter aortic valve implantation is expected to increase in these patients, coronary events occurring during the post-transcatheter aortic valve implantation period - particularly life-threatening acute coronary syndromes - remain insufficiently characterized with respect to their incidence, clinical characteristics, predictors, and outcomes. In addition to conventional atherothrombotic mechanisms, the transcatheter heart valve itself may contribute to the development of acute coronary syndromes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Furthermore, the presence of a transcatheter heart valve may complicate invasive management because of technical challenges related to coronary access. This may be of particular importance in patients presenting with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation, in whom rapid and reliable coronary access and time-critical reperfusion are essential. The Gottsegen National Cardiovascular Center is one of the leading high-volume centers nationwide for the treatment of patients with severe aortic stenosis. Since the initiation of the institutional transcatheter aortic valve implantation program in 2008, more than 3000 procedures have been performed. Analysis of this large-scale registry may contribute to a better understanding of the currently unknown incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of acute coronary syndromes among patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation in Hungary. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(47): 1887-1899.

articles.title: Health-related quality of life with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors added to standard therapy for endometrial and cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether adding programmed cell death protein 1 or programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-1/PD-L1) inhibitors to standard therapy affects health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in patients with endometrial or cervical cancer.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception through September 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus standard therapy with the identical treatment backbone, with or without placebo. Mean differences (MDs) in change from baseline were pooled using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine RCTs involving 5,933 patients were included, of which seven trials comprising 4,995 patients contributed to the meta-analysis. Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition did not significantly affect EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/quality of life (MD -0.07; 95% CI -1.50 to 1.35; I²=0%; 7 studies; 4,995 patients). Results were also non-significant for physical, role, emotional, cognitive, and social functioning; lymphedema; menopausal symptoms; peripheral neuropathy; sexual worry; symptom experience; and EQ-5D health status. Certainty of evidence was moderate for global health status/quality of life and low for the remaining outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to standard therapy did not detectably change global HRQoL, and the pooled confidence interval excluded clinically important deterioration. No functional or symptom domain differed significantly, although small effects cannot be excluded for domains informed by few trials.

articles.title: A dynamic network analysis of anxiety-related distress within a quality-of-life framework among adults undergoing chemotherapy.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To understand anxiety-related distress within the quality-of-life context, this study examined how anxiety-related distress is positioned in the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ) framework, and assessed its strongest associations with other quality-of-life factors over time.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial data included 390 adults aged ≥ 50 years (63.1% female) who were assessed across six time points: before chemotherapy (baseline, T1) and during chemotherapy (T2-T6). Longitudinal network analysis was used to evaluate the position and associations of anxiety-related distress, represented by worry and tension, within the EORTC-QLQ framework. A baseline network using all 30 EORTC-QLQ items first identified the position of anxiety-related distress. A reduced longitudinal network using key nodes was then estimated to examine contemporaneous, between-person, and temporal associations over time.

RESULTS: The baseline network revealed that worry played a central bridging role within the quality-of-life framework. In the reduced longitudinal network, the strongest evidence emerged in the contemporaneous and between-person networks. At the same assessment occasion, worry and tension were positively associated with depressed mood, trouble sleeping, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and financial difficulties. At between-person level, higher average worry was associated with higher average tension, depressed mood, and financial difficulties; while higher average tension was associated with higher average irritability, worry, and difficulty concentrating. In the temporal network, financial difficulties significantly predicted higher subsequent worry but lower subsequent tension.

CONCLUSIONS: Anxiety-related distress was centrally embedded within the EORTC QLQ framework, with worry serving as a key connector linking emotional, cognitive, sleep-related, and financial concerns. Potential leverage points for supportive care during chemotherapy were identified.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05838638; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05838638?term=NCT05838638&rank=1 .

articles.title: Youth and Young Adult Suicide by County, Race, and/or Ethnicity in the United States, 2000-2019.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate trends in suicide rates among individuals aged 10-24 by race and/or ethnicity, county, and age category in the United States from 2000 to 2019.

METHODS: Deidentified death records from the National Vital Statistics System and population estimates from the National Center for Health Statistics from January 1, 2000, to December 31, 2019, were used to estimate suicide rates per 100,000 for youth and young adults by race and/or ethnicity (American Indian/Alaska Native or AIAN, Asian, Black, Latino, and White), county, and age category (10-14, 15-19, and 20-24 years). County-level rates were calculated using small-area estimation methods and misclassification bias correction methodologies.

RESULTS: From 2000 to 2019, the age-standardized suicide rate among individuals aged 10-24 years increased by 33.6% (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 27.9%-39.9%) from 7.7 (95% [UI], 7.4-8.0) to 10.3 (95% UI, 10.0-10.6) deaths per 100,000. Suicide increased across all populations, with the AIAN population having the highest mortality rates in 2000 and 2019: 16.1 (95% UI, 13.0-19.7) and 27.2 (95% UI, 22.0-33.4) deaths per 100,000 individuals, respectively. Of the 10 counties with the highest overall suicide rates, seven were in Alaska, two in South Dakota, and one in North Dakota in 2019. From 2000 to 2019, 99.2% (3,055 of 3,079, 61.4% statistically significant) of counties experienced increased suicide rates among individuals aged 10-24 years.

DISCUSSION: Suicide rates increased among all youth and young adult populations between 2000 and 2019. There is a need for comprehensive interventions that promote prevention strategies and address social isolation especially among AIAN individuals.

articles.title: Electro-Structural Remodeling Reversal With Myosin Inhibitor in Apical Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myosin inhibitor is a novel treatment for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but evidence for the efficacy in apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (AHCM) is lacking.

CASE SUMMARY: A 41-year-old man with AHCM presented with progressive dyspnea and chest pain despite beta-blocker therapy. Besides classic electrocardiography changes, echocardiography revealed a high-velocity apical jet. Mavacamten 5 mg daily was initiated. By week 32, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide and apical flow velocity normalized. T-wave inversion was absent at week 89 and was normalized by week 135. At week 145, magnetic resonance showed no further progression of myocardial fibrosis.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of a myosin inhibitor reversing symptoms, structural remodeling, and electrophysiological abnormalities in AHCM. Patients with AHCM could benefit from long-term treatment, and the electrocardiogram may serve as a marker of therapeutic response.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Myosin inhibitors may benefit ventricular remodeling, especially electrophysiological abnormalities, in patients with AHCM. Further research is warranted.

articles.title: Predictors of sustained partial remission in acute-onset type 1 diabetes: Prospective longitudinal study in Japanese type 1 diabetes (TIDE-J).
articles.abstract:
AIM/INTRODUCTION: To identify predictors of sustained partial remission (PR) in acute-onset type 1 diabetes (AT1D), using data from the nationwide, multicenter, prospective longitudinal TIDE-J Study.

METHODS: Data were collected annually for up to 11 years in 132 patients with AT1D. Patients were classified into three groups based on an insulin dose-adjusted HbA1c (IDAA1c) of ≤9: 54 patients with no remission during the follow-up period (No PR), 45 patients with remission lasting at least 3 years (PR≥3 years), and 24 patients with remission lasting less than 3 years (PR <3 years). Predictors of sustained PR were identified by multivariate analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with the No PR group, the PR ≥3 years group had lower IDAA1c, lower insulin requirements, lower incidence of diabetic ketosis/ketoacidosis (DK/DKA), and higher F-CPR levels. PR ≥3 years also had a higher prevalence of GADA single-positivity and a lower frequency of IA-2A and/or ZnT8A than PR <3 years. Multivariate analysis identified lower IDAA1c (OR, 0.87), absence of DK/DKA (OR, 1.74), less weight loss prior to diagnosis (OR, 0.89), higher F-CPR (OR, 1.96), lower insulin requirement (OR, 2.04), and GADA single-positivity (OR, 1.50) as predictors significantly associated with PR ≥3 years compared with No PR. Compared to PR <3 years, significant predictors of PR ≥3 years were multiple daily insulin injection regimen following diagnosis (OR, 2.70), higher F-CPR (OR, 2.16), GADA single-positivity (OR, 2.03), and negativity for both IA-2A and ZnT8A (OR, 1.93).

CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that PR is more likely to be sustained in patients with preserved β-cell function from the early stages of AT1D onset, mild metabolic impairment, and GADA single-positivity.

articles.title: Evaluation of clinical, immunological, genetic characteristics and follow-up results of patients presenting with common variable immunodeficiency phenotype.
articles.journal: Asian Pacific journal of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is an antibody deficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent infections and non-infectious clinical features. Patients presenting with heterogeneous clinical findings lead to delayed diagnosis, various complications, and organ damage.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the clinical, immunological, genetic features of CVID cases diagnosed in our clinic over a 20-year period.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated 51 patients diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) according to ESID criteria and followed at the Department of Pediatric Allergy and Immunology, Ankara University Faculty of Medicine, between 2002 and 2022.

RESULTS: The median age at diagnosis was 11.08 years (range: 4-27.91), with a median diagnostic delay of 4.79 years (range: 1-22.91). The most common clinical manifestation was sinopulmonary infections (96%). The most frequent non-infectious clinical manifestation was lymphoproliferation (41.1%). Splenomegaly was significantly more common in patients with autoimmune disease (53.3%). Patients with bronchiectasis had significantly lower proportions of class-switched memory B cells (p = 0.020). CD4+ naive T-cell counts were significantly lower in patients with malignancy compared to those without malignancy (p = 0.006). Genetic analysis performed in 40 patients revealed pathogenic variants in 35%, most frequently involving TACI, followed by ICOS and NFKB2. Following immunoglobulin replacement therapy, infection-related hospitalization rates markedly decreased (from 71.4% to 9.8%).

CONCLUSIONS: CVID patients can present with a wide variety of clinical features. Early diagnosis and treatment can improve quality of life. Identification of genetic defects will enhance understanding of immunopathogenesis opening new avenues for targeted therapies.

articles.title: Factitious Disorder Presenting as Recurrent Aortic Emergencies: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Factitious disorder, historically known as Munchausen's syndrome, is a psychiatric condition characterized by the intentional fabrication or induction of symptoms without obvious external incentives. Patients frequently present with dramatic, medically convincing concerns that can mimic life-threatening illnesses and prompt extensive diagnostic evaluations. Although hemorrhagic presentations have been described, presentations mimicking catastrophic vascular disease are uncommon and pose unique challenges for emergency medicine and vascular teams. CASE REPORT A 37-year-old man with a subsequently documented diagnosis of factitious disorder repeatedly presented to multiple hospitals with dramatic hematemesis concerning for an aortoenteric fistula. Over an 8-year period, he underwent multiple diagnostic evaluations and several aortic interventions, including endovascular aortic repair and later explantation, despite repeated studies showing no aortoenteric pathology. In 2024, he developed bilateral renal artery occlusions secondary to focal aortic dissection requiring emergent stenting. A psychiatric evaluation at an outside institution ultimately diagnosed Munchausen syndrome. Recurrent presentations across healthcare systems, repeatedly negative diagnostic evaluations, inconsistent objective findings, and family-reported discovery of vials containing a red blood-like fluid provided additional evidence concerning for deliberate symptom fabrication. CONCLUSIONS This case report shows how factitious disorder can mimic life-threatening vascular disease. While urgent pathology must be excluded, recurrent high-acuity presentations accompanied by inconsistent objective findings should prompt cross-institutional record review, multidisciplinary evaluation, and broader diagnostic consideration to prevent unnecessary procedural escalation and iatrogenic harm, facilitate earlier diagnostic recognition, and support appropriate psychiatric intervention.

articles.title: Association Between Triglyceride-Glucose Index and Airflow Limitation Severity in Older Adult Nondiabetic Inpatients With Normoxemic COPD.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a reliable insulin resistance biomarker linked with impaired lung function. Existing studies enrolled patients with diabetes or hypoxemia, confounding the relationship between TyG and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) airflow limitation. This study explored the independent association between the TyG index and airflow limitation severity in older adult nondiabetic, normoxemic inpatients with COPD. MATERIAL AND METHODS This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 116 COPD inpatients aged ≥55 years and 87 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Airflow limitation severity was graded based on 2023 GOLD criteria. Ordinal logistic regression analyzed TyG-severity association. Confounders were screened via the change-in-estimate rule, the Brant test verified proportional odds assumptions, and sensitivity analyses assessed data consistency. RESULTS After adjusting for age, BMI, smoking status, and COPD Assessment Test score, elevated TyG was independently associated with more severe airflow limitation (OR = 3.16, 95% CI: 1.04-9.62, P=0.042). Consistent significant results were observed for continuous TyG values (OR=2.74, P=0.045) and TyG tertile trend analysis (P for trend=0.043). The crude intergroup TyG difference was eliminated after smoking adjustment. Sensitivity analyses were directionally consistent, although statistical significance was not uniform across all specifications. This biomarker shows potential for auxiliary severity evaluation for this specific inpatient subgroup, pending further prospective validation. CONCLUSIONS Elevated TyG index independently correlates with aggravated airflow limitation in nondiabetic, normoxemic older adult COPD inpatients. As a readily accessible laboratory index, TyG provides hypothesis-generating correlational evidence for stratifying airflow limitation severity; prospective predictive studies with clinical cutoff validation are mandatory before any routine screening use can be recommended.

articles.title: Prevalence of vascular events among antiphospholipid antibody-positive patients with systemic sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Among patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc), the prevalence of antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) positivity varies widely, and vascular manifestations are heterogeneous. This retrospective study aimed to characterize vascular manifestations among aPL-positive patients with SSc.

METHOD: Patients were included if they had been evaluated at Mayo Clinic from January 1, 1990, through December 31, 2025; diagnosed with SSc by a rheumatologist; and tested for at least 1 aPL. Patients were classified as aPL positive if they were positive for at least 1 aPL and aPL negative if they were negative for all 3 aPLs. Twenty-four vascular manifestations were compared between these groups by using linear, quantile, or logistic regression.

RESULTS: We identified 161 aPL-positive patients and 89 aPL-negative patients. Among patients with a history of pulmonary embolism/deep venous thrombosis (PE/DVT), the odds ratio for unprovoked PE/DVT among aPL-positive patients was 4.58 relative to aPL-negative patients (95% CI, 1.38-15.2; P=.01). When patients with overlap with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases were excluded, median left ventricular ejection fraction was lower for aPL-positive patients than for aPL-negative patients, although this difference was not clinically significant (adjusted median difference, -3.0; 95% CI, -4.9 to -1.1; P=.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Vascular outcomes differed between aPL-positive and aPL-negative patients, as well as between patients with vs without mixed connective tissue disease or overlap disease. However, this exploratory study is limited by its retrospective design. Prospective evaluation of a larger North American cohort or genomic studies would be helpful for understanding the factors that contribute to heterogeneity of vascular manifestations. Key Points • This retrospective study evaluates the prevalence of vascular events among patients with SSc who are aPL positive as compared with those who are aPL negative. • To our knowledge, this is the largest US cohort of aPL-positive patients with SSc. • This study aims to characterize various clinical outcomes among aPL-positive patients with SSc.

articles.title: From prophylaxis to precision immunotherapy via engineering vaccine platforms.
articles.abstract: Vaccines are evolving from antigen-delivery products into modular technologies designed to elicit specific immune functions. Although prophylactic vaccination aims to establish protective memory before exposure, therapeutic vaccination must redirect immunity in the presence of persistent antigen, immune suppression or pathological tissue remodeling. In this Review, we examine how antigen architecture, innate sensing, antigen-presenting-cell targeting, platform design and administration route jointly determine vaccine-induced immune programmes. We compare the distinct requirements of prevention and treatment, focusing on cancer, chronic viral infection and fibrosis, and assess the opportunities and limitations of RNA vaccines, viral vectors, virus-like particles, adjuvants and combination strategies. We then consider how systems vaccinology and artificial intelligence can inform immunogen design and response prediction, while distinguishing computational promise from experimentally validated benefit. We argue that clinical progress depends on matching each vaccine formulation to a defined biological barrier and demonstrating tissue-level activity, safety, durability and practical deployability. This framework connects vaccine engineering to measurable protective or therapeutic outcomes without assuming that any single platform is universally optimal. By integrating immunological principles with advances in vaccine engineering, this Review provides a conceptual basis for selecting and combining technologies according to disease-specific requirements. Ultimately, this perspective may help guide the development of more precise, adaptable and clinically relevant vaccination strategies, bridging the gap between platform innovation and improved outcomes in prevention and therapy.

articles.title: High diagnostic accuracy of 18F-fluoro-L-DOPA PET/CT) for first diagnosis and recurrence in 244 patients with nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma: a retrospective longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-scale data on the diagnostic performance of functional imaging in nonmetastatic pheochromocytoma (PCC) and paraganglioma (PGL), together PPGL, are scarce.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the accuracy of functional imaging for primary tumors and of recurrences of nonmetastatic PPGL during long-term follow-up (FU).

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (1991-2025; imaging data 2008-2025) with noncomparative analysis.

SETTING: Tertiary referral center; routine clinical practice ("real world").

OUTCOMES: Sensitivity and specificity of 18F-DOPA, 68Ga-DOTA-based and 18F-FDG PET/CT in the total cohort and stratified by primary tumor location and germline genetic results, with pathohistology as the reference standard.

PATIENTS: 244 patients with nonmetastatic PPGL, ≥1 functional imaging before first surgery (PreOP) and/or during FU, and FU ≥3 months.

RESULTS: PreOP and FU imaging comprised 154 and 177 18F-DOPA, 32 and 28 18F-FDG and 8 and 37 68Ga-DOTA-based PET/CTs in 177 and 111 patients, respectively. FU was 10.3 ± 8.7 years. Lesion-based sensitivity of the total cohort PreOP and during FU were 97% and 89% for 18F-DOPA, 92% and 100% for 18F-FDG, and 100% and 84% for 68Ga-DOTA. 18F-DOPA was false-negative in 6 of 186 PreOP lesions (one 6-cm PCC, one 5-cm abdominal PGL, four head-and-neck PGL [HNPGL] <1 cm) and in 7 of 63 lesions (in 2 of 28 recurrent patients) during FU.

CONCLUSION: 18F-DOPA, the predominant tracer, provided good accuracy PreOP and during FU, irrespective of primary tumor location or germline genetic results. Sensitivity was reduced for subcentimeter HNPGL and for recurrences presenting as pheochromocytomatosis.

articles.title: Biventricular support without blood contact: an early assessment of soft robotic mechanical circulatory support.
Preclinical progress in the target validation of viroporins: candidates for potential target therapy.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Numerous viral infections necessitate immediate attention, underscoring the urgent need for effective antiviral drugs that can directly inhibit viral functions or indirectly manipulate host factors. Most direct-acting antiviral drugs target two specific viral components: polymerases (including reverse transcriptases) and proteases. Focusing on this narrow range of targets limits the scope of drug development and favors rapid resistance emergence. Therefore, targeting alternative viral components, such as viroporins, is advantageous. Viroporins constitute a family of small, hydrophobic virally encoded proteins that oligomerize to form ion channels, thereby playing crucial roles in various stages of the viral infectivity cycle. Despite their functional significance, they have received considerably less attention from the pharmaceutical industry compared to traditional viral targets.

AREA COVERED: This review delves into the significance of viral channels as potential therapeutic targets, surveying recent advancements and the prospects for future breakthroughs. Viroporins from diverse viral families and their potential inhibition by small molecules are discussed, with special emphasis on bacteria-based channel assays that facilitate high-throughput screening of channel blockers.

EXPERT OPINION: Bacteria-based assays enable rapid discovery and preemptive resistance mapping, while conserved pore architectures raise the prospect of broad-spectrum inhibitors. However, clinical translation requires addressing selectivity, toxicity, and pharmacokinetic challenges.

articles.title: Reducing corticosteroid overuse in Spanish severe asthmatics: a pilot exploratory evaluation of the FOCUS program.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The FOCUS program aimed to improve identification, referral, and management of patients with severe asthma and systemic corticosteroids (SCS) overuse (≥1 g/year), following the recommendations of the Spanish multidisciplinary consensus document on the use of SCS for severe asthma. This pilot exploratory investigation evaluated the implementation of the measures promoted by the program.

METHODS: Aggregated data were collected through a questionnaire and interviews addressed to healthcare professionals (HCPs) experienced in managing severe asthma who participated in the FOCUS program.

RESULTS: Five pulmonologists completed the questionnaire; 80% visited >50 patients/month with asthma, of whom 60% presented severe asthma. HCPs indicated that 40% of these patients were poorly controlled, 48% required maintenance or cycles of SCS, and 21% received >1 g/year of prednisone equivalent. Of those treated with biologics (47%), <30% required SCS.After FOCUS execution, all HCPs implemented protocols for management and referral to severe asthma units, an oral corticosteroids (OCS) calculator for annual OCS dose quantitation, and questionnaires for asthma control. These measures were evaluated as useful/very useful, improving patient management positively/very positively. Furthermore, 80% of HCPs reported that of patients already eligible for biologics, 26-50% initiated treatment with a biological agent; 60% of HCPs considered that 51-75% of patients with biologics reduced SCS overuse. Additionally, 80% of HCPs reported fewer exacerbations and emergency room visits and hospitalizations, and better asthma control.

CONCLUSIONS: In this pilot exploratory evaluation, participating HCPs perceived the FOCUS program as a potential benefit for patients with severe asthma, promoting reduction of SCS overuse and helping achieve better disease control.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of intranasal simvastatin-loaded transbilosomes versus oral simvastatin suspension in attenuating heart failure in rat models induced by doxorubicin and ischemia/reperfusion.
articles.abstract: Simvastatin (SMS) has profound lipid-independent 'pleiotropic' effects that benefit heart failure (HF), but its poor solubility and bioavailability limit its efficacy. This study developed nasal simvastatin-loaded transbilosomes (SLT) to improve drug solubility and bioavailability and mitigate HF. To develop an optimal SLT formulation, the Box-Behnken design was employed. The effectiveness of the nasal SLT was evaluated in vivo using rat models of HF induced by either doxorubicin or ischaemia/reperfusion. Relative to free SMS, the optimal SLT achieved a release increase of 3.81-fold, increased bioavailability by 6.35-fold, enhanced permeation by 7.46-fold, and increased the cardiac accumulation by 1.96-fold. Compared to the oral SMS group, the nasal SLT group exhibited significantly lower levels of triglycerides, cholesterol, LDL, CK-MB, LDH, troponin I, NT-proBNP, NO, MDA, and heart rate, being 1.49-fold, 1.47-fold, 1.40-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.42-fold, 1.59-fold, 1.42-fold, 2.0-fold, 1.90-fold, and 1.99-fold lower, respectively. Conversely, HDL, GSH, SOD, ejection fraction, and fractional shortening increased by 1.5-fold, 1.95-fold, 1.48-fold, 1.48-fold, and 1.42-fold, respectively. Histopathology examination validated the efficacy of the nasal SLT formulation. While these findings represent nasal SLT as a promising insight in alleviating HF, future work is recommended to fully elucidate the distinct contribution of isolated vehicle and route controls.

articles.title: A trifluoromethyl-triggered J-aggregation switch for Cu+-Responsive fluorescence imaging and in vivo application in mice.
articles.abstract: Herein, we elucidate the structural basis of J-aggregation in our previously reported dual-locked fluorescent probe HBimmCue, a trifluoromethyl-substituted sensor for neuronal mitochondrial Cu+. By designing a methyl-substituted control probe HBimmCH3, we demonstrate that the trifluoromethyl group is the critical moiety triggering J-aggregation in PBS. This aggregation enables HBimmCue to function through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) + J-aggregation-caused quenching (J-ACQ) dual-quenching mechanism, affording an exceptional 59-fold fluorescence turn-on response. In contrast, HBimmCH3 lacks J-aggregation entirely and exhibits only a 13.2-fold enhancement via single PET quenching. DFT/TD-DFT calculations and electrostatic potential (ESP) analysis further corroborate the PET mechanism, energy-level shifts, and substituent-dependent assembly behaviors. Given its excellent photophysical performance, we further explored the in vivo imaging capability of HBimmCue. This work demonstrates a facile substituent-engineering approach to modulate J-aggregation, which provides valuable insights for the rational design of high-performance activatable fluorescent probes.

articles.title: An electrochemical sensor platform for rapid nucleic acid detection of Influenza A in unamplified samples and machine-learning-assisted infection diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Influenza A remains a major cause of respiratory infection that demands for rapid, accurate and readily accessible diagnostic tools for timely clinical decision-making and outbreak control. Here, we report a smartphone-assisted electrochemical biosensor platform for amplification-free nucleic acid detection of Influenza A based on magnetic beads enriched target capture and methylene blue (MB)-mediated signal transduction. Under optimized conditions, the platform enabled sensitive detection of both synthetic complementary DNA and RNA, with limits of detection of 0.33aM and 3.32aM, respectively, while maintaining high selectivity against mismatched and non-target sequences. Additionally, the platform is also applied to the detection of RNA extracted from nasopharyngeal swab samples and shows superior discrimination ability between positive and negative samples as well as strong correlation with reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) results. Finally, an optimal machine-learning framework based on a support vector classifier (SVC) is developed to analyze DPV signal profiles and directly classify clinical samples without explicit comparison to blank-current responses, achieving an accuracy of 100% in the clinical cohort. Unlike conventional nucleic acid detection approaches that mainly rely on predefined thresholds or quantitative signal interpretation, this study establishes a machine-learning-assisted classification strategy for direct discrimination of influenza A nucleic-acid positive and negative samples based on electrochemical DPV signal profiles. This simple algorithmic framework is particularly suitable for portable devices with resource constrained microcontrollers to realize rapid result analysis. Our results shed a light on potential portable platform for decentralized rapid nucleic acid testing and promising technique for point-of-care infectious disease diagnostics.

articles.title: Uncovering allergen presence and accumulation in glucose monitoring systems: evidence of a "sponge effect" via validated GC-MS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical benefits associated with the use of continuous and flash glucose monitoring systems (GMS), they are frequently associated with dermatological adverse effects, most notably allergic contact dermatitis (ACD). Chemical analysis of devices is often the only means to confirm the presence of suspected sensitizers or detect emerging allergens in these products. Although previous research efforts lead to the identification of some main allergens such as acrylates and colophony compounds, new allergens continue to emerge and the presence of known allergens in devices cannot be excluded. However, no validated quantitative analytical methods for these compounds in GMS have been reported.

RESULTS: A quantitative gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method was developed and validated, with a focus on optimizing the extraction from the devices. An untargeted screening workflow was incorporated to detect additional potentially relevant allergens. Targeted analysis enabled quantification (14 compounds) or estimated abundance analysis determination (5 compounds) of relevant allergens. The method was applied to unused and used Dexcom G7 and associated adhesive patches. Different allergens were detected and quantified including isobornyl acrylate, methyl dehydroabietate, and isocyanates. Other compounds were only detected in used devices, such as cetyl alcohol, isopropyl palmitate and isopropyl myristate.

SIGNIFICANCE: The analysis revealed the presence of known and new allergens in medical devices for diabetes. Several allergens were present in unused devices, but others were detected only in used devices. These additional compounds likely accumulated from daily usage, leading to what we defined as the "sponge effect".

articles.title: A scoping review to identify patient reported measurement instruments of glucocorticoid toxicity for the OMERACT Glucocorticoid Impact working group.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are commonly used in inflammatory conditions including autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRDs), but can cause considerable adverse effects. The Outcome Measurement in Rheumatology (OMERACT) GC Impact Working Group has developed a core domain set for measuring GC toxicity. Here, we describe work identifying existing patient reported outcome (PRO) measures, with clinician reported outcome measures (ClinROs) reported in a separate article.

METHODS: Medline, EMBASE, CINHAL and Cochrane Central were searched along with hand search of abstracts presented at major relevant rheumatology meetings (abstracts restricted to past 5 years (08/2019 - 08/2024) for studies referring to the use of exogenous GCs and reporting a ClinRO or PRO. Data extraction was performed in duplicate by 2 authors.

RESULTS: 3694 individual records were identified and screened. 76 eligible studies were included for data extraction. 24 studies included a PRO. 16 of these included a validated PRO including a severity rating scale, representing 14 PROs. 6 studies (37.5%) included a patient population with AIRDs, 9 (56.3%) included non-AIRD populations and one included a mixed AIRD/non-AIRD population (6.3%). The PROs most commonly mapped to the mood disturbance (n=12), fatigue (n=8) and sleep disturbance (n=6) domains.

CONCLUSION: We demonstrate the heterogeneity of instruments used to assess GC toxicity, highlighting the need for a standardised measure to adequately convey the burden of GCs on patients and allow comparison between studies. The next step will be to formally map these instruments to the core domain outcome set.

articles.title: TL1A inhibition restores corticosteroid sensitivity in ILC2s and attenuates corticosteroid-resistant asthma.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoids represent the standard therapy for asthma; however, steroid-resistant asthma remains a formidable challenge. Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), similar to T helper 2 (Th2) cells, might be implicated in the pathogenesis. To further explore this, single-cell RNA sequencing of publicly available database, flow cytometry, animal models and in vitro intervention experiments were conducted. Single-cell RNA sequencing identified enriched ILC2 populations, including death receptor 3 (DR3)-expressing ILC2s, in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples from patients with severe asthma, however, intergroup comparisons were limited by low recovery of ILC2s from healthy controls. Clinical sample analyses confirmed that there were the elevated ILC2s proportions in peripheral blood and increased serum level of DR3 ligand, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-like ligand 1A (TL1A) in severe asthma patients. In a house dust mite (HDM) plus IL-33-induced murine asthma model, ILC2s proportion and airway inflammation were increased, which were not effectively suppressed by dexamethasone (DEX). In vitro experiments demonstrated that ILC2s were resistant to steroid-induced apoptosis, and their survival and IL-5/IL-13 secretion were dependent on the TL1A-DR3 axis. TL1A neutralization rescued ILC2 sensitivity to DEX in vitro, whereas recombinant TL1A ligand re-addition under neutralizing conditions partially restored the ILC2 phenotype. Furthermore, in vivo TL1A intervention alleviated HDM + IL-33-induced airways inflammation in the experimental mice. Thus, the TL1A and DR3 pathway in ILC2s may constitute one of crucial mechanisms underlying steroid resistance in severe asthma, representing a novel therapeutic target.

articles.title: ZEBRA score, a novel specialized prognostic model for thrombotic risk in myelofibrosis.
articles.abstract: Patients with myelofibrosis (MF) face a substantial thrombotic risk, yet no MF-specific tool identifies those at highest risk. We retrospectively studied 289 patients with MF from six Croatian centers, using Fine-and-Gray models accounting for the competing risk of death. ZEBRA (AniZocytosis, Extra-leukocytes, Blood counts, and comoRbidity Assessment) was derived in 192 patients with complete data. Incidence rates of thrombosis and major bleeding were 3.66% and 1.91% patient-years, with the highest thrombotic risk in post-polycythemia vera MF. JAK2 mutation was not directly associated with thrombosis but moderated several inflammation-related predictors. Mutually independent predictors of thrombosis were leukocytosis (≥11 × 109/L), low absolute lymphocyte count (≤1.5 × 109/L), low absolute monocyte count (≤0.7 × 109/L), high red-cell-distribution-width (≥20%), and high age-adjusted Charlson-comorbidity-index (≥4 points). Combined into the ZEBRA score (5 points for leukocytosis and 1 for each other feature), these stratified patients into low- (0-3 points), intermediate- (4-6 points), and high-risk groups (7-9 points) with 24-month cumulative incidence of thrombosis of 2%, 6.9%, and 22.7%, respectively. Apparent C-index was 0.769 (optimism-corrected 0.672-0.747). The thrombosis-to-bleeding incidence rate ratio increased from 0.38 in low- to 1.43 in intermediate- and 7.33 in high-risk patients. Among patients without prior thrombosis or without JAK2 mutation with age > 60 years, ZEBRA high-risk status identified subgroups with substantial thrombotic risk. ZEBRA, the first MF-specific thrombotic risk score, uses routine parameters, identifies patients with predominantly thrombotic rather than bleeding events, and may refine risk assessment in patients considered at low risk by conventional criteria. External validation is warranted.

articles.title: Retinopathy of prematurity in ethiopia: a prospective multicenter study on prevalence, risk factors, and treatment outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is an increasing cause of childhood blindness in Africa due to absent or underdeveloped screening and treatment programs. In Ethiopia, only a few centers provide continuous screening and treatment for preterm infants with ROP, and data on its incidence and treatment outcomes remain limited. This multicenter study aimed to determine the prevalence, risk factors, and treatment outcomes of ROP in two tertiary eye care centers in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A prospective longitudinal study was conducted in two university hospitals with level-three neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). All preterm infants with gestational age ≤ 34 weeks, birth weight ≤ 2000 g, or an unstable clinical course were included. Demographic, neonatal, and treatment data were collected and analyzed using SPSS version 26.

RESULTS: A total of 173 preterm infants (346 eyes) were examined. The cohort showed a slight female predominance, with a male-to-female ratio of 0.83. Mean birth weight was 1299.6 g (range: 700-3400 g), and mean gestational age was 31.3 weeks (range: 27-40 weeks). ROP of any stage was diagnosed in 80 eyes (23.1%). The disease was bilateral in 35 infants (77.8%) and unilateral in 10 (22.2%). Stage 1 (35 eyes, 43.75%) was the most common presentation, followed by stage 2 (29 eyes, 36.25%), and Stage 3 (8 eyes, 10%). Aggressive posterior ROP (APROP) was diagnosed in 8 eyes (10%). Overall, type 1 ROP requiring treatment was seen in 15 eyes (18.75%). On multivariable logistic regression analysis, blood transfusion (AOR=2.71, p=0.028), multiple birth (AOR=4.29, p<0.001), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) (AOR=7.82, p<0.001), premature rupture of membranes (PROM) (AOR= 3.94, p=0.022), maternal hypertension(AOR=3.02, p=0.035), lower birth weight (AOR=2.67,p=0.004), lower gestational age (AOR=1.94,p=0.043) and study center (AOR = 5.08, p = 0.001) were independently associated with ROP. The majority of ROP cases (81.25%) were managed by observation, while 15.0% were treated with intravitreal bevacizumab alone and 3.75% underwent bevacizumab treatment followed by peripheral retinal laser ablation. Overall, 81.25% regressed spontaneously, 16.25% regressed after treatment, and 2.5% progressed to retinal detachment.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of ROP was lower than previously reported national data. However, a higher prevalence of APROP was observed, a finding not reported in earlier studies. In multivariable analysis, lower gestational age, lower birth weight, blood transfusion, multiple birth, IVH, PROM, maternal hypertension, and study center were independently associated with ROP.

articles.title: [A case of aortic saddle embolism with diagnosis difficulty due to transient symptom improvement following early recanalization].
articles.abstract: A 70-year-old man with obesity, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with paraplegia, sensory impairment, and lower limb pain. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed occlusion of the distal abdominal aorta, and he was initially diagnosed with Leriche's syndrome. His symptoms promptly improved; however, they recurred on hospital day 4, accompanied by progressive rhabdomyolysis and renal impairment. Magnetic resonance imaging of the lower extremities showed multiple muscle infarctions. His condition subsequently improved, and he was able to walk with a walker. Contrast-enhanced CT on hospital day 35 demonstrated recanalization of the occluded vessels, and he was finally diagnosed with aortic saddle embolism. This case illustrates that early recanalization can cause transient symptom improvement, potentially leading to diagnostic difficulty.

articles.title: [Chronic spinal muscular atrophy presenting with monomelic amyotrophy involving the ‍left lower limb].
articles.abstract: A 69-year-old man with familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (TNNT2 missense mutation) presented with gradually progressive atrophy and weakness of the left thigh. No family history of neurologic or neuromuscular disease was apparent. Weakness of the left lower limb first became apparent in his late 30s. At age 62, the patient noted atrophy of the left thigh; at 66, he underwent cervical laminectomy and at 67, lumbar laminectomy. Neither operation resulted in clinical improvement. Symptoms were limited to the left lower limb and progressed very slowly. Neurologic examination disclosed marked atrophy of the left quadriceps femoris and mild atrophy of the left tibialis anterior. Mild weakness was evident in the left hamstrings, iliopsoas, and quadriceps; in the last of these, fasciculations were noted. Deep tendon reflexes were decreased in the upper extremities and absent in the lower extremities. No Babinski or other pyramidal tract sign was elicited. No bulbar dysfunction, sensory disturbance, or autonomic dysfunction was apparent. Nerve conduction studies were normal. Electromyography (EMG) showed high amplitudes and long-duration action potentials in the left vastus medialis and tibialis anterior muscles. Abnormalities suggesting denervation were found in both arms and legs, especially on the left. While clinical signs favored monomelic amyotrophy involving the left leg, EMG findings suggested chronic spinal muscular atrophy.

articles.title: Spatial Heterogeneity of Coronary Vasomotor Dysfunction in Patients With Angina and Non-Obstructive Coronary Arteries　- Two-Territory Assessment of the Left Anterior Descending and Right Coronary Arteries.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The diagnostic paradigm for angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries assumes that vasomotor dysfunction is a global, homogeneous phenomenon, typically assessed via single-vessel interrogation. However, emerging evidence suggests that vascular pathology may be territory specific, potentially obscuring true patient-level pathophysiology and compromising clinical precision.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analyzed 213 patients from the prospective multicenter J-CMD registry (UMIN000047609) who underwent vasomotor and physiological assessment in both the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries. We evaluated spatial concordance for epicardial vasospasm (EVS), microvascular spasm (MVS), and coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD; defined as coronary flow reserve <2.5), subclassified into structural or functional CMD subtypes (index of microcirculatory resistance ≥25 and <25, respectively). Kappa statistics revealed fair agreement for EVS (κ=0.26) and slight agreement for structural (κ=0.10) and functional (κ=0.05) CMD. Overall, diagnostic discordance affected 58.7% of patients. Consequently, a conventional LAD-only strategy would have misclassified 29.1% of the cohort and failed to identify mixed-type CMD (inter-territorial discordance in CMD subtypes), occurring in 7.0% of patients. Two-territory interrogation significantly enhanced diagnostic yield, reducing the prevalence of no identifiable dysfunction from 38.0% to 27.2% by uncovering hidden, territory-specific pathologies.

CONCLUSIONS: Single-vessel assessment may provide an incomplete representation of patient-level vasomotor dysfunction. Although 2-territory assessment enables more granular phenotypic characterization and reduces the under-recognition of CMD and vasospasm, its incremental value in improving clinical outcomes remains to be established.

articles.title: γ-Polyglutamic acid enables sodium reduction via simultaneous KCl bitterness masking and saltiness amplification.
articles.abstract: High-salt diets are strongly associated with hypertension and cardiovascular diseases. Potassium chloride (KCl) is the most promising salt substitute, but its inherent metallic bitterness severely limits its food application. Here, the natural biopolymer γ-polyglutamic acid (γ-PGA) enabled a 50% NaCl reduction by simultaneously masking KCl bitterness and enhancing saltiness. Adding 10% γ-PGA lowered the bitterness score of a 1:1 NaCl/KCl blend from 5.0 to 1.9 while raising the saltiness score from 6.8 to 9.0. Mechanistically, γ-PGA chelates K+ and retards its release, while prolonging Na+ retention on the tongue surface and facilitating Na+ permeation through the mucin layer. In salted duck and French fries, the γ-PGA low-sodium salt restored saltiness to commercial-salt levels with barely perceptible bitterness. In mice, it promoted urinary Na+ and K+ excretion and lowered serum catecholamine and creatinine, suggesting potential benefits against hypertension and renal injury.

articles.title: Recorded Urinary Ketone Results After Initiation of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Patients With and Without Diabetes: A Single-Center Retrospective Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are prescribed for diabetes, chronic heart failure, and chronic kidney disease but are rarely associated with ketoacidosis, including euglycemic ketoacidosis. Although ketonuria is nonspecific and is not diagnostic of ketoacidosis, a positive urinary ketone result may prompt further clinical assessment. This study compared the proportion of participants with a recorded urinary ketone result after SGLT2i initiation between those with and without diabetes.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center descriptive study included adults who initiated SGLT2i therapy at the study hospital between April 2022 and March 2023 and continued treatment for at least 180 days. Urinary ketone results, semiquantitative grades, and selected gastrointestinal symptoms documented in the electronic health record were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 465 participants, a urinary ketone result was recorded in 273 of 350 participants in the diabetes group (78.0%) and 65 of 115 participants in the non-diabetes group (56.5%) (odds ratio, 2.73; 95% confidence interval, 1.74-4.26). During follow-up, 27 participants had a positive urinary ketone result; the highest recorded grade was 2+ or higher in 17 (63.0%). Among 127 participants without a recorded urinary ketone result, selected gastrointestinal symptoms were documented in 11 (8.7%), and no blood ketone result was identified for these participants. No documented hospital admissions for ketoacidosis were identified in the study hospital records.

CONCLUSIONS: The proportion of participants with a recorded urinary ketone result after SGLT2i initiation was lower in the non-diabetes group than in the diabetes group. Although urinary ketone positivity alone cannot confirm ketoacidosis, a positive semiquantitative result may prompt context-based clinical review and, when clinically indicated, confirmatory evaluation. These findings suggest the importance of maintaining awareness of SGLT2i-associated ketoacidosis, including euglycemic ketoacidosis, regardless of diabetes status, and a potential role for pharmacists in facilitating context-based ketone assessment when clinically indicated.

articles.title: Clinical Guideline Adherence for Acute Pain Management in Adults with Sickle Cell Disease: A Retrospective Chart Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In 2020, the American Society of Hematology released updated clinical guidelines for the management of acute and chronic sickle cell pain, emphasizing timely delivery of analgesia, non-opioid pharmacological therapy, and implementation of non-pharmacological interventions.

OBJECTIVES: The primary objectives of this study were to describe adherence to selected guidelines for the management of sickle cell pain episodes during hospital admission, as well as characterize the study population and admissions. A secondary objective was to describe temporal changes in length of stay and opioid doses.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of patients with sickle cell disease with admissions for acute pain episodes at Toronto General and Toronto Western Hospitals in Toronto, Canada between January 2020 and December 2024. Patient demographics, admissions trends, and clinical outcomes were extracted and evaluated. Emergency department opioid timing data were only available from June 2022 to December 2024.

RESULTS: There were 265 patients accounting for 823 admissions, with 43 (16%) patients accounting for 80% of total length of stay. Time from emergency admission to first opioid in less than 1 hour was met in 44.4% of admissions, with an overall median time of 1.1 hours. For pharmacologic management, 771 of all admissions (93.7%) received opioids, with 708 (86.0%) of these also receiving non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Documented use of non-pharmacological management was rare (0.0-6.2%). Length of stay at Toronto General Hospital was observed to decrease from 12.6 to 8.6 days (p < 0.001), with an increase from 6.9 to 12.2 days observed at Toronto Western Hospital (p = 0.34).

CONCLUSIONS: Further efforts are required to ensure full alignment with the American Society of Hematology guidelines, including timely administration of first opioids and adoption of non-pharmacological interventions, with future research addressing retrospective study design limitations like data unavailability.

articles.title: Fast responses of oxidative stress and antioxidant defense systems to acute temperature changes in the Yesso scallop Mizuhopecten yessoensis.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the short-term effects of acute temperature changes on early oxidative stress and stress-related responses in the Yesso scallop Mizuhopecten yessoensis. The intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), activities of antioxidant enzyme (e.g., glutathione S-transferase [GST], glutathione peroxidase [GPx], catalase [CAT], and superoxide dismutase [SOD]) and transcriptional expression of stress-related genes (e.g., GPx, CuZn/SOD, heat shock protein 70 [hsp70] and hsp90) were measured in response to acute temperature changes. At low temperature (12 °C), ROS level increased for up to 24 h and subsequently decreased, whereas at high temperature (28 °C), ROS levels slightly decreased after 24 and 48 h. Acute temperature stress significantly altered antioxidant enzymatic activities and stress-related genes expressions in M. yessoensis. Exposure to high temperate (28 °C) resulted in significant reductions in GPx and CAT activities, while GST and SOD activities increased after 72 and 48 h, respectively. In contrast, all stress-related genes were significantly downregulated in response to low temperature (12 °C). Notably, hsp70 and hsp90 expression exhibited significant modulations under high temperature (28 °C), suggesting their potential role in heat tolerance in M. yessoensis. In conclusion, high temperature led to an increase in the production of ROS and a corresponding change in the activity of antioxidant enzymes with the transcriptional expression of stress-related genes as the M. yessoensis attempts to mitigate the stress. Overall, these findings provide valuable information that acute water temperature changes induce ROS-mediated oxidative stress, resulting in cellular damage and the activation of antioxidant defense system in M. yessoensis.

articles.title: Therapeutic Endoscopic Intervention in Cirrhosis: Routine Clinical, Laboratory and Ultrasound Markers in a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy remains the reference standard for detecting and grading esophageal varices in cirrhosis, but repeated surveillance is invasive and resource-intensive. Most non-invasive strategies focus on ruling out high-risk varices. We assessed whether routinely available clinical, laboratory and ultrasound parameters are associated with clinically relevant endoscopic findings, focusing on therapeutic endoscopic intervention as a pragmatic real-world endpoint.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with confirmed liver cirrhosis treated at a German tertiary care hospital between 2014 and 2021. Only the first examination episode per patient was analyzed. Gastroscopy, abdominal ultrasound and laboratory testing were eligible when performed during the same hospital stay. The primary endpoint was therapeutic intervention during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. Secondary endpoints were presence of esophageal varices and Paquet grade II/III varices. These summaries were data-derived, unweighted and not internally or externally validated. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, and logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, esophageal varices were present in 235 (91.4%), and therapeutic endoscopic intervention was performed in 38 (14.8%). The intervention point-based summary, including ascites, hemoglobin <9.9 g/dL and alanine aminotransferase >33.5 U/L, was calculable in 248 patients and showed moderate apparent discrimination for intervention, with an AUC of 0.706. Each additional point was associated with higher odds of intervention (OR=2.80, 95%CI: 1.73-4.53; p<0.001). In multivariable analysis, hemoglobin <9.9 g/dL and alanine aminotransferase >33.5 U/L remained associated with intervention, whereas ascites did not. Secondary point-based summaries for esophageal varices and Paquet grade II/III varices showed apparent AUCs of 0.775 and 0.623, respectively, but were limited by complete-case sample size and endpoint distribution.

CONCLUSIONS: Routine clinical, laboratory and ultrasound parameters were associated with clinically relevant endoscopic findings in cirrhosis, particularly therapeutic endoscopic intervention. Low hemoglobin and elevated alanine aminotransferase were associated with intervention need, but the findings likely reflect clinical presentation and therapeutic endoscopic relevance rather than portal pressure alone. The exploratory point-based summaries are descriptive, data-derived tools and should not replace established non-invasive strategies or endoscopic assessment. Prospective external validation is required before clinical use.

articles.title: Effects of Liraglutide as Add-on to Metformin on Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis in Patients with Prediabetes and MASLD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The coexistence of prediabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common and accelerates metabolic and hepatic complications. This study evaluated the effects of liraglutide on hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in patients with prediabetes and MASLD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with prediabetes and MASLD who received either liraglutide plus metformin (liraglutide group, n=142) or metformin alone (control group, n=121) for 12 months. Primary outcomes were changes in controlled attenuation parameter (CAP), liver stiffness measurement (LSM), Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index, and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease fibrosis score (NFS). Secondary outcomes included anthropometric measurements, glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and liver enzymes.

RESULTS: After 12 months of treatment, CAP values decreased significantly in both groups (both p<0.001), with significantly lower values in the liraglutide group compared to the control group (p<0.001). LSM showed significant reductions in both groups, with more pronounced improvement in the liraglutide group (p<0.001) and significantly lower values compared to the control group at 12 months (p<0.05). FIB-4 index and NFS decreased significantly in both groups (p<0.05), though between-group differences did not reach statistical significance (p>0.05). The liraglutide group achieved significantly greater improvements in body weight, waist circumference, glycemic parameters [fasting plasma glucose (FPG), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting insulin, homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR)], triglycerides, and non-high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol compared to the control group (all p<0.05). Liver enzymes [alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST]), gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)] improved significantly in both groups, with greater reductions in the liraglutide group (all p<0.001). The most common adverse events were mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal symptoms, with no serious adverse events reported.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prediabetes and MASLD, 12-month liraglutide as add-on therapy to metformin was associated with significant improvements in hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness measurement compared to metformin monotherapy, alongside favorable metabolic effects and an acceptable safety profile. These findings support liraglutide as a potential therapeutic option for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Real-world Gastrointestinal, Pancreaticobiliary, Cardiorenal, Metabolic and Nutritional Outcomes of GLP-1 or GIP Receptors Agonists -based Therapy in Chronic Pancreatitis.
articles.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Glucagon-like peptide-1(GLP-1) receptor agonists and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonists are increasingly used for metabolic disease, but their safety profile in patients with chronic pancreatitis (CP) remains uncertain. We compared several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcomes in patients with CP exposed to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus propensity-matched unexposed controls.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX federated real-world data platform. Adults with CP were classified by recorded exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide versus no recorded exposure to those drugs. Risk analyses and Kaplan-Meier time-to-event analyses were done.

RESULTS: After matching, median follow-up was 588 (IQR 831) versus 879 (IQR 807), respectively. Nausea/vomiting occurred in 656/4,938 (risk 0.133) versus 1,099/5,585 (risk 0.197), with risk ratio (RR) 0.675 (95%CI: 0.618-0.738) and hazard ratio (HR) 0.710 (95%CI: 0.645-0.783). Bowel obstruction/ileus occurred in 241/9,103 (risk 0.026) versus 466/8,949 (risk 0.052), with RR=0.508 (95%CI: 0.436-0.592) and HR=0.556 (95%CI: 0.476-0.649). Upper gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 355/8,536 (risk 0.042) versus 608/8,657 (risk 0.070), with RR=0.592 (95%CI: 0.521-0.673) and HR=0.659 (95%CI: 0.578-0.751). Biliary/procedural outcomes were lower, including cholecystectomy (risk 0.023 vs 0.049; HR=0.486, 95%CI: 0.412-0.572) and ERCP (risk 0.026 vs 0.064; HR=0.420, 95%CI: 0.362-0.488). Recurrent acute pancreatitis occurred in 329/5,639 exposed patients (risk 0.058) versus 579/5,499 controls (risk 0.105), with HR=0.584 (95%CI: 0.510-0.669). Additional associations included lower insulin initiation (risk 0.178 vs 0.269; HR=0.731, 95%CI: 0.658-0.812), heart failure (risk 0.061 vs 0.101; HR=0.687, 95%CI: 0.613-0.770), myocardial infarction (risk 0.039 vs 0.054; HR=0.818, 95%CI: 0.712-0.939 and acute kidney injury (risk 0.086 vs 0.150; HR=0.643, 95%CI: 0.580-0.712), malnutrition (risk 0.049 vs 0.107; HR=0.491, 95%CI: 0.438-0.550).

CONCLUSIONS: Exposure to dulaglutide, semaglutide, or tirzepatide was associated with lower recorded risks across several gastrointestinal, cardio, renal and metabolic outcome domains. These findings should be interpreted with caution, and further prospective studies are required to confirm the same.

articles.title: CYP2C19 metabolizer phenotype and recurrent documented gastroesophageal reflux disease after proton pump inhibitor initiation: A cohort study from the All of Us Research Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: CYP2C19 influences proton pump inhibitor (PPI) exposure, but its association with longitudinal gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) documentation remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations between CYP2C19 phenotype and documented GERD outcomes after PPI initiation.

METHODS: This retrospective All of Us cohort included 21,135 adults with GERD, a definitive CYP2C19 phenotype, and 365-day post-index observation. Recurrent documented GERD required at least 2 diagnosis dates occurring from day 31 to day 365 separated by at least 30 days. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (ARRs). A secondary composite assessed reflux testing or antireflux interventions.

RESULTS: Recurrent documented GERD occurred in 5,927 participants (28.0%). Compared with normal metabolizers, ARRs (95% CI) were 1.11 (0.97-1.26) for poor, 1.02 (0.97-1.07) for intermediate, 1.04 (0.98-1.09) for rapid, and 0.97 (0.87-1.08) for ultrarapid metabolizers (global P = .353). Estimates were similar across alternative documentation definitions, ancestral alignment, and the restriction to omeprazole only. Among 20 928 secondary analysis participants, 245 (1.17%) underwent further reflux testing or intervention (global P = .679). Dose and ongoing exposure were not modeled.

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: CYP2C19 phenotype was not significantly associated with these documentation-based outcomes. This large genomic cohort extends evidence to longitudinal health care records, but exposure uncertainty and multifactorial GERD limit inferences about active treatment responses.
