The findings do not establish equivalence or justify changing genotype-guided dosing recommendations; clinical decisions should also consider dose, adherence, and the underlying symptom mechanisms.

articles.title: Are the nice ones left behind: a European multi-country survey on the relationship between altruism and forgone care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Forgone care was widespread during the COVID-19 pandemic and is linked to poorer health outcomes. Research on its determinants has focused mainly on sociodemographic characteristics and access barriers, but has not examined the role of individual dispositions such as altruism. Because forgoing care during a pandemic can benefit others, for instance by leaving scarce resources available or reducing infection risk for health care staff, altruistic individuals may be more likely to forgo care. This study examines whether altruism is associated with self-initiated forgone care during the COVID-19 pandemic.

METHODS: We used survey data from eight European countries (Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain, and the United Kingdom). The analytic sample comprised 6,859 participants, with approximately 830 to 930 per country.

RESULTS: Altruism was positively associated with forgone care, and this relationship remained robust when accounting for different degrees of delay, types of health care providers, and countries. Furthermore, age moderated this association.

CONCLUSION: By identifying altruism as a factor associated with forgoing care, this study contributes to a better understanding of health care utilization during crises. The results are relevant from a health policy perspective, as they have implications for health care systems and health outcomes during crises.

articles.title: Hospital frailty risk score and one-year mortality after intravenous thrombolysis in older patients with acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is a clinical syndrome characterized by a decline of function across multiple organ systems. It is also associated with higher short-term mortality following ischemic stroke. However, the impact of frailty on functional outcome in acute ischemic stroke remains uncertain. This study examines the association between frailty and one-year mortality after ischemic stroke in patients receiving intravenous thrombolysis.

METHODS: In this monocentric retrospective cohort study, we calculated the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS) for all patients over 65 years with ischemic stroke who received intravenous thrombolysis from 2014 to 2019. Kaplan-Meier-Analysis and Cox-regression analysis were used to assess the impact of frailty on one-year mortality after ischemic stroke in these patients.

RESULTS: A total of 423 patients were included in our analysis. Of these, 360 patients (85.2%) had a low risk of frailty (HFRS < 5) and 63 patients (14.9%) had an increased frailty risk with an HFRS ≥ 5. The NIHSS at discharge (3 [IQR 1-6] vs. 4 [ IQR 2-9] was higher in patients with frailty-risk. One-year mortality was 20.6% and 34.9%, respectively (log-rank p = 0.016). In multivariable Cox regression analysis adjusted for age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index, NIHSS at admission and ASPECTS, each one-point increase in the HFRS was associated with a higher hazard of one-year mortality (HR 1,085 (95% KI 1,015-1,160), p = 0,017). Adding the HFRS to the baseline clinical model improved model fit (likelihood ratio test, p = 0.028).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients aged ≥ 65 years who received intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke, a higher administratively derived HFRS was independently associated with a higher hazard of one-year mortality. These findings support further evaluation of the HFRS as a pragmatic prognostic marker but should not be interpreted as evidence for withholding reperfusion therapy.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: not applicable.

articles.title: Matrix stiffness-regulated NSUN2 Increases HSP90AA1 expression to promote endoplasmic reticulum stress and hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
articles.abstract: Extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness elevation, a prominent mechanical attribute in liver cirrhosis, is a key driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. RNA 5-methylcytosine (m5C) modification regulates multiple RNA species to influence tumorigenesis, but its role in mechanotransduction-especially in response to matrix stiffness-remains unclear. Here, we found that increased matrix stiffness enhances HCC cell proliferation and metastasis, accompanied by elevated global m5C levels. High stiffness triggers autocrine transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) secretion in HCC cells, which activates transcription factor Smad3 to upregulate NSUN2, a core m5C methyltransferase. Clinically, high NSUN2 expression and elevated m5C levels correlate with poor prognosis in HCC patients. Further studies showed NSUN2 directly binds to HSP90AA1 mRNA, enhances its m5C modification, and recruits the m5C reader ALYREF to stabilize HSP90AA1 mRNA. We also confirmed the matrix stiffness-NSUN2-HSP90AA1 axis activates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, forming a pro-tumor cascade that promotes HCC growth and progression. Notably, we identified Vilanterol as a candidate NSUN2-targeting compound that effectively downregulates NSUN2 expression and global m5C levels and suppresses HCC malignant phenotypes. Collectively, our findings uncover a previously unrecognized regulatory axis, the matrix stiffness-NSUN2-HSP90AA1-ER stress axis, in HCC, and suggest that Vilanterol may serve as a promising therapeutic agent for HCC.

articles.title: Effect of critical illness and mechanical ventilation on energy and substrate metabolism in patients with liver cirrhosis: an indirect calorimeter-based cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Energy and substrate metabolism are altered in liver cirrhosis and may worsen with critical illness. Indirect calorimetry provides accurate metabolic assessment. This study compared resting energy expenditure (REE), respiratory quotient (RQ), and substrate oxidation among healthy controls, non-critically ill, and critically ill cirrhosis patients.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This prospective observational study included 63 healthy controls (Group I; age 32.5 years; 46% male), 68 non-critically ill cirrhosis patients (Group II; age 47.5 years; 85.3% male; MELD 15), and 70 critically ill ventilated cirrhosis patients (Group III; age 49.7 years; 75.7% male; MELD 29). Valid indirect calorimetry (Quark RMR) measurements were available for all 63 controls and for 66 and 68 patients in Groups II and III, respectively. Metabolic state was classified using the measured-to-predicted REE ratio (Harris-Benedict): hypometabolic (< 0.9), normometabolic (0.9-1.1), and hypermetabolic (> 1.1). Compared with Group I, RQ declined across Groups II and III (0.86, 0.80, 0.74; p=0.003), carbohydrate oxidation decreased (60.3%, 30.3%, 13.3%; p<0.001), and fat oxidation increased (27%, 59.8%, 72.7%; p<0.001), indicating progressive starvation, while REE remained comparable (1446, 1485, 1415 kcal/day; p=0.32). Hypometabolism was more prevalent in Group III than Groups I and II (45.6% vs. 22.2% and 30.3%; p=0.015). Group III had higher pro-inflammatory markers (IL-6, CRP) and non-esterified fatty acid levels. Across Child-Pugh classes A, B, and C, RQ decreased (0.86, 0.79, 0.75) and fat oxidation increased (36.3%, 69%, 73%), with minimal changes in REE.

CONCLUSION: Liver cirrhosis is characterized by a progressive starvation phenotype without a significant increase in absolute energy expenditure. Critically ill patients with cirrhosis showed further reduction in carbohydrate utilization, without a significant increase in energy expenditure. These findings suggest that altered substrate utilization may be the predominant metabolic abnormality in cirrhosis, particularly during critical illness.

articles.title: Racial/Ethnic and Sex Disparities in Obesity: Socioeconomic, Dietary, and Physical Activity Predictors from NHANES 2017-2018.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity disparities in the United States occur across racial/ethnic, sex, socioeconomic, and age groups and are shaped by unequal social and structural conditions. An intersectionality perspective emphasizes that race/ethnicity, sex, and socioeconomic position may jointly pattern exposure to health-promoting or health-limiting resources rather than operating as isolated characteristics.

OBJECTIVE: To examine associations among socioeconomic status (SES) indicators (education, income), dietary behaviors (food outside the home [FOH] and fast food [FF]), physical activity (walking/biking, moderate recreational activity [MRA] and vigorous recreational activity [VRA]), and obesity indicators (BMI, percent body fat [POF], waist circumference [WC]) across Hispanic, non-Hispanic White (White), and non-Hispanic Black (Black) adults and by sex.

METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 3,942 adults aged 20-80 years using NHANES 2017-2018; POF analyses were restricted to 1,971 participants aged 20-59 years per the NHANES DXA protocol. Two-way MANOVA and independent t-tests evaluated associations across race/ethnicity and sex. NHANES two-year sampling weights were applied, but masked variance strata and primary sampling units were not fully incorporated; inferential estimates are therefore exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously.

RESULTS: Unweighted mean BMI was 25.1 kg/m2. Lower education was associated with higher BMI and POF in selected race/ethnicity-by-sex subgroups (P <  .05). Low annual family income (< $25,000) was associated with higher BMI, WC, and POF, particularly among Hispanic and Black women. Men reported more FOH and FF consumption than women (P <  .001). VRA showed the largest physical-activity associations with obesity measures, including among Black men (η2 = 0.049-0.057).

CONCLUSIONS: SES, dietary behaviors, and physical activity showed heterogeneous associations with obesity measures across intersecting racial/ethnic and sex groups. Because the data are cross-sectional and predate major post-2018 changes in the food, social-policy, and obesity landscape, interpret the findings as a historical, nationally representative baseline rather than current prevalence estimates or a contemporary prediction model. Future studies should assess whether these patterns persist in newer NHANES cycles and directly evaluate structural and policy contexts.

articles.title: Safety and clinical outcomes of cataract surgery follow-up at urban hospitals versus rural vision centres.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distance to healthcare facilities is a barrier to follow-up adherence after cataract surgery in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated the effectiveness of decentralised postoperative care at rural vision centres compared to urban hospital-based follow-up after cataract surgery.

METHODS: Eyes that underwent cataract surgery at Aravind Eye Hospital Pondicherry, India (urban hospital) from July 1st, 2022 to June 30th, 2023 were reviewed. Patients received postoperative month one (POM1) follow-up at either the urban hospital or one of 12 rural vision centres. Variables collected included demographics, payment type, surgical details, complications, preoperative UCVA, postoperative day one (POD1) and postoperative month one (POM1) best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and IOP. Predictors of good visual outcome (BCVA ≥ 6/12) were assessed.

RESULTS: Of 46,624 eyes, 87.1% (N = 40,619) received POM1 postoperative follow-up at the urban hospital and 12.9% (N = 6,005) at a vision centre. Vision centre patients were more often female, received subsidised care, and had better preoperative VA (p < 0.001). At POM1, BCVA was 6/6-6/18 in 94.9% of urban hospital eyes and 94.2% of vision centre eyes. Eyes receiving vision centre follow-up had fewer cases of BCVA < 6/60 (0.3% vs. 1.2%, p < 0.001). Postoperative infection rates were low across groups (0.02%). Adjusted analyses showed vision centre follow-up was associated with higher odds of good visual outcome ( ≥ 6/12) (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.37-1.63, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Decentralised follow-up at vision centres was non-inferior to urban hospitals in POM1 VA and infection rates. Vision centres offer a scalable solution to improve access to cataract care without compromising safety.

articles.title: ECG foundation models for cardiovascular screening in a cohort of young competitive athletes.
articles.abstract: AI-powered cardiac screening could evolve sports medicine by boosting accuracy, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, with automated ECG interpretation based on foundation models becoming key for large-scale athlete screening. Before deployment, it is crucial to verify whether these clinically developed models are applicable to this population. We evaluated whether ECG foundation models trained on general clinical populations can diagnose athlete-specific ECG findings. We fine-tuned three models (ECG-FM, HuBERT-ECG, ECGFounder) on PhysioNet/CinC 2021, 87,662 samples, and tested them on 43 expert-annotated ECGs from highly trained/national-level athletes. Performance was strong on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (AUROC 0.97, AUPRC 0.57, Sensitivity 0.89) but dropped on athletes' data, confirming domain shift. ECGFounder performed best (AUROC 0.84, AUPRC 0.72, Sensitivity 0.57) and detected the most frequent findings, Sinus Bradycardia (AUROC 0.87) and Sinus Arrhythmia (AUROC 0.95), well. Per-label estimates for rare classes must be interpreted cautiously, given the small cohort. This work contributes to developing athlete-focused AI frameworks for reliable ECG-based screening.

articles.title: Efficacy and mechanisms of supplementary motor area rTMS for freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease: a randomized sham-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and neural mechanisms of 10‑Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the supplementary motor area (SMA) for freezing of gait (FOG) in Parkinson's disease (PD) assessed OFF medication.

METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 52 PD patients with FOG were randomized (1:1) to receive 12 sessions of 10-Hz SMA-rTMS (n = 26) or sham (n = 26) over 4 weeks. A total of 50 patients (26 rTMS, 24 sham) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The primary outcome was the change in the New Freezing of Gait Questionnaire (NFOG-Q) score from baseline to post-intervention (T1). Secondary outcomes included motor/non-motor scales, instrumented gait parameters at T1 and 4-week follow-up (T2), with functional MRI (fMRI) to explore neural mechanisms.

RESULTS: At T1, the active group showed a significantly greater NFOG‑Q reduction than sham (between-group difference - 2.36, 95% CI - 3.47 to - 1.25, p < 0.001), with the between-group difference persisting at T2 (- 2.57, p = 0.040). Active rTMS also produced early gains in motor function, balance, and multiple gait parameters, with stride velocity and length maintained at T2. Task-based fMRI revealed enhanced SMA-parietal connectivity during FOG-provoking motor imagery that correlated with clinical and gait improvements. Non‑motor symptoms also showed improvements that were maintained at T2.

CONCLUSIONS: High‑frequency SMA‑rTMS produced reductions in FOG severity alongside improvements in gait kinematics and non‑motor symptoms in PD that were maintained at four-week follow-up, mediated by task-dependent enhancement of SMA-parietal network integration. The dissociation between transient motor benefits and retained axial and affective improvements supports SMA-rTMS as a circuit-targeted intervention with short-term therapeutic potential, particularly for OFF-state freezing and associated neuropsychiatric symptoms.

articles.title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
articles.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. Population-based and clinical studies define the epidemiology, risk factors, presentation, diagnosis, and management of PSC. Studies of human biospecimens, including microbiome and metabolomic analyses, describe biological changes associated with the disease, whereas organoid and animal models are used to investigate potential mechanisms. The available evidence links genetic susceptibility and PSC-associated inflammatory bowel disease to cholangiocyte injury, immune activation, disturbed bile acid homeostasis, and microbial alterations. At the bile duct interface, cholangiocyte senescence and barrier dysfunction may interact with microbial exposure and immune-cell recruitment to promote periductal fibrosis. PSC is therefore more plausibly viewed as a multicellular process than as the consequence of a single microbial, immune, or bile acid pathway. Whether dysbiosis and altered bile acid profiles contribute to disease development or instead reflect established PSC remains unresolved. Concomitant inflammatory bowel disease, medication use, biliary obstruction, and previous biliary interventions further complicate causal inference. Longitudinal human studies may distinguish early drivers from secondary changes. Mechanistic findings should ultimately improve patient phenotyping, surveillance, endoscopic management, and selection for targeted trials. Such trials will require biologically informed designs and endpoints that capture durable clinical benefit.

articles.title: Central line-associated bloodstream infection in preterm infants with umbilical venous catheters versus peripherally inserted catheters.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) is a serious complication in preterm infants. Umbilical venous catheters (UVCs) are commonly used, but whether CLABSI risk differs from peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) remains unclear. We compared CLABSI incidence between UVCs and PICCs placed within 72 h after birth.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included preterm infants with gestational age <30 weeks and birth weight <1000 g admitted to Amsterdam UMC (2016-2024) who received a UVC or PICC. CLABSI episodes within the first seven catheter days were analyzed. Kaplan-Meier and logistic regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 545 infants (UVC 64%, PICC 36%), 63 CLABSI events occurred. CLABSI incidence was higher with UVC than PICC (14.6% vs 6.1%). UVC use was associated with increased odds of CLABSI (adjusted OR 3.02, 95% CI 1.54-5.93; p = 0.001). CLABSI-free dwell time was shorter in the UVC group (p < 0.01). Subgroup analyses suggested a stronger association in infants ≥26 weeks' gestation.

CONCLUSION: UVC use was associated with higher CLABSI incidence and shorter CLABSI-free dwell time than PICC use during the first seven catheter days. Primary PICC placement may therefore warrant consideration, particularly in infants born at ≥26 weeks' gestation.

IMPACT: UVC use was associated with higher CLABSI incidence and shorter CLABSI-free dwell time than PICC use during the first seven catheter days. This study provides direct comparative evidence on early CLABSI risk between UVCs and PICCs. Restricting catheter placement to the first 72 h and using an identical seven-day risk window improved comparability between catheter types. Differences in catheter timing, dwell time, and risk windows may explain inconsistent findings in previous studies. Primary PICC placement may reduce early CLABSI risk compared with UVC placement, although differences by gestational age warrant further study.

articles.title: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth and cognition in middle childhood.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between socio-environmental factors, brain growth, and cognition in childhood is unknown. This study aimed to characterize associations between (i) regional brain growth from birth to 6-8 years and socio-environmental factors; and (ii) regional brain growth and cognitive outcomes in middle childhood.

METHODS: One hundred and thirty-seven 6-8-year-old children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neonatal and paediatric brain MRI and a full-scale IQ assessment. Data on household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation, and early cognitively stimulating home environment were collected. Regional brain growth (extracerebral CSF, ventricles, cortical grey matter, white matter, deep grey matter, cerebellum, brainstem) from the neonatal period to 6-8 years was assessed using Gaussian process regression.

RESULTS: Low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth (B, 95% CI -1.14, -1.88 to -0.396; pFWE = 0.044) and extracerebral CSF expansion (-1.55, -2.51 to -0.585; pFWE = 0.042). Higher cortical grey matter (3.89, 1.12-6.65; pFWE = 0.038) and brainstem (3.24, 0.894-5.58; pFWE = 0.038) growth were associated with better full-scale IQ. Brainstem (p = 0.014), but not cortical grey matter (p = 0.177), remained significant after adjustment for socio-environmental factors.

CONCLUSIONS: Support for financially vulnerable families may promote brain growth. Brainstem growth is a brain correlate of childhood cognition independent of the effects of socio-environmental factors.

IMPACT: One hundred and thirty-seven children (25 with congenital heart disease) underwent neuroimaging at birth and at 6-8 years and a full-scale IQ assessment at 6-8 years. Household income, maternal education, neighborhood deprivation and early home environment data were collected. After adjustment for other socio-environmental factors and group, low household income was associated with reduced cortical grey matter growth and extracerebral CSF expansion. Higher cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with higher full-scale IQ in middle childhood. Household poverty was linked to reduced brain growth, while cortical grey matter and brainstem growth were associated with cognitive abilities in childhood.

articles.title: Increased nitrosative stress in nasal polyp tissue of patients with chronic rhinosinusitis complicated by asthma-Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap: Association with postoperative recurrence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) and asthma are linked under the "one airway, one disease" concept. Asthma-chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) overlap (ACO) has emerged as a distinct phenotype combining asthma and COPD features. We previously reported higher nasal polyp recurrence in ACO-CRS than in CRS with asthma alone (A-CRS), but the underlying inflammatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate nitrosative stress marker expression in nasal polyp tissue from patients with ACO-CRS, A-CRS, and non-asthmatic CRS (NA-CRS), and to examine its association with postoperative recurrence.

METHODS: Forty-eight CRS patients undergoing bilateral endoscopic sinus surgery (2011-2024) with ≥ 1-year follow-up were divided into ACO-CRS (n = 15), A-CRS (n = 18), and NA-CRS (n = 15) groups. Nasal polyp specimens were immunostained for 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT), inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS), cystathionine β-synthase (CBS), and cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE). Associations with recurrence, smoking history, eosinophilic CRS (ECRS) status, blood eosinophil count, and pulmonary function were analyzed.

RESULTS: Positive cell counts for all four markers were highest in ACO-CRS and significantly higher than in NA-CRS; 3-NT and CSE counts were also significantly higher than in A-CRS (p < 0.05). These differences persisted among ever-smokers and in both ECRS and non-ECRS patients, whereas smoking history was not associated with marker expression in patients without ACO. One-year recurrence was highest in ACO-CRS (73.3%, vs. 33.3% in A-CRS and 13.3% in NA-CRS; p = 0.002). Of the four markers, only CBS-positive counts were significantly higher in recurrent than in non-recurrent cases (p = 0.008). 3-NT- and iNOS-positive counts correlated positively with blood eosinophil counts (r = 0.36, p = 0.011; r = 0.45, p = 0.001). A negative correlation between 3-NT-positive count and FEV1% (r = -0.35, p = 0.016) was not significant after adjusting for smoking history and pack-years (partial r = -0.280, p = 0.066).

CONCLUSION: ACO-CRS is associated with increased nitrosative stress marker expression in nasal polyp tissue, which was not explained by smoking history or ECRS status alone in exploratory analyses, and CBS expression was associated with postoperative recurrence. These preliminary findings suggest that nitrosative stress is involved in the upper airway pathology of ACO-CRS and warrant validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Projected Demand for Cardiac Electrophysiology Procedures in Australia to 2040: A National Population-Based Modelling Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac electrophysiology services are expanding rapidly owing to an ageing population, increasing prevalence of cardiac arrhythmias, expanding indications for catheter ablation and cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) therapy, and continued advances in procedural technology. Despite this, the future demand for electrophysiology procedures has not been estimated.

METHODS: We conducted a national population-based forecasting study using Australian Institute of Health and Welfare hospital procedural data between 2010 and 2024. Catheter ablation and CIED procedures were identified using Australian Classification of Health Interventions procedure codes. Historical trends in procedural volume and population-adjusted utilisation were evaluated. Future procedural demand to 2040 was estimated using linear regression and generalised additive models.

RESULTS: Between 2010 and 2024, 612,302 cardiac electrophysiology procedures were performed in Australia. Annual procedural volume increased from 28,805 to 55,919 procedures, representing a 94.1% increase. Catheter ablation activity increased by 200.8%, compared with 60.9% for CIED procedures. Atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation demonstrated the greatest absolute increase in procedure volume (7,582 annual procedures, 471.8%), while ventricular ablation demonstrated the greatest proportional increase (1,862.7%) from a low baseline volume. Forecast modelling projected total electrophysiology procedural activity to increase to 80,185 procedures annually by 2040 (95% confidence interval [CI], 76,237-84,133), representing a 43.4% (95% CI, 36.3-50.5%) increase from 2024. Catheter ablation demand is projected to increase by 54.2%, compared to 37.1% for CIED procedures, with AF ablation accounting for the largest increase in future procedural demand.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac electrophysiology procedural demand in Australia is projected to increase substantially over the coming decades. The anticipated growth is driven predominantly by continued growth in catheter ablation, particularly AF ablation. These findings provide an evidence base to support planning of future electrophysiology workforce requirements, procedural infrastructure and healthcare resource allocation to ensure sufficient capacity to meet the growing demand for electrophysiology services.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatrics.
articles.journal: Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pediatric practice, particularly for triage, early detection, documentation, and point-of-care decision support. Some currently available tools perform at an expert level, including bone age estimation and fracture detection. Ambient documentation is easing a persistent burden, and language models effectively draft notes and messages. However, the evidence for the technology in pediatrics lags behind adult medicine. Of the 876 AI and machine learning (ML) enabled devices currently authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), only 149 carry labeling for patients younger than 18 years, and only 19% of those report validation in children. This review article examines where AI already exists in, or is approaching, everyday pediatric use. In each domain, the discussion pairs the strength of the technology with its present limitations. Notably, strong test set statistics do not always translate into better outcomes, and few pediatric tools have been validated externally or prospectively. The reasons for that gap are examined in depth: pediatric datasets are smaller and less representative, which leaves them more prone to bias, and a child's consent binds their data for longer than an adult's. In general, the argument is neither for swift adoption nor for resistance. Instead, it is for holding the technology to a high standard, which means keeping a human in the loop and training clinicians to be exacting judges of the currently available tools.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Type 1 diabetes metabolomics and multi-omics: Current applications, limitations, and future directions - A narrative review" [Clin. Chim. Acta 594 (2027) 122900].
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Urinary tract and genital infections with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin across type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease: An indication- and sex-stratified disproportionality analysis of eudravigilance reports" [Biomed. Pharmacother. 204 (2026) 119976].
Home subcutaneous hydration as an alternative to intravenous therapy in a patient with high output ileostomy: A case report.
articles.abstract: High-output ileostomy represents a significant clinical challenge due to its association with dehydration, electrolyte imbalances, acute kidney injury, and frequent hospital readmissions, often requiring prolonged intravenous (IV) fluid therapy. We report the case of a 54-year-old woman with a terminal ileostomy following emergency intestinal resection, presenting persistent high stoma output (2200-2500 mL/day) and dependence on daily IV hydration despite optimized treatment. As early intestinal reconstruction was not feasible, a home-based subcutaneous hydration system (500-700 mL/day) was implemented, enabling hospital discharge and maintenance of adequate hydration. The patient developed one episode of local cellulitis, which resolved with oral antibiotics. During follow-up, progressive intestinal adaptation was observed, with reduced stoma output and improved diuresis. Body weight remained stable, and muscle mass and function improved. Home subcutaneous hydration appears to be a safe and effective alternative that enhances quality of life and reduces hospitalizations.

articles.title: Repeated-dose oral safety assessment of Aucuba japonica extract in rats: hematological-splenic responses and reversibility.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Aucuba japonica Thunb. has been used traditionally in Korea and Japan as warmed, roasted, or mashed preparations applied topically to burns, incised wounds, chilblains, boils, and localized swelling. Traditional oral preparations of A. japonica have also been used for edema and cystitis. Despite these topical and oral uses, repeated-dose safety data for A. japonica leaf extracts remain limited.

AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate repeated-dose oral toxicity, target-organ responses, and recovery following administration of A. japonica extract (AJE) in rats.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: AJE was prepared from leaves and stems with 30% ethanol at 85°C for 3 h. Male and female Crl:CD(SD) rats received 0, 1,250, 2,500, or 5000 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks, or 0, 625, 1,250, or 2500 mg/kg/day for 13 weeks. Separate control and high-dose cohorts underwent 4 weeks of recovery. Hematology, clinical chemistry, organ weights, and histopathology were assessed.

RESULTS: At 5000 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks, reduced erythrocyte counts, marked reticulocytosis, splenic enlargement, increased spleen weight, congestion, and extramedullary hematopoiesis constituted an adverse hematological-splenic response. Hepatocellular hypertrophy was also observed. Findings at 2500 mg/kg/day were treatment-related but considered non-adverse. After 13 weeks, 2500 mg/kg/day increased male reticulocytes and produced predominantly minimal splenic congestion and extramedullary hematopoiesis in both sexes. Corresponding abnormalities were absent in separately designated recovery cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: Hematological-splenic alterations were the principal toxicity findings at high exposure. The integrated evaluation supported 2500 mg/kg/day, the highest dose in the 13-week study, as its no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL). These conclusions apply to the tested AJE preparation.

articles.title: Cellular Senescence as a Multiorgan Driver of Diabetes-Associated Cardiovascular and Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Cellular senescence may contribute to persistent cardiovascular and kidney dysfunction in diabetes, but its effects depend on cell identity, tissue compartment and disease stage. This targeted narrative review integrates mechanistic, preclinical and early human evidence into a proposed multiorgan framework. Experimental studies support functional effects of senescent beta-cell, adipose, vascular and tubular populations, while predominantly post-mitotic cardiomyocytes and mature podocytes exhibit senescence-like states. Local paracrine mechanisms, including tubular-to-fibroblast signalling, are better established than source-specific transmission between distant organs. Adipose-derived extracellular vesicles provide an experimental adipose-to-heart example in diabetic mice, whereas the broader contributions of circulating SASP factors, metabolites and immune-cell trafficking remain incompletely resolved. We therefore present the diabetes-heart-kidney senescence loop as a conceptual interpretation of the available evidence, rather than a validated causal network. Senolytic and senomorphic interventions improve selected phenotypes in preclinical models. Major unresolved questions concern the pathogenic cell populations in patients, the direction and specificity of interorgan signalling, and the timing and safety of intervention. Clinical translation requires cell-resolved biomarkers and evidence that senescence-directed treatment adds functional benefit to established cardiometabolic care while preserving beneficial repair and immune functions.

articles.title: Restoring mitophagy and oxidative phosphorylation coupled with ferroptosis suppression through Huoxue Tongmai formula ameliorates cardiac function in heart failure.
articles.abstract: Huoxue Tongmai formula (XMT), a hospital-prepared traditional Chinese medicine formulation, has demonstrated clinical efficacy against cardiovascular diseases. However, its mechanisms in ameliorating myocardial hypertrophy remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the cardioprotective effects of XMT in a murine model of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Bioactive constituents of XMT were characterized using HPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. In vivo assessments were conducted in a transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced cardiac hypertrophy mouse model, followed by transcriptomic profiling to identify differentially regulated pathways. In vitro experiments using angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy were performed to validate the protective effects and mechanisms of XMT. XMT administration significantly ameliorated TAC-induced cardiac dysfunction, as evidenced by improved echocardiographic parameters (LVEF, LVFS, and SV), as well as attenuated ventricular wall thickening and cardiac mass enlargement. XMT also reduced myocardial injury, interstitial fibrosis, and serum levels of NT-proBNP, cTn-T, CK-MB, and LDH. Notably, XMT suppressed pathological hypertrophic remodeling, reflected by decreased HW/TL and HW/BW ratios, reduced cardiomyocyte cross-sectional area, and downregulated expression of hypertrophic marker genes (Nppa, Nppb, and MYH7). Transcriptomic analysis revealed that XMT modulated pathways associated with mitochondrial function, oxidative phosphorylation, and mitophagy. Mechanistically, XMT upregulated the mitophagy regulators PINK1, Parkin, and FUNDC1, attenuated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and preserved mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) content. Moreover, XMT suppressed ferroptosis in hypertrophic hearts, as evidenced by increased GSH content, elevated GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression, and reduced MDA, total iron, and PTGS2 levels. In vitro, XMT exerted protective effects against Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, as demonstrated by enhanced cell viability, reduced LDH release, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), and marked suppression of mitochondrial ROS generation. XMT-medicated serum also attenuated Ang II-induced lipid peroxidation as measured by C11-BODIPY assay. Moreover, Seahorse-based metabolic flux analysis indicated that XMT significantly improved mitochondrial respiratory function, evidenced by elevated basal and maximal oxygen consumption rates (OCR). Concurrently, XMT attenuated the compensatory upregulation of glycolysis, as shown by a reduced extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and diminished glycolytic reserve. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that XMT alleviates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy by enhancing mitochondrial respiration and promoting mitophagy, positioning it as a promising therapeutic candidate for hypertrophic heart failure.

articles.title: Retention Across Developmental Stages: Insights from a Longitudinal Birth Cohort.
articles.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
articles.abstract: Sustained participant retention is critical to the validity of longitudinal pediatric cohort studies yet remains an operational challenge-particularly in resource-limited settings. We evaluated retention patterns and contributing factors in the Urban Environment and Childhood Asthma (URECA) birth cohort, a multisite study that followed 609 children (49.0% female; 51.0% male) from birth through late adolescence (up to age 17) across four U.S. cities. Overall, 382 (62.7%) of participants completed final assessments at the last planned study visit. Attrition was highest during the first year of life and declined thereafter. Younger maternal age at delivery (<18 years (48% vs 64% for ≥ 18 years) and failure to complete an early-life home visit (44% vs 67% for completed) were significantly associated with lower retention, whereas most other maternal sociodemographic and psychosocial characteristics were not. Adolescent participant factors, including school enrollment, residential stability, anxiety, and depression, were similarly not associated with retention. High retention was sustained through adolescence and during COVID-19-related disruptions, alongside continuity in core study staff, strong and enduring participant-study relationships, flexible communication strategies, participant-centered engagement, and practices designed to reduce logistical barriers. These findings suggest that long-term retention in urban pediatric cohorts is associated with early engagement and the reported/perceived trust and reciprocal relationships over time. Relationship-centered, adaptive, and barrier-reducing approaches may be particularly relevant to supporting sustained participation across developmental transitions and external disruptions.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for Insulin Dosing in Gestational Diabetes: A Simulation Model.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Gestational diabetes (GDM) is a major contributor to maternal and neonatal morbidity, healthcare costs and a growing healthcare burden for clinicians. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications are increasingly used in healthcare, but data are lacking on their use in GDM management.

OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate the proof of concept of utilizing a large language model (LLM) clinical decision support tool (CDST) in GDM care we conducted a study with an objective to compare ChatGPT management of insulin dependent GDM to clinician management. Our primary hypothesis was that ChatGPT would suggest starting insulin at a higher dose than the clinicians. Our secondary hypothesis was that clinician-prescribed doses would converge with the initially recommended ChatGPT dose by the first visit occurring more than 2 weeks after insulin initiation.

STUDY DESIGN: In a retrospective cohort of patients with insulin-dependent GDM, we compared a model using ChatGPT as a simulated CDST to traditional clinician-prescribed insulin. Gestational age (GA), weight, and glucose values were entered into ChatGPT with a request to create an initial insulin regimen, and subsequent log values were entered with a request to alter the regimen as appropriate. The primary outcome was total daily insulin dose (TDD) and the exposure was regimen source (ChatGPT vs clinician). We compared TDD at the initial visit and the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation.

RESULTS: A total of 60 patients were included. The initial clinician TDD of insulin was 13.3 units lower than the ChatGPT recommendation (95% CI: 7.7-18.9, p < 0.001). At the first subsequent visit occurring 2 weeks after insulin initiation, clinicians increased their prescribed TDD by an average of 11.1 units (95%CI: 7.4-14.4, p< 0.001). At this subsequent time point clinician prescribed TDD was similar to the initial ChatGPT prescription (mean: [ChatGPT-CP]: 2.2 units (95%CI: -3.2-7.7), p=0.42), and concurrent visit (mean [ChatGPT-CP]: 1.6 units (95%CI: -0.2-3.4), p=0.08).

CONCLUSION: Clinicians initiate insulin at lower doses than recommended by ChatGPT. However, 2-3 weeks after insulin initiation, recommended doses were similar. These findings suggest the feasibility of prospective studies assessing the use of an AI-CDST in GDM management. This approach may complement clinicians as a co-management tool and expand access to earlier medical intervention, particularly in areas with limited access to high-risk obstetricians.

articles.title: Multiparameter continuous fetal monitoring for early detection of physiologic derangement in a lamb model of fetal surgery.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fetal echocardiography is the gold standard for intraoperative monitoring during fetal surgery but hinges on fetal bradycardia as the primary indicator for fetal distress. However, fetal bradycardia likely represents a terminal stage of physiologic decompensation when encountered in fetal surgery.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the relationship between fetal heart rate changes and fetal physiologic derangement during stressors relevant to fetal surgery and to assess the potential contribution of continuous multiparameter fetal monitoring in the early detection of fetal distress.

STUDY DESIGN: To challenge this hypothesis, we utilized a novel, integrated fetal monitoring probe to provide real-time core measurements of fetal oxygen saturation (SpO2), temperature, and FHR. Maternal (pre-placental) hypoxia, umbilical cord occlusion (post-placental hypoxia), and fetal hypothermia were induced to simulate clinically relevant perturbations in fetal surgery in a large animal model.

RESULTS: Fetal bradycardia (defined as FHR<110) most often occurred in the setting of FPD, with positive-predictive value of 100% for fetal hypoxia, 83.3% for acidosis, and 91.7% for hypercarbia. However, the negative-predictive value of bradycardia was 41.5% for hypoxia, 62.5% for acidosis, 37.2% for hypercarbia, and 37.8% for acidosis. Time from the onset of FPD to detection of FHR changes was significantly longer than fetal SpO2 changes in the case of pre-placental hypoxia. Distinct patterns of fetal SpO2 and FHR changes were present between pre-placental hypoxia, post-placental hypoxia, and fetal hypothermia that were detectable via multiparameter fetal monitoring probe tracings.

CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, profound fetal hypoxia, acidosis, and hypothermia occur frequently in the absence of fetal bradycardia. The novel multiparameter continuous probe detected FHR changes with minimal latency after clinically relevant fetal hypoxic stressors.

articles.title: Severe maternal morbidity in patients with cardiovascular disease and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are independently associated with increased risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM). While prior studies have characterized adverse pregnancy outcomes among patients with CVD, limited data have evaluated how the development of HDP influences non-transfusion SMM across specific cardiac subtypes, particularly through the postpartum period, in large contemporary U.S. cohorts.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the impact of HDP on non-transfusion SMM among patients with CVD during delivery and within 90 days postpartum.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using the Premier Healthcare Database of pregnant patients ≥18 years delivering between 2015 and 2020. Patients without CVD were compared to those with six CVD subtypes present on admission (aortic, ischemic, congenital, pulmonary hypertension, cardiomyopathy, and valvular). The primary outcome was non-transfusion SMM during delivery hospitalization and within 90 days postpartum, stratified by CVD and HDP subtype (gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preeclampsia with severe features), estimated as covariate-adjusted predicted rates (%). Secondary outcomes included SMM subtypes, ICU admission, and all-cause readmission within 30 and 90 days, reported as crude rates and adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

RESULTS: Of 4,606,247 births, 18,771 (0.4%) had CVD, and 12.0% had HDP. HDP was associated with higher adjusted predicted non-transfusion SMM rates, independent of CVD, with increasing risk across HDP severity and marked heterogeneity by CVD subtype. Patients with CVD had consistently higher SMM across all HDP subtypes. The highest delivery hospitalization SMM rates occurred among patients with cardiomyopathy (25.6%) and pulmonary hypertension (33.2%) with preeclampsia with severe features; this pattern persisted through 90 days postpartum. Acute respiratory distress syndrome and mechanical ventilation were the most common SMM types during delivery, while heart failure/pulmonary edema predominated postpartum. Cardiomyopathy (aOR 9.02) and pulmonary hypertension (aOR 4.37) had the highest odds of ICU admission; readmission risk was also highest in pulmonary hypertension (30-day aOR 1.77; 90-day aOR 1.76) and cardiomyopathy (30-day aOR 1.42; 90-day aOR 1.68).

CONCLUSION: HDP significantly increases risk of non-transfusion SMM in patients with CVD, particularly in pulmonary hypertension and cardiomyopathy, and in those with preeclampsia with severe features.

articles.title: Spatial heterogeneity of brain myelin aging and vascular-metabolic risk-associated alterations: An MR fingerprinting study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize spatial patterns of age-related variation in MR fingerprinting (MRF)-derived myelin water fraction (MWF) and its associations with vascular-metabolic risk.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, neurologically asymptomatic adults underwent MRF scanning at 3T MR. MWF maps were estimated using a three-compartment model. Non-negative matrix factorization identified cortical gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM) clusters in healthy participants; eight subcortical regions were analyzed separately. Generalized additive models were used to generate healthy reference curves. Deviations, aging slopes, and exposure-by-age interactions were compared between healthy controls and participants with vascular-metabolic risk.

RESULTS: Among 285 participants (57.2 ± 14.4 years; 168 females), 167 were healthy and 118 had vascular-metabolic risk. Two cortical GM and two WM clusters with distinct aging patterns were identified. GM cluster 2 (frontal-parietal-occipital cortices) showed higher MWF with age, and WM cluster 2 (projection and association fibers) showed marked negative age association after midlife. Compared with healthy participants, the vascular-metabolic risk group had a less positive age association in GM clusters (cluster 1: β = -2.77 × 10-5/year, q = 0.046; cluster 2: β = -4.14 × 10-5/year, q = 0.034) and lower deviation from the healthy reference in WM cluster 2 (β = -0.00351, q = 0.036). Continuous blood-pressure main effects on deviation were nonsignificant after FDR correction, but complementary tertile analyses showed more negative age-related slopes in the highest than the lowest tertiles in WM cluster 2 and the subcortical summary (all FDR-corrected q < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: MRF-derived MWF imaging revealed regionally distinct myelin aging patterns and selective deviations linked to vascular-metabolic risk, particularly in projection and association WM fibers. Blood pressure may be relevant to regional myelin-related aging patterns, warranting validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

articles.title: Pre-emptive TIPS Reduces Further Decompensation Following Gastric Variceal Hemorrhage: A Real-World Multicenter Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric variceal hemorrhage (GVH) carries high mortality and rebleeding rates. Pre-emptive TIPS reduces rebleeding and death in acute GVH. However, the impact of TIPS on further decompensation remains uncertain, particularly in real-world settings.

AIMS: To assess whether pre-emptive TIPS reduces further decompensation and improves survival compared with standard of care (SOC) after GVH.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with cirrhosis and acute GVH treated at three tertiary centers between October 2011 and April 2024. Of 263 patients screened, 218 were eligible (102 TIPS, 116 SOC). Propensity score matching on nine baseline covariates yielded 95 matched pairs. All TIPS procedures followed successful initial hemostasis. The primary outcome was further decompensation within 12 months according to Baveno VII. Sensitivity analyses included landmark, inverse-probability-weighted, center-adjusted, and competing-risk models.

RESULTS: Further decompensation occurred in 33/95 TIPS patients (35%) and 57/95 SOC patients (60%). Pre-emptive TIPS was associated with lower risks of further decompensation (adjusted HR 0.338, 95% CI 0.217-0.525; p<0.001, absolute risk difference 25 percentage points, number needed to treat 4), variceal rebleeding (adjusted HR 0.247, 95% CI 0.096-0.640; p=0.004), and new or worsening ascites (adjusted HR 0.209, 95% CI 0.082-0.535; p=0.001). Hepatic encephalopathy did not differ significantly between groups. Pre-emptive TIPS was also associated with improved transplant-free survival (adjusted HR 0.425, 95% CI 0.245-0.737; p=0.002) and overall survival (adjusted HR 0.219, 95% CI 0.108-0.443; p<0.001). The association with further decompensation persisted in all sensitivity analyses, including versus SOC patients receiving non-selective beta-blockers.

CONCLUSION: Pre-emptive TIPS following GVH was associated with a significantly lower risk of further decompensation and improved transplant-free survival. These real-world findings support the potential disease-modifying role of pre-emptive TIPS in GVH management.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Gastric variceal hemorrhage is associated with a high risk of recurrent bleeding and subsequent decompensation, but real-world evidence regarding the broader clinical effects of pre-emptive TIPS remains limited. In this multicenter retrospective cohort, pre-emptive TIPS after successful initial hemostasis was associated with lower risks of further decompensation, variceal rebleeding, and new or worsening ascites, as well as improved transplant-free survival, without a significant increase in overt hepatic encephalopathy. These findings are relevant to hepatologists, endoscopists, interventional radiologists, and multidisciplinary teams considering early portal decompression after gastric variceal bleeding, and may inform patient selection and future prospective studies. However, because treatment allocation and follow-up were retrospective and center-dependent, the observed associations require cautious interpretation and prospective validation.

articles.title: Comparative risk of hepatocellular carcinoma among people with chronic hepatitis B treated with tenofovir or entecavir: A population-based linkage study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence and mortality are rising in Australia and globally. Antiviral therapies entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) are widely used to treat chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and reduce HCC risk, but uncertainty persists regarding their relative HCC prevention impact. This study characterises HCC incidence among people with CHB treated with ETV or TDF, including sub-populations recommended for HCC surveillance.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study in New South Wales, Australia, using linked public health datasets: 10,698 people with CHB were eligible after receiving at least 12 months of stable antiviral therapy with ETV (n=7,139) or TDF (n=3,559). Follow-up occurred from 2007-2022. Crude annual incidence rates and adjusted Cox proportional hazard ratios were calculated for HCC.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 86.3 months, including 89.2 months and 82.3 months among participants receiving TDF and ETV, respectively. During follow-up, 300 (2.8%) participants were diagnosed with HCC, an incidence of 4.12 per 1000 person years. Participants treated with TDF had a lower hazard ratio for HCC (aHR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.46-0.82) compared to those treated with ETV. Baseline variables associated with increased HCC risk were older age (reference <50 years: 50-59 years aHR: 2.15, 95% CI: 1.45-3.18; 60-69 years aHR: 3.42, 95% CI: 2.38-4.91; 70-79 years aHR: 4.28, 95% CI: 2.89-6.34; ≥80 years aHR: 3.95, 95% CI: 2.51-6.22), male sex (aHR: 3.14; 95% CI: 2.31-4.25), alcohol use disorder (aHR: 2.33; 95% CI: 1.28-4.25), and history of decompensated cirrhosis (aHR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.27-4.07).

CONCLUSION: In people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia on stable antiviral therapy hepatocellular carcinoma risk was lower among those receiving entecavir than those receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, although confounding remains a potential explanation.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Comparative HCC risk between entecavir and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in chronic hepatitis B remains uncertain outside East Asian cohorts. This population-based linkage study of people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia found TDF was associated with lower HCC risk than entecavir, a finding relevant to clinicians and researchers working on HCC prevention. These results support consideration of TDF as a preferred antiviral where clinically appropriate and highlight the need for HCC screening guidelines to account for treatment status alongside established risk factors such as older age and alcohol use disorder. As treatment was not randomised and residual confounding could not be completely mitigated, further prospective studies are needed to confirm this association.

articles.title: Kaempferol modulates LPS-induced airway epithelial cell dysfunction and NF-κB/NLRP3-associated signaling: an integrated computational and experimental study.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical illness with a high mortality rate in intensive care units, and effective specific therapeutic agents are still lacking. Kaempferol, a natural flavonoid, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, its protective effects and mechanisms against ALI remain unclear. This study integrated network pharmacology prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, in vitro cell experiments, and in vivo animal models to systematically investigate the protective effects and mechanisms of kaempferol on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. Network pharmacology analysis identified 289 common targets from the intersection of 429 kaempferol-related targets and 9412 lung injury-related targets, with Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses revealing that these targets were predominantly enriched in inflammation-related signaling pathways such as NF-κB. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations indicated the stable binding of kaempferol to the candidate core targets PIK3CA, EGFR, and PTGS2. In vitro experiments indicated that kaempferol at concentrations of 1-20 μM did not exhibit cytotoxicity in BEAS-2B cells and dose-dependently attenuated LPS-induced reduction in cell viability, stress-induced epithelial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Association analysis revealed that kaempferol treatment was accompanied by significantly decreased secretion of IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α, reduced NLRP3-related signaling, and decreased NF-κB pathway activation. In vivo experiments further suggested that kaempferol significantly attenuated LPS-induced lung histopathological injury, reduced lung injury scores and alveolar airspace fraction, inhibited myeloperoxidase activity and pulmonary edema, decreased total protein and various inflammatory cell counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, and reduced inflammatory cytokine levels in lung tissues and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Additionally, kaempferol reduced hepatic malondialdehyde content and restored superoxide dismutase and glutathione activities, suggesting alleviation of LPS-induced systemic/hepatic oxidative stress. High-dose kaempferol did not exhibit obvious toxicity to the heart, liver, spleen, or kidney in normal mice. Collectively, these results indicate that kaempferol effectively alleviates LPS-induced acute lung injury, and these protective effects are associated with reduced NF-κB signaling and NLRP3-related signaling, providing theoretical and experimental evidence for kaempferol as a potential protective compound against LPS-induced ALI and supporting further investigation.

articles.title: OLFM4 exacerbates neutrophilic asthma progression by modulating the interaction between neutrophils and airway epithelial cells.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Neutrophilic asthma (NA) represents a distinct asthma subtype that responds poorly to standard therapies. Olfactomedin 4 (OLFM4) is a glycoprotein predominantly enriched in neutrophils, the role of which remains unclear in NA. This study aimed to elucidate the functional role and underlying mechanisms of OLFM4 in mediating communication between neutrophils and airway epithelial cells (AECs) in NA. An NA mouse model was established through ovalbumin sensitization combined with cigarette smoke exposure. Disease progression was evaluated by assessing airway hyperresponsiveness, differential leukocyte counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), and histopathological alterations. Neutrophil infiltration was detected via immunohistochemical staining for Ly6G and MPO. For in vitro experiments, neutrophil‑like cells differentiated from HL‑60 and BEAS‑2B airway epithelial cells (AECs) were exposed to cigarette smoke extract. Gene and protein expression were examined by qPCR, western blotting, and immunofluorescence, while cell migration was evaluated using Transwell assays. Protein-protein interactions were verified through co‑immunoprecipitation. Analysis of the GSE256534 sequencing dataset revealed that OLFM4 was up-regulated in peripheral blood samples from patients with acute asthma exacerbation. In vivo model demonstrated that OLFM4 was significantly upregulated in neutrophils from NA mice. Overexpression of OLFM4 promoted neutrophil migration, enhanced the secretion of inflammatory cytokines, and activated the MAPK signaling pathway, which were reversed by a MAPK inhibitor. Furthermore, neutrophils were found to transfer OLFM4 to BEAS‑2B cells via exosomes, which subsequently promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix deposition. Mechanistically, OLFM4 bound to BMP7 and impeded its secretion, thereby suppressing smad1/5/8 signaling and modulating AECs function. Finally, knockdown of OLFM4 attenuated NA progression in vivo. Collectively, our findings indicate that OLFM4 exacerbates NA by enhancing neutrophil infiltration and pulmonary fibrosis, offering novel insights into the pathological mechanisms of NA.

articles.title: Integrated transcriptomic and microbial profiling reveals associations between immune responses and microbiota alterations during GCRV-II infection in the gills of grass carp.
articles.abstract: The teleost gill mucosa serves as a frontline interface where viral pathogens initiate infection and commensal microbiota establish their residence. However, how the gill microbiota responds to pathogen challenge and interacts with local immune defenses remains poorly understood. In this study, we employed transcriptome profiling and 16S rRNA sequencing to investigate the temporal dynamics of immune responses and gill microbial communities following infection with grass carp reovirus genotype II (GCRV-II). Transcriptomic analysis indicated that GCRV-II stimulated coordinated innate immune activation in the gills, as evidenced by the upregulation of antiviral, antimicrobial, and inflammatory genes. Concurrently, GCRV-II infection induced significant disruption of the gill commensal microbiota, marked by the expansion of opportunistic pathogens and a decline in beneficial symbiotic bacteria at 7 days post-infection (DPI). At 28 DPI, the microbial community structure of gills recovered to a certain extent. Correlation analyses further revealed significant associations between microbial taxa and gill immune responses. Specifically, the Brevundimonas was significantly positively correlated with the expression of multiple immune-related genes, whereas Lactobacillus and Blautia exhibited significant negative correlations with the expression of multiple immune-related genes. Collectively, this study advances our understanding of the relationship between immune responses and microbial community changes in the teleost gill and provides a theoretical basis for developing health management strategies in aquaculture through gill immune regulation.

articles.title: Compound C6 accelerates chronic wound repair through FXR-dependent host responses and perturbation of staphylococcal arginine metabolism.
articles.abstract: Chronic and non-healing wounds remain a clinical challenge due to impaired tissue repair, persistent inflammation, and microbial infection. Compound C6 is a small-molecule farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist initially developed for fatty liver disease, but its effects on wound repair are unknown. Here, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of C6 in normal, diabetic, and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA)-infected mouse wound models. Topical C6 accelerated wound closure, improved perfusion and vascularization, and reduced inflammatory cytokines. Mechanistically, C6 promoted endothelial migration and tube formation by upregulating VEGFA and eNOS, while suppressing macrophage inflammatory responses and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation. FXR silencing abolished these pro-angiogenic and anti-inflammatory effects, whereas FXR re-expression rescued them, and cellular thermal shift assays confirmed direct FXR engagement. In parallel, C6 directly inhibited S. aureus and MRSA growth, disrupted bacterial membranes, reduced biofilm formation, and exhibited a low propensity for resistance development. Transcriptomic and metabolic analyses revealed that C6 suppresses genes involved in arginine biosynthesis and catabolism, leading to reduced intracellular arginine. L-arginine supplementation partially restored bacterial viability. Crucially, we demonstrated that C6-induced arginine depletion occurs prior to detectable bacterial growth inhibition, establishing disrupted arginine metabolism as a primary cause of its antibacterial activity. Together, C6 promotes wound repair by coordinating FXR-dependent host vascular regeneration and inflammatory control with pathogen-directed antibacterial activity via arginine metabolic perturbation, supporting its further development for chronic and infected wounds.

articles.title: 4-O-(E)-Feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine suppresses mast cell-mediated allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Previous studies demonstrated that ferulic acid exerts therapeutic effects on various inflammatory disorders, including arthritis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and asthma. We synthesized a novel ferulic acid derivative (4-O-(E)-feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine, FOA), which has not been analyzed previously. We validated whether FOA modulates airway inflammation and fibrosis and unraveled its possible underlying mechanisms. In a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA)-induced airway inflammation, FOA treatment alleviated immune cell recruitment and reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and immunoglobulin (Ig) levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and serum, respectively. In BALF and Lung tissue, pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly suppressed by FOA treatment. FOA administration decreased the recruitment of mast cells into lung tissue and activation. We focused on FOA efficacy using mast cells, which are involved in asthma development. In RBL (rat basophilic leukemia)-2H3 and rat peritoneal mast cells (RPMCs), FOA pretreatment inhibited mast cell degranulation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production through intracellular signaling pathways, including Lyn, Syk, Akt, phosphoinositide 3-kinase, phospholipase Cγ, nuclear factor-κB, and MAPKs. To determine the pro-fibrotic function of activated mast cells, we stimulated mast cells for transforming growth factor-β expression and secretion, contributing to fibrotic symptoms in lung tissues. FOA administration suppressed these fibrotic symptoms. FOA pretreatment exerted anti-fibrotic effects in human lung epithelial cell lines (A549 and NCI-H358) through the suppression of fibrotic factor expression, and in a murine model of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Collectively, our findings suggest that FOA may serve as a promising therapeutic candidate for allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: A multimodal imaging framework for characterizing chronic neuropathology after traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with progressive neurodegeneration, including chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), yet the spatiotemporal evolution of post-traumatic structural and molecular pathology remains incompletely understood. Conventional neuroimaging approaches have limited sensitivity for detecting the subtle microstructural and molecular alterations underlying chronic post-traumatic degeneration. Here, we established a multimodal molecular imaging framework in murine models of single and repetitive mild TBI by integrating high-field 9.4 T micro-MRI/diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with multitracer PET-CT using 18F-FDG, 11C-PIB, and 18FS16. This approach enabled the in vivo assessment of white matter integrity, cerebral glucose metabolism, amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, and tau accumulation. Imaging findings were further validated using molecular, histopathological, and behavioral analyses. MRI-DTI revealed widespread white matter abnormalities and hippocampal degeneration following repetitive mild TBI, while PET imaging demonstrated persistent cerebral hypometabolism accompanied by increased Aβ and tau deposition. These pathological alterations were further associated with sustained neuroinflammatory activation and cognitive impairment. Notably, correlation analyses among the PET metrics revealed inverse associations between cerebral glucose metabolism (18F-FDG) and both Aβ (11C-PIB) and tau (18FS16) accumulation, with a stronger association observed between 18F-FDG and 11C-PIB. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that integrated MRI-DTI and multitracer PET provide complementary characterization of structural, metabolic, and proteinopathic alterations following TBI. This multimodal framework provides a preclinical platform for investigating post-traumatic neurodegeneration and may facilitate the development and translational evaluation of imaging biomarkers for TBI.

articles.title: Early-Life Farm Exposure and Food Allergy.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract: Food allergy has increased substantially, increasing interest in environmental exposures that may promote immune tolerance. The "farm effect," in which children raised in traditional farming environments have lower rates of allergic disease, may also extend to food allergy. This review summarizes epidemiologic and mechanistic evidence linking prenatal and early-life farm exposures with food allergy and related atopic outcomes. Protective associations likely reflect combined exposures to livestock, farm dust, environmental microbes, diet, and farm milk during critical developmental windows. Proposed mechanisms include altered gut microbiome maturation, microbial metabolites, reduced epithelial inflammation, innate immune programming, and enhanced regulatory T-cell responses. However, direct evidence for clinically confirmed food allergy remains limited compared with evidence for asthma and allergic sensitization. Future studies should identify specific microbial, metabolic, and immune pathways that mediate protection and determine whether safe, defined surrogates of farm exposure can be translated into food allergy prevention strategies.

articles.title: 2026 updated recommendations of the Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology for biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe psoriasis: Management of special populations, comorbidities, and treatment-related risks-Part 2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The Psoriasis Working Group (GPS) of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology regularly updates its recommendations for the management of moderate-to-severe psoriasis. The expanding availability of biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments, together with emerging evidence on their efficacy and safety, requires updated guidance for special populations, patients with comorbidities, and treatment-related risk management. This document provides evidence-informed recommendations to support individualized therapeutic decision-making.

METHODS: Recommendations were developed using the nominal group technique, supported by a scoping review of the literature. Two coordinators appointed a panel of GPS experts and defined the clinical questions and topics requiring revision. With the assistance of an information specialist, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through October 2025. Evidence was selected from systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical trials, and high-quality real-world studies. Relevant national and international clinical practice guidelines and consensus documents were also reviewed. Previous recommendations were revised, and new recommendations were developed, evaluated by the expert panel, and refined through successive review rounds.

RESULTS: Updated recommendations address biologic therapies, biosimilars, and oral small-molecule treatments for moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Management considerations include older adults, pediatric patients, pregnancy, breastfeeding, conception planning, poor treatment adherence, multiple treatment failures, and psoriasis affecting special anatomical sites. Recommendations also address treatment selection in patients with obesity, metabolic syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, depression, malignancy, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, neurologic disorders, lupus, and other autoimmune diseases. Treatment-related risk management encompasses pretreatment assessment, laboratory and clinical monitoring, vaccination, infection and latent tuberculosis screening, neurotoxicity, perioperative management, adverse events, and treatment discontinuation. Multidisciplinary care is emphasized throughout.

CONCLUSIONS: These updated recommendations provide an evidence-informed framework for individualized systemic treatment of moderate-to-severe psoriasis in special populations and patients with comorbidities. Treatment selection should integrate disease characteristics, comorbidities, patient preferences, available evidence, and treatment-specific safety considerations. Ongoing risk assessment, appropriate monitoring, and multidisciplinary collaboration are essential components of long-term psoriasis management.

articles.title: AEDV recommendations for the early management of psoriasis in Spain: an expert consensus.
articles.abstract: The Psoriasis Working Group of the Spanish Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (AEDV) has developed a national consensus to define early intervention in psoriasis (PsO) and to provide practical, evidence-based recommendations for its implementation. Through a four-phase process (literature review, expert focus group, two-round Delphi consultation, and consensus formulation), dermatologists and a rheumatologist identified key clinical and conceptual priorities related to treatment timing, risk of psoriatic arthritis (PsA), and psychosocial burden, including cumulative life course impairment (CLCI). The resulting recommendations broaden the scope of disease assessment beyond cutaneous severity to incorporate disease duration, persistent inflammation, and PsA risk factors. Biologic therapies, particularly IL-17A, IL-17A/F, and IL-23 inhibitors, were recognized as agents with potential to modify the course of the disease and possibly delay PsA onset, based on expert consensus and emerging observational evidence, pending prospective confirmation. These consensus-based statements provide a structured, evidence-informed framework to guide early, risk-adapted management of PsO in Spain.

articles.title: Oligomerization of DNAJB6b involves the substrate binding domains while largely preserving J-domain autoinhibition.
articles.abstract: DNAJB6b is a molecular chaperone in the heat shock protein network, known to play a crucial role in preventing the aggregation of several disease-associated intrinsically disordered proteins. A common feature of many chaperones, including DNAJB6b, is their ability to form oligomeric assemblies. In this study, we performed all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of DNAJB6b to investigate its oligomerization and its potential link to chaperone activity. We found that DNAJB6b progressively forms oligomeric assemblies involving the S/T and G/F domains, while the autoinhibitory conformation of the J-domain remains intact. Notably, the same S/T domain responsible for oligomer formation also mediates substrate binding, suggesting a mechanistic link between DNAJB6b oligomerization and chaperone function. Furthermore, the simulated trimer conformations exhibit hydrodynamic radii comparable to the experimental ensemble-average value measured near the critical micelle concentration.

articles.title: Impact of intermittent hypoxia on drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters and drug pharmacokinetics: an underestimated concern in obstructive sleep apnea patients?
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSA) is a prevalent and life-threatening respiratory disease. Marked by intermittent hypoxia (IH) and chronic inflammation, OSA frequently co-occurs with comorbidities like hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia or depression, necessitating various medications. However, the response to some treatments is notably compromised in OSA patients, manifesting as reduced efficacy and/or increased incidence of adverse events. The mechanisms underlying this altered pharmacological response remain unelucidated. Although comorbidities may substantially contribute to these alterations, IH and inflammation, key features of OSA, are known to modify drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters (DMETs). We therefore hypothesized that OSA/IH may affect DMETs, thereby altering drug pharmacokinetics and drug response. This narrative review synthesizes existing literature regarding the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs and pharmacokinetics both in experimental models and human, along with the underlying mechanisms exploring the roles of pro-inflammatory cytokines, transcription factors and epigenetics. Subsequently, we discuss the potential consequences of these IH-induced DMETs alterations on drug response in OSA patient population. In this purpose, we examine the hypothesis of pharmacokinetic modifications for each drug (or pharmacotherapeutic class) whose response appears altered in OSA patients. Additionally, we analyze the pharmacokinetic profile of the most commonly dispensed medications in OSA patients in order to identify additional drugs whose efficacy or safety might be compromised by IH-induced DMETs alterations. Finally, in the absence of conclusive clinical evidence, we propose priority research areas to better characterize the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs, pharmacokinetics, and drug response, and the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: A previously unrecognized Francisella tularensis subsp. holarctica B.66 lineage in Germany: genomic characterization of a clinical isolate from a severe case of human tularemia. Running Title: Tularemia in Northeastern Germany.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract: We report a severe case of human tularemia in a 58-year-old man with chronic kidney disease who developed fever, thrombocytopenia, renal dysfunction, and hematuria. Francisella tularensis subsp. holarctica was isolated from blood cultures and successfully treated with ciprofloxacin followed by doxycycline. Retrospective exposure assessment identified extensive aerosol-generating outdoor cleaning activities as a potential source, although the transmission route remained uncertain. Whole-genome sequencing assigned the isolate to major clade B.12 and subclade B.66. Core-SNP phylogenetic analysis revealed an independent branch distinct from established downstream B.66 subclades, representing a previously uncharacterized genotype within the analyzed German dataset. Furthermore, the isolate occupied a distinct position within the worldwide B.66 subclade and clustered closely with isolates from Kazakhstan and Russia.
