This case highlights the value of genomic surveillance for resolving regional F. tularensis subsp. holarctica diversity.

articles.title: Diet Quality as Assessed by the Healthy Eating Index, Alternate Healthy Eating Index, and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension Score, and Health Outcomes: a Third Systematic Review Update and Meta-Analysis of Cohort Studies.
articles.journal: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: How diet quality, as measured by different diet quality indices, is associated with non-communicable disease incidence and mortality remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to update the body of evidence on the associations between diet quality, as assessed by the Healthy Eating Index (HEI), Alternate Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), and Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score, and health outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus databases were used to update the search until February 3, 2025. Pooled relative risk (RR) with 95% CI for the highest versus the lowest category of diet quality was estimated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was explored using Cochran´s Q test and I2 statistic with 95% CI. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-E tool, funnel plots, and Egger's regression test. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: The current update identified 96 new reports (total now 207), including data from 3,976,111 individuals in the general population and 55,572 cancer survivors. All HEI, AHEI or DASH scores were inversely associated with risk of all-cause mortality (all indices combined: RR 0.82, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.87), cardiovascular disease incidence (combined RR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.74 to 0.92) or mortality (combined RR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.71 to 0.85), cancer incidence (combined RR 0.88, 95% CI: 0.78 to 0.99) or mortality (combined RR 0.85, 95% CI: 0.76 to 0.95), and type 2 diabetes incidence (combined RR 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67 to 0.92), with moderate to low certainty of evidence. Among cancer survivors, moderate to low certainty of evidence was rated for the inverse association between diet quality indices and all-cause mortality (combined RR 0.83, 95% CI: 0.77 to 0.90). The etiology of non-communicable diseases contributes to the heterogeneity of findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Different diet quality indices have varying levels of certainty of evidence for each non-communicable disease incidence and mortality, underscoring the importance of defining high diet quality in nutritional guidelines.

articles.title: Antibacterial-anti-inflammatory-healing-promoting multifunctional hydrogel microneedles accelerate the repair of chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis (CIOM) is a prevalent and severe complication in patients with cancer undergoing chemotherapy. Its complex pathology involves direct mucosal damage, oxidative stress, severe inflammation, and secondary infection. In such a multifaceted environment, traditional drugs that target a single pro-repair mechanism often fail to effectively manage secondary infections driven by dysbiosis. These infections can worsen inflammation and disrupt the regenerative microenvironment, resulting in delayed healing or even recurrence. Thus, developing a multifunctional local treatment strategy that synergistically achieves antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and restorative effects is crucial. To address this, a multifunctional microneedle (MN) delivery system with both antibacterial and healing-promoting capabilities was developed in this study. The system employed a lipoic acid-modified chitosan (CL) and tannic acid (TA) composite hydrogel as a carrier for salvianolic acid B copper nanoclusters (SalB@Cu), forming SalB@Cu-CLT hydrogel MNs. These MNs exhibited excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility and could penetrate mucous membranes and release drugs sustainably. In vitro experiments confirmed their effectiveness in inhibiting bacterial proliferation and reducing inflammatory responses. Additionally, experiments using a CIOM model in Sprague-Dawley rats demonstrated that these MNs significantly promoted mucosal epithelium regeneration and angiogenesis, accelerating ulcer healing. This study offers a novel strategy with potential translational value for the clinical treatment of CIOM.

articles.title: MALDI-TOF MS and FT-IR spectroscopy for typing vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium: Comparison with PFGE in a hospital outbreak collection.
articles.abstract: Rapid and reliable strain typing is essential for investigating hospital outbreaks of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm). We evaluated MALDI-TOF MS and Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy as rapid typing approaches, and compared the resulting strain classifications with those obtained by pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE). Twenty-two VREfm isolates collected during a hospital outbreak investigation (November 2016-February 2017) were analyzed by MALDI-TOF MS and FT-IR spectroscopy; PFGE was performed for 18 isolates. Comparative analysis included 16 isolates with complete and interpretable results for all three methods. Concordance and discriminatory power were assessed using the Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) and Simpson's Index of Diversity (SID). MALDI-TOF MS identified six types among 21 classifiable isolates, FT-IR identified five clusters, and PFGE identified five major pulsotypes, with the predominant pulsotype A divided into closely related subtypes A1 and A2. In the 16-isolate comparative dataset, MALDI-TOF MS reproduced the PFGE subtype classification (ARI = 1.000; SID = 0.683), whereas FT-IR, using a dataset-specific cut-off of 0.154, grouped A1 and A2 together (ARI = 0.692; SID = 0.533). When A1 and A2 were considered variants of the same major pulsotype, FT-IR showed complete concordance with PFGE within this subset (ARI = 1.000). Epidemiological reconstruction supported a predominant Onco-Hematology cluster and a separate epidemiologically linked Neonatal cluster. MALDI-TOF MS reflected finer PFGE subtype-level differentiation, whereas FT-IR corresponded to the broader major-pulsotype structure. Both methods may have potential as preliminary typing approaches in VREfm outbreak investigations, but their results require epidemiological interpretation, while WGS remains preferable when high-resolution assessment of genomic relatedness is required.

articles.title: Pentraxin 3 polymorphisms predispose to Aspergillus infection and rejection after lung transplantation.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Polymorphisms in the pentraxin 3 (PTX3) gene have been implicated in innate immune defence and post-transplant complications. We assessed whether recipient and donor pentraxin 3 (PTX3) polymorphisms (rs2120243, rs2305619, rs3816527) were associated with post-transplant infection and rejection after lung transplantation.

METHODS: In a single-centre retrospective cohort, 203 lung transplant recipients and their donors were genotyped for three PTX3 single-nucleotide polymorphisms - rs2120243, rs2305619, and rs3816527. Primary outcomes were proven/probable invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA), clinically adjudicated Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, and CMV infection; secondary outcomes were primary graft dysfunction (PGD), acute cellular rejection (ACR), and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). Multivariable Aspergillus isolation and IPA analyses were adjusted for ICU length of stay, underlying lung disease, and anti-thymocyte globulin induction. Recipient-genotype associations were evaluated in an independent historical validation cohort of 529 recipients. PTX3 protein levels were evaluated in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and plasma.

RESULTS: Recipient, but not donor, homozygous PTX3 risk genotypes were associated with a higher hazard of proven/probable IPA after adjustment (rs2120243 AA: aHR 1.93 [1.03-3.63]; rs2305619 AA: 1.95 [1.04-3.64]; rs3816527 CC: 1.94 [1.04-3.62]; all p≤0.05). Associations with Aspergillus isolation were reproduced in the historical validation cohort (all p<0.05). Recipient variants were not significantly associated with first P. aeruginosa infection, but h1/h1 was associated with recurrent P. aeruginosa infection (HR 2.14 [1.00-4.59], p=0.050). h1/h1 haplotype was associated with ACR (HR 3.00 [1.11-8.06]) and CLAD (HR 2.21 [1.00-4.86]) in the discovery cohort, but these associations were not reproduced in the validation cohort. BALF, but not plasma, PTX3 levels increased in infection and ACR (all p<0.05) but were unrelated to PTX3 genotype.

CONCLUSION: Specific recipient PTX3 polymorphisms increase the risk of Aspergillus infection and rejection after lung transplantation. These findings underscore the clinical relevance of innate immune genetic variation and support PTX3 genotyping for post-transplant risk stratification.

articles.title: Host-directed therapy for mycobacterial disease: a clinical perspective.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both tissue-damaging inflammation and immunodeficiency play a critical role in the outcome of tuberculosis (TB) and non-tuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) disease and may be target for host-directed therapy (HDT).

OBJECTIVES: To provide a clinical perspective on use of HDT for mycobacterial disease.

SOURCES: Published literature and conference abstracts.

CONTENT: Patients with either insufficient immunity or excessive inflammation are prone to complications and poor outcomes in mycobacterial disease. Depending on the underlying immune dysregulation, HDT may improve outcomes through the addition of anti-inflammatory therapy, or immune-stimulatory treatment. For TB, guideline-recommended HDT is limited to adjuvant corticosteroids for TB meningitis and TB-associated immune reconstitution syndrome (IRIS) in HIV-positive patients. Small trials suggest functional benefit of several immune-modulatory drugs and case series have shown benefit of corticosteroids and other anti-inflammatory drugs for paradoxical inflammatory reactions during treatment of HIV-negative patients. For NTM disease, adjuvant interferon-gamma showed clinical-radiological benefit for pulmonary disease in one small trial, and benefit for difficult-to-treat disseminated disease in case reports.

IMPLICATIONS: Differentiating pathology related to immune deficiency from immune-induced pathology can be challenging but can help select appropirate HDT. In case of excessive inflammation, anti-inflammatory therapy with TNF antagonists, IL-1 receptor antagonists, and thalidomide can be considered in steroid-refractory disease or for steroid-sparing effects. In case of insufficienct mycobacterial clearance of difficult-to-treat NTM, recombinant interferon-gamma can be considered, and when applicable, immunosuppressive medication can be interruped, albeit with the risk of flares of underlying disease or 'withdrawal' inflammatory reactions.

articles.title: Machine learning-based prediction of mortality at candidemia diagnosis: development and external validation across multicentre cohorts.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early identification of candidemia patients at high risk of death may inform clinical management. We aimed to develop and externally validate a clinically interpretable machine learning model to predict 30-day all-cause mortality at candidemia diagnosis.

METHODS: The derivation cohort comprised pooled data from three prospective Spanish cohorts including adults with candidemia. Following benchmarking of seven supervised algorithms, an XGBoost algorithm was developed using nested cross-validation. Discrimination was assessed by the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and the precision-recall curve (AUC-PR). Calibration was assessed by calibration plots, intercept and slope. Overall performance was assessed by Brier score and scaled Brier score. Model interpretability was evaluated using Shapley additive explanations values. External validation used an international cohort from the European Confederation of Medical Mycology Candida III study.

RESULTS: Among 1,640 patients in the derivation cohort, 476/1,640 (29%) died within 30 days. The final model retained nine predictors of mortality: age, neoplasia, chronic kidney disease, chronic liver disease, recent surgery, septic shock, intensive care unit setting, presumed catheter-related source, and corticosteroid exposure. The derivation AUC-ROC was 0.749 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.723-0.775), AUC-PR 0.562 (95% CI 0.522-0.607), and Brier score 0.171 (95% CI 0.164-0.178). In the external validation cohort (n = 632 patients, 228/632, 36% mortality), AUC-ROC was 0.668 (95% CI 0.628-0.710), AUC-PR 0.515 (95% CI 0.467-0.574), and Brier score 0.218 (95% CI 0.204-0.232). Logistic recalibration improved the Brier score to 0.213 (95% CI 0.203-0.222) without changing discrimination.

CONCLUSION: This multicentre study developed and externally validated a machine-learning model using routinely available clinical variables that may provide a framework for early risk stratification of 30-day mortality in patients with candidemia. External validation showed lower discrimination and the need for recalibration, supporting further local validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Association Between Adjunctive Single-Ingredient Diosmin Prescribing and Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Acute Lower-Extremity Superficial Vein Thrombosis.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between documented adjunctive single-ingredient diosmin prescribing and short-term clinical outcomes in adults with acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days. The primary outcome was complete resolution or marked clinical improvement at the in-person assessment closest to day 14 within days 10 to 18. Missing baseline covariates were multiply imputed, and propensity scores were estimated within 20 imputed data sets. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting targeted the average treatment effect under measured-confounding assumptions. Secondary outcomes, including day-7 pain, were exploratory.

RESULTS: Diosmin was prescribed to 910 patients and not prescribed to 910. Primary improvement occurred in 728/910 (80.0%) and 669/910 (73.5%), respectively. Weighted standardized probabilities were 79.5% (95% confidence interval, 76.8%-82.2%) and 74.7% (71.8%-77.6%), yielding a risk difference of 4.8 percentage points (1.2-8.4) and a risk ratio of 1.06 (1.01-1.12). The E-value was 1.31 for the point estimate and 1.11 for the confidence limit. Excluding 142 patients with concomitant distal deep vein thrombosis gave a similar estimate (risk difference, 4.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-8.5). Exploratory day-7 pain-response probabilities were 75.0% and 61.5% after imputation, weighting, and marginal standardization. Thrombotic and bleeding estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSIONS: Documented adjunctive diosmin prescribing was associated with a small increase in short-term clinical improvement. Clinical importance is uncertain, and relatively weak unmeasured confounding could explain the primary association. The exploratory pain finding is hypothesis-generating. These data are insufficient to support routine diosmin use or substitution for guideline-directed anticoagulation; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

articles.title: Classical and quantum machine learning with grouped nested feature selection for diabetes and diabetic retinopathy prediction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE (S): To compare classical classifiers with simulated quantum/hybrid models using training-only feature selection and validation that separates identical predictor profiles.

STUDY DESIGN: Two UCI datasets included 1,151 retinopathy and 520 early-diabetes records. Primary validation used stratified grouped five-fold outer and three-fold inner cross-validation without resampling. Groups used complete predictor profiles, excluding labels. Four supervised selectors and all predictors were evaluated with four classical and four quantum/hybrid models. Row-based nested analyses with and without SMOTE provided sensitivity comparisons.

RESULTS: Classical and quantum/hybrid ROC-AUC values were 0.7597 ± 0.0273 and 0.7322 ± 0.0581 for retinopathy, and 0.9730 ± 0.0182 and 0.8921 ± 0.0418 for early diabetes. Early-diabetes accuracies were 93.78% and 79.24%, respectively. Classical pipelines selected all predictors in every outer fold. All 40 partition checks confirmed zero shared profile groups. Values following ± represent outer-fold sample standard deviations.

CONCLUSION (S): Under tested settings, simulated quantum/hybrid pipelines showed no observed predictive or partial final-evaluation runtime advantage. Grouped validation reduced near-perfect row-based diabetes estimates. Profile grouping does not establish patient-independent or external validation. Undocumented fixed subset-size choices remain a potential source of development bias.

articles.title: How dermatology became sexual medicine: a history of skin, sex, and venereal disease.
articles.abstract: The connection between sexuality, health, and disease predated the emergence of dermatology and venereology as medical specialties. In ancient societies, however, these associations differed from the modern concept of sexually transmitted infections. In biblical texts, genital discharges were interpreted in terms of ritual purity and impurity, whereas Greco-Roman medicine associated sexual activity with moderation, fertility, loss of strength, and bodily balance. In the early modern period, syphilis became increasingly understood as a disease associated with sexual contact. Its diverse cutaneous manifestations established a lasting link between venereal diseases and the emerging study of skin diseases. The article examines how the classification of skin lesions, clinical dermatology, research into venereal diseases, and specialized institutions contributed to linking dermatology and venereology clinically and institutionally by the 19th century. In the 20th century, microbiology, laboratory diagnostics, and antibiotic therapy transformed the diagnosis and treatment of venereal diseases. The cutaneous manifestations of HIV infection renewed the connection between dermatology, infectious diseases, and sexuality. Stigmatization, confidentiality, testing, sexual behaviour, and responsibility for transmission also became central concerns. The HIV/AIDS epidemic further reshaped the relationship between disease, sexuality, and public health, marking a transition from the traditional concept of venereal diseases towards a broader approach encompassing sexually transmitted infections and sexual health.

articles.title: Pseudorabies Virus US3 Promotes HK2 Phosphorylation and Glycolytic Reprogramming to Support Viral Replication.
articles.abstract: Although viruses commonly reprogram host glucose metabolism to support efficient replication, the molecular mechanisms underlying Pseudorabies virus (PRV)-induced metabolic alterations remain unclear. In this study, we found that PRV infection enhances host glycolytic activity. The glycolytic inhibitor 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) suppressed PRV replication both in vitro and in vivo, and this inhibitory effect was stronger when glucose was the main energy source. Mechanistically, PRV US3 interacted with HK2 and promoted HK2 phosphorylation. US3 also promoted HK2 mitochondrial localization, which was accompanied by changes in cellular HK activity and glycolytic metabolism. Importantly, mutation of the US3 kinase domain abolished its ability to promote HK2 phosphorylation, indicating that US3 kinase activity is required for the enhancement of HK2 phosphorylation during PRV infection but dispensable for the US3-HK2 interaction. Consistent with these findings, US3-deleted PRV (PRV-ΔUS3) and US3 kinase mutation PRV (PRV-US3mut) indeed showed a weakened enhancement effect on host glycolytic metabolism and exhibited attenuated replication and virulence compared to wild-type PRV. Collectively, our findings identify PRV US3 as an important regulator of HK2-associated metabolic remodeling and support a contribution of this metabolic regulation to efficient PRV replication.

articles.title: Diabetes-Associated Skeletal Fragility in Asia: Bridging the Gap Between Guidelines and Clinical Practice.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

articles.title: Genicular Artery Embolization for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Practical Guide and Future Directions on behalf of French Society of Rheumatology, Musculoskeletal Imaging Society, French Hip and Knee Society, French Society for Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery, French Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine, and of French Society of Radiology.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish considerations for the indication and performance of genicular arteries embolization (GAE) for painful knee osteoarthritis on behalf of consortium of national societies.

METHODS: Based on literature review and clinical practice, a multidisciplinary group of 16 healthcare professionals including rheumatologists, interventional and MSK radiologists, physical and rehabilitation medicine physicians, knee orthopedic surgeons, and member of people living with OA association produced the considerations. Results : The group established 11 specific considerations. GAE is indicated for patients with painful knee osteoarthritis for whom no other cause of pain can be identified, and whose pain is refractory despite usual optimal medical treatment. A pre-therapeutic knee synovitis should be searched prior to GAE using a Doppler ultrasound or, even better, a contrast-enhanced MRI. Interventional radiologists should perform pre- and post-GAE consultations in collaboration with other musculoskeletal physician, in order to integrate GAE into the multimodal management strategy. Currently, there is no consensus on GAE techniques, and these should be individualized according to patient characteristics and interventional radiologist preferences. GAE may be repeated in selected cases. There are no contraindications to undergoing knee surgery after having GAE, but after a reasonable delay of three months. GAE may be considered in selected patients with persistent knee pain after knee replacement and after exclusion of other causes, including joint infection.

CONCLUSIONS: These considerations provide a structured guide for GAE in painful knee osteoarthritis. Several questions warrant further investigation through clinical or basic research.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing responses to treatment in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.

RESEARCH QUESTION: Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m2), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) <45% predicted.

RESULTS: A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003).

INTERPRETATION: PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited.

RESEARCH QUESTION: In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation?

STUDY DESIGN: and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis.

RESULTS: When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type.

INTERPRETATION: In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

articles.title: Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus in an Immune Competent Patient: Importance of Prompt Diagnosis and Ophthalmological Evaluation.
Age-Dependent Prognostic Significance of Anemia After Acute Coronary Syndromes.
articles.abstract: Anemia is common in patients with acute coronary syndromes, but whether its prognostic significance varies according to age remains uncertain. We retrospectively analyzed 8,684 consecutive patients admitted with acute coronary syndromes to 2 tertiary hospitals in Spain. Baseline hemoglobin and anemia were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, heart failure, and major bleeding, and to long-term all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and major bleeding. Multivariable logistic, Cox regression, and competing-risk models were used. Interactions between age and hemoglobin or anemia were assessed. Median hemoglobin was 14.0 g/dL, and 21.8% of patients had anemia. Lower hemoglobin was independently associated with higher risks of in-hospital mortality, heart failure, and major bleeding. During a median follow-up of 58 months, lower hemoglobin and anemia were associated with all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and major bleeding. Significant interactions were observed between age and both hemoglobin and anemia. The excess risk associated with lower hemoglobin and anemia progressively decreased with advancing age and was markedly attenuated in patients aged ≥75 years. In conclusion, hemoglobin and anemia are independent predictors of adverse outcomes after acute coronary syndromes, but their long-term prognostic significance is strongly modified by age. Their association with adverse events is substantially greater in younger patients and attenuated in those aged ≥75 years.

articles.title: Combining Structure and Performance: The LVEDV/VO₂peak ratio Across Sport Categories in Olympic Athletes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Athlete's heart represents a morpho-functional adaptation to training. While left-ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) has traditionally been indexed to body size, recent studies suggest that indexing to oxygen consumption (VO₂peak); (LVEDV/VO₂peak) may better capture the proportional coupling between structure and function. We aimed to describe sex- and sport-specific values of LVEDV/VO₂peak ratio in Olympic athletes.

DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional, single-center, single-nation cohort study of athletes undergoing pre-participation screening, including echocardiography and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET).

METHODS: Athletes were categorized as Skill, Power, Mixed or Endurance. Linear regression was used to evaluate the LVEDV-VO₂peak relationship. LVEDV, VO₂peak LVEDVi, and LVEDV/VO₂peak were compared across sporting disciplines and by sex.

RESULTS: 1265 athletes were enrolled (mean age 25.8±5.1 years, 45.4% female). LVEDV showed a moderate-to-strong correlation with VO₂peak (R²=0.54, p<0.0001). Endurance athletes exhibited the highest LVEDV (147±35.9 mL) and VO₂peak (3.79±0.9 L/min), greater than all other groups (all p<0.0001). When indexed by BSA, LVEDVi increased stepwise from Skill (60.6±13.3 mL/m²) to Endurance (78.3±13.8 mL/m²; p<0.0001), while indexing LVEDV by VO₂peak showed the lowest in Endurance athletes (39.4±7.1 mL/L/min, p<0.0001) while no differences were found between the remaining groups (p=0.171). In females, LVEDV/VO₂peak differences did not reach overall significance (p=0.085), though Endurance athletes still had lower values than Power (p=0.015) and Mixed (p=0.020).

CONCLUSIONS: LVEDV was strongly associated with VO₂peak, with sport-specific differences in the LVEDV-VO₂peak relationship. The LVEDV/VO₂peak ratio provides a descriptive measure of LV chamber size relative to aerobic performance. Although not intended to define pathological cut-offs, values outside the distributions observed in this cohort may imply imbalanced physiologic remodeling.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Algorithm for Detection of Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Compared with a Standard Electrocardiogram.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) may facilitate detection of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), but its ability to identify higher-risk patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic performance of a commercially available AI-ECG algorithm among patients undergoing cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) for suspected or established HCM.

METHODS: We studied 102 patients with HCM and 302 age-, sex-, and year-matched controls without HCM who underwent clinically indicated CMR. An AI-ECG algorithm was applied to the first available ECG preceding CMR. Diagnostic performance, incremental value beyond standard ECG features, and associations with clinical outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: ECGs preceded CMR by a median of 1.1 years. AI-ECG demonstrated moderate sensitivity (51.1%) and high specificity (96.1%) for identification of phenotypic HCM and incrementally improved discrimination and reclassification beyond demographic and conventional ECG variables (net reclassification improvement 0.19, p<0.001). Within one year of CMR, a positive AI-ECG was independently associated with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 2.68, 95% CI 1.42-5.09; p=0.003), driven by ICD placement and septal reduction therapy. Among patients with HCM, while exploratory, an AI-ECG probability ≥ 0.99 identified those at highest risk for subsequent events (HR 2.92, 95% CI 1.59-5.35; p=0.011).

CONCLUSION: In conclusion, among patients undergoing clinical evaluation for HCM, AI-ECG provided incremental diagnostic value beyond conventional ECG parameters and identified individuals at increased risk for subsequent treatment-related clinical outcomes.

articles.title: The Impact of Preoperative Atrial Fibrillation on Outcomes Following Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
articles.abstract: A preoperative history of atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients receiving durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation has been associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality. It is uncertain how the type of preoperative AF (paroxysmal vs. persistent/permanent) impacts clinical outcomes in patients on LVAD support. We sought to determine how the presence and type of preoperative AF affect patient mortality following LVAD implantation. A single-center retrospective analysis was performed of patients who underwent LVAD implantation from 2006-2022. Patients with AF prior to LVAD implantation were characterized as having paroxysmal or persistent/permanent AF for comparison. A total of 289 patients (37%) with a history of preoperative AF underwent LVAD implantation. Paroxysmal AF (78.9%) was more common prior to LVAD implant than persistent/permanent AF (21.1%). The incidence of 30-day and 2-year all-cause mortality were significantly higher amongst patients with preoperative persistent/permanent AF compared to patients without reoperative AF (30-day mortality: 16.4% vs 6.4%, p=0.005; 2-year all-cause mortality: 44.3% vs 24.2%, p=0.001). Over long-term follow-up, the risk of all-cause mortality was significantly higher for patients with preoperative persistent/permanent AF compared to patients without preoperative AF controlling for age, sex, race, class III antiarrhythmic medications, destination therapy and device design (sdHR 1.94; 1.34-2.79 95% CI, p≤0.001). In contrast, there was no significant difference in mortality at 30-days or 2-years between patients with preoperative paroxysmal AF and those without preoperative AF (30-day mortality: 5.7% vs 6.4%, p=0.408; 2-year all-cause mortality: 27.2% vs 24.2%, p=0.010). The risk of long-term mortality was also not significantly different (sdHR 1.19; 0.95-1.5 95% CI, p=0.137). In conclusion, a preoperative history of persistent/permanent AF is associated with increased risk of mortality following LVAD implantation, but there is no significant difference in survival between patients with preoperative paroxysmal AF and those without AF.

articles.title: Association Between Prior Statin Therapy and Lipoprotein(a) Levels in Patients Admitted for Acute Coronary Syndrome.
articles.abstract: The persistence of coronary events in statin-treated patients highlights residual risk mechanisms beyond low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] playing a relevant role. Statin therapy appears to be associated with increased plasma Lp(a) levels of uncertain significance, although the clinical significance of this association remains uncertain. This study primarily aimed to evaluate Lp(a) levels according to prior statin therapy in patients hospitalized for acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondarily, it assessed the association between Lp(a) and previous atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). A total of 729 patients admitted for ACS with Lp(a) measurements were included. Clinical variables, lipid profile, statin treatment, and adherence were recorded. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to assess the association between Lp(a) and prior statin therapy, followed by propensity score matching to account for differences in baseline characteristics. The association between Lp(a) and a prior diagnosis of ASCVD was also evaluated using logistic regression. Overall, 49.5% of patients had prior statin therapy. These subjects showed lower LDL-C and apoB, but higher Lp(a) levels (77 [26-181] vs. 56 [26-133] nmol/L; p = 0.009). However, this association lost significance after multivariable (OR 1.277; 95% CI 0.807-2.021; p = 0.296) and propensity score adjustment (p = 0.686). Conversely, elevated Lp(a) was independently associated with prior ASCVD (OR 1.638; 95% CI 1.115-2.405; p = 0.012). In conclusion, in ACS patients, the unadjusted association between prior statin therapy and higher Lp(a) concentrations is explained by baseline cardiovascular risk and treatment indication. In contrast, elevated Lp(a) levels are independently associated with a prior diagnosis of ASCVD, reinforcing their role as a marker of residual cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.

CONCLUSION: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.

articles.title: Pathways into pharmacy: Career awareness, influences, and barriers among Doctor of Pharmacy students.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Racial, ethnic, cultural, and linguistic diversity in the United States underscores the need for a diverse pharmacy workforce that can effectively serve diverse communities. Efforts to strengthen workforce diversity begin in the pharmacy education pipeline, yet less is known about when students become aware of pharmacy, who introduces them to the profession, and what barriers and supports shape their pathway into Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) programs.

METHODS: A cross-sectional anonymous electronic survey was administered to currently enrolled P1 through P4 PharmD students at a pharmacy school located in a diverse metropolitan city. Items assessed career awareness and decision-making, sources of pharmacy exposure, shadowing, confidence factors, discouraging factors, supports for persistence, and retrospective early pipeline supports. Descriptive statistics summarized responses, and chi-square analyses examined differences by demographic characteristics.

RESULTS: Seventy-eight students completed the survey. The largest proportion first became aware of pharmacy during college junior/senior year (30.8%), and nearly half decided to pursue pharmacy during college junior/senior year (46.2%). Family was the most common source of introduction to pharmacy (30.8%), and 55.1% reported shadowing a pharmacist before pharmacy school. Interest in science and health was the highest-ranked confidence factor, while tuition/cost was the highest-ranked discouraging factor, with 60.3% ranking cost as most discouraging. The strongest supports for persistence were personal motivation, family encouragement, and mentorship. Students retrospectively ranked career exposure, shadowing, and PharmD program information as the most helpful earlier supports.

CONCLUSION: Earlier structured exposure, shadowing, mentorship, and clearer PharmD program information may strengthen pharmacy pipeline efforts.

articles.title: Cultural adaptation and validation of the "Nursing Research Questionnaire" in nurses of intensive care units in Chile.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Advancing and ensuring high-quality care in intensive care units (ICUs) requires nurses to be actively engaged in research. The Nursing Research Questionnaire (NRQ) is one of the few instruments available in Spanish to characterize nurses' research activity.

OBJECTIVE: To culturally adapt and psychometrically validate the Chilean Spanish version of the NRQ in a sample of ICU nurses in Chile.

METHODS: Methodological study of cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of a measurement instrument. The original NRQ underwent semantic and cultural review, followed by content validation by a panel of 10 expert nurses. It was then assessed for linguistic clarity and operational feasibility by 10 ICU nurses. Construct validity for each subscale of the NRQ was examined using exploratory factor analysis in a sample of 253 ICU nurses. Reliability was estimated using Cronbach's alpha and Mc Donald's omega.

RESULTS: The expert panel judged all items in the Chilean Spanish version of the NRQ to be relevant. Both the Research Knowledge subscale (n = 253) and the Barriers to Research subscale (n = 199) showed a two-factor structure, explaining 75% (F1: evidence-based practice; F2: research) and 53% (F1: organizational barriers; F2: confidence/external support) of the total variance, respectively. Both subscales demonstrated adequate reliability (α > .70). The Attitudes Toward Research subscale (n = 228) yielded a six-factor solution with low factor loadings, cross-loadings, and low overall reliability (α = .66).

CONCLUSION: The Chilean Spanish version of the NRQ showed adequate psychometric properties for assessing research knowledge and barriers amongst ICU nurses, but not for assessing attitudes toward research. Future studies should develop and psychometrically evaluate items that validly measure attitudes toward research in nursing.

articles.title: Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 attenuates high-salt-induced hypertension involving IL-17A signaling suppression.
articles.abstract:
SCOPE AND PURPOSE: Chronic high-salt (HS) intake induces hypertension and is associated with reduced intestinal Lactobacillus. This study investigated underlying mechanisms for Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 (CCFM639) alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Hypertensive mice were established using an 8% HS diet, and blood pressure (BP), vascular function, gut microbiota, intestinal immunity, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by radiotelemetry, pressure myography, 16S rRNA sequencing, histology, flow cytometry, qPCR, ELISA, and Western blot.

SIGNIFICANT RESULTS: CCFM639 significantly reduced BP, preserved intestinal barrier integrity, partially restored microbial dysbiosis, and suppressed ileal inflammation. Mechanistically, CCFM639 reduced IL-6 levels and inhibited the Interleukin-22 (IL-22) /STAT3/ Serum amyloid A (SAA) pathway, thereby limiting T helper 17 (Th17) cells activation and Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) production in the ileal lamina propria. IL-17A neutralization reproduced the antihypertensive and vasoprotective effects of CCFM639, accompanied by improved endothelium-dependent relaxation and reduced eNOS Thr495 phosphorylation and Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) expression. Consistently, CCFM639 supplementation reduced BP in hypertensive patients with high urinary sodium excretion, and the reduction in serum IL-17A levels was positively correlated with BP improvement.

MAJOR CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that CCFM639 supplementation increases intestinal Lactobacillus abundance and suppresses IL-17A signaling, thereby alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

articles.title: Increases in the isocapnic buffering period reduce cardiac events in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction - a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the role of the isocapnic buffering period, the difference between the oxygen consumption at the anaerobic threshold and the respiratory compensation point, to predict hospitalization and death in patients with Heart Failure (HF).

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients with HF with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF < 40%, NYHA I, II, and III).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Cardiopulmonary test data, muscle strength, and Quality of Life (QoL) were measured at baseline. Patients were followed over 48-months for cardiac events (hospitalization and cardiac-related death).

RESULTS: Seventy-three patients (∼58-years, 73% male, LVEF = 31%) were followed. Seventeen patients had cardiac events, and 56 patients were free of cardiac events. Both groups showed similar peak oxygen consumption (p = 0.597), inspiratory muscle strength (p = 0.351), and quadriceps muscle strength (p = 0.059). Using the multivariate analysis by the Cox proportional hazard model, the increase of one unit (mL/kg/min) in the isocapnic buffering period decreased the risk of cardiac events by 26% (p = 0.034) and higher scores (≥ 45-points) in the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure questionnaire were associated with increased risk (4.5-fold) of cardiac events (p = 0.020).

CONCLUSIONS: As a preliminary finding, the isocapnic buffering period is an independent predictor of hospitalization and death in patients with mild and moderate HF. Additionally, self-reported QoL is a useful tool to follow functional status and cardiac events in patients with HF.

articles.title: Barriers and facilitators to anxiety and depression treatment in epilepsy: A qualitative interview study of patient perspectives.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Anxiety and depression are common in epilepsy and often undertreated, yet little is known about epilepsy patient experiences of mental health care and patient-level barriers and facilitators to mental health care. We aimed to evaluate epilepsy patient perspectives on anxiety and depression and its treatment using qualitative methods, with primary objective to assess barriers and facilitators to care for anxiety and depression.

METHODS: Participants recruited from a study examining usual care outcomes among adults with epilepsy and anxiety and/or depression symptoms completed focused semi-structured telephone interviews (NCT03879525). The interview guide explored experiences with anxiety and depression symptoms, treatment preferences, and care barriers and facilitators. Interviews were recorded, professionally transcribed and cleaned to ensure accuracy. Thematic analysis was conducted using deductive and inductive approaches. Two experts in qualitative analysis generated the codebook, coded all interviews and completed analysis using NVIVO software.

RESULTS: The study sample (N = 16) included 11 women (69%). Four participants (25%) identified as Black, one as Native American, and one as multiracial; 10 (63%) identified as white/non-Hispanic. Most participants indicated current significant impact of anxiety and/or depression on daily life, and many discussed a link between anxiety and/or depression and their epilepsy, including fear related to Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy (SUDEP). Most participants had previously engaged in treatment for anxiety and/or depression, most often medications, psychotherapy, or healthy living behaviors. Top barriers in seeking treatment for anxiety and/or depression were provider rapport/communication, transportation limitations, and individual hesitancy to seek treatment or add medication. Treatment facilitators included family, support groups, and neurologist efforts to facilitate treatment. Trust emerged as a key theme in provider interactions across various provider specialties, including neurology.

CONCLUSION: While barriers and facilitators to mental health care in epilepsy were identified at many levels for potential intervention, ranging from individual patient-level to broader societal/social factors, key actionable contributors at the neurology provider level were identified. Trust and provider rapport/communications were important drivers of mental health treatment experience, neurologists' willingness to serve as mental health provider was a key facilitator, and participants were comfortable with their neurologist acting as mental health provider.

articles.title: Molecular and physiological role of phoenixin in reproduction and metabolic regulation.
articles.abstract: Phoenixin is a recently identified peptide derived from SMIM20 precursor that was initially characterised for its role in reproductive neuroendocrine regulation. Increasing evidence indicates that PNX signalling extends beyond the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and involves metabolic, cardiovascular and inflammatory processes. This review examines the molecular biology, tissue distribution and signalling mechanisms of PNX with particular emphasis on its proposed receptor GPR173 and the biological activities of PNX-14 and PNX-20. Experimental studies indicate that PNX influences GnRH and kisspeptin signalling, gonadotropin secretion, ovarian function, feeding behaviour, adipogenesis, pancreatic β-cell activity and hepatic metabolism, providing a potential connection between reproductive function and energy homeostasis. Evidence from different vertebrate models also reveals substantial species and context dependent variations in PNX responses. Although cAMP/PKA/CREB, ERK 1/2 and PI3K/Akt pathways have been implicated in several PNX-mediated effects. The receptor mechanism remains unresolved, particularly because direct activation of GPR173 has not been consistently demonstrated. Genetic evidence from Smim20 knockdown models further indicates that PNX may be modulatory rather than indispensable for reproductive or metabolic homeostasis. Human studies remain limited and are predominantly observational, restricting conclusions regarding causality and clinical relevance. Taken together, current findings position PNX as a potentially important interface between neuroendocrine, reproductive and metabolic regulation while highlighting substantial gaps in receptor biology, isoform-specific actions and translational validation. Resolving these issues will determine whether the PNX system represents a clinically actionable pathway or primarily a context dependent component of physiological regulation.

articles.title: Mental health as the next frontier in critical care nursing, part 1: recognizing mental health in critical care.
Immunoinformatics based design and evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting the envelopment polyprotein of Andes orthohantavirus.
articles.abstract: Andes Orthohantavirus is known to be the etiological agent for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), which is a highly dangerous disease with a very high death rate. There is no vaccine available to date to protect against this disease. This project aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine for Andes Orthohantavirus using immunoinformatics. Epitopes of CTL, HTL, and B cell types were predicted for the shortlisted Glycoprotein precursor after testing antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and subcellular location. The chosen epitopes were combined using appropriate linkers and β-defensin as an adjuvant to create a multi-epitope vaccine. The final vaccine construct had a length of 296 amino acids and showed excellent antigenicity (0.7297), non-allergenicity, structural stability, and solubility properties. The structure of the vaccine construct showed that 94.6% of residues lie in the preferred areas of the Ramachandran plot, thus ensuring good stereochemistry. Molecular docking and normal mode analysis results confirmed the stable binding of the vaccine construct to TLR-3 receptors. At the same time, immune simulation revealed a fast degradation of antigens, production of antibodies, memory B-cells, and cytokines. In silico cloning integrated the codon-optimized gene with a CAI value of 0.97 and a GC percentage of 49.77% into the plasmid vector pET-28a(+). The designed multi-epitope vaccine displayed good predicted immunogenicity, structure, and expression properties that made it suitable to be used as a potential vaccine candidate against Andes Orthohantavirus infection. Further experimental validation is needed to assess its safety and effectiveness.

articles.title: Effects of basic activities of daily living interventions in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To systematically evaluate the effect of basic activities of daily living (BADL) intervention on patients with stroke-induced hemiplegia.

BACKGROUND: Due to motor and sensory dysfunction, patients with stroke-induced hemiplegia are restricted in performing basic daily living activities, which seriously affects their ability to take care of themselves and their quality of life. BADL intervention, which involves training in basic self-care tasks such as eating, dressing, and bathing, and functional mobility, is an important measure for the rehabilitation of stroke-induced hemiplegia.

METHODS: This review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. The Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, CBM, Wanfang, Embase, PubMed, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases were systematically searched from 2015 to 2025 to identify randomized controlled trials.

RESULTS: A total of nine randomized controlled trials were included, involving 521 patients with hemiplegia after stroke. The meta-analysis results showed that compared with conventional intervention, BADL intervention could significantly improve the self-care ability of patients [standardized mean difference (SMD) = 1.10, 95% confidence interval (CI) (0.64, 1.57), P < 0.00001] and significantly improve the upper limb motor function [SMD = 0.61, 95% CI (0.33, 0.89), P < 0.00001].

CONCLUSIONS: Basic activities of daily living interventions may improve self-care ability and upper-limb motor function in patients with post-stroke hemiplegia. However, given the limited number of included studies, methodological limitations, and heterogeneity across studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Further high-quality, large-scale randomized controlled trials with standardized outcome measures and longer follow-up periods are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Who is the patient with metabolic acidosis? What six bicarbonate trials mean for critical care practice.
Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: M1 macrophage extracellular vesicles alleviate IL-33-driven group 2 innate lymphoid cell-dominant airway inflammation.
articles.abstract: Recently, an increasing number of reports have suggested that group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) play a critical role in allergic diseases. Previous studies have observed a positive correlation between the number of different types of ILCs and M1 and M2 macrophages in asthma. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from M1 macrophages (M1 EVs) have high biosafety and low immunogenicity, making them promising cell-free therapeutic agents that provide significant advantages in tumor therapy. However, their function in regulating ILC2s responses remains unclear. Therefore, in this study, M1 EVs were produced to investigate their role in IL-33-driven ILC2s-dominant airway inflammation. The morphology, size, and specific markers of the M1 EVs were successfully characterized. We observed that airway administration of low-dose M1 EVs effectively inhibited ILC2s activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and lung mucus production, and reduced levels of Th2 cytokines. Through qPCR analysis, we found that the long non-coding RNA IGF2BP1-AS may be involved in mediating these effects of M1 EVs. Furthermore, M1 EVs also displayed favorable safety performance. In conclusion, we demonstrated that low dose M1 EVs were able to at least partially block ILC2s-mediated airway inflammation via IGF2BP1-AS, suggesting that M1 EVs may be a novel cell-free means of treating type 2 immunopathologic diseases such as eosinophilic asthma.

articles.title: Phthalate-PFAS co-exposure and serum estradiol in adult U.S. men.
articles.abstract: Men are concurrently exposed to phthalates and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), but their joint association with serum estradiol remains unclear. In a repeated cross-sectional analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2018 data, we fitted survey-weighted models and examined transcriptomes and functional studies. Among 2148 adult men, the urinary molar sum of four di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate metabolites (ΣDEHP) was inversely associated with serum estradiol (β = -0.048; 95% CI -0.079 to -0.016). The association was steeper at higher serum perfluoroundecanoic acid (PFUnDA) concentrations (interaction β = -0.047). Because 45.6% of PFUnDA measurements were below detection, we assessed four joint models accounting for censoring and concentration rounding in the same participants. All four estimates were negative (β = -0.038 to -0.033), with simultaneous 95% CIs excluding zero within the eight-effect family. The broader six-PFAS model incorporating examination session yielded a smaller, less precise estimate (β = -0.022; 95% CI -0.066-0.021; n = 2083). The findings are E2-focused; matched hormone comparisons did not establish E2 selectivity. Separate functional studies reported reduced testicular steroid production after exposure to DEHP or its monoester metabolite, and inhibition of androgen and estrogen conversion by PFUnDA. Transcriptomes provided complementary context for steroid supply and estrogen processing. These findings support a conditional co-exposure association and identify steroid supply and conversion as candidate processes for direct co-exposure evaluation.

articles.title: Prenatal ambient PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy and postpartum depression: A prospective Birth Cohort study in China.
articles.abstract: Evidence on the association between prenatal fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and postpartum depression (PPD) remains inconsistent, and the potential mediating role of antenatal depressive symptoms remains underexplored. We included 10,568 women from the China Southwest Birth Cohort, a multicenter prospective cohort in China. Residential PM2.5 exposure was estimated for the entire pregnancy and each trimester. PPD and antenatal depressive symptoms were assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale at 6 weeks postpartum and during the second trimester, respectively. To mitigate potential endogeneity in PM2.5 exposure, we applied a two-stage residual inclusion approach using wind speed as an instrumental variable. We further examined effect modification by maternal age, tobacco exposure, parity, and pre-pregnancy BMI, and conducted mediation analyses to evaluate antenatal depressive symptoms as a potential mediator. PPD was identified in 2336 (22.1%) women. Each 10 μg/m3 increase in whole-pregnancy PM2.5 exposure was associated with 28% higher odds of PPD (OR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.06-1.54). The association was stronger among women exposed to tobacco smoke (OR: 1.79; 95% CI: 1.25-2.57; P for heterogeneity = 0.046). Among trimester-specific exposures, the association was most pronounced during the second trimester (OR: 1.18; 95% CI: 1.02-1.38). Mediation analyses suggested a modest indirect effect through antenatal depressive symptoms, accounting for 9.7% of the estimated total effect of second-trimester PM2.5 exposure on PPD. This prospective birth cohort study provides strengthened evidence that higher prenatal PM2.5 exposure is associated with an increased risk of postpartum depression, with mid-pregnancy emerging as a susceptible exposure window and tobacco-exposed women showing greater susceptibility. Antenatal depressive symptoms may serve as a modest intermediate pathway, explaining a relatively small proportion of the association between prenatal PM2.5 exposure and PPD. These findings support stronger air-quality policies alongside potential benefits from integrated antenatal screening and support for depressive symptoms, particularly among environmentally vulnerable women.

articles.title: Visualizing artificial intelligence predictions for clinical experts - Detection of acute rejection from cardiac magnetic resonance images of heart transplant patients.
articles.journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most current convolutional neural network (CNN)-based artificial intelligence (AI) models have a limited ability to visualize how the resulting prediction is formed. This overshadows the integration of AI models into the clinical routine. This study aimed to develop a clinician-oriented workflow for visualizing CNN predictions in cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) mapping, using acute heart transplant rejection as a clinical example.

METHODS: We developed a pipeline to visualize image regions contributing to CNN predictions in a clinically interpretable format. As a proof of concept, the workflow was applied to a CNN detecting acute rejection from CMR T1 and T2 maps of heart transplant patients. The model used T1 and T2 maps from basal, mid-ventricular, and apical regions of the left ventricle. The operation of the model was visualized by using class activation mapping (ScoreCAM and GradCAM), and normalized occlusion maps. These methods were applied to input CMR images. The outputs were masked to the myocardium, transformed into a color-coded 16-segment cardiac model, and quantitatively compared with segmental ground-truth findings.

RESULTS: The pipeline enabled automated analysis of CNN visualization activations and their presentation in a clinically familiar 16-segment model. Substantial intersegment variability was observed.

CONCLUSION: We presented a clinician-oriented workflow for visualizing and evaluating CNN predictions in CMR mapping. Using heart transplant rejection as an example, the approach transformed post-hoc AI visualizations into a clinically familiar cardiac segment model. Independent clinical validation isrequiredbefore thevisualizationoutputs can be linked toclinical phenomenaor used in clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Consensus-Based Development and Content Validation of Deliberative Criteria for the Evaluation of Innovative and High-Cost Medicines in Mexico: A Delphi Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The evaluation of innovative and high-cost medicines requires deliberative approaches that integrate clinical, economic, ethical, and contextual considerations beyond conventional health technology assessment. This study aimed to develop deliberative criteria and establish their content validity through expert consensus to support the evaluation of these medicines in Mexico.

METHODS: A modified Delphi study was conducted in four phases: development of preliminary criteria by an expert working group, pilot testing, a two-round Delphi process, and framework consolidation. Thirty-three multidisciplinary experts from healthcare institutions, academia, civil society, and the pharmaceutical industry participated. Consensus was predefined as ≥70% agreement; criteria not reaching consensus were revised using qualitative feedback and reevaluated in a second round.

RESULTS: Pilot testing expanded the 12 preliminary criteria to 14. In Round 1, 12 of 14 criteria reached consensus (agreement 75.8-90.9%). Target population size and definition and Applicability to the national context (69.7% each) were revised; in Round 2 (n = 30), both reached 100% agreement. The final framework integrates clinical benefit, safety, unmet medical need, evidence quality, implementation feasibility, ethical and equity considerations, real-world evidence, and economic impact.

CONCLUSION: A consensus-based framework of 14 content-validated criteria was developed to support transparent and multidimensional evaluation of innovative and high-cost medicines in Mexico, complementing rather than replacing expert judgment.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Survey of glucose levels in adults with T1DM attending clinic using automated insulin delivery (AID) devices compared with manual insulin delivery" [Diabetes Res. Clin. Pract. 233 (2026) 113136].
Assessment of the optimal echocardiographic profile on left ventricular assist device support: an outcome-driven definition.
Application of artificial intelligence in vestibular information detection: A critical narrative review.
articles.journal: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
articles.abstract: Vertigo diagnosis has high stakes, since one symptom spans benign positional vertigo to stroke, while common vestibular audiology tools (VOG and CDP) face limitations including dependence on human expertise, high cost, and cross-sectional evaluation. The aim of this study is to critically assess the maturity of AI applications in the detection of vestibular disorders from a clinical audiology perspective, with the criterion of "readiness for clinical use" rather than just algorithmic accuracy. This narrative critical review was conducted, according to SANRA guidelines, based on searches in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore (2006-2026) and hand-checking of reference lists of key articles. Nystagmus analysis achieved F1 above 0.97 in rotational nystagmus; vestibular schwannoma segmentation reported a pooled Dice of 0.89 (95% CI: 0.88-0.90) with a meta-analysis of 56 models from 11 studies; and CNN/fuzzy posturography demonstrated 97% accuracy in assessing postural dysfunction after stroke. For ECochG, machine learning has been applied successfully to intracochlear recordings and to MRI-based endolymphatic hydrops assessment, but within the scope of this search we identified no study applying AI to click-evoked extratympanic ECochG waveforms, specifically the summating-potential to action-potential (SP/AP) ratio, for the diagnosis of endolymphatic hydrops in Ménière's disease. The progress of AI in this domain is heterogeneous; some subfields have reached relative maturity, but the ECochG-Ménière gap remains at the intersection of otherwise well-developed areas. Future priorities include multicenter standardization, prospective validation, and addressing the debated role of interpretability. The focus on English-language sources is a limitation of this review.

articles.title: Insights into Channelopathies and Sport: The Genotype-Positive/Phenotype-Negative Athlete from Molecular Diagnosis to Management.
articles.abstract: Channelopathies, diseases with ion channel perturbations, are a major cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes. Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent. These genotype-positive/phenotype-negative (G+/P-) individuals present a distinct clinical challenge. Standard preparticipation screening, designed around phenotypic findings, provides little guidance for their management. A critical gap exists in providing prognostic guidance based on the involved gene, specific variants, and its molecular consequences. Beyond a critical review of existing literature, we provide a mechanistically anchored framework for variant-specific arrhythmic risk stratification across the major channelopathy genes. For each gene, we translate molecular pathophysiology into clinically actionable risk profiles and examine how exercise-specific triggers, including adrenergic surge, electrolyte shifts, and sympathovagal imbalance, interact with the underlying molecular substrate to modulate arrhythmic vulnerability. Standard diagnostic tools ranging from electro- and echocardiography, exercise stress testing, and pharmacological provocation to emerging modalities such as electroanatomic mapping and magnetocardiography are evaluated for their capacity to unmask subclinical disease and refine sports eligibility decisions. The case for an interdisciplinary sports-cardio-genetic board is made alongside a call for international collaborative registries, as existing evidence in G+/P- athletes is largely absent. The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection. Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.

articles.title: How Effective is Stretching for Injury Prevention? A Large-Scale Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sports injuries can impact athletes' availability, threaten their career, and have substantial financial impact. Stretching is commonly used as a prevention strategy. However, controversial evidence, methodological shortcomings, and substantial time elapsed since previous key data syntheses justify performing an updated systematic review.

OBJECTIVE: Our goal was to assess the effects of stretching interventions on injury risk.

METHODS: We followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included humans performing stretching and at least one comparator group; sports-related injury data were required. Studies were identified from six electronic databases (CINAHL Complete, Embase, PubMed, Scopus, SPORTDiscus, and Web of Science), reference lists, citation tracking, and consultation with external experts. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane tools. Raw injury data were used to assess odds ratios (OR), with OR < 1 meaning a preventive effect for stretching. Results were presented with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and prediction intervals (PIs). An inverse-variance random-effects model was employed using the DerSimonian and Laird estimator. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: Over 300,000 records were screened, with 19 studies fulfilling the eligibility criteria (> 9000 participants, > 80% male, age range 14-59 years), of which 15 were used for the meta-analyses. Interventions lasted 4-24 weeks and mostly implemented static unassisted stretching with varying volumes. Half the studies used passive controls, and half used diverse active comparators. Risk of bias was high for ~90% of randomized trials and serious for all non-randomized trials. No injury prevention effect was detected for stretching versus all other comparators (k = 15, n = 9,002; OR = 0.945, p = 0.396, 95% CI 0.828-1.078, 95% PI 0.773-1.155), passive controls (k = 10, n = 6273; OR = 0.923, p = 0.209, 95% CI 0.814-1.046, 95% PI 0.796-1.069), or active controls (k = 6, n = 2744; OR = 1.190, p = 0.312, 95% CI 0.849-1.667, 95% PI 0.738-1.919). Likewise, no injury prevention effect was found for muscle, tendon, and ligament/joint capsule injury risk, or across 19 sensitivity analyses, 3 subgroup analyses, and 3 secondary analyses. GRADE denoted very low certainty of evidence for all outcomes except bone injury risk (low certainty).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite the very low to low certainty of evidence as per GRADE judgments, the data consistently showed no chronic effect of stretching on injury risk across multiple analyses. No study assessed the acute effects of stretching on injury risk. Given the studied samples, these conclusions apply mostly to male participants aged 14-60 years performing static unassisted stretching, with little to no information about other populations or interventions. There is virtually no research using sport-specific stretching exercises. Several other caveats are discussed, as well as implications for practice, policy-making and future research.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO: CRD42024616532. OSF project ( https://osf.io/umj8h/ ) and registration ( https://osf.io/ybdvw ).

articles.title: Dental caries and enamel defects in children with coeliac disease.
articles.journal: European archives of paediatric dentistry : official journal of the European Academy of Paediatric Dentistry
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate the prevalence and characteristics of developmental enamel defects and dental caries in paediatric patients with coeliac disease compared with non-coeliac controls, and to assess the consistency and clinical relevance of the available comparative evidence.

METHODS: A systematic review of observational studies was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic searches were performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and CINAHL Complete via EBSCOhost from database inception to October 2025. Eligible studies included comparative observational designs with a predominantly paediatric age distribution, confirmed coeliac disease, non-coeliac controls, and dental caries and/or enamel-defect outcomes. Study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment were performed independently by two reviewers. Owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised using a structured narrative approach.

RESULTS: Nine studies (ten reports) met the eligibility criteria. Developmental enamel defects were more frequently reported in children with CD than in controls and were often symmetrical and chronologically distributed. Dental caries findings were inconsistent across studies and dentitions. Evidence regarding molar-incisor hypomineralisation was limited to two studies. Quantitative pooling was not undertaken because outcome definitions, units of analysis, dentition, reporting formats, and the availability of comparable effect data differed substantially between studies.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Developmental enamel defects appear to occur more frequently in paediatric patients with coeliac disease, but the available evidence does not establish their diagnostic accuracy for detecting CD. Their presence may contribute to clinical suspicion when interpreted alongside the medical history and other findings. Children with established CD, particularly those with enamel alterations, may benefit from individualised preventive dental strategies and closer follow-up.

articles.title: Shikonin in Cardiovascular Inflammatory Injury: Immunometabolic Regulation, Mitochondrial Homeostasis, and Regulated Cell Death.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular inflammation is sustained by reciprocal changes in immune-cell metabolism, mitochondrial function, and stress-responsive cell death. Shikonin, a naphthoquinone derived from the roots of Lithospermum erythrorhizon and related medicinal plants, is widely used experimentally as an inhibitor of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) and also modifies redox and stress-response signaling. Cardiovascular studies now extend from endothelial cells and vascular smooth muscle cells to experimental atherosclerosis, myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury, cardiac remodeling, pulmonary hypertension, cardiotoxicity, and thrombosis. The strongest cardiovascular evidence concerns PKM2-dependent glycolysis: shikonin suppresses inflammatory metabolic activation in macrophages and lymphocytes, reduces foam-cell formation and vascular smooth muscle-cell proliferation, and attenuates metabolic remodeling in cardiac and pulmonary vascular models. Mitochondrial membrane potential, reactive oxygen species, NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses, and fission-related proteins are also responsive to shikonin in cardiovascular models. Apoptosis and inflammasome-associated signaling show context-dependent activity, while other regulated cell-death pathways require interpretation within the specific experimental system.
