Emerging liposomal and hydrogel formulations offer avenues for tissue-selective delivery, with vascular reactivity and hemostatic safety central to cardiovascular translation. Overall, shikonin represents a promising preclinical scaffold for immunometabolic modulation and formulation-specific cardiovascular investigation.

articles.title: Mechanisms and Implications of SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Hematopoietic System.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 disrupts hematopoiesis across the entire hierarchy, from hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) to mature blood cells. Several hematological abnormalities-lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia and elevated D-dimer-are consistently associated with disease severity and mortality. Within the HSPC compartment, ACE2 and TMPRSS2 expression is largely restricted to rare CD133 + CD34+Lin-CD45 - precursors, suggesting that hematopoietic injury may arise substantially from non-infectious exposure to spike protein and inflammatory mediators rather than from direct viral infection. Downstream events include NLRP3 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis, virus-induced senescence with a senescence-associated secretory phenotype, epigenetic reprogramming, and skewed lineage output. These cell-intrinsic changes are compounded by remodeling of the bone marrow niche by stromal, endothelial, and osteoblastic cells. Clinically, these changes manifest as lymphopenia with T-cell exhaustion and disturbed regulatory T-cell balance, thrombocytopenia due to impaired megakaryopoiesis and immune-mediated clearance, coagulopathy involving neutrophil extracellular trap formation and endothelial injury, and anemia reflecting disordered iron handling and red-cell damage. These abnormalities can persist in a subset of patients long after viral clearance. These mechanistic insights inform current management, including antiviral therapy for prolonged viral shedding, corticosteroids for severe disease, severity-stratified anticoagulation, and supportive measures to promote marrow recovery. The hematological implications of vaccination are also considered: although rare immune thrombotic events have been reported, their mechanism appears distinct from spike-protein-induced injury, and the overall benefit-risk balance of vaccination remains favorable. We distinguish conclusions supported by clinical data from those based on in vitro or observational evidence and highlight open questions for future research.

articles.title: Improving Assessment Practices With Autistic Girls: Views and Experiences of Psychologists in the Republic of Ireland.
articles.journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The role of sex and gender warrants careful consideration in autism identification. Studies focusing on prevalence rates consistently report higher numbers of autistic boys compared to autistic girls, and there is increasing awareness autistic girls may be under-identified within the general population. Different reasons have been cited, including issues with assessment practices and behavioural differences between autistic girls and autistic boys.

METHODS: In attempting to understand and improve assessment practices with autistic girls, 91 psychologists working in publicly funded services in the Republic of Ireland involved in autism assessments with children completed a survey focused on their autism assessment experiences, with an emphasis on autistic girls. Survey questions were designed to gather quantitative and qualitative data, with descriptive statistics and content analysis used to provide an overview of participants' responses.

RESULTS: Psychologists reported gender-related differences in autism assessments, highlighting diverse expressions of autistic differences and different referral reasons. Specific gender-based assessment practices were noted, resulting in lengthier assessments with autistic girls. Most psychologists engaged in 'upgrading' (autism identified in cases where presentations are less clear and/or where individuals do not meet thresholds on standard diagnostic tools (Rogers et al., 2016), with nearly half reporting that it happens more frequently with autistic girls compared to autistic boys.

CONCLUSION: Further research is needed to explore the role of clinical judgement in autism assessment and identification, as well as parental and autistic girls' experiences of assessments. From a practice-based perspective universities offering psychology professional training need to develop curricula of learning in autism assessment and identification to include experiences of autistic females.

articles.title: Age- and sex-related differences in Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. on the adult ocular surface.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Ocular surface bacterial flora is a potential source of bacterial keratitis and post-operative endophthalmitis, but age- and sex-related differences in ocular surface bacterial flora and antimicrobial resistance remain unclear. We investigated these differences in bacterial isolates and levofloxacin (LVFX) susceptibility in adults.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study.

METHODS: We reviewed microbiological data on conjunctival isolates from 18,053 eyes of 11,677 adults without ocular infection undergoing ophthalmic surgery at the Miyata Eye Hospital between June 2018 and December 2023. Data were analyzed using generalized additive and log-linear model. LVFX susceptibility was determined using the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute broth microdilution protocol.

RESULTS: 22,561 bacterial isolates (11,081 from women; 11480 from men) were obtained from adults aged >19 years. The number of species isolated from women was lower than men, and increased at a rate of 1.19 and 1.09 per 10 years of age in women and men, respectively (p < 0.0001). Staphylococcus epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. were predominant across all age groups. Under 80 years of age, methicillin-sensitive S. epidermidis (MSSE) was isolated more frequently from men than from women. Corynebacterium spp. increased with age in both sexes. Between age 40-90 years, LVFX resistance in MSSE was higher in women than in men, whereas LVFX resistance in Corynebacterium spp. increased with age regardless of sex.

CONCLUSION: S. epidermidis and Corynebacterium spp. showed age- and sex-related differences in isolation frequency and fluoroquinolone susceptibility. Age and sex may influence ocular surface microbial ecology, antimicrobial resistance, and perioperative infection control.

articles.title: HPV-Associated Odontogenic Cyst with Dysplasia.
articles.abstract: HPV involvement in odontogenic cysts remains controversial because reported detection rates are low and inconsistent, and commonly used methods such as PCR or immunohistochemistry cannot confirm true infection or exclude contamination. The prevalence and any biological relevance of HPV in these lesions therefore remain unproven. We report a rare case of an HPV-associated odontogenic keratocyst with dysplasia in a 70-year-old patient supported by definitive evidence of infection and chromosomal instability.

articles.title: Diabetic foot infections with positive fungal cultures - does antifungal treatment affect outcomes?
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract: The significance of fungi in diabetic foot infections (DFI) is unclear. We examined outcomes in patients with fungi recovered from DFI cultures obtained during surgery (N = 156), and found no difference in rates of wound healing, need for additional surgery or amputation, between patients who did or did not receive antifungal therapy.

articles.title: 4-imidazolecarboxaldehyde attenuates virulence and pathogenicity of Pseudomonas aeruginosa by targeting las and rhl systems.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an important pathogen which often causes serious and difficult-to-treat infections in humans due to its high intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance, highlighting an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies or agents. QS system serves as the core regulatory network governing virulence and antibiotic resistance of PA, has been recognized as important targets for anti-virulence therapy. In this study, 4-Imidazolecarboxaldehyde, a 4-formyl imidazole derivative, was identified as a promising QS inhibitor that could significantly suppress the expression of the QS-associated genes of lasI/R, rhlI/R, pqsA/R, lasA, rhlA and phzA1, and inhibit the corresponding virulence factor production of lasA encoded protease, rhlA related rhamnolipid and phzA1 associated pyocyanin, as well as the motility and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 at sub-MICs of 80 and 160 µg/mL. The pathogenicity of PAO1 could also be attenuated by 4-imidazolecarboxaldehyde at 80 and 160 µg/mL, verified by Chinese cabbage, D. melanogaster and C. elegans infection analysis. 4-Imidazolecarboxaldehyde might target las and rhl systems to interfere with QS system based on the molecular docking analysis and the infection analysis in mutants. Less drug resistance tendency to PAO1 was observed, at least 20 generations tested. Furthermore, 4-Imidazolecarboxaldehyde could enhance the sensitivity of tetracycline and azithromycin to PAO1 obviously. Therefore 4-imidazolecarboxaldehyde was identified as a promising QSI agent of PA targeting las and rhl systems, used independently or synergistically with tetracycline and azithromycin to attenuate PA infections without obviously detectable resistance.

articles.title: Sulforaphane and Ischemic Postconditioning Provide Cardioprotection in the Hypercholesterolemic Heart Through Multitarget Effects and Modulation of KLF4/15 and Nrf2.
articles.abstract: Hypercholesterolemia (HC) is tightly associated with chronic inflammation and oxidative stress and contributes to coronary artery disease. HC can accelerate the progression of myocardial ischemia, compromising the effectiveness of protective strategies and making the myocardium more vulnerable to injury. Consequently, affecting the activation of protective mechanisms. Oxidative stress and chronic inflammation are closely interrelated; targeting both could be potentially effective for protecting the reperfused heart under HC. Among the effective strategies to alleviate oxidative damage in preclinical studies are sulforaphane (SFN) and ischemic postconditioning (iPostC). SFN is a bioactive compound that can induce protective mechanisms, such as the activation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2). Similarly, iPostC activates protective mechanisms to prevent reperfusion injury, including Nrf2 activation and inflammation diminishment, as demonstrated in healthy animal models. Therefore, there is a need to develop effective strategies to prevent myocardial damage in the presence of HC as a risk factor. This study evaluated the efficacy of combined SFN and iPostC therapy in protecting the heart against reperfusion injury in high-cholesterol-fed rats. We found that this combined strategy was associated with multitarget protective actions, correlating with attenuated inflammation, reduced nuclear accumulation of nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) p65 and Krüppel-like factor (KLF)-5, restoration of redox balance, and increased nuclear levels of Nrf2, KLF4, and KLF15. These data support the maintenance of cardiac function following myocardial infarction in the setting of HC.

articles.title: From Reactive Care to Prevention in Neurodegenerative Diseases: Biomarkers, Risk Prediction, and Early Intervention.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) are typically diagnosed only after substantial and irreversible neuronal damage has occurred, at a point when disease-modifying interventions are least likely to be effective. Increasing evidence indicates that the molecular and cellular processes driving neurodegeneration often begin years to decades before clinical onset. This preclinical phase offers an opportunity for early detection, although translating it into clinically effective prevention remains a major challenge. In this review, we examine advances in fluid-based, neuroimaging, genetic, and multi-omics biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, and other NDs. We propose a staged framework, from risk prediction to actionable intervention, to discuss how integrating these biomarkers may improve early diagnosis and risk assessment and guide interventions aimed at delaying or preventing disease onset. Finally, we discuss emerging prevention-oriented clinical trials, the potential and limitations of artificial intelligence-based prediction, and the ethical implications of moving neurological care from reactive management to predictive and preventive medicine.

articles.title: Small but still important: spatio-temporal variability of the hydrochemistry of lowland spring waters and its landscape dependence in central Poland.
articles.abstract: The current study aimed to identify the general spatio-temporal variability pattern of the hydrochemical properties of spring waters in the Mazovian Lowland, central Poland, and to evaluate its associations with the land cover of the spring proximity zones. Water samples were collected three times from November 2024 to May 2025 across 35 perennial, valley, or hillslope type springs, draining Quaternary porous aquifers; the chemical analysis included selected macro- and microelements, determined using IC and ICP-MS techniques. The studied springs were characterized by low discharge, belonging from VIII to V Meinzer classes (from 0.2 to 77.8 L/min). Their waters were usually slightly alkaline, with TDS ranging from 64 to 2055 mg/L, and represented various hydrochemical water types, from the most common HCO3-Ca to even five ionic types such as HCO3-SO4-NO3-Ca-Mg and Cl-SO4-HCO3-Ca-Na. The chemical composition, as captured and indicated by descriptive statistics, molar ratios, and PCA, reflected both geogenic and anthropogenic influences. Spring water in urbanized areas experienced high concentrations of Cl-, SO42-, Na+, and K+, which could be explained by multidimensional human pressure across cities, while significant NO3- contamination was revealed in springs across the agricultural landscape, originating from intensive fertilizer applications. The correlation analysis suggested that the land cover of the spring proximity zone could partially explain its water chemical composition; road length, building area, and the contribution of total artificial areas had a significant, statistical effect on numerous macro- and microelement concentrations. Cultivated lands were associated mainly with NO3- concentrations, whereas forest cover contribution was negatively correlated with lower concentration values. Overall, the spring proximity zone of 500 m radius provided the best correlation for artificial areas, agricultural lands, and forests, while road length and building area appeared to be the most significant in the 100 and 250 m radius zone. The results provide a comprehensive insight into spring water chemistry across lowland, post-glacial areas, crucial in terms of the effective management of groundwater, its protection, as well as future investigations.

articles.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is the leading cause of cancer-related death in neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), with a lifetime risk of 8-15% and five-year survival below 50% in most series. Imaging surveillance, most often whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WB-MRI), is offered on the premise that earlier detection of premalignant or early malignant lesions permits curative resection, but the supporting evidence has not been formally synthesized. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane CENTRAL, trial registries, and conference proceedings from 2000 to July 2026 for studies of structured surveillance or lesion characterization in people with NF1. Two reviewers screened and extracted data independently, risk of bias was assessed with design-specific tools, and certainty was graded with GRADE. Sixteen records were included: six surveillance-impact or natural-history cohorts, five imaging diagnostic-accuracy studies, two investigational cell-free DNA studies, and three contextual records (a guideline, a prognostic meta-analysis, and a registered protocol). Because the data were few and heterogeneous, no meta-analysis was possible and the primary objectives could not be addressed quantitatively. The only comparative incidence estimate came from one retrospective cohort compared with expected population-based rates. One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.

articles.title: A Scoping Review on Large Language Model Clinical Decision Support in Acute and Critical Care.
articles.abstract: Decision-making in acute and critical care relies on interpretation of heterogeneous information sources under substantial time pressure. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to aid in triage, diagnosis generation, and treatment planning. This scoping review maps the current landscape of LLM-based CDSS in acute and critical care and assesses their readiness for clinical implementation. A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of four databases (January 2026) yielded 62 studies, including 15 medical domain-adapted LLMs. Technology Readiness Levels were assigned across all 62 studies; none has progressed to clinical deployment. Within the medical LLM subgroup, medical LLMs generally outperformed their foundation model counterparts, although the evidence was heterogeneous. An exploratory PROBAST + AI-informed appraisal identified recurring methodological concerns, and thematic synthesis of implementation determinants identified regulatory constraints, workflow integration, and insufficient understanding of human-AI interaction as key barriers. This review highlights priorities for prospective validation using real-world institutional data.

articles.title: Absence of changes in experimental pain indices after transcranial electrical stimulation in chronic pain patients.
articles.abstract: Previous research has supported the analgesic effect of transcranial Electrical Stimulation (tES) in diverse chronic pain populations. The effect is thought to be due to functional changes in brain mechanisms related to pain modulation after the intervention. However, although the changes should be reflected in Quantitative Sensory Testing (QST) indices of pain perception and modulation, this has not been systematically investigated. As a response to this research gap, we attempted to explore whether tES affects pro- and/or anti-nociceptive mechanisms, assessed by QST. We carried out a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trial (RCT) to analyse the effect of home-based tES- using both direct current (tDCS) targeting M1 and alternate current (tACS) targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex - on QST indices such as pressure and heat pain thresholds, conditioned pain modulation and temporal summation of second pain. We undertook the trial in a sample of 120 patients with chronic pain and analysed both the short-term (post-treatment) and long-term (6 months) effects of the tES interventions. Classical and Bayesian repeated measures ANOVA analyses did not reveal any significant effect of tES interventions on the QST indices at any of the time points. Our findings do not allow us to assert that the analgesic effectiveness of tES in chronic pain is due to effects on pain modulation mechanisms (either pronociceptive or antinociceptive). Future research should assess whether the QST indices are sensitive enough to detect changes after tES and clarify the mechanisms by which tES alleviates clinical pain.

articles.title: Immunoblot analysis as a helpful adjunct to determine the time of a CMV infection in pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To evaluate the utility of immunoblot analysis for determining the timing of maternal CMV infection in pregnancy.

METHODS: Retrospective study including 151 pregnant women referred for suspected primary CMV infection or unclear serological results at the University Hospital Tübingen between July 2023 and November 2025. CMV-specific IgG, IgM, and IgG avidity were measured using standard chemiluminescence immunoassays (CLIA), and corresponding CMV immunoblot assays were performed. Associations between immunoblot band reactivity and CLIA IgG avidity, used as the reference test, were analyzed by Firth's penalized logistic regression. Detection and false-positive rates for identifying low IgG avidity (< 15%) were calculated for individual bands and their combinations.

RESULTS: With increasing IgG avidity, the probability of a positive reaction decreased for the IgM IE1 and p150 bands, the IgG IE1, CM2, and p65 bands, and the IgG avidity IE1 band, and increased for the IgG gB1 and gB2 bands and the IgG avidity p150 and gB2 bands. Among cases with low IgG avidity (< 15%; n = 56), absence of the IgG avidity gB2 band achieved the highest detection rate (92.9%) but at a false-positive rate of 54.7%. The lowest false-positive rate (1.1%) was observed when both the IgG gB1 and IgG avidity p150 bands were absent, at a detection rate of 23.2%. The presence of IgM IE1 or the absence of IgG gB1 detected 58.9% of low-avidity cases at a false-positive rate of 10.5%.

CONCLUSION: Immunoblot band patterns are systematically associated with CLIA IgG avidity and may serve as a helpful adjunct in determining the timing of a CMV infection in pregnancy.

articles.title: Advanced Heart Failure Therapies in Patients with Cancer or Cancer History: Review and Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes current literature on advanced HF therapies including LVAD and HT in patients with cancer or cancer history, outlining pathophysiology, evolving epidemiology, and management in the contemporary era.

RECENT FINDINGS: Cancer survivors and HF patients are a growing population. Outcomes in LVAD patients with a history of malignancy show mildly reduced survival, increased GI bleeding, though similar rates of other adverse outcomes to non-cancer survivors. Malignancy risk in HT is multifactorial with contributions from age, immunosuppression, and history of PTM. For management of post-HT malignancies, strategies including immunosuppression reduction and mTOR inhibitors may improve outcomes. Cancer and cancer history play a significant role in the evaluation and management of patients undergoing LVAD or HT. Multidisciplinary evaluation including oncology, advanced HF, and cardio-oncology is essential for ideal candidate selection and nuances of management thereafter. Future studies are needed to better understand pathophysiology and management of advanced HF therapies in this population.

articles.title: Evolution of bilirubin detection: analytical strategies, sensing platforms, and translational opportunities.
articles.abstract: Liver diseases, including fatty liver disease, viral hepatitis, cirrhosis, and cholestatic disorders, leading to hyperbilirubinemia contribute substantially to the global burden of morbidity and mortality. It is also a major clinical concern in neonates, with neonatal jaundice occurring in approximately 60% of term and 80% of preterm newborns during the first week after birth. Over the past decades, bilirubin detection has evolved from conventional laboratory-based methods to advanced sensing technologies designed for rapid, sensitive, and decentralized analysis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution of bilirubin sensing, with emphasis on well-established electrochemical and optical sensing to integrated paper-based, smartphone-assisted, and wearable sensor technologies. Recent advances in functional materials, miniaturized sensors, digital analysis, and integrated sensing platforms have expanded the potential for portable bilirubin testing across diverse diagnostic and monitoring settings. These advances hold promise for applications in point-of-care (POC) testing, resource-limited settings, and neonatal care units, where timely and accessible bilirubin assessment is essential for informed clinical decision-making. Established bilirubin-sensing techniques and emerging technologies are critically evaluated to highlight novel approaches, compare analytical performance, and assess translational potential. Alternative sample matrices, which offer considerable potential for diverse applications, are also evaluated to distinguish exploratory demonstrations from clinically validated applications. Furthermore, matrix effects, sensor drift, storage stability, reproducibility, and variations across devices and fabrication batches are critically examined in relation to their implications for measurement reliability and clinical applicability. By integrating advances in sensing mechanisms, functional materials, and device architectures, the discussion provides a foundation for understanding bilirubin-sensing principles, critically evaluating reported approaches, and addressing existing challenges, while offering insights into sensor design and technology selection and identifying key priorities for developing reliable, accessible, and clinically translatable bilirubin-sensing platforms.

articles.title: Evaluation of pulpal blood flow and postoperative pain after direct pulp capping with different materials in teeth with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare postoperative pulpal perfusion and postoperative pain following direct pulp capping (DPC) with calcium hydroxide (CH; Dycal), mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA), and Biodentine in teeth diagnosed with symptomatic irreversible pulpitis (SIP), using laser Doppler flowmetry (LDF).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty-seven mandibular molars from 39 patients were randomly allocated to receive DPC with Dycal (n = 15), MTA (n = 16), or Biodentine (n = 16). Following carious pulp exposure, the exposed pulp was disinfected using a sterile cotton pellet moistened with 2.5% NaOCl, without pulp tissue amputation. Hemostasis was achieved by gentle pressure with saline-moistened sterile cotton pellets for up to 10 min; teeth in which hemostasis could not be achieved within this period were excluded. Postoperative pain was assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), and pulpal perfusion was measured using LDF at baseline and during postoperative follow-up. Three teeth requiring root canal treatment due to severe postoperative pain were excluded from the longitudinal analyses, leaving 44 teeth for analysis.

RESULTS: Pulpal perfusion did not differ significantly among Dycal, MTA, and Biodentine at any assessment time point (p > 0.05). Pulpal perfusion showed no significant change over time following Dycal or MTA treatment (p > 0.05), whereas pulpal perfusion in the Biodentine was higher at 1 month than at baseline (p < 0.05), with no significant difference between 1 week and 1 month (p > 0.05). The material × time interaction was not significant, and changes in pulpal perfusion from baseline (ΔPU) did not differ significantly among the materials (p > 0.05). Postoperative pain decreased over time with all three materials, with no significant differences among the materials at any assessment time point (p > 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Dycal, MTA, and Biodentine showed comparable early pulpal perfusion and postoperative pain outcomes following DPC in teeth with SIP. At 1 month, pulpal perfusion was significantly higher than baseline in teeth treated with Biodentine, whereas no significant changes were observed in teeth treated with Dycal or MTA.

articles.title: T​he use of biosynthetic mesh in complex abdominal wall reconstruction - a single‑center experience.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Abdominal wall reconstruction in patients presenting with enteric fistulas and mesh infection is challenging. Synthetic mesh should be avoided in contaminated fields and to be used in selected cases. Alternative strategies include primary fascial closure with or without component separation, biologic mesh, and resorbable biosynthetic mesh. Our study aims to evaluate the use of long-term absorbable mesh in a single-stage procedure, focusing on postoperative complications and hernia recurrence rates.

METHODS: A retrospective single-arm study was conducted following Institutional Review Board approval. All incisional hernia repairs using bio-absorbable Poly-4-Hydroxybutyrate mesh were performed at our medical center between January 2017 and March 2025 were included. Adult and pediatric patients with Ventral Hernia Working Group (VHWG) grade III and IV wounds were eligible.

RESULTS: Thirty-four patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 58.7 ± 17.1 years, and the mean body mass index was 30.4 ± 7.6 kg/m². Comorbidity burden was high: 52.9% had a Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and 35.3% had an ASA score ≥ 3. Most patients (82.3%) presented with infected mesh. Mean operative time was 188.5 ± 75 min, and bowel resection was required in 18 cases. Postoperative wound infection occurred in 10 patients. Follow‑up data were available for 28 of the 34 patients with median follow-up duration of 20.5 months. A single death occurred, hernia recurrence was observed in four cases (16%), all managed with reoperation. Quality-of-life assessments demonstrated a clear postoperative improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: In this high-risk, contaminated and infected cohort, P4HB mesh demonstrated acceptable recurrence and complication rates. Its long-term resorbable properties provides a feasible alternative to use in incisional hernia repair with infected meshes.

articles.title: Can we trust a positive PSMA PET/CT before the Phoenix threshold? Positive predictive value after primary radiotherapy for prostate cancer. A retrospective cohort study.
authors: van der Voort van Zyp JRN
articles.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT is increasingly used after radiotherapy, even before the Phoenix threshold. We assessed the positive predictive value (PPV) of PET-positive findings in this setting.

METHODS: Patients restaged with PSMA PET/CT after primary radiotherapy were classified as Phoenix-negative (PSA rise < 2.0 ng/mL above nadir) or Phoenix-positive. Local findings were verified by histopathology or MRI, metastases by histopathology or follow-up imaging. A sensitivity analysis was restricted to histopathology only. PPV was compared between Phoenix groups.

RESULTS: Of 833 patients, 724 were PET-positive; 263 local recurrences and 219 metastatic findings had a reference standard. PPV was 83.7% for local recurrence and 95.0% for metastases. Local PPV was lower in Phoenix-negative than Phoenix-positive patients (77.7% vs. 88.1%, p = 0.029), but not with histopathological verification (84.1% vs. 86.9%); metastatic PPV did not differ between groups (96.3% vs. 94.2%).

CONCLUSION: Restaging PSMA PET/CT reliably identifies recurrence after radiotherapy, even before the Phoenix threshold is met.

articles.title: Rectus diastasis repair: a systematic review and metanalysis of contemporary suture techniques and materials.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Surgical treatment of rectus diastasis (RD) is a safe and effective option to address abdominal contour and improve core strength. Given advances in techniques and materials, this review aims to provide an updated report on the current use and outcomes of different suture materials and plication techniques in patients undergoing surgical treatment of RD.

METHODS: The PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were systematically searched in February 2025. Only data from patients undergoing RD repair with traditional suture or suturable mesh (Duramesh, Mesh Suture Inc., Chicago, IL) were included, excluding any planar mesh-based repairs. A pooled analysis of complication and recurrence rates was conducted to compare outcomes.

RESULTS: 50 studies involving 2,965 patients were included in analysis. Seroma rate was lower in open repairs, while rates of unfavorable scarring were lower in endoscopic repairs. Repairs done in multiple layers, had lower overall complication rates, reaching significance in skin dehiscence/necrosis, unfavorable scarring, and revision, while single layer repairs had shorter average operative times. There was no difference in complication rates between suture filament types or RD recurrence rates between absorbable versus nonabsorbable suture, interrupted versus continuous repair, varying layers, or different calibers. Recurrence rates were higher barbed suture repairs compared to other suture types.

CONCLUSION: Across 50 studies, RD suture repair was shown to be safe and effective. Taken together, evidence supports the use of single- or double-layer repairs performed with interrupted or continuous technique, using sutures of 2-0 caliber or larger, or suturable mesh to obtain durable repairs.

articles.title: Analysis of outcomes across mesh placement planes in lateral abdominal wall hernia repair: a SWiM systematic review.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines do not specify a preferred anatomical mesh plane for lateral abdominal wall hernia repair. This systematic review evaluated clinical outcomes across various mesh placement planes, focusing on 30-day postoperative complications and recurrence.

METHODS: Adhering to PRISMA and SWiM guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261379781), PubMed, Web of Science, and Ovid were searched for clinical studies (n ≥ 5) published between January 2015 and April 2026. Outcomes were categorized by anatomical plane (ICAP classification) and synthesized using vote-counting against established benchmarks: SSO/seroma/hematoma/SSI rate ≤ 10%, and recurrence rate ≤ 5%.

RESULTS: A total of 41 studies (4 comparative cohorts, 37 case series) were included. The preperitoneal plane yielded a 73.7% (14/19) of studies achieving complication rates ≤ 10%, and 100% (11/11) maintaining recurrence rates ≤ 5%, though these cohorts predominantly comprised primary hernias. The retromuscular plane demonstrated excellent long-term recurrence control (91.7%; 11/12 below threshold), though with high wound morbidity (40%; 6/15 above threshold) reflecting a high proportion of complex repairs. Intraperitoneal repairs showed high variability across techniques, though partial extraperitoneal variants showed promise. Conversely, the single onlay study reported elevated recurrence (8.7%), and the interoblique plane showed unfavorable complication (75%; 3/4) and recurrence rates (50%; 1/2).

CONCLUSION: Mesh plane choice impacts 30-day complications and recurrence in lateral hernia repair. The optimal plane remains unestablished due to substantial variations in case complexity, operative technique, and follow-up across predominantly Level 4 evidence, highlighting the need for high-quality prospective comparative trials.

articles.title: Surgical versus conservative management of acute subdural hematoma in elderly patients: a systematic review of functional outcomes and prognostic factors.
articles.abstract: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off. Evidence to date suggests the elderly see disproportionately high morbidity and mortality regardless of surgical or conservative management. To systematically review the evidence comparing surgical evacuation versus conservative management of ASDH in elderly patients and assess the impact of patient factors on outcomes, a systematic review was conducted examining six observational studies (n = 812) comparing surgical and conservative management of traumatic ASDH in patients aged 60 or older. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 6-month mortality, and functional outcomes. MEDLINE, Embase and CINAHL were searched up to December 2025. Risk of bias assessment was performed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale. Results were presented descriptively and synthesized narratively by outcome timepoint as clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Surgery was not consistently associated with improved mortality nor improved functional outcomes. Surgical patients presented with worse clinical and radiological severity. In-hospital mortality analysis of three cohorts demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with relative risks ranging from 1.37 to 13.63, favoring conservative management. Six-month mortality showed even greater heterogeneity with directionally inconsistent findings. Functional outcomes, when reported, either favored conservative management or were neutral. Current evidence does not establish a consistent mortality or functional advantage for surgical evacuation of ASDH in elderly patients. Patients with poor neurological status demonstrate high mortality regardless of intervention, while those with mild neurological impairment may not derive meaningful benefit from surgery. Future prospective studies should standardize frailty assessment alongside clinical and radiographic parameters to identify where true clinical equipoise exists and establish guidelines in this distinct patient population. No funding was received for this review.

articles.title: Molecular chaperones involved in the radiobiological response of established triple-negative breast cancer cell lines: a pilot study.
articles.abstract: Radiation therapy (RT) represents a key component of the multimodal treatment of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), however, radioresistance remains a significant clinical challenge often driven by dysregulated stress-response and survival signaling pathways. Because the efficacy of RT is strongly dependent on the intrinsic biological features of distinct tumor subtypes, including TNBC, the investigation of the molecular determinants of radiosensitivity is crucial to develop biology-driven personalized RT protocols. In this study, the radiobiological response of three established TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231, SUM-159, and BT-549) exposed to increasing X-ray doses (1-5 Gy) was evaluated. Radiation survival curves were analyzed using the linear-quadratic (LQ) model to estimate the intrinsic α and β radiosensitivity parameters. To investigate stress-mediated molecular mechanisms underlying radioresistence, cellular responses to 5 Gy radiation were analyzed by assessing heat shock protein expression Hsp27, Hsp60, and Hsp90- via Western blot and Immunofluorescence. Furthermore, downstream alterations in key oncogenic and DNA damage response pathways including p53, Akt, 53BP1, survivin, and JNK, were characterized across all models. We observed variability in the expression profiles of the target proteins among the three TNBC cell lines, potentially reflecting differences in their estimated radiobiological features.We predict that appropriately validated, biomarker-directed therapies are more likely to be successfully integrated into precision medicine strategies for hard-to-treat tumors.

articles.title: Doing more for less: declining surgeon reimbursement for ventral hernia repair despite stable operative time and rising technical complexity.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: On January 1, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services implemented a 2.5% efficiency adjustment that reduced work relative value units for ventral hernia repair. This change rests on the premise that the Relative Value Scale Update Committee overestimates operative times and that surgical efficiency has improved. We evaluated national trends in operative time and hernia complexity to determine whether contemporary practice supports these assumptions.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of all ventral hernia repairs entered in the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative between 2018 and 2023. Operative times were stratified into five categories (0-59, 60-119, 120-179, 180-239, and ≥ 240 min) and examined by hernia width (< 3 cm, 3-10 cm, > 10 cm) and operative approach. Temporal trends were assessed with descriptive statistics, crosstabulations, and nonparametric tests.

RESULTS: Of 35,996 operations, 18,453 (51.2%) were < 3 cm in width, 11,669 (32.4%) were 3-10 cm, and 5,874 (16.3%) were > 10 cm. The proportion of larger defects increased over the study period. Among < 3 cm hernias, the share of operations lasting 60-239 min rose while those lasting < 60 min declined (p = 0.01). Among 3-10 cm hernias, operations ≥ 240 min increased from 13.9% to 16.7% (p < 0.001). Operative-time distributions for > 10 cm hernias remained stable (p = 0.21). Robotic repairs increased significantly while open and laparoscopic approaches declined.

CONCLUSION: Ventral hernia repairs have grown more complex, with larger sizes and longer operative times for small- and medium-sized defects. These findings do not support the efficiency gains assumed by CMS and underscore a mismatch between surgical workload and reimbursement.

articles.title: DANTE T1-SPACE MR imaging for visualization of inferior and superior petrosal sinus anatomy in cavernous sinus DAVF.
articles.abstract: DANTE (Delay Alternating with Nutation for Tailored Excitation) is useful for investigating venous sinus conditions, including thrombosis, hypoplasia, and occlusions. The study aimed to assess the efficacy of the DANTE MRI sequence in visualizing the inferior petrosal sinus (IPS) and superior petrosal sinus (SPS) in patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). DANTE preparation provides robust suppression of flowing blood signal while preserving stationary tissue signal, which may improve delineation of venous sinus lumen and wall changes compared with conventional 3D TSE sequences. Fourteen patients with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas were retrospectively analyzed. All patients underwent contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE MRI prior to endovascular treatment. IPS patency was independently evaluated on MRI and descriptively compared with digital subtraction angiography. Nine out of fourteen patients demonstrated occlusion of the ipsilateral IPS. Two had stenotic changes in the IPS. The IPS was identified in all patients, regardless of patency, and transvenous embolization was successfully performed via the IPS in all treated cases. In the SPS, lumen continuity between SPS and Cavernous sinus was confirmed in 5 cases. 78.5% of patients achieved occlusion immediately after treatment, with the remaining patients occluded during follow-up. Contrast-enhanced DANTE T1-SPACE offers high-contrast depiction of IPS/SPS by effective blood-signal suppression with preservation of static tissue signal, facilitating preprocedural anatomical clarification in CSDAVF. This information may be particularly useful in cases with suspected IPS occlusion, where preprocedural anatomical clarification is clinically relevant.

articles.title: Genetic diversity of black queen cell virus in Italian honeybees (Apis mellifera ligustica) of Southern Taiwan.
articles.abstract: The black queen cell virus (BQCV) is an infectious disease agent causing high mortality among queen larvae and prepupae, which develop cell walls that are pale yellow, dark brown, or black. BQCV infection significantly affects apicultural productivity, leading to substantial economic losses and food insecurity. In this study, we detected BQCV in Italian honeybees (Apis mellifera ligustica) in Pingtung, Taiwan. Five pupae or adult honeybees from seven farm sites were pooled to extract RNA and test for BQCV. Two out of five (2/5) pupae and six out of seven (6/7) adult honeybee samples were BQCV-positive. Genomic sequencing of the partial capsid gene revealed Taiwan BQCV strains and a BQCV clade with European strains and Asian strains. The genetic homogeneity and diversity of the BQCV circulating in Taiwan highlight the importance of continuous surveillance to monitor viral evolution, assess potential risks to honeybee populations, and develop an effective management strategy to safeguard the apiculture industry and food security.

articles.title: Taxifolin Inhibits Biofilm Formation in Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and is Associated with Suppression of the MrkH-Regulated Type 3 Fimbrial Gene Set.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a major threat to hospital infection control, and biofilm formation contributes to persistent colonisation, antimicrobial tolerance and protracted infection. Type 3 fimbriae are the key adhesive structures for K. pneumoniae biofilm formation, and their expression is controlled by the cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP)-dependent transcriptional activator MrkH. This study examined the effect of the natural dihydroflavonol taxifolin on CRKP biofilm and its possible mechanism. Taxifolin was added at inoculation and remained present throughout biofilm development, so all assays address inhibition of biofilm formation rather than eradication of preformed biofilm. Crystal violet staining showed that biofilm biomass fell to 63.0 ± 13.0% and 28.0 ± 6.0% of the control after treatment with low and high subinhibitory concentrations of taxifolin. Confocal microscopy with SYTO 9 and concanavalin A (ConA) double staining showed corresponding falls to 63.8 ± 8.3% and 30.7 ± 8.2% for the biofilm cell signal (SYTO 9), and to 54.9 ± 6.7% and 24.6 ± 9.4% for the EPS polysaccharide signal (ConA). Viable counts within the biofilm decreased from 7.75 ± 0.04 to 7.47 ± 0.09 and 6.98 ± 0.12 log10 CFU/mL, and metabolic activity measured by the XTT assay was also significantly reduced. Quantitative reverse transcription PCR showed significant downregulation of mrkH and its downstream genes mrkA and mrkD, and dose-dependent downregulation of the type 1 fimbrial adhesin gene fimH. Molecular docking indicated that taxifolin can enter the c-di-GMP binding pocket of MrkH, forming hydrogen bonds, a cation-π interaction and π-π stacking. These results indicate that subinhibitory taxifolin inhibits biofilm formation in this CRKP strain and is associated with suppression of the MrkH-regulated gene set, whereas direct target engagement of MrkH remains unproven.

articles.title: Late-onset RANBP2-associated acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE1): a familial case series and a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Acute Necrotizing Encephalopathy (ANE) is a rare para-infectious encephalopathy typically affecting young children, characterized by symmetric bilateral thalamic lesions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Adolescent- or adult-onset remains exceptional. Familial or recurrent forms are associated with heterozygous RAN-binding protein 2 (RANBP2) variants and classified as ANE type 1 (ANE1). We describe two siblings with late-onset ANE1 from an Italian family and systematically reviewed the demographic and genetic spectrum of RANBP2-associated disease. The proband, a 20-year-old woman, presented with a mild post-infectious encephalopathy and bilateral thalamic lesions, with good recovery after immunomodulatory therapy. Her brother developed a fulminant post-febrile encephalopathy at age 15, progressing to coma, with bilateral thalamic, pontine, and external capsule involvement on MRI, and persistent sequelae. Whole-exome sequencing in the proband identified the heterozygous RANBP2 variant c.1754C > T (p.Thr585Met), confirmed by Sanger sequencing in her brother, enabling a retrospective diagnosis. Their father and another brother were asymptomatic carriers, supporting incomplete penetrance. The systematic review identified 53 reports (138 affected individuals from 85 case/family-units). Among 130 individuals with available data, 57 had recurrences. Age at onset was available for 84 patients, six presented at 12 years or older, and four in adulthood. The p.Thr585Met variant accounted for 60% of family-units and 65% of affected individuals. These findings expand the age and phenotypic spectrum of RANBP2-associated ANE and demonstrate intrafamilial variability. To our knowledge, this is the third Italian family reported, and the first with late-onset presentations. Our findings support considering RANBP2 testing beyond childhood and prompt immunomodulatory treatment in suspected cases.

articles.title: Manganese dioxide-gold nanoparticle synergistic platform for sensitive colorimetric detection of creatinine in clinical samples.
articles.abstract: A dual-nanoparticle cascade platform is reported that resolves these limitations by architecturally decoupling chemical recognition from optical transduction, thereby achieving both high selectivity and intrinsic matrix tolerance in a single colorimetric format. The platform couples δ-MnO2 nanosheets, acting as a surface-selective nanozyme, with citrate-stabilised gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as the plasmonic transducer. In the first step, creatinine undergoes a two-electron oxidation at the surface MnIV sites of δ-MnO2 nanosheets, yielding N-methylhydantoin with stoichiometric release of Mn2+ (1:1 molar ratio confirmed by LC-MS/MS and ICP-MS). The liberated Mn2+ ions subsequently displace the citrate stabilising layer of the AuNPs and compress their electrical double layer, triggering irreversible colloidal aggregation and a near-infrared shift of the localised surface plasmon resonance from 522 nm to 700 nm. This 700 nm detection window lies entirely beyond the absorption bands of the major serum chromophores, oxyhaemoglobin (415, 541, 577 nm) and bilirubin (450 nm), providing intrinsic spectral immunity to haemolytic and icteric interference without any sample pre-treatment. Under optimised conditions (MES buffer, pH 6.5; 60 °C, 10 min), the assay exhibits linearity over 26-535 µM (R2 = 0.9915), a limit of detection of 8.58 µM, and intra- and inter-assay precision of 1.9-7.4% and 2.1-8.1% RSD, respectively, with mean spike recovery of 99.4-103.6% in matrix-matched pooled human serum. The selectivity against twenty-six endogenous and exogenous interferents, including the four major serum proteins (albumin, IgG, transferrin, fibrinogen), five clinically relevant antibiotic classes (cephalosporin, penicillin, aminoglycoside, fluoroquinolone, glycopeptide), and structural analogues such as creatine, was quantified; only L-cysteine and dopamine produced deviations exceeding 10%, both of which were fully suppressed by N-ethylmaleimide pre-treatment without affecting creatinine recovery. Prospective evaluation against 120 clinical serum specimens, spanning healthy controls (n = 20), CKD stages 1-2 (n = 25), CKD stage 3 (n = 25), CKD stages 4-5 (n = 25), acute kidney injury (n = 15), and hemolytic/icteric samples (n = 10) which demonstrated excellent agreement with the enzymatic reference analyser (Pearson r = 0.997; Passing-Bablok slope = 1.024, intercept = - 3.5 µM; 94.2% of data points within Bland-Altman ± 1.96 SD limits of agreement). Subgroup-stratified recovery analysis showed no significant inter-subgroup differences (F5,114 = 0.83, p = 0.53), and CKD staging concordance with the enzymatic reference reached 100% across all 95 CKD/AKI specimens. Six independent sensor preparations synthesised on different days yielded an inter-batch calibration-slope RSD of 2.5%, with no statistically significant inter-batch differences (one-way ANOVA, F5,24 = 1.96, p = 0.12); a 180-day storage-stability study supported an in-use shelf-life of 120 days at 4 °C with full spike-recovery retention (95-105% throughout); and 50 consecutive measurements in a single working day yielded 1.7% within-run RSD with no detectable drift. Requiring only 5 µL of serum, yielding results within 10 min, and costing less than $0.08 per test, this nanozyme-plasmonic architecture offers a robust, low-cost, and interference-resistant alternative to conventional creatinine assays in central and decentralised clinical laboratories. While the present implementation requires a 60 °C heating block and a spectrophotometric reader and therefore does not yet satisfy all WHO ASSURED criteria for fully equipment-free point-of-care use, the underlying chemistry, low reagent cost and minimal sample volume make it an attractive candidate for subsequent translation to lyophilised reagent strips with smartphone-based readout.

articles.title: The role of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation in cardiac fibrotic remodeling.
articles.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is being investigated as a non-invasive approach to cardiac fibrotic remodeling. This narrative review examines auricular afferent pathways, systemic responses and their duration, myocardial collagen in animal models, and human cardiovascular observations. Tracing and nerve-interruption experiments in cats and rodents identify vagal and non-vagal sensory pathways. Human brain imaging, muscle sympathetic recordings, and heart-rate variability measure different responses without identifying the initiating auricular afferent. Plasma obtained from healthy volunteers after tragus stimulation reduced acute ischemia-reperfusion injury in recipient isolated rat hearts; pharmacological and spleen-status comparisons supported cholinergic and splenic involvement. Canine post-infarction studies and rodent models of hypertensive or cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction report lower terminal myocardial collagen. In some rodent experiments, α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor antagonism attenuated the tissue response, and comparable blood-pressure lowering did not reproduce it. These findings implicate mechanisms beyond unloading, but the reviewed studies have not demonstrated regression of fibrosis documented before treatment. Human trials report changes in acute injury, longitudinal strain, inflammation or arrhythmia alongside neutral controlled outcomes; none of the trials reviewed measured myocardial fibrosis. Further studies should connect cellular mechanisms to regional collagen measurements and assess serial fibrosis-sensitive imaging alongside function, treatment exposure and safety. taVNS may limit cardiac fibrotic remodeling, but its antifibrotic efficacy in humans remains unproven.

articles.title: Association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis: a single-center retrospective observational study.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS), a type 2-dominant form of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, is characterized by frequent postoperative relapse. Although statins exhibit pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and profibrinolytic properties that may mitigate impaired fibrinolysis in ECRS, their clinical impact remains unclear. This study evaluated the association between statin use and postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS undergoing functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS).

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, observational study included patients diagnosed with ECRS according to the Japanese Epidemiological Survey of Refractory Eosinophilic Chronic Rhinosinusitis criteria who underwent FESS between April 2015 and December 2025. Postoperative recurrence was defined as the need for any of the following treatment escalations: revision surgery, systemic oral corticosteroid therapy, local triamcinolone administration, or use of (or eligibility for) biologic therapy.

RESULTS: Forty-nine patients completed at least 6 months of follow-up, including 11 statin users (22.4%). Statin users were significantly older than non-users (60.9 vs. 52.3 years; p=0.033), whereas other baseline characteristics were comparable. Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence (27.3% vs. 63.2%; OR 0.22; 95% CI 0.05-0.96; p=0.046). In exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age and asthma, the association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.06-1.32; p=0.115).

CONCLUSION: Statin use was associated with lower odds of overall postoperative recurrence in patients with ECRS. However, this association was attenuated after adjustment for age and asthma and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Pretreatment total gross tumor volume complements TNM staging in predicting survival in locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic significance of pretreatment gross tumor volume (GTV) and determine whether volumetric assessment provides additional prognostic value beyond conventional TNM staging in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 124 patients treated with definitive radiotherapy between 2012 and 2024; 117 received concurrent systemic therapy. Pretreatment GTVprimary, GTVnodal, and GTVtotal were measured on planning CT for patients treated with upfront radiotherapy and on the CT component of pre-induction PET/CT for patients receiving induction chemotherapy. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to determine cutoff values. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. The incremental prognostic value of volumetric parameters was assessed using Akaike's Information Criterion (AIC)-based model comparison.

RESULTS: The selected cutoff value for GTVtotal was 36 cc. Although GTVprimary showed the highest AUC in ROC analysis, GTVtotal remained associated with disease-specific survival after multivariable adjustment and yielded the lowest AIC among the compared models. Patients with GTVtotal > 36 cc had poorer disease-specific survival. GTVtotal, T stage, and age > 60 years were independently associated with disease-specific survival.

CONCLUSION: Pretreatment GTVtotal provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional TNM staging and may improve risk stratification in patients with locally advanced laryngeal and hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma treated with definitive radiotherapy, predominantly with concurrent systemic therapy. The data-derived cutoff requires external validation before clinical use. The 36-cc threshold may be influenced by the predominance of hypopharyngeal tumors in the high-volume group and should be applied cautiously to laryngeal cancer cohorts.

articles.title: Patient Versus Provider Priorities in Stress Urinary Incontinence Surgery: A Cross-Sectional Ranking Survey.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Informed consent for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) surgery requires clinicians to understand patient priorities. We hypothesized that clinically meaningful divergences would exist between patient and provider priorities, alongside specific points of agreement.

METHODS: Through two parallel cross-sectional surveys, we enrolled: (1) female patients with bothersome SUI at a single tertiary center; (2) members of the Canadian Society for Pelvic Medicine. Participants were asked to rank 16 surgical outcomes and complications. We generated consensus rankings using Borda Count analysis (N-1 scoring) and compared them between groups using Spearman's rank correlation and Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: We obtained complete rankings from 25/34 patients (73.5%) and 28/40 providers (70.0%). Consensus hierarchies showed a moderate, significant correlation (rho = 0.543, p = 0.03). Divergences were bidirectional. Patients prioritized acute procedure-related injury to bladder, bowel, and nerves as top three. Providers agreed with bowel and nerve injury in top three but prioritized prolonged pain in second place. The largest divergence was for bladder infection, which was ranked significantly higher by patients than providers. Both groups ranked logistical factors, such as delay in return to daily activities, among the lowest. Minimum persistent pain difference influencing procedure preference did not differ, with approximately half of patients and providers expressing that 10% difference in pain outcomes would influence their choice (p = 0.318).

CONCLUSIONS: Patient and provider priorities are moderately aligned in SUI surgical informed consent discussions. Counseling could contextualize the risks patients may overestimate, validate common complications they fear, and proactively raise the long-term outcomes they may omit to appreciate.

articles.title: Outpatient Referral After Adolescent Sexual Health Emergency Department Visits Improves Follow-Up.
articles.journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate which methods of outpatient referral during pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for sexual health are associated with increased follow-up among adolescents otherwise at risk of being lost to care.

METHODS: A single-institution retrospective cohort study was conducted among patients 14-20 years-old who underwent testing for any sexually transmitted infection during ED visits between 1/1/2018 and 12/31/2018 and were discharged home, excluding pregnant patients or those presenting following sexual assault. The primary outcome was any follow-up within 6 months of the index ED visit. The primary independent variable was referral at discharge. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to assess associations.

RESULTS: Among 1,152 patients (median age 17 years; 76% female), 73% received a referral, and 36.5% were seen in follow-up within 6 months of the index visit. Referrals specifying time frame for follow-up were associated with increased follow-up (odds ratio [OR] 5.9, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.2-8.4), whereas "as needed" referrals were not. In multivariable modeling, attending a follow-up visit was associated with referral (adjusted OR [AOR] 3.6, 95% CI 2.5-5.2), female sex (2.74, 95% CI: 1.90-3.95), and prior preventive care (4.42, 95% CI: 3.36-5.81). Although associated with having follow-up visits, referrals were not associated with contraception initiation or decreased return to the ED within 6 months of the index visit.

DISCUSSION: Referral to outpatient care was associated with increased follow-up among adolescents with sexual health needs, particularly when referrals specified a follow-up time frame. Pediatric EDs should standardize discharge processes to include specific and consistent outpatient referrals.

articles.title: ALCAPA: Use and Necessity of Different Surgical Techniques.
articles.abstract: Anomalous left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) is a rare congenital heart disease in which the origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery leads to myocardial ischemia. Although most patients present in infancy, rare cases are diagnosed in adulthood. Coronary reimplantation remains the gold standard intervention. However, there is no consensus on the preferred secondary procedure if direct reimplantation is not possible. We present a 3-patient case series of adults with ALCAPA undergoing surgical repair. Each patient underwent a unique surgical correction: direct reimplantation, interposition graft repair, or Takeuchi repair. These cases demonstrate that with appropriate preoperative planning and familiarity with various repair techniques, satisfactory short-term postoperative outcomes can be achieved in adults with ALCAPA.

articles.title: Psychological Distress and Post-traumatic Growth During Prolonged Collective Adversity: Patterns of Association in a Large Asian Sample.
articles.abstract: Psychological distress following prolonged collective adversity has been associated not only with adverse mental health outcomes but also with post-traumatic growth (PTG). However, the relationship between psychological distress and specific PTG domains remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the associations of depression, anxiety, and stress with overall PTG and its five domains during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 2,515 adults across multiple Asian countries using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21) and the PostTraumatic Growth Inventory (PTGI). Standard multiple regression was conducted to examine unadjusted associations with overall PTG, followed by a separate hierarchical multiple regression adjusting for COVID-19 infection and bereavement. A multivariate general linear model using Pillai's Trace indicated that depression, anxiety, and stress were significantly associated with five domains of PTG (p < .001). The unadjusted regression model explained 63.2% of the variance in overall PTG, while the final adjusted model explained 63.7%. The high explained variance may partly reflect shared method variance from single-occasion self-report measures. These associations remained significant after accounting for COVID-19-related exposure. The findings suggest that psychological distress and self-reported PTG may coexist during prolonged collective adversity. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings should be interpreted as associations within the recruited sample rather than population-level or cross-cultural effects. In addition, p values may be underestimated because country-level clustering was not modelled.

articles.title: Reconsidering the Optimal Timing of PCSK9 Inhibition After Acute Coronary Syndromes in the Post-AMUNDSEN Era.
articles.abstract: Patients surviving an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remain at substantial risk of recurrent cardiovascular events, particularly during the first months after the index event. Current European recommendations support immediate oral high intensity lipid lowering therapy, targeting an LDL-C level <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L) together with a ≥50% reduction from baseline. More recently, the therapeutic approach has shifted towards earlier treatment intensification with ezetimibe during the index hospitalization. Nevertheless, real-world studies such as DA VINCI and SANTORINI continue to show poor LDL-C goal attainment and limited use of combination lipid-lowering therapy.Recent data from the SWEDEHEART registry further suggest that delayed treatment intensification and late achievement of lipid targets may translate into avoidable residual cardiovascular risk. The AMUNDSEN trial has renewed interest in the optimal timing of PCSK9 inhibition after ACS. Very early initiation of evolocumab resulted in markedly higher LDL-C goal attainment at 1 year compared with conventional care which included the possible selective and delayed use of PCSK9 inhibitors, as recommended in the guidelines (82% vs. 40%). In a disctinct objective, the possibility that early pleiotropic (non-LDL) effects of evolocumab could improve short-term clinical outcome was not confirmed at 1-year followup.These findings raise an important question: should the benefit of lipid-lowering therapy be assessed only according to the LDL-C level achieved at a given time point, or should the duration of exposure to lower LDL-C also be considered? Evidence from randomized trials, meta-analyses, and long-term follow-up studies supports the concept that both the magnitude and duration of LDL-C reduction contribute to cardiovascular benefit. This review discusses the implications of AMUNDSEN in the context of contemporary evidence and examines which patients may derive the greatest benefit from upfront PCSK9 inhibition, considering both recurrent clinical risk and the magnitude of LDL-C reduction required to achieve recommended targets.

articles.title: Anatolution, an online platform for consensus morphology.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Reliable cell annotations are essential for supervised image analysis, yet producing the annotations required for quantitative cellular morphometry is laborious, and results can vary with both tissue preparation and expert interpretation of ambiguous morphology. Nissl staining has long underpinned comparative neuroanatomy, generating extensive and taxonomically diverse records of cellular organization across the nervous system. We developed Anatolution to make this resource more amenable to standardized quantitative analysis by integrating independent annotations alongside explicit measures of rater agreement for quality control under computer vision bookkeeping.

METHOD: Anatolution is an open-source web platform for annotating single images or 3D volumes (https://anatolution.herokuapp.com/public-tool/). Multiple raters independently outline cellular structures using a shared set of labels or conventions, and the platform enables consensus analysis alongside conventional image segmentation.

RESULT: We evaluated 603,297 annotations produced by 48 raters across 1,024 image tiles and tested a subset of 68 fully annotated tiles against unsupervised segmentation. Boundary overlap in cell drawings, scored from 0 ("no overlap") to 1 ("identical"), rose from 0.30 for 1 rater to 0.79 with 7 users, and in a subset of 68 annotated tiles, 88% contained unsupervised segmentation results.

CONCLUSION: Agreement between groups of raters increased as raters were added to an optimum of ∼7 users, and within a subset of images nearly 9 in 10 annotations were spatially anchored to unsupervised methods. Anatolution supports the production of consensus labels whose stability can be quantified and improved by adding independent raters, providing structured reference data for training and evaluating cell segmentation models for quantitative histology.

articles.title: Risk factors for intracardiac thrombus during peripheral venoarterial and venovenoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support.
articles.abstract: IntroductionIntracardiac thrombus (ICT) is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening complication of peripheral venoarterial (V-A) or venovenoarterial (V-AV) extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). However, clinical predictors of ICT remain poorly defined, limiting risk stratification.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort study included 638 adults who underwent 671 consecutive episodes of peripheral V-A/V-AV ECMO between 2021 and 2025. Factors associated with ICT were evaluated using cause-specific Cox regression, with ECMO discontinuation without ICT treated as a competing event. Restricted cubic splines were used to assess nonlinearity in continuous predictors. A secondary analysis compared ICT cases managed surgically and nonsurgically.ResultsICT was detected in 58 ECMO episodes (8.6%). In multivariable analysis, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.98 per 1% increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.96-1.00; p = 0.028), day 1 pulse pressure (aHR, 0.98 per 1 mmHg increase; 95% CI, 0.96-1.00; p = 0.034), and systemic heparinization (aHR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.11-0.39; p < 0.001) were independently associated with a lower hazard of ICT. The association between LVEF and ICT was nonlinear (p = 0.033): risk was low at LVEF values above approximately 35% and increased sharply below this level. The association with pulse pressure was linear. Short-term outcomes did not differ between surgical and nonsurgical management.ConclusionsDuring peripheral V-A/V-AV ECMO, ICT was independently associated with impaired cardiac function, low pulsatility, and the absence of systemic heparinization. Assessment of LVEF, initial pulse pressure, and anticoagulation status may help identify patients who warrant closer imaging surveillance.

articles.title: From Technical Performance to Clinical Impact: Challenges and Opportunities for AI Modelling of CKD Progression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health burden, with highly heterogeneous trajectories ranging from long-term stability to rapid progression towards kidney failure and kidney replacement therapy. Accurate prediction of CKD progression is essential to support personalised monitoring, timely therapeutic intensification, nephrology referral, and preparation for advanced kidney care. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches may improve risk stratification by modelling complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent patterns in routinely collected clinical data, electronic health records, and potentially multimodal data sources. Nonetheless, it remains unclear how ready these AI-driven models are for clinical use. This structured narrative review aimed to map the current landscape of AI for predicting CKD progression, assess the robustness and clinical relevance of the evidence, and identify methodological and implementation gaps that must be addressed to translate technical accuracy into clinical impact.

SUMMARY: This review synthesised 35 studies published between 2020 and 2025 that developed and evaluated models to predict CKD progression. Most studies used retrospective cohort designs and electronic health record data, relying mainly on demographic variables, laboratory measures, comorbidities, and clinical history. Tree-based models, random forests, boosting methods, regression-based approaches, and neural networks were the most commonly investigated methods. Overall, the reviewed models often achieved favourable discriminative performance, as measured by AUROC or C-index. Nevertheless, the evidence base remains limited by substantial heterogeneity in study designs, cohort compositions, prediction targets, time horizons, feature engineering, and validation strategies. External validation was reported in only about one-quarter of studies, while calibration, clinical utility, patient-level uncertainty, and implementation-oriented evaluation were inconsistently addressed. Prediction endpoints were predominantly kidney failure-related. Multimodal data, including imaging, genomics, and social determinants of health, were rarely used, and explainability methods were more often applied for model description than for clinician-facing decision support.

KEY MESSAGES: AI models show substantial promise for predicting CKD progression, particularly when trained on routinely available clinical data. However, the field remains more advanced in model development than in clinical validation and implementation. Future research should prioritise external and temporal validation, systematic calibration assessment, decision-curve or net-benefit analysis, comparison with established clinical risk scores, clinically meaningful prediction horizons, subgroup and fairness evaluation, patient-level uncertainty estimation, and prospective testing of model-informed care. These steps are essential to move from statistically accurate models to reliable, interpretable, equitable, and actionable tools for CKD management.

articles.title: The Varying Benefits of Two Years Automated Insulin Delivery System Use on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Profiles in Children and Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems are recommended for youths with type 1 diabetes, but real-world longitudinal data remains limited despite increasing use. This study evaluates the effect of 2 years of AID use on continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) profiles and body mass index (BMI) development.

METHODS: Data from individuals with type 1 diabetes aged <18 years, diabetes duration >3 months, and AID use of >3 months from the Diabetes Prospective Follow-up (DPV) Registry between 2019 and 2025 were analyzed. CGM and HbA1c were required at the last documented time in range (TIR) (±90 days; follow-up) and 2 years earlier (±90 days; baseline). Changes were investigated using adjusted regression models with repeated measurements.

FINDINGS: Data from 2486 participants (baseline: median age: 11.9 years, diabetes duration: 5.0 years, 53% male) were analyzed over ∼23 months. The largest gains occurred in time in tight range (TiTR) (42.4% [95% confidence interval: 41.0-43.7] to 50.1% [48.8-51.4]; P < 0.001) and coefficient of variation (CV) (32.9 [32.0-33.7] to 29.5 [28.7-30.2]; P < 0.001). HbA1c (7.3% [7.2-7.3] to 7.2 [7.1-7.2]; P < 0.001), TIR (64.5% [63.9-65.1] to 66.7% [66.1-67.3]; P < 0.001), and mean sensor glucose (SG) (161.0 mg/dL [158.4-163.5] to 155.5 mg/dL [153.1-157.9]; P = 0.001) improved statistically, but below clinical relevance thresholds. Time below range (TBR) < 70 mg/dL increased (2.7% [2.6-2.9] to 3.2% [3.1-3.4]; P < 0.001), TBR < 54 mg/dL remained stable (1.7%-1.8%; P = 0.516), and severe hypoglycemia decreased (6.4-4.5/100 patient-years; P < 0.001). No changes were seen in children <6 years. In youth 6 to <12 and 12 to <18 years, TiTR and CV improved most, while TBR increased. BMI-standard deviation score (SDS) increased (0.57 [0.53-0.61] to 0.67 [0.63-0.72]; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: After 2 years of AID use, TiTR and CV showed clinically relevant improvements, while TBR < 70 mg/dL increased with stable TBR < 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycemia decreased. Changes in TIR, SG, and HbA1c were statistically significant but small, yet noteworthy, as glycemia usually deteriorates during adolescence. The increase in BMI-SDS needs to be further investigated.

articles.title: Development of a psoriasis-like eruption during treatment with mepolizumab: A case report.
articles.abstract: Mepolizumab is effective for treating eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA), and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), but unexpected adverse events associated with anti-interleukin-5 (IL-5) monoclonal antibodies have not yet been fully characterized.
