Herein, we report the case of a 56-year-old woman who developed a psoriasis-like eruption ~18 months after starting subcutaneous mepolizumab (300 mg every 4 weeks) for EGPA, SEA, and CRSwNP. She had no personal or family history of psoriasis or atopic dermatitis. Small punctate erythematous lesions first appeared on the back, before gradually spreading to the trunk and extremities. Skin biopsy showed neutrophilic infiltration within the stratum corneum, focal hypogranulosis, dilated tortuous capillaries, and increased mitotic activity in the basal layer. Prominent regular elongation of the rete ridges was not evident. The overall clinicopathological findings supported a diagnosis of a psoriasis-like eruption, with no eosinophils being identified in either the epidermis or dermis. Topical treatment with calcipotriol and betamethasone, while mepolizumab was continued at the same dose, produced only temporary improvement followed by recurrence. The eruption improved following temporary mepolizumab discontinuation, but the patient's asthma exacerbations recurred. The mepolizumab dose was therefore reduced to 100 mg every 4 weeks, and a potent topical corticosteroid was added. The eruption resolved within 3 months thereafter, without recurrence, and control of EGPA, SEA, and CRSwNP was maintained. Although the psoriasis-like eruption improved after mepolizumab dose reduction, the concurrent topical treatment intensification means this improvement cannot be attributed to the dose reduction alone.

articles.title: Severe Progressive Interstitial Lung Disease in Seronegative Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a subtype of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by severe proximal weakness and myofiber necrosis with minimal inflammation. Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is uncommon in IMNM, particularly in seronegative cases, with limited published data on its clinical features. We present a 72-year-old man, a lifelong never-smoker, with previously diagnosed "idiopathic" ILD who presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure. Despite negative myositis-specific antibodies and normal creatine kinase (CK), mildly elevated aldolase and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings prompted muscle biopsy, which confirmed IMNM. He was treated with combination immunosuppression including corticosteroids, mycophenolate, rituximab, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), with significant improvement in respiratory and muscle function at six months and sustained respiratory and muscle function through 14-18 months of follow-up. This case demonstrates that seronegative IMNM can present with severe, progressive ILD. Normal CK should not exclude the diagnosis, particularly when muscle atrophy is present. Aldolase elevation and muscle biopsy are essential diagnostic tools in seronegative cases.

articles.title: Pediatric Acute Myeloid Leukemia Treatment Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study on Prognostic Factors and Survival in a Low- to Middle-Income Country.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (AML) outcomes remain substantially lower in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where treatment-related mortality (TRM), treatment abandonment, and limited access to risk-adapted therapy and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remain important challenges. We evaluated contemporary outcomes and factors influencing survival in children with AML treated at a tertiary center in Pakistan.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients aged <18 years diagnosed with AML between 2011 and 2023. Patients in main AML cohort were compared between an early era (2011-2016) and a later era (2017-2023), following institutional availability of HSCT. Overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), and relapse-free survival (RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were estimated using competing-risk analysis. Acute myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome (AML-DS) and Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 143 patients in the main AML cohort, 114 (80%) initiated therapy and 69 (60%) achieved complete remission. Induction mortality was 16%, while TRM occurred in 27% of treated patients, predominantly due to sepsis. Three-year OS, EFS, and RFS were 35%, 17%, and 38%, respectively. Survival did not differ significantly between the early and later eras (3-year OS, 37% vs. 32%, p=0.70; EFS, 20% vs. 15%, p=0.35). The 3-year cumulative incidences of relapse and TRM were 51% and 26%, respectively, with no significant differences between eras. Thirty patients relapsed; 12 received salvage therapy, of whom nine achieved a second remission. Treatment abandonment occurred throughout the treatment course, including in 16% before therapy initiation. Intermediate- and high-risk disease and higher presenting white blood cell count were associated with increased mortality on multivariable analysis. Twelve patients underwent HSCT, all in the later era. Three-year OS was 78% in AML-DS and 75% in APL.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric AML outcomes remained limited by the combined effects of TRM, relapse, and treatment abandonment. Institutional availability of HSCT in the later era was not associated with improved population-level survival, although the small number of transplanted patients precludes conclusions regarding HSCT effectiveness. Strengthening supportive care, molecular risk stratification, treatment continuity, and timely access to salvage therapy and HSCT may improve outcomes in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Real-world effectiveness of mepolizumab for the treatment of severe asthma with overlapping eosinophilic comorbidities Running head: Mepolizumab in eosinophilic comorbidities.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe eosinophilic asthma frequently coexists with eosinophilic disorders involving other organs. Although mepolizumab is effective for severe eosinophilic asthma, real-world data on patients with overlapping eosinophilic comorbidities remain limited.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 25 patients with severe eosinophilic asthma treated with mepolizumab. Asthma Control Test (ACT) scores, forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), peripheral blood eosinophil (PBE) counts, and oral corticosteroid (OCS) doses were evaluated at baseline and week 16. Treatment response was assessed at week 16 using the Global Evaluation of Treatment Effectiveness (GETE), and subsequent treatment course was examined for up to 12 months.

RESULTS: Comorbid eosinophilic diseases included eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, chronic eosinophilic pneumonia, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, and eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis/eosinophilic otitis media. At week 16, median PBE counts decreased from 745 to 44/µL and OCS doses from 7.5 to 4.0 mg/day. Median ACT scores increased from 18 to 23 and FEV1 from 1.89 to 2.08 L. Nineteen patients (76%) had an Excellent or Good GETE response; 18 continued mepolizumab through Month 12, with follow-up unavailable for one. Of the six patients with a Moderate or Poor response, four switched biologics, one discontinued biologic treatment, and one continued mepolizumab with delayed improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Mepolizumab was associated with improved asthma control, reduced eosinophil counts, and lower OCS requirements in patients with severe asthma and overlapping eosinophilic comorbidities. Assessment at week 16 also provided a practical decision point for subsequent continuation or modification of biologic therapy.

articles.title: Estimating the incidence of stroke using national administrative health data: A validation study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is increasing interest in administrative health data as a cost-effective way to measure stroke incidence and outcomes. This study compared administrative health data with the 'gold-standard' population-based fifth Auckland Regional Community Stroke Study (ARCOS V) and calculated stroke incidence using administrative data for the whole New Zealand population.

METHODS: We linked stroke events from administrative data with ARCOS V data for two districts in the Auckland area. Sensitivity and positive predictive value (PPV) were calculated to assess the validity of administrative data, stratified by ethnicity and deprivation classifications. Population-wide age-specific and age-standardised stroke incidence was reported by sex and ethnicity.

RESULTS: In total, 1569 initial stroke events were identified in the administrative data and 1635 in the ARCOS V data between 1 September 2020 and 31 August 2021. Compared with ARCOS V, overall sensitivity was 87% [95%CI, 85%-89%] and PPV was 91% [95%CI, 89%-92%]. Sensitivity and PPVs were highly comparable among Māori, Pacific Peoples, New Zealand Europeans and other ethnicities; also, little difference was observed across different socioeconomic groupings. Age-standardised first-ever stroke incidence for those aged >15 years was estimated to be 110/100,000/year, highest in Pacific Peoples and Māori, with substantial geographic variation, which ranged from 85/100,000 to 127/100,000.

CONCLUSIONS: New Zealand health administrative data provide accurate estimates of stroke incidence including for ethnic and socioeconomic sub-groups and identified significant geographic variation. This opens opportunities for its use in epidemiological research, stroke monitoring, and development of a virtual stroke register.

articles.title: The Incidence of Stroke and the Population Attributable Fraction of Its Risk Factors in Thailand: Prospective Findings from the Thai Epidemiologic Stroke (TES) Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data on incidence of stroke are scarce in developing countries and little is known about the contribution of known risk factors in this population. The aim of our study was to determine the incidence of first-ever stroke in general population and population attributable fraction (PAF) of its risk factors in Thailand.

METHODS: Thai Epidemiologic Stroke (TES) study is a prospective community-based cohort study that recruited participants from the general population from five regions of Thailand. Between 2004 and 2006, 19,620 participants aged 45 to 80 years, free of stroke, took part in the baseline survey. The participants were followed up for first-ever stroke. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with incident stroke, with Fine-Gray competing-risk models accounting for non-stroke death as a sensitivity analysis. Mutually adjusted population attributable fractions were estimated for modifiable risk factors consistently associated with incident stroke.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10.2 years, 925 participants developed a first-ever stroke. The crude incidence rates per 100,000 person-years was 561.0 (95%CI, 526.0-598.3). Incidence adjusted to the WHO standard population (2000-2025) aged 45-74 years was 509.5 per 100,000 person-years. Hypertension had the highest PAF (21.3%), followed by low education (15.4%), low personal income (14.2%), smoking status (9.9%), and diabetes mellitus (7.2%), respectively. The total PAF for these five significant risk factors was 68.0% (95% CI: 58.4%-77.7%).

CONCLUSION: The incidence rate of stroke in Thailand is higher than that of several other countries, particularly developed countries. About 68.0% of all strokes in Thailand are attributable to five modifiable risk factors. Among these factors, hypertension is the most important.

articles.title: The Impact of Telenutrition versus In-person Nutrition Consultation Visits on Glycemic Control Among People with Type 1 Diabetes: Data from Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition consultation is essential to improve glycemic control in people with T1D. People with T1D often need frequent follow up with specialized diabetes dietitians to acquire the necessary nutrition skills including carbohydrate counting. Telehealth has made remote follow up visits with HCPs more convenient. However, studies comparing the effectiveness of virtual nutrition clinics versus traditional in-person nutrition clinics are limited.

METHOD: We performed a comprehensive assessment of changes in glycemic control (including A1C and CGM metrics), insulin doses, and patients' satisfaction over 3 months among 137 individuals with T1D who were referred to the nutrition clinic for training on carbohydrate counting. Data were compared between those who attended telenutrition clinics (n=107) versus in-person nutrition clinics (n=30).

RESULTS: Patients in both groups had significant improvements in hemoglobin A1c from baseline to the end of the study [from 9.3% to 8.1% (p<0.01) in the telenutrition group and from 9.1% to 8% (p<0.01) in the in-person group]. Likewise, time in range (TIR) improved in both groups [from 53.9% to 58.5% in the telenutrition group (p<0.01) and from 49.1% to 54.7% (p=0.13) in the in-person group]. The average prandial insulin doses decreased in both groups [from 31 to 21 units/day in the telenutrition group (p<0.01) and from 29 to 21 units/day in the in-person group (p<0.01)]. The majority (97%) of telenutrition clinic participants reported having similar if not better quality of healthcare services compared to the in-person nutrition clinics.

CONCLUSION: Telenutrition visits are as effective as traditional nutrition visits in improving glycemic control in PWT1D. Our findings highlihght how widely available tools such as smartphones and communication apps can be effectively utilized by dietitians to address the current shortage of trained dietitians.

articles.title: CADASIL Argentine Registry (CADASILAR): Establishment of a Harmonized Multicenter Registry with Preliminary Clinical and Cognitive Insights from Latin America.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is the most common monogenic small vessel disease. Despite extensive characterization in Europe and Asia, data from Latin America remain limited. This study aimed to describe the structure of the Argentine CADASIL registry (CADASILAR), a harmonized multicenter initiative, and to report preliminary findings from its cross-sectional cohort.

METHODS: CADASILAR is an observational, referral-based, multicenter registry comprising two phases: a cross-sectional cohort (CADASILAR-C) and a planned three-year longitudinal follow-up (CADASILAR-Long). Here we report preliminary descriptive and bivariate analyses from CADASILAR-C. Definitive or possible CADASIL diagnoses were included based on genetic testing, skin biopsy, or clinical and neuroimaging criteria.

RESULTS: A total of 109 patients were included in the CADASILAR-C cohort, 50.5% were female, and mean age at symptom onset was 42.4 ± 12 years. Ischemic stroke was the most frequent initial manifestation (28/109, 25.7%), followed by migraine with aura (19/109, 17.4%). History of cognitive decline was documented in 48.6% of patients (53/109). Among those with Mini-Mental State Examination data (49/109), 24.5% had scores indicative of cognitive impairment (10/49). An exploratory analysis among those with cognitive impairment showed a statistically significant difference in the frequency of hypertension (80.0% vs 33.3%, p=0.012), overweight (40.0% vs 10.3%, p=0.044), and obesity (40.0% vs 2.6%, p=0.004). On neuroimaging, periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities, and temporal lobe lesions were the most frequent features observed. All genetic variants identified were cysteine-altering variants.

CONCLUSION: CADASILAR represents the first structured, multicenter effort to systematically characterize CADASIL in Latin America, providing a harmonized framework for the collection of clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging, and genetic data across centers. This approach aims to improve case identification, facilitate inter-cohort comparability, and support future longitudinal research in the region.

articles.title: Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective.
articles.abstract: Environmental noise is a pervasive but under-recognized cardiovascular and metabolic risk factor. Drawing on prior expert reviews and large-scale epidemiologic and mechanistic studies, this review synthesizes evidence on the burden, major clinical associations, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and mitigation strategies relevant to cardiovascular health. Road traffic noise is consistently and dose-dependently associated with higher risks of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, sleep disturbance, and adverse mental health outcomes, whereas for railway and aircraft noise, the evidence base is less consistent, although important associations are increasingly reported. Translational human imaging studies, controlled exposure experiments, and animal models converge on a common pathway in which chronic and intermittent noise exposure activates stress-responsive neural circuits, increases sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, promotes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and may thereby accelerate cardiometabolic disease. Noise frequently co-occurs with air pollution, heat, and adverse social and built environments, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities, and these combined exposures may contribute additively to cardiovascular risk. These effects are especially relevant in urban populations with nighttime exposure and multiple co-exposures. Despite this growing evidence base, environmental noise remains largely absent from contemporary cardiovascular risk assessment tools, prevention guidelines, and routine patient counselling, representing a missed opportunity for risk reduction. Effective mitigation will require a hierarchical strategy combining source reduction, health-informed urban and transport planning, and targeted individual protection. Reducing environmental noise exposure should be recognized as an important opportunity to protect and advance cardiovascular and metabolic health in the 21st century.

articles.title: Vancomycin Clearance During CVVHDF With an oXiris Membrane: Pharmacokinetic Evidence of Adsorptive Drug Removal.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adsorptive hemofilters such as oXiris are increasingly used during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) in septic shock, yet their interaction with antimicrobial agents remains insufficiently characterized. Vancomycin dosing during CRRT is particularly challenging because of altered volume of distribution, protein binding, and extracorporeal clearance. Clinical data describing the magnitude and time course of vancomycin adsorption by oXiris are scarce.

METHODS: We performed an in vivo pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) assessment of vancomycin in an anuric, profoundly hypoalbuminemic patient with septic shock undergoing continuous veno-venous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF) using an oXiris membrane. Serial pre-filter, post-filter, and effluent samples were obtained during the seventh vancomycin dose while the membrane had been in use for 18 hours. Pharmacokinetic parameters, effluent saturation coefficients, pre-dilution-corrected extracorporeal clearance, and vancomycin exposure were estimated using a one-compartment model. Circuit-level concentration patterns were evaluated as observations compatible with, but not definitive quantification of, an adsorptive contribution.

RESULTS: Pre- to post-filter vancomycin concentration reductions declined over time (≈13.5% at 2 hours, 13.3% at 4 hours, and 3.1% at 7 hours), a pattern compatible with a time-dependent adsorptive contribution, although adsorption could not be quantified separately from diffusion and convection. The mean effluent saturation coefficient was 0.62. After first-order correction for pre-dilution, estimated CVVHDF-related clearance was approximately 1.25 L/h. Total clearance was estimated at 5.7 L/h, yielding a model-derived AUC24 of 526 mg·h/L and an AUC24/MIC ratio of 1,053.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single patient receiving pre-dilution CVVHDF with an 18-hour-old oXiris membrane, mixed extracorporeal vancomycin removal was observed. After first-order correction for pre-dilution, estimated CLCVVHDF was approximately 1.25 L/h. The temporal circuit pattern was compatible with an adsorptive contribution, but adsorption could not be quantified separately from diffusion and convection. Dose adjustment after membrane replacement should be guided by AUC-based therapeutic drug monitoring rather than applied routinely.

articles.title: CLINICAL PATTERNS OF SUSPECTED DRUG HYPERSENSITIVITY AND FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DRUG-RELATED ANAPHYLAXIS: A REAL-WORLD STUDY OF 1,037 ADULTS.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Drug hypersensitivity reactions (DHRs) are frequently encountered in allergy practice and encompass a broad spectrum of clinical presentations. Identifying the distribution of suspected culprit drugs and the clinical characteristics associated with drug-related anaphylaxis may help define the real-world profile of adults evaluated for suspected drug hypersensitivity.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 1,037 adults evaluated for suspected drug hypersensitivity at a tertiary allergy clinic between May 1, 2022, and May 1, 2023. Demographic characteristics, allergic comorbidities, suspected culprit drugs and drug classes, reported reaction characteristics, aeroallergen sensitization, and available laboratory findings were retrospectively evaluated. Patients with and without drug-related anaphylaxis were compared, and factors independently associated with drug-related anaphylaxis were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: The mean age was 44.71 ± 14.14 years, and 72.3% of patients were female. NSAIDs (61.3%) and antibiotics (50.7%) were the most frequently reported suspected culprit drug classes, with beta-lactams accounting for 41.5% of the overall cohort. The most common reported manifestations were urticaria (75.6%), angioedema (52.4%), and bronchospasm (29.7%). Drug-related anaphylaxis was reported in 255 patients (24.6%). Asthma (19.2% vs. 12.0%; p=0.004), NSAID-exacerbated respiratory disease (NERD) (4.3% vs. 1.4%; p=0.005), food allergy (5.1% vs. 1.8%; p=0.004), and suspected beta-lactam hypersensitivity (51.4% vs. 38.2%; p<0.001) were more frequent among patients with drug-related anaphylaxis. In multivariable analysis, asthma (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.64, 95% CI 1.09-2.47), NERD (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.13-6.93), food allergy (aOR 2.76, 95% CI 1.26-6.04), and suspected beta-lactam hypersensitivity (aOR 1.81, 95% CI 1.35-2.42) were independently associated with a recorded history of suspected drug-related anaphylaxis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this tertiary allergy clinic cohort of adults evaluated for suspected drug hypersensitivity, NSAIDs and antibiotics were the most frequently reported suspected culprit drug classes. Approximately one-quarter had a recorded history of suspected drug-related anaphylaxis. Asthma, NERD, food allergy, and suspected beta-lactam hypersensitivity were associated with this history in multivariable analysis. These findings describe associations in a referred population and do not establish causality.

articles.title: Continuous glucose monitoring in peritoneal dialysis: What the evidence supports and where it stops.
articles.journal: Peritoneal dialysis international : journal of the International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis
articles.abstract: Glycaemic assessment is particularly difficult in people treated with peritoneal dialysis (PD). Glycated haemoglobin loses accuracy and precision in advanced kidney disease, and continuous absorption of dialysate glucose creates a glycaemic load that intermittent capillary testing cannot capture. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides dense ambulatory interstitial glucose data, but PD-specific evidence remains small and heterogeneous. In the largest CGM cohort of people receiving maintenance dialysis, hyperglycaemia that was often not clinically evident was most prominent among those treated with PD. This narrative review appraises the analytical performance, clinical accuracy and practical limitations of CGM in PD and separates defensible conclusions from over-interpretation. Contemporary sensors have shown acceptable accuracy against laboratory references in small single-centre PD cohorts, including one of icodextrin-treated patients, but performance varies with device, calibration requirement, reference standard and dialysis modality, and both the magnitude and the direction of sensor error affect time-in-range metrics. The best-documented icodextrin hazard is maltose interference with non-glucose-specific blood glucose meters used for confirmation or calibration. Because glucose specificity is a property of each enzyme and sensor, and anuric patients receiving daily icodextrin have not been specifically studied, device-specific validation in this subgroup remains a safety prerequisite before sensor readings guide insulin dosing. CGM is a reasonable adjunct for selected patients, particularly when laboratory markers are discordant, but current data do not support prescriptive treatment algorithms or regulatory conclusions. Pragmatic multicentre accuracy studies, registries and trials using CGM-derived and patient-reported outcomes are realistic next steps.

articles.title: Association Between Daily Fluid Balance Trajectories and Dynamic Organ Failure Resolution (SOFA-2) in Sepsis: A Latent Class Growth Analysis of 16 262 Patients.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFluid management in sepsis has transitioned toward restrictive de-resuscitation during the intensive care unit (ICU) ebb phase (Days 3-7). The clinical heterogeneity of longitudinal fluid trajectories, their interaction with active therapeutic de-resuscitation, and their prognostic association with dynamic organ recovery evaluated under the 2025 SOFA-2 criteria require clarification in large multicenter databases.ObjectiveTo identify latent phenotypes of daily net fluid balance during the de-resuscitation phase and examine their independent associations with dynamic organ failure resolution and 28-day mortality after accounting for active de-resuscitation interventions.MethodsWe performed a retrospective observational cohort study of 16 262 adult septic patients from the MIMIC-IV v3.1 database who survived at least 72 h in the ICU. Daily net fluid balances (ml/kg/day) from Day 3 to Day 7 were modeled using group-based trajectory modeling without prior outcome stratification. Active de-resuscitation interventions, including cumulative intravenous loop diuretic dosing and renal replacement therapy (RRT), were extracted. Multivariable logistic regression and sensitivity analyses evaluated independent associations with 28-day mortality and longitudinal SOFA-2 trajectories.ResultsThree distinct trajectory phenotypes were identified: Class 1 (Rapid Recovery, 85.4%, n = 13 892), Class 2 (Late Response, 8.3%, n = 1354), and Class 3 (Persistent Failure, 6.3%, n = 1016). Class 1 maintained a steady, low net balance and experienced the lowest 28-day mortality (20.8%). Class 2 exhibited sustained high fluid retention until Day 5 before a delayed downward inflection, whereas Class 3 showed relentless fluid accumulation. Daily SOFA-2 scores resolved rapidly in Class 1 (decreasing from 4.24 on Day 3 to 1.18 by Day 7), whereas recovery was stalled in Class 2 (1.71 by Day 7) and persistently blunted in Class 3 (2.17 by Day 7). In multivariable logistic regression fully adjusted for baseline illness severity, loop diuretic exposure, and RRT, both Class 2 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.30, 95% CI 1.14-1.49; P < .001) and Class 3 (aOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.09-1.48; P = .002) were independently associated with increased 28-day mortality compared with Class 1. These associations remained consistent across sensitivity analyses restricted to non-RRT patients and loop diuretic users.ConclusionDiscrete longitudinal fluid balance phenotypes identify clinically distinct sub-populations during the de-resuscitation window of sepsis. Rather than proving direct causality, these trajectories serve as clinical markers of underlying endothelial integrity, intrinsic excretory capacity, and physiological responsiveness to de-resuscitation.

articles.title: Complications and Management of Thoracic Surgery: Pertinent Information for Intensivists and Hospitalists.
articles.abstract: Thoracic surgery presents unique postoperative challenges that intensivists and hospitalists frequently encounter in both ward and intensive care settings. This review provides a practical overview of common procedures, potential complications, and evidence-based management strategies tailored to intensivists and hospitalists. Topics include the role of imaging, ventilatory support, and pain control, as well as integration with Anesthesiology, Pulmonology, Radiology, and Respiratory Therapy. Major complications and their corresponding management-such as air leaks, atelectasis, pneumonia, atrial fibrillation, bronchopleural fistula, and empyema-are discussed in detail, with emphasis on early recognition and intervention. This paper offers a concise guide for the management of postoperative thoracic surgery patients by outlining key principles most relevant to intensivists and hospitalists in daily practice.

articles.title: Age-Specific Self-Care, Psychosocial, and Coping Competencies in Children with Type 1 Diabetes: Development of a Competency Framework from Diabetes Camp Experiences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The progressive acquisition of self-care and coping competencies is essential for children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), as these skills support increasing autonomy in diabetes management. However, limited data are available regarding the ages at which these competencies are typically acquired. This study aimed to determine the ages at which key self-care and coping competencies are acquired among children and adolescents with T1D.

METHODS: We analyzed data from competency evaluations conducted in 943 patients aged 7-17.9 years during diabetes summer camp in France in 2021. A broad range of self-care and coping competencies was assessed in patients treated with either multiple daily injections (MDI) or insulin pump therapy. Age groups were defined as 7-8, 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, and 15-17 years. Descriptive statistics were used to determine the proportion of patients acquiring each competency by age group, and treatment modalities were compared using univariate analyses.

RESULTS: Among the 114 self-care competencies classified into 14 domains, 94.1% were acquired by patients treated with MDI and 96.5% by those using insulin pump therapy by the age of 17.9 years. We established a detailed reference list of the ages at which at least 75% of patients had acquired each competency and developed a corresponding competency evaluation tool. Several competencies were acquired at younger ages in patients using insulin pump therapy than in those treated with MDI.

CONCLUSIONS: The age-specific reference list developed in this study may help healthcare professionals design and adapt therapeutic education programs to support the progressive development of autonomy in children and adolescents with T1D.

articles.title: Resting segmental strain in CABG-referred coronary artery disease.
Global Leadership Initiative on a Malnutrition-Based Muscle Assessment Using Multiple Methods in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMuscle mass assessment is integral to the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) for critically ill patients. Despite its importance, an optimal muscle volume assessment has yet to be established. We herein performed various muscle volume and nutritional assessments and conducted an exploratory evaluation of muscle volume assessment methods that may be clinically meaningful for critically ill patients.MethodsThis single-center prospective cohort enrolled adults expected to require mechanical ventilation for >2 days who ambulated independently before hospitalization. Computed tomography (CT)-derived total skeletal muscle mass at third lumbar vertebra (CT-MM) from retrospectively reviewed scans served as the reference. Within 24 h of intensive care unit (ICU) admission, we measured mid-upper arm circumference (AC), calf circumference, bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA)-derived fat-free muscle volume and intracellular water-based muscle volume (BIA-Muscle-ICW), femoral cross-sectional area, ultrasound-derived femoral muscle thickness (ultrasound-FMT), ultrasound-derived upper-limb muscle thickness, and resting energy expenditure. Malnutrition followed GLIM. Reduced muscle mass used the CT-MM index.ResultsFifty-two patients were included, 13 with GLIM-defined malnutrition. BIA-Muscle-ICW correlated most strongly with CT-MM (r = 0.80, p < 0.001). The other measures also correlated consistently, and all intercorrelated. For CT-defined sarcopenia, ultrasound-FMT index (AUC = 0.88), BIA-Muscle-ICW index (AUC = 0.83), and AC (AUC = 0.85) demonstrated good discrimination. Additionally, BIA-Muscle-ICW correlated most strongly with resting energy expenditure (r = 0.61, p < 0.001).ConclusionThe muscle volume indices assessed herein mutually correlated in critically ill patients, suggesting the potential of incorporating these measures, particularly BIA-Muscle-ICW, into initial GLIM at ICU admission. BIA-Muscle-ICW index, ultrasound-FMT index, and AC demonstrated strong discriminative performance for diagnosing sarcopenia.

articles.title: RISK SCORE FOR ONSET OF KIDNEY FAILURE IN PATIENTS WITH CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nephrology is the reference of care for patients with overt chronic kidney disease (CKD). Optimization of stratification of the risk of kidney failure (KF) is therefore essential for proper management of CKD in renal clinics.

METHODS: We analyzed data from a prospective observational study involving 3957 non-dialysis-dependent CKD (ND-CKD) patients followed in renal clinics for at least six months. A stepwise selection of predictors was conducted to develop a risk prediction model. External validation was performed in 309 patients from Groningen, The Netherlands.

RESULTS: Patients who developed KF were younger (61.3 vs. 68 years, p<0.001), had higher systolic blood pressure (142 vs. 139 mmHg, p=0.001), higher proteinuria (1.2 vs. 0.3 g/24h, p<0.001), lower eGFR (21.3 vs. 35.5 mL/min, p<0.001), and less frequent use of RAAS inhibitors (68.2% vs. 73.3%, p=0.003). The 3-year KF risk prediction model included 10 key variables: age, gender, systolic blood pressure, eGFR, 24-hour urine protein, hemoglobin, serum calcium and phosphate, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and RAAS inhibitor use at baseline. The model demonstrated good discrimination, with a C-index of 0.85 (95% CI 0.83-0.87) in internal validation and the model reached a C-index of 0.82 in external validation.

CONCLUSION: We have developed a 3-year risk prediction tool for kidney failure in G3a-G4 stage CKD patients under stable nephrology care. This tool may aid in patient communication and support multidisciplinary decision-making in nephrology.

articles.title: Mortality and causes of death among forensic psychiatric patients in Alberta: A matched cohort comparison with civil psychiatric and general population groups: Mortalité et causes de décès chez les patients psychiatriques médico-légaux en Alberta : une étude de cohorte appariée comparant des patients psychiatriques civils et des groupes de population générale.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
articles.abstract: IntroductionIndividuals with severe mental illness (SMI) experience increased mortality compared to the general population. Within this group, forensic psychiatric patients represent a subgroup for which mortality has been relatively understudied. Prior literature suggests forensic psychiatric patients experience excess mortality; however, there is limited research comparing mortality among forensic and civil psychiatric patients in a Canadian context. This study examined mortality rates and causes of death among forensic psychiatric patients in Alberta and compared rates with matched comparisons of civil psychiatric and general population cohorts.MethodsThis study employed a retrospective matched cohort design and used data from the Alberta Not Criminally Responsible Project. The sample included 571 individuals found Not Criminally Responsible on Account of Mental Disorder in Alberta. Each forensic psychiatric patient was matched by age and sex to three civil psychiatric patients and three individuals from the general population. Mortality data were obtained through Alberta Health (e.g. Vital Statistics). Descriptive analyses, crude mortality rates, standardized mortality ratios (SMRs), and chi-square tests compared mortality and causes of death across groups.ResultsBoth forensic and civil psychiatric cohorts demonstrated significantly higher mortality compared to the general Albertan population. The overall SMR was 2.73 for the forensic cohort and 2.08 for the civil psychiatric group. Forensic women showed greater mortality than men (SMR = 4.55 compared to 2.53). Both psychiatric groups died more often from unnatural causes, including suicide, while the general population died more often from natural causes.ConclusionMortality among forensic and civil psychiatric patients in Alberta remains elevated compared to the general population, reflecting shared vulnerabilities across psychiatric groups. The higher relative mortality among forensic and civil psychiatric women highlights the need for gender-responsive interventions that integrate both physical and mental health care needs for psychiatric patients and improved care following discharge from hospital.

articles.title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-23 and risk of incident stroke and dementia: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundElevated concentrations of fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23), a hormone involved in bone mineral and vitamin D metabolism, may be associated with risk of stroke and dementia through inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, vessel calcification and stiffness, and axonal degeneration.ObjectiveWe tested the hypothesis that elevated FGF23 is associated with increased risk of dementia and stroke.MethodsFGF23 was measured in serum samples collected in 1990-1992 from 12,391 participants of the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study. Participants were followed through 2019 for incident stroke and dementia. Cox regression was used to examine the associations of FGF23 (in quintiles) with risk of stroke and dementia, with adjustment for demographics, cardiovascular and dementia risk factors, and kidney function.ResultsParticipants (mean 56.9 years; 57% female) were followed a median of 24 years; 1183 developed stroke and 2402 developed dementia. Participants in the highest versus lowest quintile of serum FGF23 were at elevated risk of stroke [HR (95% CI): 1.27 (1.06-1.51)] and dementia [HR: 1.21 (1.06-1.38)] independent of baseline demographics. Associations attenuated with additional adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors [HRstroke: 1.20 (1.00-1.45); HRdementia: 1.17 (1.03-1.35)], and became even weaker after accounting for eGFR [HRstroke: 1.13 (0.94-1.37); HRdementia: 1.14 (1.00-1.31)]. The associations of FGF23 with incident stroke and dementia were not modified by categories of age, sex, race, or eGFR.ConclusionsHigher FGF23 was associated with modestly greater risk of stroke and dementia in this population-based sample, though the association was largely attenuated after adjustment for traditional cardiovascular risk factors and kidney function.

articles.title: Presepsin as an Independent Predictor of Initial Antimicrobial Treatment Failure in Acute Genitourinary Infections.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute genitourinary infections are common and may lead to treatment failure and adverse outcomes. Accordingly, early risk stratification is essential for optimizing antimicrobial therapy. Presepsin is a novel biomarker that rises rapidly after infection onset and may enable earlier assessment than conventional markers such as C-reactive protein (CRP) and procalcitonin (PCT). However, its additional predictive value beyond conventional inflammatory markers remains unclear. This study evaluated the independent and additional predictive value of presepsin for treatment failure compared with conventional markers.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 320 patients with acute genitourinary infections, including 278 with available PCT data. Treatment failure was defined as persistent fever, clinical deterioration (including sepsis or septic shock), need for intensive care, or antibiotic escalation. Clinical variables and laboratory markers (CRP, PCT, lactate, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and presepsin) were analyzed using logistic regression. Predictive models with and without presepsin were constructed, and performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), with comparisons by DeLong's test.

RESULTS: Treatment failure occurred in 126 patients (39.4%). Presepsin levels were significantly higher in the failure group (p < 0.001) and remained independently associated with treatment failure after adjustment (p = 0.03 overall; p = 0.026 in the PCT subgroup), whereas CRP and PCT were not consistently significant. Adding presepsin modestly increased AUC (0.652 to 0.658 overall; 0.654 to 0.663 in the PCT subgroup), without statistical significance. Models incorporating presepsin demonstrated higher specificity while maintaining comparable overall performance to models including conventional inflammatory markers.

CONCLUSION: Presepsin is an independent predictor of treatment failure and shows comparable performance to CRP- and PCT-based models. Despite only modest gains in overall discrimination, it may serve as a useful adjunctive biomarker for early risk stratification.

articles.title: When Hip Pain Is Vascular: Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysmal Lesion in Behçet's Disease Treated with a Covered Stent.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic relapsing systemic vasculitis in which arterial involvement is less common than venous disease but carries substantial rupture risk. Internal iliac artery involvement is rare and may be overlooked because symptoms are often nonspecific. We report a 34-year-old man with established Behçet's disease referred from orthopaedic surgery after 2 to 3 months of right hip and deep gluteal pain initially considered musculoskeletal. Plain hip x-ray was unremarkable. Pelvic imaging demonstrated a right pelvic arterial lesion, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) confirmed a 57 mm saccular aneurysmal lesion arising from the right internal iliac artery. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and perioperative immunosuppression was optimized with rheumatology input. Endovascular repair was performed via contralateral left common femoral access using a 6 × 60 mm self-expanding covered stent graft across the diseased internal iliac segment, without adjunctive coil embolization. Completion angiography showed complete sac exclusion with preserved distal internal iliac flow. Recovery was uneventful. One-month CTA confirmed persistent exclusion and stent-graft patency, and the patient remained clinically asymptomatic at 12 months. This case highlights an orthopaedic mimic and supports carefully selected flow-preserving endovascular repair under immunosuppressive cover, with lifelong imaging surveillance to detect late complications in this inflammatory disease setting.Clinical ImpactInternal iliac artery aneurysmal lesions are rare manifestations of vascular Behçet's disease and may present with hip, buttock or groin pain due to deep pelvic mass effect, leading to initial orthopaedic referral and potential diagnostic delay. This case emphasizes the need to consider a vascular cause in Behçet's disease patients with unexplained persistent pelvic or hip pain, especially when plain radiographs are normal. It also illustrates a flow-preserving endovascular strategy using a covered stent graft to exclude the lesion while maintaining internal iliac artery patency. Because Behçet's disease is an inflammatory vasculitis, technical success alone is insufficient; perioperative immunosuppression and lifelong clinical and imaging surveillance remain central to management.

articles.title: Outcomes After Fetoscopic Myelomeningocele Repair With Preoperative BMI ≥ 35.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 is associated with preterm birth and adverse maternal outcomes following fetoscopic myelomeningocele (MMC) repair.

METHOD: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing fetoscopic MMC repair from 2014 to 2026. Patients with preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 were compared with BMI < 35 kg/m2. The primary outcome was preterm birth before 37 weeks' gestation. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery, maternal complications, and procedure-related risks. Comparisons were performed using bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 209 patients, 21 (10%) had preoperative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2. Rates of preterm birth before 37 weeks were similar in patients with BMI ≥ 35 versus < 35 kg/m2 (52% vs. 49%, p = 0.80), as was gestational age at delivery (35.9 vs. 37.0 weeks, p = 0.70). BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with preterm birth after multivariable adjustment (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.37-2.62). Skin-to-skin operative time, CO2 insufflation time, and total fetoscopic time were comparable between the groups. No differences were observed in the rates of PPROM, placental abruption, intraamniotic infection, or maternal perioperative complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Pre-operative BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2 was not associated with differences in preterm birth, gestational age at delivery, operative characteristics, or maternal perioperative morbidity following fetoscopic MMC repair.

articles.title: Montelukast sodium in preventing oxygen requirements at day 28 in preterm infants: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: BackgroundEvaluating the efficacy and safety of oral montelukast in preventing oxygen requirement at day 28 of birth in preterm infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit through a randomized trial with open-label treatment administration and blinded outcome assessment.MethodsTarget Population: 92 preterm infants admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Units of four hospitals.

INTERVENTION: Daily oral administration of 1 mg/kg montelukast.

PRIMARY OUTCOME: Incidence of Oxygen requirement on days 14 and 28 of life.ResultsReduction in Oxygen requirement: Significantly lower in the intervention group (31.7%) compared to the control group (55%). Lung Disease Severity: Pulmonary Severity Score was significantly lower in the montelukast group on days 14 and 28. Safety Profile: No serious drug-related adverse effects were reported.

SECONDARY OUTCOMES: No statistically significant differences were observed regarding mortality or length of hospital stay between the two groups.ConclusionPreventive administration of montelukast in high-risk preterm infants appears to be safe and effective in reducing the incidence of oxygen requirement at day 28/discharge.

articles.title: Impact of Patient-Reported Allergies on Clinical Outcomes Following Surgical Treatment of Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPatient-reported allergies (PRAs) have been associated with worse outcomes after several orthopaedic procedures, including total hip and knee arthroplasty, but their effect after surgical treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT) is unknown. This study investigated whether the number of PRAs is associated with functional outcomes and postoperative complications after surgical treatment of IAT.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 28 patients (mean age, 54.8 years; 28.6% male; mean follow-up, 15.9 months) who underwent surgical treatment of IAT, stratified by number of PRAs: 0 (n = 10), 1 to 5 (n = 11), and >5 (n = 7). Primary outcomes were the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain, and Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary (PCS-12, MCS-12) scores at the most recent follow-up; SF-12 scores were available for 19 patients. Secondary outcomes were postoperative complications. Multivariable linear regression was used to adjust for baseline differences between groups.ResultsMedian FAAM scores were 60.0, 72.0, and 61.0 in the 0, 1 to 5, and >5 PRA groups (P = .87), and median VAS scores were 3.5, 2.0, and 3.0 (P = .47). PCS-12 (39.2, 37.4, and 51.6; P = .30) and MCS-12 (56.1, 52.3, and 56.5; P = .76) did not differ significantly. Hypertension and asthma were more prevalent in the >5 PRA group (P = .003 and P = .037). Achilles tendon rupture occurred in 2 (20.0%), 1 (9.1%), and 0 patients (P = .41) and 1 wound dehiscence occurred in the 1 to 5 group (P = .45); complication rates did not differ significantly among groups. After adjusting for ASA class, hypertension, and asthma, the number of PRAs was not significantly associated with any patient-reported outcome, although confidence intervals were wide.ConclusionIn this retrospective cohort, no statistically significant association was identified between the number of PRAs and functional outcomes or complication rates following surgical management of IAT. Given the limited sample size and heterogeneous allergy profiles, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.Level of Evidence:Level III: Retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Antimicrobial stewardship and resistance in intensive care units in the UK: a prospective national audit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Principles of effective antimicrobial stewardship include prescription of empiric therapy based on the most likely causative organism, with medication review within 72 h. Adherence to best practice in UK ICUs is unknown and the aim of this study was to evaluate patient- and unit-level antimicrobial use in UK ICUs.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective national audit of antimicrobial use in adults (aged ≥ 18 y) admitted to ICUs in the UK and Isle of Man with a point-prevalence survey. Subsequently, we collected longitudinal data on review of therapy and antimicrobial resistance in a subset of patients who had commenced therapy within the previous 3 days.

RESULTS: We studied 2626 patients from 154/292 (52.7%) ICUs. Antimicrobial therapy was prescribed in 1592 (60.6%) patients. Of 2116 empiric antimicrobial orders, 1592 (75.2%) were compliant with unit-level guidelines. For non-compliant orders, 253 (12.0% of all empiric orders) were discussed with infection specialists and 69 (3.3%) provided justification for off-guidance therapy, but 202 (9.5%) were prescribed outside guidance without justification or discussion with infection specialists. Guideline-compliant review within 72 h of prescription took place in 1488/1606 (92.7%) eligible medication orders. A pre-specified stop or review date was strongly associated with antimicrobial review within 72 h (adjusted OR 9.3, 95%CI 5.4-16.2).

DISCUSSION: We have benchmarked critical care antimicrobial stewardship and guideline compliance across the UK. We recommend that pre-specified review dates are added to all prescriptions, as the most important determinant of review identified in our audit. Future work should include national stewardship audit cycles to benchmark practice and inform quality improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Cerebellar optogenetic stimulation restores motor cortex activity and behaviour after stroke.
articles.abstract: Stroke causes severe motor deficits, but functional recovery can occur through neural circuit reorganization in areas adjacent to and remote from the infarct. Optogenetic stimulation can modulate neuronal activity and improve recovery in experimental models, yet the population-level cortical dynamics underlying these effects remain poorly understood. The lateral cerebellar nucleus projects to the cortex via the dentatothalamocortical pathway and represents a promising target for remote neuromodulation after stroke. We performed longitudinal one-photon calcium imaging of ipsilesional primary motor cortex layer V neurons in awake, behaving mice (n = 13) following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion. Mice received optogenetic stimulation of the contralesional lateral cerebellar nucleus using CaMKII-driven Channelrhodopsin-2 on post-stroke days 5 through 14. Stimulation-treated and non-stimulated stroke mice were compared across behavioral and neural activity measures for up to 28 days post-stroke. Stroke significantly reduced ipsilesional motor cortex population activity during the subacute phase, with decreased calcium peak frequency (p < 0.001) and amplitude (p = 0.004). Reduced frequency was strongly associated with lesion size at post-stroke day 6 (r² = 0.88, p < 0.001), and reduced amplitude was similarly associated with lesion size at post-stroke day 9 (r² = 0.39, p = 0.022). Cerebellar stimulation counteracted these deficits, significantly increasing both frequency (p = 0.017) and amplitude (p < 0.001) and improving behavioral recovery on the rotating beam task (p = 0.027). Critically, in stimulated animals, motor cortex activity was no longer coupled to lesion size, indicating that stimulation decoupled cortical dynamics from injury severity. Early post-stroke functional connection density among motor cortex neurons predicted long-term behavioral outcome in non-stimulated animals (r² = 0.50, p = 0.033), but this relationship was abolished by stimulation, suggesting that cerebellar stimulation reshaped the recovery trajectory independently of initial network disruption. Stroke also shifted neuronal populations toward minimally active states, and stimulation preserved a higher proportion of moderately active neurons (p = 0.029). These findings define population-level changes in peri-lesional motor cortex after stroke at cellular resolution and demonstrate that cerebellar optogenetic stimulation counteracts stroke-induced cortical dysfunction, decouples recovery from lesion burden, and promotes functional recovery.

articles.title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.
authors: EMBRACE study investigators (to be indexed on PubMed)
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.

METHODS: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.

CONCLUSION: Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

articles.title: Infection Following Achilles Tendon Repair: A Systematic Review of Pathogens and Risk Factors.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAchilles tendon rupture is a common injury in athletes. Ankle surgeries have been reported to have a higher incidence of infection than other orthopaedic surgical sites. Purpose. The purpose of this study is to systematically review the literature regarding infections following Achilles tendon repair and identify common pathogens and risk factors associated with this outcome.MethodsAn electronic systematic review was conducted via a PubMed and Cochrane search, evaluating studies published before September 2023 and reporting on Achilles repair infection. Primary factors assessed include causative microorganisms, time to infection, treatment, and risk factors.ResultsThe greatest risk factors were open wounds before surgery (P < .001), obesity (P < .0001), and age (P = .03). Most infections occurred within the first 8 weeks.ConclusionStaphylococcus and Streptococcus were the most common causative agents of infection, followed by Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas. Infections generally began within the first 8 weeks postoperatively, ranging from 10 days to 6 months. Statistically significant risk factors for postoperative Achilles infection include obesity, comorbid medical conditions, smoking, tourniquet time, blood loss, and patient age.Level of Evidence:Level I, Systematic Review.

Physiologic subtypes of gestational glucose intolerance and risk of future maternal prediabetes or diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational glucose intolerance (GGI), an abnormal initial gestational diabetes (GDM) screening test, conveys an increased risk of future diabetes, even when GDM is not present. We aimed to determine if GGI subtypes, classified according to the underlying mechanism of hyperglycemia, are at differential risk for future prediabetes or diabetes.

METHODS: We defined GGI as glucose loading test 1-hour glucose ≥ 140 mg/dL at > 22 weeks' gestation with a subsequent oral glucose tolerance test that did not meet criteria for GDM diagnosis. We applied homeostasis model assessment (HOMA-2) to fasting glucose and insulin at 16-20 weeks' gestation and classified pregnancies with GGI into subtypes based on whether they had insulin resistance (HOMA-2S <50th percentile), insulin deficiency (HOMA-2B <50th percentile), or both (mixed). We assessed the future risk of prediabetes/diabetes (HbA1c ≥ 5.7% at ≥ 3 months after delivery) in each GGI subtype, compared to pregnancies with normal glucose tolerance, using covariate-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Of 747 pregnancies, there were 123 with GGI: 51.2% insulin resistant, 26.8% insulin deficient, 17.9% mixed, and 4.1% uncategorized. Over a median of 15.9 years of follow-up, 36.4% (N=272) developed prediabetes or diabetes. All GGI subtypes were associated with an increased risk of future prediabetes/diabetes compared to normal glucose tolerance controls: insulin resistant adjusted hazard ratio (aHR)=1.80 (95% confidence interval: 1.22-2.65, p=0.003), insulin deficient aHR=2.15 (1.35-3.42, p=0.001) and mixed aHR=2.07 (1.02-4.20, p=0.045).

CONCLUSIONS: GGI confers an increased risk of future maternal prediabetes/diabetes, regardless of the mechanism underlying glucose intolerance during pregnancy.

articles.title: Past, present and future of Estetrol (E4); a natural fetal estrogen for human use.
articles.abstract: Estetrol (E4) is a natural estrogen produced by the fetal liver with a distinctive pharmacologic profile separating it from other natural and synthetic estrogens. Encompassing 25 years of research and development, this review summarizes the history, biochemistry, pharmacology, clinical development, and potential future applications of E4. Essential features of E4 are (1) its high oral bioavailability, long half-life and minimal binding to sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), enabling once-daily oral use, and (2) the limited effects on liver function, especially on hemostatic factors, resulting in a lower risk of venous thromboembolism compared to other natural and synthetic estrogens. Estetrol is further characterized as a natural estrogen with selective tissue activity, with a limited impact on breast tissue and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters, while preserving efficacy including bone mass protection. Estetrol therefore has the potential for a markedly improved safety profile. Clinically, the E4/drospirenone (DRSP) combined oral contraceptive (COC) is available worldwide since 2022 and provides effective contraception, a predictable bleeding profile, and a favorable tolerability profile. In phase 2 and 3 studies in postmenopausal women, oral E4 improves vasomotor symptoms, vaginal and urogenital complaints, and quality of life and wellbeing. Ongoing research is exploring wider uses, including combination with the oral GnRH antagonist relugolix for a COC with a focus on the perimenopausal transition and possible applications of E4 in gynecology, endocrinology, obstetrics, neurology and oncology, especially the treatment of advanced breast and prostate cancer.

articles.title: Rhabdomyolysis in Ugandan children with severe malaria.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rhabdomyolysis is a serious clinical syndrome characterized by skeletal muscle injury, release of creatine kinase (CK) and increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). Few studies have examined rhabdomyolysis in severe pediatric malaria.

METHODS: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study. We examined the association of rhabdomyolysis with mortality (Cox proportional hazards models, complete case analysis and multiple imputation by chained equations). We also examined putative mediators of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality.

RESULTS: Of 600 patients in the cohort (median age 2 years, 44% female), 512 (85%) had at least one CK measurement. The median CK was 120 U/L (IQR 44-490) and 73/512 patients (14%) had rhabdomyolysis (CK>1000 U/L). There were 44 deaths in the cohort (case fatality rate 7.3%). Rhabdomyolysis was associated with an unadjusted 2.5-fold increased hazard of mortality (95%CI 1.1-6.1, p=0.038). This estimate remained statistically significant after adjustment for age and sex and after multiple imputation for missing CK values. The odds of AKI (OR 2.0, 95%CI 1.2-3.6, p=0.0085) and hyperkalemia (OR 2.7, 95%CI 1.3-5.5, p=0.0049) were higher among patients with rhabdomyolysis. AKI and hyperkalemia attenuated the effect of rhabdomyolysis in multivariable models. We estimated that the proportion of rhabdomyolysis-associated mortality risk mediated by AKI and hyperkalemia was 23% (95% UI 12-41%) and 18% (95% UI 12-29%), respectively.

CONCLUSION: Rhabdomyolysis is common in children with severe malaria and is associated with elevated mortality. Rhabdomyolysis may be a marker of disease severity or may contribute to the pathogenesis of fatal malaria (e.g., via AKI and hyperkalemia).

articles.title: Sarcoidosis Initially Misdiagnosed as Culture-Negative Pulmonary Tuberculosis Presenting as Dialysis-Requiring Acute Kidney Injury: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disease that commonly involves the lungs. Renal involvement is uncommon, most often manifesting as granulomatous interstitial nephritis (GIN), which can progress to acute kidney injury (AKI). The clinical and radiological overlap with tuberculosis (TB), particularly culture-negative pulmonary TB, poses a significant risk of misdiagnosis. We report a 78-year-old male who presented with dialysis-requiring AKI. Renal biopsy demonstrated non-caseating GIN, and acid-fast staining of renal tissue was negative. Three years earlier, he had been diagnosed with culture-negative pulmonary TB despite repeatedly negative sputum smears, cultures, and Xpert MTB/RIF testing, and received 14-month anti-TB therapy. Serum creatinine and pulmonary imaging had fluctuated with glucocorticoid administration rather than anti-TB therapy. Hypercalcemia with suppressed parathyroid hormone, elevated serum angiotensin-converting enzyme, hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, iritis, and characteristic glucocorticoid responsiveness supported a probable diagnosis of sarcoidosis. Renal recovery followed glucocorticoid initiation, with dialysis discontinuation, normalization of serum calcium, resolution of lymphadenopathy, and stable renal function at 9-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing sarcoidosis from culture-negative pulmonary TB in endemic regions and the importance of renal biopsy, multisystem evaluation, and assessment of treatment response in unexplained tubulointerstitial nephritis with pulmonary involvement.

articles.title: Brain-derived exosomes mediate antibody-resistant PRV transmission and blood-brain barrier disruption.
articles.abstract: Exosomes are critical mediators of virus-host interactions and can transfer viral and host components that influence viral replication and tissue injury. Pseudorabies virus (PRV), a neurotropic alphaherpesvirus, has been reported to disrupt the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and cause severe neurological disease. However, the role of exosomes in PRV-induced neuropathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we systematically investigated the functional role of brain-derived exosomes generated during PRV infection. Exosomes were isolated from PRV-challenged and mock-treated mouse brains using differential ultracentrifugation coupled with cluster of differentiation (CD)9-/CD63-/CD81-based immunomagnetic enrichment. Purity was confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and western blotting, which excluded intact virion contamination. Notably, multimarker enrichment yielded higher recovery than CD63 alone. PRV-associated exosomes contained viral genomic DNA and glycoproteins and mediated efficient viral transmission in porcine kidney (PK)-15 cells. In a Transwell-based BBB model composed of bEnd.3 endothelial cells and astrocyte type I clone (C8-D1A), these exosomes induced significant barrier dysfunction. Consistently, intracranial administration of exosomes from PRV-infected mice resulted in neurological deficits and increased BBB permeability in vivo. Together, our findings identify brain-derived exosomes as previously underappreciated mediators of PRV dissemination and neurovascular injury. These findings reveal an exosome-associated pathway that may contribute to PRV neuropathogenesis.

articles.title: Managing environmental enteropathy among Egyptian infants and children with growth faltering.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental enteropathy (EE) is an acquired subclinical inflammation of the small bowel mucosa, leading to reduced nutrient absorption and increased intestinal permeability. There are currently no universally accepted protocols for the diagnosis and treatment of EE.

OBJECTIVE: The primary aim of this clinical trial was to assess the prevalence of EE among children with faltering growth (FG). Determination of the dietary requirements in pediatric FG with EE and highlighting the histopathologic changes in the small intestine in such conditions were the secondary objectives.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: The current study recruited 200 patients (their age range was 6-58 months) diagnosed as GF at the Pediatric Clinical Nutrition Clinic, Children`s Hospital, Faculty of Medicine, Ain Shams University (Cairo, Egypt), during the period from April 2022 till June 2023. The first phase of the study was a cross sectional interventional one where all patients underwent nutritional rehabilitation using diet regimen including polymeric milk formula. Patients whose weight z score was still below - 2 SD for age and sex after 12 weeks were considered as non-responders and were enrolled in the second phase, when esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and mucosal biopsies were done. In the latter phase, patients with EE received nutritional rehabilitation regimen using peptide-based milk formula with assessment of anthropometric measurements after 8 weeks of follow up.

RESULTS: Out of the studied cases, 170 were responders, and 30 were non-responders, 24 of the non-responders underwent EGD with biopsies and all were diagnosed as EE with prevalence of 12% among the studied patients with GF as the least possible prevalence. Total histology scores of the EE fell between those of the controls and celiac disease reference samples with cut off values > 3 and ≤ 14 for EE, ≤ 3 for controls and > 14 for celiac disease. There was a significant increase in weight and height z scores among patients of EE on peptide-based formula compared to polymeric formula.

CONCLUSION: EE isn`t uncommon and should be suspected when provision of catch-up nutrients can`t correct FG. Peptide-based formula has a possible beneficial effect on growth of patients with EE.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The clinical trial was registered at Protocol Registration and Results System with number NCT06497907 (12/07/2024).

articles.title: Microplastic contamination in spotted babylon (Babylonia areolata) from the artisanal fisheries along the eastern coast of Thailand.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are a serious global concern due to their potential risks to the environment, wildlife, and human health. The ingestion of MPs by organisms, such as marine invertebrates, can lead to their transfer through the trophic food chain, ultimately impacting human health. The present study investigates the quantity, shape, color, and polymer type of microplastics found in both the whole soft tissues and external surfaces of the spotted babylon (Babylonia areolata) collected in January (Northeast monsoon), April (transition period), and August (Southwest monsoon) 2024 from four sampling sites along the coast of Rayong Province, Thailand. The results revealed a total microplastic detection rate of 73.9% from the external body, with 1.14 ± 0.40 particles/individual, and 61.9% from the internal body contained at least one MP particle, with 1.01 ± 0.47 particles/individual. The overall MP contamination showed significant seasonal differences, with the highest contamination observed in August. The study also demonstrated a significant positive correlation between microplastic contamination and shellfish size. The most abundant MP shape was fiber, primarily in blue, followed by fragments and films. FT-IR analysis identified several plastic polymers, with the most common being PET, PES, and PP. Fibers were the predominant MP shape, followed by fragments and films, while PET, PES, and PP were the major polymer types identified by FT-IR. The predominance of PET-fibers suggests a potential contribution from textile-related sources. Nevertheless, MP levels in spotted babylon from Rayong Province were lower than those reported in previous studies. Our findings highlight the potential for MP transfer to humans through seafood consumption, raising concerns for food safety, and emphasize the need for regular monitoring of edible marine organisms and effective plastic waste management policies in the region.

articles.title: CCTA-derived anatomical features and exploratory risk stratification of severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery narrowing for non-true left main bifurcation lesions.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Provisional stenting is recommended in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-true left main bifurcation lesions (LMBLs); however, unexpected severe stent-jailed left circumflex coronary artery (LCX) narrowing is a clinical concern, and its prediction remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing following provisional stenting for non-true LMBLs without significant LCX lesions and to derive an exploratory risk score using coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA). This was a multicenter retrospective observational study that enrolled patients who underwent CCTA before PCI for non-true LMBLs with provisional stenting from December 2019 to May 2024. Quantitative CCTA analysis of LMBL was performed, and severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing, defined as angiographic stenosis ≥90%, was assessed. Anatomical features associated with LCX narrowing were identified using multivariable analysis, and a CCTA-derived exploratory risk score was derived. Overall, 109 patients were recruited, 16 (14.7%) of whom had severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing. Multivariable analysis identified the following parameters as associated with LCX narrowing: left anterior descending artery-LCX vessel angle ≤86°, area stenosis (AS) of the distal LM (LMd) ≥54%, AS of the ostial LCX ≥63%, and calcium thickness of the LMd ≥0.5 mm. An exploratory risk score based on these four features showed a stepwise increase in the incidence of severe LCX narrowing, with a C-statistic of 0.877. CCTA identified anatomical features associated with severe stent-jailed LCX narrowing following provisional stenting. An exploratory risk score was derived from these features.

articles.title: Separating tracer biology from regional detectability in atrial molecular PET.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging

articles.title: Integrated myocardial work phenotyping in professional football players and non-professional comparators.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To explore integrated cardiac profiles in professional football players and non-professional comparators and assess their sensitivity to demographic, body-size and haemodynamic differences. This cross-sectional analysis included 49 professional players (39 men, 10 women) and 48 hospital-staff comparators recruited as healthy volunteers (31 men, 17 women). Principal component analysis (PCA) of 28 standardised clinical, echocardiographic, deformation and myocardial-work measures preceded k-means clustering without study-group labels. Sensitivity analyses addressed age, sex, blood pressure, body-size indexing and exclusion of myocardial work while retaining global longitudinal strain (GLS). Five components explained 62.2% of variance. The three-profile solution had a silhouette coefficient of 0.252 and mean resampling adjusted Rand index (ARI) of 0.820. Profile A contained 55 participants, including 41 players (74.5%); profiles B and C contained 4/17 and 4/25 players. Profile A combined larger chambers with preserved global work efficiency; profile B had higher systolic and diastolic blood pressure, greater wasted work and lower efficiency. Age-adjusted and jointly age-, sex- and blood-pressure-adjusted analyses yielded agreement ARIs of 0.448 and 0.097. Without myocardial work, 95/97 participants and all 49 players retained profile membership (ARI 0.950). Integrated phenotyping identified overlapping cardiac profiles associated with professional football, principally reflecting chamber size, demographics and loading conditions. Myocardial-work indices described pressure-strain and efficiency patterns but had little additional influence on profile allocation beyond the remaining measures, including GLS. Their incremental clinical utility requires external validation.

articles.title: Losartan use, left ventricular function and remodeling in hypertensive patients with aortic stenosis: the HYTAS prospective comparative cohort study.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hypertension is highly prevalent in patients with aortic stenosis (AS) and contributes to adverse left ventricular (LV) remodeling. We investigated the association between losartan treatment and LV remodeling and function in hypertensive patients with mild-to-moderate AS.

METHODS: In this prospective comparative cohort study, 18 AS patients receiving losartan were individually matched with 18 controls from the PROGRESSA cohort not receiving renin-angiotensin system inhibitors. Patients underwent echocardiographic assessment at baseline and two years. Between-group changes were compared within matched pairs, with baseline-adjusted sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: All losartan-treated patients completed follow-up without permanent treatment discontinuation or treatment-related serious adverse events. Systolic blood pressure decreased significantly within the losartan group, but the between-group difference in blood pressure changes was not significant (p = 0.17). Losartan was associated with a more favorable evolution of absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS), which persisted after baseline adjustment (adjusted between-group difference: +2.34%; 95% confidence interval 0.18-4.49; p = 0.04). Although LV end-diastolic diameter and relative wall thickness showed significant differences in unadjusted longitudinal analyses, these differences were no longer significant after baseline adjustment (p = 0.40 and p = 0.30, respectively). No significant between-group differences were observed in LV ejection fraction.
