CONCLUSION: In this small, non-randomized prospective study of hypertensive patients with mild-to-moderate AS, losartan treatment was associated with a more favorable evolution of LV GLS over two years. Associations with LV remodeling were not significant after baseline adjustment. These exploratory findings do not establish causality or treatment safety and warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Coronary artery calcium burden and coronary CT angiography evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To investigate the association between coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) evaluability in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. This retrospective single-center study included 65 patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis who underwent coronary artery calcium scoring and CCTA for evaluation of suspected coronary artery disease. The right coronary artery, left anterior descending artery, and left circumflex artery were independently assessed by two blinded observers using a four-point image-quality scale. Arteries scored 3 or 4 were considered evaluable, and limited evaluability was defined as at least one non-evaluable major coronary artery. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation, established CAC-score categories, receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable logistic regression. The median total CAC score was 671 (interquartile range, 251-1,774). All three major coronary arteries were evaluable in 26 patients (40.0%), whereas 39 (60.0%) had limited evaluability. Median CAC scores increased stepwise as the number of evaluable arteries decreased from three to zero (162.5, 677.0, 1,663.0, and 2,180.0; Spearman's ρ = -0.608, P < 0.001). CAC score ≥ 400 was associated with limited evaluability (odds ratio, 6.30; 95% CI, 2.10-18.90; P < 0.001). The AUC was 0.831 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.723-0.925). After adjustment for age and sex, each approximate doubling of CAC score was associated with higher odds of limited evaluability (adjusted odds ratio, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.40-2.88; P < 0.001). Increasing CAC burden was associated with a progressive reduction in CCTA evaluability in patients undergoing hemodialysis. CAC scoring may help anticipate technical limitations of CCTA and inform coronary imaging strategy.

articles.title: Recognition and management of semaglutide overdose and intoxi​cation: a narrative review for clinicians.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Semaglutide has moved within a few years from a niche glucose-lowering agent to one of the most widely dispensed medicines in high-income countries, and reported excessive exposures have risen in parallel. This review sets out a practical framework for recognising and managing semaglutide overdose, and distinguishes recommendations supported by published overdose evidence from those resting on pharmacological reasoning or general toxicology practice.

EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to July 2026 for English-language human studies of semaglutide pharmacology, safety and excessive exposure, supplemented by reference lists and regulatory agency publications. Randomised trials and meta-analyses were prioritised for statements about incidence; case reports, case series and poison centre or pharmacovigilance analyses informed the description of the overdose syndrome itself.

RESULTS: The dominant toxidrome is gastrointestinal and protracted, with nausea, repetitive vomiting, abdominal pain and anorexia persisting for days to weeks because the terminal elimination half-life approaches one week. Volume depletion, electrolyte derangement and acute kidney injury drive serious outcome. Hypoglycaemia is uncommon in isolated overdose because insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent, but it matters with concomitant insulin or sulfonylurea therapy, in non-diabetic individuals, and where a falsified product contains insulin. Pancreatitis, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, ileus and delayed gastric emptying with aspiration risk are less frequent but potentially life-threatening. In the cases reported to date, most exposures follow therapeutic error, unit-conversion confusion with compounded multi-dose vials, and acquisition outside regulated supply.

CONCLUSION: Management is supportive and anticipatory. There is no antidote, and extracorporeal removal is futile given extensive albumin binding. Priorities are aggressive antiemesis, fluid and electrolyte correction, glucose monitoring proportionate to risk, full-stomach airway precautions, and observation that respects the drug's long half-life. Prevention through device design, dispensing standards, patient education and regulatory action is likely to yield greater benefit than any therapeutic manoeuvre.

articles.title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use.

METHODS: In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use.

RESULTS: Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSION: Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

articles.title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD.

METHODS: A MAFLD mouse model was established by administration of a high-fat diet. Serum biochemical parameters were measured, and liver histopathological injury was assessed by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson staining. Hepatocyte apoptosis was evaluated using TUNEL staining. Oxidative stress markers were quantified using ELISA, flow cytometry, and DCFH-DA staining, respectively. Cell viability and apoptosis were assessed by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay and flow cytometry. Intracellular Fe²⁺ and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels were measured using commercial assay kits. The acetylation level of the SREBP1 promoter was determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation.

RESULTS: BGN4 significantly alleviated liver injury, oxidative stress, and hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD mice. BGN4 treatment markedly increased the level of the intestinal metabolite 6-HNA. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that 6-HNA exerted a protective effect against palmitic acid (PA)-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress. Mechanistically, 6-HNA activated Nrf2 signaling, thereby suppressing the SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis through reduction of p300-mediated histone acetylation. Rescue experiments showed that treatment with ML-385 or overexpression of SREBP1 reversed the protective effects of 6-HNA on PA-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress.

CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that the protective effects of BGN4 against hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress in MAFLD are likely associated with the upregulation of intestinal metabolite 6-HNA, which appears to modulate the Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 signaling axis, thereby supporting the therapeutic potential of the "probiotic-metabolite-liver" regulatory axis in MAFLD.

articles.title: Alternative multiport robotic platforms versus da Vinci in colorectal cancer surgery: a systematic review and platform-stratified meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Alternative multiport robotic systems from manufacturers other than Intuitive Surgical are being adopted for colorectal cancer procedures, yet how their outcomes compare with the established da Vinci platform remains unclear. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and CENTRAL were searched through August 2026 for randomised trials and comparative observational studies of alternative multiport robots versus da Vinci for colorectal cancer surgery. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences were stratified by platform and resection site; RoB 2, ROBINS-I and GRADE were applied. Twelve studies (one randomised trial; 1,144 participants: 557 alternative platform, 587 da Vinci) evaluated six platforms; hinotori was assessed in six studies and four platforms in one study each. Five cohorts were at serious risk of bias. Console time was 29.38 min longer with alternative platforms (95% CI 17.87 to 40.89; low certainty; mainly hinotori). Total operative time was 20.04 min longer (95% CI 8.81 to 31.28), but heterogeneity and small-study effects made this very uncertain (trim-and-fill estimate 7.24 min, - 4.20 to 18.69). Morbidity estimates were imprecise: Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complications RR 1.17 (0.91 to 1.51), grade ≥ III RR 0.86 (0.44 to 1.69), and anastomotic leak RR 1.35 (0.47 to 3.89; 17 events). Certainty was very low for all other outcomes. Alternative multiport robots appear feasible for colorectal cancer surgery but may prolong console time. Their comparative safety and pathological quality relative to da Vinci remain uncertain, and current data do not establish equivalence or non-inferiority. Adequately powered, platform-specific prospective comparisons with predefined non-inferiority margins are required.

articles.title: Patient perception of robotic-assisted spine surgery.
articles.abstract: Patient behaviors related to pursuing robotic-assisted spine surgery remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated patients' perceptions of robotic-assisted spine surgery and behaviors related to seeking robotic-assisted care. We surveyed 116 adult spine patients at initial consultation (n = 101) or postoperative follow-up after confirmed robotic-assisted surgery (n = 15). Questions assessed perceived attributes of robotic-assisted versus traditional surgery, comfort, surgical preference, willingness to recommend robotic spine surgery, perceived robotic involvement, and whether patients had actively sought surgeons using robotics. Analyses included descriptive statistics, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and exploratory subgroup comparisons. Patients perceived robotic-assisted surgery as more accurate (65%) and less invasive (63%), with smaller incisions (74%) and shorter surgery (53%) and recovery times (46%). Robotic and traditional surgery were most commonly perceived as comparable in pain (56%) and radiation exposure (51%). 69% believed a robot could perform most or all of the surgery; 60% would recommend robotic spine surgery, and 56% were somewhat or very comfortable with robotics. For otherwise identical surgeries, 73% (85/116, 95% CI 64.6-80.5%) reported no preference, 16% preferred robotic assistance, and 11% preferred surgery without robotics. Of 94 yes/no respondents, 6 (6.4%, 95% CI 3.0-13.2%) reported actively seeking a surgeon using robotics. The other 22 selected "Not Applicable." Although perceptions were generally favorable, most patients had no preference regarding robotic assistance, and few reported actively seeking surgeons using robotics. Robotic availability was not a prominent stated selection factor in this small, single-center sample.

articles.title: Short-term postoperative outcomes of endoscopic treatment versus robot-assisted pyeloplasty for ureteropelvic junction obstruction.
articles.abstract: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction may cause hydronephrosis, infection, and renal dysfunction. Pyeloplasty remains the reconstructive standard, whereas endoscopic treatment is a less invasive alternative. Long-term outcomes of endoscopic treatment and pyeloplasty for ureteropelvic junction obstruction have already been addressed. However, contemporary multi-institutional comparisons of their short-term perioperative outcomes remain limited. This retrospective study compares 30-day postoperative outcomes between endoscopic ureteropelvic junction treatment and robot-assisted pyeloplasty in adults using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. Adults undergoing endoscopic ureteropelvic junction treatment or robot-assisted pyeloplasty were identifed from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database (2022-2024). The prinicipal CPT code 52,345 identified endoscopic treatment cases, while robot-assisted pyeloplasty cases were sampled from the minimally invasive pyeloplasty cohort under CPT code 50,544, using the robotic variable. The primary endpoint was a composite of any 30-day non-wound postoperative complication. Secondary endpoints included the broader postoperative complication composite, readmission, reoperation, operative time, and length of stay. Multivariable regression models evaluated associations between surgical approach and outcomes after adjustment for relevant covariates. The cohort included 1,133 patients (93 endoscopic treatment; 1,040 robot-assisted pyeloplasty). Overall, 79 patients (7%) experienced at least one non-wound postoperative complication with similar rates between endoscopic treatment and robot-assisted pyeloplasty (4.3% vs. 7.2%, p = 0.291). After adjustment, procedure group was not significantly associated with non-wound complications (aOR 0.491, 95% CI 0.173-1.393; p = 0.181). The same applied for readmission (7.5% vs. 5.1%, p = 0.329) and unplanned reoperation (1.1% vs. 2.0%; p = 1.000). The endoscopic-treatment group had lower odds of hospitalization beyond the day of surgery (aOR 0.043, 95% CI 0.025-0.075; p < 0.001) and a shorter adjusted median operative time (difference - 127.1 min, 95% CI - 143.3 to - 110.8; p < 0.001). In this multi-institutional ACS NSQIP cohort, the endoscopic treatment of UPJO was associated with shorter operative time and hospital stay. No significant differences in 30-day postoperative complications, readmission, reoperation and mortality rates were detected between endoscopic UPJ treatment and robotic pyeloplasty. However, the small cohort and limited events preclude conclusions regarding equivalent safety. NSQIP does not capture long-term functional outcomes or treatment durability.

articles.title: Chronopharmaceutics of In Situ Gel-Based Drug Delivery Systems in the Treatment of Nocturnal Asthma: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nocturnal asthma (NA) is characterized by airway resistance and inflammation that peak between 02:00 and 06:00, driven by circadian fluctuations in vagal tone, cortisol, and inflammatory mediators. Conventional inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β₂-agonist combinations and oral therapies may not reliably cover this window because of suboptimal adherence, heterogeneous lung deposition, and variable systemic exposure after oral dosing. In situ gels (ISGs), which are liquids that gel after administration, have been proposed as platforms for sustained nasal or pulmonary drug delivery.

OBJECTIVE: To review the circadian mechanisms of NA, the formulation science of stimuli-responsive ISGs, and the evidence for their use as chronotherapeutic systems in NA.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes literature on the molecular clock and circadian pathophysiology of asthma, polymer selection and gelation mechanisms, nasal and pulmonary delivery, pharmacokinetics and safety, and manufacturing and regulatory considerations. Evidence was classified by type (in vitro or ex vivo, animal, computational, or human) and as established, preclinical, or hypothetical.

RESULTS: Thermosensitive poloxamers, pH-responsive carbopol/chitosan systems, ion-activated gellan gum, and enzyme-degradable matrices can form mucoadhesive depots, but their gelation behaviour, mechanical stability, mucociliary clearance, and tolerability depend on formulation composition and test conditions. Hybrid architectures (nanoparticle-embedded, nanomicelle-forming, and mesoporous silica ISGs) may allow release kinetics to be separated from cellular uptake. Sustained release over several hours has been shown for gel formulations in vitro. No study has evaluated a chronotherapeutic ISG in nocturnal asthma, and benefits for airway function and adherence remain undemonstrated. Afternoon or evening dosing of inhaled corticosteroids has clinical trial support and is the main alternative chronotherapeutic strategy. Data on repeated nightly dosing and on bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration are lacking.

CONCLUSION: Chronotherapeutic ISGs are a plausible but untested approach to nocturnal asthma. Priorities for translation are studies that measure drug exposure across the 02:00-06:00 window, bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration, and the safety of repeated nightly dosing. Regulatory, manufacturing, biomarker-responsive, and digital-integration concepts remain exploratory.

articles.title: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Upper limb dysfunction (pain, reduced shoulder mobility and strength, activity limitation) is common after breast cancer treatment, with or without breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) has been proposed to improve upper limb function and range of motion (ROM). This systematic review evaluates PNF for upper limb dysfunction in women treated for breast cancer, analyzing women with and without BCRL separately.

METHODS: The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement was followed. Four databases were searched without date restrictions. Randomized or quasi-randomized English-language trials of PNF-containing interventions in women treated for breast cancer were included. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators. In women without BCRL, single trials reported improvements in ROM, strength and function. Risk of bias was low in one trial, high in one and of some concern in four; certainty of evidence was low or very low.

CONCLUSION: PNF may be a promising component of multimodal rehabilitation for upper limb dysfunction after breast cancer treatment; its independent effectiveness and its effects on BCRL remain unproven, and in women with BCRL it should complement, not replace, decongestive treatment. Trials in women with confirmed BCRL and standardized PNF protocols are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42025641774, registered on 2 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).

articles.title: Effects of Dietary Supplements on Resolution Biology.
articles.journal: Current topics in microbiology and immunology
articles.abstract: Dietary supplements are consumed by up to 50-75% of the US population with omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) being one of the most consumed. These supplements can exert diverse and potential biologically beneficial effects on the resolution of inflammation. Despite the widely available literature in clinical chronic disease settings, the influence of dietary supplements on the resolution phase of inflammation has only recently been recognized. Resolution of inflammation is a biologically active, tightly regulated process partially mediated by endogenously synthesized specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) that aid in restoration of cellular and tissue homeostasis without immune suppression. Among dietary supplements, omega-3 PUFAs, notably the 20-carbon eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and 22-carbon docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), serve as the principal substrates for SPM biosynthesis. However, the conversion of dietary omega-3 fatty acids into bioactive mediators is constrained by several factors, including enzymatic bottlenecks, metabolic disease, genetic variability, sex differences, and competing lipid pathways. Emerging evidence, much of which is from preclinical models, suggests that both omega-3 supplementation and direct SPM administration can enhance resolution capacity across multiple organ systems, including the gastrointestinal tract, cardiovascular system, musculoskeletal tissues, nervous system, respiratory system, and reproductive system. This chapter reviews the mechanistic basis by which dietary supplements influence effective resolution biology, which includes efferocytosis, macrophage reprogramming, and epithelial repair systems. The chapter also evaluates current clinical evidence and outlines possible future directions for precision nutrition strategies targeting endogenous resolution pathways.

articles.title: Five-compartment restriction spectrum imaging for noninvasive assessment of liver fibrosis in chronic liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive staging of liver fibrosis is essential in chronic liver disease (CLD). Magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is well validated but requires dedicated hardware, whereas the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) derived from conventional diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lacks specificity. Restriction spectrum imaging (RSI) decomposes the diffusion signal into multiple compartments and may capture fibrosis-related microstructural changes.

PURPOSE: To investigate the feasibility of RSI for noninvasive liver fibrosis staging in CLD and to compare its diagnostic performance with that of MRE, using liver biopsy as the reference standard.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 100 consecutive patients with CLD who underwent liver biopsy, 3.0-T multi-b-value DWI (nine b values, 0-1500 s/mm²), and MRE within 6 months. Multi-compartment RSI models (K = 2-5) were fitted to region-of-interest-averaged signals, and the optimal model was selected using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC). An RSI liver fibrosis index (RSI-LF) was derived from compartment fractions using ordinal logistic regression and internally validated with 1000 bootstrap resamples. AUCs of RSI-LF were compared with those of MRE and ADC using the paired DeLong test.

RESULTS: The five-compartment RSI model (RSI5) showed the lowest BIC. The second and fourth fractions, K5C2 and K5C4, correlated positively (ρ = 0.53) and negatively (ρ = -0.55) with fibrosis stage (both false discovery rate [FDR]-adjusted p < 0.001). RSI-LF yielded AUCs of 0.774 (95% CI: 0.651-0.898), 0.863 (0.793-0.933), and 0.911 (0.842-0.981) for ≥F2, ≥F3, and F4, respectively, with negligible bootstrap optimism. AUCs did not differ significantly from those of MRE at any threshold (all p > 0.05). RSI-LF also outperformed ADC at the ≥F3 and F4 thresholds (both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Five-compartment RSI provides diffusion metrics associated with histologic fibrosis stage, and RSI-LF showed diagnostic performance numerically comparable to that of MRE. RSI is a promising microstructure-sensitive biomarker for liver fibrosis staging that warrants multicenter validation.

articles.title: Predictors of anemia among children 6-59 months of age in Tanzania: a multilevel analysis of TDHS-MIS 2022.
articles.abstract: Anemia remains a major public health problem among children in developing countries, including Tanzania, despite ongoing nutritional and health interventions. This study aimed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with anemia in children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania. The study used data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS), a nationally representative cross-sectional survey conducted between February and July of 2022. Multilevel logistic regression was performed to identify individual- and community-level factors associated with childhood anemia. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. A total of 4334 children aged 6-59 months were included in the analysis. The overall prevalence of anemia among children aged 6-59 months was 59.9% (95% CI: 58.48-61.39). Of these, 1.9%, 32.4%, and 25.6% had severe, moderate, and mild anemia, respectively. In the final multilevel model, children aged 6-23 months (AOR = 2.48; 95% CI: 2.01-3.07), those who were fourth or fifth born (AOR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.25-2.52), those having recent diarrhea (AOR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.11-2.21), those with stunting (AOR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.08-1.59), and those with positive malaria test results (AOR = 4.87; 95% CI: 3.06-7.75) had significantly higher odds of anemia. Maternal age of 15-24 years (AOR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.05-2.27), maternal anemia (AOR = 1.74; 95% CI: 1.44-2.10), and lack of health insurance (AOR = 1.67; 95% CI: 1.09-2.55) were also associated with increased odds of childhood anemia, whereas maternal overweight was associated with lower odds of anemia (AOR = 0.75; 95% CI: 0.59-0.96). Significant geographical disparities in childhood anemia were also observed across zones. Conclusion: Anemia affects approximately six out of ten children aged 6-59 months in Tanzania, indicating that it remains a public health concern in the country. Both individual- and community-level factors contribute to childhood anemia. Integrated interventions targeting child nutrition, malaria and diarrheal disease prevention, maternal anemia, and geographically tailored strategies are needed to reduce the burden of childhood anemia in Tanzania. What is known: • Anemia is a persistent public health problem among children under five years of age in sub-Saharan Africa, including Tanzania, with several individual-level risk factors (nutritional status, infections, and maternal characteristics) previously documented. What is new: • Using nationally representative data from the 2022 Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey and Malaria Indicator Survey (TDHS-MIS) and a multilevel logistic regression model, this study found that childhood anemia remains highly prevalent. • In addition to confirming established child-related predictors (younger child age, higher birth order, diarrhea, stunting, malaria infection, younger maternal age, and maternal anemia), this study demonstrated the independent influence of household factors (lack of health insurance) and community-level geographic disparities on childhood anemia.

articles.title: From uptake to interface: rethinking molecular imaging of histopathological growth patterns in colorectal cancer liver metastases.
articles.abstract: Recent work has proposed molecular imaging signatures, including [18F]FDG and fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET, for the noninvasive characterization of histopathological growth patterns (HGPs) in colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRLM). We suggest that the spatial nature of HGPs warrants further consideration. Because HGPs are defined at the tumor-liver interface and may exhibit intralesional heterogeneity, whole-lesion tracer uptake may not fully capture the complex tumor-host interactions underlying these phenotypes. FAPI uptake may reflect fibroblast-rich stromal remodeling but should not be considered a direct surrogate for desmoplastic HGP. Future imaging-pathology studies could therefore move beyond conventional SUV-based assessment toward spatially resolved, interface-oriented molecular phenotyping. Quantifying tracer uptake and heterogeneity at the tumor-liver interface, together with longitudinal multimodal imaging, may provide complementary information on the dynamic metastatic microenvironment. Prospective studies integrating molecular imaging with standardized HGP assessment and spatially matched histopathology are warranted to determine the clinical value of this approach.

articles.title: Functional signatures of preclinical diabetic retinal neurodegeneration without clinically detectable retinopathy: a combined mfERG and mfPOP study.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare multifocal electroretinography (mfERG) and multifocal pupillographic objective perimetry (mfPOP; ObjectiveFIELD Analyzer [OFA]) in type 2 diabetic eyes without clinically detectable retinopathy (noDR), focusing on diagnostic performance, regional concordance, and short-term repeatability.

METHODS: Twenty noDR eyes and twenty age-, sex-, and laterality-balanced controls underwent ISCEV-standard mfERG and OFA 10 ETDRS (M18) testing. Outcomes were analysed across foveal, parafoveal, and perifoveal zones. Between-group comparisons used t tests or Mann-Whitney U tests with false discovery rate correction. ROC analysis with zone-matched DeLong tests assessed diagnostic performance; Spearman correlations assessed cross-modality concordance, and Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) assessed same-day OFA repeatability.

RESULTS: OFA global sensitivity and delay indices and zonal total-deviation measures were significantly abnormal in noDR eyes across all three zones. mfERG RMS and P1 amplitudes were reduced across all zones, while P1 implicit time was prolonged at the fovea and parafovea. mfERG P1 implicit time showed higher parafoveal discrimination than OFA Delay TD (p = 0.039), whereas OFA Delay TD showed higher perifoveal discrimination (p = 0.034); no significant modality differences occurred at the fovea or in sensitivity-domain comparisons. None of nine zone-matched OFA-mfERG correlations was significant within the noDR group. OFA Sensitivity MD and Delay MD showed excellent same-day repeatability (ICC = 0.980 and 0.984).

CONCLUSION: mfERG and mfPOP detect region-dependent functional abnormalities in type 2 diabetic eyes without clinically detectable retinopathy. In this exploratory pilot comparison, limited within-group concordance raises the possibility that the two modalities capture partly distinct information. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic value.

articles.title: Extravascular Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillators in Children: Real World Evidence.
articles.abstract: The extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel substernal ICD with limited reports in children and adolescents. Single-centre review of EV-ICDs in children <18-years. Clinical, peri-procedural, and electrocardiographic data reviewed, including device performance in routine exercise stress testing. Median follow-up 10.9 (IQR 7.5 - 12.5) months. Between April 2025-April 2026, 15 EV-ICDs were successfully implanted by a single cardiothoracic surgeon: median age 13.8-years, IQR 10.2-16.4; 11 (73%) male; weight 52 kg, IQR 38.2-64.1; BSA 1.6 m2, IQR 1.2-1.8. Smallest child was 4-years, 17.3 kg (BSA 0.7 m2). Indications were primary (n = 10) and secondary (n = 5) prevention. Underlying diagnoses included cardiomyopathy (n = 9), channelopathy (n = 3). One child had a previous sternotomy and another severe chest-wall deformity. Median anaesthetic time was 148 min (IQR 130-161), surgical time 68 min (59-88), fluoroscopy time 2.6 min (2.2-3.8). Median 3 (IQR 2-4) day hospitalisation. Two children experienced early complications. In one child, defibrillator threshold testing terminated ventricular fibrillation (VF) into ventricular tachycardia (VT) requiring CPR and a decision to use external cardioversion. The child fully recovered. One adolescent experienced profound bradycardia and syncope early post anaesthesia. R-wave amplitude at implant (5mV, IQR 4.2 - 6.7), discharge (5, IQR 2.8 - 8.1) and latest follow-up (5.8, IQR 3.2 - 13.7) was stable. Device sensing during routine exercise stress testing has been appropriate. There has been one successful appropriate high voltage therapy and no inappropriate high voltage therapy. This is the largest single-centre series internationally, demonstrating reliable paediatric EV-ICD implantation and short-term device performance. Ongoing paediatric surveillance is necessary.

articles.title: Efficacy of laser therapy for subacromial impingement syndrome: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: The study compared the effects of high-intensity laser therapy (HILT), low-level laser therapy (LLLT), and conventional physical therapy (CPT) on shoulder pain and function in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome (SIS). Eight databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The outcomes in this study were pain (visual analogue scale, VAS) and shoulder function (Shoulder Pain and Disability Index, SPADI). Nineteen studies involving 989 participants were ultimately included. Evidence of low to moderate certainty indicated that, compared with CPT, both HILT + CPT and LLLT + CPT reduced VAS scores; no difference in efficacy was detected between HILT + CPT and LLLT + CPT. Very low to low quality evidence indicated that neither HILT + CPT nor LLLT + CPT significantly improved SPADI scores compared with CPT, and no difference in effect was found between HILT + CPT and LLLT + CPT. Current evidence indicates no difference between HILT + CPT and LLLT + CPT in relieving pain in patients with SIS. Both may reduced pain, but no improvement in shoulder function was found.

articles.title: Impact of exercise dose on depression and mood in patients with lung cancer: a systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-response meta-analyses.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a lack of standardized exercise advice for patients with depression after lung cancer. This study evaluated the effects of high-compliance and low-compliance exercise interventions, as well as different exercise methods and dosages, on the depressive mood of lung cancer patients.

METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive literature search in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, covering the time period from the creation of these databases to April 2026. According to the recommendations of the American College of Sports Medicine (ACSM), the study was divided into the high-ACSM-compliance group and the low-ACSM-compliance group, and the effects of ACSM compliance on depression, anxiety, fatigue, and sleep in lung cancer patients were analyzed. A paired, network and dose-response meta-analysis was conducted using a random-effects model to analyze the impact of exercise on depression in lung cancer patients. We used the confidence level (CINeMA) in the network meta-analysis framework to assess the certainty of the evidence.

RESULTS: A total of 16 randomized controlled trials were included, involving 1127 participants. Overall, exercise significantly improved depression in lung cancer patients by -0.63 (95% CI,  -0.88 to -0.38; I2 = 72%, P < 0.00001). Compared with the low-compliance group, the high-ACSM group showed greater improvement (SMD,  -0.81 vs -0.38). Network meta-analysis showed that aerobic exercise had the highest degree of impact on depression in lung cancer patients (SMD,  -1.30, 95% CI [-2.08, -0.51]). According to CINeMA, the confidence level of aerobic exercise is low. Furthermore, when the total exercise dose reaches 601.72 metabolic equivalent-task-min/week, a significant improvement in depression in lung cancer patients can be observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with patients with low compliance, exercise intervention in high-compliance ACSM guidelines is more effective in improving depression in lung cancer patients. There is low-quality evidence suggesting that aerobic exercise may be an effective treatment for depression in lung cancer patients. There is a response relationship between nonlinear dose-total exercise volume and the depression level of lung cancer patients.

articles.title: Electrical pulse stimulation of skeletal muscle in vitro: A systematic review of the methods used to mimic exercise.
articles.journal: Journal of muscle research and cell motility
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of electrical pulse stimulation (EPS) as a method to induce contractions in cultured skeletal muscle has experienced rapid growth in recent years. Despite evidence demonstrating its utility in replicating some acute and chronic adaptations to exercise observed in vivo, there is a lack of evidence concerning the optimal parameters necessary to induce specific molecular adaptations.

METHODS: This systematic review adhered to the Preferred Reporting Systems for Systematic Reviews. Eligible studies were published in English within peer-reviewed articles. Searches were executed in three databases, with an additional search for grey literature conducted on Google Scholar. Studies investigating chronic EPS in C2C12, and primary human muscle cells were incorporated.

RESULTS: One hundred and twenty-seven studies spanning over twenty years of research fulfilled the criteria of this review. Outcome measures were categorised into distinct groups: Morphology, gene expression, protein abundance and/or activity, mitochondrial content/function, contractile function, metabolic changes, and cell viability.

CONCLUSIONS: EPS is effective in inducing a generalised exercise-like response in cultured muscle cells. However, unlike exercise in vivo, the observed molecular responses divergent in endurance/resistance exercises do not occur. Instead, both AKT/mTOR and AMPK/PGC-1α molecular pathways are activated concurrently across a wide range of stimulation durations and intensities. Therefore, EPS in culture is not yet suitable for investigating specific endurance/resistance training adaptations, which may be more readily observed in human and animal models.

articles.title: Effect of augmented reality on dental anxiety and pain perception in children: a randomized controlled clinical study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of an augmented reality (AR) application on children's dental anxiety using physiological, psychological, and behavioral parameters.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Ninety-six children aged 6-8 years requiring pulpotomy were randomly allocated to Control (CG), Cartoon (CaG), and AR (ARG) groups (n = 32 each). The Wong-Baker FACES (WB-FACES), Modified Child Dental Anxiety Scale [MCDAS(f)], Frankl Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS), pulse rate, and salivary cortisol, α-amylase, and chromogranin-A (CHGA) levels were assessed pre- and post-treatment.

RESULTS: Post-treatment FBRS scores were higher in the ARG than the CG and CaG (p = 0.011; p = 0.041), and WB-FACES scores were lower in the ARG than the CG (p = 0.034). Baseline MCDAS(f) scores were lower in the ARG; after adjustment, post-treatment MCDAS(f) remained lower in the ARG than the CaG (p < 0.001) but not the CG (p = 0.121). Pulse rate changed only in the ARG (p = 0.001), without between-group differences. Cortisol reduction was greater in the ARG than the CG (p = 0.030) and CaG (p = 0.020), and α-amylase reduction was greater than in the CG (p = 0.001), whereas CHGA reduction was greater in the CaG than the ARG (p = 0.005).

CONCLUSIONS: AR was associated with better cooperation; however, its effects on anxiety and physiological stress markers were inconsistent, and overall superiority was not demonstrated.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: To our knowledge, this study is among the first to integrate tell-show-do and positive reinforcement into an AR application and evaluate its effects on dental anxiety in children, highlighting the potential of AR as an adjunctive behavioral guidance approach in pediatric dentistry.

articles.title: Endocannabinoid system remodeling in human myopathies: a meta-analysis of skeletal muscle transcriptomes.
articles.journal: Journal of muscle research and cell motility
articles.abstract: Preclinical studies indicate that the endocannabinoid system plays an important role in skeletal muscle inflammation, regeneration and metabolism, yet its involvement in human myopathies remains undefined. This study systematically investigated whether endocannabinoid system remodeling occurs in muscle of patients with myopathies. A retrospective meta-analysis was performed using publicly available bulk RNA-sequencing datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus. In total, 328 muscle biopsies from patients with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, myotonic dystrophy type 1, facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy, inflammatory myopathies, Duchenne/Becker muscular dystrophy, mitochondrial and collagen VI-related myopathy, and 173 control samples were included. Differential expression analyses were conducted per dataset using DESeq2, followed by random-effects meta-analyses for endocannabinoid targets and key endocannabinoid enzymes, with false discovery rate correction. Across disease subtypes, consistent remodeling of the endocannabinoid system was observed. Cannabinoid receptor 1 (CNR1) expression was overall upregulated (log2FC = 0.43, q < 0.001), while fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), the primary enzyme responsible for anandamide and N-acylethanolamine degradation, was consistently downregulated (log2FC = -0.56, q < 0.001). CNR1 exhibited the lowest heterogeneity of all genes analyzed. Enzymes involved in 2-arachidonoylglycerol metabolism displayed disease-specific regulation. Results were robust to sex adjustment and alternative models. This meta-analysis provides the first comprehensive evidence that endocannabinoid signaling is consistently remodeled in human myopathies, across myopathies of different etiology. The downregulation of FAAH and upregulation of CNR1 suggest altered endocannabinoid tone as a shared feature of muscle degeneration. These findings support integrative studies combining longitudinal endocannabinoid and clinical data to understand how endocannabinoid remodeling drives muscle plasticity.

articles.title: Size-consistency-corrected multireference configuration interaction in COLUMBUS provides highly accurate molecular excitation energies.
articles.abstract: Accurate reference data for electronically excited states are essential for assessing multireference electronic-structure methods. We benchmark state-averaged complete-active-space self-consistent field (SA-CASSCF), exchange-scaled CASSCF (XS-CASSCF), fully uncontracted multireference configuration interaction with single and double excitations (MR-CISD), and four a posteriori size-consistency corrections against the theoretical best estimates of QUESTDB. The dataset comprises 263 valence excitations across 41 small and medium-sized molecules, including singlet and triplet nπ*, ππ*, and doubly excited states. All SA-CASSCF and MR-CISD calculations were performed with the COLUMBUS program system using molecule-specific active spaces and the aug-cc-pVDZ basis set. For the 233 safe transitions, SA-CASSCF and MR-CISD yield mean absolute errors of 0.58 and 0.32 eV, respectively, with predominantly positive biases. The Davidson-Silver/Siegbahn (+DV3) and Pople (+P) corrections reduce the mean absolute errors to 0.10 and 0.11 eV and the root-mean-square errors to 0.13 eV. They also provide a more balanced description across spin multiplicities and excitation characters. XS-CASSCF, evaluated with two distinct parameterizations, improves singlet ππ* states, particularly those with pronounced ionic character, but degrades nπ* states and does not improve the overall statistics relative to SA-CASSCF. For 36 selected unsafe or doubly excited transitions, MR-CISD+DV3 and MR-CISD+P retain mean absolute errors of 0.16 eV. Their agreement with extrapolated full configuration interaction-based reference values and discrepancies from several complete-active-space third-order perturbation theory- and partially contracted-n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory-based estimates identify states whose current best estimates merit independent re-examination. Overall, size-consistency-corrected MR-CISD provides highly accurate and broadly balanced valence excitation energies.

articles.title: Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut-brain interaction.
articles.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut-brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut-brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity. These conditions are diagnosed with a combination of clinical history, absence of alarm symptoms-such as weight loss or rectal bleeding-and targeted investigations. An empathetic management approach improves quality of life and symptoms, reduces health-care use, and enhances treatment adherence. Mainstays of treatment include education, dietary and lifestyle advice, modifying fibre intake, and drugs directed towards predominant symptoms. For severe symptoms, other treatments include specific medical devices, biofeedback, or psychological therapies. However, the effectiveness of most treatments is modest and there is an ongoing need to expand available treatments for bowel disorders, with several novel drugs currently in development.

articles.title: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.

FINDINGS: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.

INTERPRETATION: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

FUNDING: Baili-Bio (Chengdu) Pharmaceutical.

articles.title: Sacituzumab tirumotecan versus treatment of physician's choice in previously treated endometrial cancer (TroFuse-005/ENGOT-en23/GOG-3095): a randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic options for patients with endometrial cancer who progress after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy are scarce, and prognosis is poor. Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) is a trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2-directed antibody-drug conjugate with a unique, bifunctional linker that maximises delivery of a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I inhibitor payload to tumour cells. This study aimed to compare sac-TMT with the treatment of physician's choice (TPC) in patients with endometrial cancer who had been previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

METHODS: In this randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial, patients were recruited from 242 gynaecological oncology centres across 31 countries and regions. Participating centres were selected based on established expertise in gynaecological oncology and an adequate volume of potentially eligible patients. Eligible patients were female and aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma or carcinosarcoma, who had received up to three previous lines of therapy, including systemic platinum-based chemotherapy and anti-programmed death 1 or anti-programmed death ligand 1 therapy. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) via central interactive response technology to receive intravenous sac-TMT (4 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle) or TPC (intravenous doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 every 3 weeks or intravenous paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle). Investigators and patients were not masked to treatment; radiologists performing blinded independent central review were fully masked. Randomisation was stratified by mismatch repair status (deficient vs proficient), trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 expression by immunohistochemistry (TROP2 EPR20043 Formulation Locked Assay [Roche Tissue Diagnostics, Tucson, AZ, USA]; low [0% to <50% of tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity] vs medium-high [≥50% tumour cells with moderate (2+) or strong (3+) membrane staining intensity]), number of previous lines of systemic therapy (≤2 vs 3), and baseline disease status per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) by blinded independent central review (measurable vs non-measurable). Dual primary endpoints were progression-free survival per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (version 1.1) assessed by blinded independent central review and overall survival, analysed in the intention-to-treat population. The data cutoff date was March 23, 2026. Progression-free survival and overall survival were evaluated as dual primary endpoints using a graphical multiple-testing approach with prespecified alpha allocation. Progression-free survival was assessed every 8 weeks through to week 56, then every 12 weeks thereafter; overall survival was assessed continuously. The safety analysis included all randomly assigned patients who received at least one dose of study treatment. For progression-free survival, missing radiographic assessments were handled using prespecified censoring rules; no imputation was performed for missing overall survival or safety data. The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06132958) and is ongoing.

FINDINGS: Between Jan 5, 2024, and Sept 17, 2025, 776 patients were randomly assigned to sac-TMT (n=386) or TPC (n=390). 384 (99%) of 386 patients in the sac-TMT group and 367 (94%) of 390 in the TPC group received at least one dose of study treatment. At data cutoff, median follow-up was 14·0 months (IQR 11·0-16·9). Median progression-free survival was 7·2 months (95% CI 5·6-7·6) in the sac-TMT group and 3·9 months (3·7-5·3) in the TPC group (hazard ratio 0·59 [95% CI 0·50-0·70]; p<0·0001) and median overall survival was 19·0 months (16·1-not reached) in the sac-TMT group and 12·1 months (11·0-15·2) in the TPC group (0·68 [0·55-0·84]; p=0·0001). 265 (69%) of 384 patients in the sac-TMT group and 210 (57%) of 367 in the TPC group had a grade 3 or higher adverse event. Serious adverse events were reported in 133 (35%) patients in the sac-TMT group and 117 (32%) patients in the TPC group. Treatment-related adverse events led to death in three (<1%) patients in the sac-TMT group and three (<1%) in the TPC group.

INTERPRETATION: Sac-TMT significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival versus TPC in patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. These findings support sac-TMT as a new standard of care for patients with endometrial cancer who have received chemotherapy and immunotherapy and have few effective treatment options.

FUNDING: Merck Sharp & Dohme.

articles.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.

METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.

FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.

INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

FUNDING: Novartis.

articles.title: Intermittent Local Muscle Vibration Produces Smaller Knee Joint Position Sense Errors than Continuous Vibration: A Randomized Crossover Study in Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: This randomized crossover study compared immediate responses to different local muscle vibration protocols in 40 adults with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomized 1:1 to receive intermittent or continuous vibration first, then crossed over to the alternative protocol after washout. Vibration targeted the vastus medialis during 120 s of sit-to-stand exercise. Intermittent vibration was delivered only during seated and standing holds, whereas continuous vibration was delivered throughout the exercise. Knee joint position sense (JPS) errors were assessed at 20°, 40°, and 60° of flexion using inertial measurement units. Near-infrared spectroscopy recorded prefrontal and muscle hemodynamic responses during JPS testing. Assessments were performed at baseline and after each protocol. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance. Intermittent vibration produced smaller JPS errors than continuous vibration at all angles (1.96° versus 2.87°, 2.17° versus 3.20°, and 2.78° versus 4.72°, respectively, all p ≤ 0.019). Intermittent vibration elicited smaller changes in prefrontal total hemoglobin (0.23 versus 0.66 μM, p < 0.001), muscle oxygenated hemoglobin (2.32 versus 5.53 μM, p = 0.003), and muscle total hemoglobin (2.59 versus 6.13 μM, p = 0.004). Intermittent local muscle vibration produced smaller immediate knee JPS errors, whereas continuous vibration elicited larger hemodynamic responses.

articles.title: Glycocalyx Remodelling and TGFβ-Associated Endothelial Phenotypes in the Fontan Circulation: A Literature-Informed Conceptual Mechanotransduction Model.
articles.abstract: Fontan circulation is characterised by non-physiological haemodynamics, including reduced flow pulsatility, altered pulmonary arterial flow, and chronic venous congestion. These abnormalities may affect endothelial mechanotransduction, glycocalyx homeostasis, inflammatory endothelial activation, and extracellular-matrix remodelling. We aimed to integrate serum proteomic findings from two clinically distinct Fontan cohorts with published haemodynamic and experimental data to develop a literature-informed, hypothesis-generating conceptual model linking altered Fontan haemodynamics with endothelial glycocalyx remodelling and downstream endothelial signalling. Serum proteomic data generated using the ScioCD antibody microarray platform were evaluated in two previously characterised Fontan cohorts: a clinically homogeneous high-performing Fontan (HPF) cohort with a systemic left ventricle and no overt Fontan-associated complications, and a clinically more heterogeneous cohort with mixed systemic ventricular morphology and a greater burden of Fontan-associated morbidity. Each cohort was compared with its respective age- and sex-matched healthy control group. Original patient-control analyses used LIMMA-based modelling with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Selected proteins were additionally assessed in harmonised exploratory patient-control analyses. Published pulmonary arterial wall shear-stress (WSS) data in Fontan physiology and non-Fontan endothelial shear-stress experiments were integrated qualitatively to inform the proposed conceptual model. The HPF cohort showed increased circulating syndecan-1 (SDC1), whereas transforming growth factor-beta 2 (TGFβ2), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) were not significantly increased relative to matched controls. In contrast, the clinically more heterogeneous Fontan cohort showed increased circulating TGFβ2, VCAM-1, and ICAM-1, whereas SDC1 was not significantly different from controls. Nerve growth factor-beta (NGFβ) and leukaemia inhibitory factor (LIF) were decreased in both cohorts. LYAM was increased in both cohorts, although different assay targets reached statistical significance. These findings informed a conceptual model in which an SDC1-associated profile may reflect altered proteoglycan turnover and glycocalyx remodelling, whereas a TGFβ2-, VCAM-1-, and ICAM-1-associated profile may reflect broader endothelial activation and remodelling-related signalling. Integration of cohort-specific serum proteomic profiles with published Fontan WSS data and experimental endothelial literature yielded a literature-informed, hypothesis-generating model of endothelial adaptation and maladaptation in Fontan circulation. In this model, chronically altered flow conditions and reduced pulsatility may contribute to glycocalyx remodelling, altered mechanotransduction, endothelial adhesion-molecule activation, and TGFβ-associated remodelling pathways. As WSS was not measured in the studied individuals, and the analyses were cross-sectional and serum-based, the model does not establish a direct WSS-biomarker relationship, causality, or a potential transition. Prospective longitudinal studies combining patient- and compartment-specific haemodynamic assessment, standardised biomarker sampling, hepatic evaluation, and clinical outcome data are required for validation.

articles.title: Fixed-Dose Netarsudil/Latanoprost Versus Artificial Tears in Pseudophakic Bullous Keratopathy with Glaucoma: A Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Evidence for fixed-dose netarsudil/latanoprost in pseudophakic bullous keratopathy (PBK) with glaucoma is limited. The fixed-combination design cannot separate the effect of netarsudil from that of latanoprost, nor attribute any effect specifically to Rho-associated coiled-coil kinase (ROCK) inhibition. Materials and Methods: Fifty eyes of 50 participants with grade 1 or 2 PBK and primary open-angle glaucoma were randomized in a single-center, double-masked trial to netarsudil 0.02%/latanoprost 0.005% or preservative-free artificial tears for 12 weeks (25/group). Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA; primary) and central corneal thickness (CCT; secondary) were analyzed using intention-to-treat mixed-effects models. Registration NCT06960629 preceded first consent; registry discrepancies are disclosed. Results: All participants completed follow-up. One active-arm baseline CCT was missing; CCT models retained available observations from all 50 participants, whereas change-based CCT analyses included 24 active and 25 control eyes. Week-12 between-group differences in change were -0.21 logMAR (95% CI -0.28 to -0.14) and -21.0 µm (95% CI -28.4 to -13.6). Interaction p values were <0.001; CCT inference was exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. In a post hoc intraocular pressure (IOP) analysis, the week-12 difference in change was -0.96 mmHg (95% CI -1.53 to -0.39; interaction p = 0.006). Hyperemia occurred in 20/25 treated eyes and reticular epithelial edema in 2/25; no serious adverse events or discontinuations were reported. Conclusions: The combination was associated with short-term BCVA improvement and modest corneal thinning. Potential functional unmasking, the unmatched control formulation, and the combination design limit interpretation. These findings are insufficient to recommend routine off-label use for PBK edema or change clinical practice.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Risk Profiles in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting and Valvular Surgery: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Coronary artery disease (CAD) and valvular heart disease (VHD) may exhibit distinct cardiovascular risk factors, metabolic profiles, and biomarkers. The aim of this study was to compare preoperative cardiometabolic risk profiles, including traditional cardiovascular risk factors and biochemical parameters including lipid profiles, HbA1C, fibrinogen, and NT-proBNP, between patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and those undergoing valve surgery. Methods: This observational study included 261 patients (157 CAD/CABG and 104 VHD/valve surgery). Cardiovascular risk factors, laboratory parameters, and glycemic status were compared. Multivariable linear regression assessed the association between surgical group and log-transformed NT-proBNP. Results: CAD/CABG patients were younger, more frequently male, and had higher rates of hypertension. Although HDL-C was lower and fibrinogen higher in CAD/CABG patients in unadjusted analyses, these differences were no longer statistically significant after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI (p = 0.087 and p = 0.135, respectively). Despite similar rates of previously diagnosed diabetes mellitus (DM) (30.0% vs. 27.2%, p = 0.627), HbA1c was higher in CAD/CABG patients (6.26 ± 0.94% vs. 5.99 ± 0.72%, p = 0.015). This difference remained after adjustment (β = -0.294 percentage points for VHD vs. CAD/CABG, p = 0.017). Among patients without known DM, 8.6% had diabetes-range HbA1c (≥6.5%). Preoperative atrial fibrillation was more prevalent in VHD patients (23.3% vs. 8.6%, p = 0.001). NT-proBNP was higher in VHD patients (median 859 vs. 222 pg/mL, p < 0.001), persisting after adjustment for age, gender, LVEF, creatinine, atrial fibrillation, and BMI (adjusted ratio 3.00, 95% CI 2.07-4.32; p < 0.001). Conclusions: CAD/CABG patients had higher prevalence of hypertension and hyperlipidemia and exhibited higher HbA1c concentrations, whereas VHD patients had higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation and NT-proBNP concentrations. Initially observed differences in fibrinogen and HDL were no longer statistically significant after adjustment. These findings highlight differences in preoperative risk profiles in cardiac surgery populations and support preoperative glycemic assessment in both groups.

articles.title: Beyond Glucose Control: The Emerging Role of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Rheumatic and Musculoskeletal Diseases.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have become established therapies for type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity, with robust evidence demonstrating cardiovascular and renal benefits beyond glycemic control. Increasing evidence indicates that glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), an incretin hormone, exerts pleiotropic effects extending beyond metabolic regulation, including modulation of appetite, oxidative stress, endothelial function, and systemic inflammation. These properties have generated considerable interest in the potential role of GLP-1RAs in immune-mediated diseases. Rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases (RMDs) are frequently accompanied by obesity and metabolic comorbidities, both of which contribute to chronic inflammation, increased cardiovascular risk, and poorer clinical outcomes. In addition to improving metabolic health, experimental studies suggest that GLP-1RAs may modulate innate and adaptive immune responses through mechanisms involving macrophage polarization, NF-κB signaling, T-cell responses, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production. These immunometabolic effects suggest that GLP-1RAs may have therapeutic potential as adjunctive agents capable of attenuating disease activity and improving clinical outcomes in selected patients with RMDs. Conversely, emerging genetic and observational studies have reported conflicting associations between GLP-1R signaling or GLP-1RA exposure and autoimmune disease risk, while disease-specific safety data remain limited. This review summarizes the metabolic and immunological mechanisms of selective GLP-1RAs, critically appraises the available evidence for their use in RMDs, and separately discusses emerging evidence involving dual GIP/GLP-1 and triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonists, highlighting their distinct pharmacological profiles, current limitations, and future research directions in rheumatology.

articles.title: Integrative Genetic and Transcriptomic Analysis Reveals Macrophage-Associated Signatures and Predicted Macrophage-Fibroblast Communication in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: How macrophage-associated expression changes relate to fibroblast extracellular matrix (ECM) programs in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the relationship between clinically associated macrophage expression patterns and fibroblast ECM programs and to examine their spatial correspondence.

METHODS: We integrated FinnGen GWAS summary statistics with human single-cell and bulk lung transcriptomes. Candidate genes were evaluated using machine learning, hemodynamic associations, and cellular expression profiling. Cell communication and regulon inference were performed, followed by reanalysis of mouse spatial transcriptomic data comprising one wild-type section and one conditional knockout section.

RESULTS: The single-cell atlas comprised 55,158 cells, with fibroblasts among the populations showing the highest median trait relevance scores. An eight-gene tissue classifier achieved post-selection AUCs of 0.873 and 0.992 in two external cohorts used for model selection and evaluation. Bulk lung CD163 expression was inversely correlated with pulmonary vascular resistance (Spearman ρ = -0.522), while pooled single-cell summaries showed lower CD163 expression across four macrophage populations in PAH. The CD163-PVR association remained inverse but was attenuated after adjustment for clinical covariates and estimated macrophage fraction (p = 0.067). Fibroblast ECM-related pathway enrichment was also supported by sample-level analysis. CellChat predicted FN1- and SPP1-associated communication toward fibroblasts, although sample-level differences in macrophage FN1 and SPP1 expression and in fibroblast FN1 expression did not reach significance after multiple-testing correction (fibroblast FN1 FDR = 0.059). Among the candidate ECM-associated regulons, only ERG showed limited sample-level support (adjusted p = 0.049). Mouse spatial analysis showed shorter mean source-defined macrophage-fibroblast pair distances in the conditional knockout section, although the spatial block-bootstrap interval for the bin-level distance difference included zero. Within this section, detection of macrophage-associated Spp1 or Fn1 was associated with higher ECM scores in paired fibroblast-associated regions after excluding both ligand genes from the ECM signature.

CONCLUSIONS: These analyses characterize co-occurring macrophage-associated expression changes, predicted macrophage-fibroblast communication, and fibroblast ECM programs in PAH. The mouse spatial reanalysis provides complementary spatial context for these observations, while the inferred communication and regulatory relationships should be considered computationally predicted and require further experimental validation.

articles.title: Fluoropyrimidine-Associated Cardiotoxicity: Coronary Vasospasm, Rechallenge Strategies, and Vasodilator Prophylaxis.
articles.abstract: Fluoropyrimidines, principally 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and capecitabine, remain foundational agents in the treatment of gastrointestinal, breast, and head and neck malignancies, but they are also among the most clinically important non-anthracycline causes of cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity. Clinical manifestations range from asymptomatic electrocardiographic abnormalities and biomarker elevation to angina, coronary vasospasm, myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, heart failure, Takotsubo syndrome, and sudden cardiac death. Although coronary vasospasm remains the most recognized mechanism, contemporary evidence supports a multifactorial pathophysiology involving endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, direct myocardial injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, thrombosis, and microvascular dysfunction. The reported incidence varies widely because of differences in definitions, surveillance intensity, cancer populations, and fluoropyrimidine schedules. Management begins with immediate discontinuation of fluoropyrimidine and evaluation for acute coronary syndrome or other cardiac emergencies. A major unresolved question is whether fluoropyrimidine therapy can be safely resumed after cardiotoxicity. Older reports suggested high recurrence rates with rechallenge, whereas more recent cardio-oncology-guided series suggest that selected patients may successfully continue treatment using vasodilator prophylaxis, regimen modification, and close monitoring. This narrative review summarizes the epidemiology, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, acute management, rechallenge strategies, and alternatives to fluoropyrimidines when re-exposure is unsafe.

articles.title: Large Language Models for Structured Critical Appraisal of Randomized Controlled Trials in Otolaryngology: Randomized Crossover Study Comparing GPT-4o and Medical Students.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critical appraisal of medical literature is an essential skill for trainees but can be time-intensive and difficult to master. Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have emerged as potential tools to support learners; however, their accuracy and reliability in structured appraisal tasks remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to compare the performance of GPT-4o with that of medical students in structured critical appraisal of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), evaluating its potential role in medical education.

METHODS: In this prospective randomized crossover study, 12 RCTs published in The Laryngoscope in 2024 were identified and appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) checklist. Two second-year medical students independently appraised each article with and without the assistance of GPT-4o, separated by a 1-month washout period. The GPT-4o model was also used to independently appraise each study. Two otolaryngologists evaluated the randomized and anonymized appraisals using a standardized rubric assessing binary correctness, free-text accuracy, completeness, and overall quality. Medical students and evaluators also completed poststudy questionnaires regarding AI use and perceptions.

RESULTS: A statistically significant overall effect of appraisal condition was observed for free-text accuracy (F2,22=3.94; P=.04; η2p=0.263); however, no individual pairwise comparison remained statistically significant following Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. No statistically significant effect of appraisal condition was detected for binary correctness (F2,22=0.07; P=.93, η2p=.006), completeness (F2,22=0.18; P=.84; η2p=0.016), or overall quality (F2,22=0.52; P=.60; η2p=0.045). Physician evaluators identified the presence of AI involvement in approximately 56% of student appraisals completed with AI assistance and 58% of AI-only appraisals. Medical students reported that GPT-4o reduced the time required to complete appraisals and assisted with understanding study topics, interpreting results, and identifying study limitations.

CONCLUSIONS: Although a statistically significant overall effect of appraisal condition was observed for free-text accuracy, no individual pairwise comparison remained statistically significant following Holm adjustment, with the largest observed difference occurring between students without AI assistance and AI alone. No statistically significant differences were detected in binary correctness, completeness, or overall quality.
