These findings support cautious investigation of GPT-4o as an adjunct educational tool for structured critical appraisal while emphasizing the continued importance of independent critical reasoning and human oversight. Larger studies are needed to determine the generalizability of these findings.

articles.title: Why Do Patients with Mitral Valve Prolapse Exercise Less? The Emerging Role of Thoracic Geometry.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
articles.abstract: Background: Exercise intolerance is frequently reported in patients with mitral valve prolapse (MVP) despite preserved left ventricular (LV) systolic function and non-severe mitral regurgitation, but its mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether antero-posterior (A-P) thoracic diameter is associated with reduced functional capacity in symptomatic MVP and characterized exercise-related changes in LV filling, stroke volume, and cardiac output. Methods: In this prospective single-center study, 101 consecutive symptomatic individuals undergoing exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) were enrolled, including 58 with MVP and 43 symptomatic non-MVP controls. Resting and exercise assessment included indexed LV volumes, stroke volume index (SVi), cardiac index (CI), LV filling indices, and pulmonary pressures. Reduced functional capacity was prespecified as peak workload < 100 W. Logistic regression and receiver-operating characteristic analyses were performed to identify its determinants and evaluate A-P thoracic diameter. Results: Patients with MVP had a smaller A-P thoracic diameter and lower exercise capacity than controls, with more frequent exertional symptoms and greater exercise-induced ST-segment depression despite negative ESE for inducible wall-motion abnormalities. At rest, MVP patients exhibited smaller LV dimensions and volumes, lower LV mass and left atrial size, and lower SVi and CI despite comparable LVEF and E/e'. During exercise, LV contractile reserve and pulmonary pressure responses were comparable, whereas peak LVEDVi, LVESVi, SVi, CI, and E/e' were lower in MVP patients. Exercise-induced increases in LVEDVi, SVi, CI, and E/e' were also attenuated. After multivariable adjustment, female sex (adjusted OR 4.14, 95% CI 1.22-14.05; p = 0.023) and A-P thoracic diameter (adjusted OR per 1 cm increase 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.58; p < 0.001) retained statistical significance, whereas the associations with anxiety disorder, MVP, and peak-exercise SBP were attenuated and no longer statistically significant. A-P thoracic diameter showed good discrimination (AUC 0.864), with an internally derived optimal cut-off ≤ 12.75 cm. Conclusions: Symptomatic MVP was characterized by reduced exercise capacity and a smaller, low-filling cardiac phenotype with limited stroke-volume and cardiac-output augmentation despite preserved LV contractile reserve. A smaller A-P thoracic diameter remained independently associated with reduced functional capacity after adjustment for MVP status and other covariates, supporting thoracic geometry as a component of a broader thoraco-cardiac functional phenotype. The identified threshold requires external validation.

articles.title: The Effects of Simulated Occupational Physical Activity During Heat Exposure and Sex on Circulating Markers of Angiogenesis.
articles.journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
articles.abstract: Heat loss adaptations involve key mechanisms including increased skin blood flow and sweat production, although sex-specific responses are not fully understood. We hypothesized that circulating angiogenic and lymphangiogenic factors linked to post-exercise heat responses would be elevated following a simulated occupational work trial. Background and Objectives: We quantified circulating markers associated with angiogenic and lymphangiogenic responses to a simulated occupational exercise in the heat in females and males. Methods: Females and males (n = 30 each) were randomized to 7 consecutive days of exercise comprising 60 min of walking (3 × 20 min) in a hot environment (38 °C, 60% relative humidity, 3.5 mph, 5% grade). Participants were assigned to either a Sustained (90 min heat exposure, n = 30) or Periodic (3 × 30 min, 3 h separation, n = 30) heat exposure. Blood samples were collected "Pre" and "Post" the first 30 min of exposure on days 1 and 7. Results: Analyses revealed a significant time × day interaction only for sFlt-1 (p < 0.001). Following the 30 min bout of heat + exercise, females exhibited Pre-Post elevations for VEGF-A (p = 0.020) and VEGF-C (p = 0.004), while corresponding changes were not observed in males. However, sex-based differences were attenuated in VEGF-A and VEGF-C after adjusting for body composition and aerobic capacity. Independent of sex, Pre-Post changes were lower for VEGF-D (p < 0.008) but elevated for bFGF (p < 0.001) and sFlt-1 (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Contrasting males, females exposed to a hot environment had post-exercise elevations in the circulating markers VEGF-A and VEGF-C. Moreover, sFlt-1 concentrations may reflect a heat adaptation response after 7 days of exposure.

articles.title: [A case of occupational acute methemoglobinemia induced by chemical poisoning].
articles.journal: Zhonghua lao dong wei sheng zhi ye bing za zhi = Zhonghua laodong weisheng zhiyebing zazhi = Chinese journal of industrial hygiene and occupational diseases
articles.abstract: Occupational methemoglobinemia is a toxic disease occurring in workers after exposure to oxidizing chemicals such as aniline and nitrobenzene during production, in which ferrous iron in hemoglobin is oxidized to ferric iron, leading to decreased oxygen-carrying capacity. Affected patients may present with cyanosis, dizziness, headache, fatigue, and dyspnea; in severe cases, disturbance of consciousness, arrhythmia, and even death may occur. The clinical data of a patient admitted to Qilu Hospital of Shandong University in August 2024 were analyzed. The patient developed methemoglobinemia after cleaning fiber vacuum filters containing aromatic amino and nitro compounds for several consecutive days. The arterial blood methemoglobin level was markedly elevated, and the main clinical manifestations were dizziness, vomiting, dyspnea, and generalized cyanosis of the skin and mucous membranes. After admission, the patient received comprehensive treatment including respiratory support, low-dose methylene blue, and glucocorticoids, and improved and was discharged.

articles.title: Global hypertension guidelines: a comparative review of diagnostic and management recommendations.
authors: Early Career Researcher Special Interest Group of the British and Irish Hypertension Society (BIHS)
articles.abstract: Global hypertension guidelines show increasing convergence in core principles of evidence-based management, but substantial regional differences remain in diagnostic thresholds, cardiovascular risk assessment, treatment targets, and implementation strategies. Across contemporary guidelines, there is broad agreement on the value of accurate blood pressure measurement, out-of-office monitoring, cardiovascular risk assessment, lifestyle modification, and effective pharmacotherapy, with increasing support for early combination therapy and single-pill combinations. However, North American guidelines generally adopt lower diagnostic and treatment thresholds, whereas most other guidelines retain a 140/90 mmHg diagnostic threshold while increasingly recommending lower treatment targets when tolerated and according to cardiovascular risk. Recommendations for resistant hypertension, device-based therapies, and emerging treatments also vary considerably, reflecting differences in evidence interpretation, population characteristics, healthcare infrastructure, and resource availability. The review identifies implementation, treatment access, and sustained blood pressure control as major challenges. These findings support greater international harmonization where appropriate, alongside locally adapted, risk-based guidance and stronger guideline development and implementation in low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: Identification and Prioritization of Stage-Specific and Pan-Stage Therapeutic Targets in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Integrative Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Approaches.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops through a multistep process involving progressive molecular alterations from chronic liver disease to malignant transformation. Genes that change consistently across this progression, together with those unique to HCC, may offer insight into hepatocarcinogenesis and serve as candidate diagnostic and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to identify and prioritize stage-specific and pan-stage genes associated with HCC progression using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning approach, and to evaluate their biological and diagnostic relevance.

METHODS: The GEO dataset GSE89377, comprising 107 human liver tissue samples representing normal liver, hepatitis, cirrhosis, low- and high-grade dysplastic nodules, early HCC, and advanced HCC, was analyzed. Differentially expressed genes were identified using GEO2R, followed by protein-protein interaction network analysis using STRING and hub gene prioritization using Cytoscape/CytoHubba. In parallel, patient samples were classified into malignant and non-malignant groups using Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models. Feature selection was performed within the training folds, and model performance was assessed using 5-fold nested stratified cross-validation, ROC/AUC analysis, and SHAP-based feature interpretation. Genes common to the bioinformatics and machine learning analyses were identified using the E-Venn tool to obtain stage-specific and pan-stage genes. The pan-stage genes were further evaluated using UALCAN, GTEx, and GEPIA, followed by Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), LASSO regression, diagnostic nomogram construction and validation, and TIMER2.0-based immune-cell infiltration analysis.

RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified 100, 146, 220, 213, 181, and 209 differentially expressed genes in hepatitis, cirrhosis, low-grade dysplasia, high-grade dysplasia, early HCC, and advanced HCC, respectively. Machine learning analysis showed good discrimination between malignant and non-malignant samples, with RF and SVM achieving accuracies of 92.38% and 95.24%, respectively. SHAP analysis identified genes that contribute to the model's predictions, including TOP2A, KIF20A, PTTG1, and ZIC2. Integration of bioinformatics and machine learning analyses identified 14, 13, 13, 11, 12, and 19 stage-specific genes, respectively, and 10 pan-stage genes: ASPM, AURKB, CCNA2, CCNB2, CDKN3, HMMR, KIF20A, NUSAP1, PTTG1, and TOP2A. GSEA revealed predominant enrichment of cell-cycle and mitotic processes, particularly the G2/M checkpoint and E2F target pathways. LASSO regression prioritized PTTG1, HMMR, and KIF20A, which were used to construct a diagnostic nomogram with an AUC of 0.960 and a bootstrap-corrected AUC of 0.950. The model showed a sensitivity of 92.5% and specificity of 91.0%. These three genes also showed significant positive associations with immune cell infiltration in TCGA-LIHC, particularly with B cells, dendritic cells, and macrophages.

DISCUSSION: The identified pan-stage genes were predominantly associated with cell-cycle regulation and proliferation-related biological processes, as supported by GSEA. The prioritization of PTTG1, HMMR, and KIF20A highlights their potential diagnostic relevance in HCC. Their associations with immune-cell infiltration further suggest possible links between these genes and the tumour immune microenvironment.

CONCLUSION: The integrated bioinformatics and machine learning analysis identified stage-specific and pan-stage genes associated with HCC progression. The 10 pan-stage genes were mainly associated with cell-cycle and proliferation-related processes. PTTG1, HMMR, and KIF20A were further prioritized as potential diagnostic biomarkers, with PTTG1 showing the major contribution to the diagnostic model. These findings provide candidate genes for further investigation in HCC; however, independent clinical and experimental validation is required.

articles.title: Visualizing periarticular inflammation of the shoulder and pelvic girdles in polymyalgia rheumatica with [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) and giant cell arteritis (GCA) are increasingly recognized as phenotypic variants within a shared disease spectrum. While [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG)-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) can detect musculoskeletal and vascular involvement, its reliance on glucose metabolism limits inflammation-specificity. The vascular adhesion protein-1 (VAP-1)-targeted tracer [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 has shown promise in GCA. This study evaluates its potential for detecting periarticular inflammation in PMR.

METHODS: Patients with PMR underwent [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT with musculoskeletal and vascular ultrasound. Tracer uptake was measured in periarticular and vascular regions and compared with patients with active GCA. Soluble VAP-1 (sVAP-1) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2/-3/-9) were measured in patients with PMR and GCA, as well as in healthy controls, who did not undergo imaging.

RESULTS: Eight PMR patients were imaged and compared with sixteen GCA patients as well as eight healthy controls. In comparison to GCA-only patients, an increased periarticular tracer uptake across the shoulder and pelvic girdle was found in PMR (maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) 2.65±0.52 vs. 1.96±0.57; p<0.001). Tracer uptake was inversely associated with recent prednisolone exposure across periarticular and vascular territories (all p<0.05). Circulating sVAP-1 was inversely associated with MMP-2 (r=-0.58; p=0.008). Moreover, MMP-2 and MMP-3 were negatively associated with vascular tracer uptake (e.g. aortic arch SUVmax/MMP-2 r=-0.69; p=0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This pioneering study demonstrates that [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT detects periarticular inflammation in PMR. Inverse associations between tracer uptake and recent glucocorticoid exposure suggest potential treatment-related modulation. The associations between MMPs, sVAP-1, and tracer uptake provide hypothesis-generating insights into a VAP-1/MMP-axis potentially shaping the PET signal. Our findings position [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-Siglec-9 PET/CT as a promising inflammation-specific biomarker for disease activity assessment and phenotyping in PMR and GCA.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of atinvicitinib and oclacitinib in the control of pruritus in canine allergic dermatitis: a randomized, examiner-masked, positive-controlled multicenter clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atinvicitinib is a Janus kinase 1-selective-inhibitor approved for the treatment of pruritus associated with allergic dermatitis, including canine atopic dermatitis (cAD). An examiner-masked, randomized study assessed safety and clinical improvement in pruritus and dermatitis severity in dogs with allergic dermatitis following treatment with atinvicitinib (Numelvi® tablets, MSD Animal Health) or oclacitinib (Apoquel® chewable tablets, Zoetis).

RESULTS: Client-owned dogs (n = 69) with allergic dermatitis and a pruritus visual analog scale (PVAS) score ≥ 6 were enrolled at nine veterinary clinics in Portugal and Spain and treated with either atinvicitinib (0.8-1.2 mg/kg once daily with food, n = 34) or oclacitinib (0.4-0.6 mg/kg, with or without food, twice daily for 14 days then once daily, n = 35) for 28 (± 1) days. Safety was assessed based on adverse event (AE) reporting. Owners assessed PVAS on day (D) 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28, including overall response to treatment (ORTT-VAS) on D28. Veterinarians performed physical examinations and dermatitis VAS score (DVAS) on D0 and 28. Efficacy was evaluated as the percentage reduction in PVAS and DVAS from baseline. A dynamic longitudinal model was used to compare effectiveness between groups. On D28, 70% atinvicitinib- and 65% oclacitinib-treated dogs had PVAS < 2 (normal). Dynamic longitudinal modelling showed that pruritus reduction after 28 days of atinvicitinib was non-inferior to that with oclacitinib at label doses. There was a 74% reduction in DVAS in both treatments by D28. All of the few AEs observed were consistent with approved product information.

CONCLUSIONS: Atinvicitinib once daily with food is safe and effective in reducing pruritus and dermatitis severity in dogs with allergic dermatitis.

articles.title: Nile Red-positive submicron event burden in induced sputum is associated with eosinophilic inflammation and remodeling-related biomarkers in severe asthma.
articles.abstract: Human exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics has raised concerns about respiratory health, but evidence linking airway particulate signals to severe asthma remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified Nile Red-positive submicron events in induced sputum from 32 patients with severe asthma and 11 healthy controls using chemical digestion, fluorescence staining, and flow cytometry. Clinical characteristics, inflammatory phenotypes, and immunological biomarkers were assessed. Nile Red-positive events were detected in all samples. Event burden per gram of sputum dry weight was higher in severe asthma than in controls in unadjusted analysis (median 3232 versus 1730 events/g; p = 0.042), but the association was not statistically significant after adjustment for age, body mass index, and smoking status (B = 0.364; p = 0.122). Among severe asthma phenotypes, eosinophilic T2 asthma exhibited the highest event burden. Positive correlations were observed with blood and sputum eosinophilia and with MMP-3, MMP-9, and PDGF-BB, biomarkers related to airway remodeling. However, Nile Red fluorescence does not establish polymer identity, and the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation using polymer-specific analytical methods and appropriately matched cohorts.

articles.title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) with long-term survival outcomes in Chinese patients with coronary artery disease: A large-scale cohort study from the CIN-II registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, data on Lp(a) distribution and prognostic thresholds in Asian patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) remain limited and may differ from Western populations. This study investigated the association of Lp(a) with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in CAD patients.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 51,489 patients with CAD (mean age, 62.7 years; 23.5% female) from the Cardiorenal Improvement-II (CIN-II) registry. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models assessed associations of Lp(a) categories (<30, 30-50, ≥50 mg/dL) with cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis investigated the Lp(a) dose-response relationship with mortality. Mediation analysis evaluated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) and fibrinogen (FIB) as mediators.

RESULTS: Among 51,489 participants, the median Lp(a) was 17.2 mg/dL (interquartile range [IQR]: 9.0-37.1 mg/dL), with 12.77% (n = 6577) and 18.10% (n = 9317) having 30-50 and ≥ 50 mg/dL. During the median 5.2-year follow-up, 3833 (7.44%) cardiovascular and 8332 (16.18%) all-cause mortality occurred. After multivariable adjustment, patients with Lp(a) of 30-50 mg/dL and ≥50 mg/dL had higher cardiovascular mortality risk (hazard ratio [HR] 1.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.20-1.45; HR 1.42, 95% CI 1.31-1.54; both p < 0.001). RCS analysis demonstrated a non-linear association with cardiovascular mortality, rising to a plateau (p for non-linearity < 0.001). Hs-CRP and FIB statistically mediated 3.55% and 23.80% of Lp(a) association with cardiovascular mortality (both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of CAD patients had Lp(a) ≥30 mg/dL. Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with increased risk of cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, with this association statistically mediated by inflammation and fibrinolysis.

articles.title: Imaging the Tumor Microenvironment Versus Somatostatin Receptor Expression in Meningioma: A Pilot Intraindividual Comparison of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to perform a preliminary, intraindividual comparison of [68Ga]Ga-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-46 and [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-(Tyr³)-octreotate (DOTATATE) PET/CT for meningioma imaging. While [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET, targeting somatostatin receptor 2, is established in meningioma evaluation, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI PET, targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP) in the tumor microenvironment, offers a novel diagnostic approach.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Five female patients with meningiomas underwent both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT scans. A comprehensive comparison was conducted at both patient and lesion levels. Quantitative parameters, including maximum and mean standardized uptake values (SUVmax, SUVmean), metabolic tumor volumes [FAP expression tumor volume, somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-expressing tumor volume], and total lesion expression (total lesion FAP expression, total lesion SSTR expression), were analyzed.

RESULTS: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET demonstrated superior lesion detection, identifying 21 lesions compared with 19 detected by [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET. At both patient and lesion levels, [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE showed significantly higher tracer uptake and total lesion expression. The patient-level median SUVmax was 27.3 for [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE versus 6.93 for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 (P = 0.04). At the lesion level, the median SUVmax was 10.63 for [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE versus 2.52 for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 (P = 0.0001). Despite these differences, significant positive correlations were observed between the quantitative parameters of both tracers at the lesion level (eg, SUVmax R = 0.69, P = 0.001; total lesion FAP expression/total lesion SSTR expression R = 0.84, P = 0.0001). In addition, both FAP-expressing tumor volume and SSTR-expressing tumor volume strongly correlated with MRI tumor size.

CONCLUSIONS: [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET demonstrated superior lesion detection and significantly higher uptake intensity in meningiomas compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET, reinforcing DOTATATE PET's established role as a highly effective imaging modality. The lower yet present FAPI uptake and the strong positive correlation between the two tracers suggest a potential complementary role for FAPI imaging, possibly reflecting an interplay between tumor cells and their microenvironment. These preliminary findings warrant further investigation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: 18F-FAPI-04 PET/CT in the Diagnosis of IgG4-Related Hypertrophic Pachymeningitis: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-related hypertrophic pachymeningitis (IgG4-RHP) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder with high biopsy risk. A 58-year-old man had a 2-year history of persistent headache. Brain MRI revealed craniocervical dural thickening. Dual-tracer ¹⁸F-FDG and ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT were performed. Compared with ¹⁸F-FDG, ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT showed higher radiotracer uptake intensity and sharper lesion demarcation, and additionally uncovered occult inflammatory lesions that were invisible on ¹⁸F-FDG imaging. Elevated serum IgG4 confirmed the diagnosis, which fulfilled the 2019 ACR/EULAR IgG4-RD criteria. For patients unsuitable for biopsy, ¹⁸F-FAPI-04 PET/CT offers unique diagnostic advantages for this rare disease.

articles.title: Tumefactive Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System Mimicking High-Grade Glioma on F-18 FDG PET/CT.
articles.abstract: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system (PACNS) rarely presents as an F-18 FDG-avid mass lesion. A 44-year-old man presented with acute slurred speech and right hemiparesis. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a left fronto-temporo-insular mass. F-18 FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography showed intense uptake (SUVmax 12.7; lesion-to-contralateral mirror-ROI ratio 3.3; lesion-to-cortex ratio 1.2), suggesting high-grade glioma, whereas whole-body imaging excluded systemic disease. Resection histopathology identified the mass as PACNS, lymphocytic type, and the patient recovered completely after immunosuppressive therapy. Notably, reported F-18 FDG findings in PACNS are inconsistent; intense avidity does not exclude the diagnosis, and histopathologic confirmation is essential before oncologic treatment.

articles.title: Centiloid Scaling in Probable Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy: Discrimination From Deep Perforator Arteriopathy and Associations With Neuroimaging Markers and Cognition.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Centiloid (CL) scaling quantifies amyloid-β plaque burden in Alzheimer disease, but its utility in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is uncertain. We evaluated the ability of CL to discriminate probable CAA from deep perforator arteriopathy (DPA) among patients with small vessel disease (SVD) and examined its associations with neuroimaging markers and cognition.

METHODS: We enrolled 92 patients with probable CAA and 27 patients with DPA. CL values were derived from [11C]PiB PET. Classification performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic and decision curve analyses. Associations with MRI markers and cognitive function were examined using correlation and regression models.

RESULTS: CL scaling showed good discrimination between CAA and DPA (AUC: 0.837, 95% CI: 0.733-0.905). A cutoff of 5.2 yielded 78.3% sensitivity and 88.9% specificity. Higher CL values were associated with lobar microbleed burden (P<0.001), cortical superficial siderosis (P=0.002), and centrum semiovale enlarged perivascular spaces (P=0.007), as well as the CAA score (P<0.001), but not the total SVD score. After covariate adjustment, higher CL values were independently associated with lower MMSE scores (β=-0.048, P=0.025) and a trend toward greater CDR severity (OR=1.012, P=0.052). Adding CL to a clinical-MRI model improved discrimination (ΔAUC=0.077, 95% CI: 0.010-0.175, P=0.025).

CONCLUSIONS: CL scaling discriminates clinically defined probable CAA from DPA in sporadic SVD. Higher CL values are associated with greater CAA-related MRI burden and worse cognitive performance.

articles.title: Long-Term Cognitive Function Following Haloperidol Vs. Placebo Treatment in ICU Patients With Delirium.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effects of haloperidol vs. placebo on long-term cognitive function in formerly critically ill patients with ICU delirium, 1 year after randomization in the Agents Intervening against Delirium in the ICU (AID-ICU) randomized clinical trial.

DESIGN: Pre-planned 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU trial conducted from June 2019 to April 2023.

SETTING: Three university-affiliated ICUs in Denmark.

PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients previously enrolled in the AID-ICU trial.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients in the AID-ICU were randomized to either haloperidol or placebo (0.9% saline) when treated for delirium in the ICU.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The primary outcome was global cognitive function at 1 year, assessed using Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychologic Status (RBANS) Global Index Score Secondary outcomes including domain-specific RBANS scores and executive function, measured by the Trail Making Test A and B. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Non-survivors were assigned the lowest possible score on each outcome, reflecting death as a competing outcome. Missing data among survivors were handled using multiple imputations. Of the 632 randomized patients, 624 were included. Cognitive outcome data were available for 134 of 343 surviving patients: 67 in the haloperidol group and 67 in the placebo group. Median global cognitive scores were 40 (interquartile range [IQR]: 40-75) in the haloperidol group and 40 (IQR: 40-72) in the placebo group (mean difference: 2; 95% CI, -3 to 7; p = 0.48). No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. Given the high proportion of missing data, best-worst and worst-best sensitivity analyses were performed, yielding estimates in opposite directions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this 1-year follow-up of the AID-ICU treatment with haloperidol for delirium in the ICU was not associated with improved long-term cognitive function compared with placebo. However, given the extent of missing outcome data and the divergent results of our sensitivity analyses, this estimate should be interpreted as imprecise rather than conclusive; clinically relevant effects of pharmacologic delirium treatment on cognition cannot be excluded, and future adequately powered studies with more complete follow-up are warranted.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes: Why Methodology Matters.
Making AI Use Visible: Assignment-Specific AI Guidance and Student Disclosure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite growing calls for student transparency about artificial intelligence (AI) use in nursing education, little is known about what AI disclosure looks like in practice.

PURPOSE: This study describes the adaptation of the Artificial Intelligence Assessment Scale for use as assignment-specific AI guidance and examines the resulting disclosure statements.

METHODS: Using a case study design, AI disclosure statements were collected from 2 offerings of a fully online undergraduate nursing course (n = 448 coded units) and analyzed using qualitative content analysis and descriptive and inferential statistics.

RESULTS: Most assignments (448/658, 68%) included a disclosure statement, though rates varied substantially by assignment. Among AI-use disclosures, most met a basic standard of transparency; approximately one quarter demonstrated deeper professional accountability. Significant associations were identified between how students characterized their AI use and alignment with assignment guidance.

CONCLUSIONS: Assignment-specific AI guidance shows promise for eliciting student disclosure, though students need additional support to disclose with professional depth.

articles.title: Short-term loop diuretic withdrawal in optimized heart failure with diabetes: A pilot randomized study integrating POCUS and NT-proBNP for congestion monitoring.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Loop diuretics (LD) are central in the management of heart failure (HF) congestion. However, prolonged use may contribute to poor outcomes and adverse events. Evidence supporting safe withdrawal of LD and appropriate patient selection among ambulatory HF patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains limited. We evaluated the safety of LD withdrawal, utilizing multiparametric congestion monitoring, and factors associated with congestion development in such patients.

METHODS: Sixty ambulatory HF patients with T2DM were randomized to either continuation or withdrawal of LD, in our open-label pilot study. Participants underwent assessment for congestion (subclinical and clinical) using a multiparametric approach, including lung ultrasound, venous excess ultrasound, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), and six-minute walk test.

RESULTS: In this study, 35.0% of participants developed congestion (31.7% subclinical and 15.0% clinical). There were no significant differences for subclinical (36.7% vs 26.7%; p=0.405), clinical (20.0% vs 10.0%; p=0.278), or composite congestion (43.4% vs 26.7%; p=0.176) between both study arms. Abnormal hepatic vein Doppler patterns (possibly suggestive of subclinical congestion) were more frequent in the LD withdrawal arm (16.7% vs 0.0%; p=0.020). Elevated baseline NT-proBNP was independently associated with subclinical (odds ratio [OR] 1.448; p=0.008), clinical (OR 1.737; p<0.001) and composite congestion (OR 1.480; p=0.015) in exploratory multivariable analyses.

CONCLUSION: In this pilot open-label study, short-term loop diuretic withdrawal in carefully selected, clinically euvolemic ambulatory HF patients with T2DM, was feasible and not associated with a statistically significant excess of clinical or subclinical congestion over 4 weeks. These findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicentre trials with longer follow-up and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Mindful Yoga and Expressive Arts on Perceived Stress and Whole-Person Health in Individuals With Mild-to-Moderate Parkinson Disease: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People with Parkinson disease (PD) experience substantial motor, nonmotor, and psychosocial burdens that are often inadequately addressed by pharmacological treatments alone. Mind-body interventions (MBIs), including mindful yoga and expressive arts therapy (EXAT), have shown promise in alleviating stress, increasing quality of life, and improving whole-person health. However, evidence of their comparative effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remains limited, leaving clinicians and patients with little guidance when selecting between these interventions. This study aims to fill this gap.

OBJECTIVE: This trial aims to compare the effectiveness of mindful yoga and EXAT in reducing perceived stress, increasing quality of life, and improving whole-person health in people with PD. A secondary aim is to examine potential mechanisms of action, including functional, psychosocial, and gut microbiome-related pathways.

METHODS: We are conducting a 2-arm, parallel-group, active-comparator randomized controlled trial. People with PD are randomly assigned to receive either mindful yoga or EXAT, delivered in six 90-minute sessions every 2 weeks. The primary outcomes are perceived stress and PD-related quality of life. Secondary outcomes include PD-related symptoms and broader quality of life. Potential mediators will cover biopsychosocial domains, including biological and physical factors (gut microbiota, constipation severity and bowel habits, and physical activity) and psychosocial factors (self-compassion, self-efficacy, and perceived social support). Motor assessments are conducted using Mon4t and BooGuu Aspire Fall Risk Management mobile apps. Fecal samples are collected to generate reproducible taxonomic and functional profiles of the gut microbiota. Outcomes are assessed at baseline and 3 months, 9 months, and 12 months after baseline assessment. Comparative effectiveness will be evaluated using linear mixed models, and potential mechanisms, including psychosocial and microbiome features, will be examined through path analysis. We hypothesize that both interventions will reduce stress, increase quality of life, and improve whole-person health, but they will demonstrate different pathways across biopsychosocial domains.

RESULTS: This study was funded in April 2023, and ethics approval was granted in May 2024. Participant recruitment and data collection began in May 2024 and are ongoing. As of the submission of the manuscript, 144 participants had finished pre- and postintervention assessments (72 in each arm). Final follow-ups are still ongoing. Data analysis has not yet started, and primary findings are expected to be published in December 2026.

CONCLUSIONS: By directly comparing 2 active MBIs and integrating biopsychosocial-spiritual domains, this trial will provide comparative evidence on the effectiveness of MBIs. The findings are intended to guide the selection of mind-body approaches in PD, supporting preference-sensitive, whole-person care and informing integrative models that address the complex needs of this population.

articles.title: Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Outcomes in Patients of Advanced Age (PFO-COPA): Protocol for a Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) is a common cardiac abnormality associated with paradoxical embolism and ischemic stroke. Randomized trials have demonstrated the benefit of percutaneous PFO closure in patients aged <60 years with cryptogenic stroke, but nearly all trials have excluded individuals aged ≥60 years, leaving a critical evidence gap in older populations, in whom competing stroke mechanisms are prevalent. There is currently no dedicated, validated framework to guide closure decisions in this age group. Consequently, clinical practice remains highly variable, and closure decisions are made based on extrapolation from younger cohorts rather than robust evidence.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of PFO closure compared with medical therapy in patients aged ≥60 years with cryptogenic stroke and a confirmed PFO.

METHODS: This multicenter international retrospective cohort study will include consecutive patients aged ≥60 years with imaging-confirmed ischemic stroke, a confirmed PFO, and no alternative definite etiology of stroke after standard diagnostic evaluation, who underwent either percutaneous PFO closure or medical therapy between 2015 and 2025. Outcomes will be collected through standardized chart review and entered into a centralized REDCap database. The primary outcome will be the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke. Secondary outcomes will include major bleeding, new-onset atrial fibrillation, device-related complications, and mortality. Time-to-event analyses, Cox regression, and propensity score methods will be used to adjust for confounding.

RESULTS: As of October 2026, 51 centers from 10 countries (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Greece, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Portugal, Spain, and the United States) have formally agreed to participate in the study. Each site is currently in the process of securing institutional review board (IRB) approval and executing data use agreements. A standardized variable dictionary has been distributed to all centers to ensure consistency in data collection. As of October 2026, 45 centers have applied for local IRB approval, 5 centers have obtained IRB approval, and 3 centers have begun data entry into REDCap. The projected end date of data collection is June 2027. Participating centers are encouraged to propose independent research questions leveraging the pooled dataset. As of October 2026, 23 project titles have been submitted by investigators. These proposals will be evaluated once sufficient data have been accrued. Preliminary pooled analyses are anticipated for release in July 2027.

CONCLUSIONS: The PFO-COPA (Patent Foramen Ovale Closure Outcomes in Patients of Advanced Age) study will generate the most comprehensive real-world evidence to date on PFO closure in adults aged ≥60 years. By evaluating both effectiveness and safety in this understudied age group, the study will fill a major evidence gap and help guide clinical decision-making. Ultimately, these findings may inform future guideline updates and lay the groundwork for prospective multicenter trials focused specifically on older adults.

articles.title: Comparison between fixed-dose combination pioglitazone-metformin and sitagliptin-metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes exhibiting poor glycemic control: A multicenter clinical trial.
12-month trajectories of anxiety symptoms and functional recovery after new-onset stroke: A multicenter prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The longitudinal course of poststroke anxiety remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to delineate the trajectories of anxiety symptoms within 12 months post-stroke and evaluate their associations with functional recovery.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort study enrolled patients with new-onset stroke from 2018 to 2021. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the 14-item Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA) at 2 weeks and at 3, 6, and 12 months. Latent class growth modeling and growth mixture modeling identified latent trajectory classes. Multivariate logistic regression evaluated the association between anxiety trajectory and 12-month functional outcome (modified Rankin scale).

RESULTS: Among 1934 patients (1357 males; mean age 58.8 ± 10.9 years), the median initial HAMA score was 8 (4,13). Two distinct anxiety trajectories were identified: a low-decreasing group (1538 [79.5%]) with mild, descending symptoms (intercept, 8.400; mean difference, -3.510), and a high-increasing group (396 [20.5%]) characterized by escalating and persistent anxiety, with changes occurring predominantly within the first 3 months (intercept, 12.508; mean difference, 4.471). Female, moderate-to-severe stroke, depressive symptoms, poor sleep, and low resilience were independent risk factors of the high-increasing trajectory (all p < 0.01). Crucially, this trajectory was significantly associated with poor functional recovery at 12 months (aOR, 2.24; 99% CI, 1.58-3.17).

CONCLUSIONS: A trajectory of increasing and persistent anxiety, identified in one-fifth of acute stroke patients, was independently associated with 12-month disability. These findings necessitate a paradigm shift from static, cross-sectional assessment to longitudinal tracking of anxiety symptoms, particularly during the first 3 months post-stroke, to improve functional outcomes.

articles.title: Ocular Complications After 1000 Centistoke Silicone Oil Removal in Patients With Previous Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment Repair.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine the incidence, types, and outcomes of complications associated with silicone oil (SO) removal in eyes that received 1000 centistoke SO as a tamponade for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD).

METHODS: Patients with RRD who received 1000 centistoke SO tamponade and had at least 3 months of follow-up were reviewed for complications after SO removal, including ocular hypertension, hypotony, cystoid macular edema (CME), epiretinal membrane (ERM), recurrent RD, residual SO, corneal edema, and uveitis.

RESULTS: A total of 156 eyes of 156 patients were included. The median follow-up time after SO removal was 2.5 years, with an interquartile range (IQR) of 1.5 to 3.6 years. At the time of SO removal, 144 eyes (92%) had complete retinal attachment. The median time from vitrectomy with SO tamponade to SO removal was 5.6 months (IQR, 4.1-7.7 months). Retinal redetachment occurred in 34 eyes (22%) at a median of 32 days (IQR, 5.5-189 days) after SO removal. Hypotony occurred in 6% of eyes at 7 days (IQR, 1-36 days) and ocular hypertension in 11% at 36 days (IQR, 1-131 days). ERM (28%), CME (15%), and uveitis (10%) also developed with variable times of onset.

CONCLUSIONS: A large majority of eyes achieved retinal attachment. Despite these favorable anatomic outcomes, a large percentage of eyes had postoperative complications, including redetachment, ocular hypertension, hypotony, ERM, and CME. Due to the wide time range of onset for complications, regular long-term follow-up is recommended for patients after SO removal.

articles.title: Fulminant Early-Onset Sepsis Caused by Multidrug-Resistant Aeromonas hydrophila in a Preterm Neonate: A Case Report and Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract: Aeromonas hydrophila is a rare but virulent pathogen in neonates, historically associated with aquatic environments. However, the emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) strains presenting as early-onset sepsis (EOS) poses a severe diagnostic and therapeutic dilemma. We report a fatal case of a preterm neonate (33 weeks gestation) who developed fulminant septic shock at 20 hours of life. Despite the initiation of broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam), the clinical course rapidly progressed to pulmonary hemorrhage and death at 26 hours of life. Blood cultures subsequently confirmed Aeromonas hydrophila septicemia with high-level resistance to carbapenems (Meropenem MIC > 16 μg/mL) and piperacillin-tazobactam (MIC > 128 μg/mL). This case highlights the growing threat of nonfermenting MDR gram-negative organisms in EOS and underscores the limitations of standard empiric regimens against atypical pathogens.

articles.title: Ten Years of Training in a Male World-Class 800-1500 m Swimmer.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the training process of a world-class 800- to 1500-m swimmer and identify key characteristics and differences between successful and less successful competitive seasons.

METHODS: A mixed-methods case study design was used to capture quantitative and qualitative aspects of the training process. Data were collected through (1) 10 years of training logs (ages 19-28); (2) in-depth semistructured interviews with the swimmer, his club coach, and national team head coach; and (3) systematic quality assurance through negotiation among researchers and key informants.

RESULTS: Performance improved gradually until 23 to 24 years of age before slightly declining. Annual training volume ranged from ∼1000 to ∼1380 hours per year, with swimming accounting for ∼80% of total training time in most seasons (2700-3700 km·y-1), including extensive long-course, stroke-specific training. The swimmer followed a traditional periodization model with 3 macrocycles annually, characterized by high volumes of low-intensity training during preparation and increased intensity with reduced volume approaching competition. A later shift toward more zone 2 training at the expense of zone 1 and reduced long-course exposure coincided with the performance decline in his mid-twenties. Successful seasons were characterized by high quality in the holistic training process, including strong motivation and structured recovery, whereas less successful seasons were marked by slightly weaker recovery habits, and declining motivation and self-confidence.

CONCLUSION: This study provides novel information regarding the training process for a world-class long-distance swimmer, including differences between successful and less successful seasons. These data may serve as a framework for practitioners aiming to optimize long-term performance development.

articles.title: Infections following dental extractions in dogs are rare both with and without antimicrobial therapy based on a 10-year retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report postoperative local infection rates in dogs undergoing dental extractions with versus without antimicrobial treatment.

METHODS: Medical records were reviewed for dogs undergoing dental extractions at a single institution between 2014 and 2024. Use of prophylactic antimicrobials and presence of postoperative infection were recorded. The impact of different risk factors on the presence of infection was assessed with logistic regression. The number needed to treat to prevent infection in 1 dog was calculated with inverse absolute risk reduction.

RESULTS: Antimicrobial usage was common, with 62.8% (573 of 913) of dogs receiving antimicrobials. The overall rate of postoperative infections was 0.66% (6 of 913 dogs). Patients prescribed an antimicrobial had decreased odds (OR, 0.16) of postoperative infection (0.2% with and 1.5% without). However, 76 patients (95% CI, 30 to 399 patients) had to be treated unnecessarily with prophylactic antimicrobials to prevent infection in a single patient. Neither the number of extractions nor the severity of periodontal disease increased the odds of infection; rather, they were protective (OR, 0.1 to 0.2). No other risk factors were significantly associated with infection rate. All patients with identified infection at the postoperative recheck had resolution of infection with appropriate treatment. Both perioperative and postoperative extraction complications were rare, at 5.4% and 4.9% of visits, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative infection is rare with dental extractions, regardless of the number of extractions, the severity of periodontal disease, or antimicrobial use.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study provides evidence against the use of antimicrobial prophylaxis during dental extractions in immunocompetent dogs. Rather, treatment is recommended in the rare case that surgical site infections occur.

articles.title: Development and Evaluation of a Metadata-Driven Rule Repository and Daily Screening System for Diagnosis Coding Compliance Under the Korean New Diagnosis-Related Group Payment System: Implementation Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Under the new diagnosis-related group (NDRG) payment system in Korea, the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service (HIRA) applies disease-specific diagnosis coding approval criteria that differ from the coding guidelines of the Korean Classification of Diseases (KCD), frequently leading to claim denials for conditions such as acute kidney injury, pleural effusion, and malnutrition. Repeated denials also induce conservative down-coding among coders. Because denial notifications are issued 9 to 18 months after discharge, reactive, denial-triggered quality management is insufficient.

OBJECTIVE: We implemented a metadata-driven rule repository that operationalizes HIRA's review criteria as data, coupled with a daily-refreshed screening data mart (encompassing 6 clinical data domains and 14 data sources) and a robotic process automation (RPA) notification pipeline, to enable proactive, preclaim coding quality management.

METHODS: This Implementation Report describes the design, deployment, and 12-month operational experience of the system at an 820-bed NDRG pilot hospital. HIRA's criteria were externalized into a 4-layer rule repository-criteria definitions, clinical concepts, disease-specific attributes, and decision rules. A nightly extract, transform, and load pipeline populates a patient-by-attribute screening data mart within the clinical data warehouse; each morning, Python-based RPA compiles and emails review candidate lists to coders. Descriptive statistics summarized coverage and detection outcomes; precision (equivalent to positive predictive value) was calculated with Wilson score 95% CIs.

UNLABELLED: At the end of the evaluation period, the rule repository comprised 11 review criteria, 271 clinical concepts, 77 attributes, and 96 decision rules. Over the 12-month evaluation period (July 2025 to June 2026), the system evaluated 17,138 diagnosis- or episode-level targets across 15,388 distinct episodes-67% of the hospital's 22,970 NDRG episodes-and flagged 576 (3.4%) review candidates, of which 50 (8.7%, 95% CI 6.6%-11.3%) were confirmed by coders as actual coding errors. The proportion of confirmed coding errors among review candidates differed significantly across the 3 monitored categories (χ22=39.9; P<.001): present-on-admission (POA) coding items showed the highest precision (20/82, 24%), followed by the NDRG cost-outlier category (17/134, 12.7%) and frequently denied diagnoses (13/360, 3.6%). The system was designed, built, and operated by existing departmental staff without additional budget or dedicated IT support, required an estimated 1 to 1.5 hours of coder review time per week, and has continued to operate daily on weekdays since launch.

CONCLUSIONS: A metadata-driven rule repository integrated with a daily screening data mart and RPA can operationalize payer review criteria as versioned data rather than hard-coded logic, enabling proactive coding surveillance before claim submission. The approach was implemented without additional budget or dedicated IT staff, but its performance may vary across institutions. Further validation against formal HIRA review outcomes and multi-institutional evaluation are needed to establish its performance and transferability across NDRG hospitals.

articles.title: Health Utility of Thai Patients With Heart Failure Using EQ-5D-5L Instrument.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess health utility in Thai patients with heart failure and to determine the clinical and sociodemographic factors associated with their health status using the EQ-5D-5-Level (EQ-5D-5L) and EuroQol visual analog scale (EQ-VAS) instruments.

METHODS: This cross-sectional secondary analysis of baseline randomized controlled trial data was carried out at Ayutthaya Hospital between November 2022 and May 2023. Patients were interviewed to evaluate their health status. Health utility scores were derived using Thai-specific value sets. Univariate and multivariable Tobit regression models, alongside multivariable logistic regression analyses, were applied to determine independent predictors and dimensional problems.

RESULTS: Among 250 patients (mean age 63.5 ± 12.1 years, 54% female, and 59% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction), mean EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS scores were 0.82 ± 0.18 and 74.0 ± 14.5. Multivariable logistic regression revealed that age, higher education, medication burden, and diabetes mellitus significantly predicted problems in specific dimensions. In univariate analyses, older age, female sex, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, higher comorbidity, medication burden, diabetes mellitus, and hypertension lowered EQ-5D-5L scores, whereas higher income and higher education increased utility scores; meanwhile, hyperlipidemia, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and higher comorbidity reduced EQ-VAS scores. Multivariable Tobit models showed that older age, female sex, and higher medication burden independently predicted lower utility scores.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study, health utility was determined more by age, sex, and overall medication burden than by ejection fraction subtypes. These results offer key empirical inputs for national health technology assessment processes and for guiding resource allocation to strengthen medication optimization initiatives and patient-centered strategies focused on older adults and women.

articles.title: Bedside Diagnosis of Biventricular Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy With Isolated Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated right ventricular outflow tract obstruction is a rare phenotype of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), usually recognized only on imaging.

CASE SUMMARY: A 51-year-old man presented with mild exertional dyspnea and an abnormal electrocardiogram; his brother had died suddenly at 31 years of age. Before any imaging, bedside examination revealed a giant jugular a-wave without a y-descent, a fourth heart sound louder at the left sternal border than at the apex, and a systolic ejection murmur that increased on sitting and during expiration (reversed Rivero-Carvallo sign). These findings predicted biventricular HCM with right ventricular outflow tract obstruction but without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, confirmed by echocardiography, catheterization, and endomyocardial biopsy.

DISCUSSION: Jugular venous waveform analysis, multisite auscultation, and simple postural and respiratory maneuvers can both suggest HCM and localize the site of outflow obstruction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In HCM, a systolic murmur that intensifies with expiration should prompt consideration of right-sided obstruction.

articles.title: Genotype and Phenotype in Concert: An Imagenomics Approach to Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
Blood Pressure Elevation in Individuals with XY DSD: Clinical Insights from the I-DSD Registry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: XY Differences of Sex Development (DSD) may have an increased risk of high blood pressure (BP) and accelerated vascular ageing. This could be related to reduced exposure to androgens in utero and in later life.

METHODS: Data were obtained from centres using the International DSD (I-DSD) Registry on males with XY DSD.

RESULTS: At study initiation, 2,400 individuals with XY DSD were on the I-DSD Registry. Twenty-three centres worldwide participated in the study, with BP readings provided from 282 (32%) (median (range) age 10 (2, 68) years) of 875 eligible cases of boys and men with XY DSD. The most common diagnoses were non-specific XY DSD in (45%); disorders of gonadal development in 64 (23%); and disorders of androgen synthesis in 36 (13%). Of these, 76/282 (27%) had elevated or hypertensive BPs including 42/214 (20%) of boys <16 years old. In multivariable linear regression, systolic blood pressure SDS in boys was significantly associated with age (β 0.8, 95% CI 0.3-1.3, p=0.004) and presence of obesity (β 11.3, 95% CI 1.1-21.5, p=0.03), with no association seen according to presence of co-existing anomaly, type of underlying DSD, gestation at birth, birthweight or family history of hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly 1 in 4 people with XY DSD have an elevated BP at clinic, with 20% of boys with XY DSD being hypertensive at clinic review, and no clear differences between types of DSD seen. These findings highlight the importance of BP assessment as routine for individuals with XY DSD.

articles.title: MXene/berberine-loaded hydrogel microneedle patches for the regeneration of infected skin wounds.
articles.abstract: Bacteria-infected skin wounds remain challenging to treat because persistent infection, excessive oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration create an interconnected pathological microenvironment that hinders tissue healing. Herein, we developed a multifunctional polymeric hydrogel microneedle (PHMN) platform incorporating MXene/berberine (MX/BBR) conjugates to achieve localized, near-infrared (NIR)-triggered antibacterial therapy, antioxidant protection, and tissue regeneration. The PHMNs were fabricated by photocrosslinking methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA) containing MX/BBR onto a poly(vinyl alcohol) backing layer, generating well-defined microneedle arrays with adequate mechanical strength, favorable cytocompatibility, controlled degradation, and sustained BBR release. The integration of MX/BBR conjugates into the hydrogel microneedle platform provides NIR-responsive photothermal activity and sustained BBR release, offering a multifunctional strategy for antibacterial treatment and wound repair. Upon 808 nm NIR irradiation, the constructed PHMN/MX/BBR patches exhibited potent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, while effectively protecting cells against oxidative stress and promoting cell migration and endothelial tube formation. In a S. aureus-infected full-thickness skin wound model, combined PHMN/MX/BBR treatment and NIR irradiation markedly accelerated wound closure and enhanced re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, and tissue remodelling, without apparent systemic toxicity. Unlike conventional wound dressings that primarily provide passive protection or single-mode antibacterial treatment, this platform integrates localized delivery, externally activated photothermal therapy, and intrinsic antioxidant activity to simultaneously address infection, oxidative stress, and impaired tissue regeneration. Collectively, this work establishes MX/BBR-integrated hydrogel microneedles as a multifunctional and minimally invasive strategy for the coordinated management of bacteria-infected wounds.

articles.title: In vivo comparison of V.A.C.® Granufoam Silver™ and V.A.C.® Granufoam™ loaded with CZ-01179, a first-in-class bis-dialkylnorspermidine-terphenyl antibiofilm agent, in a porcine excision model.
articles.abstract: Biofilm-related infections remain a persistent challenge in chronic and traumatic wounds, particularly when delayed intervention, environmental exposure, and multidrug resistance complicate management. Many of these wounds are treated with negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT), yet current antimicrobial NPWT foams have limited antibiofilm activity. CZ-01179 is a first-in-class antibiofilm compound with demonstrated in vitro and ex vivo efficacy when incorporated into polyurethane foam for NPWT. This study evaluated CZ-01179-loaded foam in a large-scale in vivo porcine excision wound model. Full-thickness excision wounds were created on the dorsum of Yorkshire pigs and inoculated three times with mature methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or Acinetobacter baumannii biofilms. Wounds were treated for 7 days with 10.0% w/w CZ-01179-loaded Granufoam™, Granufoam™ alone, or Granufoam Silver™ under continuous NPWT. Natural flora growth was also assessed. Quantitative cultures were obtained from tissue biopsies, reported as Log10 colony forming units (CFU)/g tissue, and compared across groups. CZ-01179-loaded foam resulted in >3 Log10 CFU/g lower MRSA and A. baumannii bioburden than Granufoam™ or Granufoam Silver™ (p ≤ 0.00013). Similar efficacy was observed against natural polymicrobial flora. The porcine model validated robust biofilm-related infection and enabled translational assessment of an NPWT-compatible antibiofilm therapy. CZ-01179 demonstrated potent antibiofilm activity when combined with NPWT, providing in vivo confirmation of its efficacy in a clinically relevant large-animal model. Its stability, protease resistance, and hydrogel-based delivery support further development as a field-deployable therapy for complex wound infections, including combat-related wounds.

articles.title: Care for Sexually Transmitted Infections among Transgender Women Provided by Family Health Strategy Nurses in Brazil: A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract: This cross-sectional study examined sexually transmitted infection (STI)-related care for transgender women (TGW) reported by Family Health Strategy (FHS) nurses in Brazil and factors associated with its provision. From June 2023 to March 2024, 442 FHS nurses were recruited through non-probability referral-based sampling. An online questionnaire assessed professional characteristics, TGW care conditions, and STI-related care practices. Analyzes used descriptive statistics, chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, and multivariable Poisson regression with robust variance estimation. Multiple comparisons underwent false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment. Overall, 296 nurses (66.97%) reported providing STI-related care to TGW. The adjusted prevalence of care provision was 31% higher among nurses with training or qualifications in transgender health (aPR = 1.31, 95% CI 1.15-1.50) and 18% higher among those earning five or more minimum wages (aPR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.03-1.35). The income estimate showed greater statistical uncertainty after accounting for municipality-level clustering (p = 0.052), whereas the training association remained statistically significant. Among nurses reporting care provision, PrEP/PEP counseling was more frequently reported by trained than untrained nurses (90.59% vs. 75.36%; FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). Training in transgender health was associated with a higher prevalence of self-reported STI-related care provision for TGW, highlighting its relevance to public health nursing practice.

articles.title: Clinical presentation of Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch in an adolescent.
articles.abstract: We describe a 14-year-old boy (weight 32 kg, height 148 cm), who was brought to a tertiary care facility in North India, with complaints of progressive exertional dyspnoea, palpitations, and chest pain with a recent episode of moderate haemoptysis. Imaging findings include Chest PA-view demonstrated cardiomegaly with abnormal great vessel contour, prominent superior mediastinal shadow, and increased bilateral pulmonary vascular markings, suggestive of a single large arterial outflow tract. Similarly, transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed a large outlet ventricular septal defect (VSD) with a dilated single arterial trunk overriding the defect. Cardiac CT angiography confirmed a large outlet VSD and an interrupted aortic arch, with no continuity between the ascending and descending aorta. The right and left pulmonary arteries, descending aorta, and left subclavian artery arose directly from the truncal vessel, while a separate ascending aorta bifurcated into the right brachiocephalic and left common carotid arteries. This particular case brings a remarkably unusual paediatric presentation with Van Praagh Type A4 truncus arteriosus with interrupted aortic arch and emphasises the effects of late diagnosis. Due to the patient's severe pulmonary arterial hypertension, palliative care was the only option for treatment, and definitive surgical repair was not feasible.

articles.title: Sepsis-Induced NLRP3+ Macrophages Impair Spermatogenic Recovery Through Reprogramming of the Testicular Microenvironment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis can cause persistent multi-organ dysfunction, but its impact on male fertility and the mechanisms underlying impaired spermatogenic regeneration remain poorly defined. Here, integrating a murine sepsis model, single-cell transcriptomics and functional assays, we demonstrate that septic injury triggers spermatogonial proliferative arrest and niche dysfunction, leading to incomplete spermatogenic recovery. Single-cell analysis reveals a marked expansion and functional reprogramming of an NLRP3+ pro-inflammatory macrophage subset, accompanied by upregulation of Il1b and inflammasome-associated genes. Using ex vivo co-culture and conditioned-medium transfer, we show that NLRP3+ macrophage-derived IL-1β directly suppresses spermatogonial proliferation and disrupts niche integrity, and that NLRP3 inhibition reverses this damage. In vivo, NLRP3 inhibition similarly rescues spermatogonial proliferative capacity and preserves niche function. Notably, advanced age exacerbates this impairment of spermatogenic regeneration and prolongs NLRP3+ macrophage activation after sepsis. Transcription factor network analysis identifies AP-1 family members, particularly JUN, as candidate upstream regulators of this sustained activation. Our findings establish that sepsis-induced testicular dysfunction is driven by macrophage-intrinsic NLRP3 activation, with advanced age as a critical aggravating factor. Targeting of NLRP3 preserves spermatogenic capacity and represents a tractable therapeutic strategy for sepsis survivors, especially men of advanced age who exhibit the most severely compromised reproductive recovery.

articles.title: GZNG, a Chinese Herbal Formula, Ameliorates Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease via the NR5A2-Metallothionein Axis.
articles.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent global health burden with limited pharmacological options. Although Ganzaoning (GZN), a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulation, shows therapeutic promise, the molecular mechanisms underlying this complex herbal formula remain largely elusive. In this study, we evaluated GZNG, a modified formulation incorporating ginseng leaf, in both in vitro and murine models of MASLD. GZNG ameliorated disease progression by reducing hepatic steatosis, oxidative stress, inflammation, and fibrosis. Transcriptomic analysis of GZNG-treated livers identified metallothioneins (MTs) as the most prominently induced genes. Subsequently, Liver Receptor Homolog-1 (LRH-1, also known as Nr5a2) was predicted to be the upstream transcriptional regulator driving Mt1/2 induction by promoter motif analysis and siRNA-mediated knockdown in cultured cells. Further chemical profiling and molecular modeling identified ginsenoside F3, a constituent of GZNG, as a candidate ligand occupying the ligand-binding pocket of Nr5a2. A head-to-head comparison showed that GZNG exerted more pronounced therapeutic effects than the original GZN formulation. These findings not only establish Mt1/2 as transcriptional targets of Nr5a2 but also provide molecular evidence supporting the clinical potential of GZNG, thereby bridging traditional phytomedicine with modern molecular therapeutics.

articles.title: Cerebral redistribution in late-onset fetal growth restriction: relation between abnormalities of individual Doppler components and adverse outcomes.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cerebral redistribution consists of the preferential redirection of the arterial and well-oxygenated blood flow to the fetal brain and is commonly associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR) secondary to placental insufficiency. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the perinatal outcomes of fetuses with late-onset FGR and cerebral redistribution, examining whether outcomes differed according to the normality or abnormality of the individual Doppler components that determine a reduction in the cerebroplacental ratio (CPR).

METHODS: This was a retrospective, multicenter cohort study conducted across four tertiary maternity units in Italy (University of Parma, Parma; Fondazione Policlinico Universitario 'A. Gemelli' IRCCS, Rome; IRCCS Materno Infantile Burlo Garofolo, Trieste; and University of Brescia, Brescia), including non-anomalous singleton pregnancies complicated by late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution (defined as CPR < 5th percentile according to the Fetal Medicine Foundation reference charts). The study included cases collected at the four participating units between January 2019 and December 2024. Cases were categorized according to umbilical artery (UA) and middle cerebral artery (MCA) Doppler data (Group 1: normal UA-pulsatility index (PI) (≤ 95th percentile for gestational age) and MCA-PI (≥ 5th percentile); Group 2: abnormal UA-PI (> 95th percentile) and normal MCA-PI; Group 3: normal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI (< 5th percentile); and Group 4: abnormal UA-PI and MCA-PI), and perinatal outcomes were compared and evaluated using univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: In total, 352 cases were included, of which 117 (33.2%) were assigned to Group 1, 84 (23.9%) to Group 2, 85 (24.1%) to Group 3 and 66 (18.8%) to Group 4. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, Group 4 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (odds ratio (OR), 2.07 (95% CI, 1.08-3.96); P = 0.03), birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01), neonatal hypoglycemia (OR, 3.34 (95% CI, 1.46-7.67); P < 0.01), neonatal intensive care unit admission (OR, 2.33 (95% CI, 1.24-4.37); P = 0.01) and composite adverse perinatal outcome (CAPO) (OR, 2.44 (95% CI, 1.31-4.57); P = 0.01) compared with Group 1. Furthermore, Group 2 showed greater odds of preterm delivery (OR, 2.06 (95% CI, 1.12-3.79); P = 0.02) and birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.92 (95% CI, 1.07-3.46); P = 0.03) and Group 3 showed greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (OR, 1.79 (95% CI, 1.01-3.26); P = 0.02) and CAPO (OR, 1.88 (95% CI, 1.05-3.38); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. However, in the multivariable logistic regression analysis only Group 4 was associated with greater odds of birth weight < 3rd percentile (adjusted OR, 2.11 (95% CI, 1.11-4.00); P = 0.02) and neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted OR, 2.68 (95% CI, 1.10-6.50); P = 0.03) compared with Group 1. In the univariate logistic regression analysis, abnormal UA and MCA Doppler parameters were also associated with perinatal complications. However, none of the associations were confirmed after adjustment for gestational age at delivery and birth weight in the multivariable models.

CONCLUSIONS: In cases of late-onset FGR associated with cerebral redistribution, isolated abnormalities of the UA-PI or MCA-PI could not identify fetuses at increased risk of perinatal complications. However, the coexistence of both abnormal UA-PI and abnormal MCA-PI, indicating the highest extent of cerebral redistribution, was independently associated with perinatal complications including neonatal hypoglycemia and birth weight < 3rd percentile. In such cases, birth weight was also independently associated with perinatal complications. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: Quality of Life During Oral Peanut Immunotherapy in the OPIA Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) findings have varied between peanut oral immunotherapy (OIT) trials. The objective of this study was to compare changes in the HRQoL between the OIT and standard (control) treatment groups during the OPIA peanut OIT double-blind randomised controlled trial and at long-term follow-up.

METHODS: OPIA was a single-centre, 3-arm, double-blind placebo-controlled trial of peanut OIT in children aged 10-16 years. Standardised questionnaires (FAQLQ, FAIM, FAQLQ-Parent Burden, PSS) and bespoke surveys were administered at 0, 6, 12 and 13.5 months, with 3-year follow-up. Changes in scores at different time points were analysed descriptively and using 2-tailed T tests. A GEE model investigated the interaction between change in HRQoL score, treatment (OIT vs. standard care) and time. 3 year follow-up surveys were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative analysis.

RESULTS: Sixty-five subjects were randomised and 61 participants completed the study. There was no evidence of difference in HRQoL score changes between the OIT and standard treatment groups from baseline to 12 months or 13.5 months. Furthermore, achieving OPIA's primary efficacy endpoint (tolerance of ≥ 1000 mg of peanut protein (cumulative dose 1449 mg) at month 13.5 double blind placebo-controlled food challenge was not associated with a more favourable change in FAQLQ from baseline to end of study. Changes in global FAQLQ-Parent proxy (FAQLQ-PF) scores from baseline to 12 months were less favourable for carers of children who had experienced treatment-related serious adverse events compared to those without such events (mean change 0.10 vs. -0.97, 0.0063).

CONCLUSIONS: OIT did not confer a HRQoL benefit over standard care in this cohort, based upon the tools used to assess HRQoL. Treatment-related serious adverse effects negatively impacted FAQLQ-Parent proxy scores.

articles.title: A reversible neonatal transverse aortic constriction model prolongs cardiomyocyte proliferative activity beyond the early postnatal regenerative window in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The neonatal mammalian heart retains transient regenerative capacity during the first postnatal week, but this ability rapidly declines thereafter. Whether transient mechanical stress can prolong postnatal cardiomyocyte proliferative competence remains unclear. Here, we established a reversible neonatal transverse aortic constriction (TAC) model to investigate whether short-term pressure overload followed by debanding extends the cardiac regenerative window in mice.

METHODS: TAC was performed in 3-day-old C57BL/6 mice by ligating the aortic arch between the brachiocephalic trunk and the left common carotid artery using a 32-gauge spacer. Three days later, the ligature was surgically removed to generate debanded TAC mice. Doppler echocardiography was used to verify pressure overload and unloading. Cardiac morphology, left ventricular wall thickness, heart weight-to-body weight ratio, cardiomyocyte size, and cardiomyocyte proliferative activity were assessed by echocardiography, histology, and immunostaining.

RESULTS: TAC markedly increased aortic flow velocity and pressure gradient at postnatal day 6, confirming successful pressure overload. Transient TAC increased left ventricular posterior wall thickness and heart to body weight ratio, indicating structural remodeling. Following debanding, these changes were partially reversed, although aortic flow velocity remained modestly higher than in age-matched sham controls. Notably, TAC increased cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, as indicated by Ki67, phospho-histone H3, and Aurora B staining. This pro-proliferative effect persisted after debanding, with increased cardiomyocyte proliferative activity and abundance still detectable at postnatal day 9.

CONCLUSIONS: Reversible neonatal pressure overload prolongs cardiomyocyte proliferative activity beyond the early postnatal regenerative window. This neonatal TAC-debanding model provides a useful platform for studying the mechanical regulation of cardiac regeneration.

articles.title: Association Between Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Longitudinal Glycemic Outcomes in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To investigate the associations of peak and submaximal cardiorespiratory fitness capacity with short- and long-term glycemic outcomes in youth with type 1 diabetes, assessed using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics and longitudinal HbA1c data from type 1 diabetes onset.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of pooled clinical trials data included 77 youth (40 females) with type 1 diabetes who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). We obtained CGM data from the preceding 90 days to assess short-term glycemic outcome and longitudinal HbA1c data from diagnosis to CPET for assessing long-term cumulative glycemic exposure. We used multivariable regression analyses for evaluating associations with fitness capacity outcomes.

RESULTS: Median age was 15.8 years (IQR 14.4-19.5), and type 1 diabetes duration was 8 years (IQR 5.2-11.9). Cumulative glycemic exposure was 68.7%·years (IQR 44.0-101.3), mean time in tight range (TITR) was 42.7 ± 10.7%, and time in range (TIR) was 66.9 ± 11.9%. Median peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) was 39.1 mL/(kg·min) (IQR 34.8-44.9), median first ventilatory threshold (VT1) was 23.1 mL/(kg·min) (IQR 18.0-29.0), and median peak power output (Ppeak) was 3.1 W/kg (IQR 2.8-3.6).Higher cumulative glycemic exposure was independently associated with lower VO2peak (β = -0.053, P = 0.024), VT1 (β = -0.064, P = 0.024), and Ppeak (β = -0.0086, P < 0.001), and greater TITR was independently associated with higher VT1 (β = 0.289 mL/(kg·min) per percentage point, P = 0.003) and higher VT1 expressed as a percentage of VO2peak (β = 0.575, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Better long-term glycemic outcomes were associated with higher aerobic capacity, while favorable short-term glycemic outcomes were specifically associated with a higher submaximal ventilatory threshold. These findings support a close relationship between glycemic outcomes and exercise capacity and warrant prospective studies to determine whether improved glycemic outcomes enhance cardiorespiratory fitness.

articles.title: Surgical Outcomes and Patient-Reported Voice and Swallowing Function in Carotid Body Paragangliomas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid body paragangliomas are rare tumors near critical neurovascular structures. We aimed to identify predictors of complications and characterize long-term voice/swallowing outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-institution review of patients undergoing resection for paragangliomas using preoperative imaging and operative reports. Outcomes were evaluated using the Voice Handicap Index-10 (VHI-10) and Eating Assessment Tool-10 (EAT-10).

RESULTS: Of 43 patients, embolization was highly utilized (93.02%), and gross total resection was achieved in 93%. Complications occurred in 18.6%.
