Vagus nerve adherence and tumor dimension were associated with complications (p = 0.028 and p = 0.017, respectively). Abnormal EAT-10/VHI-10 scores were each seen in 15.79% of patients. Pulmonary disease was associated with abnormal VHI-10 (p = 0.018).

CONCLUSIONS: Both voice and swallowing outcomes were favorable overall, and pulmonary disease was associated with an abnormal VHI-10. Complications resolved within 2-5 months, with permanent deficits in 2.33% of patients. Tumor size/nerve adherence should inform preoperative counseling.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Precisely Graded Feeding Temperatures on Swallowing Function and Eating Comfort in Stroke Patients With Dysphagia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke dysphagia (PSD) impairs recovery and quality of life, yet temperature-based feeding interventions remain insufficiently studied. This trial evaluated the effects of precisely graded food temperatures on swallowing outcomes in PSD.

METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 180 acute stroke patients with moderate dysphagia (Water Swallow Test grades 2-4) were assigned to cold (15°C-25°C), moderate-temperature (35°C-45°C), or hot (45°C-55°C) feeding groups. All received viscosity-adjusted diets and standardized feeding training. Outcomes included food intake volume, coughing frequency during swallowing, eating comfort score, gastric tube duration, WST grade, and gastrointestinal complications, assessed at five time points. Repeated measures ANOVA and chi-square tests were applied.

RESULTS: Both cold and hot groups showed greater improvement than the moderate-temperature group in swallowing function (WST grade at 3 months: 1.15 ± 0.36 and 1.12 ± 0.32 vs. 1.83 ± 0.61; p < 0.05), gastric tube duration (9.75 ± 4.59 and 8.22 ± 6.14 days vs. 13.08 ± 9.09; p < 0.05), and fewer coughing episodes. The hot group had the highest eating comfort score (8.40 ± 1.08) and food intake volume (395.33 ± 20.46 mL). The incidence of gastric retention (p = 0.011) and diarrhoea (p = 0.043) differed significantly among groups, with the highest rates observed in the low-temperature group (6.60% and 8.30%, respectively) and the lowest gastric retention rate in the high-temperature group (3.30%).

CONCLUSION: Feeding at cold or hot temperatures significantly improves swallowing recovery in PSD patients compared to moderate temperature. Hot food further enhances comfort and intake, supporting temperature-controlled feeding as a practical, individualized strategy in dysphagia rehabilitation.

articles.title: Ferroptosis and Lipid Metabolic Dysregulation Are Associated With Periodontitis and Peri-Implantitis Complicated by Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although the clinical associations between T2DM and periodontal or peri-implant diseases have garnered widespread attention, metabolomic studies decoding the specific local metabolic alterations within these comorbid conditions remain scarce. This study aimed to apply untargeted metabolomics to elucidate the potential metabolic signatures of T2DM in periodontitis and peri-implantitis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty patients were enrolled in this non-target metabolomics study. Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and peri-implant crevicular fluid (PICF) samples were collected and analyzed. It further investigates the commonalities and heterogeneity in metabolic profiles between T2DM with periodontitis (T2DM-P) and T2DM with peri-implantitis (T2DM-PI). Furthermore, mitochondrial ultrastructure was evaluated via transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and select differential metabolites were cross-validated utilizing immunofluorescence (IF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC).

RESULTS: Our data indicate that T2DM is associated with lipid metabolism dysregulation. In the T2DM-P group, C8 and C10 showed exploratory signals of altered acylcarnitine metabolism. Moreover, γ-GGC and 13-HPOT in the T2DM-PI group and L-cystine in the T2DM-P group were identified as potential candidate metabolites. However, these findings did not remain statistically significant after FDR correction and should be interpreted cautiously. Integrating these metabolomic findings with our experimental findings from TEM, IF, and IHC suggests that cellular ferroptosis emerges as a potential common pathway linked to T2DM-related oral tissue destruction.

CONCLUSION: This study not only reveals the potential metabolic signatures of T2DM-P and T2DM-PI but also highlights the underlying involvement of ferroptosis. Nonetheless, these exploratory findings require rigorous empirical validation for future clinical interventions.

articles.title: Characterizing relatives who provide surrogate consent for clinical research in the ICU: a multicenter sociodemographic profiling study (PICTURE-ICU).
authors: PICTURE trial investigators and  the CRICS-TRIGGERSEP research network
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surrogate consent for clinical research in the intensive care unit (ICU) is a complex process often influenced by psychological distress and the quality of communication. While some barriers are known, there is sparse quantitative data on how sociodemographic profiles relate to a consenting relative's perception of the decision-making process. This study aimed to characterize the distinct sociodemographic profiles among consenting relatives and to describe their perceptions regarding the surrogate consent process.

METHODS: We conducted an exploratory, observational, prospective, multicenter study across 14 French ICUs. A 30-item questionnaire (including an 18-item Likert-scale assessment and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale [HADS]) was administered to 125 relatives who had provided surrogate consent for a patient's inclusion in a research protocol. Data were analyzed using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) followed by hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) to identify homogeneous respondent profiles.

RESULTS: Our analysis identified three distinct clusters of relatives. Cluster 1 (n = 4, 3.2% of the sample) comprised non-professionally active or unemployed individuals who reported lower levels of knowledge and ambivalence regarding their legitimacy to consent. Cluster 2 (n = 59) consisted of older spouses and retirees (aged 51-75 years) characterized by high trust in the healthcare team and a strong sense of legitimacy, despite reporting significant stress during the decision-making process. Cluster 3 (n = 62) was composed of younger, professionally active children of the patient (aged < 50 years) who reported higher healthcare knowledge, felt competent to judge risks and benefits, and prioritized the clarity of information received. Overall, HADS scores indicated moderate to high anxiety and depression across all clusters, though this was not directly attributed to the research participation itself.

CONCLUSIONS: This study offers a robust typology of consenting relatives in the ICU. It reveals three distinct sociodemographic profiles with specific communication needs, levels of trust, and decision-related stress. The findings can inform future research aimed at developing innovative pedagogical tools to tailor and personalize information as effectively as possible.

articles.title: Old threats anew: protecting progress in infectious disease and sexual health.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decades of international collaboration have produced extraordinary advances in infectious disease and sexual health, including effective treatment and prevention of HIV, long-acting prevention technologies, and vaccines against sexually transmitted infections. These achievements have depended not only on individual discoveries, but also on sustained investments in research institutions, clinical trial networks, laboratories, surveillance systems, health services, trained investigators, and trusted partnerships.

MAIN BODY: Recent disruptions to international health assistance and research have exposed the vulnerability of this ecosystem. Reductions in development assistance and major changes in United States foreign assistance have affected HIV testing and prevention, community outreach, health workforces, sexual and reproductive health services, and organizations serving marginalized populations. The effects have been substantial but uneven: treatment programs and mature research institutions have often proved more resilient than prevention and community-based services. This contrast is especially consequential as scientific progress produces powerful new interventions, such as long-acting HIV prevention, whose impact depends on functioning systems capable of delivering them. The experience also demonstrates the value of long-term investments in locally led scientific capacity and durable international partnerships.

CONCLUSION: The goal should not be simply to reconstruct the previous global health architecture. Protecting progress against old and emerging threats will require stronger national and regional institutions, diversified and sustainable financing, locally led science, continued investment in global public goods, and reciprocal international partnerships. Scientific capacity and trust take decades to build and should be preserved before the next breakthrough or the next epidemic requires them.

articles.title: Patient-reported experiences of malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation: a survey of waiting time, perioperative care and recovery after muscle biopsy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation in Sweden includes muscle biopsy and in vitro contracture testing and is centralized to a single national unit, resulting in prolonged waiting times. Although the diagnostic pathway is well established, patients' experiences of referral, investigation, and recovery have rarely been studied. Therefore, this study aimed to explore patient-reported experiences of malignant hyperthermia investigation, with particular focus on waiting time, perioperative care, and recovery after muscle biopsy.

METHODS: An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted using a modified version of the Swedish National Patient Survey. Questionnaires were distributed to 172 adults who underwent malignant hyperthermia investigation between 2018 and 2024 at the Swedish Malignant Hyperthermia Unit. Descriptive statistics and group comparisons were performed.

RESULTS: Seventy participants responded (response rate 41%). Prolonged waiting time negatively affected 24.3% of participants and was associated with stress, uncertainty, and restricted access to surgical care. Most participants reported receiving clear information (95.7%) and being treated with compassion and respect (97.2-98.6%). Immediate postoperative discomfort was reported by 35 participants (50.0%), while 37 participants (52.9%) reported pain lasting one week or longer after the biopsy procedure. No statistically significant differences were detected according to age, sex, or diagnostic outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory study, among survey respondents, patients generally reported positive experiences of perioperative care during malignant hyperthermia susceptibility investigation. However, findings should be interpreted cautiously due to potential recall bias and the use of a non-validated questionnaire. However, postoperative pain was common, and prolonged waiting times had clinically relevant consequences for some patients. Improved pre-procedural information regarding postoperative recovery and better management of patient expectations during the waiting period may improve the overall patient experience.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Innate Immunity in the Oral-Brain Axis: Trained Immunity as a Candidate Link Between Periodontitis and Alzheimer's Disease.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder shaped by aging, genetic susceptibility, and environmental factors. Observational studies have associated periodontitis with cognitive impairment and dementia, but its causal contribution to AD remains uncertain. This review examines trained immunity as a potential mechanism through which chronic periodontal inflammation might modify neuroinflammatory susceptibility. Trained immunity refers to persistent functional reprogramming of innate immune cells following an initial stimulus, supported by metabolic and epigenetic remodeling and altered responses to subsequent challenges, and is distinct from inflammatory activation during ongoing periodontitis. Studies suggest that experimental periodontal inflammation can reprogram bone marrow myelopoiesis, and separate studies demonstrate that peripheral inflammatory stimulation can alter microglial memory and amyloid pathology. These findings establish different components of the proposed pathway. However, clinical evidence for periodontitis-associated training is preliminary and inconsistent, and direct demonstration that such training mediates AD biomarker changes or clinical progression is lacking. Therefore, we distinguish human associations, genetic causal-inference studies, periodontal experiments, and mechanisms established in non-periodontal models. Shared risk factors, reverse causation, exposure heterogeneity, and potentially protective or tolerant immune responses provide important alternative interpretations. We propose stimulus-removal experiments, lineage-resolved perturbation studies, and longitudinal human investigations to test persistence and mediation. Supportive periodontal care remains indicated for oral health; its neuroprotective efficacy, oral-fluid biomarkers of AD, and oral-brain prediction models require prospective validation. The framework positions periodontitis as a potential modifier while retaining systemic inflammatory aging and shared susceptibility as competing explanations.

articles.title: Placental abnormalities in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: A systematic review of experimental and clinical studies.
articles.abstract: The placenta is essential for fetal organ development, and its dysfunction is implicated in several congenital anomalies. However, little is known about the status and role of the placenta in congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herein, we aimed to define the incidence of placental abnormalities in CDH and characterize gross morphology, histology, molecular pathways, and vascular function. Using a predefined search strategy, we performed a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines. Human and animal studies reporting on placental and/or umbilical cord abnormalities in CDH were analyzed. Of 2,820 records identified, 14 articles were included. Human studies reported no consistent macroscopic placental phenotype. Cord abnormalities included hypercoiling, abnormal insertion, and single umbilical artery. Fetal vascular malperfusion, thrombotic lesions, and chronic inflammation were reported at histology. Ex-vivo CDH fetoplacental arteries showed impaired function with excessive constriction and inadequate relaxation. Animal studies reported reduced placental weight, trophoblast injury and apoptosis, and altered retinoid metabolism. Despite extensive literature on CDH, the status of the placenta remains understudied. Available evidence indicates that CDH is associated with abnormalities involving fetal placental vascular pathology. Studies using standardized assessment are needed to define the role of the placenta in CDH and correlate its status with disease severity and neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Risk of fragility fractures in individuals with and without HIV infection: a population-based matched case-control study.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: HIV infection increases hip fracture risk, but evidence in Asian populations is limited. In this large nationwide matched cohort study, antiretroviral therapy mitigated overall fracture risk and reduced postoperative mortality despite persistent skeletal concerns. These findings highlight the importance of bone health monitoring and prevention in individuals with HIV infection.

PURPOSE: Patients with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection are at increased risk of comorbidities, including osteoporosis, which predisposes them to fragility fractures (FFs). Evidence from Asian populations is limited. This study investigated the risk of FFs in an Asian population with and without HIV infection.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched cohort study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. A total of 3994 individuals with HIV infection and 15,976 matched controls were identified (1:4 ratio). Matching variables included age, sex, monthly income, urbanization, liver cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, renal failure, and hepatitis B and C infection. Fragility fractures were identified using ICD-9-CM codes, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The incidence of overall fragility fractures (AFF) was similar between HIV-infected and uninfected individuals (12.9% vs. 11.9%, P = 0.097). However, HIV infection was associated with a significantly higher risk of hip fragility fracture (HFF) (HR 2.22, 95% CI 1.62-3.06, P < 0.001). Risk factors for FFs included age > 50 years, modified Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 2, hypertension, and diabetes mellitus. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) mitigated overall fracture risk and was associated with substantially lower postoperative mortality after fracture surgery (9.4% vs. 36.1%).

CONCLUSION: HIV infection was associated with increased hip fracture risk in this Asian population. ART conferred protective effects on overall fracture risk and survival after fracture, underscoring its net clinical benefit despite skeletal concerns. These findings support targeted bone health monitoring and preventive strategies in individuals with HIV in fection.

articles.title: Beyond transfusions: bleeding-related outcomes after repeat TURP.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We compared perioperative bleeding morbidity after primary transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) versus repeat TURP (re-TURP) to inform counseling and risk stratification.

METHODS: We queried the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (2013-2023) for primary TURP (Current Procedural Terminology [CPT] 52601) and re-TURP (CPT 52630). The primary outcome was perioperative transfusion. Secondary outcomes included ICD-10-based hematuria endpoints from postoperative, readmission, and reoperation diagnoses, as well as reoperation CPT categories. Multivariable logistic models adjusted for age, ASA class, bleeding disorder, urinary tract infection, hematocrit, and platelet count; additional models included surgical urgency, operative time, INR, and albumin.

RESULTS: We identified 83,539 procedures: 76,983 primary TURPs and 6,556 re-TURPs. Transfusion occurred in 1.5% after primary TURP versus 1.9% after re-TURP, while hematuria-related postoperative diagnoses accounted for 1.3% versus 3.6%. Re-TURP was associated with hematuria-related postoperative diagnoses after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.70, 95% CI 2.27-3.21), whereas its adjusted association with transfusion was nonsignificant (aOR 1.12, 95% CI 0.90-1.39). Older age, bleeding disorder, lower hematocrit, and lower platelet count were associated with both bleeding outcomes. Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Hematuria was the largest recorded readmission and reoperation diagnosis group, and clot evacuation/fulguration/irrigation was the largest reoperation procedure category in both cohorts, without significant between-group differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Re-TURP was associated with greater odds of a recorded hematuria-related postoperative diagnosis, while its adjusted association with transfusion was not statistically significant. Because diagnosis codes cannot establish bleeding severity or onset, these findings require confirmation using clinically validated bleeding endpoints.

articles.title: Admission systemic inflammatory response index and prognostic nutritional index in children with diabetic ketoacidosis-associated acute kidney injury: an exploratory retrospective study.
articles.abstract: Early identification of acute kidney injury (AKI) in children with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is important to enable timely management, but conventional markers based on serum creatinine may delay detection. The Systemic Inflammatory Response Index (SIRI) and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) have been associated with adverse outcomes in various clinical settings, but their association with DKA-associated AKI in children has not been investigated. This retrospective study included 122 children with type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by DKA. SIRI and PNI were calculated from admission blood samples. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, and multivariable logistic regression was performed. A nomogram was constructed and evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. AKI occurred in 36 children (29.5%). Spearman correlation analysis showed that SIRI was positively correlated with creatinine, uric acid, and BUN, and negatively correlated with pH and bicarbonate, while PNI showed only weak correlations with these variables. In the fully adjusted model, admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration, remained independently associated with AKI (OR 1.132, 95% CI 1.051-1.243, P = 0.003), whereas SIRI showed a positive but non-significant association (OR 1.066, 95% CI 0.981-1.166, P = 0.143). PNI remained significant after adjustment for hydration-related variables and when post-rehydration PNI was used. In an exploratory analysis, the combined SIRI-PNI model achieved an AUC of 0.845 (95% CI 0.765-0.925), which was higher than that of SIRI alone (0.752) and PNI alone (0.746) (DeLong test, both P < 0.05). The nomogram showed acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow χ2 = 3.617, P = 0.890) and potential net clinical benefit. Conclusion: Admission PNI, likely reflecting hemoconcentration and disease severity rather than nutritional immune reserve, was associated with AKI in children with DKA In an exploratory analysis, the combination of SIRI and PNI provided moderate discriminative ability , supporting further evaluation of these routinely available indices for early risk assessment.

articles.title: Paired independent child-parent symptom reporting using the Turkish SSPedi and mini-SSPedi: psychometric evaluation and discordance patterns in pediatric oncology.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The Symptom Screening in Pediatrics Tool (SSPedi; ages 8-18) and mini-SSPedi (ages 4-7) are validated pediatric oncology symptom-screening instruments. Turkish versions are available, but paired independent child self-report and parent proxy-report within the same assessment have not been systematically evaluated in Türkiye. This study assessed the psychometric properties of paired SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting and characterized child-parent discordance. In this prospective observational study, conducted from January to December 2025 at Istanbul University pediatric hematology-oncology inpatient and outpatient clinics, child-parent dyads aged 4-18 receiving cancer treatment or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation were enrolled. Children completed SSPedi or mini-SSPedi independently, followed by an independent parent proxy-report on the same items. This approach differs from consensus-based co-SSPedi, which produces a single joint score through structured child-parent discussion. Psychometric evaluation included internal consistency, test-retest reliability, known-groups validity, convergent validity, and responsiveness. Convergent validity was examined using ChIMES, PeNAT, and FPS-R. Among 131 dyads, child self-report showed high internal consistency (α = 0.884-0.956; overall α = 0.922), as did parent proxy-report (α = 0.852-0.911). Combined child-parent scores correlated significantly with ChIMES (ρ = 0.268), PeNAT (ρ = 0.263), and FPS-R (ρ = 0.270). Known-groups validity and responsiveness were supported. Discordance varied systematically by symptom domain and developmental age: parents more often overestimated emotional distress, whereas children rated internal physical symptoms as more bothersome. Several individual correlations were marginally below the prespecified r ≥ 0.25 threshold. Future studies should determine whether consensus-based co-SSPedi provides additional clinical value beyond paired independent reporting in routine practice.

CONCLUSION: Paired independent SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated acceptable-to-strong psychometric properties and supports simultaneous child-parent symptom assessment in Turkish pediatric oncology.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Child self-report is the preferred approach for assessing subjective symptoms in pediatric oncology, but parent proxy-reports are often needed and may differ from children's perceptions.

WHAT IS NEW: • Paired independent Turkish SSPedi/mini-SSPedi reporting demonstrated high internal consistency, acceptable convergent validity, and supported known-groups validity and responsiveness, and revealed systematic child-parent discordance, with parents rating emotional symptoms higher and children reporting greater burden from internal physical symptoms.

articles.title: Neurosurgical outcome in infants with low-grade glioma - systematic review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low-grade gliomas (LGGs) in infants pose significant clinical challenges due to their biologically distinct behavior and frequent location in surgically complex regions. While resection remains the preferred initial treatment, its feasibility is frequently limited by age-specific clinical and tumor-related factors. This review explores the role of tumor resection in infants and its association with survival, disease progression, and neurological outcome.

METHODS: A systematic literature search identified studies published within the last decade reporting surgical outcomes in infants with LGGs. Retrospective and prospective cohort studies and relevant case reports were included. Methodological quality was assessed, and relevant data were extracted and analyzed.

RESULTS: Complete resection was less commonly achieved in infants (20.1% vs. 30.9% in total), who demonstrate higher rates of tumor progression and more frequently require multimodal treatment strategies. Resectability was influenced by tumor location, growth pattern, and patient age. Although infants appear to experience lower overall survival rates and greater need for adjuvant, non-surgical therapies, a greater extent of resection is consistently associated with improved survival outcomes, reduced rates of reoperation, and decreased reliance on additional therapeutic modalities.

CONCLUSION: In infants with LGG, the maximal safe extent of resection should be pursued where anatomically feasible. However, particularly for midline tumors, where extensive resection is often not possible, comprehensive assessment of tumor biology and further investigation of non-surgical treatment options are essential to optimize therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Comment on"Comparative outcomes of robot-assisted and open appendicovesicostomy in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis".
articles.abstract: This letter discusses the systematic review and meta-analysis by Liu et al. comparing robot-assisted and open appendicovesicostomy in children. Although the study provides a useful synthesis of scarce evidence, several methodological concerns remain. The included studies were observational, making unadjusted comparisons vulnerable to confounding by indication. In addition, outcomes such as channel stenosis, incontinence, and reoperation are time-dependent, and unequal follow-up may underestimate late failures. Appendicovesicostomy is also often performed with bladder augmentation or bladder neck reconstruction, complicating attribution of perioperative outcomes to APV alone. Finally, reduced blood loss and shorter hospitalization may reflect surgeon experience, treatment era, or perioperative pathways rather than the robotic platform itself. Future studies require prospective, standardized, multicenter designs with adequate adjustment.

articles.title: Multimodal CT perfusion for predicting outcome in first-ever acute stroke due to ICA or MCA-M1 occlusion.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The present study aimed to assess the clinical significance of integrating multimodal computed tomography perfusion (CTP) parameters with metabolic indicators for predicting long-term outcomes among patients experiencing their first acute ischemic stroke (AIS), specifically caused by occlusions in the internal carotid artery (ICA) or middle cerebral artery (MCA) M1 segment.

METHODS: This prospective investigation included 88 patients with AIS who underwent CTP and CT angiography within 24 h of symptom onset. Analysis involved multimodal CTP parameters, metabolic variables, and patient outcomes at 1 year, measured with the Modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Participants were categorized into two groups based on clinical outcomes: favorable (mRS 0-3) and poor (mRS 4-5). Independent predictors were determined using univariate analyses, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and binary logistic regression.

RESULTS: Significant differences emerged between the outcome groups regarding core infarct volume, hypoperfusion volume, mismatch ratio, core cerebral blood volume ratio, core cerebral blood flow ratio, and blood glucose levels (all P < 0.05). Among these, core infarct volume exhibited the greatest predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.825, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.726-0.904, optimal threshold: 3.28 mL). Both core infarct volume (P = 0.022) and mismatch ratio (AUC = 0.717, 95% CI: 0.601-0.819, optimal threshold: 1.9; P = 0.023) were confirmed as independent prognostic factors. A combined predictive model incorporating these factors achieved an AUC of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.734-0.902).

CONCLUSION: Multimodal CTP-derived core infarct volume and mismatch ratio independently predict long-term outcomes, serving as robust tools for early risk stratification and guiding personalized clinical management decisions for patients with AIS.

articles.title: Local niche-derived immunosuppressive CXCR2+ cells impair antiviral immunity.
articles.abstract: Symptom severity after viral infection varies among individuals, yet its mechanism remains poorly understood. We categorize mice into recovering and non-recovering groups based on body weight after infection with the same titer of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). We reveal that in the olfactory bulb (OB) where VSV initially expands, non-recovering mice exhibit an anti-inflammatory environment, suggesting its detrimental effect. Importantly, CXCR2+ cells resembling immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are more abundant in the OB of non-recovering mice than in that of recovering mice after VSV infection. Depleting CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells from the brain increases inflammatory responses and the animal's survival after infection. Furthermore, site-specific labeling indicates that a significant fraction of these cells in the OB originate from the skull-bone marrow (skull-BM) as well as circulation. This study reveals the lethal effects of CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells on local immune responses to viral infection, highlighting their therapeutic potential for antiviral defense.

articles.title: Meta-analysis shows that immunization reduces amphibian susceptibility to the chytrid fungus.
articles.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases are increasingly impacting vertebrates, sometimes causing severe population declines. Chytridiomycosis, caused by the fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), is one of the most devastating wildlife diseases known, driving widespread amphibian collapses and extinctions. Developing strategies that improve host survival in the presence of Bd have therefore become a conservation priority. Here we conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate whether immunizing individuals reduces disease susceptibility. Using 208 effect sizes from 36 studies and 22 species, we compared infection prevalence, infection intensity and mortality between experimentally immunized and non-immunized individuals subsequently exposed to Bd, representing the first such synthesis for a major emerging wildlife disease. Immunization using live pathogens significantly reduced host infection intensity and lowered mortality after re-exposure, whereas immunization using Bd-derived natural chemicals reduced infection prevalence. Other immunization approaches showed non-significant effects across species. Immunization effects also varied across disease progression stages, host life stages and taxonomic groups. Our findings suggest that live-pathogen immunization could be an effective strategy for increasing survival during reintroductions. Supplementing vulnerable populations with immunized individuals or helping wild amphibians clear infections may thus increase survival.

articles.title: Fermentable dietary fiber controls blood pressure by lowering large intestinal pH and activating the proton-sensing receptor GPR65.
articles.abstract: High blood pressure (BP) is the most common cause of death globally due to increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Fermentable dietary fibers regulate BP through gut microbial production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), acidic metabolites. How SCFAs regulate BP remains unclear. Here we show that, in a phenome-wide association study, the proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 gene is associated with human hypertension and cardiorenal phenotypes. Fermentable dietary fibers, delivered as a type 2 resistant starch (RS2), regulated luminal and interstitial tissue pH in the large intestine through gut microbial SCFA production in mice. High RS2 intake reduced pH, increased cAMP production via GPR65 signaling and CREB phosphorylation, and restricted the release of pro-hypertensive inflammatory cytokines by CD8+ T cells. Gpr65-/- mice spontaneously developed hypertension, cardiac and renal hypertrophy, and fibrosis. The benefits of a high-RS2 diet, which prevented these effects, were reduced in Gpr65-/- mice. Adoptive transfers revealed that GPR65 deficiency in CD8+ T cells explained this phenotype.

articles.title: Benefits and harms of antihypertensive treatment a modelling study in 5.5 million electronic health records.
articles.abstract: Antihypertensive prescription is guided by cardiovascular risk prediction models. However, existing models often exclude individuals with prior cardiovascular disease or those prescribed statin treatment. Consequently, there is limited evidence regarding how the benefits and harms of treatment vary according to an individual's baseline risk. This cohort study includes 5,578,002 patients aged≥40years (mean age 59; 52% women) from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink between 1998-2018. A cardiovascular risk prediction model is developed using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink GOLD dataset and externally validated using the Aurum dataset. The model demonstrates excellent calibration and discrimination. Antihypertensive therapy is more likely to prevent serious major cardiovascular events (eight events prevented per 1,000 patients over 10 years, 95% confidence interval = 1 to 14), than to cause serious falls (two events per 1,000 patients, 95% confidence interval = -4 to 10). The risks of other adverse events indicate more nuanced or potentially harmful trade-offs. Here we show that a cardiovascular risk prediction model developed using routinely collected primary care data accurately predicts risk across a broad population of patients eligible for antihypertensive treatment. These findings will enable clinicians to better communicate individualised benefits and risks of antihypertensive therapy.

articles.title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans.
articles.abstract: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10-9). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition.

articles.title: Cardiac counseling in the setting of trisomy 18: a qualitative fetal heart society research collaborative study.
articles.journal: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore fetal cardiologists' prenatal counseling attitudes and practices around congenital heart disease (CHD) in trisomy 18.

STUDY DESIGN: An online survey presented two hypothetical scenarios regarding a fetus with trisomy 21 or 18, both with severe/complex CHD, and queried prenatal surgical counseling. This sub-analysis used inductive content analysis for free text responses on trisomy 18 and CHD prenatal diagnosis counseling.

RESULT: Of 142 respondents, 80 provided free text responses. Themes included: (1) need for nuance: individualized counseling is essential, (2) surgical criteria: clinical and institutional factors influence surgical candidacy, (3) prognosis: what constitutes a "good" outcome vary significantly, (4) moral valence: physicians' personal values influence counseling and emotional experience, and (5) lack of consensus: professional consensus and standardized guidance are lacking.

CONCLUSION: When counseling about prenatal trisomy 18 and CHD diagnoses, fetal cardiologists may benefit from palliative care communication practices and consensus-based guidance alongside case-by-case clinical judgment.

articles.title: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases drive cancer risk through subtype-specific and shared proteomic mediators.
articles.abstract: Cancer is associated with metabolic disorders, yet the impact of endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) on cancer remains unclear. Here, we show the associations of 25 ENMs with cancer trajectories, from primary cancer incidence to multi-primary cancers and mortality, using a multi-state model in a prospective cohort of 405,023 participants. Our findings reveal heterogeneous associations of ENMs across cancer sites and types, identifying 8 cancer-related ENMs that define four subtypes: C1 (iron deficiency/metabolism disorders dominated), C2 (type 2 diabetes dominated), C3 (lipid/lipoprotein metabolism disorders dominated), and C4 (osteoporosis dominated). Subtype-specific and subtype-shared proteomic mediators are identified and their contributions are quantified, with RNASET2 emerging as the major shared mediator. Furthermore, a deep-learning model integrating ENM subtypes and mediators enables personalized prediction of cancer incidence (AUCs = 0.80-0.90) and performs better than conventional Cox models. Our findings highlight the relevance of ENMs to cancer risk, providing mechanistic insights into metabolism-associated tumorigenesis.

articles.title: Expert consensus on periodontal management for medically compromised patients.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a highly prevalent oral disease that extends beyond local inflammation and tissue destruction to exert a profound influence on systemic health. With the growing burden of multimorbidity, where multiple systemic disorders frequently co-exist, periodontal management has become increasingly complex, yet clear and integrated guidance for this specific patient population remains limited. This manuscript synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional relationship between periodontitis and systemic conditions, proposes recommendations for dynamic periodontal management, and updates relevant therapeutic strategies. This expert consensus is designed to ensure both the safety and efficacy of periodontal treatment, reduce the risk of complications, and ultimately promote oral and general well-being.

articles.title: From Viral Detection to Disease Measurement: Lessons from COVID-19.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
articles.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a fundamental distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease produced by that stimulus. SARS-CoV-2 establishes infection, whereas COVID-19 reflects the interaction among viral replication, host immunity, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation and tissue injury. These processes are related but are not interchangeable measurements. A positive molecular test establishes evidence of viral genetic material; it does not, by itself, quantify tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation or disease severity. Similarly, individual biomarkers measure components of a biological response rather than necessarily defining the complete disease state. Clinical outcomes, including hospitalization and death, provide important measures of consequence but do not necessarily identify the mechanisms that produced them. COVID-19 therefore provides a case study in measurement fidelity: the quantity measured must be distinguished from the biological process that the investigator seeks to understand. Viral evolution, changing population immunity, vaccination, immune imprinting and human behaviour further demonstrate that the relationship between infection and disease changes over time. Future pandemic preparedness should integrate pathogen detection with mechanistically appropriate measurements of host response, tissue injury and clinical outcome, while maintaining explicit boundaries between measurement, inference and causation.

articles.title: Implementing a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management in Intensive Care Nursing: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine the impact of a Clinical Decision Support System for Pressure Injury Risk Management (CDSS-PIRM) on nurses' pressure injury risk management practices and pressure injury incidence in an intensive care unit, and to explore nurses' experiences of integrating the system into routine care.

DESIGN: Explanatory sequential mixed-methods study involving pre-test and two post-test evaluation stages followed by qualitative interviews.

METHODS: The study was conducted in an intensive care unit at a tertiary university hospital. The quantitative phase comprised 71 structured observations of nine ICU nurses' pressure injury risk management practices across three sequential stages: pre-test (baseline, n = 26), post-test 1 (CDSS-PIRM implementation without real-time alerts, n = 23) and post-test 2 (CDSS-PIRM implementation with real-time alerts, n = 22). Pressure injury incidence among 165 patients was tracked across the three implementation stages. Following the quantitative phase, the qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with seven nurses.

RESULTS: Risk assessment practice scores were significantly higher at post-test 1 compared with the pre-test (median 3 [IQR 2-6] vs. 2 [IQR 1-2]; p = 0.016), while wound care practice scores improved significantly at post-test 2 (median 1.5 [IQR 0-2] vs. 0 [IQR 0-1]; p = 0.015). Overall pressure injury incidence remained unchanged (10.9%; pre-test: 9.68%; post-test 1: 11.63%; post-test 2: 11.67%; p = 0.920). Two main themes were identified: (i) experienced benefits (a comprehensive clinical guide with real-time prevention support and advanced documentation); and (ii) barriers to clinical integration (workload pressure, reliance on established routines, alert fatigue and infrastructure limitations).

CONCLUSION: Clinical decision support systems can strengthen specific nursing practices related to pressure injury prevention; however, contextual and organisational barriers may constrain their translation into measurable clinical outcomes.

REPORTING METHODS: The Good Reporting of a Mixed Methods Study checklist was followed.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: These findings highlight the potential of clinical decision support systems to support nursing judgement, documentation and real-time prevention in the intensive care unit. Addressing contextual and organisational barriers is essential to optimise their integration into nursing workflows and improve patient safety outcomes.

IMPACT: This study demonstrates how a clinical decision support system can enhance pressure injury risk assessment and wound care practices in intensive care nursing. Findings reveal that improvements in nursing processes do not automatically translate into reduced pressure injury incidence, suggesting the influence of contextual and organisational factors. The study offers practical and conceptual insights for nurses, nurse managers and digital health researchers on implementing decision support technologies in complex care environments.

articles.title: Subtyping Physician Practice Patterns in the Intensive Care Unit.

articles.title: Meta-Analysis: Moderate HBV DNA Levels Are Associated With the Highest Risk of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Chronic Hepatitis B.
authors: Korean Association for the Study of the Liver (KASL)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Although serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels are generally considered to correlate linearly with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in chronic hepatitis B, recent evidence suggests a non-linear relationship, with peak risk at moderate levels. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively assess HCC risk across HBV DNA levels.

METHODS: The systematic review and meta-analysis were reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched through August 2025. HBV DNA levels were categorized as low (< 3.3 log10 IU/mL), moderate (3.3-7 log10 IU/mL), or high (> 7 log10 IU/mL). The primary outcome was HCC incidence. Hazard ratios (HRs) were synthesized using the generic inverse-variance method.

RESULTS: A total of 45 studies including 129,950 patients were analysed. Pooled HCC incidence rates per 100 person-years were 0.304 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.248-0.361), 0.859 (95% CI 0.751-0.966), and 0.409 (95% CI 0.307-0.511) in the low, moderate, and high HBV DNA groups, respectively. Sensitivity analyses applying a stricter upper HBV DNA threshold and more restrictive classification criteria showed a similar pattern, with the highest pooled incidence in the moderate group. Subgroup analyses by treatment status, HBeAg status, alanine aminotransferase levels, and presence of cirrhosis generally supported the overall pattern. The moderate group carried a higher risk than both the low (pooled HR 2.95, 95% CI 2.41-3.61) and high groups (pooled HR 3.56, 95% CI 2.69-4.72). Meta-regression further demonstrated a higher HCC incidence rate in the moderate versus high HBV DNA group (β = 0.350 per 100 person-years, 95% CI 0.191-0.509; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Moderate HBV DNA levels were associated with the highest pooled HCC incidence across the predefined categories.

articles.title: Comparing 70 kV and 120 kV photon-counting CT protocols for pediatric cardiac imaging in children weighing 10-30 kg: Radiation dose and image quality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Scanning at 70 kV on photon-counting CT (PCCT) reduces radiation dose by 50% compared to 120 kV in infants under 10 kg without loss of diagnostic quality. Whether scanning at a lower kV is of benefit in larger children, in whom greater attenuation increases image noise, has not been determined.

METHODS: We retrospectively compared ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT examinations in children weighing 10-30 kg acquired at 70 kV (n = 79) or 120 kV (n = 80), both at a CARE keV IQ level of 25. We measured signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in the ascending aorta and main pulmonary artery and compared radiation dose. Two pediatric cardiac radiologists rated image quality in five vascular structures on a 5-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: Groups were similar in age and size. Neither CNR nor SNR differed significantly. Median Likert scores were at least 4 for four of five structures in both groups. Median CTDIvol was 0.49 vs 0.63 mGy (P < 0.001), and effective dose 0.65 vs 0.75 mSv (P < 0.001) for 70 vs 120 kV.

CONCLUSION: In children weighing 10-30 kg, 70 kV ultra-high-pitch cardiac PCCT was associated with lower radiation dose than 120 kV, with no significant difference in CNR and median reader scores in the diagnostic range. A 120 kV protocol remains appropriate when metal-artifact reduction or advanced spectral reconstructions are needed.

articles.title: The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) in Cardiovascular Care: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIM: Patient education is a core component of cardiac rehabilitation (CR) and secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease, supporting disease understanding, self-management, and adoption of heart-healthy behaviours. The Coronary Artery Disease Education Questionnaire (CADE-Q) was developed as a standardised instrument to assess disease-related knowledge among individuals with cardiovascular conditions. Since its development, multiple versions and translations have been created and applied in diverse populations and settings worldwide. This scoping review aimed to map the global use of CADE-Q instruments, including populations, contexts, knowledge outcomes, and psychometric properties reported across studies.

METHOD: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Databases searched included Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, Emcare, EBSCO CINAHL, Web of Science Core Collection, Global Index Medicus and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses. Studies were eligible if they used the CADE-Q or any of its versions to assess disease-related knowledge in adults. Data were charted using a standardised extraction tool and synthesised descriptively.

RESULTS: Sixty-six studies involving 14,714 participants across 26 countries were included. The CADE-Q Short Version was the most frequently used instrument (n=36), followed by CADE-Q II (n=17) and the original CADE-Q (n=13), administered in 19 languages. Most studies were conducted in CR settings. Baseline knowledge levels were generally moderate relative to maximum scores. Lower knowledge was commonly observed in risk factor and psychosocial health domains, while knowledge related to nutrition and exercise was generally higher. In intervention and longitudinal studies, knowledge typically improved following structured educational interventions, particularly within CR programs. Twenty validation studies reported acceptable psychometric properties across versions and languages, including good internal consistency, test-retest reliability, and evidence of structural and construct validity.

CONCLUSIONS: CADE-Q instruments are widely used globally to assess cardiovascular disease knowledge and demonstrate consistent psychometric performance across diverse settings. Moderate knowledge levels and persistent gaps in risk factor and psychosocial domains suggest a need for more targeted patient education. These tools may support personalised educational interventions in clinical practice, while future research should prioritise implementation and validation in underrepresented populations and regions.

articles.title: [Translated article] Chemical stability and physical compatibility of frozen vancomycin oral solution.
articles.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oral vancomycin is a first-line treatment for Clostridioides difficile infection. When used as an oral solution, its beyond-use date is limited to 14 days in an opened container and at 2-8 °C, according to the guidelines set out in the Guide to Good Preparation Practices for Medicines in Hospital Pharmacy Services. This complicates batch preparation in order to meet the increasing demand for this medication. This study evaluated the physicochemical stability of vancomycin hydrochloride in oral solution under freezing and subsequent thawing conditions.

METHOD: An oral solution of vancomycin hydrochloride was prepared at a concentration of 12.5 mg/mL, and aliquots were packaged in two types of containers (transparent polypropylene cup and amber polyethylene terephthalate bottle). The aliquots were frozen at -25 °C. After 1, 7, 14, 21, 35, 60, 88, and 123 days, they were thawed and then stored at 2-8 °C for 14 days. Residual concentration was determined using an Agilent Technologies 1100 HPLC system (at t = 0, 3, 6, 10, and 14 days after thawing), and physical compatibility was assessed by pH measurement using a pH meter (model 3510, Jenway, UK) with a glass electrode, as well as by visual inspection.

RESULTS: The residual concentration of vancomycin hydrochloride remained ≥91.9% of its initial concentration (12.5 mg/mL) for up to 123 days under frozen storage (-25 °C) and after 14 days under refrigeration (2-8 °C). The pH variation was ≤ ± 0,18, and no changes in color, turbidity, or precipitate formation were detected in any of the aliquots.

CONCLUSIONS: Vancomycin hydrochloride oral solution at a concentration of 12.5 mg/mL maintains its physicochemical stability for up to 123 days under frozen storage and after thawing followed by storage for 14 days at 2-8 °C, regardless of photoprotection.

articles.title: Taiwanese Dermatological Association consensus for the management of atopic dermatitis: A 2024 update.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by eczematous lesions and intense itching. AD commonly arises in children, in some of whom the condition may persist into adulthood; and a significant proportion of patients experience adult-onset disease as well. Although the prevalence of AD in Taiwan has risen over the past decades, recent therapeutic advances have contributed greatly to disease management. The Taiwanese Dermatological Association (TDA) has therefore developed an evidence-based consensus for the management of AD in Taiwan, and established a consensus committee to provide regular updates. This paper presents the 2024 update, for which a literature search was conducted to include relevant papers published between January 2020- March 2023. Supplementary searches targeted to approvals of new AD medications were subsequently conducted, and information was updated to August 2026. The consensus committee included 17 dermatology experts, and a modified Delphi method was used to evaluate the recommendations, with an approval threshold of ≥ 75%. A total of 21 new recommendations were added, 4 recommendations were revised, and the treatment algorithm was updated. Special considerations for pregnant, lactating, pediatric, and geriatric patients, as well as patients with active infections or undergoing vaccination, were included. This update incorporates the latest evidence and approved therapies, and may help to enhance treatment outcomes for AD patients in Taiwan.

articles.title: High-frequency spleen stiffness measurement for noninvasive detection of esophageal varices and high-risk varices: A pilot study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) remains the reference standard for detecting esophageal varices (EV) and high-risk varices (HRV), it is invasive and frequently unnecessary in low-risk patients with cirrhosis. This pilot study compared the diagnostic performance of spleen stiffness measurement (SSM) with that of liver stiffness measurement (LSM), the aspartate transaminase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI), and the FIB-4 score for predicting EV and HRV.

METHODS: Patients with cirrhosis were prospectively recruited. Participants underwent SSM, LSM, and EGD, alongside calculation of APRI and FIB-4 scores. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed, and areas under the curves (AUCs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and maximal Youden indices were compared.

RESULTS: EV and HRV were present in 18 (47.4%) and 6 (15.8%) of 38 eligible patients, respectively. SSM was significantly higher in patients with EV and HRV than those without, while LSM did not differ. SSM demonstrated the highest AUCs for EV (0.906, 95% CI: 0.767-0.992; p < 0.001) and HRV (0.891, 95% CI: 0.772-0.985; p < 0.001) detection. SSM significantly outperformed LSM for both EV (ΔAUC: 0.235; p = 0.003) and HRV (ΔAUC: 0.279; p = 0.012). Using optimal cut-offs of 39.2 kPa and 47.5 kPa, SSM yielded 88.9% sensitivity and 85.0% specificity for EV, and 100% sensitivity and 75.0% specificity for HRV.

CONCLUSIONS: High-frequency SSM demonstrated superior performance compared with conventional LSM for identifying EV and HRV in patients with cirrhosis. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate standardized cut-offs.

articles.title: Consensus document SED-SEEN-SEMERGEN-SEMFyC-SEMG on the use of continuous glucose monitoring in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus on basal insulin therapy.
articles.abstract: In people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) on basal insulin therapy, with or without other antihyperglycemic agents, suboptimal glycemic control increases the risk of hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia, which can negatively impact patients' clinical outcomes and quality of life. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to improve glycemic control by reducing HbA1c and increasing time in range, without increasing hypoglycemic events. It also represents a cost-effective intervention in the analyzed models. This document presents the consensus recommendations of the Spanish Diabetes Society (SED), the Spanish Society of Endocrinology and Nutrition (SEEN), the Spanish Society of Primary Care Physicians (SEMERGEN), the Spanish Society of Family and Community Medicine (SEMFyC), and the Spanish Society of General and Family Physicians (SEMG) on the priority indications for the use of CGM in this population, glycemic control targets, follow-up, and discontinuation criteria.

Association of preoperative vaping-related disorder versus cigarette nicotine dependence with postoperative respiratory complications: a multicentre matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Electronic cigarette aerosols may promote airway inflammation, bronchial hyperreactivity, and impaired mucociliary defence, but their perioperative respiratory safety remains uncertain. We examined whether preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide matched cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network database, comparing surgical patients with documented preoperative vaping-related disorder and cigarette nicotine dependence. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative respiratory complications, including pneumonia, respiratory failure, bronchospasm, noninvasive ventilation, and mechanical ventilation.

RESULTS: Among 3817 matched pairs, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of 30-day respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence (10.7% vs 5.1%, relative risk [RR] 2.11, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.79-2.49). Vaping-related disorder was also associated with increased risks of pneumonia (RR 3.20, 95% CI 2.40-4.28), respiratory failure (RR 2.48, 95% CI 1.98-3.10), bronchospasm (RR 1.92, 95% CI, 1.38-2.68), and noninvasive ventilation (RR 2.56, 95% CI 1.64-3.98). Vaping-related disorder combined with cigarette nicotine dependence was associated with a higher risk of respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence alone (RR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53), whereas vaping-related disorder alone showed a larger RR increase than neither diagnosis (RR 3.11, 95% CI 2.56-3.76).

CONCLUSIONS: Among surgical patients, preoperative vaping-related disorder was associated with a higher risk of postoperative respiratory complications than cigarette nicotine dependence. These findings suggest that vaping history should be specifically assessed during preoperative evaluation and considered in perioperative respiratory risk stratification.

articles.title: Preoperative roxadustat in major elective noncardiac surgery: a phase 2a randomised clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative complications remain a leading cause of mortality. Experimental data indicate that roxadustat, a first-in-class prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor, reduces ischaemia-reperfusion injury, accelerates wound healing, and enhances survival in sepsis. Therefore, preoperative administration of roxadustat might reduce perioperative organ injury. We examined the perioperative tolerability and the potential for adverse surgical interactions with roxadustat.

METHODS: In this phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind, randomised-controlled pilot trial, 150 patients undergoing major elective noncardiac surgery were allocated to preoperative roxadustat 100 mg or placebo for three alternate-day doses, with the last dose on the operative morning. The co-primary outcomes were preoperative adverse events and postoperative complications meeting standardised endpoint definitions within 30 days.

RESULTS: Among 148 participants (52 [35.1%] females; median age 65 [range 24-84] yr) receiving at least one drug dose, at least one preoperative adverse event occurred in 21 of 75 (28%) in the roxadustat group and 20 of 73 (27%) in the placebo group (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.50-2.12). No serious adverse reactions occurred. Among 143 participants who proceeded to surgery (52 [36.4%] females; median age 65 [range 26-84] yr), ≥1 complication occurred in 23 of 74 participants (31%) who received roxadustat compared with 21 of 69 participants (30%) who received placebo (odds ratio 1.03; 95% CI 0.51-2.10). Days alive out of hospital within 30 days was similar between the groups. The annualised enrolment rate was 90 per year, with high levels of drug compliance.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative roxadustat was feasible in patients having major surgery. Uncertainty remains regarding the safety and efficacy of this intervention.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.anzctr.org.au; ACTRN12624000188538.

articles.title: Intraoperative peripheral perfusion index and mortality after noncardiac surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraoperative haemodynamic monitoring primarily targets arterial pressure and flow but might not adequately reflect tissue perfusion. The peripheral perfusion index provides a continuous, noninvasive, and readily available indicator of peripheral perfusion, but its prognostic significance across surgical populations remains uncertain. We hypothesised that greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index would be associated with postoperative complications and mortality.

METHODS: In this prespecified multicentre cohort study using electronic health record data, we included adults (≥18 yr) undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery. The primary exposure was cumulative intraoperative area under a perfusion index of 1.5 expressed in PI⋅min. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary outcome was a 30-day composite of postoperative intensive care unit admission, reoperation, acute kidney injury, or prolonged hospital stay.

RESULTS: Among 399 842 patients undergoing 540 101 procedures, a total of 7066 (1.3%) deaths occurred within 30 days: 654 (0.5%) among procedures with no exposure, 1185 (0.6%) in the lower half of exposed procedures, and 5227 (2.6%) in the upper half (split at 3.8 PI⋅min). Compared with no exposure, the adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 2.18 (95% CI 1.98-2.40, overall association P<0.001) at the 95th percentile of exposure (42.5 PI⋅min), with similar patterns observed across the major surgical specialties. For the composite outcome, the corresponding odds ratio was 1.16 (95% CI 1.14-1.18; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Greater intraoperative exposure to low perfusion index was associated with higher postoperative mortality and complications in adult patients undergoing general anaesthesia for noncardiac surgery.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT07164339.

articles.title: Impact of obesity with metabolic comorbidities on oncologic outcomes in patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) and its components have been reported with worse oncologic outcomes in several malignancies. However, the prognostic impact of obesity with metabolic comorbidities in upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) was still inconclusive.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between obesity with metabolic comorbidities and survival outcomes in patients with UTUC.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with UTUC between 1988 and 2025 comprising 21 hospitals across Taiwan. Obesity with metabolic comorbidities was defined with a modified definition based on available clinical data, including body mass index ≥27 kg/m² combined with at least one metabolic component, such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, or related medication use. Overall survival (OS), cancer-specific survival (CSS), disease-free survival (DFS) were analyzed using univariate, multivariate Cox regression analysis, BRFS was analyzed using the Fine-Gray competing-risk regression model, and Kaplan-Meier method after propensity score overlap weighting.

RESULTS: Among 2,863 patients with UTUC, 510 patients (17.8%) were classified as having obesity with metabolic comorbidities. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed no significant differences in OS, CSS, DFS, or BRFS between patients with and without obesity with metabolic comorbidities, and these findings remained consistent after overlap weighting. In multivariable analysis, obesity with metabolic comorbidities was not independently associated with any survival endpoint. The 5-year OS, CSS, DFS, and BRFS rates were approximately 68.7%, 81.3%, 70.3%, and 76.1%, respectively, in patients with obesity with metabolic comorbidities, compared with 66.3%, 82.8%, 72.4%, and 71.4%, respectively, in those without obesity with metabolic comorbidities. Among individual MetS components, hypertension was independently associated with worse OS (HR 1.30, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.50, P < 0.001), whereas diabetes mellitus was not significantly associated with survival outcomes in the overall cohort.

CONCLUSION: Obesity with metabolic comorbidities was not independently associated with OS, CSS, DFS, or BRFS in patients with UTUC. Nevertheless, individual metabolic components may have distinct prognostic implications. Further prospective studies with standardized MetS definitions are needed to better clarify the relationship between metabolic abnormalities and UTUC outcomes.

articles.title: The role of genetic background in associations with a patient's response to type 2 biologics in severe asthma.
articles.journal: Allergology international : official journal of the Japanese Society of Allergology
articles.abstract: Severe asthma often requires biologic therapy for exacerbation prevention and symptom control. In clinical practice, the selection of biologics is based on phenotypes, comorbidities, and type 2 inflammatory markers. However, specific genetic polymorphisms may influence treatment response, thereby optimizing biologic selection. Regarding the genetic background associated with asthma severity, single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in genes such as FCER1B (MS4A2), IL5, IL1RL1 (ST2), and IL4RA have been reported. While several studies have investigated the relationship between genetic background and therapeutic response to omalizumab and anti-IL-5 agents, data remain limited for dupilumab, and no reports are currently available for tezepelumab. In terms of therapeutic response to omalizumab, specific SNPs in IL1RL1, GATA2, FCGR2A/2B/3A, and FCER1B have been reported to be associated with improvements in clinical parameters or drug survival. Next, for anti-IL-5 agents, specific variants in ADRB2, ZNF415, FCER1B, and IL1RL1 have been implicated in clinical response to mepolizumab. Similarly, variants in FCER1B, IKZF2, IL5, and IL1RL1 have been linked to clinical improvements or excellent response with benralizumab. As for dupilumab, existing data suggest a potential association between SNPs in IL4 or IL4RA and clinical improvement. This review summarizes the current evidence on the association between genetic polymorphisms and treatment response to biologics in patients with severe asthma. Because current evidence is mostly derived from retrospective, candidate-gene association studies with limited sample sizes and no validation cohorts, findings should be interpreted with caution, and future prospective studies are warranted.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus as a key driver of clinically significant fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), which is linked to more advanced liver disease. We aimed to assess the relationship between T2DM and fibrosis severity in patients with MASLD.

METHODS: We analyzed 92 patients with MASLD, excluding those with chronic viral hepatitis or significant alcohol intake. Anthropometric, laboratory, and ultrasound data were collected. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) and steatosis were assessed by transient elastography. Associations between T2DM and clinically significant fibrosis (LSM ≥8kPa) were evaluated using correlation and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus was present in 55.4% of patients. Patients with T2DM had a higher prevalence of LSM ≥8kPa than non-diabetic individuals (39.2% vs 4.9%; p<.0001), corresponding to a 28-fold higher odds of clinically significant fibrosis. A moderate correlation was observed between T2DM and fibrosis stage (ρ=0.451; p<.001). After adjustment for age, body mass index, triglycerides, and sex, T2DM remained independently associated with clinically significant fibrosis, conferring a 36-fold higher odds (OR, 36.13; 95% CI, 3.08-423.0; p=0.004).

CONCLUSIONS: Type 2 diabetes mellitus is strongly associated with clinically significant liver fibrosis in MASLD. These findings support integrated hepatometabolic risk stratification and targeted fibrosis screening in patients with T2DM.

articles.title: Assessment of the Psychometric Properties of the Turkish Version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale (PPCS).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric nurses need a standardized assessment tool to assess the overall condition of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly.

OBJECTIVE: In this study, the validity and reliability studies of the Turkish version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale were conducted.

DESIGN AND METHODS: The study sample consisted of 200 pediatric patients aged 0-18 (mean ± SD: 2.14 ± 1.14; median: 2) receiving diagnostic and treatment services at the pediatric units of a hospital.

RESULTS: The Cronbach's alpha coefficient of the 11-item Pediatric Patient Classification Scale was 0.838, indicating a high level of internal consistency. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) demonstrated that the three factors in the original scale "Family," "Patient," and "Therapeutic Procedures" were preserved in the Turkish form. The CFA fit indices were RMSEA = 0.079, χ2/df = 2.24, and CFI = 0.96. These results indicate that the measurement model fits the data well. Scores of the Caregiving Burden Scale, which measures burden according to patient care levels, differed significantly across the categories identified by the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale (minimal care, moderate care, high-level care, semi-intensive care, and intensive care).

CONCLUSION: The Turkish version of the Pediatric Patient Classification Scale, developed to classify the care needs of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly, is a valid and reliable assessment tool.

PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: This tool enables pediatric nurses to assess the overall condition of pediatric patients accurately and rapidly in accordance with the patient classification system.

Autologous transfusion of noncitrated peritoneal blood in horses with haemoperitoneum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autologous blood transfusion in acute blood loss into the peritoneal cavity is widely used in small animal and human emergency medicine but is not well described in horses.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the outcomes of autologous transfusion of noncitrated blood from the peritoneal cavity in horses with haemoperitoneum.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study of clinical records.

METHODS: Data were extracted from records of 19 horses diagnosed with haemoperitoneum in years 2020-2025, treated with autologous transfusions of noncitrated blood collected from the peritoneal cavity. Data on hospitalisation period, amount of transfused blood, number of transfusions, complications, short- and long-term outcomes were collected and analysed.

RESULTS: Nineteen cases of various aetiology (13 females and 6 males) were included in the study. Horses, aged 3-28 (median age 14), were diagnosed with haemoperitoneum based on transabdominal ultrasonography and abdominocentesis. Clinical findings on initial examination included manifestations of abdominal discomfort, tachycardia, prolonged capillary refill time and pale mucous membranes. All 19 horses underwent autotransfusion of whole noncitrated blood. Total blood volume transfused was 5-38.75 L (median 19.5 L; IQR: 18.5). Rapid clinical deterioration was observed in 3 horses, necessitating euthanasia. The remaining 16 horses (survival rate 16/19) survived until discharge following 3-22 days of hospitalisation (median 8.5 days).

MAIN LIMITATIONS: Retrospective design; heterogeneous, warmblood-oriented population; unbalanced sex distribution in the studied caseload; lack of control group.

CONCLUSIONS: Autotransfusion of noncitrated blood may be a safe, time-saving, and cost-effective alternative to standard allogeneic blood transfusions and seems to be beneficial for haemoperitoneum treatment in selected haemorrhage cases.

Core outcome set for future uterine fibroid research: an international consensus development study - a study protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Uterine fibroids are prevalent non-cancerous gynaecological tumours that can cause significant morbidity, including abnormal uterine bleeding and anaemia. Treatment options include medication, surgery or image-guided therapies. Treatment decisions are influenced by patient symptoms, fertility intentions, anatomy and healthcare professional recommendations. It has been difficult to compare results from high-quality studies investigating fibroid treatment interventions due to heterogeneous outcomes and measures. For example, there has been no agreement on the outcomes to select for use in fibroid randomised controlled trials. The inability to directly compare study outcomes through meta-analysis or indirectly compare study findings may adversely affect clinical care owing to difficulties determining the most effective fibroid treatments. We recommend a standardised set of outcomes that should be reported in all future fibroid studies with the goal of improving patient clinical care.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: An international steering committee with involvement of key stakeholders, including those with lived experience of uterine fibroids, healthcare professionals, patient advocates and researchers has been established. A long list of potential outcomes has been identified from a systematic review. The study will involve a modified Delphi survey conducted in two rounds in which stakeholder participants will grade outcomes. Outcomes will be graded using a nine-point Likert scale, with scores ranging from 1 (of limited importance) to 9 (of critical importance). The Steering Group will hold a final Consensus meeting to determine the final core outcome set (COS).

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Following this, findings will be implemented and disseminated to help standardise the use of outcomes of uterine fibroid studies, with a view to providing better clinical care. Outcome selection is imperative for trial design to allow appropriate assessment of the effectiveness of different interventions. It should also harmonise reliable comparison of study outcomes between studies, generating more meaningful data while reducing research waste. The National Health Research Authority determined that the project does not require review by an NHS Research Ethics Committee. The study has been reviewed by the Imperial College London Research Governance and Integrity team and obtained favourable ethical approval.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Prospective registration of this study has been undertaken with the Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) initiative website (registration number 3280). The COMET initiative facilitates methodological research involving the development and application of COSs.

articles.title: Core Entrustable Professional Activities for Postgraduate Pharmacist Training in Taiwan: A National Consensus Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate the content and structure of core entrustable professional activities (EPAs) for Taiwan's two-year postgraduate year (PGY) hospital pharmacist training program.

METHODS: We conducted a national, multi-phase consensus and validation study. Candidate EPA topics were derived from Ministry of Health and Welfare PGY training guidelines and prioritized through a nationwide survey of teaching hospitals. EPA drafts were developed using a standardized template, refined through structured expert consensus meetings, and further reviewed by a competency-based pharmacy education task force.
