Finalized EPAs were validated through structured quality appraisal using the QUEPA tool and the EQual rubric.

RESULTS: Of 150 invited teaching hospitals, 121 responded to the national survey (80.7%). Through national prioritization, CBPE task-force review, and expert consensus meetings with 27 pharmacy educators, eight core EPAs were finalized. The consensus process generated 53 change proposals, including additions, amendments, and deletions. EPA quality appraisal involved 106 clinical preceptors across multiple hospital levels. QUEPA ratings generally supported the relevance and structural quality of the finalized EPA statements. All eight EPAs met the published EQual domain-specific and overall mean-based cut scores, providing evidence supporting their statement quality and curricular relevance.

CONCLUSIONS: A nationally informed, consensus-derived framework of eight core EPAs was developed for Taiwan's two-year PGY hospital pharmacist training. Structured quality appraisal supported the content relevance and statement quality of the framework, providing a foundation for future workplace-based assessment and evaluation of entrustment decisions.

articles.title: Characterization of infections following bispecific T-cell engager therapy in hematologic malignancies.
articles.abstract: Bispecific T-cell engagers (BiTEs) have transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, but real-world pharmacovigilance data on infection-related adverse events remain limited. This study analyzed data from the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System from October 2014 to September 2025 for seven FDA-approved BiTEs targeting CD19, CD20, B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA), and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D). Disproportionality analyses using the reporting odds ratio and Bayesian confidence propagation neural network identified safety signals at the MedDRA High-Level Term (HLT) level. Time to onset and the proportion of fatal outcomes were assessed. Comparisons with chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy were also performed. A total of 3,012 cases (22%) involved infections, with fatal outcomes reported in 33.3% of infection-related reports. At the HLT level, 37 distinct infection-related terms met the prespecified criteria for positive disproportionality signals. These terms included bacterial (n=14), viral (n=12), fungal (n=4), parasitic (n=2), organ-specific (n=3), and other infection-related HLTs (n=2). The median TTO was 36 days (interquartile range 7-124), ranging from 8 days for blinatumomab to 82 days for teclistamab. Bacterial categories showed the earliest median TTO (28 days), followed by fungal and viral categories. Compared with CAR-T, BiTE reported a higher proportion of infections in elderly patients (48% vs 39%) and a longer TTO (36 vs 6 days). Positive infection signals were largely concordant between BiTE and CAR-T. These findings demonstrate a broad spectrum of reported infection-related adverse events, variation in time to onset, and high fatal outcome proportions for certain pathogen-specific categories, highlighting the need for infection surveillance tailored to treatment, timing, and patient risk factors.

articles.title: Nutritional care and short-term mortality in alcohol-associated hepatitis: a real-world two-center study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) carries high mortality. Malnutrition is highly prevalent, and nutrition represents a central therapeutic target alongside corticosteroids and alcohol abstinence, yet real-world implementation remains unclear. We aimed to assess adherence to nutritional guidelines and its association with mortality.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we included 157 patients hospitalized with AH at a tertiary and a secondary center (2019-2023). Data on nutritional management and mortality were extracted from medical records. Cut off for energy intake was categorized at 21.4 kcal/kg/day, based on the cohort median, in patients with ≥66% of inpatient days documented. Differences in guideline adherence between centers were analyzed using χ2 and Wilcoxon tests. Survival was assessed with Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank test.

RESULTS: Most individuals had severe AH (66%) and 72% had liver cirrhosis. Median age was 57 years, 36% were female. Malnutrition risk screening was performed in 85% of patients, with 39% classified as at risk. Dietitian involvement was higher at the tertiary center (83% vs 42%), associated with more specialized nutritional care. Energy intake was more frequently monitored at the tertiary center (87% vs 48%). Parenteral nutrition was used more often than enteral nutrition (28% vs 11%), particularly at the tertiary center. Low energy intake was associated with higher 28-day mortality (p=0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Real-world nutritional care in AH is inconsistent and often deviates from established guidelines. Our findings suggest that achieving adequate energy intake may improve survival. These results highlight the need for flexible, patient-centered nutritional strategies, particularly in settings with limited hepatology expertise.

articles.title: Subcutaneous tunnel length and catheter-related infection in patients with short bowel syndrome receiving home parenteral nutrition: an observational cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Patients with short bowel syndrome receiving long-term home parenteral nutrition through tunneled central venous catheters are at risk of catheter-related infection. Whether the length of the subcutaneous catheter tunnel influences infection risk is unclear. We aimed to describe catheter-related infections in this population and to evaluate whether subcutaneous tunnel length was associated with infection risk.

METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study of 80 patients with short bowel syndrome followed at a tertiary intestinal failure center. All patients had a tunneled central venous catheter for long-term parenteral nutrition. The primary exposure was subcutaneous tunnel length, measured from the catheter exit site to the venous entry site. Catheter-related infections were defined according to ESPEN criteria. Time to first catheter-related infection was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox regression. Additional patient-, catheter-, and treatment-related factors were evaluated in exploratory analyses.

RESULTS: Catheter-related infection occurred in 44 of 80 patients (55%). Median time to first infection was 169.5 days. Exit-site infection was the most common presentation, occurring in 31 of 44 infection episodes (70.5%). Staphylococcus aureus was the most frequently identified pathogen. Subcutaneous tunnel length was not significantly associated with time to first catheter-related infection in the primary continuous analysis (hazard ratio per 1 cm increase 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.76-1.02; p = 0.098), and the exploratory dichotomized analysis was also not statistically significant. No statistically significant associations were observed in exploratory univariable analyses of patient-, catheter-, or home parenteral nutrition-related factors. Among 29 catheters retained after a first infection, 22 developed recurrent infection (75.9%).

CONCLUSIONS: Catheter-related infections were frequent in patients with short bowel syndrome and tunneled central venous catheters, but subcutaneous tunnel length was not significantly associated with time to first catheter-related infection. Prevention should therefore focus on catheter-care procedures, early recognition of exit-site infection, and strategies to reduce recurrence after a first infection.

articles.title: Current Diabetic Ketoacidosis Knowledge is not Associated with Previous Episode Frequency in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a severe complication of type 1 diabetes (T1D). Although patient education is a cornerstone of prevention, knowledge may not guarantee action. We investigated determinants of DKA knowledge and examined whether higher current knowledge was associated with a lower frequency of previous DKA episodes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 861 online participants (patients and caregivers). Knowledge was assessed using a 13-item questionnaire. Quasibinomial regression identified knowledge predictors, and a partial proportional odds model evaluated cumulative previous DKA episode frequency among 771 participants with a classifiable DKA episode history.

RESULTS: Knowledge level was not associated with DKA episode frequency (OR=1.01; p=0.70). Longer disease duration (≥10 years) was associated with higher DKA episode categories (OR=3.38; p<0.001). Among individuals with T1D, both sexes had similar odds of reporting ≥1 DKA episode, but males had lower odds of reporting ≥3 episodes (OR=0.28; p<0.001). Higher knowledge was independently associated with higher income (OR=1.22; p=0.009), ketone meter use (OR=1.39; p<0.001), and automated insulin delivery (p<0.001). Unawareness of glycated hemoglobin was associated with lower odds of correct responses (OR=0.53; p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Although advanced technologies were associated with higher theoretical knowledge, this knowledge was not associated with a lower frequency of previous DKA episodes. Instead, higher DKA episode categories were associated with longer disease duration and sex-related factors. These findings support a multifactorial approach to DKA prevention, preserving patient education as a cornerstone of care. Instrument limitations warrant caution when interpreting the null association.

articles.title: Loss-of-function variants in the NR2F2 promoter confer susceptibility to isolated congenital heart disease: A rare variant disrupts ETS1-mediated regulation.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Gene regulatory mechanisms
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the most common birth defect, with the genetic defects remaining unknown in many patients. NR2F2 is a transcription factor that regulates cardiac endocardial development in a dosage-sensitive manner; however, the association between non-coding NR2F2 variants and CHD risk remains unclear. In this study, we performed a case-control analysis of the NR2F2 promoter, and identified four rare variants in isolated CHD patients with a frequency over 3% but undetected in controls. Histone modification analysis showed that two of the candidate variants, g.96330105C > T and g.96330128C > T, overlapped with active promoter-associated histone marks. Functionally, these two variants significantly reduced NR2F2 promoter transcriptional activity and protein expression. In addition, the variant g.96330128C > T abrogated ETS1 binding, thereby impairing ETS1-mediated positive transcriptional regulation of NR2F2. These findings highlight that loss-of-function (LOF) variants in the NR2F2 promoter, particularly g.96330128C > T, confer CHD susceptibility by reducing NR2F2 expression.

articles.title: TD-DCC: An Interactive and Efficient Graphical User Interface-Based Time-Dependent Dynamic Cross-Correlation Analysis of Molecular Dynamics Trajectories.
articles.abstract: Conventional implementations of the dynamic cross-correlation matrix (DCCM) generate a single time-averaged matrix, thereby obscuring the dynamic nature of residue-residue cross-correlations. Therefore, transiently stable correlations are difficult to probe using the conventional DCCM. We are introducing TD-DCC (Time-Dependent Dynamic Cross-Correlation), a dependency-light, single-file Tkinter desktop application with a graphical user interface (GUI) that computes time-dependent DCCs directly from raw molecular dynamics trajectories using user-defined parameters. TD-DCC provides residue-pair statistics, including mean, standard deviation, and probabilities of positive or negative correlation. High computational performance is achieved through three core design choices: a non-blocking, event-driven graphical interface; a vectorized correlation engine that uses NumPy's Einstein summation routine; and a producer-consumer architecture that leverages MDAnalysis to stream trajectory data from disk rather than loading full trajectories into memory. TD-DCC enables a seamless "compute-filter-visualize" workflow for decoding the complex dynamic allosteric communications and is openly available at https://github.com/sandipandrils/TD-DCC.

articles.title: Sleep characteristics, glymphatic proxies, and ATN biomarkers in Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sleep and glymphatic dysfunction are increasingly recognized as contributing factors to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. This study examined both the main and interactive effects of sleep characteristics and glymphatic proxies on ATN biomarkers across the AD continuum.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 325 participants (50-86 years, 36% male) who underwent 18F-Florbetapir and 18F-Flortaucipir PET/MRI. We assessed sleep characteristics by obtaining habitual sleep duration and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Neuroimaging-derived glymphatic proxies were choroid plexus volume fraction (CPVF), perivascular space volume fraction (PVSF), and free water within cerebral white matter (WMFW). Linear regression was used to examine the main and interactive associations of sleep characteristics and glymphatic proxies with ATN biomarkers.

RESULTS: Prolonged sleep duration was associated with greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.25) and thinner cortical thickness (CTh, β = -0.19, both p < 0.01). Higher WMFW was associated with greater global Aβ burden (β = 0.20), greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.22), and thinner CTh (β = -0.41, all p < 0.01). Higher CPVF was associated with greater temporal tau burden (β = 0.15), and higher PVSF was associated with thinner CTh (β = -0.14, both p < 0.05). Notably, WMFW consistently moderated the associations between sleep duration and ATN biomarkers (|t| range = 2.61 to 2.78, q < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings support a role for sleep-glymphatic interactions in shaping AD pathology and suggest that this interplay warrants further investigation in longitudinal studies.

articles.title: Critical Incident Technique to Identify Factors Influencing Acute Stroke Diagnosis.
articles.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute stroke (AS) affects nearly 800,000 people/year in the US with diagnostic error occurring in ∼10% of patients. A qualitative methodology, the critical incident technique, was used to understand the diagnostic process for AS among physicians.

METHODS: Emergency medicine and neurology physicians, involved in evaluating suspected AS cases, were invited to take part in an interview using a standardized guide to learn about the (a) information gathered (e.g., history, exam, laboratory and imaging results); (b) relative importance of each type of information; (c) differential diagnoses; (d) factors affecting the diagnostic process. Interviews were conducted by video-conference, audio-recorded, and transcribed. Transcripts were uploaded into qualitative analytic software and inductively and deductively coded by 4 independent coders.

RESULTS: Twenty-five physician interviews were conducted, and 300 unique codes were reached by consensus. Codes were grouped into themes and identified 5 AS diagnostic process phases: (1) Evaluation initiation; (2) Information gathering; (3) Initial diagnostic impression (4) Detailed analysis; and (5) Final diagnosis. Barriers and facilitators of each phase were identified.

CONCLUSION: Findings suggest two key opportunities to improve the AS diagnostic process: (1) developing strategies to gather initial "event" information more rapidly and accurately, including the ability to acquire or confirm information from a witness and (2) reducing distractions and cognitive burden such as through a "sterile cockpit" during the diagnostic process.

articles.title: Effect of dietary fermented lavender supplementation on growth, immunological and biochemical parameters, gut microbial flora and disease resistance in rainbow trout.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effects of dietary raw and fermented lavender leaves on growth, immunological and biochemical parameters, gut microbial flora and disease resistance in rainbow trout, Oncorhynchus mykiss. Lavender leaves were fermented with Saccharomyces cerevisiae (PTCC 5052) for 48 h, which resulted in significant increase in bactericidal activity against Aeromonas hydrophila and antioxidant capacity. both types of lavender leaves were added at 1 and 2 % to fish diet and offered to the fish for 60 days. Then the fish were intraperitoneally challenged with A. hydrophila. Fish were sampled before and 12 h after the challenge. Fermented lavender, particularly at 1% inclusion (FLAV1), improved growth, feed utilization, and economic performance in rainbow trout. FCR decreased in LAV1, FLAV1, and FLAV2, while FLAV1 increased final weight, PEF, and ECE compared with the control. Fermented lavender enhanced intestinal digestive enzyme activities, lysozyme activity, and lactic acid bacteria counts, while reducing total bacterial and Vibrio counts, CAT activity, and MDA levels. Skin mucus lysozyme, ALP, protease, peroxidase, and bactericidal activities were also enhanced, especially in fermented-lavender groups. All lavender-supplemented diets reduced post-challenge mortality following A. hydrophila infection, with lower mortality in fermented than raw lavender treatments. Dietary lavender increased plasma lysozyme, TAC, and ascorbate concentrations and reduced plasma liver-enzyme activities, whereas fermented lavender reduced post-challenge glucose and improved leukocyte responses. Hepatic GPx and GSH increased, whereas post-challenge MDA decreased in all supplemented groups; fermented lavender also enhanced hepatic lysozyme and TAC responses. PCA consistently separated supplemented groups, particularly FLAV1 and FLAV2, from the control, confirming the overall improvement in growth, immune competence, antioxidant status, stress response, and disease resistance. Fermented lavender leaves, particularly at 1% inclusion (FLAV1), improved growth, feed efficiency, digestive activity, intestinal microbiota, immune function, antioxidant status, and resistance to A. hydrophila in rainbow trout. Compared with raw lavender, fermented lavender more effectively reduced intestinal bacterial counts, oxidative damage, stress responses, and post-challenge mortality. PCA confirmed the overall superiority of fermented-lavender treatments. Therefore, 1% fermented lavender leaf powder is a promising natural functional additive for rainbow trout diets.

articles.title: MASLD in COPD: prevalence, association with disease severity, and development of a predictive score of risk.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) represents the predominant cause of chronic liver disease worldwide and shares with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) common pathobiological pathways; however, its burden in COPD is insufficiently characterized. The study aimed to estimate the prevalence of MASLD in COPD patients, the association between MASLD and COPD severity and to develop a predictive score of MASLD risk.

METHODS: Cross-sectional monocenter study. Adults ≥60 years old with COPD and without a history of viral or autoimmune hepatitis, liver cirrhosis, high daily alcohol consumption and active malignancy were included. Participants underwent spirometry, 6-minute walking test and liver ultrasound; laboratory parameters were also collected. MASLD was diagnosed according to the EASL-EASD-EASO guidelines and the respiratory symptoms, exacerbations and lung function were compared between participants with and without MASLD. Logistic regression was used to develop a predictive model, with a bootstrapped validation.

RESULTS: 116 patients were enrolled. Patients with MASLD were 54.3% and were more comorbid, with a higher prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases, more symptomatic (mean CAT 16vs13, P-value:0.03), and with a worse BODE index (3vs2, P-value:0.04). The ROC-AUC of the "BMI, Airflow obstruction, Sex, Lung exacerbation and Dyspnea- M-A-S-L-D -" predictive score was 0.81. A cut-off ≥2 showed a diagnostic sensitivity and specificity for MASLD of 92% and 36%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: MASLD is highly prevalent in COPD, and it is associated with more severe COPD. "M-A-S-L-D" predictive score is easy-to-use and may help to stratify the risk of MASLD.

articles.title: Cost-utility and cost-effectiveness of COPD screening as an add-on to low dose computed tomography lung cancer screening in Germany.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COPD is associated with high disease burden and is a leading cause of death. In July 2024, Germany introduced regulation allowing low-dose CT for early lung cancer detection in smokers. This cost-utility and cost-effectiveness model compares hypothetical lung cancer screening with embedded COPD screening (LC+COPD screening) with lung cancer screening alone (LC-screening).

METHODS: A dynamic Markov model from the perspective of the statutory health insurance was developed including individuals aged 50-75 years meeting current German lung cancer screening criteria. The base-case assumed a smoking cessation success rate of 12% among individuals with newly detected COPD compared to 7.5% among individuals with known and undetected COPD. The model used a 40-year time horizon with 3-month cycles. Outcomes include costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and life years gained (LYG). Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Under base-case assumptions, the ICER was €59,868 per QALY gained and €32,175 per LYG. Assuming an increased smoking cessation success rate of 15% among individuals with newly detected COPD, ICERs were €35,349 per QALY gained and €17,967 per LYG. Univariate sensitivity analyses showed the greatest impact from discount rates and smoking cessation success. Probabilistic sensitivity analyses with 10,000 draws each yielded mean ICERs of €59,038 per QALY gained and €31,821 per LYG.

DISCUSSION: Our model provides a first indication of the cost-effectiveness of LC+COPD-screening. The findings are limited by, among other things, lack of knowledge about the utilization of services for undiagnosed COPD and assumptions about the utilization and success of smoking cessation measures.

articles.title: Systemic Treatment Trajectories and Comorbidity Burden in Sarcoidosis: A Retrospective Monocentric Real-World Analysis. Treatment and Comorbidity in Sarcoidosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disease with a variable clinical course. In real-world practice, treatment initiation, tapering strategies, and duration are heterogeneous, and data on the relationship between treatment exposure and comorbidity burden remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective monocentric observational study including adults with sarcoidosis followed at a tertiary referral centre from January 2010 to November 2025. Demographic, clinical, radiological, therapeutic, and comorbidity data were extracted from a prospectively maintained database. Associations between treatment variables and documented hypertension and bone mineral density (BMD) impairment were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 835 patients were included. At baseline, 81.8% received pharmacological treatment, most commonly corticosteroids alone. Extrapulmonary involvement was present in 45.4% and was associated with treatment initiation and escalation to immunosuppressive therapy. During follow-up, 664 patients received systemic corticosteroids for a mean treatment duration of 38.4 ± 64.3 months, and 25.9% received immunosuppressive agents, predominantly methotrexate. After multivariable adjustment, longer corticosteroid treatment duration was associated with documented hypertension (OR 1.008 per month, 95% CI 1.0002-1.016; p=0.045) and BMD impairment (OR 1.009 per month, 95% CI 1.0002-1.018; p=0.046), whereas initial corticosteroid dose was not significantly associated with either outcome.

CONCLUSION: Longer corticosteroid treatment duration was associated with documented hypertension and BMD impairment. However, unavailable comorbidity onset dates, cumulative corticosteroid dose data, and potential confounding by indication preclude causal interpretation. Prospective studies are needed to clarify treatment-related risks.

articles.title: Is GDF-15 the missing link between intermittent hypoxia, carotid body plasticity, and cardiometabolic disease?
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a worldwide epidemic and is strongly associated with cardiometabolic comorbidities such as hypertension, arrhythmias and heart failure. Its principal cardiovascular pathological driver is chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH). CIH induces maladaptive plasticity in the carotid body (CB), the main peripheral oxygen sensor. Profound nitro-oxidative stress and localized inflammation lead to relentless sympathetic overactivity and autonomic imbalance, causing persistent CB hyperactivity. Although this chemoreflex arc is well-characterized, the molecular messengers linking local hypoxemic stress to systemic cardiovascular decline are poorly defined. We propose that Growth Differentiation Factor-15 (GDF-15) is a very likely candidate for this bridge. GDF-15 is a well-established cardiovascular prognostic biomarker. It is strongly upregulated by hypoxia, oxidative stress and HIF stabilization. Plasma GDF-15 is related to the severity of OSA, nocturnal hypoxemia and arrhythmogenic remodeling, and is progressively reduced in clinical settings after continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. In addition to being a systemic biomarker, we speculate that local production of GDF-15 in the oxidative CB microenvironment may have autocrine/paracrine effects that maintain glomus cell hyperexcitability but this remains to be proven experimentally. Also, circulating GDF-15 may act on brainstem GFRAL receptors to enhance chemoreflex drive. We emphasize that this peripheral to central axis, localized CB signaling is a theoretical model that should be tested directly in the lab. Ultimately, therapeutic targeting of this GDF-15 axis at the CB-brainstem interface may provide a life-changing strategy to ameliorate complications of sleep-disordered breathing.

articles.title: Comment on "De novo Belatacept based immunosuppression is not associated with increased risk of invasive fungal infection in kidney transplant recipients".
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons

articles.title: Updates on management of pretransplant and peritransplant infections: Guidance from the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: An expert panel of the American Society of Transplantation Infectious Diseases Community of Practice reviewed and updated guidance highlighting developments since the prior version published in 2019. A 5-article series provides guidance on screening, diagnosis, and treatment of infections in transplantation. This section focuses on donor and recipient screening and assessment of donor-derived infections, pretransplant ventricular assist device infections, and perioperative prophylaxis. The assessment and management of posttransplant infectious syndromes, including intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and diarrhea are presented. Recommendations are made based on the modified Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

articles.title: Second multistate outbreak of tuberculosis caused by a bone allograft product.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: In 2021 and 2023, two different bone allograft products caused nationwide tuberculosis outbreaks. We assessed the morbidity and mortality of the second outbreak and reviewed donor and tissue screening to identify deficiencies. Thirty-six people residing in nine states received the product during spinal and dental procedures. Twenty-seven recipients had tuberculosis infection, 11 had microbiologic or imaging evidence of tuberculosis disease, and two died from tuberculosis within 12 months of outbreak detection. Another recipient died from tuberculosis nearly 3 years after product implantation. The bone donor died of pneumonia and septic shock. Polymerase chain reaction testing of the product before and after distribution did not detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Mycobacterial culture was not performed until after outbreak detection, when M. tuberculosis was isolated from 2 of 6 unused product units. This outbreak demonstrates persistent gaps in tissue transplant safety. Appropriate selection of donors and mycobacterial culture of donated tissues could reduce but not eliminate the risk of M. tuberculosis transmission. Therefore, it is important that clinicians monitor tissue recipients and promptly report adverse events to tissue establishments and health authorities.

articles.title: The Role of Uric Acid in Liver Injury: From Association to Mechanism and Clinical Implications.
articles.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
articles.abstract: Uric acid has traditionally been viewed as the end product of purine metabolism. However, growing evidence suggests a close association between hyperuricemia (HUA) and the development and progression of liver diseases, particularly metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This review systematically summarizes the epidemiological associations and causal links between uric acid and liver diseases, focusing on the molecular mechanisms by which uric acid drives hepatic injury. Specifically, we highlight how uric acid induces metabolic reprogramming, oxidative stress, NLRP3 inflammasome activation, and gut-liver axis crosstalk. We propose that in the context of acquired metabolic disturbances, uric acid acts not merely as a passive biomarker but as a "conditional pathogenic driver" of liver injury. This perspective provides a theoretical basis for urate-lowering therapy as a potential hepatoprotective strategy. Furthermore, this review addresses the complexities of current causal relationships and the challenges in clinical translation, outlining key directions for future research.

articles.title: Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.
articles.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Zinc (Zn) deficiency (ZnD) is a major risk factor for metabolic and inflammatory diseases associated with gut microbial alterations, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. Despite its importance, there are no established dietary recommendations for Zn supplementation in individuals with these conditions, except in cases of severe diarrhea in children. This gap stems from inconsistent outcomes in Zn supplementation trials, suggesting an incomplete understanding of Zn-mediated spatial regulation within the host-microbiome interface.

METHODS: Here, we employed a multi-omics approach to investigate Zn-driven host-gut microbial interactions along the intestinal tract of mice fed Zn-adequate (ZnA) or ZnD diets.

RESULTS: Radiotracing and metallomics analyses revealed region-specific Zn gradients across intestinal tissues and demonstrated reduced mucosal Zn levels in conventionalized compared with germ-free mice, highlighting an influence of microbial colonization on mucosal Zn availability. Transcriptomic analyses identified shared interferon-dominant immune activation in both the small intestine (SI) and the colon under ZnD conditions, accompanied by region-specific epithelial remodeling programs. In the SI, ZnD suppressed apical surface gene networks while inducing Paneth cell-associated antimicrobial responses. In contrast, ZnD colon exhibited suppression of apical junction and extracellular matrix (ECM) structural gene programs. Metagenomic profiling revealed reduced microbial diversity in the SI under ZnD, while the colon displayed enrichment of glycan-degrading taxa, including Hungatella hathewayi and Bacteroides ovatus, along with Clostridioides difficile, a glycan-responsive pathogen that benefits from microbial glycan degradation. Integrated host-microbe correlation and network analyses in the colon identified coordinated associations between ECM/cytoskeletal gene expression and glycosaminoglycan (GAG)-utilizing bacterial taxa. Functional annotation demonstrated enrichment of GAG-catabolic enzymes under ZnD conditions, with the strongest homology mapping to B. ovatus and H. hathewayi, and qPCR confirmed increased tissue-associated abundance of bacterial GAG-utilizing gene sequences alongside reduced host ECM gene expression.

CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Zn deficiency induces region-specific host epithelial and microbial adaptations, revealing a coordinated ECM-GAG-microbe axis in the colon and distinct epithelial remodeling programs along the intestinal tract.

articles.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric and adolescent gynecology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB) affects up to 40% of adolescent and reproductive-age females and is a leading cause of complications such as severe anemia, iron deficiency and hospitalization. In adolescents and young women, it is commonly linked to anovulatory cycles and underlying inherited bleeding disorders, with von Willebrand disease (VWD) being the most prevalent but frequently underdiagnosed. This systematic review explores the prevalence of VWD among adolescents and young women aged ≤25 years assessed for HMB within hospital-based settings and evaluates diagnostic setting gradients.

METHODS: This review included six databases - PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, and ProQuest that were searched electronically using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. After the search, the articles were transferred to Rayyan software for further screening. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Prevalence Critical Appraisal Tool. Data extraction was performed, and the findings were presented narratively.

RESULTS: Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting revealed a distinct diagnostic gradient: Specialized Hematology and Hemophilia Treatment Centres (HTCs) demonstrated the highest prevalence at 16.78% (77/459), followed by Inpatient / Acute Emergency Admissions at 10.20% (25/245), General Tertiary Referral Hospital Settings at 10.20% (65/637), and Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) / Multidisciplinary Outpatient HMB Clinics at 8.70% (32/368).

CONCLUSION: von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024563010.

articles.title: Predicting personal PM2.5 exposure among community-dwelling older adults using multi-source environmental, residential, and behavioral information.
articles.abstract: Individual exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) varies according to environmental, residential, and behavioral contexts. This study aimed to predict personal PM2.5 exposure among community-dwelling older adults and examine candidate variables using a Bayesian LASSO model incorporating information from multiple exposure-related domains. A total of 247 adults aged ≥60 years were recruited in Fuzhou, China. Each participant completed one 72-h personal PM2.5 monitoring session during either the summer or winter campaign, with outdoor PM2.5 measured concurrently and residential, environmental, behavioral, and time-activity information collected through a questionnaire survey. Posterior regression coefficients and their 95% credible intervals were estimated for candidate variables. The model yielded a Bayesian R2 of 0.481 (95% credible interval [CrI]: 0.412-0.539) and an RMSE of 19.260 μg/m3 (95% CrI: 18.797-19.876). Four variables had positive posterior regression coefficients, with 95% CrIs excluding zero: passive smoking only [16.157 μg/m3 (95% CrI: 7.920-24.462)], current smoking [12.949 μg/m3 (95% CrI: 7.047-18.843)], residence near a major road [7.398 μg/m3 (95% CrI: 0.655-14.195)], and outdoor PM2.5 concentration (per 1 SD) [6.531 μg/m3 (95% CrI: 3.798-9.351)]. The coefficient directions of these four variables were highly consistent across repeated cross-validation. These findings may inform future studies aimed at further evaluating and refining individualized PM2.5 exposure assessment in older populations.

articles.title: Sauchinone protects against pathological cardiac hypertrophy by targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major contributor to heart failure and remains insufficiently targeted by current therapies that primarily focus on hemodynamic regulation rather than underlying molecular mechanisms. Sauchinone, a bioactive lignan isolated from Saururus chinensis, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective effects. However, its role in pathological cardiac hypertrophy and the associated mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of sauchinone on pathological cardiac hypertrophy and to elucidate its potential mechanism. The H9c2, a rat cardiomyocyte cell line, along with human embryonic stem cells-derived cardiomyocytes (hESC-CMs), were employed to investigate the therapeutic potential of sauchinone on angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced hypertrophy in vitro. An established mouse model of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced cardiac hypertrophy model were used for the animal studies. The investigation combined proteomics with molecular docking to explore the mechanisms by which sauchinone influences pathological cardiac hypertrophy. Sauchinone significantly attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, as evidenced by reduced cell size and decreased expression of hypertrophic markers in both H9c2 cells and hESC-CMs. In vivo, sauchinone markedly improved cardiac structure and function, reduced myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis, and restored systolic and diastolic function in HCM and TAC mice. Mechanistically, quantitative proteomics and pathway enrichment analyses revealed that sauchinone significantly inhibited the PI3K-Akt and NF-κB signaling pathways, which was further confirmed by reduced phosphorylation of key pathway components. Notably, protein-protein interaction analysis, molecular docking, and target engagement assays demonstrated that sauchinone directly interacts with cyclin-dependent kinase 4 (CDK4) and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), suggesting a dual-target mechanism. Collectively, these findings indicate that sauchinone alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy by coordinately suppressing inflammatory and growth signaling pathways via targeting the TLR4-NF-κB and CDK4-PI3K-Akt axes. Sauchinone may therefore represent a promising multi-target therapeutic candidate for the treatment of pathological cardiac hypertrophy.

articles.title: A 96-well dual-sample-preparation LC-MS/MS method for integrated quantification of eight urinary catecholamines and metabolites.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrated quantification of urinary free catecholamines and their metabolites is important for the biochemical evaluation of pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma (PPGL) and neuroblastoma, but the physicochemical diversity of these analytes complicates LC-MS/MS analysis.

METHODS: A 96-well dual-sample-preparation LC-MS/MS method was developed. Six basic amines-norepinephrine, epinephrine, dopamine, normetanephrine, metanephrine, and 3-methoxytyramine-were extracted by weak cation-exchange solid-phase extraction with HEPES pH stabilization. Two acidic metabolites-homovanillic acid and vanillylmandelic acid-were analyzed after acid dilution. Detection was performed by positive/negative electrospray ionization multiple reaction monitoring.

RESULTS: The method showed good linearity with r2 ≥ 0.996 over clinically relevant ranges. Intra- and inter-assay precision were 1.62%-7.62% and 1.72%-8.53% RSD, respectively, with accuracy of 94.5%-112.8%. Carryover, matrix consistency, spike recovery, stability, and dilution integrity all met acceptance criteria. External quality assessment deviations were all within ±20%. In 15 patients with primary hypertension, urinary norepinephrine, normetanephrine, and metanephrine were significantly higher than in 15 healthy controls (P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: The method enables integrated quantification of eight urinary catecholamines and metabolites in a single workflow, providing a validated analytical platform for combined PPGL and neuroblastoma marker profiling; its diagnostic performance requires validation in confirmed disease cohorts.

articles.title: Current approaches and future directions of Endothelin-1 detection.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Endothelin-1 (ET-1) is a peptide comprised of 21 amino acids that exhibits the strongest vasoconstrictor effect identified in the human body. Beyond its role in vascular tone regulation, ET-1 functions as a critical mediator of inflammation, fibrosis, and cellular proliferation. Elevated ET-1 levels are consistently observed in cardiovascular diseases (hypertension, heart failure, atherosclerosis), pulmonary arterial hypertension, chronic kidney disease, diabetic nephropathy, and various malignancies. This establishes ET-1 as a potential biomarker for early detection, disease classification, and therapy assessment. This review offers an extensive analysis of ET-1 biology, its clinical importance, and the detection methods that are currently accessible. We assess traditional methods such as enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), radioimmunoassay (RIA), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), and surface plasmon resonance (SPR), in addition to new electrochemical biosensing technologies. Electrochemical biosensors, leveraging antibody-antigen or aptamer-target interactions, present a transformative alternative offering rapid response, portability, and suitability for point-of-care applications. This review identifies current challenges, highlights recent technological advances, and outlines future directions for translating ET-1 biosensing from research laboratories to clinical practice, ultimately aiming to improve patient outcomes through earlier and more accessible diagnostics.

articles.title: The atherosclerotic cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic burden in the Asia-Pacific, 1990-2050: A global burden of disease 2023 analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide, with the Asia-Pacific region bearing over half of this burden. The cardiovascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CKLM) framework unifies the interrelated conditions of cardiovascular disease (CVD), chronic kidney disease (CKD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, which synergistically contribute to heightened cardiovascular risk. However, the combined CKLM burden in the region has not been characterised.

METHODS: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023, we examined mortality and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) of CKLM diseases across 39 Asia-Pacific countries from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. The CKLM burden was organized into metabolic antecedents (comprising CKD, MASLD, T2DM and obesity) and downstream atherosclerotic CVD (comprising ischemic heart disease, stroke, aortic aneurysm, and peripheral artery disease).

FINDINGS: In 2023, the Asia-Pacific recorded 286.9 million CKLM-related DALYs (53.2% of global burden), with an age-standardised DALY rate of 6390.9 per 100,000 population. From 1990 to 2023, crude DALYs rose by 78.7%, outpacing the global trends (61.1%), while age-standardised DALYs fell by 25.0% - driven by improvements in atherosclerotic CVD (-35.2%) but counterbalanced by a 20.4% rise in metabolic antecedents. By 2050, age-standardised DALY rates are projected to show a 7.0% point-estimate increase regionally against an estimated 14.9% global decline, with metabolic antecedents likely to expand from 29.9% to 36.2% of the total burden between 2026 and 2050. Intraregional disparities exist across sociodemographic strata, subregions, and age-sex categories. Risk-deleted analyses identify high systolic blood pressure, high fasting plasma glucose, and dietary risks as the highest-yield modifiable targets.

INTERPRETATION: The worsening Asia-Pacific CKLM trajectory is decoupling from improving global trends, driven by a compositional shift from atherosclerotic CVD toward upstream metabolic antecedents. Integrated interventions addressing multiple key modifiable risks are needed.

articles.title: Human Pregnane X Receptor Modulates Sex-Dependent Hepatic Oxidative Stress and Inflammatory Responses in Alcohol-Induced Liver Injury.
articles.abstract: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) remains a major global health burden with limited targeted therapies. Although the pregnane X receptor (PXR) has been implicated in ALD pathogenesis, the specific contribution of human PXR signaling to ethanol-induced liver injury remains unclear. Here, we investigated the impact of human PXR on ethanol-induced hepatotoxicity, histopathology, inflammation, oxidative stress, immune-cell composition, and hepatic transcriptional profiles. Male and female wild-type (WT, C57BL/6N) and PXR-humanized (hPXR) mice were subjected to the chronic-plus-binge ethanol regimen, followed by comprehensive hepatic and systemic profiling. Ethanol-fed female hPXR mice developed more severe steatosis and hepatotoxicity than their WT counterparts. This exacerbated liver injury was accompanied by elevated circulating acetaldehyde, increased hepatic hydrogen peroxide levels, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, enhanced NF-κB activation, and reduced mitochondrial ALDH2 protein expression and activity, consistent with impaired acetaldehyde detoxification and ROS accumulation. Hepatic transcriptomics identified differential expression of genes associated with xenobiotic metabolism and pathways potentially involved in non-oxidative ethanol metabolism, including members of the Ces2a and Sult2a gene families. Splenic and mesenteric lymph node CD3+ T-cell frequencies and circulating IL-5 concentrations were elevated in females regardless of genotype or ethanol exposure, indicating baseline sex-dependent immune differences rather than broad human PXR-dependent systemic immune activation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that human PXR promotes susceptibility to ethanol-induced liver injury, particularly in females via impaired acetaldehyde clearance, oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and altered hepatic gene expression as potential mechanisms. These results establish hPXR mice as a translational model for dissecting human PXR-dependent mechanisms and therapeutic targets in ALD.

articles.title: Sema4D Deficiency Protects Against Sepsis-Associated Liver Injury by Modulating Ferroptosis-Associated Responses and Macrophage Polarization.
articles.abstract: Sema4D contributes to inflammatory responses, but its role in sepsis-associated liver injury remains unclear. We examined this role using Sema4D-knockout mice, hepatic Sema4D overexpression, and LPS-treated AML12 hepatocytes and RAW264.7 macrophages. Sema4D levels were elevated in the serum of patients with sepsis, mouse liver tissues after cecal ligation and puncture (CLP), and LPS-treated cells. Sema4D knockout reduced serum aminotransferase levels and hepatic histological injury at 24 h after CLP, whereas overexpression aggravated liver injury. Seven-day survival was numerically higher after knockout, but the difference was not statistically significant (n = 10 per group; log-rank P = 0.0751). Proteomic analysis identified ferroptosis among the enriched pathways. Sema4D knockout or knockdown reduced TFR1, NCOA4, and ROS signals and increased GPX4 expression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed changes in hepatic myeloid cell populations and gene expression. Further analyses showed lower expression of examined M1-associated markers and higher expression of selected M2-associated markers following Sema4D knockout or knockdown, with opposite changes after overexpression in RAW264.7 cells. Sema4D manipulation altered MEK/ERK phosphorylation signals, and U0126 attenuated several ferroptosis-associated changes induced by overexpression. These findings demonstrate that Sema4D deficiency protects against liver injury at 24 h after CLP, attenuates ferroptosis-associated responses, and alters macrophage polarization-associated marker expression. The U0126 experiments further support the involvement of MEK/ERK signaling in the ferroptosis-associated effects of Sema4D.

articles.title: Therapeutic effects of β-caryophyllene on urinary tract infection in diabetic mice: Comparison with nitrofurantoin.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
articles.abstract: Urinary tract infection (UTI) represents a prevalent and clinically important complication of diabetes, frequently worsening renal dysfunction and inflammatory damage. This study assessed the therapeutic effectiveness of β-caryophyllene (BCP), both independently and in conjunction with nitrofurantoin (NFN), in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice with experimentally induced UTIs. Animals were categorized into five groups: Control, Diabetic + UTI, Diabetic + UTI + NFN, Diabetic + UTI + BCP, and Diabetic + UTI + NFN + BCP. UTI induction was validated through the quantification of urinary bacterial colony-forming units. Renal function was evaluated using serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), cystatin-C, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1). Systemic inflammation was assessed through serum TNF-α, IL-6, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1). Western blotting was employed to analyze IL-6 protein expression in kidney and bladder tissues, while histopathological methods were utilized to evaluate tissue injury and repair. Diabetic mice with urinary tract infections exhibited significant increases in colony-forming unit counts, renal injury markers, pro-inflammatory cytokines, and interleukin-6 expression, alongside considerable damage to the kidneys and bladder. Treatment with BCP or NFN resulted in a significant reduction in bacterial load, renal biomarkers, and inflammatory mediators, alongside an enhancement in tissue architecture. Combined NFN + BCP therapy resulted in significant improvements, exhibiting strong antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and renoprotective effects. The findings indicate that BCP may serve as a beneficial adjunctive therapy for reducing UTI-related renal complications in diabetes.

articles.title: Temporal changes of ECG progression in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise may influence phenotypic expression in arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM). We investigated ECG progression in a large ACM cohort, focusing on exercise exposure.

METHODS: Of 202 retrospectively assessed patients, including genotype-positive/phenotype-negative individuals, 163 had ≥2 analysable ECGs and were stratified into "sedentary/low" and "moderate/high" exercise groups based on post-diagnosis exercise intensity. The primary composite endpoint included major ventricular arrhythmias, appropriate implantable cardioverter-defibrillator interventions, sudden cardiac arrest and sudden cardiac death.

RESULTS: Among 163 patients, (56% male; mean age 47 ± 16y)almost one-third (n = 52, 32%) continued moderate/high-intensity exercise and 107 (66%) exhibited abnormal baseline ECGs (anterior T-wave inversion (ATWI) n = 42, 26%). At follow-up, 9% developed new ATWI and 45% demonstrated TWI progression (TWI deepening and/or extension). PKP2 carriers more frequently demonstrated ATWI progression (p = 0.002). Baseline low QRS voltages (LQRSV) were found in 12%; 6% developed new LQRSV during follow-up and 23% exhibited substantial total limb‑lead QRSV reduction. Among 22 genotype-positive/phenotype-negative individuals, none developed ATWI progression or experienced the primary arrhythmic event. Abnormal ECG prevalence increased within the moderate/high-intensity exercise group (55% to 72%; p = 0.027), although exercise was not independently associated with composite ECG progression (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.72-3.11). Over 4.6 ± 2.5 years, 28 patients (17%) experienced primary events. Baseline inferior TWI (HR 3.79, 95% CI 1.60-8.97, p = 0.002) and total limb lead QRSV <3 mV (HR 2.40, 95% CI 1.05-5.48, p = 0.037) were independently associated with arrhythmic risk.

CONCLUSIONS: ECG abnormalities evolve across the ACM spectrum. Exercise was not independently associated with ECG progression. Baseline inferior TWI and reduced total limb‑lead QRSV may aid arrhythmic risk assessment.

articles.title: Serum EV Lipidomics identifies candidate markers associated with MASLD-related HCC.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Non-invasive tools for disease progression are still lacking in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are liquid-biopsy platforms. We aimed to characterize the lipid signature of circulating serum EVs across MASLD stages and features.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed serum EVs from 118 individuals-25 controls and 93 MASLD patients (25 steatosis, 25 steatohepatitis/MASH, 25 cirrhosis, and 18 MASLD-related HCC)-using nanoparticle tracking and EV marker analysis. Targeted LC-MS/MS quantified sphingolipids, oxysterols and bile acids in EVs. Differences were assessed using appropriate comparative testing, and candidate biomarkers were evaluated using ROC analysis. External validation was performed using a publicly available lipidomic dataset.

RESULTS: Mean age 59 years, 60% women, 70% type 2 diabetes, 96% metabolic syndrome. Several sphingolipids (C20-SM, C22-SM, C24:0-Cer and C24:1-Cer) were higher in controls/early MASLD stages than in cirrhosis/HCC. C20-SM was markedly reduced in HCC and showed good discrimination for HCC versus other MASLD stages (AUC=0.906). Multiple bile acids (CA, CDCA-3-S, and TLCA) were elevated in HCC. PNPLA3 GG genotype was more frequent in HCC, with higher EV TCDCA levels (p<0.001). External validation confirmed progressive dysregulation of C20-SM and C22-SM (higher in NASH and reduced in cirrhosis).

CONCLUSIONS: Serum EV lipid profiles are associated with MASLD disease stage, with reduced EV sphingolipids and increased EV bile acids in advanced disease. C20-SM emerged as a candidate biomarker for MASLD-related HCC, warranting confirmation in independent cohorts and with robust validation.

articles.title: The Association between Physical Activity and Higher Corticolimbic Synaptic Density is Independent of Body Mass Index.
articles.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Regular physical exercise has been linked to biomarkers of slowed biological aging, including brain aging, though the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this relationship remain unclear. Exercise may enhance neuroplasticity and attenuate synaptic decline; however, evidence supporting these effects has largely been limited to animal and postmortem studies. Whether physical activity is associated with synaptic density in the living human brain remains unknown.

METHODS: We used positron emission tomography (PET) with the radiotracer [18F]SynVesT-1 to quantify synaptic density in vivo in 51 individuals (61% female). Participants were classified as physically active or insufficiently active, and group differences in synaptic density across corticolimbic regions were examined. Additional regression and mediation analyses assessed associations among physical activity, synaptic density, body mass index (BMI), and depressive symptom severity.

RESULTS: Physically active individuals exhibited significantly higher synaptic density across corticolimbic regions compared to insufficiently active individuals (F6,44=2.41, p=0.042). These effects remained marginally significant after adjusting for BMI and depressive symptom severity (F6,42=2.33, p=0.050). Region-specific regression analyses further demonstrated positive associations between physical activity and synaptic density. Mediation analyses indicated that BMI did not account for the observed relationships.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide the first known in vivo evidence that physical activity is associated with higher synaptic density in the living human brain, particularly within prefrontal circuits. Results suggest that exercise may support synaptic integrity through mechanisms partially independent of BMI. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine causality, characterize temporal dynamics, and evaluate whether physical activity may serve as a scalable intervention to preserve synaptic health.

articles.title: The effects of size and sex mismatch on kidney functional adaption following living donor kidney transplantation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The remarkable functional adaption of transplanted kidneys is poorly understood. Conflicting results for donor-recipient body size and sex mismatches, and concerns for hyperfiltration injury are unresolved.

METHODS: This single center, longitudinal cohort study of 194 living kidney transplantations evaluated changes in isotopic 9 9mTc-DTPA measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) from side-specific donor function at implantation through 12-months after transplantation against multiple anthropometric parameters, sex mismatch, and pathological hyperfiltration.

RESULTS: Donor kidney mGFR was predicted by younger age, male sex, and heavier body weight using multivariable analysis; and strongly influenced 12-month mGFR. Post-transplant relative and absolute mGFR changes were determined by donor and recipient body sizes (weight, body surface area, and body mass index were statistically interchangeable) and donor and recipient sex using multivariable analysis. mGFR adaption was greatest in smaller female donor kidneys transplanted into large male recipients, but negligible or negative for male kidneys into female recipients. The mGFR ratio significantly correlated with mismatch in donor-recipient body surface area (r=0.285) and body mass index (r=0.248). Absolute mGFR significantly increased with recipient lean body mass (r=0.425) but not total fat content using body composition analysis. Diabetes, fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c, androgenic hormones, and hypertension were unrelated. Evidence of significant maladaptive glomerular hyperfiltration assessed by albuminuria, glomerular pathology, percentage glomerulosclerosis, glomerulomegaly, transcription factor WT1 podocyte immunostaining, chronic interstitial fibrosis, and ultrastructural podocyte effacement at 12-months was absent. Death-censored graft survivals for five-, 10-, and 20-years after transplantation were excellent at 96.9%, 94.3%, and 80.8%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: mGFR following transplantation depends on input donor quality with adaption driven primarily by larger recipient body size mismatch and male sex. Functional adaption appears as a benign physiological response appropriately calibrated to individual recipient metabolic need without evidence of pathological hyperfiltration injury.

articles.title: Persistence and Inflammation of Residual Radicular Cysts After Removal of the Endodontic Source: A Case Report and Implications for True Cyst Healing.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Residual radicular cysts may persist after extraction and are sometimes cited as indirect evidence for the true cyst hypothesis. This hypothesis proposes that a completely enclosed apical cyst may become self-sustaining after elimination of the intraradicular infection. This interpretation assumes that extraction also removes other local stimuli capable of maintaining the lesion. This report describes a case of a persistent residual radicular cyst in which histopathologic examination revealed microbial foci and associated inflammatory changes.

CASE REPORT: A 55-year-old woman had multiple cyst-like jaw radiolucencies. All remaining teeth were extracted, and periapical pathologic tissues were removed except for a large mandibular left premolar lesion that could not be retrieved through the socket. At 6 months, the other sites showed osseous repair, whereas the retained lesion persisted. Enucleation yielded a large cyst and a small separate cyst. Serial examination showed a thin, minimally inflamed lining through most of the large cyst. Bacteria were confined to a small region of necrotic luminal contents and coincided with polymorphonuclear neutrophil accumulation and transepithelial inflammatory cell migration. Abundant cholesterol clefts generally lacked a macrophage or multinucleated giant cell response. The small cyst contained infected dentin fragments with intense inflammation. Substantial osseous repair was evident 3 years 10 months after enucleation.

CONCLUSIONS: Residual cysts that persist after extraction may coexist with localized bacteria and acute inflammation. Residual microbial stimulation may contribute to continued cyst activity. Highly focal bacterial distribution also explains why limited histologic sampling may miss infection. Persistence of a residual cyst alone is insufficient to infer that a pre-existing true apical cyst was self-sustaining.

articles.title: Validation of a Simplified Multiparametric Screening Approach for Cardiac Amyloidosis using Echocardiography.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography

articles.title: Early COVID-19 Public Health Emergency Disruption and Non-COVID Infection-Related Hospitalizations in Home Health Care.
articles.abstract: Using linked national Medicare data from 2019-2020, we examined non-COVID infection-related hospitalizations across 7,956,006 home health care (HHC) episodes before and immediately after COVID-19 public health emergency onset. In adjusted models, the early public health emergency (PHE) period was not associated with hospitalization among White patients; Black patients experienced a significant increase, narrowing the pre-PHE Black-White difference. Findings highlight the need for resilient HHC infection monitoring and escalation pathways during public health disruptions.

articles.title: Public Health Nurse-Led Infection Control in an Evacuation Center: Lessons from the Eaton Wildfire Response Case Report.
articles.abstract: In January 2025, infection control strategies were implemented at an Eaton wildfire evacuation center. Standardized risk assessments, symptom screenings, and surveillance processes were implemented. Systematic daily monitoring of symptoms enabled early identification of respiratory illness (27.9%) and gastrointestinal (GI) illness symptoms (12.4%). This informed real-time decisions on isolation areas, staffing, and sanitation protocols. Despite resource-limited surveillance approaches, implementing public health nursing expertise can effectively support rapid decision-making and health prevention in disaster settings.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Infection Control Nursing Competency Scale for Intensive Care Unit Nurses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to develop an infection control nursing competency (ICNC) scale for intensive care unit (ICU) nurses and evaluate its psychometric properties.

METHODS: Scale development included item generation based on a previously developed theoretical model, expert content validity testing, and a national online survey of 355 ICU nurses in South Korea. Construct validity was examined using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). Known-groups validity, criterion-related validity, and internal consistency reliability were also evaluated.

RESULTS: The final 36-item scale comprised three factors: "Fundamental Infection Control," "Prevention of Infection Transmission and Safety," and "Infection Control Practices in ICUs." CFA demonstrated a moderate model fit. The scale exhibited high internal consistency (Cronbach's α =.92). Known-groups validity was supported, as nurses with over seven years' experience scored significantly higher in total and Factors 2 and 3 scores than junior groups. Criterion-related validity was established through a strong correlation with an existing ICNC scale for general nurses.

CONCLUSIONS: The newly developed scale demonstrates acceptable reliability and preliminary evidence of validity for assessing ICU nurses' self-reported ICNC. The instrument may be useful for identifying competency gaps and informing career-stage-appropriate education, orientation, and quality improvement initiatives in ICU infection prevention and control.

articles.title: Low-Carbohydrate, Animal-Centered Diets and Plant-Based Diets Exert Opposing Effects on Cardiometabolic Diseases.
articles.abstract: Low-carbohydrate, animal-centered (LCAC) diets are promoted for the prevention and treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D) and cardiovascular disease (CVD) because randomized trials have shown short-term reductions in select risk factors, such as body weight, triglycerides, and glycated hemoglobin. However, controlled feeding studies have shown increases in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), apolipoprotein B, and circulating free fatty acids with LCAC diets. Importantly, LCAC diets can also drive lipotoxicity and inflammation. These latter pathological biochemical effects directly act on pathways involved in the development of T2D and CVD. In contrast, high-carbohydrate, unrefined plant-based diets in these conditions reduce insulin requirements even without weight loss, lower blood pressure and medication use, and improve atherogenic lipoproteins and inflammation. Meta-analyses of randomized trials demonstrate reductions in LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and glycated hemoglobin with vegetarian or vegan diets. Further, plant-based dietary interventions have also shown regression of coronary atherosclerosis and improvements in myocardial perfusion and cardiac function, an effect absent from LCAC diet literature. Thus, public health efforts aimed at the prevention and treatment of T2D and CVD should continue to focus on improving the quantity and quality of plant foods consumed rather than carbohydrate restriction alone.

articles.title: Host defense peptide-DNA complexation alters bacterial DNA organization and immunostimulatory activity.
articles.abstract: During infection, microbial DNA released from damaged or disrupted microbes can contribute to local immune activation, while its biological activity may also depend on how it is organized and presented within the tissue microenvironment. Here, the cathelicidin host defense peptide (HDP) Hc-CATH was used to investigate how peptide-DNA complexation alters the physicochemical state and downstream immunostimulatory activity of extracellular DNA. Hc-CATH bound native bacterial DNA and promoted the condensation of CpG oligodeoxynucleotide (ODN) 2395, a defined synthetic DNA model that activates Toll-like receptor 9, into particulate assemblies. Using Hc-CATH and CpG ODN 2395 as a standardized experimental system, we revealed that complexation altered DNA diffusional behavior and local signal persistence and was associated with enhanced antigen-specific antibody and cytokine responses, early immune-cell mobilization, dendritic-cell activation, and distinct transcriptional responses. In an outer membrane vesicle immunization and bacterial challenge model, the Hc-CATH-CpG formulation was also associated with improved control of infection-related outcomes. More importantly, several structurally diverse cationic peptides similarly complexed with CpG ODN 2395 and modified its immunostimulatory effects, indicating that DNA complexation may represent a broader physicochemical property of positively charged peptides. Together, these findings show that HDP-mediated DNA complexation can reorganize extracellular microbial DNA and alter its availability and downstream immune effects.

articles.title: Deletion of thioredoxin reductase 1 in pancreatic β-cells impairs glucose metabolism and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic β-cells control whole body glucose homeostasis by secreting insulin in response to a glucose challenge. These cells are perceived to be vulnerable to damage by reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to the hypothesis that oxidative stress contributes to β-cell dysfunction and loss in diabetes. As we recently demonstrated, β-cells possess a robust antioxidant defense system dependent on thioredoxin reductase. Given the link between elevated ROS and impaired β-cell function together with the central role of thioredoxin reductase 1 (Txnrd1) in regulating ROS levels, this study tested the hypothesis that Txnrd1 is essential for normal glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. Supporting this hypothesis, we show that Txnrd1 depletion impairs glucose-stimulated calcium flux and insulin secretion in β-cells, and these effects are associated with glucose intolerance in mice with a β-cell-specific knockout of Txnrd1, although the effect only reached statistical significance in males. We further hypothesized that Txnrd1 loss may alter protein oxidation. Indeed, we detected elevated oxidation of proteins involved in regulating glucose metabolism, including the mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GPD2) and the mitochondrial voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC) in β-cells deficient in Txnrd1. Finally, we demonstrate that Txnrd1-deficient β-cells have a reduced NAD+/NADH ratio and marked impairments in glucose metabolism characterized by decreased intracellular pyruvate and increased extracellular lactate. Together, our results indicate that Txnrd1 is critical for maintaining β-cell function and glucose homeostasis, with its absence leading to redox-associated metabolic dysfunction and impaired insulin secretion.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of heart failure patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation: SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To assess the referral rate to cardiac rehabilitation (CR), the clinical profile of referred vs nonreferred patients, and the association between referral and clinical events in Spanish heart failure (HF) units.

METHODS: The SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort of patients with HF in units accredited by the Spanish Society of Cardiology. Patients were classified according to CR referral and were followed up for up to 400 days for all-cause death, HF hospitalization or decompensation, and the combined endpoint of death or HF hospitalization, with outcomes analyzed using Cox regression.

RESULTS: Of 2236 patients, 219 (9.8%) were referred to CR. Referred patients were younger (65.2  ±  11.7 vs 71.7  ±  12.2 years), more often male (73.5% vs 63.2%) and more frequently had an ischemic etiology (50.5% vs 28.8%), fewer comorbidities and more frequent use of quadruple therapy (59.4% vs 46.0%); 74.4% had HF with reduced ejection fraction (11.9% had HF with preserved ejection fraction, and 13.7% HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction). The lower crude rate of the combined endpoint (HR, 0.75; 95%CI, 0.56-1.01) was no longer observed after adjustment (HR, 0.99; 95%CI, 0.71-1.38), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: CR referral was infrequent and preferentially directed toward younger patients with ischemic HF with reduced ejection fraction, a lower comorbidity burden, and optimized therapy, whereas older patients, patients with multimorbidity, and those with HF with preserved ejection fraction remained underrepresented. The lower crude event rate was no longer observed after adjustment for measured baseline characteristics, and the observational design does not allow conclusions on the effect of CR itself.

articles.title: Nat10 is required for hepatic metabolic homeostasis and regulates Fgf1 expression and the Notch/Spp1 axis.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular and cell biology of lipids
articles.abstract: N-acetyltransferase 10 (NAT10) is the sole enzyme that catalyzes ac4C RNA modification. Recent studies have implicated NAT10 in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and liver fibrosis under pathological conditions, but its physiological role in the normal liver remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the function of hepatic NAT10 in maintaining metabolic homeostasis. Hepatocyte-specific Nat10 knockout (Nat10HKO) and adeno-associated virus-mediated overexpression models were generated. The effects of Nat10 knockout or overexpression were assessed by H&E and Oil Red O staining, and serum biochemistry. Integrated RNA-seq and acRIP-seq analyses were performed to identify downstream targets, followed by validation using qRT-PCR, western blot and acRIP-qPCR analysis. We found that Nat10HKO mice on a normal chow diet developed spontaneous hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and a pro-fibrotic gene signature, whereas Nat10 overexpression had no detectable effect. Integrated RNA-seq and acRIP-seq analyses identified fibroblast growth factor 1 (Fgf1), a well-established regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, as a candidate downstream target of Nat10-mediated ac4C modification. Moreover, Nat10HKO livers exhibited upregulation of Notch components. Nat10 overexpression in AML12 hepatocytes suppressed, whereas Nat10 knockdown enhanced, the expression of Notch1 and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (Spp1). These findings indicate that Nat10 is required for the maintenance of hepatic metabolic homeostasis. It sustains Fgf1 expression via ac4C mRNA modification and negatively regulates the Notch/Spp1 axis. Whether reduced Fgf1 expression or Notch/Spp1 activation mediates the phenotype of Nat10-deficient mice remains to be determined.

articles.title: Flow-induced endothelial lipid dysregulation in ischemic stroke: from mechanotransduction to therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) induces significant and sustained alterations in cerebral hemodynamics, which extend beyond the acute phase and actively contribute to post-stroke cerebrovascular remodeling. Accumulating evidence suggests that endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis is a critical determinant of vascular integrity, whereas its dysregulation may promote endothelial inflammation, and vascular remodeling. Abnormal shear stress, particularly low and oscillatory shear stress, may connect post-stroke hemodynamic changes to endothelial lipid dysregulation by regulating lipid uptake, intracellular lipid processing, cholesterol efflux, and lipid storage through mechanotransduction pathways. Although direct evidence demonstrating that altered shear stress drives endothelial lipid accumulation in the cerebral vasculature remains limited, findings from endothelial studies and mechanobiology suggest a functional "flow-lipid axis" implicated in post-stroke vascular pathology. In this review, we summarize the hemodynamic alterations following IS and how abnormal shear stress may regulate endothelial cholesterol and neutral-lipid homeostasis through mechanosensors and downstream pathways, including AMPK, mTOR, SREBP, and lipophagy. We further identify the existing gap in causal evidence connecting post-stroke hemodynamics to cerebral endothelial lipid accumulation, and propose targeted translational research avenues aimed at facilitating the development of hemodynamic- and metabolism-based therapeutic strategies for IS.

articles.title: The molecular interactions of viruses with apolipoproteins: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Host lipid metabolism is extensively hijacked by viruses to support their replication cycle. Apolipoproteins, the core protein components of lipoprotein particles, mediate lipid transport, receptor recognition, and immune regulation, making them key host targets for diverse viruses. This review systematically examines the molecular mechanisms underlying virus-apolipoprotein interactions and establishes a classification framework distinguishing direct from indirect modes of action. Direct interactions involve physical binding between viral components and apolipoproteins or their receptors, exemplified by hepatitis C virus (HCV) ApoE-dependent lipoviroparticle assembly, hepatitis B virus (HBV) ApoE-mediated entry, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein binding to high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-associated apolipoproteins, and rabies virus ApoD-glycoprotein interaction. Indirect mechanisms include viral regulation of apolipoprotein expression through epigenetic modifications, cytokines, and oxidative stress. We also compare the differential effects of ApoE2, ApoE3, and ApoE4 subtypes on infection susceptibility and disease severity across HCV, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), and SARS-CoV-2. The clinical-pathological consequences, including hepatic steatosis, atherosclerosis (AS), dyslipidemia, and thrombotic complications, are discussed, and therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism are critically evaluated. We close by outlining unresolved questions and suggesting future research directions leveraging single-cell multi-omics, spatial biology, and organoid models.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Natural Products: Potential Effects on Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
