BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF), the end-stage of cardiovascular disease (CVD), affects over 64 million people globally. There is an alarming trend of earlier onset, which poses a substantial healthcare burden. Although guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has significantly improved clinical outcomes, residual morbidity and mortality remain considerable, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial energy metabolism (MEM) plays an important role in HF pathophysiology and represents a potential therapeutic target. Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived natural products (TCM-derived NPs) contain diverse bioactive constituents that may influence myocardial energy metabolism and related pathological processes, warranting further investigation into their potential role in HF management.

PURPOSE: This review aims to synthesize current evidence on the involvement of MEM in HF and the potential regulatory effects of TCM-derived NPs. It further integrates mechanistic evidence with exploratory network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses to identify candidate compound-target relationships and discuss their translational implications.

METHODS: The following keywords were used: "heart failure," "traditional Chinese medicine," "ATP synthesis," "oxidative phosphorylation," "fatty acid oxidation," "glucose metabolism," "mitochondrial membrane potential," "reactive oxygen species," "energy metabolism," "mitochondrial dynamics," "calcium signaling," and "energy coupling." Potential targets of NPs were obtained from the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform. We collected disease-related targets from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, GeneCards, and the Therapeutic Target Database. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis was performed using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID). Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed using STRING and analyzed in Cytoscape 3.10.0 to identify candidate hub genes. Ten representative bioactive compounds were separately examined through exploratory molecular docking with the candidate hub proteins.

RESULTS: Herb-frequency analysis of 132 clinical studies identified 15 high-frequency Chinese medicinal herbs for subsequent computational analysis. The literature synthesis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), fatty acid and glucose metabolism as key processes involved in myocardial energetic remodeling in HF. Separately, KEGG enrichment analysis identified pathways related to metabolic regulation, cellular stress, and inflammation, including lipid and atherosclerosis, PI3K-Akt, HIF-1, insulin, and TNF signaling pathways. PPI analysis prioritized AKT1, JUN, TP53, MAPK1, and MAPK3 in the MEM-related network and STAT3, TNF, TP53, IL6, and ESR1 in the inflammation-metabolism crosstalk network, yielding nine unique candidate hub genes after deduplication. Molecular docking of ten representative bioactive compounds with these nine candidate proteins yielded predicted docking scores ranging from -4.5 to -9.7kcal/mol.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence supports MEM as an important component of HF pathophysiology and suggests that selected TCM-derived NPs may influence multiple MEM-related processes relevant to HF. By integrating mechanistic, clinical, and computational evidence, this review provides a structured framework for understanding NPs-MEM-HF relationships and offers a basis for future mechanistic validation and clinical translation.

articles.title: FAPI PET in Liver Fibrosis and Hepatobiliary Cancer: Linking Stromal Imaging to Radioligand Therapy.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) provides a shared imaging target in activated hepatic stroma and hepatobiliary tumor microenvironments. Whether this signal improves clinical decisions or identifies a therapeutic window remains unresolved. This review synthesizes imaging and translational evidence using a systematic search with a publication cutoff of 31 December 2025. Of 445 screened records, 64 reports are retained: 28 on hepatobiliary tumors, 6 on liver fibrosis, 23 on methodological, biodistribution or dosimetry questions, and 7 small series used for narrative illustration. These are report counts, not counts of independent cohorts. Small clinical studies suggest an association between hepatic uptake and fibrosis-related measures, while selected paired imaging studies report greater lesion conspicuity or detection with FAPI than with fluorodeoxyglucose PET. These findings do not establish superiority over standard liver MRI or elastography, transferable diagnostic thresholds, or improved patient outcomes. Inflammation, repair and background fibrosis limit specificity. For therapeutic translation, static uptake must be distinguished from ligand residence time, absorbed radiation dose and clinical benefit. Early radioligand-therapy reports describe feasibility alongside clinically important hematologic toxicity; safety and efficacy in cirrhotic liver populations remain unestablished. We therefore organize the evidence around tracer-specific pharmacokinetics, comparator choice and the joint assessment of lesion exposure and normal-organ vulnerability. Appraisal separates 302 entries using established tools from 104 descriptive reporting entries; non-independent checking and unresolved overlap limit certainty. The proposed clinical pathways are research frameworks requiring prospective validation, not recommendations for routine FAPI PET use.

articles.title: Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda at day 100: an ESCMID Emerging Infections Subcommittee update.
authors: European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda has challenged epidemic control despite rapid expansion of response capacity.

OBJECTIVES: To reassess the threats identified by the ESCMID Emerging Infections Subcommittee at day 100 and identify clinical and public-health priorities.

SOURCES: This narrative update draws on published literature and WHO, Africa CDC, ECDC, and national public health reports, using 22 August 2026 as the day-100 analytical cut-off, with data through 20 October for a subsequent update.

CONTENT: By 22 August, the DRC had reported 5514 confirmed cases and 2642 deaths in 57 health zones across six provinces, making it the largest recorded outbreak in the DRC and the second-largest Ebola outbreak by confirmed case count. Uganda contained 20 cases, and its outbreak was declared over on 27 August. By 20 October, the DRC had reported 9704 cases and 4687 deaths in 66 health zones across eight provinces; Kenya had reported nine epidemiologically linked cases and Nigeria one. Contact follow-up improved, but many transmission chains remained unidentified. BDBV-specific diagnostics, therapeutic and post-exposure prophylaxis trials, and vaccine studies expanded, yet no vaccine or virus-specific treatment had demonstrated clinical efficacy. Cross-reactive antibody responses after licensed Ebola vaccination do not establish protection against BDBV. ECDC assessed infection likelihood for EU/EEA residents as very low.

IMPLICATIONS: Epidemic control requires complete contact tracing complemented by active case-finding, earlier referral, high-quality supportive care, health-worker protection, community engagement, flexible financing and preservation of essential health services.

articles.title: Training the Next Generation: How Are We Preparing Pediatric Residents in Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health Care?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatricians are expected to provide sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care to adolescents assigned female at birth (AFAB), yet there is variability in the degree of clinical training pediatric residents receive. This study assesses training opportunities and comfort level of pediatric residents providing SRH care to AFAB adolescents.

METHODS: Third-year pediatric residents and their program directors completed a survey assessing resident training and comfort with SRH clinical skills, and perceived importance of topics. Descriptive statistics summarized participant demographics, and χ² or Fisher exact tests assessed associations between experiences and training settings.

RESULTS: Among 111 pediatric residents at 11 residency programs, 99.1% felt it was important to obtain training in SRH. The majority (65.8%) planned to provide SRH services in future practice. Common barriers to addressing SRH needs included insufficient training and lack of comfort of pediatric attendings. All program directors felt it was important to expand opportunities in SRH clinical skills. Conclusions Pediatric residents find value in providing SRH care and most plan to do so after graduation yet may not receive sufficient training. Multiple barriers interfere with provision of SRH care. Standardization of curricula and clinical experiences may increase resident comfort and improve quality of care provided to AFAB youth.

articles.title: Correlates of Consultant Disposition Recommendations in the California Child and Adolescent Mental Health Access Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The California Mental Health Access Program (Cal-MAP), a statewide child psychiatry access program, offers remote telephonic psychiatric consultation to pediatric primary care providers (PPCPs) statewide. This study investigated patient, provider, and practice-level factors associated with Cal-MAP disposition recommendations following telephonic psychiatric consultation.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included unique patient consultations conducted from March 2022-June 2023 (N=1,295). Descriptive statistics and logistic regression assessed differences in post-consult recommendations (i.e., remain in PPCP care for mental and behavioral health [MBH] needs or referral to specialty care) based on the PPCP's consultation question, patient clinical and sociodemographic characteristics, psychiatric complexity, current MBH supports, PPCP type, and practice setting.

RESULTS: Most consults involved Non-Hispanic White youth (N = 494, 47.6%), females (N = 652, 50.4%), adolescents aged 12-17 (N = 724, 55.9%), and those without psychiatric complexity (N = 769, 59.4%). Continued PPCP care was recommended for most consults (N = 959, 74%). Compared with consultations without psychiatric complexity, those with complexity (one indicator: adjusted OR [aOR], 0.32; 95% CI, 0.23-0.44; ≥2 complexity indicators: aOR, 0.18; 95% CI, 0.12-0.27) had lower odds of recommendations for continued PPCP management. Consultations involving households with a primary language other than English had lower odds than those involving English-speaking households (aOR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.35-0.93).

CONCLUSIONS: Telephonic psychiatric consultation through Cal-MAP supports MBH management by PPCPs, with the majority of consults recommended for continued primary care management. Consults involving psychiatric complexity and household languages other than English were associated with specialty referral recommendations.

articles.title: SLC15A3 contributes to diabetic encephalopathy through enhancing mitochondrial lipoperoxidation-mediated microglial activation.
articles.abstract: Diabetic encephalopathy (DE) is a common central nervous system complication of diabetes, characterized by cognitive decline and neuroinflammation. Mitochondrial dysfunction is closely implicated in DE pathogenesis, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, by intersecting published diabetes-associated microglial genes with mitophagy-related genes, we identified SLC15A3, which was highly expressed in microglia. SLC15A3 overexpression induced microglial activation, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation, manifested by increased IBA-1 expression, enhanced migration, elevated ROS and MDA levels, and upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines. Conversely, SLC15A3 knockdown effectively reversed high glucose (HG)-induced microglial oxidative stress and inflammatory activation. Mechanistically, Nucleotide-binding Oligomerization Domain-containing protein 2 (NOD2) was identified as a candidate interacting protein of SLC15A3. SLC15A3 upregulated NOD2 expression to activate the downstream JNK/DRP1 signaling axis, thereby aggravating mitochondrial lipid peroxidation, reducing mitochondrial membrane potential, and triggering aberrant PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy dysregulation. Notably, JNK knockdown significantly rescued SLC15A3-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. Importantly, this SLC15A3-NOD2 regulatory axis was further validated in primary murine microglia. In a microglia-endothelial co-culture blood-brain barrier (BBB) model, SLC15A3 silencing alleviated HG-evoked BBB permeability damage and restored the expression of tight junction proteins. In vivo hippocampal knockdown of SLC15A3 or NOD2 mitigated BBB disruption, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and partially attenuated cognitive deficits in DE mice. Collectively, this study demonstrates that SLC15A3 facilitated mitochondrial lipid peroxidation and mitophagy dysregulation via a NOD2-dependent JNK/DRP1 pathway, thereby accelerating BBB injury and DE progression. SLC15A3 represents a potential therapeutic target for diabetic cognitive complications.

articles.title: Failure to Rescue After Coronary Bypass Surgery: 1,613,669 Patients from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Failure to rescue (FTR), death after a postoperative complication, is an emerging quality metric because hospital mortality differences reflect complication management more than complication occurrence. Contemporary benchmarks for isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) are lacking. We hypothesized that FTR varies between hospitals independently of patient risk.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,613,669 isolated CABG operations at 1,165 hospitals in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) Adult Cardiac Surgery Database (2014-2024). FTR was death during the index hospitalization or within 30 days after stroke, renal failure, prolonged ventilation, or reoperation for bleeding. The primary analysis was multivariable logistic regression among complicated patients, adjusted for a priori covariates from the 2023 STS risk model, with hospitals grouped into observed-to-expected (O/E) mortality tertiles.

RESULTS: Of 1,613,669 patients, 147,852 (9.2%) had at least one major complication; 23,025 died, yielding a national FTR rate of 15.6%. Across O/E tertiles, FTR rose from 11.9% to 20.0% (1.68-fold) while complication frequency rose from 8.0% to 11.0% (1.38-fold). Predictors included emergent status (odds ratio 4.57, 95% CI 3.88-5.37); highest-tertile hospitals had greater FTR odds (2.33, 2.10-2.58). FTR rose from 12.5% (2014) to 17.3% (2020-2021) and was 16.1% (2024) (odds ratio per year 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.03; p<0.001), while mean predicted mortality fell from 1.92% to 1.72%.

CONCLUSIONS: FTR remains a substantial contributor to operative mortality after isolated CABG, with wide inter-hospital variation driven by institutional rescue capacity. Reducing mortality may require investment in early recognition systems, protocolized escalation pathways, and dedicated cardiovascular ICU infrastructure.

articles.title: One-Year Survival After Hybrid Stage 1 Single Ventricle Palliation - The Impact of Institutional Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hybrid stage 1 palliation (HS1P), an alternative to the Norwood procedure for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS), is often reserved for high-risk patients. We aimed to evaluate the survival of HS1P through one year when used as standard palliation strategy for HLHS and similar lesions and to assess changes in survival over time.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all infants who underwent HS1P for single ventricle palliation. A structured protocol for patient management was developed between 2009 and 2017, with all components implemented by June 2017. Patients were stratified into two cohorts based on timing of HS1P: Era 1 (January 2002 - May 2017), and Era 2 (June 2017 - December 2024). The primary outcome was survival through one year.

RESULTS: A total of 281 infants underwent HS1P, 221 in Era 1 and 60 in Era 2. Median age at HS1P was 6 days for both groups. Balloon atrial septostomy at the time of HS1P was significantly more common in Era 2 (43% vs 4% in Era 1), as was use of smaller bands (p <0.001 for both). One-year survival was significantly higher in Era 2 compared to Era 1 (83% vs 65%, p=0.01), and this benefit persisted in multivariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study of HS1P used as standard palliation, contemporary survival was excellent with significant improvements in outcomes in more recent years. Further study is needed to understand longer-term outcomes and the interplay of patient risk factors, to help guide best practices.

articles.title: Spheroids in virology: Bridging the gap between conventional 2D cultures and in vivo models.
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional cell cultures have long served as a standard tool in virological research, enabling the study of viral replication, cytopathic effects, antiviral activity, and host-pathogen interactions under controlled conditions. However, conventional monolayers often fail to reproduce the structural complexity, cellular polarity, extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, and diffusion gradients characteristic of native tissues. This compromises their physiological relevance and predictive value, especially for viruses that depend on tissue microenvironments for replication and pathogenesis. Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture systems, including spheroids, provide an intermediate platform between simplified 2D cultures and animal models, as they better recapitulate cell-cell interactions, spatial organization, nutrient and oxygen gradients, and tissue-like responses to infection. This review examines spheroid formation techniques used in virological studies, considers the influence of spheroid architecture on viral dissemination and replication, and looks at spheroid models used in clinically relevant viruses, including influenza viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, rhinoviruses, coronaviruses, bocavirus, hepatitis viruses, and herpesviruses. The evidence reviewed suggests that spheroid systems can enhance viral propagation, model host responses, support antiviral drug screening, and offer new insights into viral pathogenesis. Spheroids represent an accessible and promising platform to advance experimental virology and close the gap between in vitro and in vivo models despite technical challenges in standardization, scalability, analysis of infection dynamics, and incomplete reproduction of tissue complexity.

articles.title: Dynamics of antiviral resistance in an HIV patient with recurrent genital HSV2 infection.
Optimization of Lentiviral Transduction in NK92 Cells: A Comparative Study of Pseudotyped Vectors and Transduction Enhancers.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor-engineered natural killer (CAR-NK) cell therapy has demonstrated favorable safety profiles and considerable potential for "off-the-shelf" applications in cancer immunotherapy. However, because NK cells possess intrinsic antiviral properties, lentiviral vector (LV)-mediated gene delivery into NK cells remains substantially less efficient than in T cells, motivating efforts to optimize transduction conditions. In this study, we performed a preliminary, systematic comparison of the transduction efficiencies of three pseudotyped LVs-vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein (VSV-G), baboon endogenous retrovirus (BaEV), and feline endogenous retrovirus (RD114) envelope glycoprotein-in NK92 cells under various infection durations and multiplicity of infection (MOI) conditions. We further evaluated the differential effects of five transduction enhancers (TEs)-polybrene, dextran, protamine sulfate (PS), PAP248-286, and poloxamer F108-on the transduction efficiency of these three pseudotyped LVs. At 24h, BaEV-LV showed the highest mean transduction efficiency among the three pseudotyped LVs in NK92 cells, whereas RD114-LV showed the lowest. Polybrene enhanced BaEV-LV transduction by approximately 3.6-fold at 1μg/mL (from 10.40% to 37.07%), with comparable enhancement observed across the tested range of 1-10μg/mL. PAP248-286 increased RD114-LV transduction from 0.35% to 16.73% at 100μg/mL, the highest concentration tested. These results provide a preliminary experimental basis for optimizing lentiviral transduction conditions in NK92 cells; further validation using CAR constructs and primary NK cells will be required to assess the applicability of these findings to CAR-NK cell generation.

articles.title: Examining the intersection of extreme heat exposures, social determinants of health, and adverse pregnancy outcomes: a scoping review.
authors: P3 EQUATE Network Social Determinants of Health Core Group
articles.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Extreme heat exposure during pregnancy is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs), complications themselves linked to long-term maternal cardiovascular risk, and these effects appear to vary by social and environmental context (e.g., neighborhood deprivation, greenness, and rural-urban residence). We describe the U.S. evidence and characterize how social determinants of health (SDoH), particularly area-level measures, are defined in this literature.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched through July 14, 2025, plus secondary searches in September 2025.

STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included U.S.-focused empirical epidemiologic studies and evidence syntheses that (1) assessed extreme heat exposure in pregnancy; (2) incorporated at least one individual- or area-level SDoH as exposure, covariate, or effect modifier; and (3) reported at least one APO, from preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and gestational diabetes to composite APOs, severe maternal morbidity, and acute cardiovascular events.

STUDY APPRAISAL AND SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two reviewers independently screened records; a senior reviewer resolved conflicts. Data were extracted into standardized forms and synthesized narratively. Per scoping review guidance, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not performed.

RESULTS: We included 37 studies (28 empirical and 9 reviews). Heat exposure was typically defined using percentile-based thresholds (most commonly the 90th or 95th local percentile), heat-wave definitions, apparent-temperature metrics, or absolute cutoffs, with the week before delivery the most frequent window. Preterm birth was the most evaluated outcome, followed by birthweight-related outcomes and stillbirth. Individual-level socioeconomic measures (e.g., education, insurance) appeared in nearly all empirical studies, whereas area-level measures-neighborhood income or poverty, deprivation indices, greenness or tree canopy, heat-trapping land cover, region, and rural-urban residence-appeared in fewer than half. Five of 12 studies incorporating area-level SDoH reported stronger heat-APO associations in disadvantaged or lower-greenness settings. Examples include heat-associated stillbirth risk only in the most deprived neighborhoods; heat-preterm birth associations strongest where both greenness and socioeconomic status were low; and stronger heat-gestational diabetes associations with lower greenness.

CONCLUSIONS: U.S. studies reported associations between extreme heat in pregnancy and multiple APOs. Area-level SDoH and environmental context were inconsistently incorporated. Standardized use of place-based measures may better identify communities most vulnerable to heat and inform equity-focused, climate-resilient maternal health research and action.

TWEETABLE STATEMENT: Heat exposure in pregnancy is linked to adverse outcomes, and risk may be higher in neighborhoods experiencing socioeconomic deprivation, highlighting the need to measure area-level social determinants in climate-maternal health research.

articles.title: Dalbavancin as sequential therapy for complex osteoarticular infections: a single-center case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dalbavancin offers an alternative to prolonged inpatient antimicrobial treatment when oral therapy or conventional outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) is unsuitable. We describe its use in a selected cohort with complex, predominantly implant-associated osteoarticular infections.

METHODS: We retrospectively included all consecutive patients treated with dalbavancin for osteoarticular infections at a Danish tertiary hospital between October 2023 and November 2024. Data was collected through structured record review. The primary outcome was treatment failure within 12 months. Secondary outcomes included new infections, adverse events, treatment completion and estimated inpatient bed-days avoided.

RESULTS: Twenty patients (median age 62 years, 60% male) were included, 15 (75%) with implant-associated infections. Dalbavancin was mainly selected when linezolid or vancomycin-based OPAT was unsuitable. Eighteen (90%) completed the prescribed course; one index-infection relapse and two microbiologically distinct new infections were recorded. Four patients died from reportedly unrelated causes. No serious adverse events were reported. The estimated median number of inpatient bed-days avoided was 42 (IQR 28-72), based on a hypothetical inpatient alternative.

CONCLUSION: In this small case series, dalbavancin was well tolerated and treatment failure was uncommon among patients with complex osteoarticular infections for whom conventional oral or intravenous treatment was not feasible.

articles.title: Lung-to-heart delivery: Inhalable nanomedicine for cardiovascular disease treatment.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Although current pharmacological treatments have improved clinical outcomes, most primarily alleviate symptoms or modulate downstream pathways and have limited capacity to correct the underlying disease processes. Peptide- and nucleic acid-based therapeutics offer greater molecular specificity, but their clinical use is hampered by poor stability, low bioavailability, inefficient cardiac delivery, and off-target exposure after systemic administration. Pulmonary delivery provides a non-invasive alternative that bypasses hepatic first-pass metabolism, enables rapid absorption, and may reduce systemic adverse effects. However, effective Lung-to-Heart delivery requires careful control of aerosolization, aerodynamic deposition, pulmonary retention, biological barrier transport, and myocardial accumulation. These considerations have stimulated growing interest in inhalable nanoparticle-based cardiovascular therapeutics, yet the relevant design principles and translational evidence remain scattered. In this review, we summarize the physicochemical properties, biomaterials, formulation methods, and inhaler technologies that govern the pulmonary deposition and biological fate of inhalable nanoparticles. We discuss their interactions with airway mucus, mucociliary clearance, pulmonary immune surveillance, and the alveolar-capillary barrier, as well as strategies for enhancing myocardial targeting. We further review emerging applications in heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and cardiomyopathy, with particular emphasis on the delivery of peptides, nucleic acids, and other precision therapeutics. Finally, we examine key challenges in pulmonary safety, pharmacokinetics, manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, and regulatory evaluation. This review connects pulmonary drug delivery with cardiovascular nanomedicines and provides a practical basis for developing non-invasive, rapid-acting, and myocardium-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Elevated plasma S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) levels increase the risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Since lipophagy maintains cholesterol homeostasis through hydrolysis of cholesterol esters to support efflux, its impairment reduces cholesterol efflux. We aimed to explore the association of elevated SAH with macrophage foam-cell cholesterol handling and the potential mechanisms involving autophagy-related lipid processing and cholesterol efflux.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We explored the associations between plasma SAH levels and cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) in the Guangdong Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) Cohort. Adenosine dialdehyde (AdOx) was used to increase intracellular SAH levels in THP-1 macrophage foam cells, followed by evaluation of cholesterol efflux and autophagy-related lipid handling. We investigated the molecular mechanisms by examining regulators, including ABCA1, vacuolar-type H+-ATPase (V-ATPase) subunits, and transcription factor EB (TFEB). Torin 1 was used to assess changes in TFEB-related signaling and cholesterol efflux.

KEY FINDINGS: We found that plasma SAH levels were inversely associated with CEC in CAD patients. In vitro, AdOx treatment increased intracellular SAH and reduced ABCA1 expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. AdOx treatment was accompanied by reduced TFEB nuclear translocation, lower ATP6V1H and lysosomal acid lipase (LAL) expression, altered LC3/p62 levels, and increased lysosomal cholesterol. Torin 1 partially restored TFEB-related gene expression and ApoA-I-dependent cholesterol efflux. These findings support the involvement of TFEB-V-ATPase-related lysosomal signaling in AdOx-associated changes in macrophage cholesterol handling.

SIGNIFICANCE: Elevated S-adenosylhomocysteine is associated with impaired macrophage cholesterol efflux involving alterations in TFEB-V-ATPase lysosomal signaling, identifying SAH metabolism and TFEB-V-ATPase signaling as potential targets for further investigation.

articles.title: Gestational Zika virus infection causes oxidative distress in both mouse and human placentae.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection causes Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS) and has a greater tropism for the placenta. Placental oxidative distress is largely related to pregnancy complications. However, there is no information about how placental oxidative distress contributes to the development of CZS. Here, we hypothesized that ZIKV causes placental oxidative distress.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: C57BL/6 pregnant dams were infected at gestational day (GD)12.5. Placentae and fetuses were harvested and separated by sex at GD18.5. Human placentae from ZIKV-pregnant women were also analyzed. Immunohistochemistry, 2D OxyBlot, transmission electron microscopy, qPCR, reduced thiol content, and antioxidant enzymes activities were performed.

KEY FINDINGS: ZIKV reduced placental weight in both sexes. However, we detected increased placental efficiencies associated with normal fetal weight at term. Interestingly, we found that ZIKV increased the brain weight of female fetuses. ZIKV increased protein carbonyls and nitrotyrosine residues in the female and male placentae. Mitochondria degeneration and dilated rough endoplasmic reticulum cisternae were found in ZIKV-infected placentae of both sexes. Oxidant (Nox1 and Cybb) and antioxidant (Sod2, Sod3, Gpx1, and Gpx3) genes were upregulated in the female placentae, while only Gpx3 was upregulated by ZIKV in the male placentae. Reduced thiol levels, SOD, GPx, and CAT activities were not changed in both placental sexes. In the human placentae, ZIKV increased nitrotyrosine residues and did not change NOX expression.

SIGNIFICANCE: Gestational ZIKV infection causes oxidative distress in both mouse and human placentae. This alteration can be related to placental growth restriction and likely contribute to the development of CZS.

articles.title: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in amniotic fluid-derived cells.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Foetal sex is increasingly recognized as a critical biological variable influencing immune development and susceptibility to intrauterine stressors, including infection. However, the mechanisms by which foetal sex modulates innate immune responses at the maternal-foetal interface remain poorly understood.

METHODS: We investigated sex-dependent innate immune responses in human amniotic fluid-derived cells (AFCs) using an in vitro model of infection with two pre-term birth-related pathogens, Streptococcus agalactiae (GBS) and Escherichia coli. We evaluated gene and protein expression of key pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α), Toll-like receptors (TLR2 and TLR4), and selected microRNAs (miRNAs), involved both in pro-inflammatory signalling pathways and negative regulators of inflammation.

KEY FINDINGS: GBS infection induced a selective inflammatory response characterized by increased TNF-α production and TLR2 protein expression, with stronger responses observed in male AFCs. In contrast, female AFCs exhibited enhanced expression of regulatory miRNAs, including miR-29 family members, associated with reduced TNF-α levels. E. coli infection had a limited functional impact on the inflammatory parameters in our experimental conditions. Although it induced transcriptional activation of inflammatory genes, no significant changes were observed at the protein level. In female cells, E. coli infection was associated with increased expression of miR-146a-5p and miR-19a-3p, along with a reduction in miR-18a-5p.

SIGNIFICANCE: Foetal sex is a key determinant of pathogen-specific innate immune responses in AFCs. This sex-dependent immune modulation may contribute to differential susceptibility to inflammation-driven pregnancy complications and highlights the importance of incorporating foetal sex as a biological variable in studies of intrauterine infection.

articles.title: Serum aldosterone concentrations in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels across ACVIM stages of myxomatous mitral valve disease and their associations with echocardiographic indices.
articles.abstract: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is common in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels (CKCS) and may involve activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS). This study evaluated serum aldosterone concentrations across ACVIM MMVD stages in CKCS and its association with selected echocardiographic indices. Eighty-four client-owned CKCS were staged according to ACVIM guidelines (A, n = 11; B1, n = 58; B2, n = 7; C, n = 8), and serum aldosterone was measured using the LIAISON® Aldosterone chemiluminescent immunoassay on the DiaSorin LIAISON® XL automated analyzer. In the comparison of serum aldosterone concentrations between the combined ACVIM groups A+B1 and B2+C, the group effect did not reach statistical significance in the multivariable analysis based on complete cases (p = 0.072). In the unadjusted comparison, dogs with ACVIM-defined left-sided cardiac remodeling and/or congestive heart failure (B2+C) had higher median serum aldosterone concentrations than dogs not fulfilling ACVIM criteria for stage B2 or C disease (A+B1) (707.0 [445.0-1150.0] vs. 469.5 [333.5-730.5] pmol/L; p = 0.045), with a moderate rank-biserial effect size (r_rb = 0.332; 95% CI: 0.025-0.612). No significant associations between serum aldosterone concentration and echocardiographic variables remained after false discovery rate (FDR) correction, either in the whole cohort or in the B2+C subgroup. These results suggest a possible difference in serum aldosterone concentrations between broader clinically defined MMVD groups. However, this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment, and associations with individual echocardiographic indices were not confirmed after correction for multiple testing. The results should therefore be considered preliminary and hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Cross-tissue transcriptome-wide association analyses prioritize the 17q21.31 locus in autism spectrum disorder.
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a complex genetic architecture, and the regulatory transcripts underlying common-variant associations with ASD risks remain incompletely resolved. We integrated ASD genome-wide association summary statistics with genetically predicted expression across 29 GTEx v8 tissues using Joint-Tissue Imputation (JTI) and FUSION, followed by summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), regional conditional/joint analysis, colocalization and comparison with external ASD molecular evidence. All-tissue false-discovery-rate correction identified 264 significant JTI gene-tissue associations representing 64 genes and 561 FUSION associations representing 128 genes, with an overlap of 40 genes between JTI and FUSION and 152 unique genes in the union set. Brain eQTL and mQTL SMR identified 22 and 21 significant probes, respectively, while analyses across 16 non-brain tissues identified 59 significant probe-tissue associations. TWAS signals converged at 17q21.31. Conditional/joint FUSION retained only the Brain Cerebellar Hemisphere MAPT-AS1 model among 353 significant associations in the primary regional analysis, with the same model retained in an extended-window sensitivity analysis. BrainMeta-ASD colocalization was completed for 23 probes; none met the prespecified criterion for strong colocalization, and MAPT showed the highest PP·H4 (0.5052). Among the 152 union genes, 82 were supported by at least one of the Huang, Matoba or Gandal studies and 15 by at least two; MAPT and XRN2 were the only genes supported by all three data sets. MAPT-AS1 was supported by Matoba et al. in H-MAGMA analysis and is classified as a Category 2 gene in SFARI Gene, while Walker et al. provided additional developmental-brain context through prenatal-brain TWAS. These findings prioritize 17q21.31 as an ASD-associated locus supported across multiple genetic and regulatory evidence layers.

articles.title: Impact of weight reduction therapies on fibrosis and adverse liver outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease: an evidence-based review.
articles.abstract: Attenuation of fibrosis progression represents an important therapeutic goal in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), given the association of advancing fibrosis with adverse clinical outcomes. Guidelines recommend weight reduction in patients with MASH; however, the effects of weight loss on histologic fibrosis, noninvasive liver stiffness measures, and major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) have not been previously well-characterized. While data overall suggest that multimodal weight loss is associated with fibrosis regression and reduced risk of MALO in MASH, the interpretation and generalizability of these findings are confounded by study and disease heterogeneity and restricted indications for certain weight-loss interventions. Furthermore, evidence for weight loss as an independent predictor of fibrosis regression and reduced MALO risk is limited. Accordingly, patients with MASH with fibrosis should be continually monitored for disease progression, adjusting management as needed. MASH-specific pharmacotherapies should be considered in adults with non-cirrhotic MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis (consistent with stage F2-F3), alongside diet and exercise.

articles.title: Culprit vessel TIMI 0-1 flow identifies a high-risk subgroup of NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease: a post-hoc analysis of the SLIM randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Occlusive myocardial infarction (OMI) is a specific, high-risk subgroup of non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. To estimate the impact of this clinical entity, this post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial uses decreased TIMI flow (0 or 1) and patent flow (TIMI 2-3 flow) as surrogates to characterize these patient groups and their outcomes in a cohort with NSTEMI and multivessel coronary artery disease.

METHODS: The SLIM trial randomized NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease to complete or culprit-only revascularization; we included 474 patients with available angiographic data in the current analysis. One-year Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: all-cause death, non-fatal MI, any revascularization, and stroke) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and the association between study groups and outcomes was evaluated in crude and adjusted Cox proportional-hazards models.

RESULTS: TIMI 0-1 patients were younger (62 vs. 67 years, p<0.001), predominantly male (84.9% vs. 69.3%, p<0.001), with higher baseline biomarker levels. Routine interpretation of admission ECGs failed to differentiate occlusion status (reported ST-deviation 32.1% vs. 33.2%, p = 0.835). In the TIMI 0-1 flow group, the circumflex artery was the culprit more often (45.3% vs. 27.7%, p < 0.001). Although unadjusted MACE at 1-year follow-up was comparable (p=0.061), adjusted models showed that decreased flow was associated with MACE at one year (MACE: aHR 2.09, p=0.026).

CONCLUSIONS: This post-hoc analysis of the SLIM trial shows that TIMI 0-1 flow during the index procedure is an indicator for a high-risk subgroup of NSTEMI patients with multivessel disease who face a higher risk of MACE at one year.

articles.title: Human heat shock 70 kDa protein 6 (HSPA6) binds the α-synuclein N-terminus and inhibits protein aggregation.
articles.abstract: The Hsp70 (heat shock 70 kDa) family constitutes a major component of the cellular protein quality control system and plays an essential role in maintaining proteostasis. Its importance is demonstrated by its presence across multiple cellular compartments, including the cytosol, nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, as well as in the diversity of its isoforms. Among the less extensive characterized cytosolic members is HSPA6. Characterizing this isoform may contribute to a better understanding of how Hsp70s regulate protein homeostasis under physiological and stress conditions. Our results show that human HSPA6 was successfully cloned, expressed, and purified in a folded state. Biophysical analysis indicated that HSPA6 is monomeric and exhibits efficient ATPase activity relative to other Hsp70 isoforms. This activity was further enhanced by DNAJ co-chaperones from Class B. In addition, HSPA6 protected the client proteins insulin and α-synuclein from aggregation, even under a reduced condition. The interaction between HSPA6 and the disease-associated protein α-synuclein was further characterized. HSPA6 was found to bind the N-terminus of α-synuclein with micromolar affinity, at a region not previously reported. Taken together, these findings indicated that HSPA6 can interact directly with α-synuclein and inhibit its aggregation, supporting a role for this relatively understudied Hsp70 isoform in the regulation of α-synuclein proteostasis.

articles.title: Cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1 aggravates sepsis-associated acute kidney injury by stabilizing acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 and promoting ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) involves ferroptotic tubular injury, but the upstream mechanisms controlling ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely defined. We investigated whether cytochrome P450 family 1 subfamily A member 1 (CYP1A1) promotes SA-AKI by regulating acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) protein stability. Global and kidney tubule-targeted Cyp1a1 knockout mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture (CLP). HK-2 cells and primary mouse renal tubular epithelial cells were used for complementary validation. Protein stability assays, ubiquitination analyses, interaction assays and AlphaFold 3-guided mutagenesis were used to define the mechanism. Renal-targeted siCYP1A1/Cy5.5@LNP-CLPVASC nanoparticles were evaluated for protective efficacy and tolerability. Renal CYP1A1 was upregulated after sepsis, and its deletion reduced renal dysfunction and tubular injury. Tubule-targeted deletion conferred protection without reducing renal bacterial burden. CYP1A1 deficiency attenuated lipid peroxidation and injury in HK-2 and primary cells, whereas ferrostatin-1 attenuated injury in LPS-stimulated, CYP1A1-overexpressing HK-2 cells. CYP1A1 loss accelerated ACSL4 degradation, while overexpression enhanced its stability. CYP1A1 interacted with ACSL4 through a D393-dependent interface and limited its ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Renal-targeted CYP1A1 silencing reduced ACSL4 abundance, lipid peroxidation and renal injury. Nanoparticle administration was well tolerated over 28 days based on histological, biochemical and hematological assessments, with no significant increase in renal inflammation at 48 h. These findings identify a CYP1A1-ACSL4 protein-stability axis that promotes ferroptotic tubular injury and support renal-targeted CYP1A1 silencing as a potential intervention for SA-AKI.

articles.title: A Decade of Testicular Torsion: Management and Recurrence in a Single State from 2013-2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the treatment practices and outcomes of testicular torsion across a state-wide U.S. healthcare system over an 11-year period, with a focus on surgical technique and recurrence rate.

METHODS: With IRB approval, male patients under 35 who underwent surgery for testicular torsion between 2013-2023 were retrospectively identified within a state-wide healthcare system. Clinical and demographic data were extracted from the electronic medical record. Descriptive statistics were analyzed using R version 4.3.1.

RESULTS: We identified 155 operative cases, including 97 cases of acute torsion and 58 cases of intermittent torsion (torsion rate ~29 per 100,000 males <35-years-old). Doppler ultrasound was utilized in all cases of acute torsion. Contralateral orchiopexy was performed in a majority of cases, including all cases where the torsed testis could not be salvaged - 25.8% in the acute torsion group. Fixation technique and suture choice varied, with three-point fixation used in the majority of acute torsion with a mix of two- and three-point fixation in intermittent torsion. Both absorbable and non-absorbable sutures were used. Two recurrences (1.3%) occurred, both following two-point fixation with non-absorbable suture that detached from the dartos layer.

CONCLUSIONS: This statewide analysis describes contemporary operative management of testicular torsion in the U.S. and demonstrates substantial variation in fixation technique and suture choice. Recurrence after orchiopexy was rare (1.3%). Both recurrences followed two-point fixation with nonabsorbable suture that had separated from the dartos, an exploratory observation that warrants evaluation in larger multi-institutional cohorts.

articles.title: A comparison of UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications DESIGN: National population-based study SETTING: All births in France over 1 week in 2021 POPULATION: 11,845 women with a live-born singleton, with data abstracted from medical records and maternal interviews MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Prevalence of low-risk women and discrepancies in low-risk exclusion criteria between UK and French guidelines RESULTS: The prevalence of women at low-risk was 64.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 63.3-65.0) and 71.2% (70.4-72.0) according to UK and French guidelines, respectively. Overall, 58.9% (58.0-59.8) of women were at low-risk according to both guidelines, 5.2% (4.8-5.6) according to UK guidelines only and 12.3% (11.7-12.9) for French guidelines only. Risk level is assessed at the beginning of pregnancy in French guidelines but at the end of pregnancy in UK guidelines. Uterine scar and insulin-treated gestational diabetes were the main low-risk exclusion criteria in UK but not French guidelines. A history of a small-for-gestational age (SGA) newborn or preterm birth and antenatal suspicion of SGA for the current pregnancy were the main low-risk exclusion criteria in French but not UK guidelines.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of pregnant women at low-risk of complications differed between UK and French guidelines because of discrepancies in the timing of risk assessment and low-risk exclusion criteria. This suggests the need for complementary guidelines including criteria derived from validation studies to orient low-risk women toward both the appropriate practitioner for prenatal follow-up and the suitable place of birth.

articles.title: Effects of Dapagliflozin on Inflammatory Biomarkers and Associations With Clinical Outcomes in CKD: Findings From the DAPA-CKD Trial.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Inflammation is a key driver of chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study evaluated the effects of dapagliflozin (DAPA) on inflammatory biomarkers and examined their associations with clinical outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 2,795 participants in the DAPA-CKD trial.

EXPOSURES: Dapagliflozin, 10 mg daily, versus placebo and baseline levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6, hs-CRP, and uric acid, as well as urinary uric acid, KIM-1, and MCP-1.

OUTCOMES: Four prespecified time-to-event outcomes: the primary outcome was a composite of ≥50% eGFR decline, kidney failure, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes. A kidney outcome was defined as the primary composite without cardiovascular death, and a cardiovascular outcome was defined as a composite of heart failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death. An additional secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. Biochemical outcomes were levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6, hs-CRP, and uric acid, as well as urinary uric acid, KIM-1, and MCP-1 one year after randomization.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Multivariable proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between biomarkers and outcomes, and analysis of covariance was used to assess treatment effects of dapagliflozin.

RESULTS: Higher baseline levels of plasma TNFR-1, TNFR-2, and KIM-1, serum IL-6 and hs-CRP, and urinary KIM-1/Cr and MCP-1/Cr were independently associated with increased risk of clinical outcomes. Participants randomized to dapagliflozin had significantly reduced levels of plasma KIM-1, serum uric acid, and urinary MCP-1/Cr and KIM-1/Cr compared with placebo after 1 year of treatment, while a significant increase in urinary uric acid/Cr was observed. Early increases in TNFR-1 and TNFR-2, and urinary uric acid/Cr, KIM-1/Cr, and MCP-1/Cr from baseline to year 1 were associated with a higher subsequent risk of the primary composite outcome (HRs per SD 1.59 [95% CI 1.37-1.86], 1.19 [95% CI 1.01-1.40], and 1.36 [95% CI 1.11-1.65], 1.27 [95% CI 1.06-1.51], and 1.42 [95% CI 1.13-1.79], respectively).

LIMITATIONS: Biomarkers were measured at only two time points, analyses were post hoc with potential residual confounding. Missing biomarker data in a substantial proportion of participants creates the potential for selection bias.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CKD, inflammatory biomarkers are strongly associated with clinical outcomes and may be modifiable with dapagliflozin. Early changes in these biomarkers are associated with subsequent outcomes, supporting their role in monitoring treatment response and disease progression.

articles.title: Effect Modification by Albuminuria on the Association Between Serum Biomarkers of Kidney Failure Risk and Major Kidney Events Among Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Albuminuric and normoalbuminuric diabetic kidney disease (DKD) may represent distinct pathological subtypes of kidney complications. This study assessed the modifying effect of albuminuria on the association between serum biomarkers and risk of major kidney events (MKE) in type 2 diabetes (T2D).

STUDY DESIGN: Nested case-control study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: Individuals with T2D from the ACCORD/ACCORDION trial were included. Cases (n=383) comprised participants with baseline serum who experienced an MKE within 7 years, defined as kidney failure (KF), serum creatinine >3.3 mg/dL, and/or 50% eGFR decline. Controls (n=554) were a 15% random sample with baseline serum, at least 7 years of follow-up, and no MKE.

EXPOSURE: Baseline serum concentrations of 21 serum proteins (Joslin Kidney Panel [JKP]).

OUTCOME: MKE within 7 years.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Associations between individual JKP proteins and MKE were examined using logistic regression, adjusted for age and sex, HbA1c, diabetes duration, baseline eGFR, baseline UACR, and hypertension status. We stratified the analyses by baseline albuminuria status (ACR ≥30 mg/g; normoalbuminuria: ACR <30 mg/g) to assess for effect modification.

RESULTS: At baseline, 309 subjects had albuminuria, whereas 628 were normoalbuminuric. Five JKP proteins (TNF-R3, TNF-R10B, ANGPT2, KIM1, and WFDC2) were associated (p<0.05) with increased MKE risk in both strata, but more strongly among albuminuric participants (p for interaction with albuminuria <0.05 for all proteins but KIM1). Eleven JKP proteins were associated with increased MKE risk only among albuminuric subjects, with TNF-R11A showing the strongest effect (OR=4.23, 95% CI 2.35-7.93). One protein (TNF-L12) was associated with significantly lower MKE risk after adjustment for risk proteins, uniquely among albuminuric subjects.

LIMITATIONS: Biomarkers and albuminuria were measured only at baseline.

CONCLUSIONS: Serum biomarkers of KF risk are more strongly associated with MKE in albuminuric than in normoalbuminuric T2D patients, suggesting that albuminuria status identifies biologically distinct pathways driving kidney disease progression.

articles.title: Middle Cardiac Vein Mapping with Multielectrode Catheters to Guide Ablation of Scar-Related Ventricular Tachycardia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The coronary venous system offers an alternative route for mapping and ablation of ventricular arrhythmias, especially in presence of epicardial or intramural substrate.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the feasibility, diagnostic yield and outcomes of middle cardiac vein (MCV) mapping using multielectrode catheters to guide ablation of scar-related ventricular tachycardia (VT).

METHODS: We included patients with structural heart disease and VT undergoing ablation in which MCV mapping was performed using multielectrode catheters. Left ventricular (LV) and/or right ventricular (RV) endocardial mapping was performed depending on the VT morphology, and the ablation strategy was selected based on endocardial and MCV activation in addition to pace mapping and/or entrainment.

RESULTS: Thirty-three patients (60.5±13.6 years, 73% nonischemic) were included. VT was inducible in 97% of patients, with a median of 4 VT morphologies per patient. MCV and endocardial mapping suggested an epicardial circuit in 21 patients and epicardial access was obtained in 13 of them (percutaneous approach in 11 and surgical window in 2). Additionally, mapping was consistent with an intramural circuit in 3 patients, which were treated with sequential RF ablation from LV and RV (n = 3) and ethanol ablation (n = 2). There were no complications related to MCV mapping. Over a median follow-up of 13 months, 8 patients (24%) had VT recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: MCV mapping with multielectrode catheters is safe and facilitates identification of epicardial or intramural VT circuits, guides the need for epicardial access and provides an opportunity for therapeutic interventions such as venous RF delivery or ethanol infusion.

articles.title: Continuous local antibiotic perfusion for chronic osteomyelitis after fetlock arthrodesis.
articles.abstract: A 3-year-old Thoroughbred racehorse developed refractory osteomyelitis and subcutaneous infection following fetlock arthrodesis for proximal sesamoid bone fractures. Conventional treatments, including implant removal and antibiotic therapy, failed to control the infection. Continuous local antibiotic perfusion (CLAP) was applied by infusing gentamicin (1.2 mg/mL) at 2 mL/h into the affected bone and subcutaneous tissue, combined with a negative pressure wound therapy system to ensure proper antibiotic flow into the infected tissues. CLAP for 2 weeks markedly improved lameness and pus discharge. At day 205 after CLAP treatment, no recurrence was observed, and the horse could trot under saddle. In this case, CLAP applied to a distal equine limb effectively controlled chronic refractory osteomyelitis, providing good long-term results, although some limitations and precautions are acknowledged.

articles.title: Stratified Diagnostic Thresholds by Infection Chronicity Resolve the Controversy in Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty Periprosthetic Joint Infection: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnosing periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is complicated by the "hybrid joint" environment and contradictory literature thresholds that overlook infection chronicity. We aimed to define chronicity-stratified thresholds for standard markers and evaluate the diagnostic utility of synovial neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) in this specific context.

METHODS: There were 77 revision UKA patients (20 acute PJI, 19 chronic, and 38 aseptic) prospectively enrolled. A PJI was defined by Musculoskeletal Infection Society (MSIS)/International Consensus Meeting (ICM) criteria and stratified by Tsukayama classification (less than four weeks: acute; greater than four weeks: chronic). Synovial fluid white blood cell (SF-WBC), polymorphonuclear neutrophil (%PMN), and NGAL were analyzed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves to determine optimal cutoffs.

RESULTS: Acute PJI exhibited high inflammatory baselines (SF-WBC greater than 10,020/μL, area under the curve [AUC] 0.976; PMN% greater than 81.0%), whereas chronic PJI required significantly lower cutoffs (SF-WBC less than 2,770/μL, AUC 0.958; PMN% greater than 62.0%). Synovial NGAL demonstrated robust stability (Acute: greater than 274 ng/mL, AUC 0.995; Chronic: greater than 174 ng/mL, AUC 0.992), notably achieving 100% sensitivity in chronic cases. High-virulence organisms predominated in acute cases (35.0% Staphylococcus aureus [S. aureus]), contrasting with low-virulence organisms in chronic infections (42.1% Coagulase-negative staphylococci [CoNS]).

CONCLUSIONS: In this preliminary single-center cohort, ROC-derived synovial fluid cutoff estimates differed between acute and chronic UKA-PJI. These findings suggest that infection chronicity may be relevant when interpreting synovial biomarkers in failed UKA. Synovial NGAL showed promising diagnostic performance in both subgroups; however, its optimal cutoff estimates also differed by chronicity. Larger multicenter studies with independent external validation are required before these exploratory thresholds can be recommended for routine clinical use.

articles.title: There is a Marked Temporal Variation in the Level of Serological Markers Used for Diagnosis of Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have estimated systematic changes in erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and c-reactive protein (CRP) based on host and pathogen-related factors. This study sought to determine if a temporal variation of ESR and CRP is sufficient to affect infection diagnoses prior to arthroplasty revision.

METHODS: This cohort consisted of 218 cases (129 ESR, 196 CRP) from 2001 to 2015 with at least two ESR and/or CRP measurements after primary arthroplasty and before their first revision surgery. Those who had measurements greater than 31 days before surgery, less than three months after previous surgery, or between two revision surgeries were excluded. The first ESR measurements were categorized as low (zero to 12.9 mm/hour), elevated (13 to 29.9 mm/hour), and high (≥ 30 mm/hour). The CRP was dichotomized as low (less than 1.0 mg/dL) or high (greater than 1.0 mg/dL). Thresholds were determined using diagnostic cutoffs from the 2018 Musculoskeletal Infection Society Definition of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI).

RESULTS: The average ESR and CRP measurements were 2.16 and 2.20, respectively. The ESR increased 5.9% per day when initially low. Remaining relatively constant when elevated or high, CRP decreased 4.9% per day when the starting CRP was high and remained relatively constant when low. Bartlett's test showed differences in variance for ESR and CRP across all groups. Variation was most pronounced when initial ESR was low.

CONCLUSION: Reliance on ESR and CRP for PJI diagnosis is substantial. There is temporal variation in serological markers for a given patient. Results of these laboratory tests can vary substantially, moving above or below the recognized thresholds, and can potentially interfere with the accuracy of these tests in the diagnosis of PJI.

articles.title: Complications and Failures following Extensor Mechanism Reconstruction in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Failure of the extensor mechanism following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is a devastating complication that compromises function and patient satisfaction. The incremental risk of concomitant extensor mechanism reconstruction (EMR) during revision TKA on wound complications, reoperation, and ultimate treatment failure, including arthrodesis or amputation, remains limited.

METHODS: Using a national claims database, we identified patients who underwent revision TKA with or without preoperative periprosthetic joint infection. Outcomes of patients who underwent revision TKA with or without EMR were compared using Chi-square analyses. Multivariate analyses identified independent predictors of 2-year fusion or amputation.

RESULTS: Patients who had EMR had an increased risk of wound dehiscence in both septic (odds ratio (OR) 2.27, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.11 to 5.00) and aseptic (OR 5.00, 95% CI 3.33 to 10.00) revision TKA. The odds of subsequent debridement, skin grafting, and amputation or fusion were similar in septic revision TKA regardless of EMR status; however, in aseptic revision TKA, EMR was associated with increased odds of subsequent debridement (OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.67 to 3.33), skin grafting (OR 3.45, 95% CI 1.67 to 10.00), flap procedure (OR 4.55, 95% CI 2.00 to 10.00), and amputation (OR 4.17, 95% CI 1.11 to 10.00). Multivariate analysis of all revision TKAs demonstrated that the risk of amputation was associated with debridement (Likelihood ratio (LR) 5.97, P < 0.0001) and EMR (LR 3.24, P = 0.0008). In revision TKA with EMR, amputation was associated with flap use (LR 29.79, P = 0.18) and debridement (LR 4.52, P = 0.11).

DISCUSSION: In this large database study, EMR in aseptic revision TKA patients was independently associated with increased risk of amputation, likely due to the higher burden of soft-tissue procedures. In septic revision TKA, amputation risk was higher than aseptic revision TKA regardless of EMR.

articles.title: Histone remodeling in immune cells and its metabolic regulation and implications for metabolic disease.
articles.abstract: Immune cells continuously adapt to local tissue environments, and this functional plasticity plays a critical role in tissue homeostasis and metabolic disease. Emerging evidence indicates that histone post-translational modifications (HPTMs) contribute to immune cell adaptation by linking metabolic and environmental signals to transcriptional regulation. Beyond canonical histone acetylation and methylation, recently characterized modifications, including lactylation, crotonylation, and β-hydroxybutyrylation, have expanded our understanding of metabolism-dependent chromatin regulation. Advances in epigenomic technologies have further accelerated the characterization of these dynamic regulatory mechanisms. In this review, we summarize the molecular mechanisms through which metabolic pathways and metabolites regulate HPTMs and shape immune cell function. We further highlight emerging evidence of histone remodeling in immune cells during systemic metabolic dysfunction and within adipose and hepatic microenvironments, with particular emphasis on obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Finally, we address current knowledge gaps and future directions for understanding metabolic-epigenetic interactions within tissue niches. Collectively, this review provides an integrated perspective on how metabolism-driven histone remodeling shapes immune cell plasticity and contributes to metabolic disease, providing insights into potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Human cytomegalovirus infection impairs axon formation by inducing inhibitory GSK-3β Ser9 phosphorylation and suppressing ATP synthesis.
articles.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a globally prevalent pathogen known to significantly impact neural development in embryos and young children. Despite its well-established association with neurological disorders, the precise mechanisms through which HCMV infection induces these diseases remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we show that HCMV infection impairs neural cell differentiation by perturbing adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production during the neurogenesis. HCMV infection disrupts the neural differentiation of stem cells derived from human exfoliated deciduous teeth (SHEDs) and the human neuroblastoma cell line (SH-SY5Ys), alternating the expression of neural cell markers and impairing axon formation. Moreover, under neurogenic inductive conditions, HCMV infection in SHEDs and SH-SY5Ys increases Ser9 phosphorylation levels of GSK-3β, which suppresses GSK-3β kinase activity. This inhibition of GSK-3β activity reduces mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis, disrupting energy support for neural differentiation. This study reveals a molecular cascade connecting HCMV infection to defective neural differentiation through crosstalk between GSK-3β phosphorylation and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, offering a potential therapeutic target for congenital HCMV infection.

articles.title: The Portuguese National Registry of Cardiac Imaging (RNPIC): Initial results from a nationwide multicenter survey.
articles.journal: Revista portuguesa de cardiologia : orgao oficial da Sociedade Portuguesa de Cardiologia = Portuguese journal of cardiology : an official journal of the Portuguese Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Advanced cardiac imaging techniques, including cardiac computed tomography (CCT), cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), and nuclear cardiology, are increasingly central to cardiovascular care. This study describes the initial results of the Portuguese National Registry of Cardiac Imaging (RNPIC), focusing on center-level availability, patient profile, access, and clinical utilization.

METHODS: Between March and April 2023, all Portuguese centers performing CMR, CCT, or nuclear cardiology were invited to register prospectively all referred patients who provided informed consent over 30 consecutive days. Data on demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, clinical history, imaging modality, and delay between referral and scan were collected. Centers were also characterized in terms of institutional setting and available imaging techniques.

RESULTS: A total of 44 centers and 3315 exams were included (patient age: 62.3±12.6 years; 40.3% female). CCT was the most frequently used modality (52%), followed by CMR (33%) and nuclear cardiology (15%). Compared to CCT and CMR, patients undergoing nuclear cardiology were older and had a higher burden of cardiovascular risk factors and prior events. Among examinations with valid referral and examination dates, median time between referral and scan was shortest for CCT (26 days [IQR 9-57]), followed by CMR (31 days [IQR 11-79]) and nuclear cardiology (35 days [IQR 17-65]). Delays were consistently longer in public than in private institutions across all modalities, with an overall median waiting time of 53 versus 22 days, respectively (p<0.000001). A significant proportion of referrals to both functional or anatomical tests was related to screening for obstructive coronary artery disease in asymptomatic patients, accounting for 8.6%, 11.7%, and 32.2% of CCT, CMR, and nuclear cardiology cases, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: This first nationwide registry provides a comprehensive overview of cardiac imaging practice in Portugal. Important differences in patient profile, technique utilization, and access times were identified across imaging modalities and healthcare sectors. A relevant proportion of imaging studies were performed in asymptomatic individuals without clearly documented guideline-based indications in the registry, highlighting the need for improved referral pathways, educational efforts, and future appropriateness-focused studies.

articles.title: Bacterial Hsp90 and its interacting partners.
articles.abstract: Protein quality control depends on molecular chaperones to promote protein folding, remodeling, disaggregation, and degradation. The major families of chaperones present in nearly all organisms are Hsp90, Hsp70, Hsp60, and Clp/Hsp100. Here, we review Hsp90 chaperones with particular emphasis on bacterial Hsp90s. Unlike eukaryotic Hsp90, the bacterial Hsp90 is independent of Hsp90 cochaperones and thus provides a simpler and more accessible system to study the mechanism of action of Hsp90. Despite this simplicity, bacterial Hsp90s are highly homologous to eukaryotic family members and exhibit sensitivity to the same small-molecule inhibitors as eukaryotic Hsp90. Thus, insights gained from the bacterial systems have significantly advanced our understanding of the more complex mechanism of remodeling utilized by Hsp90 in higher organisms. A deeper mechanistic understanding of Hsp90 function, including its interactions with substrates (also known as clients), cochaperones, and other chaperones, will be useful for the development of therapeutic strategies for cancer and other diseases in which Hsp90 and associated cochaperones and other molecular chaperones play critical roles.

articles.title: Prevalence, progression and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears in patients treated for unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears: A scoping review.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotator cuff tears are common in people with shoulder pain and disability. Although management typically targets the symptomatic shoulder, people with unilateral non-traumatic rotator cuff tears may be at increased risk of contralateral pathology. However, the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral tears remain poorly understood.

PURPOSE: To identify and synthesise published evidence on the prevalence, progression, and factors associated with contralateral rotator cuff tears to inform future surveillance, prevention, and management strategies.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute framework and reported following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. MEDLINE, AMED, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were searched from inception to 20 January 2026. Studies involving adults with unilateral symptomatic non-traumatic rotator cuff tears were included. Data were summarised descriptively.

RESULTS: Fourteen heterogeneous reports from 12 studies (2001-2024) were included; 54% were based on surgical populations. Prevalence of contralateral rotator cuff tears ranged from 8.7% to 67.3%. Contralateral tear enlargement was reported in 39% to 67% of shoulders during follow- up to 13.1 years, while 26% to 57% of patients developed contralateral shoulder pain. Median time to tear enlargement ranged from 2.8 to 3.4 years; time to symptom onset ranged from 15.2 months to 3.0 years. Limited data suggests larger baseline contralateral tear size was associated with subsequent pain development (p≤0.001). Tear enlargement during follow-up was not consistently associated with symptom development. Factors associated with the presence of contralateral rotator cuff tears at baseline included older age (OR 1.1, 95% CI 1.05-1.18), increased BMI (26.1 vs 24.7 kg/m2, p<0.05), diabetes (23.1% vs 8.1%, p<0.03), and heavy repetitive work (31.8% vs 14.4%, p<0.05). Factors associated with progression included full-thickness contralateral tears (HR 2.93, 95% CI 1.71-5.03), dominant-side involvement of the contralateral shoulder (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.2-2.4), and fatty muscle degeneration within the contralateral shoulder (OR 2.6, 95% CI 1.3-5.4).

CONCLUSION: Contralateral rotator cuff tears are common and frequently progressive in patients with unilateral symptomatic tears, signalling a possible bilateral and multifactorial disease model rather than an isolated shoulder disorder. Research is needed to develop and evaluate clinically and cost-effective assessment and management strategies that extend beyond the affected shoulder and include optimisation of modifiable risk factors and consideration of bilateral rehabilitation approaches.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV; Scoping Review.

articles.title: Proceedings from the 2025 International Consensus Meeting on Orthopedic Infections: Management of Periprosthetic Shoulder Infection.
articles.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) following shoulder arthroplasty remains challenging to manage because treatment strategies vary according to infection chronicity, organism, implant characteristics, and patient factors, while high-quality shoulder-specific evidence remains limited. The purpose of this International Consensus Meeting (ICM) was to review the available evidence and develop consensus recommendations regarding the management of PJI following shoulder arthroplasty.

METHODS: The Shoulder Group of the 2025 ICM on Orthopedic Infections included international shoulder surgeons, infectious disease physicians, and microbiology experts with clinical and/or research experience in shoulder arthroplasty and PJI. Twenty-nine management questions underwent question-specific literature review, presentation, discussion, and voting using a modified Delphi process. Consensus was categorized according to percentage agreement, while strength of recommendation was assessed separately based on the quality, consistency, and directness of available evidence.

RESULTS: Thirteen questions resulted in recommendations for clinical practice and 16 identified a need for further research. All achieved supermajority consensus, with agreement ranging from 92% to 100%. Clinically, both intravenous and oral postoperative antimicrobial strategies were supported, with treatment individualized according to infection characteristics and infectious disease consultation. Gentamicin alone was considered insufficient for Cutibacterium acnes coverage in antibiotic-loaded cement, and intraoperative antibiotic redosing was supported based on operative duration. Both custom and off-the-shelf antibiotic spacers were considered reasonable, with functional metal-based spacers appropriate in selected patients. Safely extractable retained material should generally be removed without accepting substantial morbidity solely to achieve complete removal. Well-fixed glenoid components should generally be removed in subacute or chronic PJI, whereas routine exchange of well-fixed implants without evidence of infection was not supported. Modular components should be exchanged during debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) when feasible. Evidence remained insufficient to establish preferred antimicrobial routes or organism-specific regimens, indications or protocols for DAIR, timing of second-stage reimplantation, routine spacer exchange, or superiority of one- versus two-stage exchange.

CONCLUSIONS: The 2025 ICM provides an evidence-informed framework for management of shoulder PJI. Despite strong expert agreement across all 29 questions, substantial uncertainty remains because the supporting evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Prospective, multicenter, shoulder-specific comparative studies are needed to establish optimal management strategies.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level V, Consensus Statement, Voting.

articles.title: DBP K210 deacetylation suppresses BmNPV proliferation and promotes apoptosis associated with altered BmIAP regulation.
articles.abstract: The DNA-binding protein DBP, encoded by ORF16 of Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV), is a single-stranded DNA-binding protein expressed early during infection and is essential for efficient viral replication. Although DBP has been proposed to function as a transcriptional regulator, the mechanisms governing its activity remain poorly understood. In our previous study, a quantitative acetylproteomic analysis identified acetylation at lysine 210 (K210) of DBP during BmNPV infection, with its acetylation level increasing approximately 1.7-fold at 36 h post-infection. To investigate the functional significance of this modification, we generated a DBP deficient BmNPV mutant and BmNPV mutants carrying DBP substitutions designed to mimic acetylation or deacetylation at K210. No infectious virus production was detected following loss of DBP, whereas the K210 deacetylation-mimetic mutant showed markedly reduced progeny virus production, accompanied by reduced viral DNA replication and expression of the viral genes examined. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) analysis revealed that the K210 deacetylation-mimetic mutation altered the genomic binding profile of DBP and was associated with changes in host genes involved in apoptosis and cell-cycle regulation. Among them, the binding ability to the apoptosis inhibitor BmIAP decreased after the deacetylation simulation mutation. ChIP-qPCR confirmed DBP enrichment at the IAP promoter, while dual-luciferase assays demonstrated that K210 deacetylation reduced IAP promoter activity. Consistent with these findings, the DBP deacetylation-mimetic mutant increased caspase-3 activity and the expression of the pro-apoptotic genes examined while reducing that of an anti-apoptotic gene. Importantly, overexpression of BmIAP partially attenuated caspase-3 activity and the changes in apoptosis-related transcript levels associated with expression of the DBP deacetylation-mimetic mutant, supporting a contributory role for BmIAP in the observed apoptotic phenotype.
