Together, these findings support a regulatory role for DBP K210 acetylation in BmNPV replication and suggest that DBP K210 deacetylation is associated with enhanced apoptotic responses, at least partly through modulation of BmIAP expression, providing new insights into the molecular interplay between baculoviruses and their insect hosts.

articles.title: The Role of Diagnostic Tools in the Management of Ventilator Associated Lower Respiratory Tract Infections.
articles.journal: Seminars in respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a leading healthcare-associated infection in intensive care units and is closely associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, excessive antimicrobial exposure, higher costs, and poor clinical outcomes. Despite decades of clinical trials and guideline development, bedside diagnosis remains limited by the absence of a biological reference standard. Conventional criteria combine nonspecific clinical, radiographic, and microbiological findings and cannot reliably distinguish parenchymal infection from airway colonization, endotracheal tube biofilm, or sterile pulmonary inflammation. Syndromic multiplex polymerase chain reaction panels, metagenomic next-generation sequencing, and host response profiling have greatly increased analytical sensitivity and shortened the time to microbiological information. They have also exposed the amount of microbial and inflammatory noise present in the ventilated airway. Detection of an organism, a resistance determinant, or systemic inflammation does not by itself establish causality. This review examines the strengths and limitations of clinical scores, imaging, respiratory sampling, conventional culture, rapid molecular assays, antimicrobial resistance testing, systemic and alveolar biomarkers, host transcriptomics, breath analysis, and artificial intelligence-based models. It proposes that VAP should be approached as a time-updated probability of tissue invasive infection rather than a binary diagnosis. A practical host-pathogen attribution framework should integrate the timing and trajectory of respiratory deterioration, specimen quality, relative pathogen burden and dominance, resistance and virulence signals, local and systemic host responses, prior antimicrobial exposure, and competing diagnoses. Diagnostic tests should be ordered only when a predefined management decision is linked to the result, followed by structured reassessment at 48 to 72 hours. This approach may improve antimicrobial targeting while reducing treatment of colonization and other noninfectious mimics.

articles.title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis in Facial Plastics: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS AND BACKGROUND: Antibiotic prophylaxis in facial plastic surgery varies widely, with no review spanning the full breadth of procedures. The aim of the review is to determine its effect on surgical site infection (SSI) and to compare single-dose against extended-course regimens.

TECHNIQUES: PRISMA 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis registered with PROSPERO. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CDSR were searched. Odds ratios were pooled using random-effects models; bias and certainty of evidence was assessed with RoB 2/ROBINS-I and GRADE.

CONCLUSION AND CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Forty-one studies (243,454 patients) were included. Three key findings emerged: (1) A single perioperative dose significantly reduced SSI versus no antibiotic (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.25-0.86; any prophylaxis OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.33-0.93). (2) Extended-course regimens added no benefit over a single dose (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.63-1.34; I²=0%) (3) Effects did not differ significantly by procedure type. A single perioperative dose is supported as the stewardship-preferred default.

articles.title: Etomidate vs Propofol for Anesthetic Induction: Association With 30-Day Mortality and Postoperative Complications in a Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Etomidate is commonly used for induction in hemodynamically unstable patients to preserve cardiovascular stability. However, concerns persist regarding potential adverse outcomes, including adrenal suppression and increased mortality. We evaluated whether intravenous anesthetic induction with etomidate was independently associated with adverse postoperative outcomes as compared to propofol induction.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 155,667 adult surgical patients undergoing induction with etomidate or propofol at our academic health system. Patients younger than 18 years of age, those receiving preoperative mechanical ventilation, and those with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status VI were excluded. The primary outcome was all-cause 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes included sepsis, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), cardiogenic shock, and acute kidney injury (AKI). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, comorbidity, physiologic, and surgical factors. Given substantial baseline imbalance between induction groups, propensity score matching (1:1) using the same covariates was performed. Sensitivity analyses included adjustment for neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, complete-case analyses, and interaction testing.

RESULTS: A total of 155,667 patients met inclusion criteria, including 3846 (2.5%) who received etomidate and 151,821 (97.5%) who received propofol. Thirty-day mortality occurred in 1151 patients (0.74%). Unadjusted mortality was higher in the etomidate group (227/3846 [5.9%]) than in the propofol group (924/151,821 [0.61%]). After multivariable adjustment, etomidate use remained independently associated with increased 30-day mortality (aOR 1.44; 95% CI, 1.21-1.72; P < 0.001). Propensity score matching (n = 3832 per group) reduced the average standardized mean difference from 0.398 before matching to 0.023 after matching. The association persisted in the matched cohort (aOR 1.43; 95% CI, 1.14-1.78; P = 0.002), with observed mortality of 225/3832 (5.9%) among etomidate recipients and 157/3832 (4.1%) among propofol recipients, corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 1.8% and a number needed to harm of 56. In the matched cohort, etomidate was also associated with higher odds of sepsis (aOR 1.28; 95% CI, 1.08-1.52), acute coronary syndrome (aOR 1.24; 95% CI, 1.09-1.41), cardiogenic shock (aOR 1.56; 95% CI, 1.21-2.01), and acute kidney injury (aOR 1.27; 95% CI, 1.11-1.45). Post-induction hypotension was lower in the etomidate group (aOR 0.40, 95% CI 0.32-0.49; P < 0.001). Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Etomidate induction was associated with increased 30-day mortality and major postoperative complications. Given the observational design, results should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Impact of Early Reexploration on Patient Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery.
articles.abstract: Reexploration after cardiac surgery remains a rare but serious complication and consequently leads to higher morbidity and mortality. To prevent hemodynamic instability and compromised outcome early identification and treatment are crucial. In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed all consecutive patients with reexploration after elective cardiac surgery to evaluate the timing and outcome of reexploration.Between January 2012 and June 2022, a total of 520 out of 22,473 patients required reexploration following elective cardiac surgery (2.3%). Patients were stratified as follows: an early reexploration group, defined as reexploration ≤12 hours after cardiac surgery, including n = 321 patients (group 1) and a late reexploration group, defined as reexploration occurring >12 hours after the index procedure, including n = 193 patients (group 2). There were no significant differences in baseline characteristics such as age, Euroscore, or preoperative anticoagulation.Events in group 2 occurred significantly more often due to cardiac tamponade (43.8% vs. 20.4%, p ≤ 0.001). Patients in group 2 had a higher incidence of postoperative dialysis (37.0% vs. 17.1%, p ≤ 0.001) and an extended overall hospital stay (median 21.5 vs. 15.0 days, p ≤ 0.001). In-hospital mortality was also significantly increased in patients in group 2 (31.1% vs. 15.3%, p ≤ 0.001).In conclusion, timing of reexploration after cardiac surgery has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. We found that in patients with a late reexploration the postoperative complications and mortality are significantly higher than in patients with early reexploration. This emphasizes the importance of timely decision-making regarding reexploration to improve patient prognosis.

articles.title: 2027 GOLD COPD report.
Anticoagulants compared with aspirin in patients with embolic strokes of undetermined source: an individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct-acting oral anticoagulation did not reduce recurrent stroke compared with aspirin in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), and subgroup benefits suggested by analyses of individual RCTs were inconsistent across trials. We aimed to evaluate the effect of anticoagulation on the risks of recurrent stroke and major bleeding in patients with ESUS, overall and in prespecified subgroups using individual participant data from RCTs.

METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE and Scopus for RCTs published between April 1, 2014, and March 1, 2025, without language restriction, comparing anticoagulants with aspirin in patients with ESUS. Non-randomised studies and studies not enrolling patients with ESUS were excluded. We requested individual participant data from the principal investigators of all eligible trials. The primary outcomes were recurrent stroke and major bleeding. For each outcome of interest, we estimated the treatment effect for the overall trial population separately within each trial and the resulting overall treatment estimates were subsequently pooled across trials. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2.0) for the primary efficacy outcome of stroke recurrence. Hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% CIs were estimated following adjustment for prespecified covariates and pooled by use of the random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025644724).

FINDINGS: Our systematic database search identified 1170 records. Of these studies, four were eligible for inclusion in the analysis, including a total of 13 970 participants. Mean age of participants was 66 years (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participants were female and 8484 (60·7%) were male. Across all trials, 6989 patients were assigned to receive a direct-acting oral anticoagulant and 6981 were assigned to receive aspirin. The hazard for recurrent stroke was similar between participants allocated to anticoagulant or aspirin (399 of 6989 patients [4·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 417 of 6981 [4·8 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·78-1·14), without evidence of heterogeneity across studies (I2=5%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·37). The hazard for major bleeding was also similar between the two groups (149 of 6989 patients [1·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 106 of 6981 [1·1 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 1·19, 95% CI 0·52-2·73), but heterogeneity was present across studies (I2=79%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·0023).

INTERPRETATION: Anticoagulation did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke after ESUS when compared with aspirin, and the risk of major bleeding did not differ significantly between the two treatments. A possible benefit from anticoagulation in patients with ESUS and left atrial enlargement, as shown in a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis, should be investigated in future trials.

FUNDING: Division of Neurology Innovation Fund, McMaster University.

articles.title: Antimicrobial prescribing and guideline adherence in febrile inpatients in the Masanga Fever Study (MaFeStu) in Sierra Leone: a substudy within a prospective observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antimicrobial resistance is increasing in sub-Saharan Africa, yet detailed data on prescribing practices remain scarce. We aimed to characterise antimicrobial compounds prescribed at admission, assess their concordance with treatment guidelines, and examine antimicrobial compounds prescribed during hospitalisation.

METHODS: We conducted a substudy of the Masanga Fever Study (MaFeStu), a prospective observational study of febrile inpatients at Masanga Teaching Hospital in rural Sierra Leone from Sept 26, 2023, to Sept 26, 2024. Patients aged 5 months or older who were assessed within 3 h of admission and had documented fever (tympanic temperature >37·5°C) or reported fever within the previous 72 h were eligible. Patients were excluded if study procedures would delay urgent care, and those without available medication records were excluded post hoc. Clinical data and diagnoses were recorded prospectively, and antimicrobial prescriptions were extracted from patient files after discharge. The primary outcome was concordance of antimicrobial compounds initiated at admission with the hospital protocol and WHO guidance, assessed using predefined decision rules. Prescribed compounds were also classified by WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve category and indication. Secondary analyses summarised antimicrobial compounds prescribed during hospitalisation, including oral step-down and culture-directed therapy.

FINDINGS: 689 febrile inpatients included in the analysis, the median age was 14 years (IQR 1·8-34·0), 358 (52%) were female, and race and ethnicity data were not collected. At admission, 487 (71%; 95% CI 67-74) patients received one or more antimicrobial compounds. Of 882 antimicrobial compounds prescribed, 573 (65%; 95% CI 62-68) were WHO Access antibiotics, and 309 (35%; 95% CI 32-38) were WHO Watch antibiotics. Ceftriaxone was the most frequently prescribed compound (268 [30%] of 882). Lower respiratory tract infections, sepsis, and skin and soft tissue infections accounted for the largest share of compounds prescribed, overall and within the Watch category. Overall, 650 (74%; 95% CI 71-77) of 882 prescribed compounds were concordant with the hospital protocol, compared with 491 (56%; 95% CI 52-59) under WHO guidance. Discordant prescribing under both guidelines was concentrated in common indications, particularly sepsis and lower respiratory tract infection. During hospitalisation, 58 (4·9%; 95% CI 3·8-6·3) of 1183 antimicrobial compounds prescribed represented oral step-down therapy, and 73 (6·2%; 95% CI 4·9-7·7) were culture-directed.

INTERPRETATION: Most prescribed compounds were WHO Access antibiotics and were largely concordant with hospital guidance and, to a lesser extent, with WHO guidance. Prescribing patterns suggest that strengthening diagnostics, refining treatment guidelines, and improving guideline familiarity could enhance guideline-concordant prescribing and antimicrobial stewardship in similar settings with constrained diagnostic and stewardship resources.

FUNDING: Centre of Tropical Medicine and Travel Medicine, Amsterdam UMC, University of Amsterdam; Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit/Klinikpartnerschaften.

articles.title: Systematic Review Supporting the American Society of Hematology Practice Guidelines on the Management of Myelofibrosis.
articles.abstract: Myelofibrosis (MF) is a Philadelphia-negative clonal disorder of hematopoietic stem cells associated with substantial clinical practice variation. The American Society of Hematology (ASH) convened a guideline panel that prioritized ten clinical questions to inform evidence-based recommendations. We performed a comprehensive systematic review of MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane databases, and Scopus through January 2025 to identify studies that addressed the ten clinical questions. Meta-analyses were performed where feasible. Two reviewers independently selected and appraised studies. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. Of 3,007 records screened, 43 unique studies met inclusion criteria for the ten questions. Extended molecular testing identified high-risk mutations (ASXL1, EZH2, SRSF2, IDH1/2) that were significantly associated with decreased overall survival (hazard ratios ranging 1.5-4.5). JAK inhibitors improved spleen and symptom responses in symptomatic lower-risk MF and in patients with anemia, with momelotinib improving transfusion independence. However, survival effects were not clearly demonstrated and hematologic toxicity remained common. Evidence for treating asymptomatic high-risk patients with JAK inhibitors was particularly limited. Early allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation was associated with higher early mortality but improved long-term survival compared with delayed transplantation. Pretransplant JAK inhibitor exposure did not significantly affect mortality, GVHD, or graft failure. Evidence for interferon, aspirin, and iron chelation was limited and largely indirect. The certainty of evidence was very low or low across nearly all outcomes.

articles.title: Species-specific responses and mixed-cultivation buffering of emergent macrophytes exposed to combined pollution of size-fractionated polyethylene terephthalate microplastics and sulfamethoxazole.
articles.abstract: The co-occurrence of microplastics (MPs) and antibiotics is widespread in freshwater environments, yet their combined effects on emergent macrophytes remain unclear. A 42-day high-exposure pot experiment was conducted to evaluate the species-specific responses of Iris pseudacorus L. and Iris sibirica L. grown in monoculture or mixed cultivation and exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET MPs; 30 and 300 µm, at 1 g/kg soil) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX; 20 mg/kg soil), alone or in combination. SMX was the dominant toxic factor; PET MPs alone exerted weaker effects, with clear size-fraction differences; 300 µm particles generally produced stronger inhibition. I. pseudacorus maintained higher growth, biomass, and photosynthetic pigment contents, whereas I. sibirica exhibited greater oxidative stress and stronger antioxidant and osmotic responses. At these stress-test concentrations, combined PET MP-SMX exposure showed Abbott-model antagonism (RI = 0.67-0.75). Mixed cultivation generally increased biomass and photosynthetic performance, reduced oxidative damage, and partially alleviated soil nutrient imbalance, indicating preliminary species-level buffering. These findings identify species-specific response patterns and suggest that mixed cultivation may buffer combined MP-SMX stress, warranting further tests under environmentally relevant conditions in constructed wetlands.

articles.title: Correlation study between pre-stroke sleep characteristics and early neurological prognosis in patients with acute ischemic stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze the association between pre-stroke sleep conditions and 3-month functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).

METHODS: Consecutive AIS patients admitted between March 2022 and August 2024 were enrolled. The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, and Berlin Questionnaire were administered within 7 days after stroke onset to evaluate pre-stroke sleep characteristics. Poor functional outcome was defined as a 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score >2. Binary logistic regression was used to identify prognostic factors.

RESULTS: Of 782 patients completing follow-up, 18.0% had poor functional recovery. Compared with the good-prognosis group, patients with poor prognosis had a higher rate of pre-stroke excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and more frequent in-hospital sedative-hypnotic use (both P < 0.05). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that age >65 years, female sex, prior stroke history, higher admission NIHSS score, and pre-stroke EDS were independent risk factors for poor prognosis. Small-artery occlusion was protective relative to large-artery atherosclerosis (OR = 0.36, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Pre-stroke EDS appeared to be independently associated with unfavourable three-month functional outcome, apart from established clinical risk factors. Small-artery occlusion predicts better functional recovery compared with large-artery atherosclerosis.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Impact of a newly opened mechanical thrombectomy center on stroke management: volume, delays, and clinical outcomes" [J. Clin. Neurosci. 152 (2026) 112160].
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia

articles.title: Longitudinal pulmonary function in children with sickle cell disease after acute chest syndrome: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Archives de pediatrie : organe officiel de la Societe francaise de pediatrie
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute chest syndrome (ACS) is one of the most severe complications of sickle cell disease (SCD) and may contribute to long-term pulmonary morbidity. However, its impact on pulmonary function evolution in children remains insufficiently documented.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between ACS and longitudinal changes in pulmonary function parameters in pediatric patients with SCD.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective monocentric study at Reims University Hospital including children with SCD who underwent pulmonary function testing between 2017 and 2025. Patients with a history of ACS were compared with those without ACS. Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV₁), FEV₁/FVC ratio, and carbon monoxide transfer coefficient (KCO) were analyzed at baseline and after two years of follow-up. Within-group longitudinal analyses were performed. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients with asthma was also conducted.

RESULTS: No significant differences were observed in baseline FEV₁ or at two-year follow-up between ACS and non-ACS groups (p = 0.44 and p = 0.40, respectively). In contrast, the FEV₁/FVC ratio was significantly lower in the ACS group both at baseline and at two years (p = 0.01 and p = 0.03, respectively). Baseline KCO values were higher in patients with ACS (p = 0.01), but no significant difference persisted at follow-up (p = 0.07). Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with asthma yielded similar findings.

CONCLUSION: ACS was not associated with a decline in FEV₁ but was consistently associated with lower FEV₁/FVC ratios, suggesting early airflow limitation. These findings support systematic pulmonary function monitoring in children with SCD, particularly following ACS episodes, to enable early detection of respiratory involvement.

articles.title: Volume of the mammillary bodies and cognitive trajectories in preclinical Alzheimer's disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As part of the Papez circuit, the mammillary bodies (MB) play a key role in episodic memory, but their contribution to cognitive changes in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains underexplored. Here, we investigated the associations between MB volume and cognitive decline in cognitively unimpaired older individuals, and whether these associations differed by Aβ status.

METHODS: We examined 228 cognitively unimpaired older participants from the Harvard Ageing Brain Study (mean age: 73.5 ± 8.0, 64% female, all CDR = 0) who underwent baseline MRI, 11C-Pittsburgh Compound B (PiB) PET imaging and annual cognitive assessments. MB volume was quantified using the FastSurfer-HypVINN tool, and PiB status was derived from a neocortical aggregate. Cognition was assessed over up to 11 years using the Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5), as well as a memory and executive function composite.

FINDINGS: At baseline, PiB+ participants with lower MB volume showed poorer cognitive performance on the PACC5 and on memory and executive function composites. Longitudinally, lower baseline MB volume was associated with steeper memory and PACC5 decline, particularly among PiB+ participants. Control analyses showed that associations between posterior hypothalamic volume and cognitive performance, at baseline and over time, did not differ by PiB status. Similarly, associations between hippocampal volume and baseline cognition did not differ by PiB status, but hippocampal volume was associated with cognitive decline, more strongly in PiB+ individuals.

INTERPRETATION: These findings indicate that lower MB volume was associated with poorer cognitive performance and steeper decline in PiB+ individuals, suggesting that MB volume may serve as an indicator of cognitive decline in preclinical AD.

FUNDING: National Institutes of Health, Alzheimer's Association.

articles.title: Differences in patient attitudes on respiratory syncytial virus immunization among Canadian jurisdictions with and without publicly funded universal nirsevimab programs.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In 2024, Canada introduced two strategies to prevent severe infant RSV infection: maternal vaccine (RSVpreF) and infant monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab). Although Canadian guidelines recommended universal seasonal nirsevimab, implementation varied across provinces/territories. We compared attitudes and preferences towards RSV immunization in jurisdictions with and without publicly funded universal nirsevimab programs.

METHODS: Between November 2024 and March 2025, we conducted a national prospective cohort study recruiting pregnant or recently pregnant participants through social media. Participants completed a baseline survey, with follow-up at 3 and 6 months postpartum. Surveys collected demographic data, obstetrical outcomes, reported receipt of immunization products, and attitudes towards RSVpreF and nirsevimab, including perceived barriers. Participants were analyzed by residence in provinces/territories with versus without universal nirsevimab programs.

RESULTS: Among 1008 participants included in the analysis, 40.6% resided in jurisdictions with funded universal nirsevimab programs. If both immunization products were free and available, in jurisdictions with universal nirsevimab, 78.5% would accept nirsevimab, while 72.4% would accept RSVpreF. In provinces without funded nirsevimab programs, 73.9% of participants would accept nirsevimab with an 89.8% acceptance rate for RSVpreF (p < 0.001). In jurisdictions with universal nirsevimab programs, nirsevimab was perceived as more beneficial (p < 0.001) and more effective (p = 0.02) at preventing RSV disease than RSVpreF. Approximately 96% of participants agreed that the decision to obtain RSVpreF was up to them, however, fewer felt the same about nirsevimab (84.6%). When ranking vaccines in pregnancy, 43.9% of participants ranked Tdap as their top priority, while 21% ranked RSV vaccination first. Tdap was ranked higher than RSVpreF by 60.5% of participants, with no significant differences between jurisdictions.

CONCLUSIONS: During the 2024/2025 RSV season, preferences between RSVpreF and nirsevimab were associated with provincial/territorial public funding for infant monoclonal antibodies. As RSV immunoprophylaxis programs evolve, policymakers should recognize that funding decisions can influence public attitudes and preferences towards available immunization products.

articles.title: Implementing model-informed precision dosing of antibiotics in critically ill patients: a case-study with electronic health record interfacing and comparative evaluation of the Tucuxi software for cefepime therapeutic drug monitoring.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) and model-informed precision dosing (MIPD) of antibiotics are recommended to optimize care, especially in critically ill patients. There is a need to develop and evaluate MIPD tools. The aim of this feasibility study was to describe the implementation of the Tucuxi software for MIPD of cefepime in intensive care units (ICU).

METHODS: An interface was created between the ICU electronic health record (ICCA, Philips) and the MIPD software Tucuxi. Cefepime concentrations from ICU patients were retrospectively analyzed with Tucuxi and BestDose. Bias, imprecision and agreement of estimated past concentration, future concentration to be observed on subsequent TDM occasions, and predicted dosages for achieving a target exposure were compared.

RESULTS: The interface was successful for importation of TDM data from ICCA into Tucuxi. The comparative evaluation was performed with data from 34 patients (89 cefepime concentrations). Upon the first TDM occasion, the median cefepime trough concentration was 19.2 mg/L, with 46% of values above 20 mg/L. The rate of overexposure decreased to 29% after the first MIPD round. In the estimation of all observed concentration, the fits of the two programs were comparable with mean prediction error of -0.7 ± 2.6 and - 1.2 ± 3.1 mg/L for BestDose and Tucuxi, respectively. Forecasting results were also similar (-2.2 ± 16.1 and - 4.2 ± 13.3 mg/L for BestDose and Tucuxi, respectively). Dosage requirements were also in agreement, except for two cases.

CONCLUSION: The Tucuxi software has been interfaced with ICCA and showed promising performance for cefepime MIPD in ICU.

articles.title: Building climate-resilient maternity care through co-design, local leadership and the maternity workforce.
articles.journal: Women and birth : journal of the Australian College of Midwives
articles.abstract:
PROBLEM: Climate change, through changes to ambient temperature, the frequency, intensity and duration of extreme weather events, changes to infectious disease dynamics, and disruptions to food systems, threatens maternal health.

BACKGROUND: Pregnant women face disproportionate impacts from climate change, yet there are few purposefully designed, evaluated and demonstrably effective adaptation interventions. Developing and testing such interventions face logistical and complexity challenges, but these are not insurmountable.

AIM AND APPROACH: In this commentary we discuss the key challenges to effective climate adaptation for pregnant women and propose a way forward.

DISCUSSION: Progress has been constrained by challenges including restrictive research environments for studies involving pregnant women, difficulties in recruitment, workforce preparedness gaps, and broader system-level limitations. We argue that future adaptation efforts should prioritise co-design with pregnant women, communities, and healthcare workers; strengthen local leadership and ownership; and foster collaboration across disciplines including health, engineering, environmental science, and policy. Midwives and the wider maternity workforce are well placed to act as essential partners in this work, through their relationships with women and families, and their knowledge of local vulnerabilities. Emerging examples from maternal health and community-based adaptation initiatives demonstrate the potential of these approaches to generate contextually appropriate and responsive solutions.

CONCLUSION: Effective climate adaptation for maternal health will require interventions that are co-designed, locally led, cross-sectoral, and planned with long-term sustainability in mind. Advancing such approaches offers an opportunity to strengthen the resilience of maternal and newborn health systems while reducing climate-related risks for women, infants, and communities.

articles.title: In silico feasibility and robustness evaluation of a single-spot proton Bragg peak FLASH platform for small-animal irradiation using a generalized 3D-printed bolus.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveFLASH radiotherapy has shown potential to reduce normal tissue toxicity while maintaining tumour control, motivating the development of clinical delivery strategies. However, most preclinical proton FLASH studies rely on transmission beams or spread out Bragg peaks, which do not reflect conformal clinical dose distributions. This work aims to develop and evaluate an irradiation setup for ultra-high dose-rate Bragg peak proton delivery to orthotopic mammary tumours in mice, employable in image-guided research rooms powered by clinical cyclotrons. ApproachWe built a simulation framework (Python+TOPAS) to assess a single spot, ablative configuration comprising a copper degrader, collimator, and generalised (3D-printed) bolus. Performance was investigated on a Phantom Mice Cohort (N=6) using personalised boluses and a Real Mice Cohort (N=10; µCT/PET) using a cohort-derived generalised bolus. Planning goals were D99%,GTV=19.0Gy and HIGTV≤1.30. Physical dose-rate feasibility was evaluated against a nominal 40Gy/s DRmin,skin threshold under an assumed 500nA beam current cap; this metric does not establish a biological FLASH effect. Robustness evaluation included 0.35 and 0.5mm setup errors and ±3% range uncertainties.Main resultsSimulated plans met target and heterogeneity goals across cohorts, with the 40Gy/s DRmin,skin criterion met under the assumed beam current conditions (Dmean,skin≈18.5-19.3Gy). The modelled dose-rate criterion was met below the 500nA beam current limit in both cohorts. Under the evaluated 0.35mm setup and ±3% range uncertainties, reduction in D99%,GTV remained within 3% for 9/10 real mouse cases. The generalised bolus achieved the simulated dosimetric performance across ten anatomically distinct mice; applicability to independent cohorts remains unestablished.SignificanceThis in silico evaluation supports the simulated dosimetric and physical dose-rate feasibility of conformal Bragg peak proton delivery in small animals using a generalised bolus. The presented framework enables further development in image-guided proton research facilities, forming a strong basis for experimental validation and commissioning toward in situ small animal studies.&#xD.

articles.title: The ErbB4 Agonist JK07 Attenuates Heart Failure-Related Gene Expression and Activates Reparative Cardiac Pathways in a Murine HFrEF Model.
articles.abstract: Selective activation of the neuregulin-1 (NRG-1)/ErbB pathway is a promising strategy for cardiac repair in heart failure (HF), but recombinant NRG-1 therapies are limited by poor stability and nonselective receptor activation. JK07 is a novel biologic that combines the epidermal growth factor-like domain of NRG-1 with an ErbB3-antagonist antibody, enabling preferential ErbB4 activation. In a murine myocardial infarction-induced HF model (left ventricular ejection fraction <40%), mice received single or repeated doses of JK07 (1 mg/kg) or vehicle. Cardiac structure and cellular responses were assessed using echocardiography, histology, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing. JK07 reduced interstitial fibrosis and increased capillary density while inducing robust, transient, cell-specific transcriptional responses, most pronounced 1 day after treatment. Cardiomyocytes showed enhanced ErbB4 expression and metabolic pathways, fibroblasts adopted reparative phenotypes, and endothelial cells exhibited transient angiogenic activation. JK07 also preserved mitochondrial respiration in cardiomyocytes under inflammatory stress, supporting ErbB4 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy for HF.

articles.title: Association of Clonal Hematopoiesis Mutations With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has been linked to cardiovascular disease through inflammation-related pathways, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to systematically review and meta-analyze evidence on the association between CH mutations and AF, with planned analyses by hematologic cancer status, variant allele frequency (VAF), mutations, and sex.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for studies reporting adjusted quantitative associations between CH and incident AF. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Study quality was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Exposures tool.

RESULTS: Five studies comprising 7 cohorts and 299,215 participants were included. In populations without cancer, CH defined by VAF ≥2% was not significantly associated with AF (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.97-1.07; I2 = 0%). Large CH clones (VAF ≥10%) were associated with a modestly higher AF risk (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.01-1.22; I2 = 0%). Mutation-specific analyses did not show statistically significant associations for DNMT3A, TET2, or ASXL1 individually, and no sex-based effect modification was observed. In hematologic cancer populations, CH mutations were significantly associated with higher AF risk (HR: 3.22; 95% CI: 1.02-10.13; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses and wide prediction intervals warrant cautious interpretation, particularly for the VAF ≥10% and hematologic cancer analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between CH and AF may vary by clonal burden and hematologic cancer status. However, evidence remains limited and observational. Larger studies with standardized CH and AF definitions are needed to clarify clinical relevance.

articles.title: Aortic Valve Stenosis Screening Using Deep Learning on Noninvasive Arterial Pressure Waveforms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic stenosis (AS) presents a significant health burden. Early identification of significant AS, defined as at least moderate AS, may facilitate timely confirmatory testing, referral, and management.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop and externally validate a deep learning model applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a noninvasive finger-cuff system to screen for significant AS, using transthoracic echocardiography as the reference standard.

METHODS: This prospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted from December 2020 through July 2025. Participants underwent concurrent transthoracic echocardiography and noninvasive arterial pressure waveform acquisition. A 1-dimensional convolutional neural network was developed using the Cleveland Clinic development cohort and evaluated in a temporally distinct, multicenter validation cohort including sites in the United States, Spain, and the Netherlands.

RESULTS: Significant AS was present in 307 of 3,634 (8.4%) patients in the development cohort and 241 of 1,336 (18.0%) in the validation cohort. In the validation cohort, the model demonstrated an area under the curve of 0.893 (95% CI: 0.876-0.910), with a sensitivity of 92.5% (223/241; 95% CI: 88.5%-95.2%), negative predictive value of 97.5% (706/724; 95% CI: 96.1%-98.4%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 36.4% (223/612; 95% CI: 32.7%-40.3%). For severe AS, the area under the curve was 0.906 (95% CI: 0.890-0.922), with a sensitivity of 94.3% (183/194; 95% CI: 90.1%-96.8%), negative predictive value of 98.5% (706/717; 95% CI: 97.3%-99.1%), specificity of 64.5% (706/1,095; 95% CI: 61.6%-67.3%), and positive predictive value of 32% (183/572; 95% CI: 28.3%-35.9%).

CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning applied to arterial pressure waveforms obtained from a finger-cuff system serves as a promising screening test for significant AS.

articles.title: The right heart blind spot: right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation velocity, and mortality in a critical-care echocardiography study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score does not directly assess right ventricular (RV) function or pulmonary pressure.

OBJECTIVES: To examine associations of RV dysfunction and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) velocity with mortality across total SOFA bands and in patients with low cardiovascular SOFA.

METHODS: We studied adults in MIMIC-IV-ECHO with interpretable RV function and echocardiography within seven days of ICU admission, retaining one eligible stay per patient. Logistic models adjusted for first-day total SOFA, age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and Charlson index. We also examined patients with cardiovascular SOFA 0-1 and no recorded first-day continuous vasoactive treatment.

RESULTS: Among 19,686 patients, 3393 (17.2%) died in hospital. In 12,882 patients with low cardiovascular SOFA, severe RV dysfunction (adjusted odds ratio 2.30, 95% CI 1.69-3.13) and higher TR velocity (OR 1.46 per 1 m/s, 95% CI 1.30-1.65) were associated with mortality. High TR velocity with RV dysfunction was associated with 9.61 percentage points higher adjusted mortality than low measured TR velocity with normal RV function (95% CI 6.19-13.02). At total SOFA 0-4, TR velocity >3.4 m/s compared with measured velocity ≤2.8 m/s was associated with higher model-adjusted mortality (risk ratio 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15; risk difference 4.43 percentage points, 95% CI 2.46-6.39).

CONCLUSION: RV dysfunction and elevated TR velocity, suggestive of pulmonary hypertension, were associated with mortality at low cardiovascular SOFA. Elevated TR velocity also marked higher observed mortality at low total SOFA.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of bicycle ergometry for ischemic heart disease using stress computed tomography myocardial perfusion imaging with vasodilator testing as the reference standard.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise bicycle ergometry remains widely available for suspected ischemic heart disease (IHD), but its accuracy against stress computed tomography myocardial perfusion (CTP) imaging is uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of bicycle ergometry for detecting stress-induced myocardial perfusion defects on adenosine triphosphate stress CTP.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center, observational diagnostic accuracy study included 80 adults aged ≥40 years with suspected IHD/chronic coronary syndrome, written informed consent, and protocol-defined pre-test probability of IHD between 1% and 33%. Participants with diabetes mellitus, recent acute coronary syndrome or myocardial infarction, acute inflammatory disease, major respiratory disease, contraindications to exercise testing, radiocontrast or adenosine triphosphate allergy, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or other protocol-defined non-inclusion criteria were not enrolled. Recruitment was eligibility-based and was not documented as consecutive. Bicycle ergometry was the index test. Stress-induced myocardial perfusion defect on CTP was the reference standard. In the primary analysis, only clearly positive bicycle ergometry was classified as index-test positive; suspicious/equivocal and negative tests were classified as non-positive. A sensitivity analysis classified suspicious/equivocal tests as positive.

RESULTS: Stress CTP showed perfusion defects in 31/80 participants. In the primary analysis, sensitivity was 12.90% (95% CI, 3.63-29.83%), specificity 73.47% (58.92-85.05%), LR+ 0.49 (0.17-1.36), LR- 1.19 (0.96-1.47), and accuracy 50.00% (38.60-61.40%). When suspicious/equivocal tests were classified as positive, sensitivity was 48.39% (30.15-66.94%), specificity 53.06% (38.27-67.47%), LR+ 1.03 (0.64-1.65), LR- 0.97 (0.63-1.50), and accuracy 51.25% (39.81-62.59%).

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, bicycle ergometry showed limited accuracy for detecting ATP stress CTP-defined myocardial perfusion defects; these findings should not be generalized to ischemic heart disease overall.

articles.title: Early prediction of noninvasive ventilation failure in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: Development and internal validation of a clinical risk model.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is widely used in acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but failure remains common and is associated with poor outcomes. Most existing models rely on severity indicators, limiting early risk identification.

OBJECTIVES: To develop and internally validate an early prediction model for NIV failure using non-severity-based clinical variables.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 180 hospitalized AECOPD patients receiving NIV was analyzed. Candidate predictors included medical history, routine laboratory parameters, and chest radiography findings. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration analysis with 1000-bootstrap resampling, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: NIV failure occurred in 61 patients (33.9%). Independent risk factors included smoking pack-years, mucus plugging/excessive sputum production, acute heart failure/volume overload, pre-admission excessive oxygen therapy, and delayed medical consultation, while serum albumin was protective. The LASSO risk model showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.854) and calibration. Risk stratification demonstrated a clear gradient in NIV failure rates across low-, medium-, and high-risk groups (8.3%, 25.0%, and 68.3%, respectively).

CONCLUSION: A clinically accessible model based on non-severity variables can effectively predict NIV failure and may support early risk stratification and targeted management.

articles.title: Benzbromarone targets HSP47 to inhibit platelet activation via the collagen/GPVI axis and ameliorates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a major strategy for ischemic stroke. Studies have identified heat shock protein 47 (HSP47) as a safe and effective novel target for antiplatelet therapy, but clinically available HSP47 inhibitors remain lacking. Benzbromarone, a commonly used urate-lowering drug, has been reported to bind HSP47; however, whether it exerts antithrombotic effects by targeting platelet HSP47 remains unclear. In this study, cellular thermal shift assay and drug affinity responsive target stability assay demonstrated that benzbromarone directly interacted with platelet HSP47 and enhanced its stability. Benzbromarone disrupted the HSP47-collagen interaction and selectively inhibited collagen-induced platelet adhesion, spreading, aggregation, P-selectin expression, and reactive oxygen species production, with little effect on thrombin- or arachidonic acid-induced aggregation. In a FeCl3-induced mouse carotid artery thrombosis model, benzbromarone dose-dependently prolonged occlusion time and reduced thrombus formation, with efficacy comparable to aspirin and clopidogrel, without obvious bleeding risk, coagulation disturbance, or hepatic or renal toxicity at effective doses. Mechanistically, benzbromarone inhibited phosphorylation of Syk, PKC, and PLCγ2 downstream of the collagen-GPVI signaling pathway. Importantly, its antiplatelet and antithrombotic effects were largely abolished in platelet-specific HSP47 knockout mice, confirming the dependence on platelet HSP47. In a middle cerebral artery occlusion model, benzbromarone reduced cerebral microthrombosis, infarct volume, and neurological deficits, and this neuroprotection was largely HSP47-dependent. Together, these findings support benzbromarone as a clinically available HSP47-targeting candidate that suppresses platelet activation, arterial thrombosis, and cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury, warranting further evaluation for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Non-standard viral genomes in RNA viruses: from viral fitness and host responses to antiviral therapeutics.
articles.abstract: Non-standard viral genomes (nsVGs) are increasingly recognized as integral components of RNA virus populations rather than mere stochastic byproducts of replication. Emerging evidence indicates that nsVG biogenesis is governed by coordinated interactions between the viral replication machinery, RNA structural features, and host cellular environments. In this review, we summarize emerging concepts in the biology of nsVGs in RNA viruses, focusing on the mechanistic regulation of their biogenesis and their capacity to reshape fitness landscapes. In addition, we examine how heterogeneous nsVG populations influence host responses, viral persistence, and infection outcomes. Together, the experimental insights summarized here provide an updated perspective on nsVG population dynamics and their implications for the development of nsVG-based antiviral therapeutics and vaccine adjuvants.

articles.title: Reduced mortality with low-dose rivaroxaban in patients with coronary artery disease: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The optimal antithrombotic therapy (ATT) for patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) is still a matter of debate. In this regard, the role of low-dose rivaroxaban remains controversial. The authors performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCT) comparing low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT across the spectrum of CAD.

METHODS: RCTs were searched through MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases, and international meeting proceedings. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Results are reported as incidence rate ratio (IRR) of low-dose rivaroxaban vs standard ATT.

RESULTS: Five trials including 37 709 randomized patients were identified. Low-dose rivaroxaban was associated with significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality (IRR = 0.83; 95% CI, 0.70-0.98; P = .02), driven by a significant reduction in cardiovascular mortality (IRR = 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69-0.97; P = .02). Low-dose rivaroxaban was also associated with a significant reduction in myocardial infarction (IRR = 0.88; 95% CI, 0.79-0.99; P = .04), major adverse cardiovascular events (IRR = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.76-0.95; P less than .01), and stroke (IRR = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.91; P less than .01). Stroke reduction was driven by a significant reduction in ischemic strokes (IRR = 0.60; 95% CI, 0.49-0.74; P less than .01), not offset by an increase in hemorrhagic strokes. In contrast, low-dose rivaroxaban increased major bleeding (IRR = 1.46; 95% CI, 0.99-2.17), but not fatal bleeding.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CAD, low-dose rivaroxaban significantly reduces all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and stroke, but increases major bleeding compared with standard ATT.

articles.title: IRIS-Dx - The Integrated Risk Indicator System for Implant Disease Diagnosis: Retrospective Study and Framework.
articles.journal: The International journal of oral & maxillofacial implants
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This retrospective study assessed skeletal changes in the maxilla and mandible using CBCT imaging to evaluate longitudinal peri-implant bone alterations to develop a predictive risk model for implant complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Clinical, demographic, and 2D/3D radiographic data from 500 CBCT scans were analyzed. Baseline and follow-up scans were aligned to ANS-PNS (maxilla) or Go-Me (mandible) planes and superimposed using voxel-based registration. Skeletal variables, grafting procedures, implant dimensions, and positioning were correlated with buccal and lingual bone thickness at 0, 1, 3, and 5 mm from the implant shoulder. Statistical analyses included Chi-square tests and generalized estimating equations (α = 0.05, Bonferroni correction).

RESULTS: The analysis included 52 CBCT scans encompassing 125 implants from 52 patients, with a mean age of 69.5 years and a mean follow-up of 55.7 months. Implants were most commonly placed in the maxilla (57.6%) and bicuspid region (38.4%) (p = 0.015). Bone loss increased over time (p < 0.001). Narrow implants demonstrated greater buccal bone loss, whereas longer implants showed greater lingual bone loss. Socket preservation significantly increased bone thickness (p < 0.001), while guided bone regeneration showed no independent effect. Buccal bone loss exceeded lingual loss at crestal levels. History of periodontitis (OR = 6.68) and prior implant failure (OR = 5.00) were the strongest predictors of peri-implantitis.

CONCLUSIONS: Biological, skeletal, and anatomical factors influence peri-implant buccal and lingual/palatal bone remodeling. The IRIS-Dx model integrates 11 variables into a risk score (low 0-3, moderate 4-7, high 8-10) supporting early identification of high-risk patients and individualized implant planning.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Three Different Mechanical Circulatory Support Strategies in Isolated Acute Right Heart Failure.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Although acute right ventricular failure (aRVF) is commonly treated with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA ECMO), this approach may increase complications. We compared femoro-femoral VA ECMO, single-lumen cannula femoro-pulmonary artery (V-Pa), and double-lumen cannula right atrium-to-pulmonary artery (RA-Pa) support configurations in a swine model of ischemic aRVF-induced cardiogenic shock. Twenty-six adult German Landrasse swine were randomly assigned to the three study groups. Systemic oxygen delivery was the primary end-point; secondary end-points included hemodynamic parameters and complications. Systemic oxygen delivery remained stable during support without intergroup differences. Mean arterial pressure showed higher values in the V-Pa group compared with RA-Pa at 2 hours (65 ± 10 vs. 48 ± 8 mm Hg; p = 0.010) and 3 hours (62 ± 9 vs. 47 ± 10 mm Hg; p = 0.042). Mean pulmonary artery pressure was higher after V-A ECMO (20 ± 5 mm Hg) initiation compared with V-Pa (11 ± 5 mm Hg, p = 0.013) or RA-Pa (11 ± 3 mm Hg, p = 0.006) support. During support, the V-A ECMO group exhibited the lowest EtCO2 and highest carotid flow (p = 0.039 and p < 0.001, respectively). Challenges were noted with double-lumen cannulation due to anatomical constraints. Pulmonary artery cannulation-based support was noninferior to V-A ECMO in terms of oxygen delivery, with lower pulmonary pressures and preserved transpulmonary flow. Femoral vein-to-pulmonary artery configuration showed favorable short-term hemodynamics and easier cannulation compared with RA-Pa.

articles.title: Infectious Disease Diagnostic Capacity Across Hospital Tiers in China: National Cross-Sectional Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: China's notifiable infectious disease surveillance relies on clinical recognition and diagnostic testing, but uneven hospital capacity may affect case ascertainment and interpretation of reported burden.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to assess infectious disease diagnostic capacity across hospital tiers in China, including alignment with notified disease burden, regional variation, diagnostic modalities, and implementation barriers.

METHODS: We conducted a national cross-sectional web-based survey of hospitals in China in 2023. After centralized quality control and eligibility screening, 2689 hospitals were included: 124 (4.6%) primary, 1478 (55%) secondary, and 1087 (40.4%) tertiary hospitals. We assessed in-house and send-out testing availability; compared diagnostic availability with national notified incidence and mortality; and examined regional variation, selected diagnostic modalities, and reported barriers.

RESULTS: Median in-house diagnostic coverage increased from 11.6% (IQR 9.3%-18.6%) in primary hospitals to 27.9% (IQR 18.6%-37.2%) in secondary hospitals and 39.5% (IQR 27.9%-48.8%) in tertiary hospitals; corresponding overall coverage, including send-out testing, was 14% (IQR 9.3%-23.3%), 32.6% (IQR 23.3%-44.2%), and 44.2% (IQR 30.2%-55.8%), respectively. Tier differences persisted in sensitivity analyses. Diagnostic availability was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. In-house hepatitis B testing was available in 82.3% (102/124), 98% (1449/1478), and 99.3% (1079/1087) of primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals, respectively. Pulmonary tuberculosis showed a pronounced tier gradient (26/124, 21% in primary vs 910/1087, 83.7% in tertiary hospitals). Hand, foot, and mouth disease and other infectious diarrheal diseases had limited availability even in tertiary hospitals (380/1087, 35% and 456/1087, 42%, respectively) despite high incidence. Some lower-incidence but high-consequence infections also had limited local capacity, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (151/1087, 13.9%) and rabies (43/1087, 4%) in tertiary hospitals. Geographic variation was partly consistent with known disease endemicity, with higher testing availability for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in northeastern hospitals, although only 35.9% (55/153) of tertiary hospitals in this region offered in-house testing. Diagnostic depth also varied across tiers: hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA testing increased from 8.1% (10/124) in primary hospitals to 61.1% (664/1087) in tertiary hospitals. For COVID-19, primary hospitals more frequently reported antigen than nucleic acid testing (57/124, 46% vs 27/124, 21.8%). Lower-tier hospitals more often reported workforce and infrastructure constraints, whereas tertiary hospitals more frequently cited reagent-licensing and fee-schedule barriers.

CONCLUSIONS: Among surveyed hospitals, infectious disease diagnostic capacity differed substantially across hospital tiers, varied geographically, and was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. These disparities extended beyond disease coverage to specific testing modalities and barriers to capacity expansion. These findings support tiered, regionally responsive diagnostic networks that provide essential testing closer to first-contact care while ensuring timely access to specialized diagnostics through reliable, quality-assured referral pathways.

articles.title: Machine Learning Models Combining Routine Urine Dipstick Results With Age, Sex, and BMI to Triage Serum Urate Testing: Development and External Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum urate testing requires venipuncture; urine dipstick testing is inexpensive and routine. Whether dipstick results add information on hyperuricemia beyond age, sex, and BMI is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop and externally validate machine learning models estimating the probability of hyperuricemia from 9 dipstick fields, age, sex, and BMI, and to quantify what the dipstick adds.

METHODS: The development dataset included 129,535 adults with first urine tests and same-day serum urate and BMI measurements at a Korean tertiary hospital (2010-2025); 21,124 had urate levels ≥7.0 mg/dL, and 81.6% (n=105,704) had a same-day health checkup. Calibrated 12-input ensembles of Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) were trained on a person-level 80% split (103,628 persons) for serum urate ≥7.0 mg/dL (primary) and ≥9.0 mg/dL (secondary). They were tested in the remaining 25,907 persons (4225 events at ≥7.0 mg/dL) and in 49,987 adults in the KNHANES (Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey; 2016-2024; 5068 events). Inputs, KNHANES coding, split, and training procedure were fixed before fitting. We assessed discrimination, calibration, operating points by sex, decision curves, and increments over age-sex-BMI models.

RESULTS: At ≥7.0 mg/dL, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.825 (95% CI 0.820-0.831) internally and 0.845 (95% CI 0.840-0.849) externally, but 0.710 in men and 0.795 in women. Across 4 model classes, the dipstick added 0.017 to 0.024 to the external AUROC of age-sex-BMI models (0.814-0.823), or 3.1 cases per 1000 screened with top-10% referral. Externally, the models overpredicted (observed-to-expected ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.75); an intercept update fitted in half of KNHANES restored it to 1.00 in the other half. The internally derived 80%-sensitivity threshold flagged 29.8% (14,916/49,987) of adults, 97.4% (14,533/14,916) of them men; sensitivity was 77.1% (3907/5068) overall but 10.1% (53/527) in women, and positive predictive value (PPV) was 26.2% (3907/14,916). Flagging all men gave 89.6% (4541/5068) sensitivity and slightly less net benefit than the model at threshold probabilities up to 10%. At ≥9.0 mg/dL, external results were AUROC 0.860, increment 0.052 to 0.074 (1.6 cases per 1000), observed-to-expected ratio 0.48, scaled Brier score 0.002 (no better than predicting the prevalence), and PPV 2.6% at 82% sensitivity.

CONCLUSIONS: Routine dipstick results add a small increment to age, sex, and BMI for identifying serum urate ≥7.0 mg/dL. Ranking transferred from the hospital to a national survey sample, but absolute risk did not, and at the tested thresholds the models mainly selected men. Both cohorts comprised people who had blood drawn, so triage of serum urate testing in urine-only encounters, in which BMI is usually missing, remains an untested hypothesis. Before any use, the models would need local recalibration and evaluation in the intended setting.

articles.title: Cerebrospinal fluid composition and flow dynamics as predictors of shunt performance in neonates with posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH) is the leading neurosurgical complication of preterm intraventricular hemorrhage, yet ventriculoperitoneal shunt failure rates in this population remain disproportionately high and poorly understood. Abnormal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) composition following hemorrhage has been proposed as a key contributor to shunt obstruction, but the clinical relevance of CSF biochemical and flow-related factors has not been systematically evaluated. This review evaluated whether CSF composition or flow dynamics predict shunt performance in neonates with PHH.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420250642742). PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception to June 2025. Studies involving neonates directly evaluating CSF parameters in relation to shunt outcomes were included for outcome synthesis; mechanistic, biomarker, and indirect clinical studies were incorporated separately as contextual evidence to support biological plausibility. A narrative synthesis was performed owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool.

RESULTS: Direct clinical evidence linking CSF composition or flow-related factors to shunt performance in neonatal PHH is critically limited. Thirty-one studies met the inclusion criteria across 4 evidence tiers. Three studies directly related CSF parameters, or a CSF-directed intervention, to shunt outcomes. CSF protein was directly measured in only 1 of these studies and did not predict shunt failure. CSF infection was the strongest clinical predictor of shunt failure. No neonatal study directly measured CSF flow dynamics in relation to shunt outcomes. A broader mechanistic literature has demonstrated that PHH CSF is characterized by markedly elevated inflammatory mediators, growth factors, iron metabolites, and cellular debris, supporting the biological plausibility of CSF-driven shunt obstruction.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite compelling biological rationale, direct clinical evidence linking CSF composition or flow-related factors to shunt performance in neonatal PHH is critically limited. Elevated CSF protein may reflect hemorrhagic burden but does not reliably predict shunt failure as a standalone parameter. These findings do not support the use of CSF biomarker thresholds to guide clinical decision-making at this time. Prospective multicenter studies incorporating serial CSF biomarker profiling and direct flow measurements are needed to determine whether CSF-based predictors can meaningfully inform shunt management.

articles.title: AI-Based Monitoring Devices for the Identification of Circadian Parameters as Digital Predictive Biomarkers of Neurodegenerative Diseases in Older Adults: Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, and related dementias are a growing health burden among older adults. Circadian disruption is increasingly recognized as both a consequence and a potential early marker of neurodegenerative progression. Wearable sensing combined with AI enables continuous, noninvasive, and ecologically valid monitoring of circadian parameters as potential digital biomarkers.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on AI-enhanced wearable and objective sensing devices used to monitor circadian parameters in older and cognitively vulnerable adults and evaluates their potential as digital predictive biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases.

METHODS: Following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines, an original search of PubMed, Scopus, and JMIR journals (June 2025) yielded 12 studies, 7 of which met updated eligibility criteria on rescreening. A complementary search of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library (March 24, 2026) added 3 eligible studies and 3 sensitivity references (excluded records retained to delimit the corpus boundary). Two reviewers (JMH-Z and JM-R) independently assessed risk of bias with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Heterogeneous end points precluded meta-analysis; the narrative synthesis covered 4 prespecified domains: device class, circadian construct, AI and machine learning (ML) method family, and population and neurocognitive context.

RESULTS: The final corpus comprised 13 records (10 eligible studies and 3 sensitivity references) published from 2015 to 2025. Wrist actigraphy predominated, and samples ranged from community-dwelling older adults to nursing home residents with advanced dementia (n=16-7297). Circadian parameters included interdaily stability, intradaily variability, relative amplitude, midline estimating statistic of rhythm, acrophase, and circadian stimulus. AI/ML methods included supervised learning (random forests, gradient boosting, and regression models), unsupervised clustering, and algorithm development or validation; 7 studies applied deterministic algorithms without fitting a predictive model. Circadian fragmentation was associated with functional decline, dementia risk, and cognitive performance. Most studies were descriptive or observational with small, nondiverse samples; no AI model was externally validated, and no study followed an AI-specific reporting guideline.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-enhanced wearable devices show meaningful potential for noninvasive measurement of circadian disruption in older and cognitively vulnerable populations. Evidence certainty is moderate for actigraphy-derived fragmentation-function associations in institutional settings and low for predictive biomarker claims in community populations. From 6 recurring challenges along the sensing-to-biomarker pipeline, we propose a 4-layer reference architecture (sensing and acquisition, circadian parameter extraction, AI/ML inference, and a clinical and validation interface) with a layered validation pathway. Longitudinal, multisite validation studies using standardized circadian metrics, diverse populations, and explainable AI remain necessary before clinical deployment as neurodegenerative biomarkers.

articles.title: A Prospective Exploratory Single-Center Diagnostic Imaging Study Evaluating the Diagnostic Performance of 18F-labeled Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor Positron Emission Tomography in Diffuse Gastric Cancer: Protocol for the FAPI-DGC Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate preoperative staging remains challenging in diffuse gastric cancer (DGC), which is characterized by poorly differentiated or signet ring cell histology, diffuse submucosal infiltration, stromal fibrosis, and a high propensity for peritoneal dissemination. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (ceCT) may underestimate tumor depth, nodal involvement, and small-volume metastatic disease, whereas the diagnostic value of fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-positron emission tomography (PET) is limited in diffuse histological subtypes. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI)-PET targets cancer-associated fibroblasts and may provide additional biological information beyond conventional imaging.

OBJECTIVE: The FAPI-DGC (Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitor Diffuse Gastric Cancer) study aims to evaluate the diagnostic performance, potential clinical value, and safety of adding fluorine-18 (18F)-labeled FAPI positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) to conventional preoperative staging in patients with DGC.

METHODS: This prospective exploratory diagnostic imaging study will enroll 20 adults with biopsy-confirmed poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma or signet ring cell carcinoma who are scheduled to undergo curative gastrectomy or staging laparoscopy. All participants will undergo 18F-labeled FAPI-74 PET/CT in addition to standard preoperative investigations, including ceCT. Preoperative tumor, node, and metastasis (TNM) staging based on conventional preoperative staging, including ceCT, and on staging incorporating FAPI-PET findings will be compared with postoperative pathological staging as the reference standard. The primary outcome is the exploratory assessment of preoperative staging accuracy. Secondary outcomes include detection rates of primary and metastatic lesions; correlations between FAPI uptake and histopathological features, including fibrosis and fibroblast activation protein expression; associations with serum tumor markers; and safety outcomes. Accuracy estimates with corresponding 95% CIs will be reported, and paired comparisons will be performed using appropriate exact statistical methods, where applicable.

RESULTS: Research funding was approved in August 2025. Participant recruitment commenced on November 19, 2025. As of July 30, 2026, a total of 6 participants have been enrolled. Recruitment is planned to continue until March 2027, with study follow-up scheduled to be completed by June 2029. Data analysis will commence after completion of participant recruitment. The primary study results are expected to be published by the end of 2029.

CONCLUSIONS: This protocol describes a prospective exploratory diagnostic imaging study evaluating 18F-FAPI-PET/CT for preoperative staging of DGC. Publication of this protocol will enhance transparency, establish an a priori record of the study methodology, and facilitate interpretation of subsequent study findings while informing the design of future confirmatory diagnostic imaging studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials jRCTs031250386; https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/en-latest-detail/jRCTs031250386.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/105341.

articles.title: Radiation-induced versus sporadic cerebral cavernous malformations: comparative analysis of incidence and hemorrhage risk.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Radiation exposure has emerged as a recognized risk factor for cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM). Radiation-induced CCM (XRT-CCM) may arise months to decades after treatment and may carry higher hemorrhage risk than non-XRT-CCM, though studies remain limited. This study aimed to compare clinical characteristics, hemorrhage rates, and surgical management between XRT-CCM and non-XRT-CCM.

METHODS: A single-institution retrospective cohort study examined patients with MRI-confirmed CCM (1987-2024). All XRT-CCM and non-XRT-CCM patients, regardless of presentation type, were included. The primary outcome was symptomatic hemorrhage following diagnosis, and the secondary outcome was surgical intervention. Analysis included descriptive statistics, group comparisons, hemorrhage incidence, multivariable logistic regression for hemorrhage risk, and Cox regression for hemorrhage-free survival.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 612 patients: 16 XRT-CCM and 596 non-XRT-CCM patients. The XRT-CCM group included 11 incidental (68.8%) and 5 non-seizure-associated hemorrhage (31.3%) presenters, while the non-XRT-CCM group included 336 incidental (56.4%), 123 non-seizure-associated hemorrhage (20.6%), and 137 seizure (23.0%) presenters. Demographic characteristics were similar between groups. XRT-CCM patients received radiation at a median age of 11.9 years, with diagnosis a median of 13.5 years later. The mean ± SD radiation dosage was 47.8 ± 15.1 Gy, most commonly for arteriovenous malformations (31%). Multivariable analysis showed that radiation was significantly associated with hemorrhage (OR 5.23, 95% CI 1.35-20.36), while presentation type was not. Hemorrhage incidence was 7.77 per 100 person-years for XRT-CCM patients versus 4.36 for non-XRT-CCM patients (incidence rate ratio 1.78). Surgical intervention rates did not differ significantly between groups (25.0% vs 21.1%), nor did primary surgical indications, with hemorrhage being the most common indication in both XRT-CCM (75.0%) and non-XRT-CCM (43.7%) patients.

CONCLUSIONS: XRT-CCM demonstrated a higher hemorrhage incidence compared to non-XRT-CCM, with radiation exposure significantly associated with symptomatic hemorrhage. However, radiation exposure was not significantly associated with time to hemorrhage on survival analysis. The extended latency from radiation to CCM diagnosis underscores the need for long-term surveillance in patients exposed to cranial irradiation.

articles.title: Prevalence and prognosis of gait dysfunction in patients operated on for cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a Spine CORe™ analysis of QOD data.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Among patients undergoing surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM), the prevalence of gait disturbance and the likelihood of gait improvement remain unclear. The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and prognosis of gait disturbance in CSM and identify factors associated with gait improvement postoperatively.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis of the CSM cohort of the prospectively collected 14-site Spine CORe™ Study Group Quality Outcomes Database (QOD) registry. Outcomes of interest included postoperative ambulatory function at 24 months defined by lower extremity score on the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale and predictors of improved ambulation. The p values for descriptive statistics were obtained using paired and unpaired t-tests and chi-square tests as appropriate. For multivariable analysis, a logistic regression model was fit for improvement in gait in the subset of patients with baseline gait impairment.

RESULTS: Of the 1141 patients meeting prespecified inclusion criteria, 1135 had baseline gait data; of these, 877 (77.3%) had baseline gait dysfunction and 258 (22.7%) did not. At baseline, patients with gait dysfunction were older (61.5 ± 11.6 vs 57.2 ± 11.7 years, p < 0.001), had higher BMI (30.4 ± 6.6 vs 29.3 ± 6.0 kg/m2, p = 0.008), were less likely to have private insurance (46.0% vs 67.4%, p < 0.001), and had more comorbidities. Preoperatively, patients with gait dysfunction had worse neck disability (Neck Disability Index [NDI], 41.0 ± 20.8 vs 30.2 ± 18.4, p < 0.001) and quality of life (EQ-VAS, 56.2 ± 21.4 vs 70.0 ± 18.9, p < 0.001; and EQ-5D, 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 0.7 ± 0.2, p < 0.001). Patients with impaired ambulation at baseline were less satisfied with surgery at 24 months (North American Spine Society satisfaction questionnaire [NASS] score 1, 51.4% vs 60.9%, p = 0.004). Among 596 patients with gait dysfunction who received follow-up postoperatively at 24 months, 304 (51.0%) showed improvement and 292 (49.0%) did not. Patients who improved also demonstrated greater improvement in visual analog scale (VAS) neck pain (-3.3 ± 3.2 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) and arm pain (-3.2 ± 3.9 vs -2.1 ± 3.9, p < 0.001) scores, as well as better NDI (16.5 ± 17.4 vs 26.8 ± 20.9, p < 0.001), EQ-VAS (74.1 ± 20.0 vs 60.2 ± 23.2, p < 0.001), EQ-5D (0.8 ± 0.2 vs 0.6 ± 0.2, p < 0.001), and NASS (score 1, 74.0% vs 53.8%, p < 0.001) scores. Multivariable analyses revealed that lower BMI (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00-1.02, p = 0.01) and lower American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class (for ASA class I or II, OR 1.7, 95% CI 1.04-2.80, p = 0.04) were associated with gait improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, 77.3% of patients who underwent surgery for CSM demonstrated gait dysfunction preoperatively. Of these patients, 51% had gait improvement after cervical spine surgery. Lower BMI and ASA class were associated with improved gait postoperatively. Patients who improved reported superior quality of life, satisfaction with surgery, and decreased pain and disability.

articles.title: COPD-SQ Positivity and Suspected Asthma Screen Positivity From a Representative, Community-Based Sample in Xishui County, Guizhou Province, China: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma remain underdiagnosed in China, particularly in rural and resource-constrained settings. Questionnaire-based screening may support early risk identification; however, COPD-oriented and asthma-oriented screening approaches may capture different segments of the population. Single-disease screening may fail to identify the broader spectrum of people reporting respiratory symptoms or relevant exposures.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate the weighted proportions and the overlap between Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Screening Questionnaire (COPD-SQ) positivity and suspected asthma screen positivity in a community-based screening sample from Xishui County, China, and to characterize the demographic, exposure-related, and respiratory profiles of the resulting screening-defined groups.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline screening data collected between June and December 2024 from permanent residents aged 35 years or older across all 26 townships in Xishui County, Guizhou Province, China. Permanent residents were defined as individuals who had lived in Xishui County for at least 3 months before the survey and were expected to remain in the same township within the following year. Screening questionnaires were completed online or with assistance from trained local staff during household visits. Analyses incorporated stratum-specific sampling weights proportional to population-to-sample ratios and accounted for township-level clustering, with linearized SEs. COPD risk was assessed using the COPD-SQ, with a score of 16 or higher indicating high risk. Suspected asthma screen positivity was defined as at least one positive response to a symptom item from the European Community Respiratory Health Survey (ECRHS). Participants were classified into 4 mutually exclusive groups: both screen-negative, COPD-SQ-positive only, suspected asthma screen-positive only, and dual screen-positive.

RESULTS: Of 44,005 sampled residents, 41,839 completed the baseline screening, and 41,808 were included in the final analysis.
