The weighted proportions were 66.72% (95% CI 59.89%-73.54%) for both screen-negative, 11.01% (95% CI 8.88%-13.13%) for COPD-SQ-positive only, 10.97% (95% CI 8.92%-13.02%) for suspected asthma screen-positive only, and 11.31% (95% CI 8.27%-14.34%) for dual screen-positive. Overall, 22.31% (95% CI 17.36%-27.27%) were COPD-SQ-positive, 22.28% (95% CI 17.26%-27.30%) were suspected asthma screen-positive, and 33.28% (95% CI 26.46%-40.11%) screened positive on at least one instrument. The 2 screening approaches therefore identified similarly sized but only partly overlapping populations. The dual screen-positive group had the highest cumulative smoking exposure, biomass smoke exposure, prevalence of a family history of respiratory disease, and respiratory symptom burden, although several of these characteristics were components of the screening definitions.

CONCLUSIONS: Questionnaire-based COPD risk assessment and asthma symptom screening identified complementary populations in this community-based sample. These findings suggest that digitally enabled, integrated respiratory risk stratification may help organize demand for confirmatory assessment in resource-constrained primary care settings. However, a coherent care cascade pathway that follows screening should be in place to improve population health.

articles.title: Safety, Signal Quality, and Patient Satisfaction With Insertable Loop Recorder Implantation by Specialized Electrophysiology Nurses: Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insertable loop recorders (ILRs) are subcutaneous cardiac monitoring devices used in the diagnosis of arrhythmias and in the etiological investigation of syncope and cryptogenic stroke. Device miniaturization and procedural simplification have facilitated implantation in ambulatory settings. The involvement of specialized electrophysiology nurses may help meet rising clinical demand, although evidence in our setting remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to analyze implantation safety, detection signal quality, adverse events during follow-up, and patient satisfaction when the procedure was performed by specialized nurses.

METHODS: This prospective observational study (the CARDIONURSE study) was conducted in the Arrhythmia Unit of Hospital General Universitario Doctor Balmis between February 2022 and May 2023. Thirty-five patients with a clinical indication for ILR implantation were included. The procedure was performed by 2 specialized nurses under medical supervision. Sociodemographic, clinical, and technical implantation variables were collected, including detection signal amplitude (mV), together with adverse events and follow-up outcomes at 1 and 6 months. Patient satisfaction was assessed using a study-specific questionnaire at 4 time points. Descriptive statistical analysis was performed.

RESULTS: Mean age was 71.1 (SD 11.3) years, and 62.9% (22/35) were women. The most frequent indication was syncope (27/35, 77.1%), followed by suspected atrial fibrillation (AF) in cryptogenic stroke (6/35, 17.1%). No objective procedural complications occurred (35/35, 100% of procedures); mild, transient procedural pain was reported in 5.7% (2/35) of patients, and the procedure lasted less than 5 minutes in 74.3% (26/35) of procedures. Mean signal amplitude was 0.45 (SD 0.29) mV, with a visible P wave in 94.3% (33/35) of patients. No wound-related adverse events were recorded among the 85.7% (30/35) of patients with available follow-up data at 6 months; data were unavailable for the remaining 5 patients. A diagnosis was obtained in 20% (6/30) of patients with an available diagnostic outcome at 6 months. Overall, 97.1% (34/35) of patients reported maximum or very high satisfaction with the intervention, and 100% (35/35) with the care received.

CONCLUSIONS: ILR implantation by specialized electrophysiology nurses in an ambulatory setting is a safe, fast, and technically adequate procedure, with adequate signal quality and high patient satisfaction. These findings support the feasibility of specialized nursing as ILR implanters in similar ambulatory care settings, although confirmation in larger, multicenter studies is warranted before broader implementation.

articles.title: Earlier Application of Methylene Blue in Vasoplegic, Adrenergic Vasopressor-Resistant Patients is Associated with Better Clinical Outcomes. A Retrospective Analysis of 464 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe shock hails a dismal prognosis for patients in intensive care units. Vasoplegic patients, refractory to adrenergic catecholamines face an increased risk for in-hospital mortality. However, the optimal timing for Methylene Blue (MB) in these vasopressor-resistant patients, remains unclear.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center study conducted in the intensive care unit (ICU) of a tertiary medical center.

RESULTS: 464 patients were included, 183 (39%) admitted to the general ICU and 281 (61%) to the cardiothoracic ICU. All patients developed vasoplegia and were treated with MB after a median time of 11.2 hours from admission. In the aggregated cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with lower ICU mortality (30% vs. 52%, p < 0.001), lower in-hospital mortality (41% vs. 59%, p < 0.001), lower 1-year mortality (46% vs. 62%, p < 0.001), and reduced need for continuous Veno venous hemofiltration (33% vs. 53%, p < 0.001). In survival analyses of the whole cohort, earlier MB administration was associated with reduced in-hospital mortality in univariate analysis (HR = 0.64; 95% CI 0.47-0.86, p = 0.003) and remained significant after multivariable adjustment (HR = 0.69; 95% CI 0.51-0.94, p = 0.018). ICU-specific analyses attenuated the association.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective, single-center cohort, earlier administration of MB was associated with improved clinical outcomes among ICU patients treated for vasoplegia, including lower mortality and reduced need for renal replacement therapy. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether earlier MB administration should be incorporated into treatment protocols for adrenergic vasopressor-resistant vasoplegia.

articles.title: Beyond syndromic management: Re-centering Zimbabwe's sexually transmitted infection response on integration and domestic stewardship through advocacy.
Discordant serological results in people with HIV and syphilis: Treponemal Seroreversion versus False-Positive Reactivity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treponemal serological assays are assumed to remain reactive for life following syphilis infection. We established the frequency and characteristics of treponemal seroreversion in people with HIV (PWH) and syphilis, in contrast with false-positive serological treponemal results.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort of PWH with syphilis diagnosis from January 2001 to June 2025. Treponemal seroreversion was defined as prior syphilis diagnosis with negative non-treponemal (RPR, rapid plasma reagin) and negativization of one treponemal assay (CMIA, chemiluminescent immunoassay; or TPHA, T.pallidum hemagglutination) during follow up. False-positive reactivity was defined as reactive treponemal results and negative both non-treponemal and TPHA results.

RESULTS: During follow up, we identified 27 cases (6%) of discordant serological results in 467 episodes. Seroreversion was confirmed in 23 cases (5%), with three different presentations: 5 PWH (1%) with primary syphilis rapidly treated who achieved a rapid TPHA negativization; 10 cases (2%) treated during primary syphilis with progressive waning of antibodies and finally seroreversion of TPHA; and 8 (2%) previous cases of syphilis at different stages with decreasing antibodies during follow up. Of note, the cases of seroreversion after primary stage represented 26% of primary syphilis stage diagnosed. Finally, there were 4 PWH (<1%) with probable false-positive treponemal results, in all the cases with a very low level of antibodies by CMIA.

CONCLUSIONS: Treponemal seroreversion is the most frequent cause of discordant syphilis serological results in our cohort, and it is frequent as result of early treatment or/and longer follow up. In this population, a false-positive treponemal result is exceptional.

articles.title: Translational development of lower extremity extracorporeal distal revascularization: A proposed first-in-human protocol for bridging delayed revascularization in acute limb ischemia.
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a time-critical vascular emergency in which delayed revascularization markedly increases the risk of limb loss and mortality. Lower extremity extracorporeal distal revascularization (LEEDR) is a percutaneous technique designed to restore distal limb perfusion when definitive repair is delayed due to system-level or clinical constraints. After successful preclinical testing, clinical translation requires a structured, ethically grounded framework such as the IDEAL (Idea, Development, Exploration, Assessment and Long-term study) guidelines for surgical innovation.

METHODOLOGY: This single-arm, early feasibility study (IDEAL Stage 1) will evaluate the safety and technical feasibility of LEEDR in patients with Rutherford grade IIb ALI who are unable to undergo immediate revascularization. The extracorporeal circuit delivers oxygenated blood from the contralateral femoral artery to the ischemic limb via a distal tibial cannula, with adjustable flow rates between 100 and 350 mL/min under systemic anticoagulation. Continuous physiologic monitoring and serial laboratory assessments will be used to evaluate circuit performance, distal perfusion, and safety.

DISCUSSION: LEEDR may provide a temporary bridge to definitive revascularization when timely vascular care is unavailable. This initial clinical evaluation will focus on procedural safety, technical reproducibility, and practical challenges, particularly distal cannulation. Its single-arm design will inform procedural refinements and subsequent controlled studies rather than establish comparative efficacy.

CONCLUSION: This first-in-human protocol advances LEEDR from preclinical evaluation (IDEAL Stage 0) toward clinical feasibility assessment (IDEAL Stage 1). Following institutional approval and informed consent, the study will generate preliminary safety and feasibility data to guide further evaluation of LEEDR as a bridge to definitive revascularization in ALI.

articles.title: Bacterial Cellulose-Reinforced PMMA Bone Cement with Enhanced Drug Release and Osteoconductive Performance.
articles.abstract: Orthopedic implants are susceptible to complications such as implant-associated infections and prosthesis loosening. Antibiotic-loaded poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) bone cement is limited by short-term antibacterial activity and poor biological performance, restricting its potential for simultaneous infection management and bone repair. Herein, bacterial cellulose (BC) was incorporated into PMMA bone cement to improve its pore structure, drug release behavior, and biological properties. BC incorporation increased the total porosity from 4.79 to 24.9% and the proportion of open pores from 51.7 to 95.2%. Gentamicin sulfate (GS) release duration was extended from 1 to 4 weeks, while the cumulative release percentage increased from 9.44 to 33.97%. The sustained release of GS was accompanied by prolonged antibacterial activity against S. aureus. In addition, BC incorporation improved in vitro mineralization and supported cell adhesion and proliferation. In a rat calvarial defect model, the PMMA/BC composite exhibited greater new bone formation than PMMA, indicating improved bone repair performance. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of PMMA/BC composite bone cement for sustained local antibiotic delivery and bone defect repair.

articles.title: Wall teichoic acid regulates DNA-triggered innate immune receptor activation by Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: Cytosolic receptors that stimulate inflammation are commonly activated by ligands derived from microbes within phagosomes. The mechanisms that facilitate immunostimulatory ligand release into the cytosol during intraphagosomal infection are largely undefined. Using the pathogen Staphylococcus aureus, we describe wall teichoic acid (WTA) as a mediator of immune receptor activation during infection. Mechanistically, we find that the α-glycosylated form of WTA, generated by the glycosyltransferase TarM, mediates phagosome damage that enables bacterial escape into the macrophage cytoplasm. Peptidoglycan (PGN) O-acetylation reduces WTA attachment to PGN to prevent phagosomal escape. This competition among PGN-modifying enzymes determines the release of bacterial DNA into the macrophage cytoplasm and the activation of cytosolic DNA receptors AIM2 and cGAS. WTA thus controls the cytosolic exposure of microbe-derived ligands that stimulate innate immunity.

articles.title: CD36+ Kupffer cells control postprandial lipid clearance and fuel metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver diseases.
articles.abstract: Liver macrophages comprise distinct populations with specialized functions. Kupffer cells (KCs) populate liver sinusoids during embryonic development and monitor the blood, clear erythrocytes, and recycle iron. In metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), KCs acquire a lipid-associated macrophage phenotype characterized by the expression of CD36. Whether lipid-associated KCs exist at steady state and perform physiological functions remains unclear. Here, we show that CD36+ KCs, previously identified as KC2, are present at steady state in both mice and healthy human livers and that lipid handling is an intrinsic feature of this KC subset. Using KC-specific Cd36 deletion, we demonstrate that CD36 is required for postprandial hepatic lipid retention in healthy mice. CD36+ KCs also promoted lipid accumulation during MASLD, whereas KC-specific CD36 deficiency attenuated hepatic steatosis, identifying this subset as a regulator of physiological lipid homeostasis and metabolic liver disease.

articles.title: Rollout models of human planning with exact action probabilities.
articles.abstract: One proposed mechanism for human planning is the mental simulation, or "rollout," of potential action sequences to evaluate future outcomes. While rollout-based models have seen great success in artificial intelligence, cognitive models that describe how people use rollouts remain scarce, in part because they are difficult to fit to behavioral data. Existing methods rely on computationally intensive simulations that result in approximate, noisy estimates of latent planning parameters. We introduce ROSETTE (Rollouts with Stochastic Early Termination and Tractable Estimation), a rollout-based model for finite goal-directed tasks with absorbing goals that provides analytically tractable, simulation-free model fitting. ROSETTE treats planning as a sequence of mental simulations formalized as an absorbing Markov chain. The model deterministically accumulates analytically computed expected rollout evidence and performs a variable number of policy-update cycles. We fit ROSETTE to data from human participants in two multi-step planning tasks and found that it well accounted for a rich set of summary statistics of behavior. By making this specific class of absorbing-goal rollout models tractable, our framework provides a testable account of how people may simulate and evaluate possible futures.

articles.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis CpsA interferes with the TBK1-p62 axis to inhibit xenophagy.
articles.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) survives in macrophages by interfering with host lysosomal trafficking. Previously, we demonstrated that the Mtb protein, CpsA, is critical for bacterial survival in macrophages and infection in mice and that it can inhibit a noncanonical autophagy pathway. We also found that CpsA can interact with NDP52 and TAX1BP1, selective autophagy receptors that recognize cytosolic bacteria and target them for degradation, raising the possibility that CpsA also disrupts canonical autophagy. Here, we show that CpsA binds NDP52 and TAX1BP1 in their SKICH domains, which normally recruit the autophagy initiation machinery and TBK1. We demonstrate that CpsA prevents phagosomal recruitment of FIP200, a component of the autophagy initiation machinery, and blocks TBK1-dependent phosphorylation of p62, leading to impaired xenophagy. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how Mtb subverts host defenses, revealing that in addition to blocking noncanonical autophagy, CpsA inhibits the TBK1-p62 axis to block xenophagy.

articles.title: Clearance of erythrocytes after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Cranial lymphatic and dural pathways.
articles.abstract: The clearance of toxic blood products from the brain after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is critical for neurological recovery, yet the precise anatomical pathways and cellular mechanisms responsible for this process remain poorly defined. Using murine models of both arterial perforation and low-rate intracisternal injection, we have mapped a comprehensive, multifaceted network of red blood cell (RBC) distribution and clearance. We found that, while RBCs accessed peripheral lymphatic vessels via cranial nerves, an extensive distribution of extravasated erythrocytes could also be observed sequestered within nonendothelial, collagen-lined interstitial channels flanking the major dural venous sinuses. By day 2 post-SAH, regional macrophages actively cleared some trapped erythrocytes. These findings provide a detailed spatiotemporal framework of SAH blood clearance, revealing promising anatomical and cellular targets to accelerate stroke recovery.

articles.title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMDNterm). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMDNterm. Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMDNterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDMENterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

articles.title: Direct microscopic examination of lesion exudate for rapid identification of cutaneous sporotrichosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cutaneous sporotrichosis remains a diagnostic challenge due to the prolonged time required for culture. Although molecular testing and histopathology can provide additional diagnostic information, their availability, cost, or diagnostic limitations may restrict their use in some clinical settings. Clinical overlap with nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) and other infections further complicates early diagnosis, highlighting the need for rapid adjunctive approaches.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, we evaluated calcofluor white (CFW)-stained direct microscopic findings in lesion exudate from patients with culture-confirmed cutaneous sporotrichosis and examined the corresponding findings in patients with culture-confirmed nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) infection. Species-level identification was performed using molecular methods.

RESULTS: Culture confirmed 60 cases of sporotrichosis and 100 cases of NTM infection. Among these 160 culture-confirmed cases, 135 (84.4%) had available direct microscopy results and were included in the analysis. Among the 47 sporotrichosis cases examined by direct microscopy, fungal elements were observed in 30 (63.8%), including round yeast cells (23/30, 76.7%), budding yeast cells (8/30, 26.7%), and hyphae (5/30, 16.7%). All sporotrichosis isolates were identified as Sporothrix globosa. No fungal elements were observed in the 88 NTM cases examined by direct microscopy. Microscopic interpretation typically required less than 10 minutes.

CONCLUSIONS: Direct microscopic examination of CFW-stained lesion exudate may serve as a rapid adjunctive tool for the preliminary assessment of cutaneous sporotrichosis and may aid in differentiating it from clinically similar infections, such as NTM disease. However, microscopic findings should be interpreted in the clinical context, and fungal culture remains essential for confirming the diagnosis.

articles.title: Anticoagulation strategies for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation: agents, intensity, and monitoring.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Anticoagulation is among the most challenging aspects of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), during which patients remain at risk of both bleeding and thrombosis. This review synthesizes current evidence across the three interconnected domains of anticoagulation: agent, intensity, and monitoring.

RECENT FINDINGS: Unfractionated heparin remains the first-line anticoagulant, although evidence supporting its superiority over alternative agents is limited. Direct thrombin inhibitors and, more recently, therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin have emerged as alternatives. Anticoagulation intensity has historically lacked standardized definitions, while observational data linking higher activated partial thromboplastin time values to bleeding have contributed to a shift toward lower anticoagulation targets. Available assays provide complementary rather than interchangeable information, and no single test reliably reflects anticoagulant effect or predicts outcomes, although anti-Xa is emerging as the most informative single assay for unfractionated heparin.

SUMMARY: Recent evidence supports reduced-intensity anticoagulation during contemporary ECMO, although the lower limit of safe anticoagulation remains undefined and no single agent, target, or assay is optimal for every patient. Anticoagulation should therefore be individualized by integrating agent, intensity, and monitoring according to patient characteristics, circuit performance, and the evolving balance between thrombosis and bleeding.

articles.title: A novel 17-plex multi-pathogen detection for rapid and accurate diagnosis of tick-borne diseases.
articles.abstract: In recent years, anthropogenic ecological disruption has escalated tick-borne zoonoses; ticks transmit taxonomically diverse pathogens with overlapping clinical signs, challenging precise diagnosis and increasing risk of simultaneous detection in pooled samples. Despite advancements, current sequencing technologies, such as Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) assays, and antibody-based detection methods, are hampered by limitations including extended processing times and limited detection throughput. These constraints significantly hinder their effectiveness in high-throughput pathogen screening for animal or patient samples. To address these challenges, we developed an innovative multi-detection method based on the Multi-analyte Suspension Assay (MASA), enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis of a comprehensive panel of 17 vector-borne pathogens. This 17-plex panel comprises Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, Borrelia recurrentis, Babesia spp., Borrelia burgdorferi, Rickettsia prowazekii, Rickettsia heilongjiangensis, Orientia tsutsugamushi, Coxiella burnetii, Leptospira, Bartonella spp., Candidatus Ehrlichia erytraense, Hantaan Virus (HTNV), Seoul Virus (SEOV), Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV), Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV), and Tick-Borne Encephalitis Virus (TBEV). By combining this novel method with traditional techniques, including nested PCR and Real-Time Quantitative Reverse Transcription PCR (qRT-PCR), we achieved accurate detection of pathogens such as Rickettsia spp., Anaplasma phagocytophilum, and SFTSV in tick samples. Notably, the technique revealed the co-existence of multiple pathogens within the same sample group, highlighting its ability in identifying co-detection of pathogens. Additionally, in suspected cases of tick-borne pathogen infection in febrile patients, the method quickly identified positive results for SFTSV and Rickettsia spp. These preliminary results suggest the potential of this method as a promising screening tool for clinical diagnostics, although larger-scale validation is warranted. This method provides a preliminary technical candidate approach for the development of more sensitive field-deployable detection tools.

articles.title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge versus surgical repair in primary degenerative mitral regurgitation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) with surgical mitral valve repair in adults with primary degenerative mitral regurgitation (DMR).

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Ovid MEDLINE, Scopus and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to 23 October 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420251153452). The primary analysis included studies of DMR with a surgical repair comparator; cohorts with a predominantly replacement comparator and administrative registries entered separate sensitivity analyses. Odds ratios (OR) were pooled with the Mantel-Haenszel method, with random-effects models as sensitivity analyses. Certainty was rated with GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included; five (775 patients) formed the primary analysis. TEER was associated with more residual mitral regurgitation of at least moderate grade (OR 8.21, 95% CI 4.56-14.79) and more mitral reinterventions (OR 4.10, 1.69-9.94), and with fewer transfusions (OR 0.11, 0.05-0.23), less new-onset atrial fibrillation (OR 0.09, 0.03-0.28) and a shorter hospital stay (random-effects mean difference -3.6 days, -6.2 to -1.0). Early mortality did not differ significantly (OR 2.03, 0.62-6.61; 12 deaths), but the interval was too wide to establish equivalence. Four of the five primary studies ended enrolment before 2018. Certainty was low to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Surgical repair remains the reference treatment for patients with favourable operative risk and repairable anatomy. TEER is a valuable alternative for carefully selected patients in whom procedural safety or surgical risk predominates, at the cost of less complete and less durable correction. The absence of a significant difference in early mortality does not demonstrate equivalence.

articles.title: CA-PTP: Consistency-Aware Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction for Varying Crowd Densities.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural networks and learning systems
articles.abstract: Pedestrian density has a significant impact on trajectory prediction: in low-density scenarios, local influences from neighboring individuals dominate, whereas in high-density scenarios, the collective influence of the crowd prevails. The relative strength of local and global influences varies significantly across different densities, posing challenges for accurate trajectory prediction. The existing methods ignore these density differences, leading to reduced prediction accuracy, while the complex spatiotemporal dynamics of pedestrian movement further exacerbate the problem. To address this, we propose a consistency-aware pedestrian trajectory prediction (CA-PTP) framework for scenarios with varying densities. First, a consistency-based crowd movement model (CCMM) is constructed to capture density-dependent movement patterns, effectively representing the influences of both local and global consistency on pedestrian trajectories. Second, a consistency-aware spatiotemporal feature learning method (Consformer) is introduced, combining graph attention and transformer architectures to model spatial interactions and temporal dependencies under arbitrary densities. Finally, a multigranularity consistency-based trajectory prediction method (MGC-TPM) is designed, integrating individual, local, and global consistency within a unified prediction model to generate future trajectory predictions using more comprehensive information. Experiments on multiple crowd movement datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms the existing approaches in prediction accuracy.

articles.title: Visualization for Quantum Computing: Current State and Future Directions.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on visualization and computer graphics
articles.abstract: Visualization has played an essential role in understanding quantum computing (QC), from the Bloch Sphere to interactive visual analytics systems. Yet existing surveys either treat visualization as part of broader interface, education, or computer-graphics discussions, or focus on quantum rendering and data-processing pipelines; none provides a comprehensive visualization-centered taxonomy for this emerging area of visualization for quantum computing (VIS4QC). We address this gap by combining a venue search from 2015 to 2025 with agentic search and snowballing, curating 69 core publications and tools, and developing a three-dimensional taxonomy informed by QC expert co-authors. The taxonomy characterizes VIS4QC by why visualizations are created (Learning & Interpretation vs. Productivity & Utility), what QC subjects they address (Qubits &States, Gates & Circuits, Machines & Systems, and Algorithm Development), and how they visualize QC data through visual representation types and data-specific strategies. The corpus remains small but has grown rapidly since 2023, suggesting that VIS4QC is still emerging. Our support-coverage analysis shows a disconnect between academia and industry: academic work mainly supports learning about quantum states, while industry tools mainly support productivity around circuit diagrams. Visualization research provides limited tooling for practitioners, while industry tools incorporate few of the richer visual representations developed in academia. Algorithm Development and Machines & Systems receive the least coverage, and productivity tools for Algorithm Development are especially sparse despite the importance of algorithm development for practical QC applications. These gaps surface in quantum education and quantum software engineering, where users need connected support across concepts, artifacts, workflows, and outcomes. Building on this analysis, we identify future directions across quantum computing (QC) subject categories: scalable visualization of quantum states, visual support for dynamic and transpiled circuits, visual analytics for quantum hardware statistics, and mechanism-based visualization of quantum algorithms.

articles.title: Predicting Progression from Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fracture to Kümmell Disease: A Two-Centre Machine-Learning Study with External Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: A two-center retrospective cohort study with independent external validation.

OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with progression from conservatively treated osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture (OVCF) to Kümmell disease (KD) and to evaluate machine-learning models for predicting this progression.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: A subset of patients with OVCF treated conservatively subsequently develop KD, which may result in persistent pain, progressive vertebral collapse, and neurological impairment. However, factors associated with this progression remain incompletely understood, and externally validated prediction models are lacking.

METHODS: The development and external validation cohorts included 555 and 126 patients, respectively. Clinical characteristics and quantitative DXA, CT, MRI, and paraspinal muscle parameters were analyzed. Independent factors associated with KD were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Twelve machine-learning classifiers were developed and internally evaluated using nested stratified cross-validation and subsequently assessed in the independent external cohort. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret model predictions.

RESULTS: Among 555 patients in the development cohort, 175 developed KD and 380 achieved vertebral union. Older age, diabetes, fracture during the hot season, higher vertebral bone quality score, greater paraspinal muscle fat infiltration, and larger Cobb angle were independently associated with KD, whereas higher bone mineral density (BMD) and osteoporosis treatment were associated with lower odds of KD. Under nested internal validation, CatBoost achieved the highest AUC of 0.983. In the external cohort, LightGBM achieved an AUC of 0.993 and the highest accuracy and F1 score. SHAP analysis identified BMD as the most influential predictor, followed by Cobb angle and age.

CONCLUSIONS: Progression from OVCF to KD was associated with skeletal fragility, vertebral deformity, paraspinal muscle quality, age, diabetes, fracture season, and osteoporosis treatment. Machine-learning models demonstrated high discriminative performance in external validation. Prospective validation of a prespecified model is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Analysis of risk factors for multidrug-resistant bacterial infections in intensive care units and application of a nomogram prediction model: Erratum.
Bioimpedance-derived body composition and areal bone mineral density in chronic kidney disease: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Bone loss, reduced muscle mass, and impaired nutritional status often coexist in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Whether routinely available bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) measures are associated with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-measured areal bone mineral density (aBMD) independently of body size remains uncertain. We examined these relationships at the lumbar spine and femoral neck. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 192 adults with CKD who had linked InBody 770 and DXA examinations. Spearman correlations were corrected within each skeletal-site family using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate. Separate multivariable linear regression models estimated the difference in aBMD per 1-standard-deviation increase in each body-composition measure after adjustment for age, sex, height, and dialysis status. Sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for body mass index (BMI) or replaced dialysis status with CKD stage. The cohort included 102 nondialysis and 90 dialysis patients. Skeletal muscle mass was positively associated with lumbar spine aBMD (β = 0.085 g/cm2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.044-0.125) and femoral neck aBMD (β = 0.066 g/cm2; 95% CI, 0.036-0.097). Skeletal muscle index, fat-free mass index, intracellular water, and body cell mass showed similar associations. After BMI adjustment, all estimates were attenuated and their 95% CIs included zero. BIA-derived muscle and cellular-mass measures were associated with aBMD at both skeletal sites, but attenuation after BMI adjustment indicates substantial shared information with overall body size and nutritional reserve. BIA may help identify patients who warrant broader musculoskeletal and nutritional assessment, but it is not a surrogate for DXA or standard CKD-mineral and bone disorder evaluation.

articles.title: Effectiveness of mindfulness-based interventions on psychological well-being among nurses: A systematic review of randomized and non-randomized studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nurses frequently experience psychological well-being challenges in clinical settings, particularly related to burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are widely implemented to address psychological well-being in nurses. While previous reviews have primarily focused on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), incorporating non-randomized intervention studies may provide complementary evidence from a broader range of clinical settings. This review aimed to evaluate the effects of MBIs on nurses' burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Medline, Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and CINAHL up to June 2025 to identify RCTs and non- randomized intervention studies addressing the values of mindfulness-based interventions in nurses.

RESULTS: A total of 16 studies involving 1124 participants were included, comprising 12 parallel-group randomized controlled trials, one randomized crossover trial, and three non-randomized intervention studies. Study-level findings generally favored MBIs for burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality; however, the magnitude and precision of the reported effects varied across studies, and several findings were nonsignificant. Risk-of-bias assessments ranged from low to critical, and the overall certainty of evidence for all three outcomes was low.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests that MBIs may have beneficial effects on burnout, psychological resilience, and sleep quality among nurses; however, confidence in these findings remains limited by methodological weaknesses, risk of bias, heterogeneity across studies, and the small evidence base for some outcomes. The non-randomized studies provide complementary information on the application of MBIs in clinical nursing settings but do not strengthen causal inference. Further rigorously designed and adequately powered randomized studies are needed to clarify the magnitude and sustainability of these effects.

articles.title: The effect of Chinese herbal medicine nebulization therapy on chronic pharyngitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nebulization of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has shown promising results in the treatment of chronic pharyngitis, including the reduction of adverse medication reactions, the alleviation of clinical symptoms, and the reduction of recurrence rates following termination. Nevertheless, there hasn't yet been a comprehensive assessment of the research on TCM nebulization for chronic pharyngitis. Thus, the purpose of this study is to perform a comprehensive evaluation of TCM nebulization's application in the treatment of chronic pharyngitis.

METHOD: Using the Participants-Intervention-Control-Outcome-Study design framework and ‌Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses‌ reporting criteria as a reference, the study carried out an extensive search across databases, including Web of Science, PubMed, Excerpta Medica Database‌, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, VIP Chinese Science and Technology Periodical Database, and Wanfang. Publications from each database's creation to November 2025 were included. Articles about nebulized TCM treatment for persistent pharyngitis were independently screened by 2 researchers. Review Manager 5.4 was used for quality evaluation and meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Forty six randomized controlled trials with 6097 people were included in this investigation. Chinese herbal medicine nebulization was found to significantly increase the effective rate (risk ratio [RR] = 1.24; 95% confidence intervals [CI: 1.14 to 1.35]; P < .00001), the total symptom and sign score for chronic pharyngitis (standardized mean difference = -1.52; 95% CI [-3.01 to -0.03]; P < .00001), adverse reactions (RR = 0.19; 95% CI [0.10 to 0.36]; P < .001), and recurrence rate (RR = 0.19; 95% CI [0.07 to 0.51]; P = .001).

CONCLUSION: Nebulization therapy with TCM has demonstrated significant clinical efficacy in improving clinical symptoms, reducing adverse reactions and recurrence rates, and enhancing treatment efficacy for chronic pharyngitis.

articles.title: Art therapy for core symptoms in schizophrenia: An umbrella review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence on art therapy for core symptoms of schizophrenia remains uncertain. We synthesized systematic reviews (SRs) and assessed their methodological quality and outcome-level certainty.

METHODS: Eleven databases were searched through December 2025 for SRs of art therapy targeting positive, negative, or cognitive symptoms. Effect estimates were restricted to randomized controlled trials (RCTs) or RCT-only subsets. SR methods were appraised with A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2, reporting completeness with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, and evidence certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Primary-study risk-of-bias judgments were drawn from source reviews rather than independently reassessed in original trial reports. Primary-study overlap was assessed using the corrected covered area (CCA).

RESULTS: Thirteen SRs covered music, dance, drama, horticultural, visual arts, and multimodal therapies. Eleven were rated low or critically low on A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2. Of 28 effect estimates, 3 had moderate, 16 low, and 9 very low Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation certainty; none had high certainty. Negative-symptom estimates generally favored art therapy, but shared primary studies limited their independence, and selected estimates were sensitive to blinded assessment and publication bias. Positive-symptom findings were inconclusive. Only 1 eligible SR synthesized cognitive outcomes, although additional primary studies reported them. Overlap was slight within the positive- and negative-symptom domains (CCA, 3.43% and 3.65%, respectively); cognitive CCA was inapplicable because only 1 SR contributed.

CONCLUSION: Art therapy, particularly music therapy, may benefit negative symptoms, but low certainty and limitations in source reviews preclude firm clinical conclusions. Its role as an adjunctive intervention therefore remains tentative pending stronger, more independent evidence. Better-conducted, prospectively registered SRs and adequately powered RCTs are needed.

articles.title: Effects of telerehabilitation pelvic floor muscle training on urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Telerehabilitation-based pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) may improve urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), but its effectiveness remains uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with telerehabilitation PFMT as the intervention. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for eligible English-language studies published up to November 15, 2024. The revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials was used to assess the risk of bias, and data were analyzed using Stata 16.1.

RESULTS: Three RCTs involving 100 participants were included in the meta-analysis, showing that telerehabilitation PFMT significantly improved urinary incontinence symptoms (weighted mean difference [WMD] = -2.53, P < .001) and bladder overactivity (WMD = -7.13, P < .001). However, no significant improvement was found in quality of life (WMD = -0.88, P = .002). Sensitivity analysis confirmed the stability of the results with no significant publication bias.

CONCLUSION: Telerehabilitation PFMT demonstrated positive effects on urinary incontinence and bladder overactivity in MS patients, although its impact on quality of life remains unclear. Further large-scale, high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm long-term efficacy and guide the development of clinical guidelines for telerehabilitation in MS rehabilitation.

articles.title: Compartmentalized cytomegalovirus pneumonitis in a liver transplant recipient: Integrating tissue metagenomic sequencing and 18 F-FDG PET/CT for etiologic diagnosis: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Compartmentalized cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease is a rare form of invasive CMV infection in which the virus is detectable in affected tissues but is minimally detectable or absent in the peripheral blood. This atypical presentation often delays diagnosis and subsequent therapeutic intervention, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 67-year-old man presented with an intermittent chronic cough one year after undergoing living-donor liver transplantation. Chest imaging revealed newly developed right lower lobe pulmonary opacities. Despite extensive microbiological investigations, including blood CMV testing, no causative pathogen was identified.

DIAGNOSES: A computed tomography -guided lung biopsy was performed; metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) analysis of the lung tissue revealed CMV DNA with no evidence of other pathogenic organisms. Subsequent 18F-FDG positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) demonstrated increased fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) avidity within the pulmonary lesions, consistent with an active inflammatory or infectious process rather than malignancy recurrence. A diagnosis of compartmentalized CMV pneumonitis was established.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received supportive respiratory care and targeted antiviral therapy consisting of intravenous ganciclovir followed by oral valganciclovir.

OUTCOMES: The patient showed significant clinical improvement after antiviral treatment. Serial follow-up chest radiographs performed one year after completion of therapy demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary infiltrates.

LESSONS: This case highlights the diagnostic value of tissue-based mNGS for identifying occult pathogens when conventional microbiological and histopathological investigations are inconclusive. Furthermore, fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography may provide complementary evidence supporting the pathogenic significance of microorganisms detected by mNGS by correlating microbial findings with host inflammatory responses. The integration of these novel diagnostic modalities may facilitate the diagnosis of challenging transplant-associated infections. Further studies are warranted to validate their clinical utility in immunocompromised populations.

articles.title: Machine learning for early identification of delirium in ICU patients with acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Delirium is common in critically ill patients and is associated with worse outcomes, but its risk factors among adults with acute kidney injury (AKI) in the intensive care unit (ICU) are not fully described. We aimed to develop and validate a simple machine learning model to predict delirium during ICU stay in adult AKI patients and to identify the most important clinical predictors. We retrospectively included ICU patients aged 18 years or older with a diagnosis of AKI. The cohort was randomly split 70:30 into a training set and a validation set. Patients were labeled as having delirium or non-delirium based on events occurring during the ICU stay. In the training set, the Boruta algorithm was used to identify confirmed predictors, which were then fed into 9 supervised machine learning classifiers. Model performance was assessed in the validation set using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were calculated to interpret feature importance. Among the validation cohort, CatBoost showed the best discrimination with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.742 (95% confidence interval = 0.676-0.809). SHAP analysis of the final model identified diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell, and prothrombin time as the most influential predictors of delirium. A CatBoost model built on Boruta-confirmed clinical variables showed moderate discrimination for ICU delirium in adults with AKI. The most influential predictors identified by SHAP - diabetes, pneumonia, chloride, red blood cell count, and prothrombin time - may help clinicians recognize high-risk patients and prioritize preventive measures. External validation is needed before wider clinical use.

articles.title: Risk of major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality across chronic kidney disease stages: A population-based retrospective cohort study in South Korea.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is associated with increased cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk. However, few studies have assessed whether these risks vary across CKD stages in Asian populations. Using Korean National Health Insurance data (2016-2020), we analyzed a cohort of 51,352 individuals newly diagnosed with CKD. We compared incidence rates of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and all-cause mortality across CKD stages. Model 1 adjusted for age and sex; Model 2, the primary adjusted model, additionally adjusted for income and health insurance coverage type. All covariates were ascertained on or before cohort entry. During follow-up, 9708 participants (18.9%) experienced MACE and 7091 (13.8%) died. Compared with stage 1 CKD, stage 5 CKD with dialysis was associated with higher hazards of MACE (Model 2 hazard ratio = 4.67; 95% confidence interval = 4.24-5.13) and all-cause mortality (hazard ratio = 5.61; 95% confidence interval = 4.94-6.38). The corresponding incidence rates were 26,148 MACE cases and 16,441 deaths per 100,000 person-years. Advanced CKD stages were associated with higher hazards of MACE and all-cause mortality after adjustment for baseline demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Residual confounding by clinical characteristics remains possible.

articles.title: Relationship between marital adjustment, maternal role perception, social support, and perceived mental health among pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: This study examined associations among marital adjustment, maternal role perception, social support, and perceived mental health in pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 452 pregnant women at ≥ 20 weeks of gestation at a state hospital in Türkiye between November 2020 and July 2021. Data were collected using the Descriptive Information Form, the Marital Adjustment Scale (MAS), and the Myself as a Mother Scale (MMS). Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and logistic regression analyses were performed. Overall, 70.4% of pregnant women had good marital adjustment, while 29.6% had poor marital adjustment. Marital adjustment was weakly but positively associated with maternal role perception (r = 0.28, P < .001). In the regression model examining the factors associated with marital adjustment among pregnant women, age, perceived mental health, perceived social support from the spouse and spouse's first-degree relatives, and the number of pregnancies were significantly associated with marital adjustment (Model χ2 (19) = 164.072, P < .001; Nagelkerke R2 = 0.433). Increasing age was significantly associated with higher odds of good marital adjustment (OR = 1.072, 95% CI: 1.004-1.146, P = .039). Pregnant women who perceived their mental health as moderate (OR = 0.355, P < .001) or below moderate/not good (OR = 0.314, P = .028) had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived their mental health as good. Women who perceived the support they received from their spouse as inadequate had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived it as adequate (OR = 0.289, 95% CI: 0.128-0.653, P = .003). Similarly, women who perceived the support they received from their spouse's first-degree relatives as inadequate had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived it as adequate (OR = 0.278, 95% CI: 0.162-0.478, P < .001). This study suggests that marital adjustment among pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic may be associated with maternal role perception, perceived social support, and mental health status. Routine antenatal assessment of marital adjustment and perceived social support may help healthcare professionals identify potential risks early.

articles.title: Sex-specific differences in patient-prosthesis mismatch following valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract: Female sex is associated with increased rates of mortality and readmission following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and is a risk factor for patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM). Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI. This retrospective study analyzed 77 patients who underwent ViV-TAVI at Kettering Health from 2015 to 2021, evaluating PPM incidence and bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) utilization. Indexed effective orifice area following ViV-TAVI was compared between females and males using an unpaired t test. Fisher exact test assessed the association between BVF and PPM for the overall cohort and within each sex. Statistical analyses were performed using R software. Males represented 57% of patients (body mass index = 28.8 kg/m2), while females comprised 43% (body mass index = 29.1 kg/m2). There was no significant difference in average indexed effective orifice area between females and males (P = .370). BVF rates were similar between sexes (33.3% in females; 29.6% in males), with an overall reduction in PPM (P = .028) and in females (P = .029). Cramér's V showed a moderate association between BVF and PPM in the overall cohort (0.305) and females (0.475), with a weaker association in males (0.183). Similar rates of PPM between sexes suggest that appropriate patient selection and valve sizing are crucial in PPM prevention. The significant reduction of PPM with BVF in females calls for further research into sex-specific outcomes and optimization of ViV-TAVI results.

articles.title: Clinical risk factors and prediction of acute kidney injury in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury is a frequent and clinically significant complication in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and is associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes. Early identification of high-risk patients may facilitate timely prevention and individualized management. This study aimed to investigate the clinical risk factors for acute kidney injury in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and to develop a practical prediction model. This retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction treated at our institution between January 2022 and December 2025. Acute kidney injury was defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria. Demographic data, comorbidities, admission clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, imaging parameters, and treatment-related variables were collected. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of acute kidney injury. A logistic regression model was subsequently established, and its performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. A total of 265 patients were included, of whom 58 (21.9%) developed acute kidney injury during hospitalization. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified age ≥65 years, diabetes mellitus, Killip class III-IV, cardiogenic shock, left ventricular ejection fraction <50%, serum creatinine >100 μmol/L, and albumin <38 g/L as independent risk factors for acute kidney injury, whereas emergency percutaneous coronary intervention was an independent protective factor. The prediction model constructed from these variables showed good discrimination, with an area under the curve of 0.851 (95% confidence interval: 0.797-0.905). At the optimal cutoff value of 0.238, the sensitivity and specificity were 79.3% and 78.7%, respectively. Acute kidney injury in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction was independently associated with advanced age, diabetes mellitus, impaired cardiac and renal function, hemodynamic instability, and hypoalbuminemia. The proposed logistic prediction model demonstrated good predictive performance and may be useful for early risk stratification in clinical practice.

articles.title: Association of serum albumin and creatinine levels with subsequent fulfillment of laboratory criteria for T2DM in patients with hyperuricemia.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia is associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus; however, longitudinal evidence remains limited. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate clinical factors associated with the subsequent fulfillment of the study glycemic criteria (glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL or glycated hemoglobin ≥ 6.5%) among patients with hyperuricemia. Among 16,287 patients who met the criteria for hyperuricemia in the Kangwon National University Hospital common data model between 2014 and 2016, 243 patients had serum albumin and creatinine measured within 90 days of the index date and remained free of study glycemic criteria through the biomarker baseline date, comprising the primary delayed-entry cohort. The risk of subsequent study glycemic criteria was estimated using delayed-entry Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and uric acid, with albumin and creatinine evaluated individually and jointly. Uric acid quartile and 90-day landmark analyses, as well as a sensitivity analysis excluding patients with pre-index abnormal glycemic laboratory results, were also performed. In the primary delayed-entry cohort, 176 of 243 patients (72.4%) subsequently met the study glycemic criteria. In the minimal model, higher index uric acid levels were associated with a higher hazard of fulfilling the study glycemic criteria (hazard ratio [HR], 1.182 per 1 mg/dL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.044-1.340; P = .009). In the combined model, albumin was associated with a lower hazard of this outcome (HR, 0.588 per 1 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.421-0.822), whereas higher creatinine was associated with a higher hazard (HR, 1.160 per 1 mg/dL; 95% CI, 1.075-1.251). The concordance index (C-index) improved from 0.608 to 0.649 in the combined model, and the associations of albumin and creatinine remained significant in the 90-day landmark analysis. In the sensitivity analysis, albumin remained significantly associated with the outcome (HR, 0.491; 95% CI, 0.267-0.904), whereas the creatinine association was attenuated (HR, 1.165; 95% CI, 0.988-1.374), and uric acid was not associated with the outcome (HR, 1.003; 95% CI, 0.817-1.233). In patients with hyperuricemia, lower serum albumin and higher serum creatinine were independently associated with subsequent fulfillment of the study glycemic criteria. These routinely available biomarkers may provide additional information beyond serum uric acid alone, although further validation is needed.

articles.title: An interpretable AutoML framework for predicting carbapenem resistance and ICU outcomes in patients with Pseudomonas aeruginosa-positive cultures: A single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa remains an important threat in intensive care units (ICUs), but few studies have jointly evaluated carbapenem resistance and conventional ICU outcomes using leakage-controlled validation. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study of 847 adults with P aeruginosa-positive cultures from 2018 to 2023. A fixed index time was defined at 48 hours after ICU admission, and predictors were restricted to information available before that time. Nine classifiers and 8 regressors were evaluated using patient-grouped, temporally blocked 5-fold outer cross-validation. Preprocessing and variance threshold filtering-mutual information-L1 regularization feature selection were fitted within each outer training fold. Fold-specific classification thresholds were derived from inner out-of-fold predictions to target a sensitivity of 0.80. Performance, calibration, and Shapley additive explanations analyses used held-out outer-fold predictions. Pairwise comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate procedure. Resistance analyses included 846 patients. Logistic regression had the highest pooled out-of-fold receiver operating characteristic area under the curve for carbapenem resistance of the first post-index isolate (0.581; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.540-0.619). Random forest had the highest receiver operating characteristic area under the curve for resistance of the last post-index isolate (0.656; 95% CI = 0.614-0.696) and in-hospital mortality (0.856; 95% CI = 0.830-0.880). At the training-derived thresholds, sensitivity/specificity was 0.828/0.308, 0.794/0.409, and 0.785/0.753, respectively. After false-discovery-rate adjustment, the leading classifiers significantly outperformed 1, 6, and 2 of 8 comparators, respectively. Stacking regression had the lowest root mean squared error (RMSE) for ICU length of stay (46.126 days; 95% CI = 39.598-52.583; R2 = 0.711), whereas bagging regression had the lowest RMSE for total hospitalization expenses (38.949 units of 10,000 Chinese yuan; 95% CI = 33.646-44.058; R2 = 0.788). No pairwise difference in RMSE or mean absolute error among regressors remained significant after adjustment. Held-out Shapley additive explanations analyses identified endpoint-specific associations involving antimicrobial exposure, inflammatory markers, and host characteristics. Leakage-controlled internal validation showed high discrimination for in-hospital mortality, limited-to-modest discrimination for the resistance outcomes, and substantial internally estimated explained variance for the continuous outcomes. No algorithm was uniformly superior. External multicenter validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical use.

articles.title: Prenatal clinical features and clinical outcomes of fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome: A single-center case series of 22 patients.
articles.abstract: This study analyzes 22 fetuses with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion syndrome in Eastern China to investigate the prenatal clinical features and postnatal outcomes. We conducted a retrospective study of 22 fetuses diagnosed with 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion (312-855 kilobase) via chromosomal microarray analysis among 2607 prenatal cases from January 2022 to September 2024. Parental origin, ultrasound findings, and postnatal outcomes were evaluated. The 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion prevalence was 0.84% (22/2607). Prenatal ultrasound anomalies were observed in 54.5% (12/22), primarily mild cardiac findings (tricuspid regurgitation), choroid plexus cysts, and thickened nuchal translucency. Parental testing (13 cases) revealed 6 paternal, 6 maternal, and 1 de novo case. Postnatal follow-up of 18 live births (mean 14.7 months) showed normal development in most cases (17/18), with 1 child exhibiting delayed language development. Four pregnancies (18.2%) were terminated despite genetic counseling. Our study underscores that the 15q11.2 BP1-BP2 microdeletion exhibits incomplete penetrance and variable prenatal phenotypes, complicating outcome prediction. Long-term pediatric follow-up is essential, and early reassurance should be avoided even in cases with normal prenatal findings or favorable short-term outcomes.

articles.title: The effect of physical exercise on sleep quality in Chinese middle school students: A cross-sectional study on the mediating role of positive and negative emotions.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to explore the effect of physical exercise (PE1) on sleep quality (SQ) among Chinese middle school students and to further analyze the mediating roles of positive and negative emotions (NE). A total of 1056 middle school students (aged 11-15 years, M = 13.28, SD = 1.08; 516 males, 540 females) from 6 middle schools in Sichuan Province, China, voluntarily participated in this cross-sectional survey. The Physical Activity Rating Scale, Positive and Negative Affect Scale, and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index were used in this study. Descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation analyses were performed using SPSS 26.0. Mediation analyses (model 4) were conducted with the PROCESS 3.5 macro, and the significance of indirect effects was tested using a bias-corrected nonparametric percentile bootstrap method with 5000 resamples, generating 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The total effect of PE1 on SQ was not significant (P > .05). After controlling for positive and NE, the direct effect of PE1 on SQ was also non-significant (P > .05). However, both positive emotions (indirect effect = 0.032, 95% CI [0.015, 0.051]) and NE (indirect effect = 0.037, 95% CI [0.012, 0.064]) played significant mediating roles in the relationship between PE1 and SQ. These findings suggest that PE1 improves SQ in middle school students primarily by enhancing positive emotions and reducing NE, rather than through a direct effect.

articles.title: Prognostic comparison of albumin-related inflammatory ratios in sepsis-induced coagulopathy: A retrospective cohort study based on the MIMIC-IV database.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) is associated with markedly elevated organ dysfunction and mortality. Integrated albumin-related inflammatory ratios may improve prognostic assessment, yet no systematic comparison of multiple ratios exists in SIC patients. This retrospective cohort study included 2214 SIC patients from the MIMIC-IV database. Five albumin-related inflammatory ratios-neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR), lymphocyte-to-albumin ratio (LAR), monocyte-to-albumin ratio (MAR), platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR), and red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) - were calculated from the first 24-hour laboratory values. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Discrimination was evaluated using ROC curves and time-dependent AUC; prognostic associations and dose-response relationships were examined using Kaplan-Meier analysis, multivariable Cox regression, and restricted cubic splines. Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI) and Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI) quantified incremental value added to existing severity scores. Among 2214 patients, 673 (30.4%) died within 30 days. RAR and NAR showed relatively better discrimination than the other ratios, with AUC values of approximately 0.60, indicating modest prognostic discrimination. In fully adjusted Cox models, high-level RAR (T3 vs. T1) was associated with 52% increased mortality risk (HR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.21-1.89), and high-level NAR with 30% increased risk (HR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.04-1.63). NAR showed a significant nonlinear dose-response relationship with mortality (P for nonlinearity = .011). Incorporating RAR into SOFA, SIC-score, OASIS, and APS III significantly improved model discrimination and reclassification (all IDI and NRI P < .05). RAR and NAR are independent prognostic factors for 30-day mortality in SIC patients, and RAR provided statistically significant incremental value when incorporated into existing critical illness scoring systems. These readily obtainable ratios offer cost-effective tools for early risk stratification and individualized management.

articles.title: Predicting rapid progression of non-target lesions after PCI using machine learning combining coronary CTA plaque features and clinical inflammatory markers.
articles.abstract: This study investigates the value of a machine learning method combining coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA plaque features and clinical inflammatory markers for predicting rapid progression of non-target lesions after Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI). A total of 331 post-PCI patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into rapid progression (n = 78) and non-rapid progression (n = 253) groups based on follow-up CTA. Baseline clinical data, inflammatory markers (hs-CRP, IL-6, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio), and CTA plaque features (low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, noncalcified plaque volume) were collected. Patients were randomly split 7:3 into training and validation sets. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression identified predictors. Logistic regression, inflammation-only, CTA-only, and multimodal fusion models were developed and compared. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression selected 8 independent predictors: hs-CRP, IL-6, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, low-attenuation plaque, positive remodeling, noncalcified plaque volume, napkin-ring sign, and diabetes history. In the validation set, the multimodal fusion model achieved an area under the curve of 0.89 (95%CI: 0.83-0.95), outperforming the inflammation-only (0.78), CTA-only (0.83), and Logistic regression (0.72) models (all P < .05). Its accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity were 92.9%, 95.2%, and 92.3%, respectively. The fusion model showed excellent calibration (HL P = .58), the highest net benefit across threshold probabilities of 8% to 35%, and stable performance across subgroups (area under the curve 0.86-0.92). The multimodal fusion machine learning model effectively predicts rapid progression of non-target lesions after PCI, outperforming single-modality models and supporting risk stratification and individualized secondary prevention.

articles.title: Effect of inspiratory muscle training on exercise tolerance and quality of life during pulmonary rehabilitation in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.abstract: This retrospective cohort study investigates the additional effects of adding inspiratory muscle training (IMT) to a standard pulmonary rehabilitation program on exercise tolerance and quality of life in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Patients with stable COPD who completed an 8-week standard pulmonary rehabilitation program from January 2023 to December 2025 were consecutively enrolled. Based on whether they received additional IMT, they were divided into an observation group (n = 72) and a control group (n = 84). After propensity score matching, 62 patients from each group (124 in total) were included in the analysis. The observation group received threshold-loaded IMT (initial load set at 30% of maximal inspiratory pressure) in addition to the standard rehabilitation program. The primary outcomes were the 6-minute walking distance and the St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the 2 groups after matching. After 8 weeks of treatment, the improvement in 6-minute walking distance in the observation group (75.7 ± 16.2 m) was significantly greater than that in the control group (48.6 ± 16.7 m) (P = .002). The improvement in the total St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire score in the observation group (-14.0 ± 3.8 points) was also significantly superior to that in the control group (-7.1 ± 3.4 points) (P = .004), with a higher proportion of patients achieving the minimal clinically important difference (85.5% vs 67.7%, P = .006). The increase in maximal inspiratory pressure was significantly greater in the observation group (19.2 ± 3.8 cmH2O) compared to the control group (6.2 ± 2.1 cmH2O) (P < .001). The improvement in dyspnea score was more pronounced in the observation group. Subgroup analysis showed consistent benefits across patients with different characteristics. Safety and compliance were comparable between the 2 groups. For patients with COPD undergoing pulmonary rehabilitation, adding IMT to the standard program can more significantly enhance exercise tolerance, improve quality of life and dyspnea symptoms, and specifically increase inspiratory muscle strength. The benefits are consistent across patients with different characteristics, and the intervention has a good safety profile.

articles.title: Associations of personalized prenatal care with delivery and perinatal outcomes in women with high-risk pregnancies.
articles.abstract: This study examines whether the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with delivery and perinatal outcomes among women with high-risk pregnancies in a retrospective observational cohort. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 100 women with high-risk pregnancies who delivered between January 2020 and December 2023. Participants were classified according to documented receipt of personalized prenatal care or routine prenatal care. Propensity scores were estimated using maternal age, gravidity, parity, pre pregnancy or early-pregnancy body mass index, gestational age at registration, gestational diabetes mellitus, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, thyroid dysfunction, uterine scar, and history of adverse pregnancy outcomes. One-to-one nearest-neighbor matching without replacement was performed using a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score. All 100 women were retained after matching. Outcomes were analyzed using unadjusted independent-group comparisons (50 women per group). Vaginal delivery was more frequent in the personalized-care group than in the routine-care group (62.0% vs 40.0%), corresponding to an absolute difference of +22.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], +2.4- + 39.3) and an odds ratio (OR) of 2.45 (95% CI, 1.10-5.47; P = .028). Cesarean delivery occurred in 28.0% and 48.0% of women, respectively, corresponding to an absolute difference of -20.0 percentage points (95% CI, -37.1-- 1.0) and an OR of 0.42 (95% CI, 0.18-0.97). Preterm birth occurred in 10.0% versus 26.0% of women (absolute difference, -16.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -30.7- - 0.8; OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.10-0.97; P = .037). One and 5-minute Apgar scores were higher in the personalized-care group (P = .026 and P = .006, respectively). The composite adverse perinatal outcome, defined as the occurrence of at least one of preterm birth, low birth weight, neonatal asphyxia, or neonatal intensive care unit admission, occurred in 16.0% versus 36.0% of women (absolute difference, -20.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -35.8- - 2.8; OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.13-0.88; P = .023). In this study, the receipt of personalized prenatal care was associated with differences in delivery patterns, selected neonatal outcomes, nursing-compliance measures, and end-of-care psychological scores. The findings represent associations rather than causal effects and should be interpreted in light of the small sample size, residual confounding, and limited statistical power for several individual outcomes.

articles.title: Global burden of HBV/HCV-related liver diseases, 1990-2021, and projections to 2050: A global burden of disease study 2021.
articles.abstract: Despite the availability of measures to control hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related diseases, achieving elimination remains a substantial challenge. Effective action demands accurate assessment of the present and anticipation of the future. We utilized data from the Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2021 to estimate the global burden of HBV- and HCV-related diseases for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021. We defined HBV/HCV-related liver disease to include chronic hepatitis B, chronic hepatitis C, and cirrhosis attributable to chronic HBV or HCV. The burden was assessed using the age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALY rate (ASDR), stratified by region, age, sex, and Socio-demographic Index (SDI). GBD estimates were reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs); 1990 to 2021 percentage changes were calculated from point estimates. Forecasting analysis was conducted using the GBD 2021 forecast framework, supplemented by Das Gupta decomposition analysis. From 1990 to 2021, the global ASMRs of HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis declined by 41.51% and 31.47%, respectively, while liver cancer-related ASMR showed divergent changes (HBV: -16.40%; HCV: +2.35%). ASDRs also declined across both cirrhosis and liver cancer (HBV: -42.07%, -22.34%; HCV: -29.34%, -8.24%). Regionally, the highest ASMRs for chronic hepatitis B and C including cirrhosis in 2021 were observed in Eastern Sub-Saharan Africa (14.51 per 1,00,000) and Central Sub-Saharan Africa (13.92 per 1,00,000), respectively. The burden of both viruses was generally higher in men. Age-specific mortality rates were highest in older age groups across HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases. By the late 2030s, the mortality burden of chronic hepatitis C is projected to surpass that of chronic hepatitis B, amid a slowing annual decline in the ASMR of chronic hepatitis C (-1.21% to -0.24%). Although the overall burden of HBV- and HCV-related liver diseases may decrease or stabilize, sustained progress hinges on equitable access to vaccination, optimized antiviral therapies, and a renewed global focus on HCV as its relative impact grows. Achieving meaningful reductions across SDI contexts will require not only scientific advances but also strategic efforts to improve affordability and distribution, supported by the political will to implement change.

articles.title: Noonan syndrome presenting in infancy with bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Noonan syndrome (NS) is an autosomal dominant RASopathy caused by pathogenic variants in genes that regulate the rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. Hearing impairment is increasingly recognized as part of the NS phenotype and may include sensorineural hearing loss of varying severity. Severe-to-profound sensorineural hearing loss may occasionally be an early presenting feature, particularly when other manifestations are subtle.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A male infant aged 2 months and 24 days was evaluated after repeatedly failing newborn hearing screening.

DIAGNOSES: Diagnostic auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing was reported to indicate bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss; however, the original ear-specific audiological data were unavailable for independent review. The infant had poor postnatal growth, with low weight and length for age, whereas head circumference remained within the World Health Organization (WHO) reference range. No characteristic facial features were identified at the initial assessment, and echocardiography revealed no structural cardiac abnormality. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous c.182A > G (p.Asp61Gly) variant in the protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 11 gene (PTPN11). Parental Sanger sequencing did not detect the variant in either parent, supporting a de novo origin. These findings were consistent with a diagnosis of Noonan syndrome.
