INTERVENTIONS: The infant was referred to pediatric audiology for hearing-aid assessment and early auditory-verbal rehabilitation. According to parental report, hearing aids were subsequently fitted and auditory-verbal rehabilitation was initiated. Cochlear implant evaluation was under consideration because of the reported profound sensorineural hearing loss. The legal guardians also received genetic counseling regarding the diagnosis and inheritance of Noonan syndrome.

OUTCOMES: At approximately 7 months of age, the family reported ongoing hearing-aid use and auditory-verbal rehabilitation, with subjective improvement in auditory responsiveness. Cochlear implant evaluation remained under consideration. No formal post-referral records or objective audiological outcome measures were available.

LESSONS: This case illustrates that Noonan syndrome can be diagnosed in early infancy when reported profound sensorineural hearing loss is accompanied by poor growth, even when typical facial and cardiac findings are not evident at the initial evaluation.

articles.title: Nonlinear relationship between AST/ALT levels and MASLD: A secondary cross-sectional study in healthy Japanese individuals.
articles.abstract: Fatty liver disease is a prevalent condition worldwide, particularly in developed countries. Previous studies have examined the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and both metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and alcohol-associated liver disease. However, there is a scarcity of research focusing specifically on the association between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. The objective of this study is to investigate the relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD in healthy Japanese individuals. This study was a cross-sectional analysis involving 15,464 participants, comprising 7034 men and 8430 women, aged between 18 and 79 years. Data for this secondary analysis were obtained from the Dryad Digital Repository. A medical professional utilized ultrasound imaging to assess the presence of fatty liver disease and administered a questionnaire to gather information about lifestyle factors, including smoking history, alcohol consumption, and exercise habits. Hematological indicators were evaluated at Murakami Memorial Hospital from 2004 to 2015. By adjusting for sex, age, body mass index, waist circumference, regular exercise, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total cholesterol, triglycerides, HbA1c (%), alcohol consumption, smoking status, fasting plasma glucose, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, body weight, gamma-glutamyl transferase, and triglycerides, we identified a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD. This relationship exhibited a significant notable threshold at an AST/ALT ratio of 0.95, with odds ratio values of 0.03 (0.02, 0.05) when the ratio was <0.95, and 0.32 (0.22, 0.46) when the ratio was greater than or equal to 0.95. Furthermore, in subgroup analyses, we observed that the relationship between AST/ALT levels and fatty liver varied across different subgroups based on gender, alcohol consumption, and smoking status, with the exception of exercise. There is a nonlinear relationship between the AST/ALT ratio and MASLD, with a more pronounced negative correlation observed when the ratio is <0.95. These findings suggest that the AST/ALT ratio may provide supportive information for risk stratification in MASLD, particularly when interpreted in conjunction with sex and lifestyle factors. However, prospective validation of the 0.95 threshold in diverse populations is warranted before any clinical application.

articles.title: Urgent chemotherapy for advanced mediastinal malignant germ cell tumor: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Urgent chemotherapy is increasingly considered feasible for critically ill patients with hematological malignancies, although its role in solid tumors remains controversial. Primary mediastinal malignant germ cell tumors (PMMGCTs) are rare and aggressive malignancies, with limited reported cases of urgent chemotherapy in these patients.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 13-year-old boy was admitted to the hospital with chest tightness, cough, and intermittent low-grade fever.

DIAGNOSES: Computed tomography revealed a large mediastinal mass invading adjacent cardiac vessels and the anterior chest wall, along with multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. Laboratory tests showed a significant increase in serum human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) levels. Based on histopathological examination of biopsy specimens, the patient was diagnosed with advanced PMMGCT complicated by pulmonary metastases.

INTERVENTIONS: Subsequently, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit for acute heart failure and respiratory failure and received urgent BEP chemotherapy (bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin) and organ support therapy.

OUTCOMES: During subsequent treatment follow-up, the patient recovered well and achieved long-term survival.

LESSONS: This case highlights the feasibility of urgent chemotherapy for PMMGCTs complicated by organ failure, which is attributed to close collaboration between oncologists and intensivists.

articles.title: Effect modification of the association between vancomycin trough concentration and acute kidney injury: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Vancomycin exposure is associated with acute kidney injury (AKI), but the extent to which concomitant clinical factors modify this association remains uncertain. This study evaluated factors associated with vancomycin-related AKI and examined potential effect modification of the association between vancomycin trough concentration and AKI. This single-center retrospective cohort study used electronic health records of adults treated with vancomycin from January 2019 to June 2023. Factors associated with AKI were assessed using logistic regression, and interaction terms were used to evaluate whether the trough-AKI association differed according to selected comorbidities and concomitant medications. A systematic review and meta-analysis were also performed to place the cohort findings in the context of existing evidence. Among 1612 patients, 375 (23.2%) developed AKI. Higher vancomycin trough concentration, concomitant loop diuretic use, and concomitant piperacillin/tazobactam (PIP/TAZ) use were independently associated with AKI. Statistically significant interactions with trough concentration were observed for PIP/TAZ, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor/angiotensin-receptor blocker use (interaction P = .036, .023, .003, and .006, respectively). Compared with patients not receiving PIP/TAZ and with trough levels < 17 mg/L, the odds of AKI were higher among patients receiving PIP/TAZ with trough levels < 17 mg/L (odds ratio [OR]: 1.62, 95% CI: 1.42-1.85) and were highest among those receiving PIP/TAZ with trough levels ≥17 mg/L (OR: 2.03, 95% CI: 1.36-2.98). Among patients not receiving PIP/TAZ, trough levels ≥17 mg/L were associated with higher AKI odds (OR: 1.43, 95% CI: 1.26-1.63). Concomitant PIP/TAZ identified a population with increased AKI risk across trough strata, whereas the incremental association of a higher trough level was less apparent among PIP/TAZ users. These observational findings support individualized assessment of vancomycin exposure together with concurrent AKI risk factors and should not be interpreted as establishing a new therapeutic trough target.

articles.title: CT-guided intraganglionic platelet-rich plasma injection for mixed trigeminal neuropathic pain secondary to varicella-zoster virus infection: A case report.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Refractory facial pain, particularly when presenting with mixed neuropathic features following varicella-zoster virus (VZV) infection, poses a significant therapeutic challenge. Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been preliminarily used for neuropathic pain and postherpetic neuralgia in clinical practice. However, the technical feasibility and procedural details of computed tomography (CT)-guided PRP injection into the trigeminal ganglion remain underreported.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 55-year-old man presented with recurrent, severe left-sided facial pain characterized by continuous burning dysesthesia superimposed with intermittent paroxysmal electric-shock-like lancinations. He had a history of 2 prior procedures for trigeminal neuralgia (pulsed radiofrequency or radiofrequency thermocoagulation) and a history of varicella (chickenpox) infection one year prior, with subtle erythema in the left V1 dermatome noted on current evaluation.

DIAGNOSES: Mixed trigeminal neuropathic pain secondary to VZV infection.

INTERVENTIONS: Under CT guidance, 4 mL of autologous leukocyte-poor PRP (prepared from 16 mL of venous blood) was injected into the ipsilateral trigeminal ganglion via the foramen ovale.

OUTCOMES: Pain relief began 12 hours post-injection. The visual analog scale (VAS) score decreased from 8 to 9 (at onset) pretreatment to 3 to 4 at 36 hours post-treatment. This therapeutic effect was sustained through the 12-week follow-up period, with a stable VAS score of 2 to 3 and no pain provoked by daily activities. No procedure-related complications occurred.

LESSONS: CT-guided PRP injection into the trigeminal ganglion may be a technically feasible and safe minimally invasive procedure, offering an option for patients who respond poorly to conventional treatments. This case provides the procedural approach and short-term safety data for this method. The effectiveness of this method warrants further validation in larger-scale controlled studies.

articles.title: Hemoglobin glycation index and mortality in critically ill atrial fibrillation patients: A retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC‑IV database.
articles.abstract: The hemoglobin glycation index (HGI), a marker of individual glycation propensity, has demonstrated prognostic value in cardiometabolic diseases. Its association with outcomes in critically ill patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains poorly characterized, particularly over the longer term. In this retrospective cohort study, we analyzed data from 2458 ICU patients with AF in the MIMIC-IV database. HGI was calculated as the difference between measured glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and the value predicted from fasting plasma glucose. The primary endpoints were 30-day and 365-day all-cause mortality. We employed Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, restricted mean survival time (RMST), and restricted cubic splines. Subgroup analyses were exploratory. Prespecified sensitivity analyses addressed bias via exclusion of continuous enteral/parenteral nutrition or dextrose fluids, restriction of HbA1c to within 7 days, exclusion of recent transfusion or extreme hemoglobin, and a lipid complete-case analysis. The analysis revealed a reverse J-shaped relationship between HGI and all-cause mortality. Patients in the lowest HGI quartile (Q1) faced the highest risk of death across all time points. RMST was significantly shorter in Q1 versus Q2. Adjusted spline curves confirmed this nonlinear association, with inflection points at HGI values of -0.54 (30-day) and -0.65 (365-day). In the fully adjusted model, the Q2 versus Q1 hazard ratio (HR) was 0.704 (95% CI: 0.530-0.933) for 30-day and 0.714 (0.552-0.924) for 365-day mortality. Directionally consistent estimates were observed across all sensitivity analyses, for example, excluding enteral/parenteral nutrition [0.641 (0.464-0.885)], restricting HbA1c to 7 days [0.611 (0.408-0.913)], excluding transfusion/extreme hemoglobin [0.713 (0.527-0.964)], and lipid complete-case [0.647 (0.455-0.920)]. Subgroup analyses did not identify significant effect modification after FDR correction; however, these analyses were underpowered. In this MIMIC-IV cohort of critically ill AF patients, HGI exhibits a reverse J-shaped association with mortality, indicating that low HGI, and to a lesser extent high HGI, may identify higher-risk phenotypes. These findings require external validation and should not be interpreted causally. Integrating HGI into initial metabolic profiling could enhance risk stratification and inform personalized monitoring strategies in the ICU, pending prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Reconsider the diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia: A case report of tracheobronchial tuberculosis.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is transmitted through respiratory droplets, with an incubation period of 1 to 3 weeks. This bacterium is globally endemic, with infections peaking in summer and early fall. Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) poses a major global health issue, often requiring computed tomography for detection of subtle lesions. Targeted treatment for single-pathogen infections usually shows significant improvement within about a week, but the rise of mixed infections complicates clinical management.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 25-year-old male presented with a 2-month duration of intermittent cough and 3 days of shortness of breath and fever.

DIAGNOSES: Lab results showed a slightly elevated white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, and C-reactive protein. An anti-M pneumoniae immunoglobulin M test was positive, suggesting M pneumoniae infection and serving as the basis for the initial diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia. The patient was subsequently treated with levofloxacin. However, his condition worsened, leading to bronchoscopy, which revealed a positive sputum acid-fast bacilli smear and Mycobacterium tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction. He was subsequently diagnosed with tracheobronchial TB.

INTERVENTIONS: The patient received empirical levofloxacin for 5 days. Because his symptoms worsened, bronchoscopy was performed, and after a positive acid-fast bacilli smear and M tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction, standard anti-TB therapy with isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide was started.

OUTCOMES: Cough improved transiently on levofloxacin but recurred with paroxysmal exacerbations and night sweats. After anti-TB therapy, cough and fever resolved, and follow-up computed tomography 6 months later showed marked resolution of the bronchial luminal narrowing and deformity.

LESSONS: Radiologic manifestations of tracheobronchial TB vary with host factors, and diagnosis involves multiple pathological considerations, especially if other organisms are present alongside M tuberculosis.

articles.title: Metastatic G2 laryngeal neuroendocrine tumor treated with sulfatinib and sintilimab: A case report and literature review.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Laryngeal neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies with limited evidence guiding the management of metastatic disease. We report a metastatic G2 laryngeal NET initially presenting as an unusual temporal subcutaneous metastasis and subsequently treated with combined targeted therapy and immunotherapy.

PATIENT CONCERNS: A 63-year-old man with a history of invasive lung adenocarcinoma presented with a 1.3 × 1.2 cm left temporal subcutaneous nodule and a history of hoarseness accompanied by throat pain.

DIAGNOSES: Histopathological examination of the temporal lesion suggested metastatic NET. Subsequent PET-CT, laryngoscopy, and biopsy identified a primary laryngeal NET. After vertical partial laryngectomy, right neck dissection, and laryngeal function reconstruction, pathology confirmed a well-differentiated G2 NET with cervical lymph-node and temporal subcutaneous metastases, classified as pT2N1M1, stage IVC. In March 2025, hepatic metastases were pathologically confirmed. Molecular profiling identified HRAS p.Q61L, KDR p.S265L, and ROS1 p.S615Y variants, microsatellite instability-high status, and programmed death-ligand 1expression with a combined positive score of 70.

INTERVENTIONS: Combination therapy with sulfatinib (300 mg/day) and sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks) was initiated in April 2025 and continued without dose reduction, interruption, or delay.

OUTCOMES: After 10 months of combination therapy, contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a reduction in the size of hepatic metastatic lesions compared with baseline, together with a marked decrease in the number of metastatic lesions. The largest index hepatic lesion decreased from 32.68 mm to 19.05 mm in maximal diameter, corresponding to a 41.7% reduction, demonstrating a marked radiological reduction in hepatic metastatic burden. At the latest documented assessment in February 2026, no further disease progression or treatment-related adverse events were observed.

LESSONS: This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of metastatic laryngeal NET with an unusual subcutaneous presentation. Comprehensive pathological and molecular evaluation may aid treatment decision-making in advanced disease. The observed disease control with sulfatinib plus sintilimab is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in additional patients.

articles.title: Causal associations between immune cell traits and hip osteoarthritis: A bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Observational studies have reported associations between immune cell phenotypes and hip osteoarthritis (HOA), but whether these associations are causal is unknown. We, therefore, used bidirectional 2-sample mendelian randomization (MR) to examine potential causal associations between 731 immune cell traits and HOA risk. Genome-Wide Association Study summary data for 731 immune cell traits were obtained from the genome-wide association study catalog, and HOA summary data were derived from the FinnGen Consortium. Instrumental variables were selected using significance thresholds of P < 1 × 10-5 for immune traits and P < 5 × 10-8 for HOA. The primary analysis used inverse variance weighted (IVW) MR, complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode methods. Sensitivity analyses included Cochran Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, mendelian randomization pleiotropy residual sum and outlier test, and leave-one-out analysis. False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple testing. In the forward MR analysis, IVW identified 17 immune traits with FDR-significant associations with HOA risk (FDR < 0.05). Six CD33-expressing myeloid cell traits showed positive associations with HOA risk (odds ratio = 1.02, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.03 for all), while eleven immune traits including T cell, B cell, Natural Killer cell, regulatory T cell , and conventional dendritic cell phenotypes showed inverse associations (odds ratio range: 0.90-0.97), suggesting a potential protective role. Sensitivity analyses did not detect significant heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy for any of these 17 associations (all MR-Egger intercept P > .05; all Cochran's Q P > .05). Weighted median estimates were directionally concordant with IVW for all 17 traits, and every association met the prespecified cross-method consistency criterion (at least three of 5 methods directionally concordant). In the reverse MR analysis, 19 immune traits showed nominal associations (P < .05); however, none survived FDR correction (FDR > 0.05), providing no robust evidence for causal effects of HOA on immune cell composition. This MR study provides genetic evidence linking CD33-related myeloid traits and multiple lymphoid and monocyte phenotypes to HOA risk. These associations are statistical and do not establish biological mechanisms. Future experimental and clinical studies are needed to determine whether these immune phenotypes contribute to HOA pathophysiology.

articles.title: The causal relationship between frailty and pneumonia: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological studies have revealed a relationship between frailty and pneumonia; however, the causal relationship remains controversial. This study aims to explore this relationship through Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. This study utilized large-scale genome-wide association summary data to evaluate the potential causal relationship between frailty and pneumonia through two-sample bidirectional MR analysis. The inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method was employed as the primary approach, and the robustness of the results was validated using Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger regression intercept test, and MR-PRESSO test. In the forward MR analysis, the IVW results indicated that a 1-unit increase in genetically predicted frailty on the quantile-normalized frailty-index scale was associated with higher odds of all pneumonia (odds ratio [OR] = 1.295, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.151-1.457, P < .001), bacterial pneumonia (OR = 1.346, 95% CI = 1.095-1.655, P = .005), and asthma-related pneumonia (OR = 2.044, 95% CI = 1.588-2.631, P < .001). There was no causal association between frailty and viral pneumonia (OR = 1.719, 95% CI = 0.882-3.349, P = .112); sensitivity analysis showed no heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy (P > .05). In the reverse MR analysis, the IVW random-effects model results indicated a causal association between asthma-related pneumonia and frailty (OR = 1.039, 95% CI = 1.014-1.065, P = .002). No causal associations were detected between all pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, or viral pneumonia and frailty (P > .05). Heterogeneity was detected in the reverse analysis of asthma-related pneumonia, whereas the MR-Egger intercept tests provided no evidence of directional horizontal pleiotropy in the examined analyses (P > .05). This study demonstrates that frailty has a causal association with all pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and asthma-related pneumonia. The reverse MR results indicate that asthma-related pneumonia also increases the risk of frailty.

articles.title: Comparing outcomes of trigger finger release in patients with and without diabetes mellitus: A meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Diabetes increases the risk of developing trigger digits and may predispose patients to poorer clinical outcomes and a higher incidence of complications. However, conflicting results have been reported regarding surgical outcomes of trigger finger release in patients with diabetes compared to those without. We aimed to evaluate the association between diabetes and surgical outcomes of trigger finger release in terms of symptoms, complications, and patient satisfaction. A comprehensive search of the PubMed, Cochrane Library, and EMBASE databases was conducted to identify relevant comparative studies on complications and surgical outcomes following trigger finger release in diabetic and nondiabetic patients. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were evaluated to compare the risks of wound complications, persistent or recurrent symptoms, and overall satisfaction between the 2 groups. Overall, 1 prospective and 13 retrospective observational studies involving 5144 participants were included. A pooled analysis demonstrated a significantly higher risk of wound complications in patients with diabetes compared to those without (6.3% vs 2.5%; OR = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.60-3.31). Patients with diabetes were also more likely to experience persistent or recurrent symptoms after trigger finger release (19.4% vs 9.2%; OR = 2.84, 95% CI = 1.88-4.29). While overall satisfaction was high in both groups, satisfaction was significantly lower among diabetic patients (91.5% vs 96.2%; OR = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.27- 0.92). Patients with diabetes undergoing trigger finger release had higher odds of postoperative wound complications and persistent or recurrent symptoms. Although the overall satisfaction levels were high in both the diabetic and nondiabetic groups, diabetic patients reported lower satisfaction than nondiabetic patients.

articles.title: Navigating stress in a changing society: A cross-sectional study of coping mechanisms and mental health among Saudi youth.
articles.abstract: Mental health challenges among youth are growing globally, particularly in rapidly changing societies such as Saudi Arabia. This study examined the relationship between coping mechanisms and mental health among Saudi youth aged 16 to 30 years in Riyadh. A cross-sectional quantitative design was used. Data were collected digitally through a self-administered questionnaire distributed via educational and community platforms. A total of 450 participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The Brief Coping Orientation to Problems Experienced Inventory and Mental Health Continuum-Short Form were used to assess coping strategies and mental health, respectively. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, t-tests, analysis of variance, and Pearson correlation, with statistical significance set at P < .05. Participants demonstrated a moderate level of coping (mean = 2.41) and low mental health status (mean = 2.29). Problem-focused coping was significantly associated with emotional, psychological, and social well-being, whereas emotion-focused coping was significantly associated with social well-being and overall mental health, but not with emotional or psychological well-being. Avoidant coping was not significantly associated with mental health outcomes. Gender differences emerged, with males reporting higher avoidant coping. Psychological well-being showed the strongest correlation with overall mental health compared with emotional and social well-being. In conclusion, although Saudi youth demonstrated moderate coping skills, their overall mental health remains a concern. Problem-focused coping was positively associated with mental well-being, while emotion-focused coping showed more limited positive associations. Avoidant coping was not significantly associated with mental health outcomes. These findings highlight the need for culturally relevant interventions and programs in schools and communities that promote adaptive coping and resilience among youth.

articles.title: Self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination: An exploratory cross-sectional survey in Egypt.
articles.abstract: Peripheral neurological manifestations have been reported following Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection, whereas neuropathic symptoms after COVID-19 vaccination remain less well characterized. To evaluate self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination and identify factors associated with postvaccination symptom reporting, while accounting for previous confirmed COVID-19 infection. This cross-sectional survey included adults recruited from university-affiliated settings. Data were collected using a structured English/Arabic questionnaire covering COVID-19 infection, vaccination history, comorbidities, medication use, and neuropathic symptoms, including tingling, numbness, burning sensation, and electric shock-like sensations. Participants who reported symptoms were invited for neurological clinical assessment. The primary outcome was self-reported neuropathic symptoms potentially suggestive of peripheral neuropathy following COVID-19 vaccination. Previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was treated as a potential confounder in multivariable analysis. A total of 1201 individuals were screened, of whom 1166 were included in the final analysis. Postvaccination self-reported neuropathic symptoms were reported by 472 of 1090 vaccinated participants (43.3%). Following the first vaccine dose, symptom reporting differed significantly by vaccine type (P < .001), with the highest proportions observed among recipients of Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (190/316 [60.1%]) and Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine (37/92 [40.2%]). In multivariable analysis, older age, use of medications with reported or potential associations with peripheral neuropathy, and receipt of ChAdOx1-S, Gam-COVID-Vac, or Sinovac-CoronaVac were associated with increased post-vaccination symptom reporting (P < .05), whereas previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was not independently associated with the outcome. In exploratory booster-dose analysis, homologous booster vaccination was associated with lower odds of symptom reporting than heterologous boosting (adjusted odds ratio 0.38, P < .001). Self-reported neuropathic symptoms were frequently reported following COVID-19 vaccination and varied according to vaccine type. Older age, selected vaccine types, and heterologous booster schedules were associated with symptom reporting. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously because they reflect self-reported symptoms rather than confirmed peripheral neuropathy diagnoses and were not routinely confirmed by objective neurological investigations.

articles.title: Effects of a 12-week multi-strain probiotics supplementation on circulating endotoxin and antioxidant enzymes among overweight/obese Saudi adults: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several clinical trials have indicated the favorable effects of probiotics in lowering the risk of chronic diseases such as obesity; however, few of them have explored the potential in altering obesity-related biomarkers, and the present study aimed to fill this gap.

METHODS: A total of 93 overweight/obese adults (males and females, aged 19-40 years) were recruited at the clinical facility of King Saud University Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between March 2022 and January 2023 in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trial. In this study, the subjects were randomly assigned to receive 30 × 109 colony-forming units HEXBIO® containing 3 Bifidobacterium and 3 Lactobacillus species (N = 44; 64% subjects) or a placebo containing the same excipients without the live bacterial strains (N = 49; 76% subjects); all subjects consumed the product twice daily for 3 months.

RESULTS: At baseline, anthropometric measurements, the liver profile, and antioxidant enzymes did not differ significantly between the probiotic and placebo groups. Following the 12-week intervention, within-group analysis revealed significant increases in the levels of superoxide dismutase (0.06 ± 0.1 vs 0.19 ± 0.29 U/mL; P = .02) and glutathione peroxidase (GPX1; 0.66 ± 0.23 vs 0.76 ± 0.2; P = .01) among all probiotic-supplemented subjects. After stratification by sex, significant favorable changes in superoxide dismutase (0.03 ± 0.04 vs 0.29 ± 0.4; P = .05) and GPX1 (0.66 ± 0.26 vs 0.82 ± 0.18; P = .03) were observed only in the male probiotics group, and between-group comparisons showed a modest but clinically significant difference only in GPX1 in favor of the probiotics group (P = .04). These changes were not observed in females. No differences were observed in the levels of endotoxins and liver enzymes over time in both groups.

CONCLUSION: The administration of multi-strain probiotic supplements for 3 months, along with dietary intervention, was associated with a modest favorable change in GPX1 levels in males, with no apparent changes in circulating endotoxins or liver enzymes. These findings suggest a potential sex-specific effect of probiotic supplementation on antioxidant defense. However, results should be interpreted cautiously given the modest effect. Adequately powered clinical trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Non-linear association between enteral nutrition initiation time and sepsis-associated delirium: A retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC-III database.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated delirium (SAD) is a common and critical complication in sepsis patients. Early enteral nutrition is recommended for sepsis patients, yet the relationship between enteral nutrition (EN) initiation time and SAD incidence remains unclear. This study aimed to explore this relationship. The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III database was queried to identify sepsis patients who had received EN during their intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Multivariable logistic regression explored the relationship between EN initiation time and SAD incidence. Restricted cubic spline depicted the correlation shape. Subgroup and interaction analyses evaluated the robustness. Exploratory decomposition analysis was used to decompose this association. 2431 patients were enrolled. Multivariable logistic regression showed that EN initiation time was associated with SAD incidence (Tertile 2: odds ratio = 1.363, 95% confidence interval: 1.004-1.857, P = .048; Tertile 3: odds ratio = 1.452, 95% confidence interval: 1.06-1.994, P = .021). The trend test was significant (P for trend = .023). Restricted cubic spline demonstrated a nonlinear relationship between EN initiation time and SAD incidence (P-overall = 0.014, P for nonlinear = 0.01). No interactions were detected between EN initiation time and any subgroup. Exploratory decomposition analysis indicated that the duration of vasopressor use (P = .014), hospital (P = .024)/ICU (P = .034) length of stay, and mean levels of platelet count (P = .02) and mean anion gap (P < .001) during the first 3 days of ICU admission statistically accounted for a portion of the observed association between EN initiation time and SAD incidence. Earlier EN initiation showed a nonlinear association with lower SAD incidence. This relationship was partially accounted for by differences in duration of vasopressor use, hospital/ICU length of stay, platelet, and anion gap. Due to the observational nature of this study, these findings are exploratory and do not establish causation. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether this association is causal and to establish the optimal timing of enteral nutrition initiation.

articles.title: The trends and hotspots of research on polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents over the past three decades: A bibliometric analysis from 1995 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine and metabolic disorder affecting women, with increasing research attention directed toward adolescent populations. However, no comprehensive bibliometric analysis has systematically mapped the research landscape in this subspecialty. This study aimed to evaluate global research trends and hotspots in adolescent PCOS over the past 3 decades using bibliometric methods.

METHODS: Publications on adolescent PCOS from 1995 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer and Citespace were employed for data analysis and visualization, while key bibliometric indicators were computed and presented in tabular form.

RESULTS: A total of 1070 publications were included. Research output steadily increased over time, with the United States (n = 384, 35.89%), Turkey (n = 105, 9.81%), and India (n = 82, 7.66%) being the most productive countries. The most prominent institutions included the University of Pittsburgh, the University of Barcelona, and Monash University. Ibanez, Lourdes (n = 34) was the most prolific author, while the Journal of Pediatric and Adolescent Gynecology (n = 84) and the Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism (highest citations, n = 6921) were the leading publication platforms. Core research areas encompassed mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment, metabolism, and clinical outcomes. Keyword burst detection identified "diagnosis" (strength = 14.12) and "luteinizing hormone" (strength = 13.6) as the most intense hotspots. Notably, "quality of life" (2020-2024) and "depression" (2015-2024) emerged as the most recent and ongoing research frontiers.

CONCLUSION: This first bibliometric analysis of adolescent PCOS reveals growing global interest and active international collaborations in this field. Future research is expected to focus on refining diagnostic approaches and improving long-term quality of life for adolescent PCOS.

articles.title: Prognostic biomarkers for tongue squamous cell carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying prognostic biomarkers for tongue squamous cell carcinoma (TSCC) is crucial for predicting tumor behavior and guiding treatment strategies.

METHODS: This study was conducted using databases such as SCOPUS, Ovid Medline, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library for literature published examining the prognostic significance of immunohistochemical markers in TSCC. Five biomarkers with the most research were subjected to a literature quality assessment, and their overall survival was evaluated with effect size assessment and heterogeneity testing.

RESULTS: Ultimately, 22 articles were included in the meta-statistical analysis. Depending on whether the overall effect of 95% confidence interval intersects at the zero line, the results of this study show that the total effect scale of p53 (I2 = 57.8%, P = .069), E-cadherin (I2 = 32.8%, P = .203), and vascular endothelial growth factors (I2 = 0.0%, P = .912) is statistically significant, while p16 (I2 = 88.8%, P < .000) and Ki-67 (I2 = 0.6%, P = .412) do not show a statistically significant total effect scale in TSCC. Quality problems related to noncompliance with commentary guidelines exist in published research literature.

CONCLUSION: Although several biomarkers have been proposed as potential prognostic indicators for TSCC, the overall quality of the original studies and their reporting precludes definitive conclusions. Our findings suggest that p53, E-cadherin, and VEGF-C may be associated with overall survival in TSCC, but these results should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating given the predominance of unadjusted analyses and methodological heterogeneity across studies. Rigorous prospective studies with standardized protocols and multivariable adjustment are urgently needed to validate these biomarkers before clinical translation.

articles.title: Evaluating healthcare services in Saudi Arabia's private sector from patients' perspectives: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patient satisfaction is a key indicator of healthcare quality and has become increasingly important as the private sector grows under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030. Nonetheless, evidence on satisfaction with private healthcare remains fragmented.

METHODS: This systematic review examined patients' experiences and satisfaction with private healthcare services in Saudi Arabia. Articles were retrieved from PubMed, EBSCOhost via the Saudi Digital Library, and Google Scholar. Peer-reviewed studies published in English between January 2015 and January 2025 that assessed patients' experiences and satisfaction with private healthcare services were included. Dissertations, conference papers, and commentary letters were excluded. Study characteristics and findings were extracted, and recurring factors associated with patient satisfaction were grouped into broader categories.

RESULTS: Twelve studies met the eligibility criteria. The review identified recurring factors associated with patient satisfaction in private healthcare settings, including waiting time and service promptness, explanation of medical conditions or treatments, staff attitudes, accessibility of services, appointment availability, physician competence, facility environment, medication availability, and technical quality of care. Although studies emphasized different factors to varying degrees, the findings highlighted the importance of both service efficiency and quality of care.

CONCLUSION: This review provides a structured overview of patient satisfaction in the Saudi private healthcare sector. The findings highlight the importance of improving service efficiency, communication, accessibility, and quality of care. These insights can support policymakers and healthcare providers in strengthening patient-centered services amid ongoing healthcare transformation and private-sector expansion under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030.

articles.title: Prognostic impact of serum phosphorus and inflammatory indices on outcomes in critically ill oldest-old patients: A retrospective observational study.
articles.abstract: The elderly (≥ 85 years) represent the fastest-growing demographic group among critically ill patients. However, prognostic tools tailored for this population are limited. This study aimed to investigate the prognostic utility of serum phosphorus levels and inflammation-based indices in predicting in-hospital mortality, 30-day readmission, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay in critically ill patients aged ≥ 85 years. This retrospective observational study included 491 patients aged ≥ 85 years who were admitted to the ICU between January 2016 and December 2022. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory data were extracted, and a comprehensive panel of inflammation-based indices was calculated, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), multiple inflammatory indices (MII-1, 2, 3), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation. The patients were stratified into hypophosphatemia (< 2.5 mg/dL), normophosphatemia (2.5-4.5 mg/dL), and hyperphosphatemia (> 4.5 mg/dL) groups. Regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed to determine the predictive performance of all markers. Hyperphosphatemia was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 1.90; P = .07), whereas hypoalbuminemia (adjusted OR: 0.42; P < .001) and elevated CRP (adjusted OR: 1.02; P < .001) were strong predictors of all outcomes. Among inflammation-based indices, MII-3 and NLR demonstrated the highest predictive value for mortality (AUC: 0.64 and 0.65, respectively), while serum phosphorus offered high specificity (85%) despite moderate sensitivity (35%). Inflammatory markers were less predictive of 30-day readmission (best AUC, 0.55 NLR). MII-3 was the most effective index for predicting prolonged ICU length of stay (AUC: 0.66), followed by MII-2 (AUC: 0.64) and CRP (AUC: 0.61). Both serum phosphorus levels and inflammation-based indices, particularly MII-3 and NLR, provided independent prognostic values for mortality and ICU resource use in extremely elderly ICU patients. These readily available biomarkers may support early risk stratification and ICU triage decisions in geriatric critical care, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Prospective validation and integration of composite decision-support tools are warranted.

articles.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.

METHODS: The data are derived from the Web of Science Core Collection and the PubMed database, covering relevant literature on asthma during pregnancy. The time range is from 2008 to 2024. The search strategy combined asthma-related terms ("asthma" OR "bronchial asthma") with pregnancy-related terms ("pregnancy" OR "gestation" OR "gestational"). After screening, 4088 eligible publications were included in the bibliometric analysis. A separate search of PubMed identified 28 clinical trials for the supplementary analysis of clinical research progress. Bibliometric analyses and visualization were performed using the bibliometrix R package (developed by Massimo Aria and Corrado Cuccurullo, Department of Economics and Statistics, University of Naples Federico II [with an academic spin-off, K-Synth Srl, associated with its dissemination]), CiteSpace (developed by Chaomei Chen, College of Computing and Informatics, Drexel University), and VOSviewer (developed by Nees Jan van Eck and Ludo Waltman, Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Leiden University).

RESULTS: This study comprised 4088 publications focusing on asthma during pregnancy. Annual publication counts demonstrated a gradual increase with intermittent fluctuations. The United States dominated both in publication output and international collaboration. Litonjua AA, Bisgaard H, and Weiss ST demonstrated high centrality and citation influence among authors. The core contributing journals included Pediatric Allergy and Immunology and Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. Major research focuses encompassed mechanistic exploration, influencing factors, and fetal and child health. Research hotspots were primarily concentrated on "air pollution," "birth cohort," "pregnancy complications," and "maternal diet." In recent years, emerging research frontiers have included "inflammation," "impact," "gut microbiota," "climate change," and "survivors." Clinical trial analysis highlighted nutritional interventions (particularly vitamin D) and precision management using biomarkers like fractional exhaled nitric oxide as current research priorities.

CONCLUSION: This work examined the evolving trends and trajectories within pregnancy asthma research, offering a systematic roadmap for subsequent studies. The article highlighted the main contributors, research hotspots, emerging frontier topics, and key directions for future research. This study can serve as a crucial reference for researchers in this field and relevant stakeholders.

articles.title: Effects of Chinese herbal medicine with hCG on luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluated the clinical efficacy and ovarian hemodynamic effects of adjunctive Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) combined with human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) versus hCG alone in infertile women with luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome (LUFS).

METHODS: Seven electronic databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data) were searched from inception through October 6, 2024. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 (Cochrane Risk of Bias Tool for Randomized Trials) tool and modified Jadad scale. The primary outcome was ultrasound-confirmed ovulation rate; secondary outcomes included clinical pregnancy rate, ovarian artery pulsatility index (PI), and resistance index (RI). Dichotomous outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using the Mantel-Haenszel method, whereas continuous outcomes were pooled as weighted mean differences (WMDs) using the inverse-variance method, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and Cochran Q-test, and publication bias using Begg and Egger tests. The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025637729).

RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs were included in the review. After exclusion of Zhang LX 2015, the ovulation analysis included 16 RCTs and showed a higher ovulation rate with CHM plus hCG than with hCG alone (RR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.37-1.59; P < .001; I2 = 2%). The combined intervention was also associated with a higher clinical pregnancy rate (RR 2.01, 95% CI: 1.62-2.49; P < .001; I2 = 61%; 15 RCTs). Ovarian artery PI (WMD - 0.49, 95% CI: -0.81 to -0.17; P = .002; I2 = 52%) and RI (WMD - 0.18, 95% CI: -0.31 to -0.06; P = .005; I2 = 78%) were lower with combined treatment, although each analysis included only 2 RCTs. Tests for funnel plot asymmetry were not statistically significant for ovulation rate (Begg P = .260; Egger P = .080). Interpretation was limited by methodological weaknesses, variation in CHM regimens, and sparse evidence for hemodynamic outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Adjunctive CHM may enhance ovulation and clinical pregnancy rates and improve ovarian arterial hemodynamics in infertile women with LUFS. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given methodological limitations, heterogeneous herbal regimens, and sparse hemodynamic data. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs using standardized CHM formulations and live birth as a primary endpoint are warranted to confirm these findings.

articles.title: The impact of demographic variables and personality characteristics on nurse compassion fatigue: A cross-sectional analysis during and following the COVID-19 pandemic.
articles.abstract: Compassion fatigue can undermine nurses' work efficiency, care quality, and well-being, and its correlates among nurses warrant further investigation. To examine compassion fatigue among nurses during and after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, identify its demographic and personality correlates, and provide evidence to inform mitigation strategies. This study was conducted using a survey that included a basic information questionnaire and two validated instruments: the Chinese Compassion Fatigue Short Scale and the brief version of the Chinese Neuroticism Extraversion Openness Five-Factor Inventory. The sampling frame for this study consisted of nurses working at a tertiary hospital between 2022 and 2024, and a convenience sampling approach was used for data collection and analysis. Independent cross-sectional samples were surveyed at two time points (during and following the coronavirus disease 2019 [COVID-19] pandemic). For each round, 360 questionnaires were issued, resulting in 335 valid returns (93.1% valid response rate) in the first survey and 332 valid returns (92.2% valid response rate) in the second survey, yielding an overall valid response rate of 92.6%. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical regression. The average compassion fatigue score was 54.87 ± 23.81. Age, working years, professional title, income, and department influence compassion fatigue. The COVID-19 pandemic also significantly impacts it. Nurses reported a higher compassion fatigue score during the COVID-19 pandemic than following it (P < .05). The total score negatively correlates with extraversion(β=-.014, P > .05), openness(β=-.045, P > .05), agreeableness(β=-.293, P < .01), and positively with conscientiousness(β = .041, P > .05) and neuroticism(β=-.014, P < .01). After adjusting for demographic variables, only Neuroticism and Agreeableness were significantly associated with compassion fatigue among nurses, with the personality traits collectively accounting for an additional 50.6% of variance (ΔR2 = .506; total R2 = .553). Specifically, higher neuroticism increased the risk, whereas higher agreeableness appeared to be a protective factor. Based on these demographic and personality findings, nursing managers can implement tailored interventions to alleviate compassion fatigue.

articles.title: Observed pathogen- and species-specific proportions of diagnosed infective endocarditis among bloodstream infection cases: A 10-year retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) remains associated with high mortality despite advances in diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE among bloodstream infection (BSI) cases may vary according to the causative pathogen; however, pathogen- and species-specific data remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including 5816 cases of true BSI at a tertiary care hospital in Japan between April 2015 and March 2025. Eighty cases were diagnosed with definite IE according to the modified Duke criteria. Echocardiography was performed according to clinical judgment and was not systematically mandated for all BSI cases. Pathogen- and species-specific observed proportions of diagnosed IE and factors associated with in-hospital mortality were evaluated. The overall in-hospital mortality was 17.5% and was higher among cases with Staphylococcus aureus IE (39.1%). In an exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression analysis adjusted for age only, S. aureus infection was associated with in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratios, 5.697; 95% CI, 1.635-19.850), although the estimate was imprecise. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE varied according to pathogen and species. Among streptococci, relatively high proportions were observed for Streptococcus mitis (23.5%, 4/17; 95% confidence intervals (CI), 6.8-49.9), Streptococcus oralis (23.5%, 4/17; 95% CI, 6.8-49.9), and Streptococcus gallolyticus (22.2%, 4/18; 95% CI, 6.4-47.6). The observed proportions were 3.7% for S. aureus and 6.4% for Enterococcus faecalis. The observed proportion of diagnosed IE differed according to the causative pathogen and species. Despite the relatively low observed proportion of diagnosed IE in S. aureus bacteremia, in-hospital mortality among cases with S. aureus IE was high. Because echocardiography was not systematically performed, these estimates may underestimate the underlying frequency of IE. These findings should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating, and further validation in cohorts with systematic echocardiographic assessment is warranted.

articles.title: A Simple Clinical Score for Predicting Curve Progression to the Bracing Threshold in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective longitudinal cohort study.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a simple, clinically applicable scoring system to predict progression to the bracing threshold before skeletal maturity in patients with mild adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS).

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: AIS frequently presents with mild curves below the bracing threshold. Although most patients are initially managed through observation, a subset of patients progresses to require brace treatment during growth to skeletal maturity. However, a prediction model to guide early risk stratification and follow-up strategies is lacking.

METHODS: We included East Asian female patients aged ≥10 years with AIS who presented with major Cobb angles of ≥10° and <25° at baseline. Patients were followed until progression to ≥25° or attainment of skeletal maturity (Risser sign of 4-5 with <1 cm growth within 6 months and ≥2 years post-menarche). A prediction score for progression to ≥25° before skeletal maturity was developed using multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination based on the Bayesian Information Criterion. Model performance was evaluated, and internal validation was performed with 1000 bootstrap resamples. Results were validated using a separate cohort from the same source population.

RESULTS: In the final model, initial Cobb angle ≥20°, Risser sign 0-2, and time from menarche were retained. The resulting score ranged from 0 to 6 points. The model demonstrated discriminative ability, with optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.833 (development cohort) and 0.867 (validation cohort). Calibration was satisfactory, and decision curve analysis demonstrated clinical utility across a wide range of threshold probabilities. The score stratified patients into low-, moderate-, and high-risk groups with progressively increasing rates of curve progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Our simple scoring system uses readily available clinical variables to predict progression to the bracing threshold in female patients with mild AIS. This tool enables early risk stratification and may guide individualized follow-up strategies and timely clinical decision-making before brace initiation.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Long-term metformin therapy and risk of anemia in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Metformin is the cornerstone therapy for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and is prescribed long term to large patient populations, making its potential hematological effects clinically relevant. Particular attention has focused on metformin-associated vitamin B12 deficiency and its possible contribution to anemia. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that metformin reduces serum vitamin B12 concentrations and increases the risk of biochemical deficiency, particularly with higher doses and prolonged treatment. However, its overall effects on hemoglobin levels and anemia risk remain modest and variable across clinical populations. Importantly, anemia in patients with T2D is multifactorial and may result from chronic kidney disease, iron deficiency, systemic inflammation, blood loss, or other nutritional deficiencies, complicating the identification of metformin's independent contribution. Although vitamin B12 depletion represents a plausible mechanism linking metformin exposure to hematological abnormalities, additional metabolic and clinical factors may influence erythropoiesis and hemoglobin homeostasis. Furthermore, longer treatment duration and greater cumulative exposure may increase the likelihood of vitamin B12 deficiency, highlighting the importance of appropriate clinical surveillance. Accordingly, this narrative review critically examines the relationship between long-term metformin therapy and anemia risk in patients with T2D, with particular emphasis on vitamin B12 depletion, alterations in hemoglobin levels, and potential underlying mechanisms. It further explores the influence of treatment duration and dosage, identifies patient-related and disease-associated risk factors, and evaluates evidence-based approaches to early detection, prevention, monitoring, and management of hematological complications. Understanding these associations may help optimize long-term metformin therapy while minimizing preventable hematological adverse effects without compromising its established metabolic benefits.

articles.title: Integrating distributed lag non-linear models and deep learning reveals meteorological drivers of influenza A and B positivity in a 6-year subtropical surveillance study.
articles.abstract: Subtropical influenza forecasting is complicated by non-linear meteorological dynamics and surveillance bias stemming from pandemic-era testing fluctuations. Existing approaches either characterize lagged environmental associations without forecasting capacity or apply deep learning without epidemiological interpretability. We analyzed multisite influenza surveillance data from Putian, southeastern China (2018-2023); test positivity was the primary outcome to mitigate testing-related bias. Distributed lag nonlinear models estimated type-specific associations between eight meteorological variables and positivity over a 15-day lag window. A Bayesian-optimized long short-term memory (LSTM) network incorporating meteorological, autoregressive, and socio-behavioral covariates was benchmarked against covariate-matched multivariate autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models. For influenza A, the temperature-associated relative risk (RR) peaked at 15°C (3.01; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.03-8.78), and positivity was associated with narrow diurnal temperature ranges. Influenza B positivity was associated with colder conditions (8°C; RR = 26.12, 95% CI: 7.79-87.61), higher humidity (91%; RR = 1.52, 95% CI: 1.00-2.29), and lower solar radiation. The LSTM had lower mean absolute error for influenza A (0.009 vs 0.136 for ARIMA and 0.138 for XGBoost) and B (0.002 vs 0.049 and 0.070); symmetric mean absolute percentage error was 0.521 vs 1.212 and 1.081 for A and 0.484 vs 0.810 and 0.737 for B. Covariate ablation and Shapley additive explanations analyses suggested that historical positivity and testing-related variables contributed to forecast stability. External validation in Sanming provided preliminary evidence of regional portability. This framework combines interpretable meteorological associations with short-horizon forecasting under variable surveillance conditions.

articles.title: JUVENILE IDIOPATHIC ARTHRITIS IN CHILDREN WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES: IMPACT OF CURRENT MEDICAL TREATMENT OPTIONS ON ANTHROPOMETRY AND METABOLIC CONTROL.
articles.abstract: Children with both type 1 diabetes (T1D) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) face increased disease complexity due to overlapping autoimmune and inflammatory processes. This study aimed to assess anthropometric, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk factors compared to children with T1D alone. Data from the Diabetes Patient Follow-up (DPV) registry (1995-2023) were analyzed, comparing 489 children with T1D and JIA to 67,462 children with T1D only. Children with T1D and JIA used diabetes technologies (insulin pumps, CGM, AID systems) more frequently with similar HbA1c levels. Between 2014-2019 and 2020-2023, HbA1c levels significantly improved in the JIA group, while BMI and height approached the T1D only group. Despite increased disease burden, children with T1D and JIA achieve glycemic control comparable to those with T1D alone. Nonetheless, elevated cardiometabolic risks highlight the need for tailored, interdisciplinary care strategies.

articles.title: Where patients obtain GLP-1 receptor agonists: direct-to-consumer channels, compounded product use, and reason-specific nonadherence in a national survey.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine acquisition channels for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and associations with compounded use, prescription status, and nonadherence.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis used the National Center for Health Statistics Rapid Surveys System Round 7 (July-August 2025; N = 8118). Among 976 past-year users, channels were classified as clinician/pharmacy without direct-to-consumer (DTC) acquisition, any DTC telehealth/medical spa, or other. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs).

RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was reported by 9.8% of adults, approximately 25.9 million. Of users, 18.3% used a DTC or medical spa channel and 9.2% reported no clinician prescription. Among users reporting known compounded status, compounded use was 73.0% (95% CI, 62.7%-81.2%) for DTC versus 12.9% (8.8%-18.4%) for conventional acquisition (aOR, 14.56; 95% CI, 7.99-26.54). Overall, 22.6% reported compounded use and 8.6% did not know. DTC acquisition was associated with cost-attributed nonadherence (aOR, 4.94; 95% CI, 2.77-8.81); the supply-attributed association was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.56-2.38; contrast P < 0.001). Associations were also observed for side-effect-attributed reduction/discontinuation (aOR, 2.12; 95% CI, 1.05-4.27) and complete discontinuation (aOR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.01-3.32). Counseling associations were imprecise. Insurance nonpayment was associated with DTC acquisition (aOR, 8.01; 95% CI, 4.70-13.67).

CONCLUSION: DTC acquisition was associated with compounded use, insurance nonpayment, and cost-attributed nonadherence. These cross-sectional findings suggest that acquisition sources and reasons for nonadherence may be useful topics for patient assessment. They do not establish causal effects of acquisition channel or demonstrate that medication records are incomplete.

articles.title: Prognostic Models in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterior circulation stroke (PCS) ranges from isolated brainstem deficits to devastating basilar artery occlusion (BAO), and accounts for approximately 20% of all ischemic strokes. Prognostic scoring systems for PCS integrating clinical, imaging, and angiographic domains have been developed to support reperfusion treatment decisions and goals-of-care discussions. This scoping review aimed to identify, characterize, and synthesize existing prognostic scoring systems for PCS, appraise their risk of bias, and propose directions for future model development.

SUMMARY: We performed a scoping review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase through March 2026 for studies that developed structured prognostic scoring systems for PCS. Of 1,342 records identified, 16 studies published between 2007 and 2026 met eligibility criteria. The included prognostic tools were organized into four conceptual domains: clinical severity-based scores, imaging-based ischemic burden scores, collateral and angiographic scores, and integrated prediction models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool (PROBAST) in the 15 studies that developed outcome-prediction models. Model performance varied across studies, with risk of bias concentrated in the analysis domain. Discrimination and calibration were reported in 3 of the 15 studies. Direct comparison was limited by heterogeneous outcome definitions and study populations, with most models being derived from BAO cohorts, which limits their applicability across the broader PCS spectrum.

KEY MESSAGES: Prognostic assessment in PCS can be structured sequentially at treatment decision points. Future work should prioritize prospective validation across the full PCS spectrum, dedicated model development in mild-to-moderate PCS, incorporation of serial neurological assessment into this sequential framework, and standardized reporting of calibration alongside discrimination.

articles.title: Acute pulmonary embolism: long-term cause-specific mortality in a Chinese nationwide registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated cumulative mortality, temporal changes in causes of death, and associated factors in a national registry.

METHODS: This registry-based cohort study consecutively enrolled 66 192 acute PE patients from 3223 Chest Pain Centres across China (2018-2023) (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04014972). Mortality was ascertained through national registry linkage. Cumulative incidence functions estimated temporal mortality patterns, while Fine-Gray models exploratorily examined factors associated with cause-specific mortality.

RESULTS: At 60 months, cumulative all-cause mortality was 22.41% (95% confidence interval [CI] 21.92-22.91), comprising cardiovascular (CV) (11.84%, 95% CI 11.46-12.23) and non-CV mortality (10.57%, 95% CI 10.22-10.92). Causes of death varied over time: acute PE and ischaemic heart disease (IHD) predominated initially, malignancy peaked at 1-3 months, and IHD was the largest named cause in each interval beyond 12 months. Among CV deaths, IHD was the predominant cause (35.7%); malignancy (43.3%) and chronic pulmonary disease (24.6%) predominated among non-CV deaths. Men had higher cumulative CV and non-CV mortality than women; while women only had a higher proportion of CV causes among deaths. All-cause mortality increased with age (from 11.52% at <55 to 38.51% at ≥75 years); acute PE/malignancy dominated in younger patients, while CV/pulmonary disease prevailed in older ones. Exploratory analyses identified age, Western China residence, and vital signs as factors associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalised with acute PE, 5-year cumulative mortality was 22.4%, and nearly half of deaths were from non-CV causes. Shifting mortality patterns highlight the need to evaluate risk-adapted long-term follow-up strategies.

articles.title: Defective HIV DNA genomes provide ancestral relevance critical for phylogenetic inference of reservoir dynamics.
articles.abstract: During the course of infection, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) persists in anatomical sanctuary and reservoir sites that lack necessary sensitivity to antiretroviral therapy. Curative advancements rely heavily on targeting these sites, though the precise contribution of each to viral persistence remains ill-supported through current sequencing and sequence analysis strategies. As a prime example, the vast replication-defective genomic landscape that comprises the HIV DNA population targeted for sequencing is often discarded, despite providing key information regarding competent ancestry that can be used to improve viral population dynamic inferences. Here, we describe the application of single-cell DNA sequencing to blood and lymph node samples from a treatment-interrupted S[imian]IV-infected animal model and evaluation of the contribution of genome coverage and inclusion on phylogenetic resolution and phyloanatomic inference. Findings from this study point to incomplete genomes as a significant source of phylogenetic information on reservoir dynamics during therapy.

articles.title: The benefits of reducing calorie intake in patients with familial partial lipodystrophy.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Lipodystrophy syndromes (LD) are rare disorders characterised by the absence and/or dysfunction of white adipose tissue. Defects in adipose tissue function impair its capacity to optimally buffer surplus energy intake and absolute, or relative, leptin deficiency exacerbates the mismatch between energy intake and storage capacity. Recombinant leptin therapy reduces food intake and substantially improves metabolic parameters in patients with generalised lipodystrophy but is less effective in patients with PLD. Here we demonstrate the metabolic impact of reduced calorie intake in people with PLD.

METHODS: This prospective study involved a 12-week low-energy (800-1000kcal/day) diet intervention. Thereafter, food was re-introduced, and participants followed for 1 year. We recruited people with PLD and diabetes. The primary endpoint was a reduction in HbA1c at 12 weeks. Secondary endpoints included reductions in HbA1c at 1 year and reductions in fasting glucose, serum triglycerides, hepatic fat and glucose-lowering medication use at 12 weeks and 12 months.

RESULTS: Six participants (5 FPLD1 and 1 FPLD3) completed the study. Body weight fell from 89.0kg (IQR 76.5 to 90.8) to 74.7kg (IQR 61.0 to 75.7, p=0.03) and HbA1c was reduced from 66.5 mmol/mol (IQR 59 to 69.5) to 41.5mmol/mol (IQR 34.5 to 48.5, p=0.03) by week 12. Food reintroduction, typically led to weight regain but this can be effectively mitigated by use of GIP/GLP1 RAs.

CONCLUSION: Reducing calorie intake alone results in marked metabolic improvement in people with PLD but is difficult to sustain.

articles.title: High-Dose vs Standard-Dose Influenza Vaccine and Patient-Reported Symptom Burden in Older Adults - A Substudy of the DANFLU-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (HD-IIV) reduces laboratory-confirmed influenza (LCI) and severe outcomes compared with standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine (SD-IIV), but effects on patient-reported symptom burden are uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To compare symptom burden after HD-IIV versus SD-IIV among older adults with symptomatic LCI and assess feasibility of home-based self-swabbing with digital patient-reported outcomes.

DESIGN: Prespecified exploratory substudy of the randomized, open-label DANFLU-2 trial.

SETTING: Nationwide in Denmark within the DANFLU-2 randomized trial during the 2024 to 2025 influenza season.

PARTICIPANTS: Community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older enrolled in DANFLU-2 who consented to participate in the Homeswab substudy.

INTERVENTION: Participants were assigned 1:1 to HD-IIV or SD-IIV and received self-swab kits with digital symptom questionnaires for influenza-like illness episodes.

MEASUREMENTS: Symptom burden among participants with LCI, assessed with the validated Respiratory Infection Intensity and Impact Questionnaire (RiiQ). Feasibility was assessed by swab return, RT-qPCR analyzability, RNase P positivity, and questionnaire completion.

RESULTS: Among 10,140 randomized participants (HD-IIV, 5040; SD-IIV, 5100; mean age, 73.2 years; 50.3% female), 1280 swabs were received and 1273 were analyzable. 121 swabs (9.5%) tested positive for influenza (HD-IIV, 44; SD-IIV, 77), and RNase P positivity was 97.8% (1245 of 1273). Among participants with LCI, 97 (80.2%) completed at least 1 symptom questionnaire. Respiratory and systemic symptom severity did not differ between groups. Post hoc relative vaccine effectiveness of HD-IIV versus SD-IIV against LCI was 42.2% (95% CI, 16.4% to 60.0%).

LIMITATIONS: The symptom-burden analysis was limited by few breakthrough infections and incomplete questionnaire completion.

CONCLUSION: Home-based self-swabbing with digital patient-reported outcome collection was feasible at scale among older adults in a vaccine effectiveness trial, but symptom burden after LCI did not differ between HD-IIV and SD-IIV.

articles.title: Less antiplatelet therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention: how and for whom?
Outer-scale-adaptive subharmonic method for atmospheric phase screen generation.
articles.abstract: Fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based atmospheric phase-screen synthesis can omit low-frequency fluctuations that are physically important over a finite aperture. We present an outer-scale-adaptive subharmonic method for modified von Kármán phase screens. For a computational screen of side length D and turbulence outer scale L0, we use the ratio χ=L0/(2D) to set low-frequency coverage within the central square frequency cell and the adaptive order q to control logarithmic resolution. We establish the outer-scale-dependent contribution of the omitted band, the mean-square vanishing of the low-frequency correction as L0/D→0, and ultra-low-frequency residual bounds. We also establish consistency of the discrete low-frequency structure function with its continuous square-band target in a joint limit of increasing outer-scale ratio and vanishing logarithmic node spacing. Using complete-screen Monte Carlo simulations and multilayer Gaussian-beam propagation tests, we show improved recovery of low-frequency-sensitive statistics relative to FFT-only in the tested large-χ regime, while finding that relative performance across compensation methods depends on the configuration and observable. By separating the physical low-frequency deficit from finite-order low-frequency, FFT-representation, and interpolation errors, we assess complete-screen accuracy. We then use confidence-interval tests of the complete-screen ensemble statistics to formulate an observable-specific criterion for selecting the smallest passing adaptive order within the tested range at a prescribed tolerance.

articles.title: OSNR and spectral spacing monitoring using fuzzy membership features in gridless Nyquist-WDM systems.
articles.abstract: We propose and experimentally validate a low-dimensional optical performance monitoring approach based on fuzzy membership features extracted from received constellation diagrams in gridless Nyquist-wavelength-division multiplexing (Nyquist-WDM) systems. Fuzzy C-means (FCM) and Gustafson-Kessel means (GKM) are independently applied to ∼10 k-symbol windows of received 16-QAM constellations. The resulting membership statistics quantify how the fuzzy association of received symbols is redistributed among constellation-derived clusters and are used to estimate spectral spacing in GHz and optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) in dB, as well as to perform binary detection of spectral overlap and low/high-OSNR conditions. Blind and aided monitoring strategies are evaluated using K-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machine/support vector regression (SVM/SVR), and random forest (RF) models in 3×16 GBd and 3×32 GBd Nyquist-WDM systems, including back-to-back (B2B) and 270 km transmission scenarios. The best aided regression results achieved 0.463 GHz MAE and 0.606 GHz RMSE for spectral-spacing estimation, and 0.883 dB MAE for OSNR estimation. For binary monitoring, overlap detection reached 0.868 accuracy and 0.870 F1-score, while low/high-OSNR classification achieved 0.938 accuracy and 0.938 F1-score. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis shows that aided models rely strongly on the auxiliary impairment variable, whereas blind monitoring mainly relies on low-order membership-rank statistics associated with the first and second ranks of the correct-symbol membership. These results indicate that fuzzy membership features provide a compact representation of constellation geometry for multi-task optical performance monitoring in adaptive gridless optical networks.

articles.title: The Association of Fragmented QRS on Electrocardiography With Cardiovascular Events and Mortality in Hemodialysis Patients.
articles.journal: Hemodialysis international. International Symposium on Home Hemodialysis
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Fragmented QRS on 12-lead electrocardiography (ECG) is a marker of myocardial fibrosis, but its clinical significance in hemodialysis patients remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the prevalence of fragmented QRS on the baseline ECG and its association with cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 101 patients with end-stage renal disease who started hemodialysis at a tertiary center between 2008 and 2020 (mean follow-up 132 ± 102 months). Fragmented QRS was defined per Das et al.

CRITERIA: To avoid immortal time bias, exposure was defined using the baseline ECG only. Cardiovascular events were analyzed by multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified clinical covariates and mortality by Cox regression.

FINDINGS: The mean age was 70.9 ± 12.6 years and 63 patients (62.4%) were male. Baseline fragmented QRS was present in 28 patients (27.7%). These patients had a higher prevalence of coronary artery disease (57.1% vs. 28.2%, p = 0.007), lower sodium (136 ± 3.7 vs. 139 ± 3.6 mmol/L, p = 0.001), lower ferritin (476 ± 545 vs. 726 ± 582 ng/mL, p = 0.023), and lower left ventricular ejection fraction (53.4% ± 12.8% vs. 60.1% ± 6.1%, p = 0.024). Cardiovascular events occurred in 43 patients (42.6%) and were more frequent with baseline fragmented QRS (75.0% vs. 30.1%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, and dialysis duration, baseline fragmented QRS remained independently associated with cardiovascular events (odds ratio 10.9, 95% CI 2.33-50.6, p = 0.002). All-cause mortality occurred in 32 patients (31.7%) and was not associated with baseline fragmented QRS (age- and sex-adjusted hazard ratio 1.14, 95% CI 0.54-2.44, p = 0.730).

DISCUSSION: Baseline fragmented QRS was common in hemodialysis patients and was independently associated with cardiovascular events, but not with all-cause mortality. Given that ECG is readily available, noninvasive, and inexpensive, fragmented QRS may serve as a useful risk marker; however, larger prospective studies are needed before routine implementation.

articles.title: The Role of U.S.-Based Professional Societies in Advancing and Creating Space for Global Psychological Science.
articles.journal: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
articles.abstract: With growing recognition that psychological science has primarily focused on White Euro-American samples, constructs, theories, and methods, there is an urgent need to broaden the scope and inclusiveness of the discipline. Although journals, funding agencies, and individual scientists each play important roles in advancing this shift, U.S.-based professional societies are particularly well positioned to promote globally engaged psychological science.
