Recognizing this potential, the U.S. National Committee for Psychological Science, with assistance from the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences, undertook an effort to gather and compile information about what U.S.-based professional societies are doing to enhance global engagement. Representatives of 24 professional societies across clinical, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology; statistics; behavioral medicine; neuroscience; and general psychology completed an online survey. Our analysis indicated that international focus was very important or important to more than 70% of the society representatives surveyed, and various activities to promote global engagement were described, although membership of Majority World scientists remained low, with limited integration of these scientists in leadership structures. On the basis of these findings and prior scholarship, we outline key approaches for inclusive, strategic, and scaffolded efforts to promote global psychological science.

articles.title: Rituximab-responsive epilepsia partialis continua in autoimmune Polyendocrine syndrome: A video-EEG-EMG polygraphic study.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract: Epilepsia partialis continua (EPC) is a rare and challenging form of focal motor status epilepticus. Its occurrence strictly in systemic autoimmune disorders without overt encephalitis is exceptional. Corticosteroids are first-line therapy but may be limited by significant side effects and poor metabolic tolerability. We report a 54-year-old woman with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome (APS), including autoimmune hepatitis, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults, celiac disease, and hypothyroidism, presenting with continuous jerks of right III-V fingers. Neurological examination showed continuous, irregular jerks confined to the right III, IV, and V fingers. Extensive serum and CSF screenings, including neuronal antibodies, and MRI were unremarkable. Ictal HMPAO-SPECT revealed a focal hyperperfusion in the left hand-knob area of the primary motor cortex. Brain FDG-PET revealed focal hypometabolism in the same region. Video-EEG-EMG polygraphy showed intermittent spikes and polyspikes over the left central region preceding EMG bursts of the right V finger's abductor muscle with a latency of approximately 30-40 ms. These findings were consistent with EPC. Corticosteroids induced marked improvement but were discontinued due to severe glycemic worsening. Subsequent treatment with oral steroids, IVIG, and multiple antiseizure medications were ineffective. Administration of Rituximab led to complete and sustained clinical and electrophysiological remission, which persisted at the 18-month follow-up. EPC can be a severe, focal manifestation of systemic autoimmunity even without encephalitis. Rituximab represents an effective steroid-sparing option for refractory autoimmune EPC, particularly in metabolically vulnerable patients.

articles.title: FDA Approves Weekly Insulin for Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes.
Intrarater reliability of expert electroencephalographic interpretation of 100 full-length recordings.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The value of electroencephalography (EEG) relies on accurate and reliable interpretation. Prior research has demonstrated imperfect interrater reliability, but intrarater reliability remains poorly characterized. We performed a "noise audit" primarily to measure intrarater variability in EEG interpretation by epileptologists.

METHODS: Experts independently rated the same 100 full-length EEGs on two separate occasions ≥60 days apart, unaware the EEGs were the same. EEGs were recorded from adult (56%) and pediatric patients in outpatient (78%) and non-critical care inpatient settings. There were 20 studies in each of five categories: normal, focal epileptiform (FE), generalized epileptiform (GE), focal nonepileptiform (FNE), and generalized nonepileptiform (GNE) abnormalities. EEGs were presented using our online platform (EEGHub) without clinical information except for age and sex. Experts rated each recording and indicated their level of confidence (LOC) for each EEG and overall. We analyzed percent as well as chance-corrected intra- and interrater agreement.

RESULTS: Fourteen experts (mean of 19 years EEG reading experience, range = 4-52 years) were included in the study. Percent self-agreement was 96% for GE, 90% for FE, 88% for FNE, and 87% for GNE abnormalities; 90% for any epileptiform abnormality; and 82% for any nonepileptiform abnormality. Self-agreement was strongly correlated with interrater agreement (mean κML), which was almost perfect for GE (.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .87-.94) and FE (.82, 95% CI = .77-.87) and substantial for GNE (.75, 95% CI = .69-.81) and FNE (.74, 95% CI = .68-.80) abnormalities. LOC correlated with self-agreement on the presence of nonepileptiform but not epileptiform abnormalities.

SIGNIFICANCE: We found generally strong within-expert agreement in EEG interpretation, especially in the identification of epileptiform abnormalities. Nevertheless, the number of flipped decisions was high enough to be clinically consequential. This undesired variability ("occasion noise") may be addressed by interventions to (1) decrease this noise directly and (2) reduce case ambiguity with longer recordings and better EEG data whenever feasible.

articles.title: Induction of a Porcine Coronary Artery Perforation Model: A Comparison of Three Techniques.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery perforation (CAP) is a rare but life-threatening complication of percutaneous coronary intervention. Reliable preclinical models are essential for evaluating covered stents and other emerging coronary devices. This study established a reproducible porcine model capable of consistently inducing severe CAP and compared three perforation techniques for CAP induction.

METHODS: Three coronary perforation techniques were sequentially evaluated in 10 Yorkshire swine: guidewire penetration, scoring balloon pullback, and the sharpened catheter shaft technique. Perforation induction was assessed using coronary angiography according to the Ellis classification.

RESULTS: The guidewire technique produced angiographically confirmed perforations in 2 of the 10 animals (20%), whereas the scoring balloon pullback technique failed to produce perforations in any animal. By contrast, the sharpened catheter shaft technique successfully induced Ellis Class III CAP in all animals (10/10, 100%). Initial balloon tamponade achieved hemostasis in 5 of the 10 animals (50%), and final hemostasis was achieved in 6 of the 10 animals (60%) after additional balloon tamponade in selected cases. Ventricular fibrillation occurred in four animals (40%), while echocardiography demonstrated hemopericardium in four animals (40%) and scant pericardial effusion in three animals (30%). Optical coherence tomography (OCT) and histological analyses consistently demonstrated severe structural vessel wall injury at the perforation sites.

CONCLUSION: The sharpened catheter shaft technique enabled reproducible induction of Ellis Class III CAP in a porcine model, with angiographic, OCT, and histological findings consistent with severe vascular injury. This model may serve as a practical preclinical platform for evaluating covered stents and other emerging coronary devices.

articles.title: Consensus Statement on the Role of Dermoceuticals in the Management of Atopic Dermatitis in the United Arab Emirates.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease characterized by epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, microbiome alterations, and persistent pruritus. Dermoceuticals have become an integral component of AD management because of their role in restoring skin barrier function, maintaining hydration, reducing symptoms, and complementing pharmacological therapies. However, practical guidance on their optimal selection and integration into routine clinical practice remains limited within the United Arab Emirates (UAE). This consensus manuscript aimed to develop evidence-informed statements on the use of dermoceuticals in the management of AD in the UAE.

METHODS: A panel of 13 experienced dermatologists representing public and private healthcare sectors across the UAE, together with an international expert serving as an external scientific validator, developed the statements through a structured modified Delphi process informed by a targeted literature review. Consensus was defined as ≥ 80% agreement.

RESULTS: Following two rounds of anonymous voting, consensus was achieved for 13 of the 14 proposed statements. One statement concerning treatment selection in active and mild AD did not achieve consensus and was excluded. The 13 final statements addressed AD pathophysiology, treatment goals, the definition and role of dermoceuticals, moisturizer formulations, microbiome-supportive skincare, gentle cleansers, ceramide-containing formulations, proactive maintenance therapy, shared decision-making, and patient and caregiver education. The panel emphasized that dermoceuticals should be considered a lifelong component of individualized AD management, serving as monotherapy in selected patients with mild disease and as adjunctive therapy alongside pharmacological treatment in moderate-to-severe AD.

CONCLUSIONS: These consensus recommendations provide practical guidance for integrating dermoceuticals into routine clinical practice in the UAE and aim to support standardized, evidence-informed, patient-centered care while optimizing long-term disease control and quality of life.

articles.title: Distributional Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Blood-Based Noninvasive Screening for MASLD among US Veterans: Assessing Health Equity Impact in the Era of Emerging Therapies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects a substantial portion of US veterans and poses clinical and economic burdens. Blood-based noninvasive tests are recommended to stratify fibrosis and guide treatment decisions. However, the equity implications of alternative primary-care screening pathways remain unknown. This gap is especially salient in single-payer systems such as the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA), where resource allocation may involve trade-offs between maximizing total health and reducing disparities. We evaluated the efficiency and equity impact of a selected set of Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4)- and Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF)-based screening strategies among US veterans.

METHODS: We conducted a distributional cost-effectiveness analysis (DCEA) from the VHA perspective comparing six screening strategies using the ELF and/or FIB-4 at varying cutoffs. Veterans were stratified into 15 subgroups by race/ethnicity and Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) quintiles. We adapted a previously published cost-effectiveness model, supplemented with subgroup-specific epidemiologic data and explicit distributional assumptions, to estimate subgroup-specific quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) and costs associated with screening and fibrosis treatment (resmetirom). Opportunity health effects were incorporated using a $100,000/QALY threshold (in 2026 US dollars). Health inequality was quantified using the Atkinson index.

RESULTS: Compared with standard-of-care FIB-4 screening, sequential ELF screening at a 9.80 cutoff following indeterminate FIB-4 reduced referral and treatment intensity, resulting in direct health losses (91,370 QALYs) among screened veterans. However, the resulting cost savings generated opportunity health gains under the DCEA framework, yielding the largest net population health gains (185,010 QALYs) and the greatest reduction in health inequality (0.112%, or 194,690 equally distributed QALYs), assuming an Atkinson inequality aversion parameter of 12.2 and an opportunity-cost threshold of $100,000/QALY. In contrast, ELF 9.00 screening generated the largest direct QALY gains among screened veterans but was not preferred once opportunity health losses and distributional effects were incorporated. Results were generally consistent across sensitivity and scenario analyses, including scenarios with substantially reduced treatment costs, but were sensitive to assumptions regarding the extent to which cost savings were converted into opportunity health gains. Equity gains were greatest when cost savings were reinvested to improve health among more vulnerable groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Among the FIB-4- and ELF-based screening strategies evaluated, sequential ELF screening at a 9.80 cutoff following FIB-4 generated the greatest net population health and equity gains under modeled assumptions and an opportunity-cost framework, despite reducing treatment intensity and direct health benefits among screened patients. These findings should be interpreted within the restricted comparator set, the assumptions governing subgroup differences, and the conversion of cost savings into health gains. More broadly, the analysis illustrates how incorporating equity considerations through DCEA can inform resource allocation within integrated health systems such as the VHA.

articles.title: Economic Evaluations of Narcolepsy Treatments: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal to Inform Future Health Economic Models.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disease with substantial clinical, humanistic, and economic burden. Access to treatments varies across jurisdictions. This systematic review critically appraised the modeling approaches used in existing economic evaluations of treatments for narcolepsy and identified opportunities for improvements.

METHODS: Systematic literature searches were conducted in MEDLINE (Ovid), Embase, Cochrane Library, EconLit, and the International Network of Agencies for Health Technology Assessment database from inception to May 2026, supplemented by manual searches of major health technology assessment and other value assessment agency websites through June or July 2026. Trial-based or model-based cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, or cost-benefit analyses in adults with narcolepsy type 1 or 2 were eligible for inclusion, with no language or geographic restrictions. Information on model conceptualization, structure, inputs, uncertainty, validation, and transparency was extracted; quality was assessed using the Philips checklist.

RESULTS: Seven economic evaluations were included. All were cost-utility models that shared a similar structure: an initial phase to determine treatment response, followed by a longer-term Markov model based on responder status, with treatment response extrapolated beyond the trial follow-up. Treatment benefit was primarily represented through changes in excessive daytime sleepiness, while other symptoms were omitted. Comparative efficacy was frequently based on expert opinion or individual trials rather than systematic and statistical evidence synthesis. Healthcare costs focused largely on drug acquisition, indirect costs were rarely incorporated, and downstream clinical and societal consequences were not directly modeled. Utility estimation relied on mapping algorithms from non-narcolepsy populations, different measures across treatments, or unclear sources. Sensitivity analyses focused predominantly on parameter uncertainty. Validation and transparency varied substantially across models.

CONCLUSIONS: Published economic evaluations of narcolepsy treatments identified materially important aspects of the decision problem that were not incorporated into the models because of insufficient evidence, resulting in incomplete representation of the disease and the decision problem. Future evaluations require both appropriate model structures and evidence linking disease manifestations and treatment response to relevant outcomes, including downstream costs and consequences, alongside rigorous comparative evidence synthesis, utility values derived from people with narcolepsy, and comprehensive assessment of parameter, methodological, and structural uncertainty.

articles.title: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis presenting with neuropsychiatric symptoms-potential for misdiagnosis?
articles.journal: Neuropsychiatrie : Klinik, Diagnostik, Therapie und Rehabilitation : Organ der Gesellschaft Osterreichischer Nervenarzte und Psychiater
articles.abstract: Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) is a rare, immune-mediated demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system, particularly uncommon in adults and often diagnostically challenging when presenting with neuropsychiatric features. We report the case of a 41-year-old male patient with a pre-existing psychiatric history who developed subacute neurological symptoms followed by acute psychiatric deterioration leading to a psychiatric admission. During psychiatric admission, the patient experienced rapid neurological deterioration, culminating in reduced consciousness and critical illness requiring intensive care. Early investigations, including computed tomography, were unremarkable, and a provisional diagnosis of neuroleptic malignant syndrome was made. Subsequent neurological evaluation including magnetic resonance imaging revealed multifocal demyelinating lesions consistent with ADEM. The patient was treated with intravenous corticosteroids and immunoglobulins, followed by a prolonged steroid taper. Despite severe initial disability, gradual clinical improvement was observed with multidisciplinary care and rehabilitation. This case highlights the phenomenon of diagnostic overshadowing, where neurological pathology may be misattributed to psychiatric illness, leading to delayed diagnosis and treatment. It underscores the importance of thorough medical assessment, including early neuroimaging in patients presenting with atypical psychiatric symptoms, particularly when accompanied by neurological signs. Prompt recognition of ADEM is critical, as timely immunotherapy can significantly improve outcomes.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Benralizumab Among Patients with Severe Asthma from the Chinese Societal Perspective.
articles.journal: Applied health economics and health policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Treatment options for patients with severe asthma (SA) in China remain limited. A multicentre, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial (MIRACLE; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03186209) has demonstrated the therapeutic potential of benralizumab as an adjunctive treatment option for this patient group. Nevertheless, the high cost of benralizumab treatment poses significant economic challenges that may impede its widespread adoption in China. This study aimed to evaluate the cost effectiveness of benralizumab for SA patients in China from a societal perspective.

METHODS: A Markov model was developed to simulate the lifetime disease course of patients with SA, with a 4-week Markov cycle. The model incorporated rates of clinically significant exacerbations (CSEs) from the MIRACLE trial, obtained from asthma mortality rates, costs and health state utilities from extensive literature and national databases. Both costs and effectiveness outcomes were discounted at an annual rate of 5%. Multiple sensitivity analyses were performed to test model robustness. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of benralizumab versus placebo were calculated and compared with a willingness-to-pay (WTP) threshold range of ¥114,899 (US$15,934) to ¥287,247 (US$39,835) per quality-adjusted life year (QALY).

RESULTS: Across the lifetime time horizon, the ICER of benralizumab plus standard of care (SoC) compared with SoC alone was US$66,792.76 per QALY. This value exceeded the 2024 Chinese WTP threshold (US$39,834.56 per QALY), indicating that benralizumab was not cost effective for the treatment of adult patients with severe asthma in China.

CONCLUSION: Under current model assumptions, benralizumab is unlikely to represent a cost-effective therapeutic option for severe asthma in China across different patient subgroups.

articles.title: Astrocyte-related pathological mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) stands as one of the most severe complications of sepsis. Currently, the clinical management of SAE follows a comprehensive management strategy centered on treatment of the underlying sepsis, supplemented by symptomatic management of neurological dysfunction. The cornerstone of SAE management is the prompt and effective treatment of the underlying sepsis, including early source control, appropriate antimicrobial therapy, and comprehensive organ support, thereby mitigating the systemic inflammatory response that contributes to brain injury. On this basis, symptomatic and supportive management of brain dysfunction is crucial. Although no targeted specific drugs are currently available, future research will focus on targeting pathological pathways such as neuroinflammation, preserving mitochondrial function, and stabilizing the blood-brain barrier (BBB), with particular attention to how impaired astrocytic glutamate clearance, metabolic coupling, and synaptic regulation may translate glial dysfunction into neuronal bioenergetic failure, synaptic instability, delirium, and long-term cognitive impairment, with the aim of achieving genuinely neuroprotective therapy. This review summarizes the current evidence on the molecular pathology of SAE, with a particular focus on astrocyte-related mechanisms, including recent advances in the classification of astrocyte states, mitochondrial dysfunction, autophagy, and astrocyte-neuron interactions. In terms of therapeutic strategies, activating antioxidant pathways and modulation of autophagy have both shown potential therapeutic value. Future research should focus on developing multi-target synergistic intervention strategies, promoting the translation of basic research findings into clinical practice, and providing new directions for the precision prevention and control of SAE.

articles.title: Proteomic characterization of the renoprotective effects of Goreisan in high-fat diet/L-NAME-treated mice.
articles.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is frequently complicated by chronic kidney disease (CKD). A mouse model combining a high-fat diet (HFD) and N-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester (L-NAME) reproduces key features of HFpEF, including renal injury; however, the underlying renal pathophysiology remains poorly understood. This study investigated the mechanisms of renal impairment in HFD/L-NAME-treated mice and evaluated the renoprotective effects and potential mechanisms of Goreisan (GRS), a traditional Japanese Kampo medicine. C57BL/6J mice were treated with HFD/L-NAME with or without GRS. Renal parameters were assessed, and proteomic analyses of kidney and plasma samples were performed using LC-MS/MS and SomaScan®, respectively. Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analyses were conducted to explore disease-associated pathways and the pharmacological effects of GRS. GRS ameliorated HFD/L-NAME-induced albuminuria and glomerular hypertrophy. Proteomic analyses suggested enrichment of complement-related pathways in the kidney and blood coagulation-related pathways in the plasma of HFD/L-NAME-treated mice. Renal complement component 9 (C9) expression was significantly correlated with urinary albumin levels, suggesting an association with kidney injury. GO enrichment analyses suggested that GRS treatment was associated with the modulation of oxidative stress-related pathways in the kidney and, in exploratory analyses, plasma. Consistent with these findings, GRS reduced 24-h urinary 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine excretion, supporting an antioxidant effect in this model. Blood coagulation-, complement-, and oxidative stress-related pathways may be associated with renal injury in HFD/L-NAME-treated mice. GRS exerted renoprotective effects, with oxidative stress modulation identified as a candidate contributing mechanism. These proteomic data provide insight into HFpEF-associated kidney injury and a resource for future systems-level studies of GRS.

articles.title: Takotsubo syndrome: Phenotype, pathophysiology, and the problem of incomplete recovery.
articles.abstract: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is a heterogeneous acute heart failure syndrome with diverse triggers, varied phenotypes, important acute complications, and not insignificant long-term morbidity and mortality. This review examines TTS across phenotype, pathophysiology, diagnosis, management, and long-term outcomes. Contemporary registry data show that many cases arise in the setting of acute medical, neurological, or other physical stress rather than isolated emotional distress. Trigger profile, comorbidity burden, and right ventricular involvement may be more clinically informative than ventricular pattern alone. TTS is more likely to reflect several interacting processes than a single unifying mechanism. Sympathetic activation, coronary microvascular dysfunction, inflammation, endothelial injury, impaired myocardial energetics, and brain-heart axis dysregulation may all contribute to the final phenotype. Diagnosis still commonly begins with an acute coronary syndrome-like presentation but is best made through the overall pattern of presentation and multimodality imaging, rather than as a diagnosis of exclusion. Acute management remains largely supportive and should be guided by haemodynamic phenotype. A central theme of this review is that recovery in TTS is often incomplete. Although left ventricular ejection fraction frequently normalises, persistent abnormalities in myocardial function, tissue characteristics, energetics, symptoms, and exercise capacity are increasingly recognised. TTS should therefore be viewed not simply as a transient and fully reversible disorder, but as a complex clinical syndrome with acute and longer-term consequences that remain incompletely understood.

articles.title: Temporal trends and statistical relationships between deforestation and burned area in the Peruvian Amazon (2013-2024).
articles.abstract: Deforestation and burned area are important indicators of environmental change in the Amazon, yet their spatiotemporal relationship remains insufficiently understood in the Peruvian Amazon. This study evaluated temporal trends and the relationship between annual deforestation and burned area across five departments (Amazonas, Loreto, Madre de Dios, San Martín, and Ucayali) during 2013-2024 using official satellite-based annual datasets. Descriptive statistics, department-specific linear regressions, Spearman correlation analyses, and a global linear model were used to assess spatial and temporal patterns. Model assumptions were evaluated through residual diagnostics, and a generalized least squares (GLS) model with a first-order autoregressive [AR(1)] correlation structure was fitted as a sensitivity analysis. Ucayali exhibited the highest annual deforestation (33,802 ± 5675 ha year⁻1) and the largest mean burned area (53.40 ± 13.60 km2 year⁻1). Significant increases in burned area were detected in Loreto, Madre de Dios, and Ucayali, while significant increases in deforestation occurred only in Madre de Dios. The ordinary global linear model identified a positive association between deforestation and burned area (β = 0.000439, p = 0.011). After accounting for temporal autocorrelation, the GLS coefficient remained positive but was not statistically significant at α = 0.05 (β = 0.0003, p = 0.0698). In contrast, the positive temporal trend in burned area remained significant. These findings reveal marked spatial heterogeneity in deforestation-burned area relationships and provide a regional-scale baseline for future environmental monitoring and land-use assessments in the Peruvian Amazon.

articles.title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes.

RESULTS: Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially.

CONCLUSIONS: In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

articles.title: Effect of Nerandomilast in US Patients with Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Subgroup Analysis of the FIBRONEER-ILD Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In the FIBRONEER-ILD trial in patients with progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF), nerandomilast reduced decline in forced vital capacity (FVC) versus placebo, with benefits on clinical outcomes and favorable safety and tolerability. We present the effects of nerandomilast in US patients.

METHODS: Patients were randomized to receive nerandomilast 9 mg bid, nerandomilast 18 mg bid, or placebo, stratified by nintedanib use and HRCT pattern. In the US subgroup, we assessed change in FVC (mL) at week 52; time-to-event endpoints over the whole trial; and adverse events over the whole trial.

RESULTS: Of 1176 patients, 139 (11.8%) were from the US. In the US patients, adjusted mean (SE) changes in FVC (mL) at week 52 were - 160.4 (35.7) with placebo, - 115.2 (38.6) with nerandomilast 9 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 45.2 [95% CI: -57.8, 148.2]), and - 53.4 (37.3) with nerandomilast 18 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 107.0 [95% CI: 6.2, 207.9]). The hazard ratios (95% CI) for time to first acute exacerbation of ILD, hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death were 0.88 (0.42, 1.81) for nerandomilast 9 mg bid and 0.52 (0.23, 1.18) for nerandomilast 18 mg bid versus placebo. Adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 14.0, 11.4 and 8.9% of the placebo, nerandomilast 9 mg bid and nerandomilast 18 mg bid groups, respectively.

CONCLUSION: In the FIBRONEER-ILD trial, the effects of nerandomilast in US patients were consistent with the overall population, with a reduction in FVC decline, numerically reduced risk of adverse clinical outcomes, and favorable safety and tolerability.

articles.title: Effect of Nerandomilast in US Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis: a Subgroup Analysis of the FIBRONEER-IPF Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In the placebo-controlled FIBRONEER-IPF trial in patients with IPF, nerandomilast reduced decline in forced vital capacity (FVC), with benefits on clinical outcomes and favorable safety and tolerability. We evaluated the effects of nerandomilast in the US patients.

METHODS: Patients were randomized to receive nerandomilast 9 mg bid, nerandomilast 18 mg bid, or placebo, stratified by antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib/pirfenidone versus neither). In the US subgroup, we assessed change in FVC at week 52; time-to-event endpoints over the whole trial; adverse events over the whole trial.

RESULTS: Of 1177 patients, 196 (16.7%) were from the US. In US patients, adjusted mean (SE) changes in FVC (mL) were - 257.9 (33.6) with placebo, - 152.7 (32.9) with nerandomilast 9 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 105.2 [95% CI 13.0, 197.4]), and - 126.2 (36.9) with nerandomilast 18 mg bid (difference vs. placebo 131.7 [95% CI 33.8, 229.6]. Compared with placebo, the hazard ratios for time to first acute exacerbation of IPF, hospitalization for respiratory cause, or death were 0.91 (95% CI 0.49, 1.67) for nerandomilast 9 mg bid and 0.60 (95% CI 0.30, 1.22) for nerandomilast 18 mg bid. Adverse events led to treatment discontinuation in 17.1%, 12.9% and 10.7% of the placebo, nerandomilast 9 mg bid and nerandomilast 18 mg bid groups, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The effects of nerandomilast 18 mg bid in US patients in the FIBRONEER-IPF trial were consistent with the overall population. Nerandomilast 18 mg bid slowed FVC decline, with numerical reductions in the risk of clinical outcomes, and favorable safety and tolerability.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Study on Biofilm Formation Capability and Biofilm Associated Virulence Genes Carriage of Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae: Correlation between Biomass and Viability.
articles.abstract: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) has drawn wide attention due to their distinctive features in virulence and pathogenicity. This study aimed to comprehensively investigate the biofilm formation capability and biofilm associated virulence genes carriage of hvKp. 552 K. pneumoniae isolates were isolated from various sources and identified to the species level, followed by antibiotic susceptibility test and correlation analysis among antibiotic resistance, clinical characteristics, risk factors, and invasive infection occurrence. Hypermucoviscous K. pneumonia (hmKp) and hvKp were further studied on serotyping, Multi-Locus Sequence Typing (MLST), biofilm formation and associated genes. We isolated 552 K. pneumoniae strains from various sources and 51 (9.2%) were identified as hmKp, with 26 and 25 sampled from invasive and non-invasive infections, respectively. Among the 51 hmKp, 43 (84.3%) were determined as hvKp, of which 25 and 18 were from invasive and non-invasive infections, respectively. ST23 and K1/K2 were the prevalent types in hvKp. High identification rate of biofilm associated virulence genes ycfM, entB, ureA, wabG was found. Importantly, approximately 65% and 85% of hmKp and invasive hvKp strains exhibit strong or moderate biofilm biomass and viability, respectively. Also, positive association between overall biofilm biomass and biofilm viability was found among 51 hmKp and 25 invasive hvKp. Remarkably, among both groups, strains with weak biomass tend to have weak viability, strains moderate biomass tend to have strong viability and strains with strong biomass tend to have strong viability, while strains with weak biomass rarely have strong viability. Comparative analysis revealed that kfu-positive, mrkD-positive, magA-positive isolates exhibited significantly higher biofilm biomass and viability, wabG and ureA showed no significant associations with biofilm phenotypes. This study has provided an important contribution to understanding biofilm formation capability in hvKp strains.

articles.title: End-stage renal disease in people taking lithium: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lithium is an effective maintenance treatment for Bipolar Affective Disorder. However, it is also associated with renal impairment. End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) is the most severe form of chronic kidney disease (CKD) and has significant morbidity and mortality.

OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review on ESRD incidence in adult patients taking lithium for mood disorders.

METHODS: The search was conducted on EMBASE, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and CENTRAL for relevant articles. Relevant bibliographies were also searched. Original research in English, reporting on ESRD in adults with affective disorders on lithium, was included. End-stage renal disease was defined as estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) < 15mL/minute/1.73m2 or renal replacement therapy (RRT). Studies with lithium exposure for a mean duration of less than five years were excluded.

RESULTS: Eight retrospective cohort studies were included. Studies were heterogeneous, making direct comparisons difficult. Results showed that ESRD occurs rarely, less than 1% in the absence of a pre-existing renal disease, and typically after decades of lithium exposure. In the presence of chronic kidney disease, discontinuation of lithium after a point of return was not necessarily associated with lower rates of ESRD. However, the trajectory of renal function after discontinuation of lithium remains debatable warranting further prospective studies. There were inconsistent results regarding how confounding factors, such as hypertension and diabetes, contributed to ESRD risk in lithium users.

CONCLUSION: End-stage renal disease is a rare outcome that develops after decades of lithium treatment. The literature on ESRD associated with lithium is limited by the long latency of ESRD, retrospective study designs, and confounding covariates.

articles.title: Paediatric complex regional pain syndrome type 1 in Italy: a national survey of diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Complex regional pain syndrome type 1 (CRPS-1) is a rare but potentially disabling condition, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide clinical management. This study aimed to describe diagnostic and therapeutic approaches to paediatric CRPS-1 among Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. A cross-sectional electronic survey was distributed to 34 Italian centres providing paediatric rheumatology care. The questionnaire explored referral patterns, diagnosis, management strategies, availability of formal management protocols, disease burden, and follow-up procedures. Data were analysed descriptively. Twenty-three of 34 centres participated (67.6%). In most centres (17/23, 73.9%), the majority of patients were referred without a prior diagnostic suspicion of CRPS-1, and paediatric rheumatologists most frequently established the diagnosis. In 9/23 centres (39.1%), CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than 3 months after symptom onset in the majority of patients. Multidisciplinary care was widely adopted, with physiotherapy and psychological support routinely incorporated into clinical care in 22/23 (95.7%) and 21/23 (91.3%) centres, respectively. Initial management most commonly combined pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions (14/21, 66.7%). Pharmacological strategies were heterogeneous, with only 2/23 centres (8.7%) having a formal protocol. More than 90% of centres (21/23) rated the impact of CRPS-1 on patients and their families as severe or very severe.

CONCLUSION: This national survey shows substantial convergence in the core principles of multidisciplinary paediatric CRPS-1 management despite the absence of specific guidelines. Future collaborative research should strengthen the paediatric evidence base to support more robust clinical recommendations, while improving awareness among primary care paediatricians and other frontline clinicians should remain a priority to facilitate earlier recognition and timely referral.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Paediatric CRPS-1 is uncommon and potentially disabling, with limited paediatric-specific evidence to guide diagnosis and treatment. • Multidisciplinary rehabilitation and psychological support are key components of treatment, whereas pharmacological management remains poorly standardised.

WHAT IS NEW: • This first Italian multicentre survey shows substantial agreement on the core principles of multidisciplinary care, despite heterogeneity in pharmacological treatment and the limited availability of formal management protocols. • Delayed recognition remains a relevant challenge: in nearly 40% of participating centres, CRPS-1 was diagnosed more than three months after symptom onset in the majority of patients.

articles.title: Clinical analysis of rare chylous mesenteric cyst in children.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Chylous Mesenteric Cysts (CMCs) are rare intra-abdominal masses in children, and definitive preoperative diagnosis remains challenging. This study reviews the diagnosis and management of CMCs at a single institution, with particular attention to clinical characteristics and the effectiveness of laparoscopic surgery. A retrospective analysis was performed on the records of all patients diagnosed with CMCs and treated with laparoscopic surgery at our institution between January 2020 and May 2026. Clinical manifestations, preoperative imaging data, surgical techniques, postoperative complications, and patient outcomes were evaluated. The study cohort included three girls and five boys. The median age was 4.2 years (range, 0.1 to 9.0 years), and the median weight was 14.5 kg (range, 4.9 to 32.5 kg). Abdominal pain and vomiting were the most common symptoms, occurring in 62.5% of cases. Four patients experienced cyst-related complications: three developed intestinal volvulus, and one presented with intestinal volvulus accompanied by intestinal obstruction. Sole cyst excision was conducted in two cases, while en bloc resection of the cyst with bowel was performed in six cases. Laparoscopic surgery was completed successfully in seven patients; one case required conversion to open surgery. The mean operative time was 103 ± 31 min. Pathological examination identified lymphatic malformation containing chylous fluid in all patients, findings consistent with mesenteric chylous cyst. No peritoneal infection, anastomotic leakage, or cyst recurrence was observed during short and medium term follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Chylous mesenteric cysts are most often definitively diagnosed during surgery. Once confirmed, prompt removal is recommended to prevent complications. Laparoscopic cyst excision or cyst excision with bowel resection appears to be a feasible approach for pediatric patients with uncomplicated chylous mesenteric cysts.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • CMCs are rare, benign lymphatic malformations of the small-bowel mesentery in children that can result in severe complications such as intestinal volvulus and obstruction. Definitive pre-operative diagnosis of CMC is challenging, with most cases confirmed during surgery. • Surgical resection is the standard treatment. Open surgery has long been mainstream, while laparoscopy is increasingly applied.

WHAT IS NEW: • Transumbilical single-port laparoscopy appears feasible in selected paediatric patients with uncomplicated CMC. Extensive or poorly demarcated lesions may require conversion to open surgery. • Definitive preoperative diagnosis was uncommon in this small cohort and in the limited literature reviewed. The transumbilical approach may offer a cosmetically favourable incision and facilitate specimen extraction. Complete resection was followed by favourable short and medium term outcomes in this series; however, the small sample size and absence of a comparator group preclude firm conclusions.

articles.title: A negative binomial regression model for predicting scorpion sting incidence in an island context: integrating meteorological and epidemiological data from Qeshm, Iran (2019-2024).
articles.abstract: Scorpion envenomation poses a significant public health challenge worldwide, with particularly high burden in tropical and subtropical regions including southern Iran. Environmental factors, particularly meteorological conditions, influence scorpion activity and subsequent human exposure risk. This study aimed to develop a predictive model for scorpion sting incidence by integrating epidemiological and meteorological data in Qeshm County, Iran. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 744 scorpion sting cases reported at Prophet Azam Hospital between April 2019 and September 2024. Case data were combined with monthly meteorological variables. Analytical methods included descriptive statistics, Spearman's rank correlation, time series decomposition, and cross-correlation analysis. A Negative Binomial regression model was then constructed to predict monthly sting counts. The incidence of scorpion stings showed significant year-to-year variation, peaking in 2021 (n = 178). A clear seasonal pattern was observed, with more than 62% of cases occurring between May and September. Mean monthly temperature was strongly positively correlated with sting incidence (ρ = 0.72, P < 0.001), while relative humidity (ρ = -0.65, P < 0.001) and precipitation (ρ = -0.58, P < 0.001) showed strong negative correlations. The final predictive model, incorporating temperature and a one-month lag of sting count, explained 68% of the variance (Pseudo R² = 0.68). Scorpion sting incidence in Qeshm County exhibits pronounced seasonality and is closely linked to warm, dry weather conditions. The developed model demonstrates the potential to forecast sting risk using meteorological data and past incidence, offering a basis for proactive public health interventions during high-risk periods.

articles.title: SH3TC2-Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4 C: an Italian multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4 C (CMT4C), caused by biallelic variants in SH3TC2, is the most common autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathy. Italian multicentre data with detailed genotype-phenotype characterisation are lacking. Yet knowledge of the natural history is urgently needed as SH3TC2 gene replacement therapy approaches clinical trials following a successful Pre-Investigational New Drug meeting with the FDA in November 2024.

METHODS: We screened 684 patients with genetically unresolved CMT using a combination of exome analysis and a multigene next-generation sequencing panel and identified nine (from five Italian neurology centres) with biallelic SH3TC2 variants. All patients underwent standardised neurological examination, nerve conduction studies, and assessment using the Charcot-Marie-Tooth Examination Score version 2 (CMTESv2). Variant pathogenicity was assessed according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) criteria incorporating REVEL (Rare Exome Variant Ensemble Learner) and CADD (Combined Annotation-Dependent Depletion) scores.

RESULTS: Nine patients (5 males, 4 females; age 3.5-66 years) were studied. Twelve distinct SH3TC2 variants were identified, including four not previously reported: p.Glu794* (likely pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP guidelines), p.Gly18Ser (variant of unknown significance, VUS), p.Ala526Thr (VUS), and p.Thr1098Ile (VUS). Scoliosis was present in 6/9 patients (66.7%), foot deformities in 7/9 (77.8%), and sensorineural hearing loss in 2/9 (22.2%). Genotype-phenotype analysis revealed marked intra-class variability, including a 59-year-old with homozygous frameshift variants and near-normal function (CMTESv2 total score of 3). One patient was diagnosed presymptomatically at age 3.5 years through cascade genetic testing prompted by comorbid features of Angelman syndrome. All seven symptomatic patients showed motor nerve conduction velocities below 35 m/s. Novel variants p.Gly18Ser and p.Ala526Thr are of uncertain significance and require functional validation: p.Ala526Thr lies immediately adjacent to the functionally characterised pathogenic residue Arg529, whereas p.Gly18Ser lies 16 residues from the myristoylation site at Gly2, within a segment of very low predicted model confidence.

CONCLUSIONS: This Italian multicentre cohort expands the SH3TC2 mutational spectrum highlighting the marked phenotypic variability of CMT4C, and the possibility of presymptomatic identification through multigene NGS panels. Our data contribute to the evidence base required for the design of forthcoming gene therapy clinical trials.

articles.title: Assessment of Species Conservation Action Plans for Wildlife Crime Control and CITES Implementation for Four Flagship Faunal Species in Nepal.
articles.abstract: Conservation Action Plans (CAPs) are generally developed as policy documents for systematic conservation practices conducted at the species level over a given period. The Government of Nepal has extensively invested in producing CAPs for four flagship species: Bengal tiger (Panthera tigris tigris), one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis), Asian elephant (Elephas maximus), and snow leopard (Panthera uncia) since 90 s. The current CAPs of these species review the completion status of previous plans and comprise various actions related to species conservation for specific time periods. Here, we assessed the actions associated with these four species. The specific objectives of this study are to 1) assess the completion of actions set for "CITES implementation" and "law enforcement" for national wildlife crime control and "capacity building" for law enforcement of the four species, and 2) investigate the proposed objectives and actions related to "CITES implementation" and "law enforcement" and "capacity building" for law enforcement in the CAPs for these species. For each species we reviewed the current CAPs and recorded conservation actions that were "achieved", "partially achieved", and "not initiated" from the past CAPs. We extracted, reviewed, and proposed actions supporting "law enforcement" for wildlife crime control and "capacity building" for law enforcement and CITES implementation from the current CAPs, deductively based on prior knowledge of the authors. After that, we developed a rule-based categorization framework inductively to categorize these actions into "law enforcement", "CITES implementation, and "capacity building". We then used descriptive and inferential statistics to investigate the status of "law enforcement", "capacity building" and "CITES implementation" and found that they are not uniform across species; however, the distribution of the number of actions across different categories in the past and present CAPs is not different. Among the four species studied, the CAP of Asian elephant showed 100% reported completion, as all recommended actions were achieved. Although completion of overall actions as well as "capacity building" and "law enforcement" is higher for the one-horned rhinoceros, the status of completion of CITES implementing actions is slightly higher for the Bengal tiger. Most of the actions were completed for the snow leopard for "capacity building" and "law enforcement" but the completion rate of "CITES implementation" is the least for that species suggesting a need for greater emphasis on completion of "CITES implementation" actions in the current CAPs. Though completion of "law enforcement" and "capacity building" actions was better, the consistently low completion rate for "CITES implementation" actions for all these species suggests pitfalls in CITES implementation.

articles.title: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular longevity-what is established, what is hypothesis?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular aging is the rate-limiting process for human life expectancy and healthspan. Nutrition and metabolism are the most widely available geroprotective targets, yet the underlying evidence is markedly uneven.

OBJECTIVE: To define which nutritional and metabolic interventions are established for cardiovascular longevity, or better healthy aging, and which remain hypothetical.

METHODS: Narrative review of randomized trials, cohort studies, and mechanistic work on dietary patterns, energy balance, meal timing, food quality, supplements, and biomarkers of biological aging.

RESULTS: Whole dietary patterns (Mediterranean, "Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension" [DASH], sodium reduction) reduce hard cardiovascular endpoints, and the causal roles of apolipoprotein B (apoB)-containing lipoproteins, blood pressure, and adiposity are firmly established. Pharmacologically induced weight loss via glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1)-based drugs reduces cardiovascular events to a degree not achieved by lifestyle programs, shifting clinical nutrition toward preservation of lean mass and micronutrient adequacy. By contrast, isolated nutrients and supplements, a specific geroprotective effect of intermittent fasting, and the clinical utility of epigenetic aging clocks remain unproven. Randomized caloric restriction slows the epigenetic pace of aging only modestly and has so far not demonstrated mortality benefit in humans.

CONCLUSION: Nutrition acts on cardiovascular longevity mainly through established risk factors rather than through demonstrated extension of maximum lifespan. Nutritional recommendations should make this distinction explicit, and longevity research requires endpoint-driven trials rather than surrogate markers only.

articles.title: Myeloid MANF attenuates ConA-induced immune-mediated hepatitis by restraining MIF-CD74-associated macrophage activation.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is a clinically heterogeneous immune-mediated liver disease that can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure. The mechanisms that sustain hepatic immune activation and drive disease progression remain incompletely defined. Mesencephalic astrocyte-derived neurotrophic factor (MANF) is an endoplasmic reticulum stress-responsive protein with anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, but its role in AIH is unclear.

METHODS: MANF expression was assessed in liver tissues from patients with AIH and in mice with concanavalin A (ConA)-induced immune-mediated hepatitis. Myeloid-targeted MANF knockout (MKO) mice, primary bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), macrophage-conditioned medium experiments, and pharmacologic MIF inhibition with ISO-1 were used to examine the contribution of myeloid MANF to liver injury and inflammatory signaling.

RESULTS: MANF immunoreactivity was increased in human AIH liver tissue and in ConA-challenged mouse liver and was enriched in CD68-positive cells. Myeloid MANF deletion aggravated ConA-induced hepatocellular injury, liver cell apoptosis, and inflammatory gene expression. MANF deficiency increased macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) expression and circulating MIF levels, was accompanied by increased CD74 expression, and enhanced PI3K/AKT and ERK phosphorylation. MANF re-expression reduced MIF and CD74 abundance and attenuated inflammatory gene expression in MANF-deficient macrophages, whereas CD74 knockdown suppressed PI3K/AKT and ERK phosphorylation and inflammatory transcription. ISO-1 partially reversed the aggravated inflammatory and liver-injury phenotypes associated with myeloid MANF deficiency in vivo and in vitro.

CONCLUSION: Myeloid-derived MANF restrains macrophage inflammatory activation and limits ConA-induced liver injury, at least in part through suppression of MIF-CD74-associated PI3K/AKT and ERK signaling. These findings identify the MANF-MIF/CD74 network as a candidate therapeutic axis in immune-mediated hepatitis, while further validation in larger human cohorts and receptor-specific models is required.

articles.title: The human post-mortem microbiome in forensic practice: a scoping review with critical appraisal.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The human post-mortem microbiome is increasingly investigated as a potential source of complementary information in forensic practice, particularly for post-mortem interval estimation and decomposition assessment. Its relevance to other medico-legal questions remains less clearly established.

OBJECTIVE: This scoping review aimed to map and critically assess the forensic applicability of microbial communities identified in human cadaveric and post-mortem biological samples, with particular attention to applications beyond post-mortem interval estimation.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for publications available up to 19 January 2026. Original human post-mortem studies were eligible. Data were extracted using a structured framework, and methodological quality was assessed using validated tools selected according to study design.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight studies were included, encompassing multiple external and internal biological matrices and predominantly bacterial profiling. Microbial succession related to decomposition and post-mortem interval represented the most extensively investigated directly forensic domain. Evidence concerning cause or manner of death, infection-related investigation, disease- or tissue-associated signatures, and sample preservation was more limited, while drowning was supported by a single proof-of-concept study. Across domains, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, contamination-related concerns, and limited external validation restricted forensic transferability.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-mortem microbial analysis remains an investigational adjunct rather than a validated standalone forensic tool. Progress toward routine implementation requires matrix-specific, contamination-controlled protocols and independent validation in larger, geographically diverse human cohorts.

articles.title: GWAS of winter hardiness and flowering time in autumn- versus spring-sown oats across five european sites: breeding implications.
articles.journal: TAG. Theoretical and applied genetics. Theoretische und angewandte Genetik
articles.abstract: Autumn sowing of spring oat in Central Europe improves yield and agronomic performance with genomic analyses highlighting VRN1- and VRN3-linked loci as breeding targets for winter resilience. Milder winters in Central Europe enable autumn sowing of spring oats, but risks and benefits still largely remain unclear. To address this knowledge gap, a panel of 250 spring oat lines was seeded in autumn and spring across five European sites over two seasons using unreplicated augmented designs with ten replicated controls. Winterkill varied by site, occurring in four experiments (including complete loss in one site-year), primarily due to insufficient snow cover and frost durations of more than four days between - 5 and - 8 °C. Canopy damage (CAN, scored with Canopeo app) had a heritability estimate of 0.55. Across all experiments, autumn sowing increased grain yield by 5-79% compared to spring sowing, driven by advanced development, lower mildew infection and extended tillering, though associated with higher lodging. GWAS (GAPIT3; 14,614 SNPs) identified 17 robust MTAs for winter hardiness, clustering on chromosomes 2D (novel), 4A and 4D (overlapping with VRN1), 6D, and 7D (near VRN3). Genomic prediction accuracy for CAN was 0.66. Based on our observations, we suggest that breeding should prioritize region-specific trials, winter oat crosses, and genomic selection to mitigate mycotoxin/lodging risks while exploiting yield gains in autumn sown oat.

articles.title: A dynamic craniospinal state-space framework for fluid and compartmental disorders: a conceptual and testable physiological model.
articles.abstract: The classical Monro-Kellie doctrine (MK 1.0) models the cranial vault as a rigid container of invariable volume, relying on mean intracranial pressure (ICP) and volumetric equilibrium. However, contemporary physiology indicates that intracranial homeostasis is fundamentally governed by craniospinal coupling, compliance reserve, vascular-venous dynamics, pulsatile shockwave transmission, and microscopic fluid exchange. Building upon recent dynamic formulations (MK 2.0-4.0), we propose Monro-Kellie 5.0 (MK 5.0) as a unified, testable craniospinal state-space framework. Rather than postulating a single disease mechanism, MK 5.0 models four clinically divergent craniospinal syndromes as distinct configurations within a six-domain dynamic state space: (1) Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (NPH) as a compliance-pulsatility mismatch driven by centripetal systolic pulse waves and periventricular shear strain despite conventionally normal mean ICP; (2) Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (IIH) as an outflow-pressure mismatch characterized by venous sinus resistance and transmural reabsorption failure; (3) Chiari I malformation with syringomyelia as a flow-transmission boundary obstruction across the foramen magnum resulting in systolic tonsillar piston impact and transmural intramedullary fluid driving; and (4) Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension (SIH) as a volume depletion and dural elastance collapse boundary. We mathematically formalize craniospinal coupling through an analog lumped-parameter circuit, derive its frequency-domain transfer function, and operationalize the model into prospective, falsifiable multivariable regression protocols (TOST equivalence) with prespecified power and sample size. By shifting focus from a single static pressure value to composite dynamic signatures, MK 5.0 provides a quantitative bridge between physical hydrodynamics and precision neurosurgery.

articles.title: MRI radiomics of pancreatic tumours: a systematic review of methodological quality and imaging reproducibility.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Radiomics holds potential for personalised treatment, but reproducibility is hindered by inconsistent reporting of imaging parameters and methodological details. This study aims to identify and evaluate key MR imaging parameters to support radiomics reproducibility and to systematically evaluate the quality of published MRI radiomics studies focused on pancreatic tumours.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The literature search was conducted in the Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases. Human studies investigating MRI radiomics in pancreatic tumours were included. An imaging reporting checklist was developed and used to identify and evaluate imaging parameters in eligible studies. The methodological quality score (METRICS) and checklist for evaluation of radiomics research (CLEAR) score were calculated for each study.

RESULTS: Seventy-eight studies, encompassing 241 MRI pulse sequences (143 anatomical and 98 functional), were included. The imaging checklist identified ten core items as key parameters for ensuring reproducible MRI radiomics. Across all studies, none provided complete or consistent reporting of these parameters, with frequent omissions in imaging acquisition and reconstruction details. Methodological and reporting quality remained suboptimal, reflected by median METRICS and CLEAR scores of 52.4% (45-60%) and 62.3% (56-69%), respectively. Reproducibility and quality of radiomics studies would benefit from clear reporting of imaging parameters, consistent documentation of radiomics settings, and control of confounding variables. Additionally, transparency in model validation, preprocessing, and explanation methods would further enhance reproducibility and clinical relevance.

CONCLUSION: A focused imaging reproducibility checklist has been developed, and it has been demonstrated that no pancreatic tumour MRI radiomics study reported all necessary imaging parameters for reproducibility. Methodological and reporting quality on broader radiomics components was also poor, highlighting the potential value of such a checklist for improving standardised reporting in radiomics studies.

KEY POINTS: Question There is inconsistent reporting of imaging parameters across MRI protocols used for pancreatic tumours radiomics analysis. Findings The developed MR imaging reporting checklist provides structured guidelines to promote consistent documentation of MR imaging parameters and support reproducible radiomics research. Relevance statement By identifying how key MR imaging acquisition and reconstruction parameters are currently presented in MRI radiomics studies of pancreatic tumours, this study highlights inconsistencies and omissions in reporting, underscoring the need for more transparent reporting and adherence to guidelines to support radiomics reproducibility.

articles.title: Reducing Hypothermia Among Intramural Vaginally Born Preterm Neonates Admitted in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at a Tertiary Care Centre Using Quality Improvement Approach: Correspondence-2.
Vaccination in Adult Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: An Updated Practical Approach.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Due to both disease-mediated and therapy-induced immunosuppression, patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of infections, including from vaccine preventable diseases (VPDs). As such, prevention through vaccination is a key aspect of longitudinal care to decrease infection-associated morbidity. In this review, we aim to outline a practical approach to vaccination in patients with IBD.

RECENT FINDINGS: The importance of vaccination for prevention of VPDs has been highlighted in multiple societal guideline updates. In recent years, these guidelines have expanded to include updated recommendations for coronavirus disease 2019, respiratory syncytial virus, and hepatitis B virus immunization. Additional guidance regarding use of live vaccines has also been provided. Having a practical and patient-centered approach to vaccination in patients with IBD is an important part of longitudinal care and prevention of morbidity. Herein we have highlighted risks of infection, the contributing role of immunosuppressive therapy, and comprehensively reviewed recommendations for and approach to vaccination.

articles.title: Hibiscus sabdariffa (roselle) dietary intervention modulates hematology disorders, oxidative stress, and immune suppression induced by tebuconazole exposure in Oreochromis niloticus via tlr/nfkβp65 and nrf2/keap1 gene expression.
articles.abstract: The objective of this research was to ascertain whether dietary roselle (Hibiscus sabdariffa) extract (ROE) could protect Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) from the negative impacts of the fungicide tebuconazole (TNZ). Fish (n = 160, weight = 20.16 ± 0.23 g) were assigned to four groups (40 fish each, with 10 fish per replicate) for a duration of 60 days. Basal meals containing 0% and 1% ROE were administered to the CRT (control) and ROE groups, respectively. The TNZ and ROE + TNZ groups were fed the exact meals as the CTR and ROE groups, respectively, and were subjected to 0.52 mg/L of TNZ. The splenic superoxide dismutase, catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and glutathione reductase activities were inhibited, while malondialdehyde was increased by TNZ exposure. The hematology indices, including red blood cells, hemoglobin, white blood cells, and their differential counts were lowered by TNZ exposure. TNZ toxicity raised the serum cortisol and glucose, while lowering the serum immune indices (lysozyme, complement 3, myeloperoxidase, and nitric oxide). The splenic expression of toll-like receptor 2, toll-like receptor 5, kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1, and nuclear factor kappa β subunit p65 was up-regulated, while nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 expression was down-regulated as a result of TNZ exposure. Furthermore, TNZ induced depletion of the lymphoid elements in the splenic tissues. ROE dietary addition (1%) enhanced the antioxidant responses and hematology of the TNZ-exposed fish. The ROE diet improved the splenic histology and modulated the splenic gene expression. Overall, ROE dietary fortification (1%) can be applied for the improvement of the immunological and antioxidant responses of Nile tilapia, especially under TNZ exposure conditions.

articles.title: Intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness: paradigm evolution from mechanistic understanding and standardized assessment to a holographic future.
articles.abstract: Hemodynamic disorders in critical illness extend beyond simple "hypotension" or "low cardiac output." They reflect decompensation of the cardiovascular system driven by the HOUR (Host/Organ Unregulated Response). In critical illness, the heart is not merely an isolated pump; it is also a central target and effector organ directly affected by systemic stress. This review summarizes advances in intracardiac hemodynamic assessment in critically ill patients. First, we describe hemodynamic mechanisms within the HOUR framework and emphasize the need to shift cardiac assessment from reliance on macroscopic parameters toward the study of intracardiac hemodynamics. Second, we discuss the methodological core, the "Intracardiac Hemodynamics 10-Step Assessment Process (10 s-ICEe)," which uses ten standardized steps to provide a systematic, closed-loop evaluation of the physiological pathway from venous return and transvalvular blood flow to arterial ejection. This process provides a practical link between mechanistic understanding and bedside decision-making in the ICU. Third, we examine how emerging technologies, including VFM, HyperDoppler, echoPIV, and 4D Flow MRI, are advancing assessment beyond one-dimensional velocity measurements toward multidimensional analysis of intracardiac vortices, energy loss, and blood flow vectors. We also consider the potential of "holographic cardiac assessment" to integrate structural, functional, blood flow, and perfusion information. This review aims to establish a comprehensive system for assessing intracardiac hemodynamics in critical illness, spanning basic assessment, advanced technologies, and integrated interpretation. It outlines the rationale and pathway for shifting hemodynamic management from structural observation to functional optimization, and from reliance on single parameters to system-level integration.

articles.title: Long-term trends in surgical site infection after elective groin hernia repair and their association with implementation of a preventive bundle: a 17-year multicenter cohort study.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Surgical site infection (SSI) after hernia repair is rarely evaluated in prospective multicenter cohorts with standardized surveillance. We described SSI trends over a 17-year study period and explored their association with a preventive bundle.

METHODS: Cohort of 17,531 elective groin hernia repairs (2009-2025, 16 Catalan VINCat hospitals) with active 30-day post-discharge surveillance; 2020 was excluded. The 2018 bundle was assessed by interrupted time series (ITS), propensity score-matched pre- versus post-bundle and pre- versus post-COVID comparisons, and regression with hospital fixed effects. Risk factors were explored by mixed-effects logistic regression adjusted for calendar time.

RESULTS: SSI incidence was 1.29% (226 cases; 95% CI 1.13-1.47), mostly superficial and post-discharge. Annual rates declined (Spearman rho - 0.594, p = 0.015). ITS level and slope changes were not significant (45 projected avoided infections; 95% CI - 12 to 168). Matched incidence was 1.47% pre-bundle versus 1.07% post-bundle (OR 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.00, p = 0.051), but with hospital fixed effects the OR was 0.97 (95% CI 0.68-1.39) in the six hospitals contributing to both periods, whose ITS showed no change. Full adherence was documented in 8.7% of post-bundle procedures. Open approach, longer procedure duration, clean-contaminated wound class and female sex were associated with SSI.

CONCLUSION: Over 17 years, SSI after elective groin hernia repair was low and declining. The lower incidence after bundle implementation was not significant, was not apparent within hospitals, although power to detect a within-hospital effect was limited; the association is exploratory. Incomplete documentation of adherence prevented its evaluation and is a target for improvement.

articles.title: HIV-1 Vpr-Mediated GSK-3β SUMOylation Induces Tau Phosphorylation and Neurodegeneration.
articles.abstract: HIV-1-associated neurocognitive disorder (HAND) has emerged as a prevalent and debilitating neurological disorder. Analogous to Alzheimer's disease (AD), HAND manifests Tau hyper-phosphorylation and heightened activity of the tau kinase GSK-3β. Nonetheless, the exact underlying mechanism driving neurodegeneration in the context of HIV-1 infection remains elusive. In this study, we unveil that the HIV-1 accessory protein Vpr augments GSK-3β SUMOylation and exacerbates Tau hyper-phosphorylation. Notably, GSK-3β SUMOylation is essential for Vpr instigating Tau hyper-phosphorylation. Vpr enhances GSK-3β SUMOylation at K183 site, consequently bolstering its stability and enzymatic activity. Furthermore, we identify SIM (SUMO interacting motifs)- 2 within Vpr as the pivotal sequence responsible for promoting GSK-3β SUMOylation. Significantly, Vpr triggers GSK-3β SUMOylation, Tau hyper-phosphorylation, synaptic impairment, and cognitive deficits in a murine model, whereas Vpr bearing mutations in SIM2 proves to be ineffective. Consequently, our findings suggest that HIV-1 Vpr contributes to Tau hyper-phosphorylation potentially through enhancing GSK-3β SUMOylation at the K183 site. This provides novel insights into the mechanisms by which HIV-1 compromises the central nervous system, precipitating neurocognitive disorder.

articles.title: Neuropsychiatric outcomes after decompressive craniectomy and cranioplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Neuropsychiatric morbidity after decompressive craniectomy (DC) is increasingly recognised, but prevalence and trajectories remain unclear. We aimed to examine psychiatric and cognitive outcomes post-DC. The systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO-CRD 420251106085) followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Medline, Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases were searched through October 2025. Eligible studies included validated psychometric and cognitive tools to assess psychiatric and cognitive outcomes post-DC. The Random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled prevalence. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², and meta-regression explored sources of variability. Longitudinal outcomes after cranioplasty were analysed separately. Twenty-four studies were included in the qualitative analysis (N = 877), and 12 were included in the meta-analysis (N = 305). The pooled prevalence of depression was 47% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 40-54%, I²=20.2% [95% CI: 0-58.9%]), and anxiety, from four studies, was 46% (95% CI: 38-54%, I²=0% [95% CI: 0-84.7%]). Limited longitudinal data available from two studies showed a reduction in anxiety and depression after cranioplasty, with large effect sizes at 12 months (anxiety: p < 0.001, g = 5.36; depression: p < 0.001, g = 5.04). However, the effect sizes may have been inflated due to small cohorts included in these studies. Among the six studies reporting severity, the rates of moderate depression ranged from 8.3​​% to 45.5%, and severe depression from 9.1% to 36.4% across assessment tools. Most of the included studies showed improved cognitive outcome post-cranioplasty, however quantitative analysis was not possible due to varied study design. A considerable proportion of post-DC patients experience depression and anxiety. Selective screening can improve early detection and resource allocation. Future studies should focus on developing targeted patient pathways.

articles.title: Gold nanoparticles as a therapeutic strategy for Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and exploratory quantitative synthesis.
articles.abstract: Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) offer significant potential in advancing treatments for neurological diseases like Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aims to systematically review GNP effects in PD animal models and conduct an exploratory quantitative synthesis of their impact on behavioral and cellular outcomes. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched on October 10, 2024 using keywords "nanoparticle," "Parkinson," "delivery," and "therapy." Ten studies met the inclusion criteria for in vivo mammalian PD models treated with GNPs, utilizing various rodent models and GNP formulations. Three random-effects meta-analyses were performed on general locomotor activity, motor coordination, and dopaminergic system integrity; oxidative stress markers were summarized descriptively. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges' g standardized mean difference. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE's tool for animal studies. Given the limited studies and high heterogeneity, these analyses were evaluated on an exploratory basis. Across 10 pooled rodent comparisons, GNPs showed a large but imprecise rotarod effect (g = 2.33, 95% CI 0.04 to 4.62; k = 4) and improved open field activity (g = 0.89, 95% CI 0.02 to 1.76; k = 3). The dopaminergic estimate was also positive but imprecise (g = 3.31, 95% CI - 2.63 to 9.26; k = 3). Unpooled oxidative-stress markers (k = 2) showed directionally supportive results. Risk of bias analysis were majority unclear. GNPs demonstrated preliminary signals of efficacy across behavioral, dopaminergic, and oxidative stress outcomes, highlighting their potential as a therapeutic strategy. The evidence is limited by small sample sizes, statistical imprecision, methodological heterogeneity, and a predominantly unclear risk of bias; therefore, these results are strong hypothesis-generating findings that require further preclinical data and exploration. Standardization of protocols and larger scale confirmatory studies are required to enhance reproducibility and generalizability, with the goal of ultimately advancing GNPs toward clinical translation. No funding was received. Registered on PROSPERO (ID: CRD42025636600).

articles.title: Complication-specific risk profiles after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: age effects and Age-sex interaction.
articles.abstract: Major complications after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) are often analyzed within shared clinical risk frameworks despite important pathophysiological differences between complications such as vasospasm and posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus.
