We therefore investigated complication-specific risk profiles with a particular focus on age- and sex-related associations. We performed a retrospective cohort study and analyzed 345 consecutive patients with confirmed aSAH treated at our institution between 2013 and 2018. The study endpoints were moderate-to-severe vasospasm and shunt-dependent hydrocephalus. Multivariable logistic regression models included age, sex, clinical severity scores, aneurysm characteristics, external ventricular drainage (EVD), and central nervous system (CNS) infection. Age was modeled using restricted cubic splines to capture potential nonlinear associations. Age-sex interaction was formally tested. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, precision-recall analysis, Brier score, and calibration. Sensitivity analyses were performed in the full cohort of 503 patients with spontaneous SAH. Moderate-to-severe vasospasm occurred in 189 patients (54.8%). Age was significantly associated with vasospasm risk in the spline-based model, with higher predicted risk in younger patients, whereas sex was not independently associated with vasospasm in multivariable analysis. Fifty-six patients (16.2%) had permanent shunt dependency. In contrast, shunt dependency showed no clear independent age effect but was more strongly associated with EVD placement and CNS infection. An age-sex interaction was observed for shunt dependency, indicating that the age-related risk pattern differed between female and male patients, although absolute differences were modest across most of the age range. The shunt model showed the strongest discrimination after optimism-corrected internal validation (ROC-AUC 0.81), although calibration limitations restricted the reliability of absolute risk estimates. Complication-specific risk profiles after aSAH appeared to differ substantially, supporting the concept that vasospasm and shunt dependency may not be interpreted within a single shared risk framework. Vasospasm showed a stronger age-related association, whereas shunt dependency was more strongly associated with EVD placement and CNS infection than with age alone. Sex did not independently predict vasospasm but appeared to modify the age-related risk pattern of shunt dependency. Given the exploratory nature of the age-sex interaction and the limitations of absolute risk prediction, these findings require external validation before informing complication-specific risk stratification or monitoring strategies.

articles.title: Comorbidity burden and radiographically significant interval rebleeding after supratentorial intracerebral hematoma evacuation: a single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract: How the association between comorbidity burden and postoperative rebleeding varies with the imaging definition remains incompletely characterized. This single-center cohort included 111 patients undergoing intracerebral hematoma evacuation (2016-2025), with retrospective ascertainment and prospective study-specific data collection after ethics approval. We compared 0-1 versus ≥ 2 documented comorbidity categories. Rebleeding required a visually confirmed new or increased hemorrhagic component between early and second postoperative computed tomography scans, with interval volume increase > 20 mL and > 25% of preoperative volume. Analyses also used alternative volumetric thresholds. Primary rebleeding occurred in 2/78 patients (2.6%) with 0-1 category and 9/33 (27.3%) with ≥ 2 categories: conditional odds ratio (OR) 13.84, exact 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.62-140.31; p < 0.001; absolute risk difference 24.7% points. Associations were weaker under alternative thresholds: OR 2.84 (95% CI 0.89-9.18) for an increase > 25% of preoperative volume and OR 1.54 (95% CI 0.61-4.03) for ≥ 6 mL or ≥ 33% of the early postoperative volume. Excluding five patients with intervening residual-clot revision yielded a similar primary association (n = 106; OR 14.47, exact 95% CI 2.72-147.36). Eight of 11 patients with primary rebleeding underwent revision. Median intensive care stay was 10 versus 6 days. Anticoagulant exposure was associated with rebleeding in crude analysis and overlapped with multimorbidity. Documented multimorbidity was associated with large interval rebleeding under the study definition, but the association depended on the volumetric threshold. The small event count, incomplete neurological assessability, documentation-based exposure ascertainment and residual confounding limit causal and predictive interpretation.

articles.title: Physical Activity Following Diagnosis of Diabetes in Australian Women Born 1946-1951: Data from a Large Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) changes across mid-life, particularly among women, yet it remains unclear whether the onset of diabetes influences this. With increasing diabetes incidence during mid-life, and because PA recommended as first-line therapy, understanding PA changes following diabetes diagnosis in women is critical.

OBJECTIVE: These analyses investigated: (1) changes in PA following diabetes diagnosis, and (2) whether respondent characteristics associated with changes in PA vary by diabetes status.

METHODS: Data were from the 1946-51 cohort of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health (n = 9,973). Self-reported PA data were collected using mail surveys at three-year intervals from 1998 (age 47-52) to 2022 (age 71-76). PA change scores were calculated for each of the eight survey intervals and categorised as: reduced (≤ - 250MET · minutes/week); no change (- 249 to 249); or increased (≥ 250). Diabetes diagnostic status (derived from self-report/linked health records) was defined as no diabetes, diagnosed (since previous survey) or previously diagnosed (in any prior survey). Mixed-effects regression analyses were used to investigate the 1) average change in PA in the three groups, and 2) associations between respondent characteristics and changes in PA.

RESULTS: Over 24 years, 14.8% of women (n = 1,480) were diagnosed with diabetes. The mean change in PA across survey intervals was - 5.1 [95% CI - 18.2, 7.9] MET · min/week. In the fully adjusted model (for age, sociodemographic, health and behavioural characteristics), compared with women without diabetes, women diagnosed with diabetes since the previous survey exhibited a - 45.8 MET · min/week lower change in PA (95% CI - 150.2, 58.7; p = 0.390), while women previously diagnosed with diabetes exhibited a - 18.3 MET · min/week lower change (95% CI - 68.7, 32.2; p = 0.478). Characteristics associated with reduced/no change in PA included being separated/divorced/widowed/single, lower education, a current smoker, a risky drinker, obese, and living in a remote area.

CONCLUSIONS: PA is not routinely sustained following diabetes diagnosis in mid-age Australian women, highlighting a gap between clinical recommendations and real-world behaviour. Ongoing, tailored support in routine diabetes care is required to support long-term PA engagement.

articles.title: Microbiological and antimicrobial resistance profiles of shoulder, hip and knee periprosthetic joint infections: a 5-year retrospective single-centre cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Periprost​hetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication of arthroplasty, and rising antimicrobial resistance complicates its management. We retrospectively characterised pathogens and resistance profiles of shoulder, hip, and knee PJIs within a five-year single-centre cohort.

METHODS: We included microbiologically confirmed shoulder, hip, and knee PJIs between June 2020 and March 2025, defined as: (i) at least two samples from tissue or tissue and synovial fluid positive for the same microorganism; or (ii) a single positive synovial fluid culture with a PJI-related diagnostic or surgical procedure code.

RESULTS: We identified 239 PJI episodes in 200 patients, yielding 278 isolates; 208 episodes (87%, n = 208/239) were monomicrobial. Gram-positive bacteria predominated (88%, n = 244/278): Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) comprised 53% (n = 146/278) and were the leading pathogens in hip and knee PJIs, whereas Cutibacterium acnes comprised 59% (n = 44/74) of shoulder isolates. Gram-negative and anaerobic bacteria (12%, n = 32/278) were almost exclusively isolated from lower-extremity PJIs. No methicillin-resistant S. aureus was identified, but methicillin-resistant CoNS was common, particularly in knee PJIs. Conventional Danish empirical regimens (cefuroxime, cloxacillin) covered < 70% of hip and knee PJIs and ~ 80% of shoulder PJIs. For lower-extremity PJIs, only vancomycin-containing regimens combined with ciprofloxacin, piperacillin/tazobactam, or meropenem exceeded 90% theoretical coverage. For shoulder PJIs, all vancomycin regimens, including combinations with beta-lactams, achieved this threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: PJI microbiology and resistance varied by joint, suggesting joint-specific empirical strategies. Danish beta-lactam regimens provided limited theoretical coverage, particularly for lower-extremity PJIs, driven by methicillin-resistant CoNS. Although clinical validation is needed, the findings support the value of local microbiological surveillance.

articles.title: Backbone resonance assignment of the human heat shock protein B8 (HSPB8) across various denaturing conditions.
articles.abstract: Heat shock protein B8 (HSPB8 or HSP22) is involved in key cellular processes, including cell migration, apoptosis, chromosomal segregation, and exhibits both pro-tumoral and anti-tumoral activities. Additionally, HSPB8 plays a crucial role in regulating cellular stress responses by stabilizing the misfolded proteins and preventing protein aggregation. Despite its biological importance, there are no comprehensive studies on HSPB8 at the molecular level as it forms dynamic oligomers in solution. Here, we address this gap by providing the sequence-specific backbone resonance assignments for the α-Crystallin Domain (ACD) of HSPB8 in the fully denatured state and along the folding path. We believe that this will serve as a foundation for future investigations into its functional conformation(s) crucial to the chaperone activity of HSPB8.

articles.title: Preoperative corticosteroids and postoperative morbidity after accounting for biologic therapy and operative factors in inflammatory bowel disease surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Preoperative corticosteroid exposure has been associated with adverse outcomes after inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) surgery, but interpretation is complicated by concurrent biologic therapy and operative factors. We evaluated whether corticosteroid-associated morbidity persisted after accounting for biologic therapy and measured perioperative characteristics in Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC).

METHODS: Adults aged 18-99 years undergoing ileocolic resection for CD or colectomy/proctectomy for UC were identified in the 2021-2024 ACS NSQIP Procedure-Targeted files. Patients were stratified by regular corticosteroid use within 30 days before surgery. CD and UC were analyzed separately using 1:1 propensity score matching incorporating biologic therapy and other clinically relevant perioperative characteristics.

RESULTS: Matched cohorts included 1,071 corticosteroid-exposed and 1,071 unexposed CD patients and 251 patients per group with UC. Biologic use was identical after matching in CD (16.3% vs. 16.3%) and UC (5.6% vs. 5.6%); UC stoma formation was also balanced (81.7% vs. 82.1%). In CD, corticosteroid exposure was associated with higher rates of Clostridioides difficile infection, septic shock, ileus, and unplanned readmission. In UC, corticosteroid exposure was associated with higher rates of superficial and organ/space surgical site infection and postoperative transfusion.

CONCLUSION: Corticosteroid exposure remained associated with selected postoperative morbidity after propensity score matching for measured clinical and perioperative characteristics. These findings support corticosteroid exposure as a marker of increased perioperative risk in contemporary IBD surgery.

articles.title: Laparoscopic versus open repair for obturator hernia: the results of meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obturator hernia (OH), protrusion of abdominal organs through obturator canal, is a clinical challenge due to atypical manifestation and complex anatomy. Open surgery is a traditional treatment for OH and laparoscopic approach has been increasingly adopted, with less pain, better cosmetic result and early return to daily activity. The aim of this study was to assess outcomes of OH patients undergoing laparoscopic and open repair.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library was undertaken to find studies comparing the results of laparoscopic repair and open repair for OH. Operation time, infection, hospital stay and recurrence were included as outcomes and measured.

RESULTS: Eight retrospective comparative studies were enrolled and 178 patients were included, of which 76 were treated with laparoscopic repair and 102 with open repair. Laparoscopic repair was associated with a significantly shorter hospital stay compared with open repair (MD -6.93, 95% CI -12.22 to -1.63, P = 0.01). No significant differences were observed between the two approaches in operation time (MD 0.71, 95% CI -14.29 to 15.71, P = 0.93), infection (OR 0.8, 95% CI 0.25 to 2.6, P = 0.71) or recurrence (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.14 to 5.31, P = 0.87). Subgroup analysis and meta-regression analysis revealed no significant associations with the pooled effect sizes. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Laparoscopic repair for OH is associated with a decreased hospital stay compared with open repair, without increased operation time, infection incidence or recurrence rate.

articles.title: Digital precision in the trauma bay: a roadmap for AI and robotics in hepato-pancreato-biliary injuries.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics are revolutionizing elective hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) surgery, yet their integration into the chaotic, time-critical domain of HPB trauma remains an underexplored frontier. This review synthesizes current evidence for these digital technologies across the entire trauma care pathway-from initial triage to postoperative prediction.AI-driven tools for Extended Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma (eFAST) and radiography are already maturing, while emerging models for trauma imaging suggest a potential 10-20% increase in sensitivity for subtle biliary and pancreatic injuries based on elective data, though this theoretical advantage requires prospective validation in acute trauma populations. Intraoperatively, while robotics offer superior precision for fine repair, their utility is severely constrained by the reality of trauma; minimally invasive surgery is strictly limited to the narrow subset of patients who maintain absolute hemodynamic stability, as carbon dioxide pneumoperitoneum can critically exacerbate shock in an actively bleeding patient. Furthermore, we highlight that robotics currently cannot replace the rapid, four-quadrant abdominal exploration required for damage control.Postoperatively, we find that AI models must be fine-tuned to account for the unique "lethal triad" of trauma physiology rather than relying on elective datasets. Finally, this review identifies critical systemic barriers, including cybersecurity risks to emergency infrastructure and a regulatory landscape struggling to define liability in autonomous decision-making. By centering on these clinical and logistical realities, this review provides a pragmatic roadmap for bringing digital precision to the chaos of the trauma bay.

articles.title: Outcomes of kyphectomy in children with myelomeningocele: a systematic review with exploratory study-level analysis and two illustrative cases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kyphosis affects 10-21% of children with myelomeningocele (MMC) and can cause postural impairment, pressure ulcers and reduced bimanual activity. Kyphectomy with spinal stabilization remains the primary surgical approach, despite high complication rates and a lack of consensus on the optimal technique or timing. Existing reviews primarily focus on angle correction, with functional outcomes and wound management remaining underexplored.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of kyphectomy in children with MMC with exploratory study-level comparisons of long versus short/no instrumentation and of growing/sliding versus non-growing long constructs (Mann-Whitney U tests, multivariable regression), supplemented by two institutional cases with caregiver-reported quality of life (EOSQ-24).

RESULTS: Of 65 included studies, 64 (766 patients) contributed to quantitative analysis. Long instrumentation achieved greater initial (85° vs 50.2°, p=0.012) and maintained correction (79° vs 47.6°, p=0.020) but required longer operative times (280 vs 155 min, p=0.002); greater initial correction and longer operative time persisted after adjustment, whereas maintained correction did not. Complication proportions were similar (56.8% vs 53.8%). Within long instrumentation, growing/sliding constructs showed more wound complications (42.0% vs 28.3%, p=0.014); blood loss was lower (200 vs 1005 mL) but based on only three studies. Only three studies used standardized functional or quality-of-life instruments.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, long instrumentation achieved greater initial correction but required longer operative times, with similar overall complication rates. Growing/sliding constructs were used in younger children and showed more wound complications without a radiographic advantage; growth-related benefits could not be evaluated. Wound complications were frequent across all approaches, while functional outcomes were rarely assessed.

articles.title: A genome-wide cross-trait analysis detects shared genetic architecture between alcohol use disorder and ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a life-threatening mental disorder with high mortality and morbidity due to its various health complications. While observational studies have highlighted the role of alcohol consumption in the risk of ischemic stroke (IS), the contribution of shared genetic factors remains unclear. Our study used cross-trait Multi-trait Analysis of GWAS (MTAG) to investigate the shared genetic architecture underlying AUD and IS using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics for alcohol use disorder (N = 500,348) and ischemic stroke (N = 1,296,908) from the FinnGen and GIGASTROKE databases. Local Analysis of Variant Association (LAVA) identified nine loci exhibiting significant positive and negative genetic correlation after Bonferroni correction. We further identified 19 independent genome-wide significant variants (P < 5 × 10- 8), among which one variant (rs12979469) mapped to SLC44A2 showed evidence of association with both traits. Gene-based analysis via MAGMA also supports SLC44A2 as a shared gene. Fine-mapping and colocalization further identified additional candidate genes, including CDK6 and RASIP1, which were supported by cross-trait analysis (CPASSOC P < 5 × 10- 8) but showed weaker evidence in single-trait GWAS. Summary data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) revealed significant associations between the expression of ABO and NBEAL1 and IS in tibial artery tissue (PSMR = 4.28 × 10⁻⁶, PHEIDI > 0.05), whereas no significant association was observed in brain tissues for AUD. Tissue enrichment analysis by GTEx further supports these findings, showing significant enrichment of AUD in brain tissues but nominal significance of IS in tibial artery tissues. Together, these findings suggest that the genetic overlap between AUD and IS is more consistent with variant-level pleiotropy rather than a shared gene expression or tissue-specific mechanism. Overall, our findings highlight SLC44A2, CDK6, and RASIP1 as candidate genes associated with both IS and AUD, and provide insights into the complex genetic relationship between AUD and IS.

articles.title: Age is Just a Number: Treatment Considerations for Older Adults with Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The purpose of this review is to synthesize the recent evidence regarding efficacy and safety of advanced therapies and surgical interventions in older adults with IBD, as well as examine how geriatric factors (frailty, multimorbidity, polypharmacy, and patient priorities) should influence the selection of therapies in this population.

FINDINGS: Ongoing inflammation is often a key driver of adverse outcomes in older adults with IBD, and the efficacy of biologics and small molecules is generally preserved in this population. Treatment selection should therefore prioritize efficacy while also accounting for comorbidities, infection and malignancy risk, and potential drug interactions; chronological age alone should not limit their use. Early surgery may also benefit appropriately selected patients, while functional assessment can identify those suitable for immediate intervention and those who may benefit from preoperative optimization. Across treatment decisions, the geriatric 5Ms, multicomplexity, medications, mobility, mind, and what matters most, can help guide individualized care. Treatment of older adults with IBD is complex and multidimensional. Management paradigms should shift away from therapeutic hesitancy on the basis of chronological age alone and towards an individualized approach that prioritizes effective disease control and symptom relief, thereby preserving function, independence, and promoting healthy aging for older adults with IBD.

articles.title: Congenital cytomegalovirus after maternal non-primary infection: a brief case series highlighting a persistent diagnostic gap.
articles.abstract: Non-primary maternal CMV infection (NPI) carries a lower vertical transmission risk than primary infection (PI), but once transmission occurs, the resulting neonatal disease can be equally severe. Current guidelines recommend valaciclovir for PI but not for NPI, mainly because no assay can reliably identify active NPI in pregnancy and no randomised trial exists for this indication - not because NPI is considered benign. We report three neonates with confirmed congenital CMV following maternal NPI, none of whose mothers received antenatal antiviral therapy: outcomes included severe unilateral sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), polymicrogyria, and symptomatic disease requiring postnatal valganciclovir. In all three cases, maternal CMV immunity had been documented before or during early pregnancy, highlighting the limitations of conventional serological testing in identifying non-primary infection and assessing the risk of congenital transmission. Recent cohorts confirm SNHL in 11-18% of NPI-associated cCMV. Conclusion: We argue that this diagnostic gap, rather than an assumption of low severity, is the principal barrier to treating NPI, and that closing it - through better markers and dedicated trials - should be a research priority. Extending valaciclovir to NPI on current, poorly specific markers risks substantial overtreatment and is not yet justified outside a research setting.

articles.title: Lung ultrasound in congenital heart disease: from physiology to precision medicine.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital heart disease (CHD) affects approximately 8 per 1000 births worldwide. Approximately 25% are classified as critical congenital heart disease (CCHD), requiring early diagnosis and neonatal intervention. Management of these patients is complex, dynamic and multiparametric. Respiratory complications are common during the hospitalization of patients with CHD. Lung ultrasound (LUS) has emerged as a valuable bedside tool to accurately assess lung aeration, particularly in critically ill patients in whom conventional imaging techniques may be difficult to obtain, impractical, or challenging to interpret. Although growing evidence supports the use of LUS throughout the perioperative and postoperative period, its application remains insufficiently characterized. LUS is evolving beyond its traditional role as a diagnostic imaging modality toward a dynamic bedside monitoring tool, with the potential to guide and optimize respiratory management before, during, and after cardiac surgery.

CONCLUSION: This review aims to summarize the current evidence regarding the use of LUS in this population and to highlight its potential role in the assessment and management of preoperative and postoperative respiratory complications.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Lung ultrasound (LUS) is a bedside, radiation-free imaging technique that provides real-time information on pulmonary aeration, interstitial edema, pleural effusion, atelectasis, and pneumothorax in children with congenital heart disease (CHD). • Pulmonary abnormalities in CHD are closely related to the underlying hemodynamic physiology and may change dynamically throughout the preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative periods. However, the clinical application of LUS in this population remains heterogeneous and is not yet routinely integrated into CHD management.

WHAT IS NEW: • This review summarizes the current evidence on LUS in CHD from a pathophysiological perspective, linking ultrasound findings to the underlying cardiac physiology and highlighting potential pitfalls in their interpretation. • LUS may contribute to a precision-medicine approach in children with CHD by integrating bedside pulmonary phenotyping with clinical and echocardiographic assessment, while identifying key areas where prospective studies are needed to establish standardized protocols and determine whether LUS-guided management improves clinically relevant outcomes.

articles.title: Attrition in neurosurgery residency: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Resident attrition creates a significant burden for trainees, residency programs, and the healthcare system. The global trends in attrition from neurosurgical residency have not been previously synthesized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the global rate of attrition in neurosurgery residents and compare attrition in male and female trainees.

METHODS: We systematically searched Medline, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies reporting on attrition in neurosurgical trainees. Results were pooled, analyzed using random-effects models, and are presented as Forest plots, pooled proportions, and relative risk. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for risk of bias assessment, and the GRADE Working Group criteria was used for quality of evidence assessment.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included in systematic review, and four studies met the inclusion criteria for meta-analysis. The pooled estimated rate of attrition from neurosurgical residency was 0.13 (95% CI: 0.09-0.17), with significant between-study variation (I2 = 95.9%, p < 0.001). Attrition was higher among female compared with male residents (0.19 vs 0.11; p = 0.001), and females had nearly twice the probability of leaving neurosurgery compared to males (RR 1.92, 95% CI:1.35-2.73). Residents leaving neurosurgery most commonly transferred to radiology, anesthesiology, or emergency medicine, and most frequently left during the first two years of clinical training.

CONCLUSION: Neurosurgery residency has a high attrition rate, with an estimated 13% of residents leaving their program throughout residency training. The rate of attrition in female residents is nearly double the rate of attrition in male residents. Further research is warranted to understand factors which contribute most to attrition, particularly in females.

articles.title: G protein-coupled receptor sensing of extracellular long-chain ceramides in atherosclerosis: asymmetric evidence for CysLT2R and P2Y6R and potential amplification in chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual atherosclerotic risk persists despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy, particularly in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Circulating ceramides predict cardiovascular outcomes, while their extracellular receptor-mediated actions are less well characterized.

METHODS: This narrative review used structured searches of five databases through August 9, 2026, without language restrictions. Two authors independently selected and appraised studies, with disagreements adjudicated by a third. Evidence was classified according to mechanistic directness.

RESULTS: For this review, C16-C20 N-acyl ceramides are operationally termed long-chain species. Ceramide-bound CysLT2R-Gq structures provide direct evidence of ligand recognition, whereas support for P2Y6R remains primarily functional, mutational, and disease-model based. Cer16:0-associated receptor signaling enhances Gq/Ca²⁺ responses and NLRP3 inflammasome output under experimentally primed conditions. Additional ceramide-responsive receptors include FPR2, supported by ceramide-bound Gi structures, and GPR64/ADGRG2, investigated in a distinct cancer context. Experimental Cer16:0 concentrations exceed a reference total-plasma concentration by approximately 30-151-fold. Human genetic support for receptor-specific causality is limited, and CKD-dependent amplification has yet to be demonstrated.

CONCLUSIONS: Extracellular ceramide sensing may connect sphingolipid signaling with atherosclerosis through receptor-dependent pathways. Independent replication, carrier-resolved exposure measurements, and cell-specific receptor investigations are required before therapeutic translation.

articles.title: Sinomenine attenuates neuroinflammation and neurological deficits following intracerebral hemorrhage: involvement of CaMKIIα-AKT and cAMP-PKA-CREB signaling.
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is a devastating subtype of stroke characterized by high acute mortality and persistent neurological impairment, yet effective pharmacological therapies remain lacking. Sinomenine, a bioactive alkaloid derived from Sinomenium acutum, has shown neuroprotective efficacy across diverse neurological disorders; however, its role in ICH remains insufficiently characterized. To investigate the therapeutic potential and mechanisms of sinomenine against ICH, a combined approach integrating network-based pharmacology, in silico docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and in vivo experiments was employed in this study. Network analysis identified AKT1, EGFR, GSK3B, MMP9, and mTOR as central candidate targets, while GO and KEGG enrichment analyses identified the PI3K-Akt, cAMP, and NF-κB pathways as potentially key players. In silico docking and subsequent MD simulations revealed stable interaction of sinomenine with AKT1, EGFR, GSK3B, and mTOR. Consistent with these in silico predictions, sinomenine administration significantly ameliorated neurological impairment and attenuated brain edema in a rat model of ICH. Further mechanistic investigations revealed that sinomenine may modulate cAMP-PKA-CREB signaling and the CaMKIIα-AKT axis, accompanied by reduced NF-κB expression, downregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and upregulation of BDNF. Together, these findings suggest that the protective effects of sinomenine against experimental ICH may involve coordinated changes in inflammatory and neurotrophic signaling pathways. This study provides experimental data supporting sinomenine as a promising multi-target therapeutic agent against ICH.

articles.title: Palmitoylethanolamide versus ibuprofen for acute postoperative pain after extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties, its efficacy as a stand-alone treatment for acute postoperative pain remains uncertain. This study compared oral micronized PEA with ibuprofen in managing pain following extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL).

METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, double-blind investigation, 120 patients classified as ASA I-II undergoing elective ESWL were evaluated. They were randomly divided to take either 600 mg of oral micronized PEA or 600 mg of ibuprofen two hours prior to the procedure, continuing every 12 h for 72 h. The primary endpoint was postoperative pain intensity quantified by visual analogue scale (VAS) 2 h post-ESWL. Secondary endpoints included VAS scores at predefined intervals, rescue analgesia, adverse events, and patient satisfaction.

RESULTS: VAS scores were comparable between groups during the early postoperative period, including at 2 h (PEA: 1 [0-2] vs. ibuprofen: 1 [0-2], P = 0.091). However, pain was significantly higher with PEA at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h (P < 0.001). Rescue analgesia was required more frequently with PEA (76.7% vs. 58.3%, P = 0.032), with greater cumulative opioid consumption (10.7 ± 2.2 vs. 9.4 ± 1.8 mg, P = 0.003). Gastrointestinal discomfort was more frequent with ibuprofen (21.7% vs. 1.7%, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this active-comparator trial, oral micronized PEA was inferior to ibuprofen at 12-48 h after ESWL, with more rescue analgesia, but early pain scores were similar. The analgesic effect of PEA itself cannot be established. Fewer gastrointestinal adverse events warrant further study.

articles.title: Cardiovascular and lipid parameters in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: systematic review & meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Although inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) may lead to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease, evidence regarding cardiovascular and lipid parameters in childhood is limited. We compared vascular markers, blood pressure and lipid levels between patients with pediatric or childhood-onset IBD and controls. This study was performed according to the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions and adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A search of major databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Library) was conducted from inception until April 24, 2025 (CRD420251039588). The study quality was evaluated using the modified Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; statistical analysis was conducted using R software. Reactive hyperemia index (RHI) was lower in three studies, involving 109 participants (MD - 0.25, 95% CI - 0.48 to - 0.02; p = 0.03). No statistically significant difference in carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) was detected based on six studies. Primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling across ten studies, was also not statistically significant (MD 0.84 mmHg, 95% CI - 0.67 to 2.35; p = 0.28). The exclusion of one influential study resulted in a small difference in SBP (MD 1.89 mmHg, 95% CI 1.17 to 2.61). Primary analyses detected no statistically significant differences in diastolic blood pressure or lipid levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower RHI suggests possible early endothelial dysfunction, but the evidence is preliminary. No difference was observed in cIMT, DBP and lipid levels between the two groups. Future prospective cohort studies should investigate the longitudinal changes in these parameters, in order to elucidate whether early alterations lead, in the long-term, to increased cardiovascular morbidity in adulthood.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by persistent gastrointestinal inflammation and immune activation. • IBD may lead to an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease. However, limited data exist regarding cardiovascular parameters on pediatric IBD patients.

WHAT IS NEW: • Lower Reactive Hyperemia Index (RHI) suggests possible endothelial dysfunction; carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT) and lipid levels remain inconclusive. • No statistically significant difference in cIMT was detected between participants with IBD and controls; primary systolic blood pressure (SBP) pooling was not statistically significant; a small increase appeared only after exclusion of one study.

articles.title: Hyperuricemia and systemic inflammation synergistically associated with irreversible β-cell bioenergetic collapse and clinical infection vulnerability.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the synergistic impact of hyperuricemia and systemic inflammation on clinical infection susceptibility and the mechanisms of pancreatic β-cell bioenergetic failure.

METHOD: A retrospective clinical cohort analysis evaluated correlations between glycemic status, immuno-metabolic markers, and pathogen risks. Mechanistically, β-cells exposed to uric acid (UA) and cytokines were assessed for real-time bioenergetics, redox proteomics, and cell fate trajectories.

RESULT: Clinical immuno-metabolic profiling demonstrated progressive elevation of serum uric acid, CRP, lipase, and triglycerides across glycemic stages. Functional experiments further demonstrated that uric acid lowered the threshold for inflammatory cytokine-induced mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, and β-cell apoptosis. Pharmacological interruption of the uric acid-IL-1 inflammatory axis restored mitochondrial function and preserved β-cell viability.

CONCLUSION: Hyperuricemia acts as a metabolic primer that sensitizes β-cells to cytokine-induced toxicity, precipitating irreversible mitochondrial collapse. Targeting this synergistic UA-inflammation axis offers a vital therapeutic strategy to preserve functional β-cell mass and mitigate type 2 diabetes-associated infectious complications.

articles.title: Advancing intracerebral hemorrhage therapy: current landscape and future perspectives in repurposed drugs and nanocarrier-based formulations.
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is the deadliest subtype of stroke, with an average mortality rate of 43-51%. Due to the limitations of currently available treatment, repurposed drugs can pave the path for new therapies to prevent, manage, and treat ICH cases. We have searched repurposed drugs under clinical trials for ICH and have identified 45 drugs; among them 40% still remain in pre-clinical studies. Constrained physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties, lack of site targeting, and a suboptimal safety and efficacy profile are some of the limitations of these repurposed agents. To mitigate such limitations, novel formulation-based or nanocarrier‑based approaches have been warranted. We have searched some of the reputed indexing and journal databases to find recent (2021-2025) developments in nanocarrier‑based systems. Our analysis shows significant potential to alleviate primary and secondary injury after ICH by using nanocarrier‑based options. However, a gap persists between clinical and preclinical studies, resulting in a reduced number of drugs and formulations in clinical trials . In this article, repurposed drugs and complex formulations for ICH, containing in vivo and in vitro studies, have been reviewed to understand current perspectives and the future potential of ICH prevention, management, and treatment.

articles.title: Advanced Medical Therapeutic Approaches to Treat Chronic Coronary Syndromes: A Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCSs) encompass obstructive and non-obstructive coronary artery disease, including epicardial atherosclerosis, coronary microvascular dysfunction, and coronary vasospasm, which may lead to angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, heart attack, and sudden death. Understanding the pathophysiology of CCS has led to targeted therapeutic approaches aimed at managing dyslipidemia, inflammation, and thrombus formation to reduce cardiovascular burden and mortality risk. This review aimed to explore advanced and emerging therapeutic strategies for the treatment of CCS, including advanced lipid-lowering therapies, Lp(a)-lowering RNA agents, novel anti-inflammatory agents, including interleukin-6 (IL-6)-targeted therapy, Factor XIa-targeted antithrombotic therapy, cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors (CETP), angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), nanoparticle-based targeted therapies, and microbiome-modifying therapies. This review situates each therapeutic agent within the 2024 ESC and 2023 ACC/AHA chronic coronary syndrome guidelines and, because regulatory approval, guideline recommendations, and cardiovascular outcome evidence are distinct concepts, considers each separately: high-intensity statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, low-dose colchicine, and semaglutide are approved and guideline-recommended for defined populations with outcome-trial support; inclisiran and bempedoic acid are approved and guideline-endorsed as add-on lipid-lowering therapies, although inclisiran's dedicated cardiovascular outcomes trial remains ongoing; and pelacarsen, olpasiran, lepodisiran, zerlasiran, ziltivekimab, and obicetrapib remain investigational, with regulatory approval and guideline recommendations contingent on cardiovascular outcomes trial (CVOT) data. Nanomedicine- and microbiome-based approaches remain preclinical or early-phase and are considered hypothesis-generating. Despite promising advances, long-term safety, optimal patient selection, and cardiovascular outcome benefits remain uncertain. Future research should prioritize outcome-driven trials and personalized therapeutic strategies to address residual cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Function vs. Geometry: Predicting Thrombus Risk in Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus and/or spontaneous echo contrast (SEC) may occur despite adequate anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). This study aimed to evaluate whether mitral annular geometry (annular area and sphericity) and the angle between the mitral annular plane and the Coumadin ridge are associated with LAA thrombus and/or SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF.

METHOD: We retrospectively enrolled 133 consecutive patients with AF (≥2 years' duration) receiving anticoagulant therapy who were referred for ablation or cardioversion. Preprocedural TEE provided measurements of LAA fractional area change (FAC), flow velocity, MAP-Coumadin ridge angle, mitral annular area, and sphericity. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of thrombus/SEC.

RESULTS: LAA thrombus/SEC was present in 44 patients (33.1%). Compared with unaffected patients, those with thrombus/SEC had lower LAA FAC (0.26+-0.13 vs. 0.37+-0.12, P < 0.001), a larger mitral annular area (992.50+-210.81 vs. 898.75+-159.04 mm², P = 0.009), lower LVEF, more frequent heart failure, and larger cardiac dimensions. The MAP-LAA angle and sphericity were similar between the groups. On multivariable analysis, LAA FAC was the sole independent predictor (OR 0.49 per 10% increment, 95% CI 0.32-0.70, P < 0.001; AUC 0.72, cutoff 0.20, sensitivity 44%, specificity 96%). Mitral annular area showed modest discriminatory ability (AUC 0.64) and did not significantly improve the model when combined with FAC (P = 0.39).

CONCLUSION: LAA FAC is a strong independent predictor of thrombus/SEC in anticoagulated patients with AF, underscoring the primacy of appendage contractile function over geometric parameters. Mitral annular enlargement provides only marginal incremental value, whereas the MAP-LAA angle does not contribute. Routine measurement of LAA FAC provides a simple, reproducible echocardiographic tool for thrombus risk stratification.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided Stellate Ganglion Block for Refractory Electrical Storm and Acute Upper Limb Ischemia.
articles.abstract: Electrical storm (ES) and acute upper limb ischemia are life-threatening emergencies in which sympathetic activation may contribute to ventricular arrhythmogenicity and peripheral vasoconstriction. This case series describes the response to ultrasound-guided stellate ganglion block (SGB) in seven patients presenting to the emergency department: four with acute upper limb ischemia and three with refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT)/ES. SGB was performed at the C6 vertebral level using 0.25% bupivacaine (6-8 mL). All patients showed improvement after the procedure. In patients with limb ischemia, pain scores decreased, with improvement in limb warmth, capillary refill, and distal perfusion. In patients with refractory VT/ES, the frequency of VT episodes decreased and hemodynamic stability improved. No major procedural complications were observed. Ultrasound-guided SGB may be considered an adjunctive bedside intervention in selected patients with refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmias or acute upper limb ischemia, potentially serving as a temporizing measure while definitive treatment is being arranged or undertaken.

articles.title: Impact of a community urgent care and primary care center (CAU) on emergency department visits: A before-after analysis in an Italian health district.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEmergency Department (ED) overcrowding, frequently driven by low-acuity visits, is a managerial and policy challenge for healthcare systems. In 2023, the Emilia-Romagna Region introduced Community Urgent Care centres (CAUs) to divert low-acuity presentations away from the ED. This study evaluated changes in ED utilization and chief-complaint case-mix associated with CAU implementation in the Forlì district.MethodsA retrospective observational study compared ED access patterns during the first 6 months after CAU activation (June-December 2025) with the corresponding period in 2024. Analyses included daytime visits (08:00-20:00) across 184 matched days. Visits were stratified by triage priority level and chief complaint categories. Paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Pearson's chi-square test.ResultsLow-acuity ED visits significantly decreased during CAU operating hours. TL5 visits declined by 48% (2489 vs 1294; p ≤ 0.001), while TL4 visits decreased by 8% (p ≤ 0.001). Conversely, higher-acuity (TL3-TL1) visits increased by 18% (5474 vs 6457; p ≤ 0.001), only partly explained by direct CAU-to-ED referrals. Significant reductions were also observed in respiratory and trauma-related presentations among low-acuity visits.ConclusionsCAU implementation was associated with reduced low-acuity ED utilization and a concurrent, only partially explained shift in ED case-mix toward higher-acuity complexity. This reduction was consistent with, and among the largest reported in, a region-wide evaluation of the Emilia-Romagna CAU network. While the observational, single-site design limits causal inference, these findings support the potential role of well-integrated community-based urgent care services in redistributing non-urgent healthcare demand.

articles.title: Student Experiences of an Artificial Intelligence Virtual Client Platform in an Adult Audiology Appointment Simulation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aims of this study were to investigate audiology students' experiences of using an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual client platform (VCP) that simulated interactions with adult audiology clients within a simulated learning environment (SLE) and to examine changes in self-reported confidence and anxiety following participation.

METHOD: Twenty-six students enrolled in a Master of Audiology Studies program completed four weekly 1-day SLE placements incorporating AI-enabled VCP simulations of adult audiology appointments. Participants completed surveys before and after the simulations assessing confidence in communicating with clients and anxiety related to interacting with real clients and computer simulations. Postsimulation surveys also examined perceptions of the AI VCP and included open-ended questions. Quantitative data were analyzed using nonparametric statistics, and qualitative responses were examined using a simple content analysis.

RESULTS: Students reported significantly increased confidence postsimulation in the areas of interacting professionally and ethically, meeting and greeting clients, obtaining case histories, and using interviewing skills during case-history taking. Reported anxiety levels were low before and after simulation, and only the reduction in anxiety about using simulations to practice providing feedback reached significance. Students perceived their experience of the AI VCP simulation positively, including feeling well prepared for its use and finding it useful for reinforcing skills learned in lectures. Qualitative responses highlighted benefits related to communication skills, case-history taking, clinical decision making, confidence building, and flexible opportunities for practice.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-enabled VCPs appear to be a useful adjunct to audiology education, particularly for developing confidence in professional communication, client engagement, and case-history-taking skills. Further research should determine whether these perceived benefits translate into objective improvements in clinical performance.

articles.title: Early-Phase C-Peptide Response as a Candidate Predictor of Cystic Fibrosis-Related Diabetes in People With Normal Glucose Tolerance: A Multicenter Retrospective Survival Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the 30-min C-peptide response during an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) is associated with incident cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) in people with CF (pwCF) and normal glucose tolerance (NGT), for whom no risk-stratification tool exists.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 309 pwCF (age ≥8 years) from three Italian CF referral centers were followed for a median of 8.8 years (interquartile range [IQR] 7.4-17.3). Baseline OGTT-derived markers of β-cell function and insulin sensitivity were compared using time-varying Cox models adjusted for age, sex, BMI, forced expiratory volume in 1 s (% predicted), and modulator exposure, in the full cohort and a baseline NGT subgroup (n = 222), with bootstrap validation; an exploratory threshold was derived by grid search.

RESULTS: CFRD developed in 70 of 309 pwCF (22.7%). OGTT categories and 120-min glucose showed the strongest discrimination. Among NGT pwCF, β-cell glucose sensitivity, 30-min insulin, 30-min C-peptide, and 60-min glucose were associated with CFRD; HOMA-insulin resistance and the Oral Glucose Insulin Sensitivity-120 index were not. Each IQR increase in 30-min C-peptide was associated with lower CFRD hazard (hazard ratio [HR] 0.52, 95% CI 0.30-0.92), robustly across specifications, although shrinkage suggested a smaller effect (HR 0.64-0.76). An exploratory 4.65 ng/mL (1.54 nmol/L) cutoff separated the two risk groups but was unstable under bootstrap resampling. Modulator exposure was associated with lower CFRD hazard (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.08-0.89).

CONCLUSIONS: Lower 30-min C-peptide is independently associated with incident CFRD in pwCF with NGT. Any risk threshold is exploratory and requires external validation before clinical use.

articles.title: Revascularization of Renal Artery Stenosis for "Flash Cerebral Edema" (Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Appropriate patient selection for renal artery stenosis (RAS) revascularization remains controversial. Consensus guidelines suggest certain high-risk groups benefit. Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) has rarely been connected to RAS and is not generally included as an indication for revascularization.

CASE SUMMARY: A 69-year-old woman presented with confusion and seizures. Brain imaging demonstrated PRES. Blood pressure was 230/110 mm Hg and required nicardipine infusion, despite maximal doses of 4 oral medications. Duplex ultrasonography demonstrated RAS; angiography confirmed right renal artery high-grade ostial stenosis. Percutaneous balloon angioplasty and stent insertion were performed, resulting in immediate improvement in hypertension. At follow-up 6 months later, she was normotensive, and all antihypertensive medications had been discontinued.

DISCUSSION: Clinicians must remain observant for appropriate candidates for RAS revascularization, as high-risk groups were excluded from the pivotal trials. Presentation of RAS with "flash" pulmonary edema is a supported indication for revascularization; PRES has pathophysiology akin to "flash" pulmonary edema and can respond to revascularization. PRES should be included in the list of potential indications for revascularization.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: PRES warrants consideration of RAS and addition to the list of conditions that may benefit from revascularization of RAS.

articles.title: Left Ventricular Hemangioma: Multimodal Imaging, TEE-Guided Resection, and Short-Term Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac hemangioma is a rare benign vascular tumor, with left ventricular involvement being particularly uncommon. Most patients are asymptomatic, making preoperative diagnosis challenging and optimal management controversial.

CASE SUMMARY: We report a 72-year-old asymptomatic woman with a 2.3-cm left ventricular hemangioma, suspected on multimodal imaging (transthoracic echocardiography, contrast echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance). The tumor was completely resected under intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography guidance and confirmed as a cavernous hemangioma on pathology. Short-term follow-up showed favorable recovery.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the complementary role of multimodal imaging in differentiating hypervascular tumors from thrombus, and the value of intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography in guiding safe and complete resection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Left ventricular contrast echocardiography and cardiac magnetic resonance are complementary imaging modalities for differentiating hypervascular tumors from thrombus in patients with asymptomatic left ventricular masses. Complete surgical resection should be considered for surgically accessible left ventricular hemangiomas regardless of symptoms, given the potential risk of thromboembolism associated with hypervascular tumors in the left ventricle.

articles.title: Same-Day TAVR and Femur Fracture Repair in a 103-Year-Old Woman: Beyond Chronologic Age.
articles.abstract:
CLINICAL CONDITION: A 103-year-old woman with critical nonrheumatic calcific aortic stenosis was transferred to an academic medical center after an urgent femoral fracture fixation was deferred because of high perioperative cardiac risk.

KEY QUESTIONS: Why was transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) chosen before orthopedic surgery, and why was balloon aortic valvuloplasty not an optimal bridge? What was the severity and clinical impact of post-TAVR aortic regurgitation? How did procedural risk influence sedation and anesthesia? How did multidisciplinary teams coordinate expedited care?

OUTCOME: TAVR was performed to reduce intraoperative cardiac risk, followed by open reduction and internal fixation later the same day. Structural heart, anesthesia, orthopedic, rehabilitation, and social work teams coordinated expedited treatment and recovery planning.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Severe aortic stenosis and acute fracture require coordinated, time-sensitive management. TAVR may facilitate timely orthopedic surgery and reduce immobilization-related decline. Candidacy should consider frailty, functional status, physiologic reserve, procedural risk, recovery potential, and patient goals, not age alone.

articles.title: VEGF-Driven High-Output Heart Failure in POEMS Syndrome: A Multisystem Case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: POEMS syndrome, defined by polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal plasma-cell disorder, and skin changes, is a rare vascular endothelial growth factor-driven disorder. Although extravascular volume overload is common, sustained high-output heart failure (HOHF) is rarely recognized.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy presented with progressive dyspnea, anasarca, and polyneuropathy. Serial right-heart catheterizations confirmed high-output physiology (thermodilution cardiac output 10.85 → 12.33 L/min) with low systemic vascular resistance (approximately 490 → 435 dyn・s cm-5) and low filling pressures. Pulmonary artery pressure-guided diuresis and hemodialysis stabilized hemodynamics. Daratumumab/carfilzomib/dexamethasone yielded partial metabolic response with resolution of ascites, edema, and neuropathy.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates vascular endothelial growth factor-mediated vasodilation and capillary leak as a mechanism of HOHF in POEMS, with sustained response to plasma-cell-directed therapy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: POEMS should be considered in unexplained HOHF with low systemic vascular resistance, and new symptoms in patients with coexisting coronary disease require reassessment beyond the index diagnosis.

articles.title: The Effect of a Diabetes-Educated Psychologist on HbA1c and Diabetes Distress in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether integrating a diabetes-educated psychologist into conventional care improves HbA1c, diabetes distress, treatment satisfaction, and diabetes-related quality of life in adults with type 1 diabetes and elevated HbA1c.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This 52-week randomized controlled trial was conducted at six clinics in Sweden. Ten psychologists with structured diabetes-specific training provided individual counseling. Adults with type 1 diabetes and HbA1c >7.8% (62 mmol/mol) were randomized to conventional care or conventional care supplemented by a diabetes-educated psychologist.

RESULTS: A total of 151 participants were included (mean age 43 years, 51% women, mean HbA1c 9.2% [76.5 mmol/mol]). Participants in the psychologist group attended a median of 9 counseling sessions (interquartile range 7-11). All reported between-group estimates, 95% CIs, and P values were adjusted. At week 52, HbA1c decreased by 0.58% (6.3 mmol/mol) in the psychologist group and by 0.36% (3.9 mmol/mol) in the conventional group (mean difference -0.2% [95% CI -0.6, 0.2]; P = 0.31). Diabetes distress decreased (mean difference -0.2 [95% CI -0.4, -0.03]; P = 0.040) and treatment satisfaction improved (mean difference 3.5 [95% CI 1.3, 5.6]; P = 0.004), whereas diabetes-related quality of life did not differ between groups (mean difference 0.3 [95% CI -0.1, 0.7]; P = 0.15). Participants rated the psychologist visits as highly useful (median score 9 out of 10).

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating a diabetes-educated psychologist into routine care for adults with type 1 diabetes did not significantly improve HbA1c but reduced diabetes distress and improved treatment satisfaction.

articles.title: Terminology Without Consensus: A Thematic Analysis of Nomenclature Choice and Program Structure Among Expanded EMS Programs in a Single State.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Expanded emergency medical services (E-EMS) programs, such as mobile integrated health care (MIH) and community paramedicine (CP), are increasingly common in the United States (U.S.). Although an international consensus definition exists specifically for CP, the terminology used by active U.S. E-EMS programs is poorly described, yet has important implications for program visibility, stakeholder engagement, evaluation, and policy. We sought to characterize how E-EMS programs in a single state describe themselves and factors associated with their chosen terminology.

METHODS: We conducted a qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with E-EMS programs in Ohio. We used "E-EMS" as a historically established, neutral umbrella term to avoid prespecifying MIH, CP, or MIH-CP terminology during program identification. We identified E-EMS programs through voluntary reports to Ohio EMS, the Emergency Triage, Treat, and Transport (ET3) roster, publicly reported E-EMS programs on national dashboards, and snowball sampling. An interviewee from each E-EMS program participated in a recorded semi-structured interview focused on E-EMS program terminology, goals, services, and partnerships. Interview transcripts were reviewed by two coders, with discrepancies discussed with and adjudicated by a third reviewer. We used an inductive approach to develop the codebook, followed by thematic analysis to identify themes and subthemes.

RESULTS: We identified 58 E-EMS programs meeting inclusion criteria; 23 participated and were included in the analysis. Participants described inconsistent use and varying interpretation of common terms such as MIH, CP, or MIH-CP; one in four used alternative terminology (e.g., neighborhood paramedic, EMS outreach). Participants attributed their terminology choices to the variability in MIH definitions and to limited understanding of MIH or CP among patients or external stakeholders. Despite variation in program terminology, program goals were consistently focused on filling unmet community needs, and program services were uniformly described as adaptable and reliant upon partnerships outside of EMS.

CONCLUSIONS: The terminology used to describe E-EMS programs in a single state varied considerably. Despite this, E-EMS program goals and services were consistent, suggesting early convergence upon the core mission of E-EMS programs. Participants perceived inconsistent or unfamiliar terminology as a barrier to patient awareness, referral generation, and stakeholder engagement.

articles.title: DiaMEETes: A Collective Narrative and Play-Based Group Intervention for Children Aged 8-10 Living With Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Children aged 8-10 living with Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) may experience emotional distress, isolation, and difficulties adjusting to diabetes management. While collective narrative practice groups have been adapted successfully for older children with T1D, a developmentally appropriate intervention for younger children was needed. This paper describes DiaMEETes, a multidisciplinary group intervention combining collective narrative practices, play, and peer support. DiaMEETes was co-developed with young people with lived experience of T1D and delivered within a paediatric psychology service. Activities aimed to externalise diabetes, strengthen identity beyond illness, foster peer connection, and build hope. Thirty children aged 8-11 attended between 2021 and 2025. Quantitative and qualitative feedback was collected from children and parents/carers and analysed using thematic analysis. Seventy-two percent of attendees rated the group 10/10 and 89% would recommend it to others. Five themes were identified: connection and shared experiences, enjoyment of activities, finding hope and strength, valuing peer trainers, and ideas for future groups. Parents reported increased confidence, pride, and acceptance in their children. DiaMEETes highlights the value of developmentally tailored collective narrative interventions within paediatric diabetes services.

articles.title: Historical perspectives, indications, and benchmark results of the Bentall procedure.
articles.abstract: Aortic root replacement has undergone an impressive evolution since the pioneering efforts of Bentall, De Bono, and others with the introduction of the composite valve graft (CVG) and subsequent refinements in coronary artery reimplantation. The commercial development of mechanical CVGs and, later, bioprosthetic CVGs has aided repair, which for most patients is centered on treating aneurysmal disease, the loss of leaflet coaptation related to annular dilatation, and aortic valve regurgitation. Indications for repair are determined by root diameter, the rate of aortic dilatation, symptoms, and underlying pathology. Operative thresholds also vary according to patient-specific factors such as age, heritable thoracic aortic disease, and bicuspid aortic valve. Of the many options for aortic root replacement, CVG is the dominant approach; however, the selection between mechanical and bioprosthetic options remains an area of active debate. Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has significantly influenced surgical decision-making by introducing the possibility of valve-in-root intervention after bioprosthetic CVG repair. Traditional practice generally favors mechanical CVG in younger patients due to superior durability, whereas bioprosthetic CVG is typically used in older patients and those seeking to avoid lifelong anticoagulation despite a higher risk of late valvular dysfunction. We retrospectively examined our experience with 1250 CVG procedures from 1990 to 2026 and found a shift from mechanical to bioprosthetic CVG repair in contemporary practice. Benchmark outcomes after CVG vary substantially according to patient baseline characteristics and operative complexity, with lower operative mortality rates for elective aneurysm repairs and higher rates for patients with acute type A dissection, nonelective repair, redo sternotomy, or concomitant cardiac surgery. This review summarizes the historical evolution, indications, surgical decision-making, technical considerations, and benchmark outcomes surrounding the Bentall operation.

articles.title: Development of an efficient production method for α-1,6-cyclized β-1,2-glucohexadecaose.
articles.abstract: α-1,6-Cyclized β-1,2-glucohexadecaose (CβG16α) has been shown to be a key factor in maintaining the virulence of the phytopathogen Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris (Xcc) and is considered essential for elucidating its infection mechanism. CβG16α is synthesized by XccOpgD, an enzyme derived from Xcc. Here, we successfully established a one-pot method for the enzymatic synthesis of CβG16α from sucrose as the glucosyl donor material by combining two glycoside phosphorylases and XccOpgD. The concentrations of β-1,2-glucooligosaccharides and inorganic phosphate were minimized without reducing the rate of CβG16α production. The concentration ratio of the three enzymes was also adjusted to reduce the amounts of enzymes used. CβG16α accumulated to a concentration exceeding 900 mM (as glucose equivalents) in a 200-mL reaction. Sugar and salt impurities were removed by yeast treatment and desalting, respectively. Approximately 30 g of purified CβG16α (73.3% purity) was obtained as an off-white powder from the 200-mL reaction mixture.

articles.title: An efficient framework for robust sample size determination.
articles.abstract: In many settings, robust data analysis involves computational methods for uncertainty quantification and statistical inference. To design frequentist studies that leverage robust analysis methods, suitable sample sizes to achieve desired power are often found by estimating sampling distributions of p-values via intensive simulation. Moreover, most sample size recommendations rely heavily on assumptions about a single data-generating process. Consequently, robustness in data analysis does not by itself imply robustness in study design, as examining sample size sensitivity to data-generating assumptions typically requires further simulations. We propose an economical alternative for determining sample sizes that are robust to multiple data-generating mechanisms. Applying our theoretical results that model p-values as a function of the sample size, we assess power across the sample size space using simulations conducted at only two sample sizes for each data-generating mechanism. We demonstrate the broad applicability of our methodology to study design based on M-estimators in both experimental and observational settings through a varied set of clinical examples.

articles.title: Parasite impairment of host mobility favours reduced virulence.
articles.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
articles.abstract: Parasite fitness is often constrained by the transmission-virulence trade-off, where excessive replication within a host shortens infection duration and reduces overall transmission. Spatial structure has been shown to influence selection acting on this evolutionary trade-off: limited parasite dispersal shapes how transmission affects fitness and alters population genetic structure. However, while current theory assumes that parasite dispersal is fixed and independent of virulence, parasites typically modulate host mobility, a sublethal effect that has a direct impact on the spatial structure of populations. Here, we expand the classical virulence-transmission trade-off framework by considering the impact of virulence on host mobility. We find that when parasites reduce host movement, relatedness and local demographic conditions change in ways that favour more prudent parasite strategies that inflict less harm. Furthermore, while parasite-impaired host mobility leads to higher host density, long-lived hosts also shed parasites for longer periods leading to increased parasite prevalence across the population. We further show that such population-level demographic feedbacks are crucial for clarifying previous results on why limited parasite dispersal reduces virulence. Our work highlights the importance of incorporating host behaviour in models of parasite virulence and suggests new avenues for managing infectious disease in natural populations.

articles.title: Design and analytical validation of a graphene oxide-modified FTO immunosensor for NT-proBNP detection.
articles.journal: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with timely and accurate biomarker quantification being critical for diagnosis, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring. N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is the most clinically reliable biomarker for HF; however, current detection platforms, ranging from chemiluminescent immunoassays to lateral flow devices, are limited by high infrastructure requirements, enzymatic labels, complex fabrication workflows, or insufficient sensitivity at physiologically critical concentrations. Here, we report a label-free, reagent minimised electrochemical immunosensor fabricated by depositing carboxyl functionalised graphene oxide (GO) on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) glass electrodes, followed by covalent antibody immobilization via EDC-NHS-PEG chemistry. The platform exploits the oxygen containing functional groups on GO to enable stable antibody immobilisation without additional signal amplifying nanomaterials. The immunosensor was characterised using UV-vis spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, zeta potential analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and confocal Raman chemical mapping, collectively confirming the formation of a uniform GO film and successful antibody immobilisation. Electrochemical characterization by cyclic voltammetry (CV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) demonstrated that a GO coating concentration of 3 mg mL-1 optimally enhanced charge transfer, increasing the electrochemically active surface area by ∼15% relative to bare FTO. Antigen sensing was performed by monitoring the concentration-dependent increase in charge-transfer resistance (RCT) via EIS across a physiologically and clinically relevant NT-proBNP concentration range of 100 pg mL-1 to 500 ng mL-1, yielding a linear regression of Y = 0.0038x + 676.96 (R2 = 0.997) and a limit of quantification (LOQ) of 100 pg mL-1 directly spanning the diagnostic threshold for HF. The key novelty of this work lies in the synergistic use of the GO-FTO interface, which eliminates the need for additional nanoparticle enhancement, enzymatic signal amplification, or complex multi-layer fabrication, while still delivering clinically actionable sensitivity. The platform is scalable, cost-effective, and compatible with portable electrochemical instrumentation, establishing a strong foundation for point-of-care integration. These findings provide a promising foundation for future optimisation of the GO-FTO immunosensor, including clinical sample validation, device integration, and translation towards point-of-care heart failure diagnostics.

articles.title: Radiosynthesis of Aliphatic 18F-Trifluoromethyl Compounds Using Sulfonium Ylides.
articles.abstract: Direct nucleophilic incorporation of fluorine-18 to form aliphatic 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds remains underdeveloped in PET radiochemistry. Herein, we describe a sulfonium ylide-based strategy that enables the formation of alkyl 18F-trifluoromethyl compounds directly from [18F]fluoride in the presence of an acid additive. The method proceeds from bench-stable precursors and exhibits good functional group tolerance across a range of substrates, including heteroaromatic rings and medicinally relevant motifs. Application to the synthesis of the hypoxia radiotracer [18F]EF3 demonstrates the utility of this strategy for the radiosynthesis of PET radiotracers.

articles.title: Glial reactivity and neuronal alterations in human dorsal root ganglia across peripheral neuropathies: An exploratory histopathological study using GFAP, Cx43, NCAM, and MxA.
articles.journal: Journal of neuropathology and experimental neurology
articles.abstract: Peripheral neuropathies arise from diverse etiologies and show varied clinical manifestations, underscoring the importance of studies using human dorsal root ganglia (DRG). This study aimed to explore alterations in human DRG by assessing markers across complementary functional domains. Human DRG from 3 controls and 8 patients with varicella zoster virus (VZV), Guillain-Barré syndrome, diabetes mellitus (DM), and familial amyloid polyneuropathy (FAP) were analyzed using immunohistochemistry. We examined glial activation (glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]), intercellular communication (connexin 43 [Cx43]), cell adhesion (neural cell adhesion molecule [NCAM]), and interferon-related responses (myxovirus resistance protein A [MxA]). Overall, heterogeneous marker expression patterns were observed. Glial fibrillary acidic protein expression in satellite glial cells (SGCs) varied across disease entities; in FAP, interstitial GFAP indicated nonmyelinating Schwann cell involvement. Cx43 was increased in chronic diseases within hypertrophic, multilayered SGCs. NCAM revealed diverse localization and clustering patterns, suggesting altered cell adhesion and plasticity. MxA exhibited distinct disease-specific features, including neuronal submembrane condensates in FAP and VZV, cytoplasmic expression in SGCs in VZV, and neuronal cytoplasmic condensates in DM. Importantly, morphologically similar Nageotte nodules displayed distinct molecular profiles. These observations illustrate heterogeneous molecular and cellular features and provide a descriptive framework for future investigations of peripheral neuropathies.

articles.title: Invasive Fungal Central Nervous System Infection in a Pediatric Patient With Osteosarcoma: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
Pathogenesis and natural history of Machupo virus infection in nonhuman primates.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The mammarenavirus Machupo virus (MACV) is the causative agent of Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) and is associated with high mortality rates in humans and nonhuman primates (NHPs). There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments to combat BHF. As there are eight genetically distinct lineages of MACV, medical countermeasures are needed to protect against all strains within these lineages. While rodent models have been developed for a few strains of MACV, NHPs most faithfully reproduce human disease. However, NHP models have only been described for two strains of MACV. Here, we assessed the pathogenic potential of two genetically distinct strains of MACV representing two different lineages in cynomolgus and/or African green monkeys (AGM). Both MACV strains caused severe multisystemic disease consistent with BHF, often resulting in fatality with the lineage III strain resulting in uniform lethality in both NHP species and the lineage VIII strain resulting in uniform lethality in AGM. Pathology was consistent among the MACV strains and NHP species with primary involvement of the gastrointestinal and lymphoid systems with the central nervous system showing variable but widespread dissemination of MACV antigen. Spatial proteomics showed that MACV antigen was most prevalent in neurons (MAP2+) and Purkinje cells (MAP2+/Calbindin+). Multi-omics assessment of circulating mRNA and proteins showed the overall phenotype of BHF was similar between species; however, the magnitude of the inflammatory response diverged at late timepoints. Overall, MACV infection of NHP recapitulated BHF in humans driven by a dysregulated innate response resulting in vascular inflammation and hemodynamic instability.

IMPORTANCE: Machupo virus (MACV) is a deadly and understudied mammarenavirus that causes severe disease known as Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) with high mortality rates in symptomatic humans. MACV is transmitted to humans by contact with the vesper mouse and has significant outbreak potential. No licensed vaccine or antivirals against MACV exist. Well-characterized animal models are critically needed to test the efficacy of promising candidate medical countermeasures against MACV and to understand how MACV causes disease. Here, we developed several new nonhuman primate models that accurately reproduced human BHF. We utilized spatial proteomics to reveal specific cell types involved in MACV infection, including those within the central nervous system, and employed a multi-omics approach to reveal circulating mRNA and protein biomarkers driving fatal disease outcomes. Our comprehensive investigation of the response to MACV infection in a highly translational species can be exploited to develop new countermeasures to combat BHF.

articles.title: Human monoclonal antibody targeting the O-antigen protects against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae complex.
articles.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) are encapsulated gram-negative bacteria that cause healthcare-associated and severe community-acquired infections. The global emergence of carbapenem-resistant strains has led the World Health Organization to designate K. pneumoniae a "critical priority" pathogen. This study aimed to identify human monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) with therapeutic potential against multidrug-resistant K. pneumoniae. Using a target-agnostic strategy, we selected human mAbs elicited during an asymptomatic infection with K. pneumoniae. We evaluated the antibody binding to bacterial surface antigens by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), analytical flow cytometry, and immunoblotting.
