In vitro, the mAbs were tested by complement-mediated killing and macrophage uptake assays using Kp clinical isolates of differing serotypes. Finally, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of the mAbs in a murine pneumonia model with carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae. Among the four IgG antibodies identified, mAbKPNA-14 demonstrated specific binding to K. pneumoniae wzi50:O3b and cross-reactivity with O-antigen type O3/O3a. mAbKPNA-14 significantly enhanced complement-mediated killing (p < 0.01) and macrophage phagocytosis. In vivo, the therapeutic administration of mAbKPNA-14 reduced bacterial load in the lungs by over 100-fold compared to the control groups (p < 0.001) and prevented systemic dissemination. This study describes a human mAb that binds to O3b and O3/O3a O-antigens and confers in vivo protection against drug-resistant K. pneumoniae. These findings support the therapeutic potential of mAbs and describe a strategy for isolating and identifying protective mAbs targeting multidrug-resistant bacteria.IMPORTANCEMultidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae is a critical global health threat for which new therapeutic approaches are urgently needed. Here, we identify a naturally elicited human monoclonal antibody, mAbKPNA-14, which recognizes the O3b O-antigen and cross-reacts with related O3/O3a O-antigens. The antibody promotes complement-mediated killing and macrophage uptake and, when administered therapeutically, reduces pulmonary bacterial burden by more than 100-fold and prevents systemic dissemination in a mouse model of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae pneumonia. These findings demonstrate that protective human antibodies can be isolated directly from individuals following K. pneumoniae infection and identify O-antigen as a promising target for antibody-based therapy. More broadly, our target-agnostic approach provides a strategy for discovering naturally occurring protective antibodies against multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

articles.title: Comparison of Rule-Based Natural Language Processing and Diagnosis Code Approaches to Detecting Bleeding in the Electronic Health Record: Algorithm Validation Within a Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant use is prevalent and increasing. High-quality anticoagulation management balances individual thrombotic and bleeding risks to optimize care. An automated algorithm to accurately extract major bleeding events from the electronic health record (EHR) of a large health care system would be extremely useful for tracking outcomes of anticoagulated patients.

OBJECTIVE: The study aims to assess the accuracy of a natural language processing (NLP) approach, compared with and in conjunction with a diagnosis code (Dx Code)-based strategy, for detecting major bleeding from the EHR.

METHODS: Patients with at least 1 prescription for apixaban, dabigatran, edoxaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2023, were analyzed for major bleeding events. Major bleeding was defined similarly to the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis definition. For the NLP algorithm, clinical notes and radiology reports were screened for mentions of bleeding. MedTagger, an open-source, rule-based NLP tool, was then used on the notes. The NLP results were transformed into a feature set, which was used to create a support vector machine model. Three NLP models were created for central nervous system bleeding, critical site bleeding, and bleeding with a hemoglobin drop or transfusions (other major bleeding). Training and test datasets were created using an active learning approach. The model was trained using 80% of the dataset, while the remaining 20% was used for testing. After model finalization, an independent random sample was used to validate the model. Dx Codes were also used to detect major bleeding, similar to previously published approaches. Five unique algorithms were compared: (1) NLP, (2) Dx Code in the primary position, (3) Dx Code in any position, (4) NLP∩Dx Code in any position, and (5) NLP∪Dx Code in any position. All 5 algorithms were compared with manual chart review.

RESULTS: The final analysis identified 111,338 patients prescribed outpatient anticoagulation during the study. Manual adjudication was performed for 1189 of the 111,338 (1%) patients. Most of the 5 approaches performed well on the test data, with F1-scores ranging from 0.545 to 0.959, except for Dx Code-Primary, with an F1-score of 0.353 for critical site bleeding. The F1-scores for the validation data ranged from 0.509 to 0.679. The NLP∩Dx Code in any position approach yielded excellent precision of 0.864 (95% CI 0.667-0.953) but only 0.559 (95% CI 0.395-0.711) sensitivity. The NLP∪Dx Code in any position approach yielded good sensitivity of 0.824 (95% CI 0.665-0.917) but only 0.368 (95% CI 0.269-0.481) precision.

CONCLUSIONS: Electronic tools can screen the EHRs to identify major bleeding outcomes in large patient cohorts within a multisite health care network with high precision but only moderate sensitivity. Additional work is needed to enhance sensitivity while maintaining high precision.

articles.title: Local Treatment for Perineal and Perianal Rhabdomyosarcoma: Clinical Practice Guidelines and Consensus Statement From the Children's Oncology Group, European Pediatric Soft Tissue Sarcoma Study Group, the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe, and the International Soft Tissue Sarcoma Consortium.
articles.abstract: Local control of rhabdomyosarcoma in the perianal and perineal region (PRMS) is challenging due to the unfavorable tumor location, the often advanced stage of disease, the prevalence of alveolar histology with PAX3/FOXO1 fusion, and frequent regional lymph node (LN) involvement at presentation. Distant metastases are present at diagnosis in up to 49% of patients. Given the high risk of recurrence, the prognosis of patients with PRMS treated with multimodal treatment is poor, with a reported 5-year overall survival (OS) rate of 39%-52%. Due to the rarity of PRMS along with variations in treatment protocols over time and across different cooperative groups, we have developed consensus local treatment guidelines. This guideline is based on a comprehensive literature review and expert opinion and is endorsed by the International Soft-Tissue Sarcoma Consortium (INSTRuCT). It integrates insights from three leading pediatric oncology cooperative groups: the Cooperative Weichteilsarkom Studiengruppe (CWS; since December 2024 part of European pediatric Soft-tissue sarcoma Study Group [EpSSG]), Children's Oncology Group (COG), and EpSSG. This document addresses surgical therapy options, including biopsy, nodal staging, and various resection modalities, as well as options for radiotherapy, such as intensity-modulated radiation therapy, proton beam therapy, and brachytherapy.

articles.title: Cardiac involvement in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies: from clinical and autoantibody profiles to a troponin-based predictive model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: We aimed to characterize clinical and autoantibody profiles associated with cardiac involvement and to develop a practical risk-stratification model for identifying IIM patients at increased cardiac risk.

METHODS: A total of 220 patients were enrolled, including 55 with cardiac involvement and 165 without. Clinical, serological, and laboratory characteristics were compared. Three nested multivariable logistic regression models assessed the incremental value of hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI, and the final model was developed into a nomogram and evaluated by ROC analysis, calibration, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: Patients with cardiac involvement showed more severe muscle manifestations and dysphagia, accompanied by greater systemic inflammation and distinct autoantibody profiles. hs-cTnT showed high sensitivity but substantial associations with skeletal muscle injury, whereas hs-cTnI was more specific with weaker correlations. An hs-cTnI-based nomogram integrating interstitial lung disease, albumin, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and lactate dehydrogenase demonstrated excellent discrimination, good calibration, and favorable clinical utility.

CONCLUSION: Cardiac involvement in IIM is characterized by a clinically heterogeneous phenotype in which severe myopathy and dysphagia may be more prominent than typical cardiac symptoms. Our hs-cTnI-based nomogram may serve as an initial risk-stratification and triage tool to identify patients who warrant closer cardiac evaluation, including targeted cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.

articles.title: 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3 Ameliorates High-Altitude Hypoxic Injury via Modulation of Short-Chain Fatty Acids to Exert a Coordinated Anti-Inflammatory Effect.
articles.abstract: High-altitude hypoxic injury remains a major health threat with limited prophylactic options. This study evaluated the protective effects of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (1,25-(OH)2D3) against acute high-altitude sickness using parallel human and animal investigations. In the clinical trial, 48 volunteers ascending to 4,200 m received either weight-stratified 1,25-(OH)2D3 (0.102-0.135 microg/kg/day, n=23) or placebo (n=25) for 5 days. In the animal study, 40 SD rats were exposed to 6,000 m (hypobaric hypoxia) for 48 h with or without 1,25-(OH)2D3 pretreatment. Results showed that 1,25-(OH)2D3 significantly reduced Lake Louise scores, alleviated headache, improved oxygen saturation and haemodynamics, suppressed serum pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1beta) and inflammatory cell counts, and attenuated multi-organ (lung, liver, kidney) hypoxic injury. In rats, 1,25-(OH)2D3 also restored Th1/Th2 immune balance, reduced oxidative stress, and down-regulated four short-chain fatty acids ((R)-3-hydroxyisobutyric acid, (S)-2-hydroxybutyric acid, 2-hydroxybutyric acid, beta-hydroxyisobutyric acid) involved in butyrate metabolism. No toxic effects were observed in normoxic controls. Collectively, 1,25-(OH)2D3 effectively prevents high-altitude hypoxic injury by suppressing inflammation, restoring immune homeostasis, and modulating short-chain fatty acid metabolism. Our findings support 1,25-(OH)2D3 as a safe and promising prophylactic agent against high-altitude sickness. Key words Hypoxic injury " 1,25-(OH)2D3 " Immune response " Short-chain fatty acids.

articles.title: GSK2795039 Prevents Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha-Induced RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-Mediated Necroptosis in H9C2 Cardiomyocytes Through Inhibition of NADPH Oxidase.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress contribute to heart failure. Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), a major inflammatory cytokine, induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) and necroptosis in cardiomyocytes. GSK2795039 is a novel NADPH oxidase 2 inhibitor. However, it is unknown whether GSK2795039 prevents TNF-alpha-induced cardiomyocyte necroptosis and the underlying mechanisms. In the present study, we tested the hypothesis that GSK2795039 prevents TNF-alpha-induced necroptosis in cardiomyocytes through inhibition of NADPH oxidase-mediated RIP1-RIP3-MLKL pathway. The H9C2 cardiomyocytes were divided into the following groups: control, necrostatin-1, TNF-alpha, and TNF-alpha plus necrostatin-1; control, GSK2795039, TNF-alpha, and TNF-alpha plus GSK2795039. ROS were assessed by dihydroethidium staining. Necroptotic and apoptotic proteins were measured by Western blot. The RIP1 inhibitor necrostatin-1 attenuated apoptosis, necrosis, phosphorylated RIP3 (p-RIP3) and p-MLKL protein and intracellular ROS in TNF-alpha-treated H9C2 cardiomyocytes. GSK2795039 inhibited TNF-alpha-induced Nox2 expression, intracellular ROS and cell death. GSK2795039 prevented the increases in phosphorylated RIP1 (p-RIP1), p-RIP3 and p-MLKL proteins, reflective of their respective kinase activities, markers of necroptosis, in TNF-alpha-treated H9C2 cardiomyocytes. GSK2795039 prevented the decrease in anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 protein and the increases in pro-apoptotic Bax protein, phosphorylated JNK protein and cleaved caspase 3 protein, indicative of caspase activity, a marker of apoptosis, in TNF-alpha-treated H9C2 cardiomyocytes. The results indicate that GSK2795039 prevented TNF-alpha-induced RIP1-RIP3-MLKL-mediated necroptosis in H9C2 cardiomyocytes through inhibition of NADPH oxidase-derived ROS. These findings advocate for further animal testing of the specific Nox2 inhibitor GSK2795039 in myocardial infarction and heart failure, which are characterized by elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha and oxidative stress. Key words Tumor necrosis factor-alpha " Inflammatory cytokines " Reactive oxygen species " Necroptosis " Cardiomyocytes.

articles.title: Impact of Obesity on the Reparative Potency of Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells in Hypertensive Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Obesity constitutes a formidable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases; however, its implications for adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADMSCs) in the context of hypertensive cardiomyopathy remain insufficiently elucidated. This investigation seeks to illuminate the effects of obesity on the reparative potential of ADMSCs extracted from both obese (O) and normal control (NC) mice within a hypertensive model, thereby addressing a critical void in current research. A model of hypertension (HT) was developed in C57BL/6J mice through the administration of angiotensin II (Ang II). In groups of Non-HT and HT animals, vehicles, NC or obese ADMSCs were injected intravenously. Left ventricular (LV) function in vivo was estimated by echocardiogram. Hypertensive cardiomyopathy was meticulously scrutinized by serum biochemical assays, histology, immunohistochemistry, and reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The serum concentrations of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cytokines were quantified utilizing enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). The expression of autophagy-related and PI3K/AKT pathway related protein was investigated by western blotting. NC-ADMSCs but not O-ADMSCs normalized the Ang II induced elevated blood pressure and myocardial wall thickness. Both NC- and O-ADMSCs alleviated myocardial tissue damage in HT, but NC ADMSCs decreased oxidative stress and blunted myocardial microvascular rarefaction more effectively. Obese ADMSCs exhibited increased inflammation and pro-fibrosis level in vitro. The heart tissue of vehicle-injected HT mice had decreased ratio of p-mTOR to mTOR, P-PI3K to PI3K, and P-AKT to AKT, lower abundance of p62, higher level of ULK1 and Beclin 1, and elevated ratio of LC3II to LC3I compared to Non-HT animals, consistent with HT-associated promotion of autophagy. The changes were largely reversed in heart of NC- ADMSCs injected mice but partially alleviated in O-ADMSCs treating. Obese ADMSCs are less effective in protecting against Ang II induced myocardial hypertrophy in mice which might be partially relevant to its impaired regulation of autophagy through the PI3K/AKT axis. Key words Adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cell " Obesity " Hypertension " Oxidative stress " Autophagy " PI3K " AKT.

articles.title: Extended Synaptotagmin-1 Interacts With Protein Kinase A to Modulate beta-Adrenergic Signaling and Cardiac Contractility.
articles.abstract: Sympathetic activation of the heart enhances myocardial contractility via the beta-adrenergic receptor/adenylate cyclase/cAMP/PKA signaling pathway. Although Protein Kinase A Catalytic Subunit (PKAc) mediates downstream protein phosphorylation, the mechanisms governing its subcellular localization remain unclear. Extended synaptotagmin-1 (E-Syt1), a stress-activated membrane tethering protein located at endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane (ER-PM) contact sites, has been associated with compartmentalization signals. This study aimed to investigate whether E-Syt1 modulates beta-adrenergic signaling and cardiac contractility by coordinating the localization and activity of PKAc. Mice were injected the beta-adrenergic agonist isoproterenol (ISO), and cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography in E-Syt1 knockout (E-Syt1-/-) and wild-type mice. E-Syt1 knockout mice exhibit reduced cardiac contractility after ISO treatment. Despite gene expression of the beta-adrenergic pathway was not altered, ISO stimulation in E-Syt1-/- hearts resulted in reduced cytosolic cAMP levels and decreased phosphorylation of Cav1.2. LC-MS/MS and immunofluorescence verified the interaction between E-Syt1 and PKAc. Rescue experiments highlighted the critical role of E-Syt1-PKAc in mediating Cav1.2 phosphorylation through the SMP domain interactions. E-Syt1 regulates Cav1.2 phospho-rylation by forming a signaling complex with PKAc, supporting efficient beta-adrenergic signaling. Key words E-Syt1 " Protein kinase A " Cav1.2 " beta-adrenergic signaling pathway " Sympathetic stimulation.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease in Cetaceans.
articles.abstract: Cetaceans possess a highly specialized cardiovascular system that supports prolonged apnea, selective perfusion of vital organs, and tolerance to marked hemodynamic fluctuations during diving. Nevertheless, pathological and clinical observations show that they can develop a broad spectrum of cardiovascular disease (CVD). This review summarizes current knowledge on CVD in cetaceans across species and ecological contexts. We discuss the major disease phenotypes described to date, including stress cardiomyopathy, chronic myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy-like remodeling, inflammatory cardiac disease, vascular and ischemic lesions, valvular and functional abnormalities, and congenital defects. Among these, acute stress-associated myocardial injury is one of the best-supported phenotypes in stranded cetaceans, whereas chronic cardiomyopathy-like remodeling is most clearly documented in pygmy and dwarf sperm whales. Inflammatory cardiac disease appears less frequent and is usually associated with systemic infection, while vascular disease includes not only atherosclerotic and thrombotic lesions but also embolic and decompression-related pathology. Current knowledge remains limited by strong species and sampling biases, with most evidence derived from stranded animals and a smaller body of work from managed dolphins. Overall, cetacean cardiovascular pathology reflects the interaction between extreme physiological specialization, environmental exposure, systemic disease, and acute stress. Key words Cetaceans " Cardiovascular disease " Stress cardiomyopathy " Myocardial fibrosis " Myocarditis " Valvular disease " Diving physiology " Cardiovascular adaptation.

articles.title: Adaptation, validity and reliability of quality-of-life scale in pediatric familial Mediterranean fever in children (p-FMFQoL).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to adapt the Quality-of-Life Scale in Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMFQoL), a disease-specific quality of life instrument originally developed for adults, in pediatric patients, and to evaluate its validity in children and adolescents diagnosed with Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF). In addition, the study aimed to demonstrate the reliability and applicability of the scale for assessing quality of life in pediatric FMF patients within a large multicenter cohort.

METHODS: FMF patients aged 8-18 years who met the Eurofever/PRINTO were included in the study. The adult FMFQoL, in which higher scores indicate poorer quality of life, was adapted for pediatric use through expert review, and subsequently validated in patients from a single center using internal consistency and convergent validity analyses. The reliability and applicability of the pediatric FMFQoL (p-FMFQoL) were examined in a large multicenter cohort, along with its associations with clinical and laboratory findings, and genetic subtypes.

RESULTS: The p-FMFQoL demonstrated excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.884) and showed a significant negative correlation with the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory scores, supporting convergent validity (r=-0.495, p < 0.001). In this large multicenter cohort, higher p-FMFQoL scores were significantly associated with female sex, increased attack frequency, elevated acute phase reactants, higher Pras scores, incomplete response to colchicine, and biallelic exon 10 mutations.

CONCLUSIONS: This study is the first to adapt and validate the FMFQoL for pediatric use. The p-FMFQoL demonstrated reliability and applicability based on data obtained from a large multicenter cohort.

articles.title: Magneto-Optical Coupling in Chiral Nanoparticles Synergistically Boosts Photothermal Antibacterial Therapy Through Magnetic Plasmon Synergistic Effect.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic overuse has triggered a drug-resistant bacteria crisis, severely endangering global public health security. Near-infrared (NIR) light-mediated photothermal therapy based on nanomaterials offers a promising antibiotic-free strategy, but it is often hampered by the intrinsically low photothermal conversion efficiency due to the high damping constant. In this study, magneto-plasmonic nanoparticles with chiral core-shell structure (CAu NRs@Fe3O4) were constructed, where the outer magnetic Fe3O4 shell induced a magneto-optical effect. The unique chiral configuration can provide abundant parallel interfacial lattices between Fe3O4 and chiral Au nanorods to introduce stronger coupling, which strengthens the interfacial magneto-optical coupling at the Fe3O4/Au heterointerface and thus reduces the plasmon damping constant to enable more efficient utilization of incident NIR light. Under the irradiation of 808 nm NIR light, the bactericidal efficiency of CAu NRs@Fe3O4 against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) reached 97.2%. In addition, in vivo wound infection treatment confirmed that wounds can be basically healed within 10 days after treating with CAu NRs@Fe3O4. Herein, this work not only elucidates the interfacial regulation mechanism of chiral magneto-optical nanomaterials for enhanced photothermal antibiosis, but also establishes potential therapeutic reagents toward drug-resistant bacterial infectious diseases.

articles.title: Frequency of On-Scene Goal-Directed Field Interventions for Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in a Regional System of Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Early on-scene resuscitation improves outcomes from pediatric non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); however, for pediatric patients, the early evacuation strategy remains commonplace. We sought to determine the frequency of goal-directed interventions initiated by paramedics prior to transport for pediatric patients with OHCA in a regional emergency medical services (EMS) system.

METHODS: In this retrospective observational study and cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) and linked electronic patient care reports (ePCR) data for patients aged <15 years treated by EMS for nontraumatic OHCA in Los Angeles (LA) County from January 2021 to December 2022. The primary outcome was the frequency of goal-directed therapies administered on scene prior to transport, which we defined as defibrillation for shockable rhythms and administration of epinephrine and fluid resuscitation for non-shockable rhythms. We also tabulated descriptive statistics regarding arrest characteristics, scene times, frequency of other prehospital treatments, and patient outcomes.

RESULTS: Among 176 eligible pediatric OHCA cases analyzed in CARES, 112 (64%) were male, the median age was 10 months (IQR 3-51), and 162 (92%) had an initial non-shockable rhythm. Of these, 156 patients were successfully linked to electronic patient care report (ePCR) records for analyses of prehospital interventions. Among 143 patients with non-shockable rhythms, EMS administered epinephrine before transport in 58 (41%) and fluids in 12 (8%). Among 13 patients with shockable rhythms, EMS delivered defibrillation before transport in 11 (85%). Bag-valve-mask (BVM) use was documented in 80 (51%) patients, although its timing relative to scene departure could not be determined. Median on-scene time was 10 minutes (IQR 5-18). Ten patients (6%) survived to hospital discharge, including 6 (3%) with a favorable neurologic outcome.

CONCLUSIONS: In this regional EMS system, fewer than half of patients with non-shockable rhythms received a dose of epinephrine and fewer than one in ten received intravenous fluids prior to transport, whereas most patients with shockable rhythms were defibrillated on scene. Further work is needed to identify barriers to timely delivery of on-scene resuscitative interventions.

articles.title: Left-sided portal hypertension secondary to pancreatic pseudocyst presenting with anaemia: A case report and literature review.
articles.journal: Anales del sistema sanitario de Navarra
articles.abstract: Left-sided portal hypertension (LSPH) is a rare clinical condition most commonly associated with splenic vein thrombosis secondary to pancreatitis. Gastric fundal varices may develop as a consequence of impaired venous drainage and can lead to life-threatening upper gastrointestinal bleeding. We present a case of LSPH secondary to acute pancreatitis and subsequent pancreatic pseudocyst formation, resulting in splenic vein thrombosis, variceal bleeding, anaemia, thrombocytopenia, and hypersplenism. The patient underwent splenectomy combined with cystogastrostomy through a left subcostal incision. LSPH-related symptoms resolved completely and the patient was discharged on postoperative Day 5. At the 9-month follow-up, contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated complete resolution of the pancreatic pseudocyst and fundal varices. In patients with pancreatic pseudocysts accompanied by anaemia, complications related to splenic vein thrombosis should be carefully evaluated. In selected patients with LSPH, combined splenectomy and cystogastrostomy may be an effective therapeutic option.

articles.title: Association of Medications for Opioid Use Disorder Use With Addiction Medicine Consultation and Hospital Service Line: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a major public health challenge. Medications for OUD (MOUD) are effective and life-saving treatments. Our objective was to examine the frequency of MOUD treatment among OUD patients at our institution over the past 6 years.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study conducted at an academic, tertiary care hospital located in the Midwest from July 2018 to June 2024. Patients aged 18 to 85 years old were included if they were hospitalized at our hospital, had an International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision diagnosis for an opioid-related disorder, or a positive urine drug screen for fentanyl during the encounter or up to 6 months prior to the encounter. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression were used to examine predictors of MOUD use.

RESULTS: We identified 5919 patient encounters. Patients were predominantly between 27 and 59 years old (3890, 66.2%), non-white (2948, 50.9%), and male (3350, 56.6%). A minority of patient encounters received MOUD (1228, 20.7%). Ages 27 to 59, white race, Medicaid insurance status, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index were associated with MOUD treatment. Addiction medicine (AM) consultation was strongly associated with MOUD treatment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.43, 95% CI 3.64-5.4, P < .001). Patients discharged from the obstetrics and gynecology service had greater odds for MOUD receipt (aOR 2.07, 95% CI 1.65-2.6, P < .001) than those discharged from the medicine service line. Patients discharged from the psychiatry (aOR 0.37, 95% CI 0.28-0.48, P < .001) or trauma surgery (aOR 0.14, 95% CI 0.11-0.18, P < .001) service lines were associated with lower odds of MOUD treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: A minority of hospitalized patients with OUD received MOUD. Age, race, insurance status, Elixhauser Comorbidity Index, discharge specialty service, AM consult, and discharge after the Drug Enforcement Administration X-waiver removal were associated with inpatient MOUD treatment. Future research should explore how clinicians can collaborate across specialties to improve MOUD implementation.

articles.title: Aspirin in Compensated Cirrhosis: Coherent Bleeding Signals and Transportable Evidence Before Practice Change.
High prevalence of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance and diagnostic accuracy of NG-Test CTX-M Multi among ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in Vietnam.
articles.abstract: CTX-M enzymes are the predominant extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) worldwide, yet local epidemiology in Vietnam remains incompletely characterized. This study investigated CTX-M prevalence among ESBL-producing Escherichia coli from inpatients at a tertiary-care hospital in Ho Chi Minh City and evaluated the diagnostic performance of the NG-Test CTX-M Multi assay. A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at FV Hospital from January 2024 to April 2025. ESBL-producing E. coli flagged by the VITEK 2 Advanced Expert System (AES) were tested with NG-Test CTX-M Multi (NG Biotech, France). Antimicrobial susceptibility testing followed CLSI M100 guidelines (2024). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed against multiplex real-time PCR (Allplex Entero-DR Assay) in a blinded evaluation of 76 isolates. Of the 461 E. coli isolates, 180 (39.0%) were ESBL producers; CTX-M was detected in 124 (68.9%). CTX-M-positive isolates showed significantly higher resistance to cefotaxime (98.4% vs 28.5%), cefepime (78.2% vs 10.7%), gentamicin (37.9% vs 12.7%), and ciprofloxacin (74.8% vs 73.2%); all P < 0.05. Carbapenems and amikacin retained high susceptibility (>95%) in both groups. CTX-M-positive isolates exhibited broader resistance profiles (≥6 antimicrobial classes: 68.9% vs 27.8%). AmpC flagging was more frequent in CTX-M-negative isolates (69.6% vs 28.2%; P < 0.001). NG-Test CTX-M Multi demonstrated 92.1% sensitivity (95% confidence interval [CI], 79.2-97.3), 94.7% specificity (95% CI, 82.7-98.5), PPV 94.6%, and NPV 92.3%. CTX-M was the dominant ESBL mechanism and was associated with broader multidrug resistance. NG-Test CTX-M Multi showed high diagnostic accuracy, supporting its role as a rapid screening tool; however, larger validation studies are warranted.IMPORTANCEInfections caused by Escherichia coli producing extended-spectrum beta-lactamases (ESBLs) pose a significant challenge for clinical management because they limit the effectiveness of commonly used antibiotics. CTX-M enzymes are now well established as the dominant ESBL determinants worldwide; however, their local prevalence and associated antimicrobial resistance patterns continue to vary across healthcare settings. In this study, we investigated the prevalence of CTX-M-producing E. coli and their resistance profiles in a tertiary care hospital in Vietnam. Our findings demonstrate a substantial burden of CTX-M-associated multidrug resistance affecting both hospital- and community-associated infections. In addition, the evaluation of a rapid lateral flow immunoassay for CTX-M detection highlights its potential role as a practical screening tool to support timely antimicrobial decision-making and infection control efforts. Together, these results provide clinically relevant data to support antimicrobial stewardship and optimize the management of infections caused by resistant E. coli.

articles.title: Delirium prevalence and practices across intensive care units in Singapore: a point prevalence survey.
authors: for SICM NICER (Society of Intensive Care Medicine Singapore National Investigators for Clinical Epidemiology and Research)
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Delirium is characterised by a disturbance in attention and awareness, alongside an acute change in cognition that develops over a short period and fluctuates in severity. It is associated with critical illness. This study aimed to determine the point prevalence of delirium in Singapore's intensive care units (ICUs) and assess the adherence of local delirium management practices and evidence-based international guidelines.

METHODS: A point prevalence survey was conducted on World Delirium Awareness Day, 13 March 2024. Local ICU leads completed questionnaires, and data on delirium prevalence and management practices were collected and compared with international guidelines.

RESULTS: Responses were received from 12 adult and two paediatric ICU leads, representing 66% of adult and 100% of paediatric ICUs in Singapore's public health institutions. Of 143 ICU patients, 92 (81.4%) were assessed for delirium, with 32 (34.8%) screening positive. Adult ICUs generally adhered to PADIS recommendations, including limiting benzodiazepine use, routinely assessing for delirium, and implementing protocols for pain management and sedation. However, holistic non-pharmacological care was lacking. Paediatric ICUs showed strong adherence to PANDEM guidelines, although deficiencies remained in delirium assessment and noise reduction practices. The most frequently reported barriers to improving management strategies were manpower shortages, time constraints and educational gaps.

CONCLUSION: Overall, local practices aligned well with international guidelines, but gaps remained in non-pharmacological interventions, resources, time and education. Addressing these gaps through quality improvement initiatives may enhance delirium management in ICUs.

articles.title: Ertapenem Pharmacokinetics in Equine Plasma and Synovial Fluid After Administration via Continuous Rate Infusion.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary pharmacology and therapeutics
articles.abstract: This study describes the pharmacokinetics of ertapenem as a continuous rate infusion (CRI) administered to horses at a rate of 3.75 mg/kg/h. Blood (30, 60, 120, 360, 480 min) and synovial (60, 120, 240, 360 min) samples were collected throughout the 8-hour infusion. Pharmacokinetic analysis was performed with noncompartmental methods. Parameters calculated included partial area under the curve (AUC), maximum concentration (Cmax), and clearance (CL). In plasma, the Cmax was 47.10 μg/mL (CV = 21.69%) and CL was 97.86 mL/kg/h (CV 17.83%). In synovial fluid, the Cmax was 25.71 μg/mL (CV 33.49%). The ratio of the synovial fluid to plasma concentration of ertapenem was 35.86% (CV 14.7%) and 54.58% (CV 22%) for AUC and Cmax, respectively. These values represent the extent of penetration from the plasma to synovial fluid. Ertapenem was well tolerated, although it caused transient soft feces in three horses. Ertapenem use in horses should be reserved for cases where culture and susceptibility results support administration and the isolated bacteria are not susceptible to other antimicrobials. Administration via continuous rate infusion is convenient for intensive care facilities and extended orthopedic surgery cases in reducing development of resistance by decreasing the total time below MIC and total drug administered.

articles.title: Phage therapy reduces bacterial burden and inflammation in a neutropenic murine sepsis model caused by hyperinvasive carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Klebsiella pneumoniae is an emerging opportunistic pathogen associated with severe clinical outcomes, and carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has become a critical threat requiring alternative therapeutic strategies. Phage therapy has recently gained attention as a promising alternative to combat antimicrobial resistance. However, its efficacy alone and in combination with antibiotics in immunocompromised hosts remains understudied. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model due to a hyperinvasive CRKP strain carrying multiple virulence factors. In vitro, ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) at 8/4 μg/mL was required to suppress growth of this strain for 48 h, and this concentration was slightly reduced to 4/4 μg/mL when combined with a cocktail of three taxonomically distinct phages (P24, P39, and P49). In vivo, a single dose of the phage cocktail (9 × 108 plaque-forming units/mouse), administered intravenously or intraperitoneally following bacterial challenge, achieved 2.5-5.1 log10 reductions of bacterial burdens across multiple tissues and organs. Correspondingly, serum tumor necrosis factor-α, interleukin-6, and interleukin-1β levels decreased significantly, and histopathological analysis revealed markedly mitigated inflammatory infiltration and tissue damage in the lung and liver. Both administration routes achieved comparable outcomes. Furthermore, in a delayed-treatment survival experiment, treatment with the phage cocktail combined with CAZ-AVI, initiated 2 h after lethal challenge, resulted in an 83.3% survival over the 28-day observation period. In contrast, all untreated mice succumbed within 2 days, and phage cocktail alone resulted in only 8.3% survival. Collectively, these findings provide in vivo evidence supporting the combination of phage cocktail and CAZ-AVI against CRKP infection in immunocompromised hosts.

IMPORTANCE: Carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) has emerged as a critical threat to global public health, causing life-threatening infections, disproportionately affecting immunocompromised patients who often fail to respond to conventional antibiotic therapy and experience high mortality rates. However, the efficacy of phage therapy in this vulnerable population and the comparative performance of different administration routes remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a cyclophosphamide-induced neutropenic murine sepsis model to evaluate the therapeutic potential of a phage cocktail against CRKP. We demonstrate that both intravenous and intraperitoneal phage administration achieve substantial bacterial load reduction and significant attenuation of systemic inflammation, revealing that phage therapy retains a robust positive response even in the absence of a fully functional host immune system. These findings underscore the clinical translational potential of phage as a viable alternative to antibiotics for combating CRKP infections in immunocompromised patients and provide critical evidence supporting intravenous phage delivery as a feasible administration route.

articles.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies of mental health screening tools in correctional settings.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Mental health disorders are highly prevalent in correctional settings, yet the diagnostic accuracy of available mental health screening tools remains uncertain and appears to vary across contexts. We aimed to synthesise evidence on the accuracy of screening tools used to detect any and severe mental health conditions in adult correctional populations and to identify factors influencing sensitivity and specificity.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis following Cochrane and PRISMA-DTA guidance (PROSPERO CRD42024571915). PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO and CINAHL were searched from 1 January 2004 to 22 April 2026. We included studies in adult correctional settings that employed a structured clinical interview as the reference standard and reported sufficient data to construct 2 × 2 tables. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios and diagnostic odds ratios were estimated separately for tools targeting any versus severe mental health conditions. Meta-regression was used to examine the influence of setting, screening tool characteristics, reference standards and methodological quality.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies reporting 61 distinct condition-sample-tool combinations were included. For screening tools targeting any mental health condition, pooled sensitivity was 78.2% (95% CI: 72.4%; 83.0%), and specificity was 64.8% (95% CI: 59.4%; 69.8%). For tools targeting severe mental health conditions, they were 57.4% (95% CI: 50.5%; 63.9%) and 80.8% (95% CI: 76.7%; 84.4%). Diagnostic odds ratios were 6.6 (95% CI: 5.4; 8.0) for any and 5.7 (95% CI: 4.5; 7.2) for severe conditions. Screening performance may vary, among other factors, across settings, sample mean ages and other variables.

CONCLUSIONS: Mental health screening tools used in correctional settings demonstrate moderate diagnostic accuracy, with substantial variation across contexts and designs. Despite these limitations, they may be a way to identify individuals requiring further assessment. Context-specific validation and adjustment of cut-off points may improve tools' clinical utility and support timely access to mental healthcare in correctional settings.

articles.title: International consensus on quality indicators of palliative care education and training: A Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite growing expectations for healthcare professionals across all settings to deliver high-quality palliative care, consensus on the quality indicators needed to guide the design and evaluation of palliative care education and training remains lacking. In response, a European COST Action (Code-Yaa@PC-Edu CA22127) funded initiative seeks to develop the gold standard to explore and measure the quality of palliative care education and training to ensure that all patients who require palliative care will receive it at the right time and by the right care providers.

AIM: To identify consensus-based quality indicators of palliative care education and training.

DESIGN: A two-round modified electronic Delphi technique was used.

PARTICIPANTS: An international panel of experts in palliative care education participated in the study.

RESULTS: A total of 190 experts participated in the first round and 151 in the second round (overall response rate: 79.5%). Consensus was predefined as ⩾80% agreement and was achieved for 36 indicators (10 structure, 22 process, 4 outcome). The highest level of consensus was reached regarding indicators related to the integration of ethics into education, a clear definition of educational competencies and support for interdisciplinarity.

CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes international consensus on 36 quality indicators of palliative care education and training. These indicators provide a consensus-informed framework for quality development and comparison across educational contexts. This could help stakeholders involved in palliative care education develop new educational programmes and evaluate and revise existing ones, although further research is needed to examine their operationalisation in practice.

articles.title: Moral distress in teams providing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and mechanical circulatory support: A qualitative study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMoral distress occurs when clinicians perceive constraints in carrying out the ethically appropriate action. While extensively studied among nurses, less is known about the interprofessional experience of moral distress, particularly in extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and mechanical circulatory support (MCS) care settings.Research question/aim/objectivesTo describe moral distress among interprofessional CVICU clinicians caring for patients receiving ECMO and/or MCS, identify perceived barriers and facilitators to addressing morally distressing situations, and explore desired support strategies.Research designThis qualitative descriptive study used interprofessional focus groups and inductive content analysis.Participants and research contextThirty-two professionals from a cardiovascular intensive care unit (CVICU) at a large academic medical center participated in 10 focus groups with two to six individuals per group.Ethical considerationsThe study was approved by the study-site Institutional Review Board, and participants provided informed consent before participation.Findings/resultsThree major themes were identified: (1) Purpose and emotional impact of providing care; (2) Relational dynamics of care; and (3) Organizational responsiveness to the frontline realities of ECMO/MCS care. Accounts of responsibility for patient care without a corresponding voice in decisions most clearly illustrate constrained moral agency. Meaningful work, grief, and coping provided a related context that situates the complexity of the moral distress experience for those working in this practice setting.ConclusionsThe findings suggest that support should help clinicians raise and act on ethical concerns and address other sources of distress (e.g., emotional strain, exhaustion, and professional grief). Notably, moral distress in the CVICU is shaped by the emotional impact of ECMO/MCS care, relational dynamics within and around the care team, and organizational responsiveness to frontline realities. Tailored strategies that strengthen communication, ethics and palliative engagement, team support, leadership awareness, and resource alignment are needed to optimize patient and family care and promote staff well-being.

articles.title: Gut Delivery of Pentameric GLP-1 Using Genetically Engineered Bacillus subtilis.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists and GLP-1 analogs are widely used for type 2 diabetes (T2D) and weight management, but current approaches can be limited by manufacturing complexity, cost, formulation requirements, and the need for repeated administration. Living microbial delivery systems offer a potential strategy for sustained gastrointestinal production of therapeutic peptides, but achieving stable expression, intestinal survival, and biologically relevant systemic exposure remains challenging. Here, we developed an engineered Bacillus subtilis (B. subtilis) spore-based platform for the gastrointestinal delivery of pentameric GLP-1. By leveraging the stress resistance, storage stability, and genetic tractability of B. subtilis, we generated a chromosomally integrated strain that secretes a multimeric GLP-1 construct designed to be processed in the intestine into monomeric GLP-1 peptides. Oral administration of engineered spores resulted in a mean serum GLP-1-related peptide concentration of 20.61 and 23.96 nM on days 3 and 5, respectively, in the first trial and 18.72 and 29.27 nM on days 3 and 7, respectively, in an independent second trial, with minimal detectable signal in green fluorescent protein (GFP) spore-treated controls. Treatment was also associated with preliminary glucose-lowering activity in a fasting-refeeding test. In a longer-term study, engineered spore administration was associated with reduced body weight and adiposity in mice with pre-existing diet-induced obesity, with semaglutide included as a positive pharmacologic benchmark. To improve its translational application, we further generated a marker-free strain that retained probiotic-relevant features of the parental strain, including gastrointestinal stress tolerance, epithelial cell adhesion, and antibiotic susceptibility. These findings provide proof of concept that engineered spore-forming bacteria may serve as a gastrointestinal peptide delivery platform and support further evaluation of this approach in disease-relevant models of metabolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Beyond cancer surveillance: Progressive coronary calcification preceding acute coronary syndrome in a lung cancer survivor.
EXPRESS: Dry Eye Disease in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Associated Clinical and Systemic Factors.
articles.journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dry eye disease (DED) has been increasingly reported in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD); however, its frequency and associated clinical factors in this population remain incompletely characterized.

PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the frequency of DED and identify factors associated with its presence in patients with IBD who underwent ophthalmological evaluation.

STUDY TYPE: Retrospective cross-sectional study.

POPULATION: A total of 501 adult patients with confirmed IBD, including 300 with ulcerative colitis and 201 with Crohn disease, were evaluated.Assessment Technique(s) or Outcome(s):DED was defined as a Schirmer test value of ≤5 mm/5 min. Demographic characteristics, disease duration, medical treatments, extraintestinal manifestations, and comorbidities were evaluated.

STATISTICAL TESTS: Group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test and Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Multivariable binary logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with DED.

RESULTS: DED was identified in 76 of 501 patients (15.2%). Multivariable analysis showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.06 per year, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04-1.08), extraintestinal manifestations (aOR 2.46, 95% CI 1.20-5.06), asthma (aOR 3.52, 95% CI 1.62-7.65), and anxiety/depression (aOR 3.09, 95% CI 1.25-7.65) were independently associated with DED.

DATA CONCLUSION: DED was identified in approximately 15% of this clinically selected IBD cohort. Older age, extraintestinal manifestations, asthma, and anxiety/depression were independently associated with DED. These findings suggest that ocular surface involvement in IBD may be associated with patient-level factors beyond conventional measures of intestinal disease severity.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery versus chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Chemoradiotherapy (CRT) is the primary treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC). However, CRT is associated with high toxicity, and access to radiotherapy infrastructure remains limited or unavailable in some settings globally. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) followed by radical surgery has therefore been proposed as an alternative to CRT, but the evidence regarding its efficacy and toxicity compared to CRT remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To compare NACT followed by radical surgery versus CRT for LACC.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov up to 20 May 2026, with no date or language restrictions. We also searched the reference lists of included studies and contacted experts in the field.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) in women with LACC (FIGO 2018 stage IB3/IIA2/IIB/IIIA-C/IVA) comparing NACT followed by radical surgery to CRT. We excluded non-randomised studies.

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were overall survival, disease-free survival, and progression-free survival. Important outcomes included recurrence, acute and late toxicity, and quality of life.

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias in the included studies using Cochrane's RoB 1 tool.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We performed a random-effects meta-analysis using the inverse-variance method. We assessed the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach.

INCLUDED STUDIES: Three RCTs (from four reports), with a total of 1326 women, reported on the outcomes of interest and were included in the meta-analysis.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: NACT + radical surgery may result in little to no difference in five-year overall survival compared to CRT (hazard ratio (HR) 1.11, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.90 to 1.36; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1259 participants; low-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for five-year disease-free survival (HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.97 to 1.69; 1 study, 635 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and five-year progression-free survival (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.07 to 1.75; 1 study, 626 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT + radical surgery probably increases grade ≥ 3 acute toxicity (risk ratio (RR) 1.82, 95% CI 1.45 to 2.29; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1224 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The evidence is very uncertain for grade ≥ 3 late toxicity (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50 to 1.01; 1 study, 591 participants; very low-certainty evidence). NACT + radical surgery may result in little to no difference in quality of life after 24 months compared to CRT (mean difference 0.48, 95% CI -4.35 to 5.31; I² = 0%; 2 studies, 239 participants; low-certainty evidence). The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate, downgraded primarily due to risk of bias, indirectness, and imprecision.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: The current evidence does not support NACT followed by radical surgery as an alternative to CRT for LACC. While five-year overall survival may be comparable between treatments, the evidence is very uncertain for disease-free and progression-free survival, while severe acute toxicity is probably increased. Quality of life appears similar between treatments. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect on severe late toxicity, given the limited evidence base, older radiotherapy techniques used, and high cross-over rates in the included studies. CRT remains the standard of care where high-quality radiotherapy is available; where it is not, the evidence remains insufficient to recommend NACT followed by radical surgery as an alternative.

FUNDING: No external funding was received for this review.

REGISTRATION: doi: 10.1002/14651858.CD014684.

articles.title: Asthma Blitz Days: An Innovative Approach to Asthma Management in Schools.
articles.abstract: Asthma is the most prevalent chronic condition among school-aged children in the United States, contributing to emergency department visits, school absences, and diminished well-being. Inadequate asthma control is driven by medication nonadherence, psychosocial stressors, and social determinants of health. School nurses are pivotal in coordinating care, supporting medication management, and fostering asthma-friendly environments. In Pitt County, North Carolina, Asthma Blitz Days were developed as a collaborative, school-based intervention between Pitt County School Health Program and ECU Health (formerly Vidant) Maynard Children's Hospital Pediatric Asthma Program. Targeting Pre-K to 5th grade students with documented asthma, this program assessed symptoms, delivered age-appropriate education using the teach-back method, and improved medication and documentation compliance. School nurse-led, multidisciplinary interventions like Asthma Blitz Days offer a scalable approach to improving asthma control and promoting health equity in school communities.

articles.title: TTR-stabilising medicines for the treatment of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To assess the effects of TTR-stabilising medicines (tafamidis and acoramidis) compared to usual care or placebo on all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalisations in people with ATTR-CM. Secondary objectives To assess the effects of tafamidis and acoramidis compared to usual care or placebo in people with ATTR-CM according to the following predefined subgroups. Demographic subgroups, including ethnicity and sex ATTR subtype (ATTRwt versus ATTRv) Disease severity, according to NYHA functional class.

articles.title: Prefrontal mechanisms of threat-context integration in facial emotion recognition: the role of trait anxiety.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Social communication requires accurate recognition of facial expressions, which is strongly influenced by environmental context. In threatening situations, individuals typically identify danger-related signals more readily than safety-related cues. Although such threat-detection biases can be adaptive, exaggerated biases may contribute to anxious psychopathology. Here, we examined individual differences in threat perception and tested whether threat-related perceptual biases can be modified through threat-safety reversal learning.

METHODS: Using whole-head magnetoencephalography, 81 participants (58 female, 23 male) with low or high trait anxiety completed an emotion recognition task involving subtly expressive fearful and happy faces presented in either an instructed threat-of-shock or safety context.

RESULTS: Verbal instructions reliably established threat and safety contexts and, as predicted, planned contrasts show enhanced recognition accuracy for ambiguous facial expressions in a context-congruent manner, particularly in high-anxiety participants. Also consistent with preregistered hypotheses, processing of affectively incongruent face-context combinations was associated with mid-latency prefrontal activation. However, at later processing stages, high-anxiety individuals showed blunted prefrontal differentiation, suggesting reduced sensitivity to contextual deviance.During threat-safety reversal learning, early prefrontal activity indicated flexible differentiation between threat and safety in low-anxiety participants, whereas this effect was absent in high-anxiety individuals, pointing to difficulties in updating previously learned threat associations.

CONCLUSION: Together, these findings suggest that high levels of trait anxiety disrupt prefrontal mechanisms supporting flexible integration of contextual and facial information, resulting in rigid emotion recognition and reduced adaptability in updating threat-safety associations - processes that may contribute to persistent fear and maladaptive emotional responses.

articles.title: Identification of Intercellular Adhesion Molecule-1-Targeting DNA Aptamers as a Host-Directed Strategy to Inhibit Human Rhinovirus Infection.
articles.abstract: Human rhinoviruses (HRVs) are the leading viral cause of upper respiratory tract infections and major triggers of exacerbations in patients with asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. More than 150 HRV serotypes have been identified, yet no approved specific antiviral therapies are currently available. Because most HRV serotypes exploit intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) to infect airway epithelial cells, targeting this host receptor represents a promising strategy to overcome viral diversity and the limitation of virus-directed approaches. Here, we developed DNA aptamers directed against the HRV-binding region of ICAM-1 using a systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment strategy guided by a minimal peptide reproducing the receptor-viral attachment interface. A 77-nucleotide single-stranded DNA pool comprising ∼1015 molecules was subjected to iterative selection, yielding eight candidate aptamers that were evaluated by computational modeling, in vitro binding assays, and functional antiviral assays in human epithelial cells. This workflow identified two lead aptamers, I5 and I8, which inhibited HRV-A16 infection in a concentration-dependent manner, as measured by infectious viral titers and viral RNA quantification. These findings support ICAM-1-directed aptamers as promising host-targeted antiviral candidates and establish a broadly applicable framework for developing nucleic acid therapeutics against respiratory viruses.

articles.title: Temporal trends and geospatial heterogeneity in Chagas disease in Mexico, 1998-2024: a multiscale cross-registry analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chagas disease evolves over decades, and notification, hospital-discharge, and mortality systems capture different points in its natural history. We evaluated their temporal concordance in Mexico and whether clustered registered mortality was associated with municipal social deprivation.

METHODS: We analysed notification, hospital-discharge, and mortality data through 2024. We used age-stratified quasi-Poisson models to estimate annual changes, a segmented model to describe notifications, and a registry-by-year model to compare slopes during 2005-2024. We age-standardised municipal deaths, tested for clustering, and modelled them against the 2020 Social Lag Index (SLI), 2019 healthcare supply, ascertainment proxies, and a state random intercept.

RESULTS: Hospital discharges decreased by 5.38% annually (95% confidence interval (CI) = -6.59, -4.16) and mortality by 2.49% (95% CI = -3.44, -1.54). Notification was not log-linear: it rose 10.50% annually to 2017, dropped 27.96% at the category split, then showed no detectable change (-2.26%; 95% CI = -4.77, 0.32). Slopes differed (P < 0.001), although notification's common-period change was indeterminate (1.25%; 95% CI = -0.79, 3.34). Among 2,475 municipalities, 253 recorded 735 deaths, with clustered residuals (Moran's I = 0.430). A 43-municipality High-High core remained after multiplicity correction; cluster death shares are post-selection statistics. A one-standard-deviation higher SLI was associated with registered mortality (incidence rate ratio = 1.48; dependence-robust 95% CI = 1.20, 2.08), but residual spatial autocorrelation persisted (Moran's I = 0.205); the interval included one after joint adjustment for two ascertainment proxies, and no spatial model met its reliability gate; the association is exploratory. Chronic disease predominated, and acute notification rates plateaued across 25-59 years. Infant notifications averaged 1.12 per year during 2017-2024, against 2,131 modelled congenital infections (563-4259 across parameter sets), which are different estimands.

CONCLUSIONS: Mexican registries showed no concordant temporal trend. Detection was adult-centred and chronic-dominant during 2005-2024. Registered mortality was spatially clustered; its association with deprivation remains exploratory and unresolved.

articles.title: Redefining venous access device-associated fibroblastic sleeves: Improving terminological accuracy by replacing the misnomer "fibrin sheath".
articles.abstract: The connective tissue that develops around vascular access devices has traditionally been referred to as a "fibrin sheath." Although this term has remained entrenched in the vascular access literature and across related clinical specialties including nephrology, interventional radiology, oncology, critical care, and cardiology, contemporary pathophysiological evidence indicates that it lacks biological accuracy and does not adequately reflect the nature of this pathophysiological phenomenon. This inaccuracy creates confusion within the scientific community and may erroneously lead to the consideration of this condition as a specific type of catheter-related thrombosis, and to be treated accordingly. As a joint statement of the World Congress on Vascular Access (WoCoVA), the Italian Vascular Access Society (IVAS), and the Vascular Access Society (VAS), this position paper, developed consistently with current evidence, recommends discontinuing the use of the term fibrin sheath in favor of the more appropriate term fibroblastic sleeve. The latter more precisely describes the lesion's biological composition and morphological structure, for the purposes of better clarity and correct management.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics of unregulated psychoactive supplement exposures: a 15-year multicenter study of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Unregulated psychoactive "supplements" including kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine are readily accessible, raising concern for toxicity and dependence owing to their GABA and opioid receptor activity; however, clinical features associated with their use are poorly characterized. We describe hospital presentations and management of kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine exposures.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the Toxicology Investigators Consortium (ToxIC) Core Registry, which prospectively collects information on patients managed by medical toxicologists (1 January 2010-31 December 2024). All cases involving kratom, phenibut, and/or tianeptine exposures were included. Demographics, exposure circumstances, clinical presentation, management, and outcomes were examined.

RESULTS: We identified 152 patient encounters involving kratom (n = 97), phenibut (n = 44) and/or tianeptine (n = 11), with case counts increasing over time. Median age was 35 years (IQR 26-42 years), and 127 (83.6%) were male. Co-ingestions were common (n = 73; 48.0%) frequently involving other psychoactive supplements (n = 27; 17.8%), stimulants (n = 23; 15.1%) and/or opioids (n = 22; 14.5%). Most consultations involved intentional use (n = 131; 86.2%), including euphoria (n = 60; 39.5%), perceived therapeutic/wellness benefit (n = 18; 11.8%) and withdrawal self-management (n = 13; 8.6%). Thirty-five encounters (23.0%) resulted in intensive care admission and one patient died. Addiction treatment infrequently involved buprenorphine/naloxone (n = 15; 9.9%). At hospital discharge 16 (10.5%) patients received naloxone overdose prevention kit education and/or prescription.

DISCUSSION: Psychoactive supplement exposures evaluated by medical toxicologists were associated with substantial morbidity, with nearly one-quarter requiring intensive care unit admission. Withdrawal was common, and nearly half of encounters involved co-ingestants.

CONCLUSION: Hospital presentations involving kratom, phenibut, and tianeptine increased over time, supporting recognition of these substances as emerging drugs of misuse rather than benign supplements. These findings highlight opportunities to strengthen addiction-focused care, regulatory oversight and public education.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure in a multicentre emergency department cohort.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure are poorly characterised. We describe clinical features, outcomes and influence of common co-detections in patients with analytically massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure.

METHODS: Retrospective multicentre cohort study using the Emerging Drugs Network of Australia-Victoria registry. Patients presenting to 18 Victorian emergency departments between November 2021 and March 2026 with whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentrations ≥300 mg/L (2.9 mmol/L). Clinical features, complications, interventions, and outcomes were described. Multivariable logistic regression examined associations between whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration, opioid, benzodiazepine, and methamphetamine co-detection and five clinical domains: severe CNS depression (Glasgow Coma Scale of three), bradypnoea, hypoxaemia, hypotension, and hypothermia.

RESULTS: A total of 154 patients were included. Median age was 33 years (IQR 28-40); median whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration 380 mg/L (3.7 mmol/L), IQR 340-470 mg/L (3.3-4.5 mmol/L). Severe CNS depression was common (116/154 (75%) had a first Glasgow Coma Scale of three), as were intubation 101/154 (66%), intensive care admission (103/154, 67%), hypotension (39/154, 25%), vasopressor use (31/154, 20%), and hypothermia (56/154, 36%). Polysubstance exposure occurred in 150/154 (97%). Opioid co-detection (31/154, 20%) was independently associated with hypotension (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.51, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.83-11.14) and hypoxaemia (aOR 3.64, 95% CI 1.14-11.67). Higher whole blood gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration was independently associated with hypotension but not CNS depression, bradypnoea, hypoxaemia, or hypothermia. One patient died (0.6%) and 42/154 (27%) were discharged directly from the emergency department.

DISCUSSION: Massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure produced a remarkably consistent severe but largely reversible toxidrome. Within the massive exposure range studied, increasing gamma-hydroxybutyrate concentration contributed principally to haemodynamic compromise, whereas common co-detections had little influence apart from opioid-associated hypotension and hypoxaemia.

CONCLUSION: Massive gamma-hydroxybutyrate exposure was associated with profound but largely reversible toxicity and excellent in-hospital survival with supportive care. These findings support aggressive early supportive management and identify haemodynamic compromise as remaining concentration-dependent in the massive exposure range.

articles.title: Association of cumulative cholesterol-HDL-glucose index with cognitive function changes and risk of new-onset mild cognitive impairment in middle-aged and older adults: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundMetabolic dysfunction is a modifiable contributor to cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease risk. The cholesterol-HDL-glucose (CHG) index integrates atherogenic dyslipidemia and hyperglycemia, but the cognitive implications of cumulative CHG exposure are unknown.ObjectiveTo examine the association of cumulative CHG (cuCHG) exposure with cognitive trajectories and new-onset mild cognitive impairment (MCI).MethodsAdults aged ≥45 years were drawn from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS, 2011-2020). MCI was defined using ageing-associated cognitive decline criteria. K-means clustering classified longitudinal CHG trajectories, and cuCHG was calculated as [(CHG2012 + CHG2015)/2] × time interval. Linear mixed-effects models assessed cognitive trajectories, and Cox regression with restricted cubic splines evaluated incident MCI risk.ResultsAmong 2646 participants, 404 (15.3%) developed MCI over 5 years. All cognitive domains declined significantly (global cognition β/year = -0.343, 95% CI -0.367 to -0.320; all p < 0.001), but no time × cuCHG interaction was detected (all p > 0.05). In fully adjusted Cox models, the middle-CHG cluster showed 21% lower MCI risk than the low-CHG cluster (HR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.62-0.99, p = 0.043); the high-CHG cluster did not differ. Restricted cubic splines showed a non-linear relationship (p for non-linearity < 0.05), with elevated risk at both extremes. A significant sex interaction was observed (p = 0.015).ConclusionsCumulative CHG exposure showed a non-linear association with incident MCI, with a middle-range trajectory independently associated with lower risk. Balanced metabolic homeostasis, rather than indiscriminately minimizing metabolic indices, may be relevant to cognitive ageing.

articles.title: Local IL-17A neutralization reduces experimental peri-implant bone loss in type 2 diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to investigate whether local IL-17A neutralization attenuates peri-implant alveolar bone resorption in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) rats.

METHODS: Thirty male Sprague-Dawley rats with T2DM were randomly divided into three groups (n = 10): a control group (without ligature‑induced peri‑implantitis), a peri-implantitis (PI) group, and an anti-IL-17A group. Peri-implant bone changes were evaluated by micro-CT, osteoclastogenesis by TRAP staining, and inflammatory responses by H&E staining, qPCR, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence.

RESULTS: Micro-CT revealed significantly greater linear and volumetric bone resorption in the PI group versus controls, which was reduced by IL-17A neutralization. TRAP staining showed increased osteoclasts in the PI group, attenuated by IL-17A neutralization. H&E staining confirmed exacerbated inflammation and bone resorption in the PI group, attenuated by anti-IL-17A. Inflammatory cytokine mRNAs were upregulated in the PI group, with IL-17A exhibiting the most pronounced increase; IL-17A neutralization reduced these levels, with IL-17A showing the greatest reduction-confirmed at the protein level. Immunofluorescence showed increased MPO+ neutrophils, IL-6+cells, and RANKL+ cells in the PI group versus controls, reduced by IL-17A neutralization.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that local IL-17A blockade effectively attenuates peri-implant alveolar bone resorption in T2DM rats by suppressing inflammatory responses and osteoclastogenesis, supporting this targeted strategy as a promising therapeutic approach for diabetic peri-implantitis. However, as these are preclinical results, further studies are needed to validate the therapeutic relevance of this targeted strategy for diabetic peri‑implantitis.

articles.title: Impact of implementing an indication-based urinary tract infection diagnostic order menu at a veterans affairs facility.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Inappropriate treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria (ASB), particularly among patients with altered mental status (AMS), contributes to antimicrobial resistance and adverse outcomes. In June 2024, the Veterans Affairs Palo Alto Health Care System (VAPAHCS) implemented a required indication-based Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) diagnostic order menu, prompting indication selection for urinalysis with reflex to culture (UARC) or Urine culture (UC) orders. This analysis assessed the impact of the UTI diagnostic order menu on UTI-related clinical practice.

METHODS: Veterans aged 18 years and older with UARC or UC orders were included in this retrospective, quality improvement analysis comparing pre- (6/1/2023-11/30/2023) and post-order menu implementation (6/1/2024-11/30/2024) periods. Community living center (CLC) orders were excluded. The primary outcome was percent change of UARC/UC orders per month. Secondary outcomes included rates of UARC/UC order and therapeutic appropriateness, ordered vs. documented indication mismatch, AMS-related UTI diagnoses, and 30-day adverse outcomes (i.e., Clostridioides difficile infection, repeat UARC/UC order, and mortality). Data was analyzed using descriptive and chi-square statistics.

RESULTS: Following implementation, UARC/UC orders decreased by an average of 30% over six months. One hundred orders were randomized to the pre- and post-implementation groups. UARC/UC ordering appropriateness improved significantly (61% vs. 85%, p=0.0004). There were no significant differences in treatment appropriateness or 30-day adverse outcomes. Only 8% of post-implementation AMS indication orders met criteria for likely UTI.

CONCLUSION: The indication-based UTI diagnostic order menu significantly reduced UARC/UC orders and improved diagnostic appropriateness, supporting its role in enhancing diagnostic stewardship.

articles.title: Cortical and meningeal neuroimmune interactions contribute to the generation of migraine headaches.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a prevalent disorder that ranks as the second leading cause of disability among all diseases. Recent advancements have significantly enhanced our comprehension of its underlying pathophysiology. Growing evidence highlights complex neuroimmune signaling networks-particularly interactions between meningeal nociceptors and resident immune cells-as key contributors to headache generation. The clinical success of anti-calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) antibodies underscores the importance of intercellular communication between the dural nociceptive nerves and adjacent resident immune cells such as macrophages in migraine headache. Notably, the intercellular inflammatory interplay is not confined to the meninges. Disturbances within the brain parenchyma potentially act as initiating triggers, as suggested by the presence of aura and premonitory symptoms preceding the headache. Recent experimental discoveries indicate that neuronal stress triggers an inflammatory signaling cascade that, through interactions with astrocytes and microglia, propagates to the meninges, ultimately inducing meningeal neurogenic inflammation and headache. This model is supported by converging experimental evidence and human imaging studies employing PET and quantitative MRI, which document the presence of changes compatible with inflammatory activity within the brain parenchyma and overlying meninges of patients with migraine with aura. Genetic studies identifying several inflammation-related genes and pathways as risk factors for migraine further corroborate this concept. Furthermore, cell-specific transcriptomic analyses of mouse brains have revealed astrocyte-selective activation of nuclear factor kappa B -regulated inflammatory transcriptional pathways after cortical spreading depolarization, the neurophysiological correlate of migraine aura. Owing to their extensive interface with the cerebrospinal fluid, astrocytes are uniquely positioned to release inflammatory mediators to activate meningeal nociceptors and immune cells. Insights from pain research suggest that neuroimmune interactions may be responsible for the widespread parenchymal increases in 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) PET signals observed in migraine with aura patients. This discovery also identifies TSPO as a potential player in migraine pathophysiology and novel drug target. In this review, by integrating cellular and molecular findings from peripheral pain and inflammation research, we examine the dynamic interactions between neurons and glia, as well as between meningeal nociceptors and immune cells in the context of migraine headache. This perspective provides a conceptual framework for understanding how nociceptors and glial cells coordinate to signal non-homeostatic brain states-initiating protective, tightly regulated responses without progressing to overt neuroinflammatory disease and provides novel insight into the findings of PET studies involving TSPO.

articles.title: Long Term Osteoporosis Treatment with Denosumab in a Real-World Setting: Observations beyond 10 years.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Denosumab is often employed as a long-term therapy for treating patients with osteoporosis. Yet, scant data are available on the safety and efficacy of denosumab use beyond 10 years. Our objective was to retrospectively analyze our experience using denosumab for osteoporosis treatment in a real-world setting to provide efficacy and safety data, especially when used beyond a decade.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed of 4030 patients treated for osteoporosis with denosumab as part of routine rheumatology care. Patients with long-term use (n=750) were selected, as defined by ≥5 years cumulative exposure. This group was then stratified into those receiving ≥10-year cumulative exposure (n=400) and a reference group with exposure for 5-10 years (n=350), a duration established to be safe and effective from prior studies. Efficacy of denosumab was determined by analyzing sequential BMD. Safety was determined through chart review. Safety concerns of special interest, namely osteonecrosis of jaw and atypical femur fractures, were described in detail.

RESULTS: 400 patients were identified with extended denosumab exposure ≥10 years. For these patients, BMD increased steadily with no evidence of plateau and surpassed the total hip surrogate thresholds associated with reduced fracture risk. Among safety concerns of special interest, we observed 18 cases of ONJ and 2 cases of AFF from the entire cohort, with no temporal relationship to duration of use.

CONCLUSIONS: Based on our experience, we conclude that there is no evidence-based rationale for discontinuing denosumab after 10 years; rather, prolonged use appears to remain both safe and effective.

articles.title: MRI-Derived Atrial Substrate Score Predicts Recurrence After First-Time Cryoballoon Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
articles.abstract:
