BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The conventional classification of atrial fibrillation (AF) as paroxysmal or persistent may not reflect structural atrial remodeling and has limited value for predicting recurrence after pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). We investigated whether an MRI-derived substrate score combining left atrial (LA) fibrosis and size improves recurrence risk stratification after first-time cryoballoon PVI.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 69 patients undergoing first cryoballoon PVI; 67 underwent pre-procedural 3-Tesla late gadolinium enhancement MRI. LA fibrosis was graded using the UTAH classification; the maximal horizontal LA diameter in the two-chamber view was measured, and LA volume was calculated with a 3D tool. An exploratory point-based score was constructed from LA diameter categories (< 44 mm, 0 points; 44-< 48 mm, 2 points; ≥ 48 mm, 4 points) and advanced fibrosis (UTAH stage 3-4, 1 point). Discrimination for 12-month arrhythmia recurrence was assessed by ROC analysis.

RESULTS: Advanced fibrosis was present in half of the patients with paroxysmal AF, with a similar UTAH distribution in both phenotypes (p = 0.83). LA diameter and volume were larger in patients with recurrence and discriminated recurrence (AUC 0.95 and 0.92). The substrate score predicted recurrence (AUC 0.96, 95% CI 0.91-0.99), with recurrence rates of 0%, 41% and 96% in low-, intermediate- and high-risk patients. LA size was the main contributor, with fibrosis providing complementary information, whereas AF phenotype did not provide incremental predictive value.

CONCLUSIONS: An MRI-derived substrate score, with LA size as the main contributor and fibrosis as a complementary marker, predicted arrhythmia recurrence after cryoballoon PVI better than the conventional AF phenotype. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: The Ross procedure: Technical principles, operative strategy, and pitfalls for long-term success.
articles.abstract: The Ross procedure remains an attractive aortic valve replacement strategy for children, adolescents, and selected young adults. Pulmonary autograft replacement provides excellent hemodynamics, freedom from anticoagulation, growth potential in children, and favorable long-term survival in appropriately selected patients. These advantages, however, come at the cost of substantial technical complexity. Small imperfections during autograft harvest, implantation, coronary transfer, or root reconstruction can result in early dysfunction, coronary complications, or late autograft dilatation and failure. The purpose of this review is to summarize a practical and reproducible approach to the Ross procedure with emphasis on operative strategy, technical details, Ross-Konno modifications, autograft stabilization techniques, and avoidance of common pitfalls. Rather than advocating a single technique, we emphasize fundamental principles that permit adaptation to patient anatomy while maintaining the geometric integrity of the left ventricular outflow tract, aortic root, and pulmonary root.

articles.title: Aligning Care in Surgical Sepsis: Palliative Consultation and Treatment Intensity in Older Surgical ICU Adults.
articles.abstract: ObjectivesOlder adults with surgical sepsis frequently require urgent, high-risk interventions despite uncertain prospects for meaningful recovery. Although palliative care (PC) can support communication, shared decision-making, and goal-concordant care, its integration into the management of surgical sepsis remains poorly defined.MethodsA retrospective cohort study of critically ill surgical patients aged 65 years and older with surgical sepsis requiring a procedural intervention. Patients who received PC consultation were compared to non-PC patients with respect to characteristics, treatment intensity and life-saving supportive care, complications, code status, and mortality.ResultsAmong 1380 patients, 220 (15.9%) received PC consultation. The rate of PC consultation increased significantly over the study period (R2 = 0.627; p = .004). Patients receiving PC consultation had fewer baseline chronic medical comorbidities but higher 30-day mortality (59.1% vs 21.6%; p < .001). PC consultation was associated with lower rates of UTI (9% vs 17%; p = .003), bacteremia (9% vs 16%; p = .01), additional antibiotic use (82% vs 89%; p = .004) and lower rates of subsequent surgical procedures (55% vs 67%; p < .001), However, PC patients had higher rates of mechanical ventilation (68% vs 45%; p < .001). Importantly, PC consultation was not associated with any increase in do not resuscitate (DNR) status during hospitalization. On multivariable analysis, PC consultation was associated with higher odds of ventilator support (OR = 2.14; 95%CI = 1.45-3.16; p < .001) and mortality (OR = 4.90; 95%CI = 3.25-7.43; p < .001).ConclusionsIncreasing PC utilization was not associated with greater transitions to DNR status, challenging the perception that PC principally facilitates treatment limitation. These findings are consistent with a potential role for PC as a decision-support resource alongside high-quality surgical and critical care.

articles.title: Optimizing migraine care delivery: Subspecialty expertise, integrated care pathways, and centers of excellence models.
Quality benchmarks in CRS-HIPEC surgery: An 11-year single-center analysis of outcomes, safety, and perioperative performance (2014-2024).
articles.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quality indicators (QIs) are central to safe delivery of cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS-HIPEC), yet program-level benchmarking across tumor types is scarce.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the structure, process, and outcome QIs of a single-center CRS-HIPEC program (2014-2024) and to assess temporal trends in cytoreduction completeness, early mortality, length of stay (LOS), renal safety, and multidisciplinary team (MDT) integration against contemporary international benchmarks.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of consecutive CRS-HIPEC procedures (2014-2024) was conducted at a Polish tertiary center. Prespecified QIs included complete or near-complete cytoreduction (CC-0/1), 30- and 90-day mortality, LOS, LOS > 10 days, unplanned reoperation, 30-day readmission, MDT uptake, and acute kidney injury (AKI; defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) serum creatinine criteria). Time trends were displayed with Shewhart charts and funnel plots; Wilson's 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) were used for proportions.

RESULTS: Among 319 procedures (colorectal cancer (CRC) 111; ovarian cancer 87; mesothelioma/other 57; low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm/pseudomyxoma peritonei (LAMN/PMP) 52; gastric cancer 12), the CC-0/1 rate was 93.4% overall (CRC 96.4%; LAMN/PMP 100%; ovarian cancer 90.8%; gastric cancer 91.7%; mesothelioma/other 86.0%). Thirtyand 90-day mortality were 0.6% and 1.6%, respectively; tumor-specific 30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 1.9%. Median LOS fell from 8.6 to 7.4 days (2014-2018 vs 2019-2024), and LOS > 10 days declined from 25.0% to 13.2%. Peritoneal cancer index (PCI) correlated weakly with LOS (Spearman's ρ = 0.13, p = 0.019), while AKI occurred in 70/308 (22.7%, 95% CI: 18.4-27.7), predominantly stage 1; AKI did not differ by cisplatin exposure (26.0% vs 21.2%, p = 0.389). The proportion of procedures with documented MDT discussion increased to approx. 20-33% after 2018.

CONCLUSIONS: Over 11 years, a single-center CRS-HIPEC program achieved high-quality cytoreduction with low early mortality and a reduction in LOS, meeting or exceeding contemporary QI standards. Incorporating AKI and MDT uptake into routine audit supports comprehensive, program-level benchmarking.

articles.title: Inclusive entertainment for persons with disabilities in Saudi Arabia: a policy-survey comparison.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Disability inclusion in entertainment is important for quality of life. However, participation may remain limited even when formal policies exist. This study compared Saudi Arabia's policy expectations for inclusive entertainment with the experiences reported by persons with disabilities (PwDs). It also examined barriers associated with participation within the Vision 2030 context.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A comparative policy-survey design was used. First, Saudi policy and accessibility documents applicable during the 2022 survey period were coded into a policy matrix. The matrix was then compared with data from a cross-sectional survey (N = 300; valid n = 275). Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests and binary logistic regression were used. In addition, a Firth bias-reduced sensitivity analysis was applied to the sparse transport data.

RESULTS: About half of respondents (50.2%) considered entertainment provision in their place of residence or a nearby city sufficient, while 40.0% reported participation in recreational activities. In addition, only 20.0% reported easy access, special transport support, specialist/initiative support and easy access to specialists. Ease of access and special transport support were both associated with participation. The transport association was larger but had a wide confidence interval. Moreover, 60.0% reported differential treatment or distress in the entertainment context.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings show differences between formal policy expectations and the experiences reported by the recruited sample. In particular, transportation, practical accessibility, specialist support and social inclusion remained important concerns. Therefore, inclusive entertainment should be evaluated across the full participation pathway rather than only by the presence of venues.

articles.title: Impact of Rehabilitation Initiation Timing on Safety and Efficacy in Patients With Acute Stroke and Concurrent Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal timing of rehabilitation initiation in patients with acute stroke and heart failure remains uncertain due to concerns about hemodynamic instability.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and efficacy of rehabilitation timing in patients with acute stroke and comorbid heart failure.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used a nationwide Japanese inpatient database. This study included 9827 adult patients hospitalized for stroke with heart failure. Patients were categorized into 3 groups: very early rehabilitation (VER; admission day or day 1), early rehabilitation (ER; days 2-3), and delayed rehabilitation (DR; days 4-7). The primary safety outcome was a composite of major in-hospital adverse events (death, mechanical ventilation, or vasopressor use) within 30 days. The primary efficacy outcome was the Barthel Index at discharge. Multinomial propensity scores were estimated, and inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to adjust for confounding variables. Inverse probability of censoring weighting and augmented inverse probability weighting were used for the relevant outcomes. Pairwise comparisons were performed.

RESULTS: No significant differences in major in-hospital adverse events were observed between the groups. The VER group had a lower risk of in-hospital respiratory failure (risk ratio [RR] = 0.58, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.33-0.99) and 90-day stroke readmission (RR = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.12-0.87) and a higher discharge Barthel Index (mean difference = 3.66, 95% CI = 0.23-7.09) than the DR group.

CONCLUSIONS: VER was associated with better outcomes in selected measures than DR, without significant differences in major adverse events.

articles.title: Determinants of progression of filarial lymphedema in a clinic-based cohort: Implications for global elimination.
articles.abstract: Lymphatic filariasis remains a leading cause of chronic, debilitating lymphedema. Global health initiatives emphasize morbidity management and disability prevention (MMDP) through routine self-care to limit disease progression. To evaluate the long-term clinical trajectory of this condition, we objectively quantified limb volume changes and their determinants in a retrospective cohort of 110 adult patients with filarial lower limb lymphedema in Puducherry, India, over a median follow-up of nine years. Our analysis revealed that disease stability is highly attainable, with nearly half (46.4%) of the cohort exhibiting no volumetric progression. While recurrent adenolymphangitis episodes and baseline hypertension correlated with progression severity, multivariable regression identified strict adherence to home-based MMDP self-care practices as the primary independent predictor of halted or reduced limb volume change. These findings demonstrate that sustained behavioral adherence to simple self-care interventions can effectively mitigate chronic lymphedema. Integrating robust patient education and long-term adherence support into routine clinical care is therefore paramount within the global elimination program to prevent further disability in affected populations worldwide.

articles.title: Dynamic Risk Assessment of Severe Ventricular Arrhythmia in Patients With Implantable Defibrillators and Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Device shocks are associated with an adverse prognosis in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators. This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model based on dynamic changes in intracardiac electrograms to assess the risk of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation (VF) events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).

METHODS: Experimental studies were conducted in pigs with HFrEF (N=8) to characterize intracardiac electrogram and surface ECG changes during HF decompensation. Sham-operated animals (N=6) were used as controls. In patients, the study used data from 2 independent cohorts of patients with ICDs. The first cohort included 5089 patients from 50 centers (199 218 tracings), leveraging electrical parameters associated with HFrEF decompensation in the experimental model to train and internally validate a dynamic convolutional neural network model for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/VF prediction. External validation was performed in a second cohort of 2040 patients from 7 centers (369 845 tracings).

RESULTS: In pigs, HFrEF decompensation was associated with QRS prolongation on surface ECG tracings and reduced bipolar R-wave amplitude in intracardiac electrograms. Hemodynamic and electrical alterations of HFrEF decompensation significantly increased the risk of inducible VF episodes compared with sham-operated controls (87.5% versus 0%, respectively; P<0.001). In a clinical setting, a convolutional neural network-derived model predicted first VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events by analyzing temporal patterns of R-wave amplitude, QRS duration, and premature ventricular complex burden. This approach yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.787 (0.753-0.817) for the training cohort and 0.725 (0.709-0.739) for the external validation cohort. Dynamic risk prediction using the convolutional neural network model significantly outperformed static risk assessment based on clinical variables (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.617 [0.602-0.632]).

CONCLUSIONS: A convolutional neural network-derived model, grounded in the pathophysiology of HFrEF, provides dynamic risk assessment of VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillator devices.

articles.title: An exploration of the roles of cognitive reactivity and ego depletion in the relationship between entrapment and suicidal ideation.
articles.journal: The British journal of clinical psychology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Entrapment is theorized as a key driver of suicidal ideation, yet the cognitive processes leading to entrapment, particularly the activating role of negative affect, and those through which entrapment translates into suicidal ideation are not well understood. Grounded in the Integrated Motivational-Volitional Model, this study used mediation analyses to examine cognitive reactivity in relation to suicidal ideation via entrapment, and ego depletion as a mediator of the entrapment-suicidal ideation link.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional online survey was used to collect self-report data from participants recruited through opportunity sampling.

METHODS: The sample consisted of 312 adults living in the United Kingdom. Data analyses were conducted on a subsample of participants who reported a lifetime history of suicidal ideation and/or suicide attempts (N = 269; Mage = 28.50, SD = 10.06; 82.9% White; 66.5% female).

RESULTS: The relationship between cognitive reactivity and suicidal ideation was accounted for by entrapment; this indirect association was not moderated by trait mindfulness. Additionally, the entrapment-suicidal ideation relationship was partially accounted for by self-regulatory fatigue, but not by depletion sensitivity; this indirect effect remained significant after controlling for depression, but not anxiety diagnosis.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight cognitive reactivity as a cognitive vulnerability to suicidal ideation and underscore the value of understanding suicide risk through the lens of self-regulation. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the observed associations should be interpreted as correlational in nature.

articles.title: Efficacy and feasibility of prehabilitation for cardiorespiratory functional capacity and respiratory muscle strength in cardiac surgery (PRECICA-I study).
articles.journal: Anales del sistema sanitario de Navarra
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the feasibility and efficacy of a short-term, face-to-face prehabilitation programme in patients awaiting elective cardiac surgery, focusing on cardiorespiratory functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, frailty, psychological distress, quality of life, and hospital length of stay.

METHODS: This single-blind randomised controlled trial included patients awaiting coronary, valvular, or aortic surgery. Participants were assigned to a prehabilitation group (two sessions per week of respiratory physiotherapy, strength training, and health education) or a control group (incentive spirometer). Functional capacity (6MWT), respiratory strength (MIP/MEP), frailty (SPPB), handgrip strength, quality of life (SF-12), physical activity (IPAQ), anxiety and depression (HADS) were assessed before the intervention and one week after discharge; hospital length of stay was also assessed.

RESULTS: Thirty-six patients (44% female; mean age 66.5 years) were included in the prehabilitation (n=24) and control (n=12) groups. Feasibility was high, with 92% adherence and no adverse events. Waist circumference, MIP, handgrip strength, and anxiety levels decreased significantly from pre-intervention to follow-up in both groups. In the control group, MEP also decreased significantly, while frailty increased. The only significant between-group difference was observed for MEP, with greater deterioration in the control group (Cohen's d=0.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term, face-to-face prehabilitation is feasible and may help mitigate the loss of expiratory muscle strength following elective cardiac surgery, although it does not improve functional capacity. Larger trials are needed to confirm its broader clinical benefits and to assess the impact of sex.

articles.title: Prescribing of High-Risk Medications for Older Adults with Rheumatic Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with rheumatic diseases often experience multi-morbidity and polypharmacy, potentially increasing their risk of adverse events from high-risk medications (HRMs).

OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the prevalence, characterize HRM prescriptions by prescriber characteristics, and identify patient-level factors associated with HRM prescribing among older adults with rheumatic diseases.

DESIGN: National cohort study using the American College of Rheumatology's Rheumatology Informatics System for Effectiveness (RISE) registry, linked to Medicare Parts A, B, and D.

SETTING: Electronic health record-based data from practices representing approximately one-third of U.S. rheumatologists.

PARTICIPANTS: Medicare-enrolled adults ≥65 years with ≥2 visits in 2021 at RISE participating practices and ≥2 ICD-10 codes for selected rheumatic diseases.

MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was prescription for a HRM. Logistic regression models were used to predict exposure to any HRM using generalized estimating equations to account for clustering of patients within practices.

RESULTS: Among 45,455 older adults (mean age 75.8±6.4 years; 76.9% female), 13,977 (30.7%) received ≥1 HRM. Prescriptions predominantly originated from non-rheumatology clinicians (82.3%). Common HRMs included skeletal muscle relaxants, first-generation antihistamines, antidepressants with strong anticholinergic activity, non-benzodiazepine benzodiazepine receptor agonist hypnotics ("Z-drugs"), and antispasmodics. In adjusted analyses, patients with axial spondyloarthritis (OR 1.40, 95%CI 1.20-1.62) and Sjögren's disease (OR 1.39, 95%CI 1.04-1.86) had the highest odds of receiving a HRM compared with rheumatoid arthritis.

CONCLUSIONS: High-risk medications are frequently prescribed to older adults with rheumatic diseases, exceeding the prevalence reported in the general Medicare population. These findings highlight the need for individualized medication review and enhanced cross-specialty collaboration when managing this population.

articles.title: Surgical and Cosmetic Outcomes After Fronto-Orbital Advancement With Hybrid Fixation for Unilateral Coronal Craniosynostosis: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fronto-orbital advancement (FOA) remains the standard surgical treatment for unilateral coronal craniosynostosis, particularly in patients presenting beyond the age window for endoscopic treatment and in those with significant frontal and orbital deformity. However, postoperative relapse, residual asymmetry, and fixation-related limitations remain important clinical concerns. Fixation strategies aim to provide immediate structural stability while minimizing potential interference with subsequent cranial growth.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate surgical, morphometric, cosmetic, and perioperative outcomes after FOA using a hybrid fixation strategy in patients with nonsyndromic unilateral coronal craniosynostosis.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 14 patients treated between January 2023 and December 2024 at the JSC National Center for Neurosurgery, Astana, Kazakhstan. All patients had CT-confirmed unilateral nonsyndromic coronal craniosynostosis and underwent primary FOA with combined fixation using biodegradable plates in key structural regions and absorbable sutures between individual remodeled bone fragments. Cosmetic outcomes were assessed using the Whitaker classification and clinician-rated Visual Analog Cosmetic Score (VACS), with each patient's VACS calculated as the mean of independent ratings from 10 assessors. Morphometric evaluation combined cephalic index (CI), as a measure of overall cranial width-to-length proportions, with frontal asymmetry index (FAI), orbital assessment, and nasal deviation angle (NDA). Perioperative safety outcomes and follow-up data were also analyzed.

RESULTS: The mean age at surgery was 16.7±12.9 months, and mean follow-up was 16 months (range 12-24). Favorable cosmetic outcomes were achieved in all patients: 92.9% were classified as Whitaker class I and 7.1% as class II, with no class III or IV outcomes or revision surgeries. Median postoperative VACS was 9.5 (range 6-10). FAI categories decreased in 10 of 14 patients (exact sign test, P=0.002; Holm-adjusted P=0.006). CI categories decreased in 6 patients (P=0.031; Holm-adjusted P=0.063), without establishing normalization of cranial shape. NDA categories showed no evidence of a directional change (P=0.625). All 14 patients received intraoperative autologous blood reinfusion and additional allogeneic blood transfusion. Mean total hospital stay was 18.9±3.5 days, including both preoperative and postoperative inpatient care. No major postoperative complications, cerebrospinal fluid leakage, surgical-site infection, relapse, or reoperation were observed.

CONCLUSION: Extended FOA with hybrid fixation was associated with favorable early cosmetic outcomes in this retrospective cohort. These findings describe the combined reconstructive procedure and do not establish the independent contribution of fixation, preservation of physiological cranial growth, or superiority over alternative fixation methods. Larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

articles.title: Skull Clamp-Related Frontal Sinus Fracture in a Patient With Polyostotic Fibrous Dysplasia: Complication and Management.
articles.abstract: Three-pin skull clamps provide head fixation, but skull fracture and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak are rare, reported complications. Fibrous dysplasia, which structurally weakens bone, may increase this risk. A 37-year-old man with polyostotic fibrous dysplasia and previous cranioplasty underwent prone posterior fossa decompression and cranial contouring. The anterior pin caused a crush injury with an open anterior table fracture of the frontal sinus; postoperative computed tomography also revealed a minimally displaced posterior table fracture, and rhinorrhea suggested CSF leak. At next-day reoperation, a minimal dural injury was found; after mucosal removal and nasofrontal duct occlusion, the dura and posterior table fracture were sealed with fascia lata, and the sinus was obliterated with a dermofat graft. The anterior table was refixed with plates and covered with titanium mesh, and a pedicled galeopericranial flap was interposed beneath the injured skin. At 3 months, there was no hardware exposure, infection, or rhinorrhea.

articles.title: Aerobic training after stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis of walking endurance, gait speed, and balance.
articles.journal: International journal of rehabilitation research. Internationale Zeitschrift fur Rehabilitationsforschung. Revue internationale de recherches de readaptation
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: We evaluated the effects of structured aerobic training on walking endurance, gait speed, and balance after stroke. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched (January 2000-19 May 2026). Randomized trials, nonrandomized controlled studies, and prospective single-group pre-post studies were eligible. Primary analyses pooled between-group effects from randomized trials; uncontrolled pre-post changes were analyzed separately. Risk of bias was assessed; evidence certainty was evaluated using GRADE. Random-effects models used restricted maximum-likelihood estimation; multilevel models accounted for within-study dependence. Mean differences were used for Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) and Berg Balance Scale (BBS) outcomes, and Hedges' g for gait speed. Nineteen studies were included. Aerobic training did not significantly improve 6MWT distance [nine studies; 688 participants; 13 estimates; mean difference = 9.64 m, 95% confidence interval (CI) = -1.85 to 21.13; P = 0.100; I2 = 0.0%] but significantly improved gait speed (five studies; 216 participants; 13 estimates; g = 0.454, 95% CI = 0.093 to 0.815; P = 0.014; I2 = 45.4%) versus control. Between-group BBS differences were nonsignificant (three studies; 297 participants; three estimates; mean difference = -0.10 points, 95% CI = -0.93 to 0.73; P = 0.817; I2 = 0.0%). Uncontrolled pre-post improvements in 6MWT distance and gait speed cannot be attributed solely to aerobic training. Certainty was low for walking endurance and gait speed and moderate for balance. Aerobic training may improve gait speed, but controlled comparisons did not demonstrate additional benefits for walking endurance or BBS-measured balance.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261454342.

articles.title: Beyond Continuation: Early Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Initiation After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overall sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) combines continuation and new initiation. We characterized these distinct prescribing processes and the clinical profiles accompanying initiation.

AIMS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center registry included 653 patients undergoing TAVI in 2022-2025. Exposure was assessed within 90 days before and 30 days after TAVI using discharge summaries and electronic medical records. The primary measure was initiation among previously untreated patients. Admission and wait-list N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) measurements were summarized separately.

RESULTS: Early medication status was known in 639 patients; 260 (40.7%) received SGLT2 inhibitors. Among 638 patients with paired records, 184 continued therapy, 76 initiated, eight did not continue, and 370 had no use in either window. Continuation occurred in 184/192 previously treated patients (95.8%), whereas initiation occurred in 76/446 previously untreated patients (17.0%; 95% confidence interval, 13.8-20.8). Initiation was 70/351 (19.9%) in a secondary subgroup with selected clinical risk features, without established trial eligibility. Admission NT-proBNP was available in 590 patients (90.4%); wait-list values were available in 356, including 349 with both assessments. Initiators had lower ejection fraction and higher admission NT-proBNP. Urinary tract infection explained four of eight non-continuations.

CONCLUSIONS: High continuation coexisted with limited new initiation. Transition-specific reporting clarifies early prescribing and supports individualized reassessment after TAVI, but does not establish treatment effects or the appropriateness of individual non-prescription decisions.

articles.title: Dental public health in action: A regional response to oral cancer in the South West of England.
articles.abstract: Head and neck cancer is an increasing public health concern in England, with incidence and mortality rates rising and variation by geography, age, sex and deprivation. Oral cancer forms part of this disease burden and shares modifiable risk factors including tobacco use, alcohol consumption and, for some tumour sites, human papillomavirus infection. The South West reflects these national concerns, with some areas experiencing oral cancer incidence rates above the national average. This paper presents an overview of a regional dental public health response to support prevention, earlier detection and system wide action on oral cancer in the South West of England. The work included development of intelligence tools such as oral cancer profiles, snapshot infographics, an evidence-informed regional oral cancer framework with accompanying action plan, a prevention focused webinar for dental and oral health improvement teams, and targeted oral cancer training for HPV vaccination teams. The intelligence tools, framework and action plan provided a structure for healthcare systems to assess oral cancer trends and inequalities, incorporate oral cancer within needs assessments and strategies, strengthen collaborative working with stakeholders, and improve professional awareness of oral cancer risk factors and referral routes for suspected lesions. Early process-based outcomes suggest engagement across dental, oral health improvement and vaccination workforces, with feedback indicating that participants valued content on patient communication, risk-factor reduction and signposting. Future work should focus on embedding oral cancer within local needs assessments, sustaining prevention activity addressing risk factors, and upskilling wider workforces to strengthen early detection.

articles.title: Effect of fascial plane blocks providing postoperative analgesia on mechanical ventilation duration in the ıntensive care unit and early oxygenation after cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The primary objective of this study was to examine whether a combined pecto-intercostal fascial plane block (PIFB) and serratus anterior plane block (SAPB) influences the duration of mechanical ventilation in patients who underwent open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy with cardiopulmonary bypass. Secondary objectives included evaluating the effects of this analgesic approach on early postoperative oxygenation parameters, pain intensity scores, and overall opioid consumption.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study enrolled 206 adult patients who underwent open cardiac surgery through median sternotomy between January and July 2025. Participants were allocated into two groups based on the postoperative analgesic strategy employed: the Block group (G1, N.=107), which received combined PIFB and SAPB, and the Control group (G0, N.=99), which was managed with conventional multimodal analgesia. To minimize selection bias, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was applied using seven clinical covariates. Mechanical ventilation duration was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox proportional hazards regression, and the restricted mean survival time (RMST) method.

RESULTS: Patients in the Block group demonstrated a significantly shorter median duration of mechanical ventilation compared to controls (300 vs. 420 min; RMST difference: -65.8 min; 95% CI: -94.2 to -41.6; P<0.001). The incidence of prolonged intubation, defined as mechanical ventilation exceeding 480 minutes, was markedly lower in the Block group (G1=6.5% vs. G0=20.2%; Firth OR: 0.29; 95% CI: 0.11-0.75; P=0.011). Postoperative pain scores were significantly reduced across all assessment time points in the Block group (Benjamini-Hochberg corrected q<0.001), and total opioid requirements declined by approximately 28% (IRR: 0.719; P<0.001). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected with respect to the PaO<inf>2</inf>/FiO<inf>2</inf> ratio or the length of intensive care unit stay. CONCLUSİONS: The combined application of PIFB and SAPB was associated with a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation and lower opioid consumption following cardiac surgery. Incorporating fascial plane blocks into multimodal analgesia protocols may confer meaningful clinical benefits, particularly in patients considered to be at elevated perioperative risk.

articles.title: Machine learning prediction of cyclosporine nephrotoxicity in pediatric patients using therapeutic drug monitoring and clinical data.
articles.journal: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cyclosporine A (CsA) nephrotoxicity is a dose-limiting toxicity in pediatric immunosuppression, and early identification of children at risk of CsA-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) remains an unmet clinical need.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In retrospective cohorts of CsA-treated inpatients undergoing therapeutic drug monitoring (352 children; 342 adults), a regularized logistic-regression model was compared with six machine-learning classifiers under five feature-selection schemes, three small-sample strategies were evaluated, and adult-child transferability was assessed on 95 aligned features. A 14-variable model was externally validated in an independent pediatric cohort (n = 257).

RESULTS: Regularized logistic regression achieved the best discrimination in children (hold-out AUC 0.800) and adults (hold-out AUC 0.956), with complex models overfitting. Adult and pediatric risk architectures differed fundamentally, with transfer AUCs near chance (≈0.6). The 14-variable model retained discrimination on external validation (AUC 0.784, 95% CI 0.656-0.912).

CONCLUSIONS: On small clinical datasets, regularization rather than complexity determines predictive performance. We provide an interpretable, TDM-integrated pediatric CsA-AKI model, deployed as an online calculator, supporting early risk stratification in pediatric CsA therapy.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes following balloon aortic valvuloplasty for congenital aortic stenosis in children: a 29-year single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Initial treatment of critical aortic stenosis in children, balloon or surgical aortic valvuloplasty, remains debated. Our centre used the balloon procedure first in almost all patients for over 29 years, a predominantly balloon-first cohort.

OBJECTIVE: To characterise long-term outcomes of balloon aortic valvuloplasty as first-line treatment for critical aortic stenosis.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 201 patients treated between June 1996 and December 2025, grouped as neonates (0-28 days), infants (29-365 days), and children (>365 days). Freedom from surgery and reintervention were analysed with the Kaplan-Meier method; categorical comparisons used chi-square tests.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 9 years. Aortic valve surgery was required in 78 patients (38.8%), most commonly a Ross or Ross-Konno procedure (49, 62.8%). Neonates required surgery more often than infants and children (36/74, 48.6% versus 42/127, 33.1%; p = 0.042); median time to surgery in neonates was 6 months. One-year Kaplan-Meier freedom from surgery was 63% in neonates, 91% in infants, and 96% in children. Moderate-to-severe post-procedural valve dysfunction was associated with more surgery than mild dysfunction (49.3% versus 33.3%; p = 0.041). Kaplan-Meier freedom from any reintervention was 47% at 10 years and 31% at 15 years. Mortality was 3.5% overall and 8.1% in neonates, mostly in the early era.

CONCLUSIONS: Balloon aortic valvuloplasty is an effective first-line treatment for infants and children with critical aortic stenosis. However, many neonates need surgery within the first year, usually a Ross procedure. In centres with experienced cardiac surgeons, surgical aortic valvuloplasty could be considered a reasonable alternative initial approach for neonates.

articles.title: Conceptual and psychometric characteristics of instruments used in adults with CHD quality of life research: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improved survival among people with congenital heart disease (CHD) has increased the emphasis on quality of life as a long-term outcome. However, inconsistent distinctions between quality of life, health-related quality of life, health status and functioning complicate the interpretation of this evidence. Examining the conceptual basis and measurement properties of instruments used in contemporary CHD research is therefore necessary to establish which outcomes are being assessed.

AIM: To identify instruments used in studies reporting quality of life outcomes in adults with moderate or severe CHD, classify their intended constructs and summarise reported evidence of validity, reliability and suitability.

METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance. CINAHL, MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for English-language quantitative and mixed-methods studies published from 2015 in high-income countries. Citation mining identified instrument development and validation literature. Instruments were classified by their primary intended purpose, and reported psychometric evidence and study definitions of quality of life were summarised descriptively.

RESULTS: Sixty-six records published between 2015 and 2026 identified 16 instruments. Five measured overall quality of life, eight assessed health-related quality of life, health status or functioning, and three were disease-specific. Studies using overall quality of life measures more commonly defined the construct, whereas those using short-form health surveys frequently reported quality of life without conceptual clarification. Validation evidence supported some instruments in adult CHD populations, although the suitability of measures developed for paediatric populations remained uncertain.

CONCLUSION: Contemporary CHD research reports conceptually distinct outcomes under the term quality of life, limiting comparability and interpretation. Explicit definitions and instrument selection informed by the intended construct and population are required to strengthen the assessment of patient-reported outcomes.

articles.title: Maternal obesity and risk of congenital heart disease in offspring: a nationwide population-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity is a well-established risk factor for adverse pregnancy outcomes, but its association with congenital heart disease (CHD) in offspring remains uncertain, particularly across different body mass index (BMI) categories and CHD subtypes. Evidence from Asian populations is limited, despite distinct BMI distributions and classification criteria. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using the Korean National Health Information Database, including 779,091 live births from 2014 to 2021. Maternal pre-pregnancy BMI was classified according to Asia-Pacific criteria. Offspring CHD was identified using ICD-10 codes Q20-Q26. Subtype analyses were performed for ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect (ASD), pulmonary valve stenosis, and other major CHD subtypes. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance covariates across BMI categories, and robust Poisson regression was used to estimate RRs and 95% CIs. Compared with the normal BMI group (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), adjusted RRs for CHD were 1.08 (95% CI 1.06-1.10) for overweight at risk (23.0-24.9 kg/m2), 1.13 (95% CI 1.11-1.15) for obese class I (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), and 1.37 (95% CI 1.35-1.40) for obese class II (≥30.0 kg/m2). Maternal underweight (<18.5 kg/m2) was not significantly associated with CHD risk (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97-1.00). Maternal obesity was associated with a dose-dependent increase in overall CHD risk, while subtype associations were not significant after adjustment. These findings support public health strategies emphasizing weight management before conception to reduce the burden of congenital heart anomalies.

articles.title: Effects of specialised and centralised versus generalised and decentralised outpatient treatment for progressed bipolar disorder: Results from the CAG Bipolar randomised controlled trial.
authors: in cooperation with the CAG Bipolar Study Group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical Academic Group (CAG) is a new organization of treatment bringing together clinical services, research, education, and training to provide evidence-based care. We aimed, for the first time, to investigate whether specialized and centralized outpatient treatment (CAG Bipolar) versus decentralized community-based treatment improves patient outcomes and satisfaction with care in patients with progressed bipolar disorder.

METHODS: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial was undertaken with individual randomization to 1) specialized and centralized outpatient treatment in CAG Bipolar or 2) generalized and decentralized community-based outpatient treatment. The 12-month outcomes were 1) cumulated number and duration of psychiatric hospitalizations, and 2) psychotropic medication, coercion, self-rated depressive and manic symptoms, quality of life, perceived stress, and satisfaction with care.

RESULTS: There was no difference among 1,134 included patients in cumulated number (RR: 0.94 (95% CI: 0.74-1.14), p = 0.6) or duration (0.16 days, (95% CI: -4.10-4.42; p = 0.9) of psychiatric hospitalizations. Lithium (RR: 1.19 (95% CI: 1.05-1.33) and antipsychotics (RR: 1.09 (95% CI: 1.01-1.17), specifically quetiapine (RR: 1.17 (95% CI: 1.03-1.30), were prescribed more in the CAG Bipolar group, and CAG Bipolar patients were overall more satisfied with care including the skills of the professionals, information and the efficacy of the service. There was no difference in coercion, self-rated depressive or manic symptoms, quality of life or perceived stress.

CONCLUSIONS: Specialized and centralized outpatient treatment for progressed bipolar disorder does not result in improvement in robust outcome measures such as hospitalization and coercion, but in the use of psychotropic medication concordant with international guidelines, and increased satisfaction with care.

articles.title: Feasibility and Usability of Self-Collected Blood Samples for Studies of Norovirus and Acute Gastroenteritis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tasso self-collection blood kits have been validated against venous blood-derived serum samples, but not for studies of acute gastroenteritis (AGE). The authors' objectives were to describe the performance of the Tasso+ for self-collection of blood samples among adults and children enrolled in a study of medically attended AGE and to describe specimen processing and antibody testing success.

METHODS: The authors used the Tasso+ device for self-collection of blood samples within a prospective cohort study at Kaiser Permanente Northwest. Serum samples were assessed for the presence of antibodies against the norovirus capsid protein.

RESULTS: Of a total of 1353 adults and 93 children, 63% of adults and 61% of children returned a blood specimen. Of these, 88% were deemed viable for processing, and 100% of viable specimens were of sufficient volume and quality to be processed and assessed for norovirus antibodies.

CONCLUSIONS: The results suggested that Tasso+ is a feasible blood collection tool for studies of AGE and can contribute to the authors' understanding of immune response after natural infection and potentially help identify correlates of protection against severe norovirus disease.

articles.title: Natural Products Targeting Metabolic Disorders in Diabetic Kidney Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives.
articles.journal: The American journal of Chinese medicine
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major microvascular complication of diabetes. Although the emergence of new therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, aldosterone receptor antagonists, and endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs) has expanded the therapeutic options for DKD, these therapies remain insufficient to meet the urgent clinical needs of contemporary society. Recent studies indicate that the pathogenesis of DKD involves multiple signaling pathways and drug targets. DKD is closely linked to the dysregulation of glucose, lipid, and amino acid metabolism. Compared to synthetic drugs, natural products offer advantages such as broader biological activities, favorable drug-like potential, multi-target mechanisms of action, enhanced safety and tolerability profiles, as well as abundant and renewable sources. Over the past two decades, natural products have demonstrated considerable potential in preclinical DKD studies (triptolide, quercetin, berberine, baicalin, resveratrol, proanthocyanidin B2), and various natural compounds are now considered integral components of comprehensive DKD management strategies, despite their disadvantages of poor solubility and low bioavailability. This review focuses on the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which natural products alleviate DKD by targeting metabolic disorders, summarizes the contributions of nanodelivery systems in improving the bioavailability of natural products, and presents related challenges in clinical translation, aiming to provide new insights for DKD treatment.

articles.title: A Pilot Investigation of Endocannabinoid System Markers and Lipopolysaccharide Responses to 10 Sessions of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) can modulate inflammatory and redox-sensitive pathways, but its effects on endocannabinoid system markers remain unclear. This exploratory biomarker subanalysis of a randomized controlled parent trial evaluated whether repeated HBOT was associated with changes in serum anandamide (AEA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) as primary outcomes. Cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2R), fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), and the baseline AEA-LPS association were assessed secondarily or exploratorily. MATERIAL AND METHODS The resource-limited, post-randomization sample included 17 healthy, physically active men: 9 from a pre-existing morning scheduling subgroup of the frequent-treatment HBOT arm and 8 controls selected before biomarker assays to improve baseline body mass index (BMI) comparability. HBOT consisted of 10 sessions performed 6 times weekly. Each session involved 60 minutes of 100% oxygen at 2.5 atmospheres absolute, delivered as three 20-min oxygen-breathing periods separated by two 5-minute air breaks. Fasting serum was collected before and after the protocol, and biomarkers were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays. RESULTS No significant between-group differences in change scores were found for AEA (p = 0.597), CB2R (p=1.000), FAAH (p=0.885), or LPS (p=0.885). No significant within-group changes occurred in the HBOT group. Baseline AEA was positively associated with baseline LPS (Spearman's rho=0.505, p=0.039). CONCLUSIONS Receiving 10 HBOT sessions were not associated with significant changes in the measured circulating biomarkers. These exploratory findings do not exclude smaller effects, and the baseline AEA-LPS association requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

articles.title: Culture-Negative Neutrophilic Meningitis Followed by Suboccipital Abscess and Sepsis: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Aseptic meningitis is a relatively common disease but is extremely rarely complicated by a suboccipital abscess. This report describes and discusses a rare case of a patient with culture-negative pleocytosis suggestive of bacterial infection, followed by suboccipital abscess and sepsis. CASE REPORT The patient was a 65-year-old woman who developed a throbbing, holocranial headache that was initially interpreted as a tension-type headache. After signs of meningismus later developed, she was diagnosed with aseptic bacterial meningitis based on a cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cell count of 15 127 cells/µL, primarily granulocytes containing bacteria-like structures. However, blood, urine, and CSF cultures were negative. Using empirical antibiotic therapy, the patient achieved near complete recovery before discharge. More than a month after this episode, the patient developed a suboccipital abscess complicated by sepsis, necessitating repeated surgical interventions and adjustments to antibiotic therapy. Observations from this case are applicable to patients with strong CSF and clinical indicators of bacterial infection despite negative routine cultures, especially when subsequent deep soft-tissue infection or sepsis emerges. Recurrent headaches or neck pain after initial improvement should prompt reassessment for a deep extracranial infectious complication. CONCLUSIONS This case suggests that a presentation initially classified as aseptic meningitis may actually be a culture-negative infection and can be followed by deep soft-tissue abscess formation and sepsis. It also demonstrates that the precise pathogen and source of infection may remain unconfirmed but that empirical antibiotic therapy can be beneficial.

articles.title: Rheumatoid meningitis presenting with gait disturbance and urinary symptoms in a patient without a prior diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid meningitis (RM) is a rare central nervous system manifestation of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) that may occur without overt arthritis. A 77-year-old woman with no prior diagnosis of RA presented with progressive gait disturbance, dizziness, vomiting, and urinary incontinence. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed diffuse pachymeningeal thickening with leptomeningeal enhancement predominantly along the parasagittal frontal sulci. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed 4 white blood cells/μL and mildly elevated protein and detectable anti- cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibody; serum rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibody levels were markedly elevated. Probable RM was diagnosed after infection and malignancy were excluded, and symptoms and MRI findings improved after corticosteroid pulse therapy. After methotrexate was initiated during steroid tapering, the patient developed headache, fever, and neutrophil-predominant CSF pleocytosis. Infection, RM flare, and methotrexate-induced aseptic meningitis were considered. Methotrexate was discontinued and empirical antibiotics were administered, and the pleocytosis resolved rapidly; its cause remained uncertain. Subsequent rituximab treatment was associated with improved gait, allowing ambulation with a walker, together with further reduction of pachymeningeal enhancement. This case illustrates that RM should be considered in unexplained pachymeningitis and may respond to stepwise immunotherapy.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Cardiac Auscultation for Detecting Clinically Significant Valvular Heart Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Early identification of clinically significant valvular heart disease (VHD) remains challenging because echocardiography is resource-intensive and conventional auscultation is operator-dependent. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled analysis of digital heart sounds has emerged as a promising screening strategy, but its overall diagnostic performance has not been systematically evaluated. We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy studies-compliant systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of studies evaluating AI-enabled cardiac auscultation against transthoracic echocardiography for detecting clinically significant VHD, defined according to each study's echocardiographic criteria. MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched through July 2026, and pooled sensitivity, specificity, summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve, diagnostic odds ratio, and accuracy were estimated using random-effects models. Eight studies comprising 4374 analyzed participants were included. AI-enabled cardiac auscultation demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 72% (95% CI 54-85%) and specificity of 82% (95% CI 74-88%) for detecting clinically significant VHD. The summary receiver operating characteristic area under the curve was 0.814 (95% CI 0.569-0.888), and the pooled diagnostic odds ratio was 11.39 (95% CI 3.76-34.47), corresponding to positive and negative likelihood ratios of approximately 4.0 and 0.34, respectively. Overall pooled diagnostic accuracy was 78% (95% CI 67-86%). Subgroup analyses demonstrated substantially higher sensitivity for studies evaluating isolated aortic stenosis than composite VHD (92% vs. 55%; P < 0.001), whereas specificity was comparable. AI-enabled cardiac auscultation demonstrates promising diagnostic performance for identifying clinically significant VHD and may serve as a front-line screening tool to prioritize patients for echocardiography. Future prospective multicenter studies using standardized recording protocols and external validation are needed before widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors in Heart Transplant Recipients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart transplant (HT) recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) face elevated risks of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV), rejection, and cardiovascular events. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) confer cardiorenal protection in general T2DM patients, but data specific to HT recipients are scarce.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adult HT recipients with T2DM who initiated a GLP-1 RA or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor after transplantation between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2025, were matched 1:1 on 36 covariates. The primary outcome was a 3-year graft-specific composite of CAV (T86.290), HT rejection (T86.21), or HT failure (T86.22). All-cause mortality and myocardial infarction (I21) or ischemic stroke (I63) were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: After matching, 712 patients per group were analyzed. At 3 y, the graft-specific composite occurred in 12.1% of GLP-1 RA recipients versus 29.2% of DPP-4 inhibitor recipients (risk ratio [RR] 0.416; 95% confidence interval, 0.299-0.579; P < 0.001), driven by lower HT rejection (8.2% versus 22.4%; RR 0.365) and HT failure (3.5% versus 6.2%; RR 0.560); CAV did not differ (9.6% versus 10.5%; P = 0.609). All-cause mortality was 7.5% versus 17.5% (RR 0.426), and myocardial infarction/ischemic stroke 6.9% versus 15.3% (RR 0.450). Acute kidney injury and gastrointestinal adverse events did not differ. Findings were consistent at 1 and 5 y. Residual imbalance persisted for body mass index and HbA1c.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter electronic health record-based cohort, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower graft-specific outcomes and all-cause mortality than DPP-4 inhibitor use. CAV did not differ significantly. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

articles.title: Prolonged Dual Antiplatelet Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Ischemic and Bleeding Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Continued dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains controversial because continuing DAPT may reduce ischemic events while increasing bleeding compared with a transition to single-antiplatelet therapy (SAPT). We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing continued DAPT with SAPT in adults who had received an initial 1-12-month course of DAPT after PCI. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane were searched through August 2026. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with prespecified subgroup analyses according to preceding DAPT duration and SAPT regimen. Eleven randomized controlled trials comprising 52,105 randomized participants were included, with 26,070 assigned to continued DAPT and 26,035 to SAPT. Continued DAPT significantly increased all bleeding (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.34-2.40), major bleeding (RR 1.75, 95% CI 1.20-2.56), and net adverse clinical events (RR 1.30, 95% CI 1.05-1.61). No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, major adverse cardiovascular events, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, stroke, revascularization, or stent thrombosis. The association between continued DAPT and bleeding differed according to the SAPT comparator, although these analyses did not directly compare aspirin with P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy. Overall, continued DAPT was associated with increased bleeding without demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in individual ischemic outcomes, supporting individualized antiplatelet strategies based on ischemic and bleeding risk.

articles.title: Short-term outcomes and follow-up of NICU graduates in selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonatal health during the post-discharge period is critical, especially for infants discharged from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), who are at higher risk of complications and long-term developmental issues. In Sri Lanka, there are limited data on post-NICU follow-up, highlighting the need for research. This study aimed to evaluate the post-discharge follow-up status of neonates admitted to selected NICUs in Galle, Sri Lanka.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted between January 2025 and June 2025 in the NICUs of National Hospital Galle (NHG) and German-Sri Lanka Friendship Hospital for Women (GSLFHW). Neonates admitted within 28 days of birth who were discharged home or transferred to other wards were included; those who died before discharge or were transferred to another NICU or another hospital were excluded. A purposive sampling method was used. Follow-up assessments were conducted one week and one month after discharge. Data were collected using a structured guide on feeding status, feeding issues, medical problems, pharmacological management, follow-up visits, and developmental milestones. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26, and descriptive statistics were presented as numbers and percentages.

RESULTS: Respiratory distress was the most common reason for NICU admission (74.4%, n = 96). At discharge, 97.7% were breastfed, and most achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones: cognitive (92.2%, n = 119), motor (96.1%, n = 124), psychosocial (95.3%, n = 123), and communication (93.0%, n = 120). One week post-discharge, 94.4% were breastfed; feeding issues included poor sucking (12.7%, n = 16) and vomiting (6.3%, n = 8). Most infants met developmental milestones. One month post-discharge, 81.8% were breastfed, 10.9% were readmitted for complications, including infections, and the mean weight increased to 3.26 kg. Nearly all (99.1%) achieved age-appropriate developmental milestones by one month.

CONCLUSION: Most neonates showed favorable early post‑discharge status at one week and one month, with high rates of breastfeeding and attainment of age‑expected developmental milestones at these time points. While breastfeeding remained predominant, some experienced feeding difficulties and a small proportion required readmission or died. These findings describe very early outcomes only; continued and longer‑term follow‑up is essential to manage complications and support health outcomes beyond the first month.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: An Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating the Effect of Oil Massage on Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia in Stable Preterm Babies Admitted to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To study the effect of oil massage on duration of phototherapy in preterm neonates with hyperbilirubinemia.

METHODS: In this open-label randomized controlled trial, the authors included hemodynamically stable preterm neonates born at less than 37 wk of gestation. They were randomized to either of the two groups: One group received phototherapy alone, while the other received phototherapy plus oil massage. In the latter group, massage was administered twice daily for 15 min. The primary outcome (phototherapy duration) was compared between groups using an independent t-test. Secondary outcomes, including daily and cumulative stool frequency, were analysed using independent t-tests for each time point. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen's d. All tests were two-tailed, and p-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The intervention group (oil massage + phototherapy) required an average of 7.73 h (approximately 7.6%) less phototherapy compared to the control group, which is statistically significant (p-value 0.0118).

CONCLUSIONS: Oil massage, as an additive regimen to phototherapy, helps in reducing the duration of phototherapy in preterm infants with hyperbilirubinemia.

articles.title: ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI PET/CT in cardiac Anderson-Fabry disease: novel insights into disease assessment from a case series.
articles.abstract: Anderson-Fabry disease (AFD) is an X-linked lysosomal disorder in which cardiac involvement is the main cause of morbidity and mortality, manifesting as left ventricular hypertrophy, heart failure, arrhythmias, and myocardial fibrosis. Myocardial fibrosis is a key pathophysiological process associated with an adverse prognosis. While cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) identifies established myocardial fibrosis, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables the molecular assessment of FAP-associated activity. By complementing conventional CMR parameters, including late gadolinium enhancement and native T1 mapping, FAPI PET may improve the characterization and phenotypic classification of cardiac involvement in Anderson-Fabry disease. We report three cases of AFD patients, who underwent Gallium-68-fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (⁶⁸Ga-FAPI) PET-CT as part of a prospective study designed to assess myocardial fibrosis. Overall, ⁶⁸Ga-FAPI uptake closely correlated with CMR findings, reinforcing the role of cardiac fibroblast activation as a relevant pathogenic mechanism in AFD. These findings highlight this new molecular imaging as a promising tool for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic guidance in AFD.

articles.title: When the Dust Settles: Superpulsed Thulium Fiber Laser Versus MOSES Ho: YAG in Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery-A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Superpulsed thulium fiber laser (sTFL) and Lumenis MOSES pulse-modulated holmium: yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Ho: YAG) represent contemporary standards for retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS), operating through distinct photothermal and pulse-shape modulation mechanisms. Previous meta-analyses comparing these modalities have yielded conflicting conclusions largely due to pooling heterogeneous, non-modulated Ho: YAG generations and diverse surgical procedures. This study aims to systematically review and meta-analyze existing evidence evaluating sTFL exclusively against MOSES Ho: YAG regarding stone-free rates, operative efficiency, and safety in adults undergoing RIRS for stones ≤ 20 mm.

RECENT FINDINGS: Of 1,290 records identified across five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Europe PMC) through August 2026 (PROSPERO: CRD420261492557), 7 studies (3 randomized controlled trials and 4 comparative cohorts; 1,278 matched patients) met the inclusion criteria for the systematic review and meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed that the sTFL cohort demonstrated a significantly superior absolute 0-mm stone-free rate compared to MOSES Ho: YAG (pooled RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.02-1.17, p = 0.014, I²=0.0%). However, clinically insignificant residual fragment (CIRF, ≤ 2-4 mm) rates were statistically equivalent between modalities both overall (pooled RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.93-1.21, I²=87.1%) and following the resolution of registry-driven heterogeneity (pooled RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.96-1.08, p = 0.59, I²=29.2%). Operative and lasing times were comparable between platforms. Both lasers exhibited equivalent overall complications (pooled RR 1.44, 95% CI 0.92-2.26) and severe adverse events (Clavien-Dindo ≥ III: RD 0.01, 95% CI - 0.00 to 0.02). Subgroup analyses revealed that elevated complication rates with sTFL were isolated to non-randomized, pure intrarenal cohorts (pooled RR 1.83, 95% CI 1.30-2.57) and follow-up ≥ 3 months (pooled RR 1.84, 95% CI 1.30-2.61), reflecting procedural confounders-such as ureteral access sheath underutilization-rather than inherent laser physics. Most studies were rated as having a high or serious risk of bias, primarily because of confounding and outcome measurement concerns. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings. This systematic review highlights that while sTFL achieves superior absolute stone clearance (0 mm), both sTFL and MOSES Ho: YAG yield equivalent CIRF rates, operative efficiency, and safety profiles under standardized operative conditions. Relying on institutional availability and enforcing strict intrarenal pressure management may be valuable strategies for guiding clinical laser application.

articles.title: Bacterial chemosensory systems: from molecular signaling diversity to context-dependent function and engineering.
articles.abstract: Bacterial chemosensory systems conserve receptor-kinase architectures yet direct distinct outputs, from flagellar navigation and type IV pilus-driven surface migration to Wsp-like control of cellular states. The unresolved question is when these responses improve ecological performance in heterogeneous environments. We integrate molecular, cellular, and ecological evidence from plant-associated, marine, and host-associated bacteria through a framework that distinguishes demonstrated endpoints, causal resolution, and environmental realism. Studies of receptor-mediated root colonization, pilus steering, marine dissolved organic matter recruitment, and intestinal infection show that stronger sensing or directional movement does not invariably improve functional outcomes. We propose a context-matched coupling model in which environmental cue persistence and accessibility interact with sensory response and adaptation dynamics, the mode of cellular output, and downstream physiological capacity to determine the functional value of chemosensing. The model predicts that the relative performance of cells with different adaptation kinetics can reverse as gradient persistence changes; that increased receptor-array gain yields diminishing returns when physical constraints limit movement; and that receptor modification in Wsp-like pathways may filter stimulus duration or repetition to regulate cellular-state commitment. These predictions define experiments for identifying which signaling or output components limit performance under different environmental conditions. In engineering, the framework prioritizes matching receptors, signal-processing dynamics, and effectors to the intended functional endpoint over maximizing binding affinity or pathway activation alone. Together, these analyses connect chemosensory diversity to testable mechanisms of ecological performance and principles for rational engineering.

articles.title: Cancer Survivorship in Eastern Europe: Evolving Oncology Care Beyond Treatment.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This narrative review examines how selected cancer rehabilitation approaches are being integrated into survivorship care across Eastern and Central Europe. It focuses on rehabilitation as a practical indicator of whether oncology care is evolving beyond treatment, while acknowledging that comprehensive survivorship care encompasses additional domains.

RECENT FINDINGS: The literature discussed includes supervised and home-based exercise, lymphedema care, cardio-oncology rehabilitation, telerehabilitation, virtual and game-based interventions, and early implementation models. Breast cancer and selected adult long-term survivor populations are most extensively represented, particularly in reports from Poland, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia. Study designs and clinical settings vary, limiting conclusions about implementation across the region. The reviewed studies and practice reports suggest growing attention to cancer rehabilitation, but integration into survivorship pathways remains uneven. Referral processes, workforce roles, care coordination, and participation outcomes warrant further evaluation. Rehabilitation offers a practical entry point for strengthening patient-centered survivorship care, alongside other rehabilitation domains that are not examined in depth in this review.

articles.title: Addressing Disparities in Hypertension Control: The Potential Role of New Drugs and Devices in 2026 and Beyond.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Hypertension is the leading modifiable cardiovascular risk factor in the United States, with racially/ethnically diverse populations experiencing a disproportionate burden, associated with social, structural, and potentially biological determinants. This review examines how recently approved and investigational pharmacologic therapies and device-based interventions may advance hypertension control in 2026 and beyond, with deliberate attention to the strength and applicability of the available evidence in racially/ ethnically diverse populations.

RECENT FINDINGS: Aldosterone synthesis and mineralocorticoid receptor signaling represent important advances beyond the present guidelines for resistant hypertension and cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk reduction. For instance, baxdrostat, a recently approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI), has demonstrated clinically meaningful blood pressure reductions. In addition, lorundrostat, an investigational ASI, provides a model for racially representative trial design through the intentional enrollment of Black and Hispanic/Latino participants and consistent efficacy across racial subgroups. In contrast, pivotal finerenone trials demonstrated improved cardiac and renal outcomes but included limited representation of Black adults. Additional approved therapies include an agent targeting the endothelin pathway, aprocitentan, and device-based interventions via renal denervation therapy, although their effectiveness in diverse populations remains unknown. Therapies targeting natriuretic peptide signaling remain investigational but could potentially expand the therapeutic landscape. Advances in antihypertensive therapy offer new opportunities to improve blood pressure control and reduce cardiovascular risk beyond the 2025 American Heart Association (AHA) and American College of Cardiology (ACC) AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline-directed approach. Ensuring equitable benefit from these innovations requires that therapeutic innovation be coupled with deliberate efforts to ensure equitable delivery and benefit across populations.

articles.title: Label-free tracking of metal-organic framework nanoparticles by light-sheet light scattering imaging.
articles.abstract: The development of a light-sheet light scattering imaging (LSI) method for label-free dark-field imaging and analysis of metal-organic framework nanoparticles (MOF NPs) with and without doped quantum dots (QDs) is demonstrated. Using standard polystyrene beads, our method demonstrates a minimal NP diameter that can be determined by our method of 41 nm, with relative standard deviations (RSDs) below 3% for the modal diameters, and a minimal NP concentration for stable operation of 107 particles/mL for quantitative particle sizing. When applied to MOF NPs, the method revealed differences in hydrodynamic size distributions between MOF NPs with and without doped QDs through label-free single-particle analysis in suspension, where the DCA formulation shows better size control for QD-doped MOF NPs than the formic acid (FA) formulations. The modal diameters obtained by light-sheet LSI agree with transmission electron microscopy (TEM) results. Directly calculated statistics further characterized the spread and asymmetry of the measured size distributions. Our light-sheet LSI method enables sensitive, label-free single-NP characterization in liquid-phase analysis and acts as a useful complement to TEM and dynamic light scattering (DLS).

articles.title: Embolic stroke and breakthrough thrombosis on direct oral anticoagulants in Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
articles.abstract: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a characteristic cardiac manifestation of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), but its presentation and management in the era of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are poorly characterised. We describe a 37-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and recurrent unprovoked deep vein thrombosis who developed multiple embolic strokes while taking rivaroxaban. Transoesophageal echocardiography showed a sessile aortic valve mass; repeated blood cultures and 18F-FDG PET-CT were negative, and lupus anticoagulant was the only antiphospholipid antibody detected (probable APS). He was switched to low-molecular-weight heparin and acenocoumarol and the mass was excised; histology showed an organised fibrinous thrombotic vegetation, although papillary fibroelastoma could not be fully excluded. Following the CABARET recommendations, we searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and DOAJ for reports published between January 2020 and September 2026 and included 62 case reports/series (63 patients) and four cohort studies. Median age was 40 years (range 19-78); 22/60 patients (37%) were men; 34/63 (54%) had primary APS and 6 (10%) catastrophic APS. When reported, the antibody profile was triple-positive in 22/39 (56%) and lupus-anticoagulant-only in 4/39 (10%). The mitral valve was involved in 41/62 (66%), the aortic in 19/62 (31%) and the tricuspid in 7/62 (11%). Ischaemic stroke occurred in 29/63 (46%) and heart failure or severe valve dysfunction in 31/63 (49%). Of 16 patients anticoagulated at diagnosis, 10 (63%) were receiving a DOAC. Valve intervention was performed in 35/63 (56%) and 4/63 (6%) died. LSE should be sought in patients with APS who have embolic events, particularly while on DOACs; the evidence remains observational.

articles.title: Patient-reported outcomes after robot-assisted versus open pancreatoduodenectomy: a systematic review and narrative synthesis.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) is increasingly used, but its effect on patient-reported outcomes (PROs) compared with open pancreatoduodenectomy (OPD) remains uncertain. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 13 September 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults undergoing pancreatoduodenectomy, compared RPD or minimally invasive surgery with OPD, and reported validated PROs, symptoms, functional recovery, or satisfaction. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and MOOSE; AMSTAR 2 was used for self-appraisal. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and GRADE. Heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis; findings were synthesised by outcome and follow-up time. We identified 398 records; 308 remained after deduplication, and 22 reports from 21 studies were included. In high-volume trials, RPD was associated with faster functional recovery in DIPLOMA-2 (7 vs. 8 days) and PORTAL (12.1 vs. 16.0 days). Validated PROs showed no consistent advantage. In DIPLOMA-2, 6-month health utility was lower with RPD (difference - 0.08, 95% CI - 0.15 to - 0.001), and the quality-adjusted life-year difference was - 0.02 (95% CI - 0.07 to 0.01). Complications, especially pancreatic fistula and delayed gastric emptying, were consistently associated with worse symptom recovery. Survivors reported acceptable quality of life, but enzyme replacement, diabetes, and nutrition remained problematic. In high-volume trial settings, RPD was associated with faster short-term recovery but has not shown a consistent PRO advantage over OPD. Future trials should use validated PROs as primary or co-primary endpoints.Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261506534; last modified 28 September 2026.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine-associated bradycardia in perioperative and critical care settings: a cross-database pharmacovigilance study using FAERS and JADER.
