articles.abstract: Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is a highly selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist widely used for sedation in perioperative and critical care settings. Although bradycardia is a recognised adverse effect, its temporal reporting patterns and associated clinical characteristics remain incompletely characterised. This study investigated DEX-associated bradycardia using two independent spontaneous reporting systems. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER) database from 2004Q1 to 2025Q3. Reports suggestive of perioperative or critical care use were identified using predefined proxy indicators. Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect cardiovascular safety signals. Time to onset (TTO) patterns were evaluated using Weibull modelling, and factors associated with bradycardia reporting were examined using multivariable case-non-case logistic regression. Sensitivity analyses assessed the consistency of the findings. Among 2505 DEX reports, 717 involved bradycardia-associated events (FAERS, n = 327; JADER, n = 390). Bradycardia showed prominent disproportionality signals in both databases. Among 198 reports with valid TTO data, the median onset time was 0 days in both databases, with similar Weibull shape parameters (FAERS, β = 0.849; JADER, β = 0.847), suggesting early clustering of reported events. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease showed the strongest adjusted association with bradycardia reporting (OR 4.88, 95% CI 3.92-6.09), followed by concomitant opioid use (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.37-2.22) and β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure (OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.08-3.13). These associations were generally consistent across sensitivity analyses. DEX-associated bradycardia showed consistent reporting signals across FAERS and JADER, with reported onset times frequently concentrated near treatment initiation. Cardiovascular disease and concomitant opioid or β-adrenoceptor blocker exposure were associated with higher odds of bradycardia reporting. Although spontaneous reporting data cannot establish causality or quantify incidence, these findings provide complementary post-marketing evidence supporting careful cardiovascular assessment and haemodynamic monitoring during DEX administration.

articles.title: Association between preoperative omega-3/vitamin E supplementation and tissue inflammatory and redox biomarkers in persistent apical periodontitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether preoperative supplementation with an omega-3/vitamin E-containing formulation was associated with differences in the tissue inflammatory and redox biomarker profile of persistent asymptomatic periapical lesions requiring endodontic microsurgery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective non-randomized controlled clinical study included adult patients with persistent asymptomatic post-treatment apical periodontitis in previously treated teeth requiring endodontic microsurgery. Participants were allocated to a control group or to a supplementation group receiving omega-3/vitamin E for 40 days before surgery. Periapical lesion tissues were collected during surgery, and laboratory analyses were performed with laboratory personnel blinded to group allocation. Tissue extracts were analysed for inflammatory cytokines, matrix-related biomarkers, and oxidative stress markers. Sixteen participants were included in the final per-protocol analysis (n = 8 per group).

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the omega-3/vitamin E group showed significantly lower tissue levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 and TNF-α. The supplemented group also exhibited significantly lower levels of MMP-2, VEGF-A and TBARS, together with significantly higher levels of IFN-γ, IL-13 and PDGF-AB/BB. No significant differences between-group were observed for IL-1β, IL-4, IL-10, IL-17 A, MCP-1, MMP-9, or protein carbonyl levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative omega-3/vitamin E supplementation was associated with a distinct molecular profile characterized by reduced inflammatory and oxidative stress markers and selective changes in immunoregulatory mediators. These findings suggest modulation of the lesional microenvironment but should be interpreted as exploratory.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Host-modulatory strategies such as omega-3/vitamin E supplementation may influence the local biological profile of persistent apical lesions, although their clinical impact remains to be determined.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry - ReBEC, under registration number RBR-9mjf86. ( https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-9mjfj86 ).

articles.title: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children (≤ 3 years): A systematic review.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Decompressive surgery in infants and very young children presents unique challenges related to cranial development, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) disturbances, and subsequent reconstruction. This systematic review evaluated the indications, operative techniques, postoperative complications, and outcomes of conventional decompressive craniectomy and bone-preserving expansile procedures in children aged ≤ 3 years.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for English-language clinical studies involving age-eligible children. Study characteristics, operative details, complications, and outcomes were extracted and synthesized descriptively. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. Meta-analysis was not undertaken because of clinical and methodological heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Of the 1970 identified records, 46 publications were included, predominantly case reports and small case series. Indications included traumatic brain injury, cerebrovascular events, hemorrhage, and other causes of severe cerebral swelling. Procedures comprised conventional bone-out decompression and various bone-preserving techniques. Hydrocephalus, subdural and extracranial fluid collections, CSF leakage, wound complications, and bone-related morbidity were reported. Conventional decompression introduced subsequent reconstruction requirements and potential bone-resorption complications. Bone-preserving approaches maintained native cranial bone but were not free of CSF-related complications, altered bone fusion, or later reconstructive procedures. Inconsistent outcome definitions, age-specific denominators, and follow-up prevented reliable comparative estimates.

CONCLUSION: Evidence on decompressive surgery in children aged ≤ 3 years remains limited by small, heterogeneous studies and inconsistent outcome reporting. Although both conventional and bone-preserving techniques are feasible, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. CSF-related complications and reconstructive morbidity warrant particular attention. Standardized complication reporting and long-term assessment of cranial growth and neurodevelopment are essential to guide surgical decision-making.

articles.title: Fresh frozen plasma administration during cardiopulmonary bypass was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements after elective total aortic arch replacement: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) during total aortic arch replacement (TAR) is associated with coagulopathy. We investigated whether fresh frozen plasma (FFP) administration during CPB was associated with postoperative transfusion requirements and coagulation profiles after TAR.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients who underwent elective TAR. Patients were categorized according to whether FFP was administered during CPB. The primary outcome was postoperative FFP transfusion from CPB separation to 12 h after intensive care unit admission. Secondary outcomes included perioperative plasma-derived product use, postoperative bleeding, re-exploration for bleeding, and serial coagulation parameters. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to adjust for potential confounders.

RESULTS: Data from 156 patients were analyzed, including 111 patients in the Pre-FFP group and 45 in the Control group. Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although deep hypothermic circulatory arrest duration and CPB fluid management differed between the groups. The adjusted mean difference in total post-CPB FFP transfusion units between the Pre-FFP and Control groups was - 1.54 units (95% confidence interval, - 7.51 to 4.43). No significant differences were observed in perioperative plasma-derived product use or bleeding outcomes. Although fibrinogen concentrations were higher and activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time-international normalized ratio were shorter at the end of CPB in the Pre-FFP group, these differences largely resolved after CPB.

CONCLUSION: FFP administration during CPB was associated with transient improvement in coagulation parameters but was not associated with postoperative transfusion requirements or bleeding outcomes in adult patients undergoing elective TAR. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder regarding the caregiving process.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the metaphorical perceptions of caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) regarding the caregiving process. The study was conducted with 46 participants responsible for the care of children with ASD. Data were collected between March and April 2026 using a metaphor form. The first part of the form included questions regarding sociodemographic characteristics, while the second part included the statement, "Caring for a child with autism spectrum disorder is like … because …" to identify participants' metaphorical perceptions of the caregiving process. Participants produced 46 metaphors, which were analyzed using content analysis and grouped into five themes: love, belonging, and hope; struggle and resilience; patience, acceptance, and adaptation; uncertainty, learning, and discovery; and intensive care and dependency. Regarding emotional valence, 28.3% of the metaphorical expressions were classified as positive, 37.0% as negative, and 34.7% as mixed. The theme of love, belonging, and hope had the highest frequency (28.3%). Descriptive cross-tabulations were also used to present the distribution of metaphor themes according to caregiving support, psychological support, and education about ASD. As no inferential statistical tests were performed, these distributions were interpreted descriptively and were not considered evidence of statistically significant differences, associations, or causal effects. Overall, the findings demonstrate that caregivers' metaphorical perceptions of caring for a child with ASD reflect a multidimensional experience encompassing emotional attachment and hope as well as struggle, adaptation, uncertainty, and dependency.

articles.title: Expert clinical consensus on the application of vancomycin graft presoaking in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction : a modified Delphi study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Vancomycin graft presoaking in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) has been shown to reduce intraoperative graft contamination (IOGC) and postoperative infection. Establishing a consensus as to how to perform this technique can guide clinicians and be applied in any future randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating its effectiveness. This study aims to establish such a consensus, explore the willingness of experts to recruit patients in a future RCT evaluating this technique, and identify any adverse outcomes.

METHODS: A UK-based, three-round, online modified Delphi study was completed, focusing on various aspects of vancomycin graft presoaking in ACLR. We predetermined that a 70% agreement would define consensus.

RESULTS: Consensus was achieved for the following: using a concentration of 5 mg/ml (70.8%); wrapping the graft in a vancomycin-soaked swab or briefly dipping the graft into the vancomycin solution followed by wrapping in a swab (89.8%); exposing the graft to vancomycin from harvesting the graft until the surgeon is ready to use it (83.1%); and not requiring irrigation of the antibiotic soaked graft prior to implantation into the knee (96.6%). Of 80 experts, 61.3% expressed a willingness to recruit patients in a future RCT evaluating the effectiveness of this technique. No complications of vancomycin use were reported.

CONCLUSION: This study is the first national consensus agreement regarding the technical aspects of vancomycin graft presoaking in ACLR. Given the lack of robust evidence, an adequately powered RCT is required to address current scepticism towards this practice, and this study provides the necessary framework for such future work.

articles.title: Does participation in a randomized controlled trial of two surgical revision strategies for periprosthetic joint infection influence surgeons' practice?
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The translation of evidence into surgical practice is often slow, yet participation in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) may itself influence clinicians' behaviour before results are known. The INFection ORthopaedic Management (INFORM) trial compared single- and two-stage revision surgery for hip periprosthetic joint infection (PJI). This study explored whether INFORM influenced surgeons' views, confidence, and willingness to offer single-stage revision.

METHODS: All surgeons who participated in and recruited patients to INFORM were invited to complete an electronic survey after trial recruitment closed. The survey examined perceived changes in practice, confidence, and indications for single-stage revision. Quantitative items were summarized descriptively; free-text responses underwent descriptive content analysis to identify themes.

RESULTS: A total of 26 surgeons completed the survey. Although 11 (42.3%) reported that their overall opinion of single compared with two-stage revision had changed, larger proportions described more specific shifts: 16 (61.5%) reported increased confidence in performing single-stage revision, and 18 (69.2%) were more willing to consider it for patients for whom they previously would not have offered it. Across most clinical scenarios, including treating abscess, sinus tract, and Enterococcus infection, willingness to consider single-stage revision increased following trial participation. Qualitative content analysis revealed four inter-related themes: increased familiarity and comfort with single-stage revision; clarification or reinforcement of selection criteria; confirmation of existing practice for some surgeons; and the influence of local multidisciplinary and institutional context.

CONCLUSION: Participation in a pragmatic surgical RCT was associated with increased confidence and a broader willingness to consider single-stage revision for PJI, even before trial results were available. These findings suggest that trial participation itself may act as a catalyst for experiential learning, refinement of individual equipoise, and early shifts in clinical decision-making. Recognising this influence may help inform the design, conduct, and interpretation of future surgical trials.

articles.title: Access to positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography in the management of lung cancer in Te Manawa Taki Midland Region of New Zealand.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examines access to 18-F fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography-computed tomography (FDG PET-CT; PET-CT) scans among lung cancer patients.

DATA AND METHODS: Patients diagnosed with lung cancer in 2011-2021 were identified from the Midland Lung Cancer Register and the New Zealand Cancer Registry. Patients were linked to the National Non-Admitted Patient Collection to determine if they underwent PET-CT. Logistic regression was used to estimate the odds ratios of having PET-CT, adjusting for age, gender, ethnicity, year of diagnosis, socio-economic status, cancer stage, cell type, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) status and comorbidities.

RESULTS: We identified 613 patients with stage I, 300 with stage II and 3,722 with stages III and IV lung cancer, with 75% of stage I and 68.3% of stage II undergoing PET-CT. PET-CT has become more common over time. Patients aged 80 years and over, Māori, those with frailty (ECOG 2+), and those with stages II-IV of disease were less likely to receive PET-CT. Gender, socio-economic status and comorbidities did not influence the use of PET-CT.

CONCLUSION: PET-CT is a standard of care for patients with early-stage lung cancer, suitable for curative treatment. The disparity of access to PET-CT for Māori needs to be addressed.

articles.title: Benchmarking heart failure care: the ANZACS-QI Heart Failure Registry Pilot implementation and results (ANZACS-QI 86).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Heart failure is a major healthcare problem in Aotearoa New Zealand. As therapies advance and become increasingly complex it is essential that we systematically characterise phenotype and monitor adherence to relevant guidelines to drive quality improvement. Here we report the results of the ANZACS-QI Heart Failure Registry Pilot, implemented in Northern Region hospitals.

METHODS: Age-stratified random sampling was used to identify a representative cohort of patients hospitalised with heart failure (2022 and 2023) using national administrative datasets. The electronic clinical records were reviewed and data entered into the web-based registry. Pre-specified outcomes that were analysed included rates of left ventricular assessment (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF]) and prescription of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT).

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 328 patients and registry form completion rates were high (98%). LVEF assessment rates within 2 years of the index hospital discharge were 81%. Of those with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction that survived until discharge (n=137), only 13 (9%) met the composite medication indicator of being prescribed (or with documented contraindication/intolerance) all four GDMT classes. This was largely driven by 92 (67%) being ineligible for subsidy for sodium glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors; however, prescription rates of the other GDMT classes were suboptimal.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights that there is a considerable gap between guideline recommendations and real-world practice. Following pilot completion, performance indicators have been established and the registry has expanded with the goal for it to become national. The successful implementation of the registry is an important step in quality improvement for patients hospitalised with heart failure.

articles.title: Prior stroke history and functional outcomes after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage: An exploratory propensity score-adjusted analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the association between prior stroke history and 3-month functional outcome after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH).

METHODS: We analyzed 258 patients with sICH (36 with and 222 without prior stroke) in a single-center retrospective cohort; 3-month outcome was available in 218 (28 vs. 190). Propensity scores were estimated from age, sex, admission Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score, log hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage, infratentorial hemorrhage, and antithrombotic use. The primary analysis was 1:3 propensity score matching; sensitivity analyses used 1:2 and 1:4 matching, stabilized and truncated inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and overlap weighting. The primary outcome was a 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2.

RESULTS: Before adjustment, patients with prior stroke were older, more severely affected, and less often achieved an mRS of 0-2 (7.1% vs. 32.1%; odds ratio [OR] 0.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.04-0.71, p=0.006). After 1:3 matching, the rates were 8.0% and 11.9%, with no significant association on conditional logistic regression (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.16-5.37, p=0.941). Overlap weighting likewise showed none (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.06-3.57, p=0.452), whereas IPTW showed a significant association, although residual covariate imbalance remained for age and admission GCS.

CONCLUSIONS: The crude association between prior stroke history and poor functional outcome was substantially attenuated after adjustment for measured confounders. Prior stroke history alone should not drive prognostic judgment; acute severity and premorbid functional status should also be considered. These exploratory findings require multicenter validation.

articles.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion.
articles.abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

articles.title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo.
articles.abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

articles.title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection.
articles.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

articles.title: TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling.
articles.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5's cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

articles.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict.
articles.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations.
articles.abstract: From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from Drosophila embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain-mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5'-triphosphate (ATP)-dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

articles.title: Effective usage of a multidisciplinary team and supportive care for treatment adherence in heart failure patients.
Novel and emerging agents for myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Wide variance in myelodysplastic syndrome/neoplasm (MDS) disease biology informs risk and ultimately management, which leverages a relatively limited number of agents with an insufficient rate and duration of meaningful clinical response. The development of novel agents is required to address the significant unmet clinical needs of patients with these malignant diseases.

AREAS COVERED: This review focuses on novel agents that stem from a progressive understanding of MDS pathobiology and for which there are available pre-clinical and/or clinical data. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science databases; abstracts from major hematology-oncology conferences were reviewed, and the clinicaltrials.gov registry was queried for active trials. The search used the key word 'myelodysplastic syndrome' and included articles published in English up to 10 May 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: An increasing understanding of the biological underpinnings of MDS pathogenesis and progression has yielded the availability of several efficacious synthetic molecules. Efforts to target both select biological subgroups and broader mechanisms of disease are underway in both classical later-line monotherapy settings and frontline combinations with available agents. Correlative analyses from past/ongoing studies, and inclusive, yet optimized trial designs will aid the pursuit of getting more effective therapies to MDS populations in need.

articles.title: RNA-binding proteome dynamics following ischemia-reperfusion injury in the kidney.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent complication in hospitalized patients and is associated with increased mortality. Despite its relevance, no targeted therapies are available. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are essential regulators of cellular function and have been implicated in AKI, but a comprehensive analysis of their role is lacking. We investigated RBP regulation in porcine kidneys subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury following cardiopulmonary resuscitation. To assess evolutionary conservation, RBP profiles were also obtained from human kidney tissue. After ischemia-reperfusion injury, we found RBPs exhibiting altered RNA-binding capacity, including metabolic enzymes previously implicated in ischemic stress. These findings suggest that energy metabolism is linked to RNA regulation during kidney injury. Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury alters the RNA-binding landscape, affecting both regulatory and metabolic RBPs. The conservation of these proteins in human kidneys highlights their translational relevance and identifies RNA-protein interactions as potential therapeutic targets in AKI.

articles.title: Environmental phthalate and chronic kidney disease: Epidemiology, mechanistic pathways, and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major global health problem, and early detection and risk control are still limited. Phthalates-widely used plasticizers with endocrine-disrupting effects-have been increasingly implicated in CKD-related outcomes. Human studies have reported associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and kidney-related markers, commonly reflected by the albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), although the direction and magnitude of these associations vary by metabolite, population, study design, and outcome definition. Mechanistic evidence is currently dominated by studies of di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and its metabolite mono-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (MEHP), suggesting potential involvement of oxidative stress, inflammation, regulated cell death, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and extracellular-matrix (ECM) remodeling in experimental models. However, the extent to which these mechanisms apply to other phthalates or alternative plasticizers remains uncertain. The evidence remains heterogeneous across populations and exposure contexts, and key limitations include its observational nature, exposure-measurement bias, reverse causality, and uncertainty regarding temporality and mixture effects. Future longitudinal, pharmacokinetic, and intervention studies are needed to determine whether phthalate biomarkers have clinically meaningful prognostic or predictive utility.

articles.title: Functional characterization of the pheromone receptor OR67d within the genus Drosophila.
articles.abstract: Insects rely on chemosensory cues to mediate essential behaviors, including mate recognition. In Drosophila melanogaster, the odorant receptor OR67d detects the male-specific pheromone cis-vaccenyl acetate (cVA), initiating diverse behavioral responses. However, the evolutionary conservation and functional tuning of OR67d receptors across Drosophila species remain largely unexplored. Here, we characterize OR67d receptors from nine Drosophila species using phylogenetic analysis, transgenic expression, and electrophysiology. While most orthologs retained sensitivity to cVA, some exhibited broader tuning, responding to structurally similar acetates. Notably, D. bipectinata and D. navojoa responded to cVA despite not producing it, raising the possibility that cVA detection has been maintained independently of endogenous production, possibly as a heterospecific cue. Structural modeling revealed overall high sequence conservation yet identified variable regions within the putative binding pocket potentially underlying differences in ligand selectivity. These findings contribute to our understanding of pheromone receptor evolution and how chemical communication systems diversify across Drosophila species.

articles.title: Modeling congenital cytomegalovirus infection in human inner ear organoids.
articles.abstract: Congenital infection with human cytomegalovirus is a leading cause of congenital hearing loss. Investigating its effects is challenging due to the virus's strict species specificity, limiting the relevance of animal models. This study aimed to establish a human-specific model of cytomegalovirus infection in the developing inner ear using inner ear organoids derived from pluripotent stem cells. Organoids were cultured for 75 days, vibratome sectioned into 300-μm slices, and exposed to laboratory or clinical strains of human cytomegalovirus for 7 or 21 days. Viral replication was confirmed, with successful infection by clinical strains requiring a minimum viral titer. Immunofluorescence revealed targeted infection of nonsensory epithelial cells and mesenchymal cells, with occasional infection of hair cells and neurons. This model replicates the key aspects of congenital cytomegalovirus infection, providing a scalable human platform to study viral pathogenesis, identify susceptible cell types, and explore targeted therapies.

articles.title: Altered IgA-associated gut microbiota and serum IgA are associated with disease severity in alcohol-associated liver disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND:: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is characterized by dysbiosis, impaired gut barrier function, and microbial translocation driving hepatic inflammation. Immunoglobulin A (IgA), the dominant mucosal antibody, maintains intestinal homeostasis by coating bacteria. While serum IgA is elevated in advanced ALD, intestinal IgA responses and IgA-bound microbiota remain incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVE:: To define fecal and serum IgA responses and characterize IgA-bound bacterial communities across the spectrum of ALD.

DESIGN:: Stool and serum IgA were measured in 107 healthy controls (HC), 191 individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD), and 360 individuals with alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH). IgA-bound bacteria were isolated using magnetic activated cell sorting (MACS) and analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing.

RESULTS:: Fecal IgA increased with disease severity (AH > AUD > HC) and was associated with distinct microbial compositions. IgA-bound bacterial diversity was reduced in AH and partially recovered after abstinence. Beta diversity demonstrated separation by disease, with enrichment of pathobionts (e.g., Streptococcus, Enterococcus, Escherichia/Shigella) and depletion of beneficial taxa (e.g., Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae). IgA-bound taxa correlated with disease severity, with commensals showing inverse and Campylobacteraceae positive associations with MELD-Na. Serum IgA was elevated in AH, decreased after abstinence, and did not correlate with fecal IgA. While fecal IgA was not associated with survival, higher serum IgA independently predicted reduced 6-month survival.

CONCLUSION:: ALD is characterized by altered mucosal IgA responses and IgA-associated microbial alterations. The lack of correlation between fecal and serum IgA suggests regulation of mucosal and systemic IgA responses. Serum IgA may serve as a prognostic biomarker in ALD.

articles.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control.
articles.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) microstates are successive global brain states whose temporal organization may reflect cognitive dynamics that conventional summary statistics do not capture. We applied a sequence-based framework, combining conditional successor analysis with multiple sequence alignment adapted from genomics, to microstate sequences recorded during a Go/NoGo task in 30 healthy adults. Generalized estimating equations showed no condition-level differences in standard microstate metrics. Conditional successor analysis identified three motifs enriched in the NoGo-early window (100-500 ms): A-C-D (p FDR = 0.013), B-A-D (p FDR = 0.029), and E-A-D (p FDR = 0.040), all passing through microstate A and ending in microstate D, consistent with fronto-central engagement. Multiple sequence alignment showed non-random temporal organization in all conditions (all z > 11.5 and p < 0.001). These results support sequence syntax as a framework for linking millisecond-scale brain dynamics to cognitive function.

articles.title: Oleoyl-L-carnitine regulates PPM1B through BIRC6, inducing tumor concomitant cardiac fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Cancer increases the risk of heart failure progression, and cancer survivors face elevated odds of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Clinical observations link breast cancer severity to left ventricular diastolic dysfunction in patients undergoing surgical resection. Using metabolomic profiling of human breast cancer tissues and quantification in both patients and mouse models, we identified elevated levels of the tumor metabolite oleoyl-L-carnitine (OLcarn). Using affinity-enrichment proteomics with biotin-OLcarn in cardiac fibroblasts, we identified baculoviral IAP repeat-containing protein 6 (BIRC6) as a candidate interacting protein. Furthermore, binding of OLcarn to BIRC6 promoted ubiquitination of the protein phosphatase PPM1B and increased SMAD3 phosphorylation, thus activating pro-fibrotic signaling cascades. These results define a mechanism whereby a tumor-derived metabolite promotes cardiac fibrosis via the BIRC6/PPM1B/SMAD3 axis. This pathway reveals a key mode of tumor-heart crosstalk and may inform potential therapeutic strategies for cancer-associated cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: Identification of multi-omics molecular programs from the peripheral circulation of patients with PAH.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves progressive remodeling of the pulmonary vasculature and right ventricle, yet much of our understanding of disease progression relies on rodent studies because opportunities for investigation in humans are limited. We integrated plasma proteomic, metabolomic, and lipidomic profiles from 402 patients with PAH and 76 healthy controls using latent-network discovery and graphical modeling, with validation in an external cohort and comparison with human and bovine tissue. PAH was associated with broad molecular remodeling across peptides, metabolites, and lipids, with multiple multi-Omic programs converging on disruptions in the TCA cycle. Of note, elevated 2-hydroxyglutarate distinguished PAH across etiologies and comorbidity profiles, was associated with survival and treatment intensity, and was replicated externally. Related TCA-cycle changes were also observed in pulmonary vascular stromal and immune cells. These findings reveal coordinated remodeling across multiple molecular axes and highlight plasma multi-omics as a bridge between clinical phenotypes and tissue-level metabolic reprogramming.

articles.title: Deep learning detection and biological interpretation of arterial stiffness from retinal fundus images in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Pulse wave velocity is the gold standard for assessing arterial stiffness (AS) but is costly and not widely accessible. This multicenter study developed a deep learning model to predict AS from fundus images. Trained on 64,440 images from 36,412 adults with diabetes at China's National Metabolic Management Centers and externally validated on 6,217 images from two independent hospitals, the model achieved an AUC of 0.780 (95% CI: 0.769-0.792) and 0.772 (95% CI: 0.754-0.790) in internal and external validation, respectively, outperforming models using classical risk factors alone. The fusion model integrating fundus images with clinical factors significantly improved test-set performance (AUC = 0.853, 95% CI: 0.844-0.863) and demonstrated good external generalizability (AUC = 0.801, 95% CI: 0.784-0.816). Ablation studies indicated retinal arteries were associated with AS, with other retinal structures also contributing. These findings support deep-learning-based fundus-image analysis for AS screening in real-world clinical settings, and retinal-structure analyses for exploring AS pathophysiology.

articles.title: PET bottle recycling system in Asia: Lessons learned from six cities.
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of bottled water consumption has increased post-consumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottle waste, while the recycling performance varies substantially across Asian cities. This study comparatively examines PET bottle recycling systems in Tokyo, Seoul, Shanghai, Hong Kong, Bangkok, and Kuala Lumpur, focusing on policy and governance, producer and recycler practices, recycling technologies, market conditions, and informal recycling actors. The results reveal distinct recycling pathways: Tokyo and Seoul have mature policy systems and are advancing high-value recycling. Shanghai has a dynamic market-led system dominated by downcycling. Hong Kong shows gradual policy improvement but limited effectiveness, and Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur remain highly reliant on informal recycling under weak enforcement. These differences highlight the importance of coordinated policy, market, technology, and social actors in shaping urban PET recycling outcomes. The study identifies transferable practices, including source separation, inclusive integration of informal recyclers, extended producer responsibility, and effective government coordination, providing guidance for improving PET recycling systems across Asia.

articles.title: Sequence of aerobic and resistance exercise influences short- and long-term glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: A randomized trial.
articles.abstract: Combined aerobic and resistance exercise improves glycemic control in type 2 diabetes (T2D), yet whether the sequence of the two exercise modalities influences glycemic outcomes remains unclear. We examined acute and long-term glycemic responses to aerobic-then-resistance (AR, n = 28) versus resistance-then-aerobic (RA, n = 28) exercise in 56 community-dwelling adults with T2D over 8 weeks (3 sessions/week). Aerobic exercise was performed on bicycle ergometers for 30 min at 40%-70% heart-rate reserve; resistance exercise targeted major muscle groups at 60%-80% 1RM. Compared with pre-exercise levels, mean glucose (p = 0.043) and HbA1c (p = 0.007) decreased only in AR group. Among participants without insulin treatment, insulin levels fell in both groups (AR: p < 0.001; RA: p = 0.001). At week 8, AR showed lower glucose during exercise and recovery (p = 0.036) and greater nocturnal glucose reduction (p = 0.015) than RA. Similar conventional improvements seen in both sequences, yet aerobic-first lowered mean/nocturnal glucose at the cost of greater variability, while resistance-first minimized fluctuations.

articles.title: Machine learning-based classification of healthcare-associated infections in rehabilitation settings.
articles.abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) represent a challenge in rehabilitation settings, where prolonged stays and complex clinical conditions increase infection risk. This retrospective observational study applied a machine learning (ML) approach to classify HAI presence in patients undergoing rehabilitation. Cross-sectional surveillance data were collected at three time points across 22 facilities. An elastic-net logistic regression model was internally cross-validated on an initial cohort (2,966 patients) and temporally validated on an independent cohort (1,459 patients), with model interpretability assessed using SHAP analysis. Balanced accuracy was 72% and 74.5%, sensitivity 71% and 77%, and specificity 73% and 72% in internal and temporal external validation, respectively. Vascular and urinary catheterization emerged as the strongest predictors, while incontinence, pressure ulcers, and variables related to care setting and healthcare pathways showed additional contributions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of ML-based HAI classification in rehabilitation and provide insights into infection-associated factors that may help prioritize prevention efforts.

articles.title: Monocyte TNF superfamily receptor dysregulation in tuberculosis-type 2 diabetes mellitus comorbidity.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) increases susceptibility to tuberculosis (TB) and contributes to immune dysregulation, partly through altered monocyte signaling. Although our earlier work has demonstrated that T2DM alters monocyte subsets and promotes hyper-inflammatory responses during TB, the mechanisms underlying dysregulated TNF superfamily pathways in TB-T2DM comorbidity are underexplored. A study cohort of 176 individuals (TB, TB-T2DM, T2DM-only, and healthy controls) was evaluated. Classical monocytes (CD14+CD16-; n = 20/group) from peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry for cytokines and activation markers upon stimulation with purified protein derivative (PPD), whole-cell lysate (WCL), and TLR2/4 ligands. Plasma TNF superfamily receptors (n = 44/group) were quantified using Human ProcartaPlex 12-plex multiplex ELISA. Associations were analyzed using Spearman correlation, and integrated network analyses including protein-protein interaction (PPI), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and Gene Ontology (GO) were performed. In the results, TB-T2DM individuals exhibited significantly increased intercellular cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, IL-1β, IL-1α, IL-10, and TNF-α) and activation markers (PDL-2, CD163, and CD206) compared with TB or T2DM (p < 0.05). Multiplex ELISA revealed significant decreases in CD137, CD40, GITR, TNFR1/2, and TRAIL-R1/R2 and increases in CD27, CD30, and Fas (APO-1) expression in TB-T2DM. Correlation analysis revealed weak-to-inverse associations between cytokine-associated markers and activation markers with multiple TNF-receptor superfamily members (p < 0.05). PPI analysis identified a highly interconnected TNF superfamily network, with TNFRSF1A, TNFRSF9, and CD95 as central hubs and KEGG enrichment in cytokine signaling, NF-κB pathway, death signaling, and TNF receptor binding. Together, hyperglycemia-associated monocyte dysfunction alters TNF superfamily receptor expression and receptor-cytokine integration, contributing to impaired immune regulation in TB-T2DM comorbidity.

articles.title: Microbial proteins shape the development of Fab-dimerized glycan-reactive antibodies that target glycosylated HIV-1 envelope.
articles.abstract: Fab-dimerized glycan (FDG)-reactive antibodies (Abs) bind a myriad of glycosylated pathogens in a glycan-dependent manner. We defined microbial proteins that bound FDG-reactive monoclonal (m) Abs from human HIV-1 infection (2G12), HIV-1 seronegative human (DH1005), and Simian-HIV (SHIV)-infected (DH851.3) and HIV-1-vaccinated (DH717.2) rhesus macaques. FDG mAbs bound diverse proteins in Candida albicans lysates, including 1,3-beta-glucanosyltransferase PGA4 (PGA4). Recombinant PGA4 was bound by FDG-reactive mAbs in a predominantly glycan-dependent manner, and tetrameric PGA4 induced calcium flux in a Ramos B cell line expressing DH1005 IgM BCR, suggestive of B cell activation. Additionally, we identified multiple bacterial proteins in human stool-derived intestinal microbiota whole-cell lysates that bound FDG-reactive mAbs, including the Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain XcpQ protein. Recombinant XcpQ was also bound by FDG-reactive mAbs in a glycan-dependent manner. These data provide insights into microbial factors that may contribute to the induction and development of this unique category of glycan-reactive antibodies.

articles.title: Osteopontin influences weight gain and immune cell composition during ART-treated chronic HIV infection.
articles.abstract: Despite the ability of antiretroviral therapy (ART) to effectively suppress but not cure, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV), people with HIV (PWH) remain at increased risk for metabolic and inflammatory comorbidities that worsen with age. Here, we identify osteopontin (OPN) as a modulator of weight change in a humanized HIV-infected mouse model of ART-treated, chronic infection. Knockdown of OPN (OPNkd) completely abolished weight gain observed in untreated HIV-infected males. In contrast, untreated OPNkd females showed a 3-fold increase in body weight relative to OPN-expressing controls. ART-containing chow initiation was associated with an OPN-dependent 10% increase in female body weight despite a concurrent decrease in food intake. Longitudinal analyses revealed sex- and treatment-dependent shifts in myeloid and CD4+ T cell frequencies. Collectively, these findings highlight an undiscovered role for OPN, in interactions with other key study variables, in mediating immune and weight-related outcomes in chronic HIV infection.

articles.title: From epidemiology to mechanisms of inflammation in hypertensive cardiac damage.
articles.abstract: Hypertension-induced cardiac damage is a progressive, high-burden disease driven in part by immune mechanisms. We characterized global hypertensive heart disease (HHD) trends using GBD 2021 data, which revealed steadily rising prevalence and mortality. We next evaluated the associations between inflammatory indices and cardiovascular disease (CVD) in National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data (2013-2018) with weighted logistic regression, validated by ordinal logistic regression and survival analyses. Neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR), C-reactive protein (CRP)/high-density lipoprotein (HDL) ratio, systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and neutrophil-to-monocyte-plus-lymphocyte ratio (NMLR) were independently associated with prevalent CVD among hypertensive individuals and had prognostic value for survival, suggesting utility for cardiovascular risk stratification. Transcriptomic and CIBERSORT analyses of hypertensive rat hearts revealed 830 dysregulated genes and distinct immune infiltration patterns. In an angiotensin II-induced murine model, validation confirmed cardiac dysfunction, elevated inflammation, and a pro-inflammatory macrophage shift. These findings link immune-inflammatory mechanisms to hypertension-induced cardiac damage and inform future risk assessment and therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 infection and genomic diversity in Quilombola communities during Brazil's gamma VOC wave.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 has disproportionately affected vulnerable populations worldwide; yet, data on SARS-CoV-2 transmission and variant diversity in Brazil's descendants of enslaved individuals, known as Quilombola, remain scarce. We conducted a cross-sectional study in Cachoeira, Bahia, in people seeking care, between February and March 2021, testing 700 oropharyngeal swabs by RT-qPCR and 591 plasma samples for IgM/IgG antibodies. Positive samples with Cq < 25 underwent genomic sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. SARS-CoV-2 infection burden was comparable between urban (31.4%) and rural (32.0%) zones in Quilombola communities. Genomic analysis of 39 sequences identified multiple lineages, predominantly the Gamma variant (P.1), with phylogenetic evidence of numerous introductions and both local and external transmission. These results reveal complex transmission dynamics and variant diversity within marginalized Quilombola populations, underscoring the need for targeted public health interventions, expanded diagnostic coverage, and prioritization of these communities in vaccination campaigns to address health inequities.

articles.title: Magnaporthe oryzae chrysovirus 1-A confers QoI fungicide tolerance in host conidial development.
articles.abstract: Rice blast caused by Pyricularia oryzae (syn. Magnaporthe oryzae) is a major fungal disease of rice, and QoI fungicides are widely used for its control. Here, we established a conidium-based assay for evaluating mycovirus-associated fungicide responses using Magnaporthe oryzae chrysovirus 1-A (MoCV1-A)-infected and virus-free isogenic isolates. The conidial development of the two isolates was compared in the presence of azoxystrobin (AZ). MoCV1-A infection significantly reduced sensitivity to AZ at the conidial stage, although infected isolates remained susceptible at higher AZ concentrations. Quantitative RT-PCR showed that transcript levels of genes associated with mitochondrial respiration, cAMP-PKA signaling, and melanin biosynthesis were maintained in MoCV1-A-infected conidia following AZ treatment. The ATP levels of MoCV1-A-infected conidia also were consistently higher than those of virus-free conidia before and after AZ treatment. These results suggest that MoCV1-A infection reduces QoI sensitivity by maintaining cellular energy homeostasis under fungicide stress through a mechanism distinct from target-site mutations.

articles.title: Author Correction to "Changes in Hypertension Prevalence and Control in Canada After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Insights From the Canadian Health Measures Survey Cycle 7." Canadian Journal of Cardiology Volume 42, Issue 10, October 2026, Pages 2456-2463. DOI: 10.1016/j.cjca.2026.04.013.
Pantothenate Metabolic Alterations in PROS1 Mutation Carriers and the Antithrombotic Effects of Pantethine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1-mutation patients through integrated multi-omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models.

METHODS: Serum metabolomics, siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed.

RESULTS: Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA-mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE-2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM-1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL-1β-induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM-1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine-conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co-incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation-driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic-endothelial-platelet mode of interaction.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic-endothelial-platelet association in protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1-deficient in vivo models.

articles.title: Wearable IMU analysis and semi-supervised recognition of hemiparetic gait states and phases.
articles.abstract: Wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs) can extend gait assessment beyond motion-analysis laboratories, but rehabilitation applications require interpretable measures and reliable event timing. This single-center proof-of-concept pilot study developed a wearable framework for post-stroke gait assessment, gait-event detection and phase recognition. Eight participants with post-stroke hemiparesis and eight healthy controls completed walking trials instrumented with seven IMUs, Vicon motion capture, and embedded AMTI force platforms. Vicon-derived kinematics, spatiotemporal measures, and bilateral symmetry characterized the deficits represented in the wearable signals. The affected side showed reduced knee flexion and ankle plantarflexion, shorter spatial progression, and greater reliance on double support. Heel- and toe-marker trajectories generated labels independently of the ankle-IMU inputs, while vertical ground-reaction-force thresholds verified heel-strike (HS) and toe-off (TO). Only bilateral ankle signals were supplied to the classifiers; the seven-sensor setup supported labeling and sensor-location comparison. A target-contralateral lightweight convolutional neural network (TC-LCNN) classified healthy, unaffected-side, and affected-side gait. A semi-supervised gradient-reversal Transformer-BiLSTM (SSGR-TBiLSTM) recognized background (BG), HS, full-foot contact (FF), heel-off (HO), and TO, using weak-to-strong consistency learning, confidence-filtered pseudo-labeling, and gradient reversal to exploit unannotated recordings and reduce participant-dependent variation. Under participant-independent eight-fold validation, TC-LCNN achieved 99.66% ± 0.36% accuracy and 99.71% ± 0.31% macro-F1 with 16.93 K parameters and 0.145 M MACs per window. Under eight-fold leave-one-subject-out validation, SSGR-TBiLSTM achieved left- and right-side macro-F1 scores of 93.50% ± 0.98% and 92.40% ± 0.59%, respectively. Event-level precision, recall, andF1 were 97.90%, 97.40%, and 97.65%; 95.40% and 99.00% of timing errors were within ±50 and ±100 ms. Mean absolute errors were 15-19 ms for HS, 17-23 ms for TO, and 33-41 ms for FF and HO. These preliminary within-cohort findings demonstrate label-efficient gait-state modeling and more precise HS/TO timing, while supporting multicenter and closed-loop validation before phase-triggered clinical use.

articles.title: ESX-5 paralog deletions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis alter macrophage cytokine signaling and bacterial heavy metal response.
articles.abstract: The ESX-5 secretion system is critical for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) viability and pathogenesis. However, a functional understanding of its impact on the host is unknown. ESX-5 is encoded at a single site with small putative virulence paralogs (ESX-5a, ESX-5b, and ESX-5c) spaced throughout the genome. To examine host-pathogen interactions of these putative virulence clusters, we made deletion mutants lacking these paralogs and infected primary human macrophages. Independent infection with any deletion mutant led to reduced cytokine secretion. This defect was dependent on viable bacteria and is mediated by an unresolved post-transcriptional mechanism. In bacterial transcriptomic analyses, each mutant downregulated heavy metal response genes compared with the wild type. Treatment of wild-type Mtb with heavy metals led to increased ESX-5a and ESX-5c expression, driving concurrent TNF and IL-6 secretion in macrophages compared with untreated bacilli, indicating a putative link between ESX-5 cargo export and cellular cytokine levels.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Consensus recommendations for neurofibromatosis type 1 management in Asia Pacific" [iScience 29 (2026) 117002].
articles.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.isci.2026.117002.].

articles.title: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

articles.title: Deficiency of peripheral serotonin caused by Tph1 abrogation attenuates cerebral malaria severity.
articles.abstract: In cerebral malaria (CM), the most severe neurological complication caused by Plasmodium falciparum infection, accumulating evidence suggests that tryptophan metabolism mediates disease severity by modulating inflammation and, consequently, blood-brain barrier disruption. Here, we have established an experimental CM mouse model to dissect the differential role of the host tryptophan-serotonin metabolic axis in regulating disease pathogenesis. Peripheral serotonin-deficient mice (Tph1 -/- ) displayed reduced mortality and blood-brain barrier permeability defects. In addition, we found that in the absence of serotonin synthesis via the enzyme Tph1, mice develop inflammation characterized by a mixed type 1 and type 2 cytokine signature. Pharmacological depletion of peripheral serotonin through injection of the Tph1 inhibitor telotristat in wild-type mice significantly improved resistance against CM. Thus, we propose that targeting serotonin synthesis through Tph1 antagonism could have a therapeutic role in P. falciparum infection and may act as a potential treatment strategy for CM.

articles.title: Intestinal epithelial Casd1 regulates mucus sialic acid O-acetylation and limits tissue damage from large-intestinal mucosal insults.
articles.abstract: Recent studies show that intestinal epithelial sialylation is essential for homeostasis, but whether this protection depends on sialic acid O-acetylation is unclear. CAS1 domain-containing protein 1 (Casd1) governs sialic acid O-acetylation, a natural inhibitor of sialidase activity. We hypothesized that epithelial mucin O-acetylation protects the colon by limiting sialidase-mediated mucus degradation and dysbiosis. Human MUC2 and murine Muc2 were richly O-acetylated, while intestinal epithelial-specific Casd1 deletion abolished mucin O-acetylation. Unexpectedly, intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) Casd1 -/- mice maintained normal mucus structure, barrier function, physiology, and overall Muc2 sialylation, with only subtle sex-specific microbiota changes. However, IEC Casd1 -/- mice developed significantly greater ulceration during dextran sulfate sodium colitis and increased cecal and distal colonic injury following Citrobacter rodentium infection despite equivalent pathogen burdens. Thus, epithelial sialic acid O-acetylation is dispensable for baseline mucus homeostasis but critically limits tissue damage during inflammatory and infectious insults.

articles.title: Adenoviral vector co-expressing ALDH1 and ADH1 mitigates alcohol toxicity and modulates glucose and lipid metabolism.
articles.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption remains a global health concern, with ethanol and its toxic metabolite, acetaldehyde, causing significant physiological harm. Current hangover remedies fail to enhance alcohol metabolism at a fundamental level. In this study, we engineered a recombinant adenovirus, catalase 68-acetaldehyde dehydrogenase 1-alcohol dehydrogenase 1 (C68-ALDH1-ADH1), co-expressing dehydrogenases ALDH1 and ADH1 to improve alcohol metabolic capacity. In vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that C68-ALDH1-ADH1 significantly reduced hepatic alcohol and acetaldehyde levels and alleviated liver injury. Overexpression of ALDH1 and ADH1 also improved glucose and lipid metabolism. Notably, the lipid metabolism related gene fatty acyl-CoA reductase 2 (FAR2) was found to be associated with ALDH1/ADH1 expression, linking it to alcohol detoxification and the fatty alcohol cycle. C68-ALDH1-ADH1 further ameliorated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) through this pathway. These findings supported a potential protective effect of C68-ALDH1-ADH1 in treating alcohol-related disorders.

articles.title: Targeting TRP channels in hearing loss from mechanisms to otoprotection.
articles.abstract: Hearing loss, a highly prevalent global disease with complex pathogenic mechanisms, poses significant challenges due to limited treatment options and secondary complications. Recent research highlights the crucial roles of transient receptor potential (TRP) channels in auditory physiology and pathology, including cochlear electrophysiology, endolymph ionic homeostasis, neurotransmitter release, inflammation, and sensorineural injury responses. Although previous reviews synthesized TRP-mediated pathological mechanisms in hearing loss, clinical translation and otoprotective drug discovery remain underexplored. This review characterizes inner ear TRP spatiotemporal expression, traces the hair cell mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) channel research trajectory, details their dual regulatory mechanisms, and compiles emerging TRP-targeting otoprotective candidates. It further highlights limitations including restricted preclinical models, scarce otoprotective drugs, and limited target diversity among existing agents. Finally, it proposes new research directions for future basic and clinical studies on TRP channels and auditory function.

articles.title: Toll-like receptor 4-driven translational reprogramming in macrophages is unaffected by Salmonella SPI-1 activity.
articles.abstract: Changes in gene expression during bacterial infection are the combined result of altered transcription and translation, with the latter comparatively understudied. Gram-negative bacteria rapidly trigger cytokine gene transcription in macrophages through the activation of pathogen-associated molecular pattern receptors, for example the detection of Salmonella lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the bacterial cell envelope by Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4). Here, through time-resolved parallel translatomic and transcriptomic profiling, we now show temporal TLR4-specific translational upregulation of cell signaling proteins in macrophages induced by Salmonella. While transcriptional upregulation of these genes is dampened through the activity of the Salmonella SPI-1 type 3 secretion system, a robust translational response remains. These data reveal an important host-pathogen translational regulatory network that modifies the innate immune response of macrophages to infection.

articles.title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. This work addresses these challenges by integrating soft robotics with computer vision. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.

articles.title: Comparative transcriptome analysis reveals candidate genes and defence pathways associated with resistance to potato cyst nematodes in potato (Solanum tuberosum).
articles.abstract: Globodera rostochiensis and Globodera pallida are two nematode species responsible for are potato cyst nematode (PCN) that significantly reduce potato (Solanum tuberosum) productivity worldwide. To elucidate the molecular basis of PCN resistance, we compared transcriptomic responses of the highly resistant potato breeding clone SM/11-120 with the susceptible cultivar Kufri Jyoti following simultaneous infection with both PCN species. Nematode penetration assays showed that SM/11-120 completely restricted nematode invasion up to 7 days post-inoculation (dpi), whereas Kufri Jyoti was susceptible to nematode penetration within 24 h post-inoculation (hpi) and supported juvenile development at 72 hpi and 7 dpi. RNA-sequencing (RNA-Seq) generated 18-27 million high-quality paired-end reads per library, of which 51.6-68.3% mapped uniquely to the potato reference genome. Comparative transcriptome analysis identified 724, 795, 694, and 899 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between SM/11-120 and Kufri Jyoti at 0 hpi, 24 hpi, 72 hpi, and 7 dpi, respectively. The resistant genotype exhibited enhanced expression of genes involved in immune signalling (NRC1, NBS-LRR), transcriptional regulation (WRKY, MYB), calcium signalling, pathogenesis-related proteins (PR1), hormone and defence metabolism (ACO1, geraniol 10-hydroxylase), and cell wall reinforcement (HRGP, XTH3, pectinesterase, β-expansin). Gene Ontology analysis revealed stronger enrichment of stress response, biological regulation, nitrogen compound metabolism, and response to biotic stimulus in SM/11-120 than in Kufri Jyoti. Expression patterns of selected defence-related genes were validated by quantitative reverse transcription (qRT)-PCR, confirming their rapid and sustained induction in the resistant genotype.

articles.title: Left atrial appendage occlusion versus antithrombotic therapy in nonvalvular AF with ASCVD and prior embolism.
articles.abstract: Managing nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and prior embolism is challenging. This retrospective study evaluated long-term outcomes of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) compared with oral anticoagulation (OAC) and antiplatelet therapy (APT) in primary (n = 647) and external validation (n = 570) cohorts. The primary composite outcome included recurrent ischemic stroke or systemic embolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. After inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), risks of the primary outcome, major bleeding, and mortality for LAAO were comparable with or lower than those of OAC and APT. For recurrent embolism, competing-risk analyses showed both OAC (SHR = 3.578, p = 0.003) and APT (SHR = 2.494, p = 0.040) carried a higher risk than LAAO. Results were consistent in the external validation cohort. These findings suggest LAAO may be a reasonable option for this high-risk population, offering a lower risk of recurrent embolism and comparable risk of major bleeding relative to pharmacological therapies.

articles.title: PP2A-dependent downregulation of GABAB receptors modulates somatostatin interneurons function and plasticity.
articles.abstract: Cortical circuits require precise inhibitory and excitatory neurotransmission to encode information and prevent pathology. Metabotropic GABAB receptors (GABABRs) are key inhibitory regulators in mammalian neurons. In GABAergic interneurons (INs), GABABR activation reduces inhibition, leading to disinhibitory mechanisms. Hippocampal somatostatin-expressing (SST) INs provide feedback inhibition to distal dendrites of principal cells (PCs) and other INs. Plasticity of SST INs is well established to control hippocampal circuit function dependent on metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) and GABABRs. Whether GABABRs regulate SST INs function over longer time scales and if this influences circuit function remains unclear. We combine quantitative freeze-fracture replica immunoelectron microscopy, ex vivo electrophysiology, and pharmacology to show that GABABR activation regulates long-term potentiation (LTP) of SST INs through protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A)-dependent loss of cell-surface GABABR, mGluR1α receptors, and Cav1.2 (L-type) Ca2+ channels. GABABR loss in SST INs shifts hippocampal activity toward greater plasticity of long-range inputs to CA1.

articles.title: β7-Integrin worsens diet-induced metabolic syndrome in mice by altering intestinal lipid handling and colonic inflammatory monocyte infiltration.
articles.abstract: Western diet (WD)-induced metabolic syndrome (MetS) involves obesity, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and low-grade inflammation. While β7 integrin-expressing adaptive immune cells contribute to WD-induced MetS, the role of β7 integrin in innate immunity remains unclear. To address this, the effect of antibody-mediated β7 integrin blockade or β7 integrin deficiency on WD-induced MetS was studied in recombination activating gene-2-deficient mice. Loss or inhibition of β7 integrin protected mice from WD-induced obesity, dyslipidemia, and glucose intolerance, partially via loss of β7 integrin-MAdCAM-1 interactions. β7 integrin deficiency altered intestinal lipid handling and monocyte infiltration into the colon and adipose tissue. Adoptive transfer confirmed that β7-expressing monocytes promote metabolic dysfunction in WD-fed recipients. Phospho-signaling analyses revealed attenuated PI3K-Akt pathway activation in β7 integrin-deficient colonic macrophages, and antibody treatments caused minor shifts in fecal microbiota profiles. Thus, β7 integrin-expressing innate immune cells drive WD-induced metabolic inflammation through monocyte recruitment, macrophage activation, and altered intestinal fat metabolism.

articles.title: Mucin-rich environment shapes Pseudomonas aeruginosa cytotoxicity and phage-mediated epithelial protection.
articles.abstract: Chronic respiratory diseases (CRDs) are characterized by excessive mucin accumulation that alters host-pathogen interactions within airway epithelia. Although bacteriophage therapy is increasingly considered as an alternative to antibiotics, it remains unclear how mucin-rich environments influence bacterial virulence and phage efficacy. Here, we show that exogenous mucin reshapes outcomes during Pseudomonas aeruginosa in epithelial cells. Mucin exposure induces transcriptional changes, increases epithelial susceptibility to bacterial cytotoxicity, and reduces bacterial adhesion and internalization. Surprisingly, mucin simultaneously enhances phage-mediated protection, preserving epithelial viability without impairing phage amplification. Moreover, prolonged bacterial exposure to mucin increases the cytotoxicity activity of cell-free secretomes, while altering the phenotypic and genotypic characteristics of phage-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings reveal that mucin-rich environments exert opposing effects on infection dynamics by increasing host vulnerability while enhancing phage-mediated control of bacterial infection. Our results highlight the mucosal environment as a key determinant of phage therapy outcomes and bacterial adaptation.

articles.title: Chitosan-stabilized electrospun nanofiber dressings with embedded flame-made nanosilver for the treatment of resistant infections.
articles.abstract: Wound healing can be severely compromised by infections, particularly those caused by antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. We developed antibacterial wound dressings based on electrospun polyvinyl alcohol-chitosan nanofibers containing flame-made silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs). The 2-10 nm Ag NPs are embedded within ∼200 nm fibers, enabling a high and sustained Ag+ ion release with no detectable nanoparticle release, which may help mitigate concerns associated with nanoparticle exposure. Chitosan structurally stabilizes the fibers while modulating swelling and local pH to enhance Ag+ diffusion. The dressings achieved >99.9999% bacterial reduction in vitro and up to 99% ex vivo using freshly excised human skin.
