Crucially, the dressings maintained >90% viability of human keratinocytes and fibroblasts and showed no detectable impairment of short-term wound healing. This study introduces a scalable, safe-by-design nanofiber platform for infection-resistant and healing-compatible wound care and supports its further evaluation in preclinical studies.

articles.title: Vagal maneuvers and pharmacological cardioversion in stable PSVT: A systematic review with implications for emergency nursing practice.
articles.abstract: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) is a common arrhythmic emergency for which vagal maneuvers offer a non-pharmacological route to cardioversion before drug escalation. This systematic review compared the effectiveness and safety of vagal maneuvers-particularly the standard and modified Valsalva maneuvers-against pharmacological cardioversion in adults with stable PSVT. Following PRISMA 2020 guidance, eleven studies published between 2014 and 2024 were identified across six databases and synthesized narratively owing to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. The modified Valsalva maneuver consistently achieved higher cardioversion rates than the standard technique and carotid sinus massage, with a favorable safety profile, while adenosine remained effective but more frequently associated with recurrence and discomfort. Effectiveness varied by age, arrhythmia subtype, and care setting. Collectively, the evidence supports the modified Valsalva maneuver as a safe, low-cost, first-line option before pharmacological escalation, with particular relevance to nurse-led management in emergency and prehospital care.

articles.title: Diet-attributable vascular/metabolic disease burden comparisons and public health implications in Western Europe and North America.
articles.abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD), ischemic stroke (IS), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and lower-extremity vascular disease are leading causes of disability in Western Europe and North America, but their diet-attributable burden remains unclear. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data, we assessed the association between the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) and the vascular/metabolic disease burden and compared the cross-regional burden through multi-dimensional time-trend, risk contribution, and projection analyses. Mendelian randomization (MR) tested causal diet effects on disease subtypes. Frontier analysis showed diet-related IHD and IS burden declined with SDI, while T2DM increased. By 2023, Western Europe had a lower burden than North America. Processed meat and whole grain dominated T2DM and IHD burden, respectively. Joinpoint analysis revealed declining trends. Projections to 2035 indicated North America remains higher. MR identified several potential causal links. This study provides a basis for vascular/metabolic disease prevention policies and dietary interventions in Western Europe and North America.

articles.title: Periodontitis as a potential contributor to lung cancer: Epidemiological evidence, proposed mechanisms, and clinical implications.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis has been proposed as a potential contributor to lung cancer (LC), but the epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. This structured narrative review evaluates the association between periodontitis and LC, the directness of proposed biological mechanisms, and the implications for risk assessment and supportive care. Observational studies generally report positive associations, although effect estimates vary according to periodontal ascertainment, study population, and adjustment for smoking. Clinically assessed periodontitis, self-reported or administrative diagnoses, tooth loss, periodontal-associated microbial markers, and general oral microbiome profiles represent distinct exposure domains and should not be interpreted interchangeably. The absence of a clear association among lifelong never smokers and the lack of supportive Mendelian randomization evidence further limit causal inference. Human studies demonstrate oral-lower airway microbial overlap, while experimental LC models support microbiota-related inflammatory and oncogenic signaling; however, periodontal origin, directional microbial transmission, and a continuous causal pathway from periodontitis to LC have not been established. Clinically, periodontitis should not modify current eligibility for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, and oral or respiratory microbiome biomarkers remain investigational. Perioperative oral care has comparatively stronger evidence for reducing postoperative pulmonary infectious complications, but this benefit should not be extrapolated to tumor recurrence or survival. Overall, current evidence supports an observational association and biological plausibility, whereas independent causality and an oncologic benefit of periodontal treatment remain unproven.

articles.title: Non-invasive glycemic control leveraging ultrasound dose window activation of MscL in diabetic mice.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is characterized by impaired glucose homeostasis and progressive pancreatic β cell dysfunction, highlighting the need for externally controllable strategies for metabolic regulation. Here, we combined low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) with the mechanosensitive channel MscL-G22S to establish a tunable sonogenetic system for glucose regulation. Graded ultrasound stimulation was evaluated in MscL-G22S-expressing β cells and diabetic db/db mice to define an effective acoustic dose range. Within an intermediate dose window, LIPUS increased intracellular Ca2+ levels and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vitro and improved glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, islet morphology, and systemic metabolic profiles in vivo. Serum metabolomics further identified metabolic pathway alterations associated with combined LIPUS and MscL-G22S activation. These findings establish a quantitative framework for relating ultrasound dose to sonogenetic metabolic responses and support further investigation of ultrasound-controlled regulation of glucose homeostasis.

articles.title: IgM monoclonal antibodies reduce IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of Zika and dengue virus infectivity.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is an arthropod-borne flavivirus endemic to Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia for which IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of infectivity (ADE) is a phenomenon of concern. The dynamics between flavivirus-specific antibodies of the IgG and IgM isotypes are mostly unknown. Here, we used DH1017.IgM, a previously described human-derived, pentameric, ultrapotent neutralizing ZIKV IgM monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a recombinantly produced IgM version of neutralizing EDE1 mAb C8 (C8.IgM) to assess if IgM antibodies can interfere with IgG-mediated ADE in vitro. Both mAbs consistently reduced IgG-mediated ADE across a panel of ZIKV-binding IgG mAbs in a dose-dependent manner. ADE mitigation was achieved at DH1017.IgM sub-neutralizing concentrations. C8.IgM also mitigated IgG-mediated ADE for ZIKV and dengue virus (DENV), demonstrating generalizability. Finally, DH1017.IgM confirmed inhibition of ADE at sub-neutralizing concentrations in sera of ZIKV-infected individuals. In conclusion, mAbs of the IgM isotype may potently counter the adverse effects of IgG-mediated ADE.

articles.title: Metabolic network restoration, not donor microbial engraftment, associates with resolution of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection.
articles.abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) effectively prevents recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection (rCDI). However, the mechanisms underpinning FMT efficacy are incompletely understood. We used proximity-ligation metagenomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics to profile dynamic changes in rCDI. We analyzed samples collected from the first 7 responders during a clinical trial comparing two donor-based treatments (lyophilized FMT [LFMT] or lyophilized sterile fecal filtrate [LSFF], free of intact microorganisms) to prevent rCDI. LSFF is enriched in Caudoviricetes, lipids, fatty acids, and human and extracellular bacterial proteins compared with LFMT. LFMT recipients had donor microbial engraftment, while LSFF recipients achieved only partial microbial community recovery without donor's contribution. Our multi-omics analyses identified a functional convergence following both treatments, shifting away from oxidative and antibiotic stress survival pathways toward enhanced carbon-nitrogen utilization pathways, suggesting that FMT mechanisms may involve metabolic reprogramming and host-microbial amino acid co-metabolism. Our findings provide important hypothesis-generating insights that warrant further validation.

articles.title: Linking nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal microbiota to immune responses during influenza-like illness in an aging population.
articles.abstract: Older adults are vulnerable to influenza-like illness (ILI). To study how infection shapes the respiratory microbiota, we profiled nasopharyngeal (NP) and oropharyngeal (OP) communities alongside local immune mediators in adults aged 60-88, comparing asymptomatic, ILI, and recovery states. NP communities clustered into three community state types (CSTs): Moraxella-dominated (CST-1), Haemophilus/Streptococcus/Staphylococcus-associated (CST-2), and Corynebacterium/Dolosigranulum-dominated (CST-3). During infection, compositional shifts were restricted to the NP niche, where CST-1 and CST-2 were more frequent. Streptococcus, Haemophilus and Moraxella were positively associated with inflammatory and interferon-related mediators, including IL-6, CXCL9 and CXCL10, while Corynebacterium showed negative associations. Immune activation was strong in the NP but limited in the OP, and stayed above healthy levels at follow-up, suggesting incomplete recovery. NP composition was also associated with symptom burden, viral and bacterial co-detection and smoking status. These site-specific microbiota-immune relationships identify the nasopharynx as the primary site of immune modulation during ILI in older adults.

articles.title: Pharmacological AhR activation attenuates airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in a mixed allergen asthma model.
articles.abstract: Airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling are major features of asthma. We investigated whether pharmacological activation of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) modifies these responses in a mixed allergen (MA) mouse model of asthma. MA exposure increased airway resistance, contractility, inflammation, and remodeling, with elevated AhR expression in whole lung and airway smooth muscle but limited canonical AhR target gene activation. Treatment with the high-affinity AhR agonist 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) improved lung mechanics, reduced inflammatory cell and cytokine accumulation, attenuated airway remodeling, and decreased airway narrowing in precision-cut lung slices. Bulk lung RNA sequencing further showed suppression of inflammatory, neutrophil-associated, and remodeling pathways following TCDD treatment, together with induction of canonical AhR target genes. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that AhR activation suppresses inflammatory gene networks, limits airway remodeling, and improves airway mechanics in experimental asthma, supporting the therapeutic potential of targeting AhR signaling to mitigate airway dysfunction and structural remodeling.

articles.title: Generation of hypoimmunogenic cardiomyocytes from human induced pluripotent stem cells with TAPBP knockout.
articles.abstract: Immunological rejection is a challenge for the transplantation of cardiomyocytes (CMs) derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). TAP-binding protein knockout (TAPBP-KO) hiPSC-derived CMs (hiPSC-CMs) were used to reduce human leukocyte antigen class I expression and their hypoimmunogenic potential was determined. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs exhibited CM differentiation efficiency and functional properties comparable to those of controls. The immunological responses against cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) or natural killer cells (NK cells) were measured using the production of inflammatory cytokines, the expression of degranulation markers, and cell viability upon co-cultivation with hiPSC-CMs. The CTL-mediated cytotoxicity was lower in TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs than in controls. TAPBP-KO hiPSC-CMs did not induce cytotoxicity from NK cells. This approach can preclude immunological rejection from CTLs without initiating the innate immune response from NK cells, thereby expanding the access to cell therapy for patients with heart failure.

articles.title: StrokeTime: A comprehensive longitudinal scRNA-seq atlas of the ischemic mouse brain.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape. To systematically characterize these dynamics, we integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 21 mouse stroke studies (103 samples; 414,359 cells) spanning multiple models and post-stroke intervals. Using a harmonized computational workflow, we constructed StrokeTime, a single-cell mouse brain atlas covering hyperacute, acute, subacute, and chronic stages post-ischemia. The atlas contains 17 major cell classes and 120 fine-grained transcriptional states within myeloid, lymphoid, vascular, epithelial, neuronal, and glial populations. Myeloid cells showed the greatest plasticity, including disease-associated microglia/macrophage programs shared across resident and infiltrating cells, whereas lymphocytes featured activation and regulatory signatures within lineage constraints. Vascular and mural cells shifted from early inflammatory and barrier-disruptive programs to later fibrotic and angiogenic states. StrokeTime delineates both convergent and cell type-specific injury responses, offering a resource for studying post-ischemic brain immunity, tissue remodeling, and benchmarking future single-cell and single-nucleus studies of cerebrovascular disease.

articles.title: Stable truncating mutations in plakophilin-2 induce arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy-like phenotypes in adult zebrafish.
articles.abstract: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disorder characterized by arrhythmias and fibrofatty myocardial remodeling, often leading to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Mutations in plakophilin-2 (PKP2) represent the most prevalent genetic cause of ACM. Here, we establish zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a complementary vertebrate model for PKP2 mutation-based ACM. Comparative single-cell RNA-seq analyses revealed distinct cardiac expression patterns of PKP2 and its homologs across species. Using CRISPR-Cas9, we generated two truncating mutations in zebrafish pkp2, resulting in frameshifts and premature terminations (p.Glu250Glyfs∗17 and p.Glu31Glyfs∗72, respectively). Mutant zebrafish exhibited impaired cardiac contractility, arrhythmias, lipid accumulation on the ventricular surface, ultrastructural abnormalities of intercalated discs, and increased susceptibility to swimming exercise-induced sudden death. Transcriptomic analyses identified transcriptional alterations in genes involved in muscle contraction and lipid metabolism. Together, these data establish zebrafish as a useful complementary vertebrate model for studying PKP2-based ACM and gene-environment interactions underlying disease progression.

articles.title: Lactate-driven histone lactylation by AARS1 promotes pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Glycolytic reprogramming drives lactate accumulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). We used a monocrotaline-induced rat PAH model and platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-stimulated pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), together with oxamate intervention and molecular assays, to investigate lactate-mediated histone lactylation. PAH tissues exhibited increased lactate, MCT4, and histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), accompanied by reduced HDAC1. Oxamate reversed these alterations and alleviated pulmonary vascular remodeling. Manipulating MCT4 expression modulated H3K18la levels. Upregulated alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1) displayed enhanced nuclear localization after lactate exposure; AARS1 depletion suppressed lactate-triggered H3K18la and PASMC proliferation. H3K18la was enriched at the Ctnnb1 promoter and correlated with enhanced Ctnnb1 transcription. These findings suggest that lactate may act as an epigenetic signal, linking glycolysis to Ctnnb1 activation through AARS1-associated H3K18la, thereby offering a potential target for PAH treatment.

articles.title: Proteomic and extracellular particle changes in preterm neonates with suspected late-onset sepsis.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains an important cause of morbidity and mortality in neonates. In this prospective, multisite observational study, proteomics and extracellular particle analysis were performed on platelet-poor plasma from neonates at the point of clinical suspicion for sepsis (n = 110). Neonates were then classified by their clinical teams into three groups: culture-proven sepsis, culture-negative sepsis, or non-sepsis. Neonates with culture-proven sepsis demonstrated statistically significant differences in their analyzed proteome compared to neonates deemed to have non-sepsis, while those with culture-negative sepsis did not. Extracellular particle concentration and type, as determined by flow cytometry, did not differ between the three groups. This study provides further evidence that culture-proven sepsis and culture-negative sepsis are not equivalent diagnoses in the neonatal population without a consensus definition for sepsis. The proteins identified in the culture-positive group may be of utility in determining neonatal sepsis endotypes, but this would require further validation.

articles.title: Paleogenomics reveals leprosy at the late antique burial site of Fallward in northern Germany.
articles.abstract: The coastal settlement of Fallward in northwestern Germany (3rd-5th century CE) is renowned for exceptionally preserved wooden and textile grave goods, yet the genetic and pathogen landscape of its inhabitants has remained unstudied. We conducted metagenomic analyses on skeletal samples from 11 individuals to investigate their genetic affinities and infectious disease history. Three individuals yielded sufficient data for population genetic analysis: two clustered with northwestern European Iron Age and Anglo-Saxon groups, while one adult male might have originated from a Roman frontier population. This man was also infected with a strain of Mycobacterium leprae belonging to phylogenetic branch 4 and was buried in a boat accompanied by Roman-influenced grave goods, including carved furniture and a military belt. Together, these findings point to possible long-distance connections linking remote communities, such as Fallward, to the wider Roman world during Late Antiquity.

articles.title: Low-frequency parasitized cells in bone marrow alter myelopoiesis following immunization with the live attenuated Leishmania major Cen -/- vaccine.
articles.abstract: Leishmaniasis lacks an effective vaccine. We developed a live-attenuated Leishmania major Centrin-deficient strain (LmCen -/-) that is safe and protective in murine and canine models through IFN-γ-producing effector T cells. Because persistent low-level infection supports durable immunity, we investigated latent parasites and immune remodeling in the bone marrow. Dual single-cell RNA sequencing detected parasitized bone marrow cells 28 days after intradermal inoculation with either virulent LmWT or attenuated LmCen -/-. Flow cytometry showed increased myelopoiesis following LmCen -/- immunization compared with LmWT infection. Cell-cell communication analysis implicated enhanced granulin-Sort3 signaling as a potential driver of this response. Bone marrow monocytes from LmCen -/--immunized mice efficiently cleared virulent LmWT parasites in co-culture, consistent with the induction of trained innate immunity. These findings identify the bone marrow as an active site of anti-Leishmania immune programming and suggest that LmCen -/- vaccination promotes durable protection through coordinated adaptive and innate mechanisms.

articles.title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence.
articles.abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

articles.title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals.
articles.abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2, IL-12, and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges (CXCL1, CXCL5, and CXCL8) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines (CCL5 and CCL8) and interleukins (IL-6, IL-18, and IL-24) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

articles.title: Evidence for climate-mediated range expansion of hybrid wood ants.
articles.abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Hybridization can quickly increase genetic variation, potentially facilitating climate adaptation; however, it is unclear how hybrids respond to climatic changes. Here, we combine whole-genome, life-history, acute heat-shock, and climatic data of 69 wood ant populations across Finland to assess whether F. aquilonia × F. polyctena hybrids outperform their cold-adapted parent F. aquilonia in warming climates. Compared to F. aquilonia, hybrids are active and their offspring emerge earlier in spring, and they withstand acute temperatures relevant in nature better. Further, the hybrids' border has shifted 200 km northwards, coinciding with the expansion of climatic conditions suitable for hybrids. Our results provide evidence that hybrids have an adaptive advantage over F. aquilonia due to their admixed ancestry, and recent climatic changes can lead to range expansion of hybrids.

articles.title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids.
articles.abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

articles.title: Gammaherpesvirus infection of myeloid cells reveals divergent outcomes regulated by host and viral factors.
articles.abstract: The gammaherpesviruses establish a lifelong infection, with the cellular outcome of infection intimately regulated by cell type. Myeloid cells are an early infection target characterized by diverse outcomes. To investigate this, we use murine gammaherpesvirus 68 to demonstrate that macrophages are readily infectable, resulting in three divergent infection outcomes dictated by viral and host factors. Infection in vivo and in a cell culture model results in a high frequency of viable cells characterized by restricted viral transcription and unexpected transcription of the ORF75 locus, with rare cells initiating lytic replication. Restricted infection can be fully converted to productive lytic replication by pre-treatment with the host cytokine interleukin 4 (IL-4). Finally, infection with a high viral dose also results in productive infection, but it triggers increased cell death. These studies demonstrate stepwise regulation of virus infection and identify virus and host factors that dictate divergent outcomes in a single cell type.

articles.title: Characterization of an electromagnetic impact-driven needle-free injector with enhanced pulsed control in a low-jet-power regime.
articles.abstract: This study elucidates the development and performance characterization of an advanced electromagnetic impact-driven jet injector version 3 (IDM-v3), specifically engineered to achieve controllable jet formation within a low-jet-power regime. To overcome the excessive kinetic energy challenges observed in its predecessor (IDM-v2), several critical technical refinements were implemented, including the integration of a high-force solenoid, a calibrated 94 g projectile, and a reduced maximum impact stroke of 6 mm. Experimental results indicate that impact force, the calculated impact peak pressure metric, and exit jet velocity are highly sensitive to the impact configuration. The 0.2 mm nozzle produced the highest impact peak pressure,, of approximately 206 MPa, calculated from the measured peak target force using. The corresponding jet power, calculated separately from the measured exit jet velocity, was approximately 2 W. In contrast, the 0.4 mm nozzle produced a higher calculated jet power of approximately 6 W because of its larger nozzle-orifice area. High-speed temporal analysis revealed a multi-pulse response in the area-normalized target-force signal and stable jet morphology within the initial millisecond of actuation. Penetration assays using polyacrylamide gels and skin-removed ex vivo porcine tissue demonstrated that the 0.2 mm nozzle produced a narrower and more focused penetration channel, whereas the 0.4 mm nozzle produced greater lateral spreading and reached the specimen-depth limit under the tested conditions. Because the outer skin layer was removed, the porcine-tissue results represent penetration into exposed underlying tissue and do not demonstrate penetration through intact skin. These findings characterize the tunability of the IDM-v3 engineering prototype and provide a basis for further experimental development and evaluation. They do not establish biological safety or clinical or veterinary readiness.

articles.title: Key genes and pathways of pulmonary hypertension identified by integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive vascular disease, yet the underlying cell-type-specific molecular networks and diagnostic biomarkers remain incompletely defined. Integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomics, we identified 14 pulmonary cell types in PH, with smooth muscle cells (SMCs) as a central communication hub interacting with monocytes and macrophages. High-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) revealed 4 SMC modules enriched in extracellular matrix organization, TGF-β, and HIF-1 pathways. A five-gene diagnostic signature distinguished PH from controls with an area under the curve of 0.895. Immune infiltration and enrichment analysis showed that activated CD4 memory T cells, activated dendritic cells, and resting mast cells increased in the PH group, while angiogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathway were upregulated. In hypoxic human pulmonary artery SMCs, milk fat globule-epidermal growth factor-8 (MFGE8), secreted frizzled-related protein 2 (SFRP2), S100 calcium-binding protein A11 (S100A11), and procollagen C-endopeptidase enhancer 2 (PCOLCE2) were upregulated, and their knockdown suppressed proliferation, highlighting them as potential biomarkers and drivers of vascular remodeling, revealing a new molecular mechanism for PH and providing insights for potential therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Graphene-oxide-microfiber aptasensor for dynamic neutrophil monitoring: Bridging cytokine release syndrome and point-of-care sepsis diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Neutrophil granule release is critical for host defense, yet its dysregulation underpins cytokine release syndrome (CRS) in both acute (such as sepsis) and sustained inflammatory states. Distinguishing these phases requires real-time monitoring of early markers like neutrophil elastase (ELANE) and lactoferrin (LF), but conventional assays lack requisite sensitivity. Here, we developed a graphene-oxide-functionalized optical microfiber biosensor with high-affinity DNA aptamers (NE-AP and LF-AP) to quantify ELANE and LF via aptamer-protein binding-induced spectral red shifts. The sensor achieved ultralow detection limits (3.57 × 10-20 M for ELANE and 1.28 × 10-19 M for LF), eight orders below ELISA, with excellent selectivity. In a lipopolysaccharide-induced murine model, it resolved distinct temporal release profiles of ELANE and LF, and in clinical validation, it showed distinct spectral responses between septic patients and healthy controls in a preliminary clinical cohort. This platform provides a highly sensitive, real-time tool for decoding neutrophil dynamics, with preliminary translational potential for early sepsis diagnosis.

articles.title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

articles.title: Probing the role of left inferior frontal gyrus in vocal motor control: Evidence from TMS and causal inference analysis.
articles.abstract: Beyond an established role in speech initiation and planning, the left inferior frontal gyrus (IFG) may contribute to sensorimotor control of speech production. We applied continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) over the anterior (aIFG) and posterior (pIFG) regions to investigate their roles in vocal motor control. A causal inference analysis (CIA) framework was developed to characterize source-space network organization. cTBS over both left aIFG and pIFG reduced vocal responses and enhanced P2 responses to pitch feedback perturbations, with no significant differences between two active stimulations. However, global dissimilarity analysis revealed greater P2-related topographic deviation from sham stimulation following aIFG stimulation than following pIFG stimulation. CIA further identified different source-space network patterns associated with aIFG and pIFG stimulation. These findings demonstrate the causal involvement of the left IFG in auditory-vocal integration and highlight the potential of CIA for characterizing distributed network organization underlying vocal motor control.

articles.title: Dual impact of EZH1/2-targeted therapy in HTLV-1-associated inflammation: Direct and indirect mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Human T cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1)-associated inflammation, including uveitis, lacks effective targeted therapies. Here, we investigated whether epigenetic modulation through EZH1/2 inhibition could influence HTLV-1-related ocular inflammation using in vitro co-culture and infection models. HTLV-1 exposure increased EZH1 and EZH2 expression and the repressive histone mark H3K27me3 in retinal pigment epithelial cells. Treatment with the dual EZH1/2 inhibitor valemetostat reduced H3K27me3 levels. Valemetostat showed limited effects on cell viability and induced only modest, context-dependent apoptosis. Virological analyses showed model-dependent changes in proviral load, accompanied by reduced viral gene expression. Profiling of cytokines and chemokines revealed context-dependent modulation of inflammatory mediators. Functional assessment using p65 nuclear translocation assays indicated partial attenuation of NF-κB activation under inflammatory stimulation. Collectively, these findings suggest that EZH1/2-mediated epigenetic regulation is primarily involved in HTLV-1-related inflammatory responses, and that inhibiting EZH1/2 may be a potential approach to modulate inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: Development of a predictive model and nomogram using CTPA parameters for the identification of group 1 pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to identify computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA)-derived predictors of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and to develop a prediction model and nomogram for non-invasive diagnosis. We retrospectively analyzed CTPA datasets from 203 patients in the training cohort and 98 patients in the validation cohort, stratified into PAH (confirmed by right heart catheterization) and non-PAH groups. Pulmonary vascular and cardiac structural metrics were measured. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and logistic regression identified interventricular septal angle (IVSA), interventricular septal thickness (IVST), and right ventricular outflow tract wall thickness (RVOTW) as independent predictors. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.964 and 0.969 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively, with excellent calibration and clinical utility. The CTPA-based predictive model and nomogram may serve as a useful reference tool, potentially assisting in the identification of PAH and optimizing clinical workflows.

articles.title: L-Histidine alleviates tacrolimus-induced islet dysfunction via the gut-pancreas axis.
articles.abstract: Tacrolimus is widely used after organ transplantation but can impair pancreatic β-cell function and glucose homeostasis. Using rodent models, antibiotic-mediated microbiota depletion, fecal microbiota transplantation, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and MIN-6 cells, we examined whether microbiota-associated L-histidine contributes to β-cell protection. Tacrolimus altered gut microbial composition and increased histidine-associated microbial and metabolic signals. L-histidine supplementation improved glucose tolerance and insulin secretion, reduced β-cell apoptosis, and increased PI3K/Akt/mTOR/p70S6K signaling and PDX-1, NeuroD1, and MafA expression. Microbiota depletion attenuated several protective effects of L-histidine, supporting a contribution of the gut microbiota to this response. These findings connect a microbiota-associated amino acid with tacrolimus-related β-cell dysfunction and provide a framework for investigating microbiota-metabolite contributions to metabolic complications of immunosuppression.

articles.title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species.
articles.abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

articles.title: Plasma proteomic analysis identified potential therapeutic targets for pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive disease with high mortality. By integrating the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (49,272 participants, 337 incident cases) with drug-target Mendelian randomization, we identified 398 plasma proteins associated with incident PAH and 19 with potential causal relevance, 15 of which are druggable. Then we prioritized 5 candidates for expression validation in the Sugen5416 and hypoxia rat model and confirmed significant upregulation of TNFRSF10A and downregulation of UMOD in lung tissue, consistent with human plasma proteomic trends. Subsequent in vitro functional assays demonstrated that UMOD treatment attenuates PAH-related cellular phenotypes, whereas TNFRSF10A knockdown exacerbates pro-pathogenic progression. These results suggest UMOD as a promising protective therapeutic candidate and indicate the inherent complexity of the TNFRSF10A signaling. This integrative study provides a robust framework for translational research, future studies are warranted to elucidate downstream molecular mechanisms and further evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of these candidates.

articles.title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Elevated lactate is a common metabolic perturbation following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). This study evaluates the clinical predictive value of lactate and explores its mechanism involving protein lactylation. Machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to multicenter intensive care databases identified preoperative lactate as a dominant predictor of CPB-acute kidney injury (AKI) risk. To validate these predictions biologically, rat CPB and cellular models were utilized. Experimental results demonstrated that CPB induces glycolytic reprogramming, lactate accumulation, and elevated pan-lysine lactylation. Inhibiting the production of lactate was associated with decreased protein lactylation, lower oxidative stress, and reduced local tissue inflammation, thereby mitigating renal injury. Collectively, our interpretable ML predictive models identify lactate as a top clinical predictor of CPB-AKI, while our experimental data establish the lactate-lactylation axis as a potential mechanistic pathway linking metabolic dysfunction to renal damage. This axis represents a candidate therapeutic target requiring further validation.

articles.title: Pediatric RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection burden in G20 countries in 2023.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0-14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In 2023, an estimated 5,373 deaths and 483,162 DALYs occurred, with mortality and DALY rates having declined by ∼5.5% annually since 1990. The COVID-19 pandemic drove burden to a historic low in 2021, but a marked rebound followed in 2022-2023, though rates remained below pre-pandemic levels. Infants aged <1 year bore the heaviest burden (mortality 8.688 per 100,000), and India ranked highest, whereas Australia ranked lowest. Burden strongly correlated inversely with Sociodemographic Index. These findings highlight the need for precision prevention, targeting the youngest children and lower-resource G20 members.

articles.title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

articles.title: Microbiota-constrained bacterial density limits phage infection in the gut and allows persistence of susceptible cells.
articles.abstract: With the rise of antibiotic resistance, bacteriophage-based treatments against bacterial infections have regained momentum. However, phage therapy has so far shown only moderate success in complex environments like the mammalian gut, where phages are particularly promising tools for microbiome engineering and specific elimination of opportunistic pathogens. Here, we use different murine models of intestinal colonization to quantitatively assess the minimal population size of susceptible Escherichia coli cells that is required for phage replication in the gut (replication threshold). We found that the composition of the intestinal microbiota is a key factor shaping phage-bacteria interactions by restricting the carrying capacity of susceptible host cells. We further demonstrate that the replication threshold enables coexistence of susceptible and resistant bacteria in phage-treated mice, with implications for phage-based applications in complex environments like the gut.

articles.title: Phospholipase Fluorogenic Probes and Molecular Determinants of Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate-Adenosine Monophosphate Binding to Cyclic Oligonucleotide-Based Antiphage Signaling System CapV.
articles.abstract: Cyclic oligonucleotide-based antiphage signaling systems (CBASS) protect bacteria from bacteriophage infection by producing cyclic nucleotide second messengers that activate downstream effector proteins. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate-adenosine monophosphate (cGAMP)-activated phospholipase in Vibrio (CapV) is a prevalent CBASS effector whose activity is commonly monitored using the commercially available fluorogenic substrate resorufin butyrate; however, this probe is hydrolyzed by both basal and activated CapV, limiting its usefulness in CapV-related studies. Here, we report the rational design and evaluation of a series of resorufin ester probes with varying acyl chain lengths to improve the fluorogenic assay used to monitor CapV (from Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio cholerae) activation. While resorufin butyrate and pentanoate exhibited substantial cGAMP-independent hydrolysis, resorufin octanoate and decanoate provided an optimal balance between catalytic turnover and activation-dependent discrimination, displaying over 5-fold and approximately 10-fold increases in hydrolysis, respectively, upon 3',3'-cGAMP activation. Using resorufin octanoate as a fluorogenic reporter, we systematically investigated the effects of cyclic dinucleotide structural modifications on CapV activation. Phosphorothioate analogues with nonbridging sulfur (exo-S linkages) retained partial agonist activity, whereas the corresponding bridging 5'-phosphorothioester (endo-S) analogues was inactive, highlighting the importance of the native phosphodiester moiety in activating CapV. Replacement of the ribose 2'-hydroxyl groups with fluorine preserved CapV activation, whereas 2'-deoxy substitutions reduced activity, with modifications on the adenosine moiety having a greater detrimental effect than those on guanosine. These findings using the fluorogenic probes were validated using phospholipid hydrolysis and activity-based protein labeling assays. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the observed activity trends arise from differential disruption of key hydrogen-bonding interactions and ligand conformations required for productive CapV activation. Together, these fluorogenic probes provide a robust, high-throughput-compatible platform for studying CapV activation and defining cyclic dinucleotide structure-activity relationships.

articles.title: Lipid Chemistry beyond the Bilayer: Roles for Nonbilayer Lipids in Biology, Disease, and Delivery.
articles.abstract: Cell membranes are composed of both bilayer and nonbilayer lipids, whose molecular shape and interactions support or oppose their packing into flat bilayer sheets. While the role of the former in maintaining membrane structural integrity is clear, a growing body of data highlights the importance of nonbilayer lipids in membrane function, including fission and fusion processes in trafficking, and the dynamics of membrane-associated proteins. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of nonbilayer lipids and their roles in membrane biology, disease, and drug delivery. First, we introduce the lipid chemistry that gives rise to intrinsic curvature and curvature elastic stress (CES), and we survey the chemical diversity of nonbilayer lipids across organelles and cell types. Second, we discuss relevant methodological advances for characterizing the physicochemical properties of nonbilayer lipids, including X-ray scattering, lipidomics, and molecular dynamics. We then examine how nonbilayer lipids contribute to membrane fusion and fission and how the CES they generate modulates membrane protein localization and function. Next, we consider how the biophysical principles governing nonbilayer lipid behavior can inform the rational design of lipid nanoparticle formulations for therapeutic delivery. Finally, we explore how cells regulate lipid intrinsic curvature as a distinct homeostatic parameter and discuss the implications of its dysregulation in liver disease, neurodegeneration, and mitochondrial dysfunction. We highlight developments in methods spanning the interface between chemistry and biology that can help investigate the function and regulation of nonbilayer lipid chemistry, with far-reaching potential to answer questions in human health, disease, and drug delivery.

articles.title: Dose-Escalated Focal Salvage High-Dose-Rate Brachytherapy and Genomic Classifier Risk Stratification in Radiorecurrent Prostate Cancer: The F-SHARP Phase I/II Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prospective data on the management of intraprostatic radiorecurrence (IPR) after definitive radiotherapy (RT) and use of genomic classifiers (GC) in this setting are limited. We hypothesized that dose-escalated focal salvage high-dose-rate brachytherapy (DE-fsHDR) would be safe and effective, and that GC would risk stratify patients who may benefit from treatment intensification.

METHODS: F-SHARP is a multi-institutional phase I/II trial of DE-fsHDR for IPR after any form of RT for localized prostate cancer. Patients received up to 30 Gy in 1-2 fractions. The primary objective was to determine the acute RT-related grade ≥3 CTCAE v4.03 genitourinary and GI toxicity rates. Secondary end points included all-grade toxicity, quality of life (QoL; EPIC-26 and International Prostate Symptom Score), disease control, and survival. GC analysis used a clinical-grade transcriptome assay (Veracyte, San Diego, CA). Time-to-event outcomes included biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS), radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS), local recurrence-free survival (LRFS), and metastasis-free survival (MFS).

RESULTS: Twenty-four participants received one fraction and 38 received two fractions (N = 62). The median follow-up was 39.4 months. No acute grade 3 toxicities occurred. Two patients (3.2%) had late grade 3 toxicity. QoL changes did not meet criteria for a minimal clinically important difference. Three-year survival rates were 62.7% (bPFS), 67.5% (rPFS), 73.0% (LRFS), and 85.9% (MFS); there were no differences between fractionation groups (all P > .05). Among 31 patients with GC results, higher scores were associated with worse bPFS, rPFS, LRFS, and MFS. All patients with GC score >0.85 (n = 4) experienced biochemical, local, and metastatic recurrence.

CONCLUSION: DE-fsHDR is a safe and effective salvage treatment for IPR. GC score is a promising prognostic tool in patients undergoing salvage local therapy for IPR and warrants further study to guide treatment intensification.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cells in diabetic kidney disease: Potential regulatory mechanisms and related signaling pathways of mesenchymal stem cells.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a severe complication of diabetes and the leading cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). However, DKD treatment remains challenging owing to its complex etiology and unclear pathogenesis. Recent reports of the anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antifibrotic, and regenerative properties of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) indicate that they may serve as potential novel treatments for kidney disease-particularly DKD. However, current MSC-based therapies for DKD are at the initial clinical stage of research with the precise underlying mechanisms requiring further investigation. Current studies have predominantly concentrated on the renal protective effects mediated by classical signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/Akt/mTOR), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad, and nuclear factor-erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), whereas other potentially relevant pathways remain insufficiently investigated. This review comprehensively discusses the key MSC-regulated signaling pathways and their therapeutic potential to provide a theoretical foundation for DKD-related drug development and its clinical translation.

articles.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease increases the risk of cardiovascular disease occurrence in nonsmokers: A nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, and patients experience a high prevalence of concomitant cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In this study, we aimed to determine whether never smokers with COPD exhibit an increased risk of CVD compared with those without COPD and whether this risk parallels that observed in smokers with COPD.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank (CKB). Spirometry was performed on all the participants, and COPD was defined as the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity (FEV 1 /FVC) <0.7. Eligible participants in our study were free of diagnosed CVDs, including ischemic heart disease, heart failure, hypertension, or atrial fibrillation at baseline. The clinical outcomes were the incidences of these 4 CVDs and their overall incidence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate the associations of COPD and smoking status with incident CVD outcomes.

RESULTS: Among all eligible participants ( n = 366,161, including 20,887 with COPD), 40,861 incident cases of CVD events were observed during a median follow-up time of 10 years. Compared with never smokers without COPD, those with COPD exhibited a significantly higher risk of overall CVD, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.23 (95% CI: 1.09-1.39) for men and 1.24 (95% CI: 1.17-1.31) for women. Among male COPD participants, the incidence rates of overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, and hypertension, but not that of heart failure, were similar between never smokers and smokers. In contrast, female COPD participants who never smoked exhibited lower risks across all cardiovascular endpoints compared with their smoking counterparts. These results remained unchanged after propensity score matching.

CONCLUSION: In never smokers, COPD per se serves as an independent risk factor for CVD. Among men with COPD, smoking exposure confers no added hazard, whereas women with COPD who smoke remain at higher risk for CVD than their never-smoking counterparts.

articles.title: Factors associated with continued use of mission health facilities in Ghana: a facility-exit survey of user perceptions.
articles.abstract: Partnerships between the state and faith-based providers, such as the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG), are crucial for expanding healthcare coverage in lower-middle-income countries. However, limited evidence exists on how communities perceive these services and what factors are associated with continued use among those who access them. We conducted a quantitative cross-sectional facility-exit survey among 799 current and past users recruited at CHAG facility exits across four regions between October and December 2024. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire guided by the Sustainability of Innovation Framework. Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, and exploratory multivariable logistic regression evaluated factors associated with continued use of CHAG facilities among existing users. Among this facility-exit sample, continued use was remarkably high (94.1%) and 95.1% preferred mission facilities over alternatives. Geographic access and socioeconomic status were not significantly associated with continued use patterns (P > .05), though this finding reflects the sampling strategy that over-represents users and should not be interpreted as community-level prevalence. Perceptual factors dominated the exploratory regression analysis: positive self-rated health (AOR = 3.88, 95% CI: 1.98-7.63), perceived service quality (AOR = 7.48, 95% CI: 3.46-16.18), and feeling safe at the facility (AOR = 9.12, 95% CI: 4.36-19.08) were exploratorily associated with continued use. These effect sizes should be interpreted with caution given the near-complete separation in the outcome (94% users) and the small number of non-users (n = 47), which may inflate odds ratios in logistic regression. Objective factors, paying fees and medication stock-outs were not significant in the adjusted model (P > .05). Among non-users (n = 47), key barriers were high cost and service unavailability. Continued use of state-faith-based partnership facilities are exploratorily associated with trust rooted in perceived quality, safety, and responsiveness. Persistent challenges with medication stock-outs and costs highlight areas for systemic strengthening. Future community-based research is needed to identify determinants of non-utilization and test generalizability.

articles.title: Masked Bisphosphonate Inhibitors of Acid Sphingomyelinase: Improved Cell Penetration and Potency.
articles.abstract: Inhibitors of acid sphingomyelinase (ASM) with nanomolar in cellulo activity were developed by masking the amino bisphosphonate inhibitor ARC39. ASM is a key enzyme catalyzing the hydrolysis of sphingomyelin to ceramide, which plays a role in various physiological and pathological processes. Inhibitors of ASM have been proposed as potential treatment for disorders such as cancer and metastasis, acute lung injury, sepsis, atherosclerosis, and major depression. Despite the vital interest in ASM as a drug target, potent inhibitors of this enzyme are still urgently needed. The masked ARC39 derivatives developed in this study are 100 times more potent than the parent compound. Their properties such as cell uptake, stability, etc. were thoroughly investigated.

articles.title: NRG-BR002: A Randomized Phase II/III Trial of Metastasis-Directed Ablation With First-Line Systemic Therapy for Oligometastatic Breast Cancer.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Metastasis-directed therapy is increasingly used for oligometastatic breast cancer, despite its uncertain benefit during first-line systemic therapy. We evaluated whether metastasis-directed ablation improves progression-free survival (PFS) compared with first-line systemic therapy alone in patients with oligometastatic breast cancer.

METHODS: NRG-BR002 is a randomized phase II/III trial across US/Canadian institutions. Participants had ≤4 metastases, controlled primary disease, ≤12 months of first-line systemic therapy without progression with all visible metastases amenable to stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) or surgical resection and were randomly assigned 1:1 to systemic therapy alone (no ablation) or with metastasis-directed ablation (ablation). The primary end point was PFS, defined as time to progression or death. Secondary end points included overall survival (OS) and toxicity. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) were evaluated as exploratory biomarkers.

RESULTS: From December 2014 to September 2019, 129 patients were enrolled; 125 were eligible for analysis. Median age was 54 years; 79% had hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2‑negative disease, 60% solitary metastasis, 50% bone involvement, and 37% bone only. Ablation was delivered via SBRT for 93%. With 72 PFS events and a median follow-up of 29.9 months, median PFS was 23.0 months (no ablation) versus 19.5 months (ablation; hazard ratio [HR], 0.92 [70% CI, 0.71 to 1.17; 95% CI, 0.57 to 1.47]; one-sided P = .36; stratified P = .42). Thus, the trial did not proceed to phase III. OS did not differ significantly between arms (HR, 1.07 [95% CI, 0.60 to 1.89]; one-sided P = .41; stratified P = .52). No grade 5 toxicities occurred. Exploratory analysis suggested improved PFS with ablation in patients with low or absent pretreatment CTCs.

CONCLUSION: The addition of metastasis-directed ablation added to first-line systemic therapy did not improve PFS or OS in patients with oligometastatic breast cancer. Ablation should not be routinely used outside of clinical trials, except for palliation.

articles.title: Sitagliptin for Acute Graft-Versus-Host Disease Prevention in Alternative Donor Transplantation: A Randomized Phase III Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This trial evaluated whether the addition of sitagliptin to antithymocyte globulin (ATG)-based prophylaxis reduces the incidence of acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) after alternative donor hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.

METHODS: This prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial enrolled patients age 18-60 years with hematologic malignancies who received myeloablative conditioning haploidentical or unrelated donor transplantation. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to ATG-based prophylaxis (ATG + calcineurin inhibitor + methotrexate + mycophenolate mofetil) with or without sitagliptin (600 mg orally once every 12 hours, days -1 to +14). The primary end point was the cumulative incidence of grade 2-4 aGVHD by day +100.

RESULTS: From December 22, 2021, to June 16, 2023, 190 of the 251 screened patients were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 29.8 (0.7-41.3) months. The sitagliptin group had a significantly lower incidence of grade 2-4 aGVHD on day +100 (14.7% v 31.6%; subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 0.41; P = .005). Reduced grade 3-4 (6.3% v 18.9%; sHR, 0.30; P = .010) and intestinal aGVHD (12.6% v 29.5%; P = .004) and superior day +180 GVHD-free, relapse-free survival (GRFS; 86.3% v 72.6%; HR, 0.44; P = .016) were also observed. No between-group disparities were detected in 2-year chronic GVHD, nonrelapse mortality, relapse-free/overall survival, or cytomegalovirus/Epstein-Barr virus reactivation; the adverse event profiles were similar.

CONCLUSION: In this randomized trial, adjunct sitagliptin to ATG-containing prophylaxis significantly reduced the incidence of grade 2-4 aGVHD. Reductions in severe and intestinal aGVHD, as well as improved day +180 GRFS, were exploratory observations; no significant benefits were detected for long-term GRFS, overall survival, or RFS, and treatment did not alter the engraftment, relapse, or infection risk.

articles.title: Aid cuts, health financing fragility, and maladaptive resilience in Sierra Leone: a rapid mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract: Sierra Leone's health system remains highly dependent on external aid, with donor funding accounting for ∼47% of total health expenditure between 2020 and 2024, compared with a government contribution of ∼25%-26%. Recent reductions in development assistance for health, including a sharp in-year contraction of United States Agency for International Development-supported health programming during 2024-25 and an ∼15% reduction in Global Fund allocations, have exposed major structural vulnerabilities in the health financing system. We conducted a rapid mixed-methods study to examine the effects of recent and anticipated aid reductions and the resilience responses emerging across Sierra Leone's health system. The study drew on a review of 19 documents and 11 key informant interviews with stakeholders from government, development partners, civil society, non-governmental organizations, and independent experts. Documentary and interview data were analysed descriptively and thematically, and findings were integrated during interpretation. Several service areas were identified as highly exposed to financing disruption, including reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health, human immunodeficiency virus, tuberculosis, immunization, and pharmaceutical supply chains. However, available evidence indicates that immediate service disruptions have so far been limited, and current data do not support firm conclusions about which services have been most affected. Maternal health and immunization indicators remained comparatively stable in the short term. Documents and interviewees indicated that absorptive responses have prioritized core commodities and selected priority services while reducing expenditure on outreach, supervision, training, logistics, and other enabling functions. Interviewees reported that households were absorbing much of the financial burden through increased out-of-pocket spending, forgone care, and informal coping mechanisms. Sierra Leone's response shows elements of absorptive and adaptive resilience, but several coping strategies show features consistent with maladaptive resilience and risk becoming maladaptive if prolonged, because they shift costs downward, threaten to deepen inequity, and erode the operational foundations of the health system.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of the Japan Narrow-Band Imaging Expert Team and pit pattern classifications for small polyps using next-generation endoscopy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optical diagnosis of small colorectal lesions is important for the potential implementation of "resect-and-discard" and "leave-in-situ" strategies. We evaluated the performance of the Japan Narrow-Band Imaging Expert Team (JNET) and pit pattern classifications in differentiating small adenomatous and serrated colorectal lesions using a modern high-definition endoscopy system (EVIS X1), with outcomes stratified by endoscopist expertise.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of the prospective multicenter deTXIon trial included 1830 colorectal lesions for JNET evaluation, of which 93.0 % measured < 10 mm, and 1601 lesions for pit pattern evaluation. Adenocarcinomas were excluded. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and likelihood ratios were calculated. To account for multiple lesions within the same patient, 95 %CIs were estimated using a cluster bootstrap approach with patients as the resampling unit. Exploratory expert-nonexpert differences in sensitivity, specificity, and negative predictive value (NPV) were also estimated.

RESULTS: JNET showed high diagnostic performance, with no clear differences between expert and nonexpert endoscopists in sensitivity, specificity, or NPV. For pit pattern classification, expert-nonexpert differences were 5.01 percentage points for sensitivity (95 %CI 1.23 to 9.08) and 10.00 percentage points for NPV (95 %CI 1.37 to 18.56).

CONCLUSIONS: JNET showed similar observed diagnostic performance across expertise levels, whereas pit pattern classification showed greater between-group differences in sensitivity and NPV. These findings suggest that JNET may serve as a practical framework for routine optical diagnosis of small lesions.

articles.title: Non-invasive tests for early-stage liver fibrosis: Current advances and challenges.
articles.abstract: Early-stage liver fibrosis (F1-F2) constitutes a clinically silent yet pivotal phase during which therapeutic intervention may halt or reverse disease progression. However, its timely identification remains challenging given the limited sensitivity of currently non-invasive tests (NITs), including routine serological panels and elastography-based techniques. This review provides a comprehensive and systematic evaluation of the evolving diagnostic landscape aimed at addressing this unmet need. Established approaches are critically appraised alongside emerging next-generation NITs, including ultrasensitive serum biomarkers, molecular imaging probes targeting fibrogenic activity, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven analysis of conventional imaging modalities. In addition, this review examines innovative diagnostic strategies based on alternative biofluids, including urine, exhaled breath, and saliva, as well as gut microbiota-derived biomarkers and multiomics-integrated models, all of which offer distinct pathophysiological insights and potential advantages in large-scale screening. Despite their considerable promise for improving the precision of early-stage fibrosis detection, these approaches face substantial barriers to clinical implementation, including challenges related to validation, standardization, and integration into existing diagnostic pathways. Addressing these limitations will be essential for establishing a robust, multidimensional diagnostic framework capable of enabling early detection, guiding timely intervention, and advancing the paradigm of hepatology toward effective disease prevention.

articles.title: The unintended consequences of health policy processes: a qualitative systematic review of experience with the 2007 occupation-specific dispensation (OSD) strategy in the South African public nursing sector.
articles.abstract: Health policies inevitably produce unintended consequences when introduced into a health system. These consequences can be linked to factors occurring before and throughout a policy's development and implementation. Understanding unintended consequences in relation to these factors can help mitigate its unintended health system impact. Current literature reveals a paucity of information exploring this interaction. Examining the 2007 Occupation-Specific Dispensation (OSD) strategy for nurses in South Africa can help fill this gap. We conducted a health policy analysis exploring the relationship between unintended consequences and the factors which occur in a policy process using a qualitative systematic review and applying a longitudinal lens. We included literature relating to the 2007 OSD in nursing and human resources for health (HRH) from 1994 onwards. In data analysis, we applied the Walt and Gilson (Reforming the health sector in developing countries: the central role of policy analysis. Health Policy Plan 1994;9:353-70.) Health Policy Analysis (HPA) Triangle to (1) give an overall description of the OSD policy process in the nursing sector; (2) identify the main unintended health system consequences of the policy for nurses; and (3) investigate the relationship between the unintended consequences of the 2007 OSD and its relevant contributing factors occurring before, during, and after the OSD's development and implementation. Three main unintended consequences were identified: nursing demoralization, nursing division, and a breakdown in the relationship between nursing managers and frontline staff. Our findings suggest that the relationship between unintended consequences and its relevant contributing factors are rooted in the historical and socio-political realities of the health system. Frontline-level actors can help mitigate potential unintended consequences through sharing their historical and socio-political insight. We therefore urge policymakers to include these actors in policy development and implementation processes. Future research should explore the inclusion of frontline knowledge in policy processes as a method to reduce the potential severity and/or number of unintended consequences experienced.

articles.title: Changing patterns and regional inequalities of asthma burden and attributable risks in China, 1990-2023.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The national and subnational burden of asthma in China remains insufficiently characterized. We aimed to assess the long-term trends in asthma burden and associated risk factors across China from 1990 to 2023.

METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study, we assessed asthma deaths, prevalence, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) in China and its provincial-level administrative regions from 1990 to 2023, stratified by age and sex. Decomposition analyses were conducted to quantify the contributions of demographic changes and level 2 risk factors to changes in the asthma burden estimates.

RESULTS: Between 1990 and 2023, the age-standardized asthma death rate (95% uncertainty interval [UI]) in China declined from 2.4 (1.1-4.0) to 1.1 (0.7-2.0) per 100,000, while the age-standardized prevalence rate (95% UI) increased from 2902.7 (2392.7-3550.4) to 3066.8 (2529.4-3675.7) per 100,000. Age-standardized DALY rates decreased overall, with years lived with disability (YLDs) accounting for an increasing proportion of total DALYs. Substantial provincial heterogeneity was also observed. Tobacco use remained the leading contributor to the asthma burden, particularly among males, whereas the contribution of high body mass index (BMI) increased steadily. Population aging was the main driver of changes in asthma mortality, while increasing exposure to high BMI drove increases in DALYs.

CONCLUSIONS: Asthma mortality in China has declined substantially, but the non-fatal burden continues to rise, driven by increasing prevalence and metabolic risk factors. Integrated strategies targeting both respiratory risk factors and metabolic risks are required to reduce asthma-related disabilities, especially in high-burden regions.

articles.title: Twisted Benzothiazole Functionalized Boranils for Reversible Emission Modulation and Anthracene Assisted White Light Emission.
articles.abstract: Modification of boranils with dual state emissions in solution and solid states have been targeted by introducing free amine functional group at the terminal position. Herein, we designed and synthesized four new primary amine-substituted benzothiazole-based boranils from substituted salicylaldehyde. Their photophysical properties were investigated through steady-state absorption and emission measurements in both solution- and solid-states. X-ray structure analysis of the boranils revealed that the benzothiazole rings bearing the amine functional group are highly twisted, thereby avoiding the detrimental exciton interaction between the dimers and enabling emission in the solid state. In the solution-state, the naphthalene and methoxy substituted boranils exhibited significant intramolecular charge transfer and a large Stokes shift of > 150 nm. Julolidine or diethylamine substituted boranils exhibited reversible acid-base responsiveness via fluorescence ON-OFF properties. On the other hand, protonation and deprotonation of naphthalene and methoxy substituted boranils showed reversible blue and red shift emission. Computational studies revealed that the photo-induced electron transfer (PET) and photo-induced charge transfer (PICT) process were responsible for fluorescence enhancement and wavelength shift upon trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) treatment. Based on the solvent dependent wide emissive range, methoxy substituted boranil was further utilized for the generation of white light emission with anthracene as an ancillary component.

articles.title: Salvage Hypofractionated Accelerated Versus Standard Radiotherapy for Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy: A Phase III Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare hypofractionated radiotherapy (RT) with conventional RT for treating biochemical recurrence following radical prostatectomy.

METHODS: Between 2019 and 2021, 316 patients with intermediate- to high-risk prostate cancer were randomly assigned to receive salvage RT with either 65 Gy in 26 fractions (hypofractionated RT, HYPO) or 66 Gy in 33 fractions (conventional RT, CONV). RT was delivered to the prostate bed, with elective pelvic nodal irradiation performed at the discretion of radiation oncologists. Intensity-modulated RT with daily image guidance was used. The primary end point was biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS). Secondary end points included distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (CSS), toxicity profiles, and patient-reported quality-of-life.

RESULTS: One hundred fifty-one patients (51.2%) received androgen deprivation therapy, and 202 (68.5%) underwent elective nodal irradiation. Endorectal balloons were used in 186 men (63.1%). The median pre-RT prostate-specific antigen level was 0.36 ng/mL (IQR, 0.24-0.49 ng/mL). After a median follow-up of 52.6 months, the 4-year bPFS rates were 80.1% and 78.1% in the HYPO and CONV arms, respectively. There were no significant differences in DMFS (91.7% v 91.0%) and CSS (100% v 100%). The 4-year cumulative incidence of grade ≥2 GI toxicity was higher in the HYPO arm (7.9% v 0.7%), predominantly among patients without an endorectal balloon; all cases were resolved by the last follow-up. Patient-reported quality-of-life outcomes were comparable.

CONCLUSION: bPFS was not superior in the HYPO arm at 4 years. However, given the comparable oncologic outcomes, toxicity profiles, and quality-of-life measures, hypofractionated RT may be considered a viable alternative in the salvage setting. Further research is needed to determine whether the use of an endorectal balloon reduces GI toxicity.

articles.title: Effect of micropulse trans-scleral cyclophotocoagulation (MP-TSCPC) on aqueous humour dynamics in patients with glaucoma and ocular hypertension: an observational study.
Regional-specific retinal ischaemic index guided by ultra-widefield fluorescein angiography correlates with macular oedema in retinal vein occlusion.
Keep calm and think twice: methodological issues with the recommendations by Giordano (2025).
Muscle, liver and kidney biomarkers in military training: a 37-week comparative study of dropouts and finalists.
Sensitisation patterns and burden of uncontrolled respiratory allergy symptoms in military personnel.
