Emerging Burden and Inequalities of Pediatric Cardiovascular Disease Beyond Congenital Heart Disease: Implications for China.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital heart disease (CHD) has dominated pediatric cardiovascular research, with survival increasing. However, the burden of pediatric noncongenital cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains poorly characterized, with epidemiologic patterns diverging from those of CHD.

OBJECTIVES: The authors aimed to define the changing epidemiology and inequalities of pediatric noncongenital CVD and subcategories from 1990 to 2021.

METHODS: We used GBD (Global Burden of Disease Study) 2021 to characterize deaths, disability-adjusted life years, prevalence, and incidence of pediatric noncongenital CVD and subcategories by age, sex, and region. Temporal trends were assessed using average annual percent change. Health inequalities were characterized using concentration indexes and curves.

RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, death rates of pediatric noncongenital CVD declined globally, whereas prevalence and incidence rates increased. Estimates of CHD burden declined over the same period. In China, death and prevalence rates declined alongside rising sociodemographic index (SDI) levels. Stroke had the highest death rate, disproportionately affecting lower-SDI countries and neonates. Rheumatic heart disease showed the highest prevalence and incidence rates, especially in children aged ≥5 years, with deaths and prevalence concentrated in most lower-SDI countries. Cardiomyopathy and myocarditis, and nonrheumatic valvular heart disease were disproportionately concentrated in higher-SDI countries. Neonates had the highest death and disability-adjusted life year rates. Adolescents (15-19 years) showed the highest prevalence and incidence rates. Sex disparities varied across subcategories.

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric noncongenital CVD is characterized by declining death rates but increasing prevalence and incidence rates, alongside persistent inequalities. Epidemiologic data remain limited for certain subcategories. Integrating noncongenital CVD into pediatric cardiovascular research, surveillance, and prevention is needed.

articles.title: Effect of Perioperative Glutamine Supplementation on Acute Kidney Injury in Infants Undergoing Elective Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Objective: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in infants after cardiac surgery. Glutamine (GLN), a conditionally essential amino acid, has demonstrated renoprotective potential in animal models and has been shown to attenuate biomarkers of kidney damage in high-risk patients undergoing cardiac surgery. However, whether these renoprotective benefits extend to pediatric patients remains unknown. Methods: We conducted a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in infants and young children younger than 3 years undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass. Ninety-four patients were randomly assigned to receive intravenous alanyl-glutamine (0.4 g/kg/day, n = 47) or 0.9% saline placebo (n = 47), administered from anesthesia induction and continued for 4 consecutive days (the day of surgery and the first 3 postoperative days). The primary outcome was the incidence of AKI within 72 h postoperatively, defined according to the KDIGO criteria. Secondary outcomes included the requirement for peritoneal dialysis (PD), diuretic use, serum creatinine (Scr), neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), cystatin C, procalcitonin, and the lengths of ICU and hospital stay. Results: The incidence of KDIGO-defined AKI was lower in the GLN group than in the control group (14.9% vs. 40.4%; p = 0.010). Among the prespecified secondary outcomes, the requirement for PD (0% vs. 12.8%; p = 0.026) and diuretic use (6.4% vs. 23.4%; p = 0.040) were also lower in the GLN group. Postoperative NGAL concentrations were lower in the GLN group at 24, 48, and 72 h (p < 0.050 for each time point). No significant differences were observed in the lengths of ICU or hospital stay. Conclusions: In this single-center trial, perioperative GLN supplementation was associated with a lower incidence of postoperative AKI, a lower requirement for PD, and less diuretic use in infants undergoing elective cardiac surgery. These exploratory findings support a possible renoprotective role for GLN in this high-risk population but require confirmation in larger multicenter trials before adoption into clinical practice.

articles.title: Exploratory Plasma Multiomic Profiles Associated with Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Severe Aortic Stenosis.
articles.abstract: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are progressive disorders associated with high morbidity and mortality. CKD accelerates AS progression and, when both conditions coexist, significantly worsens clinical outcomes. Therefore, characterizing circulating molecular differences associated with CKD in patients with AS may help define the molecular phenotype of this high-risk comorbidity. Plasma samples from patients with AS, with and without CKD, were analyzed through a multiomics approach using PASEF technology. Results were processed and analyzed using the bioinformatics tool Metascape to select two proteins with high potential as biomarkers: pantetheinase or vanin 1 (VNN1) and alpha 1 acid glycoprotein (A1AG1). These proteins were verified in an independent cohort of samples using immunodetection. Our findings show differences in the circulating proteomic and metabolomic profiles of patients with AS with and without CKD, suggesting that inflammation, oxidative stress and lipid metabolism are associated with CKD in this setting. These exploratory findings describe CKD-associated circulating proteomic and metabolomic differences in severe AS and provide hypotheses for validation in larger, appropriately controlled and longitudinal cohorts. These studies, which simultaneously examine multiple comorbidities, lay the groundwork for personalized medicine strategies, paving the way for more effective patient management.

articles.title: Combined Mitral and Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair: Evidence, Patient Selection, and Procedural Strategy.
articles.abstract: Concomitant mitral regurgitation (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) constitute an interconnected multivalvular syndrome, but correction of MR does not consistently reverse TR. This narrative review examines TR evolution after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), patient selection, imaging, procedural strategies, and evidence for treatment of both valves. Combined TEER denotes bivalvular treatment, performed during the same session or in stages. Observational cohorts report TR improvement in approximately one-third of broadly selected patients after M-TEER, with substantial variation according to baseline severity, response definition, and follow-up. Persistent or new-onset TR is associated with adverse outcomes; these associations do not establish that subsequent tricuspid intervention improves survival. Comparative registries suggest potential clinical benefit from combined treatment, whereas uncontrolled series primarily establish technical feasibility in selected patients at experienced centers. Treatment timing remains uncertain because randomized comparisons of isolated, same-session, and staged strategies are unavailable. The proposed Heart Team framework integrates lesion-specific indications, anatomical suitability, anticipated TR reversibility, physiological reserve, and patient goals. It is an unvalidated discussion aid rather than a treatment recommendation. Randomized strategy trials are needed to establish incremental clinical benefit, comparative safety, and optimal timing.

articles.title: Modified Venous Excess Ultrasound (mVExUS) Grades and CA125 Levels in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Background and Objectives: Systemic venous congestion is a key feature of acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF). Carbohydrate antigen-125 (CA125) is a biomarker of congestion, whereas venous excess ultrasound provides a noninvasive assessment of systemic venous congestion. We evaluated the association between CA125 and congestion severity assessed by a modified venous excess ultrasound (mVExUS) protocol in patients hospitalized with ADHF. Materials and Methods: This single-center observational study included 112 consecutive patients with ADHF. mVExUS was based on inferior vena cava diameter and hepatic and portal venous Doppler patterns. mVExUS was evaluable in 108 patients, CA125 was available in 106, and 102 had both measurements. The full mVExUS spectrum was examined; grade 3 versus grades 0-2 was used for regression and discrimination analyses. Results: Median CA125 concentrations across mVExUS grades 0, 1, 2, and 3 were 63 (17-210), 61 (20-127), 48.5 (21.5-60), and 151 (88.8-331.8) U/mL, respectively (p < 0.001). Ordinal mVExUS grade correlated with CA125 (ρ = 0.42, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, eGFR, atrial fibrillation, and severe tricuspid regurgitation, ln (CA125) remained associated with mVExUS grade 3 (adjusted OR 2.73, 95% CI 1.56-4.77; p < 0.001). CA125 showed moderate discrimination for grade 3 congestion (AUC 0.790, 95% CI 0.704-0.873); a threshold of 73 U/mL yielded 80.4% sensitivity and 69.6% specificity. Grade 3 patients also had a longer hospital stay (11 (9-15) vs. 7 (6-12) days; p = 0.001). Conclusions: Higher CA125 levels were associated with severe mVExUS-defined systemic venous congestion. CA125 and mVExUS may provide complementary information, although the derived threshold requires external validation.

articles.title: Reprogramming and Epigenetic Modifications: Unraveling the Role of Histone Lactylation in Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Lactylation links cellular metabolism to histone regulation and nonhistone protein function; however, its functional consequences in atherosclerosis depend on the modified substrate, target residue, cell type, and disease stage. This narrative review distinguishes direct atherosclerosis evidence from cardiovascular but non-atherosclerosis evidence and cross-disease mechanistic context, framing mechanistic claims accordingly. Direct evidence in atherosclerosis implicates several pathogenic pathways, including endothelial H3K18 lactylation at NF-κB pathway and SNAI1 promoters, SLC22A6- and ACSS1-driven H3K9 lactylation, lactate- and AARS1-dependent FOXO1 lactylation under atheroprone flow, H4K12 lactylation at CDKN1A during endothelial senescence, and an H3K18 lactylation-METTL3 axis in macrophage ferroptosis. Conversely, direct evidence also supports atheroprotective pathways, notably nonhistone MeCP2 K271 lactylation in endothelial cells and macrophages. Observations from myocardial repair, valvular and medial calcification, aortic aneurysm, pulmonary hypertension, and oncology provide mechanistic context rather than direct proof of plaque-specific biology. Furthermore, we examine the interplay between lactylation and acetylation, methylation, and RNA modifications-including scenarios where lactylation functions upstream of acetylation-and critically evaluate the capabilities and limitations of current analytical methods. Key methodological considerations include lactyl-donor stoichiometry and site occupancy; antibody cross-reactivity; resolution of L-lactyl, D-lactyl, and carboxyethyl lysine isomers; mass-spectrometric site localization; chromatin profiling against matched acetylation controls; and stable-isotope tracing. Finally, we propose an integrative translational framework that pairs peripheral mononuclear cell and plaque sampling with single-cell and spatial multi-omics, strictly distinguishing lactate sensing from site-specific protein lactylation detection. To date, no clinically validated lactylation biomarker or lactylation-targeted therapy exists for atherosclerosis, and lactate abundance cannot be conflated with protein lactylation. Clinical translation ultimately requires site-specific causal validation in plaque-relevant models and prospective human cohorts.

articles.title: Systemic and Pulmonary Hemodynamic Tolerability of Escalating Intravenous Epoprostenol Infusion in Isoflurane-Anesthetized Healthy Dogs.
articles.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
articles.abstract: Continuous intravenous epoprostenol (prostacyclin, PGI2) is a cornerstone therapy for severe human pulmonary arterial hypertension, yet its hemodynamic safety profile in dogs remains incompletely defined. This study evaluated the systemic and pulmonary hemodynamic responses and acute tolerability of continuous intravenous epoprostenol titration in healthy, isoflurane-anesthetized dogs as a prerequisite for future pulmonary hypertension trials. Eight healthy beagle dogs were instrumented for invasive arterial and pulmonary arterial monitoring and received sequential escalating epoprostenol infusions at 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20 ng/kg/min (Epo1-Epo20; 30 min per step), followed by a 20 min washout period. All dogs completed the protocol without major complications. Systemic arterial pressures decreased in a dose-dependent manner, reaching statistical significance only at Epo20 (p < 0.05), without inducing clinically overt hypotension (mean arterial pressure < 60 mmHg). Cardiac output was preserved throughout, supported by a non-significant numerical increase in stroke volume (up to 25%) alongside a numerical reduction in systemic vascular resistance (up to 28%) and unchanged heart rate. Pulmonary arterial pressures, pulmonary vascular resistance, and oxygen delivery remained unchanged, whereas hemoglobin decreased modestly at Epo15 and Epo20 (p < 0.05). In conclusion, intravenous epoprostenol up to 20 ng/kg/min was systemically tolerated without overt hypotension, although pulmonary vasodilatory efficacy requires evaluation in dogs with pulmonary hypertension.

articles.title: Systemic immune-inflammation index for predicting pre-operative deep vein thrombosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a composite biomarker reflecting thrombo-inflammatory status. Its diagnostic performance for preoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of SII for identifying preoperative DVT.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched up to October 16, 2025, for observational studies examining SII and preoperative DVT. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality. Pooled diagnostic accuracy measures, including area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity, were calculated using random-effects models. Meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed.

RESULTS: Five retrospective cohort studies involving 4,097 patients were included. The pooled AUC of SII for predicting preoperative DVT was 0.671 (95% CI: 0.595-0.748). The pooled sensitivity was 0.591 (95% CI: 0.487-0.688), and pooled specificity was 0.780 (95% CI: 0.682-0.854). Formal tests did not suggest substantial publication bias, although their power was limited by the small number of studies. Exploratory meta-regression suggested that mean age may influence diagnostic performance, with higher accuracy observed in older populations. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results, and no substantial publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: SII may be a potential adjunctive biomarker for preoperative DVT in selected orthopedic populations, but evidence is limited by retrospective designs, geographic restriction, clinical heterogeneity, and variable cutoffs. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

articles.title: Short- and intermediate-term outcomes of microaxial flow pump-assisted versus standard-care PCI in high-risk patients: A propensity score-matched analysis.
articles.journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence comparing short- and intermediate-term outcomes after microaxial flow pump-assisted versus standard-care high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is limited. We compared major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) through 24 months and explored treatment-effect subgroups.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre retrospective propensity score-matched study of 290 patients (145 per group). Propensity scores were estimated using 31 baseline covariates, and 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching without replacement was used to estimate the average treatment effect in treated patients. MACE comprised all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, or stroke/transient ischaemic attack. Arms were compared using Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence and absolute risk differences at 30 days, 12 months and 24 months. The cohort included elective cases (20.7%), acute coronary syndromes (79.3%) and pre-procedural cardiogenic shock (20.0%); outcomes were also analysed separately in patients with and without cardiogenic shock.

RESULTS: Cumulative MACE incidence with pump support versus standard care was 26.2% versus 17.9% at 30 days (risk difference 8.3%, 95% CI 0.1% to 16.6%), 38.8% versus 30.6% at 12 months (8.3%, -3.1% to 19.4%), and 44.6% versus 39.1% at 24 months (5.4%, -5.7% to 18.0%; log-rank P = 0.206). 63 of the 64 MACE events within 30 days were deaths. The 30-day difference was confined to patients without cardiogenic shock (20.7% versus 6.9%; risk difference 13.8%, 95% CI 5.2% to 22.0%), with no difference in those presenting in shock (48.3% versus 62.1%; -13.8%, -41.4% to 14.3%).

CONCLUSIONS: Microaxial flow pump-assisted PCI was not associated with lower MACE at any time point. MACE at 30 days, almost entirely due to death, was more frequent with pump support, particularly in patients without cardiogenic shock. These observational findings do not support routine prophylactic device use.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) has emerged as an alternative to oral anticoagulation (OAC) for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. However, the comparative effectiveness and safety of LAAO versus contemporary OAC, particularly direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), remain uncertain. We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing LAAO with OAC, incorporating both vitamin K antagonist- and DOAC-based studies, with prespecified subgroup analyses of DOAC-treated populations and an exploratory analysis in patients with chronic kidney disease. We included 26 studies (6 randomized controlled trials and 20 observational studies) comprising 106,947 participants, with a mean age of 74.2 years. Follow-up ranged from 3 months to 5 years. Compared with DOACs, LAAO was not associated with a statistically significant difference in the primary composite outcome of ischemic stroke, major bleeding, systemic embolism, all-cause mortality, and cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.47-1.07; P = 0.09; I2 = 80%). No significant differences were observed in ischemic stroke or major bleeding compared with overall OAC or DOAC therapy. LAAO was nevertheless associated with significantly lower risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality compared with both overall OAC and DOAC therapy.

articles.title: Evolution of POCUS in the NICU: From a diagnostic tool to an extension of clinical examination.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly transforming neonatal intensive care practice from a discrete diagnostic modality into an extension of the bedside clinical examination. Compared to traditional monitoring tools, POCUS provides rapid, real-time physiologic and anatomic information that may improve diagnostic precision, procedural safety, and individualized clinical decision-making in critically ill neonates. Over the past decade, expanding evidence and international consensus guidelines have supported a growing range of neonatal POCUS applications, including lung ultrasound for respiratory distress and pneumothorax, targeted cardiac assessment, bowel ultrasound for necrotizing enterocolitis, vascular access guidance, and evaluation of the acutely decompensating infant. Structured protocols such as SAFE-R, the Crashing Neonate Protocol, STEP, and NeoSONAR have further advanced the integration of ultrasound into neonatal emergency assessment and resuscitation. In parallel, formal recommendations from organizations including the European Society of Pediatric and Neonatal Intensive Care, the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American Society of Echocardiography, and the National Neonatal POCUS Collaborative have accelerated the development of standardized training, credentialing, and quality assurance frameworks. This narrative review summarizes the evolving role of POCUS in neonatology, reviews current evidence supporting diagnostic and procedural applications, discusses emerging protocols for emergency and resuscitative care, and explores future directions including advanced training pathways, artificial intelligence integration, research interests, competency-based education and standardized training.

articles.title: Venous sinus stenting vs. shunting in idiopathic intracranial hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is characterized by raised intracranial pressure and may result in disabling headache and irreversible visual impairment. Venous sinus stenting (VSS) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunting are established interventions for medically refractory disease, but comparative evidence remains limited. We aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of VSS versus CSF shunting in patients with IIH.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library from inception through June 2026 for comparative studies evaluating VSS versus CSF shunting in IIH. Outcomes included treatment failure, repeat surgical treatment, papilledema resolution, residual papilledema, headache resolution, and overall complications. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences (RDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a Hartung-Knapp-adjusted random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Ten retrospective comparative studies were included. VSS was associated with significantly fewer overall complications than shunting (OR = 0.17, 95% CI 0.03-0.96; P = 0.04). For headache resolution, VSS was associated with higher odds of resolution, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (OR = 1.50, 95% CI 0.87-2.59; P = 0.098). No significant differences were observed in treatment failure (OR = 0.40, 95% CI 0.00-306.94; P = 0.33), repeat surgical treatment (OR = 0.70, 95% CI 0.22-2.19; P = 0.39), papilledema resolution (OR = 1.66, 95% CI 0.84-3.29; P = 0.10), or residual papilledema (OR = 1.00, 95% CI 0.42-2.39; P = 0.99).

CONCLUSIONS: VSS may provide a favorable safety profile compared with CSF shunting in appropriately selected patients with IIH, with a possible advantage in headache resolution that did not reach statistical significance in the primary analysis. However, uncertainty remains regarding treatment durability and ophthalmologic outcomes. Prospective comparative studies are needed to better define the relative benefits, risks, and long-term effectiveness of VSS and CSF shunting.

articles.title: Cardiovascular outcomes and mortality risk associated with GLP-1 RAs vs. SGLT-2 inhibitors in patients with incident lung cancer: A target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to evaluate whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), as compared to sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors, confer superior cardioprotective benefits and reduce all-cause mortality in patients with incident lung cancer.

METHODS: Using the TriNetX global federated database, we emulated a target trial comparing the initiation of GLP-1 RAs versus SGLT-2 inhibitors in patients with incident lung cancer. To minimize confounding, we employed 1:1 propensity score matching to balance baseline demographics and clinical comorbidities. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).

RESULTS: A total of 5,206 patients with incident lung cancer were identified, including 1,400 initiators of GLP-1 RAs and 3,806 initiators of SGLT-2 inhibitors. After 1:1 propensity score matching, which yielded two balanced cohorts, the use of GLP-1 RAs was associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.68; 95% CI, 0.57 to 0.80) and MACE (HR 0.71; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.82) compared with SGLT-2 inhibitors. Regarding secondary outcomes, GLP-1 RA initiation was also associated with a reduced risk of heart failure incidence (HR 0.60; 95% CI, 0.51 to 0.70) and all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.75; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.84).

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with incident lung cancer, the initiation of GLP-1 RAs was associated with a significantly lower risk of all-cause mortality and MACE compared to SGLT-2 inhibitors. These findings suggest that GLP-1 RAs are associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes and a reduced risk of mortality compared to SGLT-2 inhibitors in this high-risk population. However, further large-scale prospective trials are warranted to validate these comparative pleiotropic effects.

articles.title: Prognostic significance of incident microalbuminuria in a real-world population at increased cardiovascular risk: A report from a global federated research network.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Despite growing interest in biomarker-based risk stratification for incident heart failure (HF), the prognostic value of newly detected microalbuminuria is poorly defined. This study evaluated its association with incident HF and cardiorenal outcomes in a large real-world cohort.

METHODS: A total of 985,367 patients aged 40-80 years at increased cardiovascular (CV) risk but with no prior HF or chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage ≥3 was included from the TriNetX Global Research Network. Patients with persistent normoalbuminuria (UACR <30 mg/g) were compared to those with newly detected microalbuminuria (UACR 30-300 mg/g). The primary outcome was a composite of incident HF or all-cause mortality over a maximum 5-year follow-up. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: After matching, 150,250 patients were included in each group. Over a median follow-up of 2.5 [IQR range, 3.6] years, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.25-1.34]), as well as higher incident HF (HR 1.31 [95% CI 1.26-1.36]), all-cause mortality (HR 1.43 [95% CI 1.35-1.51]), HFrEF (HR 1.61 [95% CI 1.51-1.71]), HFpEF (HR 1.37 [95% CI 1.29-1.45]), acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.33 [95% CI 1.25-1.41]), ischemic stroke (HR 1.27 [95% CI 1.20-1.35]) and increased risks of CKD progression to stage 3 (HR 2.80 [95% CI 2.67-2.93]) and stage 4 (HR 4.71 [95% CI 4.11-5.40]). In exploratory subgroup analyses, renal function showed the largest number of nominal interaction findings.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients at increased CV risk, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with higher cardiorenal risk, supporting further evaluation of UACR for early risk stratification.

articles.title: Novel Accelerated Heart Rate Index (AHRI) and cardiovascular morbidity: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Conventional sleep-derived OSA metrics incompletely capture cardiovascular (CV) risk. We evaluated the association between the novel Accelerated Heart Rate Index (AHRI) and CV morbidity.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults aged ≥40 years who underwent WatchPAT sleep studies through Clalit Health Services between 2015 and 2022. AHRI was defined as the number of heart rate acceleration events per hour of sleep. Participants were followed through December 2025 for the first occurrence of the composite of hospitalization for myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. Multivariable cause-specific Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Sensitivity analyses included Fine-Gray competing-risk models treating death as a competing event.

RESULTS: Among 26,553 participants, 2217 CV events occurred during a median follow-up of 4.47 years. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association between AHRI and the risk of CV morbidity, with the lowest risk at midrange AHRI. Compared with the midrange quartiles (Q2-Q3), both the lowest (Q1) and highest (Q4) AHRI quartiles were associated with higher risks of CV morbidity with adjusted HRs of 1.12 (95% CI 1.01-1.25) and 1.13 (1.02-1.26), respectively. Findings remained consistent in Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis. HRs were higher among individuals with moderate-to-severe OSA (pAHI ≥15 events/h, P for interaction = 0.005) and among those with high hypoxic burden (P for interaction = 0.012). Among individual outcomes, only heart failure hospitalization showed significant associations with low and high AHRI levels.

CONCLUSIONS: AHRI demonstrated a U-shaped association with CV morbidity, with both low and high AHRI independently associated with increased risk.

articles.title: Association Between Adherence to USDA MyPlate Recommendations and Chronic Health Conditions Among U.S. Adults: A Population-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases remain major causes of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with diet representing an important modifiable risk factor. This study examined associations between adherence to USDA MyPlate recommendations and chronic health conditions among U.S. adults. The authors conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the 2024 Health Information National Trends Survey 7 (HINTS7), including 7278 adults representing approximately 262 million U.S. adults. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression evaluated associations between self-reported MyPlate adherence and chronic health conditions after adjustment for demographic and socioeconomic covariates. Overall, 64.7% of respondents had never heard of MyPlate. MyPlate adherence was not significantly associated with diabetes, hypertension, or chronic lung disease. However, nonadherence was associated with greater odds of heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.97; 95% CI, 1.10-3.54). Greater confidence in one's ability to care for one's health was associated with lower odds of diabetes (aOR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.33-0.90), hypertension (aOR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.35-0.86), heart disease (aOR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.19-0.67), and chronic lung disease (aOR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.25-0.77). MyPlate awareness and adherence remain limited among U.S. adults. Improving practical nutrition guidance and health self-management while addressing socioeconomic barriers may support chronic disease prevention.

articles.title: Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals.

METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement.

RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

articles.title: Severe Hypertension in the Young: Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a modifiable risk factor for neurovascular disease that has become a more prevalent threat to brain health among younger patients. Severe hypertension can present with both systemic and neurologic features that are important diagnostic clues to recognize, but may overlap with those of vasculitis, reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, and genetic leukoencephalopathies.

RESULTS: We discuss the case of a 36-year-old man who presented with likely acute on chronic hypertension and thunderclap headaches. Evaluation demonstrated a cerebral vasculopathy, diffuse cerebral white matter changes atypical for his age, multifocal subcortical diffusion restriction, pontine hemorrhages, classic hypertensive retinopathy, nephropathy without nephritis, left ventricular hypertrophy, aortic dilation, and intracranial hypertension with papilledema, bilateral transverse sinus stenoses, and bilateral abducens palsies. Vasculopathy failed to improve with intra-arterial vasodilators. Brain biopsy did not reveal vasculitis.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the clinical and radiographic spectrum of the neurologic, ophthalmologic, and systemic findings of uncontrolled hypertension. We emphasize how, due to the absence of adaptive, protective vascular changes, consequences of hypertension may occur in younger patients despite blood pressure elevations that seem less severe in comparison to the higher elevations of older and more chronically hypertensive patients.

articles.title: FTO gene in MASLD Pathogenesis: mechanisms and clinical implications - a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has emerged as the most common chronic liver disease worldwide, affecting over 38% of the global population, and imposing profound clinical and economic burdens. While its pathogenesis is multifactorial, genetic predisposition plays a critical role, with recent genome-wide association studies identifying variants in multiple genes, including fat mass and obesity-associated (FTO). FTO functions as a central regulator of energy homeostasis, adipogenesis, and lipid metabolism through its ability to modulate messenger RNA (mRNA) methylation. The role of FTO in obesity, body fat composition, type 2 diabetes and insulin resistance has been extensively discussed. Nevertheless, the role of FTO in MASLD has been scarcely demonstrated. Increasing evidence links FTO to hepatic lipid accumulation, impaired fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and inflammatory signalling, positioning it as a key player in MASLD pathogenesis. Moreover, allele-specific associations underscore its contribution to inter-individual differences in disease susceptibility and progression. In this review, we summarize current mechanistic evidence on the direct and indirect roles of FTO in MASLD, highlight its impact on metabolic and inflammatory pathways, and discuss the therapeutic potential of targeting FTO in the context of precision medicine, especially with the limited treatment options.

articles.title: Machine learning-derived discordance between predicted mortality risk and valve surgery utilisation in infective endocarditis: a nationwide population-level analysis including injection drug use-associated disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) carries high mortality, and valve surgery is indicated in selected patients on the basis of specific clinical circumstances assessed by a multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team. Predicted mortality risk is not equivalent to surgical indication; nevertheless, how surgical utilisation is distributed across the spectrum of illness severity at the population level has not been described. We used machine learning (ML) to describe population-level variation in valve surgery utilisation across strata of predicted in-hospital mortality risk, with a secondary focus on injection drug use (IDU)-associated IE.

METHODS: We analysed adult hospitalisations with an IE diagnosis code in the National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022). Co-primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and valve surgery. Weighted multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with each outcome. Machine learning models (LASSO, random forest, and XGBoost) were trained using demographic, clinical, and hospital characteristics recorded during the hospitalisation, with temporal validation (2016-2020 training; 2021-2022 testing) and supplementary 5-fold cross-validation. Because diagnoses are recorded for the entire hospitalisation, the models were framed as retrospective, discharge-level risk classification rather than prospective prediction. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and F1 score, and SHAP analysis was used for model interpretability.

RESULTS: Among 125,100 IE hospitalisations (weighted ≈ 625,500), in-hospital mortality was 10.1% and the valve surgery rate was 8.3%. In the 2021-2022 temporal test set, the XGBoost mortality model achieved an AUROC of 0.842 (95% CI 0.836-0.848) and an AUPRC of 0.395 (event rate 11.8%), and the surgery model an AUROC of 0.857 (0.850-0.864) and an AUPRC of 0.403 (event rate 8.5%). Observed mortality increased approximately 80-fold across predicted-risk quintiles (Q1: 0.4% to Q5: 35.5%), whereas surgery rates varied only modestly (Q1: 5.6%; Q4: 10.8%; Q5: 9.5%). In SHAP analysis, mortality predictions were most strongly influenced by clinical severity markers (APR-DRG mortality risk, age, APR-DRG severity), whereas surgery predictions were most strongly influenced by age and hospital characteristics (bed size, teaching status, transfer-in), together with arrhythmia. IDU-associated IE (23.3%) had lower adjusted mortality (aOR 0.64, 95% CI 0.62-0.65) and was only weakly associated with surgery after adjustment (aOR 0.97); surgery rates were comparable between IDU and non-IDU hospitalisations at similar predicted risk. Mortality increased from 8.2% (2016) to 11.9% (2022; P-trend < 0.001), while surgery rates remained stable. Findings were unchanged after excluding APR-DRG variables.

CONCLUSION: At the population level, valve surgery utilisation in IE varied little across a wide gradient of predicted in-hospital mortality and was more closely associated with patient age and hospital characteristics than with markers of illness severity. Because administrative data cannot establish surgical indication, operability, or patient preferences, these findings describe variation in utilisation rather than under-treatment of individual patients. IDU status was not a dominant correlate of surgical utilisation once predicted risk was considered. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in clinically detailed cohorts that capture guideline-defined surgical indications.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

articles.title: Unequal Access: Sociodemographic Disparities in Sport Participation for Girls With Disabilities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite federal mandates such as Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and Section 504, girls with disabilities in the United States continue to face significant barriers to sport participation. These barriers are compounded by gender and sociodemographic factors, yet national-level data on participation remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To assess lifetime sport participation among US girls aged 12-17, comparing those with and without disabilities, and to examine how sociodemographic characteristics influence participation.

METHODS: Data were drawn from a nationally representative survey conducted by the Women's Sports Foundation (N = 2956). Descriptive statistics and binary logistic regression were used to analyze differences in sport participation by disability status and sociodemographic factors.

RESULTS: Girls with disabilities were significantly less likely to report lifetime sport participation than their nondisabled peers (51.33% vs 69.80%, P < .001). Among nondisabled girls, race, parental education, and family income were significantly associated with participation. These associations were not statistically significant among girls with disabilities, suggesting that structural barriers may outweigh individual or family-level factors.

CONCLUSION: Girls with disabilities face persistent disparities in sport participation where cultural and structural barriers persist even though legal protections exist. Addressing these gaps requires targeted interventions, expanded adaptive programs, and inclusive policies that consider both gender and disability.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes of anterior/lateral versus posterior/transforaminal single-level lumbar interbody fusion: An ACS-NSQIP analysis, 2016-2024.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Anterior/direct lateral (ALIF/DLIF) and posterior/transforaminal (PLIF/TLIF) approaches to single-level lumbar interbody fusion carry distinct early complication profiles, but national comparisons have been limited. We compared 30-day outcomes between approaches using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database.

METHODS: Single-level lumbar interbody fusions from the 2016-2024 ACS-NSQIP Participant Use Files were divided into ALIF/DLIF and PLIF/TLIF arms. Outcomes were compared using multivariable regression, 1:1 propensity score matching, and year-by-approach interaction testing.

RESULTS: Of 60,228 procedures, 17,766 (29.5%) were ALIF/DLIF and 42,462 (70.5%) were PLIF/TLIF. Deep venous thrombosis (DVT) was more common after ALIF/DLIF (0.87% vs 0.48%, P < 0.001) and undergoing ALIF/DLIF independently predicted DVT (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.45-2.23); this remained significant after matching (OR 1.84, 95% CI 1.41-2.41). The major-complication composite was also higher after ALIF/DLIF (OR 1.22, 95% CI 1.09-1.38), but not significantly once DVT was removed. Mortality did not differ significantly in the full cohort (0.19% vs 0.15%; adjusted OR 1.39, 95% CI 0.90-2.11), but was higher after ALIF/DLIF once circumferential procedures were excluded (OR 1.67, 95% CI 1.05-2.59), an estimate based on few deaths. Readmission and reoperation did not differ. Transfusion did not differ overall, but the posterior-arm rate declined from 5.0% in 2016 to 2.7% in 2024, while the anterior-arm rate remained stable (interaction P = 0.003).

CONCLUSION: ALIF/DLIF carried greater odds of 30-day DVT than PLIF/TLIF, a difference that persisted after matching, whereas the large early mortality difference reported in the 2013-2014 cohort was not reproduced. Approach selection should continue to be driven by anatomy, alignment goals, and operative experience, with added attention to DVT risk after anterior and lateral approaches.

articles.title: Late-onset "clip opening while locked" of a MitraClip G5 XTW with recurrence of mitral regurgitation.
Advances in obstetric anesthesia care in patients with severe cardiac comorbidities.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review aims to update the reader about recent clinical practice recommendations in caring for the cardio-obstetric patient.

RECENT FINDINGS: The emergence of pregnancy heart teams has facilitated multidisciplinary communication for caring for a pregnant patient with cardiac disease. The utilization of noninvasive diagnostic modalities such as brain natriuretic peptide and bedside transthoracic echocardiography can yield quick actionable results regarding therapeutic options. Vaginal delivery remains the preferred mode of delivery for the vast majority of pregnant patients with cardiovascular disease. Timely and effective use of mechanical circulatory support in pregnancy can be beneficial for patients in cardiogenic shock or decompensated heart failure.

SUMMARY: Anesthesiologists are essential team members within the pregnancy heart team and should familiarize themselves with the evidence-based guidelines for caring for pregnant patients with cardiac disease.

articles.title: The right heart matters: contemporary right ventricular monitoring during thoracic surgery.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Right ventricular dysfunction contributes to perioperative cardiovascular instability during thoracic surgery. General anesthesia, positive-pressure ventilation, one-lung ventilation, and pulmonary vascular manipulation or resection can rapidly alter right ventricular loading. This review examines contemporary strategies to identify right ventricular vulnerability, assess reserve, and monitor perioperative adaptation.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent literature emphasizes right ventricular adaptation to load rather than resting function or pulmonary artery pressure alone. Multiparametric echocardiography integrates chamber size, systolic performance, septal geometry, tricuspid regurgitation, and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling. Functional capacity and clinical findings provide complementary preoperative risk information. Stress echocardiography interrogates reserve, while advanced imaging and congestion measures characterize function and systemic consequences. Intraoperatively, pressure, cardiac output, imaging, congestion, and tissue perfusion should be reassessed across key physiologic transitions.

SUMMARY: Perioperative assessment should determine whether the right ventricular can tolerate the additional load imposed by anesthesia and surgery. Integrated monitoring may identify maladaptation and guide escalation of support. Proposed assessment during a clinically indicated preceding procedure requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Prevalence and Mental and Physical Health Correlates of Cardiovascular Disease Among Older US Veterans: Results From the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study.
articles.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders
articles.abstract: Objective: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, and older military veterans are at particularly high risk. This study aims to determine the prevalence and temporal stability of CVD in a nationally representative sample of older US veterans and identify correlates of CVD and related multimorbidity. Methods: Data were analyzed from 1,944 veterans aged ≥60 years from the 2025-2026 National Health and Resilience in Veterans Study (NHRVS). Weighted z-tests, multivariable logistic regression, and Bonferroni-corrected comparisons assessed CVD prevalence trends relative to the 2019-2020 NHRVS and identified correlates. Results: Overall CVD prevalence was 25.7% (n = 486), unchanged from the 2019-2020 NHRVS (25.2%; P= .69), as were rates of heart disease (19.0% vs 19.2%) and myocardial infarction (8.3% vs 10.1%). Stroke/TIA prevalence was higher in 2025-2026 (6.3% vs 4.5%; P= .005), though comparability was limited by the addition of TIA in the later wave. CVD was associated with significantly higher odds of major depression (odds ratio [OR]= 1.88), gambling disorder (OR = 1.69), sleep disorder (OR = 1.90), and insomnia (OR=1.68) but lower odds of lifetime suicide attempt (OR = 0.31), alongside higher odds of respiratory disease (OR = 1.98), kidney disease (OR = 1.85), and chronic pain (OR = 1.65). Independent correlates included older age (OR = 1.06), male sex (OR = 2.17), hypertension (OR = 1.48), hypercholesterolemia (OR = 1.66), diabetes (OR = 1.98), and cumulative trauma burden (OR = 1.10). Conclusions:CVD prevalence among older US veterans has remained high and stable over 5 years and is marked by extensive multimorbidity. Cumulative trauma burden emerged as a distinct correlate beyond traditional cardiometabolic risk factors, supporting integrated prevention strategies addressing both medical and behavioral health. Prim Care Companion CNS Disord 2026;28(6):26m04309. Author affiliations are listed at the end of this article.

articles.title: Integrative 3D imaging and deep learning approach reveals cardiac fibroblast dynamics after myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) are key mediators of heart failure progression, driving fibrotic scar formation after myocardial infarction (MI). Conventional preclinical assessment of MI relies on two-dimensional histology, which cannot resolve the three-dimensional (3D) architecture of the injured heart. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of CF activation is critical for identifying new drug targets, yet spatial mapping of gene expression in intact hearts remains challenging. To address this, we developed a high-throughput imaging pipeline that combined single-cell-resolution gene expression profiling in cleared whole hearts with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy and an AI-driven analysis framework optimized for MI characterization. Using this approach, we mapped expression of periostin (Postn), collagen triple-helix repeat containing 1 (Cthrc1), and asporin (Aspn) - genes associated with CF activation. These markers were detected by day 3 post-infarction in the endocardium and border zone, preceding collagenous scar formation, then expanded across the infarcted myocardium before declining toward baseline during scar maturation. These findings revealed a spatially organized progression of fibrosis-associated gene expression that began in defined regions of the injured heart and subsequently extended throughout the infarcted myocardium. Whole-organ gene-expression imaging combined with deep-learning-based analysis enabled quantitative spatiotemporal mapping of molecular remodeling and provides a framework for investigating disease progression in intact organs.

articles.title: Mechanical Tricuspid Valve Thrombosis Treated With Ultrasound-Assisted Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical tricuspid valves are remarkably susceptible to acute mechanical valve thrombosis (MVT). Current guidelines suggest reoperation or systemic thrombolysis for left-sided MVT. These treatments carry substantial operative and bleeding risks, limiting their application. A better nonsurgical treatment for MVT is needed.

CASE SUMMARY: Six patients with suspected acute tricuspid MVT were treated with ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USCDT). Improvement in symptoms, leaflet mobility, and tricuspid regurgitation severity occurred in 5 of 6 cases with no observed complications. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: Tricuspid MVT is not addressed in current guidelines because of a paucity of available data.

DISCUSSION: USCDT represents a novel treatment alternative for tricuspid MVT. Direct contact between the USCDT catheter and the mechanical valve may enhance alteplase activity and thrombus dispersion.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: USCDT may represent an alternative to contemporary treatments for tricuspid MVT and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Successful M-TEER Using Curved Laryngoscope-Assisted, Endoscopy-Guided TEE Insertion in a Patient With Esophageal Diverticulum.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Real-time 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) is indispensable for mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER), but Zenker's diverticulum is generally considered a contraindication because of the risk of esophageal perforation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman with symptomatic severe ventricular functional mitral regurgitation despite optimal medical therapy was referred for M-TEER. Preprocedural evaluation revealed a Zenker's diverticulum, making blind TEE probe insertion unsafe. After multidisciplinary discussion, endoscopically guided TEE probe insertion using a Sato's curved laryngoscope (Nagashima Medical Instruments Co, Ltd) enabled safe advancement into the esophageal lumen while avoiding the diverticulum. M-TEER was successfully completed under real-time 3-dimensional TEE guidance without complications.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates a novel approach to TEE-guided structural heart interventions in a patient with Zenker's diverticulum, generally considered unsuitable for TEE.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Challenging gastrointestinal anatomy should not necessarily preclude TEE-guided structural heart interventions. Endoscopic TEE probe insertion assisted by Sato's curved laryngoscope may safely overcome this anatomical challenge in selected patients.

articles.title: Three Simultaneous Cardioembolic Sources in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The simultaneous convergence of 3 independent cardioembolic sources in a single patient is exceptional.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old man presented with an extensive left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a 30- × 30-mm left atrial myxoma and a 10- × 16-mm anterior mitral leaflet vegetation with perforation and severe regurgitation; monitoring documented new-onset atrial fibrillation. Despite negative blood cultures, infective endocarditis was diagnosed by the 2023 Duke-ISCVID criteria. He underwent myxoma resection, mitral valve replacement, and splenectomy; histopathology showed acid-fast bacilli in the myxoma and valve, with Mycobacterium tuberculosis confirmed on serum polymerase chain reaction. He died postoperatively from refractory multiorgan failure.

DISCUSSION: These 3 coexisting sources, the myxoma, a tuberculous mitral vegetation, and new-onset atrial fibrillation, constitute the "three-headed monster."

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Transesophageal echocardiography and specimen histopathology are decisive when multiple cardioembolic sources coexist, and tuberculosis should be considered in culture-negative endocarditis.

articles.title: Excimer Laser Coronary Angioplasty for Entrapped Guidewire Retrieval During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidewire entrapment is a rare (0.2%-0.8%) but serious complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), typically occurring in heavily calcified lesions, chronic total occlusions, or during bifurcation stenting. When conventional retrieval fails, surgical removal carries high morbidity.

CASE SUMMARY: A 60-year-old man with 3-vessel coronary disease, prior inferior wall myocardial infarction, hypertension, and diabetes underwent staged PCI. A workhorse guidewire became entrapped in the distal left circumflex artery. Conventional retrieval attempts using multiple guidewires, microcatheters, and low-profile balloons failed. Excimer laser coronary angioplasty (ELCA) successfully freed the wire. Postprocedure angiography revealed TIMI flow grade 3 with localized dissection hematoma.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of successful ELCA-assisted retrieval of an entrapped workhorse guidewire in a nonchronic total occlusion lesion after conventional techniques failed. ELCA offers a safe, surgery-sparing bailout option by ablating surrounding fibrocalcific tissue or polymer coating.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: For entrapped guidewires refractory to conventional PCI retrieval, ELCA offers a safe, surgery-sparing alternative by ablating adjacent tissue or polymer coating, and early use prevents wire fracture, perforation, and emergent bypass grafting.

articles.title: Ventricular Fibrillation: The Ultimate Frontier.
AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Role of Liver Biopsy: Commentary.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
DESCRIPTION: The purpose of this American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) Institute Clinical Practice Update (CPU) is to review the available evidence and best practices regarding the use of liver biopsy in liver diseases, evaluation of abnormal liver tests, and liver masses.

METHODS: This CPU was commissioned and approved by the AGA Institute CPU Committee and the AGA Governing Board to provide timely guidance on a topic of high clinical importance to the AGA membership. This CPU underwent internal peer review by the CPU Committee and external peer review through the standard procedures of Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. This expert commentary incorporates important as well as recently published data in this field and reflects the experiences of the authors.

articles.title: FTH1 Suppresses Aldosterone Biosynthesis in Association with Inhibition of cAMP-PKA-CREB Signaling Pathway.
articles.abstract: Primary aldosteronism is a leading cause of endocrine hypertension, with aldosterone-producing adenoma (APA) being a major subtype. Although ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) is reportedly elevated in APA, its role in aldosterone synthesis remains unclear. This study examined FTH1 expression in APA and non-functional adrenal tumor specimens, revealing marked upregulation of FTH1 that positively correlated with plasma aldosterone levels. To determine its function, Fth1cKO mice with Cyp11a1-Cre-mediated Fth1 knockout in steroidogenic tissues and FTH1-overexpressing H295R cells were generated. Under basal conditions, neither deletion nor overexpression affected aldosterone production. However, following sodium restriction, female Fth1cKO mice exhibited significantly increased serum aldosterone and adrenal Cyp11b2 expression without changes in adrenal iron content, a response absent in males. Transcriptomic profiling indicated enhanced steroid hormone biosynthesis and cAMP signaling. Consistently, FTH1 overexpression in H295R cells suppressed stimulated aldosterone secretion and CYP11B2 expression, accompanied by reduced PKA/CREB phosphorylation. These findings identify FTH1 as a negative regulator of aldosterone biosynthesis under pathological stimulation and raise the possibility that its elevation in APA may represent a compensatory response on excessive steroidogenesis.

articles.title: Recent progress and challenges in Schiff base-based optical chemosensors.
articles.abstract: The traditional analytical methods for detecting environmentally or biologically important analytes are sensitive, but not suitable for rapid on-site analysis because they require complex instrumentation and laboratory facilities. Optical Schiff base-based chemosensors and biosensors are promising tools owing to their tunable photophysical properties, and colorimetry or fluorescence sensing modes. Recent literature on Schiff base-based optical chemosensors developed for the detection of environmental and biologically important analytes such as metal ions, toxic anions, environmental pollutants and clinically important biomolecules published from January 2020 to 31 July 2026 is critically reviewed. This review discusses structure-property relationships and sensing performance. In addition, important photophysical processes like intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), chelation-enhanced or chelation-quenched fluorescence (CHEF/CHEQ), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and analytical performance parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, detection limits, linear ranges, response times, and applicability to real samples, were evaluated. Portability of novel sensing platforms, such as paper-based sensors, smartphone-assisted analysis, and nanomaterial-integrated sensors were specifically examined. Also, special attention was given to new approaches that combine molecular design with computational tools, chemometric data analysis, microfluidic devices and portable digital tools to enhance analytical performance and to increase applicability in real-world applications. Finally, the critical challenges and future perspectives of sustainable sensor design, novel sensing approaches using Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) for the future Schiff base-based optical sensors were surveyed.

articles.title: Impact of autoimmune disease family history on clinical features in patients with persistent antiphospholipid antibodies: The CAPSTONE (Chinese AntiphosPholipid Syndrome cohorT cOllaborative NEtworks) cohort study I.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A family history of autoimmune disease (AIDFH) is noted in patients with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), yet its clinical significance remains underexplored. This study aims to assess the impact of AIDFH on clinical and immunological features of individuals with persistent antiphospholipid antibody (aPL) positivity.

METHODS: Data were drawn from the Chinese AntiphosPholipid Syndrome cohorT cOllaborative NEtworks (CAPSTONE), the first prospective, multicenter cohort of participants with confirmed persistent aPL positivity in China. Patients from five CAPSTONE sites (Oct 2022-Oct 2024) were stratified by AIDFH status. Demographic, clinical, and serological parameters were compared. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed, and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) alleles were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 936 patients, 72 (7.7%) reported AIDFH. These patients had earlier disease onset (27.6 years vs. 29.8 years, P = 0.027), more overlap with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) (43.1% [31/72] vs. 29.4% [254/864], P = 0.016), and higher antinuclear antibody (ANA) positivity (73.9% [51/69] vs. 55.1% [441/801], P = 0.002). In those meeting the 2006 revised Sydney classification criteria for APS, AIDFH correlated with lower frequency of primary APS, and increased rates of pulmonary embolism, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, valve thickening, and various ANAs. Subgroup analysis showed that family history of SLE was linked to more SLE overlap, and elevated ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-ribosomal ribonucleoprotein antibody (anti-rRNP), and Coomb's positivity. Among 374 patients with WES data, HLA-DRB1*08:02 was significantly more frequently shown in AIDFH-positive patients (P = 9.3 × 10-5).

CONCLUSION: Our cohort shows that in patients with persistent aPL positivity, those with AIDFH may have unique clinical and immunogenetic backgrounds. This study provides preliminary evidence for further studies focusing on genetic predisposition and mechanisms. We call for raised attention of AIDFH as a potential risk factor, and further studies are needed to provide suggestions on prognosis and overall management of patients with persistent aPL positivity.

articles.title: Digital Thoracic Drainage System-Derived Circuit Pressure and Air-Flow Changes in Relation to Echocardiographic Indices of Cardiac Function after Chest Tube Placement.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chest tube drainage restores negative intrathoracic pressure, which might alter cardiac loading. Digital thoracic drainage systems continuously record pressure and airflow. We examined device-derived pressure and air-flow trends over 48 hours and echocardiographic changes between 24 and 48 hours.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: Forty-one chest tube drainage episodes in 39 adult, non-mechanically ventilated patients were studied prospectively. Device records were analysed at 10-minute intervals, providing preset suction level, measured circuit pressure, and air flow. Echocardiography was performed at 24 and 48 hours. Continuous time-series analyses included 29 episodes, 28 of which were evaluable within the predefined 48-hour window. False discovery rate correction was applied to multiple comparisons.

RESULTS: The preset suction level remained unchanged during the first 48 hours in 21 of 29 episodes (72%), and the measured circuit pressure was closely related to it at each time point (R2 = 0.838-0.955). Air leak decreased from a median of 61.6 mL/min at baseline to 2.3 mL/min at 24 hours (P < 0.001), with no further change at 48 hours (1.3 mL/min; P = 0.55). After correction, ejection fraction (q = 0.011) and mitral E velocity (q = 0.007) were higher at 48 hours. No device-derived variable was associated with echocardiographic changes after correction for multiple comparisons.

CONCLUSION: Measured circuit pressure appeared to reflect regulated drainage-system pressure more closely than pleural physiology. Most reduction in air leak occurred before the first echocardiographic assessment, potentially limiting the detection of cardiopulmonary associations. These findings support a cautious interpretation of digital drainage parameters and may help define the assessment window for future studies.

articles.title: Clopidogrel-Based Versus Aspirin-Based Double Antithrombotic Therapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Atrial Fibrillation Patients: Results of the ASAF-PCI Registry.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), current guidelines recommend a brief period of triple antithrombotic therapy (TAT) consisting of an oral anticoagulant (OAC), aspirin and clopidogrel, followed by double antithrombotic therapy (DAT) with OAC plus clopidogrel. Evidence on aspirin as an alternative to clopidogrel within DAT remains limited.

AIMS: The present analysis aimed at describing contemporary use of aspirin- versus clopidogrel-based DAT and to compare 12-month clinical outcomes.

METHODS: In this multicenter, observational study, consecutive patients with AF undergoing PCI between January 2019 and December 2023 and discharged on DAT with OAC plus aspirin or clopidogrel were included. The primary endpoint was the 12-month incidence of net adverse clinical events (NACE), composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), non-fatal stroke, urgent revascularization, and major bleeding. Secondary composite and individual endpoints were also assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for baseline imbalances.

RESULTS: Among 445 patients, 291 (65.4%) were discharged on clopidogrel-based DAT and 154 (34.6%) on aspirin-based DAT. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable. NACE occurred in 15.1% versus 13.6% of patients (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.64-1.98; p = 0.674), with no significant difference after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.59-2.26; p = 0.677). No significant between group differences were observed for secondary composite or individual efficacy and safety endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of AF patients undergoing PCI, aspirin- and clopidogrel-based DAT with OAC were not associated with significantly different 12-month outcomes. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in adequately powered randomized trials.

articles.title: Structural characterisation of the effect of 5-chloroindole on orthosteric activation of murine 5-HT3A receptors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: 5-HT3 receptors play a central role in gut-brain signalling, and their hyperactivity is associated with pathologies ranging from chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting to irritable bowel syndrome. While the principles governing 5-HT3R orthosteric pharmacology are well established (spanning antagonists, partial agonists and full agonists), structural insights into allosteric mechanisms remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which a positive modulator of 5-HT3R, 5-chloroindole, potentiates agonist response by fine-tuning orthosteric activation of this receptor.

EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Here, we investigated the molecular basis of modulation by 5-chloroindole (5-CI), a selective positive allosteric modulator, using cryo-EM and electrophysiology. We present 5-HT3AR structures in the presence of 5-CI alone, as well as in combination with either submaximal concentrations of 5-HT or saturating concentrations of the partial agonist SMP-100.

KEY RESULTS: Our results reveal that 5-CI potentiates 5-HT3R through a distinct mechanism involving co-occupancy of the orthosteric site and with additional modulation through an intersubunit site in the transmembrane domain.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: This mode of action is reminiscent of benzodiazepine modulation in GABAARs, yet it notably occurs within homomeric binding sites. Together, these findings establish the structural basis for the previously reported ago-allosteric mechanism of 5-CI, which becomes functionally apparent only in the presence of agonistic ligands.

articles.title: Admission C-Reactive Protein-Albumin-Lymphocyte Index and Risk Stratification for Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Comparison With the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many blood-based inflammatory and nutritional indices have been linked to contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but they are rarely compared with one another or tested for what they add to existing risk models. The C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) both come from routine admission blood tests, yet no study has compared them directly for CA-AKI or asked whether CALLY adds anything to a standard clinical model.

AIMS: We tested whether CALLY predicts CA-AKI independently of SII in STEMI, and whether it improves reclassification and net benefit on top of a full clinical model.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, we reviewed 1561 consecutive STEMI patients treated with primary PCI between 2021 and 2025. CA-AKI was defined by the KDIGO 48-h criterion (creatinine rise ≥ 0.3 mg/dL), with creatinine measured daily in every patient. CALLY and ln(SII) were added, alone and together, to a prespecified clinical risk model. Models were compared with the DeLong test, continuous NRI, IDI, and decision-curve analysis.

RESULTS: CA-AKI developed in 317 patients (20.3%). CALLY discriminated CA-AKI better than ln(SII) (AUC 0.632 vs. 0.559; DeLong p = 0.0003). When both were entered together, CALLY stayed independent (OR 0.872, 95% CI 0.783-0.970; p = 0.012), but ln(SII) did not (p = 0.145), even though SII was independent on its own. Adding CALLY produced only a small change in the C-statistic (0.752-0.762; DeLong non-significant), yet it improved reclassification (IDI 0.007, p = 0.003; NRI 0.166, p = 0.005) and net benefit, and calibration remained adequate (Hosmer-Lemeshow p ≥ 0.249).

CONCLUSION: In STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, a low CALLY index was independently associated with CA-AKI and improved risk reclassification when added to a clinical model, whereas SII was not independent once CALLY was included. This is the first comparison of CALLY and SII for CA-AKI, and the first assessment of CALLY for CA-AKI in STEMI.

articles.title: Silver nanoparticles against antimicrobial-resistant pathogens: in vivo efficacy, toxicokinetics, and barriers to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is responsible for an estimated 1.27 million deaths annually, driving urgent demand for novel therapeutics. Silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have attracted significant interest due to their multi-target antibacterial activity, which presents a higher evolutionary barrier to resistance compared to conventional single-target antibiotics. However, AgNP monotherapy is limited by a narrow, formulation-dependent systemic therapeutic window, whereas repeated sublethal exposure may promote adaptive phenotypes. Combination with conventional antibiotics may enhance antimicrobial activity while reducing the concentrations of individual agents. This review examines the in vivo evidence for the efficacy of AgNPs against resistant pathogens, the physicochemical determinants governing their biological activity, and the translational barriers that limit clinical application. While in vivo literature provides preclinical evidence of antibacterial efficacy and potential synergistic activity of AgNP-antibiotic combinations, systemic infections caused by priority pathogens remain understudied. Consequently, four critical translational gaps are identified: 1) the absence of a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) dosing framework; 2) insufficient systemic infection models; 3) limited understanding of potential effects on polymicrobial communities; and 4) inconsistent physicochemical characterization limiting cross-study comparison. Addressing these gaps through integrated preclinical evaluation will be essential for determining whether AgNPs can serve as safe and effective adjuvants to existing antimicrobial therapies.

articles.title: Push percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy and the risk of accidental tube dislodgement relative to pull placement in adults receiving enteral nutrition: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Enteral feeding is the first choice to treat or avoid malnutrition in patients with impaired oral intake. Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy tubes can be placed using a push or pull technique, the former of which is the preference in cases when pull method is contraindicated. We compared outcomes of push versus pull percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study combining data from patients undergoing pull placement and push placement. The primary outcome was 1-year accidental tube dislodgement, and secondary outcomes were planned removal, peristomal infection requiring antibiotics, and all-cause mortality. A parametric multistate nonlinear time-to-event model was developed using stepwise covariate modeling to identify baseline predictors of outcomes.

RESULTS: We included 305 patients in our analysis, of which 205 underwent the push placement. In multistate analyses, push placement had a higher risk of accidental tube dislodgement than pull placement, whereas peristomal infection, planned tube removal for adequate oral intake, and all-cause mortality did not differ between techniques CONCLUSION: Push placement was associated with a higher risk of accidental tube dislodgement, whereas other outcomes did not differ between techniques. Therefore, when anatomical or disease-related considerations preclude or contraindicate pull placement, push placement remains an appropriate alternative despite the increased risk of tube dislodgement.

articles.title: Neuraminidase-Mediated Desialylation Modulates Red Blood Cell Aggregation.
articles.abstract: The glycocalyx of red blood cells (RBCs) is a negatively charged surface layer rich in sialic acid residues that contributes to RBC-RBC interaction (RBC aggregation). In pathological conditions such as diabetes and sepsis, glycocalyx degradation is often observed along with abnormal RBC aggregation. However, the mechanistic relationship between these phenomena remains poorly defined. In this study, we investigate the effects of enzymatic glycocalyx degradation on RBC aggregation under physiologically controlled shear-flow conditions. Using neuraminidase from Clostridium perfringens (C. welchii) at varying activities, we selectively removed sialic acid residues from the RBC glycocalyx, simulating different levels of desialylation observed in health and disease. Confocal microscopy confirmed the reduction of membrane sialic acid, while microfluidic experiments revealed an increase in both the size and stability of the RBC aggregates after enzymatic treatment. Our findings suggest that glycocalyx integrity is a crucial biophysical determinant of RBC aggregation, likely influencing both electrostatic repulsion and hydrodynamic forces. This study provides new insights into how the enzymatic modification of the glycocalyx contributes to pathological hemorheology and may inform future strategies for the diagnosis or treatment of vascular diseases.

articles.title: Association between early increased energy and protein delivery and 60-day in-hospital mortality relative to nutrition risk after cardiac surgery: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is unclear whether nutrition risk modifies the associations of early increased energy and protein delivery with mortality in cardiac surgery patients.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used data from the International Nutrition Survey. The analysis included critically ill adults who underwent major cardiac surgery and did not permanently progress to exclusive oral feeding during the first 4 full days in the intensive care unit. Nutrition delivery and adequacy were averaged over these 4 days. Logistic regression was used to evaluate the mNUTRIC score as a modifier of the associations between early nutrition and 60-day in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 292 patients were included; 57 (19.5%) died in hospital within 60 days. Decedents received significantly more nutrition compared to 60-day hospital survivors. After multivariable adjustment, early increases in energy and protein delivery were not significantly associated with 60-day in-hospital mortality. The mNUTRIC score did not significantly modify the association between nutrition exposure and mortality. Patients with mNUTRIC scores of 6-9 had higher 60-day in-hospital mortality than those with scores of 0-5 (24% versus 13%; odds ratio 2.2; 95% CI: 1.1-4.2; P = 0.017). For each 1-point increase in the mNUTRIC score, the odds of 60-day in-hospital mortality were multiplied by 1.3 (95% CI: 1.1-1.6, P = 0.008).

CONCLUSION: In cardiac surgery patients who continued to need enteral and parenteral nutrition, the mNUTRIC score did not identify patients who benefited from early increases in energy and protein delivery.
