articles.title: Self-guided home-based rehabilitation for upper limb motor recovery in people with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This review examined the efficacy of self-guided, home-based rehabilitation (SGHBR) for upper limb recovery in people with stroke (PwS).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Web of Science, and PEDro were searched using terms related to stroke, upper limb, home-based rehabilitation, and self-rehabilitation. Included articles were randomized controlled trials involving adults with stroke receiving home-based upper limb rehabilitation assessed with standardized clinical scales. Studies were excluded if the SGHBR intervention involved technological devices, telerehabilitation, or direct therapist supervision.

RESULTS: Four reviewers screened 501 records, and 14 articles were included in the systematic review. Eight independent cohorts from 10 studies provided data for meta-analysis; remaining findings were narratively synthesized. SGHBR showed no significant advantage over other rehabilitation interventions, although the pooled estimate slightly favored SGHBR (SMD = 0.10, 95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), with low-to-moderate heterogeneity (I2 = 31.8%). Methodological quality was overall moderate, with variable risk of bias. Interventions differed in structure, duration, and strategies, but most included task-oriented or task-specific practice.

CONCLUSIONS: SGHBR may provide upper limb functional benefits comparable to conventional therapy, but higher-quality studies are needed to confirm efficacy, generalizability, and cost-effectiveness across stroke survivor populations in routine practice.

articles.title: "Every Day Is Different, and It Is Worthwhile": Defining Practice Domains for Disease Intervention Professionals.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Disease intervention (DI) professionals serve as frontline responders in preventing and controlling infectious diseases, yet the absence of a standardized national framework for DI training and practice has led to varied job expectations, skill requirements, and preparedness. This multiphase study sought to validate, refine, and define practice domains for DI professionals.

METHODS: In spring 2025, the investigators conducted a systematized review of DI job postings, job descriptions, and job classification documents to identify key knowledge, skills, and abilities required for DI roles. Investigators held listening sessions with DI professionals to gather qualitative insights into field realities, training gaps, and emerging needs, and provided feedback on the existing Certified in Disease Intervention (CDI) domains identified by the National Board of Public Health Examiners (NBPHE). These findings informed the development of domains that were then corroborated through consultations with listening session participants.

RESULTS: In the systematized review, investigators analyzed 187 documents from 29 states. Investigators held listening sessions with 39 DI professionals across 8 US jurisdictions. Job functions varied from disease-specific to generalist roles. From the job descriptions and DI professionals from all jurisdictions, we identified the following domains: confidentiality, social awareness, effective communication, and field readiness. Domains in outbreak response, emergency preparedness, and fairness-informed practices were inconsistent. Twenty of 27 listening session participants who agreed to participate in the validation consultation provided feedback on the existing 6 CDI domains identified by NBPHE. Three additional domains emerged: ethics and fairness-informed practices, infection knowledge, and positionality.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings offer a foundation for competency standardization and the creation of pathways to promote and sustain the DI workforce.

articles.title: Engineering Metal Ion-Directed Co-Assemblies: From Biological Regulation to Carrier-Free Nanotheranostics.
articles.abstract: The convergence of coordination chemistry and nanomedicine has unlocked new frontiers in disease treatment. While metal ions act as essential physiological regulators, their dysregulation is intrinsically linked to pathologies such as cancer and infection. Harnessing the therapeutic versatility of metal ions, metal ion-mediated co-assembly has risen as a transformative strategy to construct carrier-free nanodrugs. Unlike traditional formulations, this paradigm exploits coordination interactions to co-assemble drugs and metal ions into all-in-one nanostructures, delivering synergistic therapeutic efficacy, exceptional drug loading capacity, and controllable biodegradation while eliminating carrier-related toxicity. This review comprehensively summarizes the state-of-the-art design strategies, assembly kinetics, and key performance metrics of metal ion-based nanomedicines. Special attention is dedicated to their applications in multimodal treatments, spanning chemotherapy, phototherapy, chemodynamic therapy, and immunotherapy, which highlights their capability to tackle complex biological challenges. Furthermore, we critically discuss the challenges impeding clinical translation and propose future directions for this rapidly evolving field. Collectively, these coordination-driven innovations provide a framework for next-generation precision nanomedicine, but their clinical translation will depend on rigorous translational validation, scalable manufacturing, predictable in vivo fate, and data-driven optimization.

articles.title: Early Developmental Interventions for Infants Born Very Preterm: A Survey of Australian Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy Practice.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To describe clinical practices of Australian physiotherapists and occupational therapists providing early developmental interventions for infants born very preterm (VPT; <32 weeks' gestation) during the first year of life.

METHODS: A national survey was conducted with physiotherapists and occupational therapists who had cared for infants born VPT, under 12 months' corrected age. Clinician demographics and practice characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. Intervention descriptions (guided by the Template for Intervention Description and Replication for Rehabilitation checklist), and perceived barriers and facilitators, were analyzed using inductive content analysis.

RESULTS: Of 114 responses analyzed (74.6% physiotherapists), representing all Australian states, territories and care sectors, most reported more than 10 years of clinical experience (65.8%), provided care during neonatal hospital admissions (65.8%), and worked within multidisciplinary teams (93.9%). Interventions encompassed multiple interacting components, described using varied terminology. Three categories of barriers and facilitators included: systems and structures, infant and family characteristics, and clinician capabilities.

CONCLUSIONS: Physiotherapists and occupational therapists in Australia provide early developmental interventions across multiple sectors within collaborative practice settings. Variability in terminology and systems-level barriers highlight the need for greater consistency in clinical practice. Standardization of terminology and strengthening clinician capabilities are key priorities for the field.

articles.title: Comparing the clinical outcomes of different techniques for surgical management of canine cranial cruciate ligament rupture using target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Target trial emulation applies randomised controlled trial principles to observational data for causal inference. This study evaluated whether tibial plateau levelling osteotomy (TPLO), tibial tuberosity advancement (TTA) or extracapsular lateral suture stabilisation (ELSS) affects lameness, analgesia and complication outcomes in dogs with cranial cruciate ligament (CCL) rupture.

METHODS: Dogs aged 1.5-12 years with CCL rupture in 2019 within the VetCompass database undergoing TPLO, TTA or ELSS were included. Confounders were identified via a directed acyclic graph and adjusted using inverse probability of treatment weighting. Weighted logistic regression estimated risk differences (RDs).

RESULTS: The study included 387 TPLO, 263 ELSS and 242 TTA cases. No significant differences in long-term lameness risk were identified between groups. Compared with TPLO, ELSS increased short-term lameness risk (RD 22.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] 7.5-38.3), and TTA increased analgesia prescription at 3 months (RD 15.5%, 95% CI 3.3-27.8) and 6 months (RD 16.5%, 95% CI 4.0-29.0) and minor complications (RD 12.1%, 95% CI 0.8-23.5).

LIMITATIONS: Observational data may contain residual confounding despite weighting. Follow-up completeness also varied between cases, limiting comparability.

CONCLUSION: No significant differences in long-term lameness risk were identified between surgical groups. TPLO reduced risk of short-term lameness compared with ELSS and had fewer analgesia requirements and complications than TTA.

articles.title: Integrating Glycemic Variability and Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio to Stratify Mortality Risk in Patients with Sepsis-Associated AKI.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a common and severe complication in intensive care units. Although glycemic variability (GV) and stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) are associated with adverse outcomes in critical illness, their combined prognostic value in SA-AKI remains unclear.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with SA-AKI from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database. The primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations of GV and SHR with mortality. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.ResultsA total of 2638 patients were included. Both GV and SHR were independently associated with increased risks of in-hospital and 1-year mortality. Patients with concomitantly high GV and SHR had the highest mortality risk (OR 1.754, 95% CI 1.321-2.329, P < .001; HR 1.340, 95% CI 1.124-1.598, P = .001). The combined GV-SHR model yielded slightly higher AUCs than either marker alone, with values of 0.700 for in-hospital mortality and 0.708 for 1-year mortality.ConclusionCombined assessment of GV and SHR improves mortality risk stratification in critically ill patients with SA-AKI and may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients.

articles.title: A Two-Sample Mendelian Randomisation Study on the Causal Relationship between Malnutrition-Related Traits and Oral Diseases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To elucidate the correlation between malnutrition and oral diseases, the authors conducted a two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics related to eight malnutrition subtypes were obtained from the FinnGen GWAS database, and statistics relating to seven oral diseases were sourced from the UK-Biobank and GWAS Catalog database. In this two-sample MR, genetic variants associated with malnutrition-related traits were used to estimate correlations. The inverse-variance weighting (IVW) method was employed for the main analysis. Various complementary methods, including MR-Egger, weighted median (WM), and weighted mode were implemented to detect the causal relationship. The sensitivity analyses included MR-PRESSO, MR-Egger, Cochran Q and leave-one-out methods to verify the robustness of the results.

RESULTS: The IVW results showed a suggestive causal association between unspecified protein-energy malnutrition and painful gums (odds ratio 0.9993, 95% confidence interval 0.9987 to 0.9999, P = 0.025, P-false discovery rate (FDR) = 0.707). There was no significant causal association between other malnutrition and oral diseases at the genetic level. No significant heterogeneity was detected, suggesting the robustness of the present findings.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest a suggestive causal relationship between malnutrition and oral diseases and underscore the importance of nutritional assessment in routine dental care as a potential preventive strategy. Further research is needed to better understand the mechanisms of action and, more generally, to develop strategies for the prevention of oral diseases.

articles.title: CBCT Assessment of Peri-Implant Marginal Bone Changes Following Adjunctive Local Ozone Therapy: A Randomized Split-Mouth Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This prospective split-mouth randomized controlled trial evaluated the association between adjunctive topical ozone application and early peri-implant marginal bone loss using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This split-mouth randomized controlled trial included 48 patients and 152 implants. Matched implant sites were randomly allocated to the ozone (n = 76) or control group (n = 76). Ozone was applied to the implant socket during surgery and to the peri-implant site on postoperative days 1, 3, 5, and 7. Marginal bone level changes from baseline to 6 months were assessed by CBCT at the buccal, palatal/lingual, mesial, and distal surfaces and as combined measurements. Between-group comparisons were performed at the participant level using paired samples t-tests with Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. Cluster bootstrapping was performed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: At 6 months, marginal bone loss was significantly lower in the ozone group than in the control group at the buccal surface (0.43 ± 0.47 vs. 0.88 ± 0.70 mm; Holm-adjusted p 0.001) and for the buccolingual average (0.34 ± 0.33 vs. 0.68 ± 0.52 mm; Holm-adjusted p 0.001). No significant between-group differences were observed for the other measurements after Holm adjustment (all adjusted p ≥ 0.102).

CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive topical ozone application may support early peri-implant marginal bone preservation, particularly at the buccal aspect. However, larger randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Determining the Levels of Nutrition Literacy and Attitudes towards Healthy Eating among University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Nutrition literacy supports healthy food choices, yet its relationship with healthy eating attitudes among university students remains unclear. Public health nurses have important roles in nutrition education and health promotion. This study aimed to assess nutrition literacy, healthy eating attitudes, and their relationship among university students. This cross-sectional study included 1014 students from the Faculty of Education at one public university in Türkiye. Face-to-face data collection used a personal information form, the Evaluation Instrument of Nutrition Literacy on Adults (EINLA), and the Attitude Scale for Healthy Nutrition (ASHN). Descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, and Pearson correlation were used. Mean EINLA and ASHN scores were 26.4 ± 4.6 and 71.19 ± 10.5, respectively. Borderline or inadequate nutrition literacy was identified in 26.5% of students, while 26.5% had low or moderate healthy eating attitudes. Scores were weakly but positively correlated (r = 0.163, p < 0.01). The weak association between nutrition literacy and healthy eating attitudes suggests that nutrition literacy alone may be insufficient to promote positive attitudes. Public health nurses may use these findings to develop comprehensive nutrition education and health promotion strategies addressing other factors influencing healthy eating among university students.

articles.title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
articles.abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. Overfed offspring displayed increased body weight, adiposity and altered body proportions from early postnatal life onward, with more pronounced effects in females. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing identified a specific, lasting dysbiosis in the overweight female mice, characterized by reduced alpha diversity and species-level shifts in Lactobacillus, Muribaculum and Bacteroides. Crucially, upon allergic sensitization in adulthood, these animals displayed an exacerbated disease state consistent with an 'obese-asthma' phenotype, marked by heightened airway inflammation, intense eosinophilic and neutrophilic infiltration, higher Type 2 cytokine levels (i.e., IL-4, IL-5) and altered bronchoalveolar immune profiles. These findings suggest that early-life nutritional imbalance establishes an altered immunometabolic trajectory via the gut-lung axis, providing a mechanistic basis for the increased severity observed in obesity-associated asthma.

articles.title: Gender Sensitivity and Sexual Assertiveness as Moderators of the Relationship Between Depression and Cyber Dating Violence Among College Students.
articles.abstract: This study examined the associations of depression with cyber dating violence (CDV) victimization and perpetration among college students, and tested whether gender sensitivity and sexual assertiveness moderated these associations. This cross-sectional, descriptive correlational study analyzed online survey data from 208 university students aged 19 years or older who reported at least one current or previous mutually recognized romantic relationship. Measures were the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, the Cyber-violence in Adolescent Couples scale, a gender sensitivity scale, and a sexual assertiveness scale. Data were analyzed with IBM SPSS Statistics 23.0 and the PROCESS macro (version 3.2.01) using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, independent t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, and moderated regression analysis. Depression was positively associated with both CDV victimization and CDV perpetration. Gender sensitivity and sexual assertiveness each significantly moderated these associations, with the conditional associations generally attenuated at higher levels of the moderators. Johnson-Neyman analyses identified sample-specific regions of significance rather than universal clinical thresholds. This study indicates that gender sensitivity and sexual assertiveness function as potentially modifiable psychosocial competencies associated with weaker associations between depression and CDV victimization and perpetration. Because the design was cross-sectional, reverse and reciprocal pathways cannot be excluded, and the findings should be interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects. These findings suggest that CDV prevention should extend beyond mental health intervention alone and incorporate gender sensitivity and sexual assertiveness components.

articles.title: Is there an association between the -819 C/T and -1082 A/G polymorphisms in the IL10 gene and dengue risk? Results from a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Dengue is a systemic viral infection considered as one of the most prevalent diseases in the world. The literature has investigated the role of genetic variants, including those described in the IL10 gene (for instance the -819 C/T and -1082 A/G polymorphisms) in the pathogenesis of dengue, however the results remained contradictory. Therefore, the present study aimed to evaluate the influence of both, by meta-analytic calculations. A systematic literature search was conducted in Scielo, PubMed, SCOPUS, and Google Scholar, for studies published before 18 August 2026, to identify eligible studies investigating the association of both IL10 gene polymorphisms with dengue susceptibility and clinical severity. There were calculations for heterogeneity, Odds Ratio (OR) with 95% of Confidence Intervals (CI) and tests for publication bias. The values of P < 0.05 were considered as significant. Eleven studies were included in the results which there were non-significant associations between these two variants and the disease. For the -819 C/T the mutant allelic evaluation showed an increased risk of the disease (OR = 1.08, 95% CI: 0.97-1.20; P = 0.17). Likewise, the increased risk was found for the mutant allele in the -1082 A/G polymorphism and dengue (OR = 1.01 (95% CI: 0.85-1.18; P = 0.95). There was no obvious evidence of publication bias. Thus, the present meta-analysis showed the non-significant association among the -819 C/T and -1082 A/G polymorphisms in IL10 gene and dengue risk in any of its clinical forms.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Agonists or Tezepelumab for Obesity-Associated Asthma: A Cohort Study.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Obesity is associated with poor asthma outcomes. GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists induce weight loss and dampen airway inflammation independent of pathways currently targeted by biologics.

OBJECTIVE: To compare differences in respiratory outcomes and weight loss between GLP-1-based medications and tezepelumab in asthma patients without diabetes.

METHODS: A retrospective study was performed in a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Patients with specialist-treated, obesity-associated, moderate-to-severe asthma with at least one severe exacerbation in the prior year who initiated liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, or tezepelumab between January 1, 2022 and December 31, 2025 were identified. Prevalent diabetes was excluded. Patients were followed for subsequent exacerbations, rescue inhaler prescriptions, respiratory-related healthcare encounters, and time to greater than 10% loss in body mass index. Overlap weighting accounted for imbalance in baseline asthma and obesity characteristics.

RESULTS: 2779 patients were identified, of whom 133 initiated liraglutide, 1770 semaglutide, 472 tirzepatide, and 404 tezepelumab. In weighted estimates, patients starting tirzepatide experienced a lower hazard of severe exacerbation compared to tezepelumab (weighted hazard ratio [wHR] 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.70); those starting semaglutide had a similar hazard (wHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.70-1.39). Tirzepatide and semaglutide initiators attained >10% reduction in BMI sooner, had less need for rescue inhalers, and had fewer subsequent respiratory-related encounters compared to tezepelumab.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1-based medications, and in particular dual-incretin GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, may have comparable effectiveness to biologic therapy among patients with associated obesity without diabetes. Clinical trials are necessary to validate findings in this observational study.

articles.title: Lorlatinib-Associated Dyslipidemia in ALK-Positive NSCLC: Atherosclerotic Risk and the Unresolved Question of Venous Thromboembolism.
articles.abstract: Lorlatinib, a brain-penetrant third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has markedly improved outcomes in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In the CROWN trial, median progression-free survival had not been reached with first-line lorlatinib after 7 years of follow-up, compared with 9.1 months for crizotinib, with 7-year progression-free survival of 55% versus 3%. Median treatment duration was 62.6 months versus 9.6 months. This duration extends cumulative exposure to lorlatinib's characteristic metabolic toxicity: hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia. At 7 years, these occurred in 73% and 71% of patients receiving lorlatinib, with grade 3 or 4 events in 22% and 26%. Onset is rapid, at a median of about 2 weeks. At 5 years, any-grade elevations had persisted for a median of 36 to 38 months; 71% of events were managed with lipid-lowering agents. ALK-positive NSCLC carries a high risk of venous thromboembolism across observational cohorts and a meta-analysis, more so for venous than arterial events. Laboratory evidence suggests the EML4-ALK fusion raises tissue factor through the pERK1/2-AP-1 pathway. At 7 years, aggregate cardiovascular adverse events were similar between treatment groups, and venous events were not more frequent with lorlatinib; small event counts and differing treatment exposure limit comparison of individual events. Statin choice is limited because lorlatinib is a moderate cytochrome P450 3A inducer; rosuvastatin and pravastatin are preferred. We review lorlatinib-associated dyslipidemia and its management and separate two claims: prompt, guideline-concordant lipid management is supported by established atherosclerotic prevention principles, whereas any effect on venous thromboembolism remains untested.

articles.title: Risk of myocardial infarction subtypes in systemic lupus erythematosus: a matched nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is associated with an increased risk of myocardial infarction (MI), often assumed to be due to coronary artery disease (CAD), although this has not been directly demonstrated. We therefore estimated the risk of incident MI, MI with CAD (MI-CAD), and MI with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) associated with SLE.

METHODS: Individuals aged 18-80 years with incident SLE were identified in the National Patient Register (NPR) during 2006-2021 using ICD-10 codes. Up to ten population-based comparators without SLE were matched on age, sex, and residential location. Follow-up continued until fatal or non-fatal MI, death, emigration, or end of study. MI was identified using the NPR, the Cause of Death Register, and SWEDEHEART, which provided MI-CAD and MINOCA classifications defined by ≥ 50% or < 50% coronary obstruction on angiography. Incidence rates, rate differences, and cause-specific hazard ratios were estimated using Poisson and Cox regression, adjusted for age, sex, and education.

RESULTS: We included 3,894 individuals with SLE and 38,168 matched comparators (84% women; median age 45 years). During a median follow-up of 7 years, MI occurred in 129 individuals with SLE and 584 comparators. SLE was associated with increased risks of MI (HR 2.4; 95% CI 2.0-2.9), MI-CAD (HR 2.4; 95% CI 1.9-3.1), and MI with missing angiography data (HR 2.9; 95% CI 2.1-3.9), but not MINOCA (HR 0.9; 95% CI 0.4-2.2).

CONCLUSION: These findings support an important role for obstructive CAD in the excess risk of MI observed in SLE.

articles.title: The diastole-systole transition as a regulatory window for heart-brain coupling in major depressive disorder: Evidence from cardiac phase-dependent 1/f slope and periodic neural dynamics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac rhythms dynamically modulate neural activity and information processing. Disruptions in heart-brain coupling (HBC) may contribute to affective dysregulation in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet their effects on periodic and aperiodic neural activity remain unclear. This study investigated cardiac cycle-dependent modulation of oscillatory and 1/f neural components in MDD.

METHODS: Resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) and electrocardiography (ECG) were simultaneously recorded from 60 patients with MDD and 60 matched healthy controls. Patients underwent a 6-month follow-up, and remission status was assessed using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-17). The Spectral Parameterization Resolved in Time (SPRiNT) algorithm was used to separate periodic and aperiodic neural activity. Linear mixed-effects models and permutation-based statistics were applied to examine cardiac phase-dependent neural modulation and between-group differences.

RESULTS: Cardiac phase modulated both oscillatory power and aperiodic 1/f dynamics. Compared with controls, patients with MDD exhibited attenuated steepening of the aperiodic 1/f spectrum in the left insula during the diastole-to-systole transition and a greater reduction in δ-band power in the left anterior cingulate cortex during late systole. In addition, patients with MDD showed earlier α-band peak activity in the posterior cingulate cortex. Exploratory longitudinal analyses showed an increase in left insular 1/f modulation within remitters, although the formal group × time interaction was not significant.

CONCLUSIONS: MDD is characterized by disrupted cardiac cycle-dependent neural dynamics involving both periodic and aperiodic activity. Altered insular aperiodic modulation may reflect impaired excitation-inhibition balance and abnormal heart-brain synchronization in depression, highlighting cardiac rhythms as potential state-dependent targets for closed-loop neuromodulation.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension due left heart disease is associated with increased UTP-dependent contraction in pulmonary veins.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Lung cellular and molecular physiology
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) secondary to left heart disease (group II) is a fatal syndrome and the most prevalent form of PH. PH-II is characterized by an increase in total pulmonary vascular resistance (TPVR). Recent studies in patients found an association between remodeling of small-diameter pulmonary veins (SPV) and the severity of PH-II, suggesting that increased SPV contractility and/or remodeling may contribute to increased TPVR. Purinergic agonists can induce contraction and vascular remodeling via purinergic receptors on vascular smooth muscle cells, and purinergic receptor signaling is implicated in other forms of PH. Thus, we hypothesized that PH-II alters purinergic receptors in SPV, contributing to increased TPVPR. The study of PH-II is limited due to the lack of suitable experimental models. Therefore, we first evaluated three experimental strategies to induce PH-II in rats: abdominal aortic constriction, renovascular hypertension, and transverse aortic constriction (TAC). Physiologic, echocardiographic, morphometric, and molecular biology studies indicated that only TAC rats developed PH-II. Next, we evaluated whether TAC-induced PH-II modified the contractile response to purinergic agonists in SPV. Studies in precision-cut lung slices showed that SPV from TAC-induced HP-II presented an increased contractile response to UTP. Both lung tissue and laser-microdissected SPV from TAC-induced PH-II rats showed higher purinergic receptor expression as compared with lung tissue and SPV from control rats. Also, lungs from TAC-induced PH-II rats showed SPV hypertrophy and SPV wall remodeling, associated with perivascular/peribronchial immune cell infiltration. These results suggest that purinergic receptors of SPV are implicated in PH-II development.

articles.title: RETRACTION: Associated Factors for Adhesions Post Surgery: a Case Control Study.
articles.abstract: H. Mariem, S. Rakia, M. Mohamed Ali, Y. Chaima, H. Hajer, K. Nesrine, T. Fatma, B. Radhia, M. Abdelwaheb, B. Amal, Y. Yahia, M. Souhir, G. Rami, G. Brahim, S. Karim, M. Hamida, K. Hela, B. S. Mohamed, "Associated Factors for Adhesions Post Surgery: A Case Control Study," ANZ Journal of Surgery 96, no. 7-8 (2026): 1934-1940, https://doi.org/10.1111/ans.70634. The above article, published online on 02 April 2026 in Wiley Online Library (onlinelibrary.wiley.com), has been retracted by agreement between the journal Editor-in-Chief, Julian A. Smith; the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons; and John Wiley & Sons Australia, Ltd. A third party reported to the journal that the article included several statistically implausible values in Table 1 and concerns that the identification of Pfannenstiel incision as an independent risk factor for ASBO did not include mechanistic or confounding explanations. Furthermore, an independent review by the journal also concluded that the statistics reported in Table 1 and Table 2 contained several errors, that the statistical methodology lacked necessary details, and that the article contained errors in the terminology used throughout the article. The authors responded to an inquiry by the publisher and acknowledged that errors had been made in the reported statistics. However, further review of this response found that it did not adequately address the concerns. The retraction has been agreed to because the errors in the article fundamentally compromise the editors' confidence in the conclusions presented. The authors agree with the retraction and state that the errors were unintentional.

articles.title: Changes in Perinatal Management in Pregnancies With Abnormal Findings Detected on Ultrasound in the Late Second and Third Trimester.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the indications, findings, and impact on perinatal management of referrals for advanced fetal ultrasound in the late second and third trimesters in a setting without routine third-trimester screening.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study (July 2020-November 2022), we included women referred for advanced fetal sonography after a prior normal second-trimester anomaly scan, prompted by suspected congenital anomaly, abnormal biometry, poly-/oligohydramnios, or fetal arrhythmia. The primary outcome was change in perinatal management; the secondary outcome was transfer from midwifery-led to hospital-led or tertiary care.

RESULTS: Among 1116 referrals, advanced ultrasound confirmed an abnormal finding in 65.0% (725/1116): congenital anomalies (n = 266), abnormal biometry (n = 246), poly-/oligohydramnios (n = 104), and arrhythmia (n = 109). Invasive testing was performed in 2.5% (18/725), with abnormal results in six. Follow-up data were available for 96.6% (700/725), with a live birth rate of 95.0% (689/725). In total 43.9% (318/725) received perinatal follow-up, of which 20.0% (145/725) was induced for the anomaly. Hospital-led care rose from 38.9% to 69.4% after confirmation of abnormal findings.

CONCLUSION: Despite the absence of routine third-trimester ultrasound, abnormal late-pregnancy findings frequently alter perinatal management. These findings support offering all women a third-trimester scan that includes a standardized assessment of key anatomical structures to improve diagnostic consistency and equity of care.

articles.title: Vascularisation in Dental Pulp Regeneration: From Cell Transplantation to Cell-Free Strategies.
articles.journal: Australian endodontic journal : the journal of the Australian Society of Endodontology Inc
articles.abstract: Vascularisation is the prerequisite and rate-limiting step for functional dental pulp regeneration. Because the pulp receives its entire blood supply through a single apical foramen, slow ingrowth creates an ischaemic window in which transplanted cells are prone to central necrosis. This review synthesises cell-based, molecular, material-based and cell-free vascularisation strategies, and the methods used to test them. Cell-based strategies include endothelial differentiation, pericyte-like function, paracrine effects and prevascularised constructs. Molecular strategies centre on vascular endothelial growth factor and platelet-derived growth factor, with stromal cell-derived factor-1 as a key homing axis. Material strategies include blood clots, hydrogels, three-dimensional bioprinting and sustained-release systems; cell-free strategies include cell homing, extracellular vesicles and migrasomes as an exploratory hypothesis. Evidence is graded, infection control is identified as a clinical prerequisite, and lessons from failed therapeutic-angiogenesis trials argue that single-factor interventions have a functional ceiling. Standardisation of evaluation methods and cell-free products remains a priority.

articles.title: Discordant evidence on corticosteroids in sepsis: a meta-research study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite an extensive evidence base of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews (SRs), current sepsis guidelines provide only weak recommendations for corticosteroid therapy, while available SRs report conflicting mortality conclusions. We aimed to characterize the evidence landscape of SRs evaluating corticosteroids for sepsis, including their clinical scope, underlying RCT evidence bases, mortality conclusions, and to explore potential sources of discordance.

METHODS: Meta-research study of SRs on corticosteroids in sepsis published between 2015 and 2025. Study-pool overlap was assessed using a SR×RCT inclusion matrix, Jaccard similarity (J), and hierarchical clustering. SRs and RCTs were classified according to standardized Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) profiles. We explored discordance in short-term mortality conclusions among clinically comparable SRs and potential associations with study-pool composition, target populations, and methodological characteristics.

RESULTS: Forty-two SRs including 121 unique RCTs were identified. More than half of pairwise SR comparisons shared no RCTs, and only three pairs showed high overlap (J > 0.8). SRs addressing similar intervention and target population profiles frequently relied on different study pools. Among 38 SRs with short-term mortality meta-analyses, 15 (39%) reported benefit and 23 (61%) no evidence of effect. Discordance occurred exclusively among SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies; conclusions were consistent for hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone (benefit) and hydrocortisone, ascorbic acid, and thiamine (no evidence of effect). SRs including adult sepsis ± shock populations more frequently reported benefit than those restricted to septic shock (62% vs 22%), although this comparison was based on only 22 SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies and estimates were imprecise. No single methodological or clinical factor consistently explained discordance.

CONCLUSIONS: SRs addressing apparently similar clinical questions frequently synthesized different underlying evidence bases and reported discordant conclusions. When selecting SRs to inform clinical decisions and recommendations for sepsis management, clinicians and guideline developers should consider not only methodological quality and reported PICO, but also whether the included RCTs adequately represent the intended clinical question.

articles.title: Characteristics of ischemic stroke patients with left atrial appendage thrombus detected by cardiac photon-counting detector computed tomography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early identification of left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) or transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients can have relevant treatment and prognostic implications. We investigated the prevalence of LAA thrombus in AIS/TIA patients and analyzed baseline characteristics and short-term outcomes according to the presence of LAA thrombus.

METHODS: We analyzed stroke patients who were admitted consecutively in our comprehensive stroke centre between March 2023 and December 2025 and received cardiac photon-counting computed tomography (CT) implemented in the acute stroke imaging protocol. We analyzed baseline clinical characteristics, echocardiographic and laboratory biomarkers, in-hospital mortality and in-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence according to the presence of LAA thrombus.

RESULTS: We included 577 patients with a median age of 75 years, 49.6% were female, and LAA thrombus was found in 49 patients (8.5%). The presence of LAA thrombus was independently associated with atrial fibrillation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 16.09, 95% confidence interval [95%CI] = 4.55-56.90, p < 0.001), severe left atrial dilatation (aOR = 3.48, 95%CI = 1.18-10.26, p = 0.009) and higher NT-proBNP (aOR per 1000pg/mL-increment = 1.10, 95%CI = 1.01-1.19, p = 0.022). In-hospital mortality was higher in patients with LAA thrombus (p = 0.003), but this association did not persist after adjustment for clinical stroke severity. In-hospital ischemic stroke recurrence was similar in both groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Stroke patients with LAA thrombus detected on cardiac CT performed as part of the acute stroke imaging protocol have different baseline characteristics which are indicative of more severe underlying atrial substrate for arrhythmogenesis.

articles.title: Uncoupling protein 2 inhibits porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus replication via autophagic degradation of viral Nsp12.
articles.abstract: Porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS) is a common disease caused by the porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) participates in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases, immune cell activation, and insulin secretion by β cells. However, its functional role in PRRSV infection remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated the relationship between UCP2 and PRRSV replication using in vitro models. We demonstrated that UCP2 restricts replication of the highly pathogenic PRRSV (HP-PRRSV) strain XH-GD in the in vitro cell systems tested. Experiments involving exogenous plasmid expression and siRNA knockdown demonstrated that UCP2 effectively inhibited PRRSV replication. Mechanistically, UCP2 interacts with PRRSV Nsp12 and degrades Nsp12 via the autophagy-lysosomal pathway. In contrast, UCP2 reduces the release of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) induced by PRRSV infection, thereby inhibiting viral replication. As a countermeasure, PRRSV inhibits the expression of UCP2. Further screening identified PRRSV nonstructural protein 4 (Nsp4) as a viral factor that restricts UCP2 expression and antagonizes its antiviral activity. Overall, these findings reveal the interactions between host proteins and PRRSV, as well as the novel mechanisms by which PRRSV achieves immune evasion, providing crucial insights into the pathogenesis of PRRSV infection.

articles.title: Occurrence of Toxocara spp. in companion animals and serological evidence of human exposure at the human-companion animal interface in Giza, Egypt.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Toxocariasis, caused by Toxocara spp., is one of the most neglected zoonotic parasitic diseases worldwide. In Egypt, integrated One Health studies investigating human, animal, and occupational risk factors remain limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of zoonotic Toxocara spp. in companion animals and to identify associated risk factors within a One Health framework.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Giza, Egypt, including dogs (n = 70) and cats (n = 35) from animal shelters and veterinary clinics, eosinophilic children (n = 227), and shelter workers (n = 22). Animal fecal samples were examined microscopically for intestinal parasites, while human serum samples were tested for anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Demographic characteristics and potential risk factors were collected through standardized questionnaires. Associations were evaluated using Pearson's Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, followed by binary logistic regression to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Toxocara canis-like eggs were detected in a percentage of 17.1% in canine cases, with no significant difference in positivity rates regarding sex. In contrast, T. canis positivity rate was significantly correlated with younger age, lack of anthelmintic medication, and concurrent detection of Cystoisospora species. Among the studied eosinophilic children, anti-Toxocara IgG antibodies were detected in 41/227 (18.1%). In the univariable analysis, rural residence was significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (COR = 2.08, 95% CI: 1.00-4.32; P = 0.047). Similarly, contact with soil (COR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.17-5.42; P = 0.02), consumption of unpurified water (COR = 2.80, 95% CI: 1.15-6.82; P = 0.02), and interaction with pets (COR = 3.19, 95% CI: 1.48-6.87; P = 0.002) were significantly associated with anti IgG seropositivity. In the multivariable binary logistic regression model, contact with soil remained significantly associated with anti-T. canis IgG seropositivity (AOR = 3.10, 95% CI: 1.17-8.66; P = 0.02). Consumption of unpurified water (AOR = 2.64, 95% CI: 1.03-6.78; P = 0.04) and interaction with pets (AOR = 3.60, 95% CI: 1.60-8.10; P = 0.002) were also independently associated with seropositivity. In contrast, the association with rural residence was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the other variables included in the model (AOR = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.25-1.17; P = 0.12).

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates substantial exposure to T. canis-like eggs among companion animals and children in Giza, Egypt, highlighting the need for integrated One Health interventions. Regular deworming of pets, public health education, and coordinated veterinary-medical surveillance are recommended to reduce toxocariasis at the human-companion animal interface.

articles.title: What the 2026 AHA acute ischemic stroke guideline changes in emergency care.
Acute Mastoiditis in Children in the Era of Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccines.
articles.abstract: This retrospective study assessed changes in acute mastoiditis (AM) incidence, bacteriology, and complications after pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV)-7 and PCV-13 introduction at Children's Hospital of Michigan, Detroit, from 2000 to 2018. In this review of 242 children with AM, 138 cases occurred during PCV-7 use (2000-2010) and 104 during PCV-13 use (2011-2018). Incidence did not change after PCV-13 introduction (P = .31). Streptococcus pneumoniae remained the predominant pathogen in both periods (P = .375), while Streptococcus pyogenes infections increased during PCV-13 era, affecting older children (median age, 87.5 vs 30.0 months for S pneumoniae). Complications occurred throughout including subperiosteal abscess (n = 39), venous sinus thrombosis (n = 10), and intracranial extension (n = 7). Partial or complete PCV vaccination was documented in 13 with S pneumoniae AM. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine-13 use was not associated with a reduction in occurrence of AM compared with PCV-7. Research is needed to evaluate the effect of pneumococcal vaccines on AM incidence and complications.

articles.title: Could Results from the VESALIUS-CV Trial Change the Current Management of Dyslipidemia by Primary Care Clinicians?
articles.abstract: The continuum of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. While significant therapies have evolved over the years, implementation challenges still exist. This publication reviews the roles of primary care clinicians (PCCs) in managing patients with dyslipidemia with or at risk of developing ASCVD. It also discusses how lipid management guidelines have evolved over the years, how such guidelines have affected lipid management by the primary care community, and how recent findings in a pre-event cardiovascular outcomes trial (VESALIUS-CV) will likely impact the primary care community's role in lipid management. Despite new guidelines and recent clinical data, most patients with ASCVD in the real world are undertreated and above therapeutic low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals. PCCs should aim to treat lipids to guideline-recommended LDL-C goals to manage an expanding population of patients who need intensive lipid management. Furthermore, ASCVD prevention should be conceptualized as a continuum of risk rather than solely as binary primary or secondary prevention categories, and PCCs should adjust their practice accordingly.

articles.title: How Do Sexual and Gender Minority Populations Experience the Diagnostic Process in Primary and Emergency Care: An Integrative Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals face healthcare disparities, affecting health outcomes including diagnostic safety. Diagnostic vulnerabilities can be especially pronounced in primary and emergency care settings. While previous reviews explored general healthcare disparities, the experiences of SGM populations during the diagnostic process remain unexplored. We conducted an integrative systematic review (PROSPERO CRD42024608397, unfunded) to examine how SGM patients, their care partners, and healthcare providers experience the diagnostic process in primary and emergency care and how provider communication shapes these experiences.

METHODS: We systematically searched MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, and LLBA (2015-November 2025) and included English-language, empirical studies on diagnostic process experiences for SGM patients, their care partners, or providers in primary and emergency care. A qualitative integrative synthesis combined inductive thematic and deductive content analysis, mapping onto diagnostic process stages, and the approachability features communication framework. We appraised risk of bias with the QATSDD quality assessment tool.

RESULTS: From 2207 identified studies, 43 met inclusion criteria. Most involved SGM patients (67%), with fewer provider (28%) or mixed samples. Studies spanned diagnostic stages, predominantly information gathering (n = 39, especially diagnostic testing (n = 29)); fewer addressed access (n = 15); and diagnosis communication (n = 9). Diagnostic experiences were shaped by structural barriers, provider competency, and healthcare interactions. Providers' affirming communication and SGM-specific knowledge supported trust, identity disclosure, appropriate care, and diagnostic safety, whereas non-affirming communication, cisheteronormativity, provider bias, and knowledge gaps contributed to avoidance or refusal of care, missed screening, and diagnostic delays.

DISCUSSION: This is the first review to systematically map experiences of SGM patients, their care partners, and providers against diagnostic process stages. Experiences were limited to high-income Western settings, underrepresenting care partners, and asexual and intersex populations. Diagnostic inequities among SGM patients intersect across structural, competency, and interactional factors, highlighting communication and system-level interventions as key to improving diagnostic safety and equity for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Preventing retinal damage in type 2 diabetes: the role of alpha-lipoic acid and neurotropic vitamins.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Diabetic retinopathy, a significant microvascular complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus, can potentially lead to vision loss. Due to their antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) and neurotropic vitamins (NVs) are utilized in the treatment of diabetic neuropathy. The potential benefits of these compounds on the retinal structures have also recently gained attention. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of ALA and NVs on the retinal ganglion cell layer (GCL) and central retinal thickness (CRT) in patients with type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 79 patients with diabetic neuropathy who had at least 6 months of follow-up data from a pool of 1150 type 2 diabetic patients whose outpatient clinic records were screened.The patients were divided into three groups: untreated, ALA monotherapy, and ALA combined with NVs. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) measurements obtained at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months were evaluated for all patients. The effects of ALA and NVs on GCL and CRT were investigated.

RESULTS: In the group receiving the combination of ALA and NVs, bilateral GCL values increased significantly from 105.2 ± 22.0 µm to 106.2 ± 20.4 µm in the right eye (p < 0.001) and from 99.4 ± 6.0 µm to 101.2 ± 7.4 µm in the left eye (p < 0.001). Similarly, CRT values increased significantly from 257.2 ± 20.4 µm to 260.6 ± 21.0 µm in the right eye (p = 0.047) and from 251.8 ± 25.5 µm to 254.8 ± 26.1 µm in the left eye (p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: ALA and NVs may have beneficial effects on retinal structural parameters and could represent a potential retinal neuroprotective approach in patients with diabetic retinopathy.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and the risk of major age-related eye diseases.
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP), an age-related hematologic condition associated with systemic inflammation, has uncertain associations with major eye diseases. We aimed to investigate the association of CHIP, including its major genetic subtypes and clone sizes, with the risk of cataract, glaucoma, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy (DR). UK Biobank participants enrolled during 2006-2010 were followed by linked electronic health records until March 2022. Whole-exome sequencing identified CHIP as somatic driver mutations with variant allele frequency ≥ 2%. Multivariable Cox regression was applied to assess hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI). The DR analysis was restricted to participants with diabetes. Of 436,469 participants (mean age, 56.4 years; 54.5% women), 14,110 (3.2%) had CHIP. During a median 14.4-year follow-up, 31,165 cataract, 12,393 glaucoma, 13,644 AMD, and 2,692 DR diagnoses occurred. CHIP was associated with cataract (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [1.03-1.14]), AMD (HR [95%CI]: 1.12 [1.04-1.21]), and DR (HR [95%CI]: 1.48 [1.25-1.74]), but the association with glaucoma overall did not reach statistical significance (HR [95%CI]: 1.08 [0.99-1.17]). The glaucoma association was statistically significant among participants without hypertension (HR [95%CI]: 1.22 [1.06-1.40]; P for interaction = 0.012). Associations varied by clone size and driver gene. Hematologic and inflammatory biomarkers mediated less than 5% of associations. CHIP was associated with incident cataract, AMD, and DR, and with glaucoma in participants without hypertension. These findings position CHIP as a potential non-ocular risk marker for several major age-related eye diseases. However, except for DR, effect sizes were small.

articles.title: Machine learning and artificial intelligence for predicting anti-TNF treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis causes joint inflammation, progressive structural damage, and marked variability in treatment response. Anti-tumour necrosis factor (anti-TNF) therapies have transformed management, yet 30-40% of patients do not respond adequately, so predicting response before treatment would be clinically valuable. This systematic review evaluates artificial intelligence and machine learning models developed to predict anti-TNF response in rheumatoid arthritis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, arXiv, and Google Scholar were searched for studies published between 2019 and 2026 following PRISMA 2020, with an initial search in June 2025 updated in May 2026. Selection, extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment using the Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Thirty studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 14 developed or validated at least one model with a treatment-specific analysis of response to a TNF inhibitor, using random forests, gradient boosting, support vector machines, and neural networks applied to clinical, registry, genetic, and transcriptomic data. Reported discrimination was highest in small transcriptomic studies and lowest in large registry studies, but this ordering tracked validation design rather than modelling approach: internally validated models reported the highest apparent performance, whereas externally validated clinical models plateaued at an area under the curve of approximately 0.70-0.72. Applying the risk-of-bias tool according to its published categories and combination rules, most models were at high risk of bias, driven by the analysis domain. No model has been evaluated for clinical impact or is available in a deployable form. The evidence is hypothesis-generating and does not yet support use of these models in routine rheumatology practice.

articles.title: Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network for Congenital Heart Disease Identification.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a common structural birth defect, and early screening is important for improving prognosis. Clinical cardiac ultrasound combines brightness-mode (B-mode) and color Doppler images from multiple standard views to assess cardiac morphology and hemodynamic abnormalities. Existing case-level models remain limited in modeling information exchange among standard views within each modality and cross-modal fusion between B-mode morphology and Doppler hemodynamics. The proposed Cross-View Constrained Encoder and Cross-Modal Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion Network (CVCE-CMSHFNet) addresses these limitations through two complementary components: a Multi-View Constrained Encoder (MVCE) and a Bidirectional Progressive Semantic-Hierarchy Fusion (BiPSHF) module. MVCE models relationships among the eight standard views within each modality. Sinkhorn-constrained transport and a parallel gated transformation update the view representations. Training-time Intra-Modal View Covariance Diversity Regularization (IVCDR) separately penalizes covariance similarity among B-mode view representations and among Doppler view representations. BiPSHF performs bidirectional cross-modal interaction at the view, view-group, and case levels. The view-group level organizes the eight standard views into four study-specific groups based on anatomical relationships and clinical assessment roles. CVCE-CMSHFNet aims to support clinical diagnosis by providing a case-level CHD probability for physician reference. Evaluation included 384 complete eight-view dual-modality cases from a 506-subject single-center echocardiography database. CVCE-CMSHFNet achieved 95.64% accuracy, 95.23% F1 score, 97.05% AUC, 94.44% sensitivity, and 96.67% specificity.

articles.title: Outcomes following repair of complex incisional hernias after orthotopic liver transplant using transversus abdominis release (tar): an institutional review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incisional hernia is a prevalent postoperative complication following orthotopic liver transplantation (OLT), primarily due to factors such as elevated body mass index (BMI), diabetes mellitus, and chronic immunosuppressive therapy. This patient cohort poses significant challenges for hernia repair, characterized by large defect sizes and ongoing immunosuppression. The current literature provides limited data on the long-term outcomes of complex abdominal wall reconstruction (AWR) in this population. This study aims to address this gap by presenting comprehensive outcomes of posterior component separation with transversus abdominis release (TAR) for patients with hernias following OLT.

METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive retrospective review using Columbia Hernia's prospectively maintained database to identify patients with incisional hernias post-OLT who underwent complex AWR via TAR from January 2018 to January 2025. We meticulously analyzed detailed demographic data and perioperative variables using univariate analysis. The primary outcome was hernia recurrence, while secondary outcomes included surgical-site morbidity and other postoperative complications.

RESULTS: Forty-eight liver transplant recipients underwent incisional hernia repair during the study period, of whom 41 underwent TAR and were included in the final analysis. Mean age was 61.0 years and mean BMI was 28.7 kg/m2. All patients were functionally independent and receiving active immunosuppression. Mean hernia defect area was 206.6 ± 168.3 cm2. Operative approaches included open repair in 24 patients (58.5%), robotic repair in 12 (29.3%), robotic hybrid repair in 4 (9.8%), and robotic repair converted to open in 1 (2.4%). Mean postoperative length of stay was 4.7 days, and mean follow-up was 15.3 months. Five patients (12.2%) developed hernia recurrence. Ninety-day readmission and reoperation rates were 9.8% and 2.4%, respectively. Surgical site infection occurred in 3 patients (7.3%), all of which were superficial. No mesh infections or deaths occurred.

CONCLUSION: Incisional hernias following OLT represent a technically challenging problem in chronically immunosuppressed patients. In this single-center series, TAR with retromuscular synthetic mesh was associated with acceptable short- to intermediate-term recurrence and wound morbidity. Open, robotic, and hybrid approaches were selectively utilized according to defect morphology and operative requirements. Larger multicenter studies with standardized hernia classification, detailed immunosuppression data, and longer follow-up are needed to better define optimal patient selection and operative approach.

articles.title: Retinal oxidative, structural and functional outcomes following melatonin administration in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize additional retinal oxidative, structural and functional outcomes in a previously published cohort of streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats.-- Street E 42, Redenção, Vitória de Santo Antão, PE, 55,612-050, Brazil.

- METHODS: Fifty male Wistar rats were allocated to control, untreated diabetic, concurrent melatonin, delayed melatonin or insulin-treated groups (10 per group). Melatonin was administered subcutaneously at 10 mg/kg for 20 days, starting at diabetes induction or after confirmation. Retinal superoxide production, NADPH oxidase activity, histology and microvascular morphology were assessed. Morphometry used five slides from five animals per group (one slide per animal; n = 5). Pancreatic glutathione and lipid peroxidation were additional tissue-specific measures. Electroretinography was described qualitatively because numerical results were unavailable. Previously published glycemic and insulin results are not reproduced.

RESULTS: Both melatonin groups showed lower retinal oxidative measures and more favorable morphometric outcomes than untreated diabetic animals. The reported comparisons did not identify significant differences between melatonin schedules for these endpoints. Pancreatic oxidative measures were also more favorable in treated animals. Descriptive electrophysiological observations did not establish functional recovery.

CONCLUSION: These findings extend the oxidative and morphological characterization of melatonin-associated retinal changes in a shared cohort. Neither schedule showed clear superiority and functional benefits or reversal of established retinopathy remain unproven.

articles.title: The Pharmacological Basis of SGLT2 Inhibitor-Mediated Kidney Protection: From Proximal Tubular Mechanisms to Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) remains the leading cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) worldwide despite advances in glycemic control, blood pressure management, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system blockade. The introduction of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors has fundamentally changed the management of CKD by consistently reducing kidney disease progression and cardiovascular events in patients both with and without diabetes. These findings indicate that the benefits of SGLT2 inhibition extend beyond glucose lowering and reflect broader effects on cardiorenal physiology. This review examines the pharmacological mechanisms underlying SGLT2 inhibitor-mediated kidney protection, integrating experimental evidence with findings from major clinical outcome trials. Current evidence supports a hierarchical mechanistic model in which inhibition of proximal tubular sodium-glucose reabsorption represents the primary pharmacological event, restoring tubule-glomerular feedback, reducing intraglomerular pressure, and lowering tubular transport workload. These upstream hemodynamic and metabolic effects are thought to initiate downstream improvements in kidney oxygen balance, mitochondrial function, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis, although the relative contribution of these pathways remains incompletely defined. We further examine how contemporary clinical trials validate this mechanistic framework across diverse CKD populations, including patients with and without diabetes and across a broad range of kidney function and albuminuria. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for phenotype-specific treatment strategies, rational combination therapy with complementary kidney-protective agents, and future directions in biomarker-guided precision medicine. Collectively, current evidence supports SGLT2 inhibitors as integrated cardiorenal therapies that modify fundamental determinants of CKD progression and provide the pharmacological foundation of contemporary kidney-protective treatment.

articles.title: Multihit TP53 allelic state independently predicts sepsis in myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Infection is a leading cause of treatment-related mortality in myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and TP53-mutated myeloid disease is increasingly recognized as immunosuppressive. Whether infection severity depends on TP53 allelic state, and could therefore guide supportive care, remains undefined.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied adults diagnosed with MDS or AML at a tertiary center between January 2020 and September 2024, classified by TP53 allelic status as wild type (WT), monohit, or multihit. Infection episodes, sepsis, and bacteremia within one year of diagnosis were assessed. Cumulative incidence was estimated by competing-risk analysis with death as a competing event; risk factors were identified by multivariable Cox regression.

RESULTS: Among 469 patients (236 MDS, 233 AML), 399 were WT, 12 monohit, and 58 multihit. The one-year cumulative incidence of any infection was higher in multihit patients (75.9%) than in WT (62.7%) and monohit (41.7%) patients (p = 0.0331), but the difference was most pronounced for sepsis (37.9% vs. 17.3% in WT; p = 0.0008). On multivariable analysis, multihit status independently predicted sepsis (HR 2.56, 95% CI 1.60-4.07, P < 0.001) but not overall infection (HR 1.30, 95% CI 0.93-1.82; p = 0.130). Among patients with infection, the proportion who experienced sepsis was higher in the multihit group (54.5% vs. 29.4%; P = 0.0016), and the association between multihit status and sepsis was most apparent in MDS.

CONCLUSION: Biallelic TP53 inactivation is associated less with susceptibility to infection per se than with progression of an established infection to sepsis. Incorporating TP53 allelic state into infection risk assessment may help refine antimicrobial prophylaxis and surveillance alongside disease-directed therapy, particularly in MDS.

articles.title: Ten myths about milrinone in pediatric cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is a severe and increasingly common condition in children, representing a global health and economic burden. Inodilators (i.e., vasoactive agents with inotropic and vasodilator effects), most commonly dobutamine and milrinone, are the cornerstone of pharmacological treatment for CS in children. Although pediatric guidelines still recommend dobutamine as the first-line inodilator in CS, the use of milrinone has become predominant in this indication. Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase - 3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects and is commonly regarded as offering several theoretical advantages over dobutamine. Based on a critical review of current evidence, we examine here ten myths about milrinone in pediatric CS. The hemodynamic profile of milrinone in CS appears to rely primarily on vasodilation, with limited evidence for clinically meaningful inotropic or lusitropic effects. Current data support a neutral effect on myocardial oxygen consumption and an efficacy in preventing low cardiac output syndrome after pediatric cardiac surgery, while milrinone clearance is reduced in acute kidney injury with unclear clinical significance. However, no consistent evidence demonstrates milrinone's superiority over dobutamine in reducing mortality, length of hospital stay, or tachyarrhythmia, nor its greater efficacy in patients receiving beta-blockers. Its presumed benefits in newborns and in patients with right ventricular failure or pulmonary hypertension remain uncertain and warrant further investigation. What is known: • Milrinone is a phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor that is thought to exert inotropic and lusitropic effects. • Milrinone has become the preferred inodilator over dobutamine in pediatric cardiogenic shock. What is new: • Milrinone's efficacy appears to stem from vasodilation rather than significant inotropy or lusitropy. • No consistent evidence shows its superiority over dobutamine; further study is warranted.

articles.title: Prolonged prophylactic antibiotic regimens may reduce periprosthetic infection in megaprosthetic reconstruction: a case series.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Megaprosthetic reconstruction (MPR) is associated with a substantially higher risk of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) compared to primary total joint arthroplasty. However, evidence guiding the optimal duration of antibiotic prophylaxis remains limited, and institutional practices vary considerably. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the incidence of PJI, antibiotic-related complications, and surgical outcomes in patients undergoing MPR followed by a prolonged prophylactic antibiotic regimen.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included patients undergoing MPR between May 2020 and November 2022 at a tertiary sarcoma referral centre. All patients received a standardised postoperative 12-week prophylactic antibiotic regimen consisting of two weeks of intravenous ampicillin/sulbactam followed by 10 weeks of oral rifampin and levofloxacin. The primary outcome was the incidence of PJI. Secondary outcomes included surgery-related complication and revision rates, antibiotic-related adverse events, and mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included into the study, of which 83% underwent MPR for oncologic conditions. The overall PJI rate was 2.1% at a mean follow-up of 39 months. Surgery-related complications occurred in 4.3%, and the revision rate was 4.3%. No antibiotic-related adverse events were documented during inpatient treatment or follow-up. All-cause mortality was 21.3%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective case series, a low incidence of PJI was observed in patients undergoing MPR followed by a standardised 12-week prophylactic antibiotic regimen. Thus, these findings might support the notion that extended prophylaxis could be a safe and effective strategy in high-risk patients undergoing MPR. However, the study design, limited sample size and absence of a control group restrict the conclusions that can be drawn from these findings, and comparative prospective studies are required to determine the effectiveness of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis following MPR.

articles.title: Tick vectors and exposure of dogs (Canis lupus familiaris) to spotted fever group rickettsiae in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
articles.abstract: Tick-borne rickettsioses remain a public health concern in Brazil, where their distribution is determined by the ecology of vector tick species. In Minas Gerais, human cases of Rickettsia rickettsii infection are recurrent. In contrast, Atlantic Forest spotted fever caused by Rickettsia parkeri strain Atlantic rainforest (ARF) has not yet been documented in the state, despite favorable environmental conditions and records of its vector, Amblyomma ovale. This study aimed to investigate the presence of R. parkeri ARF in A. ovale ticks infesting domestic dogs across ten municipalities representing nine mesoregions of Minas Gerais and to assess their exposure to spotted fever group (SFG) Rickettsia. A total of 300 dogs were examined, yielding 1,284 ticks from eight species. Rhipicephalus sanguineus sensu lato, Amblyomma sculptum, and A. ovale were the most prevalent species, with marked geographic variation in species composition and infestation indices. Serological analysis by indirect immunofluorescence assay (IFA) revealed a prevalence of SFG Rickettsia exposure above 50% in dogs from eight of the ten municipalities, with varying geometric mean titers, some as high as 4,096. Rickettsia parkeri ARF DNA was detected in only 1.5% of A. ovale ticks. These findings demonstrate widespread exposure of dogs to SFG Rickettsia and heterogeneous tick assemblages across Minas Gerais and confirm for the first time R. parkeri ARF circulation in the state of Minas Gerais State. This study is also the first statewide systematic survey of canine ticks in Minas Gerais and provides data to improve the understanding of the eco-epidemiology of tick-borne diseases and supports targeted surveillance strategies for human rickettsioses in the region.

articles.title: Managing post-bariatric weight recurrence with new obesity management medications.
articles.abstract: Recurrent weight gain (RWG) following metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) represents a major challenge in the long-term management of obesity and is distinct from insufficient weight loss and suboptimal clinical response, which reflect a primary inadequate response. RWG is defined as regain of ≥25% of the maximum weight lost, assessed ≥24 months after surgery. It affects approximately 35% of patients within 5 years of sleeve gastrectomy and approximately 15% within 5 years after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. With longer follow-up, the number of affected patients rises to about one-third. RWG is multifactorial: genetic predisposition, preoperative metabolic phenotype, inadequate or failed surgical anatomy, and neurohormonal and adipose tissue adaptations interact over time to cause it, and no single variable accounts for it. Randomized evidence indicates that the operation itself is a determinant of long-term response: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass elicits greater postprandial GLP1 secretion, more durable weight loss and higher rates of type 2 diabetes mellitus remission than sleeve gastrectomy, so procedure selection warrants as much attention as postoperative management. Treatment should therefore be specific to phenotype and procedure, escalating from lifestyle optimization to obesity management medications, endoscopic revision and revisional surgery, if needed. Randomized data now support semaglutide after MBS, whereas evidence for tirzepatide, combined endoscopic-pharmacological strategies, or treatment sequencing remains observational and real-world adherence is a major constraint. Multimodal, integrated approaches combining behavioural, pharmacological and surgical strategies could help to improve treatment strategies for patients who experience RWG. This Review discusses the factors that contribute to RWG after MBS, considerations for clinical management of RWG, and questions that future research should aim to address to improve and maintain weight loss and other clinical outcomes after MBS. The Review also discusses clinical approaches to insufficient weight loss and suboptimal clinical response after MBS.

articles.title: [Stress factors and coping strategies in the nursing and care of patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) suffering from treatment-resistant heart failure-a qualitative study of nursing staff in German intensive care units].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critical care nurses play a vital role in the care of patients with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and must be able to cope with various challenges. The aim of this study was to gain insight into the experiences of critical care nurses in caring for patients with a LVAD, to identify potential stressors, and thereby to determine the need for support.

METHODS: As part of a qualitative research design, nine intensive care nurses from Germany were interviewed between April and June 2025 using semi-structured, guided interviews. Data analysis was conducted using content analysis structured according to Kuckartz.

RESULTS: The greatest challenges for intensive care nurses were a lack of knowledge regarding the specific nursing requirements and the use of the LVAD, as well as structural and personnel-related conditions. While coping strategies are already in place, the majority of nurses would like to expand their knowledge.

CONCLUSION: By identifying various stressors, specific support services can be expanded or established for everyday clinical practice. Potential measures include building and regularly updating foundational knowledge through structured training programs, as well as ensuring that counseling services are readily available. In addition, specialized communication training and standardized work procedures are recommended.

articles.title: Effects of exercise interventions on physical fitness, fatigue, and quality of life in adult hematologic malignancy patients receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) experience significant declines in physical fitness, fatigue, and quality of life (QoL). The optimal exercise modality to address these issues remains unclear. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared the effects of different exercise interventions on physical fitness, fatigue, and QoL in this population.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CINAHL from inception to January 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating structured exercise interventions in adult HSCT patients were included. A NMA was performed using Stata 19.0, with effect sizes calculated as standardized mean differences (SMD) or mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to rank interventions.

RESULTS: Twenty RCTs involving 1,886 patients were included. For QoL, inspiratory muscle training (IMT) was the only intervention showing significant improvement compared with usual care (SMD = 0.54, 95% CI [0.04, 1.04]), with the highest SUCRA value (0.455). For fatigue, supervised combined exercise (SCE) (SMD =  - 0.39, 95% CI [ - 0.67, - 0.12]) and multidirectional walking/exergaming/whole body vibration (MDW/EXG/WBV) (SMD =  - 0.66, 95% CI [ - 1.29, - 0.04]) were significantly effective; MDW/EXG/WBV ranked highest (SUCRA = 0.691). For physical fitness, SCE significantly improved 6-min walk test (MD = 46.24 m, 95% CI [20.87, 71.61]) and peak oxygen uptake (MD = 2.37, 95% CI [0.56, 4.19]), ranking first for VO2peak (SUCRA = 0.919). MDW/EXG/WBV showed the greatest improvement in handgrip strength (MD = 11.9 kg, 95% CI [6.34, 17.46]; SUCRA = 0.992). No intervention significantly improved 30-s sit-to-stand test.
