CONCLUSION: This NMA suggests that different exercise modalities may have differential effects on distinct outcomes in HSCT recipients. Supervised combined exercise showed the greatest improvements in cardiorespiratory fitness measures, while multidirectional walking/exergaming/whole body vibration ranked highest for fatigue reduction and handgrip strength improvement. Inspiratory muscle training was the only intervention associated with statistically significant QoL improvement, although this finding should be interpreted with caution given the moderate SUCRA value and wide confidence interval. These findings provide preliminary evidence to inform the selection of exercise modalities within individualized rehabilitation planning; however, the present analysis did not directly evaluate whether outcome-guided or individualized prescription strategies improve clinical outcomes compared with uniform exercise programs, and future confirmatory studies with head-to-head comparisons are needed before practice-changing recommendations can be made.

articles.title: Sore throat? The brain has surprising control over how ill you feel.
Real-world treatment patterns in patients receiving osteoanabolic osteoporosis therapy: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Treatment patterns were evaluated in US patients prescribed the osteoporosis therapies abaloparatide, teriparatide, and romosozumab. Despite current guidelines, many patients did not take these medications for the recommended time, nor receive recommended follow-up osteoporosis therapy after finishing the medication. Further research is needed to develop strategies to overcome these gaps in care.

PURPOSE: The goal of osteoporosis therapy is to reduce fracture risk. The persistence and sequence of therapy affect clinical outcomes. This study evaluated real-world patterns of treatment persistence and sequence in US patients prescribed osteoanabolic therapies.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used administrative claims data from ICON's Symphony Health Integrated Dataverse database. Men and women ≥50 years of age prescribed the osteoanabolic therapies abaloparatide (ABL), teriparatide (TPTD), or romosozumab (ROMO) were included. The index date was the date of the first osteoanabolic prescription claim; patients were required to have medical and pharmacy records for at least 5 years before and at least 1 year after discontinuation of the index osteoanabolic therapy.

RESULTS: This study included 43,429 men and women (16,592 [38%] ABL, 19,491 [45%] TPTD, and 7346 [17%] ROMO). The most common osteoanabolic prescriber specialties were endocrinology, rheumatology, and family medicine. Despite differences in labeled duration of use, persistence rates were low, with only 35% of ABL and 33% of TPTD patients receiving therapy for more than 12 months, while 56% of ROMO patients received therapy for more than 9 months. In the 12 months after discontinuation of osteoanabolic therapy, 28% (ABL), 26% (TPTD), and 57% (ROMO) of patients received subsequent antiresorptive therapy. The most common therapies before and after an osteoanabolic were oral bisphosphonates and denosumab.

CONCLUSION: Despite existing clinical guidelines, this analysis found major gaps in osteoporosis treatment among US adults. Further research is required to develop strategies to overcome the obstacles in applying standard of care practices.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of different exercise modalities and doses on cancer-related fatigue: a systematic review and dose-response network meta-analysis of 166 randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To comprehensively evaluate the dose-response relationship between various exercise modalities and cancer-related fatigue (CRF) in cancer population.

METHODS: Exercise dose was calculated as the product of duration, frequency, and intensity and expressed in metabolic equivalent of task minutes per week (MET-min/week) to facilitate comparisons across studies. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) were used to assess CRF, with positive SMDs indicating improvements compared with the control group. Bayesian dose-response network meta-analysis was conducted using a quadratic model to characterize dose-response relationships. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework.

RESULTS: A total of 166 studies, involving 14,076 patients, were included in the systematic review. The findings revealed that aerobic exercise, resistance training, combined aerobic and resistance training, yoga, traditional Chinese exercise, and walking were all significantly associated with reduced fatigue in cancer patients undergoing primary treatment. The model-identified greatest effect was observed for yoga at 500 MET-min/week (SMD = 1.97, 95% CrI: 0.90, 3.04) for reducing CRF in this group. For cancer survivors who had completed primary treatments, aerobic exercise, combined aerobic and resistance training, yoga, and Pilates were significantly associated with reduced CRF. The model-identified greatest effect was observed for Pilates at 310 MET-min/week (SMD = 2.05, 95% CrI: 0.07, 4.01) for alleviating CRF in cancer survivors.

CONCLUSIONS: Seven exercise modalities showed potential benefits for managing CRF, with dose-response patterns identified. These exploratory findings may serve as a reference for future intervention studies; however, further well-designed RCTs are needed to validate the findings, given the very low to moderate certainty of evidence.

articles.title: Harnessing smartwatches to spot undiagnosed hypertension.
FKBP10 dictates RAD51 stability to drive resistance of DNA-damaging therapies in breast cancer.
articles.abstract: Despite substantial advances in targeted therapeutic regimens for breast cancer (BC), clinical management remains challenging for refractory and therapy-resistant cases, especially for molecular subtypes lacking validated actionable targets. Here, we identified that FK506-binding protein 10 (FKBP10), a peptidyl-proline isomerases, was strikingly elevated in BC tissues and potentiated the malignant behaviors of BC cells in vitro and in vivo. Besides, we discovered that FKBP10 was positively correlated with enhanced homologous recombination (HR)-mediated DNA repair and drove broad resistance to multiple DNA-damaging therapies, including cisplatin, ionizing radiation (IR) and PARP inhibitor. Mechanistically, FKBP10 physically interacted with the core HR repair protein RAD51 via a proline 22-containing motif. This interaction competitively disrupted the recognition of RAD51 by heat shock cognate 70 (HSC70), thereby protecting RAD51 from chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA)-dependent degradation. Furthermore, FKBP10 attenuated excessive CMA flux to further stabilize RAD51 in the manner of ATF6-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS). Importantly, we characterized a clinically actionable repurposing strategy using selumetinib, which transcriptionally repressed FKBP10 by blocking the MEK/ERK/ELK1 signaling cascade. This pharmacological intervention robustly sensitized multiple preclinical BC models to chemoradiotherapy and PARP inhibition. Collectively, our findings uncover a previously unappreciated function of FKBP10 in driving BC progression and resistance to DNA-damaging therapies, underscoring its strong potential as a tractable therapeutic target for treatment-refractory BC subsets.

articles.title: LPAR5 restrains sepsis-induced immunosuppression by limiting STING-mediated dendritic cell ferroptosis and ISG+ cDC2 subset emergence.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced immunosuppression is a major cause of secondary infection and mortality, yet the mechanisms governing dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction and loss remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify lysophosphatidic acid receptor 5 (LPAR5) as a critical regulator of DC survival and immune competence during sepsis. Integrative analysis of septic murine transcriptomic datasets and qRT‒PCR profiling of peripheral blood from patients with sepsis revealed the conserved upregulation of LPAR5, predominantly in conventional DCs (cDCs) in mice, and lower LPAR5 expression was associated with greater disease severity. Conditional deletion of Lpar5 in cDCs accelerated DC depletion, impaired DC maturation and antigen presentation, diminished naive CD4+ T-cell priming, and exacerbated bacterial burden, secondary infection, and mortality. Single‑cell RNA sequencing of splenic DCs from LPAR5‑deficient mice revealed that excessive stimulator of interferon genes (STING)‑type I interferon signaling with two parallel features, namely, ferroptotic death of cDCs and the emergence of an immunosuppressive interferon‑stimulated gene‑positive (ISG+) cDC2 subset, exacerbated immune paralysis. Mechanistically, LPAR5 interacts with the C-terminal tail of STING, limiting TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) recruitment and restraining STING-dependent lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic death. Pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis in vivo and of STING or TBK1 signaling in vitro restored DC survival. These findings define a previously unrecognized LPAR5-STING-TBK1 axis that safeguards DC homeostasis and identify the ISG+ cDC2 subset as a pathogenic contributor to sepsis-induced immunosuppression, highlighting LPAR5 as a potential therapeutic target to preserve antimicrobial immunity in sepsis.

articles.title: NAION during incretin-based therapy: an optic nerve head still adapted to hypertension.
Insulin-independent glucose uptake into mouse skeletal muscle by a sodium/glucose linked transporter.
articles.abstract: Exercise is a cornerstone therapy for diabetes because working skeletal muscles take up glucose at dramatically greater rates than postprandial uptake and, notably, do so without a requirement for insulin. Insulin-independent glucose uptake operates normally during exercise and other conditions when adrenergic stimulation inhibits pancreatic insulin release, and it provides a means of glucose disposal in insulin resistant conditions. However, the mechanisms of insulin-independent glucose uptake are not fully understood. Here, we describe a previously unrecognized glucose uptake pathway in muscle, which we refer to as mSGLT based on shared properties with the sodium/glucose cotransporter family (SGLT/Slc5a). In contrast to the abundant muscle GLUT4 transporter, mSGLT activity is not regulated by insulin, requires Na,K-ATPase-α2 activity, and transports the hexose α-methyl-D-glucoside (αMDG), a glucose derivative that is handled by SGLTs but not GLUT4. mSGLT shares antigenicity with the kidney SGLT2 and localizes to the muscle t-tubules together with Na,K-ATPase-α2 and MAP17, the regulatory subunit of SGLT2. Skeletal muscles do not express a full-length transcript of Slc5a2, and mSGLT shows weak affinity for SGLT2-specific inhibitors. mSGLT may be a muscle SGLT isoform. mSGLT and its regulation offer potential muscle-specific targets for treating hyperglycemia and conditions when insulin-stimulated glucose disposal into muscle is impaired.

articles.title: Serum calprotectin in early neonatal infection: added value beyond interleukin-6 and C-reactive protein.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of serum calprotectin (SCP) versus C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in newborns with suspected early-onset sepsis (EOS) and to identify neonatal and maternal determinants of SCP.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of SCP measurements from residual IL-6 material. Neonates undergoing infection evaluation within 48 h after birth were included. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed by receiver operating characteristics (ROC) analyses across time windows. Multivariable regression identified predictors of SCP.

RESULTS: Of 566 screened infants, 355 were included (median gestational age 38.1 weeks); infection was confirmed in 112 (31.4%), including 20 EOS (5.6%). At 0-18 h, SCP showed moderate accuracy (area under the curve (AUC) 0.735), slightly lower than IL-6 but higher than CRP. SCP peaked at 30-45 h (AUC 0.975). IL-6 had the highest negative predictive value (NPV), combining it with SCP improved discrimination. CRP performed best at 18-30 h (AUC 0.932) and >45 h (0.943). Gestational age, meconium-stained amniotic fluid and multiple gestation predicted higher SCP.

CONCLUSION: SCP shows time-dependent performance, reaching high accuracy at 30-45 h and adding value to IL-6-based assessment. It may support multimodal sepsis diagnostics, prospective studies should validate cut-offs and its role in preterm infants.

IMPACT: Serum calprotectin showed time-dependent diagnostic performance in neonates with suspected early-onset infection. Serum calprotectin added value to early IL-6-based assessment and showed strongest stand-alone performance at 30-45 h after initiation of infection evaluation. These findings support time-adapted biomarker interpretation and warrant prospective evaluation of the potential role of SCP in neonatal antibiotic stewardship.

articles.title: Diabetic foot disease.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot disease (DFD) encompasses the lower-extremity complications of diabetes mellitus, including peripheral neuropathy, peripheral artery disease, ulceration, infection and amputation. An estimated 199 million people worldwide had DFD in 2017, including 18.6 million with foot ulcers, which precede most lower-extremity amputations. The 5-year mortality approaches 30% after ulceration and >70% after major amputation, rivalling that of many advanced cancers. DFD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged, rural and underserved populations, creating wide disparities in outcomes. Although DFD has traditionally been viewed as a neuropathic complication of diabetes mellitus, most clinically overt disease is neuroischaemic. Neuropathy permits injury to go unnoticed, whereas peripheral artery disease, which is present in ~50% of patients with foot ulcers, impairs healing and substantially increases the risk of amputation. The Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification has therefore emerged as a unifying framework for risk stratification, whereas multidisciplinary 'toe and flow' teams and advances in revascularization, wound care and pressure offloading have transformed management. Even after ulcer healing, recurrence reaches 40% at 1 year and ~60% within 3 years, reframing ulcer healing as remission rather than cure and emphasizing the need for lifelong surveillance and secondary prevention.

articles.title: Real-World Effectiveness of SGLT2i on Incident Kidney Outcomes in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Normoalbuminuria-A Territory-Wide Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Normoalbuminuric chronic kidney disease (NACKD) is increasingly prevalent in Type 2 diabetes (T2D). Here, we evaluated the kidney effects of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) among T2D patients with baseline normoalbuminuria, taking into consideration their interim development of albuminuria, a risk factor for kidney function decline.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a real-world territory-wide electronic health record database, T2D patients with normoalbuminuria between January 2015 and December 2019 were identified. Incident kidney outcome was defined as a composite of sustained ≥ 40% decline in eGFR or end-stage kidney disease. Time-dependent Cox regression was used to evaluate the kidney effects of SGLT2i, modelling SGLT2i use and interim albuminuria status as time-varying covariates. Conditional logistic regression with time-dependent propensity score matching (TDPSM) was conducted to further evaluate the effects of SGLT2i in NACKD patients.

RESULTS: Among the 226 434 T2D patients with baseline normoalbuminuria, over a median follow-up of 7.17 years (IQR: 5.50-8.17), use of SGLT2i (HR, 0.62, 95% CI, 0.57-0.66; p < 0.001) and interim development of albuminuria (HR, 1.90, 95% CI, 1.84-1.96; p < 0.001) were independently associated with incident kidney outcome, which remained statistically significant in subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In TDPSM, use of SGLT2i was associated with a lower risk of incident kidney outcome among NACKD patients (OR, 0.61, 95% CI, 0.49-0.77; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In T2D patients with normoalbuminuria, regardless of the presence of CKD, SGLT2i use was associated with a significantly lower risk of incident kidney outcome.

articles.title: Metformin in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate associations of metformin exposure with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and lactic or metabolic acidosis in adults with Type 2 diabetes and advanced CKD (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2) not receiving chronic dialysis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane from inception through 5 September 2026 for observational cohort studies evaluating metformin exposure in this population. Comparator strategies included non-use, discontinuation and alternative glucose-lowering therapy. Data were synthesized using Bayesian random-effects models with empirical heterogeneity priors (primary) and frequentist random-effects models. Certainty of the evidence was assessed using the GRADE framework.

RESULTS: Ten cohort studies were included. For ESKD, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) from the Bayesian analysis was 0.64 (95% CrI: 0.45-0.92; 99% posterior probability of HR < 1). Estimates for MACE (HR 0.88, 95% CrI: 0.72-1.08) and all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CrI: 0.73-1.10) were imprecise. Lactic or metabolic acidosis showed an increased-risk estimate with a wide CrI (HR 1.39, 95% CrI: 0.76-2.49). Certainty of the evidence was very low for all outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: For ESKD, the pooled Bayesian estimate was below the null, whereas estimates for all-cause mortality and MACE remained uncertain, and an increased risk of acidosis could not be excluded. Given the very low certainty of the evidence and the heterogeneity of treatment strategies, these findings should be interpreted with considerable caution. Further randomized or well-designed observational evidence using clearly defined treatment strategies is needed.

articles.title: Cortical Hypoperfusion in Acute Anorexia Nervosa Is Graded Along the Sensorimotor-Association Hierarchy.
articles.journal: The International journal of eating disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cortical gray-matter changes in anorexia nervosa (AN) are among the largest reported in psychiatry, but the functional-metabolic state of that tissue is largely unknown. Because cortical energy use is highest in transmodal association cortex (prefrontal, parietal, and temporal regions of the default-mode and frontoparietal networks), a reduced energy supply predicts a graded rather than uniform reduction in perfusion (blood delivery to tissue).

METHOD: A total of 44 acutely underweight women with AN and 45 healthy women underwent 3 T pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling with partial-volume correction. Cerebral blood flow was compared between groups across the Schaefer 100 regions 7 networks atlas, age-adjusted and false-discovery-rate-corrected, and the case-control map was compared with the principal functional gradient (the axis running from sensorimotor to transmodal cortex), with cortical thickness in the same participants, and with 18 PET and SPECT receptor maps.

RESULTS: Perfusion was lower in AN in 97 of 100 regions and maximal in orbitofrontal and prefrontal cortex (composite d = -0.56). The deficit scaled with position along the principal functional gradient (ρ = -0.56), an axis unrelated to perfusion in health, and was recoverable in individual brains (d = -0.53). Thinning was widespread but unrelated to gradient position, and the two effect maps did not correspond. Hypoperfusion was greater where D1, CB1, mGluR5, M1, 5-HT2A, and μ-opioid systems are dense, the dopaminergic, cannabinoid, glutamatergic, and muscarinic ones persisting after gradient adjustment.

DISCUSSION: Cortical perfusion in acute AN is not uniformly reduced but organized along the cortex's principal functional axis, dissociable from cortical thinning and aligned with reward-related neurochemistry.

articles.title: Sensitive First Line Screening for Early-Stage Type 1 Diabetes on Dried Blood Spots.
Essential Paediatric Life Support Skills: A Set of Rolling Cart-Based Simulations in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Frequent high occupancy combined with increased rates of nursing turnover in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) has led to a limited ability to perform in-room high-fidelity simulations and an increased need for focused life support training for PICU personnel.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary team of physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, and undergraduate students implemented various simulations in the PICU August through December 2022. Simulations were conducted via a rolling-cart model to capture the largest audience and included, but were not limited to, chest compressions, defibrillation, bag-mask ventilation, push-pull fluid bolus administration, emergency cart utilization, and intraosseous access.

RESULTS: Twelve simulation sessions were performed. Twenty-four participants supplied feedback, with the majority of responses being overwhelmingly positive. In answer to the question 'The content of the simulation was relevant to my current role in the PICU', over 83% of the respondents said that they 'strongly agree'. 100% of respondents would recommend the simulation they performed to colleagues. Additionally, the participation rate was high, with a median of 10 participants per session. For comparison, the PICU in-room simulations had a median of six participants per session.

DISCUSSION: Conducting rolling cart-based simulations involving life support practices is a well-received method of education and garners high participation from PICU health care workers. This model can be beneficial in times when resources are limited.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Maintaining life support competency for staff in the PICU can be well supported by brief, low-fidelity rolling cart-based simulations.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and general public were not involved in the study. Staff from the paediatric intensive care unit were involved by participating in the bedside simulations.

articles.title: Differentiating between cognitive impairment and patient non-adherence: the utility of Hospital-in-the-Home for optimisation of diabetes mellitus care.
articles.abstract: Hospital in the Home (HITH) provides a unique model for delivering acute care alongside functional and cognitive assessment in older adults. This is relevant for diabetes self-management, where cognitive impairment is of particular relevance and guidance for older patients living at home with cognitive impairment is limited. HITH enables home-environment evaluation of self-management and supports individualised care planning. In this case, home-based assessment identified mild cognitive impairment not diagnosed in hospital, prompting simplified therapy, relaxed glycaemic targets and coordinated supports. This approach facilitated safe diabetes management, potentially reduced the risk of hospital readmission and prioritised patient autonomy by enabling them to remain home.

articles.title: Improve the Move: Using quality improvement methodology in the deployed setting to enhance MEDEVAC capability and safety.
Ins and Outs of Lysosomal Ca2+: Recent Advances.
articles.journal: Cold Spring Harbor perspectives in biology
articles.abstract: Lysosomes are multifunctional organelles that store and release calcium ions (Ca2+), a key second messenger. Two-pore channels (TPCs) and members of the transient receptor potential (TRP) mucolipin (TRPML) subfamily are the principal lysosomal Ca2+ release channels, but how Ca2+ is taken up by lysosomes is less clear. TPCs have emerged as unusual ion channels that are able to dramatically switch their ion selectivity from a Ca2+-permeable state to a more Na+-selective state to differentially control cell-wide Ca2+ signals and lysosomal function in an agonist-selective manner. Long-sought accessory proteins that confer sensitivity of these channels to the Ca2+ mobilizing messenger nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NAADP) have been identified as JPT2 and Lsm12. Functional roles for TPCs in trafficking both inwardly (phagocytosis) as well as outwardly (hormone/inflammatory mediator secretion and adhesion molecule presentation) have been resolved-roles likely linked to the actions of TPCs at membrane contact sites between the endolysosomal system and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Gain-of-function in TPC2 by mutation, or by loss of a negative channel regulation (through TMEM63A), causes pigmentation and pancreatic dysfunction, respectively. Inhibiting TPCs by molecular or chemical means, in particular with tetrandrine (for which analog-bound structures exist), is proving beneficial in models of Alzheimer disease, Parkinson's disease, stroke, and melanoma. Select activation of TPC2 by new "mode-switching" agonists appears to be equally beneficial in correcting lysosomal storage disorders and Parkinson's disease. Like TPCs, TRP mucolipins are activated by the phosphoinositide PI(3,5)P2 More recently discovered endogenous TRP mucolipin activators include pressure and PI(3)P. Also, like TPCs, TRP mucolipins appear functionally coupled to Ca2+ channels on the sarcoplasmic reticulum with a surprising role for TRPML1 in generating ryanodine receptor-dependent subcellular Ca2+ signals underpinning smooth muscle contractility. Insight into regulation of autophagy by TRP mucolipins accrues; we also now know that activation of TRPML1 results in direct Ca2+ transfer from lysosomes to mitochondria at contact sites between the two organelles, and that this communication is disrupted in Mucolipidosis type IV, as well as in models of other neurogenerative diseases. TRP mucolipins are implicated in lung dysfunction and cancer, with the first identification of cancer-causing mutations in TRPML3. TRP mucolipin agonists have now been used successfully to correct phenotypes in a number of disease models, and agonist, as well as antagonist-bound structures, are providing new atomic insight into channel workings. The molecular basis for lysosomal Ca2+ uptake continues to be actively investigated. Candidates include the Ca2+ transporter TMEM165, the mutation of which is known to cause congenital disorders of glycosylation, and pumps such as ATP13A2 and those found typically on the ER.

articles.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival.

METHODS: We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.

FINDINGS: Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p<0·0001 in the training cohort). Multivariate analysis confirmed risk stratification based on the multitask hybrid model score as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. Analysis of patients with stage II or stage III disease in the training cohort and internal and external validation cohorts showed that in those with low predicted scores versus high predicted scores, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in patients with low scores but not those with high scores. In the immunotherapy cohorts, objective response rates were higher for patients with high predicted scores than for those with low predicted scores (54·5% vs 5·6%; p<0·0001 in immunotherapy cohort 1 and 53·1% vs 9·7%; p=0·0010 in immunotherapy cohort 2).

INTERPRETATION: By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: DNA methylation: tuning plant immunity.
articles.abstract: Pathogenic microorganisms threaten global food security by reducing crop yield and quality. Plants employ a two-tiered immune system, comprising pattern-triggered immunity and effector-triggered immunity, to resist infection. Beyond genetic factors, dynamic DNA methylation serves as a critical epigenetic regulator, fine-tuning immune responses by modulating gene expression, systemic acquired resistance, and transgenerational immune memory. This review synthesizes current understanding of how DNA methylation and active demethylation shape plant disease resistance, highlighting the context-dependent roles of the RNA-directed DNA methylation pathway and its components. We further integrate recent structural insights into epigenetic complexes and nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat resistosomes, linking molecular architecture to immune function. Finally, the translational potential and challenges of applying DNA methylation mechanisms to enhance crop resilience and sustainable agriculture are evaluated.

articles.title: Why organelles face the enemy.
articles.abstract: Plant cells reconfigure their internal architecture upon microbial attack by repositioning organelles toward the host-pathogen interface. Although this phenomenon is well documented, the functional significance remains an open question. Here, we propose that organelle repositioning represents a strategic spatial reorganization of cellular activities to enhance localized immune signaling, coordinate interorganellar communication, and support focal defense metabolism. At the same time, pathogens can exploit these dynamics to suppress defense responses and access host resources. We argue that organelle repositioning contributes to a dynamic host-pathogen interface, shaped by spatiotemporal organelle remodeling, metabolite exchange, resource redistribution, and membrane contact site formation. We discuss testable hypotheses explaining why plant organelles converge at infection sites, considering the plant's and the microbe's perspectives.

articles.title: Food Environments, Structural Disadvantage, and Risk of Gestational Diabetes and Preeclampsia.
articles.journal: Women's health issues : official publication of the Jacobs Institute of Women's Health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity is a modifiable risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and preeclampsia, conditions that elevate maternal morbidity, mortality, and long-term cardiovascular risk. Lifestyle interventions are standard preconception recommendations for risk reduction, yet their feasibility is shaped by neighborhood and structural contexts. To explore these relationships, we evaluated associations of GDM and preeclampsia with neighborhood food environments, access to vendors authorized to accept benefits from the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), and racialized economic segregation.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic medical records from individuals with live births (N = 12,635) at three Maryland hospitals (2016-2021). Neighborhood exposures included the following: 1) food swamps-areas with a high density of unhealthy food retailers relative to healthy ones-measured using the modified Retail Food Environment Index (mRFEI); 2) racialized economic segregation, measured using the Index of Concentration at the Extremes (ICE); and 3) WIC vendor density per 1,000 residents. All exposures were modeled in tertiles, with the lowest tertile (Q1) indicating the most disadvantaged or lowest access and the highest (Q3) as reference. We used multivariable logistic regression with generalized estimating equations to assess associations with GDM and preeclampsia.

RESULTS: Lower WIC access (lowest vs. highest tertile: adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] [1.02, 1.41]) and greater neighborhood disadvantage (ICE Q1 vs. Q3: aOR, 1.21; 95% CI [1.01, 1.44]) were associated with higher odds of GDM. No neighborhood measures were consistently associated with preeclampsia.

CONCLUSION: Structural disadvantage and lower WIC vendor density were associated with higher odds of GDM but not preeclampsia. Expanding nutrition assistance infrastructure and addressing neighborhood disadvantage may improve maternal cardiometabolic health.

articles.title: Development and content validation of entrustable professional activities for radiation oncology residency training: A modified Delphi and multi-specialty consensus study.
articles.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Competency-based medical education increasingly emphasizes structured assessment aligned with authentic clinical practice. Entrustable professional activities (EPAs) translate competencies into observable and assessable workplace tasks; however, no locally adapted EPA framework has been established for radiation oncology residency training in Taiwan.

METHODS: We conducted a three-round consensus development at National Taiwan University Hospital. In Round 1, a five-member task force developed candidate EPAs through literature review and expert discussion. In Round 2, 15 departmental faculty members and residents evaluated each EPA across multiple domains. Content Validity Indices (CVIs), interquartile ranges, and qualitative feedback informed iterative revision. In Round 3, a panel of eight multi-specialty experts assessed the revised EPAs using the Quality of Entrustable Professional Activities (QUEPA) and Queen's EPA Quality Rubric (EQual) instruments; five of the eight had not participated in the earlier rounds. Mean rubric scores and inter-rater agreement were calculated.

RESULTS: Eight candidate EPAs were proposed in Round 1. Fifteen of 20 invited participants completed Round 2 (75%). All eight EPAs were rated suitable for inclusion by at least 80% of respondents; item-level CVIs were ≥0.80 for 37 of the 40 EP A × dimension combinations, and the scale-level CVI for suitability was 0.93. In Round 3, all EPAs exceeded established quality thresholds on both QUEPA (mean 4.80-4.95) and EQual (mean 4.72-4.88). Inter-rater agreement was near-perfect (Gwet's AC2 = 0.94-0.99). All eight EPAs were retained in the final framework.

CONCLUSION: This single-centre study developed and validated the first EPA framework for radiation oncology residency training in Taiwan. The framework provides a structured foundation for competency-based assessment; its educational and clinical impact, and its transferability to other institutions, remain to be evaluated.

articles.title: High-alert medication safety in Pediatric critical care: A multinational analysis of nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-alert medications are frequently used in pediatric intensive care units and can cause serious harm when used in error. Multinational evidence on pediatric intensive care nurses' knowledge and reporting barriers remains limited.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional multinational study was conducted among 705 pediatric intensive care nurses from Egypt, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Syria, and Iraq. Data were collected using a sociodemographic and professional form, a 10-item High-Alert Medication Knowledge Questionnaire, and a 23-item Attitudes Toward Medication Errors and Error Reporting Questionnaire. Descriptive, correlation, simple regression, and dummy-coded multiple regression analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27.

RESULTS: The mean knowledge score was 5.46 ± 2.69 on the 0-10 scale, corresponding to 54.55% of the maximum possible score. Professional and organizational consequences had the highest mean percentage among attitude domains (59.18%), followed by fear and punitive barriers (50.94%); beliefs about error prevention and safety culture had the lowest percentage (33.45%). Knowledge showed weak correlations with reporting-related attitude domains. Multiple regression showed that knowledge was associated with gender, country, and high-alert medication safety training, whereas total attitude was associated with country and total nursing experience.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric intensive care nurses showed important gaps in high-alert medication safety knowledge, while reporting attitudes reflected persistent organizational and professional barriers. Findings support competency-based education, just-culture reporting systems, feedback mechanisms, and work-system redesign.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Parenteral Prostacyclin Use in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease-Associated Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIM: Robust evidence to inform the use of parenteral prostacyclin agents (PPAs) in adults with congenital heart disease-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (CHD-PAH) is lacking. We aimed to evaluate long-term haemodynamic, functional, and survival outcomes in a contemporary single-centre cohort of patients with CHD-PAH treated with PPA.

METHOD: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults with CHD-PAH treated with parenteral prostacyclin therapy at a single tertiary centre from 2000 to 2024.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients initiated a PPA between 2000 and 2024 (epoprostenol, n=17, intravenous treprostinil, n=7, subcutaneous treprostinil, n=5). Median age at initiation was 36 years, and two-thirds had unrepaired congenital lesions. At first follow-up, right heart catheterisation after starting PPA therapy, prostacyclin therapy was associated with significant reductions in mean pulmonary artery pressure (-7.7 mmHg; p=0.003) and pulmonary vascular resistance (-5.4 Wood Units; p=0.001), as well as increases in cardiac index (1.2 L/min/min2; p=0.002), and pulmonary artery oxygen saturation (9%; p=0.005). Haemodynamic improvements were similar between patients receiving epoprostenol and those receiving treprostinil. Five- and 10-year survival rates were 86% and 58%, respectively, and three patients were able to undergo delayed defect closure.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with CHD-PAH, parenteral prostacyclin therapy is associated with significant improvements in pulmonary haemodynamics and functional capacity, along with favourable long-term survival. These findings highlight the need for larger multicentre studies to refine patient selection and optimise treatment strategies.

articles.title: Heart Failure-Related Cardiogenic Shock: A Distinct Haemometabolic Syndrome.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) is increasingly recognised as a heterogeneous syndrome, with heart failure-related cardiogenic shock (HF-CS) now representing the predominant aetiology. However, contemporary diagnostic and therapeutic frameworks remain largely extrapolated from acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS), despite fundamental differences in pathophysiology and clinical trajectories. In HF-CS, pathophysiology is better conceptualised as a haemometabolic construct in which congestion, impaired forward flow, and systemic metabolic dysfunction interact to drive progressive multiorgan failure. These processes are often poorly captured by conventional blood pressure (BP)-based definitions of CS, particularly in heart failure, where patients may have persistently low yet compensated baseline BP. Although the Society of Cardiovascular and Angiographic Interventions shock classification provides a useful severity-based framework, emerging evidence supports a more integrated diagnostic approach that incorporates biomarkers such as lactate, mixed venous oxygen saturation, and invasive haemodynamic profiling. Together, these measures may improve risk stratification and better guide the timing and selection of escalation strategies. In parallel, multidisciplinary shock team models may improve outcomes in HF-CS, particularly when implemented early, before irreversible end-organ dysfunction develops. Future advances in HF-CS will require a shift away from BP-centric definitions derived from AMI-CS towards a comprehensive haemometabolic framework integrating congestion, perfusion, and haemometabolic status. Prospective HF-CS specific trials evaluating early, phenotype-guided care within structured, protocol-driven systems are essential to improving outcomes in this growing and clinically complex population.

articles.title: Prehabilitation Beneficial Effects in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIM: Cardiac surgery is associated with postoperative functional impairment that affects quality of life. Prehabilitation programmes may improve functional recovery in patients undergoing cardiac surgery who are at risk of postoperative complications. This systematic review aimed to present current evidence on the effectiveness of prehabilitation programmes in patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery.

METHOD: PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect were searched for relevant studies according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses statement and the Cochrane Collaboration Handbook. Eligible studies included adults undergoing cardiac surgery who participated in a prehabilitation programme. Only randomised controlled trials or clinical trials published in English were included. Outcomes of interest were respiratory function, exercise capacity and length of stay. Methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro (Physiotherapy Evidence Database) scale. The study was registered with the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/NV3GF).

RESULTS: The search identified 658 studies, of which 19 met the inclusion criteria. Most studies used inspiratory muscle training as the preoperative intervention. Prehabilitation significantly increased maximal inspiratory pressure in six studies and the 6-minute walk test in five of seven studies, while reducing mechanical ventilation duration in six studies, intensive care unit length of stay in four of seven studies and postoperative pulmonary complications. Methodological quality was moderate, with a median score of 5 (range, 2-8).

CONCLUSIONS: Prehabilitation exercise-based programmes improve inspiratory muscle strength and functional capacity while reducing postoperative pulmonary complications, mechanical ventilation duration and intensive care unit length of stay.

articles.title: PRovisional versus Focal OSTial Stenting for Isolated Ostial Disease Occurring in Coronary Bifurcations (The PROST Trial)-Rationale and Design.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions (Medina 0,1,0 and 0,0,1) remain one of the least studied lesion subsets in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Two techniques, provisional stenting and focal ostial stenting, are commonly used in clinical practice. However, no randomised controlled trial has directly compared these treatment approaches.

METHOD: The PRovisional vs Precision OSTial Stenting (PROST) trial is a prospective, multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled trial comparing provisional stenting with precision focal ostial stenting in patients undergoing PCI for isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions. A total of 274 patients will be randomised in a 1:1 ratio across participating Australasian centres. The trial is embedded within the Australasian Bifurcation Coronary Registry and incorporates mandatory intravascular imaging guidance, independent angiographic core laboratory assessment, and blinded clinical event adjudication. The primary endpoint is target lesion failure at 24 months, defined according to Bifurcation Academic Research Consortium criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, the PROST trial is the first randomised study evaluating provisional versus precision focal ostial stenting for isolated branch ostial coronary bifurcation lesions. Its findings will address an important evidence gap and have the potential to inform future clinical practice and guideline recommendations.

articles.title: Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration in Ventricular Arrhythmia Ablation: A New Paradigm From Procedure to a Program of Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation of ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be complex, requiring multidisciplinary expertise for safe and comprehensive patient management. We assessed the extent of perioperative multidisciplinary collaboration for VA ablations.

METHOD: We retrospectively identified 363 cases of VA ablation at an expert referral centre between 2017 and 2021. For these cases, extent of multidisciplinary involvement, PAINESD and MORTALITIES-VA scores, outcomes of ventricular tachycardia (VT) recurrence or premature ventricular complex (PVC) burden, cardiac transplantation and all-cause mortality were assessed.

RESULTS: Of the 363 cases of VA ablation, 185 (51.0%) were elective and 178 (49.0%) were emergent. Most cases required peri-procedural involvement by another specialist (in addition to a cardiac electrophysiologist) (n=231 [63.6%]), including an intensivist in 97 (26.7%), anaesthetist in 87 (24.0%), geneticist in 38 (10.5%), cardiothoracic surgeon in 32 (8.8%), a heart failure and transplant cardiologist in 24 (6.6%), and immunologist in 16 (4.4%). The median PAINESD score was 6.2 (interquartile range [IQR] 0-9), and the median MORTALITIES-VA score was 3.0 (IQR 0-9). Subgroups with higher PAINESD and MORALITIES-VA scores and requiring more specialists in their care were emergent VA ablations (median 8 vs 3 [p<0.001], median 7 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 2 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), non-PVC ablations (median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 4.5 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively), and patients with structural heart disease (median 8 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 6 vs 0 [p<0.001], median 1 vs 0 [p<0.001], respectively). In PVC ablations the median reduction in PVC burden was 96.5%, and in non-PVC ablations the VT recurrence rate was 39.9%. In the follow-up period, cardiac transplantation was required by 2.9% of patients, and 12.5% of patients died.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing VA ablation require multidisciplinary involvement for optimal care, with multiple specialties involved in the peri-ablation period.

articles.title: Association Between Immediate Postoperative Mean Pulmonary Artery Pressure and Heart Failure Readmission After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Readmission occurs frequently after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG); however, factors that specifically predict heart failure (HF)-related readmission are not well defined. To assess the relationship between immediate postoperative mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP) and the risk of HF readmission following CABG.

METHOD: A secondary analysis of 1,593 patients undergoing CABG used publicly available data to assess the association between immediate postoperative mPAP and hospital readmission for HF. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed, adjusting for relevant clinical confounders. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was performed to evaluate the ability of mPAP to predict HF readmission.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 3.8 years, 241 patients (15.13%) experienced HF readmission. A fitted curve showed a linear relationship between immediate postoperative mPAP and HF readmission risk. Multivariable analysis demonstrated that a 1 mmHg increase in mPAP was independently correlated with a greater risk of HF readmission (hazard ratio [HR] 1.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.06; p=0.005). In analysis using mPAP categories, patients with intermediate (15-30 mmHg) and high (>30 mmHg) mPAP levels exhibited significantly greater adjusted risks of HF readmission than those in the low mPAP group (≤15 mmHg), with HRs of 2.00 (95% CI 1.04-3.84) and 2.19 (95% CI 1.05-4.59), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing CABG, higher immediate postoperative mPAP was independently linked to a dose-dependent rise in the risk of HF readmission.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and 2-Year Follow-Up of Patients With Takayasu Arteritis and Pulmonary Artery Involvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIM: The frequency of pulmonary arterial (PA) involvement (PAI) in Takayasu arteritis (TAK) has been reported to range from 14.0% to 57.0%. PAI may be associated with a worse prognosis; therefore, early detection and treatment of PAI may improve the disease course. This study assessed the characteristics and follow-up of TAK patients with PAI.

METHOD: Seventy-two TAK patients (62 female, 10 male) who underwent computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) to investigate PAI were included. A radiologist reviewed CTPA images, and PAI was characterised by increased pulmonary artery wall thickness, stenosis, and/or thrombosis.

RESULTS: The mean age was 46.4±13.0 years, and nine patients had active disease. The treatments for TAK were immunosuppressives (IS) in 62 (86.1%), biological treatment in 25 (34.7%), glucocorticoids (GCs) in 30 (41.7%), and acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) in 50 (69.4%) patients. Twenty-two (30.6%) patients had pulmonary symptoms, most commonly dyspnoea and chest pain. PAI was detected in 13 (18.1%) patients, and PA thrombosis unrelated to vasculitis was present in five (6.9%) patients. Among PAI patients, IS treatment was changed in nine (69.2%), GC dose was increased in eight (61.5%), and anticoagulants were started in seven (53.8%). Pulmonary symptoms (92.3% vs 16.9%), C-reactive protein (CRP) (25.8 vs 4.0 mg/L), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (34.5 vs 16.2 mm/h) values were significantly higher in patients with PAI (p<0.001, p=0.001, p=0.008). PAI was significantly lower in patients using ASA (30.8% vs 69.2%) (p=0.002). After 2 years of follow-up, one patient with PAI had a relapse of TAK and three patients had chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.

CONCLUSIONS: PAI was present in 18.1% of TAK patients, and pulmonary symptoms, higher ESR and CRP values, and less frequent ASA use were associated with PAI.

articles.title: Tumor-Associated Brain Metabolic Heterogeneity in Patients without Intracranial Lesions: A Multicancer 18F-FDG PET Study.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Systemic malignancies may influence cerebral metabolism without direct intracranial involvement, but whether different tumor types are associated with distinct regional and network-level patterns remains uncertain.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 342 patients (219 men and 123 women) with colorectal, esophageal, gastric, or lung cancer, or lymphoma, who underwent 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography, together with 45 nontumor controls. Pons-normalized standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) from 25 brain regions were analyzed using multivariable linear regression and analysis of variance, with age, sex, tumor-related surgery, and treatment included in the models and false discovery rate correction applied. Univariable pairwise comparisons used Tukey adjustment. Principal component analysis and permutational multivariate analysis of variance assessed global patterns. Metabolic covariance networks were constructed using Pearson correlations, and topology and hub regions were evaluated.

RESULTS: Analysis of variance identified regional differences among tumor groups, and several Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons were significant. Age and sex showed broader associations than surgery or treatment. Global metabolic patterns substantially overlapped across tumor types, without clear separation. Covariance networks differed in topology and hub distribution. In the full cancer cohort, lung cancer had sparse connectivity and the greatest number of hub regions, whereas esophageal cancer showed high local clustering without hubs. The no-intervention tumor groups and nontumor controls also showed different network topology and hub distributions.

CONCLUSION: Brain metabolic covariance network analysis provides information on interregional metabolic organization alongside regional SUVR comparisons and global metabolic pattern analysis. The network findings require further validation.

articles.title: Quality and Determinants of Inpatient Imaging Requests: A Multicentre RI-RADS Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the quality and completeness of inpatient requests for general radiography, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and ultrasound using the Reason for Exam Imaging Reporting and Data System (RI-RADS), and to identify factors associated with request quality.

METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study evaluated 1091 inpatient imaging requests across four hospitals. Requests were graded using RI-RADS. Associations between RI-RADS grade and hospital, requesting specialty, imaging modality, anatomical region, clinical indication, and patient characteristics were evaluated. Multivariable ordinal regression was used to identify independent determinants of poorer request quality, and interobserver agreement was assessed using Fleiss' kappa.

RESULTS: Of 1091 requests, 141 (12.9%) were classified as RI-RADS grade A and grade D was the most frequent category (33.4%). An impression was documented in 62.1% of requests, whereas complete clinical information was present in only 19.4%. The multivariable model demonstrated explanatory performance of 46.3%. Hospital was the strongest determinant of RI-RADS grade; Orthopedic requests were associated with poorer documentation, whereas infection/inflammation and trauma, were associated with better request quality. Overall interobserver agreement was fair (Fleiss' κ = 0.231), with the highest component-level agreement observed for the diagnostic question.

CONCLUSION: Inadequate clinical documentation was common in inpatient imaging requests, although its severity varied substantially across hospitals and clinical contexts. Request quality was primarily associated with institutional and clinical factors rather than imaging modality itself. The frequent absence of a diagnostic question and marked hospital-level variation identify potentially modifiable targets for structured referral systems, clinician education, and targeted quality-improvement initiatives.

articles.title: Associations of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Usage With Clinical Outcomes of Limb Osteomyelitis in Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patients with type 2 diabetes are prone to limb osteomyelitis, a condition associated with high morbidity and mortality. The relationship between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use and outcomes in these patients remains unclear.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using a large federated database from 2015 to 2024. Adult patients with type 2 diabetes (ICD-10 E11) and limb osteomyelitis were identified. GLP-1RA exposure was defined as use within 6 months prior to the diagnosis of osteomyelitis. Patients with end-stage renal disease, malignancy, or human immunodeficiency virus infection were excluded. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, amputation, sepsis, major adverse cardiovascular events, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. Propensity score matching was applied to balance baseline characteristics and disease severity.

FINDINGS: A total of 21,858 patients were identified. After propensity score matching, 2615 patients remained in each cohort with balanced baseline characteristics. GLP-1RA use was associated with lower mortality, with rates of 1.0% at 6 months (HR 0.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.30-0.78) and 4.7% at 3 years (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49-0.78). Compared with non-users, GLP-1RA users also had lower risks of amputation, sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. No significant differences were observed in major adverse cardiovascular events at either 6 months (odds ratio [OR], 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74-1.04) or 3 years (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.78-1.02).

IMPLICATIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes and limb osteomyelitis, GLP-1RA use was associated with lower risks of mortality, sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and acute kidney injury. These findings suggest a potential supportive role for GLP-1RAs in this high-risk population, although further studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: Laryngopharyngeal Reflux Disease Symptoms in Fibromyalgia Syndrome: A Cross-Sectional Study of 112 Patients.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the risk of laryngopharyngeal reflux disease (LPRD) symptoms in a cohort of patients diagnosed with fibromyalgia syndrome (FMS) in comparison to a control group.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional METHOD: Consecutive patients aged 18 to 65 years with a diagnosis of FMS were recruited from the Rheumatology Clinic of a tertiary referral center between June 1, 2026, and July 1, 2026. Another group, frequency-matched by age and gender and with no history of FMS or chronic pain conditions, was recruited as a control group. LPRD symptoms were assessed using the Reflux Symptom Score-12 (RSS-12) and the Reflux Symptom Index (RSI) questionnaires. The severity of heartburn was also assessed using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS).

RESULTS: Fifty-six patients with FMS and 56 controls were included in the study. All patients were females. The mean age of the FMS group was 47.94 ± 11.92 years. There was a statistically significant difference in the mean RSI score between the FMS and control groups (9.57 ± 9.03 vs 3.33 ± 4.37, p<0.001). Similarly, there was a statistically significant difference in the mean RSS score between the two groups (57.46 ± 51.07 vs 14.67 ± 18.07, p<0.001). There was a statistically significant difference in the mean VAS for heartburn score between the two groups (5.59 ± 3.02 vs 2.16 ± 2.59, p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: The results of this investigation indicate that patients diagnosed with FMS have a higher rate of symptoms that could be suggestive of LPRD compared to controls. Patients presenting with laryngopharyngeal symptoms should be investigated for LPRD.

articles.title: Task-specific training for upper limb rehabilitation after subacute and chronic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Task-specific training is commonly used to improve poststroke upper-limb function through repetitive, goal-directed practice of meaningful tasks.

PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of task-specific training, alone or combined with adjunct therapies, on upper-limb motor recovery and activity/activities of daily living-related outcomes after subacute and chronic stroke.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and OTSeeker, through September 2025, for randomized controlled trials in adults with subacute/chronic stroke. Effect sizes were summarized as Cohen's d; random-effects pooling was performed when dispersion data allowed.

RESULTS: In 24 randomized controlled trials of moderate-to-high methodological quality, within-group improvements were frequently observed in motor recovery and functional outcomes across both subacute and chronic stroke. Significant between-group effects favoring task-specific training were reported in five of 17 trials assessing upper-limb motor recovery, one of 11 assessing upper-limb function in activities of daily living, one of four assessing gross manual dexterity, one of six assessing amount of use, and one of seven assessing quality of movement. Significant between-group effect sizes ranged from Cohen's d = -0.12 to -0.97 for motor recovery, while effects of d = -0.39, -1.18, and -3.03 were reported for gross manual dexterity, amount of use, and quality of movement, respectively. Statistical heterogeneity across pooled outcomes was substantial (I² = 71% = 93%), and pooling was limited by incomplete dispersion reporting.

CONCLUSIONS: Task-specific training may improve upper-limb outcomes in adults with subacute and chronic stroke. However, when delivered alone or in combination with adjunct interventions, the advantages over active comparators were not consistent across outcomes. Activities of daily living-oriented, meaningful task practice may promote functional gains, but current evidence does not support universal superiority of task-specific training over other active rehabilitation approaches.

Human Wound and Its Burden: Updated 2027 Compendium.
articles.abstract: Human wounds remain a worldwide public health challenge, driving disability, infection, amputation, and premature death. Historical estimates identify 10.5 million Medicare beneficiaries with wounds in 2019 and 18.6 million people affected annually by diabetic foot ulcers worldwide. Successful healing requires restoration of skin barrier function, not simply visible closure complicated by the known threats of leaky skin cover. The NIDDK Diabetic Foot Consortium is advancing this paradigm through multicenter evidence linking impaired barrier restoration to ulcer recurrence, rigorous biomarker evaluation, and an inclusive platform integrating longitudinal clinical data, biospecimens, and patient-reported outcomes. Major mechanistic discoveries reveal how disrupted communication among immune cells, fibroblasts, and nerves sustains wound dysfunction. Biofilm-derived wound-infection signals impair macrophage clearance of dying cells, while excessive fibroblast-directed innervation restricts regeneration. Strategies targeting inflammatory resolution, localized mRNA delivery, and glucose-powered bioelectric signaling offer opportunities to improve repair. Comparative clinical trials emphasize that technological complexity does not guarantee superior healing. Economic and policy developments demand alignment of payment with evidence and meaningful endpoints. Medicare skin-substitute spending skyrocketed 40× from 2019 to 2024. CMS's 2026 shift to incident-to-supply payment under the Physician Fee Schedule projected $19.6 billion in gross fee-for-service savings. The FDA's 2026 patient-focused initiative emphasized daily wound burden and treatment priorities; effects of payment reforms on access and outcomes require evaluation. The emerging agenda unites functional wound closure, mechanism-based innovation, equitable access, and accountable spending. Progress must deliver sustained barrier restoration endpoints, reduced recurrence, preserved mobility, and improved quality of life, grounded in prevention and etiologic care.

articles.title: Dynamic 18F-FDG Imaging of the Brain Using Total-Body PET in Patients with Genitourinary Cancer: A Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
articles.abstract: Dynamic 18F-FDG PET enables brain kinetic quantification to study central nervous system involvement in cancer and other systemic diseases, but reliable blood input functions are difficult to obtain on conventional scanners. We used total-body PET to evaluate 18F-FDG kinetic modeling of the brain in healthy subjects and patients with genitourinary cancer (GUC). Methods: Ten patients with GUC and 12 healthy participants underwent a 1-h total-body 18F-FDG dynamic scan, and image-derived input functions were extracted from the aorta. Reversible and irreversible 2-tissue compartment (2Tr and 2Ti, respectively) models were assessed in the gray matter, thalamus, putamen, and brainstem using Akaike information criterion. Microparameters (K 1, k 2, k 3), net influx rate (K i), and practical model identifiability were assessed, and differences between patients with GUC and healthy participants were investigated. Results: The 2Tr model provided significantly better fits than the 2Ti model (P < 0.05). K i and SUV were significantly lower in patients with GUC across multiple brain regions. The 2Tr model revealed significant differences in K 1, k 2, and k 3 between the cohorts, independent of age, which were absent or attenuated when the 2Ti model was used. Identifiability analysis confirmed robust parameter estimation with reasonable bias and SD. Conclusion: Total-body dynamic PET enabled robust, noninvasive quantification of brain 18F-FDG kinetics using an image-derived input function. The 2Tr model provided superior time-activity curve fitting and identifiable parameters and revealed group differences in microparameters (K 1 and k 2) that were not detected with the 2Ti model. These findings suggest alterations in brain metabolism in patients with GUC, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Wound Healing Outcomes in Diabetic Versus Nondiabetic Patients Treated with Autologous Whole Blood Clot: A Large Cohort Retrospective Comparison Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic wounds represent a significant clinical burden, driven by persistent inflammation and extracellular matrix degradation that impair healing across etiologies. Diabetes is a known risk factor; however, similar biological barriers exist in nondiabetic wounds. Advanced therapies are often focused on diabetic populations, yet effective treatments that address shared healing impairments across both diabetic and nondiabetic wounds remain limited.

APPROACH: This multicenter pooled analysis included 197 chronic wounds treated with autologous whole blood clot (AWBC). Outcomes were compared between diabetic (56%) and nondiabetic patients. Percent area reduction (PAR) was assessed at weeks 4, 12, and 20, and complete healing rates were evaluated at weeks 12 and 20.

RESULTS: Progress toward healing was observed across all wound types treated with AWBC. By week 20, median PAR improved to 96.5-100% in diabetic and 80-100% in nondiabetic wounds, with no significant differences. In a subgroup analysis, venous-treated wounds in diabetic patients showed better outcomes at week 12 than nondiabetic patients (p = 0.039). In contrast, for trauma wounds, nondiabetic patients showed greater improvement than diabetic patients at weeks 4 and 12 (p = 0.014 and 0.029, respectively). After adjustment for wound characteristics and age, diabetic status was not significantly associated with complete closure at week 20 (odds ratio, 1.91; 95% confidence interval, 0.75-4.87; p = 0.17).

INNOVATION: AWBC is a point-of-care therapy that forms a fibrin-rich, biologically active scaffold, delivering cells and growth factors, intended to support the wound-healing cascade.

DISCUSSION: Wound healing was observed in both diabetic and nondiabetic patients treated with AWBC, with no significant overall differences in complete healing rates. Although subgroup differences were observed in venous leg ulcers and trauma wounds, no overall differences in healing were detected by diabetic status, suggesting that AWBC may be considered in both populations.

articles.title: Mechanisms and management of multimorbidity in patients with COPD.
articles.abstract: Multimorbidity, defined as the presence of two or more chronic conditions, represents a significant challenge in the management of COPD, a complex and highly prevalent disease. The coexistence of chronic conditions such as cardiovascular or metabolic diseases increases the frequency and severity of COPD exacerbations, complicates treatment decisions and worsens patient outcomes. These coexisting diseases may share underlying mechanisms, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress and risk factors such as smoking, which accelerate disease progression. In this review, we discuss the prevalence and clinical significance of multimorbidity in COPD, with a focus on shared risk factors, the pathophysiological mechanisms and the impact on outcomes. Additionally, we examine current disease management strategies for COPD and multimorbidity, highlighting the need for a multidisciplinary, personalised approach, and discuss the role of biomarkers in coexisting conditions.

articles.title: Home-based pulmonary rehabilitation early after hospitalisation in COPD: A randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: COPD is characterised by respiratory exacerbations, often requiring hospitalisation. Post-hospitalisation pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) can reduce risk of readmission, but very few people attend PR post exacerbation.

OBJECTIVE: To compare hospital readmission rates between people with COPD who undertake a home-based PR program commenced early (≤2 weeks) after hospital discharge (ePR) with usual care.

METHODS: Assessor blinded, multi-centre RCT. Participants randomised 1:1 to ePR or usual care. ePR was 8 weeks (1 physiotherapy home-visit, plus 7x weekly phone calls). The primary outcome was all-cause, non-elective hospitalisation at 12 months after rehabilitation completion.

RESULTS: From Jan 2020-Jun 2024 157 participants were randomised to ePR (n=77) or usual care (n=80). The ITT analysis included 151 participants (n=73 ePR, n=78 usual care; n=6 excluded: n=5 deceased, n=1 transplant). Rate of all-cause non-elective hospitalisation was not different between groups at 12-month follow-up (ePR 60.3%, usual care 64.1%; RR 0.94 [95%CI 0.73, 1.21]). There was no difference between groups for improvements in quality of life and breathlessness at either time point. There was a clinically and statistically significant reduction in anxiety favouring ePR (10-weeks post-discharge MD -2.1 [95%CI -3.4, -0.8]; 12-months MD -1.6 [95%CI -3.0, -0.2]). ePR completion rate (≥70% sessions) was high (n=57, 74%). When compared to no rehabilitation (per protocol), ePR completers demonstrated significant improvements in breathlessness, quality of life, anxiety/depression and self-efficacy. There was one intervention-related adverse event.

CONCLUSION: ePR delivered directly to patients in their homes, commenced within 2 weeks of hospital discharge, did not reduce hospital readmissions over 12 months compared to usual care but did support high program completion. When compared to no rehabilitation, improved clinical outcomes favoured ePR in those who completed the program.

articles.title: Multiple simultaneous acute infarcts in CADASIL: a retrospective cohort study and systematic review.
Osteoporosis and fragility fracture risk in patients with bronchiectasis: a large multicentre population analysis.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Osteoporosis and fragility fractures are recognised comorbidities in chronic airway diseases such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma, but their burden in bronchiectasis beyond cystic fibrosis (CF) remains poorly defined and is not addressed in current guidelines.

OBJECTIVE: To quantify the risk of osteoporosis and fragility fractures in adults with bronchiectasis using large, multicentre electronic health record datasets.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using de-identified data from TriNetX and Epic Cosmos (2015–2024). Adults with bronchiectasis were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification code J47, excluding CF codes. In TriNetX, 1:1 propensity score matching balanced demographics and key osteoporosis risk factors between bronchiectasis and non-bronchiectasis cohorts. Absolute risks, risk differences and risk ratios (RRs) were estimated for osteoporosis and fragility fractures. Epic Cosmos was used to assess yearly prevalence and incidence trends.

RESULTS: After matching, 364 924 patients were retained per cohort. Osteoporosis occurred in 8.41% of bronchiectasis patients versus 6.69% of controls (RR 1.26, 95% CI 1.24 to 1.28; p<0.001). Fragility fractures occurred in 2.80% vs 2.50% (RR 1.12, 95% CI 1.09 to 1.15; p<0.001). Associations were stronger in a CT-restricted cohort (osteoporosis RR 1.45; fragility fracture RR 1.40; both p<0.001). Recorded prevalence of both outcomes was higher in 2024 than in 2015 in both datasets, while annual estimates fluctuated.

CONCLUSIONS: A diagnosis of bronchiectasis was associated with a higher recorded burden of osteoporosis and fracture-related diagnoses than in matched controls. These findings support greater attention to bone health and prospective evaluation of risk stratification, screening strategies and targeted interventions in this population.

Atypical pyoderma gangrenosum: a diagnostic dilemma.
articles.abstract: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) is an autoimmune inflammatory skin condition that is classified as a neutrophilic dermatosis. While the aetiology of PG remains unclear, it is hypothesised that the disease originates from inappropriate reactivity of T cells and release of cytokines, akin to that seen in inflammatory arthropathies and inflammatory bowel diseases. Among patients with ulcerative colitis, 0.5%–5% will develop PG. Here we present an atypical case of PG with rapid clinical progression. This case report evidences the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for PG to enable prompt diagnosis and commencement of treatment. Furthermore, it demonstrates that traditional surgical intervention is not efficacious and is often deleterious to the recovery process.

articles.title: What does renal replacement therapy measure after paediatric cardiac surgery? Observations on the UK national audit.
Trends in ACE inhibitor and angiotensin receptor blocker prescribing during the COVID-19 pandemic among US Medicare beneficiaries: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: During the COVID-19 pandemic, uncertainty regarding potential interactions between ACE inhibitors (ACEi), angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) and SARS-CoV-2 created concern about continued use of these medications. We aimed to examine clinician-level trends in ACEi/ARB prescribing among US Medicare beneficiaries from 2019 to 2022.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using clinician-level quarterly panel data.

SETTING: US outpatient care, using national Medicare Fee-for-Service claims from 2019 to 2022.

PARTICIPANTS: Physicians, nurse practitioners and physician assistants treating Medicare beneficiaries with Part A (hospital insurance), Part B (medical insurance) and Part D (prescription drug) coverage, identified through the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System and linked to beneficiaries via claims.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The unit of analysis was the clinician-quarter. We estimated a negative binomial model for the number of ACEi/ARB prescriptions per 100 patients. Quarter-year fixed effects were interacted with practice type, clinician type, sex and years in practice. For contextual comparison, we applied the same model to metformin, statins and evaluation and management (E&M) visits. We additionally examined overall prescribing trends for other antihypertensive medications.

RESULTS: We included 1 078 318 clinicians contributing 13.3 million clinician-quarters. The percentage of clinician-quarters with at least one fill of ACEi/ARBs declined from 30.0% in 2019 to 28.5% in 2022. Prescribing volume was largely stable, decreasing from 10.6 to 9.9 per 100 patients, with modest quarter-to-quarter variation and notable declines in Q2 2020 and Q1 2022. Statin and metformin prescriptions followed similar quarterly patterns but returned to and exceeded Q1 2019 volumes. E&M visits declined sharply in Q2 2020, then exceeded Q1 2019 by 2022. Trends were consistent across clinician characteristics, with larger declines for primary care and senior clinicians, and rapid recovery towards the end of each calendar year for early-career clinicians.

CONCLUSIONS: ACEi/ARB prescribing declined modestly and remained below Q1 2019 levels through 2022. Similar patterns were observed for other commonly prescribed cardiometabolic medications.
