articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a prevalent dyslipidemia worldwide and an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease and acute pancreatitis. Interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15), a ubiquitin-like protein involved in innate immunity, has recently been implicated in metabolic disorders, but its relationship with HTG remains unexplored.

METHODS: This study included 295 Chinese participants (184 with HTG and 111 without HTG). Serum ISG15 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and associations with HTG were assessed using logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Findings were validated in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced HTG mouse through western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and histological analyses.

RESULTS: Serum ISG15 levels were significantly elevated in HTG patients compared with controls (3.18 ± 0.29 vs. 1.64 ± 0.19, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified ISG15 as an independent predictor of HTG (OR: 1.214, 95% CI: 1.015-1.416, P = 0.033). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear dose-response relationship with an inflection point at approximately 1.52 ng/mL. ROC analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance (AUC: 0.697, sensitivity: 86.40%, specificity: 45.00% at cut-off 0.873 ng/mL). In HFD-fed mice, serum ISG15 levels were significantly elevated, and immunohistochemistry and western blotting confirmed increased ISG15 expression in liver, subcutaneous white adipose tissue, and epididymal white adipose tissue.

CONCLUSIONS: ISG15 is independently associated with HTG and exhibits a nonlinear relationship with diagnostic potential. These findings establish ISG15 as a potential biomarker and suggest its involvement in the immunometabolic crosstalk underlying HTG pathogenesis, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: Vaping-Related Pneumomediastinum in Adolescents: Characterizing Work Up and Management.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adolescent vaping, including nicotine and tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) products, carries numerous adverse effects. Case reports, primarily in young adults, describe an association between inhaled substance use and pneumomediastinum, but management of affected adolescents remains unclear. This study sought to characterize this population and identify variations in practice patterns to improve future care.

METHODS: A single center, retrospective descriptive study with 60-day follow-up was conducted. The hospital's radiology database was searched for imaging studies noting "pneumomediastinum" in patients >10 and 18 years from January 2014-May 2025. Patients with pneumomediastinum secondary to another etiology (ex: trauma, recent surgery) were excluded. Those reporting recent inhaled substance use were included.

RESULTS: Forty-one adolescents met inclusion criteria. Median age at symptom onset was 16 years (range 14-18 years). Nicotine and THC vaping were reported in 73.2% and 78.0% of patients, respectively, with >50% using daily. Hospital admission occurred in 68.3% of cases with median length of stay of 2 days (IQR 1, 3). Three patients required intensive care unit admission, one of whom was hypoxic and obtunded at presentation necessitating intubation. Admitted patients underwent more chest radiographs than those discharged from the emergency department (median 2 vs 1, p=0.027). Nineteen patients underwent esophagram, none demonstrating injury. No interventions were required and no patient experienced recurrence during follow up.

CONCLUSION: Management of vaping-related pneumomediastinum in adolescents, notably the use of imaging, varies considerably. Most patients may not require admission or transfer to a specialized pediatric facility unless presenting with hypoxia or respiratory distress.

articles.title: Chronic exposure to low-concentration urban PM2.5 promotes maladaptive kidney repair after ischemic injury via mitochondrial dysfunction and lysosomal stress.
articles.abstract: Chronic exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is increasingly associated with kidney function decline and chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly in individuals with pre-existing vulnerability, yet the mechanisms by which PM2.5 modifies kidney disease trajectories remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether prolonged exposure to low-level urban PM2.5 during recovery from ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI)-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) promotes maladaptive repair, a risk factor for AKI-to-CKD transition. Mice subjected to IRI or sham surgery were exposed for six months to filtered air or real-world ambient PM2.5. While PM2.5 induced only limited changes in sham kidneys, it markedly altered repair after IRI, promoting inflammation, microvascular rarefaction, mitochondrial injury, and metabolic reprogramming and fibrosis. PM2.5-associated elements accumulated within proximal tubular lysosomes, linking inhaled particle exposure to lysosomal stress, lipid remodeling, and tubular senescence. Transcriptomic drug-repurposing analysis identified nicotinamide as a candidate metabolic intervention, which improved mitochondrial dysfunction in PM2.5-challenged proximal tubular epithelial cells in vitro. Together, these findings show that even low-level urban PM2.5 exposure can act as a disease-modifying environmental stressor in injured kidneys, promoting maladaptive repair. Our findings reveal the post-injury recovery phase as a critical window of heightened susceptibility, during which air pollution can compromise kidney recovery.

articles.title: Progressive corneal denervation in Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma with female-predominant corneal remodeling.
articles.abstract: Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma is characterized by anterior segment dysgenesis, ocular hypertension, and optic neuropathy, but its consequences for corneal sensory innervation remain poorly defined. We examined male and female Pitx2egl1/egl1 and Pitx2+/+ mice at 1 and 3 months using intraocular pressure measurements, fundus imaging, visual evoked potentials, optic nerve ultrastructure, corneal βIII-tubulin whole-mount imaging, mechanical sensitivity testing, and bulk RNA sequencing of corneas and trigeminal ganglia. Mutant mice developed ocular hypertension, posterior segment abnormalities, reduced visual evoked potential amplitudes, and optic nerve degeneration. Corneal epithelial nerve fiber volume was preserved at 1 month but reduced in both sexes at 3 months, indicating progressive denervation in an untreated genetic model. Mechanical sensitivity was reduced in mutant males, whereas female values did not differ detectably between genotypes. Factorial transcriptomic analysis included sex, genotype, and their interaction. Female mutant corneas showed 634 strict differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of complement, cytokine, extracellular matrix, focal adhesion, p53-related, glycan, and metabolic pathways. No comparably robust gene set was detected in male corneas. Additional diagnostics indicated small male genotype effects at the gene level and a diffuse aggregate sex-conditioned signal that was not resolved at single-gene false-discovery-rate level. Whole-mount KRT17 immunolabeling showed expansion of the KRT17-positive epithelial domain in female mutant corneas, providing orthogonal spatial support for an epithelial remodeling component of this signature. Whole-trigeminal-ganglion bulk RNA-seq detected few significant changes, but dilution of cornea-projecting neurons within the whole ganglion precludes concluding that these neurons were unresponsive. These findings identify progressive corneal denervation as an underrecognized component of Pitx2-associated developmental glaucoma and define female-predominant corneal remodeling as a hypothesis-generating molecular feature rather than a proven sex-specific mechanism.

articles.title: Preclinical study of butein in diabetic nephropathy and its impact on Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant defence and TGF-β/Smad2/3 signaling axis in kidneys.
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) is a common microvascular complication associated with diabetes mellitus. Butein, a naturally occurring chalcone derivative, exhibits a spectrum of pharmacological activities. However, its precise role in DN remains unexplored. Our study employed a combined bioinformatics analysis with experimental validation in a rat model of high-fat diet (HFD)/streptozotocin (STZ)-induced DN, using biochemical, histological, and molecular analyses. Empagliflozin was used as the reference drug. In this investigation, administration of butein significantly reduced alterations in renal function, mitigated renal pathological damage, and inhibited the expression of extracellular matrix (ECM) components in rats. Diabetes-induced blood glucose and lipid profile parameters were significantly decreased in the butein treatment groups. Butein treatment considerably reduced oxidative stress and ferroptosis by upregulating the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 axis while concurrently downregulating acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4). Moreover, butein exerted antifibrogenic effects via the TGF-β1/Smad2/3 signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), thereby regulating the expression of ECM proteins. Additionally, treatment with butein markedly reduced the elevated levels of inflammatory factors, including TNF-α, IL-1β, COX2, and the pro-apoptotic factor caspase-3. Butein treatment markedly reduced the TUNEL-positive apoptotic cells in the kidneys. Further findings revealed that butein effectively reduced phosphorylation in the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β axis. Collectively, the findings suggest new potential targets for DN treatment, and the nephroprotective effect of butein is mediated by regulation of the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β, Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4, and TGF-β/Smad2/3 signaling axis.

articles.title: Rationale and Design of the MICRA-HYBRID Trial: Multivessel Minimally Invasive Coronary Bypass Grafting as HYBRID Revascularization Versus Conventional Off-pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the gold standard for patients with complex three-vessel coronary artery disease (CAD). It offers durable long-term outcomes, but introduces substantial short-term surgical trauma. Multivessel hybrid coronary revascularization (multivessel-HCR) with minimally invasive left anterior descending (LAD) and circumflex artery (Cx) grafting combined with percutaneous right coronary artery (RCA) intervention (PCI) might reduce postoperative morbidity, improve early recovery and offer similar long-term outcomes.

TRIAL DESIGN: This investigator-initiated, dual-center, randomized clinical trial investigates whether multivessel-HCR is superior to off-pump CABG (OPCAB) in patients with three-vessel CAD. Eligible patients have angiographically significant disease of all three major epicardial vessels with or without left main involvement. In total, 250 patients will be randomized 1:1 with stratification for diabetes. Both surgical strategies will use a total arterial, anaortic off-pump approach. Multivessel-HCR consists of minimally invasive LAD and Cx grafting followed by PCI of the RCA. In the OPCAB-arm, all significant coronary targets will be surgically revascularized. The primary endpoint is 30-days textbook outcome, defined as the composite absence of mortality, re-exploration, type 5 myocardial infarction requiring acute PCI or graft revision, tamponade, stroke, transient ischemic attack, wound infection, new-onset atrial fibrillation, pneumonia, pleural effusion requiring chest drainage, and prolonged hospitalization. Key secondary endpoints include quality of life and recovery questionnaires, pulmonary recovery and short-term hospital costs. Follow-up includes 5-year major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events.

CONCLUSION: The MICRA-HYBRID trial will compare in a randomized fashion multivessel hybrid revascularization with OPCAB in patients presenting with 3-vessel CAD.

articles.title: Baseline diffusion MRI markers of interstitial fluid dynamics are associated with subsequent amyloid conversion in cognitively normal individuals.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence suggests that early disruption of interstitial fluid (ISF) dynamics may precede amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, and diffusion MRI-derived indices offer noninvasive markers of ISF properties. We investigated whether baseline ISF-sensitive diffusion MRI markers differ between Aβ-negative (-) cognitively normal (CN) individuals who subsequently convert to Aβ-positivity and those who remain Aβ (-), and whether these markers are associated with subsequent Aβ accumulation.

METHODS: We included Aβ (-) CN participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts who had baseline MRI and longitudinal amyloid PET. Based on longitudinal amyloid PET standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), participants were classified as 18 converters who exceeded the Aβ-positivity threshold at least once during follow-up and 16 non-converters who remained Aβ (-) throughout follow-up. Baseline diffusion MRI-derived ISF markers, cortical free water (FW), the diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space (ALPS) index corrected for white-matter microstructural asymmetry (corrected ALPS index), and perivascular space volume fraction, were compared between groups, together with baseline Aβ, tau, and neurodegeneration biomarkers. Associations between baseline MRI measures and annualized change in amyloid PET SUVR were also assessed.

RESULTS: Converters showed higher cortical FW and lower corrected ALPS index than non-converters, despite no baseline group differences in Aβ, tau, or neurodegeneration markers. Among converters, higher baseline FW was associated with a faster annualized increase in amyloid PET SUVR.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that baseline diffusion MRI markers of ISF dynamics are associated with subsequent Aβ-positivity conversion and Aβ accumulation in initially Aβ (-) CN individuals, suggesting that alterations in ISF dynamics may be detectable before overt Aβ deposition.

articles.title: Reference-region normalization outperforms data-driven approaches in [18F]FDG PET of dementia with Lewy bodies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Data-driven intensity normalization has recently emerged as an alternative to proportional scaling (PS) and reference-region (RR) for brain [18F]FDG PET analysis. We investigate these methods in dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB; n = 110, 72.1 ± 6.7 y/o) and healthy controls (HC; n = 30, 67.6 ± 5.3 y/o) imaged with [18F]FDG PET/MR.

METHODS: RR-based methods (pons, cerebellum, white matter), PS, iterative proportional scaling (iPS), histogram normalization (HN), iterative histogram normalization (iHN), and SUV conversion were evaluated through voxel-based comparisons (DLB vs HC). Scaling factors were extracted from the pons, cerebellum and white matter for RR, a gray-matter mask for PS, the modal voxel intensity in HN, and their subject-specific data-driven counterparts for iPS and iHN. For each scaling factor, we measured (i) their normative alignment between DLB and HC distributions; (ii) disease independence via correlation with a DLB meta-ROI; (iii) interindividual stability using coefficients of variation; and (iv) temporal stability based on longitudinal annual rates of change. These metrics were combined into a composite score to identify the optimal normalization approach. A simulation study on a Hoffman phantom was conducted to evaluate how each metric affects ground truth recovery.

RESULTS: Widespread cortical hypometabolism was observed in DLB vs HC using RR and SUV normalization. In contrast, PS, iPS, HN, and iHN revealed cortical hypometabolism together with hypermetabolism in the sensorimotor cortex, basal ganglia, pons, and cerebellum (family-wise error-corrected p-value < 0.05). RR normalization yielded smaller DLB-HC differences in scaling factors, weaker correlations with the DLB meta-ROI, reduced coefficients of variation, and lower rates of change compared with PS, iPS, HN, and iHN. The white matter, followed by the pons, showed the highest composite score. The simulation study showed that larger scaling-factor mean differences between patients and controls, and higher coefficients of variation, were associated with greater recovery error.

DISCUSSION: This is the first systematic assessment of intensity normalization in the largest [18F]FDG PET DLB cohort to date. Our findings support RR-based normalization as the preferred standard in DLB, outperforming PS, HN and data-driven approaches.

articles.title: Novel VAPB variants in sporadic ALS promote protein aggregation and PERK-ISR associated apoptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vesicle-associated membrane protein-associated protein B (VAPB) has been established as a causative gene for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, VAPB mutations have been infrequently reported, and the pathogenic mechanisms underlying novel variants remain poorly characterized. In the present study, VAPB was sequenced in a cohort of Chinese patients with sporadic ALS to identify novel variants and delineate their functional consequences.

METHODS: Targeted next-generation sequencing was conducted in non-consecutive ALS patients referred to Departments of Neurology at Fujian Medical University Union Hospital between 2017 and 2024. Variant pathogenicity was assessed using PolyPhen-2, MutationTaster, and other in silico prediction tools. Functional analyses comprised immunofluorescence, solubility fractionation, immunoblotting for PERK, eIF2α, and ATF4, and Annexin V-APC/7-AAD flow cytometry.

RESULTS: Three novel heterozygous missense variants, c.38 A > C (p.Q13P), c.511G > A (p.E171K), c.659 T > G (p.L220R), and one known c.166C > T (p.P56S) mutation, were individually identified in four patients with sporadic ALS. All patients showed relatively rapid disease progression except the patient with P56S mutation. Most in silico prediction tools classified Q13P and E171K as likely damaging. Immunofluorescence analysis demonstrated that Q13P and E171K, but not L220R, formed perinuclear aggregates showing extensive colocalization with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone PDI. In Neuro-2a cells, upon tunicamycin treatment, overexpression of Q13P or E171K was associated with increased p-PERK/PERK and p-eIF2α/eIF2α ratios and elevated ATF4 expression. Furthermore, independent of tunicamycin treatment, these mutants suppressed global protein synthesis, as assessed by the SUnSET assay. Furthermore, both variants increased the protein levels of CHOP, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3 and were associated with an increased proportion of Annexin V-positive cells.

CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that the VAPB variants Q13P (MSP domain) and E171K (coiled-coil domain), but not L220R, are associated with ER aggregates and converge on activation of the PERK-eIF2α-ATF4 branch of the integrated stress response (ISR), accompanied by ER stress-associated apoptosis (increased CHOP, Bax, and cleaved caspase-3). These observations are consistent with a likely pathogenic role for these two variants and indicate that variants arising in distinct structural domains converge on a shared ER stress-PERK-ISR-apoptosis axis, a candidate therapeutic target in VAPB-associated ALS.

articles.title: Genetic Variants and Domain-Specific Cognitive Function in the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: APOE ε4 is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease and is associated with age-related cognitive decline. Whether its association with cognition, and that of other candidate variants, is uniform across cognitive domains or domain-specific remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesize single-variant candidate-gene evidence on domain-specific cognitive function (episodic memory, executive function, language, visuospatial function, attention, processing speed) in the Alzheimer's disease-indexed literature, beyond APOE alone.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, and Scopus on 18 June 2026 without date restriction (PRISMA 2020; PROSPERO CRD420261446003). Of 6,453 records, we included 111 studies; all search strings required an Alzheimer's disease term. We applied two risk-of-bias tools to every study. Two reviewers extracted and appraised data using AI assistance and verified them against the source text, without reporting agreement statistics. Synthesis was narrative by domain, with an exploratory effect-size meta-analysis for APOE.

RESULTS: APOE was examined in 70 of 111 studies (63%), and 30 further genes were examined in two or more studies each. Detrimental APOE associations were most consistent for episodic memory (48 of 75 findings; sign test p=3.3×10⁻⁹) and executive function (28 of 54; p=5.1×10⁻⁴). The direction of association did not differ between domains (χ²(5)=2.13, p=0.83; 84% detrimental), but detection frequency did (null results 28% to 65%; χ²(5)=20.16, p=0.001). In an exploratory meta-analysis of 36 studies, pooled ε4 effects on performance were small and negative in all six domains, significantly so only for episodic memory (Hedges' g=-0.14, 95% CI -0.21 to -0.07; executive function -0.07, -0.13 to 0.00), and within the same studies the episodic memory effect exceeded the executive function and language effects. The episodic memory result was robust to square-root sample-size weighting, age restriction and significance-threshold re-analysis; the executive function result was less robust, and the two risk-of-bias tools disagreed on whether either survives quality stratification.

CONCLUSIONS: The direction of APOE's association with cognition appears uniform across domains; it is detected most often on episodic memory measures, where its standardized effect also exceeds that on executive function and language measures, and part of the between-domain variation in detection, and possibly in effect size, may reflect the instruments used. Evidence beyond APOE is fragmented, with 93 of 123 non-APOE genes (76%) supported by a single study. Single-variant evidence from the Alzheimer's disease literature thus converges on APOE, with only preliminary evidence for a few other Alzheimer's disease risk loci, in contrast to the highly polygenic architecture that genome-wide studies describe for general cognitive function.

articles.title: Beyond cardiogenic shock stage: The promise and limits of CS-MORT-6.
Acute pericarditis after atrial fibrillation ablation in the pulsed-field ablation era: Energy source-specific insights from a large multicenter registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute pericarditis is a clinically relevant complication of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation, but its incidence after pulsed-field ablation (PFA) relative to thermal ablation is uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To compare clinically diagnosed pericarditis after PFA-based and thermal-based AF ablation procedures and describe events across contemporary PFA platforms.

METHODS: Data from consecutive AF ablation procedures at 20 cardiovascular centers between 2022 and 2026 were analyzed. Pericarditis was diagnosed clinically by the treating physicians, and fulfillment of the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) diagnostic criteria was assessed retrospectively.

RESULTS: Among 19,555 consecutive AF ablation procedures included in the analysis, PFA, radiofrequency (RF), and cryoballoon was involved in 5743, 12768, and 5729 procedures, respectively. Clinically diagnosed acute pericarditis occurred in 5 of 5743 among PFA-based procedures (0.09%) and 38 of 13,812 (0.28%) among thermal-based procedures (P = 0.011). Twenty-nine (67.4%) cases fulfilled definite diagnosis of the ESC 2025 criteria for pericarditis, and the remaining 14 cases (32.6%) met possible diagnosis. In multivariable analysis, mitral isthmus linear ablation was independently associated with a higher risk of pericarditis (odds ratio [OR], 2.457; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.136-5.311; P = 0.022), whereas PFA use was independently associated with a lower risk (OR, 0.382; 95% CI, 0.149-0.980; P = 0.045).

CONCLUSION: In real-world clinical practice, clinically diagnosed acute pericarditis was rare after both PFA-based and thermal-based AF ablation. In the overall cohort, the observed incidence was significantly lower after PFA-based procedures, but the small number of events limits the certainty of this association and warrants further study.

articles.title: Prognostic utility of transvalvular flow rate in patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Flow assessment helps determine the severity of low-gradient (LG) aortic stenosis (AS). Transvalvular flow rate (FR) may classify flow status differently from stroke volume index (SVi). This study compared their prognostic utility in patients with LG-AS undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI).

METHODS: This post hoc analysis of a multicenter registry included 205 patients with severe symptomatic LG-AS who underwent TAVI. Low flow (LF) was defined separately as SVi ≤35 mL/m2 or FR ≤200 mL/s. The primary endpoint was all-cause death.

RESULTS: SVi classified 74 patients (36%) as having LF, whereas FR classified 131 (64%) as having LF, including 63 with normal flow according to SVi. FR was correlated with LVEF (r = 0.457, P < 0.001) and natural-log-transformed E/e' (r = -0.205, P = 0.010). Patients with LF according to either measure showed greater recovery in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). In the multivariable Cox model, FR ≤200 mL/s was not associated with all-cause mortality (HR, 0.764; 95% CI, 0.376-1.551; P = 0.456).

CONCLUSION: FR identified more patients with LF than SVi but did not show an association with outcome after TAVI. These findings do not support prioritizing FR over SVi in patients with LG-AS.

articles.title: Redefining what matters: Anatomical mapping in the era of pulsed-field ablation.

Readmission outcomes after left atrial appendage occlusion in older adults with atrial fibrillation and bleeding or anticoagulation-alternative indications: A landmark analysis of the nationwide readmissions database, 2018-2020.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is increasingly used in older adults with atrial fibrillation (AF) at risk of bleeding or contraindication to long-term anticoagulation, but its association with age and frailty is poorly described.

METHODS: Adults ≥65 years with nonvalvular AF at elevated thromboembolic risk whose index admission carried a coded bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication were identified in the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2018-2020). Patients alive at the 90-day landmark were stratified by LAAO vs. no LAAO within 90 days. The primary outcome was all-cause readmission during days 91-270. Survey-weighted logistic regression and propensity-score matching were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Among 1,244,671 patients, 2070 underwent LAAO at a mean of 52.4 ± 23.4 days after index. LAAO was associated with higher adjusted odds of all-cause readmission (aOR 1.31, 95% CI 1.15-1.49) and cardiovascular readmission (aOR 1.33, 1.14-1.55). Bleeding readmission was also higher. In-hospital death at readmission did not differ. Age-by-frailty-by-LAAO interaction was not significant (p = 0.85), although subgroup analyses were underpowered.

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with AF and a bleeding event or an anticoagulation-alternative indication who were alive at 90 days, inpatient LAAO was associated with higher subsequent readmissions, including bleeding. Out-of-hospital deaths were not captured, and death competes with readmission, so higher readmission does not mean a worse net clinical outcome. These associations may reflect differences in baseline bleeding risk, inpatient exposure capture, and residual confounding.

articles.title: Trial design and methods of home-based exercise tele-rehabilitation in high-risk veterans: Impact of COVID-19 exposure and socioeconomic factors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Successful rehabilitation strategies for Veterans during and post Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a high clinical research priority. Long-term effects of COVID-19 on cardiopulmonary and physical function are uncertain, and rehabilitation should be feasible for Veterans. The objectives of this clinical trial are to investigate the effect of home-based supervised exercise via tele-rehabilitation on cardiopulmonary and physical function outcomes, its' impact on recovery defined by World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) components, and its effect on self-efficacy, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers in adults who have had SARS-CoV-2 infection.

METHODS: In the Home-Based Exercise Tele-Rehabilitation in High-Risk Veterans: Impact of COVID-19 Exposure and Socioeconomic Factors (BOOST) trial (NCT05425264), 80 middle-aged and older adults (>50 years) will be enrolled with documented COVID-19 > 90 days prior to enrollment and diagnosed with ≥2 conditions: hypertension, diabetes and/or pre-diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, dyslipidemia or 1 condition and BMI > 30 kg/m2. Veterans will participate from home in the 12-week exercise intervention that will consist of virtual supervised group exercise classes. Procedures before and after the intervention will include cardiopulmonary exercise testing, pulmonary function tests, assessments of physical function, and questionnaires targeting exercise self-efficacy.

DISCUSSION: This novel 12-week exercise intervention program, which was designed to promote health in Veterans who have a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection, will provide critical information on the benefits of exercise on cardiopulmonary and physical function in this heterogenous population.

articles.title: Effects of duration-matched once- and thrice-weekly aerobic exercise on liver fat in adults with central obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD): Protocol for a three-group randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common liver disease worldwide. Whether achieving the guideline-recommended amount of aerobic physical activity in a once-weekly ("weekend warrior") exercise regimen results in comparable reductions in hepatic steatosis compared to a conventional thrice-weekly exercise regimen is unknown. This study will examine the effects of duration-matched once-weekly and thrice-weekly aerobic exercise on liver fat in adults with central obesity and MASLD.

METHODS: This single-center, assessor-blinded, three-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will recruit 300 adults with central obesity and MASLD. Participants will be randomly assigned to the control, once-weekly exercise, or thrice-weekly exercise groups. In accordance with the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines, the exercise groups will receive 75 min of vigorous-intensity (6-7 metabolic equivalents) supervised treadmill training per week, delivered as one 75-min session in the once-weekly group or three 25-min sessions in the thrice-weekly group. The control group will receive a 150-min health education class every 2 weeks. The intervention will last 4 months. The outcome assessments will be conducted at baseline, 4 months (post-intervention), and 10 months (follow-up). The primary outcome will be intrahepatic triglycerides assessed by proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

DISCUSSION: This study will validate the therapeutic efficacy of once-weekly and thrice-weekly aerobic exercise for reducing liver fat in adults with central obesity and MASLD. The results of this study are expected to provide evidence for refining exercise recommendations for the management of MASLD.

articles.title: The burden, temporal patterns, and projected burden of asthma attributable to high BMI among children in China, 1990 - 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Childhood asthma and obesity represent two converging public health crises in China. High body mass index is an established modifiable risk factor for asthma, yet its specific epidemiological burden among Chinese children remains insufficiently characterized.

METHODS: Data on deaths and disability-adjusted life years attributable to high body mass index-related asthma among children aged 0 to 14 years in China from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from the Global Burden of Disease 2023 study. Average annual percent change was used to assess temporal trends, an age-period-cohort model was applied to disentangle the independent effects of age, period, and birth cohort, and a Bayesian age-period-cohort model was employed to project the burden through 2050.

RESULTS: In 2023, high body mass index-related asthma caused 8 deaths and 40,251 disability-adjusted life years among Chinese children, with males bearing a consistently higher burden. From 1990 to 2023, the age-standardized mortality rate declined significantly (average annual percent change: -4.26), while the disability-adjusted life year rate increased (average annual percent change: 1.62). Age-period-cohort analysis revealed declining mortality risk across successive periods and cohorts, whereas the risk of disability-adjusted life years increased markedly in recent birth cohorts (relative risk 1.81 for the 2014 to 2023 cohort). Projections indicate that total disability-adjusted life years will nearly triple to 102,393 by 2050.

CONCLUSION: While mortality from high body mass index-attributable asthma has declined, the morbidity burden is escalating and projected to worsen substantially by 2050. Integrated strategies targeting childhood obesity are urgently needed to mitigate this growing threat.

articles.title: Growth trajectories and metabolic profiles of low-birth-weight term and preterm infants: a 4-year longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare growth and metabolic outcomes during the first four years of life among low-birth-weight infants born moderately preterm, late preterm, and at full term.

METHODS: Cohort of singleton infants without malformations or congenital infections, weighing 1500-2499 g, followed in an outpatient clinic during the first four years of life, from 2014 to 2019. Three groups were compared: G1 (moderate preterm, n = 76), G2 (late preterm, n = 107), and G3 (term, n = 98). Weight, length, and head circumference were assessed using Z-scores. Metabolic assessment (cholesterol, triglycerides, fasting blood glucose) was performed once a year from the 2nd year onwards. Outcomes included growth failure, overweight/obesity risk, dyslipidemia, and glucose disorders. Group comparisons used ANOVA, Chi-square test, and repeated-measures ANOVA.

RESULTS: Growth Z-scores remained within normal limits but differed among groups, as moderate preterm infants maintained consistently higher Z-scores through the third year of life. Weight growth failure was more frequent in late preterm and term infants, with term infants showing a higher prevalence of thinness at 36-48 months and moderate preterm infants showing a higher risk of overweight at 24 months. No intergroup differences were found in lipid profiles, although triglycerides remained above recommended levels across all groups and time points, and preterm infants showed elevated total cholesterol at 4 years.

CONCLUSION: Growth patterns differed across groups in the first 4 years, with moderate preterm showing catch-up and higher Z-scores, while late preterm and term infants had more weight growth failure. Lipid profile abnormalities were observed in all groups from the second year of life onward.

articles.title: Early Childhood CASPR2 Autoimmunity with Prominent Autonomic Dysfunction: Diagnostic Challenges and Effective Immunotherapy.
articles.abstract: CASPR2-associated neurological diseases cover a broad clinical spectrum, with limbic encephalitis and Morvan syndrome representing the most characteristic autoimmune phenotypes. We report the case of a 2-year-old boy who presented with abdominal and generalized pain, refusal to eat or drink, weight loss, loss of mobility, and behavioral changes, including sleep disturbances. Further clinical evaluation revealed pharmacoresistant arterial hypertension and hyperhidrosis. Extensive diagnostic testing excluded infectious and toxic causes. CASPR2 antibodies were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid. Initial therapy with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulins resulted in only minimal clinical improvement. Significant clinical recovery was only achieved after escalation of immunotherapy with plasmapheresis and subsequent B-cell-depleting therapy with rituximab. At the most recent follow-up visit, seven months after the first rituximab infusion, the patient showed complete recovery without residual symptoms. This case underscores the diagnostic challenges of CASPR2-associated autoimmunity in early childhood and highlights the importance of early recognition of this rare but treatable disease.

articles.title: Bolus Volume and Mortality in Extremely Low Gestational Age Infants with Shock.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between clinical outcomes and the volume of fluid boluses administered during the first 24 hours of a shock episode in extremely low gestational age newborns (ELGANs) requiring vasoactive support.

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included ELGANs (≤28 weeks) at a single Level IV NICU between 2013 and 2021 who received vasoactive medications for shock within the first seven days of life. The primary predictor was total fluid volume (cc/kg) administered in the first 24 hours of shock. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for gestational age, birth weight, 5-minute Apgar score, systemic corticosteroid use, and highest vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS).

RESULTS: Of 97 infants, 26 (27%) died within 14 days of the shock episode. Non-survivors received a higher median bolus volume compared to survivors (40 cc/kg vs. 20 cc/kg, p<0.001). Greater bolus volume was independently associated with increased odds of 14-day mortality (aOR 1.026, 95% CI 1.004-1.048, p=0.019). Each additional 10 cc/kg was associated with an approximately 29% increase in mortality odds. No significant associations were found between bolus volume and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or bronchopulmonary dysplasia after adjustment.

CONCLUSION: Greater cumulative fluid bolus volume was independently associated with higher 14-day mortality in ELGANs with shock requiring vasoactive support. Although residual confounding illness severity cannot be excluded, these findings support cautious, individualized use of volume expansion and highlight the need for prospective studies of hemodynamically targeted resuscitation in this population.

articles.title: Moving in the right direction? A survey of clinicians' opinions on wearable fetal movement monitoring devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced fetal movements are associated with adverse perinatal outcomes and commonly prompt unscheduled care. We explored clinicians' views on self-monitoring of fetal movements, and the potential role of a fetal movement monitoring device in clinical practice.

METHODS: An anonymous online survey was distributed in Ireland and the UK. Quantitative and qualitative responses were collected on current advice for reduced fetal movements, perceived anxiety in patient groups, views on potential risks/benefits of fetal movement monitoring devices, desired device characteristics, and preferences regarding data access and responsibility. Descriptive statistics and content analysis were performed.

RESULTS: 101 clinicians responded; 44/82 (53.7%) were obstetrician-gynaecologists and 38/82 (46.3%) were midwives. The majority of participants advised hospital attendance in the event of FM-related concern, and to take note of their baby's pattern of movements. 61/82 (74%) of clinicians reported that they frequently encountered anxiety relating to fetal movements in their patients. Anticipated benefits of a home FM monitor included reassurance (31/53, 58%) and fewer hospital admissions (12/53, 23%). Key concerns were a potential for increased patient anxiety (20/52, 38%), inaccurate information (25/52, 48%) and over-reliance on a device (15/52, 29%). Accuracy/reliability (31/50; 62%), ease of use (13/50; 26%) and durability (10/50; 20%) were rated as the most important device attributes. Most clinicians wished to be able to view device data, though a minority did not want to have the responsibility for monitoring. Overall, 36/53, 68% of responders would consider using a fetal movement monitor in their practice.

CONCLUSIONS: The respondees perceived potential value for home FM monitors as an adjunct to current care but highlighted potential risks related to patient anxiety, data accuracy and professional responsibility. Evidence of clinical efficacy and safety, alongside patient-experience surveys and data governance, would be required for the introduction of a clinically-indicated home fetal movement monitoring device.

articles.title: Metabolic Profiles and insulin therapy requirements among pregnant women with Gestational Diabetes mellitus and Type 2 Diabetes across self-identified Race/ethnic groups in Brooklyn NY, USA.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and type 2 diabetes (T2 DM) presents varying metabolic patterns across populations, yet the extent to which these differences appear at diagnosis remains unclear. This study examines whether baseline metabolic profiles differ among pregnant women from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds. Our objective was to determine whether these metabolic differences may influence diabetes management during pregnancy.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a two‑year retrospective study of 200 insulin‑naïve women at NYU Langone hospital at Brooklyn, NY, diagnosed with GDM and or T2DM in the third trimester. The diagnostic criteria were standard two‑step testing , 50‑g glucose challenge (1Hr. GCT, cut off 135mg./DL) followed by a 100‑g Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT). Baseline fasting labs included glucose, C‑peptide, and lipid profiles, with insulin sensitivity estimated using IS‑HOMA (C‑peptide). Management followed standardized diet, exercise, Metformin when appropriate, and weight‑based basal-bolus insulin titrated to fasting glucose levels 85-90 mg/dL and 2‑hour postprandial 115-120 mg/dL.

RESULTS: Significant race/ethnicity‑specific metabolic phenotype differences emerged. Hispanic-Latina women and American born Black women had higher BMI, higher fasting C‑peptide, and lower insulin sensitivity, whereas Asian (Southeast and East Indian) and Caribbean/Haitian Black women showed lower C‑peptide but higher insulin sensitivity. Lipid patterns also varied. There was no statistically significant difference in birthweight across groups.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, we observed distinct metabolic profiles across racial and ethnic groups at the time of GDM or T2DM diagnosis in pregnancy. These differences, particularly in insulin sensitivity, C‑peptide levels, and BMI, suggest that metabolic phenotype varies meaningfully by race and ethnicity. Incorporating these patterns into clinical decision‑making may help refine diabetes management strategies and support more equitable perinatal outcomes.

articles.title: Departure From Planned 39-Week Delivery for Fetal Congenital Heart Disease: Indications for Earlier Birth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delivery >39 weeks' gestation is recommended for fetuses with congenital heart disease (FCHD). However, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), maternal diabetes and fetal growth restriction (FGR) are more common in these pregnancies and often necessitate early delivery. We evaluated indications for delivery at <39 weeks and examined maternal covariates, cardiac diagnoses and placental pathology.

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective observational study included maternal-fetal dyads with prenatally diagnosed, structurally isolated, genetically unremarkable FCHD delivered at a single center. Gestational age and delivery indication were obtained from medical record. Placental pathology was assessed using Amsterdam criteria. Regression models evaluated associations with gestational age and neonatal mortality.

RESULTS: 46.3% (99/214) delivered <39 weeks; 65.6% (65/99) were due to maternal or fetal compromise, and 34.3% (33/99) to obstetric indications. HDP (20.1%) was strongly associated with <39-week delivery (32.3% vs 9.6%, p<0.001) and the greatest reduction in gestational age (-2.31 weeks, p<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified preeclampsia, type 2 diabetes, lower birthweight Z-score, and race as independent predictors of earlier delivery (p<0.05). Neonatal mortality was higher with maternal/fetal indications (15.7%) versus obstetric (5.4%) or elective FCHD delivery (5.6%) (p=0.02).

CONCLUSION: Nearly half of FCHD infants delivered before 39 weeks, largely due to maternal and placental disease, underscoring the importance of placental health in this population.

articles.title: Hypercoagulable Thrombin Generation Correlates with High-Risk Clinical Features and Venous Thrombosis Recurrence.
articles.abstract: Following venous thromboembolism (VTE), predictive biomarker testing for risk assessment is hampered by the presence of anticoagulation. This study aims to remove in vitro interference caused by direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with DOAC-Stop, enabling thrombin generation testing during anticoagulation. Platelet-poor plasma was collected approximately 3 months after VTE diagnosis from adults who were therapeutically anticoagulated with apixaban or rivaroxaban. Thrombin generation testing was performed using ST-Genesia ThromboScreen, following use of DOAC-Stop. A total of 251 patients were included (mean age 55.4 years, 54.2% male). Patients with thrombophilia and/or family history of VTE demonstrated hypercoagulable thrombin generation parameters. A total of 165 patients (65.7%) were classified as clinically "high risk," defined as one or more of unprovoked pulmonary embolism (PE) and/or proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT), family history of VTE, personal prior history of VTE, and hereditary thrombophilia, with remaining cases considered "low-risk" VTE. The "high-risk" group demonstrated increased peak height, endogenous thrombin potential, and velocity index compared with the "low-risk" cohort. About 52.2% (n = 131/251) of all patients subsequently ceased anticoagulation, with five episodes of unprovoked recurrence occurring within 1 year of cessation. These patients had higher median peak height (139.4 vs. 104.6%, p = 0.043, percentile difference - 34.8, 95% confidence interval (CI): [- 68.4, - 1.81]) and ETP (119.5 vs. 103.7%, p = 0.006, percentile difference: - 27.5, 95% CI: [- 43.5, - 11.3]) without thrombomodulin. This study provides evidence that thrombin generation testing after DOAC-Stop can identify hypercoagulable VTE patients without interrupting anticoagulation. Thrombin generation was increased in several groups with clinical risk factors associated with hypercoagulability. Key thrombin generation parameters were increased and associated with unprovoked VTE recurrence in patients who later stopped anticoagulation. Larger confirmatory studies are required.

articles.title: Symptom-Based Clinical Deterioration as a Patient-Centred Endpoint in Canine Urothelial Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: This multicentre retrospective cohort study operationalized structured clinical deterioration endpoints in canine urothelial carcinoma (UC) and compared them with conventional outcomes. A total of 182 dogs with imaging-supported, cytologically and/or histopathologically confirmed UC from three referral institutions were included. Clinical signs were retrospectively mapped using prespecified grading rules anchored to VCOG-CTCAE v2 and symptom-based endpoints were defined from treatment initiation as time to lower urinary tract symptom progression (TTSP) and time to systemic deterioration (TTD), each assessed as initial (first grade ≥ 2 deterioration) and confirmed (grade ≥ 2 deterioration sustained at the next consecutive assessment) events. Imaging-based progression-free survival (PFS) was reconstructed from serial ultrasonography using VCOG cRECIST progression criteria (≥ 20% increase in longest tumour diameter or a new lesion). Confirmed TTSP and TTD were strongly associated with OS (rank correlations, 0.81 and 0.82, respectively) and remained prognostically informative in multivariable models and at most prespecified landmark times; the corresponding correlation for imaging-based PFS was 0.74. TTSP/TTD were not temporally interchangeable with imaging-based PFS or with acute kidney injury (AKI) and complete obstruction, showing broad individual-level discordance and limited overlap even within ±7- and ±14-day windows. In descriptive treatment-group comparisons, patterns differed across OS, PFS and deterioration endpoints and in the rescue-intervention subcohort, most dogs developed recurrent deterioration after decompression for malignant obstruction. These findings suggest that TTSP/TTD are feasible structured endpoints that capture clinically relevant and prognostically informative worsening not fully represented by imaging progression or catastrophic events alone.

articles.title: Interpreting thrombin and reptilase times: Beyond heparin contamination.
Mortality and prognostic factors in invasive aspergillosis: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive aspergillosis remains a life-threatening infection, but robust real-world mortality estimates are scarce. We aimed to generate contemporary overall and subgroup-specific mortality estimates for invasive aspergillosis using individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis.

METHODS: In this systematic review and IPD meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science for articles published between Jan 1, 2015, and Dec 31, 2024, that reported mortality of at least ten patients with invasive aspergillosis diagnosed using established criteria, with clearly defined and analysed follow-up periods. Corresponding authors were contacted to obtain IPD on demographics, underlying conditions, site of invasive aspergillosis, diagnostic certainty, and mortality. The primary outcome was overall all-cause mortality at 4, 6, 12, and 24 weeks, 1 year, and 2 years after invasive aspergillosis diagnosis. Secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) mortality and in-hospital mortality. One-stage IPD meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled mortality. This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025621772).

FINDINGS: 16 020 articles were identified, of which 9686 articles were screened after removal of duplicates. Of the articles screened, 209 studies including 15 357 patients were eligible. IPD were obtained from 46 studies, comprising 3880 patients. Across IPD cohorts, patients were predominantly middle-aged and had pulmonary involvement, and probable invasive aspergillosis was the most common diagnostic certainty; classic immunocompromised host factors were common in the mortality-after-invasive aspergillosis-diagnosis cohort, whereas COVID-19 predominated in the ICU mortality cohort. Estimated overall mortality was 26·7% (95% CI 21·0-38·2) at 4 weeks, 32·0% (26·9-42·6) at 6 weeks, 41·7% (34·9-55·1) at 12 weeks, 48·5% (41·4-61·4) at 24 weeks, 53·8% (46·8-64·0) at 1 year, and 57·2% (49·7-68·3) at 2 years. ICU mortality was 57·1% (47·5-66·5) and in-hospital mortality was 46·7% (39·4-54·1). By underlying condition, estimated 4-week mortality was highest among patients with ICU admission (42·9%, 30·4-53·2). By site, estimated 4-week mortality was 27·2% (21·3-40·0) for pulmonary, 21·1% (15·1-28·9) for sinus, and 40·4% (35·0-54·5) for brain invasive aspergillosis. The overall pooled estimates yielded I2 values of 93·2% (92·0-94·3) for 4-week mortality, 89·5% (87·6-91·2) for in-hospital mortality, and 92·3% (90·8-93·5) for ICU mortality.

INTERPRETATION: Mortality among patients with invasive aspergillosis remains high despite modern diagnostic and therapeutic advances. Greater vigilance, earlier diagnosis, and timely antifungal treatment are needed, particularly for patients with newly recognised host factors, including ICU admission and COVID-19.

FUNDING: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

articles.title: Early Feeding Characteristics from the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Through the First Year of Life and Neurodevelopment at 24 Months in Preterm Infants.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) oral feeding progression and feeding development during the first year of life are associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months corrected age in preterm infants.

STUDY DESIGN: This longitudinal cohort study included 94 preterm infants born at < 37 weeks' gestation in a single level III NICU. NICU feeding progression was operationalized using gestational age-adjusted z-scores for time to full oral feeding. Parent-reported feeding symptoms and feeding skills were assessed during early (1-2 months), mid (4-8 months), and late (10-12 months) infancy. Neurodevelopment was assessed at 24 months corrected age using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition (Bayley-IV). Multivariable linear regression models were used to examine associations between early feeding characteristics and 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes, adjusting for gestational age, infant sex, parent education, and parent race.

RESULTS: Delayed NICU feeding progression showed a trend toward lower motor scores at 24 months (β = -5.12, p = 0.06). Parent-reported feeding symptoms during late infancy were associated with lower motor scores (β = -0.10, p = 0.03) and a similar trend for language score (β = -0.17, p = 0.06). Higher feeding skill proficiency during mid and late infancy was consistently associated with higher motor, language, and cognitive scores (mid infancy: β = 0.19-0.37, p < 0.01; late infancy: β = 0.23-0.38, p < 0.001). The Oral-Motor Coordination, Basic Movement Patterns, and Fundamental Oral-Motor subscales also demonstrated significant positive associations across all neurodevelopmental domains in both mid and late infancy.

CONCLUSION: Feeding characteristics from NICU hospitalization through infancy, including oral feeding progression, feeding symptoms, and feeding skill development, were associated with neurodevelopment at 24 months in preterm infants. These early feeding characteristics may provide clinically accessible measures to inform developmental surveillance and follow-up care.

KEY POINTS: · Delayed NICU oral feeding progression trended toward lower 24-month motor scores in preterm infants.. · More late infancy feeding symptoms were associated with lower 24-month motor scores.. · Higher infant feeding skill proficiency was associated with higher 24-month Bayley-IV scores.. · Early feeding monitoring helps identify preterm infants needing targeted developmental support..

articles.title: Association of Excess Gestational Weight Gain with Neonatal Hypoglycemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neonatal hypoglycemia is a significant contributor to neonatal morbidity. Diabetes, preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, growth restriction, and maternal obesity have been shown to increase the risk. We hypothesized that excess gestational weight gain is associated with increased rates of neonatal hypoglycemia.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of singleton, term deliveries in a single center between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2021, excluding patients with preexisting or gestational diabetes. The primary outcome was incidence of neonatal hypoglycemia. Institute of Medicine guidelines were used to determine category of gestational weight gain based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. Secondary outcomes included rates of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit admission by gestational weight gain category. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for potential confounders (macrosomia and pre-pregnancy obesity).

RESULTS: There were 23,902 term, singleton deliveries. Patients with excess gestational weight gain were more likely to be non-white, have undergone a cesarean delivery (CD) (29 vs. 22%, p < 0.001), have higher birthweight (3,522 vs. 3,333 g, p < 0.001), and have a higher pre-pregnancy body mass index (27 vs. 26, p < 0.001) compared with patients with appropriate gestational weight gain. The odds of neonatal hypoglycemia were significantly higher for women with excess gestational weight gain (adjusted odds ratio 1.28, 95% CI: 1.12-1.47). Odds of macrosomia and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions were also increased. Conversely, appropriate weight gain was protective against neonatal hypoglycemia (adjusted odds ratio 0.73, 95 %: 0.63-0.85).

CONCLUSION: These data suggest that independent of maternal body mass index, macrosomia, or diabetes status, excess gestational weight gain is associated with an increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia. Although more research is needed to elucidate the pathophysiology and confirm these findings, these data suggest that counseling on gestational weight gain should address a potential increased risk of neonatal hypoglycemia at birth with excess gestational weight gain.

articles.title: Therapeutic targeting of circ-ZNF609 attenuates cardiac remodeling by modulating the expression of ZEB1.
articles.abstract: Currently, there are no effective therapeutic strategies to reverse heart failure. This study aims to investigate mechanisms underlying cardiac remodeling and identify potential therapeutic targets. Here, we demonstrate that circ-ZNF609 is upregulated in cardiac tissue, isolated adult cardiomyocytes, and cardiac fibroblasts 4 weeks after transverse aortic constriction (TAC) in mice. Small hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated silencing of circ-ZNF609 attenuates TAC-induced cardiac remodeling. To further assess its therapeutic potential, we use an RNA-targeting hfCas13x-crRNA system and show that circ-ZNF609 inhibition attenuates established cardiac hypertrophy in mice. In vitro, circ-ZNF609 inhibition reduces cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and fibroblast differentiation into myofibroblasts. Mechanistically, circ-ZNF609 interacts with YTHDF3 in an m6A-dependent manner to regulate ZEB1 (zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1) expression. circ-ZNF609 inhibition suppresses ZEB1. YTHDF3 knockdown also protects against cardiac remodeling. These findings support circ-ZNF609 inhibition as a potential therapeutic approach for pathological cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

articles.title: Atrial fibrillation is associated with higher stroke risk but not with higher mortality in patients with heart failure: A nationwide analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF) has been associated with increased risk of mortality in patients with heart failure (HF), it is unknown whether AF confers an increased risk on its own, i.e., not mediated through the increased risk of stroke. We aimed to investigate the age- and sex-specific prognostic impact of AF and stroke (alone and in combination) in patients with HF by using multistate modeling to account for events occurring during follow-up. Secondary aims were to investigate temporal trends in transition rates and in anticoagulant use in patients with AF and HF.

METHODS: This was a Swedish nationwide cohort study that included adult patients with HF diagnosed between 2004 and 2025. We used multistate modeling to account for occurrences of AF and stroke both at baseline and during follow-up. With Poisson regression in generalized additive models, we assessed age- and sex-specific transition rates between the different disease states, and in a separate model including time period, we assessed temporal trends in transition rates. Finally, as oral anticoagulants influence stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation, we estimated temporal, sex-specific trends in their use.

FINDINGS: We identified 704,852 patients (47% women) with HF, who were followed for a total of 2.9 million person-years. AF was associated with an increased risk of stroke but did not associate with an increased risk of death on its own. In the early study period, women, compared with men, were less likely to receive oral anticoagulants, but their use increased over time, more in women than in men. During the same period, there was a decline in stroke risk, with a greater absolute improvement in women than in men.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study of patients with HF, AF was not associated with an elevated direct risk of mortality. Over time, the risk of stroke decreased in patients with HF and AF, temporally coinciding with a marked uptake of direct-acting oral anticoagulant (DOAC) use, with the largest improvement seen among women.

FUNDING: This study was supported by unrestricted funding from Anders Wiklöf.

articles.title: Temporal deconvolution of mesoscale recordings.
articles.abstract: Mesoscale calcium recordings, such as wide-field imaging, enable high-temporal-resolution recordings of neuronal activity across extensive brain regions. However, because these recordings capture light emitted by calcium indicator fluorescence, the underlying neural activity is obscured by the temporal dynamics of the indicators. Here, we develop and evaluate four deconvolution methods to recover neuronal spiking rates from fluorescence traces recorded in wide-field imaging. The methods-dynamically binning (using adaptive discrete-time bins), continuously varying (estimating smooth spiking rates), first differences (providing efficient estimation), and a modified Wiener filter (robust to large fluorescence magnitude variations)-consistently outperform the previously used adapted Lucy-Richardson algorithm on both synthetic data and simultaneous fluorescence-spike recordings. Critically, we demonstrate that using raw fluorescence signals in advanced analysis methods can yield distorted results, including spuriously inflated correlations between brain regions' activity. This highlights the necessity of accurate temporal deconvolution for reliable interpretation of brain activity.

articles.title: Redefining blood pressure targets in refractory septic shock.
articles.abstract: Refractory septic shock was recently delineated by a set of clinical statements reflecting poor tissue perfusion despite adequate intravascular fluid volume and high doses of vasopressors. The concept of arterial pressure, which plays a pivotal role in the Sepsis-3 definition, was not incorporated by the panelists. The intensity of vasopressor treatment was found to be predominantly associated with mean arterial pressure. Indeed, the restoration of tissue perfusion is arguably the primary objective of resuscitation efforts. However, the loss of hemodynamic coherence-that is, the uncoupling between macrohemodynamics and microcirculation-suggests that, beyond a certain level of around 60-65 mmHg, tissue perfusion, as reflected by lactate and capillary refill time, is independent of arterial pressure in most patients. In this study, we propose a hypothesis derived from a physiological perspective, positing that the cost of increasing mean arterial pressure may increase disproportionately with rising norepinephrine requirements. In patients with refractory septic shock, the optimal level of arterial pressure should be investigated using time-limited challenge and adequate markers, such as capillary refill time and lactate. The approach to this evaluation should not be predicated on the analysis of isolated values; rather, it should be informed by a longitudinal and repeated examination of multiple markers that reflect global, regional, and local perfusion. Further research is necessary to ascertain the most effective strategy.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence tools for generating multimodal intensive care unit journey and discharge summaries: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesise existing evidence on computational summarisation technologies, including machine learning-based and natural language processing-based approaches, designed to generate multimodal (textual, visual, and audio) patient summaries of adult intensive care unit (ICU) stays.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Studies involving adults in any ICU setting and using artificial intelligence-enabled approaches to generate patient summaries were eligible. Searches were conducted across five major databases and grey literature sources. Two reviewers independently screened records. Data were extracted using a structured charting tool and independently verified by a second reviewer. Findings were synthesised using descriptive statistics and narrative synthesis.

RESULTS: Eleven studies met inclusion criteria. Eight generated textual summaries, three produced visual outputs, and one developed an audio interface. Ten tools were clinician-facing; only one study generated summaries for families. Approaches included large language models, rule-based natural language generation, information extraction, trajectory modelling, and speech-based systems. No study implemented a fully multimodal summarisation system. All evaluations were conducted using retrospective data, simulations, or prototypes, with no prospective testing in live clinical workflows. Five themes emerged: predominance of text-based summarisation, early feasibility of large language models with reliability limitations, predominance of clinician-facing applications, heterogeneous evaluation practices, and limited evidence of clinical implementation.

CONCLUSION: Current ICU summarisation research demonstrates technical proof-of-concept feasibility but limited clinical readiness. Progress will require rigorous evaluation, stabilisation safeguards, and multimodal, patient- and family-centred designs capable of operating within regulatory and safety-critical clinical environments.

articles.title: Hypomagnesemia during Kidney Replacement Therapy with Regional Citrate Anticoagulation: a prospective study on the differences between Continuous and Prolonged Intermittent modalities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypomagnesemia is common in critically ill patients on kidney replacement therapy (KRT) and may adversely affect outcomes. We evaluated hypomagnesemia incidence during continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH), continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration (CVVHDF), and sustained low-efficiency dialysis-filtration (SLED-f) with regional citrate anticoagulation (RCA) and explored the relationship between serum magnesium and mortality.

METHODS: We prospectively studied critically ill patients requiring KRT-RCA at our centre, all of whom received magnesium-containing dialysis/replacement solutions. Linear mixed-effects models and generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to examine difference in serum magnesium and hypomagnesemia, and time-varying Cox regression to assess association with mortality.

RESULTS: Patients received CVVH (n = 21), CVVHDF (n = 21), or SLED-f (n = 36). Hypomagnesemia (s-Mg; <1.7 mg/dL) occurred in 82%, requiring supplementation in 73%. Serum magnesium concentrations were lower during continuous modalities in unadjusted analyses, but differences were largely attenuated after adjustment for baseline characteristics; only one time point showed statistical significance (CVVH, session-day 4; P = 0.047); in GEE analyses, observed differences in hypomagnesemia between groups was no longer significant after adjustment for baseline characteristics. Exploratory analyses identified a U-shaped association between serum magnesium and mortality (P = 0.032), but this was model-dependent, absent in unadjusted analysis, and based on sparse data at distribution extremes.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypomagnesemia is a common complication during KRT with RCA despite magnesium-containing solutions and supplementation. Apparent modality differences largely attenuated after adjustment for baseline characteristics. The U-shaped magnesium-mortality association requires validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Comparison of Emergency Surgery Score and Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for Mortality and Morbidity in Emergency Laparotomies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Emergency laparotomy (EL) is associated with high morbidity and mortality worldwide. Reliable and rapid risk stratification tools are essential for predicting adverse outcomes and optimizing perioperative management. This study compared the predictive accuracy of the Emergency Surgery Score (ESS) and the Portsmouth Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the Enumeration of Mortality and Morbidity (P-POSSUM) in patients undergoing EL.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 230 adult patients who underwent EL were included between January 2017 and December 2021. Demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were collected, and ESS and P-POSSUM were calculated for each patient. Outcomes included 30-d mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, and postoperative complications. Discriminative performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, with area under the curve reported with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Overall 30-d mortality rate was 13.9%, and 63.0% of patients required ICU admission. Both ESS and P-POSSUM demonstrated good discriminatory performance for 30-d mortality and ICU admission. ESS showed a numerically higher area under the curve for mortality than P-POSSUM; however, DeLong testing demonstrated no statistically significant difference between the models. For major postoperative complications, both models demonstrated acceptable discrimination, with comparable performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Both ESS and P-POSSUM demonstrated comparable predictive accuracy for short-term outcomes following EL. ESS may offer practical advantages in emergency settings because it relies exclusively on preoperative variables, allowing early risk assessment and perioperative planning when operative information is not yet available.

articles.title: Baseline QRS duration is not an independent predictor of one-year outcomes in a large native African cohort of chronic heart failure: Insight from the Ibadan Heart Failure Project.
articles.journal: Journal of the National Medical Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prolonged QRS duration reflects ventricular conduction delay and electrical dyssynchrony. It is associated with adverse outcomes in heart failure, but evidence from contemporary African chronic heart-failure cohorts remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the relationship between baseline QRS duration and one-year mortality, rehospitalization and the composite of mortality and/or rehospitalization among adults with chronic heart failure in Ibadan, Nigeria.

METHODS: This prospective observational study analyzed data from the Ibadan Heart Failure Project. Adults aged 18 years or older with chronic heart failure, baseline QRS duration, one-year follow-up/vital-status information and valid outcome time were included. QRS duration was analyzed primarily as <120 ms versus ≥120 ms. Mortality was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox proportional-hazards models; rehospitalization and the composite outcome were analyzed using logistic regression.

RESULTS: The current analysis was based on participants recruited between 01 January 2016 and 27 June 2023. The final analytic cohort comprised 1047 patients; 380 (36.3%) had QRS ≥120 ms. Patients with prolonged QRS were older, more often male, more likely to have kidney dysfunction and had more adverse echocardiographic remodeling. One-year mortality was higher with QRS ≥120 ms than QRS <120 ms (84/380, 22.1% versus 106/667, 15.9%; log-rank p = 0.012). In univariable Cox analysis, QRS ≥120 ms was associated with mortality (HR 1.44; 95% CI 1.08 to 1.92; p = 0.012). After multivariable adjustment, this association was attenuated (adjusted HR 1.12; 95% CI 0.80 to 1.58; p = 0.504). Adjusted associations with rehospitalization (OR 1.09; 95% CI 0.55 to 2.15; p = 0.813) and the composite outcome (OR 1.19; 95% CI 0.82 to 1.71; p = 0.361) were also non-significant.

CONCLUSION: In this Nigerian chronic heart-failure cohort, QRS ≥120 ms identified a higher-risk clinical phenotype and poorer crude one-year survival. After adjustment, it was not an independent predictor of mortality, rehospitalization or the composite outcome.

articles.title: Fully Automated, Explainable AI Analysis of Coronary CTA Improves Prediction of Major Cardiovascular Events.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is central to noninvasive diagnosis and risk assessment, yet current workflows are labor-intensive and depend on semiquantitative scoring systems that do not fully leverage prognostic information in CCTA.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study were to develop and validate a fully automated, explainable artificial intelligence (AI) system (AI-automated coronary analysis [ACA]) for comprehensive CCTA analysis to predict major adverse cardiovascular events and compare its performance with conventional risk markers.

METHODS: AI-ACA automatically extracts a suite of CCTA-derived biomarkers, including stenosis severity, plaque burden, and composition; AI-derived CAD - reporting and data system (CAD-RADS) (AI-CADRADS); coronary tortuosity; and subtended myocardial mass, to generate interpretable risk estimates. In a retrospective cohort (n = 1,702), we compared AI-ACA with Agatston score, standard demographic risk markers, and AI-CADRADS. Model explainability was assessed using Shapley Additive Explanations.

RESULTS: AI-ACA demonstrated higher predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.81) than Agatston score (AUC: 0.76) and demographic markers (AUC: 0.67), and similar performance to AI-CADRADS (AUC: 0.81). AI-ACA showed better prognostic discrimination than Agatston score, reflected by a higher Harrell C-index (0.791 vs 0.742) and greater separation in event-free survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis (log-rank 31.79 vs 13.71). Shapley Additive Explanations analysis identified total plaque volume and burden, maximum stenosis severity, and AI-CADRADS as the strongest contributors to risk estimation.

CONCLUSIONS: A fully automated and explainable AI platform for CCTA enables comprehensive quantitative characterization of CAD without manual intervention. Although prognostic performance was comparable to AI-CADRADS and modestly higher than Agatston score, the platform provides transparent biomarker-based risk assessment and scalable analysis that may facilitate broader clinical implementation of quantitative CCTA.

articles.title: Impaired Orthostatic Preload Reserve in Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome-Associated Orthostatic Tachycardia.
Beyond health behaviours: Decomposing cause-specific associations between neighbourhood deprivation and mortality in Busan, South Korea.
articles.abstract: Health behaviours are widely thought to explain why residents of deprived neighbourhoods die earlier, but it is unclear whether their contribution is similar across causes of death. We analysed 203 small administrative areas (eup/myeon/dong) in Busan, South Korea, using an ecological cross-sectional design. Deprivation was measured with 11 census indicators. Twenty-two indicators from the Korea Community Health Survey were grouped into three domains: core health behaviours (such as smoking, high-risk drinking and walking), health status (such as diagnosed hypertension or diabetes, obesity and depressive symptoms), and healthcare use and awareness. Regression-based decomposition with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals estimated how much of the association between deprivation and age-standardised mortality in 2020-2024 each domain statistically accounted for, for all-cause and six cause-specific outcomes. Deprivation was associated with higher mortality from every cause. Core health behaviours accounted for 0-24% of these associations, and their share did not differ significantly between causes. Health status accounted for 49.6% (95% CI 19.1 to 99.5) of the association with cerebrovascular mortality, and after correction for multiple comparisons significantly more than for external causes (borderline for suicide). This share remained above zero with population weighting, district fixed effects, adjustment for density and urban-rural status, and spatial-error models, but not consistently in earlier overlapping periods. Cause-specific differences in the decomposition were more evident for area-level health status than for core health behaviours. Efforts to reduce inequalities in cerebrovascular mortality may benefit from attention to cardiometabolic disease burden and its management in deprived neighbourhoods, alongside behavioural and structural measures.

articles.title: Tonlamarsen-Induced Angiotensinogen Suppression: Does It Underlie Its Blood Pressure-Lowering Effect?
Tonlamarsen, a Hepatocyte-Directed Antisense Oligonucleotide Targeting Angiotensinogen: Phase 1 and 2a Clinical Studies.
articles.abstract: Tonlamarsen, a hepatocyte-directed antisense oligonucleotide targeting angiotensinogen (AGT), produced rapid, dose-dependent reductions in circulating AGT in healthy participants and patients with uncontrolled hypertension. A single dose reduced AGT by up to 75.2%, while monthly dosing achieved reductions of up to 79.0% after 4 doses. Tonlamarsen was generally well tolerated, with no clinically meaningful effects on platelet count, potassium, renal function, liver enzymes, or hypotension. Exploratory analyses demonstrated lower systolic blood pressure with tonlamarsen than placebo. These findings support further evaluation of hepatic AGT suppression as a novel therapeutic strategy for hypertension. A Study to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of Monthly Subcutaneous Administration of ION904 in Participants With Uncontrolled Hypertension: NCT05314439).

articles.title: Snapshot of pregnancy Hypertension and Preeclampsia content on TikTok - a look at themes and quality.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We analyzed the most viewed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content on TikTok, specifically characterizing the themes, assessing the quality, and determining how metrics differs for healthcare provider created content.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a cross-sectional study of the top 100 English videos by play count using the hashtags #preeclampsia, #preeclampsiaawareness, #gestationalhypertension, #pregnancyhypertension, #eclampsia, and #postpartumhypertension. Videos were generated using the TikTok Data Extractor by Apify.
