MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was content quality via the Global Quality Score (GQS) - a validated tool ranging from 1 (low, use discouraged) to 5 (high, medically useful). Secondary outcomes included the number of videos relevant to the hashtag, and assessments of medical claims content using mDISCERN. Secondary analysis included sub-stratifying by healthcare provider status.

RESULTS: Of the top 600 videos across all hashtags, 527 (87.8%) were relevant and 109 (20.7%) videos were created by healthcare providers. The median [interquartile range (IQR)] GQS for all videos was 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) suggesting videos were low quality and not useful. The GQS for healthcare provider content was higher (3 [1.5,3] versus 1 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Khosla et al., 2021 [1,2]), p < 0.01). Only 47 (8.9%) videos made medical claims and the overall median [IQR] mDISCERN score was 2 (Anonymous. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia: ACOG Practice Bulletin, Number 222. Obstet Gynecol [Internet]., 2020; Williamson et al., 2023 [1,3]) and was higher for healthcare provider content (2 [1.5,3] versus 1 [0,1], p < 0.01). Moreover, content by healthcare providers was more accurate (84.4% versus 13.3%, p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: The TikTok hypertensive disorders of pregnancy content, while relevant, is of low quality and usefulness. Of the content making medical claims, the accuracy was higher for healthcare provider created content. This identifies an opportunity for healthcare professionals to create reliable, accessible content as an alternative for patient education.

articles.title: The JRS guideline for the management of drug-induced lung disease.
authors: Japanese Respiratory Society Committee for the formulation of the Management of drug-induced lung disease [3rd Edition]
articles.abstract: This consensus statement from the Japanese Respiratory Society summarizes updated recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of drug-induced lung injury (DLI). DLI includes respiratory disorders caused by prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, herbal agents, and supplements. Clinical manifestations range widely from mild and reversible conditions to severe and life-threatening disease. Among these, diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) is particularly important because it is associated with severe respiratory failure, poor treatment response, fibrosis, and high mortality. An accurate diagnosis requires careful exclusion of other causes, especially respiratory infections, heart failure, and progression of the underlying disease. Chest computed tomography imaging has a central role in diagnosis and classification, particularly for distinguishing DAD from non-DAD patterns such as organizing pneumonia, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, and nonspecific interstitial pneumonia. Biomarkers including Krebs von den Lungen-6, surfactant protein-A, and surfactant protein-D may assist in disease evaluation and monitoring. Major causative agents include anticancer drugs, immune checkpoint inhibitors, molecular target drugs, antimicrobial agents, and antirheumatic drugs. Risk factors include older age, pre-existing interstitial lung disease, smoking history, impaired respiratory function, and combination chemotherapy. The cornerstone of management is prompt discontinuation of the suspected drug, followed by glucocorticoid therapy according to disease severity and appropriate respiratory support. Early recognition, multidisciplinary evaluation, and close monitoring are essential for improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension in rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease: A case with possible contribution of alveolar septal inflammation.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) associated with connective tissue diseases is heterogeneous, and immunosuppressive therapy has been reported to improve PH in selected patients; however, the pathological basis of such responsiveness remains unclear. We report a 39-year-old never-smoking woman with PH complicated by rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD). PH showed a marked and reproducible response to systemic corticosteroids, paralleling ILD activity. Thoracoscopic lung biopsy demonstrated lymphocytic alveolar septal inflammation with fibrotic and emphysematous changes, without significant pulmonary arterial remodeling. Although initially steroid-responsive, PH became irreversible, with progressive fibrosis and emphysema. This case suggests that inflammation-mediated alveolar-capillary injury may contribute to a transiently reversible component of PH in RA-ILD, highlighting the importance of sustained inflammatory control.

articles.title: Responsiveness of dyspnea outcome measures after pulmonary rehabilitation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: comparison of modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale and Transition Dyspnea Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scale is the gold standard for assessing dyspnea; however, its responsiveness following pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) may be limited. This study aimed to comprehensively compare the internal and external responsiveness of the mMRC scale with the Transition Dyspnea Index (TDI) following PR in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

METHODS: This retrospective, observational study included patients with stable COPD who completed a 6-week structured PR program. Internal and external responsiveness of the mMRC and TDI following PR were investigated. Internal responsiveness was assessed using effect size and normalized change, and external responsiveness was determined by the detection rate of improvement relative to the minimal clinically important difference (MCID).

RESULTS: Forty patients with COPD were included. Both mMRC and TDI scores improved significantly after PR. However, the effect size was larger for TDI (0.85) than for mMRC (0.60), and 80% of participants showed predominant improvement on TDI, as measured by normalized change. Fifteen percent of participants showed greater improvement on mMRC than on TDI, and all achieved TDI improvements exceeding MCID (≥1). For external responsiveness, 95% achieved improvements in their TDI scores above the MCID (≥1), whereas only 42.5% did so on mMRC. In addition, 52.5% showed improvement in dyspnea detected only by TDI, while none showed such improvements detected only by mMRC.

CONCLUSIONS: The TDI showed superior internal and external responsiveness compared to the mMRC scale, suggesting that TDI could be preferable for assessing dyspnea following PR.

articles.title: Application of the ICF in the functioning assessment of children with suspected developmental coordination difficulties.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) is based on a biopsychosocial model that promotes a multidimensional approach in rehabilitation. The ICF has been recommended as a framework for clinical reasoning in several health conditions, including those characterized by motor difficulties such as Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD). We compared the functioning profile of children with motor challenges (at risk [r-DCD] and probable DCD [p-DCD]) with those with typical neurodevelopment (TND) using the ICF framework.

METHODS: Cross-sectional study involving children from Southern Brazil. ICF-informed instruments included: body functions (MABC-2, 6MWT, SDQ-Por); activities (DCDQ-Br, IPAQ-SF, SDQ-Por); participation (PEM-CY) and contextual factors (sex and age). Statistics included the chi-square test, Fisher's exact test, and the Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn's post hoc test with p < 0.05.

RESULTS: 208 children (mean age 8.2 [1.3] years) classified as TND (n = 158), r-DCD (n = 25) and p-DCD (n = 25) were included. In the activities domain, except for the expected lower motor skills in the p-DCD group, no differences were found across groups. In participation, there were significant differences only for lower involvement in the community for p-DCD (p = 0.016).

CONCLUSION: The impact of motor challenges was found in activities and in participation. These findings underscore the role for physical therapy interventions targeting improved coordination and balance while encouraging social interactions. The study serves as an example of how to select and combine assessment instruments aligned with ICF domains to evaluate children with motor difficulties.

articles.title: Experiences of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings and their communication: A systematic review of expectant parent and ultrasound Practitioner perspectives.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Current evidence suggests that the identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings are associated with negative psychological outcomes for both patients and ultrasound practitioners. There remains a need to synthesise and better understand this evidence to assess the extent and nature of the problem. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences, views and preferences of ultrasound practitioners and expectant parents regarding the identification and communication of adverse prenatal ultrasound findings.

METHODS: Systematic review and narrative synthesis of studies reporting qualitative and quantitative data. The databases MEDLINE, CINAHL and Web-of-Science were searched between January-2010 and May-2026.

RESULTS: Twelve studies were included. Findings highlight a lack of formal communication training and limited emotional support for practitioners when identifying and communicating adverse prenatal findings, contributing to anxiety, burnout, and role-related uncertainty. For patients, inadequate explanations, inconsistent communication, and insufficient time to process information were associated with immediate shock and longer-term psychological burden. Additionally, environmental and organisational factors, such as time pressures, workload, and suboptimal clinical settings, further influenced communication quality and exacerbated distress for both patients and practitioners.

CONCLUSION: Identification and communication of adverse prenatal findings have significant psychological impacts on patients and practitioners, influenced by communication quality. Ongoing gaps in training, emotional support, and role clarity contribute to inconsistent practice and increased distress, highlighting the need for structured frameworks and strengthened organisational support. Future research should evaluate communication interventions and include more diverse populations to improve psychological outcomes and consistency of care.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Structured, empathetic communication of adverse findings should be supported by targeted training, clear role delineation, and organisational support to reduce psychological burden and improve consistency of care.

articles.title: ZSSS, a saponin-rich fraction from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen, alleviates neuroinflammation after CVST with mechanistic insights.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation following cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) is a critical factor leading to neurological deficits. The cGAS-STING signaling pathway, as a central pathway of the innate immune response, plays a key role in the onset and progression of neuroinflammation. Ziziphi Spinosae Semen is a medicinal plant, and modern studies have suggested its neuroprotective effects. However, its active fraction and mechanisms of action against neuroinflammation following CVST remain to be further explored.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to screen the effective fraction of Ziziphi Spinosae Semen for neuroinflammatory effects after CVST, evaluate its therapeutic effects in vivo and in vitro, and investigate the mechanism by which it relieves neuroinflammation following CVST.

METHODS: Four crude extracts were prepared from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen and screened via in vitro antioxidant and anti-neuroinflammatory assays. After purification by macroporous resin and further activity screening, the active fraction was obtained and characterized by UPLC-Q-Exactive-MS/MS. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to predict the potential targets and mechanisms. In the 40% FeCl3-induced mouse CVST model, the screened effective fraction of Ziziphi Spinosae Semen was orally administered once daily for 7 consecutive days. Neurobehavioral performance, neuronal injury, neuroinflammation, and cGAS-STING signaling were evaluated using behavioral tests, H&E staining, immunohistochemistry, TUNEL staining, transcriptome sequencing, and Western blotting. In the LPS-induced BV2 cell inflammatory model, following 24 h of ZSSS intervention, we investigated the specific mechanisms of action of ZSSS using ELISA, ROS assays, JC-1 staining, Mito-Tracker staining, Western blotting, cytoplasmic mtDNA detection, Co-IP, and Calcein-AM/PI double-staining.

RESULTS: The 70% ethanol-eluted fraction was identified as the effective fraction of Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (ZSSS). ZSSS treatment dose-dependently ameliorated neurobehavioral performance in CVST mice, alleviated neuronal injury, and suppressed microglial activation and neuronal apoptosis. Qualitative and quantitative analyses revealed that saponins were the major constituents, with jujuboside A (JuA) accounting for 15.86%. Network pharmacology predicted JuA as a candidate active component in ZSSS, showing favorable binding affinity for cGAS and STING. Meanwhile, transcriptome sequencing of brain tissue revealed that differentially expressed genes were significantly enriched in the cGAS-STING and NF-κB signaling pathways. ZSSS markedly downregulated the protein expression of cGAS and p-STING in brain tissue. Molecular analyses suggest that ZSSS could substantially alleviate LPS-induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, regulate mitochondrial dynamics-related proteins, reduce cytosolic mtDNA release, thereby inhibiting activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, decreasing the release of inflammatory cytokines, and suppressing apoptosis. Co-IP indicated that ZSSS attenuated STING-TBK1 interaction, and DMXAA rescue experiments further supported the involvement of the cGAS-STING pathway.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified ZSSS as a saponin-rich fraction from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen with potent anti-neuroinflammatory effects against CVST. Mechanistically, ZSSS may alleviate neuroinflammation by improving mitochondrial function and reducing the release of mtDNA into the cytoplasm, thereby inhibiting the cGAS-STING signaling pathway. These findings provide a pharmacological basis for ZSSS as a potential immunomodulatory candidate for treating CVST-associated neuroinflammation.

articles.title: From puerperal sepsis (Death of the puerperium) through dysentere to a Spa town. Diary entries of general practitioners František and Bohumil Bouček in Poděbrady (1841-1923).
articles.abstract: The rapid development of medicine in Central Europe in the second half of the 19th and first half ot the 20th Century was not only a question of prominent scientific centres, but also of educated specialists in regional cities. We can try to understand better the development of general practitioners of medicine in Austro-Hungaria and Czechoslovakia during 80 years through the diary entries of František Bouček (1810-1882) and his son Bohumil (1850-1926). The early publication of their entries and following reception of their texts in broad public is rather unique in the context of the Czech lands. They both served as general practitioner in Poděbrady in Central Bohemia and were involved in developing of obstetrics and surgery. Both studied as well furthering of preparing and preventing local epidemics and pandemics. No less interesting are their remarks on quality of studies at Vienna University and Charles-Ferdinand University at Prague from the middle until the end of the 19th Century. The paper is focused on the social aspects of their professional and organizational activities.

articles.title: Sir Roger Bannister (1929-2018): beyond the track, documenting his influence in the field of autonomic neurology.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract: Sir Roger Bannister, best known for running the sub-four-minute mile, was influential in establishing the field of autonomic neurology. His early experiences studying exercise physiology, spinal cord injury, and thermoregulation shaped his interest in the mechanisms underlying autonomic regulation. The development of therapeutic approaches such as droxidopa to treat dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency could not have been accomplished without Bannister's dedication and contributions. Through his research, collaborations, and leadership in establishing the Clinical Autonomic Research Society, Bannister helped transform a field that was once dismissed as 'no more than an overture' into a lasting discipline in the field of neurology.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and blood pressure in childhood: A systematic review of prospective observational studies.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal exposure to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) may affect early-life cardiovascular programming, but epidemiological findings regarding blood pressure outcomes in children remain inconsistent. This systematic review synthesized evidence on associations between prenatal PFAS exposure and blood pressure or hypertension in children and adolescents.

METHODS: Following Cochrane recommendations and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, MEDLINE (EBSCO), and Embase were searched through 02 November 2026. The search strategy was developed with an information specialist. Prospective studies reporting prenatal PFAS exposure and offspring blood pressure outcomes were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Due to substantial methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively without meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Thirteen prospective cohort studies from North America, Europe, and Asia were included. Associations between individual PFAS and systolic or diastolic blood pressure were generally small and inconsistent across compounds, exposure windows, and ages at outcome assessment. Evidence regarding PFAS mixtures was similarly heterogeneous, with some studies reporting associations with systolic blood pressure or cardiometabolic outcomes, while others observed null or inverse associations. Heterogeneity in exposure assessment, mixture modeling approaches, and outcome definitions precluded quantitative synthesis.

LIMITATIONS OF EVIDENCE: The evidence was limited by heterogeneity across studies, potential residual confounding, differences in exposure assessment and outcome definitions, and varying risk of bias.

INTERPRETATION: Current evidence suggests that prenatal PFAS exposure may influence offspring BP, but findings remain inconsistent. Harmonized longitudinal studies with standardized exposure assessment and robust mixture methodologies are needed to clarify the role of early-life PFAS exposure in pediatric cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Psychological, lifestyle, and self-management profiles among Indonesian adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia family life survey.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus requires continued psychological adjustment, healthy lifestyle behaviors, and ongoing disease management. This study examined heterogeneity in psychological functioning, well-being, lifestyle behaviors, and diabetes care indicators among adults with diabetes in the fifth wave of the Indonesia Family Life Survey (IFLS-5). The analysis included 685 respondents with a self-reported diagnosis of diabetes by a health professional and 14 binary indicators in six domains: psychological distress (depressive symptoms, sleep disturbance, neuroticism), subjective well-being (life satisfaction, general happiness), lifestyle behaviors (smoking behavior, physical activity, sweet food consumption), diabetes self-management (medication use, health monitoring), comorbidity and functional burden (comorbid chronic conditions, functional limitation), and healthcare service utilization (outpatient health service utilization, inpatient hospitalization history). A three-class solution was retained because BIC and CAIC were lowest at three classes, the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test did not support a fourth class, the smallest class comprised 16.2% of the sample, and the classes were interpretable; class separation was moderate (entropy = 0.719). The classes were Low-Distress Low-Engagement (61.1%), with low distress, high well-being, and comparatively low medication use and monitoring; High-Engagement High-Comorbidity (22.7%), with a high probability of current medication use and health monitoring and the heaviest comorbidity and functional burden; and High-Distress Low-Engagement (16.2%), with elevated depressive symptoms, lower well-being, and the lowest probabilities of medication use and monitoring. The three-class structure was reproduced when seven indicators kept their original scales, although membership in the distress class was less stable. The same three classes were obtained without the Neuroticism indicator, whose internal consistency was low, and adjusting the standard errors for household and enumeration-area clustering changed them only slightly. These co-occurring patterns require longitudinal and external validation.

articles.title: Effects of structured multimodal electronic feedback delivered through notability on expressive writing performance in elementary students with ADHD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Students with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) often experience persistent difficulties in expressive writing due to deficits in attention regulation, executive functioning, and self-monitoring. Although technology-supported feedback has shown promise, evidence regarding structured multimodal electronic feedback remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the effects of a structured electronic feedback intervention delivered through the Notability application on expressive writing performance among elementary students with ADHD.

METHOD: A multiple-probe design across participants was implemented with three elementary female students diagnosed with ADHD. The intervention combined audio feedback, written annotations, error highlighting, reinforcement, and corrective guidance. Expressive writing was assessed using an analytic criterion-referenced rubric. Data were analyzed using systematic visual analysis and Tau-U effect-size statistics.

RESULTS: Visual analysis demonstrated immediate and consistent improvements in expressive writing following intervention across all participants. Tau-U effect sizes were 1.00 for each participant (p < .001), indicating complete non-overlap between baseline and intervention phases. Maintenance probes suggested that performance improvements were generally sustained over time.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings provide preliminary evidence that a structured multimodal electronic feedback package delivered through the Notability application may improve expressive writing in elementary students with ADHD. Given the single-case design and small sample, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. The intervention may also support psychological processes associated with ADHD, including self-regulation, sustained attention, and learning motivation. Further research with larger samples is needed to confirm these findings and examine the underlying psychological mechanisms.

articles.title: Denoising filters for fast Monte Carlo and genetic algorithm-based optimization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the suitability of denoising filters for accelerating Monte Carlo (MC) dose calculation within genetic algorithm (GA) optimization frameworks for external beam radiation therapy treatment planning through preservation of optimization-relevant information in filtered low-statistic simulations.

APPROACH: Gaussian smoothing, adaptive anisotropic diffusion (AAD), and wavelet threshold denoising (WTD) were applied to Geant4-generated three-dimensional MC dose distributions. Filter parameters were tuned across varying simulation conditions and evaluated using voxel-based dose agreement metrics. Filter performance within a GA framework was then assessed using multiple realistic objective functions, with optimization robustness quantified using Spearman rank correlation, winner identification, and winner consistency across repeated filtered MC dose calculations.

MAIN RESULTS: MC particle statistics and voxel resolution had the strongest influence on optimal parameter selection for all three denoising filters, while beam energy, field size, and evaluation metric exhibited comparatively weaker effects. Filtering improved the ranking stability of candidate system configurations for low-statistic MC dose distributions, supporting faster evaluation within stochastic optimization algorithms. AAD filtering provided the highest ranking fidelity for objectives dependent on localized dose extrema, while WTD consistently identified the optimal configuration for dose-volume objectives across simulation statistics despite lower overall rank correlation. In contrast, Gaussian smoothing frequently degraded ranking fidelity for these objectives due to oversmoothing of important dose features.

SIGNIFICANCE: Denoising filters can accelerate MC-driven optimization by enabling lower-statistic dose calculations while preserving optimization-relevant ranking information. Because optimal tuning depended primarily on particle statistics and voxel resolution rather than beam configuration, filter parameters can remain applicable across a wide range of candidate treatment setups. AAD and WTD showed the greatest promise for integration into MC-driven optimization workflows, with relative performance depending on the underlying MC noise level.

articles.title: Perfectionism and burnout among pediatric intensive care unit nurses: The mediation role of workaholism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) nurses work in high-acuity environments characterized by complex clinical demands, repeated exposure to critically ill children, parental distress, and pediatric death, placing them at increased risk of burnout. Perfectionistic tendencies may promote excessive and compulsive work patterns, or workaholism, that further deplete nurses' psychological resources. However, the pathways linking perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout remain insufficiently understood in pediatric critical care nursing.

AIM: This study examined the relationships among perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout among PICU nurses and investigated the mediating role of workaholism in the perfectionism-burnout relationship.

METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 431 PICU nurses recruited from eight hospitals across five Egyptian governorates. Data were collected using a web-based questionnaire including the Short Almost Perfect Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, and Dutch Work Addiction Scale. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation, hierarchical multiple regression, and mediation path analysis.

RESULTS: Burnout was positively associated with workaholism (r = 0.218, p < 0.01) and perfectionism (r = 0.247, p < 0.01). A significant positive correlation was also observed between perfectionism and workaholism (r = 0.334, p < 0.01). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect association between perfectionism and burnout through workaholism (standardized indirect effect = 0.051, bootstrap 95% CI [0.016, 0.089]), accounting for approximately 20.6% of the total association and supporting partial statistical mediation. Hierarchical regression analysis identified alternating shifts, perceived insufficient income, a nurse-to-patient ratio of 1:3, workaholism, and perfectionism as significant predictors of burnout.

CONCLUSION: Perfectionism, workaholism, and burnout were significantly interrelated among pediatric intensive care unit nurses. Workaholism showed a partial statistical mediating role in the association between perfectionism and burnout, suggesting that compulsive work behaviors may represent a relevant behavioral pathway linking these psychological characteristics. The findings highlight the importance of addressing both individual and organizational factors through strategies targeting maladaptive perfectionism, excessive work involvement, staffing adequacy, and psychological support. Longitudinal research is needed to establish temporal relationships and evaluate interventions aimed at reducing burnout.

articles.title: [Air pollution and cancer mortality in municipalities of the Valparaíso Region, Chile (2009-2019)].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between annual concentrations of SO2, PM2,5, and PM10 and age-standardized mortality rates for all cancers and stomach cancer in five municipalities of the Valparaíso Region, Chile, between 2009 and 2019.

METHOD: An ecological time-series study was conducted in Valparaíso, Viña del Mar, Quintero, Quillota, and Catemu. Age-standardized mortality rates were calculated using the direct method, and annual air pollutant concentrations were obtained from the National Air Quality Information System. Municipality-specific Prais-Winsten regression models were fitted, adjusting for temporal trends and first-order autocorrelation. Exploratory sex-stratified analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: Positive associations were observed between SO2 and stomach cancer mortality in Catemu (β=0.62; 95%CI: 0.28-0.96), PM10 and all-cancer mortality in Quintero (β=2.81; 95%CI: 1.05-4.57), and PM2,5 and stomach cancer mortality in Viña del Mar (β=0.55; 95%CI: 0.22-0.88). Among men in Quintero, PM10 was also associated with both all-cancer and stomach cancer mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide local epidemiological evidence supporting an association between long-term air pollution exposure and cancer mortality across municipalities with contrasting environmental profiles, like in Quintero and Catemu, two industrially impacted territories with a long history of environmental contamination. Although causal inference is limited by the ecological design and the lack of individual-level data, the results support strengthening environmental surveillance and conducting longitudinal studies to better characterize the impact of chronic air pollution exposure on cancer mortality in Chile.

articles.title: Attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction in older adults: An indirect association through perceived health.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether perceived health showed an indirect association in the relationship between attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction among older adults.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 303 individuals aged 65 years and older with no prior diagnosis of hypertension in Alanya, Türkiye. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Attitudes Scale towards Prevention of Hypertension (ASPH), the Perception of Health Scale (PHS), and the Life Satisfaction in the Elderly Scale (LSES). Pearson correlation, multiple linear regression, adjusted regression, and covariate-adjusted mediation analyses with 5000 bootstrap samples were performed.

RESULTS: Attitudes toward hypertension prevention and perceived health were positively associated with life satisfaction. In the main regression model, both attitudes toward hypertension prevention (β = 0.422, p < 0.001) and perceived health (β = 0.334, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with life satisfaction, explaining 46.2% of its variance (R² = 0.462). These associations remained significant after adjustment for sociodemographic and health-related covariates (β = 0.363 and β = 0.241, respectively; both p < 0.001). Covariate-adjusted mediation analysis showed a significant indirect association between attitudes toward hypertension prevention and life satisfaction through perceived health (B = 0.0765, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0366, 0.1182], p < 0.001), accounting for 23.4% of the adjusted total association.

CONCLUSION: More favorable hypertension prevention attitudes and better perceived health were associated with higher life satisfaction. Perceived health showed a significant indirect association between prevention attitudes and life satisfaction. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal and causal nature of these relationships.

articles.title: Targeting immune cells in type 2 diabetes: Immunoregulatory mechanisms of natural products.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is no longer viewed solely as a disorder of insulin secretion and insulin action. Three decades of work have established that a chronic, low-grade, non-resolving immune response - metaflammation - operates in adipose tissue, liver, skeletal muscle, pancreatic islets and the gut, and that this response is both a consequence and a cause of metabolic failure. Every major leukocyte lineage participates. Adipose tissue macrophages accumulate, change phenotype and form crown-like structures; dendritic cells prime pathogenic T helper responses; neutrophils release elastase and extracellular traps; eosinophils and group 2 innate lymphoid cells sustain the type 2 cytokine tone that protects insulin sensitivity; natural killer cells sense adipocyte stress and license macrophage activation; CD8+ and T helper 1 cells drive effector inflammation while regulatory T cells restrain it; and B cells contribute pathogenic immunoglobulin G. Against this background, natural products have attracted sustained interest because many of them act on precisely the nodes - nuclear factor-κB, the NLRP3 inflammasome, AMP-activated protein kinase, sirtuin 1, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2, Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling - that govern immune cell fate in metabolic tissue. This review first maps the immune cell landscape of T2DM lineage by lineage, then examines ten natural products with the most developed immunological data sets: curcumin, charantin, silybin, cinnamaldehyde, resveratrol, quercetin, alpha-lipoic acid, 4-hydroxyisoleucine, berberine and avenanthramide C. We then take a deliberately sceptical view of translation, addressing pharmacokinetics and achievable tissue exposure, the gap between surrogate and true immune endpoints in human trials, drug interactions, and the biomarker and trial-design work that inflammation-stratified studies will require.

articles.title: Research progress of exhaled breath analysis in diagnosis of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).
articles.abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) has become the most common type of chronic liver disorder, which with risk of progression to cirrhosis and cancer. Due to the lack of definitive symptoms, liver biopsy is still the gold standard in the diagnosis of NAFLD. However, over the past few decades, there have been significant advancements in non-invasive biomarkers and techniques for diagnosing NAFLD. The analysis of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath is becoming one of the promising strategies for NAFLD detection as it may offer an inexpensive, rapid, and non-invasive diagnostic method. In this article,we provide a comprehensive review of the current and emerging VOCs in exhaled breath used for assessing NAFLD, highlighting their diagnostic specificity across different stages of the disease. This article reviews the application of isoprene, acetone, ethanol, dimethyl sulfide, carbon disulphide, acetaldehyde, methanol, trimethylamine, styrene, D-limonene, acetophenone, terpinene, pentane, methane, and others in the analysis of exhaled breath for NAFLD. The study shows that exhaled breath analysis has a certain value in the diagnosis of NAFLD. We believe that the role of exhaled breath analysis in the diagnosis of NAFLD may be a key area for future research. However, due to the limitations of the current studies, the practical application of exhaled breath analysis in NAFLD diagnosis remains a developing field with much progress yet to be made.

articles.title: Interference-Driven Loss of Spectral Specificity in Long-Wavelength NIR Lactate Sensing in Complex Media.
articles.abstract: Continuous lactate monitoring is valuable for managing peritoneal dialysis in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), where lactate acts both as a marker of dialysis efficacy and an early indicator of sepsis. Existing monitoring approaches are intermittent and invasive.Long-wavelength near-infrared (LWNIR) spectroscopy enables the possibility of non-invasive, real-time lactate sensing, but its translation has been hindered by calibration instability and reduced spectral specificity in complex biological media. These limitations arise fromoverlapping biomolecular absorption signatures and the strong, dispersive nature of water absorption in this region. This study investigates how biochemical and mechanical interference affects LWNIR-based lactate estimation. To do this rigorously, we developed clinically informed biophantoms incorporating glucose, albumin and urea as key interferents relevant to CKD and peritoneal dialysis. These biophantoms were first examined in buffered media and then extended to human serum to capture additional biological complexity. To emulate conditions similar to dialysis operation, serum was also circulated through a cuvette under controlled flow. Standard machine-learning regressors successfully recovered lactate concentrations; however, spectral specificity deteriorated substantially in more complex matrices, as reflected by the increased broadening of wavelength-selection profiles derived from variable importance in projection (VIP) analysis. The newly developed clinically relevant biophantoms improved wavelength localisation relative to conventional buffer-only systems. These findings underscore the need for realistic, clinically informed calibration strategies to achieve spectrally robust LWNIR-based lactate sensing, and they outline a pathway towards reliable optical monitoring technologies for dialysis and wider CKD management.

articles.title: MRAST-Net: A Lightweight Multi-Receptive-Field Residual Temporal Network for 12-Lead ECG Classification.
articles.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals play an important role in cardiovascular disease screening, clinical monitoring, and remote healthcare. However, existing high-performing ECG classification methods usually rely on complex deep learning architectures, which often involve a large number of parameters, high computational cost, and limited deployability in resource-constrained scenarios. To balance classification performance and lightweight deployment, this paper proposes MRAST-Net, a lightweight multi-receptive-field residual temporal network for 12-lead ECG classification. The proposed model first employs a lead mixing layer to enable cross-lead information interaction. It then uses a lightweight multi-scale residual depthwise convolution module to extract local waveform morphology features under different receptive fields, while an efficient channel attention mechanism is introduced to enhance informative channel responses. On this basis, a temporal convolutional network is further incorporated to model long-range dynamic dependencies, and attentive statistics pooling is used to aggregate global statistical features for final multi-label classification. Experiments on two public 12-lead ECG datasets, PTB-XL and CPSC-2018, show that the proposed model achieves AUC scores of 93.12 $\pm$ 0.16\%, 92.29 $\pm$ 0.80\%, and 92.62 $\pm$ 0.51\%, and ACC scores of 89.17 $\pm$ 0.09\%, 96.40 $\pm$ 0.02\%, and 97.72 $\pm$ 0.07\% on the 5-superclass, 23-subclass, and 44-diagnostic-class tasks of PTB-XL, respectively. On CPSC-2018, MRAST-Net achieves an AUC of 96.57 $\pm$ 0.43\% and an ACC of 96.59 $\pm$ 0.26\% under 5$\times$3 nested cross-validation. These results demonstrate that MRAST-Net achieves competitive classification performance while maintaining a low parameter scale, indicating its potential for deployment in resource-constrained scenarios such as portable monitoring devices, real-time assisted diagnosis, and primary healthcare.

articles.title: Machine learning classification of respiratory diseases using integrated breath measurements from the Inflammacheck® Device.
articles.abstract: Background:Lung cancer and pneumonia can present with non-specific symptoms that overlap with other respiratory conditions. This study evaluated whether breath measurements from the Inflammacheck® device contain sufficient diagnostic information to support machine-learning classification of lung cancer and pneumonia.Methods:A secondary analysis of 282 participants with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis, breathing pattern disorder, pneumonia, lung cancer and healthy controls was undertaken. Seven device-derived variables comprising H₂O₂, exhalation duration, sample collection time and up to 6-minutes of tidal-breathing based peak CO₂, breath humidity, breath temperature, exhalation flow rate were analysed. Eight-class and three-class shrinkage linear discriminant analysis (LDA) models were evaluated using stratified 10-fold cross-validation with out-of-fold predictions. Class-specific probability thresholds were scanned within prespecified 85-95% specificity ranges. An exploratory soft-voting ensemble combining LDA, Extra Trees, radial-basis-function support-vector machine and XGBoost was also evaluated.Results:Eight-class classification showed limited discrimination, whereas consolidation into three classes (lung cancer, pneumonia and other respiratory disease) improved diagnostic separation. At operating thresholds corresponding to approximately 89-90% specificity, the 3-class LDA demonstrated discriminatory ability for both lung cancer and pneumonia, with AUROCs of 0.650 and 0.728, respectively. The soft-voting ensemble model further improved discrimination, increasing AUROC to 0.725 for lung cancer and 0.753 for pneumonia.Conclusions:Inflammacheck® variables contain promising measurable discriminatory information for further development of a screening-tool. Future modelling of the underlying continuous breath time-series ("breathprint") using deep-learning approaches may extract additional discriminatory features not captured by participant-level summary measures.&#xD.

articles.title: A new 'tightrope' model of pro-regenerative scaffolds reveals territorial dynamics of brain immune cells interfaced with suspension nanofibers.
articles.abstract: Tissue engineering is increasingly employing aligned, pro-regenerative nanofiber scaffolds to enhance repair of neurological injuries. Such applications have prompted widespread research into neural cell (particularly neuronal) responses to aligned scaffolds. By contrast, the responses of the brain's ubiquitous immune cells (microglia), are comparatively poorly understood, representing a critical gap in our understanding. Microglia continuously surveil their microenvironment for foreign cells and materials. They can show avid uptake and destruction of biomaterials with negative implications for implantation of therapeutic neuromaterial constructs. A key research limitation is the lack of tractable experimental systems (with imaging capacity) that facilitate robust investigation of interactions of microglia at the cell-biomaterial interface. We describe a novel 'tightrope model' deploying suspended, highly-aligned polycaprolactone (PCL) nanofibers. Microglial adherence was achieved on these constructs which were compatible with multiple imaging techniques including dynamic time lapse. Microglia retained stereotypical migration and territorial behaviours on the scaffolds, supporting the inference that biomaterial-derived cues did not significantly alter these highly-programmed neurobiological behaviors/parameters observed in vivo. Our method allowed us to gain key neurobiological insights into microglial behaviours in real-time. Cell migration rates were measured (mean 1.9 ± 0.8 µm/min; max for each cell ranged from 7.4 - 24.4 µm/min), along with cumulative distance travelled, and intersomatic distancing. We consider the biological interfacing methodology described to have widespread application in evaluating the migratory cell behaviors on aligned biomaterials for basic and translational research in regenerative neurology.

articles.title: Mental Health Crisis Admissions in Patients With Cirrhosis: A Nationwide Analysis of Burden, Predictors, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with cirrhosis carry a heavy burden of psychiatric comorbidity. We aimed to characterize the burden, predictors, and clinical outcomes of mental health crisis admissions in this population.

METHODS: This is a cross-sectional, retrospective analysis of the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2023. Mental health crisis admissions were identified using primary diagnostic codes for mood disorders, self-harm, and psychotic disorders. Clinical outcomes and temporal trends were compared between patients with and without cirrhosis. Within the cirrhosis cohort, mental health crisis admissions were further compared with cirrhosis admissions for all other reasons to identify factors associated with psychiatric presentation.

RESULTS: Among 8,214,999 mental health crisis admissions, 52,285 (0.6%) involved patients with cirrhosis. Patients with cirrhosis were older (mean: 53.0 vs. 41.8 y) and more often male (62.4% vs. 52.5%). Alcohol use-related diagnoses (OR=2.31, 95% CI: 2.22-2.42), opioid use disorder (OR=3.73, 95% CI: 3.50-3.98), and homelessness (OR=8.99, 95% CI: 8.49-9.52) were independently associated with mental health crisis admission in patients with cirrhosis. Mental health crises as a proportion of all cirrhosis admissions declined over time (OR per year 0.93, 95% CI: 0.91-0.94). In all mental health crisis admissions, cirrhosis was independently associated with higher odds of nonhome discharge (aOR=1.41, 95% CI: 1.33-1.50, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Mental health crisis admissions in patients with cirrhosis are strongly associated with substance use disorders and homelessness and are associated with increased rates of nonhome discharge. These findings highlight the intersection of psychiatric, medical, and social complexity in this population.

articles.title: Caregiver-Informed Safety and System Requirements for Real-Time Feedback During Pediatric Inhaler Use: Qualitative Concept-Elicitation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Correct use of a pressurized metered-dose inhaler (pMDI), usually with a valved holding chamber, depends on use-related conditions that caregivers may not observe directly, including inhalation pattern, actuation-inhalation timing, mask seal, and device orientation. Many digital inhaler systems emphasize actuation or adherence. Systems that infer technique-related conditions from proxy signals may add real-time feedback but also create false reassurance if a positive state is displayed when evidence is inadequate. Caregiver expectations for such feedback and its failure states remain poorly characterized before prototype development.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterize caregivers' experiences of pediatric inhaler administration and translate responses to a proposed sensor concept into traceable candidate safety, system, and validation requirements.

METHODS: We conducted 23 semistructured concept-elicitation sessions through Zoom videoconference with 27 caregivers of children who currently or previously used a pMDI. Interviews consisted of 19 individual and 4 dyadic sessions pairing 2 caregivers from different households. Sessions were conducted remotely between April and July 2026 from the University of Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Recruitment originated in Calgary and was not geographically restricted. A 6-phase guide examined current practices, difficulties, prior digital-tool use, and responses to a screen-shared clip-on concept incorporating airflow-, timing-, seal-, and orientation-related sensing; on-device feedback; an optional child-facing app; and a caregiver dashboard. No working prototype was evaluated. Approximately 86,000 transcript words underwent hybrid directed and conventional qualitative content analysis using an 18-category codebook. Two researchers independently coded the complete 27×18 matrix (486 paired decisions) across 2 rounds. Consensus categories were translated into candidate requirements and assigned an earliest verification or evaluation locus. Counts are descriptive caregiver-voice tallies, not prevalence estimates.

RESULTS: Persistent uncertainty about whether administration conditions were adequate was the dominant lived experience (19/27); for 5 caregivers, existing passive cues had not resolved it. A simple, real-time on-device signal was endorsed by 25 caregivers, but willingness to consider the concept was conditional on reliability (9 caregivers named reasons for abandonment, notably a "false green"), low-friction operation during acute symptoms (12/27), minimal added bulk and technique change, and one or more of clinical validation, clinician recommendation, or a trial pathway (composite category; 23/27). Stances on gamification (20/27), dashboard cadence (18/27), aesthetics (24/27), and privacy (18/27) supported an optional, configurable software layer. Intercoder agreement was 94% (Cohen κ=0.88). The analytic synthesis yielded a conceptual architecture separating observable proxy signals, an inference and data-quality gate, and positive, corrective, or uncertain feedback states.

CONCLUSIONS: Participating caregivers prioritized immediate and interpretable feedback about use-related conditions. The findings support conservative state assignment, an explicit uncertain state for indeterminate signals, and app-independent acute-use feedback. These are candidate requirements rather than validated device specifications; subsequent work should proceed through bench verification, simulated-use human factors evaluation, and prospective clinical or field validation.

articles.title: Use of Synchronous, Interruptive Electronic Health Record-Embedded Medication Alerts to Improve Evidence-Based Medication Prescribing: Randomized Comparative Effectiveness Trial of Two Prescriber Alerts.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Antithrombotic stewardship is critical for reducing preventable harm from inappropriate anticoagulant prescribing. Electronic health record (EHR)-embedded clinical decision support (CDS) alerts can prevent prescribing errors at the point of care, but their real-world effectiveness is variable and often limited by alert fatigue and poor workflow integration. Whether augmenting interruptive medication alerts with just‑in‑time access to clinical pharmacists improves prescriber response remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) compare the effectiveness of synchronous, interruptive direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) prescribing alerts with and without an embedded clinical pharmacist referral option for correcting inappropriate new prescriptions within 7 days, and (2) evaluate the system‑level impact of implementing synchronous DOAC alerts on inappropriate prescribing over time.

METHODS: We conducted a prescriber‑level randomized comparative effectiveness trial within a large US academic health system. Prescribers who placed an inappropriate ambulatory apixaban or rivaroxaban order were randomized to receive an interruptive EHR alert either with or without an embedded clinical pharmacist referral link. The primary outcome was any change to the prescription within 7 days. In parallel, a system‑level interrupted time series analysis examined weekly proportions of inappropriate DOAC prescriptions (secondary outcomes) from 24 months before through 29 months after alert implementation. Exploratory outcomes included adverse events within 30 days and alert implementation metrics.

RESULTS: Among 2082 prescribers writing DOAC prescriptions during the study period, 300 (14.4%) triggered at least one inappropriate prescription and were randomized; after prespecified exclusions, 758 alerts across 286 prescribers were analyzed. Overall, 28.9% (219/758) of alerts led to a prescription change within 7 days. The proportion of alerts leading to a prescription change did not differ between alerts with and without pharmacist referral (difference 1 percentage point [95% CI -7 to 9]). The system‑wide proportion of inappropriate DOAC prescriptions exhibited a significant downward preimplementation trend (-0.04 percentage points per week [95% CI -0.06 to -0.02]), followed by an immediate 3.5‑percentage‑point absolute reduction at alert launch (to 9.7%), with no subsequent slope change. Adverse events within 30 days were uncommon and similar across arms.

CONCLUSIONS: Adding an embedded pharmacist referral option to an interruptive DOAC prescribing alert did not increase short‑term prescription changes. However, the implementation of synchronous, user-centered alerts was associated with a system-level reduction in inappropriate DOAC prescribing. These findings support a complementary digital stewardship model in which high‑value, point‑of‑order alerts prevent routine prescribing errors, while clinical pharmacists focus on complex and longitudinal medication management.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05351749; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05351749.

articles.title: Image-Based AI for the Diagnosis of Retinopathy of Prematurity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is one of the major causes of preventable blindness in premature infants. Early screening, accurate diagnosis, and severity classification are crucial for reducing irreversible visual impairment. Recently, image-based AI models have been widely applied to ROP screening, diagnosis, and severity classification. However, the model architecture, data source, validation method, and diagnostic task vary across studies. Consequently, the overall diagnostic efficiency and clinical utility of deep learning (DL) remain to be systematically assessed.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of image-based AI for ROP by disease type, validation method, model type, and use of transfer learning (TL).

METHODS: We performed a systematic search across Web of Science, Embase, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Cochrane Library as of October 12, 2026, to identify studies investigating image-based AI for ROP detection or clinical subtype classification. The risk of bias (RoB) of included studies was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using bivariate mixed-effects models, with analyses stratified by diagnostic task and validation method.

RESULTS: Sixty-two studies contributed 185 contingency tables. For normal vs ROP, pooled sensitivity was 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.96) and specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94-0.97). For normal vs treatment-requiring ROP (TR-ROP), sensitivity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.91-0.99) and specificity was 0.74 (95% CI 0.66-0.80). For mild vs severe ROP, specificity was 0.78 (95% CI 0.59-0.90). In external validation, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.95 (95% CI 0.89-0.97) and 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.90), respectively, while the corresponding estimates were 0.95 (95% CI 0.93-0.96) and 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) in internal validation. For DL and conventional machine learning (ML) models, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98), respectively, while specificity was 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.97) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.84-0.94), respectively. With and without TL, pooled sensitivity was 0.95 (95% CI 0.94-0.96) and 0.95 (95% CI 0.92-0.97), respectively, while specificity was 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.98) and 0.92 (95% CI 0.86-0.95), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Image-based AI may have high sensitivity for ROP assessment, but its specificity is lower for identifying TR-ROP and in the external-validation subgroup. Given the predominance of retrospective studies, heterogeneity, and limited external validation, current evidence supports AI as an adjunct to screening and referral, with clinicians retaining responsibility for diagnostic and treatment decisions. Prospective, multicenter external validation is needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261418502; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261418502.

articles.title: Lion Tracks: Protocol for a Microlongitudinal Feasibility Study of Health Behaviors and Emotional Dynamics in Mother-Child Dyads.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical activity, sleep, digital-media engagement, cognition, and emotional health become increasingly interconnected. However, reliance on retrospective self-report and low-frequency longitudinal designs limits understanding of how these domains relate within individuals and families in daily life. Few studies have integrated ecological momentary assessment (EMA), passive sensing, and wearable monitoring within mother-child dyads.

OBJECTIVE: Lion Tracks aims to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an integrated ambulatory monitoring protocol. Secondary exploratory aims are to characterize within-person, between-person, and dyadic temporal associations among health behaviors, physiological measures, cognition, and momentary anxiety.

METHODS: Lion Tracks is a prospective, observational, microlongitudinal feasibility study targeting 25 mother-child dyads (50 participants), with children aged 11-14 years. Participants complete baseline assessments, 4 weeks of ambulatory monitoring, and poststudy assessments. Garmin wearables monitor physical activity, sleep, heart rate, and heart rate variability. MetricWire (MetricWire, Inc) collects passive smartphone screen-on duration and timing and delivers repeated EMA of momentary affect, anxiety, context, and behaviors. Digital-media engagement characteristics are self-reported through EMA. Brief mobile cognitive testing assesses cognitive performance. A hybrid EMA design combines fixed, pseudorandom, and behavior-contingent assessments to capture daily experiences while limiting participant burden. Primary outcomes include recruitment, retention, acceptability, participant burden, wearable compliance, EMA completion, and data completeness. Descriptive statistics and CIs will summarize feasibility outcomes. Exploratory multilevel mixed-effects models will examine within-person and between-person associations, while time-lagged and cross-lagged analyses will explore temporal relationships and behavioral synchrony within dyads.

RESULTS: The study received approval from The Pennsylvania State University Institutional Review Board (STUDY00027664). Recruitment is ongoing, with 7 mother-child dyads enrolled as of October 2026. Data collection is anticipated to conclude by June 1, 2027. Analyses will follow completion of data collection.

CONCLUSIONS: Lion Tracks represents Phase 1 of a larger research program designed to progressively optimize ambulatory monitoring and subsequently incorporate mobile electroencephalography to examine neural correlates of daily behaviors, cognition, and emotional functioning. Findings will inform protocol refinement and assess the feasibility of a scalable, multimodal platform for future family-centered behavioral health research.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): DERR1-10.2196/107879.

articles.title: Comprehensive Clinical Decision-Support Framework for Obesity Prevention Using Large-Scale Health Checkup Data: Development and Evaluation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity prevention requires identifying nonobese adults at risk of developing obesity. Routine health checkups collect anthropometric, laboratory, medical history, and lifestyle information, but screening primarily describes current anthropometric status and does not directly provide individualized estimates of future risk for preventive counseling.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and evaluate a comprehensive clinical decision-support framework for obesity prevention using large-scale health checkup data.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used repeated examination data from the Kangbuk Samsung Health Study. Adults with BMI less than 25 kg/m², at least 3 health checkup visits, a 2-year obesity-free washout period, and postindex follow-up were included. Incident obesity was defined as the first follow-up BMI of 25 kg/m² or higher. The framework integrated a single-visit prediction tier (which we termed lite), a survival component for time-to-transition context, a repeated-measurement updating tier (which we termed plus), and an explainability layer. The primary lite-tier and survival analyses used training-set-only imputation. A previously exported lite-tier Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) component was externally evaluated in 328,268 National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) participants.

RESULTS: Among 231,683 initially nonobese participants, 38,094 developed incident obesity. In the aligned 5-year visit-1 test cohort, 4088 of 21,783 (18.8%) participants developed obesity. The lite-tier ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.918, an area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.693, a Brier score of 0.087, and an expected calibration error of 0.005. AUPRC was approximately 3.7 times the no-information reference. AUROCs were 0.913 for BMI-only and 0.914 for BMI+age+sex. Observed 5-year incidence ranged from 0.1% (6/4357) to 64.7% (2821/4357) across accelerated failure time (AFT) risk quintiles. The plus tier achieved a landmark-row AUROC of 0.899 with less favorable calibration. The previously exported lite-tier XGBoost component achieved an external AUROC of 0.857, AUPRC of 0.575, and Brier score of 0.132.

CONCLUSIONS: Large-scale health checkup data supported an integrated framework for single-visit triage, temporal risk context, risk-domain explanation, and exploratory repeated-measurement updating, providing a basis for prevention-oriented risk communication and follow-up prioritization. The overall gain in discrimination beyond BMI was modest, and the effects on clinical decisions and obesity prevention require prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Feasibility and Adherence of a Multicomponent Digital Health Monitoring Platform in Ambulatory Heart Failure: Multicenter Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital health platforms combining wearable biosensors with smartphone apps offer scalable approaches to heart failure (HF) management, yet sustained patient engagement and initial technology adoption, particularly among older adults, remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: We conducted a prospective, multicenter observational study to explore the feasibility and adherence of using a digital health monitoring platform for 8 weeks in a population of ambulatory patients with HF.

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter observational study, patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) class I to III HF were prescreened across 6 institutions in the United States and Singapore. Participants wore an Everion multisensor armband and an Apple Watch continuously and completed daily electrocardiograms (ECGs), daily symptom questionnaires, weekly voice recordings, and biweekly KCCQ-12 (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-12) assessments. Prespecified end points included recruitment yield, device wear-time, task-specific compliance, dropout rate, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Of 3386 prescreened individuals, 520 (15.4%) were clinically eligible; 66 consented (1.9% of prescreened; 12.7% of eligible), with technology-related concerns driving most declinations. Among 65 enrolled patients (mean age 56.5, SD 12.3 years; n=53, 81.5% male), 52 (80%) completed 8 weeks. Mean daily wear-time was 11.7 (SD 5.7) hours, significantly exceeding the 8-hour benchmark (P<.001). Task completion rates were 76.6% (2788/3640, daily ECG), 68.5% (2493/3640, daily symptoms), 86.5% (450/520, weekly voice), and 88.1% (229/260, biweekly KCCQ-12). Adherence did not differ significantly by age group (P=.81). No serious device-related adverse events occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: Enrolled patients with HF, including older adults, sustained robust engagement with a multicomponent digital platform over 8 weeks. However, technology-related concerns prevented most eligible patients from enrolling, identifying adoption, not adherence, as the primary barrier to scalable remote monitoring.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04191356; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04191356.

articles.title: Aligning Health Informatics Workforce Roles With Saudi Arabia's Health Sector Transformation Program: Multiphase Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Successful digital health initiatives require a sustainable health informatics (HI) workforce. The lack of standardized job roles across health sectors may result in fragmented HI workforce planning.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop a framework to guide HI workforce planning in Saudi Arabia aligned with two strategic branches of the Health Sector Transformation Program (HSTP): (1) governance and regulation and (2) data and digitalization.

METHODS: A 4-phase qualitative exploratory study was conducted. In phase 1, semistructured interviews were conducted with Saudi HI experts identified through purposive sampling based on preset inclusion criteria: (1) a master's degree or higher in HI or a related field; (2) at least 10 years of experience; and (3) a current leadership, planning, or management role in digital health. Of the experts approached, 17 agreed to participate. Saturation was confirmed retrospectively. Content analysis was used to identify HI job roles necessary to achieve the HSTP. Phase 2 involved 3 researchers mapping the identified job roles to the relevant HSTP branch and to the 4 strategic objectives under data and digitalization. In phase 3, a health-related sector guide was developed based on reviewing nationally published documents. In phase 4, HI job roles were mapped to 3 job levels and to the health sectors. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize participant demographics and the distribution of job roles across job levels, HSTP branches and objectives, and health sectors.

RESULTS: The sample had a nearly balanced gender distribution; 88.2% (15/17) held a master's degree and most (6/17, 35.3%) had 10 to 15 years of experience. Interviews identified 62 HI job roles relevant to the HSTP, of which 21 (33.9%) were mapped to the strategic objective of unified electronic health records for all under the branch of data and digitalization and 19 (30.6%) were mapped to the health sector governance and regulation branch. A health-related sector guide identified 6 potential employment sectors: health care provider organizations, health care authorities and agencies, health IT companies, research institutions, academic institutions, and health insurance. Job roles were further mapped to job levels and sectors: middle-level roles were most common (24/62, 38.7%), followed by entry-level (21/62, 33.9%) and top-level (17/62, 27.4%) roles. Health care provider organizations (55/62, 88.7%) and health care authorities and agencies (49/62, 79%) accounted for the largest share of sectors. The most frequently identified roles were health business analyst, chief information officer, HI specialist, data analyst, HI manager, and health care data scientist.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings identified job paths for HI professionals as identified by experts. These results may guide workforce planning and curriculum development. By clarifying roles and optimizing workforce placement, these findings help identify unique and overlapping positions between HI and other health specialists to ensure efficient use of human capital.

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance of Radiomics-Based Machine Learning in Differentiating Glioblastoma From Brain Metastasis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) are the most common malignant intracranial tumors in adults. Noninvasive differentiation between them remains challenging, as they frequently share similar imaging features. Although radiomics-based machine learning (ML) models show promise, systematic evidence of their performance remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically estimate the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models in differentiating GBM from BM and to explore multiclass classification involving primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL), thereby assessing their potential for clinical use.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 22, 2026, for studies reporting the diagnostic performance of radiomics-based ML models for differentiating GBM from BM. Multiclass studies involving PCNSL were also retained. Methodological quality was appraised via the Radiomics Quality Score 2.0. Binary diagnostic accuracy was pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, stratified by internal and independent external validation. Multiclass sensitivities and specificities were pooled using separate joint generalized linear mixed models. Physician assessments were evaluated as an exploratory benchmark.

RESULTS: A total of 39 studies (31 binary and 8 multiclass), involving 11,558 patients, were included. For binary classification, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 88.9% (95% CI 84.1%-92.4%) and 83.0% (95% CI 76.8%-87.9%) in internal validation, and 83.8% (95% CI 77.4%-88.7%) and 80.7% (95% CI 71.1%-87.7%) in external validation, respectively. In multiclass analyses, pooled sensitivity was 84.4% (95% CI 72.4%-91.8%) for GBM, 70.6% (95% CI 54.4%-82.8%) for BM, and 75.0% (95% CI 62.7%-84.3%) for PCNSL, with corresponding specificities of 82.5% (95% CI 70.1%-90.4%), 88.8% (95% CI 81.9%-93.3%), and 94.4% (95% CI 88.4%-97.4%), respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Radiomics-based ML models could distinguish between GBM and BM in the included cohorts. However, due to methodological limitations and scarce evidence, their generalizability and clinical utility remain unclear. Further multicenter prospective studies should conduct independent external validation in consecutive patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261295269; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295269.

articles.title: Estimated Effects of Behavior Change Components in mHealth Interventions for Physical Activity and Related Psychological Outcomes: Bayesian Component Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health (mHealth) interventions for physical activity commonly combine several behavior change and digital design components, making it difficult to determine which components contribute to outcomes. Component estimates also depend on how repeated contrasts within trials and departures from additivity are handled.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to estimate component-level contributions of 7 operationalized intervention components and examine whether their contributions differed between physical activity and related psychological outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian component network meta-analysis of 130 randomized controlled trials involving 25,369 participants after a final study-design eligibility reaudit. Component composition was coded for 310 study arms. The primary target-scope dataset contained 469 component-informative contrast-level observations from 121 trials; a broader 492-observation dataset was analyzed as a sensitivity. A Bayesian additive component metaregression used a multivariate normal likelihood by study, a shared-comparator covariance for multiarm outcome sets, a study-level random effect, and within-study residual heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses varied working cross-outcome and cross-time correlations, restricted each study to a primary outcome group, excluded cluster-coded trials, compared outcome domains, and explored component interactions.

RESULTS: In the primary hierarchical model, self-monitoring (Hedges g=0.153, 95% credible interval [CrI] 0.053-0.249) and gamification (g=0.102, 95% CrI 0.020-0.183) had CrIs above 0. Feedback retained a positive point estimate (g=0.127), but its 95% CrI included 0 (-0.004 to 0.259) after the final eligibility reaudit; intervals for the other 4 components also included 0. Across the 7 outcome-domain contrasts, social comparison was lower for psychological than physical activity outcomes (psychological-minus-physical activity difference g=-0.189, 95% CrI -0.325 to -0.052), including in the 66-trial same-study analysis (g=-0.201, 95% CrI -0.386 to -0.021), although social comparison was sparsely represented. For feedback, the corresponding differences were 0.084 (95% CrI -0.088 to 0.254) and 0.046 (95% CrI -0.163 to 0.254), respectively. The low-risk subset was rank deficient and did not support stable estimation of all 7 components.

CONCLUSIONS: Self-monitoring and gamification had the clearest evidence of positive component contributions. Feedback retained a positive point estimate, but its CrI included 0 in the eligibility-locked analysis, and the data did not support a robust divergence in feedback by outcome domain. The isolated social comparison domain contrast arose from sparse evidence and should be considered hypothesis generating. Component rankings should be interpreted alongside small absolute effects, uncertainty, the pragmatic additivity assumption, uncorrected cluster designs in the source summaries, and limited low-risk evidence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251182885; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251182885.

articles.title: A mHealth-Based Vestibular Rehabilitation Program for Postoperative Vestibular Dysfunction in Patients With Vestibular Schwannoma: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with vestibular schwannoma often experience postoperative vestibular dysfunction, including vertigo, dizziness, and imbalance, which severely impair daily functioning and quality of life. Effective and accessible rehabilitation strategies are needed to improve recovery after surgery.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health-based vestibular rehabilitation program in improving postoperative vestibular outcomes after unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery.

METHODS: A prospective randomized controlled trial comparing a customized mobile app-based vestibular rehabilitation program with standard face-to-face vestibular rehabilitation was conducted at the Otology Center, Eye & ENT Hospital, Fudan University, from October 2023 to May 2025. A total of 60 patients undergoing unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery were enrolled and randomly assigned to either an intervention group (n=30) or a control group (n=30). Both groups received a 90-day vestibular rehabilitation program. The intervention group received guidance, symptom recording, and adherence monitoring through a customized mobile app, whereas the control group received face-to-face guidance. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the change in Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) score from baseline (preoperative) to postoperative day 90. Secondary outcomes included visual analog scale scores for vestibular symptoms and the incidence of vertigo, dizziness, vestibulo-visual symptoms, and postural symptoms.

RESULTS: Of the 60 randomized participants, 52 (86.7%) had DHI scores available at postoperative day 90, and 49 (81.7%) had paired baseline and day-90 DHI scores available to calculate the primary outcome. The adjusted between-group difference in DHI change from baseline to postoperative day 90 was not significant (adjusted mean difference -0.83, 95% CI -8.79 to 7.13; P=.84). No significant differences were observed in visual analog scale scores at postoperative days 7, 30, or 90 (all P>.05). Among the assessed vestibular symptoms, postural symptoms on postoperative day 7 were reported by 53.3% (16/30) of the intervention group and 83.3% (25/30) of the control group; the difference was not significant after Holm adjustment (unadjusted P=.03; Holm-adjusted P=.30).

CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, mobile health-based rehabilitation did not demonstrate greater improvement in postoperative vestibular outcomes than face-to-face rehabilitation following unilateral vestibular schwannoma surgery. The lower proportion of patients reporting postural symptoms on postoperative day 7 remains an exploratory finding requiring confirmation in future studies.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2200056123; https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=150939.

articles.title: GESS-AEEM consensus on testosterone therapy in women: a clinical implementation framework.
authors: GESS-AEEM Expert Panel on Systemic Testosterone Therapy in Women
articles.journal: Climacteric : the journal of the International Menopause Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aims to provide a Spanish clinical implementation consensus on systemic testosterone therapy in women, translating international evidence and guidance into an operational framework for Spain and comparable European settings.

METHODS: A multidisciplinary panel of 13 experts reviewed evidence identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 to April 2026. Sources were characterized by study design, directness, applicability and key limitations. Draft statements were refined through a two-round modified Delphi process, with agreement predefined as ≥80%. A revised special-populations statement underwent focused post-review confirmatory voting. No formal Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) assessment was performed.

RESULTS: Physiological-dose transdermal testosterone may be considered for postmenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder after comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment. Serum testosterone should not be used diagnostically but supports safe prescribing and detection of supraphysiological exposure. The consensus addresses off-label prescribing, assay continuity, monitoring, discontinuation, safety communication and special populations. Non-transdermal formulations, supraphysiological dosing and use for non-sexual indications are not supported.

CONCLUSIONS: This article does not propose a new therapeutic indication or supersede existing guidance. The article provides a contextualized implementation framework to support consistent and safe clinical practice.

articles.title: Advanced Hybrid Closed-Loop Insulin Delivery System in Asian Patients With Type 1 Diabetes: Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract:
