BACKGROUND: The MiniMed 780G insulin delivery system has demonstrated improved hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), time in range, and quality of life (QoL) in clinical trials, but real-world studies are lacking in Southeast Asia.

OBJECTIVE: Our study aimed to explore the preliminary efficacy and safety of the Medtronic MiniMed 780G advanced hybrid closed-loop system, as well as the impact on QoL, in Southeast Asian adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) who were previously on either multiple daily injections or conventional pump therapy over 24 weeks.

METHODS: A prospective, single-center pilot study was conducted in patients with T1D on multiple daily injections or conventional pump therapy. Primary end points included the change in HbA1c at 12 and 24 weeks. Secondary end points included continuous glucose monitoring glycemic metrics, change in total daily insulin dose, QoL scores, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Nine patients (n=5 male) with a mean age of 35 (SD 10.9) years completed the study. Mean HbA1c improved from 7.3% (SD 0.9%; mean 56.3, SD 9.8 mmol/mol) to 6.9% (SD 0.6%; mean 51.2, SD 6.4 mmol/mol) at 12 weeks and 7.0% (SD 0.6%; mean 53.0, SD 6.1 mmol/mol) at 24 weeks, respectively. All patients achieved the target time in the target range of over 70%, time above the target range of less than 25%, and time below the target range of less than 4% at 12 and 24 weeks. Reduction in total daily dose of insulin was observed for all patients at 24 weeks.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study demonstrated the usability, safety, and possible improvement in glycemic outcomes with the MiniMed 780G system in Asian adults with T1D, independent of their baseline insulin therapies.

articles.title: Examining the Effectiveness of a Dual Executive Function Training Package: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Executive function (EF) refers to the cognitive processes that enable goal-directed regulation of thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. Two interrelated domains are commonly distinguished: "cool" EF, which involves abstract cognitive processes, and "hot" EF, which involves regulation in emotionally or motivationally charged contexts. Children with special educational needs (SEN) frequently show difficulties across both domains, yet most interventions target one in isolation.

OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a dual EF training package for 3 of the most prevalent SEN groups: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), specific learning difficulties (SpLD), and autism spectrum disorder (ASD).

METHODS: A total of 288 primary school students aged 6 to 12 years with a diagnosis of ADHD, ASD, or SpLD will be recruited. Participants will be randomly assigned to either an intervention or a waitlist control group, stratified by diagnosis. Each intervention group (n=48) will receive the dual EF training program. Participants in the waitlist control group will continue to receive usual educational and clinical support (standard care) during the study period and will be offered the dual EF program upon completion of the study. Preintervention and postintervention assessments will include neuropsychological tests of EF, teacher- and parent-reported behavioral ratings, and measures of disability impact, school satisfaction, and social participation. Changes in outcome measures will be examined using a mixed-design analysis, with diagnosis (ADHD, ASD, and SpLD) and group (experimental vs waitlist control) as between-participant factors and time (pretest vs posttest) as the within-participant factor. Baseline scores will be included as covariates where appropriate. The analysis will assess overall intervention effects and whether changes over time differ by intervention condition and diagnosis, with significant interactions followed by appropriate post hoc comparisons.

RESULTS: The study was funded by Advance Children Medical and Education Foundation Limited from September 2025 to December 2026 and received ethical approval. Recruitment commenced in early 2026, and 30 participants with ADHD, 30 with ASD, and 45 with SpLD had been enrolled by June 2026. Baseline assessments were completed for all participants. Further data collection and data analysis are scheduled for completion by early 2027, with the results to be submitted for publication thereafter.

CONCLUSIONS: This study will evaluate the effectiveness of a theme-based dual EF program that integrates hot and cool EF within a structured curriculum. Findings will provide evidence of the potential of this approach to support EF and related outcomes in children with SEN and may inform future research and inclusive educational practices.

articles.title: State of the Art Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract: Off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCAB) has evolved into a mature and reproducible strategy for myocardial revascularization. Although conventional on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (ONCAB) became the standard approach with the advent of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), advances in cardiac stabilization, positioning, intracoronary shunting, and anesthetic management have enabled complete multivessel revascularization on the beating heart without CPB. Clinical studies have shown that OPCAB achieves outcomes comparable to ONCAB in appropriately selected patients while reducing perioperative complications, particularly in high-risk populations. Advances in surgical expertise, institutional infrastructure, and techniques including minimally invasive and hybrid approaches continue to expand the role of OPCAB. This review highlights the evolution, evidence, indications, and future perspectives of OPCAB as an important complementary strategy in modern cardiac surgery.

articles.title: State of The Art of The da Silva's Cone Operation for Treatment of Ebstein's Anomaly.
articles.abstract: Ebstein's anomaly (EA) is a complex congenital heart disease caused by embryological failure of the tricuspid valve (TV) leaflet delamination, leading to displacement of the leaflets and right ventricular myopathy. In 1958, Hunter and Lillehei began developing surgical techniques for the repair of EA. Their technique was followed by many others. However, those techniques presented significant limitations due to the wide range of anatomical variations in the disease. The Da Silva Cone repair (CR) for EA emerged as the most anatomical repair technique for all forms of the disease, yielding the best results for most patients. Since CR can be performed with low mortality and morbidity, is effective and durable, and rarely requires TV replacement, it has been widely adopted. It allowed that surgical intervention can be indicated before the development of significant right ventricular dilatation or dysfunction. CR can be applied to any age, but it carries more risk in the neonate with critical EA. Therefore, neonates with critical EA may benefit from a staged approach, performing the Starnes procedure in the neonatal period and the CR later. The 2025 American Association for Thoracic Surgery expert consensus on managing EA covered preoperative evaluation, surgical indications, and contraindications in neonates, children, and adults. Additionally, the expert consensus discussed the approach to cardiac arrhythmias associated with EA and alternative procedures for select cases, including TV replacement and a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt, depending on patient characteristics. They also agreed that the CR repair of the TV is beneficial when surgery is indicated.

articles.title: Short-Term Outcomes Following Surgery for Brachial Plexus Disorders and Related Nerve Procedures: Impact of Diabetes in a National Cohort of 4,040 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brachial plexus disorders can be debilitating, yet national patterns in patient demographics, procedural complexity, and outcomes remain poorly defined. Diabetes mellitus, which is known to impair wound healing, may further worsen perioperative outcomes, but its impact across large cohorts undergoing brachial plexus surgery is still unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) from 2008 to 2024 identifying adult patients undergoing surgery for brachial plexus disorders (a heterogeneous, decompression-predominant population) using ICD and CPT codes. Demographics, comorbidities, operative details, and 30-day outcomes were characterized and compared across diabetic and nondiabetic patients. Multivariable logistic regression with Firth's penalized likelihood was performed to identify independent predictors of surgical complications (primary outcome) and of medical complications, reoperation, and readmission (secondary outcomes).

RESULTS: Among 4040 patients, the median age was 36 years (IQR 26 to 47), 55.0% were female, and most procedures were elective (96.5%). Nerve decompression was the most common procedure (85.3%), whereas complex reconstruction was infrequent (nerve transfers 4.8%, nerve grafting 4.0%), consistent with a broader, less trauma-predominant population than traditional reconstructive series. Diabetes was present in 174 patients (4.3%) and was associated with older age (median 51 vs. 35 y), higher body mass index, obesity (61.5% vs. 29.2%), hypertension (59.8% vs. 12.8%), renal failure (8.6% vs. 0.5%), and ASA class III status (59.8% vs. 18.4%). Operative time (median 143 min) and length of stay (median 2 d) did not differ by diabetes status. Diabetic patients had higher unadjusted rates of reoperation (7.5% vs. 2.7%, P<0.001), readmission (7.4% vs. 3.3%, P=0.01), surgical complications (5.2% vs. 1.4%, P<0.001), and medical complications (5.2% vs. 1.7%, P=0.003). After multivariable adjustment, diabetes remained independently associated with surgical complications (aOR 3.38, 95% CI: 1.44-7.27, P=0.007) and reoperation (aOR 2.64, 95% CI: 1.30-5.02, P=0.009), but not with medical complications or readmission.

CONCLUSIONS: Short-term complications after brachial plexus surgery are uncommon but influenced by comorbidity burden. Diabetes was independently associated with higher odds of surgical complications and reoperation. Diabetes and the broader comorbidity burden should be weighed in perioperative risk assessment and counseling for patients undergoing brachial plexus surgery.

articles.title: Knowledge, Practices, and Training Needs Related to Radiation Protection among Critical Care Staff Exposed to Portable Radiography: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portable radiography is frequently performed in critical care settings, where healthcare workers may be exposed to scattered ionizing radiation. Adequate knowledge and appropriate protective practices are important components of occupational radiation protection.

OBJECTIVE: To assess radiation protection knowledge, practices, and training needs among nurses and physicians working in critical care units during portable radiography in hospitals in Bethlehem and East Jerusalem, Palestine.

METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among nurses and physicians working in intensive care units, cardiac care units, and neonatal intensive care units in nine hospitals between November 2022 and March 2023. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, objective radiation protection knowledge, reported radiation protection practices during portable radiography, personal protective equipment use, training history and needs, and self-rated knowledge.

RESULTS: A total of 142 critical care staff participated, including 104 nurses and 38 physicians. The mean objective radiation protection knowledge score was 8.30 ± 2.83 out of 14 (59.3%). Although 85.3% of participants rated their radiation protection knowledge as good or very good, objective assessment indicated that 68.3% had poor or fair knowledge. Regarding reported practice behaviors during portable radiography, leaving the unit during image acquisition was the most common response (37.3%), followed by maintaining maximum distance within the unit (23.2%), relocating to a break room (19.0%), remaining at the nursing station (12.0%), and standing behind shielding (8.5%). Use of personal protective equipment was limited, with 48.6% reporting that they never used lead aprons, 62.7% never using thyroid shields, 68.3% never using lead gloves, and 73.9% never using protective eyewear. Most participants (72.5%) had never attended formal radiation protection training, and 85.2% reported a need for additional education.

CONCLUSION: Critical care staff demonstrated a discrepancy between perceived and objectively assessed radiation protection knowledge and reported inconsistent use of protective measures during portable radiography. The findings support structured and continuing radiation protection education and institutional measures to reinforce appropriate occupational protection practices.

articles.title: Wharton's jelly insufficiency and its implications for perinatal outcomes and regenerative medicine: A review.
articles.abstract: Wharton's jelly (WJ) is the hydrated extracellular matrix (ECM) of the umbilical cord, providing mechanical protection for the umbilical vessels and a niche for WJ-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (WJ-MSCs). This narrative review examines WJ insufficiency in relation to perinatal vascular risk and the functional quality of cells harvested for regenerative medicine. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched through October 2026 for studies of WJ structure, cord pathology, prenatal assessment, and WJ-MSC function. A lean cord, defined by a cross-sectional area below the 10th percentile for gestational age, was reported in 73.8% of fetuses with fetal growth restriction (FGR) in one cited cohort. The reported clinical spectrum includes reduced umbilical vein blood flow, thrombosis, and intrauterine fetal death (IUFD). Nine case reports and case series published between 1978 and 2021 describe structural cord abnormalities associated with WJ deficiency. Broader clinical findings are organized into a proposed five-tier severity continuum that has not been prospectively validated. WJ-MSCs from pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) or maternal obesity show functional alterations that are not captured by cell yield alone. Whether reduced WJ content or a lean cord independently lowers MSC potency remains untested. For preeclampsia and intrauterine infection, the proposed effects on WJ-MSC quality are inferred from adjacent evidence rather than demonstrated directly. Sonographic WJ-area assessment, Doppler monitoring, molecular biomarkers, and potency-based donor stratification are proposed research approaches. Prospective studies linking antenatal WJ measurements to perinatal outcomes and post-isolation MSC function are needed before the severity framework or proposed surveillance and cord-banking strategies can be adopted clinically.

articles.title: Prediction of eGFR and uACR Using Evolutionary Learning for Identifying High-Risk Individuals in Renal Disease Prevention.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Many individuals at high risk for renal disease remain undetected in clinical practice due to insufficient testing of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR). This study aims to develop models to predict reduced eGFR and elevated uACR, thereby facilitating early identification of individuals at risk.

METHODS: From 72,346 analyzed samples, we derived a dataset containing 15 features (U15). We developed three evolutionary learning-based models: PeGFR, PuACR1, and PuACR2, to predict eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, uACR ≥ 30 mg/g, and uACR > 300 mg/g, respectively. These models were built using an intelligent bi-objective combinatorial genetic algorithm (IBCGA) and SVM parameter settings optimized simultaneously. External dataset without eGFR and uACR measurements to evaluate clinical applicability.

RESULTS: In the U15 training and test datasets for uACR prediction, gender, pH, and bilirubin were not statistically significant; whereas all features were significant in eGFR prediction (p < 0.05). The areas under the curve (AUC) for PeGFR, PuACR1, and PuACR2 were 0.846, 0.827, and 0.949, respectively. In the external test, 589 individuals (11.36%) were identified as high- or very-high-risk, defined as having eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and uACR ≥ 30 mg/g.

CONCLUSIONS: The evolutionary learning framework proposed accurately predicts renal risk using clinical data as an early screening tool. It also demonstrates scalability in assisting healthcare providers in determining whether further renal-related examinations are warranted, thereby facilitating the identification of high-risk individuals for secondary prevention. An online tool has also been developed for clinical and research use: https://nycuiclab.ngrok.io.

articles.title: Myosteatosis Is Associated With Reduced Intratumoral CD45+ Leukocyte Density in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: An Exploratory Computed Tomography-Based Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In hepatocellular cancer (HCC), reduced muscle mass and quality are associated with worse overall survival, higher risk of tumor recurrence, and lower objective response rate. However, the underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. This exploratory, retrospective single-center study aimed to describe associations between CT-derived body composition and intratumoral CD45+ leukocyte density (CD45, the leukocyte common antigen) in patients with HCC.

METHODS: The sample comprised 53 treatment-naive patients. Body composition was measured semiautomatically with ImageJ on a single axial slice at the third lumbar vertebra from staging computed tomography (CT). The total tumor cell count and the mean number of intratumoral CD45-positive leukocytes were estimated in biopsy specimens. The proportion of CD45+ leukocytes (CD45+ leukocytes divided by the total cell count, expressed as a percentage) was calculated. Data were summarized with descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: Low skeletal muscle mass was diagnosed in 32 patients (60%), high visceral adipose tissue in 26 patients (49%), myosteatosis in 18 patients (34%), and high subcutaneous adipose tissue in 26 patients (49%). The median proportion of intratumoral CD45+ leukocytes was 2.7% (IQR 1.4-8.4). Patients with myosteatosis had a lower proportion of CD45+ leukocytes than those with normal muscle density (median 1.9% [IQR 0.5-4.5] vs 3.9% [2.1-10.0], p=0.026). Other parameters of body composition showed no associations with CD45+ leukocytes.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, myosteatosis was associated with lower intratumoral CD45+ leukocyte density in HCC. Because CD45 is nonspecific and the sample was small and unadjusted, this hypothesis-generating finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.

articles.title: Experiences of Families Receiving Regular Remote Review of CGM to Provide Targeted Supports: A mixed methods study evaluating a pilot model of care in children with Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To evaluate the experience of families of children (aged 7-14) with type 1 diabetes participating in a model of diabetes care that utilises regular remote review of CGM to prioritise contact and provide personalised and targeted support. This study focused on exploring the acceptability and impact of this model of care on participants and their families.

METHODS: This mixed-methods study used semi-structured interviews and a combined multiple-choice and free-text survey, completed by parents of children participating in a trial model of diabetes care. Qualitative data was analysed via reflexive content analysis to establish categories describing the experience and acceptability of the model of care. Quantitative data reflecting acceptability of the model of care were reported using frequency of response.

RESULTS: A sample of 15 surveys and 9 interviews were completed from 59 eligible participants who completed the model of care. The primary outcome, family experience of receiving contact, was most frequently referenced with 83% reporting positive personal impacts such as reassurance, support and validation, 46% reporting improved wellbeing and 70% reporting impacts on diabetes self-knowledge and management changes. Secondarily, the model was largely seen to be acceptable with 83% reporting convenient, positive and flexible communication and with potential to add-value to and reduce the requirement of traditional outpatient clinical care. Further, most participants reported a desire to continue the model of care. Participants also described potential revisions to improve the model and target specific populations who may benefit.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggested acceptability and subjective benefit of regular review of CGM by the clinical team with targeted remote intervention in a group of children with T1D. It highlights the value that families place on support and communication, independent of glycaemic benefits. This insight may be used to guide clinical contacts and future trials.

articles.title: Serum microRNA Landscape in Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Hypothesis-Generating Reference Dataset.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is an eosinophilic vasculitis arising against a background of adult-onset asthma. We investigated circulating microRNA (miRNA) profiles in EGPA and integrated them with previously reported serum protein data.

METHODS: In this retrospective, cross-sectional study, archived sera from 14 patients with active, glucocorticoid-naïve EGPA and 20 with severe eosinophilic asthma without EGPA were profiled on a 2,588-miRNA microarray. Differential expression among 1,777 quantifiable miRNAs was assessed with limma, adjusting for sex and RNA integrity number; significance required both a Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate below 0.05 and a Bonferroni-corrected p below 0.05. TargetScan-predicted target genes were intersected with 29 serum proteins previously shown to differ between the same groups. Two further paired analyses, each performed in a separate group of patients with EGPA, compared active disease with the glucocorticoid-treated phase (n = 11) and samples before versus after mepolizumab (n = 13).

RESULTS: Eight miRNAs met both criteria: hsa-miR-3126-5p, hsa-miR-921, hsa-miR-6836-5p and hsa-miR-668-5p were lower in EGPA, and hsa-miR-6857-3p, hsa-miR-1260a, hsa-miR-603 and hsa-miR-12125 were higher (within-cohort areas under the curve, 0.82-0.94). Fourteen of the 29 proteins were encoded by predicted target genes. Only hsa-miR-3678-3p changed after glucocorticoid treatment; no miRNA changed after mepolizumab, and none of the eight EGPA-associated miRNAs changed with either treatment.

CONCLUSION: This exploratory study identifies circulating miRNA differences between EGPA and severe eosinophilic asthma, and the complete result table is provided as a reference resource. Independent validation is required to establish their biological and clinical significance.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000040163.

articles.title: Screening for Cardiac Amyloidosis in Men with Angina and Non-Obstructive Coronary Finding: The CHEST-CA study.
articles.abstract: Background Cardiac amyloidosis (CA) may cause microvascular dysfunction leading to chest pain, even in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD). Whether angina in older men may represent an early clinical manifestation of previously undiagnosed CA remains unknown Methods In this prospective multicenter study, 150 men aged ≥65 years presenting with chest pain were recruited from three outpatient cardiology clinics in the Capital Region of Denmark. All par-ticipants had non-obstructive findings on coronary imaging by either cardiac computed to-mography angiography or myocardial perfusion imaging. A systematic screening protocol in-cluded clinical evaluation, electrocardiography, echocardiography, blood and urine tests for monoclonal proteins, and cardiac scintigraphy. ATTR-CA was defined by Perugini grade ≥2 myocardial uptake in the absence of monoclonal gammopathy. Results The median age was 72.6 years (IQR: 68.8-77.4). Most patients underwent perfusion imaging (63.0%) prior to inclusion. Median high-sensitive troponin T was 12.0 ng/L (IQR, 9.0-18.0), and median NT-proBNP was 173.9 ng/L (IQR 81.9-459.9). Heart failure was present in 24.0% and atrial fibrillation or flutter in 39.7% of patients. In total, two patients (1.3%; 95% CI 0.2- 4.%) were diagnosed with wild-type transthyretin CA with grade 3 cardiac uptake. One patient had manifest cardiomyopathy, and the second CA patient had normal cardiac biomarkers and echocardiography and was surveilled. Conclusions Among elderly men with suspected cardiac angina and non-obstructive coronary findings, the prevalence of undiagnosed ATTR-CA was low (1.3%). Additional enrichment criteria may be necessary to improve diagnostic yield, but this remains hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists.
articles.abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo-electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor's ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

articles.title: Acute kidney injury and death in severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria: An individual patient data meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Serum or plasma concentrations of creatinine and urea are the usual laboratory parameters measured to assess acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients with suspected severe malaria. Creatinine is preferred for estimation of the glomerular filtration rate, but the current threshold for defining severe malaria (>265 μmol/L or a urea >20 mmol/L) is based on adult values and does not reflect the large difference between children and adults in normal values resulting from differences in muscle mass. We reevaluated these thresholds and their prognostic significance in severe malaria using individual patient data from large prospective studies.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We pooled individual patient data from 22,663 patients recruited into 14 studies of severe malaria of whom 16,441 were included in the primary analysis population. Patients were included in the primary analysis population if their age (if missing, imputed from weight or height), coma status on admission, and either an admission serum or plasma creatinine or urea measurement (blood urea nitrogen, BUN), were all recorded. The primary outcome was mortality by day 28. The secondary outcome was the admission plasma Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2) concentration (a measure of parasite biomass). Bayesian penalised spline regression models were used to characterise the age-specific relationships (interaction with age) between the outcome and the absolute creatinine, the creatinine fold change relative to the age/weight predicted baseline, and the absolute urea. The models adjusted for coma status and calendar year, with nested random additive effects by study site and study. We estimated threshold plasma or serum creatinine and urea concentrations associated with >5% mortality with probability > 0.9. The majority (84%; 13,793/16,441) were children under 15 years of age. Current thresholds for AKI were associated with mortalities greater than 5%. An admission creatinine greater than three times the age/weight predicted baseline value was associated with >5% mortality. An admission urea >10 mmol/L had approximately similar prognostic value. A urea >10 mmol/L was 3.5 times more common in adults than children. In children <15 years of age, urea was a better prognostic indicator of death than creatinine and, unlike creatinine, correlated with the plasma PfHRP2 concentration. The main limitations of this analysis are the lack of metadata documenting laboratory methods and wide heterogeneity in eligibility criteria, such as creatinine or urea admission values for inclusion.

CONCLUSIONS: Admission serum or plasma creatinine >3 times the age/weight predicted baseline value (KDIGO AKI stage 3) can be used to define severe malaria AKI. In children, urea is a better predictor of the true infection biomass and a better prognostic indicator for death. We recommend the following as defining criteria for severe malaria: either a urea (BUN) threshold of 10 mmol/L for both children and adults, or simple age-based thresholds representing approximately >3 times fold change in creatinine from predicted baseline. These updated thresholds identify between 4 and 8 times more children with severe malaria AKI who are at a high risk of death.

articles.title: Vasopressor Induced Acute Limb Ischemia and the Role of Local Vasodilators: Case Report and Review of the Literature.
articles.abstract: Vasopressor induced acute limb ischemia (VIALI) is a potentially devastating disorder that presents with initial findings of peripheral ischemia and may rapidly progress to gangrene, resulting in a 30 day amputation rate of 10 to 30%. Early recognition in patients at heightened risk is key to facilitate timely intervention before development of irreversible necrosis. This case is a 59 year-old female with septic and cardiogenic shock who developed VIALI after 4 days of exposure to vasopressors. The patient presented with dry gangrene of right index finger and right toes, attributable to administration of combination vasopressor agents which were successfully discontinued. While early interventions were hampered by the sudden onset of tissue necrosis and minimal accompanying symptoms, a review of the literature involving local vasodilators, with evidence-based treatment for nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic sources of limb ischemia, is provided. Topical nitroglycerin ointment, most often 1 to 2%, applied 3 to 4 times daily, demonstrated evidence of resolution of tissue ischemia and symptoms, tolerability, and convenience. Phentolamine and botulinum toxin also proved effective in resolving digital ischemia, but their use may be hindered by availability, administration challenges, or delayed onset. The case illustrates the sudden occurrence, often advanced presentation of VIALI, emphasizing the importance of early detection and intervention, and provides evidence for the role of local vasodilators in potentially altering disease outcomes without added systemic adverse effects.

articles.title: A single amino acid switch in PilO controls planktonic-sessile lifestyle in Helicobacter pylori.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori and related Campylobacterota assemble high torque motors with many additional proteins compared to model bacteria. Despite these structural enhancements, some wild-type H. pylori strains have been previously reported to have delayed migration in the semisolid agar motility assay. The basis for this delay was characterized by identifying genetic suppressors that allowed H. pylori G27 wild type to migrate immediately. This analysis identified loss of function mutations in four genes (pilO, fliL, hcpX, and alpA) that restored migration. Targeted loss of any one of these genes resulted in strains that both migrated immediately in semisolid agar and displayed low early biofilm formation. Epistasis analysis placed PilO at the most upstream position of these proteins, acting as a possible hub for both motility and biofilm formation. A second suppressor screen carried out in the presence of two copies of pilO identified the same loss of function mutants plus ones in pilM and pilN. Comparison of seven wild-type H. pylori strains classed their semisolid agar migration behavior as either immediate or delayed. Analysis of the predicted protein sequences of the above identified suppressor genes revealed that only PilO had an amino acid that varied in a manner correlated with semisolid agar migration behavior. Using complementation with either PilO variant confirmed this amino acid can dictate whether a strain has delayed or immediate migration. Finally, loss of pilO created strains with drastic stomach colonization defects. The results suggest that PilO acts as a regulatory hub that actively suppresses flagellar motility under specific conditions and is required for normal stomach infection.

articles.title: Deltacoronavirus modulates circRNA circC3 biogenesis to accelerate MBNL1 mRNA decay.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) with diverse biological functions are frequently dysregulated upon viral infection, yet the mechanisms governing their differential expression and functional relevance during infection remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized circRNA, circC3, that is robustly upregulated following virus infection. Host RNA binding protein muscleblind-like 1 (MBNL1) was markedly induced by deltacoronavirus (δ-CoV) infection, which recognizes YGCY motifs within intron 19 and intron 21 of the C3 gene and promotes skipping of exons 20 and 21 for C3 gene, thereby enhancing circC3 biogenesis. These findings reveal an MBNL1-dependent mechanism underlying δ-CoV induced circC3 upregulation. Functionally, circC3 attenuates the antiviral activity of MBNL1 by accelerating MBNL1 mRNA decay through a direct interaction, and finally promote δ-CoV replication. Together, our study elucidates a regulatory circuit in which viral infection remodels host circRNA biogenesis to counteract antiviral defenses, highlighting circC3 as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

articles.title: Snakebite records in routine hospital data: Deduplication, encounter consolidation, patient linkage and algorithmic episode reconstruction in 14 Public Hospitals, West Bank, Palestine, 2021-2025, with a nested chart review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Snakebite surveillance often relies on routine hospital records that were not designed to count events: they are duplicated, distributed across departments and repeated across hospitals, so the count depends on whether rows, encounters, patients or episodes are taken as the unit. We made each reconstruction step explicit.

METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We analysed all records carrying ICD-10 T63 snake-venom codes from 14 public hospitals in the West Bank, Palestine, between 14 March 2021 and 26 December 2025. The extract contained 362 rows. Removing rows identical on every field left 292; consolidating records sharing hospital, patient file number and visit date gave 265 registry encounters and 184 hospital-specific patient records. A deterministic rule fixed before the results - exact patient file number with concordant full name, recorded sex and recorded age - produced 172 linked patients through 12 cross-hospital links. A non-prespecified 14-day algorithm grouped these encounters into 178 algorithmically reconstructed episodes; counts were 183 and 177 under 7- and 30-day windows. A 13th potential link found after the analysis lock is reported only as a sensitivity analysis (171 patients); across 11 linkage specifications tested post hoc during revision, the count was 171 or 172. A nested chart review at three hospitals retrieved 35 of 37 eligible charts; 31 patients were clinically assessable on arrival. Documented systemic manifestations appeared in 12, antivenom was given to 17 and intensive care to 11; there was no in-hospital death, and four documented deaths preceded arrival.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Rows, encounters, patients and reconstructed episodes are different quantities, and the same extract yields substantially different counts at each step. Routine records can support surveillance reconstruction when every step is explicit, but these are counts of hospital-recorded care, not estimates of snakebite incidence or burden, and episode counts are algorithmic reconstructions rather than clinically validated bite counts.

articles.title: Adiposity profiles in relation to cardiometabolic disease risk in South African adults with HIV on long-term antiretroviral therapy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In high-income countries (HICs), antiretroviral-treated (ART) HIV promotes adverse fat redistribution, contributing to excess cardiometabolic risk in persons with HIV (PWH). Whether this occurs in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) remains unclear. We compared adiposity and cardiometabolic profiles between ART-experienced PWH and HIV-uninfected peers in South Africa.

METHODS: Participants from the Middle-Aged Soweto Cohort completed anthropometry, blood pressure, fasting glucose and lipids, 2-h oral glucose tolerance testing and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry for regional adiposity. Prevalent diabetes, hypertension and dyslipidemia were assessed. ART-experienced PWH were propensity-score matched 1:many to peers without HIV (PWoH) on age, lifestyle, socio-economics and body mass index (BMI) category, stratified by sex. Sex-specific HIV-related cardiometabolic and regional fat differences were evaluated using standardized mean differences (SMD) and p-values. Semi-parametric models examined associations between visceral (VAT) and subcutaneous (SAT) adipose tissue and glucose homeostasis indices.

RESULTS: Eighty male PWH (mean BMI 23.2 kg/m2) and 56 female PWH (31.1 kg/m2) were matched to 159 male PWoH and 92 female PWoH (all matching SMD <0.09). Median ART duration was 5.2 years in males and 7.0 years in females; median CD4+ counts were 413 and 620 cells/mL, respectively. ART comprised predominantly non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (~86%) and protease inhibitors (~18%). There were no significant HIV-related differences in subtotal or regional fat (arm, leg, trunk, android, gynoid, VAT or SAT) in either sex. Conversely, male PWoH had significantly higher prevalences of diabetes (9.0% vs. 3.8%; SMD = 0.22; p = 0.031) and hypertension (48.7% vs. 42.5%; SMD = 0.33; p = 0.022) compared with male PWH. No such differences were observed in females. VAT, but not SAT, was positively associated with post-load glucose in both sexes (p < 0.017), regardless of HIV status-linearly in males and non-linearly in females.

CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to HIC evidence, controlled HIV on long-term ART was not associated with differential fat accumulation or adverse cardiometabolic profiles in this South African cohort. Unexpectedly, male PWH had better cardiometabolic profiles than matched PWoH, while females had comparable profiles. Further research should examine qualitative adipose tissue differences at ectopic depots-liver, skeletal muscle and pancreas-and their associations with incident cardiometabolic disease in SSA.

articles.title: Stroke Death Rates Among Adults Aged ≥18 Years - United States, 2000-2024.
articles.journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report
articles.abstract: In 2024, stroke was the fourth leading cause of death in the United States. A 2017 report found that beginning during 2013-2015, earlier declines in stroke death rates stalled or reversed among some populations of U.S. adults aged ≥35 years. This report examines 25-year trends in stroke death rates among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years across age, sex, and geographic areas, using 2000-2024 National Vital Statistics System mortality data. During 2000-2024, the age-adjusted stroke death rate among U.S. adults aged ≥18 years declined from 81.4 per 100,000 population to 51.9 (average annual percentage change = -2.0%), with declining trends across all age groups, sexes, U.S. Census Bureau regions, and U.S. jurisdictions except Delaware. Overall rates declined during 2000-2009 (annual percentage change [APC] = -5.2%), remained stable during 2009-2018, increased during 2018-2021 (APC = 4.0%), and declined again during 2021-2024 (APC = -2.4%). However, during the most recent trend periods, rates increased among adults aged 35-44 years, those aged ≥85 years, women, residents of the Midwest and South U.S. Census Bureau regions, and in 12 U.S. jurisdictions. Despite long-term declines in stroke death rates, the recent increase in trends in some demographic groups and geographic areas underscore the importance of continued surveillance to identify adults at increased risk for stroke and implement focused prevention and management efforts.

articles.title: A Multi-Model Framework for Explainable Sepsis Mortality Prediction With Dynamic Fairness and Drift Analysis.
articles.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems can materially improve risk prediction and resource allocation in critical care, yet their sustained governance raises an underexamined problem for the health informatics community: model fairness and interpretability are typically certified once, at deployment, even though both properties evolve as models are periodically retrained within feedback-laden sociotechnical environments. This study reframes algorithmic fairness as a dynamic, lifecycle property rather than a static deployment checkpoint, and develops a multi-model framework that jointly addresses predictive performance, longitudinal fairness, and explainability. Using the MIMIC-IV cohort, the LSTM achieves an AUC of 0.884 (95% CI: 0.859-0.908) on a held-out test set, comparable to contemporary tabular baselines (LightGBM 0.892, Random Forest 0.889, XGBoost 0.886, Logistic Regression 0.867) and substantially above a SOFA-only clinical baseline (0.770). Because three development-model predictors (vasopressors, mechanical ventilation, and the full SOFA score) are not consistently recorded in eICU, cross-institutional generalization is assessed with a common-feature Random Forest, yielding AUC 0.743 (95% CI: 0.738-0.749). We conduct a longitudinal simulation on the real MIMIC-IV cohort, with simulated performative feedback, across 15 retraining cycles and 16 intersectional subgroups, simultaneously monitoring TPR, FPR, and FOR gaps. Across 30 independent runs, all three strategies converge to final TPR gaps with no significant difference (Friedman $\chi ^{2}(2)=1.195$, $p=0.550$); however, the Dynamic Adaptive Fairness controller exhibits bounded, damped trajectories where static reweighing shows larger transient spikes. Under an auxiliary exogenous covariate shift, adaptive control attenuates the post-shift TPR-gap spike ($\Delta =+0.091$) relative to the no-intervention baseline ($\Delta =+0.139$). A cross-institutional eICU fairness audit reveals measurable per-hospital variability (TPR gap 0.134, FPR gap 0.060, FOR gap 0.032); subgroup estimates are reported with event counts and Wilson intervals. SHAP feature-importance rankings remain highly stable across cycles ($\rho =0.986$), anchored by clinical severity markers. The framework supports pre-deployment fairness stress testing and longitudinal governance of clinical AI.

articles.title: Two-Stage Personalized Gait Phase Estimation in Stroke Survivors During Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking: An Offline Feasibility Study.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: This study evaluated personalized gait phase estimation for stroke survivors using functional inertial measurement unit (IMU) alignment and two-stage supervised personalization of models pre-trained on healthy gait. The estimator used a thigh-mounted IMU, and heel forcesensitive resistor measurements provided reference phase labels for offline adaptation and evaluation. Stage 1 established a distillation-regularized participant-specific model, and Stage 2 performed conditional refinement using low-rank adaptation. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), and Transformer models were evaluated in five stroke survivors walking with a powered knee exoskeleton using leave-one-subject-out hyperparameter selection and sequential test-then-adapt replay. Relative to non-adapted baselines, Stage 1+2 reduced the mean participant-wise phase root mean square error by 84.2%, 77.0%, and 60.7%, respectively. The Transformer achieved the lowest final error (2.90 ± 1.13% of the gait cycle) and heel-strike timing error (23.7 ± 4.5 ms). Ablations showed no group-mean accuracy advantage of distillation regularization over standard fine-tuning. Every-cycle updating generally minimized error, whereas conditional updating reduced update counts with small accuracy differences, demonstrating an accuracy-update-frequency trade-off. After personalization, alignment produced model-dependent changes in phase error while preserving or improving heel-strike detection and reducing heel-strike timing error for the LSTM and Transformer. In concurrent embedded tests, the TCN and Transformer maintained 100-Hz inference during Stage 2 updates without deadline misses, whereas the LSTM missed the 10-ms deadline in 6.6% of inferences. All updates completed within 0.8 s. These results support the offline feasibility and embedded timing of the two-stage framework for exoskeleton-assisted walking.

articles.title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular data and longitudinal EHR trajectories for critically ill patients requiring mechanical ventilation and venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), enabling scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in high-risk cohorts.

METHODS: InterGenEHR+ uses an optional large language model (LLM) parser for text-driven input. For single-time-point generation, we integrate variational autoencoders (VAEs) and diffusion models conditioned on observed variables. Multiple diffusion architectures support conditional longitudinal generation. The framework is evaluated on a multi-institutional VV-ECMO cohort of 874 patients using distributional fidelity metrics, imputation accuracy, adherence to clinical constraints, downstream mortality prediction tasks, and clinician evaluation.

RESULTS: Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the best performance in parsing clinician prompts while maintaining a low spurious slot rate. The experimental results demonstrate strengths across IGE variants: IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE show strong performance in single-time-point generation, whereas IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI achieve the best performance on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. In downstream evaluations across five random seeds and three classifiers, models trained on synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings further indicate that the generated trajectories are clinically plausible and consistent with the requested scenarios.

CONCLUSION: InterGenEHR+ enables clinician-specified conditional generation of clinically coherent EHR trajectories with strong statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort and could be extended to other clinical settings.

SIGNIFICANCE: This framework supports the development and evaluation of machine learning systems in data-sparse critical care settings and advances clinically grounded synthetic data generation for biomedical research.1.

articles.title: Serial vaccination establishes and refines the human CD4+ T cell memory repertoire.
articles.abstract: CD4⁺ T cells coordinate protective immunity against pathogens. However, how human CD4⁺ T cell memory is established and evolves following primary and repeated vaccinations remain incompletely understood. Using COVID-19 mRNA vaccination as a model, we tracked 50 distinct antigen-specific populations directly ex vivo with peptide-MHC class II tetramers in eight SARS-CoV-2-naïve individuals from pre-exposure baseline through memory time points after three mRNA doses. We showed that primary vaccination established the architecture of antigen-specific memory. Initial vaccination leveraged pre-existing memory while preferentially recruiting high-avidity T cells, establishing an immunodominance hierarchy dominated by a small subset of precursors. Booster vaccination refined both the magnitude and quality of T cell memory. It increased select populations and enhanced differentiation of subdominant CD4⁺ T cells. Populations that did not become more abundant after boosting retained their polyfunctional potential. Beyond establishing memory to the ancestral spike, vaccinations recruited cross-reactive T cells and increased the breadth of CD4+ T cell memory. Collectively, these findings reveal how human T cell memory evolves through sequential immunizations to generate a functionally diverse and broadly responsive memory repertoire against future viral challenges.

articles.title: Ultrasound Thermal Strain Imaging for Atherosclerosis Plaque Characterization: Image Acquisition, Processing, and In Vivo Results in a Porcine Model.
articles.abstract: The accumulation of lipids in atherosclerosis plaque (AP) is one of the key features associated with plaque rupture, which can lead to heart attack and stroke. To predict rupture-pone cases, ultrasound thermal strain imaging (US-TSI) can identify lipids based on the contrast of the echo shift gradient between water-bearing tissue and lipids induced by different speed-of-sound (SoS) changes when temperature increases. However, US-TSI faces technical challenges in vivo: 1) heating a sufficiently large tissue volume within the imaging field-of-view (FOV) safely, uniformly, and effectively; 2) thermal-induced echo shifts (< 10 μm) are often masked by physiological motions greater than 50 μm. This study aimed to overcome these obstacles. We developed a new US-TSI transducer design along with image acquisition and processing techniques. Specifically, a co-registered multi-beam approach was used to enlarge the diagnostic FOV and a wavelet-based motion analysis was conducted to reconstruct extremely small SoS change-induced echo shifts in vivo. Experiments were conducted on a tissue-mimicking phantom, a human carotid endarterectomy (CEA) sample, and in the femoral artery of a hypercholesterolemic pig. Experimental US-TSI results were compared to the histology for lipid staining. Experiments with the tissue-mimicking phantom and CEA sample demonstrated the capability of large-FOV US-TSI. Successful in vivo US-TSI lipid detection was achieved, for the first time, in a large animal AP model. This work introduces new methods to enable in vivo US-TSI for AP lipid detection, paving the way for further validation in pre-clinical large animal studies and translational human subject studies on carotid artery.

articles.title: Impact of SGLT2 Inhibitors on Renal Function in Patients with Heart Failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are an integral part of heart failure (HF) therapy. The purpose of this study was to elucidate the effect of SGLT2 inhibitors on renal function, in HF patients, over longer-term follow-up. This could be compared to existing data in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus T2DM.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in patients with HF treated with SGLT2 inhibitor (PROSPERO ID: CRD42024562311). Searches were performed across five databases from inception to 31 October 2024 identifying randomised controlled trials. Included studies were appraised using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Two primary outcomes were investigated, composite renal event and AKI (acute kidney injury). Relative risk (RR) was pooled with 95% CI using the statistical software 'R'.

RESULTS: Thirteen trials involving 90,413 participants were included. Median follow-up was 2.3 years, and data of 32,957 patients with HF was extracted. In patients with HF, SGLT2 inhibition reduced renal specific composite outcomes by 28% (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.57-0.91). Additionally, AKI was reduced in HF patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors (RR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65-0.86). Subgroup analysis showed no differences in patients with and without HF, or when stratified by baseline renal function.

CONCLUSION: These results encourage use of SGLT2 inhibitors to retard progression of kidney disease and AKI. This benefit was seen in all trials, irrespective of concurrent comorbidities. Despite the acute dip in eGFR, SGLT2 inhibitors should be continued to maximise benefit, even in patients with HF.

articles.title: Protocol to infect human airway air-liquid interface cultures with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a WHO priority pathogen causing severe airway infections. Studying P. aeruginosa infections in human airways is crucial to understand treatment efficacy, antimicrobial resistance, and infection dynamics. We present a protocol to establish and infect airway air-liquid interface (ALI) cultures with P. aeruginosa. We describe human airway epithelial and P. aeruginosa culture techniques and how to perform infections of ALI cultures. We further describe downstream assays to assess infection, including barrier integrity, bacterial burden quantification, and infection visualization. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Colque et al.1.

articles.title: Reinforced hippocampus-accumbens pathway marks a shift toward cognitive decline in aging.
articles.abstract: Aging triggers early functional alterations in brain circuits preceding cognitive impairment, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unaddressed. Spatial navigation and memory, among the earliest affected, depend on the hippocampus and downstream targets such as the nucleus accumbens (NAc), which integrates spatial and motivational information to guide goal-directed behaviors. Here we identify age-related, sex-dependent changes in the dorsal hippocampus-NAc (dHPC→NAc) pathway. Combining optogenetics with electrophysiology, chemogenetics, and behavioral analyses in mice, we show that aging shifts the excitation-inhibition balance in dorsal CA1 toward pyramidal neuron hyperactivity, strengthening hippocampal outputs. This selectively enhances synaptic drive onto D1 receptor-expressing medium spiny neurons and involves a previously unrecognized long-range parvalbumin-expressing projection. Chemogenetically reducing the dHPC→NAc activity improves memory in aged mice. In humans, fMRI reveals heightened posterior hippocampal activity and stronger posterior HPC-NAc coupling during navigation. Together, we uncover a targetable pathway acting in an intervention-sensitive window of aging to correct negative cognitive trajectories.

articles.title: Microbiome-derived phenylethylamine impairs diabetic wound healing via TAAR1-mediated NETosis.
articles.abstract: Impaired wound repair is a major complication of diabetes, yet how microbiota-derived metabolites sustain inflammation remains unclear. By integrating metabolomic and microbiome profiling of individuals with type 2 diabetes, we identify phenylethylamine as an elevated microbiota-associated metabolite. In mouse cutaneous and oral wounds, phenylethylamine promotes neutrophil extracellular trap formation and delays wound healing. Mechanistically, phenylethylamine signals through trace amine-associated receptor 1 on neutrophils, engaging β-arrestin-extracellular signal-regulated kinase-reactive oxygen species signaling. Microbiota depletion lowers circulating phenylethylamine, whereas Enterococcus faecalis recolonization increases its concentration and delays repair, supporting a microbial contribution to phenylethylamine exposure. Local delivery of a receptor antagonist in a thermosensitive hydrogel reduces neutrophil extracellular traps and improves cutaneous and oral healing in diabetic mice. These findings provide preclinical support for local TAAR1 blockade as a potential approach to improving diabetic wound repair.

articles.title: A mild SCMV isolate-based vector and an enhanced agroinfiltration-mediated viral multiplication system for efficient gene function studies in maize.
articles.abstract: Functional genomics in maize (Zea mays) and sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) is constrained by the low efficiency and high cost of stable transformation, as well as the lack of robust and user-friendly transient expression tools. Virus-based overexpression (VOX) vectors offer a promising alternative; however, currently available viral vectors for these crops are limited by complex inoculation methods and the severe symptoms often caused by the viral infection. Here, we report a newly identified, mild sugarcane mosaic virus isolate, SCmDu, and its development into an efficient, agroinoculation-based VOX vector. By co-expressing the optimized tomato chlorosis virus-encoded silencing suppressor P22 (TP22) and the pro-viral maize eukaryotic initiation factor 4A-III (ZmEIF4A3) in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves, we achieved high viral titers, enabling simple mechanical transmission to maize seedlings. The resulting pSCmDu vector supports strong, systemic protein expression for over four weeks across diverse maize inbred lines, accommodates large protein fusions, and is also functional in sorghum. Its utility was further demonstrated by triggering a hypersensitive response with a fungal effector and by identifying maize gibberellin 2-oxidases 6 (ZmGA2ox6) as a regulator of plant height. Overall, this study establishes and validates a user-friendly, efficient VOX platform for maize and sorghum, thereby paving the way for accelerated functional genomics and trait discovery in these key gramineous crops.

articles.title: A glycosyltransferase pair UGT74F1 and UGT74F2 enhances antiviral resistance independent of phytohormone and RNA silencing pathways.
articles.abstract: Glycosylation by uridine diphosphate-dependent glycosyltransferases (UGTs) regulates metabolite activity and plant immunity, but their roles in plant virus infection remain elusive. Here, we report that Arabidopsis UGT74F1 and UGT74F2, established salicylic acid (SA) glycosyltransferases, function as potent inhibitors of turnip mosaic virus (TuMV). Overexpression of either enzyme attenuates TuMV local and systemic infection, while loss of UGT74F2 enhances susceptibility. AtUGT74F1 is recruited to viral replication complexes and suppresses viral replication. Strikingly, this antiviral activity is independent of SA and jasmonic acid signaling, as the resistance is fully retained in sid2-4, coi1-23, and NahG backgrounds. Furthermore, the catalytically inactive mutant that cannot produce SA glucosides retains wild-type antiviral activity, definitively uncoupling enzymatic and immune functions. The resistance mechanism also likely operates independently of RNA silencing, as UGT74F1 suppresses TuMV equally in DCL2/4i and rdr6i plants. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized, hormone- and RNAi-independent antiviral mechanism mediated by metabolic enzymes, expanding UGT functional diversity beyond phytohormone regulation and providing genetic resources for engineering virus-resistant crops.

articles.title: Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR).

METHODS AND RESULTS: 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort.

CONCLUSION: Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

articles.title: Type I IFN-induced Usp18 impairs IFN-γ-mediated intestinal epithelial cell-intrinsic defense against Cryptosporidium.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryptosporidium is an apicomplexan parasite that infects the gastrointestinal epithelium and other mucosal surfaces in humans. This parasite is a leading cause of infectious diarrhea and diarrheal-related death in children in low- and middle-income countries and a major cause of waterborne disease worldwide. Epithelial cell-intrinsic defense is the frontline of mucosal anti-Cryptosporidium defense. Whereas type II interferon (IFN-γ) and III IFNs show a profound protective role, type I IFN signaling displays a pro-parasitic effect because mice lacking Ifnar1 are resistance to C. parvum infection.

METHODS: In this study, we evaluated the expression of the ubiquitin-specific peptidase 18 (Usp18), a representative type I IFN-stimulated gene, in intestinal epithelial cells following C. parvum infection and validated its induction on cell response to subsequent stimulation to IFN-γ, using in vitro and in vivo murine models of intestinal cryptosporidiosis.

RESULTS: Activation of type I IFN signaling in intestinal epithelial cells during C. parvum infection triggers upregulation of Usp18. Induction of Usp18 attenuates the cellular response to IFN-γ in infected host cells, resulting in suppression of IFN-γ-stimulated anti-parasitic defense. Interestingly, Usp18 appears to not directly regulate the activation of the downstream JAK/STAT signaling induced by IFN-γ. Instead, Usp18 may modulate gene transcription in cells in response to IFN-γ stimulation.

CONCLUSION: Attenuation of epithelial cell response to IFN-γ stimulation following C. parvum infection is associated an upregulation of Usp18 in C. parvum infected host cells. Induction of Usp18 may suppress the chromatin recruitment of Stat1 to these IFN-γ-stimulated gene loci in intestinal epithelial cells.

articles.title: Blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the pathway between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk: exploratory mediation analysis in middle-aged and older adult men.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The extent to which blood pressure (BP) and arterial stiffness mediate the association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk, and whether individuals with metabolic impairment are more susceptible, remain unclear.

METHODS: Within the "Risk of Cardiovascular diseases and abdominal aortic Aneurysms in Varese" (RoCAV) cohort, we retained 2119 men aged 50-75 and free of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke at baseline; carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV) was measured in a subset of 1015 using an automated oscillometer. Exposure was the 12-month mean PM2.5 concentration before baseline (EXPANSE models); outcome was incident major acute CHD or stroke (MACE), fatal or non-fatal. We estimated the mediating contribution of BP and cfPWV through Marginal Structural Models and Aalen survival models, with individual- and area-level confounders.

RESULTS: In a median follow-up of 7.6 years, 178 MACE events occurred (rate=1155 per 100,000 person-years), and 76 (1086/100,000 p-y) in the cfPWV subset. Systolic BP, mean BP, brachial pulse pressure and cfPWV were highest in the most exposed. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with 151 (95%CI:21-282) additional MACE events per 100,000 p-y, of which 48 (95%CI:17-79) were mediated by cfPWV (mediated proportion: 32%). Systolic BP and brachial pulse pressure each mediated about 16% of the PM2.5-associated risk. The cfPWV-mediated effect was enhanced in men with impaired glucose (96;95%CI:38-155) and elevated LDL-cholesterol (88;95%CI:28-147).

CONCLUSIONS: Large-artery stiffness substantially contributes to the MACE burden associated with chronic PM2.5 exposure, especially in men with metabolic impairment. Monitoring cfPWV may help incorporate environmental risk into cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Empagliflozin preserves cardiac function and modulates metabolism in a mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
articles.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a fatal genetic disorder characterized by skeletal muscle degeneration and cardiomyopathy. Effective cardiac therapies remain limited. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of the sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor empagliflozin (EMPA) in the dystrophin-deficient DBA2/J-mdx mouse model of DMD. Male mice received control chow or EMPA-containing chow (~25mg/kg/day), and cardiac function was evaluated longitudinally using four-dimensional ultrasound imaging. EMPA did not alter left ventricular mass or volume but delayed the onset of systolic dysfunction, preserving ejection fraction (EF) for 12 weeks and maintaining significantly higher EF through 24 weeks. EMPA also attenuated progressive impairments in systolic and diastolic myocardial deformation. Functional preservation was accompanied by reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and reduced expression of cardiac stress genes. EMPA increased mtDNA copy number, reduced mtDNA damage, preserved the mtDNA-encoded respiratory chain protein MT-CO1, and increased myocardial ATP content, supporting improved mitochondrial integrity and myocardial energetic capacity. In addition, EMPA induced transcriptional changes consistent with enhanced fatty acid and ketone metabolism. Systemically, EMPA improved growth trajectory, preserved relative lean mass, increased skeletal muscle torque, attenuated fiber-type remodeling, and did not adversely affect renal function. Together, these findings support SGLT2 inhibitors as a promising therapeutic strategy for DMD-associated cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Temporary Diuretic Withdrawal to Restore Responsiveness in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Patients with heart failure often experience recurrent episodes of volume overload that respond to loop diuretics. However, this leads over time to neurohormonal activation, worsened sodium avidity, and tubular remodeling that contributes to diuretic resistance. Temporary diuretic withdrawal during volume removal by ultrafiltration, direct sodium removal, or other mechanical or pharmacological means may restore diuretic response at lower doses when therapy is re-introduced. This may persist for months after cessation of therapy. Collectively, these data support temporary periods of loop diuretic withdrawal or down-titration during management of volume loss by alternative means as a promising approach to overcoming diuretic resistance with heart failure.

articles.title: A common non-coding deletion confers a trade-off between gallstone disease and steroid sulfation capacity.
ZEB1-Mediated ATPAF1 Repression Impairs ATP Synthase Assembly and Promotes Tubular Epithelial Plasticity in CKD.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial metabolic defects contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression, but whether profibrotic signaling directly disrupts adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthase assembly and promotes tubular epithelial plasticity remains unclear.

METHODS: We examined mitochondrial remodeling during transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ)-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in renal tubular epithelial cells. Findings were evaluated in mouse kidney fibrosis models and human CKD biopsies.

RESULTS: TGFβ reduced ATP synthase (complex V) activity, ATP-linked respiration, and ATP production while increasing mitochondrial membrane potential; complex I-III, II-III, and IV activities were preserved. TGFβ induced zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1)-dependent repression of ATP synthase assembly factor 1 (ATPAF1), impairing ATP synthase assembly. ATPAF1 knockdown reduced ATP synthase assembly and mitochondrial bioenergetic capacity and induced EMT-associated molecular and morphological changes. Conversely, ATPAF1 overexpression restored ATP synthase assembly, ATP production, and respiratory function and attenuated TGFβ-induced EMT-associated changes. ATP supplementation also attenuated TGFβ-induced EMT-associated marker changes. Injured tubules in fibrotic mouse kidneys exhibited reduced ATPAF1 expression and defective ATP synthase assembly, whereas liposome-mediated ATPAF1 plasmid delivery attenuated tubular injury and fibrotic remodeling. In human CKD biopsies, tubular ATPAF1 expression declined with advancing disease and was associated with mitochondrial structural abnormalities.

CONCLUSIONS: ZEB1-dependent ATPAF1 repression impaired ATP synthase assembly and mitochondrial bioenergetics during TGFβ-induced epithelial plasticity. ATPAF1 perturbation and ATP supplementation findings supported reduced ATP availability as a contributor to EMT-associated changes, rather than elevated mitochondrial membrane potential as a direct driver.

articles.title: Mechanisms for Behavior Change and Adherence to Treatment for Comorbid Depression in CKD.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) disproportionately affects people with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and is associated with non-adherence. We evaluated facilitators of and barriers to adherence to treatments for MDD among people with CKD.

METHODS: The CONCORD randomized controlled trial evaluated two treatment strategies vs. control for MDD in people with CKD G3b-5: Behavioral Activation Therapy (BAT) (plus placebo) or antidepressant bupropion (plus clinical management control) administered for 8 weeks, with escalation to a combination of BAT plus bupropion for another 8 weeks in those without MDD remission. The control arm received placebo and clinical management. BAT and clinical management were administered via video-teleconferencing. Focus groups were held virtually among study completers and one-on-one interviews among non-completers. The blinded allocation was kept concealed. An applied thematic analysis approach was used for data analysis using NVivo 15.

RESULTS: Fourteen focus groups (total N=52) and seven one-on-one interviews were conducted. The cohort was 58% women, 29% Black persons, and 31% Hispanic persons. Median (IQR) age was 59 (51, 64) years and mean (SD) estimated glomerular filtration rate was 27 (9) mL/min/1.73 m2. Adherence to study capsule by pill count was higher among focus group vs. one-on-one participants, but adherence to video-teleconferencing sessions was similar. Barriers to drug adherence included polypharmacy, large pill size, side effects attributed to study capsule, and forgetting to take medication. Facilitators of adherence included expectation of symptom improvement and desire to help others by knowledge gained. Participants reported a positive impact of participation on overall functioning and symptoms and indicated that skills learned in teletherapy were helpful. Some perceived video-teleconferencing sessions as more effective than medication, others attributed benefit to a combination of medication and video-teleconferencing, and a minority perceived medication as most effective.

CONCLUSION: Facilitators of and barriers to treatment adherence can inform the management of MDD in people with CKD.

articles.title: Circadian disruption worsens postseptic pulmonary fibrotic remodeling through a CLOCK/PIEZO1-linked myeloid immunometabolic program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether circadian rhythm disruption (CRD) promotes fibrotic remodeling after septic lung injury remains unclear. We tested whether CRD drives this process through macrophage CLOCK-PIEZO1 signaling.

METHODS: Lung specimens from patients with sepsis-associated lung injury and non-injured controls were analyzed alongside public murine lung transcriptomic datasets. Mice underwent cecal ligation and puncture or sham surgery and were maintained under stable or repeatedly shifted light-dark cycles; selected experiments included LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion. Day-3 lung injury and day-28 fibrosis were assessed, and mechanisms were defined using genetic, biochemical and co-culture approaches.

RESULTS: CRD suppressed CLOCK expression in macrophage-lineage cells, leading to increased PIEZO1 expression and aggravated collagen deposition. CLOCK repressed Piezo1 transcription through a promoter E-box. Loss of myeloid Clock reduced Clock mesor and amplitude by 66.3% and 90.3%, respectively, increased Piezo1 mesor by 54.0%, and produced genotype-by-rhythm interactions for both genes (P < 0.0001). PIEZO1 activation impaired lysosomal acid lipase (LAL)-dependent lipophagy and promoted ZDHHC19-mediated peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) palmitoylation and extracellular-trap formation. LysM-lineage Piezo1 deletion attenuated fibrosis. PIEZO1 inhibition or DNase I reduced epithelial injury and fibroblast activation induced by extracellular DNA-rich macrophage signals.

CONCLUSIONS: CRD promotes post-septic fibrosis through a CLOCK-PIEZO1-linked macrophage immunometabolic program, identifying PIEZO1, extracellular DNA-rich traps and impaired lipid clearance as candidate targets.

articles.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Vaccination in Hemodialysis: A Mixed-Methods Survey of Australian Clinicians.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People receiving hemodialysis are vulnerable to vaccine-preventable infections, yet vaccination uptake remains suboptimal. Patient-level barriers are well described, but the clinical and service-level factors shaping vaccine delivery have received less attention. We examined clinician perspectives and vaccination practices in hemodialysis care to identify barriers, facilitators and clinician-proposed strategies for improvement.

METHODS: A convergent mixed-methods design combined an Australian cross-sectional online survey with qualitative content analysis of free-text responses (August 2024 -January 2025) of nephrologists, trainees and dialysis nurses. The survey covered vaccination beliefs, practice patterns, barriers and facilitators, and proposed solutions. Free-text responses were dual-coded and quantitative and qualitative findings were integrated during interpretation.

RESULTS: A total of 89 clinicians participated (71 (80%) nephrologists, 12 (14%) dialysis nurses, 6 (7%) nephrology trainees. Confidence in vaccine safety was high (96%), while confidence in vaccine efficacy was moderate (54% confident, 36% neither). Clinicians perceived patients to have limited understanding of their vaccination needs (54% little or no understanding). Although many clinicians (40%) indicated a preference for nephrologists to assume responsibility for vaccination, delivery within dialysis units was limited; vaccination review was predominantly nursing-led (28%) or ad-hoc (28%) and reminders were largely manually generated. Top barriers included logistical challenges (57%), clinician-perceived patient hesitancy (52%), poor communication with external vaccine-providers (46%) and time constraints (39%). Perceived hesitancy was attributed to misinformation (76%), mistrust (61%), complacency (56%) and previous adverse experiences (51%). Free-text findings described patient-centered approaches to perceived hesitancy, including repeated dialogue, shared decision making and respect for autonomy, alongside clinician-proposed strategies for better vaccination delivery through protocolized care and integrated digital systems.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians strongly support vaccination yet face substantial structural barriers - fragmented delivery, ambiguous responsibility at the primary-tertiary interface, and underdeveloped digital infrastructure. Improving vaccination uptake may require embedding vaccination within routine dialysis care and strengthening digital coordination.

articles.title: Epigenome-wide association study of kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio in chronic kidney disease.
Clinicians' reported adherence and perceived competence in delivering trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy: Associations with youth clinical outcomes.
articles.abstract: Trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (TF-CBT) is a phase- and component-based treatment for addressing youth posttraumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) following trauma. While studies have focused on overall model fidelity and predictors, less research has examined multiple, case-level indicators of TF-CBT fidelity, especially those derived from clinicians, and their associations with youth PTSS outcomes. Guided by the Exploration, Preparation, Implementation, and Sustainment framework, this study examined data measuring clinician-reported fidelity to TF-CBT during active implementation. Data were drawn from clinicians participating in TF-CBT learning collaboratives and youth and caregivers receiving TF-CBT from a participating clinician. Clinicians reported weekly, per client, which of 11 TF-CBT components were a focus of treatment, their perceived competence delivering those components, and caregiver participation. Youth and caregivers reported on PTSS pre- and posttreatment. Descriptive statistics examined completion of all TF-CBT components, relative emphasis of each TF-CBT phase, average clinician-perceived competence per phase, and caregiver participation. Multilevel modeling was used to examine the associations between adherence and perceived competence and youth PTSS outcomes. Most cases (∼57%) involved completion of all TF-CBT components-at least once-with adequate (2) to very good skill (3) on a 5-point Likert scale.
