On average, clinicians reported 53% of treatment focused on Phase 1, 26% on Phase 2, and 21% on Phase 3. Caregivers were involved in ∼70% of weeks. After controlling for demographics and pretreatment PTSS severity, neither adherence nor perceived competence was associated with posttreatment PTSS. Thus, adherence and competence alone may not be sufficient to promote PTSS symptom reduction in TF-CBT. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: Size effect of PET microplastics on oligomer leaching and the physiological and molecular performance of Daphnia magna.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: Microplastics are increasingly prevalent in the aquatic ecosystem largely resulting from the fragmentation and degradation of larger plastic debris. These plastics are primarily irregular fragments that vary in size, with particle dimensions potentially influencing their effects on aquatic biota. Additionally, lower molecular weight compounds can be released during the degradation of microplastics and may have stronger physiological and molecular effects on Daphnia magna (D. magna). In this study, the impact of four different sizes of polyethylene terephthalate PET contaminants was assessed using a combination of phenotypic and molecular endpoints, with a specific focus on PET-derived oligomers (dimer, trimer, tetramer, and pentamer). PET dimers and trimers exhibited pronounced size-dependent release and uptake dynamics, highlighting their active role in microplastic-associated exposure pathways. Feeding rate and key enzyme activities revealed a tendency in relation to size and impact. There was a notable decrease in feeding performance of D. magna neonates by 25-61%, while the activity of β-galactosidase, peptidase, and lipase decreased up to 71%, 56%, and 60%, respectively. In contrast, glutathione-S-transferase activity increased by 14-33%, depending on microplastic size. Metabolic profiling did not reveal significant differences among microplastic size treatments. The results indicate that the exposure to leachates from plastic materials can affect the physiology of D. magna neonates at the molecular level.

articles.title: Social jet lag in CPAP-treated cohorts: distribution, age gradients, and weekend rebound.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Social jet lag (SJL), the discrepancy in sleep timing between work and free nights, reflects schedule-related timing misalignment. We characterized CPAP-derived SJL in treated obstructive sleep apnea and assessed its distribution, behavioral correlates, age pattern, and consistency across two independent clinical cohorts.

METHODS: We analyzed longitudinal CPAP use timing from Rutgers-RWJ Health (RWJ, N = 1415) and Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH, N = 1497), with a combined analytic cohort of 2912 patients. Patients had at least 31 valid nights and at least one valid work night and free night. Mid-sleep on work (MSW) and free nights (MSF) was estimated using circular statistics. SJL was categorized as none (< 1 h), moderate (1-2 h), or severe (≥ 2 h). Work and free night CPAP use duration, free night rebound, age-stratified prevalence, and site consistency were assessed.

RESULTS: In the combined cohort, SJL was right-skewed, with a median of 0.43 h [IQR 0.19-0.82]; 17.8% had SJL > 1 h, including 14.8% with moderate and 3.0% with severe SJL. Greater SJL was associated with shorter work night CPAP use duration, later free night timing, and greater free night rebound. SJL prevalence was highest among adults aged 26-50 years and declined progressively with age. Similar patterns at RWJ and HMH supported the robustness of the combined findings.

CONCLUSIONS: CPAP-derived SJL was generally modest but identified a meaningful subgroup with work-free differences in CPAP use timing. Routinely collected CPAP records may provide a scalable, low-burden screening measure to identify patients whose work-free timing patterns warrant further behavioral or circadian assessment.      CURRENT KNOWLEDGE/STUDY RATIONALE: Standard CPAP reports focus on adherence, residual respiratory events, mask leak, and pressure but provide limited information about sleep timing or weekday-weekend schedule regularity. Social jet lag may contribute to residual symptoms in treated obstructive sleep apnea, but it is not routinely measured in clinical CPAP workflows.

STUDY IMPACT: This study shows that routinely collected CPAP adherence data can be used to estimate social jet lag, weekday sleep restriction, free night rebound, and age-related sleep timing patterns across two independent clinical cohorts. CPAP-derived social jet lag may provide a scalable screening phenotype to identify patients who warrant further behavioral, circadian, or activity-based assessment.

articles.title: Neuroinflammation Driven by the cGAS-STING Pathway Following Ischemic Stroke: Potential Links from Mitochondrial Stress to Immune Metabolism.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers mitochondrial dysfunction and the subsequent release of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) into the cytosol, where it activates the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) innate immune pathway and drives a complex neuroinflammatory response. This review synthesizes recent advances to examine how mitochondrial stress leads to mtDNA leakage across different brain cell types, how cGAS-STING signaling is activated in a cell-type-specific manner, and how this pathway interacts with immune cell metabolism to shape neurological outcomes. We propose that the net effect of cGAS-STING activation is not intrinsically protective or detrimental, but rather depends on the intensity and duration of the activating signal and on the metabolic state of the responding cell. A recurring theme from our analysis is that the consequences of pathway activation vary markedly among microglia, neurons, and astrocytes, and that this variation shifts over time as the inflammatory response evolves from the hyperacute to the chronic phase. On this basis, we evaluate three categories of therapeutic strategies, including preservation of mitochondrial integrity, direct inhibition of cGAS-STING components, and reprogramming of immune metabolism. We also discuss the barriers to clinical translation, such as limited blood-brain barrier penetration, the lack of cell-type-specific targeting, and the absence of validated biomarkers for patient selection. We conclude that effective therapy will require stage-specific and cell-selective strategies rather than uniform inhibition of the pathway, and that immunometabolic reprogramming may offer a more durable approach for promoting long-term recovery.

articles.title: Oncolytic vaccinia virus targeting HSP70 exhibits significant cytotoxic effects on pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), known as the king of cancers, has very limited treatment options and drugs. Oncolytic viruses have been used in tumor biologic therapy, but their therapeutic efficacy is restricted due to low replication levels within tumor cells. Recently, we constructed a novel recombinant oncolytic vaccinia virus (oncoVV-shHSP70) by homologous recombination of HSP70 shRNA into the TK region, which exhibited strong replication capability and cytotoxicity in PDAC. Preliminary mechanistic studies suggested that oncoVV-shHSP70 may elevate ROS levels by inhibiting activation of the NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant pathway, thereby triggering the caspase cascade and inducing apoptosis. Additionally, the virus modulated transcription levels of cytokine-related genes. In BALB/c nude mouse models, oncoVV-shHSP70 significantly suppressed tumor growth, demonstrating potent antitumor activity. In C57BL/6 immunocompetent mice, oncoVV-shHSP70 was preliminarily found to increase CD8⁺ T cell infiltration. The results of this study support the potential of oncoVV-shHSP70 as a novel strategy for PDAC, warranting further investigation.

articles.title: Dissolve, inhibit, or stabilize: matching clot-directed therapy to the patient with stroke.
Experiences and Perceptions Around Eating Among Older Adults Living with Serious Mental Illness: A Qualitative Analysis.
articles.abstract: People living with serious mental illness (SMI) have, on average, a life expectancy 10-20 years shorter than those without SMI and are at an increased risk for comorbid conditions such as metabolic syndrome (comprised of abdominal obesity, hypertension, impaired glucose tolerance, and hypertriglyceridemia), contributing to the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. External circumstances such as precarious living environments and poor socioeconomic status influence access to healthy food, and psychiatric symptoms may further impede healthy eating habits. To better understand facilitators and barriers to healthy eating among community-dwelling older adults living with SMI, we report the results of a qualitative analysis. We interviewed 10 community-dwelling older adults living with SMI (mean age 64.57, SD 6.815, range 53-76). A qualitative analysis using constructivist grounded theory methodology was conducted to assess participants' experiences and perceptions around eating and access to food. Two main themes emerged in our analyses: 1. Formative Life Course Influences and 2. Current Contextual Influences. Participants indicated that the early home environment, work experience, and time spent in mental health programs can influence eating habits. Participants also described how contextual influences guided the types of food they consume. This contextual-based approach to nutrition often determined whether participants ate non-nutrient-dense foods. Among community-dwelling older adults living with SMI, eating behaviors reflected the cumulative influence of lifelong experiences together with current contextual barriers. These findings suggest opportunities for community mental health services to support healthy eating through nutrition education, cooking experiences, and improving access to affordable, healthy foods.

articles.title: Outcomes of spontaneous portosystemic shunt embolization for hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis-the OPAL study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Embolization of large spontaneous portosystemic shunts (SPSSs) has emerged as a treatment for hepatic encephalopathy (HE). This retrospective multicenter Australian study investigated outcomes of SPSS embolization for persistent HE.

DESIGN: Patients with cirrhosis and overt HE (grade II or more) from January 2000 to April 2025 were studied for recurrence of HE 3- and 12-month post-embolization using competing-risks analysis, along with change in maximum HE grade, ascites, variceal bleeding, and hospitalisations 1 year before and after embolization. A case-control study considering cumulative incidence of HE, liver-related death (LRD) or liver transplant (LT) was compared to those with HE and large SPSSs with no embolization from the Baveno-VI-SPSS database.

RESULTS: Of 95 patients that underwent SPSS embolization with a median baseline MELD of 13 (IQR 11-16), 86 and 72% remained free of HE at 3 and 6 months. One year prior to embolization, 57 (60%) patients had West-Haven grade 3-4 HE, and 84% (48 patients) improved to HE grade ≤ 2 following embolization (p < 0.001). Higher MELD was not associated with worse outcome, and there was no difference in variceal bleeding or ascites post-embolization. Major procedural events occurred in seven patients (7%), with one LT and one death. Compared to matched historical controls without embolization (n = 149), there was a reduction in LRD/LT in the embolization group (sHR 0.59, 95% CI 0.40-0.88, p = 0.010), persisting on inverse probability of treatment weighting.

CONCLUSION: SPSS embolization reduced severity and frequency of persistent HE in cirrhosis, and was not associated with increased ascites or variceal bleeding. The association of embolization with reduced LRD/LT requires further study.

articles.title: External Validation and Clinical Readiness of Imaging Models for Axillary Nodal Metastasis: A Bibliometric Evidence Map with a Nested Full-Text Audit.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the development of imaging research on axillary nodal metastasis and assess external validation claims, clinical readiness reporting, and risk of bias in a nested literature audit. A Web of Science evidence map included 486 imaging-related records published in 2005-2025. A nested audit sampled 76 reports from the original 208 report model article frame. After removal of one non-imaging model, 75 reports were retained. Validation design, reporting features, and selected model risk were examined. Temporal validation was separated in sensitivity analyses; expansion-weighted estimates were conditional on sampling assumptions. Model-related language increased from 2.2% of mapped records in 2005-2011 to 67.6% in 2022-2025. Among 75 audited reports, broad external validation was supported in 36, unclear in two and unsupported in 37; excluding temporal-only validation left 29 supported reports. Reporting codes with targeted corrections identified calibration in 39 reports, decision-curve analysis in 40, reader comparison in ten and prospective evaluation in six. Source review distinguished reporting from model-specific adequacy. All 38 selected-model evaluations were assessed as high risk of bias. Seven of 43 primary evaluation components met 50 participants per outcome class. Imaging-model research has expanded, but independent evaluation and clinical readiness evidence remain uneven in the audited literature. Validation terminology, model-specific reporting, and evaluation design require joint appraisal before clinical translation.

articles.title: A case of acute hepatitis E associated with Graves' disease.
articles.abstract: Hyperthyroidism is a recognized cause of liver injury; however, distinguishing hyperthyroidism-associated liver dysfunction from acute viral hepatitis can be challenging. We report a man in his 50 s who presented with fever, fatigue, marked hyperthyroidism, and severe liver injury. Laboratory tests showed an alanine aminotransferase level of 1534 U/L and total bilirubin level of 12.0 mg/dL. Positive TSH receptor antibody and thyroid-stimulating antibody, together with increased thyroid vascularity on ultrasonography, supported a diagnosis of Graves' disease. Antithyroid treatment improved thyroid hormone levels and liver enzymes, although hyperbilirubinemia persisted. Subsequent testing of the admission sample revealed positive IgA anti-hepatitis E virus (HEV) antibodies, leading to a diagnosis of acute hepatitis E. HEV RNA testing was not performed. Because hyperthyroidism and liver injury were already present at admission, a causal relationship between HEV infection and Graves' disease could not be established. HEV infection and hyperthyroidism may have both contributed to the liver injury. This case highlights the importance of considering HEV infection in acute liver injury accompanied by thyroid dysfunction.

articles.title: Degradation of polyethylene terephthalate by esterases from Lysinibacillus macroides isolated from plastic-polluted soil.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) pollution presents a significant environmental challenge due to the polymer's recalcitrant structure. In this study, we explored the potential of naturally occurring soil bacteria from plastic-contaminated sites for enzymatic PET degradation. Among 150 bacterial isolates screened, PPSC46, subsequently identified as Lysinibacillus macroides, exhibited the highest PET esterase activity and PET-degrading potential. The isolate displayed a selective carbon utilization profile and a preference for p-nitrophenyl butyrate as a model esterase substrate. It also formed biofilms on both PET granules and post-consumer PET sheets, indicating its ability to colonize PET substrates of different physical forms. PET depolymerization was quantified using different analytical tools such as gravimetry, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). Scanning electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy demonstrated biofilm formation and extensive surface degradation on both PET granules as well as post-consumer PET sheets. Proteomic analysis identified two extracellular esterases a GDSL family lipolytic protein and an erythromycin esterase with strong predicted PET-binding affinity, implicating them as candidate enzymes potentially involved in PET degradation. To our knowledge, this is the first report of an extracellular erythromycin esterase and GDSL family lipolytic protein from L. macroides capable of PET depolymerization. These findings expand the repertoire of bacterial esterases with potential roles in PET depolymerization, providing promising candidates for further exploration in sustainable bioremediation and enzymatic upcycling of PET waste.

articles.title: Ultra-short-term in-hospital multimodal prehabilitation in older patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prehabilitation has emerged as a promising supportive care strategy to improve surgical outcomes; however, evidence regarding ultra-short-term interventions in elderly gastric cancer patients remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of a short-term (6-8 days) in-hospital multimodal prehabilitation program on functional recovery and postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: In this single-center, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial, 76 patients aged ≥ 60 years undergoing elective laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer were randomized (1:1) to in-hospital prehabilitation or standard care. The intervention included supervised exercise, individualized nutritional support, and psychological optimization delivered during the 6-8 days of preoperative hospitalization. The primary outcome was change in 6-min walking distance (6MWD) at 28-35 days postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included postoperative complications, recovery milestones, length of stay, and patient-reported outcomes (QoR-15 and HADS). Analyses were performed on a modified intention-to-treat population.

RESULTS: A total of 70 patients were included in the final analysis (prehabilitation: n = 34; control: n = 36). Adherence was high (exercise 98.0%, oral nutritional supplements 95.6%, psychological support 98.4% of planned sessions or servings). From baseline to the preoperative assessment, the 6MWD increased in the prehabilitation group (+ 31.53 ± 14.70 m) but declined in the control group (- 2.19 ± 15.98 m; P < 0.001). At 28-35 days postoperatively, the prehabilitation group demonstrated preserved or improved functional capacity compared with the control group, which showed a significant decline (Δ6MWD: + 6.00 ± 15.48 m vs. - 26.20 ± 13.34 m; P < 0.001). In exploratory analyses, postoperative complications were less frequent in the prehabilitation group (11.8% vs. 38.9%, P = 0.009), mainly owing to pulmonary infection (8.8% vs. 30.6%) and Clavien-Dindo grade I-II events; severe complications (grade ≥ III) did not differ significantly (2.9% vs. 8.3%, P = 0.615). Patients in the prehabilitation group achieved earlier milestones for postoperative ambulation, return of flatus, and resumption of oral intake (all P < 0.001) and had a shorter postoperative stay (10.06 ± 2.97 vs. 13.31 ± 6.34 days, P = 0.008), but a longer preoperative stay (8.71 ± 2.75 vs. 4.97 ± 2.93 days) and no difference in total hospital stay (19.76 vs. 19.28 days, P = 0.739). QoR-15 scores were significantly higher in the prehabilitation group during early recovery, while no between-group differences were observed in HADS scores.

CONCLUSION: In-hospital multimodal prehabilitation lasting 6-8 days appeared feasible and was associated with better functional capacity and, in exploratory analyses, fewer postoperative complications in older patients undergoing laparoscopic gastrectomy for gastric cancer. Recovery milestones were assessed without blinding of care providers, total hospital stay was unchanged, and no economic evaluation was performed. Larger multicenter trials are needed to confirm these findings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR), ChiCTR2300070553, registered on 17 April 2023.

articles.title: Added effects of manual lymphatic drainage and intermittent pneumatic compression on compression-based care for established upper-limb breast-cancer-related lymphedema: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To estimate the short-term added effects of manual lymphatic drainage and intermittent pneumatic compression on compression-based care for established upper-limb breast-cancer-related lymphedema.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, PEDro, and review reference lists were searched to 10 June 2026 without language limits. Randomized trials in adults with established upper-limb breast-cancer-related lymphedema reporting limb-volume outcomes were eligible. Reviewers extracted trial characteristics, therapy phase, component dose and provider, and volume data. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk of Bias 2 and confidence with Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis. Arms were decomposed into compression-based care, manual lymphatic drainage and intermittent pneumatic compression components for additive component network meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Of 84 included trials, 9 compression-anchored contrasts (472 participants) from initial decongestive treatment formed the network. Adding intermittent pneumatic compression was associated with greater short-term limb-volume reduction (standardized mean difference 0.46, 95% confidence interval 0.16 to 0.76). Adding manual lymphatic drainage had a small, uncertain effect (0.06, -0.16 to 0.28), although the two trials meeting conventional drainage schedules gave a larger, imprecise estimate (0.48, -0.01 to 0.97). The additive combination effect was 0.52 (0.13 to 0.91).

CONCLUSION: During initial decongestive treatment, intermittent pneumatic compression may add short-term limb-volume benefit to compression-based care. Manual lymphatic drainage, as usually delivered in trials, added little on average, and the effect of conventionally dosed drainage is uncertain. Given sparse evidence and retrospective registration, these findings should guide dismantling trials rather than change practice.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Open Science Framework, https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/R5Q2W , 29 June 2026, retrospectively registered.

articles.title: TRIM21 drives ferroptosis in sepsis-induced acute kidney injury through ubiquitination-dependent degradation of SIRT5.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced acute kidney injury (S-AKI) is a life-threatening complication of sepsis, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Ferroptosis has emerged as a critical contributor to S-AKI; however, the upstream regulatory pathways governing this process are largely unknown. This study investigated the role of tripartite motif-containing protein 21 (TRIM21) in S-AKI and explored its relationship with sirtuin 5 (SIRT5)-mediated ferroptosis.

METHODS: A cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced mouse model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated HK-2 cells were used to evaluate expression and function of TRIM21 in S-AKI. Renal injury, inflammatory responses, and ferroptosis-associated alterations were assessed using histological analysis, biochemical assays, ELISA, immunohistochemistry, and western blotting. Protein interactions and ubiquitination were examined by co-immunoprecipitation, GST pull-down, ubiquitination assays, and cycloheximide chase experiments.

RESULTS: TRIM21 expression was markedly elevated in septic kidneys and LPS-treated HK-2 cells and was accompanied by activation of ferroptosis. Genetic depletion of TRIM21 significantly improved renal function, reduced renal inflammation and oxidative stress, and attenuated ferroptosis-associated changes in vivo, while TRIM21 silencing suppressed ferroptotic injury in vitro. Mechanistically, TRIM21 directly interacted with SIRT5 and promoted its ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation, leading to impaired glutathione/redox homeostasis and reduced NRF2-associated transcriptional regulation, which together contributed to decreased GPX4 expression, enhanced lipid peroxidation, and ferroptotic cell death. Conversely, restoration of SIRT5 expression effectively reversed TRIM21-mediated ferroptosis, oxidative injury, and inflammatory responses.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies TRIM21 as a previously unrecognized regulator of ferroptosis in S-AKI, at least partly, via promoting ubiquitination and degradation of SIRT5 in renal tubular epithelial cells. However, because whole-body TRIM21 knockout mice were used, the renal protection observed in vivo cannot be solely attributed to tubular cells, and tubular-specific validation is still lacking.

articles.title: Pericapsular nerve group versus quadratus lumborum block for hip surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The pericapsular nerve group (PENG) block and the quadratus lumborum block (QLB) are both used to provide analgesia after hip surgery, but their comparative efficacy remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing PENG and QLB.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched through March 2025 for RCTs comparing PENG and QLB in adults undergoing hip surgery. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird estimator with Knapp-Hartung adjustment) pooled standardized mean differences (SMD) for pain, mean differences in intravenous morphine milligram equivalents (MME) for opioid consumption, and risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes. Heterogeneity was quantified with I². Prespecified subgroup analyses (surgical population and QLB approach) and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Seven RCTs (554 patients; 283 PENG, 271 QLB) were included. PENG showed a non-significant trend toward lower early (~ 2 h) resting pain (SMD - 0.25; 95% CI - 0.60 to 0.09; I²=55%). No significant differences were found for resting pain at 24 h (SMD - 0.40; -1.44 to 0.64; I²=92%), pain on movement at 24 h (SMD 0.08; -0.27 to 0.43; I²=0%), or cumulative opioid consumption (mean difference - 0.50 intravenous morphine milligram equivalents; 95% CI - 5.92 to 4.93; I²=84%).

CONCLUSIONS: No clear difference between PENG and QLB was demonstrated for pain, opioid consumption, or safety after hip surgery. The available evidence is insufficient to establish superiority between the techniques, and the early-pain and motor-sparing signals favoring PENG should be regarded as uncertain. Larger standardized randomized trials are required.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level I, systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Seroprevalence and associated factors of orf virus infection in goat farms, southern Thailand.
articles.abstract: Contagious ecthyma (CE), caused by Orf virus (ORFV), is a zoonotic viral skin disease of small ruminants that causes substantial economic losses and animal welfare concerns in goat production. Despite the recent molecular confirmation of ORFV circulation in Thailand, sero-epidemiological data are lacking for goat populations in the country. This study aimed to determine the seroprevalence of ORFV infection and to identify associated risk factors in goats in Southern Thailand. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 410 goats from 14 farms across 5 provinces (Narathiwat, Pattani, Songkhla, Satun, and Yala) between May 2024 and March 2025. Serum samples were screened for ORFV IgG antibodies using a commercial indirect ELISA, and farm management practices were assessed through a structured questionnaire administered to 13 participating farms. The overall apparent seroprevalence was 30.0% (123/410; 95% CI: 25.8-34.6%), with significant variation among provinces (χ² = 13.903, p = 0.008) ranging from 17.86% in Satun to 42.50% in Narathiwat. Multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression identified age as the only significant animal-level risk factor, with goats older than 4 years showing a three-fold higher odds of seropositivity compared with kids under 1 year (OR = 3.20, 95% CI: 1.33-7.71, p = 0.010). Only 5 of 13 farms met the threshold for proper management, and no farm practiced ORFV vaccination. These findings provide the first evidence of widespread ORFV exposure in Southern Thailand and highlight the need for farm-level biosecurity interventions to mitigate disease burden in smallholder goat production.

articles.title: Impact of photobiomodulation combined with leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin on healing, pain, and quality of life after third molar surgery: a randomized split-mouth clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Pain, edema, and transient limitation of mouth opening are expected manifestations after third molar surgery. Photobiomodulation (PBM) may modulate postoperative morbidity, while leukocyte- and platelet-rich fibrin (L-PRF) may support tissue repair. To evaluate healing, pain, and quality of life after third molar surgery using PBM plus L-PRF. In this randomized split-mouth study, 20 participants completed bilateral treatment. Both conditions received L-PRF prepared by centrifugation at 2700 rpm for 12 min. The test condition additionally received intraoral PBM (808 nm, 220 mW, 41 s per point, four points, approximately 36 J per session) immediately after surgery and at 24 h, 48 h, and 7 days; the control condition received simulated irradiation. Pain was assessed by the visual analogue scale (VAS) at 2, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h. Healing was evaluated using the Landry index at 24 h, 48 h, and 7 days. The 14-item Oral Health Impact Profile (OHIP-14) assessed quality of life before and 7 days after each surgery. No statistically significant between-condition differences were found in VAS, OHIP-14, or healing. Within-condition changes were observed for pain and healing, but these findings alone do not establish a difference in treatment effects. Under the conditions of this study, adding PBM to L-PRF did not demonstrate statistically significant additional benefits for pain, soft tissue healing, or quality of life.

articles.title: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications after severe blunt liver trauma in children: a single-center retrospective cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-operative management is standard for hemodynamically stable pediatric blunt liver trauma, but the incidence and optimal surveillance for late intra-hepatic arterial complications remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To analyze late intra-hepatic arterial complications and their management in a cohort of children with severe blunt liver injury, to confirm a clinical protocol.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients younger than 18 years referred to a quaternary liver center for grade ≥3 blunt liver injury (American Pediatric Surgical Association grading). Demographic and clinical data, imaging findings, active arterial bleeding or pseudoaneurysm not suspected at presentation and/or not detected on initial computerized tomography, and surgical and interventional radiology procedures were collected.

RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (median age 14.9 years) with grade III (n=10), IV (n=5), and V (n=17) liver injuries were included. A total of 37 procedures were performed in 19 patients (59%), including peri-hepatic packing, early and delayed surgical explorations, angiography, and 12 embolizations in 11 patients. Overall survival was 100%. In 5 patients (16% of the cohort; all grade IV-V injuries), late intra-hepatic arterial complications were documented on elective follow-up computerized tomography at a median of 10 days after trauma (when patients were asymptomatic), and all were managed successfully by selective interventional radiology, without procedure-related complications. No deaths occurred in this series.

CONCLUSIONS: Late intra-hepatic arterial complications were not rare in children with grade IV-V liver injuries. These findings support considering computerized tomography in children with very severe hepatic trauma, around days 10-15 after trauma, to allow pre-emptive interventional radiology management.

articles.title: From Competence to Expertise in Congenital Cardiology: The LENS Model for Learning to See Problems Differently.
articles.abstract: Competency-based medical education has improved how paediatric and congenital cardiology defines readiness for independent practice. Competencies and entrustable professional activities describe what trainees should be able to do, and the degree of supervision they require. Competence is an essential threshold rather than the endpoint of professional development. The mechanisms through which a competent congenital cardiologist subsequently develops expertise remain incompletely understood. Research in medical education and cognitive psychology suggests that experts do not simply accumulate more knowledge or more clinical experience. Expertise involves changes in knowledge organisation, clinical problem representation, information selection, recognition of discordance, management of uncertainty, decision-making and adaptation when familiar solutions are insufficient. These concepts are particularly relevant to congenital cardiology, where clinicians integrate complex anatomy, physiology, imaging, haemodynamics, previous interventions and longitudinal trajectories while frequently making decisions despite incomplete evidence. We propose that the expert congenital cardiologist may be distinguished not simply by knowing more answers, but by seeing problems differently. We introduce the LENS model as a conceptual framework for this process: Link information into a coherent clinical representation; Extract the discriminating signal from noise; Notice discordance, uncertainty and possible failure of the initial pattern; and Shift reasoning strategy, seek distributed expertise or learn when the existing model is insufficient. The framework integrates literature on medical expertise, deliberate practice, adaptive expertise, uncertainty and congenital cardiac decision-making. It offers a vocabulary for teaching, faculty development and future empirical study while deliberately preserving the distinction between career stage, reputation and demonstrated expertise.

articles.title: Transpulmonary pressure monitoring in neonates and infants.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Transpulmonary pressure (PL) monitoring has been extensively studied in adult critical care, but evidence remains limited in neonates and infants despite their high vulnerability to lung and cardiac injury. This narrative review summarizes the physiological rationale, measurement techniques, and clinical evidence for PL monitoring in neonates and infants. PL is the distending pressure of the lungs. PL monitoring may help characterize lung stress and strain, assess respiratory effort, guide PEEP selection, and better understand cardiopulmonary interactions. Esophageal pressure monitoring remains the reference method for estimating PL, but its invasiveness and technical limitations restrict its use, particularly in extremely preterm neonates. Alternative approaches, including diaphragmatic electrical activity or airway occlusion maneuvers, may provide less invasive estimates, although most remain insufficiently validated in neonates. Current clinical evidence is scarce but suggests that excessive respiratory effort and elevated lung stress may occur in preterm infants, including during non-invasive respiratory support. PL monitoring may also help to optimize lung recruitment and cardiopulmonary interactions in infants with congenital heart disease or right ventricular failure.

CONCLUSIONS: PL monitoring offers a promising physiological approach to individualize respiratory support in neonates and young infants. Further studies are needed to validate minimally invasive or non-invasive surrogates of PL and to determine their clinical relevance in this population. Integration of automated occlusion maneuvers and other advanced monitoring tools into neonatal ventilators may facilitate the transition towards physiology-based, individualized respiratory and cardioprotective strategies.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Neonates' physiology may increase their vulnerability to ventilator-induced injuries. • Transpulmonary pressure (PL) reflects the true lung distending pressure, but neonatal evidence remains limited and esophageal pressure monitoring is challenging.

WHAT IS NEW: • Emerging alternatives (diaphragmatic electrical activity and airway occlusion maneuvers) could provide emerging approaches to estimate lung stress and respiratory effort. • PL-informed PEEP titration may help optimize lung recruitment to optimize hemodynamics in neonates with our without congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Secondary pseudotumor cerebri syndrome following depressed skull fracture: a case report and review of the literature.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract: Secondary pseudotumor cerebri syndrome is an uncommon delayed complication of traumatic injury to the dural venous sinuses, particularly in children with skull fractures overlying venous sinuses. We report the case of a 4-year-old boy who presented with episodic headache and medial deviation of the left eye, 2 months after a conservatively managed occipital depressed skull fracture. Examination showed left lateral rectus palsy and grade III papilledema, with preserved visual acuity. Magnetic resonance venography demonstrated stenosis of the right transverse sinus at the site of the previous fracture, a hypoplastic left transverse sinus, and radiological features of raised intracranial pressure, including empty sella and tortuous optic nerves. Lumbar puncture confirmed elevated cerebrospinal fluid opening pressure with normal laboratory evaluation, establishing the diagnosis of secondary pseudotumor cerebri due to post-traumatic venous sinus outflow compromise. Given the delayed presentation and the concern that fracture elevation would not rapidly restore venous drainage due to chronicity, the child underwent lumboperitoneal shunt placement. He had prompt improvement in headache and complete resolution of the abducens palsy, with resolution of papilledema 2 weeks later. A literature review identified 36 reported cases of secondary pseudotumor cerebri following skull fracture, most commonly involving the superior sagittal sinus and usually caused by extrinsic compression from depressed bone fragments. Surgical elevation remains the most frequently reported treatment, however, CSF diversion, anticoagulation, decompressive craniectomy, venous angioplasty, and repeated lumbar puncture have also been used. This case highlights the need to consider delayed venous outflow obstruction after skull fracture and to individualize management according to timing, sinus anatomy, and mechanism of obstruction.

articles.title: Association Between Post-procedural Mean Arterial Pressure and Functional Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-vessel occlusion (LVO) strokes carry high morbidity despite advances in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Optimal post-EVT blood pressure (BP) management remains unclear, with current guidelines recommending uniform targets. We investigated the association between post-EVT mean arterial pressure (MAP) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVO stroke at Emory University Hospital (2016-2024) who underwent EVT. BP readings up to 48 h postprocedure were extracted and summarized in sequential time windows. Maximum MAP deviation from postprocedural baseline served as the primary exposure, specified a priori. Outcomes included modified Rankin Scale (mRS) grade at discharge as the primary measure dichotomized as favorable (mRS grades 0-2) versus unfavorable (mRS grades 3-6). Associations were examined using restricted cubic spline logistic regression with a likelihood-ratio test for nonlinearity. Patients were stratified by baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS).

RESULTS: Among 632 patients (median age 66 years, 53.0% male), successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] grade 2b-3) was achieved in 93.7%. Despite this, only 23.7% achieved favorable outcomes at discharge. Larger deviations in either direction from the individual baseline tended to accompany higher discharge mRS grade, but the shape of this association varied with the time window examined and with the summary metric used to define the exposure. It also differed by baseline stroke severity: severe strokes (NIHSS ≥ 16) showed comparatively flat associations, whereas in milder strokes (NIHSS ≤ 5) larger deviations tended to accompany higher mRS grades.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, single-center analysis, the association between early post-EVT MAP deviation and functional outcome differed across multiple conditions varying with the time window examined, the summary metric used, and baseline stroke severity. These findings suggest that post-EVT hemodynamic variability may be relevant in a patient-specific way, challenging the adequacy of uniform BP targets and supporting further investigation of individualized management strategies.

articles.title: Myeloid immune dynamics and potential reprogramming in high-altitude disorders: temporal trajectories, endothelial crosstalk, and translational implications.
articles.abstract: High-altitude hypobaric hypoxia rapidly alters circulating myeloid-cell distribution, inflammatory signaling, metabolism, and vascular interactions, but these changes are often interpreted without sufficient attention to exposure phase, tissue compartment, or persistence after recovery. This narrative review addresses a central conceptual problem: transient leukocyte mobilization and cytokine elevation are not equivalent to durable myeloid reprogramming. Evidence from human field studies, patient cohorts, hypobaric-hypoxia models, mechanistic normobaric-hypoxia experiments, and related vascular-disease models is organized within a three-level framework comprising transient exposure responses, functional adjustment during ongoing hypoxia, and persistent cell-intrinsic reprogramming. We map these states from the first hours after ascent through acclimatization, prolonged exposure, decompensation, and return to low altitude, emphasizing hypoxia-inducible-factor-dependent immunometabolism, mitochondrial stress signaling, inflammasomes, chromatin regulation, and myeloid-endothelial crosstalk. Disease-specific appraisal suggests that high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) involves complex interactions among elevated pulmonary vascular and capillary pressures, alveolar-capillary barrier dysfunction, and inflammatory responses, with inflammation potentially contributing to disease susceptibility and progression; experimental evidence implicates microglial-neurovascular interactions in high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE), but direct human causal evidence is limited; and high-altitude pulmonary hypertension (HAPH) currently has the most extensive combined human observational and experimental evidence for monocyte-macrophage involvement. Candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain exploratory and are discussed in relation to sampling phase, clinical context, evidence strength, and safety constraints; prospective disease-specific validation is required. Candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets are aligned with sampling phase, disease stage, evidence strength, and safety constraints. The resulting time-resolved, evidence-calibrated model separates reversible acclimatization from pathological decompensation and true persistence after stimulus withdrawal. Longitudinal within-person recovery studies combining sorted-cell functional assays, metabolic flux, chromatin profiling, and spatial localization are required to define the prevalence, cellular breadth, and clinical consequences of persistent high-altitude myeloid reprogramming and inform future trials of disease-specific adjunctive therapy.

articles.title: Discriminatory value of non-contrast CT coronary artery calcium radiomics for major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To evaluate whether radiomic features derived from non-contrast coronary artery calcium (CAC) CT provide incremental discriminatory information beyond conventional CAC measures for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). This study retrospectively analyzed 208 patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) from 2014 to 2022. Radiomics features were extracted from each coronary artery segment on non-contrast CT images. Six predictive models were constructed using logistic regression with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LR-LASSO): (1) clinical model; (2) conventional CAC measures model; (3) radiomics-only model; (4) radiomics combined with conventional CAC measures model; (5) radiomics combined with clinical model; and (6) comprehensive model integrating radiomic features, clinical features, and conventional CAC measures. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) analysis, and assessed using the DeLong test with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In this study, a total of 104 patients with MACE and 104 non-MACE patients were included. The radiomics combined with conventional CAC measures model achieved AUC of 0.830 and 0.825 in the training and testing cohorts. Compared with the conventional CAC measures model, its discriminatory performance was significantly improved in both cohorts (p < 0.001 and p = 0.008). However, further incorporating clinical features into this model did not result in a significant additional improvement in predictive performance (p > 0.05). In this cohort, adding radiomic features to conventional CAC measures improved MACE discrimination, whereas adding conventional CAC measures to radiomics did not significantly improve discrimination.

articles.title: Molecular characterization and epidemiological patterns of cutaneous leishmaniasis among returning travelers​.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is endemic in Pakistan however, documented reports on the returning travelers and tracing the CL transmission potentials are unavailable. The present study investigated the demographic, clinical aspects, and molecular characterization of the Leishmania species-specific CL infection in the returning travelers of Northern regions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In 2023-2025, a total of 13,400 travelers were screened, out of them, 177 (1.32%) individuals showed CL suspected lesions, and among them 153 (86.4%) symptomatic individuals participated, and agreed to record their information on a questionnaire. Skin scrapings and dried blood spots were taken for microscopy and DNA extraction, respectively. A partial fragment (~ 320 bp) of the internal transcribed spacer-1 (ITS1) gene was amplified, and sequenced for species identification.

RESULTS: Males (84, 82%) and adult travelers of age group 41-64 years (68, 43%) were highly infected. Clinically, most of the CL lesions were single (121, 79%), dry (126, 82%), and frequently affected facial parts (84, 55%). Double lesions were prevalent in adults (32, 21%). Duration of the CL lesions were recorded within two-month (130, 85%) showing a temporal association with recent travels. Risk factors including gender, clinical features, and travelling parameters, sandfly exposure, animals shed nearby, poor hygiene, and frequent outdoor activities were significantly associated with the CL infection (p < 0.05). Microscopically, 126 (82.3%) samples were positive and ITS1 sequence was amplified in 109 (71.9%) samples. The obtained sequences were highly identical to the corresponding sequences of L. tropica from GenBank.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an insight into the potential transmission of CL infection in returning travelers, and warrants appropriate counseling and management.

articles.title: Discontinuation and Non-Publication of Cardiotoxicity Clinical Trials: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract: Cardiotoxicity from anticancer therapies poses a major clinical challenge, yet the integrity of related clinical trials remains underexplored. We performed a cross-sectional analysis of cardiotoxicity trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, identifying 245 eligible studies with 199 completions and 46 discontinuations, of which 82 were published. Observational trials had high completion rates (59/65) yet suffered from profound dissemination failure, with only 13 published. Multicenter design showed a significant independent association with publication (adjusted OR 10.50, 95% CI 1.95-82.00, P = 0.010). In contrast, interventional trials faced greater operational attrition, with Phase II trials exhibiting a particularly high proportion of termination. Notably, trials enrolling ≤ 26 participants were associated with markedly lower odds of completion (adjusted OR 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-0.13, P < 0.001). Among interventional trials, international recruitment was the factor most strongly associated with publication (adjusted OR 3.07, 95% CI 1.27-7.66, P = 0.014). These findings delineate distinct translational barriers across study designs in cardio-oncology. Future priorities should include mandating transparent reporting of completed observational research and strengthening multinational collaboration in interventional trial networks to mitigate discontinuation risk and ensure a robust evidence base for cardiovascular protection.

articles.title: Soil-transmitted helminths modulate immune responses and attenuate disease activity in treatment-naive rheumatoid arthritis patients.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by systemic inflammation and progressive joint damage. Soil-transmitted helminth (STH) infection may modulate host immunity, but its role in RA pathogenesis remains unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 173 treatment-naïve RA patients and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Disease activity was assessed using DAS28-CRP and CDAI. Immune profiling, including ELISA, flow cytometry, and multiplex cytokine analysis, was performed. STH-positive RA patients exhibited reduced disease activity and lower acute-phase proteins. Immune dysregulation observed in helminth-negative RA was partially normalized in STH-positive individuals, with broad suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. IL-6, MCP-1, and IP-10 discriminated between groups (AUC > 0.75). Helminth infection independently predicted lower IL-6, TNF-α, and MCP-1. Key pathways included cytokine-receptor interactions, JAK-STAT signalling, and TNF signalling. STH infection is associated with attenuated inflammation and immune modulation in RA, suggesting a potential role for helminth-driven immunoregulation in disease pathogenesis and therapy.

articles.title: The role of the frailty index in new-onset cardiovascular disease among middle-aged and older adults with prediabetes and diabetes: an exploratory mediation analysis of depression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The interplay between frailty and depression as interconnected risk factors for cardiovascular disease (CVD) is increasingly recognised in ageing populations, yet it remains poorly understood among individuals with dysglycaemia. This study aims to clarify their interrelationship and the potential role of depression in the association between the frailty index (FI) and CVD.

METHODS: A longitudinal study was conducted using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) 2011-2020. After exclusions, 5,389 participants aged ≥ 45 years with prediabetes or diabetes were included. FI was calculated based on 27 health deficits and multiplied by 10, yielding a scale of 0-10. Covariates and mediator were assessed; statistical analyses included Cox proportional hazards regression and exploratory mediation analysis.

RESULTS: Among the 5,389 participants, 1,432 developed new-onset CVD during follow-up. The baseline FI was significantly higher in the new-onset CVD group (1.90 ± 1.39 vs. 1.50 ± 1.19, P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis revealed a non-linear association between FI and new-onset CVD. In the multiple imputation analysis, each 1-unit increase in FI was associated with a higher risk of new-onset CVD in the one-line model (HR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.15-1.24; P < 0.001). Two-piecewise Cox regression identified an inflection point at FI = 1.85 (95% CI 1.10-2.68). Below this threshold, the HR was 1.47 (95% CI 1.32-1.65), whereas at or above the threshold the HR was 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.17; both were P < 0.001). FI was positively associated with new-onset CVD across subgroups, with significant effect modification by sex but no significant interaction among those with hypertension. Depression accounted for 16.96% (95% CI 7.76%-27.55%) of the total association between FI and new-onset CVD.

CONCLUSIONS: The FI was independently associated with the risk of new-onset CVD in adults with dysglycaemia, with a non-linear pattern. In exploratory mediation analysis, depression may partly explain this association. These findings support incorporation of FI and depressive symptom assessment into cardiovascular risk stratification and warrant future studies evaluating integrated interventions targeting both physical and psychological vulnerability.

articles.title: Transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-β1) putatively modulates central noradrenergic neurotransmission via a TGF-β receptor type 1 (TGF-βR1)-mediated mechanism in male rats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) signaling has been implicated in neuropsychiatric disorders, but its direct electrophysiological effects on central monoaminergic neurons remain unclear. This study examined whether TGF-β1 modulates serotonergic, dopaminergic, and noradrenergic neuronal activity in vivo.

METHODS: Adult male rats received acute TGF-β1 administration, and extracellular single-unit recordings were performed from serotonergic neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN), dopaminergic neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), and noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus (LC). Additional experiments assessed the involvement of noradrenergic neurotransmission using fusaric acid-induced noradrenaline depletion and the role of TGF-β receptor type I (TGF-βR1) using the antagonist LY2109761.

RESULTS: TGF-β1 did not significantly alter the firing activity of DRN serotonergic neurons or VTA dopaminergic neurons. In contrast, TGF-β1 significantly reduced the spontaneous firing activity and burst parameters of LC noradrenergic neurons. Noradrenaline depletion with fusaric acid abolished the inhibitory effect of TGF-β1 on LC neuronal activity. Conversely, pharmacological blockade of TGF-βR1 with LY2109761 increased LC neuronal firing, suggesting that endogenous TGF-β1 signaling exerts a tonic inhibitory influence on the noradrenergic system.

CONCLUSION: These findings identify TGF-β1/TGF-βR1 signaling as a selective modulator of central noradrenergic neuronal activity. The apparent involvement of noradrenergic signaling in the suppression of LC firing may represent a mechanism linking TGF-β1 signaling with monoaminergic circuits involved in stress regulation and affective disorders.

articles.title: Beyond Bicarbonate: Renal Replacement Therapy in Refractory Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A minority of patients with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) remain profoundly acidaemic, despite receiving standard treatment as per established guidelines. This review examines the reported use of renal replacement therapy in that setting, proposes a working definition of refractory DKA, and sets out the differential diagnosis of persistent acidaemia that should be excluded before escalation is considered.

METHODS: Targeted, purposive, non-systematic search of PubMed with citation tracking of retrieved articles. No protocol was registered, and no formal screening or risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. The retrieval was not intended to be exhaustive, and completeness should not be inferred.

RESULTS: To date, no clinical trial of bicarbonate has included patients with a pH below 6.85, although the current consensus permits its consideration below pH 7.0. Expert guidance on extra-renal purification exists for metformin-associated lactic acidosis, toxic alcohol poisoning, and salicylate toxicity; however, none addresses DKA. Reported cases document escalation for persistent acidaemia, yet circuit composition, anticoagulation, and insulin handling are infrequently recorded, and insulin clearance across a haemofilter has not been measured in this setting. Continuous therapy using glucose-free solutions has itself precipitated euglycaemic ketosis, including in people without diabetes. Ketoacidosis associated with sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibition often presents below the glucose threshold used here and requires separate consideration, although escalation is more often described in that setting, including one report in which acidaemia persisted.

CONCLUSION: A working definition of refractory DKA is proposed for further evaluation. Persistent acidaemia often has an alternative cause that should be excluded first, but, where that exclusion is complete and acidaemia persists, renal replacement therapy has been used and reported, and weak expert guidance supports it in analogous acidoses; no benefit has been shown in DKA. Comparative evidence is lacking, and individual patient data synthesis is the next necessary step.

articles.title: Eosinophilic nephropathy in idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome.
Engineering metal-organic framework nanoplatforms for precision pulmonary delivery of JAK-STAT inhibitors in severe asthma.
articles.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as highly versatile nanoporous materials for nanomedicine owing to their exceptionally high surface area, tunable pore architecture, controllable surface chemistry, and stimuli-responsive drug release. These nanoscale characteristics enable efficient encapsulation of poorly soluble therapeutics, targeted delivery, and controlled release while minimizing systemic toxicity. Pulmonary delivery has gained increasing attention as an approach for localized treatment of inflammatory lung diseases. In parallel, the Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) signaling pathway has been established as a key regulator of cytokine-mediated inflammation in severe asthma, although systemic administration of JAK inhibitors remains limited by immunosuppression and dose-dependent adverse effects. While MOFs have demonstrated considerable promise as pulmonary drug delivery systems and JAK inhibitors have shown therapeutic potential in inflammatory airway diseases, no published study has directly investigated MOF-mediated pulmonary delivery of JAK inhibitors for asthma. This review critically examines the current evidence supporting both fields and proposes a conceptual framework for integrating these technologies. Specifically, it discusses the nanoscale design principles of MOFs, including structural engineering, pore modulation, physicochemical characteristics, biodegradability, and pulmonary delivery strategies relevant to inhaled nanomedicine. Recent advances in MOF-based drug delivery, preclinical evidence, comparisons with conventional nanocarriers, and emerging approaches involving biomimetic coatings, hybrid nanocomposites, and artificial intelligence-assisted nanomaterial design are critically evaluated. Current challenges, including pulmonary biocompatibility, long-term nanotoxicity, scalable manufacturing, immune interactions, and regulatory considerations, are also discussed. By distinguishing established evidence from future opportunities, this review identifies MOF-mediated pulmonary delivery of JAK inhibitors as a promising yet experimentally unvalidated strategy and outlines key research priorities required for its successful translation toward precision therapy for severe asthma.Clinical trial number: NA.

articles.title: The Changing Metastatic Landscape in the Modern Oncologic Era: Emerging Tumor Behaviors, Procedure-Related Dissemination, and Implications for [18F]FDG PET/CT Interpretation: A Structured Narrative Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Classical metastatic patterns, rooted in Paget's seed-and-soil hypothesis, have guided oncologic imaging interpretation for over a century. The widespread adoption of immune checkpoint inhibitors, targeted therapies, and minimally invasive surgical techniques has introduced new variables that may alter the metastatic geography encountered on positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT).

PURPOSE: This structured narrative review examines how modern cancer therapies, prolonged survival, and procedure-related factors have reshaped recognizable metastatic patterns and created new interpretive challenges for [18F]FDG PET/CT readers.

METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted across PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2020 to March 2026), supplemented by landmark earlier publications. The Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) guided the review. Evidence was synthesized narratively across four domains: therapy-driven clonal evolution and organotropism, emerging atypical metastatic sites, iatrogenic dissemination, and immunotherapy-era mimics and pitfalls.

RESULTS: Treatment-induced clonal selection, tracked through circulating tumor DNA, is increasingly reported as a driver of metastatic evolution toward non-classical organ sites. Atypical metastatic locations, including skeletal muscle, thyroid, and cardiac deposits, are increasingly recognized. Iatrogenic dissemination through port-site implantation (incidence 0.16-2.3%) and needle tract seeding represents a distinct, procedure-related pathway of tumor spread. Immunotherapy-related phenomena, including sarcoid-like granulomatous reactions and pseudoprogression, can mimic or obscure metastatic disease on [18F]FDG PET/CT. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor-based tracers show promise for peritoneal disease detection, where [18F]FDG PET/CT underperforms.

CONCLUSIONS: The metastatic landscape on contemporary PET/CT is shaped by treatment pressure, survival prolongation, and procedural factors. Nuclear medicine physicians should calibrate their interpretive frameworks to these evolving realities, integrating clinical context, treatment history, and awareness of emerging metastatic patterns into routine reporting practice. Prospective validation through multi-institutional registries is warranted.

articles.title: Tracer-dependent Within-acquisition Dynamics of Delayed-phase [18F]florbetaben and [18F]flutemetamol PET: Implications for Amyloid Quantification and Acquisition Duration.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To test whether relative signal within the delayed amyloid PET acquisition window differs between [18F]florbetaben and [18F]flutemetamol after accounting for actual post-injection timing, and to quantify agreement between shortened and 20-min reconstructions. Procedures This retrospective study included 117 unique participants with four consecutive 5-min frames (52 florbetaben, 65 flutemetamol). Frame midpoints were calculated from each participant's injection-to-acquisition interval. Target-to-whole-cerebellum ratios were analyzed using restricted-maximum-likelihood mixed models with participant-specific random intercepts and time slopes. The cortical time-by-tracer interaction was the primary inferential endpoint of the reviewer-requested reanalysis, and white matter was the key secondary endpoint. Same-platform, nonlinear, burden-adjusted, demographic, and cluster-robust sensitivity analyses were performed. Agreement analyses included Bland-Altman limits, absolute-error rates, and exploratory amyloid-status agreement.

RESULTS: In the full cohort, the cortical slope difference (flutemetamol minus florbetaben) was 0.00191 ratio/min (95% CI 0.00069-0.00314; p = 0.0025), and the white-matter difference was 0.00628 ratio/min (95% CI 0.00529-0.00727; p < 0.001). On Discovery IQ only, the cortical difference was attenuated (0.00149; 95% CI - 0.00001-0.00299; p = 0.052), whereas the white-matter difference remained robust (0.00663; 95% CI 0.00542-0.00785; p < 0.001). The first 15-min reconstruction showed small mean bias versus 20 min, with high classification agreement.

CONCLUSIONS: Delayed target-to-reference behavior differs between tracers, most robustly in white matter. Cortical differences remain susceptible to residual protocol confounding. The evaluated 15-min reconstruction showed small average bias in this cohort but requires prospective validation before protocol generalization.

articles.title: RSV and all-cause lower respiratory infection burden among infants residing in remote British Columbia: Retrospective population-based birth cohort study.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of public health = Revue canadienne de sante publique
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the population-based incidence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection-related hospitalization in infancy by community remoteness.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of live births within an integrated health jurisdiction in British Columbia (BC, Canada) from April 2013 to March 2024, followed for 1 year, using routinely collected health administrative data. Main outcomes were hospitalizations for all-cause and RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI). Secondary outcomes were tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admissions, length of stay, and air transport. Main exposures were community remoteness and social determinants of health. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated with Poisson generalized estimating equations accounting for clustering by community, with and without additional adjustment for sex, prematurity, and chronic conditions.

RESULTS: Among 472,623 infants, those living in remote communities (n = 3636) had higher hospitalization risk for all-cause (IRR 2.91, 95% CI 2.24-3.79) and RSV-LRTIs (IRR 1.60, 95% CI 1.17-2.19) compared to metropolitan areas. Length of stay and PICU admission rates were similar by region. Almost half (48.8%) of children from remote areas hospitalized for RSV-LRTIs required air evacuation. Infants from remote communities remained at higher risk for all-cause (aIRR 2.84, 95% CI 2.22-3.63) and RSV-LRTI (aIRR 1.56, 95% CI 1.15-2.12) hospitalizations after adjusting for covariates.

CONCLUSION: Infants in remote communities experienced a disproportionately high burden of RSV and all-cause LRTI hospitalization that is not fully explained by measured clinical or social determinants of health. These findings underscore the need for region-specific approaches and equitable implementation of prevention programs as jurisdictions move toward universal RSV immunization.

articles.title: Development and validation of a modular multi-purpose phantom for CT, PET/CT, and SPECT/CT quality control.
articles.journal: Physical and engineering sciences in medicine
articles.abstract: Commercial phantoms used for quality control (QC) of CT, PET/CT, and SPECT/CT systems are often designed for single tasks, requiring multiple devices to perform routine QC procedures. This study aimed to develop and validate a locally manufacturable, waterfillable, multi-purpose phantom capable of supporting several CT, PET/CT, and SPECT/CT quality control applications within a single modular platform. A PMMA-based phantom incorporating interchangeable inserts for CT dosimetry, spatial resolution, image registration, image uniformity, and contrast detectability assessment was designed and fabricated using thermal forming, CNC machining, and solvent bonding. Experimental evaluation was performed on clinical CT, PET/CT, and SPECT/CT systems using comparisons with standard/reference phantoms where available and established QC tolerance criteria. Manufacturer performance data were used only as secondary contextual benchmarks when an independent reference phantom was unavailable. CT dosimetry measurements demonstrated good agreement with a standard CTDI phantom, with CTDIV differences of 4.5% and 2.3% for head and body configurations, respectively. PET spatial resolution measurements yielded FWHM values of 3.72-3.91 mm, while PET/CT registration errors remained below one pixel (0.651 and 0.118 pixels). PET uniformity measurements showed values of 1.32-1.35%, with less than 10% deviation from a reference ACR phantom. SPECT spatial resolution measurements ranged from 8.6 to 10.8 mm; manufacturer catalogue values were used only as secondary contextual benchmarks for these measurements because an independent reference phantom was unavailable. SPECT/CT registration errors were 1.8 mm and 0.67 mm, both below accepted tolerance limits. SPECT uniformity measurements yielded integral and differential uniformity values of 1.5%, 0.9%, and 0.8%, respectively. In contrast detectability experiments, all inserts were visualized at 0.7 mCi, whereas the smallest insert became indistinguishable from the background at 0.3 mCi. The proposed phantom provides a practical and cost-effective solution for multi-modality quality control by integrating CT dosimetry, spatial resolution assessment, image registration evaluation, image uniformity analysis, and contrast detectability testing within a single reusable platform. The observed agreement with available reference phantoms and consistency with established QC tolerance criteria support its potential use for routine CT, PET/CT, and SPECT/CT quality control applications.

articles.title: Stable and Dynamic Influences of Parent Internalizing Symptoms and Parenting Stress on Psychopathology in Children with a Chronic Physical Illness: The Moderating Role of Child Hair Cortisol.
articles.abstract: Children with a chronic physical illness (CPI), such as diabetes, asthma, and epilepsy, experience significant stress and are at a greater risk of psychopathology. Parent distress strongly influences child psychopathology, and understanding stable and dynamic paths of transmission are critical for developing effective interventions. This study examined the between-dyad (stable) and within-dyad (dynamic) effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on psychopathology in children with a CPI. Additionally, we examined whether these associations were moderated by child hair cortisol concentration (HCC). Data come from 244 children (2-16 years at baseline) with a CPI, and their parents, who were followed for 48-months (assessments at baseline, 6, 12, 24, and 48 months). Parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress were assessed using self-report measures. Hair samples were collected from children, and parents reported child psychopathology symptoms. Previous work identified three HCC trajectories among children in this sample: Hypersecretion (68.0%), Hyposecretion (8.6%), and Hyper-to-Hypo (23.4%). There were significant between- and within-dyad effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on child internalizing and externalizing symptoms. Child HCC moderated the between-dyad effects of parent internalizing symptoms and parenting stress on child internalizing symptoms. The combination of high average levels of parent internalizing symptoms or parenting stress and cortisol hypersecretion predicted greater child symptoms. Findings highlight the importance of considering parent distress, paired with child cortisol, to understand psychopathology risk in children with a CPI. Overall, HCC may be a promising biomarker for understanding heterogeneity in associations between parent distress and child psychopathology.

articles.title: Imaging- and phenotype-guided calcium modification in complex PCI: a framework for device selection, procedural reassessment, and selective escalation.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary artery calcification presents a major challenge during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), contributing to impaired lesion crossing, inadequate balloon expansion, and stent underexpansion. Multiple calcium-modification technologies are available; however, optimal device selection depends on lesion morphology, anatomical characteristics, and procedural response.

OBJECTIVE: To provide an imaging- and phenotypeguided framework for selecting and escalating calcium modification strategies during complex PCI, integrating contemporary evidence, procedural reassessment, and emerging technologies.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes contemporary consensus statements, randomized trials, prospective device studies, observational investigations, and meta-analyses addressing intravascular ultrasound (IVUS), optical coherence tomography (OCT), calcium morphology, lesion crossability and expandability, calcium-modification mechanisms, combination strategies, anatomical considerations, procedural complications, and resource utilization.

RESULTS: Available calcium-modification modalities-including rotational and orbital atherectomy, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL), excimer laser coronary atherectomy, and specialized balloon-based techniques-provide complementary mechanisms of calcium modification. Evidence from trials such as PREPARE-CALC, ECLIPSE, and ROLLER COASTR-EPIC22 highlights the importance of distinguishing procedural success, imaging-defined stent expansion, and longer-term clinical outcomes. No single technology demonstrates universal superiority across all calcified lesion phenotypes. An integrated strategy incorporating calcium morphology, intravascular imaging, lesion crossability, balloon expandability, and reassessment after each intervention may support more rational device selection and selective escalation. Particular considerations include calcified nodules, left main and bifurcation lesions, tortuous anatomy, procedural complications, and resource availability.

CONCLUSION: An imaging- and response-guided approach offers a practical framework for calcium modification during complex PCI. The principal objective is to achieve adequate lesion preparation and optimal stent expansion while minimizing vessel injury and unnecessary device utilization. Prospective validation of this framework is warranted.

articles.title: Reporting of sex- and age-specific outcomes for antibody drug conjugate-induced nausea and vomiting in patients with cancer.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate how often studies of antibody drug conjugate-induced nausea and vomiting (ADCINV) report demographic characteristics and demographic-specific toxicity outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of 202 studies included in a systematic review of ADCINV. We summarized study country and income setting, age and sex reporting, and whether nausea and vomiting outcomes were reported by age, sex, or country/region.

RESULTS: Most studies were conducted in high-income settings (144/202, 71.3%). One hundred forty-eight studies (73.3%) reported at least one age summary, although only 22 (10.9%) reported an older-adult proportion. Overall, 123 studies (60.9%) reported the percentage of female participants. No study reported nausea or vomiting outcomes stratified by age, sex, or country/region.

CONCLUSION: ADC studies frequently report overall nausea and vomiting but do not provide the demographic-specific outcomes needed to evaluate differential risk. Standardized reporting by age, sex, and geographic setting is needed in future trials and real-world studies.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of dual-phase photon-counting detector for localization of parathyroid adenomas after inconclusive first-line imaging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate diagnostic performance, radiation dose, and quantitative spectral characteristics of dual-phase photon-counting CT (PCD-CT) for parathyroid adenoma localization after inconclusive first-line imaging.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Consecutive patients with primary hyperparathyroidism and negative, discordant, or inconclusive first-line imaging underwent paired [18F]FECh PET/CT and dual-phase PCD-CT with arterial and venous acquisitions. Three radiologists, blinded to clinical and reference-standard information, retrospectively assessed arterial and portal-venous 40- and 70-keV images and VNC reconstructions. The reference standard comprised surgery/histopathology with biochemical confirmation, concordant PET/CT with persistent biochemical disease in nonsurgical positive patients, or clinical/biochemical resolution in negative patients. Lesion-level sensitivity, positive predictive value (PPV), and interreader intraclass correlation (ICC) were calculated. Aorta-normalized attenuation and wash-in and wash-out metrics were compared among adenomas, thyroid tissue, and lymph nodes.

RESULTS: Forty-nine patients (mean age, 64.2 ± 10.9 years; 42 women) were included, with 45 patients having 49 reference-standard-positive lesions. PCD-CT lesion-level sensitivity was 67.3%-83.7%, and PPV 67.3%-90.0%, with an interreader agreement of 0.506. Aorta-adjusted wash-out was greater in adenomas (27.2%) than in thyroid (20.2%) and lymph nodes (-3.1%; both p < 0.001). Arterial adenoma-thyroid attenuation and wash-in overlapped between adenomas did not differ significantly (arterial p = 0.615 and thyroid tissue. 0.945 at 40 and 70 keV; wash-in p = 0.363). Mean estimated effective dose was 1.23 ± 0.47 mSv.
