CONCLUSION: Dual-phase PCD-CT provided reader-dependent parathyroid localization at low radiation dose in a difficult second-line cohort. Quantitative wash-out may aid differentiation from thyroid and lymph-node mimics but requires prospective threshold validation.

KEY POINTS: Question Inconclusive first-line imaging complicates parathyroid lesion localization. Findings Reader sensitivity ranged from 67.3% to 83.7% at 1.23 mSv. Critical relevance statement Aorta-adjusted wash-out differed among parathyroid lesions, thyroid tissue, and lymph nodes.

articles.title: Early-stage tendon stiffening precedes morphological thickening in pediatric type 1 diabetes: a quantitative shear wave elastography study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study aims to comparatively evaluate Achilles tendon thickness and elastographic tissue stiffness in children with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) versus healthy controls, demonstrating the early radiological reflections of chronic hyperglycemia on pediatric tendon histomorphology. This prospective cross-sectional study included 60 pediatric T1DM patients and 60 age- and gender-matched healthy controls (mean age, 11.82 ± 4.02 years; range, 7-16 years). Glycemic control was evaluated using mean HbA1c levels. Anteroposterior Achilles tendon thickness was measured via B-mode ultrasonography. Quantitative tissue stiffness was assessed using Shear Wave Elastography (SWE), recording Young's modulus (kPa) and shear wave velocity (m/s) guided by motion stability and reliability indices. Bilateral Achilles tendon thickness did not differ significantly between the diabetic and control groups (p > 0.05). However, SWE revealed a highly significantly increased Young's modulus and shear wave velocity in the diabetic group compared to healthy controls (p < 0.001). Multiple linear regression identified diabetes duration as a significant independent predictor of increased tendon thickness (p < 0.05). Furthermore, left Achilles tendon velocity demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.940) in distinguishing diabetic tissue.

CONCLUSIONS: In children with T1DM, quantitative SWE detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness before macroscopic morphological thickening occurs on B-mode ultrasonography. While histopathological confirmation is lacking, this imaging-based observation of early-stage stiffening may serve as a non-invasive surrogate marker reflecting putative glycation-related microstructural alterations within the tendon matrix, presenting a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically reported in adult diabetic cohorts.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • In adult diabetic cohorts, chronic hyperglycemia leads to macroscopic Achilles tendon thickening and biomechanical softening due to long-term collagen degradation. • The subclinical effects of type 1 diabetes on connective tissue histomorphology in the early pediatric stage remain largely unexplored.

WHAT IS NEW: • Quantitative Shear Wave Elastography detects a highly significant increase in Achilles tendon stiffness in pediatric type 1 diabetes before any macroscopic morphological thickening occurs.  • This early-stage tissue stiffening reveals a biphasic biomechanical contrast to the chronic tendon softening typically observed in adult diabetic patients.

articles.title: Intracranial aneurysm risk and cerebrovascular outcomes in thoracic versus abdominal aortic aneurysms: a national analysis of 114,805 hospitalizations.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal disease is increasingly recognized as a systemic vasculopathy, yet large-scale comparisons between thoracic (TAA) and abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) regarding intracranial aneurysm (ICa) burden and cerebrovascular outcomes remain limited. This study leverages a nationally representative database to compare the frequency of coded coexisting ICa, cerebrovascular events, and in-hospital outcomes between TAA and AAA, and to identify factors associated with coexisting ICa.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample (2000-2020) identified adult hospitalizations with TAA or AAA that included an aortic aneurysm repair; dissections and thoracoabdominal or unspecified-site aneurysms were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1, nearest-neighbor, caliper 0.2 SD) adjusted for demographic and clinical differences, with covariate balance assessed by standardized mean differences. Primary outcomes included administratively coded coexisting ICa and cerebrovascular events (ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, coded subarachnoid hemorrhage [SAH]). Secondary outcomes included mortality, length of stay, charges, and discharge disposition. Multivariable logistic regression and exploratory random forest machine learning examined factors associated with coded ICa. Counts are unweighted NIS discharge records.

RESULTS: Among 114,805 hospitalizations (2.3% TAA, 97.7% AAA), coded coexisting ICa was present in 168 (0.15%); its frequency was higher in TAA than in AAA before matching (1.0% vs. 0.1%, p < 0.001) but not after matching (1.0% vs. 0.7%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.79-2.65; p = 0.23). The propensity-matched analysis (n = 5,330) demonstrated higher rates of ischemic stroke (5.5% vs. 3.9%, p = 0.007), hemorrhagic stroke (0.5% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.007), and coded SAH (0.8% vs. ≤0.4%, p = 0.003) in TAA; E-values indicated that these hemorrhagic associations were robust to residual confounding, whereas ischemic stroke and mortality differences were sensitive to residual imbalance in atrial fibrillation and repair modality. In multivariable analysis, TAA was independently associated with coded coexisting ICa (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.07-1.27). Female sex showed the strongest association (aOR 2.56), followed by smoking, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. TAA had higher mortality (4.9% vs. 3.0%), longer stays (9.83 vs. 6.21 days), greater non-home discharge (53.7% vs. 28.3%), and higher charges (all p < 0.001). Among all hospitalizations with an unruptured aortic or intracranial aneurysm diagnosis, the TAA share increased from approximately 11% to 35% between 2003 and 2020. Machine learning identified age as the most influential variable, with key interactions involving age × female sex and age × vascular comorbidities.

CONCLUSIONS: TAA is associated with higher coded cerebrovascular event rates, worse in-hospital outcomes, and greater healthcare utilization than AAA. Because ICa in administrative data are identified through clinical recognition rather than systematic screening, these data should not be construed to mean that ICa are more prevalent among patients with TAA, although cerebrovascular events appear more frequent and more morbid in this population. Prospective imaging-based studies are needed before targeted intracranial screening can be recommended, particularly for younger women with TAA and vascular comorbidities.

articles.title: Early pharmacological thromboprophylaxis for patients with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aims to compare the effects of early and late pharmacological thromboprophylaxis (PTP) on venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with traumatic intracranial hemorrhage (ICH). A comprehensive retrieval for literature up to October 2026 was conducted across the PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases. Early PTP was defined as administration within 72 h post-admission. The analysis encompassed thirteen cohort studies, including a total of 18, 554 patients with traumatic ICH. The primary outcome measures were the occurrence of VTE, progression of ICH, cranial surgery, and in-hospital mortality. Early PTP was associated with a significantly lower incidence of VTE (OR, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.39-0.67), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed between the groups for ICH progression (OR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.64-1.29), cranial surgery (OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 0.79-1.69), or in-hospital mortality (OR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.83-1.18). Initiating PTP within 72 h of hospital admission may reduce the incidence of VTE without significantly increasing the rates of ICH progression, cranial surgery, or in-hospital mortality in patients with traumatic ICH. Nevertheless, given the observational design of the included studies and the potential for residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require confirmation in prospective, randomized controlled trials.

articles.title: Dietary supplementation with Spirulina platensis and humic acid alleviates heat stress in broiler chickens: effects on growth performance, serum metabolites, immune responses, and antioxidant capacity.
articles.abstract: While previous studies have evaluated Spirulina platensis (SP) and humic acid (HA) individually, the novelty of this work lies in providing the first comprehensive evaluation of their combined (SP + HA) effects on broiler chickens under acute heat stress, bridging a critical gap regarding the interplay between growth performance, redox status, economic efficiency, blood biochemistry, and immune response. Five hundred (500) three-day-old Ross 308 broiler chicks were assigned to 5 experimental groups in a completely randomized design. The chicks were maintained in thermoneutral settings (23 °C) (negative control, NEG CON) and fed a basal diet without supplements in the first group. The other four chicken groups received either a basal diet without supplements (positive control group (POS CON)) or were supplemented with SP (2 g/kg of feed; SP group), HA (5 g/kg of feed; HA group), or a mix of SP and HA by the same dosages (SP + HA; group 4), and were exposed to heat stress (36˚C ± 2˚C) from the 22nd to the 25th day of age for 6 h/day. All supplemented groups showed improvements in growth measures compared to the POS CON group. The HA group showed increased body weight gain and decreased feed conversion ratio compared with the NEG CON group (P < 0.01). The concentrations of growth hormone, heat shock protein 70 mRNA expression, total protein, globulin, and interferon-γ were elevated in the SP, HA, and SP + HA groups relative to the other groups. An increase in the concentration of malondialdehyde and interleukin-1β, and a decrease in the total antioxidant capacity, catalase, and superoxide dismutase were observed in the POS CON group compared to the NEG CON group, which were improved by SP and/or HA supplementation. In conclusion, supplementation with SP and/or HA mitigates the negative impacts of heat stress on growth, immune function, and oxidative status.

articles.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and acceptance of HPV vaccination in parents and patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases.
articles.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection and a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers. Children with rheumatologic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy are at increased risk for persistent HPV infection, making vaccination a critical preventive strategy. The HPV vaccine is not included in Türkiye's National Immunization Program (NIP). This study aimed to assess HPV awareness, vaccine acceptance, and factors contributing to vaccine hesitancy among children with rheumatologic conditions and their parents. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 156 parent-child pairs attending the Pediatric Rheumatology Department at Dokuz Eylul University between August 2024 and August 2025. The survey was offered to 178 eligible parent-child pairs, of whom 156 agreed to participate (response rate, 88%). Inclusion criteria were ages 9-18 years, confirmed rheumatologic diagnosis, and current immunosuppressive therapy. Separate structured questionnaires were administered to parents and children to assess demographic characteristics, disease characteristics, immunization history, HPV knowledge, vaccine awareness, attitudes, and actual vaccination status. Median child age was 13 years; 81% of parents were female. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis was the most common diagnosis [87%]. HPV vaccine coverage was low [3% in both children and parents]. Among parents, 48% had heard of HPV and 47% were aware of the HPV vaccine. The most commonly reported barriers to HPV vaccination were insufficient knowledge [65% of children and 58% of parents], safety concerns [38% of children and 39% of parents], and lack of physician recommendation [63% of parents]. Logistic regression showed that female parent respondent status [OR = 7.3, 95% CI 2.2-24.6; p = 0.001] and university education compared with primary school education [OR = 12.9, 95% CI 1.8-90.4; p = 0.010] were associated with higher HPV awareness. Parents who had not previously obtained optional vaccines [not included in the NIP] for their children had lower odds of HPV awareness than those who had [OR = 0.21, 95% CI 0.06-0.69; p = 0.010]. Conclusions: HPV vaccination rates were very low among children with rheumatic diseases receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Higher parental HPV awareness was associated with female parent sex, higher parental education, and previous uptake of optional vaccines. The most commonly reported barriers to vaccination included insufficient knowledge, safety concerns, and lack of physician recommendation. These findings highlight the need for targeted educational interventions and stronger physician-family communication regarding HPV vaccination.

articles.title: Bruceine D induces ferroptosis in ectocervical Ect1/E6E7 cells by modulating GSTP1 and MAPK14 signaling and downregulating GPX4.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical precancerous lesions and cervical cancer. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is a potential therapeutic target in HPV-associated malignancies. Bruceine D (BD), a bioactive quassinoid isolated from Brucea javanica, exhibits antitumor and antiviral activities. However, its effects on HPV-associated cervical epithelial cells remain unclear.

METHODS: The effects of BD on HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized ectocervical epithelial cells (Ect1/E6E7) were evaluated using cell viability, colony formation, EdU incorporation, and cell-cycle assays. Ferroptosis-associated changes were assessed by measuring lipid peroxidation, glutathione (GSH) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, mitochondrial membrane potential, and the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins. Pharmacological rescue experiments using ferroptosis inhibitors and pathway inhibitors were performed to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation were used to identify candidate regulatory targets.

RESULTS: BD significantly inhibited Ect1/E6E7 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 cell-cycle arrest in a concentration-dependent manner. BD treatment increased lipid peroxidation and MDA levels, depleted intracellular GSH, disrupted mitochondrial function, and downregulated GPX4. Ferroptosis inhibitors partially reversed BD-induced cell death, supporting the involvement of ferroptosis. Network pharmacology analysis and experimental validation implicated GSTP1 and MAPK14 in the cellular response to BD. Pharmacological inhibition of MAPK14 attenuated BD-induced ferroptotic responses, suggesting a role for GSTP1/MAPK14-associated signaling. BD also exhibited synergistic antiproliferative effects when combined with the ferroptosis inducer erastin.

CONCLUSION: BD reduces the survival of HPV16 E6/E7-immortalized cervical epithelial cells by inducing ferroptosis associated with GPX4 downregulation and GSTP1/MAPK14 signaling. These findings support further preclinical investigation of BD and ferroptosis-based approaches in HPV-associated cervical disease.

articles.title: Chronic Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: Microglial Autophagy, PI3K/Akt/mTOR Signaling, and Persistent Neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a major contributor to long-term disability and reduced quality of life after ischemic stroke, yet the mechanisms operating during its chronic phase remain insufficiently integrated. Increasing evidence suggests that, beyond the acute insult, dysfunction of the neurovascular unit and the blood-brain barrier, systemic immune responses, secondary neurodegeneration in distal brain regions, white matter degeneration, and structural disconnection of neural networks may all contribute to the development of PSCI, and the pathological consequences of these processes may persist into the subsequent subacute and chronic phases. Persistent neuroinflammation may contribute to these pathological processes and promote cognitive decline. Dysregulation of microglial autophagy and the class I phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) signaling may represent candidate mechanisms underlying this persistent neuroinflammatory process. Under specific pathological conditions, sustained mTORC1 activity may promote inflammatory by inhibiting the initiation of autophagy and restricting the TFEB-dependent lysosomal transcriptional program, thereby impairing the clearance of damaged mitochondria and inflammation-related substrates. This sustained inflammatory state may disrupt neuronal and synaptic function and contribute to white matter injury and neural network dysfunction. We synthesize evidence related to persistent pathology following stroke and critically examine the interactions among PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, microglial autophagy, and persistent neuroinflammation. Given the limited direct mechanistic evidence from chronic ischemic stroke, we also incorporate supportive findings from ischemia-related models and selected chronic neuroinflammatory conditions to build a more integrated mechanistic framework.

articles.title: Targeting bacterial RNA repair: the Rtc system as an emerging antibiotic-adjuvant strategy.
articles.abstract: The RNA repair and rescue (Rtc) system is an emerging bacterial stress-response pathway that may support adaptation during antibiotic exposure. It comprises RNA 3'-phosphate cyclase RtcA, RNA ligase RtcB, and, in well-characterized models, the σ⁵⁴-dependent regulator RtcR. These components process and repair damaged RNA termini and may preserve translational capacity during ribotoxic, oxidative, and other stresses. Antibiotic-induced translational disruption can cause tRNA and rRNA cleavage or fragmentation, potentially increasing dependence on Rtc-mediated repair. Experimental evidence suggests that Rtc facilitates RNA recovery and bacterial survival during transient stress, although its importance varies among species and remains poorly defined under clinically relevant conditions. Rtc-mediated survival appears more closely associated with phenotypic stress tolerance than classical heritable antibiotic resistance, although prolonged survival may create opportunities for subsequent adaptation. Considerable diversity in Rtc organization, regulation, and physiological dependence also limits extrapolation from model bacteria to multidrug-resistant pathogens. The distinct catalytic and regulatory properties of RtcA, RtcB, and RtcR provide potential opportunities for therapeutic intervention. Proposed approaches include small-molecule inhibition, suppression of rtc expression, synthetic-lethal combinations, nanocarrier-mediated delivery, and engineered bacteriophages. However, no clinically validated Rtc-specific inhibitor is currently available, and these therapeutic applications remain largely conceptual or preclinical. Overall, the Rtc system represents an important area of bacterial RNA biology that warrants further investigation as a stress-associated vulnerability and potential target for future antibiotic-adjuvant strategies.

articles.title: Minimally invasive extraction of fully impacted wisdom teeth and supernumerary teeth assisted by 3D-printed digital surgical guides: a prospective cohort study and establishment of a standardized workflow.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the clinical efficacy, safety, and technical feasibility of 3D-printed digital surgical guides for minimally invasive extraction of fully impacted wisdom teeth and supernumerary teeth, and to establish a standardized, reproducible digital workflow.

METHODS: A prospective cohort study enrolled 58 patients treated from January 2023 to December 2024, randomized into a guide-assisted group (n = 26) and a traditional surgery group (n = 32). The guide group underwent CBCT scanning, 3D reconstruction, computer-aided guide design, and 3D-printed guide-assisted minimally invasive extraction. The control group received extraction with traditional free-hand extraction using high-speed turbine handpieces based on clinical experience. Surgical duration, intra-/postoperative complication rates, and 24-hour postoperative VAS pain scores were compared between groups.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were comparable (P > 0.05). No statistically significant differences emerged in surgical duration (33.0 ± 15.66 vs. 28.31 ± 11.32 min, P = 0.192), intraoperative complication rate (7.7% vs. 0%, P = 0.197), postoperative complication rate (76.9% vs. 62.5%, P = 0.238), or 24-hour VAS score (2.88 ± 1.80 vs. 2.06 ± 1.74, P = 0.084). All 3D-printed guides were successfully seated and used intraoperatively without technical failures such as loosening or fracture.

CONCLUSION: 3D-printed digital surgical guide-assisted extraction is a safe, precise, and stable minimally invasive technique, with clinical efficacy comparable to traditional surgery. Parametric design standardizes the workflow; combined with patent protection (ZL202323112840.0) and data sharing, it offers a reliable solution for complex impacted tooth management.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This standardized digital approach reduces operator dependency, enhances the protection of vital anatomic structures, and provides a reproducible, evidence-based minimally invasive strategy for the clinical management of fully impacted wisdom teeth and supernumerary teeth.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registration number ChiCTR2600124323. Registration Time: 2026-05-11 00:00:00.

articles.title: Exploring preoperative prediction of conversion in minimally invasive colorectal cancer surgery using Swedish and Danish national register data.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Conversion of minimally invasive surgery often adds operative time and may lead to complications. The aim was to develop a preoperative prediction model for conversion and identify predictive risk factors in minimally invasive colorectal cancer resections, to be used in consideration and counselling preoperatively.

METHODS: An observational study based on data from national Swedish registries (CRCBaSE, 2019-2021). Logistic regression models were used to predict conversion, with variable selection based on statistical performance. Model discrimination, calibration, and uncertainty were evaluated using the Brier score, AUC, calibration plots, and bootstrap resampling. External validation was performed in the Danish Colorectal Cancer Registry (2016-2020).

RESULTS: Minimally invasive surgery was performed on 7,811 patients. Seven preoperative predictors were identified as risk factors of conversion: body mass index (BMI), clinical T stage, age, previous abdominal surgery, sex, robotic approach, and left-sided tumour location. Risk of conversion increased with advanced T stage, left-sided tumours, prior abdominal surgery, extremes of BMI, and age up to 80 years, whereas robotic surgery and female sex reduced the risk of conversion. A 7-variable model was created and achieved an AUC of 0.730 in the Swedish test set but demonstrated reduced discrimination and calibration on internal validation (AUC 0.681). External validation in a Danish national cohort confirmed consistent directions of the predictors but showed further reduced predictive performance (AUC 0.608).

CONCLUSIONS: Internal validation did not maintain adequate discrimination or calibration, and neither did the external validation. Several variables showed consistent associations with conversion and may be regarded as candidate predictors.

articles.title: Prevalence and pretreatment predictors of acetaminophen treatment failure for patent ductus arteriosus in preterm infants: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of acetaminophen-induced patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) closure failure and evaluate pretreatment predictors of non-response in preterm infants. This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261472267). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Epistemonikos, and ProQuest were searched from inception to August 2026. Randomized and observational studies reporting PDA closure outcomes following acetaminophen treatment were included. Random-effects models pooled study-defined failure prevalence and crude odds ratios (ORs). Subgroup analyses and exploratory univariable meta-regression examined heterogeneity. Analyses used R version 4.4.1 with the meta and metafor packages. Twenty-eight studies contributed 1559 evaluable infants. The pooled failure prevalence was 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 85.8%; τ2 = 0.5886). Crude analyses linked extreme prematurity (OR, 2.97; 95% CI, 1.44-6.13) and female sex (OR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.05-2.55) to higher failure odds. Treatment context, dose, and duration showed significant subgroup differences; administration route did not. Meta-regression identified study-level associations involving birth weight, gestational age, small-for-gestational-age status, 1-min Apgar score, preterm premature rupture of membranes, and antenatal corticosteroid exposure. Individual adjusted analyses identified greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia as potential predictors.  Conclusion: Overall, approximately one-third of treated preterm infants met study-defined criteria for acetaminophen treatment failure. Extreme prematurity, greater ductal severity, and thrombocytopenia warrant further evaluation as prognostic factors. Prospective studies should standardize outcome definitions and validate prediction models. What is Known: • Acetaminophen is used for PDA closure in preterm infants, particularly when cyclooxygenase inhibitors are contraindicated. • Treatment response varies substantially, but acetaminophen-specific predictors of failure remain poorly defined. What is New: • Across 28 studies involving 1559 infants, acetaminophen treatment failed in 34% (95% CI, 28%-42%). • Extreme prematurity showed higher failure odds, while greater ductal diameter and thrombocytopenia emerged as potential predictors requiring validation.

articles.title: Linear Mini High Submandibular Incision (LMHSI) for Open Reduction and Internal Fixation (ORIF) of mandibular condylar base fractures: a prospective clinical study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This prospective single-arm clinical study evaluated the technical feasibility and short-term clinical, functional, radiological, and aesthetic outcomes of the Linear Mini High Submandibular Incision (LMHSI) for open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of mandibular condylar base fractures.

METHODS: A study was conducted between February 2025 and April 2026. A total of 137 patients with 150 mandibular condylar base fracture sites underwent ORIF using the LMHSI approach. Clinical, functional, radiological, and aesthetic outcomes were evaluated through operative parameters, CT-based Condylar Reduction Assessment (CRA), facial nerve function, maximum mouth opening, mandibular movements, bite force, pain scores, scar quality using the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS), patient satisfaction, and postoperative complications during a 6-month follow-up period.

RESULTS: Mean incision length was 2.3 ± 0.2 cm, and mean operative time was 38.6 ± 4.2 min. Adequate exposure was achieved in all cases without conversion to another approach. No facial nerve weakness occurred. Maximum mouth opening improved from 15.8 ± 3.4 mm to 41.3 ± 7.1 mm, while bite force increased significantly by 6 months (p < 0.001). CRA Grade I anatomical reduction was achieved in 97.3% of fracture sites. Complications were limited to minor seroma (3.3%), infection (2.0%), and wound dehiscence (1.3%). Scar assessment and patient satisfaction demonstrated progressive improvement throughout follow-up.

CONCLUSION: In this prospective single-arm cohort, LMHSI provided feasible access for open reduction and internal fixation of mandibular condylar base fractures and was associated with favorable short-term functional, radiological, and aesthetic outcomes. The findings support LMHSI as a limited-incision refinement of the high-submandibular approach; however, comparative effectiveness or superiority over other approaches cannot be established without a control group.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Multifaceted therapeutic approach via thiazolidinedione-infused magnolol in chitosan nanoparticles targeting hyperlipidemia and oxidative stress in gestational diabetes mellitus in experimental mice.

Association between neonatal phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Phototherapy has been widely used for the treatment of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia. However, concerns persist about its long-term neurological effects. While some studies report an increased risk of epilepsy after phototherapy, others found no association. This systematic review and meta-analysis aim to examine the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. We followed the PRISMA guidelines for our meta-analysis. We searched six databases for studies investigating the association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy and febrile seizures. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used for quality assessment. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effect model in R software. Three studies with 632,227 participants met our inclusion criteria. Phototherapy was associated with a 37% higher risk of childhood epilepsy (HR = 1.37, 95% CI = 1.13-1.67, p < 0.01; I2 = 30%). Subgroup analysis revealed a significant risk in boys (HR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.17-2.24, p < 0.01) but not girls (HR = 1.14, 95% CI = 0.92-1.41, p = 0.23). No association was found with febrile seizures (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 0.99-1.15, p = 0.09).

CONCLUSION: In this meta-analysis of three observational cohorts, neonatal phototherapy was associated with a possible increase in the risk of childhood epilepsy, particularly in boys; this finding depends on a small and methodologically heterogeneous evidence base, and residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded. Given the limited number of studies, the conflicting result from the most methodologically rigorous study, and the exploratory nature of the sex-stratified analysis, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as grounds to alter current phototherapy practice. Further well-designed studies controlling for confounders are needed.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Phototherapy is standard treatment for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and is generally considered safe. • Prior studies on phototherapy and childhood epilepsy have shown conflicting results.

WHAT IS NEW: • Pooled analysis of 632,227 infants show an association between phototherapy and childhood epilepsy, particularlyin boys, but not febrile seizures. • The association may reflect residual confounding rather than a causal effect, and does not currently justify changingphototherapy practice.

articles.title: "Let them do it": surgeon proficiency level and outcomes after ostomy reversal: a single-center retrospective study and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ostomy reversal is a frequently performed procedure in colorectal surgery and is often considered suitable for surgical training. However, evidence regarding the impact of surgeon training level on postoperative outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate outcomes after ostomy reversal performed by residents versus consultant surgeons through a combined single-center analysis and systematic review with meta-analysis.

METHODS: A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted, including 255 patients who underwent loop ileostomy or loop colostomy reversal between 2012 and 2024. Postoperative outcomes were compared between procedures performed by residents and consultants. The observational study was conducted and reported in accordance with STROBE guidelines. In addition, a systematic review and meta-analysis were carried out according to PRISMA guidelines to assess outcomes after loop ileostomy reversal stratified by surgeon training level. The primary outcomes were overall and major postoperative morbidity.

RESULTS: In the single-center cohort, postoperative outcomes after ostomy reversal were largely comparable between residents and consultants. Residents more frequently performed direct stoma closure and had shorter operative times, and their patients were discharged sooner. Major postoperative morbidity was significantly higher in consultant-performed ileostomy reversals, likely reflecting greater procedural complexity. The meta-analysis of available comparative studies, including 1,196 patients (resident: n = 419; consultant: n = 777), demonstrated that resident-performed loop ileostomy reversal was not associated with inferior outcomes. In contrast, resident-performed stoma reversal was associated with lower rates of overall postoperative morbidity (OR = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.46-0.76; p < 0.0001) and major postoperative morbidity (OR = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.44-0.99; p = 0.04), whereas complication-specific outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Notably, serious risk of bias and low certainty of evidence were detected.

CONCLUSION: Resident-performed ostomy reversal appears safe and feasible when conducted within a structured and supervised training environment. Findings from both the single-center analysis and the meta-analysis support integrating stoma reversal procedures into surgical residency training.

articles.title: Association of differential growth and the incidence of respiratory distress in twins with birth weight discordance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Birth weight is linked to neonatal lung morbidities, including respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). Studies in singletons are often limited by confounding factors. Birth weight discordant (BWD) twins eliminate these biases, providing a unique model to isolate the impact of differential growth. Our aim is to compare the risk of RDS in the smaller twin versus the larger twin within discordant pairs. PubMed and preprint servers (medRxiv and Research Square) were systematically searched using a Boolean phrase combining terms such as twin, birth weight discordance, respiratory distress, and RDS, retrieving all relevant articles from August 21st 2025 to July 30th, 2026, with no language, geographical, or time restrictions. All studies reporting on the correlation of birth weight and the incidence of RDS in BWD twins were included in our review. The systematic review and meta-analysis is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251135439). A total of 21 studies were included in our review. RDS incidence was found to be lower in the lighter twin compared to its heavier co-twin (11.44% vs 14.67% respectively, RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.63-0.95, p = 0.01) with lower need for surfactant administration, a result which was reversed in the analysis for BPD incidence where the lighter twin was at greater risk (5.71% vs 2.76% in the heavier twin, RR 2.04, 95% CI 1.11-3.72, p = 0.02). Although the individual studies had contradicting findings, our study revealed no difference in all-cause mortality and the NICU length of stay.

CONCLUSION: Birth weight is an important risk factor for neonatal morbidities. Our review revealed that the lighter twin in BWD pairs is at a significantly lower risk of RDS and need for surfactant. On the contrary, the smaller twin demonstrated a statistically significant higher prevalence of BPD.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • The impact of intrauterine growth restriction on neonatal lung maturation remains controversial, with singleton studies often limited by genetic, maternal, and environmental confounders. Birth weight discordance in twins offers a unique naturally controlled model to isolate the effect of growth restriction on respiratory outcomes.

WHAT IS NEW: • In birth weight discordant twins, the lighter co-twin faces a significantly lower risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) and a lesser requirement for surfactant administration. Conversely, this risk profile reverses for chronic lung disease, where the smaller growth-restricted twin exhibits a significantly higher incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD).

articles.title: Cardiogenic shock phenotypes and outcomes under percutaneous left ventricular support: results from a 9-year single-center real-world cohort.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Refractory cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with unacceptably high mortality despite advances in intensive-care and coronary intervention strategies. Percutaneous left ventricular support using Impella is widely used, yet real-world outcomes may differ substantially by underlying shock etiology and phenotype.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of adults treated with Impella 2.5/CP for refractory CS over a 9-year period. Patients were classified as acute coronary syndrome (ACS), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)/myocarditis, severe aortic stenosis (AS), sepsis-associated CS, or other causes. Endpoints were all-cause in-hospital and 12-month mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, lactate, vasoactive score, Impella type was conducted; a sensitivity model additionally included creatinine.

RESULTS: Among 409 patients (mean age 69.99 ± 11.56 years; 75.6% male), ACS was the leading phenotype (n = 269), followed by DCM/myocarditis (n = 53), AS (n = 32), sepsis-associated CS (n = 36), and other causes (n = 19). Impella CP was used in 227 patients (55.5%). Overall in-hospital mortality was 48.9% and differed across phenotypes, being highest in sepsis-associated CS (80.6%; chi-squared p < 0.001). Sepsis remained independently associated with in-hospital death after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 4.65, 95% CI 2.03-12.07, p = 0.0006) for major confounders; finding was consistent after additional adjustment for creatinine (adjusted odds ratio 4.17, 95% CI 1.63-12.26, p = 0.0023). Major bleeding occurred in 14.9%, limb ischemia in 11.7%, pseudoaneurysm in 4.9%, and stroke in 1.0% of the patients. Twelve-month survival analysis also demonstrated phenotype-dependent patterns (log-rank p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: In refractory CS treated with Impella outcomes are strongly phenotype-dependent. Sepsis-associated CS represents an extreme-risk phenotype with poor short- and long-term survival, suggesting phenotype-guided patient selection and prospective validation of escalation strategies.

articles.title: [Social inequalities in allergic diseases].
articles.abstract: Allergies and allergic diseases represent a major public health challenge due to their high prevalence, their impact on quality of life and disease burden, and their socioeconomic relevance. This also raises the question of social inequalities in the occurrence and health consequences of allergic diseases. While an inverse social gradient is frequently reported for allergies overall, analyses of individual allergic diseases reveal more nuanced associations across different dimensions of social inequality. The aim of this article is to synthesize the current evidence on social differences in asthma, allergic rhinitis, food allergies, and atopic dermatitis. In addition, possible explanations for the observed social and health inequalities as well as implications for future research are discussed.

articles.title: Management and outcomes of Candida periprosthetic joint infections in a referral center.
articles.abstract: Candida periprosthetic joint infections (cPJI) remain poorly characterized, with limited data on antifungal management, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), surgery, and outcomes. We described a cohort of cPJI, focusing on prosthetic history, microbiology, treatment, and outcome. We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study at the Lyon referral center for complex bone and joint infection. Adult patients managed between 2017 and 2024 were eligible. cPJI was classified using the 2021 EBJIS definition. Outcomes were assessed at 1, 3, and 12 months, and at end of follow-up. Baseline characteristics associated with cPJI were compared to bacterial-only PJI. Thirty-one patients were included. The median number of the infected prosthesis at the same joint site was 2, and 29/31 (93.5%) had previous bacterial infection. Candida parapsilosis was the most frequent species (13/31, 41.9%). Thirty patients (96.8%) received systemic antifungal therapy, and 15 (50%) received suppressive therapy. TDM was performed in 26/31 patients (83.9%). At end of follow-up, infection control was observed in 23/31 patients (74.1%). Compared with 795 bacterial-only PJI, cPJI were associated with higher infected prosthesis number. cPJI occurred in patients with complex prosthetic histories. Most patients achieved infection control through management combining systemic antifungal therapy, surgery, and TDM-guided follow-up.

articles.title: From antidiuretics to anti-virulence: Repurposing chlorothiazide to reduce Pseudomonas aeruginosa virulence and enhance antibiotic effects.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa necessitates novel therapeutic strategies. This study aims to identify clinically approved drugs that can be repurposed as quorum sensing (QS) inhibitors to attenuate bacterial virulence and enhance antibiotic efficacy.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Through virtual molecular docking against LasR, RhlR, and PqsR receptors, we identified chlorothiazide (CTZ) as a multi-target QS inhibitor. Phenotypic assays showed that CTZ significantly inhibited biofilm formation, pyocyanin production, extracellular protease activity, and motility in P. aeruginosa without affecting bacterial growth. Mechanistic studies using exogenous signal restoration, qPCR, and signal-deficient mutants confirmed that CTZ directly interferes with the Las, Rhl, and Pqs QS systems. CTZ also exhibited synergistic antibacterial activity with polymyxin B in vitro, reducing its MIC against multiple clinical isolates. In vivo, CTZ protected Caenorhabditis elegans from P. aeruginosa infection and, when combined with subtherapeutic polymyxin B, significantly improved survival and reduced bacterial load in a mouse acute pulmonary infection model.

CONCLUSIONS: CTZ functions as a promising anti-virulence adjuvant that potentiates conventional antibiotics, offering a dual strategy to improve treatment efficacy while mitigating resistance development.

articles.title: Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Epigenetic Changes and p16-Mediated Senescence in Vascular Dysfunction in Male Mice.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVES: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a pervasive cardiovascular risk factor linked to accelerated aging. We investigated the underlying tissue-specific and systemic epigenetic mechanisms and the role of cellular senescence in the pathophysiology of OSA and associated cardiovascular disease (CVD).

METHODS: C57BL/6J male mice were exposed to intermittent hypoxia (IH) or room air (RA) (n=25 mice/group) for 7 to 210 days. DNA methylation profiling was conducted on left cardiac ventricle and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and the impact of IH duration was studied using regression models. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was calculated using a multi-tissue epigenetic clock. The role of p16-mediated senescence in IH-induced vascular dysfunction was assessed using transgenic mouse models (n=8 mice/group).

RESULTS: IH exposures increased blood pressure and altered endothelial function in male mice. IH/RA differentially methylated positions (DMPs) were identified in left cardiac ventricle (n=5,747) and PBMCs (n=1,307), with minimal overlap (n=163, p=8.03 x 10-8). Both tissues differed in the EAA trajectory throughout the exposures. Epigenetic changes linked to cardiac dysfunction and cellular senescence, highlighting the Cdkn2a gene (encoding the p16 protein, a marker of cellular senescence). p16 expression was increased in aortic endothelial cells following IH. Systemic ablation of p16-expressing cells reversed IH-induced hypertension and restored coronary flow reserve.

CONCLUSIONS: IH induces duration-dependent, tissue-specific epigenetic dysregulation and accelerated biological aging with p16-mediated cellular senescence as a primary driver. Targeting the senescent endothelium can revert OSA-induced vascular dysfunction, thereby establishing a novel mechanistic framework for cellular senescence as a therapeutic target in OSA.

articles.title: Tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement of ANCA-associated vasculitis: A diagnostic challenge mimicking infective endocarditis.
articles.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) are small-vessel vasculitides with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Cardiac valvular involvement is rare and may closely mimic infective endocarditis, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Tricuspid valve involvement, especially at the subvalvular apparatus, is particularly uncommon. We report a case of a 46-year-old man who presented with constitutional symptoms, pulmonary nodules with cavitation, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and positive c-ANCA with anti-proteinase-3 antibodies. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a serpiginous vegetation attached to the tricuspid subvalvular apparatus, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, extensive infectious evaluation, including multiple blood cultures, was negative. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune crescentic and necrotizing glomerulonephritis, supporting a diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Antibiotics were discontinued, and the patient was treated with glucocorticoids, rituximab, and avacopan, resulting in marked clinical improvement. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the subvalvular apparatus vegetation without surgical intervention. This case highlights a rare presentation of GPA with tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement and underscores the importance of distinguishing AAV-related endocardial disease from infective endocarditis. Histopathologic findings, particularly renal biopsy, can be critical in establishing the correct diagnosis. Recognition of this entity is essential, as appropriate immunosuppressive therapy may lead to resolution of valvular lesions and avoidance of unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or surgical intervention.

articles.title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata.

METHODS: Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5).

RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46).

CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

articles.title: Long-Term Milrinone as a Bridge to Recovery in Fontan-Associated Protein-Losing Enteropathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protein-losing enteropathy (PLE) occurs in 5% to 18% of post-Fontan palliation patients with a historical mortality rate of 50%. Treatment of PLE continues to be challenging because of limited understanding of its pathophysiology.

CASE SUMMARY: A 14-year-old boy with double outlet right ventricle and left ventricular hypoplasia with an extracardiac Fontan developed refractory PLE. He was started on long-term, outpatient milrinone at 0.5 μg/kg/min. Over 15 months, ventricular function improved and PLE resolved. Recovery was sustained 8 months after milrinone discontinuation.

DISCUSSION: Milrinone's augmentation of cardiac output and reduction in pulmonary vascular resistance may directly address PLE physiology. Long-term milrinone therapy has primarily been studied as a bridge to transplant. Notably, this case highlights milrinone's use as a bridge to recovery. The 15-month duration of milrinone was safe without adverse outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Long-term outpatient milrinone therapy may serve as a bridge to recovery in patients with refractory Fontan-associated PLE.

articles.title: ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Chronic Liver Disease: 2026 Update.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease, caused by a range of etiologies, can lead to progressive liver function deterioration, hepatic fibrosis, cirrhosis, and, ultimately, end-stage liver disease. With cirrhosis and end-stage liver disease, complications include portal hypertension, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, refractory ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and primary hepatocellular carcinoma. Imaging plays an important role in the diagnosis, treatment response assessment, and surveillance of chronic liver disease, specifically of hepatic hemochromatosis, steatosis, and fibrosis, in an effort to prevent progression to cirrhosis. This document reviews the imaging modalities best suited for these clinical scenarios, and a summary of current evidence is provided to support the use of various modalities for each of the clinical contexts. The American College of Radiology Appropriateness Criteria are evidence-based guidelines for specific clinical conditions that are reviewed annually by a multidisciplinary expert panel. The guideline development and revision include an extensive analysis of current medical literature from peer reviewed journals and the application of well-established methodologies (RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation or GRADE) to rate the appropriateness of imaging and treatment procedures for specific clinical scenarios. In those instances where evidence is lacking or equivocal, expert opinion may supplement the available evidence to recommend imaging or treatment.

articles.title: Recurrence of eosinophilic pneumonia after switching from mepolizumab to tezepelumab for worsening asthma in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
articles.abstract: A 50-year-old woman with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis had maintained glucocorticoid-free remission for approximately four years with mepolizumab monotherapy. Because asthma control gradually deteriorated despite sustained control of systemic disease, mepolizumab was replaced with tezepelumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin. Asthma symptoms improved rapidly, and fractional exhaled nitric oxide levels decreased. However, peripheral blood eosinophil counts progressively increased, and computed tomography approximately six months after the switch demonstrated recurrent eosinophilic pneumonia, with pulmonary consolidations closely resembling those at the initial presentation. Prednisolone and mepolizumab were reintroduced, resulting in rapid resolution of eosinophilia and pulmonary infiltrates. Glucocorticoids were subsequently discontinued again without recurrence. This case suggests that improvement in airway symptoms after biologic switching does not necessarily indicate adequate suppression of systemic eosinophilic inflammation. Even after prolonged glucocorticoid-free remission, replacement of interleukin-5-targeted therapy with thymic stromal lymphopoietin inhibition may permit recurrence of eosinophilic disease. Peripheral blood eosinophil counts and systemic manifestations should therefore be carefully monitored after such switching in patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

articles.title: Salmonella enterica strains differ in the effect of AcrABZ-TolC mutation on cell motility and susceptibility to bacteriophage Chi.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The rise in multidrug-resistant pathogenic bacteria has renewed interest in phage therapy. The lytic phage Chi is a broad host-range phage infecting Salmonella enterica, Escherichia coli, and Serratia marcescens. Chi belongs to the group of flagellotropic phages, which require a rotating flagellum to infect host cells. We previously reported that mutations in genes encoding components of the AcrABZ-TolC efflux pump greatly reduce Chi infection of S. enterica Typhimurium strain 14028S (serotype Typhimurium [STM] 14028S). Here, we tested and rejected the hypothesis that the AcrABZ-TolC complex is the cell-surface receptor for Chi. First, STM 14028S mutants with an inactivating point mutation in the AcrB pump displayed decreased susceptibility to Chi. Second, STM 14028S mutants of individual AcrABZ-TolC components showed reduced motility on nutrient soft agar, and a ∆acrAB-tolC mutant exhibited an over 80% reduction in the number of motile cells. Together, these results suggest that Chi phage resistance may be mediated by an effect on motility rather than by loss of a cell surface receptor. Additionally, deletions of acrA, acrB, and tolC in another Typhimurium strain, STM 4/74, and two other serotypes, Choleraesuis and Poona, retained susceptibility to Chi and had no apparent motility defects. Taken together, mutations in the AcrABZ-TolC pump caused reduced motility and, thereby, Chi infection in STM 14028S, but not in other tested strains. These results suggest that this pump is not a cell surface receptor for Chi.

IMPORTANCE: Phage therapy is of rising importance for combating antibiotic-resistant pathogens. Particularly, phages targeting structures important for virulence are of interest as they present an exploitable evolutionary tradeoff, as bacteria will likely lose virulence to become resistant to the phage. We previously reported that in Salmonella enterica Typhimurium strain 14028S, the AcrABZ-TolC efflux pump, an important virulence factor, was also required for infection by the flagellotropic phage Chi. We report here that this requirement for Chi infection is due to reduced motility of mutants, rather than AcrABZ-TolC being the cell-surface receptor. The reduction in motility caused by AcrABZ-TolC mutations in strain 14028S is not conserved across other strains and S. enterica serotypes, including Poona and Choleraesuis.

articles.title: Anoxia selects for high-fitness biofilms and reduces antibiotic susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Antibiotic resistance is a growing global health crisis, yet resistance is almost exclusively quantified under aerobic laboratory conditions that fail to reflect the complex microenvironments bacteria encounter during infection. Many clinically important infection sites, such as airways of individuals with cystic fibrosis or chronic wounds, are microaerobic to anoxic. To address this, we investigated how anoxia alters antibiotic resistance determinants, hypothesizing that anaerobic metabolism might change the fitness effects and selection of resistance mutations. We used experimental evolution to propagate Pseudomonas aeruginosa populations for approximately 200 generations under conditions differing in oxygen availability (oxic vs anoxic), growth mode (biofilm vs planktonic), and tobramycin exposure (subinhibitory increasing to inhibitory concentrations). Subinhibitory exposure reduced susceptibility to tobramycin by 2×-4× compared to ancestral levels, with anoxic populations consistently having higher minimum inhibitory concentrations than oxic populations. Mutations in fusA1 and ptsP arose across all conditions, but mutations in amgS were only selected in oxic populations-indicating condition-specific mutations in response to antibiotics. Notably, mexT mutations were observed in anoxic or tobramycin-exposed populations. Anoxic populations exhibited significantly increased biofilm formation, reduced twitching motility driven by type IV pilus gene mutations, and greater competitive fitness. Together, these findings demonstrate that oxygen availability shapes the response to antibiotics in P. aeruginosa, with the anoxic environment selecting for reduced antibiotic susceptibility, higher fitness, and high biofilm-forming phenotypes.

IMPORTANCE: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen capable of acute and chronic infections that develop antibiotic resistance. One aspect of P. aeruginosa that makes it so challenging to treat is its metabolic versatility. We wanted to understand how growth in different infection-relevant conditions, specifically anoxia and surface attachment, would alter the evolutionary pathways of antibiotic resistance. We found that the mutations causing reduced antibiotic susceptibility to the commonly used antibiotic tobramycin were condition dependent. We also observed that adaptation to anoxia resulted in P. aeruginosa populations that had high biofilm-forming capacity and were highly fit compared to their ancestors. This indicates that anoxic infection environments can lead to P. aeruginosa variants with increased resistance, increased recalcitrance, and potentially more virulence.

articles.title: FDA-Authorized AI/ML Tool for Sepsis Prediction: Development and Validation.
Cardiac Function Profiling of Preeclamptic Patients by Impedance Cardiography.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is associated with cardiac dysfunction during pregnancy and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Although thoracic fluid content (TFC) is increased in preeclampsia, its relationship to cardiac performance remains unclear. This study used impedance cardiography to characterize maternal hemodynamics and to evaluate the associations among TFC, cardiac performance, and disease severity. A retrospective analysis included 645 pregnant women, comprising 128 normotensive controls, 170 women with moderate preeclampsia, and 347 with severe preeclampsia. Thoracic fluid content increased progressively across preeclampsia severity groups. Stroke volume index and cardiac index were lower, while systemic vascular resistance index was higher, primarily in women with severe preeclampsia. Correlation analysis demonstrated an inverse association between stroke volume index and systemic vascular resistance index, whereas associations between thoracic fluid content and other hemodynamic measures were comparatively weak. These findings suggest that increased thoracic fluid content in preeclampsia is not strongly explained by variations in systemic vascular resistance or indexed cardiac output and stroke volume alone.

articles.title: Lessons From a Trial of Best Case/Worst Case Communication Tool in Older Adults With Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society

articles.title: Redefining glucose thresholds for hypoglycaemia management in children and young adults with type 1 diabetes on automated insulin therapy: A cross-over clinical trial protocol.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Current international guidelines for hypoglycaemia management in Type 1 diabetes recommend initiating treatment when glucose level falls below 3.9 mmol/L. However, these recommendations were developed before widespread use of diabetes technologies. This study aims to determine whether a revised hypoglycaemia treatment approach incorporating a lower treatment threshold is non-inferior to the standard threshold (<3.9 mmol/L) in children and young adults with Type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery (AID) systems. We hypothesise that the revised approach will be non-inferior to the current standard recommendations without increasing time in clinically significant hypoglycaemia.

METHODS: This single-centre, randomised, two-period, crossover, non-inferiority trial will recruit 45 participants aged 6-25 years with Type 1 diabetes, diagnosed for at least 12 months and using AID systems. Participants will complete two 4-week treatment periods in random order: standard hypoglycaemia treatment (<3.9 mmol/L) and revised hypoglycaemia treatment (≤3.6 mmol/L with consideration of CGM trends, active insulin, exercise and symptoms). Treatment periods will be separated by a 2-week washout period. The primary outcome is the percentage of time spent in clinically significant hypoglycaemia (<3.0 mmol/L), measured using CGM. Secondary outcomes are CGM metrics including time in range and time above range, along with participant acceptability of the revised treatment approach.

CONCLUSION: This study will provide prospective evidence on whether a revised hypoglycaemia treatment approach can safely reduce the glucose threshold for treatment in children and young adults using AID systems. Findings may inform future recommendations for hypoglycaemia management in the era of diabetes technologies.

articles.title: Loneliness, social isolation and all-cause mortality among 7712 individuals with type 2 diabetes: a 5.9-year Danish population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The significance of social factors in influencing health outcomes is increasingly recognised in diabetes care. However, the health-related consequences of loneliness and social isolation among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remain understudied. This study examined whether loneliness and social isolation are associated with higher mortality rates in individuals with T2DM. In addition, we examined variations by sex and age, and the synergistic impact of loneliness and social isolation on mortality rates.

METHODS: We conducted a cohort study using data on loneliness and social isolation from the 2017 Danish National Health Survey (n = 129,319). T2DM was identified in 7712 individuals using a register-based diabetes classifier, and these individuals were followed for 5.9 years. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for sociodemographic factors and baseline health were applied to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among individuals with T2DM, 9.5% were lonely, and 8.2% were socially isolated. Loneliness (HR = 1.32, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.07, 1.65) and social isolation (HR = 1.35, 95% CI = 1.07, 1.71) were associated with higher mortality rates. Joint exposure to loneliness and social isolation was associated with an HR of 1.70 (95% CI = 1.21, 2.39). Social isolation was associated with higher mortality rates in men (HR = 1.54, 95% CI = 1.17, 2.04) but not in women (HR = 1.10, 95% CI = 0.75, 1.61). Elevated effect sizes were observed among adults aged 75+ years (loneliness: HR = 1.43 (95% CI = 1.09, 1.87); social isolation: HR = 1.47 (95% CI = 1.09, 1.97)).

CONCLUSION: Loneliness and social isolation are associated with increased mortality in individuals with T2DM. Social isolation is particularly detrimental for men, and risks are heightened in older adults. Incorporating assessment of social disconnection into diabetes care may help identify vulnerable groups and inform targeted interventions to reduce premature mortality.

articles.title: Developing a fluorescent derivative of GagPol as a tool for live-cell imaging of HIV-1 assembly.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The HIV-1 assembly process is driven by the structural polyprotein Gag, which forms small cytosolic oligomers that traffic to the plasma membrane. While Gag alone is sufficient to drive particle formation, the incorporation of GagPol, a polyprotein comprising Gag and viral enzymes, is essential for productive infection. Maintenance of the proper Gag:GagPol ratio is crucial for virion infectivity. Yet, the mechanisms regulating their cytosolic interactions remain incompletely understood, in part because most studies rely on ensemble biochemical assays that hide cell-to-cell heterogeneity and lack spatial and temporal resolution. To overcome these limitations and investigate the dynamics of GagPol at the molecular level, we systematically tested different approaches to fluorescently label it. We successfully produced two functional fluorescent GagPol variants: one single-labeled GagPol and a second double-labeled variant with a fluorescent protein added within Gag, which allows concurrent visualization of Gag and GagPol. These labeled versions, in combination with the use of raster image (cross-)correlation spectroscopy, enabled the quantification of Gag and GagPol relative concentrations and intermolecular interactions at the single-cell level. Overall, these variants set the stage for in-depth investigations of GagPol during HIV assembly, providing insights into cytoplasmic trafficking, particle assembly, and the kinetics of these processes.

IMPORTANCE: The participation of Gag and GagPol in HIV-1 assembly is central to the generation of infectious virions. While the structural role of Gag and the enzymatic functions of GagPol are well described, little is known regarding the mechanisms underlying their cytosolic interactions, spatial organization, and relative incorporation into assembling particles. Here, we successfully developed two stable fluorescently labeled variants of GagPol: a single-labeled variant with a label in the Pol domain and a double-labeled construct in which the Gag domain is also tagged. Using these constructs, we can quantitatively investigate Gag and GagPol interactions at the single-cell level. Hence, they provide a framework for a comprehensive study of the oligomerization properties and trafficking of these polyproteins at different stages of HIV-1 assembly, including membrane recruitment and incorporation into nascent virions.

articles.title: Serum Renin As a Prognostic Biomarker in Children With Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) derangement contributes to acute kidney injury (AKI) and is associated with poor outcomes in critical illness. Serum renin, a clinically available biomarker of RAAS derangement, is associated with poor outcomes in critically ill adults and children. Renin has not been evaluated in children with sepsis-associated AKI (SA-AKI), either alone or in combination with other prognostic enrichment tools, including the recently derived pediatric sepsis-associated AKI (pSAKI) subphenotypes.

DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a multicenter, prospective, observational study of pediatric septic shock.

SETTING: Ten U.S. PICUs from January 2002 to February 2025.

PATIENTS: Patients 0-18 years old with early SA-AKI (serum creatinine-based Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 1-3 on days 1-2 of admission) with residual day 1 serum available for renin measurement.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Seven hundred eight patients were examined by renin tertiles. The highest renin tertile cohort (T3, > 247 pg/mL) had one fewer severe AKI-free day (4 [0-6] vs. 5 [1-7] T2 vs. 5 [2-7] T1; p < 0.001), higher day 7 severe AKI rates (47% vs. 32% vs. 27%; p < 0.001), fewer PICU-free days, and higher 28-day mortality rates. In multivariate analysis incorporating markers of illness severity, including age, T3 was independently associated with fewer severe AKI-free days (β = -0.5; se = 0.2; p = 0.01), fewer PICU-free days, and higher adjusted odds of day 7 severe AKI and 28-day mortality. Patients were assigned to either the pSAKI-1 or pSAKI-2 subphenotype to assess for additional enrichment. T3 patients had uniformly worse outcomes among the less severe pSAKI-1 subphenotype but not among pSAKI-2 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Worsening RAAS derangement, as evidenced by increasing renin concentrations, is associated with worse outcomes in children with SA-AKI. Serum renin may provide clinically useful prognostic enrichment in this population, both alone and in combination with the pSAKI subphenotypes.

articles.title: Residents' Ventilator Management Performance in an Online Pediatric Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Case Scenario: Secondary Analysis of the Game-Based Education in Residency Study, 2015-2017.
authors: Game-based Education in Residency (GamER) Study Group
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate resident performance in an online pediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) case scenario of mild/moderate severity, with the provision of individualized feedback.

DESIGN: A secondary analysis of the Game-based Education in Residency study.

SETTING: The dataset comprised residents in their first clinical rotation in any of 28 international PICUs, recruited between October 2015 and December 2017.

SUBJECTS: Residents who used the online mechanical ventilation (MV) simulator and completed PARDS tasks were included in the analysis.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: The simulated MV parameters analyzed among 125 residents were positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), Fio2, tidal volume (Vt), peak inspiratory pressure (PIP), Pao2, and pH. Residents' MV selections in relation to recommended scoring goals were: median (interquartile range [IQR]) PEEP, below or in the lower range (8 cm H2O [IQR, 7-8 cm H2O]); median Fio2, above or in the higher range (60% [IQR, 51-60%]); and median Vt, within range (5.36 mL/kg [IQR, 4.98-5.73 mL/kg]). Residents had higher than recommended median Pao2 (93 mm Hg [IQR, 83-99 mm Hg]), pH (7.37 [IQR, 7.33-7.40]), and median PIP (30 cm H2O [IQR, 28-31 cm H2O]). Progress through the case scenario was associated with greater odds (odds ratio [OR] and 95% CI) of adherence to goals in PEEP, Fio2, and Vt: PEEP (OR, 2.68; 95% CI, 1.65-4.34; p < 0.001); Fio2 (OR, 2.48; 95% CI, 1.29-4.76; p = 0.007); and Vt (OR, 2.66; 95% CI, 1.11-6.38; p = 0.028).

CONCLUSIONS: In an international PICU residents' educational dataset from 2015 to 2017, we found that progression through the simulated PARDS case was associated with greater odds of adherence to PEEP, Fio2, and Vt goals, which suggests that repeated practice and individualized feedback were of benefit. However, residents did not wean Fio2 or MV parameters when Pao2 and pH were above goal. These results may help educators design contemporary MV teaching.

articles.title: Long-Term Neurologic Complication and Healthcare Burden in Infants Receiving Extracorporeal Life Support: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate survival, neurologic complications, and healthcare burden in infant extracorporeal life support (ECLS) recipients using nationally representative administrative data from a single-payer healthcare system.

DESIGN: Retrospective, population-based cohort study.

SETTING: South Korea's National Health Insurance Service, covering 97% of the population.

PATIENTS: Infants under 1 year who received ECLS between 2009 and 2022.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Of 698 infants who underwent ECLS, 212 infants (30.4%) survived during follow-up (estimated 1-yr mortality: 67.1%). Among survivors, 128 (60.4%) developed neurologic injuries, including acute events such as ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (HIBI), as well as long-term sequelae such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, hearing loss, and developmental delay. Most acute neurologic injuries were diagnosed within the first year, whereas developmental delay showed prolonged diagnostic windows extending up to 12 years. Survivors with neurologic injury had significantly longer hospital stays (432.1 vs. 182.3 d; p < 0.001) and higher cumulative healthcare costs during long-term follow-up. Median index hospitalization costs were USD 36,000-37,000. The burden analysis showed distinct profiles across neurologic complications: developmental delay was the most prevalent sequela, whereas HIBI was associated with the highest cumulative healthcare cost despite lower prevalence.

CONCLUSIONS: Neurologic complications following ECLS in infants are common and impose substantial long-term healthcare burden. These findings highlight the need for early risk stratification, structured neurologic and neurodevelopmental monitoring, and sustained rehabilitation planning in this high-risk population. This study provides a foundation for international benchmarking and health policy planning in pediatric critical care.

articles.title: Clinical Factors Associated With Physical Restraint Use in Critically Ill Children: A Secondary Analysis of the PICU Up! Pilot Trial, 2019-2020.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify clinical factors associated with physical restraint use in critically ill children.

DESIGN: This is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected observational daily data from the baseline (preintervention) phase of the PICU Up! multicenter stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial (NCT03860168). The analytic dataset represents a shared subset of the larger parent study population.

SETTING: Six PICUs in the United States, from May 2019 to March 2020.

PATIENTS: A total of 1153 patients younger than 18 years admitted to a PICU for 3 or more days.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Children younger than 18 years old admitted for 3 or more consecutive PICU days were included. Daily data on sedation level, medication exposure, device use, and restraint status were collected, and multivariable generalized estimating equation models were used to evaluate associated factors. Physical restraints were used in 216 patients (18.7%) and 1,043 of 11,491 patient-days (9.07%), with a median duration of 3 days (interquartile range, 2-5). In multivariable analysis, the strongest predictor of restraint use was previous-day restraint (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 22.79; 95% CI, 16.72-31.07). Other significant factors included age 3-17 years vs. 0-2 years (aOR, 2.46-2.69), mechanical ventilation (aOR, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.39-6.38), benzodiazepine use (aOR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.05-2.10), and opioid use (aOR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.42-2.78). Light sedation (State Behavioral Scale [SBS] -1) was associated with restraint use compared with calm/alert status (SBS 0; aOR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.24-2.37), while agitation (SBS > 0) showed no association (SBS 1 [aOR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.52-1.80] and SBS 2 [aOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.47-2.54]). Invasive devices were associated with increased restraint use (p < 0.001). Notably, 51 patients (12.5%) of 407 patients receiving neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA) remained restrained, and 30 patients were restrained on the day of ICU discharge.

CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to previous reports linking agitation to restraint use, agitation (SBS > 0) was not associated with restraint use; only light sedation (SBS -1) was associated with increased odds of being restrained. Previous-day restraint use was the strongest predictor of continued restraint, highlighting persistence of previous-day practices with limited reassessment. The presence of restraints during periods of NMBA administration and at discharge days further suggests the need for improved reevaluation practices.

articles.title: Physiological Impact of Chest Wall Closure in Infants Post-Cardiac Surgery. Implications for Mechanical Ventilation.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the effect of delayed sternal closure post-cardiac surgery on respiratory system mechanics and hemodynamics.

DESIGN: Prospective single-center physiologic study.

SETTING: Cardiac PICU.

PATIENTS: Infants (< 1 yr old) with delayed sternal closure post-cardiopulmonary bypass for correction or palliation of a congenital heart disease.

INTERVENTIONS: Four ventilation conditions were studied: 1) baseline: positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) 5 cm H2O and low tidal volume (Vt; 6-7 mL/kg); 2) PEEP 5, high Vt (9-10 mL/kg); 3) PEEP 3, low Vt; and 4) PEEP 8, low Vt. Respiratory rate was adjusted to end-tidal carbon dioxide. Measurements were repeated after sternal closure.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Esophageal pressure (Pes), transpulmonary pressure (PL), normalized respiratory system elastance (Ers) in cm H2O/(mL/kg), and hemodynamics, including transmural pressures, were obtained before and after sternal closure. The open-sternum model used assumes that the chest wall maintains a vertical pleural pressure gradient, with the most nondependent lung exposed to atmospheric pressure. A nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O was used as a marker of overdistention, and end-expiratory PL 0-2 cm H2O was considered to prevent collapse. Ten patients were included: median (interquartile range) age 32 days (18-50 d) and weight 3.1 kg (3.0-3.5 kg). Chest closure increased Pes in all conditions and Ers in most conditions, except for PEEP 8 low Vt. Chest closure reduced expiratory PL in all conditions, at baseline from -0.5 cm H2O (-1.2 to -0.1 cm H2O) to -2.5 cm H2O (-3.1 to -1.8 cm H2O).
