Sternal closure impacted nondependent inspiratory PL differently depending on the ventilator settings. High Vt was the condition more frequently associated with high nondependent inspiratory PL greater than 23 cm H2O. Blood pressure was maintained with fluids or vasopressors. Central venous pressure increased after closure, but the transmural filling pressure remained unchanged.

CONCLUSIONS: Infants with delayed sternal closure exhibited elevated Pes and Ers after chest wall closure. Under the model assumptions, during the open-chest phase, high Vt was more frequently associated with high nondependent PL, suggesting overdistention. Sternal closure made expiratory PL more negative. These findings suggest that individualized PEEP and Vt adjustments guided by Pes could be considered to help preserve expiratory PL and minimize the risk of overdistension before and after chest closure.

articles.title: Prevalence and Characteristics of Coma in Latin American Critical Care Units: The COMA LATAM Study.
authors: and members of the Coma in Latin America (COMA LATAM) group, on behalf of the Latin American Brain Injury Consortium (LABIC) and the Curing Coma Campaign
Colombia and Costa Rica and Cuba and Dominican Republic and Ecuador and El Salvador and Guatemala and Honduras and Mexico and Panama and Paraguay and Peru and Puerto Rico and Uruguay and Venezuela
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the point prevalence of coma across Latin American critical care units, characterize its etiology, and explore short-term outcomes.

DESIGN: Multinational, cross-sectional point prevalence study with exploratory 14-day follow-up assessment.

SETTING: Three hundred ninety-two hospitals across 19 Latin American countries, including ICUs, intermediate care units, neurocritical care units, cardiovascular ICUs, and trauma ICUs.

PATIENTS: Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) meeting the Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy care survey (COME-TOGETHER) criteria on May 28, 2024. Patients under deep sedation or pharmacological coma induction were excluded unless the coma state preceded pharmacological intervention.

INTERVENTIONS: None (observational study).

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 8305 critically ill patients, 1145 met coma criteria (point prevalence 13.8%), with country-specific rates ranging from 5.1% to 36.8%. Individual patient data were available for 729 patients (63.7%). Traumatic brain injury was the leading individual cause (24.8%), followed by hypoxic-anoxic brain injury (14.6%) and intracerebral hemorrhage (13.5%). When categorized by pathophysiology, vascular causes predominated (48.6%), followed by traumatic brain injury (24.8%) and other causes (26.6%). Age-stratified analysis revealed trauma predominantly affecting younger patients, while cerebrovascular causes predominated in older groups. Among patients with 14-day follow-up data (29% of cohort), mortality was 29.2%, with 67.7% of survivors recovering from coma. Only the Charlson Comorbidity Index was independently associated with implementation of life-sustaining therapy limitations (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Coma affects nearly one in seven ICU beds across Latin America, with substantial country variation and distinct age-dependent etiology patterns. The significant burden highlights the need for targeted prevention strategies and specialized neurocritical care resources throughout the region.

articles.title: The Current State of Ventilator Liberation Practices and Outcomes in the United States-A Report From the Ventilator Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative.
articles.journal: Pediatric critical care medicine : a journal of the Society of Critical Care Medicine and the World Federation of Pediatric Intensive and Critical Care Societies
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Describe and explore interunit baseline ventilator liberation practices and outcomes related to the 2023 Pediatric Ventilator Liberation Guidelines within the original cohort of Ventilation Liberation For Kids (VentLib4Kids) Collaborative units.

DESIGN: Observational cohort study.

SETTING: Nineteen VentLib4Kids ICUs in the United States (13 general medical/surgical, five cardiovascular, and one mixed).

PATIENTS: First planned extubation attempt where code status allowed reintubation in patients younger than 19 years old, endotracheally intubated for any indication between July 1, 2023, and June 30, 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 2315 ventilator courses were included. Most were 28 days to younger than 6 years old (65.5%) and had a lower respiratory infection diagnosis (23.8%). Prematurity (13.2%) was the most common comorbidity. Spontaneous breathing trial exposure demonstrated the highest guideline concordance at 74.6% (median; interunit range [IUR], 49.6-100%), whereas maximal inspiratory pressure testing was lowest (3.7%; IUR, 0-62.4%). Most courses (55.5%; IUR, 19.8-99%) included an air leak test. Among those without an air leak noted or greater than 25 cmH2O, 70.1% were exposed to dexamethasone in concordance with the guidelines. Initiation of dexamethasone greater than or equal to 6 hours before extubation predominated (81.1%) at a median dose of 0.5 mg/kg/dose in exposed groups. Planned postextubation high-flow nasal cannula (44.3%) and bilevel positive airway pressure (18.6%) were most common. Unit-level use of any planned postextubation noninvasive respiratory support ranged from 20.6% to 100%. Among infants, planned continuous positive airway pressure was used in 6.7% of subjects. Among all courses, 10.4% (IUR, 4.5-19.2%) ended with extubation failure (reintubation within 48 hr).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline VentLib4Kids practices demonstrate varying degrees of concordance with guideline recommendations along with significant interunit variation. These results align with prior international survey data and support the need for structured, multicenter quality improvement and guideline implementation strategies.

articles.title: Privacy and Cybersecurity Guardrails for AI in Healthcare: Consensus-Based Guidance.
articles.journal: The American journal of bioethics : AJOB

articles.title: Non-Typhoidal Salmonellosis Outbreak in Humans Linked to Dry Dog Food, United States, 2023.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Salmonellosis outbreaks affecting humans have infrequently been linked to pet foods or treats, but surveillance of foodborne pathogens in pet foods is important for protecting public health. We describe how surveillance testing of dry dog food resulted in detection of an outbreak of human illnesses caused by Salmonella serotype Kiambu.

METHODS: A state agency isolated Salmonella serotype Kiambu from a bag of Brand A dry dog food purchased at a retail store as part of a US Food and Drug Administration surveillance program. Whole-genome sequencing analysis by core-genome multi-locus sequence typing determined that the isolate detected in pet food was genetically related to Salmonella isolates obtained from ill people. A multistate outbreak investigation was initiated to collect exposure information from patients and to determine measures needed to prevent illnesses.

RESULTS: Seven patients from 7 states were infected with the outbreak strain; 6 of 7 patients were aged ≤1 year. Illness onset dates spanned January 14 to August 19, 2023. Three of 5 patients reported feeding Brand A dry dog food to their dogs. Voluntary recalls were issued for all dog and cat food products produced at the same facility as Brand A. Public communications were issued regarding this outbreak and for the voluntary recalls.

CONCLUSIONS: This outbreak might not have been detected without surveillance testing of pet food products for enteric pathogens. Outbreaks related to dry pet food can be protracted because of the extended shelf life of these products. Enteric pathogens that contaminate pet products can result in infant illness. It is important to educate caregivers about the importance of handwashing after feeding pets and the proper ways to clean and disinfect pet feeding equipment.

articles.title: Spatial and molecular control of HIV-1 assembly and budding.
articles.abstract: Combination antiretroviral therapy has transformed HIV-1 infection into a chronic, manageable condition, yet lifelong treatment remains necessary due to the persistence of latent reservoirs and the continual emergence of drug-resistant variants. Most approved antivirals target early entry or enzymatic steps, leaving the late phase of replication-Gag trafficking, lattice assembly, membrane scission, envelope incorporation, and protease-driven maturation-underexplored as a target for antiviral inhibitors. Recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy, cryo-electron tomography, single-molecule and live-cell imaging, and integrative systems-level approaches reveal that HIV-1 assembly and egress are not linear, virus-autonomous reactions. Instead, they are spatially and temporally coordinated processes embedded within host cellular architecture. Viral RNA scaffolding, plasma membrane composition and curvature, microdomain identity, cytoskeletal dynamics, and endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT)-mediated membrane fission are tightly coupled to Gag lattice formation, establishing regulated checkpoints that vary across cell types and tissue microenvironments. This host-integrated framework reframes HIV-1 morphogenesis as a systems-level process and highlights structurally constrained, host-dependent nodes as promising targets for next-generation antiviral strategies.

articles.title: Persistent Fungal Mortality in the United States Following the COVID-19 Pandemic Peak, 2022-2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Fungal infection-associated deaths increased in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic, but mortality patterns after the pandemic peak are not well-characterized. We analyzed national mortality data to assess whether fungal mortality remained elevated during 2022-2025 and to describe demographic, geographic, pathogen-specific, and underlying cause-of-death patterns after the COVID-19 pandemic peak.

METHODS: We analyzed National Vital Statistics System multiple-cause-of-death data for 2022-2025. We defined fungal deaths as deaths with a fungal pathogen listed as an underlying or contributing cause of death and summarized deaths by year, month, pathogen, COVID-19 association, underlying cause of death, demographic characteristics, and US Census division. We used 2018-2019 (prepandemic) and 2021 (peak) as reference periods for selected comparisons.

RESULTS: During 2022-2025, a total of 30 225 fungal deaths occurred (annual average = 7556). The annual age-adjusted mortality rate per 100 000 population increased from 1.2 in 2018-2019 to 1.5 in 2020 and 1.9 in 2021, and remained between 1.8 and 1.9 during 2022-2025. COVID-19-associated fungal deaths declined after early 2022, but overall fungal mortality remained stable. During 2022-2025, the most common underlying causes of death among fungal deaths were malignant neoplasms, HIV disease, and diseases of the heart; the most commonly specified pathogens were Candida and Aspergillus. Mortality rates varied by age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region.

CONCLUSIONS: Fungal mortality remained elevated after the COVID-19 pandemic peak despite declines in COVID-19-associated fungal deaths. Continued efforts to monitor fungal disease-related mortality are important to inform efforts to enhance diagnostic capacity and surveillance to better characterize and ultimately reduce the impact of fungal diseases.

articles.title: Modulating Platelet Reactivity with GLP-1RAs in Diabetes: Mechanistic Insights, Potential Benefits, and Clinical Limitations in Atherothrombotic Prevention.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have redefined cardiovascular medicine, reducing major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) through pleiotropic mechanisms that transcend glycemic and weight control. While their cardioprotective benefits are well-established, their direct impact on platelet activity-a key driver of atherothrombotic risk-remains a compelling frontier. This narrative review first addresses the heightened atherothrombotic risk characteristic of patients with diabetes and the clinical challenges posed by their suboptimal response to standard antiplatelet regimens. Subsequently, it explores experimental evidence on the antiplatelet properties of GLP-1RAs. Mechanistically, GLP-1RAs exert a dual inhibitory action: direct modulation involves the activation of platelet-surface GLP-1 receptors, triggering the PKA signaling cascade and VASP phosphorylation, which in turn suppresses calcium mobilization and aggregation. Indirectly, these agents restore vascular health by enhancing nitric oxide bioavailability, preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity, and shifting perivascular adipose tissue toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. Furthermore, GLP-1RAs mitigate the pro-thrombotic milieu by attenuating glycemic variability and systemic inflammatory cascades. However, these compelling experimental findings do not currently translate into clear clinical impact, and a clinical gap persists: while reductions in mortality and stroke risk are firmly established, the specific efficacy of GLP-1RAs in preventing acute coronary events is still evolving. In conclusion, GLP-1RAs emerge as multifaceted tools with significant cardiovascular protection, offering a synergistic approach to secondary prevention in high-risk cardiometabolic patients; however, how these favorable outcomes are mediated by antiplatelet properties warrants dedicated prospective investigations to translate experimental findings into clinical certainty.

articles.title: Consensus Reached: A Delphi Study to Define Public Health Advocacy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Lack of consensus on a definition of public health advocacy is a key barrier to preparing the public health workforce to effect positive health policy changes and equitably improve health outcomes. We identified a consensus definition of public health advocacy.

METHODS: A US-based expert panel participated in a 3-round, e-Delphi process during a 3-month period in late 2024. This panel consisted of public health faculty who regularly teach advocacy in accredited schools and programs of public health (SPPH) and seasoned public health advocates who have successfully improved laws, policies, and government budgets.

RESULTS: The panel reached consensus on a public health advocacy definition and 2 core elements of any public health advocacy definition. Public health advocacy is a set of strategic efforts informed by those with lived experience that influence decision-makers and promote the enactment and effective implementation of equitable policies, systems, and public investments in order to address health inequities and improve public health outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: This study found expert consensus on a public health advocacy definition that could be adopted by SPPH and continuing education providers. Incorporating this definition and related advocacy skills into educational offerings and overall messaging could lead to a better prepared workforce ready to lead and/or participate in policy change campaigns.

articles.title: Receptor specificity and glycocalyx accessibility shape bovine P[1] and P[11] rotavirus infection.
articles.abstract: Viruses initiate infection by engaging receptors within the crowded cell-surface glycocalyx; however, how this environment affects receptor accessibility remains poorly understood. Here, we compared two bovine rotavirus field isolates, P[1] C73 and P[11] HM26, which differ markedly in replication efficiency and early disease kinetics, to examine how VP4-mediated receptor use contributes to these phenotypes. Reverse-genetics experiments identified VP4, particularly its VP8* lectin domain, as a major determinant of the replication difference. C73 recognized sialylated gangliosides, whereas HM26 bound type II precursor glycans. Although HM26 VP8* displayed higher intrinsic affinity for its type II glycan ligand, it bound less efficiently to intact cell surfaces and was associated with lower viral attachment. Neuraminidase treatment increased the detectable accessibility of type II glycans, reduced P[1] infection, and enhanced P[11] infection. Structural modeling and mutational analysis further supported a role for VP8* residue 188 in the glycan-binding phenotype. The Y188T substitution reduced detectable glycan binding, impaired replication in the rBLR/C73VP4 background, and attenuated early infection in neonatal mice. Analysis of human P[1] and P[11] VP8* proteins also revealed an association between the Y/T188 polymorphism and glycan preference in the strains examined. Together, these results indicate that intrinsic VP8* glycan-binding affinity alone does not predict effective receptor use at the intact cell surface. Receptor accessibility within the glycocalyx also contributes to bovine rotavirus attachment and infection.IMPORTANCERotavirus infection begins with specific glycan recognition on the host cell surface; however, receptor presence alone is insufficient to guarantee productive viral engagement. Comparing bovine P[1] and P[11] rotaviruses with distinct glycan preferences reveals that receptor accessibility within the glycocalyx critically dictates viral attachment and subsequent infection. Notably, higher affinity for an isolated glycan fails to confer superior binding efficiency on intact cells. These results demonstrate that the glycocalyx acts as a functional barrier and modulator at the virus-cell interface rather than an inert receptor scaffold, underscoring the role of spatial glycan organization in governing viral entry.

articles.title: Elderly in neurosurgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronological age remains an important factor in neurosurgical decision-making; however, the age threshold used to define patients as "elderly" has varied over time, across geographic regions, and between disease entities. The aim was to examine how author-defined chronological thresholds for elderly populations have evolved in the neurosurgical literature.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: A systematic PubMed review of neurosurgical literature published 1970-2025 was conducted using predefined search terms related to elderly patients. Studies were included only if they provided an explicit numerical chronological threshold defining an "elderly" population. Each publication was treated as a single unit of analysis. Extracted data included publication year, geographic region, disease category, and the author-defined age threshold. Descriptive statistics, temporal trend analyses, and subgroup analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Of 927 screened articles, 408 met the inclusion criteria. The author-defined chronological threshold was mean ± standard deviation 67.5±8.9 years (median: 65 years, range: 34-99 years). Author-defined age thresholds showed an overall upward trend over time. Regional differences were observed, with increasing thresholds in Europe, North America, and Japan, whereas an overall declining trend was observed in Asia excluding Japan. Disease-specific analyses showed variation between neurosurgical categories, including higher thresholds in spinal than cranial studies.

CONCLUSIONS: The chronological threshold used to define patients as "elderly" in neurosurgical literature is dynamic and context-dependent, varying over time, across regions, and between disease categories. These findings highlight the limitations of fixed chronological age cut-offs. Assessment of older neurosurgical patients should therefore incorporate individual factors such as frailty, physiological reserve, and functional status rather than rely on chronological age alone. Med Pr Work Health Saf. 2026;77(4).

articles.title: Prevalence of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Associated with Congenital Heart Disease Following Defect Correction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Understanding the disease burden of repaired pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease (PAH-CHD) is essential for guiding healthcare strategies, yet data are lacking in this area.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) following defect correction in patients with congenital heart disease (CHD).

DATA SOURCES: A systematic review and meta-analysis was performed using PubMed, Embase and Cochrane databases.

STUDY SELECTION: Longitudinal cohort published between 1970-2023 involving CHD patients who underwent defect correction and were subsequently diagnosed with PAH were reviewed. Eligible studies reporting the prevalence of repaired PAH-CHD at least 3 months post-repair was included. Study selection was conducted independently by two reviewers. The primary outcome was the prevalence of PAH in patients following CHD defect correction.

RESULTS: Across 58 studies (7,036 participants), the random-effects pooled prevalence of reported post-repair PAH/PH was 10.8% (95% CI 7.3-15.0, I2 = 95.6%; prediction interval 0-50.1%). Prevalence was 9.0% (95% CI 3.3-17) in studies using right heart catheterisation, 19.3% (CI 10.6-29.7) in studies using echocardiography and 16.1% (CI 8.6- 25.1%) in studies using both modalities (p=0.19). Prevalence was highest in the adult-only cohort (18.5%, 95%CI 11.8-26.2) and lower in paediatric only (7.6%, 95%CI 3-13.5) and mixed-age cohorts (7.5%,95%CI1.7-16.3), p=0.039. Preoperative pulmonary hypertension (PH) was the strongest predictor of post-repair PAH and remained predictive on adjusted meta-regression (p<0.01).

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: PAH following defect repair remains a significant clinical dilemma requiring standardised diagnostic criteria and robust risk stratification tools to guide management.

articles.title: Large Language Models Predict Functional Outcomes After Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Accurate prediction of functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke can guide clinical decision-making and resource allocation. Prior work has relied predominantly on structured predictors and conventional machine learning, while the ability of large language models (LLMs) to infer modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores from routine clinical admission notes is largely unexplored.

METHODS: We evaluated encoder (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers [BERT], NYUTron) and generative (Llama-3.1-8B, MedGemma-4B) LLMs, in both frozen and fine-tuned settings, for discharge and 90-day mRS prediction. ModernBERT-base was evaluated as a long-context encoder sensitivity analysis. We retrospectively analyzed 9485 admission history and physical notes for discharge prediction and 1898 notes for 90-day prediction from the NYU Langone Get With The Guidelines-Stroke registry (2016-2025). The most recent 12 months were held out for testing. Performance was assessed for binary functional outcome (mRS 0-2 vs 3-6) and compared with structured, hybrid, and clinical risk score baselines.

RESULTS: In frozen settings, the clinically pretrained NYUTron encoder outperformed all other models. After fine-tuning, Llama achieved the highest discrimination for discharge (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.84, area under the precision-recall curve 0.81) and 90-day (AUROC 0.87, area under the precision-recall curve 0.84) prediction, while binary accuracy was similar among NYUTron, Llama, and MedGemma. A long-context ModernBERT-base sensitivity analysis did not outperform NYUTron or eliminate differences in exact mRS prediction. For 90-day prediction, fine-tuned Llama outperformed structured (Zhang et al, AUROC 0.82), hybrid (Sung et al, AUROC 0.82), and clinical risk score (Totaled Health Risks in Vascular Events, AUROC 0.80; Stroke Prognostication using Age and NIH Stroke Scale, AUROC 0.79) baselines (all P < .05).

CONCLUSION: Fine-tuned LLMs can predict poststroke functional outcomes from admission notes alone and outperform the evaluated prognostic baselines. Task-specific adaptation altered relative model-class performance, with generative models achieving the strongest performance on several metrics; however, differences between model classes varied by metric and cannot be attributed to architecture alone. Our findings support the development of text-based prognostic tools that integrate into clinical workflows without manual data extraction.

articles.title: Theoretical Insights into Cosolvent Effects in PET Glycolysis: A Multiscale Transport-Activation Mechanism.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
articles.abstract: Despite extensive advances in polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization, the molecular-level mechanisms by which solvents and cosolvents regulate PET swelling, transport, and bond cleavage remain insufficiently understood. Herein, an integrated molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) calculation was employed to systematically elucidate the roles of eight representative cosolvents─tetrahydrofuran (THF), 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (M-THF), 1,3-dioxolane (DOL), δ-valerolactone (DVL), cyclopentanone (CP), ethylene glycol (EG), anisole (AS), and benzyl alcohol (BnOH)─in PET solvation and degradation-related environments. Analyses of free-volume evolution, diffusion behavior, and electronic structure-derived descriptors capturing local polarity and orbital localization reveal pronounced solvent-dependent differences in chain relaxation, molecular mobility, and electronic activation pathways. Ether- and carbonyl-containing cosolvents primarily promote PET swelling and molecular transport by modulating local polarity and chain relaxation, whereas the protic cosolvent benzyl alcohol forms a dynamically reconfigurable, ethylene glycol-coupled hydrogen-bond network that enhances molecular mobility and stabilizes reactive oxyanion/transition-state structures. These distinct interaction modes give rise to computed differences in activation barriers, which elucidate the depolymerization mechanisms of different cosolvents. This study establishes a unified transport-activation mechanistic understanding and provides theory-guided principles for the rational design of efficient cosolvent systems for PET recycling.

articles.title: Thermodynamic Studies of Ester-Based Gemini Surfactant and Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Quantum Dot Coacervation and Its Application in Quercetin Detection.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
articles.abstract: Coacervation is spontaneous phase separation into colloid-rich and dilute phases. Here, we report self-assembled luminescent coacervate droplets formed by mixing nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots (NGQDs) with an ester-based cationic gemini surfactant in water. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) confirmed the formation of intrinsically fluorescent spherical droplets. Double-logarithmic plot analysis and Van't Hoff thermodynamic studies revealed that the spontaneous formation of stable luminescent coacervate droplets is primarily driven by hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions. Fluorescence, UV-vis spectroscopy, lifetime measurements, and temperature-dependent Stern-Volmer studies showed that quercetin-induced fluorescence quenching of the coacervate droplets proceeds through a synergistic combination of static quenching, PET-mediated dynamic quenching, and the inner filter effect (IFE), providing a simple and selective fluorometric sensing approach. The sensor exhibited a linear response in the range of 5-50 μM, with detection limits of 5.7 nM in deionized (DI) water and 7.1 nM in tap water. The fluorescent probe effectively measured quercetin in biological samples (human serum, plasma, whole blood) and real samples (Java plum, tomato) with recovery rates ranging from 94.9% to 108.3%. This turn-off droplet-based platform provides a simple, rapid, and effective method for quercetin detection, demonstrating the potential of hybrid nanomaterials in advanced sensing applications.

articles.title: Field Cycling NMR Relaxometry as a Tool for Detecting the Quality of Biotechnological Drugs.
articles.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
articles.abstract: Biotechnological drugs mostly contain proteins or peptides; therefore, any change in ambient conditions during their storage and administration to patients may cause structural modifications, which, in turn, lower the drug quality/effectiveness. Among different drug quality issues hampering drug stability and pharmacokinetics, the commonly observed ones are aggregation and glycation. Both processes include changes at a molecular level that can indeed be probed by field cycling NMR relaxometry as an alternative to traditional techniques used in the detection of drug quality issues. In this study, as a forthcoming problem in diabetes pharmaceuticals, aggregation effects on a commercially available insulin drug (Humulin-R) and glucose-mediated glycation of bovine serum albumin (BSA, as a model serum protein for in vitro tests) were investigated by means of FFC NMR relaxometry experiments. 1H spin-lattice relaxation rate dispersion (NMRD) profiles obtained on insulin samples treated under three different stress conditions showed that, for a sample agitated at a high temperature (T = 50 °C), one observes a significant low-frequency dispersion that can be associated with rotational/reorientational motion of aggregates formed under this condition. Regarding the glycation experiments on the BSA solution, the low-frequency proton relaxation rate, R1, increases with glycation temperature and glycation time, which is related to the aggregation induced by advanced glycation end-product (AGEs) formation on the surface of BSA. Overall, for the detection of drug quality issues, FFC NMR relaxometry is promising as a noninvasive and relatively low-cost technique that does not involve any additional sample preparation procedures or use of chemicals.

articles.title: Robotic aortic valve replacement with a sutureless valve, through a 3 cm transaxillary incision: a step-by-step surgical guide.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Robotic aortic valve replacement remains a challenging procedure, limiting its widespread adoption. We present our technique of robotic aortic valve replacement with da Vinci X system, with a sutureless valve (Perceval Plus), where we have tried to simplify the procedural steps. These can be very easily adopted by surgeons worldwide. The procedure includes port placement, docking, incision planning, femoral cannulation, aortotomy, valve excision, implantation tips for the sutureless valve, and aortotomy closure. The refinement of this approach has been associated with rapid postoperative recovery, with the patient walking in less than 24 hours after surgery. This step-by-step video tutorial will help surgeons worldwide in the adoption of robotic aortic valve replacement techniques.

articles.title: Totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement for quadricuspid aortic valve.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Quadricuspid aortic valve is a rare congenital anomaly that commonly presents with progressive aortic regurgitation and requires surgical valve replacement. Whether this anatomy can be safely addressed through a totally endoscopic approach has not been demonstrated in detail. We present a 62-year-old man with severe aortic regurgitation due to a Hurwitz-Roberts type A quadricuspid aortic valve who underwent totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement. The procedure was performed through a standardized three-port right thoracotomy with femoral arterial and venous cannulation under vacuum-assisted venous drainage. After transthoracic external aortic cross-clamping, myocardial protection was achieved with blood cardioplegia delivered directly into the coronary ostia, and the four-cusped valve was excised under three-dimensional endoscopic magnification. A 23 mm bovine pericardial bioprosthesis was implanted with 15 everting mattress sutures of coated polyester braid, secured with automated titanium fasteners. The patient was extubated soon after the operation and discharged on postoperative Day 10. Echocardiography at 3.5 months confirmed normal prosthetic function with a mean gradient of 14 mmHg and progressive left ventricular reverse remodelling. This video tutorial illustrates a reproducible step-by-step workflow for totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement applied to quadricuspid aortic valve, and provides practical guidance for surgeons encountering this anatomy.

articles.title: Non-dipper Hypertension Is Associated with Multilevel Vascular Alterations but Not Capillary Rarefaction: A Cross-sectional Vascular Phenotyping Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare endothelial function, carotid remodeling, renal microvascular injury, and nailfold capillaroscopy across control, dipper, and non-dipper participants and to test whether non-dipper hypertension reflects isolated nocturnal blood pressure dysregulation or broader vascular alteration.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 74 normotensive controls and 157 treatment-naive patients with newly diagnosed essential hypertension, classified by ambulatory monitoring as dipper (n = 70) or non-dipper (n = 87). All underwent flow-mediated dilation, carotid intimamedia thickness, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and nail-fold capillaroscopy. Regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, diabetes mellitus, and 24-hour systolic blood pressure.

RESULTS: Twenty-four-hour systolic blood pressure did not differ between dipper and non-dipper hypertension (143.1 vs. 146.5 mmHg; P = .161), whereas nighttime systolic blood pressure was markedly higher in non-dippers (121.8 vs. 144.5 mmHg; P < .001). Non-dippers had lower flow-mediated dilation (-2.5 [-4.5, 0.8] vs. 3.0 [-2.5, 5.6]%; P < .001); higher carotid intima-media thickness (1.01 [0.86, 1.06] vs. 0.85 [0.67, 1.01] mm; P < .001); and more frequent dilated capillaries (43.0% vs 20.0%; P = .003), microhemorrhages (31.4% vs 15.7%; P = .026), retinopathy (36.1% vs. 19.4%; P = .030), and left ventricular hypertrophy (47.4% vs. 30.9%; P = .044). Capillary density did not differ. After adjustment, non-dipper status remained associated with flow-mediated dilation (-4.22 percentage points; 95% CI, -7.15 to -1.30), carotid intima-media thickness (0.087 mm; 0.025-0.149), and dilated capillaries (odds ratio, 3.17; 1.50-6.71). The carotid association was directionally consistent across measurement-scale strata but significant only among measurements not requiring unit conversion.

CONCLUSION: Non-dipper hypertension identified a multilevel vascular phenotype not explained by 24-hour pressure load and without capillary rarefaction.

articles.title: Minimally invasive aortic valve replacement through right anterior thoracotomy with concomitant thoracoscopic ablation.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: Both minimally invasive aortic valve replacement through right anterior thoracotomy and thoracoscopic ablation are safe and feasible techniques with proven results in terms of long-term survival, a reduced postoperative recovery period and continued freedom from disease. The combination of these techniques has not yet been documented. Here, a rib-sparing right anterior thoracotomy with percutaneous femoral cannulation and aortic valve replacement was combined with a left thoracoscopic ablation using bipolar radiofrequency energy and left atrial appendage closure with epicardial occlusion device was performed. This video tutorial depicts the surgical approach and presents short-term outcomes of a small case series.

articles.title: Type 3 aortopulmonary window: surgical repair technique.
articles.journal: Multimedia manual of cardiothoracic surgery : MMCTS
articles.abstract: A 2-week-old, 3.5 kg neonate presented with congestive heart failure and a cardiac murmur. Echocardiography demonstrated a large type III aortopulmonary window associated with a large secundum atrial septal defect. Biventricular systolic function was normal, the pulmonary valve was competent, and both branch pulmonary arteries were well formed. No coronary artery anomalies were identified. Through a median sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass was established with aortic and bicaval cannulation, and the branch pulmonary arteries were controlled. Following aortic cross-clamping and cardioplegic arrest, the window was exposed, allowing direct visualization of the defect margins, coronary artery origins, branch pulmonary arteries and pulmonary valve. The aortopulmonary septum was reconstructed with a bovine pericardial patch, preserving branch pulmonary artery alignment and avoiding distortion or obstruction. The atrial septal defect was partially closed, leaving an approximately 4 mm fenestration. The patient was weaned from cardiopulmonary bypass. Cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 67 and 49 minutes, respectively, and total operative time was 3 hours. Long-term follow-up was unavailable. This case illustrates patch repair of a large type III aortopulmonary window under direct visualization of adjacent structures, with attention to preserving great vessel geometry and branch pulmonary artery. Long-term outcomes could not be assessed because follow-up data were unavailable.

articles.title: Choline in canine and feline nutrition: Physiological roles, dietary requirements and recommendations, and implications for health.
articles.abstract: Choline is an essential nutrient in canine and feline diets with physiological roles in lipid metabolism, hepatic function, one-carbon metabolism, neurotransmission, growth, and overall health. Current published dietary recommendations by the National Research Council establish recommended allowances of 425 mg choline/1,000 kcal metabolizable energy in dogs and 637 mg choline/1,000 kcal metabolizable energy in cats. However, these recommendations are largely derived from a limited number of studies in growing puppies and kittens, in which choline deficiency resulted in impaired growth, anorexia, hepatic lipid accumulation, and/or death. In comparison, little is known about the dietary choline requirements of adult, senior, gestating, lactating, overweight, obese, or working animals, or how dietary composition may alter the need for choline. Factors such as dietary fat concentration, methionine, folate, vitamin B12, betaine, choline source, life stage, body condition, and hepatic health may influence choline utilization and dietary requirements. Emerging evidence in companion animals, together with findings from other species, suggests that dietary choline intake above current published recommended allowances may be beneficial for hepatic lipid metabolism, growth and development, cognitive health, aging, and obesity management. However, species-specific research in dogs and cats remains limited, and targeted research is needed to refine dietary recommendations according to life stage, health status, and/or diet composition. This review summarizes current knowledge of choline metabolism, published dietary recommendations, factors influencing dietary requirements, the implications of dietary deficiency and excess, and considerations for choline intake in canine and feline nutrition.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal distribution, polymer characterization, and ecological risk assessment of microplastics in the Cauvery River, Tamil Nadu, India.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) contamination in tropical river systems remains insufficiently characterized, particularly with respect to spatial variability and monsoon-driven dynamics. This study investigated the distribution, composition, and ecological risk of MPs in surface water along a 150 km stretch of the Cauvery River, India. Sampling was conducted across 19 sites during post-monsoon/winter (February 2024) and northeast monsoon (November 2024) seasons to capture contrasting hydrological conditions. The MPs were extracted using density separation and wet peroxide oxidation, followed by multi-technique identification using ATR-FTIR (n = 197), μ-FTIR (n = 28), μ-Raman spectroscopy (n = 50), Pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry for confirmatory analysis and SEM for surface morphology characterization. A total of 389 MPs were identified, with fibres as the dominant morphology (47.65%). Polymer composition was primarily polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyamide (PA). Mean MP concentrations increased significantly from 0.96 ± 0.31 particles/L in the post-monsoon/winter season to 4.68 ± 1.03 particles/L in the northeast season (t = 3.21, df=17 p = 0.005), indicating strong hydrological control. Principal Component Analysis explained 93.31% of total variance and revealed clear seasonal clustering, with northeast monsoon season sites associated with higher MP abundance and PET/PS dominance. A moderate positive correlation between MPs abundance and population density (Spearman ρ = 0.48, p = 0.037) suggests anthropogenic influence. Ecological risk assessment using Polymer Hazard Index (PHI), Pollution Load Index (PLI), and Ecological Risk Index (RI) indicated spatial variability in potential risk, with elevated risk levels observed at urban-influenced and bridge-associated sites during the northeast monsoon season. The present study demonstrates that monsoon-driven hydrological processes and localized anthropogenic inputs jointly regulate MPs distribution in the Cauvery River.

articles.title: Hypogonadism in men with type 2 diabetes: practical recommendations for diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring.
articles.abstract: Functional hypogonadism is a common complication of type 2 diabetes, particularly in patients with coexisting obesity or cardiometaboliccomplications. Nevertheless, this disorder often remains undiagnosed. This position statement provides practical recommendations forthe diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of hypogonadism in men with type 2 diabetes. In patients with type 2 diabetes who have symptoms suggestive of androgen deficiency, measurement of serum total testosterone isrecommended. The diagnosis of hypogonadism requires the coexistence of clinical symptoms and a low testosterone concentration [totaltestosterone < 12 nmol/L (350 ng/dL) and/or calculated free testosterone (cfT) < 220 pmol/L (65 pg/mL)], confirmed by two measurementsperformed at least 4 weeks apart. The diagnosis of functional hypogonadism also requires exclusion of organic causes. Management shouldbe based on a balanced diet, regular physical activity, pharmacotherapy aimed at achieving metabolic control of diabetes, and treatment ofobesity. Testosterone therapy may be considered in symptomatic men who meet the biochemical criteria, primarily to improve qualityof life, sexual function, body composition, and metabolic parameters. However, it should be regarded as adjunctive treatment supportingsustainable lifestyle change. Testosterone therapy may be initiated after contraindications, including current reproductive plans, havebeen excluded; regular monitoring is required. A targeted medical history, appropriate diagnosis of hypogonadism, lifestyle modification, careful selection of candidates for testosteronetherapy, and adequate treatment monitoring may substantially improve care for men with type 2 diabetes and hypogonadism.

articles.title: Sex-specific differences in mortality in obstructive sleep apnea: results from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex differences in mortality among patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study, including adult patients with OSA defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5 events/hour. OSA severity was classified as mild (AHI 5-14.9), moderate (AHI 15-29.9) or severe (AHI ≥30). All-cause mortality was assessed over a median follow-up of 5.9 (interquartile range 4.6-7.2) years using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, obesity, current smoking status, diabetes mellitus, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and cerebrovascular disease. Interaction between sex and OSA severity was tested, and analyses were stratified by age (≤50 and >50 years).

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 3,843 patients with 421 deaths. Despite lower OSA severity, women had an overall mortality of 10.0% (120/1,203), compared with 11.4% (301/2,640) in men. Men had higher mortality than women in severe OSA (HR 1.50; 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.09; 2.05]; p = 0.011), whereas no sex differences were observed in mild and moderate OSA (HR 0.95; 95% CI [0.61; 1.50]; p = 0.850 and 1.09; 95%CI [0.73; 1.63]; p = 0.662; interaction p = 0.110) . In age-stratified analyses, among patients ≤50 years, women demonstrated higher mortality than men irrespective of the severity of OSA (HR for men versus women 0.34; 95%CI [0.14; 0.87]; p = 0.024), while among patients >50 years, men with severe OSA had the highest mortality risk (HR 1.58; 95%CI [1.15; 2.18]; p = 0.005). Treatment was associated with reduced mortality in patients >50 years (HR 0.52; 95%CI [0.40; 0.67]; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Mortality risk among patients with OSA varied according to sex, age, and OSA severity. Our findings suggest potentially distinct risk patterns, with higher mortality observed among younger women and among older men with severe OSA. The findings in younger patients should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of events.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield and biomarker Kinetics of an institutional CK-MB trigger for emergency coronary angiography after elective cardiac surgery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the diagnostic yield, biomarker kinetics, and outcomes of an unstratified institutional CK-MB trigger (≥120 U/L) for emergency coronary angiography after elective cardiac surgery.

METHODS: In this retrospective study (2016-2023), 225 of 7,111 elective cardiac surgery patients (3.2%) with postoperative CK-MB levels ≥120 U/L underwent emergency coronary angiography regardless of symptoms. Serial CK-MB trajectories (4h to POD3) were analyzed across surgical entities.

RESULTS: New pathological coronary findings were identified in 113 patients (50.2%; CP group), while 112 showed no relevant abnormalities (49.8%; CN group). Diagnostic yield varied dramatically by procedure type: 88.5% in isolated CABG (predominantly distal anastomotic lesions) vs. <28% in isolated valve surgery (mainly mechanical suture or cannulation trauma). In serial analyses, catheter-negative valve patients exhibited a sharp early "trauma peak" at 12 hours followed by rapid clearance, whereas true ischemic compromise produced sustained plateaus through POD2. The CP group required significantly longer intensive care (7 vs. 5 days; p < 0.001) and hospital stays (16.5 vs. 14 days; p < 0.001). Thirty-day mortality did not differ significantly (17.7% vs. 14.3%; p = 0.484).

CONCLUSIONS: While an unstratified CK-MB trigger demonstrates high diagnostic yield in CABG patients, it causes a high rate of unnecessary catheterizations in valve surgery due to transient surgical trauma washout. Rigid biomarker cutoffs without kinetic tracking and procedural stratification are clinically insufficient.

articles.title: Charcot-Leyden crystals drive a localized inflammatory niche around mucus plugs in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Mucus plugging causes airflow obstruction, morbidity, and mortality in chronic respiratory diseases. Charcot-Leyden crystals (CLCs), formed from eosinophil-derived Galectin-10, are frequently observed in pathologic mucus, but their role in disease is unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To define the prevalence, inflammatory context, and functional role of CLCs in mucus plugs, using acute allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) as a model of eosinophilic muco-obstructive disease.

METHODS: Airway samples from 19 patients with acute ABPA and 61 disease controls were analyzed for CLCs and Galectin-10. Paired samples from plugged and unplugged bronchial mucosal biopsies defined the spatial relationship between CLCs and inflammation. A novel mouse model demonstrated the contribution of CLCs to airway obstruction and inflammation and enabled evaluation of CLC-directed imaging and therapy.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Airway CLCs were a sensitive and specific marker of acute ABPA. CLC-containing mucus plugs were surrounded by a localized type 2 inflammatory niche, alongside eosinophils, neutrophils and extracellular traps, whereas inflammation was minimal in unplugged airways from the same patients, or plugs lacking CLCs. In mice, CLC-containing plugs induced persistent airway obstruction and local inflammation, both reduced by a crystal-dissolving anti-Galectin-10 antibody. Galectin-10 concentrations provided a quantitative biomarker of acute ABPA, while a CLC-targeted positron emission tomography tracer enabled noninvasive visualization of crystal-rich plugs.

CONCLUSIONS: CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.

articles.title: Effect of Topical Recombinant Human Epidermal Growth Factor on Short-Term Wound Area Reduction in Chronic Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic ulcers are a main complication of diabetes mellitus and frequently require effective treatment to advance wound healing and prevent complications. This study evaluated topical Recombinant Human Epidermal Growth Factor (rhEGF) compared with conventional saline dressing for managing chronic diabetic ulcers. We conducted a randomized controlled trial at a tertiary care teaching hospital from September 2022 to May 2024. A total of 100 patients with diabetic foot ulcers were randomly assigned to receive each topical rhEGF ointment (Group A, n = 50) or conventional saline dressing (Group B, n = 50). Wound size was assessed at baseline, Day 7, and Day 14 using the graph paper method. The primary result was a reduction in wound size. Baseline demographic and clinical variables were comparable among the groups. By Day 14, Group A demonstrated a significantly smaller mean wound size than Group B (5.78 ± 2.64 cm2 vs 8.33 ± 3.71 cm2; P = .0001). Topical rhEGF was associated with greater short-term reduction in wound surface area compared with conventional saline dressing over 14 days. These findings indicate a potential short-term benefit in wound-area reduction during inpatient treatment; however, complete wound healing, time to healing, recurrence, amputation, graft take, adverse events, and post-discharge outcomes were not assessed. These findings therefore should not be interpreted as evidence of improved overall healing or long-term clinical effectiveness.

articles.title: Treatment of Severe Progressive Oral Problems in a Siberian Husky With Persistent Masticatory Muscle Myoclonus.
articles.abstract: A 5-year-old Siberian Husky with a history of canine distemper virus (CDV) infection and persistent myoclonus was presented for evaluation of severe oral pathology. Oral examination and advanced diagnostic imaging revealed marked jaw malformation, severe generalised periodontal disease, traumatic lesions, extensive palatal and maxillary osteolysis, marked symphyseal instability, and 3 oronasal fistulae. The persistent myoclonus involved the masticatory muscles, head, neck, trunk and abdomen. Neurological examination identified additional deficits, confirming that the patient was not neurologically normal in addition to the presence of myoclonus. The patient required staged near-edentation and surgical repair of the oronasal fistulae, which recurred. Persistent involuntary contraction of the masticatory muscles, loss of normal bony support, and ongoing local infection and inflammation were considered major contributors to failure of healing. While the authors would generally recommend pursuing surgical closure of all oronasal fistulas, the complexity of this case realigned the priorities. Definitive repair was not achieved; however, near-edentation resulted in improved comfort, appetite and body condition, supporting a palliative treatment approach in this case. This report highlights the long-term orofacial consequences of persistent continuous myoclonus and the challenges of oral surgical repair in patients with uncontrolled jaw movement.

articles.title: Decreased astrocytic CCL5 by Mir324 ameliorates ischemic stroke injury via the CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway.
articles.abstract: Following ischemic stroke, Ccl5 mRNA expression increased, while Mir324 expression decreased in the peri-infarct cortex of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice. However, the roles of CCL5 and Mir324 in stroke remained largely unclear. Here, we show that inhibiting CCL5 using antibodies or Mir324 not only reduced infarct area and preserved neurological function in MCAO mice but also attenuated astrocyte reactivity and microglial activation, protected dendritic structures, and maintained spine density. In an astrocyte-neuron co-culture system after oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), inhibiting astrocytic CCL5 by antibody or Mir324 decreased neuronal apoptosis and preserved dendritic structure. Importantly, the suppression of CCL5 enhanced ERK/CREB pathway signaling both in vivo and in vitro. Consistent with these findings, the application of Maraviroc, a CCR5 antagonist, reduced infarct size, decreased neuronal apoptosis, and upregulated the ERK/CREB pathway in neurons treated with OGD. In conclusion, targeting the CCL5 pathway via Mir324 represents a promising therapeutic strategy for alleviating ischemic stroke damage through modulation of the neuronal CCR5/ERK/CREB pathway.

articles.title: Application of artificial intelligence in traditional Chinese medicine: An exploratory study of a tongue diagnosis model based on machine learning and neural networks for cirrhosis risk prediction.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundLiver cirrhosis is a common end-stage of chronic liver diseases, with high morbidity and mortality.AimsThis study aimed to develop a tongue diagnosis model using machine learning and neural networks to evaluate the feasibility of predicting cirrhosis risk from tongue appearance data.MethodsTongue appearance and laboratory data were collected from 115 cirrhosis patients (July 2023-February 2024). MELD scores were calculated. After preprocessing, both image-based and text-based classifiers were constructed using five algorithms: Naive Bayes (NB), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Model performance was assessed using accuracy, F1-score, recall, precision, and AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve). A MELD-only baseline model was also developed for comparison.ResultsMulti-feature models consistently outperformed the MELD-only baseline. In image-based classification, SVM achieved the highest accuracy (85.71%) with 64-dimensional features. In text-based classification, RF, LR, SVM, and MLP all achieved 82.86% accuracy, demonstrating stable performance.ConclusionMachine learning models incorporating multiple tongue appearance features effectively addressed the limitations of MELD score alone. The SVM model with 64-dimensional image features achieved the best predictive performance, confirming the feasibility of cirrhosis risk prediction through tongue image analysis. This study offers a novel approach for non-invasive clinical risk stratification in cirrhosis patients.

articles.title: Modeling common finger movement patterns in daily activities: A quantitative framework for adaptive rehabilitation interfaces.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundHand movement involves complex joint patterns that vary across tasks and individuals, and identifying the components that underlie functional hand use is essential.ObjectiveWe aimed to construct a Commonality Model that decomposes real-world finger motions into dynamic forms and quantify probabilistic transitions to develop rehabilitation systems for post-stroke patients.MethodsFifteen healthy young adults performed upper limb tasks based on a Motor Activity Log (MAL), with hand motion captured using a camera and analyzed using MediaPipe. Joint angle data were extracted, k-means clustering was used to classify the movement patterns, and silhouette analysis was performed to determine the optimal number of clusters. Euclidean distance was used to identify overlapping forms across tasks grouped into Common Forms (CFs). A first-order Markov model was constructed to calculate the transition probabilities from CFs to unique task-specific forms.ResultsSeven operationally defined CFs were identified as recurrent image-derived hand-joint configurations observed across multiple activities of daily living (ADL) related tasks. Some tasks were largely composed of CF-associated transitions, whereas others showed higher proportions of task-dependent Individual Forms.ConclusionThe proposed Commonality Model provides an exploratory quantitative framework for identifying recurring and task-dependent hand-joint configurations during ADL-related movements in healthy young adults. Further studies are required to validate its reproducibility, generalizability, and clinical relevance in larger and clinical populations.

articles.title: Association of the Area Deprivation Index with cognitive function in individuals with acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: BackgroundNeighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with lower cognitive function, but whether this association persists in individuals with acute ischemic stroke is unclear.ObjectiveTo assess whether the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) is associated with global and domain-specific cognition in individuals with acute ischemic stroke.MethodsThe Nutrition Effects on Brain Outcomes and Recovery in Stroke after Hospitalization (NOURISH) study enrolled 266 patients with ischemic stroke aged 55 years and older. ADI is an area-level composite measure derived from 17 U.S. Census indicators spanning education, employment, income, poverty, and housing quality. Cognitive function was assessed using a standardized neuropsychological battery comprising 19 cognitive tests, from which global cognition and five cognitive domains were computed.ResultsAmong the 266 participants included in the analysis, 152 (57.1%) were women and 159 (59.8%) were Black individuals. The mean age was 68.3 years (SD = 8.0). Higher ADI at both the state and national levels was associated with lower global cognitive z-scores; each 1-decile increase in State ADI rank was associated with a 0.044-unit lower global cognitive z-score (β = -0.044; SE = 0.017; p = 0.010), and each 10-percentage-point increase in National ADI rank was associated with a 0.056-unit lower global cognitive z-score (β = -0.056; SE = 0.020; p = 0.005). Higher ADI rank was also associated with lower executive function, episodic memory, and perceptual speed.ConclusionsNeighborhood socioeconomic disadvantage, as measured by ADI, was associated with lower cognitive function in individuals with acute ischemic stroke.Trial RegistrationClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04337255.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum and morbidity of ocular parasitic infections among rural children in central India.
articles.abstract: Ocular parasitic infections are an under-recognised cause of ocular morbidity in low- and middle-income countries. We found Taenia solium (26.5%) was the most common parasite, followed by Toxocara canis/cati (19.4%), Toxoplasma gondii (17.3%) and Acanthamoeba spp. (11.2%). Reduced visual acuity (66.3%), retinitis/chorioretinitis (38.8%), uveitis (32.7%) and vitreous involvement (28.6%) were the predominant clinical manifestations. Poor nutritional status was significantly associated with infection. Frequent open defaecation, barefoot outdoor play and inadequate handwashing before meals were identified as significant behavioural risk factors for ocular parasitic infection.

articles.title: Application of a Human Nasal Mucosa Ex Vivo Culture System to Model Inflammatory Responses.
articles.abstract: IntroductionThe nasal cavity is the entry point of the upper respiratory tract and the primary site of inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens.MethodsHuman nasal mucosa (HNM) tissues were obtained from patients undergoing endoscopic nasal surgery. Six HNM specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis were used for paired Der p 1 challenge experiments, and 8 chronic rhinosinusitis-derived HNM specimens were used for paired SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points.ResultsCultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. HDM stimulation enhanced secretory activity and induced IL-4 and IL-5 expression at day 3. Both SARS-CoV-2 variants (HU-1 and Omicron BA.2) produced detectable viral RNA and viral N-protein signals in HNM expressing Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 and Transmembrane Protease Serine 2. Viral inoculation induced an interferon-associated antiviral response, which was most pronounced following HU-1 exposure, although between-variant differences in the measured antiviral markers were not significant. At 3 days postinfection under standardized infection conditions, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2 at day 3.DiscussionThe ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, including an intact epithelial barrier, stromal immune cells, and glandular components, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform that complements conventional 2-dimensional cultures. HDM-sensitized HNM showed Der p 1-associated type 2 responses, whereas the viral arm revealed an antiviral response and exploratory variant-associated differences in epithelial injury.ConclusionsShort-term ex vivo HNM may provide a practical tissue-level platform for investigating upper-airway responses to allergen exposure and SARS-CoV-2 infection. It preserves multicellular tissue architecture, while further validation in larger, better-stratified cohorts and extended culture optimization will support broader mechanistic and translational application.

articles.title: First histopathological characterization of leatherback shell syndrome in Alaskan golden king crabs Lithodes aequispinus.
articles.abstract: An abnormally soft dorsal shell condition, known as 'leatherback', has been reported for the past 3 decades in golden king crabs Lithodes aequispinus (GKCs) harvested from fisheries in the southeast Alaska (USA) panhandle and Aleutian Islands/Bering Sea, occurring almost exclusively in old-shell males. Based on large commercial sample sizes of several thousand crabs, reported prevalences of leatherbacks in the Aleutian/Bering Sea ranged from 0.29 to 2.7%, and 1.9% in crabs from southeast Alaska. This study presents the first histopathological characterization of leatherback shell syndrome based on 8 affected GKCs. Histological examination revealed severe hepatopancreatic tubular necrosis and atrophy, accompanied by fragmentation, degeneration, and atrophy of skeletal muscle bundles within the coxal and thoracic regions. These lesions indicate profound impairment of hepatopancreatic function, likely resulting in chronic nutritional deficiency and progressive muscle wasting that contribute substantially to the debilitated condition of affected crabs. No evidence of bacterial, fungal, parasitic, or viral agents was detected in histological sections of the hepatopancreas or skeletal muscle, and transmission electron microscopy of hepatopancreatic tissue from 1 representative specimen likewise failed to identify infectious agents. Furthermore, the remarkably low prevalence of the syndrome, its strong association with old-shell males, and its apparent restriction to a single king crab species are inconsistent with the epidemiological patterns expected for a transmissible infectious disease. Collectively, these findings support a non-infectious etiology for leatherback shell syndrome. We propose that the condition may represent a chronic wasting disorder associated with environmentally induced or genetically mediated metabolic dysfunction affecting hepatopancreatic development and maintenance. Progressive failure of critical physiological and biochemical pathways during aging and senescence may ultimately lead to irreversible hepatopancreatic degeneration, secondary muscle atrophy, and severe debilitation characteristic of affected crabs. These findings establish a pathological foundation for future investigations into the mechanisms, risk factors, and ecological consequences of this syndrome in wild GKC populations.

articles.title: Current Clinical Practice and Barriers to Instrumented Gait Assessment in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Cross-Sectional Survey.
authors: Stroke Gait Disturbance Task Force, Strategic Problem-Solving Committee, Japanese Society of Neurological Physical Therapy
articles.abstract: BackgroundObservational gait analysis is widely used in stroke rehabilitation but may have limited objectivity and reproducibility. Instrumented gait assessment may address these limitations, but its routine use and implementation barriers remain unclear.ObjectivesTo investigate gait assessment practices and barriers to routine instrumented gait assessment among physiotherapists treating people with stroke.MethodsA web-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among members of the Japanese Society of Neurological Physical Therapy. Respondents reporting limitations in observational gait analysis completed additional questions on instrumented gait assessment. Logistic regression examined factors associated with perceived measurement time burden among device users.ResultsOf 329 respondents, 95.4% used standardized clinical gait assessments, and 81.8% perceived limitations in observational gait analysis. Although 91.2% recognized the need for instrumented gait assessment, only 39.8% of the 269 respondents completing the second-stage questions used it routinely. Of 162 non-users, 80.2% reported that relevant equipment was unavailable. Device users commonly reported excessive measurement time, high equipment costs, and difficulty interpreting results. Measurement time ≥20 min was associated with perceived measurement time burden (odds ratio 3.59, 95% confidence interval 1.04-12.46; p = 0.044). Automated analysis (95.5%) and usability regardless of location (83.6%) were frequently desired.ConclusionsInstrumented gait assessment was widely perceived as necessary, but routine use remained limited. Improving equipment access and developing time-efficient, portable systems with automated analysis and interpretation support may facilitate integration into routine stroke rehabilitation and sustained clinical use.

articles.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Feedback During Robotic Gait Training Acutely Modulate Paretic Muscle Activation, Limb Loading, and Propulsion-Related Mechanics in Chronic Hemiparetic Stroke: A Randomised Crossover Trial.
articles.abstract: BackgroundVisual-feedback modalities, including virtual reality (VR) and screen-based augmented reality (AR), have been integrated into robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) to enhance engagement and gait control after stroke, yet their distinct and combined neuromechanical effects remain unclear.ObjectiveTo compare the acute effects of RAGT alone, VR-RAGT, screen-based AR-RAGT, and sequential combined VR + AR-RAGT on paretic gait mechanics in individuals with chronic hemiparetic stroke.MethodsTwenty participants completed four 30-min RAGT conditions (RAGT alone, VR-RAGT, screen-based AR-RAGT, and sequential combined VR + AR-RAGT) in a randomized within-subject crossover design. Paretic muscle activation, ground reaction forces and center of pressure (COP) were analyzed as time-normalized waveforms using one-dimensional statistical parametric mapping; robot-derived joint torque and torque-angle slope were analyzed as phase-averaged scalars using repeated-measures ANOVA.ResultsRelative to RAGT alone, VR was associated with greater swing-phase tibialis anterior activation and hip flexion torque, whereas AR was associated with reduced stance-phase co-contraction and greater late-stance gastrocnemius activation, knee extensor torque, and anterior-posterior COP progression. The sequential combined VR + AR condition produced the broadest acute modulation across swing- and stance-related outcomes, including reduced co-contraction-related EMG, greater paretic limb loading, and longer anterior-posterior COP progression.ConclusionsUnder identical robotic parameters and the task configurations tested, VR and screen-based AR feedback differentially modulated swing- and stance-phase paretic gait mechanics, and sequential exposure to both conditions produced the broadest acute modulation. Whether these acute, task-specific effects translate into longer-term functional recovery remains to be determined.

articles.title: Interdisciplinary Collaboration as Key Factor for the Optimization of Advanced Heart Failure Treatment.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health problem, with outcomes in advanced stages continuing to be poor despite the development of medical therapy and interventional strategies. This report proposes the concept of Interdisciplinary Heart Failure Collaboration (IHFC), a structured framework designed to optimize patient outcomes through coordinated, cross-sectoral care, focusing on the management of advanced HF. The IHFC integrates a broad spectrum of healthcare professionals-including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, nurses, anesthesiologists, intensivists, psychologists, ventricular assist device (VAD) coordinators, and many others-to provide optimal care from outpatient diagnosis to post-discharge long-term management. The model consists of three core management phases: 1) pre-hospital management, which includes outpatient clinic visits, accurate diagnosis and timely referral; 2) intra-hospital management, comprising interventional and surgical treatment including durable VAD implantation and heart transplantation; 3) post-discharge management; post-interventional and post-operative care, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up, patient education and support for self-care. In addition, this report discusses current challenges in implementation, including the need for standardized protocols and effective communication among team members. Rather than replacing existing HF care systems, the IHFC provides a practical framework for integrating established multidisciplinary principles across the entire clinical trajectory of advanced HF and may be adapted to different healthcare settings.

articles.title: Direct and Indirect Mechanisms of Cardiac Dysfunction Following Severe Acute Kidney Injury in Rats.
articles.abstract: Acute renocardiac syndrome (cardiorenal syndrome type 3) occurs when acute kidney injury (AKI) leads to acute cardiac dysfunction. The objective of this study was to determine the effects of severe AKI on cardiac function in rats and to distinguish changes driven by kidney injury from those resulting from loss of renal function.  Studies were performed in male and female Sprague-Dawley rats. Animals underwent unilateral nephrectomy (Sham), unilateral nephrectomy combined with 45 minutes of renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), or bilateral nephrectomy (NX). Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography 24 or 48 hours after surgery. Blood and tissues were collected for biochemical and histological analyses. Body, heart, and lung weights did not differ among groups, whereas kidney weight was significantly increased following IRI. At 24 hours, diastolic filling velocities were significantly elevated in IRI rats compared with Sham and NX animals, but these differences resolved by 48 hours. In contrast, indices of enhanced systolic contractility were observed in both IRI and NX groups. These changes tended to normalize in IRI animals but persisted or worsened in NX rats over time. NX rats also developed significant metabolic and electrolyte abnormalities, including reduced blood pH, bicarbonate, sodium, calcium, and hematocrit, together with elevated potassium concentrations. Diastolic dysfunction occurred only in the presence of an injured kidney, whereas systolic alterations were observed following both IRI and bilateral nephrectomy. These findings suggest that kidney injury and loss of renal function contribute to distinct components of acute renocardiac syndrome.

articles.title: Design strategies and response mechanisms of intelligent dressings and their applications in the repair of diabetic wounds.
articles.abstract: Diabetic wounds result in refractory skin defects due to hyperglycemic toxicity, microcirculatory disorders, and chronic inflammation. Traditional dressings that passively cover wounds have significant limitations. Intelligent dressings offer active sensing, precise responses, and functional integration to break this vicious cycle. This review systematically examines design principles, response mechanisms (endogenous, exogenous, and multi-response synergy), and application progress (infection monitoring, exudate management, regeneration promotion, and closed-loop regulation) of intelligent dressings for diabetic wound repair. Key challenges in technology integration, clinical translation, and individual adaptation are analyzed, and future directions toward precision, personalization, and integration are discussed. This review provides a comprehensive reference for both research and clinical translation in this field.

articles.title: Aortic Root Remodeling Patterns and Outcomes Five Years Following Contemporary Root Replacement Strategies in Young Patients: A Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Background: Long-term dimensional remodeling patterns after contemporary aortic root operations in young patients have historically not been well characterized and this may inform surgical decision-making.Methods: We evaluated longitudinal aortic root and annular remodeling patterns and clinical outcomes after the Bentall, Ross, or Valve-Sparing Root procedures from January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2024.Results: Sixty patients underwent aortic root replacement. Of these, 17 had the Bentall procedure (BP), 20 had the Ross procedure, and 23 had Valve Sparing Aortic Root Replacement (VSARR). On average Ross patients (4 years) were younger than BP (16 years) and VSARR (16 years) (p = .0001). Marfans (20%, 12/60), Down Syndrome (3%, 2/60) and Loeys-Dietz (3%, 2/60) were prevalent. All Marfan patients (n = 12) underwent VSARR (p = .006). The leading surgical indications were aortic regurgitation (78%, 47/60), aortic stenosis (58%, 35/60), and aortic aneurysm (46%, 28/60). Mortality rate was 7% (n = 4/60) and no statistically significant difference in survival was observed (p = .94). Reoperation occurred in 3 of 60 patients (5%). Four of 60 patients (7%) had endocarditis. At 5 years, the change in aortic root size was significantly different across operation types (p = .041), with significant dilation noted in the Ross cohort.Conclusions: Ross patients demonstrated greater neoaortic root enlargement at 5 years, although valve competence was generally preserved. Given the differences in age, underlying pathology, and surgical selection among the groups, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive remodeling patterns rather than evidence of the superiority of one operative strategy.

articles.title: Spectroscopic classification of non-ergodic populations.
articles.journal: Philosophical transactions. Series A, Mathematical, physical, and engineering sciences
articles.abstract: Non-ergodicity affects statistical inference in a diverse range of disciplines inside and outside physics. However, the concept of ergodicity is used inconsistently and may refer to several non-equivalent notions. To help address this, we first identify and clarify the relationship between three major interpretations of ergodicity. We then introduce a method of spectral analysis of non-ergodicity, which may be performed using data alone, and so may be applied in both numerical and empirical contexts. This may be used to identify, quantify and classify non-ergodic populations within an ergodic decomposition. This is demonstrated with an application to the Kob-Andersen (KA) kinetically constrained lattice glass model. This article is part of the theme issue 'Ergodicity and ergodicity breaking in the sciences'.

articles.title: Prognostic value of C-reactive protein/albumin ratio in predicting mortality in hemodialysis patients.
articles.journal: The International journal of artificial organs
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Systemic inflammation and malnutrition are critical determinants of mortality in hemodialysis patients. The C-reactive protein/albumin ratio (CAR) integrates these two pathways. This study aimed to assess the prognostic value of CAR for all-cause mortality in maintenance hemodialysis patients and compare it with other inflammatory biomarkers.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 204 hemodialysis patients followed between January 2022 and January 2024. Patients were stratified into survivor (n = 161) and non-survivor (n = 43) groups. Demographic data and inflammatory biomarkers, including CAR, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), were analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: Non-survivors exhibited significantly higher median CAR levels (3.86 vs 1.72, p < 0.001) and lower Kt/V values compared to survivors. In ROC analysis, 6-month average Kt/V (AUC = 0.764) and RAR (AUC = 0.751) showed high discriminatory power, followed by CAR (AUC = 0.715). However, in multivariate regression, high CAR (>2.59) remained a robust independent predictor of mortality (odds ratio: 3.61, p = 0.002), alongside age and Kt/V, whereas RDW lost its significance.

CONCLUSIONS: CAR may serve as a simple, cost-effective, and independent prognostic marker for all-cause mortality in hemodialysis patients.
