While dialysis adequacy (Kt/V) remains the dominant predictor, integrating CAR into routine monitoring has the potential to enhance risk stratification by capturing the malnutrition-inflammation burden, pending validation in future prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Cortical Silent Period Duration and Ankle Motor Performance After Stroke.
articles.abstract: The cortical silent period (CSP) which immediately follows transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) induced motor evoked potentials (MEPs) has been shown to increase in duration following stroke. However, the functional implications of increased CSP following stroke have not been thoroughly explored. Therefore, the objective of the present study was to assess the relationship between cortical silent period duration and performance on a functional ankle movement task. We explored this relationship through a retrospective analysis of data previously collected from 23 individuals with chronic stroke during a larger clinical trial which included neurophysiological and clinical testing. The measure we selected required serial reciprocal muscle activation, which we hypothesized would be impaired in individuals with prolonged CSPs. We found a negative correlation between normalized paretic CSP duration and performance on the ankle tracking task (p = .017, r2 = .242). While preliminary, these findings comport with existing mechanistic models of CSP generation as an intracortical GABAergic process involving the hyperdirect pathway of the basal ganglia and offer preliminary evidence that relative elongation of cortical silent periods in the stroke-affected hemisphere may negatively influence fine motor performance.

articles.title: Percutaneous Local Antibiotic Irrigation for Aortic Graft Infection After Endovascular Repair: A Single-Center Experience and Systematic Literature Review.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic graft infections (AGIs) are a severe complication following open aortic surgical repair (OSR) and endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction remain the gold standard treatment according to European guidelines. The aim is to present a single-center experience using a percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation strategy in selected patients with AGI after EVAR, with a systematic literature review.

METHODS: Patients with AGI after endovascular aortic repair treated with computed tomography (CT)-guided local antibiotic irrigation (2011-2023) were included. Outcomes were assessed using clinical, microbiological, and radiological follow-up, with mortality and reinfection evaluated up to 3 years. A systematic search of PubMed and Cochrane was conducted. The review was not registered, and formal bias assessment was not performed.

RESULTS: Among 665 endovascular repairs, 14 patients developed AGI. Eight patients were treated with CT-guided antibiotic irrigation. Infection resolved in 4 patients (n = 4/8), and 1 patient (n = 1/8) was treated as a bridge to open aortic surgical repair OSR. Persistent infection was observed in 3 patients (3/8). Cumulative mortality was 0% at 30 days (n = 0/8), 13% at 90 days (n = 1/8), and 50% (n = 4/8) at 1 to 3 years. Three patients (n = 3/8) died from recurrent infection. The literature review identified 6 studies, adding 28 cases. All patients were treated with antibiotic irrigation either as primary therapy or as a bridge to OSR. Short-term/30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 22%, except for 1 study, with mortality of 50%. Most studies achieved effective infection control in high-risk surgical candidates.

CONCLUSION: In highly selected groups of patients who are not candidates for extensive surgery such as aortic reconstruction, percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation may be an alternative treatment method.Clinical ImpactAGI after endovascular repair carries high mortality, current guidelines recommendation is endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction. This may not be feasible for frail patients. This single-center case series along with literature review of 6 studies suggest it may be feasible with minimally invasive CT-guided percutaneous drainage with local antibiotic irrigation in carefully selected patients who are unfit for major surgery.

articles.title: Interventions for managing immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps are difficult candidates for conventional root canal fillings. Interventions for management of such teeth include regenerative endodontic procedures (REPs), apexification, and root strengthening interventions. Basic principles involve removal of necrotic pulp, canal debridement and infection control. Currently, there is no evidence-based guidance to manage such teeth.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of different interventions to manage immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulps.

SEARCH METHODS: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Oral Health specialised register, and two trials registers, together with reference checking, to identify studies that were included in the review. The latest search date was October 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing additions to autologous blood clot (BC) scaffolds in REPs with conventional BC scaffolds in REPs for managing necrotic pulps in immature permanent teeth in children. We also included RCTs comparing different additions to BC scaffolds, coronal sealing materials, and intracanal disinfectants in REPs, different approaches to apexification, REPS (using any approach) with apexification, and root strengthening interventions.

OUTCOMES: Our outcomes were clinical measures of success (measured as absence of pain, or clinical success as defined by study authors), root apex development (prioritising measures of apical closure), discolouration, endodontic complications, patient-reported quality of life, and periodontal health. We prioritised data reported at 12 months, but collected data at later time points.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to assess bias in the RCTs.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: Although we planned to synthesise results for each outcome using meta-analysis, pooling was not possible owing to the sparse data for each outcome. Given the large number of comparisons in this review, we prioritised reporting data for scaffolds in REPs - in particular, additions to BC scaffolds compared with conventional BC scaffolds - because we believed that these were the most clinically relevant comparisons. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of the evidence for each outcome in this main comparison.

INCLUDED STUDIES: Overall, we included 30 RCTs in which 1227 teeth in 1152 children were treated. Studies included 37 different comparisons of REP interventions (scaffolds, coronal sealing materials, intracanal disinfectants), apexification approaches, and REPs versus apexification. No studies assessed root strengthening interventions.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: For our main comparison, we included eight studies (351 treated teeth) comparing platelet concentrate or synthetic additions to BC scaffolds with conventional BC scaffolds. We judged the certainty of the evidence for the following outcomes to be very low owing to risks of bias and high levels of imprecision. Therefore, we had very little confidence in the effect estimates. Platelet-rich plasma (1 study, 31 teeth). At 12 months, the evidence is very uncertain whether there are any differences between scaffold types in clinical success (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.28), or discolouration (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.36). Platelet-rich fibrin (1 study, 38 or 22 teeth). The evidence is very uncertain whether there are any differences between scaffold types in clinical success at 24 months (RR 0.99, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.15), the number of teeth with calcific bridge at the apical level at 12 months (RR 1.40, 95% CI 0.64 to 3.07), or discolouration at 12 months (presence of discolouration reported in all teeth). Platelet pellet (1 study, 38 teeth). At 24 months, the evidence is very uncertain whether there are any differences between scaffold types in clinical success (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.20). Advanced platelet-rich fibrin (1 study, 18 teeth). The study included in this comparison reported no relevant review outcome measures. Concentrated growth factor (1 study, 54 teeth). At 12 months, the evidence is very uncertain whether there are any differences between scaffold types in clinical success (RR 1.00, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.16), or periodontal health (resolution of periapical radiolucency: RR 1.45, 95% CI 0.84 to 2.53). Synthetic collagen-based addition (1 study, 43 teeth). At 18 months, the evidence is very uncertain whether there are any differences between scaffold types in discolouration (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.70), or endodontic complications: the number of teeth with pulp calcifications: RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.57). Growth factors-impregnated synthetic addition (1 study, 17 teeth). The study included in this comparison reported no relevant review outcome measures.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: We could not draw conclusions regarding the effectiveness of different additions to BC scaffolds compared with conventional BC scaffolds used in REPs owing to very low-certainty evidence in reported outcome measures, or absence of evidence for many critical outcomes (and absence of any evidence for some comparisons). We did not formally assess the certainty of the evidence for comparisons of other interventions in the review, but note that the evidence included similarly small studies with high or unclear risks of bias. No studies reported pain or patient-reported quality of life, and further research emphasising patient-reported outcomes may provide evidence for practice. Whilst studies often reported other measures, particularly for root apex development (such as increase in root length, or root canal wall thickness), these are less clinically informative. The absence of evidence using informative clinical measures in this review highlights the need for a core outcome set in this research field.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review was funded (in part) by University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine.

REGISTRATION: Protocol available via https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012709.

articles.title: Debridement Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Diabetic Foot Ulcers With Borderline Infrapopliteal Ischemia: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) complicated by infrapopliteal peripheral arterial disease (PAD) represent a major cause of morbidity and nontraumatic lower-limb amputation worldwide. In patients with borderline ischemia, the optimal management strategy remains unclear, with some clinicians advocating conservative debridement while others favor early endovascular revascularization.

AIM: To compare clinical outcomes of conservative management with surgical debridement versus an endovascular-first strategy followed by debridement in patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD.

METHODS: This prospective nonrandomized study included patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal PAD treated at a tertiary vascular center between March 2020 and March 2024. Patients with ankle-brachial index (ABI) values of 0.5-0.8 or falsely elevated ABI (>1.3) with preserved distal flow were included. Participants were managed with either conservative treatment (surgical debridement alone) or endovascular revascularization followed by debridement. Clinical, anatomical, and radiological assessments included the WIfI classification, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS), and Peripheral Arterial Calcification Scoring System (PACSS). Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics between groups. Primary outcomes included wound healing and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 12 months.

RESULTS: A total of 426 patients were analyzed (264 debridement and 162 revascularization). Patients undergoing revascularization had a greater burden of advanced limb disease, with a significantly higher prevalence of WIfI stage IV ulcers (51.9% vs 31.8%, P = .005), more advanced GLASS stage, and higher PACSS grades, whereas baseline cardiovascular comorbidities including hypertension, coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, and previous vascular intervention were comparable between groups. After PSM, 2 balanced cohorts of 100 patients each were compared. Amputation-free survival was similar between the debridement and revascularization groups (74% vs 70%, P = .824). Rates of major adverse limb events and overall mortality were also comparable. Multivariate analysis identified wound depth and GLASS stage as strong predictors of major amputation, while direct angiosomal revascularization was associated with improved wound healing and reduced limb-loss risk.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DFUs and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia, conservative management with timely debridement may achieve outcomes comparable with endovascular revascularization. Anatomical disease severity and wound characteristics appear to be stronger determinants of prognosis than the choice of revascularization strategy.Clinical ImpactThis study highlights the importance of individualized treatment selection in patients with diabetic foot ulcers and borderline infrapopliteal ischemia. Wound depth and anatomical disease complexity should be carefully considered when determining the need for endovascular intervention. In selected patients, timely debridement may be a reasonable management option, while direct angiosomal revascularization may offer additional benefits when an endovascular procedure is indicated. These findings may help clinicians refine treatment strategies and avoid unnecessary interventions without compromising limb-related outcomes.

articles.title: World Health Organization non-laboratory-based 10-year cardiovascular disease risk prediction model in adults without established disease.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (prognosis). The objectives are as follows: The objective of this review is to evaluate the prognostic performance of the World Health Organization (WHO) non-laboratory-based CVD risk prediction models in adults aged 40 years to 74 years without established CVD. To do this, we will assess the discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability of the models in external and internal validation studies. Population Adults aged 40-74 years without established CVD, in primary prevention settings. Index prognostic model The WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model, which estimates future cardiovascular risk using demographic and clinical predictors without requiring laboratory measurements. Comparator No comparator is required, as this review evaluates the external predictive performance of the WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model rather than comparing different prediction models. Outcomes Calibration and discrimination of 10-year CVD risk. Timing Risk prediction is performed at baseline using the WHO non-laboratory-based model, with outcomes predicted over a 10-year time horizon. Setting Primary prevention and routine care settings, including resource-limited contexts where laboratory-based cardiovascular risk assessment is not readily available.

articles.title: Guided bone regeneration with polytetrafluoroethylene titanium-reinforced membrane, CAD/CAM semi-occlusive titanium mesh and CAD/CAM occlusive titanium foil in partially atrophic arches: A comparative randomised controlled trial with 3-year follow-up.
articles.journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of three distinct guided bone regeneration devices, namely non-resorbable polytetrafluoroethylene membrane, semi-occlusive CAD/CAM titanium mesh and occlusive CAD/CAM titanium foil, over a 3-year period, focusing on clinical and radiographic outcomes.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-seven partially edentulous patients with alveolar atrophy requiring guided bone regeneration for implant placement were enrolled and randomly allocated to one of three treatment groups (polytetrafluoroethylene, mesh or foil). Surgical time and surgical satisfaction were assessed and compared among the groups. The present study reports the 3-year clinical outcomes update, including marginal bone loss and complications.

RESULTS: Mean marginal bone loss at 3 years was 0.82 ± 0.46 mm in the polytetrafluoroethylene group, 0.95 ± 0.36 mm in the mesh group and 0.92 ± 0.61 mm in the foil group, with no significant association between device type. Six bone augmentation-related complications occurred, with no significant difference among groups (P = 0.842). Five implant-related complications were recorded among 60 implants (P = 0.730), including one implant failure; no prosthetic failures occurred. Smoking was significantly associated with greater marginal bone loss at 3 years (P = 0.015). CAD/CAM mesh and foil were associated with shorter surgical times and greater surgeon satisfaction than polytetrafluoroethylene membrane.

CONCLUSIONS: All three guided bone regeneration devices were associated with favourable and comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes at 3 years. Customised CAD/CAM titanium mesh and foil maintained good peri-implant bone stability similar to titanium-reinforced polytetrafluoroethylene membrane, while offering advantages in intraoperative handling and surgical time.

articles.title: Expert consensus on clinical practice in pterygoid implant rehabilitation: A modified Delphi study.
articles.journal: International journal of oral implantology (Berlin, Germany)
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pterygoid implants provide distal anchorage in the atrophic posterior maxilla without sinus grafting, but protocols and implant designs vary widely. This study aimed to establish an experience-based consensus on pterygoid implant-anchored rehabilitation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The present authors conducted a two-round modified Delphi survey of 55 surgeons from 25 countries, each with over 5 years of experience and at least 50 pterygoid implants placed. Round 1 comprised 16 open-ended questions and thematic analysis produced 74 closed-ended items for Round 2. Consensus was defined a priori as agreement of at least 70% on a single option or on clinically equivalent options grouped in advance. Reporting followed the ACcurate COnsensus Reporting Document (ACCORD) and Conducting and REporting DElphi Studies (CREDES) guidelines.

RESULTS: All 55 panellists completed both rounds; mean agreement rose from 76% to 89%. Consensus was reached on mandatory CBCT (98%) and a single trajectory: entry distal to the second molar (82%), 30° to 50° posterior-superior angulation (91%), 15° to 35° medial angulation (87%) and an apex between the pterygoid plates (87%). The panel agreed on a tapered 16- to 22-mm implant with a narrow cutting apex and immediate loading when primary stability was adequate (89%); most panellists (62%) consistently required at least 45 Ncm insertion torque. No consensus was achieved on anaesthesia and sedation.

CONCLUSIONS: The panel converged on a common practice pattern for indications, planning, implant design, trajectory and loading. The osteotomy sequence and perioperative care remained operator dependent. These findings describe expert practice, not evidence-based recommendations.

articles.title: Genetic variants of transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy associated with low sensitivity to bone scintigraphy: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Amyloid : the international journal of experimental and clinical investigation : the official journal of the International Society of Amyloidosis
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) is characterized by amyloid deposition and frequently leads to a progressive cardiomyopathy with poor prognosis. Bone scintigraphy with 99mTc-labeled tracers is the cornerstone of noninvasive diagnosis, yet several hereditary TTR variants are associated with false-negative or low-grade tracer uptake.

OBJECTIVES: To identify all TTR variants associated with false-negative bone scintigraphy in hereditary ATTR-CA and discuss clinical implications.

METHODS: Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane were searched from inception to July 2025 per PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included observational studies, case series, and case reports of patients with confirmed ATTR-CA undergoing TTR genetic testing and 99mTc scintigraphy.

RESULTS: Nineteen studies (108 patients) met inclusion criteria. Thirteen pathogenic TTR variants were associated with low or absent uptake (Perugini grade 0-1); p.Val50Met, p.Phe84Leu, and p.Ser97Tyr were most consistently implicated, while p.Val142Ile showed false-negative results in ∼5-10% of carriers. In 11 of 13 variants, advanced structural cardiomyopathy was confirmed despite negative scintigraphy.

CONCLUSIONS: Bone scintigraphy has important limitations in specific hereditary TTR variants. A negative scan does not exclude cardiac involvement in genetically at-risk patients. Multimodal strategies including CMR and histological assessment are essential for timely diagnosis.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Cardiomyocyte Dysfunction and Arrhythmogenesis in a Bleomycin-induced Mouse Model of Group 3 Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Group 3 pulmonary hypertension (PH) occurs when lung diseases induce hypoxic vasoconstriction and pulmonary vascular remodeling. The increase in pulmonary vascular resistance elevates right ventricular (RV) afterload leading to progressive ventricular dysfunction. The mechanisms underlying cardiomyocyte dysfunction in Group 3 PH remain poorly characterized, despite RV pathology representing a critical component of disease progression. Using a mouse model of intratracheal bleomycin-induced PH, we tested the hypothesis that RV function and cardiomyocyte excitation-contraction coupling (ECC) are impaired in PH. Male and female mice were administered intratracheal saline (Sham) or bleomycin to induce PH and assess for sex differences across cardiac parameters. Langendorff-perfused working heart preparations revealed that PH mice display greater RV pressure development, elevated end diastolic pressure, and more spontaneous ventricular arrhythmias versus Sham. Structurally, hearts of PH mice exhibited increased RV hypertrophy and fibrosis versus Sham, with the hypertrophic response more pronounced in males versus females. To assess Ca2+ dynamics and cellular contractile function, enzymatically isolated cardiomyocytes were subjected to electrical field stimulation (0.5-4 Hz, fura-2 dye). RV cardiomyocyte ECC was impaired in PH versus Sham mice, including elevated diastolic Ca2+ and shorter diastolic sarcomere lengths, depressed Ca2+ transient and sarcomere contraction amplitudes, and slower Ca2+ decay rates with slower sarcomere relaxation. Left ventricular (LV) cardiomyocytes did not display these changes. Taken together, these data indicate impairment in RV ECC in the bleomycin-induced PH model, highlighting multiple Ca2+ handling abnormalities that may contribute to the RV dysfunction and arrhythmogenesis observed clinically in PH.

articles.title: 5-hydroxytryptamine 2B Receptor Antagonism with MARY1 Attenuates Maladaptive Repair and Fibrosis Following Ischemic Kidney Injury.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction, persistent inflammation, maladaptive tubular repair and tubulointerstitial fibrosis are major causative factors that contribute to the onset and progression of acute kidney disease (AKD) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Here, we investigate the therapeutic potential of MARY1, a novel, potent, and selective 5-hydroxytryptamine 2B (5-HT2B) receptor antagonist, on multiple key hallmarks known to drive the AKI-to-AKD transition. A mouse model of bilateral ischemia/reperfusion-induced renal injury was used to determine the therapeutic potential of MARY1 in vivo. Primary rabbit renal proximal tubule cells (RPTCs) were used to evaluate the cellular signaling effects of MARY1. Daily administration of MARY1 for 30 days (0.3 mg/kg, i.p.) post-injury restored renal function and mitochondrial biogenesis/dynamics. MARY1 also suppressed epithelial-mesenchymal and endothelial-mesenchymal transition (VE-cadherin, vimentin, FSP1, MMP-9), and reduced renal fibrosis (TGF-β, COL1A1, α-SMA). Furthermore, MARY1 attenuated inflammation as evidenced by downregulated NF-κB signaling and proinflammatory chemokine CXCL10, and augmented anti-inflammatory cytokines IL-9, IL-10, and IL-13. Importantly, MARY1 reduced p53 and p21 expression, indicating alleviated cell-cycle arrest. MARY1 also upregulated genes associated with successful proximal tubule cell repair (ACSM2A), while suppressing genes linked to failed repair (VCAM1 and PDGFRβ). These findings identify MARY1 as a novel, potent and selective 5-HT2B receptor antagonist that restores mitochondrial homeostasis, promotes adaptive tubular repair, and prevents renal fibrosis following renal injury, thereby alleviating early AKD-to-AKD transition. This work highlights 5-HT2B receptor antagonism and MARY1 as a promising therapeutic strategy to improve renal function and early recovery after ischemic injury.

articles.title: Electrifying diversity of the synaptic cleft.
articles.abstract: At synapses, the pre- and the postsynaptic cell are separated by a space of 10-50 nm wide called the synaptic cleft. Electric currents run through this synaptic cleft, particularly during synaptic transmission. Which types of currents, their size and their impact on synaptic transmission has only been systematically evaluated at a few synapses (1-5). Here, we highlight the electrical properties of the synaptic cleft. First, we discuss the subsynaptic distribution of different types of ion channels and their contribution to the cleft current. While the presence of capacitive, voltage-gated calcium, and ionotropic receptor currents at the cleft is uncontroversial, at many synapses voltage-gated potassium and sodium currents are excluded from the cleft. Second, we outline the biophysical relations between the cleft current and geometry, including the cleft potential profile and the cleft equivalent resistance, for four simplified synaptic geometries. Based on recent measurements and theory, cleft resistance does not vary dramatically, ranging between 0.5-40 MΩ for most synapses except for encapsulating synapses, whose resistance can be appreciably higher (up to 80 MΩ). Third, we demonstrate that discernable ephaptic transmission needs cleft currents surpassing 1 nA, or 500 pA for encapsulated synapses. Cleft potentials of a few millivolts may modulate synaptic transmission by changing gating of voltage-dependent channels. Fourth, we survey synaptopathies, in which dysfunctional cleft electrophysiology might be expected, yet evidence for such alterations is currently lacking. We conclude that despite its small size, the synaptic cleft is remarkably good at dissipating the currents that flow during synaptic transmission.

articles.title: Sex-Specific Association of Estrone-Estradiol Balance With B-Type Natriuretic Peptide in Older Adults With Heart Failure.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Estrone (E1), the predominant circulating estrogen after menopause, may exert biological effects distinct from, and potentially opposite to, those of estradiol (E2), raising the possibility that the relative E1/E2 balance has physiological significance. However, the clinical significance of the E1/E2 balance in heart failure (HF) remains unknown. We investigated the associations of circulating E1, E2, and their balance with B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) by sex. We analyzed a multicenter cross-sectional cohort of 260 adults aged 60-89 years (102 men and 68 women with HF; 49 men and 41 women without HF). Associations with ln(BNP) were evaluated using multivariable models with sex interactions. E1 and E2 were analyzed separately and jointly, and the joint model was reparameterized into the E1/E2 balance [ln(E1/E2)] and overall estrogen level [ln√(E1×E2)]. Neither E1 nor E2 was significantly associated with ln(BNP) in separate models. However, in joint models, E1 and E2 showed opposite associations after mutual adjustment, which were reversed between sexes. The E1/E2 balance was positively associated with ln(BNP) in men (β=0.828; P=0.003) but negatively associated in women (β=-0.961; P=0.010) (sex interaction P<0.001). In contrast, overall estrogen level was not associated with ln(BNP) in either sex. Among participants without HF, no sex-dependent pattern was observed, and the balance-by-sex association differed according to HF status (three-way interaction P=0.010). These findings suggest that the E1/E2 balance, rather than overall estrogen level, is a sex-specific hormonal correlate of BNP in older adults with HF.

articles.title: Disentangling the mechanisms of aperiodic neural activity using pluripotent stem cell-derived neural tissue models.
articles.abstract: Neural field potentials contain periodic (rhythmic) and aperiodic (arrhythmic) activity patterns. Both carry physiological information that can be inferred from the shape of the power spectrum. The emergence of pluripotent stem cell (PSC)-derived neural tissue cultures and organoid technology has paved the way for quantifying, with unprecedented access, how aperiodic activity is shaped during the earliest points of cortical development. This review examines how a framework built historically from simulations and recordings from humans and animal models could be applied to neural tissue culture systems to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of aperiodic activity.

articles.title: Physiological Impact of Mechanical Ventilation on Remote Organs.
articles.abstract: Mechanical ventilation is the most widely utilized life support modality worldwide and a necessary, lifesaving intervention in several critical illnesses. Decades of work have elucidated the deleterious impact that injurious ventilator settings have on the lung, which has translated to standard practices of ventilator support that have improved outcomes. Unfortunately, mechanical ventilation is still associated with morbidity and mortality rates that remain unacceptably high. Multiple organ failure is a major cause of death during mechanical ventilation, yet the impact of mechanical ventilation on remote organ systems, such as the brain, heart, and kidney, has received less attention. In this review, we summarize the physiological consequences of mechanical ventilation on extrapulmonary organs and highlight gaps in current knowledge that have precluded the development of novel treatment approaches.

articles.title: Sociodemographic Factors Associated With Hypertension Among People With diabetes: Evidence From Electronic Health Records in Qassim.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes and hypertension are major public health problems in Saudi Arabia. Yet, evidence from Qassim is limited. This study aims to estimate the prevalence of registered diagnosed diabetes and hypertension in 2025 and to examine the association between hypertension and selected characteristics among individuals with diabetes in the Qassim region.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study design has been used. First, we describe registered diagnosed diabetes and hypertension among people with diabetes in 2025. Then, a multivariable logistic regression model was employed to estimate the association between hypertension and covariates: age, type of diabetes, gender, and location.

RESULTS: A total of 63 094 people with diabetes were identified. The crude prevalence registered diagnosed with diabetes in Qassim in 2025 was 21.83% among Saudi adults aged 20 years and older. 42.5% had a concurrent diagnosis of hypertension. The risk of being diagnosed with diabetes and hypertension was significantly higher among females (odds ratio [OR] = 1.274, 95% CI, 1.232-1.318) and type 1 diabetes (OR = 1.274, 95% CI, 1.175-1.381) Moreover, the risk increased significantly with advancing age, with the highest odds observed among individuals aged 65 years and older (OR = 9.880, 95% CI, 9.234-10.571). There was a significant difference in the association between having hypertension and location.

CONCLUSION: Older adults and women with diabetes should be prioritized for hypertension prevention and management. Although location was significantly associated with the odds of hypertension, the observed differences did not suggest a sufficiently distinct geographic pattern. Planning culturally appropriate health promotion interventions to improve the prevention and control of both diabetes and hypertension is recommended.

articles.title: Effectiveness of a culturally tailored nutrition education program on clinical outcomes and diabetes self-management among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Lhokseumawe City, Indonesia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: nutrition education is a cornerstone of diabetes care, but programs that overlook cultural characteristics often have limited long-term effectiveness.

OBJECTIVE: to evaluate the effectiveness of a culturally tailored nutrition education program on clinical outcomes and diabetes self-management among patients with T2DM.

METHODS: a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group study included 128 participants allocated to an intervention group (n = 64) and a control group (n = 64). The intervention group received a culturally tailored nutrition education program for six months, whereas the control group received routine diabetes education. Outcomes included blood glucose, HbA1c, blood pressure, total cholesterol, body mass index (BMI), and diabetes self-management. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Generalized Linear Model Repeated Measures, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: after six months, the intervention group showed significant improvements in all measured outcomes. Mean blood glucose decreased from 236.5 ± 42.8 to 163.2 ± 30.4 mg/dL, HbA1c from 9.48 ± 1.21 % to 7.46 ± 0.82 %, systolic/diastolic blood pressure from 148.5 ± 11.2/92.4 ± 6.8 to 132.8 ± 8.7/82.7 ± 5.0 mmHg, total cholesterol from 224.8 ± 31.5 to 194.7 ± 24.2 mg/dL, and BMI from 26.4 ± 2.9 to 25.2 ± 2.7 kg/m². Self-management scores increased from 56.8 ± 8.9 to 79.8 ± 6.1. Multivariate analysis confirmed significant intervention effects across all outcomes (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: a culturally tailored nutrition education program significantly improves diabetes self-management and clinical outcomes in patients with T2DM, supporting its integration into primary healthcare services.

articles.title: Cold, dark, and hungry: Dynamic transcriptional regulation across eight months of brumation.
articles.abstract: Long-term winter dormancy in ectotherms (brumation) defines the annual cycle of many temperate-zone reptiles, yet the transcriptional regulation that supports survival across months of cold and aphagy remains poorly understood. We generated time-resolved transcriptomic profiles of liver and testis from male red-sided garter snakes (Thamnophis sirtalis parietalis) at five timepoints spanning the eight-month brumation cycle: pre-brumation, early, mid-, and late brumation, and post-arousal under continued aphagy. Time-course negative-binomial regression (maSigPro) followed by gene-set enrichment analysis identified 3,710 transcripts in liver and 5,822 in testis with significant temporal expression structure organized into five overarching temporal patterns: sustained downregulation, downregulation with post-arousal recovery, sustained upregulation, brumation-specific upregulation and cyclic modulation. Liver showed coordinated upregulation of fatty acid mobilization enzymes (ATGL, FOXO1, PPARα) and gluconeogenic regulators (CREBBP, PCK1) coincident with sustained low temperatures. Additionally, low temperature transcriptional activity was suggestive of a shift toward hepatic lipid mobilization and alanine-supported gluconeogenesis. Testis showed sustained suppression of meiosis, reproduction, and DNA-metabolism gene sets that did not fully recover at arousal consistent with this species' dissociated reproductive pattern. Both tissues showed coordinated upregulation of stress-response pathways involving heat-shock proteins, and liver showed upregulation of HIF1α and a glutathione-based antioxidant defense. Interestingly, three vitellogenin transcripts and 17β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases associated with estradiol-favoring steroid metabolism were upregulated in male liver during late brumation, which is not expected during natural physiology in adult males. Together these data support a framework in which temperature- and prolonged aphagy-associated transcriptional programs contribute to survival of one of the longest, coldest brumations documented in a squamate.

articles.title: Sustained Improvement in Time in Range After Automated Insulin Delivery Initiation in Adolescents and Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: A 12-Month Prospective Observational Study From Saudi Arabia.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated insulin delivery (AID) improves glycemic outcomes in trials, but long-term real-world data on comprehensive continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics remain limited in the Middle East.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) initiating Control-IQ (CIQ) or MiniMed 780G (MMG) at King Fahad Medical City, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, between December 2023 and November 2025. Participants were followed for 12 months. Continuous glucose monitoring outcomes included time in range (TIR: 70-180 mg/dL), time above range (TAR), time below range (TBR), glycemic management indicator (GMI), mean sensor glucose, and coefficient of variation (CV) and assessed at baseline and 6 post-initiation time points. Glycated hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) was assessed using paired pre- and post-AID values.

RESULTS: A total of 132 adults were included: 76 using CIQ and 56 using MMG. Mean age was 27.2 ± 7.7 years, 68.9% were female, and mean diabetes duration was 14.5 ± 7.9 years. Time in range increased from 59.0 ± 15.4% at baseline to 72.3 ± 10.2% at 2 weeks and remained sustained at 12 months (73.5 ± 11.5%; +15.1 percentage points; P < .001). Time below range <70 mg/dL decreased from 5.3 ± 5.3 to 1.4 ± 1.2%. Glycated hemoglobin A1c decreased from 7.42 ± 1.13 to 6.52 ± 0.73% (P < .001; n = 106). Time in range ≥70% increased from 29.0% to 71.0%, and HbA1c <7% increased from 30.3% to 74.5%. Severe hypoglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis rates were significantly reduced.

CONCLUSION: In a Saudi tertiary diabetes center, AID initiation was associated with rapid and sustained 12-month improvements in TIR, HbA1c, hypoglycemia exposure, and acute diabetes-related events.

articles.title: Prestroke and Poststroke Physical Activity and Depression, Anxiety, and Fatigue After Ischemic Stroke: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Depression, anxiety, and fatigue are common and disabling long-term sequelae of stroke. Whether habitual physical activity before stroke and engagement in physical activity during recovery are associated with poststroke psychological outcomes remains incompletely understood. We investigated associations between physical activity patterns and psychological outcomes during the first year after ischemic stroke.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, consecutive patients with ischemic stroke enrolled in the STROKE-CARD Registry were assessed for depression, anxiety, and fatigue at either 3- or 12-month follow-up after stroke using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale and Fatigue Severity Scale. Physical activity was assessed before and after stroke with the Baecke Questionnaire. Associations between physical activity and psychological outcomes were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, prestroke and poststroke disability, stroke severity and localization, thrombolysis, prestroke depression, and cognitive impairment.

RESULTS: Within 1050 patients (median age, 70 years; 35% female), 35.3% were screened positive for depression, 29.9% for anxiety, and 53.2% for fatigue at either 3 or 12 months after stroke. Both prestroke and poststroke physical activity were associated with lower odds of depression (adjusted odds ratio, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.36-0.62] and 0.45 [95% CI, 0.34-0.59]; P<0.001) and fatigue (adjusted odds ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.38-0.64] and 0.49 [95% CI, 0.38-0.64]; P<0.001), and with lower odds of anxiety (adjusted odds ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.57-1.00]; P=0.050) and (adjusted odds ratio, 0.71 [95% CI, 0.53-0.94]; P=0.016). High-intensity and high-volume activities were associated with the lowest prevalence of depression and fatigue (depression, 24.5%-25.7%; fatigue, 40.8%-44.1%). Endurance sports were associated with lower rates of depression (22.2%; P<0.001) and fatigue (40.6%; P<0.001), whereas strength training was associated with lower anxiety (12.8%; P=0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: Physical activity before and after stroke was associated with lower odds of depression, anxiety, and fatigue. These findings identify physical activity as a potentially modifiable behavioral factor associated with psychological well-being after stroke and support further evaluation in intervention studies.

articles.title: Tandem ureteral stent in malignant ureteral obstruction: developing clinically based risk-adapted follow-up protocol.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tandem ureteral stents (TUS) improve long-term decompression in malignant ureteral obstruction (MUO). Nevertheless, standardized follow-up is lacking. We aimed to evaluate real-world TUS outcomes and develop a structured, risk-adapted follow-up protocol.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent TUS insertion for MUO at our institution between 2014 and 2024. Stent failure was defined as acute kidney injury, worsening hydronephrosis, or recurrent urinary tract infections requiring stent exchange or percutaneous nephrostomy. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses identified predictors of failure. A Python-based assisted model estimated the cumulative incidence of failure (CIF) at 30, 90, 180, 270, and 365 days. The resulting nomogram enabled risk-group stratification, which was synthesized into a structured, risk-adapted surveillance protocol utilizing a large language model workflow.

RESULTS: Among 224 patients (284 renal-units), median follow-up was 18 months (IQR: 9-37). TUS failure occurred in 77 patients (34.3%) at a median of 7 months (IQR: 4-15). Of those, 52.4% were managed with stent exchange, while 47.6% required nephrostomy. Independent predictors were female sex (HR=2.59, P<0.001), age <65 years (HR=2.19, P<0.001), intra-abdominal surgery (HR=5.90, P<0.001), gynecological malignancy (HR=1.61, P=0.017), and distal stricture (HR=2.43, P=0.007). Model-based stratification classified 40.5% patients as low risk (12-month CIF of 4.1%), 29.6% moderate risk (20%), and 29.9% high risk (51.1%), supporting stent-exchange intervals of 9-12, 6, and 3 months, respectively, with corresponding adjustments to follow-up visits and testing.

CONCLUSIONS: Our risk-stratified model provides a practical framework for individualizing care during the first year after TUS insertion. It aims to reduce the treatment burden for low-risk patients while prioritizing safety for high-risk individuals, and it offers a preliminary, data-driven foundation for balancing clinical safety with optimized resource utilization.

articles.title: Platelet-Derived Factors Enhance Hepatic Endothelial Fenestration and Reduce Early Metabolic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although studies have highlighted the impact of antiplatelet therapies on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), how platelets are involved in liver metabolic dysregulation, especially in the initiation of the disease and its early progression, still remains ill-defined.

METHODS: We used nutritional preclinical murine models that exhibit steatosis and early metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis combined with genetic or pharmacological approaches to modulate platelet count and activation.

RESULTS: Our study is the first to reveal a protective role for blood platelets in maintaining liver homeostasis during the early stages of MASLD. We demonstrate that platelets safeguard the liver microenvironment by mitigating 2 key pathological features of early MASLD, lipid accumulation, and inflammation. Platelets accumulate in liver sinusoidal microvessels under steatosis and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, and ameliorate these disease stages by promoting hepatic vascular permeability and enhancing the fenestration of liver sinusoidal microvessels. Critically, we identify that platelets directly regulate liver sinusoidal endothelial cell activation and fenestration, a vital component of liver microvascular function. Mechanistically, this protective effect is mediated through platelet releasate, which increases liver sinusoidal endothelial cell fenestration via an autocrine nitric oxide-dependent signaling pathway.

CONCLUSIONS: This study uncovers a novel protective role of platelets in the early stages of MASLD by modulating the phenotype of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells and preserving microvascular integrity through their releasate. These findings challenge the prevailing view of platelets as solely detrimental in MASLD and raise important considerations for the timing of antiplatelet therapies in MASLD management.

articles.title: Adaptive Immunity Governs Regional Aortic Remodeling in Hypertension via Perivascular Adipose Tissue Plasticity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension drives heterogeneous aortic remodeling, but the mechanisms underlying regional disparities remain unclear. We hypothesized that T-cell adaptive immunity orchestrates spatial differences in hypertensive vascular dysfunction by modulating perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) phenotype and immune-metabolic crosstalk.

METHODS: Wild-type, lymphocyte-deficient Rag1-/-, and T-cell-reconstituted Rag1-/- mice were subjected to AngII (angiotensin II)-induced hypertension. We integrated biaxial mechanical testing, bulk transcriptomics, and PVAT morphological and secretome analyses to investigate the role of T-cell adaptive immunity in hypertension.

RESULTS: T cells promote maladaptive structural remodeling in the descending thoracic aorta, marked by wall thickening, reduced circumferential stiffness, and inflammatory gene upregulation (Il6, Ccl2) while simultaneously restraining a protective metabolic program (Pparg, Adipoq) in the infrarenal abdominal aorta that promotes hypertensive resilience. PVAT heterogeneity emerged as a key regulator whereby thoracic PVAT maintains a stable resident T-cell population that licenses pathological wall thickening and proinflammatory secretome shifts in response to hypertension. Conversely, the abdominal PVAT niche functions as a dynamic inflammatory environment where T-cell adaptive immunity restrains latent thermogenic plasticity (Ucp1 upregulation). Adaptive immune deficiency unmasked this compensatory abdominal adaptation in Rag1-/- mice, which paradoxically reversed hypertensive stiffening and enhanced vascular compliance. T-cell reconstitution restored the regional hypertensive vascular and PVAT remodeling, confirming that adaptive immunity manages a critical trade-off between structural stability and metabolic plasticity of the aorta-PVAT complex.

CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies PVAT as an immune-metabolic switch governing regional susceptibility to vascular remodeling, offering spatially resolved strategies to preserve aortic compliance in hypertensive disease.

articles.title: Defining Analytic Populations in Randomized Trials: Revisiting the Role of Intention to Treat.
articles.abstract: The primary goal of randomized controlled trials is typically to understand the impact of a treatment on an outcome(s) of interest. Randomization is a critical design component for making these types of cause-and-effect inferences, as it ensures balance between the treatment groups in terms of both known and unknown confounders (factors related to both exposure and outcome), which can introduce bias when imbalanced across exposure (treatment) groups. When comparing treatment groups in the primary analysis of a randomized controlled trial, participants are typically included with the group to which they were randomized, following a framework referred to as intention to treat (ITT). ITT intentionally does not account for postrandomization events (eg, protocol nonadherence) in order to maintain the integrity of the randomization. There are other non-ITT frameworks for randomized controlled trial analyses, including the common per-protocol, as-treated, and modified ITT analyses. This article summarizes ITT and non-ITT frameworks and the research questions which they address, discusses their trade-offs, and provides information about operationalizing randomized controlled trial analyses, including discussion of the available topical guidance, considerations for conducting analyses in the face of missing data, and evolving statistical methods for non-ITT analyses.

articles.title: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation in children and young adults with severe adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias: a single-centre experience.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Left cardiac sympathetic denervation is established for selected high-risk inherited arrhythmia syndromes, but evidence for an intended bilateral strategy in children and young adults remains limited. We evaluated the rationale, feasibility, safety, follow-up ascertainment, and outcomes of intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation.

METHODS: Consecutive children and young adults undergoing intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation between January 2015 and November 2025 were reviewed. The operation targeted the lower stellate component and upper thoracic sympathetic chain bilaterally, usually through single-port thoracoscopic access. Outcomes were obtained from specialist cardiology follow-up, electrocardiography, Holter monitoring, exercise testing when available, inpatient telemetry, device interrogation, and medication records.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients were operated. Mean age was 12.4 years. Bilateral denervation was completed in 36 patients; 1 underwent left-sided denervation only owing to intraoperative haemodynamic instability. Single-port access was used in 30 patients. There were no intraoperative deaths, unplanned full thoracotomy conversions, intercostal injuries, reoperations for surgical complications, or denervation-related permanent pacing. Procedure-attributable morbidity comprised one mild Horner syndrome and one self-limited axillary wound complaint. Among 36 patients with post-discharge follow-up, 32 remained free from the primary malignant ventricular arrhythmic endpoint. Estimated malignant ventricular arrhythmia-free survival was 95.8 per cent at 1 year and 89.4 per cent at 3 years.

CONCLUSION: Intended bilateral cardiac sympathetic denervation was feasible and had low procedure-attributable morbidity in selected young patients. It should be interpreted as an adjunct to multidisciplinary arrhythmia care, not as a replacement for medication, device surveillance, or follow-up.

articles.title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young, Pediatric Heart Failure and Transplantation Committee; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing
articles.abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

articles.title: SPYRAL AFFIRM: One Step in Treatment of Hypertension, One Giant Leap for Renal Denervation.
Heat stress drives contrasting redox shifts in temperate and tropical Drosophila melanogaster embryos.
articles.abstract: Redox balance is central to aerobic metabolism, yet acute heat stress can destabilize this balance by increasing metabolic rates and shifting the balance of critical electron carriers such as NADH. In early Drosophila melanogaster embryos, maintaining redox balance is particularly critical as embryos undergo a developmental redox shift and rely on oxidative phosphorylation to power nuclear divisions. Here, we assayed six isofemale D. melanogaster lines from temperate (Vermont, USA; France; Japan) and tropical (Mexico; Ghana; India) climates to assess metabolic responses to heat in heat-sensitive versus heat-tolerant embryos. We used targeted LC-MS to measure 33 metabolites and the major redox couples (NADH/NAD+, NADPH/NADP+, and GSH/GSSG) at 25°C and after a 32°C heat shock. In all embryos, heat shock induced shared shifts in metabolite profiles, with increases in nucleotide monophosphates (e.g., AMP, CMP, and GMP) and amino acids (e.g., alanine, glutamic acid, serine). In contrast, there were notable differences among genetic lines in the heat-induced responses of redox metabolites. Heat-sensitive temperate lines generally shifted toward a more oxidized state, as indicated by decreases in the NADH/NAD+ ratio, increases in oxidized glutathione, and decreases in the GSH/GSSG ratio, whereas heat-tolerant tropical lines showed little change in redox-couple ratios or, in some cases, shifted toward a more reduced state. These patterns are consistent with greater oxidative stress in the temperate embryos, versus better maintenance of redox balance in tropical embryos. Together, our results suggest that maintaining redox balance is a key element of acute heat tolerance, and healthy development overall, during early embryogenesis.

articles.title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.

METHODS: Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.

RESULTS: Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

articles.title: Venous flow dynamics in post-stroke hemiparetic lower extremity motor dysfunctions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess venous flow impairments in post-stroke hemiparetic lower limbs by comparing venous pump capacity (VPC) and venous refilling time (VRT) between affected and unaffected sides, and to examine their associations with motor function, spasticity, and functional independence.

DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional study.

SETTING: Outpatient Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation and Cardiovascular Surgery clinics at a tertiary care hospital in Türkiye. Participants: Forty-three adults (mean age: 62.6 ± 11.5 years) with hemiparesis persisting ≥ 3 months were included. Patients with hemiplegia, chronic venous disease, peripheral arterial disease, or systemic illness were excluded. Participants were identified via consecutive sampling from existing plethysmographic records.

INTERVENTIONS: Not applicable.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Primary outcomes were VPC and VRT, measured bilaterally using digital photoplethysmography (D-PPG). Secondary measures included Brunnstrom stage, Barthel Index, and Modified Ashworth Scale.

RESULTS: VPC and VRT were significantly reduced in hemiparetic limbs (VPC: 1.07 ± 0.43 vs. 2.24 ± 0.74%; VRT: 9.26 ± 3.42 vs. 19.4 ± 2.0 seconds; p < 0.001), consistent with impaired calf muscle pump function. Interlimb VRT asymmetry decreased with higher Brunnstrom stage (ρ =  -0.35, p = 0.022) and Barthel Index (ρ =  -0.38, p = 0.012) and was associated with hemiparetic side (p = 0.0027), suggesting motor function influences venous return. A borderline association with spasticity (p = 0.066) suggests altered muscle tone may further disrupt hemodynamics. VPC differences showed no significant clinical correlations.

CONCLUSIONS: Hemiparetic limbs exhibit marked venous flow impairment, likely attributable to reduced calf pump activity. This dysfunction may be physiologically linked to motor recovery and functional status. Integrating venous assessment into stroke rehabilitation may help prevent thromboembolic complications and improve circulatory outcomes.

articles.title: More than a fluid: reframing the role of albumin in sepsis.
Parasitological and entomological assessment of onchocerciasis in ivermectin-naïve, hypo-endemic communities of Ogun State, Nigeria: evidence of ongoing transmission.
articles.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
articles.abstract: Onchocerciasis remains a significant public health concern in Africa, particularly in ivermectin-naïve, hypo-endemic communities where transmission may persist undetected. Such areas are highly relevant to the WHO 2030 elimination goals. Ogun State is co-endemic for onchocerciasis, lymphatic filariasis (LF), and Loa loa, creating complex programmatic challenges for mass drug administration (MDA). This study aimed to provide an integrated parasitological and entomological assessment of Onchocerca volvulus prevalence and vector infectivity in three hypo-endemic communities in Ijebu Northeast Local Government Area (LGA), Ogun State, Nigeria. A preliminary longitudinal entomological study was conducted at the Ebute River breeding site serving Idode, Igede, and Orunwa communities in Ijebu Northeast LGA, Ogun State, Nigeria, from February 2023 to January 2024. Human skin snips (n=209) were examined by microscopy and O-150 PCR to determine infection prevalence by community, sex, and age group. Blackflies were collected monthly (7 a.m.-7 p.m.) using Human Landing Collection (HLC); specimens were dissected for parity assessment and screened for O. volvulus infectivity using O-150 PCR. Human PCR prevalence was 14.8% (31/209) compared with 10.0% (21/209) by microscopy. Orunwa had the highest prevalence (23.8% by PCR), followed by Idode (7.1%) and Igede (5.8%). Based on PCR results, Idode and Igede are classified as hypo-endemic, while Orunwa is classified as meso-endemic. Females had higher prevalence than males (24.3% vs 4.1%; P < .001). Age-specific analysis showed elevated PCR prevalence in the 5-20 years age group (17.7%) and the 50+ years age group (42.3%). Entomologically, 418 Simulium damnosum complex flies were collected, with monthly biting rate peaks of 1260 and 1890 bites/person/month during rainy and late rainy seasons, respectively. Parity rates ranged from 52% to 78%. No infective flies were detected, and annual transmission potential for this study is zero. The 14.8% human PCR prevalence provides direct evidence of ongoing onchocerciasis transmission in these ivermectin-naïve communities. The presence of infection across all age groups, including children, confirms active transmission. Although no infective.

articles.title: An online support program for patients with heart failure: Co-designing with patients and heart failure nurses.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Persons with heart failure may need support to manage the symptoms and recommended treatment. Therefore, we aimed to develop an online support program for patients newly diagnosed with heart failure through a co-design process.

METHOD AND RESULTS: The co-design process evolved over four phases: gathering experiences, identifying needs, developing, and finalizing a prototype of the online support program. The process included interviews with oncology nurses with experience of using a support program (n = 7) and workshops with heart failure nurses (n = 5) and patients with heart failure (n = 10). Designers and content creators were also involved in the process. The co-design process resulted in a prototype of a support program "Living with heart failure", including eight modules with a total of 49 web pages that provide information on the diagnosis, treatment, self-care, and lifestyle adaptation. The information is presented in texts, recorded lectures, interviews, pictures, images, and patient narratives. The program includes features such as reporting weight and blood pressure and allows secure messaging between patients and nurses.

CONCLUSION: The co-design method was feasible for developing a support program to be used by patients with heart failure and heart failure nurses. The implementation and effectiveness of the support program remain to be evaluated.

articles.title: Early TSH-FT4 discordance and subsequent biochemical TSH elevation in NICU-admitted neonates: An exploratory retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether relative thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)-free thyroxine (FT4) imbalance on postnatal day 2 was associated with subsequent TSH elevation in neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).Study DesignThis single-center retrospective cohort included 154 NICU-admitted neonates with simultaneous serum TSH, free triiodothyronine, and FT4 measurements on postnatal day 2 and at least one subsequent serum TSH measurement. The primary predictor was the TSH-FT4 Δ score, defined as cohort-standardized TSH minus cohort-standardized FT4. The primary outcome was new threshold crossing or a further TSH increase after day 2 using an operational threshold of >15 mIU/L. Associations were evaluated using Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for gestational age.ResultsEight infants met the primary outcome. Each 1-standard-deviation increase in the day-2 TSH-FT4 Δ score was associated with higher odds of subsequent TSH elevation (adjusted odds ratio, 2.47; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-5.91; p = 0.024). Day-2 TSH, day-2 FT4, and the TSH-FT4 average score showed no clear associations. A three-analyte score incorporating free triiodothyronine showed a similar association.ConclusionRelative TSH-FT4 discordance during early neonatal thyroid testing was associated with subsequent biochemical TSH elevation. These exploratory findings should not be interpreted as establishing a clinical predictive tool and require prospective external validation using standardized follow-up and clinically meaningful thyroid outcomes.

articles.title: The ZebHLH35-ZeTIFY9-ZeSWEET12 module regulates susceptibility to soft rot caused by Pectobacterium carotovorum in coloured calla lily.
articles.abstract: The ornamental and commercial value of coloured calla lily (Zantedeschia elliottiana) is severely reduced by soft rot. Previous studies have demonstrated that Sugars Will Eventually be Exported Transporters (SWEETs) are involved in plant-pathogen interactions. While, the role of SWEETs in coloured calla lily infected with soft rot remains unclear. In this study, transcriptome sequencing and RT-qPCR were used to analyze SWEETs in coloured calla lily infected with Pectobacterium carotovorum (Pc), identifying 17 ZeSWEETs. Among them, ZeSWEET12 markedly responds to Pc infection. Functional characterization revealed that ZeSWEET12 is localized in the plasma membrane and possesses sucrose transport activity, and overexpression of ZeSWEET12 increases the susceptibility of Z. elliottiana to soft rot, whereas silencing ZeSWEET12 enhances plant resistance. Furthermore, yeast one-hybrid screening revealed that ZeTIFY9, a transcription factor related to jasmonic acid (JA) regulation, directly interacts with the promoter of ZeSWEET12 and negatively regulates its expression, whereas ZebHLH35 directly binds to the G-box element in the ZeSWEET12 promoter and positively regulates its expression. Additionally, we confirmed that ZeTIFY9 can interact with ZebHLH35. Our study elucidated a mechanism by which the ZebHLH35-ZeTIFY9-ZeSWEET12 module regulates susceptibility to soft rot in Z. elliottiana, providing new insights and precise genetic targets for future molecular breeding for disease resistance in coloured calla lily.

articles.title: Deprivation Still Costs Lives: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Melanoma Care and Outcomes in England.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Melanoma incidence continues to rise in England, but inequities in cancer outcomes persist despite universal healthcare. Socioeconomic deprivation has been linked to poorer outcomes across several cancer types, yet comprehensive national data on its impact in melanoma are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To examine the influence of socioeconomic status upon malignant melanoma incidence, stage at diagnosis, treatment and outcomes in England.

METHODS: This population-based cohort study included 68,869 patients diagnosed with malignant melanoma in England between 2016 and 2020, identified from the National Disease Registration Service and linked to Hospital Episode Statistics, mortality data and the Systemic Anti-Cancer Therapy (SACT) dataset. Logistic regression examined associations between deprivation (Index of Multiple Deprivation quintiles) and stage at presentation, treatment received and mortality, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates.

RESULTS: Compared with patients in the least deprived quintile, those in the most deprived quintile were diagnosed at a younger median age (62 vs 67 years) and more often with stage 4b disease (10% vs 8%). After adjustment, patients in the least deprived quintile were more likely than those in the most deprived quintile to receive systemic therapies (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.02-1.25, p = 0.02) and less likely to die from any cause within one year (aOR 0.71, 95% CI 0.62-0.82, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In England, living in a more deprived area is modestly associated with more advanced melanoma at diagnosis, lower receipt of systemic therapy and higher one-year mortality. Melanoma awareness, early detection and access to systemic therapy should be targeted towards patients living in the most deprived areas.

articles.title: Elevated serum KIF20A in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploring its potential as a circulating biomarker.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: To evaluate serum KIF20A expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and assess its association with HCC status using a bioinformatics-guided clinical RT-qPCR approach.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 110 participants: 50 with HCC, 10 with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without HCC, and 50 healthy controls. Serum hsa-miR-5192, HSPA1B, LPH02229A/CRHR1-IT1, and KIF20A were quantified by RT-qPCR as relative quantification (RQ). Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) was the conventional comparator. Secondary analyses evaluated AFP with KIF20A using logistic regression, AUC comparison, and repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: KIF20A showed significant overall differential expression (P=0.003), with higher expression in HCC than in healthy controls (P=0.007) and the HCV non-HCC group (P=0.004). Median KIF20A RQ was 2.95 in HCC, 0.40 in healthy controls, and 0.255 in HCV. For HCC versus all non-HCC participants, KIF20A remained associated with HCC after accounting for AFP (OR 2.10 per 1-SD increase in log-transformed KIF20A; 95% CI 1.01-4.37; P=0.048), but the combined model did not materially improve discrimination over AFP alone (AUC 0.968 vs 0.964; DeLong P=0.606).

CONCLUSIONS: Serum KIF20A showed HCC-associated upregulation and retained an exploratory association with HCC after accounting for AFP. However, it did not provide meaningful incremental discrimination beyond AFP; the small disease-control group and absence of external validation preclude claims of HCC specificity or clinical diagnostic readiness.

articles.title: Evaluating Pharmacist Authorship Trends in Leading Emergency Medicine Journals.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pharmacists are essential members of interdisciplinary emergency medicine (EM) teams, yet their involvement in high impact research remains underexplored. This study evaluated trends in pharmacist authorship, specifically in first and last positions, in leading EM journals to assess the pharmacist's role in shaping evidence-based EM practice.

METHODS: The current top four U.S. based EM journals (Academic Emergency Medicine, Western Journal of Emergency Medicine, Annals of Emergency Medicine, and American Journal of Emergency Medicine) were identified via Scientific Journal Ranking scores. PubMed was searched from journal inception through December 31, 2024, using pharmacy affiliated search terms. Randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and case reports were manually reviewed to verify first or last authors holding a PharmD or BSPharm degree. Trends were analyzed using best-fit line slopes.

RESULTS: Of 46,073 articles screened, 811 met inclusion criteria. The American Journal of Emergency Medicine contained the highest number of articles with pharmacists as the first or senior author (n=539). All journals demonstrated an upward trend in pharmacist first and last authorship over the study period, with a significant increase observed over the last decade. In 2024, the American Journal of Emergency Medicine recorded the highest pharmacist authorship (54 authors), while other journals showed more modest but consistent growth.

CONCLUSION: Pharmacists serving in first or senior author roles on research published in high impact EM journals has increased steadily through the lifespan of each journal evaluated.

articles.title: Delayed Recognition of Inferior ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction After Blunt Chest Trauma With Rib Fractures and Severe Right Coronary Artery Stenosis: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Blunt thoracic trauma can produce chest wall pain that obscures concurrent acute coronary syndrome. This report describes delayed recognition of inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) after blunt chest trauma with rib fractures and emphasizes the limitations of attributing the event to a trauma-specific coronary mechanism. CASE REPORT A 56-year-old man developed persistent chest pain immediately after an anterior chest impact. At a local hospital, computed tomography showed fractures of the left seventh to ninth ribs, and no electrocardiogram (ECG) was initially obtained. Approximately 11 hours after injury, the first ECG showed inferior STEMI. He was transferred 13 hours after symptom onset; his pain had improved, he was hemodynamically stable, and repeat ECG showed ST-segment resolution with Q-wave formation. The cardiac troponin I level was 8.05 ng/mL on arrival and later peaked at 48 ng/mL. Coronary angiography on hospital day 10 showed approximately 90% stenosis of the proximal-to-mid right coronary artery. After balloon predilatation, optical coherence tomography showed a complex lipid-rich lesion with thrombotic features and localized dissection. Because imaging was performed after predilatation, the original mechanism could not be established. Percutaneous coronary intervention restored Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 3 flow. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging 5 days later confirmed an ischemic-pattern infarction in the right coronary artery territory with microvascular obstruction. CONCLUSIONS Persistent or unexplained chest pain after blunt thoracic trauma warrants early ECG and troponin testing, even when rib fractures are present. Post-predilatation intracoronary imaging can characterize a culprit lesion but cannot, by itself, establish that trauma caused plaque disruption or coronary dissection.

articles.title: Ultrasound Shear Wave Elastography for Liver Stiffness and Attenuation Imaging for Liver Steatosis in Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Fatty Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is a prevalent chronic liver condition. Non-invasive assessment of hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness using attenuation imaging (ATI) and shear wave elastography (SWE) has become increasingly important in clinical practice. However, the association between ATI-defined steatosis grades and SWE-based liver stiffness categories in patients with MAFLD remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between ATI-based steatosis severity and SWE-based stiffness category in MAFLD. MATERIAL AND METHODS A total of 739 consecutive patients with MAFLD who underwent both ATI and SWE examinations between December 2022 and October 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Hepatic steatosis was graded using ATI (S0-S3), and liver stiffness was categorized using SWE according to established clinical cut-off values. Descriptive statistics, Spearman correlation analysis, and the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test were performed to evaluate the association between ATI and SWE measurements and categories. RESULTS Both ATI and SWE measurements showed non-normal distributions. A weak but statistically significant positive correlation was observed between ATI and SWE values (Spearman's R=0.097, P=0.008), whereas Pearson correlation did not show a statistically significant linear association (R=0.066, P=0.073). The Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test showed no statistically significant association between ATI-defined steatosis grades and SWE-based liver stiffness categories (P=0.063), with a small effect size (Cramer's V=0.083). Notably, most patients in the indeterminate liver stiffness category were classified as having S2 or S3 steatosis. CONCLUSIONS ATI and SWE measurements showed a weak positive association in patients with MAFLD, whereas no significant association was found between ATI steatosis grades and SWE stiffness categories.

articles.title: Barriers to post-stroke hand function recovery: A Delphi-based expert consensus on contributing factors and rehabilitation strategies.
articles.journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke hand function impairment affects 60-70% of survivors at six months, persisting despite abundant guidelines that rarely differentiate protocols by Brunnstrom recovery stages-creating a critical gap in stage-specific guidance for Stage III challenges like synergistic overflow.

PURPOSE: To achieve expert consensus on primary barriers, neurophysiological mechanisms, and most effective rehabilitation strategies for hand function recovery in stroke survivors specifically at Brunnstrom Stage III.

STUDY DESIGN: Modified three-round e-Delphi consensus study.

METHODS: Purposive sampling recruited 15 Indian neurorehabilitation experts (8 academicians with ≥10 years teaching/3 recent publications, 7 clinicians with ≥5 years experience/≥20% stroke caseload) from 50 invitees (30% response rate). Round 1 used three open-ended questions yielding 42 themes refined to 28 Likert-scale items (Supplementary Files S1-S2). Rounds 2-3 rated agreement (≥70%=strong consensus); thematic analysis and descriptive statistics (mean %, 95% CI) applied.

RESULTS: Finger extensor weakness achieved highest consensus as primary barrier (81.2% mean agreement, 95% CI ±5.6%). Motor Relearning Program (MRP: 80.5%, ±4.9%) and Neurodevelopmental Therapy (NDT: 76.4%, ±5.4%) emerged as top strategies. Brunnstrom Stage III challenges (synergistic overflow, movement initiation: 67.2%, ±6.5%) reached moderate consensus; low-consensus items included robotics (38.7%) due to resource constraints.

CONCLUSION: Muscle weakness-particularly finger extensors-dominates Stage III hand recovery barriers; MRP and NDT offer highest-priority interventions. Clinicians should prioritize stage-specific strengthening protocols over generic approaches, informing tailored guidelines for resource-limited settings.
