REGISTRATION NO: - Ethical approval for the study was granted by the Institutional Ethics Committee (Approval No. LPU/SOP/50/210527/15619/002).

articles.title: FGF23 and Cardiac Remodeling in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Rapid Review and Exploratory Quantitative Synthesis.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), elevated left ventricular mass index (LVMI), diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, and cardiovascular mortality are common in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) rises early in CKD and is linked to cardiac remodeling, but consistency across studies is unclear. We conducted a rapid review of FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD, incorporating a reanalyzed unpublished single-center cohort, and pooled effect estimates where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics. A structured web-based search (August 2026) identified 11 candidate studies on FGF23 and cardiac outcomes in CKD; 9 met eligibility, including 1 unpublished investigator-held cohort (n = 80) reanalyzed for this review. Pooling (inverse variance) was performed only where at least 2 studies reported comparable metrics; all pooled estimates are exploratory, below the prespecified 3-study minimum. For FGF23 and LVH, using a derived LVH variable from the present cohort, a pooled log-FGF23 odds ratio (OR) across 2 adult-CKD studies (n = 242) was 1.33 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.92-1.93), I2 = 78%; a pediatric study (OR 2.53, n = 587) was consistent in direction but unpooled. For LVMI, correlations were not pooled; a Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort cohort showed higher LVMI only in the top quartile. For heart failure/cardiovascular mortality, a pooled hazard ratio across 2 studies (n = 374) was 2.37 (95% CI 1.47-3.84), I2 = 0%, with LVMI mediating only 7-22% in Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort. FGF23 was not significantly associated with diastolic dysfunction after adjustment (OR 1.51/standard deviation, 95% CI 0.92-2.47). The available evidence, though sparse and heterogeneous, is directionally consistent with a positive FGF23-cardiac remodeling association in CKD. Certainty is very low throughout; a full multi-database search is needed before a definitive conclusion.

articles.title: Not a panacea: the role of presenting descriptive statistics and effect sizes in abstracts on medical students' misconceptions about p-values.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most scientific studies report inferential statistical results using p-values. For clinical decision-making, correctly interpreting the results of significance tests is particularly important, for example, to differentiate between statistical significance and clinical relevance. However, p-values are frequently misinterpreted, and reporting effect sizes alongside p-values has therefore been recommended to support the interpretation of statistical results.

METHODS: We examined 121 medical students' misconceptions about p-values when presented with three fictitious but realistic medical abstracts containing comparisons of group means and t-tests. Medical context, sample size, p-value, and effect size were systematically varied across the abstracts (abstract 1: N1 = N2 = 7,500; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 0.12; abstract 2: N1 = N2 = 10; p = 0.04; Cohen's d = 1.00; abstract 3: N1 = N2 = 40; p = 0.09; Cohen's d = 0.38). We varied the amount of statistical information provided in each abstract (information set 1: sample size and p-value; information set 2: sample size, p-value, means, and standard deviations; information set 3: the same information and effect size Cohen's d). We examined whether additional statistical information was associated with fewer misconceptions and how the provided information influenced students' perceived effect size.

RESULTS: In all versions, a high proportion of medical students across all semesters of study demonstrated multiple misconceptions about p-values. The number of endorsed misconceptions substantially decreased with the provision of more statistical information only in the context with a large sample size, a statistically significant result, and a very small effect size. In this context, providing additional statistical information reduced the tendency to infer clinical relevance and effect magnitude directly from statistical significance.

CONCLUSIONS: Although reporting standardized effect sizes has repeatedly been recommended, their inclusion alone appears insufficient to prevent mis- and overinterpretations of inferential statistical results. The interpretation of statistical evidence should be addressed more intensively and longitudinally throughout medical education, including by explicitly addressing typical misconceptions. Alternative teaching approaches to statistical inference, including simulation-based approaches, should also be considered.

articles.title: Pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL): a practical clinical guide to contrast-free cerebral perfusion imaging in stroke and steno-occlusive disease.
articles.abstract: The past decade has witnessed the emergence of multiple arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based imaging techniques, with growing evidence supporting their utility across diverse neurological diseases. ASL represents a paradigm shift in perfusion imaging as a noninvasive, contrast-free MRI technique that provides both cerebral perfusion quantification and detection of arterial stenosis or occlusion, offering diagnostic capabilities comparable to the established dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) technique while avoiding contrast-related risks. This review article provides a focused clinically oriented overview of Pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) technique in stroke imaging, discusses the fundamental physical principles of arterial spin labeling, examines various acquisition and optimization strategies, and evaluates clinical applications with primary emphasis on acute ischemic stroke and steno-occlusive cerebrovascular disease, the predominant risk factor for recurrent stroke.

articles.title: A Journey Through Development of Pediatric Endocrinology in India : Based on 19th Dr. K. C. Chaudhuri and Dr. Amala Chaudhuri Oration​, on 4th October 2026.
articles.abstract: Pediatric endocrinology offers an intellectually stimulating clinical career marked by the opportunity to manage complex, highly varied hormonal disorders and witness the tangible impacts of treatment on childhood growth and development. Pediatric endocrinology emerged as a distinct medical subspecialty in the United States during the 1940s, pioneered by Dr. Lawson Wilkins in Baltimore and Dr. Nathan Talbot at in Boston. Dr. Andrea Prader of Zurich is credited with founding the Pediatric Endocrine Club in Europe 1962. The credit for organizing the first national symposium in India is given to Dr. Meena Desai. She along with Dr. PSN Menon and Dr. P. Raghupathy and several colleagues helped to set up the Indian Society for Pediatric and Adolescent Endocrinology. Training programs began in the major institutions in India as short and long-term fellowships for pediatric faculty which developed into post-doctoral certificate and DM training courses. There is a pronounced paradigm shift within pediatric endocrinology away from generalized clinical care and toward specialized, data-driven registries and highly targeted clinical programs.

articles.title: Molecular evidence of vector/blood borne and hemotropic bacteria in dogs and cats from El Salvador, Central America.
articles.abstract: Latin America's high biodiversity, together with socioeconomic and ecological conditions, favors the persistence of vectors and vector-borne bacterial pathogens in domestic animals. Data on vector-borne pathogens in domestic dogs and cats in Central America remain limited, and reports from El Salvador are scarce. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence of Bartonella spp., Anaplasma spp., Ehrlichia spp., and hemotropic Mycoplasma spp. in domestic dogs and cats from the metropolitan area of San Salvador, El Salvador. For this purpose, blood samples were collected from 269 dogs and 59 cats in veterinary clinics. Four feline (6.78%; 95% CI: 2.67-16.18%) and one canine (0.37%; 95% CI: 0.07-2.08%) samples were positive for Bartonella spp. by a quantitative real-time TaqMan based PCR (qPCR) based on the NADH dehydrogenase gamma subunit (nuoG) gene. In a TaqMan-based multiplex qPCR targeting the gene encoding the 60-kDa heat shock protein (groEL gene), whereas 19 canine (7.06%; 95% CI: 4.57-10.77%) and our feline (6.78%; 95% CI: 2.67-16.18%) samples were positive for Ehrlichia spp., eight canine (2.97%; 95% CI: 1.51-5.76%) and one feline (1.69%; 95% CI: 0.30-9.00%) samples were positive for Anaplasma spp. Five feline (8.47%; 95% CI: 3.67-18.35%) and three canine (1.12%; 95% CI: 0.38-3.23%) samples were positive in a SYBRGreen-based qPCR targeting the 16 S rRNA gene of hemotropic Mycoplasma spp. Sequencing and phylogenetic analyses allowed the identification of Bartonella henselae in four (one dog and three cat samples) of the five Bartonella-positive animals, and 'Candidatus Mycoplasma haemominutum' in three out of five hemoplasma-positive cats analyzed. In dogs, hemoplasma species could not be determined due to the lack of sequencing data. The Anaplasma spp. and Ehrlichia spp. positive samples did not yield amplicons in the conventional PCR assays for sequencing, precluding molecular identification at the species level. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of Bartonella spp. and hemoplasmas in domestic dogs and cats from El Salvador and the first molecular evidence of Anaplasma spp. and Ehrlichia spp. in domestic cats in the country.

articles.title: Evaluation of a rapid batch export system for electroretinography waveform data.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Accurate application of electroretinography (ERG) remains challenging due to the heterogeneity of retinal disorders. Despite its potential as a diagnostic tool, the clinical use of ERG is limited by the expertise required for interpretation and the error-prone manual extraction of waveform data. At scale, waveform analysis in academic research and clinical trials is made difficult by these challenges. This study performed external validation and quality assessment of automated compared to manual extraction and collection of raw ERG waveforms.

METHODS: Raw waveform data was collected using International Society for Clinical Electrophysiology of Vision (ISCEV) standard ERG studies from the ophthalmology practice at Columbia University. A recently developed automated batch exporting tool (Espion, Diagnosys LLC, Lowell, MA) was used to retrieve and compile data and compare with manually collected data for 357 patient sessions.

RESULTS: The automated and manually exported data had 99.75% ± 0.17% similarity using a Jaccard similarity test, suggesting the automated tool is both rapid and highly accurate. We identified several inconsistencies leading to errors in the automated batch export. The most common errors in compiled batch exported data included: improperly merging two ERG files taken on the same day and lack of accounting for missing data.

CONCLUSIONS: Use of batch export with manual oversight for sources of potential error can allow for faster, more effective data gathering and analysis of large-scale ERG waveform datasets in academic and clinical trial settings.

articles.title: Er: YAG laser for lip and perioral remodelling with emphasis on SMOOTH® mode: a systematic review of clinical evidence.
articles.abstract: This review aimed to assess the current evidence on the use of Er: YAG laser for non-injective lip and perioral aesthetic remodelling, with emphasis on SMOOTH® mode and to determine whether the reported treatment outcomes reflect true lip-volume augmentation or perceived fullness resulting from tissue remodelling. A systematic literature search was conducted in MEDLINE/PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library, with no date restrictions. Studies were eligible if they reported clinical outcomes after 2940-nm Er:YAG laser treatment relevant to the lips, labial mucosa, perioral region, nasolabial folds, or anatomically related areas. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized or split-face randomized studies and ROBINS-I for non-randomized prospective studies. Five studies involving 80 participants across mixed facial cohorts were included; only a subset received labial or isolated perioral treatment. Two studies were classified as Level 2b evidence and two as Level 4 evidence. No study measured objective lip volume, vermilion height, lip projection, Cupid's bow definition or validated lip-specific fullness outcomes. One study measured upper-lip morphology with three-dimensional stereophotogrammetry, reporting shortening of the philtral length and a decreased nasolabial angle, but did not quantify lip volume. Evidence was more consistent for perioral rejuvenation, nasolabial fold remodelling, rhytid reduction, dermal thickening, skin texture improvement, and collagen remodelling. Reported adverse events were generally transient, although post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation and labial herpes simplex reactivation were clinically relevant safety considerations. Current evidence supports Er:YAG laser as a biologically plausible and clinically promising modality for perioral rejuvenation and tissue-quality improvement. However the five eligible studies were heterogeneous, drew on mixed facial cohorts, and only one of them assessed the labial unit directly, measuring upper-lip morphology rather than volumeThe evidence is therefore insufficient to demonstrate true objective lip-volume augmentation - though this does not mean such augmentation does not occur. Er:YAG laser should be described as a non-injective remodelling approach that may enhance perceived fullness through tissue remodelling, rather than as a proven volumetric substitute for injectable fillers, and its effects should not be extrapolated between modalities.

articles.title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared.

RESULTS: Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. 4.3%, p = 0.048).

CONCLUSION: Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

articles.title: Childhood arterial ischemic stroke revealing Kyphoscoliotic Ehlers-Danlos syndrome due to PLOD1 deficiency: expanding the cerebrovascular phenotype.
Vacuum-assisted elevation as a minimally invasive strategy for ping-pong skull fractures: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ping-pong skull fractures, although rare, represent a distinctive form of depressed skull fracture that primarily affects newborns and infants following traumatic brain injury, birth-related trauma, or compression during delivery. Due to the high malleability of the cranial vault at this age, the application of negative pressure over the depressed area has emerged as a minimally invasive therapeutic alternative capable of promoting bone elevation through local suction. The present study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of this technique in the treatment of ping-pong skull fractures.

METHODS: A systematic search of publications was conducted in databases including PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, covering studies published up to April 2026. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Case Series. Data analysis was performed using RStudio (version 2026.01.1).

RESULTS: Among the included studies, comprising a total of 81 patients, complete elevation of the ping-pong skull fracture was achieved in 86.52% of cases (95% CI 71.81-94.17; I2 = 25.0%). General complications were reported in 9.82% of patients (95% CI 4.84-18.90; I2 = 0%). The pooled rate of patients requiring a subsequent surgical approach after vacuum-assisted treatment was 10.58% (95% CI 3.95-25.40; I2 = 0%).

CONCLUSION: The vacuum-assisted elevation represents a therapeutic option for PPF, showing encouraging results across clinical, radiological and safety outcomes. However, more and larger studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Natural polyacetylenes induce heat shock protein gene expression and enhance heat tolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana.
articles.abstract: Heat waves negatively impact crop growth and quality. Chemical priming, which enhances plant stress tolerance through treatment with natural compounds, offers a promising strategy. While established chemical priming agents such as acetic acid and ethanol are well-researched, it is crucial to identify novel compounds. To that end, we investigated the stress response-inducing activity of various wild plant extracts using an Arabidopsis thaliana reporter gene assay. This revealed that falcarindiol, a polyacetylene found in Chamaele decumbens, induces a heat stress response (HSR). Arabidopsis treated with falcarindiol exhibited increased expression of three genes of different HSP families and improved heat tolerance. Atractylodin, another polyacetylene that induced HSR in Arabidopsis, inhibited the chaperone activity of wheat germ extract in a dose-dependent manner. In contrast, 2,4-hexadiyne - 1,6-diol, a polyacetylene that did not enhance HSR, showed no inhibitory activity. Since previous studies indicate that inhibitors of HSP chaperone activity induce HSR in plants, falcarindiol and atractylodin may alleviate heat stress through a similar mechanism. In conclusion, it was shown that some natural polyacetylenes exhibit a chemical priming effect.

articles.title: Intra-sulcular compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel for procedural pain during ultrasonic scaling: a randomized, single-blind, split-mouth, sham-controlled superiority trial in adults with plaque-induced gingivitis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate whether intra-sulcular application of a compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel (Kami-Gel) reduces procedural pain during ultrasonic supragingival scaling in adults with plaque-induced gingivitis compared with a sham procedure.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single-center, randomized, single-blind, split-mouth, sham-controlled superiority trial was conducted involving 114 adults with plaque-induced gingivitis. Participants received a sequential split-mouth treatment. The test side received intra-sulcular application of Kami-Gel, while the control side received a sham application (mimicked injection). The primary outcome was procedural pain intensity measured on a 0-10 Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Secondary outcomes included the number of pain complaints, procedural duration, patient satisfaction, and plaque index (PI). Safety was assessed immediately and at 24 h.

RESULTS: All 114 participants completed the study. Median VAS score was significantly lower in the test group (1.7 [IQR: 0.62-2.58]) than the control group (4.1 [IQR: 2.42-5.7]), with an estimated treatment difference of - 2.35 (95% CI: -3.0 to - 1.7)-the upper limit of which fell below the pre-specified superiority margin of - 1.2, confirming superiority (P < 0.001). The test group also demonstrated significantly fewer pain complaints (median 0 vs. 1), shorter procedural duration (median 10 vs. 12 min), and higher patient satisfaction (all P < 0.001). Post-scaling plaque index was significantly lower in the test group (median 0.75 [IQR: 0.55-0.86] vs. 0.89 [IQR: 0.75-0.96]; P < 0.001), though this difference may reflect improved patient cooperation rather than a direct pharmacological effect. No adverse events were reported.

CONCLUSIONS: Intra-sulcular application of compound chamomile and lidocaine hydrochloride gel reduces procedural pain during ultrasonic supragingival scaling compared to a sham procedure. Its use was associated with shorter active scaling time and higher satisfaction. Whether these acute benefits translate to improved long-term periodontal treatment compliance warrants further investigation.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Intra-sulcular application of compound chamomile and lidocaine gel (Kami-Gel) prior to ultrasonic supragingival scaling reduces procedural pain and was associated with higher patient satisfaction. A lower post-scaling plaque index was observed in the test group, potentially attributable to improved patient cooperation during instrumentation. This safe, non-injectable chairside technique provides clinicians a practical tool to enhance patient comfort during scaling procedures.

articles.title: Targeting neuroinflammation in diabetic peripheral neuropathy: Mechanistic perspectives, phytochemical pharmacology, and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a debilitating neurodegenerative complication of diabetes mellitus characterized by the convergence of metabolic dysregulation, microvascular ischemia, and chronic low-grade neuroinflammation. While intensive glycemic control and cardiometabolic risk-factor modification slow neuropathy progression-most notably in type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM)-approved central analgesic pharmacotherapies primarily manage nociceptive symptoms without directly reversing established structural axonal loss. Preclinical studies indicate that endoneurial inflammation mediated via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB), and the nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich-containing family, pyrin domain-containing-3 (NLRP3) inflammasome contributes to microvascular dysfunction and Schwann cell dedifferentiation. Investigational phytochemicals, including curcumin, resveratrol, berberine, and quercetin, modulate these inflammatory and oxidative nodes in experimental rodent models. However, clinical translation remains constrained by poor aqueous solubility, extensive phase II enterocytic and hepatic conjugation, active efflux, and restricted transport across the diseased blood-nerve barrier (BNB). Using a structured narrative synthesis and a three-tier evidence hierarchy, this Brief Report distinguishes established human pathogenic and clinical trial evidence from preclinical mechanistic findings, critically evaluates clinical trial limitations (sample size, duration, and subjective endpoints), and defines rigorous pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic criteria required to validate nanocarrier-mediated endoneurial target engagement.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of thromboembolic adverse events associated with osimertinib using the Japanese adverse drug event report database.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the disproportionality, times to onset, and outcomes of thromboembolic adverse events (AEs) associated with osimertinib using data from the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database (JADER), with a specific focus on real-world evidence from Japan, an East Asian country with high EGFR mutation prevalence. We analyzed JADER data from April 2004 to December 2024. Disproportionality was assessed by calculating reporting odds ratios (RORs). Time-to-onset was evaluated, and Weibull distribution parameters were calculated for major AEs with detected signals, while rare AEs were summarized descriptively. Among 3,221,393 reports, 7134 AEs were associated with osimertinib, including 153 thromboembolic AEs. Significant disproportionality signals were detected for six thromboembolic AEs: deep vein thrombosis (ROR = 2.89), pulmonary embolism (ROR = 2.78), embolism venous (ROR = 6.64), peripheral vein thrombosis (ROR = 3.16), pulmonary artery thrombosis (ROR = 2.93), and thrombophlebitis migrans (ROR = 7.49). Median onset times ranged from 28 to 85 days after osimertinib initiation. Weibull analysis of major thromboembolic AEs suggested no clear time-dependent increase in reporting frequency over time (random failure type). Fatal outcomes were observed for several thromboembolic AEs, particularly pulmonary embolism and pulmonary artery thrombosis. Several thromboembolic AEs associated with osimertinib were identified, including potentially fatal events. These findings suggest that thromboembolic events may be reported relatively early after the initiation of osimertinib treatment and highlight the importance of clinical awareness and appropriate monitoring during treatment. However, these findings do not establish a causal relationship between osimertinib and thromboembolic events.

articles.title: Roxadustat for treatment of suspected erythropoietin(EPO)-induced pure red cell aplasia in a hemodialysis patient: a case report.
articles.abstract: Anemia is a prevalent complication in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), particularly those undergoing dialysis. Recombinant human erythropoietin (rhEPO) is widely administered to patients both on and off dialysis to manage this anemia. However, despite an initial favorable therapeutic response, a sudden and unexplained decline in hemoglobin (Hb) levels often prompts the need for further diagnostic evaluation. In this context, we report a clinical case involving a 48-year-old male patient who had been undergoing hemodialysis (HD) for two years. During the course of his rhEPO treatment regimen, he may have developed pure red cell aplasia (PRCA), a rare but serious adverse reaction. Upon recognition of this complication, the administration of rhEPO was promptly discontinued, and the patient was initiated on roxadustat therapy. Following nine months of continuous roxadustat treatment, the patient experienced a significant and sustained increase in his Hb levels. This clinical outcome underscores the importance of prompt diagnosis and intervention in cases of suspected erythropoietin (EPO)-induced PRCA. Furthermore, our findings suggest that roxadustat may serve as a viable and effective therapeutic option for patients with suspected EPO-induced PRCA, potentially obviating the need for immunosuppressive therapy and its associated risks.

articles.title: Hearing Preservation and Efficacy Outcomes in CI632 Recipients with Sloping High-Frequency Hearing Loss: Multicenter Trial Results.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adults with substantial residual low-frequency (LF) hearing are increasingly considered for cochlear implantation. This study evaluated hearing preservation and speech performance outcomes using a slim perimodiolar electrode (CI632) in adults under expanded indications.

METHODS: In a prospective, open-label, single-arm feasibility trial at three US tertiary centers, ten adults with LF thresholds ≤50 dB HL at 500 Hz, sloping high-frequency loss, and aided CNC scores ≤60% in the ear to be implanted received the CI632 device. Participants were followed for 12 months postactivation. Assessments included air and bone conduction audiometry, electrode impedances, unilateral and bilateral CNC in quiet and AzBio sentences in noise, patient-reported outcomes, and postoperative computerized tomography (CT) imaging.

RESULTS: The LF pure-tone average (125-500 Hz) showed a mean shift of 19.3 dB at activation and remained stable at 22.4 dB at 12 months. Impedances were stable across visits. Due to preserved acoustic hearing, all participants utilized electric-acoustic stimulation in the implant ear. Speech recognition improved significantly across all measures, with an average improvement at 12 months ranging from 22 to 54 percentage points, depending on the condition. Patient-reported outcomes also improved. CT imaging confirmed scala tympani placement for all electrodes, with a mean angular insertion depth and wrapping factor of 406.6° and 59.4%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The slim perimodiolar electrode can preserve LF acoustic hearing in adults implanted under expanded indications, with meaningful improvements observed in both objective and subjective outcomes. Hearing preservation outcomes in this cohort exceeded those typically reported for perimodiolar arrays. While all participants achieved functionally aidable hearing preservation, the small sample size limits the generalizability of this finding, and larger studies are needed to confirm these results.

articles.title: Intratympanic Steroid Regimen for Prevention of Cisplatin-Induced Hearing Loss: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin exhibits a steep dose-response relationship, wherein its therapeutic efficacy increases significantly with higher doses. This dose escalation, however, is limited by severe adverse effects, notably ototoxicity, which can lead to permanent and disabling hearing loss. The objective of this review was to evaluate the potential efficacy of intratympanic steroid administration (ITD) in preventing cisplatin-induced hearing loss (CiHL).

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Scopus databases for evidence-based research articles published between January 2004 and July 2023. The search strategy focused on intratympanic steroids for cisplatin-related ototoxicity. Two independent reviewers performed the search, screening, and study selection according to predefined Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Study design (PICOS) criteria. Only randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving patients receiving cisplatin and treated with an intratympanic steroid regimen were included. The review process adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.

RESULTS: The initial database and manual searches identified 383 records. Following title and abstract screening, 42 articles underwent full-text review. After applying the eligibility criteria, 38 studies were excluded, resulting in four RCTs for qualitative synthesis. Risk of bias (RoB) assessment revealed a high-risk concerning allocation concealment in all four studies. Additionally, a substantial risk of detection bias was present in three RCTs. According to the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations (GRADE) framework, the overall quality of evidence was rated as high in one study, moderate in two, and low in one.

CONCLUSION: This review did not confirm a consistent otoprotective benefit of intratympanic steroid administration against CiHL. None of the included studies demonstrated high-quality evidence for a significant protective effect. The available RCTs report inconsistent outcomes and collectively fail to establish a definitive therapeutic advantage for ITD in this context. These discrepancies may be attributable to methodological variations across studies, including differences in steroid dosage, concentration, timing of administration relative to cisplatin therapy, and patient populations. Further rigorously designed RCTs with standardized protocols are warranted to definitively assess the potential role of ITD in mitigating cisplatin ototoxicity.

articles.title: Intracranial Subdural Empyema Associated with Streptococcus Dysgalactiae Subsp. Equisimilis in a Patient with Chronic Subdural Hematomas.
articles.abstract: A 73-year-old man with conservatively managed bilateral chronic subdural hematomas presented with fever and vomiting, followed by a seizure and impaired consciousness. Craniotomy revealed subdural pus, supporting intracranial subdural empyema arising in these hematomas. Streptococcus dysgalactiae subsp. equisimilis (SDSE) was recovered from blood and subdural cultures, although a polymicrobial infection could not be excluded because subdural sampling followed antibiotic initiation. He improved after drainage and four weeks of antibiotic treatment. SDSE bacteremia with neurological deterioration should prompt consideration of subdural empyema. Hematogenous seeding was considered to be the most likely route of infection.

articles.title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Preceded by Vocal Fold Atrophy.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that affects the upper and lower motor neurons of the brain and spinal cord, ultimately leading to respiratory failure. Vocal fold atrophy (VFA) is characterized by vocal fold arch atrophy, prominent vocal processes, and a spindle-shaped glottis gap. We herein report an 81-year-old male patient diagnosed with ALS shortly after VFA onset. VFA is generally associated with aging and Parkinson's disease; however, our report indicates that dysphonia may precede bulbar symptoms, and VFA is a suggestive sign in an atypical ALS diagnosis.

articles.title: A Pragmatic Framework for Lifetime-oriented eGFR Trajectory Assessment in Japanese Primary Care and Health Screening.
articles.abstract: Objective　Chronic kidney disease (CKD) risk assessment relies on estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and albuminuria, but urine testing is not always available, and cross-sectional eGFR may miss a sustained decline. We developed the long-term eGFR slope-eGFR-age (LSEA) score to structure long-term eGFR trajectories using the Long-term eGFR Plot (LTEP).Methods　Long-term eGFR slope was estimated by the linear regression of serial eGFR measurements. Projected age at eGFR 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 was calculated under a linear "if unchanged" assumption as a lifetime-oriented trajectory marker. The LSEA score integrated categorized slope, most recent eGFR, and age, with a high category defined as ≥7. We studied 500 consecutive Japanese primary-care patients from seven clinics with at least 5 years of follow-up and 3,315 health-screening participants with at least five eGFR measurements. A descriptive dialysis-initiation series examined the first high LSEA assessment in 14 patients.Results　In the primary-care cohort, 53.6% had eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and the median long-term eGFR slope was -1.0 mL/min/1.73 m2/year. Overall, 31.8% were projected to reach eGFR 10 before age 100, including 21.1% of those with eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2. LSEA showed a clearer ordering of projected trajectories than eGFR alone or eGFR plus slope, with similar ordering observed in the health-screening cohort. In the dialysis-initiation series, the first high LSEA assessment occurred from 4-20 years before dialysis initiation.Conclusion　LSEA may provide a pragmatic flagging framework to identify longitudinal eGFR trajectories warranting individualized clinical review. LTEP-based assessment may support interpretation, but outcome-based validation is still required.

articles.title: Autoantibodies in Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Endocrinopathies.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have been established as a standard treatment for many types of cancer; however, they present a clinical challenge due to unique side effects known as immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Endocrine irAEs include the more frequently reported thyroid and pituitary dysfunctions, as well as less frequent, but potentially severe conditions, such as ICI-related type 1 diabetes and primary adrenal insufficiency. These can lead to life-threatening complications, thus requiring careful management. Their pathogenesis is thought to be an autoimmune response. Recent reports have identified various autoantibodies in patients with endocrine irAEs, drawing attention to their clinical significance. This review describes the clinical features and presumed pathogenic mechanisms of endocrine irAEs. Furthermore, it comprehensively summarizes the autoantibodies reported for each endocrine irAE and discusses their significance based on the latest findings, focusing on their utility as predictive biomarkers for irAE onset, their diagnostic value, and their potential involvement in the pathogenesis.

articles.title: Post-treatment Serum Autotaxin and Subsequent Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development During Nucleos(t)ide Analog Therapy for Chronic Hepatitis B: An Exploratory Study.
articles.abstract: Objective　The risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) persists despite nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We investigated whether post-treatment serum autotaxin (ATX), a noninvasive fibrosis-related biomarker, is associated with subsequent HCC development during NA therapy.Methods　We measured the serum ATX levels at baseline and at week 48 of NA therapy. Patients were followed for HCC development. The optimal ATX cutoff value was determined using a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and cumulative HCC incidence was evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier method.Patients　This retrospective single-center cohort study included 67 treatment-naïve patients with chronic hepatitis B who received NA therapy for at least 48 weeks.Results　The median age was 59 years, and 58.2% of the patients were men. During a median follow-up period of 6.3 years, five patients developed HCC. The serum ATX levels decreased significantly after 48 weeks of NA therapy (0.93 vs. 0.84 mg/L, P < 0.001). Patients who subsequently developed HCC had significantly higher post-treatment ATX levels than those who did not (1.32 vs. 0.84 mg/L, P = 0.010). Among the evaluated fibrosis-related biomarkers, ATX showed the highest discriminative ability for HCC development, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.90. With an ATX/upper limit of normal ratio cutoff of 0.92, patients with elevated ATX levels that showed a significantly higher cumulative incidence of HCC than those with lower levels (10-year incidence: 25.0% vs. 1.96%, log-rank P = 0.001).Conclusions　The serum ATX levels decreased after NA therapy, but remained elevated in patients who subsequently developed HCC. Validation of these preliminary findings in larger prospective cohorts is needed.

articles.title: LabRI: A data-source-agnostic, multi-method statistical consensus framework for laboratory reference interval estimation.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Reference intervals (RIs) are essential for interpreting clinical laboratory results; their verification is required under ISO 15189 standards. No single estimation method is consistently accurate across distributions, sample sizes, and contamination levels. This study introduces LabRI (Laboratory Reference Interval), a data-source-agnostic multi-method consensus framework, benchmarked against Truncated Minimum Chi-square (TMC), Truncated Maximum Likelihood (TML), refineR, and reflimR.

METHODS: LabRI is an R/Shiny application integrating modified refineR, reflimR, a nonparametric percentile procedure for low-count datasets, and Expectation-Maximization with Gaussian Mixture Modeling. Real-world data (Group 1) comprised 12 analytes with directly established RIs; simulated data (Group 2) comprised refineR testcase1, testcase2, and testcase4 across five subsample sizes each. Performance was assessed using Performance Ranking by Index of Deviation of Reference Limits (PRIDe-RL), prioritizing conformity with equivalence intervals (EIs) and incorporating proximity, tail behavior, and severity. Statistical uncertainty was assessed using ratios of model-based 90% confidence interval widths to RI widths (WCI/WRI).

RESULTS: LabRI ranked first in both groups and overall. Its pooled PRIDe-RL score was 0.925, followed by reflimR (0.793), TMC (0.792), refineR (0.737), and TML (0.646). LabRI placed 50/54 reference limits (92.6%) within their EIs, comprising 24/24 in Group 1 and 26/30 in Group 2. No LabRI deviation exceeded twice the permissible difference. Only the upper reference limit for thyroid-stimulating hormone exceeded the predefined uncertainty threshold (WCI/WRI = 0.234; target <0.20).

CONCLUSIONS: LabRI showed the closest overall agreement with the adopted comparative references across the evaluated datasets, suggesting that multi-method consensus may reduce reliance on single-estimator assumptions. Appropriate data curation and clinical plausibility review remain essential for practical application.

articles.title: Behind the Breathlessness: Defining Pulmonary Phenotypes in Post-COVID Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent respiratory symptoms after COVID-19 may conceal distinct pulmonary disorders despite normal routine lung function. We characterized clinical phenotypes and three-month physiological outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included all 122 eligible patients. Multimodal evaluation informed phenotype-directed management. Available paired measurements were compared with two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 10 parameters; a separate sensitivity analysis carried baseline values forward when follow-up was missing.

RESULTS: Alveolitis/ILD-dominant, bronchiolitis-dominant, and asthma-dominant presentations accounted for 61 (50.0%), 47 (38.5%), and 11 (9.0%) patients; 3 (2.5%) remained unclassified. Baseline routine lung function was categorized as normal in 98 (80.3%). Median paired changes were +2 percentage points for FEV₁ (adjusted p=0.0032), +1 for FVC (p=0.0036), +2 for DLCO (p=0.0032), and -7 for RV/TLC expressed as percent predicted (p=0.0432). Paired sample sizes differed by parameter. Carrying baseline forward did not alter the signed-rank p-values.

CONCLUSION: Multimodal assessment identified pulmonary phenotypes alongside modest physiological changes after treatment. These uncontrolled observations do not establish treatment efficacy or a measured quality-of-life benefit and require prospective controlled validation.

articles.title: Community pharmacy involvement in palliative care in Aotearoa New Zealand: a national survey.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The extent of community pharmacy involvement in managing individuals in their last year of life is poorly understood.

AIM: This study aims to describe palliative care-related services provided by community pharmacies and the challenges faced by community pharmacies in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ).

METHODS: A cross-sectional, online, anonymous questionnaire was developed and piloted, and an invitation was emailed to all community pharmacies in NZ between May and June 2024. Data were collected on pharmacy characteristics, palliative care services provided, interprofessional communication methods, capability to provide safe and accessible services, and the challenges of providing palliative care. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, and free-text data were inductively themed using manifest content analysis.

RESULTS: Complete responses were received from 98 of the 1053 pharmacies invited to participate (response rate 9.3%). More than 83% of respondents reported that palliative care medications were stocked in their pharmacies. Although 58.3% engaged in interprofessional communication, 21.3% of responding pharmacies lacked access to the patient clinical information required to provide palliative care. The top-ranked challenges reported by community pharmacies were funding shortages, staff availability, lack of access to patient records, unpredictable demand for palliative care medications, and lack of staff expertise in palliative care.

DISCUSSION: Community pharmacies in NZ provide a range of services for people with palliative care needs and their whānau/care supporters. However, there are service provision challenges which can negatively impact patient outcomes.

articles.title: Curcuma longa (turmeric) or its active ingredients for osteoarthritis.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Osteoarthritis is a major cause of disability worldwide. Current treatments have limited efficacy. Curcuma longa (turmeric) contains curcuminoids with anti-inflammatory properties that may modulate osteoarthritis pathophysiology. However, the clinical benefits and safety of Curcuma longa in osteoarthritis remain uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of Curcuma longa extracts or сurcuminoids for osteoarthritis.

SEARCH METHODS: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, five other databases, and two trials registers, together with reference checking, to identify the studies included in the review. The latest search date was 7 November 2025. We applied no restrictions on language, publication date, or publication status.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing Curcuma longa extracts or curcuminoids to placebo, in people with osteoarthritis in any joint. Other comparators included no treatment, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), non-NSAID analgesics, or other active comparators. We focused on oral formulations of Curcuma longa, with or without bioavailability enhancers, and excluded combination products containing other active herbal compounds.

OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes included pain, function, quality of life, participant-reported global assessment of success, adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events. The primary time point was up to three months.

RISK OF BIAS: We used Cochrane's RoB 2 tool to assess bias in the RCTs.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We used a random-effects model for meta-analysis. We assessed the trustworthiness of all trials eligible for inclusion using the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Trustworthiness Screening Tool.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included nine RCTs involving 1245 participants with knee osteoarthritis. The mean age of participants ranged from 52 years to 62 years; 67% of participants were female. All trials were short (up to 90 days) and investigated different Curcuma longa formulations. One trial evaluated a bioavailability-enhanced Curcuma longa formulation, while others did not report the use of bio-enhancers. Two trials used Curcuma longa extract with essential oils. Four trials used standardised or rhizome extracts of Curcuma longa, with curcuminoid content varying from 23% to 88%. Four trials compared Curcuma longa with placebo (379 participants), four with NSAIDs (673 participants), and one with paracetamol (193 participants). Here, we limit reporting to the primary comparison, Curcuma longa versus placebo. We judged three (75%) placebo-controlled trials to be at low risk of bias for pain, function, and quality of life outcomes. Two trials (50%) were at low risk of bias for safety outcomes.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Low-certainty evidence downgraded for indirectness and publication bias showed that, compared with placebo, Curcuma longa may result in little to no difference in pain, function, or quality of life, and may improve participant-reported global assessment of success. We are very uncertain about the effect of Curcuma longa on adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events due to very low-certainty evidence, downgraded for publication bias, imprecision, and indirectness. By three months, the mean change in pain (0 to 10 scale, 0 = no pain) was -1.57 points with placebo and 0.72 points lower (95% confidence interval (CI) 1.39 points lower to 0.06 points lower) with Curcuma longa (I² = 0%; 4 studies, 349 participants). The effect did not reach clinical significance of 1.5 points. By three months, the mean change in function (0 to 100, 0 = best function) was -5.42 points with placebo and 3.5 points lower with Curcuma longa (95% CI 7.29 points lower to 0.29 points higher; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 348 participants). By three months, the mean change in quality of life (0 to 100 scale, 100 = best quality of life) was 9.83 points with placebo and 2.19 points higher (95% CI 1.56 points lower to 5.94 points higher) with Curcuma longa (I² = 0%; 3 studies, 291 participants). By three months, 107 of 1000 participants receiving placebo reported treatment success, compared with 191 of 1000 receiving Curcuma longa (risk ratio (RR) 1.78, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.67; 2 studies, 170 participants). At the end of follow-up, 224 of 1000 participants in the placebo group reported adverse events compared with 226 of 1000 in the Curcuma longa group (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.51; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 379 participants). At the end of follow-up, 46 of 1000 participants in the placebo group withdrew due to adverse events compared with 66 of 1000 in the Curcuma longa group (RR 1.45, 95% CI 0.61 to 3.43; I² = 0%; 3 studies, 321 participants). Three trials reported no serious adverse events, while one trial reported two serious adverse events in the placebo group that were unrelated to the study.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Compared with placebo, Curcuma longa may result in little to no improvement in pain, function, or quality of life, and may improve participant-reported global assessment of success in people with knee osteoarthritis. We are very uncertain about the effect of Curcuma longa on adverse events, withdrawals due to adverse events, and serious adverse events. Future studies should last longer than three months; the maximum duration of the included studies was three months. The current evidence is limited to knee osteoarthritis, and future studies should include people with hand and hip osteoarthritis.

FUNDING: No external funding was received for this work.

REGISTRATION: Protocol (2021): 10.1002/14651858.CD014683.

articles.title: Meta-Analyses of Observational Studies: Principles, Challenges, and Recommendations.
articles.abstract: Observational studies play a crucial role in pediatric research by assessing disease burden, real-world effectiveness and safety, risk factors, and rare outcomes. They are particularly important for questions for which randomized controlled trials would be unethical, impractical, or not well aligned with the clinical question. The incorporation of observational studies into meta-analyses allows for greater synthesis of observational data; however, conducting these evidence syntheses introduces unique methodological challenges. These include increased heterogeneity, residual confounding, and a higher risk of within- and between-study biases, which can compromise the validity of pooled estimates. This article outlines key considerations for conducting meta-analyses of observational studies. Guidance is provided on protocol development, defining inclusion criteria, selecting appropriate study designs, extracting effect estimates, and managing confounding and heterogeneity. Using a published meta-analysis on the association between particulate matter exposure and childhood asthma, we illustrate practical challenges and strategies for interpretation.

articles.title: Night shift work and subclinical cardiac remodelling: a multi-omic CMR study in 42 671 individuals.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Whether frequent night-shift work is associated with a distinct subclinical cardiac phenotype and accompanying molecular alterations remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 42 671 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Night-shift frequency was classified into four categories, and 15 CMR measures were assessed using multivariable regression. Compared with day workers, frequent night-shift workers showed greater left ventricular global wall thickness [standardized β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.050-0.135; false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.001] and left ventricular mass-to-volume ratio (β = 0.072, 95% CI 0.021-0.123; FDR = 0.019), with lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular stroke volume index, and maximal right atrial volume index (all FDR < 0.05). Left ventricular global circumferential strain was less favourable (β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.040-0.144; FDR = 0.002), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain were not significantly associated. Proteomic (n = 4889) and metabolomic (n = 42 671) analyses identified exploratory inflammatory, vascular, and lipid-related correlates. Mediation analyses identified FDR-significant indirect-effect estimates involving left ventricular end-diastolic volume index for three proteins and four metabolites. Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified associations between selected molecular features and CMR traits, although directions were not uniformly concordant with the observational estimates.

CONCLUSION: Frequent night shift work was associated with greater concentric left ventricular geometry, lower cardiac chamber volumes, and less favourable circumferential strain, together with inflammatory and lipid-related molecular correlates. Prospective studies are required to determine temporal relationships and long-term clinical relevance.

articles.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine
articles.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

articles.title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and management in nursing practice.
articles.journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
articles.abstract: Asthma is one of the most common chronic respiratory conditions in the UK, affecting both children and adults. It is characterised by airway inflammation, variable symptoms, and reversible airflow limitation. This article provides a nursing-focused overview of asthma, exploring the definition, altered pathophysiology, diagnosis, and both pharmacological and non-pharmacological management. It highlights the importance of accurate assessment, early differentiation from other respiratory conditions, and the use of structured diagnostic tools within national guidance. Education, adherence support, and awareness of excessive reliever use are identified as key nursing priorities. By following national and local guidelines, promoting the use of combination and anti-inflammatory therapies, and providing holistic, person-centred education, nurses can improve symptom control, reduce preventable hospital admissions, and enhance quality of life for individuals and families living with asthma.

articles.title: Emergency department ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter insertion training with virtual reality.
articles.journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter (USG-PIVC) insertion is a challenging skill for emergency department (ED) clinicians to master. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising, cost-effective tool for procedural training. Unlike manikins or phantoms, VR enables immersive, repeatable and scalable training with real-time feedback, simulating real ED conditions to improve skill transfer and learner engagement. However, its use in USG-PIVC education within EDs has not been evaluated despite persistent training barriers to USG-PIVC insertion in this setting.

AIMS: To assess the feasibility of conducting a large-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT) that integrates a VR intervention into USG-PIVC training, addressing these challenges before evaluating effectiveness.

METHODS: A single-site feasibility RCT will be conducted in an Australian ED. Twenty ED doctors will be randomly assigned to either standard training or standard training plus VR simulation. In addition to feasibility outcomes, the study will assess clinical metrics including first-attempt success rate, number of attempts, time to insertion, vein difficulty, completion of procedural steps, immediate complications, time spent practising, and clinician confidence and satisfaction.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: Although limited by a small sample size and single-site design, the findings from this pilot trial will provide valuable insights into the feasibility of integrating VR into USG-PIVC training. These results will help inform the design and implementation of a larger-scale, multi-site trial to evaluate effectiveness and broader applicability.

articles.title: Hazardous medicines: turning consensus into safer health care.
articles.journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)

articles.title: Patient experience and engagement during acute non-invasive ventilation.
articles.journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore patients' experiences of acute non-invasive ventilation (NIV) and examine the role of patient engagement in treatment acceptance and tolerance.

METHODS: A descriptive qualitative design was employed using semistructured interviews with five patients who had recently received acute NIV. Data were analysed using content analysis to identify recurring themes within participant accounts. Interviews were conducted in 2012 and the findings are reported as an exploratory account, interpreted with reference to contemporary practice.

RESULTS: Three key themes were identified: patient engagement during NIV initiation, perceived benefits outweighing associated discomfort, and coping with the mask and ventilator interface. Most participants reported significant physical and psychological discomfort during treatment. However, four of the five participants indicated willingness to undergo NIV again if clinically required, reflecting recognition of its therapeutic benefit. Participants' perceptions of NIV and its delivery often differed from those assumed by health professionals, particularly in relation to communication and involvement in decision-making.

CONCLUSION: Within this small exploratory sample, patient engagement, clear communication and involvement in decision-making appeared central to treatment acceptance during acute NIV. Greater attention to patient-centred approaches during initiation and management of NIV may improve both patient experience and treatment tolerance in acute respiratory care.

articles.title: A Self-Management Support Intervention to Improve BP among Patients with CKD: Kidney Awareness Registry and Education Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-income patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) face a high burden of adverse health outcomes. We assessed the effectiveness of a community health worker (CHW)-led self-management support intervention to improve health among adults with CKD and hypertension who receive primary care in urban safety-net clinics.

METHODS: Randomized controlled trial [Kidney Awareness Registry and Education) in which low-income, English-, Spanish-, or Cantonese-speaking adults with CKD and systolic blood pressure (SBP) >130 mmHg recruited from two different public health care delivery systems in San Francisco, California, and Oakland, California, were randomized to participate in a 6-month self-management support intervention or usual care. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in SBP change after one year. Secondary outcomes included the between-group differences in changes of: urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR), patient-reported awareness of CKD, self-efficacy of chronic disease management, communication with providers, medication adherence, and quality of life at one year.

RESULTS: Among 238 participants with mean age of 62 years, a median (interquartile range, [IQR]) SBP of 144 (134, 159) mmHg, median (IQR) eGFR of 54.2 (42.1, 76.6) ml/min/1.73 m2 and UACR of 203 mg/g (IQR: 43, 827), of whom 34.5% had limited English proficiency and 62.0% had food insecurity, 129 were randomized to the self-management support intervention and 109 were randomized to usual care. Randomization to intervention led to a statistically larger decline in SBP compared to usual care at 12 months (difference-in-differences estimate: -10.8 mmHg; 95%CI: -16.8, -4.8). Change in UACR was not statistically different by study arm. Change in CKD awareness was higher in the intervention arm compared to usual care (ratio-in-odds ratios estimate: 2.9; 1.0-8.1), but no statistically significant differences in other behavioral outcomes were noted.

CONCLUSION: A CHW-led self-management support program improves SBP and CKD awareness among low-income patients with moderate CKD.

articles.title: miRNA Regulation of the FGF23-Klotho Pathway Mitigates Adverse Cardiac Remodeling During Nocturnal Hemodialysis.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with ESKD. Dysregulation of the fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)/Klotho axis has been implicated in uremic cardiomyopathy, however the mechanism linking dialysis intensity to the regulation of this pathway remains poorly defined.

METHODS: We analyzed serum samples from ESKD patients transitioning from conventional to nocturnal hemodialysis (NHD). Left ventricular mass (LVM) was measured by echocardiography before and after transition. Patients were stratified as LVM regressors [ ≥ 10% decrease in LVM; n = 6] or LVM progressors [ ≥ 10% increase in LVM; n = 7]. Circulating microRNAs (miRs) and serum FGF23 and alpha Klotho were quantified. Mechanistic relevance was tested in an angiotensin-II model of cardiac hypertrophy using FGF23 suppression via an antisense oligonucleotide gapmer, or antagomirs targeting miR-200c-3p.

RESULTS: Among 13 patients transitioning to NHD, LVM regressors required fewer antihypertensive medications than at baseline (P<0.001) with improved metabolic parameters (urea 12.9 vs. 16.6 mmol/L, P<0.01) and higher hemoglobin (109 vs. 95 g/L, P<0.01). We identified six differentially expressed miRs (let-7a/g/i, miR-200c, miR-1 and miR-30c) that targeted the FGF23/Klotho signaling axis. LVM regressors also demonstrated significantly lower circulating FGF23 levels than LVM progressors [60 (28, 160) vs 668 (73, 1734) pg/mL, P<0.05]. In the angiotensin-II murine model of cardiac hypertrophy, FGF23 gapmer treatment or miR-200c-3p inhibition reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and attenuated interstitial fibrosis while restoring FGF23/Klotho signaling through the suppression of extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 phosphorylation, activation of dual specificity phosphatase-1 and inducing antioxidant gene expression.

CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, these exploratory findings link dialysis intensification to miR-mediated regulation of the FGF23/Klotho axis, demonstrating that targeting this regulatory network is sufficient to suppress pathological cardiac remodeling. These data provide a mechanistic basis for the cardiovascular benefits of nocturnal hemodialysis and identify the FGF23/Klotho axis as a candidate therapeutic target warranting further validation.

articles.title: Experiences From Implementation of a Hospital Ward Sepsis Response Team at a Large Academic Medical Center.
articles.abstract: Hospital-onset sepsis is associated with high mortality and dedicated sepsis response teams can expedite identification and interventions for high-risk patients. Many such teams described in the literature are primarily active in emergency departments or intensive care units. For large academic medical centers with multiple care teams and nursing units, a sepsis response team focused on hospital ward (HW) patients may standardize care of hospitalized septic patients before they develop irreversible organ injury and require critical care stabilization. Here we present our experience establishing the Sepsis Emergency Response Team, an Advanced Practice Provider-led team designed to identify patients with early signs of sepsis on HWs across a large academic medical center.

articles.title: Characteristics of HIV-1 molecular transmission networks among older men, their spouses, and female sex workers in Southwest China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The rising incidence of HIV-1 infection in older adults is a challenge in China. We have previously reported a close transmission connection between older men and female sex workers (FSWs). This study aimed to characterize the transmission network and explore the potential transmission directions among older men, their spouses, and FSWs.

METHODS: Participants with HIV-1, including older men, their female spouses, and FSWs, were recruited from Guigang City, Guangxi, China. Sanger-derived HIV-1 pol sequences were used for transmission network construction. Conjugal pairs within the largest cluster and the associated FSWs were subjected to next-generation sequencing (NGS) to infer transmission direction via Phyloscanner.

RESULTS: A total of 726 HIV pol sequences were obtained by Sanger sequencing, including 595 older men, 88 female spouses, and 43 FSWs. Seven HIV-1 subtypes were identified, with CRF01_AE being the predominant subtype (75.8%, 550/726). Overall, 70.5% (512/726) participants were clustered in transmission networks; 63.9% (327/512) of them belonged to clusters with older men, their spouses, and FSWs. NGS and transmission inference were performed for 30 individuals, revealing 12 source-recipient pairs: three from FSWs to older men, three from older men to spouses, three from spouses to older men, and the remaining three were same-sex pairs.

CONCLUSION: This exploratory study identifies transmission networks among older men, their spouses, and FSWs, and provides preliminary evidence for putative transmission directions. We propose a study strategy combining Sanger sequencing and NGS for population-level identification of HIV-1 transmitters, which helps determine local epidemic drivers and inform targeted interventions.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of umeclidinium/vilanterol versus aclidinium monotherapy for symptomatic COPD in Colombia: a lifetime Markov model.
articles.journal: Expert review of pharmacoeconomics & outcomes research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the lifetime cost-effectiveness of once-daily umeclidinium/vilanterol (UMEC/VI) versus twice-daily aclidinium monotherapy for symptomatic chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in Colombia.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A lifetime Markov model with monthly cycles simulated moderate-to-very-severe COPD in a cohort aged 65 years, incorporating age- and severity-specific background mortality and a 12% case-fatality probability after each severe exacerbation. Comparative efficacy came from a published network meta-analysis; comparator exacerbation probabilities were derived on the rate scale. Costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) were discounted at 5% annually. Deterministic, scenario, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: UMEC/VI yielded 8.108 QALYs at US$24,956 per patient versus 6.312 QALYs and US$29,994 for aclidinium (incremental 1.796 QALYs; US$5,038 saved), making UMEC/VI dominant (net monetary benefit US$14,341). UMEC/VI was dominant in 94.7% and cost-effective in 98.6% of probabilistic simulations. Without its exacerbation benefit, UMEC/VI was not cost-effective (net monetary benefit -US$859).

CONCLUSIONS: UMEC/VI is a high-value COPD maintenance therapy in Colombia, driven by exacerbation reduction rather than drug pricing and conditional on persistence of its clinical benefit.

articles.title: Genetics of hypertension.
articles.journal: Current opinion in nephrology and hypertension
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Hypertension genetics is transitioning from discovery into clinical applications: there are numerous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of blood pressure (BP) and more recently resistant hypertension, polygenic risk scores are available, and there is regulatory approval of a novel class of antihypertensive treatment. This review highlights recent discoveries and clinical implications.

RECENT FINDINGS: A GWAS of greater than 1 million individuals identified 2103 independent BP signals, explaining more than 60% of common-variant heritability; many candidate genes are expressed in kidney tubular epithelia and adrenal zona glomerulosa. A GWAS (>23 000 cases) of resistant hypertension identified 24 loci with candidate genes mapping to the aldosterone-potassium axis, providing genetics support for selective aldosterone synthase inhibitors and overlap with BP loci. Clinical trials using aldosterone synthase inhibitors, and angiotensinogen-silencing RNA therapies are in Phase 2-3 trials; aprocitentan received regulatory approval for resistant hypertension in 2024.

SUMMARY: The genetic architecture of hypertension spans Mendelian disease genes to thousands of common variants, with kidney tubular biology and the aldosterone axis as central biological themes. Multigene panels, primary aldosteronism screening, and mineralocorticoid axis evaluation before accepting apparent resistance are ready for clinical implementation. Polygenic risk scores show promise for trial enrichment and pharmacogenomic stratification, but are not yet ready for individual clinical decisions.

articles.title: Consensus-based recommendations on cilostazol and standardized Ginkgo biloba combination therapy for secondary stroke prevention and post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) management.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI), particularly in patients with cerebral small vessel disease (SVD), remains an important challenge. This Korean NeuroEndovascular Society (KoNES) expert consensus evaluates the rationale for combining cilostazol with standardized Ginkgo biloba extract to address vascular and cognitive aspects of post-stroke care.

METHODS: An expert panel formulated clinical questions and reviewed randomized trials, meta-analyses, and translational evidence. Recommendations were refined through iterative discussion and review, considering clinical applicability in South Korea.

RESULTS: Cilostazol reduces recurrent ischemic stroke risk with a relatively low risk of hemorrhagic complications and may slow white matter lesion progression. Standardized Ginkgo biloba extract, particularly EGb 761, has shown cognitive and functional benefits in selected populations. A standardized extract used in Korea has a broadly similar phytochemical composition, but direct comparative bioequivalence data are lacking. Available pharmacological and clinical evidence suggests complementary mechanisms for the combination, without a clear bleeding signal under studied conditions. Nevertheless, direct evidence of efficacy and safety for combined treatment in stroke populations is limited. Fixed-dose combinations may reduce pill burden when both treatments are indicated.

CONCLUSIONS: Combining cilostazol with standardized Ginkgo biloba extract may offer a multi-target approach for stroke survivors with SVD or PSCI. Its clinical use should acknowledge the limitations of indirect evidence; prospective randomized trials are needed to establish long-term efficacy and safety.

articles.title: Gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles in ischemic stroke: mechanisms of neurovascular injury and repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine how gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles (GMEVs) may link post-stroke intestinal dysbiosis and barrier dysfunction with secondary brain injury and recovery after ischemic stroke (IS).

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on GMEV biogenesis, cargo, transport, and signaling across the gut-brain axis, with emphasis on peripheral immune activation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) injury, glial responses, neurovascular dysfunction, and repair. Evidence from endogenous and engineered bacterial vesicle studies was considered separately.

RESULTS: IS disrupts intestinal homeostasis through autonomic, endocrine, hemodynamic, and immune pathways, potentially altering GMEV release, composition, and translocation. Vesicles from pathobionts may promote endothelial activation, complement and inflammasome signaling, oxidative stress, leukocyte recruitment, regulated cell death, BBB disruption, and maladaptive glial responses. In contrast, vesicles from selected commensal or probiotic bacteria may support epithelial integrity, immune resolution, and restorative neurovascular signaling. Engineered bacterial vesicles have shown promise as targeted therapeutic carriers in preclinical IS models; however, these findings do not establish equivalent effects for endogenous gut-derived vesicles. GMEV actions are likely dependent on microbial source, molecular cargo, route of exposure, dose, host state, and timing, and may be harmful or beneficial rather than intrinsically producing both effects.

CONCLUSIONS: GMEVs are plausible mediators of gut-brain communication after IS and may represent both therapeutic targets and delivery platforms. Translation will require source-resolved tracing, rigorous vesicle characterization, physiologic dosing, clinically relevant models, and longitudinal human studies to define their causal and therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Nutritional and metabolic profile of children with type 1 and 2 spinal muscular atrophy managed at a referral center.
articles.abstract: Introduction. Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a degenerative genetic disorder that primarily affects motor neurons. Disease-modifying therapies have altered the disease's natural course and led to new clinical phenotypes. Recent evidence suggests a systemic impact, including metabolic abnormalities. Objective. To describe the anthropometric, nutritional, and metabolic profiles of children with SMA types 1 and 2 treated at a referral center. Population and methods. We conducted a descriptive cross-sectional study at a tertiary care hospital between 2020 and 2023. We analyzed anthropometric measurements, lipid profile, glucose profile, and nutritional status in 17 children under 12 years of age with type 1 and 2 SMA during their first visit. Results. A high prevalence of overweight, as well as abnormalities in lipid and glucose metabolism-including insulin resistance-was observed in a significant proportion of patients. An exploratory comparison between type 1 and type 2 SMA revealed a heterogeneous profile: some parameters, such as low HDL and high BMI, were more common in type 1 SMA, while elevated insulin levels were more common in type 2 SMA. These findings do not allow for definitive conclusions regarding differences between subtypes. The only patient treated during the presymptomatic stage had a nutritional and metabolic profile within expected parameters. Conclusion. This study highlights the need for a multidisciplinary approach that includes nutritional and metabolic assessment in the follow-up of patients with SMA, tailored to their new phenotypes and increased life expectancy.

articles.title: Septo-optic dysplasia and congenital panhypopituitarism associated with complicated gastroschisis.
articles.abstract: Gastroschisis is a rare defect of the abdominal wall, rarely associated with other malformations. Septo-optic dysplasia (SOD) is a midline abnormality characterized by hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction and cerebral parenchymal abnormalities, both of unknown causes. I present the case of a preterm newborn with a weight appropriate for her gestational age and a prenatal diagnosis of gastroschisis. Surgical repair was performed 8 hours after birth. Subsequently, she developed fluid and electrolyte imbalances and polyuria; central diabetes insipidus was diagnosed based on a positive desmopressin test. A brain MRI was performed, showing findings consistent with SOD, and hormonal studies confirmed congenital panhypopituitarism. Hormone replacement therapy was initiated, and the patient's clinical course has been favorable. SOD and congenital panhypopituitarism are difficult to diagnose due to their variable and nonspecific presentation. Hypoglycemia is the predominant finding in newborns. Early detection allows for treatment and prevents irreversible complications.

articles.title: Development and validation of an intra-procedural predictive model for radial artery spasm in patients undergoing transradial percutaneous coronary intervention-chronic total occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To develop and internally validate a robust predictive model for radial artery spasm (RAS) to facilitate real-time intra-procedural risk stratification and intraoperative strategy optimization during chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 1,327 patients undergoing CTO-PCI between January 2020 and November 2025. The dataset was divided into a derivation cohort (n = 929) and an internal validation cohort (n = 398) using a 7:3 ratio. Independent risk factors for RAS were identified through multivariate analysis to construct a logistic regression model. Model performance was rigorously assessed via AUC, calibration plots, bootstrap validation with optimism correction, Brier score, calibration slope, and decision curve analysis.
