articles.title: Managing acute bromazolam intoxication in a custodial setting: a prison health case study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Synthetic benzodiazepines pose significant health risks, especially within prison settings where substance use, multi-morbidity and constrained healthcare environments intersect. As the illicit drug market continues to evolve, prisons face increasing challenges in responding to changing patterns of use. This paper aims to present a case study of a bromazolam-related drug incident in a Scottish prison to identify operational learnings that can support future approaches to meeting the health needs of those within prison settings.

DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: The authors conducted a descriptive observational case study as part of a public health response and wider service evaluation to a drug-related outbreak. Approval for the analysis and inclusion of routinely collected clinical and incident data was granted by the Caldicott Guardian. Information was extracted using a standardised data collection template. The authors incorporated qualitative insights from stakeholder reflections to understand operational challenges and perceived drivers of the outbreak.

FINDINGS: Thirty prison residents were affected, four requiring hospitalisation and three of these requiring intensive care admission. While the clinical response was timely and prevented any fatalities, the incident exposed vulnerabilities in operational preparedness, communication pathways and incident coordination.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: This case highlights the need for strengthened preparedness for illicit substance outbreaks, particularly benzodiazepines, in prisons. This includes development and awareness of clear major incident protocols, workforce resilience planning and integrated harm-reduction approaches.

ORIGINALITY/VALUE: This paper provides practice-based insight into the management of an emerging synthetic benzodiazepine incident within a prison setting, offering practice-based learning that may support preparedness and multi-agency responses to similar incidents in prison settings.

articles.title: Impact of HIV-1 RNA Assay Selection on Low-Level Viremia and Clinical Trial Endpoint Interpretations.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate plasma HIV-1 viral load quantification is essential for monitoring responses to antiretroviral therapy (ART) and defining efficacy in clinical trials. Differences in assay performance characteristics may result in discordant results and affect clinical interpretation. We evaluated concordance between the Roche cobas 6800 and Abbott RealTime HIV-1 RNA assays in 2 ongoing, multicenter, phase 3b trials.

METHODS: Stored paired plasma aliquots from adults with HIV-1 who were virologically suppressed or initiating ART (271 and 348 paired samples, respectively) were batch re-tested using the RealTime assay; sample selection included all specimens from pre-specified key study visits and was enriched for selected centrally reported cobas 6800 results ≥50 copies/mL. Concordance was evaluated at clinically relevant categorical thresholds (50 and 200 copies/mL).

RESULTS: Overall, among samples with cobas 6800 HIV-1 RNA results ≥50 copies/mL, 92% (91/99) of samples from participants who were virologically suppressed and 68% (159/233) from participants initiating ART were <50 copies/mL by RealTime. Among samples with cobas 6800 HIV-1 RNA results ≥200 copies/mL, 78% (14/18) and 83% (44/53), respectively, were <200 copies/mL by RealTime. Most samples classified as <50 copies/mL by cobas 6800 were <50 copies/mL by RealTime. All samples classified as <200 copies/mL by cobas 6800 were <200 copies/mL by RealTime. In both studies, per-protocol case review identified no clinical contributors in most cases of viremia.

CONCLUSIONS: Marked discordance between assays was observed near clinically relevant low HIV-1 RNA thresholds. These findings highlight the importance of assay-specific interpretation of low-level viremia in trials and routine care, particularly near decision-making thresholds.

articles.title: Birth in the Neonatal Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) Vaccination Era and Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Seroclearance in People With HIV-1 and HBV Coinfection on Tenofovir-containing Antiretroviral Therapy.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The impact of long-term tenofovir-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART) on hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance in people with HIV-1 (PWH) and HBV coinfection remains under-defined, particularly in HBV-hyperendemic regions with universal neonatal vaccination programs.

METHODS: HBsAg-positive PWH receiving tenofovir-containing ART between 2011 and 2023 were followed until December 2025. Demographics, HBV serologic markers, plasma HBV DNA, and liver fibrosis stage were collected. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with HBsAg seroclearance. Clinical and hepatic outcomes were compared with seroclearance status.

RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 9.4 years, 35 (8.4%) of 415 PWH achieved HBsAg seroclearance during a total of 3600 person-years of tenofovir-containing ART, corresponding to an incidence rate of 0.97 per 100 person-years. Among them, 37.1% (13/35) tested positive for anti-HBs at the time of seroclearance. In multivariable analysis, birth in universal neonatal HBV vaccination era (after July 1986) (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 13.56, 95% confidence interval [CI] 6.08-30.28, P < .001), baseline HBsAg ≤250 IU/mL (aHR 7.36, 95% CI 3.29-16.50, P < .001), and higher baseline ALT level (aHR 1.00 per 1-U/L increase, 95% CI 1.00-1.01, P < .001) were independently associated with HBsAg seroclearance. None of PWH who achieved HBsAg seroclearance developed seroreversion, cirrhosis, or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), whereas 6.6% and 2.1% of PWH without seroclearance developed cirrhosis and HCC, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite long-term tenofovir-containing ART, HBsAg seroclearance was uncommon (0.97% annually) among PWH with HBV coinfection. Birth in the neonatal HBV vaccination era and lower baseline HBsAg level were 2 independent predictors of HBsAg seroclearance.

articles.title: Impact of primary care physician continuity on survival in patients with atrial fibrillation: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIM: To assess the impact of continuity of care (COC)-care provided by the same primary care physician (PCP)-on outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).

METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including all patients with AF referred by PCPs (n = 17 889) between January 2010 and December 2023 in the Santiago de Compostela healthcare area (Spain). COC was categorized as 'PCP stability' (care by the assigned PCP) or 'interrupted COC' (care by multiple rotating PCPs). The association between COC and outcomes (hospitalization, mortality, stroke, and haemorrhage) was estimated using Cox regression and Fine-Gray competing risk models, adjusted for potential confounders. Patients with PCP stability had a significantly lower annual referral rate (1.5 vs. 1.8, P < 0.001) and a higher rate of adequate oral anticoagulation (OAC) indication according to the CHA2DS2-VASc score (79.5% vs. 69.1%, P < 0.001). COC was independently associated with reduced all-cause mortality (hazard ratio; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79; 0.69-0.91), a benefit that remained robust after sensitivity analyses. No significant differences were observed in stroke or haemorrhagic complications; however, competing risk analysis suggests that the higher mortality rate in the interrupted COC group likely precluded the observation of non-fatal events in this high-risk subset.

CONCLUSION: Longitudinal COC in primary care is associated with improved clinical management, including better OAC indication, and a significant reduction in all-cause mortality among patients with AF. The survival benefit of seeing the same physician appears to extend beyond anticoagulation optimization, highlighting the pleiotropic value of the patient-physician relationship.

articles.title: One echocardiographic or hemodynamic parameter improves mortality prediction by the ESC/ERS four-strata model: a flexible approach to follow-up risk stratification in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The European Society of Cardiology (ESC)/European Respiratory Society (ERS)-recommended four-strata mortality risk stratification of prevalent patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) does not incorporate echocardiographic or right heart catheterization (RHC) measures.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Within the multicentre, observational study FOCUS-PAH, we selected those patients who underwent both echocardiography and RHC (primary analysis) or at least one of these exams (secondary analysis) in the first 12 months after PAH diagnosis and with known vital status over the following 6 years. The association of echocardiographic and RHC variables with all-cause mortality was evaluated by Cox regression. Risk prediction model performance was assessed using ROC curves and net reclassification improvement. The primary analysis included 197 patients (58% female; median age 55 years). In multivariable analyses, right atrial area (RAA, HR 1.09 per 1-cm2 increase) and the percentage change in pulmonary vascular resistance (ΔPVR, HR 1.01 per 1% change) at follow-up were independent predictors of all-cause mortality when added to ESC/ERS categories. The four-strata model AUC was 0.66 and improved to 0.73 (P = 0.02), 0.74 (P = 0.002), and 0.77 (P = 0.0005), respectively, with RAA, ΔPVR, or both. Including RAA and ΔPVR reclassified 25% of patients into more appropriate risk groups. RA pressure, instead of RAA, also predicted mortality (HR 1.08 per 1-mmHg increase) and similarly enhanced ESC/ERS four-strata discrimination (AUC 0.73 vs. 0.66, P = 0.009). Moreover, RAA (AUC 0.73, P = 0.007) and/or ΔPVR (AUC 0.68, P = 0.004) improved ESC/ERS risk prediction in the secondary analysis including 394 patients.

CONCLUSION: Adding one echocardiographic or RHC parameter interchangeably improves mortality risk prediction by the ESC/ERS four-strata model in PAH.

articles.title: Protection Against Recurrent Typhoid Fever Conferred by a Prior Episode: Evidence From a Large Cohort Study in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Understanding the extent of protection against typhoid fever conferred by naturally occurring typhoid is essential for transmission modeling and vaccine policy development. However, data on the level of protection from natural typhoid against recurrent typhoid episodes are sparse.

METHODS: We analyzed data from a cluster-randomized trial of a typhoid conjugate vaccine conducted in Dhaka, Bangladesh. A cohort of blood-culture confirmed typhoid patients (index cases) and matched controls (1:4 ratio) from the community who had not received the typhoid vaccine were followed for up to 6 years to identify recurrent typhoid episodes. A recurrent typhoid episode was defined as one occurring more than 30 days after the onset of the initial episode and/or involving a strain with a different antimicrobial resistance profile. Febrile patients who tested negative for Salmonella Typhi through passive surveillance were also evaluated as facility-based controls. Stratified Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for recurrent typhoid episodes.

RESULTS: We identified 13 recurrent episodes among 940 index cases and 12 episodes among 3760 community-based controls, yielding incidence rates of 741 and 158 per 100 000 person-years, respectively, with an adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) of 3.7; 95% CI: 1.8, 7.9; P < .001. However, when using facility-based controls to prevent healthcare utilization bias, there was no statistically significant difference between groups (aHR: 1.5, 95% CI: 0.8, 2.8; P = .160).

CONCLUSIONS: In this typhoid-endemic population comprising both children and adults, we found no evidence that natural typhoid fever confers protection against recurrent typhoid episodes.

articles.title: Andes Virus Exposure and Nosocomial Transmission Events to Healthcare Personnel: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Andes virus (ANDV) is a high-consequence infectious disease with substantial mortality. On 2 May 2026, the World Health Organization reported a multinational ANDV outbreak, raising questions regarding the risk of transmission to healthcare personnel (HCP).

METHODS: We performed a systematic review per PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO:CRD420261283806) for studies describing healthcare-associated ANDV exposure or transmission events to HCP.

RESULTS: Eight studies reporting on 7 events were included, describing a total of 17 healthcare-associated cases. Overall, 207 individuals were exposed, including 118 HCP, resulting in 8 infections and 4 deaths among HCP. Studies describing HCP infections reported none or inadequate personal protective equipment (PPE) use.

CONCLUSIONS: Transmission of ANDV to HCP has been reported in the setting of delayed implementation of transmission-based precautions or breaches in infection control practice. Limitations in published exposure events highlight the need for standardized reporting of exposure events and outcomes as well as infection prevention measures implemented.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Prognostic Relevance of Valve Strands in Patients With Suspected Infective Endocarditis.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical significance and impact of valve strands, also known as Lambl's excrescences, on management in patients with suspected infective endocarditis (IE) remain unclear. The study aimed to assess the impact of the diagnosis of valve strands on the outcomes of patients investigated for suspected IE.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study at Lausanne University Hospital (2014-2024) including adult patients with a valve strand identified on cardiac imaging. Episodes were classified as IE or non-IE by a multidisciplinary Endocarditis Team (2018-2024) or by expert clinicians (2014-2017). One-year outcomes included recurrence of bacteremia/candidemia or IE by the same microorganism.

RESULTS: Among 305 episodes with valve strands, 101 (33%) were diagnosed as IE by the Endocarditis Team or expert clinicians. Among the 204 episodes without IE, 165 (81%) had bacteremia/candidemia. Valve strands were identified by transthoracic echocardiography in 141 (50%) out of 282 episodes and by transesophageal echocardiography in 191 (79%) out of 244 episodes. Among the 257 episodes with bacteremia/candidemia, recurrence of bacteremia/candidemia caused by the same microorganism within 1 year occurred in 7/92 (8%) among those with IE and 11/165 (7%) among those without (P = .971). Recurrence of IE due to the same microorganism within 1 year was significantly more frequent among episodes with IE compared to those without (6/92; 7% vs 2/165; 1%; P = .029).

CONCLUSIONS: Most valve strands detected in patients with suspected IE do not represent infectious lesions. Careful evaluation by expert cardiologists and multidisciplinary discussion can safely differentiate valve strands from vegetations, reducing unnecessary treatment.

articles.title: Long-Term Vascular Remodeling after Headache-Onset Intracranial Vertebral Artery Dissection.
articles.abstract: Vertebral artery dissection (VAD) presenting with isolated headache is a specific clinical presentation characterized by dynamic, yet poorly understood, long-term vascular remodeling. We aimed to characterize the spectrum of chronic morphologic outcomes in headache-onset VAD and identify clinical and imaging factors associated with incomplete healing and delayed morphologic progression. We retrospectively investigated 179 consecutive patients diagnosed with isolated headache-onset intracranial VAD without acute ischemic or hemorrhagic complications. Patients underwent standardized longitudinal MRI follow-up. Based on long-term imaging, morphologic remodeling was categorized into complete healing, quiescent residual abnormality, and morphologic progression (delayed enlargement of >1 mm). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of incomplete healing and progression, including the evaluation of intramural signal on DWI. Over a median follow-up of 67 months, complete healing was observed in 135 patients (75.4%), whereas 44 (24.6%) exhibited incomplete healing. Within the incomplete healing group, 28 (15.6%) remained morphologically quiescent, and 16 (8.9%) demonstrated delayed morphologic progression. Progression occurred sporadically over extended follow-up. Multivariable analysis revealed that hypertension (adjusted OR, 3.98; P = .009) and habitual alcohol consumption (adjusted OR, 4.51; P = .04) were independently associated with morphologic progression. Conversely, incomplete healing was independently associated with male sex (adjusted OR, 2.60; P = .04), nondominant vertebral artery involvement (adjusted OR, 2.68; P = .02), and the presence of intramural signal on DWI at the 2-week subacute phase (adjusted OR, 2.63; P = .03). Headache-onset intracranial VAD is a dynamic disease process. Delayed morphologic progression is associated with modifiable systemic stressors, whereas incomplete healing is associated with local structural vulnerabilities, for which the subacute manifestation of intramural signal on DWI serves as a practical imaging surrogate. These findings emphasize the potential value of risk-stratified imaging surveillance and targeted hemodynamic management.

articles.title: Comparison of different long-term cardiovascular disease risk prediction horizons to guide preventive drug treatment in apparently healthy individuals.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Guideline-recommended long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction models use varying time horizons. This study compared which risk horizon (risk until ages 80 or 95 years, or 30-year risk) most effectively guides preventive treatment in apparently healthy individuals.

METHODS AND RESULTS: CVD risks for all horizon were estimated using the LIFE-CVD2 model in individuals aged 35-69 years without CVD or diabetes from the Dutch ELAN registry (2007-2024; n = 364 003) and the EPIC-InterAct subcohort (1992-1998; n = 8813). Individuals in the top risk decile were compared across time horizons. Simulating blood pressure- and lipid-lowering therapy, the impact of using either time horizon was assessed by the expected gain in CVD-free life years and lifetime CVD events prevented. Individuals identified by 30-year risk were predominantly older and largely overlapped with 10-year risk (46%). In contrast, risk until ages 80 and 95 years showed less overlap with 10-year risk (18% and 20%, respectively) and identified more young men in the highest risk decile. Treatment guided by risk until ages 80 and 95 years yielded a median gain of 2.6 [IQR 2.2-2.9] CVD-free life years per person treated, with prevention of 4434 and 4658 CVD events, respectively, compared with 1.8 [IQR 1.4-1.9] years and 4215 events for 30-year risk. A hybrid strategy combining 10-year risk with risk until age 80 years yielded a median gain of 2.5 [IQR 2.1-3.0] CVD-free life years.

CONCLUSION: Long-term CVD risk estimation until age 80 years offers a pragmatic approach to identify younger high-risk individuals not captured by 10-year risk who may benefit from preventive treatment.

articles.title: Efficacy and Acceptability of Liraglutide for Obesity in People With HIV: Results of an Open-Label Clinical Trial in South Africa.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the Liraglutide for Obesity in HIV (LIROH) trial, we evaluated the efficacy and acceptability of liraglutide plus lifestyle counseling on weight and cardiometabolic health markers, along with the effect of discontinuation of therapy, among people with HIV (PWH) and a body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 in rural South Africa.

METHODS: From May-September 2024, we enrolled 40 PWH in KwaZulu-Natal in a Phase IV, open-label clinical trial of liraglutide 3.0 mg daily for 12 weeks. Key cardiometabolic health outcomes included changes in weight, waist circumference, and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). We also assessed depression, quality of life (QoL), and sleep quality. Finally, we assessed acceptability of the intervention based on enrollment fraction and retention at 12 weeks and 24 weeks.

RESULTS: We screened 52 participants, of whom 44 (85%) were eligible and 40 (91%) consented to enroll. Thirty-eight (95%) completed the study, with 2 (5%) discontinuing treatment due to relocation. Participants experienced substantial reductions in weight and waist circumference, and mean HbA1c (weight: -2.9% [-1.0%-4.5%]; waist: -5.6 cm [-8.2 to -2.9]; HbA1c: -0.3% [-0.4 to -0.2]). Moreover, depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and psychological QoL all improved significantly with treatment. Weight and waist circumference rebounded significantly off treatment. The changes in depression, sleep quality, and QoL were negligible post-treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial is among the first studies of GLP-1 RAs in Southern Africa and demonstrates that this class for obesity treatment among PWH in this region has efficacy to improve metabolic health and that the study intervention was acceptable in this population.

articles.title: Air travel in patients with acute coronary syndromes or heart failure: current evidence, guidance and gaps.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: As more people live with cardiovascular disease, commercial flights increasingly include patients recovering from acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or living with heart failure (HF), who face unique physiological and logistical challenges due to hypobaric hypoxia, reduced pressure, prolonged immobility, and limited onboard medical resources.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We reviewed current guidelines, observational studies, and registry data to synthesize evidence and define major gaps regarding air travel in patients with ACS or HF. Available data although derived from small, heterogeneous cohorts and different therapeutic eras, suggest that many clinically stable patients after ACS and those with compensated HF (New York Heart Association classes I-III) can generally fly with low short-term event rates when appropriately assessed. The risk may be higher in the very early post-discharge period, with the magnitude of this excess risk remaining poorly defined. No universally accepted waiting period after ACS or HF decompensation is recommended by guidelines although they broadly concordant in emphasizing clinical stability, euvolemia, and absence of ongoing ischemia prerequisites for travel; yet, these recommendations have not been validated against in-flight outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Commercial air travel is likely safe for patients with ACS or HF who are clinically stable, but decisions should be individualized and incorporate both patient- and flight-specific factors. Substantial evidence gaps persist, particularly regarding optimal timing after ACS or HF decompensation and the development of aviation-specific risk models. Prospective cohorts and international registries integrating contemporary clinical, airline, and in-flight medical event data are needed to refine guidance and support patient mobility without compromising safety.

articles.title: Adult congenital cardiac interventional training, competencies, and organization. A Statement of the ESC ACHD Working Group, the EAPCI, the AEPC, and the PICS-Society.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The growing population of adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) has prompted global initiatives to define standards of care, training pathways, and institutional requirements for catheter-based interventions. High-quality care and effective training rely on specialized, multidisciplinary centres integrating paediatric and adult cardiologists, surgeons, and anaesthesiologists with congenital expertise, supported by advanced catheter labs and hybrid theatres. This work outlines essential elements for optimal ACHD catheterization training, emphasizing a structured, competency-based curriculum covering theory, procedural skills, and post-procedural care.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Collaboration between paediatric and adult cardiologists is highlighted as vital for comprehensive care. To meet national and regional needs, a two-tier model of 'level 1' and 'level 2' centres-each with specific capacities-is proposed. Scientific societies play a key role in establishing guidelines, certifications, and facilitating trainee mobility and international collaboration. Emerging tools such as augmented reality and virtual case libraries can improve accessibility and quality of training. The framework also addresses global equity, considering regional and socio-economic differences. Proctorships and partnerships with industry are integral for introducing innovations and maintaining skills in evolving techniques.

CONCLUSION: By fostering collaboration, harmonized standards, and multidisciplinary expertise, this model aims to improve ACHD training and meet growing patient needs.

articles.title: Evolving epidemiology of cardiomyopathies at a national referral centre: a 30-year longitudinal study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes

articles.title: Septic Arthritis of the Left Ankle Caused by Brucella suis Biovar 5: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a rare case of human brucellosis caused by Brucella suis biovar 5 in a 75-year-old man from Nagano Prefecture, Japan. He had no history of immune disorders and presented with fatigue, left ankle pain, and swelling. Initial antimicrobial therapy for suspected cellulitis and tenosynovitis failed, leading to admission to our hospital. Imaging and synovial fluid analysis suggested septic arthritis with a periarticular abscess. Gram-negative rods were recovered from synovial fluid obtained via arthrocentesis of the left ankle joint. Although the isolate could not be identified using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry using a MALDI Biotyper system, it was successfully identified as B. suis biovar 5 using species-specific PCR and nine-locus multilocus sequence typing (MLST). The patient was successfully treated with surgical debridement and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. This is the third documented human case of B. suis biovar 5 infection in Japan, all originating from Nagano Prefecture, suggesting a localized cluster. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of brucellosis, the limitations of routine identification methods, and the biosafety concerns for clinical laboratories. Enhanced awareness and surveillance are warranted in regions with emerging cases.

articles.title: Clinical and economic outcomes following first-time myocardial infarction: a nationwide cohort study from the SWEDEHEART registry.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: This study aimed to estimate consequences of myocardial infarction (MI) on long-term outcomes and resource needs by comparing outcomes, healthcare resource use, and associated costs between first-time MI patients and matched controls.

METHODS AND RESULTS: First-time MI patients from the nationwide SWEDEHEART registry, along with matched controls without prior MI (matched by sex, age, and region) 2012-2022, were included. Follow-up continued through November 2024 and assessed major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as cardiovascular death, MI, ischaemic stroke, acute limb ischaemia, or urgent arterial revascularization, as well as, healthcare resource use and associated costs. Among 118 810 first-time MI patients and 588 687 matched controls, followed for a median (IQR) of 6.6 (4.2-9.4) years, the 10-year MACE probability was 48.5% vs. 21.1% (HR [95% CI] 3.65 [3.61-3.69]), mainly due to higher rate of cardiovascular death (21.7% vs. 11.1%), MI (18.4% vs. 5.9%), and arterial revascularization (22.9% vs. 4.2%). Associations attenuated after adjustment for baseline characteristics but remained significant (MACE: adjHR[95%CI]: 3.18[3.15-3.22]). Cases had twice as many inpatient visits (0.65 vs. 0.32/patient year) and inpatient days (3.05 vs. 1.67/patient year), with nearly double the mean annual total costs (€7266 vs. €3934) when outpatient visits and medication also were included. Differences were greatest in the first year but persisted, especially among females and those with risk factors such as hypertension or diabetes.

CONCLUSION: First-time MI patients have persistently higher risks of cardiovascular death, MI, and ischaemic stroke, along with greater healthcare use and costs, underscoring the need for effective prevention.

articles.title: Advanced maternal age at first delivery as a risk factor for long-term cardiovascular disease.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: An increased number of women initiate motherhood at an advanced age. Advanced maternal age (AMA) at first delivery poses unique clinical challenges; however, limited literature exists regarding potential long-term implications. We investigated the association between AMA at first delivery and maternal long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD).

METHODS AND RESULTS: A population-based retrospective cohort study included all primiparous women at a tertiary medical centre (1991-2021). Participants were stratified by age (<30, 30-34, 35-40, and > 40 years). Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated cumulative incidence rates of morbidity, and a Cox regression model investigated the association between AMA and long-term maternal CVD while adjusting for confounding variables. The study included 47 046 primiparous women; 43 426 (92.3%) were <30 years, 2807 (6.0%) were aged 30-34 years, 658 (1.4%) were aged 35-40 years, and 155 (0.3%) were >40 years. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed a significant increase in the cumulative incidence of CVD associated with AMA, particularly among aged >40 years (Log Rank: P < 0.001). Specifically, hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, central vascular events, and peripheral vascular disease were significantly more frequent in older age groups. Cox regression analysis indicated that AMA was independently associated with an increased risk of long-term CVD after adjusting for confounders [aHR = 1.81 (95% CI, 1.41-2.68); P < 0.001].

CONCLUSION: AMA at first delivery is associated with increased long-term risk of cardiovascular morbidity. These results suggest the importance of tailored monitoring and preventive strategies for women of AMA at first delivery to potentially mitigate future cardiovascular risks.

articles.title: Regional and socioeconomic disparities in the diagnosis of primary electrical diseases in a universal healthcare system: a nationwide Danish study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Quality of care & clinical outcomes
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Primary electrical diseases (PED) carry a significant risk of sudden cardiac death (SCD). Diagnosis, management, and access to care vary across regions even within universal healthcare systems. We examined nationwide geographic, socioeconomic, and treatment disparities in Denmark.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a nationwide registry-based study of individuals diagnosed with PED (long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia) between 2007 and 2024 in Denmark. Cases were compared with sex- and age-matched individuals in the background population. Outcomes included disease prevalence, proximity to specialized clinics, treatment patterns, comorbidities, and socioeconomic status. We identified 1132 individuals with PED. Overall prevalence was 19.0 per 100,000, with regional variation highest in North Denmark (26.8) and lowest in Central Denmark (12.9). Prevalence was higher in capital municipalities than in other municipality types. Cases lived closer to specialized inherited cardiac clinics than matched controls (50% shorter distance in the Capital Region; 18.9% shorter in Southern Denmark). Psychiatric comorbidities, notably anxiety and affective disorders, were more frequent in cases than controls (15% vs. 11%). Beta-blocker use and ICD implantation were markedly higher in cases with regional variation. Socioeconomic differences were modest, with immigrants underrepresented among diagnosed cases.

CONCLUSION: Even within a universal healthcare system, geographic and systemic factors contribute to disparities in the diagnosis and management of PED. Differences in proximity to specialized clinics, regional referral practices, and treatment patterns may influence detection and care. Targeted strategies to improve awareness, referral pathways, and equitable access are needed to optimize diagnosis, management, and SCD prevention.

articles.title: Association of Trust in COVID-19 Information Providers and Media with 3Cs Avoidance and Infection Anxiety among Residents in Tokyo and Osaka.
articles.abstract: We investigated the association between frequenting 3Cs (closed spaces, crowded places, and close-contact settings) and trust in information on COVID-19, to elucidate information sources affecting public preventive measures. Nonprobability quota sampling was used to recruit 2,000 residents of Tokyo and 2,000 of Osaka. The retrospective survey was conducted in April 2024. These participants responded to an online survey about two periods: one with an emergency declaration and one without. Multiple regression analyses were performed and standardized partial regression coefficients for the independent variables calculated. Without an emergency declaration, a negative association between frequenting 3Cs and trust in family/relatives and a positive association with daily conversation were observed. 3Cs anxiety was positively associated with trust in three sources: medical professionals, family/relatives, and television (TV). During the emergency declaration period, a negative association between frequenting 3Cs and trust and a positive association between 3Cs anxiety and trust in the three sources above were observed, while there was a positive association between frequenting 3Cs and trust in celebrities, weekly magazines, or social networking services. A mediation analysis showed that trust in medical professionals, family/relatives, or TV increased 3Cs anxiety, and frequenting 3Cs decreased in state of emergency situations.

articles.title: Fecal Carriage of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae among Hospital Food Handlers: Implications for Institutional Food Safety Management and Infection Control.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the prevalence and persistence of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-E) carriage among hospital food handlers. A prospective, single-center study was conducted in Sagamihara, Japan, from July to December 2021. Residual fecal specimens from routine examinations of 119 hospital food handlers were analyzed for ESBL-E and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE). ESBL-E were detected in 32 isolates from 11 participants (9.2%), with Escherichia coli as the predominant species and a mean monthly positivity rate of 4.48%. The frequency of ESBL-E carriage was higher in individuals younger than 40 years of age (17.5%) than in those aged 40 years or above (5.1%). Highly homologous strains were detected within and between participants; the most common resistance genes were blaCTX-M-1 group and blaCTX-M-9 group. Six participants showed persistent ESBL-E carriage but CRE was not detected. These findings suggest that ESBL-E carriage is common among hospital food handlers, particularly among younger individuals, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance and targeted hygiene interventions to limit ESBL-E transmission in healthcare food services.

articles.title: Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction After Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement: Prevalence, Prognosis and Predictors.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Symptoms of heart failure (HF) often persist even after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). However, the prevalence and prognostic significance of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) after SAVR remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, long-term outcomes, and predictors of HFpEF after successful SAVR. Methods: In total, 320 patients were prospectively followed with a comprehensive clinical and echocardiographic evaluation before and after SAVR. Results: One year after surgery, 63 patients (19.7%) met the diagnostic criteria for HFpEF, 36 patients (11.3%) had heart failure with (mildly) reduced ejection fraction (HF(m)rEF), and 221 patients (69.1%) were free from HF. Six-year follow-up revealed that HFpEF was associated with an increased risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (aHR 2.73, 95% CI 1.14-6.50; p = 0.024), primarily driven by HF-related hospitalizations (aHR 4.69, 95% CI 1.24-17.75; p = 0.023). Independent predictors of HFpEF were age (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; p < 0.001), body mass index (aOR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.13; p = 0.018), smoking (aOR 2.33, 95% CI 1.20-4.53; p = 0.013), and a preoperative HFA-PEFF score ≥ 5 (aOR 2.76, 95% CI 1.41-5.42; p = 0.003). Conclusions: HFpEF was diagnosed in one out of five patients after successful SAVR and was associated with adverse long-term outcomes. Age, obesity, smoking, and HFA-PEFF scores were found to be independent predictors of postoperative HFpEF, which may guide perioperative risk stratification and early postoperative management.

articles.title: Non-Invasive Physiological Stratification of Echocardiographic Right Ventricular Involvement in Suspected Pulmonary Hypertension: The NIRV Score and Its TAPSE/PASP-Defined Binary Classification.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: In suspected pulmonary hypertension (PH), functional limitation may reflect right ventricular (RV) involvement and non-RV comorbidity. We developed the Non-Invasive Right Ventricular (NIRV) score, integrating RV-pulmonary arterial coupling and myocardial stress, to identify objective RV disease and assess prognostic information beyond World Health Organization functional class (WHO-FC). Methods: This single-centre retrospective cohort included consecutive adults evaluated for suspected PH. NIRV assigns 2 points for tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion to pulmonary artery systolic pressure ratio (TAPSE/PASP) ≤0.31 mm/mmHg and 1 point for N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) ≥1400 pg/mL, yielding a 0-3 score. Thus, binary NIRV classification (0-1 vs. 2-3) depends exclusively on TAPSE/PASP ≤ 0.31 mm/mmHg. Objective RV disease required abnormalities in at least two of three prespecified echocardiographic domains and was defined independently of WHO-FC, TAPSE/PASP, NT-proBNP, and NIRV-derived classifications. Results: Of 490 patients, 379 had an available NIRV score, and objective RV disease was evaluable in 379 patients, of whom 158 (41.7%) met the echocardiographic RV involvement criteria. Among 358 patients with valid WHO-FC data, TAPSE/PASP-defined classification showed higher sensitivity (77.5% vs. 35.8%) but lower specificity (61.8% vs. 75.8%) than WHO-FC III-IV. In the 379-patient cohort, the AUC increased only marginally when continuous NT-proBNP was added to TAPSE/PASP (0.777 to 0.782). WHO-low/NIRV-high discordance occurred in 126/361 (34.9%); 71/126 with outcome data (56.3%) had objective RV disease. The date-complete survival cohort included 379 patients (140 deaths), with a median follow-up of 727 days. In the clinically adjusted Cox model (n = 354; 128 deaths), NIRV 3 was associated with higher mortality hazard than NIRV 0 (HR, 2.59; 95% CI, 1.46-4.59), although the association across score categories was nonmonotonic. Conclusions: The TAPSE/PASP-defined binary NIRV classification was associated with the study-defined echocardiographic RV involvement phenotype, whereas the full 0-3 score retained information from both physiological components. Categorical NIRV was associated with all-cause mortality in exploratory Cox analyses, without a monotonic mortality gradient. Prospective external validation is required before use.

articles.title: Subtotal Gastrectomy in a Patient with Systemic Sclerosis-Associated Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and an Implantable Treprostinil Pump: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: We describe the perioperative management of an implanted abdominal treprostinil pump during subtotal gastrectomy for gastric cancer in a patient with systemic sclerosis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Methods: The patient was a 66-year-old woman with chronic hypoxemia requiring home oxygen. Before surgery, PAH therapy had reduced mean pulmonary artery pressure to 19 mmHg and pulmonary vascular resistance to 2.88 Wood units. The pump was localized preoperatively. Laparoscopic exploration was followed by planned laparotomy through an incision that avoided the pump pocket. An external syringe pump and a written conversion protocol were available for backup intravenous treprostinil delivery. Results: The pump remained in situ, with no documented device complication or clinically apparent interruption of treprostinil delivery. Bosentan and sildenafil were resumed on the evening of surgery. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7 on her usual home oxygen regimen. Conclusions: Preoperative pump localization and incision planning helped preserve the implanted treprostinil system during subtotal gastrectomy, with a contingency plan for external infusion.

articles.title: Support Needs, Care Gaps and Preferences Across the Paediatric Congenital Heart Surgery Care Continuum: A Scoping Review Based Primarily on Parent and Caregiver Reports.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Congenital heart surgery combines episodes of critical illness with continuing family caregiving. This scoping review mapped child- and parent-reported support needs, preferences and care gaps across the surgical continuum and identified implications for family-centred nursing care. Methods: Following JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR, PubMed, CINAHL Complete and Scopus scientific databases were searched to identify English-language primary evidence published between January 2010 and July 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed the original full texts; both confirmed the eligibility of four revision-stage additions. Descriptive mapping and content analysis classified reports by care stage, support domain and reporter. Results: The findings primarily reflect parent and caregiver accounts of support needs, care gaps and preferences across the surgical continuum. Database searching yielded 2263 records. Following record reconciliation and reference checking, 154 reports were assessed, with 73 included in the study. Information or education was represented in 55 reports (75.3%), followed by emotional or psycho-social support (43, 58.9%), communication or participation (40, 54.8%), and discharge or home-care support (32, 43.8%). Discharge, home and interstage care was the care stage grouping most represented (21, 28.8%). Five reports (6.8%) included the perspectives of children and adolescents alongside caregivers. The limited inclusion of child and adolescent perspectives restricts conclusions about children's own priorities and highlights the need for developmentally appropriate research that elicits their views directly. Conclusions: The review provides a stage-specific map linking reported support requirements to potential nursing responses. Priorities include repeated needs assessment, tailored communication, family participation, discharge preparation and coordinated support. These responses require evaluation, while the limited representation of children's perspectives restricts conclusions about their own priorities.

articles.title: Combining Peripheral Inflammatory Biomarkers and aEEG Background Monitoring to Predict Neurological Outcome in Neonates Undergoing Cardiac Surgery for Congenital Heart Disease: A Real-World Pilot Experience.
articles.abstract: Background: Neonates with congenital heart disease (CHD) are at increased risk of neurological deficits. We investigated perioperative trajectories of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and monocyte-to-albumin ratio (MAR), their association with amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) background, and their contribution to short-term neurological outcome prediction. Methods: We retrospectively studied 64 neonates with CHD admitted for surgical evaluation. Combined conventional EEG/amplitude EEG (cEEG/aEEG) monitoring was performed pre-operatively (T0), within 24 h after surgery (T1), and 7-10 days post-operatively (T2). aEEG background was dichotomized as normal or abnormal. NLR and MAR were calculated from routine laboratory parameters. Associations with aEEG background and neurological outcome at intensive care unit discharge were assessed using non-parametric analyses and receiver operating characteristic curves. Results: Both NLR and MAR values showed significant perioperative longitudinal variation, characterized by a transient post-operative increase followed by normalization at one week. NLR demonstrated a consistent association with worsening aEEG background across all timepoints (T0: ρ = 0.566, pFDR < 0.001; ρ = 0.363, pFDR = 0.013; T2: ρ = 0.477, pFDR < 0.001), whereas MAR showed no significant association with neurophysiological abnormalities. Higher T2 NLR was associated with unfavorable short-term neurological outcome (ρ = 0.397, p_FDR = 0.016). T2 aEEG background and NLR showed comparable discriminative performance (AUC = 0.783 and 0.760, respectively). The combined NLR + aEEG model yielded a numerically higher AUC (0.844), although the improvement was not statistically significant. Conclusions: Our findings suggest an exploratory association between perioperative systemic inflammation and neurophysiological dysfunction in neonates with CHD. NLR may represent a potential adjunctive marker of perioperative cerebral dysfunction, although with susceptibility to systemic and perioperative complications. These preliminary findings warrant further investigation of inflammatory biomarkers alongside aEEG monitoring to better characterize their potential role in neurological risk stratification.

articles.title: Lewis ladder: A web application that draws ladder diagrams from the surface electrocardiogram.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ladder diagrams represent proposed arrhythmic activation sequences, but they are still drawn by hand, and the intracardiac recording that each diagram predicts is rarely made explicit. No available tool derives the diagram from intervals measured on the patient's own tracing.

DESCRIPTION: Lewis Ladder is a free web application for teaching surface electrocardiographic interpretation with ladder diagrams. The user marks P-wave and QRS onsets on a calibrated strip; the engine measures the intervals, applies 11 exclusion and 24 caution rules taken from published electrophysiologic criteria to 14 candidate readings, and draws the ladder diagram of each reading that remains, including paced rhythms. All rules, thresholds, and assumed conduction times are tabulated. On 28 synthetic tracings of known mechanism, the intended reading was never excluded, with exact marks or with every mark displaced by random error (standard deviation up to 20 ms; 11,200 classifications), and 794 automated checks cover the engine. A free-drawing mode supports diagrams built by hand. Two schematic extensions, an electrophysiology view of the implied intracardiac channels and a network model of conduction that the user can pace, are proofs of concept.

CLINICAL ROLE: The application is a teaching aid that makes mechanistic hypotheses explicit and checkable against the tracing. It is not a diagnostic device.

CURRENT PROBLEMS: Educational benefit has not been measured, and the schematic electrograms have been checked only against published sources. Onsets and QRS duration are entered manually, and the network model does not reproduce every pacing response observed during catheter studies.

articles.title: Balancing Feasibility and Validity: A Delphi Consensus on Frailty Assessment Tools in Perioperative Care.
Practice analysis: Developing a content outline for the pediatric gastroenterology certification exam.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To ensure board certification in pediatric gastroenterology reflects current clinical practice, the American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) conducted a comprehensive practice analysis to update the certification content outline.

METHODS: An 11-member panel of practicing pediatric gastroenterologists identified key practice domains, tasks, and knowledge areas. These were organized into testable content domains and subdomains. All ABP board-certified pediatric gastroenterologists were surveyed for feedback, which informed final revisions to the content outline.

RESULTS: The panel produced a practice analysis document and an updated content outline. Survey feedback validated the relevance of the revised outline, which was finalized and approved by the subspecialty board.

CONCLUSIONS: The updated content outline ensures that certification reflects contemporary clinical practice and supports the development of a relevant examination for pediatric gastroenterologists.

articles.title: Plastic Surgery Learning Objectives for Undergraduate Medical Education: A National Delphi Survey to Establish Consensus.
authors: Canadian Plastic Surgery Undergraduate Medical Education Curriculum Development Working Group
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Dedicated exposure to plastic and reconstructive surgery (PRS) in undergraduate medical education is limited, with most Canadian medical students receiving no exposure throughout their training. The lack of standardized PRS learning objectives leaves graduating medical students unaware of basic PRS principles, emergent presentations, and indications for referral. This study aims to develop a national consensus-based set of undergraduate PRS learning objectives.

METHODS: A literature search was conducted to identify PRS learning objectives. The Canadian PRS Undergraduate Medical Education Curriculum Development Working Group, composed of PRS program directors (PDs), family medicine PDs, and surgical educators, was convened to assess the appropriateness of learning objectives for medical students. A 3-round Delphi consensus was completed (January-September 2025). Objectives achieving ≥75% consensus are included in the ratified list of objectives. Institutional research ethics board approval was obtained.

RESULTS: Of 70 invited experts, 27 completed survey round 1, with a response rate above 70% in subsequent rounds. Panelists include 14 plastic surgeons across 7 provinces. A total of 56 objectives were included in the initial list of proposed objectives. After 3 rounds, 42 objectives were included in the final list, across the following subdomains: general principles of surgery and reconstruction, upper extremity, skin, burns, breast, craniofacial, and gender-affirming surgery.

CONCLUSIONS: A standardized set of PRS learning objectives is available for all Canadian medical students to address current knowledge gaps in medical education. These consensus-based objectives should supplement current resources, such as the existing Medical Council of Canada Examination Objectives, and future plastic surgery-focused education initiatives.

articles.title: Peripartum infective endocarditis in complex congenital heart disease: Melody valve infection after caesarean delivery.
articles.abstract: We describe the pregnancy and postpartum course of a 26-year-old nulliparous woman with repaired double outlet right ventricle, ventricular septal defect, and severe pulmonary stenosis who was managed by a multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team. She underwent emergency caesarean delivery at 38 weeks. Her postpartum course was complicated by suspected pulmonary embolism and infective endocarditis of a Melody valve, requiring right ventricle-pulmonary artery conduit replacement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of postpartum cardiopulmonary symptoms in women with complex congenital heart disease and raises important questions regarding infective endocarditis prophylaxis in women with prosthetic cardiac material.

articles.title: Managing Acute Asthma Exacerbations: A Survey Study of Real-world Practice Patterns and Specialty-related Differences.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although acute severe asthma (ASA) affects 55% of asthma exacerbations, variations in physicians' management of ASA have received less attention than practice trends for patients with stable asthma. Moreover, differences in care provided by specialists have not been addressed. This study aims to explore physicians' knowledge, attitudes, and practice trends regarding pharmacological and ventilatory management of ASA, and to verify practice variations between pulmonologists and non-pulmonologists.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional survey, a non-probability convenience sample of physicians entitled to manage ASA was surveyed using Google Forms to collect data on identification of exacerbations, triage decisions, pharmacological and ventilatory management practices, and beliefs about prognosis. Subgroup responses (pulmonologists versus non-pulmonologists) were compared.

RESULTS: Ninety-three respondents were recruited mainly from the Middle East-North Africa region (59.1%), Europe (13.9%), and South/East Asia (12.9%). Sixty percent used predefined criteria to diagnose ASA, but these criteria were used less frequently for triage decisions. High-flow nasal cannula was readily available (93.5%), but "usually or mostly" used by only 29.03%. Pulmonologists demonstrated higher non-invasive ventilation (NIV) use "within and beyond" intensive care unit (P = 0.001), and more identified appropriate NIV settings (P = 0.048). 47% preferred individualizing the invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) mode. Multiple organ failure, cardiac arrest, asthma severity, and comorbid pneumonia were most frequently rated as strongly correlated with mortality or endotracheal intubation. Respondents believed that ASA patients who receive IMV after a failed NIV trial have worse prognosis.

CONCLUSION: The use of pre-defined criteria for identifying ASA and triage decisions remains suboptimal. Several caveats related to optimal ventilatory settings exist, with significant differences between pulmonologists and non-pulmonologists.

articles.title: Predictors of Mortality in Patients with Acute Respiratory Failure in a Respiratory Intensive Care Unit: A Chaid-Based Classification Model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify demographic, clinical, and laboratory parameters associated with mortality among patients admitted to the respiratory intensive care unit (RICU) for acute respiratory failure, and to develop an interpretable mortality classification model.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 765 patients admitted between January 2018 and January 2023. A CHAID tree was developed using admission variables and internally evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation. Classification measures and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression complemented the tree analysis and was compared with APACHE II alone.

RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was 40.9% (313/765). CHAID selected APACHE II, albumin, platelet-to-neutrophil ratio (PNR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and malignancy. The full-sample AUC was 0.816 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.786-0.844]; sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 58.5%, 85.8%, and 74.6%, respectively. In stratified 10-fold cross-validation, sensitivity was 53.0%, specificity was 84.1%, positive predictive value was 69.7%, negative predictive value was 72.1%, and accuracy was 71.4%. In multivariable analysis, higher APACHE II, higher neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, male sex, and malignancy were independently associated with mortality, whereas higher albumin and PNR were inversely associated with mortality. The combined logistic model outperformed APACHE II alone in repeated cross-validation (AUC difference 0.060, 95% CI 0.032-0.087; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: APACHE II was the principal mortality discriminator, while albumin, inflammatory cell ratios, CRP, and malignancy refined risk within specific severity strata. The internally evaluated models require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Association Between Serum Asprosin, FABP4, and Vaspin Levels and Coronary Artery Disease in Patients with COPD.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is linked to systemic inflammatory activity and an increased burden of cardiovascular comorbidity, particularly coronary artery disease (CAD). This study aimed to examine serum asprosin, fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4), and vaspin levels in COPD patients according to the presence or absence of CAD.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 120 participants: COPD (n = 40), COPD with CAD (n = 40), and healthy controls (n = 40). Serum biomarker levels were compared among groups. Receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression were used to assess discriminative performance and independent associations.

RESULTS: Biomarker levels differed significantly among groups (P < 0.001). Median asprosin levels were 8.32, 14.98, and 11.88 ng/mL; median FABP4 levels were 205.86, 708.63, and 416.18 ng/L; and median vaspin levels were 4.37, 6.17, and 5.50 ng/mL in the COPD, COPD+CAD, and control groups, respectively. Area under the curve values were 0.898 for asprosin, 0.891 for vaspin, and 0.860 for FABP4 (all P < 0.001). After adjustment for age and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, asprosin [odds ratio (OR) 1.965, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.436-2.691], FABP4 (OR 1.014, 95% CI 1.007-1.021), and vaspin (OR 2.896, 95% CI 1.767-4.745) remained independently associated with CAD (all P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Serum asprosin, FABP4, and vaspin levels were elevated in COPD patients with CAD, and showed discriminative ability in this cohort, with each biomarker remaining associated with CAD after adjustment for age and LDL cholesterol. These findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

articles.title: Expert Consensus Recommendations for Risk-Adapted Management of Myeloproliferative Neoplasms 2026.
articles.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), including polycythemia vera (PV), essential thrombocythemia (ET), and myelofibrosis (MF), are clonal hematopoietic disorders, with ET representing the most common Philadelphia chromosome-negative MPN in Korea. Since the previous Korean MPN guideline was published in 2020, the field has advanced considerably: diagnostic criteria have been further refined, the molecular landscape informing prognosis and treatment decisions has broadened, and new agents have become available. These developments have created a need to update the previous recommendations for the Korean clinical context. These expert consensus recommendations were developed by the Korean Society of Hematology MPN working Party to provide practical, evidence-informed recommendations for the risk-adapted management of PV, ET, and MF in Korean clinical practice. Recommendations are based on a comprehensive review of current international guidelines, including those of the European LeukemiaNet (ELN) and the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), alongside emerging data from Korean and Asian patient populations. They address risk stratification frameworks, treatment goals evolving from hematologic response toward molecular response, and therapeutic options including phlebotomy, aspirin, cytoreductive agents, and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Special clinical situations, including MPN in pregnancy and advanced-phase disease (accelerated and blast phase), are also addressed. These recommendations aim to support individualized, biology-informed treatment decisions, and to facilitate the integration of evolving therapeutic strategies into routine Korean hematology practice.

articles.title: Simultaneous UPLC-MS/MS determination of apalutamide, atorvastatin and their metabolites in rat plasma for pharmacokinetic interaction studies.
articles.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
articles.abstract: Apalutamide and atorvastatin are frequently co-prescribed for prostate cancer patients complicated with dyslipidemia, yet the pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions (DDIs) between the two agents remain poorly characterized. Herein, we established and fully validated a rapid ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) assay for simultaneous quantitation of apalutamide, its active metabolite N-desmethyl apalutamide, atorvastatin, and two primary active atorvastatin metabolites (2-hydroxy-atorvastatin and 4-hydroxy-atorvastatin) in rat plasma, followed by in-vivo evaluation of their reciprocal DDIs. The selectivity of UPLC-MS/MS assay was satisfactory and the proposed method was linear (All r2 >0.99). The intra-day and inter-day precision of all the analytes were within 15%, and the accuracy ranged from 85.47% to 113.98%. The mean extraction recoveries for all components exceeded 84%. All components demonstrated good stability under conditions of storage at room temperature for 3 h, freeze-thaw conditions, storage at 4°C, and long-term freezing. In-vivo pharmacokinetic data revealed markedly elevated systemic exposure of apalutamide upon co-administration with atorvastatin; conversely, apalutamide co-treatment substantially reduced plasma atorvastatin concentrations while elevating levels of its oxidative metabolites. To our knowledge, this is the first pre-clinical report describing such interactions between antihyperlipidemia drugs and androgen receptor inhibitors. Our results indicate that the combination of apalutamide and atorvastatin may alter blood drug concentrations of each other in rats, thereby influencing their efficacy or toxicity, which may be due to their inducing or inhibiting effect on metabolic enzymes and transporters.

articles.title: Assessing proper patient-reported outcomes after recent discharge in acute heart failure - a longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Acute decompensation of heart failure (HF) is a major cause of hospital admissions and adverse outcomes. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) offer valuable insights into patient experience and may support treatment decisions. This study aimed to assess PROMs in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated HF at multiple time points after discharge to evaluate the feasibility of repeated PROM assessments and to capture changes in health status, medication management, and quality of life.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Consecutive patients hospitalized for decompensated HF completed PROMs at 30 days, 6 months, and 12 months post-discharge. Collected data included demographics, comorbidities, hospitalizations, medication use, and PROMs using the KCCQ-12, PROMIS Physical Function Shortform 4a (PROMIS-4a), and PHQ-2. Generic quality of life was assessed with the EQ-5D. Among 99 patients (median age 66 years, 33% women, 90% NYHA III/IV on admission, 89% rehospitalized for HF within 12 months), all PROM instruments indicated substantial disease burden. Strong internal consistency observed (Cronbach's alpha 0.75-0.90). PROMIS-4a was negatively associated with age (p < 0.01) and with sex (p = 0.04), while KCCQ-12 was associated with age (p = 0.04). All PROM scores improved during follow-up. Cardiovascular events-including transplantation, rehospitalization, emergency treatment, and therapy failure-did not significantly affect PROM trajectories.

CONCLUSION: Repeated assessment of patient-reported outcomes after HF decompensation is feasible. Using one or two PROM instruments may be sufficient, as the measures showed parallel development. Preliminary findings indicate that PROMs capture aspects of patient health not fully explained by HF severity or treatment modalities.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Pre- and Post-Treatment PET-CT Metrics After Definitive Chemoradiation for Anal Canal Cancer.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although post-treatment FDG-PET/CT is frequently obtained following definitive chemoradiation (CRT) for locally advanced anal canal cancer (LAACC), its prognostic utility remains uncertain. We hypothesized that quantitative PET/CT metrics would be associated with overall survival (OS) and that pre-treatment metabolic parameters would provide greater prognostic information than post-treatment metabolic response.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients with LAACC who underwent definitive CRT and both pre-treatment and post-treatment fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT. Quantitative PET metrics were extracted, including mean SUL, total lesion glycolysis (TLG), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), maximum SUL, and peak SUL. OS was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Associations between PET-derived variables and OS were evaluated using univariable Cox proportional hazards regression, with optimal cutoffs identified using maximally selected rank statistics (MaxStat).

RESULTS: Forty-five patients were included (median age 57.7 years), with post-treatment PET/CT performed at a median of 4.4 months following CRT. Lean body mass (HR 3.10, 95% CI 1.01-9.50; p = 0.049) and pre-treatment primary tumor mean SUL (HR 4.93, 95% CI 1.40-17.37; p = 0.013), size (HR 4.01, 95% CI 1.22-13.17; p = 0.022), TLG (HR 3.68, 95% CI 1.11-12.14; p = 0.033), and peak SUL (HR 3.31, 95% CI 1.02-10.72; p = 0.046) were associated with OS in exploratory univariable analyses. Post-treatment, higher weight (HR 4.94, 95% CI 1.06-22.96; p=0.041; cutoff 60.42 kg; N=45) and lean body mass (HR 4.82, 95% CI 1.06-21.90; p=0.042; cutoff 44.50 kg; N=44) were associated with worse OS. No post-treatment PET-derived metabolic parameters met the nominal threshold for statistical significance. Among patients with higher baseline metabolic activity, greater reduction in mean SUL following CRT demonstrated a nonsignificant trend toward improved OS.

CONCLUSION: Pre-treatment FDG-PET/CT metabolic parameters demonstrated stronger associations with OS than post-treatment metabolic parameters in this exploratory cohort. Baseline tumor metabolic activity may provide useful prognostic information in patients with LAACC, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Resting State Functional Connectivity in Women With Depression Following Pregnenolone Administration.
articles.abstract: Background: Neurosteroids, such as pregnenolone, have potential in mood disorder treatment. Because depression is associated with dysregulated connectivity in brain networks, a systems-level biomarker for neurosteroids modulation of large-scale brain networks can offer critical insight into circuits underlying treatment response. To our knowledge, no studies have examined resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) in people with depression following pregnenolone administration. Methods: In this crossover design study conducted between 2019-2021, women (n=29, mean age=45.6 years) with major depressive disorder (DSM-5) were randomized to 7 days of oral pregnenolone 500 mg/d, pregnenolone 800 mg/d, and placebo with a 14-day washout between conditions. After each treatment, steroid levels and resting-state fMRI (rsfMRI) data were collected. A seed-based voxel-wise analysis, with bilateral amygdala as seed, investigated rsFC alterations following treatment conditions in a per-protocol sample (n=11). Results: Compared to placebo, pregnenolone 500 mg/d was associated with decreased connectivity between the bilateral amygdala and left frontal pole (PFDR=.011). Difference in amygdala connectivity between pregnenolone 800 mg/d and placebo was nonsignificant. Allopregnanolone serum levels increased significantly with administration of either pregnenolone dose as compared to placebo. Conclusions: Findings suggest that pregnenolone 500 mg/d was associated with decreased connectivity between the amygdala and frontal pole, brain regions pertinent to depression and cognitive control. Presence of rsFC changes at 500 mg/d but not 800 mg/d suggests an inverted-U dose-response pattern, where moderate dosing optimally engages neural circuits compared to higher doses. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03645096.

articles.title: Beyond the Threshold: Why Heritable Aortic Disease Demands Individualized, Interdisciplinary Care.
Recalibrating the Risks and Benefits of Parenteral Prostaglandin Therapy After Sotatercept.
Acute Coronary Syndromes in Hemophilia: Insights From a Case of Hemophilia A and Contemporary Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Improved survival in patients with hemophilia has resulted in an aging population increasingly exposed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Acute coronary syndromes pose complex therapeutic challenges because ischemic and hemorrhagic risks must be balanced.

CASE SUMMARY: An 82-year-old man with partial factor VIII deficiency presented with high-risk non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. After hematology-guided factor VIII replacement, coronary angiography showed nonobstructive atheromatosis, supporting a working diagnosis of myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries. Cardiac magnetic resonance was declined because of claustrophobia. In the absence of stent implantation, aspirin monotherapy was selected.

REVIEW SUMMARY: This review addresses factor replacement, antithrombotic and revascularization strategies, evaluation of myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, and emerging hemophilia therapies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Management of acute coronary syndrome in hemophilia requires individualized, multidisciplinary balancing of thrombotic and bleeding risks.

articles.title: Treat Downstream, Reassess Upstream: A Staged Strategy for Combined Aortic and Mitral Regurgitation.
Right-to-Left Shunting During Mitral TEER: How to Be Prepared.
Stent-Edge Dissection and Intramural Hematoma: Current and Evolving Management Strategies.
Percutaneous Closure of Unroofed Coronary Sinus: A Novel Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Unroofed coronary sinus (CS) is a rare cause of left-to-right shunting and right-sided volume overload. Transcatheter treatment is feasible only in selected anatomies.

CASE SUMMARY: A 48-year-old woman with prior congenital heart surgery presented with acute heart failure and massive pleural effusion. Multimodality evaluation, including cardiac magnetic resonance and cardiac catheterization, diagnosed an unroofed CS with a significant left-to-right shunt. At the heart team evaluation, a percutaneous approach was planned because the patient refused surgery. However, because of the large size and unfavorable morphology of the defect, direct closure was deemed unfeasible. Thus, after confirmation of the tolerability of the procedure by a temporary balloon occlusion test, closure of the CS ostium into the right atrium was performed. At 5-month follow-up, no residual shunt was detected, pulmonary pressure improved, and functional capacity was preserved without exercise-induced desaturation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the importance of individualized, anatomy-driven percutaneous strategies in complex congenital heart disease.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CS ostial occlusion may provide a feasible percutaneous option when conventional closure is anatomically unsuitable. Three-dimensional preprocedural simulation, multimodality imaging, and temporary balloon occlusion are key to procedural planning and safety assessment.

Where There Is a Will, There Is a Way.
Medical Assistance in Dying: A New Way Forward in End-of-Life Care for Patients With an LVAD.
Rapid-Onset Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Causing Cardiogenic Shock Due to Thrombotic Coronary Occlusions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) is one of the most common but potentially fatal immune-mediated adverse drug reactions and may develop with a rapid onset in patients re-exposed to heparin within 90 days of prior heparin administration.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient with chronic coronary syndrome developed recurrent thrombotic coronary occlusions during percutaneous coronary intervention because of rapid-onset HIT, resulting in in-hospital cardiac arrest complicated by cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support. Intravenous immunoglobulin was administered as rescue therapy.

DISCUSSION: Unexplained and recurrent periprocedural coronary thrombosis during invasive coronary angiography should prompt consideration of HIT as a differential diagnosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Periprocedural coronary thrombosis during percutaneous coronary intervention because of rapid-onset HIT is a rare and potentially life-threatening condition that may occur in patients re-exposed to heparin following recent heparin administration. Intravenous immunoglobulin G should be considered in severe refractory HIT.

articles.title: Incidental ARCAPA: When the Adult Coronary Workup Finds a Congenital Lesion.
Catecholamine-Induced Cardiomyopathy Masquerading as Acute Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy (CICMP) is a rare but reversible condition that closely mimics acute myocardial infarction (AMI), often leading to misdiagnosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A 61-year-old woman with previous coronary stenosis presented with chest tightness, troponin elevation, and electrocardiographic changes suggesting AMI. Markedly elevated plasma and urinary catecholamines and DOTATATE-positron emission tomography/computed tomography identified CICMP secondary to a retroperitoneal paraganglioma. Coronary angiography and cardiac magnetic resonance effectively excluded AMI. After α blockade and surgical resection, cardiac function fully recovered.

DISCUSSION: CICMP should be suspected in patients with disproportionate biomarker elevation, preserved ventricular function, blood pressure lability, or an abdominal mass. Multimodal imaging and catecholamine testing facilitate accurate diagnosis; abdominal compression is emphasized as a potential trigger for catecholamine crisis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Catecholamine-secreting tumors can present as AMI mimics. Key diagnostic clues include biomarker-ventricular function mismatch, blood pressure lability, and multiorgan dysfunction. Early α blockade and surgical resection enable complete recovery.

articles.title: Coronary Trophoblastic Embolism Causing STEMI in a Female With Twin Pregnancy With Partial Mole.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) during pregnancy is rare. Spontaneous coronary artery dissection and atherosclerotic coronary disease are leading causes, whereas coronary embolism is less common.

CASE SUMMARY: A 27-year-old woman with a twin pregnancy consisting of 1 viable fetus and 1 partial hydatidiform mole developed preeclampsia. Because of growth restriction, a cesarean delivery was performed at 32 weeks. During delivery, she developed acute dyspnea and circulatory shock, requiring intensive care. Electrocardiography demonstrated inferolateral STEMI. Coronary angiography revealed embolic occlusions in the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery. Thrombus aspiration restored flow without stent implantation. Histopathology showed human chorionic gonadotropin-positive syncytiotrophoblast cells, confirming trophoblast embolism. Computed tomography demonstrated a patent foramen ovale, suggesting paradoxical embolization.

DISCUSSION: Trophoblastic embolization through a patent foramen ovale represents an extremely rare cause of STEMI associated with molar pregnancy, preeclampsia, and disseminated intravascular coagulation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case highlights the importance of considering coronary embolism in peripartum myocardial infarction and the diagnostic value of thrombus histopathology.

articles.title: Intraplaque Hemorrhage: Current and Prospective.
One Shunt Hides Another: Doppler and the Case for Single-Stage Repair in Dual-Shunt Aorto-Atrial Fistulae.
[Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure and do-not-intubate order].
articles.abstract: The management of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) has been extensively studied; however, patients with a do-not-intubate (DNI) order have been excluded from clinical trials. For these patients with moderate to severe AHRF, non-invasive respiratory supports represent an alternative to intubation. Given the highly variable prognosis, which depends on pre-existing frailty and the underlying etiology of the AHRF, careful patient selection is essential to identify those most likely to benefit from these interventions. A time-limited trial provides a structured framework for the patient, their relatives, and the healthcare team to pursue predefined therapeutic goals despite a substantial risk of treatment failure, during which the possibility of transitioning to comfort-focused care should be discussed openly.

articles.title: A rare presentation of coeliac crisis in a patient with Neurogenin-3 mutation congenital enteropathy.
articles.abstract: Neurogenin-3 (NEUROG3) mutations have been associated with congenital enteropathy, anendocrinosis, and early-onset diabetes and patients often require parenteral nutrition (PN). We present a case of homozygous NEUROG3 mutation who, having established enteral autonomy by 2.5 years old, re-presented with acute intestinal failure (IF) characterised by high stool output and metabolic acidosis. Investigations revealed positive coeliac serology, with duodenal histology confirming coeliac disease as the cause for relapsed IF. Institution of a gluten-free diet led to clinical recovery and PN cessation, although serological and histological markers of coeliac disease were slow to improve. Subsequently, the patient developed autoimmune thyroid disease.
