This case expands the recognised phenotype of NEUROG3-related disease, highlighting the importance of considering alternative causes for relapsed IF. Persistently elevated coeliac serology despite gluten-free diet, alongside development of autoimmune thyroid disease, suggest the possibility of broader immune dysregulation or autoimmune association with atypical phenotype in NEUROG3 mutation.

articles.title: Cognitive Correlations With Cholinergic Signaling in Parkinson Disease Depend on Global Cognitive Status.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine the cholinergic pathway differences in Parkinson disease (PD) and healthy controls and whether correlations between cholinergic function and cognitive domains within PD relate to global cognitive status.

METHODS: Cholinergic activity was measured in PD (N = 50) and control (N = 28) participants using the vesicular cholinergic transporter PET tracer, [18F]VAT. Scans were reconstructed and partial volume corrected. Regional binding potentials were calculated using the multilinear reference tissue model 2 (MRTM2). Global cognitive status was assessed using the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) scale with PD participants stratified as cognitively intact (CDR = 0, N = 28) and cognitively impaired (CDR = 0.5, N = 22). Cognitive performance was measured across attention, memory, language, visuospatial, and executive function domains. Regions of interest (ROIs) were defined using all PD and control participants, identifying regions with [18F]VAT-cognitive domain correlations for subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: PD participants demonstrated significantly lower [18F]VAT binding relative to controls but not between PD subgroups. [18F]VAT correlations were identified in whole-group analysis for attention and visuospatial function. Stepwise linear regression revealed significant regional associations between [18F]VAT and attention for the whole-PD group and both attention and visuospatial function for the cognitively impaired PD group. In fact, the PD group with cognitive impairment exhibited strong correlations (r > 0.5, 5% FDR) between [18F]VAT and visuospatial function in almost all ROIs.

INTERPRETATION: These results demonstrate that the relationship between cholinergic signaling and visuospatial function differs based on global cognitive status in PD. Significant differences in VAT binding across the full PD sample suggest that cholinergic denervation precedes cognitive impairment in PD and imply other compensatory mechanisms may exist in cognitively intact participants but this needs confirmation in longitudinal analysis.

articles.title: BMI percentile trajectories and liver enzyme changes in children with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A longitudinal cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The incidence of pediatric obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) are rapidly rising. However, the impact of dynamic body mass index (BMI) changes on liver chemistries remains understudied. We investigated the association between longitudinal changes in BMI percentile and changes in liver chemistries among children with MASLD.

METHODS: In this multicenter study, 1169 children with biopsy-confirmed MASLD enrolled in the Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis Clinical Research Network were followed for a mean of 4.0 years. BMI percentiles were calculated using the lambda-mu-sigma method with an extended metric to capture nuances at extreme values. Generalized linear mixed-effects models with random effects for patients and clinics were applied, and inverse probability treatment weighting adjusted for demographics and baseline histologic features. Sensitivity analyses stratified by sex and ethnicity assessed robustness.

RESULTS: Participants (mean age 13 years; 72% Hispanic) with higher BMI percentiles exhibited elevated blood pressures, increased insulin levels, and a lower frequency of the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) GG variant. Each 5-unit increase in BMI percentile was independently associated with a 23% increase in alanine aminotransferase (1.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.17-1.30), a 13% increase in aspartate aminotransferase (1.13; 95% CI, 1.09-1.17), and a 12% increase in γ‑glutamyl transferase (1.12; 95% CI, 1.08-1.16).

CONCLUSIONS: Longitudinal increases in BMI percentile are independently associated with worse liver chemistry in pediatric MASLD. Routine monitoring of BMI trajectories, alongside early weight management strategies, may be critical to mitigating disease progression. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT01061684, NCT04454463.

articles.title: Clinical practices and professional support needs in Childhood Apraxia of Speech: A survey of Slovak and Czech speech-language pathologists.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Childhood Apraxia of Speech (CAS) is a complex motor speech disorder for which evidence is largely derived from English-speaking contexts, while data from Central Europe remain limited. This study examined diagnostic and therapeutic practices of speech-language pathologists in Slovakia and the Czech Republic and identified clinical challenges and support needs.

METHOD: A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 121 speech-language pathologists. The questionnaire included closed-ended and open-ended items and Likert-scale questions. Analyses comprised descriptive and exploratory inferential statistics.

RESULT: Speech-language pathologists reported limited CAS-related preparation during initial professional education and a persistent need for further training. Diagnostic reasoning emphasised broader motor difficulties, while inappropriate prosody and syllable segregation were selected less frequently. Therapeutic approaches and access to expert consultation differed between countries, but both samples reported limited structured support and clinically applicable resources. Therapy frequency was generally low, with most respondents providing less than one session per week.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest areas in which routine clinical practice may not fully align with evidence-based recommendations and highlight the need for structured professional support and accessible, clinically applicable guidance for CAS.

articles.title: Functional Somatic Symptoms in Paediatric Patients With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health
articles.abstract: Aberrant stress-system activation or dysregulation affects the cardiovascular system through various pathways, including the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, autonomic nervous system, neuro-endocrine system, and a range of neurophysiological intermediaries. In children with congenital heart disease-who have high rates of adverse childhood experiences, comorbid medical conditions, and neurodevelopmental issues-this activation/dysregulation commonly results in functional cardiac symptoms such as orthostatic intolerance, (functional) chest pain, and syncope-like presentations. Despite the obvious need, research into stress-system responses in children with congenital heart disease is limited. This article reviews commonly encountered clinical scenarios with the goal of encouraging practitioners to recognise the interconnections between structural cardiac lesions in children, stress-system activation/dysregulation, and functional somatic symptoms. Children with congenital heart disease and comorbid functional symptoms require comprehensive management strategies. We propose a framework to help clinicians facilitate appropriate treatment.

articles.title: Early Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Lower the Risk of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus in Women With Pre-Pregnancy Obesity: Protocol for the Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial (GLOW).
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Pre-pregnancy obesity substantially increases the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet preventive strategies before routine GDM screening remain limited. The Glucose monitoring to Lower risk of GDM in Obese pregnant Women (GLOW) trial aims to determine whether continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) initiated in early pregnancy reduces the incidence of GDM in women with pre-pregnancy obesity.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: GLOW is a national, multicentre, open-label, parallel-group randomised controlled trial enrolling 1034 women with pre-pregnancy body mass index ≥ 28 kg/m2, a singleton pregnancy and gestational age ≤ 14+6 weeks at eight hospitals in China. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to routine antenatal care alone or routine antenatal care plus CGM. In the CGM group, five consecutive 14-day sensors will be used from 14+0-14+6 to 24+0-24+6 weeks of gestation (70 days in total), with access to glucose values and standardised CGM education. The primary endpoint is the incidence of GDM diagnosed by a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test at 24+0-24+6 weeks. Secondary outcomes include gestational weight gain, maternal metabolic and anthropometric measures, lifestyle behaviours and maternal and neonatal outcomes.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: GLOW will determine whether early CGM introduced before routine GDM screening can reduce GDM incidence and favourably influence maternal metabolic and pregnancy outcomes in women with pre-pregnancy obesity. The findings may inform the role of early CGM as a preventive strategy in this high-risk population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2600130043.

articles.title: Insulin Secretion Modelling to Characterize Post-Bariatric Hypoglycaemia After Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) is an effective treatment for obesity and Type 2 diabetes. Some individuals develop postprandial hypoglycaemia, termed post-bariatric hypoglycaemia (PBH). PBH is associated with marked postprandial increases in incretin and insulin levels. This study investigates how insulin secretion differs between post-RYGB patients with and without hypoglycaemia by identifying key secretion parameters.

METHODS: Insulin secretion was modelled using plasma glucose, insulin and C-peptide concentration data obtained from mixed meal tolerance test in three cohorts: healthy individuals without a history of upper gastrointestinal surgery (controls, n = 11), post-RYGB individuals without hypoglycaemia (RYGB-non-hypo, n = 18) and post-RYGB individuals with hypoglycaemia (RYGB-PBH, n = 20).

RESULTS: Meal-driven insulin secretion differed across groups (p = 0.008) and was significantly higher in RYGB-PBH than controls (0.23 vs. 0.14 pmol/mg, p = 0.006), but not in RYGB-non-hypo (0.22, p = 0.071). Glucose-driven insulin secretion decreased in RYGB-non-hypo (0.04 vs. 0.07 pmol/kg/min per mg/dL, p = 0.005) but did not differ from controls in RYGB-PBH (0.08, p = 0.948), differing significantly between the two post-RYGB groups (p < 0.001). Meal absorption was significantly faster in both post-RYGB groups (9.08 and 8.44 vs. 11.48 min, both p < 0.001). Models fit plasma insulin and C-peptide well (mean joint nRMSE: 0.60-0.92 across groups). Parameters were estimated with good precision (CV < 100%).

CONCLUSIONS: Insulin secretion dynamics differ between post-RYGB patients with and without hypoglycaemia. Both groups showed faster meal absorption and a shift towards higher meal-driven secretion, significant only in RYGB-PBH, but only those without hypoglycaemia showed a reduction in glucose-driven secretion. This PBH model can support in silico development of glucagon-based interventions.

articles.title: Letter: Does Faecal Calprotectin Meaningfully Change Biopsy Decisions in Microscopic Colitis?
Turkish Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life Measure for Children/Adolescents With Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to adapt the Oral Health-Related Quality of Life for Adolescents with Down Syndrome (OH-QOLADS) scale into Turkish and evaluate its psychometric properties. It also explored oral health status and quality of life among children with Down syndrome (DS).

METHODS: The study included 100 children with DS and their mothers. Sociodemographic and oral health data were collected through structured questionnaires. The OH-QOLADS, comprising child and family forms with two timeframes, was translated and culturally adapted following international guidelines. Internal consistency, CFA, and item-total correlations were conducted to assess psychometric validity.

RESULTS: The Turkish OH-QOLADS showed excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α and McDonald's ω > 0.94) across all forms and timeframes. CFA supported the original four-factor structure (symptoms/functioning, emotional well-being, social participation, and family impact) with strong model fit indices (CFI > 0.98; RMSEA < 0.05). Most participants reported poor oral health, low tooth brushing frequency, and minimal preventive care. Oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) scores were significantly associated with comorbidities like thyroid disease, diabetes, and hearing impairments.

CONCLUSION: The Turkish OH-QOLADS is a valid, reliable tool for assessing OHRQoL in children with DS. The findings highlight the need for better access to preventive dental services and caregiver support.

articles.title: The Central Role of O-GlcNAcylation in Regulating Macrophages in the Pathogenesis of Periodontitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dental plaque biofilm, characterized primarily by dysregulated host immune-inflammatory responses and progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which the dynamic M1/M2 polarization of macrophages serves as a pivotal regulatory factor. O-GlcNAcylation is a nutrient-sensitive post translational modification, and the relationship between O-GlcNAcylation and periodontitis needs further elucidation.

METHODS: This article systematically reviews recent advances concerning the regulatory role of O-GlcNAcylation in macrophage-mediated periodontitis pathogenesis. Particular emphasis is placed on the bidirectional dose and site-specific effects of O-GlcNAcylation on macrophage polarization. In addition, the molecular mechanisms underlying pathological O-GlcNAcylation-mediated aggravated alveolar bone loss in diabetes-associated periodontitis are summarized.

RESULTS: Existing evidence identifies O-GlcNAcylation as a critical molecular hub linking metabolic derangements to periodontal osteoimmune destruction: it either potentiates M1-like pro-inflammatory responses and osteoclastogenesis, or facilitates M2-like reparative phenotypes and periodontal bone regeneration. In diabetes-associated periodontitis, aberrantly elevated O-GlcNAcylation significantly accelerates alveolar bone loss by enhancing inflammatory signaling and suppressing bone formation.

CONCLUSION: O-GlcNAcylation lays novel theoretical foundations and translational strategies for precision immuno-metabolic therapy of periodontitis, especially in patients complicated with metabolic syndrome.

articles.title: Longitudinal Blood Eosinophil Profiles and Response to Anti-IL-5/IL-5Rα Biologics in Severe Asthma.
authors: Asma Grave HULP Study Group and FJD UMA
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology

articles.title: Transcatheter Thrombus Removal With the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System in Children With Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Thromboembolic complications in children with congenital heart disease (CHD) carry significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients with single ventricle physiology. Current management strategies, including systemic anticoagulation, thrombolytics, and surgical thrombectomy, each carry substantial risks in this population. Transcatheter aspiration thrombectomy represents an emerging alternative. We retrospectively reviewed all pediatric patients with CHD at our institution who underwent transcatheter aspiration thrombectomy using the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System between January 2024 and February 2025. Patient demographics, cardiac diagnosis, thrombus location, procedural details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Five patients (age 5 months to 9 years; weight 6.3-25.9 kg) with diverse CHD diagnoses underwent six thrombectomy procedures. Thrombus locations included the Fontan circuit, inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, and internal jugular veins. Technical success with angiographic restoration of antegrade flow and no residual gradient across the segment of interest, was achieved in all cases (100%). Blood loss ranged from 6 to 23 mL/kg; all patients required packed red blood cell transfusion. No significant intraprocedural hemodynamic instability occurred. Three patients were discharged home with confirmed vessel patency on follow-up imaging (echocardiography and/or vascular ultrasound at 4-6 months post intervention). Two patients, both on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support prior to the procedure, subsequently died from causes unrelated to the thrombectomy intervention. In this limited case series, the Penumbra Indigo Lightning System demonstrated feasibility for transcatheter thrombus removal in pediatric patients across a spectrum of CHD. Given the limited number of available catheter systems in this population, this approach may be considered as a first-line or adjunct therapy in select patients when conventional medical management is insufficient or contraindicated. Further prospective studies are needed to define optimal patient selection, procedural techniques, and post-procedural management.

articles.title: Improved inverse probability weighting estimation and its application to predictive covariates.
articles.abstract: Inverse probability weighting (IPW) estimators are widely used to estimate average causal effects, primarily because they do not require explicit modeling of the outcome. However, by relying solely on the propensity score, they fail to fully utilize information from the outcome, often resulting in low estimation efficiency in practice. To address these limitations, we propose an improved IPW estimator that incorporates flexible outcome working models with zero marginal treatment contrast to enhance statistical efficiency, extending the existing linear regression adjustment framework. We compare adjustment strategies with and without predictive covariates. Under certain conditions, the proposed estimator exhibits double robustness: it yields consistent estimates if either the propensity score model or the constrained outcome regression model is correctly specified. Moreover, when both models are correctly specified, it achieves asymptotic variance no greater than that of the standard augmented IPW estimator. Extensive simulation studies are conducted to evaluate finite-sample performance. We also apply the proposed method to a diabetes dataset and find strong evidence of a causal link between retinopathy and high HbA1c levels. Thus, incorporating such covariates into both the propensity score and outcome models does not increase optimized asymptotic variance with known or correctly estimated propensity scores.

articles.title: Association of apolipoprotein E gene polymorphism with cognitive function and brain structural burden in elderly patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether apolipoprotein E (ApoE) ε4 carrier status is associated with 3-month cognitive performance and structural brain injury in older patients with intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS).

METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 150 patients aged ≥60 years with ICAS (≥50% stenosis on MRA/CTA). ApoE ε4 carriers (n = 21, 14.0%) were compared with noncarriers. Primary outcome was 3-month Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary cognitive outcome was 3-month Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score. White matter hyperintensity burden defined as Fazekas score ≥2 was primary structural outcome. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, education, symptomatic ICAS, hypertension, and diabetes. Firth's penalized logistic regression addressed near-complete separation in the Fazekas analysis. .

RESULTS: ApoE ε4 carrier status was associated with lower 3-month MoCA (β = -1.887, 95% CI: -3.359 to -0.415, P = 0.013) and MMSE scores (β = -1.931, 95% CI: -3.177 to -0.685, P = 0.003). The structural analysis yielded association with Fazekas score ≥2 (Firth OR = 6.144, 95% CI: 1.331 to 59.563, P = 0.017), although this estimate was imprecise and hypothesis-generating. Additional adjustment for baseline cognitive scores changed the cognitive estimates.   .

DISCUSSION: In older patients with ICAS, ApoE ε4 carriage is associated with poorer 3-month global cognitive performance. Given the modest sample size, few ε4 carriers, short follow-up, and single-center design, larger multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the longitudinal relationship between ApoE ε4 status and cognitive change.

articles.title: HIV proteins disrupt a network of phosphatidylinositol (4,5)-bisphosphate binding sites on the dopamine transporter to regulate amphetamine behaviours.
articles.abstract: Amphetamine (AMPH) use has been linked to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) transmission because HIV can spread through unprotected sex that is associated with AMPH use disorder (AUD). Thus, AUD and HIV have been termed a double epidemic. In this bidirectional relationship, the role played by AUD in HIV-dependent neuropathogenesis is well documented. By contrast, how HIV infection regulates the development of AUD remains elusive. In rodents, expression of HIV viral proteins, such as the trans-activator of transcription (Tat), enhances AMPH escalation (i.e. a progressive intensification of drug use), a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) criteria for addiction. In humans, HIV infection increases AMPH frequency of use, as well as the total amount used. Thus, it is possible that HIV/HIV proteins promote the progression of AUD. AMPH-associated behaviours stem, at least in part, from the ability of AMPH to reverse the dopamine (DA) transporter (DAT) function, causing non-vesicular DA release (NVDR) and an increase in extracellular DA. Previously, we provided the first evidence that specific domains of DAT engage in direct association with the plasma membrane lipid, phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2). These interactions are essential for AMPH-induced NVDR and specific behaviours. HIV Tat is a protein that binds PIP2 through its basic domain. We demonstrate that Tat impairs NVDR by disrupting the network of PIP2 binding sites on DAT. Our study provides an atomic scale mechanistic description on how Tat disrupts human DAT/PIP2 association and blunts AMPH-induced NVDR. Using Drosophila as an animal model, we show that Tat by blunting NVDR in the setting of AUD promotes AMPH escalation. KEY POINTS: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) trans-activator of transcription (Tat) impairs non-vesicular dopamine (DA) release (NVDR) by disrupting the network of PIP2 binding sites on human Da transporter (DAT). Our study provides an atomic scale mechanistic description on how Tat disrupts human DAT/phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate association and blunts amphetamine (AMPH)-induced NVDR. We associate Tat blunting of NVDR to the ability of Tat to foster AMPH escalation, using Drosophila as an animal model.

articles.title: Gestational Age and Birthweight in Risk Analyses of Retinopathy of Prematurity.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Low gestational age (GA) and birthweight (BW), the strongest risk factors for retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), are routinely adjusted for without consideration of variable structure. We explored how to model them, using sepsis, oxygen exposure, and small for gestational age (SGA) as illustrative exposures.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the prospective ELGAN cohort (23-27 weeks' gestation; 14 US hospitals, 2002-2004), excluding infants without eye examination or missing data, leaving 1,259 of 1,506 infants. Any ROP was modeled by logistic regression, with GA and BW as continuous, categorical, or indicator variables. Parameterizations were compared by likelihood ratio test and Akaike information criterion; effect modification was assessed by interaction terms.

RESULTS: ROP prevalence was 67%, declining from 91% at 23 to 47% at 27 weeks. A linear GA term fitted less well than week-specific indicators (p = 0.03). The crude oxygen OR, 4.3 (3.1-6.0), decreased to 2.2 (1.4-3.5) after GA adjustment, but exposure was confined to the lower GA group (331/638 vs 10/621). Sepsis estimates were stable (1.6 to 1.5; interaction p = 0.2). SGA was associated with ROP (1.8, 1.3-2.7), but only in the more mature half (3.0, 1.9-4.7 vs 1.1, 0.6-2.0; interaction p = 0.01).

CONCLUSION: GA and BW are not interchangeable proxies for immaturity; uncritical adjustment can attenuate, mask or reverse associations. As screening and prevention rely on such estimates, studies should state the assumed role of GA and BW, justify their functional form and report GA-specific estimates.

articles.title: Loneliness intervention in later life: a gerontological social work perspective.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Loneliness in later life is recognized as a determinant of health and wellbeing, yet its integration into gerontological social services and social work practice remains underexplored. This study examines how social services address loneliness among older adults, focusing on its incorporation into intervention processes, the distribution of responses across intervention levels, and the organizational barriers shaping preventive approaches.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: An exploratory mixed-methods study was conducted in Barcelona (Spain) with 388 participants. Qualitative data were obtained through 15 interviews and two focus groups with 22 professionals working in services for older adults. The quantitative component consisted of a questionnaire completed by 351 gerontological social workers. Data were analyzed using grounded-theory-informed coding and descriptive statistics, with findings integrated through triangulation.

RESULTS: Loneliness was addressed in intervention processes mainly once it had developed into an established problem, reflecting the predominance of secondary intervention. Preventive engagement was less frequent and constrained by crisis-driven access pathways, limited time and resources, and eligibility frameworks prioritizing administratively codified vulnerability. Participants described gerontological social work as playing a central coordinating role within interdisciplinary practice. Core actions emphasized the professional relationship, empowerment, family involvement, and community activation, whereas structural strategies such as addressing ageism and promoting digital inclusion were less consistently embedded.

DISCUSSION AND IMPLICATIONS: Findings reveal a preventive governance gap: loneliness is recognized as relational and structural, yet service architectures remain largely reactive. Strengthening responses requires aligning eligibility criteria with life-course transitions and reinforcing community-based infrastructures capable of sustaining belonging over time.

articles.title: Revisiting the gold standard: why 2-stage revision THA remains relevant for hip PJI: a 10-year experience with excellent infection-free survival.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 2-stage revision total hip arthroplasty (THA) remains the reference standard for the management of hip periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), despite increasing interest in 1-stage revision. This study reports the 10-year experience of a tertiary referral centre and evaluates infection control, implant survivorship, functional outcomes, and complications following staged revision.

METHODS: A retrospective review of prospectively collected data was performed for patients undergoing staged revision THA for hip PJI between 2014 and 2024. 65 patients met the inclusion criteria and were followed for a mean of 69.3 ± 28.9 months. Functional outcomes were assessed using the modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS). Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to determine implant survivorship, with reoperation, re-revision, recurrent infection, or mortality within 1 year of PJI treatment as survival endpoints.

RESULTS: An infection-free survival of 97.0% (63/65) was achieved at final follow-up. Only 2 patients (3.1%) developed recurrent infection, managed with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) (n = 1) or repeat 2-stage revision (n = 1). Overall, implant survivorship was 87.6% (57/65). The remaining reoperations were attributable to mechanical failures, including aseptic loosening (n = 3, 4.6%), recurrent dislocation (n = 1, 1.5%), and periprosthetic fracture (n = 1, 1.5%). The mean mHHS improved significantly from 26.0 ± 11.8 preoperatively to 68.9 ± 7.4 at final follow-up (mean improvement, 42.9 ± 9.6; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: 2-stage revision THA provides excellent infection control, high implant survivorship, and significant functional improvement in patients with hip PJI. These findings reinforce its continued role as a reliable and reproducible treatment strategy, particularly in complex patients managed in real-world clinical practice.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of imaging techniques for aseptic loosening in total hip arthroplasty; a systematic review.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: As the number of total hip arthroplasties (THAs) performed worldwide increases, the burden of revision surgery rises, with aseptic loosening being a leading cause. Diagnostic imaging strategies remain suboptimal, potentially leading to unnecessary revision or undertreatment. This systematic review aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of imaging modalities for detecting aseptic loosening in THA, using intraoperative findings as the reference standard.

METHODS: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review included a search in PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library. Eligible studies included adult patients with suspected aseptic loosening of THA, comparing at least one imaging modality to the intraoperative finding. Risk of bias was assessed using the QUADAS-2 tool. Diagnostic performance metrics were extracted or calculated.

RESULTS: The search and selection yielded 11 articles. Imaging modalities included plain radiography, CT-scans, SPECT/CT, FDG-PET, bone scintigraphy, arthrography, and MRI. Risk of bias was high in all studies, primarily related to patient selection and applicability of the reference standard. The overall certainty of evidence ranged from low to moderate. Dual-energy CT and inducible motion CT showed the highest reported diagnostic performance, based on single-centre studies.

CONCLUSIONS: All included studies demonstrated a high risk of bias, and surgeons were not blinded at the time of revision surgery. As a result, no reliable diagnostic strategy can currently be recommended. The favorable findings for CT-based techniques are hypothesis-generating. Methodologically robust, double-blinded studies are required to determine the true accuracy of advanced imaging techniques.PROSPERO registration number:CRD42024584480.

articles.title: Long-Term Cardiovascular Adverse Events in Patients with Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: patients with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are at risk for cardiotoxicity. Risk estimates from clinical trials may be limited by healthier populations and short follow-up durations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: we evaluated the incidence of cardiovascular adverse events (CVD-AE) and echocardiographic changes as a secondary outcome in CML patients on TKIs, accounting for cardiovascular risk from prior TKI exposure. CML patients treated with TKIs at Cleveland Clinic (2007-2022) were included. TKIs analyzed were imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, and asciminib. Data included demographics, comorbidities, treatments, and follow-up. Outcomes were overall survival and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): acute coronary syndrome (ACS), heart failure, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, and revascularization. Pleural effusions, pericardial effusions and pulmonary hypertension were assessed. Echocardiograms were collected at baseline. Multivariable Cox regression and generalized linear mixed models were applied.

RESULTS: among 357 patients (median age 56; 57% male; 85% White), 518 CVD-AE occurred during median follow-up of 7.2 years. Compared with imatinib, nilotinib was associated with increased ACS (HR 3.5, P = 0.02), dasatinib with heart failure (HR 2.5, P = 0.04), and dasatinib, and asciminib with pleural (HRs 3.5, 5.8; P < 0.05) and pericardial effusions (HR 5.1, 21.6; P < 0.05). Dasatinib was associated with lower venous thrombosis (HR 0.1, P = 0.02). MACE incidence did not differ significantly among TKIs. Among 69 patients with serial echocardiograms, ponatinib decreased left ventricular ejection fraction (β = -5.2, P = 0.008) and bosutinib increased global longitudinal strain (β = 3.0, P = 0.037).

CONCLUSION: Cardiovascular risks differ among TKIs, and therapy duration influences echocardiographic changes.

articles.title: Feasibility and factors associated with successful back transfer after maternal transfer for postpartum hemorrhage: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) requires multidisciplinary management at tertiary care centers. Back transfer after clinical stabilization is an important component of regional perinatal care, but the clinical characteristics associated with back transfer decisions remain poorly understood. This study examined the rate of back transfer and the factors associated with actual back transfer decisions among women transferred for PPH.

METHODS: A retrospective single-center cohort study was conducted among postpartum women transferred to the Kyoto University Hospital for established or impending PPH between April 2013 and September 2025. The primary outcome was the rate of back transfer, and associated clinical factors were assessed using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 163 eligible women, 92 (56.4%) underwent successful back transfer. A higher shock index at admission was negatively associated with successful back transfer (odds ratio, OR = 0.12; 95% confidence interval, 95% CI = 0.02-0.46; P = 0.005). Compared with tone, trauma (OR = 0.10, 95% CI = 0.03-0.28, P < 0.001) and tissue (OR = 0.26, 95% CI = 0.09-0.74, P = 0.013) were negatively associated with successful back transfer. A higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration was positively associated with successful back transfer (OR = 1.32, 95% CI = 1.02-1.74, P = 0.041).

CONCLUSION: More than half of the women in this selected cohort underwent back transfer after maternal transfer for PPH. Lower shock index at admission, hemorrhage caused by uterine atony, and higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration were associated with back transfer. These exploratory findings may inform future efforts to develop standardized back transfer criteria.

articles.title: Speckle-tracking echocardiographic strain parameters in cardiac magnetic resonance-confirmed myocarditis: associations with myocardial edema and subsequent left ventricular functional improvement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the noninvasive reference standard for diagnosing myocarditis and assessing myocardial inflammation, but its routine use may be limited by availability, cost, and patient-related factors. Speckle-tracking echocardiography may provide an accessible approach to evaluating myocardial dysfunction and outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of global longitudinal strain (GLS), peak atrial longitudinal strain (PALS), and time-to-peak longitudinal strain (TPLS) with CMR-defined myocardial edema, biomarkers, and subsequent left ventricular (LV) functional improvement in patients with CMR-confirmed myocarditis.

METHODS: This single-center ambispective observational cohort study included 40 adults with CMR-confirmed myocarditis and baseline echocardiography suitable for strain analysis. Cross-sectional associations between baseline strain parameters, CMR findings, and biomarkers were assessed, with longitudinal evaluation of subsequent LV functional improvement among patients with follow-up echocardiography. Receiver operating characteristic and regression analyses were exploratory; data-derived thresholds were not internally or externally validated.

RESULTS: Among 40 patients with CMR-confirmed myocarditis, TPLS ≥ 447 ms showed 52.4% sensitivity and 86.7% specificity for CMR-defined myocardial edema (area under the curve [AUC], 0.58). The combined GLS-TPLS model showed 81.0% sensitivity, 53.3% specificity, 69.4% accuracy, and an AUC of 0.64. GLS and PALS correlated inversely with peak N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP; r = -0.438, P = 0.006 and r = -0.396, P = 0.017, respectively). Thirty-five patients had evaluable longitudinal LV ejection fraction (LVEF) measurements; 11 (31.4%) met criteria for LV functional improvement. Baseline GLS was associated with subsequent LV functional improvement, although interpretation is limited by its strong relationship with baseline LVEF.

CONCLUSIONS: In CMR-confirmed myocarditis, strain parameters provided complementary functional information across imaging, biomarker, and longitudinal domains. TPLS was associated with CMR-defined myocardial edema, while GLS and PALS were associated with NT-proBNP. Baseline GLS was associated with subsequent LV functional improvement. These exploratory findings support prospective evaluation of strain alongside CMR and development of multimodal risk stratification models in larger, controlled cohorts.

articles.title: Circulating biomarkers in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma for risk stratification, diagnosis and prognosis.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

articles.title: High early burden of post-stroke spasticity and persistent treatment gaps in structured follow-up care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke spasticity (PSS) is a frequent and disabling complication after stroke. Real-world data on the implementation of guideline-recommended antispastic treatment within structured follow-up programs are limited.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, patients with persistent motor deficits after stroke were followed within a structured post-stroke care program. Spasticity was assessed using the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) at predefined follow-up intervals (3 and 12 months after stroke onset). Clinically relevant spasticity was defined as MAS ≥ 2 in at least one joint. Antispastic treatments, including botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A), were recorded. The implementation gap for BoNT-A was defined as the proportion of patients with a treatment recommendation who had not initiated therapy.

RESULTS: Using a cumulative 12-month MAS-based definition among patients with persistent paresis and available follow-up assessments, clinically relevant spasticity was observed in 40/55 patients (72.7%, 95% CI 59-83.9), while 51/55 patients (92.7%, 95% CI 82.4-97.9) showed any increase in muscle tone (MAS > 0). Clinically relevant spasticity was present in 34/53 patients at 3 months (64.2%, 95% CI 49.8-76.9) and in 26/46 patients at 12 months (56.5%, 95% CI 41.1-71.1). Among patients with clinically relevant spasticity, BoNT-A treatment was recommended in 11.8% at 3 months and 26.9% at 12 months, while no patient with a documented recommendation had initiated therapy.

CONCLUSIONS: PSS occurs early and affects a substantial proportion of patients with persistent motor deficits after stroke. Despite structured follow-up and systematic screening, implementation of guideline-recommended BoNT-A therapy remained absent in patients with documented treatment recommendations, indicating substantial barriers to evidence-based outpatient spasticity care.

articles.title: Prehospital antibiotics in septic shock of digestive origin: target-trial alignment, effect modification, and source-control interpretation.
articles.abstract: Jouffroy et al. reported lower 30-day mortality associated with prehospital antibiotics and suggested that the association varied by presumed septic shock origin. However, treatment assignment and covariate timing require clarification; formal treatment-by-origin interaction testing was not reported; and several effect measures and subgroup counts are inconsistent. Resolving these issues is central to interpreting the findings. Confirmed digestive diagnoses, antimicrobial appropriateness, and source-control timing were not described in the published report. These factors warrant future investigation, whereas current evidence does not establish that infection origin modifies the treatment effect.

articles.title: When elimination leaves patients behind: clinical, serologic and molecular evidence of a human African trypanosomiasis case highlighting diagnostic, surveillance and treatment gaps in Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite substantial progress toward elimination, human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) remains vulnerable to under-recognition in low-surveillance settings. Nigeria, historically endemic for HAT, has reported very few recent cases, which raises questions about whether declining incidence reflects true interruption of transmission or limitations in surveillance and diagnostic systems. Here, we report a case that illustrates the unique challenges of case detection and surveillance, confirmation and treatment in Nigeria, which resulted in poor patient outcomes and ongoing transmission that may hinder sustainable HAT elimination.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 17-year-old male from Imo State, Nigeria, first developed recurrent seizures in 2020 at the age of 12 and received treatment for epilepsy for approximately 4 years before progressive neurological deterioration prompted further investigations for HAT. Serological and molecular testing supported infection with Trypanosoma brucei, and cerebrospinal fluid findings were consistent with second-stage HAT. Tested family members also showed positive serological and molecular results, suggesting possible undetected transmission within the household. Despite the cumulative clinical, serologic and molecular evidence, treatment was not initiated owing to prevailing operational practices in the country. Patient's symptoms remain unabated with continued anti-epilepsy treatment and no access to HAT medications.

CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates how prolonged clinical misdiagnosis, gaps in surveillance, and barriers to accessing treatment can delay recognition and management of HAT in low-prevalence settings, especially in the absence of parasitological confirmation. It also highlights broader challenges facing elimination programmes, illustrating how the gap between international diagnostic/treatment guidelines and operational practice affects patient care. The detection of infection markers among family members further raises concern about under-recognized transmissions in Nigeria. Strengthening clinician awareness, enhancing surveillance systems, conducting family-based case investigations, and ensuring timely access to adequate diagnosis and treatment will be essential for achieving equitable HAT elimination.

articles.title: Dual-targeting BCMA/CD19 CAR T cells with asymmetric 4-1BB/CD28-YMFM costimulation in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma: a phase 1/2 trial with single-cell profiling of extramedullary disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extramedullary disease (EMD) predicts poor outcomes after B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM). KQ-2003 is a bicistronic BCMA/CD19 CAR T-cell product incorporating 4-1BB and CD28-YMFM costimulatory domains. We assessed its activity and intralesional biology, focusing on EMD.

METHODS: Twenty-four patients received KQ-2003 (21 trial participants; three compassionate-use patients). Hematologic and EMD responses were assessed using International Myeloma Working Group (IMWG) and Italian Myeloma criteria for PET Use, respectively. Bone marrow minimal residual disease (MRD) was assessed by next-generation flow cytometry (10- 5 sensitivity). Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox methods. Longitudinal single-cell RNA sequencing profiled one patient's infusion product, serial blood, and spatially distinct EMD biopsies.

RESULTS: Patients had received a median of five prior lines; 18 (75.0%) were triple-class refractory, six (25.0%) penta-refractory, 23 (95.8%) had high-risk cytogenetics, and 15 (62.5%) had EMD. All 20 patients with measurable hematologic disease achieved hematologic responses (18 [90.0%] complete/stringent complete); IMWG-defined overall response rate was 95.0%. Fourteen (93.3%) of 15 EMD patients achieved metabolic responses (13 [86.7%] complete). Among 19 baseline MRD-positive patients, 12 (63.2%) became MRD-negative by month 6; 10 and six also had documented negativity at months 12 and 24, respectively. At 29.2 months' median follow-up, median PFS was 24.0 months (95% CI, 15.0-not reached); no significant difference was detected by baseline EMD status (HR, 0.92; P = 0.89). Among the 21 trial participants, grade ≥ 3 cytokine release syndrome and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome occurred in one (4.8%) and two (9.5%), respectively; two treatment-related fatal pneumonias occurred. Single-patient longitudinal profiling revealed proliferating lesion-infiltrating CAR T cells with increased CCL3/CCL4 expression and tumor-cell apoptotic and necroptotic transcriptional programs. Trajectory analysis suggested transcriptional links between tissue effectors and circulating CCL5-positive memory-like CAR T cells. CellChat predicted BCMA-related tumor-microenvironment interactions and immune-cell interactions involving circulating CAR T cells.

CONCLUSIONS: KQ-2003 produced deep, durable hematologic and metabolic responses in heavily pretreated, high-risk RRMM, including EMD. Intralesional profiling identified CAR T-cell proliferation, tumor-cell death-associated programs, and candidate microenvironmental interactions. These findings warrant further evaluation of this dual-targeting strategy in EMD.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04714827; registered 19 January 2021.

articles.title: The efficacy of adding leg wrapping to prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of post-spinal hypotension in elective cesarean section: a prospective double-blinded randomized clinical trial.
articles.journal: Journal of anesthesia, analgesia and critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Various pharmacological and non-pharmacological methods have been studied in the literature to reduce the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of adding bilateral lower-limb wrapping to a prophylactic norepinephrine infusion in reducing the incidence of hypotension in parturients receiving intrathecal anesthesia for cesarean delivery.

METHODS: This prospective randomized trial included parturients undergoing elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Parturients were divided into the following: norepinephrine group (N) (n = 84), and norepinephrine and leg wrapping group (NW) (n = 84). The 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion continued until 5 min after fetal delivery. The primary outcome was the incidence of post-spinal maternal hypotension. Secondary outcomes included the incidence of maternal severe hypotension, bradycardia, tachycardia, hypertension, nausea, vomiting, post-delivery hypotension, and neonatal outcomes.

RESULTS: The final analysis included 168 patients. The incidence of hypotension in the NW group was lower than in the N group (7/84 [8.3%], 18/84 [21.4%], respectively) with P = 0.017, RR = 0.39, and CI: (0.17-0.88). According to the Kaplan-Meier curve with the log-rank test, the time to post-spinal maternal hypotension differed significantly (P = 0.016), with a restricted mean time of 21.1 min in the NW group and 19.7 min in the N group (hazard ratio = 2.82 for the N group vs. NW, 95%CI: (1.18-6.76). Furthermore, a repeated-measures analysis revealed significant group-by-time interactions for both heart rate (P = 0.003) and systolic blood pressure (P = 0.028), demonstrating superior longitudinal hemodynamic stability in the NW group. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected for secondary maternal and neonatal outcomes.

CONCLUSION: When added to a prophylactic 0.05 µg/kg/min norepinephrine infusion, leg wrapping decreased the incidence of postspinal maternal hypotension and enhanced hemodynamic stability over time during elective cesarean delivery.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06496061; principal investigator: Mohamed Ahmed Hamed; date of registration: 11/07/2024; no protocol amendments or study changes after trial start).

articles.title: Early prediction of ICU-acquired weakness with quadriceps ultrasound: outcome verification, prediction timing, and transportability.
articles.abstract: Zou et al. developed and temporally validated a prospective multicentre model combining quadriceps ultrasound and clinical variables to predict intensive care unit-acquired weakness. We focus on its intended clinical use: outcome verification depends on patients later becoming assessable by volitional strength testing, whereas some predictors are collected throughout the first 24 h. The later cohort appropriately evaluates performance across time within the participating centre network. Clarifying the verification population, prediction landmark, threshold selection, and imputation pipeline would support reproducible use; subsequent evaluation in independent hospitals would address geographic transportability.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of a modular intervention to support self-management in cardiovascular prevention: a health economic evaluation of the DECADE cluster-randomized trial.
articles.journal: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of two modular components of the DECADE intervention, structured patient-centered follow-up consultations ('Consultations') and patient materials for tailored use ('Materials'), for cardiovascular disease (CVD) prevention in German primary care.

METHODS: The health economic evaluation was conducted alongside a 2 × 2 factorial cluster-randomized trial in German general practices. Patients aged 30-75 years with at least one lifestyle-related CVD risk factor were included. The cost-effectiveness of 'Consultations' was assessed by comparing groups that received structured follow-up consultations with those that did not. The cost-effectiveness of 'Materials' was assessed by comparing groups that received patient materials with those that did not. Incremental costs were combined with effects on the patient-reported Patient Activation Measure (PAM13) and the calculated 10-year cardiovascular risk (CVR) score. Incremental Cost-Effectiveness Ratios (ICERs) were calculated, and statistical uncertainty was assessed using non-parametric bootstrapping and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves.

RESULTS: The 'Consultations' intervention showed a slight, significant improvement in the PAM13 score at 6 months of 1.14 points (95% CI 0.09 to 2.19, p = 0.033). The corresponding ICER was €89.48 (95% CI €46.42 to €1,105.30) per one-point PAM13 improvement. The 'Consultations' intervention did not affect the CVR score (p = 0.72). The 'Materials' intervention was associated with a noninformative result regarding the PAM13 score (p = 0.57), but was associated with a difference of - 1.63% points in the 10-year cardiovascular risk score relative to no materials, which was not statistically significant (95% CI - 3.28 to 0.02, p = 0.053). This difference reflects a stable risk score in the arms using materials (IG1 + 0.09, IG3 - 0.17) against a rising score in the arms without them (control group + 1.16, IG2 + 2.01) rather than an absolute reduction in risk. Based on an incremental cost of €15.03, the resulting ratio was €9.23 per percentage point of 10-year cardiovascular risk avoided (not statistically significant).

CONCLUSIONS: Structured, patient-centered follow-up consultations slightly increased patient activation at moderate additional cost; as no willingness-to-pay threshold exists for this outcome, cost-effectiveness cannot be established. The low-cost patient materials did not improve patient activation; the calculated 10-year cardiovascular risk remained stable in the arms using them while it rose in the arms without them, but this difference is statistically uncertain. The modular design allows flexible implementation, and further evaluation with long-term and preference-based outcomes is needed.

articles.title: Usability of an artificial intelligence enabled Participation and Environment Measure prototype for family-centered goal setting support in pediatric rehabilitation.
articles.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family-centered care coordination (FC-CC) in pediatric rehabilitation benefits from tools that support caregivers in contributing to personalized service planning for their children. Participation and Environment Measure (PEM) is a digital application that is being further developed to support FC-CC in early intervention (EI). PEM is being further developed to include the Young Children's Participation and Environment Measure (YC-PEM) electronic patient-reported outcome and a companion PEM-Plus (PEM+) goal setting intervention. This study examined usability of the first artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled PEM prototype.

METHODS: Caregivers from an urban EI program met these eligibility criteria: (1) were at least 18 years old; (2) identified as the parent or legal guardian of a child enrolled in EI services; (3) read, wrote, and spoke English; (4) had internet and telephone access; and (5) had a child 0-3 years old who received EI services for 3 or more months. Participants completed the AI-enabled PEM application with access to a debiased prototypic conversational agent. PEM usability was assessed using the System Usability Scale (SUS), and chatbot usability was assessed along four BOT Usability Scale (BUS-11) domains: 1) accessibility of chatbot functions; 2) functional interactive conversation; 3) privacy and security; and 4) timely response. Univariate logistic regression models were used to examine associations between each of the four BUS-11 domains and PEM+ engagement.

RESULTS: Eleven female caregivers of children (mean age: 24.5 months) enrolled, 66.7% of whom interacted with the prototypic chatbot during one or more iterations of the PEM+ intervention. Overall PEM usability remained acceptable. While overall chatbot usability was very poor (Mdn = 53.4%, IQR = 50.0, 55.4), caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability were average for accessibility of chatbot functions (Mdn = 3.8, IQR = 3.0, 4.0) and good for privacy and security (M = 3.1, Range = 2.0-5.0). Higher caregiver perceptions of chatbot usability did not significantly increase odds of PEM+ intervention use.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings indicate that an AI-enabled PEM retains adequate usability. A chatbot integrated within the PEM+ intervention is accessible and secure, though its functional interactive conversation and timely responses could benefit from further development to increase odds of its use in an EI service context.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT06458959 (Registration date: 2024-06-14).

articles.title: Breastfeeding interventions for low-birth weight and very low birth weight infants in South Asia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate interventions promoting breastfeeding practices among Low Birth Weight (LBW) and Very Low Birth Weight (VLBW) infants in South Asia.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in five databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINHAL, and the Cochrane library). Evidence was synthesized to estimate the duration to establish breastfeeding practices among LBW and VLBW infants. Meta-analysis was performed to estimate the effect size on breastfeeding practices using random effect model. Heterogeneity was explored by sub-group and meta-regression analyses. Risk of bias and strength of evidence was assessed by the RoB2, ROBINS-I and NIH Quality Assessment tools considering the study design of the selected articles.

RESULTS: From a pool of 2,524 records screened, 16 studies met the inclusion criteria. The systematic review revealed that various interventions aimed at improving breastfeeding practices among LBW infants largely resulted in positive breastfeeding outcomes such as initiation of breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding. The Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) care was intervened in most cases together with other interventions, including Non-nutritive suckling, Premature Infant Oromotor Intervention, Nutrition Education and Mother Baby Friendly Initiatives Plus. Meta-analysis showed mothers who received KMC demonstrated an earlier initiation of breastfeeding (pooled SMD: -1.08, 95% CI: -2.15, to -0.01) as compared to mothers who received conventional care. However, these estimates should be interpreted with caution due to high heterogeneity and significant publication bias.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence from India and Bangladesh suggests that KMC and other breastfeeding-support interventions may improve selected breastfeeding outcomes among LBW and VLBW infants. However, heterogeneity, risk-of-bias concerns, and limited evidence for individual outcomes restrict confidence in these findings.

articles.title: The Mylk3 variant associated with loss of full-length MLCK3 is widespread in C57BL/6N and related NIH-derived mouse substrains.
articles.abstract: Genetic variation among C57BL/6 mouse strains may influence cardiovascular phenotypes and contribute to inter-study variability in biomedical research. We investigated the distribution of the Mylk3 c.-5T>A variant, previously shown to cause loss of cardiac myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK3) and late-onset dilated cardiomyopathy, across C57BL/6 lineages. The variant was homozygously present in C57BL/6N and C57BL/6By strains but absent from C57BL/6J-derived mouse strains. This distribution indicates that the variant was established before divergence of the C57BL/6By branch, although its precise origin cannot be determined from contemporary samples. Despite preserved Mylk3 transcript abundance, C57BL/6N hearts lacked full-length MLCK3 protein. These findings exemplify how genetic differences between seemingly identical wild-type backgrounds can introduce significant confounding factors, highlighting the importance of accurate substrain identification and reporting for experimental design, interpretation, and reproducibility. Highlighting the broader relevance of these findings, a survey of 1238 recent open-access articles from cardiovascular journals found that 35% reported the use of C57BL/6 mice without specifying the N or J substrain. Altogether, our findings identify the Mylk3 variant as a lineage-defining feature of C57BL/6N mice and related substrains, with potential implications for cardiovascular studies using this background.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Early Clinical Prediction Model for Post-Encephalitic Epilepsy in Children With Viral Encephalitis: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Post-encephalitic epilepsy (PEE) is a serious long-term sequela of pediatric viral encephalitis, yet early risk stratification tools are lacking. In this single-center retrospective cohort study of 206 children with viral encephalitis, 43 (20.87%) developed PEE during follow-up. A multivariable logistic regression model incorporating 4 early clinical predictors-acute seizure count, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) white blood cell count, consciousness disturbance, and cortical involvement-demonstrated good discrimination and acceptable calibration. Decision curve analysis showed higher net benefit than treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.06 to 0.99. Sensitivity analyses, including false-discovery rate correction, adjustment for follow-up duration, pathogen-stratified analyses, and a time-to-event (Cox) model, did not materially alter the principal findings. This model, built from routinely available variables, showed promise for early identification of children at elevated risk for PEE in internal validation. External validation in independent multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Absent fluorodeoxyglucose uptake in thoracic aorta and subclavian arteries as a potential indicator for visual impairment in giant cell arteritis: A hypothesis-generating study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the risk of visual impairment in giant cell arteritis (GCA) by integrating the findings of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging with clinical and laboratory parameters.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 54 patients with GCA who underwent PET/CT. We evaluated the association between visual impairment and clinical characteristics, including C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and the anatomical distribution of vascular lesions on PET/CT (e.g., proximal large-vessel [LV] uptake). Furthermore, an unsupervised hierarchical cluster analysis was performed based on FDG uptake patterns.

RESULTS: The absence of FDG uptake in the thoracic aorta and subclavian arteries (LV uptake (-)) was associated with visual impairment. In patients presenting with cranial symptoms, the combination of LV uptake (-) and low CRP levels identified a subgroup at a high risk for visual impairment (incidence: 90.0%, odds ratio: 49.1). Furthermore, the cluster analysis identified a subgroup (Cluster 1: upper and lower limb pattern) that shares the low-inflammatory characteristic of this clinical profile.

CONCLUSION: The absence of systemic large-vessel lesions on PET/CT may be associated with an increased risk of visual impairment in GCA. This clinical profile lacking systemic inflammation (LV uptake (-) and low CRP) may be clinically important to identify patients at high risk of visual impairment. Key Points • The absence of large-vessel lesions on PET/CT may be associated with an increased risk of visual impairment in GCA. • Combining cranial symptoms, low CRP, and absent large-vessel inflammation may suggest a higher ocular ischemia risk. • Excluding large-vessel vasculitis via PET/CT assists in stratifying these high-risk patients.

articles.title: Incidence and Factors Associated with Newly Recorded Database-Defined Central Nervous System-Related Diagnoses During and Shortly After Metronidazole Therapy: A Large-Scale Japanese Hospital-Based Administrative Claims Database Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Metronidazole (MNZ) is widely used to treat anaerobic and protozoal infections. However, evidence regarding the factors associated with newly recorded, database-defined central nervous system (CNS)-related diagnoses during or shortly after MNZ therapy remains limited. This study evaluated the incidence of newly recorded, database-defined CNS-related diagnoses during and shortly after MNZ therapy and identified the associated factors using a Japanese hospital-based administrative claims database.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the JMDC hospital-based administrative claims database from April 2014 to August 2022. Adults prescribed oral or injectable MNZ were included. The primary outcome was a newly recorded, database-defined CNS-related diagnosis during the risk period after MNZ initiation. Prespecified factors were evaluated using conventional and Firth-penalized Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: Among 58,195 patients, 59 (0.1%) had a newly recorded, database-defined CNS-related diagnosis, including 52 coded as R26.8 (unsteadiness on the feet). Age ≥ 60 years (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 4.18; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.70-10.30), female sex (adjusted HR 1.96; 95% CI 1.16-3.31), and renal failure (adjusted HR 1.93; 95% CI 1.08-3.47) were significantly associated with the outcome. In contrast, liver disease and initial daily MNZ dose > 1500 mg/day showed no significant associations.

CONCLUSIONS: This study estimated the incidence of newly recorded, database-defined CNS-related diagnoses during and shortly after MNZ therapy and identified age ≥ 60 years, female sex, and renal failure as associated factors in the primary Cox regression analysis. Age ≥ 60 years showed the most consistent association across the sensitivity analyses, whereas the associations with female sex and renal failure were less precise in some analyses. However, these findings do not establish causality or a dose threshold.

articles.title: Support needs and psychosocial stress among LGBTQ+ cancer caregivers: implications for supportive care across the continuum.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: LGBTQ + caregivers of individuals with cancer experience heightened psychosocial stress due to minority stress, social exclusion, and discrimination in healthcare settings. Despite increasing attention to LGBTQ + health, caregiver-specific needs across the cancer care continuum remain insufficiently synthesized in relation to supportive care policy and practice. This review synthesizes empirical evidence on the experiences, challenges, and support needs of LGBTQ + cancer caregivers.

METHODS: A mixed-methods systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies published between January 2010 and June 2025 were identified through searches of 12 databases, including CINAHL, Cochrane CENTRAL, Embase, PubMed, PsycINFO, and Web of Science. Eligible studies employed qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods designs and explicitly examined LGBTQ + caregivers of individuals with cancer.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies met inclusion criteria. Caregivers reported high levels of psychological distress, minority stress, medical mistrust, and fears of discrimination. Structural challenges included financial hardship, limited legal recognition, and lack of tailored resources. Dyadic and chosen family relationships shaped caregiving dynamics, while social support networks provided partial buffering effects. Intersectional inequities (e.g., race, gender identity, and income) compounded caregiving burdens, with implications for supportive care access and delivery. Few studies examined bereavement in depth, highlighting a critical gap.

CONCLUSION: LGBTQ + cancer caregivers face psychosocial and structural challenges, demanding equity-focused interventions. Findings underscore the need for affirming communication, inclusive caregiving policies, and culturally responsive supportive care, particularly during palliative and end-of-life care and bereavement. Future research should prioritize intersectionality, caregiver mental health, and legal recognition to advance supportive care practice and policy.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity and functional disability in middle-aged and older adults: a harmonized multicohort study.
articles.abstract: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is highly prevalent in aging populations, yet its association and underlying mechanisms with functional disability (FD) remain insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate CMM-FD relationship, quantify the influencing mechanisms, and explore heterogeneity across different CMM patterns and population subgroups. A multicohort study was conducted by pooling harmonized longitudinal data from three international aging cohorts. CMM was defined as the co-occurrence of at least two cardiometabolic diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, heart diseases, and stroke. FD was measured through difficulty performing basic or instrumental activities of daily living. Logistic regression models were used to estimate associations and heterogeneities, and Kohler-Holm-Breen decomposition was used to quantify mediating contributions. CMM prevalence was 22.53%, and FD prevalence was 23.01%. CMM was strongly associated with higher odds of FD (OR = 2.940; p < 0.001), with consistent findings across all countries and FD subtypes. Respiratory, neuropsychiatric, and sensory conditions jointly explained 20.44% of the association, with psychological problems contributing the largest share. CMM patterns involving stroke generally showed high odds of FD, while the four-disease combination had the largest overall point estimate. Middle-aged, male, married, childless, non-retired, and smoking older adults exhibited a stronger CMM-associated elevation in odds of FD. Early identification of high-risk CMM patterns, routine screening for functional and psychological, cognitive, respiratory, and sensory symptoms, and targeted follow-up for individuals with stroke-containing or complex CMM patterns may reduce the risk of functional deterioration and support independent living in aging populations.

articles.title: Harnessing the Antibacterial Potential of Star Fruit Extract against MRSA: Metabolic Profiling, Molecular Docking, and In Vitro Wound-Healing Effects.
articles.journal: Plant foods for human nutrition (Dordrecht, Netherlands)
articles.abstract: Averrhoa carambola L. (star fruit) is recognized for its nutritional value and bioactive constituents. This study investigated its antibacterial and antibiofilm activities against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and its potential to promote wound healing. The in vitro antibacterial activity of the extract was evaluated against six MRSA strains by determining the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), and time-kill kinetics. The extract exhibited a uniform MIC of 1.95 mg/mL against all tested MRSA strains, while MBC values ranged from 15.6 to 125 mg/mL. Biofilm inhibition was assessed using a crystal violet assay, while transmission electron microscopy and intracellular ion leakage analysis were used to investigate the antibacterial mechanism. The extract significantly inhibited biofilm formation at 0.5 × and 0.25 × MIC, particularly against MS3 and MS15 strains (p ≤ 0.05). The extract induced membrane damage and significant leakage of intracellular phosphate (p = 0.0036) and potassium (p = 0.0001). Its cytocompatibility and wound-healing activity were evaluated using primary human adult dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) and an in vitro scratch assay. The extract showed an EC50 of 2.96 mg/mL without reducing HDFa viability and significantly enhanced wound closure to 70%, compared with 82% for dexamethasone. UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS profiling identified 130 metabolites, with flavonoids representing the predominant class (49 compounds). Molecular docking further predicted favorable binding interactions between selected flavonoids and collagenase, elastase, and lipase. These findings demonstrate the antibacterial, antibiofilm, and in vitro wound-healing potential of star fruit extract against MRSA.

articles.title: Association of Spiritual Caregiving and Clinical Reasoning Competency with Nursing Care Quality Among Intensive Care Nurses in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to examine the associations of intensive care nurses' spiritual caregiving and clinical reasoning competency with nursing care quality. This descriptive study included 520 intensive care nurses in Türkiye. Data were collected between July 2025 and September 2025 using the Descriptive Characteristics Form, the Spiritual Care-Giving Scale (SCGS), the Clinical Reasoning Competency Scale for Nurses (CRCSN), and the Quality Nursing Care Scale (QNCS). Data collection was performed online via Google Forms, using the convenience sampling method. The mean age of the participants was 29.68 ± 5.72 years, and 82.5% were female. Male nurses, high school graduates, nurses working in private or university hospitals, those with ≥ 4 years of ICU experience, and those caring for ≥ 3 patients daily had higher scores in the respective scales (p < 0.05). According to multiple linear regression analysis, SCGS and CRCSN scores predicted 37.4% of the variance in QNCS scores (R2 = 0.374). A one-unit increase in the SCGS score and the CRCSN score increased the QNCS score by 0.160 points and 0.697 points, respectively (p < 0.01; p < 0.001). Intensive care nurses' competencies in spiritual care and clinical reasoning significantly predicted the quality of nursing care services. The findings indicate a positive correlation between spiritual care, clinical reasoning skills, and improved care quality, thereby justifying further longitudinal studies and randomized controlled trials to determine the causal relationship between these constructs.

articles.title: Association between COPD and functional disability in adults with a history of cancer: a cross-sectional analysis of ELSI-Brazil.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To explore associations between chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and functional disability across mobility, instrumental activities of daily living (IADL), and basic activities of daily living (BADL) among Brazilian adults with a history of cancer.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from ELSI-Brazil. Participants aged 50 years and older with a self-reported history of cancer were classified according to self-reported physician-diagnosed COPD status. Functional disability was assessed across three domains: mobility, IADL, and BADL. Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs). Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg corrections were applied only to the unadjusted outcome-specific tests. Sensitivity analyses included Firth's penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 504 participants with a history of cancer, 502 had available information on COPD status, of whom 42 (8.4%) reported COPD. In unadjusted analyses, COPD was nominally associated with higher odds of difficulty running 1 km (OR = 4.57; 95%CI: 1.08-19.28) and walking 1 km (OR = 2.31; 95%CI: 1.21-4.42). After adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, and the number of other comorbidities, the corresponding ORs were 4.77 (95%CI: 1.12-20.39) and 2.47 (95%CI: 1.25-4.88), respectively. Neither unadjusted association remained statistically significant after multiplicity correction. The multivariable and Firth analyses were not corrected for multiple testing. No nominally significant associations were observed for IADL or BADL.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, self-reported COPD showed nominal associations with greater difficulty performing selected mobility activities among adults with a history of cancer. These findings were not robust to correction for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously.

articles.title: Perioperative Systemic Therapies for Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: An Updated Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary perioperative systemic therapies have improved outcomes in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), but comparative evidence between novel strategies is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To explore the comparative efficacy and safety of systemic treatment strategies initiated before radical cystectomy.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched on 7 March 2026 for phase III randomized trials. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis evaluated overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), and adverse events (AEs). Potential effect modifiers were compared across trials, and sensitivity analyses restricted the network to contemporary gemcitabine/cisplatin (GC)-controlled trials. Evidence certainty was assessed using Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA).

PROSPERO: CRD420261277299.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs were included. Compared with GC, enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab (EVP) and durvalumab + GC were associated with improved OS (hazard ratio [HR] 0.65; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.89; and HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.60-0.94, respectively) and EFS (HR 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.69; and HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.56-0.82, respectively). GC-referenced survival estimates were unchanged in sensitivity analyses. EVP had the highest survival P-scores, but rankings did not establish clinical superiority.
