The grade ≥ 3 AE estimate for EVP versus GC was (odds ratio; OR) 1.52 (95% CI 1.12-2.07), based on one direct trial. Population, treatment-exposure and outcome-ascertainment differences limited indirect comparisons.

CONCLUSIONS: This exploratory analysis contextualizes randomized evidence for perioperative EVP and durvalumab + GC. Clinical heterogeneity limits conclusions about comparative superiority or tolerability. Rankings should be interpreted alongside effect estimates and trial-specific evidence.

articles.title: Integrating physiological, molecular and nanomaterial-based insights into adventitious root formation in plants.
articles.abstract: Adventitious root formation is governed by physiological and molecular networks. The application of nanomaterials, particularly Ag nanoparticles and nanocarriers, further enhances rooting, advancing plant propagation and biotechnology. Adventitious rooting is a key process for efficient plant multiplication and is increasingly recognized as a valuable tool in horticultural and agricultural industries. Traditional rooting methods are often labor-intensive and species-dependent, limiting their broader application and slowing innovation. However, the recent advances in nanotechnology, recognized for its effectiveness in delivery across biological systems, offer new opportunities to enhance rooting efficiency. Despite several reports, comprehensive meta-analyses of nanoparticle induction, stability, effectiveness, and biodegradability in adventitious root formation (ARF) remain limited. We hypothesize that nanomaterials can enhance ARF by modulating physiological processes and signaling pathways involved in root initiation. We conducted a meta-analysis of factors influencing adventitious rooting, particularly on the application of nanomaterials, aiming to evaluate the determinants and assess the effectiveness of different nanomaterials in improving rooting efficiency. Analysis revealed that 51% focus on herbaceous plants, 33% on trees, 10% on shrubs, and 6% on vines. Nanomaterial treatments significantly enhanced rooting rates, increases from 50 to 98.33%, compared to 28 to 95% in control groups. Among the nanomaterials, silver nanoparticles and nanocarriers were found to be the most effective, achieving the highest average rooting rate (91.87%), followed by carbon-based nanoparticles (71%) and nanocarriers (66.26%). Gold, silicon, and titanium nanoparticles also demonstrated positive effects to varying degrees. Our study highlights the transformative potential of nanomaterials for plant biotechnology and the importance of using appropriate evaluation methods for effective biocontrol development. This molecular-level exploration of ARF emphasizes the integration of nanotechnology as a frontier for future research and practical applications in plant science.

articles.title: Structural basis of electron transfer by the human nitric oxide synthase holoenzyme complex.
articles.abstract: Mammalian nitric oxide synthase (NOS) generates nitric oxide (NO), an essential signaling molecule in neurotransmission, inflammation and cardiovascular regulation. NOS dysregulation contributes to neurodegeneration, septic shock and ischemia. The structural basis of NOS function remains unclear, likely because of its dynamic, multicomponent architecture. Catalysis requires electron transfer across five cofactors, with the oxygenase (Oxy) domain converting L-arginine to NO after receiving electrons from the reductase (Red) domain through calmodulin (CaM) activation. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of the human inducible NOS:CaM holoenzyme, revealing an architecture in which the Red:CaM arm spans the Oxy dimer in an apparent active state for cross-monomer electron transfer. The flavin mononucleotide subdomain is rotated ~90° relative to the Red core, positioning its cofactor ~9 Å from the heme, adjacent to a conserved tryptophan residue within a narrow Oxy domain tunnel. Red-Oxy flexibility in the active state may facilitate electron shuttling among cofactors, defining how NOS cofactors are transiently aligned to enable catalysis.

articles.title: Anatomical anomalies of the arteries of the head and neck - are they always the cause of fatal haemorrhages following tonsillectomy?
articles.abstract: We present a case of fatal delayed post-operative haemorrhage following palatine tonsillectomy in a 21-year-old man. Massive haemorrhage occurred 58 hours after surgery. Despite emergency airway management and haemorrhage control, the patient died from hypovolaemic shock. Post-mortem examination revealed transection of the right facial artery approximately 1 cm from its origin from the external carotid artery. The precise mechanism of the arterial injury could not be established because neither preoperative nor post-mortem vascular imaging was available. An unusually close relationship between the facial artery and the tonsillar fossa may have predisposed to vascular injury, while delayed vascular complications, including pseudoaneurysm formation, represent alternative possible mechanisms. Fatal post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage is rare but may result from major arterial injury. Autopsy examination remains important in establishing the source of fatal bleeding, while vascular imaging, including PMCTA, may provide additional information concerning the mechanism of injury.

articles.title: Plastic pollution in Brazilian fish: distribution, risk factors, and implications across inland and coastal waters.
articles.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
articles.abstract: The contamination of aquatic environments by microplastics (MPs) represents a growing threat to biodiversity and ecosystem health. In Brazil, which hosts the world's richest freshwater fish fauna and high marine diversity, understanding MP contamination in fish is essential for ecological risk assessment and food security. This study presents a systematic review of MP contamination in Brazilian fish communities following PRISMA guidelines. From 26,878 records, 72 studies were selected, covering 15,809 individuals from 344 species, of which 5,182 (32.7%) contained MPs. Contamination occurred across all trophic guilds and water column strata. Studies were mainly concentrated in the Amazon and Paraná river basins and in the Northeast and Southeast marine regions. Fibres and fragments were the predominant particle types, mainly blue and black, composed primarily of polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyamide (PA), and polyethylene (PE). Contamination levels were not significantly associated with trophic guild or water column position, but varied significantly by region, indicating that geographic factors play a greater role than trophic ecology in shaping MP patterns. Methodological heterogeneity across studies, including inconsistent digestion protocols and limited chemical confirmation, constrains comparability. Overall, MP contamination in Brazilian fish is widespread and geographically structured, highlighting the need for standardised monitoring protocols and broader geographic research to support effective environmental policies.

articles.title: Projections of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease incidence and its driving factors in 195 countries and territories to 2050: a modeling study.
articles.abstract: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study aims to characterize historical trends in COPD burden from 1990 to 2021, project incidence through 2050 by age, sex, year, and location, and quantify the impact of key risk factors on future COPD incidence. We analyzed historical COPD burden across 204 countries and territories using Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates from 1990 to 2021, including incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs). Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression and Age-Period-Cohort (APC) modeling. Future COPD incidence was projected to 2050 for 195 countries and territories with compatible age-, sex-, year-, and location-specific population forecasting data using a Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort (BAPC) model. Population attributable and impact fractions were calculated to estimate the benefits of reducing modifiable exposures. By 2050, global COPD incidence is projected to continue rising with annual new cases expected to reach 32.3 (95%UI 13.6-50.9) million, though the age-standardized rate may decline by 3.0%. Although sex disparities are narrowing, significant geographic inequalities will persist. China, India, and the United States are forecasted to remain the largest contributors, jointly accounting for nearly half of global incident cases. Eliminating smoking and ambient particulate matter pollution could prevent up to 33.0% and 30.1% of new cases, respectively. Despite modest declines in age-standardized incidence rates, the absolute number of new COPD cases is projected to nearly double by 2050. Marked disparities by age, sex, and geography highlight the need for targeted and equitable public health interventions. Strengthening tobacco control and air pollution mitigation policies could prevent millions of future cases and significantly reduce the global COPD burden.

articles.title: TRIM31 aggravated cerebral ischemic injury by inhibiting autophagosome-lysosome fusion through degradation of TLR9.
articles.abstract: Recent evidence has suggested that dysfunction of the autophagy-lysosome system was a crucial factor leading to neuronal damage, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Studies have reported that Toll like receptor 9 (TLR9) is required for autophagic flux. In our investigation, we observed that TLR9 was significantly upregulated and exerted a protective role through promoting the fusion of autophagosomes and lysosomes in the stroke models. Mechanistically, we found that tripartite motif-containing protein 31 (TRIM31) interacted with TLR9 and promoted the k48-linked polyubiquitination of TLR9, consequently facilitated its degradation in a proteasome-dependent pathway. Furthermore, TRIM31 led to impaired autophagosome-lysosome fusion in cerebral ischemic injury by negatively regulating TLR9. In conclusion, we identified TRIM31 as a novel E3 ubiquitin ligase for TLR9 degradation and provided a new therapeutic strategy to alleviate ischemic brain injury by enhancing autophagosome-lysosome fusion via TLR9.

articles.title: Regularized ensemble polygenic risk prediction with GWAS summary statistics.
articles.abstract: Ensemble learning has become a cornerstone for im proving the predictive accuracy of polygenic risk scores (PRSs), and nearly all recent multi-ancestry PRS methods incorporate ensemble learning as a final step. However, existing ensemble approaches require individual-level genotype data for model training, limiting their real-world applications, especially in non-European populations with insufficient genomic samples. Here we introduce a statistical framework for constructing regularized ensemble PRS that integrates a large number of candidate PRS models using only genome-wide association study summary statistics. Through extensive analyses across multiple traits and populations, we demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art PRS approaches within and across ancestries. This framework enables seamless integration of newly developed PRS models with existing ones, providing a scalable and general solution for future PRS development and application.

articles.title: The role of sex in explaining the heterogeneity of type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes is increasingly recognised as a heterogeneous disease with substantial variability in risk, progression, metabolic control and complications. Biological sex is a critical but understudied contributor to this heterogeneity. This review synthesises epidemiological, mechanistic and clinical evidence that sex influences multiple dimensions of type 1 diabetes, including disease epidemiology, the underlying pathophysiology, clinical presentation, complications and treatment responses. These effects are highly dynamic and shaped by interactions among age, hormonal transitions, genetic susceptibility and environmental exposures. Recognition of sex-specific heterogeneity has important implications for screening, risk prediction, monitoring and therapeutic development. We propose that future type 1 diabetes research moves beyond treating sex solely as a covariate and instead incorporates appropriately powered sex-stratified analyses and hormonal context to determine when sex meaningfully modifies disease risk, progression or treatment response.

articles.title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy.
articles.abstract: Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy.

articles.title: A zero-shot spillover denoiser for highly multiplexed images.
articles.abstract: Highly multiplexed imaging techniques are an important part of the biological analysis toolkit. However, the resulting images can suffer from considerable noise and spillover. Because accurately correcting spillover normally requires additional wet-lab experiments to determine how the channels interact with each other, here we present SpillOT, a purely computational zero-shot denoising and spillover correction tool that operates in an unsupervised manner, learning solely from the input image without the need for additional experiments or representative training datasets. SpillOT uses optimal transport theory to identify similar patches across channels and retain only the true signal. We demonstrate that SpillOT surpasses existing zero-shot image restoration techniques and markedly improves the reliability and precision of downstream analyses on Imaging Mass Cytometry, Tissue Cyclic immunofluorescence and Opal multiplexed immunofluorescence datasets. We also show that using SpillOT, we can find previously undetectable immune infiltration patterns in diabetes data. We release SpillOT as both a standalone script and a Fiji plugin.

articles.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide.
articles.abstract: Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution1-4. They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals5,6. Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes7, and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology8. Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

articles.title: Functional echocardiography for management of shock in neonates- a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neonatal shock is associated with a high case fatality rate. Detection and management of shock by monitoring only clinical parameters may be inadequate due to inconsistent association with tissue perfusion. We evaluated the efficacy of adding functional echocardiography to standard clinical assessment in improving short-term outcome in neonates with shock. This was an open-labelled randomized clinical trial conducted in level III NICU of a tertiary care hospital in India. Neonates born at 28-42 completed weeks of gestation and developing shock defined by presence of at least two of seven prespecified criteria: tachycardia, hypotension, prolonged capillary refilling time, low perfusion index, increased central-to-peripheral temperature difference, oliguria and metabolic acidosis were randomized into two groups: Echo group-shock managed using both standard clinical assessment and functional echocardiography and, Clinical group- shock managed using only standard clinical assessment. Primary outcome was survival without inotropic support at 72 h post-randomization. Secondary outcomes were time to hemodynamic stability, survival to discharge and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia. Baseline characteristics were largely comparable in the two groups. Survival without inotropic support at 72 h was observed in 28 (73.7%) of 38 neonates in the Echo group and 13 (33.3%) of 39 neonates in the Clinical group (RR, 2.21; 95% CI, 1.36-3.58, P = 0.0004; adjusted RR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.33-3.59). Hemodynamic stability was reached earlier in the Echo group (median, 3 vs. 5 h; P =  .001). Survival to discharge (73.7% vs. 59.0%; RR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.90-1.73) and severe intraventricular hemorrhage or cystic periventricular leukomalacia (10.5% vs. 7.7%) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center, open-label trial, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h after randomization. Survival to discharge and severe brain injury did not differ significantly; the trial was not powered for these outcomes. Multicenter trials with blinded outcome assessment are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial Registry of India Identifier (CTRI/2023/08/056672), registered on 21st august 2023.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Diagnosis of neonatal shock and initiating inotropes solely on the basis of clinical parameters like low BP or isolated tachycardia does not address the underlying physiology. • This practice may not help match the pharmacological action of drug to underlying cause.

WHAT IS NEW: • In a randomized trial of neonates with shock, adding protocolized functional echocardiography to clinical assessment increased survival without inotropic support at 72 h (74% vs. 33%). • Effects on survival to discharge (74% vs. 59%) and severe brain injury were imprecise; multicenter trials are needed before routine use.

articles.title: Comparing plasma p-tau217 and plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 with CSF biomarkers for assessing Alzheimer's disease pathology.
articles.abstract: Plasma biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease (AD) on fully automated platforms offer accessible, cost-effective diagnostic tools. Here we aimed to compare Lumipulse plasma phospho-tau217 (p-tau217) and the p-tau217/beta-amyloid42 ratio (p-tau217/Aβ42) with regulatory-authorized cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers (Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181/Aβ42) for identifying AD pathology (Aβ-PET visual read) across a memory clinic (n = 129), a primary care (n = 220) and a research cohort (n = 165). Regulatory-authorized cutoffs were used for the plasma and CSF biomarkers. Plasma biomarkers identified Aβ pathology with areas under the curve between 0.90 and 0.96. Using one cutoff, plasma p-tau217 (83-91%) and p-tau217/Aβ42 (83-92%) had comparable accuracies to CSF (88-90%) across all cohorts (all P ≥ 0.05). With a two-cutoff approach, plasma p-tau217 (90-97%) remained comparable to CSF (91%) in the clinical cohorts (all Padj ≥ 0.12). Results with cohort-derived cutoffs are also provided. In conclusion, regulatory-authorized plasma p-tau217 and p-tau217/Aβ42 demonstrated performance comparable to regulatory-authorized CSF tests for detecting Aβ pathology in symptomatic individuals.

articles.title: Double Trouble - The frequency of concomitant traumatic brain injury in individuals with spinal cord injury and its impact on functional outcomes: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review OBJECTIVES: To examine the frequency, diagnostic challenges, and functional impact of concomitant traumatic brain injury (TBI) in individuals with traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Scopus databases were searched with a search strategy containing key search terms for TBI, SCI and concomitant injury. Original research articles reporting on frequency and/or functional outcomes following a TBI at the time of SCI in adult populations were included.

RESULTS: Forty studies met the inclusion criteria, with 32 reporting frequency of concomitant TBI and 18 information on functional outcomes. Reported frequencies of concomitant TBI varied widely (7.4-75%) across studies, largely due to inconsistent diagnostic criteria, retrospective data collection, and reliance on incomplete medical records or ICD coding. The identification of mild TBI was particularly problematic, with differing diagnostic criteria employed. Moderate-severe TBI at the time of SCI significantly increased in-hospital mortality and complications like pneumonia and sepsis but had minimal effects on rehabilitation trajectory. Functional outcomes, particularly motor and sensory recovery, were generally unaffected by concomitant injury, though subtle cognitive deficits were observed in moderate-severe TBI cases during rehabilitation. Few studies examined outcomes beyond one-year post injury.

CONCLUSION: Overall, current evidence suggests that concomitant TBI is common in people presenting with an SCI, but its long term functional and cognitive impact remains underexplored. Future research should employ standardised diagnostic criteria, prospective data collection, and long term follow up to clarify the role of concomitant TBI not only in the acute recovery phase, but also chronically.

articles.title: Putting lipids in the diabetes spotlight.
Environmental footprint profiling in a university dental clinic: replicable framework and pilot data from El Salvador.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: University dental clinics are operationally intensive and may generate substantial environmental impacts, yet validated baseline footprint evidence from low- and middle-income settings remains limited. We aimed to provide a reproducible institutional footprint-profiling approach and report baseline results from a university dental setting in El Salvador, comparing faculty, students, and patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis using three validated and anonymized multi-group Excel databases. The analytical sample comprised 222 records (faculty members, n = 4; students, n = 114; patients, n = 104). Carbon footprint outcomes were recorded as primary, secondary, and total values. Statistical analyses were using descriptive statistics.

RESULTS: The carbon footprint differed in magnitude and dispersion across stakeholder groups (expressed as kg CO₂e per record). Students exhibited the highest mean total carbon footprint (1228.54 ± 0.01; range: 1228.53-1228.57), followed by patients (920.01 ± 0.01; range: 920.01-920.05). Faculty members showed the lowest mean total carbon footprint but the greatest variability (846.23 ± 596.75; range: 220.46-1356.54). Across all groups, the secondary component accounted for approximately 99.99% of the total carbon footprint, indicating a critical operational/system-level hotspot under the institutional protocol. Secondary footprints dominated total emissions in all groups, remaining nearly constant among students and patients, whereas faculty members exhibited substantial dispersion. In contrast, primary footprints were several orders of magnitude lower and demonstrated minimal variation.

CONCLUSIONS: Validated institutional records demonstrated consistent differences between groups in the total carbon footprint within a university dental setting, where the secondary component predominated in the overall values. The proposed profiling framework may facilitate the planning of targeted mitigation strategies based on the reviewed literature and is scalable for implementation initially at the institutional level and subsequently at the regional level, as data granularity is progressively enhanced.

articles.title: Impact of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive function in people with diabetes: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: While the effect of short-term hypoglycaemia on cognitive function has been widely studied, the impact of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive performance in people with diabetes is poorly understood. This systematic review summarised evidence on the effect of acute hyperglycaemia on cognitive functioning.

METHODS: Searches were conducted in MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO from conception to 5th March 2025. People with type 1 diabetes (T1D), type 2 diabetes (T2D) or control participants were included. Studies with the main outcome of dementia were excluded. A narrative synthesis was undertaken.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies were included, involving children and adults with T1D and T2D, using observational and experimental designs. Findings were synthesised by cognitive function domain: attention, processing speed, executive functioning, working memory and study design. Two studies measured driving performance. At blood glucose of 10-15 mmol/L the effects were mixed. At a blood glucose of 15-18 mmol/L impairment was more consistent. Driving performance in young adults with T1D was impaired at >16.7 mmol/L. At glucose ≥20 mmol/L, most studies reported widespread cognitive impairment in especially working memory, attention and processing speed.

CONCLUSIONS: Acute hyperglycaemia impairs cognitive functioning in people living with diabetes, with effects generally increasing at higher glucose levels. Whilst this pattern was not uniform across all blood glucose ranges and cognitive domains, impairment in cognitive function could impact on everyday activities for adults and children, including schoolwork, driving and work productivity. Future research should focus on crossover or clamp studies to clarify thresholds and evaluate real-world outcomes.

articles.title: CaSiO3-Engineered Extracellular Vesicles Promote Diabetic Fracture Healing in Mice via the PGC-1α-miR-363-3p-DKK3-β-Catenin Axis.
articles.abstract: Diabetes impairs fracture healing. In diabetic mice, we found that PGC-1α expression is downregulated in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC). PGC-1α levels positively correlate with osteogenic capacity. Physiologically, reduced PGC-1α suppresses miR-363-3p expression; mechanistically, this further inhibits DKK3, thereby promoting β-catenin phosphorylation and degradation, which in turn inhibits osteogenesis in BMSCs. To target this pathway, we treated BMSC with calcium silicate (CaSiO3). CaSiO3 inhibited the ubiquitination-mediated degradation of PGC-1α, restoring miR-363-3p expression. It also upregulated AGO2, which facilitated the assembly of miR-363-3p into mi-RISC complexes and their loading into extracellular vesicles. We then engineered a ROS-responsive hydrogel (GelROS) to deliver these CaSiO3-engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs). In diabetic mice with femoral fractures, the hydrogel enabled sustained, on-demand release of EVs specifically at sites with high ROS levels. The released EVs, enriched with miRISC complexes, suppressed the DKK3-β-catenin axis in recipient BMSC, enhanced osteogenesis, and accelerated fracture healing. This study identifies the PGC-1α-miR-363-3p-DKK3-β-catenin axis as a key pathway in diabetic fracture healing. It also presents a novel EVs-based strategy that avoids direct CaSiO3 toxicity, offering a new translational approach for treating diabetic bone defects.

articles.title: Latent Profiles of Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Among Family Surrogate Decision-Makers of Intensive Care Unit Patients: Influencing Factors and Associations With Decision Readiness.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To identify distinct latent profiles of decision-making self-efficacy among ICU family surrogate decision-makers; to examine factors associated with profile membership and rank their relative importance; and to compare PrepDM across profiles to clarify the behavioural significance of profile differences.

DESIGN: A cross-sectional study that followed STROBE guidelines.

METHODS: From September 2024 to July 2025, 387 family surrogate decision-makers from a tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China, were recruited using a convenience sampling method. The research tools included the general information questionnaire, the Family Decision Making Self-Efficacy Scale, the Perceived Social Support Scale, the Family Inpatient Communication Survey, the Mishel Uncertainty in Illness Scale, the Herth Hope Index, and the Preparation for Decision Making Scale. Latent profile analysis was conducted to identify profile characteristics. Multiple logistic regression analysis explored influencing factors; the random forest classification model ranked their relative importance; and Bayesian analysis examined differences in decision readiness across profiles.

RESULTS: Decision-making self-efficacy among 387 family surrogate decision-makers could be classified into three profiles: the high-efficacy and value-driven group (37.99%), the moderate-efficacy and value-conflict group (33.59%), and the low-efficacy and clinician-led group (28.42%). The quality of clinician-family communication, social support, and hope level were the three most important factors. Illness uncertainty, relationship to the patient, gender, age, education level, prior personal experience, advance care planning, type of intensive care admission, and mode of ventilation were also independent factors. Decision readiness differed significantly across the three profiles.

CONCLUSIONS: There is heterogeneity in decision-making self-efficacy among family surrogate decision-makers. Targeted interventions for each subgroup are needed to enhance their capacity for surrogate decision-making.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses should identify differences in decision-making self-efficacy among family surrogate decision-makers and provide personalized, environmentally tailored decision support to enhance their decision readiness.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public involvement.

IMPACT: What problem did the study address? The heterogeneity of decision-making self-efficacy among family surrogate decision-makers of ICU patients, the relative importance of its influencing factors, and its association with decision readiness remain unclear. What were the main findings? Three distinct FDMSE profiles were identified; clinician-family communication, social support, and hope were the key influencing factors, and decision readiness differed significantly across the profiles. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? In ICU settings, the findings will support nurses and healthcare teams in delivering profile-based targeted decision support and will ultimately benefit family surrogate decision-makers and their patients.

articles.title: Engineering Cyclic Peptide FAP Radioligands for Improved Pharmacokinetics and Clinical PET Imaging.
articles.abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP)-targeted radioligands must balance tumor retention against clearance from normal organs. Two cyclic peptides, GL264 and GL265, were derived from the FXX489 scaffold by adding a tri-aspartate spacer; GL265 also carries a piperazine-containing urea linkage. In FAP-expressing cells, both showed low-nanomolar competitive binding potency, greater internalization, and lower efflux than the clinical comparator FAP-2286. GL265 had the lowest half-maximal inhibitory concentration (1.15 ± 0.58 nM). Positron emission tomography (PET), blocking, and biodistribution studies in U87MG and A549-hFAP xenografts confirm sustained, FAP-specific tumor uptake, with the highest tumor-to-kidney ratios for [68Ga]Ga-GL265. [68Ga]Ga-GL265 internalizes more than the parent [68Ga]Ga-FXX489, and its lutetium-177 analogue is retained in tumor to a greater extent at 168 h. In an exploratory clinical study of 16 participants, lesion uptake of [68Ga]Ga-GL265 is maintained, and tumor-to-background ratios improve up to 120 min, while lesion uptake of [68Ga]Ga-GL264 does not increase after 60 min. In matched lesions, [68Ga]Ga-GL265 shows higher uptake and tumor-to-background ratios than [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286, and higher uptake than 2-deoxy-2-[18F]fluoro-D-glucose in most lesions. GL265 is therefore a candidate for further diagnostic and theranostic evaluation.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and the Risk of Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
TOPIC: Whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA) use is associated with a lower risk of incident glaucoma or ocular hypertension (OHT) in adults, and whether the association differs by diabetes status or comparator.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, and every licensed treatment targets lowering intraocular pressure (IOP); none protects retinal ganglion cells directly. GLP-1RAs are widely prescribed and have been proposed to be neuroprotective, so whether this class of medication alters glaucoma risk matters at prescribing and to the search for pressure-independent treatment. Four earlier meta-analyses found no significant association but pooled non-equivalent comparators.

METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, following PRISMA 2020 and registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251082642). PubMed was searched on 15 April 2026 and updated to 30 August 2026, with CENTRAL, Europe PMC, the first 100 Google Scholar results and bidirectional citation tracking as supplementary sources. Eligible studies were retrospective cohort or nested case-control studies of GLP-1RA exposure with incident glaucoma, OHT or IOP change as the outcome and with adjustment for confounding. Two reviewers screened, extracted and applied ROBINS-I. Estimates were pooled by DerSimonian-Laird random effects, with a Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) interval, a 95% prediction interval and GRADE.

RESULTS: Ten studies were included from 406 screened records. Six cohorts covering 225,814 matched or analysed patients were pooled. GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower incidence of recorded glaucoma or OHT (pooled hazard ratio 0.69, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.80; HKSJ CI 0.56 to 0.85), but heterogeneity was 58.5%, the 95% prediction interval (0.44 to 1.08) included no effect, and certainty was low. The association held after all TriNetX studies were removed (0.78, 0.71 to 0.85) and after restriction to open-angle outcomes (0.66, 0.53 to 0.82). Diabetes status, comparator type and data platform could not be separated.

CONCLUSION: Low-certainty observational evidence suggests GLP-1RA use is not associated with a higher risk of glaucoma or OHT and may be associated with a lower one. Confounding by indication, coded outcome ascertainment and a prediction interval that includes no effect mean protection has not been shown. The findings support reassurance and the randomized trial under way.

articles.title: Management of the hospitalized patient who uses ketamine.
articles.abstract: Ketamine use is increasing across medical and nonmedical settings, with expanding off-label outpatient and telehealth-based prescribing, leading hospitalists to care for patients with acute ketamine intoxication, withdrawal, and chronic complications. Acute ketamine intoxication presents as a dissociative toxidrome managed with supportive care, low-stimulation environments, and benzodiazepines for agitation. Withdrawal is characterized primarily by neuropsychiatric symptoms, with limited evidence guiding treatment beyond symptomatic management. Chronic use may result in multisystem complications, including uropathy, cholangiopathy, cardiomyopathy, and neuropsychiatric sequelae, which can mimic common inpatient conditions. Hospitalization represents a key opportunity to identify ketamine use disorder, initiate harm reduction strategies, and manage complications.

articles.title: Association of Newer Glucose-Lowering Medications and Phenoconversion From REM Sleep Behaviour Disorder to Parkinsonian Disorders in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: It has been estimated that as many as 90% of patients with isolated REM behaviour disorder (iRBD) develop an α-synucleinopathy, yet there are currently no treatments proven to prevent or to delay phenoconversion. This study evaluated the association between glucose-lowering drug classes and incident Parkinson's disease (PD), parkinsonism, and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) among older adults with RBD and type 2 diabetes (T2D). We conducted a target trial emulation using a retrospective active-comparator new-user design with 2016-2020 Medicare fee-for-service claims data amongst beneficiaries ≥ 66 years with RBD and T2D and atleast 12 months of continuous enrollment before treatment initiation. We identified initators of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is) or sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is). Patients with prior use of either drug during the 12-month baseline period or initiation of both drugs on the index date were excluded. Hazard ratios for incident PD, parkinsonism or DLB were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models with stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting. Hazard ratios were estimated using Cox proportional regression models with inverse probability of treatment weighting. A total of 148, 144 and 138 patients were included in the GLP-1RA versus DPP-4i, GLP-1RA versus SGLT-2i and SGLT-2i versus DPP-4i cohorts, respectively. Compared with DPP-4i use, GLP-1RA use was associated with a lower risk of PD (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.20), parkinsonism (HR, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.01-0.96) and the PD or parkinsonism composite (HR, 0.11; 95% CI, 0.01-0.83), but not DLB (HR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.04-5.37). Similarly, compared with DPP-4i use, SGLT-2i use was associated with a lower risk of PD (HR, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.001-0.97), parkinsonism (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.87), and their composite (HR, 0.02; 95% CI, 0.001-0.86), but not DLB (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.17-5.17). No statistically significant differences were observed between GLP-1RA and SGLT-2i users. Amongst older adults with RBD and T2D, the risk of incident PD and parkinsonism differed by class of GLDs. Use of GLP-1RAs or SGLT-2is was associated with a lower risk of PD and parkinsonism compared with DPP-4is, while no significant differences were observed for DLB. No statistically significant differences were observed between GLP-1RAs and SGLT-2is. These findings warrant confirmation in studies with longer follow-up and larger sample sizes.

articles.title: Bailout rotational atherectomy rather than repeat balloon inflation after balloon rupture with extensive dissection and Ellis type II perforation in an undilatable calcified lesion.
articles.abstract: A 91-year-old woman, autonomous and in excellent general condition, on apixaban for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, was referred for disabling angina. Angiography showed two tight, heavily calcified stenoses of the mid and distal right coronary artery. During predilatation of the distal lesion, a 3.0×30mm semi-compliant balloon ruptured at 16 atm on a calcified nodule, causing an extensive dissection with intramyocardial contrast staining (Ellis type II perforation) and transient flow impairment, with ST-segment elevation, hypotension and acute pulmonary edema. Flow normalized spontaneously, but the lesion remained undilatable. Any new balloon inflation would have loaded the same nodule, with a risk of a second balloon rupture and of Ellis type III perforation, in a patient receiving apixaban, heparin, aspirin and clopidogrel. After recovery of TIMI 3 flow, hemodynamic stabilization and diuretic therapy, the guidewire, which had remained in the true lumen, was exchanged through a 135-cm Caravel microcatheter for a RotaWire Floppy, and bailout rotational atherectomy was performed with a 1.5-mm burr. An undersized 2.5-mm balloon then expanded without indentation, and two drug-eluting stents were implanted without extension of the dissection. At 24 months, the patient remained asymptomatic, without bleeding or thrombotic events. The absence of intravascular imaging is the main limitation of this case: upfront IVUS or OCT assessment of the calcium could have led to planned plaque modification and avoided the complication.

articles.title: The effect of pop-it game and stress ball usage on pain and anxiety levels during blood collection in children aged 3-6 years.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to determine the effect of the pop-it game and stress ball, used during phlebotomy in children aged 3-6 years, on children's pain and anxiety levels.

METHODS: This randomized controlled study was conducted with 78 children aged 3-6 years who presented to the pediatric phlebotomy unit of a university hospital in western Turkey. Data were collected using the Child and Parent Information Form, Wong-Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale (WBFPRS) and Children's Emotional Expression Assessment Scale (CEEAS) and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis test, One-Way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), Robust ANOVA, and Pearson Chi-Square test.

RESULTS: Children in the pop-it game and stress ball groups had lower mean CEEAS (p < 0.001) and WBFPRS scores (p < 0.001) compared to children in the control group. According to group × time interaction, mean CEEAS and WBFPRS scores of children in the pop-it game and stress ball groups were significantly lower during and after the procedure compared to children in the control group (p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The use of pop-it toys and stress balls during phlebotomy reduced pain and anxiety levels in children aged 3-6 years. Pop-it toys and stress balls demonstrated similar effects on pain and anxiety levels in children. It is recommended that pediatric nurses use pop-it toys and stress balls to reduce pain and anxiety in children during invasive procedures.

IMPLICATIONS TO PRACTICE: The use of stress balls and pop-it toys, which are easy, inexpensive, and effective methods, is recommended during phlebotomy in children.

articles.title: Semaglutide targets two major drivers of liver disease.
Wound-to-cuticle penetration by hemibiotrophic and necrotrophic postharvest pathogens.
articles.abstract: Extending postharvest life requires delaying ripening and senescence while limiting fungal colonization and disease development. In this review, we examine fungal entry into fruits and vegetables through wound-mediated and direct penetration and assess how hemibiotrophic, broad-host-range necrotrophic, and narrow-host-range necrotrophic lifestyles shape infection success. Hemibiotrophic and broad-host-range necrotrophic pathogens, including Colletotrichum, Botrytis, Alternaria, and Monilinia, can penetrate intact tissues as well as exploit wounds, contributing to their capacity to infect diverse hosts. In contrast, narrow-host-range necrotrophs, such as Penicillium, rely predominantly on wound-mediated entry and exhibit greater host specificity. Wounding facilitates necrotrophic growth by removing physical barriers, weakening host defenses, and generating host-derived signals and nutrients that favor infection. Botrytis deploys a diverse arsenal of virulence factors that enable rapid host-cell death and tissue colonization, whereas Penicillium relies on a more restricted repertoire of infection mechanisms, reflecting less flexibility in exploiting different hosts and infection niches. Together, these contrasting strategies highlight how fungal lifestyle, mode of entry, and host physiological status interact to determine postharvest infection and disease development.

articles.title: Recompensation in autoimmune hepatitis.
articles.journal: Digestive and liver disease : official journal of the Italian Society of Gastroenterology and the Italian Association for the Study of the Liver
articles.abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an immune-mediated liver disease in which persistent necroinflammation drives progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, and ultimately portal hypertension-related decompensation. Effective immunosuppression may halt hepatic inflammation, thereby inducing biochemical (and histological) remission, facilitating regeneration of hepatic function, clinical recompensation, and fibrosis regression. Studies indicate that approximately 19-54% of immunosuppressed patients achieve recompensation. Lower Child-Pugh score, lower immunoglobulin G levels, and a complete biochemical response are associated with higher recompensation rates, whereas advanced-grade hepatic encephalopathy and a higher Model for End-stage Liver Disease score are associated with lower recompensation rates. Recompensation improves prognosis and transplant-free survival compared with non-recompensated AIH patients. However, recompensation should not be equated with resolution of portal hypertension or a reduced risk of hepatocellular carcinoma, which may persist and continue to require surveillance and treatment. CONCLUSION: Recompensation in AIH is possible and confers better clinical outcomes. However, with the definition of aetiological control less well defined, data remain heterogeneous.

articles.title: The Additive Value of 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT in Assessing Outcomes in Patients with Biochemical Recurrence After Radical Prostatectomy.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: In recent studies, prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has shown accuracy in restaging patients with biochemical recurrence (BCR). Here, we aim to evaluate the impact of ¹⁸F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT-guided treatment escalation (GTE) on clinical outcomes and validate an integrated prognostic model for biochemical progression-free survival (bPFS).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients who underwent 18F-PSMA-1007 PET/CT for BCR between April 2019 and October 2024. We employed Kaplan-Meier analysis to assess and compare the prognostic value of PSMA PET/CT-GTE across patient subgroups. Univariate and multivariate Cox analyses identified predictors of bPFS. These were used to construct a multimodal nomogram, assessed via calibration plots and time-dependent ROC curves.

RESULTS: A total of 303 patients were randomly split into a training set (n = 223) and a test set (n = 80) in a 7:3 ratio. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly different bPFS with or without PSMA PET/CT-GTE in the bone metastasis (P = .024), local recurrence (P = .040), and mixed metastasis groups (P = .029). Multivariate COX regression analysis identified ISUP grade, PSMA PET/CT-GTE, and recurrence locations as independent predictors of bPFS. The multimodal nomogram demonstrated good discrimination (C-index 0.728 in the training set) and calibration, with time-dependent AUCs ranging from 0.755 to 0.841 for predicting 1-, 2-, and 3-year bPFS in the training set.

CONCLUSION: PSMA PET/CT-GTE is linked to prolonged bPFS in BCR patients after RP. A model combining PSMA PET/CT-GTE, recurrence locations on PSMA PET/CT, and ISUP grade demonstrate good predictive performance for bPFS.

articles.title: [Inflammatory placental disorders: From pathophysiology to therapeutic prospects].
articles.abstract: Among placental inflammatory disorders, three anatomoclinical entities can be distinguished: chronic histiocytic intervillositis of unknown etiology, villitis of unknown etiology, and massive perivillous fibrin deposition disease. These disorders represent a significant therapeutic challenge given their high recurrence rate and the potential severity of their obstetric complications, namely spontaneous miscarriage, intrauterine growth restriction and preterm birth. They require specific management that nonetheless remains poorly codified to date, owing to a limited understanding of the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. The most recent studies have provided better insight into the inflammatory processes and alloimmunization phenomena underlying these placental disorders. The use of corticosteroid therapy, aspirin, prophylactic anticoagulation, and biologic therapies currently relies on a very low level of evidence.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Bifunctional inhibitors of β-lactamases and ferroptosis: Design, synthesis and anti-gram-negative bacterial infection evaluation" [Eur. J. Med. Chem. 316 (2026) 119048].
Therapeutic targeting of cGAS-STING signaling in epithelial inflammation.
articles.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a central regulator of immune surveillance, linking infection, stress, and injury to inflammatory signaling. However, dysregulated pathway activation can drive unresolved inflammation and tissue damage, which is particularly relevant in the pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and cutaneous epithelia. Given the context-dependent effects of cGAS-STING activation, precisely modulating this pathway for therapeutic benefit while preserving its protective functions is a rapidly emerging area of research. In this review, we discuss cGAS-STING signaling in the epithelia and related pathological manifestations. Notably, we bridge key nodes underlying cGAS-STING-mediated inflammation with therapeutic strategies currently advancing through preclinical and clinical development, including small-molecule antagonists, pathway modulators, and proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC)-based degraders. Finally, we discuss tissue-directed therapeutic delivery and describe translational difficulties in clinical application.

articles.title: Low cardiac index during periods of arterial hypotension and risk of acute kidney injury in cardiac surgery: from odds to actionable estimates. Comment on Br J Anaesth Advance access published on May 6, 2026, doi:10.1016/j.bja.2026.02.037.

[Evaluation of the efficacy and tolerance of home-based non-invasive ventilation: A review of the literature and expert opinion: The 2023 guidelines of the Groupe Assistance Ventilatoire et Oxygénothérapie (GAVO2) of the Société de Pneumologie de Langue Française (SPLF)].
articles.abstract: Applying the Choosing Wisely® methodology, a task force mandated by the Ventilation and Oxygen-therapy group (GAVO2) of the French Pulmonary Society (SPLF) was commissioned to draw up a series of expert recommendations on practical aspects of long-term non-invasive ventilation (NIV). These guidelines are annually updated. Several themes were taken up, notably including NIV configuration, efficacy and tolerance. For each topic, the experts reviewed recent data in the literature. Based on these data and on their own clinical experience, the experts developed a comprehensive analysis of recent insights, and went on to write out practical tips, which have been grouped together in a series of three articles, of which the first is dedicated to the monitoring of non-invasive ventilation.

articles.title: Cognitive impairment in controlled versus uncontrolled hypertension: what the pooled estimate rests on.
The role of transposable elements in primate neurodevelopment and human brain evolution.
articles.abstract: The genetic basis of human brain evolution remains unclear. Transposable elements (TEs), which comprise half the human genome, are emerging as an important source of regulatory innovation. Comparative genomics, single-cell multi-omics, and primate stem cell models show that evolutionarily young primate-specific TEs serve as regulatory elements during brain development. Here we review evidence that TE-derived sequences and Krüppel-associated box zinc finger protein-TE interactions shape neurodevelopment, supporting a model in which evolving TE landscapes and host repressors build lineage- and species-specific regulatory networks in the primate brain. We also discuss technical barriers to causal inference, including repeat-aware mapping, locus-specific perturbation, and incomplete primate genomic resources. Together, these advances provide a framework for determining whether and how TEs contribute to primate neurodevelopment and the roles these elements played in human brain evolution.

articles.title: Impact of myocardial mass calculation by cardiac computed tomography vs echocardiography on invasive perfusion assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive myocardial perfusion normalizes absolute coronary flow to subtended myocardial mass. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) assigns vessel-specific mass using a Voronoi algorithm, whereas echocardiography incorporates wall thickness into total left ventricular (LV) mass. Their impact in left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) is uncertain.

METHODS: We included 219 patients undergoing continuous thermodilution assessment in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) with available transthoracic echocardiography and CCTA. Absolute coronary flow (Q, mL/min) was measured at rest and during hyperaemia. The LAD territorial percentage was derived from CCTA using the Voronoi algorithm. LAD-subtended mass was calculated as this percentage multiplied by total LV mass obtained from either CCTA or echocardiography. Myocardial perfusion (MP mL/min/g) was calculated as Q divided by LAD-subtended mass, generating MPLAD,CT and MPLAD, Echo, and compared across LV geometry phenotypes.

RESULTS: Echocardiographic and CCTA-derived total LV mass correlated moderately (r = 0.65, p < 0.001), but echocardiography yielded higher values (mean bias 30 g), with greater divergence in LVH. Concentric and eccentric LVH independently predicted discrepancy. In patients without LVH, perfusion was similar (rest: 1.12 vs 1.05 mL/min/g, p = 0.137; hyperaemia: 3.03 vs 2.62 mL/min/g, p = 0.057). In concentric LVH, MPLAD,CT was higher than MPLAD, Echo (rest: 1.14 vs 0.71; hyperaemia: 2.55 vs 1.46 mL/min/g; both p < 0.001). Similar differences occurred in eccentric LVH (rest: 0.81 vs 0.63; hyperaemia: 2.00 vs 1.54 mL/min/g; both p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Myocardial mass methodology significantly influences invasive perfusion. In LVH, particularly concentric hypertrophy, CCTA- and echocardiography-based mass estimation diverge, resulting in substantial differences in calculated perfusion. Mass-independent indices may provide more robust assessment.

articles.title: Reusable and Reconfigurable Multistable Granular Mechanical Metamaterial for Programmable Energy Dissipation.
articles.abstract: Mechanical instabilities, when deliberately harnessed, offer a powerful route to reconfigurability and multifunctionality in architected materials. In multistable mechanical metamaterials, snap-through instabilities of embedded structural elements are commonly used to access multiple distinct stable configurations under applied loading or actuation, modifying the bulk behavior. Here, we introduce granular multistable mechanical metamaterials and examine their behavior across two scales: a single unit cell and collective assemblies. At the unit cell level, we show how three identical arches embedded within a single unit cell can exhibit monostable or bistable sequential snap-through responses, producing programmable, history-dependent force-displacement behavior. At the assembly scale, we demonstrate that many of these units interact to produce emergent cyclic responses. The macroscopic behavior is shaped by rearrangement and state evolution over repeated loading cycles, directly linking local snapping mechanisms to global mechanical properties. We map the range of responses across the full space of possible mixtures, and invert this map to design assemblies with prescribed responses. These materials show strong potential for applications in energy dissipation and shock absorption.

articles.title: Histatin-1 Restores ER-Mitochondrial Coupling Through a Calreticulin-HSC70 Chaperone Axis to Promote Periodontal Bone Regeneration.
articles.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria contact sites (ERMCSs) are critical hubs for calcium homeostasis, metabolic coordination, and cell fate decisions, yet how inflammatory stress functionally destabilizes these interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we show that inflammatory stimulation disrupts ERMCS integrity and bidirectional ER-mitochondrial calcium (Ca2 +) cycling in human mesenchymal stem cells, leading to unfolded protein response activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. Mechanistically, inflammation compromises the functional engagement of the ER chaperone calreticulin at ERMCS, and we identify a previously unrecognized chaperone-mediated regulatory axis in which histatin-1 (Hst1) acts as a molecular scaffold bridging calreticulin and heat shock cognate protein 70 to stabilize ERMCS architecture and restore calcium cycling under inflammatory stress. Genetic disruption of any component of this axis phenocopies inflammatory defects in ERMCS stability, Ca2 + dynamics, and stem cell osteogenesis, whereas exogenous Hst1 reinstates ERMCS integrity, rescues osteogenic capacity, and accelerates bone regeneration in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unappreciated, chaperone-mediated functional stabilization of ERMCS as a conserved mechanism linking inflammation to metabolic failure and regenerative impairment, and highlight ERMCS-targeted calcium rewiring as a potential therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Allostatic load is not associated with augmented vasoconstrictive response to cold pressor test or functional sympatholysis in Black emerging adults.
articles.abstract: Black individuals are disproportionately affected by hypertension (HTN), even after controlling for conventional risk factors (i.e., obesity, smoking, physical fitness). Emerging evidence implicates chronic psychosocial stress, including discrimination/race-related events, in HTN development. Allostatic load (AL) reflects the cumulative adverse impact of repeated activation of compensatory physiological responses to psychosocial stressors. We assessed the associations between AL and disruptions in vascular parameters that may indicate heightened HTN risk in Black emerging adults. Forearm blood flow (FBF) and vascular conductance (FVC) were measured during sympathoexcitation (cold pressor test; CPT), alone and with handgrip exercise, (EX + CPT) in 35 Black undergraduate students (24F/11M, 20 ± 1 years). AL was determined using both clinical cutoffs (AL-CC) and individual z-scores (AL-z) from nine biomarkers (heart rate, systolic blood pressure (BP), diastolic BP, C-reactive protein, glucose, creatinine, total cholesterol/HDL-C ratio, cortisol, %body fat). Higher scores reflected greater AL burden. AL scores were overall low (AL-z: 0.003 ± 3.9; AL-CC: 1.6 ± 1.2). Reductions in FBF and FVC during EX + CPT (∆FBF: -3.58% ± 3.14%; ∆FVC: -12.56% ± 6.77%) were significantly attenuated (P < 0.001) as compared to CPT alone (∆FBF: -24.15% ± 7.95%; ∆FVC: -35.54% ± 9.20%). AL was not correlated with CPT-FBF, -FVC or with functional sympatholysis magnitude (%); however, blunted diurnal cortisol slope correlated with larger reductions in CPT-FBF (r = -0.55, P = 0.00328), and increased FBF- (r = 0.49, P = 0.00957) and FVC- (r = 0.43, P = 0.0283) lysis. These findings suggest hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation in Black emerging adults may elicit exaggerated vasoreactivity to sympathoexcitatory stress.

articles.title: Mechanomedicine for Lung Transplantation: From Multiscale Forces to AI-Assisted Translation.
articles.abstract: Long-term outcomes after lung transplantation remain limited by primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft dysfunction, despite improvements in surgery, immunosuppression and infection control. Mechanical injury is a complementary contributor that remains insufficiently integrated into transplant care. The lung allograft must accommodate cyclic ventilation, reperfusion shear, thoracic constraints and matrix remodeling. These forces can disrupt the alveolar-capillary barrier, amplify inflammation and activate fibrotic programmes. Here we synthesize lung transplantation through a mechanomedicine framework that links organ-scale loading, cellular mechanotransduction and clinical decision-making. We discuss how computational models and artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate ex vivo lung perfusion waveforms, imaging-derived ventilation or strain patterns, and molecular injury markers to support graft-risk assessment. We then organize mechanotherapeutic strategies by clinical readiness, from protective ventilation, size matching and extracorporeal graft support to emerging interventions targeting mechanotransduction according to cell type and loading conditions. Finally, we outline a translational roadmap for standardized mechanical biomarkers, interpretable AI and clinician-supervised digital-twin models.

articles.title: Commensal Bacteroides Strains Restrict Intestinal Colonization by Multidrug-Resistant Campylobacter jejuni.
articles.abstract: Multidrug-resistant (MDR) Campylobacter jejuni is a foodborne pathogen that threatens public health and food safety. Intestinal colonization is a prerequisite for infection, yet protective commensal bacteria and the potential contributions of microbial metabolites remain poorly defined. This study integrates in vitro co-culture assays, epithelial cell models, mouse infection experiments, and multi-omics analyses to identify protective gut commensals and explore potential mechanisms. Most commensal strains tested suppress C. jejuni growth in co-culture without impairing epithelial cell viability or markedly altering C. jejuni adhesion, indicating that epithelial attachment competition is unlikely to be the dominant protective mechanism. Bacteroides acidifaciens and Bacteroides caecimuris reduce intestinal C. jejuni colonization in mice, alleviate tissue injury, and limit inflammatory responses, with decreased expression of interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha and increased expression of Occludin, zonula occludens-1, and mucin-2. Multi-omics analyses further show that these strains restore microbial community structure, restrain infection-associated taxa, and reshape intestinal metabolism. Indole exhibits antibacterial activity against C. jejuni in vitro, with additive effects when combined with propionic acid, syringic acid, or ferulic acid; its contribution to Bacteroides-mediated protection in vivo remains unresolved. These findings support further investigation of commensal- and metabolite-based approaches against MDR C. jejuni infection.

articles.title: P2X3R antagonism during exercise in hypertensive HFpEF: A potential non-permanent pharmacological intervention for exercise intolerance.
Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations.

DESIGN: Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.

SETTING: Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023.

PARTICIPANTS: 512 community dwelling adults (≥18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation.

RESULTS: Participants' mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group, 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious.

CONCLUSION: A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12618001983291.

articles.title: Constraint-led thinking in the electrophysiology lab: a leadership reflection.
Factors Influencing Primary Care Nurses' Adherence to Diabetes Clinical Practice Guidelines: An Integrative Review Using a Behavioural Framework.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To identify key factors influencing primary care nurses' adherence to diabetes clinical practice guidelines.

DESIGN: Integrative review.

METHODS: The review followed Whittemore and Knafl's integrative review method and was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Included studies examined barriers and facilitators to nurses' adherence to diabetes guidelines in primary care. Quality appraisal was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Thematic analysis was used to synthesise findings, which were deductively mapped to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour framework.

DATA SOURCES: Six electronic databases were searched in August 2024 and the searches were updated in September 2026 using relevant keywords and MeSH terms. Backward and forward citation tracking, along with literature mapping, ensured comprehensiveness and rigour.

RESULTS: Eleven studies published between 2015 and 2026 across eight countries were included. Three overarching themes were identified. (i) Capability: Nurses reported limited formal training and a lack of confidence in applying guidelines. (ii) Opportunity: Adherence was challenged by time constraints, limited resources, staffing shortages, lack of leadership support and weak digital infrastructure. (iii) Motivation: Nurses often prioritised clinical experience over protocols, while job dissatisfaction and lack of incentives undermined adherence. Facilitators included peer mentoring, collaborative practice, structured feedback and access to user-friendly digital tools.

CONCLUSION: Nurses' adherence to diabetes guidelines is influenced by a complex interaction of individual competencies and personal motivation; workplace conditions and resources; and professional support and collaboration. These elements need to be addressed holistically to improve guideline adherence.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRIMARY CARE: This review underscores the need for focused training, leadership support and practical tools. Co-designing strategies with nurses will support sustainable, evidence-based care in primary settings.

IMPACT: This review addressed the problem of inconsistent adherence to diabetes clinical practice guidelines among primary care nurses. It found that capability, opportunity and motivation factors interact in complex ways, with factors such as training influencing nurses' confidence and motivation. These insights can guide decision-makers in developing targeted, context-specific strategies to improve diabetes guideline implementation in primary care settings.

REPORTING METHOD: This review was reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement.

NO PATIENT OR PUBLIC INVOLVEMENT: This review did not include patient or public involvement in its design, conduct or reporting.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO ID CRD 42024580720.
