ASFNR Clinical State-of-Practice in Neuroimaging of Minor Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor ischemic stroke (MIS) with anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) is a distinct stroke subtype in which mild neurological deficits may mask a substantial volume of threatened but salvageable brain tissue. Despite a baseline NIHSS≤5, nearly one-third of patients experience poor functional outcomes, often due to early neurological deterioration (END).

CURRENT EVIDENCE AND ONGOING TRIALS: Patients with LVO-MIS were markedly underrepresented in landmark thrombectomy trials, resulting in limited evidence to guide treatment. Retrospective studies have identified imaging biomarkers of END, including proximal occlusion, clot length, collateral status, and perfusion mismatch, but the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains uncertain. Ongoing randomized controlled trials, including STEP and MOSTE, are expected to define the role of EVT and imaging-based patient selection in this population.

PURPOSE: To summarize the current state of neuroimaging in anterior circulation LVO-MIS and provide a practical imaging workflow and reporting checklist for diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment selection.

KEY POINTS: CTA remains the primary modality for LVO detection and collateral assessment, while CT and MR perfusion identify salvageable tissue and predict END beyond baseline NIHSS. MRI further refines infarct core, perfusion deficit, and thrombus characterization. Current AI-based LVO detection tools improve stroke triage but require careful human oversight because proximal M2 and non-terminus ICA occlusions may be missed.

CONCLUSION: Pending results from ongoing trials, tissue-based imaging with CTA, CT perfusion, and MR perfusion can complement clinical assessment to improve risk stratification and individualized treatment decisions. Advances in quantitative imaging and artificial intelligence are expected to further enable precision imaging-guided management of LVO-MIS.

articles.title: Design Thinking in Advance Care Planning for Emerging Adults: Enhancing Control and Customization to Support Engagement.
articles.abstract: Objective: This study examined how emerging adults with serious illness engage with advance care planning (ACP) through a design-informed lens.Background:ACP enables individuals to communicate their preferences and goals for medical care if they are unable to make decisions for themselves. Although ACP is widely recognized as critical for individuals with serious illness, engagement remains low among emerging adults (ages 18-29), a distinct developmental subgroup within the adolescent and young adult population. Traditional ACP approaches emphasize documentation and legal requirements, which may limit engagement among individuals navigating identity development, autonomy, and future-oriented life transitions.Methods: A secondary analysis was conducted using data from 39 emerging adults with oncology or hematology diagnoses who reviewed the ACP communication guide, Voicing My CHOiCES (VMC). Structured interviews assessed participant perspectives on usability, preferences, and emotional responses. Data were explored using thematic content analysis.Results:Two central themes emerged: (1) affording choice and control and (2) designing for customization and usability. Participants valued opportunities for personalization, structured guidance, and revisable formats. Design elements that supported autonomy, reduced cognitive burden, and facilitated reflection were associated with more positive experiences of engagement, while overly rigid features constrained expression.Discussion: Across themes, ACP engagement with emerging adults was closely tied to how the VMC tool structured interaction. Design features that enabled choice, reduced complexity, and allowed for iterative engagement were associated with more positive experiences. This suggests that designing ACP as a flexible, user-centered, developmentally tailored process may better support meaningful participation.

articles.title: Initiation of lenacapavir with dose escalation in a patient receiving rifabutin: A case report with therapeutic drug monitoring.
articles.abstract: Lenacapavir is a first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor with long-acting pharmacokinetics that enable 6-monthly subcutaneous dosing after initiation with oral lead-in. Lenacapavir is a CYP3A4, UGT1A1 and P-gp substrate; inducers of these enzymes and P-gp can significantly decrease lenacapavir concentrations. In patients receiving lenacapavir for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), supplemental lenacapavir doses can be administered if rifabutin (moderate inducer) or rifampin (potent inducer) are initiated. However, these recommendations have not been extended to lenacapavir when used for HIV treatment, and little is known about initiating lenacapavir in patients on stable therapy with inducers. We describe a 30-year-old man with advanced HIV infection and disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex infection receiving rifabutin and concurrent darunavir/ritonavir in whom lenacapavir was initiated with a 50% increase in both oral (900 mg on Days 1 and 2) and subcutaneous loading doses (1390.5 mg on Day 1). Therapeutic drug monitoring using validated UPLC-MS/MS method demonstrated that lenacapavir plasma concentrations remained above the target of 15.5 ng/mL (4× protein-adjusted 95% effective concentration [PA-EC95]) over the dosing interval, with Cmax of 245.7 ng/mL and a projected Cmin of 19.5 ng/mL at 6 months. HIV viral load remained suppressed. This case demonstrates that dose-adjusted lenacapavir can achieve therapeutic exposures in the presence of pre-existing moderate induction. These findings provide clinically relevant pharmacological insight to support the use of lenacapavir in complex patients requiring rifamycin therapy.

articles.title: Routine Prenatal Ultrasound at 36 Weeks: Impact on Obstetric Clinical Outcomes.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of introducing a routine prenatal ultrasound scan at 36 weeks' gestation, integrated with a predefined clinical management pathway, on obstetric outcomes.

DESIGN: Single-centre retrospective study.

SETTING: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London, UK.

POPULATION: 37 001 singleton term pregnancies delivered between April 2016 and October 2024.

METHODS: From January 2020, universal 36-week ultrasound replaced targeted scanning within a predefined national management pathway; its impact was assessed using interrupted time-series analysis (ITSA).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Primary outcomes were gestational age at birth in SGA and LGA neonates, and prenatal detection rate of breech presentation. Secondary outcomes included rates of neonatal intensive care unit admission, severe perineal trauma, shoulder dystocia and stillbirth.

RESULTS: SGA infants delivered at 37-38 weeks' gestation increased from 18.7% to 38.1% post intervention (p = 0.04) with a concomitant overall reduction in NICU admissions (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.66-0.82). The prenatal detection rate of breech presentation increased significantly from 78% to almost 90% (p = 0.002). The intervention was also associated with a significant reduction in third- and fourth-degree perineal tears (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.65-0.84).

CONCLUSIONS: Routine 36-week scan embedded within a structured clinical management pathway was associated with significant changes in obstetric metrics and improved pregnancy outcome. Overall, these findings provide real-world evidence on how a universal third-trimester ultrasound may selectively influence obstetric management and inform the ongoing debate on routine prenatal screening strategies.

articles.title: Ross procedure: state-of-the-art review for cardiologists.
articles.abstract: The Ross procedure is an alternative to prosthetic aortic valve replacement in patients with aortic valve disease. Proponents of the Ross procedure argue that it is associated with life expectancy close to that of the general population in patients with aortic valve disease due to avoiding the major pitfalls of both biologic (valve degeneration) and mechanical (valve-related thrombotic complications and bleeding associated with lifelong anticoagulation) prostheses.1 Critics remain concerned about higher perioperative risk and the potential need for reintervention on the pulmonary autograft and homograft. This paper reviews the existing literature and provides expert recommendations on patient selection and preoperative and postoperative care of the Ross patient.

articles.title: African Cancer Immunology and Infection Initiative (TACII): reframing cancer research in Africa through immunology, infection, and the microbiome.
Sensitivity to infection threats and HIV-related attitudes among medical students: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: HIV-related stigma remains a major barrier to effective HIV prevention, treatment, and care. Although infection-related psychological processes have been proposed as potential contributors to stigmatizing attitudes, their role among future healthcare professionals remains poorly understood. This study examined the association between sensitivity to infection threats and HIV-related attitudes among medical students and evaluated the associations of HIV/AIDS education, clinical training, and prior contact with people living with HIV. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 450 medical students at Ahi Evran University Faculty of Medicine, Turkey. Participants completed the Sensitivity to Infection Threats Scale (SITS) and the HIV/AIDS Attitude Scale. Spearman correlation analyses, Mann-Whitney U tests, and hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses were performed. Overall sensitivity to infection threats was not associated with HIV-related attitudes. However, higher avoidant sensitivity remained independently associated with less favorable HIV-related attitudes (β = -0.112, p = .019). In addition, HIV/AIDS education and clinical training were associated with more favorable attitudes in the HIV Avoidance domain. These findings suggest that avoidance-related responses to perceived infection threats may contribute to HIV-related stigma among future physicians and support the value of HIV/AIDS education and clinical training in promoting more positive attitudes toward people living with HIV.

articles.title: Extracting patient-reported cannabis use and reasons for use from EHR in rheumatology: a benchmarking study of language models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a scalable natural language processing pipeline to identify cannabis use status and reasons for use among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (ARDs) from unstructured electronic health record (EHR) data.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We conducted a retrospective study using EHR clinical notes from patients with ARDs (2015–2024). Cannabis-related mentions were screened by lexicon-based keyword matching and extracted as 50-word snippets. Two experts annotated 840 snippets for use-status classes (not a true mention/uncertain, denial, past use, current use) and 773 snippets for reason-for-use categories (pain, nausea, sleep, relaxation/stress/anxiety, not mentioned/unknown). We compared multiple large language model (LLM) prompting strategies, a fine-tuned clinical encoder model (GatorTron) and a logistic regression baseline using held-out class-balanced test sets (status n=40, reason n=50; 10/class) using accuracy and F1.

RESULTS: Fine-tuned GatorTron achieved the highest point estimates for use status (accuracy=0.88, 95% CI (0.78 to 0.98); F1=0.88, 95% CI (0.77 to 0.97)) and GPT-OSS-20B for reason for use (accuracy=0.84, 95% CI (0.74 to 0.92); F1=0.83, 95% CI (0.78 to 0.94)). For both tasks, CIs of the best and second-best models overlapped, calling for cautious interpretation. We also characterised clinical trends in documented cannabis use from 2015 to 2024.

DISCUSSION: This benchmarking framework offers a scalable approach to characterising documented cannabis use from EHR. Findings are exploratory and validation in prevalence-representative samples is needed in future work.

CONCLUSIONS: Extraction of cannabis use status and reasons for use from EHR notes is feasible using fine-tuned language models and generative LLMs. This approach can support real-world evidence research on symptom self-management in ARDs.

A study on olfactory mucosa-derived stem cells for ischemic stroke is registered in Hainan.
articles.abstract: On November 4, 2026, China announced that a study on autologous olfactory mucosa-derived mesenchymal stem cells for ischemic stroke was registered in Hainan. Initiated by Hainan Susheng Biotechnology Co., Ltd., the project lists Haikou People's Hospital as its clinical research institution. Olfactory mucosa-derived cells provide a distinct source for investigating immunomodulation and neural repair. A 2025 study of hypoxia-preconditioned cells reported reduced microglial ferroptosis and neuroinflammation and improved neurological outcomes in experimental stroke models. These findings provide a preclinical rationale; the registered product's preparation and its effects in humans need to be clinically evaluated. For Hainan, the project links local scientific work with collaboration between a biotechnology enterprise and a hospital. Its contribution will depend on appropriate patient selection, credible study design, meaningful functional outcomes, reproducible cell manufacture, and long-term safety monitoring. Transparent reporting can make this experience informative for future stroke research and the development of regulated regenerative medicine.

articles.title: Effect of intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide and sodium bicarbonate on spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women after induction of labour (SAINT): multicentre randomised placebo controlled factorial trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour.

DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT).

SETTING: 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care.

PARTICIPANTS: Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour.

INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery).

RESULTS: Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Although small beneficial effects cannot be excluded, the findings do not support routine intrapartum use of either agent to facilitate spontaneous vaginal birth after induction of labour.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Clinical Trials Database (EudraCT; 2021-000392-37); EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS; EU CT number 2024-511848-55-00); ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05719467).

articles.title: N6-methyladenosine-mediated down regulation of hsa_circ_0002420 promotes macrophage M1 polarisation in sepsis by regulating the miR-5586-5p/RAD23B axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Macrophage polarisation plays a crucial role in sepsis-associated inflammatory responses; however, the underlying molecular regulatory mechanisms remain to be further explored.

AIM: This study aimed to explore the role of circ_0002420 in regulating macrophage polarisation.

METHODS: Quantification of key molecules was performed using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for mRNAs, western blotting for proteins and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay for secreted proteins. The genomic locus of circ_0002420 was validated via Sanger sequencing. The stability of circ_0002420 was assessed after RNase R digestion and actinomycin D treatment. CD80-, CD86- and CD206-positive cells were detected via flow cytometry. Molecular interactions were verified using RNA immunoprecipitation, dual-luciferase reporter and miRNA pull-down assays. The m6A modification was detected via a methylated RNA immunoprecipitation assay.

RESULTS: Circ_0002420 was down regulated in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with sepsis-induced lung injury and in M1 macrophages. Mechanistically, methyltransferase-like 3-mediated m6A modification recruited YTH N6-methyladenosine RNA binding protein F2 to suppress circ_0002420 expression. Circ_0002420 directly sponged miR-5586-5p to modulate its availability. MiR-5586-5p targeted RAD23 nucleotide excision repair protein B (RAD23B) mRNA and suppressed its expression. Circ_0002420 overexpression inhibited M1 polarisation and inflammation through mediating the miR-5586-5p/RAD23B axis.

CONCLUSION: The circ_0002420/miR-5586-5p/RAD23B axis regulates macrophage M1 polarisation and inflammatory responses, providing insights into sepsis-associated macrophage inflammation.

Major Bleeding After Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Acute Pulmonary Embolism: Derivation and Transferability of the F-HARP Risk Assessment Model.
articles.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter-directed thrombolysis is an established reperfusion strategy for intermediate- or high-risk acute pulmonary embolism. No validated model exists to predict early major bleeding in this population.

OBJECTIVES: To derive a baseline-only risk assessment model for major bleeding after catheter-directed thrombolysis, and to assess its transferability in an independent cohort.

PATIENTS/METHODS: We pooled patient-level data from 16 cohort studies and randomized trials of catheter-directed thrombolysis for acute pulmonary embolism. The most stable baseline predictors of major bleeding were identified by adaptive LASSO across 1000 bootstrap iterations. Candidate models including 2 to 6 of these predictors were compared on optimism-corrected discrimination and calibration. The selected model was applied to an independent cohort from the RIETE registry.

RESULTS: Of 1246 patients with outcome data and without contraindications to thrombolysis, 75 (6.0%) experienced major bleeding, including 10 intracranial hemorrhages. On internal validation, the F-HARP model (Female sex, Hypertension, Age, high-Risk Pulmonary embolism) showed an optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.695 (95%CI: 0.639-0.755). In the independent cohort (N=566), patients classified as high risk had higher odds of major bleeding within 30 days than the remainder (11.2% vs. 3.8%; OR 3.18, 95%CI: 1.44-7.05). AUROC was 0.638 (95%CI: 0.519-0.742) and calibration slope 0.630 (95%CI: 0.153-1.107).

CONCLUSIONS: The F-HARP model uses four readily available baseline predictors to identify a subgroup at meaningfully higher odds of major bleeding after catheter-directed thrombolysis. A powered external validation is required prior to its use for precise risk quantification.

articles.title: A Bailout Strategy for CRT Implantation: Retrograde Coronary Venous Wiring with Venoplasty and Wire Externalization.
articles.abstract: Left ventricular (LV) lead delivery failure remains a major limitation of cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), particularly in patients with complex coronary venous anatomy. We report a 65-year-old woman with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 30%, LBBB, QRS 170 ms) referred for CRT-D after a failed implantation attempt elsewhere. Coronary sinus angiography revealed a small-calibre high lateral vein and a lateral vein with severe post-ostial stenosis. After unsuccessful antegrade wiring, a retrograde strategy was employed: a microcatheter and Fielder XT-A guidewire traversed epicardial collaterals from the posterior to the lateral vein. The Fielder XT-A was then exchanged for a 300-cm RG3 guidewire, which was externalized using a gooseneck snare to create a through-and-through rail. Sequential balloon venoplasty (1.5-2.5 mm) dilated the stenotic segment, enabling successful quadripolar LV lead placement. The D1-M2 vector achieved a capture threshold of 1.2 V at 0.5 ms without phrenic nerve stimulation. At 12-month follow-up, the patient improved to New York Heart Association class I with LVEF 45% and no heart failure admissions. This case demonstrates the sequential application of retrograde coronary venous wiring, wire exchange, snare-assisted externalization, and balloon venoplasty-techniques adapted from interventional cardiology-to overcome severely stenotic coronary venous anatomy when conventional antegrade approaches fail. Advanced coronary intervention techniques may provide a reproducible bailout strategy for achieving optimal LV lead positioning in patients with complex coronary venous anatomy.

articles.title: Crystal Structure of Equine Coronavirus Main Protease in Complex with the inhibitor GC376-Considerations for Pan-Coronaviral Inhibitor Design.
articles.abstract: Coronaviruses are highly transmissible pathogens that infect a broad range of hosts, with some causing severe illness in both humans and animals. Considerable research effort for the treatment of acute infection has been directed towards human coronaviral targets, including SARS-CoV-1/-2, MERS-CoV and other human coronaviruses. However, comparable study of related animal coronaviruses that may cross-over to humans is less prominent. Here we describe the cloning, isolation and purification of the genomically proposed equine coronavirus main protease (EqCoV-Mpro) and its C59S and C225S mutants to facilitate drug development. FDA-approved and investigational SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors, including GC376, inhibit EqCoV-Mpro with nanomolar potency. A surface-cysteine C59S mutation enabled the first X-ray co-crystal structure of EqCoV Mpro with GC376 at 2.0 Å. It reveals a deeper, more hydrophobic active site than related human and animal CoV Mpros, favoring compact inhibitors and informing future pan-coronaviral inhibitor design.

articles.title: Osteoarthritis year in review 2026: Imaging.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To narratively review the literature on osteoarthritis (OA) imaging published between March 2025 and March 2026 and to identify current trends and emerging directions in imaging-based OA research.

METHODS: PubMed was searched for original English-language human in vivo studies published during the period. Trends by imaging modality and target-joint distributions were analyzed. For narrative synthesis, studies were selected subjectively by consensus among the authors based on methodological novelty, clinical or trial relevance, contribution to understanding OA pathophysiology or progression, and potential future impact.

RESULTS: Of 1,910 publications identified, 1,035 specified a target joint. Approximately 70% investigated the knee, followed by the hip. Radiography and ultrasound yielded the most records, encompassing heterogeneous applications such as trial eligibility and image-guided procedures. Although publication counts for these modalities have gradually declined in recent years, those for MRI have remained stable. Semiquantitative MRI analysis linked worsening bone marrow lesions and Hoffa-synovitis to greater cartilage loss, and suggested differing associations between injection type and subsequent structural progression. Quantitative MRI studies linked cartilage T2 to BMI in a population-based cohort, while muscle radiomics predicted incident knee OA. Among emerging technique, magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) provided rapid cartilage T2 mapping, and [18F]NaF PET-MRI linked increased metabolic activity at enthesis to worse knee-related outcomes. For clinical-trial eligibility, MRI detected exclusionary abnormalities in 10% of otherwise DMOAD-eligible knees. AI-related publications gradually increased, with applications including prediction of future total knee replacement (TKR) and automated tissue segmentation.

CONCLUSION: Studies highlight the use of imaging for longitudinal assessment of structural progression, clinical-trial eligibility, and quantitative tissue characterization. MRI remains central to understanding disease mechanisms and progression, while emerging techniques such as MRF and [18F]NaF PET-MRI broaden quantitative and metabolic assessment. AI may support prediction of future TKR and automated cartilage morphometry.

articles.title: What we have learned from a decade of meta-analyses on lithium: an umbrella review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lithium remains the cornerstone treatment for bipolar disorder and has been studied across a widening range of psychiatric and somatic outcomes. This umbrella review synthesized and critically appraised meta-analytic evidence on lithium published in the past decade.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EBSCO, Embase and Cochrane Library were systematically searched for meta-analyses of lithium published between January 2016 and June 2026. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR 2, and primary study overlap using the Corrected Covered Area.

RESULTS: Of 3136 identified records, 83 meta-analyses across seven clinical domains were included. Evidence confirmed lithium's efficacy for acute mania and relapse prevention in bipolar disorder; but not its acute antidepressant efficacy as monotherapy in bipolar depression. Lithium augmentation was supported for difficult-to-treat unipolar depression. Anti-suicidal effects were consistent in direction, but often imprecisely estimated. Adjunctive lithium improved outcomes of radioactive iodine therapy in hyperthyroidism. Renal, parathyroid and dermatological adverse effects and first-trimester malformation risks were identified, whereas metabolic and cognitive tolerability appeared favorable. Associations with reduced risks of stroke, fracture and cancer and a possible neuroprotective effect were found, although often based on few meta-analyses of low quality. Evidence in minors was scarce. Methodological quality was predominantly (critically) low, with substantial primary study overlap.

CONCLUSION: Current meta-analytic evidence reinforces lithium's role in acute mania and maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder, while supporting broader psychiatric and somatic applications, including unipolar depression, suicide prevention, and hyperthyroidism. In contrast, evidence for neuroprotective and other emerging indications remains uncertain, highlighting the need for higher-quality studies in understudied areas.

articles.title: Local ablative therapy for oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer with actionable mutations: A consensus from Hong Kong SBRT Study Group.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract: Oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly encountered in clinical practice, owing to advances in imaging techniques and the emergence of new therapeutic options. This manuscript presents the outcomes of a meeting of experts from Hong Kong, convened to review the evidence and provide guidance on the use of local ablative therapies (LATs) for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC harboring actionable mutations. The discussion addressed key topics, including the definitions of oligometastatic and oligoprogressive disease, criteria for selecting patients for radiotherapy and other LAT modalities, optimal radiotherapy dosage, and the sequencing and timing of LATs in conjunction with targeted molecular therapies. Guidance was also developed regarding whether to pause or continue systemic treatments during LAT, and the evidence supporting emerging biomarkers in this context was reviewed. Consensus statements were formulated using a modified Delphi approach, and several case examples were presented to illustrate the application of these recommendations in clinical management. The consensus statements from this meeting could provide an important basis for tailoring treatment for patients with NSCLC who have actionable mutations, as well as pointing out key areas to explore in upcoming research.

articles.title: Sexual exposure to HIV-1 is associated with lower systemic inflammation and differential activation of CD8+, CD4+, and regulatory T cells in blood and genital mucosa.
articles.abstract: A continued challenge for the development of efficacious HIV-1 vaccines is the lack of detailed knowledge of immune correlates of exposure or protection. Studies of HIV-1 exposed seronegative individuals (HESN) have been conducted in attempts to define host strategies to prevent infection upon natural HIV-1 exposure. Here, we utilized blood and cervicovaginal tissue samples collected from a cohort of heterosexual Kenyan couples wherein we compared HIV-seronegative women who were HIV-1-exposed or HIV-1-unexposed to characterize in detail the circulating and genital mucosal immune landscape associated with HIV-1 sexual exposure. HIV-1 exposure was associated with significantly lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in serum without significant differences in the cervicovaginal fluid. Further, sexual HIV-1 exposure was associated with lower frequencies of activated circulating CD8 T cells yet higher levels of circulating conventional CD4 T cells expressing Ki67, a marker of recent proliferation. Finally, we report that HIV-1 exposure was associated with higher expression of immunosuppressive, migration, and proliferation markers by cervical tissue and circulating regulatory T cells. Overall, we demonstrate signatures indicating the possibility of both active immune surveillance and immunoregulation in circulation and genital tissues upon sexual HIV-1 exposure and highlight the importance of investigating T cell responses across relevant anatomic sites.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Precision Nutrition: From Multi-Omics Integration to Personalized Dietary Interventions.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being investigated as a tool for precision nutrition because it can analyse heterogeneous dietary, clinical, physiological, behavioural, and molecular data. This narrative review critically examines how machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, natural language processing, explainable AI, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable technologies, and multi-omics approaches may support individualized nutritional assessment and decision-making. Particular attention is given to the distinction between predictive research, digital personalized nutrition, AI-enabled clinical interventions, and commercial nutrition platforms. Current evidence shows that personalized digital nutrition can improve selected dietary behaviours, while observational AI and multi-omics studies can predict substantial inter-individual variation in metabolic responses. Importantly, evidence that an AI-enabled intervention improves clinical outcomes is still limited and is concentrated in selected settings, including a multicentre randomized trial of an AI-based dietary management platform in adults with type 2 diabetes. Emerging technologies such as large language models, digital twins, federated learning, and adaptive algorithms remain promising but require prospective clinical validation. Major barriers include data quality, algorithmic bias, privacy, interoperability, model transparency, regulatory uncertainty, and limited external validation. Future research should prioritize pragmatic multicentre randomized trials, transparent reporting of model performance, independent validation, health-economic evaluation, and clinically meaningful outcomes. AI should therefore be considered an adjunct to evidence-based nutritional care rather than a replacement for professional clinical judgement. The review differs from technology-centred and methodology-focused reviews by explicitly linking AI modalities and multi-omics data with evidence maturity, clinical trial findings, implementation barriers, and the level of inference justified for each technology.

articles.title: Trajectory of influencing factors for post-thrombolysis early neurological deterioration and long-term functional recovery: insights from parallel explainable machine learning models.
articles.abstract: Ischemic brain injury after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) produces highly variable early deterioration and later disability, yet most prognostic models treat risk as a static, admission-only construct. This leaves the temporal reorganization of influencing factors poorly defined. In 609 consecutive patients treated with IVT alone within 4.5 h of last known well, we built three parallel explainable machine-learning models for 24-hour early neurological deterioration (END), poor function at 1 week, and poor function at 3 months. Stage-specific predictor sets followed the information actually available at each decision point, while an identical analytical pipeline (multi-method feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and synthetic minority oversampling) kept the comparisons methodologically aligned. Cross-validated areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.742, 0.831 and 0.914. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis showed a coherent trajectory after ischemic injury: metabolic load and early infarct burden (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score) dominated the hyperacute window; baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score and intracranial hemorrhage rose in the subacute window; discharge disposition, age and large-vessel occlusion dominated chronic outcome. A glucose × stroke-severity interaction further indicated that metabolic stress is not uniform across severity strata. These results provide a computational description of how clinically measurable factors re-weight over time after reperfusion, and they support phase-specific management of post-ischemic recovery.

articles.title: Irisin alleviates hepatic glucolipid disorders in MASLD by activating PHF8-dependent IGF1 transcription to inhibit endoplasmic reticulum stress.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a global health burden with limited therapeutic options. Irisin has been shown to alleviate MASLD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: Free fatty acid (FFA)-treated HepG2 cells and high-fat diet (HFD)-fed mice were used as MASLD models. Endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) markers (GRP78, PERK, p-PERK, CHOP) were examined. Integrative bioinformatic analysis of transcriptomic datasets (GSE63067, GSE89632, GSE232188) identified PHF8 as a candidate mediator. PHF8 function was assessed via overexpression of wild-type or catalytically inactive H283A mutant, as well as knockdown approaches. IGF1 was identified as a downstream target and validated via knockdown rescue experiments. ChIP-qPCR detected histone methylation at the IGF1 promoter. In vivo, AAV-mediated hepatic PHF8 overexpression was performed to evaluate therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: In vitro, irisin rescued FFA-impaired HepG2 cells, reduced lipid loading and triglyceride (TG)/total cholesterol (TC), and suppressed ERS and apoptosis; CCT020312 reversed these benefits. In HFD-fed mice, irisin alleviated hepatic steatosis and metabolic disturbance. Mechanistically, irisin restored FFA-suppressed PHF8 expression. Wild-type PHF8, but not H283A mutant, mimicked irisin's protective effects, whereas PHF8 knockdown abrogated them. IGF1 was identified as a transcriptional target of PHF8; IGF1 knockdown reversed PHF8-mediated ERS suppression. PHF8 activated IGF1 transcription by removing repressive H4K20me1 and H3K9me2 at its promoter. Hepatic PHF8 overexpression in vivo elevated circulating IGF1, suppressed ERS, and alleviated HFD-induced metabolic disorders.

CONCLUSION: Irisin promotes PHF8 expression, which reduces histone methylation at the IGF1 promoter, thereby increasing IGF1 level, suppressing ERS, and ameliorating HFD-induced hepatic glucolipid metabolic disorders.

articles.title: A Nucleolus-Penetrating Peptide Platform Enables DDX24 PET Imaging and Targeted Degradation Therapy for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), particularly the prevalent PSMA-negative subtype, lacks effective imaging-guided therapy options. Here, we report a nucleolus-penetrating peptide platform targeting DDX24, an oncogenic RNA helicase overexpressed in CRPC. Using bacterial surface display with iterative MACS/FACS screening, a leading DDX24-binding peptide (TDP-2, Kd = 17.63 ± 7.72μM) is identified. This single peptide is engineered into two imaging-guided therapy modalities: (1) a 64Cu-labeled PET probe ([64Cu]Cu-DOTA-TDP-2, >99% radiochemical purity) enabling specific, non-invasive imaging of DDX24-positive CRPC tumors in vivo (SUVmean 0.55 ± 0.08, T/M ratio 6.59 ± 0.71); and (2) a peptide-based PROTAC (TDP-2-PROTAC) that recruits the VHL E3 ligase to induce targeted, proteasome-dependent degradation of DDX24 (DC50 =49.1μM). TDP-2-PROTAC selectively suppresses CRPC cell proliferation (PC-3, DU145) while sparing non-malignant cells, and significantly inhibits tumor growth in xenograft models, accompanied by a reduction in tumoral [18F]FDG uptake and influx ([18F]FDG PET: SUV 1.29 ±0.45 vs 2.48 ± 0.24 in controls, p < 0.001). This integrated platform establishes DDX24 as a viable target for PSMA-negative CRPC and demonstrates the power of peptide-based tools for accessing intracellular oncogenic drivers.

articles.title: Association of premorbid TyG index with Sepsis-Associated acute kidney injury and 60-Day mortality in patients with or without Obesity: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Association of premorbid triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the risk and outcomes of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI).

METHODS: In this historical cohort study, we enrolled adult patients with sepsis at Mayo Clinic between 2018 and 2025. The primary outcome was SA-AKI incidence, and the secondary outcome was 60-day mortality. Logistic regression, Cox regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 3,960 patients with sepsis, 2,144 (54.1%) developed AKI, and 23.3% died within 60 days. Higher premorbid TyG index showed a statistically significant but modest association with SA-AKI (OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.07-1.32). This association was evident in non-obese patients but not in obese patients (P for interaction = 0.022). Higher TyG-BMI was associated with lower 60-day mortality, with each 10-unit increase corresponding to a 2.3% reduction in risk; however, this finding appeared to be predominantly driven by BMI and should be interpreted cautiously in light of the obesity paradox. Severe AKI remained independently associated with increased 60-day mortality (HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.14-1.54).

CONCLUSIONS: A higher premorbid TyG index is associated with increased SA-AKI risk, particularly among non-obese patients with sepsis. The noted association was largely driven by BMI, and severe AKI remained a strong predictor of death.

articles.title: Brain volumes and their relationship with cerebral microbleeds and cognition in middle-aged adults with type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is associated with brain volumetric alterations, cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and cognitive deficits. We examined brain volumes and their direct and combined associations with CMBs on cognitive performance in T1D.

METHODS: Adults with T1D (n = 163; age 46 ± 8 years; diabetes duration 31 ± 10 years; 53% women) and 48 matched controls underwent brain MRI and clinical and neuropsychological evaluations. Volumetric MRI measures included total brain (TBV) and white matter volume (WMV), and volumes of cortex, thalamus, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens, and choroid plexus.

RESULTS: Individuals with T1D had smaller TBV, WMV, cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens volumes, and larger choroid plexus, than controls (Cohen's d = 0.39-0.54). Those with T1D and ≥3 CMBs (n = 25) had smaller TBV, WMV, and cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens than those with 0-2 CMBs (n = 138; Cohen's d = 0.54-0.92). Brain volumes were not directly linked to cognition, but CMB burden moderated the associations between TBV, WMV, nucleus accumbens, and choroid plexus and cognitive performance (standardized β: -0.61-(-0.51) and 0.54-0.75, pFDR = 0.006-0.048).

CONCLUSIONS: Middle-aged individuals with T1D showed smaller global and regional brain volumes and larger choroid plexus than healthy controls. Individuals with CMB burden showed associations between brain volumetric alterations and cognitive deficits.

articles.title: Right-Dosing, Not Underdosing: Rethinking Microdosing in Endocrinology.
articles.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists

articles.title: Proteome- and phenome-wide studies identify circulating protein drivers of kidney diseases.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (PWMR) provides a genetic framework to identify circulating proteins causally implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and prioritize them for drug discovery. However, the diverse etiologies of CKD and clinical presentations make it difficult to translate proteomic findings into actionable targets. Here, we studied protein associations with longitudinal kidney outcomes, CKD subtypes, and phenome-wide traits to identify proteins that are causally relevant and pharmacologically actionable.

METHODS: We performed a PWMR study using cis-pQTLs as genetic instruments for 2807 circulating proteins from four proteogenomic cohorts (ARIC, Fenland, deCODE, and UK Biobank) and tested their effects across four kidney outcomes (eGFR, incident CKD, incident kidney failure, annualized eGFR slope) in up to 464,631 of Million Veteran Program participants. Proteins meeting proteome-wide significance underwent sensitivity testing, Bayesian colocalization, and external replication in CKDGen Consortium information. The same instruments were re-tested against nine diagnosis code-defined CKD subtypes using genome wide association studies meta-analysis across the Million Veteran Program participants, UK Biobank, and FinnGen, and against 1020 phecodes to distinguish kidney-restricted from systemic effects. Druggability was evaluated using ChEMBL annotations layered onto high-confidence STRING protein-protein interaction networks.

RESULTS: We identified 93 proteins with proteome-wide significance, and twelve remained robust across sensitivity testing (ANGPTL3, FAM213A, GCKR, GSTA1, IDI2, INHBA, INHBC, MANBA, MICB, MST1, NRG4, UMOD). Forty-seven proteins mapped to at least one of nine kidney disease subtypes, with distinct patterns across diabetic, hypertensive, and glomerular kidney diseases. Phenome-wide testing separated seven proteins with kidney-restricted associations from those with broader systemic effects. Thirty-four proteins were pharmacologic targets, nominating candidates such as IL-1 pathway blockade for diabetic kidney disease and ANGPTL3 inhibition for podocyte protection.

CONCLUSIONS: Our integrative PWMR framework resolves circulating protein targets across CKD etiologies, separates kidney-restricted from systemic effects, and delivers actionable targets that may accelerate therapeutic innovation for CKD. About one-third of the 93 proteins could be targeted with existing or investigational medications.

articles.title: Characterization of the Urine Proteome Using the Olink Explore 3072 Platform.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urinary proteins are valuable biomarkers for physiological processes and early detection/monitoring of kidney diseases. However, comprehensive quantification and characterization of the urine proteome using a high-throughput platform remains limited.

METHODS: Using the affinity-based Olink Explore 3072 proteomics assay, we quantified 2868 proteins in urine samples from 1268 participants of the German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study.

RESULTS: Protein detectability in urine, defined as the percentage of samples with measurements above the limit of detection, showed a bimodal distribution: 659 (23%) proteins had high (over 80%) and 1336 proteins (47%) had low (under 20%) detectability, with stable detectability across strata of albuminuria and kidney function. More than 95% of highly detectable proteins had previously been identified in urine by mass spectrometry. Highly detectable proteins were enriched for extracellular, exosomal, and cell surface localization, and for expression in hepatocytes, immune cells and kidney proximal tubule cells. Comparison with plasma detectability from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project identified proteins of likely kidney origin, including LRP2 (megalin) and NPHS2 (podocin). In a multivariable adjusted model of 13 clinical variables, albuminuria and an individual's sex showed significant associations with 779 and 670 proteins, respectively. Specific chronic kidney disease etiologies showed associations with 105 proteins, although etiology explained only a small proportion of protein variance. Correlation analysis revealed biologically meaningful protein clusters reflecting shared cellular compartments, tissue of origin, and molecular interactions.

CONCLUSIONS: Large-scale urine proteomic profiling using a high-multiplex affinity-based platform captures biologically meaningful molecular variation associated with clinical variables and chronic kidney disease, providing a valuable resource for biomarker discovery and future targeted studies.

articles.title: Transfer RNA-derived small RNA-1:34-Asp-GTC-2 promotes sepsis-associated acute kidney injury by regulating kinase SNRK/transcription factor NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a severe condition characterized by dysregulated inflammatory responses. Transfer RNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs), including transfer RNA-derived fragments (tRFs) and transfer RNA halves (tiRNAs), have emerged as regulators of pathological processes in the kidney. However, their roles in SA-AKI remain unclear.

METHODS: To help define this, tRF and tiRNA sequencing was conducted to screen dysregulated tsRNAs in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced SA-AKI in male C57BL/6J mouse kidneys. tiRNA-1:34-Asp-GTC-2 (tiRNA-Asp) was identified as a potential tsRNA candidate. Its expression was quantified using qRT-PCR and its localization was examined by fluorescence in situ hybridization. tiRNA-Asp was silenced in vivo using the antagomir to assess its function in LPS-induced AKI. The biodistribution of Cy7-labeled tiRNA-Asp antagomir was assessed by in vivo and ex vivo fluorescence imaging. Mouse kidney tubular epithelial cells were transfected with tiRNA-Asp mimics or inhibitors to evaluate its pro-inflammatory effects. RNA-seq, dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA pulldown assays, and rescue experiments were performed to identify downstream targets and elucidate the mechanisms of tiRNA-Asp.

RESULTS: tiRNA-Asp showed the most pronounced upregulation in SA-AKI kidneys and was predominantly localized in tubular epithelial cells. It was consistently upregulated across different AKI models. In vivo inhibition of tiRNA-Asp with antagomir alleviated LPS- and ischemia-induced inflammatory responses and kidney injury while suppressing nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) activation. In kidney tubular epithelial cells, tiRNA-Asp overexpression promoted NF-κB activity and enhanced inflammatory cytokine expression, whereas tiRNA-Asp knockdown suppressed NF-κB activation and reduced cytokine production. Mechanistically, sucrose nonfermenting-related kinase (SNRK), a key anti-inflammatory regulator, was identified as a direct target of tiRNA-Asp. tiRNA-Asp enhanced NF-κB activation and inflammatory responses by downregulating SNRK expression. Angiogenin and ribonuclease inhibitor 1 are associated with tiRNA-Asp biogenesis during sepsis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study reveals a novel pro-inflammatory tiRNA involved in the pathogenesis of SA-AKI and demonstrates that the tiRNA-Asp/SNRK/NF-κB pathway may represent a potential therapeutic target for sepsis-induced inflammation and AKI.

articles.title: Prophylactic Intraoperative Norepinephrine Infusion during Major Noncardiac Surgery: A Systematic Review and GRADE assessed Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prophylactic norepinephrine infusion has gained increasing attention to prevent intraoperative hypotension during major non-cardiac surgery, but its effect on haemodynamic stability, tissue perfusion, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes remains uncertain.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched through May 9, 2026 for randomised trials comparing prophylactic norepinephrine with standard reactive management. Outcomes included change in serum lactate, haemodynamic measures, fluid administration, and postoperative outcomes, including complications and mortality. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) and the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, respectively. Sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed.

RESULTS: Eleven trials (1688 patients) were included. Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a lower rise in lactate (mean difference (MD) -0.13 mmol/L, 95% CI -0.25 to -0.01; P = 0.03; I²=67.2%), higher post-induction mean arterial pressure (MD 10.79 mmHg, 95% CI 5.53 to 16.04; P < 0.01; I²=95.3%), higher postoperative mean arterial pressure (MD 2.78 mmHg, 95% CI 0.63 to 4.92; P = 0.01; I²=69.8%). Prophylactic norepinephrine use was associated with lower crystalloid administration (MD-548.22 mL, 95% CI -1087.16 to -9.28, P = 0.05, I²=99%) although substantial heterogeneity and protocol-driven differences limit interpretation. Exploratory analyses suggested lower incidences of myocardial infarction (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-0.98), pneumonia (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.36-0.95), and 30 day-surgical site infection (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.41-0.97). No statistically significant differences were demonstrated for acute kidney injury, atelectasis, length of stay, or mortality. Certainty of evidence was low for most outcomes. TSA indicated insufficient evidence to establish a definitive treatment effect.

CONCLUSIONS: Prophylactic norepinephrine was associated with a statistically significant but small reduction in intraoperative lactate rise, higher post-induction and post-operative mean arterial pressures. Postoperative complication findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in adequately powered randomised trials.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO (CRD420261345140).

articles.title: Prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score models II and 3 in critical care: a systematic review and meta-analysis of external validation studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic performance of the Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) models has not been thoroughly investigated. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed SAPS mortality prediction metrics across diverse intensive care unit (ICU) populations worldwide.

METHODS: PubMed and Scopus were queried for external validations of SAPS in ICU settings. The "CHARMS" and "PROBAST" tools were applied for data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment, respectively. C-statistics and observed-to-expected ratios were summarised using random-effects models. Heterogeneity sources were explored using meta-regression. Evidence certainty was evaluated using the "GRADE" approach. PROSPERO registration CRD42023446721.

RESULTS: Ninety studies (89 articles) were reviewed, totalling 565,994 ICU patients across 87 countries, and validating the SAPS II (n = 35), SAPS 3 global (n = 37), and/or SAPS 3 region-specific (n = 28) models. Endpoints were in-hospital (n = 70), in-ICU (n = 16), and/or 28/30-day mortality (n = 12). Nine studies performed recalibrations of SAPS II and 7 of SAPS 3. The meta-analyses provided high-certainty evidence of excellent discriminatory ability across all SAPS models in predicting in-hospital mortality, whereas data on unsatisfactory overall calibration were graded as low certainty. Successful recalibration was graded as high certainty for SAPS II and moderate certainty for SAPS 3. For ICU and 28/30-day mortality, the evidence was low to very low certainty for all SAPS models. Five decision curve analyses were conducted in three studies, all yielding positive net benefit across meaningful risk thresholds.

CONCLUSIONS: SAPS models remain reliable as mortality risk-ranking tools in critical care. With adequate sample sizes, local recalibrations and dynamic updating of in-hospital mortality predictions are essential to ensure clinical utility.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42023446721.

articles.title: Scoping review on dosing of anaesthetic and perioperative drugs in patients with obesity: which body weight for which molecule.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prevalence of obesity is rising. Patients with obesity are increasingly exposed to anaesthesia, critical care, and perioperative pharmacotherapy. Obesity alters drug pharmacokinetics in a non-linear, drug-specific manner, so that simply scaling doses to total body weight (TBW) exposes patients to overdose or underdose. A recurring clinical question is therefore: which body weight descriptor should be used for which molecule?

METHODS: This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews. We synthesized pharmacokinetic evidence, recent meta-analyses, and French and European guidelines on dose adjustment in adults with obesity for five drug classes of anaesthesia and critical care: hypnotics, opioids, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBA), perioperative antibiotics, and non-opioid analgesics. We summarised the recommended dosing weight for each molecule in a table and a figure.

RESULTS: No single weight descriptor applies. Lipophilic induction agents (propofol), most opioids (alfentanil, fentanyl, sufentanil), and non-depolarising NMBA are best dosed on lean or ideal body weight, whereas succinylcholine, neuromuscular reversal, and aminoglycosides use total or adjusted body weight. Maintenance of hypnosis and pain management in the post-anaesthesia care unit are titrated to monitored effect. Cephalosporin-based antibiotic prophylaxis relies on fixed doses (e.g., cefazolin 2 g) up to high body mass index values due to their hydrophilic properties. Paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are given at standard doses and never scaled to TBW. Findings are consolidated in a single bedside reference table.

CONCLUSION: Dosing in obesity must be molecule-specific, guided by the relevant weight descriptor and by intraoperative monitoring rather than by TBW alone.

articles.title: Severe Puumala virus infection and secondary haemophagocytic syndrome: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

articles.title: Early Posaconazole Step-Down After 1 Week of Initial Combination Therapy Versus 4-Week Liposomal Amphotericin B Monotherapy for Pulmonary Mucormycosis: An Open-Label Randomized Trial.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Liposomal amphotericin B (LAMB) is recommended as first-line therapy for pulmonary mucormycosis (PM). However, the optimal duration of intravenous LAMB before transition to oral step-down therapy is uncertain. We evaluated an early step-down strategy of oral posaconazole in an exploratory randomized trial.

METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, open-label, exploratory randomized trial conducted at a tertiary center, adults with suspected PM were randomized pending diagnostic confirmation. The prespecified modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population included participants with proven/probable PM confirmed within 4 working days of randomization. Participants received either LAMB 5 mg/kg/day for four weeks (4-week LAMB arm) or LAMB plus oral posaconazole (delayed-release tablets) for one week followed by 3 weeks of posaconazole alone (early-step-down arm). Maintenance posaconazole was planned thereafter in both groups. The primary outcome was treatment success at six weeks (complete/partial clinico-radiologic response), assessed by a multidisciplinary panel. Secondary outcomes included 12-week treatment success, 90-day mortality, and treatment-emergent adverse events. Risk differences (RDs) are reported as early-step-down minus 4-week LAMB.

RESULTS: Of the 82 randomized participants, 72 comprised the mITT population (4-week LAMB, n=34; early-step-down, n=38). All participants had diabetes mellitus. At six weeks, treatment success occurred in 20/38 (52.6%) participants in the early-step-down arm and 16/34 (47.1%) in the 4-week LAMB group (RD, 5.6% [95% CI, -20.3% to 31.5%]). Twelve-week treatment success was 62.2% vs. 47·1% (RD, 15.1% [95% CI, -10.6% to 40.9%]), and 90-day mortality was 35.1% vs. 44·1% (RD, -9% [95% CI, -34.5% to 16.5%]) with the early-step-down and 4-week LAMB arms, respectively. Thrombophlebitis occurred in 26.3% versus 50.0% (RD, -23.7% [95% CI, -48.3% to 1.0%]).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory trial of diabetes-associated PM, early posaconazole step-down after 1 week of combination therapy showed numerically higher treatment success, but estimates were imprecise and compatible with meaningful benefit or harm. A larger multicenter trial is warranted.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: clinicaltrials.gov: NCT05468372.

articles.title: [Urinary incontinence as a factor for poor functional prognosis in stroke patients: a retrospective observational study].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urinary incontinence (UI) has been associated with greater stroke severity and poorer functional outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: To analyse the association between UI and functional outcomes, length of hospital stay, and discharge destination in stroke patients admitted to a neurological rehabilitation unit, and to describe UI symptom severity and its impact on daily life.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective observational study of 97 patients with stroke was conducted. The Barthel Index at admission and discharge, length of hospital stay, and discharge destination were recorded. In patients with UI, its impact was assessed using the International Consultation on Incontinence Questionnaire-Short Form (ICIQ-SF). The association between UI and Barthel index at discharge was analysed using linear regression adjusted for baseline Barthel Index score, sex, and stroke severity.

RESULTS: Of the 97 patients included, 27 (27.8%) had UI. Mean hospital stay was longer in patients with UI than in those without UI (22.8 vs. 14 days; p = 0.005). Referral to intermediate care facilities was more frequent among patients with UI (55.6% vs. 17.1%). The mean ICIQ-SF score was 13 (SD 5.2), indicating substantial symptom burden. In 44% of patients with UI, incontinence predated the stroke. After adjustment, the association between UI and the Barthel Index score at discharge was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: UI was associated with longer hospital stays and more frequent referral to intermediate care facilities. The association with functional status at discharge was no longer significant after adjustment. These findings do not establish UI as an independent prognostic factor for functional recovery but highlight its clinical relevance in post-stroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Analysis of single-cell sequencing data reveals metabolic reprogramming characterized by high PDK4 expression in non-inflammatory myocardial fibrosis.
articles.journal: Translational research : the journal of laboratory and clinical medicine
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) is a metabolic disorder that poses a notable threat to human health, with post-MI heart failure (HF) markedly affecting patient prognosis. The overactivation of inflammation and fibrosis serves an important role in the progression of post-MI HF; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. The present study aimed to investigate the associations among metabolic reprogramming, inflammation and fibrosis after MI. By integrating single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data from MI and dilated cardiomyopathy, a common metabolic feature, glycolysis, was identified. This feature was shared by cardiomyocytes and monocytes in myocardial infarction and was specifically localized to the peri-infarct region. Pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 was identified as a core gene linking metabolic reprogramming to fibrosis. A mouse model of MI was established by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending coronary artery. PDK4 knockout was applied to evaluate its role in post-infarction fibrotic remodeling. Furthermore, the results of the present study revealed a cross-cellular metabolic reprogramming process mediating chronic inflammatory cell interactions. In conclusion, the findings of the present study suggested that targeting metabolic reprogramming may offer a promising strategy for preventing inflammation and fibrosis to mitigate post-MI HF.

articles.title: Prognostic Utility of the Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis in Infants: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC) score was developed in adults, but its prognostic utility in children remains uncertain. This study evaluated the conventional admission LRINEC threshold of ≥6 for predicting adverse clinical outcomes in infants with necrotizing fasciitis.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included 93 infants with clinically diagnosed necrotizing fasciitis at a tertiary pediatric surgical center between February 2021 and August 2023. Admission LRINEC scores were categorized as <6 or ≥6. The primary endpoint was a composite of unplanned repeat surgical debridement for persistent or progressive infection, hospitalization exceeding 21 days, worsening sepsis, or in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: The mean age was 187.9 ± 96.6 days. Composite adverse outcomes occurred in 77 infants (82.8%), and seven (7.5%) died. Unplanned repeat debridement was required in 43 patients (46.2%). Among infants with LRINEC ≥6, 19/20 (95.0%) experienced an adverse outcome, compared with 58/73 (79.5%) with LRINEC <6. Sensitivity was 24.7% (95% CI, 16.4%-35.4%) and specificity was 93.8% (95% CI, 71.7%-98.9%). Positive and negative predictive values were 95.0% and 20.5%, respectively. The association was not statistically significant (risk ratio, 1.20; 95% CI, 0.95-1.40; P = 0.178). Overall, 75.3% of adverse outcomes occurred among infants with LRINEC <6.

CONCLUSIONS: The conventional LRINEC threshold demonstrated poor sensitivity for adverse clinical outcomes in infants with necrotizing fasciitis. A low score should not provide prognostic reassurance or replace clinical assessment. Larger multicenter studies are needed to validate pediatric-specific prognostic tools.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III - Prospective observational cohort study.

articles.title: Natural Killer Cell Decrease at Admission Is Associated With Severe Outcomes in Hospitalized Influenza and COVID-19: An 8-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Natural killer (NK) cells are central effector cells in early innate antiviral immunity, but the clinical significance of NK cells at admission in hospitalized respiratory viral infection remains insufficiently defined.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with influenza (n=366) from December 2016 to June 2024, with a COVID-19 validation cohort (n=1,072) from December 2021 to June 2024. NK cell counts were measured in peripheral blood within 48 hours of admission and NK cell decrease was defined as below the hospital laboratory lower reference limit of 136 cells/μL. The associations between NK cells and clinical outcomes were assessed using logistic regression and restricted cubic splines (RCS).

RESULTS: NK cell decrease occurred in 48.6% (178/366) of the influenza cohort and 51.0% (547/1,072) of the COVID-19 cohort. After adjustment for age, sex, and comorbidities, NK cell decrease was associated with prolonged hospitalization (influenza: aOR 2.3 [1.5-3.5], P<0.001; COVID-19: aOR 1.7 [1.3-2.2], P<0.001), ICU admission (influenza: aOR 5.0 [3.0-8.3], P<0.001; COVID-19: aOR 3.2 [2.3-4.4], P<0.001), prolonged ICU stay (influenza: aOR 4.6 [2.4-9.0], P<0.001; COVID-19: aOR 3.3 [2.1-5.2], P<0.001), and death (influenza: aOR 2.5 [1.2-5.0], P=0.010; COVID-19: aOR 2.1 [1.4-3.0], P<0.001). RCS analyses showed non-linear associations in both cohorts (P for nonlinear <0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Decreased NK cell at admission was independently associated with severe clinical outcomes in hospitalized viral infections. NK cell counts may help identify patients who warrant closer clinical monitoring.

articles.title: Transforming Heart Failure Care through Lessons from Oncology.
Computational modeling of bioresorbable flow-diverting stents: Insights into approaches for coupling hemodynamics and material degradation.
articles.abstract: Bioresorbable flow diverters (BRFDs) represent an emerging treatment for intracranial aneurysms (IAs) that reduces complications associated with permanent flow diverters, as BRFDs-due to their temporary nature-restore native blood flow following degradation. The therapeutic efficacy of BRFDs depends on material degradation, hemodynamics, thrombosis, and endothelialization. To this end, computational models enabling a holistic evaluation of the interplay between these processes could provide considerable insight into optimizing BRFD designs. This review summarizes degradation modeling approaches for bioresorbable metals, including continuum damage mechanics (CDM), mechanochemical phase-field, and reaction-diffusion models. It evaluates the suitability of each framework for integration with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for guiding BRFD design. CDM approaches focus on the degradation of mechanical integrity and do not directly consider electrochemical transport, whereas mechanochemical models account for mechanical, chemical, and electrochemical processes, providing detailed information on localized corrosion, albeit at a higher computational cost. Reaction-diffusion models are the most practical option for coupling with CFD, offering a balance between accuracy in describing key mechanisms and computational feasibility, although the most suitable approach ultimately depends on how each metal degrades. Critical gaps in BRFD models include the limited modeling of iron, zinc, and molybdenum, and specific aspects of blood chemistry. Additionally, since no standardized validation protocol currently exists for computational models of BRFDs, we recommend a staged pathway: a framework integrating material degradation and hemodynamics and considering thrombosis and endothelialization, validated against in vitro and/or in vivo data, will be essential for advancing the design and therapeutic efficacy assessment of BRFDs. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Bioresorbable flow diverters (BRFDs), when compared to permanent flow diverters, allow mitigation of long-term complications in treating intracranial aneurysms, but their development remains limited by an incomplete understanding of the interaction between material degradation, blood flow, and biological responses such as thrombosis and aneurysm healing. The design choices of FDs ultimately depend on this interplay, yet no computational framework currently exists to guide it. This review is the first of its kind to systematically evaluate the use of degradation models for coupling with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to elucidate physiologically relevant information of aneurysm healing with BRFDs. Coupling these frameworks provides a practical guide to accelerate the translation of bioresorbable devices from conceptualization, design, and development to clinical use.

articles.title: Isolated Tibial and Both Component Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty for Loosening Have Similar 10-Year Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Isolated tibial revisions are relatively uncommon, and data comparing them to both component revision total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is limited. The purpose of this study was to review implant survivorship, radiographic, and clinical outcomes after isolated tibial revision and compare to a matched cohort of both component revision TKAs.

METHODS: We identified 112 cases of isolated tibial revision TKAs at a single tertiary care academic center from 2000 to 2022. All were performed for tibial component aseptic loosening. Metaphyseal fixation was utilized in 53%. There were 74 cases that were propensity-score-matched 1:1 to 74 both-component revision TKAs based on surgical indication, age, sex, surgical year, and American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA) Classification. The patient's mean age was 66 years, 63% were women, and their mean body mass index was 35. The mean follow-up was seven years (range, 2 to 20).

RESULTS: After isolated tibial revision, the 10-year survivorship free from re-revision of the tibial component for aseptic loosening, re-revision for instability, and any re-revision was 84, 96, and 82%, respectively. The most common indications for re-revision were infection (n = 6), aseptic loosening of both the femur and tibia (n = 2), aseptic loosening of the tibial component only (n = 2), and instability (n = 2). There were two of the four tibial components re-revised that had metaphyseal fixation. The 10-year survivorship free from any reoperation was 75%. In the matched cohort analysis, there were no differences in 10-year survivorship free from re-revision of the tibial component for aseptic loosening (P = 0.31), any re-revision (P = 0.32), or any reoperation (P = 0.32). The mean Knee Society Score improved from 52 to 65 at the most recent follow-up (P = 0.71).

CONCLUSION: Isolated tibial revision for aseptic loosening demonstrated modest 10-year survivorship from any re-revision of 82%. There was no difference in 10-year survivorship between isolated tibial revision and both-component revision, as infection was the most common failure mode in all groups.

articles.title: Certain Second-Generation Antipsychotics Increase Risk of Complications Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Certain second-generation antipsychotics (SGAs) are increasingly prescribed for both psychiatric disorders and off-label indications. Through dopaminergic and serotonergic pathway inhibition, SGAs may impair bone remodeling, and antipsychotic-induced hyperprolactinemia has been associated with increased fracture risk. Despite these associations, the impact of SGA use on total hip arthroplasty (THA) outcomes remains unclear. This study evaluated postoperative outcomes following THA in patients receiving SGAs.

METHODS: A large national database was queried for adults undergoing primary THA between 2006 and 2024. Patients who had SGA exposure within one year before surgery were compared with non-users after propensity-score matching for demographics, comorbidities, body mass index, and medication use. After matching, 10,818 patients were included (5,409 per cohort). The primary outcome was revision THA within two years. The secondary outcomes included periprosthetic fracture (PPF), surgical site infection (SSI), and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: The SGA exposure was associated with higher risks of revision THA (relative risk (RR) 1.6, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.3 to 2.0), PPF (RR 2.0, 95% CI 1.5 to 2.7), SSI (RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.1 to 1.8), and all-cause mortality (RR 2.0, 95% CI 1.6 to 2.5) within two years.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SGA use was associated with significantly higher risks of revision arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, surgical site infection, and mortality after THA. These findings support closer perioperative optimization, medication review, and postoperative surveillance in patients receiving SGAs.

articles.title: Patient, caregiver, and other knowledge user engagement in research processes within consensus-building healthcare initiatives: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Knowledge user engagement in health research can lead to more meaningful and relevant outcomes. However, questions remain on how to effectively incorporate knowledge user engagement in healthcare research using consensus-building methods, despite the rising use of engagement in recent years. To identify and synthesize how knowledge users are engaged in the research processes of healthcare studies using consensus-building methods.

STUDY DESIGN AND SETTING: Using the Joanna Briggs Institute scoping review methodology, we conducted a literature search using MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO from inception to December 2024. We also conducted a grey literature search using relevant repositories from inception to May 2025. Two researchers screened all titles/abstracts and full-text articles. Studies using consensus-building methodologies within the healthcare context that also used knowledge user engagement strategies in the research process were included. Data were extracted in duplicate and analyzed quantitatively and qualitatively.

RESULTS: This scoping review included 177 articles. Knowledge user engagement in the research processes within consensus-building in healthcare research has been increasing steadily since 2014, often involving the engagement of multiple knowledge user groups. Of the included studies, 80 specified the use of a knowledge user engagement approach. Authors' reporting of engagement was inconsistent, varying in both terminology and the level of detail provided. Engagement activities were most common during recruitment and data collection, and least common during implementation. Facilitators of engagement included providing role clarity, addressing ethical concerns such as power imbalances, and familiarizing knowledge users with the research process. Barriers included limited resources, time constraints, and logistical hurdles. Researchers reported that engagement enhanced the rigor, validity, and relevance of study findings.

CONCLUSION: While knowledge user engagement in the research processes of healthcare studies using consensus-building methods is increasing, the engagement activities often remain underreported and limited to specific research phases, such as recruitment and data collection. Further research is required to address these gaps and understand how to broaden the scope of knowledge user engagement in health research.

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Knowledge user engagement in health research is important for producing meaningful research outcomes. Knowledge users are people who may use, apply, or be affected by research findings, such as patients, caregivers, healthcare providers, researchers, and decision-makers. Although knowledge user engagement in research has increased, we do not know enough about how knowledge users are involved in research studies that use consensus-building methods, such as Delphi surveys. We reviewed published healthcare studies that used consensus-building methods and involved knowledge users in the research process. We identified 177 articles. Knowledge user engagement became more common after 2014, and many studies involved engagement with more than one type of knowledge user. However, only about half of the studies clearly described how engagement was carried out, and reporting was often inconsistent. Knowledge users were most often involved in recruitment and data collection. Authors reported that clearly defined roles, addressing ethical concerns, and educating knowledge users about the research process supported meaningful engagement, while limited resources, lack of time, and logistical challenges were reported as barriers. Overall, knowledge user engagement in studies using consensus-building methods is often poorly described and tends to occur during only certain stages of the research process. More research is needed to better understand how to engage knowledge users in all aspects of the research process.

articles.title: The Completeness of Surgery Index (CoSI) in Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps: A Multi-Institutional Study.
articles.journal: Annals of allergy, asthma & immunology : official publication of the American College of Allergy, Asthma, & Immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Completion of Surgery Index (CoSI) is a CT-based scoring system designed to identify patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) who have had previously incomplete endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Single-institution studies have shown that a CoSI <70, reflecting incomplete prior surgery, is associated with greater improvement in sino-nasal outcome test (SNOT-22) and asthma control following high-quality revision surgery.

OBJECTIVE: To validate CoSI in a large multi-institutional CRSwNP cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed CRSwNP patients who underwent revision ESS across eight tertiary care centers from 2022 to 2024. Demographic, clinical, and treatment-related data were collected, including preoperative CoSI scores, timing of treatment, and pre- and postoperative SNOT-22 scores.

RESULTS: 160 subjects undergoing revision ESS for CRSwNP were included. Patients with incomplete prior surgery (CoSI <70) experienced significantly greater postoperative improvement in SNOT-22 scores (6-24 months) than patients with CoSI ≥70 (35.2 ± 17.8 vs 18.7 ± 18.6 points; p<0.001).
