This association remained significant after adjustment for demographic factors, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease status, asthma, number of prior ESS, biologic use, and baseline SNOT-22 score. Nonlinear and threshold analyses were consistent with a clinically relevant transition near the CoSI 70 threshold.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative CoSI is an independent predictor of symptomatic improvement after revision ESS in CRSwNP. A CoSI <70 identifies patients who are most likely to benefit from complete revision surgery. In the biologic era, inadequate prior surgery remains an important and correctable contributor to persistent symptom burden in CRSwNP.

articles.title: Adjunct Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis following Endovascular Thrombectomy in Different Patient Subgroups: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Ten Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite successful endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), many patients with acute ischemic stroke fail to achieve excellent functional outcome. We evaluated whether adjunct intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) improves this outcome and whether patient subgroups modify its effect.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive IAT following EVT with EVT alone. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days. Subgroup analyses were stratified by bridging intravenous thrombolysis (IVT), thrombolytic agent, occlusion site, and Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (TICI) reperfusion grade.

RESULTS: Ten RCTs comprising 2,988 randomized participants were included, of whom 2,958 contributed to the primary-outcome analysis. Excellent functional outcome occurred in 44.9% of patients receiving adjunctive IAT and 36.9% receiving EVT alone (RR 1.22, 95% CI 1.10-1.35). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in functional independence, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or mortality. However, these confidence intervals did not exclude clinically important harm. Formal interaction tests did not detect effect modification by bridging IVT status, thrombolytic agent (alteplase or tenecteplase), or TICI reperfusion grade. The benefit was statistically significant in anterior but not in posterior circulation occlusion, although the test for subgroup interaction was not significant.

DISCUSSION: Adjunctive IAT improved excellent functional outcome. However, the safety estimates were imprecise, and the optimal patient population requires further investigation.

articles.title: Safety and Feasibility of Percutaneous Microwave Ablation of Liver Tumors in Patients with Presumed Colonized Biliary Systems: A Single-Institution Retrospective Study.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of percutaneous microwave ablation of liver tumors in patients with prior biliary intervention. We hypothesized that microwave ablation could be performed in this population with an acceptable rate of infectious adverse events (AEs), despite the loss of a competent sphincter of Oddi.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study examined all patients at a single institution who underwent liver microwave ablation following a prior biliary intervention resulting in an incompetent or absent sphincter of Oddi. Baseline patient and procedure characteristics, and the prevalence and management of any subsequent infectious AEs, were reviewed.

RESULTS: A total of 44 microwave ablation sessions were performed in 24 patients targeting 64 lesions. The technical success rate was 100%. Postprocedural oral antibiotics were prescribed after 36 of 44 sessions. Four hepatic abscesses and one case of cholangitic sepsis occurred after ablation, representing 11.4% of ablation sessions (5 of 44) and 20.8% of patients (5 of 24). All infections were successfully treated. Median overall survival for the entire cohort was 33.5 months. No patient or procedure factor was significantly associated with infectious AEs. Streptococcus viridans, a rarely reported organism in this setting, was isolated from 60% (3 of 5) of patients who developed infectious AEs.

CONCLUSION: Microwave ablation was feasible in patients with prior biliary intervention, with high technical success and a higher but acceptable risk of infectious AEs, all of which were successfully treated. These findings support microwave ablation as a valuable modality in this patient population.

articles.title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

METHODS: A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).

RESULTS: One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).

CONCLUSION: In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.

articles.title: Revascularisation Outcomes in Symptomatic Elderly Nonagenarians with Peripheral Arterial Disease: The ROSEPAD International Registry.
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Data regarding the outcomes of revascularisation for symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD) in nonagenarians are scarce, limited by short follow up periods and confounded by the competing risk of death. This multicentre, retrospective analysis of nonagenarians who underwent invasive treatment for symptomatic PAD (Rutherford category 3 - 6) between December 2017 and December 2023 aimed to analyse the safety and efficacy, as well as short term and medium term revascularisation outcomes in selected nonagenarians with lower limb PAD.

METHODS: The primary endpoint was amputation free survival (AFS). Overall survival (OS), amputation free time, and freedom from any re-intervention of the index limb were additionally analysed. The cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention were also estimated, accounting for the competing risk of death.

RESULTS: A total of 566 patients were included. The majority underwent endovascular (81.6%), followed by open (10.6%), and hybrid revascularisation (7.8%). At 36 months, AFS was 21.4%, freedom from amputation was 85.7%, OS was 23.7%, and freedom from re-intervention was 73.7%. Men and history of coronary artery disease were associated with reduced AFS (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06 - 1.76; and hazard ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.2 - 1.99, respectively). Accounting for the competing risk of death, the cumulative incidence of major amputation was 7.3% (95% CI 5 - 9.7), 7.6% (95% CI 5.2 - 10), and 9.2% (95% CI 6.4 - 12), while the cumulative incidence of re-intervention was 14.6% (95% CI 11.4 - 17.9), 16.2% (95% CI 12.8 - 19.6), and 17.3% (95% CI 13.7 - 20.9), after 12, 24, and 36 months of follow up, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower limb revascularisation in selected nonagenarians with PAD was associated with a low cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention. However, a high overall mortality was observed after three years of follow up.

articles.title: Prospective Real-World Evaluation of Empagliflozin on Pulmonary Function and Exercise Capacity in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and are associated with increased morbidity, systemic inflammation, impaired exercise capacity, and reduced quality of life. Beyond glycemic control, empagliflozin has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and metabolic benefits that may potentially improve respiratory outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of empagliflozin on pulmonary function, inflammatory markers, exercise capacity, and COPD-related symptoms in patients with coexisting COPD and T2DM.

METHODS: A prospective, single-arm, before-and-after interventional study was conducted in 31 patients with coexisting COPD and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants received empagliflozin (10 mg/day) for three months in addition to their stable antidiabetic therapy. Pulmonary function, inflammatory markers, oxygen saturation, six-minute walk distance, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score, body weight, and HbA1c were evaluated at baseline and after treatment. Changes in outcome measures were compared between the two time points.

RESULTS: After three months of treatment, significant improvements were observed in FEV1 (P < 0.001) and MMEF (P = 0.019), whereas the change in FEV1/FVC ratio was not statistically significant (P = 0.106). CRP levels decreased significantly (P = 0.007), while ESR showed a non-significant reduction (P = 0.108). Significant improvements were also observed in SpO2 (P = 0.033), six-minute walk distance (P < 0.001), and CAT score (P < 0.001). Furthermore, empagliflozin significantly reduced body weight (P < 0.001) and HbA1c levels (P = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Empagliflozin therapy was associated with significant improvements in pulmonary function, exercise capacity, COPD symptom burden, inflammatory status, glycemic control, and body weight in patients with coexisting COPD and T2DM. These findings suggest that empagliflozin may provide clinically relevant benefits beyond glucose lowering and could represent a promising therapeutic option in this patient population. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Linked deletions in BCP and preS1 enhance HBV replication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) persists as genetically heterogeneous viral populations during chronic infection, yet how linked variants and complementation among coexisting genomes shape viral phenotypes remains unclear. The BCP is a critical transcriptional control element embedded within the X open reading frame and that the preS1 region, aside from encoding a protein domain, controls the transcription of the LHBs protein. We investigated the genomic linkage and cooperative effects of disease-associated BCP and 5' preS1 deletions during chronic HBV infection.

METHODS: Full-length HBV genomes from 246 treatment-naive patients with genotype B and C infection were analyzed by nanopore sequencing. Representative variants were investigated in HepG2 replication, NTCP-dependent infection and hydrodynamic-injection mouse models.

RESULTS: Linked BCP-5' preS1 deletions were identified exclusively in genotype C among 3,886 full-length HBV haplotypes and were more prevalent in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B (Phase II) than in HBeAg-positive chronic HBV infection (Phase I) (26% vs. 9%; p = 0.013). Carriers had higher HBV DNA levels than non-carriers (8.57 ± 0.21 vs. 8.36 ± 0.30 log10 IU/ml; p = 0.028). Linked deletions increased extracellular HBV DNA approximately 8.0-fold relative to WT in transfected HepG2 cells. This replication advantage resulted from complementary effects of increased pgRNA production by BCP deletions and enhanced reverse transcription by the mutant Polymerase generated by the 5' preS1 deletion. However, BCP deletions also impaired productive infection through HBx truncation. HBx supplied in trans restored infectivity in cells and rescued the linked-deletion phenotype in vivo.

CONCLUSIONS: Distantly linked BCP and 5' preS1 deletions cooperatively enhance HBV replication, revealing how linked variants within heterogeneous HBV populations cooperative to shape viral evolution, persistence, and pathogenicity.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: HBV mutation studies have traditionally focused on individual genomic regions. However, linked variants within heterogeneous viral populations may exhibit distinct biological and clinical effects. Our findings revealed that low abundance BCP-5' preS1 deletion haplotypes can acquire enhanced replication and infection capacity through intra-genomic cooperation and inter-genomic complementation, highlighting the potential clinical relevance of minority HBV variants. Full-length haplotype based-analyses may uncover previously unrecognized cooperative viral populations that influence persistence and treatment response, warranting validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.

articles.title: Postoperative Infections in Titanium Mesh Cranioplasty After Penetrating Brain Injury in a Conflict-Affected Setting: A Single-Institution Experience from Yemen.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Penetrating brain injury (PBI) causes severe tissue damage, contamination, and complex cranial defects. Evidence regarding cranioplasty outcomes after PBI remains limited, particularly in conflict-affected settings. We evaluated complications following titanium mesh cranioplasty for PBI, focusing on infection.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients undergoing titanium mesh cranioplasty for PBI at 48-Model Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen, between January 2021 and December 2024. Complications within 6 months were categorized as infectious, wound/implant-related, cerebrospinal fluid-related, neurological, or others. Rates are reported with 95% CIs. Associations with infection were explored using unadjusted Fisher's exact tests and RR; multivariable analysis was not feasible.

RESULTS: Seventy-one male patients (mean age, 26 ± 7 years) were included; 80% sustained gunshot wounds and 20% blast injuries. Complications occurred in 28% (95% CI, 19.0%-39.5%), with infection being the most common (13%), followed by persistent pain at the cranial defect site (10%). Staphylococcus aureus was isolated in seven infections and Pseudomonas aeruginosa in two. Infection occurred in 6/20 patients (30%) undergoing cranioplasty within 3 months versus 3/51 (6%) undergoing later surgery (RR, 5.10; 95% CI, 1.41-18.45; P = 0.012). Infection occurred in 5/5 patients with repeat cranial surgery before cranioplasty versus 4/66 without (RR, 16.50; 95% CI, 6.38-42.66; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Complications occurred in 28% of patients, with infection being the most frequent. Early cranioplasty and repeat cranial surgery were associated with infection in unadjusted analyses. Given the small number of infection events and potential confounding, these findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality or optimal surgical timing.

articles.title: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in individuals with and without impaired spirometry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease risk scores likely underestimate risk in individuals with impaired spirometry (airflow obstruction and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)).

RESEARCH QUESTION: How do risk scores perform between individuals with impaired and normal spirometry, and can they be improved by adding spirometry and dyspnea?

STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Ten-year incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) ie., myocardial infarction, stroke or death from coronary heart disease, from 7 US population-based cohorts was used for this analysis. The pooled cohorts' equations' (PCE) ability to predict MACE was compared between normal and impaired spirometry. Cox-models adding spirometry, dyspnea to PCE variables were evaluated for improvement in MACE prediction.

RESULTS: Among 26523 participants, those with impaired (N=7547) compared with normal (N=18932) spirometry had a higher incidence of MACE (14% vs 7%), hazard ratio 95%CI 1.25[1.17,1.34] adjusted for PCE variables. Discrimination using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)95%CI of the PCE for MACE was 0.792[0.780,0.803] vs 0.740[0.724,0.755] in normal vs impaired spirometry. Discrimination of MACE improved slightly by adding to the PCE: dyspnea plus 1)impaired spirometry 0.792[0.783,0.800], 2)PRISm, mild, moderate+ airflow obstruction 0.792[0.783,0.801], 3)FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC splines 0.793[0.784,0.802], compared with PCE variables 0.790[0.781,0.798]. The differences in AUC[95%CI] were: 1)0.002[0.001,0.003]p=0.002, 2)0.002[0.001,0.004]p=0.002, 3)0.003[0.002,0.005]p=0.0005 respectively. Among participants with impaired spirometry, only the model that added FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC continuous and dyspnea to the PCE showed improvement in AUC[95%CI], 0.750[0.735,0.765] vs 0.746[0.730,0.761] for PCE variables, difference of 0.004[0.001,0.008]p=0.008. There were no differences among models in calibration, sensitivity, specificity, overall performance, and after bootstrapping 1000 samples.

INTERPRETATION: Performance of the PCE was better among individuals with normal vs impaired spirometry, despite the latter having an excess burden of MACE. Adding spirometry and dyspnea to PCE variables showed a small statistically significant improvement in MACE prediction, which may not be meaningful clinically, so other risk factors should be considered.

articles.title: Associations of 6PPD-quinone exposure with macrophage-related LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 signatures in cardiometabolic multimorbidity.
articles.abstract: N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine quinone (6PPDQ) is a widespread tire-derived contaminant linked to cardiotoxicity and metabolic dysfunction, but its role in cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) remains unclear. Using chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, and ischemic heart disease as surrogate models, we combined network toxicology, multi-omics, machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to identify candidate common molecular drivers of 6PPDQ toxicity and CMM pathogenesis. LYN, SOCS3, and TIMP2 were consistently dysregulated across the three disorders. Docking and MD simulations indicated plausible 6PPDQ binding and relative conformational stability to all three proteins, without confirming actual binding or quantitative affinity ranking. Single-cell RNA-seq of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) and diabetic nephropathy (DN) showed predominant enrichment of these targets in macrophages, while CellChat predicted disease-associated communication patterns (macrophage-fibroblast in DCM; macrophage-endothelial in DN). Dose-response screening identified 20 ng/mL-an estimated high-exposure dose under heavy pollution-as the peak-effect concentration for target-gene modulation and M1-marker (iNOS, CD80) induction; it was used thereafter, although extrapolation to typical exposure warrants caution. At this concentration, 6PPDQ induced RAW264.7 morphological remodeling, intracellular ROS accumulation, and M1-like polarization, characterized by upregulation of iNOS, CD80, LYN, and SOCS3, repression of TIMP2, and elevated proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β). These findings associate 6PPDQ-induced macrophage inflammation and ECM-related changes with coordinated LYN/SOCS3/TIMP2 dysregulation, providing a framework linking 6PPDQ exposure to CMM-related inflammatory-fibrotic signatures.

articles.title: Biochemical and biophysical evaluation of the effects of phytochemicals isolated from Ziziphus mucronata on Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 70-1 (PfHsp70-1).
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Ongoing Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) resistance to first-line treatment threatens the livelihoods of people in Sub-Saharan African tropical regions, necessitating the development of new antimalarials. Ziziphus mucronata (Z. mucronata) is a native South African medicinal plant, used in Traditional Southern African Medicine to treat malaria. Its antimalarial properties have been validated, but its phytochemistry remains largely unexplored.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to isolate bioactive compounds from the dichloromethane bark extract of Z. mucronata and evaluate their inhibitory potential against Plasmodium falciparum Heat shock protein 70-1 (PfHsp70-1), a molecular chaperone whose inhibition has been linked to parasite death.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Isolation of compounds was done using bioassay-guided isolation, followed by structural elucidation and characterisation using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and distortionless enhancement by polarization transfer (DEPT-135). The antiplasmodial activity of the bioactive compounds was determined against the chloroquine-sensitive P. falciparum (NF54) strain to establish baseline efficacy, and the haemolytic activity was tested on non-parasitised human red blood cells. The binding potential of the compounds to PfHsp70-1's ATP-binding pocket was explored computationally using molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Their effects on the molecular chaperone's structure and function were assessed experimentally using far-ultraviolet (UV) circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy and a lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) aggregation assay.

RESULTS: Two primary active compounds, oleanolic acid (OA) and betulinic acid (BA), were successfully isolated. OA exhibited potent antimalarial activity (IC50 at 1.71 ± 0.19 μM) and low haemolysis (2.24 ± 1.05%) at 10 μM, whereas BA showed moderate activity (IC50 = 10.39 ± 4.10 μM) and negligible haemolysis (0.11 ± 0.12%) at 10 μM. OA (- 6. 346 kcal/mol) showed a high binding affinity for PfHsp70-1 compared to BA (- 5.720 kcal/mol). MD simulations revealed that both compounds form stable interactions with PfHsp70-1, although OA interacts with more residues compared to BA. Far-UV CD spectroscopy showed that protein unfolding at high concentrations (500 - 1000 μM) was induced by BA, whereas OA elicited a stable conformational change at a lower concentration (250 μM).

CONCLUSION: This study isolated OA for the first time in Z. mucronata and demonstrates its potential as an inhibitor of PfHsp70-1.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance for the Diagnosis and Monitoring of Takayasu Arteritis in Children.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Imaging evidence of vasculitis is mandatory for classification of Takayasu arteritis (TA) in children, yet the ability of a negative study to exclude the diagnosis has not been evaluated. We aimed to determine the negative predictive value (NPV) of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for excluding TA in children, to describe the imaging phenotype at diagnosis, and to characterise interval change on serial imaging.

METHODS: This retrospective study included all children who underwent CMR for suspected or established large vessel vasculitis at a single tertiary centre between May 2018 and November 2025. The protocol comprised contrast-enhanced angiography, 3D balanced steady-state free precession (bSSFP) imaging, black-blood imaging and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of vessel walls. TA was classified by the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES paediatric criteria. A true negative was defined as a negative baseline CMR with no emergence of TA over at least 6 months of documented follow-up. Interval change on serial CMR was classified per scan pair as improved, unchanged or worsened, recording wall findings (thickening, LGE) and luminal findings (stenosis, dilation) separately, by two readers.

RESULTS: 161 children underwent 222 CMR studies. Of 156 initial diagnostic studies, 10 (6%) showed TA and 146 were negative. No child with a negative baseline CMR developed TA during a median follow-up of 3.6 years (IQR 2.1 to 4.7), corresponding to an observed NPV of 100% (95% CI 97.5 to 100). Positive initial studies were characterised by aortic wall thickening and LGE in 7 of 10 children (70%), these were concordant in every child; extra-aortic involvement was present in 7 (70%). Fifteen children with TA underwent serial CMR (51 interval comparisons; inter-reader agreement 90%, weighted κ 0.86, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.96): 11 intervals (22%) showed improvement, 20 (39%) no change and 20 (39%) worsening. Two children had a previously undescribed imaging finding of focal 3D bSSFP signal abnormalities at sites of disease, consistent with a local susceptibility effect that improved or resolved with treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: In a tertiary referral population, no child with a negative CMR developed TA during follow-up. Serial CMR detected interval change with high agreement between readers. These findings support CMR as a reliable investigation for both the exclusion and longitudinal monitoring of TA in children.

articles.title: Fraudulent COVID-19 prevention and treatment claims online: A content analysis of FDA warning letters, 2020-2023.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The digital age has brought about a major change in how health-related information is created and disseminated, particularly through the internet and social media platforms. During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media amplified unverified or misleading claims and misinformation that could have resulted in serious public health consequences. The FDA issued warning letters to companies marketing products with fraudulent COVID-19 prevention or treatment claims.

OBJECTIVES: Using a content-analysis approach, the purpose of the study was to review FDA issued warning letters between March 2020-December 2023 for products with fraudulent claims regarding COVID-19 prevention, treatment, or cure.

METHODS: Full-text copies of all warning letters are available on the FDA website. A data abstraction form was developed based on past literature on the relevant topic, and pilot tested on warning letters issued in March 2020. Information collected in the form included product name, company name, product details, type of media, number of violations, target audience for promotional claims, corrective action taken, and current product status. Two researchers reviewed the warning letters issued March 2020-December 2023 using this form. Data were analyzed using SAS. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and Firth's penalized logistic regression were used to evaluate trends.

RESULTS: A total of 218 WLs were analyzed, with most issued in 2020 (61.9%). Drugs (64.2%) and medical devices (23.9%) were most frequently cited. Websites combined with social media were the predominant channels (45.0%), with Facebook, X (formerly known as Twitter), and Instagram most implicated. Consumers were the primary target (96.8%). Corrective actions were documented in 63.1% of cases, yet 36.9% remained non-compliant. Clinical outcome claims comprised 79.7% of violations. Firth's penalized logistic regression revealed significantly higher odds of non-compliance among dietary supplements (OR=11.5) and medical devices (OR=3.6) relative to drugs.

CONCLUSION: This study revealed COVID-19 related fraudulent and unproven claims included in the warning letters issued by the FDA. Protecting consumers from products with such claims is crucial to promote consumer safety during COVID-19.

articles.title: Two Cases of Group G Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome Complicated by Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: We report two cases of necrotizing soft tissue infection with streptococcal toxic shock syndrome caused by group G Streptococcus(Streptococcus dysgalactiae subsp. equisimilis). Both patients showed no macroscopic necrosis on initial bedside incision but subsequently developed progressive local findings and rapid systemic deterioration within 24 hours, prompting repeated reassessment and leading to the diagnosis of NSTI. Because the rapid antigen detection test (RADT) used in these cases targets group A Streptococcus (GAS), negative results did not exclude GGS-associated NSTI. These cases highlight that GGS-associated NSTI should be considered even when initial bedside exploration reveals no macroscopic necrosis, particularly when clinical suspicion persists because of disproportionate pain or systemic inflammatory findings. Both patients survived after intensive care and repeated surgical procedures and were transferred to other facilities on hospital days 177 and 108, respectively.

articles.title: The Crisis of Pseudoscience and the Erosion of the Therapeutic Alliance in Critical Care.
SGLT2 Inhibitors Versus Metformin as First-Line Therapy for Cardiorenal Outcomes: A Target Trial Emulation Among New Users With Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare cardiorenal and mortality outcomes associated with initiation of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors versus metformin as first-line glucose-lowering therapy among new users with type 2 diabetes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Using a target trial emulation design with TriNetX Global Collaborative Network data, we identified adults (≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes who were new users of SGLT2 inhibitors or metformin from January 1, 2018, through December 31, 2023, with follow-up through June 10, 2025. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary outcomes included individual MACE components, major adverse kidney events (MAKE), acute heart failure, all-cause mortality, and kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy. Propensity-score matching yielded 36,720 pairs.

RESULTS: Over median follow-up of 2.5 and 3.5 years in the SGLT2 inhibitor and metformin groups, respectively, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with lower risks of MACE (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.84-0.92), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.68-0.77), stroke (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.79-0.90), cardiac arrest (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.95), and acute heart failure (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97). Myocardial infarction risk was similar between groups (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.91-1.04). Kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy also did not differ significantly between groups (HR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87-1.14).

CONCLUSION: Among new users with type 2 diabetes, first-line SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with lower risks of MACE and all-cause mortality than metformin, while the risk of kidney failure requiring kidney replacement therapy was similar between groups.

articles.title: Emerging inhalation risks: Global distribution of airborne algal and cyanobacterial toxins.
articles.abstract: Harmful algal and cyanobacterial blooms (HABs/CHABs) are increasing globally due to climate change and anthropogenic pressures, raising concerns regarding human exposure to associated toxins. Although traditionally associated with ingestion and dermal contact, these toxins can become aerosolized, creating an understudied inhalation exposure pathway for populations living, working, or recreating near bloom-affected waterbodies. Inhalation has been associated with respiratory irritation and asthma exacerbations, while systemic and potential neurotoxic effects remain less characterized. This review synthesizes global evidence on aerosolized HAB/CHAB toxins in marine and freshwater environments. We identified 27 studies across North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. Fourteen toxins were detected in aerosols, including microcystin (MC), brevetoxin (PbTx), β-N-methylamino-L-alanine (BMAA), nodularin, saxitoxin, and others, with MC and PbTx most frequently reported. MC appeared in 41% of studies (2 marine, 9 freshwater), PbTx in 37% (all marine), and BMAA in 11% (all freshwater). Aerosol toxin concentrations varied widely. MC was the only toxin detected in both marine and freshwater settings, with maximum concentrations of 40.0 ng/m3 in aerosols. Sampling methodologies differed substantially, employing filter samplers, cascade impactors, and impingers, alongside ELISA, LC-MS/MS, and LC-HRMS analyses. Early marine studies focused predominantly on PbTx in Florida, while subsequent studies expanded geographically and taxonomically. Freshwater studies documented airborne MC across four continents. Available evidence indicates that aerosolized toxins can travel kilometers to hundreds of kilometers inland, depending on particle size, meteorological conditions, and toxin stability, suggesting that airborne transport extends exposure risks beyond bloom-affected areas. Despite growing evidence, atmospheric monitoring remains sparse. Exposure assessment frameworks are poorly developed, and chronic inhalation effects remain largely unknown. Co-exposure to multiple toxins and potential long-range transport warrant further attention. Standardized aerosol sampling, validated congener-specific toxin quantification, and interdisciplinary research are needed to address gaps in global surveillance, mechanistic understanding, and exposure assessment and evaluate the public health implications.

articles.title: Micro- and nanoplastic exposure and cardiometabolic health: A nutrition-focused critical review.
articles.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) have emerged as potential environmental determinants of human health because of their widespread presence in food, drinking water, food-contact materials, and the broader environment. This nutrition-focused critical review evaluates current evidence linking MNP exposure with cardiometabolic health by integrating dietary exposure pathways, toxicological mechanisms, experimental findings, emerging human evidence, and precautionary exposure-reduction approaches. Available studies suggest that MNPs may interfere with metabolic homeostasis through oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endocrine disruption, intestinal barrier impairment, gut microbial dysbiosis, and the release or transport of plastic-associated chemicals. These processes have been implicated in biological alterations related to cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, obesity, hypertension, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. However, the strength of evidence differs substantially across outcomes. Most mechanistic findings originate from in vitro and animal studies, frequently using particle types and exposure doses that may not fully represent typical human exposure. Human studies remain limited and are predominantly observational, precluding firm causal inference. Major knowledge gaps include the absence of standardized analytical and biomonitoring methods, heterogeneity in particle size and polymer composition, uncertainty regarding environmentally relevant doses, and the scarcity of prospective epidemiological studies. Overall, current evidence supports biological plausibility but remains insufficient to establish MNP exposure as an independent causal cardiometabolic risk factor. Standardized exposure assessment, long-term human studies, and better integration of dietary, environmental, and clinical data are needed.

articles.title: Creatinine-Only eGFR in the Low-eGFR-Only Phenotype of Diabetic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In UK Biobank participants with diabetes, Claudel et al. found a higher hazard of cardiovascular death with low estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) without albuminuria than with albuminuria alone, the reverse of a United States cohort's ranking. An eGFR cut-off of 60 mL/min/1.73 m² defines two of the four phenotypes, so this report examined whether the filtration marker could affect phenotype assignment.

METHODS: Index-study methods were compared with the 2021 Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equations, the 2024 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline, and published UK Biobank and meta-analysis data on creatinine-based versus cystatin C-based eGFR.

RESULTS: All eGFR values came from the creatinine-only equation, although a combined creatinine-cystatin C version exists. The low-eGFR-only phenotype comprised 758 participants with 120 cardiovascular deaths (hazard ratio 2.42 versus 1.88 for albuminuria only). Nearly all UK Biobank participants had baseline cystatin C. KDIGO recommends combined creatinine-cystatin C eGFR when cystatin C is available (grade 1B). In the meta-analysis, eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² occurred in 13.7% of people by cystatin C versus 9.7% by creatinine. In UK Biobank, cystatin C-based eGFR was most strongly associated with cardiovascular disease and mortality; with creatinine-based eGFR of at least 45 and no albuminuria, ten-year risks were low whenever cystatin C-based eGFR was at least 60.

CONCLUSIONS: Assignment to the low-eGFR-only phenotype depends on the filtration marker. A creatinine-cystatin C re-analysis, needing no new data, would show how many of the 758 participants change phenotype and whether the hazard ratio of 2.42 changes.

articles.title: The Heart Likes It Dry, the Kidneys Like It Wet? Time to Retire the Myth.
Design and rationale of MIRACLE, a prospective multicenter cohort study with integrated biobanking in cardiogenic shock.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Cardiogenic shock carries high mortality, yet most evidence comes from patients with shock related to acute myocardial infarction. Cohorts that combine serial staging, repeated biobanking, and structured assessment of survivors across severity stages and etiologies are scarce.

OBJECTIVE: MIRACLE (multimodal phenotyping in patients referred with acute cardiac failure) aims at multimodal phenotyping and risk stratification of patients with cardiogenic shock across etiologies. The primary endpoint is all-cause mortality at 30 days.

DESIGN: Prospective, observational, multicenter cohort study with an embedded biobank. Adults with Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stage B preshock or stage C to E shock of any etiology are enrolled in intensive and intermediate care units. Patients with a large anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction without shock are enrolled as controls (SCAI A) for shock related to myocardial infarction. SCAI stages are reassessed during the first 24 hours after admission to intensive care and at study visits on days 1, 3, and 5 and at discharge from intensive care, each with biobanking. Follow-up extends to 12 months and includes a visit at 6 months with repeat biobanking, exercise testing, cognitive assessment, and patient-reported outcomes.

SITES: Four centers in Germany.

ESTIMATED ENROLLMENT: Approximately 600 patients, ≥ 500 day-1 samples.

ENROLLMENT DATES: August 2024 to the middle of 2027 (estimated).

CURRENT STATUS: As of 30 September 2026, 449 patients with shock or preshock and 22 controls had been enrolled. Blood samples on day 1 were obtained in 88% of eligible patients, and follow-up at 6 months was completed in 86% of eligible survivors, at the study site in 148 and by telephone in 62. Mortality at 30 days was 15% in SCAI stage B and 63% in stage E (overall 35%). Enrollment is limited to German academic centers, and very early deaths may have been missed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07515508, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07515508.

articles.title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors And Depression in Atrial Fibrillation: Design of the SAD-AF Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation and depression are frequently comorbid, with autonomic dysfunction as a potential shared underlying pathophysiology. However, the effect of the treatment of depression on atrial fibrillation has not been well characterized, despite previous investigation of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors into other forms of cardiovascular disease such as coronary artery disease.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether escitalopram, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, reduces AF-related symptoms, AF burden and AF presentations to hospital compared to placebo, in addition to standard of care.

METHODS: Multicenter, randomized, single-blind, parallel-group superiority trial. Eligible participants are aged 18-80 years with paroxysmal or persistent atrial fibrillation, with the goal of rhythm control, who also score 8 or more on the PHQ-9 questionnaire (out of a maximum score of 27). 154 patients will be randomized to escitalopram or placebo in doses of 5mg to 20mg, titrated to individual patient response. The primary outcome is the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality of Life (AFEQT) score. Secondary outcomes include AF burden, adherence to lifestyle risk factor management including self-rated physical activity index (EPIC-PAQ-S questionnaire), general quality of life (SF-36 questionnaire), and hospital presentations for atrial fibrillation. Rhythm monitoring for AF burden will be undertaken with either mobile single lead ECG monitoring (Alivecor Kardiamobile), ECG-capable smartwatch, Holter monitoring or interrogation of pre-existing cardiac electronic implantable device. Autonomic metrics will be assessed by non-invasive recordings of blood pressure and heart rate variability.

CONCLUSIONS: The study aims to determine the impact of managing AF with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, with a patient-centered primary outcome.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus DOAC Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Phenotype-Centered Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) has emerged as a selective alternative to long-term oral anticoagulation in appropriately selected patients with non-valvular high-risk atrial fibrillation (AF). However, individual contemporary RCTs remain underpowered to detect infrequent but clinically important outcomes.

METHODOLOGY: This meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261384938). A systematic literature search was conducted to identify RCTs comparing LAAC with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) therapy in patients with non-valvular high-risk AF. Statistical analyses were performed using R, with a two-sided significance threshold of p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Five RCTs (n = 6,239; LAAC: 3,126; DOACs: 3,113) with 1:1 non-inferiority design were included. There were no significant differences between LAAC and DOACs for the composite endpoint, all-cause mortality or stroke. Systemic thromboembolism was significantly higher with LAAC (RR 2.53, 95% CI 1.04-6.19; p = 0.04; I² = 28.9%). LAAC was associated with significantly lower rates of minor bleeding (RR 0.48, 95% CI 0.40-0.58; p < 0.01; I² = 6.9%) and nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding (RR 0.56, 95% CI 0.48-0.65; p < 0.01; I² = 0.0%). Pericardial effusion was significantly higher with LAAC (RR 2.35, 95% CI 1.15-4.83; p = 0.02; I² = 0.0%). Serious adverse events were modestly but significantly higher in the LAAC group (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.02-1.14).

CONCLUSION: In contemporary randomized trials, LAAC and DOAC-based therapy showed no significant differences in mortality or overall stroke outcomes but demonstrated divergent safety tradeoffs. LAAC was associated with less nonprocedural clinically relevant bleeding, while systemic thromboembolism, pericardial effusion, and serious adverse events occurred more frequently with device-based therapy. These findings support phenotype-specific selection of LAAC rather than routine substitution for evidence-based anticoagulation.

articles.title: Drug Development in Pediatric Heart Failure: Current Landscape and Future Directions.
articles.abstract: Pediatric heart failure (HF) remains an important area of unmet medical need. Pharmacological treatments primarily consist of adult drugs used off label in children. HF regulatory guidance specific to pediatric drug development is limited. The diversity in underlying pathophysiology necessitates a shift toward a mechanism-of-action driven approach. We examine the current landscape of pediatric HF, identify key challenges and opportunities for drug development, and discuss a paradigm shift to a new high-level HF phenotype classification system for pediatric HF. Pediatric extrapolation utilizing pharmacokinetics and bridging biomarkers, especially given the absence of validated surrogate endpoints, remains a promising strategy for subsets of pediatric HF physiology. Ongoing reorganization of pediatric regulatory frameworks presents a key opportunity to promote harmonization between pediatric requirements from regulatory agencies across jurisdictions. We describe innovation in pediatric HF treatment through use of extrapolation, bridging biomarkers, and adaptive trial design.

articles.title: Clinical Risk, Carotid Plaque Burden, Cardiac Remodeling, and Left Ventricular Diastolic Dysfunction in Asymptomatic Adults Referred for Exercise Stress Echocardiography.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise stress echocardiography (SE) assesses inducible ischemia but may not identify subclinical atherosclerosis or early cardiac remodeling. We evaluated the prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis and its relationships with clinical risk estimates, cardiac remodeling, and diastolic function in asymptomatic adults referred for exercise SE.

METHODS: In this prospective, blinded cohort study, 73 consecutive asymptomatic adults without known cardiovascular disease (CVD) underwent treadmill SE, carotid ultrasonography for carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT), plaque presence and burden, and resting echocardiography. Radial-artery tonometry (RAT) was performed in 33 participants. Ten-year risk was estimated using the Framingham general CVD risk score (FRS), Pooled Cohort Equations for atherosclerotic CVD (PCE-ASCVD), and Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations for ASCVD, total CVD, and heart failure (PREVENT-HF).

RESULTS: Among 70 evaluable participants, 69 (98.6%) had negative SE findings for inducible ischemia; one demonstrated a hypertensive myopathic response. Carotid plaque was present in 46 participants (65.7%), and isolated CIMT >75th percentile without plaque was present in 6 (8.6%), yielding a combined prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis of 74.3%. Plaque prevalence increased across FRS, PCE-ASCVD, and PREVENT-ASCVD categories but remained 45.8% among participants classified as low risk by PREVENT-ASCVD. All five clinical risk estimates correlated with plaque number, maximum plaque thickness, total plaque area, and relative LV wall thickness. Greater plaque area was associated with higher relative wall thickness, left ventricular (LV) mass index, and diastolic-function grade. PREVENT-HF showed the strongest numerical correlations with diastolic-function grade and average E/e'. In a model incorporating plaque area and PREVENT-HF, PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction (OR per SD, 2.60; 95% CI, 1.30-5.20; P=.007), whereas plaque area was not. Exercise duration and rate-pressure product were not associated with plaque burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Among asymptomatic adults with CVD risk factors referred for exercise SE, inducible ischemia was uncommon despite a high prevalence of subclinical carotid atherosclerosis. Carotid plaque burden and clinical risk estimates were associated with cardiac remodeling and diastolic function, while PREVENT-HF was independently associated with diastolic dysfunction. These findings support complementary characterization of subclinical vascular and cardiac abnormalities but do not establish incremental outcome prediction, altered treatment eligibility, or replacement of clinically indicated stress testing by carotid imaging.

articles.title: Adverse childhood experiences, social isolation and loneliness across adulthood: A nationwide cross-sectional study of Chinese adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loneliness and social isolation are distinct risk factors for depression and other affective disorders but are often conflated. Whether adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) relate differently to the two, and whether this varies across adulthood, is unclear.

METHODS: We analysed 24,219 adults from the nationwide 2024 Psychology and Behaviour Investigation of Chinese Residents. Seven ACE domains were assessed with items adapted from the WHO ACE-IQ. Social isolation (three-item structural index, score ≥ 2) and loneliness (two-item functional index, score 2) were defined using indices adapted from the UK Biobank. Adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated by modified Poisson regression with city-clustered standard errors; a stacked model compared the two outcomes.

RESULTS: Social isolation (30.0%) and loneliness (11.0%) overlapped weakly (kappa 0.17). Each additional ACE was associated with higher prevalence of loneliness (PR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.28) and, more weakly, isolation (PR 1.04, 1.01-1.08; ratio of PRs 1.19, 1.17-1.22). All seven domains were associated with loneliness; only emotional abuse, witnessed violence and, marginally, physical abuse were associated with isolation; sexual abuse, household substance use, household mental illness and parental incarceration were not. The association of ≥4 ACEs with loneliness strengthened with age (P for interaction <0.001; PR 2.71, 1.98-3.72, at ≥60 years).

LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design and retrospectively self-reported ACEs preclude causal inference.

CONCLUSIONS: ACEs were more strongly associated with loneliness than with social isolation, particularly in later life. Among adults with ACE histories, asking about loneliness may capture disconnection that structural indicators such as living arrangements or contact frequency miss.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes of renal denervation in patients with resistant hypertension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the medium- and long-term outcomes of renal denervation (RD) in patients with resistant hypertension (RH), focusing on blood pressure (BP) control, antihypertensive drug burden, and renal safety.

METHODS: Prospective observational study including 51 patients with RH treated between 2020 and 2024 with radiofrequency RD using the Symplicity Spyral™ system. BP values, antihypertensive therapy, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and procedural complications were assessed over a 24-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Systolic BP was significantly reduced, with a mean overall decrease of -12.3 mmHg at the end of follow-up (p < 0.001), while diastolic BP decreased by -5.1 mmHg at 24 months (p = 0.01). The number of antihypertensive drugs was significantly reduced, and 82.6% of patients achieved clinical success. A mild decline in eGFR was observed without clinical relevance. Age ≥50 years was associated with a higher likelihood of response. Major complications were infrequent (4.3%).

CONCLUSIONS: RD is an effective and safe therapeutic option for selected patients with RH, providing sustained BP reduction and a decreased need for antihypertensive medication.

articles.title: Quality of Life and Participant Satisfaction in the ACAF Clinical Trial: Advanced Care Planning in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: A clinical trial, the ACAF study (Advanced Care Planning in Heart Failure), was designed to evaluate the effectiveness of an Advance Care Planning (ACP) programme in patients with advanced heart failure (HF). This article presents the results regarding quality of life and participant satisfaction in the ACAF study.

METHODS: A multicentre randomised clinical trial was conducted in four hospitals. Patient allocation to the study groups was performed using alternate sampling. The ACP programme was applied to the intervention group, while the control group received the routine follow-up in heart failure outpatient clinics. Quality of life was assessed using the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire, and satisfaction was evaluated using a questionnaire specifically developed for the project.

RESULTS: A total of 67 patients were recruited and randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 29; 43.3%) and the control group (n = 38; 56.7%). Quality of life was assessed at baseline and at 1-year follow-up: 58 in the baseline analysis and 42 at 1 year, with 18 losses to follow-up (8 voluntary withdrawals, 5 deaths, 7 incomplete questionnaires, and 1 exclusion due to tumor diagnosis). After one year, quality of life improved in both groups, with no statistically significant differences between them. The satisfaction questionnaire indicated a very satisfactory experience among patients who participated in the programme.

CONCLUSIONS: The implementation of a PADS programme in patients with advanced heart failure is associated with a high level of satisfaction among participants, who positively value shared decision-making. Furthermore, the programme does not worsen quality of life compared with standard follow-up in heart failure clinics, supporting its safety and acceptability in this clinical setting.

articles.title: Smoking Cessation Duration and Risk of Incident Hospitalized Acute Kidney Injury: A Nationwide Cohort Study in Korea.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Cigarette smoking is a modifiable risk factor for kidney disease, but the degree to which smoking cessation reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) remains unclear. This study evaluated whether smoking status and duration of smoking cessation were associated with AKI risk.

STUDY DESIGN: Population-based retrospective cohort study.

SETTING & PARTICIPANTS: 1,151,722 adults without evidence of kidney disease who had a health examination recorded in the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) database between 2009 and 2013 and who completed at least three prior biennial health examinations subsequent to 2002 that included assessment of smoking status.

EXPOSURE: Smoking status and duration of sustained smoking cessation.

OUTCOMES: Incident hospitalized AKI defined by ICD-10 codes N17.0-N17.9 taken from inpatient administrative claims data.

ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Crude incidence rates and multivariable cause-specific hazard models estimated adjusted hazard ratios (HRs).

RESULTS: The cohort included 885,299 never smokers, 55,391 quitters, and 211,032 current smokers. A total of 11,972 study participants experienced an incident hospitalization for AKI occurring over a mean follow-up of 10.73 years. Among quitters, the crude AKI incidence was highest in those whose smoking cessation was less than 2 years in duration and declined with progressively longer durations. In the multivariable-adjusted analysis, never smokers had a significantly lower AKI risk than current smokers (adjusted HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.60-0.68). Among quitters, adjusted HRs decreased progressively with longer durations of smoking cessation (P for trend <0.001).

LIMITATIONS: Observational design, self-reported smoking status, inability to update smoking status during follow-up, claims-based AKI ascertainment, and a single-ethnicity population.

CONCLUSIONS: The risk of AKI was highest in current smokers and lowest in never smokers. Sustained smoking cessation was associated with a lower risk of hospitalized AKI with longer durations of smoking cessation being associated with less risk. These findings support long-term smoking cessation as an important kidney-protective strategy.

articles.title: Nephrology Fellowship Training in the United States by the Numbers.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Nephrology fellowship programs in the United States have severe recruitment challenges. Only 65% of clinical positions are filled in the National Residency Matching Program (NRMP), and <50% Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)-approved clinical programs are full. 20-30% of fellows are recruited post-match. Ultimately, 80-85% of positions fill, and >60% of fellows are international medical graduates. Despite chronically unfilled positions, the number of NRMP-offered positions and programs has increased, including the number of large programs (>10-fellows). 86% of positions created after 2018 are at large programs (15% of programs; 30% of on-duty fellows). Although recruitment efforts have been modestly successful, barriers include work-life balance, low salaries, patient complexity, and perceived non-competitiveness. Applicant demand is low and increased recruitment unlikely in the short term. We propose a democratically elected program director working group tasked with developing a national management plan that preserves programs, aligns offered positions with NRMP applicant number, and accounts for patient need. The working group could consider a moratorium on increasing program size and number, capping 2-year programs at 10 fellows, NRMP alternatives for programs in rural/underserved areas, and service demands on fellows and faculty. Low morale may contribute to poor recruitment, and nephrology may be perceived as a low prestige specialty because of low applicant to position ratio.

articles.title: Geranylgeranylacetone Attenuates Atherosclerosis via the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 Signaling Axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains a leading global health threat, driven by macrophage foam cell formation and chronic inflammation. Geranylgeranylacetone (GGA), an anti-ulcer drug known to induce heat shock proteins, may confer cardiovascular benefits, yet its direct anti-atherosclerotic mechanisms are not fully understood.

METHODS: ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet received GGA (400 mg/kg/d) for 12 weeks. Atherosclerotic lesions, plaque composition (necrotic core, collagen, macrophage infiltration), plasma lipids, and cytokine levels were evaluated. In vitro, THP-1-derived foam cells were treated with Ox-LDL and GGA (0.1-100 μmol/L). Cholesterol efflux, lipid accumulation, and the expression of Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, apolipoproteins, and inflammatory factors were measured. siRNA silencing was used to validate the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis.

RESULTS: GGA significantly reduced aortic plaque burden, increased collagen content, decreased macrophage infiltration, lowered total cholesterol, triglycerides, and LDL-C, raised HDL-C, and improved inflammatory cytokine profiles (decreased IL-6 and TNF-α; increased IL-10) in ApoE-/- mice. In foam cells, GGA enhanced cholesterol efflux, reduced cholesteryl ester content and lipid droplets, and upregulated Matcap2, Apelin, ABCA1/ABCG1, and ApoA1/A2/A4, while downregulating ApoB, IL-6, and TNF-α. Silencing either Matcap2 or Apelin abrogated GGA-induced upregulation of ABCA1/ABCG1, cholesterol efflux, and the protective apolipoprotein and anti-inflammatory phenotypes.

CONCLUSION: GGA attenuates atherosclerosis by activating the Matcap2-Apelin-ABCA1/ABCG1 signaling axis, thereby promoting reverse cholesterol transport and resolving inflammation. These findings support GGA as a promising repurposed drug with both cardioprotective and gastroprotective benefits.

articles.title: Luteolin, a component of Salvia miltiorrhiza, attenuates renal interstitial fibrosis progression by targeting the PTGS2-mediated inflammatory axis.
articles.abstract: The progressive decline of renal function in chronic kidney disease (CKD) inevitably culminates in renal interstitial fibrosis (RIF), yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking. While Salvia miltiorrhiza (SM) constitutes a rich reservoir of nephroprotective natural products, the precise chemical-protein interactions underlying its anti-fibrotic efficacy remain largely elusive. In the present study, a target-driven in silico screening was employed to identify the principal active component of SM and characterize its direct biophysical target. Computational analysis identified luteolin as the constituent exhibiting the highest binding affinity toward prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2/COX2). Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a highly stable luteolin-PTGS2 complex, which was experimentally authenticated by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), demonstrating a direct and strong biophysical interaction (KD = 2.73 μM). In vivo validation showed that luteolin administration significantly ameliorated renal dysfunction and attenuated extracellular matrix deposition in a folic acid-induced RIF mouse model. This protective phenotype was mechanistically linked to the suppression of PTGS2 and its downstream pro-inflammatory mediators (EP2, EP4, MCP-1, IL-1 β, and TNF-α). Cell experiments demonstrated that, consistently with the effects of the PTGS2 inhibitor meloxicam, luteolin reduced the expression of both the PTGS2 axis and pro-fibrotic proteins in RIF cell model. Furthermore, clinical data demonstrated that PTGS2 is significantly upregulated in human fibrotic kidneys and correlates inversely with renal function. In conclusion, as a component of SM, luteolin directly binds to and inhibits PTGS2, thereby blocking the downstream pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic cascades.

articles.title: Finding the Right Lesion for Side Branch Wire Jailing.
Differential Reverse Remodeling but Preserved Clinical Benefit of Sacubitril/Valsartan in Ischemic vs Non‑Ischemic HFrEF.
authors: Working Group on Heart Failure of the Italian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sacubitril/valsartan is associated with left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) and improved outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). However, differences in LVRR between ischemic and non-ischemic HFrEF and its relationship with clinical outcomes remain unclear.

METHODS: In this multicenter, open‑label study, cardiac remodeling changes from baseline to 8-12 months after sacubitril/valsartan initiation were retrospectively compared between ischemic and non‑ischemic HFrEF patients. The outcome endpoint was a composite of all‑cause mortality/HF-rehospitalization.

RESULTS: Among 608 patients enrolled, 302 (49.7%) had ischemic etiology. Baseline LVEF, end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVi) and end-systolic volume index (LVESVi) were similar between ischemic and non-ischemic groups. Both groups showed significant improvement at follow-up in LV volumes and LVEF (P<0.001 for all). However, adjusted mixed-effects models showed smaller LVEF gains (2.44% vs 4.51%, interaction P<0.0001) and smaller LVESVI reductions (-4.68 mL/m2 vs -7.43 mL/m2, interaction P<0.0001) in ischemic patients, while LVEDVi changes did not differ between the two groups (interaction P=0.263). Over a median follow-up of 63 months (IQR 32-77), 249 patients reached the composite endpoint. In multivariable analysis, LVRR was associated with the endpoint independent of etiology. In an exploratory analysis, LVRR accounted statistically for approximately 9% (95% CI 1.40-26.1%; p=0.0164) of the modeled pre-to-post association with outcome.

CONCLUSION: Significant LVRR after sacubitril/valsartan was observed in both ischemic and non-ischemic HFrEF, although the magnitude of improvement was smaller in ischemic disease. LVRR was associated with more favorable outcomes regardless of etiology, but only a modest proportion of the modeled pre-to-post association with outcome was statistically attributable to LVRR.

articles.title: First Use of a Bioresorbable Everolimus-Eluting Scaffold for Coronary In-Stent Restenosis.
Beyond Composite Outcomes: Reassessing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation.
Immune checkpoint inhibitors-induced -induced vs. Conventional Myocarditis: Navigating Pathophysiological and Clinical Divergences.
articles.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but have introduced immune-related adverse events, among which ICI-induced myocarditis (ICI-M) is one of the most severe cardiovascular complication. Compared with conventional myocarditis (CM), ICI-M is a distinct entity characterized by a hyper-acute, T-cell-mediated autoimmune response due to loss of immune tolerance. While CM typically follows a viral or autoimmune trigger and often evolves toward resolution, ICI-M occurs early after treatment initiation (within 30-60 days) and is associated with high mortality and a significant burden of major adverse cardiovascular events. Clinical presentation differs substantially. CM commonly presents with chest pain and progressive myocardial dysfunction, whereas ICI-M often manifests with non-specific symptoms such as fatigue and carries a higher risk of early conduction abnormalities and malignant arrhythmias. Diagnosis is challenging, as conventional imaging may underestimate disease severity in ICI-M: left ventricular ejection fraction is often preserved and late gadolinium enhancement may be absent in early stages. Advanced techniques, including global longitudinal strain and cardiac magnetic resonance parametric mapping, are therefore crucial for early detection. Diagnosis of ICI-induced myocarditis may also be challenging because of symptom and biomarker overlap with other immune-related adverse events, particularly myositis. Non-specific manifestations and concomitant elevations of troponin and skeletal muscle injury markers can complicate early recognition and differential diagnosis. Management strategies reflect these differences: CM is generally treated with supportive approaches, whereas ICI-M requires immediate discontinuation of ICIs and prompt high-dose immunosuppression. Despite advances, prognosis remains worse in ICI-M, underscoring the need for early recognition and dedicated cardio-oncology pathways.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence and Cardiovascular Disease Prevention: Newton's Second Law Readdressed with a Cautionary Note.
articles.abstract: The persistent burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) reflects not simply a lack of concrete evidence, but limitations in identifying risk early, characterizing its complexity, and translating risk information into timely and sustained intervention. Cardiovascular prevention has evolved from assessment of individual risk factors toward estimation of absolute global cardiovascular risk and expected treatment benefit. However, conventional approaches remain largely static and constrained by the data routinely available in clinical practice. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers an opportunity to provide the technological acceleration needed to strengthen the Force of cardiovascular prevention, in line with Newton's second law. This review discusses how AI can integrate multimodal and longitudinal data from various clinical assessments to improve risk prediction, uncover latent cardiovascular phenotypes, and characterize evolving individual risk trajectories. Hence, it can enable earlier detection of subclinical disease, continuous monitoring, personalized interventions, and population-level identification of missed preventive opportunities. Finally, the review highlights how the future value of AI in cardiovascular prevention will depend on its ability to move beyond prediction toward risk modification and reductions in cardiovascular events and mortality, in a sustainable and equitable manner.

articles.title: Molecular detection and therapeutic management of Babesia gibsoni and Ehrlichia canis co-infection in dogs along with characterisation of the pathogens.
articles.abstract: Tick-borne hemoparasitic infections constitute an important cause of clinical morbidity in dogs, particularly in endemic regions where vector exposure facilitates concurrent transmission of multiple pathogens. This study aimed to molecularly detect and characterise Babesia gibsoni and Ehrlichia canis co-infection in dogs, assess associated clinico-hemato-biochemical alterations, and evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of artesunate-atovaquone-doxycycline (AAD) regimen. A total of 184 clinically suspected dogs were screened by internally controlled multiplex PCR, and positive cases were further confirmed by species-specific real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) and sequencing. The prevalence of B. gibsoni and E. canis co-infection was 7.6% (14/184). Eight infected dogs were treated with AAD protocol and the relative abundance of parasite target DNA was assessed on days 0, 10, 28, and 90 using relative quantification (RQ) qPCR targeting B. gibsoni 18S rRNA and E. canis VirB9 gene that has been normalized to canine β-actin by the 2-ΔΔCt method. Infected dogs exhibited normocytic-normochromic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoproteinaemia, hyperglobulinaemia, hyperbilirubinemia, azotaemia, high serum alkaline phosphatase and aspartate transaminase level whereas, mean creatinine level were found within normal physiological range. Following AAD therapy, dogs showed rapid clinical recovery, with significant improvement in hemato-biochemical parameters by day 90. Significant reduction in parasite DNA load was noted, reflected by rising Ct values and progressively declining log RQ values for both pathogens. These findings indicated that the AAD regimen showed potential effectiveness against canine B. gibsoni and E. canis co-infection, however this preliminary clinical observation may be validated through further controlled trials.

articles.title: Extrapulmonary rapidly growing mycobacterial infections in Far North Queensland, tropical Australia, 2008-2024, a retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The global incidence of rapidly growing mycobacterial (RGM) infections is rising. We examined, retrospectively, cases of extrapulmonary RGM infection managed at a referral hospital in Far North Queensland (FNQ), tropical Australia, to characterise their presentation and the challenges in their management.

METHODS: All RGM isolated from extrapulmonary sites in FNQ residents between January 2008 and December 2024 were identified; the isolates' microbiological characteristics and the patients' clinical course were reviewed.

RESULTS: Mycobacterium fortuitum group (59/144, 41%), Mycobacterium abscessus complex (46/144, 32%) and Mycobacterium chelonae (21/144, 15%) were the most frequently isolated RGM. Clinical infection was confirmed in 103/144 (72%) isolates. The annual incidence of RGM clinical infections increased over the study period from 0.4 to 2.4/100,000 population (rs=0.57, p=0.02). Patients had a median (interquartile range (IQR)) age of 52 (33-66) years; 10/103 (10%) were immunosuppressed while only 6/103 (6%) had other significant comorbidity. Preceding environmental trauma was documented in 39/103 (38%), 38/103 (37%) followed surgery and 23/103 (22%) infections involved prosthetic material. The median (IQR) duration of symptoms at diagnosis was 5 (2-12) weeks. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing demonstrated high rates of resistance; 78 patients were treated with antibiotics for a median (IQR) duration of 18 (16-24) weeks with 47/78 (60%) experiencing an adverse drug reaction. Surgical management was necessary in 64/103 (62%). There were 6 microbiologically confirmed relapses but no deaths directly attributable to the infection or its treatment.

CONCLUSION: Extrapulmonary RGM infections are increasing in frequency in tropical Australia and predominantly affect younger, healthy individuals. Delayed diagnosis and adverse events from antimicrobial therapy are common.

articles.title: Multifunctional hyaluronic acid-based photothermal microneedle patch for enhanced healing of infected wounds.
articles.abstract: Bacterial biofilm infection is a key factor contributing to the persistence and impaired healing of wounds. This study presents a dual-layer microneedle (MN) patch with photothermal and antioxidant stress capabilities for treating Staphylococcus aureus-infected acute wounds. The MN tip, composed of hyaluronic acid (HA), encapsulates chlorogenic acid (CGA) and Prussian blue nanoparticles (PB NPs), while the polyvinylpyrrolidone K60 (PVP K60) backing layer incorporates asiaticoside (AS). The HA tip rapidly dissolves for localized drug release, and the PVP backing offers flexible structural support. PB NPs exhibit efficient photothermal conversion under near-infrared irradiation and possess nano-enzymatic activities, scavenging reactive oxygen species and synergizing with CGA to suppress biofilm formation. AS enhances cell proliferation and accelerates tissue repair. Animal experiments demonstrate that under photothermal conditions (approximately 46 °C), the MN group significantly accelerates wound healing by promoting angiogenesis, collagen deposition, and re-epithelialization, while effectively suppressing bacterial infection, mitigating inflammation, with certain efficacy in reducing scar formation. The overall therapeutic efficacy surpasses that of commercial 3 M dressings. This study provides an integrated strategy for multifunctional wound dressings combining antibacterial, antioxidant, and healing properties.

articles.title: Comment on "Endoscopy timing in managing acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective study".
Developing Static Perimetry Thresholds to Assess Visual Field Loss Severity in Patients with Retinitis Pigmentosa.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the correlation between kinetic and static perimetry measurements in patients with retinitis pigmentosa and to develop thresholds that translate 1) mean retinal sensitivity (MRS) from static perimetry and 2) Visual field (VF) area from kinetic perimetry, into kinetic perimetry-derived VF diameter using the International Council of Ophthalmology (ICO) Visual Standards classification of vision loss severity.

DESIGN: Retrospective cross-sectional study.

SUBJECTS: Data were obtained from charts of 100 adults with retinitis pigmentosa who had undergone full-field static and kinetic perimetry within a 30-day interval during routine practice at Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, US.

TESTING: Full-field static and kinetic perimetry using the Octopus 900 perimetry device.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Static perimetry full MRS and kinetic perimetry VF area cut-off values were derived from Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis by mapping the ICO kinetic perimetry VF diameter cut-offs to classify patients into vision loss severity groups. Youden Index and Area Under the Curve were used to determine optimal cutoff values that maximized diagnostic performance. Weighted Kappa statistics assessed the level of agreement between the derived severity classifications, and the ICO VF diameter classification standards.

RESULTS: Among the 100 patients, median age was 48.5 years, disease onset at median 28 years, 52% male, 16% with XLRP. MRS correlated strongly with kinetic VF diameter (Spearman's rho 0.83) and with kinetic VF area (rho 0.81); diameter and area were correlated at rho 0.94. ROC analysis derived MRS (dB) cut-offs for vision loss severity were: ≥7.4=mild, 5.3- <7.4=moderate, 3.2- <5.3=severe, 0.6- <3.2=profound, and <0.6=near-blindness/blindness (weighted Kappa coefficient 0.59). Optimal VF area (deg2) cutoffs for distinguishing severity levels were ≥5706=mild impairment, 410 - <5706=moderate, 688- <4100= severe, 71 -<688=profound, <71=near-blindness/blindness (weighted Kappa coefficient 0.73).

CONCLUSIONS: Strong correlations between MRS and VF diameter measures support the feasibility of mapping static perimetry to kinetic VF diameter ICO standard to classify vision loss severity. This study addresses a critical gap in interpreting retinitis pigmentosa research findings in visual field loss assessment.

articles.title: Development and validation of Erns-based lateral flow assay and sandwich ELISA for bovine viral diarrhea virus antigen detection.
articles.abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) control relies on the accurate detection and isolation of persistently infected cattle that often appear clinically normal yet continuously shed the virus. We developed and evaluated BVDV antigen (Ag) Rapid kits (kit-SP for serum/plasma and kit-FE for feces/ear notches) and Ag ELISA targeting the envelope glycoprotein Erns. Analytical sensitivity was assessed using BVDV-1a, -1b, and -2a subgenotypes spiked into BVDV-negative specimens. The rapid tests detected all three genotypes with limits of detection ranging from 7.81 × 102 to 3.13 × 103 TCID50/mL and showed comparable performance across specimen types. The Ag ELISA demonstrated high analytical sensitivity, with limits of detection as low as 0.78 × 102 TCID50/mL. No cross-reactivity was observed among the tested bovine pathogens, and cross-reactivity was detected only with the classical swine fever virus. No interference from anticoagulants or endogenous substances was observed, and the assay performance was reproducible across lots, operators, days, and laboratories. Using reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction as the reference method, the rapid test set achieved 92.31% sensitivity and 100% specificity, whereas the Ag ELISA achieved 93.33% sensitivity and 100% specificity. These Erns-targeting rapid tests and ELISA are reliable tools for persistent infection-focused herd screening and BVDV control.

articles.title: Fluvoxamine disrupts Enterococcus faecalis biofilms by downregulating adhesion genes and binding biofilm proteins: a promising strategy for antimicrobial urinary catheter coatings.
articles.abstract: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections (CAUTI) are predominantly driven by biofilm formation on indwelling devices, which significantly complicates treatment and contributes to high morbidity and mortality. The increasing antimicrobial resistance has intensified the need for novel therapeutic and preventive strategies.
