In this study, we investigated fluvoxamine, a selective serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, for its antibacterial and antibiofilm potential against Enterococcus faecalis, a common CAUTI pathogen. Fluvoxamine exhibited potent antibacterial activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 12.5 µg/mL. Time-kill kinetics revealed rapid bactericidal activity within 1 h, and combination studies demonstrated synergistic effects with conventional antibiotics. Fluvoxamine significantly inhibited biofilm formation and eradicated up to 89% of preformed mature E. faecalis biofilms. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) corroborated these findings, revealing substantial disruption of biofilm architecture and morphological damage to bacterial cells. In an in vitro catheter model, fluvoxamine-coated catheter tubes effectively reduced bacterial colonization and maintained antibacterial efficacy for up to 48 h. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) combined with FDA/PI staining confirmed reduced biofilm thickness and increased proportion of dead cells. Molecular docking analysis indicated a strong binding affinity of fluvoxamine to key E. faecalis biofilm-associated adhesion proteins. Furthermore, quantitative RT-PCR analysis showed significant downregulation of biofilm-related genes, including GelE, EbpA, AS, and EfaA. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that fluvoxamine possesses promising antibacterial and antibiofilm properties and highlight its potential as a novel catheter-coating agent for the prevention and management of E. faecalis-associated CAUTI.

articles.title: The spectrum of airway dysfunction in asthma: a focus on small airways from the Turkish adult asthma registry.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Small airway dysfunction (SAD) increases airway resistance, impacting asthma outcomes and lung function. We aimed to determine the distribution of SAD and to describe its clinical and functional features within the spectrum of airway involvement in adult asthmatics.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study is a subgroup analysis of the multicenter Turkish Adult Asthma Registry (TAAR) between 2018-2022. Patients were classified into three functional groups based on pulmonary function tests: normal lung function (NLF; FEV1≥80%, FEF25-75% ≥65%), SAD (FEV ≥80%, FEF25-75%<65%), and large-small airway dysfunction (LSAD; FEV1<80%, FEF25-75%<65%). Clinical characteristics, asthma phenotypes, and spirometric indices were compared across groups.

RESULTS: Among 989 patients, 347(35.1%) were classified as NLF, 232(23.5%) as SAD, and 410(41.5%) as LSAD. Patients with NLF were younger with shorter disease duration, whereas obese asthma, poorer asthma control, higher GINA step, and severe asthma were more frequent in LSAD. Well-controlled asthma was observed in 56.6%, 50.2%, and 34.0% of patients with NLF, SAD, and LSAD, respectively. Median FEV1, FEV1/FVC, and FEF25-75% values showed a graded decline from NLF to SAD and LSAD (all p < 0.001). In allergic and in eosinophilic asthma, FEV1 and FEF25-75% were lower in SAD than in NLF, and LSAD had the lowest values.

CONCLUSION: In this multicenter registry sub-analysis, SAD was present in approximately one quarter of adult asthmatics and showed an intermediate clinical-functional profile between NLF and LSAD, with poorer asthma control and greater treatment intensity than NLF but less impairment than LSAD. These findings position SAD as a distinct intermediate stage of airway dysfunction and suggest that identifying SAD may help quantify disease burden and refine treatment strategies, particularly in type-2 phenotypes.

articles.title: Automating the Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 in the Electronic Health Record: Automated Risk Scoring Using Structured Clinical Documentation.
articles.abstract: Background The Pediatric Index of Mortality 3 (PIM3) is a validated severity-of-illness score widely used for risk adjustment, benchmarking, quality improvement initiatives, and research in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs). Its use in electronic workflows is limited by required variables that rely on clinical judgement and are traditionally abstracted manually from narrative documentation. Objectives To design, implement, and evaluate an automated PIM3 calculation within the electronic health record (EHR) using structured clinical documentation to capture non-discrete variables, and to assess clinician adoption, documentation accuracy, and concordance with manual abstraction. Methods A structured documentation template with standardized response options was developed to capture non-discrete PIM3 variables, including ventilation status, elective admission status, procedural recovery, and diagnosis category. These clinician-entered data were mapped to discrete structured data elements and combined with physiologic and laboratory inputs for automated score calculation. Documentation completion and accuracy were evaluated over a 12-month period. Automated scores were validated against manually abstracted gold standard PIM3 scores in a convenience sample of 20 targeted encounters. Results Among 923 PICU encounters, clinician compliance with structured PIM3 documentation was 95% (n=877). Of the completed entries, 84% (n=773) contained no documentation errors. Identified errors were primarily related to binary clinical judgements rather than diagnostic clarification. Of the 20 encounter validation sample, automated PIM3 scores and associated probabilities of death demonstrated near-complete concordance with manually calculated gold standard values, with no clinically meaningful discrepancies. Conclusion Automated PIM3 calculation using structured clinical documentation within the EHR is feasible and reliable for supporting standardized data capture and timely availability of risk-adjustment information. This approach reduces reliance on manual abstraction and provides a scalable informatics framework for quality improvement, benchmarking, and research in pediatric critical care.

articles.title: Vitreous vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 levels in vitreoretinal pathologies: a prospective analysis of 181 eyes.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify vitreous vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) across vitreoretinal pathologies and identify associated factors.

DESIGN: Prospective, single-centre, cross-sectional observational study.

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 181 eyes of 171 adults undergoing pars plana vitrectomy (PPV).

METHODS: Undiluted midvitreous specimens were aspirated before infusion. Eyes were formed into 5 subgroups: advanced proliferative diabetic retinopathy (n = 80), rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (n = 65), vitreomacular interface (VMI) disease (n = 17), retained lens fragments (n = 14), and endophthalmitis (n = 5). VCAM-1 was measured by sandwich enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. VMI disease was the reference category; no disease-free controls existed. Log-transformed VCAM-1 was analysed by univariable and multivariable regression with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate adjustment.

RESULTS: VCAM-1 differed across subgroups (P < 0.001), greatest in endophthalmitis (45 972.61 ± SE 22 130.67 pg/mL; n = 5) and lowest in VMI disease (3669.46 ± 642.42 pg/mL). Chronic kidney disease (P = 0.031) and longer duration of diabetes (unstandardised coefficient B = 411.15 ± 173.65 pg/mL per year; P = 0.020) were associated with greater VCAM-1, although neither group survived false discovery rate adjustment (q = 0.109 and 0.093). Pre-existing glaucoma was independently associated with elevated VCAM-1 (20 126.36 ± 4784.77 vs 9946.15 ± 1147.22 pg/mL; P = 0.003; q = 0.021).

CONCLUSIONS: Vitreous VCAM-1 varied across vitreoretinal diagnoses, greatest in endophthalmitis, although on only 5 eyes. Longer duration of diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and pre-existing glaucoma were each associated with greater VCAM-1. These cross-sectional associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish a mechanistic or causal role.

articles.title: Psychological Trauma Among Labor and Delivery Nurses and Trauma-Informed Care.
articles.journal: Journal of obstetric, gynecologic, and neonatal nursing : JOGNN
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore relationships among labor and delivery nurses' psychological trauma and their attitudes toward and experiences with trauma-informed care.

DESIGN: Convergent mixed-methods design via cross-sectional survey.

SETTING: Online distribution during May and June 2025.

PARTICIPANTS: Labor and delivery nurses who worked in the United States (N = 149).

METHODS: We calculated descriptive statistics of participants' demographic characteristics and scores on three scales. We used deductive content analysis of open-ended survey responses.

RESULTS: The mean Secondary Traumatic Stress Scale (STSS) score was 48.19 (SD = 11.16), and 82.6% of participants (n = 123) scored above the screening cut point consistent with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The mean PTSD Checklist for Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.) score was 37.44 (SD = 14.17), and the scores of 66.4% of participants (n = 99) were indicative of probable PTSD. The mean Attitudes Related to Trauma-Informed Care scale (ARTIC-45) score was 4.26 (SD = 0.62). Using Gaussian mixture modeling, we identified no predictive relationships between trauma levels and care attitudes; secondary traumatic stress and posttraumatic stress symptoms demonstrated negligible conflicting directional effects (all ps ≥ .432) However, the ARTIC scores had a bimodal distribution with peaks at 5.34 (SD = 0.32, n = 31) and 3.98 (SD = 0.25, n = 118). Through deductive content analysis, we identified barriers to and facilitators of trauma-informed care that centered on organizational support, particularly training, staffing, resource allocation, and collaboration.

CONCLUSION: Participants reported substantial psychological trauma, but trauma measures were not associated with trauma-informed care attitudes. Qualitative findings showed the organizational supports and barriers that may influence implementation of trauma-informed care.

articles.title: Assisted reproductive technology and the risk of urinary tract infection in offspring: a nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) increases the risk of certain childhood illnesses. However, its specific relationship with UTI in offspring remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the risk of UTI in ART offspring.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study linked Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database and Maternal and Child Health Database between 2004 and 2020. First live-born children conceived via ART were matched 1:2 with naturally conceived children based on maternal age, infant sex, and birth date. Pediatric UTI was defined as a hospitalization with a newly diagnosed UTI and concurrent antibiotic prescriptions before three years of age.

RESULTS: A total of 89,520 children were evaluated (29,840 in the ART group; 59,680 in the non-ART group). The cumulative incidence of UTI was significantly higher in the ART group (5.8% vs. 5.0%, p < 0.001). After adjusting for potential confounders, the ART group demonstrated a higher risk of UTI (aHR 1.16, 95% CI 1.09-1.24, p < 0.001). Notably, among children without genitourinary tract anomalies, ART remained significantly associated with offspring UTI (aHR 1.17, 95% CI 1.10-1.25, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Children born via ART carry an increased risk of developing UTI that is independent of known congenital structural anomalies.

articles.title: Real-world glycemic monitoring in pediatric cystic fibrosis: implementation of OGTT screening and multidisciplinary endocrinology care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess OGTT screening, glycemic abnormalities, HbA1c, and endocrinology follow-up in pediatric cystic fibrosis (CF).

METHODS: This retrospective study assessed 83 patients aged 10-18 years during 2024-2025; 20 younger patients were analyzed separately. Five with established CF-related diabetes (CFRD) were excluded from screening analyses. Historical OGTT findings were assessed separately. OGTT and HbA1c results within 90 days were compared descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 78 eligible patients, 45 (57.7%) had OGTT, 65 (83.3%) had HbA1c, and six (7.7%) had neither documented during 2024-2025. Historical OGTT results (n = 69) included normal glucose tolerance (n = 36), impaired glucose tolerance (n = 19), indeterminate glycemia (n = 10), and CFRD (n = 4). Among 26 paired results, three patients with impaired glucose tolerance had HbA1c < 5.7%, while ten with normal glucose tolerance had HbA1c 5.7-6.4%. Endocrinology follow-up was documented for 27/83 patients, including all five with CFRD.

CONCLUSIONS: OGTT documentation was incomplete, and HbA1c and OGTT categories differed. Improving OGTT completion and coordinated care remains important.

articles.title: Impact of dynamic pump speed adjustment versus constant speed in left ventricle assist device patients on exercise performance: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAdjusting pump speed in patients with left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) during exercise may improve hemodynamics and enhance functional capacity in advanced heart failure, but its clinical benefit over fixed-speed operation remains uncertain. We evaluated whether dynamic, exercise-driven LVAD speed modulation improves physical performance compared to fixed-speed settings.Methods and resultsPubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched for studies comparing dynamic adjustment versus fixed pump speed control during exercise in patients with LVADs. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using mean differences (MD), and binary outcomes using risk ratios (RR), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical analysis was performed using R (version 4.3.1). Eight studies were included, with study sample sizes totaling 124 participants; seven used crossover designs and one used a non-randomized repeated-measures design. Potential overlap between two reports from Jung et al. precluded interpretation of this total as the number of unique participants. Dynamic pump-speed modulation was associated with higher peak oxygen uptake (VO2) (MD 1.07 mL/kg/min; 95% CI 0.73 to 1.41; p < 0.001; I2 = 42%) and LVAD pump flow at peak/end of exercise (MD 1.24 L/min; 95% CI 0.68 to 1.79; p < 0.001; I2 = 89%). No differences were observed in peak cardiac output (MD 0.12 L/min; 95% CI -0.74 to 0.98; p = 0.786; I2 = 67%) or ventilatory efficiency, assessed by the VE/VCO2 slope (MD -1.58; 95% CI -3.25 to 0.09; p = 0.063; I2 = 76%).ConclusionDynamic LVAD speed adjustment may improve exercise capacity, as suggested by higher peak VO2, although peak cardiac output and ventilatory efficiency showed no clear improvement. Given the small studies, heterogeneous protocols and possible participant overlap, it remains uncertain whether this apparent benefit is sustained or clinically meaningful to patients.

articles.title: National blood transfusion and component utilisation trends in Colombia, 2019-2024: A time-series analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterise national trends in blood transfusion activity, blood component utilisation, blood supply indicators and regional variability in Colombia between 2019 and 2024, encompassing the pre-pandemic, pandemic and recovery phases.

BACKGROUND: Monitoring national transfusion activity provides insight into healthcare system performance and blood-supply management. While several high-income countries have reported stable or declining transfusion rates, longitudinal national data from middle-income settings remain limited.

METHODS/MATERIALS: A retrospective time-series study was conducted using national blood transfusion surveillance data from Colombia (2019-2024). Annual reports from the Colombian National Institute of Health were analysed to evaluate blood donation activity, blood component utilisation, transfusion practices and regional transfusion rates.

RESULTS: A total of 8 438 003 blood components were transfused across 653 healthcare institutions. National red blood cell (RBC) collection rates increased from 27.2 units per 1000 population in 2019 to 27.9 in 2024. RBC transfusion rates decreased from 18.6 per 1000 inhabitants in 2019 to 15.8 in 2020 and partially recovered to 16.8 in 2024. Buffy coat-derived platelet utilisation decreased from 14.6% to 10.0%, whereas apheresis platelet and cryoprecipitate utilisation increased from 7.8% to 9.2% and from 5.0% to 6.8%, respectively. Adult intensive care units remained the largest consumers of blood products, accounting for 27%-30% of all transfusions. Regional variability in transfusion rates persisted despite post-pandemic recovery.

CONCLUSION: The Colombian blood network demonstrated resilience following the COVID-19 pandemic. By 2024, blood collection and utilisation had stabilised at levels approaching those observed before the pandemic, suggesting the establishment of a new equilibrium in blood supply and demand.

articles.title: Progress towards the elimination of transmission of Trypanosoma brucei gambiense in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a 25-year spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gambiense human African trypanosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease caused by the parasite Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Multiple epidemics over more than two centuries have started in known risk areas termed human African trypanosomiasis foci, with DR Congo having historically carried the highest burden of disease. Since the latest resurgence of the disease in the 1990s, annual case notifications have decreased by 98%. In view of the WHO target to eliminate T b gambiense transmission globally by 2030, we aimed to outline areas of DR Congo that require intervention, aimed either at the elimination of ongoing transmission or at post-elimination surveillance.

METHODS: We conducted a spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data on gambiense human African trypanosomiasis from across DR Congo. Screening and diagnosis data from TrypElim and the WHO Atlas of human African trypanosomiasis, geolocated at the village level and covering the period from Jan 1, 2000, to Dec 31, 2024, were combined with population data from LandScan. We then used WHO methods to outline areas at low or greater risk (≥1 case per 100 000 population) and at moderate or greater risk (≥1 case per 10 000 population) of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis for the periods 2000-04, 2005-09, 2010-14, 2015-19, and 2020-24. We assessed trends in surface area at risk over the whole study period, combining these results with infection rate data to define human African trypanosomiasis foci and estimate populations recommended to be kept under post-elimination surveillance.

FINDINGS: We included data on 137 690 cases of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis identified in 12 090 unique locations. Marked decreases in the areas at risk were observed over the time period studied: the area at low or greater risk decreased from 586 508 km2 (bootstrap SE 5028) at its peak in 2005-09 to 185 216 km2 (4550) in 2020-24, a 67% reduction, and the area at moderate or greater risk decreased from 340 730 km2 (2409) in 2002-06 to 8406 km2 (1385) in 2020-24, a 97% reduction. We identified 15 distinct human African trypanosomiasis foci, three of which accounted for more than 80% (99 625 of 124 467) of reported cases. At the national level, we observed a substantial decrease in infection rate among people screened in active screening campaigns, from more than 60 cases per 10 000 population in 2000 to less than one case per 10 000 population in 2024, divided into three distinct periods: a steep decline in infection rate between 2000 and 2004 (average of 29·9% per year [95% CI 25·3 to 34·3]), no significant change between 2005 and 2010 (+1·4% [-5·0 to 8·2]), and a further decrease between 2011 and 2024 (23·5% [18·9 to 27·9]), with considerable variation at a subnational level across the 15 foci.

INTERPRETATION: The gambiense human African trypanosomiasis epidemic in DR Congo is now concentrated within a few foci, and elimination of transmission appears to be within reach. In foci with active transmission, sustained interventions remain imperative. New approaches, such as the presumptive treatment of individuals with suspected infection, could pave the way to the elimination of transmission, after which post-elimination surveillance across foci that have historically been affected will be crucial.

FUNDING: None.

articles.title: Reappraising muscarinic acetylcholine receptors as targets in substance use disorders.
articles.abstract: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptors reside in key meso-cortico-limbic areas. Their modulation of dopamine, glutamate, and GABA transmission across multiple processes (e.g., reward learning, behavioral flexibility, and motivation) makes them promising targets for novel medications treating substance use disorders (SUDs). Most of the available literature is preclinical and suggests that agonists/positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) of muscarinic M1 and M4 receptors, as well as antagonists/negative allosteric modulators (NAMs) of M5 receptors, could be beneficial. Studies investigating knockout animals and paradigms testing effects of drug consumption suggest that the absence of M1/M4 and M5 receptors leads to higher and lower drug consumption, respectively, while exposure to drugs can downregulate and upregulate M1/M4 and M5 receptors, respectively. The emergent availability of selective PET imaging ligands and medications targeting specific muscarinic receptors (e.g., KarxT, marketed as Cobenfy) holds significant promise for advancing clinical translational research investigating SUD treatment.

articles.title: Rapid prey capture learning slowly resets activity set points in rat binocular visual cortex.
articles.abstract: Neurons within primary visual cortex (V1) possess stable firing rate set points to which they faithfully return when perturbed by passive sensory manipulations. Chronic recordings in vivo suggest that these set points are present early in postnatal development and are stable through adulthood, raising the possibility that once they are established, they are largely immutable. Here, we challenge this idea using an ethological, vision-dependent prey capture learning paradigm in juvenile rats. Juvenile rats rapidly (in 1 day) became proficient at catching crickets. This learning was impaired when V1 was inactivated and was accompanied by an increase in the number of binocular V1 (V1b) neurons with firing reliably tied to specific behavioral epochs during hunts, indicating that hunting drives rapid functional plasticity within V1b. Remarkably, this rapid learning set in motion a slow, state-dependent increase in V1b firing that began after learning was complete and persisted for days. This upward firing rate plasticity was gradual, occurred selectively during wake states, and in L2/3 was driven by a TNF-α-dependent increase in excitatory synaptic drive onto pyramidal neurons-all features of homeostatic forms of V1 plasticity. Finally, TNF-α inhibition administered after learning was complete prevented this change in network excitability and impaired the consolidation of hunting skills. Taken together, these data suggest that naturalistic learning co-opts homeostatic forms of plasticity to reset firing rate setpoints within V1b, in a process that facilitates consolidation of learning.

articles.title: Nutritional and rumen microbiome determinants of enteric methane emissions in sheep: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Enteric methane (CH4) production in sheep represents both a significant global greenhouse gas challenge and a metabolic energy inefficiency, with energy losses of 6-10% of gross energy intake. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to quantitatively synthesise evidence on the genetic, nutritional and rumen microbiome determinants of methane production and methane yield (methane emitted per unit of dry matter intake, g CH4 /kg DMI) in sheep, and to evaluate integrated strategies for mitigation, including their associated carbon and water footprints. A systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library databases for peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies meeting pre-defined PICOS criteria (species: sheep; sample size ≥ 20; traits: methane production/yield; study designs: experimental and observational) were included. Data were extracted on methane emissions (g/day; g/kg dry matter intake [DMI]), dietary composition (including starch and water-soluble carbohydrate content, where reported), rumen microbial taxa and heritability estimates. Statistical synthesis employed a random-effects meta-analytic model, with heterogeneity quantified using I2 statistics and publication bias assessed via funnel plots and Egger's regression test. A total of 67 studies encompassing approximately 12,500 animals from 14 countries were included. A pooled heritability estimate of h2 = 0.19 (95% CI: 0.14-0.24; I2 = 64%) indicated moderate genetic control of methane production. High-forage, low-tannin diets significantly elevated methane output relative to concentrate-based diets, which promoted propionate fermentation pathways and reduced methanogenesis. Rumen microbiome composition, particularly the relative abundance of Methanobrevibacter spp. was significantly associated with inter-animal variation in methane yield (r = 0.58; p < 0.001). Defaunation interventions reduced methane emissions by approximately 11%. Integration of rumen microbiome data into genomic prediction models substantially improved accuracy from 0.42 (genomic-only) to 0.61 (genomic + microbiome). Carbon footprint estimates across production systems ranged from 15.8 to 17.1 kg CO2-eq/kg mutton carcass weight, and water footprint estimates ranged from 140 to 210 m3/kg mutton, tracking the same production-intensity gradient. Methane emissions in sheep are governed by the complex interplay of host genetics, rumen microbiome architecture and dietary substrate availability. Integrated approaches combining precision nutrition with microbiome-informed genomic selection represent the most effective and feasible pathway to simultaneously enhance feed efficiency and reduce environmental impact in small ruminant production systems.

articles.title: OCTA Assessment of Retinal Vascular Reactivity to Breath-Holding in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the impact of breath-holding-induced hypercapnia on retinal vessel density (VD) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) with no diabetic retinopathy (noDR) or mild non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR), using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled 90 participants equally divided into three groups: healthy controls, T2DM without diabetic retinopathy, and mild NPDR. OCTA scans of the macula and optic disk were acquired before and immediately after a 30-second breath-holding maneuver. VD was measured in the superficial and deep capillary plexuses (SCP, DCP), choriocapillaris, and radial peripapillary capillary plexus. Intra- and intergroup comparisons were performed.

RESULTS: VD in the SCP and DCP was significantly lower in the diabetic groups than in controls at baseline and after breath-holding, particularly in the mild NPDR group (Holm-adjusted p < 0.05), and the differences involving the mild NPDR group largely persisted after adjustment for systemic confounders. No significant within-group VD change was detected after breath-holding in any group, including controls, and the magnitude of change did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Retinal vessel density was reduced in patients with type 2 diabetes, particularly in those with mild NPDR, both before and after breath-holding. The response to a 30-second breath-hold did not differ from that of healthy controls, suggesting predominantly static microvascular impairment. Objective quantification of the hypercapnic stimulus is needed to establish the value of breath-holding as a simple provocation test.

articles.title: Reconsidering HPV/p16-stratified post-test risk after [18F]FDG PET/CT in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
The minimum temporal derivative of the unipolar electrogram downslope as a measure of local 3D conduction velocity in arrhythmogenic myocardium.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Re-entrant arrhythmias may be non-inducible or haemodynamically poorly tolerated, requiring substrate mapping to assess myocardial electrophysiological properties. Abnormally slowly conducting tissue, deemed critical to the initiation and maintenance of re-entrant circuits, serves as a potential catheter ablation target. However, obtaining in-procedure local conduction velocity (CV) measurements remains challenging. A more robust approach for determining local CV may enhance accurate ablation target identification.

OBJECTIVES: We sought to determine whether the minimum temporal derivative of the unipolar electrogram downslope voltage, [Formula: see text] , provides a novel quantitative measure of local 3D myocardial CV, presenting a unique parameter for identifying arrhythmogenic tissue.

METHODS: Bidomain simulations with a realistic computational ventricular slab model were performed to establish the impact of altering sodium channel conductance, gap junction conductivity, fibrosis density, fibrosis depth, tissue thickness and electrode size on unipolar electrogram metrics. Furthermore, [Formula: see text] was correlated with local CV during sodium channel block, gap junction inhibition, and ischemia, with findings corroborated in a computational human ventricular model.

RESULTS: In computational simulations, increasing fibrosis density or reducing sodium channel conductance and gap junction conductivity slowed CV, producing a corresponding inverse linear correlation between [Formula: see text] and 2D surface-based and 3D volume-based CV. During non-planar stimulation with a transmural component, a similar relationship was identified between [Formula: see text] and 3D CV. Findings were additionally supported by quantitatively comparable trends in a computational human ventricular model.

CONCLUSION: The study indicates that [Formula: see text] is directly correlated with local 3D CV, and may have utility in substrate mapping of non-inducible or haemodynamically compromising arrhythmias and intra-procedural in-silico model parameterisation.

articles.title: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in adults without HIV infection: diagnostic uncertainty, treatment-limiting toxicity, and individualized management.
articles.abstract: Contemporary immunosuppressive and anticancer therapies have broadened the population at risk of developing Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) among adults without HIV. Compared with HIV-associated PCP, disease in this population is characterized by a lower organism burden with more rapid hypoxemic deterioration, and host comorbidities and concurrent therapies may limit treatment tolerance. This focused narrative review addresses three linked problems: diagnostic uncertainty, treatment-limiting toxicity, and individualized management. Diagnosis requires assessment of the probability rather than binary interpretation as present or absent based on Pneumocystis detection, integrating immune trajectory and prophylaxis received with imaging and oxygenation, specimen adequacy, PCR results, serum β-D-glucan, and competing diagnoses. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole remains the first-line therapy, but organ dysfunction and treatment-emergent toxicity may prevent completion of treatment. Reduced-dose strategies may improve tolerability but are not established as a universal replacement for conventional dosing; apparent treatment failure should prompt reassessment of the working diagnosis and evaluation for co-infection. Current evidence does not support routine use of adjunctive corticosteroids for all patients. Selective use may be considered when evidence of PCP is strong, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure is present and competing causes of deterioration have been assessed. Primary and secondary prophylaxis should be reassessed as immune status, treatment phase, and tolerance evolve. A structured, standards-based approach applied at treatment initiation, early reassessment, and treatment completion or discharge, provides a practical framework for individualized care.

articles.title: Support for substance use problems in Swedish social services: a comparative analysis of younger and older clients' background characteristics and service use.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Young adults with substance use problems often have needs that differ from those of older adults. However, knowledge about their characteristics and service use within social services remains limited. This study compared client characteristics, interventions received, and external service use among young and older adults engaged with social services in Sweden.

METHODS: We draw upon data from an ongoing cohort study that includes journal data on 1170 clients (290 aged 18-29 years and 880 aged ≥30 years) engaged with social services. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to examine age-group differences.

RESULTS: Many clients were men, unemployed, had low educational attainment and received social assistance, although employment was more common among young adults. Young adults were more likely to have problems with illicit substances or criminality, whereas alcohol or physical health problems were more common among older adults. Mental health problems were highly prevalent in both groups. Age groups differed in part with regard to interventions received and external service contacts. Young adults were more likely to receive psychosocial treatment and to have contact with public employment services but less likely to receive case management or to have contact with harm reduction services.

CONCLUSIONS: Young adults and older adults differed in problem profiles, and to some extent in interventions received and external service contacts. The lower likelihood of young adults receiving case management despite having multiple needs and external contacts raises questions about how support is coordinated across services and warrants further research.

articles.title: Integrating the common-sense model of self-regulation into early progressive mobilization program in patients hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) have impaired physical function. Concerns about safety, falls and a perceived need for bed rest, may restrict mobility and contribute to deconditioning.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate an early progressive mobilization program based on the Common-Sense Model of Self-Regulation (CSM) in patients hospitalized for ADHF.

METHODS: A randomized trial with blinded assessment assigned 174 patients to routine care (n = 87) or the CSM-based program (n = 87). The intervention comprised four 40-60-minute face-to-face interviews and one 15-20-minute telephone consultation. Outcomes included 6-minute walk distance (6MWD), grip strength (GS), 30-second arm curl test (30s-ACT) performance, cardiac output (CO), thoracic fluid content (TFC), systolic time ratio (STR), and Exercise Benefits/Barriers Scale (EBBS) scores.

RESULTS: Least-squares mean differences (95% CIs) favored the intervention for 6MWD (16.91 m, 1.98-31.83; P = 0.026), exercise-benefit scores (6.00, 0.99-11.01; P = 0.019), and exercise-barrier scores (-2.54, -4.82 to -0.26; P = 0.029). Quantile-regression differences (95% CIs) were significant for GS (males: 3.20 kg, 1.10-5.60; P = 0.006; females: 3.10 kg, 0.50-5.80; P = 0.007), 30s-ACT performance (2.00 repetitions, 0.00-4.00; P = 0.046), CO (0.80 L/min, 0.40-1.20; P < 0.001), TFC (-3.00 kΩ⁻¹, -5.00 to 0.00; P = 0.01), and STR (-0.05%, -0.08 to 0.02; P = < 0.001). Subgroup analyses suggested greater 6MWD improvement in subgroups defined by BMI 18.5-23.9 kg/m², NYHA class I-III at admission, and anemia.

CONCLUSION: The CSM-based program improved functional and hemodynamic outcomes and exercise perceptions.

articles.title: Psychological Impact of Severe Intraoperative Complications on Surgeons: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Severe intraoperative complications may cause death or long-term morbidity. Although patient consequences are recognized, the psychological burden on surgeons remains insufficiently addressed. Surgeons involved in adverse events may become "second victims," experiencing distress that can affect their well-being, professional confidence, decision-making, and subsequent practice. This study aimed to evaluate surgeons' psychological responses following severe intraoperative complications, describe coping and support-seeking behaviors, assess changes in surgical practice, and examine perceptions of institutional psychological support.

METHODS: A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among surgeons using an anonymous questionnaire developed in French and English. The questionnaire was distributed via e-mail and WhatsApp to surgeons working across a hospital network in Lebanon. It assessed professional characteristics, exposure to severe intraoperative complications, emotional responses, coping and support-seeking behaviors, debriefing experiences, changes in practice, and perceptions of institutional support. Data were exported to Microsoft Excel and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics, version 26 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY). Descriptive analyses were performed, and an exploratory ten-item Emotions score was assessed for internal consistency using Cronbach's alpha. Its association with age was explored using Pearson correlation.

RESULTS: Sixty-nine surgeons participated, and 51 (73.9%) reported at least one severe intraoperative complication. Stress and anxiety were reported at moderate or higher levels by 94.1% and 90.2% of exposed surgeons, respectively. Sleep disturbance affected 68.6%, and 56.9% feared damage to their professional reputation. The exploratory Emotions score demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.91). In an exploratory analysis, older age was modestly associated with a lower Emotions score (r = -0.305; P = 0.029). More than half sought no professional or personal support, 62.7% participated in no debriefing, and 92.2% considered institutional psychological support insufficient.

CONCLUSIONS: Severe intraoperative complications are associated with psychological distress among surgeons, yet structured support remains uncommon. Confidential peer support, systematic debriefing, mentorship, stress-management training, and psychological care should be integrated into quality-improvement and patient-safety strategies.

articles.title: Risk factors for surgical site infection in microvascular head and neck reconstruction: Development of a I-IV stratification model.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract: Microvascular free flap reconstruction has become the standard of care for complex head and neck defects, achieving flap survival rates exceeding 90%. Despite this progress, surgical site infections (SSI) remain a major complication with incidence rates from below 10% in low-risk patients to above 40% in previously irradiated cohorts - yet no SSI specific risk stratification framework exists. 537 patients undergoing microvascular head and neck reconstruction were retrospectively analyzed. Multivariate logistic regression identified three independent SSI predictors: Prior radiotherapy, osseous reconstruction and age below 65 years were operationalized into four clinical risk factor groups (I-IV) and characterized against SSI incidence, microbiology and Cox-derived hazard accumulation. Overall SSI incidence was 25.3%. Infection rates escalated stepwise: 12.9% (I), 19.8% (II), 27.3% (III), 50.5% (IV) (p < 0.001). Risk factor group IV showed the highest proportion of patients with gram-negative SSI cultures (24.3% vs. 4.3% in group I; p < 0.001), whereas the pathogen spectrum among culture-positive SSIs did not differ significantly between groups. Three preoperative variables stratify SSI risk across a heterogeneous reconstruction cohort. Risk factor group IV - prior radiotherapy plus at least one further risk factor - identifies a high-risk free flap subgroup in which risk-adapted prophylaxis should be evaluated prospectively.

articles.title: Profile and outcomes of severe cervicofacial odontogenic infections requiring tertiary hospital admission in northeast Brazil: a 4-year cohort study with emphasis on diabetes mellitus.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Data on severe cervicofacial odontogenic infections in public tertiary centres of Latin America are scarce. The aim was to characterise the clinical and outcome profile of patients with such infections in Northeast Brazil and to assess the association between diabetes mellitus and in-hospital death.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort of all patients admitted with cervicofacial odontogenic infection at the Hospital Instituto Doutor José Frota (Fortaleza, Brazil) between January 2022 and January 2026. Exposure was diabetes mellitus; outcome was in-hospital death. Relative risk (RR), odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and Fisher's exact test were used. Fatal cases were described in detail.

RESULTS: Of 196 patients (56.6% female; mean age 33.3 years), 33 (16.8%) had diabetes. Six died, yielding in-hospital mortality of 3.1%. Mortality was 12.1% (4/33) in diabetics versus 1.2% (2/163) in non-diabetics (RR 9.9, 95% CI 1.9-51.7; OR 11.1, 95% CI 1.9-63.4; Fisher p = 0.008). Among fatal cases, the mandible was the source in 5/6; all had bilateral submandibular involvement and progressed to severe sepsis with multiple organ dysfunction; tracheostomy was required in 4/6 and acute kidney injury in 5/6. Microorganisms were isolated in 3/6 cultures (Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Candida tropicalis).

CONCLUSIONS: This cohort from a public tertiary centre in Northeast Brazil confirmed a strong association between diabetes mellitus and in-hospital death in severe cervicofacial odontogenic infection. The findings reinforce the need for early source control and intensive multidisciplinary management in diabetic patients, and contribute regional data to a literature dominated by series from other continents.

articles.title: Multi-dimensional blue-green space affordance and type 2 diabetes: A six-year longitudinal study.
articles.journal: International journal of hygiene and environmental health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Longitudinal evidence on urban blue-green spaces (UBGS) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) incidence has focused primarily on vegetation availability, with little consideration of blue-space availability or UBGS accessibility and visibility.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined the associations between multidimensional UBGS affordances and T2D incidence rates in Jiande, China.

METHODS: We followed 2048 adults aged 45-95 years without baseline T2D from 2017 to 2023. UBGS affordance encompassed availability (vegetation/water coverage), accessibility (walking distance to parks/waterfront), and visibility (window-view and street-view blue-green elements). Modified Poisson regression models with robust standard errors and a log person-time offset were used to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRRs), adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). Sensitivity models additionally included area-level housing price. Exploratory categorical analyses and interaction tests were conducted.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 288 participants (14.1%) developed T2D. Per 1-SD increase, vegetation coverage within 300 m (adjusted IRR, 0.888; 95% CI, 0.793-0.995), vegetation coverage within 500 m (0.891; 0.796-0.997), walking distance to waterfront (0.881; 0.781-0.995), and window green view index (WGVI; 0.875; 0.779-0.983) were inversely associated with T2D incidence rates. Water coverage within 1000 m was positively associated with T2D incidence rates (1.145; 1.005-1.305). After adjustment for area-level housing price, only WGVI remained inversely associated (0.880; 0.779-0.995). Interaction tests provided no evidence that the associations differed by sex, age, BMI, or follow-up period.

SIGNIFICANCE: Residential window-view greenness showed the most consistent inverse association with T2D incidence rates. Further studies should replicate this finding and investigate potential pathways.

articles.title: Macroporous resins for BHET decolorization via synergistic adsorption and photocatalysis in PET chemical recycling.
articles.abstract: Downstream purification of bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) recovered from post-consumer mixed-color polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste glycolysis is currently bottlenecked by severe 20-30 % monomer yield losses during traditional multi-stage recrystallization. To resolve this yield loss and enable high-efficiency plastic waste upcycling, this study demonstrates a bench-scale, dual-action purification strategy using an aminated macroporous resin (ATGS50) with in situ embedded TiO2 nanoparticles. By combining rapid non-covalent surface adsorption with localized UV-A photocatalytic advanced oxidation, the hybrid system eliminates complex colorants directly from crude glycolysis solutions. Process evaluations show that this dual-action strategy achieves near-complete colorant removal (99 %) while restricting single-pass monomer mass loss to 14 % (with ∼ 12.5 % attributed to physical retention and only ∼ 1.5 % to photocatalytic degradation), outperforming conventional physical separation methods. Furthermore, the functionalized resin framework displays exceptional durability, exhibiting a minor decolorization efficiency decay from 99 % to 90.1 % (a net activity loss of ∼ 8.9 %) across a 10-cycle operational reusability matrix. By converting low-value, mixed-color plastic waste into high-purity, bright-white BHET monomer with minimal material loss, this work provides a promising proof-of-concept to support future process development in sustainable PET chemical recycling.

articles.title: Baseline sarcopenia and subsequent dementia after incident atrial fibrillation or flutter in the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between sarcopenia and dementia after incident atrial fibrillation or flutter (AF/flutter) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We studied 30,743 UK Biobank participants free of AF/flutter at recruitment who subsequently had a first recorded AF/flutter event. Sarcopenia was assessed at recruitment; dementia follow-up began at that event. Analyses used Cox and Fine-Gray models, propensity-score matching and restricted cubic splines. Exploratory analyses tested interactions with AF/flutter, heart failure and coronary artery disease status at entry.

RESULTS: Sarcopenia was present in 2,279 participants (7.4%). Over a median 4.27 years after AF/flutter entry, 1,155 developed dementia. Recruitment preceded entry by a median 8.50 years. Fully adjusted analyses included 26,430 participants and 998 all-cause dementia events. Sarcopenia was associated with all-cause dementia in Cox (hazard ratio [HR], 1.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.72) and Fine-Gray models (subdistribution HR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.08-1.59). The matched Cox HR was 1.35 (95% CI, 1.09-1.66). Fully adjusted Cox HRs were 1.64 (95% CI, 1.15-2.35) for vascular dementia and 1.34 (95% CI, 0.92-1.93) for Alzheimer's disease. No interactions with cardiovascular condition status were detected.

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia assessed at recruitment was associated with all-cause dementia after incident AF/flutter. Prospective studies should assess the clinical value of muscle measurements near AF/flutter diagnosis.

articles.title: Targeting T follicular helper (Tfh) Cells for Improved Vaccine Efficacy: Lessons from Diverse Disease Models.
articles.abstract: Despite remarkable progress in vaccinology, many vaccines fail to generate durable and broadly protective immunity against rapidly evolving and deadly pathogens. Conventional vaccine strategies often rely on quantifying antibody titers or neutralizing antibodies, but accumulating evidence suggests that humoral responses alone may not ensure long-term protection. An effective vaccine must engage multiple components of the immune system, harnessing intricate cellular interactions to generate durable immunological memory. Among these, CD4+ T follicular helper (Tfh) cells have emerged as central players in orchestrating germinal center (GC) dynamics, where they provide essential signals to B cells for affinity maturation, class switching, and differentiation into memory B cells and long-lived plasma cells. Tfh cells thus directly shape the magnitude and quality of vaccine-induced antibody responses. Clinical and experimental studies across infections such as influenza, HIV, HBV, and SARS-CoV-2 highlight that robust Tfh responses correlate with effective immunity and reduced disease severity. However, most licensed vaccines elicit suboptimal or short-lived Tfh activation, underscoring a critical limitation in current vaccine design. This review provides a comprehensive overview of vaccines targeting Tfh cells across various diseases, elucidating their mechanistic contributions to vaccine-induced immunity, and how their modulation could improve next-generation vaccine strategies. By harnessing Tfh biology, future vaccines could achieve durable, high-quality antibody responses, offering improved protection against emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.

articles.title: Lenalidomide versus bortezomib maintenance after autologous stem cell transplantation in patients with high-risk multiple myeloma and chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lenalidomide maintenance is the standard of care after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) for multiple myeloma. However, evidence guiding post-transplant maintenance selection in patients with high-risk multiple myeloma and renal impairment is limited.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted an exploratory secondary analysis of the data from a previously reported retrospective Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) study. Patients with HRMM and CKD stage 3-5 undergoing ASCT between 2013 and 2018 who subsequently received lenalidomide or bortezomib maintenance were included. Renal impairment was defined as recorded diagnosis eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m². OS and PFS were analyzed from ASCT with Cox models; relapse and NRM were summarized using competing-risk cumulative incidence.

RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 136 patients (lenalidomide 100; bortezomib 36). Among 133 patients with usable survival outcomes, 11 deaths and 37 PFS events were recorded. Adjusted for age and diagnosis eGFR, the lenalidomide-versus-bortezomib HR was 1.11 (95% CI 0.29-4.20) for OS and 0.87 (95% CI 0.43-1.78) for PFS. At 24 months, relapse cumulative incidence was 26.5% versus 27.7%, respectively; NRM estimates were 1.0% versus 6.4%, based on only three NRM events.

CONCLUSIONS: No clear survival difference was observed; small event counts, treatment selection bias, and unavailable maintenance initiation dates preclude causal interpretation.

articles.title: Association of objectively measured physical activity with incident spinal stenosis in a Fitbit-linked cohort from the All of Us Research Program.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical activity is associated with numerous health benefits, but its relationship with the development of spinal stenosis remains unclear. We evaluated whether objectively measured physical activity using consumer wearable devices is associated with incident spinal stenosis.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected wearable and electronic health record data from the NIH All of Us Research Program. Adults with at least 6 months of qualifying Fitbit data linked to electronic health records were followed from the end of their sixth qualifying month. Physical activity was quantified using monthly mean daily step counts and minutes of fairly and very active activity. Incident spinal stenosis, cervical stenosis, and lumbar stenosis were identified using standardized SNOMED concepts mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model. Time-varying Cox proportional hazards models with physical activity lagged by 12 months estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for the 75th versus 25th percentile of exposure, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, education, race, smoking, diabetes, osteoarthritis, hypertension, prior spine pain, comorbidity burden, and health care use, with multiple imputation for missing covariates.

RESULTS: Among 48,709 participants free of spinal stenosis at baseline, 1,494 developed spinal stenosis during 161,900 person-years of follow-up (median 3.42 years), including 640 cervical and 982 lumbar cases. Participants at the 75th percentile of daily steps had a lower hazard of spinal stenosis than those at the 25th percentile (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.92). Estimates were similar for cervical stenosis (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.71-0.92) and lumbar stenosis (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.95), and formal tests found no difference between the two. Very active minutes were associated with a lower hazard of any and cervical stenosis (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.83-0.96, and HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.74-0.94) but not, after adjustment for multiple testing, lumbar stenosis (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-1.00). Fairly active minutes were not associated with stenosis, and we found no evidence of nonlinear dose-response relationships. The association of steps with lumbar stenosis weakened to the null with a 36-month lag, and the association with cervical stenosis was not confirmed under a stricter case definition.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher daily step counts were associated with a lower hazard of coded spinal stenosis, with similar associations for cervical and lumbar disease. The associations were modest, and reverse causation, outcome misclassification, and unmeasured confounding could explain part or all of them. LOE: III.

articles.title: Long cervicothoracic posterior instrume ntation and fusion: A retrospective complication analysis of 15 years of ACS-NSQIP data.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion carries known perioperative risk, yet 30-day morbidity and independent predictors remain poorly characterized at scale. Therefore, this study aims to provide a multi-institutional analysis of 30-day adverse events and predictors of morbidity following long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion.

METHODS: Patients undergoing long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion (2010-2024) were identified in the ACS-NSQIP database using a CPT-derived cohort definition framework composed of three query pathways, utilizing primary procedure codes for cervical arthrodesis, thoracic arthrodesis, and multi-level posterior segmental instrumentation. The primary outcome was any adverse event (AAE) within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included major, minor and infection-related complications. Exploratory multivariable logistic regression identified independent associations with AAE, with threshold analysis performed for significant continuous predictors.

RESULTS: A total of 235 patients were included (mean age = 64.4 ± 11.0 years; 51.1% male; body mass index = 29.1 ± 6.9 kg/m2). AAE occurred in 30.2% of patients, most commonly postoperative transfusion (16.6%) and return to the operating room (7.7%). Major, minor, and infection-related complications occurred in 25.1%, 11.1%, and 9.8% of patients, respectively, while 30-day mortality was 0.9%. Operative time (odds ratio [OR] = 1.004), chronic steroid use (OR = 7.080), medication-required hypertension (OR = 2.677), and neoplastic/pathologic fracture diagnostic family relative to the degenerative/myelopathic reference family (OR = 4.804) were independently associated with AAE. Threshold analysis identified a 495.5-minute operative time cut-point (95th percentile), above which the AAE rate increased from 27.8% to 75.0% (OR = 7.935), highlighting disproportionate morbidity among extreme cases.

CONCLUSION: Nearly one-third of patients experienced a 30-day adverse event following long cervicothoracic posterior instrumentation and fusion, with considerably elevated risk concentrated among exceptionally prolonged surgeries. Identified predictors further characterize the procedure-specific perioperative profile of this cohort and may help to inform risk stratification and case planning, pending validation through future large-scale, longitudinal investigation.

articles.title: Inflammatory protein trajectories and severe respiratory failure in COVID-19: a secondary analysis of the SAVE-MORE randomised trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe COVID-19 is characterised by maladaptive host inflammation. In the SAVE-MORE trial (EudraCT no. 2020-005828-11; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04680949), suPAR-guided anakinra treatment reduced mortality and progression to severe respiratory failure (SRF), but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: We performed longitudinal proteomic profiling (Olink Inflammation panel, 67 proteins) in 587 SAVE-MORE participants (400 treated with anakinra and 187 with placebo), of whom 453 had samples at all three time points (baseline, Day 4, and Day 7). Analyses aimed to (i) identify baseline predictors of SRF, (ii) define inflammatory trajectories using mixed-effects models, and (iii) characterise proteomic changes at SRF onset. Cox models identified prognostic markers, validated in an independent anakinra-treated cohort from the SAVE trial (n = 153).

FINDINGS: Multivariate Cox regression models adjusted for sex, age, BMI, and dexamethasone treatment showed that baseline IL-6 concentrations predicted SRF across both treatment arms (placebo HR = 1·99, CI: 1·31-3·02; anakinra HR = 2·12, CI: 1·56-2·87), while PD-L1 predicted SRF only in the placebo group (HR = 2·75, CI: 1·79-4·24). Anakinra allocation was associated with changes in inflammatory trajectories related to SRF progression. Patients developing SRF showed sustained activation marked by elevated concentrations of IL-6, MCP-1/3, EN-RAGE, and PD-L1, whereas SRF-free patients had higher levels of proteins linked to regulatory and adaptive immunity, including CD6, CD244, TRAIL, TNF-B, and FLT3L. Event-aligned analyses showed an acute inflammatory surge at SRF onset involving IL-6, CXCL5, OSM, and VEGFA, which was significantly attenuated by anakinra. Results were further confirmed in the SAVE cohort.

INTERPRETATION: Progression to SRF was associated with an inflammatory amplification programme involving cytokine, chemokine, tissue-injury, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Anakinra allocation was associated with smaller changes in proteins associated with inflammatory amplification and acute inflammatory changes accompanying respiratory deterioration. These findings provide biological context for the clinical benefit observed in the SAVE-MORE trial.

FUNDING: Hellenic Institute for the Study of Sepsis (sponsor) and Swedish Orphan Biovitrum (funder).

articles.title: Diurnal phase disruption as a framework to characterise stroke recovery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Daily physiological homoeostasis varies with time of day, following diurnal cycles partially regulated by the central autonomic network (CAN). Experimental studies suggest that acute ischaemic stroke disrupts these rhythms, impairing recovery, but translation to humans has been limited by the lack of robust methods to quantify diurnal phase shifts.

METHODS: We developed a framework that uses continuous heart rate data to characterise shifts in diurnal cardiac rhythms relative to the phase expected at a given time of day, providing a dynamic marker of heart-brain axis function. We applied this approach to retrospective data from patients with ischaemic stroke in the Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin Data Warehouse (DWC) and the MIMIC-III/IV cohorts, quantifying rhythm shifts and examining their associations with lesion size, location, and clinical outcomes.

FINDINGS: Stroke was associated with systematic disruption of diurnal cardiac cycles, with larger shifts associated with worse clinical scores, impaired short-term recovery, and higher mortality. Within the CAN, greater rhythm shifts corresponded to larger infarcts, indicating region-specific vulnerability.

INTERPRETATION: These findings identify diurnal cardiac rhythm shifts as a clinically accessible biomarker of heart-brain-axis function. Given the observational design, these associations are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

FUNDING: The Schilling Foundation and the Schilling Professorship, DFG EXC-2049/NeuroCure.

articles.title: Perceived stigma, social support, and associated factors among adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is frequently associated with perceived stigma and inadequate social support, both of which adversely affect patients' psychosocial well-being and quality of life. This study aimed to investigate perceived stigma, perceived social support, the relationship between these variables, and factors associated with both among adults with epilepsy. A descriptive, cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted with 147 adults diagnosed with epilepsy who attended the Neurology Outpatient Clinic of Harran University Hospital between June 2025-June 2026. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Perceived Stigma Scale, and the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support. The mean perceived stigma score was 26.58 ± 9.34, while the mean total perceived social support score was 51.91 ± 18.87. Higher perceived stigma was significantly associated with lower educational level, unemployment, work impairment due to epilepsy, lower income, the presence of another chronic disease, concealing the epilepsy diagnosis, and perceiving that others avoided them because of epilepsy (p < 0.05). Higher educational level and not perceiving social rejection were associated with greater perceived social support (p < 0.05). Perceived stigma demonstrated a significant weak negative correlation with total perceived social support (r = -0.405, p = 0.001). These findings highlight the importance of considering stigma and social support in the psychosocial care of people with epilepsy. Healthcare professionals should assess these needs and facilitate access to appropriate psychosocial resources, including peer support and self-management programmes. In addition, public education initiatives and targeted support programmes may help address misconceptions about epilepsy, reduce stigma, and enhance social acceptance.

articles.title: From rescue to precision: breaking the salvage-therapy curse in refractory septic shock.
articles.abstract: Refractory septic shock is managed with a small core of evidence-based treatments and a growing number of salvage therapies, including methylene blue, the vitamin C cocktail, and several blood purification devices. Each has a plausible mechanism, may improve physiological or haemodynamic surrogates, and most remain without definitive evidence of survival benefit in unselected patients. Recent biomarker-selected evidence with polymyxin B, however, suggests that patient selection may be critical. This article argues that most remain unproven because of how they are deployed and tested, not because their mechanisms fail. Given late to the sickest patients, they are subject to confounding by indication, a ceiling effect on attribution, and responder-biased reporting, which together generate a misleading reputation independent of any true effect. Drawing on oXiris, vitamin C, and polymyxin B as worked examples, and on methylene blue and therapeutic plasma exchange as unresolved cases now in trials, the article contends that the way to resolve this problem is to identify a measurable treatable trait and randomise the patients who have it. Polymyxin B illustrates this, having been neutral in an unselected trial and beneficial once patients were selected by endotoxin activity.

articles.title: Therapeutic lactate in critically ill patients: Fuel, fluid, or drug?
articles.abstract: Lactate occupies a paradoxical position in critical care. Traditionally regarded as a marker of physiological stress, it is increasingly recognized as an important metabolic substrate with potential therapeutic effects. In their meta-analysis of randomized trials, Labenbacher and colleagues summarize the current clinical evidence for hypertonic sodium lactate treatment (HSL) across heterogeneous critically ill populations. Although no mortality benefit can be established, the available evidence raises several important mechanistic and methodological questions. First, "lactate therapy" is not a single intervention as HSL simultaneously alters lactate availability, sodium load, tonicity, and acid-base balance. Second, currently used regimens differ markedly in dose, duration, and achieved plasma lactate concentrations, precluding a meaningful dose-exposure-response framework. Third, the physiological response may depend strongly on the underlying hemodynamic and metabolic phenotype with signals of improved cardiac output in some cardiovascular settings but inconsistent findings across other disease states. At this stage, the key question is therefore not simply whether lactate "works" nor whether it improves mortality, but which physiological effect is being targeted, in which patient phenotype, at what exposure, and through which mechanism. Future studies should disentangle the metabolic, osmotic, vascular, and acid-base effects of lactate-containing solutions before definitive clinical outcome trials are undertaken.

articles.title: Rehabilitation prescription tools in critical care: why reinvent the wheel?
Hepatitis C seroprevalence and its association with injecting drug use among people who use drugs in the West Bank, Palestine: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: The International journal on drug policy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People who use drugs (PWUD) are at increased risk of blood-borne viral infections. Evidence on hepatitis C virus (HCV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) among PWUD in Palestine is limited. This study determined the seroprevalence of HCV, HBV, and HIV among PWUD attending governmental substance use disorder (SUD) treatment centers in the West Bank.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 397 PWUD in SUD treatment centers in the West Bank during 2019-2023. Serological results for anti-HCV, HBsAg, and anti-HIV were obtained from routine clinical records. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) for the association between injecting drug use and anti-HCV seropositivity were estimated using modified Poisson regression.

RESULTS: HCV seroprevalence was 23.0%, HBsAg prevalence was 2.0%, and no HIV was detected. HCV seroprevalence was 55.4% among injecting versus 6.7% among non-injecting users. After adjustment for age, education, employment status, and previous treatment attempts, injecting drug use remained strongly associated with HCV seropositivity (adjusted PR = 6.43, 95% CI 3.82-10.82). HCV prevalence increased with longer duration of drug use (p for trend <0.001), and varied significantly across governorates.

CONCLUSIONS: HCV is the predominant infection among PWUD receiving SUD treatment in the West Bank, whereas HBV prevalence was low and HIV was not detected. Injecting drug use was strongly associated with HCV seropositivity, and prevalence increased with longer duration of drug use. Integrating HCV screening, RNA testing, antiviral treatment, and harm-reduction policies into SUD services is essential to achieve the WHO 2030 hepatitis elimination targets.

articles.title: "I hardly fall asleep because I keep thinking about my child": Psychosocial experiences of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James Centre Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, Malawi.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Admission of a child to a paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) is highly distressing for caregivers, who face uncertainty about the child's outcome and disruption of normal caregiving roles. In low-resource settings such as Malawi, where psychosocial support is limited, little is known about caregivers' experiences during their child's PICU admission.

OBJECTIVES: This study explored psychosocial experiences, coping mechanisms and support needs of caregivers of children admitted to Mercy James PICU in Malawi.

METHODS: A qualitative exploratory-descriptive study was conducted between October and December 2024 at Mercy James PICU within Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre. Eleven caregivers of children admitted for over 48 h were purposively sampled for in-depth, semi-structured interviews, which were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, translated and analysed thematically. The transactional theory of stress and coping guided interpretation of findings.

RESULTS: Four themes were identified: emotional and psychological distress, caregivers' perceptions of care delivery, coping mechanisms and perceived support needs. Caregivers experienced both immediate and ongoing distress associated with sudden PICU admission, uncertainty, separation from family and financial strain. Perceptions of care were shaped by interactions with staff and hospital environment. Caregivers used both problem-focused strategies, like information seeking, and emotion-focused strategies like reliance on God, social support and acceptance. They reported unmet needs for psychological support, compassionate care and access to food.

CONCLUSION: Caregivers of children in PICU experience significant psychosocial challenges shaped by admission context, environment and limited support. Strengthening communication and information-sharing practices, compassionate care, structured emotional support and addressing basic needs is essential.

articles.title: Congestion Assessed With Inferior Vena Cava Ultrasound Predicts Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inferior vena cava (IVC) parameters relate to clinical outcomes in retrospective acute decompensated heart failure (ADHF) studies, but prospective data on long-term outcomes and quality of life are unavailable.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to evaluate the prognostic value of IVC parameters for clinical outcomes and their association with quality of life.

METHODS: Patients admitted for ADHF were prospectively enrolled from January 2022 to May 2024. Point-of-care IVC ultrasound was performed at admission and discharge. The Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) was evaluated at baseline, 1, 6, and 12 months. The primary endpoint was the composite of all-cause mortality and ADHF rehospitalization at 12 months.

RESULTS: A total of 100 patients (median age 67 years, 28% women, 45% NYHA functional class III/IV, 65% heart failure with reduced ejection fraction) were included. The primary endpoint occurred in 50 patients (9 deaths and 41 ADHF hospitalizations). In multivariable analysis, admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm (HR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.97-7.01; P < 0.001), admission maximum IVC diameter >2.3 cm (HR: 2.70; 95% CI: 1.46-4.96; P = 0.001), discharge minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.3 cm (HR: 2.27; 95% CI: 1.24-4.14; P = 0.008), and discharge sniff IVC collapsibility index <36% (HR: 3.16; 95% CI: 1.64-6.06; P < 0.001) were independent predictors of the primary endpoint. KCCQ scores improved during follow-up (Ptime<0.001) but were not associated with the primary endpoint. Patients with admission minimum IVC sniff diameter >1.6 cm had lower KCCQ scores throughout the study period (Pgroup = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: In ADHF patients, IVC parameters predict 12-month outcomes and may serve as objective markers to identify residual congestion and stratify risk.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation and Risk of Late-Onset Dementia: A Danish Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity, but its relationship with dementia remains incompletely understood.

OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to examine the association between AF and late-onset dementia in a nationwide Danish cohort.

METHODS: In this Danish nationwide registry-based cohort study, individuals aged ≥50 years with first-time AF between 2005 and 2025 were matched 1:5 with controls from the general population on age, sex, and calendar year. Late onset dementia was defined as a first-time dementia diagnosis or antidementia medication initiation at age ≥65 years. Cumulative incidences were estimated at 1, 3, and 5 years, and associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. Secondary outcomes were thromboembolic events and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 326,687 AF patients and 1,633,435 matched controls were included (median age 75 years; 55% male). The median follow-up was 8.6 years. AF was associated with an increased hazard of late-onset dementia (HR: 1.14; 95% CI: 1.12-1.17), which persisted after adjustment for cardiovascular comorbidity (HR: 1.17; 95% CI: 1.15-1.19) and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events (HR: 1.16; 95% CI: 1.13-1.18). The association remained stable across calendar periods, whereas the hazard of thromboembolic events attenuated over time.

CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with late-onset dementia after adjustment for cardiovascular risk factors and exclusion of individuals with prior thromboembolic events. The stable association over 2 decades, despite attenuation of the association with thromboembolic events, suggests that dementia is an important long-term consequence of AF.

articles.title: Dynamic Exposome-Based Cardiovascular Prevention: The SENTINEL EXPOSOME.
Thermodynamic Response During Invasive Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Core temperature is continuously measured during invasive cardiopulmonary exercise testing (iCPET), but its physiologic and clinical significance remains poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to characterize exercise core temperature responses during iCPET and determine whether temperature-derived metrics are associated with cardiopulmonary reserve, abnormal physiologic phenotypes, and clinically relevant iCPET thresholds.

METHODS: We studied 396 adults undergoing iCPET for unexplained exertional intolerance. Core temperature was measured using the thermistor of a pulmonary artery catheter. Temperature-derived metrics included peak exercise temperature, increase in temperature from baseline to peak exercise, and increase in temperature indexed to peak workload. Associations with hemodynamic and gas-exchange variables were assessed using age- and sex-adjusted models. Area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve (AUC) analyses evaluated discrimination for normal vs abnormal iCPET findings and selected physiologic thresholds.

RESULTS: Participants were 50.6 ± 16.0 years old, and 66% were female. Core temperature increased during exercise from 37.0 °C ± 0.34 °C at baseline to 37.5 °C ± 0.51 °C at peak exercise, with a mean increase of 0.40 °C ± 0.37 °C. Temperature-derived metrics were directly associated with peak cardiac index and percent-predicted peak oxygen uptake and inversely associated with pulmonary artery occlusion pressure/cardiac output slope and minute ventilation/carbon dioxide production slope. Temperature responses were blunted in heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, chronotropic incompetence, and impaired peripheral oxygen extraction. For identifying a normal test, age- and sex-adjusted AUCs were 0.70 for peak exercise temperature, 0.74 for increase in temperature, and 0.68 for workload-indexed temperature increase.

CONCLUSIONS: Exercise core temperature responses during iCPET reflect hemodynamic augmentation and aerobic performance and may provide a simple adjunctive physiologic marker for clinically relevant exercise abnormalities.

articles.title: Early Outcomes of M-TEER in Patients With Connective Tissue Diseases: Insights From a Real-World Database.
Beyond Short-Term Relief: From External Dependence to Sustainable Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in Africa.
Outcomes Among Patients Receiving Watchman LAAO vs Antiplatelet Therapy: A Report From the GWTG-AFIB Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was approved for patients with atrial fibrillation who can tolerate short term anticoagulation, many patients are poor candidates for any duration of anticoagulation.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare 1-year outcomes among patients receiving Watchman LAAO vs antiplatelet monotherapy.

METHODS: We performed an overlap weighted observational comparative effectiveness analysis of postdischarge outcomes among Medicare beneficiaries in the Get With The Guidelines-AFIB Registry who received LAAO or antiplatelet therapy. Cox Regression was used for all-cause mortality and cause-specific hazard models were used for nonfatal outcomes. A win ratio was calculated with the following endpoint hierarchy: 1) all-cause death; 2) stroke, systemic embolism, or transient ischemic attack (TIA); 3) major bleeding (excluding gastrointestinal bleeding); and 4) gastrointestinal bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 1,427 patients who received LAAO and 2,284 patients who received antiplatelet therapy were studied (overall median age 77 years, 49.3% female, median CHA2DS2-VASC score 5). Through the first 45 days, the adjusted risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.26; CI: 0.17-0.41; P < 0.001). Between 46 days and 1 year, the risk for the composite outcome was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.61; CI: 0.48-0.78; P < 0.001). The win ratio at 1 year was 2.71 (95% CI: 1.92-3.83; P < 0.0001), indicating significantly better outcomes among LAAO patients.
