CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrial fibrillation, treatment with LAAO was associated with a lower risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death compared to antiplatelet therapy.

articles.title: Multiview Integration for Robust Echocardiographic Embeddings: Accessible AI for Clinical Practice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although recent artificial intelligence (AI) foundation models have shown superior performance in medical imaging, their high computational demands and reliance on large data sets limit accessibility. These issues are especially pronounced in echocardiography, where integrating complex multiview measurements for individual cases hinders AI development and clinical translation. Vector embedding approaches offer promising solutions by leveraging compact representations in AI applications.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop a transformer-based multiview encoder that integrates multiple echocardiographic videos into unified vector embeddings and uses adversarial learning to reduce reliance on demographic shortcuts.

METHODS: Using the MIMIC-IV-ECHO (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV-Echocardiography) data set (7,169 studies), we trained a multiview encoder to produce study-level embeddings and evaluated them on 21 binary classification tasks covering echocardiographic measurements and clinical diagnoses. We varied adversarial weights to assess their impact on demographic shortcut reliance and overall performance.

RESULTS: The multiview encoder raised the mean area under the curve (AUC) across clinical tasks from 0.742 to 0.831 compared with the foundation model embedding (ΔAUC +0.090; 95% CI: 0.078-0.100), with significant gains in 20 of 21 tasks. The embeddings remained robust with a limited number of views (mean ΔAUC +0.071; 95% CI: 0.043-0.113). Adversarial learning reduced sex and race predictability only at strong weights and at substantial cost to clinical performance.

CONCLUSIONS: The multiview encoder framework integrates multiple echocardiographic views into unified study-level embeddings, enabling substantial diagnostic improvements across diverse cardiac tasks. By producing compact, informative embeddings without requiring extensive computational resources, this approach lowers the cost of building echocardiographic AI on an existing foundation model.

articles.title: Effect of Prereperfusion Dapagliflozin Loading on Infarct Size, Mitochondrial Function, and Ventricular Remodeling in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors demonstrate cardioprotective effects in preclinical ischemia-reperfusion models, potentially mediated by mitochondrial modulation, but their benefit in acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction remains uncertain. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 60 patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention were assigned to dapagliflozin (20 mg prereperfusion followed by 10 mg daily) or placebo for 12 weeks. The primary endpoint was enzymatic infarct size assessed by the 72-hour area under the curve of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I. Dapagliflozin did not reduce infarct size compared with placebo (adjusted difference: -0.89 × 106 arbitrary unit; P = 0.47). Although mitochondrial respiratory capacity increases transiently at 2 weeks, this effect was not sustained. Left ventricular function improved similarly in both groups, and cardiac magnetic resonance-derived infarct size did not differ significantly. Prereperfusion dapagliflozin was not associated with reduced infarct size despite transient mitochondrial modulation. The neutral findings should be interpreted in the context of the brief drug-to-wire interval and the limited statistical power of this pilot trial.

articles.title: Factors influencing nurse-family communication in intensive care units in the Canary Islands: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Communication between nurses and families in intensive care units (ICUs) is an essential component of humanized care. Effective communication is associated with greater family satisfaction and a lower incidence of post-intensive care syndrome in families. However, training and organizational barriers persist that hinder its development.

OBJECTIVE: To explore nurses' perceptions of communication with families in the ICUs of public hospitals in the Canary Islands and to identify factors associated with a greater predisposition and communicative capacity.

METHOD: A multicenter, cross-sectional, descriptive study was conducted between March and July 2025 with ICU nurses in public hospitals in the Canary Islands. Nurse-family communication was assessed using the validated Nurse Activities for Communicating with Families questionnaire and a complementary ad-hoc form. Descriptive, bivariate, and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 215 nurses participated, with a mean age of 37 ± 8 years; 71% were women and 41% had postgraduate training. Participants showed high involvement in communication related to treatments, care, and patient comfort, as well as a high perception of the usefulness of communication in family support and the prevention of post-intensive care syndrome in families (91%; 95% CI 87-95). However, emotional, spiritual, and cultural dimensions were addressed less frequently. Postgraduate training (p = 0.001), self-perception of specific training (p = 0.034), and the consideration of communication as a professional duty (p = 0.003) were independently associated with a greater predisposition and communicative ability.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings show that nurses' communicative competence is conditioned by educational, ethical, and organizational factors. Advanced training and certain ethical-professional factors were associated with greater perceived communicative competence, reinforcing the need to implement training and organizational strategies that strengthen nurse-family communication in intensive care.

articles.title: Severe cytopenia in dogs treated with fenbendazole for Heterobilharzia americana.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report the features and outcomes of dogs experiencing severe febrile cytopenia following treatment with fenbendazole for Heterobilharzia americana.

ANIMALS: 6 client-owned dogs that received fenbendazole for treatment of H americana and subsequently developed severe transient cytopenia with accompanying clinical illness were evaluated.

CLINICAL PRESENTATION: In this observational retrospective multicenter case series, medical records of affected dogs reported by veterinarians through consultation with the Gastrointestinal Laboratory at Texas A&M University between June 2023 and November 2025 were reviewed. Dogs were included if they had a diagnosis of H americana by fecal PCR or saline sedimentation, received treatment with fenbendazole, and developed an episode of cytopenia with accompanying clinical signs within 21 days of beginning treatment.

RESULTS: All dogs were spayed females, representing a variety of breeds. Six dogs received praziquantel and fenbendazole for treatment. Five of these dogs received concurrent doses of pyrantel pamoate and febantel through use of a combination tablet as the source of praziquantel, resulting in high total benzimidazole drug exposure. Dogs developed marked neutropenia, variable thrombocytopenia, fever, and severe clinical illness warranting hospitalization. All dogs experienced hematologic and clinical recovery following discontinuation of fenbendazole, supportive care, and administration of short-term parenteral antimicrobials.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Prescribing veterinarians should remain aware of the risk for cytopenia with extralabel use of fenbendazole to treat H americana infection in dogs. The use of combination products to dose praziquantel is contraindicated, as it may also contain febantel and could expose dogs to toxic doses of benzimidazole.

articles.title: The role of 18F-AlF-NOTA-octreotide PET/CT in assessing recurrent carotid body paraganglioma and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy eligibility: A case report.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
articles.abstract: Paragangliomas (PGLs) are a rare class of neuroendocrine tumors arising from the autonomic nervous system ganglia, which may be either parasympathetic or sympathetic. We present the case of a 49-year-old female patient with a history of cervicalgia and paroxysmal adrenergic symptoms. Her medical history included surgical resection of functional bilateral carotid body PGLs (Shamblin III on the right and Shamblin II on the left), as well as a positive family history of PGL. Cervical magnetic resonance imaging showed no evidence of lesions. However, ¹¹¹In-octreotide scintigraphy revealed a discrete focal area of abnormal radiotracer uptake on the left side of the neck. Further evaluation with Al¹⁸F-1,4,7-triazacyclononane-1,4,7-triacetate-octreotide (¹⁸F-AlF-NOTA-octreotide) PET/CT identified three hypermetabolic cervical foci. Despite its rarity, PGL should never be excluded from the differential diagnosis when clinical symptoms and diagnostic findings are consistent with its etiology. This report serves as a reminder that rare diagnoses deserve consideration and contributes an additional case of PGL to the current literature.

articles.title: Preoperative Cervical Epidural Steroid Injection Within Three Months of ACDF Is Associated with Increased Long-Term Pseudoarthrosis and Reoperation Rates: A Propensity Matched Retrospective Analysis.
articles.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective Cohort Analysis.ObjectiveA mainstay in the nonoperative management of symptomatic degenerative cervical spondylosis (DCS) remains cervical epidural corticosteroid injections (CESI). Given the increasing burden of DCS and the resultant number of patients likely to receive CESI before ACDF, it is integral to clarify the implications of these injections. The objective of the present study was to clarify the associations between preoperative CESI and postoperative outcomes amongst ACDF patients.MethodsA retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX database. Patients undergoing ACDF were identified and stratified by preoperative CESI exposure. After 1:1 propensity score matching for demographics and comorbidities, 1,193 patients remained in each cohort. The primary outcome was a coded diagnosis of pseudarthrosis after fusion or arthrodesis; secondary outcomes were new-onset cervicalgia, new-onset cervical disc displacement, surgical site infection, and all-cause coded cervical reoperation.ResultsIn those patients exposed to CESI within 3 months of ACDF at 1, 3, and 5 years postoperatively, elevated rates of pseudoarthrosis (13.33% vs. 8.72%, RR 1.53, 95% CI 1.21-1.93, p < 0.001) and new onset cervicalgia (35.42% vs. 23.52%, RR 1.51, 95% CI, p = 0.001) were found. Reoperation rates were significantly higher in the injection group at 5 years (3.86% vs. 2.18%, RR 1.77, 95% CI 1.10-2.84, p = 0.018). No significant differences were noted among patients injected 3-6 months, 6 months to 1 year, and those injected more than 1 year before ACDF.ConclusionsCESI performed within three months of ACDF was associated with higher rates of pseudoarthrosis and of subsequent cervical reoperation.

articles.title: Frequency and Patient Throughput Characteristics of Implanted Cardiac Device Interrogation in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs), such as pacemakers and implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, frequently present to the emergency department (ED) with complaints potentially attributable to their devices. Device interrogation can characterize arrhythmias and guide management, but whether it represents a bottleneck to disposition has not been systematically studied.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study at two academic centers (2024-2026). Visits were identified via consultations. Control cohorts of patients with general cardiology and EP consultations with pacemakers were propensity score matched. Intervals were compared via Kruskal-Wallis tests. Logistic regression investigated associations between demographic factors, time intervals, and admission.

RESULTS: We identified 677 visits from 479 unique patients involving CIED-related EP consultation. The median ED length of stay (LOS) was 24.3 hours (IQR 10.2-36.1), with 80.4% admitted. General cardiology and EP consults without interrogation demonstrated similar times to consultation (4.0 [IQR 1.8-11.1] and 3.0 [IQR 0.9-12.4], p=0.4 and p=0.1), but shorter from consult to disposition (13.3 hours [IQR 12.7-14.4] vs. 5.2 [IQR 4.5-5.9] and 6.8 [IQR 6.0-7.5], both p<0.001). Consults with interrogation after hours were prolonged (14.9 [IQR 7.1-20.5] vs 7.1 [IQR 5.4-11.1], p<0.001). In the logistic regression, longer consultations were associated with higher likelihood of admission (aOR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.07 per hour). No other factors were significant.

CONCLUSION: Patients requiring CIED interrogation experienced delays relative to other patients, with interrogation as the proximate step before disposition. Consults after hours took longer, and delays were independently associated with admission. These findings highlight an operational bottleneck in acute CIED management, and efforts to expedite device interrogation warrant further investigation.

articles.title: FAIR-Lupus: A Descriptive Monte Carlo Exploration of Excess-Risk Scores in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFAIR-Lupus explores the Normalized Excess-Risk Contribution (NERC), a descriptive mathematical index comparing selected prevalence-weighted association scores in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). It does not estimate causal attribution or attributable disease fractions.MethodsA newly specified analysis replaced the submitted results. Two fixed synthetic cohorts of 100,000 subjects represented female SLE susceptibility and established SLE. We propagated multiplier uncertainty through 10,000 Monte Carlo draws and examined determinant exclusions, correlations preserving exposure frequencies, an illustrative interaction, and EBV prevalence scenarios. All exposure prevalences and the four flare risk multipliers were illustrative. No observed outcomes were analysed.ResultsIncident-scenario median NERC was 50.3% for family history and 34.7% for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) seropositivity; their rank-one frequencies were 75.31% and 24.66%. Flare-scenario medians were 35.6% for stress, 26.7% for respiratory infection, 21.5% for occupational ultraviolet exposure, and 14.8% for PM2.5. Excluding family history increased EBV median NERC to 70.8%. Correlation alone produced no change when marginal exposure counts were fixed. Varying EBV prevalence from 70% to 98% changed its median share from 28.1% to 35.4%.ConclusionsNERC percentages depend on the selected determinants, exposure prevalences and multipliers; they are not proportions of disease attributable to those determinants. FAIR-Lupus is a methodological exploration without empirical validation and cannot support clinical, occupational-health or individualized causal decisions.

articles.title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Predicting Significant Fibrosis in Steatotic Liver Disease: Model Development Study.
articles.journal: Online journal of public health informatics
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent, and noninvasive identification of patients with significant fibrosis remains a clinical challenge.

OBJECTIVE: We conducted an exploratory evaluation of explainable machine learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a US-based cohort of adults with SLD, with particular attention to sensitivity, false-negative risk, and the limitations of using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) alone to assess screening suitability.

METHODS: We evaluated explainable machine learning models for predicting significant fibrosis in a US population-based dataset. A total of 43 routinely available clinical, demographic, anthropometric, laboratory, and lifestyle variables were included. After preprocessing and imputation, data were split into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets. The synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) was used to address class imbalance in the training set. Logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), k-nearest neighbors, naive Bayes, an artificial neural network, and a stacked ensemble were trained and evaluated. Performance metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Cohen κ, and the AUROC. Because the intended use case was screening or triage, sensitivity was given particular interpretive importance. In addition to overall discrimination, a primary analytical objective was to examine sensitivity trade-offs, false-negative classifications, and the implications of model performance for screening suitability. Global and local model interpretability were assessed using feature importance, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) values, individual conditional expectation (ICE) plots, and individualized explanations.

RESULTS: Among 7056 participants, 716 (10.1%) had significant fibrosis. XGBoost achieved the highest discrimination (AUROC 0.79), followed by random forest (AUROC 0.78) and logistic regression (AUROC 0.77); however, XGBoost had low sensitivity (0.17), indicating limited utility for screening at the evaluated threshold. Logistic regression and naive Bayes demonstrated the highest sensitivity (0.65 and 0.55, respectively), suggesting that models with slightly lower discrimination may be more appropriate for triage-oriented use. Across models, waist circumference, BMI, cardiovascular comorbidity, sex, hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), and liver enzymes were the most influential predictors.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory model development study, moderate discrimination did not necessarily translate into clinically meaningful screening performance. The model with the highest AUROC showed poor sensitivity, indicating a substantial risk of false-negative classifications and limiting its usefulness for screening in its current form. Because imputation was performed before the train-test split, the reported performance estimates may be optimistic and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of clinical readiness. Leakage-free preprocessing, threshold optimization, calibration assessment, decision curve analysis, external validation, and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical application.

articles.title: A Propensity-Matched TriNetX Cohort of Preoperative Opioid Exposure Compared to No Opioid Exposure Following Partial Colectomy or Proctectomy.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPreoperative systemic opioid exposure is common in colorectal surgery and may identify patients at increased risk for postoperative complications. We evaluated 30-day outcomes after partial colectomy or proctectomy.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using de-identified TriNetX Global Collaborative Network data. Adults undergoing partial colectomy or proctectomy were compared according to systemic opioid exposure between 3 months and 1 day before surgery. Patients with opioid-related disorders, chronic pain diagnoses, palliative-care encounters, medications for opioid use disorder, selected acute abdominal conditions, or preexisting outcomes were excluded. Cohorts were propensity-matched 1:1 using demographic, comorbidity, malignancy/treatment, nutritional, IBD/immunosuppressive, BMI, albumin, and colorectal procedure-code variables. The primary outcome was postoperative wound dehiscence. Secondary outcomes were infection, ileus, sepsis, and gastrointestinal complications. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied.ResultsAfter matching, 10,077 patients were included in each cohort. Preoperative systemic opioid exposure was associated with higher 30-day wound-dehiscence risk (1.57% vs 1.15%; RR 1.362, 95% CI 1.074-1.728; absolute risk difference 0.42 percentage points, 95% CI 0.10-0.70; P = .011). No secondary outcome remained significant after correction; gastrointestinal complications were nominally higher (RR 1.222, 95% CI 1.031-1.450; raw P = .021; adjusted P = .084).ConclusionsPreoperative systemic opioid exposure was associated with a modest absolute increase in 30-day postoperative wound dehiscence. Secondary outcomes did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support opioid exposure as a perioperative risk marker rather than proof of causality.

articles.title: A Mobile Diabetes Prevention Intervention Among Chinese Americans at Risk for Diabetes: Qualitative Analysis of Barriers and Facilitators to Intervention Engagement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chinese Americans experience a high prevalence of prediabetes and face barriers to accessing diabetes prevention services. Adapted from the National Diabetes Prevention Program, the Integrating Cultural Aspects into Diabetes Education (INCLUDE) program is a culturally and linguistically tailored mobile health (mHealth) diabetes prevention intervention for Chinese Americans. The 12-week program combines 2 to 3 educational videos per week delivered through WeChat or text messaging, biweekly coaching calls with community health workers, and weekly produce provision. A randomized controlled trial evaluated the efficacy of INCLUDE on weight loss among Chinese Americans at risk for diabetes in New York City.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine barriers and facilitators to engagement in INCLUDE and elicit participants' recommendations for intervention improvement.

METHODS: This study was embedded within the INCLUDE trial. Among 75 trial participants in the intervention arm, 32 were purposively selected by engagement level (high vs low) and study year (year 1 vs year 2), and 25 completed postintervention qualitative interviews between February and December 2024. Twenty participants attended 1 of 4 focus groups (4 to 7 participants per group) stratified by engagement level and study year, and 5 completed one-on-one in-depth interviews due to scheduling conflicts preventing them from focus group participation. Semistructured interviews explored 4 domains, including reasons for participation, perceptions of INCLUDE, barriers and facilitators to engagement, and recommendations for improvement. Interviews were conducted in Mandarin or Cantonese, audio-recorded, and transcribed verbatim in Chinese. Three bilingual coders (NJ, JL, and AM) conducted thematic analysis using deductive and inductive approaches.

RESULTS: Participants had a mean age of 53.6 (SD 12.3) years; 20 of 25 (80%) were women, 13 (52%) participated in year 1, and 12 (48%) participated in year 2. Eleven (44%) participants had low engagement and 14 (56%) had high engagement. Six facilitators of engagement were identified, including motivation to prevent diabetes, trust in community organizations, perceived gains from participation, culturally and linguistically concordant content, accessibility through digital delivery, and personalized guidance and human support. Three barriers were identified, including time constraints, challenges related to the produce component, and insufficient support for translating knowledge into sustained behavior change. Participants recommended more actionable dietary guidance, additional home-based physical activity options, shorter or alternative coaching formats, and more flexible and culturally responsive produce support.

CONCLUSIONS: INCLUDE was generally well received among Chinese Americans at risk for diabetes. Future research should focus on addressing identified barriers by making diabetes prevention guidance more actionable and delivery more compatible with daily life. These findings may inform future diabetes prevention strategies for Chinese American populations.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05492916; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05492916.

INTERNATIONAL REGISTERED REPORT IDENTIFIER (IRRID): RR2-10.2196/65455.

articles.title: Development of PRECISE, a Data-Driven Personalized Suicide Prevention Intervention: Protocol for an Intervention Refinement Pilot and Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STBs) are heterogeneous in their causes and course, yet most interventions rely on nomothetic, one-size-fits-all models. Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) is an evidence-based treatment for STBs, but its standard year-long format is resource-intensive and difficult to access. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) combined with idiographic (person-specific) statistical modeling offers a way to identify which emotion regulation processes are driving an individual's risk, and in turn to select the DBT skills most relevant for that person.

OBJECTIVE: This protocol describes the refinement (aim 1) and preliminary evaluation (aim 2) of PRECISE (Personalized Clinical Intervention for Suicidal Events), an 8-week, EMA-informed, idiographically tailored adjunctive treatment for adults with active suicidal ideation.

METHODS: In aim 1, an existing PRECISE treatment manual and clinician dashboard will be iteratively refined with a mentorship and advisory panel and tested for feasibility and acceptability in a small, randomized pilot study (n=10; n=5 per arm), comparing high- and low-intensity personalization schedules. In aim 2, 60 adults with active suicidal ideation will be randomized to a high-intensity (weekly idiographic model updates across all 8 EMA-monitored weeks) or low-intensity (single idiographic model generated after an initial 2-week EMA burst) version of PRECISE. Both arms will receive coach-delivered DBT skills selected according to each participant's idiographic model, which will be generated using the group iterative multiple model estimation (GIMME) algorithm. Primary outcomes include usability, retention, EMA adherence, acceptability, and fidelity; secondary and exploratory analyses will examine trajectories of suicidal ideation and a within-person mediation model linking emotion regulation to STBs.

RESULTS: The trial registration record (ClinicalTrials.gov) was first posted on February 5, 2025, and enrollment began on November 14, 2025. The study is currently recruiting. Estimated total enrollment across aim 1 and aim 2 is 70 participants. Primary and final data collection are anticipated to be complete by March 2030. The study was funded in May 2025, and data collection began in November 2025. As of November 9, 2026, 7 participants had been enrolled. Results are expected to be published in approximately the beginning of 2030.

CONCLUSIONS: PRECISE is, to our knowledge, the first idiographically personalized, EMA-informed adjunctive treatment developed specifically for STBs. This trial will provide feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy data to inform a subsequent fully powered efficacy trial.

articles.title: Five-year risk of cardiovascular events in women with history of pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between fetal growth restriction (FGR) and adverse maternal cardiovascular outcomes within 5 years postpartum.

METHODS: This was a retrospective study that used a global federated health research network (TriNetX) in which diagnoses are coded using the International Classification of Diseases, tenth revision, Clinical Modification system (ICD-10-CM). Nulliparous women aged ≥ 18 years, without prior cardiovascular disease and with a singleton pregnancy delivered between April 2006 and December 2020, were categorized by the presence or absence of FGR (ICD-10-CM: O36.5). 1:1 propensity-score matching (PSM) was applied using two models: Model 1, matching for pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors; and Model 2, matching for both pre-existing and other pregnancy-related cardiovascular risk factors. Cox regression proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CI for a maternal composite cardiovascular outcome including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke within 5 years postpartum, and for each of these components individually.

RESULTS: After PSM, 84 863 women per group were analyzed in Model 1 and 84 861 per group in Model 2. FGR was associated with an increased risk of the composite cardiovascular outcome (Model 1: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.16-1.52); Model 2: HR, 1.31 (95% CI, 1.15-1.50)), as well as with an increased risk of each of the components of the composite outcome individually: heart failure (Model 1: HR, 1.29 (95% CI, 1.08-1.54); Model 2: HR, 1.30 (95% CI, 1.09-1.56)), acute myocardial infarction (Model 1: HR, 1.55 (95% CI, 1.16-2.08); Model 2: HR, 1.53 (95% CI, 1.15-2.05)) and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke (Model 1: HR, 1.38 (95% CI, 1.09-1.74); Model 2: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.06-1.68)) within 5 years postpartum.

CONCLUSIONS: FGR in a first pregnancy is associated with increased maternal composite cardiovascular risk, including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke, within 5 years postpartum. These findings suggest that FGR may be a marker of early cardiovascular vulnerability. However, residual confounding, particularly by unmeasured timing or severity of pre-eclampsia, cannot be excluded. Also, FGR was identified using coding constructs based on electronic health records, which may include overlap with broader 'suspected poor growth' phenotypes such as small-for-gestational age, hence potentially diluting the observed associations. Earlier risk assessment and preventive strategies may help to reduce the risk of long-term morbidity and mortality in this population. © 2026 The Author(s). Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

articles.title: 24-hour Movement Guideline Adherence and Cardiometabolic Health among Adults with Disabilities: Analysis of NHANES 2013-2018.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.abstract: A growing body of evidence has examined the association between adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines and cardiometabolic health outcomes. However, it remains unclear whether these associations extend to adults with disabilities, a population experiencing substantial health disparities. Therefore, this study examined the association between adherence to the 24-hour movement guidelines and cardiometabolic health among adults with disabilities. This cross-sectional study used data from the 2013-2018 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A nationally representative sample of U.S. adults with disabilities (n = 4,985) was included. Survey-weighted logistic regression models with multiple imputation were used to examine associations between guideline adherence and cardiometabolic health. Subgroup analyses were conducted across cardiometabolic outcomes and functional disability types. The results showed that participants meeting three guidelines had higher odds of being free from cardiovascular disease (AOR = 2.05, 95% CI: 1.42-2.94), obesity (AOR = 1.99, 95% CI: 1.44-2.75), hypertension (AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.22-2.50) and type 2 diabetes (AOR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.14-2.24), than those meeting none of the guidelines. Meeting two guidelines was associated with higher odds of being free from hypertension and obesity. Associations between guideline adherence and cardiometabolic health varied across functional disability subgroups. These findings suggest that adherence to a greater number of movement guidelines is associated with having more favorable cardiometabolic health profiles for adults with disabilities. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed variation in the associations across disability types, further research is needed to determine whether associations differ across functional impairment groups and whether movement recommendations should be tailored accordingly.

articles.title: A National Study of Ischemic Times and Outcomes in DCD Liver Transplantation in the Era of Normothermic Regional Perfusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver donation after circulatory death (DCD) is associated with severe graft ischemia and poorer outcomes, forcing stringent graft selection and reducing utilization. Outcomes after donor normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) are superior to standard DCD liver transplantation, with less cholangiopathy and better survival. These observations prompted re-assessment of DCD selection criteria when NRP is used.

METHODS: United Kingdom Transplant Registry data (2011-2023) were interrogated for donor and recipient demographics, ischemic timings, and graft and patient outcomes. Contemporaneous cohorts of standard DCD and NRP liver donors and transplants were collated and compared.

RESULTS: Compared with standard DCD (n = 1629), NRP donors (n = 263) were significantly older, had a greater body mass index, longer functional warm ischemic time (FWIT), donor warm ischemic time (DWIT) and cold ischemic times (CIT), yet had superior death-censored (96.0% versus 89.0%; P < 0.001) and uncensored (93.0% versus 86.7%; P = 0.004) graft survival. NRP liver recipients had greater mobility by day 90 (No restrictions; 51% versus 27%; P<0.001), less postoperative renal support (11% versus 19%; P = 0.002) and fewer biliary readmissions (6% versus 12%; P = 0.018) by 1 y, despite higher transplant acuity (UK model for end-stage liver disease 54 versus 53; P = 0.001). There were no significant effects of FWIT, DWIT, or CIT on NRP liver transplantation for graft, patient, or transplant survival.

CONCLUSIONS: In spite of adverse donor factors, NRP doubled utilization of DCD livers and improved outcomes. Prejudice against prolonged FWIT, DWIT, and CIT in DCD NRP liver donation needs re-evaluation to prevent unnecessary organ discard.

articles.title: Curcumin@ZIF-8-Embedded Janus Electrospun Dressing with Unidirectional Exudate Transport and Blue Light Photodynamic Therapy for Infected Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: This study developed a smart Janus wound dressing with asymmetric wettability that integrated antibacterial and antioxidant activities, exudate management, wound microenvironment regulation, and tissue repair promotion. Curcumin-loaded ZIF-8 composite nanoparticles (Cur@ZIF-8, CZ NPs) were first prepared using a one-pot method. A PLA-based hydrophobic functional layer containing CZ NPs and a PVP-based hydrophilic layer were subsequently electrospun onto opposite sides of medical gauze to fabricate the J-PCZ Janus dressing. The resulting dressing exhibited a wettability gradient and unidirectional water transport properties, enabling the directional transfer of wound exudate. Cur@ZIF-8 further endowed the dressing with pH-responsive release of Cur and Zn2+, as well as excellent antioxidant activity. Under blue light irradiation, the combined effect of Cur-mediated photodynamic antibacterial action and the auxiliary antibacterial activity of released Zn2+ resulted in antibacterial rates of 98.9% and 98.2% against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. The results from a mouse full-thickness infected skin wound model demonstrated that the J-PCZ Janus dressing promoted wound healing, collagen deposition, and re-epithelialization while helping to alleviate infection-related inflammatory responses. The dressing also exhibited good hemocompatibility and biocompatibility. Overall, through structural partitioning and functional integration, the J-PCZ Janus dressing achieves the organic integration of exudate management, infection control, and wound microenvironment regulation, providing a promising multifunctional dressing platform for the repair of infected skin wounds.

articles.title: Flavonoid Intake Diversity, Metabolic Signatures, and Risk of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Nutrition Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Higher flavonoid intake has been associated with a lower risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, flavonoids vary substantially in chemical structure, bioavailability, and metabolism. Therefore, whether greater diversity in flavonoid intake confers additional protection against COPD remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between flavonoid intake diversity and incident COPD and to explore potential metabolic mediators underlying this association.

METHODS: This prospective study included 93,068 participants from the UK Biobank. Flavonoid intake was estimated from 24-h dietary assessments, and intake diversity was quantified using the Shannon entropy and Hill number indices. Elastic net regression was applied to derive metabolic signatures associated with flavonoid intake diversity, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of flavonoid intake diversity and its metabolic signature with incident COPD.

RESULTS: Greater diversity of dietary flavonoids was associated with a lower risk of incident COPD independent of total intake. Participants in the highest quintile of flavonoid intake diversity had a 27% lower COPD risk than those in the lowest quintile (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.62, 0.85). Similar associations were observed across flavonoid subclasses. In joint analyses, the lowest risk was observed among participants with both moderate-to-high flavonoid intake and high diversity. The diversity-related metabolic signature was also inversely associated with COPD risk (HR for Q5 vs Q1: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.70). This signature significantly mediated the association between flavonoid intake diversity and COPD risk, primarily through pathways related to lipid and amino acid metabolism, inflammation, and fluid homeostasis.

CONCLUSION: Greater diversity in flavonoid intake was associated with a lower risk of COPD and may operate through multiple metabolic pathways. These findings support flavonoid intake diversity as a potentially modifiable dietary factor for COPD prevention.

articles.title: Single-Time-Point Time-integrated Activity Estimation for Dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA Therapy: Evaluation of Analytical and Machine Learning Methods.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The routine clinical implementation of patient-specific dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy can be challenging due to the need for multiple-time-point posttherapy SPECT/CT imaging to estimate time-integrated activity (TIA). Single-time-point (STP) approaches offer a more practical alternative, although their accuracy has yet to be fully established. This study aimed to evaluate existing analytical STP methods and to assess the feasibility and performance of a machine learning (ML) framework.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Thirty-four patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer undergoing 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy were retrospectively analyzed. Reference TIAs were derived from multiple-time-point 177Lu SPECT/CT imaging at 3 or 4 time points (TPs) postinjection (TP1: 0.7-2.1 h, TP2: day 1-2, TP3: day 3-4, TP4: day 5-7) in cycle 1 for 147 tumors, 64 kidneys, and 65 parotid glands using monoexponential or biexponential fitting. Analytical STP methods, proposed by Hänscheid and Madsen, were evaluated across different TPs. For each organ, a ML model was developed using a residual learning approach, in which the log-transformed ratio between reference TIAs and analytical STP TIA estimates was modeled. Input features included combinations of STP SPECT-derived parameters, baseline 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET-derived biomarkers (for individual structures and whole-body tumor volume), and clinical variables. Model performance was evaluated by using multiple quantitative metrics within a 10-times repeated 5-fold nested cross-validation framework and compared with purely analytic STP approaches. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations.

RESULTS: Analytical methods showed strong performance at optimal imaging TPs (TP2 for kidney/parotid, and TP3 for tumor), with the largest errors observed at early imaging (TP1). Overall, ML models provided modest improvement over analytical methods across structures at most TPs. The best performance was achieved using a ML model combining PET/SPECT imaging features with analytical TIA estimates. The mean percentage errors of the models, across TPs, ranged from -1.7 ± 17.9% (TP2) to 7.4 ± 65.3% (TP1) for kidneys, -0.4 ± 12.1% (TP2) to 4.5 ± 26.7% (TP4) for parotid glands, and 1.4 ± 14.8% (TP3) to -4.1 ± 100.5% (TP1) for tumors. Within the present cohort and modeling framework, the inclusion of clinical variables did not significantly improve model performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis showed that the ML models applied a positive correction to the analytical TIA estimates at early imaging TPs and a negative correction at late TPs.

CONCLUSIONS: Analytical STP methods yield accurate TIA estimates when applied at appropriate imaging TPs. ML models that integrate analytical estimates with imaging features provide modest improvements in accuracy with less sensitivity to TP selection. However, optimal timing remained structure-dependent, requiring a compromise when a single acquisition is used. These findings support the potential of ML-driven STP dosimetry in 177Lu-PSMA-617 radiopharmaceutical therapy to enable more flexible and clinically feasible workflows, pending further validation with larger and more diverse data sets.

articles.title: Microbial exopolysaccharides as mediators of gut microbiota-host interactions.
articles.abstract: In recent years, the gut microbiota has emerged as an important regulator of metabolic health and a potential therapeutic target for metabolic disorders, including obesity and diabetes. Among the diverse metabolites and bioactive compounds produced by gut bacteria, bacterial exopolysaccharides (EPS) have attracted increasing attention. This is largely due to their structural similarity to dietary fiber and their potential prebiotic effects on the intestinal environment. Accumulating evidence suggests that bacterial EPS can modulate host immune responses and glucose metabolism, thereby maintaining metabolic homeostasis through interactions between the gut microbiota and the host. Understanding the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these effects may provide new insights into the role of bacterial EPS in host metabolic regulation. This may aid in revealing their potential as novel targets for the prevention and treatment of metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Clinical and operational practices to facilitate safe medication use in the care of hospitalized patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this manuscript is to review evidence-based practices for the safe inpatient use of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) medications and facilitate effective transitions of care.

SUMMARY: Patients with PAH can present to the hospital with clinical conditions related to PAH, acute conditions unrelated to PAH, or complications of targeted PAH medications. Rapid triage and assessment of hospital capabilities pertaining to PAH medication use is essential to facilitate continued care or transfer to an expert PAH center. An assessment of hospital-specific capabilities should include the availability of specialists experienced in PAH, the formulary status of PAH medications, and clinician proficiency in the use of parenteral prostacyclin agents. Continuation or modification of PAH medications should be coordinated with the patient's primary PAH specialist. The use of targeted medications for PAH should be guided by multidisciplinary policies with procedures to ensure safe practices and compliance with risk evaluation and mitigation strategy programs, where applicable. Coordination of medication access and facilitating safe transitions of care at hospital discharge is multifaceted as agents are specialized and some are only dispensed by specialty pharmacies.

CONCLUSION: Management of a patient's PAH pharmacotherapies in the hospital setting should involve clinicians with expertise in the use of PAH targeted therapies, be guided by standardized medication-use procedures, and involve care coordination to facilitate safe hospital discharge.

articles.title: Rehabilitation across the hemodynamic continuum: Opportunities for better functional recovery in cardiogenic shock.
Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

articles.title: Is there evidence of increased risk of upper respiratory infection and common cold for air travelers?
Average Acceleration as a Measure of Physical Activity Across Sensor Locations in Participants With Heart Failure or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease and Healthy Volunteers: Secondary Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Average acceleration derived from wearable sensors offers a simple, continuous measure of physical activity and mobility that may overcome the limitations of complex accelerometer algorithms or site-based assessments in clinical trials. However, evidence supporting the use of average acceleration in patients with heart failure (HF) and/or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate how average acceleration can be used to assess walking-related outcomes in both laboratory and free-living settings and to assess the influence of sensor location on these measurements in participants with HF or COPD and healthy volunteers.

METHODS: Using data from the Mobilise-D Technical Validation Study, including structured, laboratory-based tasks and free-living assessments using sensors placed on the foot, lower back, and wrist, we analyzed average acceleration metrics computed as Euclidean norm minus one (ENMO), ENMO >0, and Euclidean norm (EN) from band-pass filtered triaxial acceleration (0.29-10 Hz; fourth-order Butterworth). During walking bouts, average acceleration was correlated with walking speed and cadence for each sensor location and cohort (HF, COPD, and healthy adults); sensor-location effects and cohort-specific sensitivity were evaluated. Linear mixed-effects models included participants as random intercepts and walking speed as both a fixed effect and a random effect.

RESULTS: Average acceleration showed a strong positive association with walking speed during straight-walking laboratory tasks across all sensor locations, with foot sensors showing the strongest association, followed by lower-back sensors and then wrist sensors. In complex walking tasks and free-living walking bouts, the strength of these associations decreased, and location effects were more pronounced. Across cohorts during free living, filtered EN r2 ranged from 0.711 to 0.818 for the foot, from 0.439 to 0.673 for the lower back, and from 0.067 to 0.146 for the wrist. The strength of the association for wrist data improved only during free-living sustained walking bouts (>10 seconds), although these associations were weaker than those for the foot and lower back. The Pearson correlation was marginally stronger for ENMO >0 than for filtered EN, but filtered EN preserved more signal by mitigating the influence of gravity and noise. Linear mixed-effects models showed that the variance could be largely attributed to stable participant-specific differences.

CONCLUSIONS: Average acceleration showed potential as a measure for capturing walking-related activity in adults with HF or COPD and in healthy adults when using appropriate sensor placement. The strength of the association depended strongly on sensor placement, with the foot showing the most consistent relationship, the lower back providing a reasonable alternative, and the wrist showing weaker performance, particularly during free living. We recommend that trials use standardized reporting of sensor location, filtering parameters, and walking-bout definitions and prioritize foot or lower-back placement for walking-related end points.

articles.title: From Priority Questions to Registry-Nested Trials: An AJRR-C Road Map for Advancing Arthroplasty Research.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The American Joint Replacement Research-Collaborative (AJRR-C) is a National Institutes of Health-funded P30 Core Center for Clinical Research and seeks to accelerate practice-changing arthroplasty research by leveraging the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) and shared multicenter research infrastructure. The AJRR-C convened 2 complementary meetings to establish a scalable coordinated pathway from the identification of high-priority clinical questions to the initiation of prospective studies.

METHODS: In July 2025, leaders from The Hip Society, The Knee Society, the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons, the AJRR, the Orthopaedic Research and Education Foundation, and the broader research community identified and prioritized clinical research questions regarding infection, perioperative management, new technologies, surgical techniques, implants, and quality. In April 2026, orthopaedic surgeons, methodologists, and artificial intelligence experts reconvened to evaluate contemporary approaches for addressing these priorities.

RESULTS: A central theme of the meetings was the importance of utilizing a fit-for-purpose approach in which study design is tailored to the clinical question, available data, and potential sources of bias. Clinical questions with clear equipoise and feasible interventions may warrant randomization, whereas questions involving rare outcomes, rapidly evolving technologies, surgeon preferences, or long-term surveillance may be better addressed with observational studies. Participants emphasized the need for a robust, sustainable network for arthroplasty clinical trials that provides the shared infrastructure necessary for coordinated site engagement, standardized data definitions, reliable longitudinal follow-up, and AJRR linkage across multicenter trials. Two new AJRR-nested randomized trials arose from the priority-topics meeting, and their development demonstrates the potential of the AJRR-C consensus model to translate research priorities into practice-changing evidence generation.

CONCLUSIONS: The AJRR-C established a coordinated pathway from the prioritization of research to the implementation of multicenter studies to address high-priority arthroplasty research questions. Sustaining this model requires continued collaboration among orthopaedic societies, investigators, methodologists, and the AJRR, as well as reliable funding mechanisms.

articles.title: Temporal interference stimulation targeting the ventromedial prefrontal cortex enhances reward learning and improves depression scores.
articles.abstract: Reward learning depends on dynamic interactions within frontostriatal circuits that encode reward prediction errors (RPEs). Disruptions in these interactions contribute to neuropsychiatric disorders, yet noninvasive modulation of deep reward circuits remains challenging. Here, we identify frontostriatal neural dynamics underlying reward learning and develop a circuit-targeted neuromodulation approach based on transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS). Neuroimaging and computational modeling in healthy adults revealed a bidirectional excitatory-inhibitory loop between the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) and ventral striatum (VS), encoding RPEs and scaling with individual learning rates. Oscillatory signatures suggested that vmPFC alpha and theta frequencies tracked RPEs, with no corresponding pattern identified for punishment processing. Alpha-frequency tTIS (10 hertz) over the vmPFC enhanced reward learning and reshaped frontostriatal connectivity, whereas theta-frequency tTIS (5 hertz) showed no effect. In a randomized trial in a cohort of 69 individuals with subclinical depression, three daily sessions of alpha-frequency tTIS alleviated subclinical depressive symptoms, with delayed benefits at 7-day follow-up. These findings provide a potential noninvasive circuit-targeted intervention for reward dysfunction and related disorders.

articles.title: An indirect wing steering muscle stabilizes flight by regulating wing pitch angle in Drosophila.
articles.abstract: Flapping flight is inherently unstable, requiring Drosophila to fine-tune their wing motions on a milliseconds timescale. Pioneering studies have shown that the direct steering muscles, which attach to the wing hinge, are important for generating these rapid flight reflexes. Recent connectome data, however, reveal that indirect steering muscles or tension muscles, which alter the mechanics of the thorax, receive some of the same synaptic inputs from the sensory apparatus as the direct steering muscles. This discovery suggests that the indirect steering muscles may also be important for flight control. Here, we show that the indirect tergopleural muscles indeed contribute substantially to stabilization, particularly for large pitch perturbations. We find that for small perturbations (less than 1,000 °/s), flies modulate their wing stroke amplitude to generate lift-based corrective torques, a strategy that has been previously documented. For larger perturbations, however, we observe that Drosophila engage an additional wing degree of freedom-the wing pitch angle-to leverage additional lift and drag forces during the corrective maneuver. Quasi-steady aerodynamic simulations reveal that this strategy minimizes power consumption, anaolgous to how some mammals (including humans) adjust their steady-state gaits in a near energy-optimal manner. Using optogenetics and a control theory framework, we demonstrate that the tergopleural muscle is activated by a proportional gain component of a nonlinear proportional-integral controller responsible for determining the wing pitch angle during large perturbations. A simplified torsional spring model for the wing hinge captures the changes in the wing pitch dynamics observed during correction maneuvers by using the tergopleural muscle to adjust the rest angle of the wing. These findings provide a striking example of reflex strategy selection in time-critical behaviors and underscore the vital role of indirect steering muscles in flight stabilization.

articles.title: Papilledema as a Manifestation of Secondary Intracranial Hypertension in an Adolescent With a Growth Hormone-Secreting Pituitary Macroadenoma.
articles.journal: Journal of neuro-ophthalmology : the official journal of the North American Neuro-Ophthalmology Society

articles.title: IncD is an essential type III effector that supports Chlamydia propagation.
articles.abstract: The obligate intracellular bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common bacterial cause of sexually transmitted infections worldwide. C. trachomatis replicates within a specialized intracellular compartment, the inclusion, whose membrane contains bacterial inclusion membrane (Inc) proteins, a family of type III secreted effectors that manipulate host pathways to support bacterial development and nutrient acquisition. Acquisition of host sphingolipids is essential for C. trachomatis development, but the relative contributions of the two CERT-dependent pathways that deliver sphingomyelin to the inclusion remain unclear. CERT mediates both vesicular trafficking from the Golgi and non-vesicular trafficking at endoplasmic reticulum-inclusion membrane contact sites through its interaction with the inclusion membrane protein IncD. Because genetic and pharmacological approaches targeting CERT disrupt both pathways simultaneously, their individual contributions have been difficult to dissect. Here, we sought to define the contribution of the IncD-CERT pathway to bacterial development using C. trachomatis, C. muridarum, and host genetics to generate conditional and null incD mutants. Conditional depletion of IncD or expression of an IncD mutant with impaired CERT binding resulted in smaller inclusions, reduced production of infectious progeny, and premature inclusion lysis. Complete loss of IncD prevented bacterial propagation unless CERT was artificially recruited to the inclusion independently of IncD, demonstrating that CERT recruitment to the inclusion alone is sufficient to support bacterial propagation in the absence of IncD. Consistent with its essential role in cell culture, IncD was also required for infection in a mouse model. Together, these findings demonstrate that IncD is an essential T3S effector and that the IncD-CERT pathway is essential for Chlamydia development, revealing that the vesicular and non-vesicular pathways of host sphingomyelin acquisition contribute differently to Chlamydia infection.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights into benzoxaborole activity against Cryptosporidium parvum: CPSF3 targeting genetically validated for AN3661, with implications for resistance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cryptosporidiosis is a major enteric disease affecting humans and animals worldwide, with severe consequences in young children and neonatal livestock, yet treatment options remain extremely limited. Benzoxaboroles have emerged as promising broad-spectrum antiparasitic compounds, but their mechanisms of action, molecular targets, and resistance pathways in Cryptosporidium spp. remain incompletely understood, limiting their optimal therapeutic deployment. We previously showed that the benzoxaborole AN3661 inhibits the endonuclease Cleavage and Polyadenylation Specificity Factor 3 (CPSF3) in Cryptosporidium hominis, likely by disrupting pre-mRNA processing and restricting parasite growth. Here, we further investigated the mode of action of AN3661 and compared it with two additional benzoxaboroles, AN13762 and AN7973.

METHODOLOGY: Cell culture assays combined with imaging-based quantification were used to assess drug activity and determine the impact of treatment on parasite growth and development. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was used to introduce a point mutation into Cryptosporidium parvum CPSF3 and evaluate resistance to benzoxaboroles in vitro and in vivo. Nanopore sequencing was performed to examine the effects of drug exposure on parasite mRNA processing.

PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: We identified a single mutation in C. parvum CPSF3 (Y385N) that conferred strong resistance to AN3661. In contrast, this mutation did not reduce sensitivity to AN13762 or AN7973, which are also suspected to target CPSF3. All three benzoxaboroles impaired mRNA processing, a process mediated by the CPSF machinery, and exhibited parasiticidal activity, with pronounced effects during late-stage maturation of first-generation meronts, including inhibition of parasite egress; two compounds also affected gametogenesis. Notably, AN7973 controlled severe infection in susceptible mice challenged with the AN3661-resistant C. parvum CPSF3 Y385N mutant. In Toxoplasma gondii, AN7973 remained active against strains resistant to AN3661 and AN13762, supporting a distinct mechanism of action. Finally, AN3661 and AN7973 were active against Eimeria tenella, and AN3661 against Giardia duodenalis.

CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Together, these results identify a resistance mechanism affecting AN3661 in Cryptosporidium, and highlight AN7973 as a promising alternative compound with broad antiparasitic activity and efficacy against AN3661-resistant parasites.

articles.title: A statistical framework to identify gene-gene interactions underlying multiple dichotomous phenotypes from genotype data.
articles.abstract: Identifying gene-gene (G × G) interactions across multiple dichotomous phenotypes is challenging due to the extreme sparsity of SNP-derived interaction matrices and the reduced statistical power associated with binary outcomes. Existing G × G association methods are restricted to either single or multiple continuous phenotypes. Here we introduce GiMat (Gene Interaction and Multiple-phenotype Association Test), a statistical framework that extends multivariate kernel regression to model G × G interactions jointly across dichotomous phenotypes, while explicitly capturing homogeneous and heterogeneous interaction effects. Extensive simulations demonstrate that GiMat controls type I error conservatively and adapts power flexibly to different types of relationships between interaction effects and phenotypes. Applied to type 2 diabetes and hypertension comorbidity in the UK Biobank, GiMat identified four previously unreported G × G interaction pairs associated with both phenotypes. This scalable framework enables robust discovery of complex genetic interactions underlying multiple correlated phenotypes.

articles.title: Leishmania exploits the macrophage endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein CLIMP-63 to modulate mitochondrial biogenesis and bioenergetics.
articles.abstract: In Leishmania-infected macrophages, interactions between parasitophorous vacuoles and the host cell endoplasmic reticulum are critical for parasite replication. Whether the complex architecture of this organelle influences these interactions remains unknown. Here, we identify the endoplasmic reticulum-shaping protein CLIMP-63 as a host factor promoting Leishmania infection. Following parasite internalization, we observed a redistribution of CLIMP-63 to parasitophorous vacuoles where it associates with VDAC2, a component of endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria contact sites, in a process dependent on the virulence glycolipid lipophosphoglycan. Mechanistically, we found that CLIMP-63 is required for Leishmania-induced mitochondrial DNA replication, cristae biogenesis, and enhanced mitochondrial respiration, which collectively contribute to parasite colonization of macrophages. Altogether, our findings identify a role for CLIMP-63 as a link between parasitophorous vacuoles, the endoplasmic reticulum, and host mitochondria, illustrating how Leishmania exploits the host cell endoplasmic reticulum to reprogram mitochondrial functions and bioenergetics.

articles.title: Loss to follow-up during tuberculosis treatment and 5-year mortality in Brazil: A target trial emulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loss to follow-up (LTFU) during tuberculosis treatment is a major programmatic gap, but how much excess mortality it causes has been difficult to estimate, because individuals who disengage differ from those who do not, and they must survive long enough to be recorded as having disengaged. Quantifying this excess and identifying which populations are at greatest risk are critical to informing program design and resource allocation.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We followed 171,048 people aged 15 years or older starting a first course of tuberculosis treatment in São Paulo State, Brazil, between 2013 and 2023, linking surveillance and mortality registries; 20,830 (12.2%) were LTFU, defined as interruption of treatment for at least 30 consecutive days. Among those LTFU, 65% had received directly observed therapy (DOT). Using a clone-censor-weight target trial emulation, we contrasted two strategies over 60 months from the first day of treatment: disengagement at any point during the first 6 months and remaining in care throughout. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, race, education, HIV status, diabetes, alcohol use, drug use, incarceration, homelessness, hospitalization at diagnosis, clinical form of tuberculosis, DOT, and municipality. A rolling landmark analysis addressed the timing of disengagement and cause-specific mortality excess. LTFU increased standardized 5-year mortality by 2.49 percentage points (95% CI [1.94, 3.17]). In a rolling landmark analysis, tuberculosis accounted for 61% of the 5-year excess mortality. Relative effects were largest in younger, stably housed individuals, whose baseline mortality was low; the largest absolute excess fell on people living with HIV (5.16 percentage points, 95% CI [3.76, 6.60]). The excess was similar for disengagement at any point in the first 4 months of treatment and attenuated thereafter. Limitations include the absence from the registry of severity markers such as radiographic extent and bacillary load, so residual confounding cannot be excluded.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite high DOT coverage, disengagement during the first 6 months of tuberculosis treatment was common and increased 5-year mortality under the stated identification assumptions, with the excess concentrated in deaths attributed to tuberculosis. Interventions that provide support throughout treatment should be tested for their effectiveness in sustaining engagement and reducing mortality.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Prediction Model for Reversible Cognitive Frailty in People Living with HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reversible cognitive frailty may be an important target for early identification among people with HIV (PWH). We developed a prediction model for reversible cognitive frailty and assessed its internal validity using clinical, laboratory, and medication-related data.

SETTING: Positive Brain Health Now cohort, including adults recruited from five Canadian HIV clinics between 2013 and 2018.

METHODS: Data from 824 adults with HIV aged 35 years or older were analysed. Reversible cognitive frailty was defined as co-occurring physical frailty and self-reported cognitive difficulty without dementia. Twenty candidate predictors were entered into least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression (LASSO) with 10-fold cross-validation to select the final predictor set. Internal validity was assessed through discrimination (apparent and optimism-corrected C-statistic via bootstrap resampling), calibration, and clinical utility (decision curve analysis).

RESULTS: Reversible cognitive frailty was present in 7.5% of participants. The final model retained 10 predictors; the strongest were female sex, greater comorbidity burden, higher anxiety and depression scores, and higher anticholinergic medication burden, with additional contributions from hepatic, nutritional, HIV-related, and medication variables. On internal assessment, the model showed strong discrimination (optimism-corrected C-statistic 0.882), acceptable calibration, and net benefit over assess-all and assess-none strategies. At the optimal threshold, sensitivity was 91.9%, specificity 76.1%, and negative predictive value 99.1%.

CONCLUSION: This is the first prediction model developed for reversible cognitive frailty in PWH, showing strong discrimination, acceptable calibration, and clinical utility within the development cohort. External validation in independent samples is needed before clinical use.

articles.title: A temporary fix: assessing the safety, efficacy, and various applications of temporary externalized pacemakers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporary active-fixation pacemakers (TAF-PMs), consisting of a screw-in pacing lead connected to an external generator, may offer advantages over conventional balloon-tipped temporary pacemakers, including more secure lead placement, greater patient mobility, and reduced need for intensive care monitoring. We evaluated the safety and clinical utility of this strategy across multiple pacing indications.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study of 100 adults who underwent TAF-PM placement between June 2019 and November 2024. Through chart review, data were collected on demographics, pacing indications, duration of temporary pacing, complications, and subsequent need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI). The primary outcome was successful discontinuation of temporary pacing without subsequent PPMI.

RESULTS: Pacing indications included spontaneous progression of conduction system disease (60%), transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR)-related conduction abnormalities (12%), acute myocardial infarction (AMI)-related conduction abnormalities (12%), and ongoing infection precluding PPMI (16%). Thirty-eight patients (38%) did not undergo subsequent PPMI. Among patients with TAVR- and AMI-related conduction abnormalities, 75% avoided PPMI. Three patients (3%) experienced lead dislodgement. No new infections, lead perforations, significant bleeding, or cardiac arrests attributable to the TAF-PM strategy were documented.

CONCLUSION: Temporary pacing using a screw-in lead affixed to an external generator is safe, effective, and reversible across multiple clinical scenarios, allowing sufficient time to assess the need for permanent pacing.

articles.title: Socioeconomic and psychosocial disparities associated with suicidal risk among stroke survivors in Cameroon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke survivors are at increased risk of psychological complications, including suicidal ideation, yet this outcome remains poorly characterised in sub-Saharan Africa. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of suicidal risk and identify associated factors among post-stroke patients in Douala, Cameroon.

METHODS: An analytical cross-sectional study with a matched control group was conducted from January to May 2025 in the neurology departments of two referral hospitals. Adults with confirmed stroke assessed ≥3 months after onset were enrolled alongside non-stroke controls. Suicidal risk was assessed using the suicidality module of the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI). Conditional logistic regression was used for the matched case-control analysis, and multivariable logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with suicidal risk among stroke patients, with adjustment for selected covariates available in the dataset.

RESULTS: Four hundred participants were enrolled (200 stroke patients, 200 controls). Suicidal risk prevalence was significantly higher among stroke survivors than controls (9.5% vs 4.0%; OR = 2.519; 95% CI: 1.083-5.857; p = 0.028). In multivariate analysis, depression (aOR = 6.380; 95% CI: 1·170-34.794; p = 0.032), moderate neurological severity at assessment (NIHSS 5-15; aOR = 6.124; 95% CI: 1.415-26.498; p = 0.015), and having four to five children (aOR = 4.096; 95% CI: 1.318-8.622; p = 0.029) were associated with suicidal risk after adjustment for selected covariates.

CONCLUSIONS: Suicidal risk affects approximately one in ten post-stroke patients in Douala. Depression and moderate neurological severity at assessment were associated with suicidal risk after adjustment for selected covariates. The association with having four to five children should be considered exploratory and requires replication in larger studies. Residual confounding by unmeasured clinical and psychosocial factors cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Hybrid Closed-Loop Use Mediates the Relationship Between Social Determinants of Health and Glycemic Outcomes in a Canadian Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Clinic.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sociodemographic disparities continue to impact people living with type 1 diabetes (T1D), despite advances like hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems, which improve glycemic outcomes and quality of life. This study evaluated whether HCL system use mediates the relationship between social determinants of health (SDH) and glycemic outcomes in children living with T1D (CLWT1D).

METHOD: A retrospective chart review included CLWT1D followed at the Children's Hospital of Eastern Ontario between May 2023 and May 2024. Demographics, management, and glycemic outcomes (hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) and percent time in range (%TIR)) were collected. SDH were measured using the Canadian Index of Multiple Deprivation, which categorizes individuals into quintiles (Q1= least to Q5= most deprived) across four dimensions using postal codes. Regression models examined mediation effects.

RESULTS: Data from 581 children (mean age 13.4±3.8 years; 46.6% female; mean T1D duration 6.1±3.8 years; mean HbA1c 8.0±1.5%) were analyzed. Of these, 46% used HCL systems, while 54% used injections or stand-alone pumps. HbA1c was associated with situational vulnerability (p<0.001) and residential instability (p<0.001), with HCL system use significantly mediating differences in HbA1c between Q1-4 vs Q5. No mediation effect was found for economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. %TIR results were consistent with HbA1c findings.

CONCLUSION: HCL system use mediated the relationship between glycemic outcomes and residential instability and situational vulnerability, but not economic dependency or ethnocultural composition. Access to HCL systems may mitigate health inequities in CLWT1D; however, technology alone does not eliminate these disparities, and parallel interventions are needed to promote equitable care.

articles.title: Associations between atherogenic index of plasma, Alzheimer's biomarkers, and the risk of cognitive impairment: Hubei Memory and Aging Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) is a reliable marker of atherogenic dyslipidemia, but prospective evidence on its association with cognitive impairment in older adults is limited. We examined whether AIP was associated with incident cognitive impairment, and explored associations with plasma Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarkers and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 status.

METHODS: This study included 1,143 adults aged ≥ 65 years from the Hubei Memory and Aging Cohort Study. AIP was calculated as log(triglyceride/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol). The association of AIP with incident cognitive impairment and its joint effects with plasma AD biomarkers were evaluated using Cox models. Dose-response associations were assessed by restricted cubic splines. Cognitive domain declines were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Analyses were stratified by APOE ε4 status.

RESULTS: After adjustment, higher baseline AIP was independently associated with greater risk of cognitive impairment, showing a nonlinear dose-response relationship (inflection point: 0.758). Compared to the lowest quartile, the highest quartile exhibited a higher risk (Hazard Ratio [HR] = 2.15; 95% Confidence Interval [CI]: 1.47-3.12). Higher AIP also correlated with faster memory decline (β = -0.14, 95% CI: -0.26 to -0.01). Participants with higher AIP and elevated p-tau181 had an increased risk of cognitive impairment (HR = 3.46, 95% CI: 1.58-7.61). These effects were more pronounced among APOE ε4 carriers.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher AIP was associated with cognitive impairment and faster memory decline. High AIP combined with elevated p-tau181 was associated with greater risk, particularly among APOE ε4 carriers, supporting refined risk stratification in older adults.

articles.title: Coreceptor expansion in an HIV-1 infected individual with an N332/V3 broadly neutralizing antibody response.
articles.abstract: The HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env) mediates host cell entry through interactions with CD4 and either coreceptor CCR5 or CXCR4 and is the target for neutralizing antibodies. During infection, some clade B viruses evolve from a CCR5- to CXCR4-using phenotype, a transition associated with accelerated AIDS progression. The mechanisms driving this coreceptor expansion remain poorly understood. Env regions involved in CCR5/CXCR4 interactions overlap with the N332/V3 epitope targeted by broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) suggesting antibody pressure could influence coreceptor expansion. Here, we use single genome amplification (SGA) to study Env evolution over 250 weeks in an HIV-infected individual from the SPARTAC Trial who develops an N332/V3 bnAb response and subsequently undergoes a coreceptor expansion. We show that Env mutations that facilitate coreceptor expansion overlap with those mediating escape from the host neutralizing antibody response, supporting a role for N332/V3 bnAbs in the emergence of X4-tropic Envs in this individual.

articles.title: Listening to the venous wall: SDC4-PIEZO1 mechanotransduction as an early driver of deep vein thrombosis.
Adaptive deep learning for diabetes detection: Integrating progressive-growth DNN with PSO-GA optimization.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundDiabetes mellitus has become one of the prominent global health issues that demand early and precise predictions to avoid complications. Thus, an adaptive deep learning method for classifying diabetes is proposed in this work.ObjectiveThe proposed technique Progressive-Growth Deep Neural Network (PG-DNN) with Particle Swarm Optimization and the Genetic Algorithm (PSO-GA) to adjust the parameters. The experiments use PIMA, LMCH, and the large-scale diabetes prediction dataset.MethodsA comprehensive preprocessing technique is used to enhance data quality. Missing values are handled through imputation using polynomial regression models. Outliers are detected using the interquartile range and the Isolation Forest algorithm. For feature selection, Spearman correlation analysis is used. Data standardization and SMOTE-based imbalance handling are also considered. Stratification and repeated k-fold validation techniques have been used to compare the performance of the proposed PG-DNN with existing models, such as support vector machines, random forests, and standard deep neural networks. The PG-DNN architecture is incrementally expanded by learning deeper-level features; the GA-PSO optimization technique enables faster learning and improved convergence.ResultsExperiments demonstrate a consistent performance advantage for all datasets.
