The proposed approach achieves 95.6% accuracy on the primary dataset, 97.4% on the PIMA dataset, and 99.5% on the LMCH dataset. The interpretability analysis using LIME and SHAP identifies biologically significant features.ConclusionThe work presents a scalable and practical solution for predicting early diabetes.

articles.title: Child abuse and mental health outcomes in Canada: A population-based study with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity: Violence faite aux enfants et résultats en matière de santé mentale au Canada : étude fondée sur la population axée sur le sexe à la naissance et l'identité sexuelle.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
articles.abstract: BackgroundContemporary nationally representative Canadian statistics on child abuse and mental health outcomes with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity are essential in determining approaches to prevention and the need for services. The objectives of the current study were to examine the relationship between experiences of abuse during childhood (physical, sexual, exposure to intimate partner violence, and any) and past-year mental health conditions (depression, generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, social phobia, and suicidal ideation) among adult Canadians, and whether these relationships are moderated by sex at birth and sexual identity.MethodsData were obtained from the cross-sectional 2022 Statistics Canada Mental Health and Access to Care Survey (2022; n = 9,409; 18+ years).FindingsAny child abuse history and each individual child abuse type were associated with an increased likelihood of all poor mental health indicators in the sample after adjusting for sociodemographic covariates (Adjusted Odds Ratio ranging from 1.66 to 4.67). Generally, an increasing dose-response trend was noted for increasing counts of child abuse types (multitype abuse) experienced and increased odds of poor mental health indicators. Sex at birth and sexual identity moderated models for both child abuse and depression and child abuse and social phobia, with stronger associations for females compared to males and for some sexual identities other than heterosexual.InterpretationThe current study provides updated nationally representative data on child abuse history and mental health indicators among adults in Canada. The development and evaluation of child abuse prevention strategies must remain a priority in reducing violence against children and mental health problems among Canadians. Sex at birth and sexual identity differences highlight the need for policies and practices to address the unique needs of women and individuals identifying as lesbian/gay, bisexual, and other nonheterosexual identities.

articles.title: Enhanced photodynamic performance of violet phosphorus nanosheets via covalent polyethylene-glycol modification for bacterial-infection therapy.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infections within the wound microenvironment and the exacerbation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) present significant challenges to skin tissue regeneration. Endowed with a "nano-knife" effect and photodynamic therapy (PDT) potential, violet phosphorus nanosheets (VPNS) have emerged as promising non-antibiotic antibacterial materials. However, their inherently poor colloidal stability severely limits their biomedical applications. To overcome this bottleneck, we functionalized VPNS with a diazonium-terminated polyethylene glycol (HO-PEG-AD) via the formation of stable C-P covalent bonds, successfully constructing VPNS@PEG-AD nanocomposites. This modification significantly enhances the stable dispersion time in aqueous solutions and subsequently improves the efficiency of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation under light irradiation. In vitro assays demonstrated that VPNS@PEG-AD exhibits a potent synergistic antibacterial effect against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus upon irradiation, driven by the dual action of physical piercing and ROS-mediated oxidative damage. Furthermore, in a murine model of S. aureus-infected epidermal wounds, the VPNS@PEG-AD effectively eradicated infection, suppressed inflammatory cell infiltration, and significantly accelerated wound healing without exhibiting obvious systemic toxicity. In summary, this highly stable PEGylated VPNS nanoplatform provides a safe and highly efficient strategy for combating AMR and promoting the healing of infected wounds.

articles.title: Semaglutide Effect on Kidney, Cardiovascular, and Mortality Outcomes in Racial and Ethnic Groups: FLOW Trial Post Hoc Analyses.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Potential variation in semaglutide treatment response across racial and ethnic groups of people with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes has not been assessed. In a post hoc analysis of the international FLOW randomized controlled clinical trial, we assessed the efficacy of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg vs placebo on kidney and cardiovascular outcomes in racial and ethnic subgroups.

METHODS: Using FLOW trial data, we compared semaglutide 1.0 mg vs placebo (in addition to the standard of care) on the primary kidney outcome (onset of kidney failure, ≥50% reduction in estimate glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] from baseline sustained for ≥28 days, or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes) and three confirmatory secondary outcomes (annual change [total slope] in eGFR, major adverse cardiovascular events [MACE], and all-cause death) between Black/African American and non-Black/African American participants and between Hispanic/Latino and non-Hispanic/Latino participants. Cox proportional hazards models were used to compare semaglutide 1.0 mg vs placebo groups on the occurrence of the primary kidney outcome, MACE, and all-cause death. Random-effects linear regression models were used to compare groups on the change in eGFR. Models included interaction terms for treatment by race or ethnicity.

RESULTS: Of 3,533 total participants in the FLOW trial, 3,454 had race data available (Black/African American, n=160; non-Black/African American, n=3,294), and 3,388 had ethnicity data available (Hispanic/Latino, n=556; non-Hispanic Latino, n=2,832). Over a median 3.4 years of follow-up, the effect of semaglutide on the primary kidney outcome, MACE, all-cause death, and annual change in eGFR did not statistically significantly differ between Black/African American and non-Black/African American participants or between Hispanic/Latino and non-Hispanic/Latino participants (all interaction P-values >0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this post hoc exploratory analysis of the FLOW trial, there was no statistical evidence that the efficacy of semaglutide treatment on kidney and cardiovascular outcomes differed by race or ethnicity.

articles.title: Skin Deep: Dermatologic Complications of Kidney Disease.
articles.journal: Clinical journal of the American Society of Nephrology : CJASN
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects more than 700 million individuals worldwide, and its complications extend across specialties. While dermatologic manifestations are estimated to affect nearly all patients with CKD, they remain significantly under-recognized and under-treated. These issues can be profoundly distressing for patients, significantly impacting their quality of life. Prompt diagnosis and treatment are essential for improving outcomes and reducing morbidity and mortality. However, dermatologic complications of CKD can be difficult to manage as many may present similarly and lack standardized guidelines. Moreover, varying cutaneous manifestations can be observed from early to late stages of kidney disease with progression of clinical features as disease worsens. Dermatologic manifestations may act as a sentinel sign for progression of internal disease. Therefore, better understanding of clinical characteristics of dermatologic complications is of particular importance in patients with kidney disease to allow for prompt diagnosis, further prevention and effective management. In this review, we discuss the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical features, diagnosis, management and prognosis of both common and life-threatening dermatologic complications of kidney disease, including CKD-associated pruritus (CKD-aP), uremic xerosis, uremic frost, porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT), acquired perforating dermatoses (APD), calcinosis cutis (CC), calciphylaxis, nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF), pigmentary changes, and nail and hair changes.

articles.title: Identifying Players' Performance Profiles in Elite Men and Women 3 × 3 Basketball: Evidence From the Olympic Games.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.abstract: Zhang, S, Gasperi, L, Gomez-Ruano, M-A, Conte, D, and Sansone, P. Identifying player's performance profiles in elite men and women 3×3 basketball: Evidence from the Olympic Games. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to cluster the performance profiles of elite male and female 3 × 3 basketball players according to their stature. Data from the 2021 and 2024 Olympic Games were retrieved, involving 128 players (64 per sex). The players' stature was noted, alongside the game-related statistics (GRS) for all tournament games. Two-step cluster analyses classified male and female players according to their stature, whereas comparisons of GRS across clusters were performed using independent samples t test, Mann-Whitney U test, or 1-way ANOVA. For men, 2 clusters were identified: perimeter and internal. The analyses of performance profiles showed how perimeter players registered more 2-point shots made, 2-point shots attempted, key assists, and drives than internal players (all p < 0.05, effect size [ES]: small-moderate), whereas internal players had more 1-point shots made, 1-point shots attempted, free-throws attempted, and blocked shots than perimeter players (all p < 0.05, ES: small-moderate). For women, 3 clusters were identified: perimeter, all around, and internal. Perimeter players achieved more 2-point shots made, 2-point shots attempted, and drives than internal players (all p < 0.05, ES: moderate-large). All-around players only differed from internal players in their lower 1-point shots attempted (p = 0.043, ES: moderate). Internal players recorded more 1-point shots made than both perimeter and all-around players (all p < 0.05, ES: moderate) and more defensive rebounds than perimeter players (p = 0.010, ES: moderate). Current results provide initial information on the positional performance profile of elite male and female 3 × 3 basketball players, which can inform player selection, talent identification, strength and conditioning practices, and technical-tactical strategies.

articles.title: Effect of Acoramidis on Heart Failure-Related Health Status-Reply.
Effect of Acoramidis on Heart Failure-Related Health Status.
Effect of Acoramidis on Heart Failure-Related Health Status.
Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy vs Surgery for Stage IA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is a well-established alternative to surgery for nonoperable patients with early-stage non-small cell (NSCLC) lung cancer. However, the role of SBRT in operable patients is unclear as 3 randomized clinical trials comparing SBRT with surgery were closed early because of poor accrual. Existing observational comparisons are limited by confounding because patients who receive SBRT are generally frailer and more comorbid.

OBJECTIVE: To compare cancer-specific mortality between surgery and SBRT using proximal causal inference to adjust for unmeasured confounding due to frailty and comorbidity using proxy variables.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study was a national database analysis of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-Medicare dataset. Three treatment effect estimates were obtained with increasing control of confounding: unadjusted, standard-regression adjusted for measured confounders as in existing studies, and proximally adjusted for unmeasured confounders. Participants were patients with stage IA NSCLC who underwent sublobar resection or SBRT from 2010 to 2019, followed up through December 21, 2021. Data analysis was performed from April 2023 to August 2026.

EXPOSURES: Sublobar resection vs SBRT. Negative control exposures were constructed from billing codes.

MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURES: Lung cancer-specific mortality. Negative control outcomes were constructed from other-cause mortality. Results are reported as hazard differences (HD) and 95% CI.

RESULTS: A total of 4251 patients met inclusion and exclusion criteria; 2581 (60.7%) were female and 1670 (39.3%) were male. Their mean (SD) age was 75.6 (6.3) years. A total of 2558 patients underwent SBRT and 1693 underwent surgery. In the unadjusted and covariate-adjusted analyses, SBRT was associated with higher lung cancer cause-specific mortality, HD of 0.047 person-years (95% CI, 0.038-0.055) and 0.024 person-years (95% CI, 0.014-0.034), respectively. However, there was also compelling evidence of confounding due to a strong estimated association with other-cause mortality. In the proximal analysis, other-cause mortality together with negative control exposures were used to indirectly control for hidden confounders, yielding an HD of 0.012 person-years (95% CI, 0.0013-0.027).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study empirically showed that existing observational comparisons of SBRT and surgery are biased because of unmeasured confounding. When proximal causal inference was used to better control for confounding due to frailty and comorbidity, there continued to be a smaller but significant improvement in outcomes associated with surgery, though the effects of residual bias due to differences in pathologic and clinical staging could not be ruled out. This study demonstrates that proximal causal inference can be used to control for unmeasured confounders in a variety of settings.

articles.title: Clinical Frequency and Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Dermatomyositis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The occurrence of peripheral neuropathy (PN) in dermatomyositis (DM) is poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the occurrence, clinical patterns, and electrophysiological features of PN in patients with DM.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used data from a single academic center database of patients with DM who were enrolled between July 2008 and December 2025. Patients with PN were identified through medical record review of problem lists, encounter diagnoses, and clinical notes. PN diagnosis was established by clinical examination, nerve conduction study (NCS), or skin punch biopsy. Patients with PN that was associated with diabetes or prediabetes, vitamin deficiency, infection, trauma, nerve compression, radiculopathy, or neurotoxic medication were excluded.

EXPOSURES: DM subtype, autoantibody positivity, and systemic manifestations.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Main outcomes were frequency and clinical/electrophysiological characteristics of PN among patients with DM.

RESULTS: Among 640 patients with DM (median [IQR] age, 60 [40.8-70.0] years; 546 [85.3%] female; 94 [14.7%] male), 120 (18.8%) had clinically documented PN (median [IQR] age, 60 [50.5-70.8] years; 104 [86.7%] female; 16 [13.3%] male), ascertained at a median (IQR) of 3 (1-9) years after DM diagnosis. Patients with PN were significantly more likely to have classic DM than patients without PN (75 of 120 [62.5%] vs 269 of 520 [51.7%]; P = .03). Patients with PN had higher rates of arthralgia (95 of 120 [79.2%] vs 93 of 511 [18.2%]; P < .001) and Raynaud syndrome (67 of 120 [55.8%] vs 198 of 511 [38.7%]; P < .001), and lower myositis-specific antibody positivity (28 of 104 patients [26.9%] vs 112 of 295 [38.0%]; P = .04), than patients without PN. NCS was performed in 61 patients, with positive findings in 39 patients (63.9%) and negative findings in 22 patients (36.1%). Mixed sensory-motor polyneuropathy was most common (23 of 39 patients [58.9%]), followed by pure sensory neuropathy (12 of 39 patients [30.8%]), with axonal features predominating (37 of 39 patients [94.9%]) over demyelinating features (2 of 39 patients [5.1%]). Small-fiber neuropathy was biopsy-confirmed in 4 patients (3.3%) and clinically suspected without biopsy confirmation in 16 patients (13.3%).

CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, clinically documented PN was identified in nearly one-fifth of the DM cohort after exclusion of secondary causes and was associated with classic DM subtype and higher rates of arthralgia and Raynaud syndrome. The predominance of axonal over demyelinating patterns on NCS suggests inflammatory axonal injury as one possible mechanism, though other causes cannot be excluded. These findings suggest PN is an underrecognized systemic association of DM warranting heightened clinical awareness and further mechanistic investigation.

articles.title: Anemia and Iron Status in Pregnant and Postpartum Women With Acute Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), iron-deficient anemia is highly prevalent and may compound the cardiovascular stress of pregnancy, yet its contribution to maternal acute heart failure (AHF) is poorly understood.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association of maternal anemia and iron status with AHF in pregnancy and post partum in India.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, unmatched, prospective case-control study recruited participants from 10 hospitals across 4 Indian states from February 2019 to November 2024. Incident cases were pregnant or postpartum women with clinically diagnosed AHF. Controls were women without history or symptoms of heart disease within 48 hours post partum. Data were analyzed from March 2025 to April 2026.

EXPOSURES: Maternal anemia and iron status. Blood samples collected at recruitment were analyzed for hemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor, and hepcidin.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The outcome of interest was AHF, defined using clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of iron status and anemia with AHF, adjusting for potential confounders, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Subgroup analyses were performed in women with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. The discriminatory capacity of a model including anemia present before AFH onset vs a model with established risk factors only was examined using receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: Among 532 women with clinically diagnosed AHF (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-29] years) and 1091 controls (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-28] years), moderate and severe anemia were associated with 1.5-fold (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.05) and 5-fold (aOR, 5.06; 95% CI, 3.02-8.48) increased odds of AHF, respectively, compared with women without anemia. Higher soluble transferrin receptor levels (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.31-1.57) and the lowest hepcidin quintile (aOR, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.69-4.14), both indicative of iron deficiency, were independently associated with AHF. These associations persisted after adjusting for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and after excluding women with preexisting cardiac conditions, and they were consistent in subgroups with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. Adding anemia to established risk factors improved model discrimination for identifying AHF risk, increasing the AUC from 78% (95% CI, 76%-81%) to 83% (95% CI, 80%-85%) (P < .001).

CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: This case-control study found that maternal anemia and iron deficiency were independently associated with AHF during pregnancy and post partum. Further studies are needed to determine whether preventing or treating iron deficiency and anemia can reduce AHF risk and improve maternal outcomes.

articles.title: Low Disease Activity and Drug-Free Remission in Anti-MDA5 Dermatomyositis.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5)-positive dermatomyositis (MDA5-DM) is associated with rapid progression and high early mortality, but long-term outcomes beyond the early high-risk phase remain poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the attainability, associated factors, and durability of low disease activity (LDA) and drug-free remission (DFR) in patients with MDA5-DM.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center in China included consecutive patients with MDA5-DM who were enrolled between August 2003 and July 2023 and followed up through August 2025. Median follow-up was 5.7 (IQR, 3.4-7.4) years. The data were analyzed from September 2025 through December 2025.

EXPOSURES: Baseline demographic, clinical, and laboratory characteristics.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were experiencing LDA and DFR. Secondary outcomes included relapse after LDA or DFR and patient-reported outcomes assessed using the Patient Global Assessment and Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index.

RESULTS: Of 561 screened patients, 523 (93.2%) were included. Among 523 patients with MDA5-DM, 345 (65.9%) were female, 178 (34.1%) were male, and the median age at disease onset was 50.0 years (IQR, 41.0-57.5 years). Interstitial lung disease was present in 488 patients (93.3%) at baseline. Cumulative 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year all-cause mortality was 28.1%, 30.5%, 30.8%, and 31.7%, respectively. The 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year cumulative incidences of LDA were 3.1%, 47.1%, 59.0%, and 66.8%, respectively; corresponding incidences of DFR were 0%, 5.0%, 15.1%, and 31.0%, respectively. The median time from enrollment was 23 months (IQR, 18-34) for LDA and 46 months (IQR, 37-67) for DFR. Respiratory failure was associated with lower rates of LDA (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 0.31; 95% CI, 0.19-0.51) and DFR (sHR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.12-0.87), whereas a higher CD8-positive T-cell count was associated with higher rates of LDA (sHR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.08-1.22) and DFR (sHR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.09-1.31). The 5-year relapse-free probabilities were 76.7% after LDA and 82.0% after DFR. LDA and DFR were associated with lower Patient Global Assessment and Health Assessment Questionnaire Disability Index scores compared with non-LDA or non-DFR states.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The findings of this cohort study suggest that LDA was an attainable and durable long-term outcome for many patients with MDA5-DM, whereas DFR occurred less frequently. These findings may inform long-term disease control targets and treatment expectations in MDA5-DM.

articles.title: National guidelines for colorectal cancer screening in Saudi Arabia: Recommendations from the multi-society guideline development task force.
articles.journal: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association
articles.abstract: These updated national guidelines were developed jointly by the Saudi Gastroenterology Association, Saudi Society of Colon and Rectal Surgery, Saudi Society of Gastrointestinal Oncology, and Saudi Society of Family and Community Medicine, and provide evidence-based recommendations for colorectal cancer (CRC) screening in Saudi Arabia, superseding the 2015 national guidelines. This update incorporates new epidemiological data from Saudi Arabia, including updated incidence estimates, polyp prevalence studies, colonoscopy quality audit data, and national screening uptake surveys, to provide a comprehensively evidence-anchored and locally contextualized framework. A national multidisciplinary group formulated 25 key Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) questions across seven domains. Systematic literature searches were performed from inception to March 2026. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence profiles were prepared for critical outcomes, and recommendations were developed through an iterative consensus process requiring ≥80% agreement for strong recommendations. The Task Force strongly recommends implementing an organized national CRC screening program for all asymptomatic average-risk adults aged 45 to 75 years. Biennial fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) is recommended as the primary population-based screening modality. Colonoscopy every 10 years is a recommended alternative. All positive FIT results must be followed by timely, high-quality colonoscopy. Specific recommendations are provided for high-risk groups. High-certainty evidence from multiple randomized trials and large-scale implementation studies demonstrates that organized CRC screening substantially reduces CRC-specific mortality and incidence. A phased, FIT-based national implementation strategy is recommended, tailored to Saudi epidemiology, population preferences, and healthcare infrastructure, with iterative quality improvement as new evidence emerges.

articles.title: Associations between cesarean delivery and adverse maternal and newborn outcomes by Robson Group: An analysis of the PRISMA study cohort in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Rising cesarean section (CS) rates in low- and middle-income countries may mask a triple burden of unmet need, overuse, and unsafe provision. Using the Robson ten-group classification, a global standard for monitoring institutional deliveries, we examined CS incidence and associations with adverse outcomes.

METHODS: Data were drawn from the Pregnancy Risk, Infant Surveillance, and Measurement Alliance Maternal and Newborn Health Study, an open cohort study in Kenya, Zambia, India, and Pakistan (2022-2025). We generated descriptive statistics for Robson groups and within-group relative risks of adverse events for CS versus vaginal delivery using multivariable adjusted log Poisson models.

RESULTS: Among 10 996 women, 29% delivered by CS. Group 5 (prior CS) and group 10 (preterm) were the largest contributors, accounting for 28% and 17% of all CS deliveries, respectively. Between-site differences in CS incidence were most pronounced for groups 2 and 4 (induced labor/pre-labor CS), ranging from 20% to 60% for nullipara and from 7% to 44% for multipara. Compared with vaginal delivery, CS was associated with an increased risk of maternal near miss, prolonged hospitalization, hemorrhage, and newborn intensive care unit admission. Stratified by Robson group, adverse outcome risk was concentrated among lower-obstetric-risk groups.

CONCLUSION: Repeat CS, preterm deliveries, labor induction, and pre-labor CS were drivers of CS. Although differences in risk magnitude associated with CS across Robson groups revealed important patterns for quality improvement, these estimates should not be interpreted as causal effects. Equipping facilities to manage labor induction, trials of labor after cesarean, and preterm deliveries is critical to improving quality of care.

articles.title: Estimating Prevalence of Early Symptomatic Alzheimer's Disease and the Demand for amyloid-targeting therapies in China: A Meta-analysis and Modelling Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Amyloid-targeting therapies provide disease-modifying treatment for early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the number of individuals potentially eligible for treatment in China remains uncertain. We aimed to synthesize the prevalence of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD among older adults in China and quantify the population potentially eligible for amyloid-targeting therapies.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, SinoMed, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure were searched from January 1, 2020 through August 6, 2026. Population-based observational studies reporting MCI or AD prevalence among adults aged ≥ 60 years in mainland China were included; studies restricted to selected disease subgroups and non-primary reports were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Checklist for Prevalence Studies. Prevalence estimates were synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis and incorporated into a stepwise funnel model accounting for healthcare consultation, clinical diagnosis, biomarker testing, and amyloid positivity. Scenario and probabilistic sensitivity analyses assessed uncertainty.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies involving 312,204 participants were included; most were of moderate quality. Pooled prevalence was 21.21% [95% confidence interval (CI) 17.41-25.01%; I2 = 99.7%] for MCI and 4.72% (95% CI 3.13-6.31%; I2 = 99.8%) for AD. Under current healthcare consultation, diagnostic, and biomarker testing conditions, an estimated 39,825 individuals were potentially eligible for amyloid-targeting therapies. When these constraints were removed, the estimated potentially eligible population increased to 14.17 million. Study heterogeneity was substantial, and age-stratified evidence was limited.

CONCLUSION: China has a substantial population potentially eligible for amyloid-targeting therapies, but current healthcare consultation, diagnostic, and biomarker testing constraints markedly limit treatment access. These estimates can inform diagnostic capacity planning, resource allocation, treatment access, and reimbursement decisions.

articles.title: The Societal Burden of Sickle Cell Disease: A Life Course Perspective.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sickle cell disease (SCD) places a lifelong burden on patients and family members. Our objective was to review the available evidence to understand the impact of SCD across the life course, including childhood development, education, employment, quality of life, and life expectancy.

METHODS: This targeted literature review examined empirical studies from 2001 to 2026 that assessed the burden of SCD among patients and family caregivers across different life stages, including childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Outcomes included early childhood development, education, labor market outcomes, life expectancy, and impact on family caregivers.

RESULTS: Overall, 23 unique studies were included. Studies consistently demonstrated that SCD places a large burden on patients and family caregivers across all life stages, especially for those with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises. Many children with SCD experience significant developmental delays in cognition, while adolescents often experience greater school absenteeism, worse academic performance, and a higher likelihood of school dropout. Caregivers for children with SCD experience lost labor market opportunities and diminished mental health. Adults with SCD are less likely to work (unemployment), and when they do, they often have greater work absenteeism and presenteeism, worse job opportunities, and less income. Ultimately, people with SCD experience both lower overall life expectancy and lower quality of life.

CONCLUSION: Patients with SCD experience a burden associated with the disease across the life course. These outcomes should inform future evaluations of treatment and supportive services for SCD, which have the potential to generate substantial societal value.

articles.title: DISC-OSA: A European Delphi Consensus on OSA Screening in People with Obesity.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is common among people with obesity (PwO) but remains frequently underrecognized and undertreated. The absence of harmonized screening frameworks in Europe leads to delayed diagnosis, preventable cardiometabolic complications, and increased strain on health systems. This study aimed to establish a Europe-wide expert consensus on the principles, target populations, and practical approaches to OSA screening in adults with obesity, thereby providing a structured framework to guide clinical and policy decisions.

METHODS: A two-round, modified mixed-methods Delphi study was conducted in accordance with the ACcurate COnsensus Reporting Document (ACCORD) 2024 reporting guidelines. A total of 20 draft statements across nine domains, informed by a pragmatic literature review, were considered by 26 multidisciplinary experts from European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO) Collaborating Centres for Obesity Management. An independent Steering Committee oversaw governance and ethics. Consensus was defined as 70% or greater agreement and an interquartile range (IQR) of ≤ 1 on a 5-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: All 20 statements met the predefined consensus criteria, particularly those emphasizing prioritization of PwO with cardiometabolic comorbidities, embedding screening within structured care pathways, and timely referral for diagnostic assessment. The STOP-Bang questionnaire was recommended as a first-line tool, with nocturnal oximetry or polysomnography as supplementary options. Consensus-endorsed statements informed a European consensus algorithm detailing who, how, and when to screen.

CONCLUSIONS: This expert consensus provides a practical, scalable, and evidence-informed framework for systematic OSA screening within obesity care, supporting harmonized practice, early detection, and multidisciplinary management across European health care.

articles.title: Sustained Anlotinib-Based Combination Therapy Beyond Progression in Advanced Soft Tissue Sarcoma: A Large Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Multitarget antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors play a pivotal role in the treatment of soft tissue sarcoma (STS), but acquired resistance is common, and treatment discontinuation at progression may trigger tumor rebound. Evidence for continuing antiangiogenic therapy beyond progression in STS remains limited. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of sustained anlotinib-based combination therapy in patients with advanced STS who had progressed on prior anlotinib therapy.

METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed patients with advanced STS from four representative Chinese sarcoma centers. Patients who received anlotinib-based combinations after progression on prior anlotinib were included. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, disease control rate (DCR), and safety.

RESULTS: Between February 15, 2020, and March 31, 2023, 217 patients were included. The median age was 61 (range, 26-88) years, and 131 patients (60.4%) were male. With a median follow-up of 7.4 months, the median PFS was 4.2 (95% CI, 3.7-4.5) months, with a 21.9% 6-month PFS rate. The median OS was not reached, and the 6-month OS rate was 91.4%. No objective responses were observed, but stable disease was achieved in 158 patients, resulting in a DCR of 72.8%. The most common treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20.7%) and hand-foot syndrome (14.7%), and no unexpected toxicities were observed.

CONCLUSION: Sustained anlotinib-based treatment beyond disease progression showed promising clinical activity in patients with advanced STS, with a safety profile generally consistent with that previously reported for anlotinib. These findings warrant validation in future studies.

articles.title: Rethinking type 2 diabetes: a bone marrow disease under metabolic disguise?
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is traditionally viewed as a metabolic disorder driven by insulin resistance and progressive pancreatic β-cell failure. This review examines how metabolic stress remodels the bone marrow (BM) niche and whether these alterations contribute to inflammatory haematopoiesis, defective vascular repair and disease progression. The BM niche is a specialized microenvironment integrating endothelial, mesenchymal, neural, adipocytic, and immune components that cooperatively regulate hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) maintenance, mobilization and immune homeostasis. Evidence from animal models, together with more limited human observations, indicates that obesity-associated inflammation, lipotoxicity and hyperglycaemia can alter these compartments, favour myeloid-biased haematopoiesis and induce persistent metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. The resulting inflammatory myeloid output may subsequently amplify adipose-tissue and pancreatic islet inflammation, while vascular and autonomic niche dysfunction may constrain endogenous repair, creating bidirectional feedback between systemic metabolic dysfunction and the BM. We integrate these processes within diabet(ogen)ic nicheopathy, a proposed research framework encompassing BM alterations that may arise from and potentially reinforce metabolic disease. Particular attention is given to BM adipose tissue, BM-pancreas inflammatory crosstalk, progenitor mobilopathy and the therapeutic implications of BM programming. However, whether BM alterations precede overt T2D, contribute independently to its progression or predominantly reflect cumulative metabolic injury remains unresolved. The BM niche should therefore be regarded as an emerging mechanistic and therapeutic target rather than an established determinant of T2D progression.

articles.title: Pregnancy as an important factor in female autoimmunity.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases (ADs) affect 5-10% of the population, with 80-85% of diagnosed patients being women. This pronounced sexual dimorphism is influenced by genetic factors (X chromosome), fluctuations in sex hormones, and unique immunological changes occurring during pregnancy and the postpartum period. These factors contribute to women's distinct susceptibility to autoimmune disorders and may influence their clinical course. This narrative review critically evaluates the immunological, hormonal, and pregnancy-related factors contributing to female autoimmunity with particular emphasis on the bidirectional interactions between pregnancy-induced immunomodulation and maternal autoimmunity. By contrasting four distinct diseases systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), multiple sclerosis (MS), and type 1 diabetes (T1D), representing different immune paradigms (type 1 T helper (Th1) vs. type 2 T helper (Th2), systemic vs. organ-specific), we aim to analyze how mechanisms like placental tolerance and fetal microchimerism specifically shape disease trajectories and obstetric outcomes, contextualized within the evolutionary pregnancy compensation hypothesis. A literature review (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) was conducted to synthesize clinical and molecular evidence. The mechanisms of placental immune tolerance, the phenomenon of fetal microchimerism, and the evolutionary pregnancy compensation hypothesis were analyzed. Selected autoimmune diseases were used to illustrate disease-specific manifestations of these mechanisms. The literature highlights the complex interplay between genetic, hormonal and immunological factors in female autoimmunity. Estrogens, progesterone, androgens and prolactin exert distinct immunomodulatory effects influencing immune cell activity, cytokine production and immune tolerance. Fetal microchimerism (FMc) may have long-term immunological consequences, potentially contributing to either immune regulation or autoimmune pathology. These mechanisms may help explain the variable effects of pregnancy on autoimmune disease activity and obstetric outcomes, as illustrated by SLE, RA, MS, and T1D. The pregnancy compensation hypothesis offers an additional evolutionary perspective. However, it remains speculative and requires further investigation. Pregnancy induces complex, disease-specific immunomodulatory changes. Instead of one-size-fits-all regimens, caring for pregnant women with autoimmune disease requires a highly personalized and multidisciplinary approach based on risk stratification and monitoring of specific biomarkers. Current evidence suggests an intriguing influence of molecular changes on the course of autoimmunity; however, a full understanding of these mechanisms requires further, targeted research.

articles.title: The hepatic immune niche in liver diseases and transplantation: from homeostasis to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: The liver combines continuous exposure to gut-derived antigens and metabolites with immune surveillance and tissue repair. Its immune niche is organized by interactions among sinusoidal endothelial cells, Kupffer cells, recruited leukocytes, and parenchymal and stromal cells. At homeostasis, these interactions support antigen clearance and restrained immune activation. Persistent injury changes antigen presentation, metabolite availability, leukocyte recruitment, and extracellular matrix composition, allowing local immune responses to contribute to continued tissue damage. In chronic viral, steatotic, alcohol-associated, cholestatic, and autoimmune liver diseases, distinct patterns of myeloid activation, lymphocyte dysfunction, cytotoxicity, and fibrogenesis emerge at parenchymal, biliary, and vascular interfaces. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) adds tumor-derived signals that suppress antitumor immunity within a heterogeneous hepatic environment. In liver transplantation, perioperative injury intersects with donor-specific cellular and humoral immunity, with outcomes ranging from controlled donor reactivity to distinct, sometimes overlapping forms of rejection and chronic remodeling. Xenotransplantation further exposes the graft to interspecies antibody, complement, endothelial, and coagulation incompatibilities. In inflammatory liver disease and transplantation, blocking local signals that support pathogenic lymphocyte survival or myeloid activation may reduce continued tissue injury. In HCC, limiting tumor-derived metabolic signals that suppress immune-cell function may instead help restore antitumor responses. Continued recruitment from the circulation may replenish pathogenic populations despite suppression of cells already within the liver, making cellular recruitment an additional potential target. Effective treatment must therefore interrupt the processes sustaining injury while preserving antimicrobial defense, antitumor surveillance, graft regulation, and tissue repair.

articles.title: Thrombotic and Hemorrhagic Events in Myeloproliferative Neoplasms.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: MPNs are clonal hematopoietic disorders characterized by a propensity for venous and arterial thrombosis in addition to bleeding complications, which contribute substantially to disease morbidity and mortality. This review outlines the epidemiology, risk factors and management approach for these entities, with attention to special circumstances such as atypical thrombosis. We additionally highlight knowledge gaps and propose a future research agenda.

RECENT RINDINGS: JAK2 mutation status has emerged as an important risk factor for thrombosis pathogenesis, particularly at atypical sites. Uncontrolled cytoses, particularly erythrocytosis and leukocytosis are other important risk factors. There is emerging evidence that interferon and ruxolitinib may have disease-modifying potential particularly in PV and ET, however more high-quality data is needed and guidelines do not currently indicate a preference for a particular cytoreductive therapy (apart from hydroxyurea in ET). Prevention and treatment of thrombosis is the primary goal of therapy for MPNs. A high index of suspicion for occult MPN is required in the setting of splanchnic vein thrombosis even in the case of normal blood counts. The approach to management is based on risk stratification and involves the use of antiplatelet therapy, hematocrit control, and cytoreduction, along with anticoagulation for patients who develop thrombosis. Patients are at risk of iatrogenic bleeding as a result of therapy, and due to the development of acquired Von Willebrand syndrome. The field will continue to benefit from a more detailed understanding of the currently available disease-modifying therapies, development of new ones, and continued improvement of risk stratification models.

articles.title: Urinary Sodium-to-Potassium Ratio in Hypertension: From Epidemiologic Marker to Clinical Tool?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review evaluates whether the urinary sodium-to-potassium (Na/K) ratio can move from an epidemiologic biomarker of dietary electrolyte balance to a clinically useful tool in hypertension care, focusing on biological rationale, measurement, interpretation, blood pressure associations, cardiovascular-kidney outcomes, and limitations.

RECENT FINDINGS: Population-based, repeated-measurement, and treated-hypertension studies link higher urinary Na/K ratios with higher blood pressure, hypertension risk, poorer blood pressure control, and selected cardiovascular outcomes. Associations appear strongest when measurements are repeated and interpreted alongside home blood pressure. Emerging consensus recommendations and self-monitoring studies suggest practical implementation pathways, while salt-substitution trials support the broader importance of modifying sodium-potassium balance. The urinary Na/K ratio is physiologically grounded and clinically promising, but it is not yet a validated treatment target. Clinical translation requires standardized measurement protocols, validated thresholds across diverse populations, intervention trials, and safety data in high-risk groups.

articles.title: Immunosenescence in Metabolic Disorders: From Cellular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review comprehensively examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the crosstalk between metabolic disorders and immunosenescence and elucidates the fundamental roles of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and immune surveillance while critically evaluating both classical and emerging therapeutic strategies that target these pathways.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence indicates that immune cells displaying senescence-associated phenotypes accumulate in adipose tissue, liver, and vasculature, where they exhibit mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodeling, and a maladaptive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) driven by NF-κB and C/EBPβ. Key SASP components, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and CCL2, together with p53/p21- and p16/RB-mediated cell-cycle arrest and cGAS-STING pathway activation, contribute to adipocyte hypertrophy, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and dyslipidemia. These changes are associated with the accelerated progression of obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and atherosclerosis. Additionally, CH and impaired immune surveillance exacerbate chronic metabolic inflammation. This review discusses classical interventions, including metabolic modulators, senolytics, and senomorphics, alongside emerging strategies such as Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTAC)-based senolytics, CH-targeted approaches, and mitochondrial-targeted therapies, emphasizing mechanistic differences and supporting clinical evidence. Nevertheless, challenges related to achieving tissue-specific delivery while minimizing systemic toxicity remain unresolved. Immunosenescence plays a dual role; transient and context-dependent SASP signaling can contribute to tissue repair, whereas persistent or dysregulated SASP activity can promote pathology. Currently, validated clinical tools for assessing immune-driven metabolic dysfunction are lacking. This absence of standardized evaluation frameworks hinders the translation of these therapies into clinical practice, highlighting the necessity for a theoretical foundation to guide precision treatment of obesity-related metabolic diseases and to promote healthy aging.

articles.title: Nanomaterial-based glucose sensors: detection platforms and highlight applications.
articles.abstract: Glucose acts as a fundamental energy substrate sustaining human physiological homeostasis, and aberrant blood glucose levels are tightly correlated with a spectrum of metabolic disorders, particularly diabetes mellitus, which has evolved into a severe global public health crisis. Precise, rapid, and stable glucose monitoring is therefore indispensable for the early diagnosis, clinical intervention, and long-term management of diabetes. Conventional enzyme-dependent glucose sensors suffer from inherent limitations, including high manufacturing costs, inferior environmental stability, short service lifespan, and susceptibility to fluctuations in pH and temperature, which substantially constrain their practical clinical and industrial applications. Benefiting from their unique structural tunability and superior physicochemical properties, nanomaterial-based glucose sensing platforms have emerged as high-performance alternatives to traditional enzymatic sensors, achieving remarkable advancements in detection sensitivity, selectivity, and operational stability, while enabling continuous and non-invasive glucose monitoring. This comprehensive review systematically elaborates the state-of-the-art progress of nanomaterial-enabled glucose sensing technologies, focusing on two dominant detection modalities: electrochemical and optical sensing strategies. We emphatically discuss the rational design of functional nanomaterials, innovative construction of multicomponent nanocomposites, development of flexible wearable sensing systems, and emerging signal transduction mechanisms. Meanwhile, this review comprehensively categorizes and evaluates the performance characteristics and application progress of diverse nanomaterial-based glucose sensors, covering precious/non-precious metal nanomaterials, metal-organic frameworks, carbon-based materials, multifunctional nanocomposites, and molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)-integrated sensing platforms. Furthermore, we thoroughly analyze the current commercialization landscape of continuous and non-invasive glucose monitoring devices. Finally, the core challenges hindering the clinical translation and large-scale commercialization of high-performance glucose sensors are highlighted, and targeted future research directions and development prospects are prospected, aiming to provide insightful theoretical guidance and technical references for the design and optimization of next-generation clinical glucose sensing technologies.

articles.title: The Pathological Roles of β-adrenergic Receptors in Melanoma and Their Potential as Therapeutic Targets: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: β-adrenergic receptors (ADRBs) are key mediators of stress responses, which have important roles in cancer growth and dissemination. β-blockers, inhibitors of ADRBs that are well established for treating cardiovascular conditions, have been proposed to be potentially useful, cost-effective, repurposed drugs for treating various cancers, including melanomas. This study aims to critically appraise the evidence for the diverse roles of ADRBs in melanoma cell biology and pathogenesis, through a systematic review of the literature and a meta-analysis of clinical applications of β-blockers in melanoma patients.

RECENT FINDINGS: In vivo and in vitro experimental studies have shown β-blockers to have various beneficial effects on melanoma cell proliferation, tumor growth, differentiation, angiogenesis, metabolism, immune evasion, invasion and metastasis. However, many of these studies have used high drug concentrations that have questionable specificity for ADRBs and are clinically unattainable. The role of ADRBs in interactions between melanoma cells and tumor-infiltrating nerve and immune cells is being defined. Clinical application of β-blockers in melanoma patients may provide some progression-free survival benefit when taken prior to disease onset, indicating a role for ADRBs in melanoma progression. New approaches to administering β-blockers via synthetic particles are being developed to improve their effectiveness. Our understanding of the importance of ADRBs in the pathogenesis and treatment of cancer has grown rapidly in recent years. ADRBs are at the nexus between the sympathetic nervous system and immune cells in melanomas. Determination of the optimal approach to implementing β-blockers to treat melanomas awaits further biological and clinical studies that will clarify their intrinsic effects and their interactions with existing treatments.

articles.title: Potential of novel indigenous bacteria in the biodegradation of polyethylene terephthalate: morphological and molecular insights.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) polyester accumulation in ecosystems has emerged as a significant environmental concern due to its slow degradation and the release of hazardous substances. Addressing this issue has become critical to mitigating plastic pollution. Microbial degradation has recently provided promising insights into the biodegradation of various plastics. A plastic-contaminated site was sampled, and enrichment-based isolation was performed using terephthalic acid (TPA), resulting in the isolation of 32 distinct bacterial strains. These strains were screened for their ability to utilize PET as a sole carbon source, resulting in the selection of 10 potential degraders, among which three bacterial strains were identified as the most promising. The strains were identified through 16 S rRNA gene amplification and classified as Glutamicibacter endophyticus PGP1, Paracoccus pantotrophus PGS1, and Ochrobactrum teleogrylli PGLW4. Further, the strains were tested for PET degradation, achieving degradation rates of 36.6%, 25.6%, and 27.7% for PGP1, PGS1, and PGLW4, respectively. Interestingly, these strains were not reported for their ability to degrade PET microplastic (MP). The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal morphological changes, such as the formation of pits, cavities, and cracks, in PET sheets treated with the tested strains, and no cracks were seen in the control sheet. Changes in the chemical bonds of PET sheets revealed by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) showed the degradation potential of isolated bacterial strains.

articles.title: Individualized Amplitude-Time Models of Post-activation Performance Enhancement Using the Velocity-Loss Method in Trained Populations: A Systematic Review and Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Five study-level models describe post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) amplitude-time characteristics: (i) nil or fluctuating, (ii) immediate enhancement, (iii) inverted-U enhancement, (iv) skewed or delayed inverted-U enhancement, and (v) performance impairment. However, the moderators of these models at the individual level remain unclear. Velocity-loss (VL) approaches, which reflect neuromuscular fatigue, may provide a useful framework to better understand these amplitude-time characteristics.

OBJECTIVES: The aims of this study were (i) to establish an individualized PAPE amplitude-time model using VL-based conditioning activities (CAs); (ii) to examine how relative maximal strength (RMS) affects performance changes across recovery times at the individual level; and (iii) to investigate how VL methods influence study-level PAPE amplitude-time characteristics through within- and between-study analyses.

METHODS: Three databases were systematically searched. Studies were included if CA involved squats or bench presses prescribed using the VL method and reported performance outcomes reflecting PAPE magnitude. Individual performance-recovery relationships were modeled using linear and nonlinear regression. A generalized linear mixed-effects model was applied to analyze the one-stage (individual participant data) effects of RMS on performance changes, while a three-level (multilevel) model was used for two-stage (study-level) meta-analysis. Multivariate linear and nonlinear models tested moderators including recovery time, sex, CA type, VL threshold, %1-repetition maximum (RM), and number of sets.

RESULTS: Fifteen studies were included, with individual data from nine studies (248 participants: 224 males, 24 females). Individual performance-recovery responses generally matched the five established study-level PAPE amplitude-time patterns, though random deviations were observed. One-stage analyses revealed that individuals with low RMS (< ~ 1.5, unstable estimates) exhibited early enhancement followed by decline, whereas those with high RMS (> ~ 1.5) showed early decrements followed by an inverted-U response. Greater RMS was linked to smaller peak improvements (β = - 2.65) but was unrelated to minimum values (β = - 0.86). In females, maximal improvements occurred at RMS ~ 1.00-1.25, with lowest minimum values at ~ 1.25-1.50. Two-stage analyses indicated that VL alone did not significantly improve performance (standardized mean change = 0.11), but yielded greater improvements than control conditions (rest or traditional CA; standardized mean difference = 0.35). Recovery time, %1-RM, and VL threshold emerged as key moderators.

CONCLUSIONS: Individual PAPE amplitude-time models exhibited random deviations from, but generally reflected, study-level patterns. Strength level influenced individual responses, with distinct PAPE profiles observed across participants. At the study level, 5% VL, 10% VL, and 60-90% 1-RM CAs appeared most effective for inducing peak PAPE responses. However, at the individual level, there was no single 'optimal' prescription, only a 'most suitable' one.

PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: The original protocol was prospectively registered ( osf.io/hf6px ) with the Open Science Framework.

articles.title: Limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed to pool risk ratios for early binary outcomes and hazard ratios for long-term outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-five reports were included in the updated systematic review. After endpoint-specific adjudication of potentially overlapping institutional cohorts, the number of reports contributing to each pooled analysis varied by outcome. EAR was associated with a higher risk of early mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.01-1.70) and re-exploration for bleeding (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45). No statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.96-1.20) or dialysis (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.99-1.49). HR-based analyses showed no statistically significant association with overall survival (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.91-1.92) or distal aortic reintervention (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.07-13.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In retrospective observational comparisons, EAR was associated with higher early mortality and re-exploration for bleeding, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke or dialysis. No statistically significant associations were detected for overall survival or distal aortic reintervention. These findings do not establish causal effects of repair extent and remain limited by confounding by indication.

articles.title: Alcohol-Tolerant Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01 Prevents Acute Alcoholic Liver Injury by Reducing Blood Alcohol Concentration and Modulating Gut Microbiota in Mice.
articles.abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health concern with limited effective interventions. This study screened and identified a lactic acid bacterial strain with potent ethanol-degrading capacity, designated as Lactiplantibacillus plantarum LBP-L01. Sequence alignment-based annotation of the L. plantarum LBP-L01 genome identified genes involved in alcohol metabolism. LBP-L01 exhibited robust safety profiles, as demonstrated by its tolerance, adhesive capacity, low biogenic amine production, and genomic analysis. LBP-L01 significantly accelerated alcohol metabolism possibly by increasing hepatic alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH) and acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) activities, leading to reduced blood ethanol and acetaldehyde levels in a model of ALD. Concurrently, LBP-L01 alleviated hepatic oxidative stress, as evidenced by decreased malondialdehyde (MDA) level and increased superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activities. It also suppressed inflammation by reducing TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels, which may involve the attenuation of TLR-4 signaling and activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. These hepatoprotective effects were associated with modulation of gut microbiota (characterized by increases in beneficial genera such as Dubosiella, norank_f_Muribaculaceae, and Lachnospiraceae NK4A136_group; alongside a reduction in harmful bacteria such as Escherichia-Shigella) and elevated production of short chain fatty acids (SCFAs). These findings suggest that LBP-L01 protects against ALD possibly through a dual mechanism involving ethanol degradation and gut microbiota-mediated antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects, highlighting its potential as a functional probiotic for ALD prevention.

articles.title: Therapeutic and Epigenetic Effects of Bee Venom on Acute Toxoplasmosis in Mice: A Parasitological, Histopathological, and MicroRNA Analysis.
articles.abstract: Acute toxoplasmosis can cause severe complications, while available treatments may be associated with adverse effects. Bee venom (BV) has potential antiparasitic and immunomodulatory properties; however, its therapeutic effects against acute toxoplasmosis, particularly in combination with spiramycin (SPI), remain insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated the effects of BV alone and in combination with SPI on parasitic burden, histopathological alterations, and serum microRNA expression in experimental acute toxoplasmosis. Acute toxoplasmosis was induced in Swiss albino mice using the virulent RH strain of Toxoplasma gondii. Infected mice received different BV and/or SPI treatment regimens. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed by determining tachyzoite counts in peritoneal fluid, examining liver and lung histopathology, and measuring serum expression of mmu-miR-712-3p and mmu-miR-146b-5p using real-time PCR. The different treatment regimens demonstrated varying degrees of therapeutic efficacy, with the combined BV + SPI regimen producing the greatest reduction in tachyzoite counts (96%) compared with untreated infected mice. Infection was associated with 24.47-fold and 83.64-fold increases in mmu-miR-712-3p and mmu-miR-146b-5p expression, respectively. Treatment significantly reduced the expression of these microRNAs, with the greatest reduction observed following combined therapy. Histopathological examination revealed improvements in hepatic and pulmonary lesions following treatment, with the most pronounced amelioration observed in the BV + SPI group. These findings suggest that BV has promising therapeutic potential against acute experimental toxoplasmosis, both alone and in combination with SPI. The observed changes in mmu-miR-712-3p and mmu-miR-146b-5p expression warrant further investigation to clarify their roles in the host response to infection and their potential value as indicators of treatment response.

articles.title: Biopsy-Validated Performance of Non-Invasive Tests for Preoperative Liver Assessment in Adults with Grade II-III Obesity Undergoing Metabolic Bariatric Surgery.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with advanced liver fibrosis in metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) candidates influences perioperative risk and management. The diagnostic performance of non-invasive liver tests (NITs) remains insufficiently validated in grade II-III obesity. We aimed to evaluate biopsy-validated diagnostic performance of liver NITs in this population.

METHODS: Adults with grade II-III obesity and MASLD scheduled for MBS underwent preoperative vibration controlled elastography (VCTE) with controlled attenuated parameter (CAP) (Fibroscan®, Echosens, Fr), Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) and Fibroscan®-AST (FAST) score calculation and systematic intraoperative liver biopsy. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curve analysis and Youden index.

RESULTS: Overall, 585 participants were included (BMI 44.7 ± 5.1 kg/m²; 40.8 ± 9.6 years, 87% female). Significant (≥F2) and advanced (≥F3) liver fibrosis prevalence was 6.3% and 3.9%. FIB-4 discrimination for ≥F3 was excellent (AUROC 0.91). An optimized cut-off of 1.07 yielded 96% sensitivity and 99.8% negative predictive value. VCTE showed an AUROC of 0.89 for ≥F3 with 97.8% success rate. For fibrosis ≥F3, using the cohort-derived FIB-4 threshold of 1.07 instead of 1.30 increased the sensitivity of sequential FIB-4/VCTE testing from 65.2% to 82.6%. CAP demonstrated good accuracy for steatosis detection (AUROC 0.80). FAST score was able to rule out at risk-MASH with negative predictive value over 97%.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large grade II-III obesity cohort, FIB-4 and VCTE demonstrated high accuracy for ruling out advanced fibrosis. A lower FIB-4 threshold of 1.07 improved the sensitivity of sequential FIB-4/VCTE testing; however, external validation is required before its clinical implementation. CAP and FAST provided good performance for steatosis and at-risk MASH detection. These results may support the incorporation of NITs into the routine preoperative evaluation of MBS candidates, allowing identification of patients requiring specialized hepatology care.

KEY POINTS: • Large biopsy-validated severe obesity cohort undergoing MBS. • FIB-4 showed excellent negative predictive value for advanced fibrosis. • FIB-4 cut-off 1.07 improved sensitivity for advanced fibrosis diagnosis. • VCTE showed strong accuracy for ≥F2 and ≥ F3 fibrosis detection.

articles.title: Adverse Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors in Pediatric Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Proportions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have become a foundational therapy for adult heart failure across the entire spectrum of ejection fraction, but their safety profile in children with heart failure has not been quantitatively synthesized. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions to summarize the incidence of adverse events associated with SGLT2 inhibitors in pediatric heart failure.

STUDY DESIGN: In this systematic review and meta-analysis of proportions (PROSPERO CRD420261355711; PRISMA 2020), five databases were searched through June 2026 for studies of any design reporting adverse events among pediatric patients receiving an SGLT2 inhibitor for heart failure. Random-effects incidence estimates were pooled using logit-transformed proportions with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman confidence intervals; risk of bias and GRADE certainty were assessed.

RESULTS: Ten studies (573 unique children; 2023-2026) were included; eight studies (572 patients; maximum pooled denominator 474) were meta-analyzed, and one case report was summarized narratively. Dapagliflozin accounted for 94.1% of exposures. Study-level dapagliflozin doses ranged from 0.11 to 0.23 mg/kg/day, while the single cohort reporting empagliflozin used a median dose of 0.13 mg/kg/day. No regimen was derived from pediatric heart-failure pharmacokinetic data, and in the only cohort reporting a comparison, infants received a higher weight-normalized dose than older children (0.18 versus 0.16 mg/kg/day). Pooled incidences were: any adverse event 21.2% (95% CI 10.7-37.8%), acute kidney injury 10.7% (3.5-28.1%), urinary tract infection 7.8% (4.8-12.4%), treatment discontinuation 7.0% (4.5-10.6%), all-cause mortality 5.6% (2.4-12.5%), hypoglycemia 2.9% (0.9-9.3%), genital mycotic infection 2.7% (0.9-8.2%), and diabetic ketoacidosis 1.3% (0.4-3.9%). No deaths were attributed to therapy, and no cases of euglycemic ketoacidosis or Fournier gangrene occurred. Directional efficacy signals were consistently favorable, with left ventricular ejection fraction improving in five of six cohorts and natriuretic peptide levels declining across all seven in which they were assessed.

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitors had a tolerable safety profile in pediatric heart failure, mirroring the adult experience. Adequately powered randomized trials with standardized adverse-event grading are needed.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier no. CRD420261355711.

articles.title: Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Pre-mix 70/30 Insulin Initiation in Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes: a Multicentre Pakistani Cohort.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In lower- and middle-income countries, insulin choice at initiation is driven as much by cost as by clinical need. Low-cost human pre-mix 70/30 insulin predominates in Pakistan, yet prospective real-world evidence on its outcomes and true cost is scarce.

METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, single-arm, prospective observational study at 12 sites in Pakistan, insulin-naïve adults with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c 9% or higher despite two or more oral drugs were started on human pre-mix 70/30 insulin at physician discretion and followed for 6 months, with assessments at baseline, day 90 and day 180. The primary outcomes were change in HbA1c and incidence of hypoglycaemia (classified by American Diabetes Association levels). A descriptive cost-consequence analysis (patient out-of-pocket perspective) was a pre-specified secondary exploratory objective.

RESULTS: A total of 384 of 430 screened patients were enrolled, with a mean baseline HbA1c of 11.2 ± 1.5%. HbA1c fell to 9.3 ± 1.5% at day 90 and to 8.8 ± 1.5% at day 180, a mean reduction of 2.3 ± 1.8% (p < 0.001), with no significant change in body weight. By day 180, 242 of 310 patients (78.1%) had achieved at least a 1% reduction in HbA1c, and 28 patients (9.0%) reached below 7%. Confirmed hypoglycaemia below 70 mg/dL occurred in eight patients (2.1%), and no severe or treatment-limiting events were recorded. Mean 6-month direct medical cost was 36,269 Pakistani Rupee (PKR) per patient. Insulin acquisition accounted for just PKR 7200 of this (19.8%), while consultations, injection consumables, diagnostics and self-monitoring made up the remainder.

CONCLUSIONS: In routine practice, human pre-mix 70/30 insulin produced clinically meaningful and sustained HbA1c reductions with a favourable safety profile, supporting its effectiveness for insulin initiation in poorly controlled type 2 diabetes. Affordability, however, was governed by the total cost of care rather than insulin price alone.

articles.title: Weighted Cumulative Exposure of HbA1c and LDL-C and All-Cause Mortality in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The long-term impact of glycemic and lipid control on prognosis in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains incompletely understood, as conventional metrics fail to capture the temporal accumulation of exposure. This study aimed to apply the weighted cumulative exposure (WCE) model to quantify the time-weighted cumulative effects of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) on all-cause mortality.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used electronic health records from January 2000 to April 2025 from the Tianjin Health and Medical Big Data Platform. WCE models with one-knot constrained splines were fitted for HbA1c and LDL-C, with the optimal lag window selected by the Akaike and Bayesian information criteria (AIC/BIC). Multivariable Cox models were constructed with HbA1c-WCE and LDL-WCE as separate exposures, forcing glucose- and lipid-lowering medications into the models. Model fit of baseline, time-weighted mean, and WCE definitions was compared.

RESULTS: A total of 7978 patients were included (median follow-up 5.04 years; 402 deaths). A uniform 60-month lag window was adopted. HbA1c weight peaked at approximately 17 months before death and then declined; LDL-C weight peaked at about 33 months and remained non-negative throughout. After adjustment, sustained HbA1c 8% versus 6.5% had a hazard ratio of 1.14 (1.04-1.27); sustained LDL-C 3.4 versus 1.8 mmol/l had a hazard ratio of 1.40 (1.10-1.74). The time-weighted mean yielded the lowest AIC for both markers.

CONCLUSIONS: HbA1c's effect peaked early and declined, suggesting that recent values carry greater prognostic weight and supporting regular reassessment rather than reliance on a single baseline value, whereas LDL-C's effect emerged more slowly and persisted longer, suggesting a role for early initiation and sustained adherence.

articles.title: Prevalence and Clinical Determinants of Frailty in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Attending a Diabetes Centre in India.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diabetes and frailty are both increasing in prevalence due to population ageing. However, data on these comorbid occurrences and real-world outcomes are scarce. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of frailty and its metabolic, nutritional and clinical associations in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) attending a diabetes centre in India.

METHODS: A total of 1171 individuals aged 65 years and above with T2DM were assessed for frailty using the validated Frailty Assessment and Screening Tool (FAST) questionnaire. Dominant-hand grip strength (HGS) was measured using a Jamar dynamometer, utilizing the American Society of Hand Therapists (ASHT) criteria. Additionally, sensitivity analysis was done using the Sarcopenia-Chandigarh Urban Bone Epidemiological Study (Sarco-CUBES) criteria. Standardized definitions were employed to evaluate microvascular complications associated with diabetes.

RESULTS: Individuals with T2DM had a mean age of 71.5 ± 5.4 years, and male participants constituted 65.3% of the study population. The overall prevalence of frailty was 59.0% (691/1171). Among the 691 individuals, FAST-defined frailty alone identified only 6.2% (43/691) individuals, whereas HGS-defined low muscle strength alone identified 80.7% (558/691), and 13.0% (90/691) met the FAST/HGS composite classification. Using Sarco-CUBES-derived cut-offs, the prevalence was 76.4% (895/1171). Logistic regression analysis showed that physical inactivity along with uncontrolled diabetes was associated with higher odds of frailty (adjusted odds ratio: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.48-3.03; p<0.001). Multivariable models identified advanced age,physical inactivity, lower protein intake, sulfonylurea use and uncontrolled diabetes as independently associated with frailty.  The prevalence of diabetic retinopathy was higher in the cohort with frailty compared to those without (74.3% vs. 65.6%; p = 0.032),even after adjusting for age, sex, HbA1c, and diabetes duration.

CONCLUSIONS: Among older Indian adults with T2DM attending a diabetes centre, 59.0-76.4% were classified as having frailty depending on criteria used. Increasing age, physical inactivity, inadequate protein intake and uncontrolled diabetes were significantly associated with frailty. Implementing routine screening along with targeted, comprehensive interventions and appropriate medications are essential to manage frailty in elderly patients with T2DM in India.

articles.title: State and trait anxiety following prenatal moderate- versus light-intensity exercise: a secondary analysis of a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prenatal anxiety may increase as pregnancy progresses, yet little is known about longitudinal patterns of state and trait anxiety among pregnant individuals participating in exercise interventions of differing intensities. This study examined state and trait anxiety across late pregnancy among pregnant individuals with obesity randomized to moderate-intensity walking or light-intensity stretching and explored associations between changes in anxiety and gestational hypertension.

METHODS: This secondary analysis used data from the Prenatal Heart Smart randomized trial. Seventy-six pregnant individuals with obesity completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) at approximately 28, 32, and 37 weeks' gestation after randomization to moderate-intensity walking (n = 42) or light-intensity stretching (n = 34). Linear mixed-effects models compared state and trait anxiety between intervention groups at the two follow-up assessments, accounting for baseline anxiety and repeated measurements. Because no significant intervention-group differences were observed, groups were combined to examine changes in anxiety across late pregnancy using paired t-tests. Exploratory analyses examined associations between anxiety change scores and gestational hypertension.

RESULTS: State and trait anxiety did not differ significantly between the walking and stretching groups at either follow-up assessment (all p ≥ .38). Despite previous evidence that anxiety may increase during late pregnancy, both state and trait anxiety remained relatively stable from approximately 28 to 37 weeks' gestation. Mean state anxiety scores were 30.0, 29.6, and 29.6 across the three assessments, respectively, while mean trait anxiety scores were 31.1, 32.1, and 30.4; neither measure changed significantly over time (all p ≥ .19). Exploratory analyses identified no significant associations between changes in anxiety and gestational hypertension after covariate adjustment. The small number of preeclampsia cases precluded analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: State and trait anxiety remained stable across late pregnancy among pregnant individuals with obesity participating in either moderate-intensity walking or light-intensity stretching, with no significant differences in anxiety outcomes between intervention groups. The stability of both situational and dispositional dimensions of anxiety across the third trimester adds to limited longitudinal evidence on prenatal anxiety during structured exercise participation. Because both groups received active exercise interventions and baseline anxiety was relatively low, the observed stability cannot be attributed to exercise. Studies including non-exercise comparison groups and participants with greater baseline anxiety are needed to determine whether exercise modality or intensity contributes to the maintenance of psychological well-being during late pregnancy.
