articles.title: An aging risk-factor scale: biomarkers of renal disease and anemia are primary predictors of three-year survival in common marmosets (Callithrix jacchus).
articles.abstract: Valid animal models are needed to evaluate how age-related changes in kidney function influence healthspan. Aging marmosets frequently develop renal insufficiency with anemia and exhibit reductions in body mass and metabolic rate. However, it remains unclear which age-related changes predict survival and which thresholds indicate increased mortality risk. We prospectively evaluated age, body composition, resting energy expenditure, hematology, and blood chemistry as predictors of 3-year survival in female and male marmosets (n = 66), 2-16 years of age. Objectives were to identify prognostic markers, define high-risk thresholds, and to develop and test a composite risk-factor scale for mortality screening in captivity. A 10-variable model showed the best predictive performance in multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling, and was retained for further analysis (concordance = 0.881, p < 0.001). ROC curves using Youden's Index and AUC identified high-risk thresholds for predictors in the multivariable model, and threshold-defined categories were evaluated by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. The 10 binary risk-factors were combined into a composite scale scored from 0 to 10 and tested with Cox regression. The scale explained approximately 42% of variance in survival and each additional risk factor increased mortality risk 1.75-fold (95% CI: 1.43-2.14, p < 0.001). Marmosets with ≥ 7 risk factors exhibited a 19-month reduction in survival, and this high-risk threshold predicted 3-year survival with 89.4% accuracy. Results support the scale as a screening tool for mortality risk and highlight the high prevalence of age-associated renal disease and anemia in marmosets.

articles.title: Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation on cardiovascular-related functional health status in older adults: secondary findings from the COSMOS randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Declines in cardiovascular-related functional health status are common with aging, yet the long-term effects of multivitamin-mineral (MVM) and cocoa extract (CE) supplementation on patient-reported outcomes remain unclear in older adults. This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline. All participants were included in intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses of physical ability score (PAS), symptom burden (SB), and clinical summary score (CSS), representing KCCQ outcomes over 3 years. Linear mixed-effects models estimated treatment effects, with prespecified subgroup analyses among participants with cardiac conditions. Among a total cohort of over 21,000 participants, those taking a daily MVM versus placebo had small but statistically significant improvements in SB (MD 0.44, 95% CI 0.13-0.74) and CSS (MD 0.33, 95% CI 0.09-0.57) (both P < 0.05), with no significant effect on PAS, compared to placebo. CE supplementation had no overall effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity in MVM effects according to carotid stenosis status, with year 3 ITT differences of 5.13 points for PAS and 4.95 points for CSS (P-interaction = 0.012 and 0.009, respectively). For CE, the primary ITT analysis provided limited evidence of subgroup benefit. This is the first large randomized clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effects of MVM and CE supplementation on KCCQ-assessed cardiovascular functional health in older adults. Our findings provide new evidence that daily MVM supplementation, but not CE, is associated with small improvements in cardiovascular-related functional health status among older adults, warranting further investigation. The trial was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02422745 ; unique identifier: NCT02422745.

articles.title: miR-6891 predicts atrial fibrillation recurrence and promotes fibroblast dysfunction.
articles.abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying AF pathogenesis and post‑ablation relapse remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the expression profile and prognostic value of miR‑6891 in AF, as well as its functional role and downstream mechanism in Ang II‑stimulated atrial fibroblasts. Serum miR‑6891 levels were measured by RT‑qPCR, and its recurrence‑predictive performance was evaluated by ROC curve. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent risk factors for post‑ablation recurrence. In vitro assays, human atrial fibroblasts were treated with Ang II to mimic pathological remodeling. Cellular migration, proliferation, ferroptosis markers (GSH‑Px, ROS, MDA, Fe²⁺), inflammatory cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑6, IL‑1β), and fibrosis‑related proteins (Collagen I, MMP9, Collagen III) were assessed. Target prediction and validation were conducted using bioinformatics and dual‑luciferase reporter assays. Functional rescue experiments were performed by co‑transfection with PTEN siRNA. miR‑6891 was significantly upregulated in serum of AF patients compared with controls and exhibited favorable predictive accuracy. Multivariate logistic regression identified miR‑6891 and hs‑CRP as independent predictors of recurrence. In vitro, miR‑6891 inhibition suppressed Ang II‑induced migration, proliferation, ferroptosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, Ang II downregulated PTEN, an effect reversed by miR‑6891 inhibitor. Silencing PTEN partially abrogated the protective effects of miR‑6891 inhibition on cellular dysfunction, ferroptosis, inflammation, and fibrosis. miR‑6891 is upregulated in AF and serves as a novel candidate independent predictor of post‑ablation recurrence. It mediates Ang II‑induced pathological changes in atrial fibroblasts by directly targeting PTEN, suggesting that miR‑6891 may represent a novel therapeutic target for AF management.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics, temporal trends, and predictors of liver transplantation-free survival in patients with autoimmune hepatitis: a nationwide Japanese registry study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Complete biochemical response (CBR) is a key therapeutic target in autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), but nationwide Japanese data linking treatment response, temporal changes in practice, and liver transplantation (LT)-free survival remain limited. We evaluated clinical characteristics, diagnostic period trends, and predictors of LT-free survival using the Japanese Autoimmune Hepatitis Study Group registry.

METHODS: Patients newly diagnosed with AIH between 1998 and 2024 were screened. Baseline diagnostic data were available for 3992 patients, and 2494 patients with follow-up data were included in the survival analysis. Landmark analyses were performed at 6 and 12 months after treatment initiation. CBR was defined as the normalization of serum AST, ALT, and IgG levels. LT-free survival was assessed using Kaplan‒Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 3992 patients, 1163 were diagnosed from 2018 onward. Recent patients were older and had a slightly lower female proportion, more frequent cirrhosis at diagnosis, and more frequent azathioprine and ursodeoxycholic acid use. In the survival cohort, the median age was 63 years, 82.6% were female, and 10.8% had cirrhosis. During a median follow-up of 3.2 years, CBR was achieved in 53.5% at the 6-month landmark and 66.9% at the 12-month landmark. The estimated LT-free survival rates were 96.6% at 3 years and 95.8% at 5 years. Older age, male sex, cirrhosis at diagnosis, and a lack of CBR at the 6- or 12-month landmark independently predicted poorer LT-free survival. In liver-specific analyses, cirrhosis at diagnosis and lack of early CBR remained associated with liver-related death or LT.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline cirrhosis and failure to achieve early CBR may help identify high-risk AIH patients who require closer monitoring and clinical reassessment.

articles.title: Metabolic risk factor burden and quantitative fibrosis are distinct prognostic modifiers in alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The 2023 steatotic liver disease (SLD) nomenclature separates MetALD {moderate alcohol intake plus at least one metabolic risk factor (MRF)} from alcohol-associated-liver-disease (ALD; heavy drinking), which is classified irrespective of metabolic burden. We examined whether MRF burden and histology modify one-year prognosis in alcohol-associated cirrhosis.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 409 adults with biopsy-proven alcohol-associated SLD cirrhosis. MetALD was defined by alcohol intake of 140-350 g/week in women or 210-420 g/week in men with at least one metabolic risk factor (MRF), and ALD by intake above 350 g/week in women or 420 g/week in men. Quantitative fibrosis was measured. The primary endpoint was the composite of death or liver transplantation at one year.

RESULTS: CPA rose stepwise across subtypes (p < 0.001). Death or transplantation rose from 9.4% (ALD 0-1) to 23.3% (MetALD) and 51.9% (ALD-hm; p < 0.001), and death alone (7.8%, 20.4%, 51.9%). On multivariable analysis, CPA (1.08; 95% CI 1.05-1.11) and MRF count (1.83; 95% CI 1.34-2.49) independently predicted death or transplantation. A CPA-plus-MRF prognostic model achieved a bootstrap-corrected AUROC: 0.818 (95% CI 0.762-0.873) versus 0.492 for MELD in a cohort whose MELD range was narrowed by biopsy eligibility (11.4-20.3); validation was by internal bootstrap only. Non-fatal liver events did not differ across subtypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-centre, biopsy-confirmed, predominantly male cohort, MetALD, ALD (0-1 MRF) and ALD-hm were prognostically distinct. Quantitative fibrosis and MRF count independently predicted death or liver transplantation. ALD-hm should be regarded as an observational finding.

articles.title: Alloplastic bone graft combined with injectable platelet-rich fibrin versus xenograft for horizontal ridge augmentation in the posterior mandible: a split-mouth randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare 6-month horizontal bone gain and early postoperative morbidity between an alloplastic graft with injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF) and xenograft alone, both placed simultaneously with implants using the decompression technique in the posterior mandible.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective split-mouth randomized controlled trial, 20 patients with bilateral posterior mandibular edentulism and insufficient horizontal bone width were enrolled. Each received a randomly assigned treatment: alloplastic graft with i-PRF (test) on one side and xenograft (control) on the other, both with simultaneous implant placement and a collagen membrane. The primary outcome was horizontal bone gain (6-month minus baseline) assessed by cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Secondary outcomes were postoperative edema, pain measured on a visual analog scale (VAS) from the first to the seventh postoperative days, and soft-tissue healing evaluated using the Landry index.

RESULTS: At 6 months, horizontal bone width was comparable between groups (test: 4.96 ± 0.48 mm; control: 5.03 ± 0.46 mm; p = 0.147), with a similar mean gain of approximately 0.95 mm in both groups. The alloplastic graft with i-PRF protocol resulted in significantly lower postoperative edema at days 2 and 7 (p = 0.003 for both), lower VAS pain scores throughout the first week (p < 0.001 for group effect), and higher Landry healing scores at days 2 and 7 (p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The alloplastic graft with i-PRF protocol was associated with enhanced early postoperative comfort and soft-tissue healing, while achieving 6-month horizontal bone width comparable to xenograft, and may be a clinically feasible alternative for selected augmentation procedures.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The alloplastic graft with i-PRF protocol may enhance early postoperative comfort and soft-tissue healing while providing horizontal bone width outcomes comparable to xenograft in simultaneous implant placement with guided bone regeneration.

articles.title: Metastable chromatin state defines incomplete-type intestinal metaplasia and underlies its high carcinogenic potential.
articles.journal: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Incomplete-type intestinal metaplasia (iIM) has both gastric and intestinal mucin phenotypes, often persists even after Helicobacter pylori eradication, and has a particularly high risk of gastric cancer. However, the molecular basis remains unclear.

METHODS: snRNA-seq and scATAC-seq were performed on normal human gastric tissue without HP infection, HP-infected gastric tissue without and with IM, and small intestinal mucosa. Mouse gastric mucosa with spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM), mucous neck cell-mimicking metaplasia from chief cells, was also analyzed.

RESULTS: snRNA-seq of IM cells showed a distinct cluster of iIM cells with hybrid expression of gastric and small intestinal genes. The iIM cells, but not complete-type IM (cIM cells), displayed aberrant transcriptional activation of genes silent in both tissues, such as REG4 and BBOX1. By scATAC-seq analysis using biological replicate samples, iIM cells were consistently shown to have hybrid open chromatin at both gastric (SOX2) and small intestinal (CDX2) master regulators. The iIM cells showed extensive chromatin closure and an abrupt transition to cIM, supporting the relatively stable chromatin state. The iIM cells had aberrant opening of the posterior HOXA genes, presenting a feature of embryonic reprogramming. Analysis of mouse gastric spasmolytic polypeptide-expressing metaplasia (SPEM), pyloric metaplasia of body chief cells, also showed hybrid chromatin openings of SOX2 and CDX2, and aberrant closure of many chromatin regions.

CONCLUSIONS: iIM cells exhibit a metastable chromatin state with features of embryonic reprogramming, suggesting increased stemness and a potential role in the acceleration of gastric carcinogenesis.

articles.title: Analysis of outcome predictors in traumatic brain injury patients requiring intensive care management reveals an independent role of dynamic measures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Research in traumatic brain injury (TBI) mediation and outcome have developed many methods of assessing patient state and response. While several outcome calculators for TBI have been suggested, these calculators do not include all collected variables in the management of these patients; with a paucity of studies on how these hundreds of variables contribute statistically to long-term outcome. Thus, this work endeavors to assess the statistical relationships between commonly collected variables at admission, and during the first 24 h of critical care, with overall patient outcome.

METHODS: From a retrospective dataset of 1,266 TBI patients requiring intensive care, unique patient variables (including demographic, injury pattern, pathophysiological, treatment and biochemical/imaging biomarkers) were explored. Intra-variable and variable reduction analysis were completed with importance assessed through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method. From all of this we developed predictive models to assess the 6-12-month Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) using general linear and XGBoost models.

RESULTS: Of the 321 variables assessed, a final 36 variables were found to be the important and non-redundant, that included common variables (Glasgow coma scale (GCS), age, heart rate and blood pressure at scene of accident) and individualized measures (S100B level and long pressure reactivity). Survival based on these non-redundant variables resulted in an accuracy of 88.8% 0.723 AUC (0.65-0.795) vs the IMPACT LAB 80.9% 0.608 AUC (0.54-0.677). Notable combining the IMPACT LAB model with the non-redundant variables found an accuracy of 90.3% 0.765 AUC (0.693-0.838) and an improvement of the Nagelkerke R2 value from 0.317 to 0.499.

CONCLUSION: These results found that overall general linear and XGBoost models behave similarly with an increase in non-IMPACT LAB variables performing better in XGBoost models. Broad categories of patient states like survival and favorable outcome can be determined by basic patient variables, however more dynamic measures of individualized response improve the predictive capacity for patient outcomes. Thus, to better understand patient state and more effectively monitor patient outcomes, dynamic and individualized patient physiology needs further evaluation.

articles.title: Bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants: a prospective ultrasound study of intestinal structural development.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: The preterm intestine undergoes rapid structural and functional maturation during late gestation and early postnatal life. Although abdominal ultrasound is increasingly used in neonatal care, quantitative descriptions of developmental variation in bowel wall structure and motility remain limited. In this prospective observational study, preterm infants born at ≤ 34 weeks' gestation underwent serial abdominal ultrasound examinations in a level III neonatal intensive care unit. A total of 260 longitudinal ultrasound scans were performed from early postnatal life through term-equivalent age. Bowel wall thickness (BWT) was measured in four abdominal quadrants using a standardized high-frequency ultrasound protocol. Small-bowel loops were identified using established sonographic criteria. Peristaltic activity was graded semi-quantitatively (0 = absent, 1 = intermittent, 2 = active) during standardized cine observation. Associations between postmenstrual age and ultrasound measures were evaluated using regression and correlation analyses accounting for repeated measurements within infants. Fourteen preterm infants contributed serial examinations spanning 26 to 37 weeks' postmenstrual age. BWT demonstrated a progressive increase with advancing maturity and consistent regional variability across abdominal quadrants. Peristaltic activity similarly increased with postmenstrual age, with a transition from absent or intermittent motility in earlier scans to active peristalsis at later ages. Structural and functional findings showed parallel maturational trends.

CONCLUSION: Bedside ultrasound enables quantitative assessment of intestinal structure and motility during preterm development. These findings provide longitudinal developmental imaging data describing intestinal maturation and support future studies examining intestinal adaptation and clinical outcomes in preterm infants.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Real-time assessment of neonatal bowel health remains a major clinical challenge with important knowledge gaps. Reliance on nonspecific clinical signs, delayed laboratory changes, and adjunctive abdominal radiographs often leads to late recognition of bowel injury, reducing opportunities for timely and targeted intervention. Abdominal ultrasound is emerging as a valuable tool for early detection of gut injury and for real-time monitoring, offering neonatologists a way to guide bedside decision-making more precisely..

WHAT IS NEW: • Provides prospective ultrasound characterization of bowel wall thickness across postmenstrual age in preterm infants. • Demonstrates maturational and regional variation in intestinal wall structure during early life. • Establishes foundational developmental imaging data to support future longitudinal and outcome-based studies.

articles.title: Who addresses work engagement in the head and neck cancer journey? A cross-sectional survey of cancer patients.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Head and neck cancer (HNC) incidence is rising, with increasing numbers of working-age patients. Return to work (RTW) is an important part of recovery, yet patients with HNC have lower RTW rates than other cancer types. This study asks who is addressing work engagement in the HNC journey?

METHODS: A cross-sectional ad hoc online questionnaire (34 items; closed and open-ended) was distributed via HNC support groups, clinical teams, and charities (November 2020-March 2022). Analyses were conducted on patients with HNC working at the time of diagnosis. Outcomes were time to RTW post-treatment and type of RTW. Descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and chi-square tests were conducted; free-text data were analysed using content analysis.

RESULTS: For 29.6% of participants, no RTW discussions took place with either a healthcare professional (HCP) or their employer. Approximately half reported no HCP discussion (49.3%) and half reported no employer/occupational entity discussion (49.3%). Time to RTW was shorter when discussed with HCPs (p = .029) or employers (p < .001). Employer discussions were associated with type of RTW (p = .007). Single participants took longer to RTW (p = 0.008) and marital status and age were both associated with the type of work returned to (p = 0.009 and p = 0.004). Key self-reported work-related difficulties included speech/communication (50%) and fatigue (22%).

CONCLUSIONS: Work engagement/RTW is inconsistently addressed across the HNC journey, with substantial gaps in both clinical and workplace discussions. Findings indicate RTW discussions are associated with RTW outcomes and there is an unmet need for structured, timely, and coordinated RTW support spanning treatment through recovery.

articles.title: Goal Management Training for Adolescents with ADHD: A Multi-Center Randomized Controlled Effectiveness Trial.
articles.journal: Research on child and adolescent psychopathology
articles.abstract: Non-pharmacological interventions targeting executive functions (EF), such as Goal Management Training (GMT), may augment treatment as usual (TAU) for adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We examined whether GMT plus TAU improves EF, ADHD symptoms, and functional impairment more than TAU only. In this preregistered multi-center randomized controlled trial, 116 participants (Mage = 14.69 years; 66% female) were randomized to GMT plus TAU or TAU only. GMT comprised seven weekly 2-hour group sessions, supplemented by parent and teacher sessions. TAU was standard outpatient mental health services. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the parent-reported Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function (BRIEF-2), Global Executive Composite (GEC). Secondary outcomes were teacher-, self-, and parent-reported BRIEF-2 subdomains; parent- and teacher-reported ADHD Rating Scale-IV scores; and parent-reported functional impairment measured with the Weiss Functional Impairment Rating Scale-Parent Report (WFIRS-P). GMT plus TAU showed no additional benefit over TAU only. Intention-to-treat analyses showed no significant between-group difference in GEC (adjusted b = - 2.12, 95% CI [- 7.64, 3.41], p = .449, d = - 0.14), parent-reported ADHD symptoms (d = - 0.27, p = .323) or other secondary outcomes (all p > .10). Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05874791; registered April 14, 2023).

articles.title: Epigenetic activation of BCL11B is associated with profibrotic cardiac remodeling induced by colitis-associated gut dysbiosis.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but the mechanisms linking gut dysbiosis to cardiac pathology remain poorly defined. We investigated whether transplantation of a dysbiotic microbiome (DM) from colitic mice alters cardiac function and explored the underlying mechanisms. Germ-free mice were colonized with normal microbiomes from wild-type donors or DMs from Il10-/- mice. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography, and gut microbiota and cardiac transcriptomes were analyzed by 16 S rRNA- and bulk RNA-sequencing, respectively. Chronic colitis was induced by repeated dextran sodium sulfate (DSS) administration, with or without fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy controls. Epigenetic mechanisms were investigated using chromatin immunoprecipitation and methylation-specific qPCR. DM transplantation impaired cardiac contractility and increased collagen deposition. Cardiac RNA-seq revealed extensive transcriptional remodeling, particularly in females, with enrichment in histone acetylation and immune signaling pathways. Nat8f7 and Tet1 were upregulated, accompanied by increased histone acetylation and reduced DNA methylation at the Bcl11b promoter, enhancing RNA polymerase II recruitment and Bcl11b transcription. NAT8F7 and TET1 additively increased Bcl11b transcription and P1NP production in C2C12 cells. Similar molecular changes occurred during DSS-induced colitis and were reversed by healthy FMT. BCL11B overexpression promoted myoblast proliferation and collagen production. In conclusion, DM promotes cardiac fibrosis through epigenetic activation of Bcl11b, revealing a novel gut-heart axis. Healthy FMT mitigates these effects, highlighting microbiome-targeted strategies for IBD-associated cardiovascular complications.

articles.title: Clinical research progress in the application of laser therapy for ankyloglossia.
articles.abstract: Ankyloglossia restricts breastfeeding, speech articulation and maxillofacial skeletal development. Although laser-assisted surgical correction for ankyloglossia has replaced conventional scalpel-based frenotomy as the first-line intervention, inconsistent operation parameters, unpredictable thermal tissue injury and high postoperative re-adhesion rates hinder standardized clinical popularization. This narrative review systematically integrates current clinical evidence of multiple laser modalities and establishes standardized stratified diagnosis-treatment and multi-dimensional evaluation frameworks for laser-assisted ankyloglossia correction. This narrative review was conducted, referring to key reporting items of extended PRISMA-N for narrative reviews to improve report transparency, rather than complying with full systematic-review PRISMA procedural standards. Clinical studies published from January 2021 to June 2026 were retrieved from six authoritative databases (SCIE, ESCI, Scopus, PubMed, PMC, DOAJ), covering five mainstream dental laser systems. Independent literature screening, data extraction and bias evaluation were completed to synthesize cross-age clinical evidence of different laser therapies. Lasers yield minimally invasive advantages through photothermal, photochemical, and photobiomodulation (PBM) mechanisms, with minimal intraoperative tissue trauma, reliable haemostasis, and attenuated postoperative inflammation. Distinct laser wavelengths present unique tissue absorption characteristics and targeted clinical indications. This study innovatively constructs a three-dimensional stratified treatment model, multi-faceted multi-dimensional efficacy evaluation system and individualized dynamic laser parameter regulation protocols to resolve current clinical inconsistencies in surgical practice. Laser-assisted surgical correction for ankyloglossia represents a safe and promising minimally-invasive intervention. Individualized laser selection and dynamic parameter optimization may improve surgical precision and long-term clinical outcomes. The proposed theoretical frameworks await prospective clinical validation before achieving real-world standardization. Establishing unified clinical operation specifications and improving accessibility of high-precision laser devices will be required to support future potential standardized, large-scale clinical application of laser therapy for ankyloglossia. This work provides theoretically-derived stratified laser treatment protocols suitable for primary and tertiary dental institutions. Such protocols have the theoretical potential to reduce thermal injury and postoperative re-adhesion risks, though prospective clinical verification is still required. It addresses the absence of unified postoperative rehabilitation criteria and proposes low-cost laser equipment and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted parameter matching as promising future directions to realize precise, accessible minimally invasive management for patients of all age groups.

articles.title: Protective role of hydroxytyrosol and oleuropein on duodenal tissue in experimental diabetes: evaluation of ISM-1, PODXL, AKT, and mTOR expression.
articles.abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the pathological changes occurring in the duodenal tissue of rats with streptozotocin (STZ)-induced experimental diabetes and to evaluate the potential protective effects of hydroxytyrosol (HT) and oleuropein (OLE). In addition, the effects of these compounds on isthmin-1 (ISM-1) and podocalyxin (PODXL) expression, as well as p-AKT and p-mTOR expression, were examined to assess their potential involvement in diabetes-associated cellular and molecular alterations. In this study, 42 rats were divided into 6 groups (control, HT, OLE, DM, DM + HT, DM + OLE), each consisting of 7 animals. Experimental diabetes was induced by a single dose of streptozotocin (50 mg/kg, i.p.). HT (100 mg/kg/day) and OLE (20 mg/kg/day) were administered orally for 6 weeks. Body weight and blood glucose levels were monitored throughout the experiment. At the end of the study, duodenal tissues were collected and ISM-1, PODXL, p-AKT, and p-mTOR expression levels were evaluated using immunohistochemical methods. Diabetes was found to suppress body weight gain and cause a significant increase in blood glucose levels. In addition, PODXL and ISM-1 expression levels were significantly increased in the diabetic group, whereas p-AKT and p-mTOR expression levels were significantly decreased. HT and OLE treatments significantly reduced blood glucose levels and decreased both PODXL and ISM-1 expression, while partially restoring p-AKT and p-mTOR expression.HT and OLE similarly reduced ISM-1 and PODXL expression compared with the DM group. HT treatment, on the other hand, showed a more pronounced beneficial effect on body weight and blood glucose levels. HT and OLE demonstrated protective effects in the STZ-induced diabetes model by reducing hyperglycemia and modulating diabetes-associated molecular alterations in the duodenal tissue, potentially through the AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. HT and OLE produced comparable reductions in final blood glucose levels, with no significant difference between the two treatment groups, whereas both HT and OLE similarly reduced ISM-1 and PODXL expression compared with the DM group. However, neither treatment completely restored the evaluated parameters to control levels, indicating partial protective effects against diabetes-associated intestinal alterations. These findings suggest that ISM-1 and PODXL may represent potential molecular markers of diabetes-associated duodenal alterations and treatment response.

articles.title: Caffeic acid phenethyl ester and markers of IRE-1α/TRAF2/NF-κB-related endoplasmic reticulum stress, inflammation, apoptosis and autophagy in methotrexate-induced nephrotoxicity in rats.
articles.abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) is widely used in oncology and rheumatology, and nephrotoxicity is among its recognised adverse effects. Caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE), an active component of propolis, has antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. We examined whether markers of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress related to the IRE-1α/TRAF2/NF-κB axis accompany MTX-induced renal injury in rats, and whether CAPE co-treatment modifies them. Twenty-four female Wistar albino rats were allocated to four groups (n = 6): Control, MTX (20 mg/kg i.p. on day 1), MTX+CAPE (MTX followed by CAPE 10 µmol/kg per day for 5 days) and CAPE, with vehicle exposure matched across groups. On day 7, serum urea, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and creatinine were measured; right kidneys were processed for haematoxylin-eosin damage scoring and for IRE-1α, TRAF2, NF-κB, caspase-3 and beclin-1 immunohistochemistry, and left kidneys for qRT-PCR of the same targets. MTX was associated with body weight loss, higher serum urea, BUN and creatinine, higher cortical and medullary damage scores, higher immunoreactivity of all five markers, and higher IRE-1α and TRAF2 transcript levels. In the MTX+CAPE group, weight loss was attenuated and damage scores were lower than in the MTX group for cortical vascular congestion and medullary apoptotic bodies/necrosis. At the protein level, a significant reduction relative to MTX was detected only for medullary IRE-1α, and no gene differed significantly. Under this single-dose, 7-day protocol, the apparent benefit of CAPE was limited, and because pathway activity was not measured directly, the molecular findings indicate associations rather than a mechanism.

articles.title: Acellular dermal matrix for soft tissue augmentation in scalp wound reconstructions: a retrospective surgical case series of neuro-oncology patients with previous craniotomy and/or radiation.
articles.abstract: Scalp reconstruction in neuro-oncology patients undergoing repeat craniotomy is complicated by cumulative tissue injury, resulting in high-tension closures and increased risk of wound complications. While acellular dermal matrices (ADM) have been used in reconstructive surgery, their role in this population remains incompletely characterized. We report our experience using ADM to facilitate galea tension relief and soft tissue augmentation in this setting. We performed a retrospective review of 23 neuro-oncology cases (2017-2022) in which ADM was used during scalp closure following cranial surgery. Patient demographics, treatment history, operative characteristics, and postoperative outcomes were collected. Primary outcomes included treated and/or eroded scalp, exposed cranioplasty and/or hardware, surgical site infection, and reoperation for any of the aforementioned complications. Patients had a mean age of 57.8 years, with nearly all patients having prior cranial surgery and radiotherapy. Multiple prior surgeries were present in 34.8%, and 13.0% had prior infection. ADM was used to facilitate tension-free closure in all patients, covering a mean area of 83.0 ± 30.0 cm². Mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 19.4 months. One patient (4.3%) developed a wound complication requiring reoperation for hardware exposure. All other ADM-assisted closures remained intact, including in patients undergoing subsequent surgery or radiotherapy. ADM-assisted closure appears to be a safe and effective adjunct for managing high-tension scalp wounds in neuro-oncology patients with compromised soft tissue. Its use may mitigate wound morbidity and broaden reconstructive options in previously treated fields.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and diagnostic challenges of Kawasaki disease in infants younger than 3 months: a 21-year single-center retrospective study from China.
articles.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) in infants younger than 3 months is uncommon but poses substantial diagnostic challenges because classical clinical manifestations are frequently incomplete during the early phase of illness. Delayed diagnosis increases the risk of coronary artery abnormalities (CAA), yet the clinical characteristics and diagnostic evolution of this age group remain insufficiently understood. We retrospectively reviewed all infants younger than 3 months diagnosed with KD at Peking University First Hospital between January 2005 and January 2026. Clinical characteristics, laboratory findings, echocardiographic features, treatment, and follow-up outcomes were analyzed. Particular attention was paid to the temporal evolution of clinical manifestations and coronary artery abnormalities during the diagnostic process. Fifteen infants were included in the study. Incomplete KD accounted for 86.7% (13/15) of cases. Gastrointestinal manifestations (53.3%), bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) scar reactivation (60.0%), and respiratory symptoms (40.0%) were common and frequently resulted in an initial diagnosis of infection. Coronary artery abnormalities developed in ten patients during the disease course. Three infants had normal initial echocardiographic examinations but subsequently developed coronary artery abnormalities on repeat evaluation between fever days 7 and 10. Fourteen patients responded to initial intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) treatment, whereas one patient was IVIG-resistant. Coronary artery abnormalities and other cardiac echocardiographic involvement resolved in all patients during follow-up.Conclusion: KD in infants younger than 3 months is characterized by an evolving clinical presentation in which classical clinical manifestations and echocardiographically detectable coronary artery abnormalities emerge sequentially rather than simultaneously. Recognition of this evolving diagnostic process may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Persistent clinical suspicion, together with longitudinal clinical reassessment and appropriately timed repeat echocardiography, may improve recognition before clinically significant coronary injury develops.

articles.title: Latent tuberculosis infection conversion and TST-IGRA agreement in BCG-vaccinated children with rheumatic diseases receiving biologic therapy: a 10-year single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: To assess agreement between the tuberculin skin test (TST) and QuantiFERON-TB Gold In-Tube (QFT-GIT) assay and describe latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening conversion during biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs). This 10-year retrospective cohort included children receiving bDMARDs. Baseline screening comprised TST and/or QFT-GIT and chest radiography, with follow-up testing as available. TST positivity was defined as ≥ 5-mm. Agreement and paired TST positivity were assessed using Cohen's kappa, and McNemar's test, respectively. Among 106 patients (49.1% female), median age at bDMARD initiation was 11.6 years. New LTBI screening positivity occurred in 14/87 (16.1%) with no positive baseline result. Overall, 31 (29.2%) received isoniazid, 19 before bDMARD and 12 during follow-up. TST-QFT-GIT agreement was moderate at baseline (n = 90; κ = 0.472) and fair at follow-up (n = 76; κ = 0.213). Paired TST positivity increased from 8.8% to 20.0% (n = 80; p = 0.012). New QFT-GIT positivity occurred in 6/74 patients (8.1%) with negative or indeterminate baseline results. Of 14 conversions, two were detected by both tests, eight by TST only, and four by QFT-GIT only. Conversion occurred with both tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors and non-TNF biologics, without significant between-group differences. No active tuberculosis developed during available follow-up.

CONCLUSION: New LTBI screening positivity occurred after initiation of both biologic classes in BCG-vaccinated children. Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at first follow-up. The clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain and requires interpretation in the context of BCG vaccination, prior tuberculin testing and TB exposure risk.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Children receiving biologic therapy require LTBI screening because of risk of active tuberculosis. • BCG vaccination, immunosuppression, and the absence of gold standard complicate interpretation of TST and IGRA results.

WHAT IS NEW: • Agreement between TST and QFT-GIT was moderate at baseline and fair at follow-up, the clinical significance of isolated TST conversion remains uncertain. • New LTBI screening positivity was documented during follow-up, after initiation of both anti-TNF and non-anti-TNF biologic agents.

articles.title: Image quality and procedural safety in neonatal brain MRI with and without sedation.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neontal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is susceptible to motion artefacts, whereas pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia may cause cardiorespiratory adverse events. We compared image quality and adverse events across three MRI strategies in newborns: natural sleep without sedation, pharmacological sedation, and imaging during mechanical ventilation. We retrospectively analysed 151 brain MRI examinations performed in a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit between August 2013 and August 2024. Examinations were classified as non-sedated using a feed-and-swaddle approach (n = 21), pharmacologically sedated without intubation (n = 67), or performed in intubated and mechanically ventilated infants (n = 63). Motion artefacts and documented adverse events were compared between groups. Motion artefacts were more frequent in non-sedated examinations than in sedated or intubated examinations (85.7% vs. 32.8% and 25.4%, respectively; p < 0.001). Moderate/severe artefacts occurred in 14.3%, 7.5%, and 0%, respectively. No adverse events were documented in the non-sedated group, compared with 8/67 (11.9%) in sedated and 7/63 (11.1%) in intubated infants; this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.275). Within the sedated cohort, artefacts were more frequent with chloral hydrate, whereas respiratory complications occurred predominantly with propofol-based sedation.

CONCLUSION: Neonatal MRI strategies involve a clinically relevant trade-off between image quality and procedural safety. Natural-sleep MRI avoids pharmacological exposure and was not associated with documented adverse events but resulted in more motion artefacts. MRI strategies should therefore be individualized according to clinical condition and required diagnostic image quality.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Motion artefacts may compromise neonatal MRI, and pharmacological sedation or anaesthesia is frequently used to improve image quality. • Feed-and-swaddle MRI can avoid drug exposure, while sedative and anaesthetic agents may cause respiratory and haemodynamic adverse events.

WHAT IS NEW: • Direct comparison of three real-world neonatal MRI strategies demonstrates a trade-off between image quality and procedural safety: sedation and controlled ventilation reduced motion artefacts, whereas no adverse events were documented during natural-sleep MRI. • Exploratory analyses suggest differences between sedation regimens, with more artefacts after chloral hydrate and respiratory events occurring predominantly with propofol-based sedation.

articles.title: Correspondence: Reply to "Heterogeneity in dosages and treatment conditions forms a blurred picture of the results".
articles.abstract: Jumani et al. raised concerns about our systematic review and meta-analysis of zilebesiran in adults with hypertension, concerning dose heterogeneity, differences in trial conditions, and statistical methods. In this reply, we clarify that the primary analysis was pre-specified to include one comparison per trial, using the 300 or 400 mg dose at 6 months. The pooled blood pressure estimates therefore did not combine different doses. We agree that the dose subgroup analyses were underpowered and exploratory, and we did not conclude that doses are equivalent. We also acknowledge that trial populations, background antihypertensive therapy, and follow-up differed, and that the "mild to moderate" label should be interpreted cautiously. With only two trials per efficacy outcome, between-study variance cannot be estimated reliably and prediction intervals cannot be calculated. The pooled estimates should therefore be regarded as preliminary. These points support our call for larger, long-term trials with active comparators.

articles.title: Pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To review visual, anatomical, microbiological, and management-related outcomes in pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through June 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261422377). We included cohort studies, case-control studies, and case series (five or more patients) of patients aged 18 years or younger with endophthalmitis after open-globe injury. We excluded postoperative or endogenous endophthalmitis and cohorts without separable pediatric post-traumatic data. Proportions were pooled using a random-effects model with Freeman-Tukey transformation. Risk of bias was assessed with JBI, Newcastle-Ottawa, or QUADAS-2 tools.

RESULTS: Fifty-seven studies (4,558 eyes) were included, 29 in quantitative synthesis. Pooled random-effects estimates are shown with crude event counts. Favorable final visual acuity (≥ 20/200) was achieved in 28% (95% CI 16-42%; 317/787 eyes) and no light perception in 27% (13-44%; 160/466). Globe retention was 98% (96-100%; 870/920), evisceration or enucleation 2% (0-4%; 50/920), and phthisis bulbi 14% (4-26%; 74/498). Culture positivity was 39% (27-52%; 442/976), with Gram-positive organisms predominating among 880 isolates. Pars plana vitrectomy, intravitreal therapy, and systemic antibiotics were used in 90% (883/1,085), 97% (775/907), and 81% (781/915) of eyes, respectively. Delay to presentation and to primary repair were the most consistent predictors of endophthalmitis and poor outcome.

CONCLUSION: Pediatric post-traumatic endophthalmitis is associated with poor visual outcomes despite aggressive multimodal treatment, although globe preservation is achievable in most eyes. Early recognition, prompt antimicrobial therapy, and timely surgical intervention appear critical to optimizing outcomes, emphasizing the need for rapid referral and standardized management.

articles.title: Implementation of quality indicators for ovarian cancer in gynecological cancer centers certified by the German Cancer Society (DKG).
articles.journal: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Since 2008, the German Cancer Society (DKG) has certified gynecological cancer centers to ensure high-quality care with guideline-based quality indicators (QI) as a core component. This article summarizes the German development and update of ovarian cancer (OC) QI based on the current S3-guideline (2026) and presents their performance.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, descriptive, observational analysis of aggregated annual-report data for treatment years 2019-2024; no inferential statistics were performed. QI were derived from strong S3-guideline recommendations through a structured multi-step process. Experts identified potential QI according to standardized criteria (including feasibility and impact on care). QI required ≥ 75% agreement. Since 2017, each tumor entity has been limited to five key QI in the certification dataset.

RESULTS: Eight guideline-derived QI are currently defined for OC, five QI are included in the certification program. In 2024, 184 certified centers treated 4.951 primary OC cases. At center level, the predefined target values were met for surgical staging (93.5% of centers; target ≥ 40%), offering genetic testing (97.8%; target ≥ 70%), complete macroscopic resection (99.5%; target ≥ 30%), and surgery by a gynecologic oncologist (98.9%; target ≥ 80%). All centers (100%) met plausibility limits for first-line chemotherapy (75.1% of advanced-stage patients). At patient level, pooled adherence rates improved over time; the median rate of offering genetic testing rose from 61% (2019) to 84% (2024). Two QI were retired in 2021, and one QI is pending until further guideline updates.

CONCLUSION: Guideline-based QI translate essential recommendations into measurable metrics, allowing objective assessment of quality. High and increasing adherence rates were observed in certified centers. These findings support the use of guideline-based QI for benchmarking and continuous quality improvement, although the observational design precludes causal attribution to certification.

articles.title: Structured management of postoperative bile leakage after major liver resection with bilioenteric reconstruction: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative bile leakage following major liver resection with bilioenteric reconstruction may lead to abdominal sepsis and contribute to post-hepatectomy liver failure, the leading cause of postoperative mortality. No standardized management strategy currently exists. This study evaluated outcomes of a structured, predominantly minimally invasive management approach.

METHODS: All patients undergoing major liver resection with extrahepatic bile duct resection and bilioenteric reconstruction for proven or suspected malignancy between 2018 and 2025 were included. Bile leakage was defined according to International Study Group of Liver Surgery criteria. The management strategy prioritized early detection, percutaneous peritoneal drainage, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and delayed biliary intervention.

RESULTS: Among 100 patients, clinically relevant bile leakage occurred in 23 (23.0%). Leakage resolved with drainage alone in eight patients after a median of 12 days. Additional percutaneous drainage or biliary stenting resulted in resolution in most remaining cases. Two patients were reoperated for bile leakage. The median time to bile leak resolution was 22 days. No statistically significant differences in postoperative mortality or post-hepatectomy liver failure were observed between patients with and without bile leakage.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective cohort, a conservative management strategy emphasizing early drainage and delayed biliary intervention was feasible and resulted in resolution of bile leakage without reoperation in most patients following major liver resection with bilioenteric reconstruction. These findings support the potential role of this approach, although larger studies are needed to further evaluate its safety and effectiveness.

articles.title: Stone density measurement on NCCT: 2D ROI versus semi-automated 3D methods for predicting shock wave lithotripsy success.
articles.abstract: Stone density on non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) predicts the outcome of shock wave lithotripsy (SWL), but its measurement technique is not standardised. We compared a conventional two-dimensional (2D) region-of-interest (ROI) measurement with semi-automated three-dimensional (3D) measurements obtained with Horos and 3D Slicer for agreement and prediction of SWL success. In this prospective single-centre study, 238 patients with radiopaque stones ≤ 20 mm underwent NCCT before SWL. Mean and maximum Hounsfield units (HU), the standard deviation (SD) of HU and the variation coefficient of stone density (VCSD) were measured with each method. Agreement was assessed with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, and predictive performance with receiver operating characteristic analysis and exploratory multivariable logistic regression. SWL was successful in 114 patients (47.9%). 2D ROI mean HU was approximately 320 HU higher than with both 3D methods (ICC 0.19-0.25), whereas Horos and 3D Slicer agreed well for mean HU (ICC 0.82) and closely for stone volume (ICC 0.96). The area under the curve of mean HU was 0.839 for Horos and 0.843 for 3D Slicer, both higher than 0.744 for the 2D ROI (p < 0.001). Youden cut-offs were 875, 539 and 514 HU for the 2D ROI, Horos and 3D Slicer, respectively, and mean HU at or below the method-specific cut-off independently predicted success (adjusted odds ratios 5.64, 12.67 and 14.36). Stone density is strongly method-dependent. In this cohort, 3D mean HU predicts SWL success better than 2D measurement; the method-specific thresholds require external validation and should not be transferred between techniques.

articles.title: Heat shock-responsive genes in Brassica napus: from omics-driven discovery to gene editing.
articles.abstract: Heat shock-responsive genes in Brassica napus provide candidate targets for thermotolerance, with genomic clustering, co-expression hubs, polyploid expansion, and epigenetic regulation guiding functional validation and gene-editing-assisted breeding of heat-resilient canola. Heat stress is a major constraint to the productivity and stability of Brassica napus, particularly in the current climate change era. Heat shock-responsive genes (HSRGs), including heat shock transcription factors and heat shock proteins, are candidate regulators of thermotolerance. Integrating multi-omics evidence, we compiled 242 putative HSRGs candidates and identified 27 genomic clusters, suggesting synergistical regulation by gene duplication and evolutionary expansion. Co-expression network analysis across independent RNA-seq datasets revealed six modules and 50 hub genes, with 17 hub genes co-localizing with genomic clusters. Comparative orthology across 32 Brassicaceae species suggests substantial HSRG expansion in polyploids with B. napus exhibiting pronounced expansion ratios and identifies Brassica-specific orthogroups. Pangenomic evidence further indicates that structural variation is associated with heat-adaptive allelic diversity. Epigenetic regulation adds further complexity with HSRGs interacting with chromatin modifications and transcriptional memory to fine-tune stress responses. This integrative framework, connecting gene discovery, network architecture, evolutionary genomics, and breeding application positions HSRGs as candidate targets for developing heat-resilient canola to sustain productivity under future extreme climate challenges.

articles.title: Thirteen-month real-world effectiveness and safety of lecanemab in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease: integrating objective clinical outcomes and caregiver-reported experiences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The longer-term real-world effectiveness of lecanemab and predictors of treatment response remain unclear in Chinese patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD).

METHODS: This prospective multicenter cohort enrolled patients receiving lecanemab (10 mg/kg biweekly) across nine medical centers in Southwest China. Longitudinal cognition, 13-month amyloid-β positron emission tomography/computed tomography (Aβ-PET/CT), safety, treatment discontinuation, and caregiver-reported Clinical Global Impression (CGI) outcomes were assessed. Cognitive trajectories were compared with propensity score-matched local controls and an external Alzheimer's disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) natural-history cohort.

RESULTS: Among 122 lecanemab-treated patients, 38.52% had mild cognitive impairment due to AD and 40.98% had mild AD dementia. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating 222 follow-up visits demonstrated generally stable cognitive performance, with modest favorable changes in cognitive scores at certain follow-up time points. At 13 months, 84.00% maintained or improved Clinical Dementia Rating stage, and 66.67% achieved amyloid-negative conversion, defined as a Centiloid value < 12. Lecanemab-treated patients showed more favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories than matched ADNI and local natural-history controls. Amyloid reduction was not robustly associated with cognitive improvement, and routine baseline clinical variables did not reliably predict treatment response. CGI assessments indicated clinical improvement or stability in 77.55% of participants. Amyloid-related imaging abnormalities and infusion-related reactions occurred in 10.66% and 5.74% of patients, respectively, while treatment discontinuation was most commonly driven by the inconvenience of repeated infusions rather than safety concerns.

CONCLUSION: Lecanemab was associated with favorable longitudinal cognitive trajectories, substantial amyloid clearance, and acceptable safety in Chinese patients with AD. However, amyloid reduction and routine baseline clinical characteristics did not reliably predict treatment response.

articles.title: Complications Within 30 Days After Minimally Invasive Sacrocolpopexy by Robotic Versus Laparoscopic Approach: A National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) Database Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Robotic MISCP is increasingly used for improved ergonomics and visualization but comparative evidence to standard laparoscopy is limited. This study compares 30-day surgical complications after minimally invasive sacrocolpopexy (MISCP) performed laparoscopically versus robotically.

METHODS: Patients undergoing MISCP by laparoscopic and robotic approach (2022- 2024) were identified in the ACS National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database. The primary outcome was a composite of surgical site infection, blood transfusion, return to the operating room, or readmission within 30 days or surgical length of stay > 7 days. Multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for age, race, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, ASA class, concurrent incontinence procedure, concurrent adnexectomy, and concurrent hysterectomy.

RESULTS: Of the 9824 patients who met the inclusion criteria, 7296 (74.3%) underwent a robotic approach. Patients having a robotic MISCP were older, higher BMI, higher ASA class, and more often non-Hispanic white (all P < 0.001). The composite surgical complication outcome occurred in 4.5% of patients overall and occurred for fewer patients having robotic approach (4.3% vs 5.3%, P = 0.04). Surgical site infection was lower for the robotic approach (2.2% vs 3.0%, P = 0.01). There was no difference in conversion to abdominal or vaginal approaches, urinary tract injury and no difference in Clavien-Dindo 4 complications. On multivariable analysis, robotic MISCP was associated with lower odds of the composite outcome (aOR 0.72, P = 0.008) and surgical site infection (aOR 0.66, P = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Robotic MISCP may be associated with slightly fewer 30-day complications than laparoscopic MISCP although overall complication rates are low.

articles.title: Integrated radiomics-deep learning modeling of hepatic vasculature for enhanced noninvasive prediction of portal hypertension and high-risk gastroesophageal varices.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether CT-derived radiomics and deep learning features can improve non-invasive risk stratification of clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) and high-risk gastroesophageal varices (HRVs) in cirrhotic patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 454 cirrhotic patients from center A and 77 from center B. CSPH labels were available only for patients from center A. Patients in both centers with available endoscopic findings were classified as HRVs or non-HRVs. A dual-path modeling framework integrating radiomics and deep learning-derived features extracted from multiple major hepatic vessels was developed, and was compared with single-path (radiomics-only and deep learning-only), single-vessel, vascular geometric, and clinical-feature-based models. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).

RESULTS: For CSPH prediction, the dual-path model achieved the highest AUC (0.892 vs. 0.678-0.870 for the other models; P < 0.05 for most comparisons). For HRVs prediction, the proposed model achieved AUCs of 0.790 and 0.782 in the internal and external test set, respectively. The proposed model consistently outperformed the single-path models (0.625-0.648; all P < 0.05), single-vessel models (0.526-0.642; all P < 0.05), the vascular geometric model (0.528; P < 0.01), and the clinical-feature-based models (0.327-0.728; P < 0.001 for the APRI-based model) in the external test set.

CONCLUSION: A dual-path model integrating multi-vessel radiomics and deep learning features demonstrates robust predictive performance for CSPH and HRVs in cirrhotic patients. This approach may provide a new non-invasive alternative for risk stratification and clinical management of portal hypertension-related complications.

articles.title: The path towards precision transfusion medicine in critical care: focus on patient physiology, not only on study populations.
Patients with Congenital Heart Disease have Inferior Intent-to-Treat Outcomes When Listed for Pediatric Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: While the impact of patient characteristics on waitlist and post-transplant mortality in pediatric heart transplantation has been widely studied, these metrics are limited in their ability to provide a complete picture for patients and their families. In contrast, less prevalent in the literature is an intent-to-treat analysis approach, which provides a single data point that encompasses both of these measures. This retrospective study examines pediatric patients listed for heart transplantation in the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database between 2016 and 2025, evaluating the impact of transplant indication on intent-to-treat outcomes following the implementation of the 2016 allocation policy, which prioritizes children with congenital heart disease (CHD) on inotropic support. Kaplan-Meier analysis by transplant indication was performed across all pediatric patients listed during the study period, followed by Cox regression analyses using clinical and demographic covariates. In this initial analysis, CHD patients had poorer intent-to-treat outcomes. Risk and protective factors in this particularly high-risk population were then identified using univariable Cox regression. Significant factors (p < 0.05) were entered into a multivariable Cox regression, which was used to generate a predictive score for one-year intent-to-treat mortality (c-statistic = 0.74). Risk factors significant in the multivariable analysis were age 0-1 years, geographic region, public (rather than private) insurance, need for life support and/or hemodialysis, and low serum albumin level. Following external validation and study of transplant timing on outcomes, these findings may serve as an additional tool to identify and prioritize high-risk patients and target modifiable risk factors.

articles.title: Impact of Implant Surface Texture on Complication Rates in Primary Breast Augmentation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast augmentation remains a leading esthetic procedure, with an ongoing debate regarding smooth versus textured implant surfaces. While texturing enhances stability and reduces capsular contracture, it is associated with an increased risk of BIA-ALCL. Conversely, smooth devices introduce other risks such as increased mobility and bottoming-out deformities. Adding further complexity, systemic symptoms described as breast implant illness (BII) have been reported across all implant types, and their relationship to specific surface topographies unclear. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the safety and performance of different surfaces.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus following PRISMA guidelines. Data extraction included patient demographics, surgical techniques, and outcomes such as capsular contracture, hematoma, infection, bottoming-out deformity, seroma, reoperation, and BIA-ALCL. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models to calculate risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Twelve studies involving 17726 patients were included. Textured implants showed a significantly lower risk of bottoming out (RR = 0.10; 95% CI, 0.03-0.33; p < .001). No significant differences were observed for capsular contracture, infection, seroma, or reoperation rates. Subpectoral/retropectoral placement significantly reduced infection rates compared to prepectoral placement (p < .001). The pooled reoperation rate for clinical complications was significantly higher than reoperations performed at the patient's request (p = .015). No BIA-ALCL cases were detected within the study period.

CONCLUSIONS: Implant selection must transcend market trends, prioritizing a personalized approach. While textured surfaces may offer mechanical advantages, particularly in anatomical devices, their indication should be balanced against regulatory considerations, local availability, and patient preference. For round implants, careful risk-benefit consideration is also recommended. Success depends on aligning surface technology with precise surgical planes and requiring strict asepsis. Further long-term studies are needed to better understand surface-immune system interactions.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE III: This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

articles.title: Abbreviated brain magnetic resonance imaging protocol using fluid-attenuated inversion recovery and diffusion-weighted imaging in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rapid brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) protocols may reduce radiation exposure and sedation requirements in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and clinical adequacy of an abbreviated brain MRI (abMRI) protocol featuring fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in pediatric emergency neuroimaging.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included pediatric emergency department patients who underwent abMRI between July 2023 and July 2025. The protocol consisted of axial diffusion-weighted imaging and axial fluid-attenuated inversion recovery obtained with motion-resistant radial filling, with an acquisition time of approximately 220 s. Technical success and clinical adequacy were evaluated using image quality, emergency observation, pediatric neurology follow-up, and full-protocol MRI when clinically indicated.

RESULTS: Among 971 attempted examinations, diagnostic-quality images were obtained in 951, yielding a technical success rate of 97.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] 96.8-98.7%). The mean age was 7.61±5.46 years, and 480 patients (50.5%) were boys. Of the 951 diagnostic examinations, 649 underwent no further neuroimaging. Full-protocol MRI was performed in 302 patients. Eight false-negative cases were identified. The overall clinical adequacy rate was 99.2% (943/951; 95% CI 98.4-99.6%). Clinically inadequate examinations were more frequent in patients with suspected intracranial hypertension (P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: Diffusion-weighted imaging- and motion-resistant radial FLAIR-based abMRI appears feasible and clinically adequate as an initial imaging approach for selected pediatric emergency neuroimaging indications. Full-protocol MRI remains preferable when intracranial hypertension is suspected.

articles.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Mortality in Pediatric Medical Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) using extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is increasingly used in pediatric refractory cardiac arrest. This study investigated the association between ECPR and mortality in pediatric patients receiving venoarterial ECMO (VA-ECMO) for medical indications. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients aged 28 days to <18 years who received VA-ECMO at a tertiary referral children's hospital between January 2010 and May 2025. The primary outcome was pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) mortality. Among 73 patients (non-ECPR, n = 58; ECPR, n = 15), ECPR was associated with increased mortality in unadjusted analysis (odds ratio [OR], 5.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.47-18.53; p = 0.010). After adjustment for pre-ECMO physiologic variables, the association between ECPR and mortality was no longer significant (adjusted OR, 1.74; 95% CI, 0.37-8.08; p = 0.483). Lower pre-ECMO arterial pH remained associated with higher mortality (adjusted OR, 1.87 per 0.1 decrease; 95% CI, 1.20-2.92; p = 0.006). In a sensitivity analysis, underlying cardiac disease was associated with lower mortality than noncardiac disease (adjusted OR, 0.23; 95% CI, 0.07-0.79; p = 0.020). These findings highlight the associations of pre-ECMO physiologic status and underlying disease category with PICU mortality.

articles.title: Fermented Laminaria japonica ameliorates type 2 diabetes in mice via modulation of insulin signaling, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota.
articles.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a global health challenge; therefore, safe and effective dietary interventions are required. We investigated the hypoglycemic effects of fermented Laminaria japonica in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms through integrated transcriptomic and gut microbiota analyses. Diabetic mice were orally administered fermented L. japonica, non-fermented L. japonica, or metformin for 4 weeks. Fermented L. japonica treatment significantly ameliorated hyperglycemia, improved insulin sensitivity, increased hepatic glycogen storage, and restored antioxidant enzyme (catalase, glutathione peroxidase, and total superoxide dismutase) activities compared to the NFS treatment. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that fermented L. japonica modulated key metabolic pathways, including PI3K-Akt signaling and AMPK activation, with upregulated gene expression associated with glucose metabolism (Prkag3 and Tmem100) and oxidative stress response (Ddit4 and Apod). Additionally, 16S rRNA sequencing demonstrated that fermented L. japonica reshaped the gut microbiota by enriching beneficial short-chain fatty acid-producing taxa (Limosilactobacillus and unclassified Lachnospiraceae) and suppressing potentially harmful genera. Overall, fermentation enhanced the anti-diabetic efficacy of L. japonica through the multi-target regulation of insulin signaling, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota composition, establishing fermented L. japonica as a promising functional food candidate for the adjunctive management of T2DM.

articles.title: Quantitative assessment of diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of cine MRI.
articles.abstract: Diaphragmatic dysfunction is a key determinant of dyspnea and impaired respiratory mechanics in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, objective quantification remains limited. This study quantitatively assessed diaphragmatic motion in COPD using pixel-wise optical flow analysis of sagittal cine magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Sagittal cine MRI of the right hemidiaphragm during quiet breathing was performed in 35 patients with COPD and 9 healthy participants. Optical flow was computed within the diaphragmatic region of interest after semiautomatic segmentation. Three indices were derived during expiration: the direction agreement ratio (DAR; proportion of pixels showing upward motion), the proportion of motionless areas (PMA), and mean diaphragmatic velocity (MDV). These indices were compared between patients with COPD and healthy participants across Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) stages and were stratified by the presence of visually assessed paradoxical motion. Pulmonary function associations were evaluated. Compared with healthy participants, patients with COPD showed a lower DAR, higher PMA, and reduced MDV (all p < 0.001). The DAR decreased and the PMA increased with advancing GOLD stages. Patients with paradoxical motion exhibited a lower DAR and higher PMA than those without paradoxical motion. DAR and PMA were correlated with FEV1%pred (ρ = 0.71 and - 0.71, respectively), whereas MDV correlated negatively with RV %pred (ρ =  - 0.79). Pixel-wise optical flow analysis using cine MRI provides a potential quantitative framework for evaluating diaphragmatic dysfunction in COPD by capturing synchrony, regional immobility, and motion velocity.

articles.title: Uncovering non-thrombotic roles of platelets in sepsis pathophysiology.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Thrombocytopenia is a common manifestation of this dysregulated response and represents a life-threatening condition in patients with sepsis. Analyses of large-scale datasets demonstrate that platelet count is an important determinant of in-hospital death in sepsis. Although thrombocytopenia is a well-established mortality risk factor not only in sepsis but also in hematologic malignancies and solid tumors, sepsis exhibits a distinctive feature: Platelet counts exceeding the normal range are also associated with poor outcomes. This bidirectional association between platelet abnormalities and prognosis appears unique to sepsis, suggesting a sepsis-specific role of platelets beyond hemostasis. Beyond their role in thrombus formation, platelets interact with leukocytes and tissue-resident macrophages during sepsis. In the liver, platelets accumulate around bacteria captured by Kupffer cells and promote bacterial clearance. Platelet-neutrophil interactions promote neutrophil crawling, transendothelial migration, and the release of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). While these mechanisms contribute to host defense against infection, excessive accumulation of neutrophils and NETs can exacerbate tissue damage and organ dysfunction, potentially outweighing their protective effects. This review summarizes the non-thrombotic roles of platelets in sepsis and their potential contributions to host defense and organ injury.

articles.title: Comprehensive comparison of echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamics in a real-world pulmonary hypertension cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is the preferred initial modality for evaluating suspected pulmonary hypertension (PH), yet its accuracy compared with right heart catheterization (RHC) remains variable, particularly in heterogeneous populations. We assessed multiple TTE-derived hemodynamic parameters against invasive measurements in a real-world PH cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 125 adults who underwent TTE and RHC within 72 h (2020-2023). Hemodynamic parameters included systolic, diastolic, and mean pulmonary artery pressure (sPAP, dPAP, mPAP), pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR). Mean PAP was estimated from pulmonary regurgitation velocity and right ventricular outflow tract acceleration time (AT). We evaluated correlation, Bland-Altman agreement, diagnostic accuracy, and inter-observer reproducibility.

RESULTS: PH prevalence by RHC was 81.6%. TTE correlated moderately with RHC for sPAP (r = 0.62), mPAP (r = 0.48-0.50), PCWP (r = 0.51), and PVR (r = 0.50). TTE systematically underestimated pulmonary pressures and PVR, and overestimated PCWP, with wide limits of agreement across all parameters. Against RHC-defined PH (mPAP > 20 mmHg), TTE showed high positive predictive values for TTE sPAP ≥ 25 mmHg (86.4%) and AT-derived mPAP ≥ 20 mmHg (94.7%), but low to modest negative predictive values (53.3% and 38.8%, respectively). Doppler PVR showed high specificity (93.3%) and positive predictive value (97.5%), but modest sensitivity (60%). Inter-observer agreement was excellent for sPAP (ICC = 0.87).

CONCLUSIONS: In a real-world, mixed-etiology PH cohort, TTE reliably identifies elevated pulmonary pressures but lacks precision for exact hemodynamic quantification. While valuable for screening, TTE cannot replace RHC for definitive diagnosis or hemodynamic classification, supporting a complementary diagnostic approach.

articles.title: Hemodynamic burden of mitral annular calcification: improved estimation by left atrial expansion index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is associated with heart failure, yet its independent hemodynamic impact on pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) remains incompletely defined. Moreover, accurate non-invasive estimation of PCWP in patients with moderate-to-severe MAC remains challenging.

AIM: We sought to quantify the independent association between MAC and PCWP and evaluate whether the left atrial expansion index (LAEI) improves the detection of elevated PCWP.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective study enrolling patients undergoing right heart catheterization with transthoracic echocardiography performed within 24 h. Patients were divided into the no/mild MAC and moderate-to-severe MAC groups. To assess the independent association between MAC severity on PCWP, a propensity score matching analysis was performed. In the subgroup of patients with moderate-to-severe MAC, the diagnostic performance of LAEI for the identification of elevated PCWP was compared against the current guidelines proposed algorithm.

RESULTS: Propensity score matching yielded 70 well-balanced matched pairs (N = 140) from 1,029 eligible patients. Moderate-to-severe MAC was independently associated with higher PCWP (+ 3.6 mmHg; 95% CI: 1.5-5.7; p < 0.001) compared with no/mild MAC. In patients with moderate-to-severe MAC and sinus rhythm, the current guideline algorithm showed lower performance (sensitivity 60.0%, specificity 65.7%) than lnLAEI < 3.69 (sensitivity 74.3%, specificity 77.1%). In addition, LAEI remained applicable even in the presence of atrial fibrillation.

CONCLUSIONS: Moderate-to-severe MAC is independently associated with higher PCWP. In this population, lnLAEI improves non-invasive estimation of PCWP and may represent a valuable adjunctive echocardiographic marker for refining the assessment of hemodynamic burden and diastolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Zoonotic Hybridization of Schistosoma bovis and Schistosoma haematobium: Implications for Human Morbidity and the Unexplored Territory of Appendiceal Schistosomiasis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: African schistosomiasis control has traditionally focused on human-only transmission. However, emerging molecular evidence demonstrates widespread hybridization between the human parasite Schistosoma haematobium and the livestock parasite Schistosoma bovis, challenging the traditional anthroponotic paradigm and reshaping our understanding of parasite virulence and tissue distribution.

METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to synthesize evidence on S. haematobium × S. bovis hybridization, zoonotic multi-host transmission pathways, and associated clinical manifestations, with a particular focus on the unexamined pathology of appendiceal schistosomiasis.

RESULTS: Out of 847 records, 15 high-quality studies met the eligibility criteria. Genotypic evidence confirms widespread bidirectional introgressive hybridization across West Africa, with hybrid prevalence reaching up to 100% in some human cohorts.
