One Health investigations support a multi-host cycle where S. bovis spills over from cattle to humans, pairs with S. haematobium, and propagates through Bulinus snails via human-to-human transmission. Clinically, hybrid infections are linked to altered morbidity profiles, notably increased hepatomegaly and reduced post-treatment resolution of bladder lesions. While histopathological reviews show that schistosomal appendicitis affects up to 4.15% of appendectomies in endemic areas, every identified study relied solely on microscopy without molecular characterization.

CONCLUSION: Zoonotic hybrid schistosomes alter human clinical profiles and transmission dynamics across Africa. However, their specific involvement in ectopic pathologies like appendiceal schistosomiasis remains entirely unknown, highlighting a critical research gap at the intersection of molecular epidemiology and surgical pathology.

articles.title: Bacterial profile, antimicrobial resistance, and predictors of mortality in necrotizing fasciitis: a multicentre prospective study in Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Necrotizing fasciitis carries a high mortality burden in low-resource settings, yet data from Uganda are scarce. This study aimed to describe the bacterial profile, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and predictors of mortality among patients with necrotizing fasciitis in Uganda.

METHODS: A prospective hospital-based study was conducted among patients with surgically confirmed necrotizing fasciitis at Mubende, Hoima, and Fort Portal Regional Referral Hospitals between April and August 2025. Wound swabs and tissue samples were cultured for bacterial identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and patients were followed until discharge or death. Modified Poisson regression was used to identify independent predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: Among 64 patients (56.3% male), median age group was 13-18 years, most had Type I polymicrobial necrotizing fasciitis (60.9%), while Type II monomicrobial infections accounted for 29.7%. Streptococcus spp. (24.6%) and Staphylococcus spp. (20.2%) were the most common isolates. While Streptococcus spp. remained highly susceptible to Ceftriaxone (92.9%) and Clindamycin (96.4%), Staphylococcus spp. resistance to Ampicillin (73.9%), though retained sensitivity to Vancomycin (87.0%); Escherichia coli (18.4%) and Klebsiella spp. (14.9%) exhibited multi-drug resistance but remained largely susceptible to carbapenems (Imipenem/Meropenem, 95-100%) and Ciprofloxacin (> 90%). Anaerobes: Bacteroides and Clostridium spp were reported. Diabetes mellitus, prior use of herbal medicine, undernutrition, and anaerobic bacterial infection (all p < 0.05) despite anaerobes showing high sensitivity to Metronidazole (75-100%).

CONCLUSION: Necrotizing fasciitis carries high mortality in Uganda, with anaerobic infection, diabetes, herbal medicine use, and undernutrition as key predictors; empiric therapy in low-resource settings should include anaerobic coverage with metronidazole or clindamycin.

articles.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Influenza A can cause encephalopathy or encephalitis, yet adult data are scarce and the two entities are seldom distinguished systematically. This small retrospective study of five adults explored the feasibility and limitations of classifying these complications with the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) 2013 criteria and describes their clinical, radiological, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and treatment characteristics.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive adults admitted to a tertiary center with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, all evaluated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), lumbar puncture, and electroencephalography (EEG). Encephalitis was defined by the IEC 2013 criteria (altered mental status > 24 h plus ≥ 2 minor criteria of central nervous system (CNS) inflammation). Data were analyzed descriptively.

RESULTS: Three patients met criteria for encephalitis and two for encephalopathy (four women; age 44-68 years). Respiratory influenza A PCR was positive and CSF PCR negative in all. CSF pleocytosis occurred in two patients, bilateral thalamic and subcortical white matter MRI hyperintensities in two, generalized EEG slowing in four, and focal status epilepticus in one. All received oseltamivir; three received high-dose methylprednisolone, two of whom also required intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange. The categories overlapped substantially: EEG slowing and negative CSF PCR occurred in both, and treatment escalation followed clinical course rather than category, with the most intensive regimen required by one patient in each. At 3 months, three patients were asymptomatic and two, both with encephalitis and structural MRI lesions, had persistent deficits.

CONCLUSION: In this small, hypothesis-generating study, IEC-based classification was feasible, but encephalitis and encephalopathy overlapped substantially and the distinction did not determine treatment. The main contribution lies in illustrating both the feasibility and limitations of criteria-based classification in adults with influenza A, rather than in establishing its clinical utility.

articles.title: Microvascular decompression compared with other surgical interventions for trigeminal neuralgia: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Microvascular decompression (MVD) is often considered the standard of care operation for medically refractory primary trigeminal neuralgia (PTN), yet there is variable evidence comparing its effectiveness with other procedures such as percutaneous balloon compression (PBC) or stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched CINAHL, Cochrane Library, Embase, PubMed, and Scopus from inception through April 1, 2026. Studies of surgically naïve PTN patients undergoing procedural and surgical interventions for PTN comparing MVD with at least one other procedural or surgical intervention were included. Outcomes focused on pain relief, recurrence, repeat procedures, and complications. A total of 26 studies (7 prospective, including two randomized controlled trials, and 19 retrospective) comprising 3,806 patients were included. Across predominantly retrospective cohorts, MVD was associated with higher short‑term and long‑term pain relief and lower crude recurrence and reoperation rates than SRS (e.g., short‑term 94.7% vs. 67.3%; long‑term 79.4% vs. 55.4%; recurrence 9.5% vs. 32.0%). Versus RFR, MVD showed higher short‑term (89.0% vs. 68.5%) and long‑term pain relief (72.1% vs. 54.7%), with lower crude recurrence (20.7% vs. 38.3%) and fewer repeat procedures (10.7% vs. 53.5%). MVD and PBC demonstrated similar short‑term (89.3% vs. 91.8%) and long‑term relief (83.9% vs. 79.7%), whereas crude recurrence rates favored MVD (11.1% vs. 18.3%). Limited data suggested higher long‑term pain relief with MVD versus partial sensory rhizotomy (88.9% vs. 70.9%). MVD generally showed lower rates of persistent sensory complications than ablative or radiosurgical procedures. These patterns arise largely from nonrandomized studies with baseline imbalances and variable follow‑up. Recurrence and long‑term estimates are crude proportions without time‑to‑event adjustment and are therefore exploratory and descriptive. This systematic review and meta-analysis suggests that MVD is an important option for appropriately selected PTN patients, with observational comparative data showing higher crude long‑term pain relief, lower crude recurrence, and fewer persistent sensory complications than several alternatives. Given the predominance of retrospective, nonrandomized cohorts and heterogeneous follow‑up, the pooled recurrence and long‑term estimates are exploratory descriptive findings and cannot establish comparative durability or superiority of MVD over alternative interventions.

articles.title: Paediatric Lagenidiosis Involving the Lacrimal Sac: A Rare Oomycete Infection in an Immunocompetent Child.
articles.abstract: Lagenidium giganteum, an oomycete, causes invasive disease in dogs and horses following freshwater exposure, but only two human infections have been reported, both in adults. We describe a healthy 3-year-old boy who developed a firm lacrimal sac mass over three weeks, following freshwater exposure. Inflammatory markers were normal, and antibacterial therapy was ineffective. Biopsy demonstrated broad, sparsely septate hyphae within granulomatous and eosinophilic inflammation. Routine cultures were initially negative. Prolonged incubation yielded a slow-growing, submerged colony, and internal transcribed spacer sequencing identified Lagenidium giganteum forma caninum. The isolate did not grow sufficiently to facilitate susceptibility testing. Two surgical debridements, performed one week apart, did not achieve complete source control. Twelve months of oral posaconazole and terbinafine with topical natamycin produced sustained clinical and radiologic improvement, maintained after cessation of therapy. This is the first reported paediatric human lagenidiosis and the first involving the lacrimal apparatus.

articles.title: Phenotypic cellular responses of Macrocystis pyrifera gametophytes to biotic and abiotic stressors: a morphological atlas.
articles.abstract: Brown algae remodel their cellular architecture in response to biotic and abiotic stress including cell wall organization, chloroplast structure, pigmentation, and cell shape. Here, we present an image-centered, qualitative morphological atlas of the female gametophytes of the giant kelp Macrocystis pyrifera (Phaeophyceae) generated under controlled laboratory conditions across a temperature gradient (10, 15, and 20 °C) and during infection by three phylogenetically distinct intracellular parasites: the oomycetes Anisolpidium ectocarpii (CCAP 4001/1) and Eurychasma dicksonii (strains 05 CCAP 4018/1 and 96 CCAP 4018/2) and the phytomyxid Maullinia ectocarpii (CCAP 1538/1). Using differential interference contrast (DIC) and epifluorescence microscopy, we document temperature-associated shifts in cellular organization and architecture of M. pyrifera gametophytes and describe parasite-associated cellular signatures across this temperature gradient. We compare these observations with established infection phenotypes to clarify convergent and distinguishing features between thermal stress and endobiotic infection. This provides a visual reference for recognizing temperature-driven stress phenotypes and pathogen-specific cellular signatures in M. pyrifera gametophytes. While broader environmental implications are beyond the scope of this microscopy-based study, these curated observations offer a baseline for interpreting cellular responses to thermal regimes and intracellular parasitism in brown algal systems. With ocean temperatures on the rise, the findings shared here are relevant, hinting at a shift in algal fitness and parasite infection pressure.

articles.title: Gut Microbiota, Red Wine and Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To review the relationships among gut microbiota, dietary patterns, red wine (RW) consumption, and atherosclerosis, with emphasis on microbiome-related metabolic pathways and their potential relevance to cardiovascular prevention.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent evidence has expanded our understanding of the microbiome-metabolome interface in cardiometabolic disease. Dietary patterns can modify microbial diversity and metabolites involved in inflammation, glucose homeostasis, and cardiovascular risk. Recent studies also support associations between wine-related dietary exposures, gut microbiota composition, and circulating metabolites. In the Wine Flora Study, moderate RW consumption was associated with broad shifts in gut microbiota and plasma metabolomic profiles without modifying plasma trimethylamine N-oxide. The gut microbiota participates in multiple metabolic pathways relevant to cardiovascular health and atherosclerosis. Diet is an important determinant of microbiome composition, and RW polyphenols may influence microbial and metabolic profiles. Nevertheless, a healthy diet, regular physical activity, smoking avoidance, and weight control remain cornerstones of cardiovascular prevention.

articles.title: Providencia spp. as emerging clinical pathogens in the era of antimicrobial resistance: From opportunism to global threat: A review.
articles.abstract: Providencia species are increasingly recognized as clinically important opportunistic pathogens, particularly in healthcare settings where the presence of vulnerable patients, prolonged hospital stays, invasive devices, and exposure to antibiotics contribute to their persistence and spread. Although Providencia spp. are historically viewed as relatively rare causes of human infection, some species such as Providencia stuartii and Providencia rettgeri have emerged as significant pathogens of urinary tract, bloodstream, respiratory, and other healthcare-associated infections. Recent studies have greatly expanded our understanding of this genus, revealing previously unknown species diversity, improved taxonomy, and identified the emergence of internationally disseminated high-risk lineages. Of particular concern is the growing burden of antimicrobial resistance. Providencia combines an intrinsically limited susceptibility profile with an increasing ability to acquire extended-spectrum β-lactamases, carbapenemases, aminoglycoside resistance determinants, quinolone resistance mechanisms, and other resistance genes. Carbapenem resistance, particularly that mediated by NDM-type metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs), has become a major clinical threat. Of great concern, the emergence of multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains was reported in Providencia and it is increasingly limiting treatment options. This review summarizes the latest developments in taxonomy, epidemiology, healthcare-associated transmission, mobile genetic elements, antimicrobial resistance, and therapeutic challenges for Providencia species, with emphasis on necessity of future research to strengthen genomic surveillance and antimicrobial resistance monitoring, promote the prudent use of antimicrobials, implement infection prevention measures, and conduct future therapeutic studies to limit further spread and improve the management of these emerging pathogens.

articles.title: Dietary oat protein hydrolysate and B-glucan improve glycemic control in diet-induced obese male mice.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Oat protein hydrolysate (OPH) has been shown to inhibit dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) in vitro, thereby potentially enhancing the effect of glucagon like peptide-1 (GLP-1) to improve glucose metabolism. However, its physiological effect in vivo has not been tested. This study aimed to investigate the preventive and therapeutic effects of OPH on glucose regulation in non-obese and obese male mice, respectively.

METHODS: Two different animal trials were conducted; trial-1 using non-obese mice and trial-2 using diet-induced obese mice. In both trials, mice were randomized into one of five dietary groups: a high-fat (HF) diet as control, HF with 25% protein replaced by oat protein (OP), HF with 25% protein replaced by OPH (OPH), HF with 10% fiber replaced by β-glucan (BG), and HF combining OPH and BG (OPH+BG). Glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity were assessed, along with plasma insulin and active GLP-1 levels. At week 5 of intervention, a subset of control obese mice underwent a meal tolerance test (MTT) following an oral dose of dextrose combined with OP, OPH, or casein.

RESULTS: OPH reduced body weight gain in both non-obese and obese mice, while food intake was similar across the groups. Improvement in glucose tolerance was observed in obese mice receiving OPH+BG, whereas no significant differences were seen in insulin sensitivity, plasma insulin, or GLP-1 levels. The MTT revealed no differences in glucose tolerance or insulin responses across the diets.

CONCLUSION: Despite OPH being associated with reduced body weight gain in both non-obese and obese mice, it did not improve glucose metabolism. Findings suggest that the combination of OPH and BG improved glucose tolerance in obese male mice.

articles.title: Multiple genes regulating the extracellular matrix are involved in groin hernia development: a systematic review of genetic and transcriptomic evidence.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Previous studies have provided evidence that patients with groin hernias may have a genetic predisposition. This systematic review evaluated the role of gene alterations in the development of groin hernias.

METHODS: We included studies reporting original data on participants with a history of groin hernia. Any control groups were considered. Studies must have analysed biological samples from participants to investigate genetic variants in DNA or changes in gene expression by studying mRNA. The outcomes focused on outlining gene expression patterns and identifying genes relevant to groin hernia biology. PubMed, Embase Ovid, and CENTRAL were searched on 25 September 2024. The risk of bias was assessed using the Quality of genetic association studies tool. Results were presented and synthesised narratively and through in silico analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 26 observational case-control studies with between 6 and 552,102 patients were identified, including 6 GWAS. Transcriptomic data in adults with medial and lateral inguinal hernias revealed altered expression of specific procollagen types, and more pronounced changes in enzymes regulating extracellular matrix homeostasis were observed in medial hernias. Genetic data in adults indicated that several hundred genes likely contribute to inguinal hernia development. In silico analyses identified 33 candidate genes, most of them involved in extracellular matrix homeostasis.

CONCLUSION: Genetic and transcriptomic data on inguinal hernia in adults indicate that alterations in expression or function of numerous genes contribute to disease susceptibility, with extracellular matrix dysregulation as a central mechanism. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may enable more personalized surgical strategies.

articles.title: Intragastric administration of the bitter tastant, quinine, reduces postprandial plasma glucose without affecting gastric emptying in health.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: In health and type 2 diabetes, intraluminal administration of quinine stimulates glucoregulatory hormones and slows gastric emptying, key determinants of postprandial plasma glucose, following oral carbohydrate. We have now investigated these effects following a mixed solid-liquid meal, with gastric emptying quantified using scintigraphy, the 'gold-standard' technique.

METHODS: On three separate days, nine middle-aged individuals without diabetes (age: 51 ± 8 years) received 0 ('control'), 300 ('Q300') or 600 ('Q600') mg quinine hydrochloride intragastrically, 60 min before a standardised mixed solid-liquid meal (100 g beef burger radiolabelled with 99mTc-phytate and 150 mL 10% glucose drink radiolabelled with 67Ga-EDTA), in randomised, double-blind fashion. Plasma glucose, insulin and glucagon were measured at baseline, for 60 min before, and for 120 min after, the meal. Gastric emptying was measured using scintigraphy. Data were analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA.

RESULTS: Q600 and Q300 both reduced plasma glucose immediately before the meal, at t=-5 min, as well as overall and peak postprandial glucose, when compared with control, in a dose-dependent manner (P < 0.05). Q600 stimulated plasma insulin before the meal at t=-20 min (P = 0.04), and the postprandial plasma insulin-to-glucose ratio (P = 0.02), compared with control. Both overall and peak postprandial plasma glucose were inversely related to plasma insulin at t=-20 min (R<-0.51, P < 0.05). Quinine did not affect plasma glucagon or gastric emptying.

CONCLUSION: Intragastric quinine lowers the plasma glucose response to a mixed solid-liquid meal in middle-aged individuals without diabetes by stimulating preprandial insulin, without affecting either plasma glucagon or gastric emptying.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered as a clinical trial with the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ( https://www.anzctr.org.au/Trial/Registration/TrialReview.aspx?id=383933&isReview=true ; ACTRN12622000735752, date of registration: May 23, 2022).

articles.title: Gorham-Stout disease with recurrent osteolysis after microsurgical flap reconstruction of the mandible: Case report.
articles.abstract: Gorham-Stout disease (GSD) is a rare idiopathic disorder characterized by progressive osteolysis associated with angiolymphatic proliferation, in the absence of malignancy or infection. Craniofacial involvement is uncommon and poses major diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when the mandible is affected. This report describes a case of mandibular GSD with recurrent osteolysis following microsurgical reconstruction. A 45-year-old male presented with progressive mandibular pain and bone loss initially suspected to be a benign vascular bone lesion. He underwent subtotal mandibulectomy with reconstruction using a free fibular flap fixed to a titanium plate. Despite initial flap viability, progressive osteolysis of the remaining mandibular rami and subsequent resorption of the bone flap occurred over the following months, accompanied by hardware instability and soft tissue failure. By 20 months postoperatively, complete resorption of both the reconstructed mandible and the fibular flap was observed, necessitating hardware removal and tracheostomy for airway protection. Histopathological reassessment of surgical specimens, combined with clinical and radiological findings, confirmed the diagnosis of Gorham-Stout disease. Subsequent follow-up revealed further disease progression involving adjacent craniofacial bones, leading to referral for medical therapy with bisphosphonates. This case highlights the unpredictable course of GSD and demonstrates that microsurgical bone reconstruction performed during an active phase of the disease may be compromised by recurrent osteolysis. Given the rarity of mandibular GSD and the limited number of reports addressing surgical outcomes, this case contributes valuable longitudinal data and underscores the importance of recognizing disease activity when planning reconstructive strategies.

articles.title: Cannabis-related disorders, hospitalization, and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure: A real-world propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical implications of cannabis exposure in patients with heart failure remain uncertain. We evaluated the associations between a documented cannabis-related disorder (CRD) and hospitalization and cardiovascular outcomes in a large real-world heart failure cohort.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Adult patients with heart failure (ICD-10-CM I50) were identified and stratified by the presence or absence of cannabis-related disorder (ICD-10-CM F12) recorded within 1 year on or before the first heart failure diagnosis, which served as the index date. The primary outcome was all-cause hospitalization at 1 year. Secondary outcomes included stroke, myocardial infarction, end-stage renal disease, atrial fibrillation/flutter, and all-cause mortality. Follow-up began 1 day after the index date; patients with a prior history of a given outcome were excluded from that analysis. One-to-one propensity score matching was performed using 26 baseline covariates.

RESULTS: After matching, 30,624 patients were included in each cohort. At 1 year, a documented CRD was associated with a higher risk of hospitalization (57.5% vs. 45.1%; HR, 1.468; 95% CI, 1.436-1.501; p < 0.001). A documented CRD was also associated with significantly higher all-cause mortality (10.4% vs 9.3%; HR, 1.147; 95% CI, 1.090-1.207; p < 0.001), stroke (2.9% vs 2.3%; HR, 1.263; 95% CI, 1.138-1.401; p < 0.001), and myocardial infarction (6.0% vs 4.4%; HR, 1.415; 95% CI, 1.307-1.531; p < 0.001). Atrial fibrillation/flutter and end-stage renal disease did not differ. The hospitalization association persisted after excluding the first 30 days of follow-up (HR 1.252; 95% CI 1.226-1.280; p < 0.001), was similar in women and men, and remained in multivariable Cox models (adjusted HR 1.521; 95% CI 1.503-1.539; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world propensity score-matched cohort of patients with heart failure, a documented cannabis-related disorder was associated with higher risks of hospitalization and selected adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Prospective studies with precise cannabis exposure characterization are needed to confirm these associations.

articles.title: A Mitochondria-Targeted Fluorescent Probe for the Real-Time Tracking of Hypochlorous Acid During Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is a key reactive oxygen species involved in redox and immune regulation. We report Mito-HOCl, a rationally designed naphthalimide-based probe for rapid, mitochondria-targeted HOCl detection. HOCl-induced oxidation of the thiomorpholine receptor suppresses photoinduced electron transfer (PET), causing a 20-fold fluorescence enhancement. Featuring high sensitivity and physiological stability, Mito-HOCl enables real-time mitochondrial imaging of exogenous and endogenous HOCl elevation during LPS-induced inflammation.

articles.title: M2-like-microglia membrane-modified Chuanxiong essential oil liposomes regulate microglial polarization to improve neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke presents a major therapeutic challenge, where modulating microglial polarization is a promising strategy. To enhance the brain delivery and targeting of Chuanxiong essential oil (CXEO), we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform, CXEO-loaded liposomes hybridized with M2-like-microglia membranes (CXEO-LP@M2M). In vitro BV2 cell experiments assessed uptake and inflammatory response. In vivo evaluation used a BCCAO/R mouse model to investigate targeting, anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative, and neuroprotective effects. CXEO-LP@M2M showed stable properties with a 150.6 ± 2.80 nm particle size and -12 ± 2.52 mV zeta potential. SDS-PAGE, western blot and dual-dye colocalization supported the retention of M2-like microglial membrane proteins on CXEO-LP@M2M. The encapsulation efficiency and drug loading were 80.19% and 2.22%. The formulation showed acceptable storage and colloidal stability at 4 °C, and its release was slower than that of free CXEO and similar to that of CXEO-LP. The cellular uptake of CXEO-LP@M2M by BV2 cells was higher than that of CXEO-LP. In vitro, CXEO-LP@M2M significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 levels and modulated microglia polarization. In vivo, it alleviated neurological deficits, brain edema, and histopathological changes, reduced inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, and promoted M2-like polarization. CXEO-LP@M2M combines cell membrane delivery and nano-carrier systems, showing stability, safety, and efficient brain targeting in the present models. The M2-like-microglia membrane modification was intended to enhance microglial recognition and uptake, while nasal delivery may help bypass the blood-brain barrier. This study highlights CXEO-LP@M2M as a potential early intervention/protective strategy for ischemic stroke by combining biomimetic delivery with the modulation of neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Decreased circulating conventional dendritic cells in polycythaemia vera: a cross-sectional case-control study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Polycythaemia vera (PV) is characterised by chronic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but circulating dendritic cell (DC) subsets have not been well characterised. We evaluated circulating DC subsets and inflammatory cytokines in PV and explored their associations with clinical features.

METHODS: This cross-sectional case-control study included 112 patients with PV and 30 community based controls frequency matched by age group and sex. Plasmacytoid DCs, conventional DC1 (cDC1), and conventional DC2 (cDC2) were quantified by flow cytometry, and serum IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 levels were measured by ELISA. Associations with risk category, age, prior thrombosis, splenomegaly, treatment status, and symptom burden were examined.

RESULTS: Patients with PV had lower total DC counts and percentages than controls (0.020 vs 0.034 ×10⁹/L and 0.26% vs 0.50%; both p<0.001), primarily reflecting lower cDC1 counts and percentages (0.015 vs 0.028 ×10⁹/L and 0.19% vs 0.42%; both p<0.001). Serum IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10 levels were higher in PV (all p<0.001). Lower cDC2 counts in high risk patients may reflect age, a component of PV risk classification. The association between older age and lower cDC2 counts was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for cytoreductive treatment. Splenomegaly was associated with lower total DC and cDC1 counts. cDC1 percentages remained lower in untreated patients than in controls. DC measures were not associated with prior thrombosis or MPN-10 symptom burden, and cytokine levels did not correlate with absolute DC subset counts.

CONCLUSION: PV is associated with reduced circulating DCs, particularly cDC1, alongside increased inflammatory cytokines. Untreated patients had lower cDC1 percentages, but their absolute cDC1 counts were not significantly different from those of controls. A contribution of cytoreductive treatment to the lower absolute cDC1 counts in the overall PV cohort cannot be excluded. Longitudinal studies with disease comparator groups are required to determine its specificity and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Hospital Volume, Stroke Severity, and In-Hospital Mortality after Basilar Artery Thrombectomy in the United States.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospital volume is associated with outcomes after anterior-circulation thrombectomy, but its relationship with mortality after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is uncertain. We examined trends, hospital volume, and the influence of coded stroke severity on mortality after BAO thrombectomy.

METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2023. Adults with a principal ischemic stroke diagnosis and a basilar artery infarction code (ICD-10-CM I63.02, I63.12, I63.22) were included; the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) was derived from R29.7xx codes. Hospital volume was measured within each year as BAO-specific and all-stroke EVT volume. Analyses used survey-weighted regression, interrupted time series, and propensity matching with and without NIHSS.

RESULTS: Among 9,049 BAO admissions (weighted 45,245), 2,335 (25.8%) received EVT. EVT use rose from 16.4% to 32.0%, and EVT-recipient mortality declined from 33.3% to 27.2%, without a robust change at trial publication. Highest-volume centers treated more severe and more often transferred patients and had lower NIHSS-adjusted mortality (BAO-specific volume: odds ratio [OR] 0.76, 95% CI 0.56-1.02; all-stroke volume: OR 0.82, 0.61-1.10; sensitivity analyses 0.73-0.83), without a monotonic gradient. NIHSS adjustment attenuated the matched mortality OR for EVT from 2.46 (2.16-2.80) to 1.31 (1.12-1.53); by severity stratum, ORs ranged from 7.74 (NIHSS 0-4) to 0.80 (NIHSS 21-42).

CONCLUSION: US basilar thrombectomy use doubled across the trial era while in-hospital mortality declined gradually. Highest-volume centers had consistently but imprecisely lower severity-adjusted mortality. Coded NIHSS materially changes treatment associations and should be standard in administrative stroke research.

articles.title: Clinical Remission and Disease-Modifying Potential of Biologics in Severe Asthma Running Head: Clinical Remission and Disease-Modifying Potential in Severe Asthma.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biologics have shifted therapeutic ambition in severe asthma from disease control toward clinical remission. However, on-treatment remission remains a treatment state rather than proof of disease modification because residual biological, physiological, or structural abnormalities may persist and benefits observed during ongoing exposure cannot distinguish pharmacological suppression from durable change in disease course.

SUMMARY: This review evaluates disease-modifying potential within a multidomain interpretive framework spanning clinical remission, biological change, physiological recovery, structural change, longitudinal trajectory, and durability as pharmacological exposure is reduced or withdrawn. Human mechanistic and clinical studies show that biologics can alter selected local-airway biological processes and, in some settings, physiological abnormalities, although responses across domains may dissociate. Structural effects are endpoint-dependent: mucus-plug burden is treatment responsive, and selected airway-wall remodeling features may change in defined cohorts, but universal or synchronous structural reversal has not been established. Earlier biologic initiation is associated with better subsequent outcomes, yet causal modification of long-term trajectory remains unproven. Withdrawal and dose-spacing studies show heterogeneous durability and variable pharmacological dependence, with both disease re-emergence and persistent benefit.

KEY MESSAGES: Biologics can achieve profound disease suppression and selected disease-domain changes relevant to a disease-modifying interpretation. However, current evidence does not establish universal, durable disease modification or cure. Confidence in a disease-modifying interpretation would increase with convergent evidence of underlying-process change, altered longitudinal trajectory, and durability beyond continuous pharmacological exposure.

articles.title: Five-Year Functional Outcome Trajectories After Acute Ischemic Stroke and Their Associated Clinical, Biomarker, and Imaging Features: A Longitudinal Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary substantially, yet the heterogeneity of long-term trajectories and their associated baseline features remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to identify distinct 5-year functional outcome trajectories and characterize their associated clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles.

METHODS: This longitudinal multicenter study included 9073 patients with AIS from the Third China National Stroke Registry (2015-2018). Group-based trajectory modeling was applied to repeated modified Rankin Scale assessments from discharge to 5 years. We then compared clinical, biomarker, and imaging features across the identified trajectory groups, and applied machine learning coupled with SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify and rank the key features associated with each trajectory group. Data were split by center to compare model performance and select the best-performing model for feature interpretation.

RESULTS: Four trajectories were identified: Favorable Rapid Recovery (33.8%), Favorable Steady Improvement (44.8%), Adverse Fluctuating-Worsening (15.0%), and Adverse Progressive Deterioration-Death Group (6.3%). These trajectories differed in their clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles. LightGBM achieved the best internal validation performance (AUC = 0.711) and was selected for subsequent SHAP interpretation. The key features associated with each trajectory group included younger age and lower National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) for Trajectory 1; lower coagulation markers and lacunar infarction for Trajectory 2; higher NIHSS, large vessel impairment, and low education for Trajectory 3; and advanced age, multimorbidity, and elevated inflammatory markers for Trajectory 4. Sensitivity analyses showed broadly similar feature patterns.

CONCLUSIONS: Four heterogeneous 5-year functional outcome trajectories were identified after AIS, ranging from rapid and sustained recovery to progressive disability and mortality. These trajectories were characterized by distinct clinical, biomarker, and imaging profiles. Baseline features, including age, NIHSS, coagulation, inflammation, and vessel impairment, were key features associated with trajectory groups, with varying weights and directions. These findings provide a foundation for hypothesis generation in future research on risk stratification, personalized rehabilitation, and secondary prevention.

articles.title: New Insights and Effectiveness of Digital Interventions for Health Anxiety: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health anxiety (HA), classified in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) under illness anxiety disorder (IAD) or somatic symptom disorder, is an increasingly prevalent condition associated with substantial psychological and health care burdens. Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer scalable and accessible approaches to care, with digital behavioral interventions (DBIs), particularly internet-delivered cognitive and behavioral therapies, among the most frequently studied. However, their effectiveness in reducing HA has not been comprehensively synthesized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effectiveness of DBIs for reducing HA in adults and to examine their effects on related psychological outcomes.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 statement and Cochrane guidance. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library were searched from database inception to November 1, 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental studies, and cohort studies involving adults with HA. HA severity was the primary outcome. Random-effects meta-analyses were restricted to RCTs. Methodological quality was appraised using Joanna Briggs Institute tools, risk of bias in RCTs using Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2), and certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: Sixteen studies involving 2581 participants were included, comprising 9 RCTs, 6 quasi-experimental studies, and 1 cohort study. Six RCTs involving 585 participants contributed to the primary meta-analysis. Digital interventions significantly reduced HA compared with control conditions (Hedges g=-0.77, 95% CI -1.25 to -0.30; P=.002), although between-study heterogeneity was substantial (I²=86.7%). Leave-one-out analyses showed that this effect remained significant after exclusion of any individual trial. By contrast, pooled effects on illness-related attitudes, general anxiety, anxiety sensitivity, and depressive symptoms were not statistically significant and were characterized by substantial heterogeneity. Among the 9 RCTs, 4 were judged as having low overall risk of bias, 2 had some concerns, and 3 were at high risk. GRADE certainty was low for HA and very low for the secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Digital interventions show potential for reducing core health-anxiety symptoms, but confidence in the magnitude and generalizability of the effect is limited by substantial heterogeneity, risk-of-bias concerns, and low certainty of evidence. Evidence for broader psychological outcomes remains inconclusive. Adequately powered, well-reported RCTs using rigorous outcome assessment, appropriate active comparators, and longer follow-up are needed to confirm effectiveness and clarify which patients benefit most and under what delivery conditions.

articles.title: The Association of Oral and Anogenital Human Papillomavirus Genotypes With Head and Neck Cancers in Brazil: A Nationwide Case-Control Study.
articles.abstract: This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer-free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50-65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high-risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV-16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV-16/18-positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case-control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high-risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. 9%; p = 0.049). Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten-fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92-34.6). Oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52-26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site-specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV-16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Dissection in Unrepaired Patent Ductus Arteriosus: Hemodynamic-Guided Ductal Closure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary artery (PA) dissection is a rare and potentially fatal complication, usually associated with severe pulmonary hypertension, PA aneurysms, or congenital heart disease. Evidence regarding management remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with unrepaired patent ductus arteriosus presented with acute chest pain and was diagnosed with PA dissection, giant PA aneurysm, severe pulmonary regurgitation, and pulmonary hypertension. He underwent urgent surgical repair, pulmonary valve replacement, and PA reconstruction. Given uncertain operability, transient intraoperative ductal reopening produced acute hemodynamic deterioration and right ventricular dysfunction, whereas occlusion improved pulmonary hemodynamics, supporting definitive closure.

DISCUSSION: PA dissection associated with patent ductus arteriosus is exceptionally uncommon and presents complex management challenges. This case illustrates the value of intraoperative hemodynamic assessment when conventional operability evaluation is not feasible.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Intraoperative hemodynamic testing may help guide ductal closure in selected high-risk patients with uncertain operability.

articles.title: A Novel Tip Balloon Extension Catheter Use in Complex PCI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guide extension catheters are increasingly used in complex and high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), particularly with growing applications in chronic total occlusion (CTO). However, conventional guide extension catheters exhibit suboptimal performance in certain anatomically challenging lesions encountered during PCI.

CASE SUMMARIES: We report the clinical utility of a novel tip balloon extension (TBE) catheter, with an integrated balloon-anchoring feature, for enhancing procedural backup support in 4 patients undergoing complex PCI. This case series illustrates the application of the TBE catheter across a spectrum of anatomically and technically challenging coronary interventions, including anomalous coronary artery origin, highly resistant CTO lesions, reverse-controlled antegrade and retrograde tracking, and anterograde dissection and reentry.

CONCLUSION: This novel TBE catheter demonstrates clinical utility in addressing anatomically challenging coronary lesions, particularly those associated with CTO. Its use as a bailout device requires careful procedural consideration and operator expertise.

articles.title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Under Deep Sedation With Spontaneous Ventilation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The SAPIEN M3 is a transseptal system for transcatheter mitral valve replacement, and published experience of implantation has been under general anesthesia. We describe its implantation under deep sedation with spontaneous ventilation, without tracheal intubation.

KEY STEPS: Confirm adequate midesophageal and transgastric image quality and favorable computed tomographic anatomy. Place the patient under deep sedation with dexmedetomidine, propofol, and fentanyl, under arterial pressure, bispectral index, and capnographic monitoring, with predefined conversion criteria. Obtain transseptal access, position the dock under prolonged transgastric imaging, and deploy the valve under rapid pacing. Monitor ventilation and oxygenation with serial arterial blood gases.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Aspiration with an unprotected airway during prolonged probe manipulation, and loss of the stable conditions needed throughout a long procedure, require meticulous anesthetic monitoring and immediate capability for conversion.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: This case demonstrates that SAPIEN M3 implantation is feasible under deep sedation with spontaneous ventilation. In selected patients at increased risk from general anesthesia, deep sedation may extend this therapy, a possibility that larger series should now test.

articles.title: Miniaturizing Slipstream and Tip Detection to a 7-F Transradial System for Chronic Total Occlusion PCI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To demonstrate that the combination of the slipstream and tip detection can be miniaturized to a 7-F radial system using the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter and AnteOwl intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) for a chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesion.

KEY STEPS: Treat the in-stent restenosis in left circumflex artery #14 and insert the AnteOwl IVUS over the same wire (first-wire lumen only) to delineate the spatial relationship between the stent struts and the jailed ostium of left circumflex artery #15 CTO. Advance the SIDEPASS short-monorail dual-lumen catheter over the same wire within a 7-F guiding catheter, pass a second guidewire through an optimal stent-strut cell into the CTO, and complete lesion preparation.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Narrow clearance within a 7-F guide, first-wire instability when removing the dual-lumen catheter, and inaccurate ostium identification can hinder the procedure.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Miniaturizing slipstream and tip detection to a 7-F system provides a smaller radial access footprint for complex CTO percutaneous coronary intervention while preserving advanced IVUS-guided wiring.

articles.title: Massive Right Ventricular Subepicardial Hematoma After CTO-PCI: CT-Based Evolution and Multidisciplinary Management.
articles.abstract:
CLINICAL CONDITION: A 55-year-old man developed a large compressive subepicardial right ventricular (RV) hematoma 8 hours after unsuccessful right coronary artery chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention. Despite near-complete RV collapse and outflow tract obstruction, he remained hemodynamically stable, and cardiac computed tomography showed no active contrast extravasation.

KEY QUESTIONS: How should immediate management and rescue strategies be selected despite severe right ventricular compression and preserved hemodynamics? How should the hematoma's time course influence monitoring, intervention, and later revascularization decisions?

OUTCOME: The heart team selected intensive monitoring and serial multimodal imaging. Hematoma volume increased by 16.1% by day 3 and remained above baseline at day 7, then regressed slowly, with near-complete resolution by day 131 and complete echocardiographic resolution at 1 year.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Preserved hemodynamics and no evidence of active bleeding may support surveillance despite severe anatomical compression. Deterioration should prompt timely decompression because spontaneous regression is slow.

articles.title: The Blanking Period after Pulsed Field Ablation: Time to Rethink, Not Yet to Abandon.
Mitochondria as the hub for drug tolerance during fungal aging and starvation.
articles.abstract: Opportunistic fungal pathogens, including Candida, Aspergillus, and Cryptococcus species, employ metabolic and organellar adaptations to survive host stresses and antifungal treatments. Cryptococcus neoformans thrives in a nutrient-limiting environment and undergoes prolonged replicative stress during chronic infection. Nutrient limitation is modeled as calorie restriction (CR), while replicative stress is manifested through replicative aging (RA). C. neoformans adapts to these stresses and undergoes many physiological changes. These changes include increased azole tolerance and higher drug efflux pump activities during CR and RA, which correlate with altered mitochondrial structures and functions. Mitochondrial pathways behave differently under RA and CR stress. For example, mitochondrial mass is significantly higher in aging cells, while it is significantly lower in CR-adapted cells. The role of mitochondria in antifungal tolerance in both RA and CR cells remains poorly understood. Multiple mitochondrial pathways contribute to antifungal tolerance. These include regulation of respiration, mitochondrial genome and protein functions, and calcium and iron homeostasis. Several inhibitors have been identified to target these mitochondrial pathways. The effects of these inhibitors on lowering antifungal tolerance in CR and RA-adapted cells need to be studied. This will aid in next-generation drug designing to combat the growing frequency of antifungal tolerance, especially in C. neoformans.

articles.title: Beyond pathogen-intrinsic resistance: the host context in AMR evolution.
articles.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is traditionally viewed as a pathogen-intrinsic, genetically encoded trait. However, growing evidence indicates that antimicrobial susceptibility is dynamically shaped by the host context during an infection. Gradients in oxygen, nutrients, pH, immune effectors, spatial structure, and polymicrobial interactions generate a highly dynamic microenvironment that can profoundly influence microbial physiology and drug response. Within each of these gradient niches, pathogens can frequently occupy metabolic states that alter their kill kinetics, promote tolerance, and enable persistence even without intrinsic genetic elements. Experimental models of infection further demonstrate that antimicrobial efficacy depends not only on drug potency and microbial genotype, but also on host-imposed constraints. In this review, we highlight a systems-level framework in which AMR emerges from dynamic interactions between the pathogen, host microenvironment, and antimicrobial exposure. Such a framework takes into account tolerance, persistence, and resistance along a physiological continuum shaped by a dynamic host-pathogen-drug interaction. Therefore, recognizing AMR as an emergent property of a dynamic interplay between host-pathogen and drug exposure challenges reliance on standardized in vitro susceptibility testing and underscores the need for physiologically relevant infection models. By incorporating host context into experimental design and therapeutic strategy, this framework offers a more mechanistic understanding of antimicrobial susceptibility and resistance evolution, and suggests new avenues to be explored for therapeutic development and future research.

articles.title: Basophil FcεR1γ signaling regulates gut barrier integrity and systemic antibacterial immunity during malaria with a sex bias.
articles.abstract: Malaria predisposes individuals to concurrent bacteremia, a complication associated with increased intestinal permeability and mast cell (MC) activation. These effects correlate with elevated type-2 cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-3, IL-4, and IL-10. We previously demonstrated that basophils regulate MC activation and protect intestinal barrier integrity during malaria. Because FcεR1γ signaling is required for basophil IL-4 production, we monitored parasitemia, barrier integrity, bacteremia, and cytokine and chemokine profiles in male and female mice with basophil-specific deletion of FcεR1γ [baso Fcer1g (-)], generated by crossing Mcpt8-Cre and Fcer1gflox/flox mice. Baso Fcer1g (-) mice retain IL-3 responsiveness but fail to produce IL-4 upon activation. Mice were infected with Plasmodium yoelii 17XNL to assess the role of basophil FcεR1γ signaling during infection. Basophil FcεR1γ deficiency had no effect on parasitemia. However, female baso Fcer1g (-) mice exhibited significantly increased intestinal permeability by day 6 post-infection (PI) compared to genotype controls. Despite this enhanced barrier disruption, bacterial 16S levels in blood were reduced in female baso Fcer1g (-) mice by day 10 PI relative to female controls and mutant males. Increased permeability was associated with elevated ileal IL-6 and CCL4, and increased plasma CCL3 and CCL5 at day 6 PI. At day 10 PI, reduced bacteremia correlated with increased systemic IL-17A and GM-CSF, and reduced IL-10 and Mcpt1, indicating reduced MC activation. These findings demonstrate that basophil FcεR1γ signaling shapes female-biased mucosal and systemic immune responses during malaria, extending our understanding of sex-specific gut-systemic immune crosstalk during infection.

articles.title: Species-specific responses of bovine and ovine macrophages to Coxiella burnetii infection.
articles.abstract: Cattle and sheep are reservoir hosts for Coxiella (C.) burnetii, and their role is crucial in transmitting the bacterium to humans. Therefore, understanding immune responses is essential for preventing and managing Q fever. Macrophages play a dual role in Coxiella infections. They eliminate the pathogen and serve as host cells in which it can multiply. Our comparative studies of Coxiella infection in primary bovine and ovine macrophages reveal host-specific immune responses. After Coxiella infection, cattle macrophages predominantly express inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and produce nitric oxide (NO), whereas sheep macrophages principally express indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1). Although macrophages from both species exhibit similar infection rates, there are differences in cytokine expression. This pattern holds for both live and chemically inactivated Coxiella. In ovine macrophages, formalin-inactivated Coxiella triggers a much stronger transcriptional response for TLRs, IDO1, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, and IL-23 than live Coxiella, suggesting a host-specific immune subversion strategy by Coxiella in sheep. For the antigen processing/presentation machinery, we found comparable induction of surface MHC and CD40 proteins in both macrophages, whereas expressions of CD11b, CD80, and CD86 are higher in ovine than in bovine macrophages, indicating different strategies for macrophage activation. Consistent with this, the regulatory effects of self-produced NO on MHC II antigen presentation via transcriptional regulation are observed in cattle but not in sheep macrophages. Our current findings highlight the immunological traits of closely related reservoir host species in shaping cellular responses to Coxiella and have significant implications for understanding disease progression, susceptibility, and treatment.

articles.title: Lactate oxidase (LctO) acts as a metabolic checkpoint restraining Streptococcus pneumoniae invasion of respiratory epithelial barriers.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae rapidly translocates across polarized human bronchial epithelial barriers, with viable bacteria recovered from the basolateral compartment within 1 h post-infection. Disruption of the pyruvate node through combined deletion of pyruvate oxidase (spxB) and lactate oxidase (lctO) markedly enhanced transmigration of S. pneumoniae across polarized Calu-3 monolayers without causing early cytotoxicity or loss of monolayer integrity. This hyper-invasive phenotype was conserved in the TIGR4 and EF3030 background and under air-liquid interface conditions. Importantly, single ΔlctO mutants exhibited significantly greater translocation than ΔspxB mutants or wild-type strains across bronchial (Calu-3), alveolar (A549), and pharyngeal (Detroit 562) epithelial models. Enhanced translocation correlated with increased bacterial adherence but was independent of capsule expression, extracellular H₂O₂ production, pneumolysin, or tight junction disruption, as evidenced by stable transepithelial electrical resistance, lack of caspase-3/7 activation, and preserved host-cell viability (SYTOX staining) at early time points. High-resolution confocal microscopy revealed intracellular ΔlctO pneumococci localized within N-acetylglucosamine/sialic acid (GN/SA)-containing compartments as early as 1 h post-infection. In murine macrophages, ΔlctO mutants were phagocytosed at rates similar to wild-type bacteria but induced greater pneumolysin-dependent cytotoxicity at 24 h. These findings demonstrate that LctO functions as a metabolic checkpoint that restrains pneumococcal invasion of respiratory epithelia, revealing a previously unrecognized role for lactate oxidase in controlling the transition from colonization to invasive disease.

articles.title: Food Insecurity Patterns and Risk of Poor Glycemic Control, Acute Complications of Diabetes, and Ability to Obtain Diabetes Technologies in Youth and Young Adults With Youth-Onset Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Household food insecurity (FI) is linked cross-sectionally to diabetes-related outcomes. However, prior studies have not fully considered temporal relationships or the evolving nature of FI. We explored the patterns of FI and associations with hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), severe hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), health care use, and the ability to obtain diabetes technologies among youth and young adults (YYAs) with youth-onset type 1 diabetes (T1D).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Longitudinal data (2016-2022) from 956 YYAs with T1D were analyzed using multivariable logistic and linear regression. Food security was measured thrice (t1, t2, and t3) with the Household Food Security Survey Module and patterned into persistent food security (PFS), intermittent FI (IFI), and persistent FI (PFI). We evaluated FI patterns derived from repeated assessments with follow-up diabetes-related outcomes.

RESULTS: The prevalence of IFI was 20.8% and PFI was 7.7%. Compared with YYAs experiencing PFS, the odds of inability to obtain continuous glucose monitors were higher for IFI (1.9, 95% CI 1.1, 3.3) and PFI groups (2.3, 1.0, 5.2), independent of individual characteristics. PFI was additionally associated with higher HbA1c (β = 0.6, P < 0.01), 3.6-fold higher odds of DKA, 3.4-fold higher odds of severe hypoglycemia, 3.1-fold higher odds of HbA1c >9.0%, 3.0-fold higher odds of diabetes-related emergency department visits, and 2.5-fold higher odds of inability to obtain an insulin pump.

CONCLUSIONS: Among YYAs with T1D, IFI and PFI over time both seem to be associated with severely impaired ability to maintain glycemic targets, increasing the risk of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: A Tsr-family Chemoreceptor Controls Xylem Sap Chemo-sensing, Swimming Motility, and Several Virulence Associated Functions in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae.
articles.abstract: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) is a major phytopathogen that causes devastating diseases in rice. Although several virulence-associated factors have been identified in Xanthomonas spp., the functions of many predicted proteins remain poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize Mcp3, a membrane-associated putative chemoreceptor of the Tsr (transducer of serine receptor) family, as a critical determinant of virulence in X. oryzae. Deletion of mcp3 resulted in reduced virulence and impaired host colonization. Bioinformatic analyses, homology modelling, and membrane localization studies demonstrated that Mcp3 is a membrane-associated protein. Functional characterization of the Δmcp3 mutant revealed defects in chemotaxis and flagellum-mediated motility, indicating a role in bacterial movement and environmental sensing. In addition, loss of Mcp3 altered multiple virulence-associated traits, including cellulase production, biofilm formation, and exopolysaccharide production, uncovering a previously unrecognized role for this chemoreceptor in the regulation of key virulence-associated traits. Ligand interaction analyses along with chemotaxis assays further revealed that Mcp3 recognizes multiple xylem sap-derived chemical cues, while deletion of mcp3 reduced chemotaxis toward serine and xylose but enhanced chemotaxis toward methionine, suggesting a role in fine-tuning chemotaxis, host niche sensing, and adaptive navigation during infection. Collectively, these findings establish Mcp3 as a previously uncharacterized regulator of virulence in Xoo and reveal a novel role for a Tsr-family chemoreceptor in controlling biofilm and EPS formation, in addition to mediating chemotaxis-driven host niche sensing and adaptation during infection.

articles.title: A Pair of Copper Radical Oxidase and Peroxidase Secreted at the Appressorium Pore Coordinates Timely Plant Penetration by the Rice Blast Fungus.
articles.abstract: Appressorium-mediated host invasion is a key step in infections caused by plant pathogenic fungi that form melanized appressoria. We previously identified a conserved oxidase pair composed of a copper radical alcohol oxidase (AlcOx) and a peroxidase (Perox). In the cucumber anthracnose fungus Colletotrichum orbiculare, the Perox-AlcOx pair functions specifically at the onset of penetration peg formation and localizes to the pore formed at the fungus-plant interface. Oxidation of long-chain primary alcohols in the plant cuticle by the Perox-AlcOx pair generates aldehydes, which were proposed to trigger a cascade leading to appressorium-mediated penetration. Beyond its conservation in most Colletotrichum species, genes encoding the Perox-AlcOx pair are also present in Magnaporthe species. Here, using the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae (syn. Pyricularia oryzae) as a representative model, we analyzed the contribution of the Perox-AlcOx pair to appressorium-mediated penetration and lesion development. Gene disruption analyses showed that both enzymes are required for efficient plant infection, as mutants showed delayed host penetration despite forming normal appressoria. Fluorescence microscopy revealed that the Perox-AlcOx pair accumulates at the appressorial penetration pore, a highly specialized pathogen-host interface. Transcriptome analyses indicated that Perox-AlcOx-dependent oxidative reactions provide chemical signals required for host invasion by inducing gene expression changes associated with penetration peg formation. Together, these findings suggest that the conserved tandem oxidase pair contributes to the spatial and biochemical control of the appressorial invasion site and constitutes a lineage-specific module supporting efficient host penetration by high-turgor appressorium-forming fungi.

articles.title: Patient Factors Associated With Delayed Cholecystectomy and Prolonged Hospitalization.
articles.abstract: Gallstone disease requires hospitalization and surgery, yet cholecystectomy timing varies. This study evaluated factors associated with delayed cholecystectomy and hospital length of stay (LOS) and the relationship between operative timing and resource utilization. We retrospectively studied 200 randomly selected patients undergoing cholecystectomy at a level one hospital from January 2024 to January 2026. Surgery was classified as early (<24 h), average (24-72 h), or delayed (>72 h). The co-primary outcomes were delayed surgery, evaluated with logistic regression, and total LOS, evaluated with negative binomial regression; prolonged hospitalization (LOS ≥7 days), a secondary outcome, was evaluated with logistic regression. Forty-four patients (22.0%) underwent early, 104 (52.0%) average-timing, and 52 (26.0%) delayed surgery. Older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.22 per 10 years, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.01-1.47) and diabetes (aOR 2.23, 95% CI 1.03-4.85) were associated with delayed surgery, whereas male sex was associated with lower odds (aOR 0.45, 95% CI 0.22-0.92). Age was the only patient characteristic associated with longer total LOS (adjusted incidence rate ratio 1.12 per 10-year increase, 95% CI 1.06-1.19) and with prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.43 per 10 years, 95% CI 1.16-1.77); results were consistent in penalized-likelihood and alternative comorbidity analyses. Delayed surgery was associated with greater hospital utilization, with median LOS increasing from 2 days after early surgery to 6 days after delayed surgery, partly because preoperative time is included in total LOS. These observational findings cannot establish that delay causes greater resource utilization; older age and diabetes may serve as signals identifying patients who warrant earlier assessment.

articles.title: The Answer Lies within the Puzzle Piece: PET-Derived Defect-rich MOFs Boosting Ethylene Glycol Oxidation for Total-Product PET Upcycling.
articles.abstract: Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a "one-stone-three-birds" strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal-ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm-2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm-2. Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Electroelasticity-Regulated Vacancy Diffusion Enables Frequency-Adaptive Neuromorphic Perception and Control.
articles.abstract: Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic-ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color-direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.

articles.title: Fungal lignocellulose-degradation potential is associated with bacterial metabolic dysbiosis in the human gut.
articles.abstract: Fungi encode diverse carbohydrate-processing functions, yet the genomic basis of their lignocellulose-degradation potential and its relevance to the human gut remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally assessed cellulase-, xylanase-, and laccase-associated activities across 762 environmentally derived fungal isolates and sequenced 170 representative strains, retaining 160 genomes for genome-phenotype analyses. By integrating functional annotations with orthogroup presence-absence variation and machine-learning models, we identified lignocellulose-degradation-associated genomic features that improved phenotype prediction beyond conventional annotation alone. We then applied this framework to 2,116 publicly available fungal genomes and 704 cultivated gut fungal genomes from a previously published collection to construct a non-redundant catalogue of lignocellulose-degradation-associated genes (LDAGs), comprising canonical degradative enzymes, annotated phenotype-associated features, and candidate orthogroups. Across fungal lineages, xylanase-associated potential was broadly distributed, cellulase-associated potential showed an intermediate pattern, whereas laccase-associated oxidative potential was concentrated in a more restricted subset of taxa. Analysis of approximately 1,500 publicly available human gut metagenomes identified disease-associated differences in LDAG profiles in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ACVD), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and obesity. Under stringent read-remapping criteria, total LDAG abundance differences remained significant in ACVD and IBD but were attenuated in obesity, whereas compositional differences persisted across all three cohorts with modest effect sizes. These fungal genomic signatures covaried with bacterial taxa, including Escherichia coli, and pathways involved in central carbon and carbohydrate metabolism. Together, our findings establish a phenotype-informed genomic framework for resolving fungal lignocellulose-degradation potential and reveal its consistent association with disease-related bacterial and metabolic configurations in the human gut.

articles.title: Population-Scale, Genotype-First Characterization of Monogenic Diabetes in 374,973 Individuals Across Ancestries in the NIH All of Us Research Program.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Current understanding of maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) has been shaped by phenotype-first studies in predominantly European ancestry cohorts, leaving population-level prevalence and penetrance in a multiancestry population incompletely defined. Using a genotype-first design, we analyzed whole-genome sequencing and clinical data from 374,973 unrelated All of Us participants (42.0% non-European ancestry). We identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 10 established MODY genes and assessed carrier prevalence, diabetes penetrance, and age-dependent diabetes risk, including comparisons with noncarriers stratified by type 2 diabetes polygenic risk score (T2D PRS) and associations between T2D PRS and diabetes risk among carriers. We identified 370 carriers (0.099%; 1 in 1,013), with similar prevalence among European and African ancestry participants (0.105% in both). Diabetes penetrance was incomplete (13.4% by age 40; 43.5% by age 60) and varied by etiology: highest for GCK (56.0% by age 60), intermediate for HNF genes (HNF1A, HNF1B, and HNF4A; 45.4%), and lowest for non-GCK/HNF genes (ABCC8, INS, KCNJ11, NEUROD1, PDX1, and RFX6; 29.0%). In Cox models, carriers of variants in non-GCK/HNF genes had modestly increased diabetes risk (hazard ratio [HR] 1.64; 95% CI 1.19-2.27), which was numerically lower than among noncarriers in the top 10% of T2D PRS (HR 1.91; 95% CI 1.87-1.95). Higher T2D PRS was also associated with greater diabetes risk among carriers (HR per SD 1.32; 95% CI 1.13-1.56). These findings support equitable consideration of MODY genetic testing across ancestries and highlight substantial heterogeneity in diabetes risk among carriers of pathogenic variants in MODY genes.

ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS: Understanding of maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) has been shaped by phenotype-first, predominantly European ancestry studies. We asked what the prevalence and penetrance of pathogenic MODY variants were in 374,973 unrelated All of Us participants from multiple ancestry groups and whether type 2 diabetes polygenic risk modified diabetes risk. Variants were present in 1 in 1,013, with similar prevalence in European and African ancestry individuals; penetrance varied by etiology, with diabetes risk among some carriers overlapping that of noncarriers with high polygenic risk. Higher polygenic risk was associated with greater risk among carriers. Findings support equitable consideration of MODY testing across ancestries and highlight variation in diabetes risk among carriers.

articles.title: Challenging the "Lethal" Label in LCCS11: A Report on Three Patients With GLDN Variants.
articles.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part C, Seminars in medical genetics
articles.abstract: GLDN encodes gliomedin, required for the formation and long-term maintenance of Na + channels at the nodes of Ranvier. Biallelic variants in GLDN, associated with lethal congenital contracture syndrome 11 (LCCS11), may prevent the formation of functional nodes, causing a peripheral neuropathy leading to arthrogryposis and respiratory insufficiency. This clinical phenotype falls within the spectrum of anomalies included under the umbrella term fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS) and is often associated with perinatal lethality. However, survival beyond the neonatal period has been documented. Moreover, significant advances in the respiratory care of infants-based on experience from preterm infants and those with congenital diaphragmatic hernia-along with improvements in neonatal intensive care, appear to be increasing survival rates for these patients. In this report, we describe three patients with biallelic variants in GLDN from two unrelated families, two of whom have survived infancy. We also highlight the importance of recognizing fetal akinesia in utero, pursuing further investigation when identified, and planning delivery in appropriate neonatal care settings. Additionally, we address potential bias in treatment decisions arising from the term "lethal" in LCCS11.

articles.title: Structural basis of avian-to-human receptor-binding adaptation in H9Ny influenza A virus hemagglutinin.
articles.abstract: The receptor-binding specificity of influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) is a major determinant for viral host tropism, enabling interspecies transmission. The molecular determinants for receptor-binding properties of HAs vary among different IAV subtypes. In this study, we performed a comprehensive analysis on the receptor-binding determinants of IAV subtype H9 HA and found that the receptor-binding characteristics of H9 subtype influenza viruses have exhibited temporal variations over decades. Q226L (hydrophobicity switch) substitution in the 220-loop is the key determinant for H9 subtype HA to acquire human receptor-binding preference. The amino acid residues of the 130-loop greatly affect the binding of HA protein to canonical receptors. Organoid infection models demonstrate that all three representative viral strains could infect human bronchial epithelial organoids. These findings increase our understanding of the molecular determinants of receptor-binding properties of different HA subtypes and call for the surveillance and response to potential influenza outbreaks, or even epidemics/pandemics.IMPORTANCEInfluenza A virus (IAV) subtype H9 poses persistent zoonotic spillover risks due to its adaptive receptor-binding capacity, yet the molecular determinants remain incompletely defined. This study systematically characterizes the receptor-binding determinants of H9 hemagglutinin over decades of viral evolution and identifies two critical functional domains: the 220-loop residue Q226L substitution, which serves as the key mutation conferring human receptor-binding preference, and the 130-loop residues that predominantly modulate canonical receptor-binding affinity. Functional assays using human bronchial epithelial organoids further confirm the robust human infection ability of prevalent H9 viral strains. These findings clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying H9 IAV host tropism and adaptive evolution, provide critical theoretical evidence for targeted influenza surveillance and pandemic preparedness against emerging H9 influenza outbreaks.

articles.title: ICU Mortality Associated With Clinically Important Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multistate Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding may increase mortality and time to discharge from the ICU. Conventional analyses ignore timing and treat bleeding as a binary event. We evaluated the association between time-dependent clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding and ICU mortality.

DESIGN AND SETTING: A multicenter cohort study using data from an international stress ulcer prophylaxis trial.

PATIENTS: A total of 4821 invasively ventilated adult participants.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A multistate model was specified with two transient ICU states (bleed-free and post-bleed) and four absorbing states (ICU discharge or death, each with or without bleeding). The Aalen-Johansen method was used to estimate transition and state occupancy probabilities and to describe risks of different clinical courses. Follow-up was censored at 90 days. We fit two Cox models for time to death in the ICU regressing on time-dependent bleeding history while adjusting for age, sex, baseline Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score, admission category (medical/surgical/trauma), vasopressor/inotrope use and renal replacement therapy on study day 1 and randomized allocation of pantoprazole or placebo; a second model also adjusted for time-dependent covariates of advanced life support (invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressor/inotrope use, and renal replacement therapy). Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding developed in 104 patients (2.2%) in the ICU. Median ICU length of stay for those who experienced bleeding was 19 days (interquartile range [IQR], 11-30 d) vs. 9 days (IQR, 5-15 d) for those who did not. Accounting for immortal time bias, the time-dependent indicator of clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding was associated with increased ICU mortality (hazard ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.13-2.15). At any time, patients who experienced bleeding had approximately 1.6 times the hazard of ICU mortality compared with those without a history of bleeding.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding as a time-dependent event is associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality.
