articles.title: Age-Related Differences in the Organ Donation Process Among Pediatric Brain-Dead Donors: A Nationwide Study in Japan.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To characterize the pediatric organ donation process and age-related differences among brain-dead donors in Japan and evaluate organ-specific transplantation rates and graft survival across age groups.

DESIGN: Nationwide retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: National donor records maintained by the Japan Organ Transplant Network.

PATIENTS: All pediatric (≤ 17 yr old) brain-dead organ donors in Japan between July 17, 2010, and March 31, 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENT AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 100 pediatric brain-dead organ donors were included. Donors were categorized into three age groups: younger than 6 years (n = 32), 6-14 years (n = 48), and 15-17 years (n = 20). The time intervals from hospital admission to organ procurement showed marked age-dependent prolongation, with median durations of 28, 19.5, and 13.5 days, respectively (p < 0.01). Younger donors were more frequently managed in children's hospitals and pediatric departments, whereas older donors were increasingly managed in emergency and critical care settings. Organ transplantation was achieved in 99% of donors. Organ-specific transplantation rates were consistently high for the heart, liver, and kidneys across all age groups, whereas lung and pancreas transplantation rates increased with donor age. During donor management, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic function were generally maintained or improved until procurement. No significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed for any organ type.

CONCLUSIONS: The pediatric organ donation process in Japan was substantially prolonged in an age-dependent manner, particularly among donors younger than 6 years. Despite prolonged donor management, transplantation rates remained high, and no significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed. These findings highlight the importance of sustained multidisciplinary and family support throughout the donation process and may provide insights for pediatric donation systems in low-volume settings.

articles.title: Propranolol administration following traumatic brain injury induces distinct neuroinflammatory gene expression profiles.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major cause of morbidity and is frequently followed by prolonged intensive care stays with sustained physiologic stress. Beta-blockade has been investigated as an adjunct therapy for TBI given its potential to reduce sympathetic hyperactivation. The molecular mechanisms underlying neuroinflammatory signaling remain incompletely defined. We hypothesized that propranolol (BB) administration following TBI would modify neuroinflammatory transcriptional responses consistent with attenuation of maladaptive inflammatory signaling.

METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats (n=6-8/group) were divided into 6 groups: (1) TBI7d (controlled cortical impact) followed by 7 days of daily handling, (2) TBI7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI BB7d), (3) TBI with chronic restraint stress for 7 days (TBI CRS7d), (4) TBI CRS7d with daily propranolol administration (TBI CRS BB7d), (5) CRS7d (n=7) who underwent daily stress exposure for 7 days; and (6) CRS BB7d (n=7) underwent daily stress exposure with propranolol injections for 7 days. RNA was extracted from the injured frontal lobe and analyzed using the NanoString Neuroinflammation panel. Differential gene expression was analyzed using ROSALIND. Significant differentially expressed genes (sDEGs) were defined as fold change ≥1.5 or ≤-1.5 with p<0.05. Functional pathway analysis was performed using Qiagen Ingenuity Pathway Analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with TBI alone, TBI BB7d demonstrated 83 sDEGs, including genes associated with neuronal signaling, neurotransmitter regulation, and epigenetic modulation. Pathway analysis identified significant involvement of the IL8 signaling and FXR/RXR. In the TBI CRS7d model, propranolol treatment yielded 21 sDEGs. These genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular stress responses and inflammatory regulation. Propranolol downregulated IL6, IL8, and neuroinflammation signaling pathways.

CONCLUSIONS: Propranolol administration following TBI, with and without stress, resulted in distinct neuroinflammatory transcriptional profiles. Propranolol was associated with alterations in multiple pathways involved in stress response, immune regulation, and neurorecovery. These findings suggest beta-blockade may modulate stress-related neuroinflammatory signaling following TBI.

articles.title: High-Flow Nasal Cannula Versus Conventional Oxygen Therapy in Adults With De Novo Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) compared with conventional oxygen therapy (COT) in adults with de novo acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) using a meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA).

DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception to April 7, 2026.

STUDY SELECTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing HFNC with COT in adults with de novo AHRF.

DATA EXTRACTION: Two investigators independently performed study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, and certainty assessment, with discrepancies resolved through discussion.

DATA SYNTHESIS: A total of 13 RCTs involving 4294 patients were included in the analysis. Compared with COT, HFNC was associated with a lower risk of intubation (Risk ratio [RR], 0.88; 95% CI, 0.78-0.99; low certainty), but not mortality (RR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.83-1.10; moderate certainty). TSA indicated that the cumulative evidence was insufficient to establish a conclusive effect for either outcome. Although HFNC was associated with a statistically significant reduction in hospital length of stay (mean difference, -0.84 d; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.43; low certainty), the clinical importance of this reduction remains uncertain. No significant differences were observed in escalation of therapy (RR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.75-1.01; very low certainty), ICU admission (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.50-1.39; very low certainty), or ICU length of stay (mean difference, -0.10 d; 95% CI, -0.82 to 0.61; very low certainty).

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with de novo AHRF, HFNC may reduce the need for endotracheal intubation but probably does not improve survival compared with COT.

articles.title: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Multicenter PICUs.

PATIENTS: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.

CONCLUSIONS: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

articles.title: Religion and Religiosity in End-of-Life Decisions in Neurocritical Care.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: End-of-life decisions are shaped by diverse biographical, social, and cultural factors. Few studies have systematically examined the impact of religion on end-of-life decisions, and even less data are available on religiosity (i.e., strength of religious faith). The Religion and religiosity in End-of-life deCisiOns in neuroCritIcaL carE (RECONCILE) study aimed to investigate whether religiosity, rather than religion, plays a decisive role in shaping end-of-life decisions.

DESIGN: Prospective observational study.

SETTING: The study was conducted between 2021 and 2024 at two neuro-ICUs at Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin.

PATIENTS: We prospectively studied patients with acute brain injury and poor neurologic prognosis defined by the absence of regaining decision-making capacity or sufficient autonomy. A total of 100 patients were included.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS: Relatives were consulted to ascertain the patients' presumed wishes regarding the continuation or withdrawal of life-sustaining intensive care. The 10-item Santa Clara Strength of Religious Faith questionnaire was applied to measure the patient´s religiosity on a scale between 10 and 40 points. We applied the t-test for independent variables to evaluate the influence of religiosity on end-of-life decisions. To adjust for possible confounders like age, sex, nationality, and religion, we calculated a logistic regression as well as an analysis of variance calculation.

MAIN RESULTS: In patients in whom intensive care was continued, the median score was significantly higher compared with patients in whom intensive care was withdrawn (28.1 ± 9.0 vs. 20.5 ± 8.3; p < 0.001; Cohens d = 0.875). This finding was reproduced in each denominational group. Religion, age, and sex showed no significant association with the end-of-life decision behavior. Germans chose withdrawal of therapy significantly more often than non-Germans (p = 0.01) but also showed significantly lower religiosity scores (21.9 vs. 27.9; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: The RECONCILE study demonstrates that religiosity looks more important in influencing end-of-life decisions than religion. Higher levels of religiosity were associated with a preference for more aggressive treatment, even when neurologic prognosis is poor.

articles.title: Communicative Participation in School Entrants: An Analysis Across Four Profiles of Language Ability.
articles.journal: Language, speech, and hearing services in schools
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to advance the understanding of the functional impact of language difficulties on everyday life by (a) describing communicative participation in children during their first year of school and (b) comparing the capacity and performance components of communicative participation across four distinct profiles of language ability.

METHOD: We drew on data from a previous cross-sectional study of the oral language abilities of 126 Australian school entrants aged 55-73 months. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize capacity and performance component scores on the Focus on the Outcomes of Communication Under Six (FOCUS-34). Differences among language profiles on these components were examined using a multivariate analysis of variance with follow-up pairwise comparisons.

RESULTS: Communicative participation broadly reflected the language profiles. Children with stronger language abilities demonstrated greater participation, and a progressive decline in scores was observed across the other profiles. Measures of language capacity differed significantly between profiles, while performance measures were more similar. As indicated by FOCUS-34 scores, the lowest performing profiles showed relative strengths in coping skills but weaknesses in expressive language and independence in communication.

CONCLUSIONS: While communicative participation broadly aligns with language abilities, this study revealed both differences and similarities in functional language performance across profiles. These findings highlight the importance of assessing functional communication directly, rather than inferring performance from test scores. Further research is needed to develop tools suitable for evaluating functional impact in the school-aged population.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.35027770.

articles.title: Maternal HFD-Induced Energy Metabolic Defect Drives Hepatic Inflammation and Fibrosis in Mouse Offspring.
articles.abstract: Perinatal high-fat diet (HFD) exposure predisposes offspring to metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), yet how it reprograms hepatic energy metabolites alongside post-weaning dietary challenges remains unclear. This study investigates distinct and interactive impacts of maternal and post-weaning HFD on hepatic energy metabolite profiles and transcriptomics in adult mouse offspring. Female C57BL/6 mice were fed CHOW or HFD for 2 weeks before mating, throughout gestation and lactation. At weaning, male offspring were assigned to four groups based on maternal and post-weaning diets: CHOW-CHOW, CHOW-HFD, HFD-CHOW, and HFD-HFD. UPLC-MS/MS-based targeted metabolomic profiling of energy-related metabolites was performed on adult offspring livers. These hepatic metabolic signatures were correlated with lipid metabolism transcriptional profiles and circulating adipokine levels. Maternal HFD acted as the primary determinant of adult offspring hepatic pathogenesis, significantly exacerbating inflammation and fibrosis via upregulating Tnfα, Col1a1, and Acta2, whereas post-weaning HFD alone exhibited no individual aggravation. Mechanistically, targeted metabolomics demonstrated that both dietary phases altered the hepatic profile through distinct metabolic nodes: maternal HFD selectively disrupted mitochondrial redox states, accumulating fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, NADH, and GTP; conversely, post-weaning HFD primarily impaired terminal energetics and pentose phosphate pathway activity, increasing ATP and GTP but reducing 6-phosphogluconate. Pearson correlation analysis further connected these metabolites with circulating resistin and leptin, bridging localized hepatic energy stress with systemic metabolic regulation. This study demonstrates that maternal and post-weaning HFD program adult offspring liver dysfunction through distinct biochemical mechanisms, establishing that maternal mitochondrial redox disruption, rather than post-weaning energetic shifts, drives maternally programmed MAFLD.

articles.title: First Evidence of Isoflavone Production by the Oomycete Aphanomyces euteiches, the Causal Agent of Legume Root Rot.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Aphanomyces euteiches is a destructive soilborne oomycete affecting legumes worldwide. Although its pathogenic mechanisms have been extensively investigated, its specialized metabolism remains largely unexplored. In this study, organic extracts of A. euteiches grown on two different media were tested across five legume species. The PDA-EtOAc extract induced the most severe yellowing and necrotic lesions on leaves, especially in pea and lentil, and markedly reduced root growth, with associated necrosis, in all legumes evaluated. GC-MS and 1H NMR profiling identified major fatty acids together with phenolic compounds and diketopiperazines potentially involved in microbial signaling. Daidzein and genistein, two plant isoflavones, were also identified in A. euteiches organic extracts for the first time. This finding challenges the current view that these metabolites detected during infection originate exclusively from legume hosts and suggests that they may also participate in pathogen biology and host-pathogen interactions.

articles.title: Klebsiella Pneumoniae Induces Mitochondrial and Lactation Dysfunction in Bovine Mastitis via FNIP1-Mediated FOXO3 Phosphorylation and Ubiquitination.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Bovine mastitis caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) poses a serious threat to dairy production and milk quality, with mitochondrial dysfunction acting as a core pathological driver. As an important transcription factor regulating mitochondrial function, Forkhead box O 3 (FOXO3) plays a role in mastitis caused by K. pneumoniae infection that has not been deeply studied. This research established in vivo and in vitro mastitis models through K. pneumoniae infection. The results showed that K. pneumoniae upregulates FOXO3 mRNA but reduces its protein abundance. Mechanistically, K. pneumoniae-activated folliculin-interacting protein 1 (FNIP1) inhibits AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-mediated FOXO3 phosphorylation to block its nuclear translocation, while upregulating E3 ligase mouse double minute 2 (MDM2) to promote FOXO3 ubiquitination and degradation. FOXO3 overexpression rescues mitochondrial dysfunction, restores milk synthesis and alleviates inflammation, verifying that FOXO3 activation is a promising strategy for mastitis prevention and control.

articles.title: Dietary Control of MGAT-Dependent N-Glycan Branching: Implications for Metabolic Homeostasis.
articles.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
articles.abstract: Mannosyl-glycoprotein N-acetylglucosaminyltransferases (MGATs) build branched complex N-glycans that shape the cell-surface glycoproteome and tune lectin-glycan control of receptor stability, endocytosis, and signaling. Although MGAT-dependent branching is well studied in cancer and immunity, its role as a diet-responsive regulator of metabolic homeostasis remains underexplored. Here, we review tissue-specific MGATs expression and metabolic roles in the pancreas, liver, adipose tissue, and skeletal muscle. We discuss how macronutrients, N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) availability, and dietary bioactives, including geniposide, anthocyanins, resveratrol, curcuminoids, and vitamin D, reshape MGATs expression, branching capacity, and glycoprotein function. Current evidence positions MGAT-dependent N-glycan branching as a nutrient-sensitive interface linking diet to receptor signaling and metabolic adaptation. However, most data remain preclinical. Integrating controlled nutrition studies with glycomics and glycoproteomics will be essential to define its translational potential in precision nutrition and metabolic disease prevention.

articles.title: High-resolution transcriptome analysis reveals a multilayered and dynamic transcriptional architecture in the archaeal virus SSV1.
articles.abstract: Members of Fuselloviridae infecting thermoacidophilic Sulfolobales are among the best-studied archaeal viruses, with the Saccharolobus spindle-shaped virus 1 (SSV1)-Saccharolobus solfataricus interaction serving as a model system. After infection, SSV1 establishes a chronic infection with new virions continuously budding from the infected cell. UV irradiation triggers virus replication, increased virion production, and a tightly orchestrated temporal transcription cycle. However, gene regulatory mechanisms post-UV induction remain elusive. In this study, we investigated the SSV1 transcriptomic landscape post-UV induction using high-resolution, long-read Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) cappable RNA sequencing. Through end-to-end sequencing of primary transcripts, we generated a comprehensive transcript map of SSV1, identifying 21 transcription start sites (TSSs), including 12 newly described sites, and 19 termination sites (TTSs), of which 9 are novel. This enabled refinement of transcription units and operon structures across the genome. Five new start sites of antisense transcription were discovered, including one antisense to the open reading frame of a putative viral toxin gene a291, which we hypothesize to be a cis-encoded regulatory RNA. In addition, spontaneous recombination between two direct repeats in the SSV1 structural genes vp1 and vp3 was confirmed. To our knowledge, this is the first implementation of cappable-seq for an archaeal virus and the first base-resolution analysis of the SSV1 transcriptome. It reveals a previously unappreciated level of transcriptional complexity, illustrating how high-resolution transcriptomics can deepen understanding of viral transcriptome architecture and regulatory networks.IMPORTANCEArchaeal viruses remain among the least understood viruses in the virosphere, despite their ecological and evolutionary significance. Saccharolobus spindle-shaped virus 1 (SSV1) is a key model for the study of virus-host interactions in archaea. Yet, its gene regulatory mechanisms have remained poorly resolved. Here, we provide the first base-pair resolution transcriptome of an archaeal virus, revealing a complex and multi-layered transcriptional architecture. We uncover alternative transcription start and termination sites, as well as antisense transcription, pointing to regulatory mechanisms beyond a simple temporal gene expression program. These findings suggest that archaeal viruses use sophisticated transcriptional and post-transcriptional mechanisms similar to those in bacterial and eukaryotic viruses. By establishing a high-resolution map of the SSV1 transcriptome, this work advances our understanding of archaeal virus biology.

articles.title: Hepatitis C virus remodels lipid droplets to promote mitochondrial fatty acid accumulation and metabolic activation.
articles.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) depends on host lipid metabolism and lipid droplets (LDs) for genome replication, assembly, and particle production, yet how LD structure and lipid utilization change over the course of infection remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the temporal remodeling of LD-associated metabolic pathways during HCV JFH-1 infection of human hepatoma Huh7 cells. HCV infection transiently increased LD fluorescence intensity at 24 h post-infection (hpi), followed by normalization or relative loss of LD signal at later time points. Concomitantly, LDs became progressively clustered and enlarged during late infection, despite reduced protein levels of the canonical LD fusion proteins CIDEA, CIDEB, and CIDEC, suggesting that HCV-induced LD enlargement is not associated with increased expression of CIDE proteins. Transcriptomic, RT-qPCR, and immunoblot analyses revealed time-dependent regulation of genes and proteins involved in LD structure, triglyceride synthesis, lipolysis, lipid uptake, and mitochondrial fatty acid utilization. Subcellular fractionation demonstrated preferential accumulation of fatty acids in mitochondrial fractions at 24-72 hpi. This redistribution was accompanied by increased oxygen consumption rate, elevated extracellular acidification, and progressive reactive oxygen species accumulation, indicating infection-associated metabolic activation and oxidative stress. Pharmacological inhibition of DGAT1-dependent LD biogenesis, LIPA-dependent lysosomal lipid hydrolysis, LIPE/HSL-dependent lipolysis, or CPT1-dependent mitochondrial fatty acid transport markedly reduced mitochondrial fatty acid accumulation and suppressed HCV-induced respiratory activity. Inhibition of LIPA or LIPE/HSL reduced both HCV RNA and core protein levels, whereas inhibition of CPT1 or DGAT1 had more pronounced effects on core protein than on viral RNA. Together, these findings support a model in which HCV dynamically remodels LDs, mobilizes LD-associated fatty acids, and redirects them toward mitochondria to support infection-associated metabolism and downstream stages of the viral life cycle. Lipid hydrolysis and mitochondrial fatty acid trafficking therefore represent potential host-directed targets for limiting HCV infection.IMPORTANCEHepatitis C virus depends on host lipid metabolism for replication, assembly, and production of infectious particles, but how it uses lipid droplets over time remains incompletely understood. This study shows that hepatitis C virus dynamically remodels lipid droplets, causing an early increase in lipid storage followed by droplet enlargement and mobilization of fatty acids during later infection. The released fatty acids preferentially accumulate in mitochondria, where they are associated with increased cellular respiration and oxidative stress. Blocking lipid droplet formation, lipid breakdown, or fatty acid transport to mitochondria reduced this metabolic response and decreased viral RNA or core protein accumulation. Inhibition of lysosomal acid lipase and hormone-sensitive lipase suppressed both viral RNA and protein levels. These findings identify lipid droplet breakdown and mitochondrial fatty acid trafficking as important host processes used by hepatitis C virus and as potential targets for host-directed antiviral intervention.

articles.title: Changes in the chromatin accessibility landscape during human adenovirus infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Viral infections rewire the cellular environment, and this is often achieved through chromatin remodeling. Human adenovirus (HAdV) can directly modify specific cellular chromatin features; however, we still lack a global view of the changes in the cellular chromatin landscape induced during infection. To address how host chromatin accessibility changes during HAdV-C5 infection, we performed assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) in growth-arrested diploid human lung fibroblast (IMR-90) cells at 48 and 72 h post-infection. We detected widespread changes in chromatin accessibility, with 7,055 and 10,736 differentially accessible regions (DARs) on host chromatin at 48 and 72 h post-infection, respectively. At both time points, these changes mostly occurred in enhancer/intergenic regions and intronic regions. Furthermore, the pattern of changes in accessibility differed between protein-coding and non-coding genes. Integration of the ATAC-seq data with RNA-seq data demonstrated that significant changes in chromatin accessibility coincided with significant changes in gene expression during infection. Additionally, we found that increased DARs were enriched for forkhead and TEA domain transcription factor family motifs, while decreased DARs were enriched for motifs from zinc finger and basic leucine zipper domain families. Pathway enrichment analysis revealed that Wnt signaling pathway genes displayed increased chromatin accessibility during infection. Inhibition of the Wnt signaling pathway reduced viral gene expression and infectious viral progeny production, suggesting that this pathway is important for productive infection. Together, these data demonstrate that cellular chromatin is extensively remodeled during HAdV infection and expand our understanding of host-cell transcriptional regulation by human adenovirus.

IMPORTANCE: Human adenovirus-C5 (HAdV-C5) infection extensively modifies the cellular transcriptome and proteome. However, other important aspects of the cellular environment, such as global changes in chromatin accessibility, have yet to be fully characterized during infection. Here, we performed assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) in infected growth-arrested diploid human lung fibroblast (IMR-90) cells at 48 and 72 h post-infection. We observed genome-wide changes in cellular chromatin accessibility and identified specific transcription factor motifs located in differentially accessible regions during infection. This work contributes another key piece to our understanding of how human adenovirus infection reprograms the host-cell environment and will inform future work directed toward specific chromatin modifications manipulated by HAdV that impact host-cell chromatin accessibility.

articles.title: Viral reprogramming of cGAS functional states: from DNA-sensing failure to multilayered immune-evasion networks.
articles.abstract: Cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) detects viral and mislocalized host DNA to initiate antiviral immunity. Productive cGAS activation requires coordinated DNA accessibility and engagement, catalytic activation, higher-order assembly, and appropriate subcellular context. Viruses counteract this pathway by shielding DNA, disrupting cGAS-DNA interactions, modifying or depleting cGAS, remodeling cGAS assemblies and condensates, and exploiting nuclear regulatory mechanisms. Similar phenotypes, such as reduced production of 2'3'-cyclic GMP-AMP (2'3'-cGAMP), or loss of cGAS puncta, can arise from distinct molecular lesions, complicating mechanistic interpretation. Here, we organize viral cGAS antagonism around discrete but interconnected functional states, and emphasize the experimental evidence needed to distinguish direct inhibition from secondary effects. This framework integrates viral genome biology, host factors, cellular compartments, and infection stage to clarify conserved and context-dependent strategies of immune evasion.

articles.title: Establishment and characterization of a recombinant VSV-based pseudotyping platform for studying RSV F-mediated entry and antibody-mediated neutralization.
articles.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract disease, underscoring the need for safe, scalable platforms to evaluate neutralizing antibodies, and entry-targeting antivirals. Here, we established and characterized a vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV)-based pseudovirus neutralization assay for RSV that uses fusion (F) proteins from RSV A and RSV B strains as functional entry glycoproteins. Key assay parameters were systematically evaluated, including target cell type, F-expression plasmid input, packaging multiplicity of infection, pseudovirus inoculum, detection time point, and cell seeding density. Western blotting confirmed F expression and incorporation into pseudovirus particles, and a GFP reporter-based syncytium assay verified fusion activity. Under the selected assay conditions, the assay showed strong signal linearity, low background, and reproducible reporter readouts in HEK293T cells at 24 h post-infection. Neutralization by monoclonal antibodies targeting six major antigenic sites on RSV F (sites Ø and I-V) supported the functional preservation and accessibility of multiple neutralization-relevant epitopes on the pseudovirus surface. RSV-specific fusion inhibitors selectively blocked both pseudovirus entry and F-mediated cell-cell fusion in a dose-dependent manner, whereas SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitors had no effect, consistent with the expected virus-specific inhibition profiles. Importantly, pseudovirus neutralization titers showed positive correlations with live-virus neutralization results in both human and mouse sera. Together, these findings establish the VSV-RSV pseudovirus neutralization assay as a robust and scalable platform for measuring F-directed neutralizing activity and for supporting vaccine evaluation, serological surveillance, monoclonal antibody characterization, and antiviral discovery.IMPORTANCERespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial disease in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, underscoring the need for robust assays to evaluate vaccines, antibodies, and antivirals. Authentic-virus assays remain essential because they measure neutralization in the context of intact RSV, but the involvement of multiple viral components can complicate attribution of neutralization differences specifically to F. The vesicular stomatitis virus-based pseudovirus system developed here uses F as the sole RSV envelope glycoprotein and restricts infection to a single reporter-expressing round, enabling controlled comparisons of F variants, F-directed antibodies, and entry inhibitors. Its positive correlation with authentic-virus neutralization further supports its utility as a complementary platform for mechanistic and comparative studies of RSV F-directed entry and neutralization.

articles.title: HIV-1 and SIV virions are cleared from the blood of SIV-infected macaques with similar triphasic kinetics.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Defining the clearance kinetics of lentiviral particles is essential for understanding infection dynamics in vivo, but previous studies have yielded a >10-fold difference in the estimated clearance rate for HIV-1 in humans compared to SIV in macaques. These prior analyses often employed insensitive assays, short observation periods, disparate methodologies, and the assumption of monophasic clearance kinetics, complicating interpretation of discordant findings. Here, we investigated virion clearance by intravenously infusing non-infectious SIV, HIV-1 wild-type (WT), and envelope-negative HIV-1 (Env-) into SIV-infected macaques exhibiting a range of baseline plasma viral loads. Using highly sensitive virologic assays, we monitored infused virion clearance over eight hours across ~6 logs of dynamic range. We show that virion clearance is universally multiphasic, with triphasic models providing the best fit. SIV and HIV-1 WT were cleared with indistinguishable kinetics, including a rapid first phase (mean half-life: ~2.5 min) during which >99% of infused virus was cleared. We also identified previously undetected second and third clearance phases with progressively slower kinetics, with mean half-lives of ~17 and ~126 min (when estimable), respectively, for both SIV and HIV-1 WT. HIV-1 Env- virions showed modestly but significantly slower first-phase clearance rates, suggesting a potential role for Env in early virion clearance. Baseline viral burden did not correlate with clearance kinetics, providing no evidence for a saturable clearance capacity. Our results indicate that clearance kinetics are largely independent of viral load and virus type, suggesting that prior discrepancies stem from methodological limitations, modeling assumptions, or species-specific differences between macaques and humans.

IMPORTANCE: Accurate characterization of HIV-1 clearance from the blood is fundamental for understanding viral pathogenesis, infected-cell lifespans, and the dynamics of antiretroviral therapy-mediated suppression. Historically, distinct experimental systems suggested that HIV-1 clearance in humans is significantly slower than SIV clearance in macaques. This study resolves proposed explanations for this longstanding discrepancy by directly comparing the clearance of non-infectious SIV and HIV-1 particles from macaque blood using highly sensitive virologic assays. We demonstrate that both viruses are cleared at nearly identical rates, regardless of the total amount of virus circulating in each animal, and reveal for the first time that virion clearance is not a simple monophasic decay process but represents a complex, multiphasic process that alters how we understand viral biology. Our findings indicate that previous disparities were likely driven by technological limitations, monophasic modeling assumptions, and/or species-specific differences rather than virus-specific differences or a saturable virion clearance mechanism.

articles.title: Primer: Virus entry and uncoating.
articles.abstract: Viruses deliver their genetic material to a replication site in the host cell to initiate infection. To accomplish this task, viruses must co-opt cellular factors to promote the steps of virus entry and uncoating. This Primer highlights how select DNA and RNA viruses accomplish these steps. Consistent themes, unresolved questions, and potential therapeutic implications are discussed.

articles.title: Performing Follow-Up Imaging After 90Y Radioembolization in a Patient With Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
Electron cryo-tomography reveals the Caulobacter vibrioides tight-adherence pilus machine architecture.
articles.abstract: The type IV filament superfamily is a widespread group of molecular machines involved in natural transformation, motility, adhesion, nutrient uptake, and secretion of a wide spectrum of protein substrates. The gram-negative bacterium Caulobacter vibrioides expresses the tight-adherence (Tad) pilus, a type IV machine involved in surface colonization. Here, we investigated the proteins involved in Tad pilus production by ΦCbK resistance screening and the order of machine assembly and its polar remnant by fluorescence tagging. Using electron cryo electron tomography and subtomogram averaging of wild-type and mutant strains, we resolved the Tad pilus machine architecture and built an integrative model of its structure. The resulting model suggests the individual roles of multiple Tad proteins. Together, the data also reveal the Tad pilus machine's assembly order.IMPORTANCEMany bacteria rely on microscopic, hair-like appendages, called pili, for survival and infection of host cells. Pili are separated into several structural families, the type IV tight-adherence (Tad) pilus, which help bacteria like Caulobacter vibrioides attach to surfaces of host tissues and prey cells. Despite its critical role in bacterial infection, the exact structure of the Tad pilus and the machine that assembles it is not fully understood. Understanding the structure and function of the Tad pilus and its machine is a developing conversation between genetics, bioinformatics, biochemistry, microscopy, and structure-predicting artificial intelligence (AI) programs. In this study, we combined all this information with our own advanced cell-imaging technology (cryo-ET) to add another layer of understanding to how the Tad pilus machine is organized. This model suggests dozens of hypotheses to be tested in the future and represents the next step forward in understanding the structure and function of Tad pili.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Longitudinal Echo-Dynamic Assessment in Patients with Cardiogenic Shock A multi-center prospective study.
articles.journal: European heart journal. Acute cardiovascular care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In cardiogenic shock (CS), early hemodynamic changes are associated with in-hospital outcomes, but evidence on non-invasive assessment is limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of a comprehensive non-invasive hemodynamic assessment by echocardiography ("echo-dynamics") at presentation and 48 hours in CS.

METHODS: Consecutive CS patients at four Cardiac Intensive Care Units were prospectively enrolled. Echo-dynamics were obtained at baseline and 48 hours, including stroke volume index (SVi), cardiac index (CI), cardiac power output (CPO), estimated left atrial pressure (E/e'), systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (eSPAP) and right atrial pressure. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital mortality, left ventricular assist device implantation or heart transplantation.

RESULTS: Among 457 patients (37.9% acute myocardial infarction-CS, 42.9% SCAI CS stage ≥C, 28% mean ejection fraction), the primary outcome occurred in 30.0%. Each echo-dynamic parameter was associated with the outcome at both time points after adjustment for age, sex, CS etiology and severity. Changes from baseline to 48 hours showed a stepwise risk increase across improving, worsening, or persistently abnormal trajectories (p-trend<0.01). In fully adjusted models, baseline CPO<0.6 W (adj-OR 2.05, 95%CI 1.29-3.26) and eSPAP ≥35 mmHg (adj-OR 2.45, 95%CI 1.44-4.15) were associated with outcomes; at 48 hours, CPO<0.6 W (adj-OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.57-4.66), increased E/e' (adj-OR 1.86, 95%CI 1.09-3.15) and eSPAP ≥35 mmHg (adj-OR 1.90, 95%CI 1.12-3.22) remained independently associated. Results were consistent when adjusting for SCAI stage.

CONCLUSIONS: In CS, longitudinal echo-dynamic assessment identifies distinct trajectories with prognostic implications. Persistently low cardiac power, and elevated filling and pulmonary pressures showed the strongest association with adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Long-term feasibility of permanent antibiotic-impregnated PMMA cement cages for lumbosacral pyogenic spondylodiscitis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study presents a long-term follow-up case series of lumbosacral spondylodiscitis and proposes a therapeutic strategy.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Spondylodiscitis is a potentially destructive infection requiring surgical interventions. However, optimal surgical management approach remains controversial.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed patients with lumbosacral spondylodiscitis who underwent surgery at China Medical University Hospital between 2010 and 2024. Clinical data included demographics, risk factors, level affected, causative pathogens, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and disc height changes.

RESULTS: Nine patients, aged 42-85 (mean age 60), were included, with male predominance and a mean follow-up period exceeded 6 years. The ESR and CRP level decreased from admission to discharge, while postoperative disc height increased significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective case series demonstrates that staged posterior debridement with permanent antibiotic-impregnated PMMA cement cage followed by delayed percutaneous pedicle screw fixation is a feasible for selected patients with pyogenic lumbosacral spondylodiscitis. Favorable long-term outcomes suggest the potential safety and durability of this approach, although larger comparative studies are required to determine its efficacy.

articles.title: A disproportionality analysis of differences in hypersensitivity reactions to iodinated contrast media using the FDA adverse event reporting system (FAERS).
articles.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the disproportionality of hypersensitivity reactions (HSRs) associated with clinically used iodinated contrast media (ICMs) for enhanced patient safety.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We analyzed ICM-related HSR reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database between the Q1 of 2004 and the Q4 of 2024. Disproportionality analyses were performed to evaluate ICM-related HSR reporting odds ratio and to compare reporting rates of specific HSR subtypes across age, sex, and geographical subgroups.

RESULTS: Among 22,375,298 adverse event reports retrieved, 7,515 cases were identified as ICM-induced HSRs. All the studied ICMs were associated with over-reporting frequencies of HSRs, with iopromide showing the highest reporting odds ratio (ROR = 214.11, 95% confidence interval (CI) 197.07 - 232.64). Iopromide and ioversol (ROR = 104.58, 95% CI 93.31 - 117.22) were more likely associated with angioedema than other ICMs, particularly in males and the 45 - 65 age group. Iodixanol (ROR = 17.23, 95% CI 7.95 - 37.34) was associated with the largest disproportionality for severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs), while iodixanol, iopamidol (ROR = 11.90, 95% CI 9.13 - 15.52), and iohexol (ROR = 9.37, 95% CI 7.65 - 11.46) were more likely associated with SCAR than other ICMs, particularly in the 45 - 65 age group. Regarding anaphylactic shock, iopamidol (ROR = 117.18, 95% CI 103.13 - 133.14) and ioversol (ROR = 83.91, 95% CI 74.68 - 133.14) presented a higher disproportionality, especially in males and seniors aged > 65 years.

CONCLUSION: The disproportionality signal profiles of ICM-related HSRs vary significantly across specific agents and are influenced by age and sex.

articles.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.
articles.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline in an easy-to-use GUI. The pipeline combines existing tools with a rule-based algorithm that applies user-defined criteria to positions the variant caller reports as ambiguous and to the insertions and deletions (indels) it proposes, logging every decision with its statistics. The application works with both segmented and non-segmented viral genomes. Tested on eight influenza A isolates with Illumina-derived genomes, the consensus agreed at 99.97% of positions with each isolate's own genome as reference, and 36 of 37 resolved positions agreed. With close genomes as references, 99.98% of called positions agreed. However, agreement decreased as the reference diverged. Where the hemagglutinin cleavage site differed in length from the reference, indel adjudication reproduced it in four of five isolates, against none without it. In known mixtures, an ambiguity code was retained only when the minor allele exceeded ~40%. In essence, the refined sequence is a dominant consensus, not a record of within-sample variation. Therefore, DeGenRESOLVE facilitates offline, reproducible, and auditable sequencing analysis, reducing ambiguity in consensus generation and minimizing reproducibility errors.

articles.title: A LINE1-associated circular RNA circRLn1 modulates apple Alternaria blotch resistance by sequestering mdm-miR398b to tune ROS homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Alternaria blotch causes severe apple yield loss. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) participate in plant stress defense, but their antifungal pathways remain poorly understood. Retrotransposons modulate gene transcription; yet, Long interspersed nuclear element 1 (LINE1)-associated circRNA formation is rarely characterized in fruit trees. We combined circRNA sequencing, RNA pull-down, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), dual-luciferase assays, stable/transient transformation, and pathogen inoculation to dissect the biogenesis of a LINE1-associated circRNA, circRLn1, and its role in apple immunity against Alternaria blotch. circRLn1 overexpression restrained lesion expansion and pathogen growth under Alternaria alternata infection. Minigene assays suggest that LINE1-derived intronic inverted repeats promote circRLn1 production. Cytoplasmic circRLn1 may act as a sponge for mdm-miR398b, thereby de-repressing MdCSD1, MdCSD2 and MdCCS, elevating copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (Cu/Zn-SOD) activity to balance reactive oxygen species (ROS) and reduce oxidative injury. Functional dependency assays indicate that mdm-miR398b is required for circRLn1-mediated resistance. We identify a LINE1-circRLn1-mdm-miR398b-CSD/CCS regulatory module, revealing a potential retrotransposon-associated circRNA biogenesis pathway contributing to fungal immunity in apple.

articles.title: Systemic Type 2 Immune Responses During Acute Wheeze in Preschool Wheeze and School-Age Asthma.
The Role and Molecular Mechanism of E4BP4 in Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy via Targeting TRAIL.
articles.journal: The Kaohsiung journal of medical sciences
articles.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy (PCH) leads to heart failure. Tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL), a multifunctional cytokine, affects cardiovascular diseases. E4-binding protein 4 (E4BP4), implicated in cardiac stress, reportedly suppresses TRAIL. However, their role in PCH remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of E4BP4 in PCH and its underlying mechanism. Transverse aortic constriction (TAC) was used to induce PCH in mice. Echocardiography assessed cardiac function at 4, 6, 8, and 12 weeks post-surgery. Masson staining, immunofluorescence, qRT-PCR, and western blot were used to evaluate myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, and expression of E4BP4, TRAIL, and related receptors. Angiotensin II (Ang II)-induced hypertrophy was established in primary mouse cardiomyocytes. Cells were transfected with E4BP4 silencing or overexpression vectors. qRT-PCR, western blot, ELISA, phalloidin staining, and luciferase reporter assays measured E4BP4, TRAIL, receptors, hypertrophy/apoptosis markers, cell size, and E4BP4-TRAIL promoter binding. In hypertrophic mice, left ventricular ejection fraction and fractional shortening decreased, while left ventricular end-systolic diameter and mass increased, accompanied by aggravated myocardial fibrosis and abnormal hypertrophy markers. Ang II-induced cardiomyocytes showed increased cell area and abnormal expression of E4BP4, TRAIL, hypertrophy markers, and apoptosis-related proteins. Silencing E4BP4 exacerbated these changes, whereas overexpression reversed them. Luciferase assay confirmed that E4BP4 directly inhibited TRAIL promoter activity. In conclusion, E4BP4 mitigates hypertrophy and apoptosis by inhibiting TRAIL promoter activity and regulating TRAIL and its receptors, offering a potential therapeutic target for PCH.

articles.title: Patent Foramen Ovale and Cryptogenic Stroke: From 2D Assessment to 3D Morphological Risk Stratification.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Current guidelines for patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure rely on 2D echocardiography and clinical risk scores, assuming anatomical homogeneity. Three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D-TEE) enables detailed morphological assessment, but validated classification systems remain limited. This narrative review integrates evolving mechanistic and clinical evidence to critically evaluate the limitations of 2D assessment, contextualize the major randomized trial evidence base and guideline frameworks, and present a validated 3D morphological classification of PFO distinguishing funnel-type (wider right atrial inlet, narrower left atrial outlet) from cone-type anatomy. In a validation cohort (n = 95), funnel-type morphology was more prevalent in stroke patients (81.1% vs. 50%, p = 0.001) and independently predicted events (OR 6.47, 95% CI 1.28-32.77). Funnel-type morphology showed synergistic risk amplification with cardiovascular risk factors, reaching 100% event rates with smoking and dyslipidemia. These findings challenge the assumption that vascular risk factors argue against PFO causation and support a precision-based approach to patient selection for closure integrating 3D morphology with clinical profiling. Prospective multicenter validation and morphology-guided randomized trials are needed before routine guideline incorporation.

articles.title: Integrated Multi-Platform Profiling of Serum Bisphenol A and Circulating microRNAs With Comprehensive Biochemical Characterization Across Leukemia Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Leukemia accounts for ~3.1% of cancer burden in the world and there are no reliable noninvasive markers for subtyping and monitoring. The paper sought to characterize hematological, hepatic, renal, and cytokine profiles across the four major leukemia subtypes, quantify serum bisphenol A along with the profiling of three circulating microRNAs (miR-34a, miR-17, miR-155), and integrate bisphenol A and microRNAs data into a unified biomarker framework using correlation and ROC analyses. The study was a case-control study, with 100 participants (80 cases and 20 healthy controls). The expression level of microRNAs was quantified using the RT-qPCR technique (2-ΔΔCt method, normalized to miR-16-5p). Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis and binormal ROC analysis were used in the statistics. The biochemical characteristics of each of the subtypes were different: acute leukemias (ALL, AML) had severe cytopenias, coagulopathy, hepatic and renal impairment, and peak cytokine activity; CLL had extreme lymphocytosis and the highest β2-microglobulin; CML had marked leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, and elevated vitamin B12. Serum bisphenol A was significantly elevated in all subtypes versus controls (6.12-8.44 vs. 2.30 ng/mL, p < 0.0001), with ROC AUCs of 0.770-0.842. miR-34a was significantly suppressed in all the subtypes and miR-17 and miR-155 were constantly upregulated, with miRNA ROC AUCs ranging from 0.718 to 1.000 (91.7% excellent, ≥ 0.90). BPA was increased with IL-6, ferritin and LDH and decreased with miR-34a. A first cross-subtype, cross-platform analysis of all four leukemia subtypes suggests that a combined bisphenol A and miRNA signature is a promising noninvasive approach to leukemia detection, subtyping, and monitoring.

articles.title: RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention. Updated Evidence, Recommendations, Knowledge Gap Analysis, and Guidelines for Education in Veterinary CPR.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary emergency and critical care (San Antonio, Tex. : 2001)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To update the RECOVER CPR Preparedness and Prevention Domain's recommendations on education through a systematic review of relevant evidence and the creation and presentation of recommendations, and to identify and present critical knowledge gaps.

DESIGN: Standardized, systematic evaluation of literature pertinent to didactic, simulated, and in-clinic education regarding CPR following Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation methodology. Identified literature regarding prioritized questions in the Population-Intervention-Comparator-Outcome (PICO) format was reviewed independently by Evidence Evaluators, and findings were reconciled by Domain Chairs and Reassessment Campaign on Veterinary Resuscitation (RECOVER) Co-Chairs to arrive at recommendations. This process used a standardized Evidence Profile Worksheet for each PICO question including introduction, consensus on science, recommendations, justification of recommendations, and knowledge gaps sections. Recommendations underwent a 4-week comment period among international veterinary stakeholders prior to finalization. This 2026 RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention-Education paper summarizes recommendations for CPR education of veterinary professionals.

SETTING: Transdisciplinary, international collaboration in university, specialty, and emergency practice.

RESULTS: Seven PICO questions pertaining to CPR education were addressed in this section of the RECOVER CPR Preparedness and Prevention Domain. These seven PICO questions resulted in 14 recommendations. All recommendations are supported by very low-certainty evidence (11) or based on expert opinion (3).

CONCLUSIONS: This 2026 RECOVER CPR Guidelines: Preparedness and Prevention-Education update presents recommendations for individual and team CPR training to optimize veterinary resuscitation team readiness and, hopefully, improve patient outcomes. However, uncertainty remains regarding specific, ideal educational methods to optimize resuscitation team readiness, and high-priority knowledge gaps are presented to guide collaborative research in this area.

articles.title: Small-Tilt Automated Reconstruction (STAR): A Machine-Learning-Based Stereo Method for Realization of Real-Time 3D Microscopy Characterization.
articles.abstract: In situ scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) typically records two-dimensional projections, limiting interpretation of three-dimensional defect positions and orientations. We present Small-Tilt Automated Reconstruction (STAR), a machine-learning-enabled stereo framework for automated reconstruction of discrete features from views separated by small angular tilts (<5°). STAR integrates automated defect localization, tracking-based angular correspondence, video-frame interpolation, and small-angle double-tilt geometric reconstruction. Controlled benchmarks yielded a mean 3D position error of ∼0.51% of image width for synthetic loops and an average reconstruction error of ∼0.73% for latex spheres. Under assumed irradiated face-centered cubic crystallography, STAR correctly assigned habit-plane families for 97% of synthetic loops, with failures confined to the smallest {111} loops. Applied to post-irradiation images, STAR reconstructed cavity and dislocation-loop populations at computational throughputs of 0.50 and 1.18 reconstructions/s, respectively, providing depth-resolved statistics and loop-orientation distributions. STAR provides rapid, feature-level 3D reconstruction for discrete objects with prescribed geometries. Coupled with rapid stereo-pair acquisition, this computational framework supports time-resolved in situ and in operando defect characterization.

articles.title: Guidelines for Diagnosis, Reporting and Management of Intraductal Papillary Neoplasm of the Bile Duct (IPNB): Recommendations of Bangkok Consensus Meeting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are no international consensus guidelines on IPNB.

METHOD: An international-multidisciplinary panel performed a critical appraisal of the literature and used a two-round Delphi process to evaluate 24 critical clinical questions, incorporating community feedback from a dedicated 2025 A-PHPBA meeting session in Bangkok.

RESULTS: Salient aspects of the recommendations: (1) IPNB is analogous to intracholecystic papillary neoplasm (ICPNs)/intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMNs), ranging from innocuous cystic lesions to papillary in situ carcinomas to invasive carcinomas. (2) Possible etiologic factors like stones, parasites, PSC, and PBM/choledochal cysts should be assessed in every case. (3) All nonmetastatic IPNBs are candidates for oncologic resection, preferably along with lymph node dissection. (4) Pre- and intraoperative assessment for multifocality is important. (5) Liver transplant is a consideration in selected cases. (6) Individualized IPNB-focused synoptic pathology reports were devised for use. (7) For invasive IPNBs, adjuvant treatment should follow standard cholangiocarcinoma protocols. (8) Follow-up should mirror main-duct IPMN protocols, adjusted for invasion and margin status. (9) For isolated IPNB recurrence, resection or transplant is advisable; if infeasible or metastatic, consider ablative and systemic therapies. (10) These recommendations are also applicable to IOPN/ITPN but with subtle differences.

CONCLUSION: These recommendations should aid in cross-national standardized classification, diagnosis, reporting, and management of IPNBs, and serve as a launching pad for further studies.

articles.title: Enhanced antihypertensive efficacy of selenium-enriched black tea is associated with galloylated catechin enrichment: integrating chemical profiling, molecular modeling, and animal studies.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Selenium-enriched tea has been reported to exhibit enhanced antihypertensive efficacy; however, the key bioactive constituents and their molecular targets remain undefined. To elucidate the relationship between selenium-induced compositional alterations and antihypertensive effects, we employed a high-salt diet-induced hypertensive rat model combined with chemical profiling, network pharmacology, and molecular dynamics simulations.

RESULTS: Selenium biofortification of the tea plant increased the contents of galloylated catechins (epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) and epicatechin gallate (ECG)) in the resulting black tea. In hypertensive rats, selenium-enriched black tea (Se-BT) exhibited superior antioxidative, anti-inflammatory, and antihypertensive effects compared with conventional black tea (BT), increasing serum endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) activity and nitric oxide (NO) levels (+39.32% and +12.20%, respectively, compared with BT). Network pharmacology identified galloylated catechins (EGCG, ECG, and gallocatechin gallate (GCG)) as major bioactive constituents associated with hypertension, and KEGG (Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes) enrichment pointed to pathways converging on eNOS-mediated NO signaling. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations suggested that galloylated catechins preferentially occupy a common binding pocket adjacent to the eNOS BH4-binding region and that EGCG, as the representative galloylated catechin, maintained a stable binding mode throughout the simulation.

CONCLUSION: Selenium enrichment enhances the antihypertensive efficacy of black tea, primarily through the accumulation of galloylated catechins. These findings suggest that the stable binding of galloylated catechins to eNOS may provide a structural basis for the experimentally observed enhancement of eNOS activity and NO production. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: Editorial: Alcohol Use Quantification by Phosphatidylethanol in Large Steatotic Liver Disease Cohorts.
Inulin-Type Fructans: Structural Determinants, Gut Microbiota-Host Crosstalk, and Advanced Oral Delivery for Disease Modulation.
articles.abstract: Inulin-type fructans (ITFs) are predominantly β(2 → 1)-linked fructans that resist digestion by human enzymes in the upper gastrointestinal tract and are widely studied as prebiotic fibers. However, ITF should not be regarded as a single, fixed exposure. Plant source, degree of polymerization, chain-length profile, solubility, and processing history influence gastrointestinal persistence, microbial accessibility, and fermentation kinetics. These features are also relevant to oral delivery. Longer-chain inulin can contribute to scaffold formation and hydration behavior, whereas short-chain fructooligosaccharides generally lack comparable matrix-forming capacity on their own. In this review, we explore ITFs as structurally defined gut exposures rather than a single ingredient. We connect microbial utilization and short-chain fatty acid production with bile acid remodeling, barrier function, immune responses, and endocrine-metabolic signaling. Evidence in obesity, insulin resistance, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, type 2 diabetes, and intestinal inflammation is assessed by distinguishing changes in disease-related markers from established therapeutic effects. We also review inulin-based nanoparticles, hydrogels, colon-targeted systems, and hybrid platforms as strategies for controlling release, intestinal residence, and local payload exposure. This structure-based perspective connects nutritional ITF research with inulin-based oral delivery while keeping disease-related claims within the limits of current evidence.

articles.title: International Consensus on Clinical Trial Endpoints in Autosomal Dominant Osteopetrosis.
articles.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
articles.abstract: Autosomal Dominant Osteopetrosis (ADO) is a disorder of mineral metabolism caused by gene defects that impair osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and result in diffuse skeletal sclerosis and increased bone mineral density. There is no approved medical therapy for ADO; however, therapies are being developed that hasten the need for clinical trial readiness. A key part of this process is the development of a core set of endpoints for inclusion in both natural history and interventional studies for ADO. To identify these endpoints, we used a modified Delphi approach to reach consensus among panelists on prioritization of 92 candidate endpoints developed from a detailed literature search and panelist nomination. The international panel was comprised of 11 physicians from four countries (Canada, Finland, France, and the United States) with expertise in ADO plus clinical trials in metabolic bone diseases. After three rounds of anonymous voting, with a structured discussion prior to the final vote, complete consensus (100% agreement) was reached for prioritization of 1) imaging using dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry and plain radiographs, 2) patient-reported outcome measures of pain and global impression of change, 3) blood-based biomarkers of bone metabolism, and 4) clinical outcomes such as fracture and osteomyelitis. We recommend that the prioritized endpoints described in more detail in this manuscript be uniformly incorporated into therapeutic clinical trials and natural history studies in ADO. Consistent evaluation of endpoints in both natural history studies and investigational therapies, with appropriate standardization of the underlying methodologies, will facilitate comparison among therapeutic approaches and support the use of historical control data, ultimately leading to acceleration of therapeutic development for patients with ADO.

articles.title: Inositol for infertile women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
authors: Supported by the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Review Group
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: This is an update of a previously published review. Women with infertility may use adjunctive therapies to improve reproductive outcomes. Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol are dietary supplements widely available and commonly used by women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS; renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in May 2026). The use of inositol for women with PCOS and infertility is based on proposed effects on insulin sensitivity and ovarian function. In clinical practice, myo-inositol is frequently prescribed for women with PCOS undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination or before in vitro fertilisation (IVF). However, the quality and certainty of the evidence supporting this practice remains unclear. This review aimed to assess the benefits and harms of inositol (including myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol) in women with PCOS experiencing infertility.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the benefits and harms of inositol oral supplementation for reproductive outcomes among women with polycystic ovary syndrome experiencing infertility.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL (which includes trial registries), the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Specialised Register, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, AMED, and Epistemonikos to 10 November 2025. We also checked reference lists and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any type, dose, or combination of oral inositol versus placebo, no treatment, or another active intervention in women with PCOS and infertility. Trials that compared different types of inositol were also eligible.

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were live birth and any adverse event (including miscarriage, multiple pregnancy, and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS)), as reported by trial investigators. Our important outcomes were clinical pregnancy and gestational diabetes.

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two review authors independently selected eligible studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. We pooled studies using a fixed-effect model, and calculated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We assessed the overall certainty of evidence by applying GRADE. The primary analyses of all review outcomes were restricted to studies at low risk of selection bias. We also conducted sensitivity analyses including all studies.

INCLUDED STUDIES: This review update included 21 studies involving 1634 women with PCOS and infertility who were trying to become pregnant. Sixteen studies and 1481 participants are new to this review. Studies took place in Iran, India, Italy, Albania, Germany, and Vietnam. All women included in these studies were receiving usual preconception care. All studies that met our eligibility criteria and had data for the outcomes of interest investigated myo-inositol.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: We considered the certainty of the evidence to be low and very low, downgraded mainly due to indirectness and imprecision. The primary analysis included five studies. Myo-inositol compared to placebo or no treatment in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination One study with 120 women evaluated this comparison. As the certainty of the evidence was very low for all outcomes of interest, we are unsure whether myo-inositol, compared with no treatment, has an effect on live birth (OR 3.45, 95% CI 1.63 to 7.32), miscarriage (OR 1.27, 95% CI 0.32 to 4.99), multiple pregnancy (OR 5.36, 95% CI 0.61 to 47.36), OHSS (OR 11.99, 95% CI 0.65 to 221.86), clinical pregnancy (OR 3.45, 95% CI 1.63 to 7.32), or gestational diabetes (OR 1.73, 95% CI 0.39 to 7.58). Myo-inositol compared to placebo or no treatment in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing in vitro fertilisation We are uncertain whether myo-inositol, compared with no treatment, has an effect on live birth (OR 2.42, 95% CI 0.75 to 7.83; 2 studies, 84 women; very low-certainty evidence) and miscarriage (OR 2.09, 95% CI 0.18 to 24.61; 2 studies, 84 women; very low-certainty evidence). The analysis for multiple pregnancy included one trial with no events in either arm (34 women; very low-certainty evidence). Myo-inositol may increase clinical pregnancy rates slightly compared with no treatment (OR 2.34, 95% CI 1.07 to 5.11; 3 studies, 164 women; low-certainty evidence). No studies reported OHSS or gestational diabetes. Myo-inositol compared to another insulin-sensitising agent (metformin) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing in vitro fertilisation One study with 102 women evaluated this comparison. As the certainty of the evidence was very low for all reported outcomes of interest, we are unsure whether myo-inositol, compared with metformin, has an effect on live birth (OR 3.03, 95% CI 1.12 to 8.17), miscarriage (OR 2.17, 95% CI 0.38 to 12.43), OHSS (OR 0.37, 95% CI 0.12 to 1.14), or clinical pregnancy (OR 3.19, 95% CI 1.28 to 7.95). The study did not report multiple pregnancy or gestational diabetes.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: In light of the very low-certainty evidence available from one study, we are unsure whether myo-inositol, compared with no treatment, has an effect on live birth, miscarriage, multiple pregnancy, OHSS, clinical pregnancy, or gestational diabetes in women with PCOS and infertility undergoing ovulation induction/intrauterine insemination. In studies comparing myo-inositol with no treatment in women undergoing IVF, the certainty of the evidence was very low for live birth, miscarriage, and multiple pregnancy. Low-certainty evidence from three of these studies indicated there may be a slight increase in clinical pregnancy rates for women taking myo-inositol compared with those receiving no treatment. In light of the very low-certainty evidence available from one study, we are unsure whether myo-inositol, compared with metformin, has an effect on live birth, miscarriage, OHSS, or clinical pregnancy in women undergoing IVF.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol (2016) available at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012378. Previous review (2018) available at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012378.pub2.

articles.title: The New Kid on the Block: A Retrospective Multicenter Real-World Experience with Maribavir for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Pediatric Transplant and Cellular Therapy Recipients.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract: This multicenter retrospective case series characterizes maribavir (MBV) use for cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in 62 immunocompromised children treated at 18 United States centers from 2015 through 2024. The most common indications for use were suspected antiviral resistance (45.2%), documented resistance (19.4%), and lack of appropriate alternative agents (11.3%). Among 59 participants with detectable CMV DNAemia when their first course began, 66.1% had complete response, 5.1% had partial response, 27.1% had no response, and one relapsed before treatment cessation. CMV DNAemia ≥50,000 IU/mL was associated with a lower response rate, and MBV resistance was identified in four participants. Across 70 total treatment episodes, 21.4% reported adverse events and discontinuation attributed to MBV occurred in 5.7%. Concomitant use of MBV and other anti-CMV directed medications occurred frequently. Although efficacy results are limited by the observational design, these results highlight real-world pediatric experience and safety.

articles.title: 3-Day Artemether-Lumefantrine Regimen in Non-immune Adults with Imported Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria: An 11-Year Retrospective Study (MALARIA3).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The standard artemether-lumefantrine regimen for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria comprises six doses over three days. Reports of late recurrence in non-endemic settings have prompted recommendations for longer regimens despite limited direct comparative evidence. We described early parasite clearance and 42-day recurrence after 3-day therapy in a selected cohort of adults without a documented previous malaria episode.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre cohort study of adults with imported uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, no documented history of previous malaria, and initial treatment with oral artemether-lumefantrine at Geneva University Hospitals between 2015 and 2025. The primary outcome was asexual parasitaemia at 72 ± 8 hours. Secondary outcomes included parasite-clearance time, parasitological recurrence within 42 days, hospitalisation, intensive care unit admission, and mortality.

RESULTS: Fifty-three patients were included. Median baseline parasitaemia was 0.2% (IQR, 0.05-0.5; range, 0.001-7.5). At 72 ± 8 hours, 51 of 52 evaluable patients had cleared parasitaemia (98.1%; 95% CI, 89.9-99.7), whereas one remained parasitaemic (1.9%; 95% CI, 0.3-10.1). Median parasite-clearance time was two days (IQR, 2-3). Day 2 was the most frequent clearance day, accounting for 24 of 53 patients (45.3%), and 36 of 53 (67.9%) had cleared by the end of day 2. Recurrence within 42 days occurred in 2 of 49 evaluable patients (4.1%; 95% CI, 1.1-13.7). No intensive care admissions or deaths occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort of non-immune adults with imported uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, standard 3-day artemether-lumefantrine achieved rapid parasite clearance, with only one day-3-positive patient and two documented late recurrences. These findings provide clinically relevant real-world evidence supporting the continued evaluation of the standard regimen and question whether its routine upfront extension to 5 days is warranted for all non-immune patients.

articles.title: Chronotype, Mediterranean diet adherence, and FINDRISK score in adults: A cross-sectional mediation analysis.
articles.abstract: Chronotype has been linked to both dietary behavior and diabetes risk, but whether Mediterranean diet adherence statistically accounts for part of the association between chronotype and diabetes risk screening scores remains insufficiently characterized. In this cross-sectional study of 2,302 adults recruited via snowball sampling, chronotype was assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ-19), Mediterranean diet adherence using the Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS-14), and diabetes risk using the Finnish Diabetes Risk Score (FINDRISK). Multiple linear regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis examined associations among chronotype, dietary adherence, and FINDRISK score, adjusting for age, BMI, and sex. MEDAS-14 scores increased progressively from evening-type to intermediate-type to morning-type participants (5.5 ± 1.4, 5.9 ± 1.5, and 6.4 ± 1.5, respectively; p < 0.001). After adjustment, higher MEQ-19 score was associated with higher MEDAS-14 score (β = 0.030, p < 0.001) and lower FINDRISK score (β = -0.021, p = 0.033), and higher MEDAS-14 score was independently associated with lower FINDRISK score (β = -0.162, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis identified a small but statistically significant indirect association between MEQ-19 and FINDRISK scores through MEDAS-14 (ACME = -0.005, 95% CI [-0.008, -0.002], p = 0.002). A small indirect association between chronotype and FINDRISK score through Mediterranean diet adherence was observed. Given the cross-sectional design and conceptual overlap between MEDAS-14 and FINDRISK, this finding should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in longitudinal studies using outcomes independent of the proposed mediator.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Supracutaneous Locking Compression Plating versus Conventional External Fixation in Open Tibial Fractures: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Open tibial fractures pose significant management challenges due to the bone's subcutaneous location, limited soft-tissue coverage, and high risk of infection. While conventional external fixators (EF) provide rapid damage-control stabilization, they are associated with pin-tract infections, bulky hardware, and delayed union. Supracutaneous locking compression plating (SLCP) offers a low-profile, biologically friendly alternative.

AIM: To compare functional and radiological outcomes, union times, and complications between open tibial fractures treated with EF versus supracutaneous plates.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This randomized controlled trial evaluated 36 patients (aged 18-70 years) with open tibial fractures (Gustilo-Anderson Types I-IIIB) allocated into Group A (External Fixator, n = 18) and Group B (Supracutaneous Plate, n = 18). Serial clinical and radiological follow-ups were conducted at 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, 9 months, and 12 months postoperatively. Radiological healing was tracked using the Radiographic Union Score for Tibia (RUST) until complete cortical bridging was achieved while functional outcome was evaluated using the duration to achieve full weight-bearing ambulation and return to preinjury occupational activity.

RESULTS: Mean radiological union was significantly faster in the supracutaneous plate group (4.11 ± 0.76 months) than the external fixator group (5.39 ± 1.20 months, P = 0.001). Group B patients also returned to preinjury activity significantly earlier (5.28 ± 0.58 vs. 6.44 ± 0.98 months, P < 0.0001). Serial RUST scores demonstrated earlier cortical consolidation in Group B (P < 0.0001).
