CONCLUSION: Supracutaneous plating achieves significantly faster fracture union and earlier functional recovery with a low complication rate, serving as an effective alternative to traditional EF.

articles.title: Prevalence of Japanese Encephalitis in Pediatric Patients with Positive Vaccination History among Acute Encephalitis Syndrome Cases at a Tertiary Care Center in Ranchi, Jharkhand: A Retrospective Observational Cross sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) remains a leading cause of pediatric neuro-morbidity in India. Japanese Encephalitis (JE) is a major viral contributor. Despite mass immunization, breakthrough infections present an emerging public health challenge.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of JE among vaccinated pediatric AES patients, evaluate real-world vaccine effectiveness, and identify risk factors for breakthrough infections.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective observational cross-sectional study at Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences, Ranchi, analyzing 267 pediatric patients (aged 3-18 years) admitted with AES over 12 months. Diagnosis was confirmed using cerebrospinal fluid MAC-ELISA or serum MAC-ELISA for JE-specific IgM antibodies and brain magnetic resonance imaging.

RESULTS: Among 267 enrolled cases, 189 (70.8%) had documented JE vaccination. JE positivity was significantly lower among vaccinated than unvaccinated children (24.3% vs. 46.2%; P < 0.001), representing a 47.4% relative reduction in JE prevalence among AES admissions. JE prevalence significantly increased with time elapsed since vaccination (14.3% at <1 year vs. 40.0% at >5 years; P = 0.012). In multivariable logistic regression, time since vaccination ≥3 years (adjusted odds ratios [aOR] = 2.84, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.24-6.51; P = 0.014), proximity to rice fields (<500 m) (aOR = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.02-6.42; P = 0.045), and monsoon season admission (aOR = 3.18, 95% CI: 1.35-7.48; P = 0.008) were independent risk factors for breakthrough infections. Vaccinated JE-positive cases had higher mortality (21.7% vs. 10.5%; P = 0.045) and neurological sequelae rates (52.2% vs. 33.6%; P = 0.026) than vaccinated JE-negative controls.

CONCLUSION: Among hospitalized pediatric AES admissions, a notable hospital-based breakthrough prevalence of 24.3% was observed, driven primarily by waning immunity over time and intense environmental exposure. Implementing booster schedules at -year intervals and integrated vector control are urgently needed.

articles.title: Electroconvulsive Therapy in a Patient with Schizophrenia and Coexisting Right Frontoparietal Neoplastic Lesion: A Case Report with Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Co-occurrence of primary brain tumors and schizophrenia presents diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) has historically been considered contraindicated in patients with intracranial lesions. A 27-year-old female with an 11-year history of schizophrenia presented with worsening psychosis, irritability, and aggression. She was previously diagnosed with diffuse midline glioma, which was inoperable and treated with temozolomide. Due to partial response to amisulpride, she received four sessions of modified ECT (mECT) following a multidisciplinary evaluation ruling out intracranial hypertension. The treatment was well-tolerated with rapid reduction in psychotic symptoms, agitation, and aggression, without neurological deterioration or seizure-related complications. Thus, this case demonstrates that mECT can be safely administered in select patients with schizophrenia and co-occurring high-grade glioma, challenging historical contraindications. Early neuroimaging is essential in treatment-resistant or atypical psychosis to exclude underlying structural pathology.

articles.title: The Landscape of Interventional Clinical Trials in Hairy Cell Leukemia.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hairy cell leukemia (HCL) is a rare chronic B-cell lymphoproliferative malignancy characterized by the accumulation of abnormal mature B-lymphocytes in the bone marrow, spleen, and peripheral blood. Although HCL accounts for approximately 2% of all leukemias, clinical trials are essential for advancing therapeutic strategies and addressing unmet clinical needs.

AIM: To analyze the landscape of interventional clinical trials in HCL registered between 1997 and 2026 and evaluate variations in trial characteristics based on intervention type, trial phase, study design, and funding source.

METHODOLOGY: A retrospective registry-based study was conducted using data from the U.S. National Library of Medicine ClinicalTrials.gov database. Interventional clinical trials related to HCL registered between 1997 and 2026 were included. Variables analyzed included participant characteristics, study design (allocation and masking), intervention type, trial phase, and funding source. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize trial characteristics, and temporal trends were assessed across predefined time periods.

RESULTS: A total of 26 interventional clinical trials related to HCL were included in the final analysis. Drug-based interventions constituted most studies (n = 23; 88.46%), followed by biological interventions (n = 2; 7.69%). Most trials were conducted in Phase 2 and utilized a nonrandomized design. National Institutes of Health funding represented the largest funding source (n = 12; 46.15%), whereas industry-sponsored trials accounted for a smaller proportion. Temporal analysis demonstrated a relatively stable trend in clinical trial activity over time, with limited diversification of intervention types and no significant changes in study design characteristics across study periods.

CONCLUSION: The clinical trial landscape of HCL demonstrates relatively stable trends in intervention strategies and study design. The limited trials on novel therapeutic approaches reveal ongoing research gaps, emphasizing the necessity for extensive investigation of emerging treatments to enhance the evidence base for managing HCL.

articles.title: Ultrasound Elastography in Fatty Liver Disease: A Noninvasive Assessment of Hepatic Fibrosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fatty liver disease, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), has become one of the most common chronic liver disorders worldwide because of the increasing prevalence of obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and metabolic syndrome. Progressive hepatic fibrosis is the most important predictor of adverse outcomes, including cirrhosis and liver failure. Early diagnosis and staging of fibrosis are, therefore, essential for timely management. Although liver biopsy remains the reference standard, it is invasive, costly, and associated with potential complications. Ultrasound elastography has emerged as a reliable non-invasive imaging technique for assessment of liver stiffness and fibrosis.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the role of ultrasound shear wave elastography in assessing hepatic fibrosis in patients with fatty liver disease.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This time-limited observational cross-sectional study included 499 adult patients with ultrasonographical diagnosed fatty liver disease. Shear wave elastography was performed using a standardized protocol with measurements obtained from the right hepatic lobe through an intercostal approach. Three valid acquisitions were recorded for each patient, and average liver stiffness values were calculated in kilopascals. Fibrosis grading was categorized according to METAVIR-equivalent scores. Clinical variables such as age, sex, obesity, and diabetes were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Liver stiffness values showed a progressive increase with worsening fibrosis stage. A substantial proportion of patients demonstrated mild-to-moderate fibrosis, while a smaller group had advanced fibrosis. Patients with obesity and diabetes had significantly higher liver stiffness values compared with those without metabolic risk factors. Elastography effectively differentiated early from advanced fibrosis stages.

CONCLUSION: Ultrasound elastography is a safe, rapid, and noninvasive modality for evaluating hepatic fibrosis in fatty liver disease. It provides valuable quantitative information for fibrosis staging, risk stratification, and follow-up, and may reduce the need for liver biopsy in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Menarche in Young-Onset Type 1 Diabetes: Data from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) Registry.
articles.abstract: Aim Data on age at menarche in youth with type 1 diabetes (T1D) remain limited. We examined factors associated with age at menarche and longitudinal trajectories of insulin dose, glycaemia, and body mass index (BMI) before and after menarche in an Australasian cohort. Method Longitudinal sociodemographic and clinical data for females with T1D and a documented menarche date were extracted from the Australasian Diabetes Data Network (ADDN) registry. Generalised estimating equations were used to examine factors associated with age at menarche (< vs. ≥ cohort median age), including Index of Relative Socioeconomic Disadvantage score, T1D duration, total daily insulin dose/kg (TDD/kg), HbA1c, insulin pump use, and BMI standard deviation score (SDS). Trajectories of TDD/kg, HbA1c, and BMI SDS across nine clinically defined pre- and post-menarche time intervals were analysed using linear mixed models with time modelled as a categorical fixed effect, accounting for repeated measures and within-subject correlation. Results Overall, 601 females from nine centres were included. Median (IQR) age at menarche was 12.6 (12.0, 13.3) years. Later menarche was associated with longer T1D duration (B = 0.10; 95% CI 0.01-0.19; p = 0.04), lower TDD/kg (-1.20; -2.00 to -0.42; p = 0.003), higher HbA1c (0.21; 0.02-0.39; p = 0.03), and lower BMI SDS (-0.48; -0.79 to -0.17; p = 0.002). TDD/kg increased in the pre-menarcheal period, peaking around menarche then declining; BMI SDS increased progressively from pre- to post-menarche; and HbA1c rose over time from pre- to post-menarche (all p < 0.001), demonstrating distinct trajectories. Conclusions Increasing insulin requirements preceded menarche, while HbA1c and BMI SDS continued to rise during the post-menarcheal period. These findings suggest that metabolic changes associated with pubertal maturation extend beyond menarche itself and highlight the importance of considering pubertal progression in diabetes care and anticipatory management during adolescence.

articles.title: Unrecognized Drivers of Hyperkalemia: The Synergistic Impact of Statins and High Salt Intake in At-Risk Patients.
articles.abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who are treated with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibitors face a high risk of hyperkalemia, frequently necessitating the withdrawal of these foundational cardiorenal therapies. While the risk of RAAS blockade is well known, many hyperkalemic events remain unexplained despite dietary restriction and stable kidney function. We propose a novel hypothesis regarding an unrecognized etiology for hyperkalemia in this vulnerable cohort: the synergistic suppression of the adrenal axis by ubiquitous outpatient variables. A standard high-sodium Western diet suppresses renin and Angiotensin II, while lipophilic statins inhibit adrenal cholesterol availability and Rac1-mediated signaling, significantly crippling aldosterone synthesis. Furthermore, statins dismantle the kidney's aldosterone-independent rescue mechanisms by inhibiting the mTOR signaling pathway. Together, these factors induce a profound "hidden hypoaldosteronism". In healthy individuals, high distal tubular flow and WNK kinase adaptations trigger a mechanical rescue via calcium-activated K+ (BK) channels. However, in advanced CKD, diminished nephron mass and tubulointerstitial fibrosis dismantle this flow-dependent safety valve. Crucially, the statin-induced pharmacological blockade starves the adrenal gland of essential substrates, actively blunting "aldosterone breakthrough", the patient's final compensatory defense against rising serum K+. The convergence of high dietary salt and lipophilic statins creates a dangerous "second hit" that leaves the failing kidney defenseless against K+ loads, such as in the "à la croque-au-sel" phenomenon. If validated, this hypothesized mechanism warrants enhanced metabolic monitoring and consideration of transitioning at-risk patients to hydrophilic statins to preserve residual aldosterone breakthrough capacity.

articles.title: Clarifying IDSA's Position on Antibiotic Timing in Sepsis: Distinguishing Hospital Strategies from Clinical Guidance.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

articles.title: Letter: Commentary on "The FAITHS2 Model Predicts Functional Disability in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke".
Audit of procedural sedation in a remote Australian hospital 2010 - 2021.
articles.abstract: Procedural sedation is commonly provided in rural hospitals; however, there is little published safety data. The authors conducted a retrospective audit of anaesthetic records from 2010 to 2021 of procedural sedation in a remote hospital in South Australia. The data were collected from 1912 cases, which were provided mainly for gastroenterology procedures in day case theatre and emergency department settings. Sedation was provided by a general practitioner anaesthetist giving boluses of fentanyl, midazolam and propofol. All patients were low risk (American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status 1-3). There were few anaesthetic problems and no mortality during sedation or in the recovery area. The most common problem was desaturation requiring airway support and oxygen, and occurred in 2% of cases. Procedural sedation was practiced safely in this remote setting.

articles.title: Freshwater drowning with profound hypofibrinogenaemia and refractory vasoplegic shock.
articles.abstract: We present a challenging case of freshwater drowning complicated by profound hypofibrinogenaemia and refractory vasoplegic shock in a 39-year-old male admitted following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The constellation of physiological and laboratory abnormalities initially precluded a unifying diagnosis. The haemolysis, hyper-fibrinolysis and disseminated intravascular coagulation observed in our patient were likely sequelae of freshwater drowning and cardiac arrest. The refractory vasoplegic shock necessitated rescue off-label administration of hydroxocobalamin, resulting in restoration of haemodynamic stability.

articles.title: Perioperative methadone: Clinical use and knowledge among Australian anaesthetists.
articles.abstract: Intravenous methadone has re-emerged as a perioperative analgesic, yet uncertainty persists regarding its optimal use. Variation in clinician practice and interpretation of pharmacological principles may influence its safe and effective application. We conducted a mixed-methods survey-based study within a national anaesthesia educational programme (ADVANCE). A voluntary, anonymous pre-presentation clinician survey was distributed to predominantly Australian anaesthetists to characterise methadone use, dosing strategies, adjunct prescribing and patient selection. Real-time audience polling during the educational session assessed clinician responses to pharmacology-based and clinical decision-making scenarios. Survey and polling datasets were analysed independently using descriptive statistics. A total of 726 clinicians completed the survey. Overall, 50.6% (n = 367) of respondents reported using methadone. Among users (n = 367), practice varied widely across surgical contexts and dosing strategies, including weight-based, fixed and procedure-dependent approaches. Concurrent administration of additional opioids and central nervous system depressants was common (86.1%). Clinicians reported avoiding methadone in specific patient groups, most frequently frail patients, those with prolonged QT interval, or obstructive sleep apnoea. Polling responses demonstrated variability in clinician interpretation of pharmacological principles, particularly regarding timing of central effects. Perioperative methadone use is characterised by substantial variation in uptake, dosing and adjunct prescribing. Variability in clinician responses relative to pharmacological reference data, combined with frequent co-administration of additional opioids and sedatives, highlights potential areas for targeted education and institutional safeguards to support safe implementation.

articles.title: Multimorbidity, Mental Health, and Quality of Life in Endometriosis: Insights from the NIH All of Us Program.
articles.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic, multifactorial disease affecting around 10% of women worldwide and is often accompanied by systemic inflammation, comorbidities, and reduced quality of life. Using the All of Us database, we conducted a large-scale analysis to characterize demographic and clinical features of women with endometriosis and evaluate the impact of inflammatory conditions and mental health conditions. To conduct these studies we created two cohorts; cohort A aimed to establish associations between inflammatory conditions and endometriosis, while cohort B was used to study the impact of endometriosis on mental health and quality of life outcomes. In cohort A, a history of inflammatory conditions (asthma, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), or migraine) was associated with higher odds of incident endometriosis (adjusted odds ratio = 3.06, 95% CI: 2.92-3.20, p < 0.0001). Women with inflammatory comorbidities were diagnosed at a younger age (42.9 ± 11.2 vs. 44.9 ± 12.1 years), suggesting earlier recognition or onset. In cohort B, participants with endometriosis had higher odds of EHR-documented depression (age-adjusted odds ratio = 2.29, 95% CI: 2.17-2.41) and anxiety (age-adjusted odds ratio = 2.44, 95% CI: 2.32-2.57). Participants with endometriosis also reported poorer general health, physical health, mental health, social satisfaction, and overall quality of life, with all five associations remaining statistically significant after adjustment for age, race, ethnicity, and household income (all p < 0.001). These findings underscore the interplay among systemic inflammation, early disease manifestations, and psychosocial burden in endometriosis, offering population-level insights to inform early detection strategies and promote equitable, multidisciplinary care for affected women.

articles.title: Safety, Gastrointestinal Tolerance, and Digestibility of Lamb Protein Yeast in Healthy Adult Cats.
articles.abstract: Lamb protein yeast (LPY) is a novel protein source produced using precision fermentation and may be used as an alternative protein ingredient in pet foods. The objective of this study was to assess the safety, gastrointestinal tolerance, and apparent total tract digestibility (ATTD) of extruded feline foods containing LPY and to evaluate its effects on serum chemistry, hematology, urine characteristics, and fecal characteristics, metabolites, microbiota, and immunoglobulin A concentrations of healthy adult cats. Thirty-six adult domestic shorthair cats were used in a randomized design with allocation balanced for sex, BW, and age. After a 2-wk acclimation phase, when all cats were fed the control food containing 0% LPY, cats were assigned to one of four treatments and fed for 26 wk: control or foods containing 15%, 22.5%, or 30% LPY. Food intake, body weight, and body condition scores were measured and blood, urine, and fecal samples were collected throughout the study. ATTD was assessed after 5 wk of food consumption. Data were analyzed using the Mixed Models procedure of SAS 9.4, with P < 0.05 accepted as significant differences and P < 0.10 accepted as trends. All foods were well accepted, and food intake, body weight, and body condition score were not different among treatments. No clinically relevant changes in serum chemistry, hematology, or urine parameters were observed. At wk 5, fecal scores were greater in cats fed the 15% and 30% LPY foods than in control cats, but fecal dry matter was not different. At wk 26, fecal scores were greater in cats fed all LPY-containing foods than those fed the control food, and fecal dry matter was lower in cats fed the 15% and 22.5% LPY foods. The ATTD of dry matter, organic matter, and nitrogen-free extract was greater in cats fed LPY-containing foods. The ATTD of protein was lower in cats fed the 30% LPY food and the ATTD of fat was lower in cats fed the 22.5% and 30% LPY foods, but digestibility values remained high for all treatments. Fecal butyrate and total branched-chain fatty acid concentrations were greater in cats fed LPY-containing foods. Treatments also affected the fecal microbiota community, with differences in alpha and beta diversity metrics and the relative abundances of several bacterial phyla and genera being observed. Overall, extruded foods containing up to 30% LPY were well tolerated by healthy adult cats, and no safety concerns were identified under the conditions of this study.

articles.title: Identifying important behavioural change techniques to deliver in communication partner training for people with cognitive-communication disorder following acquired brain injury: A national e-Delphi of UK speech and language therapists.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo establish consensus regarding the behaviour change techniques considered most important when delivering communication partner training to people with acquired brain injury and their communication partners.DesignThree-round e-Delphi. Participants rated 86 behaviour change techniques linked to 16 mechanisms-of-action using a 9-point Likert scale. Consensus for techniques was defined as >70% agreement. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, latent content and sentiment analysis.SettingUK clinical practice in acquired brain injury rehabilitation.ParticipantsSpeech and language therapists working with people with acquired brain injury.ResultsA total of 118 speech and language therapists participated in Round 1, 90 participated in each of Rounds 2 and 3, and 81 completed all three rounds. Consensus was reached on 80 behaviour change technique-to-mechanism of action links, representing 47 distinct techniques. Ratings did not differ by years' experience or clinical setting. Most agreement (>90%) was linked to setting goals, practising skills and goal feedback. Qualitative comments were largely positive (67%), especially for goal setting and skills practice. Therapist reservations focused on material and monetary rewards, while therapist comments on feedback techniques underlined a need for individualised and tailored training.ConclusionsThis is the first UK e-Delphi of speech and language therapists in acquired brain injury. Behaviour change theory provided a framework to identify key techniques, highlighting the complexity of training. Analysis revealed diverse attitudes and areas for further consideration. Consensus on the importance of communication partner training techniques offers an opportunity to develop a clinically relevant programme with potential for uptake in clinical practice.

articles.title: Intelligent detection of chronic kidney disease using machine learning: A comparative evaluation with nested cross-validation.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is progressive, and early diagnosis improves outcomes.ObjectiveWe assessed how reliably routine clinical and laboratory variables identify CKD, and whether differences between common classifiers exceed the sampling error of a 400-patient dataset.MethodsWe analysed the UCI CKD dataset (250 CKD and 150 non-CKD patients, 24 predictors) with ten classifiers: logistic regression (LR), K-nearest neighbours (KNN), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), AdaBoost, support vector machine (SVM), gradient boosting (GB), extra trees (ETs), XGBoost and LightGBM. A majority-class baseline served as reference. Imputation (KNN, k = 5), scaling and hyperparameter search were fitted inside the training folds of a nested, repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (CV) (three repeats). We report mean ± SD with Nadeau-Bengio 95% confidence intervals and compared models with corrected paired t-tests and Holm adjustment.ResultsNine classifiers reached a cross-validated accuracy of 98.25-99.50% (AUC ≥ 0.990); KNN reached 93.33% and the baseline 62.50%. LightGBM (99.50 ± 0.63%), RF (99.42 ± 0.80%) and XGBoost (99.25 ± 0.79%) had the highest mean accuracy, but no pair among the nine non-KNN classifiers differed significantly. Permutation importance and SHAP highlighted specific gravity, haemoglobin, serum creatinine, albumin and packed cell volume.ConclusionNo classifier could be ranked above another. The data come from one public dataset with almost completely separable classes, so external validation is needed.

articles.title: Genetic modifiers of airway infection by nontuberculous mycobacteria in people with cystic fibrosis.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Persistent lung infection by nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) is a prerequisite for progression to NTM pulmonary disease, a serious clinical outcome for people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF). Understanding risk factors for persistent infection will improve patient care.

OBJECTIVES: We sought to identify genomic loci associated with persistent lung infection by Mycobacterium avium and Mycobacterium abscessus complexes in PwCF.

METHODS: We performed genome-wide association studies of persistent NTM infection in PwCF enrolled in the CF Genome Project, as well as several secondary studies to assess test sensitivity. Persistent NTM airway infection was defined as two positive sputum cultures within three years, and two NTM species complexes were independently tested as primary outcomes.

MEASUREMENTS: The primary genome-wide association study included whole genome sequencing data for 2,068 participants with NTM culture data who met demographic inclusion criteria. Persistent infection by Mycobacterium avium complex and Mycobacterium abscessus complex were the primary outcomes of study.

MAIN RESULTS: A significant association signal was observed for each primary outcome. The genotype of a locus near ICOS (p = 8.48 x 10-9) was associated with persistent Mycobacterium avium complex infection, while the genotype of a locus overlapping ASB13 (p = 2.19 x 10-9) was associated with persistent Mycobacterium abscessus infection.

CONCLUSIONS: The detection of associations between specific genomic loci and persistent NTM airway infections allows for better assessment of individual risk in PwCF, guides surveillance intensity, provides clues regarding underlying biology of infection, and identifies pathways that may be targeted by therapeutics.

articles.title: Development and validation of an online predictive model for athlete sports injury risk using 12 machine learning algorithms.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundSports injuries critically constrain athletes' competitive performance and career longevity. Current warning methods struggle with multidimensional data, and complex machine learning models often lack interpretability.ObjectiveThis study aims to construct and validate a highly accurate, interpretable multimodal sports injury risk prediction model, offering a transparent, potential decision-support tool for sports medicine teams.MethodsUtilizing a 5430-sample dataset partitioned at a 7:3 ratio, we applied SMOTE to mitigate class imbalance. A tri-stage feature selection strategy (Boruta, LASSO, MRMR) screened core predictive metrics across physiological, biomechanical, environmental, and training workload dimensions. We compared 12 machine learning models using AUC, accuracy, calibration curves, Brier scores, and DCA. SHAP and LIME frameworks provided interpretability, leading to the exploratory deployment of an R-Shiny interactive warning platform.ResultsFeature engineering established 18 core metrics. The Random Forest (RF) model demonstrated superior overall performance, achieving 0.971 validation accuracy, 0.982 AUC, and favorable internal stability. RF also excelled in probability calibration (Brier: 0.0332) and intervention net benefit. Interpretability analyses identified elevated electromyography amplitude, excessive ground reaction force, acute heart rate spikes, and previous injury history as primary acute injury drivers, exhibiting pronounced nonlinear threshold effects.ConclusionThe RF-based multimodal prediction model effectively balances predictive efficacy, internal stability, and interpretability. The developed online warning system represents a beneficial exploration in translating complex algorithms into practical applications, showing future promise to provide frontline coaching teams with objective support for personalized risk profiling and workload management.

articles.title: Attention-enhanced TransUNet for ultrasound liver parenchyma segmentation toward assessment of schistosomiasis-associated liver disease.
articles.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundSchistosomiasis-associated liver disease is the most common clinical form of chronic schistosomiasis. Chronic hepatic schistosomiasis is mainly manifested as liver fibrosis, cirrhosis and other liver dysfunction, and even induces liver cancer in the late stage. Ultrasound is widely used for the diagnosis of schistosomiasis-associated liver disease, grading of liver fibrosis, and assessment of of therapeutic effects.ObjectiveThe study aims to detect and segment the ultrasound liver parenchyma with high accuracy.MethodsWe propose an attention-enhanced TransUNet that improves skip-connection feature transfer by integrating axial attention with residual connections, while retaining the Vision Transformer module for global context modeling. Axial attention re-weights features along spatial axes to emphasize direction-sensitive structures such as liver boundaries, and residual refinement mitigates information degradation during multi-scale fusion. We compared the proposed method against UNet and the original TransUNet using Dice, IoU, and Sensitivity. Ablation studies further demonstrated that combining axial attention with residual connection outperformed axial attention alone.ResultsThe proposed model achieved a satisfactory performance in the delineation of the ultrasound liver parenchyma region, with a Dice coefficient of 0.965, an IoU of 0.931 and a Sensitivity value of 0.970.ConclusionThe results support the feasibility of the attention-enhanced TransUNet model as an upstream module for accurate ultrasound image analysis in schistosomiasis-associated liver disease such as fibrosis staging and cirrhosis.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Liver Abscess Drainage: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Comparative and Single-Arm Studies.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver abscess drainage (EUS-LAD) is an alternative to percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD), but comparative evidence remains limited. We evaluated its efficacy and safety using comparative and single-arm studies.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched through January 13, 2026. Clinical and technical success were primary outcomes; recurrence, mortality, and adverse events were secondary outcomes. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled comparative risk ratios (RRs) and single-arm proportions.

RESULTS: Ten studies involving 501 patients were included. EUS-LAD had higher clinical success [RR: 1.07, 95% CI: (1.01, 1.13); P=0.03] and fewer overall complications [RR: 0.26, 95% CI: (0.12, 0.55); P<0.01] than PCD. No significant differences were found in technical success [RR: 0.99, 95% CI: (0.95, 1.02); P=0.43], mortality [RR: 0.53, 95% CI: (0.10, 2.85); P=0.46], or recurrence [RR: 0.82, 95% CI: (0.29, 2.28); P=0.70]. Single-arm pooled clinical success and complication rates were 98% and 7%, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: EUS-LAD is a promising alternative to PCD, with higher pooled clinical success and fewer overall complications. These findings require cautious interpretation because the evidence is predominantly retrospective and observational.

articles.title: Additive Renoprotection of SGLT2 Inhibitors and ACEi/ARBs Against Contrast-Induced Nephropathy in PCI: A Prospective Observational Study.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) is a common complication of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have renoprotective effects; however, data on chronic SGLT2i therapy for CIN prevention, particularly when combined with renin-angiotensin system (RAS) blockade, remain limited.

METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 249 patients undergoing PCI between August 2024 and December 2025, comprising 126 SGLT2i users and 123 non-users. Low-osmolar non-ionic contrast media were used during the procedures. CIN was defined as an increase in serum creatinine of ≥0.5 mg/dL or ≥25% from baseline within 48 hours of contrast exposure, potentially missing cases with later peaks. Given the occurrence of only 29 CIN events, predictors were identified using Firth's penalized regression. Sensitivity analyses were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and the KDIGO acute kidney injury criteria. The interaction between SGLT2i and ACEi/ARB use was tested using penalized regression for CIN and factorial analysis of variance for ΔCr and ΔeGFR.

RESULTS: Despite higher rates of diabetes and heart failure among SGLT2i users, the incidence of CIN was lower in this group (7.1% vs. 16.3%, p=0.025), with smaller increases in ΔCr (0.05 vs. 0.08 mg/dL, p<0.001) and smaller declines in ΔeGFR (-3.30 vs. -5.20 mL/min/1.73 m², p=0.009). Penalized regression confirmed independent protective associations for SGLT2i use (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.16-0.91) and ACEi/ARB use (OR 0.17, 95% CI 0.06-0.41). IPTW yielded consistent estimates (OR 0.30 and 0.12, respectively), with all standardized mean differences <0.05. The results were robust when the KDIGO criteria were applied, and the protective effects were most pronounced in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). The greater effect associated with ACEi/ARB use may have been related to hydration volumes of 16.9-17.6 mL/kg, which are within a beneficial range.

CONCLUSION: Chronic SGLT2i therapy was associated with a lower incidence of CIN and attenuated renal function decline after PCI. Concomitant ACEi/ARB use provided additive and independent protection, particularly in patients with CKD. These findings support the continuation of SGLT2i therapy during contrast exposure; however, randomized controlled trials are required to establish causality because of the observational design and small number of events.

articles.title: The Design of a Seniors Emergency Medicine Centre Using Virtual Reality as a Pre-Occupancy Evaluation Tool: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: PurposeThis pilot study aimed to gather end-user feedback using an immersive VR experience as part of a pre-occupancy evaluation (PrOE) to generate design recommendations to improve the experience for patients, caregivers, and staff in our planned Seniors Emergency Medicine Centre (SEMC) at the Toronto Western Hospital, and to explore the feasibility of VR as a PrOE tool.BackgroundVR offers a highly accurate, immersive, and cost-effective method for evaluating healthcare environments, allowing rapid iteration and realistic assessment of design options. As our hospital prepares to build a new SEMC, VR provides an opportunity to incorporate patient and staff perspectives to optimize the proposed design.MethodsThis was a pilot study informed by quality improvement principles and a mixed-methods approach. Surveys and semi-structured interviews were used to gather feedback. Qualitative and quantitative data were analyzed to generate themes and prioritize and propose design recommendations.ResultsDesign recommendations, informed by participant feedback, were fed back to the architectural and clinical team.ConclusionsThis pilot study resulted in tangible pre-construction design recommendations for our SEMC utilizing the end-user perspective. This study also adds to the growing body of literature on the use of VR in PrOE, and how it can be leveraged to optimize patient and staff experience in a healthcare setting by developing a framework for VR PrOEs.

articles.title: Glenn Takedown Reconstruction Technique During Biventricular Conversion: A Contemporary Single-Center Experience.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: BackgroundGlenn takedown is an important component of staged biventricular conversion after superior cavopulmonary connection. We evaluated contemporary superior vena cava (SVC) reconstruction strategies, their evolution, and outcomes.MethodsWe reviewed consecutive patients undergoing Glenn takedown during biventricular conversion at Boston Children's Hospital from 2014 through 2024. Rescue takedowns returning patients to a systemic-to-pulmonary artery (PA) shunt or continued single-ventricle palliation were excluded. Reconstruction was classified as direct SVC-right atrial anastomosis, anterior patch/right atrial flap, interposition conduit, or mixed/asymmetric reconstruction.ResultsAmong 162 patients, reconstruction techniques used were anterior patch/right atrial flap in 120 (74.1%), interposition conduit in 33 (20.4%), direct anastomosis in 3 (1.9%), and mixed/asymmetric reconstruction in 6 (3.7%). Median age was 3.9 years (interquartile range [IQR], 2.8-5.6). Interposition use increased from 2 of 66 (3.0%) from 2014 to 2018 to 31 of 96 (32.3%) from 2019 to 2024 (P < .001). SVC reintervention occurred in two of 162 patients (1.2%) and pulmonary artery reintervention in 4/162 (2.5%) patients during a median follow-up of 1.52 years (IQR, 1.08-4.42). Temporary junctional rhythm occurred in 8/162 (4.9%); 7/162 (4.3%) received permanent pacemakers for atrioventricular block. All-cause mortality was 9.3% (15/162).ConclusionsGlenn takedown during biventricular conversion can be achieved using several reconstruction techniques selected according to individual anatomy. Our current practice favors interposition grafting when a tension-free native-tissue connection cannot be achieved, or additional space is required. SVC- and PA-related reinterventions were uncommon during available follow-up; longer surveillance is needed to assess late conduit-related outcomes.

articles.title: Delayed Diagnosis of Coronary Sinus Ostial Atresia in a Single-Ventricle Patient.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Coronary sinus ostial atresia is a rare congenital anomaly that is often clinically silent; however, hemodynamic compromise can occur if venous drainage is interrupted. We present a 4-month old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome who previously underwent palliation with a Norwood procedure. During bidirectional Glenn palliation, ligation of a 2-mm left superior vena cava resulted in coronary sinus dilation and myocardial edema, raising suspicion for coronary sinus ostial atresia. The coronary sinus was unroofed, and the child recovered well.

articles.title: Mechanical Atrioventricular Valve Thrombosis After Warfarin Interruption in Two Patients with Single Ventricle Physiology.
articles.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
articles.abstract: Thrombosed mechanical atrioventricular (AV) valves are catastrophic in patients with functional single-ventricle physiology; however, anticoagulation management during intercurrent illness is not well defined. We retrospectively reviewed 2 patients with functional single-ventricle physiology who underwent mechanical AV valve replacement at our institution. Mechanical valve thrombosis with leaflet immobility was diagnosed by cinefluoroscopy or echocardiography and confirmed intraoperatively. Two patients developed thrombosed mechanical AV valves after temporary warfarin cessation for supratherapeutic PT-INR during gastroenteritis. Case 1 (hypoplastic left heart syndrome following Glenn procedure, mechanical tricuspid valve) developed single-leaflet immobility after warfarin was withheld and low-dose vitamin K2 was administered for a PT-INR of 7.1. Case 2 (right atrial isomerism, Fontan circulation, mechanical common AV valve) developed bilateral leaflet immobility despite sustained PT-INR >4.0. Operative findings confirmed fresh thrombus without pannus in both cases. Valve thrombosis may occur after warfarin interruption even when PT-INR remains therapeutic, and reliance on PT-INR alone may underestimate thrombotic risk.

articles.title: Children at the Crossroads of War: A Snapshot of Pediatric Food Insecurity in Ukraine and Palestine, 2024.
articles.abstract: BackgroundFood insecurity remains a central objective for world development although some populations as children or those affected by conflict may face higher challenges for its achievement.ObjectiveTo produce timely and transparent estimates of child food insecurity in Ukraine and Palestine in 2024, and to compare the prevalence and absolute figures of moderate and severe food insecurity across the 2 countries.MethodsCross-sectional study using United Nations data. Nationally representative datasets from both countries were analyzed using the FAO's methodology. The prevalence of moderate or severe and severe food insecurity among children was calculated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Estimates were combined with child population totals to derive absolute numbers of affected children.ResultsIn Ukraine, the prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity among children was 0.382 (95% CI: 0.318-0.447), with severe food insecurity at 0.051 (95% CI: 0.025-0.077). In Palestine, moderate or severe food insecurity was 0.310 (95% CI: 0.269-0.351), while severe food insecurity reached 0.112 (95% CI: 0.088-0.136). Although overall levels of moderate or severe food insecurity were broadly comparable, severe food insecurity was more than twice as prevalent among Palestinian children. In absolute terms, Ukraine's larger child population resulted in a greater number of affected children.ConclusionsChild food insecurity remains high in both countries, with important differences in severity and population figures. Compared with FAO's publicly available multi-year averages, these estimates provide more timely and granular insights into ongoing crises. Transparent documentation of methods strengthens epidemiological monitoring and supports evidence-informed policy and humanitarian response in conflict-affected contexts.

articles.title: Risk Period for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Rupture During Skiing: A Multicenter Epidemiological Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alpine skiing carries a substantial risk of knee injuries, particularly anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) ruptures. Despite improvements in equipment and safety standards, ACL injuries remain frequent and are influenced by modifiable and unmodifiable risk factors. Identifying temporal and situational patterns may support more effective prevention strategies.

HYPOTHESIS: ACL ruptures in recreational skiers occur more frequently early in ski vacations and earlier in the ski day, reflecting insufficient neuromuscular adaptation.

STUDY DESIGN: Multicenter retrospective observational study (2024-2025 season).

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted between January and April 2025 in 3 sports medicine centers in France. Patients with magnetic resonance imaging scan-confirmed ACL rupture sustained during recreational skiing within the preceding 3 months were included. Data were collected using a standardized questionnaire assessing injury timing, skiing experience, injury mechanism, and environmental conditions. Descriptive statistics were used.

RESULTS: A total of 138 patients were included; 68.1% were female, with a mean age of 33 years. ACL injuries occurred predominantly at the beginning of ski vacations (46%) and before midday (64.6%). Most injuries involved intermediate or expert skiers (83.3%). Falls and changes of direction were common injury mechanisms. Injuries occurred more frequently (58.3%) under average or poor snow conditions, whereas visibility showed no clear association. Associated injuries were observed in 36 (28.5%) patients and were mainly vertical tears of the medial meniscus. Specific lesions were also identified, including 3 ramp lesions (8.3%) and 3 lateral meniscal root lesions (8.3%).

CONCLUSION: ACL ruptures in skiing occur most commonly early in ski vacations and during the morning, particularly among intermediate and expert skiers. These findings underscore the role of neuromuscular readiness, fatigue-independent factors, and environmental conditions in ACL injury risk.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Prevention strategies for skiing-related ACL injuries should prioritize early-session and early-vacation interventions, including structured warm-up routines, progressive skill adaptation, and neuromuscular training. Targeted prevention programs, particularly for female and higher-level recreational skiers, may reduce the incidence of severe knee injuries.

articles.title: Psychological Anxiety and Depression Among Primary Caregivers of Infants With Unilateral Cleft Lip and Palate: A Cross-Sectional Analysis From the NAMUC Trial Using GAD-7 and PHQ-9 Scales.
articles.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
articles.abstract: BackgroundCaregivers of infants with unilateral cleft lip and palate (CLP) are at increased risk of anxiety and depressive symptoms, which may influence treatment adherence and child outcomes.AimTo estimate the prevalence and severity of anxiety and depressive symptoms among primary caregivers of babies under seven weeks of age with unilateral CLP.Materials and methodsThis cross-sectional analysis utilised baseline data from a multicentre clinical trial (NAMUC trial) evaluating nasoalveolar moulding (NAM) in infants (≤7 weeks) with complete unilateral CLP across ten centres in India. Primary caregivers completed Generalised Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) in their native language. Descriptive statistics were used to summarise anxiety and depression scores and the association between GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores was assessed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.ResultsAmong the 205 caregivers who completed both questionnaires, nearly half reported symptoms of anxiety and depression. Moderate to severe anxiety was observed in 17.1% of caregivers, while 21.5% reported moderate to severe depressive symptoms. The median GAD-7 score was 4 (IQR: 1-7) and the median PHQ-9 score was 4 (IQR: 1-9). No statistically significant difference in anxiety or depression scores was observed with respect to centre region, birthweight, marital status, cleft width, mode of delivery or caregiver age. A strong positive correlation was observed between GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores (p < 0.001), indicating a substantial overlap between anxiety and depressive symptoms.ConclusionsThe findings support the integration of early psychosocial assessment and targeted support within multidisciplinary cleft services to improve caregiver well-being.

articles.title: Novel opportunities to tackle heart failure with natriuretic peptides.
Exploring the upper spectrum of physiological cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes: insights from a CMR study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is essential for distinguishing physiological from pathological remodelling in athletes. However, cardiovascular screening protocols vary across studies, leaving uncertainty regarding the true upper limits of physiological adaptation.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterise the full spectrum of cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes and to describe CMR-derived upper limits of cardiac remodelling according to sport category and sex.

METHODS: Olympic athletes with negative comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation underwent voluntary non-contrast CMR. Left and right ventricular volumes, mass, and ejection fraction (EF) were quantified. Cardiac parameters were analysed according to the ESC sport classification and sex. Cluster analysis was performed to identify patterns of cardiac remodelling independently of sport category.

RESULTS: A total of 320 athletes (age 26±5 years, 57% male; 13% skill sports, 19% power, 28% mixed, 40% endurance, 97% Caucasians) were included. Endurance athletes had the largest biventricular volumes and LV mass (all p-values <0.001), with no differences in EF across sport categories. Maximal interventricular septal thickness did not exceed 13 mm in males or 11 mm in females. Only 1% and 2% of athletes had LV or RV EF <50%, respectively, predominantly cyclists. Cluster analysis identified two phenotypes reflecting lower and higher degrees of remodelling, with substantial overlap across sport categories. The sex and sport categories were independently associated with the high-remodelling phenotype.

CONCLUSION: CMR-derived cardiac adaptation in predominantly Caucasian, Olympic athletes varies according to sport category, with endurance athletes demonstrating the most pronounced remodelling. Maximal physiological LV wall thickness was 13 mm in males and 11 mm in females in this cohort, whereas LV EF <50% was uncommon despite marked cardiac remodelling. Finally, the overlap across sport categories and the identification of distinct remodelling phenotypes suggest that cardiac adaptation reflects a continuum rather than discrete sport-specific patterns.

articles.title: Habitual Coffee Consumption, Genetic Susceptibility, and Incident Stroke: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between habitual coffee consumption and incident stroke remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 490 889 UK Biobank participants without prevalent stroke. Average self-reported coffee intake across available assessments was categorized as ≤0.5, 0.6 to 1.67, 1.68 to 3.0, and >3.0 cups/d. Incident stroke was ascertained through linkage to hospital and death registries and self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable Cox models and restricted cubic splines characterized associations. Analyses assessed effect modification by CYP1A2 genotype and stroke polygenic risk score and used multiple-imputation and competing-risk sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 22 579 incident strokes occurred. Compared with ≤0.5 cups/d, adjusted hazard ratios were 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89) for 0.6 to 1.67 cups/d, 0.92 (95% CI, 0.89-0.96) for 1.68 to 3.0 cups/d, and 0.98 (95% CI, 0.94-1.02) for >3.0 cups/d. Splines showed a nonlinear J-shaped association, with the lowest estimated risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. Associations were broadly consistent across CYP1A2 and polygenic-risk strata, with no significant interaction. Moderate intake was associated with lower risk among participants reporting sugar addition, whereas high decaffeinated-coffee intake was associated with higher risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Moderate habitual coffee consumption was associated with lower incident stroke risk, with the lowest observed risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. These observational findings should not be interpreted as evidence to prescribe coffee for stroke prevention.

articles.title: Postoperative Inflammatory Response After Cardiac Surgery: Magnitude, Timing, and Prognosis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac surgery triggers a systemic inflammatory response. While this response is commonly interpreted as a marker of postoperative complications, its prognostic significance on short- and long-term death remains poorly characterized. We assessed the association between postoperative inflammation and short- and long-term all-cause death after cardiac surgery.

METHODS: In a single-center retrospective cohort of patients undergoing cardiac surgery between 2011 and 2024, postoperative CRP (C-reactive protein) measurements and peak of postoperative CRP (CRPmax) and its timing were assessed. Association between CRPmax tertiles, delayed CRPmax (after postoperative day 3), and 30-day or 5-year all-cause death were evaluated using multivariable Cox regression models.

RESULTS: A total of 7283 patients were included (mean age, 64.9 years; 72% men; 54% underwent coronary artery bypass grafting, 31% aortic valve replacement, and 94% on-pump surgery). Median CRPmax was 184 interquartile range, 134-246) mg/L. Median postoperative CRP peaked on postoperative day 3. Patients in the highest CRPmax tertile (tertile 3) more frequently presented with obesity, diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and chronic kidney disease. Compared with the lowest tertile, CRPmax tertile 3 was independently associated with higher 30-day (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.56 [95% CI, 1.78-3.68]; P<0.001) and 5-year all-cause death (adjusted HR, 1.41 [95% CI, 1.22-1.62]; P<0.001). A delayed CRPmax was independently associated with increased 30-day (adjusted HR, 2.61 [95% CI, 1.94-3.52]; P<0.001) and 5-year mortality rate (adjusted HR, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.37-1.77]; P<0.001). These associations persisted after adjustment for postoperative infection.

CONCLUSIONS: Both the magnitude and timing of postoperative CRP peak were independently associated with short- and long-term death after cardiac surgery, irrespective of postoperative infection. These findings support close postoperative inflammatory monitoring after cardiac surgery.

articles.title: Standardized Ultrafast Transcranial Ultrasound Acquisition in Acute Stroke: The HYPER-AI-SCAN Pilot Study With Exploratory Artificial Intelligence Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage requires rapid mechanism-specific treatment, yet early stroke triage relies on clinical severity scales that do not reliably distinguish hemorrhage from ischemic stroke. We assessed the feasibility of a standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound protocol designed to support subsequent artificial intelligence (AI)-based intracerebral hemorrhage detection.

METHODS: HYPER-AI-SCAN (Hyper-Acute AI-Assisted Sonographic Cerebral Hemorrhage Assessment Network) was a single-center prospective feasibility study with embedded exploratory AI analysis. Between March and December 2025, 102 adults with acute computed tomography (CT)-confirmed stroke were prospectively enrolled according to trained operator availability. Primary feasibility outcomes were protocol completion, operator-rated adequate transtemporal windows, and acquisition time. In patients with retrievable paired baseline CT, exploratory AI analyses compared CT-only, ultrasound-only, and cross-modal CT-guided ultrasound models using patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, and specificity.

RESULTS: Two patients were excluded after acquisition because insonation depth was <19 cm, yielding 100 evaluable patients (33 intracerebral hemorrhage; 67 ischemic stroke). The protocol was completed in all evaluable patients; adequate transtemporal windows were identified in 87%, and median acquisition time was 22 seconds (interquartile range, 13-31). Paired baseline CT images were available in 91 patients. Mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.86 (SD, 0.07) for the CT-only model, 0.85 (SD, 0.14) for the ultrasound-only model, and 0.92 (SD, 0.07) for the cross-modal model.

CONCLUSIONS: Standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound acquisition was feasible at the bedside in acute stroke and generated brief cine-loops suitable for exploratory AI development. Multicenter external validation is required before diagnostic or triage application.

REGISTRATION INFORMATION: Clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07319013.

articles.title: Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction in Low-Income Settings: Performance and Challenges of Screening Scores in a Population-Based Cohort in Haiti.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is rapidly increasing in low- and middle-income countries, however detection remains challenging. We assessed 2 screening scores developed in high-income settings, H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF, against physician-adjudicated HFpEF in a population-based cohort from Haiti.

METHODS: The primary outcome was prevalent HFpEF defined by (1) physician adjudication, (2) H2FpEF score, (3) HFA-PEFF score. The cross-sectional cohort comprised 3003 adults from the Haiti Cardiovascular Disease Cohort, with sociodemographic, clinical, electrocardiography, echocardiography and BNP data available. We compared physician-adjudicated HFpEF participants to those screening positive (intermediate-high H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF scores) using interrater reliability (Cohen's kappa, Krippendorff's alpha). Diagnostic performance of H2FPEF and HFA-PEFF against physician adjudication, used as a pragmatic reference standard appropriate for Haiti and similar settings, was calculated via sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.

RESULTS: Age-adjusted HFpEF prevalence was 9.5% (95% CI: 8.3-11.0) by physician adjudication, 10.2% (95% CI: 9.0-11.7) by H2FPEF, and 8.6% (95% CI: 7.5-10.0) by HFA-PEFF. Adjudicated HFpEF participants were young (median age 57), had high prevalence of hypertension (70%), obesity (33%), and no atrial fibrillation. Agreement between all 3 scores was moderate-substantial (alpha 0.57, 95% CI: 0.55-0.59), with the highest pair-wise agreement between physician adjudication and HFA-PEFF (kappa 0.62, 95% CI: 0.57-0.67). HFA-PEFF had higher sensitivity and similar specificity relative to H2FPEF.

CONCLUSIONS: In this Haitian cohort, prevalent HFpEF occurred in relatively young participants with high hypertension and obesity rates and negligible atrial fibrillation. HFA-PEFF exhibited higher concordance and sensitivity than H2FPEF versus physician adjudication. Tailored, non-invasive HFpEF screening scores for low- and middle-income countries are needed to address this growing global epidemic.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Anticoagulation for Stroke Prevention in Atrial Fibrillation: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Multiscale RR Interval Dynamics Reveal Early Electrophysiological Dysfunction in LMNA Cardiomyopathy.
Short- and Long-Term Effects of His Bundle Pacing on Myocardial Perfusion, Metabolism, and Function.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular apical pacing (RVAP) has been reported to affect myocardial metabolism and perfusion, leading to impaired left ventricular function. Right ventricular septal pacing (RVSP) and His bundle pacing (HISP) have been introduced as alternatives to RVAP. We sought to investigate the effect of RVSP and HISP on myocardial perfusion, fatty acid metabolism, and function.

METHODS: We prospectively studied 104 patients (RVSP, n=44; HISP, n=17; RVAP, n=11; and sinus rhythm or right atrial pacing, n=32 as the control group) admitted for pacemaker implantation, excluding patients with coronary artery disease. Patients underwent technetium-99m methoxyisobutylisonitrile single-photon emission computed tomography and iodine-123 β-methyl iodophenyl pentadecanoic acid single-photon emission computed tomography imaging during the short-term period (3-12 months after device implantation) and in the long-term period (24 months after short-term assessment). Regional tracer activity in 17 segments on a polar map was calculated as %uptake.

RESULTS: On both short- and long-term imaging, RVSP and RVAP groups showed relatively reduced sestamibi and BMIPP %uptake in septal and inferior regions compared with the control group, whereas no apparent reduction was observed in the HISP group. No significant difference in left ventricular ejection fraction was seen among RVSP, HISP, and control groups, although the RVAP group showed lower left ventricular ejection fraction. Average sestamibi and BMIPP %uptakes in 17 segments were significantly associated with left ventricular ejection fraction.

CONCLUSIONS: HISP may be associated with relatively preserved myocardial perfusion, metabolism, and function compared with right ventricular pacing.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Left Ventricular Kinetic Energy Assessed by 4D Flow CMR in Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alterations in left ventricular intracavitary hemodynamics can occur early in the course of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). However, the association between 4-dimensional (4D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters and adverse outcomes in patients with DCM remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters can predict adverse outcomes in patients with DCM.

METHODS: In this multicenter prospective cohort study, 675 adult patients with DCM (mean age, 56 years; 399 men) from 3 medical centers and 80 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance. Left ventricular flow components and kinetic energy parameters were quantified. The primary end point was a composite of heart failure events, including heart failure-related death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, or cardiac transplantation.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 42 months, 58 patients (8.6%) experienced the primary end point. Compared with controls, patients with DCM exhibited reduced peak systolic kinetic energy normalized to EDV (KEiEDV) and peak E-wave KEiEDV; these differences were more pronounced in those who developed the primary end point. In univariable Cox regression, direct flow, residual volume, peak systolic KEiEDV, and peak E-wave KEiEDV were significant predictors of the primary end point (all P<0.05). After adjustment for left ventricular ejection fraction, NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide), extracellular volume fraction, extent of late gadolinium enhancement, peak systolic KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.28-0.53]), and peak E-wave KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.26-0.48]) remained independently associated with the primary end point (both P<0.001). Furthermore, these 2 kinetic energy parameters provided incremental prognostic value beyond clinical markers and conventional imaging markers for predicting the primary end point.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DCM, decreased peak systolic KEiEDV and peak E-wave KEiEDV, as measured by 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance, are independently associated with poor prognosis and provide incremental prognostic value for risk stratification beyond clinical and conventional imaging markers.

articles.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

articles.title: Performance of AI-based Search Platforms for Identifying Blood Pressure Device Validation Status.
Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined.

METHODS: We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models.

RESULTS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets.

CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

articles.title: Shifting the Pressure-Natriuresis Curve: The Cellular Mechanisms of Female Renal Resilience.
articles.abstract: Female and male kidneys exhibit markedly different patterns of transporter abundance and activity along the nephron, yet the physiological significance of the differences remains incompletely understood. Recent experimental and computational studies suggest that many of these differences can be interpreted through the lens of pressure natriuresis, the kidney's primary mechanism for long-term regulation of extracellular volume and arterial pressure. We review evidence that the female nephron exhibits a transport architecture that may facilitate enhanced pressure natriuresis and greater flexibility in effective circulating volume regulation. This framework provides new insights into sex differences in acute and chronic blood pressure control and connects pressure-natriuretic mechanisms with renal adaptations during pregnancy and lactation, hypertension, and aging.

articles.title: PREVENT Risk Stratification for Intensive Blood Pressure Intervention and Life Expectancy in Rural China: A Post Hoc Analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guideline adopted the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide antihypertensive treatment, but whether PREVENT risk groups identify patients who benefit more from intensive blood pressure (BP) control is uncertain. We evaluated intensive BP control across PREVENT risk groups in the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.

METHODS: We analyzed 21 872 hypertensive adults from 326 Chinese villages. Participants received intensive BP control (target <130/80 mm Hg) or usual care and were classified as low risk (<5%), borderline risk (5.0%-7.4%), intermediate risk (7.5%-19.9%), or high risk (≥20%). The primary outcome was a composite of major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Safety, net benefit, and life expectancy were assessed.

RESULTS: Over a median of 3.02 years, intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the low-risk (hazard ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.29-0.97]), intermediate-risk (hazard ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.49-0.69]), and high-risk groups (hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.47-0.77]), but not the borderline-risk group (hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.51-1.26]). No significant treatment-by-risk interaction was observed. Adverse events increased mainly in intermediate- and high-risk groups. Net benefit was favorable across all groups and greatest in the high-risk group. At 45 years of age, estimated life expectancy gains were 0.94 years overall, 0.71 years in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.26 years in the high-risk group.

CONCLUSIONS: Intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in 3 PREVENT risk groups, with favorable net benefit across all groups. Absolute benefit and estimated life expectancy gains were greatest among high-risk participants. PREVENT risk stratification may inform intensive BP control in community-based hypertensive populations.

articles.title: Next-Generation Oleic Acid Ufasomes: Emerging Trends in Targeted, Controlled, and Stimuli-Responsive Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Ufasomes are vesicles formed from unsaturated fatty acids and are being investigated as carriers for pharmaceutical compounds. This review summarizes their structure, preparation methods, characterization, drug-release behavior, and emerging applications, with particular attention to reported studies involving rosuvastatin for diabetic wound healing, nintedanib for pulmonary delivery, and Glycyrrhiza glabra extract in wound dressings. Despite promising preclinical findings, translation remains limited by potential of hydrogen-dependent stability, challenges in reproducible scale-up, and insufficient safety and clinical evidence. The review critically considers these findings and identifies priorities for further development.

articles.title: Late Gadolinium Enhanced Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Versus Intracardiac Echocardiography for Detecting Nonischemic Myocardial Scar in Ventricular Arrhythmia Ablation.
Ventricular Morphology and Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation in Adults Post-Fontan: Associations With Exercise Hemodynamics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dominance and atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) are associated with adverse outcomes post-Fontan palliation, but their underlying hemodynamic correlates, particularly during exercise, remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional cohort, exercise hemodynamics by ventricular morphology and AVVR severity were assessed invasively (supine exercise catheterization) in 108 individuals and semi-invasively (semisupine exercise with echocardiography and peripheral venous pressure) in 108.

RESULTS: Age of the invasive cohort was 32.1 (25.6-37.2) years; 41 had RV dominance, 19 had moderate or severe AVVR, and 16 had both. Resting and peak mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary artery wedge pressure were similar across ventricular morphologies and AVVR severity. However, RV dominance was associated with lower systemic (systemic blood flow, 67% [22-93] versus 86% [63-105] predicted; P=0.006) and pulmonary (pulmonary blood flow, 57% [33-75] versus 72% [61-89] predicted; P<0.001) cardiac output responses to exercise and steeper Δpulmonary artery pressure/Δpulmonary blood flow, (4.3 [2.6-10.6] versus 3.0 [1.7-4.8] mm Hg/L per minute; P=0.004). Patients with moderate or severe AVVR showed a similar pattern, with lower systemic blood flow (64% [19-92] versus 77% [57-101], P=0.10) and pulmonary blood flow (57% [36-74] versus 70% [55-88] predicted, P=0.03) responses. Findings were replicated in the semi-invasive cohort, where RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR were associated with lower peak systemic blood flow and higher Δperipheral venous pressure/Δ systemic blood flow, despite similar peak peripheral venous pressure.

CONCLUSIONS: Resting and exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, and peripheral venous pressure are unrelated to ventricular morphology and AVVR severity. Conversely, impaired flow augmentation and steeper pressure-flow relationships during exercise were associated with RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR, emphasizing the role of dynamic provocation to unmask occult cardiovascular reserve limitations.

articles.title: Myocardial Hmgcs2-Driven Ketogenesis Promotes Atrial Fibrillation in Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Elevated circulating ketone bodies (β-hydroxybutyrate [β-OHB]) in T2DM are considered hepatic in origin and benefit the heart via energy provision. Although we found ketogenesis enzyme Hmgcs2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2) upregulated in both atrial and ventricular tissues of T2DM mice, alongside increased cardiac and circulating β-OHB. Whether enhanced Hmgcs2 is related to AF, ketogenesis-dependent or independent, remained unclear.

METHODS: T2DM mice were induced by high-fat diet and followed by streptozocin injection. Cardiac-specific Hmgcs2 overexpression and cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockout were conducted in T2DM mice. Cardiac function and left atrial diameter were evaluated using echocardiography, and cardiac electrophysiology was examined through electrical mapping. Programmed electrical stimulation was delivered to induce AF. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria of patients with or without T2DM were analyzed.

RESULTS: The heart functioned as a primary ketogenic organ in T2DM mice via upregulating Hmgcs2, surpassing the liver. Hmgcs2-mediated shunting of fatty acid-derived acetyl-CoA into ketogenesis depleted myocardial energy reserves, exacerbated oxidative stress, and caused mitochondrial injury, ultimately increasing AF inducibility and diastolic dysfunction. In addition, cardiac-derived β-hydroxybutyrate released into circulation prolonged action potential duration in atrial cardiomyocytes. Mechanistically, Hmgcs2-mediated cytosolic β-hydroxybutyrylation targeted Oxct1 (3-oxoacid CoA-transferase 1) for degradation, blocking cardiac ketolysis. Blood metabolomics from the coronary sinus and left atria confirmed active cardiac ketogenesis in patients with T2DM and heart-derived ketone release into systemic circulation. Venous plasma β-OHB levels positively correlated with atrial low-voltage burden and postablation AF recurrence. Cardiomyocyte-specific Hmgcs2 knockdown improved cardiac utilization of fatty acids, β-OHB, and glucose in T2DM mice by suppressing cardiac ketogenesis; this intervention, with reduced circulating β-OHB, attenuated diabetes-associated AF.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac Hmgcs2 represented a novel therapeutic target for diabetic AF and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

articles.title: MINOCA and INOCA: What Is the Risk?
The multidimensional role of Platelet-Related factors in the occurrence and development of colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: Platelets, traditionally recognized as core components of the coagulation system, have emerged as critical regulators in the multistep progression of colorectal cancer (CRC) beyond their hemostatic functions. Accumulating evidence demonstrates that platelets orchestrate a multidimensional network to promote CRC initiation, proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and immune escape through direct interactions with tumor cells, modulation of the tumor microenvironment, and regulation of angiogenic processes. Two key platelet surface molecules, P-selectin (CD62P) and C-type lectin-like receptor-2 (CLEC- 2), serve as central hubs in these pro-tumorigenic cascades: CD62P mediates platelet-tumor cell aggregation, extravasation, and immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while CLEC-2 interacts with its ligand podoplanin (PDPN) to drive platelet activation, tumor cell epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and cancer-associated thrombosis. In-depth research into their mechanisms of action is of great significance for the development of targeted therapeutic drugs for colorectal cancer.

articles.title: An unexpected diagnosis behind a simple oral sore: asymptomatic neurosyphilis.
articles.journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
articles.abstract: Oral manifestations of syphilis are uncommon and may represent an important diagnostic clue. A 29-year-old man who has sex with men, newly diagnosed with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, presented with throat pain and a greyish-white plaque with surrounding erythema involving the soft palate and oropharynx. Microbiological investigations were negative while syphilis serology revealed a Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) titre of 1:128 and reactive Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay. The lesion resolved completely following benzathine penicillin. Despite the absence of neurological symptoms, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination, prompted by a high serum VDRL titre and HIV co-infection, demonstrated lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein and reactive CSF-VDRL, confirming asymptomatic neurosyphilis. This case illustrates how an isolated oral mucous patch served as an important diagnostic clue to clinically silent central nervous system involvement in selected high-risk patients.

articles.title: Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative.
