The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology.

METHODS: 520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features.

RESULTS: 50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope.

CONCLUSION: The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

articles.title: A VAPG Incorporating Targeted Self-Assembling Peptides for Efficient VSMC Restoring and Imaging in Abdominal Aortic Models.
articles.abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction is closely associated with vascular remodeling during abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression, making VSMC repair a vital therapeutic strategy. Although peptides capable of VSMC recruitment have been reported, their application is severely limited by poor accumulation in AAA lesions because of rapid clearance following systemic administration. The enzyme-triggered self-assembling peptide strategy has emerged as a safe and effective approach to prolong local retention while enabling specific responsiveness. In this study, we identified ADAMTS4 and MMP-2 as highly expressed proteases in AAA lesions, serving as ideal targets for in situ retention. We developed a Targeted Responsive Assembly Peptide (TRAP) strategy by incorporating the VSMC-recruitment peptide VAPG, an ADAMTS4 recognition motif for AAA targeting, and an MMP-2-responsive cleavage motif that triggers self-assembly of the Fmoc-FF fragment. Following enzymatic activation, VAPG-containing fragments undergo self-assembly into hydrogels, significantly enhancing VSMC recruitment. The secondary structure transitioned from random coils to β-sheets upon MMP-2 cleavage. The assembled hydrogels exhibited moderate viscoelastic behavior, with stable elastic properties, favorable mechanical strength, and shear resistance. Moreover, PET/CT imaging revealed that 68Ga-labeled peptide enables non-invasive monitoring of peptide accumulation and retention at AAA sites. Ultimately, this TRAP strategy potentially serves as an efficient approach for AAA treatment through long-acting VSMC repair.

articles.title: First Cases of Allergic Contact Dermatitis From the New FreeStyle Libre 3 Sensor: Small Device, Multiple Allergens.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD) from glucose sensors has become increasingly common. Newer devices, such as FreeStyle Libre 3 (Abbott Diabetes Care, UK), have been developed to enhance performance and reduce skin reactions. No ACD cases linked to this particular device have been reported to date.

OBJECTIVE: To document the first cases of ACD linked to the FreeStyle Libre 3 sensor and to identify potential culprit allergenic components through patch testing and chemical analyses.

METHODS: A retrospective chart review was conducted on 15 patients with suspected ACD related to the FreeStyle Libre 3 device who underwent patch testing at Antwerp University Hospital between November 2023 and November 2025. Chemical analyses of the device and associated adhesive components were performed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS).

RESULTS: Ten patients (67%) were diagnosed with ACD and most had prior exposure to other glucose sensors. The most frequent allergens were colophonium and related compounds, followed by (meth)acrylates, isocyanates and tert-butylphenol (TBP) derivatives. GC-MS analyses revealed the presence of most of these chemicals.

CONCLUSIONS: Multiple newly identified as well as (modified) classic sensitizers contribute to ACD from the FreeStyle Libre 3 glucose sensor. Comprehensive ingredient disclosure and extended patch testing are essential for accurate diagnosis and prevention.

articles.title: IVUS-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Long-Segment Traumatic Right Coronary Artery Dissection After Blunt Chest Trauma: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract: Traumatic coronary artery dissection is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of blunt chest trauma that may be difficult to distinguish from myocardial contusion or chest-wall injury. We report the case of a 55-year-old man who developed persistent severe chest pain after falling approximately 2 m and sustaining a direct anterior chest impact. Despite two initially normal cardiac troponin I measurements, electrocardiography revealed inferior ST-segment elevation with reciprocal ST-segment depression, and echocardiography demonstrated inferior-wall hypokinesis. Emergency coronary angiography showed complete proximal right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion with Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) grade 0 flow. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) identified an intimal tear and extensive intramural hematoma compressing the true lumen over approximately 90 mm, confirming traumatic RCA dissection. Given the ongoing myocardial ischemia, emergency percutaneous coronary intervention was performed. After the initial guidewire entered the false lumen, IVUS was used to identify the true-lumen entry point and guide a second wire into the distal true lumen. Three overlapping drug-eluting stents were subsequently implanted from distal to proximal to cover the entire dissected segment. IVUS-guided balloon post-dilatation corrected incomplete stent apposition and restored TIMI grade 3 flow. Postprocedural coronary computed tomography angiography revealed an abnormally high anterior RCA ostium above the junction of the left and right coronary sinuses. No recurrent chest pain, bleeding events, or clinically diagnosed stent thrombosis occurred during follow-up at 6 months and 1 year. This case highlights the importance of recognizing coronary artery injury after blunt chest trauma despite initially normal cardiac biomarkers and demonstrates the value of IVUS in true-lumen identification, precise stent placement, and procedural optimization. Coronary ostial anatomical variation may contribute to susceptibility to traumatic coronary injury, although its causal significance remains uncertain.

articles.title: Short- and median-term disease outcome after Clostridioides difficile infection in paediatric inflammatory bowel disease patients.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a recognised complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). In adults, CDI has been linked to increased long-term colectomy risk, but data on its impact in paediatric IBD remain scarce. We aimed to assess the medium-term course of IBD after CDI in children.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single-centre, case-control study in the paediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition Department at Necker-Enfants Malades Hospital. All paediatric IBD (pIBD) patients hospitalised with CDI between January 2008 and December 2020 were included. Each case was matched 1:3 with IBD controls by sex, age, IBD subtype, disease location, and year of diagnosis. Outcomes at 12, 24 and 36 months included disease activity scores, number of exacerbations, hospitalisations, digestive surgeries, and treatment escalation.

RESULTS: Forty-five pIBD patients with CDI were enrolled and matched with 152 pIBD controls. Compared with controls, children with CDI experienced a more severe disease course, characterised by higher mean activity scores each year of follow-up, more flares requiring hospitalisation at 24 and 36 months, and greater need for therapeutic escalation over time (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In paediatric patients, CDI is associated with a significantly more severe medium-term course of IBD. Early recognition and targeted management of CDI are therefore crucial in this population.

articles.title: Venous Vascular Closure System Versus Conventional Figure of Eight Suture Following Single Shot Device Pulmonary Vein Isolation: The VASC-AF Study.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Optimization of femoral venous access management has become increasingly important as catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF) continues to evolve towards greater safety with accelerated recovery pathways. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of a bioabsorbable venous vascular closure system (VCS) compared with a conventional figure-of-eight (F8) suture and manual compression following contemporary single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).

METHODS AND RESULTS: VASC-AF was a prospective, multicentre, randomized controlled trial performed at three German electrophysiology centres. One hundred consecutive patients undergoing single-shot PVI were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to femoral venous closure using the VASCADE MVP VCS; (n=50) or conventional F8 suture (n=50). The primary efficacy endpoint was time to ambulation. The primary safety endpoint comprised major periprocedural adverse events requiring medical intervention before hospital discharge.Baseline characteristics and procedural variables were comparable between study groups. Median time to ambulation was significantly shorter following vascular closure with VCS compared with F8 sutures (120 [120-150] vs. 180 [180-240] min; P=0.015). Likewise, time to haemostasis (0.5 [0.5-2] vs. 1 [1-2] min; P=0.021) and time to discharge eligibility (2.5 [2.1-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-5.0] h; P=0.019) were significantly reduced.Major adverse events occurred infrequently and did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, vascular closure using VCS significantly reduced minor vascular access complications (6% vs. 26%; P=0.006), groin pain, and patient discomfort while improving overall post-procedural satisfaction.

CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing contemporary single-shot AF ablation, use of a bioabsorbable VCS significantly accelerated post-procedural recovery while maintaining a comparable major safety profile. Reduced access-site complications and improved patient-reported outcomes support VCS as an important component of enhanced recovery pathways following AF ablation especially in an ambulatory or Same-Day Discharge setting.

articles.title: Association of Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection With Reduced Helicobacter pylori Positivity: Findings From Four Diagnostic Tests.
articles.journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest burden of both Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infections. The acquisition and disease manifestation of these two infections are different, but both are chronic and cannot be spontaneously cleared by human immunological mechanisms. We sought to determine the association between HIV and H. pylori infection in a cohort from Zambia.

METHODS: We prospectively enrolled patients presenting for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and tested them for HIV and H. pylori infection. HIV testing was performed serologically using Determine for screening and Tri-Dot for confirmation. The presence of H. pylori infection was determined by serology, histology, stool antigen, and rapid urease testing. Patient demographic details were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. Data were analysed using R statistical software employing standard methods.

RESULTS: Among the 300 participants enrolled, 61 (20%) were HIV-positive and 239 (80%) were HIV-negative. Overall, H. pylori positivity was significantly lower in HIV-positive than in HIV-negative participants (65% vs. 81%; p = 0.015). HIV-positive participants had lower positivity rates by serology (51% vs. 72%; OR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.21-0.76), histology (20% vs. 36%; OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.22-0.87), and rapid urease test (15% vs. 30%; OR: 0.42, 95% CI: 0.18-0.86). Stool antigen positivity did not differ significantly by HIV status. Using a composite reference standard for active infection, plasma serology showed lower sensitivity (63.2% vs. 83.7%) and accuracy (61.9% vs. 81.3%) in HIV-positive participants than in HIV-negative participants. Among participants with active H. pylori infection, HIV-positive individuals were nearly three times more likely to have false-negative serology results (OR: 2.97; p = 0.06).

CONCLUSIONS: HIV-positive individuals demonstrate lower H. pylori positivity and reduced serological test performance than HIV-negative individuals. Therefore, serology may underestimate active H. pylori infections in people living with HIV.

articles.title: Feasibility, safety, and preliminary effects of haptic cane-assisted gait training in chronic hemiparetic stroke: a pilot randomized crossover trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and safety of haptic cane-assisted gait training in chronic hemiparetic stroke and to estimate the between-treatment difference in self-selected gait speed to inform future studies.

DESIGN: Randomized, single-centre, assessor-blinded, 2-period crossover pilot trial.

SUBJECTS/PATIENTS: Twenty patients with chronic hemiparetic stroke.

METHODS: Participants received haptic cane-assisted and conventional gait training in 2 x 4-week periods (12 sessions each), separated by a 4-week washout. The primary outcome was self-selected gait speed measured using the 10-metre walk test. Secondary outcomes included fast gait speed, balance, functional ambulation, activities of daily living, quality of life, and working memory.

RESULTS: 17 of 20 participants completed the first period and 15 completed both periods. Session adherence was 97.1%, with no intervention-related adverse events. The adjusted between-treatment difference in self-selected gait speed was -0.009 m/s (95% confidence interval -0.032 to 0.013; p = 0.41). No secondary outcome differed significantly between treatments. Both interventions produced modest within-treatment improvements in gait speed.

CONCLUSION: Haptic cane-assisted gait training was feasible and safe under therapist supervision but provided no additional improvement in gait speed over dose-matched conventional gait training. Further studies should evaluate outcomes more closely aligned with the proposed mechanism of haptic cane use before considering a large confirmatory trial.

articles.title: Clinical Perspectives on Heart-Kidney-Brain Crosstalk.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular, kidney, and neurological diseases are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur, reflecting an integrated heart-kidney-brain axis linked by shared hemodynamic, neurohormonal, and inflammatory pathways. This crosstalk maintains perfusion, blood volume, and metabolic homeostasis through coordinate signaling via the circulation, autonomic nervous system, and renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. When dysregulated, these same pathways perpetuate injury across organs, transforming adaptive responses into maladaptive cycles of dysfunction.This review synthesizes current understanding of the physiology and molecular mechanisms underlying heart-kidney-brain interactions, emphasizing hypoperfusion, neurohormonal activation, and convergent pathways of oxidative stress and inflammation as central drivers. Key amplifiers, including iron dysregulation, uremic toxin accumulation, and disordered mineral metabolism, extend injury systemically, contributing to cardiac remodeling, kidney disease, progression, and neurological disease. Clinically, this axis manifests as interconnected syndromes such as cardiorenal syndrome, cerebrovascular disease, and cognitive impairment. Emerging biomarkers and imaging modalities reveal overlapping signals across organs yet are rarely integrated in practice. Notably, neurological outcomes remain underrepresented in cardiovascular and kidney research despite their profound impact on quality of life, particularly in the pediatric population where disease affects lifelong development. We highlight gaps in mutli-organ diagnostic frameworks, biomarker standardization, and translational models, and propose future research directions in the heart-kidney-brain axis. Recognizing the heart, kidney, and brain as a unified system is essential to improving risk stratification, preventing multi-organ injury, and advancing patient-centered care.

articles.title: Photoacoustic imaging assessment of acute kidney injury associated with experimental necrotizing enterocolitis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
articles.abstract: Background: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a devastating gastrointestinal condition increasingly recognized to cause systemic complications, including acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the underlying mechanisms and variations in renal impairment remain largely unknown, and there is a lack of non-invasive imaging methods for detecting early kidney injury. Methods: We evaluated kidney injury through a multimodal approach, using a neonatal rat model of experimental NEC. Plasma and renal tissue were analyzed for pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) by ELISA. Histological analysis and immunofluorescence staining were used to identify renal abnormalities and expressions of KIM-1 and NGAL. Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) was used to assess renal oxygenation and total hemoglobin as functional imaging biomarkers of kidney injury. Results: NEC pups showed significant elevations of systemic and renal cytokines, as well as increased expression of KIM-1, NGAL and CD31 in proximal tubules of the kidney. Histological examination further confirms renal injury in the NEC cohort. PAI demonstrated reduction in renal oxygen saturation, offering non-invasive assessment of physiological kidney damage. Conclusion: This study characterizes AKI associated with NEC as an inflammatory and hypoxic response in the neonatal rat NEC model and introduces PAI as a promising imaging modality for non-invasive evaluation of renal injury in NEC.

articles.title: Loss of the clock protein PERIOD1 causes sex-specific impacts on the heart in Dahl salt-sensitive rats.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Salt-sensitive (SS) hypertension is a driver of cardiovascular disease. Circadian biology is implicated in hypertension. One component of the circadian molecular clock, the protein PERIOD1 (PER1), is involved in blood pressure regulation. We previously published that loss of PER1 (PER1 KO) in a rat model of SS hypertension, the Dahl SS rat, is associated with exacerbated renal injury and hypertension, as well as disrupted circadian regulation of heart rate. The cardiac and sex-specific impacts of PER1 KO in SS hypertension are undetermined. We utilized male and female PER1 KO and Dahl SS rats to investigate changes in the cardiac transcriptome, revealing sex-dependent shifts in gene expression. Male PER1 KO rats exhibited upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling. Consistent with this, male, but not female PER1 KO rats showed higher cardiac fibrosis compared to their Dahl SS counterparts. Terminal measurements revealed that male, but not female PER1 KO rats had increased blood pressure compared to Dahl SS controls. Given the lack of an apparent phenotype in females, only male subjects were used for subsequent ultrasound echocardiography studies. We determined longitudinal in vivo cardiac function in male rats during normal salt and 14 days of high salt diet. This revealed reduced stroke volume and decreased cardiac output at baseline, prior to exposure to high salt diet in male PER1 KO rats. These results indicate that impaired cardiac function may predispose PER1 KO rats to salt-sensitive hypertension.

articles.title: Heart and Skeletal Muscle Contributions to Exercise Intolerance in Type 2 Diabetes: An Integrated Physiological Perspective.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Exercise intolerance is a hallmark of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). It is typically characterised by a reduction in peak oxygen uptake (V̇O2peak), which is a strong independent predictor of cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Reduced V̇O2peak in T2DM has traditionally been attributed to central cardiovascular abnormalities which ultimately limit oxygen delivery to the exercising muscles. However, these abnormalities do not always fully account for the observed reduction. Increasing evidence suggests more peripheral involvement affecting oxygen transport through the skeletal muscle microvascular networks to the mitochondria, as well as mitochondrial oxygen extraction and utilisation. At the same time, the diabetic skeletal muscle exhibits intrinsic abnormalities such as insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, metabolic inflexibility, and endothelial dysfunction, all of which may further compromise exercise capacity. Sarcopenia is another clinically relevant manifestation of skeletal muscle dysfunction in T2DM that may play a role in exercise limitation. In particular, muscle quality may be more functionally relevant than muscle mass or strength alone. Emerging evidence also suggests that cardiac and skeletal muscle abnormalities interact through inter-organ crosstalk, potentially exacerbating dysfunction in both tissues and compounding exercise intolerance. This review examines the independent and interacting contributions of cardiac and skeletal muscle dysfunction to reduced V̇O2peak in T2DM, with particular emphasis on evidence from multivariable analyses. Preclinical studies are also considered where they provide mechanistic insight. Finally, we identify priorities for future research, including integrated cardiac and skeletal muscle phenotyping, to better define the mechanisms of exercise intolerance in T2DM and inform targeted therapeutic interventions in T2DM.

articles.title: Adaptive host manipulation by parasites: From phenomena to a causal framework.
articles.abstract: Parasite-induced alterations in host phenotypes are widespread across diverse taxa, yet their evolutionary significance remains difficult to establish. A central challenge in this field is not the scarcity of examples, but distinguishing adaptive parasite manipulation from host responses to infection or incidental pathological consequences. The adaptive manipulation hypothesis proposes that parasites modify host traits in ways that increase transmission or reproductive success, but empirical evidence for this interpretation remains largely correlative, with few studies establishing a direct causal relationship between altered host phenotypes and parasite fitness. In this review, we critically examine the evidence for adaptive host manipulation and develop a framework for distinguishing parasite adaptations from alternative explanations. We identify four criteria for evaluating putative manipulation: stage-specific temporal alignment, independence from host compensatory responses, demonstration of a net parasite fitness advantage, and evidence of mechanistic causality. These criteria provide a hierarchical basis for assessing the strength of evidence across host-parasite systems. Applying this framework to widely cited examples reveals that several canonical cases lack sufficient evidence to establish adaptive manipulation. We further examine the molecular processes implicated in host phenotypic modification, including neural interference, immune modulation, endocrine disruption, and gene regulatory changes, highlighting the limited functional evidence linking these processes to parasite-induced phenotypes. To address these gaps, we propose an integrated research strategy combining spatially and temporally resolved transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, and targeted functional perturbations, to establish causal links among molecular mechanisms, host phenotypic changes, and parasite fitness. By emphasizing causal evidence rather than descriptive associations, this review provides a conceptual and methodological framework for critically evaluating adaptive host manipulation and clarifying its evolutionary significance in host-parasite interactions.

articles.title: Angiotensin and high-salt diet induce systemic inflammation and alter cardiac resident macrophage phenotype in Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J mice.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: Acute decompensation of heart failure is associated with high mortality and the role of genetic risk factors remain poorly understood. Balb/CJ mice rapidly decompensate following a treatment with angiotensin II and high-salt diet (AngII+Salt). They present with reduced cardiac output, peripheral edema, and high mortality while C57BL/6J are protected. The aim of this study was to identify molecular pathways that explain the detrimental cardiac adaptations in Balb/CJ compared to C57BL/6J mice. Both Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J mice showed signs of cardiac hypertrophy after treatment with AngII+Salt, whereas only Balb/CJ mice developed substantial pulmonary edema and reduced cardiac output. Cardiac gene expression was measured using microarrays in Sham, AngII, Salt and AngII+Salt treated Balb/CJ and C57BL/6J. Already at baseline, cardiac gene expression was significantly different between the strains. Following AngII and AngII+Salt treatment, angiotensin II was the main driver of cardiac gene expression. Enrichment analysis of genes containing SNPs and exhibiting differential expression following AngII, Salt or AngII+Salt treatment identified several immune-related pathways. Angiotensin II was the dominant driver of systemic inflammation in both strains, measured as plasma IL-6, IL-16 and CCL2. Interestingly, combining angiotensin II and high-salt diet exhibited a synergistic effect on systemic inflammation. AngII+Salt altered phenotype of cardiac resident macrophages in both strains without affecting immune cell infiltration. In conclusion, angiotensin II is the main driver of cardiac gene expression following AngII+Salt treatment which is associated with systemic inflammation and altered cardiac resident macrophage phenotype in both Balb/CJ mice and C57BL/6J mice.

articles.title: Genetically homogeneous C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N mice exhibit differential physiological dysfunction compared to genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
articles.abstract: The most commonly used animal models in biomedical research are genetically homogeneous C57BL/6 mice. We recently demonstrated that genetically heterogeneous UM-HET3 mice have greater vascular function than C57BL/6 substrains, including lower aortic stiffness and greater endothelium-dependent dilation. To expand on our previous studies, we examined metabolic, microcirculatory, hematological, and inflammatory phenotypes in C57BL/6J, C57BL/6N, and UM-HET3 mice. UM-HET3 mice exhibited greater body mass and lower non-fasting blood glucose compared to C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). Glucose tolerance was greater in UM-HET3 and C57BL/6N compared to C57BL/6J mice (P<0.05), while insulin sensitivity was greater in UM-HET3 and C57BL/6J compared to C57BL/6N mice (P<0.05). UM-HET3 mice had greater mesenteric microvascular density, glycocalyx integrity, and glycocalyx thickness than both C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). UM-HET3 mice also had lower total white blood cell concentration, higher neutrophil and lower lymphocyte proportions than C57BL/6J, and higher hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, and MCH than C57BL/6 substrains (P<0.05). Cytokine profiling revealed differences between UM-HET3 and C57BL/6J in G-CSF, IL-1β, IP-10, MIP-2, and VEGF, as well as between UM-HET3 and C57BL/6N in IFN-γ, IL-5, and IP-10 (P<0.05). Coefficients of variation were similar across strains for most outcomes, indicating that genetic heterogeneity in UM-HET3 mice did not increase variability. These findings demonstrate metabolic, microcirculatory, hematological, and inflammatory differences in UM-HET3 compared to C57BL/6 substrains, and between C57BL/6J and C57BL/6N mice. UM-HET3 mice appear to have a healthier physiological phenotype than C57BL/6 mice, indicating their potential as a research model; however, whether these differences persist with aging or predict later-life health outcomes remains unknown.

articles.title: Dedicated devices for the treatment of calcified coronary artery disease: a three-year Belgian survey of utilization trends.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adoption of calcium-modifying devices in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is shaped by international recommendations, published evidence, national reimbursement policy, and local catheterisation-laboratory practice, all of which influence the distribution of these technologies.

AIMS: To evaluate the adoption of calcium-modifying devices across Belgium through a national survey.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Procedural data on total PCI volume and six calcium-modifying devices - rotational and orbital atherectomy, intravascular lithotripsy, cutting, scoring, and super-high-pressure balloons - were collected from 26 Belgian catheterisation laboratories (Belgian Calcium Survey) over three consecutive years (2023-2025). Centre-level and survey-wide usage rates were calculated annually and benchmarked against international registries. Total device-use instances increased by approximately 70%, from 2,418 in 2023 to 4,136 in 2025, against an essentially unchanged PCI volume. The increase was driven predominantly by cutting and scoring balloons (85% of additional instances), with a smaller rise in rotational atherectomy; orbital atherectomy remained marginal (4/26 centres). Between-centre use was highly variable, spanning approximately 48-fold. Rotational atherectomy was concentrated in a minority of centres, with the 5 highest-volume centres performing 47-49% of national volume.

CONCLUSIONS: Calcium-modifying device use increased substantially across Belgium between 2023 and 2025, driven mainly by cutting balloons and rotational atherectomy, possibly accelerated by the 2024 reimbursement change for the latter. Distribution across centres was highly variable. Atherectomy use rates remained within the range reported by international registries. Imaging-guided device selection may improve consistency of use, as current evidence provides no single gold-standard solution and available technologies continue to expand.

articles.title: Mechanical thrombectomy with CEREGLIDE 71 Intermediate Catheter: A single-center post-market experience.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the efficacy and safety of the CEREGLIDE 71 Intermediate Catheter in a real-world clinical setting.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, post-market observational study. All consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) who underwent mechanical thrombectomy (MT) with CEREGLIDE 71 between October 2024 and September 2025 were included. The primary outcome was the rate of successful recanalization (final modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] ≥2b). Secondary efficacy outcomes included complete revascularization (final mTICI ≥2c), first-pass mTICI ≥2c, and first-pass mTICI ≥2b. Safety and clinical outcomes included device-related adverse events, such as vessel dissection, perforation, or catheter breakage, and good functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score ≤2). The subgroup of patients treated with a direct aspiration first-pass technique (ADAPT) as the first-line approach was also analyzed.

RESULTS: A total of 75 patients underwent MT with CEREGLIDE 71 between October 2024 and September 2025. First-line technique was ADAPT in 76% of procedures (57/75) and combined technique in 24% (18/75). Successful revascularization (mTICI ≥2b) was achieved in 88.0% of patients (66/75). Good functional outcome (90-day mRS ≤2) was observed in 57.3% of patients (43/75). No device-related adverse events were recorded. In the ADAPT subgroup, the SNAKE technique allowed the catheter to reach the clot in 93.0% of cases (53/57).

CONCLUSIONS: CEREGLIDE 71 appeared to be a feasible and effective option for MT in patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion (LVO), reaching the occlusion site with the SNAKE technique alone in most procedures.

articles.title: B cells infected with Salmonella downregulates BCR signaling complex.
articles.abstract: Salmonella Typhimurium (S. Typhimurium) can infect B cells, and this cellular microenvironment can confer on changes or capabilities such as persistence. These changes can occur in both the bacterium and the B cell. Therefore, the objective of the study was to analyze changes in B cells after S. Typhimurium infection. Using an In vitro infection model, the data indicates that the expression of molecules such as CD79a and CD79b, which are part of the B cell receptor (BCR) complex, is downregulated in infected B cells. An increase in the I-Ab molecule was observed in infected cells, while H2-Kb levels were reduced, suggesting impaired antigen presentation. Proteomics analysis shows that various proteins were altered by infection. One of the processes affected is the B-cell activation pathway and the adaptive immune response. In general, these changes could indicate B-cell dysfunction due to S. Typhimurium infection.

articles.title: Life-Threatening Pancytopenia and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Associated With Hydralazine-Induced Lupus and Vasculitis Overlap: A Comprehensive Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND This report presents a life-threatening case of pancytopenia and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) related to hydralazine-associated, drug-induced lupus and drug-induced anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (DIL/DIV) overlap syndrome. Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges are discussed. CASE REPORT A 52-year-old man presented with severe pancytopenia, fever, and possible pneumonia. He developed altered mental status, severe DIC with gastrointestinal bleeds requiring large amount of blood product transfusions, acute respiratory failure requiring intubation, acute kidney injury needing hemodialysis, acute liver injury, possible acute pancreatitis, and hypotension. Extensive investigations revealed no source of infection. Further workup was consistent with hydralazine-induced DIL/DIV overlap spectrum. Hydralazine was stopped. He was treated with steroids daily and intravenous cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks (7 doses). However, pancytopenia did not improve. Therefore, on the seventh day after the second cyclophosphamide dose, a repeat bone marrow biopsy was performed to guide further therapy. He later recovered, and hemodialysis was discontinued. A total of 104 units of blood products were transfused. After discharge, steroids were tapered off and mycophenolate mofetil was given for 2 years. In August 2026 (6 years after initial presentation), he was doing well, with normal complete blood count, stable renal function, and normal urinalysis. Array genotyping revealed NAT2 diplotype *5.002/*6.002, indicating slow acetylation (poor metabolizer status). CONCLUSIONS This case supports, rather than proves, hydralazine-induced DIL/DIV overlap as the leading explanation for life-threatening pancytopenia with overt DIC. It highlights diagnostic and therapeutic challenges and eventual recovery after hydralazine withdrawal and immunosuppressive treatment. Salient features include the detailed autoimmune workup, severe presentation, coexistence of pancytopenia and overt DIC, and extended follow-up within a rare clinical context.

articles.title: Hypophosphatemia in Pediatric Diabetic Ketoacidosis: Incidence, Determinants, and Clinical Impact in a Tertiary Emergency and Intensive Care Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Serum phosphate levels commonly decline during treatment of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), but the determinants and clinical implications of hypophosphatemia remain incompletely defined. We aimed to determine its incidence, predictors, and clinical impact during pediatric DKA.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 116 DKA episodes managed in a tertiary pediatric emergency department and intensive care unit between January 2022 and June 2025 were analyzed. Demographic characteristics, admission biochemical parameters, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Hypophosphatemia was defined according to age-specific reference ranges. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of hypophosphatemia, while length of hospital stay was assessed using multivariable linear regression of log-transformed values.

RESULTS: Hypophosphatemia occurred in 72/116 episodes (62.1%). Compared with those without hypophosphatemia, affected patients had lower admission pH (7.03±0.13 vs. 7.12±0.17; P=0.002), bicarbonate (7.8±2.4 vs. 9.8±3.3 mEq/L; P<0.001), and potassium levels (4.43±0.96 vs. 4.81±0.66 mEq/L; P=0.024). Hyponatremia and hypokalemia were more frequent, whereas hyperkalemia was less common (all P<0.05). Lower admission pH (OR: 0.008, 95% CI: 0.000-0.219; P=0.004) and lower baseline phosphate concentration (OR: 0.67, 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; P=0.031) independently predicted hypophosphatemia. Although hospitalization was longer in the hypophosphatemia group (85.3±75.2 vs. 56.2±36.4 h; P=0.018), hypophosphatemia was not independently associated with length of stay. Higher admission pH independently predicted shorter hospitalization (β=-0.957, P=0.026). Baseline phosphate positively correlated with nadir phosphate during treatment (r=0.303, P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Hypophosphatemia is common during pediatric DKA and is closely associated with the severity of metabolic acidosis at presentation. However, it does not independently affect hospitalization duration, suggesting that it primarily reflects disease severity rather than independently determining short-term outcomes.

articles.title: Insurance status and in-hospital outcomes in cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insurance-related differences in outcomes of cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction (AMI-CS) remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: Using the 2017-2022 National Inpatient Sample, we compared Medicare (reference), Medicaid, private, and other/uninsured payers among adults with AMI-CS. Survey-weighted regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for in-hospital mortality and nonhome discharge among survivors, and adjusted differences in length of stay and cost separately among survivors and nonsurvivors. Models adjusted for demographic, hospital, comorbidity, and calendar-year factors; sequential models added clinical severity indicators and procedures.

RESULTS: Among 447 435 weighted hospitalizations, unadjusted mortality ranged from 27% (private) to 39% (Medicare). Relative to Medicare, other/uninsured patients had higher adjusted mortality [aOR: 1.26, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19-1.34], private insurance lower mortality (aOR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.83-0.91), and Medicaid no significant difference (aOR: 1.01, 95% CI: 0.95-1.07). The other/uninsured association persisted after adjustment for coded severity indicators and procedures (aOR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.10-1.26), was strongest among self-pay patients (aOR: 1.42), and was consistent across years and sensitivity analyses. Adjusted receipt of revascularization and mechanical circulatory support did not differ significantly between other/uninsured and Medicare patients.

CONCLUSION: Insurance status was associated with in-hospital mortality in AMI-CS. Excess mortality among other/uninsured patients, particularly self-pay patients, persisted after adjustment for available coded severity indicators and procedure use. Hemodynamic severity and treatment timing were unavailable; residual confounding cannot be excluded.

articles.title: The Diagnostic Value of Overnight Fluid Deprivation to Distinguish AVP Deficiency from Primary Polydipsia.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Overnight fluid deprivation is widely used to differentiate arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) from primary polydipsia (PP), yet its diagnostic performance has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed its diagnostic performance using high-specificity rule-in thresholds.

METHODS/DESIGN: A secondary analysis of a prospective, international multicentre study. Patients with hypotonic polyuria underwent an indirect water-deprivation test and copeptin-based hypertonic saline test. Serum sodium, calculated and measured serum osmolality, urine osmolality, and plasma copeptin were analysed at baseline and after 8 hours of overnight fluid deprivation. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using rule-in thresholds. The final diagnosis was established by two independent endocrinologists based on all available clinical, biochemical, imaging, and 3-month follow-up data.

RESULTS: Among 141 patients, 59(42%) had AVP-D and 82(58%) had PP. For AVP-D, serum sodium >146 mmol/L and calculated serum osmolarity >300 mOsm/L achieved 100% specificity both at baseline and after overnight fluid deprivation, with sensitivities increasing from 5% to 20% and from 9% to 25%, respectively. For PP, urine osmolality >650 mOsm/kg achieved 100% specificity at baseline and 97% after overnight fluid deprivation, and a plasma copeptin >5.6 pmol/L showed high specificity for PP at baseline and after overnight fluid deprivation (100% and 98%, respectively). Baseline assessment classified 23% of patients with 100% accuracy. Overnight fluid deprivation increased the proportion classified to 40%, with an overall accuracy of 98%, leaving 60% diagnostically indeterminate.

CONCLUSION: Overnight fluid deprivation combined with high-specificity thresholds enables reliable rule-in of AVP-D and PP and may reduce the need for complex diagnostic testing.

articles.title: Drug-Coated Balloons Versus Drug-Eluting Stents in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Reconstructed Individual Patient Data and GRADE Assessment.
articles.abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face high ischemic and bleeding risks. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) avoid a permanent implant and permit shorter dual antiplatelet therapy. We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through May 2026 for studies comparing DCB with drug-eluting stents (DES) in adults with CKD undergoing PCI. Study-level hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled with random-effects inverse-variance models; individual patient data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves, and certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Five studies (two prespecified CKD analyses of randomized trials and three cohorts) comprising 2527 patients (1149 DCB and 1378 DES) were included. DCB and DES did not differ in the composite of major adverse cardiovascular or device-oriented events [HR 0.98; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.77-1.24; IPD HR 0.96; 95% CI, 0.74-1.25], target-lesion revascularization (HR 1.02; 95% CI, 0.73-1.42), cardiac death (HR 0.94; 95% CI, 0.64-1.39), or myocardial infarction (HR 0.62; 95% CI, 0.36-1.06). Major bleeding did not differ significantly (HR 0.39; 95% CI, 0.13-1.17; IPD HR 0.51; 95% CI, 0.25-1.02). Stent or lesion thrombosis occurred only after DES (0/594 vs 12/810). Certainty was moderate for the composite endpoint and low for other outcomes.

articles.title: Morning Versus Evening Antihypertensive Medication and Risk of Cardiovascular Disease: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Hypertension significantly contributes to the risk of cardiovascular disease and associated mortality. The timing of medication use and associated cardiovascular outcomes is not well established, with conflicting results. We evaluated the association between morning versus evening antihypertensive medication and cardiovascular outcomes. We performed a systematic literature search on PubMed, Scopus, and ClinicalTrial.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) from inception until June 5, 2026. Studies were considered eligible for inclusion if patients with hypertension received antihypertensive medication in the intervention group during the morning/daytime and in the control group in the evening. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using a random-effect model, and a P value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Six RCTs with 46,857 patients (23,488 assigned to morning antihypertensive medication and 23,369 assigned to evening antihypertensive medication) were included in the analysis. The mean age of patients was 63.3 years. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant difference between morning and evening antihypertensive medication dosing for all-cause mortality (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.92-1.85, P = 0.14), major adverse cardiovascular events (OR 1.28, 95% CI 0.93-1.76, P = 0.13), or stroke (OR 1.45, 95% CI 0.96-2.19, P = 0.08). This meta-analysis supports the findings of the BEDMED 2025 trial, with no significant differences between morning and evening administration of antihypertensive drugs and cardiovascular outcomes.

articles.title: Vernakalant Versus Other Antiarrhythmic Drugs for Pharmacological Cardioversion of Recent-Onset Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis.
articles.abstract: Vernakalant is an atrial-selective antiarrhythmic drug for the rapid conversion of recent-onset atrial fibrillation, but its effectiveness relative to alternative drugs remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis included studies comparing intravenous vernakalant with another antiarrhythmic drug in adults with recent-onset atrial fibrillation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through March 2026. The primary outcome was conversion to sinus rhythm; secondary outcomes were time to conversion, electrical cardioversion, and adverse events. Random-effects models, trial sequential analysis, and GRADE were used. Nine studies (3 randomized, 1 quasi-randomized, and 5 observational; 1788 patients or episodes) compared vernakalant with amiodarone, ibutilide, flecainide, procainamide, or propafenone. Conversion occurred in 69.0% of patients receiving vernakalant and 53.0% of those receiving a comparator (odds ratio [OR], 2.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.51-4.21; I2 = 72%). Heterogeneity was explained by the amiodarone comparisons (OR, 18.14; interaction P < 0.001); against the other comparators, the OR was 1.77 (95% CI, 1.41-2.22; I2 = 0%). Vernakalant shortened time to conversion among responders (mean difference, -19.3 minutes; 95% CI, -24.2 to -14.4) and reduced electrical cardioversion (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.34-0.73), without a significant difference in adverse events (OR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.57-1.08). The cumulative Z-curve crossed the trial sequential monitoring boundary, but the certainty of evidence was low for all outcomes.

articles.title: Limitations in the Definition of Cardiogenic Shock and the Prospect of Total Body Impedance Cardiography: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The mortality rate of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (CS) has remained unchanged over the past 3 decades despite advances in cardiac critical care interventions and numerous clinical trials focused on this subject. This is likely in part due to an inconsistent and sometimes subjective definition of CS used in the literature, which has limited the ability to identify patients in the earlier stages of shock and intervene promptly. No prior research has objectively assessed the reliability of the current definitions of CS utilized in the literature for identifying patients at risk of adverse outcomes, or characterized the hemodynamic profile of all-comer ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients in a manner that predicts outcomes. The identification of early predictors of poor outcomes in patients presenting with STEMI-CS would allow for earlier intervention and potentially improved outcomes. Total body impedance cardiography is a modality that can be utilized to monitor the hemodynamics in STEMI patients in real-time and could be useful in future research on this critically ill patient population.

articles.title: Cardiac Structure and Function After Preeclampsia, Including Global Longitudinal Strain: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Preeclampsia is associated with an increased long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and heart failure, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Whether abnormalities of cardiac structure and function persist after delivery, and whether global longitudinal strain (GLS) detects subclinical myocardial dysfunction when left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved, remains incompletely defined. We updated the evidence on postpartum cardiac structure and function after preeclampsia and synthesized postpartum GLS. Of the 27 studies in the index review, 25 provided re-extractable arm-level data; with 5 new studies, the data set comprised 30 reports and 32 comparisons. Prior preeclampsia was associated with a higher left ventricular mass index (MD, 5.24 g/m2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.77-7.70; k = 25), greater relative wall thickness (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; k = 16), higher E/e' (MD, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; k = 15), and lower E/A (MD, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.02; k = 23). Left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (MD, -0.62 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.51 to 0.27; k = 25), nor did isovolumic relaxation or deceleration time. GLS was less negative after preeclampsia (MD, 2.05 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.34-3.76; k = 4).

articles.title: Evaluating Tau Accumulation in a Patient Undergoing Long-Term Maintenance Electroconvulsive Therapy: A Case Report Using Florzolotau (18F) Imaging.
articles.abstract: While modified electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is highly effective for treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders, concerns persist regarding its long-term impact on neurodegenerative pathologies, such as tau protein accumulation. We report the case of an 82-year-old female with bipolar disorder who underwent over 120 sessions of modified maintenance ECT (mECT) over 12 years. To investigate potential neurodegenerative changes associated with prolonged electrical stimulation, we performed positron emission tomography (PET) using florzolotau (18F), a high-sensitivity ligand for a broad range of tauopathies. The standardized uptake value ratio in the cerebral cortex was 0.72, indicating no significant tau deposition. Furthermore, clinical cognitive assessments, including the Revised Hasegawa's Dementia Scale (HDS-R) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), demonstrated no clinically significant progression of cognitive decline over the 4-year period leading up to the PET scan. These findings suggest that appropriately managed long-term mECT using brief-pulse stimulation may not induce or accelerate tau-related neurodegenerative pathology, even in elderly patients.

articles.title: High Prevalence of Multidrug-resistant Gram-negative Bacteria on Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Surfaces at a Tertiary Hospital in Kampala, Uganda.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: About 60% of neonatal sepsis cases are hospital-acquired and are often caused by Gram-negative bacteria, with a high rate of antimicrobial resistance. Outbreaks of multidrug-resistant bacteria in neonatal units occur at rates 20 times higher in low- and middle-income countries than in high-income settings. We conducted 4 rounds (R1-4) of environmental sampling in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in Kampala, Uganda, to inform an infection prevention and control (IPC) program tailored to a resource-limited setting.

METHODS: Eighty-two swabs were taken over 12 months (2021-2022) from n = 13 high-touch surfaces, n = 10 low-touch surfaces (R1-3) and n = 6 staff items (R4). Potential pathogens were identified using standard biochemical methods. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion. Hand hygiene audits were conducted throughout the study period. A collaborative working group of NICU, IPC and research staff co-developed IPC interventions.

RESULTS: Of 146 organisms isolated, 127 (82%) were potential pathogens, predominantly Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp. and Citrobacter spp. High-touch sites such as sinks, cots and drug trolleys showed persistent contamination. Resistance to first-line antibiotics was high: gentamicin (48/91, 52%), ampicillin (25/25, 100%) and ceftazidime (30/91, 33%). After color-coded feedback, a unit-wide deep clean reduced potential pathogens by 60% from R1 (n = 63) to R2 (n = 25). However, levels rebounded in R3 (n = 32), representing a 21% increase compared with R2 (n = 25), highlighting inconsistencies in cleaning.

CONCLUSIONS: Targeted environmental cleaning can reduce NICU contamination by multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens. Sinks were persistent reservoirs, underscoring the need for consistent daily cleaning and staff engagement. In low- and middle-income country settings, simple, low-cost IPC measures informed by environmental surveillance may support sustainable hospital-acquired infection reduction.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model.

METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach.

RESULTS: Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.

articles.title: Levosimendan in Acute Myocardial Infarction After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Levosimendan may improve myocardial recovery after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for acute myocardial infarction, but randomized evidence remains uncertain. We assessed clinical effects after PCI versus placebo or active inotropes. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and CENTRAL from inception through November 19, 2025, for randomized controlled trials of adults with acute myocardial infarction treated with PCI. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled mean differences (MDs) or risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, and certainty using GRADE. Nine randomized controlled trials reported in 11 publications enrolled 662 unique participants. Compared with control, levosimendan did not significantly improve left ventricular ejection fraction (5 studies; MD, 6.20 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.63 to 13.03; P = 0.065; I2 = 84.2%). The left ventricular ejection fraction estimate became significant after excluding one influential trial (MD, 8.11; 95% CI, 0.97-15.25), indicating sensitivity. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (2 studies) was lower with levosimendan (MD, -7.50 mL/m2; 95% CI, -14.94 to -0.05; P = 0.0497), but certainty was low. No significant differences were observed in left ventricular end-diastolic or end-systolic volume, wall motion score index, heart rate, cardiac index, mean arterial pressure, or all-cause mortality. Certainty was low or very low across all seven assessed GRADE outcomes.

articles.title: Pectus Excavatum and Cardiopulmonary Function: Pathophysiology, Cardiovascular Assessment, and Outcomes After Minimally Invasive Repair.
articles.abstract: Pectus excavatum (PEx) is the most common congenital chest wall deformity, occurring in 1:250 to 1:1000 live births. PEx is a condition in which the anterior chest wall is depressed, creating an "excavation" of the sternum. Many patients with PEx report symptoms, including chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, and exercise intolerance. Current literature links these symptoms to physiological abnormalities, such as decreased peak oxygen consumption (VO2 max) and stroke volume. Furthermore, electrocardiographic conduction defects and axis deviation are common. Recent data suggest that surgical repair, utilizing the minimally invasive Nuss procedure, may improve cardiopulmonary function in patients with PEx. Further research is necessary to better characterize the impact of the Nuss procedure on cardiopulmonary metrics, as well as to better inform patient selection for surgical repair.

articles.title: Functional and lncRNA changes in ovine blood monocytes and derived macrophages following paratuberculosis vaccination.
articles.abstract: Vaccination is central to control paratuberculosis in ruminants. Commercial vaccines such as Gudair®, although not fully preventing infection, reduce clinical signs and faecal shedding. Nevertheless, their protective immunological mechanisms remain unclear. This study evaluated the effect of Gudair® vaccination on mononuclear phagocyte function in sheep (Ovis aries) and correlated it with their long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) expression. Ten Assaf lambs were divided into vaccinated (n = 5) and non-vaccinated (n = 5) groups. Peripheral blood was collected before vaccination and at 30-, 60- and 90-days post-vaccination (dpv) to assess antigen-specific IFN-γ and antibody responses. Phagocytosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production were evaluated in the monocyte fraction following in vitro Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (Map) infection of whole blood. At 90 dpv, monocytes were also isolated from peripheral blood to generate ovine monocyte-derived macrophages (OvMDMs) to assess Map phagocytosis and intracellular survival and lncRNAs expression analysis by RNA-seq. Vaccination induced increased IFN-γ and anti-Map antibody responses over time. Monocytes from vaccinated lambs showed significantly higher ROS production at 90 dpv (p < 0.05), whereas phagocytosis did not differ between groups. No significant differences were observed in OvMDMs regarding Map phagocytosis or bacterial survival. Transcriptome analysis of monocytes at 90 dpv identified 6854 lncRNAs (4719 annotated and 2135 novel), of which four were differentially expressed between groups. Cis- and trans-based computational analyses identified potential associations with genes involved in immune-related pathways. These findings improve our understanding of the innate immune responses induced by paratuberculosis vaccination and identify candidate lncRNAs for further investigation in vaccine-induced immunity.

articles.title: Mortality prediction at the tracheostomy decision point after liver transplantation: development and internal validation of a bedside risk score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Liver-transplant (LT) recipients requiring prolonged ventilation and considered for percutaneous dilatational tracheostomy (PDT) have high short-term mortality, but LT-specific tools to support prognosis-aligned communication at this decision point are lacking. We developed and internally validated a simple PDT-day model and an integer Tracheostomy Decision-Point Risk Score (TRS) to estimate 90-day mortality from the PDT decision point in LT recipients undergoing PDT.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 83 adult LT recipients undergoing PDT between December 2010 and June 2024. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 90 days from the PDT decision point, operationalized as the day of PDT. The model estimates risk after the PDT decision point and not the causal effect of PDT. Logistic regression used routinely available PDT-day variables; internal validation used bootstrap shrinkage. Discrimination and calibration were assessed by AUC, Brier score, calibration-in-the-large, and calibration slope. Coefficients were converted to an integer TRS.

RESULTS: 90-day mortality was 62.7% (52/83). Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD; +5 points), age (+ 10 years), and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT; +5 s) measured on the PDT day were independently associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratios 2.54 [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.45-4.47], 1.97 [1.16-3.36], and 1.53 [1.02-2.28], respectively; all p ≤ 0.040). Discrimination was good (AUC 0.846; bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.829 [95% CI 0.74-0.93]) with favorable calibration (calibration-in-the-large - 0.01; slope 1.02). The TRS (+ 2 points per + 5 MELD, + 2 per + 10 years, + 1 per + 5 s aPTT) retained discrimination (AUC 0.831) and stratified observed 90-day mortality: 38% (14/37) low, 72% (13/18) intermediate, and 89% (25/28) high. 90-day survival differed across bands (global log-rank p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: For LT recipients who reach the PDT decision point and undergo PDT, the TRS provides internally validated 90-day mortality estimates that may support prognosis-informed multidisciplinary deliberation and bedside risk communication. It should be used only as one component of decision-making and does not estimate the causal effects of PDT, no-PDT strategies, or PDT timing. Use in prolonged-ICU LT recipients without PDT requires separate validation.

articles.title: Perceived impact of epilepsy on key life domains among people with epilepsy in Damascus, Syria: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy affects multiple aspects of daily life beyond seizure control, yet evidence regarding its psychosocial impact remains scarce in conflict-affected settings such as Syria. This study assessed the self-reported impact of epilepsy on key life domains and explored associated clinical and psychosocial factors among people with epilepsy in Damascus, Syria.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among patients with neurologist-confirmed epilepsy attending three private neurology clinics and an outpatient neurology clinic at a governmental hospital in Damascus. Participants (n = 64) completed a study-specific, culturally tailored, self-administered questionnaire that included demographic and clinical variables and a four-item composite measure assessing the perceived impact of epilepsy on key life domains.

RESULTS: Overall, the perceived impact of epilepsy was very high or high in 40.6% of participants, moderate in 21.9%, and absent in 14.1%. Greater perceived impact was significantly associated with a higher number of adverse drug reactions (P = 0.009), more self-reported psychiatric symptoms (P = 0.002), and perceived stigma (P = 0.017), whereas no significant associations were observed with age, sex, or seizure frequency. Although 35.9% of participants reported fewer than one seizure per year, many continued to report substantial adverse effects on important areas of daily life.

CONCLUSIONS: Even among a sample that included participants reporting infrequent seizures, epilepsy was associated with a considerable self-reported impact on important aspects of daily living. These findings highlight the importance of comprehensive epilepsy care that addresses psychosocial as well as biomedical determinants of patient well-being.

articles.title: Ultrasound screening and secukinumab intervention for subclinical and clinical psoriatic arthritis: a prospective real-world study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This prospective real-world study primarily evaluated clinical and ultrasonographic outcomes after 24 weeks of secukinumab treatment in participants with subclinical or clinical psoriatic arthritis (PsA) identified through a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound screening pathway. A secondary descriptive objective was to characterize the screening pathway and the identification of ultrasound-detected subclinical PsA.

METHODS: Participants with psoriasis were enrolled at the Department of Dermatology, Tianjin Medical University, from September 1, 2022, to December 31, 2023. Participants considered at increased risk of PsA underwent musculoskeletal ultrasound assessment. They were classified as having subclinical PsA, clinical PsA, or no qualifying inflammatory ultrasound findings according to clinical and imaging findings. Participants who initiated secukinumab and completed 24 weeks of treatment and follow-up were included in the therapeutic outcome analysis. The primary outcome was the proportion achieving PASI100 at week 24. Secondary outcomes included PASI75/90 responses, ACR20/50/70 responses in clinical PsA, ultrasound changes, quality-of-life measures, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Of 358 enrolled participants, 249 (69.6%) were classified as being at high risk of PsA based on the PEST score and/or prespecified clinical risk features. Among 194 high-risk participants who underwent musculoskeletal ultrasound screening, 159 had qualifying inflammatory ultrasound findings, leading to diagnoses of 42 with subclinical PsA and 117 with clinical PsA. A total of 38 participants completed a 24-week course of secukinumab. At week 24, 87.5% of subclinical PsA participants and 95.45% of clinical PsA participants achieved complete skin clearance (Psoriasis Area and Severity Index, PASI100). In the clinical PsA group, American College of Rheumatology (ACR) 20/50/70 response rates were 95.45%, 86.36%, and 72.73%, respectively. Ultrasound findings of synovitis and enthesitis improved descriptively in both groups. No serious adverse events were reported among the 38 treatment completers.

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, single-arm real-world cohort, a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound pathway identified participants with imaging positive for inflammatory synovio-entheseal involvement compatible with subclinical or clinical PsA. Among the small group who completed 24 weeks of secukinumab, substantial descriptive improvements in skin outcomes, clinical measures, and selected inflammatory ultrasound findings were observed. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound or demonstrate that secukinumab prevents progression from subclinical to clinical PsA. Key Points • In this exploratory cohort, a risk-based musculoskeletal ultrasound pathway identified imaging inflammatory abnormalities compatible with subclinical PsA in selected high-risk participants with psoriasis; the diagnostic accuracy of ultrasound was not assessed. • Among 38 treatment completers who received secukinumab for dermatologic indications, high PASI75/90/100 and ACR20/50/70 response rates were observed at 24 weeks; given the single-arm, uncontrolled design, these responses cannot be attributed specifically to secukinumab. • Inflammatory ultrasound findings of synovitis and enthesitis improved descriptively in both groups, supporting ultrasound as a complementary tool for monitoring treatment response rather than as a stand-alone diagnostic tes. • Enthesitis most frequently involved the finger flexor and extensor tendons, the quadriceps tendon, and the Achilles tendon; isolated structural entheseal abnormalities (e.g., bone spurs and calcifications) were common and were not interpreted as active inflammation.

articles.title: Liver Disease in Older Adults: Diagnosis, Management, and Transplantations.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize age-specific considerations in the diagnosis and management of liver disease in adults aged 65 years and older, with emphasis on cirrhosis, liver transplantation, frailty, and cognitive impairment.

RECENT FINDINGS: Age alters the performance and tolerability of commonly used diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Age-adjusted interpretation of serum fibrosis tests, sequential use of elastography, careful titration of cirrhosis therapies, and routine frailty assessment can reduce avoidable harm. Transplant outcomes in carefully selected older recipients remain acceptable, and chronological age alone should not determine candidacy. The care of the older adults with liver disease should integrate disease severity with physiologic reserve, comorbidity, function, medication safety, and cognition. A structured evaluation is particularly important when hepatic encephalopathy overlaps with delirium or dementia.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid alleviates blast wave-induced lung injury by promoting macrophage polarization and efferocytosis.
articles.abstract: Blast wave-induced lung injury is one of the leading causes of death in individuals exposed to explosions, and there is still no well-established treatment available. Rosmarinic acid (RA), a naturally occurring phenolic compound, has long been recognized for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, but whether it can protect against blast-induced lung damage has not been clearly defined. In this study, we screened the anti-inflammatory activity of RA in vitro. Then evaluated its therapeutic potential in a mouse model of blast wave-induced lung injury established using a shock tube. Bioinformatics analysis and molecular docking, identified ​extracellular signal-regulated kinase(s) (ERK) as a ​ candidate target of RA. scRNA-seq data revealed that lung injury was accompanied by a reduction in M2 macrophages and weakened communication between macrophages and epithelial cells, both of which appeared to be linked to ERK signaling. Western blotting and IHC assays confirmed that ERK phosphorylation was significantly upregulated following injury. Furthermore RA could restore the phagocytic capacity of macrophages toward apoptotic cells, and this effect was mediated through ERK. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that RA effectively ameliorates blast wave-induced lung injury by inhibiting ERK, thereby promoting M2 polarization of pulmonary macrophages and enhancing their clearance of damaged epithelial cells.

articles.title: Serum lipidomic remodeling associated with MASLD in Alström syndrome: comparison with BMI-matched obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alström syndrome (ALMS) is an ultra-rare monogenic ciliopathy with early-onset metabolic dysfunction and a high burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). However, the metabolic and lipidomic features of MASLD in ALMS remain poorly defined.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional case-control study including patients with ALMS, BMI z-score-matched obesity controls, and healthy controls. Clinical phenotyping, metabolomics, lipidomics, network analysis, regression, and Random Forest analysis were integrated to characterize MASLD-associated lipid remodeling and prioritize candidate lipid signatures.

RESULTS: Ninety-four participants were included: 30 with ALMS, 33 obesity controls, and 31 healthy controls. MASLD assessments were available for 83 participants (24 with ALMS, 30 obesity controls, and 29 healthy controls). MASLD was present in 75.0% (18/24) of patients with ALMS versus 23.3% (7/30) of obesity controls, despite comparable obesity severity. Lipidomic analyses revealed coordinated remodeling. Ether-linked phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine species were predominantly inversely associated with MASLD, whereas diacylglycerols, phosphatidic acids, and triglycerides showed positive associations. Integrated analyses further prioritized candidate lipid signatures for future validation.

CONCLUSION: ALMS-associated MASLD is characterized by distinct structural lipid remodeling beyond obesity alone, particularly depletion of ether-linked phospholipids and enrichment of glycerolipid intermediates. These candidate lipid signatures warrant independent validation and mechanistic investigation in ALMS and broader MASLD populations.

articles.title: Field evaluation of Biorespirim-T in young cattle: clinical, growth, and exploratory immune outcomes.
articles.abstract: Bovine respiratory disease is an important cause of morbidity, impaired growth, and antimicrobial use in young cattle, creating a need for complementary approaches that may support host defense under field conditions. We conducted a prospective controlled field evaluation of Biorespirim-T, a multicomponent hyperimmune biogenic preparation, in young cattle on a commercial farm in Kazakhstan. Clinical and production outcomes were evaluated in 80 animals (40 treated and 40 contemporaneous controls), while a separate exploratory longitudinal cohort of ten 1.5-year-old male cattle (five treated and five controls) was used to characterize selected cellular, phagocytic, and innate-defense indicators. Farm-recorded respiratory disease occurred in 5/40 treated calves and 11/40 controls (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.17-1.19; p = 0.161), while mortality was 0/40 and 2/40, respectively. Average daily gain was higher in treated animals (615 vs. 565 g/day; p = 0.0039; Hedges' g = 0.77). Among affected calves, recorded treatment duration was shorter in the treated group (4.6 vs. 8.8 days; p < 0.001), although this post-enrollment subgroup outcome was interpreted cautiously. Exploratory immune profiling showed the largest between-group effect estimates for lysozyme activity and interferon-associated activity. Biorespirim-T administration was associated with higher average daily gain and several exploratory clinical and biological signals; however, the non-randomized design and small immunological cohort preclude causal inference and require confirmation in an adequately powered randomized field trial.

articles.title: Epidemiological survey of Blastocystis sp. infection in Yaks and Tibetan sheep in the area around Qinghai Lake.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blastocystis sp. is a common protist that can infect both domestic and wild animals. Yaks and Tibetan sheep are ancient species adapted to alpine environments, providing essential necessities for generations of inhabitants on the plateau. However, Blastocystis sp. infection in these animals has long been overlooked.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the infection status and subtype distribution of Blastocystis sp. in Tibetan sheep and yaks around Qinghai Lake, and provided a scientific basis for the prevention and control of parasitic diseases on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

METHODS: Blastocystis sp. was detected by PCR amplification and sequencing of the small subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA) gene.

RESULTS: Both yaks and Tibetan sheep harbored eight subtypes.In yaks, the overall Blastocystis sp. infection rate was 20.45% (164/802). ST10 was the dominant subtype, accounting for 62.20% (102/164) of positive samples. In Tibetan sheep, the overall infection rate was 45.83% (368/803), and ST10 was likewise the dominant subtype, accounting for 71.20% (262/368) of positive samples.

CONCLUSION: This study systematically revealed, for the first time, the subtype distribution characteristics of Blastocystis sp. infection in yaks and Tibetan sheep around Qinghai Lake. It also identified, for the first time, previously unreported subtypes in Qinghai Province: ST4 and ST24 in yaks, and ST4, ST5, ST24, ST25, and ST26 in Tibetan sheep. These findings expand the host spectrum and geographical distribution of Blastocystis sp. in plateau ruminants, providing an important scientific basis for epidemiological surveillance, zoonotic disease prevention and control, and public health safety management of Blastocystis sp. on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

articles.title: Lipid-lowering, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects of Erythrina speciosa and its triterpenoids in acute dyslipidemia.
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is a health concern that contributes to metabolic and cardiovascular complications. The present study evaluated the anti-dyslipidemic potential of the chloroform fraction of Erythrina speciosa leaves and its isolated constituents, with particular emphasis on lipid regulation, redox balance, and inflammatory mediators. Chromatographic separation of the chloroform fraction led to the isolation of five triterpenoids, reported here for the first time from E. speciosa. The biological activity was assessed in a poloxamer-407-induced acute hyperlipidemia model in rats.
