Treatment with the chloroform fraction, isolated compounds, or atorvastatin significantly attenuated elevations in serum total cholesterol and triglycerides and improved low-density lipoprotein-cholesterol (LDL-C). These effects were accompanied by restoration of lipoprotein lipase (LPL) activity, upregulation of hepatic LDL receptor (LDL-R), downregulation of fatty acid synthase (FAS), and suppression of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMG-CoA) reductase. Moreover, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids markedly alleviated oxidative stress and inflammation, as evidenced by reduced malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB) p65, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and interleukin (IL)- 1β and enhanced antioxidants. Molecular docking provided supportive computational evidence by predicting favorable binding interactions of the isolated compounds with NF-κB p65, LDL-R PCSK9 binding domain, and FAS. In conclusion, E. speciosa and its triterpenoids are promising candidates for the management of dyslipidemia and related inflammatory and oxidative disturbances.

articles.title: Controversy: Adjunctive ablation lesions are needed beyond pulmonary vein isolation in treating persistent atrial fibrillation: Pro and Contra.
articles.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation remains less effective than for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, despite pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) forming the foundation of both procedures. Ablating beyond the pulmonary veins, including treatment of non-pulmonary vein triggers, posterior wall isolation, linear lesions, vein of Marshall ethanol infusion, isolation of the superior vena cava, coronary sinus or left atrial appendage, and modification of regions identified by fibrosis or low voltage has grown interest. Although observational and mechanistic studies have often been encouraging, randomized trials of empirical adjunctive ablation have produced inconsistent or neutral results. Pulsed field ablation has renewed the debate by facilitating rapid ablation of extra-pulmonary vein tissue. The PIFPAF-PFA trial did not demonstrate a significant reduction in its primary endpoint of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence lasting at least 30 seconds with adjunctive posterior wall isolation. However, separation of the recurrence curves and exploratory signals for reduced arrhythmia burden and fewer prolonged episodes raise questions about lesion strategy and the clinical relevance of conventional recurrence definitions. These findings do not establish routine posterior wall isolation, but they illustrate why a neutral binary endpoint may not fully characterize treatment effects on recurrent AF. The controversy now extends beyond whether additional ablation is beneficial to which mechanisms should be targeted, which patients should receive adjunctive lesions, how energy source affects lesion durability and safety, and whether success should be defined by any brief recurrence or by clinically meaningful arrhythmia burden. This article examines the evidence supporting and opposing ablation beyond PVI in persistent AF.

articles.title: Euglycemic DKA in an Adolescent Treated With a Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are a class of glucose-lowering medications that were recently approved for pediatric type 2 diabetes (T2D). A serious adverse effect of SGLT2i is euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (euDKA), a rare life-threatening metabolic emergency that was recognized after an increase in adult cases noted in postapproval safety surveillance programs. To our knowledge, SGLT2i-assoicated euDKA has not yet been described in youth with T2D since SGLT2i received pediatric approval in 2023. We report on a 17-year-old female patient with T2D on an SGLT2i who developed euDKA. She initially presented with vomiting that improved with antiemetics; however, she had persistent ketosis and developed significant acidosis, prompting diagnosis of euDKA. She was treated with intravenous insulin, dextrose-containing fluids, and electrolyte replacement with resolution of euDKA. This case highlights the challenges of recognizing SGLT2i-asosciated euDKA because of its rarity and the lack of hyperglycemia. As an increasing number of youth are started on SGLT2i, practitioners must be aware of the risk of SGLT2i-associated euDKA to allow for early recognition, adequate treatment, and prevention of serious complications.

articles.title: Risk factor for developing iliopsoas tendinopathy after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Iliopsoas tendinopathy (IPT) is an under-recognized cause of persistent groin pain following total hip arthroplasty (THA), yet reported risk factors remain incompletely synthesized. The purpose of this study was to systematically identify and synthesize risk factors associated with the development of IPT after THA.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was performed from database inception to 9 September 2025, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies that evaluated IPT following primary THA, and reported at least one associated risk factor, were included. Owing to substantial heterogeneity, a qualitative synthesis was performed. A random-effects meta-analysis was additionally conducted for risk factors reported by at least three studies.

RESULTS: A total of 17 studies comprising 7,873 hips were included, with a reported incidence of IPT ranging from 2.2% to 21%. In all, 15 modifiable implant- and technique-related risk factors were identified. Acetabular component overhang and anterior cup prominence were the most consistently reported, each identified in five studies and associated with significantly increased odds of IPT (odds ratio (OR) 5.53 to 35.2). Meta-analysis of three studies demonstrated that acetabular component overhang was associated with a significantly increased likelihood of IPT (pooled OR, 13.63; 95% CI 1.26 to 147.55). Thresholds for symptomatic anterior overhang ranged from 1 mm to 19.1 mm. Cup protrusion greater than 4.7 mm was associated with increased IPT risk (OR 1.16 to 15.43). Overall, 14 non-modifiable patient-related factors were reported. Female sex was associated with higher IPT risk in four studies (OR 1.15 to 3.88), and secondary osteoarthritis due to dysplasia or femoroacetabular impingement conferred increased risk (OR 3.4 to 10.9).

CONCLUSION: IPT following THA is a multifactorial complication influenced by surgical and patient-specific characteristics. While acetabular cup overhang and anterior cup prominence represent the most consistently identified modifiable risk factors, IPT can occur despite acceptable component positioning. Improved recognition of these factors may enhance preoperative planning, patient counselling, and postoperative diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation in Patients With Cirrhosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Efficacy and Safety.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cirrhosis constitutes a major burden, owing to frequent decompensations, rehospitalizations, and significant clinical implications. Current standard, symptom-targeted therapies are limited in effectiveness. Targeting the gut-liver axis as the upstream driver of decompensation, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may be beneficial.

METHODS: Following PRISMA, we searched Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov for studies investigating FMT for cirrhosis. Quality of randomized trials was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias (RoB) 2.0, nonrandomized studies using Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomised Studies-of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and case series using the Joanna Briggs Institute tool. Inverse-variance random-effects models were fitted in R 4.5.2, with between-study variance estimated by restricted maximum likelihood. Pooled risk ratios (RR) were derived from participant-level event counts for binary outcomes and Hartung-Knapp adjusted standardised mean differences (SMD) for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence was rated using GRADE.

RESULTS: Nine studies with 245 participants were included; 4 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. FMT reduced hepatic encephalopathy (HE) recurrence (4 comparisons, 80 participants, 16 events; RR=0.22 [95% CI: 0.08-0.62]; P=0.0040; I²=0%) and liver-related hospitalisation [4 comparisons, 80 participants, 19 events; RR=0.29 (95% CI: 0.12-0.69); P=0.0050; I²=0%], although the hospitalisation effect was not retained when all-cause admissions were analysed [RR=0.69 (95% CI: 0.35-1.36); P=0.28]. Serious adverse events were borderline lower with FMT [5 comparisons, 100 participants, 42 events; RR=0.54 (95% CI: 0.29-0.99); P=0.0461; I²=13.2%], but this estimate was not robust to leave-one-out analysis. Only one serious event across all 9 studies was adjudicated as FMT-attributable. FMT did not significantly change MELD scores [SMD= -0.12 (95% CI: -0.48 to 0.24)] or serum ammonia [SMD= -0.27 (95% CI: -0.67 to 0.12)]. Certainty of evidence was low for HE recurrence and very low for all other outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence from 4 small trials suggests that FMT may reduce HE recurrence in cirrhosis, with no signal of excess treatment-related harm. The evidence base is still limited, and future adequately powered randomised trials are still required to compare routes of administration, or to support a change in practice.

articles.title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Cytomegalovirus Infection in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, epidemiology, and outcomes of children with active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and to identify risk factors associated with mortality.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, medical records of patients admitted to a tertiary-level PICU between January 2015 and January 2023 were reviewed. Patients aged 1 month to 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CMV infection during PICU stay were included. Demographic, clinical, and outcome data were collected. Disease severity was assessed using pediatric risk of mortality (PRISM) and pediatric logistic organ dysfunction (PELOD) scores. Risk factors for mortality were analyzed using regression models, and the predictive value of CMV viral load was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.

RESULTS: During the study period, a total of 3320 patients were admitted to the PICU, of whom 79 (2.38%; 95% CI, 1.9-2.9) had laboratory-confirmed CMV infection. Nearly half of the patients (n = 36, 45.6%) were immunocompromised. Overall mortality was 25.3% (n = 20). The main cause of death was septic shock (85%, n = 17). In most non-survivors (80%, n = 16), CMV polymerase chain reaction remained positive prior to death. A PELOD score ≥ 3 independently predicted mortality (crude RR 3.42; 95% CI, 2.98-7.78). Each 1-point increase in PRISM score was independently associated with mortality (crude RR 1.12; 95% CI, 1.05-1.20). Cytomegalovirus viral load demonstrated poor discriminative performance for mortality prediction ( Area Under the Curve-AUC 0.57; 95% CI, 0.47-0.63).

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of CMV infection in critically ill children was low but associated with high mortality. Organ dysfunction severity, particularly elevated PELOD scores, was a significant predictor of mortality. Pediatric risk of mortality score was statistically associated with mortality despite limited discriminative performance, whereas CMV viral load was not associated with mortality. These findings suggest that CMV infection in PICU patients likely reflects disease severity rather than being a direct determinant of outcome.

articles.title: [Membrane transport of glucose and glucose homeostasis: molecular basis, physiological mechanisms and pathophysiological implications].
articles.abstract: Glucose is an essential energy substrate whose cellular utilization largely depends on membrane transport. GLUT (Glucose Transporter) and SGLT (Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter) proteins perform complementary functions in glucose uptake and reabsorption and are therefore central to energy homeostasis. This narrative review summarizes the molecular and physiological basis of glucose transport, the main characteristics of GLUT and SGLT isoforms, and their hormonal and metabolic regulation. Particular attention is given to GLUT4, whose membrane translocation is regulated by insulin and muscle activity, as well as to intestinal and renal SGLT transporters. The pathophysiological consequences of transporter dysfunction are illustrated through several genetic and metabolic disorders, including GLUT1 deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption, and type 2 diabetes. The emerging role of glucose transporters in cancer is also discussed. Tumor metabolic reprogramming, characterized by increased glycolysis, HIF-1α activation, and altered GLUT expression, illustrates the metabolic plasticity of cancer cells and the complexity of targeting glucose metabolism therapeutically. Finally, the clinical benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors and the development of experimental strategies targeting specific GLUT isoforms highlight the therapeutic potential of glucose transport systems. A better understanding of tissue-specific regulation, metabolic plasticity, and compensatory mechanisms may contribute to the development of more selective and context-adapted therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Therapeutic options to support septal reduction therapy for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is characterized by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction that can cause substantial symptoms and morbidity. The expanding range of pharmacologic, surgical, and transcatheter options has made treatment selection increasingly complex.

AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines conventional medical therapy, cardiac myosin inhibitors, surgical septal myectomy, alcohol septal ablation, and emerging investigational septal reduction strategies. It also discusses patient selection, procedural risks, multimodality imaging, and the importance of experienced hypertrophic cardiomyopathy centers. A targeted narrative search of English-language literature indexed in PubMed was conducted from April through 31 July 2026, considering clinical trials, observational studies, guidelines, and relevant reviews.

EXPERT OPINION: Cardiac myosin inhibitors are likely to modify the timing of septal reduction therapy rather than replace it. Future progress will depend on mechanism-based treatment selection, appropriate early referral, rigorous validation of emerging procedures, and integration of advanced imaging and multidisciplinary expertise to match each patient with the most suitable therapy.

articles.title: Morphological Features of Murine Pulmonary Arterial Networks for Diagnosing Vascular Disease.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia-induced pulmonary hypertension results from prolonged time spent in a low-oxygen environment. The induced pulmonary hypertension leads to vascular remodeling, including vessel dilation and decreased compliance. This study aims to identify changes in vascular morphology in mice with pulmonary hypertension induced by hypoxia. To do so, we examine the pulmonary arterial network morphology using methods from geometry, topological data analysis, and statistical shape analysis. Tools from these fields are applied to arterial networks excised from micro-CT images of thirteen mice at four pressures. Networks from the hypertensive mice were normalized via a radius pruning algorithm, and analysis was conducted on the entire arterial network, as well as on a per-lobe basis. The main objective of this study was to present an adaptable pipeline for extracting features from micro-CT images to study how vascular disease affects arterial network morphology. Using this pipeline, we showed that the hypertensive mice have increased radius ratios and decreased length-to-radius ratios. Persistent homology analysis revealed that hypertension leads to lower branch-to-branch proximity and lower directional complexity in both the posterior and anterior directions. Persistence curves, particularly Betti curves, revealed lobe-specific differences in the left and inferior lobes. The first two shape principal component scores were also able to discriminate between control and hypertension at lower pressures. Importance metrics for each feature are computed using a boosted decision tree, and then an SVM classification model is fit with the most informative predictors for hypertensive classification.

articles.title: Aggregation induced emission based fluorescent and colorimetric sensor for selective detection of Fe2+: experimental and computational insights with real-time applications.
articles.abstract: A highly responsive fluorescent and colorimetric sensor (N 2,N 6-bis(4-(phenylamino)phenyl)pyridine-2,6-dicarboxamide) DPD has been developed for the selective detection of Fe2+ ions. DPD was readily synthesized through a nucleophilic substitution reaction and characterized through spectroscopic techniques. Sensor DPD displayed aggregation-induced emission (AIE) accompanied by an increase in fluorescence intensity with a bathochromic shift. The aggregation behavior of DPD was further examined by dynamic light scattering analysis (DLS). Among the different metal ions investigated, DPD showed a distinct and highly selective response toward Fe2+, resulting in substantial fluorescence quenching due to photo-induced electron transfer (PET) and the paramagnetic behaviour of Fe2+. The interaction of DPD with Fe2+ was investigated by fluorescence and UV/visible spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and 1H NMR titration and cyclic voltammetry which collectively provide the evidence of DPD@Fe2+ interaction. Theoretical calculations, including frontier molecular orbital analysis and QTAIM analysis, were performed to support the experimental findings. Sensor DPD was successfully employed for the colorimetric detection of Fe2+ in the solid phase and in real potato samples. Furthermore, the sensor was evaluated for the detection of acidic vapors.

articles.title: SPARC: sectorized partial-angle reconstruction based motion correction method for multi-phase CCTA.
articles.abstract: Objective.Multi-phase coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) provides a clear visualization of coronary arteries, offering comprehensive and reliable imaging support for the clinical diagnosis of coronary artery disease. However, traditional motion correction reconstruction algorithms lack reconstruction robustness despite their interpretability, while deep learning reconstruction methods achieve high imaging quality at the expense of interpretability and anatomical reliability in clinical CCTA practice. This study aims to simultaneously achieve interpretable and robust multi-phase coronary reconstruction.Approach.We propose a motion trajectory estimation and motion correction framework termed sectorized partial-angle reconstruction-based motion correction (SPARC) for CCTA. The proposed framework integrates sectorized partial-angle reconstructions, a spatio-temporal cascaded network for coronary centerline extraction, and a phase-accumulated fuzzy C-means clustering algorithm for motion trajectory estimation. These components work together to minimize motion estimation errors and enhance the quality of motion-corrected reconstruction.Main results. Experimental results from both simulations and clinical studies demonstrate that SPARC achieves superior reconstruction performance compared with existing methods. SPARC effectively reduces coronary motion artifacts and restores clear vessel structures while preserving reconstruction fidelity, achieving the best scores on all metrics.Significance.By preserving both interpretability and anatomical reliability while effectively reducing motion artifacts, SPARC provides a clinically deployable solution for motion-corrected multi-phase CCTA, supporting more reliable imaging for coronary artery disease diagnosis.

articles.title: Sampling-free Monte Carlo dropout approximation for single-pass uncertainty quantification in deep learning-based PET reconstructions.
articles.abstract: Objective. Medical image reconstructions using deep learning (DL) can rapidly generate high-quality images from degraded measurements, but their clinical adoption remains challenging, largely due to the lack of fast and reliable methods to quantify aleatoric (data-driven) and epistemic (model-driven) uncertainties on a per-prediction basis. We aim to develop a computationally efficient approach for estimating both uncertainties at the voxel level in DL-based image reconstruction within a single inference run.Approach. We present a moment propagation-based framework that analytically approximates the conventional, multi-realization Monte Carlo (MC) dropout by propagating feature-map means and marginal variances through network layers, followed by a pre-calibrated correction table to compensate for covariance effects omitted in the approximation. This enables joint estimation of reconstruction, aleatoric uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. The proposed framework was implemented on top of FastPET-a network model synthesizing PET reconstructions from time-of-flight histo-images-and evaluated in a patient pilot study of 26 total-body PET/CT acquisitions (16F-FDG and 10F-PSMA cases).Main results. Proposed method achieved relatively strong agreement with the 50-pass MC approach, with absolute differences0.5% for reconstruction,4.2% for aleatoric uncertainty and9.8% for epistemic uncertainty, along with narrow spreads across patients and tracer types, while reducing computation time by40-fold. In a complementary proof-of-concept low-count experiment, regional tracer uptake confidence intervals (CIs, derived from propagated uncertainties) widened with increased noise level, and reference uptakes consistently fell within and close to CI boundaries, indicating the proposed method could provide roughly calibrated uncertainty magnitudes reflecting quantitative prediction errors.Significance. The proposed approach provides a sampling-free and relatively accurate approximation to the multi-pass MC-based uncertainty estimation in the histo-image-based DL PET reconstruction framework. Per-prediction uncertainty quantification enables direct assessment of AI confidence and potentially supports more reliable and informed decision-making.

articles.title: CMRCUNet: a cross-modal calibration U-Net for acute ischaemic stroke lesion segmentation from multi-sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Purpose:Acute ischaemic stroke is a major cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, and rapid delineation of infarct lesions on brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is important for supporting time-sensitive treatment decisions. Multi-sequence MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), provides complementary information for characterising acute ischaemic lesions. However, many deep learning approaches process these modalities using shared encoders and direct skip connections, which may limit modality-specific feature learning and remain challenged by the severe foreground-background imbalance characteristic of stroke lesion segmentation.Method:We propose CMRCUNet, a multimodal segmentation framework that combines modality-specific residual encoders, a cross modal calibration (CMC) module, and an attention-gated decoder. The modality-specific encoders independently learn sequence-dependent representations from DWI, ADC, and FLAIR, while the CMC module performs adaptive, input-dependent weighting of modality-specific features at multiple resolution levels before decoder fusion. Focal Tversky Loss is used to address severe lesion-background imbalance. The framework is evaluated in both 2D and 2.5D configurations; the 2.5D configuration incorporates neighbouring axial slices to provide limited through-plane contextual information while retaining two-dimensional convolutional operations. Test-time augmentation (TTA) is additionally evaluated to improve inference robustness.Results:CMRCUNet was evaluated on the Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation 2022 dataset using a patient-level evaluation protocol with an independent 37-patient test cohort. The 2.5D configuration combined with TTA achieved a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.792 ± 0.142, sensitivity of 0.854 ± 0.132, specificity of 0.996 ± 0.012, and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 8.21 ± 8.70 mm.Conclusion:CMRCUNet provides a multimodal framework that integrates modality-specific feature extraction, adaptive CMC, attention-gated decoding, and limited inter-slice contextual information for acute ischaemic stroke lesion segmentation. The results support further investigation of adaptive CMC, particularly through external multi-centre validation.

articles.title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance.
articles.abstract: Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

articles.title: Thermoresponsive Adhesive Hydrogel Enabling Dynamic Adhesion Switching for Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, increased susceptibility to bacterial infection, and impaired tissue regeneration, which collectively hinder wound repair. Hydrogel dressings have emerged as promising candidates for chronic wound management; however, achieving stable tissue adhesion for wound protection while enabling gentle removal during dressing replacement remains challenging. Although stimuli-responsive adhesive hydrogels have been developed to achieve on-demand debonding, their reliance on external chemical triggers and limited adaptability in complex wound environments restrict their further application. Herein, we developed a thermoresponsive multifunctional hydrogel dressing (HG-CT@Al) that integrates dynamic adhesion regulation with wound microenvironment modulation through a one-pot photopolymerization strategy. The NIPAM/AAm/AA copolymer network endowed HG-CT@Al with temperature-responsive adhesion switching, while the chitosan (CS) semi-interpenetrating network and dynamic coordination interactions between tea polyphenols (TP) and Al3+ enhanced structural stability and provided antibacterial and antioxidant functions. By optimizing the network composition, HG-CT@Al maintained strong tissue adhesion at physiological temperature (35 °C, 167.22 N/m) and reduced adhesion strength after mild heating (45 °C, 97.99 N/m), enabling on-demand gentle debonding. Meanwhile, HG-CT@Al exhibited excellent antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus (99.65 and 99.69%, respectively) and strong antioxidant capacity (95.61% DPPH radical-scavenging efficiency). In a full-thickness diabetic wound model, HG-CT@Al significantly accelerated wound closure and promoted re-epithelialization, collagen deposition, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage early enrichment. This study presents a multifunctional hydrogel strategy integrating temperature-responsive dynamic adhesion regulation and wound microenvironment modulation, providing an effective approach for diabetic chronic wound management.

articles.title: Synthesis and preclinical evaluation of a novel 2-[18F]fluoropyridine-bearing rhodamine for myocardial perfusion imaging with PET.
articles.abstract: [18F]Rho6G-DEG-F is a rhodamine-based PET radiotracer for myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) that exhibits excellent first-pass myocardial extraction, persistent cardiac retention, and high heart : liver ratios in rats and pigs. However, in human volunteers, heart : liver contrast was suboptimal. The primary goals of this study were to design an [18F]Rho6G-DEG-F analogue of attenuated lipophilicity for radiolabelling via nucleophilic heteroaromatic 18F-fluorination ([18F]Rho6G-DEG-Py-F; [18F]6), and to evaluate [18F]6 in rats and mice. To that end, precursors bearing 2-nitro- (5) and 2-trimethylammonium triflate (8)- pyridine groups were prepared in overall yields of 48% and 29%, starting from rhodamine 6G; final purification did not require C18 chromatography. Manual standard radiofluorination conditions (TEA[18F]F/TEAHCO3/DMSO/160 °C/20 min) afforded a best decay-corrected radiochemical yield (DC-RCY) of 31% from 5 and 7% from 8. In the latter case, precursor and radiotracer were easily separated by HPLC (molar activity = 33 ± 8 GBq per µmol). Upon translation to an automated synthesizer, [18F]6 was obtained in DC-RCYs of 9.3% and 0.7% from 5 and 8 respectively; best molar activities were 50 and 144 GBq per µmol respectively. [18F]Rho6G-DEG-Py-F exhibited complete stability in rat and mouse serum over 120 min (37 °C). A radiometabolite assay in two rats showed differing metabolic profiles between sexes, but similar % intact tracer at 60 min (32-34%). Micro-PET imaging in rats demonstrated extended myocardial retention (SUV > 1.0 at 120 min), gradual liver washout, and high heart : liver ratios (3.7 in male, 2.5 in female at 120 min); however, similar experiments in mice revealed low heart uptake and rapid metabolism (SUV ∼ 0.3; heart : liver ratio = 1.0 at 120 min).

articles.title: Highly efficient glycolysis of polyethylene terephthalate catalyzed by a Zn-modified 5A zeolite prepared through ion exchange.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most widely produced polyesters worldwide, but its low recycling efficiency has caused serious environmental pollution and resource waste. Glycolysis is considered an optimal method for closed-loop PET recycling because it works under mild conditions and allows direct recovery of the valuable monomer bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET). Catalysts are very important in glycolysis, but most zinc-based solid catalysts reported so far have high costs and are not stable enough, and this makes them hard to use in industrial applications. To solve these problems, this study prepared a series of zinc-modified zeolite catalysts (ZnX-LTA/N&T) using industrial 5A zeolite (LTA) as the support with a simple ion exchange method, and evaluated the effects of the zinc precursor types, ion-exchange cycles, and calcination temperatures on the structure and performance of the catalysts. ZnCl2-LTA/3&400 (prepared with using ZnCl2 as precursor, calcination at 400 °C, and three ion exchange cycles) showed the best catalytic performance with 87.33% PET conversion and 74.23% BHET yield, and also maintained well stability after few recycling runs. Kinetic studies showed that the PET glycolysis followed shrinking core model with activation energy of 184.41 kJ mol-1. In addition, this catalyst also exhibited excellent activity for depolymerizing various real post-consumer PET wastes (films, trays, and beverage bottles), achieving 100% conversion for PET films with a BHET yield of up to 81.93%.

articles.title: Development of AIE active carbazole based fluorescent probe for rapid detection of 4-nitrotoluene in solution and solid phases: experimental and DFT insights.
articles.abstract: A fluorescent probe CPT has been strategically designed and synthesized via Ullmann and Claisen-Schmidt condensation reactions, and its photophysical properties were systematically investigated. Aggregation-induced emission (AIE) with a 25 nm hypsochromic shift, was attributed to aggregate formation. Further, probe CPT exhibited distinct solvatochromic behavior with a 31 nm bathochromic shift. Owing to these unique optical properties, probe CPT serves as an efficient sensing tool for 4-nitrotoluene (4-NT), exhibiting a fluorescence-quenching response via a twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) and photoinduced electron transfer (PET) mechanism. Probe CPT exhibited a hypsochromic shift of 39 nm upon treating with 4-NT. The interaction mechanism was investigated using 1H NMR, FTIR, mass spectrometry titration, DLS, and DFT calculations. CPT exhibited excellent selectivity and high sensitivity toward 4-NT, with an LOD of 0.16 nM and an LOQ of 0.55 nM. Furthermore, probe CPT exhibited remarkable efficacy in solid and solution-phase sensing of 4-NT, highlighting its potential applicability for monitoring 4-NT in real industrial effluents.

articles.title: A volatilomics approach for the identification of volatile organic compounds as biomarkers of ventilator-associated pneumonia using GC-MS.
articles.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious complication of patients at intensive care units (ICUs), contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Current diagnostic approaches for VAP rely on clinical, radiological, and invasive methods, which are time-consuming, carry risks, and may result in delayed or inconclusive findings. The need for rapid, reliable, and non-invasive diagnostic tools is critical. Biomarkers and specifically volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, we applied gas chromatography-mass spectrometry with solid-phase microextraction to analyze breath VOC profiles in critically ill children and explore their potential as early indicators of VAP. Results reveal significant challenges in breath volatilomics, including batch effects and variability in VOC detection. However, normalization strategies allowed for meaningful comparisons across multiple time points, revealing subtle trends in VOC profiles that could differentiate patients with high and low suspicion of VAP. Notably, VOCs such as o-xylene and pentadecane showed reduced levels in patients with higher suspicion of VAP at Day 3, suggesting potential associations with respiratory infection severity. While preliminary, these findings support further investigation into breath-based VOC signatures as a non-invasive, early diagnostic tool for VAP in pediatric ICUs. This approach could enhance diagnostic accuracy and inform timely clinical decisions, improving patient outcomes.

articles.title: EGCG@ZIF-8@Polydopamine-Functionalized Janus Nanofibrous Dressing with Directional Exudate Transport and Photothermal Antibacterial Activity for Infected Wound Treatment.
articles.abstract: The treatment of infected skin wounds continues to face multiple challenges, including bacterial resistance, persistent inflammation, oxidative damage, and inadequate exudate management. To address these issues, a multifunctional Janus wound dressing was constructed to achieve coordinated infection control and tissue repair. Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) was used as a nanocarrier for the natural antioxidant molecule, and polydopamine surface coating endowed the composite nanoparticles with photothermal antibacterial activity. The composite nanoparticles were subsequently incorporated into a hydrophobic polycaprolactone layer by electrospinning and combined with a hydrophilic polyacrylonitrile layer containing a pH indicator, thereby forming a bilayer structure with unidirectional liquid transport, visual monitoring, and wound protection functions. The dressing promotes the outward transfer of wound exudate and produces an observable color response to changes in environmental pH. Under near-infrared irradiation, the antibacterial rate of the dressing reached 98.89% against E. coli and 99.99% against S. aureus. The dressing also possesses excellent free-radical-scavenging capacity, indicating its potential to alleviate excessive oxidative stress in infected wounds. Animal experiments further demonstrated that the dressing reduced the local infection burden, promoted wound closure, collagen deposition, and tissue formation, and caused no obvious histopathological abnormalities in major organs. Overall, this study presents a multifunctional Janus nanofibrous dressing that integrates antibacterial activity, antioxidant function, exudate regulation, and wound-status monitoring, providing a material-design approach for the repair of infected skin wounds.

articles.title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

articles.title: Reactive Oxygen Species-Scavenging Nanozyme Hydrogel for Microenvironment Modulation in Diabetic Chronic Wound Healing.
articles.abstract: Diabetic chronic wounds are difficult to heal because persistent hyperglycemia is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), impaired angiogenesis, and prolonged inflammation. Here, we developed an Fe3O4@PDA-containing PVA/gelatin/borate hydrogel (FP-PVG) with catalase-like activity. FP-PVG scavenged ROS and promoted H2O2-responsive oxygen generation, while the FP nanocomposite and hydrogel matrix contributed to antibacterial activity. In vitro, FP-PVG showed strong ABTS radical-scavenging activity (98.97% at 2 mg mL-1), favorable cytocompatibility, and improved cell migration under oxidative stress. It also reduced CD86 expression and increased CD163 expression in macrophages, consistent with a shift toward a reparative phenotype. In a diabetic mouse wound model, FP-PVG accelerated wound closure and was associated with reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, increased angiogenesis, and improved tissue regeneration. These findings support FP-PVG as a multifunctional hydrogel dressing for regulating the diabetic wound microenvironment.

articles.title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair.
articles.abstract: Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

articles.title: High-Fat Diet Feeding Rapidly Induces Sex-Specific Neuronal Plasticity in Lateral Hypothalamic Glutamatergic Neurons.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Hypothalamic circuits play a central role in coordinating feeding and energy balance, yet how these circuits adapt to dietary excess to regulate body weight remains poorly understood. Lateral hypothalamic area glutamatergic (LHAVglut2) neurons critically mediate food intake and body weight, but how they adapt their function to acute overfeeding and whether such adaptation is sexually dimorphic are unknown. Here, we examined the impact of high-fat diet (HFD) on LHAVglut2 neurons in mice. Whole-cell recordings revealed baseline sex differences in neuronal properties: female LHAVglut2 neurons exhibited higher basal excitability and differential synaptic input compared with males. HFD feeding produced distinct forms of neuronal plasticity between sexes within 1 d. In males, HFD increased intrinsic excitability while excitatory synaptic input was decreased. In contrast, excitability of female LHAVglut2 neurons remained unchanged, but inhibitory synaptic strength was selectively reduced. To test the causal relationship between enhanced LHAVglut2 neuron excitability and weight gain during overfeeding, we expressed the depolarizing sodium channel NaChBac to chronically increase LHAVglut2 neuron excitability. Chronic elevation of LHAVglut2 neuron excitability suppressed body weight gain during acute HFD exposure in males, whereas females displayed significant weight loss during HFD exposure. Together, these results suggest that female mice may be protected from diet-induced obesity via sexually dimorphic LHAVglut2 neurons. In males, overfeeding rapidly induces compensatory changes in LHAVglut2 neuron excitability that may act to limit body weight gain. Further enhancement of LHAVglut2 neuron excitability can suppress weight gain in an obesogenic environment for both males and females.

articles.title: Correction: Emerging investigator series: unpacking PET: comparative analysis of leachable and extractable contaminants from virgin and recycled polyethylene terephthalate bottles and textiles.
articles.abstract: Correction for 'Emerging investigator series: unpacking PET: comparative analysis of leachable and extractable contaminants from virgin and recycled polyethylene terephthalate bottles and textiles' by Yanan Li et al., Environ. Sci.: Processes Impacts, 2025, 27, 3431-3439, https://doi.org/10.1039/D5EM00615E.

articles.title: Probing polymer effects on interfacial Li-ion transport in hybrid solid electrolytes: LLZO-PCL compared with LLZO-PEO.
articles.abstract: Hybrid polymer-ceramic electrolytes are promising candidates for solid-state lithium-ion batteries, making it essential to identify the key factors governing interfacial ion transport. Atomistic molecular dynamics simulations at elevated temperatures are used to investigate differences in Li+ transport between PCL- and PEO-based polymer-ceramic interfaces. The investigated interface is built of Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) ceramic and poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) polymer doped with bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (LiTFSI) (LLZO-PCL), and a direct comparison is established with an analogous interface composed of LiTFSI-doped poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and LLZO (LLZO-PEO). The LLZO-PCL interface exhibits pronounced interfacial structuring, including strong adsorption of hydroxyl oxygen atoms at the ceramic surface. Li+ transfer across the interface is quantified from transition statistics and analyzed using free-energy profiles. Remarkably, LLZO-PCL exhibits an approximately 35-fold larger phase-exchange barrier (PEB) rate than LLZO-PEO, primarily due to a significantly lower PEB height for polymer-ceramic transfer. Analysis within the framework of overdamped Kramers theory indicates strongly damped interfacial dynamics and suggests spatially heterogeneous friction along the reaction coordinate. Overall, the results demonstrate that the substantially different interfacial Li+ transfer in PCL and PEO is mainly associated with differences in the PEB height. Our previously developed multiscale framework is used to evaluate which of the two polymer systems is more likely to enhance the overall conductivity in hybrid solid electrolytes by facilitating Li+ transport through the fast ceramic phase. Finally, effective Li-polymer coordination strength and polymer adhesion at the ceramic surface emerge as key factors governing interfacial ion transport and the efficient utilization of ceramic transport pathways in hybrid solid electrolytes.

articles.title: Advancing NTM research with citizen science.
articles.abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) is a generic term for the >200 species of environmental mycobacteria. NTM are ubiquitous, but there is extensive variation in the distribution of individual species. In a recent article published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, Wilsey et al. describe how community-based citizen science efforts helped map the distribution of NTM in Hawai'i (R. N. Wilsey, L.-H. Ding, S. N. Dawrs, C. K. Raulerson, et al., Appl Environ Microbiol 92:e00269-26, 2026, https://doi.org/10.1128/aem.00269-26). Mycobacterium chimaera, an opportunistic pathogen and the leading cause of NTM pulmonary disease in Hawai'i, was among the most common species isolated.

articles.title: DAPK3 activates STING to enhance antiviral response via IRF3 and NF-κB pathways in teleosts.
articles.abstract: Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is critical for the induction of type I interferons (IFN-I) and inflammatory responses against viral infection. The activity of STING is tightly regulated by various post-translational modifications (PTMs) to effectively defend against viral infection or prevent excessive immune responses. However, the regulatory mechanisms of STING activity remain largely unknown in teleosts. In this study, we discovered that zebrafish death-associated protein kinase 3 (DAPK3) enhances the STING-mediated antiviral innate immune response through two synergistic mechanisms: the induction of an interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)-dependent IFN-I response and a nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-dependent pro-inflammatory cytokine response. Specifically, viral stimulation triggers the expression of DAPK3, resulting in its autophosphorylation at Ser21 and Thr87. Activated DAPK3 subsequently interacts with STING, promoting its phosphorylation. Moreover, DAPK3 also recruits tripartite motif-containing protein 32 (TRIM32), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, thereby increasing K63-linked polyubiquitination of STING. Subsequently, activated STING orchestrates two key responses: (i) it recruits TBK1 to enhance IRF3 phosphorylation and dimerization, thereby promoting IFN-I production; (ii) it recruits the IKK complex (IKKα/IKKβ) to activate p65-mediated expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β, TNFα), ultimately inducing apoptosis. At the cellular level, DAPK3 overexpression significantly enhances cellular antiviral capacity and inhibits viral proliferation. In vivo, zebrafish embryos injected with DAPK3 mRNA display reduced lethality and decreased viral mRNA levels compared to controls. This is accompanied by the induction of immune-related genes and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Conversely, knocking down DAPK3 in zebrafish enhances spring viremia of carp virus (SVCV)-induced lethality and viral proliferation, a phenomenon associated with a reduction in immune-related genes and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical role of zebrafish DAPK3 in enhancing the antiviral response through two synergistic mechanisms that target STING.

articles.title: Spatial transcriptomics and N-glycoproteomics reveal breed-dependent immune and structural responses in Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae-infected pig lungs.
articles.abstract: Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae (Mhp) is a major cause of enzootic pneumonia in pigs, yet the molecular and spatial determinants underlying breed-specific susceptibility remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, and N-glycoproteomics to compare lung responses to experimental Mhp infection in Chenghua pigs with higher susceptibility and Yorkshire pigs with relative resilience. Under an identical inoculation dose, Chenghua pigs exhibited more severe clinical and pathological manifestations than Yorkshire pigs, despite comparable pulmonary Mhp loads at this late stage of infection. This observation suggests that disease severity is associated with differences in host response organization rather than with overall pathogen burden. Spatial analyses revealed a shared spatial and cellular infection framework across breeds, with marked differences in regulatory balance. Across spatial clusters, Chenghua pigs exhibited coordinated activation of TNF-α-NF-κB and IL-6-JAK-STAT3 signaling, accompanied by relative attenuation of IFN-I responses. These inflammatory features co-occurred with hypoxia- and mTORC1-related metabolic reprogramming, activation of stress-response pathways, and engagement of tissue remodeling programs. Transcription factor analyses further indicated increased activity of HIF1A, RELA and STAT3, together with reduced IRF9/ STAT2-associated regulatory activity. Immune deconvolution and multiplex immunofluorescence revealed enrichment of M0/M2 macrophages, plasma cells, and activated mast cells, alongside reduced M1 macrophage and CD8 + T-cell signatures. These changes delineated inflammatory niches characterized by relatively high IL1B expression and enrichment of mast cells. Ligand-receptor analysis revealed enhanced BAFF/APRIL-B-cell signaling features and amplification of MHC-II, RESISTIN, and CXCL networks in Chenghua pigs. Proteomic and N-glycoproteomic profiling further revealed disruption of junctional and extracellular-matrix components, together with extensive breed-specific remodeling of barrier and antigen-presentation-related glycoproteins in Chenghua pigs. Together, these findings provide a spatially resolved description of breed-dependent differences in immune, metabolic, and structural responses observed during chronic Mhp infection.

articles.title: From expression profiling to functional validation: evidence hierarchy and biomarker readiness of circular RNAs in aquatic animals.
articles.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5' and 3' ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence supporting the potential of circRNAs as candidate biomarkers for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. Overall, aquatic animals provide valuable non-model systems for expanding our understanding of circRNA biology, although many proposed regulatory mechanisms and translational applications remain to be further validated.

articles.title: Bamboo-Inspired Homogeneous Porous Aerogel via Gas Foaming Assisted by Freeze-Drying for High-Sensitivity Flexible Pressure Sensors.
articles.abstract: Flexible piezoresistive sensors are pivotal in personalized healthcare. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and a broad linear range remains a formidable challenge owing to rapid structural densification of porous materials. Inspired by the multiscale composite structure of bamboo, this study addresses the existing challenge by proposing a novel MXene aerogel sensor, reinforced by compounding cellulose nanofiber (CNF) and bamboo cellulose. By leveraging a uniform conductive network constructed on CNF (simulating bamboo parenchyma cells to disperse the vascular bundles) and the supporting effect of the bamboo cellulose skeleton (mimicking vascular bundles to provide support), premature collapse is effectively resisted. Moreover, inspired by the hollow cell cavity structure of bamboo, a stable porous architecture is constructed via gas foaming and freeze-drying, enabling it to effectively reconcile the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and the detection range. The sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 148.29 kPa-1 (0-15 kPa) and a wide effective working range extending up to 100 kPa. This superior electromechanical performance enables the precise detection of full-spectrum physiological signals ranging from subtle pulse waveforms to large-scale joint movements and facilitates assistive rehabilitation for post-stroke finger therapy via human-computer interaction. Augmented by a support vector machine algorithm, the sensor has a wireless sleep monitoring capability and achieves a high classification accuracy of 96.5% in identifying distinct breathing states. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant application potential in next-generation intelligent home health management systems.

articles.title: Bioadaptor Implantation in Complex Calcified Coronary Lesions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Calcified coronary lesions remain among the most challenging subsets in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) because of their morphological complexity. Restoring physiological vasomotion and vascular remodeling is an emerging goal in PCI.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with severely calcified coronary lesions treated with PCI. Lesion preparation included rotational atherectomy was performed in 2 of 3 cases, followed by implantation of a bioadaptor-a sirolimus-eluting cobalt-chromium hybrid stent system. In 1 case, a super high-pressure OPN balloon was used for postdilatation. Six-month follow-up angiography showed favorable outcomes with sustained vessel patency in all cases.

DISCUSSION: This is the first case series reporting bioadaptor use in heavily calcified coronary lesions. Adequate lesion preparation is essential for procedural success and clinical outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In this case series, bioadaptor implantation in severely calcified coronary lesions was feasible, with favorable short-term outcomes at 6 months. In calcified lesions, more aggressive lesion preparation than for conventional drug-eluting stents may be required, as adequate calcium modification is a prerequisite for full device expansion and for realizing the bioadaptor's long-term functional benefits after uncaging.

articles.title: Time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired model for late dynamic PET frame prediction from early [11C] raclopride.
articles.abstract: Objective. To reduce the burden of dynamic positron emission tomography (PET) acquisition while preserving quantitative analysis, we propose a time-aware frame-aligned diffusion-inspired residual denoising framework for predicting late dynamic PET frames from a short early acquisition window (10 min in this study) of [11C] raclopride.Approach. Irregular native dynamic frames were converted to a uniform 1 min indexing grid using overlap-weighted rebinning. The first 10 min were used as the early input and to derive the spatial and intensity preprocessing parameters. For each requested late time, a shared time-aware 3D U-Net predicted an anchor-relative residual with respect to the last available early frame. A training-only denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM)-inspired Gaussian perturbation and noise-prediction branch shared the prediction backbone and regularized residual learning, while temporal-consistency loss constrained predicted frame-to-frame changes. All learning-based methods used identical subject-wise five-fold cross-validation within the development cohort, followed by evaluation on a fixed internal test set; the external cohort was held out from model selection.Main results. The proposed approach achieved higher Peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index measure and lower mean absolute error than the comparison methods, while providing closer agreement with reference TACs and simplified reference tissue model-derived parameter estimates across the limbic, associative, and sensorimotor striata.Significance. The proposed framework provides deterministic time-resolved late-frame estimates from early dynamic PET while using a DDPM-inspired noise-prediction objective only as an auxiliary training regularizer rather than as an iterative diffusion inference process. This design may support shortened dynamic PET protocols while retaining TAC and kinetic-parameter fidelity.

articles.title: Tortuous Coronary Artery Fistula Closed Using a Microvascular Plug in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large coronary artery fistulas may result in ischemia and heart failure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 74-year-old woman was found to have an ejection fraction of 20%-25% with apical and anterior akinesis. A large fistula from the left anterior descending artery to the pulmonary artery was identified as the likely etiology. Multiple attempts at closure failed in the setting of extreme tortuosity with nearly 180° bends. Eventually, a 5-mm vascular plug was advanced through a microcatheter and successfully deployed. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated improvement of the ejection fraction to 40%-45% and complete resolution of the previous wall motion abnormalities.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates a reversible coronary steal-mediated cardiomyopathy. It highlights the clinical utility of microcatheter-compatible vascular plugs for transcatheter closure of anatomically complex coronary fistulas, even in elderly patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Percutaneous closure of coronary artery fistulas with microcatheter-compatible devices improves cardiac function even in elderly patients.

articles.title: Successful Guidewire-Guided Ethanol Ablation for PVCs Originating From Epicardial Anterior Interventricular Groove Adjacent to LAD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from epicardial anterior interventricular groove and closely adjacent to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) are difficult to eliminate and carry high risks of coronary damage or occlusion. We describe a successful guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation in this high -risk patient.

CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man who presented with palpitations and high-burden PVCs was admitted to our hospital. Pace mapping performed at the epicardial anterior interventricular groove yielded QRS morphology nearly identical to the native PVCs. Coronary angiography revealed that the target site was directly adjacent to the proximal-middle segment of the LAD. Guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation via a small branch of the anterior interventricular vein successfully eliminated the PVCs. Postprocedural coronary angiography showed no coronary artery injury and the patient remained free of PVCs during the 2-month follow-up period.

DISCUSSION: Epicardial PVCs arising within the anterior interventricular groove where the LAD runs carry a high risk of coronary artery injury during ablation. Guidewire-assisted anhydrous ethanol ablation serves as an effective and safe therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Tachycardia Initiation by Dual-Mode PVC on Ambulatory ECG: Pattern Discovery and Invasive Electrophysiological Characteristics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanisms of premature ventricular complex (PVC)-induced long-RP tachycardia warrant investigation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with palpitations underwent 24-hour ambulatory electrocardiogram (ECG). The recording showed 4,150 monomorphic PVCs and 800 episodes of long-RP tachycardia, all triggered by the same PVC morphology. Two initiation patterns emerged. One involved direct retrograde conduction, the other showed retrograde conduction only after PR prolongation. In both patterns, induction occurred across a broad range of PVC coupling intervals. Invasive electrophysiology study (EPS) then demonstrated slow-slow atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (SS-AVNRT) involving multiple atrioventricular nodal pathways, consistent with the dual-mode patterns seen on ambulatory ECG. Ablation succeeded, with no recurrence at 6 months.

DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of SS-AVNRT to show distinctive PVC-induced tachycardia patterns on ambulatory ECG, corroborated by EPS.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ambulatory ECG patterns of PVC-triggered long-RP tachycardia may suggest a dual-pathway substrate for SS-AVNRT, warranting EPS confirmation.

articles.title: Coronary Visual Intelligence System (CorVIS) Guided Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is usually displayed in 2-dimensional planes with few fixed 3-dimensional (3D) views, which may limit appreciation of the spatial relationship between plaques and vessel. We describe initial clinical experience with CorVIS, an artificial intelligence-based coronary visualization system, in complex percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 cases-2 chronic total occlusions and 1 heavily calcified lesion-in which CorVIS provided freely rotatable 3D reconstructions with plaque characterization. In each case, the CorVIS corresponded to specific procedural decisions, including the chosen crossing approach and calcium-modification strategy. All 3 procedures were completed successfully.

DISCUSSION: These cases suggest that artificial intelligence-based 3D CCTA reconstruction may complement conventional imaging for preprocedural planning of complex PCI. The efficacy of CorVIS in facilitating complex PCI remains to be verified in further prospective studies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: In this initial case series, CorVIS delivered freely rotatable 3D CCTA reconstructions and plaque characterization, informing key procedural decisions for complex PCI.

articles.title: First-in-Human Axillary Vein Implantation of a Leadless Pacemaker: Breaking the Access Barrier.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are conventionally implanted transfemorally, with transjugular and subclavian routes reported as alternatives. Axillary access has not previously been reported.

FIH SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman with chronic sacral wounds became temporary-pacing dependent following an inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. An LP was selected given infection risk. Because of a right femoral deep venous thrombosis, an abscess at the left femoral site, and restricted neck mobility limiting internal jugular access, she underwent left axillary vein implantation of an LP.

DISCUSSION: Axillary access served as a feasible alternative route. A septal position was achieved by rotating the delivery system counterclockwise, opposite the transfemoral direction, while a perpendicular sterile table supported the extracorporeal catheter length.

NOVELTY: This is the first reported axillary vein implantation of an LP.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Axillary venous access is a feasible bailout route for LP implantation when femoral and internal jugular access are unavailable.

articles.title: Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Calcium Modification for a Complex Calcified Nodule With Circumferential Calcium: From Debulking to Fracturing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The study objective was to describe an optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided strategy for stepwise calcium modification in a large protruding calcified nodule with circumferential calcium.

KEY STEPS: Rotational atherectomy was used to establish device crossability and modify superficial calcium. Serial OCT was performed to assess residual calcified nodule protrusion, circumferential calcium, lumen gain, and calcium fracture. When crossability was restored but substantial mechanical constraint persisted, the strategy was escalated to intravascular lithotripsy, followed by cutting-balloon dilation. Final OCT was used to confirm stent expansion and apposition.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Restoration of device crossability does not necessarily indicate adequate lesion preparation, whereas excessive burr escalation may increase procedural risk. Serial OCT should be used to assess the response to each modification step and guide timely strategy escalation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: OCT assessment may guide precise calcium modification and prevent stent underexpansion in complex calcified lesions.

articles.title: Progressive Dilated Cardiomyopathy in a 24-Year-Old Man: A Rare Manifestation of Propionic Acidemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adult onset propionic acidemia (PA) is exceedingly rare, particularly when manifesting as dilated cardiomyopathy.

CASE SUMMARY: A previously healthy 24-year-old man presented with cardiac dilatation and acute progressive heart failure. His condition was refractory to guideline-directed medical therapy, deteriorating to cardiogenic shock within 6 weeks. Plasma acylcarnitine profile revealed elevated propionylcarnitine and an increased propionylcarnitine-to-acetylcarnitine ratio. Urinary organic acid analysis showed elevated methylcitric acid. Whole-exome sequencing identified a homozygous mutation in the PCCA gene. A diagnosis of PA presenting as metabolic cardiomyopathy was established. Cardiac function and hemodynamics improved with targeted metabolic treatment combined with guideline-directed medical therapy.

DISCUSSION: Adult onset, metabolic cardiomyopathy because of PA is prone to being overlooked or misdiagnosed as refractory idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, potentially leading to premature escalation to advanced heart failure therapies. Early etiologic recognition and targeted metabolic treatment are crucial in the management of such cases.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Metabolic and genetic screening is recommended for patients with idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, particularly in younger individuals. Early diagnosis and targeted intervention may preclude or delay the progression to left ventricular assist device implantation or heart transplantation in patients with dilated cardiomyopathy secondary to PA.

articles.title: Perioperative B-Cell-Targeted Therapy for High-Risk Valve Surgery in Active Primary Sjögren's Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disease driven by B-cell dysregulation. Clinically significant valvular involvement is uncommon, and evidence guiding perioperative immunomodulation remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman with SjD and severe aortic stenosis required valve replacement. Preoperative evaluation demonstrated active SjD with elevated inflammatory markers and hypergammaglobulinemia. Following multidisciplinary discussion, telitacicept, corticosteroids, and hydroxychloroquine were initiated before surgery. After improvement in inflammatory activity, the patient underwent aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement. Histopathologic examination showed degenerative valvular changes with focal inflammatory cell infiltration. The postoperative course was uneventful, with normal prosthetic valve function at 1-year follow-up.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the challenges of managing severe valvular heart disease in patients with active primary SjD and a multidisciplinary perioperative strategy incorporating B-cell-targeted therapy. Although preoperative immunomodulation may have attenuated the histopathologic evidence of immune-mediated valvular involvement, the case offers insights when guidance is limited.

articles.title: Low-Frequency Whole-Body Vibration and Isometric Exercise in Cardiac Rehabilitation: Improved Capacity and Triglyceride-Glucose Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise intolerance may persist in patients with chronic coronary syndrome despite successful percutaneous coronary intervention. Evidence regarding low-frequency whole-body vibration training (LF-WBVT) remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 62-year-old woman underwent cardiac rehabilitation for reduced exercise capacity 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention. Baseline peak oxygen uptake was 14.3 mL/kg/min. She completed an 8-week program consisting of moderate-intensity continuous aerobic training, LF-WBVT (3-9 Hz), and isometric lower-extremity resistance exercise. Peak oxygen uptake increased to 22.2 mL/kg/min, and oxygen pulse increased from 8.7 to 9.6 mL/beat. No major adverse cardiovascular events occurred.

DISCUSSION: This combined strategy improved both cardiorespiratory fitness and metabolic health. The triglyceride-glucose index reduction is a novel finding, suggesting lower future cardiovascular risk.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: LF-WBVT with isometric exercise is safe in selected patients with chronic coronary syndrome. Triglyceride-glucose index may serve as a metabolic biomarker for rehabilitation outcomes.

articles.title: Ablation in Dextrocardia With Interrupted Inferior Vena Cava and Azygos Continuation to Coronary Sinus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation ablation in dextrocardia with interrupted inferior vena cava presents formidable technical challenges, particularly when anomalous systemic venous return distorts interatrial septal relationships.

CASE SUMMARY: A 58-year-old man with drug-refractory paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, situs inversus totalis with dextrocardia, and inferior vena cava interruption with azygos continuation to the coronary sinus underwent catheter ablation. Lacking an inferior route, a superior approach through the left internal jugular vein was selected. Under intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) guidance, transseptal access was obtained using a dedicated wire-based system. Pulmonary vein isolation and roofline ablation were safely completed using radiofrequency energy.

DISCUSSION: Azygos continuation to the coronary sinus drastically distorts interatrial geometry. ICE-guided, wire-based transseptal access via a superior route is a safe, practical alternative when conventional inferior access is unavailable and needle-based puncture poses high risks.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: In situs inversus, the left internal jugular vein offers an optimal trajectory for transseptal puncture via a superior approach. Using a dedicated transseptal guidewire instead of a rigid needle, strictly guided by ICE, reduces the risk of mechanical complications during atypical transseptal punctures in complex congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Vascular Plug Closure of Delayed Leaflet Perforation Post-TEER in Patient With Multiple Implantable Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is the main minimally invasive therapy for severe mitral regurgitation (MR) in patients at high surgical risk. Roughly 10% of patients develop recurrent MR within 1 year postoperatively. Postprocedural mitral anatomical distortion complicates reintervention, rendering recurrent MR management a common clinical challenge.

CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old man with multivalvular heart disease, chronic heart failure, multiple implantable devices and dialysis-dependent end-stage renal disease presented with symptomatic severe recurrent MR secondary to delayed anterior mitral leaflet perforation after TEER. Under combined fluoroscopic and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, our multidisciplinary team performed transcatheter closure of the perforation using a vascular plug. MR was markedly alleviated, heart failure symptoms resolved, and the patient recovered uneventfully before discharge.

DISCUSSION: TEER-related leaflet perforation caused severe recurrent MR. Percutaneous plug closure successfully downgraded MR to trivial, confirming the feasibility of this approach for mitral leaflet perforation.

articles.title: Pregnancy-Related Right Atrial Appendage Tachycardia Requiring ECMO and Hybrid Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right atrial appendage atrial tachycardia (AT) during pregnancy is rare and can progress to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy and shock.

CASE SUMMARY: A 22-year-old woman at 36 weeks and 5 days of gestation presented with fatigue, dyspnea, and narrow-complex tachycardia at 190-210 beats/min. Echocardiography showed an ejection fraction of 18%. After failed medical therapy, cardioversion, and esophageal pacing, she underwent emergency cesarean delivery and venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Mapping localized the AT to the base of the right atrial appendage; endocardial radiofrequency (RF) and pulsed field ablation produced only transient sinus rhythm. Thoracoscopic bipolar RF ablation with surgical clamping restored durable sinus rhythm.

CONCLUSIONS: Appendage-origin AT in pregnancy can progress rapidly to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy, and timely venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation support improves the prognosis. RF and pulsed field ablation may be insufficient for deep or possibly epicardial substrates; surgical ablation should be considered when catheter ablation fails.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Renal Denervation and Perirenal Adipose Tissue Debulking for Refractory Hypertension in End-Stage Renal Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Both renal sympathetic nerves and perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) drive hypertension. However, evidence regarding renal denervation (RDN) in end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains limited.

FIRST-IN-HUMAN SUMMARY: A 74-year-old man with diabetic chronic kidney disease stage 5 presented with refractory hypertension despite treatment with 4 antihypertensive agents and intravenous nitroprusside. He underwent bilateral laparoscopic-assisted RDN combined with PRAT debulking without complications. At 5-month follow-up, office and ambulatory blood pressures were substantially reduced, while renal function and medications remained stable.

DISCUSSION: Our case provides preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility of a combined laparoscopic RDN and PRAT debulking strategy in a patient with ESRD and refractory hypertension.

NOVELTY: To our knowledge, this is the first report of RDN combined with PRAT debulking using the laparoscopic system in ESRD.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This combined intervention offers a promising new therapeutic option for refractory hypertension in patients with advanced kidney disease.

articles.title: An Adrenal Adenoma as the Culprit Behind 30 Years of Recurrent Syncope.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary aldosteronism (PA) is a treatable endocrine cause of secondary hypertension and, rarely, ventricular tachycardia (VT), syncope, or sudden cardiac death.

CASE SUMMARY: A 59-year-old woman with hypertension presented with recurrent syncope for 30 years, worsening over 2 weeks. Electrocardiogram showed multifocal premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), with one dominant morphology triggering predominantly monomorphic VT, plus corrected QT interval prolongation. Hypokalemia, renal potassium wasting, left ventricular enlargement, and mild systolic dysfunction were also present.
