Ventricular arrhythmias recurred despite electrolyte repletion, beta-blocker therapy, and radiofrequency catheter ablation. A positive saline infusion test and a 3.6-cm left adrenal adenoma supported PA. After adrenalectomy, potassium normalized, palpitations improved, VT burden decreased, and syncope did not recur at 1 month.

DISCUSSION: PA may present primarily with ventricular arrhythmias and syncope. In patients with ventricular arrhythmias accompanied by hypertension and hypokalemia, PA should be considered as a treatable endocrine-metabolic cause.

articles.title: Novel SCN5A Variant in a Patient With Dilated Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Conduction Disorders and Recurrent Ventricular Arrhythmias.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit 5 (SCN5A) was traditionally linked to electrophysiological disorders, growing evidence underscores its significant involvement in structural abnormalities.

CASE SUMMARY: A young dilated cardiomyopathy patient presented with a distinctive electro-structural dual phenotype, characterized by progressive left ventricular systolic dysfunction, conduction disorders, and concomitant severe ventricular arrhythmias. Comorbidities included coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous nonsense variant in the SCN5A gene. Comprehensive management included guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, antiarrhythmic agents, along with comorbidities management and risk factor modification.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of dilated cardiomyopathy in young patients with multiple overlapping etiologies-genetic, ischemic, metabolic. A de novo SCN5A variant may contribute to the arrhythmic phenotype and progressive cardiomyopathy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Beyond its classical electrophysiological role, SCN5A is increasingly implicated in structural remodeling. This case emphasizes the complexity of genotype-phenotype correlation and gene-environment interaction.

articles.title: Exercise-Induced Ventricular Arrhythmia: Initial Presentation of Occult Barlow Syndrome Unmasked by Stress Testing.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Barlow syndrome, a form of myxomatous mitral valve prolapse, often presents with nonspecific symptoms and may be missed on resting examination.

CASE SUMMARY: A 38-year-old woman presented with recurrent palpitations triggered by stress and poor sleep. Resting physical examination was unremarkable. Exercise stress test (EST) revealed frequent premature ventricular contractions and a midlate systolic apical click postexercise, which were both previously absent at rest. Echocardiography confirmed Barlow syndrome with 7 mm mitral annular disjunction (MAD). Beta-blocker therapy was initiated with symptomatic improvement.

DISCUSSION: The EST unmasked both electrophysiological and auscultatory abnormalities entirely occult on standard resting evaluation. This case offers a practical diagnostic reference for recognizing latent cardiac diseases in patients with nonspecific symptoms.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: EST plays a crucial role in diagnosing atypical Barlow syndrome by unmasking both arrhythmias and characteristic auscultatory findings. Beta-blocker therapy effectively improves symptoms in patients with mitral annular disjunction-associated exercise-induced arrhythmias.

articles.title: Cardiac CT Planning of Surgical Treatment of Multiple Coronary-Pulmonary Fistulas With Chronic Coronary Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
ANATOMY: Coronary fistulas are rare congenital anomalies that may lead to myocardial ischemia through a coronary steal phenomenon, particularly when associated with coronary artery disease.

PATHOLOGY: We describe a case of cardiac computed tomography angiography (CCTA) diagnosis of multiple coronary-pulmonary artery fistulas associated with chronic occlusion of the right coronary artery, in a 66-year-old man presenting with unstable angina.

IMAGING CORRELATION: CCTA and echocardiography were used for evaluation of procedural planning in an acute setting.

TREATMENT: The fistulas were effectively treated with surgical exclusion combined with coronary artery bypass grafting, yielding an optimal result on the postoperative computed tomography scan.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Coronary fistulas are rare but important causes of myocardial ischemia. This case highlights the importance of CCTA definition of anatomical complexity and multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of complex coronary fistulas. Surgical repair remains the preferred approach in complex anatomy cases or associated coronary artery disease requiring revascularization.

articles.title: Microglial Presenilin-1 Modulates Neuronal Function and Memory-Associated Behaviors.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Microglial cells, the macrophages of the brain parenchyma, are increasingly recognized to play a key role in synaptic plasticity and function. Presenilin 1 (PS1) is an essential protein involved in learning and memory; the loss of neuronal Presenilin function causes cognitive deficits and impaired synapse plasticity in mice. Here we show memory enhancement in male mice lacking PS1 in microglia (PS1ΔMG). Leveraging high-throughput RNA sequencing with single-cell deconvolution analysis, we estimate that PS1ΔMG increases Cd52-lo microglial population, a proliferative group enriched in AP-1 responsive genes; and increases chemokines Ccl7 and Ccl8 In silico prediction of binding partners showed that microglial CCL7 may act via inhibition of neuronal CCR5, a receptor known to negatively regulate learning and memory. By profiling active neuronal populations via PhosphoTRAP, the data showed a nonautonomous cell effect of microglial PS1 by modulating genes involved in neuronal excitability and synaptic plasticity. Ex vivo electrophysiology and in vivo calcium imaging in freely behaving mice confirm these effects with functional changes in CA1 hippocampus as seen by increased NMDA/AMPA ratios and increased amplitude of neuronal Ca2+ transients in freely behaving animals, respectively. Remarkably, PS1ΔMG mice exhibited increased memory retention in contextual fear conditioning and novel object recognition. Together, these data suggest a novel mechanism where microglial PS1 negatively regulates neuronal activity through modulation of NMDAR and memory-associated behaviors.

articles.title: [The blood biomarker breakthrough in Alzheimer's disease: what applications in 2026? Part I: Blood biomarkers transitioning to clinical practice].
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of cognitive decline, and its diagnosis increasingly relies on a clinicobiological approach combining cognitive assessment with disease-specific biomarkers. Until recently, these biomarkers were mainly measured in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), requiring lumbar puncture. Advances in ultrasensitive analytical technologies now enable their detection in blood, providing a less invasive, more accessible, and potentially earlier diagnostic alternative. This review summarizes the current state of blood-based biomarkers available for clinical use, focusing on markers of the amyloid pathway (Aβ1-42, Aβ1-40, and their ratio) and the Tau pathway (pTau181, pTau217, pTau231, and BD-Tau). Amyloid peptides reflect early amyloid pathology but show limited diagnostic performance when used alone. In contrast, phosphorylated Tau biomarkers, particularly pTau217 and the pTau217/Aβ1-42 ratio, demonstrate excellent diagnostic accuracy and strong correlations with established CSF and amyloid PET biomarkers. These blood biomarkers have recently been incorporated into national and international diagnostic recommendations and are progressively entering routine clinical practice. Their implementation represents a major advance in the diagnosis, patient stratification, and therapeutic monitoring of AD. Despite these promising developments, challenges remain regarding analytical standardization, interpretation thresholds, and ethical considerations related to very early diagnosis. Nevertheless, blood-based biomarkers are expected to play a central role in future Alzheimer's disease management and precision medicine strategies.

articles.title: STEMI at Term Managed With IVUS-Guided Percutaneous Coronary Intervention and Cesarean Delivery.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicating pregnancy is rare, with a maternal case-fatality rate of 4.5%. ST-elevation myocardial infarction in a near-term gravida requires revascularization, fetal radiation protection, and multidisciplinary coordination.

CASE SUMMARY: A 32-year-old woman at 38 weeks of gestation with no cardiovascular risk factors presented with anterior STEMI from total left anterior descending artery occlusion. Emergent radial-access percutaneous coronary intervention was performed without sedation; intravascular ultrasound confirmed wire position through a thrombus-laden occlusion. Overlapping drug-eluting stents restored TIMI flow grade-3, with air kerma below fetal thresholds. Uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy continued through cesarean delivery, with blood loss controlled by hemostatic agents. Mother and neonate were discharged in good health.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the ambiguity between thrombotic occlusion and spontaneous dissection in pregnancy, the role of intravascular ultrasound when angiography is unreliable, and antiplatelet decision-making when surgery follows percutaneous coronary intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Emergent intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention is feasible at 38 weeks of gestation. Multidisciplinary planning, radiation mitigation, and individualized antiplatelet strategy determine outcomes.

articles.title: [Correlation between albuminuria and glycated haemoglobin in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²].
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage chronic kidney disease worldwide. Albuminuria, assessed by the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), is an independent marker of both renal prognosis and cardiovascular risk. To assess the correlation between HbA1c and ACR in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and to determine the prevalence of pathological albuminuria in this population. A retrospective case-control study conducted from June 2023 to June 2026. Cases were diabetic patients (HbA1c ≥ 6.5%) and controls were non-diabetic subjects (HbA1c < 5.7%), all with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (KDIGO stages G1: ≥ 90 and G2: 60-89) and an available ACR measurement. Albuminuria was classified according to KDIGO as A1 (> 30 mg/g), A2 (30-300 mg/g) and A3 (> 300 mg/g). eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI 2021 equation. Statistical analysis used Spearman, Mann-Whitney and Chi² tests. Four hundred and twenty subjects were included: 232 diabetic patients and 188 non-diabetic controls. The prevalence of pathological albuminuria was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in controls (44.0% vs. 21.3%; p > 0.0001), as was the median ACR (23.5 vs. 9.0 mg/g; p > 0.0001). Within the diabetic group, no significant correlation was found between HbA1c and ACR (Spearman r = 0.016; p = 0.814). In contrast, ACR was significantly higher in stage G2 than in stage G1: 33.5 vs. 15,0 mg/g (p = 0.003), and increased with age (r = 0.169; p = 0.010). This study reveals a high prevalence of pathological albuminuria in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Point HbA1c does not predict the degree of albuminuria, whereas eGFR stage and age are its main biological determinants. These findings support an integrated biological approach combining ACR and eGFR with HbA1c monitoring.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Surgical Challenges in Atypical Right Coronary Sinus-Right Atrial Rupture With Concurrent VSD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm is a rare anomaly that, when ruptured, causes high-flow shunts and rapid-onset heart failure. We report a rare anatomical variant of right coronary sinus aneurysm rupturing into the right atrium with a concurrent perimembranous ventricular septal defect (pmVSD).

CASE SUMMARY: A 16-year-old male with known pmVSD presented with progressive NYHA functional class III dyspnea for 15 days. Volume overload was initially misattributed to ventricular septal defect progression. However, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a restrictive pmVSD (3.4 mm opening, peak gradient 60 mm Hg), elevated right ventricular systolic pressure (76 mm Hg) as a flow-mediated surrogate for pulmonary artery systolic pressure, and a ruptured sinus of Valsalva aneurysm with a high-velocity jet into the right atrium. Because of "washout" artifacts, coronary computed tomography angiography failed to visualize the fistulous tract. Single-stage surgical repair of both lesions achieved complete recovery.

DISCUSSION: This case emphasizes color Doppler echocardiography's value in dual-shunt physiology when coronary computed tomography angiography is inconclusive, supporting single-stage surgical repair for multilesion presentations.

articles.title: Beyond Mirror Imaging: Rotational Atherectomy in Dextroversion.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe, to our knowledge, the first reported case of how to safely and effectively complete complex percutaneous coronary intervention in a patient with dextroversion and a severely calcified obstructive lesion in the left anterior descending coronary artery.

KEY STEPS: A 68-year-old man with self-reported dextrocardia and progressive angina underwent preprocedural coronary computed tomography angiography, which diagnosed dextroversion, multivessel disease, and a calcium score of 1,089. Horizontal fluoroscopic inversion was applied and improved visual familiarity but did not restore true anatomical orientation. Under intravascular ultrasound guidance, a severely calcified left anterior descending lesion was treated with rotational atherectomy (1.5-mm burr) and drug-eluting stent implantation.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: In patients with dextrocardia, including dextroversion, defining anatomy before cardiac catheterization can help increase efficiency and enhance safety in this group, especially for complex percutaneous coronary intervention.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Unlike mirror-image dextrocardia, dextroversion lacks true mirror anatomy, so fluoroscopic mirroring alone cannot "normalize" orientation. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography and intraprocedural intravascular imaging were essential for anatomic clarification and allowed safe, effective complex percutaneous coronary intervention.

articles.title: Ventricular Fibrillation in PRKAG2 Cardiomyopathy: A Genetic Arrhythmia Substrate Beyond Wolff-Parkinson-White.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant glycogen storage cardiomyopathy characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy, ventricular pre-excitation, and progressive conduction system disease.

CASE SUMMARY: We report the case of a 25-year-old woman with genetically confirmed PRKAG2 syndrome who presented with an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Echocardiography revealed preserved left ventricular systolic function with mild concentric hypertrophy and marked apical thickening. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed anterolateral trabecular hypertrophy without evidence of myocardial fibrosis. Electrophysiological study excluded Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome and instead identified a fasciculoventricular accessory pathway. Given the occurrence of ventricular fibrillation and the associated arrhythmic risk, a transvenous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted for secondary prevention.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates the atypical presentation of arrhythmias that deviate from classical patterns, such as those seen in Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Individualized risk assessment, close electrophysiological monitoring, and consideration of early implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation are important in PRKAG2-related cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: Durable Vessel Patency Achieved by Drug-Coated Balloon-Only Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Triglyceride Deposit Cardiomyovasculopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Triglyceride deposit cardiomyovasculopathy (TGCV) causes triglyceride accumulation in cardiomyocytes and vascular smooth muscle cells, leading to diffuse coronary artery disease and frequent restenosis after percutaneous coronary intervention.

CASE SUMMARY: A 37-year-old man with diabetes mellitus presented with diffuse 3-vessel coronary disease. Angiography and computed tomography revealed concentric diffuse coronary stenoses, and intravascular ultrasound demonstrated periadventitial low-echoic structures. Iodine-123-β-methyl-iodophenyl pentadecanoic acid scintigraphy showed a severely reduced washout rate, supporting the diagnosis of TGCV. The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention using a cutting balloon followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty without stent implantation. No restenosis was observed by angiography at 1 year or computed tomography at 3 years.

DISCUSSION: This case suggests that a stentless revascularization strategy using a drug-coated balloon may be a feasible option in TGCV, potentially avoiding pathological vascular responses associated with permanent metallic scaffolds.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Stentless intervention may represent a promising therapeutic option in patients with TGCV.

articles.title: Primary aldosteronism severity grading: missing the mark for the moderate majority.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

articles.title: Paradoxical Embolism in Young Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Without Coronary Atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in young patients (<50 years) accounts for 2%-10% of all ACS presentations. We describe a case series of young patients who presented with ACS in the absence of coronary atherosclerosis or other identifiable causes such as spontaneous coronary artery dissection and Takotsubo syndrome. Further diagnostic evaluation, often initiated after cryptogenic stroke or a recurrent systemic embolic event, revealed the presence of significant right-to-left shunting because of an atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale. After exclusion of other etiologies for thromboembolic events (ie, atrial fibrillation, endocarditis, thrombophilia, and antiphospholipid syndrome), patients underwent successful percutaneous septal closure. These cases underscore the importance of considering paradoxical embolism in the differential diagnosis of ACS in young patients without other etiologies. Percutaneous septal closure may be considered for secondary prevention when paradoxical embolism is suspected.

articles.title: Leadless Atrial Pacemaker Migration Presenting as Gluteal Spasms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers are associated with high procedural success and low complication rates; however, device dislodgement and embolization remain rare but recognized adverse events. Most reported cases involve embolization to the pulmonary vasculature.

CASE SUMMARY: An 80-year-old woman underwent uncomplicated implantation of a leadless atrial pacemaker for symptomatic sinus node dysfunction. Overnight, she developed rhythmic unilateral lower extremity spasms. Telemetry and electrocardiogram demonstrated atrial undersensing and loss of capture. Physical exam revealed involuntary leg and gluteal contractions at 60 beats/mins. Imaging localized the pacemaker to the right internal iliac vein. Device deactivation resulted in immediate symptom resolution, confirming extracardiac pacing-induced skeletal muscle stimulation.

DISCUSSION: This represents the first reported case of leadless pacemaker embolization into the iliac venous system presenting with neuromuscular stimulation, expanding the spectrum of leadless pacemaker complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: New-onset rhythmic muscle spasms after leadless pacemaker implantation may be an early sign of device migration and extracardiac pacing.

articles.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Requiring Modification of a Protruding RCA Stent.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Protruding ostial stents represent a unique hazard for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

CASE SUMMARY: An 81-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and recent right coronary artery stenting with a 10-mm segment protruding into the aortic root presented for TAVR evaluation. After multidisciplinary discussion, the decision was made to proceed with TAVR with stent modification. The right coronary artery was wired through the stent struts at the distal end of the protruded segment and was ballooned, creating a neo-ostium. The protruded segment was crushed against the aortic wall using a valvuloplasty balloon. A balloon-expandable TAVR valve was deployed, with no coronary obstruction.

DISCUSSION: This case represents a challenging TAVR procedure requiring a unique strategy to modify a protruding stent.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: A structured sequence of: 1) neo-ostium creation (displacement of protruding stent segment); 2) balloon aortic valvuloplasty crush (aortic wall alignment); 3) controlled TAVR valve deployment; and 4) ostial optimization is reproducible.

articles.title: Mechanistic insights for the preparation of improved metal-fluoride based radioimaging agents.
articles.abstract: Metal-fluoride complexes incorporating fluorine-18 are advancing PET imaging, and creating new opportunities for Total Body PET and theranostics, but the factors governing metal-chelator selection, radiofluorination mechanisms, and hydroxide competition remain unclear. Although several Al-18F tracers based on NOTA and NODA chelators have reached clinical use, mechanistic understanding is limited and has hindered both extension to other metals and chelators and understanding of the relative merits of "one-pot" (radio)fluorination protocols vs. late-stage (radio)fluorination of pre-formed complexes and the design criteria to optimise (radio)metal/18F tracers for theranostics. Here, density functional theory (DFT) calculations are used to investigate F-/Cl- and OH-/Cl- substitution in the archetypal [MCl(Bn-NODA)] (M = Al, Ga). These reactions proceed through a concerted one-step pathway involving temporary dissociation of a carboxylate arm and formation of a transient ionic intermediate, as well as a two-step pathway. Hydroxide substitution is exothermic, favouring formation of [M(OH)(Bn-NODA)], and provides insight into hydroxide competition during radiolabelling. Parallel DFT studies reveal how OH- influences [MF(Bn-NODA)] and radiolabelling efficiency. The computational results align with experimental observations of rapid, late-stage 18F radiolabelling of pre-formed gallium complexes under mild conditions and provide design principles for developing new metal-fluoride radiotracers for imaging and therapy. More broadly, the study highlights the value of computational screening in guiding the development of a wider range of metal-fluoride-based agents for imaging and therapy.

articles.title: OCT-Derived FFR-Guided Management of Iatrogenic RCA Deformation During Transcatheter Tricuspid Annuloplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iatrogenic right coronary artery (RCA) deformation is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter tricuspid annuloplasty (TTA) with K-Clip. Although bailout coronary stenting may restore vessel patency, unnecessary stent implantation exposes patients to long-term risks.

CASE SUMMARY: A 77-year-old woman with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent TTA with K-Clip. Angiography demonstrated RCA deformation; optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealed extrinsic mechanical deformation without intraluminal injury, and OCT-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) demonstrated the absence of physiologically significant flow limitation; hence, percutaneous coronary intervention was deferred.

DISCUSSION: Angiography may overestimate the severity of RCA deformation following TTA with K-Clip. This case demonstrates the potential of OCT-derived FFR to optimize procedural decision-making and improve the safety of TTA. Further prospective studies are needed to validate this strategy and establish its role in routine clinical practice.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: OCT-derived FFR adds objective physiological assessment and avoids unnecessary coronary stenting during TTA and may represent a novel imaging-guided algorithm to improve procedural safety.

articles.title: Mavacamten for Obstructive HCM in Malignancy With Life-Threatening Symptoms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A 79-year-old woman admitted to critical care with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and metastatic pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor presented with recurrent pulmonary edema and hemodynamic compromise from dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.

CASE SUMMARY: Mavacamten was initiated, leading to rapid symptomatic improvement. However, during the course of treatment, the patient developed marked liver enzyme elevation, raising concern for drug-induced liver injury or an alternate oncological diagnosis.

DISCUSSION: Multidisciplinary discussion was essential for reaching the final diagnosis of biliary obstruction and restarting mavacamten, breaking the vicious circle of recurrent presyncope and pulmonary edema secondary to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multidisciplinary decision-making is paramount when considering novel therapies in complex cardio-oncology patients.

articles.title: Algorithm-Facilitated Pacemaker-Mediated Tachycardia Mimicking Refractory Septic Shock.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Algorithms that minimize right ventricular pacing, such as atrioventricular (AV) hysteresis, prolong the AV delay to promote intrinsic conduction. With intact ventriculoatrial (VA) conduction, this can facilitate pacemaker-mediated tachycardia (PMT).

CASE SUMMARY: A 62-year-old woman with a dual-chamber pacemaker presented with respiratory failure and hypotension at a paced rate of 110 beats/min, treated for presumed sepsis with escalating vasopressors. Interrogation showed an upper tracking rate of 130 beats/min, AV hysteresis ON, and postventricular atrial refractory period (PVARP) (225 milliseconds) shorter than VA conduction (360 milliseconds), producing a 550-millisecond endless-loop PMT (∼109 beats/min) that escaped device detection. Disabling hysteresis and extending PVARP terminated it, allowing vasopressor weaning.

DISCUSSION: When PVARP is shorter than the VA interval, a long AV delay converts retrograde conduction into a slow re-entrant circuit that escapes device diagnostics and mimics sinus tachycardia.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Suspect slow PMT in paced patients with fixed tachycardia near 100-110 beats/min when AV hysteresis is active. Disabling hysteresis and extending PVARP beyond VA conduction is diagnostic and lifesaving.

articles.title: The Delipidation of Coronary Plaques.
Acute Rheumatic Fever: Atrial Flutter Associated With Carditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is an immune-mediated sequela of group A streptococcal infection that can progress to rheumatic heart disease (RHD), defined by permanent rheumatic valvular damage. Although uncommon in the United States, delayed recognition may lead to advanced valve disease and arrhythmias.

CASE SUMMARY: A 10-year-old African-American male presented after syncope following 4 months of unexplained bilateral ankle arthritis. He was found to be in atrial flutter. Echocardiography showed a flail mitral valve with severe regurgitation, moderate tricuspid regurgitation, and mild-to-moderate aortic insufficiency. After several cardioversions to re-establish sinus rhythm, he underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid annuloplasty 1 week after presentation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the need for a high index of suspicion for ARF in children presenting with unexplained inflammatory symptoms and new cardiac findings, even in low-prevalence settings. Early recognition, treatment, and secondary prophylaxis help prevent recurrent ARF and progression to RHD.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Children with unexplained arthritis, systemic inflammation, arrhythmia, and multivalvular disease should be evaluated for ARF and evolving RHD to reduce morbidity and prevent disease progression.

articles.title: Retained Coronary Guidewire With Proximal Systemic Extension Requiring Emergent Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Retained coronary guidewire fracture with proximal systemic extension is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of percutaneous coronary intervention, occurring in approximately 0.02% to 0.08% of procedures.

CASE SUMMARY: A 66-year-old man with myocardial infarction underwent intravascular ultrasound-guided percutaneous coronary intervention for subtotal right coronary artery occlusion. High-pressure post-dilation of overlapping drug-eluting stents caused guidewire entrapment, fracture, and proximal extension into the ascending aorta and right subclavian artery. Following failed percutaneous retrieval, emergent coronary artery bypass grafting with aortotomy enabled extraction of 35.5 cm of guidewire while a 2.5-cm distal coronary fragment was intentionally retained. The patient recovered without recurrent ischemia and was discharged on clopidogrel and rivaroxaban.

DISCUSSION: Proximal systemic extension beyond the coronary ostium represented the inflection point for surgical escalation. A structured review of 23 published cases supports a practical location- and risk-based management framework.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Failed percutaneous retrieval with proximal systemic extension beyond the coronary ostium should prompt early multidisciplinary surgical evaluation.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Mitral Valve Repair Through a Native Atrial Septal Defect: An Anatomy-Guided Strategy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe an anatomy-guided transcatheter edge-to-edge mitral valve repair (M-TEER) strategy using a native secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) as the sole transseptal access route.

KEY STEPS: Preprocedural computed tomography and 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography to assess the access route, ASD anatomy, and anticipated guide catheter alignment. Guidewire and steerable guide catheter advancement through the native ASD under real-time 3-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography guidance. Sequential M-TEER device deployment with continuous hemodynamic and oximetric monitoring. Confirmation of mitral regurgitation reduction and planned staged ASD closure.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: Preprocedural multimodality imaging may help determine procedural feasibility. In patients with decompensated heart failure, staged ASD closure after M-TEER may be preferable.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Preprocedural multimodality imaging may identify patients in whom a native secundum ASD can serve as the sole transseptal access route for M-TEER, avoiding additional septal puncture. In patients with decompensated heart failure, staged ASD closure after successful M-TEER may be preferable.

articles.title: Superior Vena Cava Syndrome Immediately After Transvenous Lead Extraction: A Rare But Important Complication.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior vena cava syndrome is recognized as a complication of cardiac implantable electronic devices, usually resulting from a chronic venous obstruction related to transvenous leads. However, acute presentation is uncommon and may represent a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge.

CASE SUMMARY: A 45-year-old man with long-standing pacemaker dependency due to complete heart block underwent transvenous lead extraction due to pacing-induce cardiomyopathy. Shortly after the procedure, he developed facial edema and cyanosis. Imaging revealed chronic right axillary vein thrombosis and acute-on-chronic left subclavian vein thrombosis associated with abandoned leads. Management included temporary femoral pacing, lead removal, serial venous angioplasty, and subsequent leadless pacemaker implantation, with favorable clinical outcome.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights acute superior vena cava syndrome as a rare but important periprocedural complication of lead extraction, particularly in patients with high lead burden and preexisting venous disease. Prompt diagnosis and multidisciplinary management are critical to achieve successful outcomes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Acute superior vena cava syndrome may occur shortly after transvenous lead extraction procedures.

articles.title: Managing High-Output Heart Failure Secondary to Prostacyclin Analog and Sotatercept Toxicity in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We present a rare case of high-output heart failure (HF) resulting from prostacyclin analogue toxicity following the addition of sotatercept.

CASE SUMMARY: A 36-year-old woman with World Health Organization Group I pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a history of suspected but hemodynamically unconfirmed heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and morbid obesity maintained on treprostinil and sildenafil therapy, developed progressive hypoxia, anasarca and dyspnea 3 months after sotatercept initiation. Serial right heart catheterizations demonstrated a shift from severe precapillary pulmonary hypertension to a high-output state with elevated biventricular filling pressures. The patient required intensive care unit admission for diuresis, vasopressors and continuous renal replacement therapy. Treprostinil discontinuation improved hemodynamics, followed by normalization after sotatercept discontinuation.

DISCUSSION: Severe obesity in association with synergistic vasodilatory effects from sotatercept and treprostinil therapy reduced systemic vascular resistance, increased cardiac output and raised biventricular filling pressures, culminating in high-output HF and unmasking occult diastolic dysfunction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: High-output HF may occur with prostacyclin toxicity after sotatercept initiation, underscoring individualized careful hemodynamic assessment in complex patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension.

articles.title: Parallel Septal Balloon Occlusion for Acute Right-to-Left Shunt During Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) requires large-bore transseptal puncture, creating an iatrogenic atrial septal defect (IASD). Right-to-left shunting across an IASD is rare but can cause significant hypoxemia in high-risk patients.

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old man with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation underwent M-TEER. Profound hypoxemia secondary to acute right-to-left shunt developed immediately after transseptal instrumentation with a large-bore sheath. A compliant sizing balloon was inflated across the septal defect in parallel with the transseptal sheath, restoring oxygenation and allowing safe deployment of the PASCAL (Edwards Lifesciences) valve, with septal closure performed at the end of the procedure.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates a distinctive predeployment presentation of right-to-left IASD shunting and a novel bailout technique that preserves transseptal access without requiring additional venous puncture.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Right-to-left IASD shunting should be anticipated in patients with high-risk hemodynamic profiles before transseptal puncture. Parallel balloon septal occlusion represents a practical bridging strategy enabling safe M-TEER completion.

articles.title: Microvessel Rupture and Intraplaque Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is an important mechanism of plaque progression and destabilization, primarily attributed to disruption of fragile intraplaque microvessels; however, in vivo demonstration of this process remains limited.

CASE SUMMARY: A 56-year-old woman presented with unstable angina. Coronary computed tomography angiography demonstrated a noncalcified, low-attenuation plaque with positive remodeling in the proximal right coronary artery. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealed intraplaque microvessels, a crescent-shaped hypointense plaque region consistent with IPH, and findings suggestive of microvessel disruption. The lesion was successfully treated with drug-eluting stent implantation.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the value of OCT in identifying intraplaque mechanisms of acute coronary syndrome beyond classical intimal disruption and provides in vivo findings suggestive of microvessel disruption associated with IPH.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES/LEARNING OBJECTIVES: IPH resulting from disruption of fragile intraplaque microvessels may represent an underrecognized mechanism of acute coronary syndrome. OCT enables detailed assessment of intraplaque architecture and may provide mechanistic insights beyond angiographic evaluation.

articles.title: Staged Transcatheter Treatment of Combined Aortic and Mitral Regurgitation: A Downstream Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Concomitant severe aortic (AR) and mitral regurgitation (MR) affects up to 25% of patients with aortic valve disease and portends poor prognosis. Evidence on a sequential downstream approach in native AR is limited.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 4 patients with high surgical risk (mean age 82 years, Society of Thoracic Surgeons score >8) with severe AR and MR treated with transcatheter aortic valve replacement for native AR. In 2 patients with secondary MR, AR correction was followed by reverse remodeling and downstaging of MR from severe to moderate, avoiding mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair. In the remaining 2 patients, MR remained severe, and staged mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair was performed.

DISCUSSION: These cases support the hypothesis that MR etiology, rather than AR correction alone, determines whether MR regresses after isolated AR treatment.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: MR etiology and post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement reassessment may guide a staged transcatheter strategy, sparing unnecessary mitral intervention in inoperable patients with combined AR/MR.

articles.title: Reply to 'Cautious interpretation of the association between topical corticosteroid exposure and type 2 diabetes'.
Cautious interpretation of the association between topical corticosteroid exposure and type 2 diabetes.
Plasma proteins are integral to cross-tissue gene regulatory networks implicated in cardiometabolic disorders and coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract: The plasma proteome has demonstrated promise for identifying diagnostic markers for cardiometabolic disorders (CMDs) and coronary artery disease (CAD). However, identifying the organ of origin for these biomarkers is critical for establishing biological relevance. We performed a multi-omic integrative analysis across multiple tissues from the STARNET study by profiling 974 plasma proteins in 532 CAD patients, integrating RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from the arterial wall, major metabolic organs, and blood. We identified 144 cis-protein quantitative trait loci in plasma, colocalizing with tissue cis-expression quantitative trait loci. Additionally, by mapping tissue mRNA "seed genes," we traced 262 plasma proteins to their source organs, primarily the liver. Crucially, we found that 851 plasma proteins are associated with the activity of cross-tissue gene regulatory networks (GRNs), including GRNs implicated in CMD and CAD development. Our findings demonstrate that plasma proteins are integral components of GRNs, with potential for developing reliable diagnostics and precise therapeutic targets. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

articles.title: Bridging the Global Implementation Gap in Immediate Weight-Bearing After Hip Fracture Surgery: The WAIT-Free Consensus for Low-Adoption Regions.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract: Postoperative care for hip fractures remains globally inequitable. Immediate weight-bearing as tolerated (WBAT) after surgery is widely recommended in North America and Europe, yet it is not routinely implemented across regions that collectively represent over half of the world's population, including the People's Republic of China, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Africa (hereafter referred to as low-adoption regions [LARs]). To address this gap, the WAIT-Free Consensus was developed to support the safe and sustainable implementation of immediate WBAT for older adults with a hip fracture in these settings. A multidisciplinary Consensus Development Group of 31 international experts from 15 countries reviewed the available evidence and used a structured, 3-round Delphi process with a consensus threshold of ≥2/3 to develop and refine recommendations. The final consensus statement comprised 13 recommendations organized around 4 domains: (1) shared decision-making with proportionate documentation of informed discussions about benefits and realistic risks, (2) mobility-based stratification that prioritizes immediate WBAT for patients who were independently ambulatory before the fracture, (3) structured fall prevention and multidisciplinary perioperative optimization, and (4) postoperative stability-related triage to individualize weight-bearing protocols after internal fixation versus arthroplasty. In addition, a pragmatic supportive-factor checklist is provided to guide phased implementation. This consensus statement provides a structured, evidence-informed pathway for LARs to adopt immediate WBAT after hip fracture surgery in older adults. The recommendations can be adapted to local resource constraints, with implementation audited using context-specific indicators and refined iteratively as capacity and evidence evolve.

articles.title: ARCAPA Unveiled During Preoperative Assessment for Mitral Valve Repair: Clinical Implications of an Incidental Finding.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anomalous origin of the right coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ARCAPA) in association with primary mitral regurgitation is an exceedingly uncommon congenital anomaly.

CASE SUMMARY: A 56-year-old man with progressive dyspnea for 12 years, apparently because of degenerative mitral regurgitation, was incidentally diagnosed with ARCAPA on coronary angiography during preoperative evaluation for mitral valve repair. Coronary computed tomography angiography confirmed ARCAPA, detailing the aberrant anatomy. The patient underwent successful complex mitral valve repair, closure of the coronary-pulmonary artery connection, and reimplantation of the right coronary artery into the ascending aorta, with modified cardioplegia. Postoperative imaging demonstrated effective repair and restoration of normal coronary perfusion.

DISCUSSION: ARCAPA is diagnosed by dilated right coronary artery, retrograde flow, and extensive collaterals on imaging. Correction of coronary steal and restoration of 2-vessel anatomy can be achieved through surgical repair or an endovascular approach.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: ARCAPA should be considered in the differential diagnosis of adult onset exertional dyspnea. A missed preoperative diagnosis may lead to catastrophic ischemia following cardioplegia delivery.

articles.title: Letrozole in pediatric females for peripheral precocious puberty: a systematic review of efficacy and safety.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Letrozole, a third-generation aromatase inhibitor, has been increasingly investigated as an off-label treatment to improve growth outcomes in pediatric boys, whereas its use in girls has remained limited because of concerns regarding safety and efficacy, given the critical role of estrogens in female physiology. This gender gap has delayed research on letrozole in girls.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the clinical efficacy, growth outcomes, and safety profile of letrozole in girls with peripheral precocious puberty (PPP).

EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to May 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261423918). Eligible studies evaluated letrozole monotherapy in girls aged ≤18 years. Risk of bias was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute checklists and the Murad tool. Data were synthesized narratively according to the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Twenty-two observational studies encompassing 151 female patients were included. Twenty-one studies evaluated letrozole for PPP, predominantly McCune-Albright syndrome, where treatment effectively slowed pubertal progression, reduced bone age advancement, and improved predicted adult height. One exploratory study evaluated girls with short stature without pubertal disorders. Transition to central precocious puberty occurred during follow-up in 41.3% of patients. Safety was favorable (adverse events: 3.3%), with no clinically significant hyperandrogenism or hepatotoxicity.

CONCLUSION: Letrozole demonstrates meaningful clinical benefits in girls with PPP, particularly regarding pubertal control and predicted adult height, accompanied by a favorable safety profile. Well-designed prospective studies are needed to establish optimal dosing, long-term safety, and final adult height outcomes in the female pediatric population.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of recibokibart, an interleukin-36 receptor antibody, in generalized pustular psoriasis: a phase II randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP) is a rare, severe inflammatory skin disease characterized by acute flares. Recibokibart is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin (IL)-36 receptor. In a phase Ib open-label study, a single intravenous dose of recibokibart was associated with an acceptable safety profile and rapid improvements in pustulation, overall skin disease severity and systemic inflammatory markers through 12 weeks.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of recibokibart in patients with acute flares of GPP.

METHODS: In this multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II trial conducted in China, patients with moderate-to-severe acute GPP were randomly assigned in a 2 : 1 ratio to receive a single intravenous dose of recibokibart (1050 mg) or placebo at day 1. Patients with persistent disease activity at day 8 were eligible to receive open-label recibokibart, and patients with recurrent flares after achieving a Generalized Pustular Psoriasis Physician Global Assessment (GPPGA) total score of 0 or 1 could receive an additional open-label dose. The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients who achieved a GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 or 1 at week 1 (day 8).

RESULTS: A total of 33 patients were randomized (recibokibart, n = 22; placebo, n = 11). At week 1 (day 8), the primary endpoint of achieving a GPPGA pustulation subscore of 0 or 1 was met by 86% of patients in the recibokibart group vs. 9% in the placebo group (between-group difference 77.3%, 95% confidence interval 42.5-88.9; P < 0. 001). At week 1 (day 8), greater improvements were observed with recibokibart vs. placebo across key secondary endpoints, including achievement of a GPPGA total score of 0 or 1 (64% vs. 0%), complete pustule clearance (55% vs. 0%), and mean percentage change from baseline in GPPASI (-59.3% vs. 0%). By week 4, 73% of patients treated with recibokibart achieved ≥ 75% improvement from baseline in Generalized Pustular Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (GPPASI). Clinical improvements were observed as early as 24 h after treatment and were maintained through week 12, although assessments after day 8 included patients who received open-label treatment. The most frequently reported adverse events with recibokibart included hypoproteinaemia, hypertriglyceridaemia, hyperlipidaemia and pruritus.

CONCLUSIONS: A single intravenous dose of recibokibart resulted in rapid improvement in pustular and overall skin disease severity in patients with acute GPP flares, with an acceptable safety profile.

articles.title: Type A Dissection at Subthreshold Dimensions in Loeys-Dietz Syndrome: When Guideline-Directed Surveillance Is Not Enough.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) is a heritable connective tissue disorder associated with aggressive aortic disease.

CASE SUMMARY: A 45-year-old woman with a family history of aortic dissection and a TGFB2 variant associated with LDS underwent surveillance demonstrating an aortic root diameter of 3.7 to 4.0 cm. Five months later, she developed an acute Stanford type A aortic dissection requiring emergent Bentall aortic root and hemiarch replacement. Her postoperative course was complicated by graft-adjacent infection, giant graft-adjacent pseudoaneurysms requiring redo aortic root replacement with Cabrol coronary reconstruction, and inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by thrombotic occlusion of the right coronary graft.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates catastrophic vascular progression despite guideline-directed surveillance and highlights the challenges of long-term management after aortic root reconstruction.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Patients with LDS may experience life-threatening aortic complications despite subthreshold aortic dimensions. Improved individualized risk stratification beyond maximal aortic diameter is needed to optimize prophylactic intervention.

articles.title: Approach to the patient: ethics cases in pediatric endocrinology and their management.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: With advancing technologies and expanding indications for existing therapies, ethical dilemmas increasingly arise in pediatric endocrinology practice.

AIM: This article presents practical, case-based scenarios to guide clinicians in navigating common ethical challenges in pediatric endocrinology.

CASES: We present 4 case vignettes which present ethical dilemmas regarding (1) growth hormone treatment prescribed for idiopathic short stature; (2) precocious puberty management in a child with neurodevelopmental delay; (3) technology use in type 1 diabetes care; and (4) glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist use for obesity management. For each case, we outline patient presentations and management approaches which highlight the application of the four-principle ethical framework based on Beauchamp and Childress. Salient historical events are mentioned to serve as a basis to contextualize and situate the specific ethical dilemmas.

CONCLUSION: Ethical dilemmas have the potential to arise in the everyday practice of pediatric endocrinology. Application of the principles of beneficence, non-maleficence, respect for autonomy, and justice will allow for a pragmatic incorporation of ethical decision making in medical care.

articles.title: Does the higher asthma prevalence in preterm children with atopic dermatitis indicate a distinct allergic pathway?
Management of cirrhosis in diabetes: a pragmatic approach to the patient.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: As the global burden of cirrhosis shifts toward metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), diabetes and metabolic syndrome act as key upstream drivers of liver injury. At the same time, diabetes is increasingly recognized even in cirrhosis of nonmetabolic etiologies, including viral hepatitis, reflecting both shared risk factors and cirrhosis-related disturbances in glucose homeostasis. This coexistence amplifies morbidity, mortality, and therapeutic complexity, while conventional diabetes paradigms often prove inadequate in the management of cirrhosis. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes a pragmatic framework for managing diabetes across the full spectrum of cirrhosis. We examine the evolving concept of hepatogenous diabetes, limitations of HbA1c in advanced liver disease, and the complementary roles of oral glucose tolerance testing and continuous glucose monitoring in improving diagnostic accuracy. The pharmacologic landscape is critically evaluated, integrating contemporary diabetes guidelines with hepatic stage-specific considerations. Metformin remains the backbone of therapy in compensated cirrhosis. Among newer agents, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors show promise in compensated disease, particularly in patients with MASLD and cardiorenal comorbidities. In contrast, sulfonylureas, insulin secretagogues, and agents associated with fluid retention require caution or avoidance as hepatic reserve declines. Insulin therapy remains the cornerstone in decompensated cirrhosis and during hospitalization, where conservative dosing and dynamic titration are essential to minimize hypoglycemia. The review emphasizes nutritional optimization, frequent reassessment, and coordinated hepatology-endocrinology care. As diabetes in cirrhosis increasingly reflects the convergence of 2 metabolic disorders, management must prioritize hepatic safety, metabolic stability, and individualized outcomes over rigid glycemic targets.

articles.title: Cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in acromegaly-associated diabetes: a Swedish nationwide study.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Secondary diabetes mellitus occurs in 30% to 50% of patients with acromegaly despite a lean phenotype, whereas type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with adiposity.

OBJECTIVE: We compared mortality, morbidity, and treatment patterns between patients with acromegaly-associated diabetes (ACRO-DM) and T2DM.

DESIGN: Nationwide, retrospective, matched-cohort study in Sweden.

METHODS: The ACRO-DM group included patients with an acromegaly diagnosis in the Patient Register, with diabetes registered in the National Diabetes Register (NDR) or a dispensed glucose-lowering drug in the Prescribed Drug Register. Controls with T2DM from the NDR were matched 10:1 for sex, age, calendar year, and diabetes duration. We derived mortality and morbidity outcomes from the Death and Patient Registers.

RESULTS: We included 348 patients with ACRO-DM and 3480 with T2DM. Mean (SD) age was 60.3 (13.2) and 59.5 (15.6) years, whereas diabetes duration was 2.8 (5.8) and 3.0 (7.1) years in ACRO-DM and T2DM, respectively. Baseline cardiovascular morbidity was more common in ACRO-DM than T2DM group (61% vs 43%), including hypertension (48% vs 29%), heart failure (11% vs 5%), arrhythmia (13% vs 9%), and stroke (8% vs 5%).The hazard ratio (HR) for overall mortality was 1.18 (95% CI, 0.96-1.46) in ACRO-DM compared with T2DM group. The ACRO-DM group had a higher risk of cardiovascular morbidity (HR = 1.55; 95% CI, 1.24-1.94), with increased hazards for venous thromboembolism, specifically pulmonary, and arrhythmia, whereas cardiovascular mortality was not increased (HR = 1.12; 95% CI, 0.78-1.60).

CONCLUSION: The risk of cardiovascular morbidity was increased in patients with ACRO-DM compared to T2DM.

articles.title: Willingness to pay among individuals from the Dutch general population for artificial intelligence-based applications for skin cancer detection: a survey-based mixed-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rising incidence of skin cancer is increasing pressure on healthcare systems. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based mobile health applications (mHealth apps) are being offered to the general population to be used on their own initiative. However, the exact willingness to pay (WTP) for the apps and the factors influencing individual valuations remain unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate individuals' relative WTP for AI-based mHealth apps for skin cancer risk detection, and to explore the reasons underlying WTP using a mixed-methods approach.

METHODS: This survey-based study, embedded in a randomized controlled trial, invited 11 621 participants in the Netherlands between 29 August 2022 and 23 February 2023. Participants were offered a questionnaire about their experiences with an mHealth app, asked about their WTP in three hypothetical scenarios (AI alone, AI with teledermatologist involvement and physical dermatologist consultation) and could provide open-text explanations. Associations between participant characteristics and WTP were assessed using regression analyses, and qualitative analysis was applied to open-text responses.

RESULTS: A total of 1953 participants (17%, n = 1953/11 621) completed the questionnaire. Participants had a mean (SD) age of 58.4 (13.1) years, and 58% (n = 1125/1953) were women. Most participants self-reported as having a light skin type (95%, n = 1864/1953). A high educational level was reported by 50% of participants (n = 971/1953), and a large proportion reported prior app use (79%, n = 1550/1953). Median [interquartile range (IQR)] WTP was significantly higher for AI combined with a teledermatologist compared with AI alone [€20 (0-45) vs. €5 (0-20), P < 0.001], but lower than for a physical dermatologist consultation [€50 (22-75), P < 0.001]. Increasing age was the only participant characteristic positively associated with WTP across all scenarios. Qualitative analyses revealed that similar valuations could range from pragmatic to fundamental and reflect different rationales.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals place the highest monetary value on dermatologist involvement compared with AI-based apps alone. However, this study suggests that WTP does not always reflect perceived importance. Future studies could explore which features of these apps users value most and how to improve engagement.

articles.title: Relationship between metabolic remodeling of pancreatic β-cells and pancreatic histology in type 2 diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: 6-Phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-biphosphatase 3 (PFKFB3) is a key glycolytic regulator involved in the compensation for β-cell dysfunction under diabetic conditions, but its upstream regulation is incompletely understood. Here, we have characterized the relationship between the underlying pancreatic pathology and PFKFB3 expression in pancreatic β-cells.

METHODS: Pancreatic sections from deceased individuals with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D) were immunostained for PFKFB3. The ratios of PFKFB3-positive β and α cells were compared, and the relationships with islet amyloid and pancreatic fibrosis were assessed. PFKFB3 expression was also evaluated in caerulein-treated mice and INS-1 832/13 cells co-cultured with pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs), as models of fibrosis.

RESULTS: Eighteen individuals with and 18 without T2D were evaluated. The proportion of PFKFB3-positive β-cells, but not α-cells, was higher in those with T2D (23.9% ± 16.1% vs 8.7% ± 6.3%, P < .05). PFKFB3 expression negatively correlated with β-cell mass (ρ = -0.34, P < .05). Both the amyloid deposition and area of fibrosis positively correlated with the proportion of PFKFB3-positive β-cells (ρ = 0.50 and 0.84, respectively; P < .05). In mice, β-cell PFKFB3 positivity was higher in the fibrosis model vs controls (20.5% ± 10.5% vs 5.6% ± 5.1%, P < .05). Additionally, Pfkfb3 expression in INS-1 cells was significantly higher after co-culture with PSCs. In this co-culture model, RNA sequencing identified transforming growth factor (TGF)-β-related gene clusters; enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay confirmed high TGF-β levels, and western blotting showed greater phosphorylation of Smad.

CONCLUSION: PFKFB3-mediated metabolic remodeling occurs in the β-cells of individuals with T2D, and is linked not only to β-cell overload, but to pancreatic fibrosis and local TGF-β/Smad signaling.

articles.title: Partial lipodystrophy mimicking Cushing syndrome: clinical and metabolic insights from a multicenter study.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Partial lipodystrophies (PLD) can closely mimic the clinical presentation of Cushing syndrome (CS). Simplified risk scores have been developed to estimate the clinical probability of CS. However, their ability to discriminate CS from overlapping conditions such as PLD remains unclear. Moreover, reduced leptin action in lipodystrophy may influence the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, although human data are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To compare clinical and metabolic features of PLD and CS, evaluate the discriminatory ability of clinical risk scores for CS, and explore leptin-HPA axis interactions in PLD.

METHODS: Retrospective multicenter study including 61 patients with PLD and 56 patients with CS. Clinical and laboratory data were retrieved from medical records. Two clinical risk score for CS were calculated, and PLD and CS features were compared.

RESULTS: Most PLD patients showed at least one feature suggestive of hypercortisolism. Facial fullness, facial plethora, dorsocervical fat pad, and hirsutism (P < .001, P = .049, P < .001, and P < .001, respectively) were more frequent in PLD, while proximal muscle atrophy and osteoporosis (P < .001 and P = .010) were more common in CS. Higher rates of diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia were also observed in PLD (P < .001). PLD patients achieved similar or even higher clinical CS score values than CS patients. In multivariable regression analysis, proximal muscle atrophy and osteoporosis were associated with CS (P < .04), whereas diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia were associated with PLD (both P < .001). No correlation was found between leptin levels and glucocorticoid-related hormonal parameters.

CONCLUSION: PLD patients often exhibit cushingoid features, limiting the specificity of simplified clinical risk scores for CS. Increased awareness of lipodystrophy phenotypes and their distinguishing features is essential to reduce misdiagnosis.

articles.title: Change in bone mineral density after parathyroidectomy for secondary hyperparathyroidism: a review.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a common complication of chronic kidney disease that accelerates bone loss and increases fracture risk. While parathyroidectomy (PTx) is the definitive treatment for medically refractory cases, its impact on bone mineral density (BMD) has not been comprehensively evaluated.

EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus was conducted from inception through January 2026. Studies were included if they reported dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-measured BMD before and after PTx in adults with secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic kidney disease. Two reviewers independently screened and selected studies using the Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcomes, Study Design framework, and additional articles were identified through reference searching.

EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS: Across 11 studies encompassing 452 patients with paired measurements, all demonstrated significant improvement in BMD following a site-specific hierarchy favoring cancellous bone. The lumbar spine (+7-50% g/cm2) and femoral neck (+8-23% g/cm2) showed the most consistent gains, while the distal radius showed minimal change. Higher preoperative parathyroid hormone levels, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and lower baseline BMD were associated with greater skeletal recovery. The only available randomized trial confirmed the superiority of PTx over cinacalcet for bone density improvement.

CONCLUSION: PTx consistently improves BMD in patients with refractory secondary hyperparathyroidism, with the greatest gains at cancellous-rich skeletal sites. Clinicians should consider the skeletal benefits of PTx when counseling patients with medically refractory disease, particularly those with low baseline bone density and markedly elevated parathyroid hormone levels.

articles.title: Low-renin hypertension: a distinct phenotype enabling mechanism-based treatment.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Low-renin hypertension is increasingly recognized as a common and clinically important form of hypertension. Expanded screening for primary aldosteronism has revealed many individuals with suppressed renin who do not meet the diagnostic criteria for aldosterone excess, yet exhibit features consistent with sodium retention or increased mineralocorticoid receptor activity. This review synthesizes evidence from targeted literature searches on the epidemiology, mechanisms, diagnostic challenges, and treatment of low-renin hypertension. Early studies proposed renin, in the presence of hypertension, as a marker of excess sodium retention and volume expansion, suggesting that renin could guide individualized therapy. Adoption of a renin-guided treatment approach was historically limited by assay variability and concerns regarding adverse effects from high-dose mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists. However, improvements in renin assay performance, increased accessibility and use of renin testing, and the availability of lower-dose and better-tolerated mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists have renewed interest in this strategy. Low-renin hypertension encompasses primary aldosteronism, conditions that mimic mineralocorticoid excess, and disorders of renal tubular sodium transport. Across this spectrum, patients respond more favorably to therapies targeting sodium retention: mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, epithelial sodium channel inhibitors, or thiazide diuretics, than to agents directed primarily at vasoconstriction. Recognition of low-renin hypertension as a distinct phenotype enables mechanism-based therapy and may improve blood pressure control, reduce medication burden, and mitigate long-term cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: Delgocitinib cream formulation demonstrates a dose-dependent response in adults with mild to severe atopic dermatitis: results from an 8-week randomized phase IIb trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delgocitinib is a topical, pan-Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. Use of delgocitinib ointment 0.5% has shown efficacy in treatment of atopic dermatitis (AD).

OBJECTIVES: To investigate the dose-response relationship, efficacy and safety of delgocitinib cream in adults with mild to severe AD.

METHODS: In this phase IIb trial (NCT03725722), adults with mild to severe AD were randomized 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 to delgocitinib cream 1, 3, 8 or 20 mg g-1 or cream vehicle applied twice daily for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was change from baseline to week 8 in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score. Secondary endpoints included Validated Investigator's Global Assessment for AD treatment success (vIGA-AD TS) and achievement of EASI 75 (≥ 75% improvement in EASI from baseline).

RESULTS: Overall, 251 patients were randomized (delgocitinib cream groups, n = 201; cream vehicle group, n = 50). At week 8, treatment with delgocitinib cream resulted in dose-dependent changes in EASI from baseline vs. cream vehicle (-5.0 for 1 mg g-1, -4.9 for 3 mg g-1, -5.8 for 8 mg g-1 and -7.6 for 20 mg g-1 vs. -1.9 for cream vehicle; all delgocitinib cream groups P < 0.05). A greater proportion of patients treated with delgocitinib achieved vIGA-AD TS [18% (n = 9/49) for 1 mg g-1, 29% (n = 14/48) for 3 mg g-1, 30% (n = 15/50) for 8 mg g-1 and 48% (n = 24/50) for 20 mg g-1] than those using cream vehicle (10%, n = 5/48) at week 8. EASI 75 was achieved by 41% of patients (n = 20/49) in the 1 mg g-1 group, 44% (n = 21/48) in the 3 mg g-1 group, 56% (n = 28/50) in the 8 mg g-1 group, 66% (n = 33/50) in the 20 mg g-1 group and 21% (n = 10/48) in the cream vehicle group at week 8. Incidence of adverse events was similar with delgocitinib cream (44.5%, n = 89/200) and cream vehicle (56%, n = 28/50).

CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with delgocitinib cream was more effective than cream vehicle in a dose-response manner. Delgocitinib cream was well tolerated and no safety concerns were identified.

articles.title: A national epidemiological study of inherited ichthyoses in England from 1998 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ichthyoses (epidermal differentiation disorders) cause significant morbidity and mortality; however, national epidemiological data that link diagnoses of ichthyoses with systemic comorbidities are lacking.

OBJECTIVES: To report epidemiological data on inherited ichthyoses in England, together with patient-level comorbidities and genetic testing status.

METHODS: This national retrospective cohort study identified ichthyosis case records from healthcare databases in England, using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes from 1998 to 2024. Cohort demographics, comorbidities, genetic testing data and mortality data were extracted from routinely collected National Health Service data.

RESULTS: We identified 4330 patients with ichthyosis, of whom 3758 were categorized as having a rare ichthyosis. The prevalence of rare ichthyoses was 51.6 per million (95% confidence interval 49.7-53.5). Compared with the reference population, the overall cohort was younger [median age 22 (interquartile range 11-49) vs. 41 years], more likely to identify as Asian (17.1% vs. 9.6%; P < 0.001) and were more frequently in the most deprived quintiles (48.1% vs. 40.0%; P < 0.001). The rates of comorbidities, including asthma, inflammatory arthropathies and atrial fibrillation, were higher than in the reference population. Nineteen per cent of deaths occurred before the age of 25 years compared with 1% of deaths at this age threshold in the reference population (P < 0.001). Genetic testing data revealed a low proportion of tested cases; pathogenic variants in genes known to cause ichthyosis were found in 56.3% of the tested cases (n = 90/160).

CONCLUSIONS: We report an increased range of comorbidities in patients living with rare ichthyoses, highlighting the systemic burden in patients categorized as having nonsyndromic ichthyosis. These data inform healthcare planning, research design and the redressing of inequities of care. An author video to accompany this article is available online.

articles.title: Racial/ethnic inequities in diabetes mellitus: a narrative review.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract: Inequities in diabetes diagnosis, management, and outcomes are deeply rooted in social determinants of health and structural racism. Historical policies such as redlining and concentrated poverty in low-income neighborhoods have shaped environments characterized by limited access to healthy food and proper healthcare, which ultimately led to a disproportionate burden of diabetes in these populations. The consequences of these disparities for racial and ethnic minoritized groups include a lower ability to achieve glycemic targets, receive novel glucose-lowering agents, and/or have access to diabetes technology. The downstream effect is that this population experiences worse health outcomes from complications (ie, amputation, blindness, end-stage renal disease) and mortality. This narrative review synthesizes current literature on racial/ethnic inequities in diabetes care, highlighting differences in screening, glycemic control, complication rates, and mortality in people living with diabetes from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds, but also identifies opportunities for intervention to ensure equitable access to evidence-based care.

articles.title: Consensus on biomarker utility for ACTH-dependent Cushing syndrome: a Pituitary Society Modified Delphi Panel.
authors: Pituitary Society International Cushing Syndrome Delphi Panel Consensus Group
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Biochemical test results are central to clinical decision-making for the diagnosis and management of Cushing syndrome (CS). With emerging research and increasing availability of different tests, updated consensus on the utility of these biomarkers is warranted.

OBJECTIVE: To establish an updated consensus on the role of biomarkers in the diagnosis and monitoring of adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent CS, address novel therapeutic approaches, and identify areas for future research.

DESIGN: A modified 2-round Delphi panel was conducted. Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement/disagreement for Likert-scale statements or ≥70% selection of the same option for single-choice questions.

SETTING: Participants represented a range of international expertise.

PARTICIPANTS: Forty-one participants took part in the Delphi panel, with no attrition between rounds (one nonclinician was not required to complete the second round). An 8-member Steering Committee guided statement development.

RESULTS: Of statements designed to reach consensus, 45% (14/31) and 44% (11/25) statements reached consensus in Rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Notably, most panelists reported the use of late-night salivary cortisol for diagnosis of mild CS and for monitoring following pituitary surgery or medical or radiation therapy. Most panelists responded that block-and-replace therapies can be considered in patients with cyclical or severe CS, and consensus was reached that restoration of circadian rhythm is a treatment goal for patients with CS.

CONCLUSION: Areas of alignment among experts on the diagnosis and monitoring of CS are presented. The findings from this study are intended to support clinicians in their clinical decision-making and highlight priority areas for future research.

articles.title: Proteomic signatures of loss of glycemic control in youth-onset type 2 diabetes in the TODAY study.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Youth-onset type 2 diabetes (T2D) is characterized by accelerated β-cell decline and early treatment failure, and there is an urgent need to improve the understanding of molecular drivers of loss of glycemic control (LOGC).

OBJECTIVE: To identify multiprotein signatures associated with LOGC in youth-onset T2D.

DESIGN: Longitudinal observational study with a mean follow-up of 10.8 ± 3.8 years using data from the Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth (TODAY) study, with external validation in 3 youth cohorts and 1 adult-onset T2D cohort.

SETTING: Multicenter clinical research study.

PARTICIPANTS: Participants from the TODAY study (N = 374; age 14 ± 2 years; 37% male), of whom 72% experienced LOGC over 10.8 ± 3.8 years.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Loss of glycemic control, defined as hemoglobin A1c ≥8% for ≥6 months or inability to discontinue insulin after acute metabolic decompensation.

RESULTS: Plasma proteomics quantified 7604 aptamers representing 6596 proteins using the SomaScan 7K platform. Sixty-seven proteins were associated with LOGC after false discovery rate correction and multivariable adjustment. Key proteins included plexin-B2 (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.46 [95% CI: 1.29-1.66]) and semaphorin-6A (HR: 1.31 [1.18-1.47]), which were also associated with glycemic outcomes in independent youth and adult cohorts. Enrichment analyses implicated pathways related to axon guidance, immune response, inflammation, and metabolism.

CONCLUSION: Novel proteins involved in axon guidance, immune response, inflammation, and metabolism were associated with LOGC in youth-onset T2D with proteins demonstrating consistent associations across the lifespan and proteomic platforms.

articles.title: Children's neurodevelopment at school age after hysterosalpingography with iodinated contrast: a cohort study.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Hysterosalpingography (HSG) with iodinated contrast used during fertility work-up can transiently disrupt thyroid function during early neurodevelopment due to the Wolff-Chaikoff effect. We examined neurodevelopmental outcomes in school-aged children conceived after HSG.

METHODS: Sixty-nine children conceived within <6 months after HSG with oil-based (iodine content: 480 mg/mL) or water-based contrast (iodine content: 250 mg/mL) within the H2Oil randomized clinical trial (NCT05168228) were compared with children of similar age, sex, and parental education conceived without fertility treatments (n = 44) (NTR9574). Primary outcomes were intelligence quotient, behavior, and academic performance. Secondary outcomes were neurocognitive domain scores. We used linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and parental education, applying false discovery rate correction. We examined timing subgroups (<4, 4-12, >12 weeks post-HSG) vs the control group using polynomial contrasts.

RESULTS: Children conceived within 6 months after HSG had lower mean IQ (104.3 vs 113.1; adjusted estimate: -6.81; 95% CI -10.97 to -2.65; P = .02) and lower information processing and attention control scores (-0.52 SD; 95% CI -0.84 to -0.19; P = .02). Intelligence quotient scores were lowest when conception occurred shortly after HSG, while children conceived >12 weeks after HSG did not differ from the control group. No differences were observed for behavior or academic performance. Sensitivity analyses did not support confounding by prematurity, low birth weight, maternal smoking during pregnancy, or conception using assisted reproductive technologies.

CONCLUSION: Replication in larger, adequately powered cohorts is needed to assess the potential long-term implications of HSG with iodinated contrast for neurodevelopmental outcomes of the offspring.

articles.title: Pathophysiology-based classification of male infertility: evidence from an 800-patient prospective cohort.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Male factor infertility (MFI) is frequently labeled idiopathic when evaluation relies primarily on semen analysis, potentially overlooking endocrine and pathophysiological mechanisms relevant for targeted management.

OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to phenotypically define MFI and develop a pathophysiology-based classification aimed at reducing idiopathic infertility following comprehensive evaluation.

DESIGN AND SETTING: This was a prospective monocentric cohort study conducted at a tertiary referral academic center.

PATIENTS: A total of 800 partners of infertile couples were evaluated between October 2024 and January 2026 after exclusion of isolated female factor infertility.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Prevalence of MFI categories, hormonal patterns across phenotypes, and proportion of idiopathic infertility after comprehensive work-up.

METHODS: All patients underwent standardized clinical evaluation, hormonal assessment (total testosterone, follicle-stimulating hormone [FSH], luteinizing hormone), testicular ultrasound, and complete semen analysis. Microbiological testing, transrectal ultrasound, and genetic analyses were performed according to guidelines.
