RESULTS: Primary spermatogenic failure was the most prevalent category (56.0%), followed by infection/inflammation (22.4%) and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (8.5%). Idiopathic infertility was identified in only 5.3% of cases. Distinct endocrine profiles were observed, with high-FSH spermatogenic failure representing the dominant phenotype.

CONCLUSION: Comprehensive phenotyping markedly reduces the proportion of patients classified as having idiopathic infertility and identifies clinically relevant subgroups. This prospective study provides validation of a pathophysiology-based classification and supports a shift toward endocrine-integrated diagnostic strategies in male infertility, with potential implications for targeted management.

articles.title: Genetic and clinical factors associated with metformin plasma concentrations following an acute metformin challenge.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The glycemic response to metformin is highly variable, yet the genetic determinants of metformin pharmacokinetics remain poorly characterized.

OBJECTIVE: In the Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans (SUGAR-MGH), an ancestrally diverse cohort, we evaluated clinical and genetic factors associated with plasma metformin concentrations.

METHODS: Plasma metformin concentrations were measured in 745 participants who completed a standardized acute metformin challenge in SUGAR-MGH.

RESULTS: Higher metformin concentrations were associated with older age (β = 2.5 ng/mL per year, P = .02), lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (β = -3.5 ng/mL per mL/min/1.73 m2, P = 4.5 × 10-4), and lower body mass index (β = -7.3 ng/mL per kg/m2, P = 1.3 × 10-4). African ancestry was associated with lower metformin concentrations compared to European ancestry (β = -72.6 ng/mL, P = .036). A genome-wide association study (GWAS) identified 4 African ancestry-specific genetic variants significantly associated with higher metformin concentrations (P < 5 × 10-8) as well as several suggestive loci near genes implicated in glucose metabolism, including USP36 and DGKB. Top variants associated with metformin concentration were not associated with glycemic response endpoints following the metformin challenge, including fasting glucose at Visit 2, change in HOMA-IR, and change in fasting insulin between visits. Previously reported metformin transporter variants showed no significant associations with metformin concentration.

CONCLUSION: These findings represent the first GWAS of metformin plasma concentrations and provide a novel resource for future studies of metformin pharmacogenetics.

articles.title: Continuous glucose monitoring-derived time in range is associated with changes in arterial stiffness in type 2 diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Current guidelines recommend continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) to complement HbA1c in glycemic assessment. While cross-sectional studies have reported associations between CGM-derived metrics and arterial stiffness in type 2 diabetes (T2D), longitudinal evidence remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the longitudinal associations of CGM metrics, particularly time in range (TIR) and coefficient of variation (CV), with changes in brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV).

METHODS: This exploratory study analyzed data collected over 260 weeks from an ongoing prospective, multicenter, observational cohort. A total of 348 participants with type 2 diabetes and no history of symptomatic cardiovascular disease underwent baPWV measurements at baseline, 104 weeks, and/or 260 weeks. Participants were divided into 2 groups based on the median values of CGM-derived metrics and HbA1c at baseline, and the associations between each baseline value and longitudinal changes in baPWV were evaluated using mixed-effects models for repeated measures, adjusting for conventional atherosclerotic risk factors.

RESULTS: The median change in baPWV from baseline was 60.1 cm/s (95% CI: 34.6-85.6) at 104 weeks and 130.3 cm/s (95% CI: 98.6-162.1) at 260 weeks (P < .001). The change over time in baPWV differed between the higher and lower TIR groups, with a significant interaction between group and time (P = .013) in the multivariable-adjusted model. This interaction remained significant even after further adjustment for HbA1c (P = .013). In contrast, baseline CV, other CGM-derived metrics, and HbA1c were not associated with longitudinal changes in baPWV.

CONCLUSION: TIR was significantly associated with longitudinal changes in arterial stiffness in participants with type 2 diabetes, independent of HbA1c.

articles.title: Association of the primary aldosteronism severity classification with lateralization and treatment outcomes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: The 2025 clinical guideline for primary aldosteronism (PA) recommends a diagnostic and therapeutic pathway stratified by lateralization risk. The PA severity classification (PASC) integrates biochemical and clinical features and is intended to inform graded recommendations for adrenal venous sampling (AVS).

OBJECTIVE: We examined whether PASC is associated with AVS-defined lateralization and treatment outcomes.

DESIGN: A retrospective multicenter cohort study.

SETTING: Eight tertiary centers.

PATIENTS: A total of 833 patients with PA who underwent AVS. PASC severity was classified as mild, moderate, or severe.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: We evaluated associations between severity, AVS-defined lateralization, and outcomes using the Primary Aldosteronism Surgical Outcome (PASO) and Primary Aldosteronism Medical Treatment Outcome (PAMO) criteria.

RESULTS: Among 833 patients, 52 (6.1%), 563 (67.6%) and 218 (26.2%) had mild, moderate, and severe PA, respectively. Higher severity was associated with a stepwise increase in AVS-defined lateralizing PA (19.2%, 48.0%, and 76.1%, respectively; P < .001). In unilateral PA treated surgically, PASO clinical outcomes differed by severity (P = .002), with complete clinical success in 40.2% (moderate) and 31.3% (severe), and a marked increase in partial clinical success in severe disease (55.1%). PASO biochemical outcomes were similar across severity groups (P = .389). In bilateral PA treated medically, PAMO clinical outcomes varied by severity (P = .005), with complete clinical response decreasing from mild to severe disease (36.8%, 27.0%, and 8.8%), whereas biochemical outcomes were comparable (P = .993).

CONCLUSION: PASC-defined severity correlated with AVS-defined lateralization. Greater severity was associated with lower rates of complete clinical success/response despite preserved biochemical outcomes, supporting a severity-informed framework to complement AVS in PA management.

articles.title: Open-label 9-year follow-up extension phase 2 study of once-weekly somatrogon in children with growth hormone deficiency.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Growth hormone deficiency (GHD) can lead to significant growth and developmental issues, necessitating long-term treatment. Once-weekly somatrogon is a long-acting recombinant human growth hormone analog, approved for treatment of children with GHD.

OBJECTIVE: Assess the long-term safety and efficacy of somatrogon in children with GHD.

DESIGN: Open-label extension (OLE) study following an initial 12-month open-label phase 2 study.

SETTING: Conducted at 14 centers across Hungary, Bulgaria, Belarus, Ukraine, Russia, Greece, and the United States.

PATIENTS OR OTHER PARTICIPANTS: Fifty-three children with GHD (67.9% male, mean age 6.0 ± 2.1 years) completed the phase 2 study and 48 entered the OLE.

INTERVENTION(S): Participants received once-weekly somatrogon for up to 9 years.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Safety endpoints included adverse events (AEs), antidrug antibodies (ADAs), local site injection reactions, and insulin-like growth factor-I SDS. Efficacy endpoints included annual height velocity (HV), change in height SDS, and annual bone maturation.

RESULTS: Treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs) incidence was 52.1% at OLE year (Y) 1, decreasing to 23.8% by Y9. Serious AEs were rare with only isolated cases reported. ADA positivity was observed, but no neutralizing antibodies were found. No correlation between ADA presence and TEAE incidence or severity was noted, nor was there a difference in growth based on ADA presence. Mean annualized HV remained >5 cm/year, and mean height SDS improved from -4.0 at baseline to -0.2 by Y8. No changes in the ratio of bone age/chronological age were observed.

CONCLUSION: Once-weekly somatrogon is a well-tolerated and viable long-term treatment for GHD in children. More real-world data are needed.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of once-daily oral paltusotine in acromegaly: ACROBAT Advance open-label extension up to 4 years.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Paltusotine is the first nonpeptide selective somatostatin 2 receptor agonist approved as once-daily oral treatment for acromegaly.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate long-term treatment with paltusotine in patients with acromegaly previously on an injected somatostatin receptor ligand (SRL)-based regimen.

METHODS: ACROBAT Advance is an ongoing open-label extension (OLE) study. Interim results (up to year 4) are reported. Enrolled patients had completed a phase 2 parent study: ACROBAT Edge (baseline insulin-like growth factor I [IGF-I] >1× upper limit of normal [ULN] on injected octreotide or lanreotide ± cabergoline, or baseline IGF-I ≤1×ULN with combination therapy or pasireotide) or ACROBAT Evolve (baseline IGF-I ≤1×ULN on injected SRL monotherapy). Maximum paltusotine dose was initially 40 mg, then 60 mg, when a tablet formulation became available in year 3. Adjunctive treatment with cabergoline or pegvisomant was allowed as clinically indicated.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients (88% of eligible patients from ACROBAT Edge and Evolve) enrolled in the OLE. Median (interquartile range) IGF-I levels were: 1.15×ULN (0.84, 1.46) at parent study baseline (n = 43), 1.17×ULN (0.98, 1.54) at Advance week 3 (n = 43), and 1.01×ULN (0.83, 1.13) at Advance week 207 (n = 20). Growth hormone levels, acromegaly symptoms, and pituitary tumor size remained stable. Paltusotine was well tolerated, with no unexpected safety findings observed. As of this analysis, 8 (18.6%) patients had discontinued from the study, including 2 (4.7%) due to adverse events.

CONCLUSION: Once-daily oral paltusotine treatment was well tolerated and resulted in long-term disease control, including biochemical, symptom, and pituitary tumor stability, for up to 4 years.

articles.title: Reversible mitochondrial iron toxicity in Wolfram syndrome type 2 monogenic diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Wolfram syndrome type 2 (WS2) is a rare monogenic diabetes syndrome caused by CISD2 mutations. Its cellular pathophysiology remains poorly understood, and no targeted therapies exist.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize the clinical phenotype and cellular pathophysiology of the largest WS2 cohort to date, and to evaluate a novel, mechanistically targeted pharmacological intervention.

DESIGN: Observational cohort study paired with ex vivo functional cellular assays and a proof-of-concept pilot clinical intervention.

SETTING: Multicenter academic and clinical institutions in Israel and the Palestinian territories.

PATIENTS: Twenty-two patients from 11 unrelated Palestinian families presenting with atypical juvenile-onset diabetes and gastrointestinal bleeding. Patient-derived fibroblasts (n = 4) were utilized for functional assays.

INTERVENTION(S): Fibroblasts and 2 patients were treated with a combination of the iron chelator deferiprone (DFP) and the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE(S): Clinical phenotype, CISD2 genetic analysis, mitochondrial labile iron (mLI) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, organelle morphology, and preliminary clinical response (HbA1c, platelet aggregation).

RESULTS: Patients were homozygous for a CISD2 c.109G>C founder mutation (carrier rate 1:40). The clinical phenotype was expanded to include prevalent psychiatric morbidity and congenital heart defects. Patient fibroblasts exhibited profound mitochondrial and endoplasmic reticulum damage, with increased mLI (+25%, P < .0001) and mROS (+28%, P < .0001). In vitro DFP-NAC treatment fully reversed these cellular anomalies. In a preliminary pilot study, 2 patients receiving DFP-NAC demonstrated improved reported glycemic control and corrected platelet aggregation.

CONCLUSION: WS2 is an underdiagnosed monogenic diabetes driven by mitochondrial iron dysregulation and oxidative stress. Repurposing DFP-NAC reverses this toxicity, offering a strong mechanistic rationale for future clinical trials.

articles.title: Alcohol and steatotic liver disease exhibit divergent associations with high plasma small dense LDL-C concentration.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Within the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)/MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD)/alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) framework, cardiovascular risk varies by alcohol exposure. As small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (sdLDL-C) is highly atherogenic, this study assessed the relative effects of steatotic liver disease (SLD) and alcohol consumption on sdLDL-C elevation and the effects of conventional fasting lipids (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol [LDL-C]/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol [HDL-C]/triglycerides [TGs]) on these associations.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 55 745 participants who underwent health screenings in Niigata, Japan between April 2024 and March 2025. Alcohol consumption was self-reported as low, moderate, or excessive. Participants were grouped by SLD status and alcohol consumption. sdLDL-C was directly measured, with high sdLDL-C defined as ≥35 mg/dL. Multivariable linear regression (sdLDL-C) and logistic regression (high sdLDL-C) analyses used 2 models: model 1 was adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking, lipid-lowering medication, antihypertensive medication, and diabetes, and model 2 was further adjusted for LDL-C, HDL-C, and TGs. Marginal standardized prevalence and standardized prevalence differences (PDs) were estimated using g-computation with 2000 bootstrap iterations.

RESULTS: The crude prevalence of high sdLDL-C was influenced by SLD and alcohol consumption, being highest in the SLD(+)/excessive alcohol consumption group (76.4%). In model 2, SLD-related associations were attenuated, as reflected by markedly reduced PDs between SLD(+) and SLD(-) within each alcohol category, whereas alcohol-related associations remained robust.

CONCLUSION: Alcohol exposure contributes to an atherogenic sdLDL-C phenotype beyond conventional fasting lipids within contemporary SLD categories, indicating potential relevance for risk profiling in MetALD/ALD.

articles.title: Incisional Infiltration of Liposomal Bupivacaine in Geriatric Hip Fracture Surgery: A Randomized Parallel-Group Trial.
articles.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture volumes are rising with population aging, and inadequate analgesia following hip fracture surgery has been shown to impede early mobilization and recovery. Liposomal bupivacaine (LB) may extend analgesia, but previous orthopaedic trials have yielded mixed results. We therefore tested whether adding local incisional infiltration of LB to multimodal analgesia confers clinically relevant advantages in geriatric hip fracture surgery.

METHODS: This study was a single-center, prospective, randomized, participant and assessor-blinded, parallel-group exploratory trial in older adults undergoing hemiarthroplasty or total hip arthroplasty for a hip fracture. The intervention was local LB infiltration; the control was no local infiltration. The primary end point was resting pain measured on a visual analog scale (VAS, 0 to 10) at 48 hours postoperatively. Prespecified key secondary end points included early pain with activity, morphine milligram equivalents (MME) of the patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) infusion volume and of the total perioperative oral and intramuscular rescue counts, sleep quality measured on a numerical rating scale (NRS, 0 to 10), total sleep time, and nocturnal awakenings.

RESULTS: A total of 76 patients (median age, 77 years; 49 female) were included in the analysis. The primary end point did not differ between the groups (median 0 for both; p = 0.143; point estimate of between-group difference: Cohen d = -0.506, 95% confidence interval: -0.962, -0.048), whereas several secondary outcomes significantly favored LB, including resting pain at 24 hours; activity pain at 8, 24, and 48 hours; and oral rescue administrations (median and interquartile range: 25 [0, 50] versus 50 [25, 100] MME). The LB group had a higher NRS sleep quality score after surgery, with a longer total sleep duration on the operative night, than the control group; the number of awakenings was similar between the groups. Ambulation at 48 and 72 hours and the number of postoperative days to discharge did not differ between the groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In the context of a standardized multimodal analgesic pathway, local incisional infiltration of LB did not improve the prespecified primary end point of resting pain at 48 hours after geriatric hip fracture surgery. Overall, the current evidence does not support routine clinical use, and further investigation is warranted.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I . See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

articles.title: Clinical Evaluation of Two Different Healing Protocols for the Single Implant-Retained Mandibular Overdenture: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To record implant stability and marginal bone height (MBH) changes for submerged and nonsubmerged protocols for the single implant-retained mandibular overdenture (SIMRO).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A single symphyseal implant was placed in a completely edentulous mandible. At implant placement, the implant stability quotient (ISQ) was recorded using the Osstell device. Using sealed envelopes, patients were randomized into nonsubmerged (NS) and submerged (S) groups. After 3 months, implant stability for both groups was recorded using an Osstell device (ISQ). The Periotest device was used to follow up implant stability (PTV), and MBH changes were recorded at pickup and after 12 months. Comparison of ISQ within groups was done using paired t test. Mann-Whitney U test for two independent groups was used to compare MBH changes and PTV. P < .05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: A significant decrease in the ISQ values for both groups was observed, and the NS group showed a statistically significant higher ISQ value (74.89 ± 3.473) than the S group (71.53 ± 6.122; P = .017) after 3 months. MBH changes and PTV did not show any significant difference but were in favor of the NS protocol.

CONCLUSIONS: Both healing protocols showed physiologically acceptable implant stability and MBH changes after 12 months. The NS protocol improved stability with minimum MBH changes for SIMROs.

articles.title: Esthetic Outcomes of the One Crown One Time Concept Compared to Conventional Soft Tissue Conditioning in Single Implant- Supported Restorations: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effect of the one crown one time (OCOT) protocol compared to soft tissue conditioning involving multiple abutment disconnections on the esthetic outcomes of single implant- supported restorations in healed implant sites.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In total, 29 patients over the age of 25 years, each receiving a single implant in the anterior or premolar region, participated in this study. Half of the submerged implants were restored immediately after uncovering using a final screw-retained zirconia crown, luted to a titanium base. The remaining submerged implants initially received a healing abutment, followed by a soft tissue conditioning phase with provisional restorations prior to delivery of the definitive crowns. All patients were followed for 12 months. Esthetic outcomes were assessed using Pink Esthetic Score (PES), analysis of peri-implant soft tissue volumetric alterations, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).

RESULTS: The control group (CG) and OCOT group exhibited mean PES of 8.9 ± 2.6 and 10.5 ± 1.6, respectively, at baseline (P > .05) and 10.8 ± 2.2 and 11.1 ± 1.2 at 1-year follow-up (P > .05). Regarding volumetric soft tissue alterations, the CG presented a higher root mean square (RMS) discrepancy (median: 336) compared to the OCOT group (median: 192 μm; P < .05). The CG exhibited a median linear gain of 329 μm, while the test group showed a slight median reduction of -19 μm. PROMs remained consistently high in both groups over time, with no statistically significant differences in median values at baseline (P > .05) or at 1-year follow-up (P > .05).

CONCLUSIONS: When appropriate surgical and prosthetic protocols are followed, omission of the provisional phase does not compromise the short-term esthetic outcomes of single-implant restorations, rendering the OCOT concept a viable treatment alternative.

articles.title: Incidence of Caries and Periodontal Disease in Abutment vs Nonabutment Teeth Among Removable Partial Dental Prosthesis Wearers: A Systematic Review Using Synthesis Without Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the incidence of caries and periodontal parameters of disease activity in abutment vs nonabutment teeth in removable partial dental prosthesis (RPDP) wearers.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two reviewers independently searched five electronic databases (PubMed, EBSCO-CINAHL Complete, EBSCODentistry and Oral Sciences, Wiley Cochrane Library, and Scopus) to retrieve studies published until September 9, 2023, and selected randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and longitudinal studies (LSs) reporting at least 3 months of recall post-delivery. Frequency of new and recurrent caries, periodontal probing depth (PPD) in millimeters, and sites with bleeding on probing (BoP) were recorded.

RESULTS: Among the 11,260 records identified, 21 reports from 20 studies (2 RCTs and 18 LSs) were included. Of these, 4 reports described PPD with BoP, 16 reported caries incidence, and 1 reported both. Synthesis without meta-analysis guidelines were followed for data analysis. Relatively stable periodontal health with 3-month to 10-year follow-up was observed. Caries incidence ranged from 11.9% to 46.96% over 2 to 5 years, and 6 of the 8 reports showed higher caries incidence in abutments than in controls. Cochrane risk of bias (RoB-2.0) assessment indicated high risk in one RCT and moderate risk in another. Four LSs were rated 'good' per the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale with Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality standards. Certainty of evidence was evaluated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).

CONCLUSIONS: Increased BoP at recalls of 3 months to 7 years was observed. Weak evidence supported stable PPD in RPDP patients. Increased caries risk in abutments compared to nonabutments suggested a need for regular follow-ups.

articles.title: Congenital Heart Disease Diagnosis Using Minimax Guided Context Attention (MG-CAT) Transformer Framework.
articles.abstract: Background: Congenital heart disease is a major cause of mortality in small babies and children, where early diagnosis is very important for proper treatment and improving clinical outcomes. Unfortunately, conventional auscultation-based diagnosis methods mostly rely on expert interpretation that limits their scalability in very far and mountain regions having comparatively low-resource environments. To address these major problems, we propose a deep learning-based method with a spectral minimax-guided context attention transformer framework. Methods: The input signal to the framework is phonocardiogram signals. The proposed framework leverages the optimal use of spectral representation of heart sounds to capture time-frequency features and introduces a novel minimax transformation block designed for cardiac sound mapping analysis. The minimax attention block enhances spectral discrimination by mapping features to a relatively high-dimensional space to improve stratification, thereby compressing them to reduce sensitivity to repetition and noise. Additionally, we employ a cosine-oriented contextual attention module to improve feature representation, adaptively adjusting spatial and temporal features. This approach allows the proposed framework to highlight important acoustic differences and more effectively understand interlayer variations in heart sound patterns. The design also incorporates window-based focus and hierarchical feature clustering to efficiently represent local and global correlations. Results: We conducted experiments on the heart sound dataset known as the ZCHSound. We found that the proposed framework outperforms the basic methods on many assessment metrics. Conclusion: Although some challenges remain in multi-class classification with unbalanced datasets, the results demonstrate the potential of simple spectral learning and cosine-oriented attention to improve the automated diagnosis of congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Aortic Sclerosis and Aortic Stenosis: Two Entities or a Continuum?
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic valve sclerosis (ASc) and aortic stenosis (AS) are traditionally regarded as distinct entities with different clinical prognosis, yet their classification relies on arbitrary echocardiographic measurements. Whether these conditions represent separate diseases or a single disease continuum remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the progression and mortality in patients with early aortic valve disease based on the relationship between transvalvular peak velocity (Vmax), clinical outcomes, and aortic valve replacement (AVR).

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 181,167 adults with morphologically abnormal aortic valves and a Vmax of 1.0 to 3.9 m/s on transthoracic echocardiography between 2010 and 2022. Patients with severe AS, significant aortic regurgitation, or AVR within 6 months were excluded. Outcomes included AVR, all-cause mortality, and their composite. Cox proportional hazards models and penalized smoothing spline analyses were used to assess associations between Vmax and outcomes, adjusting for demographics, valve morphology, and comorbidities.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 3.2 years, 4,112 patients underwent AVR and 61,654 died. The risk of AVR increased gradually across the entire Vmax range, particularly beyond 3 years, without an identifiable threshold separating ASc from AS. The cumulative incidence of AVR at 5 years increased progressively from 0.1% at 1.0 to 1.4 m/s to 31.2% at 3.0 to 3.9 m/s (P < 0.001). The association between Vmax and outcomes, including mortality, persisted after multivariable adjustment and across multiple sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: Transvalvular velocity associated with AVR across Vmax 1.0 to 3.9 m/s gradually increase without a clear threshold, consistent with a disease continuum between ASc and AS.

articles.title: Echocardiographic Ventricular Strain Imaging Reflects Alterations in Myocardial Mechanics During and After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease
articles.abstract: Assessment of ventricular function during and post cardiac surgery remains challenging, as conventional echocardiographic indices may not adequately capture subtle and dynamic changes in myocardial performance. Speckle-tracking echocardiography, particularly left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LV GLS) and right ventricular longitudinal strain, provides a more sensitive assessment of myocardial deformation and has increasingly been applied in the perioperative setting. Available studies indicate that LV GLS may deteriorate following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) and cardiac surgical intervention despite relatively preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, highlighting the ability of deformation imaging to detect myocardial dysfunction that may remain undetected by conventional parameters. Right ventricular longitudinal mechanics may also undergo substantial perioperative alterations, reflecting the particular susceptibility of the right ventricle to changes in loading conditions, pulmonary vascular resistance, and ventricular interdependence. Importantly, perioperative strain measurements should be interpreted in the context of the cardiovascular effects of general anesthesia and mechanical ventilation, that may alter preload, afterload, and myocardial contractility. The potential influence of anesthetic technique and depth on myocardial deformation represents an emerging research question requiring further investigation. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on alterations in left and right ventricular strain and cardiac mechanics in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, with particular emphasis on perioperative changes observed in CABG and valve surgery and on the effects of general anesthesia and mechanical ventilation. By integrating findings across these perioperative stages, it aims to highlight the pathophysiological and procedural factors that should be considered when interpreting myocardial deformation, including anesthesia, altered loading conditions, CPB, and the surgical intervention itself.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Inferior Vena Cava Reconstruction for Malignancy: Outcomes of 53 Consecutive Patients and Retrospective Concordance with the 2025 Delphi Consensus.
articles.abstract: Tumours involving the inferior vena cava are rare and require complex oncovascular surgery, for which standardised recommendations have only recently been proposed. This study evaluated perioperative, oncological, and vascular outcomes of inferior vena cava resection and reconstruction in a contemporary multidisciplinary cohort and assessed its retrospective concordance with the 2025 Delphi Consensus. We retrospectively reviewed 53 consecutive patients undergoing surgery for malignant tumours involving the inferior vena cava at a tertiary referral centre between February 2009 and April 2022. Clinical, operative, postoperative, oncological, and vascular outcomes were collected from a prospectively maintained database. Vena cava reconstruction was performed in 48 patients (91%), predominantly using ringed polytetrafluoroethylene interposition grafts. Complete (R0) tumour resection was achieved in 72% of patients. R0 resection was associated with significantly better 5-year overall survival (59.0% vs. 24.0%, p = 0.006) and recurrence-free survival (57.2% vs. 15.6%, p = 0.008) compared with R1 resection. In-hospital and 90-day mortality were 3.7% and 7.5%, respectively, while 21% required urgent reintervention during the index hospitalisation. At a median follow-up of 45 months, overall survival was 78.2% at 1 year and 48.7% at 5 years. Primary venous patency was 86.0% at 1 and 2 years and 78.4% at 5 years. Surgical management showed high retrospective concordance with the Delphi Consensus recommendations, published after the study period. Inferior vena cava oncovascular resection and reconstruction can be performed with acceptable early mortality and durable venous patency in experienced multidisciplinary centres. These findings support specialised referral and provide real-world data for further standardisation of reconstruction, anticoagulation, and surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Intensive early and sustained lowering of LDL-C and inflammation after index PCI and cardiovascular outcomes.
articles.journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Atherogenic dyslipidemia and inflammation are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, yet the relationship between their target achievement patterns and cardiovascular outcomes remains unclear.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were measured at admission, 2 months, and 1 year after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the composite of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, cardiovascular death, and unplanned revascularization. Four target achievement patterns were defined based on whether LDL-C and CRP targets were reached at 2 months and 1 year. The association between LDL-C and CRP levels, target achievement patterns and outcomes were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines. During a median follow-up of 714 days, 505 patients experienced MACE. Early and sustained achievement of LDL-C or CRP targets was individually associated with the lowest risk of MACE compared to those who never achieved the respective targets (HR = 0.600, 95% CI 0.448 - 0.805; HR = 0.688, 95% CI 0.489 - 0.970, respectively). Moreover, the combined effect of achieving early and sustained targets for both LDL-C and CRP was associated with the greatest reduction in MACE risk (HR = 0.539, 95% CI 0.387 - 0.752).

CONCLUSIONS: Early and sustained target achievement patterns of both LDL-C and CRP after index PCI are associated with a significantly lower risk of MACE. These findings support the early initiation and long-term maintenance of combined lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory strategies to optimize outcomes in post-PCI patients.

articles.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
articles.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate binding modes were generated via molecular docking using the experimentally resolved active-state CXCR4 structure (PDB ID: 8K3Z) and then subjected to extensive multireplica molecular dynamics (MD) simulations within a biomimetic lipid bilayer. Consensus analyses integrating solvent-accessible surface area (SASA), dynamic contact profiling, and hydrogen bond occupancy across independent conformational ensembles were used to characterize recurrent features of the proposed interface. The results support a structural model in which TcP21 engages CXCR4 through a continuous interaction region localized within the LYS23-PHE39 segment, whereas CXCR4 presents a hierarchically organized and distributed interface. Within this model, a relatively stable interaction core involving the TM5, TM6, and TM7 domains is predominantly characterized by van der Waals contacts, while a more conformationally adaptable peripheral anchoring region involving the ECL2, TM1, and N-terminal domains contributes additional intermolecular interactions. The recurrence of these features across independent simulations supports their consideration as candidate determinants of TcP21-CXCR4 recognition, although their structural and biological relevance remains to be experimentally established. Overall, the resulting computational model provides atomistic structural hypotheses for TcP21-CXCR4 recognition and a basis for future experimental studies to examine the predicted interface and assess its potential relevance to TcP21-CXCR4-mediated interactions.

articles.title: Management of Sjögren disease: recent advances in systemic treatment.
articles.abstract: Sjögren disease is an autoimmune connective tissue disease predominantly affecting women characterized by dryness of mucosal surfaces, arthralgia with or without arthritis, and fatigue. To date, treatment has been predominantly symptomatic with topical agents for dryness and limited evidence for systemic treatment. Most of the conventional disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs used in rheumatology have shown little or no benefit in Sjögren disease, and the biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs routinely used in other rheumatic diseases have proven disappointing. Recent advances in the understanding of pathogenesis and the development of novel biologic agents may alter the future treatment landscape and allow effective treatment and disease modification to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Clinical and biomarker significance of interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in acute exacerbations and the frequent exacerbator phenotype of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are one of the major causes of morbidity, mortality, and hospitalization; reliable inflammatory biomarkers predicting exacerbation risk and guiding emerging interleukin (IL)-targeted therapies are still undefined. IL-4 and IL-13 are key T-helper 2 cytokines implicated in eosinophilic airway inflammation and remodeling, but their clinical and prognostic relevance in COPD is still controversial. MEDLINE and EMBASE databases were manually searched from inception to December 2025, including observational studies reporting quantitative IL-4 and/or IL-13 levels in adults with COPD and healthy controls, with measurements in serum by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay or V-PLEX immunoassay. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment (Newcastle-Ottawa Scale) were performed independently by three reviewers, following PRISMA recommendations. Of 1147 records screened, 5 cohort studies (total patient number: 1168) met inclusion criteria. Across studies, serum IL-4 was consistently higher in AECOPD than in healthy controls, with IL-13 also frequently elevated during exacerbations. Comparisons between AECOPD and stable COPD yielded non-significant results. Two studies reported higher serum IL-4 in frequent versus infrequent exacerbators, whereas IL-13 was not as significantly high as IL-4. In stable COPD, IL-4 and IL-13 showed only modest, often non-significant increases versus controls. Available evidence suggests that IL-4 and IL-13 are variably upregulated in COPD, with more pronounced elevations during AECOPD and a possible association between higher IL-4 and frequent exacerbations. However, small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and limited longitudinal data can't lead to definitive conclusions, requiring the need for larger, well-designed studies to validate IL-4/IL-13 as prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets in COPD.

articles.title: Favorable follow-up of a patient with severe pulmonary hypertension as a rare complication of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Self-care interventions to reduce, prevent or monitor disability in those affected by leprosy: a systematic review.
articles.journal: International journal for equity in health
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-care is a widely promoted strategy for the prevention and management of disability among people affected by leprosy. However, the content, delivery, and reported outcomes of self-care interventions have not been systematically analysed. This review aimed to identify and describe self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy, assess their outcomes, and map the interventions to the transtheoretical model of behaviour change.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted across PubMEd, Medline ALL, Web of Science Core Collection, EMBASE, LILACS, and SciELO. Studies were eligible if they reported a peer-reviewed self-care intervention for people affected by leprosy, including self-care interventions delivered within broader interventions. Data were extracted and formulated in an extraction table. Study quality was assessed using the relevant Critical Skills Appraisal Programme checklist. Findings were synthesised narratively. PROSPERO (CRD42025649623).

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies were included. The studies were conducted in Brazil, Ethiopia, Nepal, Nigeria, China, India, Mozambique and Indonesia. Interventions included self-care or self-help groups; structured self-care education programmes and prevention of disability programmes; family-based or integrated disability-management interventions; assistive technology or adaptive devices; and tele-health interventions or follow-up. Foot-care was the most consistently reported intervention, and was most often linked to measurable outcomes, including ulcer healing and ulcer prevention. Hand-care and eye-care were more often embedded in larger broad self-care packages and did not report measurable outcomes. Evidence for ulcer impairment and prevention was promising but largely derived from uncontrolled non-randomised trials. Cost evidence for interventions was limited and no randomized control trials for self-care were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: This review shows that self-care interventions for people affected by leprosy may be effective in reducing disability, especially when they combine practical education, repeated follow-up, peer or family support, provisions of materials and devices, and access to wider health services. However, as shown by the review the evidence base remains limited by a lack of control trials and limited economic data. Future studies should use clearer intervention reporting, longer follow-up, and increased sample sizes to provide more evidence for which models are effective, sustainable, and transferable across leprosy endemic settings.

articles.title: Emergency department care experiences of patients with a migration history: a systematic mixed-studies review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Migration is a global phenomenon with significant implications for healthcare systems, requiring emergency departments (EDs) to adapt to increasingly diverse populations. While the ED often serves as the primary access point to the healthcare system for patients with a migration history (PMH), their specific care experiences have remained fragmented across literature.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic mixed-studies review synthesizes research on the care experiences of PMH in the ED in order to identify actionable insights for making ED care more equitable.

METHODS: MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO were systematically searched, complemented by reference screening. Eligible studies reported primary empirical data on adult PMH in general EDs. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Study characteristics were extracted using a piloted form. Findings were synthesized using convergent qualitative synthesis with inductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: 37 studies from high-income countries were included. The findings can be divided into three major themes: (1) patient evaluations of ED care, (2) language as a central barrier, and (3) perceived discrimination, fairness and exclusion. Satisfaction varied and was often lower for PMH in specific domains, while moderate to high overall satisfaction frequently coexisted with unmet needs. These evaluations were shaped by patients' prior experiences and expectations. Language barriers strongly influenced patient understanding, autonomy and participation, with inconsistent and ad-hoc interpreter use contributing to communication gaps. Many PMH reported experiences of discrimination or unfair treatment linked to race, ethnicity, language, or migration status, often embedded in broader structural conditions of healthcare.

CONCLUSION: Language barriers and discrimination are important factors shaping how PMH experience ED care, while satisfaction ratings may not reliably reflect the quality or equity of care. Addressing these inequities requires sustained institutional and policy-level action, including consistent access to professional interpreters, strengthened communication practices, and institutional strategies to prevent discrimination, support patient participation, and embed equity in clinical routines and policies.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42020105332.

articles.title: Safety of home treatment for incidental pulmonary embolism in cancer patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) is increasingly detected in computed tomography (CT) scans for scheduled cancer staging, but the safety of outpatient management in these patients with active cancer remains uncertain, as current guidelines usually do not define patients with pulmonary embolism and cancer as low risk.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival. Events were unscheduled consultations or emergency department presentations, progression of venous thromboembolism, clinically relevant bleeding or death.

RESULTS: Of 212 patients included, 89.2% were managed as outpatients. Patients treated at home were less likely to have bilateral pulmonary embolism, evidence of right ventricular dysfunction, an elevated troponin or hypoxemia. 90-day all-cause mortality was 5.2%, deaths occurred usually while the patient was receiving hospice care. For patients treated at home clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1.6% and progression of thromboembolism in 2.1%.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients diagnosed with iPE, most patients were treated at home. With 90-day mortality likely being mainly caused by the malignancy, home treatment appears safe if cancer is the only risk factor present.

articles.title: Author Correction: Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure.
Heart Failure Beyond Valve Treatment　- Mechanisms, Predictors, and Therapeutic Strategies After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across the spectrum of surgical risk, substantially improving symptoms and clinical outcomes. However, heart failure (HF) remains a major cause of hospitalization and mortality after TAVR, indicating that relief of valvular stenosis alone may not completely eliminate HF risk. HF after TAVR is multifactorial, reflecting residual cardiac damage and incomplete reverse remodeling, concomitant cardiovascular abnormalities, procedure- and prosthesis-related factors, underlying HF substrate, and systemic comorbidities. Importantly, both the baseline extent of cardiac damage and its persistence after TAVR are associated with adverse outcomes, highlighting the importance of serial assessment beyond procedural success. In addition, many patients undergoing TAVR are elderly and have features of HF with preserved ejection fraction, which may contribute to persistent HF despite successful valve intervention. Emerging evidence, including randomized trial data on sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, suggests that targeted pharmacological therapy may reduce residual HF risk after TAVR. In this review we summarize the epidemiology, clinical impact, mechanisms, risk stratification, and management of HF after TAVR, and discuss future strategies for its prevention and treatment.

articles.title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society
articles.abstract: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

articles.title: Epidemiology of Bloodstream Infections and Impact of Antibiotic Prophylaxis: A 10-Year Experience at a Tertiary Care Pediatric Oncology-Hematology Center in Italy.
articles.abstract: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in pediatric oncology-hematology patients. The local epidemiological landscape varies across centers, requiring continuous institutional surveillance. BSI episodes at a tertiary pediatric oncology-hematology center (Bari, Italy) were retrospectively reviewed over 10 years (2014 to 2024), analyzing microbiological spectrum, antimicrobial susceptibility, and the impact of 2 prophylactic policies: amoxicillin-clavulanate prophylaxis (2014 to 2019) versus its discontinuation (2019 to 2024). Among 568 newly diagnosed patients, 208 BSIs were documented in 144 (25.4%), with 93.8% monomicrobial. Gram-positive organisms predominated (61.6%), with coagulase-negative staphylococci as the most frequent isolates. Escherichia coli was the leading Gram-negative pathogen (9.5%). Eight fungal BSIs occurred exclusively in hematologic malignancies, half caused by Candida parapsilosis; 2 were polymicrobial. Peak C-reactive protein independently predicted Gram-negative BSI in multivariable analysis (OR: 1.005; 95% CI: 1.001-1.010; P<0.05), with limited discriminatory performance (AUC: 0.62). Blood culture positivity was significantly higher during prophylaxis (5.75% vs. 3.65%; P<0.001). Multidrug-resistant organisms remained rare (3.8%), with no methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus or vancomycin-resistant enterococci detected. BSI-related mortality was 1.4%, confined to Gram-negative and fungal episodes. Prophylaxis discontinuation was associated with lower positivity rates. An empirical escalation strategy ensured adequate coverage while minimizing antibiotic exposure, supporting its use in this setting.

articles.title: USP14 Gene Expression Combined with Clinical Factors for Predicting Symptomatic Recurrence After Surgery for Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Deep infiltrating endometriosis (DIE) exhibits high postoperative recurrence rates, yet current prediction models lack molecular insights for precise risk stratification. This study aimed to determine whether ubiquitin-specific protease 14 (USP14) mRNA expression in DIE lesions is independently associated with postoperative symptomatic recurrence and to construct a combined clinico-molecular predictive model with enhanced accuracy. A retrospective cohort of 235 surgically treated DIE patients was analyzed. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was applied for variable selection. Subsequently, Cox multivariate regression was performed to identify independent risk factors. Multivariate Cox regression revealed that high USP14 expression (HR = 1.656; 95% CI: 1.307-2.099; P < 0.001), adhesion (HR = 1.861; 95%CI: 1.013-3.419; P = 0.045), bowel lesions (HR = 2.168; 95%CI: 1.278-3.679; P = 0.004), and adenomyosis (HR = 2.645; 95%CI: 1.568-4.462; P < 0.001) were independent risk factors, while GnRH-a therapy ≥ 6 months (HR = 0.126; 95%CI: 0.044-0.363; P < 0.001) and postoperative pregnancy (HR = 0.402; 95%CI: 0.200-0.807; P = 0.010) were independent protectors. The combined model integrating USP14 with these clinical factors achieved a superior C-index of 0.896 (95%CI: 0.879-0.912), outperforming the clinical-only model [C-index: 0.870 (95%CI: 0.849-0.892)]. Bootstrap internal validation (2,000 resamples) yielded optimism-corrected C-indices of 0.888 and 0.863 for the combined and clinical-only models, respectively. The integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) was 0.044 (95% CI: -0.013 to 0.11; P = 0.047); as the bootstrap confidence interval narrowly included zero, this result was interpreted as borderline, while complementary analyses supported the incremental value of USP14 (continuous net reclassification improvement: 0.655, P = 0.026; bootstrap-validated ΔC-index: 0.020, 95% CI: 0.002-0.048, P = 0.033). In conclusion, high USP14 expression is independently associated with postoperative symptomatic recurrence in DIE, and its incorporation into a combined prediction model provides a modest but consistent improvement in prognostic accuracy; as a retrospectively developed, internally validated model, it is hypothesis-generating and requires external, multi-center validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Hydroxycitrate Accelerates Renal Refusion Following Ischemia but Does not Affect the Severity of Acute Kidney Injury in Rats.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: The effects of pretreatment with hydroxycitrate (HC), an inhibitor of ATP citrate lyase, were investigated in a rat model of renal ischemia/reperfusion. A single administration of HC 1 h prior to ischemia modeling significantly accelerated the restoration of renal perfusion, as detected by laser speckle contrast imaging, but did not affect blood concentrations of creatinine and urea, the urinary levels of NGAL and KIM-1, or the renal tissue levels of PCNA and TNFα assessed 1-2 days after ischemia/reperfusion. HC stimulated the proliferation of EA.hy926 endothelial cells in vitro, but produced no direct vasoactive effect on isolated renal interlobar arteries. These findings suggest that HC pretreatment selectively enhances microvascular perfusion recovery in the kidney during the acute phase of reperfusion without affecting the tone of larger arteries or the biochemical markers of acute kidney injury.

articles.title: Expert consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wheezing is a very common symptom in preschool children. Compared with that of older children with wheezing or asthma, the morbidity and health care utilization of preschool are disproportionately high, imposing a heavy economic burden on the health care system and society. Furthermore, severe and frequent wheezing in early life is associated with a trajectory of poor lung function, which is associated with respiratory and non-respiratory health outcomes in later adulthood, including high-risk chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and high-risk cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in middle age. However, recurrent preschool wheezing, which is defined as two or more wheezing episodes in children younger than 6 years, excluding bronchiolitis, is highly heterogeneous in etiology and prognosis and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges for pediatricians.

METHODS: Thirty Chinese experts majoring in pediatric pulmonology and epidemiology were invited to write this practical consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of recurrent wheezing in preschool children on the basis of evidence collection and experience. Elucidation and reviews were conducted using electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and Wanfang databases. We used variations in terms for "wheezing", "asthma", "wheezing bronchitis", "preschool", "children", and "pediatric".

RESULTS: The etiology, evaluation, management of acute wheezing exacerbation, and strategy of long-term anti-inflammatory therapy in recurrent preschool wheezing are highlighted. The most common causes of preschool wheezing are virus-induced wheezing and asthma (typical wheezing), some of which require long-term anti-inflammatory therapy. Some other children had identifiable underlying diseases (atypical wheezing). On the basis of the confirmation of wheezing, the underlying diseases and phenotypes of typical wheezing should be carefully investigated. For acute wheezing, inhaled short-acting β₂-agonists are the first-line agents, and systemic corticosteroids should be reserved only for severe cases. Routine use of azithromycin is not recommended in acute wheezing. The decision to initiate long-term anti-inflammatory therapy for recurrent preschool wheezing should be based on a comprehensive evaluation of clinical risk indicators and treatable traits such as type 2 inflammation. Immunomodulators such as bacterial lysates may be considered for use in trials in preschool children with recurrent virus-induced wheezing.

CONCLUSIONS: This symptom-based, phenotype-oriented consensus provides practical guidance for the individualized management of heterogeneous recurrent wheezing in preschool children. Further studies are needed to identify clinical risk factors and biomarkers for persistent wheezing and asthma. More appropriate long-term treatment regimens should also be explored.

articles.title: Echoes of infection: viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes in long COVID: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10-20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite its substantial global burden, the pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology. Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings. Forty-five reports were included: 16 in stratum A, 23 in stratum B, three autopsy studies, and three isolated case/fetal reports. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay. No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators. The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

articles.title: Comparative Effects of Different Neuromuscular Training Modalities and Doses on Lower-Limb Injury Prevention in Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower-limb injuries are common in athletes. Neuromuscular training (NMT) is widely promoted, but the comparative effectiveness of different modalities and the optimal dose remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Cochrane Library and Embase were searched to 1 August 2025. Eligible trials compared NMT with a control in athletes and reported lower-limb injury outcomes. Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Two reviewers screened, extracted and assessed risk of bias. Prespecified subgroups examined modality and dose (frequency, session duration, intervention length), age, sex and sport. Certainty was rated with GRADE.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven RCTs (27,663 participants) were included. NMT was associated with reduced lower-limb injury risk (RR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.64-0.82), although trim-and-fill adjustment attenuated the estimate. Structured (RR = 0.68, 95% CI 0.56-0.82) and multidimensional programmes (RR = 0.76, 95% CI 0.61-0.93) showed favourable pooled estimates, with no statistically significant between-modality difference. Favourable pooled estimates were also observed in adolescents (RR = 0.67, 95% CI 0.55-0.81) and young adults (RR = 0.70, 95% CI 0.50-0.99), and in football (RR = 0.71) and basketball (RR = 0.66); however, the between-age difference did not remain statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, and no statistically significant differences were detected between sport subgroups. Low-certainty, study-level subgroup analyses yielded favourable pooled estimates for programmes delivered 2-3 times per week, for 16-25 min per session, and over intervention periods of 1.5-12 months; however, these associations did not establish a causal or optimal dose. Certainty was very low overall and low to very low across dosage comparisons.

CONCLUSIONS: NMT may reduce lower-limb injury risk, but the magnitude of benefit remains very uncertain. Structured and multidimensional programmes, together with programmes delivered at moderate frequency and duration, showed favourable pooled estimates in exploratory subgroup analyses; however, the dose-related findings represent study-level associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of a causal or optimal dose. These findings may inform the design of routine training programmes, while future high-quality RCTs should address adherence, long-term sustainability, and dose-response interactions across sports and populations.

articles.title: AI-driven precision anti-infective therapy in critical care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe infections, including sepsis and those caused by multidrug-resistant organisms, remain a persistent and significant global critical care challenge, leading to substantial morbidity, high mortality rates, and immense healthcare resource strain. Effective management is critically dependent on addressing the complex and time-sensitive needs for rapid diagnosis, timely antimicrobial therapy, accurate prediction of pathogenic microorganisms and antimicrobial resistance, and personalized therapeutic adjustment. Traditional methods, which often rely on non-specific scores and delayed results, are frequently insufficient for these dynamic, high-stakes clinical decisions. Artificial Intelligence have thus emerged as highly promising, transformative tools.

METHODS: We searched five databases (PubMed, Embase, Web of science, Cochrane library, and Scopus) from inception to October 2025 for studies involving AI methods applied to patients with severe infections. Eligible study designs included randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, and case series. Data extraction focused on AI models, patient populations, outcomes, and management strategy application across five key clinical domains.

RESULTS: A total of 78 studies met the inclusion criteria. AI models demonstrated significant utility in infection types and sepsis risk assessment, achieving high sensitivity and specificity in early detection. Substantial progress was also identified in the prediction of antimicrobial resistance and the implementation of optimal antimicrobial therapy and timing. Furthermore, AI enhanced the prediction of prognosis and mortality and provided tailored strategies for optimization for special populations. The continuous advancement and development of machine learning models have improved the accuracy of predictions.

CONCLUSION: AI technologies show immense promise across the entire spectrum of severe infection management, from early risk assessment to precision antibiotic dosing and prognosis prediction. While the field is burgeoning with high-performing models, standardized clinical validation and rigorous implementation studies are essential to translate this technological potential into widespread clinical practice and improved patient outcomes.

articles.title: Redox-active copper nanoparticles attenuate colistin-induced nephrotoxicity by restoring Akt/GSK3β/mTOR-TFEB signaling and autophagic homeostasis in HK-2 cells and mice.
articles.abstract: Colistin is an indispensable last-line antibiotic against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, but its use is limited by dose-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI) with proximal tubular damage. Although oxidative stress is implicated, how it translates into tubular injury remains poorly defined, and antioxidant therapy alone shows limited efficacy. We investigated whether ultrasmall copper nanoparticles (Cu NPs), which approach the glomerular filtration threshold and accumulate in renal tubules, protect against colistin nephrotoxicity, using human proximal tubular epithelial HK-2 cells (colistin 200 µg/mL; Cu NPs 200 ng/mL) and female C57BL/6 mice (colistin 30 mg/kg/day; Cu NPs 250 µg/kg twice weekly). In HK-2 cells, colistin induced apoptosis, excess cytosolic and mitochondrial superoxide, mitochondrial fission, and dysregulated autophagy with LC3B accumulation and impaired flux, alongside Akt/GSK3β and mTOR suppression and excessive nuclear TFEB translocation. Pharmacological TFEB activation aggravated injury, indicating that maladaptive autophagy contributes to tubular death. Cu NPs scavenged these oxidants, reactivated Akt/GSK3β/mTOR signaling, and restored productive autophagic flux without suppressing nuclear TFEB, reducing apoptosis and preserving mitochondrial integrity, whereas N-acetylcysteine failed to reproduce these signaling effects. Autophagic flux, rather than the absolute level of nuclear TFEB, therefore determined tubular outcome. Cu NPs accumulated preferentially in the kidney and were protective at sub-toxic doses; in vivo, they attenuated tubular injury and apoptosis and modulated autophagy-related signaling, although functional renal improvement was not demonstrated. Thus, Cu NPs attenuate colistin-induced tubular injury by modulating the Akt/GSK3β/mTOR-TFEB axis and restoring autophagic homeostasis rather than acting solely as antioxidants, supporting their potential as a nephroprotective strategy.

articles.title: Cutting to the Heart of CPVT: Who Benefits From Cardiac Sympathetic Denervation?
OpenPose-assisted 3D biomechanical analysis of Wushu jumping kicks with virtual reality visualization and postural stability.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Wushu jumping kicks require highly coordinated whole-body motion during take-off and aerial execution, while landing imposes substantial biomechanical stress on the lower limbs. This study aimed to develop an integrated framework for performance and landing-safety assessment.

METHODS: The OpenPose human pose-estimation framework, using a VGG-19 convolutional backbone for feature extraction, detected anatomical joints in 2D video frames. These 2D joint coordinates were subsequently reconstructed into 3D poses using individualized anthropometric segment lengths, body proportions, anatomical constraints, and temporal continuity across sequential frames.

RESULTS: Reconstructed 3D models showed a proximal-to-distal energy-transfer sequence, with joint angular velocities peaking from 420.5 to 940.8°/s and time lags shortening from 122 to 56 ms. Landing analysis showed a 44.3° ± 2.5°foot angle, deep knee flexion (63.2°-108.5°) for shock attenuation, and asymmetry below the 10 % risk threshold. Stabilization was achieved within 0.85 s, while VR enabled detailed visualization of joint trajectories, movement sequencing, and landing asymmetries.

CONCLUSIONS: The proposed marker-free framework integrates deep-learning-based 3D pose estimation, biomechanical analysis, and VR visualization to provide a comprehensive tool for evaluating Wushu kicking performance and landing safety.

articles.title: Keeping Up Appearances-Or Measuring What Matters?
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions: The VICTORY Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL).

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions.

METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation).

RESULTS: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26).

CONCLUSIONS: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

articles.title: Prevalence and determinants of undetected and uncontrolled hypertension: findings from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension awareness and control are widely used indicators of health system effectiveness, quality, and reach in managing chronic disease. This study estimated the prevalence of undetected and uncontrolled hypertension among middle-aged and older Canadian adults and examined the factors associated with each.

METHODS: We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA) for adults aged 45 years and older. Hypertension was identified from interviewer-administered blood pressure measurements or self-reported diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine associations with predisposing, enabling, and need factors.

RESULTS: The prevalence of hypertension was 42.9%. Of those with hypertension, 17.2% were unaware of their condition, and 26.2% of those who were aware had uncontrolled blood pressure. Not having blood pressure measured in the previous year was strongly associated with undetected hypertension (OR 3.15, 95% CI 2.39-4.15) and was also associated with uncontrolled hypertension (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10). Not having seen a physician in the previous year was similarly associated with both undetected (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.19-2.08) and uncontrolled hypertension (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.77). Younger age and better self-rated general health were associated with undetected hypertension, with odds declining progressively as self-rated health worsened (poor vs excellent: OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.14-0.55). Older age and male sex were associated with uncontrolled hypertension.

CONCLUSION: Undetected and uncontrolled hypertension are common among middle-aged and older Canadians, consistent with gaps in access to primary care and routine screening. Undetected hypertension was most common among adults reporting excellent health, which suggests that care prompted by symptoms may miss a substantial share of cases. Future research should identify and evaluate system-level policies targeted to the populations most affected, including opportunistic and community-based blood pressure measurement.

articles.title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA: From Diagnosis to Phenotyping.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis established after coronary angiography and requires further evaluation to distinguish true ischemic MINOCA from alternative non-ischemic diagnoses. Accurate identification of the underlying etiology is essential because prognosis and management vary substantially among disease entities. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) has emerged as the central noninvasive imaging modality in the diagnostic evaluation of MINOCA. This review summarizes the role of CMR in patients presenting with MINOCA, focusing on diagnostic pathways, tissue characterization techniques, phenotypic classification, prognostic assessment, clinical practice, and emerging technologies. CMR enables comprehensive assessment of ventricular function, myocardial edema, fibrosis, necrosis, and microvascular injury through cine imaging, T1- and T2-based tissue characterization, and late gadolinium enhancement. By integrating these findings, CMR differentiates patients with true ischemic MINOCA from those with alternative non-ischemic diagnoses, thereby guiding subsequent investigations and management. Early CMR substantially increases diagnostic yield and frequently identifies a specific etiology that directly influences treatment decisions. Beyond diagnosis, CMR provides important prognostic information through the quantification of infarct size, microvascular obstruction, myocardial edema, and scar burden. Advanced parametric mapping techniques and artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis may further refine disease phenotyping and improve risk stratification.

articles.title: Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes After Transcatheter Fontan Fenestration Closure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the indications, hemodynamic changes, and intermediate-term outcomes of transcatheter Fontan fenestration closure in a single-center retrospective cohort.

METHOD: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included all consecutive patients who underwent transcatheter closure of a surgically created Fontan fenestration between January 2015 and April 2025. Demographic, anatomical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, procedural, and follow-up data were collected from medical records. The primary endpoint was the change in resting systemic arterial oxygen saturation. Secondary endpoints included changes in mean Fontan pressure, periprocedural complications, late Fontan-related morbidities, and the need for re-fenestration. Patients were also classified as undergoing early (≤24 months after Fontan completion) or late (>24 months after Fontan completion) fenestration closure.

RESULTS: Sixteen patients (50% male) were included, and 75% had an extracardiac conduit Fontan. The median interval between Fontan completion and fenestration closure was 18.5 months, and 62.5% of the patients underwent early closure. Desaturation was the primary indication (87.5%), whereas suspected or documented systemic embolism accounted for 12.5% of cases. The baseline mean Fontan pressure was 12.0+-3.0 mmHg, and systemic oxygen saturation was 82.7+-10.0%. After closure, the mean Fontan pressure increased slightly to 12.9+-3.0 mmHg (P = 0.056), whereas oxygen saturation improved to 95.4+-3.5% (P < 0.001). During a median follow-up of 5.7 years, 93.8% of the patients remained free from major Fontan-related complications and the need for re-fenestration.
