CONCLUSION: In carefully selected patients with a fenestrated Fontan circulation, transcatheter closure guided by balloon test occlusion was associated with a marked improvement in systemic oxygenation and only a small increase in mean Fontan pressure. Given the limited sample size and retrospective design, comparisons related to the timing of closure should be interpreted as exploratory, and closure decisions should be individualized based on clinical and hemodynamic assessments.

articles.title: Diastolic Function Classification in Acute Myocardial Infarction: Comparison of the 2016 ASE/EACVI Guideline and the 2025 ASE Recommendations.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diastolic dysfunction (DD) and elevated left ventricular filling pressure (LVFP) commonly occur after acute myocardial infarction (MI) and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. This study aimed to compare the 2016 American Society of Echocardiography/European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (ASE/EACVI) guideline and the 2025 American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) recommendations for assessing diastolic function (DF) in patients with acute MI.

METHOD: This prospective, single-center, observational study included consecutive patients admitted with acute MI between November 2025 and April 2026. Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was performed during hospitalization in the coronary intensive care unit (CICU). The presence of DD, LVFP categorization, and DD grading were evaluated according to both the 2016 ASE/EACVI guideline and the 2025 ASE recommendations. Agreement between the two algorithms was assessed using Cohen's kappa analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 99 patients were included (mean age, 59.3+-12.2 years; 82.8% male). According to the 2016 guideline, DD status remained indeterminate in 3 patients and LVFP categorization remained indeterminate in 13 patients, whereas all patients could be classified using the 2025 recommendations. Among the patients who could be classified using both algorithms, 18 patients classified as having DD according to the 2016 guideline were reclassified as having normal diastolic function according to the 2025 recommendations (P < 0.001). Agreement between the two approaches was substantial for LVFP categorization (Cohen's kappa=0.721, P < 0.001) and moderate for DD grading (weighted Cohen's kappa=0.606, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In patients with acute MI, the 2025 ASE recommendations reduced the number of indeterminate DF classifications and resulted in lower DD grades than the 2016 ASE/EACVI guideline while maintaining substantial agreement for LVFP categorization.

articles.title: Candidemia in patients with intestinal failure: Diagnostic utility of fungal blood cultures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pediatric patients with intestinal failure (IF) receiving parenteral nutrition are at increased risk for candidemia. Evaluation of central line-associated bloodstream infection often includes aerobic, anaerobic, and fungal blood cultures, but the diagnostic yield of dedicated fungal cultures is uncertain. We evaluated fungal blood cultures compared with aerobic cultures for detecting candidemia.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients with IF and central venous catheters admitted to Children's National Hospital from 2010 through 2020 was conducted. Candidemia episodes were identified through microbiology records. Primary analysis included episodes with both aerobic and fungal blood cultures obtained on the first day of fungemia. Time to positivity (TTP) was compared between paired cultures.

RESULTS: Among 121 hospitalizations, 20 candidemia episodes occurred in 17 patients; 14 had paired aerobic and fungal cultures and were included in the primary analysis. Median age was 3.3 years (interquartile range [IQR] 1.0-8.7), and median length of stay was 25.5 days (IQR 17.0-36.3). Candida parapsilosis and Candida guilliermondii were most common (13/20 episodes). Ninety percent were receiving parenteral nutrition, and 90% had antimicrobial exposure within 6 months. In all paired cases, Candida grew in both cultures. Aerobic cultures had faster TTP than fungal cultures (23.8 ± 8.5 vs. 67.2 ± 18.0 h; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Aerobic cultures detected all candidemia identified by fungal cultures and had faster TTP. Dedicated fungal cultures provided no observed incremental diagnostic yield, although sample size limits precision. Larger studies should determine whether selective rather than routine fungal cultures are appropriate in pediatric IF.

articles.title: Improving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in hospitalized pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Youth hospitalized with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. Using quality improvement methods, we aimed to increase the rate of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst select hospitalized patients with IBD by reaching 90% algorithm adherence by June 2023 and sustaining.

METHODS: Current evidence, external institutional algorithms, and multidisciplinary collaboration (hematology, pharmacy, surgery) were used to create an algorithm for providing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin. The algorithm was implemented in February 2023 for all patients admitted with active IBD to a large, tertiary care children's hospital. Rates of algorithm adherence and rates of enoxaparin receipt during the project period were compared to baseline rates. Patient and provider education, electronic data tracking, and regular data auditing and review with providers were used to improve algorithm adherence. Reasons for non-adherence to the algorithm and rates of VTE, bleeding complications, and medication side effects during hospitalization were tracked.

RESULTS: The proportion of patients who appropriately followed the algorithm reached 94%, increased from 50% when the algorithm was retrospectively applied to the pre-project period (p < 0.001). The total proportion of hospitalized patients who received pharmacologic prophylaxis increased from 1% to 31% (p < 0.001). Following algorithm introduction, there were no VTEs or reported complications from enoxaparin during hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of a standardized algorithm was associated with significantly increased rates of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst children hospitalized with IBD with no recorded adverse in-hospital events.

articles.title: Low Uptake of Guideline-Recommended MRI Screening for Silent Cerebral Infarcts over the Lifespan in Sickle Cell Anemia.
articles.abstract: Silent cerebral infarcts (SCIs) are common and clinically consequential in individuals with sickle cell anemia (SCA; HbSS or HbSβ⁰-thalassemia). In 2020, the American Society of Hematology recommended magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based screening in childhood (strong recommendation) and adulthood (conditional recommendation); however, real-world implementation remains poorly characterized. We conducted a multicenter sequential mixed-methods study integrating site-level MRI utilization data, clinician surveys, and semi-structured interviews. Eleven academic SCD programs contributed MRI data for patients aged 5-18 years and >18 years. Clinicians completed the Clinician Guideline Determinants Questionnaire (CGDQ), adapted for pediatric and adult SCI screening, and a purposively sampled subset participated in interviews guided by the Tailored Implementation for Chronic Diseases framework. Thirty-eight clinicians completed surveys, and 25 participated in interviews. Clinicians endorsed the evidence supporting SCI screening; however, readiness to implement adult screening was lower than for pediatric screening (mean CGDQ score 117.0 vs. 126.4). Across 6,959 patients with SCA, fewer than 1 in 8 (11.75%) had undergone brain MRI over the study period (2015-2024), with consistently lower utilization in adult-only programs. Qualitative analysis identified 5 modifiable, multilevel determinants influencing implementation: unclear guideline expectations, patient and family readiness, interprofessional workflows and interpretation capacity, clinic resources and staffing infrastructure, and structural and policy barriers. Despite strong clinician support for SCI screening, implementation remains inconsistent, particularly in adult SCA care. Identified determinants highlight actionable targets for multicomponent implementation strategies to improve uptake and sustainability of MRI-based SCI screening across the lifespan.

articles.title: [Pilot estimation of the prevalence of myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome and multiple chemical sensitivity in the adult population of the Community of Madrid (Spain) using Primary Care-based sampling].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Multiple Chemical Sensitivity (MCS) are severe multisystem diseases whose clinical recognition has been hindered by social invisibility and diagnostic variability. This has limited the availability of reliable epidemiological data. The aim of this study was to estimate the prevalence of ME/CFS and MCS in the adult population of the Community of Madrid.

METHODS: A cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among adults over eighteen years belonging to the patient panels of primary care nurses within the Primary Care Services Management. A two‑stage cluster sampling strategy was applied, with a planned sample size of 2,000 participants (550 in the pilot study). Case identification was carried out using the DSQ‑SF, SF‑36, and QEESI questionnaires. The analysis included descriptive statistics (medians, interquartile ranges, and frequencies), chi‑square tests, and mean comparisons using ANOVA and Student's t‑test.

RESULTS: This paper presents the findings of the pilot study conducted in the Western Primary Care Directorate. Of the 530 individuals who agreed to participate, 280 (52.8%) completed the screening. The estimated prevalence was 2.26% for ME/CFS and 2.64% for MCS. Half of the individuals who met criteria for ME/CFS also met criteria for MCS, resulting in an estimated dual‑condition prevalence of 1.13%.

CONCLUSIONS: The results highlight the epidemiological significance of ME/CFS and MCS. The estimated prevalences are high, clearly exceeding the threshold for rare diseases.

articles.title: Influence of non-surgical periodontal therapy on inflammasome biomarkers in periodontitis with and without diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic inflammatory conditions linked through common pathogenic processes. Interleukin-18 (IL-18), absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2), and interferon gamma-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) have been associated with inflammatory pathways of both diseases. Limited data exist regarding the effect of non-surgical periodontal therapy (NSPT) on these biomarkers. This study was designed to evaluate and compare the effect of NSPT on serum levels of AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 in stage III periodontitis patients with and without T2DM.

METHODS: Ninety participants were allocated into three groups: periodontally healthy controls (group I), stage III periodontitis (group II), stage III periodontitis with T2DM (group III). The plaque index (PI), gingival index (GI), papillary bleeding index (PBI), probing pocket depth (PPD), clinical attachment level (CAL), gingival recession (GR), periodontal inflamed surface area (PISA), periodontal epithelial surface area (PESA), random blood sugar (RBS), HbA1c, AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 were assessed at baseline in group I and also at 6 weeks in groups II and III.

RESULTS: Serum AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 levels were significantly elevated in periodontitis patients, with the highest concentrations observed in group III, followed by group II at baseline. NSPT significantly improved PPD, CAL, PISA, PESA, and glycemic status; serum biomarker levels were observed in both treatment groups with greater improvements observed in group III.

CONCLUSION: Serum AIM2, IFI16, and IL-18 levels increased progressively from group I to group III and decreased significantly following NSPT, reflecting reduced periodontal and systemic inflammation. These biomarkers may serve as potential indicators linking periodontal inflammation with metabolic dysregulation in T2DM.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with the Clinical Trials Registry-India (CTRI/2024/06/068456).

PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Periodontitis and type 2 diabetes are closely linked because both are associated with inflammation. This study examined whether treating severe periodontitis without surgery could improve gum health and reduce inflammation in the body. Ninety participants, including healthy individuals and patients with periodontitis with or without diabetes, were evaluated before and after treatment. Patients with both periodontitis and diabetes had the highest levels of inflammation-related blood markers. Following treatment, periodontal health, blood sugar, and these blood markers improved, with the greatest benefits observed in patients with diabetes. These findings suggest that periodontal treatment may improve both oral and overall health. Non-surgical periodontal therapy improved periodontal health and reduced inflammatory blood biomarkers in patients with stage III periodontitis, with greater improvements in those with type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Tissue monocyte chemoattractant protein-1-induced protein 1 and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1 levels in peri-implant diseases: A cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the peri-implant tissue levels of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1-induced protein 1 (MCPIP-1) and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma translocation protein 1 (MALT-1) in relation to peri-implant diseases and peri-implant tissue interleukin (IL)-1β, -6, -8, -17A, and Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) arginine-specific gingipain A (RgpA) levels.

METHODS: Granulation tissues were collected from 25 patients with peri-implantitis and 23 patients with peri-mucositis during treatment for peri-implantitis and peri-implant mucositis. For controls, 24 primary soft tissues covering the submerged cover screws were collected during the second stage surgery of implant treatment. The tissue levels of MCPIP-1 and MALT-1 were quantified by ELISA and IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-17A were analysed by multiplex immunoassay. P. gingivalis RgpA levels were measured using an immunoblot assay.

RESULTS: The peri-implant mucositis group had higher MCPIP-1 levels than the controls (p = 0.001) and the peri-implantitis group (p < 0.001). The control group had higher MALT-1 levels compared with the peri-implant mucositis group (p < 0.001) and the peri-implantitis group (p < 0.001). Linear regression analysis indicated associations between MCPIP-1 and IL-6 levels (β = 0.880, p < 0.001), MCPIP-1 and IL-8 levels (β = 0.609, p < 0.001), MCPIP-1 and IL-17A levels (β = 0.619, p < 0.001), MALT-1 and IL-1β levels (β = -0.389, p = 0.027) after being adjusted for the modified gingival index.

CONCLUSION: The MCPIP-1 and MALT-1 protein expressions in tissues covering the submerged cover screw, with peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis showed distinct profiles. The variations in their associations with peri-implant diseases and proinflammatory cytokine levels can be related to their dual functions in the regulation of acute inflammation and infection.

articles.title: Efficacy of action observation therapy in patients with dementia or cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate the therapeutic effects of action observation therapy (AOT) on patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: The authors performed the literature search in the PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases in August 2025. Randomized controlled trials comparing the outcomes of AOT with controls among patients with dementia or cognitive impairment were included.

RESULTS: Nine studies involving 348 patients were included in a systematic review, of which seven were included in a meta-analysis. The meta-analysis results revealed that AOT was associated with significantly improved cognitive function [Standard mean differences (SMD) = 0.86, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.53 to 1.19], activities of daily living (SMD = 0.67, 95% CI = 0.22 to 1.12), and naming aphasia (SMD = 0.53, 95% CI = 0.01 to 1.05); with significantly improved motor function (gait velocity [SMD = 0.70, 95% CI = 0.24 to 1.16] and result on the timed up-and-go test [SMD = -1.05, 95% CI = -1.89 to -0.21]) in patients with dementia without stroke; and with significantly improved cognitive function (SMD = 0.96, 95% CI = 0.41 to 1.50) at the 1-month follow-up.

CONCLUSION: AOT may exert beneficial effects for patients with dementia or cognitive impairment.

articles.title: Ocular hyperemia with netarsudil/latanoprost fixed combination in glaucoma: an exploratory association analysis of tolerability outcomes by prior topical therapy and baseline ocular hyperemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This post hoc analysis of MERCURY-3 evaluates factors associated with baseline ocular hyperemia and tolerability outcomes with netarsudil/latanoprost fixed combination (NET/LAT).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: MERCURY-3 was a prospective, randomized, double-masked, multicenter, Phase 3, European trial. Adults with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension inadequately controlled on topical therapy were randomized to once-daily NET/LAT (n = 218) or bimatoprost/timolol fixed combination (BIM/TIM; n = 212) for 6 months. Patients were stratified by baseline ocular hyperemia status (none vs any grade) and associations with prior treatment, adverse events (AEs), and hyperemia evolution evaluated.

RESULTS: In the NET/LAT arm, prior combination therapy was associated with a greater prevalence of baseline ocular hyperemia than prior monotherapy (distribution: p = 0.003). Patients with baseline hyperemia experienced higher rates of AEs (85% vs 63%), ocular treatment-related AEs (74% vs 39%), and conjunctival hyperemia (45% vs 26%) during treatment. Ocular hyperemia remained predominantly mild throughout follow-up, with a more stable severity trajectory linked to prior monotherapy compared with prior combination therapy. No comparable associations were observed with BIM/TIM.

CONCLUSIONS: Prior treatment complexity and baseline ocular hyperemia status are associated with tolerability outcomes during NET/LAT therapy. These exploratory findings suggest that earlier step-up after monotherapy could be associated with more favorable tolerability.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CT.gov identifier: NCT03284853.

articles.title: Clinical, Electrophysiological Profile and Outcomes in Patients With Permanent Junctional Reciprocating Tachycardia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Permanent junctional reciprocating tachycardia (PJRT) is an uncommon form of re-entrant supraventricular tachycardia that can lead to tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy (TIC). This study aims to describe a cohort of individuals with PJRT, outline their clinical and electrophysiological profiles, and evaluate various treatment strategies and long-term outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with PJRT. Electrophysiological confirmation of the diagnosis was available for 24 patients who underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA). Outcomes were assessed from the index ablation to the most recent follow-up at the time of data collection.

RESULTS: 31 patients (median age 15 years [IQR 6.5-25 years]) with PJRT were included of whom 14 (45.2%) had TIC. 24 patients (77.4%) underwent RFCA, while 7 (22.5%) received medical management. Initial procedural success was achieved in 23 of 24 patients (95.8%). Recurrence occurred in 2 of 24 patients (8.3%); both were successfully re-ablated. Ultimately, all ablated patients were arrhythmia-free (24/24; 100%) at a median follow-up of 5.5 years (IQR 2.75-16.3 years). Two patients experienced major complications: spasm of the right posterolateral branch (RPLB), which was managed medically, and occlusion of the posterolateral branch (PLB) requiring stenting. Complete regression of TIC was observed in patients who underwent ablation (11/11).

CONCLUSIONS: This is the largest single-center report from Asia characterizing clinical spectrum of PJRT. RFCA provides an effective and durable treatment for PJRT. Careful attention to the proximity of the ablation site to the coronary circulation and atrioventricular node is essential to minimize rare but serious complications.

articles.title: Diagnosis of infectious disease pathology on whole slide images: a multi-platform evaluation with implications for digital laboratory practice.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adoption of whole slide imaging (WSI) is accelerating across anatomic pathology practices, yet there is a lack of evidence guiding its use for infectious disease diagnoses. WSI systems usually operate at a maximum of 40X magnification without z-plane depth, appropriately raising concerns about detecting microorganisms.

METHODS: We assembled a 15-case panel (with immunohistochemistry [IHC]/special stains where indicated) spanning bacterial, viral, parasitic and fungal infections of various organ systems, including five organism-negative 'controls'. An infectious disease pathologist independently reviewed all glass slides to confirm the diagnoses. Eight board-certified pathologists reviewed cases (blinded to diagnoses) scanned on one of four high-throughput scanner platforms (Philips SG300, Hamamatsu S360, Pramana (Spectral HT2) and Leica GT450 designated A-D (not in order), two pathologists/platform). As a control group, two additional pathologists reviewed the same cases on glass slides. Additionally, in an attempt to compare image quality among the four WSI platforms, 10 pathologists (blinded to the platform) rated image quality from side-by-side screenshots in 12 representative cases.

RESULTS: Aggregate diagnostic scores were: Scanner A: 78%, Scanner D: 71%, Scanner C: 69% and Scanner B: 65%, (mean 71%) vs. 79% for glass-slide reviewers. Intra-platform variability between the two pathologists on the same scanner (up to 23% on platform D) exceeded inter-platform differences. WSI reviewers performed near-equivalently to glass-slide reviewers for large organisms (92% vs. 89%) but lower for small/low-burden organisms (36% vs. 63%).

CONCLUSIONS: Diagnostic performance on WSI for infectious disease pathology in this exploratory study varied primarily with organism size and burden, not by platform-specific image quality differences. WSI is non-inferior to glass for large organisms, but glass slide review may be superior for small (and low burden) organisms.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Advancement of Mechanical Circulatory Support and Cardiac Care: A Systematic Review of Its Role and Potential.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In recent years, there has been a notable surge in the ability of machines to perform complex and intelligent human-centered tasks, particularly within the domain of cardiovascular health. Rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms reflect the considerable potential for such analyses to meaningfully extend into translational device development and clinical usage of medical devices, especially mechanical circulatory support (MCS) therapies. Here, we investigate and report the applications, limitations, and strategies in which AI is currently being employed in MCS and the potential opportunities of AI approaches to advance the field of MCS.

METHODS: To effectively assess the scope and impact of AI in MCS, we conducted a systematic literature review. A comprehensive search of 4 recognized research databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, Ovid MEDLINE, and ProQuest) was performed using this Boolean string: "(Artificial Intelligence) AND (AI) AND (Mechanical Circulatory Support) AND (MCS) NOT (Heart Transplant) NOT (Cardiogenic Shock) NOT (Critical Care)." This strategy was designed to identify the application of AI in MCS only. Database search results were then screened by titles and abstracts, followed by full-text eligibility assessment and duplicate removal. Following these screening and eligibility steps, 30 of the 328 identified articles remained for inclusion.

RESULTS: Most relevant publications covered two main subjects: the prediction and management of postoperative outcomes, and the development of personalized device-patient matching and timing. Across the reviewed studies, AI/ML models demonstrated promising performance in study-specific predictions of complications, recovery-related outcomes, and survival and were investigated as tools to support clinical decision-making. Barriers to broad implementation of AI include the necessity for sizable, high-quality datasets to achieve algorithm training benchmarks, the lack of organized and complete databases, such as INTERMACS, and limited computational resources. Emerging frontiers of MCS recognize the potential for AI and ML techniques to refine image recognition capabilities, diagnostic assessment, device placement, and post-implantation monitoring approaches in the future.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-driven approaches demonstrate a promising convergence of computational power and clinical expertise, with the potential to support more personalized, efficient, and informed management of MCS patients. However, the current evidence remains largely exploratory, and broad implementation will require robust clinical validation together with attention to data integrity, model accuracy, resource access, and clinical acceptance.

articles.title: Association Between the Pre-Implant "I Need Help" Score and Survival After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The "I Need Help" score is a tool to facilitate referral of patients with advanced heart failure (HF). Although its prognostic value has been demonstrated in chronic HF, evidence regarding patients undergoing durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation remains limited.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients with advanced HF who underwent durable LVAD implantation at a tertiary HF center between January 2018 and December 2019. The pre-implant "I Need Help" score was calculated, and patients were stratified into higher-score (≥ 6) and lower-score (< 6) groups. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality during LVAD support. Survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 93 patients analyzed (median age, 59 years), 64 (68.8%) had a score ≥ 6. The higher-score group had a more advanced disease stage, reflected by a higher prevalence of INTERMACS profiles 1-3. During the follow-up, 63 patients died and nine underwent heart transplantation. The higher-score was associated with increased mortality in univariable analysis (hazard ratio [HR] 2.05, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-3.73, p = 0.018), but the association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted HR, 1.76; 95% CI, 0.71-4.33; p = 0.221).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with a higher pre-implant "I Need Help" score had worse unadjusted survival after LVAD implantation, but this association was attenuated after adjustment. The score may reflect the cumulative burden of advanced HF features, although its independent prognostic value in LVAD recipients remains uncertain. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Machine Learning and DFT Decoding Lanthanide-Doped Lignin Carbon Dots: Multicolor Sensor Arrays for Ultrasensitive Profiling Biothiols.
articles.abstract: Biothiols are key small molecules that maintain the redox balance in living organisms, and their abnormal levels are closely associated with various diseases. The development of rapid and accurate detection methods is of great significance to precision medicine. However, traditional detection methods often rely on a single signal output, making it difficult to effectively distinguish between structurally similar biothiol congeners, and they are susceptible to interference from complex biological matrices. In this study, four types of lanthanide (Nd, Pr, La, Sm)-doped fluorescent carbon dots were synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal method using lignin extracted from corn straw as a green carbon source. The abundant functional groups on the surface of these carbon dots generate differential interactions (coordination, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic interactions) with various thiol molecules, forming characteristic fluorescence response fingerprints. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms were employed to model and classify the multi-dimensional response data collected from the four-channel sensor array. The results demonstrate that the sensor array exhibits a detection limit as low as 0.42 nM for five biothiols (GSH, Cys, Hcy, NAC, DTT), with LODs ranging from 0.42 to 3.63 nM across the four carbon dots. The random forest model achieved 98.2% accurate identification on the test set, and the spiked recovery rates in serum samples ranged from 92% to 106%. Meanwhile, density functional theory (DFT) calculations preliminarily revealed that the fluorescence quenching mechanism is predominantly governed by photoinduced electron transfer (PET), validating the modulating effect of lanthanide ions on the energy levels of the carbon dots at the atomic level. This work not only provides a new pathway for the high-value utilization of agricultural waste but also opens up a versatile sensing platform for the rapid and intelligent identification of similar analytes in complex samples.

articles.title: Rapid and Controlled Single-Nanopore Insertion via Hydrogel-Confined Localized Delivery.
articles.abstract: Controlled insertion of a single protein pore, also referred to as a nanopore, into a free-standing lipid bilayer underpins high-resolution single-channel electrophysiology. Hitherto, conventional bulk reconstitution is stochastic, slow, and prone to multiple insertions. To overcome this, we adapted a hydrogel-confined delivery strategy in which an agarose-filled glass capillary delivers nanopores directly to the bilayer. An optimal window of agarose concentration, aerolysin concentration, and membrane potential raised the single-pore yield to >70% and shortened the waiting time to the first insertion from tens of minutes to a few minutes, without altering native pore conductance. The approach generalizes across the β-barrel toxin aerolysin, the mitochondrial TOM core complex, and a DNA nanopore, making nanopore insertion rapid, controlled, and reproducible.

articles.title: Designing of a Test Tube Containing Aptamer-Immobilized Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Network-Based Optical Photonic Sensors for the Multiplex Detection of Doping Substances in Human Blood Serum.
articles.abstract: The detection of doping substances in human serum is a critical concern in both clinical diagnostics and anti-doping efforts. In this study, we present a novel, portable, and cost-effective biosensor system based on cholesteric liquid crystal networks (CLCN) for multiplexed drug detection. The system employs aptamer-immobilized CLCN-based optical sensors, fabricated on flexible polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrates, for the onsite detection of cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, tramadol, and salbutamol. The biosensor platform utilizes the unique optical properties of CLCNs, where the helical pitch change in response to analyte binding results in visible color shifts. These sensors are easy to fabricate, as all liquid crystals used are commercially available and inexpensive, making the technology highly accessible. Additionally, the sensors are easy to use, requiring minimal training, and the results can be quickly interpreted via a simple visual readout. The system was evaluated for its performance in spiked human serum samples, demonstrating high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy in detecting low concentrations of doping substances. The inclusion of QR codes on the sensors allowed for convenient comparison with calibrated reference standards, ensuring reliable results. This biosensor system offers a promising solution for on-site and multiplexed detection of doping substances in human serum, with significant potential for monitoring in clinical and athletic settings.

articles.title: Large Language Model-Enhanced MFSSG Enables Effective and Accurate Integration Analysis for Microbiome-Metabolome Data.
articles.abstract: The massive volume of paired microbiome and metabolome measurementsgenerated through high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometryhas created an urgent need for dedicated, integrative analytical pipelines. Existing tools lack the capacity to simultaneously support sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification using matched dual-modal datasets. To overcome this analytical bottleneck, we introduce the matrix factorization with shared and specific graph learning (MFSSG) toolkit: an unsupervised matrix factorization framework that jointly learns both shared and modality-specific graph structures. MFSSG preserves cross-omics spatial consistency by leveraging shared nearest-neighbor graphs derived from analytical profiles and incorporates two complementary regularization termsentropy regularization to enhance cluster discriminability and a pre-trained microbial graph Laplacianto mitigate measurement bias inherent in microbiome sequencing versus metabolomic mass spectrometry data. Validated across three independent multi-omics cohorts derived from gastric and gut biospecimensincluding gastric cancer, end-stage renal disease, and type 1 diabetesMFSSG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art integration methods in disease classification. Furthermore, a novel pairwise learning module enables parallel and accurate quantification of the metabolic age and microbial age, facilitating refined patient risk stratification. This versatile toolkit provides a robust chemometric strategy for uncovering latent biological patterns embedded within heterogeneous multi-omics analytical data.

articles.title: Oligomer-Responsive ThT Derivative for Early Deterioration Evaluation of Insulin Injections.
articles.abstract: Insulin, an essential drug for diabetes, is prone to be aggregated due to its inherent amyloidogenicity. Particularly for insulin injections, improper handling or storage (e.g., vibration and heat) can lead to drug deterioration, namely, formation of early oligomers that are highly toxic. Compared to the cloudy amyloid fibrils, the early oligomers are highly soluble and less viscous, thus posing a great challenge for their detection. Thioflavin T (ThT) is the "gold-standard" fluorescent probe for protein aggregation and insulin fibrils but fails in recognition of the early soluble oligomers. Herein, a ThT derivative with a stronger donor unit and a larger molecular volume, namely, ThTPD, was designed with improved viscosity sensitivity and oligomer-binding affinity. In the model of insulin aggregation, ThTPD exhibited an obvious fluorescence response in the very early oligomer stage (∼30 s), whereas ThT only responded to the protofibrils and fibrils (∼30 min). For circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy that is typically explored for protein aggregation study, a signal emerged until the protofibril formation stage (∼10 min). Real-sample analysis with commercial insulin injections demonstrated that ThTPD could achieve early deterioration evaluation, making it a promising, convenient, and rapid probe for the early deterioration monitoring of insulin injections.

articles.title: Current Status and Epidemiologic Perspectives on Mite-, Flea-, and Louse-Borne Diseases in Korea.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This narrative review summarizes the epidemiology and public health relevance of mite-, flea-, and louse-borne infections in Korea.

METHODS: We combined English- and Korean-language literature with national surveillance data. Annual and monthly notifications of scrub typhus and murine typhus were summarized for 2001-2024, and mean annual regional incidence was assessed for 2015-2024 using population statistics.

RESULTS: National surveillance recorded 149,303 scrub typhus cases and 660 murine typhus cases during 2001-2024. Scrub typhus showed a pronounced autumn peak and higher incidence in southern and southwestern regions. Murine typhus showed a recent increase in annual case notifications, reaching 60 cases in 2024, with heterogeneous regional patterns. Bartonella henselae infection has been documented in Korea, but its burden remains uncertain. Epidemic typhus and louse-borne relapsing fever have not been officially reported for several decades, although reemergence in vulnerable populations remains possible.

CONCLUSION: Mite-, flea-, and louse-borne infections remain neglected components of the febrile illness landscape in Korea. Improved diagnostic awareness, strengthened surveillance, and continued collaboration are needed to better define their burden and to detect potential reemergence.

articles.title: Inhalable IL-10 as an Aerosolized Therapeutic Approach to Acute Lung Injury in Mice.
articles.journal: Journal of aerosol medicine and pulmonary drug delivery
articles.abstract: Background:Acute lung injury (ALI) is a severe inflammatory condition with substantial morbidity and mortality, with no approved pharmacologic therapies targeting its underlying inflammatory pathways. Prior studies demonstrated that intratracheal interleukin (IL)-10 reduces lipopolysaccharide (LPS)- and organic dust-induced lung and systemic inflammation.Methods:The present study evaluated the aerosol performance and efficacy of nebulized IL-10 against a high-dose LPS-induced ALI model with comparisons to shock-dose dexamethasone (5 mg/kg, intraperitoneal injections). C57BL/6 male mice were challenged with LPS (5 mg/mL) and treated with low- (0.1 mg/mL), mid- (0.5 mg/mL), or high-dose (1 mg/mL) IL-10, or vehicle, all by nose-only aerosol inhalation (15-minute exposure duration), with euthanasia on day 2. Results:Aerosolized IL-10 exhibited a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 1.66 µm (geometric standard deviation 2.04). Pulmonary deposited doses were 5.5-5.7 µg/mouse for LPS and 10.4, 21.3, and 38.4 (ug/kg) for low-, mid-, and high-dose IL-10. LPS-induced weight loss (18.6%) was reduced by high IL-10 (8.4%) and dexamethasone (7.0%), with no significant difference between treatments. Increased lung weights (40.8%) following LPS challenge were significantly reduced by mid- and high-dose IL-10 and dexamethasone. LPS-induced airway total cell and neutrophil counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid were not reduced by either treatment. In contrast, IL-10 treatment produced dose-dependent reductions in LPS-induced pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-12p70, IFN-γ, KC/CXCL1, MCP-1, and MIP-1α), with beneficial responses at the high IL-10 dose comparable to dexamethasone. Histopathology demonstrated dose-responsive reductions in LPS-induced peribronchovascular mixed cellular lung inflammation, significant at mid- and high IL-10 doses and comparable to dexamethasone.Conclusion:Overall, aerosolized IL-10 demonstrated aerodynamic properties consistent with deep lung penetration and dose-dependent efficacy at ≥21.3 µg/kg, achieving anti-inflammatory effects comparable with dexamethasone in this ALI murine model.

articles.title: Changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention in pelvic organ prolapse and urinary incontinence care: a quasi-experimental single-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the assessment of pelvic organ prolapse (POP), approximately half of women may present with varying degrees of pelvic organ descent, although many do not exhibit clinical symptoms. Therefore, nurses have an important role in timely assessment, prevention of complications, and provision of appropriate supportive care. This study aimed to evaluate changes in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice following a competency-based educational intervention for the care of women with POP and urinary incontinence (UI).

METHODS: The study followed a quasi-experimental, single-group pretest-posttest design and included 60 nurses working in the outpatient department of the Urology and Nephrology Center, Mansoura University, Egypt. Data were collected using three researcher-developed instruments: the Demographic Structured Interview Schedule, the Nurses' Knowledge Structured Interview, and the Nurses' Observational Practice Checklist. Nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice were assessed before the intervention and reassessed immediately after completion of the educational intervention.

RESULTS: Statistically significant immediate post-intervention improvements were observed in nurses' knowledge and clinical practice. The mean overall knowledge score increased from 17.05 ± 1.92 at baseline to 19.18 ± 1.97 immediately after the intervention (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < .001). Perineal care practice scores increased from 26.80 ± 6.93 to 49.33 ± 3.93, pessary insertion practice scores increased from 25.33 ± 6.81 to 50.73 ± 3.85, and pelvic floor muscle exercise instruction scores increased from 9.80 ± 3.25 to 20.42 ± 1.94 (all p < .001).

CONCLUSION: Participation in the competency-based educational intervention was associated with significant immediate improvements in nurses' knowledge and observed clinical practice related to POP and UI care. These findings represent short-term post-training changes, and further controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to determine whether these improvements are sustained over time.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06639217, registered on 10 October 2024. Retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Integrative Computational Analysis of the Putative Molecular Crosstalk Between Diabetes Mellitus and Pancreatic Cancer: A Network Pharmacology Study of Nisha-Amalaki.
articles.journal: Omics : a journal of integrative biology
articles.abstract: Nisha-Amalaki (NA), an Ayurvedic formulation of Curcuma longa (Nisha) and Emblica officinalis (Amalaki), is traditionally used for glycemic control and antioxidant support. Since diabetes mellitus (DM) and pancreatic cancer (PC) share metabolic-inflammatory mechanisms, this study employed integrative computational approaches to identify NA phytochemicals and their putative molecular targets mediating dual antidiabetic and anticancer effects. NA phytochemicals were retrieved from databases and literature, filtered through ADMET and drug-likeness criteria, and mapped to DM- and PC-related genes. From 311 reported NA phytochemicals, curcumin (an.), divanillalaceton, and caffeic acid emerged as principal phytochemicals. Enrichment analysis implicated IL-6/JAK/STAT3, apical junction, and apoptosis pathways. Box plot analysis showed all 14 hub genes were upregulated in PC tissues, while high EGFR and MMP1 expression correlated with poorer survival. Among the 14 hub genes, eight key genes were further refined by topology algorithms, that is, APP, TLR4, NOS2, EGFR, MMP9, STAT3, NFE2L2, and ALOX5. Cytotoxicity predictions suggested potential antiproliferative activity of the phytochemicals against multiple PC cell lines. Molecular docking and dynamics indicated thermodynamically stable phytochemical-target interactions, with curcumin (an.) showing stronger EGFR binding than gefitinib. This study provides computational evidence supporting NA's potential in treating PC and DM; probably via modulating inflammatory, metabolic, and junctional pathways.

articles.title: Effectiveness, acceptability, and completeness of intervention reporting of psychological interventions for people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment: a mixed-methods systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People living with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) commonly experience difficulties with mental health and psychological well-being. Given the dyadic interdependence of well-being, these difficulties may also affect informal caregivers. However, access to psychological interventions remains limited for people living with dementia. Our overall aim was to perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of the current research evidence for psychological interventions intended to improve mental health and psychological well-being in people living with dementia or MCI.

METHODS: We systematically searched electronic databases ASSIA, CENTRAL, CINAHL, EMBASE, MEDLINE and PsycINFO for eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and identified qualitative studies associated with eligible RCTs via hand searching. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts, assessed full-texts, and completed quality appraisal. Quantitative studies with sufficient data were included in a meta-analysis, and qualitative studies were synthesized using framework analysis. A convergent mixed-methods design was adopted to integrate quantitative and qualitative results in the discussion.

RESULTS: We included 15 quantitative studies in the review (n = 1,742 people living with dementia or MCI). Our meta-analysis showed a small-to-moderate effect size favoring the intervention for depressive symptoms in people living with dementia or MCI (n = 11 studies; Hedges' g = -0.36 [95% CI = -0.61 to -0.11] p<.05). Substantial heterogeneity was observed, prediction interval crossed the null, and certainty of evidence was very low. No effect was found for depressive symptoms in caregivers (n = 5 studies; Hedges' g = 0.01, p>.05). It was not appropriate to conduct a meta-analysis for other outcomes associated with mental health and psychological well-being in people living with dementia, MCI, or their caregivers due to insufficient data. We included six qualitative studies related to the included quantitative studies. In our meta-synthesis (n = 6 studies), we identified factors associated with intervention acceptability corresponding to six of the seven Theoretical Framework of Acceptability constructs. Completeness of intervention reporting was inadequate across studies.

CONCLUSION: Higher-quality RCTs with larger sample sizes, improved intervention reporting, and methodological rigor are needed to strengthen the evidence base for psychological interventions for people living with dementia or MCI, and their caregivers. Further research should explore intervention acceptability from the perspectives of key interest-holders.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42023400514.

articles.title: A Stearyl-Peptide Based Versatile Strategy to Design Enzyme-Responsive Liposomes for Targeted Drug Delivery.
articles.abstract: Liposomes are a prominent class of drug delivery nanoparticles. For currently approved liposomal therapeutics, drug is released predominantly via diffusion which has spatio-temporal kinetic and bioavailability challenges, especially in a dynamic environment. Next-generation liposome designs focus on stimuli-triggered enhancement of drug release. One exciting approach here is liposomes that can be site-specifically destabilized by disease-associated enzymes. Feasibility of this has been demonstrated with certain phospholipases or metalloproteases, but a versatile strategy for designing liposomes triggerable by any disease-specific enzyme remains lacking. We report a unique liposome design using enzyme-cleavable stearyl-peptide conjugates. Stearylamine has been explored for cationic liposomes in gene delivery, but the cationic charge poses significant cytotoxicity. We demonstrate that conjugating enzyme-cleavable peptides to stearylamine and assembly of stearyl-peptide conjugates within liposomes mitigates the cationic charge and significantly enhances biosafety. Surface-decorating such liposomes with target-specific ligands enables their active target-anchorage under flow. Exposure of target-anchored liposomes to disease-relevant enzymes renders stearyl-peptide cleavage and liposome destablization, enhancing drug release. We demonstrate the design versatility utilizing microfluidic models of three different vascular pathologies (hyperfibrinolysis, thrombosis and thromboinflammation) and delivering three corresponding drugs (tranexamic acid, tissue plasminogen activator and deoxyribonulease) triggered by three different enzymes (plasmin, thrombin and neutrophil elastase), respectively.

articles.title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus.
articles.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium-the primary site of viral entry and replication-remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo-relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

articles.title: Tracking Brucella abortus Infection in Immunized Mice Using In Vivo Bioluminescence Imaging.
articles.abstract: Brucella is the pathogen responsible for brucellosis, an important zoonotic illness, which affects humans and livestock worldwide. Currently, animal vaccination is used to prevent transmission of brucellosis from livestock to humans. The spread of luminous bacteria in laboratory animals can be monitored by bioluminescence imaging (BLI). In this study, therefore, we aim to develop an in vivo BLI strategy for assessing the immunogenicity of the brucellosis Rev1 vaccine, taking its benefits of shorter assay duration and reduced safety risks for the laboratory personnel. We have constructed a recombinant Brucella abortus 544 (BAPGH5) in which the firefly luciferase is expressed under the control of the PgroE promoter using the pPGH6-BSF22 plasmid. The parB locus was included in the plasmid to stabilize it in the absence of the antibiotic. The recombinant Brucella showed intense bioluminescence in vitro without using the antibiotic typically used for plasmid maintenance. It exhibited better growth compared to the parental strain. BAPGH5 showed strong bioluminescence in vivo when administered to mice intraperitoneally and colonized the mice spleens at a level comparable to that of the parental strain administered at the standard dose for the Rev1 vaccine immunogenicity testing. The recombinant Brucella isolated from the mice spleens showed strong bioluminescence, indicating in vivo stability of the pPGH6-BSF22 plasmid. The dissemination pattern of BAPGH5 in mice immunized with the Rev1 vaccine was clearly distinct from that of the control mice, as revealed by BLI. These results suggest the usefulness of the developed in vivo BLI strategy for assessing the immunogenicity of the Rev1 vaccine.

articles.title: Fractional Flow Reserve in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Review of the Current Literature.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Given the global prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD) and atherosclerosis, there is a critical need for accurate non-invasive diagnostic approaches. The current diagnostic procedures in the hospital are invasive, costly, and may pose potential risks to the patients. While computational fluid dynamics (CFD) based diagnostic approaches can have high accuracy, their extensive computational requirements render them impractical for local hospital use. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based methodologies for predicting fractional flow reserve (FFR) in coronary arteries with stenosis have gained attention for their nearly instantaneous and accurate results, holding significant potential for impacting healthcare outcomes. The objective of this study is to present the current uses of AI for non-invasive FFR computation and understand the current state of this technology, address current limitations and suggest potential directions for future research.

METHODS: This work provides a comprehensive review of AI-based approaches for the non-invasive measurement of the FFR. This research emphasizes key factors including the different possible algorithms, their inputs, the sample of patients, and statistical indexes such as accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of the predictions.

RESULTS: The reviewed literature shows that AI methodologies lead to low computational times and high accuracy values and, therefore, are promising alternatives for accurate FFR prediction in atherosclerotic coronary arteries. The accuracy of the results was highly linked to the inputs used in the algorithms, and there is no consensus as to the most relevant inputs. Despite the evident advantages, the widespread implementation of ML approaches in hospitals still faces challenges such as lack of data, image quality, and result interpretability and explainability.

CONCLUSION: AI emerges as a promising tool for non-invasive FFR computation, leading to high accuracy in CAD assessment. Addressing the identified challenges is crucial for enhancing diagnostic capabilities and patient care for CAD in hospitals.

articles.title: Achieving High Tuberculosis Treatment Completion Rates in a Student-Run Free Clinic Model: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading infectious cause of death globally. HAVEN Free Clinic is a student-run free clinic that provides TB screening and treatment.

OBJECTIVE: To assess the feasibility of a student-run free clinic model for TB screening and treatment as well as evaluate patient retention through the cascade of care.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study using electronic medical record data.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients who required TB screening between January 1, 2019, and February 1, 2025 (n = 742).

MAIN MEASURES: Data were collected on rates of retention at each step of screening, diagnosis, and treatment. Logistic regression was used to assess whether age, gender, treatment regimen, or distance from clinic were associated with treatment completion. For patients who completed treatment, the TST/IGRA interpreter tool TSTin4D was used to estimate risk reduction for developing TB disease and disability.

KEY RESULTS: Forty-eight of the patients initiated on treatment successfully completed it for a treatment completion rate of 87.3%. As estimated using the TSTin4D tool, treatment completion was associated with an average relative risk reduction of 80.7% for developing TB disease in the next 20 years and an average relative risk reduction of 68.7% for long-term disability and death from TB disease. Age, gender, treatment regimen, and distance to clinic were not associated with treatment completion.

CONCLUSIONS: A student-run free clinic model of TB screening and treatment is effective and has treatment completion rates exceeding standard benchmarks. Strengths of this model include focused scope and patient education. Opportunities for improvement include access to in-person interpreters and close follow-up with patients during their treatment course.

articles.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Detecting Reduced Left Ventricular Systolic Function: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess the diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) for detecting reduced left ventricular systolic function (LVSF) using visual qualitative assessment (VQA), E-point septal separation (EPSS), and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted assessment, compared with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE).

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 1, 1985, through July 8, 2025. Eligible studies compared POCUS-assessed LVSF with left ventricular ejection fraction measured by TTE (or cardiac MRI in one study). Data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis to determine the diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) and likelihood ratios (LR) for each of the three methods.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies, including 4,647 participants, met inclusion criteria. Nine studies evaluating VQA yielded a DOR of 40.53 (95% CI, 15.07 to 109.00; P < 0.001) and a positive LR (LR + ) of 6.90 (95% CI, 3.75 to 12.69). Seven studies evaluating EPSS resulted in a DOR of 21.77 (95% CI, 10.25 to 46.28; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 5.70 (95% CI, 2.89 to 11.22). Five studies evaluating AI-assisted POCUS resulted in a DOR of 47.35 (95% CI, 16.87 to 132.93; P < 0.001) and a LR + of 8.37 (95% CI, 4.40 to 15.93). Meta-regression analyses revealed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic performance among the three methods. Subgroup analysis by operator experience level also showed no statistically significant difference between novice and experienced operators for each method.

CONCLUSIONS: VQA, EPSS, and AI-assisted POCUS all demonstrate moderate-to-high diagnostic accuracy for identifying reduced LVSF, with no significant differences among methods on meta-regression or by operator experience level. Moderately strong LR + across all three methods supports the use of POCUS for ruling in reduced LVSF. EPSS cutoffs at the lower and upper ends of the reported range showed higher sensitivity and specificity, respectively, suggesting utility as a rule-in or rule-out tool where formal echocardiography is not readily available.

REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD42024626542.

articles.title: Differences in Patient Characteristics and Heart Failure Readmissions by Marital Status and Sex: A Case Study from a Single-Center Hospital in Northwest Georgia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) is a major cause of death in the USA and Georgia, with high annual readmission rates.

OBJECTIVE: To examine differences in 30-day HFR and length of stay (LOS) by marital status, adjusting for age and race.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of HF-related hospital discharges between February 1, 2023, and March 30, 2024, with a 30-day readmission follow-up.

PARTICIPANTS: 1122 adult patient discharges with HF, identified using diagnosis-related group and ICD-10 codes, were initially identified; 97 were subsequently excluded (2 missing sex data, 95 duplicate records), yielding an analytic cohort of 1025 categorized by sex and marital status.

MAIN MEASURES: All-cause hospital readmission within 30 days of discharge, total LOS, geographic status, tobacco risk, age, and race.

RESULTS: The HFR rate was 13.95% (143/1025). Observed married female patients had lower readmissions than expected prior to multiple-comparison correction (9 vs. 18.276, P = 0.030), and single females had significantly higher 30-day readmission than married females (15.07% vs. 6.87%; P = 0.016). In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age and race, all groups had significantly higher odds of readmission compared to married females (MM: aOR = 2.28, P = 0.046; SF: aOR = 2.36, P = 0.023; SM: aOR = 2.31, P = 0.027). A marital status by sex interaction model showed marriage was associated with significantly lower readmission odds among women (aOR = 0.42, P = 0.023) but not among men (aOR = 0.99, P = 0.964). LOS did not differ significantly by marital status or sex group.

CONCLUSIONS: Married females had the lowest readmission risk, suggesting a protective role of partner-based social support post-discharge. This protective association of marriage was significant among women but not men, suggesting a sex-specific effect. LOS did not differ by marital status or sex group, suggesting that inpatient care delivery may be less sensitive to sociodemographic factors than post-discharge outcomes. This underscores the need for better transitional care for patients without home support networks.

articles.title: Anti-Inflammatory and Antifibrotic Effects of Hyaluronidase Versus a Phosphodiesterase Type 4 Inhibitor in C57BL/6 Mice with Emphysema.
articles.journal: Bulletin of experimental biology and medicine
articles.abstract: Using a model of pulmonary emphysema induced by LPS and cigarette smoke extract, the effects of hyaluronidase (HYAL) were compared with those of the phosphodiesterase type 4 (PDE4) inhibitor roflumilast. Roflumilast (5 mg/kg) reduced inflammation and collagen deposition in peribronchial zones without affecting emphysematous changes. HYAL at a dose of 16 IU/mouse increased inflammatory infiltration in the upper and lower lung regions, leading to the degradation of perivascular and peribronchial collagen and elastin in the middle and lower lung regions and exacerbating emphysema and vascular hyperemia. HYAL at a dose of 8 IU/mouse reduced inflammation in the lungs, limited fibrotic remodeling of the parenchyma, bronchi, and vessels by reducing the area of elastin and collagen fibers, and prevented the destruction of interalveolar septa. Thus, the administration of HYAL in low doses is a promising strategy for combating peribronchial and perivascular deposition of fibrotic masses in pulmonary emphysema. These results may serve as a basis for developing therapies against fibrosis in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and pulmonary emphysema.

articles.title: An appraisal of the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition clinical practice guidelines.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Clinical practice guidelines produced by the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (NASPGHAN) guide clinical decision-making across pediatric gastroenterology in North America, yet their methodological quality has not been systematically evaluated. We aimed to assess the quality of NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines using the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research & Evaluation II (AGREE-II) instrument.

METHODS: We identified 11 NASPGHAN clinical practice guidelines published between 2005 and 2024. Each guideline was independently appraised by ≥4 reviewers using the AGREE-II tool, which evaluates six domains across 23 items on a 1-7 scale. Scaled domain scores were calculated according to the AGREE-II rubric. To assess reproducibility, domain-specific and pooled intraclass correlation coefficients were estimated using linear mixed-effects models with crossed random effects for raters and items.

RESULTS: Domain scores varied substantially across guidelines. Scope and Purpose (mean 83.8%, SD 7.6) and Clarity of Presentation (mean 80.4%, SD 9.9) received the highest ratings, reflecting clear objectives, defined target populations, and well-structured recommendations. Stakeholder Involvement (mean 58.1%, SD 7.8) and Applicability (mean 53.6%, SD 5.1) scored lowest, indicating limited reporting of patient or caregiver engagement, implementation tools, barriers, or resource implications. Inter-rater reliability ranged from poor to moderate across AGREE-II domains, consistent with the subjectivity inherent in AGREE II scoring and variability in guideline reporting detail.

CONCLUSIONS: NASPGHAN guidelines demonstrate strengths in defining scope and presenting recommendations clearly. Opportunities for improvement include greater stakeholder involvement, enhanced transparency in guideline development methodology and conflict-of-interest reporting, and clearer guidance on implementation and resource considerations.

articles.title: VCon-Net: A Cerebral Artery Segmentation Network with Enhanced Topological Connectivity.
articles.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
articles.abstract: Precise segmentation of cerebral artery from computed tomography angiography serves as a fundamental prerequisite for the clinical evaluation and morphological analysis of cerebrovascular diseases, particularly stroke. However, oversegmentation and undersegmentation routinely compromise topological connectivity and accuracy. This study aims to develop a novel deep learning network to mitigate these challenges, enhancing topological connectivity and accuracy. To enforce topological connectivity, we propose a novel skeleton points distance loss that combines skeleton points with a 3D Euclidean distance field to penalize oversegmentation and undersegmentation via interskeleton point distance constraints. Built upon the U-Net architecture, VCon-Net integrates an axialdynamic convolution module and a multiattention mechanism to enhance the perception of slender arteries and capture spatial-channel-temporal features. A total of 202 cases were included in this study, with 141 cases utilized for model development, 35 for independent testing and performance evaluation, and the remaining 26 analyzed as special clinical cases. On the independent test set, VCon-Net achieved a Dice of 0.8552, a Jaccard of 0.7513, a precision of 0.8568, a sensitivity of 0.8645, with HD95 reduced to 3.16 mm, and β0 error reduced to 2.85. Compared with existing segmentation methods, the proposed framework yields favorable performance. VCon-Net achieves cerebral artery segmentation with enhanced topological connectivity, providing a reliable morphological foundation, which offers an essential morphology basis for downstream clinical evaluations.

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist use is associated with higher severity of acute pancreatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are widely used for obesity, type 2 diabetes, and MASLD. Although an association with pancreatitis has been reported, the clinical features, severity, and course of acute pancreatitis in patients receiving GLP-1RA therapy remain poorly characterized. We aimed to compare pancreatitis severity and outcomes in patients with and without GLP-1RA exposure.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients admitted with acute pancreatitis from March 2017 to August 2024. Patients were stratified by GLP-1RA exposure for at least 3 months prior to diagnosis. The primary outcome was disease severity measured by the Bedside Index for Severity in Acute Pancreatitis (BISAP). Secondary outcomes included liver biochemical abnormalities (AST, ALT, ALP, bilirubin), imaging findings, clinical complications, length of stay, and post-pancreatitis sequelae. An exploratory analysis compared biliary pathology (gallstones, choledocholithiasis, or biliary sludge) between GLP-1RA users with antecedent weight loss and patients with prior bariatric surgery.

RESULTS: Among 149 patients, 49 (32.9%) were receiving a GLP-1RA. In adjusted analysis, GLP-1RA use was independently associated with a BISAP score ≥ 2 (OR 5.25, 95% CI 1.13-24.34, p = 0.034), and increasing age was also associated with higher severity (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.12, p = 0.001). GLP-1RA users had higher rates of pancreatitis-associated ascites but lower rates of new-onset diabetes and exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, with no significant differences in other clinical outcomes. GLP-1RA users exhibited greater antecedent weight loss (p < 0.001), but biliary pathology did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1RA use was associated with higher predicted severity of pancreatitis at presentation, reflected by a greater probability of a BISAP score ≥ 2, without a corresponding increase in post-pancreatitis complications. Nearly, half of GLP-1RA users developed pancreatitis within 1 year of therapy initiation. Most experienced antecedent weight loss, raising concern for a biliary contribution, although biliary pathology was observed both with the gallbladder in situ and after prior cholecystectomy.

articles.title: Fetal hemoglobin fraction: a potential predictor of late-onset sepsis in very preterm infants.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Late onset sepsis (LOS) is included between the so-called oxidative stress-related diseases in preterm infants. Increasing evidence supports a protective role of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) against oxidative stress. We hypothesized that HbF blood fractions measured during the first weeks of life may be associated with the risk of developing LOS. We carried out a retrospective observational study on 166 preterm infants with gestational age <30 weeks. The primary endpoint of our study was the comparison of HbF fraction values between infants who developed LOS and those who did not during the first week of life. Fifty-six (34%) infants had LOS at the mean age of 14±8 and 22±15 days of life. Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life (HbF14) to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF14 decreased (OR 0.974, 95% CI 0.956-0.992; P=0.004) the risk of LOS. In ROC analysis, HbF14 showed moderate discriminative ability in predicting LOS, with an AUC of 0.676 and 95% CI 0.593-0.758.

CONCLUSION: Lower HbF fractions during the first weeks of life were associated with an increased risk of LOS, with HbF14 emerging as an independent protective factor. These findings confirm the role of HbF in modulating susceptibility to oxidative stress-related complications in this vulnerable population and the importance of maintaining its levels high.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Low fetal hemoglobin (HbF) fractions are associated with increased risk of oxidative stress-related complications of prematurity. Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is included among oxidative stress-related diseases.

WHAT IS NEW: • Infants with LOS had lower HbF fractions from the 14th day of life to 36 weeks of postmenstrual age. Regression analysis showed that higher HbF fraction at 14 days of life is associated with decreased risk of LOS.

articles.title: Access to systemic anti-cancer treatment in mesothelioma: a systematic review of inequities in treatment access and decision-making.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesise evidence on factors influencing access to and uptake of systemic anti-cancer treatment (SACT) for people with mesothelioma, an incurable cancer, with a focus on inequities in treatment pathways and decision-making within supportive oncology care.

METHODS: An integrative systematic review with narrative synthesis (PROSPERO: 603309) was conducted. APA PsycInfo, ASSIA, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PubMed Central, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for English-language publications between 1 January 2008 and 18 October 2024. Eligible studies included empirical research and reproducible reviews reporting factors affecting access to or receipt of SACT among individuals with mesothelioma.

RESULTS: The search yielded 716 records, of which 18 met inclusion criteria. Four interrelated themes were identified: (1) demographic characteristics; (2) information provision and decision-making; (3) clinical and disease-related factors; and (4) healthcare system and structural factors. An overarching theme of intersectionality demonstrated how social, clinical and organisational influences interact to shape treatment access and decision-making.

CONCLUSION: Access to and uptake of SACT in mesothelioma is shaped by complex, interacting patient- and system-level factors, resulting in persistent inequities in treatment pathways. As SACT is typically delivered with palliative intent in this population, these findings highlight its role within supportive oncology care and the importance of equitable access, shared decision-making and consistent information provision across services.

articles.title: European LeukemiaNet clinical signs and symptoms as prognostic markers in polycythemia vera during ruxolitinib.
articles.abstract: European LeukemiaNet defines the clinical signs and symptoms (CSSs) of polycythemia vera (PV) as progressive splenomegaly, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, inadequate hematocrit control, and cardiovascular risk factors. In PV patients receiving hydroxyurea, CSSs indicate a phenotype with higher thrombosis risk across the standard risk categories. However, the prognostic value of CSSs for thrombosis or progression to secondary myelofibrosis (SMF) or acute leukemia (AL) during second-line ruxolitinib therapy remains unknown. We assessed the incidence rate ratios (IRRs) of thrombosis and disease progression during ruxolitinib treatment, and the prognostic impact of CSSs at treatment initiation, in 254 PV patients from the PV-ARC multicenter cohort. CSSs were identified in 50.4% of patients, with similar proportions in low- and high-risk groups (50% vs 50.5%). The IRRs for thrombosis and progression to SMF/AL were 1.0 and 4.2 %p‑y, respectively. Conventional thrombotic risk categories did not predict thrombosis or progression. In contrast, CSSs were associated with higher IRRs of both thrombosis (1.8 vs 0 %p‑y, p = 0.05) and progression (6.0 vs 2.3 %p‑y, p = 0.02). Persistent or progressive leukocytosis was the strongest predictor of disease progression. In conclusion, CSSs refine conventional risk stratification by improving prediction of thrombosis and disease progression during ruxolitinib, supporting their integration into routine clinical assessment.

articles.title: Correction: A comparison of health-related quality of life between continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis and automated peritoneal dialysis in children with stage 5 chronic kidney disease in Thailand: a randomized controlled trial.
Kidney phenotype and clinical course in children with AMN-related Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome: a multicenter cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney manifestations of Imerslund-Gräsbeck syndrome (IGS) caused by pathogenic AMN variants remain poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the kidney phenotype and clinical course in children with AMN-related IGS presenting with proteinuria.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort included nine children with homozygous pathogenic AMN variants followed at six pediatric nephrology centers in Turkey. Initial presentations occurred between 2009 and 2024; clinical, laboratory, genetic, and follow-up data were reviewed.

RESULTS: Median age at diagnosis was 41 months (range, 4-97), and median follow-up was 30 months (range, 12-171). Five patients presented with vitamin B12 deficiency-related manifestations, three with isolated urinary abnormalities, and one through family screening. Persistent subnephrotic-range proteinuria was present in all patients; median uPCR was 1.2 mg/mg at admission and 0.88 mg/mg at last follow-up. One patient had a 25% eGFR decline from 144 to 108 mL/min/1.73 m², but final eGFR remained >90 mL/min/1.73 m² in all patients. No patient developed stage 2 or more advanced CKD, nephrotic syndrome, or required kidney replacement therapy. Six patients received RAS inhibitors; changes in uPCR were heterogeneous, and treatment efficacy could not be determined. Eight patients carried homozygous c.208-2 A > G, whereas one harbored the novel c.354 G > A (p.Trp118*) variant.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter cohort of children with AMN-related IGS presenting with proteinuria, persistent subnephrotic-range proteinuria was accompanied by generally preserved kidney function during the observed follow-up. Early genetic diagnosis may help avoid unnecessary kidney biopsy and inappropriate immunosuppressive treatment.

articles.title: Imaging for localizing and therapeutic management of primary aldosteronism: the primary aldosteronism imaging outcome consensus.
articles.abstract: This Consensus Statement (the primary aldosteronism imaging outcome (PAIO) consensus) from an international, multidisciplinary team of experts offers evidence-based graded consensus recommendations and key summary points for clinical practice on the use of conventional and molecular imaging in the diagnosis and therapeutic management of primary aldosteronism. We review the evolving role of these imaging techniques and offer practical recommendations for clinical management. The following predefined clinical questions relevant to the management of primary aldosteronism were addressed: (1) What radiological parameters define normal versus altered adrenal morphology in primary aldosteronism? (2) What imaging morphological abnormalities are observed in the different subtypes of primary aldosteronism (lateralized and non-lateralized primary aldosteronism)? (3) How reliable are features detectable by CT, MRI and molecular imaging for predicting biochemical remission following unilateral adrenalectomy? Among other key topics, these recommendations address CT-, MRI- and molecular imaging-based approaches to guide patient selection for unilateral adrenalectomy in primary aldosteronism.

articles.title: Microbial targeting of inhibitory immune receptors in human disease.
articles.abstract: Host cells express many types of immune receptors to detect microbes, mount immune responses and prevent infection. This includes pattern recognition receptors, activating receptors and inhibitory receptors. These receptors exert an evolutionary pressure for microbes to evade the host immune response. Indeed, many microbial pathogens evade host immune receptors by 'hiding' antigenic molecules or by producing molecules that antagonize activating immune receptors or their signalling components. There is also emerging evidence that microbes from all kingdoms produce molecules that can interact with and agonize inhibitory immune receptors.
