Microbial targeting of inhibitory immune receptors can promote cell entry, interfere with innate immune responses and subvert adaptive immune responses, essentially providing opportunities for microbial survival and for disease pathogenesis. Here, we review the mechanisms that human-infecting microbes use to target inhibitory immune receptors, the functional consequences of these interactions and the potential of targeting these host-pathogen interactions in disease.

articles.title: Measles is back in the US: what worries scientists.
Risk factors for congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT) are a leading cause of pediatric renal failure. This study evaluated risk factors and assessed their robustness.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus searches yielded 33 studies (24 case-control, 9 cohort). Frequentist and Bayesian random-effects meta-analyses estimated associations between CAKUT and maternal/neonatal risks.

RESULTS: Frequentist analysis identified increased risk for pre-pregnancy BMI 25.0-29.9 (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.06-1.45), ≥30 (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.51), and ≥25 kg/m² (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.11-1.37). Maternal age <20 years was protective (OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51-0.73). Other predictors included family history of CAKUT/kidney disease, maternal diabetes subtypes (type 1, type 2, pre-gestational, and gestational diabetes), preterm birth (OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.25-2.03), small-for-gestational-age (SGA), and large-for-gestational-age (LGA). Bayesian analysis validated most factors. Although 95% CrIs crossed unity for BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m², BMI ≥ 30 kg/m², T2DM, SGA, LGA, alcohol consumption, RASi use, and hypertension, their posterior distributions were predominantly above 1. High BMI, family history, and diabetes remained robust in high-quality subsets.

CONCLUSIONS: Confirming established risks and identifying novel associations, these findings identify maternal metabolic factors as consistent correlates of CAKUT and support their evaluation as potentially modifiable targets.

IMPACT: Current meta-analyses lack synthesis on novel CAKUT determinants (maternal exposures, comorbidities, gestational weight gain, extreme fetal weight) and Bayesian approaches, which are essential to robustly address heterogeneity in sparse data. Our frequentist analysis confirmed established risks and identified novel associations: family history, SGA, LGA, and type 1 and 2 diabetes. Bayesian meta-analysis supported the main findings and showed posterior probabilities that OR > 1 of ≥90% for BMI subgroups, T2DM, RASi use, and hypertension. Maternal metabolic factors are consistently associated with CAKUT and represent potentially modifiable targets that warrant evaluation in future prospective and interventional studies.

articles.title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer.
articles.abstract: Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

articles.title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict.
articles.abstract: Humanitarian emergencies test the resilience of global health systems, yet policy is constrained by limited empirical evidence on the magnitude and timing of service delivery disruptions. Here, we assess the association between measured childhood vaccination-as a proxy for health service delivery-and forced displacement, armed conflict, and natural disasters. Across 193 countries from 2000 to 2023, sudden increases in displaced populations were associated with declines in vaccination coverage of approximately 3 to 6 percentage points, persisting for 2 to 3 years before recovery. Dose-response analyses revealed a nonlinear relationship: coverage fell steeply at low displacement levels and plateaued at extreme exposure. Conflict intensity followed a similar nonlinear pattern that plateaued near 3000 annual battle-related deaths while mortality from natural disasters showed no detectable association with coverage. Displacement's association was largely independent of armed conflict, indicating that displacement may act as a distinct, additive shock rather than a proxy for violence.

articles.title: Dietary interventions and stroke clinical outcomes: a systematic review.
articles.journal: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal nutrition is biologically essential for supporting neural repair mechanisms post-stroke, yet clinical guidelines provide limited and non-specific dietary recommendations that are largely extrapolated from primary cardiovascular prevention rather than stroke recovery populations.

AIMS: To systematically review and synthesise evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of food-based or whole-diet interventions on clinical outcomes in adults with stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA), including disability, neurological function, cognition, mood, quality of life, and stroke recurrence.

SUMMARY OF REVIEW: Following Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, four databases (Medline, Embase, CINAHL, CENTRAL) were searched to February 2026 for RCTs testing oral dietary interventions (≥4 weeks) in adult stroke/TIA survivors. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Eight RCTs (n=15,974) were included (1 low risk, 6 some concerns, 1 high risk). Quantitative meta-analysis was precluded by marked heterogeneity. Interventions included salt substitution (n=2), Mediterranean diets (n=2), ketogenic diet (n=1), partial meal replacement (n=1), Trigona honey (n=1), and soy milk (n=1). Reduced-sodium salt substitution decreased stroke recurrence (RR 0.86, 95%CI 0.77-0.95) and mortality (RR 0.88, 95%CI 0.82-0.96) in large Phase III trials, while Mediterranean diets improved quality of life (EQ-5D mean difference: 10.1, 95%CI 1.8-18.4). For functional recovery, small Phase I/II pilot trials yielded exploratory, domain-specific proof-of-concept signals (e.g., post-exercise soymilk enhancing walking performance; Trigona honey improving MoCA scores), but were constrained by high susceptibility to Type I errors and effect size overestimation. Ketogenic diet improved NIHSS (5±2 vs 7±2, p<0.01) and disability (mRS: 2±1 vs 3±1, p<0.05), but was accompanied by high adverse event rates (keto-flu 25%, GI distress 15%, hyperlipidemia 10%).

CONCLUSIONS: Salt substitution and Mediterranean diets show clear promise for secondary prevention and recovery. Given the limited and heterogeneous evidence base, high-quality, phase-specific RCTs are urgently needed to establish stroke-specific nutrition strategies.

articles.title: Two International Delphi Surveys on Labels and Descriptors to Inform the New Classification Criteria for Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritides.
authors: Paediatric Rheumatology INternational Trials Organisation (PRINTO) and the Pediatric Rheumatology Collaborative Study Group (PRCSG)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Developing an evidence-based classification of the group of juvenile idiopathic arthritides (JIA) is a topic of high relevance. A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among paediatric rheumatologists to identify the most appropriate names (labels) and the most relevant descriptors used by physicians to define JIA categories.

METHODS: In Delphi 1, participants reported with open-ended responses the descriptors they used to identify JIA categories, and whether and how, these categories should be re-labeled. In Delphi 2, respondents ranked the top three disease labels and the top ten disease descriptors that emerged from Delphi 1 from best to worst for each JIA category; a weighted score was calculated multiplying the sum of ranks for the selection frequency.

RESULTS: Overall, 330 and 470 physicians responded to Delphi 1 and Delphi 2, respectively. The highest-ranking labels and descriptors were: "juvenile-onset Still's disease" and response to interleukin-1 inhibitors for systemic arthritis, "rheumatoid factor (RF) or anti-cyclic citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPA) positive JIA" and RF/ACPA positivity for RF-positive polyarthritis; "polyarticular JIA" and age at onset <18 years for RF-negative polyarthritis; "juvenile psoriatic arthritis" and dactylitis for psoriatic arthritis; "early-onset spondyloarthritis" and HLA-B27 positivity for enthesitis-related arthritis, "oligoarticular JIA" and antinuclear antibodies (ANA) positivity for oligoarthritis, "early-onset ANA positive arthritis" and ANA positivity with RF negativity for early-onset ANA-positive arthritis; and "undifferentiated JIA" and arthritis fitting more than one category for undifferentiated arthritis.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the category labels and descriptors to be prioritised in the future development of the new JIA classification criteria.

articles.title: Brain organoid technology, gene editing, and high-throughput screening.
articles.abstract: This review aims to summarize recent progress in brain organoid technology for research into neural regeneration, focusing on its theoretical foundations, technical development, translational challenges, and future directions. Brain organoids are three-dimensional biomimetic in vitro models that capture some key features of neural development and pathology. They provide platforms for investigating brain tissue organization and the molecular and cellular processes underlying neural regeneration. Their potential applications include studying disease mechanisms and brain injury, testing neurotoxicity, and screening drugs for neurological disorders. Organoids may also inform research on tissue repair and transplantation, although their clinical applications remain under investigation. This review examines current approaches to generating and improving brain organoids, as well as the technical, ethical, and regulatory issues that may affect their use and translation. Key limitations include incomplete maturation and vascularization, the absence of important immune components, and variation between models arising from limited standardization. Future research could explore guided culture and assembly, high-throughput screening, and bioprinting to improve model performance. Multi-omics approaches may also help characterize organoids and support efforts to strengthen standardization. In addition, combining organoid platforms with gene-editing techniques may offer further opportunities for studying disease mechanisms. This review identifies research priorities and discusses how more accurate models, rigorous quality control, and appropriate oversight may support the further development of brain organoids for neural regeneration research.

articles.title: Review Article: Cirrhosis Recompensation- Definition, Natural History, Clinical Implications and Considerations for Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Decompensated cirrhosis has traditionally been considered irreversible. However, evidence shows that patients who achieve control or cure of the underlying liver disease aetiology can experience substantial clinical improvement, termed 'cirrhosis recompensation', formally defined by Baveno VII and further modified during Baveno VIII. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the pathophysiology, predictors, aetiology-specific outcomes, clinical implications and trial design considerations relevant to recompensation.

METHODS: We conducted a narrative review synthesizing data across six domains: pathophysiology of decompensation and recompensation; predictors of recompensation; prevalence and prognostic impact by aetiology; unresolved controversies in definition; clinical implications, including medication de-escalation, transplant delisting and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance; and methodological considerations for clinical trial design.

RESULTS: Recompensation occurs in an estimated 35% of patients with decompensated cirrhosis and is associated with reduced liver-related mortality, though rates vary substantially by aetiology. Proposed mechanisms include reduced portal pressure, restored gut barrier integrity and possible fibrosis regression. Despite improved outcomes, HCC risk and, in some patients, portal hypertension persist, warranting ongoing surveillance. Some aspects of the definition remain unresolved, including uncertain applicability to etiologies lacking a clear curative therapy. As a trial endpoint, recompensation is clinically meaningful and sufficiently prevalent, though it requires appropriate handling of competing risks and consideration of multi-state modelling and outcome-ranking approaches.

CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhosis recompensation represents a paradigm shift in the understanding and management of decompensated liver disease. Future work should focus on validating recompensation criteria across diverse etiologies, clarifying underlying mechanisms and durability and establishing standardized methodological frameworks for incorporating recompensation into clinical trial design.

articles.title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Unravelling paediatric abdominal tuberculosis in a tuberculosis endemic country: diagnostic pathways and outcomes from a prospective cohort study.
Health service delivery for children with congenital limb differences: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of hand therapy : official journal of the American Society of Hand Therapists
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Health service delivery pathways for children with congenital hand and upper limb differences (CLD) are heterogeneous, with access to specialized pediatric hand therapy influenced by geographic location, resource availability, and broader healthcare system structures.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to describe and evaluate health service delivery for children with CLD, illustrated through the service pathway for camptodactyly from diagnosis through specialized clinics and hand therapy follow-up for contracture management.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort design.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted of children with camptodactyly (0-18 years) and were assessed by specialists at the [de-identified] clinic, over a 11-year period. Demographic, follow-up and no-show history, and location of primary residence data were extracted. Geographical distance between primary residence, specialist upper limb clinic, and community rehabilitation centres were mapped. Descriptive statistics and Fisher's Exact Test were conducted to describe the population and evaluate impacts of geographical distance and health services outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 110 children with camptodactyly were included (50.9% female), 72 (65.5%) had isolated camptodactyly and 38 (34.5%) had arthrogryposis. The average travel distance to the specialist clinic was 34.5 ± 22.7 km for participants living in the Greater Toronto Area and 324.7 ± 370.9 km for those outside the catchment area. Loss to follow-up was significantly higher among participants outside the catchment area (p=.03). Mapping of referrals indicate that children rehabilitation centres are geographically strategic, suggesting potential partnerships.

CONCLUSION: Children with CLD from outside the hand specialist catchment area travelled substantially greater distances and had higher odds of being lost to follow-up, highlighting geographic disparities in care continuity. Strengthening partnerships between tertiary centers and community pediatric rehabilitation centres, developing and expanding pediatric hand therapy resources, and leveraging virtual care models may help reduce travel burden and improve equitable access to health services for children with CLD.

articles.title: Intraoperative use of closed-loop continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion systems during bariatric surgery.
articles.abstract: Obesity associated with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) is becoming increasingly prevalent. Bariatric surgery may be indicated for its treatment. The incidence of acute complications in these patients is high, and instability in glycaemic profiles often requires intravenous insulin therapy during surgery. The use of closed-loop insulin delivery systems for the management of T1DM has increased in recent years. There is limited information regarding their use during surgery, particularly in bariatric procedures. We present the results of two patients using closed-loop systems who underwent Roux-en-Y gastric bypass between 2022 and 2023, without discontinuation of the system during the intervention. Both patients demonstrated well-controlled mean blood glucose levels (142 and 147 mg/dL, respectively), with no hypoglycaemic events observed during the procedure. Further studies are needed to establish protocols in this area.

articles.title: Wear time matters: optimising wearables for clinically aligned and personalised health monitoring.
articles.abstract: Wearable devices hold transformative potential for healthcare, yet their clinical impact is undermined by suboptimal long-term adherence. Although 24/7 always-on monitoring remains the default for maximising data completeness, achieving sustained wear could be limited by discomfort, inconvenience, or perceived lack of relevance, particularly during longitudinal monitoring. The clinical utility of wearables also depends on intelligent systems that filter, contextualise, and prioritise the resulting data into timely and actionable insights for individuals and clinicians. In this Viewpoint, we reframe wear time as a strategic design opportunity rather than a technical requirement. We provide illustrative examples of varying wear time requirements across clinical contexts: for instance, continuous monitoring is valuable for detecting intermittent episodes of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, whereas periodic blood pressure monitoring may be appropriate for managing stable hypertension. Our systemic analysis identified nine interconnected dimensions influencing wear time adherence, spanning clinical contexts, human factors, and technological reliability. Building on these insights, we propose a strategic implementation framework grounded in human-centred design, adaptive precision, and intelligent engagement. By aligning wear time strategies with specific clinical contexts and individual characteristics, wearables can evolve from passive data collectors into personalised health companions that balance clinical precision with real-world usability, fostering sustainable adherence and clinically meaningful insights.

articles.title: Inter-/Intra-Reader Variability in Ultrasound Measurement of Skin-to-Liver Capsule Distance and Hepato-Renal Index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), if untreated, results in cirrhosis. Skin-to-liver capsule distance (SCD) and hepato-renal index (HRI) are ultrasound-derived biomarkers used in the quantitative assessment of hepatic steatosis, but manual measurements introduce operator variability. This study quantified inter- and intra-reader variability in SCD and HRI among patients with cirrhosis and assessed whether measurement precision differed by disease etiology.

METHODS: A total of 1825 ultrasound examinations from 560 adults with cirrhosis were retrospectively identified. SCD and HRI reproducibility coefficients (RDC) were quantified between two independent readers; repeatability coefficients (RC) were quantified for repeated measurements by a single reader with a ≥28-d washout period. Precision was compared among MASLD, alcohol-related liver disease, metabolic dysfunction and alcohol-associated liver disease and chronic hepatitis C virus subgroups using one-way ANOVA with pairwise t-tests and false discovery rate (FDR) correction (p ≤ 0.05).

RESULTS: A total of 1616 images were evaluable for SCD and 1065 for HRI. Median SCD was 21.2 mm and 20.8 mm; median HRI was 1.11 and 1.14, for Reader 1 and Reader 2, respectively. RDCs were 19.9% (SCD) and 55.8% (HRI) and RCs were 19.7% (SCD) and 52.2% (HRI). Neither SCD nor HRI reproducibility differed by etiology. HRI showed overall inter-reader variability differences (p = 0.023), but no pairwise comparison remained significant after FDR correction.

CONCLUSION: SCD was repeatable and reproducible, supporting its viability as a quantitative ultrasound biomarker in the assessment of hepatic steatosis. HRI was imprecise, limiting its utility as a standalone metric. Measurement precision did not significantly differ among etiologies of cirrhosis.

articles.title: Prediction-aided tapering in rheumatoid arthritis patients treated with biOlogicals (PATIO): a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate whether prediction-aided tapering of biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (bDMARDs) reduces flare occurrence compared with disease activity-guided dose optimisation (DGDO) in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and sustained low disease activity.

METHODS: Prediction-aided tapering in rheumatoid arthritis patients treated with biOlogicals was a pragmatic, multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled superiority trial. Patients with RA receiving stable bDMARD therapy with stable-controlled disease, eligible for tapering, were randomised 1:1 to DGDO alone or DGDO supported by a previously validated dynamic prediction model estimating 3-monthly flare risk. Follow-up was 18 months. The primary outcome was the flare rate per patient. Secondary outcomes included any flare, major flares (> 12 weeks), disease activity score using 28 joint counts-C-reactive protein (DAS28-CRP) over time, mean bDMARD dose fraction, infections, and patient-reported outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 162 patients were included (81 per group). Over 18 months, the mean number of flares per patient was 1.00 (95% CI, 0.73-1.27) in the prediction-aided group and 0.73 (95% CI, 0.51-0.95) in the DGDO group (rate ratio, 1.32; 95% CI, 0.90-1.95). Any flare occurred in 57% of prediction-aided and 44% of DGDO patients, and major flares in 22% and 15%, respectively. DAS28-CRP trajectories, mean bDMARD dose reduction, patient-reported outcomes, and infection rates were similar between strategies. Nonadherence to tapering advice occurred in 23% of visits: 72% of these regarded advices to continue tapering, and 28% regarded advice to stop tapering or escalate medication.

CONCLUSIONS: Prediction-aided bDMARD tapering using this model did not improve flare rates or medication use. Prediction models require sufficient and robust accuracy and prospective evaluation before implementation.

articles.title: Liposuction as a single stage for cross leg flap debulking with the use of harvested fat for improving donor site aesthetics.
articles.journal: Annales de chirurgie plastique et esthetique
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cross-leg flap remains a reliable reconstructive option for dorsal foot defects, particularly in resource-limited settings. However, flap bulkiness and donor site scarring have a significant functional and aesthetic challenges. This study evaluates the effectiveness of liposuction debulking combined with simultaneous autologous fat grafting to improve both flap contour and donor site appearance in a single-stage procedure.

METHODS: A prospective uncontrolled study included 30 patients with prior cross-leg flap reconstruction presenting with bulky flaps and unsatisfactory donor site scars. Suction-assisted liposuction debulking was performed, followed by excision of redundant skin. Harvested fat was processed into microfat and injected into the donor site scar. Outcomes were assessed by measuring foot circumference reduction and evaluating scar quality using the Vancouver Scar Scale (VSS). Follow-up ranged from 5 to 12 months.

RESULTS: The mean patient age was 9.5±3.2 years. Liposuction was performed between 3 months and 6 years after flap inset. The mean aspirated fat volume was 117.06±12.64cm3. Foot circumference showed a significant reduction (mean 32.1±3.66%, P<0.001). All cases healed uneventfully with no flap compromise, infection, or functional impairment. Donor site scar quality improved significantly, with VSS scores decreasing from 4-7 preoperatively to 1-3 postoperatively.

CONCLUSIONS: Liposuction is a safe and effective method for cross-leg flap debulking as early as 3 months postoperatively. Simultaneous use of harvested fat for microfat grafting enhances donor site aesthetics, offering a single-stage solution that improves outcomes and reduces surgical burden.

articles.title: Abdominal body-contouring surgery: Multivariate analysis of complication risk factors and development of a predictive score in 1,308 patients.
articles.journal: Annales de chirurgie plastique et esthetique
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal contouring surgeries are common but carry a risk of complications. This study aims to analyze risk factors and develop a multivariate preoperative prediction score.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study involved 1,308 procedures performed between January 2015 and May 2023 at the Rennes University Hospital Center, France. Patients who underwent abdominoplasty, fleur-de-lys abdominoplasty, lower body lift, or fleur-de-lys lower body lift were included. Risk factors for complications were analyzed using logistic regression. A preoperative risk score was developed and validated based on a test group.

RESULTS: Among the 1,308 patients, the majority were women (94%) with an average body mass index (BMI) of 28.0kg/m2. The procedures included 62.1% (n=812) standard abdominoplasties, 6.5% (n=85) fleur-de-lys abdominoplasties, 24.8% (n=325) lower body lifts, and 6.6% (n=86) fleur-de-lys lower body lifts. Complications were recorded in 29.2% of cases, including wound dehiscence (22.6%), hematoma (6.3%), fat necrosis (3.4%), infection (2.1%), skin necrosis (0.9%), seroma (0.6%) and pulmonary embolism (0.3%). Significant risk factors identified through multivariate regression were diabetes, BMI, sex, and the type of surgery (fleur-de-lys/horizontal body lift). A complication prediction score was developed based on the identified risk factors, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.639.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results in a robust series confirm that BMI, diabetes, and the type of surgery (fleur-de-lys/horizontal body lift) are significant risk factors for postoperative complications. The developed risk score may serve as a useful tool to guide surgical decisions and inform patients about the associated risks.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Blood pressure and adverse cardiovascular events and death in patients receiving hemodialysis: A nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the high risk of cardiovascular disease in patients with end-stage kidney disease, the optimal blood pressure (BP) remains unclear. We aimed to explore the association between pre-dialysis systolic BP (SBP) and cardiovascular outcomes.

METHODS: Data from patients in the Korean National Periodic Hemodialysis Quality Assessment Program were used. Participants were categorized into five groups according to mean pre-dialysis SBP during the assessment period. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), a composite of non-fatal myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure, or all-cause death.

RESULTS: In total, data from 39,974 patients were included. During 221,634 person-years of follow-up (median of 5.6 years), MACCE occurred in 25,135 patients (62.9%). In the multivariable Cox proportional hazards model, hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for MACCE were 0.93 (0.87-1.00), 1.06 (1.01-1.11), 1.12 (1.06-1.17), and 1.22 (1.17-1.28) for the <120, 130-139, 140-149, and ≥150 mmHg groups, respectively, compared with the 120-129 mmHg group. Each SBP 10 mmHg-increase was associated with a 1.06-fold higher risk of MACCE. In an exploratory analysis, the association between pre-dialysis SBP and MACCE differed across quartiles of intradialytic weight loss (IDWL, %), being more pronounced at higher IDWL.

CONCLUSIONS: Pre-dialysis SBP was linearly associated with the risk of MACCE after adjusting for individual IDWL. In the exploratory analysis, the magnitude of this association differed according to IDWL, suggesting that pre-dialysis SBP may need to be interpreted together with the fluid removed at each session.

articles.title: Real-world adherence to ERS/ATS recommendations for non-invasive ventilation in exacerbations of COPD: A prospective multicenter Italian cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is recommended for exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (ECOPD) complicated by respiratory acidosis, yet real-world adherence remains uncertain. We evaluated adherence to ERS/ATS recommendations, patterns of non-adherence, and their association with short-term outcomes.

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter cohort study, consecutive patients with ECOPD-related acute hypoxemic-hypercapnic respiratory failure were enrolled across nine Italian hospitals and classified as guideline-adherent, NIV underuse, or NIV overuse according to ERS/ATS pH-based recommendations. The primary objective was to assess adherence to recommendations; the association between adherence patterns and the composite outcome of in-hospital death or endotracheal intubation was a secondary objective.

RESULTS: Among 456 patients, 315 (69%) were guideline-adherent, 60 (13%) had NIV underuse, and 81 (18%) had NIV overuse. Underuse occurred predominantly in patients with mild respiratory acidosis receiving alternative respiratory support, mainly high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), whereas overuse occurred primarily in hypercapnic patients without respiratory acidosis. The composite clinical outcome occurred in 48 patients (11%) and did not differ across adherence groups. After adjustment, neither NIV underuse (odds ratio [OR] 0.85, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.33-2.20) nor overuse (OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.20-1.46) was associated with the composite clinical outcome, whereas higher Simplified Acute Physiology Score (SAPS) II was independently associated with it (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08).

CONCLUSIONS: Deviations from ERS/ATS recommendations followed distinct clinical patterns and were not independently associated with the composite clinical outcome. Overall illness severity was consistently associated with adverse outcomes, highlighting the complexity of implementing NIV recommendations in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: A multipathogen view of Epstein-Barr virus pathogenesis and tumorigenesis.
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 95% of the global population and contributes to multiple human cancers and autoimmune diseases. Co-infection with pathogens including Helicobacter pylori, human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus, and Plasmodium falciparum can reshape host immunity and the EBV latency-lytic balance and, in some settings, promote reactivation. Collectively, these interactions may exacerbate chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and epigenetic dysregulation to accelerate disease progression and tumor formation. Existing clinical treatments control only the active pathogens but fail to target latent EBV. Emerging strategies such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) gene editing and EBV-targeted immunotherapy aim to eliminate latent viral reservoirs. This review outlines the synergistic mechanisms of EBV co-infection in oncogenesis, highlighting that further research on pathogen interactions is vital for developing better prevention and treatment options.

articles.title: Beyond Potassium and Phosphorus: The Broader Health Impact of Food Additives in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Food additives are widely used in processed and ultra-processed foods to improve shelf life, safety, texture, appearance, and palatability. Among them, potassium- and phosphorus-containing additives, which cover several technological functions in food products, may substantially increase dietary exposure to highly bioavailable forms of these minerals. Beyond mineral metabolism, emerging evidence suggests that food additives, including emulsifiers, artificial sweeteners, and food colorings, may affect cellular, intestinal, inflammatory, and metabolic processes relevant to kidney health, such as cytotoxic effects in renal tubular cells, gut dysbiosis, intestinal permeability, chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic dysfunction. However, much of the mechanistic evidence originates from animal and in vitro studies, and direct evidence linking specific additives to chronic kidney disease progression remains limited. Estimating additive intake remains challenging owing to variability in labeling regulations and the lack of mandatory disclosure of additive quantities in foods. This review summarizes the occurrence, technological functions, and regulatory aspects of food additives; discusses the emerging evidence linking food additive classes to kidney health; and highlights practical considerations for dietary counseling in chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Anaphylactic Shock With Bovine Serum Albumin Tissue Adhesive (BioGlue) in Cardiac Surgery: Case Series of an Under-Recognised Phenomenon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Anaphylaxis during cardiac surgery is a rare but life-threatening condition in which a severe systemic allergic reaction occurs in response to a specific allergen. BioGlue is a haemostatic agent used in cardiac surgery, composed of 45% purified bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 10% glutaraldehyde. Its use has been associated with anaphylactic shock in rare but well-described cases, typically mediated through immunoglobulin E (IgE) cross-reactivity between feline albumin (Fel d 2) and BSA. We aimed to assess the link between the use of BioGlue in cardiac surgery and anaphylactic reactions, and to identify potential measures to mitigate this risk.

METHOD: This article presents a case series of three patients who developed anaphylactic shock during cardiac surgery following application of BioGlue at a single UK centre within a period of 3 years. A structured literature review was conducted to explore the incidence, potential mechanisms, and management strategies of anaphylactic reactions associated with BioGlue.

RESULTS: All three patients developed profound vasoplegia and bronchospasm during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) shortly after BioGlue application, with markedly elevated serum tryptase. Skin-prick testing confirmed hypersensitivity to the BSA component in all cases. Feline serum albumin (Fel d 2)-specific IgE was detected in all three patients; alpha-galactose sensitisation and overt dietary pork intolerance were absent.

CONCLUSIONS: We emphasise the need for vigilance regarding anaphylactic reactions during cardiac surgery involving BioGlue. Its use should be avoided in patients with known Cat-Pork syndrome. We propose a practical mitigation strategy-saline field washout after BioGlue application-to reduce antigen recirculation via the CPB circuit.

articles.title: Phase-Structured Neuronal Recruitment in Motor Cortex during Skilled Movement Reorganized Early after Stroke.
articles.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
articles.abstract: Skilled forelimb movement engages both oscillatory and spiking activity in the motor cortex. However, how oscillatory phase organizes neuronal recruitment during behavior remains unclear. Here, we performed longitudinal bilateral recordings of local field potentials and single-unit activity in the rat (male) caudal forelimb area during a single-pellet retrieval task before and after stroke. Stroke altered spectral organization and redistributed neuronal recruitment across hemispheres. In the CFA contralateral to the reaching forelimb, which was the lesioned hemisphere, firing rates decreased and spike timing became more variable, whereas spike-LFP phase consistency increased in low-frequency bands. In contrast, the CFA ipsilateral to the reaching forelimb showed increased firing and reduced low-frequency phase consistency. These results demonstrate that early post-stroke motor cortical reorganization does not simply weaken neural activity but reshapes neuronal recruitment into a phase-structured form within ongoing oscillatory activity, providing insight into the dynamical principles underlying motor cortical reorganization during skilled movement.Significance Statement Skilled movement depends on coordinated interactions between populationlevel oscillations and neuronal spiking, but how this organization changes after cortical injury remains unclear. Using longitudinal bilateral recordings during skilled forelimb behavior, we show that early post-stroke reorganization is not characterized by a uniform loss of cortical activity. In the CFA contralateral to the reaching forelimb, firing was reduced and spike timing became more variable, yet low-frequency spike-LFP phase consistency increased. The ipsilateral CFA showed the opposite pattern, with increased firing and reduced low-frequency phase consistency. These findings demonstrate that firing output and spike-phase organization can reorganize independently after stroke, revealing a phase-structured dimension of motor cortical activity that is not captured by firing rate alone.

Data-Driven Respiratory Motion Correction in 18F-FDG PET for Cardiac Sarcoidosis: A Location-Dependent Phantom Study.
articles.abstract: Respiratory motion (RM) may affect quantitative accuracy in 18F-FDG PET for cardiac sarcoidosis (CS). Here, we evaluated the location-dependent effects of RM and RM correction (RMC) using a CS phantom with focal myocardial lesions. Methods: CS lesions were simulated by coin-shaped inserts attached to the anterior, septal, and inferior walls of a cardiac phantom. PET data were acquired under static conditions and simulated RM conditions with motion amplitudes of 10, 20, and 30 mm. RMC images were generated using data-driven respiratory gating. Both SUVmax and SUVmean were measured, and percentage changes relative to static images were calculated. Results: RM caused progressive underestimation of SUV with increasing motion amplitude. The degree of SUV reduction differed with lesion location. With motion of ±15 mm, SUVmax decreased by 44% in anterior, 39% in inferior, and 27% in septal walls. With motion correction of ±15 mm, SUVmax reductions improved to 39% in anterior, 23% in inferior, and 6% in septal walls, with the greatest improvement observed in the latter. SUVmean showed trends similar to those of SUVmax Conclusion: RM causes a region-dependent decrease in the quantitative accuracy of 18F-FDG PET for CS lesions. Although RMC decreased SUV underestimation, a substantial underestimation remained at larger motion amplitudes. Therefore, both RM and lesion location are relevant factors to consider in quantitative PET evaluations for CS.

articles.title: Clinical Applications of 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in the Evaluation and Management of Meningiomas: A Mini Review.
articles.abstract: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, and accurate imaging plays a central role in their diagnosis, risk assessment, treatment planning, and follow-up. Although many meningiomas are slow-growing, their clinical behavior can vary widely, with some tumors showing aggressive growth, postoperative recurrence, or complex extension into the skull base, bone, orbit, or dural venous sinuses. MRI and CT remain the standard imaging modalities for anatomic assessment; however, both have important limitations. MRI may be unable to reliably distinguish a residual or recurrent tumor from postoperative scarring, fibrosis, or radiation-related changes, whereas CT may be limited in differentiating reactive hyperostosis from true osseous tumor infiltration. Molecular imaging with 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT has emerged as a valuable complementary technique because of its high affinity for somatostatin receptor subtype 2, which is strongly expressed in most meningiomas. By providing high lesion-to-background contrast, 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT may improve lesion conspicuity and provide complementary information about disease extent in selected cases. Available evidence is strongest for problem-solving applications involving equivocal lesions and delineation of skull base, osseous, or optic nerve sheath disease, as well as confirmation of somatostatin receptor expression when receptor-targeted therapy is being considered. Other proposed applications, including tumor grading, prognostication, surgical planning, radiotherapy target refinement, quantitative response assessment, and routine surveillance, remain emerging and require prospective validation. This mini review summarizes the current applications, technical considerations, and limitations of 68Ga-DOTATOC PET/CT in meningioma management.

articles.title: Feasibility of Simulated Low-Count [18F]FDG PET/MR for Patients with Pediatric Epilepsy.
articles.abstract: To minimize radiation risks in pediatric PET imaging, injected dose should be kept as low as reasonably achievable. The aim of this study was to explore whether simulated low-count [18F]FDG PET/MR could preserve diagnostic quality in pediatric epilepsy, thereby supporting the design of future lower-activity validation studies. Methods: Twenty-seven pediatric patients with epilepsy were enrolled. List-mode PET data acquired over 20 min were truncated to 10, 7, and 4 min to simulate count reductions of 50%, 65%, and 80%, respectively. Image quality of the PET images was assessed visually using a 5-point Likert scale and quantitatively using contrast-to-noise ratio and coefficient of variation. The intraclass correlation coefficient was used to evaluate SUV ratio (SUVR) consistency across the simulated count reduction levels in different brain regions. Two computer-assisted methods, region of interest (ROI)-based methods and voxel-based methods, were used for epileptogenic zone (EZ) lateralization. For the ROI-based method, a machine learning model using regional SUVRs as features was applied, and performance was evaluated via receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis and the area under the curve, with statistical significance assessed by the DeLong test. For the voxel-based method, EZ lateralization was determined on the basis of the hemisphere of hypometabolic clusters identified through asymmetry analysis. Lateralization agreement with the clinical consensus was compared across simulated levels of count reduction. Results: Quantitative analysis showed that the contrast-to-noise ratio decreased and the coefficient of variation increased significantly with simulated count reduction. Visual assessment indicated that, although overall image quality declined, count reduction up to 65% remained clinically acceptable under these simulated conditions. High consistency in mean SUVRs was observed between full-count and simulated low-count PET images across brain regions. Both ROI-based and voxel-based methods demonstrated that EZ lateralization agreement with the clinical consensus did not decline with simulated count reduction. Conclusion: Our study in pediatric epilepsy suggests that a 65% simulated count reduction preserved clinically acceptable [18F]FDG PET image quality, stable SUVR quantification, and concordance of EZ lateralization with the clinical consensus. These findings support the need for prospective validation of a low-activity protocol in pediatric epilepsy.

articles.title: Delayed hospital admission and severe outcomes in community-acquired pneumonia: a cohort study.
Intestinal ultrasound in the UK: current challenges and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Optimal inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management increasingly relies on treat-to-target strategies incorporating assessment of transmural inflammation. Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is an accurate, non-invasive, repeatable and patient-centred imaging modality that enables real-time assessment of disease activity and timely therapeutic decision-making. Supported by a robust evidence base and international guideline endorsement, IUS demonstrates diagnostic performance comparable to magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) while offering advantages including rapid access, excellent patient acceptability, lower cost and integration into routine clinical encounters. Despite the UK’s early contribution to IUS development and a growing evidence base, adoption remains limited and concentrated within a small number of specialist centres. This review examines the current status of IUS in the UK, including the evidence base, patient experience, service delivery models, training, governance and practical considerations for implementation. Successful integration requires multidisciplinary collaboration between radiologists, gastroenterologists, IBD nurses and sonographers, supported by defined clinical indications, standardised scanning and reporting, competency-based training, supervised case acquisition, quality assurance and regular audit. Hybrid models combining point-of-care assessment within gastroenterology clinics with dedicated radiology-led or sonographer-led pathways may optimise capacity and clinical efficiency. Implementation requires investment in equipment, digital infrastructure and workforce development, supported by robust business cases recognising the potential for reduced reliance on MRE and endoscopy. With coordinated national efforts and multidisciplinary engagement, IUS has the potential to become an integral part of IBD care across the NHS.

articles.title: Fatal pulmonary-renal syndrome due to overlap of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis and proteinase 3-anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis in an adolescent.
Antibody-confirmed Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome following severe acute respiratory syndrome SARS-CoV-2 infection in an adolescent.
DARC OA: Understanding the prevalence and treatment of Osteoarthritis within UK Defence Primary Healthcare through a collaborative audit.
Early Screening for Depression in Adults With Diabetes in the Outpatient Setting.
articles.abstract: Background: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a complicated, chronic, endocrine disorder that can affect an individual's mental well-being. Thus, screening for depressive symptoms among patients with diabetes seeking specialist care in endocrinology may be helpful in the early detection and further treatment of depression. Objective: The objective of this quality improvement project was to evaluate if early screening using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) depression screening tool would improve detection of major depressive disorder (MDD) in individuals who have a previous diagnosis of DM, type 1 or type 2, who seek health care in a specialty endocrinologist office. Methods: The PHQ-9 screening tool was used to analyze depressive symptoms in adult patients aged 18-85 prior to their endocrinology visit. Results: Among the patients with DM screened for MDD using PHQ-9 (n = 135), the scores ranged between 0 and 26, with a median score of 3. Of the patients, 88 (65.2%) had no MDD, 18 (13.3%) had mild, 17 (12.6%) had moderate, 10 (7.4%) had moderate to severe, and 2 (1.5%) had severe level of depression. There was no significant relationship between blood sugar level and MDD (p = .188). However, a significant positive relationship was found between task difficulty and MDD (p ≤ .001). Conclusions: Although there was no significant relationship between blood sugar levels and MDD, a significant number of individuals were experiencing task difficulties that may contribute to mental well-being. Patients with comorbid DM and MDD can face task difficulties exacerbated by the interplay between these illnesses, as highlighted in previous literature. Early screening in a specialty office environment can provide a continuum of care, especially if an individual stops seeing their primary care physician and only sees their specialist. Implications for Nursing: Routine screening and addressing strategies for the management of DM and MDD in an endocrinology practice could improve future treatment outcomes.

articles.title: Quantra and ROTEM in Decompensated Cirrhosis: Method Comparison and Prognostic Value of Clot Time Ratio.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Viscoelastic testing (VET) is increasingly used to assess coagulation abnormalities in patients with cirrhosis, yet cross-platform comparability and the clinical significance of VET parameters remain uncertain. This study compared analogous parameters across Quantra, ROTEM delta, and conventional coagulation tests (CCT) and examined associations with clinical outcomes in hospitalized patients with decompensated cirrhosis.

METHODS: In this prospective observational study, hospitalized adults with decompensated cirrhosis underwent concurrent CCT, Quantra, and ROTEM delta testing. We assessed cross-platform associations and bias using weighted Deming regression. Prespecified VET parameters were evaluated for association with composite bleeding, thrombosis, and 30- and 90-day mortality. Because Quantra clot time ratio (CTR) was the only VET parameter associated with mortality, we further assessed its prognostic performance across severity scores, including Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD-3.0).

RESULTS: Among 108 patients, comparable VET parameters showed strong-to-very strong correlations (r = 0.69-0.94), though we observed systematic bias between platforms. No parameters were associated with bleeding/thrombosis. CTR was associated with higher 30- and 90-day mortality; 90-day mortality was 35.7% with CTR > 1 vs. 18.8% with CTR ≤ 1. Adding CTR to MELD-3.0 showed the largest numerical increase in 90-day mortality discrimination (AUC 0.71 to 0.75), with smaller increases across other severity scores, though confidence intervals for change in AUC included zero for all models.

CONCLUSION: Analogous Quantra and ROTEM showed strong-to-very strong correlations, although systematic differences limit their direct interchangeability. Exploratory analysis showed that Quantra CTR was associated with mortality, although further studies are needed to determine potential prognostic relevance.

articles.title: Personal and environmental factors associated with allergic disorders among adolescents in Lusaka, Zambia: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between wheezing, allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema and selected environmental, lifestyle and personal factors among school-going adolescents aged 13–14 years.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional study.

SETTING: Participants were enrolled from schools in Lusaka, Zambia.

PARTICIPANTS: Adolescents aged 13–14 years attending urban schools.

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOMES: Three primary outcomes including symptoms of asthma (wheeze), rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema were determined using the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood–Global Asthma Network questionnaire. Multivariate mixed effect logistic regression models were used to assess the association between selected exposure variables and each outcome. The study was reviewed and approved by the Levy Mwanawasa Medical University Research Ethics Committee (ref: LMMU-REC 00003/21) and the Zambian National Health Research Authority (ref: NHRA 0000001/23/03/2022). The Ministry of Education, headquarters in Lusaka, gave permission to access the schools (ref: MOE/101/1/45). All participants assented while their guardians consented.

RESULTS: The prevalence of symptoms of asthma (current wheeze), allergic rhinoconjunctivitis and eczema was 13.6%, 11.8% and 6.5%, respectively. In mixed-effect multivariable analysis, exposure to environmental pollutants including smoke from cigarettes, vehicle emissions, use of charcoal and pet exposure as well as lifestyle factors such as physical activity and frequent paracetamol intake were significantly associated with all the outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: This study indicates a significant burden of allergic diseases among adolescents in this population. Additionally, the study reveals an association between these symptoms and modifiable environmental, lifestyle and personal factors. Although further studies are needed to elucidate the observed associations, the findings highlight the potential benefit of reduced exposure to indoor and outdoor air pollutants, promotion of healthier lifestyle choices among adolescents and encouraging cautious use of paracetamol

articles.title: EaRly impAct theraPy with ceftazidime-avibactam via rapID diagnostics versus standard of care antibiotics and diagnostics in patients with bloodstream infection, hospital-acquired pneumonia or ventilator-associated pneumonia due to Pseudomonas aeruginosa or carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (RAPID): protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
An observational study protocol characterising pain trajectories, opioid use and predictors of chronic postsurgical pain in children with cerebral palsy undergoing orthopaedic surgery.
Analysis of risk factors for perioperative blood transfusion in hip arthroplasty and model construction using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator-logistic regression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Perioperative blood transfusion in hip arthroplasty is associated with increased morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and higher costs. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors and develop a validated predictive nomogram using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-logistic regression.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study enrolled 825 patients undergoing primary hip arthroplasty (January 2020-December 2024) from two Chinese centers. The training cohort (n = 573) and external validation cohort (n = 252) were analyzed. LASSO regression was used for feature selection, followed by multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Perioperative allogeneic transfusion occurred in 148 patients (17.9%). Independent risk factors included age ≥70 years (odds ratio [OR] = 1.84), female sex (OR = 1.52), American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class III-IV (OR = 1.93), coronary artery disease (OR = 1.61), prolonged operative duration (OR = 1.18 per 10 min), lower hemoglobin (OR = 0.72 per 10 g/L), and lower albumin (OR = 0.91 per 1 g/L). Tranexamic acid use was found to be protective (OR = 0.48). The nomogram showed good discrimination in training (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.866, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.812-0.880) and external validation (AUC = 0.816, 95% CI: 0.761-0.873) cohorts. Calibration and DCA confirmed excellent model performance and clinical utility.

CONCLUSION: We developed and externally validated a clinically practical nomogram for predicting perioperative transfusion risk in hip arthroplasty patients. This tool may aid individualized risk stratification, preoperative optimization, and blood management strategies.

articles.title: From Four Steps to Zero: Following Guidelines for Sustainable Preoperative Skin Preparation in Urology.
Carbohydrate quality and progression trajectories of cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective cohort study with multi-omics analyses.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbohydrate quality is associated with cardiometabolic health, but its relationships with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) progression and molecular and genetic characteristics remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate associations of carbohydrate quality with CMM progression and explore potential multi-omics signatures, pathways, and genetic effect modification.

METHODS: We included 177,763 UK Biobank participants free of baseline cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs). Carbohydrate quality was assessed using correlation and principal component analyses. Multivariable Cox and multi-state models evaluated CMD incidence and CMM progression. Carbohydrate-associated proteomic and metabolomic signatures were derived for exploratory mediation analyses, and genomic data were used for gene-environment-wide interaction study (GEWIS).

RESULTS: During a median 12.56-year follow-up, 37,527, 5,751, and 650 participants developed first, double, and triple CMDs, respectively. High- and low-quality carbohydrates showed opposing associations with CMM accumulation, strongest for ≥3 CMDs [HRs (95% CIs): 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) and 1.11 (1.05, 1.19), respectively]. In multi-state analyses, associations were particularly evident for progression from hypertension to comorbid T2D [HRs (95% CIs): 0.98 (0.96, 0.99) and 1.05 (1.03, 1.06), respectively]. Exploratory multi-omics mediation analyses yielded statistical mediation signals, with estimated pathway-level mediation proportions for T2D of 40.1% for PPAR signalling with high-quality carbohydrates and 36.2% and 36.4% for PI3K-Akt and MAPK signalling with low-quality carbohydrates. GEWIS identified candidate interaction loci with genotype-dependent differences in carbohydrate-CMD associations. High-quality carbohydrates were inversely associated with CHD onset among rs17589271 TT carriers but positively associated among GT/GG carriers [HRs (95% CIs): 0.95 (0.93, 0.98) and 1.22 (1.10, 1.35), respectively]. Low-quality carbohydrates showed a stronger association with progression from prior CMDs to comorbid T2D among rs144465069 AG/AA carriers [HR (95% CI): 2.09 (1.57, 2.78)].

CONCLUSIONS: Carbohydrate quality was differentially associated with CMM progression. Exploratory multi-omics and genetic analyses highlighted potential pathways and genotype-specific associations. These findings may inform future research on personalised nutritional strategies for cardiometabolic prevention.

articles.title: Plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins overlap with the hyperinflammatory phenotype in acute respiratory failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of acute respiratory failure (ARF) identifies patients with high mortality, but its underlying pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, and cell injury in critical illness. We investigated whether plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins characterize the hyperinflammatory phenotype and whether they contribute to its association with mortality.

METHODS: We analyzed 285 emergency department patients with ARF and suspected or confirmed COVID-19. Inflammatory phenotypes were derived by latent class analysis using nine biomarkers and clinical indicators. A mitochondrial-protein score was calculated from 59 MitoCarta3.0-matched proteins, and mitochondrial clusters were derived by principal component analysis and k-means clustering. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.

RESULTS: Latent class analysis identified 185 hypoinflammatory (65%) and 100 hyperinflammatory (35%) patients, with a significant difference in 28-day mortality (14/185, 7.6% vs. 31/100, 31.0%; p < 0.001). The mitochondrial-protein score increased with the probability of hyperinflammation (ρ=0.46, p < 0.001). Forty-three of 59 mitochondrial-associated proteins were more abundant in the hyperinflammatory phenotype, with prominent differences in apoptosis regulation, oxidative stress, and oxidative phosphorylation proteins. In a mutually adjusted model, the hyperinflammatory phenotype remained associated with mortality (odds ratio [OR]=6.40, 95%CI:3.08-13.95; p < 0.001), whereas the mitochondrial-protein score was not (OR=0.83 per SD, 95%CI:0.58-1.17; p = 0.30). Mitochondrial clusters yielded consistent findings.

CONCLUSIONS: The hyperinflammatory phenotype of ARF is characterized by increased plasma mitochondrial-associated proteins, linking inflammation with mitochondrial biology and cellular injury. This mitochondrial signature did not account for mortality independently of inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that it represents a biological component of the hyperinflammatory state.

articles.title: Effects of pneumoperitoneum pressure on perioperative atelectasis assessed using lung ultrasonography in patients undergoing robotic-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery: A prospective, randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery commonly requires prolonged pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning, which promote perioperative atelectasis and may increase complication risk. We aimed to investigate the effect of low pneumoperitoneum pressure (LPP) on atelectasis following robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, surgeon- and assessor-blind, randomised controlled trial in women undergoing elective robot-assisted laparoscopic gynaecological surgery. Participants were randomly allocated to the LPP (12 mmHg) or standard pneumoperitoneum pressure (SPP: 15 mmHg) group. Primary outcomes were modified lung ultrasound (mLUS) scores assessed after surgery and 30 min post-extubation. Secondary outcomes included incidence of atelectasis, percentage of desaturation in the post-anaesthesia care unit (PACU), lengths of PACU and hospital stay, surgeon satisfaction with the operative visual field, numeric rating scale pain score and modified clinical pulmonary infection score on postoperative day 1, and postoperative pulmonary complications 7 days postoperatively.

RESULTS: Sixty patients were enrolled (30 per group). The mLUSs were significantly lower in the LPP group versus the SPP group postoperatively (P < 0.001) and 30 min post-extubation (P < 0.001), particularly in the posterolateral lung region (P < 0.001). Compared with the SPP group, the LPP group experienced a 1.59-fold reduction in the risk of postoperative atelectasis 30 min post-extubation in the PACU (P = 0.004). Other secondary outcomes showed no significant intergroup differences.

CONCLUSIONS: A low pneumoperitoneum pressure during robotic-assisted gynaecological surgery reduced perioperative modified lung ultrasound scores and the incidence of early postoperative atelectasis. However, this imaging difference was not accompanied by significant improvements in oxygenation. Further studies powered for clinical pulmonary outcomes are needed.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, https://www.chictr.org.cn/; ChiCTR 2400085515.

articles.title: Optimal Control of Intermittent LRA-bNAb Pulse Timing and Intensities for Prolonged HIV Suppression.
articles.abstract: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses HIV-1 viremia but fails to eliminate the latent reservoir that drives rapid rebound after treatment interruption. Intermittent "shock-and-kill" strategies combining latency-reversing agents (LRAs) with broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) are promising, yet principled schedule design remains lacking. We develop a mechanistic HIV-1 model incorporating viral replication, virus-immune interactions, and LRA-bNAb combination therapy, and propose an interval-wise optimal control framework for intermittent treatment in which interventions are implemented as finite-duration pulses rather than instantaneous impulses. The admissible controls explicitly include both pulse initiation times and drug intensities, enabling the joint optimization of cumulative viral suppression while minimizing treatment toxicity. We establish the existence of optimal controls and derive adjoint-based necessary optimality conditions that account for treatment-dependent switching times. Numerical results reveal a non-monotonic dependence of viral suppression duration on pulse spacing and therapeutic intensities, demonstrating that more frequent or intensive treatment does not necessarily improve viral suppression. Optimal regimens typically feature intensive early treatment followed by more widely spaced maintenance pulses, with LRA administration concentrated in the initial phase and bNAb-mediated inhibition maintained thereafter. Comparisons among alternative control strategies indicate that flexibility in pulse timing can provide greater benefits than intensity adjustment alone. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating treatment timing, LRA and bNAb intensities, providing a theoretical basis for designing intermittent combination strategies aimed at prolonged HIV-1 suppression after ART interruption.

articles.title: Diabetes and Low-Fiber Nutritional Pattern-Driven Gut Barrier Dysfunction Axis in Risk Stratification of Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study Defining an Ultra-High-Risk Phenotype.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the synergistic mortality risk of diabetes mellitus (DM) and persistent microinflammation (PMI) in patients requiring maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) and to elucidate the underlying pathophysiological pathway involving nutritional fiber intake and gut barrier dysfunction.

DESIGN AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study enrolled 372 patients on MHD. PMI was defined as two consecutive high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) measurements >8 mg/L one month apart. Using a 2×2 factorial design, patients were categorized into: DM+PMI+, DM+PMI-, NDM+PMI+, NDM+PMI-. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox model was used to analyze interaction. A matched DM sub-cohort (n=80) was used to measure serum endotoxin and soluble CD14 (sCD14).

RESULTS: PMI prevalence was higher in patients with diabetes (60.9% vs. 35.6%, P<0.001), who had lower nutritional fiber intake (14.2±4.5 vs. 19.8±5.1 g/d, P<0.001). The DM+PMI+ group had the highest crude mortality (40.7%). A significant positive multiplicative interaction was found between DM and PMI (adjusted HR=1.65, 95%CI: 1.05-2.59, P=0.003). In patients with albumin ≥35 g/L, DM+PMI+ mortality remained high (52.8%). The matched DM+PMI+ group had higher endotoxin [7.12 vs. 3.05 EU/mL] and sCD14 (796±98 vs. 512±84 ng/mL) (both P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: "DM+PMI+" constitutes an ultra-high-risk phenotype independent of traditional nutritional markers. Low nutritional fiber intake is a core driver of the "Diabetes-Gut Barrier Dysfunction-Microinflammation" axis.

articles.title: Ultra-low-field MRI assesses brain volumes and age-related changes: validation against high-field MRI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: High-field MRI is the standard for assessing brain atrophy in neurodegenerative disorders, but limited access can restrict research and clinical care, particularly outside urban centers. Portable ultra-low-field (ULF) MRI may improve access, but their suitability for quantitative morphometry and detection of neurodegenerative-related atrophy is not well established. We evaluated agreement between 64 mT ULF MRI and 3T MRI for brain volumetric measurements and explored their potential utility in neurodegenerative disorders.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective, cross-sectional study of adults, including patients with neurodegenerative, subacute stroke, and healthy controls. Participants underwent both 3T and 64 mT ULF MRI with T1-weighted imaging. Regional brain volumes were extracted from both modalities using WMH-SynthSeg. Agreement between ULF- and 3T-derived volumes were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analyses. Where applicable, 3T FreeSurfer-derived volumes were used as an additional reference standard. Analyses in the neurodegenerative disorder subgroup were considered exploratory because the subgroup was not powered for formal inferential comparisons.

RESULTS: ULF and 3T volumetric measures show variable agreement (ICC ranged from 0.29 to 0.95), with the highest agreement for large structures such as total ventricles (ICC 0.85 to 0.95) and the lowest for the Pallidum (ICC 0.34 to 0.51). Age-related trajectories of gray and white matter decline, and ventricular expansion show the same pattern for WMH-SynthSeg and FreeSurfer-derived volumes. Exploratory analysis suggests pathological atrophy might differ from healthy aging trajectories.

INTERPRETATION: Portable ultra-low-field MRI combined with automated segmentation produced brain volumetric estimates that were broadly consistent with 3T MRI, particularly for larger structures relevant to atrophy assessment. These findings support the feasibility of ultra-low-field MRI for accessible morphometric evaluation in clinical research and potentially in under-resourced settings. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to define diagnostic accuracy, prediction intervals, and clinical utility in specific neurodegenerative disorder populations.

articles.title: Ten-Year Surveillance of Occupational Blood and Body Fluid Exposures Across COVID-19 Pandemic Phases: A Profession- and Experience-Stratified Analysis at a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Blood and body fluid exposures (BBFEs) remain persistent occupational hazards for healthcare workers. Long-term profession- and experience-specific trends across pandemic phases remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We analyzed a 10-year BBFE surveillance dataset (2016-2025) from a tertiary hospital. Exposure rates per 1,000 healthcare workers were stratified by profession (nurses and physicians) and clinical experience (first-year, 2-3 years, ≥4 years) across four pandemic phases: pre-pandemic, early-pandemic, pandemic-stabilization, and post-pandemic transition.

RESULTS: First-year nurses experienced a marked early-pandemic exposure surge (90.9 per 1,000 healthcare workers) compared with pre-pandemic baseline (33.9 per 1,000; Rate Ratio [RR] = 2.68, p = 0.0075), followed by post-pandemic normalization (30.4 per 1,000; RR = 0.33, p = 0.0034). Experienced nurses showed no significant early-pandemic increase. Physicians maintained stable exposure patterns across all experience strata, with rate variability reflecting small cohort size.

CONCLUSIONS: Early-pandemic workforce redistribution and reduced supervisory availability temporally coincided with increased BBFE rates among first-year nurses, whereas physician exposure patterns remained stable. Staffing restoration during the post-pandemic period aligned with novice nurse rate normalization. Accessible supervisory support and structured procedural guidance may help safeguard early-career personnel during operational disruptions.

articles.title: Watermelon supplementation lowers blood pressure: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Watermelon contains L-citrulline, polyphenols, lycopene, and other bioactive compounds that may influence vascular function and blood pressure regulation. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of watermelon supplementation on blood pressure, arterial stiffness-related indices, autonomic function, lipid metabolism, and anthropometric parameters.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 13, 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing watermelon, watermelon juice, or watermelon extract with non-watermelon control interventions were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the revised Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, and evidence certainty was evaluated using the GRADE framework. Continuous outcomes were synthesized using mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Crossover trials were analyzed as paired data, with each participant counted once; when paired variance information was unavailable, a within-participant correlation coefficient of 0.50 was assumed. Primary analyses used post-intervention values, and analyses based on change-from-baseline values were conducted as supplementary analyses. Heterogeneity was explored using subgroup analysis, meta-regression, restricted cubic spline analysis, and leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Trial sequential analysis was conducted using unique participant counts.

RESULTS: Sixteen randomized controlled trials were included. Five trials were judged to have a low risk of bias, eight had some concerns, and three had a high risk of bias. In the post-intervention primary analysis, watermelon supplementation was associated with lower systolic blood pressure (SBP; 12 studies; WMD, -5.53 mmHg; 95% CI, -8.99 to -2.06; P=0.002; I2=89.7%) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP; 12 studies; WMD, -2.55 mmHg; 95% CI, -3.77 to -1.33; P<0.001; I2=57.1%). Significant pooled reductions were observed for first systolic peak pressure and pulse pressure, whereas second systolic peak pressure, mean arterial pressure, reflection time, heart rate, pulse-wave velocity, augmentation index, and anthropometric and lipid outcomes were not statistically significant. Among autonomic outcomes, RMSSD and high-frequency power increased, whereas SDNN, low-frequency power, and the LF/HF ratio did not show statistically significant changes; these outcomes were each informed by two studies. Exploratory subgroup and study-level meta-regression analyses showed nominal differences across study characteristics, but these analyses were based on sparse, potentially confounded evidence and were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Restricted cubic spline analyses found no evidence of nonlinearity. In the TSA analysis, 236 unique participants represented 15.9% and 28.9% of the required information sizes for SBP and DBP, respectively, and neither cumulative Z-curve crossed the trial sequential monitoring boundary. Potential small-study effects could not be excluded. According to the current GRADE profile, certainty was very low for SBP and low for DBP.

CONCLUSIONS: Watermelon supplementation was associated with lower SBP and DBP, but substantial heterogeneity, limited accrued information, and low certainty of evidence restrict confidence in the estimated effects. Evidence for haemodynamic, autonomic, arterial-stiffness, lipid, and anthropometric outcomes was inconsistent and was usually based on few studies. The subgroup and meta-regression findings are exploratory study-level observations and do not establish patient-level effect modification or an optimal intervention regimen. Larger, well-designed randomized controlled trials with prespecified analyses are needed.

articles.title: High rates of carbapenem resistance and inappropriate empirical antimicrobial therapy in Acinetobacter bloodstream infection in Vietnam: A single-centre retrospective study.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We described the antimicrobial resistance profile of Acinetobacter spp. isolated from blood cultures and assessed the appropriateness of empirical antimicrobial therapy in patients with Acinetobacter bloodstream infection (BSI) in Vietnam.

METHOD: This was a retrospective cohort study of all culture-confirmed Acinetobacter BSI episodes at Hanoi Medical University Hospital (HMUH) between January 2021 and December 2024. Empirical treatment was defined as any systemic antimicrobial initiated before the blood culture result was available and administered for at least 48 hours. It was classified as appropriate when the isolate was susceptible to at least one administered antimicrobial, and as inappropriate when the isolate was intermediate or resistant to all administered antimicrobials.

RESULTS: Fifty-six Acinetobacter BSI episodes were included, of which 51 (91.1%) were caused by the Acinetobacter calcoaceticus-baumannii (ACB) complex and 5 (8.9%) by non-ACB species. Carbapenem resistance was present in 39/56 isolates (69.6%). Overall in-hospital mortality proportion was 21/56 (37.5%).
