Empirical antimicrobial treatment was appropriate in only 6/56 (10.7%) episodes, inappropriate or absent in 37/56 (66.1%), and indeterminate in 13/56 (23.2%). Appropriate empirical therapy was less frequent in carbapenem-resistant than in non- carbapenem-resistant episodes (1/39, 2.6% versus 5/17, 29.4%; p = 0.008). Among ACB complex episodes, in-hospital mortality proportion was 16/35 (45.7%) in the inappropriate group versus 1/5 (20.0%) in the appropriate group.

CONCLUSIONS: Inappropriate empirical antimicrobial therapy was common in Acinetobacter BSI due to the high prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter. These findings highlight the urgency of developing risk-stratified empirical treatment guidance for Acinetobacter BSI in Vietnam.

articles.title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).

CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

articles.title: Cerebellar structural and electrophysiological alterations associated with neuropathic pain in mice.
articles.abstract: The cerebellum is increasingly implicated in pain, yet direct electrophysiology in neuropathy is scarce. We tested whether sciatic nerve chronic constriction injury (CCI) alters cerebellar dynamics and structure. Adult male mice underwent CCI, von Frey testing, structural MRI, spontaneous LFP recordings in lobules IV-V, and spontaneous/evoked single-unit recordings under anesthesia. CCI produced rapid, persistent mechanical hypersensitivity. Deformation-based morphometry (DBM) revealed regional volumetric alterations including localized contractions in the IV-V cerebellar lobules. Spontaneous LFPs showed reduced absolute δ/θ power, with unchanged relative (normalized) power, while β/γ were unchanged. Multi-unit activity in CCI mice exhibited higher firing rates, shorter inter-spike intervals, and larger spike amplitudes. Peripheral stimulation evoked larger responses in CCI. Neuropathic pain is associated with structural remodeling, suppressed spontaneous slow-band cerebellar activity and enhanced unit/evoked responsiveness, which we interpret, as a working hypothesis, as a low-synchrony/high-gain operating regime. These structural and electrophysiological changes are candidate signatures that motivate future mechanistic and causal studies of cerebellar involvement in neuropathic pain.

articles.title: L-Alanine Inhibits the AKI-to-CKD Transition by Restoring MCT2-Mediated Metabolic Reprogramming in Tubular Epithelial Cells.
articles.abstract: Dysregulated amino acid metabolism is a prominent feature after acute kidney injury (AKI), but its contribution to chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression remains unclear. The therapeutic potential of targeting these metabolic alterations also remains poorly understood. Quantification of 20 circulating L-amino acids revealed that L-alanine (Ala) showed the most pronounced reduction in patients with cardiac surgery-associated AKI and renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) mice. Notably, supplementation of exogenous Ala attenuated the AKI-to-CKD transition in IRI mice. Mechanistically, Ala restored monocarboxylate transporter 2 (MCT2) expression by preventing heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein M (hnRNPM)-mediated destabilization of D-box binding protein (DBP) mRNA. Subsequently, DBP was identified as a transcriptional regulator of MCT2 and enhanced its transcription by directly binding to its promoter region. Furthermore, renal tubular epithelial cell (RTEC)-specific deletion of MCT2 blunted Ala-mediated restoration of mitochondrial oxidative metabolism and renal protection. These findings reveal a mechanism by which Ala promotes tubular metabolic recovery and provide preclinical evidence supporting further evaluation of Ala supplementation to limit AKI-to-CKD progression after cardiac surgery.

articles.title: From broad suppression to precision targeting: the new era of antigen-specific immunotherapy for type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the selective destruction of pancreatic β-cells driven by autoreactive immune responses. In recent decades, the global incidence of T1D has risen markedly, with the most rapid increase observed among children and adolescents, imposing a substantial burden on healthcare systems worldwide. Conventional treatment primarily relies on exogenous insulin administration, which manages hyperglycemia but does not address the underlying autoimmune pathology or restore endogenous insulin production. Antigen-specific immunotherapy (ASI) has emerged as a promising strategy that may restore antigen-specific immune tolerance via multiple mechanisms, including clonal deletion/ anergy, immune deviation, induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and type 1 regulatory T (Tr1) cells, and tolerogenic antigen presentation. ASI may help preserve residual β-cell function and potentially modify disease progression. This review comprehensively summarizes recent advances in ASI for T1D, with a focus on the biological features of key T1D autoantigens, optimization of antigen delivery strategies, and prospects for clinical translation.

articles.title: MicroRNA networks at the crossroads of Campylobacter jejuni infection and Guillain-Barré syndrome: A new paradigm in autoimmune neuropathology.
articles.abstract: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), the leading cause of acute flaccid paralysis, is often triggered by Campylobacter jejuni. Classical molecular mimicry explains autoantibody induction but not clinical heterogeneity, penetrance, or outcomes. We propose a "Triple Rheostat Paradigm" positioning microRNAs as dynamic regulators across three axes: mucosal glyco-miR, systemic immune threshold, and neural vulnerability. We also propose a "Bidirectional Glyco-miR Feedback Loop," in which host miRNAs may shape bacterial phenotype via extracellular vesicles, though direct evidence that miRNAs regulate C. jejuni LOS biosynthesis is lacking. Presenting this as a testable framework, we assess miRNA biomarkers and therapeutic prospects, and outline a miR-guided precision medicine framework. GBS may be reframed as failure of miR-mediated immune rheostasis.

articles.title: Biomarkers and molecular determinants of T-cell engager response, resistance and toxicity.
articles.abstract: T-cell engagers redirect endogenous T cells against malignant cells and have produced clinically meaningful responses across haematological malignancies and selected solid tumours. Responses vary, while cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, infection and on-target, off-tumour injury constrain treatment. Target positivity alone is therefore insufficient for selecting patients, molecules or dosing strategies. This Review synthesises evidence across five interacting domains: host immune reserve and T-cell fitness; engager molecular design and pharmacology; tumour antigen ecology and genomic vulnerability; the tumour immune ecosystem; and toxicity risk. Productive engagement requires functionally competent T cells, adequate active exposure at the tumour site, accessible and persistent antigen, tissue trafficking and calibrated T-cell activation. Candidate host markers include circulating lymphocyte and T-cell subsets, differentiation and exhaustion states, systemic inflammation, prior immunotherapy and microbiome-metabolic features. Molecular format, pharmacokinetics, activation threshold and synapse geometry influence the balance between cytotoxicity and systemic inflammation. Antigen density, coverage, accessibility, heterogeneity and treatment-induced loss shape sensitivity and resistance, whereas suppressive immune cells, stroma and metabolic constraints restrict tissue activity. Circulating tumour DNA, measurable residual disease and soluble antigen can support longitudinal response assessment. Baseline inflammation, cytokine kinetics and normal immune-lineage depletion may inform safety monitoring, but risk factors, pharmacodynamic changes, early-warning signals and manifestations of established toxicity serve different purposes. Most reported markers remain prognostic, pharmacodynamic or useful for resistance classification rather than validated predictors of treatment benefit. Clinical translation requires standardised assays, context-specific thresholds, external validation and prospective trials showing that biomarker-guided decisions improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Coronary coronary microvascular dysfunction and physiologically non-obstructive plaque progression in patients with acute coronary syndromes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction is common in coronary heart disease, yet its role in plaque progression remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the association between coronary microvascular dysfunction and the progression of physiologically non-obstructive atherosclerotic plaques.

METHODS: A total of 198 patients with acute coronary syndrome who underwent optical coherence tomography imaging of at least one non-culprit vessel at both baseline and 1-year follow-up were included. Angiography-derived microcirculatory resistance (AMR) was measured in non-culprit vessels with a Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (μQFR) > 0.80. Serial changes in plaque morphological characteristics were compared between plaques in high (AMR ≥ 2.50) and low (AMR < 2.50) AMR vessels.

RESULTS: Among 172 non-culprit vessels (278 plaques) with μQFR >0.80, elevated AMR was identified in 60 vessels (92 plaques). Plaques in the high AMR group exhibited significantly less fibrous cap thickening and a smaller reduction in maximum lipid arc than those in the low AMR group. Furthermore, thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFAs) in the high AMR group showed a significantly lower rate of regression to non-TCFAs (43.8% vs. 81.5%, p = 0.011). Multivariate analysis identified AMR as an independent predictor of changes in fibrous cap thickness (β: -3.12 [-5.53-0.70], p = 0.011) and maximum lipid arc (β: 1.91 [0.10-3.73], p = 0.039).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that coronary microvascular dysfunction is associated with attenuated plaque stabilisation in physiologically non-obstructive lesions, suggesting that integrated microvascular and plaque assessment warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Acute lung allograft dysfunction: incidence, etiology, severity, alloimmune burden and graft outcomes in a single-centre cohort.
articles.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
articles.abstract: Acute lung allograft dysfunction (ALAD) was recently defined by ISHLT consensus. Its severity scale has not been evaluated against outcomes, and the contributions of etiology and alloimmune injury are uncertain. This retrospective single-centre cohort included recipients transplanted between 2018 and 2024 surviving ≥30 days. Every post-transplant visit was reviewed; episodes were adjudicated for etiologies and graded on the ISHLT severity scale and a pre-specified six-point scale. Graft loss within 90 days was modelled by landmark Cox regression; graft loss and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) over the whole follow-up by time-dependent Cox models. ALAD occurred in 238 of 303 patients (78.5%), with 862 episodes. Infection predominated; 130 episodes (15%) were alloimmune (cellular or antibody-mediated rejection) and 268 (31.1%) had no FEV1 decline. Severity according to the ISHLT scale predicted graft loss at 90 days (severe, HR 14.8 (4.97-44.0)) and over follow-up (adjusted HR 3.67 (1.78-7.57)), but not CLAD (1.32 (0.67-2.59)). Each additional alloimmune episode predicted both graft loss (1.64 (1.31-2.04)) and CLAD (1.57 (1.06-2.32)). ALAD affects most lung transplant recipients, with nearly a third of episodes lacking documented spirometric decline. Episode severity predicts graft loss, while each additional alloimmune episode is associated with both graft loss and CLAD.

articles.title: From Obesity to Cancer Cachexia: PI3K/AKT/MTOR Signaling Across the Energy Balance Spectrum - A Scoping Review of Body Size, Composition, and Cancer Outcomes.
articles.abstract: The PI3K/AKT/MTOR signaling pathway is overactivated in cancer. Obesity is an established risk factor for several cancers, also variably associated with prognosis. Cancer cachexia is at the opposite end of the energy balance spectrum and is similarly linked to poor prognosis. Preclinical studies link obesity to activation of this pathway, whereas cachexia is associated with its suppression in skeletal muscle. However, human findings are inconsistent and often ignore the metabolic influence of body composition on MTOR activity. This scoping review summarizes how body size and composition-spanning obesity to cachexia-relate to PI3K/AKT/MTOR signaling in cancer risk and outcomes. A systematic search in Web of Science, Embase, and PubMed through January 19, 2023, identified 6,285 studies; 139 met the inclusion criteria across 15 cancer types: gastrointestinal (n=48); gynecological (n=34); breast (n=30); male reproductive (n=7); lung (n=6); thyroid (n=6); renal (n=2); and skin (n=1) cancers, plus cachexia (n=5). Body size was associated with components and effectors of the PI3K/AKT/MTOR pathway, but findings were inconsistent, reflecting heterogeneity in cancer type, subtype, exposure and biomarker measurement, and unmeasured host factors. Insulin resistance and diabetes were more consistently associated with pathway markers than BMI. Across six studies, obesity and pathway markers often interacted, modifying each other's associations with cancer outcomes. Interventional studies of weight loss, metformin, and bariatric surgery reported changes in some tumor biomarkers, but none assessed cancer outcomes, limiting weight management guidance for patients with obesity. In cachexia, pathway analysis suggested increased catabolic and decreased anabolic muscle signaling, though findings varied by muscle site, and the effects of dietary interventions remain untested. Evidence predominantly relied on BMI rather than body composition components, leaving their relationship to PI3K/AKT/MTOR signaling understudied. Standardized and longitudinal designs, body composition measurement, and assessment of metabolic status, diet, and physical activity are needed to advance precision nutritional oncology. REVIEW REGISTRATION: INPLASY202450036 https://doi.org/10.37766/inplasy2024.5.0036 STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This scoping review is the first to comprehensively examine the associations between alterations in body size and composition-including both obesity and cancer-associated cachexia-and PI3K/AKT/MTOR signaling in tumors, adipose tissue, and skeletal muscle across cancer types in relation to clinical outcomes and patient survival. Findings reveal heterogeneity in study designs and highlight research gaps, including the need for more consistent measurement of body composition and incorporating host metabolic context, such as insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction. These efforts could harmonize results, improve comparability across studies, and advance nutritional and precision oncology.

articles.title: Atomic layer deposition of antigen-decorated phage-like particles as a platform for thermally stable, single-injection antiviral vaccines.
articles.abstract: Overcoming barriers to the distribution, availability, and effectiveness of vaccines, are major public health challenges. For example, thermal instabilities of vaccines result in the need for strict cold-chain conditions during storage and shipping. In addition, many vaccines require the administration of multiple vaccine doses per individual for protective and durable immunity. In this study, we describe the combination of a SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain (RBD) lambda phage-like particle (PLP) vaccine platform with our spray-drying and atomic layer deposition (ALD) formulation to generate highly thermostable single-dose immunogens. We show that ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines retain potent immunogenicity in mice following incubation for one month at temperatures up to 50°C. In addition, mice immunized with a single dose of ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines developed SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody responses similar to those induced by standard prime-boost regimens and were strongly protected against SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease. These data suggest that ALD-coated PLP-based vaccine formulations can address two critical barriers to effective deployment of antiviral vaccines-thermal stability and single-shot dosing.

articles.title: Underrecognized Localized Alopecia Following Conventional Transcutaneous Skull-Pin Fixation: Incidence and Risk Factors in a Two-Center Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Localized alopecia after three-point skull fixation remains poorly characterized. We evaluated the incidence of pin-site complications after conventional transcutaneous skull-pin fixation and explored associated factors.

METHODS: This two-center retrospective cohort study included consecutive adults undergoing neurosurgical procedures requiring Mayfield fixation in 2025. Patient characteristics, surgical factors, and scalp thickness were analyzed using Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: Of 141 patients, 138 had evaluable postoperative pin-site outcomes. Localized alopecia occurred in 22 (16%); no ulceration or infection was observed. No skull fracture or fixation instability occurred among all 141 patients. Increasing age was associated with lower odds of alopecia (adjusted odds ratio [OR] per 10-year increase, 0.556; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.365-0.804; p = 0.001). Male sex (adjusted OR, 6.471; 95% CI, 1.715-31.125; p = 0.005) and longer operative duration (adjusted OR per 60-minute increase, 1.459; 95% CI, 1.207-1.840; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds. Combined subcutaneous tissue and muscle thickness was not independently associated.

CONCLUSIONS: Localized alopecia was observed in 16% of evaluable patients. Younger age, male sex, and longer operative duration were independently associated with its occurrence. Permanence and patient-reported impact remain uncertain. These findings support prospective evaluation of preventive strategies.

articles.title: Nattokinase ameliorates post-SAH microcirculatory dysfunction by targeting CTSG-MMP9/PAR4 signaling.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral microcirculatory dysfunction significantly contributes to early brain injury and long-term neurological deficits following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Nattokinase (NK), a serine protease derived from fermented natto beans, has shown potential in preventing cardiovascular diseases owing to its anticoagulant and thrombolytic properties. Nonetheless, its exact role in microcirculatory disturbances post-SAH is yet to be elucidated.

METHODS: The key pathways and proteins related to microcirculation disorders after SAH were identified through 4D-DIA proteomics analysis of human cerebrospinal fluid. A rat model of SAH was established by the intravascular perforation method. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) were utilized to predict the potential targets of NK. The alterations in microcirculation function were evaluated through neurobehavioral tests, brain water content, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and cortical blood perfusion detections. The related molecular mechanisms were further verified by immunofluorescence, western blot, and flow cytometry.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis revealed significant upregulation of the complement and coagulation cascade pathway post-SAH. NK markedly reduced microvascular thrombosis after SAH, restored cortical blood perfusion, reduced BBB disruption and brain edema, and ameliorated neurological function. Cathepsin G (CTSG) was identified as a potential binding target of NK. NK treatment was associated with restored BBB integrity and reduced platelet activation/microthrombus formation, possibly through modulation of the CTSG-MMP9/PAR4 axis. In a Re-CTSG gain-of-function experiment, exogenous CTSG partially reversed the effects of NK, supporting a contributory role of CTSG, although strict pathway causality was not established.

CONCLUSION: Our data suggest that CTSG may be a promising therapeutic target for NK, and modulating the CTSG-MMP9/PAR4 axis through NK might be a beneficial strategy for salvaging post-SAH microcirculatory dysfunction.

articles.title: Survival and Aortic Reintervention Following Hemiarch vs. Extended Arch for Acute Type A Dissection in Patients Over Age 65.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ascending hemiarch replacement is considered standard, some have advocated extended arch reconstruction as the preferred strategy in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

METHODS: Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-elective hemiarch or extended arch for ATAAD in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services linkage (July 2017-2023,N=3,562;2,442[68.6%] hemiarch;1,120[31.4%] extended arch) were compared. Primary endpoints were long-term mortality and aortic reintervention beyond 30 days and were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence functions, followed by multivariable regressions.

RESULTS: Hemiarch patients tended to be slightly older (73.8±6.1vs.73.1±5.9 years), female (46.6%vs.39.6%), and hyperacute ATAAD (80.1%vs74.7%). Malperfusion was more frequent in extended arch (27.8% vs 20.6%). Extended arch patients had: i) longer cardiopulmonary bypass, cross-clamp, and circulatory arrest times and ii) more frequent antegrade and/or retrograde cerebral perfusion. Short-term outcomes and rates of concomitant procedures were similar between groups. Risk-adjusted analysis showed no treatment effects for survival, aortic reintervention, operative mortality, and stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Extended arch for treatment of ATAAD in patients aged ≥65 years was not associated with improved mortality or aortic reintervention compared to hemiarch at intermediate followup. Absent patient-specific indications, hemiarch may be sufficient in patients aged ≥65 years with ATAAD.

articles.title: Projected Cardiovascular Benefit of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy in Obese Patients Without Diabetes Undergoing Complex Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Rotablator Burr Entrapment: A Systematic Review of 215 Published Cases, Mechanisms, and Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Burr entrapment is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of rotational atherectomy. We reviewed all related publications, classified the mechanisms of entrapment, and summarized management strategies.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar were searched for English-language publications reporting Rotablator burr entrapment or related retained-burr or device-loss events from inception through August 31, 2026.

RESULTS: One hundred fourteen publications were included, representing 215 unique eligible cases after exclusion of one overlapping case. The mechanism was reported in 117 cases, management in 162, and final outcome in 160. Among 34 studies reporting the total number of rotational atherectomy procedures, burr entrapment occurred in 118 of 19,672 procedures (0.6%). The most common classified mechanism was intralesional embedding or wedging (32.5%), followed by the Kokeshi phenomenon (30.8%), stent-related entrapment (26.5%), and primary driveshaft fracture or burr disconnection (10.3%). Among the 162 cases with available management data, 86.4% were managed percutaneously, including 3.7% with intentional burr retention or exclusion (crushing or jailing), and 13.6% required surgical bailout. Management strategies shifted over time, with surgical bailout declining from 66.7% before 2010 to 22.7% in 2010-2019 and 5.5% in 2020-2026. Procedural outcomes differed according to mechanism. Successful burr resolution with completed or otherwise acceptable PCI was most frequent in Kokeshi-type entrapment (80.6%), whereas stent-related entrapment had the highest surgical bailout rate (29.0%).

CONCLUSIONS: Burr entrapment was reported in approximately 0.6% of rotational atherectomy procedures. Our findings support a mechanism-based, stepwise approach to burr retrieval. Percutaneous treatment is successful in most contemporary cases.

articles.title: Feasibility and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation via the right internal jugular vein: primary results of the VAMPIRE multicenter prospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are usually implanted through the femoral vein. The right internal jugular vein (RIJV) approach has emerged as an alternative, but evidence remains limited to retrospective single-centre series.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural success, and 30-day safety of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation.

METHODS: The VAMPIRE study (NCT06455566) is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter registry enrolling consecutive patients with a guideline-directed LP indication across 15 tertiary centres in France (May 2024-May 2026). The primary endpoint was major procedure- or system-related complications within 30 days.

RESULTS: Of 294 screened patients, 272 (92.5%) underwent a first-line RIJV approach. The cohort was elderly (median age 79 [73-85] years), predominantly male (63.6%), with high comorbidity burden including atrial fibrillation in 51.5%, chronic kidney disease in 34.9%, and cancer in 22.4%. High-degree atrioventricular block was the primary indication in 84.9%; 65.8% of procedures were performed urgently. Successful LP implantation was achieved in 266 of 272 patients (97.8%; 95% CI 95.3-99.2%), with septal deployment in 94.3%. Median procedure time was 30 [25-40] minutes and median fluoroscopy time 2.5 [1.1-7.0] minutes. Major complications occurred in 6 of 272 patients (2.2%; 95% CI 0.8-4.7%; p<0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this prospective multicenter registry of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation, feasibility and procedural success were high, and 30-day major complications rate low. These results support the RIJV route as a safe and broadly applicable access strategy for LP implantation. However, dedicated studies are needed to compare safety versus the femoral approach.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Symptoms and Arrhythmias During Continuous ECG Monitoring After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wearable ECG patches after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) enable continuous rhythm monitoring and allow symptoms reporting via trigger buttons and diary entries. However, the reliability of triggered events to identify clinically relevant arrhythmias after TAVI is uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: We systematically analyzed patient-triggered events and their corresponding rhythm findings during 14-day ECG patch monitoring after TAVI.

METHODS: Adult patients undergoing TAVI at a Swiss tertiary centre were prospectively enrolled and monitored with a 14-day ECG patch before discharge. Patients recorded any cardiac-related symptoms using the patch trigger button and/or diary function.

RESULTS: Among 315 patients (median age 82 years [78-87], 43% female), median analyzable duration was 14 days [13-14]. At least one patient-triggered event was recorded in 94 patients (30%), with a median of 2 events per patient [1-4]. Atrial fibrillation (AF) was detected in 85 patients (27%), including 17 patients (5.4%) with new AF; however, only 20 patients with AF (24%) reported symptoms during AF episodes. Pauses occurred in 58 patients (18%) and high-grade atrioventricular block in 32 patients (10%), with no associated patient-triggered events. Ventricular tachycardia (≥4 beats) occurred in 165 patients (52%) and was entirely asymptomatic. Of 348 evaluable symptom-triggered events, 153 (44%) occurred without associated arrhythmia. The most frequent arrhythmias associated with symptom-triggered events were premature atrial contractions (21%), AF (14%), and premature ventricular contractions (11%).

CONCLUSIONS: After TAVI, patient-triggered events during ECG patch monitoring poorly reflect objectively documented arrhythmias and fail to identify many clinically relevant rhythm disturbances. These findings support systematic continuous ECG surveillance beyond symptom-driven monitoring strategies after TAVI.

articles.title: Developing and prospectively validating a reproducible graph representation specification for clinical guideline algorithms: The measurement foundation of the clinical guideline complexity index.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Translating a clinical guideline decision algorithm into a computational graph requires judgment, and unconstrained coding yields divergent graphs; any complexity measure computed from such a graph inherits that variation, so its reproducibility must be demonstrated rather than assumed.

OBJECTIVE: To develop, and prospectively test, an empirical method for making graph extraction reproducible, using the Clinical Guideline Complexity Index (CGCI), a previously described structural complexity measure, and four guideline algorithms as a case study.

METHODS: We built a Graph Representation Specification (an ontology, a catalogue of recurring structural motifs, disambiguation conventions, decomposition rules, and a deterministic validator) and refined it by error-driven grammar induction: measure inter-coder disagreement, localize its dominant class, induce a single grammar rule, and prospectively test whether that rule improves agreement in the anticipated class. Reproducibility was quantified with a pre-specified, topology-based endpoint (Decision Topology Agreement) rather than edge agreement, which is oversensitive to representational choices that do not affect the score. Two trained coders independently coded the decision algorithms of four clinical practice guidelines (diabetes, dyslipidemia, heart failure, and hypertension).

RESULTS: A rule (assessment topology) derived from coder disagreement on the comorbidity panel of the diabetes guideline's treatment algorithm generated a pre-specified prediction that the heart-failure guideline's figures, which contain the same structural pattern, would converge; on a fresh, independently coded pair they did, with an absolute CGCI difference of approximately one. The ordering of decisions reproduced closely (decision-order agreement 0.90 to 1.00 across the four guidelines), while breadth counting was rule-sensitive: an explicit modifier-counting rule reduced the largest disagreement from 27 to 4 tokens. Residual disagreement was bounded and localizable to specific, nameable representational choices.

CONCLUSIONS: Graph-extraction reproducibility can be systematically improved through iterative grammar refinement, and a prospectively derived rule can be confirmed to improve agreement. These results concern reliability, not construct validity. The method is not specific to medicine and may apply wherever graphs are extracted from structured source artifacts.

articles.title: Integrating bioinformatics and machine learning reveals SETD7 as a potential ferro-aging gene in asthma.
articles.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic inflammatory airway disease closely associated with dysregulated iron metabolism and oxidative stress. Ferro-aging, a recently described form of cellular senescence driven by iron overload, is characterised by sustained lipid peroxidation, but its gene-level links to asthma remain poorly defined. By intersecting differentially expressed genes from the GEO induced-sputum dataset with a ferro-aging gene set and applying five machine learning algorithms, we identified SETD7 as a hub ferro-aging gene. SETD7 was consistently downregulated in asthma in the discovery cohort and in two independent external cohorts (induced sputum GSE41863 and BALF GSE74986), with AUCs of 0.749, 0.763 and 0.834. Single-cell analysis revealed predominant SETD7 expression in goblet and Club cells, positively correlated with ferro-aging scores. In vitro, house dust mite stimulation reduced SETD7 expression, whereas SETD7 knockdown attenuated HDM-induced TSLP, IL-1β and MUC5AC expression and SETD7 overexpression exacerbated inflammation and promoted senescence through lipid peroxidation. Both trichostatin A and the selective SETD7 inhibitor (R)-PFI-2 attenuated these responses, and SETD7 overexpression partially reversed the protective effect of trichostatin A. Collectively, these findings identify SETD7 as a candidate ferro-aging gene in asthma and provide a theoretical basis for alleviating ferro-aging-associated airway inflammation.

articles.title: Redox signaling in skeletal muscle: From physiological adaptation to disease-associated muscle weakness.
articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle is a major determinant of whole-body energy expenditure and a prominent site of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Rather than acting solely as damaging by-products, ROS and particularly hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) function as spatially and temporally constrained signals that regulate contraction, metabolism, and adaptation to exercise. This review examines how the compartmental organization of skeletal muscle shapes redox signaling and how disruption of this organization contributes to muscle weakness. We discuss peroxiredoxins as peroxide scavengers, sensors, and signal transducers; compare mitochondrial and NADPH oxidase-derived ROS at rest and during contraction; and evaluate current approaches for monitoring ROS and oxidative posttranslational modifications. We then integrate evidence from aging, inflammatory myopathies, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, obesity and type 2 diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis, and cancer cachexia to show how persistent or misplaced oxidant production can impair excitation-contraction coupling, cross-bridge function, glucose uptake, and mitochondrial metabolism. The inconsistent efficacy of general antioxidant interventions likely reflects their limited spatial and temporal specificity and the risk of suppressing physiological redox signals. By contrast, exercise promotes mitochondrial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory adaptations across aging and several myopathies, although these benefits depend on sustained participation and support. A clearer definition of source-, compartment-, and target-specific ROS dynamics, combined with improved biosensors and redox-proteomic approaches, will be essential for developing therapies that limit pathological oxidation while preserving adaptive redox signaling in skeletal muscle.

articles.title: Serum untargeted metabolomics reveals infection-associated metabolic alterations in chikungunya, dengue, and influenza A virus infections.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and influenza A virus (IAV) infections may present with overlapping febrile symptoms during the early clinical phase. Routine laboratory tests provide useful clinical information but do not fully capture the circulating metabolic alterations associated with different viral infections. This study aimed to characterize serum metabolic profiles in CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics.

METHODS: In this comparative cross-sectional study, serum samples from patients with CHIKV, DENV, or IAV infection and healthy controls were analyzed using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Data were acquired in both positive and negative electrospray ionization modes, and the datasets were processed to characterize infection-associated metabolic alterations. Quality-control assessment, principal component analysis, orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis, differential metabolite screening with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway classification, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed.

RESULTS: Thousands of metabolic features were detected across positive and negative ion mode datasets, and annotated features were retained for downstream comparative analyses. Principal component analysis revealed group-dependent metabolic clustering with partial overlap between healthy controls and viral infection groups. Compared with healthy controls, 319, 300, and 295 differential metabolic features were identified in the CHIKV, DENV, and IAV groups, respectively, in positive ion mode, whereas 52, 40, and 33 differential features were identified in negative ion mode. Downregulated features predominated in the positive-ion comparisons, while the direction of metabolic alterations varied across groups in negative ion mode. KEGG pathway classification showed that differential metabolites were mapped to several major categories, including lipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, metabolism of cofactors and vitamins, xenobiotics biodegradation and metabolism, and chemical structure transformation maps. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis within the discovery cohort identified multiple metabolites with high discriminatory performance for distinguishing viral infection groups from healthy controls, although these findings were not independently validated. Additional mode-specific analyses further characterized shared differential metabolic features, their directional changes, and the distribution of candidate metabolites with high AUC values.

CONCLUSIONS: CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections were associated with broad serum metabolic alterations compared with healthy controls. The CHIKV-versus-control comparison yielded the largest number of altered metabolic features in the current dataset, although this observation should be interpreted cautiously because of unequal sampling proportions and the absence of direct comparisons between infection groups. Given the relatively small sample size, single-center and single-outbreak design, and lack of an independent validation cohort, the candidate metabolites identified in this study should be regarded as exploratory and require validation in larger independent cohorts and targeted metabolomic assays.

articles.title: Cytokine-mediated lipid storage disturbances in pancreatic beta-cells: the role of sphingosine-1 phosphate degradation.
articles.abstract: During type 1 diabetes (T1D) development pancreatic beta-cells are specifically destroyed due to the autoimmune process that is strongly mediated by proinflammatory cytokines released by activated immune cells. In the present study we evaluated how diabetogenic cytokines may influence intracellular distribution and storage of lipids. The cytokine-mediated changes in the expression of the key proteins regulating lipid storage were analyzed after acute vs. chronic exposure. Upon acute exposure to diabetogenic cytokines significant intracellular lipid rearrangements were observed. Cytokines induced formation of intracellular lipid deposits and lipid droplets (LD) in the early phase of cytokine toxicity. Although the LD biosynthetic machinery maintained its activity upon chronic cytokine exposure, no further increase in LD number was observed. This went along with an increased lipophagy. Interestingly, the cytokine-mediated changes in lipid storage and composition were at least partially regulated by the cell ability to degrade sphingosine-1 phosphate (S1P) by S1P lyase (SPL). High SPL activity correlated with a weaker LD formation, a stronger ability to form lipid rafts, more potent lipophagy and accumulation of proapoptotic ceramide in mitochondria, resulting in an accelerated cell death upon chronic exposure. In beta-cells in human islets analysed in pancreatic sections from non-diabetic donors, SPL was less abundantly expressed, while LD-mantle protein was well expressed. In beta-cells in islets of T1D pancreata a heterogeneous pattern of stronger SPL expression was observed. Thus, the lipid storage of pancreatic beta-cells is modified by proinflammatory milieu of T1D and likely dependent on the individual expression abundance of SPL.

articles.title: How to navigate infectious disease mathematical models: a guide for clinicians.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infectious diseases are characterised by transmission between hosts, creating population dynamics that distinguish them from non-communicable diseases. Because these dynamics are difficult to measure empirically, mathematical models are used to capture them and evaluate interventions, including scenarios that would be impractical or impossible to study directly. Clinicians increasingly encounter such modelling studies in decisions about clinical practice and public health, and need to be able to understand and interpret them.

OBJECTIVES: To introduce fundamental concepts in infectious disease transmission modelling and provide practical guidance for clinicians to understand modelling studies and critically interpret their findings in clinical and public health contexts.

SOURCES: This narrative review draws on peer-reviewed literature on infectious disease transmission modelling, using bacterial infections and interventions to reduce antimicrobial resistance (AMR) as illustrative examples.

CONTENT: We propose a practical checklist to support the interpretation of infectious disease modelling studies. The checklist guides clinicians in understanding which clinical or public health question a model addresses, which assumptions and parameters shape the model, how uncertain the results are, whether the model and its results are valid, and what the results mean for clinical and public health.

IMPLICATIONS: As with empirical studies, understanding how an infectious disease modelling study was conducted is essential for critically interpreting findings before applying them to practice. The proposed checklist offers clinicians a practical framework to do so.

articles.title: Clinical spectrum and outcomes of pediatric Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever: a systematic review and individual patient data analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever (CCHF) is a tick-borne infection generally assumed to be milder in children than in adults. The pediatric evidence is scattered across small series, and the determinants of severity and death remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: To define the clinical spectrum and outcomes of pediatric CCHF and to characterize fatal disease.

METHODS: Data sources: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, searched from inception to 5 December 2025 (PROSPERO CRD420261336826).

STUDY ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Original studies of any design reporting clinical data on laboratory-confirmed CCHF; reviews and studies without extractable pediatric data were excluded.

PARTICIPANTS: Patients younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed CCHF.Assessment of risk of bias: Two reviewers independently applied the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools for each study design.Methods of data synthesis: Descriptive synthesis of all included studies was combined with an individual-patient-data (IPD) analysis of children with paired clinical and outcome data. Survivors and non-survivors were compared descriptively; the small number of deaths precluded inferential testing.

RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies reporting 1,499 children were included, concentrated in Türkiye (1,261) and Iran (225). Pooled study-level mortality was 3.3%. The IPD cohort comprised 40 children from 26 studies (32 survivors, 8 non-survivors). Hypotension (5/8 vs 4/32), bradycardia (3/8 vs 2/32), major hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and shock were more frequent among fatal cases, likely reflecting advanced disease or late presentation. Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) was evaluated in 20 children and diagnosed in 16. Nausea and vomiting (18/40) and abdominal pain (8/40) were frequent yet absent from adult-based screening case definitions. Ribavirin and intravenous immunoglobulin were reported more often among survivors, although effectiveness could not be inferred.

CONCLUSIONS: Most pediatric patients with CCHF survive, but a severe hyperinflammatory course with frequent HLH can occur. Pediatric CCHF cannot be fully assessed with adult-derived frameworks, supporting pediatric-specific diagnostic and management strategies.

articles.title: Tnfaip2 Promotes the Antifungal Effects of Mannoprotein Against Cutaneous Candida albicans Infection by Enhancing NF-κB-mediated M1 Macrophage Polarization.
articles.abstract: Mannoprotein (MP), a major cell wall component of Candida albicans (C. albicans), has been increasingly recognized for its immunomodulatory properties, especially in inducing macrophage polarization. However, the molecular determinants that mediate MP-driven macrophage antifungal immunity remain poorly defined. Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling was performed to identify key responsive factors involved in macrophage polarization and to elucidate the signaling mechanisms that support enhanced antifungal defense. Tnfaip2 was identified as a prominently upregulated host-response molecule. In a murine model of cutaneous candidiasis, MP administration markedly reduced epidermal damage and fungal burden, accompanied by enhanced M1 polarization, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS)/inducible NO synthase (iNOS) levels, elevated superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, increased Ca2+/Mn2+ influx, and augmented NF-κB activation, whereas Tnfaip2 knockdown elicited the opposite effects. In macrophages, MP engaged the C-type lectin receptor Dectin-3, and Dectin-3 knockdown attenuated NF-κB activation and Tnfaip2 induction, placing Dectin-3 upstream of the NF-κB-Tnfaip2 axis. In conclusion, MP upregulates macrophage Tnfaip2, a molecule associated with M1 macrophage polarization and antifungal activity. These findings suggest that Tnfaip2 represents a potential mechanistic node through which MP regulates macrophage function, providing a theoretical basis for the further exploration of MP in the management of cutaneous C. albicans infection.

articles.title: Variation in Inferior Vena Cava Filter Retrieval Across U.S. Veterans Health Administration Facilities.
articles.journal: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters prevent pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients unable to receive anticoagulation but require prompt retrieval once protection is no longer needed. Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included Veterans who underwent IVC filter implantation at VA facilities between 2016 and 2023. Veterans who died within 90 days of implantation or lacked 1 year of follow-up were excluded. IVC filter implantation and retrieval were identified using procedure codes in the VA Corporate Data Warehouse. A multivariable Bayesian mixed-effects model estimated risk-adjusted retrieval rates across facilities. Logistic regression was performed to identify specific patient- and facility-level factors associated with non-retrieval.

RESULTS: Among 3,670 Veterans (median age 69 years; 95.9% male), retrieval occurred in 10.5% within 90 days, 22.2% within 1 year, and 24.7% overall. Risk-adjusted 1-year retrieval varied widely across facilities: 0-60%. Older veteran age (> 75 years), facility academic affiliation, and Southern census region were associated with lower retrieval, whereas implantation at higher-complexity facilities and pre-COVID years were associated with higher retrieval.

CONCLUSIONS: IVC filter retrieval rates among Veterans remain low but exceed those reported in non-VA Medicare cohorts. Substantial inter-facility variation highlights opportunities to standardize structured device surveillance, with clear responsibility for follow-up.

articles.title: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy type 1 associated with a novel RANBPe2 variant: Clinical, radiological, molecular, and computational analysis.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: RANBP2/Nup358 is the largest human nucleoporin and a major structural and functional component of the cytoplasmic filaments of the nuclear pore complex. Heterozygous missense variants in RANBP2 are associated with Acute Necrotizing Encephalopathy type 1 (ANE1), a rare autosomal dominant pediatric encephalopathy often triggered by viral infection and characterized by rapid neurological deterioration and symmetric thalamic lesions. In this study, we report a 5-year-old girl who presented with status epilepticus following fever and viral nasopharyngitis. Brain MRI revealed bilateral thalamic and brainstem lesions consistent with acute necrotizing encephalopathy initially suggestive of Leigh syndrome. Full mitochondrial DNA sequencing, long-range PCR, and quantification of mitochondrial DNA copy number revealed no pathogenic mtDNA variants, no detectable large-scale mtDNA rearrangement, and no mtDNA depletion. Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel heterozygous missense variant in RANBP2, c.3163C > T (p.Pro1055Ser), affecting a highly conserved proline residue located in the FG repeat region in the inter-domain linker between the N-terminal domain and the first Ran-binding domain (RanBD1). The variant was not detected in either tested parent. "Residue 1055 was predicted to lie within a low-confidence, intrinsically disordered region. Therefore, the structural models were considered descriptive and were not interpreted as evidence of mutation-induced structural or interaction changes. The clinicoradiological phenotype and genetic findings support p.Pro1055Ser as a candidate ANE1-associated variant, although its pathogenic role remains unproven due to the absence of variant-specific functional validation. This report expands the spectrum of RANBP2 variants observed in ANE-compatible phenotypes.

articles.title: Evaluation of a new ELISA for fully automated detection of anti-GAD autoantibodies in type 1 diabetes and anti-GAD-associated neurological diseases.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Autoantibodies against glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) support diagnostics and classification of type 1 diabetes (T1D) and anti-GAD antibody-associated neurological diseases. This study evaluated the analytical and clinical performance of the newly developed, IVDR-compliant Euroimmun Anti-GAD ELISA, which is based on a bridge format and enables fully automated sample processing. Analytical assessment included precision, interference, and linearity. Clinical performance and comparison with the predecessor ELISA and the Medipan CentAK anti-GAD M radioimmunoassay (RIA) were examined using sera from patients with T1D (median age at diagnosis: 11 years; median diabetes duration: 4 years), stiff-person spectrum and other neurological conditions, latent autoimmune diabetes in adults, Addison's disease, various non-T1D control groups, and samples from the Islet Autoantibody Standardization Program (IASP). The new ELISA demonstrated excellent analytical characteristics (intra-/inter-lot CV ≤ 6%), linearity (5-2000 IU/mL), and no interference from hemolysis, lipemia, or bilirubin. Diagnostic sensitivity reached 59.9% in the clinical T1D cohort (newly diagnosed T1D: 73.9%) and 84.0% in IASP samples, with a specificity of 97.3%. Diagnostic sensitivity for anti-GAD antibody-associated neurological diseases was 74.8%. Concordance with the predecessor ELISA was almost perfect (98.7%, κ = 0.968) and was supported by strong quantitative correlation. Comparison with the RIA showed substantial agreement (83.3-84.7%, κ ≈  0.7) and higher sensitivity of the ELISA, detecting additional, predominantly low-level-positive T1D samples. In conclusion, the new Euroimmun Anti-GAD ELISA provides strong analytical and diagnostic performance for T1D and anti-GAD antibody-associated neurological diseases. Its rapid, fully automated format supports efficient high-throughput testing for routine diagnostics and population-based screening. Parallel testing for multiple pancreatic islet autoantibodies may enhance diagnostic coverage and aid clinical decision-making.

articles.title: Continuous Kidney Replacement Therapy in Patients Requiring Mechanical Circulatory Support: A Practical Review.
articles.journal: American journal of kidney diseases : the official journal of the National Kidney Foundation
articles.abstract: Mechanical circulatory support (MCS) devices, including intra-aortic balloon pumps, micro-axial flow pumps, venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and ventricular assist devices, have become increasingly common in managing advanced heart failure and cardiogenic shock. Acute kidney injury (AKI) occurs in up to 85% of MCS patients, with 30-45% treated with kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Continuous KRT (CKRT) is generally preferred in this population due to superior hemodynamic tolerability and precise volume control. However, providing CKRT to MCS patients presents unique challenges, including securing a functional vascular access, circuit integration considerations, dual-device blood flow optimization, and anticoagulation management. This review provides practical guidance for nephrologists caring for patients treated with both MCS and CKRT. We describe current MCS technologies and discuss evidence-based approaches to CKRT prescription including modality selection, timing of initiation, vascular access techniques, and anticoagulation strategies. We also address volume management, safety monitoring, and troubleshooting common complications. Despite high short-term mortality, many survivors achieve renal recovery by hospital discharge, emphasizing the importance of optimized CKRT delivery in this complex population.

articles.title: Key molecules, diagnostic models and immune microenvironment analysis of ischemic stroke based on pyroptosis and immunosuppression-related genes.
articles.abstract: Ischemic Stroke (IS) represents a significant global health challenge due to its high morbidity and mortality rates, necessitating an urgent need for enhanced diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. The present study aimed to construct a multi-gene diagnostic model for IS while elucidating the underlying molecular mechanisms and identifying critical genes associated with pyroptosis and immune suppression. Utilizing data from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) repositories, specifically datasets GSE16561 and GSE22255, we initially identified 5,992 nominally significant differentially expressed candidate genes that were subsequently cross-referenced with gene sets related to pyroptosis and immune suppression. Employing Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), we isolated pivotal genes within key modules, which, through rigorous cross-validation combined with protein-protein interaction networks and multiple machine learning algorithms, culminated in the identification of six core model genes: TNF, STAT3, MMP9, MYD88, TLR2, and JAK2. These genes demonstrated significant involvement in inflammatory responses, lipid metabolism, and Toll-like receptor signaling pathways, contributing to the construction of a diagnostic model. This model exhibited favorable discriminative performance in the training dataset; however, external evaluation in an independent cohort (GSE22255) with fixed model coefficients did not support its cross-cohort generalizability. Furthermore, consistency clustering revealed two distinct IS subtypes characterized by unique molecular profiles, while immune cell infiltration analysis highlighted notable alterations in the IS immune microenvironment. Collectively, our findings identify candidate biomarkers and two exploratory expression-based subtypes associated with IS, and reveal immune microenvironment alterations; these results are hypothesis-generating, and their diagnostic and therapeutic implications require functional and prospective clinical validation.

articles.title: The World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement: 2026 update.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the 5 years since the publication of the original ADHD International Consensus Statement, a great deal of new evidence has emerged. This updated consensus statement reflects the current state of the science with respect to ADHD, with a goal of reducing misconceptions and stigma around the disorder.

METHODS: Studies eligible for inclusion were published between January 1, 2021 and July 1, 2025 and were either: 1) large cohort studies of 2000 or more participants, or 2) meta-analyses of at least 5 studies or 2000 participants in which publication bias was considered. Eligible studies were summarized and consolidated by theme. Manuscript contents were reviewed and approved by 118 authors from 29 countries and 6 continents.

RESULTS: Two hundred and fifty-two empirically-supported statements were generated from these studies, offering readers an up-to-date understanding of the most robust findings in the areas of prevalence, how genes and environmental factors shape ADHD, psychiatric and somatic comorbidities, cognitive and neurological differences among individuals with ADHD, functional outcomes, and treatments for the disorder.

CONCLUSIONS: Many of the conclusions of the original Consensus Statement are supported, but this update adds important nuance to some findings as a result of more recent evidence. It also highlights a few areas in which the balance of findings has shifted in the last 5 years, providing a transparent overview of the current scientific state of the field.

articles.title: A Metabolite-Centered Framework for Microbiota-Gut-Brain Communication Linking Constrained Signaling to Behavior and Stress Physiology.
articles.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis links gut microbial activity with host neurophysiology and behavior, but its mechanistic interpretation remains fragmented across individual metabolites, biological compartments, and experimental systems. Here, we propose a metabolite-centered conceptual framework that organizes current evidence according to the constraints that determine whether microbial metabolic activity is translated into host effects, including metabolite production and host transformation, bioavailability and barrier access, host sensing, cross-system integration, and ultimately phenotype. Using short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan metabolic pathways, bile acids, neurotransmitter-related compounds, and emerging microbial signals as representative examples, we synthesize evidence for receptor-mediated, metabolic, neuroimmune, neuroendocrine, and barrier-dependent mechanisms. We further distinguish microbiota-level from metabolite-specific causality and preclinical from human evidence across stress reactivity, affective and stress-coping responses, social interaction, learning and memory, feeding, and sleep/circadian regulation. Finally, we evaluate the translational potential of metabolite-targeted interventions and biomarkers while highlighting unresolved challenges related to source attribution, bioavailability, species translation, and causal inference. Rather than providing another catalogue of microbial metabolites, this Review presents a mechanistic framework that links microbial metabolism to neural and behavioral outcomes while identifying the evidence needed to advance toward reproducible and clinically relevant applications.

articles.title: Enzymatic strategies for PET valorization: Advances in discovery, engineering, and cyanobacterial chassis development.
articles.abstract: The global accumulation of plastic waste has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of replacing conventional mechanical and chemical recycling. During the past decade, enzymatic plastic biodegradation has rapidly evolved from the identification of individual depolymerases to an interdisciplinary research field integrating environmental microbiology, artificial intelligence, protein engineering, systems biology, and synthetic biology. Despite remarkable progress, current research remains largely fragmented, with enzyme discovery, catalytic optimization, and downstream plastic valorization often being developed independently, thereby limiting the establishment of integrated plastic biomanufacturing platforms. In this review, we critically synthesize advances in plastic-degrading enzymes, covering meta-omics and AI-assisted enzyme discovery, protein engineering strategies that improve catalytic efficiency, thermostability, and substrate specificity, and metabolic engineering approaches for assimilating plastic-derived monomers into value-added products. Rather than viewing these advances as separate research directions, we propose an integrated biotechnology framework that connects environmental enzyme mining, AI-driven protein engineering, microbial metabolic rewiring, and photosynthetic cell factories into a unified plastic-to-product strategy. Recent progress in heterologous protein secretion and metabolic engineering in cyanobacteria supports the continued exploration of solar-powered microbial platforms; however, complete PET-to-product bioconversion in cyanobacteria remains conceptual and has not yet been experimentally demonstrated. We anticipate that the convergence of multi-omics, artificial intelligence, enzyme engineering, and synthetic biology will shift the field from improving individual plastic-degrading enzymes toward constructing complete microbial plastic bioconversion systems, thereby accelerating the realization of a sustainable circular plastic bioeconomy.

articles.title: Natural product-derived compounds as modulators of the Klotho family: Molecular mechanisms and evidence across aging-related and disease models.
articles.abstract: Klotho is a longevity-associated protein involved in regulating oxidative stress, inflammation, fibrosis, mineral metabolism, and cellular senescence. Reduced Klotho expression is associated with aging and age-related disorders, including chronic kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, and neurodegenerative diseases. Consequently, plant- and fungal-derived natural products have attracted interest as potential modulators of Klotho expression and related signaling pathways. This review summarizes evidence on how natural products may influence klotho expression and related signaling pathways through epigenetic mechanisms, including DNA methylation and histone acetylation; transcriptional regulation involving activating transcription factor 3 (ATF3)/c-Jun and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ); and modulation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/Akt-forkhead box O (FOXO) axis. Other reported effects involve inflammation- and fibrosis-related pathways, including nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT), and transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) signaling. Some compounds have also been associated with changes in α-Klotho-FGF23 signaling, which regulates mineral homeostasis, and β-Klotho-dependent FGF21 signaling, which contributes to metabolic regulation. Overall, preclinical findings suggest that natural products can modulate Klotho expression and related pathways, although evidence varies across compounds and experimental models. Concurrent changes in Klotho and disease outcomes do not establish direct causal mediation, and improvements in tissue injury or oxidative stress do not necessarily indicate delayed biological aging or healthier aging. Human evidence remains limited, highlighting the need for well-controlled clinical studies using standardized preparations and validated Klotho-related biomarkers.

articles.title: Homelessness Is Associated With Increased Wound Complications and Revision Following Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: People experiencing homelessness face barriers to musculoskeletal care and may be at increased risk for adverse outcomes after major orthopaedic surgery. Outcomes after elective primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) remain poorly characterized in this population. We examined associations between homelessness and 90-day medical and 1- and 2-year surgical outcomes after primary THA.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was performed using a national healthcare database. Adults undergoing primary THA were stratified by documented homelessness within six months preceding surgery. A one-to-one propensity score matching was performed on age, sex, race/ethnicity, body mass index, and cardiovascular, renal, hepatic, nutritional, substance use, and psychiatric comorbidities. From 1,585 homeless and 287,986 non-homeless patients, matching yielded 1,582 per cohort with well-balanced baseline characteristics (all standardized mean differences less than 0.1). Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated; significance was set at P < 0.05.

RESULTS: At 90 days, homeless patients had a higher risk of sepsis (RR 2.20, 95% CI 1.20 to 4.04), surgical site infection (RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.13 to 4.64), and wound dehiscence (RR 1.95, 95% CI 1.25 to 3.04). At one year, homelessness was associated with a higher risk of revision THA (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.05 to 2.29), periprosthetic joint infection (RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.00 to 2.36), and wound dehiscence (RR 2.18, 95% CI 1.37 to 3.49). At two years, elevated revision (RR 1.72, 95% CI 1.08 to 2.73) and wound dehiscence (RR 2.26, 95% CI 1.36 to 3.76) persisted. There were no significant differences observed in transfusion, pneumonia, or emergency department utilization.

CONCLUSIONS: After matching on comorbidities, substance use, and psychiatric conditions, homelessness remained independently associated with a persistent two-fold elevation in wound complications and a 55 to 72% increase in revision risk through two years following primary THA. Housing status may warrant consideration in preoperative risk stratification and postoperative care planning, although prospective work is needed to clarify mechanisms and whether targeted interventions modify these associations.

articles.title: Mean 6-Year Follow-Up Outcomes of Two-Stage Revision for the Treatment of Fungal Periprosthetic Joint Infection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fungal periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) often results in severe outcomes. However, few studies have reported the outcomes of two-stage revision for fungal PJI at a mean follow-up of six years.

METHODS: Following institutional review board approval, we conducted a retrospective review of our institutional periprosthetic joint infection registry, identifying all patients who underwent two-stage revision arthroplasty for culture-confirmed chronic PJI between April 1, 2004, and April 1, 2023. The final cohort comprised 58 fungal PJI cases and 183 non-fungal PJI cases. Treatment success was defined according to Delphi consensus criteria, with survival analysis employed to determine infection-free survival rates.

RESULTS: During post-two-stage-revision survival analysis, most treatment failures occurred within five years following initial spacer implantation. Non-fungal PJIs demonstrated significantly higher overall success rates than fungal PJIs (87.4 versus 41.4%; P < 0.0001), with relapse occurring in 58.6% (34 of 58) of fungal PJI cases at a median of 14 months versus 12.6% (23 of 183) of non-fungal PJI cases at a median of 13 months. Survival analysis further revealed superior infection-free survival for Candidal PJIs compared to filamentous fungal PJIs (P = 0.034), where recurrence affected filamentous fungal PJIs (11 of 15) at a median of six months versus 53.5% (23 of 43) of Candidal PJIs at a median of 21 months.

CONCLUSIONS: A two-stage revision arthroplasty represents the optimal treatment protocol for PJIs. Patients who have fungal PJI demonstrate higher failure rates following two-stage revision compared to non-fungal PJI cases. Most treatment failures occur within five years post-revision, establishing five-year follow-up as the critical benchmark for evaluating PJI treatment outcomes. Furthermore, PJIs caused by filamentous fungi are markedly more difficult to eradicate than Candidal PJIs, exhibiting substantially worse clinical outcomes and survival rates.

articles.title: Proximal Realignment of the Extensor Mechanism During Total Knee Arthroplasty for Chronic Patellar Dislocation in Knee Arthritis: Results at a Median Follow-Up of Four Years.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proximal realignment of the extensor mechanism (PREM) can anatomically reduce the patella; however, its effectiveness in the setting of knee arthritis remains unclear. This study aimed to determine complication rate following PREM combined with total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for knee arthritis with chronic patellar dislocation (CPD), prosthetic survival, and functional outcomes.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted between September 2012 and June 2024. The study included 34 knees that underwent PREM during TKA for knee arthritis with CPD, a median follow-up of 48 months (IQR, 26 to 82). The PREM-related complications and prosthetic survival were recorded. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Knee Society Score (KSS), range of motion (ROM), and extension lag.

RESULTS: Complications secondary to PREM occurred in five knees (14.7%, 5 of 34). In two knees, infection required debridement, antibiotic therapy, and implant retention; two knees underwent manipulation under anesthesia for stiffness; and one knee developed recurrent patellar dislocation without any treatment. The estimated 5-year survival with reoperation as the endpoint was 88.0% (95% confidence interval [CI], 77.7 to 99.8), whereas survival with recurrent patellar dislocation as the endpoint was 96.9% (95% CI, 91.0 to 100.0). The Knee Score and Function Score components of the KSS improved from preoperative medians of 35 points (interquartile range [IQR], 29 to 57.5) and 30 points (IQR, 20 to 40) to medians of 85 points (IQR, 80 to 88) and 80 points (IQR, 71.3 to 83.8) at final follow-up, respectively (P < 0.001). Median ROM improved from 90° (IQR, 70 to 90) preoperatively to 102.5° (IQR, 95 to 110) postoperatively (P < 0.001). Except for the single knee with recurrent patellar dislocation, no extension lag occurred in the remaining knees.

CONCLUSIONS: Proximal realignment of the extensor mechanism during TKA for CPD in knee arthritis demonstrated acceptable complication rates, prosthetic survival, and functional recovery at medium-term follow-up.

articles.title: Molecular basis of behavioral and cognitive changes induced by neurotropic viruses.
articles.abstract: Neurotropic viruses induce behavioral and cognitive alterations through diverse molecular and cellular mechanisms that extend beyond simple neuronal damage. Comparative analysis of rabies virus (RABV), pseudorabies virus (PRV), Borna disease virus (BoDV-1), SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus (NiV), West Nile virus (WNV) and Herpes Simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) reveals distinct pathogenic strategies targeting specific neural circuits. While neuroinflammation characterized by microglial activation, astrocytic responses, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production contributes significantly to synaptic and network dysfunction in WNV and NiV infections, other mechanisms predominate in different pathogens. RABV selectively disrupts cholinergic, serotonergic, and glutamate/GABAergic pathways while preserving neuronal integrity to facilitate transmission, whereas BoDV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 induce dopaminergic and serotonergic dysfunctions through persistent immune activation and endothelial damage. Additionally, systemic factors such as the gut-brain axis and microbiome alterations, particularly evident in SARS-CoV-2 infection, modulate neurotransmitter metabolism and neuroimmune responses. Considering the lack of even diffuse neuronal loss observed during infection, behavioral changes may arise more from selective, circuit-dependent vulnerabilities, involving specific disruptions to emotion, cognition, and motor control networks. To provide a clear review of the knowledge regarding how targeted neuronal population alterations translate into behavioral phenotypes, we here integrate molecular, cellular, and systems-level insights across these seven neurotropic viruses used as models, with the aim of identifying common pathways linking infection to behavioral changes and cognitive dysfunction. Understanding these discrete mechanisms ranging from acute synaptic manipulation to long-lasting neuroimmune dysregulation is essential for developing therapeutic strategies that address both the infectious agent and the specific neural networks mediating acute disturbances and long-term neurological sequelae.

articles.title: An accurate multiplex orthopoxvirus IgG panel for distinguishing vaccinated or exposed individuals from naïve individuals using machine-learning-guided feature selection.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a major human orthopoxvirus (OPXV) disease in the post-smallpox-eradication era. Rapid, scalable serology that distinguishes immunologically naive individuals from those with prior OPXV vaccination or exposure is important for surveillance, outbreak response, and vaccine-program evaluation.

METHODS: We evaluated a custom 15-plex Luminex xMAP IgG assay comprising 11 recombinant OPXV antigens (VARV: M1R, B6R, A36R; VACV: A33R, A27L, L1R; MPXV: M1R, B6R, A35R, A29, E8L) and four internal controls. The primary cross-sectional analysis included 229 de-identified human serum or plasma specimens provisionally classified as naive (born after 1972; n = 116), presumed smallpox-vaccinated (born before 1972; n = 89), or MPXV-exposed/infected (n = 24). Median fluorescence intensity (MFI) values were analyzed using partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and Boruta/Random Forest feature selection under stratified nested cross-validation. Performance metrics included apparent sensitivity, apparent specificity, overall accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), and balanced accuracy.

RESULTS: The 11-antigen profile broadly separated naive specimens from presumed smallpox-vaccinated and MPXV-exposed/infected specimens. Using per-antigen cutoffs derived from the presumed naive group, the highest apparent discrimination was observed for MPXV A35R, VARV A36R, VACV A33R, and MPXV B6R. Boruta/Random Forest analysis identified a compact five-antigen signature - MPXV A35R, VARV A36R, MPXV B6R, MPXV E8L, and VACV A33R - that achieved 89.52% overall accuracy and 83.07% balanced accuracy for three-class discrimination and 96.51% overall accuracy with 96.46% balanced accuracy for binary discrimination (naive vs. OPXV-reactive).

CONCLUSIONS: The selected five-antigen profile yielded 96.51% binary classification accuracy against the supplied cohort labels but does not establish clinical differentiation between vaccination and infection.

articles.title: Urate oxidase modulates proline homeostasis and cold tolerance in the small brown planthopper Laodelphax striatellus.
articles.journal: Comparative biochemistry and physiology. Part B, Biochemistry & molecular biology
articles.abstract: The small brown planthopper (SBPH), Laodelphax striatellus (Hemiptera: Delphacidae), is a major rice pest that can overwinter in high-latitude regions, but the physiological mechanisms underlying its cold tolerance remain unclear. Here, we identified and functionally characterized three purine metabolism genes (purine nucleoside phosphorylase (LsPNP), urate oxidase (LsUO), and 2-oxo-4-hydroxy-4-carboxy-5-ureidoimidazoline decarboxylase (LsURAD)) and investigated their roles in development, reproduction, and cold stress response through integrated RNA interference (RNAi), enzyme concentration, and metabolomic analyses. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that these genes are evolutionarily conserved among delphacid planthoppers. Spatiotemporal expression profiling showed that all three genes were more highly expressed in adult females than in nymphs.
