Among female tissues, LsPNP and LsURAD were predominantly expressed in the salivary gland, whereas LsUO was most highly expressed in the gut, suggesting both tissue-specific and developmental stage-specific functions. RNAi-mediated silencing of LsUO increased mortality at -15 °C, shortened adult longevity, and reduced female fecundity. Metabolomic analysis revealed that LsUO knockdown disrupted amino acid homeostasis, causing a significant decrease in proline and significant increases in leucine, phenylalanine, valine, and tyrosine, indicating a coordinated pattern of amino acid redistribution. Notably, exogenous proline supplementation significantly decreased the overall mortality of nymphs under acute cold shock. Collectively, these findings suggest that LsUO is associated with cold tolerance, at least in part through proline homeostasis, and identify LsUO as a candidate for further functional dissection.

articles.title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
authors: Zero Iodine Contrast EVAR Collaborative Study Group
articles.journal: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

CONCLUSION: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

articles.title: Psychological distress and vascular reactivity to mental stress as determinants of outcomes in coronary artery disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Psychological stress and abnormal cardiovascular reactivity to mental stress are both associated with adverse outcomes in coronary artery disease (CAD), but their independent and combined prognostic significance remains unclear.

METHODS: We studied 648 participants with stable CAD from two prospective cohorts. A psychological distress score (PDS) was derived as a rank-based composite of depressive symptoms, anxiety, anger, perceived stress, and post-traumatic stress symptoms evaluated using questionnaires, with higher scores indicati greater distress. A cardiovascular reactivity risk (CRR) score was derived from laboratory mental stress testing by assigning quartile-based points for three maladaptive responses, previously shown to be associated with adverse outcomes: lower rate-pressure product reactivity, greater stress-related decline in flow-mediated dilation, and lower peripheral arterial tonometry ratio, a measure of digital vasoconstriction. CRR scores ranged from 0 to 9, with higher scores indicating more maladaptive reactivity. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or heart failure hospitalization. Fine-Gray models tested associations with MACE after adjustment for demographic and clinical risk factors.

RESULTS: Mean age of the cohort was 58.7 ± 10.1 years; 32.4% were women and 40.3% were Black. The PDS and CRR scores were weakly correlated. Over a median of 5.9 years, 121 MACE occurred. In mutually adjusted models, each 1-SD higher PDS was associated with a 20% higher risk of MACE (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.11-1.30), and each 1-SD higher CRR with a 44% higher risk (sHR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.33-1.56; both p < 0.01). There was no statistically significant evidence of nonlinearity for PDS or CRR. Addition of CRR to the base model increased the 5-year AUC from 0.77 to 0.79 (ΔAUC = 0.03; p = 0.03), whereas PDS alone did not materially improve discrimination. In complementary median-defined analyses, participants with high PDS and high CRR had the highest observed risk compared with those with low PDS and low CRR (sHR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.93-3.09), without significant multiplicative interaction.

CONCLUSIONS: In stable CAD, psychological distress and maladaptive cardiovascular reactivity were independent determinants of incident MACE, indicating that both the burden of psychological distress during life and the pathophysiologic reactivity to stress are indicators of psychological stress-mediated residual risk in CAD.

articles.title: Low-glycemic load diet enhances pancreatic β-cell function through the fucose-Rnf183 axis in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Our previous studies demonstrated that low-glycemic load (GL) diets reduced diabetes risk and promoted remission in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: Serum samples from newly diagnosed T2DM patients with random 3-month low-GL dietary intervention or conventional energy-restricted diet were analyzed using LC-MS-based metabolomics. High glucose (HG)-treated MIN6 cells with or without fucose were used to assess β-cell function, apoptosis, and transcriptomic sequencing. Rnf183 was knocked down in MIN6 cells.

RESULTS: Metabolomic analysis revealed that metabolites identified by LC-MS were mostly classified as carboxylic acids and derivatives, fatty acyls, and glycerophospholipids. Fucose exhibited the highest VIP score among all differential metabolites and was significantly upregulated in T2DM patients with a low-GL diet compared to those without a low-GL diet. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that fucose-associated fructose and mannose metabolism was affected by the low-GL diet. Fucose enhanced the expression of key β-cell functional genes (Pdx1, Nkx6.1, Mafa, and Insulin2) and attenuated HG-induced apoptosis in MIN6 cells. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that fucose regulated T2DM progression-related pathways (Notch signaling and insulin secretion) and protein ubiquitination in HG-induced MIN6 cells. Correspondingly, fucose reduced global ubiquitination of MIN6 cells and downregulated ubiquitination regulator Rnf183. Rnf183 knockdown increased expression levels of key β-cell functional genes in HG-treated MIN6 cells.

CONCLUSIONS: Low-GL diet reshapes the serum metabolome of T2DM patients and increases fucose abundance. Fucose enhances pancreatic β-cell function, partly through suppression of ubiquitination and Rnf183. These findings provide mechanistic insights into dietary interventions for diabetes management.

articles.title: Bergapten ameliorates type 2 diabetes mellitus by modulating hepatic glycogen metabolism, inflammation, and endoplasmic reticulum stress: involvement of AKT signaling.
articles.abstract: Bergapten (BP), derived from traditional Chinese medicinal herbs, exhibits therapeutic efficacy across multiple diseases. Its specific impact on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and the underlying mechanisms, including the involvement of the serine/threonine kinase AKT, remain unclear. A T2DM animal model was induced using a high-fat diet and streptozotocin injection, and an insulin-resistant cell model was established via glucosamine treatment. Chronic treatment with BP for eight weeks ameliorated hyperglycemia and dyslipidemia and restored glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity in a murine model of T2DM. Histologically, BP reduced hepatic steatosis and preserved hepatic glycogen reserves. At the hepatic level, BP treatment was accompanied by increased GSK3β Ser9 phosphorylation, reduced phosphorylation of the inflammatory mediators IκBα and NF-κB, decreased mRNA expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6), and reduced expression of the endoplasmic reticulum stress-related proteins GRP78 and IRE1α. Network pharmacology and pathway enrichment identified PI3K-AKT signaling as a pathway of interest, while molecular docking suggested a potential BP-AKT1 interaction. In insulin-resistant HepG2 cells, the AKT inhibitor MK-2206 attenuated several BP-associated effects. Taken together, these findings are consistent with an involvement of AKT signaling in the effects of BP on hepatic glycogen-related changes, inflammation, and endoplasmic reticulum stress in T2DM. These results provide a basis for further investigation of BP in T2DM and its associated hepatic metabolic dysfunction.

articles.title: Beyond catheter insertion: Maintenance and economic evidence in nurse-led vascular access units.
How I do… endoscopic breast revision surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of gynecology obstetrics and human reproduction
articles.abstract: Breast implant reconstruction is widely used but is associated with complications in approximately 30% of cases, with capsular contracture being the most common. Its incidence increases substantially after radiotherapy and may lead to aesthetic deformity, pain, and revision surgery. This article describes a minimally invasive endoscopic approach to breast revision surgery, including capsulotomy and capsulectomy. The technique is performed through a small incision placed away from the implant pocket, preferably using a pre-existing axillary or inframammary scar. A single-port device provides access for endoscopic instruments, while insufflation at 10 mmHg improves operative exposure and facilitates identification of capsular retractions. The main advantages of this approach are improved surgical ergonomics, enhanced visualization, precise dissection, and effective hemostasis. Endoscopic visualization also facilitates surgical education by allowing the entire operating team to follow the procedure. Implant insertion can be performed using a Keller Funnel®-type sleeve, enabling a no-touch technique. The procedure takes approximately 40 minutes and can generally be performed on an outpatient basis. Postoperative complications remain similar to those of conventional surgery, including hematoma, seroma, and prosthetic infection. Endoscopic revision surgery is a promising alternative to conventional surgery, particularly for minimizing scars near the implant. However, its clinical benefits and potential reduction in complications require confirmation through larger cohort studies.

articles.title: Diagnostic performance of an automated qRT-PCR assay using a peripheral blood host 5-mRNA signature for active tuberculosis: a single-center prospective cohort study and external validation in public databases.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis remains a major global public health concern. Current sputum-based etiological assays have limited diagnostic performance in patients with smear-negative tuberculosis, atypical clinical manifestations, or restricted access to specimens containing Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB). Novel molecular tools for clinical triage in healthcare settings are urgently needed.

METHODS: A total of 438 participants were enrolled and classified into five groups based on comprehensive clinical data: confirmed active tuberculosis (Group 1), suspected tuberculosis after antibiotic treatment (Group 2), undetermined diagnosis (Group 3), non-tuberculous infectious disease controls (Group 4), and non-infectious controls (Group 5). mRNA expression levels of FCGR1A, FCGR1B, GBP5, GBP6, and CXCL10 in peripheral blood were measured, and the TB active score (TBA-Score) was calculated to identify TB infection. Multiple public microarray and RNA-seq datasets were used for external validation of the diagnostic performance of this 5-host-gene signature for tuberculosis infection.

RESULTS: The TBA-Score was significantly elevated in patients with active tuberculosis and effectively discriminated active tuberculosis from non-tuberculous infectious and non-infectious controls. The AUC for Group 1 versus Group 4 was 0.905 (95% CI, 0.850-0.959), with a sensitivity of 83.6% and specificity of 95.1%; the AUC for Group 1 versus Group 5 was 0.916 (95% CI, 0.869-0.962), with a sensitivity of 83.6% and specificity of 90.6%. During external validation, this 5-mRNA signature retained robust discriminative ability across six public transcriptomic datasets, with AUC values ranging from 0.824 to 0.970 for distinguishing active tuberculosis from latent tuberculosis infection.

CONCLUSIONS: This automated qRT-PCR system enables rapid detection using peripheral-blood-derived 5-mRNA TBA-Score. The signature shows cross-platform and multi-ethnic population reproducibility, supporting its further evaluation for non-sputum near-point-of-care TB testing.

articles.title: In vitro simulated digestive properties of degraded sweet corn cob polysaccharides and their mechanisms for alleviating type II diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the in vitro simulated digestion properties of degraded sweet corn cob polysaccharides (UE-DSCCP-A) and elucidate the underlying mechanisms by which UE-DSCCP-A alleviates type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The structural changes and biological activities of UE-DSCCP-A, including in vitro hypoglycemic and antioxidant activities, were evaluated using simulated digestion models representing the oral, gastric, and small intestine environments. The results indicated that digestion reduced the molecular weight of UE-DSCCP-A from 12.9 to 8.26 kDa, accompanied by an increase in reducing sugar content from 0.341 to 0.836 mg/mL. In vitro analysis revealed that UE-DSCCP-A retained its antioxidant and hypoglycemic activities following simulated digestion. Furthermore, UE-DSCCP-A exhibited therapeutic potential in alleviating T2DM symptoms through various pathways. It significantly inhibited the activities of glycolytic enzymes in the small intestine and alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses in the pancreas and kidneys. In the colon of T2DM mice, UE-DSCCP-A markedly attenuated oxidative stress and inflammation through modulation of the toll-like receptor 4/nuclear factor kappa-B signaling pathway. Additionally, UE-DSCCP-A decreased myosin light-chain kinase levels and increased the expression of intestinal tight junction proteins (zonula occludens-1 and occludin), thereby ameliorating T2DM-induced intestinal barrier dysfunction and reducing the translocation of enterotoxins into the bloodstream. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insights into the antidiabetic effects of plant-derived polysaccharides, and establish a theoretical foundation for developing UE-DSCCP-A as a natural hypoglycemic functional food.

articles.title: Echocardiographic Left Atrial Stiffness Index as a Predictor of All-Cause Mortality in Non-Ischemic Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Reliable predictors of adverse outcomes in non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (NIDCM) remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the association between the left atrial stiffness index (LASI) and all-cause mortality in patients with NIDCM and to assess its prognostic value beyond established left atrial and diastolic markers.

METHODS: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively recruited cohort of patients diagnosed with NIDCM between 2018 and 2022. All patients underwent comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography at the time of diagnosis. Left atrial (LA) strain was measured retrospectively from stored baseline echocardiograms using two-dimensional speckle-tracking analysis, and LASI was calculated as the ratio of E/e' to LA reservoir strain. Multivariable analyses were performed to identify variables independently associated with all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Among 200 patients (mean age 61.7 years; 40% women), 33 (16.5%) died over a median follow-up of 43.8 months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, variables independently associated with all-cause mortality were LASI (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.92, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.33-2.77), age (HR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.08) and right ventricular-pulmonary artery (RV-PA) coupling index (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.07-0.89); the model showed good discrimination (optimism-corrected C-index 0.766). LASI remained independently associated with mortality when modeled together with left atrial volume index (LAVi) and with E/e'.

CONCLUSION: In NIDCM, LASI provides prognostic information for all-cause mortality beyond other morphological and functional LA markers. Given the single-center design and the limited number of events, these findings warrant external validation.

articles.title: Mitral Annular Calcification - Association with Comorbidities and Left Ventricular Mechanics.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is common in the general population, more pronounced in women and patients with left ventricular (LV) pressure overload conditions, which may increase stress on the mitral valve inducing and exacerbating the calcification process. The pathogenesis of MAC is presumed multifactorial but remains poorly understood. Women display a different LV response to pressure overload compared to men, but this association has rather not been thoroughly investigated.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The DANCAVAS (Danish Cardiovascular Screening) pilot study included randomly selected individuals from the general population aged 60-75 years to undergo a computed tomography (CT)-based screening program. MAC was graded by mitral valve calcification (MVC) score assessed by CT and compared to echocardiographic data. Among 463 participants, MAC was found in 165 (35.6%) with MVC scores ≤100 AU in 20.7%, 100-400 AU in 8.2% and >400 AU in 6.7%. While MAC was most prevalent in men, women presented with higher MVC scores and severe MAC on echocardiography. Patients with MAC were elderly with cardiovascular risk factors. Concentric LV geometry with smaller LV cavities and higher relative wall thickness were highly associated with MAC (p<0.001). From multivariable analyses, relative wall thickness and the mechanical load on the mitral valve (i.e. StressMV) strongly associated with MAC (SD-adjusted OR 28.8, 95% CI [15.6;53.5] and 2.97 [2.25;3.91], respectively) and MAC severity (10.9 [7.74;15.5] and 2.98 [2.33;3.82], respectively). The predictive performance was high with AUC of 0.78 [0.74;0.82] by including StressMV in the model of age, sex and cardiovascular comorbidity (p<0.001). However, relative wall thickness had distinctive importance (AUC 0.96 [0.94;0.98], p<0.001) regardless of sex.

CONCLUSION: MAC is common in the general population with the highest prevalence among men. LV geometry and the pressure on the mitral valve are crucial factors in the pathogenesis of MAC, and sex-specific differences in LV response to pressure overload may elucidate why more extensive grades of MAC mainly affect women.

articles.title: International Expert Consensus Statement on Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Gastric Variceal Coil Embolization Using the Modified Delphi Process: Best Practices and Future Directions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided gastric variceal coil embolization (EUS-GVE) has emerged as a safe and efficacious treatment for gastric variceal bleeding. However, significant practice variability exists for this novel technique. Using the modified Delphi process, we aimed to establish consensus among international experts on best practices and future research directions for EUS-GVE.

METHODS: A steering committee drafted statements encompassing four principal domains: pre-procedural protocol, intra-procedural technique, post-procedural monitoring, and future research directions. Thirty-seven advanced endoscopists with clinical and research expertise in EUS-GVE and representing international practice settings were invited to participate in online surveys where statements were independently ranked using a Likert numerical scale. Consensus was defined as ≥70% agreement. Statements not reaching consensus were revised based on comments and brought for a re-vote.

RESULTS: Thirty of 37 (81%) experts responded to the first round with 24 of 30 (80%) participating in the second round. Half of the participants represented North America while the other half practiced internationally. Fifty of 52 (96%) statements met consensus after 2 voting rounds. Final statements emphasized general themes of the importance of proper variceal description and classification, preference for EUS-GVE with adjunctive therapies, and the safety and versatility of the procedure. Definitions for clinical outcomes and future research topics were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: The results of this modified Delphi process represent the first consensus document for EUS-GVE and capture best practices from an international expert base. These statements provide practical guidance to optimize procedural performance and could aid future research involving EUS-GVE.

articles.title: A Phase I/II Trial of the Metalloporphyrin Radioprotectant BMX-001 in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Head and Neck Cancer Receiving Concurrent Radiation Therapy and Cisplatin.
articles.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE/OBJECTIVES: MnTnBuOE-2-PyP5+ (BMX-001) is a manganese metalloporphyrin superoxide dismutase mimic that inhibits radiation stress-induced pathways and may mitigate treatment-related side effects. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of BMX-001 on severe oral mucositis (OM), xerostomia, dermatitis, quality of life, and patient reported outcomes (PROs) among patients undergoing chemoradiation for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).

MATERIALS/METHODS: This multicenter, phase I/II trial included patients with stage III-IVB HNSCC (AJCC 7th ed) undergoing definitive or postoperative chemoradiation (CRT). Patients received a subcutaneous BMX-001 loading dose followed by twice-weekly maintenance dosing through one week post-CRT at three loading/maintenance dose levels (7/3.5 mg, 14/7 mg, and 28/14 mg), with level 3 expanded for phase II endpoints. OM, xerostomia, and dermatitis were assessed weekly during treatment, within one month, and at six and 12 months post-chemoradiation. PROs and saliva production (stimulated and unstimulated) were measured at baseline, end of CRT, and one, six and 12 months post-CRT. Descriptive statistics summarized adverse events, symptom duration, and PROs.

RESULTS: Between 5/2017 and 12/2019, 29 patients were enrolled; 86% had oropharynx primaries (n=25; n=24 HPV+) and 89.7% (n=26) underwent definitive CRT. One patient experienced two serious adverse events possibly related to BMX-001. Grade 3 OM occurred in 41.4% (n=12); acute and chronic grade ≥2 xerostomia occurred in 17.9% (n=5) and 9.1% (n=2), respectively, and 6.9% (n=2) experienced grade 3 dermatitis. At a median follow-up of 24 months, 96.6% were alive without progression. In exploratory longitudinal analyses of the 23 patients treated at the recommended phase II dose, patient-reported symptom and quality-of-life measures generally worsened at the end of CRT and subsequently improved. Several measures were no longer statistically different from baseline by six months, while measures of xerostomia remained elevated.

CONCLUSIONS: BMX-001 is safe and feasible in patients with advanced HNSCC. In addition, BMX-001 shows promising efficacy for mitigating CRT-associated toxicity and warrants further study in larger, controlled trials.

articles.title: StHSFB2A enhances potato tolerance to combined heat-drought stress by modulating redox homeostasis and osmotic adjustment.
articles.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
articles.abstract: Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.) is highly sensitive to heat, which often coincides with drought in the field. However, the mechanisms governing potato responses to combined heat-drought stress remain poorly understood. In this study, 'Atlantic' potato seedlings were subjected to control, heat, drought, and combined heat-drought treatments. Physiological measurements, RNA sequencing, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), transcription factor screening, and functional assays were used to identify key regulators of stress tolerance. Combined stress caused greater growth inhibition and cellular injury than either stress alone, with lower chlorophyll content, greater reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, enhanced membrane lipid peroxidation. These responses indicate that heat-drought stress elicits effects beyond the simple sum of the individual stresses. RNA-seq identified 2814 differentially expressed genes, many of which were associated with heat shock responses, redox homeostasis, and osmotic adjustment. WGCNA and transcription factor analysis, together with physiological trait correlations, highlighted StHSFB2A as a strongly induced heat shock factor (HSF) candidate. RNAi-mediated suppression of StHSFB2A intensified leaf wilting, ROS accumulation, and membrane lipid peroxidation. In contrast, StHSFB2A overexpression improved growth under heat, drought, and their combination, while increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) activities and the accumulation of proline and soluble sugars. These results support a positive role for StHSFB2A in stress tolerance. StHSFB2A may enhance adaptation to combined heat-drought stress by strengthening antioxidant defense, maintaining ROS homeostasis, and promoting osmotic adjustment.

articles.title: Prevalence of elevated fasting blood glucose and associated factors among 87,361 patients with diabetes mellitus attending a specialised tertiary diabetes centre in Bangladesh, 2022-2025.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Diabetes mellitus burden is rising in Bangladesh, with variable glycemic status and associated complications. To characterize the demographic, anthropometric, and urinary profiles of patients with diabetes mellitus attending a tertiary hospital and identify factors associated with elevated fasting glucose.

STUDY DESIGN: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted using data from 87,361 patients attending Chittagong Diabetic General Hospital, Bangladesh, between January 2022 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, body mass index (BMI), urinalysis findings, and fasting blood glucose (FBG) levels were analyzed. Elevated fasting blood glucose was defined as FBG ≥ 7.0 mmol/L. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with elevated fasting blood glucose.

RESULTS: Elevated fasting blood glucose was highly prevalent, observed among 83.7% of patients. Urinary acetone markedly increased the odds of elevated fasting glucose (trace: adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 74.98; present: AOR = 115.14), while albuminuria was also significantly associated (AOR = 2.74). Male sex (AOR = 1.29) and middle age (40-65 years; AOR = 1.27) increased the likelihood of elevated fasting blood glucose.

CONCLUSION(S): Elevated fasting blood glucose is highly prevalent among diabetic patients in Chattogram. Urinary acetone and albumin, together with demographic and BMI-related factors, may serve as practical indicators for identifying patients at risk of inadequate glycemic status and guiding targeted management strategies.

articles.title: Tirzepatide and risk of nutritional deficiency anemia compared with GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutritional deficiency anemia (NDA) is a potential concern during incretin-based treatment, but its comparative occurrence with tirzepatide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX database. Adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity who initiated tirzepatide or a GLP-1RA between January 1, 2022, and August 31, 2026, were identified. Patients with prior use of either treatment, NDA, type 1 diabetes, or bariatric surgery were excluded. After 1:1 propensity score matching, outcomes were assessed from day 1 through day 365. The primary outcome was a composite of iron, vitamin B12, or folate deficiency anemia.

RESULTS: The matched cohorts included 67,608 patients each. NDA occurred in 1,440 tirzepatide users (2.13%) and 1,917 GLP-1RA users (2.84%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.88; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.83-0.95). Tirzepatide was associated with less iron deficiency anemia (HR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.81-0.93), whereas estimates for vitamin B12 deficiency anemia (1.07; 0.83-1.38) and folate deficiency anemia (0.98; 0.56-1.71) were inconclusive.

CONCLUSION: Tirzepatide initiation was associated with a modestly lower hazard of diagnosed NDA, predominantly iron deficiency anemia, than GLP-1RA initiation. Residual confounding and differences in follow-up and ascertainment limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: "Are monoclonal antibodies going to be used the same way they are currently prescribed in asthma?".
articles.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
articles.abstract: Biologics targeting IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, TSLP, and IgE continue to expand the therapeutic options for patients with severe asthma. Although they reduce exacerbation frequency, lower systemic corticosteroid exposure, and improve symptom control in selected patients with T2-high severe asthma, their benefits are incomplete and are unevenly distributed across the whole spectrum of the severe asthma population. Several unmet needs exist with the current use of biologics in asthma including the need for development of validated biomarkers, the conduct of adaptive trials with multi-biomarker and omics-guided selection coupled with pharmacogenetic studies and interventions evaluating therapies for neutrophilic, pauci-granulocytic and mixed disease. Early interventions targeting immune hyperresponsiveness and structural remodeling coupled with pragmatic comparative trials, disease registries, multi-omic biomarkers, prevention trials for the pediatric population and with integrated severe-asthma/comorbidity models are also need and hold the potential to improve the impact of biologics in severe asthma. In this review, we discuss the limitations and opportunities for the use of current biologics and describe future research needs within the framework of achieving disease modification and complete remission.

articles.title: Model-Free Dynamic PET Quantifies Renal Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-Mediated Glucose Handling In Vivo.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal glucose handling via sodium-glucose cotransporters (SGLT1/2) is central to glucose homeostasis and a major therapeutic target. However, no established non-invasive imaging method provides an organ-specific quantitative readout of renal SGLT-mediated glucose handling in vivo, and static PET measures fail to reflect renal glucose handling.

METHODS: We developed a clinically interpretable dynamic PET approach using the tracer α-methyl-4-deoxy-4-[18F]fluoro-D-glucopyranoside (Me4FDG) to quantify renal SGLT-mediated glucose handling, expressed as SGLT-activity. The method was validated in mice (diabetes, surgical impairment, short-term SGLT2 inhibition, controls) and translated to patients with type 2 diabetes (n = 17) imaged at baseline and after 2 weeks of SGLT2 inhibition. Results were benchmarked against urinary glucose excretion, static PET measures, and an established renal compartmental kinetic model.

RESULTS: In mice, RFT-derived SGLT-activity changed in the expected direction across pathology and intervention and correlated with SGLT2 protein expression when function was not pharmacologically blocked, whereas static PET uptake and the kinetic tubular return parameter did not consistently reflect SGLT-mediated renal glucose handling. In patients, SGLT2 inhibition reduced SGLT-activity from 33 ± 6% to 10 ± 6% and markedly increased urinary glucose (3 ± 9 vs 155 ± 7 mmol/L, P < 0.001), yielding a strong inverse correlation between SGLT-activity and urinary glucose (R = -0.74, P < 0.001), which was not achieved with static PET measures. Baseline SGLT-activity was additionally associated with age, diabetes duration, hypertension, and glomerular filtration rate.

CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic Me4FDG PET enables non-invasive quantification of renal SGLT-mediated glucose handling in vivo using a single, physiologically interpretable functional metric. This readout captures renal pharmacodynamics and disease burden beyond static PET and routine metabolic markers and performed more consistently than the tested compartmental kinetic parameter, supporting its potential clinical utility for stratification and monitoring of SGLT-targeted therapies EudraCT 2018-002972-42.

articles.title: NKCC1 in Sepsis-Related Acute Lung Injury: Emerging Links to Macrophage-Neutrophil Crosstalk.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis-related acute lung injury (ALI) is a critical condition characterized by intense inflammation and damage to the lung tissue. Excessive activation of immune cells, particularly macrophages and neutrophils, is a key factor in the development of ALI. The sodium-potassium-chloride cotransporter 1 (NKCC1) plays a pivotal role in managing pulmonary fluid balance and inflammation and is critically involved in ALI.

METHODS: A comprehensive literature review was conducted to evaluate studies examining macrophages, neutrophils, and NKCC1 in ALI, focusing on NKCC1 and its interactions with macrophages and neutrophils.

RESULTS: Recognition of damage-associated or pathogen-associated molecular patterns by pattern recognition receptors on macrophages and neutrophils initiates downstream signaling cascades, including the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathways, which drive the production of proinflammatory mediators. The subsequent release of cytokines, including chemokines, promotes neutrophil recruitment to the lungs, where these neutrophils subsequently produce reactive oxygen species, proteases, and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), thus amplifying inflammation and contributing to tissue injury. Excessive NET formation causes lung tissue injury, increases pulmonary vascular permeability, and disrupts gas exchange. During ALI, NKCC1 expression is elevated, which exacerbates lung inflammation and pulmonary edema.

CONCLUSION: Sepsis-related ALI is characterized by excessive macrophage and neutrophil activation and activation of the MAPK and NF-κB pathways. Increased NKCC1 expression and activity contribute to pulmonary edema and inflammation in experimental ALI. However, the proposed role of NKCC1 in regulating macrophage-neutrophil interactions in sepsis-related ALI remains to be established.

articles.title: Isoalantolactone suppresses non-small cell lung cancer progression by inducing ferroptosis through HSC70-mediated GPX4 degradation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isoalantolactone (IAL), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from Inula helenium L. and Inula racemosa Hook. f., exhibits anti-inflammatory and anticancer properties. This study investigated the effects of IAL against non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

METHODS: The anticancer activity and potential mechanisms of IAL were evaluated in A549 and H1299 cells using CCK-8 proliferation assays, colony formation assays, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. The molecular target of IAL was identified through Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) coupled with mass spectrometry. The binding between IAL and its target, HSC70, was validated by molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The functional role of HSC70 was confirmed via co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and lentiviral-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA) knockdown. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in subcutaneous xenograft models, with IAL administered every other day.

RESULTS: IAL directly bound to HSC70 with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 1.07 μM and promoted glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) degradation. IAL induced hallmark features of ferroptosis, including lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, glutathione (GSH) depletion, and oxidized glutathione (GSSG) elevation. In vitro, HSC70 knockdown abrogated IAL-induced GPX4 degradation and ferroptosis. In subcutaneous xenograft models, IAL significantly suppressed tumor growth without evident toxicity and was accompanied by HSC70/GPX4 changes consistent with the in vitro mechanism.

CONCLUSIONS: IAL directly targets HSC70 and promotes GPX4 degradation, inducing ferroptosis in NSCLC cells. In subcutaneous xenograft models, IAL suppresses tumor growth with HSC70/GPX4 changes consistent with this mechanism and no overt toxicity at the tested doses. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of IAL.

articles.title: From Environment to Biota: Distribution, Characteristics, Ecological Risk of Microplastics and The Bioindicator Potential of Freshwater Mussels in The Nile River.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) represent a growing environmental concern however, their distribution and biological impacts in freshwater ecosystems remain poorly documented. This study investigates MP pollution in water, sediment, and four freshwater mussel species, Nitia teretiuscula, Coelatura aegyptiaca, Chambardia rubens, and Corbicula fluminalis, from the Nile River, Egypt. MPs were detected in all examined samples, with mean concentrations of 12.5±2.89 items/L in water and 4550±751 items/kg dry weight in sediment. Microplastic loads were significantly varied among the mussel species (p < 0.01), with mean concentrations of 4.8 ± 1.9 items/individual in N. teretiuscula and 4.2 ± 1.5 items/individual in C. aegyptiaca. The abundance of MP was strongly correlated with the studied species' biometric traits, particularly tissue weight (R2 = 0.89; p < 0.001). Fibers were the most common MP type in all samples; blue particles were the most prevalent color. The size-frequency distribution showed that MPs ranged from 50 to ≥3000 μm, with particles smaller than 500 μm accounting for 25.0% in N. teretiuscula, 47.6% in C. aegyptiaca, 38.9% in C. fluminalis, and 41.4% in C. rubens. The dominant size class was 1000-1999 μm, and PET was the main detected polymer. The target group index revealed that the studied species exhibited selective ingestion of specific shapes, colors, and size, particularly fragments and smaller blue particles, whereas N. teretiuscula showed more general and less selective feeding patterns. Water-to-biota bioaccumulation factors (BAF: 42.29-245.84 L/kg wet tissue) and sediment-to-biota accumulation factors (SBAF: 0.116-0.675) revealed clear interspecific differences in MP accumulation among the four mussel species, with N. teretiuscula showing the highest accumulation and C. rubens the lowest. The Microplastic Diversity Index showed that sediment had the highest diversity (0.610), followed by mussels (0.466) and water (0.334). While ecological risk assessment index indicated severe contamination, MP pollution in water samples from the investigated Sohag reach was classified as extremely high (RI > 1200). Estimated exposure through drinking water suggested annual ingestion rates of 8,905-13,430 MPs kg-1 for adults and 4,361.5-6,600 MPs kg-1 for children. This study provides an integrated assessment of microplastic pollution at a sampled reach of the Nile River in Sohag, Egypt, by comparing microplastic abundance and characteristics in water, sediment, and four freshwater mussel species. It also evaluates the potential of these mussels as bioindicators of microplastic contamination and associated ecological risks.

articles.title: Association Between Newly Diagnosed Dyslipidemia and Joint-Specific Incident Osteoarthritis: A Nationwide Propensity-Score-Matched Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Whether dyslipidemia raises the risk of incident osteoarthritis (OA) is uncertain given inconsistent prior cohort evidence. We examined the association between newly diagnosed and treated dyslipidemia and incident OA, overall and by joint site.

DESIGN: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified adults with newly diagnosed dyslipidemia (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] code E78 plus a lipid-lowering prescription) between 2007 and 2012, with the same 2-year washout applied to both groups. Participants with dyslipidemia were propensity-score matched (target ratio 1:3), with exact matching on index year, to comparators with no E78 claim during 2007-2012. Incident OA (≥1 inpatient or ≥3 outpatient claims, ICD-10 M15-M19) was assessed overall and for the knee, hip, hand, and multiple joints. Cox regression with robust variance estimates accounting for matched sets provided the primary adjusted estimates, complemented by competing-risk and period-specific analyses.

RESULTS: The matched cohort included 32,684 participants with newly diagnosed dyslipidemia and 76,375 comparators. Overall OA occurred in 12,594 and 25,089 participants, respectively, corresponding to incidence rates of 51.60 and 43.41 per 1,000 person-years (rate difference, 8.186; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.136-9.235). The primary adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) for overall OA was 1.133 (95% CI, 1.109-1.159; crude, 1.191), and the 10-year cumulative incidence was 38.62% versus 33.14% (risk difference, 5.48 percentage points; 95% CI, 4.87-6.14). Dyslipidemia was also associated with knee OA (aHR, 1.119; 95% CI, 1.090-1.148), hip OA (1.214; 1.078-1.366), and multiple-joint OA (1.294; 1.113-1.503), with no clear association for hand OA (1.135; 0.837-1.537). For overall and knee OA, the relative associations were stronger earlier in follow-up and weaker after exploratory cut points of 6 and 9.5 years, respectively. Analyses treating death as a competing event yielded similar findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Newly diagnosed and treated dyslipidemia was positively associated with incident clinically diagnosed OA in this nationwide Korean cohort, most consistently for overall and knee OA, although the associations attenuated with longer follow-up. These findings add population-based evidence for an association between dyslipidemia and OA, and further studies are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and clinical relevance.

articles.title: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA.

METHODS: MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC).

RESULTS: Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99.

CONCLUSION: MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

articles.title: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Early defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet bystander defibrillation remains uncommon despite the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). We investigated whether HeartRunner community first responder activation increased the likelihood of bystander defibrillation and 30-day survival in relation to the distance to the nearest accessible AED.

METHODS: Linking data from the Danish Cardiac Arrest Registry, Danish AED Network, and HeartRunner application, we identified patients with OHCA eligible for HeartRunner activation during 2017-2021. Using street-network distances to the nearest accessible AED, we examined associations between HeartRunner activation, bystander defibrillation, and 30-day survival using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).

RESULTS: Among 5,753 OHCAs (median age, 74 years; 64% male; 78% in private locations), HeartRunner activation (41%) was associated with higher bystander defibrillation across AED distances (p-interaction = 0.004), with no interaction for 30-day survival (p-interaction = 0.054). Predicted bystander defibrillation with versus without HeartRunner activation was 9.6% vs 5.5% at Q1 (389 m), 10.0% vs 4.3% at median (717 m), and 13.0% vs 4.8% at Q3 (1,183 m). TMLE estimated a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of bystander defibrillation (95% CI, 4.5-7.8; p<0.001) and a modest 1.8-percentage-point increase in 30-day survival (95% CI, 0.1-3.6; p=0.038) with HeartRunner activation.

CONCLUSION: HeartRunner activation attenuated the decline in bystander defibrillation with increasing AED distance following OHCA, without a corresponding distance interaction for 30-day survival. Overall, TMLE supported higher bystander defibrillation and suggested a modest increase in 30-day survival with HeartRunner activation.

articles.title: Mapping the shared genetic architecture between anorexia nervosa and metabolomic biomarkers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) has the highest mortality rate of any psychiatric disorder yet lacks effective treatments. While recent genomic efforts have reframed AN as a metabo-psychiatric condition that overlaps with cardiometabolic traits, AN's relationship to circulating metabolomic markers remains unknown.

METHODS: We examined shared genetic architecture between AN and 249 metabolomic biomarkers, and compared profiles with related mental health, anthropometric and cardiometabolic traits. Genetic and biological overlap was assessed with global genetic correlations, conjunctional false discovery rate, bivariate Gaussian mixture modeling, and gene set enrichment analysis across body tissues. We also explored putative causal relationships between AN, body mass index (BMI), and metabolomic biomarkers.

RESULTS: Significant genetic correlations emerged between AN and 142 metabolomic biomarkers, which were opposite in direction to cardiometabolic traits such as BMI and type 2 diabetes (rs<-0.94), and stronger than correlations with anxiety. Shared variants between AN and metabolomic biomarkers, particularly lipid-based metabolites, exhibited a mixture of positive and negative effects. These were mapped to genes involved in lipid-related cell signals, developmental growth, and inflammation, and were widely expressed in the brain, most internal organs and female reproductive organs. Bidirectional associations between AN and metabolomic biomarkers were found to act through their respective influence on BMI.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings reveal a complex, bidirectional mixture of positive and negative genetic relationships between AN and systemic metabolism, which would be obscured by examination of broader cardiometabolic traits. Uncovering specific shared lipid and developmental pathways provides a genetically-anchored mechanistic understanding of the illness, while highlighting promising metabolomic targets for weight restoration approaches.

articles.title: When to Refer - Guidelines for Approaching Transfers to Centers of Excellence in Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.abstract: Cardiogenic shock (CS) remains associated with high in-hospital mortality despite advances in reperfusion and temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS). Regionalized hub-and-spoke networks aim to improve outcomes through early recognition, standardized management, multidisciplinary decision-making, and timely transfer to specialized centres. This review proposes a practical framework to optimize referral and interhospital transfer of patients with CS. Early identification of CS requires systematic assessment of clinical presentation, objective markers of hypoperfusion, underlying etiology, and shock severity. Referral decisions should incorporate both the initial shock stage and its trajectory, response to treatment, hemodynamic status, and potential eligibility for advanced therapies. Early referral is particularly important when escalation to advanced circulatory support is anticipated. Safe transport requires appropriate previous stabilisation and coordination between referring and receiving teams while minimizing avoidable delays. Current evidence is predominantly observational, and validated referral thresholds, optimal transfer timing, and criteria for pre-transfer tMCS initiation remain uncertain. Further prospective studies are needed to determine which regionalized care strategies improve outcomes across different CS etiologies and patient populations. Conclusion: Effective management of CS requires coordinated regional networks, early multidisciplinary communication, systematic assessment of shock severity and trajectory, and timely access to specialized centres. Standardized referral pathways and efficient transfer protocols may facilitate appropriate treatment escalation.

articles.title: Antithrombotic therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation and acute coronary syndrome treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. -insights from the SWEDEHEART registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The aim of this study was to study temporal changes in antithrombotic therapy and to assess associations between common treatment strategies and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing PCI between 2010 and 2022 were identified from the SWEDEHEART registry. The three most common antithrombotic treatment strategies were: 1. Vitamin K antagonist (VKA)-based, 2. Direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based, and 3. Platelet inhibition (PI) only. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; all-cause death, myocardial infarction (MI), or stroke), and net adverse cardiovascular event (NACE; MACE or major bleeding). Cox regression models were created to adjust for differences in baseline characteristics.

RESULTS: In total, 15,358 patients were included, 29% were women and median age was 76 years. At discharge, 4155 (27%) received VKA-based, 4962 (32%) DOAC-based therapy, and 6241 (41%) PI only. The proportion treated with oral anticoagulants increased from 27% in 2010 to 82% in 2021. VKA-, and DOAC-based strategies were both associated with adjusted lower adjusted risk of MACE, (aHR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.89) and (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.74-0.90) and NACE (aHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.94) and (aHR 0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93), respectively, compared with PI only, with no difference between the two OAC strategies.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with AF undergoing PCI for ACS, the use of oral anticoagulants increased over time. Both a VKA- and DOAC-based strategy were associated with lower MACE and NACE, with no significant difference between the two strategies.

articles.title: Association between Physical Function and Incidence of Atrial Fibrillation: The Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poor physical function is linked to higher cardiovascular disease risk, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains understudied. Investigating this relationship could highlight a novel target for AF prevention.

METHODS: 4,803 participants without AF from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study cohort assessed in 2011-2013 were studied. Physical function was measured using Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB), 4-meter walk time, and grip strength. Hospital discharge codes and death certificates ascertained incident AF through 2022 (through 2020 for Jackson participants). Cox regression assessed the association between physical function and incident AF risk, adjusting for multiple covariates. Z-score transformations identified the measure most strongly associated with incident AF risk, and SPPB component analysis identified the most influential SPPB component.

RESULTS: Mean age of study participants was 75.1 ± 5.0 years (41.2% male, 22.2% black). During a median follow-up of 9.2 years, 809 incident AF events occurred. SPPB (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.90-0.96, per 1-point increase) and grip strength (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.78-0.96, per 10kg increase) were inversely associated with incident AF risk, while 4-meter walk time (HR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.03-1.13, per 1-second increase) was positively associated with incident AF risk. SPPB had the strongest association with incident AF risk. Within SPPB, only the chair stand component was significantly associated with incident AF risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Better physical function is associated with reduced incident AF risk, with SPPB showing the strongest association. Given the modifiable nature of physical function, these findings highlight a potential novel target for AF prevention in aging populations.

articles.title: Clinical recommendations on monitoring and management of bone health in adults with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy and transition to adult care: A national Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract: Poor bone health and low-trauma fractures are common in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), reflecting the combined effects of progressive muscle weakness, reduced mechanical loading, delayed puberty and/or hypogonadism, and long-term glucocorticoid exposure. Although paediatric bone health guidance in DMD is well established, adult-specific recommendations remain limited, particularly for individuals who enter adult services having received many years of bisphosphonate therapy during childhood or adolescence. We developed national expert consensus recommendations for the monitoring and management of bone health in adults with DMD, with particular emphasis on transition from paediatric to adult care. Recommendations were informed by review of the literature, a clinician survey, input from adults with DMD and carers, and discussion within a multidisciplinary expert group. A modified Delphi process was undertaken, with 16 clinicians voting on draft statements using a 9-point agreement scale; consensus was defined as at least 80% of participants scoring 7-9. Thirteen evidence-informed expert consensus clinical recommendations were agreed, covering fracture risk assessment, DXA and vertebral fracture monitoring, vitamin D and gonadal status, indications for specialist bone review, initiation and review of osteoporosis therapy, management of possible treatment failure, and structured review of long-term therapy during transition. The recommendations emphasise individualised decision-making, recognising the technical challenges of imaging, limited adult DMD-specific evidence, cumulative treatment burden, and the functional impact of fractures in this population. These consensus recommendations provide a practical framework to support adult neuromuscular and bone clinicians managing bone health in a rare, high-risk and increasingly adult DMD population.

articles.title: Microbial Genotoxins and Oncometabolites as Potential Codrivers of Hepatocarcinogenesis.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma affects only a subset of patients with chronic liver disease, suggesting that additional mutagenic and microenvironmental stressors influence cancer risk. In this review, we explore the gut-liver axis as a contributor to this heterogeneity. We propose a model in which direct microbial genotoxins, microbiota-derived genotoxic metabolites, and dysbiosis-associated oxidative stress may contribute to hepatocyte DNA damage. In parallel, microbial metabolites and structural immune stimuli may modulate hepatic stellate cell states and tumor-promoting inflammation. The deoxycholic acid-hepatic stellate cell senescence axis is supported in experimental obesity-associated liver cancer, whereas colibactin-specific hepatic mutagenesis, microbiota-derived acetaldehyde-induced DNA damage and hydrogen sulfide-dependent stromal reprogramming remain unproven in hepatocellular carcinoma. Collectively, these mechanisms could couple hepatocyte genomic diversification with microenvironmental selection. In conclusion, whether this proposed interplay contributes to human hepatocarcinogenesis remains to be established.

articles.title: Global Research Landscape of Recurrent Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Bibliometric Analysis of Risk Factors, Prevention, and Prediction (1993-2024).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (ROVCFs) remain a clinical challenge because they are associated with pain, spinal instability, and disability, particularly in older populations. This study presents a bibliometric and visual analysis of global research on risk factors, prevention, and prediction related to ROVCFs from 1993 to 2024.

METHODS: The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on January 10, 2025, for English-language Articles and Review Articles published from 1993 to 2024. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package bibliometrix were used to analyze publication and citation characteristics, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence patterns, thematic clusters, and keyword citation bursts.

RESULTS: A total of 381 eligible publications on risk factors, prevention, and prediction related to ROVCFs were included in the analysis. Annual publication output generally increased over the study period, particularly after 2008. China, the USA, and Germany were the most productive countries, while Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, Capital Medical University, and Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine were leading institutions. Spine, European Spine Journal, and Osteoporosis International were the top publishing journals. Within the present dataset, Chen Hao and Lin Wei-Che had the highest h-index values, followed by Chen Zhi. Keyword co-occurrence analysis revealed seven major research clusters: (1) osteoporosis-related risk factors, (2) percutaneous vertebroplasty (PVP)-related factors, (3) intravertebral clefts (IVC) factor for cemented vertebrae, (4) anti-osteoporosis drugs for refractures, (5) predictive model validation, (6) adjacent vertebrae refractures, and (7) kyphotic deformity. Keyword-burst analysis highlighted growing research attention to bone mineral density, management, prevention, vertebroplasty, and kyphoplasty.

CONCLUSION: This bibliometric analysis delineated the global research landscape and thematic structure of ROVCF research. The major themes involved osteoporosis-related risk factors, vertebral augmentation-related factors, intravertebral clefts, anti-osteoporosis treatment, adjacent vertebral fractures, kyphotic deformity, and prediction-model development. Further multicenter research is needed to evaluate and externally validate refracture-risk prediction approaches.

articles.title: Chronic Low-Dose Dietary Toxicant Exposure: An Integrative Review of the Framework Linking Food Contaminants, Inflammation, and Non-Communicable Diseases.
articles.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) account for over 74% of global deaths, with growing evidence implicating environmental chemical exposures as additional contributors to chronic disease risk. Chemical contaminants in food, including heavy metals, pesticide residues, and industrial pollutants, can result in repeated low-dose exposure and promote oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling involving nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB), c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways. However, existing frameworks, including the exposome, Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD), and One Health, do not specifically integrate the chronicity, low-dose nature, cumulative burden, and complexity of everyday dietary chemical exposure with inflammation-related NCD outcomes. This integrative review therefore proposes the chronic low-dose dietary toxicant exposure (CLDTE) framework to address this gap. By synthesizing toxicological, mechanistic, epidemiological, and human biomonitoring evidence, the framework links chronic dietary contaminant exposure with oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, systemic low-grade inflammation, and multi-organ dysfunction associated with diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, and chronic kidney disease. The CLDTE framework provides an integrated, system-level perspective on how cumulative and mixture-based dietary exposures may contribute to NCD risk and highlights the need for improved exposure assessment, biomonitoring, and preventive food safety strategies.

articles.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials investigating cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia in stroke and traumatic brain injury populations.
articles.abstract: Insomnia is highly prevalent following stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), and can contribute to challenges with mood, psychological functioning and quality of life. Emerging evidence supports the efficacy of cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for those who have experienced stroke or TBI, however a broader review incorporating sleep and mood-related outcomes has not yet been conducted. A systematic literature search was performed on Scopus, PubMed, Embase, and PsycINFO databases. Risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2.0 tool. Random-effects meta-analyses calculating pooled effect sizes were performed, alongside assessment of heterogeneity and sensitivity analyses. Nine randomised controlled trials were included, with seven contributing to the primary meta-analysis. CBT-I was associated with lower insomnia disorder severity on the ISI (MD = -3.07, 95% CI [-4.46; -1.67], p = 0.0037) and lower sleep disturbance on the PSQI (MD = -1.81, 95% CI [-2.82; -0.80], p = 0.0058). Secondary analyses demonstrated a small, significant effect on anxiety symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.30, 95% CI [-0.49; -0.12], p = 0.0106), and a small-moderate non-significant effect on depressive symptoms (Hedges' g = -0.36, 95% CI [-0.84; 0.12], p = 0.1146). CBT-I appears a promising intervention for improving insomnia after stroke or TBI, with additional modest benefits for depression and anxiety.

articles.title: Therapeutic plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy for severe dengue with multiorgan failure: a case report and focused review.
authors: Medauar Reis de Andrade Moreira F
articles.abstract: Severe dengue can progress to acute liver failure, haemolysis, encephalopathy, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction, but the role of therapeutic plasma exchange in treatment remains uncertain. We report a 17-year-old adolescent with NS1-positive dengue managed with continuous renal replacement therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange, and comprehensive intensive care, and provide a focused narrative review of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue. The patient developed abrupt massive intravascular haemolysis, profound anaemia, thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, encephalopathy requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, oliguric acute kidney injury, shock, and acute liver failure. She also met five of eight HLH-2004 criteria for secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Continuous renal replacement therapy was initiated before three therapeutic plasma exchange sessions, beginning with an exchange of 1·5 estimated plasma volumes using fresh frozen plasma. Haemodynamic, hepatic, renal, and coagulation parameters subsequently improved. Secondary infection and haemothorax requiring video-assisted thoracoscopic drainage complicated recovery; she was discharged 38 days after admission. Published evidence on the use of therapeutic plasma exchange in severe dengue consists mainly of case reports, small series, and observational cohorts. Therapeutic plasma exchange can be considered an adjunctive rescue therapy in selected refractory cases, particularly acute liver failure or thrombotic microangiopathy phenotypes, but its independent benefit, optimal timing, prescription, and target population remain undefined.

articles.title: Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.
articles.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) such as evolutionary scale modeling (ESM) are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction in clinical genomics, yet their adversarial robustness remains underexplored. We present SafeGenes, an evaluation framework combining input-space attacks, a discrete single-nucleotide variant (SNV)-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt-triggered backdoor. Across cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets, iterative attacks severely degrade discrimination: projected gradient descent (PGD) reduces the area under the curve (AUC) by more than 30 percentage points, and the false-positive rate at 95% sensitivity collapses to nearly 1.0, misclassifying virtually all benign variants as pathogenic. The backdoor selectively elevates the pseudo-log-likelihood ratio (PLLR) scores of benign variants and transfers across ESM architectures. A single population-observed background substitution inverts pathogenicity ranking below chance, lowering the AUC from 0.76 to 0.39, showing that these vulnerabilities are biologically realizable. SafeGenes provides an open auditing framework for adversarial robustness in genomic AI.

articles.title: A phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial of the safety and efficacy of the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in Down syndrome.
articles.abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is characterized by strong immune dysregulation and hyperactive interferon/JAK/STAT signaling. We report a phase 2, open-label, single-arm clinical trial testing the JAK1/3 inhibitor tofacitinib in persons with DS and immune skin conditions. Participants received treatment for up to 9 months with extensive safety monitoring and assessments of biomarkers, skin pathology, and neuropsychological measures. The primary safety endpoint was met, with tofacitinib showing a safety profile similar to that observed in the general population. Tofacitinib decreases interferon scores, cytokine scores, and neurotoxic immunometabolites without overt immune suppression. Participants experienced benefits for immunodermatological conditions, most prominently hidradenitis suppurativa and alopecia areata, and improvements in multiple neuropsychological assessments. Multi-omics analyses reveal specific inflammatory pathways modulated by tofacitinib in DS. Given the lack of a placebo control arm, efficacy findings remain exploratory. These results support JAK inhibition as a safe strategy to attenuate immune dysregulation in DS. This study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04246372).

articles.title: Sex-related biochemical response to chronic microplastic exposure in the reef-building polychaete Sabellaria spinulosa (Leuckart, 1849).
articles.abstract: Microplastic contamination of coastal systems is now chronic and pervasive. However, its sub-lethal impact on habitat-forming benthic invertebrates, which provide key coastal ecosystem functions and services through their ecosystem-engineering activities, remains largely unexplored. We present the first exploratory experimental assessment of the biochemical response of the reef-building polychaete Sabellaria spinulosa (Leuckart, 1849) to chronic polyethylene terephthalate microplastic exposure. We incorporate organism sex as an explanatory variable of the ecotoxicological response. Sexually mature individuals collected from the Mediterranean Torre Mileto reef (southern Adriatic Sea) were maintained for 28 days in tanks under controlled conditions and exposed to 1.89 PET mL-1. This concentration and polymer profile matches the environmental MP signature documented at the source microhabitat. Sampling encompassed an in situ reference and four sequential time points, utilizing biological pools as observational subsample within each tank. Collected data reveal highly significant sex, treatment and phase interactions within the primary antioxidant axis: exposed females diverged from controls earlier, more acutely, and for a longer duration than exposed males. Furthermore, phase-II detoxification exhibited a delayed, sex-asymmetric modulation consistent with a hypothesized response to polymer-leached substrates, while glycolytic markers were dominated by a treatment-independent acclimation peak. Multivariate dispersion was transiently elevated in exposed individuals at the first time point, suggesting an acute-phase pattern of condition-associated stress. Because treatment was applied at the single-tank level to preserve bioconstruction homogeneity, these differences should be interpreted as exploratory, condition-associated observations. Nonetheless, these findings suggest that sex may acts as an important modifier of biochemical response in habitat-forming polychaetes.

articles.title: Quantifying Possible Secondary Overtriage and Injury-Type Transfer Bias in Pediatric Trauma.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Secondary overtriage of pediatric trauma patients are patients transferred to higher levels of trauma care despite no future surgery, intensive care unit admission, and have an early discharge. It imposes substantial clinical and financial burdens on trauma systems. We evaluated and compared predictors of interfacility transfer among low-severity pediatric trauma patients at a community adult Level II trauma center and estimated associated costs.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of trauma patients aged <18 y presenting to a community adult Level II trauma center from 2016-2024. Patients with Injury Severity Score (ISS) ≥9 were excluded. Possible secondary overtriage was defined as interfacility transfer among patients with ISS <9. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of transfer. Dominance analysis and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve comparisons assessed the relative contribution of injury type versus ISS. Transfer costs were estimated using a fixed per-transfer cost of $8301.

RESULTS: Among 1439 low-severity pediatric trauma encounters, 399 patients (27.7%) were identified as a possible secondary overtriage. Burns (adjusted odds ratio 19.6) and axial skeletal fractures (adjusted odds ratio 3.2) were the strongest predictors of transfer. Injury type provided greater explanatory value than ISS (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.777 versus 0.704, P < 0.001). Estimated transfer-related costs totaled $3.3 million, with fractures accounting for 46.6%.

CONCLUSIONS: Possible secondary overtriage among minimally injured pediatric trauma patients was common, better explained by injury pattern than physiologic severity, and generated substantial system-level costs. Future quality improvement efforts should target injury-specific bias and protocolize transfer algorithms related to transfer decisions.

articles.title: Assessing Rurality as a Social Determinant in Trauma Care: A Survival Study Post discharge.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Rurality is an established social determinant of health, but its association with survival after trauma discharge remains unclear. We evaluated whether rural residence was associated with 1-y mortality among trauma survivors discharged from an urban Level I trauma center serving a large rural population.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 19,045 adults discharged alive after trauma hospitalization from 2019 to 2024. Trauma registry records were linked to state death certificate data using Social Security numbers. Rurality was assigned by county of residence using Rural-Urban Continuum Codes. Univariate and multivariable logistic regression analyses evaluated associations with all-cause mortality within one year after discharge.

RESULTS: Of 19,045 patients, 12,003 (63.0%) lived in rural counties. One-year mortality was 9.5% in both rural and urban patients. Rural patients more often had Injury Severity Scores ˃15 (23.8% versus 19.1%) and required intensive care unit admission (15.8% versus 12.6%). Rural residence was not associated with 1-y mortality in univariate analysis (odds ratio, 1.00; 95% confidence interval, 0.90-1.11) or after adjustment for age, sex, race, injury severity, and payer type (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.87-1.09; P = 0.61). Male sex, increasing age, severe injury, and Medicare or Medicaid coverage were independently associated with higher mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Rural trauma survivors had greater injury severity and intensive care use, but rural residence was not independently associated with 1-y mortality after discharge. Postdischarge interventions may be better targeted toward patients with advanced age, severe injury, and public insurance. These findings identify clinically vulnerable populations for follow-up.

articles.title: Paediatric respiratory syncytial virus healthcare associated infection (RSV-HAI) surveillance: A pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infection in young children and an important healthcare-associated infection (HAI) in paediatric settings. This study aimed to describe the epidemiology and clinical impact of RSV-HAI and assess the potential feasibility of prospective surveillance.

METHODS: Single-centre surveillance study using retrospective and prospective weekly case ascertainment over four years (2018-2020, and 2024). RSV positive children with symptom onset greater than 72 h post presentation were eligible and followed for two weeks. Surveillance by a specialist IPC nurse was supported through a digital report in the electronic medical record system. Data were reported on RSV-HAI per 1000 occupied bed days, child characteristics, and clinical outcomes. Surveillance feasibility indicators included surveillance workload and screening yield.

RESULTS: A total of 79 children with RSV-HAI were identified with an overall rate of 0.22 cases per 1000 occupied bed days. The median age of children was 2.1 years (interquartile range 0.4-6.8) and most had a medical comorbidity (65/76, 85.5%). One third of children received antibiotics to treat acute lower respiratory infection (26/79, 32.9%) and 11.4% (9/79) were new admissions to the intensive care unit. The overall screening yield was 42.9% (79/184 screened records), and surveillance screening was completed within 15 min in most surveillance weeks (175/199 weeks, 87.9%).

CONCLUSION: RSV is an important and potentially preventable HAI which is highly relevant to paediatric hospital care. This pilot study demonstrates a potentially feasible surveillance approach which could support IPC program implementation.

articles.title: Diffuse sclerosing osteomyelitis as a potentially immune-mediated disease: Evidence from HLA class II allele-group frequencies.
articles.journal: Journal of cranio-maxillo-facial surgery : official publication of the European Association for Cranio-Maxillo-Facial Surgery
articles.abstract: Diffuse sclerosing osteomyelitis (DSO) is a rare bone disease of unknown etiology in which infection is typically absent and antibiotic therapy is ineffective. Given recent evidence of elevated ANA titers in affected patients, this study aimed to determine whether specific HLA allele groups are enriched in DSO, addressing whether the disease has an immune-mediated or autoimmune basis. Twenty patients with confirmed DSO were included. HLA genotyping was performed on peripheral venous blood using a sequence-specific oligonucleotide (SSO)-based assay. Allele-group frequencies from healthy German individuals served as controls. Differences were assessed using the exact two-sided binomial tests and the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, with significance defined as p < 0.05. Among HLA class II allele groups, DRB1*13 occurred in 31.3% of typed DRB1 alleles and DQB1*06 in 46.9% of typed DQB1 alleles.
