Compared with the respective German AFND reference frequencies (12.87% and 25.55%), both DRB1*13 (p = 0.0054; q = 0.0216) and DQB1*06 (p = 0.0130; q = 0.0260) were significantly enriched. No statistically significant differences were observed in HLA class I alleles. The enrichment of HLA class II alleles, particularly DRB1*13, which is linked to enhanced responses in autoimmune and antibody-mediated diseases, may indicate an immune-mediated component of DSO. However, these preliminary findings from a small cohort cannot establish causation or an autoimmune etiology and require confirmation in larger cohorts using high-resolution HLA typing.

articles.title: Chest CT manifestations of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis: A pathophysiologic approach and differential diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a rare form of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis characterized by asthma, peripheral blood eosinophilia, and systemic small-vessel inflammation. The lungs are among the most frequently involved organs, and chest computed tomography (CT) may also provide useful information during follow-up. However, the pulmonary manifestations of EGPA are highly variable and often overlap with those of other eosinophilic lung diseases. EGPA has historically progressed through three clinical phases: prodromal allergic, eosinophilic, and vasculitic. Moreover, clinical manifestations vary according to ANCA status. ANCA-positive patients exhibit vasculitic features, whereas ANCA-negative patients exhibit eosinophilic tissue infiltration, particularly in the lungs. This review summarizes the current understanding of thoracic CT manifestations in patients with EGPA. These findings were categorized into parenchymal abnormalities (transient ground-glass opacities, peripheral consolidations, and nodules), large airway abnormalities (bronchial wall thickening, bronchiectasis, and mucus plugging), and small airway abnormalities (mosaic attenuation and air trapping). Emphasis is placed on the clinical significance of airway-centred disease and its relationship to specific clinical phenotypes. Furthermore, this review summarizes major original studies of thoracic CT findings in EGPA and discusses the differential diagnosis of EGPA from other eosinophilic lung diseases, including chronic eosinophilic pneumonia and allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis. In conclusion, chest CT findings should always be interpreted in conjunction with clinical manifestations, laboratory data, and ANCA status. Familiarity with these characteristic imaging patterns and a multidisciplinary approach are essential for the early diagnosis and appropriate management of patients with eosinophilic lung disorders. (Word count: 243).

articles.title: Identifying Plasma Proteins for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Penetrance and Severity in Pathogenic Variant Carriers and Noncarriers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically variable disease in onset and progression. Pathogenic MYBPC3 variants account for a substantial proportion of HCM diagnoses.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to identify protein biomarkers associated with HCM penetrance and severity.

METHODS: Olink-assayed plasma proteins of 144 pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers were evaluated for associations with HCM severity based on diagnostic criteria (unaffected, mildly, or severely affected). Identified proteins were replicated in the UK Biobank considering time to onset of HCM (67 cases), cardiomyopathy (156 cases), and associations with left ventricular maximum wall thickness (6,492 participants). After prioritizing proteins on cardiac tissue expression and druggability, we examined disease penetrance through associations with heart failure (HF) and arrhythmic outcomes in 272 UK Biobank participants with known pathogenic HCM variants free of cardiomyopathy at proteomics assessment.

RESULTS: Among pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers, we identified 27 proteins associated with HCM severity, of which 22 replicated in the UK Biobank. Six proteins were prioritized (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], growth/differentiation factor [GDF]-15, fibroblast growth factor [FGF]-23, adrenomedullin [ADM], renin [REN], and neural cell adhesion molecule 1 [NCAM1]), of which 5 associated with disease penetrance in pathogenic variant carriers: NT-proBNP and REN associated with increased HF and arrhythmic risk, GDF-15 and FGF-23 with HF risk, and NCAM1 with arrhythmic risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Through the integration of proteomic analyses in both clinical and general population cohorts, we replicated and prioritized 6 proteins associated with HCM penetrance and severity. These findings highlight potential plasma-based markers for diagnosis and disease monitoring, as well as promising targets for future therapeutic development.

articles.title: Residual Structural, Behavioral, and Social Barriers to Blood Pressure Control in an EHR-Integrated Remote Hypertension Program.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote hypertension programs improve blood pressure (BP) control, but which patient-level barriers matter once a program supplies education, monitoring, and pharmacist titration is unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To quantify BP improvement in a pharmacist-led, electronic health record-integrated remote program and identify barriers independently associated with control.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study included 1,948 adults with uncontrolled hypertension (baseline BP >140/90 mm Hg) enrolled at least 6 months (median observation: 9.7 months). Health literacy and medication-affordability concerns were recorded at enrollment, with engagement measures and the ADI (Area Deprivation Index). Linear (systolic change) and logistic (control) models were adjusted for both barriers and clinical covariates (n = 1,744).

RESULTS: Mean systolic reduction was 24.1 mm Hg (95% CI: 23.5-24.7); HEDIS (Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set) (<140/90 mm Hg) and clinical (<130/80 mm Hg) control reached 90.5% and 66.4%. Limited health literacy was associated with lower control (clinical OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.50-0.88; HEDIS OR: 0.66) in a graded, linear fashion (per-level OR: 0.81; P < 0.001). Medication-affordability concern (HEDIS OR: 0.48; 95% CI: 0.29-0.78) and loss of a marital partner (HEDIS OR: 0.53) were likewise associated with lower control, with concordant linear estimates. Educational uptake, but not measurement frequency, was associated with control; no barrier acted through engagement, and associations survived ADI adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: A digital hypertension program achieved large BP reductions, yet limited literacy, medication affordability, and loss of a partner persisted as residual, overlapping barriers not explained by engagement or neighborhood deprivation. Screening for these barriers may extend program benefit through targeted support.

articles.title: Rethinking cardiac monitoring in patients receiving trastuzumab-based HER2-directed therapies for breast cancer: a meta-analysis and cost-effectiveness analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Quarterly echocardiographic surveillance during trastuzumab-based human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-directed therapy was established in the early 2000s. With lower left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) decline rates with newer regimens, the justification for frequent cardiac surveillance warrants re-evaluation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We carried out a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of clinical trials of patients receiving trastuzumab, trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1), or trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd), using pooled estimates of study-reported cardiac dysfunction, predominantly decreased LVEF, to evaluate echocardiographic surveillance strategies. For early-stage disease (12-month treatment duration), strategies evaluated included baseline echocardiography plus imaging at 6 months, baseline plus imaging at 6 and 12 months, and baseline plus imaging at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. For metastatic disease (continuous treatment), strategies included baseline echocardiography plus annual imaging, baseline plus imaging every 6 months, and baseline plus imaging every 3 months.

RESULTS: Fifty-seven studies conducted from 1999 to 2026 (37 847 patients) were included. Pooled rates of study-reported cardiac dysfunction, predominantly decreased LVEF, were 4.5%, 1.7%, and 1.4% for trastuzumab, T-DXd, and T-DM1, respectively, in early-stage disease, and 7.7%, 3.3%, and 2.3%, respectively, in metastatic disease; grade 3 events were rare. At a willingness-to-pay threshold of $120 000/quality-adjusted life year (QALY), baseline echocardiography plus one follow-up study at 6 months was preferred for early-stage trastuzumab, whereas baseline-only imaging was preferred for early-stage T-DM1 and T-DXd. Monitoring every 3 months was not cost-effective for any early-stage regimen, with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of $12 974 923/QALY for trastuzumab, $3 033 636/QALY for T-DM1, and $4 388 134/QALY for T-DXd. In metastatic disease, baseline-only imaging was preferred for all three regimens; annual monitoring exceeded the willingness-to-pay threshold for trastuzumab, T-DM1, and T-DXd, with ICERs of $191 781/QALY, $537 175/QALY, and $353 098/QALY, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiography every 3 months was not cost-effective for any regimen or disease setting. Monitoring should be regimen- and setting-specific, with prospective validation of less intensive strategies. These findings are only applicable to lower-risk, trial-eligible patients.

articles.title: Caregivers' understanding and responses to sarcopenia in post-stroke care: A qualitative study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To explore how family caregivers of stroke survivors understand sarcopenia and how these understandings influence their caregiving practices.

METHODS: This qualitative descriptive study recruited 30 family caregivers (mean age = 52.2 years; range: 26-73) of stroke survivors (mean age = 65.83 years; range: 35-88) from a medical center in northern Taiwan using purposive sampling with convenience-based recruitment. In-depth, semi-structured interviews were conducted between August 2024 and May 2025. Data were analyzed using inductive content analysis through the preparation, organization, and reporting phases.

FINDINGS: Four categories were identified. (1) Caregivers understood sarcopenia through everyday language, such as "skin wrapped around bones," and through visual and tactile observations rather than biomedical terminology. (2) Preventive actions were intuitive but fragmented, often reflecting general beliefs about stroke recovery rather than structured knowledge of sarcopenia prevention. (3) Contextual constraints, including limited information and survivors' low motivation, hindered consistent preventive practices. (4) Caregivers expressed a need for practical, professionally guided education in accessible formats, such as short videos and step-by-step instruction.

CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS: Caregivers' understanding of sarcopenia was grounded in experiential observation rather than structured medical knowledge, leading to intuitive and fragmented preventive practices. Educational strategies should address this gap by offering clear, practical, and context-sensitive guidance tailored to post-stroke caregiving. These findings are relevant to geriatric nursing practice, as geriatric nurses can incorporate brief, step-by-step sarcopenia-prevention education into bedside teaching, discharge planning, and caregiver support, using accessible formats such as short videos.

articles.title: Cavitary effusion patterns are associated with different survival times in dogs with pulmonary hypertension and right-sided congestive heart failure.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe and compare clinical characteristics and survival among dogs with pulmonary hypertension-associated right-sided congestive heart failure (RCHF) according to cavitary effusion pattern.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter observational study included client-owned dogs with pulmonary hypertension-associated RCHF presented to 3 referral hospitals from February 2021 through April 2025. Pulmonary hypertension was assessed echocardiographically, and RCHF was defined by ascites with caudal vena cava dilation. Dogs were categorized as having ascites alone, ascites with pleural effusion, or ascites with pericardial effusion. Clinical and imaging characteristics were compared among groups, and survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and exploratory Cox regression analyses.

RESULTS: 61 dogs were included: 40 with ascites alone, 16 with pleural effusion, and 5 with pericardial effusion. Median survival was 157, 42.5, and 7 days, respectively. In an exploratory multivariable Cox model adjusted for age and grouped etiology, pericardial effusion was associated with a higher mortality hazard compared with ascites alone. Pleural effusion was not significantly associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Survival differed according to cavitary effusion pattern in this retrospective cohort of dogs with RCHF. Dogs with concurrent pericardial effusion had the shortest observed survival and a higher adjusted mortality hazard, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously because only 5 dogs had pericardial effusion.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Cavitary effusion pattern may provide additional descriptive information when assessing dogs with RCHF. Concurrent pericardial effusion may identify a subgroup with shorter observed survival, but its prognostic value requires confirmation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Distribution and clinical features of raccoon roundworm (Baylisascaris procyonis) infection in dogs and cats as detected by fecal quantitative polymerase chain reaction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe the geographic distribution and clinical features of dogs and cats with Baylisascaris procyonis detected by fecal quantitative PCR (qPCR).

METHODS: Dogs and cats in the US and Canada that were diagnosed with B procyonis via fecal qPCR performed by a veterinary diagnostic laboratory from March 3, 2022, through November 1, 2023, were identified. Details about patient demographics, clinical signs, treatment, and outcome were retrospectively captured via questionnaires sent to each pet's primary care veterinarian. Descriptive statistics were calculated.

RESULTS: B procyonis was detected in 74 dogs and 3 cats through fecal qPCR screening. Dogs were from Canada (n = 22) and the US (52), and cats were from the US (3). The US-detected samples were from the Midwest (35%) and Northeast (22%). Most US-detected cases (69%) resided in a suburban environment, and most Canadian cases (80%) resided in an urban environment. Clinical signs were not reported in most (62%) cases with fecal qPCR-detected B procyonis. Gastrointestinal signs were reported in 36% of cases, and resolution of gastrointestinal signs following anthelmintic treatment was reported in most (72.9%) of those.

CONCLUSIONS: The geographic distribution of detected B procyonis in dogs and cats is similar to that reported in raccoons. Reported clinical disease appears mild and responsive to anthelmintic treatment in most dogs and cats.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Veterinarian awareness of risk regions for raccoon roundworm detection is critical for One Health. Detection of B procyonis through routine fecal screening of dogs and cats informs risk of environmental exposure and zoonoses and allows for targeted antiparasitic prevention.

articles.title: An early prediction model for MODS in patients with traumatic sepsis: a development and external validation study.
articles.abstract: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome (MODS) is a severe complication of traumatic sepsis and is associated with high mortality and healthcare costs. Early risk stratification is critical, but clinically validated tools for predicting MODS in traumatic sepsis are lacking. We developed and validated a machine learning model for early MODS prediction in patients with traumatic sepsis. We enrolled 650 ICU patients with traumatic sepsis: 338 from a tertiary hospital ICU (development cohort; randomly divided into training and internal validation sets at 8:2) and 312 from MIMIC-IV (external validation cohort). Logistic regression, decision tree, extreme gradient boosting machine, neural network, random forest, and LightGBM were trained using independent risk factors identified by multivariable logistic regression. The development cohort MODS incidence was 38.46% (130/338). Seven independent risk factors were identified: age, open trauma, Injury Severity Score, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), procalcitonin, D-dimer, and serum creatinine. In internal validation, random forest achieved the highest AUC (0.933, 95% CI: 0.905‒0.961), followed by LightGBM (0.911, 95% CI: 0.879‒0.943) and extreme gradient boosting (0.910, 95% CI: 0.878‒0.942). In external validation, LightGBM achieved the highest AUC (0.751, 95% CI: 0.698‒0.804), followed by extreme gradient boosting (0.748, 95% CI: 0.695‒0.801) and neural network (0.739, 95% CI: 0.685‒0.793). A composite score integrating AUCs, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, Brier score, and log loss ranked LightGBM first (score 92), making it the optimal model for early MODS risk prediction in this patient population.

articles.title: Sarcopenia, a proteomics-derived sarcopenia score, and risk of incident liver outcomes: a prospective cohort study.
articles.journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is associated with adverse outcomes in established liver disease, but its prospective associations with subsequent liver outcomes and the associated circulating proteomic features remain incompletely characterized.

AIMS: To examine the prospective associations of sarcopenia with incident liver outcomes, develop a proteomics-derived sarcopenia score (ProSS), evaluate its predictive value, and explore associated biological pathways.

METHODS: A two-phase analysis was conducted in the UK Biobank. In 492,305 participants, multivariable Cox models assessed the associations of sarcopenia with incident liver outcomes. In a proteomic subcohort of 51,637 participants, ProSS development and internal validation were conducted within a nested five-fold cross-validation framework incorporating multivariable screening, bootstrap-based LASSO, and elastic-net modelling. The incremental prognostic value of ProSS for MASLD and cirrhosis was evaluated using pooled out-of-fold predictions from six Cox models. Functional enrichment and exploratory single-protein indirect-effect analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of approximately 14 years, sarcopenia was associated with higher risks of incident MASLD (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.26-1.48), cirrhosis (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.39-1.79), liver cancer (HR 1.86, 95% CI 1.37-2.52), and liver-related mortality (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.53-2.38). In cross-validation analyses, fold-specific out-of-fold ProSS values were associated with incident MASLD (HR 1.49 per 1-SD increase, 95% CI 1.38-1.61) and cirrhosis (HR 2.39, 95% CI 2.15-2.65). Adding ProSS to a clinical model containing sarcopenia status increased the 10-year AUC from 0.765 to 0.788 for MASLD (ΔAUC 0.023, 95% CI 0.014-0.033; P<0.001) and from 0.780 to 0.846 for cirrhosis (ΔAUC 0.067, 95% CI 0.043-0.091; P<0.001). Enrichment analyses highlighted immune and inflammatory signalling, extracellular matrix organization, and cytokine/receptor-related pathways. Exploratory indirect-effect analyses highlighted GDF15, IGFBPL1, and BST2 as the leading protein signals for both MASLD and cirrhosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Sarcopenia was prospectively associated with higher risks of multiple liver outcomes. ProSS provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical factors and sarcopenia status, particularly for cirrhosis, while the associated circulating proteins may provide biological context for these associations.

articles.title: Editorial consensus: writing rigorous qualitative research papers.
articles.journal: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences

articles.title: TREML4 deficiency attenuates renal ischemia-reperfusion injury by limiting oxidative stress and NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (RIRI) is one of the major causes of acute kidney injury (AKI), and the molecular mechanisms underlying its initiation remain incompletely understood. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-like 4 (TREML4) is an important regulator of inflammation and immune cell death; however, its role in RIRI remains unclear.

METHODS: A bilateral RIRI model was established in mice by 45 min of ischemia followed by 24 h of reperfusion, and a hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model was established in human kidney cortex proximal tubular epithelial (HK-2) cells. H&E staining, periodic acid-Schiff staining, ELISA, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, TUNEL staining, immunohistochemistry, transmission electron microscopy, RT-qPCR, siRNA transfection, and Western blotting were used to assess TREML4 expression and markers of inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and pyroptosis. TREML4 function was examined using Treml4 knockout mice and Treml4 siRNA-mediated knockdown in HK-2 cells. In addition, the NLRP3 inflammasome was directly activated using lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in combination with nigericin to determine whether the protective effect of TREML4 was dependent on NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

RESULTS: TREML4 expression was upregulated in both the renal tissues of RIRI mice and H/R-treated HK-2 cells. RIRI significantly increased renal levels of TNF-α and IL-6, elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, reduced superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, increased the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio and the number of TUNEL-positive cells, and upregulated the expression of NLRP3, caspase-1 p20, GSDMD-N, and IL-1β p17, indicating the activation of inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and pyroptosis. Treml4 gene knockout reversed these alterations and reduced serum creatinine (SCr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels, renal tubular injury scores, and kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) expression. In vitro, Treml4 knockdown similarly attenuated H/R-induced oxidative stress and pyroptosis in HK-2 cells and suppressed the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway. However, Exogenous activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome using the LPS + nigericin activation protocol reversed the protective effects of Treml4 knockdown.

CONCLUSION: TREML4 deficiency attenuated inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and pyroptosis during RIRI. Following exogenous activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome using the LPS + nigericin activation protocol, these protective effects were abolished, suggesting that the protective effects of TREML4 deficiency are associated with the suppression of NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Its inhibitory effect on pyroptosis may be associated with reduced ROS accumulation. TREML4 may represent a potential candidate mechanistic target for AKI.

articles.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cardiovascular immunological memory: From epigenetically reprogrammed hematopoiesis to precision cardiovascular immunology.
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis is an age-related condition characterized by somatic mutations in hematopoietic stem cells and progenitor cells, resulting in an imbalance in the production of circulating blood cells, but not meeting the diagnostic criteria for hematological malignancies. Initially regarded as a precursor state of a myeloid tumor, it has now been confirmed as an important regulator of cardiovascular disease risk. The strongest evidence pertains to atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases, but there are also reports indicating its association with heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ischemic stroke, and thrombotic complications. Current research increasingly suggests that the mechanisms linking hematopoietic clonality to cardiovascular damage include inflammatory bone marrow hematopoiesis, alterations in the innate immune signaling pathways, activation of inflammasomes, interactions between platelets and neutrophils, and abnormal tissue remodeling. This review explores the role of innate immune reprogramming related to clonal hematopoiesis in cardiovascular diseases. Clonal hematopoiesis and trained immunity are related but distinct phenomena: clonal hematopoiesis originates from somatic mutations and clonal selection, while trained immunity refers to the continuous functional reprogramming of innate immune cells and their precursor cells. The potential fusion of these two factors may affect the generation of bone marrow cells in subsequent stress states, inflammatory responses, and interactions with cardiovascular tissues. This article focuses on three mechanism axes. Firstly, experimental models have confirmed that TET2 mutations are related to the hematopoietic process and can activate inflammasomes and the IL-1β signaling pathway. Secondly, DNMT3A mutations may affect hematopoietic function and bone marrow cell function through different epigenetic programs, although their impact on the cardiovascular system is not yet fully clear. Thirdly, the hematopoietic process related to JAK2V617F may be involved in the interaction between platelets and neutrophils, as well as the thrombotic-inflammatory process. Finally, we explore how the type of driver mutation, variant allele frequency (VAF), clonal dynamics, inflammatory activity, and cardiovascular phenotype can provide guidance for precise cardiovascular research. This comprehensive framework is currently still a mechanistic hypothesis that requires further validation, rather than an established clinical diagnosis.

articles.title: Placental microplastic exposure and neonatal cardiovascular biomarkers: Evidence from umbilical cord blood using advanced mixture modeling.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly detected at the maternal-fetal interface, yet human evidence linking placental MP burden with neonatal cardiovascular perturbations remains limited. This study investigated associations between placental MP polymers and cardiovascular, inflammatory, and oxidative-stress biomarkers in umbilical cord blood (UCB). In this cross-sectional study, 198 mother-neonate dyads were evaluated. Six placental MP polymers, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polystyrene (PS), polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polyurethane (PU), were quantified using μ-FTIR and pyrolysis-GC/MS with batch-specific blank correction. Seven UCB biomarkers (NT-proBNP, cTnT, cTnI, CK-MB, IL-6, TNF-α, and hs-CRP) and three oxidative-stress biomarkers (MDA, SOD, and 8-OHdG) were measured. Multivariable regression, weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression, quantile g-computation, Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR), and exploratory mediation analyses were applied. MPs were detected in all placentas, with a median total burden of 11.47 μg/g dry tissue. Higher MP burden was positively correlated with all seven cardiovascular and inflammatory biomarkers (Spearman's ρ=0.41-0.63; all p < 0.001), accompanied by increased MDA and 8-OHdG and decreased SOD activity. PVC showed the strongest individual association with NT-proBNP (β=0.48, 95% CI: 0.31-0.65), while PET was strongly associated with cTnT. WQS, qg-comp, and BKMR consistently demonstrated positive associations between the six-polymer mixture and all seven biomarkers. PVC, PET, and PS were the principal contributors. Exploratory mediation analyses identified statistical indirect associations involving oxidative-stress and inflammatory biomarkers in relation to NT-proBNP and cTnT; however, these findings do not establish temporal or causal mediation. Placental MP burden was associated with an adverse neonatal cardiovascular biomarker profile, accompanied by oxidative and inflammatory alterations. These findings support potential biological perturbation associated with prenatal MP exposure, warranting confirmation in larger prospective studies.

articles.title: Molecular targets and potential pathways associated with DEHP-exacerbated atherosclerosis: A combined bioinformatics and experimental study.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by lipid deposition and plaque formation in arterial walls, representing the leading cause of cardiovascular disease. Recent studies indicate that the environmental endocrine disruptor di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) may aggravate atherosclerosis, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. This study integrates bioinformatics and experimental approaches to elucidate the molecular targets and pathogenic mechanisms of DEHP in atherosclerosis. ADMET and ProTox analyses revealed multi-organ toxicity risks, particularly nephrotoxicity and hERG blockade. Network toxicology identified 55 shared targets between DEHP and atherosclerosis, with 7 candidate hub targets (BCL2, MAPK8, CASP3, MMP9, STAT1, CTSS, MAPK14) showing significant interactions. Functional enrichment indicated involvement in oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammatory pathways, validated by differential expression in human atherosclerotic plaques (GEO: GSE100927). Molecular docking revealed strong binding of DEHP to MMP9 (-7.8 kcal/mol), moderate binding to MAPK14 (-6.9 kcal/mol), MAPK8 (-6.4 kcal/mol), BCL2, CASP3, and CTSS (all -5.2 kcal/mol), and weak binding to STAT1 (-4.7 kcal/mol). In vivo, DEHP exposure accelerated high-fat diet induced atherosclerotic lesions, manifesting as dyslipidemia, increasing plaque area, reducing collagen content, and compromising plaque stability. Mechanistically, DEHP may promote atherosclerosis through altered expression of candidate hub targets in oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and extracellular matrix degradation pathways.

articles.title: Cardiovascular physiology of respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness: A hemodynamic guided approach.
articles.abstract: Respiratory support is traditionally regarded as a treatment for respiratory failure. However, interventions that modify pleural pressure, transpulmonary pressure, lung volume, or the work of breathing simultaneously influence venous return, ventricular loading conditions, pulmonary vascular resistance, ventricular interdependence, myocardial oxygen demand, cardiac output, and systemic perfusion. Consequently, similar respiratory interventions may produce different haemodynamic effects according to the predominant cardiovascular physiology. This narrative review examines heart-lung interactions during respiratory support in acute cardiac critical illness and proposes a physiology-based framework organized around three predominant haemodynamic phenotypes: left ventricular congestion/afterload excess, left ventricular low-output/cardiogenic shock, and right ventricular pressure overload/failure. Acute pulmonary embolism is considered an important aetiology of the latter phenotype rather than a separate haemodynamic category. We discuss how high-flow nasal oxygen, continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel non-invasive ventilation, and invasive mechanical ventilation modify cardiovascular physiology and how their effects may be anticipated and reassessed using clinical examination, systemic perfusion, haemodynamic monitoring, focused echocardiography, and lung ultrasound. These phenotypes are dynamic and may overlap or evolve during critical illness; therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as a conceptual bedside approach rather than a validated therapeutic algorithm. Respiratory support may consequently be considered a cardiovascular as well as a respiratory intervention, requiring repeated assessment of both respiratory benefit and haemodynamic cost.

articles.title: The SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol and Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS) for dynamic assessment of peripheral edema burden in critically ill patients: a prospective, longitudinal observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Excessive fluid resuscitation may lead to pathologic fluid accumulation and increased mortality. Cumulative fluid balance (CFB) correlates poorly with outcomes. Ultrasonographic central congestion metrics (VExUS/Lung ultrasound) inherently overlook critical fluid shifts within the peripheral reservoir. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed the SUBcutaneous Comprehensive UlTrasonographic (SUBCUT) protocol for standardized, semi-quantitative assessment of peripheral edema burden.

METHODS: Ultrasonographic assessment was performed bilaterally across six core anatomical regions using the SUBCUT protocol on days 1, 3, and 7. Individual sites were graded semi-quantitatively using the Ultrasonographic Subcutaneous Edema Grade (USEG, 0-4), yielding the Severity of Water and Edema Level Score (SWELS, 0-48) as the cumulative sum across 12 evaluation sites. The primary endpoint was ICU mortality, evaluating the prognostic performance of Day 3 SWELS.

RESULTS: Among 111 patients analyzed (ICU mortality 23.4%; 26/111), baseline SWELS and CFB were similar between survivors and non-survivors. By Day 3, median SWELS surged in non-survivors (24 vs. 8; P < .001), yielding greater unadjusted, apparent discrimination than CFB (AUC 0.86 vs. 0.65). In competing-risk analysis, a 5-point increase in Day 3 SWELS was independently associated with ICU mortality (sHR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.22-1.86; P < .001). Incorporating Day 3 SWELS into a contemporaneous clinical base model (Age, Admission Sepsis, Day 3 SOFA) enhanced model fit and discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.043; P = .008).

CONCLUSIONS: The SUBCUT protocol provides a novel framework for assessing peripheral edema burden. At Day 3, its derivative, SWELS, demonstrates incremental prognostic association beyond contemporaneous organ dysfunction, offering an extravascular perspective for multi-compartment fluid mapping.

articles.title: Health-care utilization, costs, and quality of life in patients with sepsis: Results from the SAGA trial in the Netherlands.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis imposes a substantial clinical and economic burden, yet detailed patient-level data on long-term healthcare costs and quality of life (QoL) is mainly based on intensive care unit (ICU) survivors and relies on model-based projections for patients treated in general wards.

AIM: To assess direct and indirect healthcare costs and QoL during the first year after community-onset sepsis.

METHODS: Data were obtained from a cluster-randomized trial of patients hospitalized with sepsis of urological, abdominal or unknown origin in the Netherlands. Mean direct hospitalization costs were collected from hospital data. Additional healthcare utilization and productivity losses were obtained through structured questionnaires in a subset of patients followed for 12 months. We used inverse probability weighting to adjust for differences between the subset and full cohort. QALYs were estimated using the EQ-5D-5L at months 0 (then-test), 2, 6, and 12, and the SF-36 was administered at 12 months.

RESULTS: Among 472 patients, 91 (19%) required ICU admission. Mean direct hospitalization costs were €8858 (95% CI: 7988-9855) per patient: €6697 (95% CI: 6185-7251) for general ward-admitted patients and €18,155 (95% CI: 14,856-22,342) for ICU-admitted patients. Over 12 months, mean total costs per patient were €30,889 (95% CI: 22,485-43,105): €25,839 (95% CI: 19,089-35,845) for general ward-admitted patients and €41,769 (95% CI: 23,132-48,943) for ICU-admitted patients. The weighted mean QALY during follow-up was 0.62 (95% CI: 0.51-0.74) compared with 0.65 (95% CI: 0.54-0.75) before sepsis. SF-36 at 12 months showed the greatest limitations in general health, physical role functioning, and energy/fatigue.

CONCLUSION: Sepsis is followed by substantial healthcare and societal costs during the first year after admission, with a significant burden among patient treated in general wards. By providing Dutch patient-level cost and QoL data across ICU and non-ICU settings, this study enables improved economic evaluations and better-informed health policy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: European Union Clinical Trials Register (2021-001,840-83). Count = 296.

articles.title: Prevention and control of noncommunicable diseases: A global analysis of hypertension and cardiovascular disease burden.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cardiovascular diseases, a major category of noncommunicable diseases, are the leading disease burden cause worldwide. Despite this, many countries appear to prioritise clinical interventions over onset prevention. This study examines the relationship between prevention and control of hypertension and cardiovascular disease burden.

STUDY DESIGN: Cross-national longitudinal analysis using country-level data.

METHODS: Analysing the information from 1856 country-year observations from 164 countries between 2000 and 2018 by a fixed-effects model, we adjusted for confounders including population health status, behavioural risks, health system indicators, social determinants, and both country- and year-fixed effects.

RESULTS: Most countries show substantially greater improvement in hypertension control than in hypertension prevention. Our econometric analysis suggests that both hypertension prevention and control are statistically associated with cardiovascular disease burden, with substantial overlap in their estimated counterfactual magnitudes.

CONCLUSIONS: Health systems for noncommunicable disease globally may exhibit a shifting-the-burden dynamic, where reliance on downstream clinical interventions becomes self-reinforcing and crowds out prevention efforts. Effectively addressing noncommunicable diseases requires both preventing disease onset and treating and controlling existing conditions, as each is interconnected and offers comparable potential to reduce mortality and disability.

articles.title: Faculty perspectives on pharmacy resident roles and impact in skills laboratory education.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Colleges and schools of pharmacy (C/SOP) often use a layered learning model with pharmacy residents as educators to support skills training, yet limited research exists on the scope and impact of their involvement. This study aimed to evaluate how C/SOP integrate residents into skills lab courses and examined faculty-perceived benefits and challenges associated with their involvement.

METHODS: A cross-sectional, 34-item electronic survey was distributed in January 2025 to 140 United States C/SOP. The survey gathered information on resident involvement, resident training and evaluation, and faculty-perceived benefits and challenges of resident involvement in skills lab teaching. Descriptive statistics and inductive content analysis were used to analyze quantitative and qualitative responses.

RESULTS: Thirty-four faculty representatives completed the survey (response rate: 24.3%), with twenty-four respondents (70.6%) reporting resident involvement in skills lab teaching. Residents participated across first- (70.8%), second- (87.5%), and third-year (75%) skills labs, most commonly providing feedback and grading (95.8%), in-lab instruction (83.3%), and facilitation (58.3%). Residents primarily supported single activities (66.7%) rather than providing longitudinal course support (25%). Resident training was common and was done in-person and online. Most respondents reported providing feedback to residents (83.3%), although 79.2% reported no formal competency evaluation. Respondents identified benefits for faculty, residents, and students, though challenges included scheduling, training demands, and inconsistent engagement.

CONCLUSION: Faculty respondents perceived benefits from pharmacy residents serving as instructors, facilitators, and evaluators in skills laboratory courses through a layered learning model, despite notable challenges. Opportunities remain to enhance resident integration, involvement, and development to further maximize the impact of this educational model.

articles.title: Assessing Differences in Timeliness of Emergency Department Pain Treatment for Adult Sickle Cell Pain and Renal Colic.
articles.abstract: The American Society of Hematology (ASH) adopted a site-level quality measure (QM) quantifying differences in median time to first pain medication between adult sickle cell disease (SCD) vaso-occlusive episodes (VOE) and renal colic in emergency departments (EDs). Large-scale evaluation of this QM is lacking. We analyzed records from 103 U.S. adult EDs using 2019-2025 Epic Cosmos electronic health record data. Included sites had at least 100 SCD VOE and 100 renal colic encounters. The QM was calculated per site as median time to first pain medication for SCD VOE minus median time for renal colic, in minutes. Sites were categorized as SCD-Advantaged (<-10 min), Equivalent (±10 min), or SCD-Disadvantaged (>+10 min). Spearman correlations assessed relationships between QM scores and site-level SCD encounter volume, ED length of stay (LOS), and hospital admission rates. Across 103 adult EDs, 436,692 SCD VOE and 5,596,964 renal colic encounters were analyzed. QM scores ranged from -145 to +91 minutes (median: +4). Most sites (56.3%) demonstrated equivalent first-analgesia timeliness; 15.5% provided faster analgesia for SCD VOE, while 28.2% showed delays for SCD VOE (>+10 minutes, median gap: +19 min). QM scores were not associated with SCD encounter volume (p = 0.42), ED LOS (p = 0.94), or hospital admission rate (p = 0.34). We found no major differences in acute pain-care timeliness for SCD versus renal colic across most sites; however, several EDs demonstrated opportunities for improvement. These findings establish the first national baseline for the ASH QM.

articles.title: Associations Between Technology Attitudes, App Use, and Health Outcomes in a Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support Intervention: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mobile health (mHealth) apps are increasingly incorporated into diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) programs to improve access to behavioral and clinical support. Although digital DSMES interventions have demonstrated benefits for self-management and glycemic control, considerable variability exists in app use, and less is known about whether preintervention technology attitudes are associated with subsequent app use and related outcomes.

OBJECTIVE: This study examined whether baseline technology attitudes are associated with app use and whether app use is associated with diabetes self-care and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) among adults participating in a digital DSMES intervention.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the Living Healthier with Diabetes randomized controlled trial (RCT) in Texas (2020-2022). The RCT included 3 study arms: virtual DSMES, smartphone app-based DSMES, and a combined intervention. Analyses were restricted to the 2 intervention arms with app access. Baseline technology attitude was assessed using a 4-item composite scale. App use was measured using 2 indices: a primary app use index derived from days per week, minutes per day, and overall 3-month usage, and a feature-use index summing use across 10 app functions. Outcomes included HbA1c and diabetes self-care. Multivariable linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate associations after adjustment for intervention arm, age, gender, past month financial situation, and baseline outcome values.

RESULTS: Of the 189 participants enrolled in the primary trial, 129 randomized to the intervention arms with smartphone app access were included. Follow-up HbA1c and diabetes self-care data were available for 116 (89.9%) and 114 (88.4%) participants at 3 months and 117 (90.7%) and 116 (89.9%) participants at 6 months, respectively. More positive baseline technology attitudes were associated with greater app use at both 3 months (β=0.64, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.99; P<.001) and 6 months (β=0.78, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.17; P<.001) but were not associated with feature use. App use was not associated with HbA1c at 3 months but was associated with lower HbA1c at 6 months (β=-0.04, 95% CI -0.074 to -0.013; P=.005) and in longitudinal models (β=-0.04, 95% CI -0.074 to -0.006; P=.02). Greater app use was associated with higher self-care at 3 months (β=0.56, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.82; P<.001) and 6 months (β=0.38, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.62; P=.002) and remained associated with self-care in longitudinal analyses (β=0.44, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.68; P<.001). App and feature use did not change significantly between 3 and 6 months (P=.14 and P=.11, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that preintervention technology attitudes are associated with greater app use within digital DSMES programs and that greater use of the app may represent an important pathway linking mHealth interventions with behavioral and clinical outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06370494; http://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT06370494.

articles.title: Parents' Perspectives on the Use and Development of Predictive AI in Neonatology: Focus Group Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predictive AI models, such as AI-generated early warning systems for detecting critical conditions, are being praised as promising applications in neonatology. Despite technological advancements in predictive AI, the integration of AI at the bedside remains challenging, and few AI technologies are currently integrated into routine neonatal care. A better understanding of the wishes and barriers of patients and, in the case of neonatal patients, their parents, is essential to bridge this gap. Yet, parental perspectives on the use of AI remain underexplored.

OBJECTIVE: This study explored the perspectives of parents whose child had previously been admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit about the development and use of predictive AI in neonatal clinical settings.

METHODS: We conducted 3 focus groups with 18 Dutch parents of children admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit to explore their views on AI in neonatal care. Participants were purposively recruited via a neonatology parent and patient organization. Discussions focused on predictive AI in acute settings and on AI to predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in later life. A reflexive thematic analysis of the focus group data was performed.

RESULTS: Parents generally welcomed predictive AI as a supportive tool for the medical team, anticipating improvements in patient outcomes. AI for short-term predictions was especially appreciated, whereas longer-term predictions were received with some reservations. Overarching concerns regarding predictive AI systems included AI undermining parental intuition, overreliance on AI in decision-making, and undesirable ethical and psychological implications of long-term health predictions. Interestingly, in addition to predictive AI systems that support medical judgment, parents also hoped that other AI tools could be developed to better involve parental input in the decision-making process. Specifically, they envisioned applications that extend beyond clinical decision support to provide parents with information, emotional support, and tailored guidance on the right course of action.

CONCLUSIONS: Parental perspectives highlight both opportunities and challenges for predictive AI integration in neonatal care. Engaging parents in the design and implementation of AI informs the development of family-centered, ethically responsible AI solutions and may identify opportunities for developing parent-centered AI tools alongside systems designed to support clinicians.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Estimation for Hemodynamic Monitoring Using Reduced Photoplethysmography Features in Intensive Care Units: Prospective Machine Learning Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Continuous, noninvasive blood pressure (BP) monitoring is clinically important for managing hemodynamic instability in the intensive care unit (ICU). However, current ICU practice primarily relies on invasive arterial catheterization. While this is the clinical gold standard for continuous measurement, it carries risks such as infection and thrombosis and is typically limited to select critical care settings.

OBJECTIVE: To reduce reliance on invasive arterial lines, we developed an interpretable estimation framework for systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) from single-sensor photoplethysmography (PPG).

METHODS: Synchronized PPG and arterial line 10-minute recordings from 100 patients in the ICU were analyzed. Using a hybrid feature selection strategy (RReliefF and intrinsic model-specific rankings), we reduced 201 initial features to an optimized subset of 30 core features. Model development and evaluation were designed to minimize information leakage and overfitting, incorporating nested cross-validation and patient-wise testing to assess generalizability across heterogeneous ICU populations. We developed and validated predictive models using machine learning techniques, specifically XGBoost (XGB), random forest, and support vector regression, with XGB serving as our primary model.

RESULTS: Among the evaluated models, the Hybrid Top 30 XGB configuration provided the best balance between estimation performance, model compactness, and computational efficiency. The model achieved mean absolute errors of 8.61 mm Hg (SBP), 3.50 mm Hg (MAP), and 2.62 mm Hg (DBP). For MAP and DBP, mean difference (SD) values of -0.09 (4.54) mm Hg and -1.07 (3.51) mm Hg, respectively, satisfied the Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation numerical criteria, while performance corresponded to Grade A according to the British Hypertension Society grading criteria. Although SBP exhibited greater variability, estimation performance was largely preserved using a physiologically informed subset of 30 features (approximately 15% of the original feature set). Feature importance analysis revealed distinct physiological feature patterns across SBP, MAP, and DBP estimation.

CONCLUSIONS: Interpretability analysis identified key predictors associated with wave reflection, systolic timing, low-frequency vasomotor activity, and autonomic regulation. By explicitly linking predictive features to underlying cardiovascular physiology, the proposed framework addresses a key limitation of existing black-box cuffless BP models. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that an optimized XGB framework using physiologically informed PPG features can provide accurate and computationally efficient BP estimation in ICU settings and may support the assessment of clinically relevant hemodynamic states using a single-sensor PPG platform. These findings provide a foundation for future development of more robust and generalizable interpretable BP estimation models and cuffless monitoring technologies.

articles.title: Effect of Teledermatologist Supervision in AI Skin Cancer Apps on Patients' Trust and Adherence Intentions: Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Skin cancer incidence is rising globally, increasing pressure on dermatology services and making efficient triage increasingly important. AI-driven skin cancer mobile health apps may help address this need, but their usefulness depends on whether users trust the advice and intend to follow it. Teledermatologist supervision has been proposed to combine AI efficiency with human clinical oversight, but dermatologist shortages make it critical to understand whether such supervision improves patient trust and adherence at the population level, or whether AI-only advice suffices for most users.

OBJECTIVE: This study tests whether teledermatologist supervision in an AI-driven skin cancer app affects patient trust and adherence intentions, compared with AI-only advice, and whether these effects differ by motivational context and risk assessment level.

METHODS: The randomized controlled, online vignette experiment with repeated measures was conducted from May to June 2025 as a single-center study among Dutch adults via an academic hospital-based patient panel. Eligible participants were adult members of the Erasmus MC Digital Patient Panel invited by email; those not completing all 4 vignette trials were excluded from the analysis. Participants completed 4 simulated mobile app scenarios varying in advice source (AI-only vs hybrid teledermatologist and AI) and risk assessment level (high vs low). The primary outcomes were trust in the advice (0-100 scale) and adherence intention (recoded 3-level ordinal scale). Mixed-effects models were used to analyze the data.

RESULTS: Of the 2707 patient panel members, 879 participated (response rate: 32.5%). Participants were aged 18 to 93 (mean 62.5, SD 12.64) years; 50.4% (n=443) were female, and 21.4% (n=188) had a history of skin cancer. Participants were randomly allocated to motivation conditions (concern: n=438 vs curiosity: n=441). Trust was higher for hybrid advice than AI-only advice (mean 76.9, SE 0.73 vs mean 65.7, SE 0.73; estimated difference 11.98; partial η²=0.22; P<.001). The odds of adherence were 1.7 times greater with hybrid vs AI-only (odds ratio 1/0.59=1.7, 95% CI 1.28-2.22; P<.001). High-risk assessments increased adherence (odds ratio 2.9, 95% CI 2.2-3.8; P<.001), with a moderated effect by motivation (P=.03), showing stronger adherence with concern vs curiosity. The effect of advice source on adherence was fully mediated by trust.

CONCLUSIONS: Teledermatologist supervision of AI-based advice robustly increased patient trust and adherence intentions, particularly for high-risk assessments and concerned users. Our experiment is innovative in testing teledermatologist supervision in a population-level AI skin cancer app and in examining how motivational context shapes responses to advice. Unlike studies focused on postreferral teledermatology or chatbot-based advice, this study isolates the effect of hybrid AI-human advice in a store-and-forward screening context. These findings suggest that developers and health care implementers may consider integrating teledermatologist supervision to maximize patient trust of and adherence to advice, potentially improving triaging efficiency and safety.

articles.title: The Rising Tide of Cardiovascular Risk in Younger Women.
articles.abstract: Menopause management is in the midst of a paradigm shift as enthusiasm, fueled by the lay press and online influencers, increases amongst women, yielding an escalating interest in hormone therapy (HT) that has not been experienced since the turn of the last century. Updates to regulatory labeling of menopausal HT products include the removal of boxed warnings and language that recommended using the lowest dose for the shortest time while focusing on risks and benefits to those seeking menopause symptom relief-women younger than 60 or within 10 years of menopause. This renewed desire for menopausal HT must be tempered with the understanding that risks for cardiovascular disease (CVD) are also rising in premenopausal women as are hospitalizations for acute coronary syndromes. Factors that contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk include adverse pregnancy outcomes, which are occurring with increasing frequency. The metabolic changes that accompany the menopause transition further complicate a woman's cardiovascular risk profile. Many women today will arrive at menopause with more advanced CVD risk than what was encountered in the past. If women are considering HT for menopausal symptom relief or bone preservation, careful consideration is required to identify and treat modifiable CVD risks-dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, hypertension, and, increasingly, obesity-to targets established by guidelines before initiating HT. Risk assessment with validated risk calculators can help stratify CVD risk, a factor that determines lipid lowering therapy, and the advisability and choice of menopausal HT. The rising tide of cardiovascular risk does not have to make waves at menopause.

articles.title: A Randomized Trial of Fractionated CO2 Laser With Topical Clobetasol Compared With Fractionated CO2 Laser With Placebo for Treatment of Vulvar Lichen Sclerosus.
authors: Society of Gynecologic Surgeons Collaborative Research in Pelvic Surgery Consortium (SGS CoRPS)
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare skin-related outcomes in women with vulvar lichen sclerosus treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser with concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% with women treated with fractionated carbon dioxide laser plus placebo ointment.

METHODS: This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial was conducted at nine U.S. sites from March 2022 to April 2025. English- or Spanish-speaking adult women with lichen sclerosus electing vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment were eligible. Women were excluded if they had prior vaginal mesh prolapse repair, previous radiation therapy, prior laser, immunomodulators or systemic therapy for lichen sclerosus, active genital infection, suspicious vulvar lesion or malignancy, active treatment for malignancy, or poor wound healing or if they were currently pregnant, lactating, or planning pregnancy. All participants underwent three vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatments 4-6 weeks apart and were randomized 1:1 to concomitant clobetasol propionate 0.05% or petrolatum-based ointment (placebo) 0.25-0.5 g nightly for 4 weeks starting at first laser treatment and then twice weekly until end of study. The primary outcome was proportion of women with improvement of 16 or more points on the Skindex-29, a validated questionnaire measuring a patient's skin-related symptoms and functioning, assessed at 4-5 weeks after completion of fractionated carbon dioxide laser treatment. Additional outcomes included Skindex-29 domain scores, patient impression of improvement (PGI-I [Patient Global Impression of Improvement] score), treatment satisfaction, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Two hundred one participants were randomized, and 180 (89 clobetasol vs 91 placebo) had complete data. Most women indicated symptom onset 1 year or more before lichen sclerosus diagnosis, and approximately 90% had previously used topical corticosteroids. Nearly a third of all participants achieved the primary outcome (30.3% clobetasol vs 27.5% placebo, P=.67). Participants in the clobetasol arm demonstrated a greater improvement in Skindex-29 symptom score (mean change -19.0±18.5 clobetasol vs -10.1±19.8 placebo, P<.01) and total score (mean change -13.0±15.9 clobetasol vs -8.1±15.5 placebo, P=.04). More participants were "satisfied" or "very satisfied" with treatment after clobetasol (85.4% clobetasol vs 69.2% placebo, P=.01). Fifteen adverse events occurred in 12 participants (6 per cohort).

CONCLUSION: There was no difference in the proportion of patients improving at least 16 points on the Skindex-29 after combined vulvar fractionated carbon dioxide laser and clobetasol compared with placebo. The clobetasol group reported greater improvement in lichen sclerosus-specific symptoms and higher treatment satisfaction. The rates of adverse events were low regardless of concomitant therapy.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04951206.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Outcome Measures Used for Clinical Assessment in Adults Across the National Cancer Institute Community Oncology Research Program Practices.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) have been used to monitor patient response during cancer treatment and have resulted in improved clinical outcomes. This study examined the use of PROMs implemented for clinical assessment across the National Cancer Institute Community Oncology Research Program (NCORP) community practices.

METHODS: This study used data from the 2017 and 2022 NCORP cancer care delivery landscape surveys. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze survey item data. Logistic regression models examined the relationship between geographic region and the organizational characteristics of practice settings that used and recorded PROMS in the electronic health record (EHR).

RESULTS: Although most practices routinely assessed distress in 2017 (87.8%) and 2022 (91.1%), only 32.1% of practices used PROMs aimed at assessing health-related quality of life (HRQOL) or symptoms in 2017 and the rate decreased in 2022 (23.2%). A wide variety of questionnaires were used to measure distress and HRQOL/symptoms. No geographic or organizational factors were associated with use of PROMs for distress, whereas practices in the West and those with lower cancer patient volume were less likely to use PROMs to assess HRQOL or symptoms. Geographic location and participation in the Oncology Care Model (OCM) were associated with recording distress screening PROMs in the EHR, whereas participation in the OCM was the only factor associated with recording HRQOL or symptom assessment PROMs.

CONCLUSION: Given that most adults with cancer are treated in their communities, it is critical to gain a better understanding of the factors associated with the low use of PROMs for HRQOL/symptom assessment in community-based practices. Alternative models for collecting PROMs may be needed to minimize future inequities in patient-centered cancer care delivery.

articles.title: Optimizing use of GLP-1 receptor agonists: safety, tolerability, adherence, and patient selection in cardiovascular practice.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have fundamentally transformed modern cardiometabolic care, moving beyond glycemic control to become a cornerstone of obesity management and potent cardiovascular risk reduction. Large-scale clinical trials consistently highlight their cardioprotective benefits, demonstrating significant reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), cardiovascular mortality, and obesity-related heart failure complications. However, translating these remarkable clinical trial successes into routine clinical practice reveals a marked gap between efficacy and effectiveness, primarily driven by suboptimal patient persistence and adherence. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence regarding the pharmacology, safety, tolerability, adherence, and patient selection of GLP-1RAs to support optimal therapeutic decision-making in cardiovascular practice. While long-term data disprove clear causal relationships with pancreatic or thyroid malignancies, a high incidence of predictable, dose-related gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) remains the leading cause of early treatment discontinuation. Additionally, treatment persistence in clinical practice is heavily influenced by financial burdens, supply chain instability, and formulation choices. Cardioprotective benefits are well-established for patients with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Mitigating challenges in clinical practice requires a systematic, multi-step prescribing framework focused on targeted patient selection, gradual individualized dose titration ("start low and go slow"), and proactive multidisciplinary symptom management.

articles.title: An Integrated Approach for Early In Vitro Sedation Prediction Utilizing hiPSC Neurons and Human Ion Channel Assays.
articles.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) liabilities remain a significant cause of failure in drug development. Two complementary in vitro safety assays were previously developed, combining automated patch-clamp electrophysiology and multielectrode array techniques, to detect and avoid seizurogenic compounds. Further to seizure risk, sedation and fatigue are commonly encountered CNS side effects during drug safety testing. Here, the aim was to extend the capability of the in vitro safety assay to enable earlier detection of sedative potential. Fourteen compounds with reported sedative activity and five non-sedative controls were screened in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons using multielectrode array. These compounds were further screened with automated patch-clamp electrophysiology using cells expressing CNS ion channels implicated in sedation: KV1.1, KV2.1, KV3.1, KV7.2/7.3, NaV1.2, K2P2.1, or the α1β2γ2 GABAA, and α4β2 nicotinic receptors. Known sedative compounds reduced neural firing and network burst activity in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-neurons, indicating sedative effects, whilst negative control compounds did not significantly change multielectrode array parameters. Of the 19 compounds screened, 94% were accurately classified. Automated patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed that several sedative compounds interacted with CNS ion channels within a 30-fold margin to their total therapeutic blood plasma concentration. These results support the use of the combined in vitro safety models for detecting sedative as well as seizurogenic effects, offering valuable human-based tools for early hazard identification and prioritization of drug candidates. These platforms are also useful for interpretation of CNS-related findings in vivo supporting the principles of 3Rs to minimize and replace the use of animals in scientific testing.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Hepatology: Emerging Opportunities and Translational Challenges.
articles.abstract: In December 2025, the Food and Drug Administration assessed and qualified the first artificial intelligence (AI)-powered tool for use in drug development trials; this AI system evaluates digital liver biopsies for steatohepatitis and fibrosis. However, AI is still being investigated before it can be applied directly to patient care in the field of Hepatology. Current patient-facing applications at most institutions are limited to assistive tools such as computer-aided polyp detection and large language model documentation tools that draft clinic notes and patient communications, although there exist radiographic and pathologic liver AI tools that could function at and may even exceed human capabilities. This review provides a broad introduction to AI and highlights clinical research that use AI to enhance the diagnosis, prognostication, and management of liver diseases. It will also discuss the challenges that will need to be overcome before AI can be adopted to clinical practice.

articles.title: High-Frequency Chest Wall Oscillation in Critical Care: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Airway secretion retention represents a major clinical challenge in critically ill patients, promoting gas exchange impairment and atelectasis, precipitating failure of noninvasive respiratory support, and prolonging invasive mechanical ventilation, with an associated increase in respiratory-related complications and mortality. High-frequency chest wall oscillation (HFCWO) is a noninvasive airway clearance technique widely used in chronic respiratory diseases, but its role in the intensive care unit (ICU) remains unclear. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the available evidence on the efficacy and safety of HFCWO in adult ICU patients.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library from inception to December 2025 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies evaluating HFCWO in adult ICU patients, including those receiving invasive or noninvasive respiratory support, were eligible. Primary outcomes included duration of mechanical ventilation, ICU length of stay, and mortality. Secondary outcomes included impact on secretion airway clearance and its radiographic/functional surrogates as well as safety and treatment tolerance.

RESULTS: A limited number of studies met the inclusion criteria, mainly small randomized controlled trials and observational studies, characterized by substantial heterogeneity in patient populations, intervention protocols, and assessed outcomes. HFCWO effects on clinically meaningful primary endpoints, including duration of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU stay, and mortality, remain variable and inconclusive. Overall, HFCWO was well tolerated and appeared to enhance secretion clearance, with some studies reporting modest improvements in oxygenation and respiratory mechanics.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence suggests that HFCWO is a safe and feasible airway clearance strategy in selected ICU patients with secretion burden and without proved effects on the main clinical outcomes. Lack of physiopathologically driven criteria for selection of patients more likely to respond to HFCWO either alone or integrated with other cough-assisting techniques may partially explain these scanty findings from the overall published studies. This precludes its routine use in clinical practice. Well-designed, adequately powered randomized trials are needed to define patient selection criteria, optimal timing, and the true clinical impact of HFCWO in the ICU setting.

articles.title: Paediatric Long-Term Home Respiratory Support: Recommendations of the Swiss Society of Paediatric Pulmonology.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract: The number of paediatric patients evaluated for long-term home respiratory support has risen sharply in recent years, reflecting both improved survival of children with complex chronic conditions and expanded therapeutic indications. This population is characterized by substantial clinical heterogeneity, encompassing obstructive, restrictive, or central ventilatory disorders. Contributing comorbidities - such as severe obesity, chronic aspiration with secondary lung disease, neuromuscular weakness, impaired central respiratory drive, and dynamic upper airway obstruction - further complicate diagnostic assessment and long-term management. This consensus statement, developed by the Special Interest Group of the Swiss Society of Paediatric Pulmonology, provides comprehensive recommendations for Switzerland. It defines current indications for non-invasive and invasive home respiratory support, proposes criteria for patient selection, and outlines key competencies and composition of an optimal multidisciplinary care team. The document also specifies requirements for equipment provision, safety measures, and training of caregivers, while offering structured guidance for monitoring strategies, long-term follow-up, and management of acute exacerbations. Ethical considerations and best practices for transitioning adolescents to adult respiratory care are additionally addressed, with the aim of standardizing care pathways and improving clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Safety and Feasibility of the Lung Volume Reduction Reverser System in Patients with Severe Emphysema: A First-in-Human Pilot Study.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endoscopic lung volume reduction with coils is a symptomatic treatment approach for patients with severe pulmonary emphysema and positive collateral ventilation. In this study, we evaluated the safety and feasibility of the new Lung Volume Reduction Reverser (LVR-R) system.

METHODS: Prospective, nonrandomized, exploratory, single-center, first-in-man study in 15 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and severe emphysema. Most affected lung lobes were treated sequentially with the LVR-R coils from May 2019 to JUL 2022. Pulmonary function, 6-min walking distance (6-MWD), questionnaires and adverse events were recorded from baseline to 1-year post-procedure. Computer tomography was acquired at baseline and 6 months.

RESULTS: A total of 28 procedures were performed, in which 10 (n = 22, 78.6%), 9 (n = 2, 7.1%), or 8 (n = 4, 14.3%) LVR-R coils were implanted, predominantly in the upper lobes (n = 26/28, 92.86%). Two patients refused a second treatment, one of whom refused follow-ups. Adverse events at 3 months included severe pneumonia and/or COPD exacerbations (n = 7), ventilatory failure (n = 2) and 1 pneumothorax requiring thoracic drainage. Mild hemoptysis occurred in 18 and mild pneumonia and/or COPD exacerbations in 9 patients. Overall, neither FEV1, residual volume, 6-MWD, CAT nor mMRC improved within 1-year (n.s. all). In 2 patients, response in FEV1 >500 mL occurred.

CONCLUSION: In this severely diseased and small patient cohort, LVR-R implantation was technically feasible. The complication rate was similar to other coil studies and requires a careful pre-procedure benefit-risk evaluation. Two of fourteen bilaterally treated individuals demonstrated a notable improvement in lung function.

articles.title: Treatment Outcomes of Endoscopic Lung Volume Reduction with Valves in Advanced Lung Emphysema Patients Are Largely Independent of Body Mass Index: Data from the German Lung Emphysema Registry.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endoscopic lung volume reduction (ELVR) via valves is a proven therapeutic option for patients with advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema without collateral ventilation. Body mass index (BMI), a simple measure of adiposity, has a complex relationship with COPD. A lower BMI is associated with increased mortality in this patient population. However, the influence of BMI on the outcome of ELVR remains unclear.

METHODS: This analysis was conducted with data from the Lung Emphysema Registry (www.lungenemphysemregister.de), a national, prospective, multicentric, producer-independent, open-label clinical trial. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of baseline BMI on treatment outcomes after ELVR. Patients were grouped according to their BMI as follows: underweight (BMI <20 kg/m2, n = 76), normal weight (20-24.9 kg/m2, n = 282), overweight (BMI = 25-30 kg/m2, n = 146), and obese (BMI >30 kg/m2, n = 45).

RESULTS: Baseline parameters were characteristic of patients with advanced lung emphysema. Emphysema scores and heterogeneity indices of the target lobe were greater in patients with lower BMI. Patients with a lower BMI had worse lung function parameters (FEV1, RV, DLCO, pCO2) and a higher CAT score. All groups showed significant improvements after ELVR at the 3-month follow-up in terms of lung function parameters, exercise capacity, and quality of life. Treatment outcomes were comparable across BMI groups, with the notable exception of more pronounced improvement in CAT scores among underweight patients. The complication rates were low and comparable among the groups, although obese patients had a higher rate of ICU admissions.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that ELVR provides meaningful clinical benefits regardless of BMI in patients with advanced lung emphysema, particularly when dyspnea is primarily attributable to pulmonary pathology. The findings suggest that BMI should be considered as a reflection of disease phenotype and clinical state rather than serving as a predictor for treatment response after ELVR.

articles.title: Sex-Based Comparison of Remission in Patients with Severe Type 2 Asthma Treated with Biologics: A Real-World Analysis from the "Southern Italy Network on Severe Asthma Therapy".
authors: Southern Italy Network on Severe Asthma Therapy
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sex influences asthma phenotypes and treatment outcomes. However, real-world data on sex-related differences in severe asthma patients treated with biologics are limited. The objective of this study was to assess sex differences in baseline characteristics and treatment outcomes in a cohort of severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA) patients treated with biologics.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 370 SEA patients (235 females, 135 males) treated with mepolizumab, benralizumab, or dupilumab. Clinical remission was defined as no OCS use plus at least two of: no exacerbations, ACT ≥20, or FEV1 >80%. Logistic regression was used to identify sex-specific predictors of remission at 24 months.

RESULTS: Severe type 2 asthma showed a prevalence in females (female-to-male ratio of 1.7:1). Baseline characteristics revealed higher prevalence of obesity (p = 0.015) and osteoporosis (p = 0.006) in females, and greater tobacco exposure (p = 0.05), FeNO (p = 0.03), and nasal polyposis (p = 0.0002) in males. Males had greater reduction in FeNO (p ≤ 0.05) and more male patients stopped exacerbations at 24 months (p < 0.0001), while females showed greater FEF25-75% (p ≤ 0.05) improvement and larger IgE drops (p < 0.0001). Remission rates were similar across sexes at both 12 months (64.3% versus 74.1%; p = 0.06) and 24 months (71.5% versus 77.0%; p = 0.27). In females, remission was associated with eosinophils >300/μL (OR: 2.68; 95% CI: 1.41-5.07; p = 0.003), FeNO >50 ppb (OR: 21.05; 95% CI: 10.24-43.34; p < 0.0001), and nasal polyposis (OR: 2.74; 95% CI: 1.46-5.13; p = 0.001); obesity (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.37; p < 0.0001), smoking (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.21-0.70; p = 0.002), anxiety (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.23-0.94; p = 0.04), and reflux (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27-0.84; p = 0.01) were negative predictors. In males, OCS dependency (OR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.13-0.94; p = 0.03) and FEV1 <80% (OR: 0.18; 95% CI: 0.05-0.63; p = 0.004) were negative predictors.

CONCLUSION: Biologics were equally effective in inducing clinical remission across sexes, but different predictors influenced outcomes. Sex-aware strategies may support personalized asthma care.

articles.title: The Montafon Proposal: New Insights and Emerging Concepts in Pulmonary Rehabilitation.
articles.journal: Respiration; international review of thoracic diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is beneficial, yet outcome assessment remains inconsistent. A multidisciplinary D-A-CH working group reviewed evidence, introduced new measures, and explored emerging PR concepts.

SUMMARY: The meeting emphasized patient-reported and clinician-reported outcome measures. A key focus was the minimal clinically important difference (MCID), a widely used metric which is applied inconsistently and is highly dependent on the baseline value. The "performance score" (T2D = T2 + (T2-T1)) takes baseline status (T1) into account by combining the discharge value (T2) with the improvement (T2-T1) before and after treatment, based on the distribution. This simple descriptive approach results in a baseline-adjusted MCID estimator, with a planned multicenter study to validate its use in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease rehabilitation. Further discussions addressed epistemic trust, crucial for patient adherence and interdisciplinary collaboration, with a study planned to assess its impact. Dysfunctional breathing (DB), often overlooked in PR, was highlighted, emphasizing the need for standardized diagnostic tools. The role of artificial intelligence (AI) in PR, including large language models, was explored, with surveys planned to evaluate patient and provider perceptions.

KEY MESSAGES: The T2D performance score offers a dynamic approach to assessing PR progress, addressing MCID limitations.
