Standardized methods for epistemic trust and DB diagnosis are essential for better recognition and management. AI integration in PR presents opportunities for personalized rehabilitation but requires further evaluation. The D-A-CH working group remains committed to advancing PR through evidence-based strategies and international collaboration.

articles.title: Early Loop-Diuretic Administration and Subsequent Kidney Deterioration in Hospitalized Patients with Heart Failure: A MIMIC-IV Landmark Study.
articles.abstract: Early loop diuretics are central to decongestion in heart failure, but their association with subsequent kidney deterioration remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective 6-hour landmark study of adults with ICD-coded heart failure in MIMIC-IV. Exposure was documented administration of furosemide, bumetanide, or torsemide before 6 hours. Eligible admissions required baseline creatinine and a follow-up measurement from 6 to <48 hours. Kidney deterioration was defined as a creatinine increase of ≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5-fold from baseline. We estimated crude and adjusted associations using propensity-score weighting and augmented inverse probability weighting (AIPW); adjusted and weighted confidence intervals accounted for repeated admissions by patient, whereas the crude interval did not. Among 23,336 admissions from 15,764 patients, 2,453 (10.5%) received early treatment and 4,506 (19.3%) met the endpoint. Kidney deterioration occurred in 22.7% of early-treated admissions versus 18.9% of comparators (crude risk ratio [RR] 1.20, 95% CI 1.11-1.30). The directly adjusted RR was 1.30 (95% CI 1.20-1.41), the overlap-weighted RR was 1.31 (95% CI 1.21-1.43), and the AIPW RR was 1.31 (95% CI 1.20-1.44). The overlap-weighted absolute risk difference was 5.5 percentage points (95% CI 3.7-7.4). Mortality was not significantly associated with early treatment (RR 1.12, 95% CI 0.96-1.30). Restricting the endpoint to the first follow-up creatinine attenuated the association (overlap-weighted RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17), highlighting sensitivity to monitoring intensity. Early loop-diuretic administration was associated with higher subsequent creatinine-defined deterioration, but differential surveillance and confounding by indication preclude causal conclusions or recommendations to delay treatment.

articles.title: Cranial Injuries due to Misuse of Infant Carriers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Infant carriers (car seats, bouncy chairs) can cause injuries when used for other than their intended purpose.

METHODS: We studied children aged 0-24 months with carrier related injuries reported to the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study (PTOS) dataset (2001-2022 inclusive).

RESULTS: There were 562 injured children, averaging 23 injuries per year. Mean age was 3.3 months; 54.3% were male. Most (82.7%) fell from an elevated surface; 88.7% fell an estimated 2-5 feet. Head injuries (intracranial injury/hemorrhage and/or skull fracture) were present in 85.6%. Admission Glasgow Coma Scores were most commonly 15 (79.1%); 7 had GCS <12. Average Injury Severity Score was 9.3 (range 1-30). Average length of stay was 1.4 days; 30% spent >1 day in the intensive care unit. Two children underwent cranial operations. There were no deaths, and 82.9% were discharged home.

CONCLUSION: Falls in, or from, infant carriers are a significant public health concern. Education, advocacy, and changes in carrier design may help reduce the frequency of these injuries.

articles.title: The effects of environmental temperature on the extrinsic incubation period of arboviruses in their mosquito vectors: A systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arboviruses are an increasing global public health concern, driven by both human and environmental factors. A key parameter shaping vectorial capacity for transmission is the extrinsic incubation period (EIP), the time required for a mosquito that has ingested an infectious blood meal to become capable of transmitting the virus via its saliva, which is strongly influenced by temperature. However, the temperature-EIP relationship remains poorly characterized across arboviruses and mosquito species.

METHODS: We conducted the first systematic review of laboratory studies evaluating temperature effects on EIP across all reported mosquito-arbovirus pairings identifiable in the literature. We searched three databases and extracted data on infection and transmission efficiency (TE), applying a binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model to estimate the median extrinsic incubation period, the time post-infection at which 50% of infected mosquitoes become infectious.

RESULTS: Our synthesis included 53 studies covering 17 arboviruses. We found substantial heterogeneity in temperature effects on TE. Zika and West Nile viruses generally showed increased TE and shorter EIP at higher temperatures. However, similar trends based on published data were not clear for many viruses, such as Sindbis and chikungunya viruses, because of limited data granularity and small sample sizes. Even across different vectors of the same virus, findings varied widely, reflecting both biological differences and inconsistent experimental designs.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings revealed gaps in the understanding of the temperature effects on the EIP of arboviruses in mosquito vectors. Standardisation of reporting in vector competence experiments and expanded research on neglected viruses are urgently needed. Real-world environmental conditions should also be incorporated to improve modelling and support robust vector control and public health planning under changing climatic conditions.

articles.title: Cytolethal distending toxin promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition by modulating AKT-dependent β-catenin Ser552 phosphorylation.
articles.abstract: Bacterial genotoxins, Cytolethal Distending Toxin (CDT) and colibactin, cause DNA damage in intoxicated epithelial cells of the host. DNA damage influences β‑catenin signaling, altering its stability and nuclear translocation, potentially contributing to cancer development. Using non-transformed hepatocytes and cancer-derived intestinal and hepatic epithelial cell lines, we showed that CDT/CdtB induces the phosphorylation of β‑catenin at serine 552, along with the loss of β‑catenin from adherens junctions. This leads to the subsequent cytoplasmic accumulation and nuclear translocation of β‑catenin, ultimately driving TCF/LEF transcription, the crucial downstream event of Wnt/β‑catenin signaling, as well as the transcription of some β‑catenin target genes. Colibactin induces similar effects. MK‑2206, a direct AKT inhibitor, and metformin, a common diabetes drug that indirectly inhibits AKT, both protected cells against various effects induced by CdtB exposure. These effects include β‑catenin phosphorylation at Ser552, the disassembly of cell-cell junctions and the subsequent nuclear accumulation of phosphorylated β‑catenin, leading to enhanced TCF/LEF-mediated transcription-early molecular shifts driving the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Specifically, both drugs protected against CdtB-induced EMT features, including increased nuclear accumulation of SNAIL, enhanced matrix degradation, and motility. Overall, these data show that infection with genotoxin-producing bacteria promotes key EMT features through β‑catenin and AKT-dependent signaling.

articles.title: Implantation Technique, Continuous Implant Geometry, and Longitudinal Low-Voltage Impedance After Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Defibrillation efficacy of the subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) depends on shock vector geometry and tissue impedances influenced by implantation technique. Whether longitudinal low-voltage impedance (LVI) measurements differ across contemporary implantation strategies, and whether these differences are explained by quantitative radiographic geometry, remains incompletely characterized.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether S-ICD implantation technique is associated with longitudinal LVI trajectories and whether continuous radiographic implant geometry provides information beyond categorical PRAETORIAN risk classification.

METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of 136 adults receiving an S-ICD between 2014 and 2024, classified by operative documentation as subcutaneous (SC; n = 27), fluoroscopy-marked intermuscular (FIM; n = 73), or fluoroscopy-marked ultrasound-guided intermuscular (FUSIM; n = 36) techniques. Per-device LVI was summarized overall and across prespecified windows (0-30 days, 6 months-1 year, 2-5 years). Technique differences were analyzed. We fit a prespecified mixed-effects interaction model that included coil-sternum distance, scaled in 5 mm increments, and assessed correlations between LVI and radiographic measures.

RESULTS: In paired analyses, LVI increased by a mean of 13.3 Ω between the 0-30-day and 2-5-year windows. Overall LVI differed by implantation technique (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.019), driven by higher values in SC versus FIM (Holm-adjusted p = 0.041) and FUSIM (p = 0.022). Additional impedance differences across techniques were absent in the 0-30-day window but emerged during follow-up. In the prespecified interaction mixed-effects model, SC exhibited a significant additional rise relative to FUSIM during the 2-5-year window (interaction β = 7.82 Ω, 95% CI 0.98-14.67; p = 0.025). Greater coil-sternum distance was independently associated with higher LVI (13.6 Ω per cm, 95% CI 4.2-23.0; p = 0.005) and correlated with chronic LVI (n = 76; r = 0.441; Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.001). The PRAETORIAN score was computable in 76 devices and classified 84% as low risk; within that low-risk stratum, coil-sternum distance remained associated with chronic LVI (ρ = 0.320, p = 0.010) whereas the score did not (ρ = 0.136, p = 0.282), and each 5 mm of coil-sternum distance corresponded to 10.7 Ω higher LVI after adjustment for BMI (95% CI 2.68-18.73, p = 0.010). High-voltage shock impedance at implant correlated strongly with chronic LVI (n = 99; r = 0.71, p < 0.001), and the association persisted over 2-5 years (n = 69; r = 0.61, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Longitudinal LVI varies with S-ICD implantation strategy, with time-dependent divergence between SC and intermuscular implants. Within the low-risk PRAETORIAN category, where the categorical score has no dynamic range, continuously measured coil-sternum distance remains associated with chronic impedance. Continuous implant geometry and longitudinal impedance complement, rather than replace, radiographic scoring of implant position.

articles.title: c-di-AMP regulates virulence of Staphylococcus aureus via targeting the SarA-family regulator SarS.
articles.abstract: Cyclic di-AMP (c-di-AMP) is a second messenger that plays a pivotal role in regulating many physiological processes in bacteria. The fluctuation in intracellular levels of c-di-AMP are often associated with virulence of many bacterial pathogens, but c-di-AMP receptors involved in virulence regulation and the underlying mechanisms are still largely unclear. Here, we report that the SarA-family virulence regulator SarS in Staphylococcus aureus is a c-di-AMP-responsive transcription factor. We show that c-di-AMP specifically binds to SarS at a ratio of 2:1. We further demonstrate that binding of c-di-AMP to SarS interferes with the binding of SarS to its target promoters, thereby downregulating the expression of the SarS-activated gene spa and upregulating the expression of SarS-repressed genes/operons such as hla, lukED, and lukSF-PV. In an intravenous mouse infection model, SarS is found to act as a virulence repressor and elevated c-di-AMP levels enhance the virulence of S. aureus via targeting SarS. Thus, our results reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism by which c-di-AMP signaling regulates the virulence of S. aureus.

articles.title: Phosphorylation-dependent LEF-6 promotes nuclear export of viral RNA polymerase transcripts to ensure the expression of viral very late genes.
articles.abstract: The baculovirus late expression factor 6 (LEF-6) has long been considered as a regulator of late transcription. Our recent study found that knocking out the lef-6 gene in Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV) markedly down-regulates the expression of the polyhedrin gene (polh), but the specific regulatory mechanism remains unclear. Previous studies indicated that LEF-6 may be involved in viral mRNA nuclear export. Here, through a combination of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq), and genetic approaches, we demonstrated that LEF-6 is crucial for the nuclear export of viral RNA polymerase mRNA, consequently affecting the transcriptional activity of very late genes, such as polh. During viral infection, nuclear-imported LEF-6 binds to viral RNA polymerase subunit mRNAs and undergoes nuclear export via the host CRM1 pathway, thereby ensuring the generation of sufficient viral RNA polymerase to guarantee the hyperexpression of the very late gene polh. Further investigation revealed that LEF-6 nuclear export heavily relies on host endogenous kinase-mediated phosphorylation at S156/159, serving as the key molecular switch driving this process. In summary, our study elucidated the molecular mechanism of BmNPV LEF-6-mediated viral RNA polymerase mRNA transport and revealed how this mechanism activates baculovirus very late gene transcription.

articles.title: Incidence of Pacing-Induced Cardiomyopathy in Active-Fixation Leadless Pacemakers.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a known complication of high right ventricular (RV) pacing burden with transvenous pacemakers, but its incidence with active-fixation leadless pacemakers (LPs) is unknown. This study's aim was to determine the incidence of PICM among patients implanted with LPs using helix-based active fixation and assess its association with heart failure hospitalizations (HFH).

METHODS AND RESULTS: This multi-center retrospective cohort study included patients implanted with active-fixation LPs between 2021 and 2025. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) measurements were obtained pre- and post-implant. Inclusion criteria were: de novo pacemaker implant, ≥ 20% RV pacing burden, baseline LVEF of > 50%, and > 30 days of follow-up. PICM was defined as a ≥ 10% reduction in LVEF from baseline to a value < 50%, with no other identifiable causes for left ventricular dysfunction. Patient demographics, comorbidities, procedural history, and baseline pacemaker, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic data were compared between patients with and without PICM. Categorical variables were analyzed using the "N-1" Chi-squared or Fisher's exact test and continuous variables with Welch's t-test. Cox proportional hazards models were used for univariate analysis of PICM and HFH. Among 164 patients implanted with active-fixation LPs, 57 met inclusion criteria (mean age 78 ± 11 years). Dual-chamber systems accounted for 47.4% of implants, and 96.5% of ventricular devices were placed in the low RV septum. Six patients (10.5%) developed PICM during 14.2 ± 10.9 months of follow-up, with a mean time to onset of 7.5 ± 2.4 months. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between patients with and without PICM. At the time of diagnosis, those with PICM had a greater decline in LVEF (23% vs. 2%, p < 0.001). Although RV pacing burden was higher in PICM patients (88.8% vs. 76.6%), this difference was not statistically significant. PICM was a strong predictor of HFH (HR: 6.9, p = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: PICM occurred in 10.5% of patients receiving active-fixation LPs with high ventricular pacing burden. Our findings highlight the importance of standardized follow-up echocardiography within the first year post-implant to improve surveillance and timely recognition of PICM.

articles.title: Economic value of gonorrhea resistance testing in the United States: A multi-perspective modeling study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rising antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae threatens the effectiveness of existing therapies. Ceftriaxone is the only recommended first-line (empiric) treatment for uncomplicated gonorrhea in the United States. Ciprofloxacin is no longer recommended for empiric use because of widespread resistance, but it is inexpensive, taken orally, and effective against susceptible infections, which a resistance test can identify. In the context of rising resistance, resistance-guided treatment (RGT) may reduce treatment failures, complications, and inappropriate use of last-line agents while slowing resistance emergence and preserving the efficacy of new and existing drugs. Understanding where RGT provides economic value-across near-term cost savings, delayed resistance emergence, and avoided antibiotic development costs-can illuminate the broader case for investing in resistance testing and help guide pricing and reimbursement decisions.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: We developed an individual-level stochastic simulation model of gonorrhea diagnosis and treatment in the United States, incorporating infection prevalence, symptom status, diagnostic accuracy, resistance profiles, treatment pathways, and partner management (costs in 2025 US dollars[USD]). We evaluated three resistance testing strategies, ciprofloxacin-only, ciprofloxacin + ceftriaxone, and triple-target (including a novel drug A), across a wide range of resistance scenarios. We quantified economic value across three dimensions: (1) per-episode direct medical cost savings, (2) system-level costs attributable to ceftriaxone resistance emergence among men who have sex with men (MSM), and (3) avoided costs of new antibiotic development, estimating the maximum per-test price at which RGT remains cost-neutral. Per-episode cost-neutrality thresholds ranged from near $0 when ceftriaxone resistance was absent to up to $48 per test at 15% prevalence of ceftriaxone resistance (proportion of infections resistant to ceftriaxone). At a prevalence of 50% ciprofloxacin resistance and 5% ceftriaxone resistance, the population-weighted threshold was $7 (95% uncertainty interval [UI] ($3, $11) for a ciprofloxacin-only test and $13 (95% UI [$8-$19]) for a triple-target test. Among MSM, incorporating system-level resistance emergence costs and avoided antibiotic development costs increased the total per-test value to $31 to $114 for a single-target test and $73 to $106 for a triple-target test, depending on whether prescribing practices shift when ceftriaxone resistance reaches 5%. The main limitations are that the model assumes resistance results are available at the same clinical visit to guide initial treatment, does not represent onward transmission or co-resistance between antibiotics, and could estimate longer-term value only for MSM.

CONCLUSIONS: Resistance-guided therapy offers economic benefits across multiple dimensions even at relatively high diagnostic prices, supporting investment in gonorrhea resistance testing to improve partner outcomes, delay resistance emergence, and enhance the long-term cost-efficiency of gonorrhea management.

articles.title: Urban-Rural Disparities in Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis: A Nationwide Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of hospital location on clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis (AP).

METHODS: We used the National Inpatient Sample database (2016-2022) to identify adult patients with AP. Patients were stratified by hospital location into urban and rural groups. Data on demographics, comorbidities, infections, and clinical outcomes were collected. Multivariate regression was used to assess the association between hospital setting and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 2 467 234 patients hospitalized with AP, 246 820 (10%) received care in rural hospitals. Patients in urban settings had a higher incidence of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35-1.62), sepsis (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.24), shock (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.64-1.92), acute kidney injury (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.29), intensive care unit admission (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.51-1.75), pulmonary embolism (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.05-1.47), and deep vein thrombosis (aOR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.09); (all P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that patients with AP treated in urban hospitals experience worse clinical outcomes and greater health care utilization than those in rural settings. These results underscore the importance of early diagnosis and risk stratification, particularly in high-volume urban hospitals, to improve patient outcomes.

articles.title: Doxycycline Post-Exposure Prophylaxis Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among HIV and PrEP Providers in Two NYC Academic Medical Centers: A Cross-Sectional Pilot Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) reduces sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among vulnerable populations. Effective implementation depends on willingness to prescribe, yet data on provider knowledge, attitudes, and practices in New York City (NYC) remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of providers at two NYC academic medical centers between May-September 2025. Eligibility required prescribing antiretroviral therapy or PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis) to ≥ 5 patients in the prior year. The online questionnaire adapted from a PrEP acceptability instrument measured provider doxy-PEP knowledge, attitudes, prescribing practices, and perceived barriers. Knowledge scores were summed from correct responses; attitudes on a 4-point Likert scale were transformed to reflect positive views and summed. Median total scores were compared between primary care (non-specialists) and Infectious Disease/HIV (specialists) providers using one-sided Mann-Whitney U-tests to assess whether non-specialists had lower knowledge and attitude scores. Prescribing practices were compared with Fisher's exact test.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight eligible providers completed the survey (28 specialists, 10 non-specialists); 97% prescribed doxy-PEP previously. Specialists managed significantly larger HIV/PrEP patient panels (p<0.01). Non-specialists demonstrated lower objective doxy-PEP knowledge than specialists (median composite score 57% vs 86%, p < 0.01), particularly regarding efficacy and dosing. Doxy-PEP attitudes were favorable in both groups (median composite score 3.3 vs 3.4, max 4, p = 0.05). Concerns about antimicrobial resistance (49%) and side effects (30%) were the most reported prescribing barriers.

CONCLUSIONS: Non-specialists endorsed favorable doxy-PEP attitudes but had lower objective knowledge. Barriers including resistance and adverse effects highlight opportunities for targeted education to improve doxy-PEP knowledge and prescribing confidence among generalist providers.

articles.title: Costs of Common Sexually Transmitted Infection Tests from 2024 MarketScan Commercial Outpatient Claims.
articles.abstract: We estimated 2024 per-unit costs for commonly used sexually transmitted infection tests and selected ancillary services using outpatient claims from the Merative™ MarketScan® Commercial Database. These updated estimates may provide useful inputs for cost-effectiveness analyses, cost-of-illness studies, and related economic analyses.

articles.title: Epicardial Pulsed Field Ablation Across the Intact Pericardium: Feasibility, Safety Margins, and Tissue Selectivity in a Porcine Model.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epicardial pulsed field ablation (PFA) holds promise, but in vivo safety, dose-responses, and the intact pericardium's barrier effect remain largely unexplored.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Six pigs received 5, 10, 15, or 30 PFA shots via a pentaspline catheter (FARAWAVE system, 2.0 kV) placed externally on the intact left ventricular pericardium. Lesions were evaluated macroscopically and histologically at 1 month. PFA universally induced ventricular fibrillation requiring rescue shocks, and an observed numerical decline in left ventricular ejection fraction was noted at 1 month (72.6% to 50.1%). A distinct, nonlinear dose-response emerged. Standard doses (5-10 shots) yielded minimal true necrosis (0.15-2.63 cm3) despite broader gross lesions. At 15 shots, true necrosis expanded to 4.39 cm3, approaching the safety threshold. Conversely, an extreme 30-shot dose breached the pericardial impedance, causing a catastrophic spike in transmural necrosis (22.5 cm3) and early lethal heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: Epicardial PFA over an intact pericardium using a pentaspline catheter system could still create predictable lesions in the subepicardial area. The profound discrepancy between gross lesions and true necrosis suggests the pericardium acts as an electrical barrier. While massive overdoses cause non-selective damage, PFA's ability to create scars through a biological membrane inspires future catheter designs that could trap electrolytic microbubbles to eliminate embolic risks.

articles.title: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries: A Narrative Review of Diagnosis, Management, and Clinical Considerations.
articles.abstract: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries is a rare congenital heart defect caused by abnormal looping of the developing heart that results in double discordance of the atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial connections. In these patients, blood will flow through the heart in a physiologically correct direction; however, the morphologic right ventricle becomes responsible for pumping blood to the systemic circulation. The tricuspid valve also becomes the systemic atrioventricular valve. This places patients at risk for progressive right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, heart failure, arrhythmias, and atrioventricular block. The clinical presentation is highly variable, with some patients being diagnosed during infancy, while others remain asymptomatic and may be diagnosed in adulthood. Typically, the diagnosis is made using echocardiography as the main first-line imaging test. Management is nuanced and consists of surgical versus nonsurgical intervention. Surgical treatment has increasingly shifted from physiologic repair toward anatomic repair, including double-switch procedures that place the morphologic left ventricle in the systemic position. Despite major improvements in diagnosis and treatment, important questions remain about the best timing of intervention, long-term medical therapy, and risk prediction. Larger registries, prospective studies, improved imaging, and new biomarkers may help guide more individualized care and improve long-term outcomes for patients with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. However, due to the high risk for deteriorating cardiac function and cardiac-related events, these patients should be carefully monitored for life.

articles.title: Mortality and inpatient hospitalizations by anti-plasma cell dyscrasia treatment patterns among patients with cardiac light chain amyloidosis: results from a US administrative claims database.
articles.abstract: Aim: To gain insights into real-world mortality and hospitalization among newly diagnosed patients with light chain (AL) amyloidosis initiating anti-plasma cell dyscrasia treatment. Materials & methods: This retrospective, noninterventional, observational study evaluated real-world mortality by treatment patterns and hospitalization among adult patients newly diagnosed with AL amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy in the US IQVIA PharMetrics claims database. Data from treatment initiation (index date) to 365 days postindex were evaluated. Patients receiving treatments for AL amyloidosis in the year prior to the index date were excluded. AL-, cardiac-, and cardiac/renal-related healthcare resource utilization were assigned using the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision. Summary statistics are reported by cardiac or cardiac/renal involvement. Results: A total of 198 patients with cardiac AL amyloidosis were included in this study (mean age, 64.8 years; 70.7% male). The 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates among all patients were 9.1% (18 of 198) and 65.7% (130 of 198), respectively. Daratumumab was prescribed for 138 (69.7%) patients, with 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates of 7.2% (10 of 138) and 67.4% (93 of 138), respectively. Daratumumab was not prescribed for 60 (30.3%) patients, with 1-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates of 13.3% (8 of 60) and 61.7% (37 of 60), respectively. One-year mortality and condition-related hospitalization rates among patients with only cardiac involvement (n = 66) were 7.6% (5 of 66) and 45.5% (30 of 66), respectively, and 9.8% (13 of 132) and 75.8% (100 of 132), respectively, among patients with cardiac and renal involvement (n = 132). Conclusion: Treatment patterns varied considerably among patients with AL amyloidosis. Mortality and hospitalizations were higher among patients with both cardiac and renal involvement than among those with only cardiac involvement.

articles.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Outcomes of Smartphone-Based Remote Patient Monitoring in Patients With Solid Tumors: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remote patient monitoring (RPM) using mobile apps and wearable devices may support symptom reporting and communication between patients with cancer and health care professionals. However, evidence regarding sustained engagement, wearable-data completeness, and preliminary clinical outcomes in routine oncology practice remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: This pilot randomized controlled trial aimed to assess the feasibility of implementing a smartphone-based RPM system integrated with a wearable device among patients with solid tumors and to generate preliminary estimates of between-group differences in quality of life, emergency department (ED) use, and side-effect literacy over 6 months.

METHODS: Thirty patients from a single outpatient oncology clinic were randomized 1:1 to receive either the WellHealth RPM intervention plus standard care or standard care alone. The intervention included smartphone-based symptom reporting, medication recording, wearable-device monitoring, and provider-facing alerts. Feasibility outcomes included participant retention, symptom-reporting engagement, wearable-data completeness, and alert generation. The principal exploratory clinical outcome was quality of life measured using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-General (FACT-G) at baseline and at 1, 3, and 6 months. Secondary exploratory outcomes included cancer- or treatment-related ED visits and side-effect literacy.

RESULTS: Twenty-six of 30 participants (86.7%) completed the 6-month follow-up. All 15 intervention participants generated symptom-monitoring data, although only 6 (40%) continued symptom recording at week 26. Wearable-device integration was substantially less complete: 8 of 15 intervention participants had any successfully synchronized wearable data, 7 never successfully synchronized their device, and wearable data were available for only 27.2% (n=2715) of expected participant-days. The provider system generated 56 alerts. At 6 months, the mean total FACT-G score was numerically higher in the intervention group than in the control group (84.23, SD 12.13 vs 77.15, SD 14.00; Hodges-Lehmann estimate 6.50, 95% CI -0.83 to 16.50; P=.07), but no FACT-G total or subscale comparison remained statistically significant after Holm adjustment for multiple comparisons. Cancer- or treatment-related ED visits occurred in 0 of 13 intervention participants and 3 of 13 control participants (P=.22). Side-effect literacy did not differ significantly between groups at 3 months (P=.46).

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study supports the feasibility of initial smartphone-based symptom reporting among patients with solid tumors but provides less support for sustained engagement and reliable wearable-device integration. Exploratory clinical outcomes did not provide confirmatory evidence of effectiveness. Future studies should improve wearable synchronization, incorporate strategies to sustain patient engagement, standardize clinical alert-response pathways, and evaluate the intervention in a larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trial.

articles.title: Bacteria-responsive programmed antibacterial liposome to modulate the inflammatory microenvironment for intracranial methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections.
articles.abstract: For intracranial methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections, conventional antibiotics exhibit poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability and limited anti-inflammatory activity. To address these challenges, we developed a precisely targeted liposomal system, QAI-lipo, which combines passive BBB accumulation, potent antibiotic-free antibacterial activity, favorable biosafety, and effective modulation of inflammation. Benefiting from lipophilic properties resembling those of cell membranes, QAI-lipo can efficiently cross the BBB. Upon reaching intracranial infection foci, the liposomes are triggered to rupture and release encapsulated payloads by α-toxin secreted by MRSA. Meanwhile, QAI-lipo achieves robust antibacterial effects via dual mechanisms: direct disruption of bacterial membranes and photodynamic action. Animal experiments further verify that QAI-lipo exerts anti-inflammatory activity by inhibiting the MyD88/TRAF-6 signaling pathway, which downregulates the expression of downstream proinflammatory cytokines and upregulates that of anti-inflammatory factors. Moreover, QAI-lipo attenuates the activation of inflammatory cells (including microglia and astrocytes) and suppresses proinflammatory microglial polarization, ultimately improving the survival outcomes of infected animals. This platform offers a general strategy for central nervous system drug delivery and holds promise for broader therapeutic applications, such as the treatment of bacteremia and sepsis.

articles.title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity.

METHODS: A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes.

RESULTS: A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons.

CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits.

articles.title: Long working hours and cardiometabolic multimorbidity progression: a prospective multistate analysis in the UK Biobank.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: The association of long working hours with cardiometabolic disease accumulation remains unclear. Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) was defined as the coexistence of at least two of the following conditions: type 2 diabetes, ischaemic heart disease and stroke.

METHODS: We studied 269,197 employed UK Biobank participants free of cardiometabolic disease (CMD) at baseline. Weekly working hours were analysed in five categories, with 35-40 h/week as reference. Cox models assessed incident first CMD (FCMD), CMM and all-cause mortality. Multistate models assessed progression from no CMD to FCMD and from FCMD to CMM, with death possible from each state. Models were adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, occupational and family-history factors. Estimates were pooled across 50 multiply imputed datasets.

RESULTS: Within the disease observation window, 25,190 participants developed FCMD and 2,824 developed CMM. Working ≥55 h/week was associated with FCMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.057-1.180). Incident CMM from baseline was associated with 41-48 h/week (1.128, 1.010-1.260) and 49-54 h/week (1.205, 1.042-1.393); the estimate for ≥55 h/week was 1.144 (0.973-1.346). For FCMD-to-CMM progression, the corresponding HR were 1.141 (1.021-1.274), 1.129 (0.976-1.306) and 1.093 (0.929-1.286). Spline analyses supported overall associations with FCMD and incident CMM from baseline (both P<0.001), but not a clear association with FCMD-to-CMM progression (P=0.083).

CONCLUSION: Long working hours were associated with first CMD onset and incident CMM in some working-hour groups; FCMD-to-CMM progression showed no clear increasing gradient. These findings support considering working time in cardiometabolic risk assessment while distinguishing initial disease development from subsequent progression.

articles.title: Apparent membrane lung dysfunction during veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation following methylene blue administration: Case report.
articles.abstract: We report the case of a 72-year-old man who underwent cardiac surgery for Group B Streptococcus infective endocarditis with embolic hepatic abscesses. Severe postoperative vasoplegia was treated with repeated methylene blue boluses and infusions while on central veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-A ECMO) for refractory cardiogenic and vasoplegic shock. Following multiple methylene blue administrations, the ECMO return tubing appeared dark, raising concern for membrane lung dysfunction (MLD). However, post-membrane lung blood gases confirmed adequate oxygen exchange and visual inspection on the post-membrane lung side of the circuit revealed bright red blood within the membrane lung (ML) and all rigid connectors. The discoloration was determined to have resulted from methylene blue staining of the flexible PVC tubing which mimicked the appearance of the post-ML flexible PVC tubing in a failed membrane lung despite the oxygenator functioning appropriately. Awareness of this artifact is critical to avoid unnecessary interventions; evaluation of post-ML blood gases and visual comparison with unstained ECMO circuit components can distinguish this benign finding from true MLD.

articles.title: Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation for bacterial infection: A multicentre cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AIMS: Hyperammonaemia is traditionally linked to overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE), but growing evidence suggests it also contributes to cirrhosis-associated immune dysfunction. We evaluated the association between plasma ammonia and bacterial infection and compared ammonia, the AMMON-OHE model and prognostic scores for predicting bacterial infection and other liver-related events in outpatients with cirrhosis.

APPROACH RESULTS: This is a multicentre, retrospective study in 1855 cirrhosis patients on prospectively followed cohorts from five European and one Singaporean centres. The primary endpoint was hospitalisation with bacterial infection. Within one year, 8% of European patients developed infection; these patients had higher ammonia (1.75 vs. 0.97 times ULN; p<0.001) and a sevenfold higher risk of liver-related death (37% vs. 5%; p<0.001). Ammonia remained associated with infection, each unit increase raising risk by 12-14%, and was selected by every variable-selection method. The 1.4 times ULN threshold identified patients at increased risk of infection and OHE (both p<0.001). Ammonia alone discriminated well for infection (C-index 0.725 in Europe, 0.877 in Singapore), and integration into the AMMON-OHE model improved prediction (C-index 0.805 in Europe), with good calibration and clinical utility comparable to Child-Pugh and greater than MELD. Both also predicted OHE (C-index up to 0.904), whereas performance was weaker for ascites and variceal bleeding.

CONCLUSION: Hyperammonaemia is associated with hospitalisation due to bacterial infection and predicts both infection and OHE. These findings support an ammonia-related vulnerability phenotype characterised by immune dysfunction and neurocognitive susceptibility, for which the AMMON-OHE model provides individualised risk stratification.

articles.title: Changes in Acute Stress Over the Course of a Picture Naming Treatment for People With Poststroke Aphasia: A Repeated-Measures Study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to explore the trajectory of perceived stress over the course of a restorative language treatment for anomia. The primary aims were to (a) estimate the change in presession perceived stress across baseline and treatment sessions in people with aphasia participating in restorative speech-language therapy and (b) estimate the change in perceived stress levels from pre- to posttreatment.

METHOD: A secondary analysis of 16 stroke survivors with chronic aphasia (> 6 months poststroke) was completed. Participants completed the Simple Aphasia Stress Scale before and after each of the 19 baseline and treatment sessions as part of cued picture naming treatment, resulting in 38 total administrations. Linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate the trajectory of perceived stress.

RESULTS: Average perceived stress before each treatment session significantly decreased over time (p = .007), suggesting that stress reduced as participants acclimated to the treatment protocol. The effect of session number on postsession perceived stress change was not significant across all sessions (p = .197), but the magnitude of average postsession perceived stress increase diminished over time (p = .006).

CONCLUSIONS: The present study presents the group-level trajectories of perceived stress across a picture-naming protocol for stroke survivors with aphasia. Average presession stress decreased over the course of treatment, suggesting acclimation to the picture naming treatment. Perceived stress was often higher after sessions than before, but the magnitude of this increase diminished over time. These findings lay the groundwork for future research examining how perceived stress interacts with treatment engagement and outcomes in aphasia rehabilitation.

SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL: https://doi.org/10.23641/asha.35030998.

articles.title: Masked hypertension in pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Masked hypertension, defined as normal office blood pressure with elevated out-of-office blood pressure, has increasingly been recognized as a clinically important hypertensive phenotype during pregnancy. Emerging evidence have suggested that masked hypertension is associated with increased risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes. Recent studies also have indicated that abnormal ambulatory blood pressure patterns, specifically nocturnal hypertension, may provide prognostic information beyond office blood pressure measurements alone. Major international guidelines increasingly acknowledge the role of home and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring during pregnancy, although recommendations and diagnostic thresholds remain heterogeneous. In addition, digital health technologies for remote monitoring of out-of-office blood pressure have expanded rapidly and may improve risk stratification. This review summarizes current evidence on masked hypertension in pregnancy, discusses existing knowledge gaps, and highlights priorities for future research and clinical implementation.

articles.title: Computed Tomography Scan Zone-of-Injury Modeling Predicts Need for Definitive Soft-Tissue Coverage and Complications in Open OTA 42A-C Tibial Shaft Fractures.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the ability of a CT-derived soft-tissue zone-of-injury (ZOI) model to predict the need for soft-tissue (ST) coverage in open 42A-C tibial shaft fractures and compare its discriminatory performance with the Gustilo-Anderson (GA) classification for fracture-related complications.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Urban, multi-site academic center, 2014-2024.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients with operatively treated open OTA 42A-C tibial shaft fractures, preoperative tibial CT imaging, and ≥6-month follow-up were included.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the need for ST coverage (skin-graft, dermal matrix, local flap, free flap, or amputation). Secondary outcomes included ST- and fracture-related complications. CT-derived ZOI measurements, demographics, and injury characteristics were entered into a multivariable regression with stepwise elimination to develop a CT-derived ST coverage model (CTzoi-STC), which was compared with GA classification and with a model without CT-derived data. Patients were further stratified by risk for secondary outcome comparisons.

RESULTS: 122 patients (40.5 years (range 18-72), 95 (77.9%) male, GA I: 19 (15.6%), II: 30 (24.6%), III: 73 (59.8%); III: 73 (59.8%), of which IIIA: 62 (84.9%), IIIB: 8 (11.0%), IIIC: 3 (4.1%)) met inclusion criteria, with 37 (30.3%) requiring ST coverage. The final CTzoi-STC model, which included longitudinal free air extent on CT scan, wound size, and wound location (tibial third), demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting ST coverage compared with GA classification (AUC 0.845 vs 0.731, p = 0.041). A model without CT-derived data (GA classification, wound size, and wound location) had an AUC of 0.829 (p = 0.654 vs CTzoi-STC). Free air extent remained independently associated with ST coverage after adjustment (OR 8.1, 95% CI 1.4-47.2, p = 0.021). Using the Youden-derived cutoff (0.278), 30 of 47 high-risk patients (63.8%) required ST coverage compared with 7 (9.3%) of low-risk patients. High-risk patients had higher rates of nonunion (40.4% vs 16.0%, p = 0.003), fracture-related infection (38.3% vs 17.3%, p = 0.010), and ST coverage failure (14.9% vs 0.0%, p < 0.001), with longer length-of-stay, more operations and readmissions (all p ≤ 0.006). GA-based stratification showed limited discrimination.

CONCLUSIONS: For open tibial shaft fractures, a CT-derived soft-tissue zone-of-injury model incorporating longitudinal free air extent, wound size, and wound location more accurately identified patients requiring soft-tissue coverage and those at risk for soft-tissue- and fracture-related complications than the Gustilo-Anderson classification. Free air extent on CT was an objective, independent predictor of soft-tissue coverage, although a model without CT-derived data had similar discrimination.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: III, Prognostic.

articles.title: Perioperative outcomes after total coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT): A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundTotal coronary revascularization via left anterior thoracotomy (TCRAT) is a sternum-sparing approach to multivessel coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Published evidence is predominantly observational. This review summarizes reported perioperative outcomes after TCRAT; its principal quantitative synthesis is single-arm and does not establish comparative effectiveness against conventional CABG.MethodsThis systematic review followed PRISMA 2020 guidance and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437661). PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception to May 1, 2026. Studies reporting perioperative or clinical outcomes in adults undergoing TCRAT were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and the JBI checklist for case series. Random-effects meta-analysis of proportions used the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation; continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation.ResultsSeven cohorts comprising a reported total of 1869 patients were included. The pooled in-hospital/short-term mortality estimate was 0.92% (95% CI, 0.28-1.83%; I2 = 48.8%), and the pooled stroke estimate was 0.76% (95% CI, 0.10-1.82%; I2 = 61.6%). Pooled incidences of postoperative atrial fibrillation and re-exploration were 11.53% and 3.44%, respectively; deep wound infection was uncommon (0.15%). Pooled mean cardiopulmonary bypass and aortic cross-clamp times were 146.17 and 78.05 minutes. Estimates for operative times and length of stay were highly heterogeneous. The exploratory diabetes-stratified analysis did not detect a statistically significant mortality difference (p = 0.8443).ConclusionThe available cohorts describe the perioperative outcomes reported after TCRAT in selected patients and centers. These single-arm pooled estimates should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence, superiority, or non-inferiority compared with conventional CABG. Larger, well-adjusted comparative studies with standardized outcomes and long-term follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Management of hypertension in older persons: what do the 2023/2024 European Society of Hypertension, 2024 European Society of Cardiology and 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guidelines tell us?
authors: ESH Working Group on Hypertension in the Older Persons
articles.abstract: Treatment of hypertension in older people is associated with significant health-related benefits. However, at very old age, in patients with frailty, multimorbidity, and polypharmacy, the benefits of treatment must be balanced against the potential for harm from adverse events. The evidence for treatment in such populations is limited because they typically have not been included in many clinical trials. In this article, we discuss the differences in the approach to management of hypertension in older patients between the three recent clinical guidelines: the European Society of Hypertension (2023-2024), European Society of Cardiology (2024) and the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology (2025) guidelines. We conclude that the therapeutic approach to older persons should be personalized and should include a comprehensive evaluation of functionality and frailty. Balancing potential health-related benefits and harms should be the basis of all clinical decisions in this population, especially for individuals eluding simplistic classifications.

articles.title: Assessing the Evidence Base for the Association of Perioperative Registered Nurses Guideline for Sterile Technique.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sterile technique guidelines shape operating room practice, resource utilization, and surgical site infection (SSI) prevention. However, whether recommendations are supported by studies demonstrating clinically meaningful infection outcomes rather than surrogate contamination remains unclear. We evaluated the clinical relevance of evidence cited by the 2025 Association of periOperative Registered Nurses (AORN) Guideline for Sterile Technique.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a methodological review of references cited in Chapters 1-7 of the 2025 AORN guideline. Primary studies were classified by study design and measured outcomes. The primary endpoint was the proportion directly evaluating postoperative SSI. Secondary endpoints included surrogate contamination outcomes, statistically significant SSI findings, and potential conflicts of interest. Findings were summarized using frequencies and proportions.

RESULTS: Among 268 cited references, 188 were primary studies. Only 38 (20.2%) evaluated postoperative SSI, whereas 106 (56.4%) assessed surrogate contamination and 57 (30.3%) evaluated other nonclinical outcomes; categories were not mutually exclusive. Among SSI-measuring studies, 23 (60.5%) reported at least one statistically significant infection-related difference. Only one randomized clinical trial demonstrated a statistically significant SSI reduction attributable to a sterile technique intervention. Potential conflicts of interest were disclosed in 30 primary studies (16.0%), including 17 with relationships plausibly relevant to the intervention or outcome evaluated.

CONCLUSIONS: Evidence cited to support the 2025 AORN sterile technique recommendations predominantly measures surrogate contamination rather than postoperative SSI. These findings identify a gap between the outcomes supporting widely adopted perioperative standards and the clinical infections those standards aim to prevent. Guideline interpretation should distinguish contamination reduction from demonstrated SSI prevention, while future research prioritizes patient-centered infection outcomes.

articles.title: The association of sildenafil and sexual function in women with pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with congenital heart disease: Subanalysis of the COHARD-PH registry.
articles.abstract: Globally, approximately 1% of live births are associated with congenital heart disease (CHD), representing the most common congenital abnormality. Roughly 10% of adult CHD patients suffer from pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), a condition that may progress to right heart failure and mortality if untreated. Sildenafil is frequently prescribed for PAH; however, its effects on sexual function in patients with CHD remain poorly studied. We performed an observational study employing a retrospective cohort design to evaluate clinical data from patients with CHD treated at Sardjito Hospital, Yogyakarta, between January 2019 and July 2025. Study participants were stratified into two groups, consisting of those receiving sildenafil therapy and those not treated with sildenafil. Eligible participants were required to have been sexually active within the preceding four weeks. Sexual function in both treatment groups was evaluated using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) questionnaire. As many as 78 subjects met the criteria and completed the FSFI questionnaire. Fifty-seven and 21 participants were assigned to the sildenafil-exposed group and to the non-exposed group, respectively. Among those receiving sildenafil, 35.1% (20 patients) experienced sexual dysfunction, while 64.9% (37 patients) had normal sexual function. Bivariate analysis revealed a significant relationship between sildenafil use and sexual dysfunction in the study subjects (p=0.033; 95% CI 0.12-0.94). Multivariate analysis revealed that sildenafil consumption was linked to a lower occurrence of sexual dysfunction (OR 0.13; p=0.005; 95% CI 0.03-0.53). To conclude, sildenafil therapy in women with PAH-CHD was associated with reduced likelihood of sexual dysfunction.

articles.title: Lactate-induced histone lactylation drives PRMT5-mediated Foxp3 symmetric dimethylation to promote Treg differentiation and sepsis immunopathology.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by persistent immune dysfunction but how metabolic alterations contribute to immunosuppression remains unclear. Here, we identify lactate as a regulator of regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation and show that Treg accumulation contributes to persistent organ injury during sepsis. In patients with sepsis, plasma lactate correlates with circulating Treg frequencies and disease severity. Lactate uptake through MCT1 increases H3K9 and H3K18 lactylation and Prmt5 transcription. Lactate also increases S-adenosylmethionine, supporting PRMT5-mediated symmetric dimethylation of Foxp3 at R51 and R146, which stabilizes Foxp3 and promotes Treg differentiation and suppressive function. CD4+ T cell-specific Prmt5 deletion attenuates lactate-induced Treg responses and improves outcomes in septic mice. Dexmedetomidine binds the PRMT5/MEP50 complex, reduces Treg accumulation and organ injury, and improves host defense against secondary infection. These findings link lactate metabolism to PRMT5-dependent Foxp3 stabilization and suggest a potential therapeutic pathway for sepsis-associated immunosuppression.

articles.title: Explainable Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Identifying Compensatory Motor Behavior in Stroke Rehabilitation.
articles.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
articles.abstract: The occurrence of compensatory motor behaviors is common after stroke and other movement disorders, and can hinder patient rehabilitation. Detection of such behaviors is essential but traditionally relies on subjective, labor-intensive manual assessment. While supervised learning has been explored for automation, its effectiveness is constrained by inter-individual variability in compensatory strategies and the difficulty of obtaining detailed labels. To address these challenges, we present an unsupervised anomaly detection framework that models healthy motion distributions using Probabilistic Movement Primitives and quantifies deviations to detect potential compensations. The transparent structure of the proposed framework enables localization of compensation sources and differentiation between compensating and inhibited degrees of freedom, thereby enhancing its explainability and providing deeper insight into its outcomes. The framework was validated on a reaching-motion dataset, and achieved high accuracy in detecting compensation among stroke patients (F1 = 0.95). Trials from the evaluation dataset were further annotated with one or more compensation sources by multiple raters, yielding a rich dataset with quantifiable label uncertainties. Evaluation indicated that the framework achieved high performance in isolating compensation sources, particularly when annotator agreement is high.

articles.title: One-Step Rectified Flow Reconstruction with Spectral Weighting for Limited-angle Cardiac CT.
articles.abstract: Limited-angle cardiac computed tomography (CT) suffers from severe directional artifacts and resolution degradation due to missing wedges in the frequency domain. Diffusion-based reconstruction methods have demonstrated strong artifact suppression capabilities but typically require iterative sampling at a high computational cost. To accelerate limited-angle CT reconstruction, we propose a rectified-flow framework trained with paired supervision for fast inference. Instead of generating images from Gaussian noise, the model learns a deterministic transport from artifact-contaminated Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions to full-view reference images. A 2.5D slice-context modeling strategy is introduced to exploit inter-slice information while reconstructing only the central slice, improving structural consistency. Furthermore, we introduce a reconstruction-aware spectral loss that applies frequency-domain supervision to an approximate endpoint reconstruction inferred from the predicted flow velocity. By embedding spectral priors into the learning objective and using one-step rectified-flow inference (a single network evaluation), the proposed framework achieves fast reconstruction while preserving image fidelity. Experiments on XCAT simulations and clinical cardiac CT data show superior quantitative performance and substantially reduced inference time compared to the state-of-the-art baselines. A qualitative review by an experienced cardiac radiologist further suggests improved visualization of motion-sensitive coronary structures with reduced motion blur.

articles.title: Extreme Heat Exposure and Clinical Outcomes in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients.
articles.abstract: Background Climate change has led to a progressive increase in global temperatures, making extreme heat exposure an emerging environmental risk to human health. The kidney is particularly vulnerable to heat stress due to its dependence on adequate perfusion and fluid balance. Increasing evidence suggests that heat exposure is associated with adverse kidney outcomes, especially in high-risk populations. However, heat-related adverse clinical outcomes in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients remain unclear. This review aims to summarize the current evidence on the impact of extreme heat on diverse outcomes in CKD patients. Summary Elevated ambient temperatures and heatwaves are associated with increased risks of acute kidney injury (AKI), long-term renal function decline, hospitalizations, and mortality. Repeated or subclinical kidney injury during heat exposure may contribute to cumulative renal damage over time. Mechanistically, heat stress promotes sweating and salt and water loss, which can lead to extracellular fluid volume depletion, reduced effective circulating volume, and impaired renal perfusion, thereby increasing susceptibility to ischemic injury and urolithiasis. In addition, activation of inflammatory, oxidative stress pathways and mitochondrial dysfunction, further exacerbates kidney damage. Beyond kidney-specific effects, heat exposure is also associated with increased cardiovascular risk and overall mortality in CKD patients. Integrated clinical and public health strategies should be needed to reduce extreme heat related adverse outcome. Key Messages • Heat-related kidney damage involves both hemodynamic and inflammatory mechanisms. • Extreme heat is associated with acute eGFR decline, progression toward ESKD, dysnatremia, hospitalization and mortality in CKD patients. • Prevention requires individualized rather than fixed fluid targets, proactive medication review, and locally adapted public health measures.

articles.title: A Personalized Exercise Assistant Using Reinforcement Learning: Results From a Large-Scale Mobile Health Randomized-Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Consistent physical inactivity among adults and adolescents poses a major global health challenge. Mobile health (mHealth) interventions, particularly just-in-time adaptive interventions (JITAIs), offer a promising avenue for scalable and personalized physical activity promotion. However, developing and evaluating such adaptive interventions at scale, while integrating robust behavioral science, presents methodological hurdles.

OBJECTIVE: The Personalized Exercise Assistant Using Reinforcement Learning (PEARL) study aimed to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm, informed by health behavior change theory (capability, opportunity, and motivation-behavior [COM-B]), to personalize the content and timing of physical activity nudges via the Fitbit app (Google LLC) compared to fixed and random nudging strategies, and to a control group with no nudges.

METHODS: We conducted a large-scale, 4-arm randomized controlled trial (RCT) enrolling 13,463 Fitbit users. Participants were randomized to: (1) control (no nudges), (2) random (random content/timing), (3) fixed (logic based on baseline COM-B survey), and (4) RL (adaptive algorithm). The primary outcome was the change in average daily step count from baseline to 2 months. Secondary outcomes included user engagement and survey responses regarding capability, opportunity, and motivation.

RESULTS: A total of 7711 participants were included in the primary analysis (mean age 42.1, SD 9.0 years; 6657/7711, 86.3% female). At 1 month, the RL group showed a significant increase in daily steps compared to control (+296 steps; P<.001), random (+218 steps; P=.005), and fixed (+238 steps; P=.002) groups. For the prespecified primary analyses at 2 months, the RL group sustained a significant increase against the control (+210 steps; P=.01), but pairwise differences comparing the RL group against the random and fixed groups were not statistically significant. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) models confirmed a sustained significant increase in the RL group (+208 steps; P=.002). In exit surveys, the RL group reported higher favorable responses regarding nudge customization (224 of 605, 37%) compared to other groups.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility and early efficacy of using RL to personalize digital health nudges at scale. To our knowledge, this represents one of the largest, nonincentivized randomized trials of this duration to evaluate RL for physical activity. While the magnitude of the observed step increase is modest, a sustained daily improvement of 200-300 steps can contribute to broader public health goals by reducing sedentary behavior in large populations. The adaptive approach outperformed static behavioral rules, showcasing the promise of dynamic personalization in a real-world mHealth setting. Notably, participants receiving nudges based on fixed, theory-informed rules did not show a significant advantage over the random group, underscoring the challenge of using static baseline assessments to address nonstationary, day-to-day behavioral contexts. However, several limitations warrant consideration: the findings are specific to a 2-month follow-up, the study population was predominantly female (6657/7711, 86.3%) self-selected Fitbit users, and the observed step gains were modest in magnitude.

articles.title: Gelatin-Coated High-Strength Commercial Sutures Show Antibiotic Elution With Distinct Release Kinetics: An In Vitro Study.
articles.journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop a reproducible technique for coating high-strength sutures with doxycycline or vancomycin and to compare the antibiotic elution profiles of round and tape-style sutures over time in an in vitro model.

METHODS: In this in vitro study, 2 round (No. 2 FiberWire [PE-R, polyethylene-core round], No. 2 ActivBraid [COL-R, collagen-integrated round]) and 2 tape-style (1.5 mm LabralTape [PE-T, polyethylene-core tape], 1.5 mm ActivBraid [COL-T, collagen-integrated tape]) sutures were dip-coated in gelatin solutions containing low (C1) or high (C2) doxycycline or vancomycin concentrations. After drying, 1-cm segments were incubated at 37°C, and daily aliquots were collected over 7 days. Antibiotic release was quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

RESULTS: Total doxycycline and vancomycin elution ranged from 83.6 to 151.8 ng and 261.3 to 319.1 ng, respectively. Doxycycline showed first-order-like elution, with the greatest occurring during days 1 to 3. In contrast, vancomycin showed near-constant elution with minor fluctuations over time. At individual timepoints, COL-T (C1D) released more doxycycline than COL-R on days 2 and 3, whereas COL-T released more than COL-R on day 5 in C2D. COL-R (C1V, C2V) released more vancomycin than PE-R on day 5. Conversely, COL-R (C2D) released less doxycycline than PE-R on day 6. Intergroup comparisons showed that PE-T released more vancomycin in C2V versus C1V on day 3, and PE-R released more vancomycin in C1V versus C2V on day 5 and more doxycycline in C1D versus C2D on day 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Coating commercial high-strength sutures with either doxycycline or vancomycin using a gelatin-based dip-coat produced measurable, but low-level, antibiotic elution over 7 days in this in vitro model. Doxycycline exhibited a release profile consistent with first-order kinetics characterized by a higher initial burst followed by tapering elution, whereas vancomycin showed a more sustained release pattern consistent with near zero-order kinetics. Among the coated constructs, COL-T sutures exhibited the greatest doxycycline elution, whereas COL-R sutures exhibited the greatest vancomycin elution relative to PE-R sutures.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Antimicrobial coating of high-strength orthopaedic sutures enables sustained local antibiotic elution and may provide a potential strategy for reducing the early postoperative infection risk in tendon and ligament repairs.

articles.title: Behavior Change Techniques Associated With Abstinence in a Chat-Based Smoking Cessation Intervention: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial Using Machine Learning.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolating the candidate intervention components that drive the success of digital behavioral interventions is crucial for understanding intervention mechanisms and optimizing future interventions.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify behavior change techniques (BCTs) delivered in a chat-based smoking cessation intervention and determine their independent associations with biochemically validated abstinence.

METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of a pragmatic, cluster-randomized clinical trial conducted in Hong Kong. From June 18 to September 30, 2017, 624 adult daily smokers were recruited from 34 community sites and randomized to the intervention group. Participants received 3 months of personalized, real-time chat-based cessation support delivered by a live counselor via a mobile instant messaging app. The analytic sample included 230 participants (n=170, 73.9% male; mean age 43.0, SD 13.6 years) who engaged with the chat support. All chat dialogues during the real-time support were retrieved and systematically coded using an established BCT taxonomy for smoking cessation (BCTTsm). Four machine learning methods, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination, were used to identify the BCTs that are most predictive of biochemically validated tobacco abstinence outcomes at 3 and 6 months. A prespecified supermajority rule retained only BCTs selected by at least 3 of the 4 models for subsequent analysis. The stability of the selected BCTs was assessed using 500 bootstrap resamples for each model. Poisson regression with robust variance was subsequently used to examine the independent associations between the selected BCTs and abstinence outcomes. Covariates included sex, age, educational level, nicotine dependence, intention to quit in 30 days, and quit attempts at baseline.

RESULTS: Systematic coding identified 35 distinct BCTs from the BCTTsm as having been delivered. Three BCTs were consistently selected by machine learning as the most predictive of both 3- and 6-month abstinence, with moderate to high stability (ranging from 61% to 100%): "provide rewards contingent on successfully stopping smoking" (BM4), "provide information on withdrawal symptoms" (RC6), and "provide information on consequences of smoking and smoking cessation" (BM1). In multivariable analyses, 6-month abstinence was significantly associated with BM4 (risk ratio [RR] 7.9, 95% CI 4.2-14.6), RC6 (RR 3.3, 95% CI 1.6-6.5), and BM1 (RR 2.7, 95% CI 1.4-5.5), with consistent results for 3-month abstinence.

CONCLUSIONS: Three BCTs, contingent rewards (BM4), information on withdrawal symptoms (RC6), and information on consequences (BM1), were identified as candidate intervention components associated with success in a chat-based smoking cessation intervention. This study is the first to apply machine learning for BCT identification, moving beyond simple frequency counts to data-driven feature selection. These findings provide empirical evidence for the candidate components of effective digital behavioral intervention that may warrant further testing and offer guidance for future intervention optimization.

articles.title: Food-derived bioactive peptides with hypoglycemic and antidepressant effects: sources, structure-activity relationships, comorbidity mechanisms, and applications.
articles.abstract: Diabetes and depression exhibit a high rate of comorbidity worldwide, yet traditional drug treatments are often associated with side effects, poor compliance, and limited effectiveness in addressing both conditions simultaneously. Bioactive peptides have emerged as a promising strategy for managing metabolic and emotional disorders due to their high specificity, low toxicity, and multitarget regulatory potential. This review systematically examines the sources, structure-activity relationships, shared mechanisms of action, and potential applications of bioactive peptides with hypoglycemic and antidepressant effects. Hypoglycemic peptides primarily regulate blood glucose by inhibiting enzymes such as α-glucosidase and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-IV), whereas antidepressant peptides improve mood by modulating neurotransmitters, neuroplasticity, and anti-inflammatory pathways. These peptides share notable similarities in amino acid composition (e.g., Pro-rich and aromatic-rich motifs), secondary structural motifs (e.g., β-sheet and β-turn conformations), and cyclic architecture, as supported by recent dual-target peptide studies, and converge multiple signaling pathways, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), brain-derived neurotrophic factor/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (BDNF/TrkB), hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt), and inflammatory pathways, highlighting their potential for multitarget intervention in metabolic-emotional comorbidities. The review further explores the prospects and challenges of applying these peptides in functional foods, drug delivery systems, and personalized nutrition interventions, emphasizing the need for in-depth research on target complexity, delivery system optimization, and clinical translation to advance the practical application of multifunctional peptides in treating comorbid metabolic and emotional disorders.

articles.title: Questionnaire-based nociplastic-like and neuropathic-like pain profiles in rheumatoid arthritis: a multicenter cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pain in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is traditionally interpreted as a consequence of inflammatory and structural mechanisms; however, neuropathic-like and nociplastic-like features may contribute to persistent symptoms and clinical heterogeneity. This study aimed to describe the distribution of questionnaire-based pain profiles and to characterize their clinical and symptomatic burden in patients with RA.

METHOD: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted in rheumatology outpatients from two university hospitals in Spain. Patients with RA and chronic pain (> 3 months) were included. Four mutually exclusive profiles were defined using the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI ≥ 40) and PainDETECT (≥ 19): nociceptive-predominant (both negative), nociplastic-like (CSI only), neuropathic-like (PainDETECT only) and mixed (both positive). Clinical variables included general pain, foot pain, Brief Pain Inventory severity and interference, Widespread Pain Index, and Symptom Severity Scale. Between-group comparisons used Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn-Bonferroni tests.

RESULTS: Of 111 patients analyzed, the nociceptive-predominant profile was the most frequent (43.2%; 95% CI 34.4-52.5), followed by mixed (31.5%; 23.6-40.7), nociplastic-like (17.1%; 11.2-25.2) and neuropathic-like (8.1%; 4.3-14.7) profiles. Overall, 56.8% (47.5-65.6) of patients showed neuropathic-like and/or nociplastic-like features. All pain and symptom variables differed between profiles (p < 0.001; ε2 0.23-0.44), mainly mixed versus nociceptive-predominant. The mixed profile showed the highest clinical and symptomatic burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Questionnaire-based pain profiling identified substantial heterogeneity in chronic pain among patients with RA. These screening-based profiles, not assessed against inflammatory disease activity, support a multidimensional assessment of pain in RA but do not establish distinct pain mechanisms. Key Points • More than half of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and chronic pain screened positive for neuropathic-like and/or nociplastic-like features on self-report questionnaires. • The mixed profile was associated with the highest burden of pain intensity, pain interference, widespread pain, associated symptoms, and foot pain. • Questionnaire-based pain profiling may help identify patients who could benefit from a multidimensional pain assessment, although its relationship with inflammatory disease activity remains to be established.

articles.title: Association of atrial fibrillation with mortality across quantitatively assessed tricuspid regurgitation severity.
articles.abstract:
