BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently coexists with tricuspid regurgitation (TR), but whether its association with mortality differs across quantitatively defined TR categories remains uncertain.

METHODS: In this prospective referral-based cohort, 397 consecutive patients with at least mild holosystolic TR underwent standardized quantitative echocardiographic assessment, including PISA-derived effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) and regurgitant volume. The primary analytic cohort comprised 391 patients with complete baseline AF status and EROA-defined TR classification. Patients were categorized as having mild-to-moderate TR when EROA was <0.40 cm2 and severe TR when EROA was ≥0.40 cm2. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: AF was present in 220 of 391 patients (56.3%) and was more frequent in the severe than in the mild-to-moderate TR category (63.4% vs. 52.5%; P=0.039). During a median follow-up of 1.18 years, 157 deaths occurred. In the clinical-plus-echocardiographic Cox model, AF was not independently associated with mortality (adjusted HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.64-1.38; P=0.757). A significant categorical AF-by-severe-TR interaction was observed in the fully adjusted model (interaction HR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.17-5.33; P=0.018), although the stratum-specific AF estimates were not individually statistically significant. In a sensitivity analysis using continuous EROA, the AF-by-EROA interaction was not significant (interaction HR per 0.10-cm2 increase, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.95-1.15; P=0.389).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline AF was common in this quantitatively characterized TR cohort. The categorical interaction analysis suggested possible heterogeneity in the association between AF and mortality according to EROA-defined TR category; however, this finding was not supported by the continuous EROA analysis and should be considered exploratory. These observational findings do not establish treatment indications or the benefit of AF- or TR-directed intervention.

articles.title: Sustainability Strategies and Practices in the Management of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects over 850 million people worldwide and is projected to become a leading cause of death by 2040. Kidney care is resource-intensive, contributing to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water and energy consumption, and healthcare costs. Addressing sustainability in CKD management is critical for aligning kidney health delivery systems with global climate and health goals. A multidisciplinary narrative review was undertaken to qualitatively synthesize literature on CKD management, integrating clinical nephrology, environmental sustainability, and planetary-health perspectives. Studies examining dialysis, kidney transplantation (KT), and preventive kidney management (PKM) were analyzed through the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework, encompassing environmental, economic, and social dimensions. Dialysis, though life-sustaining for people with CKD G4-G5, is the least sustainable option due to its high ecological footprint and cost. KT often provides superior survival and long-term cost-effectiveness but faces barriers such as donor availability, inequitable access, and procedural and pharmaceutical emissions. PKM, including early detection, lifestyle improvements, appropriate virtual care, and optimized pharmacologic management, is important for slowing disease progression and may reduce the need for resource-intensive kidney replacement therapy (KRT). Although the environmental and economic effects of PKM have not been consistently quantified, avoiding or delaying progression to advanced CKD may reduce healthcare resource use, costs, and environmental impacts. Findings support a coordinated, value-based model of kidney care that aligns preventive, interventional, and supportive practices, while recognizing gaps in environmental and economic evidence. Embedding sustainability into CKD care will necessitate technological innovation, policy reform, and equitable access. Future collaborative research should employ long-term life-cycle assessments to guide sustainable, patient-centered kidney care. It should account for variability in CKD pathways and balance effectiveness, sustainability, and equitable access worldwide.

articles.title: Economic and Humanistic Burden of Cardiovascular Comorbidity in Kidney Failure: Findings from a Systematic Literature Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its impact on economic and humanistic burden remains insufficiently characterized. We aimed to systematically review the published literature reporting economic outcomes, healthcare resource utilization (HRU), and humanistic impact of the association between advanced CKD and CVD.

METHODS: A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted using MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, and conference abstracts to identify evidence published between 2020 and December 31, 2025. Studies reporting economic or humanistic burden outcomes among adults with CKD G4-G5 or kidney failure and coexisting cardiovascular conditions were included.

RESULTS: In total, 6350 records were screened, with 87 studies meeting inclusion criteria. Across studies, coexisting CVD markedly increased costs and HRU in advanced CKD. In the USA, the costs per event ranged from $12,410 USD for systolic heart failure to $92,898 for chronic heart failure. Compared to CKD G4, patients in G5 incurred higher annual per patient hospitalization costs (77%), outpatient costs (65%), and total healthcare costs (61% (US) to 64% (non-US)). Emergency visits, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and rehospitalizations were more frequent among patients with coexisting CVD and advanced CKD compared to those without CVD, with 30-day readmission rates of 41% for critical limb ischemia. Evidence on humanistic burden, though limited, showed significant declines in mental health and quality of life among patients with CVD.

CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant CVD and advanced CKD or kidney failure substantially elevates the economic and humanistic burden compared to CVD or CKD alone, driving higher costs, increased healthcare utilization, and impaired quality of life. Targeted strategies addressing cardiovascular risk in patients with advanced CKD are essential to mitigate downstream clinical and financial consequences.

articles.title: Synthesized V8-V9 ST-segment elevation and clinical characteristics in patients with inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Posterior involvement in inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is associated with greater myocardial injury and adverse outcomes. However, posterior leads are not routinely recorded because they require additional electrode placement. A synthesized 18-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) derives posterior leads from a standard 12-lead ECG without additional electrode placement. We investigated the clinical significance of synthesized V8-V9 ST-segment elevation in inferior STEMI. We retrospectively evaluated 209 patients with inferior STEMI who underwent successful emergency percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) between January 2016 and December 2025. Patients were classified according to the presence of ST-segment elevation ≥ 0.1 mV in both synthesized V8 and V9 leads. The primary endpoint was peak serum creatine kinase (CK), which was log-transformed for multivariable analysis. Secondary endpoints included echocardiographic parameters and in-hospital clinical outcomes. Among 209 patients, 100 (47.8%) had synthesized V8-V9 ST-segment elevation and 109 (52.2%) did not. Peak CK was significantly higher in patients with V8-V9 ST-segment elevation than in those without (2925 [1341-4052] vs. 1384 [762-2443] U/L, P < 0.001). Chronic-phase E/e' was also significantly higher in the V8-V9 ST-segment elevation group (12.6 ± 4.9 vs. 10.6 ± 4.0, P = 0.01). Ischemic ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation (VT/VF) (13.0% vs. 3.7%, P = 0.01) and cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support (20.0% vs. 9.2%, P = 0.04) were more frequent in patients with V8-V9 ST-segment elevation. In multivariable analysis, synthesized V8-V9 ST-segment elevation and age were independently associated with log-transformed peak CK. Synthesized V8-V9 ST-segment elevation was associated with greater myocardial injury and higher observed rates of ischemic VT/VF and cardiogenic shock requiring mechanical circulatory support. These clinical-outcome findings are exploratory, and further studies are needed to determine whether synthesized posterior leads provide incremental information beyond conventional ECG findings and clinical assessment.

articles.title: Modulating Growth Conditions and Microenvironment to Boost Antimicrobial Efficacy of Probiotics Against Pathogens.
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance and biofilm-associated infections highlights the need for alternative strategies to control pathogenic microorganisms. Probiotics have emerged as promising candidates due to their ability to inhibit pathogen growth. However, their potential ways of application in human medicine remain insufficiently understood. Here we investigate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity of selected probiotic strains, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Fibro 1 and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus Fibro 2, against clinically relevant pathogens, with the aim of generating insights to support the design of improved probiotic-based systems for wound infection treatment. Probiotics were investigated for their growth, lactic acid production, and biofilm formation in different media. A range of in vitro antimicrobial activity assays were employed, including growth inhibition and antibiofilm assays. In addition to free probiotics, probiotics incorporated into electrospun fiber mats via microchip electrospinning were investigated in in vitro biofilm models. Probiotics exhibit strain- and condition-dependent inhibitory effects, influencing both planktonic growth and biofilm development of pathogens, while metabolic analysis showed marked medium-dependent glucose utilization and lactate production. Probiotics incorporated into fiber mats retain measurable metabolic activity after encapsulation and preserve their antibiofilm activity. Overall, this study provides a deeper understanding of probiotic effects on pathogens and identifies key factors influencing antimicrobial efficacy. These findings support the rational design of enhanced probiotic-based formulations for applications in infection control and wound care.

articles.title: Self-advocacy in chronic kidney disease: health literacy, family, faith, and the dialysis team.
Wearable artificial kidney: potential for patient-centric approach to kidney replacement therapy.
articles.abstract: As the global burden of chronic kidney disease (CKD) increases, with many progressing towards end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), there is an urgent need to focus our attention towards kidney care. Kidney replacement therapy (KRT) is a form of life-sustaining intervention used in patients with kidney failure. Although kidney transplantation remains the most effective long-term treatment for this, a severe lack of donors has led to an increased dependence on dialysis modalities. Traditional dialysis modalities including hemodialysis (HD) and peritoneal dialysis (PD), despite being widely used, also carry significant drawbacks including high treatment burden, complication risks, and reduced patient quality of life. Wearable artificial kidneys (WAK) have the potential to emerge as a patient-friendly alternative, providing higher autonomy to CKD patients. Innovations in dialysate regeneration could enable the development of lightweight, resource-friendly and effective WAK designs. Despite ongoing research efforts, modern WAKs are still in their investigational phase. Major limitations in device miniaturization while maintaining effective functionality hinder their clinical translation. Constraints at both technological and regulatory levels need to be addressed with multidisciplinary collaborations and sustained research efforts. This review provides an update on recent innovations in WAK technologies, highlighting their future potential as a patient-centric kidney therapy.

articles.title: Adhesion and proliferation behavior of human fibroblast on porous Ti6Al4V topographies-impact of Voronoi density.
articles.journal: Journal of materials science. Materials in medicine
articles.abstract: The breach of the cutaneous barrier is considered an issue of transcutaneous osseointegrated prosthetic systems (TOPS). Three-dimensional-structured topographies are expected to allow for soft-tissue in-growth, leading to re-establishment of the cutaneous barrier functionality. Five specifications of Voronoi density (VD)-based manufactured, porous Ti6Al4V-topographies and controls were cultivated 42 days with adult human dermal fibroblasts. Adhesion and proliferation were evaluated by fluorescence imaging and scanning electron microscopy. Viability, metabolism, and cell count were determined using MTT, ALP and qMTT assays. Cell counts (pD0/D42 < 0.00001), viability (pD1/D42 < 0.00001), and vitality increased up to day 42 with VD-dependent progressions. High viability and cell counts at each measurement accompanied with homogeneous cell distribution to nearly complete matrix capture at later measurements occurred on VDs 1000 pp/cm3 and 1500 pp/cm3. VDs 2000 pp/cm3 and 3000 pp/cm3 in contrast showed predominantly a more enveloping type of matrix colonization. This study highlights the impact of Voronoi density on cellular capture modes of three-dimensional topographies. The image shows a graphical overview of Voronoi density-based three-dimensional implant surfaces for promoting soft-tissue in-growth in transcutaneous osseointegrated prosthetic systems (TOPS). Left-hand schematics illustrate disruption of the skin barrier by an implant extending into bone and the proposed in-growth of surrounding tissue into a porous implant surface to restore the cutaneous barrier function and reduce infection risk. The experimental workflow compares porous cubic structures and circular specimes with Voronoi densities of 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, and 3000 point per cubic centimeter, showing progressively finer pore networks with increasing density. Petri dishes with cells represent cultivation of specimens with human dermal fibroblasts for 42 days, with assessment time points marked at days 0, 1, 7, 28, and 42. Assessment methods include fluorescence imaging, scnanning electron microscopy, and assays of cell viability (MTT), metabolism (ALP), and cell count (qMTT). Result schematics depict cellular colonization of porous structures. Reported findings for Voronoi densities of 1000 and 1500 points per cubic centimeter include high cell counts and viability, homogeneous cell distribution, and nearly complete matrix capture. At Voronoi densities of 2000 and 3000 points per cubic centimeter, colonization predominantly envelops the matrix.

articles.title: Targeting Energy Metabolism and Tryptophan Pathways in Alzheimer's Disease for Developing Therapeutic Strategies.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the primary cause of dementia worldwide and carries a high socioeconomic burden. However, despite the fact that such pathological features as amyloid-beta plaques and neurofibrillary tangles are considered hallmark traits of AD, therapeutic approaches targeting these pathological features have shown limited clinical efficacy to date. Recent scientific discoveries have drawn attention to the importance of metabolic processes preceding neurodegeneration. Reduced glucose utilization and impaired oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) are associated with bioenergetic deficits that may increase neuronal vulnerability to damage. In addition, neuroinflammation is associated with altered tryptophan metabolism through the kynurenine pathway and may favor the production of potentially neurotoxic metabolites. Despite these separate aspects of AD, the interaction between impaired bioenergetics and altered tryptophan metabolism in the brain has not been sufficiently studied. This gap complicates the development of multi-targeted treatment strategies. The purpose of this narrative review is to examine how gut dysbiosis, immune activation, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) impairment, redox imbalance, and tryptophan-kynurenine pathway dysregulation interact and may contribute to AD development and progression, including associated neuropsychiatric symptoms. We examine whether NAD⁺ depletion and rerouting of tryptophan metabolism may act as key nodes linking mitochondrial respiratory failure with the generation of neurotoxic kynurenine metabolites, excitotoxic glutamatergic signaling, loss of neurotrophic support, and synaptic dysfunction, and to analyze existing and emerging therapeutic strategies that target these interconnected pathways. In addition, this review highlights potentially promising interventions, such as NAD⁺ precursor supplementation, central nervous system insulin delivery, and modification of gut microbiome. Here we propose that the energy-tryptophan metabolic axis is a promising but underexplored area of AD research. Targeting these convergent bioenergetic and metabolomic pathways may support precision intervention strategies that could extend beyond conventional amyloid-centric paradigms to address broader neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric syndromes.

articles.title: Stroke unit capacity and acute stroke care systems in Sub-Saharan Africa: progress, gaps, and implementation challenges.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), yet the infrastructure required for effective acute management remains severely limited across much of the region.

METHODS: This narrative review critically appraises the available evidence on stroke unit availability and acute stroke care capacity in sub-Saharan Africa, including data on reperfusion therapies, neuroimaging infrastructure, workforce capacity, and implementation studies from diverse SSA settings.

RESULTS: The literature reviewed demonstrates major deficits in dedicated stroke units, reperfusion therapies, neuroimaging infrastructure, and trained stroke specialists. Only a minority of SSA hospitals have functional stroke units, and intravenous thrombolysis rates remain extremely low in most settings. However, implementation studies from Guinea, South Africa, and Kenya demonstrate that organized stroke care is feasible and can improve outcomes even under substantial resource constraints. These findings challenge the assumption that evidence-based stroke care is inherently unsuitable for SSA health systems; rather, they point to failures in policy prioritization and structural underinvestment as the primary drivers of current deficits. Hemorrhagic stroke management, particularly structured intracerebral hemorrhage care bundles, represents a distinct and largely unaddressed gap in the SSA literature. The methodological limitations of the available evidence base are critically appraised throughout.

CONCLUSIONS: Coordinated investment in stroke infrastructure, workforce development, prehospital systems, and context-specific implementation strategies is urgently needed to address the growing stroke burden across sub-Saharan Africa.

articles.title: Serum-derived extracellular vesicle-associated miRNA profiling in Mycobacterium abscessus pulmonary disease: an exploratory proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: Differentiating Mycobacterium abscessus pulmonary infection from pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) continues to be an unmet medical need due to their similar clinical, radiographic and microscopic features which may lead to delayed diagnosis and suboptimal therapy. Serum-derived extracellular vesicle-associated miRNAs represent potential minimally invasive biomarkers that warrant investigation for their diagnostic utility in differentiating M. abscessus pulmonary disease from other respiratory infections. Herein, we conducted a proof-of-concept small RNA sequencing of serum exosome for developing serum exosomal miRNA diagnostic signature against M. abscessus pulmonary disease. We analyzed 12 participants with serum derived from: (1) M. abscessus pulmonary infection (n = 3); (2) pulmonary TB (n = 3); (3) pneumonia (n = 3); and (4) healthy controls (n = 3). Exosomes were isolated from serum, followed by sequencing small RNAs using the Illumina platform. Differential expression was identified using DESeq2; candidate biomarkers were selected based on fold changes, nominal p-values, and reproducibility in comparisons. A total of 854 known miRNAs and 1,730 previously unknown (putative novel) miRNA candidates were detected. Among the annotated miRNAs, hsa-miR-5584-5p demonstrated the largest observed fold change in the comparison between M. abscessus pulmonary disease and pulmonary TB ([Formula: see text] fold change [Formula: see text]; nominal [Formula: see text]); however, this association did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing (FDR [Formula: see text]). Among the computationally predicted putative novel small-RNA candidates, the sequence TTGAGGTCGGACATGGTGGCTC exhibited the largest observed fold change; however, its identity as a bona fide miRNA remains to be experimentally established. This exploratory proof-of-concept study provides preliminary insights into serum-derived extracellular vesicle-associated small RNA profiles in M. abscessus pulmonary disease and identifies candidate miRNAs that require independent validation using RT-qPCR in larger, well-characterized patient cohorts.

articles.title: Current trends in evaluation and management of superficial venous thrombosis (SVT).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Superficial venous thrombosis (SVT) is characterised by thrombus formation accompanied by inflammation within the superficial venous system, most commonly affecting the lower limbs. SVT is relatively common, with an estimated incidence of 0.3 to 0.6 per 1,000 person-years in younger individuals and 0.7 to 1.5 per 1,000 person-years in older populations. These rates are comparable to those observed in DVT, which occurs in approximately 1 per 1,000 individuals annually.

METHODS: We performed a narrative review of the existing literature to evaluate current evidence and identify gaps in knowledge.

RESULTS: According to current National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance, SVT can be categorised into low and high-risk groups. Low-risk SVT is defined by thrombus length less than 5 cm, below knee location, and the absence of significant thromboembolic risk factors. In contrast, high risk SVT includes thrombus greater than or equal to 5 cm in length, above-knee involvement, proximity within 3 cm of the saphenofemoral (SFJ) or sapheno-popliteal junction (SPJ), or the presence of risk factors. High-risk SVT is therefore considered analogous to DVT, requiring equivalent therapeutic anticoagulation and follow-up. Current SVT management Guidelines rely on risk stratification, but recommendations vary because the evidence base is limited. Key gaps remain, particularly for high-risk patients, including optimal treatment duration, management strategies, and recurrence prevention.

CONCLUSION: Future research should prioritise large-scale randomised controlled trials and real-world cohort studies to refine anticoagulant selection, optimise treatment duration, and support personalised risk prediction. Strengthening the evidence base will be essential to reducing practice variation and improving patient-centred outcomes in SVT management.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and outcomes of older adults who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery for symptomatic Rathke cleft cysts.
articles.abstract: Rathke cleft cysts (RCCs) are benign cystic lesions in the sellar and suprasellar regions that are often asymptomatic but may cause symptoms due to the compression of adjacent structures. With the aging of population, the incidence of symptomatic RCCs in older adults is increasing. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, surgical outcomes, and follow-up between older and younger adult patients systematically. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients aged ≥ 18 years who underwent endoscopic endonasal surgery (EES) for RCCs at a single center from 2011 to 2023. Patients were categorized into two groups: nonelderly (18-59 years) and elderly (≥ 60 years). A total of 153 patients were analyzed, with 120 younger and 33 older adult patients. Older adults presented more frequently with dizziness and fatigue. The elderly group had a shorter operation time, whereas the other surgical outcomes were similar between the two groups. The incidences of perioperative diabetes insipidus and mortality during follow-up were significantly higher in the elderly group. The recurrence rate was also higher, but no significant difference was observed. In multivariable Fine-Gray competing risk analysis, older age (adjusted SHR: 3.99, 95% CI: 1.45-11.00, p = 0.007) and cyst location, including both suprasellar (adjusted SHR: 12.70, 95% CI: 1.39-115.00, p = 0.024) and sellar-suprasellar extension (adjusted SHR: 8.67, 95% CI: 1.09-68.70, p = 0.041; vs. sellar), were associated with recurrence, whereas preoperative hypopituitarism was not (adjusted SHR: 2.20, 95% CI: 0.76-6.36, p = 0.200). EES is safe and effective for elderly patients with symptomatic RCCs. Elderly patients often present with atypical symptoms, leading to a delayed diagnosis. RCCs seem to be more likely to recur in older patients than in younger adults; thus, more careful monitoring and longer follow-up period is needed on the older adults.

articles.title: Effect of Adjunctive Topical Cyclosporine A on Ocular Surface Recovery after Pars Plana Vitrectomy: A Prospective Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ocular surface dysfunction is a common but underrecognized complication of vitreoretinal surgery. This study investigated whether adjunctive topical cyclosporine A (CsA) 0.05% improves postoperative ocular surface recovery compared with hyaluronic acid (HA) 0.15% alone in patients undergoing pars plana vitrectomy.

METHODS: In this prospective, examiner-masked, randomized controlled trial, 54 patients with dry eye disease undergoing 25-gauge pars plana vitrectomy were randomized 1:1 to receive topical HA 0.15% alone or HA 0.15% plus CsA 0.05%. Ocular surface parameters were assessed at baseline and postoperative day 1, week 1, month 1, and month 3. The primary outcome was the National Eye Institute (NEI) corneal staining score at postoperative month 3, analyzed by analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) adjusting for baseline score and combined phacovitrectomy status. Secondary outcomes included tear break-up time (TBUT), Schirmer I test, Oxford corneal staining score, tear matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) grade, conjunctival hyperemia grade, meiboscore, and Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) score.

RESULTS: A total of 50 patients (25 per group; 26 men and 24 women) completed the study. At postoperative month 3, the adjusted NEI corneal staining score was significantly lower in the HA 0.15% + CsA 0.05% group than in the HA 0.15% group (adjusted mean difference -2.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] -3.73 to -1.34; p < 0.001). A linear mixed-effects model confirmed a significant group-by-time interaction (p = 0.030). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed within-subgroup differences favoring HA 0.15% + CsA 0.05% in patients with longer operation time, diabetes mellitus, and no sclerotomy suturing. A significant treatment-by-operation time interaction was observed, but not for diabetes or sclerotomy suturing status. TBUT was transiently longer in the HA 0.15% + CsA 0.05% group at postoperative week 1 (p = 0.018); no other secondary outcomes differed significantly between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Adjunctive topical CsA 0.05% was associated with significantly greater improvement in NEI corneal staining score, an indicator of corneal epithelial integrity, at 3 months after vitrectomy, whereas most secondary outcomes, including patient-reported symptoms, did not differ between groups. These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting a potential role for adjunctive CsA in postoperative corneal epithelial recovery and warrant confirmation in larger trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service (CRIS) identifier, KCT0012351; registered 29 July 2026, retrospectively registered.

articles.title: Metabolic disease engineers the colorectal cancer ecosystem.
articles.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D) increase colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, yet the mechanisms linking systemic metabolic dysfunction to carcinogenesis are usually considered independently. I propose that metabolic disease can act as an ecosystem engineer, altering the selective conditions in which neoplastic cells emerge and evolve. Nutrient availability, adipose dysfunction, metabolic-epigenetic coupling, immunometabolic rewiring, microbial remodeling, and bile acid metabolism interact across the colonic environment, redistributing metabolic fitness among epithelial, immune, and microbial populations. These interactions may establish a self-reinforcing ecosystem that favors metabolically adaptable clones and reduces constraints on their persistence. Metabolic dysfunction may thus alter which cellular populations can most effectively exploit available resources and evade antitumor surveillance. This hypothesis predicts that tumors with similar molecular characteristics may exist within biologically distinct environments according to the host metabolic state, and therefore could show differential responses to immune activity and therapy. Integrating systemic metabolic parameters, including adiposity distribution, insulin resistance, glycemic control, circulating metabolites, and microbial features, with molecular tumor classification could reveal distinct CRC ecological states and host-tumor dependencies. Such metabolic stratification could generate opportunities for personalized prevention and therapy by identifying vulnerabilities that remain obscured by current tumor-centric classification.

articles.title: Ivabradine Versus Digitalis Glycosides in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Comparative Appraisal of Two Additional Medical Therapies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Resting heart rate predicts outcome in heart failure (HF) with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but lowering it benefits only hemodynamically stable patients. This narrative review compares ivabradine and the digitalis glycosides, the only additional medical therapies in the 2026 ESC guidelines that slow the heart rate, as add-ons to foundational medical therapy (FMT).

METHODS: We searched PubMed and the Cochrane Library through August 2026 and current guidelines, giving greatest weight to large randomized trials and contemporary meta-analyses.

RESULTS: Ivabradine reduced cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.75-0.90) without a mortality benefit; it is restricted to sinus rhythm with LVEF ≤ 35% and heart rate ≥ 70 bpm (Class IIa B1). The digitalis glycosides act in any rhythm, with LVEF ≤ 40% (Class IIa B1), and reduce worsening-heart-failure events (pooled HR 0.75, n = 9,013) without affecting mortality, within narrow, agent-specific therapeutic windows (digoxin 0.5-0.9 ng/mL; digitoxin 8-18 ng/mL). DIGIT-HF (digitoxin) was positive and DECISION (digoxin) neutral; their estimates are similar in direction and magnitude, but differences in drug, population and endpoint preclude calling them concordant. Digoxin withdrawal is associated with deterioration, although contemporary data rest on few events.

CONCLUSION: Ivabradine and the digitalis glycosides are not symmetric alternatives. Ivabradine is a narrow add-on for sinus-rhythm patients who remain tachycardic despite beta-blockade; the glycosides serve both ventricular rate control in atrial fibrillation and prevention of worsening HF irrespective of rhythm. Both reduce morbidity rather than mortality and belong only after FMT is optimized. No randomized trial has compared them directly.

articles.title: Miracle and/or Minefield? GLP-1 RA Drugs and Eating Disorders.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have transformed the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes (T2D), but their rapid uptake has outpaced understanding of their effects in individuals with eating disorders (EDs). GLP-1 RAs produce sustained effects on appetite, satiety, food reward, and energy intake, raising the possibility of markedly different consequences across ED presentations.

RECENT FINDINGS: Preliminary studies suggest potential benefit for binge-eating symptoms, consistent with emerging evidence of overlap between binge eating and reward- and impulse-related pathways. Conversely, appetite suppression and attenuation of compensatory responses to negative energy balance could facilitate or mask restriction in individuals vulnerable to anorexia nervosa (AN) or atypical anorexia nervosa (AAN). Empirical evidence remains sparse. We review neurobiological and genetic evidence relevant to these potentially divergent effects, summarize the clinical literature, and highlight implications for screening and monitoring. Determining who may benefit, who may be harmed, and how to identify risk before treatment should be priorities for future research.

articles.title: The Effects of Pelvic Radiation on Ileal-Anal Pouches: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) is the gold-standard treatment for ulcerative colitis and familial adenomatous polyposis. Pelvic radiation for co-existing malignancies has been associated with pouch complications, yet guidance is still limited. This review synthesized current evidence on effects of pelvic radiation in patients with IPAA. A systematic search of Embase, MEDLINE, and Scopus was conducted in February 2025 using IPAA and pelvic-radiation terms. Eligible studies included patients who underwent IPAA and received pelvic radiation before or after surgery, and reported a pouch-related clinical outcome. Twelve studies (2004-2024) met inclusion criteria, comprising 101 patients who received radiation (83 external beam radiation therapy [EBRT], 18 brachytherapy). The pooled pouchitis rate was 28% (95% CI, 24%-34%). Complications were more common when radiation was delivered after IPAA than before: pouchitis occurred in 53.7% versus 7.7%, and pouch failure in 39.0% versus 3.8%. Brachytherapy was associated with numerically lower pouchitis (16.7% versus 25.3%) and pouch failure (11.1% versus 18.1%) rates than EBRT; however, differences were not statistically significant. Pelvic radiation in patients with IPAA is associated with adverse outcomes. Radiation timing and modality should be considered when balancing oncologic benefit against pouch function.

articles.title: Comparative epidemiology and outcomes of gram-negative and non-gram-negative External Ventricular Drain (EVD)-related infections: a 10-year single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: External ventricular drainage (EVD) is a device used in neurosurgical intensive care to monitor intracranial pressure and treat acute hydrocephalus. Ventriculostomy related infections (VRI) remain the major complications, with reported rates of 8 to 11 cases per 1000 EVD days. Most VRI cases are caused by skin commensal bacteria but Gram-negative bacilli (GNB) infections may carry a worse prognosis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, observational study in a neurosurgical ICU, from January 2014 to December 2023. All patients who developed VRI were included. A composite endpoint of poor clinical outcome was defined a priori and included cerebral abscess or antibiotic treatment failure.

RESULTS: Among the study period, 1868 patients had an EVD, and we included 71 patients who developed a VRI (2.05 / 1000 EVD days; mean age 50 ± 14 years), with a mortality rate in ICU of 10% (n = 7). The most frequent pathogens were methicillin-sensitive coagulase-negative Staphylococci (n = 26, 38%) and GNB (n = 24, 35%). Between GNB and non-GNB VRI, there was a significant difference between groups regarding the primary endpoint (p = 0.040), no significant difference for the occurrence of cerebral abscess (p = 0.262) but there was more antibiotic treatment failure in the GNB group (p = 0.015). Patients with GNB-related VRI had higher SAPS II scores (47 vs. 33, p < 0.001), longer durations of mechanical ventilation (34 days vs 20, p < 0.005), longer ICU stays (48 days vs. 28, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In our study, the incidence of VRI was 2.05 cases per 1000 EVD days. GNB related VRI accounted for 34% of cases. Significant differences in poor clinical outcomes were observed between GNB-related VRI and other VRI types. A higher rate of treatment failure, a higher initial severity score and a longer duration of mechanical ventilation and ICU hospitalization were observed in the GNB-VRI group.

articles.title: Functional recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a patient-centred perspective.
articles.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) and urinary incontinence (UI) are among the most distressing sequelae after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), substantially affecting quality of life. Exploring patients' perceptions of functional recovery and willingness to undergo corrective surgery may improve rehabilitation and shared decision-making. This cross-sectional survey included patients previously treated with RARP, identified from a single-center IRB-approved prostate cancer database. Baseline demographic, clinical, and pathological data were collected. Erectile function was assessed using the IIEF-5. Patients completed the Sexual Recovery and Urinary Continence Recovery questionnaires after receiving standardized information on penile prosthesis (PP) and artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) implantation. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and ANOVA analyses were performed. Between April and September 2025, 214 patients completed the questionnaires. Mean age was 65 years, and 67% underwent nerve-sparing surgery. At a mean follow-up of 21 months (range 2-77 months), 89% reported postoperative ED, with a mean IIEF-5 score of 7; 93% had mild-to-severe ED. The mean importance of erectile function recovery was 8/10. Overall, 15% of patients with ED expressed interest in PP implantation. Younger men were more likely to consider PP surgery (p < 0.001). Although older men expressing willingness reported higher interest scores (9/10), differences across age groups were not statistically significant (p = 0.33). Overall urinary continence was rated 7/10, 39% reported UI, and 19% of patients with UI expressed willingness to undergo AUS implantation, with no significant age-related differences. Recovery of erectile and urinary function remains a major priority after RARP. Patients' willingness to consider definitive surgical rehabilitation highlights the importance of individualized counselling and shared decision-making.

articles.title: Impact of high-intensity foundational medical therapy on outcomes across risk profiles in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a major global health challenge, characterized by high morbidity, mortality, frequent hospitalization, and substantial healthcare costs, despite recent therapeutic advances. In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF; LVEF < 50%), foundational medical therapy (FMT), as defined in the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines-comprising renin-angiotensin system inhibition or angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, beta-blockers, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors-reduces morbidity and mortality, but its benefit depends on how completely, how quickly, and how intensively these therapies are implemented. This narrative review evaluates whether the benefit of early, comprehensive, high-intensity FMT in HFrEF differs according to specific baseline risk modifiers, drawing on the STRONG-HF trial and its secondary analyses, other randomized evidence, and real-world studies. In STRONG-HF, a high-intensity care strategy that combined rapid up-titration of renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, beta-blockers, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists with close post-discharge follow-up reduced the composite of all-cause death or HF readmission at 180 days, driven mainly by fewer HF readmissions; all-cause mortality alone was not significantly reduced, and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors were not part of the protocolized strategy. Secondary analyses found no significant heterogeneity of this effect across MAGGIC risk tertiles or systolic blood pressure strata, whereas associations between higher attained doses and better outcomes were observational. Meta-analyses of randomized trials additionally support early initiation of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors after decompensation. Prognostic scores, physiological parameters, and treatment-exposure measures are treated as distinct constructs rather than as an interchangeable single risk category. The review also addresses tools for risk prognostication, the boundary between FMT optimization and evaluation for mechanical circulatory support in advanced HF, and the real-world barriers to implementation, including patient comorbidity, therapeutic inertia, health-system constraints, and cost. Available evidence supports early initiation and structured optimization of FMT in appropriately selected HFrEF patients, with no convincing evidence that higher baseline risk alone justifies therapeutic inertia; however, the independent contributions of treatment completeness, dose intensity, and monitoring intensity, the optimal sequencing, and individualized dose targets remain uncertain, particularly in very high-risk and underrepresented populations, and warrant further prospective study.

articles.title: Adapting patient experience measurement to care trajectory in a multidisciplinary brain metastases program: a quality improvement evaluation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Patient experience is a core dimension of oncology care quality, but cognitive burden, emotional distress, and complex care trajectories in brain metastases populations may limit traditional survey approaches. This study evaluated the feasibility and interpretability of a locally developed, self-administered patient experience survey administered after initial brain-directed intervention within a multidisciplinary brain metastases program.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective quality improvement evaluation of a patient experience survey administered on tablets at follow-up visits two to three months after initial consultation. Eligible participants were new patients seen in a multidisciplinary brain metastases clinic. Descriptive statistics characterized response patterns, including agreement rates, "not applicable" responses, and missing data. Reasons for non-completion were categorized descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 70 eligible patients, 41 completed the survey (59%). Overall ratings were high, with most respondents reporting that they were always treated with courtesy and respect and always received the best care possible. Communication and decision-making items showed high agreement. Treatment-dependent items showed reduced applicability, including explanations of medication and treatment impact on daily activities, with substantial "not applicable" responses. A subset strongly disagreed with items addressing clarity of results and functional impact. Open-ended responses were generally positive despite structured disagreement.

CONCLUSION: Surveys administered after brain-directed intervention yielded high overall experience ratings but revealed variation in domain applicability, which may reflect treatment exposure and position along the disease trajectory. As a single cross-sectional administration of an instrument without formal psychometric validation, these findings primarily inform survey feasibility and design; trajectory-informed assessment strategies warrant prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for improving apraxia in corticobasal syndrome (CBS): an interventional pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder. We investigated, whether CBS is associated with a GABA deficiency in the cerebral cortex, whether inhibitory repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) affects cortical GABA+/Cr levels, and whether this improves apraxia.

METHODS: In this bicentric, open-label intervention study, we performed 20 daily sessions of inhibitory rTMS, applied over the clinically more affected parietal cortex. Over a period of 6 months, we examined 18 patients using the Apraxia DATE Testscore Version and, in 15 of these patients, measured cortical GABA+/Cr concentrations in the parietal cortex using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS). The secondary endpoints included motor and cognitive performance before and after the intervention.

RESULTS: The Intervention revealed an improvement in the DATE Pseudoword subtest (p = 0.025). For the DATE Finger (F) subtest, the analyses showed a significant improvement from pre-intervention to 4 weeks post-intervention (p = < 0.001). Cognitive performance revealed an improvement for the Wordlist Recall in the CERAD-plus battery that remained significant also for the follow-up period (all p < 0.002). The baseline MRS measurements showed a significant deficiency of GABA+/Cr in the parietal cortex on the clinically more severely affected side (p < 0.05) and, post-intervention, a significant increase in GABA+/Cr concentration (p < 0.05). Pearson correlation indicated a marginally significant positive correlation in the DATE-Pseudoword subtest and parietal GABA+/Cr concentration (r = 0.632, p = 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Inhibitory rTMS applied to the clinically more affected parietal cortex in severely affected CBS patients resulted in significant improvements across two apraxia subtests, an improvement of a pre-existing parietal GABA+/Cr deficiency and enhanced cognitive performance.

articles.title: Holistic neuroimaging compression to improve clinical predictivity of post-stroke mood symptoms at 6 months.
articles.abstract: Post-stroke mood impairments are frequent yet difficult to predict using neuroimaging markers. While voxel-level analyses have struggled to identify reliable predictors, network-level approaches may offer greater sensitivity. Accordingly, we developed a pipeline to predict post-stroke mood status using whole-brain components derived from MRI sequences routinely acquired in clinical practice. Three heterogeneous stroke cohorts (ntotal = 672) were included, with mood evaluated six months post-stroke using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression-Anxiety (HAD-A), HAD-Depression (HAD-D), and Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression (CES-D) scales. For model training, diffusion-weighted signal from one cohort was compressed using principal component analysis (PCA) and components associated with numerical mood scores were fitted using K-Nearest Neighbour regression. Predictive performance was externally validated and compared with disconnectome-based models and models comprising baseline clinical and demographic variables. Disconnectome-based models showed minimal predictive power across datasets (R²<0.01) and were inapplicable in certain cases. Clinical models performed best for HAD-A (R2 = 0.215, AUC = 0.735) and HAD-D (R² = 0.265, AUC = 0.795) scores, with baseline mood status as the strongest predictor. The imaging-based pipeline showed weak predictive performance overall but improved clinical models for HAD-A (ΔR² = 0.0366, p = 0.004) and HAD-D (ΔR² = 0.023, p = 0.037). For CES-D, where baseline mood status was unavailable, the pipeline outperformed the clinical model (ΔAUC = 0.046, p = 0.01), with modest association between predicted and observed scores (r² = 0.073). This framework to capture global diffusion patterns without requiring advanced imaging sequences may provide clinically relevant information to stroke neuropsychiatric outcomes. Although showing limited predictivity, our pipeline may complement clinical predictors.

articles.title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.

articles.title: Comparison of laterally closed tunnel and free gingival graft for isolated anterior mandibular recessions: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the laterally closed tunnel (LCT) technique combined with connective tissue graft (CTG) and free gingival graft (FGG) in the treatment of isolated gingival recessions in the anterior mandibular region.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-one patients were divided into two groups: the LCT group (n = 10), treated using the LCT technique with CTG; and the FGG group (n = 11), treated using FGG. Periodontal clinical parameters were evaluated at baseline and after 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The Landry index, root coverage esthetic score, and visual analog scale for pain were also evaluated. Statistical modeling was used to assess the impact of treatment and clinical factors on 12-month root coverage, with scenario-based predictions supporting personalized planning.

RESULTS: A progressive improvement in root coverage and keratinized tissue thickness was observed in both groups, although no significant differences were found. Greater keratinized tissue height was observed in the FGG group at all follow-up periods (p < 0.05). No differences were found in healing patterns, esthetic evaluation by professionals, or patient-reported esthetic outcomes. The FGG group reported higher pain levels after 7 days (p < 0.05). Tooth type had a significant effect (p = 0.046) on 12-month root coverage, and the best outcomes were observed in aligned incisors treated with FGG.

CONCLUSIONS: Both techniques were effective, promoting root coverage and increasing keratinized tissue. While FGG showed greater keratinized tissue gain, LCT resulted in less postoperative discomfort.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The findings highlight the specific clinical benefits of each technique, supporting personalized treatment planning based on expected outcomes and patient needs.

articles.title: Opioid-free anaesthesia versus opioid-based anaesthesia for laparoscopic radical prostatectomy: a prespecified analysis of a single-centre randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Opioid-free anaesthesia (OFA) is increasingly used to limit intraoperative opioids in oncological surgery, but evidence in radical prostatectomy is scarce. We compared OFA with a remifentanil-based technique in laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (LRP) on a uniform multimodal and regional analgesic background.

METHODS: Adult men undergoing LRP were randomized to OFA (dexmedetomidine plus ketamine, no intraoperative opioids) or a remifentanil-based technique. Both groups received identical multimodal premedication, bilateral quadratus lumborum block, sevoflurane maintenance and identical oxycodone patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). The primary outcome was total oxycodone consumption over the first 24 postoperative hours. Pre-specified secondary outcomes included Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), serum creatinine change to day 1, and the demanded-to-delivered PCA bolus ratio.

RESULTS: Fifty-seven patients were analysed (OFA n = 32; remifentanil n = 25). Total 24-h oxycodone consumption did not differ (location-shift estimate - 2.0 mg, 95% CI -8.0 to 6.0; p = 0.556), and neither NRS scores nor PONV differed significantly. The demanded-to-delivered PCA bolus ratio was lower with OFA (location-shift estimate - 0.20, 95% CI -0.267 to 0.000; p = 0.006), as was the early rise in serum creatinine (location-shift estimate - 7.7 µmol/L, 95% CI -13.9 to -1.1; p = 0.034). Intraoperative bradycardia and hypotension did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: In LRP, no statistically significant difference in 24-hour oxycodone consumption or pain scores was detected between OFA and remifentanil-based anaesthesia. The trial was not designed or powered for equivalence or non-inferiority, and these findings therefore do not establish comparable efficacy. Differences in two pre-specified secondary outcomes (a lower demanded-to-delivered PCA ratio and a smaller early creatinine rise) are hypothesis-generating. Because recruitment was curtailed, findings require confirmation in adequately powered trials, ideally in robot-assisted prostatectomy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06380244, registered 23 April 2024.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cell secretome alleviates testicular oxidative stress and ultrastructural alterations in a type 1 diabetes rat model.
articles.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are considered promising candidates for the treatment of type 1 diabetes (T1D) due to their paracrine effects mediated by the secretome, which exerts immunomodulatory, cytoprotective, antiapoptotic, and antioxidant functions. Beyond their primary therapeutic role, MSC-derived products may also contribute to the alleviation of secondary complications associated with chronic hyperglycemia. One of these complications is male reproductive dysfunction, characterized by impaired spermatogenesis, decreased testosterone production, and altered Sertoli cell metabolism. Within this framework, we examined the therapeutic impacts of conditioned media (CM) collected from human umbilical cord-derived MSCs cultured in two- and three-dimensional (2D and 3D) environments on diabetes-induced testicular alterations in rats. T1D was established in Sprague-Dawley rats through multiple low-dose streptozotocin administrations. The experimental design consisted of control, diabetes, diabetes-2DCM, and diabetes-3DCM groups. Following T1D induction, the rats received intraperitoneal CM three times weekly for a duration of 4 weeks. Then, reproductive hormone levels, histological findings, oxidative stress parameters, and ultrastructural alterations were evaluated. Accordingly, diabetes significantly reduced gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), luteinizing hormone (LH), and testosterone levels, increased oxidative stress in testes, and induced marked ultrastructural testicular alterations. CM treatment attenuated oxidative stress and partially preserved testicular architecture, accompanied by a modest but nonsignificant increase in GnRH levels. Improvements were generally better in the 3DCM group, particularly regarding preservation of seminiferous epithelial integrity and acrosomal organization. These findings indicate the protective potential of MSC-derived secretomes against diabetes-associated male reproductive dysfunction. More broadly, secretome-based therapies may help limit secondary organ complications in multisystemic diseases such as diabetes.

articles.title: Pelvic osteotomy in classic bladder exstrophy and cloacal exstrophy: a systematic review and qualitative evidence synthesis with separate clinical pathways.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesise evidence on pelvic osteotomy in classic bladder exstrophy (CBE) and cloacal exstrophy (CE), with separate interpretation of their reconstructive pathways.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched to 9 September 2026. Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data. MINORS and Cochrane RoB 2 assessed methodological limitations. Findings were synthesised qualitatively in separate CBE/bladder-exstrophy, CE and mixed-cohort strata.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included: nine addressing CBE or bladder exstrophy as reported, three CE-specific studies and one mixed cohort. One was a pilot randomised trial; the remainder were observational. CBE studies described osteotomy-assisted primary closure and selective mobilisation when approximation was difficult, without establishing superiority over closure without osteotomy. CE studies described osteotomy within complex primary or repeat reconstruction involving staging, fixation and immobilisation. In one CE cohort, unadjusted closure success was 77.6% with osteotomy versus 41.7% without, but the association did not persist after adjustment. No technique showed consistent superiority. Evidence for independent improvements in continence, pelvic-floor anatomy or gait was insufficient; functional findings from CBE were not extrapolated to CE.

CONCLUSION: CBE and CE require distinct interpretation. Osteotomy should be planned together with postoperative stabilisation and immobilisation to protect the reconstruction. Osteotomy selection in CBE depends on pelvic mechanics; CE requires specialist planning of pelvic mobilisation and stabilisation. Referral to experienced multidisciplinary centres should be prioritised. The proposed framework is conceptual, requires validation and cannot replace specialist expertise.

articles.title: Liver and spleen stiffness by 2D shear-wave elastography for identifying high-risk varices in cirrhosis: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings.

RESULTS: 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year.

CONCLUSION: LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Perioperative pulmonary aspiration reports associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists: a pharmacovigilance analysis of FAERS.
articles.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly prescribed for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. Although these agents provide substantial metabolic and cardiovascular benefits, they also delay gastric emptying, which may increase the risk of perioperative pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia. Real-world evidence evaluating this potential safety concern remains limited. We conducted a retrospective pharmacovigilance study using reports from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from January 2016 through March 2024. A perioperative-enriched cohort was identified by restricting reports to those listing general anesthetic or neuromuscular blocking agents as surrogate markers of a perioperative setting. Patients were classified into three mutually exclusive groups: GLP-1 receptor agonists, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors as an active comparator, and a background surgical population. Pulmonary aspiration events were identified using MedDRA preferred terms. Disproportionality analyses were performed using reporting odds ratios (RORs), and Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate independent predictors of aspiration after adjustment for age, sex, and concomitant opioid use, because exposed events were sparse. After deduplication, a total of 41,308 unique perioperative reports were identified, including 158 reports involving GLP-1 receptor agonists and 174 involving SGLT-2 inhibitors. Pulmonary aspiration showed non-significantly higher reporting odds among GLP-1 RA users (ROR 1.27, P = 0.56). In the Firth penalized adjusted analysis, GLP-1 RA exposure was associated with numerically higher, but statistically non-significant, adjusted reporting odds of pulmonary aspiration (aOR 2.08; P = 0.185). SGLT-2 inhibitor exposure showed numerically lower but statistically non-significant reporting odds of pulmonary aspiration than the background cohort (aOR 0.27; P = 0.059); this estimate rests on a single event and should not be interpreted as a protective effect. Concomitant opioid use was independently associated with aspiration (aOR 2.12; P < 0.001). In this perioperative-enriched FAERS analysis, neither the unadjusted disproportionality analysis nor the adjusted model demonstrated a statistically significant association between GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure and pulmonary aspiration, although a non-significant numerical trend was observed. Given the small number of events and the inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting data, these findings are hypothesis-generating, require prospective validation, and should not on their own guide individual perioperative decision-making.

articles.title: Outcome After Late Pulmonary Valve Replacement in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
articles.abstract: The optimal timing of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) in adults with repaired Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) and severe pulmonary regurgitation remains controversial. Current recommendations rely largely on right ventricular volumetric thresholds derived from cohorts undergoing intervention during adolescence or early adulthood, although their prognostic value remains debated. To identify predictors of postoperative morbidity and mortality after PVR in patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF, with a specific focus on invasive preoperative hemodynamic parameters. We conducted a retrospective single-center study including patients aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF who underwent surgical PVR between 2009 and 2018. The primary outcome was a composite endpoint including supraventricular arrhythmia, cardiovascular rehospitalization, or all-cause death during follow-up. Clinical, imaging, and hemodynamic variables were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Forty-eight patients (mean age at PVR 41 ± 9.8 years) were included, with a mean follow-up of 52 months. The primary outcome occurred in 23 patients (48%). Preoperative signs of advanced disease, including right heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and a history of syncope or ventricular tachycardia, were associated with adverse outcomes. Although right ventricular end-diastolic volumes were markedly increased in both groups, they were not associated with the primary outcome. Conversely, right ventricular end-systolic volume and, particularly, right ventricular end-diastolic pressure (RVEDP) showed stronger prognostic value. In multivariable analysis, RVEDP remained the only independent predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality (OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.01-3.40; p = 0.04). In adults aged ≥30 years with repaired TOF undergoing PVR, elevated RVEDP is a key predictor of postoperative morbidity and mortality, whereas right ventricular end diastolic volumes on MRI are not. Invasive hemodynamic assessment may help refine the timing of PVR in this "senior" population.

articles.title: [From a broken shock absorber to robot-assisted TKA : Two-stage conversion for fracture and metallosis of a subcutaneous unloading system].
articles.abstract: A KineSpring® system (an extra-articular medial shock absorber) failed after 10 years with ring fracture and local metallosis in a 70-year-old obese patient with diabetes. Because of the infection risk, conversion was two-staged: removal, then robot-assisted TKA after 6.5 months, planned on a metal-free CT. At 12 months the patient is nearly pain-free (KOOS Pain 97.2; baseline 41.7). To our knowledge, a robot-assisted conversion has not been described before.

articles.title: Identifying accuracy-preserving truncation thresholds of the time-attenuation curve in CT perfusion for acute anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion stroke.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To quantify the impact of progressively increasing time-attenuation curve (TAC) truncation on CT perfusion (CTP) parameters in acute anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion (AC-LVO) stroke, and to identify truncation thresholds that preserve quantitative accuracy and the reliability of treatment selection.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 113 consecutive patients with acute AC-LVO stroke. CTP datasets acquired at 1.5- or 2.0-second sampling intervals were processed using two fully automated AI-based software packages (CTPDoc and United Imaging). TAC truncation was simulated by sequential removal of terminal frames from full-scan datasets. Using full-scan maps as the reference standard, quantitative deviations were analyzed with Friedman tests and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Qualitative agreement regarding treatment eligibility (based on DEFUSE 3, TRACE-III, and SELECT Late criteria) was assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and percent agreement. Truncation thresholds were defined as the latest time points showing no significant differences (p > 0.05) and good agreement (ICC ≥ 0.75; percent agreement ≥ 82%).

RESULTS: Increasing TAC truncation increased parameter deviations and reduced agreement in treatment selection across four groups. Relative to standardized onset, truncation thresholds were 27 and 28 s for CTPDoc (1.5-second and 2.0-second intervals), and 34.5 and 40 s for United Imaging (1.5-second and 2.0-second intervals).

CONCLUSION: Although TAC truncation degrades CTP accuracy and treatment-selection concordance, algorithm- and protocol-specific truncation thresholds exist. Adherence to these thresholds may support reliable treatment selection and reduce unnecessary repeat CTP examinations, thereby preventing treatment delays, cumulative radiation exposure, and contrast load when TACs are partially truncated.

articles.title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints.

RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Carotid plaque morphology on computed tomography angiography associated with cervical recanalization strategy in acute ischemic stroke with anterior circulation tandem lesions.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether carotid plaque morphology on preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) is associated with the cervical recanalization strategy used during endovascular treatment (EVT) of acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation tandem atherosclerotic lesions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospective single-center database of consecutive adults treated with mechanical thrombectomy within 24 h of last known well between January 2022 and February 2025. CTA features of the extracranial internal carotid artery lesion included plaque composition, occlusion-cap morphology, string sign, and calcification pattern (none, eggshell, or dystrophic). Patients were categorized according to cervical recanalization strategy: aspiration alone or percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with or without stenting (PTA±stent). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with PTA±stent.

RESULTS: Seventy-nine patients were included (median age, 68 years). Cervical recanalization was achieved with aspiration alone in 40 patients (50.6%) and with PTA±stent in 39 (49.4%); stents were implanted in 14 patients. Dystrophic calcification was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (38.5% vs. 17.5%; p = 0.038). Dystrophic calcification (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 4.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-17.05; p = 0.014) and male sex (adjusted OR, 4.97; 95% CI, 1.43-17.31; p = 0.012) were independently associated with PTA±stent. Successful intracranial reperfusion was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (89.7% vs. 70.0%; p = 0.029), with no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or 90-day functional outcome.

CONCLUSION: Dystrophic calcification on preprocedural CTA was independently associated with the use of cervical PTA with or without stenting in patients with anterior circulation tandem lesions. This finding may help anticipate the potential need for cervical angioplasty and facilitate technical procedural preparation.

articles.title: Hedgehog Signaling-Dependent Heterochronic Control of Cardiomyocyte Differentiation Establishes Distinct Cardiac Progenitor Fields.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The mammalian heart is formed from distinct cardiac progenitor fields: the first heart field (FHF), second heart field (SHF), and juxta-cardiac field (JCF). How these fields are established remains one of the oldest questions in cardiac biology and is central to understanding congenital heart disease, which differentially affects derivatives of the individual fields. Previous work has demonstrated that the fields emerge and differentiate at distinct times; however, the mechanisms underlying their establishment have remained elusive. Here, we implicate Hedgehog signaling-dependent heterochronic control of cardiac differentiation in the emergence of different heart fields.

METHODS: We assessed Hedgehog signaling activity by assembling a cardio-mesodermal single-cell atlas. We analyzed Hedgehog ligand gene expression by confocal imaging in gastrulating mouse embryos. We investigated the necessity of Hedgehog signaling using 2 distinct genetic Hedgehog loss-of-function mouse models, analyzed by single-nucleus RNA sequencing analysis.

RESULTS: Our results show that Hedgehog signaling mediates field-specific heterochronic control of differentiation timing that orchestrates the establishment of the SHF and JCF as distinct from the FHF. We identify a common cardiac progenitor transcriptomic state from which all 3 fields emerge. We show that the SHF and JCF are established coincident with Hedgehog signaling reception, whereas the FHF evades Hedgehog pathway activity and rapidly differentiates. We find that Hedgehog ligand expression sandwiches the cardiac mesoderm emerging from the primitive streak, spatially coordinating SHF and JCF establishment. Partial depletion of Hedgehog signaling causes premature activation of the cardiac differentiation program in the SHF and JCF. Complete ablation of Hedgehog signaling results in failed SHF and JCF establishment.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal a Hedgehog signaling-dependent, non-cell-autonomous heterochronic mechanism required for SHF and JCF formation. This heterochronic mechanism provides a new paradigm for understanding the ordered temporal emergence of the cardiac progenitor fields that support the development of the 4-chambered heart, as well as a general model for the emergence of progenitor fields that drive organogenesis across the mammalian body plan.

articles.title: Asiatic acid attenuates sepsis-induced acute kidney injury by dual suppression of STING-driven inflammation and ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) carries high mortality due to unresolved inflammatory and oxidative stress. Although ferroptosis has emerged as a critical contributor to tubular damage, targeted therapies remain limited. Here, we report that the natural triterpenoid asiatic acid (AA) confers potent renoprotection in a murine model of cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced sepsis. AA administration significantly improved renal function, mitigated histopathological injury, and reduced systemic and renal inflammation. Mechanistically, AA suppressed the activation of STING pathway, decreasing phosphorylation of STING, TBK1, and IRF3, and downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines. In parallel, AA inhibited ferroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells, as evidenced by reduced lipid peroxidation, restored glutathione and SOD activity, and normalized expression of ferroptosis-regulating proteins (GPX4, ACSL4, COX2). Collectively, our findings identify AA as a multi-target agent that alleviates sepsis-induced AKI through concurrent inhibition of STING-mediated inflammation and ferroptosis, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for this lethal clinical syndrome.

articles.title: Laparoscopic versus open abdominoperineal resection in rectal cancer: lower successful resection and higher 3-year local recurrence: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Laparoscopic abdominoperineal resection (LAPR) is widely assumed non-inferior to open APR (OAPR), yet existing evidence derives from small retrospective series or randomised trials that pre-labelled patients as "definite APR" before surgery-thereby sacrificing any opportunity for intra-operative sphincter preservation and compromising patient autonomy. This post-hoc emulation of the LASRE trial compared successful resection rates and 3-year oncological outcomes between LAPR and OAPR using a "randomise-to-route, decide-at-surgery" design that preserves sphincter-saving options.

METHODS: Adults with rectal cancer ≤ 5 cm from the dentate line enrolled in the multicentre LASRE RCT (22 Chinese Centres, 2013-2018) were randomised 2:1 to laparoscopic or open resection; the final decision to perform APR was made intra-operatively. The primary endpoints were successful resection (complete or near-complete total mesorectal excision plus a circumferential resection margin ≥ 1 mm) and 3-year local recurrence (LR). Sensitivity analyses comprised as-treated and conversion-excluded sets, multivariable adjustment, and formal interaction testing.

RESULTS: Of 321 patients whose final operation was APR (215 LAPR, 106 OAPR), baseline characteristics were balanced except age (58 vs 57 years, P = 0.048) and clinical stage I (43.7% vs 29.3%, P = 0.012). Successful resection was achieved less frequently with LAPR (89.1% vs 96.6%, P = 0.038).
