Three-year LR was higher after LAPR (8.1% vs 1.9%; HR 4.445, 95% CI 1.027-19.240; P = 0.029), and this association persisted in as-treated and conversion-excluded sensitivity analyses (HR 4.66 and 4.52, respectively), whereas 3-year disease-free survival (76.3% vs 73.4%; HR 0.888, 95% CI 0.558-1.413; P = 0.616) and overall survival (89.3% vs 89.5%; HR 1.019, 95% CI 0.494-2.102; P = 0.959) did not differ. LAPR reduced blood loss (50 vs 100 mL, P < 0.001), 30-day morbidity (13.7% vs 24.5%, P = 0.017) and perineal wound infection (6.2% vs 13.2%, P = 0.034).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, even among credentialed surgeons, LAPR was associated with short-term recovery benefits but lower successful-resection rates and a higher observed rate of 3-year local recurrence. These findings represent a local-control signal rather than definitive evidence of overall oncological inferiority, and require validation before any change in practice.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Parent trial: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01899547.

articles.title: Effects of Health Behaviour Change Interventions on Pain Intensity, Functional Disability, and Safety Behaviour Among Nurses with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate and synthesise the effects of health behaviour change interventions on pain intensity, functional disability, and safety behaviours among nurses with work-related musculoskeletal disorders.

METHODS: This study adhered to the PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines. Six electronic databases (PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, EMBASE, and Ovid MEDLINE) were searched for randomised controlled trials published before 16 February 2026. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for randomised trials and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach via GRADEpro. Primary meta-analyses used fixed-effect models in Review Manager 5.4; supplementary random-effects analyses estimated 95% prediction intervals. Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran's Q test and the I2 statistic. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted where appropriate.

RESULTS: Ten randomised controlled trials comprising 1,208 nurses met the inclusion criteria. In the primary fixed-effect analyses, health behaviour change interventions reduced pain intensity (SMD = -0.32; 95% CI: -0.49 to -0.15; P = 0.0003; I2 = 61%) and functional disability (SMD = -0.66; 95% CI: -0.83 to -0.50; P < 0.00001; I2 = 84%) and improved safety behaviours (SMD = 1.04; 95% CI: 0.87 to 1.22; P < 0.00001; I2 = 89%). Supplementary random-effects analyses showed that the effects on pain and functional disability were no longer statistically significant, while the effect on safety behaviours remained significant.

CONCLUSIONS: This review identified associations between health behaviour change interventions and improvements in pain, functional disability, and safety behaviours among nurses with work-related musculoskeletal disorders. However, due to methodological bias, study heterogeneity, and short follow-up periods, the evidence remains limited.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CRD420251042168 (PROSPERO).

articles.title: Acute effects of transcranial direct current stimulation on repetition volume, blood lactate concentration, and perceived exertion during back squat exercise.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the acute effects of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) applied over the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) on the total number of repetitions completed during high-load back-squat exercise performed until muscular failure, as well as on perceptual and metabolic responses, in resistance-trained men. Sixteen resistance-trained men (24.4 ± 3.7 years) completed a randomized, sham-controlled, triple-blind, crossover study involving three stimulation conditions: anodal tDCS, cathodal tDCS, and sham. Following 20 min of stimulation (2 mA), participants performed successive sets of five repetitions at 80% of one-repetition maximum (1RM), separated by 1-min rest intervals, until task failure. Repetition volume was considered the primary outcome, whereas blood lactate concentration (pre-exercise and 5 min post-exercise) and session rating of perceived exertion (sRPE) were considered secondary outcomes. Repetition volume was significantly greater following anodal tDCS than cathodal tDCS (67.5 [40.5-99.8] vs. 43.0 [33.0-70.3] repetitions, Z = - 2.642, P = 0.002) and sham (67.5 [40.5-99.8] vs. 43.5 [31.0-78.3] repetitions, Z = - 3.517, P = 0.004), with no difference between cathodal tDCS and sham (P = 1.00). Blood lactate concentration increased from pre- to post-exercise across all conditions (P ≤ 0.001), with higher post-exercise values following anodal than cathodal tDCS (P = 0.005). No significant differences in sRPE were observed among conditions (P = 0.275). Anodal DLPFC tDCS acutely increased repetition volume during high-load partial back squats in resistance-trained men, with higher blood lactate concentrations than cathodal stimulation, but not sham, and no corresponding increase in perceived exertion.

articles.title: A Modified Method for the Quantification of Trigonocephaly Following Minimally-Invasive Surgery and Helmet Therapy to Correct Metopic Craniosynostosis.
articles.abstract: Introduction Previous publications have described various means of measuring surgical and morphological outcomes in craniosynostosis using optical surface scanning technology; however, they are often cumbersome to acquire and require specialized software. In this study, our group sought to adapt these methods using a free, widely available measurement tool and evaluate its discriminating ability for use in outcome assessment of patients with metopic craniosynostosis. Methods 10 patients treated with strip craniectomy and orthosis for metopic craniosynostosis were retrospectively analyzed. Patients with known syndromes were excluded. Previous methods were adapted to a novel workflow using software available to our cranial remolding clinic. Frontal Angle 30 measurement (FA30) was performed on patients at the preoperative, 6-month, and end of treatment (EOT) intervals by multiple raters on the craniofacial team. A control group of 12 patients without craniofacial abnormalities was also measured and compared to assess the discriminating ability of the angle measurement tool. Preoperative measurements were compared to preoperative interfrontal angle (IFA) measured on CT. Standard descriptive statistics were calculated, and statistical significance was assessed using non-parametric tests for paired and unpaired samples due to the small sample sizes. Interrater reliability and intraobserver repeatability for measurements were assessed using Intraclass Correlation. Spearman correlation was calculated between preoperative IFA and FA30 measurements. Results Average Frontal Angle 30 (FA30) measurement increased from 129.85˚ to 134.08˚ (p = 0.0025) at 6 months postoperatively. There was no statistically significant difference between measurements at 6 months and end of treatment (EOT mean = 134.13˚, p = .443). A significant difference was observed between all groups when compared to non-metopic patients (141.99˚, p < .001, p = .0015, and p = .014). Preoperative Starscanner® FA30 measurements demonstrated a significant Spearman correlation with CT based IFA (ρ = 0.77, p = .009). Intraclass Correlation analysis revealed a high degree of reliability between three raters (ICC = 0.994, Cl: 0.988-0.997) and between ratings of a single rater (ICC = 0.993, Cl: 0.988-0.997). Conclusion Previously described methods for angle measurement can be adapted to different scanning modalities and software with similar discriminating ability. Adaptation of angle measurement methods to free and open-source software enables use of these tools in a wider variety of clinical environments. Treatment beyond 6 months of helmet therapy may not result in additional improvement of angle correction, but may serve to stabilize the achieved result.

articles.title: A Narrowly Tuned Olfactory Receptor in the Sunda Pangolin Identifies 1-Octen-3-One as a Key Chemical Cue in Foraging Behavior.
articles.abstract: The Sunda pangolin (Manis javanica) is considered a critically endangered species, partly due to its highly specialized diet, which consists mostly of ants and termites. Field observations have shown that pangolins rely on olfaction to locate ant and termite nests even from distances of several kilometers. However, the specific chemical signal used to locate food in the field remains unknown. Based on transcriptome sequencing, 1033 olfactory receptors (MjavORs) of M. javanica were identified and analyzed. Four MjavORs (OR118, OR171, OR215, and OR276) were functionally characterized using the Xenopus laevis oocyte system co-expressing CFTR, RTP1, and Gαolf. Notably, MjavOR215 showed a robust response to 1-octen-3-one, a compound released from termite nests. An odorant-binding protein, MjavOBP3, also demonstrated the highest binding affinity for 1-octen-3-one. Behavioral tracking assays confirmed that pangolins are significantly attracted to 1-octen-3-one, a volatile emitted from termite nests (p < 0.05), rather than to volatiles from termites themselves. These results clarify the molecular mechanisms underlying pangolin foraging, demonstrating that volatile from termite nests guide this behavior.

articles.title: A prospective, comparative cohort analysis of influenza antibody waning in Michigan and Hong Kong during periods of low influenza circulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted concern about waning of population immunity that could lead to subsequent surges in circulation. We compared longitudinal influenza antibody titers in Michigan and Hong Kong, two regions with reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic.

METHODS: In two prospective cohort studies (HIVE, Michigan; EPI-HK, Hong Kong), we analyzed longitudinal serum samples collected from 2020 through 2023 from participants without influenza infection or vaccination. Sera were tested using hemagglutination inhibition assays (HAI) and microneutralization (MN) against vaccine strains. Two-year fold changes in titers were estimated using multivariable power-law models adjusted for age and baseline titer.

RESULTS: We analyzed 173 sera from 57 HIVE participants and 259 sera from 60 EPI-HK participants. Initial HAI geometric mean titers ranged from 12.3-123.4 in HIVE and 6.3-40.9 in EPI-HK. Among those with >1:40 baseline titers in HIVE, fold-change estimates indicated waning for H1N1 strains, including A/Brisbane (0.70 [95% CI: 0.56,0.86]), A/Idaho (0.40 [0.32,0.50]), and A/Michigan (0.43 [0.34,0.52]), while H3N2 and influenza B showed minimal or no waning. In EPI-HK, fold-change estimates demonstrated heterogeneous patterns by strain for H1N1, and waning for selected H3N2 strains, including A/Cambodia (0.44 [0.29,0.65]) and A/Singapore (0.48 [0.33,0.69]). MN results were consistent with HAI findings.

CONCLUSION: Influenza antibody responses during the pandemic showed heterogeneous, strain-specific changes rather than uniform decline. These findings suggest that population immunity was maintained for many strains despite reduced viral circulation, with waning occurring in particular strains and varying by population.

articles.title: The Joint Impact of Deleterious Mutations, Dominance, and Gene Flow on Linked Neutral Variation in Structured Populations.
articles.abstract: Most species are geographically structured, which leaves characteristic signatures in neutral genomic regions used to reconstruct demographic history. Yet, these signatures can be distorted by linked selection due to deleterious mutations. This can reduce genetic diversity through Background Selection, or increase diversity through Associative Overdominance. While their effects are well characterized in panmictic populations, they remain largely unexplored in structured populations. We investigated an Isolation-with-Migration model using simulations across a range of migration, selection, dominance, and recombination parameters. We quantified the effects of deleterious mutations on standard summary statistics by simulating either genotypes at neutral and deleterious mutations (genotype-based approach) or genealogies and deleterious mutations (Ancestral Recombination Graph-based approach). The latter recovered similar patterns, directly relating genomic patterns to underlying coalescent processes. For lower recombination rates, we found a Background Selection-driven regime for weakly codominant mutations, characterized by lower diversity and increased genetic differentiation. For recessive mutations, we identified an Associative Overdominance-driven regime, characterized by increased diversity and lower genetic differentiation. This is reflected in the genealogies: Background Selection shrunk coalescence times and led to lineage sorting topologies, while Associative Overdominance stretched coalescence times and led to incomplete lineage-sorting topologies. Migration strongly affected genetic differentiation and topology frequencies but had weaker effects on diversity and coalescence times. Our results provide evidence of a transition from Associative Overdominance to Background Selection for recessive deleterious mutations in an isolation-with-migration model. Importantly, these processes leave distinct signatures on genealogies, highlighting that Ancestral Recombination Graph-based approaches have the potential for inferring linked-selection in structured populations.

articles.title: One to move, one to clip: double transcatheter edge-to-edge repair technique for mitral regurgitation after annuloplasty ring dehiscence.
Co-administration of DTaP with COVID-19 mRNA vaccine in mice alters immune responses and induces increased protection from Bordetella pertussis challenge.
articles.abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, children received COVID-19 mRNA vaccines alongside other regularly scheduled immunizations, such as the acellular Bordetella pertussis vaccine DTaP. It is known that mRNA vaccines are pro-inflammatory in nature, leading to protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 infection. The goal of this study was to investigate the potential adjuvanticity of co-administration of a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP. Mice were immunized with DTaP alone or with a co-administration of DTaP plus COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. To understand the impact of co-administration, we evaluated protection against B. pertussis aerosol challenge in mice and potential correlates of protection, including cytokine responses to vaccination, antibody responses, and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the draining lymph node. Three decreasing doses of each vaccine were used to simulate waning immunity. Overall, compared to mice immunized with DTaP, co-administration of DTaP + COVID-19 mRNA vaccines elicited higher pro-inflammatory cytokine responses, higher IgG2b antibody responses, and mice were afforded increased protection against aerosol challenge of B. pertussis. Single-cell transcriptomics studies on the lymph node of vaccinated mice at 1 day post-boost further characterized how co-administration of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP vaccine shapes immunity. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that co-administration of DTaP and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine generated populations of B and T cells with upregulated expression of interferon-stimulated genes, which were absent when vaccinating with DTaP alone. Altogether, these data suggest that administering DTaP alongside COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alters immune responses and provides increased protection from an aerosol challenge of B. pertussis compared to DTaP alone in mice.

articles.title: Correction to: Novel oblique dynamic chest radiography for retrocardiac pulmonary blood flow imaging in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
Correction to: Hypertension awareness, treatment, and control in coronary heart disease patients: results of the EUROASPIRE V survey conducted in 27 countries.
Cross-Level Responses of Freshwater Zooplankton to Micro/Nanoplastics: A Meta-Analysis Integrating Individual- to Community-Level Evidence.
articles.abstract: Despite the known threats of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) to freshwater ecosystems, their risks to zooplankton remain poorly resolved because existing evidence is fragmented across biological levels. Consequently, associations between lower-level responses and population- and community-level outcomes remain unclear. Here, we synthesized 3042 research cases from controlled experiments worldwide covering 12 response categories. We found significant overall negative effects of MNPs in systems without predators, with predators, and with predator-conditioned medium. Although molecular-level evidence remains limited, a consistent hierarchical response pattern emerged under predator-absent conditions. We therefore propose a conceptual hierarchical effect pathway (HEP) framework integrating effect sizes and cross-level associations. Within this framework, MNPs exposure was associated with increased ingestion of MNPs, physiological damage, feeding impairment, and reduced activity and defense. These responses formed an upstream tier associated with life-history impairments, including impaired growth and development, reduced reproductive capacity, and reduced survival, although these associations do not establish temporal ordering or causation. Under predator-present conditions, negative population- and community-level effects were also observed. Effect magnitudes also varied with MNPs characteristics, exposure duration, and zooplankton group. Together, the HEP framework clarifies cross-level associations and helps identify informative endpoints and incorporate food-web context into risk assessment of MNPs.

articles.title: Differential Risks of Incident Heart Failure Subtypes Associated with PM2.5 Chemical Constituents in China between 2006 and 2021.
articles.abstract: Despite substantial declines over the past decade, China's PM2.5 levels remain far above current WHO guidelines. PM2.5 is a recognized non-negligible risk factor for heart failure (HF), as a mixture, but the specific chemical constituents driving risks across HF subtypes remain unclear. Considering the significant heterogeneity in the etiology and pathophysiology among different HF subtypes, we explored the relationship between chemical constituents of PM2.5 and these HF subtypes. Additionally, we identified the most critical toxic constituent in the Kailuan prospective cohort of 101,521 Chinese adults followed from 2006 to 2021. Over a 14.83-year median follow-up, all chemical constituents of PM2.5 were associated with elevated risk across various HF subtypes, with notably stronger effects on early onset compared to late-onset HF. Moreover, black carbon (BC) (40.2%-48.7%) was the main contributor to overall HF, late-onset HF, and HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and mildly reduced (HFmrEF), whereas NH4+ (28.2%) and BC (28.1%) primarily drove early onset HF, and OM (34.8%) was the key constituent for HFpEF. Chronic exposure to specific-constituents of PM2.5 increases various HF subtypes risk, underscoring the importance for regional and constituent-specific regulations to alleviate HF burden.

articles.title: Nanotechnology-Integrated Diagnostic Platforms toward Decentralized Infectious Disease Management.
articles.abstract: Nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms are increasingly being developed across infectious disease management, from screening and diagnosis to potentially treatment-guiding assessment and monitoring. Yet current progress has rarely been synthesized from a clinical management perspective, making it difficult to determine which technologies are ready for decentralized use, where progress remains fragmented, and which clinical needs remain unmet. This review examines nanotechnology-enabled strategies according to how they enable the sample-to-answer workflow, rather than classifying them by material type. Major diagnostic platform architectures are then assessed in terms of practical implementation, with emphasis on platform-specific limitations and emerging solutions. Current applications are further mapped across the infectious disease management continuum to identify established capabilities, missing links, and disconnects from clinical workflows. The broader changes needed to close these gaps are also discussed. This review aims to clarify how nanotechnology-integrated diagnostic platforms can be better developed toward decentralized, reliable, and clinically actionable infectious disease management.

articles.title: Biologic Therapy in Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis with Class-based Comparisons.
articles.abstract: Pityriasis rubra pilaris is a rare inflammatory dermatosis with off-label biologic use. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261282142) of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase (Ovid) up to 9 January 2026. Observational evidence was analysed at the therapeutic-line level. The primary outcome was complete/near-complete response (PASI100, IGA/PGA 0-1 or mapped equivalents); the secondary outcome was any response. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions used a logit-scale generalized linear mixed model. Fourteen observational studies contributed 464 biologic therapeutic lines. The pooled any-response was 0.73 [95% Pityriasis rubra pilaris is a rare inflammatory dermatosis with off-label biologic use. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD420261282142) of PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase (Ovid) up to 9 January 2026. Observational evidence was analysed at the therapeutic-line level. The primary outcome was complete/near-complete response (PASI100, IGA/PGA 0-1 or mapped equivalents); the secondary outcome was any response. Random-effects meta-analyses of proportions used a logit-scale generalized linear mixed model. Fourteen observational studies contributed 464 biologic therapeutic lines. The pooled any-response was 0.73 [95% confidence interval 0.64-0.81] and the pooled complete/near-complete response was 0.36 (0.23-0.52). In class-stratified analyses, complete/near-complete response was 0.27 for tumour necrosis factor inhibitors (N=200), 0.21 for interleukin-17 inhibitors (n=84) and 0.55 for interleukin-23 pathway inhibitors (n=135), with no significant between-class difference (p=0.057). In an exploratory analysis, complete/near-complete response rates were 0.71 (95% confidence interval 0.46-0.88; n=28) for interleukin-12/23 inhibitors and 0.58 (0.24-0.86; n=12) for interleukin-23p19 inhibitors; small sample sizes and overlapping confidence intervals preclude conclusions on target-specific differences. Adverse events or adverse event-related treatment discontinuations were reported in 12/183 courses with available safety information. Three prospective single-arm studies (n=35) reported PASI90 at week 24-28; pooled PASI90 was 0.26 (0.14-0.42). Overall, biologics were associated with frequent clinical improvement, whereas complete/near-complete clearance was less common; comparative inference across classes remains limited by observational designs and small denominators.

articles.title: Clinical Trial Endpoints for Cryptococcosis: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education & Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: This European Confederation of Medical Mycology-Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium joint cryptococcosis working group presents a comprehensive review of clinical trials conducted since 1979. The working group offers consensus guidance for clinical trial endpoints, aiming to standardize, streamline, and enhance the clinical significance of trial design based on past practices. Consensus recommendations are provided for phase 3 trials of cryptococcal meningitis, including the use of 2-week mortality for the primary endpoint, with secondary endpoints including ≥ 10-week survival and rate of cryptococcal clearance from cerebrospinal fluid, incidence of relapse or paradoxical immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, and potential future exploratory composite endpoints or functional outcomes. Additionally, specific recommendations are offered for phase 2 trials prioritizing early fungicidal activity as a validated treatment response biomarker, unique considerations for trials in individuals without human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and design considerations for preemptive therapy in people with HIV and asymptomatic cryptococcal antigenemia. Furthermore, the working group proposes standardized eligibility criteria for clinical trials.

articles.title: Correction: Efficacy and Safety of a Telemedicine System in Patients With Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (TELEGLAM): Single-Center, 2-Arm, Randomized, Open-Label, Parallel-Group Study.
SGLT2 inhibitors: infection and bleeding risk after endourological prostate surgery.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the perioperative safety of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy in patients undergoing transurethral resection of the prostate (TUR-P) or holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia, with particular focus on infectious and bleeding-related complications.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study screened 258 patients undergoing TUR-P or HoLEP between January 2024 and March 2025. After exclusion of eight non-diabetic patients receiving SGLT2 inhibitors, 250 patients were included in the final analysis. Patients without diabetes mellitus served as controls (Group 1, n=150). Patients with diabetes mellitus were stratified into Group 2 (without SGLT2 inhibitors, n=50) and Group 3 (with SGLT2 inhibitors, n=50). Outcomes included postoperative urinary tract infections, bleeding-related complications, bladder tamponade, and postdischarge re-presentations within 30 days. Multivariate logistic regression analyses were adjusted for age, body mass index, age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, and duration of postoperative indwelling catheterization.

RESULTS: Group 3 had a significantly longer hospital stay (p=0.003) and longer postoperative catheterization duration (p=0.009). Overall complications and bladder tamponade occurred more frequently in Group 3 (p=0.003 and p<0.01), but there were no significant differences regarding the need for surgical revision. Rates of postoperative urinary tract infections did not differ between groups. Postdischarge bladder tamponade was more frequent in Group 3 (p=0.03). In multivariate analyses, SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was independently associated with bleeding-related outcomes, while postoperative catheterization duration was associated with inpatient complications, inpatient bladder tamponade, and inpatient urinary tract infection.

CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was not associated with increased infectious complications after TUR-P or HoLEP. An association with bleeding-related events was observed, but these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the retrospective design, limited event numbers, and wide confidence intervals in some adjusted analyses. These results support further investigation and individualized perioperative assessment of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

articles.title: Trial Endpoints for Endemic Mycoses: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endemic mycoses, caused by Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Emergomyces, Histoplasma, Paracoccidioides, Sporothrix, and Talaromyces marneffei, represent an important global health challenge. Expanding endemic regions, climatic change, improved diagnostics, increased disease awareness, and an increasing at-risk population have contributed to rising case numbers. These infections affect both immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts and exhibit marked clinical heterogeneity. Current treatment response guidance, established by the Mycoses Study Group and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer in 2008, are primarily tailored for invasive yeast and mold infections and are inadequate for endemic mycoses due to their complexity and heterogeneity.

METHODS: An international, multidisciplinary expert panel convened through the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology to develop consensus guidance for treatment response assessment in endemic mycoses. The process included a structured literature review, expert discussion, regulatory consultation, patient input, and public comment, culminating in consensus-based response criteria.

RESULTS: The proposed guidance response criteria encompass clinical, mycologic, and radiologic assessments.

CONCLUSIONS: The new criteria aim to improve the accuracy and standardize the assessment of treatment response, enabling comparison and pooling results across clinical trials while addressing the unique challenges posed by these diverse pathogens.

articles.title: Trial Endpoints for Candidemia and Invasive Candidiasis: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education & Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: Invasive candidiasis (IC) remains the most common invasive mycosis world-wide, responsible for a wide range of infections that can range from superficial mucosal infections to life-threatening systemic diseases. Clinical trials of antifungal agents for IC are pivotal to its management. Therapeutic responses in these trials are currently based on consensus criteria initially presented by the Mycoses Study Group (MSG) and the European Organization for Research and the Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) in 2008. These 2008 definitions originally described by Segal et al are still employed by both investigators and regulatory agencies when evaluating antifungal drug efficacy and patient outcomes. However, advances in clinical mycology, the change in epidemiology of Candida infections due to the increase in non-albicans Candida species, and the increase in newer antifungal agents currently under development require a revision of these criteria to ensure appropriate and standardized adjudication of patient outcomes and to accurately capture responses to newer therapeutic regimens and modern interventions. Therefore, the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) have decided to revise the criteria to be used for future studies.

articles.title: Revised Consensus Clinical Trial Response Criteria by the Mycoses Study Group Education & Research Consortium and European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract: Invasive fungal diseases remain a significant cause of patient morbidity and mortality. Improvement in clinical outcomes have been the result of progress in risk stratification, diagnostics, adjunctive care, antifungal therapy, and/or prophylaxis. Yet significant challenges remain, requiring the development of novel treatment strategies. Outcome evaluation in most mycology clinical trials is currently based on consensus criteria published in 2008. However, advances in diagnosis and management of various mycoses and the ever-expanding population of patients at risk necessitate a revision and refinement of these criteria. Appropriate categorization of antifungal treatment response is crucial in assessing the effects of new therapeutic interventions. An international expert panel nominated by the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) was convened to update the current outcome evaluation criteria. The panel achieved consensus on updated guidelines for assessing treatment responses and defining study outcomes in clinical trials of aspergillosis and other mold diseases, invasive candidiasis, cryptococcosis, and dimorphic fungi in both adults and children. This summary manuscript provides details on the methods, outlines key changes in the criteria, and discusses the next steps and areas for future research.

articles.title: Trial Endpoints for Aspergillus and Rare Molds: Consensus Recommendations by the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive mold disease (IMD) remains a substantial cause of patient morbidity and mortality. Aspergillosis and mucormycosis remain the predominant infections encountered, although rare molds continue to emerge as important pathogens. Improvement in patient outcomes has been the result of progress in risk stratification, diagnostics, supportive care, antifungal therapy, and/or prophylaxis, yet substantial challenges remain, requiring the development of novel treatment strategies. Clinical trials evaluating treatment response are currently based on consensus criteria published in 2008. However, advances in clinical mycology and the broadening variety of mold diseases in clinical trials necessitate a revision of these criteria to ensure that adjudication of patient outcomes accurately captures responses to therapeutic intervention.

METHODS: To tackle this task, an international expert panel nominated by the European Confederation of Medical Mycology (ECMM) and Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium (MSGERC) was convened.

RESULTS: The panel produced updated consensus guidance for assessing treatment responses and defining study outcomes in clinical trials of IMD in both adults and children.

CONCLUSIONS: Along with guidance, potential pitfalls in assessing outcome, such as discordant clinical, radiologic, and/or mycologic data and areas for future research are discussed.

articles.title: Epidemiology of the non-diabetic kidney diseases in chronic kidney disease. A nationwide study in Hungary.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The prevalence of non-diabetic primary kidney diseases (16% - 22%) appears overrated among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), however, precise epidemiological data are lacking. We determined the estimated incidence, prevalence and mortality of non-diabetic kidney diseases in Hungary.

METHODS: In this retrospective nationwide observational study, we analyzed data taken from the Hungarian National Health Insurance Fund database. We identified 15,897 patients with ICD-10 codes N00-N07 between January, 2021 and June, 2024, based on two identical ICD-10 codes with a minimum of 30-days and a maximum of 365-days apart. Age- and sex-specific incidence, prevalence, mortality rates, and regional distribution were calculated.

RESULTS: The incidence of non-diabetic kidney diseases was 1,423 patients/year, with a slight male dominance. The total number of prevalent patients with non-diabetic kidney diseases was 6,231 in 2023. The prevalence of non-diabetic kidney diseases in the general CKD population was estimated 0.4-0.5% in Hungary. Most patients had nephrotic syndrome (N04), the second most frequent disorder was chronic nephritic syndrome (N03), followed by persistent hematuria (N02), acute nephritic syndrome (N00). The largest proportion of affected patients was at 60-79 years of age, while mortality rates were highest among those over 80 years of age. Significant inequalities were noticed in the incidence, prevalence and death rates, showing a two-fold difference of counties with the highest and the lowest rates.

CONCLUSIONS: Non-diabetic kidney diseases occur far less frequently than diabetes- or hypertension-associated CKD. To our knowledge, descriptive data on the above topic have not yet been published.

articles.title: Evaluating and predicting independent gait recovery after stroke within the international classification of functioning, disability and health framework.
articles.abstract: Restoration of independent gait is one of the primary goals of rehabilitation care in patients after stroke and significantly influences their functional autonomy and quality of life. Gait impairments result from a complex interaction between structural damage to the central nervous system (CNS), disturbances in body functions, activity limitations, and the influence of environmental factors. This narrative review summarizes current approaches to the assessment and prediction of independent gait recovery within the framework of the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF). Clinical tests such as the Functional Ambulation Categories (FAC), the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE) for sensorimotor examination of the paretic lower limb, the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT) for gait speed, the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) for gait endurance, and the Trunk Control Test (TCT) for trunk function cover key ICF domains. These valid and reliable tools for evaluating gait also demonstrate substantial predictive value. According to internationally recognized consensus recommendations, a comprehensive assessment should additionally include tests evaluating stability and reactive postural control in standing and during gait, including the Mini-BESTest and the Dynamic Gait Index (DGI), when feasible. This standardized set of measures enables consistent evaluation of functional status in poststroke patients and supports its broader implementation in both clinical practice and research. Furthermore, structured prediction models that allow early patient stratification and improve the accuracy of estimating the likelihood of achieving functionally independent locomotion are increasingly used. The integration of clinical, imaging, and functional indicators within the ICFframework contributes to more precise neurological prognostication and supports individualized rehabilitation planning.

articles.title: Whole-exome sequencing reveals the neurogenetic spectrum of pediatric epilepsy in Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is a clinically and genetically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder, and diagnostic yield from next-generation sequencing varies substantially across cohorts and health-care settings. Population-specific data remain particularly limited for pediatric patients from underrepresented regions. In this retrospective two-center study, we evaluated 690 individuals with epilepsy onset at 18 years of age or younger who underwent whole-exome sequencing between January 2020 and April 2025. Patients with congenital infection, brain trauma, stroke, or perinatal asphyxia as the primary cause of epilepsy were excluded. Pathogenic or likely pathogenic findings were identified in 205 of 690 patients (29.7%). Single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) and insertions/deletions (indels) accounted for 195 patients (28.2%), whereas clinically relevant copy number variants accounted for 10 patients (1.4%). The cohort included 370 males (53.6%) and 320 females (46.4%). We identified 68 rare SNVs and indels, of which 48 were classified as novel because they were absent from ClinVar, gnomAD, and dbSNP and had not been reported in the published literature at the time of analysis. In addition, four variants with rs identifiers lacked ClinVar records and prior case-based publications, and 15 variants had previously been reported only once. Eleven copy number variants were detected in 10 patients; all but one were confirmed by orthogonal testing. Several findings were considered of particular neurogenetic interest, including variants in genes with synaptic or ion-channel relevance and rare recurrent findings that may broaden the recognized phenotypic spectrum of pediatric epilepsy. Overall, this study supports the clinical utility of whole-exome sequencing in pediatric epilepsy and provides population-specific neurogenetic data from Türkiye, while also highlighting a subset of rare findings that require replication and functional validation.

articles.title: Clinical and Radiological Improvement Following a Switch to Upadacitinib in Giant Cell Arteritis with Recurrent Ischemic Strokes During High-Dose Glucocorticoid and Tocilizumab Treatment: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is a systemic rheumatic disease that affects the large vessels. Although ischemic stroke is an uncommon complication of GCA, intracranial vasculitis may lead to recurrent strokes. An 81-year-old man presented with progressive gait disturbance. Physical examination revealed bilateral temporal artery tenderness with markedly diminished pulsation. His serum C-reactive protein level was elevated. Temporal artery ultrasonography demonstrated bilateral halo signs. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple acute strokes. Vessel wall imaging demonstrated circumferential wall thickening with contrast enhancement of the bilateral intracranial internal carotid and vertebral arteries. He fulfilled the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria for GCA. Treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone followed by high-dose glucocorticoid (GC) and weekly subcutaneous (SC) tocilizumab (TCZ) was initiated. However, recurrent ischemic strokes occurred early after treatment initiation, accompanied by progression of intracranial arterial stenosis. Therefore, TCZ was subsequently switched to upadacitinib (UPA) 15 mg/day. Following the switch to UPA, the serum C-reactive protein level normalized, no further ischemic strokes occurred, and follow-up contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrated resolution of vascular wall enhancement. This case describes clinical and radiological improvement observed following the switch to UPA in rapidly progressive GCA with intracranial involvement.

articles.title: Phage-Host Dynamics in Food Systems: Rethinking the "Lytic" and "Temperate" Paradigm.
articles.abstract: Phage-host dynamics are central to food systems because bacteriophages can threaten microbial stability while serving as tools for microbial control. In fermentations, phages compromise starter culture performance and product consistency, whereas in foods, animal production, and processing environments they are increasingly used as biocontrol agents against foodborne pathogens. Temperate phages may also influence virulence, tolerance, competition, and horizontal gene transfer, including antimicrobial resistance gene mobilization, placing phage ecology within a One Health framework. These roles have traditionally been interpreted through a binary model in which virulent phages lyse and temperate phages persist. However, reports of pseudolysogeny, carrier state, and delayed lysis have long suggested that this distinction is incomplete. Recent large-scale studies showing that virulent phages can persist through colony purification and bacterial genome assembly workflows provide the central motivation for this review. These findings suggest that long-term non-lysogenic association may be more widespread than appreciated and challenge the assumption that "lytic" phages necessarily cause immediate host elimination. In food systems, this has implications for fermentation reliability, biocontrol, surveillance, and One Health interpretation. We argue that food systems are informative settings for reassessing phage lifestyle categories, and that "lytic" should be understood as infection potential rather than guaranteed ecological outcome.

articles.title: Effects of Anti-Diabetic Drugs on Satellite Cell Function: A Mini Review.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
articles.abstract: Metformin, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium glucose cotransport 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are the most frequently prescribed medications for the treatment of diabetes. While the efficacy of these anti-diabetic drugs is clear, the underlying mechanisms of how they improve metabolism and produce other seemingly beneficial off-target effects are not clear. Several tissues including skeletal muscle have been implicated in the on-target and off-target actions of these drugs. Satellite cells are muscle stem cells that are important for skeletal muscle adaptation to stimuli such as exercise. In this mini-review, we present the emerging evidence exploring whether Metformin, GLP-1RA, SGLT2i modulate satellite cell function and if this is a relevant therapeutic target.

articles.title: Maternal adiponectin restores cholinergic vasodilation in mesenteric arteries from adult mice exposed to obesity in utero.
articles.abstract: Maternal obesity increases the risk of cardiovascular and metabolic disease in the offspring during childhood and adult life. Pregnant women and mice with obesity have lower circulating levels of adiponectin (ADN) than normal weight controls. ADN is an adipokine that regulates energy metabolism, vascular function, and placental function. We hypothesized that offspring of obese dams have impaired resistance artery vasodilation, which could be prevented by late-pregnancy normalization of circulating ADN concentrations. Adult female mice were fed either a control or obesogenic diet and mated with control diet-fed males. Control dams received a continuous infusion of phosphate saline buffer (PBS) during late pregnancy whereas obese females received either PBS or ADN. After weaning, offspring were fed a control diet. Mesenteric arteries (MsA) were dissected from adult offspring and mounted in a wire myograph. MsA responses to the vasoconstrictors phenylephrine or endothelin-1 were not different between groups. However, the vasodilatory responses to acetylcholine were reduced in offspring from obese dams as compared to control-fed dams. Furthermore, ADN supplementation during pregnancy restored the MsA cholinergic vasodilatory responses in offspring from obese dams. The reduced vasodilatory response to acetylcholine in MsA from offspring of obese dams was mediated by a decrease in prostaglandin signaling. Vasodilation induced by bradykinin or by activation of AMP-activated protein kinase did not differ with maternal obesity or ADN treatment, whereas vasodilation to sodium nitroprusside was reduced by ADN treatment. These observations suggest that normalizing circulating ADN in pregnancies with maternal obesity prevents in-utero programming of cholinergic dysfunction in the offspring.

articles.title: Machine learning-based proteomics analysis identified 23 protein biomarkers for enhanced risk prediction of myocardial infarction in Chinese and Europeans.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advances in proteomics assays enable measurement of thousands of plasma proteins, which could facilitate machine learning-based approaches to enhance risk prediction of disease.

METHODS: We measured plasma levels of >9500 proteins among 4000 Chinese adults (1937 myocardial infarction [MI] cases and 2026 subcohort), using both Olink Explore (2923 proteins) and SomaScan (6597 proteins) platforms. Protein-based risk prediction models were constructed, using conventional and machine learning approaches, with model performance assessed via discrimination (C-statistic), classification (net reclassification index; NRI) and calibration. Protein scores were compared and combined with conventional risk factors and polygenic scores (PGS), and externally validated in 37,187 Europeans (630 MI cases) in UK Biobank.

FINDINGS: Overall, 451 Olink and 530 SomaScan proteins were significantly associated (5% false discovery rate) with MI risk after adjustment for conventional risk factors. The protein prediction models based on Olink, SomaScan, or both platforms combined, outperformed conventional risk factors and PGS using discrimination, classification and calibration. The protein score using 23 Boruta-selected (Olink/SomaScan: 11/12) proteins yielded a 3.3-fold difference in 10-year cumulative incidence of MI between the top and bottom 20% risk groups (3.6 [95%CI: 3.1-4.1] vs 1.1 [0.9-1.2] per 100), compared with 2.5-fold (2.5 [2.2-2.9] vs 1.0 [0.9-1.2]) and 1.5-fold (1.9 [1.6-2.1] vs 1.3 [1.1-1.4]) differences for conventional and PGS, respectively. Adding this protein score to conventional risk factors increased C-statistics from 0.846 (0.829-0.862) to 0.864 (0.849-0.879), yielding an NRI of 72%. External validation in 37,187 participants in UK Biobank by adding 23 Boruta-selected proteins to conventional risk factors yielded comparable improvement in C-statistics for MI (from 0.710 [0.688-0.731] to 0.733 [0.710-0.756]) and 45% improvement in NRI (NRI 45%).

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning identified subsets of proteins for improved MI risk prediction beyond conventional risk factors and PGS, showing the potential for developing small panel proteomics assays to improve disease risk prediction.

articles.title: Benralizumab as Switch Therapy in Patients with Airway-Predominant Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.journal: Journal of investigational allergology & clinical immunology

articles.title: TyCHE enables time-resolved lineage tracing of B cells and other heterogeneously-evolving populations.
articles.abstract: Phylogenetic methods for cell lineage tracing have driven significant insights into organismal development, immune responses, and tumor evolution. While many methods estimate trees with branch lengths representing mutations, time-resolved lineage trees with branch lengths representing calendar time are more interpretable and could relate events like cellular migration and differentiation to perturbations like vaccines and drug treatments. However, in many evolving systems such as B cells, tumor lineages, and hypermutating bacterial populations, evolutionary rates often vary dramatically by genomic background or cell state, significantly biasing existing methods that build time trees using either a fixed molecular clock rate or uncorrelated relaxed clock models without a mechanistic model of molecular clock rate variation. We introduce TyCHE (Type-linked Clocks for Heterogeneous Evolution), a Bayesian phylogenetics package that infers time-resolved phylogenies of populations in which the molecular clock rate is linked to discrete states like genomic background or cell type. We demonstrate that TyCHE improves the accuracy of estimated time trees using a new simulation package SimBLE (Simulator of B cell Lineage Evolution). We use TyCHE to infer patterns of memory B cell differentiation during HIV infection, dynamics of recall germinal centers following influenza vaccination, evolution of a glioma tumor lineage, and progression of a bacterial lung infection, showing the applicability of our model to a wide range of systems and across different scales. TyCHE and SimBLE are available as open-source software packages compatible with the BEAST2 and Immcantation ecosystems.

articles.title: Netrin-3 attenuates metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease by activating the AMPK-PPARα axis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is characterized by hepatic steatosis and can progress to steatohepatitis. Netrin-3, an axon guidance protein linked to metabolic homeostasis, has not been characterized in MAFLD.

METHODS: MAFLD was induced in mice by high-fat diet. Netrin-3 and UNC5A expression was measured in serum and liver. Recombinant Netrin-3 was administered with or without Compound C. Hepatic AMPK/ACC phosphorylation, PPARα and target genes, lipid and glucose profiles, insulin, and liver injury were assessed. AML12 hepatocytes with fatty acid overload were treated with Netrin-3, Compound C, or AMPKα siRNA.

RESULTS: Netrin-3 and UNC5A were downregulated in MAFLD mice. Netrin-3 treatment reduced body weight, adiposity, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, ALT/AST levels, and hepatic steatosis. It increased AMPK and ACC phosphorylation and restored PPARα, Fabp1, and CPT1α expression. Compound C reversed these protective effects in vivo. In AML12 cells, Netrin-3 activated AMPK/ACC signaling, and this effect was abolished by Compound C and AMPKα siRNA.

CONCLUSIONS: Netrin-3 attenuates MAFLD progression by activating the hepatic AMPK-PPARα axis and promoting fatty acid oxidation, identifying Netrin-3 as a candidate therapeutic molecule for fatty liver disease.

articles.title: Timing of platelet-rich plasma administration in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has been widely investigated as a biologic adjunct in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (ARCR), yet clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. One potential source of variability is the timing of PRP administration, which may influence tendon-to-bone healing. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of PRP augmentation on structural healing and clinical outcomes following ARCR, with particular evaluation of outcomes according to the timing of PRP administration.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered on PROSPERO. PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL and Web of Science were searched through 19 February 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing PRP augmentation with control in adult patients undergoing ARCR were included. Trials were stratified by timing of PRP administration (intraoperative, post-operative-only or combined). The primary outcome was retears assessed by post-operative imaging at ≥6 months. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics.

RESULTS: Fifteen RCTs (1214 patients; 647 PRP and 567 control) met inclusion criteria. Overall, PRP administration at ≥6 months was associated with a reduced risk of retears (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.40-0.70; p < 0.001; I2 = 0%). Subgroup analysis demonstrated that intraoperative PRP significantly reduced retear rates at ≥6 months (RR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.35-0.68; p < 0.001; I2 = 0%) and ≥12 months (RR, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.30-0.91; p = 0.021; I2 = 0%). Post-operative-only PRP did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in retears (RR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.01-8.12; p = 0.54). Absolute risk reduction at ≥6 months was approximately 12%, corresponding to a number needed to treat of 8. Functional outcome scores improved in both PRP and control groups, with significant differences between groups in included studies, but pooled analyses did not demonstrate consistent between-group differences. PRP was not associated with increased complication rates.

CONCLUSION: Intraoperative PRP augmentation during ARCR is associated with a statistically significant reduction in retears. The limited post-operative-only PRP protocols do not demonstrate a comparable benefit and preclude a definitive conclusion that efficacy differs according to timing. These findings suggest a potential timing-dependent structural effect of PRP. However, structural improvements did not consistently translate into superior functional outcomes.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level I.

articles.title: Copper Oxide-Decorated Zinc Metal-Organic Framework as a Catalyst for Efficient Methanolysis of PET Plastic Waste.
articles.journal: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids
articles.abstract: Plastic upcycling into value-added chemicals is an important approach toward reducing environmental pollution and achieving a circular plastic economy. Herein, a CuO-loaded Zn-MOF (CuO@Zn-MOF) nanohybrid was synthesized and employed as an efficient heterogeneous catalyst for the methanolytic depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into dimethyl terephthalate (DMT). The structural and physicochemical properties of the CuO@Zn-MOF were characterized using ATR-IR, BET, TGA, PXRD, FESEM, HRTEM, EDAX, DLS, and XPS analyses, which confirms the successful incorporation of CuO within the porous Zn-MOF framework. The CuO@Zn-MOF nanohybrid exhibited excellent catalytic performance toward PET methanolysis, affording 93% DMT within 8 h under optimized reaction conditions (catalyst amount, 30 mg, and temperature, 160 °C) as confirmed by ATR-IR, 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, and GC-MS analysis. The enhanced catalytic activity of the nanohybrid was attributed to the cooperative role of CuO active sites and the porous Zn-MOF framework, which facilitates efficient substrate adsorption and catalytic transformation. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrated excellent structural stability and recyclability over multiple catalytic cycles, highlighting its potential as an efficient catalyst for PET plastic upcycling.

articles.title: Intracranial Complications of Orbital Cellulitis in Children.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract: This single-center retrospective cohort study of 355 children hospitalized with orbital cellulitis from 2007-2023 found that 6.2% developed intracranial complications, most commonly intracranial abscess and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. Adolescence, positive bacterial culture results, and growth of Streptococcus intermedius were associated with increased risk for central nervous system involvement.

articles.title: Molecular Residual Disease After Definitive Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Cancer: Clinical Value and Optimal Timing for ctDNA Assessment.
articles.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate post-treatment assessment after definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC) remains challenging due to limitations of standard imaging. We evaluated the diagnostic performance, prognostic value and optimal timing of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for molecular residual disease (MRD) detection.

METHODS: Seventy-four patients with LA-HNSCC treated with definitive CRT were prospectively enrolled. Plasma samples were collected before treatment, at 8 and 12 weeks after CRT, and during follow-up. ctDNA was analysed using a plasma-only methylation-based assay. Diagnostic performance for recurrence detection and associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated and compared with 12-week PET/CT findings.

RESULTS: Baseline ctDNA was detectable in 85.1% of patients. Among post-treatment timepoints, week-12 ctDNA showed the highest diagnostic accuracy for recurrence detection, with 69% sensitivity, 100% specificity, 100% positive predictive value, and 76% negative predictive value. Detectable week-12 ctDNA was associated with shorter PFS (HR, 6.44; 95% CI, 2.73-16.74; p<0.001) and OS (HR, 7.31; 95% CI, 2.80-22.31; p<0.001 ). Longitudinal ctDNA surveillance identified additional recurrences among patients with initially undetectable week-12 ctDNA. Exploratory analyses integrating PET/CT and ctDNA identified prognostically distinct PFS groups (log-rank P=0.033), with the greatest additional prognostic stratification observed among PET partial-responders.

CONCLUSIONS: Plasma-only methylation-based ctDNA provided high-specificity prognostic information after definitive CRT in LA-HNSCC, particularly at week 12 and in PET partial-responders. ctDNA may complement PET/CT for post-treatment risk stratification, but should not be used as a stand-alone test to exclude recurrence.

articles.title: Global overview and regional protocols for molecular diagnosis of human T-cell lymphotropic virus.
articles.abstract: Human T-cell lymphotropic virus type-1 (HTLV-1) has been recognized as an infection of global importance by the World Health Organization (WHO) in their published HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Global Health Sector Strategy 2022-2030; however, there are no commercial molecular assays for HTLV-1 available globally. While some countries are strengthening their efforts to diagnose HTLV-1 and prevent transmission (i.e., Brazil introduced universal antenatal screening in 2024), the prevalence of HTLV-1 in many parts of the world is unknown. Unsurprisingly, there is great inequity in access to molecular HTLV testing services, which can importantly contribute both as part of a diagnostic confirmatory testing algorithm and be used to monitor disease. Due to the lack of commercially available molecular assays, laboratories rely on in-house developed protocols, resulting in substantial variability in methodologies and access to testing. An HTLV Testing Working Group was established by the International Retrovirology Association in 2023 with the objective to improve access to and the quality of molecular testing for HTLV-1 globally. Representatives from nine laboratories in Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Iran, Japan, Sweden, and the United Kingdom have collaboratively compared their in-house molecular protocols. The methods are presented and summarized with a discussion of the relative strengths and limitations of each platform and key considerations for laboratories establishing molecular HTLV testing capacity. This analysis provides a practical framework supporting equitable expansion of HTLV molecular diagnostics globally, aiming to help countries with varying access to funding to be able to select the assay best suited to their means while recognizing the relative risks and benefits.

articles.title: Kappa prophage impacts Vibrio cholerae fitness and is restricted by the BREX phage defense system.
articles.abstract: Vibrio cholerae's pathogenicity largely stems from the acquisition of cholera toxin genes via lysogenic conversion mediated by the CTX prophage. However, the strong association of other prophages with epidemic strains has not been linked to lysogenic conversion. During the first wave of the seventh cholera pandemic, the Kappa prophage was commonly found in clinical isolates and was later shown to confer a competitive fitness advantage in the environment and to accelerate evolution by stimulating horizontal gene transfer; however, its role in virulence remains unknown. Here, we report that the Kappa prophage confers a competitive fitness advantage in vitro and during intestinal tract infection in both Wave 1 and Wave 3 strains. This competitive fitness advantage is due to phage predation on neighboring cells, and not to lysogenic conversion. Furthermore, we show that loss of Kappa coincides with the acquisition of novel phage defense systems from SXT integrative and conjugative elements VchBan9 and VchInd5. Phage defense systems BREX and AbiC inhibited Kappa predation and restricted horizontal gene transfer, thereby reducing Kappa's competitive fitness advantage.IMPORTANCEAs prophages are found in many bacterial genomes, understanding their roles in bacterial fitness advances our understanding of bacterial evolution and virulence drivers. The work presented here contributes to our understanding of the temperate phage-host arms race and highlights how the acquisition of phage defense systems can be a double-edged sword in Vibrio cholerae, protecting it from phage predation, yet limiting lysogenic conversion and evolution.

articles.title: Husbandry of a False Catshark, Pseudotriakis microdon (Elasmobranchii, Carcharhiniformes, Pseudotriakidae), Originating From a Depth of 1300 m.
articles.abstract: This study describes the maintenance of a rare deepwater shark, Pseudotriakis microdon (Elasmobranchii, Carcharhiniformes, Pseudotriakidae), accidentally caught by fishermen at a depth of 1300 m. To date, this collection depth is the deepest reported for captive elasmobranchs. Despite our husbandry efforts using a pressurized chamber at the Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium, the shark did not recover from the capture and transport damage and died after 23 days under human care. During this period, for the first time, we used urea-containing fluid with a salinity and osmotic pressure nearly equivalent to those of the shark blood plasma as environmental water to support shark osmoregulation, which was disrupted by capture and transport stresses. A hematological study further suggested that the fluid positively affected the osmotic status of the stressed shark, though this should be confirmed in further studies.

articles.title: Real-World Outcomes After Dupilumab Initiation for Pediatric Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps.
articles.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether dupilumab initiation is associated with reduced short-term flare burden, healthcare utilization, and surgical escalation in pediatric patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP).

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: TriNetX United States Collaborative Network.

METHODS: Patients aged ≤18 years with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps were identified between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Dupilumab-treated patients were indexed at treatment initiation and propensity score-matched 1:1 to nondupilumab controls indexed at a systemic corticosteroid burst based on asthma, atopic dermatitis, allergic rhinitis, and prior endoscopic sinus surgery. Outcomes within 12 months were compared using risk ratios.

RESULTS: In 442 matched patients (221 per cohort), dupilumab-treated patients had lower rates of acute sinusitis (12/221 [5.4%] vs 31/221 [14.0%]; risk ratio [RR] 0.39; 95% CI: 0.20-0.73; P = .002), systemic corticosteroid bursts (80/221 [36.2%] vs 101/221 [45.7%]; RR 0.79; 95% CI: 0.63-0.99; P = .042), and functional endoscopic sinus surgery (19/221 [8.6%] vs 38/221 [17.2%]; RR 0.50; 95% CI: 0.30-0.84; P = .007). Nasal polyp diagnoses were more frequently documented in the dupilumab-treated cohort (148/221 [67.0%] vs 95/221 [43.0%]; P < .0001), while emergency department visits (16/221 [7.2%] vs 27/221 [12.2%]; P = .078) and inpatient admissions (12/221 [5.4%] vs 16/221 [7.2%]; P = .435) were similar between cohorts.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that dupilumab may be a steroid-sparing and surgery-sparing option in pediatric CRSwNP.

articles.title: A chicken interferon-stimulated gene screen reveals limited genes restricting influenza virus replication.
articles.abstract: Avian influenza A virus (IAV) is a major global health threat. Not only does it cause significant economic losses to the agricultural industry, but it also presents a risk of spillover into the human population. However, several obstacles must be overcome for a successful cross-species transmission event to occur. One of these obstacles is the innate immunity of the host. While the innate immune response to IAV in humans has been well-studied, the innate immune response to IAV in birds is not as well understood. Here, we explore the interferon-induced immune response by identifying interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in chicken, quail, and duck cells, and find that they are largely species-specific. Using this data, we performed a CRISPR knockout ISG screen against two strains of IAV, the mouse-adapted PR8, and the low pathogenicity avian IAV isolate WF10. We find that for PR8, IFITM3 is the dominant restrictor of viral replication with several additional hits with modest effects, consistent with previous work in mammals. For avian WF10, IFITM3 was also a hit; however, there were two additional hits absent for PR8, the HSP70 co-chaperone protein BAG5 and the deubiquitinase OTUD4. Overall, these findings confirm the divergence of interferon-mediated immunity between species and establish a screening system that can be used to identify ISGs important for viral restriction in avian species.IMPORTANCEWild birds, especially waterfowl and shorebirds, are the primary natural reservoir for influenza A viruses. These birds can transmit IAV to domestic poultry, where the spillover risk to humans increases. Chickens are the most common species of domestic poultry worldwide and frequently infected with avian influenza viruses. Despite this, relatively little is known about how their immune system responds to influenza infection. This lack of knowledge creates a barrier to finding ways of preventing or mitigating IAV infection in chicken flocks. In this study, we characterized the interferon-induced immune response to IAV in chickens and found that only a small subset of ISGs were responsible for restricting IAV in chicken cells.

articles.title: Evaluating the Impact of Opioid and Glucocorticoid Use on Complications in Hallux Valgus Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study examined whether preoperative exposure to glucocorticoids, opioids, or their combination is associated with increased postoperative complications after hallux valgus (HV) surgery.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis of the TriNetX Research Network identified adults who underwent HV correction. Patients were grouped by preoperative glucocorticoid use, opioid use, combined use, or neither (control), with exposure assessed in 2 windows: 1-90 and 90-365 days preoperatively. Each of the 6 exposure-timeframe comparisons was separately propensity score matched on demographics and comorbidities. Significance was set at P < .01. Bonferroni correction for all 96 comparisons was additionally reported.

RESULTS: Combined glucocorticoid and opioid use was associated with sepsis at 1-90 days (P = .005) and with infection and stiffness at 90-365 days (P ≤ .007). Isolated opioid use was associated with infection in both windows, acute kidney injury at 1-90 days, and sepsis at 90-365 days. Isolated glucocorticoid use was associated with pneumonia and stiffness at 90-365 days. Absolute risk differences were small (0.7% to 2.0%; numbers needed to harm 49 to 141). Most outcomes, including thromboembolic, cardiovascular, and mortality outcomes, did not differ; only glucocorticoid-associated stiffness and pneumonia and opioid-associated acute kidney injury remained significant after Bonferroni correction.

CONCLUSION: In this retrospective database study, preoperative opioid and combined exposure were associated with small absolute increases in specific complications, most consistently infection; isolated glucocorticoid exposure was associated with pneumonia and stiffness, findings vulnerable to confounding by indication. Because dose, duration, and patient-level co-occurrence of outcomes were unavailable and residual confounding is likely, these findings are hypothesis generating.

articles.title: Anterior Cervical Diskectomy and Fusion Complicated by Salmonella Infection: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior cervical diskectomy and fusion (ACDF) is a commonly performed spinal procedure with low rates of postoperative infection. Reported infections are typically caused by skin or nosocomial flora, such as Staphylococcus species. Salmonella has been reported rarely after posterior cervical and lumbar spinal procedures but has not been described following an anterior cervical approach.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We report a 35-year-old immunocompetent woman who developed a prevertebral abscess on postoperative day 15 following C5-C7 ACDF performed after a traumatic cervical spine injury was sustained abroad. She presented with incision site erythema, swelling, and purulent drainage but remained afebrile with a normal white blood cell count. Imaging demonstrated a rim-enhancing prevertebral fluid collection from C5-C7. She underwent irrigation and debridement with retention of instrumentation. Cultures obtained from purulent fluid overlying the anterior plate grew Salmonella group D and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus. Blood and stool cultures were negative.

RESULTS: On structured literature search, this represents the first reported Salmonella infection following ACDF or any anterior cervical approach, and the first presenting as a prevertebral abscess. Recent travel and environmental exposure, with probable hematogenous seeding of a recently operated site, may have contributed. Infection occurred without systemic symptoms, underscoring the importance of clinical suspicion despite normal laboratory values.

CONCLUSION: Salmonella should be considered a rare potential pathogen in postoperative spinal infection, particularly with relevant exposure history.

articles.title: Surgical Site Infection After Posterolateral Lumbar Fusion: Incidence and Risk Factors in a Nationwide Database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Posterolateral lumbar fusion (PLF) is a widely performed procedure for degenerative lumbar spine disease, yet postoperative surgical site infection (SSI) remains a consequential complication. The aim of this study was to estimate the national 90-day incidence of SSI following PLF and identify independent predictors of 90-day SSI.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of adults undergoing PLF in the PearlDiver Mariner database from 2016 to 2023. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of 90-day SSI, adjusting for demographic, procedural, and comorbidity variables. Significance was set at P < .001.

RESULTS: Among 291,435 PLF procedures, 14,725 (5.1%) developed a 90-day SSI. SSI occurred in 4.0% (6,105/151,951) of single-level PLF cases and 6.2% (8,620/139,484) of multilevel cases. Multilevel fusion significantly increased infection risk compared with single-level PLF (odds ratio [OR] 1.47, P < .001). Independent predictors included obesity (OR 1.60, P < .001), anemia (OR 1.70, P < .001), fluid and electrolyte disorders (OR 1.59, P < .001), essential hypertension (OR 1.34, P < .001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.22, P < .001), depression (OR 1.21, P < .001), diabetes (OR 1.15, P < .001), cardiac arrhythmias (OR 1.21, P < .001), coagulopathy/hemorrhagic disorders (OR 1.18, P < .001), substance-related disorders (OR 1.18, P < .001), peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.17, P < .001), and tobacco use (OR 1.11, P < .001).

CONCLUSION: Ninety-day SSI after PLF was more frequent following multilevel fusion and among patients with substantial cardiometabolic, hematologic, and behavioral comorbidities.

articles.title: Exploring Sunburns and Sun Protection-Related Habits, Attitudes and Knowledge in a Medical Sciences University Community in Cuba.
articles.journal: American journal of health promotion : AJHP
articles.abstract: PurposeTo investigate the prevalence of sunburn and its social and behavioral determinants in a Cuban medical sciences university community, and to identify key insights for the design of future health promotion strategies and policies.DesignDescriptive cross-sectional study.SettingA Cuban Medical Sciences University community.SampleA total of 778 participants were included: 683 students (87.8%) and 95 teachers (12.2%).MeasuresSun-related habits, attitudes, knowledge, and sunburn prevalence were assessed using the validated CHACES questionnaire.AnalysisDescriptive statistics were used to summarize the data. Comparative analyses between students and teachers were conducted. Additionally, a multivariable logistic regression model was constructed, with sunburn occurrence in the previous year as outcome variable.ResultsStudents demonstrated deficient photoprotection behaviors, with ≤56.5% frequently using recommended measures. Teachers reported higher use of sunglasses (62.1%) and shade (69.5%). Both groups exhibited favorable attitudes toward sun protection, while knowledge levels were modest (teachers: 6.7±1.1; students: 6.2±1.3; P < 0.001). Nevertheless, a high proportion reported at least one sunburn in the previous year (58.1% students, 51.6% teachers).ConclusionThese findings emphasize the need for targeted, policy- and training-based interventions to improve sun protection practices. As current and future health professionals and educators, improving their behaviors is critical, as it may generate a ripple effect on the broader population.

articles.title: Impact of 22 Comorbidities on Number of Hospitalizations and Emergency Department Visits in U.S. Community-Dwelling Older Adults With Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (AD/ADRD).
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: ObjectivesExamine the impact of 22 comorbidities on number of hospitalizations and Emergency Department (ED) visits among community-dwelling persons with Alzheimer's Disease and Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias (AD/ADRD).MethodsAnalyzed 2018-2019 Medicare Claims data for 7.1 million beneficiaries aged ≥65 with AD/ADRD. Each comorbidity's impact was assessed using net effect (NE), a measure of attributable risk for multiple interacting factors.ResultsPneumonia showed the highest contribution to all-cause hospitalizations (NE = 1.58), indicating that pneumonia contributed 1.58 all-cause hospitalizations per year. Acute myocardial infarction had an NE of 1.37; hip fracture, 1.20; anemia, 0.89; and stroke, 0.78. Stroke had the highest contribution to all-cause ED visits (NE = 0.477), followed by arthritis (0.421), pneumonia (0.400), depression (0.394), hypertension (0.325), and hip fracture (0.323).ConclusionOur results highlight a large discrepancy in how the various comorbidities of AD/ADRD impact healthcare utilizations. Certain conditions, particularly pneumonia and arthritis, may be key targets for reducing hospitalizations and ED visits.

articles.title: Programming Photodynamic Therapy with Glycopolymeric Photosensitizers: From Carbohydrate Recognition to Light-Activated Nanomedicine.
articles.abstract: Glycopolymers are synthetic macromolecules that display multiple carbohydrate motifs and mimic the multivalent presentation of glycans in biological systems. Advances in controlled polymerization now allow chain length, sugar density, sequence, composition, and topology to be tuned with increasing precision. As a result, glycopolymers have progressed from models of carbohydrate-lectin recognition to materials for receptor- and transporter-mediated targeting, drug delivery, and precision therapy. Studies of fructose-containing micelles showed that cellular interactions depend not only on sugar identity or total sugar content but also on chain length, local density, spatial arrangement, and carbohydrate accessibility. These principles were then applied to drug delivery, where polymer composition and self-assembly improved the aqueous encapsulation of poorly soluble drugs, regulated nanoparticle size, and promoted intracellular distribution. Glycopolymers therefore became functional materials that control both biological recognition and the organization of therapeutic molecules.
