Glycopolymeric photosensitizers extend this concept to photodynamic therapy (PDT), in which photosensitizers convert light into localized photochemical effects. Porphyrins are attractive because of their optical properties and ability to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), but their use is limited by poor aqueous dispersibility, aggregation, nonspecific uptake, altered photochemical activity, and inadequate intracellular localization. Photosensitizer delivery is therefore not simply a solubilization problem; it requires coordinated control over molecular organization, biological targeting, and intracellular transport. Glycopolymers can address these challenges through physical loading or covalent incorporation. Physical loading is simple and adaptable but may provide limited control over loading and retention, whereas covalent attachment allows more precise regulation of photosensitizer content and placement. To combine photosensitizer organization with carbohydrate-mediated targeting, we developed several covalent glycopolymeric photosensitizers. Porphyrin-containing random and block glycopolymers revealed how polymer sequence influences aggregation, intracellular ROS generation, and photocytotoxicity. Porphyrin-core star glycopolymers further showed that arm length, carbohydrate identity, and corona composition affect recognition, uptake, and PDT response, while related systems enabled combined therapeutic functions. Their synthesis also evolved from conventional ATRP, which requires added catalytic systems and does not directly link photosensitizer function with polymer formation, toward light-mediated polymerization. In photoATRP, we developed a triple-function zinc porphyrin that serves as initiator, photocatalytic component, and photosensitizer. A complementary self-photocatalyzed PET-RAFT strategy used a polymerizable porphyrin that participates in polymerization and becomes covalently embedded in the glycopolymer. This Account traces the evolution of glycopolymers from multivalent recognition to targeted drug delivery and glycopolymeric photosensitizers. Here, "programming" refers to the deliberate design of molecular architecture, the control of nanoscale assembly, and the integration of polymer synthesis with photosensitizer function. It emphasizes how carbohydrate presentation, polymer architecture, self-assembly, and photochemistry jointly govern recognition, intracellular transport, and therapeutic performance and how integrating polymer synthesis, targeting, and photosensitization may guide next-generation precision phototherapeutics.

articles.title: Yeast culture extract of grape seed meal attenuates ETEC K88-induced inflammation in host by modulating AHL-like quorum-sensing signaling molecules.
articles.abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is a primary pathogen inducing diarrhea in young animals. ETEC colonization and proliferation rely on quorum sensing (QS), predominantly mediated by N-acyl homoserine lactone (AHL) signal molecules. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether yeast culture extracts relieve intestinal inflammation via interfering with ETEC QS systems. This study aimed to investigate whether grape seed meal-derived Saccharomyces cerevisiae culture (GSMSC) mitigates inflammatory responses in ETEC K88-challenged BALB/c mice through regulating AHL-type QS signaling. GSMSC substantially alleviated ETEC K88-triggered intestinal injury, inflammatory reaction, and intestinal barrier impairment in mice. Mechanistically, GSMSC suppressed intestinal inflammation and oxidative stress by modulating fecal butyric acid, AHL, and 3-oxo-C12-HSL concentrations, reshaping the relative abundance of Odoribacter, and regulating the production of methyl (9E)-9-hexadecenoate. Collectively, these correlational findings highlight AHL-like QS molecules as a potential biomarker and regulatory target associated with the colonization and growth of ETEC K88 in the host.IMPORTANCEEnterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is a primary cause of diarrhea in young animals, and its intestinal colonization depends on N-acyl homoserine lactone (AHL)-mediated quorum sensing (QS). However, few effective natural agents targeting QS have been identified to alleviate ETEC-triggered intestinal inflammation. This study demonstrated that grape seed meal-derived Saccharomyces cerevisiae culture extracts (GSMSCs) mitigate intestinal injury, inflammatory response, and barrier dysfunction in ETEC K88-infected mice via modulating QS signals, gut microbiota, and microbial metabolites. These correlational findings suggest that AHL-type QS may represent a promising regulatory target to mitigate ETEC infection, and hint at a potential natural quorum-quenching strategy for alleviating pathogen-triggered intestinal inflammation.

articles.title: Perinatal influences on the gut resistome and bacteriome in South African infants from birth to 6 months of life: insights from a shotgun metagenomics study.
articles.abstract: Antibiotic resistance (AR) is a major global health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where neonatal infections remain a leading cause of death, compounded by limited surveillance and uncontrolled antibiotic use. The neonatal gut is a reservoir for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet LMIC data remain scarce. Using shotgun metagenomics, we investigated gut resistome and bacteriome dynamics in infants during their first 6 months of life. Analysis of 68 longitudinal fecal samples from 17 infants revealed 211 ARGs across 7 antibiotic classes. Beta-lactam genes (blaTEM-1 and blaTEM-10-MGH-1) dominated, accounting for 64.0% of detections and indicating substantial early-life resistance load. Non-blaTEM ARGs (e.g., cat4, tetC, aphA2) emerged between 16 and 26 weeks, reflecting ongoing microbial evolution. In this small, exploratory cohort, infant antibiotic exposure, maternal HIV with highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART), and cesarean delivery with maternal antibiotics were associated with higher ARG diversity; given the small, uneven subgroups, this pattern is hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive, suggesting a role for clinical and maternal factors in resistome development. The bacteriome featured diverse, resilient taxa with persistent opportunistic pathogens, including Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus aureus, which are potential ARG reservoirs. Despite sample size limitations, these findings offer valuable insight into neonatal ARG acquisition, persistence, and bacterial profiles in an LMIC setting, and point to a plausible, multifactorial interplay of maternal, clinical, and environmental influences on resistome dynamics requiring confirmation in larger cohorts. This early, pervasive resistance reservoir supports tailored antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention, and microbiome-informed strategies, alongside future genotypic-phenotypic surveillance.IMPORTANCEThis study provides region-specific insight into the early-life gut resistome and bacteriome of infants from a low- and middle-income setting, addressing a gap in global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance. Universal detection of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) from birth highlights the establishment of a genetic resistance reservoir, even in antibiotic-naïve populations. In this small, exploratory cohort, perinatal factors, including antibiotic exposure, maternal HIV/HAART status, and delivery mode, showed patterns associated with resistome diversity and microbial succession. Although not statistically definitive, these findings suggest multifactorial drivers of early AMR emergence warranting confirmation in larger studies. Persistence of clinically important ARGs alongside opportunistic pathogens raises questions for neonatal infection management; however, these genotypic findings indicate potential rather than confirmed resistance, underscoring the need for paired phenotypic susceptibility data. This work establishes foundational longitudinal data for South Africa, informing antimicrobial stewardship, infection prevention, and microbiome-informed interventions to mitigate AMR risk and improve infant health outcomes.

articles.title: Niche-specific transcriptional responses of Staphylococcus epidermidis during host colonization and infection.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a ubiquitous skin commensal but can act as an opportunistic pathogen causing foreign body-associated infections, including prosthetic joint infections (PJIs). The molecular mechanisms underlying this commensal-to-pathogen transition remain poorly understood. To investigate niche-specific transcriptional adaptations, RNA was isolated from nasal swabs and synovial fluid samples collected from patients with PJIs. Comparative quantitative real-time PCR was used to assess S. epidermidis gene expression in nasal samples, representing the colonizing niche, and synovial fluid, representing the infectious niche. Paired nasal and synovial fluid samples from individual patients were analyzed where available. The analysis focused on genes associated with virulence, adhesion, immune evasion, and metabolism. Three distinct expression profiles were identified: (i) a core profile, comprising genes with consistent expression in both niches, including immune evasion factors (capC, dltA, and mprF) and the adhesin sdrG; (ii) a niche-specific profile, comprising genes whose expression differed between niches, including increased expression of sdrH and the major autolysin atlE in synovial fluid; and (iii) a variable profile, comprising genes with heterogeneous expression patterns across patients, suggestive of strain- or patient-specific adaptation. Notably, central metabolic genes (fumC, gltA, and icd), together with agrC and its downstream target psmβ1, showed pronounced downregulation in synovial fluid. These findings provide direct ex vivo evidence for site-specific S. epidermidis gene expression during human colonization and PJI. They reveal distinct transcriptional patterns associated with adaptation to the colonizing and infectious environments and provide a basis for further investigation of potential targets for infection prevention and treatment.IMPORTANCEStaphylococcus epidermidis normally lives harmlessly on human skin but is also a major cause of infections involving prosthetic joints and other implanted medical devices. How this common bacterium adapts from colonization to persistent infection remains poorly understood. We compared S. epidermidis gene expression in nasal swabs, representing colonization, with that in synovial fluid from patients with prosthetic joint infections, representing the infectious niche. This patient-based comparison revealed distinct patterns of bacterial gene activity: some genes were consistently expressed in both niches, whereas others showed niche-specific changes. Infection was associated with increased expression of genes involved in bacterial attachment and adaptation, together with reduced activity of genes linked to metabolism. These findings provide direct evidence that S. epidermidis adapts its behavior to the host environment during infection and identify bacterial processes that may contribute to the transition from commensalism to pathogenicity.

articles.title: An engineered Zika virus recombinant adenovirus vaccine induces protective immune response in mice.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in many countries/territories. Our previous publication reported that the antibodies (Abs) induced by ZIKV infection could exacerbate the mortality of JEV-infected mice, bringing challenges to the development of traditional Zika vaccines. Here, we developed two recombinant adenoviruses (Ad5-ZIKV-EWT and Ad5-ZIKV-Emut) encoding the ZIKV wild-type E protein and an E protein mutant carrying five amino acid substitutions (replaced by alanine) in the bc loop and fusion loop regions of the E protein, respectively. The levels of JEV-cross-reactive or DENV-cross-reactive Ab responses induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut immunization in mice are lower than those induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The level of ZIKV-neutralizing Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is comparable to that elicited by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The ability of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut to enhance JEV or DENV infections in vitro is attenuated as compared with that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. The in vivo protective role of Abs induced by Ad5-ZIKV-Emut is similar to that induced by Ad5-ZIKV-EWT. Mice receiving Ad5-ZIKV-EWT-immune mouse sera exhibited antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) post-DENV challenge, whereas passively transferred Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immune mouse sera did not lead to obvious ADE of DENV infection in recipient mice. Notably, maternally acquired Abs did not enhance the mortality of 2-day-old neonates born to Ad5-ZIKV-Emut-immunized mice post-JEV challenge. These results suggest that optimizing the E protein amino acid sequence of ZIKV could significantly reduce the level of cross-reactive Abs to JEV and DENV, and abrogate the ADE of JEV and DENV infections, providing a promising strategy to develop an effective and safe ZIKV vaccine.

IMPORTANCE: Zika virus (ZIKV), Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), and dengue virus (DENV) co-circulate in some countries or territories. The results of preliminary animal experiments and clinical cohort studies support that antibodies induced by ZIKV infection can enhance JEV or DENV infection in vitro and in vivo. Therefore, the ZIKV vaccine encoding the wild-type E protein constructed by conventional methods has the antibody-dependent enhancement risk against JEV and DENV infections. In this study, we obtained an E protein mutant by mutating key amino acids in the bc loop and FL sequences of the ZIKV wild-type E protein to alanine. The recombinant adenovirus vaccine based on this E protein mutant is not only effective but also safer in preventing ZIKV infection in the future.

articles.title: Pulmonary rehabilitation following exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Guidelines have provided positive recommendations for pulmonary rehabilitation after severe exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but results are heterogeneous and new randomised controlled trials (RCTs) continue to be published.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation after COPD exacerbations on hospital admissions (critical outcome) and other important and patient-centred outcomes (mortality, health-related quality of life (HRQL) and exercise capacity).

SEARCH METHODS: We identified studies through searches of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE ALL, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP). Searches were current to 2 June 2026.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: RCTs comparing pulmonary rehabilitation of any duration (at least exercise training but no minimum number of exercise sessions) after exacerbation of COPD versus usual care were eligible. Usual care groups received conventional community care without rehabilitation.

OUTCOMES: The four main outcomes were hospital readmissions, mortality, HRQL and exercise capacity.

RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias in the included RCTs as high, low or unclear, using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We expected substantial heterogeneity across trials due to the diversity of rehabilitation programmes (i.e. number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision of exercise training; and patient education), duration of follow-up (under three months versus three months or longer) and risk of bias (random sequence generation, allocation concealment and blinding). Therefore, we conducted prespecified subgroup analyses. We used random-effects models and standard Cochrane methods for this update, and assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE.

INCLUDED STUDIES: For this update, we added 20 studies and included a total of 40 studies (2825 participants).

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Rehabilitation programmes showed great diversity in terms of exercise training (number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision), patient education (from none to extensive self-management programmes) and how they were organised (within one setting, e.g. pulmonary rehabilitation, to across several settings, e.g. hospital, outpatient centre and home). In 12 studies, participants completed extensive pulmonary rehabilitation, and in 25 studies, participants completed pulmonary rehabilitation ranging from not extensive to moderately extensive. We could not determine how extensive the programmes were in three studies, owing to missing information. Thirteen studies (1229 participants) contributed data on hospital readmissions, with follow-up ranging from three months to 18 months. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation likely reduces the risk of hospital readmission when compared with usual care (pooled odds ratio (OR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.32 to 0.84; I2 = 69%). Twenty-two studies (1677 participants) contributed data on all-cause mortality, but only 11 trials (1196 participants) were included in the pooled effect estimate because the remaining studies reported no deaths in either group. Follow-up in these studies ranged from the duration of the hospital stay to 48 months. Low-certainty evidence suggests that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation may reduce all-cause mortality slightly when compared with usual care (pooled OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.49 to 1.43; I2 = 33%). Twelve studies (1118 participants) used the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) to assess HRQL, with follow-up ranging from the duration of the hospital stay to 12 months. High-certainty evidence indicates that, when compared with usual care, pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in HRQL, as measured by the SGRQ total score (mean difference (MD) -9.05, 95% CI -12.60 to -5.50; I2 = 70%), exceeding the minimal important difference (MID) of four points. There was evidence of a difference between pulmonary rehabilitation and usual care for the SGRQ activity and impacts domains (effects exceeding the MID), but no evidence of a difference for the symptoms domain. Twenty-two studies (1464 participants) used the six-minute walk distance (6MWD) to assess exercise capacity, with follow-up ranging from four days to 208 weeks. High-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in 6MWD when compared with usual care (MD 57.79 m, 95% CI 41.68 to 73.91; I2 = 89%). Heterogeneity appeared to be driven mainly by differences between studies showing very large effects and those showing smaller effects but still evidence of between-group differences. The overall results of this review have not changed to an important extent compared with results reported in the previous version of this review. Overall, the risk of bias was judged to be low or unclear across most domains. However, the lack of participant blinding raised concerns for subjectively reported outcomes (HRQL). High risks of selection bias and attrition bias were identified in a small number of studies, while a larger proportion of studies were at high risk for reporting bias. Egger's test indicated evidence of funnel plot asymmetry for hospital readmission (P = 0.02) and mortality (P = 0.02), but not for SGRQ (P = 0.45) or the six-minute walk test (P = 0.12). Visual inspection suggested that the asymmetry was more consistent with small-study effects than with clear evidence of missing negative studies.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation likely reduces hospital readmissions, while evidence for mortality is of low certainty. However, some recent studies showed no benefit of rehabilitation on hospital readmissions and mortality. Such heterogeneity of effects on hospital readmissions and mortality may be explained to some extent by the extensiveness of rehabilitation programmes and by the methodological quality of the included studies. High-certainty evidence shows moderate to large effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on HRQL and exercise capacity in people with COPD after an exacerbation. While additional RCTs comparing rehabilitation to no rehabilitation seem questionable scientifically and ethically, future research must investigate how rehabilitation programmes can be designed and implemented to be feasible, cost-effective and attractive and accessible for patients and healthcare providers in the long term. Research must also investigate how the organisation of such programmes within specific healthcare systems determines their effects after COPD exacerbations on hospital readmissions and mortality.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol (2005) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305 Original review (2009) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub2 Review update (2011) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub3 Review update (2016) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub4.

articles.title: Complications of total hip arthroplasty in patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder, with the hip being the most commonly involved joint. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is the mainstay of treatment for degenerative arthritis of the hip. The purpose of the present study was to utilise a meta-analysis of the literature to investigate whether there is any difference in the incidence of complications after THA between patients with and without AS. Our hypothesis was that postoperative dislocation, periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), periprosthetic fracture and blood transfusion rates are similar for both ankylotic patients and patients without AS.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus and Cochrane Controlled Register of Trials (CENTRAL) databases were searched for studies directly comparing directly postoperative dislocation, PJI, periprosthetic fracture and transfusion rates in THA, for patients with and without AS, between 01.01.2000 and 01.01.2025. The PRISMA guidelines were used to ensure transparent, complete, and accurate reporting of our meta-analysis. The quality of studies was assessed using the MINORS criteria. The random effects model was used for the meta-analysis.

RESULTS: The initial search resulted in 864 papers. 95 duplicate articles were removed. Of the remaining articles, 4 were compatible with our inclusion criteria and were included in our study. The overall odds ratio (OR) of THA dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, PJI and blood transfusion in ankylotic patients compared to non-ankylotic patients was 1.63 (95% CI, 1.28-2.09; p < 0.001), 1.62 (95% CI, 1.34-1.96; p < 0.001), 2.35 (95% CI, 1.39-3.95; p < 0.001) and 1.27 (95% CI, 0.79-2.05; p = 0.33) respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that ankylotic patients have a higher incidence of postoperative THA dislocation, periprosthetic fracture and PJI as opposed to non-ankylotic patients. No statistically significant difference was found regarding postoperative blood transfusion rate.

PROSPERO ID: Our study was registered on the PROSPERO platform and published online under the ID: CRD420250646593.

articles.title: Prophylactic granulopoiesis-stimulating factors for people with solid tumors undergoing cancer treatment.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Many chemotherapy agents used in the treatment of solid tumors can induce myelosuppression, resulting in hematologic toxicities such as neutropenia and febrile neutropenia (FN), which are major causes of treatment-related morbidity and mortality. Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) are well-established stimulators of myelopoiesis and hematopoietic stem cell mobilization. Although previous reviews have suggested improved overall survival among individuals receiving intensified chemotherapy supported by primary G-CSF, it remains unclear whether prophylactic administration of G-CSF or GM-CSF itself improves overall survival, freedom from treatment failure (FFTF), or FN-associated complications when compared with placebo or no prophylaxis under the condition of identical treatment regimens.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the efficacy of prophylactic granulopoiesis-stimulating factors compared with placebo or no prophylaxis on survival outcomes and preventing adverse effects of cancer treatment in people with solid tumors.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, and Embase and ongoing trials registers, together with reference checking, in June 2025. There were no restrictions on language or publication status.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing primary granulopoiesis-stimulating factors with placebo or no prophylaxis in participants aged 18 years and older with solid tumors.

OUTCOMES: Our outcomes were overall survival, FFTF, risk of infection, quality of life, all-cause mortality during chemotherapy, risk of bone pain, and duration of hospitalization.

RISK OF BIAS: We used Cochrane's RoB 1 tool to assess risk of bias in the included studies.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesized results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible. We assessed statistical heterogeneity between studies using a Chi2 test and I2 values. We used hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for time-to-event data and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs for dichotomous outcomes. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 26 RCTs with a total of 5320 participants.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: We assessed two trials as having a high risk of bias, and the remaining studies as having a low or unclear risk of bias. Primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared with control likely results in a reduction in risk of infection (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.49 to 0.83; P = 0.001; 7 studies, 915 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), but may result in little to no difference in overall survival (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.28 to 2.54; P = 0.59; 3 studies, 537 participants; low-certainty evidence) and FFTF (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63 to 1.25; P = 0.50; 1 study, 259 participants; low-certainty evidence). Primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared with control likely results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality during chemotherapy (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.53 to 1.60; P = 0.75; 11 studies, 3001 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Regarding adverse events, primary prophylaxis G-CSF compared with control probably results in a large increase in risk of bone pain (RR 3.55, 95% CI 1.09 to 11.56; P = 0.04; 10 studies, 3152 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), a clinically important adverse outcome. One study reported that participants in the GM-CSF group had a significantly longer mean hospitalization duration (9.7 days versus 5.2 days, P < 0.01). Quality of life was not reported in any of the included studies.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: There is moderate-certainty evidence that primary prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF likely reduces risk of infection versus control. In contrast, low- to moderate-certainty evidence suggests little to no improvement in overall survival and FFTF, and likely little to no difference between groups in all-cause mortality during chemotherapy. Regarding adverse events, moderate-certainty evidence shows a likely large increase in risk of bone pain. Data on the effects of prophylaxis G-CSF or GM-CSF compared to control on duration of hospitalization were inadequate to draw any conclusions, and no studies evaluated quality of life. We identified no new ongoing studies, and the number of recent publications is limited. Further research in this field is warranted.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review was funded by the "Innovation Star" project of outstanding graduate students in Gansu Province (2023CXZX-142), China.

REGISTRATION: Protocol was available via 10.1002/14651858.CD015656.

articles.title: Interventions for women with endometrioma prior to assisted reproductive technology.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: The link between endometriosis and infertility has been firmly established; however, the mechanism remains controversial. Management of ovarian endometriosis (endometrioma) in the context of assisted reproductive technology (ART) varies greatly both in regard to the intervention chosen or, indeed, the decision to treat at all. Management remains a key clinical decision for patients requiring fertility treatment and guidance from scientific evidence is vital. This is an update of a Cochrane review first published in 2010.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of surgery, medical treatment, combination therapy (both medical and surgical) or no treatment for improving reproductive outcomes among women with endometrioma, prior to undergoing ART cycles.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group's specialised register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and PsycINFO on 7 October 2025. We also searched trial registries, checked reference lists of relevant studies and contacted experts in the field for any additional trials.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We selected randomised controlled trials (RCTs) that compared any medical and/or surgical intervention with another medical and/or surgical intervention or placebo/no intervention for the treatment of endometrioma prior to ART. The included population was women with endometrioma diagnosed by laparoscopy or pelvic imaging such as ultrasound, computed tomography (CT), or magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI).

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes of interest, as presented in the summary of findings tables, were: live birth and adverse events.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 1 tool to assess bias in the included studies.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: Due to significant heterogeneity between the included studies, we synthesised the results into a narrative review. We summarised key findings from individual studies descriptively and we structured them by outcome domain. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for the critical outcomes.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included a total of seven parallel-arm RCTs with 646 participants randomised. Two studies (173 participants) evaluated medical interventions and five studies (473 participants) evaluated surgical interventions for endometrioma prior to ART. No studies evaluated combination therapy.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: No clear benefit was found for any treatment over no treatment. We judged all studies to have a high or unclear risk of bias in at least two domains and graded the evidence as very low certainty as a result of this and imprecision due to low study numbers and wide confidence intervals. Below we report the critical outcomes, as presented in the summary of findings tables. Medical intervention: GnRH agonist protocol compared to control for ART The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of a GnRH agonist protocol compared to control on live birth (OR 3.70, 95% CI 1.25 to 10.90; 1 study, 64 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Adverse events were not reported. Surgical intervention (s): Endometrioma aspiration versus no aspiration The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of endometrioma aspiration compared to control on live birth (OR 1.66, 95% CI 0.59 to 4.62; 1 study, 81 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Adverse events were not reported. Endometrioma cystectomy versus no cystectomy The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of endometrioma cystectomy compared to control on live birth (OR 1.97, 95% CI 0.71 to 5.49; 1 study, 73 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Zero adverse events were reported in each study arm (1 study, 73 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Endometrioma transvaginal sclerotherapy versus no sclerotherapy No included study assessed live birth. Adverse events were not reported.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: This narrative review highlights the uncertainties regarding the management of endometrioma prior to ART. There is no high-certainty evidence that might change the current guidance for management plans to be developed on an individual basis, taking into account previous outcomes, ovarian reserve, and patient's wishes. Further robust, adequately powered studies are required to guide future clinical decision-making which include critical outcomes as per the core outcome set for endometriosis.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571. Original review (2010) https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008571.pub2.

articles.title: Real-world safety profiles of newer antiseizure medications: A pharmacovigilance study based on FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database.
articles.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the post-marketing safety of four newer antiseizure medications (ASMs)-brivaracetam (BRV), cannabidiol (CBD), cenobamate (CNB), and fenfluramine (FFA).

METHODS: A pharmacovigilance study was conducted using data from the FAERS database (Q1 2016-Q4 2024). Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect adverse event (AE) signals using three algorithms. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, reporter, and treatment strategy. We employed multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for covariates including age, sex, weight, dose, and concomitant medications, to validate associations between ASMs and specific AEs and to identify potential influencing factors. Bayesian network analysis was conducted to explore conditional dependencies among variables. Hospitalization risk was evaluated based on system organ classes.

RESULTS: After data cleaning, 13 763 reports were included. We identified 308 positive preferred term (PT) signals. Seizure-related AEs were frequently reported. All four ASMs had the PT of seizure cluster, with each exhibiting distinct AE profiles: BRV with psychiatric disorders, CBD with gastrointestinal events, CNB with visual dysfunction, and FFA with valvular heart disease (VHD). Children had higher reporting odds of seizure with BRV and CBD, while reporting odds of FFA-related VHD were lower in children; polytherapy was associated with higher reporting odds of somnolence, and AE reporting patterns varied by reporter source. Both CBD-related gastrointestinal events and FFA-related cardiac events exhibited dose-dependent effects. Infection-related AEs were associated with higher odds of hospitalization for multiple ASMs.

SIGNIFICANCE: This study comprehensively characterizes the safety profiles of newer ASMs and highlights the importance of tailored AE monitoring based on specific ASM and patient characteristics.

articles.title: Peripheral blood CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ T cells as an adjunctive diagnostic biomarker in adult hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis: Comparison with an adapted strict Fardet-style HScore.
articles.abstract: Adult hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) is diagnostically challenging due to clinical overlap with sepsis, autoimmune disorders, and malignancy-associated hyperinflammation, and existing criteria were developed primarily in pediatric cohorts. We evaluated peripheral blood CD8+ T-cell immunophenotyping as a diagnostic adjunct in adults with suspected HLH, compared against an adapted Fardet-style HScore. This single-center observational cohort study enrolled 106 consecutive adults with cytopenias and hyperferritinemia undergoing bone marrow examination. Patients were classified as HLH (n = 50) or non-HLH (n = 56) by revised HLH-2004 criteria with expert adjudication. Multiparametric flow cytometry quantified single-positive CD8+CD38+ and CD8+HLA-DR+ and dual-positive CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ subsets. Diagnostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis with Youden-index-derived cut-offs. CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ was the strongest flow-cytometric marker (AUC 0.824). At the Youden-optimal threshold (>16.71% of parent CD8+ T cells), sensitivity was 78% and specificity 81%; at an exploratory 22.69% threshold (same parent CD8+ subset), sensitivity was 64.0% and specificity 87.5%. Single-positive CD8+CD38+ (AUC 0.564) and CD8+HLA-DR+ (AUC 0.427) subsets did not discriminate. The adapted HScore achieved an AUC of 0.970; at a threshold of >196, sensitivity was 94.0% and specificity was 87.5%. The adapted HScore provided the strongest clinicobiochemical framework. CD8+CD38+HLA-DR+ was the best-performing flow-cytometric adjunct, offering high specificity for rule-in in gray-zone adult HLH. An integrated strategy combining clinical scoring with immune activation profiling is recommended.

articles.title: Conversion hip arthroplasty has a higher risk of venous thromboembolism disease at 30 days than primary total hip arthroplasty and revision total hip arthroplasty.
articles.journal: Hip international : the journal of clinical and experimental research on hip pathology and therapy
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), represents a serious postoperative complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA.

METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was performed using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database. Adult patients undergoing primary, conversion, or revision THA were identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. A total of 475,002 patients met inclusion criteria (primary THA: 428,245 [90.2%], conversion THA: 10,637 [2.2%], revision THA: 36,120 [7.6%]) with a mean age of 65.6 years (range, 18 to 89); 55.0% women. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative DVT. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated associations between procedure type and DVT, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class, smoking status, chronic steroid use, and operating time.

RESULTS: Adjusted odds of DVT were significantly lower after primary THA (odds ratio (OR) 0.48, 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.28-0.88; p = 0.010) and revision THA (OR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.23-0.87; p = 0.014) compared with conversion THA. Independent predictors of higher DVT risk included older age, longer operating time, and chronic steroid use. Sex, BMI, ASA class, and smoking status were not independently associated with DVT.

CONCLUSIONS: Conversion THA is associated with higher 30-day DVT risk compared with both primary and revision THA on multivariable analyses. Recognition of conversion THA as a distinct procedural category associated with higher relative thromboembolic risk may improve perioperative risk stratification and guide more individualised thromboprophylaxis strategies.

articles.title: The Muheza Approach: A 7-Year Experience of Sustainable and Affordable Mesh Hernia Surgery in a Lower-Middle Income Country.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hernias are a public health priority in Africa, with a focus on hernia surgery providing the potential to reduce the significant burden of hernia-related morbidity. Only a minority of patients in Africa are currently receiving a gold-standard mesh repair, owing to the cost of commercial mesh. In this study, we describe the long-term outcomes for patients undergoing hernia repairs utilising an affordable polyethylene 'mosquito-net' mesh (MNM) in Muheza, Tanzania.

METHODS: Data from consecutive patients undergoing MNM hernia repair in a single centre in Muheza between November 2018 and February 2026 were recorded in a prospectively maintained database. Operative technique using a tension-free sublay technique and postoperative care, where feasible, was standardised. Follow-up was performed through a mix of face-to-face and telephone consultation.

RESULTS: A total of 268 hernia repairs were included in the final analysis with a 596-day median follow-up. Most cases were inguinal hernias (89.9%) and primary repairs (85.1%). Thirty-day morbidity rate was 3.5%, including one (0.4%) mesh infection and two patients (0.7%) who required a return to theatre. Chronic pain was reported in 17 (6.3%) patients. There was one hernia recurrence during the study period.

CONCLUSION: Following our reporting of the early results in 2020, we now offer the longer-term data to demonstrate that the Muheza Approach to hernias utilising MNM is a safe, effective, affordable and sustainable strategy that could provide a platform for wider implementation across LMICs to address the shortfall in high-quality hernia surgery.

articles.title: What matters more in the time to flap: injury-to-flap or definitive-fixation-to-flap?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To determine the optimal threshold between injury, first debridement, and fixation-to-flap that minimizes infection risk in adult patients who sustained an open fracture requiring acute flap coverage.

METHODS: Design: A retrospective, secondary analysis using data from two prospective randomized controlled trials (XXX and XXX trials) to evaluate infection and time to flap coverage.

SETTING: Multinational clinical trial at 25 institutions.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: This secondary analysis included patients 18 years and older, who underwent definitive fracture fixation with an implant, and operative debridement within 72 hours of injury. Patients also had to receive a free or pedicled flap for acute injury management, rather than for wound dehiscence or infection.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Infection rate at 3-months was assessed using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) criteria with a sensitivity analysis at 12-months. Time from injury-to-flap, first debridement-to-flap and definitive fixation-to-flap intervals were evaluated using multivariate logistic regression models while adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. Included covariates were selected based on a stepwise procedure, using the Akaike Information Criterion, and on their clinical or sociodemographic relevance.

RESULTS: The analysis included 138 patients. 32 patients (23.2%) developed an infection and 106 did not (76.8%). The two groups were similar with regards to demographic and injury-related characteristics, with a mean age of 44.9 years (standard deviation [SD] 16.0) in the group of patients with a primary infection versus 44.8 years (SD 16.0) in those who did not develop an infection. Seventy-five percent of patients with a primary infection were male compared to 63.2% in the other group. Mean time to flap was 9.7 days (range 0.0 - 30.0). Multivariate analysis showed that a flap within 7 days following injury (OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.09-0.74, p=0.01) or first debridement (OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.12-0.89, p<0.05) was associated with lower rates of infection, compared to those who underwent a flap in 7 days or greater following injury or first debridement. Time from injury to flap (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.91-1.03, p = 0.343) and time from fixation to flap (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.95-1.10, p = 0.699) were not associated with lower rates of infection.

CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that limiting the time from injury and first debridement to flap to less than 7 days was associated with decreased risk of infection. However, infection was not found to be associated with time from definitive fixation-to-flap.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Genetic testing strategies for neonatal cholestasis in the neonatal intensive care unit.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cholestasis in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) has a broad differential diagnosis, including genetic diseases. Advances in next generation sequencing (NGS) have expanded the ability to identify genetic etiologies. Studies evaluating testing strategies, diagnostic yield, and clinical characteristics of those undergoing genetic testing for cholestasis in the NICU are limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied patients at a single-center Level IV NICU with cholestasis, genetic testing and Hepatology consultation between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Microarray, targeted gene panel and exome or genome sequencing (ES/GS) results and clinical characteristics of those tested were reviewed. Diagnostic yield was defined as identification of pathogenic variants determined to be causative of cholestasis. Categorical variables were compared using Chi-squared test or Fisher's exact as appropriate. Continuous variables were compared using Wilcoxon rank sum tests or Kruskal-Wallis tests as appropriate.

RESULTS: A total of 174 patients were included for analysis. Patients with three modalities of testing had higher peak direct bilirubin and alanine aminotransferase. Diagnostic yield increased by comprehensiveness: microarray 5% (3/54), targeted gene panel 10% (12/125) and ES/GS 33% (23/70). Seven patients with non-diagnostic targeted panels had diagnostic ES/GS. Those with diagnostic ES/GS were younger at Hepatology consultation, had higher peak direct bilirubin and were less likely to have sepsis compared to those with diagnostic targeted panels.

CONCLUSIONS: ES/GS demonstrated greater diagnostic yield for cholestasis in the NICU than other modalities. Confounding by year of testing is possible, but differences in yield support preferential use of ES/GS for neonatal cholestasis evaluation.

articles.title: Antibiotic Nails Outperform Implant Retention in Preventing Recurrent Infections After Intramedullary Nail Fixation of Tibial Shaft Fractures Complicated by Infection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare infection recurrence rates between patients treated with antibiotic nail versus implant retention for open tibial shaft fractures initially treated with an intramedullary (IM) nail complicated by infection.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Level I trauma center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Adults with tibial shaft fractures (OTA/AO 42A-C) treated with an IM nail between 2007 and 2023 who developed deep surgical site infections after index fixation were included.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was infection recurrence within 2 years requiring reoperation and antibiotics. Secondary outcomes included amputation rate, all-cause mortality rate, days in hospital within 1 year of index infection surgery, time to recurrence, and number of surgeries needed after recurrence. The association between treatment and the study outcomes was estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, controlling for potential confounders.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients were included, 75 (78%) [62 males; median age 47 years (interquartile range (IQR), 31 to 53)] were treated with conversion to antibiotic nail and 21 (22%) [18 males; median age 36 years (IQR, 27 to 48)] with implant retention. The antibiotic nail group was more likely to have chronic infections, requiring surgery 6 or more weeks after index IM nail fixation (65% vs. 38%, P = 0.03). The 2-year infection recurrence rate was significantly lower with implant removal and antibiotic nail (33%) than with implant retention (54%) (HR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.20 to 0.92; P = 0.03). For the secondary outcomes collected, only the average number of surgeries required after recurrence differed significantly between the two groups, with 3.9 for antibiotic nail and 3.0 for implant retention (IRR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.01 to 1.91; P = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: Conversion to an antibiotic nail was associated with lower rates of infection recurrence compared with implant retention. The overall infection recurrence rates of 33% in the antibiotic nail cohort and 54% in the implant retention cohort highlight the challenges associated with treating infection after IM nail fixation of tibial shaft fractures, regardless of treatment strategy.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic, Level III.

articles.title: Before the score: delirium detection and a geriatric approach in neurology and stroke wards.
Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients older than 50 years who sustained a low-energy hip fracture (AO/OTA 31A, B, and 32A) and underwent prophylactic IVC filter insertion before hip fracture surgery between 2005 and 2025 were included. Prophylactic IVC filter placement was selectively performed in patients with either objectively confirmed deep vein thrombosis on preoperative screening or absolute contraindications to mechanical and pharmacological venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Those who had multiple trauma at the time of injury, a clinical follow-up duration ≤6 months after surgery, or undergone IVC filter placement following a confirmed diagnosis of PTE based on pulmonary computed tomography or lung perfusion scanning were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the rate of newly developed symptomatic PTE. Secondary outcomes included IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: One hundred fifty-six patients were included in the prophylactic IVC filter group (39 men 25.0%], 117 women [75.0%]; mean age, 75.8 ± 11.1 years; femoral neck [AO/OTA 31B], n = 71 [45.5%]; intertrochanteric [31A], n = 75 [48.1%]; subtrochanteric [AO/OTA 32A], n = 10 [6.4%];mean indwelling time, 9.1 days; retrieval rate, 88.5%). Among these patients, no cases of newly developed symptomatic PTE were observed (0%), whereas the incidence in the overall hip fracture cohort (n=4,568) was 0.44%. Filter-related complications occurred in 3.9% of patients (minor tilting, 2.6%; vessel adhesion, 1.3%), with no major mechanical failures such as migration or perforation. Although no thrombi were detected at insertion, 4.5% of the patients had trapped thrombi at the time of removal. The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 1.3% (2/156) in the prophylactic IVC filter group, compared with 1.5% (67/4,568) in the overall hip fracture cohort. (p=0.845). Neither death in the prophylactic IVC filter group was attributed to PTE or an IVC filter-related complication.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study's selected extreme pulmonary thromboembolism risk cohort, including patients with CT-confirmed preoperative DVT, those clinically expected to undergo prolonged perioperative immobilization, or those with contraindications to prophylactic anticoagulation, such as GI bleeding, prophylactic inferior vena cava filter served as an effective and safe temporary bridge therapy rather than a routine prophylactic strategy.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.

articles.title: Ileal bile acid transporter inhibitors.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract: Pediatric cholestatic liver diseases, such as Alagille syndrome and progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis, are rare genetic disorders characterized by impaired bile flow, systemic bile acid accumulation, and debilitating pruritus. Historically managed with supportive care or invasive surgical interventions, the therapeutic landscape has recently expanded with the introduction of ileal bile acid transporter (IBAT) inhibitors. These luminal, ileum-targeted agents block bile acid reabsorption, thereby increasing fecal bile acid excretion and effectively reducing the systemic bile acid pool to relieve pruritus. However, this pharmacological blockade also attenuates the intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR)-fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19) feedback loop, leading to a compensatory increase in hepatic bile acid synthesis. Consequently, the clinical efficacy and safety of IBAT inhibitors are heavily dependent on a sufficiently preserved enterohepatic bile flow and canalicular export capacity. When luminal bile acid delivery is impaired, therapeutic benefits diminish, and the unchecked compensatory synthesis may contribute to hepatocyte stress and elevated transaminases. Thus, optimizing the use of these therapies will require a shift from broad disease-label indications toward precision, genotype- and physiology-informed patient selection, utilizing non-invasive biomarkers to assess target engagement and guide clinical management.

articles.title: Operative Strategies for Treating Tibial Plateau Fractures in Patients Aged 55 Years and Older: A Five-Year Comparison of Acute Total Knee Arthroplasty with Open Reduction and Internal Fixation, Conversion Total Knee Arthroplasty, and Total Knee Arthroplasty for Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare outcomes of acute total knee arthroplasty (TKA) for tibial plateau fracture in patients aged 55 years and older with matched patients undergoing open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF), conversion TKA after failed ORIF, and primary TKA for osteoarthritis.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching.

SETTING: Federated multi-institutional electronic health records database (TriNetX United States Collaborative Network).

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients aged ≥55 years with tibial plateau fracture treated with acute TKA, ORIF, or conversion TKA after failed ORIF were identified. A separate cohort undergoing primary TKA for osteoarthritis without fracture history was identified as a non-traumatic comparator. The study period was restricted to January 1, 2005 through December 31, 2020 to ensure a minimum of five years of potential follow-up for all included patients.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was revision surgery at 5 years, defined as conversion to TKA after ORIF and as revision TKA after arthroplasty. Secondary outcomes were a composite "return to the operating room (OR)" outcome (selected major reoperations), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), surgical site infection (SSI), aseptic loosening, manipulation under anesthesia (MUA), and periprosthetic fracture. Three 1:1 propensity score-matched comparisons were performed (acute TKA versus ORIF; acute versus conversion TKA; acute TKA versus primary TKA for osteoarthritis), with risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) calculated. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age (55-70 years; ≥70 years).

RESULTS: After matching, 1,321 patients per cohort were compared in the primary acute TKA versus ORIF analysis. Mean age was 66.1 years in the acute TKA cohort and 66.6 years in the ORIF cohort (range, 55 to 90 in both), and 65.3% and 66.7%, respectively, were female. Acute TKA had higher 5-year revision rates than ORIF (7.0% versus 0.8%; RR 8.36, 95% CI 4.50-15.56; P < 0.001) and elevated PJI rates (6.2% versus 1.3%; RR 4.82, 95% CI 2.88-8.09; P < 0.001). Return to OR rates did not differ significantly between acute TKA and ORIF (25.6% versus 23.5%; RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.95-1.25; P = 0.21). Revision did not differ between acute and conversion TKA (9.0% versus 10.0%; RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.58-1.35; P = 0.589) but was higher after acute TKA than after primary TKA for osteoarthritis (7.4% versus 3.5%; RR 2.12, 95% CI 1.48-3.00; P < 0.001). Revision was higher after acute TKA than ORIF in patients aged 55-70 years (9.3% versus 1.7%; RR 5.41, 95% CI 2.80-10.48; P < 0.001) and was not reportable in those aged ≥70 years owing to small cell counts.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients aged 55 years and older, acute TKA for tibial plateau fracture was associated with higher risks of revision and complications compared with ORIF. Revision and complication rates after acute TKA were comparable with those after conversion TKA following failed ORIF but higher than those after primary TKA for osteoarthritis. Acute TKA should be reserved for patients at highest risk of ORIF failure requiring subsequent conversion to TKA.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, therapeutic study.

articles.title: Network-Based Brain Stimulation: Targeting the Frontoparietal Network for Cognitive Rehabilitation After Stroke Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: BackgroundPost-stroke cognitive impairment is a common and disabling condition, frequently involving executive dysfunction, attention deficits, and working memory impairments. Traditional cognitive rehabilitation yields modest benefits. Recently, non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) targeting large-scale brain networks particularly the frontoparietal network (FPN) has emerged as a promising strategy to enhance neuroplasticity and cognitive recovery.Objectiveo systematically review and meta-analyze the evidence on the effectiveness of NIBS techniques targeting the FPN in improving cognitive outcomes among stroke survivors.Methodscomprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL was conducted through June 2025, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental, and controlled observational designs investigating non-invasive brain stimulation techniques, namely transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), targeting frontoparietal network (FPN) regions such as the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and posterior parietal cortex. Data were extracted on cognitive outcomes, stimulation parameters, and effect sizes. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0 and ROBINS-I tools. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed.ResultsTwenty-eight studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which 21 were randomized controlled trials published between 2020 and 2024. Seventeen studies provided sufficient data for quantitative synthesis (meta-analysis). Most targeted the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) using anodal tDCS or high-frequency rTMS; eight employed dual-site stimulation. Meta-analysis demonstrated moderate improvements in executive function (Hedges' g = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.30-0.66), working memory (g = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.22-0.60), and attention (g = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.17-0.59). Heterogeneity was low to moderate (I² = 32%-58%), and minimal publication bias was detected. Combining NIBS with cognitive training yielded superior outcomes.ConclusionNIBS targeting the FPN is a promising intervention to enhance post-stroke cognitive function, especially executive control and attention. Future trials should employ standardized, neuroimaging-guided protocols to assess long-term clinical utility.

articles.title: Treatment of pediatric autoimmune liver disease beyond prednisolone and azathioprine in a cohort of 115 patients.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric autoimmune hepatitis (pAIH) is an acute or chronic inflammatory liver disease, caused by a dysregulation of the immune system. Autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis (ASC) additionally affects the bile ducts. Traditional first-line treatment (FLT) consists of prednisolone and azathioprine. If pAIH/ASC remains untreated or biochemical remission (BR) is not achieved, end-stage liver disease develops. We aimed to analyze the 6-months-outcomes of various second- and third-line therapies for pAIH/ASC.

METHODS: This is a retrospective single-center analysis, including all cases of patients with pAIH or ASC between 2000 and 2025. All patients were diagnosed based on published European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition diagnostic criteria.

RESULTS: Of 115 patients with pAIH or ASC, 26 patients required an alternative therapy (altT) other than prednisolone and azathioprine, most of them due to non-BR, including due to non-compliance. The 6-month outcome shows, that tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-alpha inhibitors overall achieved the best results with a BR rate of 40% (n = 2/5). This was closely followed by cyclosporin A (CSA), with a BR rate of 36.4% (n = 4/11), which was the most commonly used drug in our study. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are significantly more likely to need altT.

CONCLUSIONS: The overall BR rate 6 months after start of altT is low and decreases with each stage of therapy, the TNF-alpha inhibitors demonstrated the highest BR rate for altT. Non-compliance is a significant problem in general, so it is unclear whether the success of this therapy is solely attributable to the drug's inherent immunomodulatory function or to its controlled administration via intravenous injection. The prospective evaluation of this novel, low-side-effect management option warrants further explorations.

articles.title: Does Hemiplegic Side Matter? A Cross-Sectional Study of Laterality Impacts on Mobility, Balance, Hand Dexterity, and Cognition in Stroke Patients.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo investigate the impact of laterality on mobility, balance, hand dexterity, and cognition in stroke patients.MethodsBetween January and June 2024, 51 patients (34 males) aged 18-64 years with first-ever stroke were enrolled and assigned to groups based on the affected side of the body. Outcome measures were functional mobility, fall risk, postural control, hand dexterity and cognition. Group differences were analyzed using linear regression, while associations among outcomes were examined using Spearman's rank correlation coefficients.ResultsCompared to right hemiplegic patients, left hemiplegic patients exhibited reduced functional mobility, poorer postural control, and an increased risk of falls. Regarding cognitive and manual performance, they demonstrated higher cognitive scores, reduced dexterity in the impaired hand, increased dexterity in the preserved hand, and an overall reduction in combined dexterity for both hands. Except for the association between fall risk and preserved hand dexterity, all other outcomes showed significant correlations (p < .05).ConclusionLaterality significantly influenced mobility, balance, hand dexterity, and cognition, highlighting the need for stroke rehabilitation strategies to be tailored to side-specific deficits.

articles.title: The Illusion of Scale: Divergent Orthopaedic Trauma Outcomes Across Large Healthcare Databases.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare demographic characteristics and postoperative complication rates between the TriNetX and PearlDiver national databases across three common orthopaedic trauma procedures.

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: National United States electronic health record and administrative claims databases (TriNetX and PearlDiver).

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent open treatment of proximal femur fracture (PFFx)(CPT 27236), femoral shaft intramedullary nail (fIMN)(CPT 27506), or tibial shaft intramedullary nail (tIMN)(CPT 27759) between 2015 and 2020 were identified.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: Demographic characteristics and postoperative surgical site infection, transfusion, anemia, acute kidney injury, urinary tract infection, pneumonia, wound dehiscence, and pulmonary embolism were compared between databases at 30, 60, and 90 days.

RESULTS: TriNetX and PearlDiver identified 61,110 and 91,106 patients undergoing open treatment of proximal femur fracture (PFFx), 35,130 and 21,478 undergoing femoral shaft intramedullary nailing (fIMN), and 34,945 and 24,742 undergoing tibial shaft intramedullary nailing (tIMN), respectively. At 30 days, TriNetX demonstrated higher PE incidence than PearlDiver following PFFx (1.6% vs 0.2%), fIMN (2.4% vs 0.9%), and tIMN (1.1% vs 0.2%), whereas pneumonia incidence was lower (3.9% vs 4.7%, 2.9% vs 4.5%, and 1.7% vs 3.2%, respectively; all p<0.0001). At 60 days, PE remained higher in TriNetX (PFFx: 2.1% vs 0.3%; fIMN: 2.8% vs 0.5%; tIMN: 1.3% vs 0.3%), while UTI was lower (9.5% vs 14.2%, 4.2% vs 9.5%, and 2.0% vs 4.6%, respectively; all p<0.0001). At 90 days, PE remained higher in TriNetX (2.3% vs 0.3%, 3.0% vs 0.5%, and 1.4% vs 0.3%), whereas pneumonia remained lower (5.9% vs 6.9%, 3.6% vs 6.1%, and 2.3% vs 4.2%, respectively; all p<0.0001.

CONCLUSIONS: TriNetX and PearlDiver produced different demographic characteristics and complication rates following proximal femur fracture fixation and femoral and tibial shaft intramedullary nailing, suggesting that database-specific characteristics may influence reported outcomes.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III.

articles.title: Interpreting Risk-Stratified Prognostic Value of the Triglyceride-Glucose Index After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

articles.title: The CLEAR Classification for Coronary Bifurcation In-Stent Restenosis: An Exploratory Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In-stent restenosis (ISR) following percutaneous coronary intervention for bifurcation lesions remains a challenging clinical entity. Existing classifications do not fully characterize bifurcation ISR by integrating relevant anatomical and procedural characteristics.

AIMS: To propose a novel classification for bifurcation ISR and to explore its associations with observed management patterns and long-term outcomes.

METHODS: A novel classification for bifurcation ISR, incorporating core involvement, stent layer number, and morphological pattern, was applied to angiographic data from 98 patients (from a cohort of 600 patients with angiographic follow-up after bifurcation stenting). Interobserver reproducibility of the classification was assessed using paired ratings obtained from two independent observers. Subsequently, treatment approaches and clinical outcomes were evaluated over a median follow-up of 3.5 years.

RESULTS: The classification identified several angiographic phenotypes that appeared to be associated with different observed treatment patterns and numerically different clinical outcomes. Interobserver agreement was excellent, with kappa values from 0.843 to 0.882. Isolated side branch (21 patients) and focal main branch (31 patients) ISR, particularly without core involvement (22 patients), were associated with favorable outcomes and were predominantly managed with repeat stenting, plain balloon angioplasty, or optimal medical therapy. In contrast, patients with ISR involving both branches (n = 23) or diffuse main-branch ISR (n = 23) were managed using a wider range of approaches and had higher recurrence rates. Restenosis within areas of multiple stent layers (13 patients) also correlated with complex management.

CONCLUSION: The CLEAR classification provides a structured angiographic framework for describing bifurcation lesion ISR. In this exploratory cohort, CLEAR phenotypes were associated with different observed treatment patterns and clinical outcomes; however, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before the classification can be used to guide treatment strategies.

articles.title: Stage-Wise Identification of Gait Biomarkers Across the Progression of Diabetes and Diabetic Neuropathy.
articles.journal: The international journal of lower extremity wounds
articles.abstract: Purposeof the research: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy induces progressive gait deterioration, yet most Machine Learning (ML)-based gait studies rely on binary classification frameworks that fail to capture the stage-wise biomechanical changes occurring across the diabetes neuropathy continuum. To identify stage-consistent and stage-specific gait biomarkers across three clinical groups healthy controls (N), diabetes without neuropathy (D), and diabetes with peripheral neuropathy (DPN) using an interpretable machine learning framework.MethodsGait data were collected from 394 participants (N = 109, D = 163, DPN = 122) using the Zebris FDM platform. Spatiotemporal, plantar pressure, and symmetry parameters were extracted. Four pairwise classification tasks (N vs D, D vs DPN, N vs DPN, Healthy vs Diseased) were evaluated using Results: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Logistic Regression under stratified five-fold cross-validation. Cross-validated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based feature selection and a final XGBoost model were used for biomarker identification and interpretation. SVM achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across all tasks (N vs D: 0.80, D vs DPN: 0.75, N vs DPN: 0.91, Healthy vs Diseased: 0.85). SHAP analysis identified bilateral heel contact time and step length as stage-consistent core biomarkers, present across all four classification tasks. Stage-specific discriminators included forefoot load-timing disruption in early diabetes, midfoot unloading and lateral symmetry reversal at the neuropathic transition, and posterior Centre of Pressure (CoP) displacement in established neuropathy.ConclusionsDiabetic gait pathology progresses in a measurable, stage-ordered sequence from early forefoot load-timing disruption through midfoot redistribution and symmetry reversal at the neuropathic transition, to global spatiotemporal deterioration in established neuropathy. The stage-wise biomarker framework presented here provides an interpretable, clinically grounded basis for gait-based screening of diabetic neuropathic progression, warranting prospective validation.

articles.title: Long-term impact of anorexia nervosa on cardiovascular morbidity in men and women: A longitudinal cohort study: Incidence à long terme de l'anorexie mentale sur la morbidité cardiovasculaire chez les hommes et les femmes : étude de cohorte longitudinale.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
articles.abstract: BackgroundAnorexia nervosa is associated with cardiovascular morbidity in women, but the relationship is less studied in men. We assessed the association between anorexia nervosa and the long-term risk of cardiovascular disease in men and women.MethodsWe analyzed a cohort of 7332 patients with anorexia nervosa and 73,215 matched controls from Quebec, Canada. The exposure was anorexia nervosa diagnosed between 1989 and 2023. The outcome was cardiovascular hospitalization for heart failure, conduction disorders, cardiac arrest, and other cardiovascular events up to 34 years later. We derived adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association of anorexia nervosa with cardiovascular morbidity using Cox regression, with men and women analyzed separately.ResultsAmong 7332 patients with anorexia nervosa, 467 (6.4%) were men. Compared with matched controls, anorexia nervosa was associated with 1.43 times the risk of cardiovascular hospitalization in men (95% CI [1.08-1.90]) and 2.23 times the risk in women (95% CI [2.06-2.42]). Risk of cardiovascular hospitalization was highest within one year of diagnosis for anorexia nervosa among both men and women. Anorexia nervosa was particularly associated with conduction disorders (HR 3.24, 95% CI [2.84-3.69]) and heart failure (HR 1.99, 95% CI [1.54-2.56]) in women, but similar associations did not stand out in men.ConclusionBoth men and women with anorexia nervosa have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease later in life, although women appear to be more affected. Men and women with anorexia nervosa may benefit from closer monitoring to prevent adverse cardiovascular events.

articles.title: When the Valve Is the Dominant Lesion: Rethinking Coronary Revascularization in Severe Aortic Stenosis With Stable Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

articles.title: Deoxynivalenol in Fusarium Head Blight: From Mycotoxin to a Mediator of Plant-Pathogen Interactions.
articles.abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON), a type B trichothecene produced predominantly by Fusarium graminearum, is a major mycotoxin associated with Fusarium head blight (FHB) and a persistent threat to grain safety. Beyond its toxicological effects, DON functions as a virulence-associated metabolite at the plant-pathogen interface. Here, we review recent advances in DON biosynthesis and its multilayered regulation. DON production is coordinated through TRI cluster expression, chromatin regulation, toxisome organisation and fungal cellular differentiation, with environmental and host-derived signals converging through interconnected signalling networks. During infection, DON promotes fungal spread and shapes host defence responses, whereas plants counter DON through enzymatic detoxification, DON-responsive signalling and protein-mediated resistance. These insights point to mechanism-guided strategies that target DON induction, regulatory processes and pathogenic functions, while harnessing host defences and detoxification capacity. DON therefore represents a metabolite tightly coupled to infection-stage fungal physiology and a key mediator of host-pathogen interactions, providing opportunities for more precise control of mycotoxin accumulation in disease management.

articles.title: Response to 'Controlled hypertension or a heterogeneous treated phenotype? Rethinking the CPET findings of the HyperVasc study'.
Experiences and perceptions of community-based, group exercise interventions for stroke survivors: A scoping review of multiple stakeholders' perspectives.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveThis scoping review aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the literature that has investigated experiences and perceptions of stroke stakeholders (stroke survivors and individuals involved in their care or the delivery, management or support of services for stroke survivors) involved with a community-based, group exercise intervention.Data sourcesEmbase, MEDLINE, CINAHL, APA PsycINFO, SPORTDiscus, Scopus and grey literature sources were searched on 29/09/26 using a combination of subject headings and free-text strings. Citation tracking was also performed.Review methodsThe review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute Scoping Review guidance. Studies that included stroke stakeholders (stroke survivors, carers and staff) and investigated perceptions or experiences of community-based, group exercise programmes were eligible for inclusion. Screening and data extraction was completed in duplicate. Qualitative content analysis was used to identify common categories in the included studies, which were then used for mapping.ResultsA total of 73 studies were included, of which 37 included only service users, one included only carers, nine included only staff and 26 included participants from multiple stakeholder groups. There was significant heterogeneity in the specific exercise programmes being evaluated. Following coding, seven categories were identified: Benefits, motivators and facilitators, barriers, positive aspects, areas for improvement, need for community exercise programmes and evaluation and outcome data.ConclusionStakeholders perceived community-based group exercise as offering physical, psychosocial and behavioural benefits, although experiences and preferences varied. Programmes should accommodate individual needs and address barriers, including accessibility, transport, communication and staffing. Carer-specific evidence remains limited.

articles.title: Association of single intrauterine fetal demise with severe brain injury and death in liveborn cotwins delivered before 32 weeks: large single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent association in twin pregnancy between single intrauterine fetal demise (sIUFD) and major short-term adverse outcomes, particularly severe brain injury (SBI) or death, in extremely and very preterm liveborn cotwins (delivered < 32 weeks), to examine whether this association extends beyond chorionicity and to identify critical gestational windows of vulnerability and potential mediating pathways.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included twin pregnancies, with or without sIUFD, delivered < 32 weeks at Shengjing Hospital of China Medical University, Shenyang, China, between January 2014 and December 2024, with neonates admitted immediately after birth to the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations between sIUFD and the primary outcome, a composite of SBI or death of the liveborn cotwin prior to hospital discharge. Subgroup analyses stratified by chorionicity and gestational age at sIUFD were performed to identify risk patterns and critical gestational windows of vulnerability. Mediation analyses were conducted to explore whether the association between sIUFD and SBI or death was mediated by early-onset sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth or the 5-min Apgar score, and sensitivity analyses incorporating propensity-score matching to balance baseline confounders were performed to assess the robustness of the results.

RESULTS: In total, 1069 twin pregnancies delivered < 32 weeks were included (113 with and 956 without sIUFD). sIUFD was independently associated with significantly increased odds of SBI or death (adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 2.85 (95% CI, 1.61-4.97)). This association was consistent across monochorionic and dichorionic subgroups. The highest point estimate was observed when sIUFD occurred at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks' gestation (aOR, 3.72 (95% CI, 1.64-8.06)). Mediation analysis identified a 5-min Apgar score < 7, suggestive of perinatal asphyxia, as the primary mediator of SBI or death (proportion mediated: 24.30%), while disseminated intravascular coagulation within 24 h after birth and early-onset sepsis acted as significant secondary mediators (proportions mediated: 6.60% and 4.30%, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: sIUFD is independently associated with an increased risk of SBI or death in liveborn cotwins delivered < 32 weeks, regardless of chorionicity, particularly when demise occurs at 28 + 0 to 29 + 6 weeks. Perinatal asphyxia is the primary mediator of this association. These findings support intensified monitoring of all surviving cotwins, with surveillance guided by the gestational age at sIUFD. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
