articles.title: Clinician Perspectives on Having Family Building Discussions With People With Sickle Cell Disease.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe potential impacts of sickle cell disease (SCD) and its treatments on multiple aspects of family building are emerging. Literature shows individuals with SCD desire biologic parenthood, yet few receive reproductive health counseling. This study aimed to explore SCD clinicians' perspectives on family building discussions with men and women with SCD.MethodParticipants were clinicians from across the United States, recruited via online SCD clinician listservs. Participants completed a survey capturing their demographics, clinical characteristics, and attitudes, practice patterns, challenges, and needs regarding family building discussions. Descriptive statistics summarized the quantitative data, and qualitative responses were categorized into challenges, needs, and resources needed to have these conversations.ResultsOf the 38 participants, 74% were pediatric SCD clinicians and 97% practiced at an academic medical center. Forty-two percent and 30% of clinicians reported not feeling comfortable initiating family building discussions with men and women with SCD, respectively. Reported challenges included lack of time during visits and these discussions not being within the perceived scope of the clinician (e.g., patients being too young, clinicians only practicing inpatient hematology). Needs included culturally informed resources for patients, additional training for clinicians, and clear referral options to specialists.DiscussionSCD clinicians experience multiple barriers that may prevent them from having family building discussions with people with SCD. Future studies investigating the best ways to incorporate family building discussions into SCD care are needed to ensure that people with SCD are able to achieve their family building goals.

articles.title: High rates of flares after anti-tumor necrosis factor withdrawal in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: A multi-center study.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Outcomes of anti-tumor necrosis factor (anti-TNF) discontinuation in pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remain unclear. We aimed to quantify relapse and biologic re-initiation rates following anti-TNF withdrawal in patients in sustained clinical remission for at least 6 months.

METHODS: Patients' characteristics were recorded at the time of anti-TNF discontinuation, at the time of flare, or at the end of follow-up, with a minimum follow-up of 1 year. A flare was defined as clinical, biochemical, or endoscopic activity leading to hospitalization, systemic corticosteroids, and/or initiation of a biologic.

RESULTS: This multicenter retrospective study from the Pediatric IBD Porto Group of the European Society for Paediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) included 83 children from 21 centers (46 [55%] males, 59 Crohn's disease [CD], 24 ulcerative colitis [UC]), who discontinued anti-TNF. At the time of anti-TNF withdrawal, the median age was 14.8 years (interquartile range 12.4-16.9); 93% had biochemical remission, and 68% of those undergoing endoscopy were in endoscopic remission. Within 12 and 24 months, 45/83 (54%) and 56/74 (76%) experienced a flare, and 29/83 (35%) and 47/68 (69%) re-initiated a biologic, respectively. Overall, flare and biologic re-initiation rates were similar in CD and UC, between those with biochemical or endoscopic remission, and among those maintained on immunomodulators (n = 33) or 5-aminosalicylates (n = 20). Univariate and multivariable Cox models did not identify baseline predictors of relapse or biologic re-initiation.

CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing anti-TNF therapy in pediatric IBD patients in clinical remission is associated with high rates of disease flare and treatment re-initiation. This provides quantitative data to help balance the benefits and risks when considering anti-TNF withdrawal.

articles.title: Preserved Right Ventricular Function With Early Remodeling in Pediatric Sickle Cell Disease: Comprehensive Echocardiographic Assessment and Longitudinal Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiopulmonary complications contribute substantially to morbidity in sickle cell disease (SCD), but right ventricular (RV) involvement in children remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to assess RV structure and function in pediatric SCD using conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography, and to examine associations with clinical features, hydroxyurea use, hemolysis markers, and longitudinal changes.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of children with SCD followed at a single tertiary center from 2015 to 2023. Clinical, laboratory, and treatment data were collected, and age- and sex-matched healthy children served as controls. Echocardiographic assessment included RV dimensions, systolic indices, tricuspid regurgitant velocity (TRv), and RV free-wall strain.

RESULTS: A total of 185 children were included (118 with SCD and 67 controls; mean age, 11.7 ± 5.3 years). Compared with controls, children with SCD had larger RV dimensions, slightly lower RV fractional area change, and higher TRv, whereas RV free-wall strain remained largely preserved. RV strain correlated with age, RV size, fractional area change, and TRv, but not with hydroxyurea use, anemia, hemolysis markers, or most clinical complications. RV indices were similar across genotypes. Elevated TRv (≥2.5 m/s) was present in 12.9% of patients. Longitudinal follow-up demonstrated stable RV function over time.

CONCLUSIONS: Children with SCD exhibit subtle RV remodeling and mildly increased pulmonary pressure despite preserved RV systolic function. These findings suggest that early right-heart changes in pediatric SCD are predominantly structural and hemodynamic rather than functional.

articles.title: Reply to the Letter to the Editor: "Complication Risk in Contemporary Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention".
Complication Risk in Contemporary Chronic Total Occlusion Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.
Combined Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Different Mitral and Tricuspid Regurgitation Combinations: A Contemporary and Comprehensive Review. Concomitant or Staged Procedure?
articles.abstract: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has become an effective treatment option for mitral regurgitation (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR), with high procedural success and low complication rates. Moderate-to-severe MR and TR coexist in approximately 11% of patients with heart failure, and patients with both conditions have a worse prognosis than those with either lesion alone. Current guidelines recommend treatment of concomitant TR during mitral valve surgery when tricuspid annular dilation is present. However, there are no clear recommendations for combined TEER, as mitral and tricuspid TEER are addressed separately in the guidelines. In this review, the available evidence and current clinical approaches to combined vs. isolated TEER across different combinations and severities of MR and TR were evaluated.

articles.title: Comparison of Cryoballoon and Pulsed Field Ablation in Patients with Symptomatic Atrial Fibrillation: First 6-Month Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation is an effective treatment for patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF), and pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) is the cornerstone of AF ablation. Unlike thermal ablation, pulsed field ablation (PFA) uses nonthermal energy to irreversibly electroporate myocardial tissue without affecting adjacent structures such as the esophagus, phrenic nerve, and PV tissue. The aim of this study was to compare the efficacy and safety of the 2 most widely used single-shot ablation techniques worldwide: Cryoballoon (CB) and PFA. To date, this is the first PFA study to be published from Türkiye.

METHODS: Consecutive AF patients who underwent PFA and CB-based PVI between July 2025 and February 2026 were enrolled. Cryoballoon PVI was performed using the 28-mm CB; PFA was performed using a 31 mm pentaspline catheter under fluoroscopic guidance.

RESULTS: A total of 100 patients were included in the study (66% male, 64% with paroxysmal AF, mean age: 61.7 ± 11.8 years). There were 55 patients in the CB group and 45 patients in the PFA group. The skin-to-figure-of-8 time was significantly shorter in the PFA group than in the CB group (30.00 [25.00-35.00] vs. 53.00 [47.00-55.00] minutes, P < .001). No cerebrovascular events, groin complications, or pericardial effusions were observed in patients in either group. During the 6-month follow-up period, 4 (8.9%) cases of atrial arrhythmia were observed in the PFA group, compared to 7 (12.7%) in the CB group (P = .406).

CONCLUSION: Both CB and PFA are safe and effective treatment methods for symptomatic patients diagnosed with AF. Compared to CB, acute procedure success rates and complications are similar in PFA, but procedure times are shorter.

articles.title: The Recruitment of Systemic-to-Pulmonary Arterial Collaterals in Chronic and Severe Precapillary Pulmonary Hypertension as an Adaptive or Misguided Mechanism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical impact of systemic-to-pulmonary arterial collaterals (SPCs) across pulmonary hypertension (PH) groups remains unclear. The authors evaluated the prevalence, clinical correlates, and prognostic relevance of SPCs in a comprehensive PH cohort.

METHODS: The authors retrospectively analyzed 434 adult PH patients diagnosed per European Society of Cardiology and European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) guidelines. Baseline risk was evaluated using multiparametric risk scores. All patients underwent diagnostic heart catheterization and angiography, with SPC recruitment semi-quantitatively graded from 0 (none) to 3 (severe, high grade: 2-3).

RESULTS: Mean age was 51.9 ± 18.2 years (61.1% female; groups 1, 2, 3, and 4 comprised 51.6%, 3.4%, 10.1%, and 33.2%, respectively). High-grade SPCs were significantly more prevalent in group 4 (58.3%) compared to groups 1 (30.4%), 2 (20.0%), and 3 (6.8%) (P <.001). Higher SPC grade significantly correlated with PH severity across clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and risk score measures (P <.001). Although higher SPC grades were linked to clinical worsening requiring parenteral prostacyclins (P = .027), they were not associated with overall 5-year survival, regardless of pulmonary vascular resistance severity or non-CTEPH etiology (P = .920). Only the Registry to Evaluate Early and Long-Term PAH Disease Management 2.0 score independently predicted mortality (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.19, P <.001, 95% CI: 1.13-1.26).

CONCLUSION: Systemic-to-pulmonary arterial collaterals are recruited across all PH etiology groups beyond group 4. While SPC recruitment serves as a marker of advanced pulmonary vascular involvement and elevated risk status, it does not act as an independent driver of long-term mortality.

articles.title: Safety of Recombinant Human Bone Morphogenetic Protein-2 Versus Iliac Crest Bone Graft in Alveolar Cleft Repair: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo compare the safety and complication profiles of recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein (rhBMP-2) and iliac crest bone graft (ICBG) in alveolar cleft repair.DesignA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and prospectively registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261340773).SettingPublished comparative studies identified through a comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL up to September 2026.Patients, Participants808 patients undergoing alveolar cleft repair, 395 with ICBG, 413 with rhBMP-2; across 7 studies (2 RCTs, 5 observational studies).InterventionsRhBMP-2 versus ICBG.Main Outcome MeasuresPrimary outcomes are graft failure, infection, oronasal fistula formation, postoperative swelling and wound dehiscence; secondary outcomes were operative time, length of stay and cost.ResultsSeven studies were included in the analysis. There were no statistically significant differences observed in graft failure (odds ratio [OR] = 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.43-1.71, P = 0.67), wound dehiscence (OR = 1.33; 0.57-3.14) and fistula formation (OR = 0.46; 0.04-5.05). RhBMP-2 was associated with lower postoperative infection rates (OR = 0.20; 0.05-0.72; P = 0.01), although it was also associated with higher postoperative swelling (OR = 9.74, 95% CI 3.91-24.27, P < 0.00001). However, certainty of the evidence remained low.ConclusionsAlthough rhBMP-2 may be associated with lower infection rates, the increased postoperative swelling risk remains a concern. The limited number of studies, predominantly observational evidence, imprecision and heterogeneity limit the interpretation of these findings. Adequately powered RCTs are needed to establish the safety of rhBMP-2 relative to ICBG.

articles.title: Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering.

RESULTS: Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14-0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16-0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23-0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

articles.title: Eye-Tracking Use for Assessment and Rehabilitation of Driver Performance: A Scoping Review.
articles.journal: Canadian journal of occupational therapy. Revue canadienne d'ergotherapie
articles.abstract: BackgroundDriving rehabilitation increasingly incorporates eye tracking to quantify visual-cognitive performance; however, its clinical relevance and patterns of use remain unclear.PurposeThis scoping review maps how eye-tracking technologies, metrics, and applications are used in driving assessment and rehabilitation, and characterizes the populations studied.MethodFollowing Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR, five databases were searched (January 2001-July 2026). Thirty-nine eligible studies were charted for population, driving task, eye-tracking metrics, and device type.FindingsStudy populations included older adults (24 studies), autism spectrum disorder (5), traumatic brain injury (3), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (3), visual field impairment (3), and stroke (1). Eye tracking was applied to hazard perception, visual exploration and scanning, visual-motor coordination, and cognitive workload. Simulator studies mostly used remote screen- or dashboard-mounted systems, whereas on-road studies mostly used head-mounted systems. Drivers in several populations showed delayed first fixation on hazards, fewer fixations on relevant targets, and narrower or spatially biased visual search than comparison drivers.ConclusionThese population-specific gaze signatures indicate that eye tracking offers an ecologically relevant complement to occupational therapy driving assessment. Normative gaze datasets, standardized reporting, and validated clinical thresholds are needed before eye-movement metrics can guide routine return-to-drive decisions.

articles.title: Higher incidence of paediatric autoimmune liver disease post-COVID.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: A higher incidence of autoimmune conditions with greater disease severity is reported post-Coronavirus Disease (COVID). The incidence and disease severity of paediatric autoimmune liver disease (AILD) post-COVID has not been assessed.

METHODS: Data on children <16 years of age diagnosed with AILD between 2015 and 2024 from a United Kingdom quaternary liver specialist centre was captured. Comparison of AILD incidence and presenting clinical characteristics in pre and post-COVID pandemic time-periods were made.

RESULTS: 199 patients were newly diagnosed with AILD within the study period (82 pre-COVID [2015-2019]; 47 autoimmune hepatitis type 1 [AIH-1], 11 AIH-2, 9 primary sclerosing cholangitis [PSC], 15 overlap/autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis [ASC], and 117 post-COVID [2020-2024]; 64 AIH-1, 10 AIH-2, 20 PSC, 23 overlap/ASC). A sharp rise in the incidence of AIH-1, PSC and overlap syndrome/ASC was observed post-COVID, being most marked in the AIH-1 cohort (p < 0.0001). Children were older at disease presentation for AIH-1, PSC and overlap/ASC compared to pre-COVID, particularly in AIH-1 (p = 0.0093). Minimal variation was observed in AIH-2 patients. Most patients presenting with AIH-1 and overlap/ASC post-COVID did not have a personal history of autoimmunity. High viral coinfection rates were observed in post-COVID AIH-1 and AIH-2 presentations.

CONCLUSION: The higher incidence and older presenting age of newly diagnosed AILD patients post-COVID may have resulted from immune dysregulation in susceptible children following the sudden exposure to viral infections after long periods of social isolation, triggering the onset of autoimmunity even in individuals without an autoimmune predisposition.

articles.title: Updated clinical recommendations for cardiovascular risk assessment to facilitate hormone therapy prescribing: incorporating PREVENT risk calculator and the 2026 multisociety lipid guidelines.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women and is a key consideration when evaluating candidates for menopausal hormone therapy (HT). Over the past two decades, recommendations regarding HT use have evolved substantially and now include the understanding that cardiovascular risk varies according to age, time since menopause onset, and baseline cardiovascular health. Consequently, cardiovascular risk assessment has become an integral component of menopause management. The recent introduction of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) calculator and incorporation of PREVENT into the 2026 American College of Cardioloty/Amercian Heart Association multisociety dyslipidemia guideline represent an important shift in CVD prevention. PREVENT includes contemporary cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk factors and estimates both 10-year and 30-year cardiovascular risk for adults ages 30-79 years without known CVD. Concurrently, updated lipid management recommendations emphasize individualized risk assessment and consideration of risk-enhancing factors, and in some cases, coronary artery calcium scoring, along with more explicit lipid-lowering targets. This perspective provides a practical framework for integrating PREVENT-derived risk categories into menopause care. We outline cardiovascular risk stratification strategies for women considering HT, discuss the role of coronary artery calcium scoring and female-specific risk enhancers, and align contemporary lipid management recommendations with decisions regarding initiation of HT, including route of administration. By integrating cardiovascular risk assessment and menopause management, clinicians can optimize cardiovascular risk reduction and individualize treatment decisions for symptomatic midlife women.

articles.title: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women: a cross-sectional NHANES analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To estimate associations between bilateral oophorectomy performed after natural menopause and prevalent cardiometabolic and skeletal outcomes in US women.

METHODS: We pooled 10 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cycles (1999-2018). The analytic cohort included 321 women with chronology-confirmed bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause and 5,363 referent women with natural menopause, no hysterectomy, and no confirmed bilateral oophorectomy. Survey-weighted quasi-Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PRs), adjusted for age, body mass index, education, smoking, alcohol use, and physical activity measured at the NHANES assessment. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control was applied across seven prespecified outcomes.

RESULTS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher cardiovascular disease prevalence (PR: 1.58; 95% CI: 1.13-2.21; P=0.008; q=0.039). Associations did not meet the false discovery rate threshold for diabetes (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.94-1.71), hypertension (PR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.93-1.22), osteoporosis (PR: 1.20; 95% CI: 0.90-1.60), or wrist fracture (PR: 1.54; 95% CI: 0.94-2.54). Hip and spine fractures were not estimable because of sparse exposed events. Adjustment for age at natural menopause attenuated the cardiovascular estimate (PR: 1.43; 95% CI: 1.02-2.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher self-reported cardiovascular disease prevalence. Because outcome timing relative to surgery was unavailable and residual confounding remains, this cross-sectional association should not be interpreted as causal or as a basis for clinical recommendations.

articles.title: Goodbye to randomized controlled trials on mechanical circulatory support.

Phenotypic age acceleration mediates the association between plant-based diet and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome among postmenopausal women: a population-based cross-sectional analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework highlights the links among metabolic disorders, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular complications. Research examining how plant-based dietary indices influence the progression of CKM and the potential role of biological aging remains limited.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from 2,988 postmenopausal women participating in NHANES 2005-2018. Weighted logistic regression models estimated the associations between plant-based dietary indices and advanced CKM. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate the mediating role of phenotypic age acceleration.

RESULTS: Among the study population, 658 participants (22.0%) were identified with advanced CKM. A one-unit increase in the plant-based diet index (PDI) and the healthful PDI was associated with a lower odds of advanced CKM (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.96-1.00 and OR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.94-0.99, respectively). In contrast, each one-unit increase in the unhealthful PDI was associated with 4% higher odds of advanced CKM (adjusted OR: 1.04; 95% CI: 1.01-1.07). These associations were consistent across population subgroups. Furthermore, phenotypic age acceleration partially mediated the association between PDI and advanced CKM, accounting for 16.0% (95% CI: 8.2%-25.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to healthy plant-based dietary patterns is associated with a lower likelihood of advanced CKM among postmenopausal women. The association between PDI with advanced CKM may be partly mediated through reduced phenotypic age acceleration.

articles.title: Development and validation of a TRUS-based prostate cancer prediction model with PSAD stratification in a two-center Western Chinese cohort: a retrospective cohort study with cost-effectiveness analysis.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific antigen screening has a low positive predictive value in low-incidence populations, leading to unnecessary biopsies. In this study, we developed and validated a prostate cancer prediction model incorporating transrectal ultrasound features and prostate-specific antigen density stratification and evaluated its cost-effectiveness. This dual-center retrospective study included 767 men with prostate-specific antigen levels of ≥4 ng ml-1 (training cohort, n = 558; validation cohort, n = 209). Prostate-specific antigen density was stratified into five categories. A logistic regression model was developed and validated. The cost-effectiveness of four screening strategies was evaluated. Five independent predictors were identified: age, prostate-specific antigen density stratification, extraprostatic extension, solid hypoechoic lesions, and unclear boundary. The model showed good discrimination (0.915 and 0.943 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively) and calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.57). The high-threshold strategy (≥0.5) avoided 47.0% of biopsies, and had the lowest total cost. In the biopsy cohort, the cost per cancer detected was the lowest in men with prostate-specific antigen density ≥0.15 ng ml-2 (83 295 Chinese Yuan). This model can reduce unnecessary biopsies in men with elevated prostate-specific antigen levels identified from opportunistic testing, but it is not suitable for population-wide screening given its unfavorable cost-effectiveness. It provides incremental value in resource-limited settings rather than serves as a practice-changing alternative to contemporary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based pathways.

articles.title: Clinical utility of the triglyceride-glucose index in assessing metabolic dysregulation among pulmonary tuberculosis patients.
articles.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health burden, particularly in resource-limited settings. Our cross-sectional study, conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Delhi (September 2022-February 2024), evaluated 130 newly diagnosed pulmonary TB patients to assess the utility of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index as a screening tool for insulin resistance and metabolic dysregulation in pulmonary tuberculosis patients. Diabetes was present in 26.2% of participants. The TyG index demonstrated strong positive correlations with HbA1c in both diabetic and non-diabetic groups. It was significantly associated with microbiological severity indicators, including sputum grading, culture positivity time and Ct values. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance for detecting diabetes, with a cut-off ≥4.895 achieving 100% sensitivity and 94% specificity. Overall, the TyG index emerges as a simple, cost-effective marker for early identification of metabolic derangement and disease severity in pulmonary TB, supporting its potential role in screening in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Implementation of the PaliEnf Digital Technology Based on Standardized Nursing Languages to Improve Nursing Documentation in Pediatric Oncology Palliative Care.
articles.abstract: AimTo evaluate the effect of the PaliEnf application on the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care.MethodsThis quasi-experimental study compared pre- and post-intervention periods and was conducted in accordance with the Transparent Reporting of Evaluations with Nonrandomized Designs (TREND) guidelines in a Pediatric Oncology Intensive Care Unit at a Brazilian national cancer referral center. The intervention consisted of implementing the PaliEnf application, a digital technology structured according to the NANDA International (NANDA-I), Nursing Interventions Classification (NIC), and Nursing Outcomes Classification (NOC) systems. Ten nurses were trained to use the application. The quality of nursing process documentation was assessed before and after the intervention using the Quality of Diagnoses, Interventions and Outcomes (Q-DIO) instrument. Comparisons between periods were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test, adopting a significance level of 5%.ResultsA total of 40 medical records were analyzed, including 20 from the pre-intervention period and 20 from the post-intervention period. Significant improvement in nursing process documentation was observed following implementation of the PaliEnf application, with increased scores across all Q-DIO dimensions (p < 0.001). The overall Q-DIO score increased from a median of 16.5 (IQR: 15.75-19.75) to 43.5 (IQR: 41.00-44.25). The greatest improvements were identified in items related to diagnostic structuring, coherence among nursing diagnoses, interventions, and outcomes, and documentation of patients' clinical progress.ConclusionImplementation of the PaliEnf application was associated with significant improvement in the quality of nursing process documentation in pediatric oncology palliative care. The findings suggest that digital technologies grounded in standardized nursing languages may support structured documentation and improve the internal coherence of the nursing process in complex clinical settings. Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (REBEC): UTN U1111-1297-9546.

articles.title: Carbamylome analysis reveals regulatory roles for lysine carbamylation in β-cell glycolytic and insulin-processing enzymes.
articles.abstract: In type 1 diabetes (T1D), insulin-producing β cells are destroyed by an autoimmune response driven by pro-inflammatory cytokines. The signaling of these cytokines is partially mediated by post-translational modifications, such as phosphorylation and acetylation. However, the role of other post-translational modifications in β-cell cytokine signaling represents an important knowledge gap. In the context of autoimmune diseases, lysine carbamylation has gained attention for its role in pathogenesis. Here, we investigate possible roles of carbamylation in T1D. We found that pancreata from the T1D model, non-obese diabetic (NOD) mice, at pre-diabetic stage (8-9 weeks old) exhibit 11% carbamylation-positive β cells, whereas non-diabetic CD1 mice have only 5%. Proteomics analysis of the MIN6 insulin-producing cell line treated with a cocktail of three pro-inflammatory cytokines IFNγ + IL-1β + TNFα identified 284 carbamylated peptides from 222 proteins regulated by the cytokine treatment. Integration of carbamylation and acetylation provided a deep view of the cytokine-regulated PTMs and potential points of interplay. A functional-enrichment analysis revealed that carbamylation was enriched in pathways related to autoimmune diseases, metabolism, DNA replication, and protein translation. Moreover, functional testing demonstrated that carbamylation inhibits the glycolytic enzyme aldolase A and the insulin-processing enzyme carboxypeptidase E, identifying a possible role for cytokine-induced β-cell dysfunction. In summary, NOD mice have more carbamylated β cells than CD1 mice, and pro-inflammatory cytokine treatment regulates protein carbamylation in MIN6 cells. These data identified carbamylation as a potential regulatory mechanism for β-cell metabolism and insulin production in insulitis.

articles.title: Impact of age on implementation and tolerability of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Elderly patients constitute a growing proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated the impact of age on the implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in HFrEF.

METHODS: TITRATE-HF is a prospective, multicentre registry (enrolment June 2022-February 2024) including patients with de novo, chronic, and worsening heart failure (HF). For the current analysis, HFrEF patients were categorized by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). We assessed GDMT implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes (composite endpoint: first HF hospitalization or all-cause death).

RESULTS: The cohort included 980 patients aged <65 years (29%), 1120 patients aged 65-74 years (33%), and 1267 patients aged ≥75 years (38%). At 12-month follow-up, younger patients more frequently received GDMT, with quadruple therapy prescribed in 68% of those aged <65 years, 61% aged 65-74 years, and 51% aged ≥75 years (P < .001). In de novo HFrEF, age-related differences were observed within weeks after diagnosis, with faster and more extensive GDMT intensification in younger patients. Still, rates of treatment downgrades and the distribution of side effects were largely similar across age groups. Significant left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement was observed in all age groups (all P < .001). The use of quadruple therapy at 6 months was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint between 6 and 12 months (adjusted hazard ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.86, P = .002), with consistent associations across age groups (P for interaction = .46).

CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with HFrEF received less intensive GDMT. Age-related differences emerged early after diagnosis, with fewer treatment intensifications in elderly patients but largely similar downgrade rates across age groups. These findings highlight the need for improved implementation strategies to optimize guideline-directed therapy and dosing levels in the ageing HFrEF population.

articles.title: Temporal and Vessel-Specific Relationship Between Post-PCI Fractional Flow Reserve and Long-Term Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) fractional flow reserve (FFR) reflects residual physiological impairment after stent implantation and is a proven predictor of procedural success and prognosis. However, the temporal dynamics of its prognostic utility and its potential variation according to the target vessel remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore vessel-specific post-PCI FFR thresholds and evaluate their prognostic consistency over 5 years.

METHODS: We analyzed 2128 patients undergoing successful drug-eluting stent implantation from the international Post-PCI FFR Extended registry. Patients were stratified according to the target vessel: left anterior descending artery (LAD) versus non-LAD. The primary end point was 5-year target vessel failure, defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization. Restricted cubic spline models were used to explore the continuous association between post-PCI FFR and target vessel failure and to identify vessel-specific risk thresholds. Temporal prognostic performance was assessed via 3-year landmark analysis and time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: During 5-year follow-up, target vessel failure occurred in 176 patients (11.7%) with LAD lesions and 74 patients (11.7%) with non-LAD lesions. Lower post-PCI FFR was independently associated with a higher risk of target vessel failure in both LAD and non-LAD vessels. Spline analyses characterized vessel-stratified risk patterns, and exploratory comparisons used post-PCI FFR cut points of 0.83 for LAD and 0.94 for non-LAD vessels. Landmark analysis indicated that the excess hazard associated with suboptimal FFR was predominantly concentrated within the first 3 years postprocedure. Nevertheless, time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic analysis demonstrated modest but stable discriminatory power of post-PCI FFR throughout the 5-year follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI FFR provides sustained 5-year prognostic insight, though the exploratory vessel-stratified cut points require external validation. Although the associated risk is highest in the early to mid-term period, predictive discrimination persists long-term. These findings advocate for vessel-specific interpretation of post-PCI physiology to refine risk stratification and patient management.

articles.title: Preoperative Telehealth Versus In-Person Appointments Prior to Lumbar Fusion: Influence on Surgical Planning and Postoperative Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective study.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of attending a preoperative telehealth appointment, compared to in-person, on intraoperative surgical plan change and postoperative outcomes following lumbar fusion.

SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Telehealth utilization for orthopedic appointments has greatly increased due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Spine surgery remains controversial, as surgical planning relies heavily on objective physical exam and imaging data. As such, controversy surrounding the utility and safety of telehealth in preoperative spine surgery planning remains.

METHODS: Adult patients who underwent elective lumbar fusion (2020-2022) were identified at a single tertiary center. Patients with a surgical indication of revision, malignancy, trauma, or infection were excluded. The final preoperative appointment type (telehealth vs. in-person) was determined. Surgical and clinical outcomes, including intraoperative surgical plan change, postoperative phone calls, in-person office visits, emergency department (ED) visits, opioid usage, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), were collected. An α was set at 0.05.

RESULTS: Of 544 patients were included (18.8% telehealth). Utilization of telehealth appointments was similar before versus after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted in October 2021. Changes from preoperative surgical plan occurred at a similar rate between groups. Preoperative telehealth appointment was found to be an independent predictor of requiring fewer postoperative office visits (estimate: -0.55, P=0.002), but a higher likelihood of visiting the ED (OR: 4.59, P=0.011). Although telehealth users had decreased opioid utilization from 90 to 365 days postoperatively and improved VAS Back scores at 1 year after surgery, these findings were not significant on multivariable analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Telehealth utilization in spine surgery remains common postpandemic. The current work showed that lumbar fusion preoperative planning via telehealth is reliable compared to in-person appointments. Interestingly, telehealth decreased postoperative office-visit utilization but increased ED visits. Further study is needed to investigate the clinical significance of these observations.

articles.title: Genetically Predicted MRI Phenotypes Are Associated with Risk of Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Brain atrophy is a hallmark of multiple sclerosis (MS) and precedes clinical symptom onset. However, whether brain development and morphological measures contribute to MS susceptibility remains unclear. We investigated whether genetically determined brain imaging phenotypes are associated with MS risk.

METHODS: We applied causal inference approaches using genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for 170 heritable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived phenotypes from 39,691 United Kingdom (UK) Biobank participants and leveraged with MS susceptibility GWAS data from 14,802 MS patient and 26,703 controls. Generalized summary-data-based Mendelian randomization with HEIDI filtering was used to assess putative causal associations while accounting for horizontal pleiotropy, with orthogonal sensitivity analysis using 2-sample Mendelian randomization. Significant loci underwent functional annotation, Bayesian colocalization with brain expression quantitative trait loci, integration with single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from MS postmortem tissue, and druggability assessment. False discovery rate adjustments were applied.

RESULTS: Four MRI phenotypes were associated with MS susceptibility: cerebellar vermis VIIIa gray-matter volume, mean diffusivity of the right anterior corona radiata, intracellular volume fraction of the corpus callosum, and orientation dispersion index of the right external capsule. Functional analyses identified 120 candidate genes, including several within the complex 17q21.31 locus. Cell-type-specific Mendelian randomization identified higher genetically predicted PLEC expression in inhibitory neurons and microglia as associated with lower MS susceptibility. Differential gene expression analyses highlighted convergent dysregulation of MAPT, EGFR, and HBEGF, implicating neurodevelopmental, neurovascular, and autophagy-related pathways. Twenty-five candidate genes were identified as potentially druggable targets.

INTERPRETATION: Genetically determined brain structural traits are associated with MS susceptibility, supporting the concept that premorbid brain architecture contributes to disease vulnerability and highlighting potential therapeutic targets. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: Association between excess body weight and adverse effects using real body weight-based teprotumumab dosing in thyroid eye disease.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Monoclonal antibody therapies are often dosed using real body weight (RBW) to theoretically minimize inter-patient variability in drug distribution and elimination. However, pharmacokinetic modeling suggests that monoclonal antibodies primarily distribute to plasma and extracellular fluid compartments, which increase less than proportionally with excess body weight. Intravenous teprotumumab is currently administered using RBW-based dosing, but the impact of deviations from ideal body weight (IBW) on treatment response or adverse effects remains unclear.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 95 patients treated with teprotumumab for Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). AEs were graded with Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE); high-grade was defined as grade ≥2. An IBW multiple (IBWM) for each patient was derived from RBW/IBW. Proptosis improvement was the millimeters reduction in Hertel exophthalmometry of the worse eye. Associations with IBWM were assessed using logistic and linear regression adjusted for age and diabetes.

RESULTS: Median IBWM was 1.30 (range 0.84-2.98). Grade ≥1 AEs occurred in 86.3% and grade ≥2 in 30.5%. Higher IBWM was associated with greater odds of grade ≥2 AEs (adjusted OR 7.0, 95% CI 1.6-30.8; p = 0.010) and grade ≥2 AEs excluding hyperglycemia (adjusted OR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-24.3; p = 0.020), but not with proptosis improvement (β ≈ 0.08 mm; p = 0.89). No patient at or below ideal body weight (IBWM ≤ 1; n = 7) experienced a grade ≥2 AE.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher RBW dose intensity was associated with more high-grade toxicity without greater proptosis benefit. These findings suggest that RBW dosing may expose overweight patients to increased toxicity and support investigation of alternative dosing strategies for teprotumumab.

articles.title: Preliminary Stakeholder Evaluation of a Novel Weight History Interview for Eating Disorders: A Qualitative Analysis.
articles.journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Measures of weight history, such as weight suppression (the difference between one's highest past weight and current weight), have been associated with behavioural, cognitive, and biological facets of eating disorders (EDs), including purging frequency, leptin levels, and future weight gain (Lowe et al. 2018; Lowe 2020). Given these consistent associations, it would be desirable to develop a systematic framework to gather patients' weight history in clinical settings. This study was the first stage in developing a weight history interview (WHI).

METHOD: Ten former patients and three clinicians from a residential ED treatment facility participated in separate focus groups to elicit feedback on the relevance, clarity, utility, and potential emotional impact of the first iteration of the WHI. Additionally, we administered surveys to gather quantitative feedback.

RESULTS: Thematic analysis (Braun and Clarke 2006) of qualitative data identified seven themes highlighting participants' feedback and suggestions for future development of the WHI. Descriptive statistics of quantitative data largely reflected participants' mixed reactions.

CONCLUSIONS: Key stakeholders' feedback was used to identify suggested modifications for future versions of the WHI, including strategies to increase acceptability. The ultimate goal of this effort is to establish a weight history interview for use in clinical settings.

articles.title: Reconstructive Surgical Outcomes in War Trauma During the Sudan Current Conflict: A 491-Patient Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic injuries resulting from armed conflict are complex and require urgent and efficient reconstructive surgical care. In a resource-limited environment, such as the situation in Sudan during the ongoing armed conflict, delivery of such care is affected by the delayed presentation of patients with contaminated injuries and infrastructure destruction. Our study evaluates the patterns of conflict-related injuries, reconstructive surgical interventions, and postoperative outcomes during the current conflict in Sudan.

METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study from a major tertiary hospital in Sudan that included 491 patients who underwent reconstructive surgical interventions between October 2023 and December 2024. Data were collected from hospital records and operative logs.

RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 31.7 ± 10.5 years, with most patients aged 18-35 years. The main mechanisms of injury were shrapnel/explosive fragmentation (42.8%) and gunshot wounds (41.8%). Extremities were most commonly affected, particularly the hand (23.8%). Skin and soft tissue procedures were the most frequently performed (42.6%), while only 7.7% required flap reconstruction. General anesthesia was used in 64% of cases, and most procedures were performed within 90 minutes. The length of hospital stay was 5 days for the majority of patients (63.1%). Postoperative complications occurred in 25.5% of patients, with postoperative wound infection being the most common (14.3%). Significant associations with complications were observed for injury site (p < 0.001), flap type (p = 0.031), and length of hospital stay (p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Armed conflict-related injuries in Sudan primarily affect young adults and are mostly caused by High-energy trauma, including penetrating injuries. Due to severe resource constraints, most cases were managed with relatively simple reconstructive techniques and achieved acceptable short-term outcomes. The study's findings emphasize the importance of adaptable, mindful surgical strategies tailored to available resources and highlight the critical role of reconstructive surgery in conflict settings.

articles.title: Metagenomic analysis of peritonitis with filamentous bacteria in dogs and cats reveals polymicrobial communities beyond bacteria with filamentous morphology.
articles.journal: Journal of veterinary diagnostic investigation : official publication of the American Association of Veterinary Laboratory Diagnosticians, Inc
articles.abstract: Filamentous bacteria commonly cause chronic cutaneous or subcutaneous infections in dogs and cats; abdominal infections restricted to the mesentery are rare. We reviewed 12 cases (6 dogs, 6 cats) of peritonitis associated with filamentous bacteria, including 7 biopsies and 6 autopsies. We extracted DNA from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues in 10 cases for 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Recent abdominal surgery was reported in 4 cases. Two dogs had chronic disease, and 2 cats had lymphoma. Cytologic examination of peritoneal fluid was performed in 5 cases; 4 had neutrophilic inflammation with filamentous bacteria, rods, and cocci. Autopsy revealed a diffusely thickened, pale-tan and firm mesentery. Pyogranulomatous peritonitis with filamentous bacteria was found on histology in 11 cases. Filamentous bacteria had variable histochemical staining properties and were consistently argyrophilic. Bacterial culture, performed on the peritoneal fluid or mesentery of 6 cases, rarely isolated filamentous bacteria and had poor agreement with sequencing results. Metagenomic analysis demonstrated heterogeneous bacterial communities, indicating that filamentous bacteria were part of a broader microbial population rather than the sole etiologic agents. Sequencing profiles suggested environmental, cutaneous, oral, or gastrointestinal origins, supporting abdominal contamination secondary to surgery, bite wounds, or gastrointestinal perforation as likely sources of infection.

articles.title: Anti-ZIKV IgG Subclass Profiles and Anti-DENV IgG Are Associated With Neonatal Outcomes Following ZIKV Infection During Pregnancy.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Most infected individuals present mild symptoms; however, vertical transmission of ZIKV can lead to Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS), which includes microcephaly, neurological, hearing, ophthalmological, and morphological abnormalities. Given the high prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) exposure and antibody cross-reactivity among flaviviruses, understanding how maternal humoral antibody profiles relate to neonatal outcomes after ZIKV infection is important. In this exploratory study, we evaluated maternal and neonatal anti-ZIKV total IgG, anti-ZIKV IgG1 and anti-ZIKV IgG3, and anti-DENV IgG reactivity in relation to maternal-neonatal antibody patterns and neonatal outcomes. Samples from pregnant women and their newborns were collected in Brazil, including pregnancies with microcephaly and other clinical or imaging abnormalities. Anti-ZIKV and anti-DENV IgG reactivity was measured by ELISA. Lower neonatal anti-ZIKV IgG3 reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities in the individual comparison, although this association did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Lower neonatal anti-DENV IgG reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities and with any clinical or imaging abnormality, and both associations remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. These exploratory associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish functional protection or a causal role for the measured antibody profiles.

articles.title: Somatic-to-autonomic ilioinguinal nerve grafting for post-radical prostatectomy erectile dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of a novel somatic-to-autonomic nerve grafting procedure for erectile function restoration in men with persistent erectile dysfunction (ED) following radical prostatectomy (RP).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 10 patients with normal pre-RP erectile function defined by a five-item International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) score ≥17, and persistent ED (IIEF-5 score ≤7) for >18 months after RP were enrolled in this pilot trial. A novel bilateral end-to-side neurorrhaphy was performed between the dorsal penile nerves and the corpora cavernosa using an ilioinguinal nerve autograft. Baseline assessments included the IIEF-5 and Clinical Evolution of Erectile Function (CEEF) questionnaires for erectile function and McGill University's validated short-form pain questionnaire. Postoperative evaluations were performed at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Data collection includes demographics, perioperative outcomes, and both primary (safety/feasibility) and secondary (erectile function) endpoints.

RESULTS: The median (interquartile range [IQR]) patient age was 63.5 (57.5-67.3) years. Three patients had undergone non-nerve-sparing, four had unilateral nerve-sparing, and three had bilateral nerve-sparing RP. The median (IQR) IIEF-5 score before RP was 25 (25-25), dropping to 5 (5-5) after RP. The median (IQR) time from RP to nerve grafting was 34.7 (22.5-39.2) months with a median (IQR) operative time of 76.5 (70-82.8) min. Postoperative incisional pain was minimal. Six patients reported mild ipsilateral scrotal numbness. One patient developed a Clavien-Dindo Grade II wound infection, while two patients had Grade I haematomas. At the 12-month follow-up, all patients experienced a significant improvement in subjective erectile function from a median score of 0/10 to 7/10 (P = 0.004). The median (IQR) IIEF-5 score at the 12-month follow-up was 10 (5-14) achieving statistical significance (P = 0.031), and five patients had regained erections sufficient for penetrative intercourse.

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that bilateral end-to-side neurorrhaphy using an ilioinguinal nerve autograft is feasible and safe. The 1-year erectile function recovery data is promising, showing meaningful improvements from baseline. This technique may offer a novel therapeutic avenue for post-RP ED and warrants further investigation in larger trials.

articles.title: Pediatric Le Fort Fractures: Does Surgical Timing Predict Complications and Length of Stay?
articles.abstract: Operative timing, complications, and length of stay (LOS) across pediatric Le Fort fracture types remain poorly characterized. Using Pediatric Health Information System data from 2015 to 2025, the authors identified patients with isolated Le Fort type I, II, or III fractures undergoing repair and compared time to procedure, complications, hospital LOS, as well as rates of concomitant traumatic brain injury (TBI) and cervical spine injury (CSI). Among 350 patients (I, 150; II, 114; III, 86), time to first procedure did not differ by type, but time to repair increased with fracture type (2.9, 5.1, 6.7 d; P < 0.001). Respiratory, neurologic, ophthalmologic, hematologic, and metabolic complications increased stepwise across fracture types, whereas dental and occlusal complications predominated in type I. Likewise, concomitant TBI and CSI increased with fracture type. In multivariable analysis, Le Fort type was not an independent predictor of LOS (P = 0.2). Presence of any complication (incidence rate ratio: 2.60), intensive care unit admission (1.46), concomitant TBI (1.43), high-acuity CSI (1.44), and longer time to repair (1.48 per log-day) independently predicted longer hospital LOS (all P < 0.01). Higher grade Le Fort fracture type aligned with delayed repair, greater complication burden, and longer stay, but appeared to mark injury severity rather than independently determine LOS.

articles.title: A Graded Immune-Cell-Resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian Randomisation Screen Across Systemic Lupus Erythematosus and Related Immune Phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a genetically complex autoimmune disease. Whole-blood expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses capture average regulatory effects across leukocytes, whereas SLE involves immune processes that depend on cell context. Therefore, a cell-resolved screen requires rigorous verification of instrument identity, allele orientation, and the multiple-testing denominator before biological interpretation.

AIMS: To conduct an identity-first, immune-cell-resolved cis-eQTL Mendelian randomization (MR) screen across SLE and related immune phenotypes and distinguish statistical signal counts from variant-level, regional, and cross-cell evidence.

STUDY DESIGN: Two-sample summary-data cis-eQTL MR and secondary evidence synthesis using 15 primary human immune-cell types from Database of Immune-Cell Expression (DICE) and eight disease outcomes from FinnGen release 12.

METHODS: All 19,009 gene-cell-type instruments were audited before outcome testing. Only 6,525 instruments with exact variant identities and concordant DICE effect information were retained for analysis. Wald ratios were calculated for 48,958 outcome-instrument tests, with the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure applied separately to each outcome to control the false discovery rate (FDR). Both prespecified infection-negative controls were then matched exactly by cell type, gene, and rsID, with each contributing 6,119 tests. For the sensitivity analysis, each chi-square statistic was divided by its outcome-specific genomic control inflation factor (lambda GC), and the BH procedure was reapplied within each outcome. Audited signals were summarized by unique single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), linkage disequilibrium (LD)-independent index signal, gene-outcome relationship, and MHC location. Regional colocalization, bounded multivariable MR, and Gene Ontology analyses provided additional layers of evidence.

RESULTS: The identity-first audit retained 6,525 of 19,009 instruments. Of these, 6,122 matched at least one outcome, whereas 403 did not. Among the 48,958 strict tests, 1,186 rows reached an outcome-specific FDR of less than 0.05, corresponding to 304 genes, 494 SNPs, 868 cell-gene pairs, and 424 gene-outcome relationships. LD auditing resolved 670 outcome-specific lead-SNP records into 639 reference-matched records and 31 separately reported records, yielding 288 LD-independent index signals. The primary SLE analysis identified 55 FDR-significant signals, 23 genes, 29 SNPs, and 11 index signals; 16 of the 23 genes and 6 of the 11 index signals were located in the MHC. The second SLE definition showed a similarly strong concentration of signals in the MHC. Most non-MHC disease signals were associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and autoimmune hypothyroidism (AIH). Lambda GC ranged from 1.17 to 2.03 across disease outcomes. Following outcome-specific lambda adjustment, 483 disease rows remained FDR-significant. The greatest reductions in significant rows occurred for AIH (691-211), RA (213-103), and strict MI (83-11). The negative controls, other sepsis and bacterial infection not otherwise specified (NOS), each matched 6,119 tests and had lambda GC values of 1.06 and 1.08, respectively. No FDR-significant rows were identified for bacterial infection NOS.

CONCLUSION: This revised analysis provides a graded and auditable screening framework rather than a definitive list of SLE risk genes. The primary SLE evidence is concentrated in the 6p21/MHC region, whereas broader non-MHC candidate signals arise predominantly from related immune phenotypes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require independent replication and experimental validation.

articles.title: Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis in Cirrhosis: A Network Meta-analysis of Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: The relative efficacy of antibiotic prophylaxis for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) remains uncertain. We performed a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of prophylactic antibiotic regimens.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for RCTs of antibiotic prophylaxis in cirrhosis. Primary outcomes were SBP incidence and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight RCTs were included. For all-cause mortality, the network was coherent, and rifaximin (risk ratio [RR], 0.50; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.33-0.76), trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (RR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.25-0.90), norfloxacin plus rifaximin (RR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.17-0.86), and norfloxacin (RR, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.52-0.91) were associated with lower mortality. For SBP incidence, node-splitting revealed significant incoherence for rifaximin (P=0.015): direct evidence from five double-blind placebo-controlled trials (RR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.27-1.25) diverged from indirect evidence via open-label head-to-head trials (RR, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.07-0.33). In primary prophylaxis, rifaximin (RR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.22-0.76), norfloxacin (RR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.22-0.78), and norfloxacin plus rifaximin (RR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.10-0.75) reduced SBP incidence. In secondary prophylaxis, rifaximin showed the largest reduction in recurrence (RR, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.02-0.29), anchored on one placebo-controlled trial. The preventive effect attenuated with calendar year for SBP (ratio of risk ratios, 1.038 per year; 95% CI, 1.008-1.068; P=0.012) but not for mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: Antibiotic prophylaxis is associated with lower all-cause mortality in cirrhosis with ascites, with rifaximin showing the most consistent survival benefit. However, its SBP estimate was not reproduced in blinded placebo-controlled trials, and the preventive effect against SBP attenuated over time.

articles.title: Podocarpusflavone A sensitizes MASLD-related hepatocellular carcinoma to lenvatinib by targeting ABAT and ALDH2.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Despite the rising global incidence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease-related hepatocellular carcinoma (MASLD-HCC), immunotherapy offers limited survival benefits in this non-viral etiology, positioning lenvatinib as a critical treatment that necessitates novel strategies to enhance its efficacy. This study aimed to identify MASLD-HCC signature genes and to explore a novel agent to overcome lenvatinib resistance.

METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing identified signature genes, validated by immunohistochemistry, qPCR, Western blot, and spatial transcriptomics in human and murine specimens. Virtual screening identified a natural compound targeting hub genes. Direct binding was confirmed using molecular dynamics simulations, cellular thermal shift assays, and surface plasmon resonance. Therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms were comprehensively evaluated in vitro under lipotoxic stress conditions and in vivo using diet-induced orthotopic MASLD-HCC mouse models.

RESULTS: A 170-gene signature was established, with ABAT and ALDH2 prioritized as hub genes. Podocarpusflavone A (PCFA) emerged as a dual-targeting agent that robustly reverses acquired lenvatinib resistance. Instead of increasing protein abundance, PCFA directly binds these targets, which is accompanied by markedly enhanced cellular ABAT and ALDH activities. This diminishes the protective GABA shield and disrupts the mitochondrial NAD⁺ balance, precipitating a lethal mitochondrial superoxide burst and inhibiting key oncogenic pathways. In vivo, the PCFA and lenvatinib combination profoundly suppressed orthotopic tumor progression and was associated with short-term improvements in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis-related histological findings, with no evident toxicity under the conditions tested.

CONCLUSIONS: PCFA combined with lenvatinib represents a promising strategy for MASLD-HCC and provides mechanistic insights into its antitumor activity.

articles.title: Target Trial Emulation: A Practical Introduction for Hepatology Research.
articles.abstract: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are considered the gold standard for causal inference; however, in hepatology research, their feasibility is often limited by ethical constraints, long disease trajectories, and complex treatment decisions. As a result, real-world data (RWD) are increasingly used, but conventional observational analyses remain vulnerable to biases such as immortal time bias, confounding, and misalignment between clinical questions and study design. Target trial emulation (TTE) addresses these limitations by explicitly defining a hypothetical randomized trial and emulating it using observational data. TTE can estimate clinically relevant causal estimands, including observational analogues of the intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol effects, by explicitly defining treatment strategies and follow-up procedures. This paper provides a practical guide to the application of TTE in hepatology research, focusing on key principles of causal inference design using the TTE framework. Using the HEROES study as an illustrative example, we show how target trial components-eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, and estimand-can be explicitly specified from clinical questions. We describe the sequential trial emulation (STE) approach, in which a single observational cohort is reformulated into a series of risk-set-based hypothetical trials over time to address time-varying treatment initiation, and the cloning-censoring-weighting (CCW) approach, which enables the emulation of dynamic treatment strategies in observational data. Overall, this paper emphasizes the importance of aligning clinical questions with the causal estimand and improving the transparency and validity of real-world evidence in hepatology.

articles.title: A Novel Competing-Risk Model Integrating Systemic Inflammation to Predict Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure.
authors: Korean Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (KACLiF) study group
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Absolute risk of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) can be overestimated when the hazards of competing events, such as liver transplantation (LT) or death without ACLF, are not incorporated. We developed and validated a novel competing-risk-based model integrating systemic inflammation to predict ACLF development.

METHODS: The derivation cohort comprised 1,146 patients with acute decompensation of cirrhosis from the prospective, multicenter Korean Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure (KACLiF) cohort. External validation used a retrospective 1,104-patient cohort. The study followed the TRIPOD+AI reporting guidelines and applied a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model accounting for the competing risks of death or LT, with predictive performance evaluated using the C-index and time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

RESULTS: The KACLiF-ACLF score integrated C-reactive protein, albumin, total bilirubin, international normalized ratio, and creatinine. In derivation, the competing-risk C-index (0.806 at 28 days; 0.791 at 90 days) significantly exceeded all eight comparators at 90 days, but not MELD or MELD-Na at 28 days. In external validation, it (0.892 and 0.889) significantly exceeded all comparators at both horizons. Time-dependent AUROCs at 28 days were 0.815 and 0.894, significantly exceeding all comparators at both horizons except MELD-Na at 28 days in derivation. Transported absolute risks were overpredicted, requiring recalibration. The model stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups, correlating with cumulative ACLF incidence and transplant-free survival (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: The KACLiF-ACLF score discriminates ACLF development with high accuracy in external validation and supports risk stratification within a competing-risk framework. Recalibrated absolute risks require independent validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: KASL Consensus Statement for Pharmacologic Treatment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis: Focus on Semaglutide.
authors: Korean Association for the Study of the Liver (KASL)
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) impose a rapidly increasing hepatic and cardiometabolic burden worldwide and in Korea. Following the phase 3 ESSENCE trial, which demonstrated the histological efficacy of semaglutide in noncirrhotic MASH with fibrosis, practical guidance for routine clinical care is needed. The Korean Association for the Study of the Liver developed this expert consensus statement on semaglutide treatment in MASH. Using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, a 15-member expert panel rated 98 clinical scenarios covering patient selection, dosing, response assessment, adverse event management, and metabolic comorbidities over two rating rounds with a structured panel discussion. Semaglutide is primarily intended for patients with noncirrhotic MASH and stage 2-3 fibrosis. Eligibility should be assessed using a two-step strategy of age-adjusted Fibrosis-4 index screening followed by vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE). A VCTE-derived liver stiffness measurement (LSM) of 10-15 kPa defines the preferred treatment range; 15-20 kPa is acceptable when cirrhosis and portal hypertension are excluded, whereas 8-10 kPa requires repeat VCTE, magnetic resonance elastography (eligible range, 3.1-4.4 kPa), or liver biopsy. Semaglutide is initiated at 0.25 mg once weekly and escalated every 4 weeks to a target maintenance dose of 2.4 mg. Response should be assessed with noninvasive tests after at least 18 months; a ≥30% reduction in VCTE-derived LSM suggests response. This consensus provides a structured framework for semaglutide use in MASH, integrated with management of obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk, and chronic kidney disease.

articles.title: Combined Nonsurgical Endodontic Treatment and Palatal Endodontic Microsurgery for Oehlers Type IIIa Dens Invaginatus: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Dens invaginatus (DI) is an uncommon developmental dental anomaly. In complex cases, its aberrant anatomy, often combined with pulpal infection and periapical disease, presents substantial therapeutic challenges. This report describes a case of Oehlers type IIIa DI associated with chronic apical periodontitis in a maxillary lateral incisor. The patient presented with recurrent suppuration and pain in the maxillary anterior region. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) revealed a typical type IIIa DI in tooth 22, accompanied by extensive periapical bone destruction involving both teeth 21 and 22. Following a comprehensive evaluation, both teeth underwent nonsurgical root canal treatment, fibre-reinforced splinting, and palatal endodontic microsurgery. Follow-up examinations at 3, 10, 16 and 28 months demonstrated complete resolution of clinical symptoms and favourable radiographic healing, with progressive reduction of the periapical radiolucency and new bone formation. This case suggests that a combination of nonsurgical endodontic treatment and palatal endodontic microsurgery, guided by detailed CBCT assessment, may be considered in carefully selected cases of Oehlers type IIIa DI with extensive periapical lesions. The favourable outcome observed in this patient adds to the limited literature on tooth-preserving management of complex type IIIa DI.

articles.title: Severe Pannus Formation with Coronary Artery Obstruction after the Ozaki Procedure: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a case of severe pannus formation causing coronary artery obstruction after aortic valve neocuspidization (the Ozaki procedure). A 64-year-old woman who had undergone the Ozaki procedure for aortic stenosis presented with chest pain. She was diagnosed with obstruction of the right coronary artery ostium and moderate aortic regurgitation and stenosis. Redo aortic valve replacement and coronary artery bypass grafting were subsequently performed. Surgery revealed severe circumferential pannus on the aortic side of the neocusps, with obstruction of the right coronary artery ostium. The pannus and cusps were removed completely; after aortic annular enlargement, the aortic valve was replaced. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful. This is the first case report of coronary obstruction due to pannus formation after the Ozaki procedure.

articles.title: Opioid-Sparing Pain Control in Lung Transplantation: A Single-Center Experience with Intraoperative Intercostal Nerve Cryoablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pain following lung transplantation is substantial and contributes to opioid exposure, delirium risk, and prolonged recovery. We evaluated the impact of intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation on postoperative opioid use, delirium incidence, and early clinical outcomes.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective matched cohort study of adult lung transplant recipients. Patients who underwent intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation (intervention) were compared with a historical matched cohort of recipients who did not undergo cryoablation (control). The primary outcome was cumulative opioid use, measured in oral morphine milligram equivalents (MME), during the first 14 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included delirium incidence, ventilator days, intensive care unit and hospital lengths of stay, and early postoperative complications.

RESULTS: The study included 19 patients in the cryoablation group and 38 matched controls. Cryoablation was associated with a reduction in cumulative opioid use through postoperative day 14 (428 MME vs. 603 MME, p=0.681). Rates of postoperative delirium were slightly lower in the intervention group (58% vs. 66%, p=0.571). Cryoablation was not associated with increased complications. There were trends toward shorter median ventilator duration and total hospital length of stay in the intervention group, although results were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSION: Intraoperative intercostal nerve cryoablation is a feasible and safe adjunct in lung transplantation and is associated with reduced early postoperative opioid use. These findings support further prospective evaluation of cryoablation as an opioid-sparing strategy in lung transplant recipients.

articles.title: Coronary Artery Bypass Graft versus Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Patients with Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction: A Meta-Analysis of 29,554 Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of death worldwide, with coronary artery disease (CAD) and heart failure among its major contributors. This meta-analysis aimed to compare outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with CAD and left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction.

METHODS: The study followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Electronic databases were systematically searched for studies published from January 2006 to November 2025. Studies comparing CABG and PCI in patients with multivessel CAD and an LV ejection fraction <50% were eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 24 studies comprising 29,554 patients. CABG was associated with a higher risk of postoperative stroke (within 30 days or during hospitalization; odds ratio [OR], 1.98; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-3.78; p=0.04). Perioperative mortality, myocardial infarction, and heart failure incidence were comparable between the procedures. At 5-year follow-up, CABG was associated with lower risks of mortality (OR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.47-0.70; p<0.01), myocardial infarction (OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.20-0.50; p<0.01), worsening heart failure (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.28-0.823; p<0.001), and repeat revascularization (OR, 0.22; 95% CI, 0.16-0.30; p<0.01). The association between CABG and lower long-term mortality remained significant at 10-year follow-up (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.54-0.92; p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with multivessel CAD and LV systolic dysfunction, CABG was associated with lower mortality at 5 and 10 years than PCI, despite a higher risk of early postoperative stroke.

articles.title: A Biophysical Perspective on Microwave-Induced Neurobiological Effects.
articles.abstract: Microwave radiation interacts with the nervous system through a cascade of electromagnetic, thermal, and mechanical perturbations that drive a broad range of neurobiological responses. Although exposure guidelines are based on specific absorption rate (SAR), substantive evidence indicates that neurobiological effects arise across frequencies, waveforms, and SAR levels that SAR alone cannot characterize. We distinguish net-thermal, transient-thermal, and non-thermal mechanisms according to whether a response is mediated by the net temperature rise, by the heating rate and temperature gradients, or largerly independent of temperature change. This review traces the physical perturbation cascade from electromagnetic field distribution through thermal dynamics to thermoelastic stress, and reviews five biological endpoints: genotoxicity, molecular dysregulation and signaling, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, electrophysiology, and behavioral changes. A consistent finding is that many studies report associations with only SAR and frequency, omitting the intermediate physical quantities that drive the responses, and thus obscuring a mechanistic understanding of the causal chain. Mapping of reported studies into the SAR-frequency space reveals a clustering within the 0.9-3 GHz band and near SAR = 2 W/kg, with biological alterations reported below these limits under both continuous and pulsed exposures. These findings motivate future work that directly quantifies spatiotemporal physical perturbations to close the gap between exposure conditions and neurobiological outcomes.

articles.title: Serial changes in myocardial fluorodeoxyglucose uptake on routine oncologic PET during breast cancer chemotherapy: are they clinically relevant?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction is an important prognostic factor in patients with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy. We evaluated serial changes in myocardial fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) uptake on routine oncologic PET and assessed whether these changes differed according to chemotherapy regimen.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 535 FDG PET examinations obtained before and after chemotherapy in 108 patients with breast cancer. Mean FDG uptake was measured in the myocardium with the highest accumulation and in the descending aorta on the same cross-section, and their ratio was defined as the myocardial standard uptake ratio (M-SUR). Chemotherapy regimens were classified as anthracyclines, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), and others. Pre- and post-treatment M-SUR values were compared using the paired t-test.

RESULTS: A total of 309 paired examinations were analyzed: anthracyclines, 34 pairs (n = 17); HER2 inhibitors, 146 pairs (n = 40); ICI, 20 pairs (n = 9); and others, 109 pairs (n = 54). M-SUR significantly increased after anthracycline therapy (3.45 ± 2.44 to 5.37 ± 3.67, P = 0.046) and ICI therapy (3.78 ± 2.94 to 4.98 ± 4.27, P = 0.0328). No significant change was observed in the HER2 inhibitor or other regimen groups.

CONCLUSION: Serial FDG PET demonstrated regimen-dependent increases in myocardial FDG uptake after anthracycline and ICI therapy. Routine oncologic PET may reflect chemotherapy-related myocardial metabolic alterations.

articles.title: Return to Alcohol Use After Liver Transplant: Who Is at Risk?
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Alcohol-associated liver disease remains the leading indication for liver transplant (LT), yet there has been limited analysis of what psychosocial factors correlate with biomarker-confirmed return to alcohol use in the post-LT setting.
