MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a single-center, retrospective, cohort study of all adult patients with alcohol-associated liver disease who received a liver transplant (LT) between 2016 and 2022. Medical records were queried for demographics, psychosocial variables, pre-LT sobriety duration, and 1-year post-LT mortality. Logistic regression and time-to-event analysis was used to correlate these factors with post-LT biomarker-confirmed return to alcohol use, defined as at least 1 positive urine ethyl glucuronide, urine ethyl sulfate, or serum phosphatidylethanol. RESULTS Of 194 LT recipients, 52 (27% of all patients, 42% of those tested) tested positive for 1 or more alcohol biomarkers at least once. Female sex and younger age, but not pre-LT sobriety duration, were identified as independent risk factors for biomarker-confirmed post-LT return to alcohol use. Survival analysis identified a shorter time to biomarker confirmed return to alcohol use for patients with <6 months (P<0.0001) and 6-12 months (P<0.0001) of pre-LT sobriety, compared with those with ≥12 months sobriety. However, patients with shorter pre-LT sobriety duration underwent biomarker testing significantly earlier following LT (P<0.0001). There was no difference in 1-year post-LT mortality between patients with <6 months and those with > 6-month pre-LT sobriety. CONCLUSIONS In this retrospective cohort study, we observed that 1-year mortality and biomarker-confirmed return to alcohol use outcomes were not affected by pre-LT sobriety duration, supporting evolving standards that favor individualized risk assessment over fixed abstinence periods.

articles.title: Severe Cholestatic Jaundice With Negative Biliary Imaging in Decompensated Liver Cirrhosis: A Case Report.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Cholestatic jaundice with markedly elevated bilirubin levels usually raises concern for extrahepatic biliary obstruction or malignant hepatobiliary disease. However, marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia can occasionally occur in patients with cirrhosis despite repeatedly negative biliary imaging, creating substantial diagnostic uncertainty and management challenges. CASE REPORT We report a diagnostically challenging case of a 63-year-old Egyptian man presenting with progressive jaundice, dark urine, pale stool, pruritus, abdominal pain, fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and recent ascites. Laboratory investigations revealed severe conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with total bilirubin level reaching 19.45 mg/dL. Extensive infectious and viral investigations were negative. Autoimmune assessment demonstrated only weak anti-smooth muscle antibody positivity with otherwise negative autoimmune markers. Radiological evaluation including ultrasonography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated cirrhotic liver morphology, portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and gallbladder calculi without evidence of common bile duct obstruction, biliary dilatation, or pancreatic mass. The marked discrepancy between the severity of cholestasis and the absence of obstructive pathology created substantial diagnostic uncertainty, while the marked discrepancy between severe cholestasis and persistently negative biliary imaging raised concern for a possible nonobstructive cholestatic process associated with advanced chronic liver disease. The patient was treated conservatively with supportive medical therapy and careful clinical monitoring. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights that severe cholestatic jaundice in patients with cirrhosis does not necessarily indicate extrahepatic biliary obstruction. Integrating clinical, serological, and multimodal radiological findings is essential for excluding alternative etiologies and preventing unnecessary invasive biliary procedures.

articles.title: Diabetes care across the Islamic calendar: Ramadan fasting and Hajj pilgrimage.
articles.journal: Current opinion in endocrinology, diabetes, and obesity
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review highlights the unique considerations in managing diabetes among Muslims, focusing on Ramadan fasting and the Hajj pilgrimage, and offers practical guidance for clinicians and nurses.

RECENT FINDINGS: As the global population of Muslims with diabetes increases, periods such as Ramadan fasting and Hajj pilgrimage call for a structured approach to glycaemic management at scale. Wider availability of newer glucose-lowering therapies with lower hypoglycaemia risk and continuous glucose monitoring has made fasting safer. Under medical guidance, Ramadan fasting can be undertaken more safely through pre-Ramadan evaluation, including risk stratification, education and treatment optimization, followed by monitoring and timely intervention for complications during Ramadan. Hajj preparation also requires predeparture planning, early fitness preparation, and monitoring during travel and the rituals.

SUMMARY: With newer treatments and technologies, adequate and timely preparation enables safer Ramadan fasting under medical guidance. For Hajj, early physical fitness preparation, vaccinations and foot screening are needed alongside glycaemic optimization. A trusting, culturally sensitive patient-clinician relationship underpins safe fasting and pilgrimage.

articles.title: Dexmedetomidine Versus Propofol Induction for Sedated Radiologic Procedures in Patients With Trisomy 21.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patients with Trisomy 21 (T21) are more susceptible to sedation-related adverse events (AEs). Few studies address the risk of propofol or compare natural airway sedation regimens in this population. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) is less likely than propofol to result in AEs as it promotes a more natural sleep and less airway muscle relaxation.

METHODS: This study is a secondary analysis of prospectively collected data. We queried the Pediatric Sedation Research Consortium (PSRC) Database from the years 2020 to 2025. The demographic characteristics were summarized using descriptive statistics. The incidence of sedation-related AEs and sedation failures were described by induction drug (DEX vs. propofol). Any medication used other than DEX or propofol were excluded. We performed a propensity score analysis comparing the DEX cohort to the propofol cohort. All the statistical work was performed using SAS 9.4.

RESULTS: A total of 337 patients met inclusion criteria. The average age was 7 years. Forty-four percent of AEs were partial airway obstruction. For the bivariate analyses, the AE outcome variable is statistically significant with the medication variable (χ2df=1=33.249, P<0.001). Induction with propofol had a 5 times higher odds of an AE (OR=5.069, 95% CI: 2.829-9.082). After propensity score matching, there are a total of 216 matched observations.

CONCLUSION: In patients with T21 undergoing radiologic procedures, the odds of having any AE are higher with induction using propofol compared with DEX. Greater consideration should be given for use of DEX induction for patients with T21 undergoing sedated radiologic procedures.

articles.title: Biomarkers in Cardiology: A Critical Appraisal of Historical Successes, Pitfalls, and Emerging Uses.
articles.abstract: In preventive cardiology, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and blood pressure are validated surrogate endpoints, with multiple randomized trials demonstrating that their reduction improves cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. In contrast, raising high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) with niacin or cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitors failed to improve outcomes despite promising observational data and biological plausibility. In the Cardiac Arrhythmia Suppression Trial of class IC antiarrhythmics to suppress premature ventricular complexes, biomarker-targeted therapy increased mortality. Contemporary biomarkers, including lipoprotein(a), coronary artery calcium scoring, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, are increasingly used to refine risk and guide therapy. However, despite favorable guideline recommendations, randomized trials showing that biomarker-guided or biomarker-targeted treatment improves hard clinical endpoints are lacking. This review presents historical biomarker reversals in cardiology and critically appraises the evidence supporting emerging biomarkers. Our core argument is that practice recommendations for biomarker-guided therapy should await appropriately designed randomized trials adequately powered for cardiovascular events and mortality.

articles.title: Ventricular Assist Devices Effectively Bridge Pediatric Patients to Heart Retransplantation: An ACTION Registry Study.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: The use of ventricular assist devices (VAD) in pediatric patients as a bridge to heart transplantation has increased over the past two decades. However, the use of VAD to bridge pediatric transplant recipients to retransplantation is rare and under-studied. We performed a retrospective study using the Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network (ACTION) registry to evaluate patient characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients bridged to retransplant with VAD. A total of 24 patients were identified and supported for a median duration of 64 days (interquartile range [IQR]: 15.0-101.25). Of these, 54% (n = 13) were implanted as a bridge to retransplant candidacy (BTC) and 46% (n = 11) as a bridge to retransplant (BTT). We found a high prevalence of major adverse events, including infection in 75% (n = 18), bleeding in 42% (n = 10), renal dysfunction requiring dialysis in 33% (n = 8), and stroke in 8% (n = 2). Despite this, 71% (n = 17) survived to retransplant, with an 88% 1 year survival following retransplant. Device mortality was higher in BTC compared to BTT (46% vs. 9%; p = 0.046). Our study is the first multicenter study evaluating the use of VAD as a BTT. We exhibit a high prevalence of adverse events on VAD, but a favorable waitlist and post-retransplant survival.

articles.title: Prospective Evidence of Concomitant Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Risk Among Patients With Branch-duct Intraductal Papillary Mucinous Neoplasms Without Worrisome Features/High-risk Stigmata at Baseline.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the natural history, especially concomitant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (cPDAC) risk in patients with branch-duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (BD-IPMN) without worrisome features (WF) or high-risk stigmata (HRS).

SUMMARY BACKGROUND DATA: BD-IPMNs without WF/HRS are considered low-risk, yet optimal surveillance strategies remain uncertain.

METHODS: In a prospective multicenter Japan Pancreas Society registry, 1234 patients with BD-IPMN without WF/HRS underwent imaging and laboratory surveillance every 6 months for up to 5.17 years. Cumulative incidence, standardized incidence ratios (SIRs), and competing-risk analyses were performed to assess advanced pancreatic neoplasia, defined as IPMN high-grade dysplasia (IPMN-HGD), invasive IPMN, or cPDAC, and associated risk factors. Outcomes were also evaluated under simulated guideline-recommended extended surveillance intervals.

RESULTS: During 5.17 years of follow-up, advanced pancreatic neoplasia developed in 26 patients: 10 IPMN-HGD/invasive IPMN and 16 cPDAC. The 5.17-year cumulative incidence was 2.48%; SIRs relative to the general population were 8.01 overall, 3.07 for IPMN-HGD/invasive IPMN, and 4.91 for cPDAC. The cPDAC SIRs were 6.21 and 3.02 for cysts <20 mm and ≥20 mm, respectively. Diabetes history and mural nodule development predicted IPMN-HGD/invasive IPMN, whereas CA19-9 elevation and new or worsening diabetes predicted cPDAC. Of 19 patients eligible for surveillance interval extension, 13 (68%) had a later simulated detection date.

CONCLUSION: Patients with BD-IPMN without WF/HRS at baseline had 3.07 and 4.91 times the incidences of IPMN-HGD/invasive IPMN and cPDAC expected in the general population, respectively. Surveillance based solely on cyst stability may warrant caution regarding the timely detection of surgically resectable pancreatic cancer.

articles.title: Timing of transition from mechanical thrombectomy to intra-arterial alteplase and reperfusion quality in thrombectomy-refractory stroke.
articles.journal: Journal of cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO), but a subset of lesions remains refractory or technically challenging despite repeated mechanical attempts. Intra-arterial (IA) alteplase may be used as rescue therapy, but the optimal timing of transition from mechanical to pharmacological therapy remains unclear. We examined the association between the timing of this transition and reperfusion quality.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 90 consecutive patients with LVO treated with MT between July 2021 and December 2022. Sixteen patients received rescue IA alteplase after ineffective or unfeasible MT. Procedure time was divided into an MT phase (femoral puncture to IA alteplase initiation) and an IA phase (IA alteplase initiation to the end of the procedure). The primary outcome was excellent reperfusion, defined as modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) 2c-3.

RESULTS: Successful reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b) was achieved in 15 patients (93.8%), including excellent reperfusion in 8 (50.0%). The MT phase was shorter in the excellent than in the non-excellent reperfusion group (median, 49.5 vs. 87.5 minutes; p=0.028), whereas the difference in the IA phase was not statistically significant (36.5 vs. 75.5 minutes; p=0.068). No symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage occurred. Good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale ≤2) at 3 months was observed in 2 patients (12.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory series, a shorter period of MT before transition to IA alteplase was associated with excellent reperfusion. This hypothesis-generating finding suggests that the timing of transition may matter and warrants evaluation in larger, controlled studies.

articles.title: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted daily routines, physical activity, eating behaviors, and social interactions, all of which may have influenced body image. Previous research suggests that body image concerns differ by gender and may be particularly pronounced among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals, who face unique challenges due to internalized appearance ideals and societal stigma. This systematic review examined gender differences in body image-related concerns in the general adult population during the pandemic. Supported by: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (01KX2121).

METHODS: This systematic review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42023421727) and conducted according to PRESS, PRISMA guidelines. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO were searched for original studies published January 2019-July 2024. Studies were eligible if they 1) examined body image-related outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and reported gender-specific analyses in non-clinical adult populations. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Studies were narratively summarized according to body image-related constructs assessed and the reported gender-specific findings.

RESULTS: Sixteen studies comprising 9,813 participants were included. Across most studies, women reported greater body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame and guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men. Men generally reported lower body dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction and were more likely to perceive their bodies as slimmer or more athletic. However, three studies found no significant gender differences, and one study reported higher body dissatisfaction among men. Longitudinal evidence suggested increases in body dissatisfaction among men over the course of the pandemic, whereas weight concerns decreased among women over time. One study found higher levels of weight- and body-related shame and guilt among gender minority participants compared with cisgender men, while another study reported no association between sexual orientation and body appreciation.

CONCLUSIONS: Women generally reported greater body image-related concerns than men during the COVID-19 pandemic, although findings were not entirely consistent across studies. Evidence regarding SGM individuals remains limited due to their underrepresentation in the literature. Additional longitudinal and gender diverse research is needed to better understand body image changes during public health crises and to inform targeted prevention and intervention.

articles.title: Insulin Efsitora Alfa: First Approval.
articles.abstract: Insulin efsitora alfa (Onswik™) is a once-weekly ultra-long-acting recombinant basal insulin being developed by Eli Lilly and Company for the treatment of diabetes mellitus. Administered once weekly as a subcutaneous injection, insulin efsitora alfa is designed to provide a simplified treatment regimen relative to standard daily basal insulins. On 20 August 2026, insulin efsitora alfa received its first approval in the EU for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in adults. On 24 September 2026, insulin efsitora alfa was approved in the USA as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with T2DM. Insulin efsitora alfa is approved in the EU, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein and the USA and is under regulatory review in the UK and Japan for T2DM. This article summarizes the milestones in the development of insulin efsitora alfa leading to this first approval for T2DM.

articles.title: Structural dynamics of phosphorylated and ATP-bound glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta revealed by microsecond molecular dynamics simulations.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β) is a multifunctional serine/threonine kinase involved in a variety of cellular signaling pathways and has been associated with cancer, diabetes, and neurodegenerative disorders. Phosphorylation of Tyr216 is an important regulatory modification of GSK3β, but the effect of this modification on the structural dynamics of the kinase remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the effect of phosphorylation of Tyr216 on GSK3β in both apo and ATP-bound states using microsecond molecular dynamics simulations. We simulated the unphosphorylated apo, phosphorylated apo and phosphorylated ATP-bound GSK3β for 1 µs.Tyr216 phosphorylation decreased conformational fluctuations in important functional regions such as the activation loop, hinge region, glycine-rich loop, and αC-helix. The phospho-ATP bound system exhibited improved structural stability, continuous salt-bridge interactions and a more constrained conformational landscape than the respective apo state. Further analysis of the principal component and free energy landscape also suggested that phosphorylation stabilizes energetically favorable and dynamically conserved conformations. These findings provide atomic details on the phosphorylation-mediated regulation of GSK3β and its consequences on protein structural dynamics.

METHODS: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed for 1 µs under explicit-solvent conditions in the Schrodinger Maestro molecular modeling environment for each system. Structural and dynamic properties were evaluated by root-mean-square deviation, root-mean-square fluctuation, salt-bridge analysis, principal component analysis, and free-energy landscape analysis.

articles.title: Study on the occurrence and potential risks of microplastics in landscape water bodies with different supplementary water sources in Xi'an city.
articles.abstract: Urban landscape water bodies usually serve as buffer zones for human-nature interactions, which are replenished primarily by reclaimed and surface water. Thus, these areas have now become new hotspots for microplastic pollution due to the low-efficiency removal of microplastics after water treatment. In this study, water samples were collected from six typical landscape water bodies in Xi'an city, with different supplementary water sources, covering both wet and dry seasons. And the ecological risks were also assessed by using the pollution load index (PLI) and potential ecological risk index (PERI). The results indicate that the primary morphologies of microplastics in landscape water bodies are fibrous (66.24% ~ 67.52%) and fragmented (25.61% ~ 27.58%), with the predominant types being polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP). Concentration analysis revealed that the microplastic concentration in landscape water bodies during the nonflood season (7.64 ~ 20.78 n/L) was significantly higher than during the flood season (3.82 ~ 12.98 n/L); furthermore, landscape water bodies replenished with reclaimed water (nonflood season: 12.72 ~ 17.14 n/L) exhibited higher concentrations than those replenished with surface water (nonflood season: 10.47 ~ 13.17 n/L). Risk assessment results demonstrated that the ecological risk induced by microplastic pollution in landscape water bodies during the nonflood season (PLI = 1.25 ~ 1.59, PERI = 19.62 ~ 31.59) was generally higher than during the flood season (PLI = 0.89 ~ 1.27, PERI = 6.80 ~ 13.93); moreover, the pollution risk associated with replenishment by reclaimed water (nonflood season: PLI = 1.36 ~ 1.59, PERI = 23.11 ~ 31.59) was greater than that associated with replenishment by surface water (nonflood season: PLI = 1.25 ~ 1.41, PERI = 19.62 ~ 24.83). The study demonstrates that the microplastic pollution levels in Xi'an urban landscape water bodies are significantly influenced by the replenishment water sources and seasonal variations. This conclusion can provide scientific basis and technical guidance for further exploration of the microplastics migration and transformation patterns and ecological risks assessment.

articles.title: Gastric ulcers in cats with feline infectious peritonitis.
articles.abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) is one of the leading causes of death in cats worldwide. Although multiple organs can be affected, gastric ulcers have not been previously described as part of the pathological picture. Here we describe the macroscopic, histopathological, and immunohistochemical features of gastric ulcers of four domestic cats with FIP. The mean age of affected cats was 19 months. The affected cats had multisystemic involvement and the disease was classified as three mixed and one non-effusive case of FIP. Gross changes in the stomach were identified in all cases and consisted of single or multiple ulcers of variable diameter that were surrounded by a hyperemic halo. Histologically, ulcerated lesions consisted of areas of mucosal loss with coagulative necrosis surrounded by fibrin and cellular debris and, in some cases, pyogranulomatous inflammation. In the submucosa there was pyogranulomatous vasculitis, thrombosis, and fibrinoid vascular necrosis. All cases had positive immunolabeling for FCoV in the cytoplasm of macrophages within the gastric mucosa and submucosa. Although ulcerative gastritis is not a classic manifestation of FIP, the vasculitis and thrombosis observed in these cases likely contributed to the development of gastric ulcers. FIP should be considered as a differential diagnosis in cats with gastric ulcers associated with pyogranulomatous inflammatory infiltrate.

articles.title: Cellular Senescence at the Blood-Brain Barrier: a Potential Driver of Vulnerability and Poor Recovery in Ischaemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Advancing age is the strongest non-modifiable risk factor for ischaemic stroke and a major determinant of injury severity and functional recovery, yet the biological mechanisms through which ageing amplifies cerebrovascular vulnerability remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence indicates that ageing-associated vascular dysfunction and cellular senescence converge at the level of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), transforming it from a protective interface into a critical mediator of ischaemic injury. In this review, we synthesise clinical, experimental, and translational data demonstrating that BBB dysfunction develops early during ageing, exhibits regional and genetic vulnerability, and is closely linked to senescence of endothelial cells and pericytes within the neurovascular unit. Senescence-associated alterations in cellular metabolism, inflammatory signalling, fibrinolytic balance, and endothelial-pericyte crosstalk compromise barrier integrity, promote leukocyte infiltration, and lower the threshold for ischaemic damage. Importantly, cerebral ischaemia itself accelerates senescence programmes, establishing a self-reinforcing cycle in which vascular ageing and ischaemic injury potentiate one another and constrain post-stroke repair. We further highlight emerging preclinical evidence that targeting senescent cells or rejuvenating the ageing BBB restores barrier function, attenuates neuroinflammation, and improves neurological outcomes, particularly in aged models. Collectively, these findings position BBB senescence as a central and modifiable mechanism linking ageing to ischaemic stroke susceptibility and recovery, and identify senescence-directed strategies as a promising therapeutic avenue for the ageing stroke population.

articles.title: Multi-omics Mendelian randomization and cartilage transcriptomics prioritize genetic loci and candidate genes for osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a complex joint disorder in which inherited susceptibility intersects with immune and metabolic processes. We integrated gut-microbiota, 731 immune-cell-trait and 1,400 plasma-metabolite genome-wide association study summary statistics with an OA genome-wide association study (n = 403,124) using two-sample Mendelian randomization. All screening analyses are reported with false-discovery-rate (FDR) control, and nominal findings are framed as exploratory. Associations passing prespecified sensitivity filters underwent colocalization, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization with the HEIDI test using blood cis-eQTLs, and expression assessment in a merged 43-sample cartilage resource. Screening identified 8 microbial taxa, 39 immune traits and 97 metabolites or ratios at nominal significance; no exposure-OA association survived FDR correction. Two associations, the glycine-to-serine ratio and CD45RA on TD CD8br, replicated at Bonferroni significance in FinnGen (61,356 cases, 315,115 controls) with concordant effect sizes, whereas neither colocalization signal reproduced. In the discovery analysis, colocalization provided moderate support for a shared signal between a long-chain sphingomyelin trait (GCST90200134) and OA at SPTLC3 (PP.H4 = 0.82; stable for p12 ≥ 1 × 10⁻5 but lower under the most conservative prior), whereas the signal between a CD8 T-cell phenotype and OA at DHX16 was weak (PP.H4 = 0.49) and depended on the analysis window. Integration of SNP-annotated and SMR-prioritized genes yielded 92 candidates; 60 were assessable in cartilage; six showed nominal expression differences and one (TBC1D17) survived FDR correction. Together, the results provide a hypothesis-generating prioritization of one moderate colocalization signal and cartilage-expressed candidate genes, requiring validation in tissue-specific experimental systems.

articles.title: Systemic inflammatory biomarkers in hospitalized patients with odontogenic infections: a retrospective evaluation of treatment-related changes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate longitudinal changes in leukocyte count and CBC-derived inflammatory indices and their association with odontogenic infection severity in hospitalized patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included hospitalized patients with odontogenic infections who had complete laboratory data available at hospital admission (T0) and post-treatment assessment (T1). Leukocyte count and the CBC-derived inflammatory indices were evaluated. Patients were classified according to Severity score. Statistical analyses included paired comparisons, Mann-Whitney analysis of Δ values (T0 - T1), and Multivariable linear mixed-effects models.

RESULTS: Eighty-two patients were included (43 mild and 39 severe infections). Leukocyte count, SIRI, AISI, and NLR decreased significantly between T0 and T1 in both groups. Regarding the comparison of median changes between groups, these were significantly greater in patients with severe infections for SII (P = 0.009), SIRI (P = 0.014), AISI (P = 0.016), NLR (P = 0.002), and leukocyte count (P = 0.003). Multivariable linear mixed-effects models demonstrated significant effects for time for all inflammatory markers except for PLR; significant effects of infection severity were observed for leukocyte count (6.95; P = 0.010), SII (4.16; P = 0.045), SIRI (6.64; P = 0.012)., and AISI (7.99; P = 0.006); and significant time × severity interactions were observed for leukocyte count (9.27; P = 0.003), SII (5.71; P = 0.019), and NLR (6,03; P = 0.016). Neither treatment modality (P = 0.265) nor antibiotic regimen (P = 0.140) was significantly associated with infection severity.

CONCLUSION: Leukocyte count, SII, and NLR showed the most consistent longitudinal changes during hospitalization and appear to be useful complementary inflammatory parameters for monitoring treatment response and clinical recovery in patients with odontogenic infections. SIRI and AISI also demonstrated significant longitudinal changes, although their performance was not consistent for time x severity.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Routine complete blood count parameters and CBC-derived inflammatory indices may complement clinical assessment by monitoring the longitudinal inflammatory response to treatment in hospitalized patients with odontogenic infections.

articles.title: Mapping satellite NO2 hotspot typology: India's shifting pollution burden from Delhi-NCR to eastern energy-industrial corridors.
articles.abstract: Tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a useful satellite-based indicator of combustion-related emissions, yet national-scale hotspot assessments often obscure localized intensification and source-context differences. Here, we develop a multiscale NO2 hotspot typology for India by integrating Sentinel-5P/TROPOMI (TROPOspheric Monitoring Instrument) annual tropospheric NO2 columns for 2019-2025 with district and sub-district burden metrics, temporal-change indicators, peak-year dynamics, thermal power plant proximity, and Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research (EDGAR) sectoral NOₓ emissions. Rather than defining hotspots from current burden alone, the framework distinguishes critical active hotspots (Type 1), legacy severe hotspots (Type 2), emerging elevated-burden hotspots (Type 3 a), low-baseline emerging signals (Type 3 b), high-burden watch-list zones (Type 3c), and stable/lower-priority areas (Type 4). Results reveal a dual NO2 hotspot structure across India. Delhi-NCR remains a dominant region of severe legacy burden, characterized by high current and persistent NO2 burden but weak or declining recent trends. In contrast, the central-eastern energy-industrial belt, particularly the Odisha-Chhattisgarh, Singrauli-Sonbhadra, Korba-Angul, and Sambalpur-Jharsuguda-Raigarh-Sakti corridors, shows the strongest active intensification. Sub-district analysis identified severe local cores that were masked by district-level averaging, demonstrating the importance of fine-scale administrative assessment. Type 1 critical active hotspots were strongly aligned with thermal power infrastructure and energy-industrial EDGAR NOₓ emission profiles, while Delhi Type 2 hotspots exhibited a more urban legacy profile. These findings show that India's NO2 hotspot geography is shifting beyond traditional megacity cores toward industrial-energy corridors. The proposed typology provides a transparent, policy-relevant framework for separating chronic burden, active intensification, emerging risk, and watch-list areas, supporting spatially differentiated NO2 mitigation strategies.

articles.title: Impact of exogenous nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide and its precursors supplementation in adults with heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial dysfunction and NAD⁺ depletion contribute to heart failure (HF), but trials of NAD⁺ and nicotinamide riboside (NR) have shown inconsistent results. We systematically evaluated their effects on cardiac function, biomarkers, clinical outcomes, and safety in adults with symptomatic HF.

METHODS: A systematic search was conducted through PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane from inception to September 2025. Adults with HF receiving guideline-directed therapy were included. Interventions comprised intravenous NAD⁺ or oral NR versus placebo. Primary outcomes were HF hospitalization, all-cause mortality, and change in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Secondary outcomes included cardiac structural and functional measures, biomarkers, and laboratory safety outcomes. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager version 5.4.1.

RESULTS: Four randomized controlled trials involving 387 patients were included. NAD⁺-related interventions did not significantly reduce HF hospitalization (3 studies, 268 patients; RR = 0.63, 95% CI 0.36-1.09; P = 0.10; I2 = 0%) or mortality (2 studies, 238 patients; RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.09-2.86; P = 0.45; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were observed in LVEF at 1 month (2 studies, 238 patients; MD = 2.10%, 95% CI - 0.18 to 4.38; P = 0.07; I2 = 0%), 3 months (2 studies, 87 patients; MD = - 0.48%, 95% CI - 4.74 to 3.78; P = 0.83; I2 = 0%), or last follow-up (3 studies, 267 patients; MD = 1.54%, 95% CI - 0.69 to 3.77; P = 0.18; I2 = 4%). No significant differences were observed in global longitudinal strain (GLS) (2 studies, 89 patients; MD = 0.03, 95% CI - 2.10 to 2.16; P = 0.96; I2 = 61%), left atrial diameter (LAD) (2 studies, 240 patients; MD = - 0.29 mm, 95% CI - 1.80 to 1.22; P = 0.71; I2 = 0%), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) (2 studies, 240 patients; MD = 0.24 mm, 95% CI - 2.25 to 2.73; P = 0.85; I2 = 18%), or left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) (2 studies, 202 patients; MD = 10.08 mL, 95% CI - 23.55 to 43.70; P = 0.56; I2 = 66%). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) did not differ significantly between groups (2 studies, 238 patients; MD = - 382.76 pg/mL, 95% CI - 1091.62 to 326.11; P = 0.29; I2 = 0%). Serum creatinine increased significantly with NAD⁺ (2 studies, 209 patients; MD = 7.46 μmol/L, 95% CI 2.21-12.71; P = 0.005; I2 = 48%), whereas alanine aminotransferase (ALT) did not differ significantly between groups (2 studies, 209 patients; MD = 1.62 U/L, 95% CI - 3.18 to 6.42; P = 0.51; I2 = 81%).

CONCLUSION: NAD⁺ and NR did not significantly improve cardiac function, biomarkers, or clinical outcomes in adults with symptomatic HF, although numerical trends favored treatment. The interventions appeared generally well tolerated in the short term, but the observed increase in serum creatinine warrants further evaluation. Larger, longer-term randomized controlled trials are needed to clarify their clinical efficacy and safety in HF. PROSPERO Registration: CRD420251251462.

articles.title: Interatrial Septal Disorders are Independently Associated with Delayed Post-Exercise Heart Rate Recovery in Athletes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial septal disorders (IASD) are among the most common congenital cardiac anomalies. Their impact on cardiac autonomic function in athletes remains poorly defined. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the prevalence of IASD and their association with cardiac autonomic function, assessed by heart rate recovery (HRR), in a cohort of adult athletes.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study enrolled 1,018 adult athletes undergoing pre-participation cardiovascular screening at the Exercise and Sports Medicine Unit of ''A. Cardarelli'' Hospital, Campobasso, Italy, between January 2024 and May 2025. Trans-thoracic echocardiography with contrast imaging was performed to diagnose IASD. HRR was assessed during exercise stress testing using the Modified Bruce Protocol. ΔHRR was calculated as the change from peak heart rate during exercise to that measured during 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th minutes of recovery.

RESULTS: IASD were identified in 331 athletes (32.5%), including patent foramen ovale (12.5%), redundant interatrial septum (21.7%), atrial septal aneurysm (3.3%), and ostium secundum (1.7%). Athletes with IASD exhibited significantly lower ΔHRR at 1 min (30.8 ± 13.9 vs. 39.9 ± 18.1 bpm, p < 0.001) and 2 min (61.0 ± 17.9 vs. 66.1 ± 16.7 bpm, p < 0.001) post-exercise. On multivariable regression, IASD was the strongest independent predictor of impaired ΔHRR 1 (β =- 11.19, p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: IASD are prevalent in athletes and independently associated with delayed post-exercise early HRR, suggesting an impairment in post-exercise vagal reactivation.

articles.title: Adherence to secondary preventative medications one year post stroke.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prior stroke is a major risk factor for future stroke events, but this risk can be reduced through a combination of medication and lifestyle interventions. Adherence to secondary preventative medications is critical to reducing subsequent vascular events but is poor in up to 40% of stroke survivors. We examined factors influencing medication adherence in an Irish stroke population.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of patients 1 year post stroke. During an in-home or clinic review, participants were asked about adherence to three medication categories: antithrombotics, antihypertensives and lipid-lowering drugs, using the MMAS-4 questionnaire and medication reconciliation to dichotomise adherence into high and low. The effects of ethnicity, sex, caregiver status and functional outcomes on adherence were examined.

RESULTS: A cohort of 197 stroke survivors was recruited at a median of 386 days post stroke. High adherence was observed in 79% of participants, however, many patients did not know why they were taking their medications. There were no significant differences between ethnicity or sex subgroups. Longer length of stay (p= 0.03), post stroke disability (p<0.001) and caregiver involvement (p<0.001) were associated with high medication adherence.

CONCLUSION: Self-reported adherence to secondary prevention medication following a stroke was high in our cohort, with 4 out of 5 stroke survivors reporting high adherence at 1 year. Caregiver involvement and greater disability were strongly associated with high adherence, with the lowest adherence seen in mild strokes. In contrast with data from other countries, we found no differences in medication adherence by ethnicity.

articles.title: Adenosine deaminase co-immunization reverses age‑associated immunosenescence by restoring germinal center T follicular helper cell function.
articles.abstract: Older adults experience disproportionate morbidity and mortality from Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI); however, existing toxoid- and receptor binding domain (RBD)-based vaccines elicit suboptimal protection in aged hosts due to the age-associated defects in CD4+ T cell function, T follicular helper (TFH) cell activation, and antibody quality. We evaluated whether adenosine deaminase (ADA), an enzymatic immune modulator that degrades immunosuppressive adenosine, and improves GC TFH differentiation and survival, could reverse these age-related impairments when co-delivered with DNA vaccine plasmids targeting toxin A and B RBDs (pRBD). In aged mice, pRBD vaccination alone produced markedly reduced toxin-specific effector/memory CD4+ T cells, diminished TFH activation, and poor toxin A neutralization compared to vaccinated young mice. Co-immunization with plasmid-encoded adenosine deaminase-1 (pADA) restored toxin-specific CD4+ T cell generation and cytokine production, activation-induced marker (AIM) TFH responses, and antibody-mediate toxin neutralization to levels comparable to young adults. Mechanistically, pADA co-immunization was associated with the reduction of CXCR4 on germinal center (GC) TFH cells-a phenotype previously linked to impaired GC positioning and diminished B cell help in aging-suggesting that ADA may improve humoral quality through modulation of CXCR4 expression, a pathway previously associated with GC TFH positioning. These immune enhancements corresponded with improved clinical outcomes in morbidity, mortality, and weight loss following C. difficile spore challenge of aged mice. Finally, pADA significantly reduced adenosine levels in aged lymph nodes, implicating a potential enzymatic-based regulation of GC immunosenescence. Together, these findings identify ADA as a metabolic adjuvant capable of reversing key features of vaccine immunosenescence and highlight adenosine-dependent CXCR4 regulation as a tractable axis for improving vaccine efficacy in older populations.

articles.title: Modulation of cell to cell action potential conduction by the dynamic clamp: gap junction and ephaptic coupling.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Cardiac conduction is primarily attributed to gap junctions (GJs), although ephaptic mechanisms involving Na⁺ channels (Nav1.5) in the intercalated disc (ID) have been suggested to contribute to action potential (AP) conduction when GJ coupling is reduced. We used a two-cell preparation combined with dynamic clamp to experimentally modulate cell-to-cell AP transmission by varying gap junction conductacleft across the two disc membranesnce (gj). In passive HEK293 cells expressing connexin 43 (Cx43) and Nav1.5, APs were generated by injecting computer-simulated inward rectifier (IK1) and pacemaker (If) currents via patch pipettes under current-clamp conditions. Three experimental configurations were examined: (1) physically GJ-coupled pairs (cells connected by actual Cx43 channels); (2) virtually coupled pairs (no physical GJ connection; coupling imposed in real time by dynamic clamp); and (3) physically GJ-coupled pairs rendered virtually uncoupled (physical GJ connection computationally negated by dynamic clamp, while physically preserving ID-like architecture). Intercellular AP conduction delay (Δt) was measured in physically and virtually coupled cell pairs. In all configurations, Δt increased nonlinearly as gj decreased, with conduction failure occurring below ~ 1 nS in the absence of ephaptic contributions. Ephaptic transmission was observed in Cx43 knockout HEK293/Nav1.5 cells and GJ-coupled HEK293/Nav1.5 pairs in which gj was computationally negated via dynamic clamp. In both cases, AP conduction persisted even when gj was eliminated entirely or reduced below 1 nS. A structurally based mathematical model of the intercalated disc accurately predicted the voltage response of ephaptically activated current in the recipient cell. Together, these data provide direct experimental evidence of ephaptic coupling in closely apposed cell pairs and demonstrate that, in a cardiac-analogue HEK293 system, ephaptic mechanisms can sustain AP conduction when GJ conductance is reduced or absent.

articles.title: Lenabasum attenuates CLP-induced sepsis-associated acute lung injury with coordinated modulation of redox balance and inflammation-resolution profile.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury is a major experimental counterpart of human acute respiratory distress syndrome and involves inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, and structural lung damage. Lenabasum (JBT-101), a selective cannabinoid receptor type 2 (CB2) agonist, has shown anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory properties in non-septic inflammation, but its effects in acute polymicrobial sepsis-associated lung injury remain poorly defined. This study evaluated lenabasum in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced polymicrobial sepsis model during the acute 24-h phase, focusing on lung oxidative/antioxidant indices, the serum inflammation-resolution profile, and histopathological changes. 30 male Wistar rats were allocated to Sham, CLP, CLP + lenabasum 1 mg/kg, CLP + lenabasum 5 mg/kg, or CLP + dexamethasone 1 mg/kg groups. Interventions were administered intraperitoneally after sepsis induction. At 24 h, lung reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and reduced glutathione (GSH) were measured. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-8 (IL-8), C-reactive protein (CRP), and lipoxin A4 (LXA4) were assessed as the inflammation-resolution profile. Lung injury was evaluated under blinded conditions using hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining and lung injury score (LIS). CLP increased lung ROS and MDA, decreased GSH, elevated serum TNF-α, IL-8, CRP, and LXA4, and induced histopathological lung injury. Both lenabasum doses reduced MDA, serum inflammatory markers, and LIS and shifted LXA4 toward Sham levels. At 5 mg/kg, lenabasum also reduced ROS, increased GSH, and attenuated histopathological lung injury. Lenabasum, particularly at 5 mg/kg, attenuated biochemical disturbances and histopathological lung injury at 24 h after CLP. These findings support further preclinical investigation of lenabasum, while the receptor dependence of its effects remains to be established.

articles.title: Integration of machine learning and transcriptomics analysis identifies candidate molecular associations between parthenolide and sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are both life-threatening diseases. Sepsis-related ALI frequently presents with complications of sepsis, which are mostly identified by the presence of non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema and refractory hypoxia. Despite the advancements in the field of drug discovery and delivery science, the understanding and management of sepsis-associated ALI are insufficient. WGCNA and differential expression analyses were integrated across multiple transcriptomics database cohorts to determine the core common candidate genes associated with sepsis-associated ALI and PTL. A Lasso model with SHAP interpretability was trained for feature selection. Molecular docking was performed for all candidate targets using PyRx with AutoDock Vina as the docking engine. Intersection of predicted parthenolide (PTL) targets and ALI-associated genes yielded 17 candidate genes. The Lasso algorithm used nested cross-validation, yielding an AUC of 0.827 (95% CI 0.767-0.928) and external validation with AUC values of 0.918 (GSE76293) and 0.667 (GSE10361). Molecular docking analysis indicated that the potential binding energies of the selected targets were - 5.9 to - 8.5 kcal/mol. These computational findings identify candidate PTL-associated molecular targets and provide a structural hypothesis to guide experimental validation.

articles.title: Ethical issues in the care of patients with head and neck cancers: A systematic review.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck cancers (H&NCs) raise distinctive ethical challenges due to their profound impact on communication, sensory function, bodily identity, and social participation. Although ethical concerns frequently arise in clinical practice, the scope and structure of these issues across the H&NCs care trajectory have not been systematically synthesized.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review to identify ethical issues discussed in the literature on the care of patients with H&NCs. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched on July 2025 using combinations of terms related to H&NCs and ethics. No restriction on publication year was applied; only English-language articles were included. After removal of duplicates, titles, abstracts, and full texts were screened against predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Eligible publications had to contain substantive ethical analysis related to clinical care rather than incidental references to ethics. Additional studies were identified through citation tracking and snowballing. Data extraction and synthesis followed the five preparatory coding steps of the Qualitative Analysis Guide of Leuven (QUAGOL), enabling thematic identification of ethical domains.

RESULTS: The search yielded 406 records, of which 54 publications met inclusion criteria. Included studies encompassed empirical research, narrative and systematic reviews, and conceptual or normative analyses. Most publications originated from high-income countries. Indeed, only six studies (11.1%) originated from middle-income countries, while no studies from low-income countries were identified. Thematic synthesis identified six recurring ethical domains: (1) disease-inherent ethical issues linked to disfigurement and loss of communicative or sensory function; (2) ethical dilemmas in managing pregnancy during H&NCs; (3) communication and decision-making processes, including diagnosis disclosure and shared decision-making; (4) proportionality and ethical challenges in advanced and life-limiting disease; (5) survivorship-related issues including persistent functional impairment and unmet needs; and (6) context-specific ethical concerns such as HPV-related stigma, behavioral risk factors, pandemic-related triage, and care in resource-limited settings.

CONCLUSIONS: Ethical challenges in H&NCs extend across the entire care trajectory and are closely linked to the disease's impact on identity, communication, and social functioning. Integrating ethical reflection into multidisciplinary care, survivorship planning, and public health strategies may improve alignment between treatment decisions and patient values.

REGISTRATION: The review protocol was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; CRD420261297228).

articles.title: Does timing of decompressive craniectomy influence outcomes in pediatric traumatic brain injury? A scoping review of institutional series and cohort studies.
articles.journal: Child's nervous system : ChNS : official journal of the International Society for Pediatric Neurosurgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) is a leading cause of disability and death in the pediatric population, frequently complicated by refractory intracranial hypertension. While decompressive craniectomy (DC) is utilized to relieve elevated intracranial pressure (ICP), the optimal timing for surgical intervention remains undetermined.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed to identify studies evaluating the timing of DC in pediatric patients (< 18 years) with sTBI.

RESULTS: Eleven retrospective studies (ten independent cohorts) met the inclusion criteria. The mean or median admission GCS ranged from 3.5 to 6, and the mean preoperative ICP ranged from 27.2 to 49.8 mmHg. The definition of "early" DC varied substantially, ranging from under one hour to 24 h post-injury. A large database study observed higher in-hospital mortality after DC within 2 h of admission, most likely reflecting confounding by indication, as these patients had greater injury severity. Smaller cohorts found no association between timing and mortality. Overall, the synthesized evidence demonstrated no statistically significant correlation between time to surgery and long-term favorable neurological outcomes, except for one study that observed a correlation between favorable outcomes and DC within 4 h.

CONCLUSION: Current clinical evidence is limited and methodologically heterogeneous, precluding the establishment of definitive timing thresholds for DC in pediatric sTBI. No consistent association between surgical timing and long-term functional outcomes has been demonstrated, and the higher mortality after very early DC likely reflects baseline injury severity.

articles.title: Perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation after initial burn surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Early surgical intervention, including debridement and grafting, is crucial in acute burn injury management. Although early extubation in operating rooms (ORs) reduces intensive care unit length of stay and ventilator-associated complications, extubation feasibility following initial burn surgery remains uncertain. We investigated perioperative factors associated with postoperative continuation of mechanical ventilation (MV) after initial burn surgery.

METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed patients with burns who underwent acute-phase debridement between 2018 and 2024. Patients requiring postoperative MV were compared with those extubated in ORs. Factors independently associated with postoperative MV were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among 418 patients, 75 required postoperative MV. Age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.03, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.00-1.06), percentage of total body surface area (%TBSA) burned (aOR = 1.08, 95% CI 1.03-1.12), preoperative intubation (aOR = 11.8, 95% CI 3.02-46.4), intraoperative fluid administration volume (ml/kg) (aOR = 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.06), and intraoperative maximum vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) (aOR = 1.18, 95% CI 1.10-1.26) were independently associated with postoperative MV continuation. This association between the intraoperative maximum VIS and postoperative MV continuation was maintained in the sensitivity analysis excluding preoperatively intubated patients (aOR = 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.25).

CONCLUSION: Age, %TBSA burned, preoperative intubation, intraoperative fluid administration volume, and maximum intraoperative VIS were independently associated with postoperative continuation of MV after initial burn surgery. Maximum intraoperative VIS may provide additional information regarding the hemodynamic component of perioperative severity by quantifying the intensity of vasoactive and inotropic support required during surgery.

articles.title: Engineering signal transduction for closed-loop gene and cell therapies.
articles.abstract: Chronic diseases are still treated largely with interventions that are constitutive, intermittently administered and poorly aligned with real-time physiology. Synthetic biology is changing this paradigm by treating gene circuits as programmable genetic software that can be deployed across cellular therapeutic hardware spanning from prokaryotic to eukaryotic systems, including probiotic cells, designer cells, immune cells and stem‑cell‑derived platforms. In this framework, engineered systems can sense disease-associated signals, compute them through synthetic or repurposed transduction pathways and adjust therapeutic output to maintain physiological variables within a desired range. Closed-loop therapeutics therefore begin to merge diagnosis, treatment and prevention within the same living platform. Across metabolism, inflammation, infection, cardiovascular regulation and cancer, early mammalian systems show that endogenous sensing, intracellular computation and therapeutic actuation can be combined in clinically relevant architectures. The emerging concept of setpoint medicine captures the clinical ambition of these systems: not simply to deliver a dose, but to keep physiology within an interpretable and therapeutically desirable range. Realizing this vision will require durable and modular control circuits, hardware-aware delivery strategies, interpretable safety frameworks, controller-style performance metrics and increasingly AI-assisted design, calibration and oversight. If these challenges can be met, the future of therapy may be defined less by intermittent dosing than by the continuous control of physiology.

articles.title: [Resarch Progress in Crosstalk between Renal Tubular Epithelial Cells and Podocytes in Diabetic Kidney Disease].
articles.journal: Zhongguo yi xue ke xue yuan xue bao. Acta Academiae Medicinae Sinicae
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) has emerged as the predominant etiology of chronic kidney disease (CKD).Injuries to renal tubular epithelial cells and podocyte constitute a central pathogenic mechanism in the development and progression of DKD.The pathological environment of DKD,characterized by glomerular hyperfiltration,hypoxia,oxidative stress,and inflammatory responses,serves as a critical pathway for triggering and mediating pathological crosstalk between renal tubular epithelial cells and podocytes.Within this environment,both cell types secrete a spectrum of crosstalk mediators that elicit complex biological effects:specific mediators induce cellular damage through activation of metabolic dysregulation,oxidative stress,fibrotic signaling,and apoptotic pathways,whereas others exert cytoprotective functions.Current experimental therapeutics targeting these mediators demonstrate promise in preventing and curbing DKD progression by modulating such intercellular crosstalk,thereby providing novel therapeutic targets for DKD management.

articles.title: [Research Progress in Macrophage-Mediated Efferocytosis in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease].
articles.journal: Zhongguo yi xue ke xue yuan xue bao. Acta Academiae Medicinae Sinicae
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common chronic respiratory disorder characterized by airflow limitation and persistent airway inflammation.In recent years,macrophage-mediated efferocytosis,a crucial mechanism responsible for the clearance of apoptotic cells,maintenance of pulmonary homeostasis,and resolution of inflammation has emerged as a new focus in the research on COPD.This review systematically summarizes the fundamental processes and key molecular pathways of efferocytosis,with an emphasis on macrophage dysfunction and defective efferocytosis observed in COPD,and their correlations with disease severity,clinical manifestations,and therapeutic responses.Furthermore,potential intervention strategies targeting efferocytosis pathways,including receptor modulators,signaling pathway inhibitors,and herbal extracts,are discussed.

articles.title: Refining antibiotic dosing regimens for the treatment of sepsis in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Critically ill patients experience significant and dynamic changes in physiology, risking suboptimal antibiotic exposure. Dose optimization strategies can help address this therapeutic gap.

AREAS COVERED: The effect of significant and dynamic physiological derangements on antibiotic exposure and patient-centered outcomes in critically ill patients is known but incompletely understood. This review synthesizes the current literature on the role of antibiotic dose optimization strategies in critically ill patients with sepsis, including loading doses, prolonged infusions, nomograms, therapeutic drug monitoring and model-informed precision dosing. A literature search was conducted using the Ovid Medline database on 27 April 2026. The database was searched using keyword terms of intensive care/critical illness, sepsis, and antibiotic dosing.

EXPERT OPINION: Dose optimization strategies should be considered a foundation of antibiotic management in critically ill patients with sepsis. Specifically, these strategies should be used to optimize drug dosing in patients with significant pharmacokinetic (PK) and/or pharmacodynamic (PD) derangement with high clinical suspicion for excessive exposure or treatment failure, and/or pathogens with high minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs). Where clinical benefit is established, dose optimization strategies should be incorporated into standard clinical care. Further research is required to determine exposure-outcome relationships and identify patient parameters, exposure targets, key outcomes and barriers to implementation.

articles.title: Daily iron supplementation for prevention or treatment of iron-deficiency anaemia in infants, children, and adolescents.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Globally, 604.8 million women and 269 million children are living with anaemia; reducing anaemia is a key goal of the 2030 Global Strategy for Women's, Children's, and Adolescents' Health.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the benefits and harms of daily oral iron supplementation in infants, children and adolescents 0-19 years of age with or without anaemia caused by iron deficiency (IDA).

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, CINAHL, 16 additional databases, and two trial registries up to January 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included 0-19-year-olds regardless of baseline iron or anaemia status. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and quasi-RCTs assessing the effects of daily oral supplementation of iron alone, iron with folic acid (IFA), or iron with other vitamins or minerals or both (iron + vitamins/minerals) versus no intervention/placebo.

OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes were anaemia, ID, IDA, growth, morbidity (respiratory illness, cough/difficulty breathing, diarrhoea, fever), and adverse events (AE) (vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, and stool discolouration).

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Risk of bias (RoB) 1 tool.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We used random-effects for meta-analysis and GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We meta-analysed 101 studies (50,325 participants) and narratively described 13 additional studies.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Daily oral supplementation with iron alone versus no intervention/placebo Iron supplementation versus no intervention/placebo makes little to no difference to height/length-for-age z-score ((H(L)AZ), MD -0.01, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.02; 17 studies, 5534 participants; high-certainty evidence); weight-for-height/length z-score ((W(H(L)Z), MD 0.06, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.14; 10 studies, 2683 participants; high-certainty evidence); cough (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.86 to 1.11; 4 studies, 2259 participants; high-certainty evidence), fever (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.92 to 1.02; 5 studies, 763 participants; high-certainty evidence), and respiratory illness (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.18; 3 studies, 549 participants; high-certainty evidence), but probably decreases IDA (RR 0.24, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.30; 13 studies, 3193 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Iron supplementation may result in little to no difference in vomiting (RR 1.09, 95% CI 0.83 to 1.43; 5 studies, 2208 participants; low-certainty evidence) and diarrhoea (RR 1.32, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.92; 5 studies, 2018 participants; low-certainty evidence), but evidence is very uncertain for constipation (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.23 to 3.66; 6 studies, 1002 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Evidence is very uncertain, but supplementation may decrease anaemia (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.63; 19 studies, 5093 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and ID (RR 0.29, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.57; 13 studies, 3977 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but may increase stool discolouration (RR 6.13, 95% CI 3.30 to 11.38; 3 studies, 315 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Daily supplementations of IFA versus folic acid (FA) alone No data were found. Daily oral supplementation of IFA versus no intervention/placebo IFA versus no intervention/placebo probably decreases ID (RR 0.17, 95% CI 0.08 to 0.39; 1 study, 225 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) and IDA (RR 0.15, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.37; 1 study, 225 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), but evidence is very uncertain about the effects on anaemia (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.24 to 1.16; 5 studies, 1757 participants; very low-certainty evidence). IFA makes little to no difference to morbidity (diarrhoea: RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.15; 2 studies, 12,981 participants; high-certainty evidence; or respiratory illness: RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.21; 1 study, 12,679 participants; high-certainty evidence). Daily oral supplementation of iron with vitamins/minerals versus the supplementation of the same vitamins/minerals without iron Supplementation of iron with vitamins/minerals makes little to no difference to H(L)AZ (MD -0.08, 95% CI -0.17 to -0.00; 7 studies, 1638 participants; high-certainty evidence), WH(L)Z (MD 0.00, 95% CI -0.10 to 0.10; 6 studies, 1376 participants; high-certainty evidence), and diarrhoea (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.02; 4 studies, 1038 participants; high-certainty evidence). Iron supplementation probably decreases IDA (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07 to 0.38; 4 studies, 559 participants; moderate-certainty evidence); probably makes little to no difference to cough (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.20; 2 studies, 430 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) and respiratory illness (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.27; 2 studies, 430 participants; moderate-certainty evidence), and probably increases vomiting (RR 1.50, 95% CI 1.11 to 2.02; 1 study, 243 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Evidence is very uncertain, but iron supplementation may decrease anaemia (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.87; 9 studies, 1772 participants; very low-certainty evidence); however, the effects on ID (RR 0.31, 95% CI 0.05 to 1.79; 5 studies, 923 participants; very low-certainty evidence) and fever (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.71 to 2.03; 2 studies, 430 participants; very low-certainty evidence) are very uncertain. Daily oral supplementation of iron with vitamins/minerals versus no intervention/placebo Supplementation of iron with vitamins/minerals versus no intervention/placebo increases H(L)AZ (MD 0.08, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.11; 10 studies, 1525 participants; high-certainty evidence) and probably decreases ID (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.55; 9 studies, 1254 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). Iron supplementation may increase vomiting (RR 1.96, 95% CI 1.29 to 2.96; 1 study, 162 participants; low-certainty evidence; 0-5 month-old infants) but may decrease IDA (RR 0.30, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.83; 6 studies, 912 participants; low-certainty evidence), and may reduce anaemia, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.83; 13 studies, 2254 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Evidence is very uncertain about the effects on cough (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.25; 2 studies, 387 participants; very low-certainty evidence), fever (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.53; 2 studies, 290 participants; very low-certainty evidence), respiratory illness (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.38 to 1.34; 4 studies, 14,061 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and diarrhoeal morbidity (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.23 to 2.21; 3 studies, 13,861 participants; very low-certainty evidence).

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Daily oral supplementation of iron alone, iron with FA, or iron with vitamins/minerals may result in a significant reduction of iron-deficiency anaemia across our target population with little to no difference in morbidity, and a probable increase in stool discolouration.

articles.title: Kangaroo mother care to reduce morbidity and mortality in low birthweight infants.
authors: supported by Cochrane Sweden and the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) comprises three core components: prolonged skin-to-skin contact between infants and caregivers; support for exclusive breastfeeding; and early discharge with appropriate follow-up. It provides thermal regulation and stabilizes cardiorespiratory and feeding functions. For low birthweight infants, KMC provides a feasible, low-cost approach to care that promotes thermal regulation, stabilizes cardiorespiratory and feeding functions, and minimizes parent-infant separation. This review updates a Cochrane review first published in 2003, with subsequent updates in 2011, 2014, and 2016.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the benefits and harms of kangaroo mother care (KMC) in low birthweight infants as an alternative to conventional neonatal care before or after the initial period of stabilization with conventional care.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, CINAHL and trials registries in August 2025. We checked reference lists of included studies, and systematic reviews where subject matter related to the intervention or population examined in this review.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) where participants were hospitalized preterm infants (defined as < 37 weeks' gestation) or low birthweight infants (defined as birthweight < 2500 g). We included studies that evaluated KMC, defined as skin-to-skin contact between caregiver and infant, regardless of duration ('any KMC'), as well as KMC meeting the World Health Organization (WHO) definition (minimum duration of eight hours per day). Eligible comparisons were: any KMC compared with conventional neonatal care (CNC).

OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes were: in-hospital mortality or before 40 to 41 weeks' postmenstrual age (PMA); weight (g) at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; exclusive breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; any breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; length of hospital stay; nosocomial (hospital-acquired) infection or sepsis (as defined in individual studies) at any time point, and hypothermia (as defined in individual studies) at any time point.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane Risk of bias tool 2.0 (RoB 2).

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We conducted meta-analyses using fixed-effect models to calculate risk ratios (RR) and risk difference (RD) for dichotomous data, and mean differences (MDs) for continuous data, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We evaluated the certainty of evidence using GRADE.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 49 RCTs enrolling 7724 infants. Studies were published between 1988 and 2024. All studies compared any KMC with CNC; 13 delivered WHO-defined KMC for 8 to 24 hours/day, while the remainder offered KMC for different durations. Thus, the 'any KMC' comparison encompasses a range of exposure durations, not solely the WHO-defined intervention. Twenty-two studies were conducted in low- or middle-income countries. We identified eight ongoing studies.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Any KMC likely reduces in-hospital mortality or before 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.99; I² = 0%; 14 studies, 4389 participants; moderate-certainty evidence; RD -0.01, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.00, I2 = 0%) and nosocomial infection or sepsis (as defined in individual studies) (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.54 to 0.82; I² = 45%; 15 studies, 3852 participants; moderate-certainty evidence; RD -0.03, 95% CI -0.05 to -0.02, I2 = 75%) compared to CNC. KMC may increase exclusive breastfeeding (RR 1.18, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.27; I² = 58%; 9 studies, 1846 participants; low-certainty evidence; RD 0.10, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.14, I2 = 73%) and reduce hypothermia (as defined in individual studies) at any time point (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.86; I² = 87%; 13 studies, 3493 participants; low-certainty evidence; RD -0.11, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.09, I2 = 93%). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of any KMC on weight (g) at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (MD 63.00, 95% CI 40.57 to 85.43; I² = 80%; 7 studies, 1648 participants; very low-certainty evidence), any breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (RR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.21; I² = 68%; 6 studies, 1282 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and length of hospital stay (days) (MD 1.19, 95% CI 1.18 to 1.21; I² = 98%; 14 studies, 3765 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Subgroup analyses suggested differences in some outcomes by KMC definition and country income, but these findings require cautious interpretation. Certainty of the evidence varies from moderate for mortality and nosocomial infection or sepsis, low for exclusive breastfeeding and hypothermia, and very low for weight, any breastfeeding and length of hospital stay. Downgrading reflected risk of bias (unclear allocation concealment, unblinded outcome assessment, maternal-reported breastfeeding outcomes), inconsistency from heterogeneity and variable outcome definitions, indirectness from heterogeneous KMC delivery, and imprecision.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: KMC probably provides clinically important benefits compared with CNC, particularly by reducing mortality and nosocomial infection or sepsis. It may also improve breastfeeding outcomes and reduce hypothermia. Effects on growth and duration of hospitalization remain very uncertain because of substantial heterogeneity and very low-certainty evidence. Evidence for mortality and infection came predominantly from low- and lower-middle-income countries, with limited and imprecise evidence from high-income settings, restricting conclusions about applicability across settings. These conclusions apply to a broad definition of KMC; only a minority of trials evaluated KMC that met the WHO duration criterion, so the pooled results should not be taken as specific estimates of WHO-defined KMC. Future research should prioritize how KMC can be delivered effectively across health systems, income settings, and infant populations, including contemporary high-income neonatal care settings. Studies should clearly describe intervention components, including whether KMC meets the WHO definition, timing of initiation, daily duration, continuity, setting, provider, and implementation fidelity. Adequately powered trials and implementation studies should use standardized outcome definitions and address outcomes for which evidence remains very uncertain, including growth, hypothermia, and duration of hospitalization. Longer-term follow-up should assess mortality, neurodevelopment, breastfeeding, growth, family-centred outcomes, adverse effects, resource use, cost-effectiveness, equity, and feasibility.

FUNDING: None.

REGISTRATION: Original review (2003): doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002771 Last review update (2016): doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002771.pub4.

articles.title: Ischemic Mitral Regurgitation: A Changing Paradigm.
Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.

METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.

RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.

CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05648825.

articles.title: Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation.

METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation.

RESULTS: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P=0.01). Freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation was noted in 97.0% (159 of 164) of the biatrial group and 98.1% (156 of 159) of the LA group, meeting the predefined noninferiority criterion with a margin of -5% (adjusted difference, -1.1% [1-sided lower 95% CI, -3.9%]; Pnoninferiority=0.01).
