CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic cardiac valve surgery, biatrial maze ablation was superior to LA maze ablation in reducing recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias, while maintaining noninferiority with respect to permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings provide direct evidence to inform lesion-set selection for surgical ablation during cardiac surgery.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05021601.

articles.title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy.
articles.abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

articles.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

articles.title: Surgical Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation.
articles.abstract: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, mortality, and reduced quality of life. Although catheter ablation is the most widely used rhythm control strategy, its efficacy is limited in patients with non-paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and large left atria. To address this therapeutic gap, surgical approaches, including minimally invasive ablation, hybrid epicardial-endocardial strategies, and left atrial appendage exclusion, have continued to evolve. In this review, we focus on recent evidence to guide clinical decision-making on patient selection, advances in minimally invasive surgical and hybrid techniques, left atrial appendage exclusion, and postoperative anticoagulation management. Minimally invasive standalone Cox-Maze IV procedure and hybrid epicardial-endocardial ablation have demonstrated superior long-term freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias compared with thoracoscopic epicardial surgical ablation or catheter ablation alone. Five-year arrhythmia-free survival has approached 85% to 95% in experienced centers after the Cox-Maze IV procedure and approximately 60% to 70% after hybrid ablation, compared with 35% to 45% after thoracoscopic epicardial ablation and 30% to 35% after single catheter ablation alone. Surgical left atrial appendage exclusion performed at the time of ablation may further reduce thromboembolic risk, although the optimal strategy for postprocedural anticoagulation remains uncertain. Careful patient selection remains essential, with atrial fibrillation type, duration, left atrial size, and previous treatment failure known to be key predictors of procedural success. As surgical techniques and supporting evidence continue to grow, standalone surgical ablation may assume a more important role in the contemporary management of atrial fibrillation, particularly for patients with advanced disease who are unlikely to achieve durable rhythm control with catheter ablation alone.

articles.title: Venous Thromboembolism in Necrotizing Pancreatitis A Nationwide Analysis of Incidence, Risk Factors, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including portal vein thrombosis (PVT), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE), represent complications of NP. However, comprehensive characterization of individual VTE subtypes, risk factors, and outcomes in NP remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2020 National Inpatient Sample, among adult patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis. The patients were categorized into NP and interstitial pancreatitis (IP) groups, with focus on impact of VTE in NP cohort. Outcomes included VTE incidence, risk factors, complications, mortality, length of stay, hospitalization charges, and intensive interventions. Multivariable regression analyses were performed adjusting for demographic and hospital-level covariates.

RESULTS: Of 199,190 AP hospitalizations, 5.74% had NP and 94.26% had IP. NP was associated with significantly higher incidence of PVT (6.08% vs. 0.48%, aOR 11.53), DVT (8.36% vs. 0.69%, aOR 11.19), and PE (1.44% vs. 0.24%, aOR 5.58) compared to IP (all P<0.001). All VTE subtypes significantly increased length of stay, hospitalization charges, and complication rates. Malnutrition (PVT aOR 2.79, DVT aOR 1.61, PE aOR 6.86) and coagulopathy (PVT aOR 2.41, DVT aOR 2.15) were consistent risk factors across all VTE subtypes. Among NP patients, PVT was uniquely associated with mortality (aOR 2.71, P=0.007), while DVT and PE were not.

CONCLUSIONS: NP is associated with markedly increased risks of all VTE subtypes compared to IP. VTE in patients with NP is associated with increased morbidity, with PVT uniquely associated with mortality. Malnutrition and coagulopathy represent potentially modifiable risk factors that may help identify high-risk patients. These findings support the need for prospective study of VTE screening and prophylaxis strategies in NP patients.

articles.title: Immune control of SIV in nonhuman primates: insights for HIV cure strategies.
articles.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the exceptional clinical results of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in reducing morbidity and mortality, HIV infection cannot be cured due to a pool of infected cells, mainly memory CD4+ T cells, that is established within weeks of initial infection and persists under ART; this virus reservoir causes rapid rebound of viral replication if ART is stopped.

RECENT FINDINGS: The preclinical animal model of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) infection in rhesus macaques (RMs) recapitulates key features of HIV infection, pathogenesis, immunology, and persistence in humans, including early establishment and long-term survival of the virus reservoir and rapid viral recrudescence after ART interruption. The SIV infection model is fundamental for investigating biological mechanisms that, when specifically targeted, may reduce and eliminate the reservoir pool.

PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The goal of this review is not to provide an overview of the most recent findings in HIV persistence. Instead, it focuses on three biological mechanisms of viral persistence that our team of investigators, as well as others in the field, have described and for which we are testing innovative targeted interventions to: preferentially kill infected CD4+ memory T cells by targeting intracellular mechanisms favoring their survival; induce a stronger and durable cytolytic response by CD8+ T cells, and eliminate the CD8+ T cell remodeling of CD4+ T cell metabolism that promotes viral latency.

articles.title: Killer lifestyle: natural killer cells, obesity, and HIV/simian immunodeficiency virus infections.
articles.journal: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The success of antiretroviral therapy (ART) that transformed HIV infection in a chronic clinical condition, and reversed the typical failure to thrive characteristic for HIV disease progression to weight gains, resulted in new challenges for the clinical management of the persons living with HIV (PLWH). Prolonged survival also dramatically increased the average age of PLWH, and the frequency of comorbidities associated with HIV. Most of these clinical challenges stem from the persistent inflammation and accelerated aging characteristic to PLWH, which are also associated with obesity.

RECENT FINDINGS: Natural killer (NK) cells, which suffer multiple alterations during HIV infection and in obese people, such as a reduction in the frequency of circulating NK cells, alterations in their surface receptor repertoire and expression, unbalanced anti and proinflammatory profiles, with a dysregulated cytokine production. In the meantime, while NK cells are increasingly activated, their functionality (i.e., cytotoxicity) is impaired and their metabolism is altered in obese individuals and in PLWH.

SUMMARY: These multiple effects of HIV and obesity on NK cells call for interventions aimed at reversing the immunometabolic reprograming. Multiple such interventions are currently tested, and their impact on the NK cells functionality is still to be evaluated.

articles.title: Novel markers for atrial substrate characterization: implications on atrial fibrillation risk stratification.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Atrial fibrillation is increasingly recognized as a manifestation of an underlying atrial disease process that is incompletely captured by conventional temporal classification. This review examines established and emerging markers of atrial substrate and their potential role in atrial fibrillation risk stratification.

RECENT FINDINGS: Electrocardiographic indices, left atrial volumetric and strain measures, computed tomography-derived left atrial wall characteristics, late gadolinium enhancement and flow assessment by cardiac magnetic resonance, high-density electroanatomic mapping, circulating biomarkers and genetic profiling provide complementary measures of electrical, structural, mechanical and hemodynamic remodelling. Recent studies have refined noninvasive identification of low-voltage substrate and risk stratification of atrial fibrillation progression and complications, evaluated substrate-guided ablation strategies, and expanded understanding of the prognostic significance of emerging substrate markers.

SUMMARY: Multimodal atrial substrate characterization may improve prediction of atrial fibrillation onset and progression, thromboembolic complications and outcomes after rhythm-control therapy. Clinical translation requires standardized acquisition and analytical methods, reproducible thresholds, prospective validation of integrated risk models, and prospective trials demonstrating improved outcomes with substrate-guided management.

articles.title: Advanced coronary computed tomography angiography plaque phenotyping for precision prevention.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: In this review, we outline the role coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) plays in the diagnosis of coronary artery disease (CAD) and in facilitating risk assessment. Plaque quantification and phenotyping using CCTA is a promising approach in guiding cardiovascular preventive management.

RECENT FINDINGS: There is growing interest in how artificial intelligence-based quantitative plaque analysis using CCTA (AI-CPA) can guide preventive therapy. The review summarizes studies that show prognostic utility of CCTA-derived plaque quantification and phenotyping as well as outlines more recent studies that show the impact of AI-CPA in patient management decisions, allowing a more individualized approach to preventive strategies.

SUMMARY: CCTA provides a comprehensive assessment extending beyond coronary luminal stenosis to include plaque quantification, plaque phenotyping, functional assessment of stenotic lesions and vascular inflammation, further refining traditional approaches of risk prediction.In summary, the growing evidence highlights the importance of incorporating CCTA-based plaque volume and plaque phenotype analysis in better informing physicians about individual's risk and in guiding preventive management.

articles.title: Quality control in degenerative mitral repair: repair rates, durability, benchmarking, and the reference center model.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The purpose of this report is to describe contemporary practice patterns and recommendations for the surgical management of degenerative mitral regurgitation.

RECENT FINDINGS: The centralization of mitral valve surgery has allowed for expansion of minimally invasive approaches within a mentorship model, offering excellent patient outcomes. Approximately half of the national surgical volume is attributed to a relatively small group of experienced surgeons. Reoperation most commonly occurs due to technical failure, and re-repair at an experienced center offers better patient survival than replacement.There has been a sharp rise in transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) with limited understanding of late durability, although prior TEER decreases the likelihood of future surgical repair. Mild or less mitral regurgitation without stenosis defines the threshold for procedural success. In centers with both experienced surgeons and structural interventionalists, anticipated success of surgical repair is significantly higher, supporting the concept of a heart team model of multidisciplinary valve care. A modern quality improvement tool by the American Association of Thoracic Surgery, Adult Quality Gateway, has shown promise in both patient outcome reporting and risk assessment.

SUMMARY: For patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, early surgical referral to an experienced center with a multidisciplinary heart team is recommended.

articles.title: Antioxidant amino acids: impact on metabolism and health.
articles.journal: Current opinion in clinical nutrition and metabolic care
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Oxidative stress has been implicated in a plethora of metabolic diseases including diabetes, obesity, gout, and many more. Owing to their chemical diversity, several amino acids are increasingly recognized as notable antioxidants. Antioxidant amino acids scavenge free radicals, chelate metal ions, regulate cellular redox homeostasis and enhance antioxidant systems. Thus, this update highlights their antioxidant roles and beneficial effects on metabolism and health.

RECENT FINDINGS: Amino acids such as cysteine, methionine, tryptophan, tyrosine, phenylalanine, glycine, and glutamine have been found to demonstrate significant antioxidant activities in clinical and preclinical studies. In addition to their roles as precursors for the biosynthesis of glutathione, antioxidant amino acids modulate cellular signaling pathways, especially the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 signaling, and play key roles in energy production, detoxification, building of biomolecules, and many amino acid-regulated redox systems.

SUMMARY: Some metabolic diseases may arise from the dysfunction of amino acid-dependent systems in the body, highlighting antioxidant amino acids as beneficial molecules for metabolism and health. The current review provides foundation for future research and development of amino acid-based interventions that will aid drug discovery.

articles.title: Validation of weight-based formulae for estimating paediatric epidural depth.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Accurate prediction of epidural depth in children enhances procedural success and safety in regional anaesthesia. Multiple weight-based formulae exist, yet comparative validation using both actual procedural and imaging data is limited. We aimed to evaluate and identify the most reliable formulae for estimating lumbar and thoracic epidural depth in paediatric patients using retrospective needle depth and prospective ultrasound measurements.

METHODS: Seven published formulae were applied to a retrospective cohort (n = 140) with recorded needle depth at 'loss of resistance' and a prospective cohort (n = 70) with ultrasound-measured posterior dura depth. Performance was assessed using goodness-of-fit statistics adjusted for age, mean absolute error (MAE), the proportions of estimates within ±0.5 cm and ±1.0 cm of the measured depth, and Bland-Altman agreement analyses.

RESULTS: For lumbar epidurals, Hasan's formula (Depth = 0.8 + 0.05 × weight in kg) demonstrated the best fit across both measurement methods, yielding a MAE of 0.16-0.26 cm, with 88.7%-95.7% of predictions within ±0.5 cm and up to 98.6% within ±1.0 cm. For thoracic epidurals, Wong's formula (Depth = 1.06 + 0.067 × weight in kg) showed the strongest correlation, with a MAE of 0.21-0.33 cm and up to 92.9% of estimates within ±0.5 cm.

CONCLUSION: These two formulae provide bedside estimates of dura depth in paediatric patients with clinically acceptable accuracy and may support pre-procedural planning, although their clinical impact on complication rates and procedure time requires prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Prevalence and clinical correlates of elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) reflects systemic inflammation. The frequency of hsCRP >2 mg/L, a threshold used in anti-inflammatory trials, among patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients presenting with ACS at Sismanoglio General Hospital of Athens between January 2023 and May 2024 who had hsCRP measured on arrival. We assessed the frequency and magnitude of hsCRP elevation, clinical and laboratory associations, and factors associated with hsCRP >2 mg/L after adjustment for age.

RESULTS: Of 103 patients, 93 (90.3%) had hsCRP measured and were included (median age: 65 years; interquartile range: 58-73; 84.9% male). Elevated hsCRP (>2 mg/L) occurred in 67.7%, and 25.8% had hsCRP >10 mg/L. Median hsCRP was 3.8 mg/L (interquartile range: 1.3-10.2), without a significant difference between ST-segment elevation and non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction presentations (3.2 vs. 6.0 mg/L; P = 0.15). After mutual adjustment and adjustment for age, diabetes (adjusted odds ratio: 4.46; 95% confidence interval: 1.40-14.15; P = 0.011) and current smoking (adjusted odds ratio: 4.74; 95% confidence interval: 1.65-13.59; P = 0.004) remained associated with elevated hsCRP.

CONCLUSIONS: Two-thirds of patients had hsCRP >2 mg/L at ACS presentation. Diabetes and smoking were independently associated with elevation. These findings quantify the proportion meeting an inflammatory trial entry criterion but do not establish persistent inflammation or support anti-inflammatory treatment. Prospective studies with serial measurements and clinical outcomes are needed to determine whether elevation persists and identifies modifiable risk.

articles.title: Patterns, outcomes and predictors of severe hospital course among people in prison admitted for poisoning in northwest Iran: a retrospective analytical cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: People in prison may be at heightened risk of poisoning and overdose because of substance use, psychiatric morbidity and the stresses of incarceration. This study aims to describe the demographic, toxicological and clinical characteristics of people in prison who required hospital admission for poisoning in northwest Iran.

DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: A retrospective cross-sectional review was conducted using hospital records of all people in prison admitted to the poisoning service of Taleghani Hospital, Urmia, Iran, from 12 January 2017 to 31 December 2020. Demographic variables, poisoning agent, route and intentionality of exposure, psychiatric history, previous poisoning-related admission, intensive care unit admission, length of stay and treatment outcome were summarised descriptively.

FINDINGS: The study included 276 admissions. Most patients were male (98.2%), and the mean age was 35.05 ± 10.43 years. Opioids (30.0% of recorded substances), benzodiazepines (21.0%) and stimulants (17.0%) were the leading recorded agents. Oral exposure was most common (84.1%), and 66.7% of episodes were documented as intentional. Psychiatric history was recorded in 47.8%, previous poisoning-related admission in 54.7% and ICU admission in 15.6%. Most patients were discharged (94.2%); in-hospital mortality was 2.2%.

RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: This was a single-centre retrospective study based on hospital records, which may have involved incomplete documentation and limited generalisability. The small number of deaths limited mortality-specific modelling. Findings should be interpreted as exploratory and require validation in larger multicentre studies.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: The findings support structured clinical risk assessment at admission, closer monitoring of patients with decreased consciousness, supervised medication access in correctional settings and routine psychiatric and substance-use assessment after poisoning. Strengthened communication between hospitals and prison health services may help reduce recurrent poisoning and improve continuity of care.

SOCIAL IMPLICATIONS: Poisoning among people in prison represents an important public health and social concern. Improving prevention, timely identification and continuity of care may help reduce avoidable harm and support better health outcomes for this vulnerable population.

ORIGINALITY/VALUE: This study adds regional evidence on hospital-treated poisoning among people in prison and extends the descriptive thesis data set with exploratory outcome analysis. The findings highlight the need for integrated prison mental health, substance-use, medication-safety and emergency transfer pathways.

articles.title: Diabetes care and self-management in correctional facilities and after return into the community: a qualitative investigation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study is to explore previously incarcerated peoples' experiences of diabetes care and self-management in correctional facilities and after return into the community and the experiences of staff at community organizations that work with this population.

DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Interpretive description methodology was used. Telephone interviews were used to collect data at two timepoints. Timepoint 1 was a retrospective evaluation of incarceration, whereas Timepoint 2 was a short-term three-month community follow-up. The data was coded using inductive conventional content analysis then longitudinal trajectory analysis was applied to develop the findings.

FINDINGS: Four previously incarcerated people and three staff members from community organizations participated in this study. Despite the small sample size, the authors found three themes illustrating the trajectory of diabetes care and self-management from incarceration to post-incarceration: autonomy over blood glucose control; freedom to participate in healthy behaviors; and accessibility of diabetes education and resources. Diabetes care and self-management were challenging in correctional facilities because of the context of incarceration (e.g. restricted healthy behaviors). There was some reported improvement in the facets of diabetes care like more autonomy with blood glucose control after returning into the community. However, previously incarcerated people still struggled to manage diabetes and required support in the community.

RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: While this study is notable because it adds to the limited body of literature in this important area, there are several limitations. First, this qualitative research was conducted in Canada. Therefore, the findings of this study are not representative of all people with experiences of incarceration living with diabetes and the community staff who work with this population. Second, data saturation was not fully achieved because of the small sample size. However, the purpose of this study was to begin to explore experiences of diabetes care and self-management in the context of incarceration, as there is very little published literature on this topic.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Administratively, leaders of correctional facilities and correctional health-care services can collaborate to develop diabetes-friendly policies and procedures (Dhaliwal et al., 2023). With respect to clinical practice, previous work highlighted how diabetes-related interventions could benefit this population (Dhaliwal et al., 2023). In the domain of education, leaders and frontline staff can implement education programs suitable for these restrictive environments (Mangan et al., 2013) including group education (Thomas et al., 2016). Further research is required to understand how incarceration impacts diabetes care, self-management and outcomes (Shabil et al., 2025) including how different governance models and sentence lengths impact diabetes management.

SOCIAL IMPLICATIONS: Qualitative research can effectively illuminate behaviors, beliefs and experiences (Ritholz et al., 2011) such as those from people with experiences of incarceration (Heidari et al., 2017). Findings from these studies can facilitate integration of patients' experiences into care delivery models and are paramount for improving health-care services and health outcomes (Knottnerus and Tugwell, 2012).

ORIGINALITY/VALUE: The perspectives from the participants of this study demonstrate that diabetes care and self-management are difficult in correctional facilities. Some improvements occur in the facets of diabetes care after people return to the community. However, they still require support to overcome struggles faced in the community.

articles.title: [Incidence and risk factors of facial palsy in petrous bone cholesteatoma: a meta-analysis].
articles.abstract: Objective: To explore the incidence and risk factors of facial palsy in patients with petrous bone cholesteatoma (PBC). Methods: The CNKI, Wanfang, Chinese Medical Journal Full-text Database, PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were comprehensively searched from inception to September 2025 to retrieve studies that reported preoperative facial palsy in PBC cases. Studies that met the eligibility criteria were included in the meta-analysis. The incidence of and risk factors for facial palsy in PBC were evaluated, and subgroup analyses were also performed. Results: A total of 556 potentially relevant studies were identified, of which 54 (29 English and 25 Chinese publications) met the inclusion criteria, encompassing 1 835 patients with PBC. The pooled analysis revealed an overall facial palsy incidence of 66.0% (95%CI: 60.0%-72.0%). The included studies exhibited significant heterogeneity due to variations in publication periods, geographical regions, and national settings. Stratified by Sanna classification, the palsy incidence rates were 51.0% (95%CI: 42.0%-60.0%) for supralabyrinthine, 26.0% (95%CI: 15.0%-39.0%) for infralabyrinthine, 28.0% (95%CI: 15.0%-41.0%) for infralabyrinthine-apical, 66.0% (95%CI: 59.0%-72.0%) for massive, and 51.0% (95%CI: 11.0%-90.0%) for apical type, demonstrating statistically significant intergroup differences (P=0.001). Lesions involving the facial nerve at or above the labyrinthine segment showed a 4.35-fold higher risk of facial palsy (OR=4.35, 95%CI: 1.32-14.35) compared to lesions below the labyrinthine segment. No statistically significant difference was observed in the incidence of facial palsy between PBC patients with and without a history of temporal bone surgery (P=0.38). There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of facial palsy between congenital and acquired PBC cases (P=0.64). Conclusions: Facial palsy occurs frequently in PBC cases, particularly in massive-type PBC, which shows the highest incidence. Lesions affecting the facial nerve at or above the labyrinthine segment are significantly associated with elevated facial palsy rates in these patients.

articles.title: [Efficacy and safety of hydromorphone hydrochloride extended-release tablets in patients with moderate-to-severe chronic cancer pain: a multicenter, double-blind, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial].
articles.abstract: Background: To compare the efficacy and safety of domestically produced hydromorphone extended-release (ER) tablets with oxycodone controlled-release (CR) tablets in patients with moderate-to-severe cancer pain. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter, non-inferiority trial was conducted at 32 centers in China between March 2021 and March 2022, patients who required daily opioid analgesia (morphine equivalent daily dose ≥40 mg) were randomized 1∶1 by stratified block randomization to receive hydromorphone ER (once-daily, oral) or oxycodone CR (twice-daily, oral), with titration (≤12 days) followed by a 14-day maintenance period. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in the Brief Pain Inventory(BPI) "worst pain in the past 24 hours" score at the end of maintenance (end-of-maintenance score minus baseline score), with a non-inferiority margin of 1.5, analyzed by analysis of covariance. Secondary endpoints included changes in other BPI item scores, breakthrough pain rescue medication use, time to stable analgesic dose, and treatment satisfaction. Safety assessments included adverse events and treatment-related adverse events, which were analyzed descriptively. Results: The full analysis set included 239 patients: 116 in the hydromorphone group [age (58.1±10.8) years, 74 males (63.8%)] and 123 in the oxycodone group [age (59.0±10.5) years, 76 males (61.8%)]. The least-squares (LS) mean change in the primary endpoint of hydromorphone group (-0.87, 95%CI: -1.41 to -0.34) was non-inferior to oxycodone group (-0.92, 95%CI: -1.43 to -0.40), with a LS mean difference of 0.04 (95%CI:-0.46 to 0.54). Secondary endpoints including "pain on average" (-0.57 vs -0.63), "pain right now" (-0.92 vs -0.83), "pain relief" (4.71% vs 5.52%), and "pain at its least" (-0.23 vs -0.36) showed no statistically significant differences between the hydromorphone group and oxy-codove groups (all P>0.05). The time to reach a stable analgesic dose was 3.0 (3.0, 3.0) days in both groups. The number of rescue medication doses for breakthrough pain during the entire study period was 4.0 (0, 12.5) in the hydromorphone group versus 2.0 (0, 11.0) in the oxycodone group, and during the maintenance period was 4.5 (0, 13.0) versus 1.0 (0, 9.0). The treatment satisfaction scores was 3.0 (3.0, 5.0) in both groups with no statistically significant differences (all P>0.05). Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 76.7% (89/116) in the hydromorphone group and 71.5% (88/123) in the oxycodone group of patients. Conclusion: Once-daily hydromorphone ER was non-inferior to twice-daily oxycodone CR for managing moderate-to-severe chronic cancer pain, with similar safety profiles and no statistically significant difference in satisfaction scores, providing an effective therapeutic option with a simplified dosing regimen.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on targeted biologic therapy for inflammatory airway diseases (2026 edition)].
authors: Chinese Society of Allergy, Chinese Medical Association
Asthma Group of Chinese Thoracic Society, Chinese Medical Association
articles.abstract: To standardize the clinical application of biologic targeted therapy for airway inflammatory diseases in China, Chinese Society of Allergy and Asthma Group of Chinese Thoracic Society, Chinese Medical Association, with multidisciplinary experts, developed the"Expert consensus on targeted biologic therapy for airway inflammatory diseases (2026 edition)"using an evidence-based approach, which formulated 15 recommendations. The consensus systematically elaborated on the classification, characteristics, and core inflammatory mechanisms of airway inflammatory diseases; described the mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, and safety profiles of biologics for asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chronic rhinosinusitis and allergic rhinitis, and highlighted upper and lower airway comorbidities and their shared inflammatory pathways, thereby providing a reference for the precise and safe use of biologics in clinical practice.

articles.title: [Interpreting the 2026 consensus guidance on immune checkpoint inhibitors: evolving landscape of perioperative therapy for locally advanced rectal cancer].
articles.abstract: The treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) is shifting from traditional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy to the transformative advent of immunotherapy. In early 2026, the "Consensus guidance of immune checkpoint inhibitors in locally advanced rectal cancer" led by experts from the Colorectal Surgery Section of the Chinese Society of Surgery (CNSCRS), was published in the journal Gut. This consensus synthesized the latest clinical evidence and formulated 18 recommendations focusing on mismatch repair/microsatellite instability (MMR/MSI) testing, multidisciplinary team (MDT) decision-making, stratified treatment for both deficient mismatch repair/high microsatellite instability (dMMR/MSI-H) and roficient mismatch repair/microsatellite stability (pMMR/MSS) patients, Watch and Wait (W&W) strategy, local excision, and immune-related adverse event management. This article provides a systematic interpretation on the core tenets and a systematic review of the supporting clinical evidence, and then extends the discussion by incorporating the latest research findings. Furthermore, we compare these recommendations with current domestic and international guidelines to serve as a practical reference for colorectal surgeons and oncologists in China.

articles.title: A real-world feasibility and workflow experience using 4D intracardiac echocardiography to guide left atrial appendage closure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE) is increasingly being used to guide left atrial appendage closure (LAAC).

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: This is an evaluation of a single operator's outcomes treating an all-comers patient population referred for LAAC between September 2022 and September 2024. The operator transitioned from TEE to AcuNav Volume 4D-ICE guidance in August 2023. The primary objective was successful device implantation. Secondary objectives were the rate of complications and cessation of anticoagulation at 45 days.

RESULTS: 81 patients had LAAC with 4D-ICE guidance compared to 35 patients with TEE. Baseline characteristics were similar. Device implantation was successful in 94% with ICE and 100% with TEE. There was 1 non-disabling stroke in the ICE group and 2 mortality events in the TEE group within 30 days of the procedure. Rates of anticoagulation cessation at 45 days were 91% with ICE and 89% with TEE.

CONCLUSIONS: 4D-ICE can be used to guide LAAC with the Watchman FLX with excellent procedural success and minimal periprocedural complications comparable to TEE.

articles.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury in thoracic noncardiac surgery: incidence, impact on outcomes, risk and protective factors, and evolving preventive strategies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) significantly impairs short- and long-term clinical outcomes after thoracic noncardiac surgery, including increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. This review synthesizes current evidence on the incidence, prognostic impact, risk factors, and evolving preventive strategies for AKI in thoracic surgery.

RECENT FINDINGS: Intraoperative fluid imbalance and hypotension are robust, modifiable risk factors for AKI. While goal-directed fluid therapy and machine learning-based Acumen Hypotension Prediction Index (Edwards Lifesciences, Irvine, California, USA) monitoring effectively optimize intraoperative hemodynamics and reduce hypotensive episodes, recent clinical trials and meta-analyses indicate they do not directly reduce postoperative AKI rates after general thoracic surgery. However, optimizing drug administration - such as continuous intravenous tacrolimus and shortened vancomycin duration - has demonstrated clinical benefit. Furthermore, evidence outside thoracic surgery demonstrates that the biomarker-guided Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes care bundle significantly decreases moderate-to-severe AKI in high-risk surgical populations, suggesting potential applicability in thoracic surgical care.

SUMMARY: Given the multifactorial etiology of AKI, single hemodynamic interventions alone are insufficient for prevention. Perioperative care should integrate multimodality strategies, including optimal fluid and pressure management, pharmacological stewardship, and high-risk screening with care bundles. Further studies are needed to establish tailored preventive protocols, particularly for high-risk thoracic procedures such as lung transplantation and pneumonectomy.

articles.title: Physical distancing to prevent influenza-like illness on a college campus: The eX-FLU trial.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Public health recommendations often advise people to isolate when infected with influenza-like illness (ILI) with the goal of promoting physical distancing and limiting face-to-face interactions when risk of transmission is highest. Because isolation may have negative consequences, it is important to carefully assess whether encouragement to physically distance actually prevents cases of ILI. College campuses can be especially vulnerable to outbreaks of ILI and are ideal environments for assessing the impact of encouragement-to-physically-distance interventions. The eX-FLU cluster-randomized trial followed 579 students on a college campus over a ten-week period during flu season to evaluate such an intervention. Students in the trial were randomized to receive the intervention-encouragement to isolate in their dorm room when symptomatic for ILI-or control. Evaluating the effect of this intervention is challenging because of dependence between students in the trial and an anticipated spillover effect of the intervention. Moreover, while the intervention was designed to affect both face-to-face interactions and ILI infections, the effect on ILI infections is of primary public health interest. In this paper, a randomization-based testing procedure is proposed to assess the intervention effect specifically on ILI infections in the presence of dependent data and spillover effects. The testing procedure is shown theoretically and empirically to control the type I error rate and have good statistical power to detect an intervention effect in trials similar to eX-FLU. When applied to the eX-FLU data, this testing procedure gives moderate evidence that the intervention reduced ILI infections.

articles.title: ChREBP drives diabetic kidney disease, and its inhibition confers renal protection.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a major medical burden. Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of CKD, but intracellular pathways that can be pharmacologically targeted are poorly defined. Using transcriptome screening of DKD model mice we found that a carbohydrate-responsive element-binding protein (ChREBP)-dependent transcriptional cascade is markedly up-regulated in diabetic kidneys. Genetic ablation of ChREBP in diabetic mice ameliorated DKD, establishing ChREBP as a potential causal driver. A chemical screen based on ChREBP transcriptional activity identified D-532 as a small-molecule inhibitor that is effective in human and rodent cells. Oral administration of D-532 protected multiple diabetic mouse models from DKD progression and suppressed ChREBP and its downstream targets, including genes associated with excessive reactive oxygen species production. These findings position ChREBP as a pharmacologically targetable transcriptional driver of DKD and provide proof of concept that ChREBP inhibition can confer renal protection.

articles.title: Non-invasive and invasive imaging for guiding PCI of chronic total occlusions.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for chronic total occlusions (CTO) remains technically challenging, with lower technical success than non-CTO PCI. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) may improve procedural and stent-related outcomes by supporting procedural planning, lesion crossing, and stent optimization.

AREAS COVERED: A literature search of PubMed, Google scholar, identified randomized trials, registries, observational studies, meta-analyses, and consensus documents on CCTA and IVUS in CTO PCI. CCTA enables three-dimensional assessment of cap morphology, occlusion length, tortuosity, calcification, and distal vessel quality, refining complexity assessment and strategy selection. IVUS provides real-time guidance for proximal cap identification, guidewire position, reentry techniques, vessel sizing, and stent optimization. Artificial intelligence and image co-registration are also discussed.

EXPERT OPINION: CCTA and IVUS provide complementary information across the stages of CTO PCI. Selective preprocedural CCTA may be most valuable in anatomically complex lesions, whereas IVUS supports lesion crossing and should be strongly considered for stent optimization. Wider adoption will depend on workflow integration, operator training, automated image analysis, and prospective validation of imaging-guided strategies.

articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Cardiovascular and Microvascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Analysis of the UK Biobank.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its associations across cardiovascular and microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 893 UK Biobank participants with type 2 diabetes, whole-exome sequencing, and no prevalent cardiovascular or microvascular complications. CHIP was defined from the curated UK Biobank call set by ≥1 driver variant with a variant allele fraction ≥2%. Associations with incident outcomes were evaluated using Fine-Gray models with multiple imputation for missing covariates. Driver-gene, clone-size, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses were exploratory.

RESULTS: CHIP was present in 670 participants (3.7%) over a median follow-up of 14.6 years. CHIP was associated with the composite cardiovascular outcome (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR], 1.19 [95% CI, 1.00-1.42]), with heart failure showing the clearest component association (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.13-1.81]); acute coronary syndrome and stroke were not significantly associated. CHIP was also associated with the composite microvascular outcome (SHR, 1.34 [95% CI, 1.15-1.56]), broad chronic kidney disease (SHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.05-1.57]), and retinopathy (SHR, 1.43 [95% CI, 1.15-1.77]) but not neuropathy or strict diabetes-specific nephropathy. Ten-year adjusted risk differences were 1.94% and 3.46% for the cardiovascular and microvascular composites, respectively. Among 2919 proteins, ZBP1 (Z-DNA-binding protein 1) was the only protein retained after false-discovery-rate correction; no metabolite module was associated with CHIP after correction, whereas selected lipoprotein and amino acid/lactate modules were associated with cardiovascular outcomes, particularly heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with type 2 diabetes, CHIP was associated with a higher risk of incident microvascular complications and, among cardiovascular outcomes, most consistently with heart failure. Exploratory multiomic findings, including a protein-wide ZBP1 signal and selected metabolic associations with cardiovascular outcomes, provided additional biological context but require independent validation.

articles.title: Sex-Stratified Outcomes in Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis: The BASIS Subgroup Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The BASIS (Balloon Angioplasty for Symptomatic Intracranial Artery Stenosis) trial demonstrated that balloon angioplasty plus aggressive medical management was superior to aggressive medical management alone for symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. However, whether sex modifies this treatment effect is unknown.

METHODS: This prespecified secondary analysis of the BASIS randomized controlled trial included 501 patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis from 31 Chinese centers (November 2018 to April 2022). Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between sexes and across treatment arms within each sex. The primary outcome was stroke or death within 30 days, or ischemic stroke in the qualifying artery territory or revascularization beyond 30 days through 12 months.

RESULTS: Among 501 patients (mean age, 58 years), 158 (31.5%) were women. No significant sex-by-treatment interaction was observed for primary or key secondary outcomes (all P for interaction >0.05). In sex-stratified analyses, balloon angioplasty reduced primary outcome risk versus aggressive medical management in men (2.9% versus 11.1%; hazard ratio [HR]=0.21 [95% CI, 0.07-0.65]; P=0.01). In women, the effect favored balloon angioplasty but was not statistically significant (7.8% versus 18.5%; HR=0.37 [95% CI, 0.14-1.01]; P=0.051).

CONCLUSIONS: No significant interaction between sex and treatment effect was found, suggesting balloon angioplasty's benefit relative to aggressive medical management does not clearly differ by sex. Sex-stratified results showed significant benefit in men and a nonsignificant trend in women, but the study lacked power for definitive interaction testing, so findings are exploratory. Further research is needed to confirm these findings in broader populations.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT03703635.

articles.title: Acute Kidney Injury Disrupts Cardiac Remodeling via SerpinA3N.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiorenal syndrome type 3 describes cardiac injury triggered by acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI caused by ischemia reperfusion injury represents a model for kidney injury during kidney transplant. It is well known that kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk to develop cardiac fibrosis; however, the molecular mechanisms linking renal injury to myocardial remodeling or cardiac fibrosis remain unclear.

METHODS: Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of ischemia reperfusion injury-AKI, we combined proteomics and RNA seqencing transcriptomics to define early cardiac responses. We validated the proteomics and RNA sequencing data with quantitative polymerase chain reaction, ELISA, cytokine array, and western blotting for profibrotic and injury markers. We assessed SerpinA3N function using a granzyme B activity assay kit and XAV939, an inhibitor of SerpinA3N. Ingenuity pathway analysis further confirmed serine protease activity inhibition and increased expression of cardiac fibrosis-related genes after AKI.

RESULTS: Successful establishment of renal ischemia reperfusion injury causing AKI, followed by significant induction of cardiac injury. AKI significantly upregulated SerpinA3N in the heart while suppressing serine protease (granzyme B) activity. Concomitantly, AKI hearts displayed elevated profibrotic genes (FN1, COL1A1, TGF-β1), mitochondrial dysfunction, and heightened inflammatory signaling. In vitro, inhibition of SerpinA3N with XAV939 restored granzyme B activity, confirming direct suppression by SerpinA3N.

CONCLUSIONS: We conclude that SerpinA3N serves as a key mediator of cardiorenal syndrome type 3 pathogenesis, by inhibiting granzyme B, which promotes profibrotic remodeling in the heart following AKI. Targeting SerpinA3N could be a potential therapeutic approach that restores balanced extracellular matrix turnover and mitigates cardiac fibrosis.

articles.title: Metabolic and Renal Dysfunction Are Associated With Intraplaque Lipid Burden Assessed by Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Intravascular Ultrasound: Insights Into the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Axis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework emphasizes the interrelated contributions of metabolic and renal dysfunction to cardiovascular risk. Whether these disturbances are reflected in coronary plaque composition remains incompletely understood. We evaluated the association of metabolic and renal dysfunction with intraplaque lipid burden using near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound.

METHODS: Intraplaque lipid burden was assessed by the maximum lipid core burden index (LCBI) within a 4-mm segment (maxLCBI4mm), and lipid-rich plaque (LRP) was defined as maxLCBI4mm≥324.7. Multivariable linear regression models were constructed with maxLCBI4mm as the dependent variable, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations with LRP.

RESULTS: Among 483 patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention with pre-intervention near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound imaging, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate and higher hemoglobin A1c were independently associated with greater intraplaque lipid burden and higher odds of LRP. In analyses standardized per 1 SD, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed the strongest association with maxLCBI4mm (β=52.51; 95% CI, 27.49-77.53), followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate (β=33.38; 95% CI, 9.97-56.80) and hemoglobin A1c (β=24.71; 95% CI, 3.71-45.71). Similarly, lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (odds tatio [OR], 1.36; 95% CI, 1.06-1.75) and higher hemoglobin A1c (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.05-1.77) were independently associated with LRP. No significant interaction between estimated glomerular filtration rate and hemoglobin A1c was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic and renal dysfunction are independently associated with intraplaque lipid burden assessed by near-infrared spectroscopy intravascular ultrasound. These findings provide intracoronary imaging evidence linking the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic framework to plaque-level lipid accumulation.

articles.title: Thirty-Day All-Cause Readmissions After Pregnancy-Associated Hospitalizations With Heart Failure in the United States: Analysis of the Nationwide Readmissions Database.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of pregnancy-related morbidity and mortality in the United States. There is a paucity of data regarding pregnancy-associated heart failure readmissions. This study aims to characterize the 30-day heart failure readmission patterns in pregnancy-associated admissions.

METHODS: The National Readmission Database from 2016 to 2021 was used to identify women aged 13 to 49 with an index hospitalization with heart failure as the primary or secondary diagnosis during a pregnancy-related admission, identified by diagnosis-related group codes and International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause readmission. Survey-weighted descriptive analyses and hierarchical multivariable logistic regression were used to characterize readmission patterns and identify independently associated factors.

RESULTS: Among 19 452 eligible index hospitalizations, 2659 were followed by a 30-day readmission; the survey-weighted readmission rate was 13.5%. In the fully adjusted model, Medicare and Medicaid coverage, residence in a small metropolitan area, greater All Patient Refined Diagnosis-Related Group severity, discharge with home health care, and discharge against medical advice were associated with higher odds of readmission. Deficiency anemia, chronic pulmonary disease, diabetes without chronic complications, renal failure, solid tumor without metastasis, and cardiovascular or respiratory disorders complicating pregnancy were also independently associated with increased readmission.

CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 pregnancy-associated hospitalizations complicated by heart failure was followed by a 30-day all-cause readmission. Readmission risk reflected a combination of illness severity, discharge disposition, payer status, geographic location, and selected medical and pregnancy-related comorbidities. These findings support the development and evaluation of individualized, multidisciplinary transitional-care strategies for patients at highest risk.

articles.title: Rationale and Design of a Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial: LEAP-Block.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrioventricular block with normal cardiac function is common with right ventricular pacing, which raises risks of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and symptomatic heart failure in some patients with high pacing burden. Left bundle-branch area pacing demonstrates protective potential to reduce the risk of heart failure on the basis of observational studies. Evidence from a large multicenter randomized controlled trial remains limited.

METHODS: The LEAP-Block (Impact of Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing Versus Right Ventricular Pacing in Atrioventricular Block) study is a prospective multicenter, investigator-initiated randomized controlled trial aiming to verify the hypothesis that left bundle-branch area pacing might have superior impact to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in patients with atrioventricular block requiring high burden of ventricular pacing and left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%. A total of 484 patients will be randomized to either left bundle-branch area pacing or right ventricular pacing (1:1). The primary end point is the composite events of all-cause death, heart failure events, and upgrade to biventricular pacing-delivered cardiac resynchronization therapy during at least 24 months of follow-up. Secondary end points include changes in echocardiographic, electrocardiographic, and pacing parameters and device-related complications.

CONCLUSIONS: The LEAP-Block study aims to compare the impact of left bundle-branch area pacing versus conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved cardiac function with respect to midterm clinical outcomes. This trial will provide high-quality evidence for the selection of optimal pacing strategies in clinical practice.

REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT04730921.

articles.title: Evaluating the Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Paradox in Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypercholesterolemia is an established cardiovascular risk factor. However, studies in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) showed an association between low low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and increased mortality, termed the "LDL-C paradox." This study examined the impact of LDL-C on clinical outcomes in patients with HFrEF and identify distinct hypocholesterolemia subgroups using latent class analysis.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with HFrEF (left ventricular EF <40%) from national registries (2016-2022) were stratified by LDL-C quartiles, with the lowest quartile ≤1.73 mmol/L. Latent class analysis was performed to identify subsets of patients in the lowest quartile. Outcomes included 1-year all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, readmission, and composite end points.

RESULTS: Among 2188 patients, the lowest LDL-C quartile had higher 1-year all-cause mortality than Quartile 2 and 3 (P<0.05) but not Quartile 4, with no intergroup differences in cardiovascular mortality, readmissions, or composite outcomes between groups. Latent class analysis identified 2 hypocholesterolemia subgroups: pathological and nonpathological hypocholesterolemia. The pathological subgroup was older, lower weight, with higher comorbidity burden. Compared with patients with hypercholesterolemia, the pathological hypocholesterolemia subgroup had higher 1-year all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.14 [95% CI, 1.17-2.69], P<0.001), cardiovascular mortality (adjusted HR, 1.93 [95% CI, 1.46-2.54], P<0.001), and composite end points (adjusted HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.01-1.30], P=0.037), and the subgroup with nonpathological hypocholesterolemia showed comparable outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: A distinct subset of patients with HFrEF with low LDL-C demonstrates different clinical characteristics (older and higher comorbidity burden) and poorer outcomes, potentially elucidating the "LDL-C paradox" cause in patients with HFrEF.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

articles.title: Racial and Ethnic Disparities in Postarrest Cardiac Procedures for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Effective postarrest care facilitates optimal outcomes for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Relatively little research has evaluated whether there may be racial or ethnic disparities in the workup and management of the patient post arrest.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied out-of-hospital cardiac arrests using the TriNetX research database. We defined out-of-hospital cardiac arrest as any emergency department visit (2013-2024) with a diagnosis of cardiac arrest and included patients who survived to admission. Multivariate adjusted logistic regression was used to compare rates of the following cardiac interventions across race or ethnicity: (1) echocardiography; (2) left heart catheterization; (3) percutaneous coronary intervention; (4) ventricular assist device placement; and (5) automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement.

RESULTS: A total of 58 394 cases of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest met inclusion criteria. Compared with White patients (left heart catheterization: 13.9%, percutaneous coronary intervention: 7.1%, ventricular assist device: 3.0%, automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator: 0.9%), Black patients had lower odds of receiving left heart catheterization (7.2%, adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.60 [95% CI, 0.55-0.64]), percutaneous coronary intervention (2.6%, aOR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.42-0.53]), ventricular assist device placement (1.6%, aOR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.60-0.80]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.41-0.70]). Hispanic/Latino patients were also less likely to receive left heart catheterization (8.9%, aOR, 0.72 [95% CI, 0.64-0.80]), percutaneous coronary intervention (3.7%, aOR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.53-0.74]), and automated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement (0.4%, aOR, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.33-0.81]).

CONCLUSIONS: Our large multicenter analysis identifies racial or ethnic disparities in postarrest cardiac workup and management. Further research is needed to identify potential causes for these disparities with the hope of developing strategies to address them.

articles.title: Poorly Controlled Hypertension Alters Coronary Microvascular Contractile Response to Endothelin-1 Before and After Cardiac Surgery.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic hypertension have worse outcomes following on-pump (cardioplegia and cardiopulmonary bypass [CP/CPB]) cardiac surgery. Altered vasomotor function of the coronary microvasculature to ET-1 (endothelin-1) and other agonists may underlie these differences.

METHODS: Heart samples were collected from 85 patients undergoing CP/CPB enrolled in this observational study. Ex vivo coronary microvascular responses to ET-1, adenosine diphosphate, and sodium nitroprusside were assessed using video microscopy. Immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and multiomics approaches were also used.

RESULTS: Coronary microvascular contractile response to ET-1 in patients with uncontrolled hypertension was increased compared with the other 2 cohorts pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05 across ET-1 10-10 to 10-7 mmol/L). Adenosine diphosphate-induced coronary microvascular vasodilation was conversely decreased (P<0.05 for adenosine diphosphate 10-5 and 10-4 mmol/L). Post-CP/CPB microvascular responses to ET-1 and adenosine diphosphate were blunted overall (P<0.05). Antagonism of pro-vasoconstrictive endothelinA receptor diminished contractile response (P<0.05). Transcriptomics and proteomics showed wide regulation of pro-vasoconstrictive pathways. Regression showed that hypertension status and cardiac mass reliably approximated ET-1-induced coronary microvascular contraction (R2 0.95 pre-CP/CPB, R2 0.86 post-CP/CPB), which, in turn, estimated change in ejection fraction pre- and post-CP/CPB (P<0.05). Patients with uncontrolled hypertension had -11% change in EF when compared with the other 2 groups pooled (P<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Altered coronary microvascular vasomotor function in patients with uncontrolled hypertension may jeopardize myocardial perfusion. Hypertension status and cardiac mass may be used to prognosticate this physiology, which, in turn, estimates change in ejection fraction postoperatively. Perioperative endothelin receptor blockers may benefit patients with uncontrolled hypertension and thus warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Side Effects of Low-Dose Colchicine in Chronic Coronary Disease: A Post Hoc Analysis of the LoDoCo2 Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose colchicine reduces cardiovascular events in patients with chronic coronary disease. However, side effects may compromise compliance and lead to discontinuation of treatment. Therefore, we aimed to assess the incidence of side effects leading to discontinuation of treatment in the LoDoCo2 (Low-Dose Colchicine 2) trial.

METHODS: The LoDoCo2 trial was a randomized controlled trial evaluating colchicine versus placebo in patients with chronic coronary disease. Participants entered a 30-day open-label run-in phase during which all participants received colchicine 0.5 mg once daily, followed by randomization to colchicine or placebo. Tolerability-related side effects leading to treatment discontinuation were evaluated at the end of the 30-day run-in phase and during the randomized phase (median follow-up, 29.5 [interquartile range, 21.6-47.4] months). Cumulative incidence of side effects was presented using Kaplan-Meier curves and compared by treatment arm using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: During the 30-day run-in phase, 618 of 6519 (9.5%) participants reported side effects. Women had a higher risk of side effects than men during the 30-day run-in phase (odds ratio, 1.53 [95% CI, 1.23-1.89]). After randomization, 114 participants (4.2%) in the colchicine group and 120 (4.4%) in the placebo group discontinued treatment due to side effects (hazard ratio [HR], 0.95 [95% CI, 0.73-1.22]). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common (colchicine 2.0% versus placebo 1.7%) followed by myalgia (colchicine 1.2% versus placebo 1.6%). No differences in the risk of side effects between colchicine and placebo were seen for any of the subgroups. Women did have a higher risk of reporting side effects compared with men, regardless of assigned treatment (HR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.22-2.25]).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with chronic coronary disease that tolerated initial treatment with low-dose colchicine, long-term discontinuation due to side effects was uncommon and did not differ between colchicine and placebo.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org/au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12614000093684.

articles.title: Greenspace Exposure Reduces the Risk of Hypertension: A Large Prospective Cohort Study in Northwestern China.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effects of greenspace on hypertension remain unconfirmed. This study aimed to validate this by performing a large prospective cohort study in China.

METHODS: PEAHEN-China (Prospective Environment and Health Epidemiological Study in Northwestern China) recruited 5 484 119 adults in 2017 and followed them to 2021. Blood pressure levels and hypertension were measured and defined using recommended standards. Greenspace exposure was estimated using the normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index. Cox regression models and generalized estimating equation models were used to assess the associations of greenspace with hypertension incidence and blood pressure levels, respectively. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were also performed.

RESULTS: During a median 3.21-year follow-up, 1 290 003 new hypertension cases occurred. Living in greener areas was significantly associated with a lower risk of hypertension and lower blood pressure levels. For example, in the adjusted models, compared with the first quartile of normalized difference vegetation index and enhanced vegetation index within a 500-m buffer, the hazard ratios of incident hypertension in the fourth quartile of the 2 metrics were 0.871 (95% CI, 0.861-0.881) and 0.896 (95% CI, 0.885-0.906). In addition, stronger associations of greenspace exposure with hypertension risk and blood pressure levels were observed in younger, male, rural, and less educated participants than their counterparts.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study indicates that neighborhood greenspace may reduce residents' odds of having hypertension, offering robust evidence for developing policies and strategies to mitigate the burden of hypertension.

articles.title: Effects of Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair on Right Heart Dimension and Function.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) has developed as a treatment option for patients experiencing severe tricuspid regurgitation. T-TEER consistently reduces tricuspid regurgitation, but data on subsequent right heart remodeling remain limited. The aim of this study was to evaluate changes in right heart dimension and function after T-TEER using extended echocardiographic follow-up.

METHODS: The study was based on the international EuroTR (European Registry of Transcatheter Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation), including patients undergoing T-TEER between 2016 and 2024 at 18 European centers. Eligible were patients with available baseline and follow-up (≥90 days postprocedure) echocardiographic assessment.

RESULTS: A total of 699 patients (mean age, 78±8 years; 56% women) were included in the analysis. Echocardiographic follow-up was performed at a median of 407 days (interquartile range, 205-801 days). Right heart dimensions significantly decreased: right ventricular (RV) midventricular diameter from 40.2±8.9 to 37.1±8.4 mm (P<0.001) and end-diastolic area from 28.7±9.0 to 26.2±9.6 cm2 (P<0.001). Procedural success was significantly associated with positive RV remodeling (odds ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.07-3.09]). For RV function, a decline of fractional area change from 37.8%±10.2% to 33.3%±10.1% (P<0.001), and tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion from 17.4±4.7 to 16.6±4.7 mm (P<0.001) was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In the subset of surviving patients with available echocardiographic follow-up, treatment with T-TEER led to favorable long-term changes with reduced RV dimension, associated with procedural success. RV function modestly decreased, likely reflecting normalization after volume unloading.

articles.title: Adeno-Associated Virus-Induced Humanized Hypertensive Mouse Model Validates N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Angiotensinogen as a Long-Acting Antihypertensive Therapy.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, yet current therapeutic strategies lack sustained efficacy and long-term stability. Our study aimed to construct a humanized rodent model for drugs development especially currently prevalent small interfering RNA medication.

METHODS: A humanized hypertensive mouse model was generated by subcutaneous injection of neonatal mice with adeno-associated viruses encoding hAGT (human angiotensinogen) and hRENIN (human renin). Blood pressure was monitored weekly via tail-cuff plethysmography. Expression of hAGT and hRENIN was assessed by ELISA, Western blot, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography at 4 and 6 months postinjection. Hypertension-associated comorbidities were examined through histological analysis and ELISA. A modified N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated small interfering RNA targeting human hepatic AGT (GalNAc-siAGT) was screened and subcutaneously administered to humanized hypertensive mice, either alone or in combination with valsartan, to evaluate therapeutic efficacy.

RESULTS: The dual adeno-associated virus-induced humanized hypertensive model exhibited a sustained hypertension for 6 months and manifested prevalent comorbidities, including heart failure and kidney disease. This modified GalNAc-siAGT demonstrated significant activity in knocking down hAGT both in vitro and in vivo. Only a single subcutaneous injection of GalNAc-siAGT in humanized hypertensive mice led to a sustained reduction in blood pressure lasting for 2 months, accompanied by cardio- and renoprotective effects. Moreover, combining GalNAc-siAGT with the renin-angiotensin system blocker, valsartan, significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study validated the antihypertensive therapeutic effect of GalNAc-siAGT in a humanized hypertensive murine model while highlighting the translational potential of this model for clinical drug development.

articles.title: Incidence of Cardiovascular Disease in a Primary Care Population of Young Adults by Disaggregated Race and Ethnicity.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death in the United States, with well-documented racial and ethnic disparities. Data are limited on incidence among patients aged <50 years, particularly within disaggregated Asian and Hispanic subgroups and individuals identifying with multiple racial or ethnic groups. We estimated CVD incidence rates for these groups and assessed whether disparities are explained by other clinical and demographic risk factors.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used Sutter Health Electronic Health Record data (2010-2024) for adults aged 18 to 49 years with at least 2 primary care visits and a 2-year observed baseline period free of CVD. Incident CVD was defined as myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. We estimated incidence rates, applied age and sex standardization, and fit Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for additional risk factors.

RESULTS: In a cohort of 1 178 551 patients, incidence was 1.14 cases per 1000 person-years (95% CI, 1.12-1.17). After standardization, Pacific Islander individuals (hazard ratio [HR], 2.90 [95% CI, 2.29-3.52]) and non-Hispanic Black individuals (HR, 2.82 [95% CI, 2.58-3.06]) had the highest incidence. Within the Asian group, Filipino individuals had the highest incidence (HR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.42-1.79]). Hispanic subgroups showed less heterogeneity. Elevated HRs persisted among some groups after adjustment with Cox models.

CONCLUSIONS: Young adult CVD incidence varied across racial and ethnic subgroups. Elevated risk persisted in several groups after adjustment, consistent with the influence of unmeasured social drivers. These findings support collection of granular racial and ethnic data and validation of existing risk prediction tools in young adult subgroups.

articles.title: Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Versus Direct Oral Anticoagulation in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion With Watchman FLX.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy after left atrial appendage occlusion remains uncertain.

METHODS: We studied 2817 patients undergoing left atrial appendage occlusion at 8 hospitals from 2016 to 2023 using registry data linked to Medicare claims. Among 2448 Watchman FLX recipients, the primary exposure was time-varying dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) versus pooled direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC)-based therapy. Outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), major bleeding, and device complications. The primary instrumental-variable analysis used operator FLX preference; overlap weighting was secondary and pairwise regimen comparisons exploratory.

RESULTS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE (absolute risk difference [ARD], -1.5% [95% CI, -1.9% to -1.0%]; number needed to treat, 67) and major bleeding (ARD -1.6% [95% CI, -2.0% to -0.9%]; number needed to treat, 63) than pooled DOAC-based therapy, without increased device complications. Overlap-weighted associations with MACE and major bleeding were nonsignificant. In exploratory pairwise analyses, DAPT did not differ significantly from DOAC monotherapy for MACE or major bleeding; lower major bleeding was limited to DAPT versus DOAC plus single antiplatelet therapy (ARD, -0.6% [95% CI, -1.1% to -0.2%]; P=0.008). Most estimated benefit accrued within 6 months.

CONCLUSIONS: DAPT was associated with lower MACE and major bleeding than pooled DOAC-based therapy after Watchman FLX implantation. The safety benefit was concentrated in the comparison with DOAC + single antiplatelet therapy, whereas DAPT and DOAC monotherapy did not clearly differ in either outcome. These findings support randomized trials comparing DAPT with DOAC monotherapy.

articles.title: Associations of Cumulative Wrist Accelerometer-Derived Physical Activity and Proxies of Sedentary Behavior With Early Cardiac Remodeling in Healthy Adolescents.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior are associated with adverse cardiac remodeling in adults, but evidence in adolescence remains limited. This study examined associations of cumulative accelerometer-derived physical activity and proxies of sedentary behavior during adolescence with early subclinical cardiac features assessed by cardiovascular magnetic resonance.

METHODS: A total of 111 adolescents (55.9% girls) wore a wrist-worn triaxial accelerometer at ages 12, 14, and 16 years to measure physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies. A 3-Tesla cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan was performed at final follow-up to assess cardiac structure and function.
