Multivariable linear regression models examined associations between cumulative physical activity and sedentary behavior proxies and cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived metrics.

RESULTS: Daily step counts were positively associated with indexed end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes of the left ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.90 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.42-1.37]; 0.36 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.10-0.63], respectively) and the right ventricle (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 1.03 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.44-1.61]; 0.44 mL/m2.7 [95% CI, 0.05-0.82], respectively), and with reduced right ventricular longitudinal strain (adjusted β per 1000 steps/d, 0.53% [95% CI, 0.16-0.91]). Greater time spent in sedentary bouts and a higher number of sedentary bouts were associated with increased left atrial active emptying fraction (adjusted β per 100 min/d, 8.21% [95% CI, 0.09-16.34]; adjusted β per 1 bout/d, 1.76% [95% CI, 0.17-3.35], respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Physical inactivity and sedentary behavior proxies during adolescence were independently associated with early markers of ventricular and atrial remodeling. These findings highlight early cardiac adaptations related to lifestyle behaviors and underscore the importance of promoting active lifestyles from a young age.

articles.title: Association of Stroke Severity With Efficacy of Early Tirofiban Infusion After Intravenous Thrombolysis.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to assess the effects of stroke severity at admission on the efficacy and safety of early tirofiban infusion following intravenous thrombolysis in patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke using data from the ASSET-IT (Advancing Stroke Safety and Efficacy Through Early Tirofiban Administration After Intravenous Thrombolysis) trial.

METHODS: All 832 patients with acute ischemic noncardioembolic stroke from the ASSET-IT database were included in this exploratory post hoc analysis. The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were an excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-1 at 90 days) and intracranial hemorrhage.

RESULTS: Among the 832 patients included, the median age was 69 (interquartile range, 59-76) years, 531 (63.8%) were men, 367 (44.1%) had minor stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6), and 465 (55.9%) had moderate-to-severe stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥6). There were significant interactions between the primary efficacy and safety outcomes (Pinteraction=0.008, Pinteraction=0.03; respectively). We observed that among patients with NIHSS score ≥6, tirofiban markedly increased odds of achieving an excellent functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.44-3.17]; P<0.001) without significantly increasing the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.37-2.09]; P=0.77). In contrast, no significant benefit was observed in the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score <6 group (adjusted odds ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.64-1.63]; P=0.94) but there was a significant increase in the risk of intracranial hemorrhage (adjusted odds ratio, 6.51 [95% CI, 1.42-62.03]; P=0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: Early tirofiban infusion may be more beneficial for patients with moderate-to-severe stroke treated with intravenous thrombolysis within 4.5 hours of onset, while simultaneously suggesting an increased potential risk of intracranial hemorrhage in minor stroke.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT06134622.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of Right Ventricular-Pulmonary Artery Coupling in Mitral Valve Surgery and Impact of Concomitant Tricuspid Valve Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic impact of baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling on clinical outcomes following mitral valve surgery with specific consideration of concomitant tricuspid valve repair remains uncertain.

METHODS: A total of 214 patients who underwent mitral valve surgery and presented with moderate tricuspid regurgitation at the index procedure were included. Patients were classified after baseline right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling (impaired versus normal). The primary study end point was a composite outcome of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization. Secondary study end points included all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization.

RESULTS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was observed in 112 patients (52%), while 102 patients (48%) had normal right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling. The rate of concomitant tricuspid valve repair was similar between study groups (50.0% versus 49.0%, P=0.886). Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling was associated with a higher hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 2.60, 95% CI 1.32-5.14, P=0.006), heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio 3.29, 95% CI 1.27-8.54, P=0.014), and all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 2.25, 95% CI 1.11-4.59, P=0.025) during follow-up. Additionally, concomitant tricuspid valve repair in patients with moderate tricuspid regurgitation was associated with a lower hazard of the composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.26-0.80, P=0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: Impaired right ventricular-pulmonary artery coupling is a predictor of adverse outcomes after mitral valve surgery. Concomitant tricuspid valve repair for moderate tricuspid regurgitation seems to be associated with improved outcomes.

articles.title: Population Impact of the 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Dyslipidemia Guideline on Lipid-Lowering Therapy Eligibility Among US Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia guideline replaces the pooled cohort equations with the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease component of the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events equations for primary prevention risk estimation and modifies lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) eligibility by lowering the risk-based treatment threshold and expanding diabetes and chronic kidney disease criteria. The population-level impact of this transition is uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 participants aged 40 to 75 years without self-reported atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and with available low-density lipoprotein cholesterol. Survey weights were used to generate national estimates. Guideline-supported LLT eligibility was assessed under the 2018 pooled cohort equations-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association cholesterol framework and the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association dyslipidemia framework. Current LLT use was assessed among guideline-supported adults.

RESULTS: The analytic sample included 1662 participants, representing 115.05 million US adults. LLT was supported for 42.82 million adults under the 2018 framework and 42.17 million under the 2026 framework, a net decrease of 0.65 million. Reclassification was substantial: 37.42 million remained supported, 5.40 million lost support, 4.75 million newly gained support, and 67.48 million remained unsupported. Among supported adults, current LLT use was 39.4% under the 2018 framework and 40.5% under the 2026 framework.

CONCLUSIONS: Transition to the 2026 Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events-based framework produced little net change in LLT eligibility but meaningfully changed who was supported for therapy. Persistent undertreatment remains a major implementation gap.

articles.title: High on the Heart? Cannabis Use and Cardiovascular Disease: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract: Cannabis use has increased substantially over the past 2 decades following shifts in public perception, legalization, and medical usage. Although neurological and psychiatric effects are well known, the cardiovascular effects of cannabis exposure are largely understudied. This review evaluates the cardiovascular effects of cannabis use by examining clinical evidence, epidemiological data, and underlying biochemical mechanisms. This review examines cannabis-related cardiovascular conditions, including atherosclerosis, arrhythmias, heart failure, and stroke. The analysis focused on cannabinoid composition, route of administration, frequency of use, and cardiovascular outcomes. Evidence indicates that acute and high Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol/cannabidiol ratio cannabis use is associated with increased risks of various cardiovascular outcomes, especially among younger individuals without cardiovascular risk factors. Given rising use and increasing Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol potency, clinicians must routinely assess cannabis exposure when evaluating cardiovascular disease, especially in younger patients. Future research must prioritize the development of standardized exposure metrics in cannabis-related cardiovascular disease research, thus allowing clinicians and patients to better understand the cardiovascular risks of cannabis use and initiate effective cessation strategies.

articles.title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored.

METHODS: Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA.

RESULTS: A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P<0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P=0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P<0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort (P<0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement (P=0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement (P=0.08).

CONCLUSIONS: Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

articles.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Electroencephalography (EEG) detects clinical and subclinical seizures, but national utilization patterns remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Pediatric Health Information System (2016-2025) of neonates ≤28 days with dextro-transposition of the great arteries or single-ventricle physiology undergoing surgical repair or palliation. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization.

RESULTS: Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.

CONCLUSIONS: EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Apixaban Therapy for Coronary Artery Aneurysms After Kawasaki Disease.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation combined with aspirin lowers the risk of coronary thrombosis in patients with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms following Kawasaki disease. We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of apixaban in this high-risk pediatric population and compare it to conventional anticoagulant therapy.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, we described our experience with the use of apixaban in patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms. In patients who were previously exposed to conventional anticoagulation, we compared rates of new coronary thrombosis or myocardial infarction (effectiveness) and clinically relevant bleeding (safety) during apixaban versus antecedent conventional therapy. All patients received concomitant antiplatelet agents. Apixaban dosing was guided by weight and anti-Xa chromogenic assays.

RESULTS: Between 2018 and 2025, 28 patients with Kawasaki disease (median age 6.7 years; 75% male) with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms were prescribed apixaban. Of these, 27 (96%) had previously received vitamin K antagonists or low molecular weight heparin. The rates of new coronary thrombosis and new myocardial infarctions were not higher when patients received apixaban versus conventional anticoagulation (0.025 versus 0.041 events per person-year; incidence rate ratio [IRR], 0.61 [95% CI, 0.06-3.3] and 0.013 versus 0.041 events per person-year; IRR, 0.31 [95% CI, 0.01-2.5], respectively). Rates of clinically relevant bleeding were also not higher for apixaban versus conventional therapy (0.038 versus 0.058 events per person-year, IRR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.11-2.5]).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective single-center series of pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease with large/giant coronary artery aneurysms, apixaban combined with antiplatelet therapy was well tolerated and demonstrated no evidence of increased harm relative to conventional anticoagulants. Multicenter research is needed to confirm these findings and define the optimal therapeutic range for apixaban in this high-risk population.

articles.title: Safety and Efficacy of Topical Nitroglycerin for Radial Artery Dilation (The RADial Trial): A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transradial coronary catheterization is associated with a reduced risk of bleeding and vascular complications. Prior studies have evaluated nitroglycerin to improve transradial access by vasodilating the radial artery, but the optimal route of administration for preprocedural arterial dilation remains unclear.

METHODS: In the RADial Trial (Radial Artery Dilatation Trial) patients undergoing transradial coronary catheterization were randomized in a double-blind fashion to receive either a placebo or topical nitroglycerin ointment (nitropaste). The primary outcome was the mean change in radial artery dimensions, assessed using paired t tests. Categorical outcomes were analyzed using odds ratio (OR) with 95% CI.

RESULTS: A total of 260 patients (130 placebo, 130 nitroglycerin) were enrolled. Nitropaste significantly increased the mean diameter (2.65±0.6 versus 2.48±0.6 mm), circumference (8.37±1.63 versus 7.77±1.66) and cross-sectional area (5.63±2.28 versus 4.94±2.0 mm) of the radial artery, whereas no significant difference was observed in the placebo arm. Nitropaste was associated with a significant reduction in the number of skin punctures and risk of vasospasm (OR 0.34 [95% CI, 0.13-0.91], P=0.04). There was no significant difference between nitropaste and placebo groups in the odds of hematoma (OR, 0.32 [95% CI, 0.03-3.1], P=0.61), crossover to femoral access (OR, 2.29 [95% CI, 0.9-5.8], P=0.12), need for ultrasound-guided access (OR, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.13-1.15], P=0.13), and hypotension or headache (OR, 1.5 [95% CI, 0.24-9.2], P=1.0).

CONCLUSION: Preprocedural administration of nitropaste significantly increases radial artery size and reduces the risk of vasospasm without causing headache or hypotension.

REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05239013.

articles.title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a multi-omics characterization of FW-WM that connects genetic susceptibility, vascular factors, and neurological outcomes, supporting FW-WM as a tract-specific imaging phenotype with potential utility for neurological risk stratification.

articles.title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway-molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

articles.title: Microbiome-antibiotic-immune interactions influence mortality in preterm infant gut microbiota-humanized gnotobiotic mice.
articles.abstract: Infants born preterm are treated with antibiotics when bacterial infection is suspected. Antibiotics disrupt the gut microbiota, leading to unfavorable immune and infectious consequences. However, the impact of specific antibiotics on gut microbial and immune responses is largely unknown. We develop a humanized gnotobiotic mouse model where we gavage preterm infant stool into germ-free dams. We treat microbiota-humanized pups with subcutaneous antibiotics with probenecid to model empiric sepsis treatment regimens. Pups humanized with microbiota including ampicillin-resistant Enterobacteriaceae die during ampicillin with probenecid treatment with increased gut permeability and systemic microbial spread. Conversely, pups with microbiota containing gelatinase-expressing Enterococcus faecalis die during meropenem with probenecid treatment with increased gut E. faecalis and systemic immune dysregulation. Gut E. faecalis, especially strains containing gelE and fsr, increase in human preterm infant gut microbiomes after meropenem. These data raise concerns about the unintended consequences of antibiotic treatment and provide a framework for understanding microbiome-antibiotic-immune interplay.

articles.title: Comparison of artifact elimination strategies during postprocessing for the numerical assessment of localized low frequency magnetic field exposure of the hand.
articles.abstract: Numerical computations of induced electric field strengthEiinside the human body are prone to so-called 'staircasing errors', i.e. physically incorrect local enhancements of the computedEiat the edges of the cubical cells. Similar artifacts can occur due to imperfections in the anatomical body models used. In order to eliminate such numerical artifacts, International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection suggested in their 2010 guidelines to use the 99th percentile of the distribution of the 2 × 2 × 2 mm3averaged induced electric field strengthEi,avgfor comparison with the basic restrictions instead of the maximum computedEi,avgvalue. However, this suggestion was based on very early computational studies using anatomical body models with relatively low spatial resolution. Moreover, a 99th percentile-based assessment ofEi,avgappears generally questionable in case of highly localized exposure scenarios, where large fractions of the body remain almost unexposed, and therefore true local hot spots ofEi,avgthat should be considered may be excluded from the analysis, simply because the exposed tissue fraction is less than 1% of the total body volume. Although this problem has been repeatedly pointed out by several research groups in the past, the 99th percentile-based assessment unfortunately spread out as a 'general rule' into some guidelines for exposure assessment. Consequently, the compliance of many devices on the market with exposure limits can be questioned. In this paper we are quantifying the potential underestimation of exposure when using the 99th percentile-basedEi,avgfor several representative scenarios of a highly localized magnetic field exposure of the hand using a state-of-the-art anatomical body model. Besides comparing the 99th percentile-basedEi,avgvalues with values obtained when using higher percentiles, we also compare withEi,avgvalues obtained by applying a statistics-based outlier elimination method proposed by Arduinoet al(2020IEEE Trans. Electromagn. Compat.625). Our results clearly demonstrate the inappropriateness of the 99th percentile-based assessment, as it may lead to underestimations of the actual inducedEi,avgby more than a factor of 100, depending on the exposure scenario. In contrast, the statistics-based artifact elimination strategy proves to be a reasonable and robust method for estimating the actual valueEi,avgfor highly localized magnetic field exposure of the hand.

articles.title: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae, reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore-lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

articles.title: IFITM1-mediated restriction of henipavirus entry is associated with ephrinB2 reorganization and confinement in membrane nanodomains.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Nipah (NiV) and Hendra (HeV) viruses are prototype henipaviruses (HNV) within the family of Paramyxoviridae. They are highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxoviruses that cause fatal encephalitis in humans, with case fatality rates of 40 to 70%. These viruses use the receptor-binding protein (G) to engage host receptors ephrinB2 and/or ephrinB3, while the fusion protein (F) drives membrane fusion leading to virus entry and cell-cell fusion. Interferon-inducible transmembrane (IFITM) proteins restrict the infection of many unrelated viruses at virus entry. We show that the knockdown of IFITM1 enhances HNV entry and cell-cell fusion in both human epithelial and endothelial cells, while overexpression of IFITM1 inhibits both. Using single-molecule localization microscopy, we observed that IFITM1 forms nanoclusters on the plasma membrane that are enlarged upon interferon stimulation. IFITM1 clusters spatially co-occur with GM1-enriched, raft-like membrane domains. EphrinB2, a lipid raft resident, organizes into larger and denser clusters when associated with IFITM1, suggesting a preferential partitioning into membrane domains organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. Using single-particle tracking, we further show that lateral diffusion of ephrinB2 on the plasma membrane is confined in the presence of IFITM1. This confinement is not reversed by amphotericin B, nor is IFITM1-mediated NiV restriction. Our data show spatial reorganization and confinement of ephrinB2 within membrane domains that may be organized and/or influenced by IFITM1. These changes may contribute to HNV restriction, potentially by increasing the energy barrier for virus-cell membrane fusion and reducing productive virus-receptor encounters.

articles.title: Disruption of the NTCP-EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP-EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction. Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV-NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles. Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras-MAPK and PI3K-Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry. Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP-EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency. These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP-receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

articles.title: Host infection selects for sRNA variants that drive bacterial social cheating.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: Single-nucleotide mutations in regulatory small RNAs (sRNAs) represent a largely unexplored route to social cheating during bacterial infection. Here we show that arcZ, encoding a conserved Hfq-dependent sRNA in the plant pathogen Dickeya solani, undergoes recurrent single-nucleotide mutations during potato tuber infection. Five distinct arcZ alleles define a graded series of ArcZ functional impairment in which antifungal and protease activities are progressively reduced while virulence is compromised only in a subset of alleles. All five variants gain a fitness advantage exclusively during coinfection with wild-type arcZ1 cells. This advantage is strongest when variants are rare and declines as cheater frequency increases, ultimately correlating with reduced total bacterial productivity, the canonical signature of social cheating and a tragedy of the commons. No fitness benefit is detected in vitro. Transcriptomic profiling of five arcZ variants identifies a conserved core of 186 downregulated genes enriched in secreted and diffusible functions. Systematic genetic dissection, supported by quantitative proteomics, establishes BudAB-dependent limitation of tissue acidification as the dominant cooperative public good exploited during infection. Wild-type arcZ1 cells divert pyruvate flux toward acetoin via the BudAB pathway, maintaining a less acidic tissue environment that sustains disease progression; arcZ variants, which show reduced expression of this pathway, benefit from the less acidic environment maintained by wild-type cells without contributing to it. These results establish pleiotropic regulatory sRNAs as a previously unrecognized class of mutational targets for the emergence of social cheaters during host infection.

articles.title: The highly heat-inducible HspA6 and the thermolabile DnaJB5 are potent regulators of heat shock transcription factor 1 activity.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: In response to proteotoxic stress the central regulator of the heat shock response (HSR) in mammalian cells, Hsf1, trimerizes, binds DNA, and drives transcription of heat shock genes. We previously showed that Hsc70 (HspA8) assisted by its J-domain protein (JDP) cochaperone DnaJB1 dissociates Hsf1 from DNA by monomerizing the trimeric Hsf1 and thereby attenuates the HSR. Whether this feedback mechanism is specific to the HspA8-DnaJB1 pair or instead reflects a broader, isoform- and JDP-selective Hsp70 network controlling Hsf1 remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate that of all cytonuclear Hsp70s the highly heat-inducible HspA6 is most efficient in monomerizing Hsf1 in the presence of DnaJB1 and of all cytonuclear class A and class B JDPs, only DnaJB1, DnaJB4, and DnaJB5 assist in Hsf1 monomerization. Whereas cooperation of HspA6 and HspA8 with DnaJB1 and DnaJB4 absolutely depends on Hsp70s' C-terminal glutamate-glutamate-valine-glutamate (EEVD)-motif, cooperation with DnaJB5 does not. Consistent with these data, overproduction of EEVD-deleted HspA8 and HspA6 down-regulate the HSR in HeLa cells. DnaJB5 knockdown reduces HspA8-Hsf1 interaction under nonstress conditions revealing DnaJB5 as major targeting factor for HspA8 binding to Hsf1. On temperature upshift DnaJB5 partially unfolds and partitions into insoluble cell fractions, suggesting it is a thermosensor that allows for increased Hsf1 activity by reducing HspA8's ability to monomerize Hsf1. During ongoing heat shock, upregulated HspA6 and HspA8 then limit the HSR presumably targeted by heat-induced DnaJB1. HspA6 knock-down and overproduction in HeLa cells suggest that HspA6 functions in preventing an overshoot of the HSR.

articles.title: Off-Pump Versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain.

METHODS: This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated.

RESULTS: A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099).

CONCLUSIONS: In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes.

REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

articles.title: Structural basis of hypervariable region 1 dynamics on HCV envelope glycoproteins in immune evasion.
articles.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.abstract: The hypervariable region 1 (HVR1) of the hepatitis C virus E1E2 glycoprotein plays a crucial role in immune evasion through rapid mutation and shielding of conserved neutralizing epitopes. Despite its important role, the structural properties of HVR1 remain poorly understood, particularly how its conformation influences shielding mechanisms and receptor recognition. To date in all published E1E2 or E2 structures, the C-terminal part of HVR1 (394 to 411) remains unresolved. Using neutralizing antibody (nAb) RM1-38, which targets C-terminal HVR1 (residues 399 to 409), we investigated the folding, positioning, flexibility, and shielding function of the RM1-38 epitope, or antigenic site 399 (AS399), on HVR1 by X-ray crystallography and negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM). The crystal structure of RM1-38 Fab with the HVR1 AS399 peptide, combined with mutagenesis analysis, delineated the molecular basis of its strain-specific recognition and neutralization. nsEM and competition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay revealed that HVR1 exhibits pronounced conformational flexibility even in the presence of other nAbs bound to E1E2. Virus neutralization assays using a combination of RM1-38 and broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) demonstrated antagonistic effects of RM1-38 with the bnAbs. Furthermore, RM1-38 reduced E1E2 binding to cells expressing the scavenger receptor SR-BI, an HVR1-dependent receptor, but did not affect binding to CD81 tetraspanin. Together, these findings support a model in which HVR1 functions as a dynamic shield, where its conformational plasticity contributes to both receptor engagement and evasion of humoral immunity in persistent infection.

articles.title: Unimodal imaging foundation models and vision-language models in MRI: A systematic review of emerging methods and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence in medical imaging is shifting from task-specific algorithms toward adaptable foundation models (FMs) and vision-language models (VLMs). However, applying these models to MRI remains challenging because clinical interpretation requires integrating multi-parametric, volumetric imaging across multiple sequences with clinical context. This systematic review evaluates 35 studies on unimodal FMs and multimodal VLMs in MRI, summarizing emerging architectures, downstream applications, and challenges to clinical translation. Current research is concentrated in neuroimaging, with diagnostic classification representing the most mature application. Segmentation and outcome prediction also show promise, whereas automated report generation remains limited by poor clinical fidelity despite strong linguistic fluency. Broader adoption is hindered by heterogeneous MRI acquisition, limited large-scale paired image-text datasets, and inadequate safety-focused evaluation metrics. Advancing clinical translation will require standardized multicenter datasets, stronger integration with electronic health records and pathology, robust evaluation frameworks, and improved model explainability.

articles.title: Effects of dietary carbohydrate-to-fat ratio on the gut microbiome following weight loss.
articles.abstract: Reducing dietary carbohydrates can improve metabolic health, yet the precise influence of carbohydrate restriction on the gut microbiome remains uncertain. Here, we report an ancillary study to the Framingham State Food Study, or FS(2), a controlled, randomized feeding trial involving adults with overweight and obesity. After a calorie-restriction phase to induce weight loss, we randomized participants to diets varying in energy from carbohydrate and fat (low-carb: 20% carb, 60% fat; moderate-carb: 40% carb, 40% fat; high-carb: 60% carb, 20% fat) for weight-loss maintenance for 20 weeks. Weight loss results in significant microbiome shifts, mirroring known associations. We do not detect compositional changes in the microbiome when diets vary carbohydrate-to-fat ratio, while controlling for other potentially confounding dietary factors. Changes in Shuttleworthia abundance correlate positively with maintenance of total energy expenditure following weight loss, suggesting a link between the gut microbiome and energy metabolism.

articles.title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
articles.journal: Blood coagulation & fibrinolysis : an international journal in haemostasis and thrombosis
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 10 9 /l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

articles.title: Clinical stewardship for medical AI translation: A systematic review of technological, human, and organizational barriers.
articles.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems may perform well in controlled evaluations, yet challenges remain in their translation and implementation into routine clinical practice. This systematic review examines 247 original studies identified through searches limited to 2024-2025 publication dates and 31 clinical and translational journal titles. The most frequently coded translation-relevant evidence indicator is retrospective design (158 studies, 64.0%), followed by demographic or geographic data limitations (125, 50.6%), lack of qualifying independent external validation (71, 28.7%), small sample or data scarcity (51, 20.6%), and noisy or context-dependent labels (33, 13.4%). Categories are not mutually exclusive, and the estimates describe the sample defined by these filters, rather than all medical AI research. We integrate these findings with a "clinical stewardship" framework that distributes responsibility across clinical teams, developers, health systems, and patients while preserving the capacity of AI to reduce routine workload.

articles.title: Should We Test for Inherited Thrombophilia in Cancer-associated Thrombosis?
Impact of Inherited Thrombophilia on Cancer-associated Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing genetic determinants in patients with cancer with and without venous thromboembolism (VTE). Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), respectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies including 4,479 patients (1,115 with VTE) were included. Factor V Leiden (FVL) was associated with increased odds of CT (OR 2.48, 95% CI: 1.75-3.51; I 2 = 32%), with consistent findings after exclusion of device- or catheter-related thrombosis. Heterozygous FVL was associated with CT (OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.27-2.73), whereas the homozygous estimate was imprecise (OR 3.42, 95% CI: 0.75-15.59). Prothrombin G20210A was associated with CT (OR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.56-4.58; I 2 = 0%). Exploratory analyses yielded estimates for methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR; OR 1.40, 95% CI: 1.02-1.93) and blood group O (OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.23-0.70); the latter was based on only two studies. Evidence for rarer determinants was sparse. Certainty was moderate for FVL and low or very low for other determinants.

CONCLUSION: FVL and prothrombin G20210A are associated with increased odds of CT. Current evidence does not support universal genetic screening but warrants prospective evaluation of the incremental predictive value of genetic markers beyond established CT risk models.

articles.title: Establishment of urinary hydrogen peroxide as an early indicator for AKI monitoring and its electrochemical detection.
articles.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) features high incidence and mortality rates, delayed diagnosis, and oxidative stress as its core mechanism. Urinary hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) has biomarker potential, but it is only confirmed that its level rises synchronously with serum creatinine (SCr) and blood urea nitrogen (BUN) in the late stage of AKI. The temporal sequence is unclear, and thus, it is unable to prove its diagnostic value in early AKI. In this study, cellular experiments reveal that the onset of cisplatin-induced cellular oxidative stress is far earlier than the node of decline in cell viability. Animal experiments further confirm that, in an AKI mouse model constructed via tail vein injection of cisplatin, H2O2 levels in the kidney and urine significantly increase 3 hours after injection, at which time no substantial necrosis is observed in the kidney. In contrast, traditional indicators SCr and BUN show significant abnormalities only after 24 hours and 48 hours, respectively. This finding clarifies the biological basis of urinary H2O2 as an early detection indicator for AKI. On this basis, a CuO/ZnPc-Cu composite material is prepared. After the performance of the glassy carbon electrode system is verified, the material is modified onto a screen-printed electrode, successfully realizing the precise and rapid quantitative detection of low-concentration H2O2 in real mouse urine. This study provides a new indicator for the rapid and convenient diagnosis of early AKI and also lays a foundation for the future development of detection terminals to achieve low-cost, home-based, non-invasive screening for high-risk AKI patients.

articles.title: Microbiota-dependent citrulline metabolism alleviates sepsis by activating the aryl hydrocarbon receptor/IL-22 pathway to restore intestinal homeostasis.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: This study investigated whether citrulline ameliorates sepsis-associated immune inflammation and intestinal barrier injury by modulating gut microbiota metabolites. Using an in vitro co-culture system and a cecal ligation and puncture mouse model, we found that citrulline fermentation products significantly increased the production of short-chain fatty acids and indole derivatives. These metabolic changes activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathway, upregulated interleukin-22 (IL-22) secretion, STAT3 phosphorylation, and restored the Treg/Th17 cell balance. Consequently, intestinal barrier function was improved, as evidenced by enhanced expression and membrane localization of tight junction proteins, and increased antimicrobial peptide production. Inhibition of AhR or STAT3 weakened the immunoregulatory and barrier-restorative effects of citrulline fermentation products in vitro. In vivo, citrulline treatment improved sepsis severity scores, reduced intestinal neutrophil infiltration, attenuated intestinal mucosal injury, increased goblet cell numbers, and decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines while increasing IL-10 levels in serum. Citrulline also alleviated CLP-induced lung and liver inflammatory injury. These protective effects were diminished by antibiotic treatment or AhR inhibition. RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that citrulline activates AhR and IL-22-responsive barrier gene programs while suppressing NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling. In conclusion, citrulline modulates the gut microbial metabolic environment to activate the AhR/IL-22/STAT3 axis, thereby rectifying immune imbalance, restoring intestinal integrity, and alleviating systemic inflammation in sepsis. These findings provide a novel theoretical foundation for nutritional and immune interventions in sepsis management.

IMPORTANCE: Sepsis, a life-threatening response to infection, often damages the gut, leading to a vicious cycle of inflammation and organ failure. While gut bacteria are known to influence health, how specific nutrients shape their protective effects in sepsis is unclear. This study reveals that the amino acid citrulline acts as a fuel for beneficial gut bacteria. When these bacteria metabolize citrulline, they produce molecules that act as signals to the body's immune system. These signals help calm harmful inflammation, repair the gut lining, and restore immune balance during sepsis. Our findings identify citrulline not just as a nutrient, but as a targeted regulator of the gut-immune axis, offering a promising new dietary strategy to support sepsis treatment by working with the body's microbial allies.

articles.title: [Renal and systemic involvement in Erdheim-Chester disease and targeted therapy with BRAF and MEK inhibitors].
articles.abstract: Systemic BRAF V600E-mutated Erdheim-Chester disease was diagnosed in a 71-year-old patient presenting with bilateral perirenal infiltration ("hairy kidney"), bilateral renal hilar infiltration with right renal atrophy, retroperitoneal fibrosis, and mesenteric infiltration (mesenteric panniculitis). 99mTc bone scintigraphy and PET/CT revealed typical bone involvement. Brain MRI showed central nervous system (CNS) involvement, while echocardiography, cardiac CT, and MRI identified a right atrial pseudotumor with pericardial effusion. Treatment with a BRAF inhibitor (vemurafenib) and a MEK inhibitor (cobimetinib) was initiated.

articles.title: Micromobility Injury Patterns and Resource Use in US Trauma Centers.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Micromobility-related injuries increasingly contribute to trauma care, but differences in injury patterns and resource use across bicycle, e-bike, and e-scooter injuries remain incompletely characterized. We compared injury severity, injury patterns, and resource use among injured riders presenting to participating trauma centers.

STUDY DESIGN: We queried the American College of Surgeons National Trauma Data Bank (2023-2024) for injured bicycle, e-bike, and e-scooter riders ≥18 years. The primary outcome was severe injury (Injury Severity Score ≥16). Secondary outcomes included serious regional injuries (Abbreviated Injury Scale ≥3), craniofacial fractures, operative and critical care resource use, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: Among 47,102 injured riders, 32,100 (68%) rode bicycles, 8,744 (19%) e-bikes, and 6,258 (13%) e-scooters. Compared with bicycle riders, e-scooter riders had lower risk of severe injury (aRR 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-0.99) but higher risk of serious head/neck injury (aRR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.17). Risks of serious chest (aRR 0.77, 95% CI 0.71-0.82) and extremities/pelvic girdle injuries (aRR 0.92, 95% CI 0.86-0.99), emergency surgery (aRR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.87), early transfusion (aRR 0.71, 95% CI 0.54-0.94), and in-hospital mortality (aRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.64-0.94) were lower. Helmet use was associated with lower craniofacial fracture risk, most strongly among e-scooter riders (aRR 0.49, 95% CI 0.41-0.58).

CONCLUSIONS: Among injured riders presenting to participating trauma centers, e-scooter injuries were associated with lower overall severity and resource use than bicycle injuries but greater serious head/neck injury risk. Helmet use was associated with lower craniofacial fracture risk, supporting continued helmet promotion.

articles.title: [When machines estimate kidney function and predict risk: Clinical applications of machine learning].
articles.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence, and particularly machine learning, is rapidly expanding in medicine. In nephrology, these approaches have generated growing interest owing to the availability of large clinical, biological, and administrative datasets, as well as the need for more accurate assessment of kidney function and changes over time. Two major areas of application have emerged: estimation of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and prediction of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. Initial studies focused on improving GFR estimation through supervised learning algorithms such as artificial neural networks, random forests, and ensemble methods. Although several studies reported encouraging results, recent large multicenter studies suggest that machine learning provides only marginal improvements over modern equations such as EKFC or CKD-EPI when the same clinical and biological variables are used. These findings indicate that current limitations in GFR estimation are more likely attributable to the information provided by available biomarkers than to the predictive capacity of the algorithms themselves. In contrast, machine learning appears particularly well suited for predicting kidney disease progression. By integrating numerous clinical and laboratory variables, these models can identify patients at high risk of rapid kidney function decline or kidney failure. Nevertheless, only a limited number of models have demonstrated a clear clinical advantage over established prediction tools such as the Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE). This review summarizes current applications of machine learning for GFR estimation and CKD progression prediction, discusses their strengths and limitations, and highlights future directions for their integration into nephrology practice.

articles.title: [Cold ischemia time in kidney transplantation: From reduction to personalization].
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cold ischemia time is a modifiable determinant of kidney transplant outcomes. Minimizing its duration remains a major goal, although allocation, transportation, and organizational constraints make some of this time unavoidable.

METHODS: We reviewed the literature published in PubMed over the past five years, supplemented by relevant landmark studies and institutional recommendations.

RESULTS: Prolonged cold ischemia is primarily associated with delayed graft function and, to a lesser extent, impaired long-term graft survival. Its impact varies according to donor and recipient characteristics. Prediction models can now estimate graft failure risk across different cold ischemia times for a given donor-recipient pair. Recent data on hypothermic machine perfusion further suggest that preservation strategies may mitigate the consequences of prolonged cold ischemia.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Personalizing cold ischemia could help identify situations in which its reduction should be prioritized and provide additional information for organ allocation and clinical decision-making. However, the moderate performance of currently available models and the lack of prospective validation preclude their use as standalone decision-making tools. Cold ischemia should therefore remain as short as possible, while its expected consequences could increasingly be assessed based on the characteristics of the donor-recipient pair and the graft preservation strategy used.

articles.title: Steatotic Liver Disease Is Becoming a Higher Priority Worldwide.
Global Heart Failure Burden Increased Between 1990 and 2023.
ACC Releases Guidance for Managing Resistant Hypertension.
Pooled intravenous immunoglobulins exhibit broad binding and Fc-mediated activity against diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants.
articles.abstract: During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), antibody-based therapies such as COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) and monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) emerged rapidly. However, many CCP clinical trials failed to show consistent benefits, and mAbs lost effectiveness as new SARS-CoV-2 variants emerged. These studies consistently indicated that antibody therapies are effective when given very early in disease and in patients with delayed or suppressed immune responses. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), which is pooled IgGs from thousands of donors, has been explored as an additional source of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies to treat acutely ill patients because IVIG was shown to prevent disease and death in animal models against variants even without neutralizing activity. As antibodies can also protect via Fc-mediated activation of innate immune effector functions, in this study, we compared the qualitative and quantitative properties of CCP and IVIG to determine if IVIG might serve as a clinical therapeutic alternative to CCP. We measured SARS-CoV-2 spike (S)- and nucleocapsid (N)- specific antibody-binding titers across variants and evaluated their ability to induce antibody-dependent effector functions. We found that IVIG and CCP had comparable binding and Fc-effector activity against ancestral SARS-CoV-2. Remarkably, IVIG manufactured before the emergence of XBB.1.5, JN.1, KP.2, XEC, and XFG demonstrated strong binding and Fc-effector activity against these newer variants.IMPORTANCEDespite the availabilities of vaccines for SARS-CoV-2 for most individuals, there remain vulnerable populations for which vaccination is ineffective. As the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants has rendered many monoclonal antibody therapies ineffective, there remains a need to understand the role of polyclonal antibody therapies for SARS-CoV-2, such as COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). While CCP is variable and donor-dependent, IVIG is pooled from thousands of donors with a range of vaccine- and natural infection-derived antibody responses and may represent a consistent source of polyclonal antibodies. We compared high neutralizing antibody titer CCP, previously shown to be associated with reduced time to hospital discharge, with IVIG produced post-2021. We find that IVIG offers expanded antibody binding to SARS-CoV-2 variants, including those that emerged after the IVIG was collected, and enhanced induction of Fc-mediated innate immune effector functions, highlighting the potential utility of IVIG as an adjunct treatment of SARS-CoV-2.CLINICAL TRIALSThis study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT04524507.

articles.title: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Children and Adolescents.
Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood.

OBSERVATIONS: Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

articles.title: METTL3 destabilizes RFX7 to ameliorate PDGF-BB-induced airway smooth muscle cell dysfunction and inflammation in an in vitro model of childhood asthma.
articles.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood asthma represents a significant global health burden, characterized by chronic airway inflammation and remodeling. Regulatory factor X7 (RFX7) has emerged as a potential key player in asthma pathogenesis. However, its specific role in modulating airway smooth muscle cell (ASMC) dysfunction-a hallmark of asthma pathology-remains poorly understood.

METHODS: An in vitro asthma model was established by stimulating airway smooth muscle cells (ASMCs) with platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB). Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blotting were employed to measure the mRNA and protein expression levels of RFX7 and METTL3, respectively. Functional assays, including 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine incorporation, Transwell, and wound-healing assays, were utilized to evaluate ASMC proliferation, invasion, and migration. Inflammatory responses were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) targeting interleukin-6 (IL-6).

RESULTS: RFX7 expression levels were significantly elevated in the serum of pediatric asthma patients and in PDGF-BB-induced ASMCs, whereas METTL3 expression was downregulated. PDGF-BB stimulation enhanced ASMC proliferation, invasion, and migration, all of which were markedly attenuated by RFX7 knockdown. Furthermore, RFX7 deficiency reduced PDGF-BB-induced production of IL-6, TNF-α, ROS, and MDA, as well as the proportion of CD86-positive macrophages. Notably, METTL3 exhibited a negative correlation with RFX7 in patient sera and destabilized RFX7 transcripts in a YTHDF2-dependent manner. Consequently, overexpression of METTL3 alleviated PDGF-BB-induced ASMC dysfunction by downregulating RFX7.

CONCLUSION: METTL3-mediated destabilization of RFX7 ameliorated PDGF-BB-induced ASMC proliferation, migration, and invasion, while simultaneously suppressing inflammation, oxidative stress, and macrophage polarization. Targeting this METTL3-RFX7 axis may offer a novel therapeutic strategy to mitigate airway remodeling and inflammation in childhood asthma.

articles.title: Combined pharmacologic and lifestyle intervention for breast cancer prevention: Results of the randomized phase II TOLERANT trial in high-risk women.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer (BC) prevention strategies include lifestyle modification and preventive agents such as selective estrogen receptor modulators and aromatase inhibitors. Sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) is a breast cancer risk-associated biomarker; however, it is not a validated surrogate endpoint for breast cancer risk reduction.

METHODS: Population: women with hereditary BC risk, a ≥ 5% 10-year BC risk, or a history of intraepithelial neoplasia were enrolled.

TRIAL DESIGN: a four-arm randomized phase II biomarker trial: Tamoxifen 10 mg every other day (LDT); LDT + Intermittent Caloric Restriction (ICR); Lifestyle intervention with a step counter (LI); LI + ICR.

PRIMARY ENDPOINT: Post intervention levels of circulating SHBG. Secondary endpoints: modulation of IGF system, adipokines, inflammatory markers, quality of life. Main analysis was LDT+ ICR vs LI+ICR.

RESULTS: One hundred and ten participants were randomized to: LDT, LDT plus ICR, LI, or LI plus ICR, for 6 months. Mean age was 52 years and mean BMI was 25 kg/m²; 62% were unaffected carriers, and 65% were postmenopausal. LDT±ICR significantly increased SHBG and IGFBP-3 and decreased IGF-I (absolute change p < 0.0001, p = 0.004, and p < 0.001, respectively). ICR arms showed higher adiponectin than non-ICR arms (p = 0.003). Furthermore, in adherent subjects (>90%), LI plus ICR was significantly associated with higher SHBG compared with LI alone (p = 0.045). No differences in adverse events between arms; LDT demonstrated a mild, although significant, worsening in quality of life.

CONCLUSIONS: LDT favorably modulates BC risk-associated biomarkers, and ICR adds a complementary metabolic effect, supporting further investigation of these combined strategies.

articles.title: Analysis of quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity (Q-TWiST) in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer from the ARASENS trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To identify patients likely to benefit from intensified darolutamide treatment while minimizing adverse events (AEs), this analysis applied quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity (Q-TWiST) to evaluate quality-adjusted survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in ARASENS, comparing triplet therapy (darolutamide + androgen deprivation therapy [ADT] + docetaxel) with placebo doublet therapy (ADT + docetaxel).

METHODS: Time with toxicity (TOX; with grade 3/4 symptoms/toxic effects), time without symptoms or toxicity (TWiST), and time in relapse/disease progression (REL) were estimated using 53-month restricted means based on grade 3/4 AEs, time to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, and overall survival ARASENS data. Q-TWiST was calculated as the utility-weighted sum of time spent in each health state per treatment arm.

RESULTS: Patients gained an additional 6.3 months of Q-TWiST with darolutamide versus placebo (p < 0.001) driven by increased TWiST (mean 17.6 months vs 10.9 months), and decreased REL (2.4 months vs 8.7 months). Longer treatment resulted in more TOX (17.2 months vs 11.3 months) at 53 months. Partitioned Kaplan-Meier survival curves showed sustained TWiST with darolutamide versus placebo over 53 months. Relative Q-TWiST gain was 16.0% (clearly clinically important).

CONCLUSION: Darolutamide triplet therapy offers longer survival benefits without symptoms or toxicity versus placebo, aiding evaluation of efficacy-tolerability balance and supporting patient-centered decision-making.

articles.title: Lazertinib plus pemetrexed and carboplatin in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced non-small cell lung cancer after progression on lazertinib.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Therapeutic strategies after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) remain suboptimal in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We investigated whether continuing EGFR inhibition with lazertinib combined with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy could extend clinical benefit after progression on prior lazertinib.

METHODS: In the multicenter, single-arm, phase II LUCAS study (NCT05786430), patients with advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC who had progressed on lazertinib received lazertinib 240 mg daily plus pemetrexed-carboplatin for four cycles, followed by maintenance lazertinib and pemetrexed. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS); secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate (ORR), intracranial PFS, safety, and exploratory ctDNA analyses.

RESULTS: Of 86 patients, 46.5% had a history of brain metastases. Among 81 response-evaluable patients, median PFS was 9.5 months (95% CI: 6.3-9.6; one-sided p = 0.017 against a null median of 6.0 months). In the safety population, median OS was 15.9 months (95% CI: 12.4-20.0) and ORR was 36.0% (95% CI: 26.0-47.1). Outcomes were similar irrespective of prior lazertinib line or EGFR subtype. Baseline ctDNA-detected EGFR amplification was associated with inferior survival. Among 36 patients with radiologically evident baseline brain metastases, median intracranial PFS was 9.9 months (95% CI: 7.8-16.4) with infrequent isolated intracranial progression. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events occurred in 69.8%, predominantly hematologic, without new safety signals.

CONCLUSIONS: Continuation of lazertinib with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy after progression on prior lazertinib was associated with meaningful systemic and intracranial activity and manageable toxicity. Randomized evaluation is required to establish the incremental benefit of lazertinib continuation.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of high-current tTIS targeting left sgACC for major depressive disorder: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading cause of disability, and non-invasive stimulation of deep brain circuits such as the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) remains challenging. This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial recruits 96 adults with moderate-to-severe MDD who received 10 sessions of 2 mA low-current, 15 mA high-current, or sham transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) targeting the left sgACC. The high-current group shows significantly greater reductions in depressive symptoms (17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale [HDRS-17] score) post-treatment and at 1-month follow-up compared with sham and outperforms the low-current group post-treatment. Exploratory Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) analyses suggest improved sleep quality in both active groups, whereas anxiety outcomes show no intergroup differences. High-current tTIS is safe and well tolerated, with only transient tingling. These findings provide preliminary evidence that sgACC-targeted tTIS relieves depressive symptoms safely, with more robust short-to medium-term effects observed under the 15 mA protocol. This trial registers on Chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR2400094971).

articles.title: FNR/ArcA-2,3-butanediol regulatory axis enhances glucose uptake and adhE expression in high alcohol-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Previously, we found that Klebsiella pneumoniae is a high-alcohol producer, which contributes to the development of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its high-alcohol production remain unclear. By comparing biological phenotypes of K. pneumoniae with those of Escherichia coli, we found that the former is better at metabolizing high concentrations of glucose, exhibits faster growth rates, and produces higher levels of alcohol, with the 2,3-butanediol (2,3-BD) pathway being the key determinant underlying these differences. More importantly, species possessing the 2,3-BD pathway, including Klebsiella aerogenes, Klebsiella oxytoca, Enterobacter cloacae, and Enterobacter hormaechei, have all demonstrated high-alcohol production capabilities similar to that of K. pneumoniae, suggesting a conserved mechanism for alcohol production among 2,3-BD-positive Enterobacteriaceae. Deletion of the 2,3-BD pathway reduced the expression of the phosphotransferase system (PTS) and the alcohol dehydrogenase gene adhE, which normally confer enhanced glucose metabolism and alcohol production. Pathway deletion also downregulated multiple virulence determinants, including capsular polysaccharides (CPS), lipopolysaccharides (LPS), and type 1 and 3 fimbriae, thereby attenuating virulence in a murine pneumonia model. In addition, the regulator FNR enhanced alcohol production by upregulating adhE and 2,3-BD pathway genes, whereas ArcA activated the 2,3-BD pathway in an ArcB-independent manner, revealing a non-canonical signaling mechanism that couples metabolic adaptation with virulence. Collectively, our findings identify the "FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD pathway axis" as a key molecular mechanism driving high alcohol production in K. pneumoniae, highlighting the 2,3-BD pathway as a key link between bacterial metabolism and virulence and a potential therapeutic target for controlling K. pneumoniae infections.IMPORTANCEKlebsiella pneumoniae has emerged as a novel cause of NAFLD due to its high alcohol-producing capacity. However, the molecular basis of this phenotype remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that the FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD pathway axis drives high levels of alcohol production by enhancing glucose-PTS system and adhE expression, and that this pathway is conserved among Enterobacteriaceae with strong alcohol-producing abilities. Moreover, loss of the 2,3-BD pathway reduces the expression of multiple virulence factors and attenuates pathogenicity in a murine pneumonia model. These findings identify the FNR/ArcA-2,3-BD axis as a potential target for mitigating excessive alcohol production and virulence in bacteria.

articles.title: Learning From NATURE: A Second Chance for Thrombectomy in STEMI.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

articles.title: [Urinary biomarkers: A promising tool for modern nephrology].
articles.abstract: To avoid the need for renal biopsy, which remains an invasive procedure, numerous urinary biomarkers have been investigated for the detection, risk stratification, and prediction of disease progression in patients with acute or chronic kidney disease. Often referred to as a form of "liquid biopsy," some of these molecular candidates, particularly proteins and peptides, have shown considerable robustness and clinical potential. This review outlines the concept of a biomarker and the key stages involved in its development, drawing on practical examples such as prognostic signatures for antenatal renal developmental abnormalities and the prediction of acute kidney injury, as well as diagnostic applications in common clinical settings, including glomerular diseases using urinary soluble CD163 and acute interstitial nephritis using CXCL9. Methods used for biomarker measurement are also discussed. Despite encouraging results, even the most advanced biomarkers have struggled to progress beyond external multicenter validation because of methodological challenges related to both the underlying technologies and the heterogeneity of patient cohorts. As of 2026, these biomarkers remain primarily research tools, and a broad consensus on their routine clinical use has yet to emerge.

articles.title: Frozen section analysis assisted MRI targeted prostate biopsy - results of the randomized clinical FAST trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) targeted prostate biopsy is still commonly combined with systematic biopsy, resulting in a high number of extracted biopsy cores. This study evaluated whether a frozen section analysis (FSA) guided biopsy strategy enabling immediate assessment of targeted biopsy and omitting systematic biopsy in case of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is non-inferior to standard combined biopsy while substantially reducing the number of biopsy cores.

MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this prospective randomized trial, men with PI-RADS ≥ 4 lesions were randomized to standard combined biopsy (Arm A) or FSA guided primarily MRI-targeted biopsy (Arm B). In Arm B, three targeted cores were obtained, with two immediately analyzed by FSA. Additional systematic biopsy was performed only if FSA was negative or inconclusive. The primary endpoint was detection of csPCa (ISUP grade group ≥2). A non-inferiority margin of -10 %age points was prespecified.

RESULTS: A total of 160 patients were randomized (Arm A: 80, Arm B: 80). csPCa detection rates were 93% in Arm A and 97% in Arm B, yielding a risk difference of 5.0% (95% CI -5.2-14.7), meeting non-inferiority criteria. The median number of biopsy cores was reduced from 15 to 3 in Arm B (p < 0.001). Pain, discomfort, macrohematuria, and hematospermia were significantly lower in the experimental arm (all p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: FSA guided prostate biopsy enabling immediate assessment of targeted biopsy cores is safe, minimally invasive, and non-inferior regarding the detection of csPCa to standard biopsy in men with suspicious mpMRI lesions. This approach substantially reduces biopsy cores and patient burden by omitting systematic biopsy in case of positive FSA while maintaining oncological safety.

articles.title: Exploration of tumor genomics associated with prolonged benefit from or resistance to talazoparib monotherapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition is synthetically lethal in cells with deleterious alterations in DNA damage response genes involved in homologous recombination repair (HRR).
