Logistic regression was used to investigate associations between maternal asthma (treated, untreated, and medication exposure) and pregnancy outcomes: stillbirth, iatrogenic and spontaneous preterm delivery, small/very small for gestational age (SGA/VSGA), and low Apgar score.

RESULTS: Of the 324,238 infants, 39,040 (12.0%) had mothers with asthma: 20,840 (6.4%) had treated asthma, 8,230 (2.5%) had untreated asthma, and 9,970 (3.1%) were prescribed asthma medications without recorded asthma diagnoses. Compared to offspring of mothers with no maternal asthma (reference group), those whose mothers had treated asthma had higher odds of SGA (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.07-1.19), VSGA (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26), Apgar score < 7 (aOR 1.14, 95% CI 1.01-1.29), and iatrogenic preterm delivery (aOR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26). Associations were observed across multiple classes of asthma medication with stronger associations among the offspring of mothers prescribed more than one medication class and those with add-on therapies including long-acting muscarinic antagonists, short-acting muscarinic antagonists, leukotrienes antagonist and theophylline, consistent with more severe, or poorly controlled, asthma rather than medication effects. Untreated asthma was associated with higher risk of iatrogenic preterm delivery, and treated asthma was associated with lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery (aOR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.89). No associations were observed with stillbirth.

CONCLUSIONS: The non-specific associations observed across different classes of asthma medication and dose-relationships with polytherapy suggested confounding by indication and severity. The findings for iatrogenic preterm delivery further supported an effect of the underlying disease rather than its treatment. These findings, together with the lower risk of spontaneous preterm delivery among treated mothers, support guideline recommendations to continue asthma treatment during pregnancy.

articles.title: Medically Important Microbial Proteases and their Applications.
articles.abstract: Microbial proteases are hydrolytic enzymes with immense potential in medicine and biotechnology. Originating from various bacterial and fungal sources, these enzymes exhibit a remarkable diversity in their specificity, pH tolerance, and modes of action. The review highlights several proteases that have transitioned from being mere subjects of academic interest to becoming pivotal components of medical treatment strategies. The therapeutic applications of these proteases span a wide spectrum of medical conditions. Nattokinase and serrapeptase, with their fibrinolytic properties, offer hope in managing cardiovascular diseases by dissolving blood clots and reducing the risk of thrombosis. Collagenase from Clostridium histolyticum has proven invaluable in treating conditions in which excess collagen deposition is problematic. In the field of autoimmune diseases, enzymes such as IgA protease and IdeS (Immunoglobulin G-degrading enzyme of Streptococcus pyogenes) show promise. The review also sheds light on enzymes with antimicrobial, antimetastatic, and anti-inflammatory properties, including lysostaphin, arazyme, and others. Future advances in enzymology and the development of protein engineering techniques will make it possible to increase the stability and specificity of proteases and reduce their immunogenicity, which in turn will facilitate the translation of more microbial enzymes into clinical practice.

articles.title: Development of a specialised reproductive rheumatology consultation service: analysis of referral patterns across preconception, pregnancy, and lactation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women with inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease (iRMD) face unique challenges during preconception, pregnancy, and lactation. In 2024, a specialised consultation service was developed and implemented at the tertiary rheumatology centre of the Rheumazentrum Ruhrgebiet, Ruhr University Bochum, Herne, Germany, to address these specific needs.

METHODS: Demographic characteristics, disease- and treatment-related data, reproductive status, referring physician, reasons for consultation, and recommendations for disease management were collected between 1 January 2024 and 3 April 2025.

RESULTS: Overall, 57 patients were included; the mean age was 33.3 ± 4.4 years and the mean disease duration was 6.3 ± 4.8 years. Almost all patients (94.7%) had a confirmed diagnosis of an iRMD. 57.9% were planning a pregnancy, 40.4% were pregnant, and 1.8% were breastfeeding. At baseline, 21.8% were receiving csDMARDs and 50.9% were receiving bDMARDs. Glucocorticoid use was documented in 16.1%. Patients were referred by rheumatologists (35.7%), the in-house outpatient clinic (37.5%), general practitioners (14.3%), gynaecologists (10.7%), and the in-house inpatient clinic (1.8%). The most frequent reasons for consultation were patient concerns regarding pregnancy and medication safety. Consultation reasons differed descriptively between patients in the preconception period and pregnant patients; however, these exploratory differences should be interpreted with caution. Recommendations made during consultation included modification of DMARD therapy (35.1%), initiation of fetal bradycardia screening (19.3%), and preeclampsia prophylaxis (8.8%).

CONCLUSION: A dedicated reproductive rheumatology consultation service provides structured support for women with iRMDs throughout preconception, pregnancy, and lactation. Medication adjustments and targeted preventive measures were recommended for more than one-third of patients, highlighting the potential value of preconception referral and specialized reproductive rheumatology consultation.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: All-Trans Retinoic Acid (ATRA) Attenuates Alcoholic Steatohepatitis (ASH) via reprogramming hepatic lipid metabolism in male mice.
articles.abstract: Alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation, oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum stress, inflammation, and impaired autophagy, yet pharmacological options remain limited. All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), the transcriptionally active metabolite of vitamin A, regulates retinoid receptor-dependent metabolic and stress-response pathways. We investigated whether ATRA protects against ethanol-induced liver injury in male C57BL/6 N mice fed a control Lieber-DeCarli diet, an ethanol-containing Lieber-DeCarli diet, or the ethanol diet plus ATRA (15 mg/kg, oral gavage, three times weekly). ATRA reduced hepatic triglyceride accumulation, serum alanine aminotransferase activity, and histological steatosis. These protective effects were associated with downregulation of the lipogenic and ethanol-metabolizing genes together with increased Rxra expression. ATRA also increased LC3B-II abundance and reduced p62 accumulation, consistent with improved autophagy, and attenuated markers of endoplasmic reticulum stress, oxidative stress, and inflammatory signaling. Metabolomics analysis showed that ATRA produced a distinct metabolic profile, with higher choline, dimethylamine, sarcosine, and taurine and enrichment of methionine, betaine, phosphatidylcholine, cysteine, and taurine/hypotaurine pathways. These findings indicate that ATRA mitigates ethanol-induced hepatic injury by coordinating retinoid signaling with lipid metabolism, cellular quality control, stress responses, and one-carbon/redox metabolic remodeling supporting hepatic vitamin A signaling as a pharmacologically relevant modifier of alcohol-associated liver injury.

articles.title: Number of Surgical Levels, Rather Than Frailty or JOA Score, Is Associated With Spine-Specific Complications After Adjustment for Surgical Region.
articles.abstract:
STUDY DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study.

OBJECTIVE: To identify independent predictors of SAVES-V2-graded complications after elective spine surgery, and whether frailty (mFI-5) and JOA score remain associated after adjusting for surgical region.

METHODS: A total of 691 adult patients undergoing elective spine surgery (cervical, thoracic, lumbar, or deformity; 2014-2024) were analyzed. The primary outcome was SAVES-V2 ≥3 complications (90 patients, 13.0%). Three multivariable models addressed hypertension/mFI-5 overlap (r=0.753): Model A (n687), Model B (hypertension excluded; n=687), and Model C (Model B plus region; n=635), designated primary as region improved fit (P=0.036). Surgical levels' functional form was assessed with a spline and clinically grouped categories.

RESULTS: Transient neurological deficit (n=41; C5 palsy, n=29) and surgical site infection requiring reoperation (n=19) were most frequent. A linear per-level specification was not well supported (P<0.001); risk rose through 4-6 levels and plateaued thereafter (OR 13.89 for 4-6 vs. 1 level; P<0.001). Surgical levels were independently associated with complications in Model C (OR 1.281/level) and Model B (OR 1.258/level; both P<0.001). After region adjustment, JOA score, age, male sex, and BMI were no longer significant (all P>0.1); lumbar carried lower risk than cervical (OR 0.408; P=0.014). The mFI-5 remained paradoxically protective (OR 0.720; P=0.034). Discrimination was poor for both mFI-5 (C=0.487) and JOA score (C=0.582; DeLong P=0.007), a secondary finding; Model C showed the best discrimination overall (C=0.731).

CONCLUSIONS: Number of surgical levels, not frailty or JOA score, remained the most robust predictor after region adjustment, though non-linear and not a comprehensive complexity measure. Both frailty and JOA showed limited discrimination, insufficient alone for perioperative risk stratification.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III (Surgery; Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine, 2009).

articles.title: Association of Betel Quid Chewing with Anthropometric Parameters and Lipid Profile in Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Betel quid chewing is a rising concern, linked to various diseases. Several studies show an increased risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among chewers. With the increasing prevalence of diabetes and metabolic disorders, the association between betel nut use and cardiovascular diseases worsens morbidity and mortality, establishing a significant socioeconomic burden. Inflammation, insulin resistance, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) metabolism may underlie the association between betel nut use and atherosclerotic adverse outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of betel quid chewing on anthropometric parameters and lipid profiles in T2DM patients.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: T2DM patients were screened and recruited from an endocrinology outpatient department. Patients were divided into two groups: one group with a history of betel quid chewing and another group without it. Patients with a history of ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, hypertension, chronic inflammatory diseases, or other forms of tobacco use were excluded. Comparison of anthropometric parameters and lipid profiles was performed among the two groups.

RESULTS: Significant differences were observed in hip circumference (P = 0.002), waist-to-hip ratio (P = 0.0001), and high-density lipoprotein (P = 0.0002) between the two groups of patients.

CONCLUSION: Inflammation, insulin resistance, and LDL-C metabolism may contribute to the link between betel nut usage and T2DM. Quitting the habit of chewing may have the potential to reduce the atherosclerotic vascular adversities.

articles.title: Chicken Bone-induced Esophageal Perforation in a Child Presenting with Extensive Cervico-Thoracic Prevertebral Abscess and Sepsis: A Rare Case Report.
articles.abstract: Esophageal perforation following foreign body ingestion is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening condition in children, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. Sharp foreign bodies such as chicken bones may result in deep tissue injury, abscess formation, mediastinitis, and sepsis. We report the case of an 8-year-old boy who presented with throat pain, cough, vomiting, and epigastric pain following accidental ingestion of a chicken bone. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed an extensive cervico-thoracic prevertebral abscess extending from C2 to T6 with multiple air pockets and a retained foreign body at the T5-T6 level, suggestive of esophageal perforation. The patient underwent emergency right posterolateral thoracotomy with drainage of the abscess and removal of the impacted chicken bone. Intraoperative flexible esophagoscopy demonstrated a 1 cm perforation at the cricopharyngeal level. Definitive repair of the posterior esophageal rent was subsequently performed through a left cervical approach with reinforcement using a sternohyoid muscle flap. The postoperative course was complicated by anastomotic leak, high-output esophageal fistula, right vocal cord dysfunction, and Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis. Conservative management with feeding gastrostomy and nutritional support resulted in gradual recovery, and follow-up contrast studies showed complete healing without residual leak or stricture formation. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion in children with persistent symptoms following foreign body ingestion. Early imaging, prompt diagnosis, and multidisciplinary individualized management are essential to prevent severe complications and improve outcomes in pediatric esophageal perforation.

articles.title: Neutrophil-Lymphocyte Ratio and Platelet-Lymphocyte Ratio as Markers of Diabetic Nephropathy: A Hospital-Based Prospective Study in South Indian Population with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In relation to diabetic nephropathy, a leading cause of chronic kidney disease worldwide, chronic inflammation is a major contributor to its development. Unfortunately, conventional kidney markers do not pick up on the very early stages of inflammation, and this is where Neutrophil-Lymphocyte Ratio, or NLR and Platelet-Lymphocyte Ratio, or PLR, step in. Coming from regular blood tests, these two markers have been found to be simple and affordable ways to monitor the degree of inflammation.

AIM: To find out how NLR and PLR are related to the progression of diabetic nephropathy in people with type 2 diabetes mellitus in South India.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Looking at 90 patients with type 2 diabetes, this study sorted them into three groups based on their Urine Albumin-Creatinine Ratio, or UACR. They found that the 30 patients in the normoalbuminuria group, the 30 in the microalbuminuria group and the 30 in the macroalbuminuria group all had different clinical profiles. Glycemic status, renal function, and complete blood counts were also examined. NLR and PLR were calculated, and looked at in relation to renal function. The statistical analysis consisted of Analysis of Variance, Pearson correlation, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: When looking at the progression of albuminuria, both the NLR and PLR saw significant increases, but with NLR having a much stronger correlation to the UACR (r = 0.782, P < 0.001) and serum creatinine levels (r = 0.721, P < 0.001). It also had a negative correlation with estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate, r = -0.789, P < 0.001. The diagnostic accuracy of NLR was found to be better, as indicated by a higher Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.86, compared to PLR with an AUC of 0.74. On multivariate analysis, NLR was found to be an independent predictor of diabetic nephropathy, odds ratio =3.45, 95% confidence interval: 2.12-5.67, but PLR did not show any independent association.

CONCLUSION: Concerning diabetic nephropathy, NLR, has proven to be a more effective marker for the disease than PLR. Coming in at a relatively low cost and requiring no special equipment, NLR's superior correlation with diabetic nephropathy severity could make it a valuable screening tool for the early detection of kidney disease in type 2 diabetes patients. Integrating NLR into regular clinical care would allow doctors to identify which patients are more at risk of renal complications, and potentially put them on a more rigorous treatment and monitoring plan.

articles.title: Epidemiology, Clinical Characteristics, and Temporal Patterns of Thrombosis Following Vaccination: A 35-Year Analysis of the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, 1990-2025.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thrombosis is an uncommon but clinically important adverse event following vaccination because of its potential for serious morbidity and mortality. Although concerns increased during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination era, comprehensive analyses of thrombosis reports in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) remain limited.

AIM: To analyze thrombosis reports submitted to VAERS between 1990 and 2025 and evaluate demographic characteristics, vaccine associations, onset intervals, clinical outcomes, and differences between serious and nonserious reports.

METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted using publicly available VAERS data extracted in May 2026. Reports containing the adverse event term "thrombosis" from 1990 to 2025 were analyzed. Variables included age, sex, vaccine type, onset interval, clinical outcomes, and seriousness classification. Descriptive statistics and Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used.

RESULTS: A total of 5565 thrombosis reports were identified, including 2398 (43.1%) serious reports. Females accounted for 59.3% of reports, whereas males were overrepresented in serious cases. Serious outcomes were more common among adults aged ≥65 years. COVID-19 vaccines accounted for the largest proportion of reports. Most documented cases occurred within 1-3 days of vaccination. Hospitalization (33.1%), life-threatening events (17.8%), and death (6.2%) were the most frequent outcomes. Significant differences were observed for age, sex, vaccine type, and onset interval (all P ≤ 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Thrombosis reports showed distinct demographic and clinical patterns, supporting continued postmarketing pharmacovigilance while acknowledging the limitations of passive surveillance in establishing causality.

articles.title: Clinico-epidemiological Insights of Patients with Varicose Veins from Tertiary Care Teaching Hospitals - A Cross-sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Varicose veins are a prevalent venous disorder causing functional limitations and cosmetic concerns. Despite its global burden, limited epidemiological data exist for the Indian population. There is a notable gap in the demographics regarding the prevalence of varicose veins among Indian populations.

OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study is to assess the clinico-epidemiological profile, diagnostic modalities, treatment patterns, and outcomes among patients with varicose veins admitted to tertiary care hospitals.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, cross-sectional study was conducted in July 2024 using hospital records from 2019 to 2024 of tertiary care teaching hospitals affiliated to a medical college from Coastal South India. Data were extracted on demographics, clinical features, diagnostics, treatment, and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 42 patients included, 64.3% were male and most were aged 31-50 years. Hypertension (75%), diabetes (60%), and obesity (50%) were common comorbidities. Clinical features included lower limb swelling (53.7%), engorged veins (51.2%), and leg pain (48.8%). Doppler ultrasound was the primary diagnostic tool (97.1%). All patients received pharmacological treatment; 40.5% underwent nonpharmacological therapy, and 38.1% received surgical intervention. Posttreatment complications occurred in 26.8% of patients.

CONCLUSION: Varicose veins predominantly affected middle-aged males in this study, with hypertension and diabetes as common comorbidities. Doppler ultrasound remains the diagnostic standard. While conservative and surgical treatments were employed, the high rate of complications underscores the need for early diagnosis, preventive strategies, and increased awareness among high-risk occupational groups.

articles.title: Cognitive Dysfunction in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Cross-sectional Study of Prevalence, Domain Patterns, and Functional Correlates.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive dysfunction is increasingly recognized as a significant nontraditional complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), with important implications for daily functioning and quality of life. However, domain-specific cognitive patterns and their relationship to functional independence remain underexplored in non-Western populations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of 72 adults with CKD stage ≥3, including maintenance hemodialysis patients, at a tertiary referral center in southern India. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), while activities of daily living (ADLs) were measured using the Barthel Index. The pattern of cognitive dysfunction as well as its risk factors were studied.

RESULTS: The mean MoCA and Barthel Index scores were 22.1 ± 4.5 and 81.4 ± 12.2, respectively. Cognitive impairment (MoCA <26) was present in 69.4% of participants. Both MoCA and Barthel Index scores declined significantly with advancing CKD stage (P < 0.001), with dialysis patients showing the lowest scores. Subgroup analysis of dialysis patients revealed that memory (median 40% of domain maximum) and abstraction (50%) were the most affected domains. MoCA and Barthel scores were strongly correlated (ρ = 0.71, P < 0.001). On multivariate regression, older age and dialysis vintage independently predicted lower MoCA scores, while dialysis vintage predicted poorer Barthel Index performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Cognitive dysfunction is highly prevalent in CKD and most pronounced in dialysis patients, with selective vulnerability of memory and abstraction. Cognitive dysfunction is associated with impaired ADLs.

articles.title: Prospective Cohort Study Comparing Spirometry, Asthma Control Test, and Fractional Exhaled Nitric Oxide in Predicting Asthma Exacerbations in a Tertiary Care Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a chronic airway disease that causes patients to experience breathing difficulties together with restricted airflow. The disease causes patients to experience acute exacerbations which lead to increased healthcare costs and higher levels of illness. The current methods of predicting asthma exacerbations through symptom assessment and lung function tests face substantial difficulties.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the ability of fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) in predicting future exacerbations of Asthma. To assess and compare the ability of FeNO, spirometry, and the Asthma Control Test (ACT) in predicting future exacerbations of asthma and their correlation with each other.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted among 86 individuals with bronchial asthma at a tertiary care center. Assessment at baseline included ACT scoring, spirometry, and FeNO levels. The patients were then followed up for the development of asthma exacerbations. The statistical analyses involved the Chi-square test and Mann-Whitney U test. P < 0.05 was used to determine statistical significance.

RESULTS: There were 26 (30.2%) cases of asthma exacerbation among the study population. Those with asthma exacerbations exhibited significantly lower ACT scores and lower Forced Expiratory Volume in one second (% predicted) values than those without exacerbations (P < 0.001; P < 0.01, respectively). An increased level of FeNO was strongly correlated with an increased risk of future asthma exacerbations, and those with FeNO > 50 ppb were at the highest risk (P < 0.001). In comparison with the other two assessment techniques, FeNO proved to have higher predictive value than the ACT score and spirometry parameters.

CONCLUSION: FeNO is a strong and independent predictor of future asthma exacerbations. The combination of symptom-based assessment and spirometry fails to provide reliable prediction of exacerbation risk. The combined assessment method, which includes ACT and spirometry and FeNO measurement, establishes an asthma risk assessment and management method that offers complete and precise results.

articles.title: Cognitive Trajectories After Traumatic Brain Injury: A NIDILRR TBI Model Systems National Database Study.
authors: TBI Model Systems Cognitive Trajectory Module Investigators
articles.journal: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify subgroups of individuals with traumatic brain injury (TBI) who follow distinct trajectories of cognitive performance from years 2-5 and 5-10 postinjury, and to identify demographic, injury, and health-related predictors of cognitive trajectories.

SETTING: Ten TBI Model Systems Centers.

PARTICIPANTS: Eight hundred ninety seven individuals who underwent inpatient rehabilitation for TBI enrolled in a longitudinal TBI Model Systems substudy. Two separate cohorts were studied: those followed at years 2, 3, 4, and 5 postinjury (Year 2 cohort; n = 494), and those followed at years 5, 6, 7, and 10 postinjury (Year 5 cohort; n = 403). Participants contributing ≥2 assessments were included in primary analyses (n = 420 and n = 339, respectively).

DESIGN: Prospective cohort study. We fit group-based trajectory models to identify distinct longitudinal patterns of cognitive performance. We used least absolute shrinkage and selection operator procedure to identify a parsimonious set of predictors associated with trajectory membership to evaluate in multinomial models.

MAIN MEASURE: Brief Test of Adult Cognition by Telephone (BTACT).

RESULTS: We identified 4 trajectories in the Year 2 cohort (high/improving; medium/improving; low/stable; low/declining) and 3 trajectories in the Year 5 cohort (medium/improving; low/stable; low/declining). While most participants exhibited stable or slightly improving patterns differentiated by analytic baseline BTACT performance, in both cohorts approximately 6%-7% showed low/declining cognitive trajectories and 37%-53% had low/stable cognitive trajectories. Consistent predictors of low/declining trajectories included lower functional cognition, longer duration of post-traumatic amnesia, lower education, non-White race, and female sex. Post-traumatic stress disorder and stroke were associated with low/declining cognitive trajectories 5-10 years postinjury.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides novel insights into cognitive trajectory subgroups 2-10 years post-TBI. While most participants exhibited stable or improving trajectories, a clinically important minority demonstrated low baseline cognition with further deterioration over time. Research is needed to determine whether post-traumatic stress and cerebrovascular disease may be modifiable targets to improve cognitive trajectories after TBI.

articles.title: Towards alpha-blockade-free surgery for pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma: experience from a newly established adrenal center.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pheochromocytomas are rare catecholamine-secreting tumors for which surgical resection is the definitive treatment. Traditionally, preoperative alpha-adrenergic blockade is strictly recommended. However, recent evidence has questioned its necessity. In this study, we report our experience with pheochromocytoma surgery at a newly established adrenal center without prior specialization in adrenal surgery.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: From May 2022 to May 2026, 18 patients (14 female, 4 male; median age 63.1 years, interquartile range (IQR) 46.2-70.1) with catecholamine-producing tumors (15 pheochromocytomas and 3 paragangliomas) underwent surgical resection in our institution. Seventeen patients did not receive any preoperative alpha-adrenergic blockade, whereas one patient underwent surgery while already receiving phenoxybenzamine therapy initiated by the referral physician prior to admission. Intraoperative management included general anaesthesia, central venous access, and invasive arterial blood pressure monitoring. Urapidil and/or nitroglycerin were used as the primary antihypertensive agents. Data were prospectively collected and retrospectively analyzed, including patient demographics, preoperative metanephrine and normetanephrine secretion, intraoperative treatment of hypertension and hypotension, and postoperative outcomes.

RESULTS: The median operative time was 49.5 min (IQR, 30-90). Sixteen procedures were performed minimally invasively (15 retroperitoneoscopic and one laparoscopic), and two by open approach. Partial adrenalectomy was performed in seven cases. Histology confirmed chromaffin cell tumors in all cases, with a median tumor size of 4.0 cm (IQR 3.15-5.15). Median peak intraoperative systolic blood pressure was 195 mmHg (IQR, 166-200). For intraoperative blood pressure control, urapidil was administered to 4 patients (22.2%), nitroglycerin to 3 (16.7%), and both agents to 3 (16.7%). The remaining 8 patients (44.4%), did not require pharmacological treatment. Ten patients (55.6%) had a maximum intraoperative noradrenaline requirement < 0.2 µg/kg/min, 5 (27.8%) required intermediate doses of 0.2-0.4 µg/kg/min, and 3 (16.7%) required high doses > 0.4 µg/kg/min. Median postoperative hospital stay was 2 days (IQR, 2-3). Two patients developed transient atrial fibrillation. No major complications or mortality occurred.

CONCLUSION: Our results support the feasibility of alpha-blockade-free surgery for pheochromocytoma, even in centers with limited prior experience in pheochromocytoma surgery. Education of the anaesthesiology team, structured perioperative protocols, and close interdisciplinary collaboration appear to be important for ensuring safe perioperative management.

articles.title: Early outcomes of tricuspid valve replacement in patients with tricuspid regurgitation: the Trisol Early Feasibility Study.
authors: on behalf of the Trisol investigators
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) could lead to a paradigm shift in treating tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improving patient quality of life.

AIMS: We aimed to report the 30-day outcomes of the Trisol Early Feasibility Study (EFS).

METHODS: The Trisol EFS was a single-arm, multicentre study that enrolled patients with symptomatic ≥severe TR despite optimal medical therapy to undergo TTVR with the Trisol system via transjugular access. The primary safety endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events, including death, myocardial infarction, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding, renal failure requiring dialysis, and the need for surgery. The primary performance endpoints included technical and procedural success, while secondary endpoints included echocardiographic as well as functional and quality-of-life measures.

RESULTS: A total of 19 patients, who were treated with a latest-generation Trisol 12-anchor valve, were included from August 2023 to September 2025. The mean age was 75.8 years (range 62 to 91), 78.9% were female, and 78.9% were in New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV. TR was reduced to mild or less in 87.5% of the subjects and moderate or less in 100% of the subjects. The 30-day composite major adverse event rate was 10.5% (2/19) due to one cardiovascular death and one pacemaker implantation. No other complications were observed. NYHA Class significantly improved to Class I/II (87.5%), and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved by a mean of 13.6±34.6 points.

CONCLUSIONS: In this early clinical experience, the Trisol TTVR system demonstrated technical feasibility, overall safety, significant TR reduction, and the ability to improve quality of life and functional status in TR patients.

articles.title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

articles.title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

articles.title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement after failed edge-to-edge repair.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual or recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is a growing concern in clinical practice and is associated with inferior outcomes.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the early experience of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) in patients with failed TEER.

METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing TTVR for recurrent or residual severe TR after TEER. Clinical, echocardiographic, and computed tomography findings were evaluated. The primary outcome was clinical success at 30 days after TTVR.

RESULTS: Of the 28 patients included (age 78.5±6.3 years, 61% female), 20 (72%) had residual TR and 8 (28%) had recurrent TR diagnosed within a median of 182 days after TEER. Patients were severely symptomatic (New York Heart Association [NYHA] III/IV in 97%), and 64% had massive/torrential TR. In 6 patients (21%), a commissural TEER device was evident, enabling direct TTVR (neocommissure strategy). Engagement of TEER devices with single leaflet device attachment during TTVR was carried out in 12 patients (43%), and electrosurgical laceration and stabilisation to facilitate TTVR in 10 patients (36%). Clinical success at 30 days was 93%. NYHA Functional Class improved in 93% of patients, with 85% being in NYHA I/II at 1 month after TTVR. Two patients died from non-cardiac reasons, and during a median follow-up of 69 days, 4 patients suffered a heart failure hospitalisation despite procedural success.

CONCLUSIONS: In this small patient cohort, three different TTVR strategies after failed TEER resulted in significant clinical success at 30 days and led to substantial symptom relief during short-term follow-up.

articles.title: Three-year outcomes of balloon-expandable valve-in-valve aortic valve implantation for failed transcatheter versus surgical valves.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve (TAV)-in-TAV compared with TAV-in-surgical aortic valve (SAV) implantation for failed bioprosthetic valves have been limited to short-term outcomes.

AIMS: This study compared midterm outcomes between patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and those undergoing TAV-in-SAV.

METHODS: From June 2015 to June 2024, 543 consecutive patients undergoing valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were identified at our centre. After exclusion of ineligible patients, 109 patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and 349 undergoing TAV-in-SAV were included. Following propensity score matching, 214 patients (107 per group) were analysed.

RESULTS: Three-year all-cause mortality did not differ between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups (hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-1.98; p=0.867). Similarly, no significant differences were detected in secondary outcomes. Over 3 years, the aortic valve mean pressure gradient was consistently lower and the aortic valve area was consistently larger in the TAV-in-TAV group compared with the TAV-in-SAV group. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary obstruction were more frequent in the TAV-in-SAV group than in the TAV-in-TAV group (22.4% vs 8.4%; p=0.006; 10.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.018, respectively). Post-ViV-TAVI computed tomography analysis showed that the waist level was the least expanded segment in both groups. However, expansion at this level was significantly greater in the TAV-in-TAV group than in the TAV-in-SAV group.

CONCLUSIONS: There was no significant difference in 3-year mortality between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups. However, TAV-in-SAV was associated with higher rates of concomitant PCI and coronary obstruction, as well as lower valve expansion.

articles.title: Bicuspid aortic valve phenotypes and transcatheter aortic valve implantation feasibility in an all-comers population with severe aortic stenosis.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology

articles.title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
articles.journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined.

AIMS: We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact.

METHODS: This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood.

RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

articles.title: Retrograde Approach Through Arteriovenous Loop Creation for Difficult Balloon Pulmonary Valvuloplasty.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty (BPV) is traditionally performed using antegrade femoral venous approach. However, in severe pulmonary stenosis with challenging anatomy where conventional strategy fails, an arteriovenous loop approach through the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) can be successful. We describe successful BPV in a 4-year-old child using this approach.

KEY STEPS: 1) Traverse the pulmonary valve retrogradely from the aorta through the PDA. 2) Externalize the guidewire using a snare. 3) Perform stiff-wire exchange. 4) Introduce a valvuloplasty balloon over the arteriovenous loop for serial dilatation.

POTENTIAL PITFALLS: 1) Arterial access site complications in young children: ensure appropriate sheath size, adequate anticoagulation, patent hemostasis. 2) Tricuspid subvalvular apparatus injury and balloon entrapment. Meticulous echocardiographic and fluoroscopic guidance is needed during retrograde crossing. Track a balloon-wedge or standard diagnostic catheter over the arteriovenous loop before rigid hardware.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Retrograde arteriovenous loop creation via the PDA is an effective and safe bailout strategy for BPV in severe pulmonary stenosis when the pulmonary valve is not crossed antegradely.

articles.title: Percutaneous Closure of Postinfarction Ventricular Septal Rupture: First Reported Use of Intraprocedural 4DCT With Echocardiography.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy have limitations in defining apical septal anatomy after ventricular septal rupture (VSR). To our knowledge, this is the first reported use of intraprocedural 4-dimensional cardiac computed tomography (4DCT) during percutaneous closure of a post-myocardial infarction (MI) VSR.

CASE SUMMARY: An 81-year-old man developed a post-MI apical VSR. Percutaneous closure was initially attempted sequentially with 24-mm and 22-mm Amplatzer post-infarct muscular ventricular septal defect (VSD) occluders. Device positioning appeared suboptimal but could not be fully characterized by TEE and fluoroscopy. Intraprocedural 4DCT revealed undersizing of the left ventricular disc of the 22-mm device. The device was exchanged for a new 24-mm VSD Occluder. Repeat 4DCT confirmed appropriate positioning and apposition along the VSD margins.

DISCUSSION: Intraprocedural 4DCT provides complementary imaging guidance during percutaneous VSR closure, particularly when TEE or fluoroscopic assessment is limited.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Intraprocedural 4DCT provides high-resolution anatomic guidance during percutaneous closure of complex post-MI VSRs.

articles.title: Chronic Organizing Mediastinal Hematoma Causing Mechanical Prosthetic Tricuspid Valve Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mechanical prosthetic valvular dysfunction is typically thought to be secondary to thrombosis or pannus formation on the valve. Cross-sectional imaging can help with identification of the etiology of prosthetic valvular dysfunction.

CASE SUMMARY: A 39-year-old man with tricuspid atresia and prior biventricular repair with a right atrial to right ventricular conduit presented for an increasing mechanical tricuspid valve gradient and change in his valve clicking sound. Fluoroscopy revealed reduced disc excursion. Three doses of low-dose thrombolytics were trialed without improvement. Computed tomography imaging suggested an intermediate-density mass compressing the conduit and causing extrinsic dysfunction of the tricuspid prosthesis. Surgical examination revealed a chronic mediastinal hematoma causing conduit compression in addition to pannus formation.

DISCUSSION: Mediastinal hematomas are rare and typically provoked by trauma but can be spontaneous particularly with warfarin anticoagulation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Mechanical tricuspid prosthesis dysfunction is often from thrombosis or pannus formation, but extrinsic compression should additionally be considered.

articles.title: Adverse childhood experiences and oral health outcomes among adults in the United States: 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) can have lasting effects on oral health. The authors examined the relationships between ACEs and dental outcomes among adults in the United States.

METHODS: The authors used the 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data (with an overall response rate of 45.0%). The study included 73,537 adults from 12 states. The authors used SAS Release 9.4 (SAS Institute Inc) to conduct multiple logistic regression analyses to assess the association of ACEs with tooth loss and past-year dental visits, and they examined the interactions between ACEs and covariates (age, sex, race, education, income, cigarette smoking status, general health, diabetes, health insurance).

RESULTS: Less than one-half (48.5%) of the study population was male; 62.5% were White, 38.0% had no college education, and 51.5% reported at least 1 ACE. Those with ACEs had higher odds of missing 6 or more teeth than those without ACEs after adjusting for covariates. The adjusted odds ratios of participants with 1, 2 through 3, and 4 or more ACEs were 1.22 (95% CI, 1.06 to 1.40), 1.20 (95% CI, 1.04 to 1.38), and 1.45 (95% CI, 1.26 to 1.68), respectively, compared with those without ACEs. Adults with 4 or more ACEs were less likely to have had a past-year dental visit than those without ACEs (adjusted odds ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.67 to 0.82]).

CONCLUSIONS: Having 1 or more ACEs was significantly associated with a higher risk of tooth loss, and having 4 or more ACEs was significantly associated with a lower likelihood of a past-year dental visit among adults in the United States.

PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dental care providers should be encouraged to incorporate trauma-informed care into their practice through patient-centered communication, shared decision making, and strategies that promote safety and trust for patients with ACEs.

articles.title: The interpretation of heterogeneity in meta-analysis: A tutorial.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The volume of meta-analyses in the dental literature has grown rapidly, but clinicians and reviewers receive little training in interpreting heterogeneity. Heterogeneity is not a nuisance parameter; it is a diagnostic concept that determines whether a pooled estimate is meaningful or a statistical artifact.

TYPES OF STUDIES REVIEWED: The author conducted a narrative review of the methodological literature on heterogeneity in meta-analysis and applied key principles to a worked example using low-level laser therapy for oral mucositis, illustrated with an annotated hypothetical forest plot, with the aim of providing a tutorial on heterogeneity.

RESULTS: Six patterns are commonly recognized in the methodological literature as sources of interpretive error: (1) statistical, methodological, and clinical heterogeneity are routinely conflated; (2) I2 is misread as an absolute measure of variance rather than a relative index requiring τ2 and a 95% CI; (3) the Cochran QP value is mistakenly attributed to I2 itself; (4) CIs around pooled estimates are treated as the range of plausible effects across settings, when only the prediction interval (PI) serves that role; (5) Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation inconsistency ratings are driven mechanically by I2 thresholds rather than judgment about unexplained variability; and (6) narrative synthesis under the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis framework is treated as a fallback rather than a methodologically sound alternative.

CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: Judicious interpretation by authors, reviewers, and readers requires triangulating Cochran Q and its P value, I2 with its CI, τ2, and the PI. No single statistic suffices, and the PI is the most clinically actionable of the 4 statistics.

articles.title: Effects of workplace bullying on cardiovascular health: A prospective cohort study of the Gutenberg Health Study with a ten-year follow-up.
articles.journal: Scandinavian journal of work, environment & health
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): Evidence on long-term cardiovascular effects of workplace bullying is limited. We investigated prospectively the association between workplace bullying and the ten-year incidence of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and hypertension.

METHODS: In a cohort of 4137 employees (<65 years) from the Gutenberg Health Study (Mainz/Mainz-Bingen, Germany), workplace bullying at baseline (2007-2012) was assessed using a single- and five-item instruments. Incident CVD and hypertension at the ten-year follow-up (2017-2022) were clinically verified. Cox models were used for CVD, and robust Poisson regression for hypertension, adjusting for sex, age, and socioeconomic status (SES). Analyses were sex-stratified and considered exposure trajectories.

RESULTS: Bullying prevalence was 15.3% (single item) and 19.3% (five items). For incident CVD, hazard ratios (HR) were 1.08 [95% confidence interval (CI) 0.74-1.59] using the single-item, and 1.28 (95% CI 0.95-1.72) using the five-item instrument. Participants reporting bullying at baseline and five-year follow-up had the highest CVD risk (HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.09-5.44). No association was observed with incident hypertension (single-item: RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.84-1.28, five-item: RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.78-1.13).

CONCLUSION(S): Findings indicate an increased CVD risk when repeated experiences of workplace bullying were reported. No clear elevation of CVD risk was observed when workplace bullying was only considered once at baseline. No evidence was found for elevated hypertension risk. Workplace bullying may represent a relevant psychosocial factor in cardiovascular prevention, underscoring the need for further longitudinal and intervention studies.

articles.title: Latent tuberculosis infection in patients with rheumatoid arthritis receiving conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: a prospective cross-sectional study from the Himalayas.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and its treatments increase the susceptibility to tuberculosis (TB), mainly in TB-endemic settings. Latent TB infection (LTBI) screening is mandatory before biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. However, data on LTBI among RA patients receiving conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (csDMARDs), particularly from north India, are limited. Tuberculin skin testing (TST) may underestimate LTBI in patients with RA because of impaired cell-mediated immunity and reduced delayed-type hypersensitivity responses. In this prospective cross-sectional study, to exclude active TB, 146 consecutive adults with RA (ACR/EULAR 2010 criteria) receiving csDMARDs for ≥3 months underwent Mantoux TST (2 tuberculin units purified protein derivative; reading at 48-72 hours) and chest radiography . Using the conventional cut-off (≥10 mm), LTBI prevalence was 8.2% [12/146; 95% confidence interval (CI) 4.3-13.2%]. Using an immunosuppression-adjusted threshold (≥5 mm), prevalence was 23.3% (34/146; 95% CI 17.8-29.4%). The frequency of 0 mm TST induration was high (76.7%; 112/146). According to univariate analysis, LTBI positivity was linked to higher C-reactive protein (CRP), diabetes, fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL, current smoking, smoking index >200, and urban residency. In multivariable logistic regression (outcome defined as ≥5 mm), smoking index >200 [adjusted odds ratio (OR) 11.47; 95% CI 1.52-86.6; p=0.018] and higher CRP (adjusted OR 1.036 per mg/L; 95% CI 1.006-1.070; p=0.018) remained independently associated with LTBI. Among RA patients on csDMARDs in a north Indian tertiary center, LTBI prevalence ranged from 8.2% (≥10 mm) to 23.3% (≥5 mm). Application of the ≥5 mm TST threshold substantially increased the estimated LTBI prevalence. The high proportion of participants with 0 mm TST induration suggests reduced TST responsiveness in this population. Further studies incorporating interferon-γ release assays are needed to determine the optimal LTBI screening strategy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis receiving csDMARD therapy.

articles.title: Most National Football League Players Return to Play After Achilles Tendon Repair, Yet Only One-Half Regain Preinjury Performance With Persistent Pass-Rush Decline at Year 2.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate National Football League (NFL) player performance using advanced statistics after Achilles tendon (AT) repair.

METHODS: NFL players who underwent AT repair between 2017 and 2023 were identified from a publicly available injury database. Demographic and performance data were collected preinjury and up to 2 seasons postinjury, with a minimum follow-up of 1 regular-season game required to assess return to play (RTP). RTP was defined as being active for a regular-season game and return to performance as achieving ≥90% of preinjury performance. Performance was assessed using Sports Information Solutions' points above replacement (PAR). Factors associated with RTP and return to performance were analyzed using binary logistic regression, with pre- and postinjury performance compared using paired t tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, as appropriate.

RESULTS: Seventy-seven NFL players with AT repairs were identified. Ten were excluded for no prior regular-season play, leaving 67 included. Overall, 77.6% (n = 52) returned to play. Increasing age reduced the odds of RTP (odds ratio 0.75, 95% confidence interval [0.60-0.95], P = .02). Index games preinjury increased the odds of RTP (odds ratio 1.12, 95% confidence interval [1.01-1.24], P = .04). Body mass index, position, index games played, and index PAR were not significant. Among returnees, 50% (n = 26) achieved at least 90% of preinjury performance. Higher index PAR predicted lower odds of meeting this threshold (odds ratio 0.77, 95% confidence interval [0.66-0.90], P = .00). Pass-rush PAR declined at year 2 after injury from 1.17 (±5.19) preinjury to -0.66 (±2.15), P = .02.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study using publicly available data, 77.6% of NFL players returned to play after AT repair; however, only one-half of these players regained ≥90% of their preinjury performance. Older age reduced the likelihood of RTP, whereas more preinjury games started increased it. Higher preinjury PAR reduced the likelihood of performance recovery. Pass-rush performance declined by the second postinjury season.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV, retrospective therapeutic case series.

articles.title: A multifunctional magnetic composite Fe3O4@MOF-919 for dual-function bacterial clearance and IL-6 removal in hemoperfusion.
articles.abstract: Magnetic materials derived from metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have garnered considerable interest as adsorbents for hemoperfusion. Herein, a novel magnetic metal-organic framework composite adsorbent, Fe3O4@MOF-919, was designed and synthesized to address the clinical challenge of dual-functionally removing drug-resistant pathogens and inflammatory mediators in bloodstream infections (BSI). Under identical experimental conditions, Fe3O4@MOF-919 exhibited exceptional antibacterial efficacy, achieving removal efficiencies of 99.4% against CREO, 99.8% against CRKP, and 99.6% against MRSA. These results are attributable to the synergistic coordination between bacterial surface moieties and the Cu2+/Fe3+ sites and carboxylate ligands of the MOF-919(Fe-Cu) shell. Simultaneously, the composite demonstrated a high adsorption efficiency for IL-6 in simulated serum (96.68% within 3 h, equivalent to 70.58 ng g-1), following a physical adsorption mechanism. Crucially, Fe3O4@MOF-919 also shows a hemolysis rate below 5%, negligible impact on coagulation function and blood cells, and Grade 1 cytotoxicity. By physically removing pathogens and cytokines without inducing drug resistance, Fe3O4@MOF-919 provides a safe and effective adsorbent platform for drug-resistant BSI and sepsis, demonstrating considerable potential for future biomedical applications.

articles.title: Does Mild Anemia Associate With 3-Month Vascular Outcomes in Severe Acute Ischemic Stroke?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anemia has been shown to be independently associated with poor outcomes in critically ill patients. Despite this, the impact of hemoglobin (Hb) levels on prognosis among patients with severe acute ischemic stroke (AIS) requiring neurocritical care has not been well established. We therefore sought to evaluate the relationship between Hb levels and clinical outcomes in this population.

METHODS: This study was an analysis of a prospective, multicenter, nationwide stroke registry between January 2011 and April 2023. We included patients within 7 days of onset AIS whose severity of National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale more than 16 scores. Hb levels were categorized into 4 groups; 1) moderate to severe anemia (Hb < 11 g/dL), 2) mild anemia(men: 11.0-12.9 g/dL, women: 11.0-11.9 g/dL), 3) normal (men: 13.0-17.0 g/dL, women: 12.0-15.5 g/dL), 4) polycythemia (men > 17.0 g/dL, women > 15.6 g/dL). The primary outcome is defined as a composite of recurrent stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and all-cause mortality within 3-month.

RESULTS: A total of 8,615 patients with severe AIS were included in the final analysis (mean age, 74.3 ± 12.1 years; 47.8% male). The prevalence of moderate-to-severe anemia was 15.9%, mild anemia 17.0%, normal Hb levels 62.4%, and polycythemia 4.6%. Compared with patients with normal Hb levels, those with mild or moderate-to-severe anemia exhibited higher 3-month rates of the composite outcome of recurrent stroke, MI, and all-cause mortality. After multivariable adjustment, both mild and moderate-to-severe anemia remained independently associated with an increased risk of the 3-month composite outcome (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.15; 1.04-1.28; P = 0.009).

CONCLUSION: In patients with severe AIS requiring neurocritical care, lower Hb levels were independently associated with an increased risk of 3-month composite vascular outcomes, even at the level of mild anemia.

articles.title: Association of Nontraumatic Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head With Major Cardiovascular and Cerebrovascular Events: A Nationwide Cohort Study of Korea.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is associated with systemic comorbidities and vascular risk factors, raising the possibility of an association with major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). This study aimed to evaluate its long-term association with MACCEs.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the Korean National Health Insurance Service Sample Cohort 2.0 (2006-2015). Incident ONFH cases diagnosed between 2008 and 2010 (n = 1,150) were initially matched with 1:5 controls (n = 5,750) by age, sex, residential area, and index year. To further improve covariate balance, additional propensity score (PS) matching was performed (1:5), yielding a PS-matched cohort of 6,038 participants (ONFH, n = 1,130; controls, n = 4,908). MACCEs (myocardial infarction, unstable angina, revascularization, heart failure, and stroke/transient ischemic attack) were tracked for up to seven years, and associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: In the PS-matched cohort, MACCEs occurred more frequently in the ONFH group than in controls (19.4% vs. 15.3%), with reduced MACCE-free survival (log-rank P < 0.001). Incidence-rate analysis showed an increased risk of MACCEs (incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.29; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.11-1.50) and cardiovascular events (IRR, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.18-1.71), whereas cerebrovascular events were not significantly different (IRR, 1.11; 95% CI, 0.86-1.43). In multivariable Cox models, ONFH was associated with a higher risk of MACCEs (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.02-1.38). Sensitivity analyses excluding patients with systemic autoimmune diseases and excluding glucocorticoid users showed consistent results.

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide cohort, nontraumatic ONFH was associated with an increased long-term risk of MACCEs, driven mainly by cardiovascular events. These findings suggest that nontraumatic ONFH may serve as a clinically relevant marker of increased cardiovascular risk, supporting attention to cardiovascular risk assessment in patients with ONFH.

articles.title: Exploratory Pilot Randomized Crossover Study of Transcutaneous Vagus Nerve Stimulation on Sleep Quality and Mood in Healthy Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tcVNS) has been reported to influence autonomic regulation and sleep in various clinical settings. However, evidence in healthy populations is limited. This study investigated the effects of tcVNS on subjective sleep quality, mood, and autonomic function in healthy adults.

METHODS: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial in which 29 healthy participants underwent two four-week stimulation phases (Active and Sham). Active stimulation was delivered at subthreshold intensity, whereas Sham stimulation involved identical device use without electrical current. Outcomes included the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index-Korean version (PSQI-K), Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D), and daily heart rate variability (HRV) indices collected using a validated smartphone-based application. Linear mixed-effects models were used to analyze questionnaire scores.

RESULTS: PSQI-K scores showed a statistically significant but modest reduction during Active stimulation compared with Baseline (P = 0.013) and Sham (corrected P < 0.001), although the mean change did not exceed the minimal clinically important difference. No significant changes were observed for BDI-II or HAM-D. HRV responses were heterogeneous across participants, with no significant group-level differences. No serious adverse events occurred, and mild transient ear discomfort or tingling was reported by 3 participants (10.3%) during Active stimulation.

CONCLUSION: This exploratory pilot trial suggests that tcVNS was safe and well tolerated and may produce modest changes in subjective sleep quality in healthy adults. The absence of mood effects likely reflects low baseline symptom burden. These findings provide preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence that stimulation parameters may warrant further investigation, and confirmation in adequately powered trials and clinical populations is required.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0009790.

articles.title: A Deep Learning-Based Prediction Model for Mortality in Severe COVID-19 Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Admission: A Multicenter Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has been associated with substantial global mortality. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based models have shown promise for mortality prediction, evidence focused specifically on critically ill patients remains limited. In addition, meaningful clinical implementation requires models that rely on a minimal set of readily available variables to enable rapid risk stratification. This study aimed to develop a deep learning-based model for predicting mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission, with an emphasis on efficiency and clinical applicability.

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 900 critically ill patients with COVID-19 admitted to ICUs across 22 centers in Korea between January 1, 2020, and August 31, 2021. A deep learning-based tabular model was constructed, and systematic feature reduction strategies were applied to optimize predictive performance while enhancing practicality.

RESULTS: Of the 900 patients, 365 (40.6%) survived and 535 (59.4%) died. Compared with survivors, non-survivors were older, demonstrated more severe clinical and chest X-ray (CXR) findings, had lower respiratory rate-oxygenation (ROX) indices, and required vasopressors and continuous renal replacement therapy more frequently (all P < 0.05). The initial model incorporating 66 variables achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8500. Following stepwise feature selection, the model was reduced to seven key variables (age, C-reactive protein, lactate dehydrogenase, pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, CXR infiltration, CXR consolidation, and ROX index), resulting in a simplified model with an AUC of 0.8247.

CONCLUSION: A deep learning-based AI model was developed to support clinical decision-making in critically ill patients with COVID-19, offering an efficient and clinically practical approach to mortality risk assessment.

articles.title: Development of a model of tick-borne encephalitis virus transmission from experimentally infected bank voles to Ixodes ricinus ticks.
articles.abstract: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is an important arbovirus in Europe. TBEV is transmitted mainly by ticks of the Ixodes ricinus (Ixodes ricinus-Ixodes persulcatus) species complex and causes infections of the central nervous system, making it one of the most important viral tick-borne diseases of humans in Europe. The natural transmission cycle relies on a complex interplay of arthropod vector and mammalian host factors. Besides the infection of ticks by feeding on viremic animals and co-feeding, transstadial transmission of the virus within the tick is also essential for further TBEV transmission to the next vertebrate host during the subsequent bloodmeal. In this study, we attempted to establish a mammalian host-tick transmission model for the simulation of the natural transmission under controlled laboratory conditions in order to study virus transmission from the reservoir host bank vole (Myodes glareolus) to I. ricinus larvae and to evaluate transstadial transmission of TBEV when engorged larvae moult into nymphs. We demonstrated acquisition of TBEV by larval ticks that blood fed on TBEV-infected viremic bank voles, although the TBEV infection prevalence of the engorged larvae was low (9.3%). Fully and partially engorged larvae were collected and further kept in the insectary and were allowed to moult into nymphs to assess transstadial virus transmission. No transstadial virus transmission was observed, as all nymphs tested negative by real-time RT-PCR. Although no general conclusions on transstadial transmission could be drawn yet, the establishment of this model forms a basis for future research.

articles.title: Biopsychosocial Determinants of Mode of Birth in the United States: A Systematic Review of Maternal Clinical and Contextual Influences.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mode of birth (cesarean or vaginal) is critical to long-term maternal and child health, with cesarean delivery, whether planned or unplanned, linked to child morbidities. However, the rates of cesarean deliveries have accounted for one-third of United States births for more than a decade, with global trends reflecting substantial variation in access and use. A comprehensive synthesis of the factors that condition decisions about the mode of birth within this period is lacking. Understanding the role of contextual and maternal risk factors is essential for designing interventions that support equitable and healthy birth experiences, reduce postnatal complications, and improve child health trajectories.

OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate evidence examining clinical and contextual factors influencing the mode of birth, including planned and unplanned cesarean deliveries in the United States.

METHODS: The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guided the review report. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CINAHL on February 27th, 2025, for studies published between 2015 and 2025. The quality of evidence was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools and the Prediction model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool.

FINDINGS: We included N = 24 studies in this review. Maternal medical conditions were associated with higher odds of cesarean delivery. In contrast, contextual factors such as participation in childbirth education and flexible work schedules were linked to a greater likelihood of vaginal birth. Socioeconomic deprivation and access to healthcare contributed to disparities in the mode of birth. Findings reiterate the multifactorial nature of mode of birth decisions and highlight the need for integrated approaches in maternal care.

CONCLUSION: Mode of birth decisions extend beyond maternal medical conditions. Health workers and future research should integrate contextual, psychosocial, and clinical evidence to design multilevel, equitable interventions.

articles.title: The strategic integration of emergency obstetric and neonatal care with contraceptive services.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (CEmONC) indicators have strengthened health systems' capacity to manage acute obstetric emergencies and remain central to global maternal health monitoring. However, current EmONC frameworks omit contraception, despite its established role in preventing unintended pregnancy, supporting healthy interpregnancy intervals, and reducing recurrent exposure to obstetric risk. This gap reflects an artificial divide between emergency response and preventive care. This commentary argues that contraception should be recognized as an essential, integrated component of EmONC rather than a separate postpartum service. We outline the clinical rationale for embedding contraceptive counseling and provision within each EmONC signal function, noting that the nature of an obstetric emergency-hemorrhage, infection, hypertensive disease-often directly informs contraceptive eligibility and method selection. We further describe why the postpartum period after an obstetric emergency represents a critical, frequently missed opportunity for contraceptive counseling, particularly in low-resource and humanitarian settings where subsequent access to care is uncertain. We propose practical strategies for integration at the facility, health system, and global levels, including standardized counseling prompts, aligned supply chains, updated training curricula, and incorporation of contraceptive indicators into EmONC guidance and monitoring tools. Embedding contraception within EmONC would strengthen continuity across the maternal health continuum and better align global frameworks with the clinical realities of obstetric risk.

articles.title: Examination of treatment responses with mycophenolate mofetil in Black vs White patients with systemic sclerosis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Black patients with systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) have more severe disease than White patients. We investigated whether racial differences in therapeutic responses to mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) could explain this differential disease severity.

METHODS: Self-identified Black and White patients with scleroderma who had MMF exposure were selected from the Johns Hopkins Scleroderma Center Research Registry. We used linear mixed effects models to study the trajectory of forced vital capacity % predicted (pFVC) and modified Rodnan skin scores (mRSS) during follow-up.

RESULTS: Among 662 patients with measured baseline pFVC, the average (SD) baseline pFVC was 64.3 (15.6) for Black patients and 86.9 (18.6) for White patients (p<0.001). During follow-up, the estimated annual change ±SE in pFVC among Black patients was -0.53±0.46 pre-MMF and -0.58±0.27 post-treatment (pre-post difference of -0.04±0.54 (p=0.939)). Among White patients, estimated annual changes in pFVC pre- and post-MMF were -1.20± 0.23 and -0.56±0.13, with a pre-post difference of +0.64±0.27 (p=0.019). Among 452 patients with diffuse scleroderma, the baseline mRSS was 17.2 (SD 10.1) for Black patients and 21.4 (SD 11.1) for White patients (p<0.001). The estimated difference in annual change in mRSS post-MMF treatment compared to pre-treatment was -0.87±0.32 for Black patients, compared to -0.68±0.16 among White patients (p=0.598).

CONCLUSION: Black patients have more severe pulmonary disease at presentation. While Black and White patients have similar rates of change in pFVC and mRSS after MMF exposure, Black patients did not have a meaningful difference in pFVC change post-MMF compared to pre-MMF, suggesting further study is needed in this population.

articles.title: Root gene regulatory network analysis reveals roles for defense hormones and secondary metabolites in establishment of disease-suppressive soil.
articles.abstract: Plants recruit beneficial microbiota in their rhizosphere to alleviate stresses. In Arabidopsis thaliana, foliar infection by Hyaloperonospora arabidopsidis (Hpa) has been shown to establish a disease-suppressive microbiome that promotes protection against Hpa infection of the subsequent plant generation grown in conditioned soil - a phenomenon known as soil-borne legacy (SBL). The root responses involved in SBL establishment have remained largely unclear. In this study, time-series RNA-seq of roots from Hpa-infected plants grown in natural soil was conducted over 7 d post inoculation. A gene regulatory network of the responding roots was constructed. The role of predicted key components was verified in follow-up assays. Root transcriptional reprogramming started within 1 d after foliar infection. Genes associated with salicylic acid (SA)-mediated defense were upregulated, while those linked to secondary metabolism and jasmonic acid (JA) responsiveness were downregulated. SA accumulation increased at 1 d post inoculation (dpi), and JA decreased by 3 dpi. Transcriptional regulation occurred in the tips of the roots. Mutant analyses confirmed that SA, JA, indole glucosinolates, camalexin, and flavonoids contribute to SBL establishment. Our findings reveal systemic transcriptional reprogramming in roots upon foliar pathogen attack, uncovering roles of hormone signaling and secondary metabolism in shaping a disease-suppressive soil beyond their known defense functions.

articles.title: Characterization of gastrointestinal pathology in a fatal ehrlichiosis mouse model.
articles.abstract: Ehrlichiosis is a zoonotic, tick-borne, and potentially life-threatening disease affecting animals and humans that is caused by infection with Ehrlichia species. While our understanding of these obligate intracellular bacteria has expanded, the mechanism of in vivo pathogenesis remains a critical knowledge gap. Ehrlichia japonica-challenged immunocompetent mice, such as ICR and C57BL/6, have been used to recapitulate human monocytic ehrlichiosis and to study disease-associated deaths. We reproduced this fatal ehrlichiosis mouse model and reevaluated the lesions in the gastrointestinal tract and draining lymph nodes, which were poorly described in the literature. The mice developed progressive clinical signs of illness by day 7 post-inoculation and were euthanized between days 8 and 9. Postmortem examination revealed subtle yet grossly visible lesions, including hemorrhages in mesenteric lymph nodes (12/13, 92%) and Peyer's patches (7/13, 54%), petechial hemorrhages on the intestinal serosa (10/13, 77%), and segmental intraluminal hemorrhages (7/13, 54%). Acute intraluminal hemorrhages in the jejunum and ileum were confirmed histologically (9/13, 69%). In the mesenteric lymph nodes, lymphofollicular hyperplasia and sinus histiocytosis were also prominent (13/13, 100%). We developed an in situ hybridization assay and demonstrated that Ehrlichia-infected cells were disseminated throughout the gastrointestinal tract with the highest counts in the small intestine compared with those in the stomach, cecum, and colon (P < .01). Our data show that severe ehrlichiosis induces reproducible pathological changes in the gastrointestinal tract, which may play a role in disease progression and mortality in the mammalian host. Further research is required to determine the clinical significance of these lesions.

articles.title: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
articles.abstract: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups.
