Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.

articles.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in the Presence of Aortic Coarctation: Current Evidence and Practical Approaches.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis across a wide spectrum of surgical risk. As TAVI is increasingly used in younger patients and in those with congenital valve disease, the coexistence of aortic stenosis and untreated coarctation of the aorta (CoA) is being encountered more frequently. However, evidence guiding the procedural strategy in this complex anatomical setting remains limited.

AIMS: To systematically review the published literature on TAVI in adult patients with untreated or residual coarctation of the aorta, focusing on patient characteristics, procedural strategies, vascular access selection, management of coexisting CoA, and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed, Wiley Online Library, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library to identify published reports describing TAVI in adult patients with angiographically confirmed native or residual severe CoA. Case reports and case series published between January 2013 and September 2025 were included. Studies involving repaired CoA without restenosis or surgical aortic valve replacement were excluded. Clinical characteristics, access routes, procedural strategies, and outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: Nine patients from published reports met the inclusion criteria. Hemodynamically significant CoA was present in five patients (55.6%). Bicuspid aortic valve anatomy was reported in six cases. Transcatheter access routes included transcarotid (44.4%), transfemoral (33.3%), transsubclavian (11.1%), and transaxillary (11.1%) approaches. A staged strategy with initial CoA stenting followed by TAVI was performed in two patients (22.2%), whereas seven patients (77.8%) underwent single-procedure management, including concomitant treatment of both lesions in two cases. Procedural success was achieved in all cases, although technical challenges related to valve delivery and stent expansion were occasionally encountered.

CONCLUSIONS: TAVI in patients with untreated or residual CoA is feasible and can be performed with high procedural success when individualized strategies are applied. Access selection and the timing of CoA intervention should be guided by anatomical characteristics and hemodynamic severity. Given the limited evidence base, careful preprocedural planning and a multidisciplinary approach are essential to optimize outcomes in this complex patient population.

articles.title: Experience of Microwave Ablation of Liver Tumors in Special Sites Under Ultrasound Guidance: Review of the Literature With Image Illustration.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the therapeutic effect and safety of microwave ablation for liver tumors in special sites under ultrasound guidance.

METHODS: A total of 69 cases of liver tumor lesions in special sites that could not or were unwilling to undergo surgical operation in Mianyang Central Hospital in the past 5 years were selected (10 cases of lesions near the abdominal wall, 25 cases of lesions under the diaphragm, 11 cases of lesions beside the gallbladder, and 23 cases of lesions near the gastrointestinal tract). Microwave ablation of liver tumors in special sites was performed through methods such as establishing a normal saline separation zone, artificial ascites, and laparoscopic ultrasound guidance. After ablation, the operation time, the range of tumor coagulation and necrosis, and the presence of complications were observed.

RESULTS: The pain score of 69 cases of liver tumors in special sites after microwave ablation was mild. No complications such as diaphragm injury, gallbladder injury, gastrointestinal injury, bleeding, or infection occurred. Postoperative contrast-enhanced ultrasound, contrast-enhanced CT, or enhanced magnetic resonance imaging showed that the range of coagulation and necrosis covered the original lesion range.

CONCLUSION: Microwave ablation of liver tumors in special sites under ultrasound guidance is safe and effective, and can be used as an effective alternative treatment method for this type of disease.

articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology

articles.title: Practitioner Perceptions of Factors Influencing the Continued Use of Clean Cut Practices in Ethiopia and Madagascar: A Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clean Cut is a surgical quality improvement program focused on six perioperative infection prevention practices. Although it has been implemented across multiple hospitals in sub-Saharan Africa and shown to reduce surgical site infections (SSIs), its long-term sustainability remains unclear. This study explored perceptions of the sustainability of Clean Cut at three hospitals in Ethiopia and one hospital in Madagascar by identifying factors that support or hinder long-term adherence.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten healthcare providers involved in Clean Cut implementation, including surgeons, nurses, and anesthesiologists. Interviews explored experiences with the program, perceived barriers and facilitators to sustainability, and integration into hospital workflows. Audio recordings were transcribed, coded, and analyzed thematically using a standardized codebook.

RESULTS: Participants reported sustained improvements in infection prevention practices, teamwork, and operating room protocols following Clean Cut implementation. Standardized workflows, multidisciplinary collaboration, and data-driven quality improvement initiatives were identified as key facilitators of sustainability. Lifebox is one of many organizations that have helped the Ethiopian Ministry of Health standardize surgical care. However, participants also described barriers to long-term adherence, including limited hands-on training, staff turnover, leadership changes, resource constraints, and inconsistent access to supplies and equipment. Participants recommended refresher training, stronger collaboration with infection prevention departments, continued leadership engagement, and expanded stakeholder involvement to strengthen sustainability.

CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that Clean Cut had a sustained perceived influence on infection prevention practices, quality improvement efforts, and surgical safety culture. Long-term success depends on addressing resource and training gaps while promoting institutional ownership and leadership support. These findings provide insight into perceived facilitators and barriers to sustainability that may inform future efforts to scale and sustain surgical quality improvement programs in low-resource settings.

articles.title: Investigating the association between blood lipid profiles and insulin resistance and β-cell function indices in pregnant women.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine the associations between first-trimester lipid markers and second-trimester insulin resistance (IR) and pancreatic β-cell function (BCF) indices in pregnant women. An exploratory aim was to explore the apparent discrimination of lipid markers for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity.

METHODS: This retrospective secondary analysis used prospectively collected cohort data from 1202 pregnant women in Beijing, China. Lipids were measured at 4-8 weeks of gestation, and a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test was performed at 24-28 weeks. The Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR) and the Matsuda index were analyzed as continuous measures of IR and insulin sensitivity. BCF was assessed using surrogate indices: the Homeostatic Model Assessment of β-cell function (HOMA-β) and the 60-min insulinogenic index (IGI60). Linear-regression models adjusted for age and early-pregnancy body mass index examined the associations between each lipid marker and continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index as the primary analyses and with HOMA-β and IGI60 as the secondary analyses. Binary logistic-regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses of cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity were exploratory.

RESULTS: After adjustment for age and early-pregnancy body mass index, all seven lipid markers were significantly associated with continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index (all nominal P < 0.05). No statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate β-cell-function indices HOMA-β or IGI60. In the exploratory analyses, the lipid markers were associated with the cohort-defined low-Matsuda category. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol had the highest observed area under the curve in the total population (0.723; 95% confidence interval 0.689-0.756). The exploratory cutoff selected by maximizing Youden's index was 0.65, with a sensitivity of 74.1% and a specificity of 62.5%.

CONCLUSION: First-trimester lipid markers were associated with second-trimester IR and insulin-sensitivity indices, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate BCF indices used in this study. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed moderate apparent discrimination for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity and should be considered a hypothesis-generating candidate marker requiring external validation.

articles.title: Development, Implementation, and Assessment of a Computer Decision Support System for Monitoring and Management of Oral Anticoagulation With Warfarin in Resource-Constrained Settings: Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Warfarin remains the mainstay of oral anticoagulation in low- and middle-income countries and in specific clinical conditions, despite its complex management and the risks associated with poor anticoagulation control. In this context, clinical decision support systems (CDSS) have the potential to improve anticoagulation safety and efficacy, particularly in primary care.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to develop a CDSS aimed at enhancing anticoagulation management in primary care, to implement it in a resource-constrained region, and to evaluate its usability and satisfaction among health care professionals.

METHODS: The study followed a mixed methods, 4-phase design based on the Medical Research Council framework. Phase 1 involved a cross-sectional assessment of primary care units to identify gaps in usual anticoagulation care. In phase 2, a baseline prototype of a secure, web-based application was developed, featuring structured patient data entry and tools for monitoring anticoagulation quality, but without decision-support messages. Formative evaluation was conducted over 8 months through real-world use of the prototype by health care professionals, assessing system functionality, usability, and data entry processes to guide refinement of system features; these professionals assessed 514 patients in 4022 consultations. Phase 3 focused on the development of individualized decision-support messages. Phase 4 consisted of a pilot implementation during routine outpatient consultations, in which trained clinical pharmacists used the CDSS, and usability and acceptability were evaluated through semistructured interviews, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically.

RESULTS: The final CDSS included 210 tailored clinical recommendations addressing anticoagulation indication, dose adjustment, drug-drug interactions, and bleeding management. Internal validation demonstrated the logical consistency of the algorithms and accurate triggering of decision support messages. The system was successfully adopted by all trained pharmacists and integrated into routine workflows. Users reported high usability, intuitive navigation, and perceived usefulness of graphical tools for monitoring international normalized ratio (INR) and time in therapeutic range. The system was perceived to improve consultation organization, standardize clinical decision-making, enhance patient education, and support longitudinal follow-up. Key barriers included time constraints, competing demands, occasional technical issues, and lack of integration with electronic health records.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the feasibility and acceptability of a CDSS for anticoagulation management in primary care in a resource-constrained setting. The iterative development process, including extensive real-world formative evaluation prior to implementation of decision-support logic, strengthened system usability and alignment with clinical workflows. Future studies should evaluate its effectiveness on clinical outcomes and explore strategies to enhance integration, scalability, and sustainability.

articles.title: Outcomes of Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Hispanic/Latino Hospitalizations: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2016-2022.
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (MTEER) is an established treatment for severe symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). However, Hispanic/Latino patients remain underrepresented in structural heart research, and contemporary national data on their in-hospital outcomes and resource utilization are limited.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. MTEER hospitalizations were identified using ICD-10-PCS codes and restricted to non-Hispanic White and Hispanic/Latino hospitalizations, without a concomitant major cardiovascular procedure, with non-Hispanic White hospitalizations serving as the reference. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression and generalized linear models evaluated in-hospital mortality, total hospital charges, length of stay, individual adverse events, and a composite in-hospital adverse event outcome.

RESULTS: Among 50,795 weighted MTEER hospitalizations, 3655 were Hispanic/Latino. Hispanic/Latino hospitalizations involved younger patients, were less often elective, and had greater socioeconomic disadvantage and a higher burden of selected comorbidities. After adjustment, no statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was detected (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.11; 95% CI, 0.59-2.12), while Hispanic/Latino ethnicity was associated with higher total hospital charges (adjusted ratio 1.16; 95% CI, 1.09-1.23) and higher odds of the composite outcome (aOR 1.23; 95% CI, 1.00-1.51). Adjusted length of stay did not differ. In exploratory analyses, Hispanic/Latino hospitalizations also had higher adjusted odds of blood transfusion and pericardial effusion or tamponade.

CONCLUSIONS: No statistically significant difference in in-hospital mortality was detected, but Hispanic/Latino hospitalizations for MTEER had more in-hospital adverse events and higher hospital charges than non-Hispanic White hospitalizations. These differences warrant further study with clinical data.

articles.title: Neurology eConsult Content and Adoption of Consultant Recommendations at a Large Academic Health System: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Telemedicine journal and e-health : the official journal of the American Telemedicine Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interprofessional consultations ("eConsults") can improve access to specialist expertise, but the content of neurology eConsults and rates of consultant recommendation adoption remain under-characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of neurology eConsults submitted at the Mount Sinai Health System between August 2020 and July 2024, excluding canceled, unanswered, and duplicate eConsult submissions. Two reviewers independently categorized consultative questions and consultant recommendations. The primary outcome was adoption of at least one consultant recommendation within 12 months of the eConsult submission. Secondary outcomes were adoption by recommendation type. Multivariable logistic regression analysis identified factors associated with overall recommendation adoption.

RESULTS: We identified 771 eConsults comprising 872 consultative questions for 736 patients (median age 56 years; 67.7% female). The most common questions concerned diagnostic work-up (n = 226, 29.3%), initial treatment or medication choice (n = 123, 16.0%), and interpretation of the clinical presentation (n = 88, 11.4%). Consultants most frequently recommended an in-person neurology evaluation (n = 322, 41.8%) and neuroimaging (n = 244, 31.6%). Overall, at least one recommendation was adopted in 408 of 567 eConsults (72.0%). Recommendations for neuroimaging, medications, and laboratory testing were adopted in 55.7% (n = 136/244), 72.7% (n = 88/121), and 76.0% (n = 38/50) of applicable eConsults, respectively, and 66.5% (n = 214/322) of patients recommended for in-person evaluation completed a neurology visit within 1 year. In multivariable analysis, adoption of at least one recommendation was more likely when consultants recommended addition of a medication [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 3.41, 95% CI: 1.71-6.82] or an in-person neurology evaluation (aOR = 2.45, 95% CI: 1.41-4.26).

DISCUSSION: Neurology eConsults addressed a broad range of diagnostic and management questions, and most eConsults with a recommendation had at least one adopted within 12 months. Adoption was lowest for recommendations requiring an additional encounter, and one-third of patients were advised to see a neurologist and did not complete a visit within 1 year, highlighting a gap in continuity of specialty care.

articles.title: Alcohol consumption is associated with increased prediction error in a buccal swab-based DNA methylation age prediction model.
articles.abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm)-based age estimation is a promising forensic tool, but prediction accuracy may be affected by lifestyle factors such as alcohol consumption. This study evaluated a buccal swab DNAm age prediction model, developed in non-drinking individuals, when applied to individuals with varying drinking patterns. Buccal swabs were collected from 90 healthy non-drinkers (mean age 44.9 years; range 22-93) for model development and from 62 regular alcohol consumers (mean age 32.8 years; range 19-63), classified as light (n = 29), moderate (n = 21), or heavy (n = 12) drinkers per NIAAA criteria, for model evaluation. Stepwise multivariate linear regression across seven candidate age-associated CpG loci identified a 3-CpG model (SLC12A5, ASPA, FHL2) explaining 61% of age variance (adjusted R2 = 0.613; MAE = 7.7 years; r = 0.791, p < 0.001). When applied to the alcohol-consuming cohort, prediction error increased significantly (MAE = 9.9 years; p = 0.046), with light and heavy drinkers showing markedly elevated error while moderate drinkers did not differ from non-drinkers. The association remained significant after adjusting for smoking status and chronological age. An extended model incorporating alcohol consumption as a predictor, retrained on the combined cohort (n = 152), achieved comparable accuracy (adjusted R2 = 0.605; MAE = 7.4 years) and retained alcohol consumption as a significant negative predictor of age (B = -6.84, p < 0.001). At the locus level, ASPA's age association was attenuated in alcohol consumers, whereas FHL2 and SLC12A5 showed no significant alcohol interaction. As lifestyle data are usually unavailable in casework, alcohol-robust CpG sites should be prioritized in forensic model development.

articles.title: Pre-eclampsia screening and prevention: Implementing FIGO guidelines in a Thai population.
articles.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world implementation, screening performance, aspirin uptake, and safety of a FIGO (the International Federation of Gynecology & Obstetrics)-based first-trimester pre-eclampsia screening and prevention program.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included women initiating antenatal care before 14 weeks of gestation at a tertiary referral center in southern Thailand from 2021 to 2024. Screening incorporated maternal factors, mean arterial pressure, and uterine artery pulsatility index. Women with a calculated risk of 1:100 or greater were classified as being at high risk and offered aspirin 162 mg nightly. Outcomes included screening coverage, detection rates, aspirin uptake, pregnancy outcomes, and bleeding complications.

RESULTS: Among 1713 pregnancies, 71 developed pre-eclampsia (4.1%), including 49 with severe features. Overall, 1106 women were screened (64.6%), but coverage reached 93.6% by the end of implementation. The screen-positive rate was 11.3%. Detection rates were 61.7% for overall pre-eclampsia, 69.6% for delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, 87.5% for delivery before 34 weeks of gestation, and 100% for delivery before 32 weeks of gestation, with false-positive rates of approximately 9%-11%. Aspirin uptake among screen-positive women was 99.2%. Pre-eclampsia was associated with higher rates of cesarean delivery, preterm birth, lower birth weight, and neonatal intensive care unit admission. No eclampsia, placental abruption, maternal intensive care unit admission, maternal death, stillbirth, or neonatal death occurred. After adjustment for potential confounders, aspirin was not associated with the risk of an estimated blood loss of 500 mL or more, and the risk of an estimated blood loss of 1000 mL or more did not differ significantly between groups.

CONCLUSION: FIGO-based first-trimester screening was feasible in routine care, with increasing coverage as implementation matured, near-universal aspirin uptake, and clinically useful detection of preterm pre-eclampsia. Aspirin use was not significantly associated with severe bleeding.

articles.title: Nonlinear amplification of classical intensity noise and its impact on g(2)-measurements.
articles.abstract: The emerging field of "strong-field quantum optics" re-examines intense light-matter processes such as high-harmonic generation from a quantum-optical perspective. Here, we demonstrate that the classical intensity noise of the fundamental elevates the second-order correlation function (g(2)) of perturbative harmonics above the coherent limit (g(2) = 1). To leading order, this excess scales quadratically with the harmonic order and the relative intensity noise. We derive explicit expressions for this effect, experimentally validate them in second-harmonic generation with controlled intensity noise, and introduce a conditioning protocol to suppress this classical noise, thereby establishing an operationally meaningful baseline against which genuine deviations from coherent statistics can be identified in pulsed strong-field experiments.

articles.title: Reference-free per-measurement assessment of lensless reconstruction quality under imperfect PSF models.
articles.abstract: Mismatch between a nominal point-spread function (PSF) and the effective response can decouple reprojection residuals from lensless reconstruction quality. We introduce the multi-evidence reconstruction risk descriptor (MRRD), a fixed 54-field representation that combines residual structure, reconstruction statistics, and local PSF sensitivity for reference-free, per-measurement risk ranking after a fixed reconstructor. On 12 prespecified held-out masks (1,200 measurements; 10,800 records), frozen predictors attained a pooled PSNR-risk Spearman correlation of 0.7756 and an AUROC of 0.8589. In zero-shot tests on two physical lensless systems, PSNR-risk rankings remained positive (ρ = 0.523 for diffuser and ρ = 0.600 for random multi-focal lenslet, RML). These results establish MRRD as a reference-free ranking and selective-review layer for composite reconstruction-quality risk under the tested protocols.

articles.title: Analytical Markov chain for spatiotemporal flux evolution of the inner filter effect in fluorescent media.
articles.abstract: Characterizing emission and decay time spectra in multi-component fluorescent media is essential for identifying intrinsic material properties and optimizing detectors. However, wavelength evolution from the secondary inner filter effect (IFE) distorts these observable spectra. While Monte Carlo (MC) ray-tracing can simulate this distortion, accumulating adequate tracking statistics requires long computation times, which hinders parameter optimization within high-dimensional spaces. This paper presents an analytical Markovian transport model based on spatiotemporal decoupling. A Laplace transform converts the multi-nested convolution integrals over continuous domains into a discrete Markov transition matrix, reducing the computational complexity from an exponential scale with respect to wavelength bins N λ and cascade order n, O(N λ n ), to a linear scale, O(N λ +n). The resulting algebraic solutions evaluate transient decay time spectra as a continuum superposition of Gamma wave packets and predict steady-state wavelength spectrum distortions driven by the IFE within a sub-second timescale. Validations across orthogonal and front-face spectrometer configurations show that the calculated spectra match MC simulations in lineshape. This model can serve as a fast forward engine to accelerate parameter space screening, provide early-stage detector design references, and act as a physics-constrained input for event vertex reconstruction algorithms.

articles.title: Australian and New Zealand Living Guidelines for Cochlear Implantation in Adults: A Consensus-Based and Evidence-Informed Guideline Adaptation Process.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cochlear implantation is an established, effective intervention for adults with moderately severe to profound hearing loss. Despite strong evidence of benefit, access to adult cochlear implantation in Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) has been limited and inconsistent, with variation in referral practices, candidacy evaluation, and outcome assessment. In 2023, the Global Living Guidelines for adult cochlear implantation were published and provided a framework for regional adaptation.

METHODS: The ANZ Hearing Health Collaborative (ANZ HHC) convened a multidisciplinary working group to adapt the Global Living Guidelines for the ANZ context. Over 18 months, the group used an ADAPTE-informed process and a modified Delphi approach across five virtual workshops, incorporating multidisciplinary representation, lived experience input, anonymous voting, peer review, public consultation and endorsement.

RESULTS: The adapted ANZ Living Guidelines provide consensus-based, evidence-informed recommendations across four domains: referral for cochlear implant (CI) evaluation, CI evaluation, candidacy recommendation and outcome evaluation. The recommendations retain alignment with the global evidence base while incorporating ANZ-specific service delivery, funding, and workforce considerations. Final endorsement exceeded 80% agreement across hearing health respondents.

CONCLUSIONS: The ANZ Living Guidelines for Cochlear Implantation in Adults are the first regionally endorsed consensus framework for adult CI care across ANZ. This adaptation process provides a transparent and reproducible model for contextualising global living guidelines while supporting equitable, standardised, patient-centred care.

articles.title: Exploring the Delivery of Advanced Practice by Critical Care Outreach Practitioners: A Multi-Site Mixed Methods Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To examine how advanced practice is interpreted and enacted by critical care outreach practitioners within rapid response systems.

DESIGN: A convergent mixed methods study.

METHODS: Patient-facing critical care outreach practitioners and service managers from two critical care networks in England were included. Quantitative data were collected between February and May 2025 using a cross-sectional survey. Qualitative data were gathered between March and May 2025 using focus groups. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively. Qualitative data were analysed thematically. Data were integrated using the Pillar Integration Process to generate meta-themes.

RESULTS: Six meta-themes were identified. Within this respondent sample, advanced practice was situated within a predominantly nursing-based workforce. Participants described variable education and development pathways, uneven access to funding and protected time, and variation in supervision and mentoring. Broader professional diversity was valued, while expertise was described as developing through exposure to complexity, uncertainty and decision-making responsibility. Progression beyond advanced practice was unclear, with implications for role development, legitimacy and sustainability. Across findings, advanced practice was delivered mainly through clinical activity, with leadership, education, and research less consistently embedded in routine practice.

CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that clearer career pathways may be needed, alongside consistent education standards, equitable access to development, and stronger supervision structures. These changes could support sustainability and fuller integration of advanced practice across clinical, leadership, education and research domains within critical care outreach services.

IMPACT: The study examined how advanced practice is implemented within critical care outreach and highlights potential gaps between policy and practice. It identified inconsistent role definition, variable use of frameworks, and limited protected time for non-clinical work. These findings have implications for workforce development, service design, and national policy. They support benchmarking critical care outreach roles against response and deterioration-focused teams internationally.

REPORTING METHOD: This study is reported in accordance with the Good Reporting of A Mixed Methods Study (GRAMMS) framework.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: A patient representative offered feedback on the research proposal and supported the development of research materials including the questionnaire and focus group topic guide.

articles.title: Polish Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Preliminary Psychometric Evaluation of the Left Ventricular Assist Device Self-Care Behaviour Scale: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
AIM(S): To cross-culturally adapt the Left Ventricular Assist Device Self-Care Behaviour Scale into Polish and obtain preliminary evidence on its psychometric properties in patients supported with a left ventricular assist device.

DESIGN: Cross-sectional, single-centre psychometric evaluation study.

METHODS: Following forward-backward translation, multidisciplinary expert review and cognitive debriefing, the Polish version of the 20-item scale was administered to 48 adult patients supported with a left ventricular assist device. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega. Item-level construct evidence was explored using multitrait scaling, inter-subscale correlations and exploratory known-groups comparisons with correction for multiple testing. Confirmatory factor analysis was not performed because of the limited sample size.

RESULTS: Monitoring and device self-care showed acceptable internal-consistency point estimates, whereas heart failure self-care was borderline. Item-level evidence was mixed, with cross-domain overlap for several items and inter-subscale associations provided only limited support for domain separation. Pronounced ceiling effects were present, particularly for device-related items. Education-related differences in heart failure self-care and total score remained significant after correction for multiple testing, whereas differences by support duration and therapeutic indication did not.

CONCLUSION: This study provides a developer-approved Polish cross-cultural adaptation of the scale with preliminary psychometric evidence. Larger multicentre studies are needed to establish factorial validity, temporal stability, external convergent validity and responsiveness before the scale is used as a validated longitudinal outcome measure.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: The translated scale may support structured assessment and discussion of self-reported self-care behaviours in clinical follow-up, but repeated scores should not yet be interpreted as reliable longitudinal change or treatment effect.

IMPACT: What problem did the study address? No Polish-language version of the scale had published psychometric evidence, limiting standardised assessment of self-care behaviour in patients supported with a left ventricular assist device. What were the main findings? Internal consistency was acceptable for Monitoring and device self-care and borderline for heart failure self-care; item-level construct evidence was mixed and ceiling effects in device-related items were pronounced. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The findings are relevant to nurses, clinicians and researchers caring for Polish-speaking patients supported with a left ventricular assist device by providing a standardised translated version for structured assessment and further psychometric evaluation.

REPORTING METHOD: This study adhered to the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) reporting guideline.

PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No Patient or Public Contribution.

articles.title: Patient-specific three-dimensional titanium plate versus conventional two-miniplate fixation for mandibular angle fractures: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mandibular angle fractures are clinically challenging because of their anatomical complexity and biomechanical loading. Conventional two-miniplate fixation requires intraoperative plate adaptation and transbuccal instrumentation. Patient-specific three-dimensional titanium plates are designed to conform to individual mandibular anatomy and may facilitate intraoperative fixation. This study aimed to clinically and radiographically evaluate patient-specific three-dimensional titanium plate versus conventional two mini-plate fixation in the management of mandibular angle fractures.

METHODS: Sixteen patients with recent mandibular angle fractures were randomly allocated into two equal groups (n = 8). Group I underwent fixation using a patient-specific three-dimensional titanium plate positioned according to the preoperative virtual plan, whereas Group II received conventional two-miniplate fixation. The primary outcome was functional recovery assessed by maximal mouth opening (MMO). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative time, postoperative pain, facial edema, postoperative occlusion, wound healing, and CT bone density measurements in Hounsfield units (HU). Clinical outcomes were evaluated on postoperative days 1, 7, 14, and 30, whereas bone density was assessed immediately postoperatively and after 4 months.

RESULTS: Intraoperative time was shorter in the patient-specific plate group than in the conventional two-miniplate group (40.00 ± 9.35 vs. 73.25 ± 11.22 min; P < 0.001). Postoperative pain was lower in the patient-specific plate group on postoperative day 1 (P = 0.015), while facial edema was lower on postoperative days 1 (P = 0.012) and 7 (P = 0.031). No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in maximal mouth opening, postoperative occlusion, Landry wound healing index scores, or CT bone density at the four-month follow-up. One patient in each group developed wound dehiscence, with complete healing after conservative management.

CONCLUSIONS: Patient-specific three-dimensional titanium plate fixation was associated with shorter intraoperative time and lower early postoperative pain and edema. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in the other assessed clinical and radiographic outcomes during the four-month follow-up.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07390734) on 29 January 2026.

articles.title: Application of appropriate use criteria, triage, and diagnostic yield of overnight transthoracic echocardiograms.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There are limited data to guide the appropriate use and triage of transthoracic echocardiograms (TTE) overnight when resources may be limited. The appropriate use criteria (AUC) assess whether a TTE is reasonable to perform, but do not address urgency or which overnight studies may be deferred until business hours. The purpose of this study was to describe the appropriateness, institutional triage classification, and diagnostic yield of overnight TTE studies completed during the study period.

METHODS: This was a retrospective review of inpatient TTEs completed between the hours of 17:30 to 07:00 from June 2021 to May 2022 at two academic centers. All studies were performed by sonographers on adult patients. Electronic medical records were reviewed to determine the context in which TTEs were performed. The indications were then rated using the 2011 AUC and the authors' institutional criteria for triaging overnight TTEs. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with new and clinically important TTE findings.

RESULTS: Of 251 studies completed overnight, 97.6% of indications were "always" appropriate according to the 2011 AUC and 91.6% met institutional "emergency/STAT" criteria. These two classifications reflect separate dimensions, appropriateness of performing the study versus urgency of timing, and are reported independently. New and clinically important findings were noted in 49% of the studies. In multivariable analysis, new and clinically important echocardiographic findings were associated with an elevated troponin (odds ratio [OR], 2.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.22-4.19; P < 0.01) and the absence of a prior echocardiogram (OR, 3.19; 95% CI, 1.67-6.01; P < 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: TTE studies completed overnight were nearly always appropriate by AUC, were frequently classified for overnight performance, and demonstrated a high diagnostic yield of new and clinically important findings; this study did not assess whether these findings changed clinical management. Future work should examine the clinical impact of overnight echocardiography and triage algorithms for directing limited resources. This study describes only TTEs that were completed overnight and does not capture the performance of the triage process among all overnight requests, including those deferred, cancelled, or not performed.

articles.title: Survival following 14% Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia: cerebral malaria and anaemic heart failure in a Nigerian toddler.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malaria remains a leading cause of mortality amongst children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. Complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria frequently presents with multiple life-threatening sequelae, including cerebral malaria, profound anaemia, and hyperparasitaemia. Although parasite densities exceeding 10% are independently associated with high mortality, achieving full recovery in a young child presenting with simultaneous extreme parasitaemia, deep coma, and severe malarial anaemia remains exceptionally noteworthy.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 20-month-old male from Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria, who presented with a five-day history of fever, cough, and diarrhoea, progressing to unconsciousness. Clinical examination revealed a Blantyre Coma Scale of 2/5, profound pallor, tachycardia (158 bpm), and tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory investigations confirmed an extreme 14% P. falciparum parasitaemia and a life-threatening packed cell volume of 8%. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis ruled out bacterial meningitis though an elevated protein level (71 mg/dL) supported the diagnosis of cerebral malaria.

MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOME: The patient was stabilised in the cardiac position to optimise venous return and alleviate signs of incipient heart failure, and was initiated on a multi-modal therapeutic regimen. Antimalarial therapy was commenced with intravenous artesunate (3 mg/kg), supported by two sessions of sedimented red blood cell transfusions and empiric IV Ceftriaxone. By the fourth day of treatment, the child regained full consciousness and was transitioned to oral artemether-lumefantrine. The patient was discharged in a stable condition on day seven with a recovered packed cell volume of 35%.

CONCLUSION: This case highlights the critical importance of the "24-h window" in treating severe malaria. The successful outcome confirms the efficacy of intravenous artesunate and the necessity of aggressive supportive care-including blood transfusion-in managing the severe triad of hyperparasitaemia, cerebral sequestration, and severe anaemia in paediatric patients within endemic regions. This report emphasises the need for public health initiatives that educate caregivers on the early recognition of malaria symptoms to facilitate prompt care. Furthermore, it reaffirms that urgent microscopic evaluation remains the gold standard for the immediate diagnosis of hyperparasitaemic cases in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Association of SLC2A9 and ABCG2 variants with hyperuricemia stratified by body mass index in a Korean population.
articles.abstract: Elevated serum uric acid (SUA) is a major risk factor for gout and has also been associated with chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders. Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci associated with SUA levels, the heterogeneity of genetic associations across clinically relevant subgroups in Korean populations remains incompletely understood. We performed genome-wide association analyses of SUA levels independently in two Korean population-based cohorts from the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES), including 8884 participants. Representative variants associated with SUA levels were further evaluated for their associations with hyperuricemia using multivariable logistic regression models. Stratified analyses and formal interaction tests were performed according to sex and body mass index (BMI). GWAS identified suggestive associations at the SLC2A9 locus in the HEXA cohort and genome-wide significant associations at the SLC2A9 and ABCG2 loci in the Ansung-Ansan cohort. Among the representative variants, rs4529048 in SLC2A9 showed associations with hyperuricemia in both cohorts (HEXA: adjusted OR, 1.72; 95% CI, 1.17-2.53; Ansung-Ansan: adjusted OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.25-2.02). No significant interactions with BMI category or obesity status were observed. These findings support the relevance of established urate-associated loci in Korean populations, while further studies are needed to clarify potential subgroup-specific genetic effects.

articles.title: Occlusal Macrowear Patterns and Initial Tooth Contacts in Patients With Temporomandibular Disorders and Asymptomatic Controls.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies investigating the aetiological role of occlusion in temporomandibular disorders (TMD) have primarily focused on forms of malocclusion, whereas occlusal wear patterns and initial tooth contacts have received comparatively little attention.

OBJECTIVE: This study investigated possible associations between occlusal wear facets, centric initial tooth contacts, and the tissue-specific localization of TMD-related symptoms.

METHODS: A total of 52 fully dentate individuals were included in this blinded study. Occlusal wear facet patterns of 24 individuals with symptoms involving the bilaminar zone of the temporomandibular joint and/or the mandibular retractor muscles (patient group: P) were compared with 28 asymptomatic individuals (control group: C). Individual interocclusal silicone records were obtained in a habitual pain-free mandibular position, documenting the first tooth contact during gentle closure. Occlusal Fingerprint Analysis (OFA) was applied to quantify and compare wear facet patterns and initial contact.

RESULTS: No significant between-group differences were observed for premolars or molars in any quadrant (p = 0.072-0.869). The P-group exhibited significantly more pronounced wear facets on maxillary incisors (p = 0.015-0.047). In 58% of the P-group, initial occlusal contacts were anterior, compared with 14% in the C-group, representing a significant between-group difference (p = 0.002).

CONCLUSIONS: Occlusal wear facets may reflect the power stroke. The position and orientation of initial contacts in a relaxed, pain-free mandibular position may be functionally relevant. Wear facets indicating premature incisor contacts may reflect increased retractor muscle activity and associated posterior mandibular displacement, potentially resulting in increased loading of the bilaminar zone. However, causal relationships remain unclear and require further investigation.

articles.title: Seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and associated factors among dogs in Cocody, Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Canine monocytic ehrlichiosis is an important tick-borne disease in tropical settings, but local epidemiological evidence from Côte d'Ivoire remains limited. This study estimated the apparent seroprevalence of Ehrlichia canis antibodies and evaluated associated host, management and preventive factors among dogs sampled in Cocody, Abidjan.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted from 1 November 2025 to 31 January 2026. A convenience sample of 150 dogs underwent clinical examination, rapid antibody testing and complete blood count assessment; owners completed a structured questionnaire. Univariable analyses and parsimonious multivariable logistic regression were performed. Model discrimination, calibration, prediction error, bootstrap optimism and decision-curve net benefit were evaluated.

RESULTS: Seventy-one dogs were seropositive, giving an apparent seroprevalence of 47.3% (95% CI: 39.3-55.3%). In the adjusted model (n = 149), tick presence was associated with higher odds of seropositivity (AOR = 3.94; 95% CI: 1.44-10.75; p = 0.007), whereas regular veterinary care was associated with lower odds (AOR = 0.20; 95% CI: 0.08-0.51; p < 0.001). Male dogs had lower adjusted odds than females (AOR = 0.34; 95% CI: 0.14-0.86; p = 0.023). The model had an AUC of 0.829, an optimism-corrected calibration slope of 0.896 and useful net benefit across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.17-0.80. Each one-point increase in a four-component prevention score was associated with a 49% reduction in adjusted odds of seropositivity (AOR = 0.51; 95% CI: 0.35-0.73; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial serological exposure was observed among sampled dogs. Tick control, supervised roaming and sustained veterinary care appear to be priority preventive actions. Because sampling was non-probabilistic and serology does not confirm active infection, population-level and causal interpretations should remain cautious. Nearly half of the dogs tested in this study in Cocody, Abidjan, carried antibodies against the bacterium that causes canine ehrlichiosis, a tick-borne illness. Dogs with ticks, dogs allowed to roam freely, and dogs without regular veterinary check-ups were most likely to test positive, while dogs receiving regular veterinary care and combined preventive measures (tick treatment, restricted roaming and informed owners) were markedly less likely to do so. Because the test used detects past or present exposure rather than active infection, these findings show how common exposure is in this population rather than how many dogs are currently sick; they point to tick control, supervised roaming and regular veterinary care as practical ways for owners to protect their dogs.

articles.title: Baseline frailty severity and survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive mechanical ventilation in patients with sepsis: a multicenter cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty has been associated with adverse outcomes during mechanical ventilation (MV). We evaluated the association between frailty severity, assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), and survival to intensive care unit (ICU) discharge without ongoing invasive MV.

METHODS: We analyzed adults with sepsis enrolled in the prospective, multicenter Korean Sepsis Alliance registry between September 2019 and December 2023 who received invasive MV on ICU day 1. Patients with CFS 9 were excluded. The primary outcome was survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. Frailty was defined as CFS 5-8 versus CFS 1-4 and was examined across increasing CFS severity using categorical and restricted cubic spline analyses. Mixed-effects logistic regression with a participating-center random intercept was adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, ICU day 1 Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score, and infection site.

RESULTS: Among 2,204 patients, 1,458 (66.2%) had CFS 5-8. The primary outcome was achieved by 1,120 patients (50.8%); crude rates were 52.9% in patients with CFS 1-4 and 49.7% in those with CFS 5-8 (P = 0.152). Frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of the primary outcome (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.73; 95% CI 0.59-0.90). Compared with CFS 1-4, the estimate for CFS 5 was close to the null (OR, 1.08; 95% CI 0.78-1.49), while the odds were lower for CFS 6, 7, and 8 (ORs, 0.68, 0.73, and 0.59, respectively; global P < 0.001). In spline analysis, the adjusted probability of the primary outcome decreased from 58.6% at CFS 1 to 43.3% at CFS 8 (P overall < 0.001; P for nonlinearity = 0.55). In pairwise analyses of ICU discharge status, frailty was associated with higher odds of survival with ongoing invasive MV versus survival without ongoing invasive MV (adjusted OR, 1.94; 95% CI 1.26-2.98); the corresponding estimate for ICU death versus survival without ongoing invasive MV was 1.22 (95% CI 0.97-1.53).

CONCLUSIONS: Among invasively ventilated patients with sepsis, baseline frailty was associated with lower adjusted odds of survival to ICU discharge without ongoing invasive MV. These findings support considering frailty severity when discussing recovery and care needs, but do not establish a treatment threshold or a causal effect of frailty.

articles.title: Genetic and pharmacological inactivation of soluble epoxide hydrolase ameliorates diet-induced MASH.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Pharmacological interventions for MASH remain limited, establishing the need to identify and validate novel therapeutic targets. Soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH; EPHX2) hydrolyzes anti-inflammatory epoxy fatty acids into less bioactive diols.

METHODS: We investigated the role of hepatic sEH in MASH using genetic and pharmacological approaches. Expression of hepatic EPHX2 was determined in liver samples from MASH patients and control subjects. We also fed control (Ephx2fl/fl) and liver-specific sEH-deficient mice (Alb-Cre; Ephx2fl/fl) either regular chow or a fructose-supplemented fast-food diet (FFD) for 27 weeks. We evaluated metabolic parameters and markers of liver injury, steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, as well as oxylipin profiling. Moreover, we treated FFD-fed control mice with the sEH pharmacological inhibitor TPPU in preventive, early, and late therapeutic intervention modalities.

RESULTS: We report significant elevation in hepatic EPHX2 in MASH patients compared with controls. Hepatic sEH deficiency improved glucose tolerance, with trends toward lower fasting glucose and fed insulin levels, independent of body weight. Remarkably, hepatic sEH deficiency ameliorated FFD-induced liver injury, steatosis, and lipid dysregulation. Additionally, sEH deficiency mitigated hepatic and systemic inflammation and fibrosis triggered by prolonged FFD feeding. Furthermore, sEH deficiency remodeled the hepatic oxylipin profile and preserved anti-inflammatory epoxides. Importantly, sEH pharmacological inhibition recapitulated these findings, significantly reducing liver injury and steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in the FFD across preventive and therapeutic intervention modalities, with the greatest effect in the preventive arm.

CONCLUSIONS: Together, these findings establish that genetic and pharmacological inactivation of sEH rebalances the oxylipin landscape, enhances the metabolic profile, and ameliorates steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis in a dietary mouse model of MASH. The concordance between the genetic and pharmacological approaches, along with the efficacy of sEH inhibition across preventive and therapeutic modalities, supports developing sEH-targeted interventions for MASH.

articles.title: Efficacy of iodine-125 seed implantation for differentiated thyroid cancer: a time-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative and single-arm studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To systematically evaluate the efficacy of 125I seed implantation for differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) and to provide evidence-based information to inform clinical decision-making.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, CNKI, WanFang, and SinoMed from inception to July 6, 2026, and queried ClinicalTrials.gov (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO]: CRD420261469053; reported per the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses [PRISMA] 2020). Controlled comparisons were pooled as risk ratios (RR) using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect or DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models; single-arm rates were combined by Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation with Miller back-transformation. Because efficacy evolves with follow-up, all pooled estimates were computed within each follow-up time point (3, 6, 12, and 24 months) without cross-time pooling. Quality was appraised with the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tools and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) checklist (single-arm studies). Egger regression was not performed because no time point contained 10 or more studies; funnel plots were inspected visually. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 1,205 records screened, 12 studies (5 controlled, 7 single-arm) met the inclusion criteria; at 12 months, the pooled RR for objective response rate (ORR) was significantly higher in the 125I seed group than in the control group (RR 3.06, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.18-4.27; I2 = 0%), as did the 6-month ORR (RR 2.33, 95% CI 1.16-4.65; I2 = 92.4%), whereas the single 3-month controlled comparison (sorafenib comparator) was non-significant (RR 0.79, 95% CI 0.59-1.06). Disease control rates (DCR) did not differ between groups at any time point. Single-arm pooled rates were 82.0%, 78.9%, and 69.4% for ORR and 95.1%, 88.4%, and 92.8% for DCR at 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively. Leave-one-out and exclusion analyses confirmed the findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Given the very low certainty of the available evidence, 125I seed implantation is a potentially effective locoregional treatment modality for DTC, with higher ORR than comparator treatments. However, given the limited number of studies, substantial heterogeneity, and short follow-up duration, larger randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Mismatched findings on ancillary examinations in virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis: pathological mechanisms and clinical significance.
articles.abstract: In this review, we group three mechanistically distinct categories of acute brain dysfunction after viral infection under the term "virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis": (1) viral encephalitis, caused by direct invasion and replication of neurotropic viruses in the central nervous system; (2) post-infectious autoimmune encephalitis, triggered by infection-induced central nervous system autoimmune responses; and (3) acute encephalopathy syndromes without direct central nervous system infection, resulting from systemic inflammatory storms or hypoxia. The three entities are grouped as a conceptual framework rather than an established classification because they all present as acute brain dysfunction occurring in association with viral infection and differ only in mechanism. The diagnosis of virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis relies mainly on ancillary examinations, including neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and electroencephalography. In clinical practice, ancillary findings are frequently mismatched: some tests may be negative while others are positive, and results can evolve with the pathological mechanism and disease stage. Recognizing these mismatches can help clinicians identify the possible mechanism of central nervous system injury and avoid diagnostic and treatment delays, and guide further testing. In particular, empirical intravenous acyclovir should be started promptly when herpes simplex virus (HSV) or varicella-zoster virus (VZV) encephalitis is clinically suspected. This article reviews the mechanisms of virus-associated acute encephalopathy and encephalitis, and discusses the common causes of such mismatches and strategies to manage them; the proposed framework is hypothesis-generating and is not intended as a validated diagnostic algorithm.

articles.title: Outcomes of Same-day Discharge Versus Inpatient Admission with Monitoring After Mastectomy ± Immediate Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The optimal discharge strategy after mastectomy, with or without reconstruction, remains debated. Same-day discharge has emerged as a potential paradigm shift in postoperative care, driven by Enhanced Recovery After Surgery protocols and value-based, patient-centered care. This study systematically reviews same-day discharge versus inpatient admission after mastectomy and compares outcomes in a meta-analysis.

METHOD: MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL were searched for studies comparing same-day discharge versus inpatient admission after mastectomy, with or without reconstruction. Primary outcomes were 30-day readmission and reoperation. Secondary outcomes included postoperative bleeding, wound infection, unplanned ED or clinic visits, and 30-day mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale and evidence certainty via GRADE. The protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024520256).

RESULTS: Of 6,377 studies, 18 non-randomized cohort studies encompassing 182,743 patients were included. Same-day discharge was associated with lower odds of reoperation (OR 0.49; 95% CI, 0.41-0.58), postoperative bleeding (OR 0.30; 95% CI, 0.14-0.64), wound infection (OR 0.65; 95% CI, 0.49-0.87), and 30-day mortality (OR 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19). No significant differences were observed in 30-day readmission (OR 0.96; 95% CI, 0.51-1.81) or unplanned ED or clinic visits (OR 0.62; 95% CI, 0.33-1.16). Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis supports the feasibility of same-day discharge after mastectomy, but underscores the need for high-quality randomized trials to validate these findings.

articles.title: Associations of peripheral neuropathy with patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures in women with breast cancer: from pre-chemotherapy to three or more years post chemotherapy.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: This study investigates numbness/tingling in hands and feet (peripheral neuropathy/PN) at long-term follow-up (LTFU) and quality of life (QoL) in women treated with chemotherapy for non-metastatic breast cancer.

METHODS: Women with stage I-III breast cancer were consented and responded to questionnaires prior to and during chemotherapy treatment and were then reconsented for questionnaires three or more years after treatment completion. Descriptive statistics for clinical and demographic characteristics, patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures, and patient-reported symptoms (PRO-CTCAE) are provided. Univariable and multivariable modified Poisson modeling, adjusting for age and body mass index (BMI), was conducted to describe PN and QoL measures at LTFU.

RESULTS: In a sample of 108 patients, average age at breast cancer diagnosis was 54 (range 24-77) and 27% non-White. At LTFU, 37% reported no PN symptoms and 63% reported mild, moderate, or severe/very severe symptoms. In adjusted multivariable modeling, the following pre-chemotherapy variables were associated with PN symptoms at LTFU: older age (RR 1.02), higher BMI (RR 1.02), and FACT-General measures for Physical, Social/Family, and Emotional well-being (RR 0.96 to 0.99). PRO-CTCAE symptoms assessed during chemotherapy were similarly associated with PN at LTFU: arm/leg swelling (RR 1.96), general pain (RR 1.71), myalgia (RR 1.95), and numbness/tingling in hands/feet (RR 1.63). In multivariable analysis of variables assessed at LTFU, significant associations were again similar to those observed for variables assessed pre- and during chemotherapy treatment.

CONCLUSION: Patient-reported outcome measures assessed pre- and during chemotherapy treatment can signal increased risk for PN symptoms at LTFU. Even mild PN at FU can have associations with QoL and function. These findings underscore the need for rigorous monitoring of PN symptoms and timely interventions from pre-treatment through long-term follow-up, when patients are scheduled for annual or routine clinic visits.

articles.title: Impact of Metabolic Syndrome on COVID-19 Outcomes and Gastrointestinal Health in an Urban African American Hospitalized Cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: African American patients have experienced disproportionate morbidity and mortality from COVID-19, and metabolic syndrome (MetS) has emerged as a key contributor to adverse outcomes in this population. Adverse COVID-19 outcomes in African American patients may reflect a syndemic interaction of metabolic, inflammatory, and gastrointestinal (GI) processes rather than isolated risk factors.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate how metabolic syndrome, gastrointestinal manifestations, and metabolic-organ injury markers collectively relate to COVID-19 severity and outcomes among hospitalized African American patients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,221 African American patients hospitalized with COVID-19 at Howard University Hospital. Patients were categorized as having MetS (n = 318, 26%) or not having MetS (n = 903, 74%) based on American Heart Association criteria. Demographics, comorbidities, clinical presentation, laboratory findings, treatments, and outcomes were compared between groups, with age-adjusted analyses performed given baseline age differences.

RESULTS: Patients with Metabolic syndrome were older (65.1 vs. 56.6 years) and had longer hospital stays (11.6 vs. 9.4 days) than patients without MetS. They also had higher ICU transfer rates (n = 77, 25.5% vs. n = 132, 15.5%; p = 0.001), greater prevalence of cardiometabolic comorbidities including cardiovascular disease (46.9% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.001) and chronic kidney disease (26% vs. 15.5%, p = 0.001), and more frequent GI symptoms (n = 127, 43.5% vs. n = 293, 35.4%; p = 0.01). Patients with MetS also required more intensive treatment, including higher rates of insulin use (66.3% vs. 21.8%) and glucocorticoids (45.1% vs. 36.5%), and showed greater laboratory evidence of organ dysfunction. In-hospital mortality was numerically higher among patients with MetS (n = 54, 17.5% vs. n = 110, 12.7%) but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.42).

CONCLUSION: Metabolic syndrome is associated with greater COVID-19 disease severity, critical care burden, and gastrointestinal involvement in African American patients, consistent with a syndemic interaction of metabolic, inflammatory, and gastrointestinal pathways. Targeted metabolic and gastrointestinal-focused interventions may help mitigate COVID-19 disparities in this population.

articles.title: FDG PET Biodistribution Patterns of Patients on GLP-1 Therapies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The use of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) therapies continues to increase, but there is limited literature on their effect on fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) biodistribution and minimal society guidelines. This study presents observations on a cohort of findings associated with GLP-1 use among patients undergoing oncologic FDG PET/CT, with attention to factors that may complicate image interpretation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 116 adult patients from a single academic center who reported use of a GLP-1. Medical information and demographic information were compiled, and images were analyzed for abnormal biodistribution. Statistical analysis was performed to determine association between these factors and atypical uptake.

RESULTS: This study found areas of altered FDG biodistribution in 75.9% (88/116) of patients with uptake noted in the esophagus, small intestines, large intestines, and muscles. Muscle uptake was seen in 21.6% of patients including one patient whose scan was considered nondiagnostic. There was no significant association between muscle uptake and age, sex, BMI, time since last GLP-1 dose, NPO time, blood glucose level, individual GLP-1 medications, insulin usage, metformin usage, other antidiabetic drug usage, systemic steroid usage, or GI symptoms. However, there was a significant association with gastric solid contents (p value 0.01).

CONCLUSIONS: This observational study found that patients using GLP-1 therapies exhibit multiple areas of altered biodistribution. Notably, increased muscle uptake had a statistically significant association with concomitant gastric solid contents. There was no association with fasting time (which ranged from 6 to 24 h in our sample). As patients were often on other medications, including other medications for diabetes, uptake may be related to a combination of factors. Further studies are needed to delve into the causes of altered biodistribution on FDG PET/CT performed on patients taking GLP-1s, with close attention to patients with muscle uptake, to inform future guidelines on image interpretation and patient preparation.

articles.title: Environmental Exposures and Diagnosed Dyslipidemia Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults in China.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Dyslipidemia is shaped not only by biological aging but also by historically structured social and environmental conditions experienced across cohorts and periods. Rapid urbanization, environmental degradation, and population aging in China provide a critical context for examining how life-course processes intersect with contemporary exposures to influence dyslipidemia risk. Drawing on Age-Period-Cohort (APC) analysis, this study investigated how age, birth cohort, and period-specific environmental conditions jointly structured dyslipidemia among middle-aged and older adults. Individual-level data were drawn from five waves (2011-2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). City-level environmental characteristics were compiled from the Google Earth Engine and China City Statistical Yearbook to construct measures of physical and social environments. Multilevel models incorporating APC specifications were used to estimate age, period, and cohort effects, and to assess associations between environmental exposures and the risk of dyslipidemia. Results reveal a nonlinear age pattern, with dyslipidemia risk peaking in the mid-50 s before declining in later life. Period effects indicate rising prevalence across survey waves, consistent with broader nutritional, behavioral, and diagnostic transitions. Cohort disparities were observed: later-born cohorts exhibited substantially lower risk than earlier-born cohorts (born in 1949 and earlier). Environmental exposures further structured these inequalities. Summer land-surface temperature showed a U-shaped association with dyslipidemia, while winter temperatures demonstrated inverted U-shaped relationships. Air pollutants were positively associated with risk in largely monotonic patterns. Importantly, cohort-stratified analyses revealed greater environmental susceptibility among earlier-born cohorts, suggesting cumulative disadvantage across the life course. These findings demonstrate how early-life conditions interact with contemporary environmental stressors to produce intergenerational disparities in cardiometabolic health. Integrating life-course perspectives with environmental governance may be essential for reducing chronic disease burdens in rapidly aging and ecologically transforming societies.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of Thunder-fire moxibustion with or without Yiqi Wenyang Tincture for cancer-related fatigue: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating symptom with limited treatment options. This study evaluated whether thunder-fire moxibustion (TFM) combined with Yiqi Wenyang Tincture (YWT) could provide additional benefit for CRF beyond conventional integrative management (control).

METHODS: In a three-arm randomized controlled trial, 255 cancer patients were allocated (85 per group) to TFM alone, TFM plus YWT (TFM + YWT), or conventional integrative management (control). The primary outcomes were the Revised Piper Fatigue Scale (PFS-R) total score and EORTC QLQ-C30 global quality-of-life score at week 6.

RESULTS: In conservative intention-to-treat analyses using baseline observation carried forward for five missing week-6 assessments, with ANCOVA adjusted for baseline score and HC3 robust standard errors, TFM + YWT had lower PFS-R scores than TFM alone (adjusted mean difference, -0.459; 95% CI, -0.793 to -0.126; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.021) and higher global quality of life (2.552; 0.589 to 4.515; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.033). Exploratory outcomes were analyzed in the complete-case set.

CONCLUSION: TFM, particularly when combined with YWT, may provide incremental clinical benefit for CRF; confirmation in larger trials with matched attention controls and longer follow-up is warranted.   TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2200063288, and International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR), ChiMCTR2200006558; registered on September 3, 2022.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Bedside Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score to Predict Mortality in Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sarcopenia is a common but often overlooked complication of advanced liver cirrhosis and is independently associated with decompensation and mortality. Because CT-based muscle quantification is not always feasible in resource-limited settings, we developed and validated a bedside Cirrhotic Sarcopenia-Nutrition Score (CSNS) incorporating anthropometric, ultrasonographic, and metabolic variables to predict 12-month morbidity and mortality in patients with end-stage liver disease.

METHODS: This prospective observational cohort study included 350 adult patients enrolled from December 2023 to April 2026. Patient selection was sequential and prospective into a development cohort (n = 250) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 100). All participants met sarcopenia criteria based on gait speed and handgrip strength. Six bedside parameters: triceps skinfold thickness, mid-upper arm circumference, mid-arm muscle circumference, mid-thigh circumference, ultrasound-derived psoas muscle thickness, and nitrogen balance were combined via penalized logistic regression to generate the CSNS on a 0-100 scale. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC and compared with MELD-Na and Child-Turcotte-Pugh (CTP) scores. External validation was performed in the independent cohort.

RESULTS: Nitrogen balance and psoas muscle thickness contributed most strongly to the final model. At an optimal cutoff of 61.2, the CSNS showed good discrimination for 12-month mortality in both the development (AUROC 0.816) and validation (AUROC 0.803) cohorts, with higher AUROC values than MELD-Na and CTP. High CSNS remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted HR 1.023; p = 0.002) and was significantly associated with major cirrhosis-related complications, including hepatic encephalopathy, acute kidney injury, refractory ascites, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding (all p ≤ 0.003).

CONCLUSION: The CSNS is a simple, radiation-free bedside tool that improves prognostic assessment beyond conventional scores and may support risk stratification in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: [Emergency critical care in the emergency department].
articles.abstract: Emergency critical care (ECC) provides early, ongoing critical care outside the intensive care unit (ICU). This narrative review describes organizational models and evidence in emergency medicine. Predominantly retrospective, single-center studies indicate that critical care is initiated earlier and that there are fewer subsequent inpatient ICU admissions. Neither a consistent mortality benefit nor the superiority of any model has been established. ECC supports early care, coordination of complex care pathways, and needs-based resource allocation, guided by the principle: the right patient in the right care setting.

articles.title: Plasma proteomics identifies insulin resistance signatures predictive of cardiometabolic disease risk.
articles.abstract: Insulin resistance drives cardiometabolic disease, yet its molecular signatures and tissue origins remain incompletely characterized. Here we define a circulating protein signature that enables scalable assessment of insulin sensitivity. We applied multiworkflow proteomics to plasma from 161 individuals spanning the insulin sensitivity spectrum defined by the hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp and identified 488 proteins associated with insulin sensitivity, capturing contributions from liver, adipose tissue and immune cells. A subset of these proteins shifted towards a more insulin-sensitive profile following an exercise intervention in men. We further developed a model combining 13 proteins, including IGFBP1, LEP, GDF15, PON3 and LDLR, with clinical variables (sex, HbA1c and the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio) to predict insulin sensitivity (R2 = 0.67). In ~20,000 UK Biobank participants, the model outperformed the triglyceride-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio in predicting type 2 diabetes (concordance index, 0.86 versus 0.74) and, unlike HbA1c, predicted hepatic, renal, cardiovascular and respiratory disease. In an independent cohort of 1,700 individuals, the model also showed greater predictive utility than fasting insulin resistance indices, including the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance. Together, these findings establish a tissue-resolved plasma proteomic framework for characterizing insulin resistance and provide a scalable approach to precision cardiometabolic risk stratification.

articles.title: Monitoring of pulmonary outcomes in paediatric cystic fibrosis patients treated with modulator therapy-a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Recently introduced CFTR modulator drugs have transformed the disease trajectories in people with cystic fibrosis. Children with cystic fibrosis, who would once have experienced progressive lung damage and pulmonary function decline from early life onwards, now, when treated with effective modulators, appear to have preserved lung structure and pulmonary function using conventional monitoring tools. However, since cystic fibrosis lung disease may still progress despite effective therapy, early detection of disease manifestation, disease progression, and the tracking of treatment responses remain crucial. Monitoring of lung disease in the current era of CFTR modulators, therefore, poses a fundamental challenge for cystic fibrosis clinicians and researchers. This narrative review summarises currently available monitoring tools for paediatric cystic fibrosis patients.

CONCLUSION: In children with cystic fibrosis receiving effective CFTR modulator therapy, spirometry remains an important component of pulmonary monitoring but may be insufficient to detect early or residual lung disease. Complementary approaches, including multiple-breath washout, oscillometry, and structural and functional lung imaging, can provide more sensitive assessment of pulmonary abnormalities and treatment responses. Further development of sensitive, non-invasive biomarkers of airway infection and inflammation, alongside evidence to guide the integration of these tools into routine clinical care, remains an important priority.
