WHAT IS KNOWN: • CFTR modulator therapy has transformed clinical outcomes in cystic fibrosis, and children initiating effective modulators early in life frequently maintain normal or near-normal pulmonary function. • Conventional monitoring with spirometry, particularly FEV₁, has limited sensitivity for detecting early or residual cystic fibrosis lung disease.

WHAT IS NEW: • Clinical monitoring of cystic fibrosis lung disease in children has shifted towards the use of technologies allowing for detection of subtle, potentially reversible, structural, functional, and inflammatory abnormalities that may persist despite modulator therapy. • Multiple-breath washout, quantitative computed tomography (CT), functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the chest, as well as emerging biomarkers provide complementary information beyond spirometry and are reshaping contemporary monitoring of CF lung disease.

articles.title: The impact of structured care versus usual care on service uptake and distress among distressed callers to a cancer telephone support service: outcomes of the START stepped wedge trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 45% of people with a cancer diagnosis and 44% of caregivers experience distress. Evidence-based guidelines recommend psychosocial screening with structured referrals in all settings.

AIM: To identify whether the implementation of a co-designed distress screening and structured referral intervention at Cancer Information and Support (CIS) telephone services resulted in increased referral uptake and reduced distress for people with cancer and caregivers versus those receiving usual care.

METHOD: As part of the stepped wedge trial, caller distress was measured using the Distress Thermometer (DT) and Generalised Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28) and uptake of referrals offered by the CIS were recorded. Referral uptake and GHQ-28 scores were assessed using generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) with fixed effects for the intervention period and structured care. Subgroup analyses were also performed to assess the difference between caller type (patients vs caregivers) and previous mental health treatment.

RESULTS: This study of 2348 patients and caregivers found insufficient evidence to support increased referral uptake or decreased distress in the structured care group, or a relationship between referral uptake or distress by caller type (patient/caregiver) (p > .05 for adjusted ORs in each comparison).

CONCLUSION: Although the structured care model did not improve referral uptake or distress, these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to a lack of intervention fidelity. Recommendations for improving intervention fidelity and future co-design research strategies are discussed.

articles.title: Threshold dynamics and spatial stability in an oncolytic virotherapy model with tumor-burden-dependent immune motility.
articles.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy can stimulate antitumor immunity while tumor maintained immunosuppression remains active, raising a spatial question that cannot be resolved by invasion thresholds alone: can infection and antitumor immunity persist, yet local tumor control still deteriorate? We formulate a reaction diffusion model for uninfected and infected tumor cells, antitumor immune cells, and immunosuppressive cells, in which the motilities of both immune populations depend on the total tumor burden. We prove global existence of nonnegative classical solutions and point dissipativity of the semiflow in a two-dimensional bounded domain. Then, we identify an infection threshold R V  and an antitumor immune threshold R T  . The threshold R V  governs infection invasion and uniform persistence, while R T  governs invasion and uniform persistence of the antitumor immune population once infection occurs. Under additional sufficient conditions, solutions converge globally to the corresponding infected or coexistence equilibrium. When the immunosuppressive population has a stronger motility response to tumor burden than the antitumor population, numerical simulations show loss of spatial homogeneity and deterioration of local tumor control. Thus, these thresholds alone do not guarantee effective local tumor control.

articles.title: Evaluation of pediatric patients diagnosed with food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Food Protein-Induced Enterocolitis Syndrome (FPIES) is a non-IgE-mediated food allergy typically presenting in infancy with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. The absence of specific biomarkers complicates diagnosis and management. This study aimed to evaluate demographic characteristics, trigger food distribution, clinical phenotypes, and tolerance development in pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES. This cross-sectional study included pediatric patients diagnosed with FPIES and followed at Ankara Etlik City Hospital between October 2022 and December 2025. Patients were re-evaluated for demographic data, trigger foods, phenotypic features, oral food challenge (OFC) outcomes, and tolerance development. A total of 63 patients were included (63.5% male), with a median age of 26 months (IQR 16-37). A total of 134 reactions were documented, with a median age at first reaction of 7 months (IQR 6-8). During first acute episodes, 19 patients required emergency care; three were hospitalized, and two required intensive care unit admission. Egg yolk was the most common trigger (51.5%), followed by cow's milk (21.2%), fish (18.1%), egg white (6%), and red meat (3%). Multiple trigger foods were identified in three patients. Phenotypic analysis revealed atypical FPIES in 10 patients and chronic FPIES in one patient. A total of 34 OFCs were performed for diagnostic confirmation and tolerance assessment. Reactions occurred in 11 tests, and eight required medical treatment. During follow-up, tolerance developed in 47.6% (n = 30) of patients, with a median tolerance age of 18 months (IQR 14-26). Tolerance was confirmed by OFC in 18 patients and by successful home reintroduction in 12.

CONCLUSION: In this single-center cohort, egg yolk was the predominant trigger food. Nearly half of the patients achieved early tolerance. Given the heterogeneous phenotypic spectrum of FPIES, increased clinical awareness and standardized management approaches are essential for optimal follow-up and prognosis assessment.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • FPIES shows geographic variation in trigger foods and clinical presentation, and tolerance acquisition may differ according to the culprit food.

WHAT IS NEW: • Egg yolk was the predominant trigger in this cohort, while fish-induced FPIES showed significantly later tolerance acquisition, supporting food-specific timing of follow-up and re-evaluation.

articles.title: A robotics- and machine learning-integrated workflow for discovering all-natural plastic substitutes.
articles.abstract: The global accumulation of nondegradable petrochemical plastic waste is driving the search for biodegradable substitutes derived from natural resources. However, discovering all-natural composite materials that match the optical, thermal and mechanical performance of commercial plastics remains challenging because traditional iterative optimization is inefficient. Here the workflow described in this Protocol accelerates the screening process by using automated robotics for liquid handing and machine learning to predict material properties. The procedure begins by commanding a pipetting robot to prepare a library of 286 nanocomposites. Basic physical properties of these products are used to train a support vector machine classifier that locates the decision boundary separating feasible from infeasible film compositions in the four-component system, thereby defining the feasible design space. Next, through 14 active learning loops coupled with data augmentation (for example, adding small random changes to the characterization data within the observed experimental error range), the robot fabricates 135 all-natural nanocomposites in a stagewise manner to construct an artificial neural network prediction model. The model is used to predict (1) the physicochemical properties of a nanocomposite from its composition and (2) which compositions are likely to have the desired, user-specified properties (for example, transparency or fire resistance). This protocol further details methods for model interpretation using Shapley Additive Explanations, validation via molecular dynamics simulations and model expansion to incorporate new building blocks. This hybrid approach takes ~2 months and enables the accelerated discovery of eco-friendly materials with programmable functions using components drawn from the generally recognized as safe database.

articles.title: Frequent mechanical bathing as integrative supportive care for patients with advanced cancer: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mechanical bathing is used to promote cleanliness and comfort in patients with advanced illness, but limited evidence and resource requirements restrict its use in palliative care.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether frequent mechanical bathing improves symptom distress and comfort among patients with advanced cancer receiving inpatient palliative care.

METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, patients were assigned to mechanical bathing every other day for 1 week or once weekly. Primary outcomes were symptom distress and comfort, assessed at baseline and every other day for 1 week. Generalized estimating equations were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Of 64 randomized participants, 42 completed follow-up assessments (19 experimental and 23 control). The mean age was 69.8 years (SD = 11.3), and 50.0% were men. Although total Edmonton Symptom Assessment System scores showed greater reductions in the experimental group at selected time points, the overall group-by-time interaction was not significant. Exploratory symptom-specific analyses showed greater improvements in appetite loss, depression, shortness of breath, and well-being at selected time points. After adjustment for multiple comparisons, early improvements in shortness of breath and well-being remained significant. Among participants able to complete the Hospice Comfort Questionnaire, comfort increased in the experimental group but decreased in the control group; however, the small subsample warrants cautious interpretation.

CONCLUSION: Frequent mechanical bathing showed potential benefits for selected symptoms and comfort, but the findings are exploratory, and evidence for reducing overall symptom distress remains inconclusive. Larger, adequately powered trials are needed to confirm these potential benefits.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06620146).

articles.title: Epigenetics in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic insights to personalized therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic immune-mediated disorder arising from interactions between genetic susceptibility, environmental exposure, microbial signals and immune regulation. Although genome-wide association studies have identified over 300 risk loci, known common variants and current genetic risk scores capture only part of disease liability and have limited ability to predict disease course or therapeutic outcomes. Environmental exposures acting across the life course are therefore likely to be substantial contributors of residual risk, yet mechanistic frameworks capable of integrating these diverse and time-varying influences remain incomplete. Epigenetic regulation provides a molecular interface through which genetic risk and environmental exposure converge, encoding durable yet environmentally responsive changes in gene regulation across immune and epithelial compartments. In this Review, we synthesize evidence from blood-based and tissue-based methylation studies to define reproducible regulatory signatures in inflammatory bowel disease, examine how the exposome shapes these landscapes, and evaluate emerging applications in diagnosis, prognosis and prediction of treatment response. We discuss how causal inference, multi-omics integration and single-cell technologies are refining interpretation and enabling mechanistically grounded stratification. Together, these advances position epigenetics as an important framework for understanding inflammatory bowel disease heterogeneity and informing clinical translation.

articles.title: Candidalysin: a decade of discovery.
articles.abstract: Candida albicans is a globally prevalent commensal fungus and a major pathogen of humans that causes both superficial infections and lethal disease. Identifying the biological mechanisms that advance our understanding of C. albicans colonization and pathogenicity, and that may lead to disease prevention, is of critical importance. A decade ago, C. albicans was found to secrete a peptide toxin called candidalysin, the first of its kind produced by a human fungal pathogen. Here we review the first decade of candidalysin research and focus on the critical function that candidalysin plays in commensalism, infection and disease. Specifically, we discuss its role as a classical virulence factor, how it activates host immune responses in different disease models and its emerging role as a commensal factor in the gut microbiota. We outline how this decade of discovery is facilitating the development of therapeutics and what research questions are waiting to be answered.

articles.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis exploring the effects of tDCS on metabolic syndrome parameters in adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome is a group of health conditions associated with obesity, increased risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and mortality. Interventions, including lifestyle changes, pharmacological treatments, and surgical interventions, have limited long-term efficacy, and do not adequately address some underpinning factors in overweight/obesity, such as cognitive/inhibitory control related to eating behaviours. There is emerging evidence for the successful use of neuromodulation techniques, such as transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), as potential adjunctive therapies for eating and weight disorders. This systematic review and meta-analysis have investigated the potential effects of tDCS on weight and metabolic parameters, in adults with or without excess body weight.

METHODS: In accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement, a systematic search of Embase, PsychInfo and PubMed electronic databases was performed to identify randomised clinical trials (RCTs) of tDCS which reported at least one metabolic syndrome parameter. Primary outcomes were weight, body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, blood pressure, blood glucose, insulin, and lipid profile.

RESULTS: A total of 28 studies (1129 participants) were included. tDCS protocols varied in stimulation sites, current intensity, and number and duration of sessions. Meta-analyses showed small but statistically significant weight loss (MD = -1.16 kg, 95% CI: -2.29 to -0.02; p = 0.04) and waist circumference reduction (MD = -0.67 cm, 95% CI: -1.14 to -0.19; p = 0.02) following active tDCS compared to sham. A non-significant reduction in food cravings traits was observed (SMD = -0.21, p = 0.06). Effects on glucose and blood pressure were variable.

CONCLUSION: The modest positive effects of tDCS on weight and waist circumference, nonetheless, highlight its potential clinical relevance for treating obesity and metabolic syndrome. Well-powered RCTs using standardised assessment procedures are essential to clarify the therapeutic mechanisms of tDCS and to identify optimal dosing for this population.

articles.title: LCK promotes proliferation while restraining effector differentiation of CD8+ T-cells.
articles.abstract: LCK is an SRC family kinase involved in the initial steps of T-cell receptor signaling and the regulation of thymic T-cell selection. While its role in thymocyte development is well established, its functions in peripheral T-cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we use whole-body and inducible Lck knock-out models to investigate the responses of LCK-deficient T-cells across three infection models and an autoimmune diabetes model in monoclonal and polyclonal setups. LCK is not essential for primary CD8+ T-cell responses, but LCK-deficient T-cells exhibit reduced antigen-induced proliferation and enhanced effector T-cell differentiation in vivo. LCK deficiency in effector T-cells does not compromise their tissue infiltration or functional capacity. Our results also indicate that LCK deficiency disproportionately impairs NFAT-dependent signaling among downstream T-cell receptor signaling pathways. T-cells deficient in the related kinase FYN also exhibit a modest increase in effector T-cell formation, suggesting that the two kinases may act additively to restrain this process. Our results reveal that LCK has two intrinsic roles in peripheral T-cell responses, namely promoting proliferation of these cells while restraining their differentiation into effector T-cells.

articles.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals.
articles.abstract: Understanding human motor control requires integrating cortical and spinal activity, muscle mechanics, and electrophysiology, which are typically studied in isolation. We present MyoGen, an open-source framework that unifies spinal circuitry, proprioceptive feedback, musculotendon dynamics, and multimodal electromyography generation. Using data-driven optimization benchmarked against human motor unit recordings, MyoGen produces motor unit population activity matching experimental discharge-rate distributions and variability across muscles. The framework generates decomposable surface and intramuscular electromyography, reproduces beta-band modulation of descending drive and its transformation into force, and implements key sensorimotor loop components. Dimensionality reduction of simulated agonist-antagonist electromyography reveals low-dimensional control manifolds consistent with recordings from able-bodied individuals and those with spinal cord injury. Here, we show that MyoGen provides a physiologically grounded simulation substrate, enabling systematic investigation of motor control principles, benchmarking of signal-processing algorithms, and exploration of experimentally inaccessible sensorimotor interactions.

articles.title: Circulatory failure requiring extracorporeal life support in ARDS: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionVenovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation is established support for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome with refractory respiratory failure, but some patients also have circulatory failure and receive cardiac or cardiorespiratory extracorporeal life support. Mortality in this group is poorly defined.MethodsWe conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of observed hospital and intensive care unit mortality according to the initial extracorporeal life support configuration, with certainty of evidence assessed using GRADE. Odds ratios are expressed for respiratory support relative to cardiac or cardiorespiratory support, so that a value below 1 indicates lower mortality with respiratory support alone.ResultsTwelve observational studies contributed data from 5,875 patients. Hospital mortality was lower with respiratory support (9 studies; odds ratio 0.59, 95% confidence interval 0.37-0.92; I2 = 62.5%; 95% prediction interval 0.21-1.60; low-certainty evidence), as was intensive care unit mortality (5 studies; odds ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.23-0.69; very-low-certainty evidence). The cohorts were clinically heterogeneous and rarely adjusted for shock severity, vasoactive support, lactate, cardiac function or general severity scores.ConclusionsBecause the configuration was selected in response to haemodynamic compromise and may also reflect centre practice, these pooled estimates describe an association and not the effect of an extracorporeal support strategy. Higher observed mortality in patients receiving cardiac or cardiorespiratory support is likely to be explained in large part by greater baseline illness severity and residual confounding.

articles.title: Real-World Initiation of Resmetirom and Recorded Incretin Exposure in the United States.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Resmetirom and semaglutide 2.4 mg are approved for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis but have not been tested together. We examined recorded incretin exposure among resmetirom initiators and the frequency and correlates of co-initiation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user cohort study used TriNetX US Collaborative Network health records of patients first prescribed resmetirom from 14 March 2024 to 16 July 2026. Among patients without incretin prescriptions in the prior 5 years, those with an incretin prescription 0-30 days after resmetirom (co-initiators) were compared with non-co-initiators using standardized mean differences (SMDs) and Mantel-Haenszel analysis stratified by overweight/obesity and Type 2 diabetes.

RESULTS: Of 6837 initiators, 76.6% had overweight/obesity (code or body mass index [BMI] ≥ 30 kg/m2), 44.0% Type 2 diabetes and 16.8% a cirrhosis code. An incretin prescription was recorded in 37.2%, mostly before resmetirom (33.8%; excluded from the comparison). Of the remaining 4524, 231 (5.1%) were co-initiators. Coded overweight/obesity (49.4% vs. 49.0%; SMD: 0.01) and Type 2 diabetes (30.3% vs. 33.1%; SMD: 0.06) were similar; co-initiation was about 5% in every stratum (Mantel-Haenszel odds ratios: overweight/obesity 1.08 [95% CI: 0.80-1.46]; diabetes 1.00 [0.75-1.34]). Co-initiators had higher mean BMI (35.3 vs. 33.0 kg/m2; SMD: 0.33) and were more often prescribed metformin (27.7% vs. 19.0%; SMD: 0.21).

CONCLUSIONS: Because more than one-third of resmetirom initiators had a recorded incretin prescription, mostly before initiation, trials of combined treatment are needed. Co-initiation was uncommon and not clearly associated with overweight/obesity or Type 2 diabetes, despite higher BMI in co-initiators.

articles.title: Assessing the Risk of Neonatal Opioid Toxicity from Breastfeeding: Challenge to the Pediatric Clinical Pharmacology Modeling and Simulation Community.
articles.abstract: The safety of maternal codeine use during breastfeeding remains controversial, largely due to debate surrounding the "Toronto Case," in which a neonatal death was associated with elevated morphine exposure following maternal postpartum codeine therapy. Critics have argued that this outcome requires an exceptionally unlikely combination of several factors. This review details the physiological and pharmacokinetic complexities of infant opioid exposure and toxicity in breastfed infants by reexamining assumptions underlying the physiology-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model frequently cited to challenge the plausibility of the Toronto Case. When advances in developmental pharmacology, pharmacogenomics, and maternal and neonatal drug disposition that have occurred over the past 15 years are considered, an integrated mother-milk-infant system emerges in which individualized risk assessment can be conceptualized as the convergence of multiple factors, each of which contributes to the overall risk for a given mother-child dyad. Future modeling and simulations must include the maternal and neonatal determinants that predispose specific breastfeeding mother-newborn pairs to excessive sedation and respiratory failure after codeine administration, and generate evidence to support safer opioid therapy in breastfeeding mothers, breastfed infants, and older children.

articles.title: Critical methodological vulnerabilities, data discrepancies, and mechanistic paradoxes in evaluating repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with Tai Chi for mild cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract: This correspondence provides a critical methodological and statistical re-appraisal of the recent clinical trial by Bai et al. (2026) [1], which investigated the combination of Yang-style Tai Chi and neuronavigated 1-Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for older adults with mild cognitive impairment and co-occurring sleep disorders. While evaluating non-pharmacological multimodal interventions in psychogeriatric populations represents a vital scientific pursuit, our in-depth evaluation reveals substantial vulnerabilities that undermine the trial's confirmatory conclusions. First, improper post-randomization exclusions of baseline-ineligible individuals resulted in an attrition rate exceeding 32%, fundamentally violating the intention-to-treat principle. Second, Table 1 displays critical computational discrepancies, including missing participant counts, impossible non-integer frequencies, and mathematically implausible test statistics (x² and P-values). Third, reliance on raw change-score analyses rather than baseline-adjusted ANCOVA leaves the behavioral findings vulnerable to Lord's paradox and regression to the mean. Fourth, the neuroimaging findings present a mechanistic paradox-wherein functional connectivity gains in the sham arm significantly exceeded those in the active group-compounded by non-independent seed selection ("double dipping"). Finally, the twice-daily high-density regimen incurs feasibility challenges, while evening inhibitory rTMS introduces chronobiological inconsistencies lacking objective sleep verification. We urge the authors to clarify these data discrepancies and recommend that the proposed synergistic effects be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Multimodal Ultrasonography for Preoperative Differentiation of the Tall Cell Subtype of Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Dual-Center Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate preoperative B-mode ultrasound (BMUS) and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features associated with tall cell subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma (TC-PTC) and to develop a Bayesian logistic regression model for differentiating TC-PTC from classical papillary thyroid carcinoma (C-PTC).

METHODS: This dual-center retrospective study included 177 histopathologically confirmed PTC patients, comprising 21 patients with TC-PTC and 156 with C-PTC. BMUS and CEUS features were compared between groups. Variables with a univariable p value <0.10 were considered candidate predictors and were subsequently assessed for redundancy and multicollinearity. Bayesian logistic regression with weakly regularizing normal priors was used to develop the final prediction model. Model convergence was assessed using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) diagnostics. Model performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC) estimation, posterior predictive checking, and 1000 bootstrap resamples.

RESULTS: The final Bayesian model included four predictors: isoechoic area, distance to capsule ≤0 mm, isoenhancement and early washout. All showed positive posterior associations with TC-PTC. MCMC diagnostics indicated satisfactory convergence and sampling performance. The posterior median AUC was 0.830 (95% CrI, 0.766-0.859). Internal validation using 1000 bootstrap resamples yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.822. The observed TC-PTC event proportion was consistent with its posterior predictive distribution.

CONCLUSION: The Bayesian model integrating BMUS and CEUS features showed good discrimination for differentiating TC-PTC from C-PTC. However, caution is advised when interpreting positive predictions given the limited positive predictive value. Further external validation is necessary before routine clinical application.

articles.title: Life-history trade-offs: the constraints underlying mosquito-borne pathogen transmission.
articles.abstract: Mosquito-borne pathogen transmission models typically assume that vector life-history traits vary independently. While survival, reproduction, and immunity are shaped by evolutionary forces to maximize fitness, life-history theory predicts that resource and physiological constraints create trade-offs among these traits. These trade-offs can shape pathogen development and transmission in nonintuitive ways. We argue that incorporating trade-offs into epidemiological and ecological modeling could improve predictive capacity for disease establishment and spread. Environmental variation alters resource allocation and, thus, trait covariation, so environmental variability may have cascading effects on transmission potential. This perspective unifies infection biology, local adaptation, vector-pathogen coevolution, invasion dynamics, and vector control under a common mechanistic framework to improve predictions of disease risk in a rapidly changing world.

articles.title: AI-supported screening for systematic literature reviews informing EULAR recommendations and points to consider.
authors: Working Group for EULAR AI-driven Screening
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to improve the efficiency of title and abstract screening in systematic literature reviews (SLRs) supporting European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) recommendations and points to consider, by developing and validating stopping criteria for active learning-assisted screening that achieve ≥95% recall (ie, sensitivity).

METHODS: Simulation studies analysed 40 development and 5 validation datasets (202,177 records) from completed and ongoing EULAR SLRs, using active learning models (h3, u3, and u4) in ASReview. Time-to-event analyses estimated the proportion of records that required screening to reach 95% recall and the minimum safe streak length (longest sequence of irrelevant records before reaching 95% recall). Empirical stopping criteria were derived, tested on independent datasets and evaluated for workload reduction and time savings.

RESULTS: Datasets averaged 4493 records (SD, 2851), with a mean of 67 (SD, 46) records included. The u4 model was optimal for balancing screening efficacy and computational efficiency. Target recall was achieved after screening 35% of records or reaching sequences of 15% nonrelevant records. A combined criterion (26% screened plus 10% irrelevant streak) provided an alternative stopping criterion. Validation met target recall. Screening workload was reduced by 67.1%.

CONCLUSIONS: Empirically derived stopping criteria using an active learning tool can substantially accelerate SLR screening while maintaining high recall (≥95%), allowing reviewers to skip about two-thirds of records during title and abstract screening. Artificial intelligence-assisted screening can substantially reduce evidence synthesis workload, thus supporting more efficient development of EULAR recommendations and points to consider.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Dual L/T calcium channel blocker exerts both antihypertensive and renoprotective effects in L-NAME-induced hypertension model" [Vasc. Pharmacol. 160 (2025) 107524].
What's Hot in Arrhythmia, 2026?
Association between polycystic ovary syndrome and asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is common in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and several plausible shared mechanisms may link the conditions, including metabolic dysfunction, systemic inflammation and hormonal pathways. We conducted a systematic review to synthesise the evidence, quantify any association, assess lung function data and identify gaps for future studies.

METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science Core Collection in April 2026. We included observational studies reporting asthma prevalence or lung function in women with PCOS. Crude and adjusted effect estimates were pooled separately using random-effects model meta-analyses. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2 statistics. Quality assessment was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools.

RESULTS: 13 studies (including over 28 million women, 11 cross-sectional and 2 longitudinal) were included. Of these, eight were assessed as moderate or high risk of bias. Meta-analyses showed that PCOS was associated with a higher odds of asthma in both crude (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.44 to 1.76, I²=72.0%, τ²=0.009) and adjusted analyses (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.40 to 1.77, I²=90.6%, τ²=0.007). The associations were not substantially different by PCOS or asthma ascertainment method. Only two lung function studies showed conflicting results.

CONCLUSIONS: PCOS appeared to be associated with asthma but this was driven by findings from cross-sectional studies which are at risk of reverse causation. Lung function evidence remains inconclusive. Future studies should prioritise standardised methods and longitudinal designs to establish temporality.

articles.title: Surgical management of spontaneous tendon rupture in rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Spontaneous, non-traumatic rupture of the extensor or flexor tendons of the hand and wrist is an uncommon disabling complication of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Management is mainly surgical, and decisions must account for perioperative disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) and biologic therapy. The evidence remains fragmented, with no existing systematic synthesis specific to RA. This review aims to estimate re-rupture, functional recovery and complication rates after surgery and to examine prognostic factors and perioperative antirheumatic management in relation to these outcomes.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, Embase and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature Ultimate will be searched from inception, without language restrictions, supplemented by trial registries and backward and forward citation searching. Case series, cohort, case-control and randomised studies reporting surgical management of RA-related spontaneous hand or wrist tendon rupture will be included; single-patient case reports will be summarised narratively only. Two reviewers will independently screen records, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool for comparative studies, the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for case series and the Risk of Bias 2 tool for randomised trials. Single-arm proportions will be pooled using a random-effects generalised linear mixed model, and comparative outcomes will be expressed as ORs or mean differences with 95% CIs, prioritising adjusted estimates. Pooling will follow prespecified clinical comparability criteria. Certainty of evidence will be rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethical approval is not required, as this review involves only previously published data. Findings will be disseminated through publication in an open-access peer-reviewed journal, presentation at hand surgery and rheumatology meetings and a plain-language summary shared with RA patient organisations.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261477222.

Comparison of the incidence and association of perioperative organ injury with surgical outcomes before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: a retrospective cohort analysis using the National Inpatient Sample database.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate and compare the incidence, pattern distribution and association of perioperative organ injury (POI) with in-hospital mortality and hospital length of stay (HLOS) in surgical patients before and during the COVID-19 pandemic.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: US National Inpatient Sample between 2016 and 2022.

POPULATION: 48 million adult surgical hospitalisations.

COHORTS: Pre-COVID-19 (2016–2019) and during COVID-19 (2020–2022).

PRIMARY AND SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. The secondary outcome was POI incidence and HLOS.

RESULTS: Cohorts before and during the COVID-19 pandemic were similar in ages, gender distributions and comorbidity burden. The incidence of POI increased significantly from 17.4% in the pre-pandemic period to 22.2% during the pandemic (p<0.001). Acute kidney injury (AKI) was the most frequent POI in both cohorts (13.0% pre-pandemic vs 16.2% during pandemic), while acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and liver injury (LI) were associated with the highest mortality rates (24.1% vs 50.6% for ARDS; 32.8% vs 36.6% for LI, before and during pandemic, respectively). After adjustment for confounders, the odds of in-hospital death in the presence of any POI increased from 3.8-fold (95% CI 3.77 to 3.82) before pandemic to 4.1-fold (95% CI 4.09 to 4.14) during the pandemic. Additionally, patients with increasing numbers of POIs demonstrated progressively higher in-hospital mortality and longer HLOS.

CONCLUSION: Surgical patients during the COVID-19 pandemic experienced worse outcomes, including a higher incidence of POI, prolonged hospitalisation and higher mortality. These findings highlight the association between POIs and adverse surgical outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and support efforts to improve recognition, prevention and management of POIs in future healthcare crises.

Differential roles of sit-to-stand and walking assessments in symptomatic and radiographic knee osteoarthritis: a secondary cross-sectional and longitudinal analysis of the osteoarthritis initiative and multicentre osteoarthritis study cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the classification and time-to-event discrimination of static parameters derived from sit-to-stand (STS) and 20-metre walking tests for symptomatic and structural knee osteoarthritis (knee OA).

DESIGN: Secondary analysis of two prospective US cohort studies.

SETTING: Data were obtained from the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) and the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study (MOST).

PARTICIPANTS: A total of 4796 participants from OAI and 3026 from MOST were included.

OUTCOME MEASURES: STS parameters included pace, completion ability and arm support. Walking parameters included gait speed, cadence, relative step length and walking-aid use. Logistic regression was used to assess classification of symptomatic knee OA, defined by the American College of Rheumatology (ACR) criteria and radiographic OA, defined as Kellgren-Lawrence grade ≥2. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine prediction of 96-month knee replacement. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), concordance index and bootstrap resampling. Principal component analysis and SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis was used to support interpretation.

RESULTS: Walking parameters showed better discrimination of radiographic OA than STS parameters in both cohorts (OAI: AUC 0.701±0.018 vs 0.668±0.017, p=0.0161; MOST: 0.714±0.020 vs 0.656±0.022, p<0.0001) and were more strongly associated with structural features, including medial joint space narrowing and osteophytes. STS and walking performed similarly for classification of symptomatic knee OA (OAI: 0.664±0.020 vs 0.643±0.021, p=0.1051; MOST: 0.719±0.023 vs 0.707±0.024, p=0.5621), although STS performed better for identifying pain on stairs in both cohorts (OAI: p=0.0220; MOST: p=0.0460). STS also showed stronger correlations with Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index subscores than walking. Prediction of 96-month knee replacement was similar for the two tests.

CONCLUSIONS: STS and walking assessments reflect distinct aspects of knee OA, with STS more closely associated with symptom burden and walking with radiographic abnormalities. Together, they may support more comprehensive functional characterisation in clinical and research settings.

articles.title: Coincidence detection in aspiny interneuron dendrites.
articles.abstract: Recent evidence for long-term potentiation (LTP) at glutamatergic synapses on GABAergic interneurons calls for close attention to the sub-cellular phenomena that underlie the induction of plasticity in aspiny dendrites. Neurogliaform interneurons exhibit large NMDA receptor-mediated currents, Hebbian LTP and supralinear summation of glutamatergic signals converging on dendritic compartments. Dendritic supralinearity in interneurons does not require sodium channels. Here we investigate the principles governing supralinear synaptic integration and its interaction with backpropagating action potentials in the synaptic plasticity context. We developed a biophysically realistic, multi-compartmental model of a murine (Mus musculus, male and female) hippocampal neurogliaform interneuron, with dendritic architecture and ion channel densities tuned to match ex vivo recordings. The interaction between synaptic inputs and action potentials was tested with patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon imaging of dendritic calcium-dependent fluorescence transients. Whether simulated glutamatergic excitatory postsynaptic potentials are clustered on a dendritic fragment or dispersed across the entire arbor, they summate supralinearly as assessed from the calculated somatic voltage response. Clustered inputs induce more pronounced local depolarizations and calcium transients than dispersed inputs. Action potentials generated at the soma backpropagate throughout the dendritic arbor but are attenuated at branch points. Coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials relieve this attenuation, further enhance dendritic depolarizations, and greatly potentiate calcium influx via NMDA receptors. Despite differences in dendritic anatomy and in the roles of sodium channels, the interplay of orthodromic and antidromic voltage propagation and resultant calcium signal amplification exhibits remarkable similarities between neurogliaform interneurons and principal cells.Significance Statement Neurogliaform interneurons are key regulators of brain circuit activity, yet the dendritic mechanisms that enable these inhibitory cells to undergo synaptic plasticity remain poorly understood. Combining biophysically realistic computer modeling with electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we show that coincident synaptic input and backpropagating action potentials strongly amplify dendritic depolarization and calcium influx in these interneurons. Although their dendrites lack spines and do not rely on sodium-channel-dependent dendritic spikes, neurogliaform interneurons nonetheless use computational principles remarkably similar to those of excitatory principal neurons. These findings advance the understanding of how inhibitory circuits support learning-related plasticity and may provide foundational insight into disorders such as epilepsy and schizophrenia, in which abnormal dendritic signalling and inhibitory dysfunction are implicated.

Towards gender equity in rheumatology: proposals for achieving gender equity.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Despite an almost equal proportion of male and female physicians in early career stages across Europe, women remain markedly under-represented in senior academic and leadership positions in medicine. We aimed to identify and prioritise actionable strategies to promote gender equity across medical and academic workplaces in rheumatology.

METHODS: During the tri-national ‘D/A/CH gender equity in rheumatology working group meeting’ (Germany, Austria and Switzerland), a structured two-phase consensus process was conducted. In the first phase, participants (n=22) identified key barriers and developed potential requirements to promote gender equality in medical and academic workplaces in rheumatology. In the second phase, following the consolidation of these proposals, an online post-meeting survey was conducted among all participants to identify and vote for the most relevant and feasible measures.

RESULTS: A total of 28 distinct strategies were proposed and reached full consensus (88%–100%) among participants. The main thematic items included: creating a fair and transparent working environment, flexibilisation of working hours, development of mentoring programmes and professional networks, increasing awareness of gender and diversity issues, improving compatibility of caregiving responsibilities and career progression, enhancing visibility of female ‘role models’ and advancing sex/gender- and diversity-sensitive medicine.

CONCLUSIONS: The identified consensus-based strategies provide a practical framework to promote gender equity and foster a fair, inclusive and supportive working environment in academic medicine.

articles.title: Study of 34 prospective pregnancies in women receiving IL-1 inhibitors for autoinflammatory diseases and comparison to unexposed pregnancies (GR2 study).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Interleukin-1 (IL-1) inhibitors are widely used in autoinflammatory diseases (AID) such as Still’s disease and monogenic inflammasomopathies, including cryopyrinopathies (CAPS) and familial Mediterranean fever. As these conditions frequently affect women of reproductive age and data are limited, concerns remain regarding anti-IL-1 therapy safety during pregnancy. We aimed to evaluate maternal and neonatal outcomes in women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception and pregnancy.

METHODS: This prospective observational study included pregnant women from the Groupe de recherche sur la Grossesse et les Maladies Rares (GR2) prospective cohort, spanning 76 French centres before September 2024. Women exposed to anti-IL-1 therapy during conception or pregnancy were selected. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes were compared with a 1:1 matched control group of unexposed women with similar conditions and with the nationwide 2021 French National Perinatal Survey.

RESULTS: Thirty-four pregnancies (three twin pregnancies) in 31 women were exposed to anakinra (n=30) and/or canakinumab (n=5) for Still’s disease (n=15), familial Mediterranean fever (n=15), CAPS (n=3), undifferentiated systemic AID (n=2), tumour necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome and recurrent pericarditis (n=1 each). Reported outcomes included infections (n=6), intrahepatic cholestasis (n=3), gestational diabetes (n=2), gestational hypertension (n=1) and intrauterine growth restriction (n=1). Median gestational age was 39 weeks with five preterm births between 32 and 37. One baby was diagnosed with laryngomalacia but did not require surgery. Paediatric follow-up (33 babies to 6 months, 30 thereafter for a median of 14.5 months (13–24)) confirmed normal infant development. Maternal and obstetrical outcomes did not differ between treated with anti-IL-1 and untreated with anti-IL-1 patients with AID.

CONCLUSION: Anti-IL-1 therapy, particularly anakinra, appears safe during pregnancy in women with systemic AID.

articles.title: Post-stroke atrial fibrillation detection with insertable cardiac monitors in older adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults bear the greatest burden of atrial fibrillation (AF)-related stroke, yet national data on AF detection after insertable cardiac monitor (ICM) implantation following ischaemic stroke are limited. We evaluated the cumulative incidence of post-stroke AF detection and ICM monitoring intensity among Medicare beneficiaries receiving ICMs in routine clinical practice.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries aged ≥66 years who underwent ICM implantation in 2017–2020 after ischaemic stroke, TIA or systemic thromboembolism without prior AF or oral anticoagulant (OAC) use. Outcomes were new AF and OAC-treated AF within 1 year, estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method with death as a competing risk. In a 90-day landmark cohort, we described monitoring intensity (interrogation encounters during days 1–90) and estimated associations between patient characteristics and subsequent AF detection using Poisson regression with and without monitoring intensity.

RESULTS: Among 9284 beneficiaries (mean age 76.1 years; 54.0% women), the 1-year cumulative incidence of new AF was 24.4% (95% CI 23.5% to 25.3%), ranging from 21.6% to 27.6% across alternative AF definitions. AF detection was higher among individuals aged ≥75 versus 66–74 years (27.7% vs 20.7%). In the landmark cohort (n=8230), 14.3% had no interrogation encounter during days 1–90, with higher proportions among black (18.8%), Hispanic (22.3%), frail (16.3%) and dually eligible (21.8%) patients. Monitoring intensity was not associated with AF detection and did not explain lower detection among Black (incidence rate ratio (IRR), 0.64 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.83)), Hispanic (IRR, 0.71 (95% CI 0.51 to 1.00)) and frail (IRR, 0.86 (95% CI 0.77 to 0.97)) patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Older adults undergoing ICM implantation after ischaemic stroke had a higher 1-year incidence of claims-based AF detection than reported in prior clinical trials. Monitoring intensity was lower among black, Hispanic, frail and dually eligible patients but did not explain the lower AF detection among black, Hispanic and frail patients.

articles.title: Clinical presentation and pattern of diagnostic work-up leading to specialist referral: a retrospective citywide analysis of 11 primary care centres in Turku, Finland.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart-related symptoms are common in primary care. We aimed to describe characteristics and symptoms among patients referred from primary care to secondary care cardiology clinics and to evaluate the diagnostic investigations performed and diagnoses made by cardiologists.

METHODS: This register-based study included 704 patients referred from 11 primary care centres in Turku, Finland, to cardiology specialists for heart-related symptoms in 2016. Data were collected from referral letters, primary and secondary care medical records and the angiography register.

RESULTS: The mean age was 63 (SD 16) and 62% of patients were women. Typical chest pain was documented in 13 (2%) patients among whom the use of preventive medications was scarce. In total, 1069 diagnostic investigations were performed in cardiology clinics. The most common diagnosis was unspecified symptoms and signs, recorded in 221 (31%) patients and more often in patients with chest pain/discomfort than in those without (p<0.001). Coronary artery disease was diagnosed in 56 (8%) patients, of whom 14 (25%) presented with non-anginal pain or symptoms other than chest pain/discomfort.

CONCLUSION: Typical angina symptoms were uncommon among primary care patients referred for cardiology assessment. Despite extensive diagnostic investigation, many patients did not receive a specific cardiac diagnosis.

articles.title: A systematic review of prediction models for tuberculosis infection and incident tuberculosis disease among adolescent and adult household contacts.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tuberculosis remains a leading global health threat, with household contacts of people with tuberculosis at high risk of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection and disease progression. Currently used diagnostic tools for Mtb infection, such as tuberculin skin tests (TST) and interferon-gamma release assays (IGRA), lack predictive accuracy for identifying individuals who will progress to tuberculosis disease. This systematic review evaluates and compares prediction models developed for Mtb infection and tuberculosis disease among household contacts to inform targeted preventive strategies.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD42024507409). We searched MEDLINE and Embase for studies that developed or validated diagnostic models for Mtb infection or prognostic models for tuberculosis disease among adolescent and adult household contacts. Extracted data were synthesised narratively. Risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST).

RESULTS: 10 studies were included, with 8 conducted in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and two in high-income countries (HICs). Five of the total 10 studies developed models for Mtb infection and 6 developed models for incident tuberculosis disease (one study addressed both). Common predictors included proximity to the index case, crowding, HIV status and age. Mtb infection prediction models demonstrated limited discrimination in LMICs (area under the curve (AUC) 0.61–0.71), with better performance in HICs (AUC up to 0.92). Tuberculosis disease models performed moderately well (AUC/C-statistics ranging from 0.70 to 0.76) and showed greater clinical utility than infection models.

CONCLUSIONS: Models predicting Mtb infection in high-tuberculosis incidence settings remain suboptimal, hence limited clinical utility, especially given that they target surrogate outcomes (IGRA and TST) with poor prognostic value for disease prediction. Tuberculosis disease models demonstrate better performance and practical relevance. Shifting focus toward models that predict incident tuberculosis disease and integration of clinical, epidemiological and biomarker data may enhance tuberculosis prevention strategies and improve targeting of preventive therapy.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42024507409.

articles.title: Xenotransfusion using red blood cells from genetically modified pigs: Current preclinical research status and clinical application prospects.
articles.abstract: Aging of population and emerging infectious diseases increasingly threaten stable blood supply, underscoring the need for alternative blood sources. Porcine red blood cells (pRBCs) offer notable advantages over human RBCs, including morphological and physiological similarity, established pathogen-free breeding systems, and freedom from ABO- and Rh-compatibility constraints. Recent advances in gene editing have enabled triple-knockout (TKO) pigs lacking the three major xenoantigens recognized by human natural antibodies, reviving interest in xenotransfusion as a potential solution to blood shortages. This narrative review examines preclinical and translational studies on pRBC xenotransfusion, focusing on immunological compatibility, in vivo survival, and adverse reactions across nonhuman primate (NHP) models, genetic engineering strategies, and emerging regulatory frameworks. In Old World NHP studies, TKO pRBCs corrected acute anemia but were cleared within 24-72 h, and retransfusion elicited acute hemolytic reactions from antibody formation. Rapid, multifactorial, immune-mediated clearance of pRBCs remains the principal barrier to clinical use, currently limiting application to emergencies such as acute massive hemorrhage. Future strategies include engineering pigs that express human complement-regulatory proteins and applying immunomodulatory regimens to prolong pRBC survival. Although a dedicated regulatory framework for xenotransfusion is still lacking, recent clearance of pig-organ xenotransplantation trials offers important precedent. Continued progress in genetic engineering and immunosuppression may extend xenotransfusion to emergency medicine and the care of patients with rare blood types.

articles.title: Standardizing Teach-Back Education to Reduce Heart Failure Readmissions.
articles.abstract: Background: Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of hospitalization among older adults and contributes substantially to preventable readmissions and health care costs. Although patient education can reduce readmissions, teaching practices are often inconsistent and may not address health literacy needs. Objective: This quality improvement initiative aimed to reduce 30-day all-cause HF readmissions by implementing standardized, nurse-delivered education using the teach-back method and a modified Heart Failure Stoplight Checklist Tool. Methods: Guided by the Johns Hopkins Evidence-Based Practice Model and the Institute for Healthcare Improvement Model for Improvement, a multidisciplinary team implemented a structured education intervention incorporating teach-back and a color-coded checklist. Nurses completed online and in-person training to ensure consistent delivery. Results: The 30-day HF readmission rate declined from 19.3% preintervention to 10% during the implementation and early postimplementation phases. Staff demonstrated strong posteducation knowledge scores but lower confidence in consistently applying teach-back. Conclusions: A standardized, teach-back-based education tool reduced HF readmissions and improved staff engagement. Ongoing mentoring and structured workflows support sustainability. Implications for Nursing: Nurses play a key role in reducing HF readmissions through consistent, literacy-sensitive communication. Standardized tools and teach-back methods enhance patient understanding, self-care, and nursing contributions to quality outcomes.

articles.title: [Willingness to participate in clinical trials and ethical dilemmas among patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy].
articles.journal: Zhejiang da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Zhejiang University. Medical sciences
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the awareness of and willingness to participate in drug clinical trials among patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and their families, to analyze the ethical dilemmas these participants face and the characteristics of these dilemmas.

METHODS: A mixed-methods design combining a cross-sectional survey and qualitative research was used, with participants recruited through domestic DMD patient organizations. Based on 3,102 valid questionnaires, descriptive statistics and rank analysis were used to examine patients' and families' awareness, willingness to participate, and influencing factors. Thirty-seven semi-structured interviews were thematically analyzed to further explore the underlying ethical dilemmas.

RESULTS: Three typical ethical dilemmas were identified. First, the quality of informed consent was suboptimal: patients and families had limited awareness of emerging therapies, yet 76.15% were willing to participate in clinical trials, indicating a prominent risk of therapeutic misconception. In addition, 60.80% of respondents based their decisions on the authority of the trial institution, which may undermine the prudence of informed decision-making because of excessive trust. Only 38.36% of family members considered the wishes of the minor patients during decision-making, indicating insufficient protection of the rights and interests of child participants. Second, the risk-benefit trade-off showed signs of distortion: although 86.65% of respondents identified trial drug safety as the primary consideration, the risk acceptance threshold was passively raised under the dual constraints of irreversible disease progression and insufficient payment capacity in 94.90% of families. Third, equity in trial participation was inadequate: 56.61% of respondents were constrained by the location of trial institutions, and patients in underdeveloped areas faced both geographic and economic barriers to participation.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with DMD participating in drug clinical trials face three major ethical dilemmas: suboptimal quality of informed consent, distortion in the risk-benefit trade-off, and inequitable distribution of trial resources. These dilemmas essentially result from the combined effects of the irreversible progression of DMD, the uneven distribution of clinical research resources, and the multiple vulnerabilities of the patient population.

articles.title: Continuous vs stent-removal antibiotic prophylaxis after cystectomy: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the efficacy and microbiological consequences of continuous prophylaxis (CP) vs stent-removal prophylaxis (SRP) in patients undergoing cystectomy with urinary diversion.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 223 patients undergoing cystectomy with urinary diversion from 2015 to 2024. All patients received identical perioperative intravenous prophylaxis (cefazolin and metronidazole for up to 48 h). Groups were defined by the subsequent oral strategy: SRP (n = 119), a 3-day course of amoxicillin-clavulanate around stent removal, vs CP (n = 104), amoxicillin-clavulanate given continuously from completion of intravenous prophylaxis until the day after stent removal. Primary endpoints included surgical site infection (SSI), urinary tract infection (UTI), readmission rates, and new isolation of organisms not covered by the prophylactic regimen. Multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression models adjusted for pre-specified confounders.

RESULTS: The CP group had a higher median Charlson Comorbidity Index (4 vs 3, P = 0.023). Despite a median antibiotic duration of 16.0 (CP) vs 7.0 days (SRP) (P < 0.001), no significant differences were observed in UTI (27.9% vs 31.9%, P = 0.6), SSI (28.8% vs 28.6%, P > 0.9), or 30-day readmission (26.0% vs 29.4%, P = 0.7). CP was associated with significantly higher isolation of new organisms not covered by the prophylactic regimen (32.7% vs 19.3%, P = 0.031) and new Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolation (15.4% vs 2.5%, P < 0.001). CP was associated with postoperative Pseudomonas isolation after adjustment using Firth's penalised logistic regression (odds ratio 5.50, 95% confidence interval 1.77-22.36, P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: Continuous prophylaxis was not associated with fewer infectious complications or readmissions but was associated with increased isolation of organisms not covered by prophylaxis, particularly P. aeruginosa. Given the non-randomised historical before-after design, non-overlapping study periods, and baseline differences, these findings remain hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: "No Room for Doubt": Evidence-Based Strategies of Operating Room Nurses to Maintain the Sterile Field in the Event of a Delay: A Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Research and theory for nursing practice
articles.abstract: Background: Delays at the start of a case in the operating room (OR) disrupt the surgical workflow, hinder sterility, increase the risk of infection, and threaten patient safety. Purpose: This study aimed to identify evidence-based strategies used by OR registered nurses to maintain a sterile field during delays in the start of procedures. Methods: Transcripts from in-depth interviews with 15 OR registered nurses were analyzed using descriptive phenomenological analysis, and themes and subthemes were systematically generated. Results: The analysis identified five main themes: (a) experiences with practices for maintaining a sterile field; (b) reasons for case start delays; (c) perceptions and safety awareness regarding sterility; (d) training gaps, needs, and recommendations; and (e) institutional systems and suggestions for improvement. These themes comprised 16 subthemes that reflected participants' experiences, perceived challenges, and recommendations for improving sterile field management during case start delays. Implications for Practice: These findings support the development of evidence-based institutional protocols for sterile field management during case start delays. Health care institutions should implement structured communication processes, including checklists and safety briefings, to strengthen interdisciplinary teamwork and promote consistent and sterile practices. Regular scenario-based simulation training, particularly for newly employed OR registered nurses, should be incorporated into continuing education programs in the future. In addition, system-level analyses of the causes of surgical delays and proactive management of patient safety risks may improve the perioperative workflow, strengthen sterile field maintenance, and enhance patient safety.

articles.title: CD45RA-depleted T-cell therapy for EBV infections after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation: a multicenter retrospective study.

Peptides and Obesity: Evaluating Intranasal Administration of Peptides for Therapeutic Potential.
articles.journal: Obesity reviews : an official journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
articles.abstract: Obesity is a complex global health issue characterized by an imbalance in energy homeostasis and associated with significant health risks, including cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and cancer. While various therapeutic approaches exist, peptide-based treatments have emerged as promising candidates due to their specificity and reduced side effects. Because many of the mechanisms are centrally regulated in the brain, effective intervention requires peptides with good brain penetration or alternative delivery strategies. In this context, this review explores the potential of intranasal delivery of therapeutic peptide candidates for obesity management, highlighting its advantages in bypassing the blood-brain barrier, targeting central pathways regulating appetite and energy expenditure, and minimizing systemic exposure, while also considering the translational limitations of this delivery route. The review analyses established and emerging peptides, including leptin, GLP-1 analogs, and oxytocin, focusing on their central mechanisms of action, specifically their ability to target the brain. It highlights how these peptides regulate energy homeostasis, appetite, and metabolism through direct activation of neural circuits in the hypothalamus, brainstem, and other key regions involved in obesity management. Furthermore, it evaluates the prospects of intranasal peptide therapeutics as an innovative strategy in obesity treatment, addressing both the opportunities and limitations in the context of clinical and preclinical evidence. Continued research and technological advancements are essential to optimize peptide formulations and delivery systems, ensuring efficacy, safety, and patient compliance in combating the obesity epidemic.

articles.title: [German-Speaking Society for Reconstructive Microsurgery (GSRM) Consensus Statement:Orthoplastic Surgery for Primary Reconstruction of Complex Extremity Injuries -Timing, Strategy, and Technical Aspects].
articles.journal: Handchirurgie, Mikrochirurgie, plastische Chirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Handchirurgie : Organ der Deutschsprachigen Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Mikrochirurgie der Peripheren Nerven und Gefasse : Organ der V...
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The goal of acute orthoplastic care is to ensure functional limb salvage through stable bony fixation and soft-tissue reconstruction. Despite the reported benefits of early interdisciplinary planning and treatment, structural deficits and the limited availability of microsurgical expertise in the DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) continue to hinder patient care.

METHODS AND OBJECTIVES: At its 46th annual meeting in November 2025, an expert panel of the GSRM analyzed procedural limitations and formulated cross-disciplinary recommendations to optimize acute orthoplastic care. In a two-step process, the committee of 132 experts first defined five core questions regarding patient navigation and centralization, quality assurance of interdisciplinary debridements, the establishment of interdisciplinary limb boards, timeframes for bony and soft-tissue reconstruction, and the interval between osteosynthesis and flap-based reconstruction. Subsequently, five corresponding consensus recommendations were unanimously adopted.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: The five consensus recommendations include directed navigation of patients to designated centers with sufficient expertise and interdisciplinary team meetings, the a priori interdisciplinary nature of debridements, and the earliest possible definitive management of open fractures within a maximum of 10 days - whereby osteosynthesis and soft-tissue reconstruction should be achieved in a single- or delayed single-stage procedure within 24 hours.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: 1. Primary care of open limb fractures in supra-regional trauma centers with 24/7 availability of plastic-reconstructive, microsurgical, and vascular surgical expertise.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: 2. A priori interdisciplinary initial debridements of open limb fractures involving a plastic surgeon, at the latest before definitive osteosynthesis.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: 3. Establishment of interdisciplinary limb boards for the collaborative development and definition of interdisciplinary treatment plans.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: 4. Earliest possible definitive management of open limb fractures via fixation and coverage, no later than 10 days post-injury.

RESULTS AND CONSENSUS RECOMMENDATIONS: 5. Immediate or delayed single-stage execution of both soft-tissue reconstruction and definitive osteosynthesis within a maximum of 24 hours.

articles.title: Risk factors for antepartum venous thromboembolism in pregnant people with sickle cell disease.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a thrombophilia exacerbated by pregnancy. However, there is not strong evidence for thromboprophylaxis, perhaps because most data addressing pregnancy-related thrombosis in SCD is limited by derivation from administrative datasets. We studied venous thromboembolism (VTE) in a retrospective cohort of pregnant people with SCD who delivered singleton pregnancies at two academic centres between 1990 and 2021. Among 289 pregnancies to 197 SCD subjects, 6% had VTE. We compared characteristics of the first study pregnancy in which a VTE occurred (cases) to the first study pregnancy in subjects without pregnancy-related VTE (controls). Preconception complications associated with VTE were history of VTE (cases: 33% [n = 5/15] vs. controls: 4% [n = 7/182], p < 0.001), acute chest syndrome (ACS) (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 37% [n = 68/182], p = 0.001) and acute care for vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC) in the year before pregnancy (80% [n = 12/15] vs. 43% [n = 70/182], p = 0.006). Prenatal complications associated with VTE were ACS (47% [n = 7/15] vs. 10% [n = 19/182], p < 0.001) and VOC (93% [n = 14/15] vs. 65% [n = 119/182], p = 0.026). Fetal outcomes associated with VTE included gestational age at delivery (median [IQR] 37.0 [34.0-38.1] weeks vs. 38.3 [36.9-39.3], p = 0.004). Studies are needed to establish interventions that attenuate VTE risk and define prophylactic anti-coagulation parameters for this high-risk population.

articles.title: Externally anchored fully covered metal stents with plastic stent versus uncovered metal stents for unresectable distal malignant biliary obstruction: a multicenter randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Self-expandable metal stents (SEMS) are commonly used to treat malignant biliary obstruction (MBO). External plastic stent anchoring for fully covered SEMS (FCSEMS-EPS) has shown potential to improve stent patency; however, randomized evidence comparing this strategy with uncovered SEMS (USEMS) is limited.

METHODS: This multicenter trial was conducted at nine tertiary referral centers in South Korea. Patients were enrolled from October 2021 to February 2024 and followed for 12 months after stent placement. Those with unresectable distal MBO were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either FCSEMS-EPS or USEMS. The primary outcome was biliary stent dysfunction. Time-to-event analyses were performed using time to stent dysfunction within a competing risk framework.

RESULTS: 113 patients were enrolled, of whom 99 were included in the final analysis (FCSEMS-EPS 48; USEMS 51). Stent dysfunction occurred less frequently in the FCSEMS-EPS group compared with the USEMS group (27.1% vs. 49.0%; P = 0.04). The cumulative incidence of stent dysfunction at 6 months was lower in the FCSEMS-EPS group (21.1% vs. 29.8%; Gray's test, P = 0.03). In multivariable competing risk analysis, FCSEMS-EPS was independently associated with a lower risk of stent dysfunction (subdistribution hazard ratio 0.44, 95%CI 0.21-0.90; P = 0.03). Procedure-related adverse events and overall survival did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: FCSEMS-EPS significantly reduced stent dysfunction compared with USEMS without increasing adverse events, supporting its effectiveness and safety as long-term biliary drainage in unresectable MBO.

articles.title: Longitudinal Changes in Left Atrial Stiffness Index Improve Risk Stratification in Patients with Hypertension.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography : official publication of the American Society of Echocardiography
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffness index is a non-invasive echocardiographic parameter reflecting left ventricular filling pressure; however, its prognostic significance in hypertension remains unclear. We aimed to assess the prognostic value of the longitudinal change in LA stiffness index in patients with hypertension.

METHODS: We analyzed 1,442 hypertensive patients from the STRATS-HHD registry who underwent echocardiography including LA and left ventricular (LV) strain at baseline and 6-18 months. Patients were categorized into four groups according to longitudinal changes in LA stiffness index: Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High, and High-High, using a data-driven prognostic cut-off of 0.63 (Low <0.63; High ≥0.63). The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) and cardiovascular death, and secondary outcomes included HHF and incident atrial fibrillation.

RESULTS: Among 1,442 patients, 996 (69.1%) were classified as Low-Low, 173 (12.0%) as High-Low, 91 (6.3%) as Low-High, and 182 (12.6%) as High-High. Over 5 years, Low-High (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.175, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.048-4.515, P=0.037) and High-High (aHR 2.935, 95% CI 1.697-5.076, P<0.001) groups were associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome, whereas the High-Low group showed a similar risk to the Low-Low group. Similar trends were observed for HHF and incident atrial fibrillation. Beyond clinical factors and LV mass index, LA stiffness index provided greater incremental prognostic value than individual echocardiographic markers, including LASr and E/e'.

CONCLUSION: LA stiffness index was associated with clinical outcomes in hypertension, and longitudinal changes provided additional prognostic information. Trajectory assessment may refine risk stratification.

articles.title: Impact to Healthcare-Associated Viral Gastroenteritis Infection Rate Using Different Visitation Models in a Pediatric Hospital.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric healthcare-associated viral gastroenteritis infections (HA-VGI) contribute to morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and outbreaks. Visitor-related transmission is a recognized risk factor; associations between visitation models and HA-VGI incidence remain understudied.

METHODS: HA-VGI rates were compared across four visitation models: (Period 1) seasonal visitation, visitors <13 years restricted December 1-April 30; (Period 2) two legally authorized representatives (LAR) permitted, mandatory masking; (Period 3) masking with an LAR-approved 10-person visitor list, including siblings; (Period 4) identical visitation model without masking (December 2017-June 2025). HA-VGI was defined as gastroenteritis on or after hospital day 3. Changepoint analysis, interrupted time series modeling, nonparametric comparisons, and multivariable linear regression assessed differences across periods. Regression models adjusted for community GI viral activity and calendar month. Rates were compared by unit and pathogen.

RESULTS: Median HA-VGI rates declined significantly during Period 2 compared with Period 1 (0.93 vs. 5.14 per 10,000 patient days; p<0.001). Although rates increased in Period 3, they remained below Period 1. Adjusted regression demonstrated lower rates during Periods 2 and 3 than during Period 1 (β=-3.01 and -3.07, respectively; both p<0.001). Period 4 did not significantly differ from Period 1. Community GI viral activity was independently associated with HA-VGI rates (β=5.94; p=0.002). ICU rates were lower than non-ICU rates; norovirus predominated.

CONCLUSIONS: Year-round sibling visitation with visitor limits was not associated with increased HA-VGI incidence compared to seasonal visitation. Mandatory masking was associated with lower HA-VGI rates independent of community viral activity and seasonality and may provide protection during increased GI viral circulation.

articles.title: Nudging hand hygiene behaviour among hospital visitors in Greece.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hand hygiene is a cornerstone of infection prevention and reducing healthcare-associated infections, yet compliance among hospital visitors remains low. Nudging may encourage preventive behaviours without restricting choice. This study evaluated two poster-based visual nudges to improve visitor hand hygiene compliance.

METHODS: A quasi-experimental observational study was conducted at a hospital entrance in Athens, Greece. Visitors' hand hygiene behaviour was assessed through direct, unobtrusive observation across five phases: baseline, Intervention 1, Post-intervention 1, Intervention 2, and Post-intervention 2. Each phase lasted four days. Sanitiser use was analysed using chi-square tests, effect size measures, and generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 24,651 visitors were observed. Sanitiser use increased from 11.39% at baseline to 38.60% during Intervention 1 and 38.21% during Intervention 2 (both p < 0.05). Following poster removal, compliance returned to baseline levels in both post-intervention phases. No difference was observed between poster designs. GLMM analysis identified poster presence as the strongest predictor of sanitiser use (OR = 4.98, 95% CI: 4.67-5.32, p < 0.05).

DISCUSSION: Poster-based nudging improved visitor hand hygiene compliance, but effects were not maintained after removal.

CONCLUSION: Visual nudging may support hospital infection prevention programmes. Nevertheless, the non-randomized observational design, inability to identify repeat visitors, and potential influence of external contextual factors should be considered when interpreting these findings.

articles.title: Structure, Staffing, and Strain: Lessons from U.S. Infection Preventionists on Building Resilient Systems Post-COVID-19.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic placed unprecedented strain on infection prevention and control (IPC) departments. Infection Preventionists (IPs) were required to sustain routine activities while managing crisis-driven demands, exposing gaps in staffing, communication, preparedness, and organizational support. First-hand accounts from IPC professionals remain limited and often focus on the peak-pandemic timeframe. This study examines retrospective lessons learned to inform future preparedness and response efforts.

METHODS: We analyzed responses to an open-ended item from the 2023 AHRQ-funded Prevention of Infection Through Appropriate Staffing (PITAS) survey.
