However, in multivariable analysis adjusting for clinical parameters the associations did not remain significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons. Carriers of at least one polymorphic MMP14 rs1042703 allele had nominally higher HbA1c levels (P = 0.025) and more macrovascular complications (OR = 2.05 (1.06-3.96), P = 0.033). After adjustment for multiple comparisons, the association of rs1042703 heterozygotes with macrovascular complications was at the pre-specified significance threshold in univariable analysis (OR = 2.28 (1.17-4.44), P = 0.015) and statistically significant after adjustment for clinical covariates (OR = 2.50 (1.22-5.13), P = 0.012). In haplotype analysis, MMP14 CGC haplotype was significantly associated with an increased risk of macrovascular complications (OR = 4.02 (1.60-10.09), P = 0.003). STRING network analysis identified interactions with proteins involved in ECM remodeling, collagen turnover and inflammatory signaling. While several associations were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons, MMP14 genetic variability might contribute to glycemic control and vascular complications in T2D. Observed findings support a potential role of ECM remodeling pathways in diabetic vascular pathology and warrant further investigation of MMP14 polymorphisms in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: Multi-cohort external validation of personalized uncertainty-aware short-term glucose forecasting in type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To determine whether a personalized, uncertainty-aware glucose-forecasting tool provides clinically acceptable 30-minute glucose forecasts in people with type-1-diabetes (T1D) when applied to populations it was not trained on, without patient-specific retraining.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 412 participants with T1D from five independent cohorts. A fixed individualized profile from each participant's initial valid 24 h was combined with 60 min of recent CGM/insulin history to generate 30-minute forecasts. Five-fold leave-one-cohort-out-validation withheld each cohort entirely from model development. Clinical acceptability (Clarke-Error-Grid), prediction-interval coverage, participant-level accuracy (MAE/RMSE), and non-personalized comparator were assessed.

RESULTS: Across held-out cohorts, 93.9-98.3% of forecasts fell in clinically acceptable adapted Clarke Error Grid Zones A + B (mean 96.8%), and dangerous Zone-E errors were rare (0.000-0.014%). Mean 90% prediction-interval coverage was 90.04%. Participant-level MAE ranged between (15.5-21.65 mg/dL) and RMSE (20.6 to 29.0 mg/dL). The cohort with the lowest numeric error did not have the most favorable clinical-risk profile, and the personalized model achieved lower participant-macro MAE and RMSE than the matched non-personalized one across all five held-out cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: A brief, one-time individualized profile supported clinically acceptable and uncertainty-aware glucose forecasting across previously unseen T1D populations without patient-specific retraining, supporting the feasibility and cross-cohort robustness of this low-burden personalization strategy.

articles.title: Empiric Antifungal Therapy in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Surgery for Severe Intra-Abdominal Infection: a Large Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-abdominal candidiasis is frequent in critically ill surgical patients and is associated with high mortality. Whether empiric antifungal therapy improves outcomes after surgery for intra-abdominal infection (IAI) in critically ill patients remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center data warehouse-based cohort study of 1,061 adults admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) after surgery for IAI between 2018 and 2024. Patients who received systemic antifungal therapy within 24 hours after surgery were compared with those who did not. The primary endpoint was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were day-5 renal dysfunction, assessed by the renal SOFA component and the creatinine-based KDIGO stage, and the need for surgical reintervention. Adjusted analyses used propensity-score overlap weighting. Prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses used a Peritonitis Score ≥3, the identification of at least one organism in peritoneal samples, and a yeast-positive peritoneal sample.

RESULTS: Empiric antifungal therapy was initiated in 46.0% of patients. Peritoneal sampling was available in 957 patients (90.2%); 21.4% had no organism identified and 25.2% had a yeast-positive sample. In adjusted analyses, empiric therapy was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality (OR 1.53, 95% CI 0.83-2.78), lower day-5 renal SOFA score, lower KDIGO stage, or fewer reinterventions. Findings were consistent in patients with Peritonitis Score ≥3, with at least one identified organism, and with a yeast-positive sample. ICU and hospital stays were longer in treated patients after weighting.

CONCLUSIONS: Empiric antifungal therapy initiated within 24 hours after surgery for severe IAI was not associated with improved short-term outcomes.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: NA.

articles.title: Monitoring of Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in the ICU: the MAVERIC pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous congestion is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of organ dysfunction during acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Although the Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) score is a promising bedside marker of systemic venous congestion, its dynamic evolution during CRRT remains unknown. We aimed to describe serial changes in VExUS during CRRT and explore their association with ultrafiltration intensity and fluid balance.

METHODS: MAVERIC was a prospective single-centre observational pilot study including adults undergoing CRRT for acute kidney injury. VExUS was assessed before CRRT initiation and after 24 and 48 hours. The primary objective was to describe temporal changes in VExUS using an alluvial plot. Patients were classified into three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution. Associations with net ultrafiltration (NUF) and cumulative fluid balance were explored.

RESULTS: Forty-seven patients were included. Overall, VExUS grades decreased significantly during the first 48 hours of CRRT (p =  0.0048). Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were identified: persistently low congestion (45%, n = 21), resolving congestion (32%, n = 15), and persistent or worsening congestion (23%, n = 11). Patients with resolving congestion had the highest NUF rates (1.35 [0.85-1.66] mL/kg/h) and the most negative cumulative fluid balance (-36.7 [-74.6 to -21.1] mL/kg), with significant differences across groups (p =  0.003 and p <  0.001, respectively). Patients with persistent or worsening congestion had lower NUF rates.

CONCLUSIONS: Serial VExUS assessment provides dynamic information on systemic venous congestion during CRRT. Three a priori-defined patterns of congestion evolution were associated with differences in net ultrafiltration and fluid balance. Serial VExUS monitoring may help identify patients with persistent or worsening congestion, raising the hypothesis that it could inform reassessment of decongestion strategies. Whether integrating serial VExUS assessment into individualised decongestive strategies improves renal outcomes should be evaluated in prospective interventional studies.

articles.title: Repeated Chlamydia trachomatis nucleic acid amplification test positivity after multiple antimicrobial regimens: a case report with phenotypic susceptibility testing and a literature review.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Repeated detection of Chlamydia trachomatis after antimicrobial treatment is challenging because a positive nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) does not distinguish residual nucleic acid from reinfection, nonadherence, untreated extragenital infection, or persistent viable organisms. We describe a 22-year-old nulligravid woman with serous vaginal discharge and C. trachomatis cervicitis diagnosed using the COBAS AMPLICOR® CT/NG Test (Roche Diagnostics). The NAAT remained positive 3 weeks after each of four successive regimens: azithromycin 1 g as a single dose on two occasions, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days, and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days. She denied sexual intercourse during treatment, and pharyngeal and rectal NAATs were negative before the 14-day doxycycline course. A clinical isolate recovered before sitafloxacin underwent phenotypic testing against eight agents. All MICs were within Japanese surveillance ranges, although several were at the upper end of the distributions. Sitafloxacin 100 mg twice daily for 14 days was followed by a negative NAAT 3 weeks later. The isolate supports viability at one point but does not prove uninterrupted persistence across treatment courses. Interpretation is limited by testing all post-treatment specimens at 3 weeks, lack of objective adherence and partner-treatment verification, and absence of serial genotyping or whole-genome sequencing. This case documents repeated post-treatment NAAT positivity and recovery of viable C. trachomatis at one sampling point; it does not establish refractory infection or continuous persistence of the same strain. The temporal association with sitafloxacin does not establish its superiority or the mechanism of subsequent NAAT negativity.

articles.title: Re-evaluating the 6-cm threshold for invasive intervention in lung abscess: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung abscesses are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet evidence-based treatment guidelines are lacking. Antibiotic therapy is primary, although cavities ≥6 cm are considered for percutaneous drainage or surgical resection. However, the prognostic significance of this threshold remains unclear. We evaluated whether an abscess cavity diameter ≥6 cm is associated with conservative antibiotic therapy failure.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients hospitalized with lung abscesses and initially treated with antibiotics between April 2004 and June 2024 was conducted. The primary endpoint was treatment failure, a composite of computed tomography-guided percutaneous drainage, surgical resection, and in-hospital death. Patients were classified into small-size (<6 cm) and large-size (≥6 cm) groups. Propensity score overlap weighting adjusted for baseline differences and restricted cubic spline logistic regression (four knots, adjusted for age and sex) assessed nonlinear associations.

RESULTS: Among 109 patients (mean age, 71.2 years; 21 women [19.3%]), unadjusted treatment failure was higher in the large-size group than in the small-size group (38.5% vs. 12.5%, P = 0.044) but did not differ after weighting (39.8% vs. 28.8%, P = 0.483). No significant differences were observed in percutaneous drainage, surgery, or in-hospital mortality. Spline analysis showed a gradual increase in the estimated coefficient for treatment failure without a distinct threshold at 6 cm.

CONCLUSIONS: We found no clear evidence of an independent association between abscess cavities ≥6 cm and treatment failure or mortality after adjustment. Antibiotic therapy remains a valid initial approach, and intervention should be guided by clinical characteristics and response.

articles.title: Dose-Dependent Effects of Dietary Adenine on Renal Dysfunction, Uremic Toxin Accumulation, and Renal Protein Expression in Rats.
articles.journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
articles.abstract: Adenine (Ade) is widely used to induce chronic kidney disease in rodents; however, the effects of different dietary concentrations remain unclear. In this study, rats were fed diets containing 0.125-1.50% Ade to characterize concentration-dependent renal and systemic effects. Ade concentrations of 0.25% or higher caused body-weight loss and marked renal dysfunction, including increased serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen, renal histological damage, and accumulation of indoxyl sulfate. Renal histological alterations were also observed in the 0.25% Ade group. Renal expression of antioxidant proteins, including SOD1 and CAT, was decreased, whereas HO-1 expression was increased, indicating alterations in antioxidant- and redox-related protein expression. In contrast, 0.125% Ade did not cause clear changes in serum renal function markers but increased urine volume and altered renal protein expression. These findings demonstrate that the effects of dietary Ade vary substantially with concentration and suggest that lower-dose, longer-term administration may be useful for investigating progressive renal dysfunction.

articles.title: Injurious Falls and Mortality With Intensive Blood Pressure Treatment in SPRINT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials of blood pressure (BP) treatment intensity have shown no difference in nonfatal injurious falls. However, whether the occurrence or timing of injurious falls modifies the association between intensive BP treatment and all-cause mortality remains uncertain.

METHODS: This secondary analysis of 9,361 SPRINT participants compared intensive (<120 mm Hg) versus standard (<140 mm Hg) systolic BP treatment. Two Cox proportional hazards approaches evaluated associations with all-cause mortality: (1) subgroup and interaction analyses by injurious fall status, irrespective of timing, and (2) analyses incorporating fall timing to assess associations before and after an injurious fall.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 3.3 years in all 9,361 SPRINT participants, 666 participants experienced an injurious fall. In subgroup analyses without consideration of fall timing, the association of intensive treatment with mortality was as follows: [no fall: adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 0.73, 95% CI: 0.58-0.92; fall: adjusted HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.42-1.32; Pint=0.9]. When timing was incorporated, the association of intensive treatment with all-cause mortality was as follows: [before fall: adjusted HR 0.75, 95% CI: 0.59-0.94; after fall: adjusted HR 0.71, 95% CI: 0.38-1.32, Pint =0.85].

CONCLUSIONS: In this secondary analysis of SPRINT, the occurrence or timing of an injurious fall did not significantly modify the association between intensive BP treatment and all-cause mortality, although post-fall estimates were imprecise.

articles.title: Seven-day treatment with combined acetoacetate and D-β-hydroxybutyrate, at concentrations representative of nutritional ketosis, increases basal glucose uptake in L6 skeletal muscle myotubes.
articles.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have suggested a link between ketone bodies and glucose metabolism in skeletal muscle. However, the nature of this connection is unclear, particularly in the long-term.

METHODS: To better understand the effect of ketone bodies on glucose metabolism, we exposed L6 muscle cells to ketone bodies over 7 days and measured the effect on basal glucose uptake.

RESULTS: We found that a mix of acetoacetate (0.2 mM) and D-β-hydroxybutyrate (1 mM) increased basal glucose uptake in L6 myotubes. The effect on glucose uptake was unique to a combination of these ketone bodies at concentrations that meet the threshold for nutritional ketosis, as basal glucose uptake was unchanged in response to a more extreme set of concentrations or with individual ketone bodies. The increase in basal glucose uptake was not linked to the phosphorylation of Akt, AMP-activated protein kinase, or the expression or translocation of glucose transporter type 1 or 4 in the L6 myotubes.

GENERAL SIGNIFICANCE: These results provide insight into the long-term impact of increased circulating ketone bodies on glucose metabolism, which has implications for metabolic diseases like type 2 diabetes or during adherence to ketogenic diets. Last, by comparing the 7-day exposure presented here with our previously published results using 3-h ketone body exposure, we propose that ketone bodies influence basal glucose uptake in L6 myotubes in a time and concentration dependent manner.

articles.title: Debridement, Antibiotics, and Implant Retention for Periprosthetic Joint Infection Following Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Outcomes and Predictors of Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) is uncommon, but serious and differs from total knee arthroplasty (TKA) PJI because native cartilage and soft tissues are retained. Evidence for debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) in this setting is limited. We evaluated DAIR outcomes and predictors of failure.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and EMBASE were searched in May 2026 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews [PROSPERO] CRD420261389798), following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Studies reporting five or more adults treated with DAIR for PJI after primary UKA were eligible. Infection eradication was pooled with a random-effects logit model (restricted maximum likelihood [REML] with Hartung-Knapp correction; DerSimonian-Laird as sensitivity analysis) and a prespecified study-level subgroup analysis by infection timing. Predictors could not be pooled and were synthesized narratively following Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidance. Quality was assessed with the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS) and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) framework.

RESULTS: There were 10 observational studies (206 patients who had UKA PJI, 175 treated with DAIR) included; no randomized trials existed. Pooled DAIR success was 72.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 60.4 to 81.4; I2 34.5%; 95% prediction interval 46.5 to 88.5). Success was 79.3% (95% CI 55.2 to 92.3) in acute-only cohorts and 64.1% (95% CI 47.6 to 77.8) in mixed cohorts, but this study-level difference was not significant (P = 0.067), and patient-level analysis identified only four patients in the literature treated with DAIR for chronic infection. There was no study that reported an adjusted analysis of predictors; narratively, Staphylococcus aureus (particularly methicillin-resistant S. aureus [MRSA]) was the commonest correlate of failure and thorough synovectomy of success, both hypothesis-generating. Of 87 successfully treated patients, 12 (14%) later required aseptic conversion to TKA. Certainty was very low.

CONCLUSION: A DAIR eradicated infection in approximately three of four selected patients, most with acute infection, but roughly one in four required further surgery. Because only DAIR-treated cohorts were eligible and none compared DAIR with staged revision, relative effectiveness cannot be established. A DAIR appears a reasonable implant-retaining option in carefully selected patients rather than a demonstrated first-line treatment.

articles.title: The Effects of Non-Psoriatic Dermatitis on Total Hip Arthroplasty Outcomes: A Propensity-Matched Analysis with Longitudinal Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While psoriasis has been associated with increased complications following total hip arthroplasty (THA), the effects of non-psoriatic dermatitis (NPD) on THA outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between NPD and postoperative outcomes following primary THA with additional stratification by dermatitis-related medication use.

METHODS: In a large national database, patients aged ≥ 18 years undergoing primary THA anytime between 2003 and 2020 were identified. Patients who had NPD were compared with a control cohort of patients who did not have NPD. Additional pairwise comparisons evaluated the effect of dermatitis-related medication use. After multiple demographics and comorbidities were propensity-matched using a 1:1 ratio, postoperative medical outcomes and surgical complications were examined with follow-up at 90 days, one year, and two years.

RESULTS: At 90 days, NPD was associated with a higher rate of emergency department admission and a lower rate of periprosthetic dislocation or instability (P ≤ 0.048). There were no other significant associations observed at one or two years. Compared to patients who do not have NPD, patients who have NPD with concurrent medication use had higher rates of inpatient readmission, emergency department admission, deep vein thrombosis, falls, and periprosthetic fracture at 90 days (P ≤ 0.027), and periprosthetic fracture remained elevated at one and two years (P ≤ 0.012). Patients who have NPD without medication use showed no significant differences for all measured outcomes across every timepoint.

CONCLUSION: Although some 90-day outcomes were significant, NPD was not independently associated with one- and two-year complications following THA. Patients receiving medications for NPD treatment may represent a high-risk subgroup with increased healthcare utilization, thromboembolic events, falls, and periprosthetic fracture. Among THA candidates who have NPD, the effects of pharmaceutical management may be considered, especially for thromboembolic risk, fall prevention, and bone health optimization.

articles.title: Worse Fixation of Cemented Patellar Components on Magnetic Resonance Imaging is Associated with Increased Patellar Component Surface Damage.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cemented patellar components demonstrate high rates of fibrous tissue at the bone-cement interface on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), suggesting worse fixation than femoral and tibial components. A paucity of data exists on modern patellar component wear patterns and the relationship with patellar fixation as assessed by MRI. We aimed to evaluate the in vivo wear patterns of patellar components and to determine if patellar components with worse fixation on MRI are associated with increased surface damage.

METHODS: There were 122 cemented all-polyethylene patellar components (32 periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), 90 aseptic revision) revised between 2019 and 2024 that were analyzed. Surface damage was evaluated using the Hood scoring system (scale, 0 to 3). Preoperative multi-acquisition variable-resonance image combination (MAVRIC) MRI scans were reviewed following a validated method to evaluate the bone-cement interface and percentage of bone-cement integration for each patellar quadrant.

RESULTS: Scratching, burnishing, and pitting were the most common modes of patellar component surface damage. The mean total Hood score was 10.4 (range, 1 to 24.5). The number of quadrants with an abnormal interface and the number of quadrants with ≤ 33% integration were associated with higher damage scores (P = 0.015 and P = 0.007, respectively). In multivariable analyses, men who had longer implantation duration and ≤ 33% integration in all quadrants on MRI were independently associated with higher articular surface damage scores. Increased patellar surface damage and poor bone-cement integration on MRI were associated with component loosening.

CONCLUSION: Cemented patellar components with MRI findings of an abnormal bone-cement interface and poor bone-cement integration demonstrated significantly higher surface damage scores. This relationship suggests that biomechanical factors such as wear and the accompanied increased contact loads are important factors in controlling component fixation.

articles.title: Monoflange Versus Multiflange: Custom-Made Acetabular Implants in Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe acetabular bone loss remains a major challenge in hip reconstruction. Custom-made acetabular components (CMACs) represent a valuable treatment option, with monoflange designs potentially offering advantages over multiflange constructs by reducing implant size and soft-tissue exposure while maintaining mechanical stability.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study analyzed 154 CMACs (101 monoflange and 53 multiflange) and assessed clinical outcomes (Oxford Hip Score), radiographic findings, complications, implant survival, and revision procedures. The mean follow-up was 37.0 months (range, 6.2 to 168.2), with longer follow-up for multiflange than monoflange constructs (55.5 versus 27.3 months; P = 0.011).

RESULTS: Monoflange constructs showed shorter hospital stays (P = 0.030), reduced blood losses (P < 0.001), and shorter operative times (P = 0.006). Both groups improved in Oxford Hip Score (OHS), with higher postoperative scores for monoflange constructs (P = 0.010), although adjusted mean change in OHS did not differ (P = 0.566). Periprosthetic joint infection rates were higher for multiflange constructs (18.9 versus 6.9%; P = 0.034). Complete osseointegration was achieved in 93.1% of monoflange and 67.9% of multiflange constructs (P < 0.001). Horizontal center of rotation restoration was comparable (0.9 ± 5.0 versus 2.0 ± 5.7 mm; P = 0.236), whereas monoflange constructs showed less cranialization (3.5 ± 4.5 mm versus 7.6 ± 5.6 mm; P < 0.001). Multiflange design was associated with a higher risk of implant removal (odds ratio = 4.42; P = 0.007).

CONCLUSION: Monoflange CMACs demonstrated favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes and, after adjustment for patient factors, a significantly lower risk of implant removal than multiflange constructs. As implant design and era are confounded in this cohort, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require confirmation in prospective series.

articles.title: Can Outpatient Total Hip Arthroplasty Be Done at a Complex, Academic, Quaternary Referral Center?
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary outpatient (same-day discharge) total hip arthroplasty (THA) has gained popularity, but results from academic medical centers remain limited. Same-day discharge shifts perioperative responsibilities to the surgeon. In contrast, surgeon reimbursements continue to decline. We retrospectively evaluated 90-day rates of emergency room (ER) visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches associated with outpatient THAs at our complex, academic, quaternary referral center.

METHODS: At our institution, 1,970 outpatient primary THAs were performed between 2019 and 2024 in 1,813 unique patients. The mean age was 61 years, 56% were men, the mean body mass index (BMI) was 30, the mean American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) score was 2.2, and the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 1.2 (range, 1 to 10). Medical comorbidities, ER visits, reoperations, revisions, and postoperative touches within 90 days after THA were collected. Univariate logistic regression analyses were completed.

RESULTS: Rates of ER visits, reoperations, and revisions within 90 days of surgery were 8.6, 1.5, and 0.9%, respectively. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches, and total touches increased from 131 in 2019 to greater than 4,800 in 2024. The most common first-time ER visit reason was a medical issue unrelated to surgery (39%), followed by dislocation (14%) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) evaluation (12%; actual VTE incidence 0.3%). The most common reason for reoperation and revision was acute periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; incidence 0.7%). Increasing BMI was associated with risk of reoperations (odds ratio [OR] 1.1; P = 0.02), revisions (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), and PJI (OR 1.1; P = 0.03), but not with ER visits or dislocations. Increasing CCI was associated with risk of first-time ER visits (OR 1.2; P < 0.001) and dislocations (OR 1.3; P = 0.02). Increasing ASA score was associated with risk of ER visits (OR 1.8; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Outpatient THA patients had a high rate of ER visits within 90 days postoperatively, with almost 40% unattributable to surgery. Increasing BMI was associated with increased reoperation, revision, and PJI risk, while increasing CCI and ASA score increased ER visit risk, and increasing CCI increased dislocation risk. Hips averaged nine postoperative touches. As outpatient THA grows, surgeon compensation should be reevaluated given the heightened administrative burden.

articles.title: Preoperative Supplementation to Optimize Clinical Outcomes After Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to synthesize evidence on preoperative supplementation in total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA), identifying supplement categories associated with improved postoperative outcomes and areas where evidence remains insufficient for routine use.

METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, Cochrane, and Web of Science was performed in November 2025 according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Comparative studies in English evaluating preoperative supplementation in THA/TKA were included without time restrictions. There were 25 studies, including 3,629 patients undergoing THA/TKA, meeting the inclusion/exclusion criteria. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2.0) for randomized controlled trials and the Risk Of Bias In Non-Randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I) for comparative studies. Certainty of evidence was evaluated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. When feasible, meta-analyses were conducted using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Preoperative carbohydrate loading was associated not only with shorter lengths of stay (mean difference [MD] = -0.41 days, P = 0.036), but also with higher postoperative blood glucose increase (MD = 8.83 mg/dL, P = 0.003). Amino acid supplementation was associated with a slightly increased lengths of stay (MD = 0.20 days, P < 0.001), but was associated with better preservation of postoperative thigh muscle area (standardized mean difference [SMD] = 0.36, P = 0.040). Iron supplementation showed no significant reduction in lengths of stay, and exploratory analyses did not demonstrate consistent effects on perioperative hemoglobin or transfusion rates. Evidence for vitamins, fatty acids, and combined formulations was limited and inconsistent. Overall certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative supplementation for THA and TKA may provide some benefits in selected outcomes, particularly lengths of stay with carbohydrate loading, early muscle preservation with amino acid supplementation, and lower infection rate with vitamin D supplementation. However, the current evidence remains sparse, heterogeneous, and often underpowered for key outcomes, hindering the ability to recommend routine use for all arthroplasty patients. While the available literature suggests the potential to improve the postoperative outcome of THA and TKA, future high-quality research is needed to elucidate the optimal preoperative supplementation strategies to optimize the management of patients undergoing these procedures in clinical practice.

articles.title: Higher Doses of Perioperative Dexamethasone are Not Associated with an Increased Risk of Infection Following Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dexamethasone has been used with increased frequency perioperatively during total knee (TKA) and hip arthroplasty (THA) to prevent postoperative nausea and vomiting. Higher doses of dexamethasone have been shown to decrease pain and prevent complications such as pulmonary embolism and acute kidney injury. However, less is known regarding the effect of increasing doses on infectious complications, particularly among patients who have diabetes.

METHODS: Utilizing a national healthcare database, we identified adult patients undergoing primary total joint arthroplasty (TJA) between 2016 and 2023. Patients were stratified with respect to the dexamethasone dose administered on the day of surgery into a no-dose, low-dose (four to five- miligrams[mg]), medium-dose (eight to 12 mg), or high-dose (16 to 32 mg) group. The primary outcome, the 90-day risk of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), was compared across all dexamethasone dosing levels using mixed-effect logistic regression, with the no-dexamethasone group as the reference, in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients.

RESULTS: Of the identified 1,483,703 TJA patients, 618,654 (41.7%) received no dexamethasone, 252,978 (17.1%) received a low dose, 481,551 (32.5%) received a medium dose, and 130,520 (8.8%) received a high dose on the day of surgery. Among non-diabetic patients, high-dose dexamethasone was not associated with an increased risk of PJI following either TKA (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.93, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.79 to 1.09, P = 0.354) or THA (aOR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68 to 1.00, P = 0.050). Low- and medium-dose dexamethasone were also not associated with an increased risk of PJI after either procedure. These findings held true among diabetic patients.

DISCUSSION: Higher perioperative doses of dexamethasone were not associated with an increased risk of infection even among patients who have diabetes. Higher doses of dexamethasone appear safe in medically optimized patients undergoing TKA and THA.

articles.title: Durability of a Proximally Coated, Dual-Tapered Cementless Femoral Stem Through 20 Years After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies of total hip arthroplasty (THA) through 20 years should distinguish failure of the femoral stem from revisions of components. This study evaluated revision-free survival of a proximally coated, dual-tapered cementless femoral stem and characterized causes of late revision and reoperation.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort included 730 THAs in 622 patients between February 1999 and June 2007. The primary endpoint was removal or exchange of the index stem. Revisions retaining the stem were analyzed separately. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated from institutional follow-up. Hips without a qualifying postoperative orthopaedic visit or radiograph were censored at the index date and contributed no observation time. Stem-specific follow-up was available for 391 hips (53.6%), contributing 6,145.4 hip-years; median follow-up was 16.1 years (range, 3.9 to 26.3). Of these, 221 remained at risk at 15 years, including 112 at 20 years.

RESULTS: There were three stems revised: two after periprosthetic fracture and one for instability/component malposition. There was no stem revision for aseptic loosening. There was one periprosthetic joint infection (PJI)-related head and liner exchange that was identified in institutional records and retained the index stem; no PJI-related stem revision was observed. Stem revision-free survival was 99.1% at 15 and 98.6% at 20 years. At 20 years, freedom from revision of any THA component and ipsilateral reoperation was 79.9 and 79.5%. Bearing wear/osteolysis accounted for 14 of 29 first component revisions (48.3%), due to conventional polyethylene. The 339 hips lacked qualifying postoperative institutional follow-up and were censored at the index date. Among patients represented by these hips, 17 were deceased; implant status remained unverified.

CONCLUSION: Under documented stem-specific institutional follow-up, this cementless femoral stem demonstrated high revision-free survival through 20 years. Late stem revisions were related to fracture or instability rather than aseptic loosening; no PJI-related stem revision was observed in institutional records. Most reinterventions involved non-femoral components.
