articles.title: Psychosocial and ergonomic factors of work-related musculoskeletal disorders among oral healthcare workers in Malaysia.
articles.journal: International journal of occupational safety and ergonomics : JOSE
articles.abstract: Objectives. Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are a leading occupational health challenge in dentistry, often compounded by overlooked psychosocial stressors. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence of MSDs and identify associated psychosocial risk factors among Malaysian primary oral healthcare personnel. Methods. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from April to July 2024 involving 330 government-employed oral healthcare workers across six Malaysian states using the Nordic musculoskeletal questionnaire (NMQ) and Copenhagen psychosocial questionnaire (COPSOQ). Descriptive statistics, χ2 tests, simple linear regressions and multivariable linear regression were used to evaluate associations with cumulative MSD burden (Nordic score). Results. MSD prevalence was notably high, with the lower back (69.4%), shoulder (66.1%) and neck (65.5%) the most affected regions. Company perception was positively associated with MSD burden (B = 0.149, p < 0.001). Conversely, self-rated health demonstrated an expected protective inverse association with MSD burden (B = -0.386, p < 0.001), while work-life conflict exhibited an unexpected inverse association (B = -0.309, p < 0.001). Conclusions. These findings highlight the complex interplay between physical and psychosocial stressors in oral healthcare settings. Integrated interventions that combine ergonomic redesign, mental health support and organizational reforms are essential to safeguard the well-being and sustainability of this vital workforce.

articles.title: A connectome and transcriptome identity shift through a single transcription factor isoform.
articles.abstract: The brain exhibits remarkable neuronal diversity. The sheer number of cell types emerging from extensive transcriptional, morphological, and connectome datasets provokes the question of how the brain is capable of generating so many unique identities. Proper neuronal specification and subsequent features of identity, such as wiring, are essential for normal cognitive and behavioral function. However, we still know little about how identity and wiring are encoded within developmental programs. Here, we turn to the visual system of Drosophila melanogaster. We use its unprecedented combination of single-synapse-resolution wiring diagrams from electron microscopy (EM) connectomes and developmental gene expression profiles from single-cell transcriptomic atlases to study the molecular basis of cell-type-specific terminal identity specification and downstream wiring patterns. We integrate analyses of neuronal anatomy, whole-cell electrophysiology, and single-cell RNA sequencing after perturbation (scRNA-Perturb-seq) to establish that the transcription factor broad functions to control terminal features of identity between two visual projection neuron cell types, LPLC1 and LPLC2. We demonstrate the first characterization in functional connectivity changes following changes in neuronal identity specification. We find broad acts through a single isoform (broad-z4) that is selectively expressed in LPLC1 and has the capacity to reprogram the morphology, functional connectivity, and transcriptional identity of postmitotic LPLC2 neurons into an LPLC1-like cell type. Our findings establish a single transcription factor isoform as the smallest unit required to differentiate neuronal identity, a strategy that may be conserved within developmental programs to expand the capacity for cell-type diversity across animal species.

articles.title: The effect of two different interventions applied during the transfer of children to the operating room for circumcision on fear, anxiety, comfort and pain levels: Randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of an animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope on the fear, anxiety, comfort, and pain levels of children while transferring them to the operating room for circumcision surgery.

METHODS: This randomised controlled trial with pretest-posttest design included 96 children aged 7-10 years who were scheduled for circumcision surgery at the urology and paediatric surgery departments of a State Hospital and met the inclusion criteria (animal-assisted intervention group = 31, kaleidoscope group = 32, control group = 33). The interventions were administered while transferring them to the operating room. Data were collected using five tools: a Child Information Form, the Children's Fear Scale, the Children's Anxiety Meter-State, the Comfort Behaviors Checklist, and the Wong Baker Faces Pain Rating Scale. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance, dependent samples t-test, and Bonferroni post-hoc test.

RESULTS: The posttest mean scores of CFS, CAMS, and FACES were significantly lower in the animal-assisted intervention and kaleidoscope groups than in the control group, while posttest CBC mean scores were significantly higher (p < 0.05). Both interventions alleviated their fear, anxiety, and pain and improved their comfort during the transfer. The animal-assisted intervention was more effective than the kaleidoscope intervention.

CONCLUSIONS: These interventions should be integrated into standard nursing practice for paediatric surgery, particularly during operating room transfer.

IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Integrating AAI and kaleidoscope interventions into paediatric perioperative nursing care may promote child-friendly practices and improve children's surgical experiences.

articles.title: AI and systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease registries: usefulness of AI in the evolution of database management.
articles.abstract: Rheumatology and clinical immunology registries present two distinct paradigms for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). In higher-prevalence diseases (e.g. rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, spondyloarthritis), high-volume databases like the ACR RISE registry, CorEvitas, and SCQM enable AI/ML to transition from descriptive epidemiology to individualized outcome prediction and subgroup discovery. Conversely, in rare diseases (e.g. systemic sclerosis in EUSTAR, ANCA-associated vasculitis, idiopathic inflammatory myositis, autoinflammatory conditions), registries constitute the primary available evidence base. Here, ML's capacity to handle missing data, without the strict imputation required by classical statistics, unlocks otherwise unusable real-world data. This review summarizes recent registry-based AI/ML advances across both settings while addressing key limitations, including data harmonization barriers, algorithmic bias, and a lack of prospective validation. We argue that unlocking the future value of AI depends less on algorithmic complexity and more on transforming registries into AI-ready, federated, and continuously curated infrastructures.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Urology Residency Match: Use, Perceptions, and Implications.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate artificial intelligence (AI) use and perceptions among urology applicants during the 2025 to 2026 residency match cycle.

METHODS: An anonymous survey was distributed to all applicants at a single academic urology residency program after rank list submission and before match day. A 29-item subset of the survey was analyzed, which assessed applicant demographics, application components, AI use patterns, and perceptions regarding various AI-related issues. Both descriptive and between-group comparison statistics were utilized to summarize responses.

RESULTS: Seventy complete responses were analyzed, resulting in a 45% response rate. Overall, 51% of applicants reported using AI during the application process, but inaccurately perceived higher rates of use among their peers. ChatGPT was the most used AI tool (83%). Inaccurate or misleading AI-generated information was common, and though 86% encountered it at least once, only 44% of applicants always verified AI outputs. AI was most often used for personal statement writing, application content, and interview preparation, with these also rated as most helpful. Among AI users, 61% reported at least slight improvement in application material quality, whereas only 44% reported the same for interview preparation. Few respondents supported restricting applicant AI use (23%), while the majority (54%) supported prohibiting AI use by residency programs.

CONCLUSIONS: Urology applicants report wide but varied use of AI across the residency match cycle, with modest perceived benefits despite mixed opinions on allowing AI use going forward. Nevertheless, thoughtfully designed and ethically integrated AI tools have immense potential to increase efficiency, equity, and outcomes in the competitive urology match process.

articles.title: From evidence to bedside: A decade of critical care pharmacotherapy and implications for ICU training.
articles.abstract: Pharmacotherapy management is integral to the care of critically ill patients, yet decisions are frequently made in dynamic and uncertain conditions. Over the last decade, a series of large trials and shifts in understanding have reshaped how therapies are selected and applied in the intensive care unit (ICU), often challenging long-standing practices and refining established treatment strategies. This review examines influential studies and paradigm shifts across four major areas of ICU pharmacotherapy: respiratory failure and acute respiratory distress syndrome, infectious disease and antimicrobial therapy, hemodynamic management in sepsis and septic shock, and sedation and delirium. We highlight how emerging evidence led to pharmacotherapeutic evolution within each domain and identify common patterns across these domains supporting a movement toward individualized, context-dependent care and more deliberate use of pharmacologic therapies. For trainees, the last decade provides important lessons regarding application of pharmacotherapy in the ICU, including the need to integrate evidence interpretation with clinical judgement.

articles.title: Capillary refill time at the admission of trauma patients: A prospective, observational study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The early identification of tissue perfusion is a significant challenge in the management of severe trauma cases. Capillary refill time (CRT) is a simple clinical marker of peripheral perfusion. The objective of this study was to ascertain the correlation between CRT and serum lactate levels in patients with severe trauma.

METHODS: A prospective, single-center observational study was conducted in a 20-bed intensive care unit (ICU) of a level 1 trauma center between April 2025 and January 2026. Adult patients who were directly admitted to the ICU from the scene of the accident for severe trauma, as defined by an injury severity score above 15, were included in the study. The CRT and serum lactate were measured on admission to the ICU. The primary endpoint was the association between admission serum lactate and admission CRT ≥ 3 s (abnormal CRT). Secondary analyses included the correlation between CRT and serum lactate at admission and the association between CRT and duration of vasopressor exposure during the first 3 days. Multivariate linear regression was performed on logarithmically transformed serum lactate, adjusted for age, core body temperature, prehospital weight-adjusted fluid administration, prehospital use of norepinephrine and prehospital timing.

RESULTS: Of 627 patients screened, 196 were included in the analysis. The admission CRT was 2.4 [1.7-3.1] s with serum lactate level at 2.1 [1.3-3.4] mmol/L. Admission serum lactate did not differ significantly between the patients with abnormal CRT and those with normal CRT (2.6 [1.4-4.6] versus 1.9 [1.3-3.1] mmol/L; p = 0.07) while CRT and serum lactate levels were correlated (r = 0.33; p < 0.01). In multivariate analysis, continuous analysis of CRT was independently associated with serum lactate levels with a 15% increase in serum lactate per additional sec of CRT (95% CI 1.06-1.25; p < 0.01). Among patients with serum lactate >2 mmol/L, abnormal CRT was associated with longer vasopressor exposure at day 3 and increased ICU mortality.

CONCLUSION: Admission lactate did not differ significantly between normal and abnormal CRT groups. Exploratory subgroup findings suggest that CRT may complement serum lactate in characterizing patients with severe trauma.

articles.title: Elevated concentrations of 78Se and 208Pb isotopes in cerebrospinal fluid but not in blood plasma from patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by motor neuron degeneration and muscle atrophy, ultimately leading to death through respiratory failure. In addition to genetic factors, environmental exposures have been investigated as potential ALS risk factors. Elevated concentrations of cadmium, lead and selenium have previously been detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood from ALS patients, suggesting an association between metal dysregulation and disease progression. Here, we conducted a detailed analysis of CSF and blood plasma from seven ALS patients and seven healthy controls, where samples were collected using ultraclean techniques. Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was used to measure isotopes of a wide range of elements. Significantly higher concentrations of 208Pb and 78Se (p < 0.01) were recorded in CSF but not in plasma of ALS patients compared to controls. Interestingly, no significant differences were observed for the 206Pb and 207Pb isotope concentrations as such. However, the 208Pb/207Pb ratio was elevated in CSF of ALS cases compared to controls, which might be due to biological isotope fractionation, or exposure to lead from different geological sources. Taken together, our data supports previous reports of Pb and Se contributing to ALS pathogenesis. The results also suggest that investigating metal dyshomeostasis at the isotope level can improve understanding of disease pathologies, especially for conditions and diseases where metal exposure is a risk factor.

articles.title: Deep Learning With Longitudinal Electrocardiograms Predicts Atrial Fibrillation Better Than a Single Electrocardiogram.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is often paroxysmal and asymptomatic, yet early identification could enable targeted surveillance. Deep learning can predict future AF from a single 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), but AF develops through progressive atrial remodeling.

OBJECTIVES: We hypothesized that modeling each patient's longitudinal ECG history would improve 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model.

METHODS: We developed a transformer-based model that accepts variable-length sequences of prior 12-lead ECGs with time-aware encoding of irregular intervals. We compared it with a single-ECG model sharing the same encoder, covariates, preprocessing, outcome definition, and splits. Models were developed at Weill Cornell Medicine/NewYork-Presbyterian and evaluated on MIMIC-IV-ECG without and with fine-tuning. The outcome was AF documented more than 1 and within 365 days after an index ECG. Discrimination used patient-cluster bootstrapping with 1 random index ECG per patient.

RESULTS: Cohorts included 107,811 institutional and 55,307 MIMIC-IV-ECG patients. The fine-tuned longitudinal model with age and sex discriminated best (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.85; C-index 0.84), exceeding the single-ECG model with age and sex (paired area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: +0.007; 95% CI: 0.003-0.012; +0.014 with ≥1 prior ECG). Without retraining on MIMIC-IV-ECG, the ECG-only advantage was confined to patients with ≥1 prior ECG (+0.014; 95% CI: 0.004-0.024). After external-domain adaptation, the matched advantage was +0.007 (95% CI: 0.002-0.012). High-risk patients had lower AF-free survival (HR: 8.8; 95% CI: 7.8-10.0).

CONCLUSIONS: A longitudinal deep learning model using serial 12-lead ECGs improved 1-year AF prediction over a matched single-ECG model. Longitudinal ECG modeling may provide a scalable approach to identify patients warranting enhanced AF surveillance.

articles.title: Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO2i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO2i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization.

RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO2i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m2), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO2i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO2i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m2, 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO2i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO2i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO2i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO2i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO2i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure.

CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

articles.title: Exercise Test Findings in the Long-Term Outcomes After Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MUSIC) Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) commonly presents with cardiovascular involvement, but the frequency of exercise-related arrhythmias and exercise capacity are poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe exercise stress testing (EST) and cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) after MIS-C.

METHODS: We summarized EST and CPET results from the MUSIC (Long-terM OUtcomes after the Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome In Children) study (1,204 participants, 32 North American sites). Demographics and details of hospitalization from participants undergoing clinical EST were compared to participants ≥5 years who did not undergo EST. Site reported results of EST and CPET were described.

RESULTS: EST was performed in 22% (208/932) at a mean of 150 ± 110 days after hospitalization. Compared with those who did not undergo EST (n = 724), the EST cohort was older (12.2 vs 10.5 years) and had higher rates of intensive care unit admission (77.4% vs 63.8%), vasoactive infusions (57.2% vs 46.1%), troponin elevation (64.4% vs 51.0%), and coronary artery aneurysm (22.7% vs 0.4%) (all P ≤ 0.01). During EST, only 1% (2/208; 95% CI: 0.1%-3.4%) exhibited premature ventricular contractions and no sustained ectopy. Among 160 participants undergoing CPET, 75.6% (121/160; 95% CI: 68.2%-82.1%) achieved oxygen consumption/kg ≥ 80% predicted, and 83.8% (134/160; 95% CI: 77.1%-89.1%) achieved an oxygen pulse ≥80% predicted.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing exercise testing after MIS-C, most had normal exercise capacity, no sustained arrhythmias occurred, and premature ventricular contractions were rare.

articles.title: Exercise Capacity and Mental Health in Adults With a Systemic Right Ventricle.
Fluoroscopy-Only Versus TEE-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Closure: A Comparison of Disk-Type and Plug-Type Devices.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopy alone is emerging as a guidance modality for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO).

OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of fluoroscopy-only vs transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided LAAO and compared the fluoroscopic views required for plug-type and disk-type devices.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, patients undergoing LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only or by TEE with fluoroscopy were divided into a fluoroscopy-only group (n = 603) and a TEE group (n = 156) and further into a fluoroscopy-only disk-type (FODT) (n = 382), fluoroscopy-only plug-type (n = 221), TEE disk-type (n = 76), and TEE plug-type (n = 80) subgroups. Follow-up included TEE at 3 to 6 months and clinical event monitoring.

RESULTS: The fluoroscopy-only group exhibited comparable implantation success (99.8% vs 100%; P = 1.000), peridevice leak rates (≥3 mm: 1.0% vs 1.3%; P = 0.671) and clinical outcomes during follow-up to the TEE group, with significantly shorter LAAO procedure times (40.9 ± 21.7 vs 78.9 ± 35.0 min; P < 0.001). The FODT subgroup required more views under fluoroscopy (3 [3, 3] vs 2 [2, 3]; P < 0.001) despite comparable peridevice leak rates. The clinical outcomes were similar between the TEE and fluoroscopy-only groups and between the FODT and fluoroscopy-only plug-type subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: Whether a disk-type or plug-type device is employed, LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only appears to be as feasible and safe as guidance by TEE. However, disk-type device needed more fluoroscopy views for accurate implantation than plug-type device. In the absence of randomized data, these hypothesis-generating findings should not be extrapolated to less experienced operators or centers.

articles.title: Atrial Fibrillation Screening-to-Anticoagulation Pathways in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an important cause of preventable stroke in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic and treatment gaps may limit screening effectiveness.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate AF screening in LMICs as a screening-to-anticoagulation pathway, focusing on reach, equity, diagnostic confirmation, anticoagulation uptake, and health-system capacity.

METHODS: MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to July 2026. LMIC studies reporting population-facing AF screening or screening-linked care were included. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp CIs; binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models were used in sensitivity analyses. Pathway stages were synthesized from outcome-specific study subsets rather than a single longitudinal cohort.

RESULTS: Thirty-seven reports from 13 LMICs and 1 multinational cohort were included. Across 22 community- or population-based studies, confirmed AF averaged 1.24% (95% CI: 0.79%-1.94%; I2 = 98.8%; 95% prediction interval: 0.16%-8.83%). Newly detected AF averaged 0.95% (95% CI: 0.43%-2.11%; I2 = 99.2%; prediction interval: 0.08%-9.97%). In separate study subsets, prior AF awareness was 50.7%, study-defined high stroke risk or oral anticoagulation indication was 78.9%, and oral anticoagulation coverage among study-defined eligible/high-risk participants was 22.8%. Reach ranged from 9.7% to 98.8%, and confirmation completion was 57.5% to 61.8% in 2 programs.

CONCLUSIONS: AF screening in LMICs identifies substantial but highly variable detection and treatment gaps. Pooled proportions should be interpreted as cross-study summaries rather than expected rates for a specific setting. Effective programs require representative reach, timely confirmation, appropriate stroke-risk and valvular assessment, access to anticoagulation, and longitudinal follow-up.

articles.title: Dietary inflammatory index and continuous glucose monitoring metrics in children with cystic fibrosis: An exploratory cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cystic fibrosis (CF) experience chronic inflammation and early glucose abnormalities. Whether dietary inflammatory potential is associated with glycemic outcomes in pediatric CF remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To examine associations of the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) with continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics and systemic inflammatory markers in children with CF.

METHODS: This exploratory cross-sectional study included 24 clinically stable children with CF aged 6-18 years who were not receiving CFTR modulator therapy. DII scores were calculated from three non-consecutive 24-h dietary recalls. CGM-derived outcomes included mean glucose, time in range (TIR), time above range (TAR), glucose variability, and glucose management indicator (GMI). Inflammatory markers were measured using ELISA. Associations were examined using multivariable regression adjusted for age and sex.

RESULTS: After adjustment for age and sex, higher DII scores were associated with higher mean glucose (β = 0.512, p = 0.021), GMI (β = 0.583, p = 0.011), and TAR (β = 0.466, p = 0.044). The inverse association with TIR was not statistically significant (β = -0.421, p = 0.070). DII was also positively associated with log-CRP (β = 0.528, p = 0.037), whereas other inflammatory markers were not significantly associated with DII.

CONCLUSION: Higher dietary inflammatory potential was associated with greater glycemic exposure and CRP in children with CF. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation in larger longitudinal studies, including CFTR modulator-treated cohorts.

articles.title: Prognostic value of a three-dimensional right atrial volumetric-mechanical coupling index in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right atrial (RA) remodeling is closely related to disease severity and outcomes in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), but the prognostic value of coupling RA structure with mechanical performance remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical correlates, reproducibility, prognostic value, and incremental prognostic information of a three-dimensional right atrial coupling index (RACI) in PAH.

METHODS: In this single-center bidirectional cohort, 158 treatment-naïve patients with PAH underwent right heart catheterization and echocardiography. RACI was calculated as the three-dimensional right atrial volume index divided by tissue Doppler a' velocity. The primary outcome was all-cause death or hospitalization for worsening right heart failure. Prognostic associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC analysis, nested models, and bootstrap internal validation.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 27 patients died and 36 were hospitalized for right heart failure. Each 2-unit increase in RACI was independently associated with the composite outcome (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.04-1.41; P = 0.016), while the cohort-derived cutoff of 3.84 was associated with higher risk (HR 4.09, 95% CI 1.95-8.58; P < 0.001). Higher RACI correlated with larger RA size, higher mRAP/NT-proBNP, and worse RV function. Adding RACI to COMPERA 2.0 and mRAP yielded only a modest increase in C-index (ΔC=0.011, 95% CI -0.008-0.052; P = 0.456), although model fit improved. Intra- and interobserver ICCs were 0.98 and 0.96, respectively.

CONCLUSION: RACI was reproducible and independently associated with adverse outcomes in PAH, providing complementary prognostic information that requires prospective multicenter validation.

articles.title: Cucurbitacin B inhibits the P2RY2/MYC transcriptional axis to disrupt ATP-mediated neuroinflammatory amplification loops.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sustained microglial activation drives neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia. Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a naturally occurring tetracyclic triterpenoid compound mainly found in Cucurbitaceae, exerts anti-neuroinflammatory effects, yet its precise mechanism remains unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the self-amplifying circuit perpetuating neuroinflammation and to determine how CuB disrupts it.

METHODS: The anti-inflammatory effects of CuB were assessed in LPS-stimulated BV-2 microglia. Untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-QTOF-MS) was employed to characterize metabolic alterations. Molecular mechanisms were further investigated in LPS- or ATP-stimulated BV-2 microglia using siRNA knockdown, overexpression, dual-luciferase assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative PCR (ChIP-qPCR), electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) and specific pharmacological inhibitors. The pathophysiological relevance and neuroprotection were validated in a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model.

RESULTS: CuB suppressed inflammatory mediator expression and cytokine secretion in LPS-stimulated microglia. Metabolomics in LPS-stimulated microglia revealed profound dysregulation across eight interconnected metabolic modules, including purinergic signaling and calcium homeostasis. Mechanistically, danger-associated ATP activated P2Y2 receptors, triggering PLC/IP3R-mediated Ca2+ overload that stimulated calcineurin to induce MYC. MYC in turn bound the P2RY2 promoter (confirmed by ChIP-qPCR and EMSA) to drive its transcription, establishing a pathogenic ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop. CuB disrupted this circuit at multiple nodes by reducing ATP release, blocking P2RY2, suppressing Ca2+ overload, inhibiting calcineurin-MYC, and normalizing metabolic dysregulation. In vivo, MYC/P2RY2 upregulation coincided with glial activation, inflammatory cytokine production and infarct expansion.

CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies an ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop that amplifies neuroinflammation. CuB acts as a multi-target circuit breaker, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: A Plasma eMTBR-Tau Immunoassay for Detection of Advanced Insoluble Tau Pathology.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET).

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort.

EXPOSURES: Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243.

RESULTS: The study included 728 participants in 4 cohorts (median age by cohort, 71.0-83.5 years; 41.3%-56.6% female). In the 2 autopsy cohorts (n = 241 and n = 240), eMTBR-tau age- and sex-adjusted geometric means were 0.0021 pg/mL and 0.0040 pg/mL, respectively, at Braak stages I-II vs 0.107 pg/mL and 0.101 pg/mL at Braak stage VI (50.5-fold [95% CI, 26.3-97.0] and 25.2-fold [95% CI, 15.8-40.3] higher for stage VI vs stages I-II; P < .001 for both cohorts). In one imaging cohort (n = 99), compared with tau-PET Braak stage 0, eMTBR-tau levels were 11.0-fold (95% CI, 6.9-17.5) higher at stages III-IV and 59.9-fold (95% CI, 39.5-90.7) higher at stages V-VI. Among participants positive for amyloid-β (Aβ) in another imaging cohort (n = 50), the Spearman rank correlations for eMTBR-tau with tau-PET SUVRs were ρ = 0.52 (95% CI, 0.28-0.70) in Braak regions I-II, 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.86) in regions III-IV, and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.91) in regions V-VI (all P < .001). Immunoassay and mass spectrometry measurements were strongly correlated (Spearman rank correlation, ρ = 0.93 in all participants [n = 108] and ρ = 0.96 in Aβ-positive participants [n = 54]) and discriminated tau-PET positivity similarly (n = 102; AUC range, 0.96-0.99 for the immunoassay and 0.97-0.99 for mass spectrometry).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: A plasma eMTBR-tau immunoassay identified neocortical tau pathology in autopsy and tau-PET cohorts and correlated strongly with mass spectrometry measurements, a proof of principle that eMTBR-tau can be measured by immunoassay as a marker of advanced neurofibrillary tangle pathology.

articles.title: AI Predictive Models for Discharge Disposition in Patients Following Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although a growing number of AI-based predictive models for discharge disposition in patients following primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA) have been constructed, their performance, quality, and applicability remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the performance, quality, and applicability of published AI-based predictive models for discharge disposition in patients following primary TKA.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Database, China Science and Technology Journal Database, and SinoMed Database were searched from inception to May 26, 2025. We included original studies that developed AI-based predictive models for discharge disposition in adult patients (age ≥18 years) undergoing primary TKA. Studies involving simultaneous bilateral or revision TKA or those that did not develop a predictive model were excluded. Risk of bias and reporting quality were assessed using the PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+AI) and TRIPOD+AI (Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis+AI), respectively. Pooled area under the curve values and 95% CIs were estimated using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using the Cochran Q test and I² statistic. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to algorithm type, categorized as machine learning (ML)-based and deep learning (DL)-based models.

RESULTS: A total of 5 retrospective studies from the United States involving 4 ML-based models and 1 DL-based model were included, with sample sizes ranging from 175,042 to 434,550 patients. Age and sex were the most frequently used predictors. All included studies were rated as having a high risk of bias according to the PROBAST+AI checklist. The pooled area under the curve was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67-0.82; I²=99.9%; P<.001) for internal validation and 0.77 (95% CI 0.51-1.00; I²=99.8%; P<.001) for external validation, indicating a high degree of heterogeneity. Subgroup analysis showed no statistically significant difference between ML-based and DL-based models (P>.05).

CONCLUSIONS: AI-based predictive models for discharge disposition following primary TKA demonstrate a certain level of discriminative performance. However, the current evidence is limited, as all included studies were at high risk of bias and showed a high degree of heterogeneity. In addition, all included studies were conducted in the United States, which may limit the generalizability of these findings to other health care settings. Future studies should follow PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI checklists while developing and validating models across different countries and health care systems.

articles.title: A Social Media Mining and Questionnaire Survey Hybrid Approach to Characterizing Caregiver Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices on House Dust Mite Control: Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: House dust mite (HDM) sensitization commonly begins in early life and contributes to persistent allergic airway inflammation and asthma chronicity. Primary prevention via early-life environmental control is a potential pathway to reduce HDM sensitization and asthma risk.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to characterize child caregivers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding pediatric HDM control using a hybrid literature/expert-driven and social media-driven approach and to examine associations between KAP levels, child age, and caregiver HDM-related online engagement.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study comprised two interconnected components: (1) mining of content published between August 2023 and July 2025 from 5 major Chinese social media platforms, analyzed via latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), and (2) a social media-enhanced web-based KAP survey administered in November 2025 to child caregivers in Chongqing, China. In total, 132,341 social media documents and 2275 caregivers of children younger than 18 years were included in the analysis. The main outcomes included social media discourse patterns and domain-specific KAP levels across 5 dimensions: foundational knowledge (K1), recommended control knowledge (K2), attitude toward social media topics (A1), attitude toward recommended methods (A2), and control practices (P). Stratified analysis was conducted by 2 exposure variables: child age (≤3 years vs >3 years) and caregiver HDM-related online engagement (engaged vs nonengaged).

RESULTS: LDA topic modeling identified 5 distinct topic clusters in the social media content. Commercial, emotional, and misleading content collectively dominated the information landscape, accounting for 83.3% (n=110,254) of the included documents (65.8% of the tokens), with commercial content often systematically conflating the concepts of "disinfection" and "mite elimination." Only 16.7% (n=22,087) of the documents (34.1% of the tokens) were classified as health educational content focusing on HDM allergy prevention, reflecting that this valid educational content is substantially longer and more information-dense than other social media posts. The average KAP levels of K1, K2, A1, A2, and P domains were 62.9%, 84.7%, 57.0%, 37.8%, and 25.8%, respectively. Social media emerged as the primary knowledge source (80.7%, n=1836), with methodological knowledge gaps (47.5%) being the top implementation barrier. Caregivers of children ≤3 years had significantly lower self-rated knowledge (23.5% vs 28.3%; P=.01), stronger endorsement of recommended methods, but also greater information overload (odds ratio [OR] 1.39, 95% CI 1.15-1.67; P<.001) and efficacy uncertainty (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.01-1.52; P=.04). Caregivers with HDM-related online engagement showed better performance across multiple items in 5 domains, but also increased traditional practice with uncertain evidence (ultraviolet irradiation: OR 1.85, 95% CI 1.35-2.53; P<.001) and misconception acceptance (allergy impact exaggeration: OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.04-1.87; P=.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Complex and suboptimal KAP levels exist, particularly among caregivers of young children (≤3 years). HDM-related online engagement is associated with both enhanced implementation of control practices and elevated misconception endorsement. These findings reveal critical educational gaps and the necessity of social media intervention.

articles.title: COL4A1 mutation underlying recurrent spontaneous intraparenchymal hemorrhage in an adolescent: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COL4A1-associated vasculopathy is a rare genetic small-vessel disorder characterized by structural fragility of the cerebral vasculature and an increased risk of ischemic stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and leukoaraiosis. Its implications for acute neurocritical care management remain incompletely defined.

OBSERVATIONS: An 18-year-old male with a prior history of unexplained intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse cerebral microhemorrhages presented 1 year later with acute neurological deterioration due to a large cerebellar hemorrhage, requiring emergency external ventricular drain placement and suboccipital decompressive craniectomy. Extensive imaging, vascular, infectious, and inflammatory evaluations were unrevealing. During hospitalization, he experienced recurrent intracranial hemorrhages, including a pontine hemorrhage, out of proportion with underlying coagulopathy. Following initiation of pharmacological deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis, an additional hemorrhagic event occurred. Genetic testing ultimately revealed a pathogenic heterozygous COL4A1 mutation.

LESSONS: COL4A1-associated disease should be considered in young patients with recurrent or unexplained intracranial hemorrhage and extensive cerebral microbleeds. Early recognition is critical, as standard neurocritical care algorithms including pharmacological thromboprophylaxis may confer increased hemorrhagic risk in the setting of diffuse structural vessel fragility. When identified early, genetic diagnosis should prompt proactive awareness of rebleeding risk and prospective modification of DVT prophylaxis timing and blood pressure targets rather than rigid application of standard ICH guidelines. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26379.

articles.title: Salvage strategies for spinal cord ischemia after flow diverter treatment of a vertebral artery-dissecting aneurysm: illustrative case.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Flow diverters (FDs) are increasingly used for vertebral artery-dissecting aneurysms (VADAs), but coverage of the anterior spinal artery (ASA) may cause spinal cord ischemia.

OBSERVATIONS: A 50-year-old man with an unruptured intracranial VADA underwent FD placement. The FD covered the origin of a large ASA adjacent to the aneurysm. Shortly after treatment, the patient developed quadriplegia and respiratory failure. Angiography showed preserved but delayed ASA flow without in-stent thrombosis. Recurrent neurological deterioration occurred 12 hours later. Suspecting ASA hypoperfusion, retrograde microcatheter-assisted stent massage was performed, successfully repositioning the FD away from the ASA ostium and improving ASA perfusion. MRI confirmed anterior spinal cord infarction. Following rehabilitation, the patient achieved substantial neurological recovery, with a modified Rankin Scale score of 1 at 6 months. Follow-up angiography demonstrated near-complete aneurysm occlusion and preserved ASA patency.

LESSONS: FD coverage of the ASA can result in spinal cord infarction, particularly when collateral circulation is limited. Careful evaluation of ASA anatomy and avoidance of ASA ostial coverage are critical during FD treatment of VADAs. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26617.

articles.title: Medical Interview Performance Using an AI-Based Standardized Patient vs a Human Standardized Patient: Randomized Crossover Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Japan, standardized patients (SPs) have traditionally been recruited to teach medical interview competencies. Recent advances in large language models have enabled increasingly natural conversational interactions, raising the possibility of using AI-based SPs (AI-SPs) for medical interview training. However, medical interview performance during interactions with AI-SPs compared with human SPs remains insufficiently understood.

OBJECTIVE: This randomized single-center crossover trial aimed to compare medical interview performance and learner-reported experiences between encounters with a large language model-based AI-SP and a human SP.

METHODS: Participants were fifth-year medical students undertaking clinical clerkships at Chiba University Hospital. The AI-SP was a text-based simulated patient implemented using GPT-4o. Participants were randomized to AI-SP followed by human SP, or the reverse. A washout period of at least 3 days was set between conditions. Each participant completed 2 cases, depression and appendicitis, in both conditions. For the AI-SP interviews, chat logs were retained, and a physician provided feedback after completion of the 2 cases. Human SP interviews were video recorded, and the physician portraying the SP provided feedback immediately after each interview. Medical interview performance was assessed using selected items from the Mini-Clinical Evaluation Exercise (Mini-CEX), with ratings performed independently by 2 general medicine specialists. Participants completed a self-rated questionnaire (7-point Likert-type scale) regarding learning satisfaction, perceived rapport formation, and active engagement in history taking.

RESULTS: Forty-eight participants were analyzed. The Mini-CEX-based mean total score was significantly higher for the human SP than for the AI-SP (23.9, SD 1.7 vs 22.7, SD 1.7, respectively; mean difference 1.24; t47=3.7; P=.001). Scores for history taking and overall clinical competence were higher in the human SP condition. Interrater reliability (intraclass correlation coefficient of 2,1) was 0.76 (95% CI 0.66-0.83). No significant differences were found between conditions for learning satisfaction (human SP: mean 5.9, SD 1.1; AI-SP: mean 6.0, SD 0.8) or perceived rapport formation (human SP: mean 5.4, SD 1.3; AI-SP: mean 5.3, SD 1.3). Active engagement in history taking was significantly higher in the AI-SP condition (human SP: mean 5.8, SD 1.1; AI-SP: mean 6.2, SD 0.7; t47=2.7; P=.009).

CONCLUSIONS: Medical interview performance differed between the 2 SP conditions, with higher history taking and overall clinical competence scores in the human SP condition. The text-based nature of the AI-SP and the absence of nonverbal cues may have contributed to these differences. Although no significant differences between conditions were observed in most other assessment outcomes, learning satisfaction, or perceived rapport, self-rated active engagement in history taking was higher with the AI-SP condition. AI-SPs may offer a complementary modality for medical interview practice; however, this study assessed performance during simulated encounters rather than subsequent learning gains or performance with real patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN Clinical Trials Registry UMIN000056228; https://center6.umin.ac.jp/cgi-open-bin/ctr_e/ctr_view.cgi?recptno=R000064153.

articles.title: Eliciting Reader Preferences for Automated Systematic Gray Literature Reviews: Best-Worst Scaling Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automation can be a useful efficiency tool for saving time in systematic reviews, but a trust gap and a steep learning curve persist concerning its accuracy and ease of use. It remains unknown whether these adoption barriers apply to the more complex process of systematic gray literature reviews (SGLRs), especially given the rapid evolution of large language models.

OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to identify the preferred features of SGLRs generated using an automation tool (automated SGLRs).

METHODS: Participants aged 18 years or older with experience using evidence from systematic reviews were recruited. A cross-sectional online Best-Worst Scaling Questionnaire was distributed through the authors' contacts, professional networks, and social media platforms. Descriptive statistics and multinomial logistic regression were used to estimate the baseline model for preferred features of automated SGLRs, while mixed logit analyses were used to explore subgroup heterogeneity.

RESULTS: A total of 168 respondents, comprising researchers, academicians, health care professionals, health policymakers, and postgraduates, completed the study. Multinomial logistic regression found that the top 3 preferred features for automated SGLRs were (1) high precision and sensitivity comparable to manual methods (best-worst [BW] score 269, and M-logit estimate B=2.26, odds ratio [OR] 9.60, 95% CI 7.72-11.93; P<.001), (2) acknowledgment and detailed explanation of the AI algorithms (BW score: 218, B=2.06, OR 7.85, 95% CI 6.35-9.7; P<.001), and (3) involvement of more than 2 independent human reviewers in the process (BW score: 118, B=1.54, OR 4.68, 95% CI 3.84-5.72; P<.001), when compared to the reference feature, which was the acceptance of automated SGLR output by peer colleagues. Subgroup analysis using a mixed logit model suggested that respondents aged 18 to 29 years exhibited the highest relative utility weights for detailed explanations (B=0.60, OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.29-2.55) and acceptance by everyone (B=0.35, OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.05-1.90) compared to other age groups. In contrast, academicians (B=1.36, OR 3.91, 95% CI 1.51-10.17) might prefer the detailed explanation feature of automated SGLRs more than those in other professions.

CONCLUSIONS: The study concludes that automation tool developers should prioritize the accuracy of automated SGLRs, ensure algorithmic transparency, and integrate human-in-the-loop processes, as respondents most strongly preferred these features, which may support user trust.

articles.title: A North American experience with the "French Paradox" technique in total hip arthroplasty: up to 5-year follow-up.
articles.journal: Bulletin of the Hospital for Joint Disease (2013)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cement use in total hip arthroplasty (THA) is a topic of ongoing research and debate. The French Paradox cement technique, first described in European arthroplasty literature, achieves a thin (<2 mm) cement mantle by preparing the femoral canal only slightly larger than the femoral implant. The technique was coined the "French Paradox" because a French-designed stem showed excellent long-term outcomes despite previous evidence that thin cement mantles can be prone to failure.

PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to describe a North American experience with femoral stems implanted using the French Paradox cement technique.

STUDY DESIGN/METHODS: This was a retrospective study of 125 patients who underwent primary, unilateral THA using the French Paradox cement technique between 2020 and 2023 at 3 academic health systems and had minimum 2-year follow-up. Demographic, implant-related, perioperative, radiographic, and complication variables, as well as patient-reported outcome measures and postoperative variables, were collected at baseline and all available postoperative follow-ups. Chi-square, t test, and ANOVA were used to assess statistical significance, with a significance level of 0.05.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV.

RESULTS: Of the 125 patients, 84% were women, 86% were White, and 5% were current smokers. The mean age of the cohort was 73 years, the mean Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was 3.6%, and 96% of patients had an ASA score of either II or III. There was 1 readmission (0.8%) within 90 days of surgery, which was due to sepsis of gastrointestinal origin. Two patients (1.6%) underwent revision at a mean time of 14 months, 1 for acute PJI and 1 for acetabular component loosening. There were no femoral stem complications, including no instances of loosening, periprosthetic fracture, or stem subsidence. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) showed consistent and meaningful improvements in HOOS, JR and Forgotten Joint Score (FJS).

CONCLUSION: The French Paradox cement technique demonstrated exceptional outcomes up to 5 years with no instances of femoral complications (loosening, subsidence, periprosthetic fracture, or stem failure). In appropriately selected patients and with compatible femoral stem designs, the French Paradox cement technique represents an effective cemented femoral fixation strategy with excellent early to mid-term survivorship.

articles.title: Consensus Statements on the Clinical Practice for Patients With Fontan-Associated Liver Disease.
articles.journal: Hepatology research : the official journal of the Japan Society of Hepatology
articles.abstract: The Fontan procedure has been transformative for patients with univentricular physiology. By using a single ventricle as the systemic pump and relying on passive venous return to drive pulmonary circulation, Fontan circulation alleviates cyanosis and heart failure, allowing children to engage in normal activities during school and adolescence. Nevertheless, Fontan circulation is characterized by chronically elevated systemic venous pressure, which leads to systemic venous congestion and long-term multiorgan effects. Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD) is now recognized as a major long-term complication. Approximately 50% of patients develop hepatic abnormalities within 10-20 years after surgery, and some progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Despite this risk, strategies to identify individuals at high risk for early HCC and to provide better prognostic information remain limited. This article compiles knowledge from congenital heart disease specialists and hepatologists on FALD, including areas where evidence is limited. By facilitating early diagnosis, structured follow-up, and multidisciplinary management of FALD, this initiative aims to improve outcomes, build a nationwide clinical experience, and ultimately support the development of formal, evidence-based guidelines for FALD management.

articles.title: Preoperative Six-Minute Walk Distance Predicts Mortality After Durable Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification remains a challenge in advanced heart failure before durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. We assessed whether preoperative six-minute walk distance (6MWD) was associated with all-cause mortality and compared its discrimination with peak oxygen uptake (pVO2). In this retrospective single-center cohort (January 2016-May 2025), 136 of 206 implanted patients had an eligible preoperative 6MWD. Deaths through May 29, 2026, were ascertained from recorded death dates. During follow-up, 85 patients died; median observed follow-up was 871.5 days. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.712 for 6MWD (n = 136) and 0.639 for pVO2 (n = 127); paired comparison in 127 patients showed no significant difference (DeLong p = 0.212). Each 50 m increase in 6MWD was associated with lower mortality (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.88, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.79-0.98). Patients walking less than 350 m had worse survival (log-rank p = 0.002; HR: 1.98, 95% CI: 1.27-3.11). The association persisted after adjustment for age, INTERMACS profile, and device type (HR: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.27-3.54). Preoperative 6MWD may contribute to risk stratification before durable LVAD implantation; the threshold requires external validation.

articles.title: The Diversity of Mitochondrial Calcium Signaling.
articles.abstract: Mitochondria are central hubs of intracellular Ca2+ signaling, sensing, integrating, and responding to cytosolic Ca2+ transients through tightly regulated uptake and efflux pathways. Despite its fundamental role in cellular physiology, the mechanisms by which mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling contributes to tissue-specific pathologies remain poorly understood. Disruption of this ancient and ubiquitous process can lead to various disease phenotypes, including neurological disorders, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, and liver disease. This review highlights how extensive heterogeneity in the molecular composition, regulation, and spatial organization of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling machinery underlies these pleiotropic outcomes. Physiological insights are examined alongside systems-level approaches, such as comparative genomics, evolutionary analyses, and protein-protein interaction mapping, to reveal context-specific architectures of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling. Collectively, these advances provide a framework for understanding how mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and efflux pathways are tailored to organ-specific functions and vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Nonenzymatic Asn Deamidation of GAD65 Generates HLA-DRB1*03:01-Restricted Neoepitopes in Type 1 Diabetes.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: GAD65-reactive antibodies are common in individuals with DRB1*03:01 haplotypes and diabetes, and benefits from GAD65 therapy are linked to DRB1*03:01 genotypes. DRB1*03:01 prefers Asp in binding pocket 4, such that Asn deamidation, a modification documented in islets, could generate neoepitopes. DRB1*03:01 should present GAD65 epitopes, but few have been reported. We aimed to identify DRB1*03:01-restricted GAD65 epitopes recognized in individuals with type 1 diabetes (T1D). We defined wild-type and Asn-deamidated GAD65 epitopes that are bound by DRB1*03:01 and assessed their immunogenicity through in vitro T-cell assays. In total, three deamidated and four unmodified GAD65 peptides elicited detectable T-cell responses in individuals with T1D. T-cell clones and lines recognizing each GAD65 epitope were isolated and studied, demonstrating that Asn-deamidated GAD65 epitopes are recognized with higher affinity than unmodified GAD65 epitopes. Furthermore, islet-derived T cells from pancreatic organ donors with T1D recognized Asn-deamidated and unmodified GAD65 epitopes. In total, our work identifies wild-type and deamidated epitopes that drive GAD65-specific T-cell responses in individuals positive for DRB1*03:01. These epitopes can now be applied to characterize GAD65-specific T-cell responses during diabetes progression and in the setting of clinical trials.

ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS: DRB1*03:01 is associated with GAD65 autoantibodies and immune modulation with GAD65 protein, but few reliable epitopes have been reported. We aimed to identify relevant GAD65 epitopes recognized in individuals positive for DRB1*03:01. We identified regions of GAD65 that are recognized by CD4+ T cells in individuals with DRB1*03:01 haplotypes and type 1 diabetes, including wild-type and Asn-deamidated epitopes. T cells recognized deamidated GAD65 with higher affinity than wild-type GAD65. GAD65-specific T cells are present among islet-derived T cells from pancreatic organ donors, suggesting a direct role in islet autoimmunity.

articles.title: Characterization of Image-Negative Hyperinflammatory Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure and its Outcomes in Acute Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is the commonest organ failure in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (AP), a hyperinflammatory condition. However, its causes and pathophysiology, though often attributable to acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), are not well-known.

METHODS: We prospectively studied patients with severe AP and AHRF. These patients were evaluated with blood gas analysis, chest imaging including lung ultrasonography, computed tomography, and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels in a subset of patients. The causes of AHRF were the primary outcome measure.

RESULTS: We included 297 patients with AP. Of them, 104 (35%) patients (mean age 37.4±14.4 y) developed AHRF: 65 (62.5%) had grade II, 27 (26.0%) had grade III and 12 (11.5%) had grade IV AHRF. Among those with AHRF, 24 (23%) met the criteria for ARDS, 10 (9.6%) had pleural effusion contributing to hypoxemia, and 4 (3.8%) had interstitial alveolar syndrome. However, the majority i.e., 63 (60.5%) patients had no radiologic correlate of AHRF and had signs of severe systemic inflammation, including high serum IL-6 levels. This was termed as 'Image-negative hyperinflammatory AHRF'. The mortality in patients with AHRF was 35.6%.

CONCLUSION: AHRF develops in one-third of patients with severe AP with a high mortality. The majority of patients have 'Image-negative hyperinflammatory AHRF'.

Genetic architecture of skeletal maturity and pleiotropic links with adiposity.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Advanced bone age is associated with obesity, precocious puberty, and insulin resistance, but its genetic basis and pleiotropic relationships with endocrine and metabolic traits remain poorly understood in East Asians. We aimed to characterize the genetic architecture of skeletal maturity and investigate shared genetic and potential causal relationships with anthropometric, metabolic, and reproductive traits.

METHODS: We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of skeletal maturity in 3,851 Han Taiwanese participants and used GWAS summary statistics from six East Asian biobanks for cross-trait analyses. Genetic correlations and potential causal relationships were assessed using linkage disequilibrium score regression and Mendelian randomization (MR). Body mass index (BMI) polygenic risk scores (PRSs) were evaluated for advanced bone age using Cox regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. Shared BMI-skeletal maturity loci were identified by cross-trait meta-analysis and colocalization.

RESULTS: A genome-wide significant locus for skeletal maturity was identified at ARHGAP39. Skeletal maturity showed positive genetic correlations with adiposity-related traits and type 2 diabetes liability and an inverse correlation with age at menarche. MR findings were consistent with a potential causal contribution of adiposity to skeletal maturity. Each 1- SD increase in BMI PRS was associated with a 35% higher risk of advanced bone age (adjusted hazard ratio 1.35, 95% CI 1.25-1.46). Cross-trait analysis identified shared loci with BMI, including a colocalized signal near TFAP2B.

CONCLUSIONS: Skeletal maturity shares genetic architecture with adiposity and metabolic traits, with genetic evidence suggesting a potential contribution of adiposity to advanced bone age risk in East Asians.

Integrated medical and nutritional therapy with low dose peritoneal dialysis in patients with severe CKD (I-COPE CKD): a multicentre prospective study in Italian nephrology units.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In chronic kidney disease (CKD), efficacy of medical and nutritional treatment (MNT) decreases with worsening of residual kidney function. The integration of MNT with a "low-dose" peritoneal dialysis (PD) may associate with better control of complications and delayed need of "full-dose" dialysis.

METHODS: We performed a multicentre, prospective, study enrolling consecutive adult patients with CKD stage 5 under stable nephrology care, who required dialysis start because of complications not responsive to MNT, as recommended by current guidelines. Patient enrolled in I-COPE arm added a low-dose PD - defined as CAPD 1-2 exchanges/24h or APD≤4 sessions/week - to MNT. We used as control group patients who refusing any kidney substitutive therapy did continue their MNT. The main outcome was the time to the composite endpoint of full-dose dialysis (defined as CAPD≥3 exchanges/24h, or APD≥5 sessions/week, shift to haemodialysis) or all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: We studied 405 patients (I-COPE=205, Controls=200) with a mean age of 64±14 years, basal eGFR 8.7±2.1 ml/min/1.73m2, with at least two complications unresponsive to MNT, from 24 Nephrology Units in Italy. Median time to the composite endpoint was 23 months [95% CI, 18-27] in I-COPE and 10 months [95% CI, 9-12] in the control arm (P<0.001). The adjusted risk of composite endpoint was reduced by 69% in I-COPE arm vs the control group (HR:0.31, 95% CI:0.23-0.40; P<0.001).

CONCLUSION: An integrated strategy combining low-dose PD with MNT associates with a delayed transition to full-dose dialysis as compared with patients that continue only MNT.

articles.title: Cosmetic-Oriented Deep Brain Stimulation: A No-Shave Cranial and Trans-Axillary Fossa Implantable Pulse Generator Implantation Technique.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an established therapy for movement disorders. However, conventional DBS often involves complete scalp shaving and a visible subclavicular incision for implantable pulse generator (IPG) placement, which may cause cosmetic and psychological burden, particularly in younger or female patients. To address these issues, we developed a cosmetic-oriented DBS technique combining a no-shave cranial approach with trans-axillary fossa IPG implantation.

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective series, we analyzed 60 consecutive patients who underwent DBS implantation using a no-shave cranial approach with trans-axillary fossa IPG placement. Procedural characteristics and postoperative complications were reviewed retrospectively.

RESULTS: Sixty patients underwent DBS implantation with this cosmetic-oriented protocol. The mean age at surgery was 50.4 ± 14.7 years, and the mean follow-up was 31.6 ± 18.3 months. The mean operative time, including IPG placement, was 159.1 ± 64.4 min (range 70-353). Early postoperative infection occurred in 2 patients (3.3%), both confined to the axillary IPG pocket within 1 month; no cranial infections or hematomas were observed. Non-infectious complications occurred in 3 patients (5.0%) (one cervical extension foreign-body reaction, one cranial insertion-site reaction, and one lateral IPG displacement requiring revision). Mild transient axillary tightness was reported in 10 patients (16.7%) and resolved without intervention.

CONCLUSION: This cosmetic-oriented DBS method demonstrated a low infection rate and consistent concealment of cranial and axillary incisions, with no apparent signal of increased risk in this series. The approach appears technically feasible across different ages and in both sexes, although patient satisfaction was not formally evaluated.

articles.title: Seasonal and weekly variation in drug-induced deaths in Australia, 2000-2021.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Drug-induced deaths are a critical public health problem; understanding the trends in these deaths may inform targeted prevention and harm minimisation strategies. This study aimed to examine long-term temporal trends and seasonal and weekly variation in drug-induced death rates in Australia.

DESIGN: Time series using national mortality records and population estimates from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

SETTING: Australia.

PARTICIPANTS: All unintentional and intentional drug-induced deaths in individuals aged ≥15-years in Australia between 1 January 2000 and 31 December 2021.

MEASUREMENTS: Temporal trends in daily death rates were assessed separately for unintentional and intentional drug-induced deaths, including long-term (entire study period), seasonal (within year) and weekly (within week) trends, and the impacts of national and state public holidays and major sporting events. A data-driven approach using the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) was used for model selection, using polynomial functions and harmonic terms. In secondary analyses, results were stratified by sex, age group, state/territory of residence and whether deaths were attributed to opioids or non-opioid drugs.

RESULTS: Between 2000 and 2021, 29 524 drug-induced deaths were recorded in Australia (21 693 unintentional; 7831 intentional). Unintentional drug-induced death rates showed clear long-term (P < 0.001), seasonal (P = 0.007) and weekly variation (P < 0.001). Unintentional death rates peaked in late winter [0.0148 per 100 000 population in August, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.0145-0.0152] and were lowest in summer (0.0139 per 100 000 population in February, 95% CI = 0.0136-0.0143). Rates were also highest on Saturdays (0.0154 per 100 000 population, 95% CI = 0.0151-0.0158) and lowest on Tuesdays (0.0133 per 100 000 population, 95% CI = 0.0130-0.0137). Temporal trends for unintentional deaths varied by age and sex, with higher rates on Fridays-Saturdays among males in most age groups. Intentional drug-induced death rates showed a clear long-term trend (P < 0.001) and some seasonal variation (P = 0.039), with no weekly variation (P = 0.169). Long-term trends in both unintentional and intentional drug-induced deaths were largely driven by opioids.

SUMMARY: Seasonal and weekly variation in unintentional drug-induced death rates are evident in Australia, highlighting opportunities to target prevention and harm minimisation efforts during high-risk periods. In contrast, intentional drug-induced death rates show little seasonal variation, indicating the need for sustained prevention strategies throughout the year.

articles.title: The World Health Organization's Early Adolescent Skills for Emotions: A Systematic Review on Current Evidence regarding Effectiveness and Implementation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adolescents in many low- and middle-income countries are frequently exposed to adversities such as armed conflicts and economic hardship. These stressors occur during a critical developmental period marked by profound physical, social, and psychological changes, increasing vulnerability to mental disorders. To address this mental health-care need, the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) developed Early Adolescent Skills for Emotions (EASE), a 10-session group intervention for adolescents and their caregivers. This systematic review summarizes current evidence regarding the effectiveness and implementation of EASE.

METHODS: We searched five electronic databases up to July 26, 2025, for trials evaluating the effects of EASE on adolescents' mental distress and caregivers' parenting behaviors. Random-effects multilevel meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences (SMDs) at post-intervention and 3-month follow-up, complemented by a qualitative synthesis of implementation outcomes. Preregistration ID: CRD42023488490.

RESULTS: No evidence was found for superiority of EASE over a 1-session psychoeducation control on overall mental distress or caregiver outcomes. However, for the primary outcome, internalizing symptoms, there was strong evidence of a very small to small favorable effect at post-intervention, SMD = -0.17, 95% CI: [-0.31, -0.04], which was maintained at follow-up. Implementation studies indicated that EASE is acceptable, feasible, and delivered with good fidelity; yet low caregiver engagement and contextual challenges hindered implementation.

CONCLUSION: Observed effects were smaller than those reported for a comparable WHO intervention for adults, highlighting substantial scope for optimization. Additional high-quality trials are warranted to improve the effectiveness of EASE and maximize its potential public health impact.

articles.title: Sustainability of Treatment Success 5 Years after Exposure-Based Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy for Anxiety Disorders.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Achieving sustainable success in the treatment of anxiety disorders remains a central objective in mental health care. Although research has demonstrated the short-term efficacy of psychotherapy, evidence regarding long-term sustainability is limited. This study examined treatment outcomes 5 years after prediction-error-based exposure therapy.

METHODS: For 355 patients (616 eligible; 58% follow-up rate), newly collected follow-up data on anxiety symptoms and psychosocial functioning were compared to pretreatment, posttreatment, and 6-month follow-up data from a multicenter clinical trial characterized by high treatment fidelity.

RESULTS: Improvements in anxiety symptoms and psychosocial functioning that were evident at posttreatment and 6-month follow-up were largely preserved after 5 years. No significant differences emerged between randomized groups of temporally intensified and non-intensified exposure. From 6 months to 5 years, overall remission rates remained stable, with the majority of patients exhibiting no reliable change in symptom severity. Reliable relapse occurred in 4.9% and reliable new remission in 6.5%. Most patients (63.4%) did not seek additional treatment. Among those who did, depression (64.2%) and anxiety (60.5%) were the most frequently cited reasons, although only a minority (6.0%) sought further treatment exclusively for anxiety. Additional treatment during the follow-up period was associated with higher symptom severity throughout assessments.

CONCLUSION: These findings highlight the sustainability and long-term public health benefits of exposure-based CBT for anxiety disorders. Most patients do not need additional treatments for mental disorders even 5 years after treatment. Nevertheless, further efforts are needed to optimize interventions for those patients who do not achieve remission or experience relapse.

articles.title: Placebo Effect of Verbal Instructions Coupled with Pharmacological Treatment: Results from a Randomized Controlled Trial in Migraine Patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Verbal instructions modulate the expectation concerning a given drug. Knowing that the prescribing clinician is positive and enthusiastic toward the prescribed treatment may lead to positive expectations. We tested whether administering strongly positive verbal instructions together with a pharmacological prescription might trigger a placebo effect in migraine patients.

METHODS: Outpatients (n = 102) were randomly assigned to: (a) an experimental condition: the pharmacological prescription was coupled to strongly positive verbal instructions; (b) a control condition: the prescription was coupled to positive verbal instructions. Subjects were assessed before the prescription (T0), 7 days (T1), 15 days (T2), 1 month (T3), 2 months (T4), and 3 months after it (T5). At each assessment point, Headache Impact Test (HIT-6) and two Numeric Rating Scales (NRSs) were proposed. Kellner's scale of change was administered at T1-T5.

RESULTS: Patients who received strongly positive instructions had no HIT decrease (p = 0.177; η2 = 0.034). Patients who received positive instructions had HIT decrease (p = 0.006; η2 = 0.770). No difference was found between the groups. No significant across timepoints change of expectations was observed in the group who received strongly positive instructions (p = 0.433; η2 = 0.021) or in the group who received positive instructions (p = 0.151; η2 = 0.037). Since the first group had a decrease across timepoints of the score while the second group had a peak at T2, difference between them was statistically significant (p = 0.029; η2 = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: Strongly positive verbal instructions did not produce placebo effect.

articles.title: Therapeutic Change May Begin before the Therapist and Patient Ever Meet: Pretreatment Alliance Changes Predict Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Mechanisms of change are widely assumed to be activated by the onset of treatment. This foundational premise underlies decades of psychotherapy research and guides the timing of measurement and intervention in clinical science. The present study challenges this assumption by demonstrating that one of the most well-established predictors of treatment outcome - the therapeutic alliance - not only changes before therapy begins, but that these early, pretreatment changes predict both alliance development and symptom reduction throughout treatment.

METHODS: In a randomized controlled trial for depression (N = 100), the therapeutic alliance was assessed twice before patients met their therapist and weekly thereafter.

RESULTS: The pretreatment change in alliance significantly predicted subsequent alliance dynamics and clinical improvement, above and beyond baseline levels. The findings remained robust even after controlling for pretreatment outcome expectations and previous treatment experience.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that mechanisms traditionally viewed as the result of treatment targeting may, in fact, be antecedents. By revealing pre-treatment shifts in a mechanism once thought to be non-existent prior to patient-therapist contact, this work may challenge fundamental assumptions in clinical psychology and highlights the need to reconceptualize mechanisms of change as person-specific dynamic signatures that characterize individuals even before psychotherapy begins. Such a shift has implications for how we define, measure, and intervene on core mechanisms of human change.

articles.title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning.
articles.abstract: Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations. Third, we formulate coordinated testing and isolation as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem with a flow-based responsibility-aware reward that attributes transmission costs across connected regions. Using community-level mobility data from Shenzhen, China, we show that ODE-DynNet reduces infection cost by 88% (from 4,930 to 590) relative to the non-steady partially observable, decoupled policy that uses the raw proxy without reconstruction. The same pipeline remains effective across transmission intensities and reporting-delay settings, indicating that explicit observation modeling and state reconstruction are useful preprocessing steps for learned epidemic-control policies under incomplete surveillance.

articles.title: NF-κB/Dif-driven miR-1000 feedback restrains toll signaling via targeting Myd88 to restore Drosophila immune homeostasis.
articles.abstract: Innate immune homeostasis is vital for animal survival and requires precise control of both the intensity and duration of immune signaling. Although microRNAs (miRNAs) are known to fine-tune immune responses, their transcriptional regulation mechanisms during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify an NF-κB-dependent miRNA feedback loop essential for Drosophila Toll pathway.
