Through dynamic expression profiling and functional genetics, we demonstrate that the NF-κB transcription factor Dif directly activates miR-1000 transcription upon Gram-positive bacterial infection, while miR-1000 in turn targets the adaptor Myd88 mRNA for degradation. Moreover, we show that upon immune challenge, miR-1000 is significantly induced in the fat body, and fat body-specific manipulations confirm that Dif activates miR-1000 transcription and miR-1000 directly targets Myd88 in this key immune tissue. This dual function of Dif - concurrently inducing immune effectors (e.g., Drosomycin) and their suppressor miR-1000 - establishes a self-limiting circuit: Dif/miR-1000/Myd88 axis. Crucially, miR-1000-mediated suppression of Myd88, the hub of Toll pathway, constrains signal transduction and enables timely termination. Disruption of this axis prolongs Toll pathway activation and compromises host fitness during infection. Furthermore, this miRNA-adaptor regulatory paradigm is evolutionarily conserved, as miRNAs targeting MyD88 (such as miR-155) also inhibit TLR signaling in mammals. Our work reveals a transcriptionally connected feedback mechanism that dynamically restores animal innate immune homeostasis by targeting a central signaling adaptor.

articles.title: Accessory regions shape genome evolution in the cereal pathogen Fusarium poae.
articles.abstract: Fusarium poae is a widespread component of Fusarium head blight (FHB) pathosystems, frequently detected in cereal crops despite limited symptom development during infection. Populations of F. poae comprise closely related lineages with limited evidence of sexual recombination, raising questions about the genomic variation present within this comparatively cryptic pathogen and how it is organized. Here, a genomic analysis of 84 F. poae isolates, including 12 long-read assemblies, was used to characterize population structure and genomic variation within a predominantly contemporary Canadian collection supplemented by isolates from diverse international origins. Long-read assemblies showed that genomes are partitioned into gene-dense core regions and repeat-rich accessory regions (ARs) predicted to encompass entire chromosomes as well as regions near telomeres of core chromosomes. Homologous AR sequences were broadly shared among strains but showed variable organization across the most contiguous assemblies, precluding consistent assignment of discrete accessory chromosome identities. AR-associated loci also exhibited distinct patterns of sequence similarity across distantly related Fusarium species, including unusually high similarity to sequences present in F. langsethiae and F. oxysporum genomes. In addition to genes predicted to be involved in regulation, transport, and metabolism, F. poae ARs encode candidate effectors, secondary metabolite biosynthesis gene clusters, putative antifungal resistance loci, enzymes predicted to be involved in plant host interactions, and an expanded family of hydrophobins. Across long-read assemblies, copy number variation within ARs showed similar locus-specific amplification patterns, consistent with both non-random genome dynamics and shared evolutionary history. Together, these findings support a model of compartmentalized genome evolution in F. poae, in which ARs contribute to genomic plasticity and functional variation in a largely recombination-limited population.

articles.title: Impact of COVID-19 surgical delays on chronic venous disease: a multicenter observational study in France.
articles.abstract: IntroductionCOVID-19 lockdowns led to widespread postponement of elective procedures, including endovenous interventions for chronic venous disease (CVD). This study aimed to evaluate the clinical impact of delayed thermal ablation in a real-world French multicenter cohort.MethodsThis prospective, multicenter observational study included 203 adults with documented great or small saphenous vein insufficiency or recurrent varicose veins whose endovenous procedures were postponed during the 2020-2021 lockdowns. Clinical severity was assessed using the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) and CEAP classification at the postponement assessment and at the rescheduling assessment. The primary analysis was performed on patients with a VCSS available at both time points. Paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to assess within-patient change over time.ResultsAmong 203 enrolled patients, 86 (42.4%) had a VCSS available at both time points and were included in the primary analysis. The median delay between the postponement and rescheduling assessments was 80 days (IQR 69-101). Mean VCSS remained unchanged (5.4±3.0 vs 5.4±2.8; mean difference 0.0, 95% CI -0.4 to 0.4). CEAP classification was stable in 89.5% of patients, with no significant overall shift (p = 0.246). Adverse events occurred in 3.5% of cases, mainly superficial vein thrombosis. Physicians reported a negative impact of the delay in 60% of assessments, and a physician-perceived potential loss of therapeutic opportunity in 7.5% of the full cohort (n = 199) and 20.9% of the paired cohort at rescheduling (n = 86).ConclusionIn this real-world cohort, delayed endovenous treatment for CVD was not associated with clinically evident short-term deterioration in this sample. However, the high rate of missing paired data, the resulting risk of selection bias, and limited statistical power mean that a clinically relevant effect cannot be excluded. These findings suggest relative clinical stability in mild-to-moderate CVD during short-term delays, but further adequately powered studies are required.

articles.title: Etentamig in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Pooled Phase 1 Data of an Investigational BCMA Bispecific Antibody.
articles.abstract: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

articles.title: Coordinated regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism restores endocrine homeostasis in diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic endocrine disorder characterised by impaired glucose and lipid metabolism, resulting in hyperglycaemia, insulin resistance, and endocrine dysfunction. Current treatments mainly focus on glycaemic control, often neglecting interconnected signalling pathways that are essential for metabolic homeostasis and personalised therapy.

METHODS: This study proposes a pathway-specific metabolic regulatory framework (PSMRF) that integrates pathway-centric metabolic analysis with intelligent optimisation to regulate dysregulated glucose and lipid metabolism. The framework includes metabolic biomarker preprocessing, pathway interaction modelling, multi-pathway optimisation, and XGBoost-based prediction. Using clinical biomarkers, including fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, insulin sensitivity, lipid profile, inflammatory markers, and endocrine indices, it simultaneously regulates insulin, AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathways.

CONTEXT: Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed PSMRF achieved 99.18% prediction accuracy, with an insulin sensitivity improvement (ISI) score of 93.74%, outperforming the comparative machine-learning models and demonstrating improved computational assessment of metabolic regulation.

articles.title: A fluorescence sensor based on N-doped carbon dots@molecularly imprinted polymers for detection of ethyl carbamate.
articles.abstract: Ethyl carbamate (EC) is a class 2A carcinogen widely generated during the fermentation of alcoholic beverages, condiments and other foods, and it poses severe threats to human health. Traditional detection methods for EC suffer from complicated operation, high cost and tedious sample pretreatment. Herein, a fluorescence sensor based on nitrogen-doped carbon dots encapsulated within molecularly imprinted polymers (N-CDs@MIPs) was fabricated for the specific detection of EC. The N-CDs with excellent fluorescence performance were synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method and served as fluorescent signal probes. Molecularly imprinted polymers were prepared by a sol-gel strategy, using 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (APTES) as a functional monomer and tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS) as a cross-linker. The fluorescence of N-CDs@MIPs was quenched after specifically binding with EC via the photoinduced electron transfer (PET) effect. Benefiting from the specific recognition of MIPs and the outstanding optical characteristics of N-CDs, the proposed sensor exhibited high sensitivity, excellent selectivity and strong anti-interference ability. The linear detection range for EC was 1-100 μg L-1, and the LOD was calculated to be 0.9412 μg L-1. The sensor was successfully applied to the detection of EC in actual wine samples, with recoveries ranging from 100.70% to 104.12% and relative standard deviations (RSD%) below 5%. This work provides a low-cost, convenient and rapid detection strategy for EC, showing great application potential in food safety monitoring.

articles.title: Group Consensus-Based Secondary Control for Islanded AC Microgrids With Communication Link and Actuator Faults.
articles.abstract: This article proposes an adaptive hybrid event-triggered group consensus-based secondary (GCBS) control method for islanded AC microgrids (MGs) with communication link and actuator faults to achieve voltage restoration. First, a fault-tolerant GCBS protocol is proposed to relax the restrictions on the severity of communication link faults (CLFs) and actuator faults without requiring the exact values of fault bounds. Second, novel hybrid event-triggered mechanisms (HETMs) are designed to reduce communication and computational burdens while maintaining system stability. Then, to address the coordination and control challenges arising from the different operating characteristics of various types of distributed generation (DG), a grouping consensus control method is proposed. The method divides the DGs within the MGs into multiple groups to ensure voltage restoration and flexible coordination under different generation and demand conditions. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in achieving voltage restoration and fault tolerance.

articles.title: Efficacy of Early Ivermectin Administration in Acute Chikungunya Virus Infection: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute and chronic joint pain is the hallmark of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection, often progressing to debilitating persistent joint pain. No approved antiviral therapy is available. We evaluated the clinical and virological efficacy of early ivermectin administration in acute CHIKV infection.

METHODS: This open-label, randomized trial enrolled and randomized 127 adult patients with acute chikungunya within 72 hours of symptom onset in Thailand. Patients were assigned (1:1) to oral ivermectin (400 µg/kg/day for 3 days) plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Before the 1-month endpoint, 7 patients were lost to follow-up, leaving a finalized complete-case cohort of 120 participants (n = 60 per arm) for primary efficacy analysis. Co-primary outcomes were time to acute joint pain clearance and the proportion of patients with persistent joint pain at 1 month.

FINDINGS: Early ivermectin significantly accelerated acute joint pain resolution compared to controls (median 3.5 days [IQR 2, 6] vs 12.0 days [IQR 8, 35]; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 3.65, 95% CI 2.28, 5.84; p < 0.0001). Ivermectin was associated with a 92% reduction in the odds of persistent joint pain at 1 month (6.6% vs 30%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.08, 95% CI 0.03, 0.21; p < 0.0001). It also shortened fever clearance (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days; p < 0.0001) and accelerated viral clearance by day 7.

CONCLUSIONS: Early ivermectin intervention within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly accelerates clinical recovery, suppresses viral replication, and profoundly reduces persistent joint pain at 1 month. These findings position ivermectin as a promising, scalable therapeutic strategy against CHIKV.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06259383 (Retrospectively registered on February 20, 2024 prior to thawing bio-banked samples for sequential assays, laboratory assay and final analysis).

UNLABELLED: Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06259383..

articles.title: Genetic imprinting of HLA-DP variability on cellular and humoral immunity to cytomegalovirus.
articles.abstract: The influence of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genetic variability on immunity to human cytomegalovirus (CMV) is poorly understood. We conducted a translatome-wide prediction of CMV-encoded peptide binding to frequent HLA class II DP molecules, and investigated DP-restricted CD4+ T cell responses and CMV serostatus in healthy individuals. The results were correlated with genetic DP variants, which were classified into four composite functional supergroups (SG), defined by natural killer receptor NKp44 binding, expression levels and peptide presentation. DP variants with low expression and predicted CMV-peptide presentation but the capacity for NKp44 binding (SG1) were associated with weaker anti-CMV CD4+ T cell responses compared to DP variants with opposite features. Intriguingly, SG1 homozygosity increased the likelihood of CMV seropositivity in hematopoietic stem cell donors. Our data demonstrate opposing footprints of genetic DP variability on CD4+ T cell and serologic responses to CMV, highlighting a central role for HLA-DP in governing innate and adaptive CMV immunity.

articles.title: Component specific sleep-cognition associations in ICU professionals in India.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rotating shift work in intensive care units (ICUs) disrupts circadian alignment and sleep homeostasis, impairing cognition. Global sleep and cognitive scores may obscure component- and domain-specific effects, and testing multiple sleep components against multiple cognitive domains risks false-positive findings unless corrected.

AIMS: To examine associations between individual Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) components and item-level Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) performance in ICU healthcare workers, with multiple-comparison correction and adjustment for confounders.

METHODS: Cross-sectional study in a tertiary hospital in eastern India. Forty-five ICU professionals working rotating shifts completed the PSQI (seven components, scored continuously) and MoCA (eight item scores plus one derived composite). Spearman correlations were computed for all 63 pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction within each PSQI-component family. Associations reaching nominal significance were tested in multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, occupation and ICU experience, with robust standard errors and bootstrap confidence intervals.

RESULTS: Five of 63 correlations reached nominal significance (P < 0.05). Only daytime dysfunction with the attention-executive composite survived both correction and adjustment (rho = -0.43, corrected P = 0.026; adjusted beta = -0.94, 95% CI -1.50 to -0.38, P < 0.001; adjusted R-squared = 0.31). Sleep latency with digit span and sleep medication use with trail making persisted after adjustment but not after correction.

CONCLUSIONS: Only daytime dysfunction was associated with cognitive performance, specifically attention-executive performance, after both correction for multiple testing and adjustment for confounders, supporting a targeted rather than global approach to sleep-related cognitive risk in critical care.

articles.title: Matching the Fixation to the Fracture: Who to Fix, When to Operate, and How to Choose the Technique for Surgical Stabilization of Rib Fractures.
articles.abstract: BackgroundAdvances in surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) include extra-thoracic (ET) and intrathoracic (IT) plating, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), and cryoablation. As techniques and indications for SSRF expand, the literature guiding selection of optimal fixation strategies remains limited. We reviewed our institutional experience using extra-thoracic (ET), intrathoracic (IT), and combination (COMBO) plating to illustrate how fracture anatomy and associated thoracic injuries may assist with surgical decision-making.MethodsA retrospective review was performed of adults undergoing SSRF at a level I trauma center between January 2019 and March 2026. Demographics, injury characteristics, operative details, and clinical outcomes were analyzed along with resource utilization and fracture location. Multivariable generalized linear models explored potential predictors of intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay (LOS), hospital LOS, postoperative opioid requirements, and hospital cost. An exploratory subgroup analysis evaluated cryoablation.ResultsAmong 116 patients who underwent SSRF, 72 received ET plates, 20 IT, and 24 COMBO. Intrathoracic and COMBO fixation were associated with greater use of VATS and cryoablation (P < 0.001). Combination was more frequently used for flail segments (P = 0.002). Intrathoracic fixation was associated with shorter ICU LOS (P = 0.029) and lower opioid requirements (P = 0.038). Cryoablation was associated with shorter ICU LOS, ventilator days, hospital LOS, and lower opioid use. Posterior fractures were more commonly managed with ET plates (P = 0.002).DiscussionIntrathoracic fixation facilitates adjunctive VATS and cryoablation use without an associated increase in operative time. Combining IT and ET techniques may optimize access and stabilization of flail fracture patterns. An anatomy-based approach to SSRF may guide selection of rib fixation methods.

articles.title: The Influence of Race and Socioeconomic Status on Response to Walking Intervention Poststroke: A Secondary Analysis From a Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of neurologic physical therapy : JNPT
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Daily walking activity supports cardiovascular health, reduces recurrent stroke risk, and improves quality of life, making it a primary rehabilitation goal for individuals poststroke. While racial and socioeconomic disparities in general poststroke functional outcomes are well documented, less is known about their influence on real-world walking activity. This study examined whether race moderated the relationship between neighborhood socioeconomic status (SES) and change in walking performance following a 12-week intervention in individuals with chronic stroke.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of the Promoting Recovery Optimization with WALKing Exercise after Stroke (PROWALKS) clinical trial, which tested 3 interventions to improve walking activity. Walking performance was measured as steps per day (SPD), neighborhood SES was represented by the Area Deprivation Index, and race was self-reported. A moderated multiple regression tested whether race (White vs. non-White) moderated the association between SES and change in SPD, adjusting for age, sex, time since stroke, baseline walking capacity, and intervention group.

RESULTS: A total of 187 individuals with complete pre- and postintervention step activity data and complete race and SES information were included in this analysis. The overall model explained 14.4% of the variance in SPD change (adjusted R2 = .100, P < 0.001). Neither SES (P = 0.641) nor the Race × SES interaction (P = 0.835) was a significant predictor of change in SPD.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSIONS: Race did not moderate the relationship between neighborhood SES and walking performance in this group of people poststroke. Current literature and findings suggest that structured interventions with participant support may be a potential approach to mitigating disparities observed in stroke recovery.

articles.title: Concordance of a Laboratory-Data Integrated Fluid Targeting Algorithm with Bioimpedance-Derived Volume Measures in Maintenance Hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Objective fluid assessment in hemodialysis often requires dedicated bioimpedance equipment. The Laboratory-Data Integrated Fluid Targeting algorithm uses routine biochemical and dialysis treatment data to estimate extracellular water, intracellular water, and euvolemic body weight. We evaluated its concordance with the Fresenius Body Composition Monitor and explored determinants of method differences.

METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 61 adults receiving stable maintenance hemodialysis for at least 3 months underwent paired assessment during one dialysis session. Agreement was evaluated using Pearson correlation, Deming regression, and Bland-Altman analysis. Exploratory multivariable models were used to examine age, sex, dialysis vintage, diabetes, heart failure, and ischemic heart disease. Clinically prescribed dry weight was analyzed as a separate clinical comparator.

RESULTS: Extracellular-water estimates were strongly correlated (correlation coefficient, 0.87). The mean difference between the Laboratory-Data Integrated Fluid Targeting and Body Composition Monitor estimates was +0.22 L, with 95% limits of agreement from -4.1 to +4.6 L. The correlation for intracellular water was lower (correlation coefficient, 0.80), with a mean difference of +2.7 L and limits of agreement from -3.5 to +8.9 L. Estimated euvolemic weight was strongly correlated (correlation coefficient, 1.0 after rounding), although this partly reflected the shared body-weight component (mean difference, -0.67 kg; limits of agreement, -4.0 to +2.6 kg). Older age was associated with a smaller extracellular-water difference, whereas sex, dialysis vintage, diabetes, heart failure, and ischemic heart disease were not independently associated with method differences.

CONCLUSIONS: The laboratory-based algorithm approximated Body Composition Monitor outputs at the cohort level; however, proportional bias and wide individual limits, particularly for intracellular water, preclude interchangeability. These findings support method concordance but do not constitute independent physiological or outcome validation. Clinical actionability and outcome benefit remain untested.

articles.title: Pulmonary and Critical Care for General Internists: Updates from the American Thoracic Society Conference 2026.
Sleeve Gastrectomy with Adjunct Intestinal Bypass ("Sleeve Plus") Procedures Versus Sleeve Gastrectomy Alone: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Sleeve gastrectomy (SG) has limitations, prompting the development of adjunctive "Sleeve Plus" procedures. This meta-analysis compared outcomes of SG Plus procedures versus SG alone. Thirty-seven studies (4 RCTs, 33 observational) with 4,692 patients were included. Procedure-specific analyses revealed that SADI-S and SASI were associated with significantly greater weight loss and T2DM remission versus SG. No statistically significant differences in major complications were detected; however, the estimates were imprecise and did not exclude a clinically important increase in risk. SG-JJB demonstrated modest weight loss benefits, while comparative safety estimates were limited by sparse events and imprecision. SG-DJB showed modestly higher major complication rates without significant efficacy benefits. Given the predominance of observational data, substantial heterogeneity, short follow-up (median 12 months), and predominantly low-to-very-low certainty of evidence, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Comparative safety and efficacy profiles vary across individual SG Plus techniques, supporting procedure-specific shared decision-making and underscoring the need for long-term randomized controlled trials. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251161779.

articles.title: Evolution of Automated Insulin Delivery Devices in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Insulin delivery has evolved through distinct technological phases, each improving the usability and dosing control and accuracy. This review traces the historical evolution of insulin delivery devices through distinct eras, beginning with the early use of insulin syringes for manual administration, followed by the introduction of insulin pens that improved portability and dosing precision. Subsequently, the emergence of continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII), sensor-augmented pump (SAP) therapy, and finally, the automated insulin delivery (AID) systems, have created a significant breakthrough in the evolution of modern diabetes care. Safety-oriented automation, including low-glucose suspend (LGS) and predictive low-glucose suspend (PLGS), marked the first steps toward closed-loop control. The commercialization of hybrid closed-loop (HCL) systems represented a paradigm shift, enabling real-time, algorithm-driven basal insulin modulation and significantly improving glycemic outcomes, including increased time in range (TIR) and reduced hypoglycemia. Advanced hybrid closed-loop (AHCL) systems have since introduced customizable targets, automated correction boluses, and interoperability standards, creating flexible ecosystems for personalized diabetes management. Fully closed-loop systems have entered clinical trials offering automated insulin delivery independent of meal announcements. Despite these advances, adoption remains limited by suboptimal user-friendliness, intensive training requirements, and high costs leading to inequitable access, with an ongoing need for user engagement, alarm management, and periodic troubleshooting in real-world settings. Looking ahead, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and neural network-based algorithms is expected to drive the next wave of innovation, enabling more adaptive, autonomous, and patient-centered diabetes care.

articles.title: Stepping up from ICS/LABA to FF/UMEC/VI in Patients with Uncontrolled Asthma: Outcomes from the 52-Week PERFORM Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Asthma remains uncontrolled in many patients receiving inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β2-agonist (ICS/LABA), suggesting that guideline-recommended escalation to triple therapy is often delayed. We report outcomes in patients with uncontrolled, infrequently exacerbating asthma (understudied in traditional randomized controlled trials) stepping up from ICS/LABA to fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol (FF/UMEC/VI) from the PERFORM trial.

METHODS: PERFORM, a randomized, open-label, active-controlled, pragmatic trial in symptomatic adults with uncontrolled, infrequently exacerbating asthma, evaluated the effectiveness and safety of FF/UMEC/VI versus usual care ICS/LABA. Outcomes included trough forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1), asthma control (Asthma Control Questionnaire [ACQ-5/-6/-7]), and achieving clinical remission at Week 52 for the step-up (participants treated with ICS/LABA pre-randomization) and overall population. Safety was assessed throughout the study.

RESULTS: Overall, 783 of 1236 participants in PERFORM received ICS/LABA pre-randomization, with 392 and 391 randomized to FF/UMEC/VI and ICS/LABA, respectively. Statistically significant improvements in trough FEV1 were observed for FF/UMEC/VI versus ICS/LABA at Week 24 and were durable to Week 52 (least squares means treatment difference in change from baseline [95% confidence interval (CI)]: 66 ml [29, 103] and 67 ml [28, 106] at Weeks 24 and 52). FF/UMEC/VI showed greater odds of achieving ≥ 0.5-point improvement from baseline in ACQ-7 total score at Week 24 and achieving clinical remission at Week 52 versus ICS/LABA (adjusted odds ratio [95% CI]: 1.54 [1.12, 2.12] and 2.78 [1.82, 4.24]; not multiplicity adjusted). Results (including the Week 52 safety profile) were similar to the overall PERFORM population.

CONCLUSION: Escalation to FF/UMEC/VI from ICS/LABA improved lung function, asthma control, and clinical remission, with no unexpected safety findings versus usual care ICS/LABA at Weeks 24 and 52, consistent with the overall PERFORM population. Initiation with FF/UMEC/VI may address the unmet need for optimized treatment in patients with uncontrolled, infrequently exacerbating asthma.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: GSK ID: 219912/NCT06372496. Supplementary file1 (MP4 149035 KB).

articles.title: Design Strategies in Discrete Choice Experiments for Individuals with Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Patient preference evidence is increasingly important for value assessment and decision making in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). Discrete choice experiments (DCEs) are widely used to elicit patient preferences but may raise feasibility concerns in individuals with cognitive impairment. We aimed to systematically review studies that explicitly evaluated design choices in DCEs for preference elicitation in individuals with cognitive impairment.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL/PsycINFO through January 23, 2026 for studies that evaluated DCE design adaptations or feasibility in cognitively impaired populations. Findings were synthesized narratively according to adaptations and their reported effects on comprehension, task performance, and respondent burden.

RESULTS: We identified six studies. Four categories of design adaptations were identified: attribute description, simplification of choice task structure, visual design and layout, and survey administration. We learned that attribute familiarity and concreteness improved understanding; respondents struggled when the status-quo state was not anchored to their own current health state. Limiting to three options per task and three attributes per option improved completion rates. Greater overlap in attribute levels across options made tasks easier to complete. Use of icons as illustrations improved attribute comprehension, and caregiver involvement in interviewer-administered surveys aided completion.

CONCLUSIONS: Existing evidence suggests that DCEs can be successfully completed by individuals with mild cognitive impairment or early-stage dementia when tasks are appropriately adapted to lessen complexity. However, the evidence base remains limited. Additional methodological research is needed to identify design strategies that improve accessibility of these tasks to those with cognitive challenges while generating meaningful preference information.

articles.title: Neurocognitive Alterations Manifested as Reaction Time Deficits Following ACL Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is associated with changes in cognitive-motor processing that may persist beyond physical recovery and are not fully identified by conventional physical performance assessments.

OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate neurocognitive function as expressed through cognitive-motor performance following ACLR compared with healthy individuals, with particular emphasis on reaction time and higher-order cognitive outcomes.

METHODS: Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase) were searched from inception to December 2025. Eligibility criteria included observational studies on cognitive-motor outcomes in individuals from ACLR recovery and healthy controls. Data extraction followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal tools. Random-effects models were used to calculate standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2, subgroup analyses and publication bias evaluations.

RESULTS: Twenty-one non-randomised studies involving 986 participants Twenty-one non-randomised studies involving 986 participantswere included. Neurocognitive performance showed a significant impairment in reaction time from ACLR recovery with a moderate effect size (standardized mean difference = 0.56, 95% confidence interval 0.41-0.71, p < 0.001) and high heterogeneity (I2 = 78%). In contrast, pooled analyses showed no statistically significant differences for error rate, accuracy, visual memory, or visual motor speed.

CONCLUSIONS: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is associated with persistent reaction time deficits, whereas pooled analyses of error rate, accuracy, visual memory, and visual motor speed did not demonstrate statistically significant differences compared with healthy controls. This pattern suggests selective impairment in the temporal efficiency of cognitive-motor processing rather than generalized cognitive dysfunction. Reaction time may represent a potential marker of altered cognitive-motor processing following ACLR; however, prospective studies are needed to determine its prognostic value and clinical utility for post-ACLR assessment and return-to-sport decision making.

articles.title: Prognostic nutritional index as an independent predictor of mortality after surgical pericardial window.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Surgical pericardial window is an established treatment for symptomatic or recurrent pericardial effusion; however, mortality predictors remain poorly defined.

AIMS: To assess the prognostic value of the prognostic nutritional index (PNI) and inflammation-related indices. We hypothesized that lower PNI would be independently associated with higher mortality.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 72 patients. Associations with mortality were assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression. PNI and the neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) were evaluated in separate models because both include albumin.

RESULTS: Mean age was 69.5 years; 54.2% were male. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and preoperative cardiac tamponade were associated with mortality (p = 0.021 and p = 0.006). Patients who developed mortality had lower lymphocyte counts and albumin levels, higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (all p < 0.05), higher NPAR (2.27 ± 0.56 vs. 1.90 ± 0.50; p = 0.006), and lower PNI (39 vs. 45; p = 0.001). COPD, malignancy, and tamponade were associated with shorter survival. The neutrophil-to-albumin ratio was not significantly associated with mortality (p = 0.058). In adjusted models, higher PNI was associated with a lower mortality hazard (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.907; p = 0.003), whereas NPAR remained associated with mortality (HR = 1.985; p = 0.049). Malignancy was significant in both models; COPD only in the NPAR model.

CONCLUSIONS: Lower PNI was independently associated with mortality after surgical pericardial window. NPAR also showed an adjusted association, although its estimate was imprecise. These exploratory findings require validation in larger cohorts.

articles.title: Pelvic fixation and risk of deep infection in spinal deformity surgery: a comorbidity-aware, matched cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Pelvic fixation is often used in scoliosis surgery to enhance distal stability but may increase deep infection risk due to expanded dissection and subfascial dead space over the sacrum. This study compares the proportion of deep surgical site infection (dSSI) between patients with and without pelvic fixation (PF) and identifies associated risk factors.

METHODS: Patients within the Scoliosis Research Society Morbidity & Mortality Database were divided into a PF and non-PF cohort. After splitting into posterior-only and non-posterior approaches, the cohorts were propensity score matched on 18 patient and procedural variables. A multivariable logistic regression was performed to find independent predictors of dSSI.

RESULTS: In the analytic cohort (n = 4660), dSSI was reported in 44.3% with PF vs 30.7% without PF (p < 0.001). After matching, posterior-only cases showed higher dSSI with PF (43.1% vs 36.9%, p = 0.038), as did non-posterior cases (29.9% vs 24.2%, p = 0.314). Across all 737 matched pairs, the covariate-adjusted conditional logistic regression was not statistically significant (OR 1.22, 95% CI 0.95-1.58; p = 0.124). In the full-cohort regression, PF was associated with dSSI (OR 1.31, 95% CI 1.10-1.56). Posterior approach was associated with higher odds of dSSI (1.41), whereas osteotomy was protective (0.79). Patient predictors included diabetes (1.63), previous spinal infection (1.59), ASA class III-V (1.39), neuromuscular etiology (1.70), body mass index and number of levels fused.

CONCLUSION: PF is associated with more frequent dSSI, although not significantly in the covariate-adjusted matched analysis. dSSI was also associated with several comorbidities. These findings support careful consideration of pelvic fixation in patients with significant comorbidity burden.

articles.title: A quantitative approach to evidence triangulation: development of a framework to address rigour and relevance.
articles.abstract: Triangulation is an approach to strengthen causal inference by integrating evidence from multiple sources. Most studies using triangulation have qualitatively examined whether different studies agree upon the presence of a causal effect, rather than estimated the effect by quantitatively integrating results. Here, we develop a framework for quantitative triangulation. We first address how to relate study-specific research questions to an overall target causal question (relevance) and then assess the directions and magnitudes of bias in each study (rigour), before combining the results using meta-analysis adjusted for the biases. We illustrate our framework by triangulating evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs), Mendelian randomization (MR) and conventional multivariable regression (MVR) to estimate the effect of beta-carotene on coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiovascular disease (CVD). Three RCTs and one MR study showed little evidence of a causal relationship between beta-carotene and CHD (risk ratio (RR) = 1.00 with 95% CI = 0.98 to 1.01 and RR = 1.02 with 95% CI = 0.98 to 1.07, respectively). Seven MVR studies indicated that high intake of beta-carotene reduces CHD risk (RR = 0.83 with 95% CI = 0.76 to 0.91). After applying our framework, the three study designs agreed that there is no strong evidence against the null hypothesis that beta-carotene intake does not affect risk of CHD (RR = 0.99 with 95% CI = 0.82 to 1.21). Findings were similar for CVD. Our framework shows how to address rigour and relevance quantitatively when triangulating evidence from different study designs. We highlight the importance of explicitly defining the target and study-specific research questions.

articles.title: Nasogastric tube malposition despite gastric-appearing aspirate and positive auscultation: the importance of radiographic verification.
Nanoparticle therapeutics for infectious diseases integrating AI-guided design, crispr delivery, phage synergy, and immune modulation.
articles.abstract: Infectious diseases continue to pose a global health challenge, intensified by antimicrobial resistance and limitations of pharmaceutical countermeasures. Nanotechnology offers a promising front against these barriers using intelligent, multifunctional systems. This review explores the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), CRISPR gene editing, bacteriophage therapy, and immune modulation within the framework of second-generation nanoparticle therapeutics. AI-guided modelling enables predictive optimization of nanoparticle design on the basis of size, charge, and surface proteins, targeting specific pathogens and providing enhanced stability. Consequently, nanoparticles serve as precision nanocarriers and protective delivery vehicles for the CRISPR-Cas system, shielding nucleic acid cargo from enzymatic degradation and enabling targeted intracellular delivery via pH-responsive endosomal escape mechanisms. The nanoparticles not only provide protection but also enable tissue-targeting and infection-site-specific delivery of the CRISPR-Cas system, facilitating precise genome editing to reverse resistance in specific pathogens such as HIV and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Phage nanoparticle hybrids further expand antimicrobial potency by enhancing phage stability, delivery, and host range. Moreover, engineered nanoparticles modulate the immune system via immunosuppressive and immunostimulant strategies for reducing hyperinflammation and enhancing pathogen clearance, respectively. Despite such encouraging laboratory outcomes, the clinical translation of AI-integrated nanoparticle platforms still faces a number of obstacles. Large-scale manufacturing, scalability, and reproducibility pose a significant challenge. Regulatory approvals for such multi-modal nano-drugs seem to get bogged down due to vague and scarce exemplary proofs. Furthermore, safety and efficacy apprehensions, unpredictable and complex host-phage interactions, cost-effectiveness, and equitable access remain a subject matter of concern. Conclusively, the convergence of advanced nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and synthetic biology marks the dawn of a transformative era in infectious disease therapeutics where treatment is not only intelligent and adaptive but also ethically and globally inclusive.Clinical trial registrationNot applicable.

articles.title: Prevalent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is associated with osteoporosis and osteopenia in people referred for bone mineral density testing.
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) are common in older adults. This cross-sectional study examined whether ASCVD prevalence differs by bone mineral density (BMD) category in the Manitoba BMD registry (n = 86,991 adults, mean age 64.7 ± 11.0 years, 90.2% women). Total hip (TH), femoral neck (FN), and lumbar spine (LS) BMD was assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and categorized from T-score as normal (≥ - 1), osteopenia (- 1.0 to - 2.5), or osteoporosis (≤ - 2.5). Prevalent ASCVD (hospitalized coronary artery disease, acute myocardial infarction, non-hemorrhagic cerebrovascular disease, peripheral arterial disease; coronary revascularization; and/or congestive heart failure) was ascertained from linked data. Multivariable adjusted logistic regression assessed associations. Among individuals, 10.7% had prevalent ASCVD, 39.1% had osteopenia, and 8.6% had osteoporosis. ASCVD prevalences for the normal, osteopenia, and osteoporosis groups were 9.2%, 11.2%, and 18.2%, respectively. Compared to normal BMD, osteopenia and osteoporosis were associated with higher odds of prevalent ASCVD adjusted for fracture risk factors (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.03-1.15; OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.27-1.49). Associations persisted with further adjustment for cardiometabolic and socioeconomic factors (osteopenia OR 1.18, 95% CI 1.12-1.25; osteoporosis OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.46-1.73). In stratified analyses, ORs were greater in individuals aged 40-64 versus ≥ 65 years (p =< 0.001); no differences were observed for sex (p = 0.225). Similar results were seen at the FN but were inconsistent for the LS. ASCVD is a common comorbid condition with osteopenia, but more so osteoporosis in a routine BMD examination setting. Osteopenia or osteoporosis documentation represents an opportunity for optimized risk factor management, perhaps altering disease trajectory.

articles.title: Emerging formulation strategies of Ageratum conyzoides for enhanced wound repair and tissue regeneration: a review.
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a complex, multistage biological process often compromised by persistent inflammation, oxidative stress, and microbial infection, necessitating the development of effective and targeted therapeutic strategies. Ageratum conyzoides, a traditionally used medicinal plant, has gained significant attention due to its potent anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The present review highlights emerging formulation strategies of A. conyzoides for enhanced wound repair and tissue regeneration. Unlike other reviews that have concentrated on the conventional applications and pharmacological effects of medicinal plants, this review critically examines the integration of A. conyzoides phytoconstituents with advanced drug delivery systems, emphasizing formulation potential, mechanistic relevance, and translational challenges. The botanical profile and rich phytochemical composition, comprising flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and phenolic compounds, form the basis of its pharmacological potential. Mechanistically, these bioactives modulate key pathways involved in wound healing pathophysiology, including cytokine regulation (IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β), growth factor expression (VEGF, PDGF, TGF-β), extracellular matrix remodelling, and oxidative stress attenuation. Emerging and future drugs incorporate phytochemicals from plants combined with innovative drug delivery systems that can address the shortcomings associated with traditional medicine. In this regard, bioengineered drug delivery mechanisms, including nanoparticles, liposomes, time-release matrices, and intelligent bandages, allow for specific and sustained release of phytochemicals, increasing their bioavailability. Enhanced formulations of A. conyzoides might enhance stability, skin permeability, and sustained drug delivery, possibly facilitating the modulation of inflammatory and regenerative pathways; however, these potential benefits require further experimental and clinical validation. Despite this potential, the lack of formulation standardization, limited evidence regarding dermal penetration and pharmacokinetics, together with the lack of well-designed clinical trials remains a significant research gap. Therefore, future research should focus on developing advanced delivery systems for efficient and safe use of A. conyzoides as wound care agents. Overall, these advances highlight the potential of A. conyzoides as a candidate for future wound-care formulations.

articles.title: Flavonoid modulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: The NLRP3 (NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3) inflammasome is a critical mediator of innate immune signaling and plays an important role in the pathogenesis of several chronic inflammatory diseases, including gout, type 2 diabetes, atherosclerosis, and neurodegenerative disorders. Although NLRP3 represents an attractive therapeutic target, clinically approved agents that directly inhibit NLRP3 inflammasome activation remain limited. Flavonoids, a diverse group of plant-derived polyphenolic compounds, have attracted considerable interest because of their ability to modulate multiple molecular events associated with NLRP3 activation. This review critically examines the molecular mechanisms by which six flavonoids- quercetin, fisetin, luteolin, apigenin, kaempferol, and epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG)-modulate the NLRP3 inflammasome. Particular emphasis is placed on their effects on inflammasome priming, NF-κB signaling, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, ASC oligomerization, autophagy, oxidative stress, and related signaling pathways. The available evidence is evaluated according to the strength of mechanistic support and experimental evidence from cellular, animal, and clinical studies. Among the flavonoids reviewed, quercetin and fisetin demonstrate comparatively stronger mechanistic evidence, whereas evidence for luteolin, apigenin, kaempferol, and EGCG is more frequently associated with indirect modulation of NLRP3-related signaling. Despite promising preclinical findings, limitations including poor bioavailability, insufficient NLRP3-specific clinical biomarkers, and limited human evidence remain major barriers to translation. Overall, flavonoids represent promising but clinically unvalidated modulators of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and future studies should prioritize mechanistically specific biomarkers, improved formulations, and well-designed clinical investigations.

articles.title: Opportunistic screening for diabetes and hypertension in dental settings and its implications for Saudi Arabia's health sector transformation: a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Saudi Arabia carries one of the highest global burdens of undiagnosed diabetes mellitus and hypertension, while its dental sector risks marginalisation from the public health agenda under Vision 2030's Health Sector Transformation Program (HSTP). This narrative review aimed to synthesise international evidence on the feasibility, clinical validity, and health system value of opportunistic screening for diabetes mellitus and hypertension in dental settings, and to evaluate these findings against the structural components of the HSTP.

METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Reviews (SANRA) as a quality framework. A structured literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (January 2000 to July 2026), and records were screened against predefined eligibility criteria. Peer-reviewed studies, systematic reviews, and institutional policy documents addressing opportunistic dental screening for diabetes mellitus and hypertension, Saudi epidemiology, and the HSTP architecture were included. Of 953 records identified, 172 studies met the eligibility criteria and 31 were selected for the synthesis using predefined rules.

RESULTS: Global literature consistently demonstrates detection of undiagnosed or poorly controlled diabetes mellitus and hypertension in dental clinic populations, with dental risk scores and point-of-care glycated haemoglobin testing showing moderate accuracy and high patient acceptability, although single chair-side blood pressure readings require confirmation. Referral pathway integrity is the critical implementation determinant. Saudi Arabia's epidemiological profile, dental workforce density, and emerging digital health infrastructure, including the Sehhaty platform and Health Cluster architecture, create favourable conditions for formalising this screening role, although no Saudi study has yet evaluated referral outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Integrating opportunistic non-communicable disease screening into dental workflows within Saudi Health Clusters is supported by consistent observational evidence and aligned with Vision 2030's population health targets, but should be piloted before wider adoption. The Centre for National Health Insurance could incorporate dental screening metrics into its value-based reimbursement framework, and oral health should be embedded within the national primary care pathway. Targeted recommendations are proposed for the Health Holding Company, the Centre for National Health Insurance and the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties.

articles.title: Recurrent prosthetic valve endocarditis with suspected perivalvular abscess caused by Staphylococcus caprae in a bone marrow transplant recipient: a case report.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infective endocarditis (IE) in bone marrow transplantation (BMT) recipients is uncommon but carries high mortality. Recurrent prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) in immunocompromised hosts presents particular challenges in surgical decision-making. Staphylococcus caprae, a coagulase-negative staphylococcus of caprine origin, is rarely implicated in human IE. We report a rare case of recurrent S. caprae PVE with suspected perivalvular abscess in a BMT recipient managed with advance care planning (ACP) and home-based palliative care.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old male had undergone allogeneic BMT for high-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) and was receiving immunosuppression for chronic graft-versus-host disease. Approximately 13 months after BMT, he developed cardiogenic shock due to S. caprae IE causing severe aortic regurgitation and underwent emergency aortic valve replacement (AVR) with a 27-mm INSPIRIS RESILIA bioprosthesis (Edwards Lifesciences) and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting. The initial event has been previously reported. Approximately eight weeks after completion of a 42-day antimicrobial course, he was readmitted with fever and rigors, and blood cultures again grew S. caprae with an antimicrobial susceptibility profile indistinguishable from that of the index isolate; strain-level molecular typing was not performed. Transesophageal echocardiography approximately one month later showed an isoechoic structure at the subaortic curtain, raising suspicion of a perivalvular abscess. Blood cultures remained positive, and a new paravalvular leak developed during follow-up. Through serial multidisciplinary consultations, re-operation was judged to carry prohibitive risk, and the patient declined further surgery. Home-based palliative care with long-term suppressive oral linezolid was chosen in accordance with his preferences. He died peacefully at home with his family approximately 13 months after the index cardiac surgery and 10 months after recurrent bacteremia.

CONCLUSIONS: Recurrent S. caprae PVE with suspected perivalvular involvement in a BMT recipient poses difficult management decisions. Residual prosthetic or perivalvular infection is a plausible explanation, but re-infection cannot be excluded. When reoperation is high risk and inconsistent with the patient's wishes, ACP-guided palliative care with suppressive antimicrobial therapy may be an individualized option.

articles.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a potentially life-threatening condition and often diagnosed late, with many patients presenting in advanced heart failure. This study aimed to examine the demographics, risk factors, comorbidities, clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and maternal and neonatal outcomes METHODS AND RESULTS: This meta-analysis followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 4,341 records up to May 2025, were identified and 122 eligible studies reporting PPCM clinical characteristics, treatments, and outcomes were included. Heterogeneity was explored through meta-regression analyses assessing demographic, clinical, and study-level variables. An aggregate of 66,908 PPCM patients were reported across the included studies, with a pooled mean age of 30.1 years. Black or African women accounted for a disproportionately large proportion of the reported population compared with other racial groups. Approximately 62% of women presented with advanced heart failure (NYHA class III/IV). Pre-existing diabetes mellitus (OR 5.09) and hypertensive disorders, including pre-existing hypertension (OR 10.07), gestational hypertension (OR 7.75), and pre-eclampsia (OR 9.27), were associated with higher odds of PPCM. The pooled mean LVEF at diagnosis was 29.98%, which subsequently improved to 46.47% at 6 months and 49.12% at 12 months. Despite over half of PPCM patients achieving LVEF recovery (55%), maternal mortality remained high at 6% and neonatal mortality at 4%. Pharmacological treatments for PPCM varied widely, with high heterogeneity suggesting substantial differences in prescribing practices across studies.

CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

articles.title: Background Gastric Mucosal Pathology in Diffuse-Type Gastric Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sporadic diffuse-type gastric cancer (DGC) lacks a validated precursor sequence analogous to the Correa cascade in intestinal-type gastric cancer, limiting precursor-based surveillance. We aimed to characterise histological abnormalities in the non-neoplastic background mucosa of DGC resection specimens.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and Scopus were searched from inception to November 2025. Eighteen publications contributed 21 non-overlapping analytical cohorts. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled prevalences and odds ratios (ORs) comparing DGC with intestinal-type gastric cancer.

RESULTS: Pooled prevalences in DGC were 56.8% for Helicobacter pylori (95% CI 39.3-72.8%), 52.9% for chronic gastritis (32.2-72.6%), 30.8% for glandular atrophy (15.3-52.4%) and 37.5% for intestinal metaplasia (24.4-52.7%). Comparative ORs were 0.48 for H. pylori (0.22-1.06), 0.77 for chronic gastritis (0.44-1.34), 0.35 for atrophy (0.17-0.70) and 0.24 for intestinal metaplasia (0.15-0.40).

CONCLUSIONS: Histologically abnormal background mucosa is common in DGC resection specimens, but these cross-sectional findings cannot establish temporality or causality. Prospective studies should distinguish candidate precursor lesions from markers of increased field risk and assess their potential for DGC-specific risk enrichment and earlier detection.

articles.title: Prevalence and utilization of insulin pump and continuous glucose monitoring data in Finnish forensic autopsies.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a common metabolic condition with significance in the forensic context due to the associated risk for fatal dysglycemic events. In all deaths of individuals with diabetes, careful inspection of diabetes management devices is advisable, as they may provide invaluable insights into the circumstances preceding death. This study investigated the prevalence of insulin pumps and Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) devices in Finnish forensic autopsies during the past decade and assessed their utilization in the cause-of-death investigation. Data was retrospectively extracted from a national electronic platform containing all forensic autopsy records 2016-2025, using predefined keyword searches targeted at diabetes, insulin pumps, and CGM devices. Cases were manually reviewed. We found records of 37 autopsied insulin pump cases (median age 41 years (range 18-72); 3.4% of all autopsied type 1 diabetics). Documentation about the insulin delivery system was variable. Cannula fixation was noted in 32.3% and pump history in 32.4% of the cases. The proportion of CGM-associated autopsies among all diabetic autopsies increased from 0.1% in 2016 to 4.1% in 2025, with a total of 352 autopsied CGM cases during the study period (median age 61 years (range 15-94)). CGM data was utilized in 9.1% of the associated cause-of-death investigations. Our findings suggest non-systematic examination of insulin pumps and CGM data in current Finnish forensic cause-of-death investigation practices. Education and standardized protocols for insulin pump examination and CGM data review are recommended to ensure quality and reliability in diabetes-related forensic cause-of-death investigations.

articles.title: A comparative analysis of the safety and tolerability of oral small-molecule versus injectable peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare the safety and tolerability profiles of oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) against established injectable peptide GLP-1RAs, with emphasis on orforglipron, the most clinically advanced class member.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesises receptor pharmacology, Phase 3 clinical trial data, network meta-analyses, and regulatory prescribing-information documents for orforglipron; early-phase data for GSBR-1290 and CT-996 are considered separately as hypothesis-generating only.

RESULTS: Orforglipron occupies a non-canonical orthosteric pocket and elicits Gs-protein-biased signalling; as a chemically stable small molecule, it also eliminates cold-chain dependence and parenteral administration burden. Gastrointestinal adverse events remain the dominant class-effect liability: in ATTAIN-1, nausea occurred in 33.7% of participants receiving orforglipron 36 mg (investigational capsule dose, equivalent to approved 17.2 mg tablet dose), with adverse-event discontinuation at 10.3%; in ACHIEVE-3, orforglipron produced approximately twice the discontinuation rate of oral semaglutide. The six-step dose-escalation protocol (minimum 30 days per step) is the primary modifiable tolerability variable. Orforglipron undergoes hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism with 87% faecal elimination, introducing hepatic-impairment and drug-interaction liabilities absent for peptides while avoiding renal dose adjustment. Shared class risks include pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, acute kidney injury, and a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumour.

CONCLUSION: Orforglipron removes injection, cold-chain and fasting requirements, but its gastrointestinal tolerability is not superior to injectable peptides, and gastrointestinal events were more frequent than with oral semaglutide in direct comparison. Findings should not be extrapolated to other oral small molecules, and although cardiovascular non-inferiority to insulin glargine has now been shown (ACHIEVE-4), placebo-controlled outcome trials are required before cardiovascular or renal benefit can be assumed.

articles.title: Platelet CLEC-2 as an amplifier of synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis.
articles.abstract: Platelets have well-established roles in hemostasis and thrombosis and are increasingly recognized as active regulators of inflammation and immune responses. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), experimental and clinical studies have implicated platelets in synovial inflammation. Platelet depletion markedly attenuates arthritis in the K/BxN serum-transfer mouse model, and collagen-dependent glycoprotein VI (GPVI) signaling promotes platelet microparticle production, which activates fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs) through interleukin-1 (IL-1). More recently, we reported that platelet C-type lectin-like receptor 2 (CLEC-2) promotes proliferation of fibroblast-like synoviocytes derived from patients with RA (RA-FLSs) in vitro and induces the expression of inflammatory mediators, including IL-6. In the same mouse model, platelet- and megakaryocyte-specific CLEC-2 deficiency suppressed arthritis progression without substantially affecting disease onset. These findings support a role for platelet CLEC-2 in the amplification rather than the initiation of synovial inflammation. This review focuses on the emerging role of platelet CLEC-2 in RA and its relationship with podoplanin-positive FLSs. We discuss platelet access to the synovial compartment, CLEC-2-dependent FLS responses, and the possible relationship between CLEC-2 and other platelet-dependent pathways in synovial inflammation. Taken together, current evidence supports a role for platelet CLEC-2 as an amplifier of ongoing synovial inflammation.

articles.title: Beyond BMI in obesity: unsupervised biomarker profiling reveals distinct inflammatory-mucosal immune phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Body mass index (BMI), though remaining the most widely used measure for obesity classification, may not fully capture the biological heterogeneity associated with excess adiposity. We investigated whether biomarker-defined immune phenotypes emerge independently of anthropometric classification in adults without diabetes.

METHODS: Seventy adults across the spectrum of body weight were enrolled. Circulating concentrations of presepsin, β-defensin-2, ferritin, interleukin-6 (IL-6), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP), regenerating islet-derived protein 3 alpha (REG3α), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] were measured. Unsupervised k-means clustering was applied to log-transformed and standardized concentrations of presepsin, β-defensin-2, ferritin, IL-6, hsCRP, and REG3α. BMI, age, and sex, and 25(OH)D concentrations were excluded from cluster generation and subsequently evaluated as external explanatory variables.

RESULTS: Unsupervised clustering identified two distinct immune phenotypes comprising 47 and 23 participants, respectively. Compared with the low-activation phenotype, the high-activation phenotype exhibited significantly higher concentrations of presepsin, IL-6, hsCRP, β-defensin-2, and REG3α (all p < 0.001). Despite these marked biological differences, BMI category distribution was similar between clusters (p = 0.39). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, BMI (odds ratio 1.08 per kg/m2, 95% confidence interval 0.97-1.21; p = 0.14), age, sex, and 25(OH)D concentrations were not independently associated with phenotype assignment.

CONCLUSIONS: Biomarker-defined inflammatory-mucosal profiles showed limited correspondence with conventional BMI categories, suggesting heterogeneity without necessarily establishing distinct underlying biological mechanisms. These exploratory findings support further investigation of biomarker-based approaches to obesity phenotyping in larger studies.

articles.title: Molecular screening of arboviruses in asymptomatic blood donors from Northern Brazil.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asymptomatic infections caused by the arboviruses dengue virus (DENV), zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) pose a hidden risk to blood safety, as viremic donors may contribute to transfusion-transmitted infections with severe outcomes.

METHODS: Viral RNA from 5,954 pools (each pool contains six samples) was extracted using the Chemagic™ Prime™ platform, as part of the Brazilian NAT PLUS system from pooled plasma samples collected at Amazonas Hematology and Hemotherapy Hospital Foundation (HEMOAM) and analyzed by RT-qPCR using the ZC D-Tipagem molecular assay (Bio-Manguinhos).

RESULTS: Over eighteen consecutive epidemiological weeks, 11 CHIKV-positive cases were identified, 4 DENV-positive cases, and no ZIKV-positive detections on the blood bags samples analyzed.

CONCLUSION: The detection of asymptomatic arboviral infections during the rainy season, when environmental conditions favor mosquito proliferation and arbovirus transmission, suggests ongoing silent viral circulation in the region and reinforces the importance of blood donor surveillance.

articles.title: Viral Infections and Dysregulation of Neurotrophin Signaling: Potential impact in the Central Nervous System.
articles.abstract: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

articles.title: Outcomes of Pancreatectomy with Superior Mesenteric Artery Resection: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior mesenteric artery (SMA) involvement is commonly considered a contraindication to surgical resection in locally advanced pancreatic cancer. The role of SMA resection during pancreatectomy remains controversial, with historical data suggesting prohibitive morbidity and poor survival.

METHODS: A systematic search of the literature was performed. Studies reporting on patients undergoing pancreatectomy with concomitant SMA resection were included. Primary endpoints were perioperative morbidity, 90-day mortality, and survival. Additional data on neoadjuvant treatment, patient selection, anticoagulation, reconstruction techniques, and oncological outcomes were also extracted.

RESULTS: In total, 12 studies reporting on 320 patients undergoing pancreatectomy with SMA resection were included. All included studies showed a serious risk of bias and described highly selected patients. Concomitant venous resection was performed in 97% (n = 244/252) of patients and a total pancreatectomy in 63% (n = 173/275). Arterial reconstruction was achieved by graft interposition in 48% (n = 128/269), primary end-to-end anastomosis in 39% (n = 106/269), and splenic artery transposition in 13% (n = 34/269) of patients. Major morbidity and 90-day mortality were 31% (n = 88/284) and 8% (n = 27/320), respectively. Complications included post-pancreatectomy hemorrhage in 19% (n = 39/202) of patients and mesenteric ischemia in 3% (n = 6/202). R0 resection was achieved in 80% (n = 136/171) of patients. Median reported survival from surgery ranged from 8 to 20 months. The highest reported 5-year survival was 21%.

CONCLUSIONS: Pancreatectomy with SMA resection is associated with specific perioperative morbidity and an 8% mortality rate. Since these outcomes were achieved by expert groups under highly selected circumstances, only implementation at high-volume centers with dedicated vascular pancreatic surgery expertise should be considered.

articles.title: Eosinophilic gastritis and duodenitis with esophageal involvement becoming clinically apparent during long-term omalizumab therapy and successfully treated with dupilumab.
articles.abstract: We present a case of non-eosinophilic esophagitis eosinophilic gastrointestinal diseases (non-EoE EGIDs) that became clinically apparent during long-term anti-immunoglobulin E (IgE) therapy with omalizumab for bronchial asthma (BA). A 53-year-old woman with severe BA, atopic dermatitis, multiple drug allergies, and diabetes mellitus presented with upper abdominal discomfort. Her asthma had been well controlled for more than 10 years with omalizumab. Initial esophagogastroduodenoscopy revealed mild edema in the distal esophagus and patchy discolored areas in the lower gastric body. Gastric biopsy showed marked eosinophilic infiltration, and non-EoE EGIDs were suspected. Although her symptoms initially improved after montelukast initiation, they worsened 6 months later. Repeat endoscopy showed persistent esophageal edema and gastric discoloration and newly detected erythema in the gastric antrum. Biopsy demonstrated pathological eosinophilic infiltration in the distal esophagus, stomach, and duodenum. She was diagnosed with eosinophilic gastritis and eosinophilic duodenitis with esophageal involvement, considered to have become clinically apparent during long-term omalizumab treatment. Omalizumab was switched to dupilumab, and her abdominal symptoms improved within 1 month. Follow-up 5 months later confirmed endoscopic improvement and histological remission. In conclusion, anti-IgE therapy may be insufficient to control gastrointestinal eosinophilic inflammation, and switching to dupilumab may be effective in selected patients with non-EoE EGIDs.

articles.title: ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement following surgical aortic valve replacement failure in triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome and systemic lupus erythematosus-associated libman-sacks endocarditis: a case report.
articles.journal: The Egyptian heart journal : (EHJ) : official bulletin of the Egyptian Society of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a non-infective valvular manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), affecting 15-30% of patients with APS. Characterized by sterile vegetations predisposing to thromboembolism and valvular dysfunction, optimal anticoagulation and intervention strategies remain challenging, particularly with rapid prosthetic failure.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old African American man with a 20-year history of SLE and triple-positive APS presented with cardiogenic shock five months after surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) for LSE. Echocardiography revealed severe bioprosthetic obstruction (mean gradient 79.6 mmHg, valve area 0.30 cm²). Given prohibitive redo surgical risk (STS-PROM 18.2%), he underwent ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with a 26 mm Edwards SAPIEN 3 valve. Left ventricular ejection fraction improved from 25-29% to 55-59% at 4.5 months, sustained at 50-54% at 8-month follow-up. He remained stable on warfarin (INR 2-3), hydroxychloroquine, and rituximab under multidisciplinary care.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates diagnostic challenges differentiating LSE from bioprosthetic valve thrombosis (BPVT); a competing diagnosis that could not be excluded without histopathologic confirmation, critical limitations of DOACs in triple-positive APS, and feasibility of ECMO-supported TAVR as an exceptional rescue strategy. Rituximab was administered for refractory APS, though its independent contribution to the favorable outcome cannot be determined.

CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first reported ECMO-assisted valve-in-valve TAVR following SAVR failure in APS/SLE-associated LSE. It emphasizes multidisciplinary care, warfarin-based anticoagulation, immunosuppression escalation, and long-term surveillance for complex autoimmune valvular disease.

articles.title: Remnant cholesterol and incident type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remnant cholesterol (RC), the cholesterol content of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and their remnants, has emerged as a potential cardiometabolic risk marker. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between RC and incident type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to November 14, 2025, for cohort studies examining RC and incident T2DM. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Exposures (ROBINS-E) tool. Pooled risk estimates with 95% CIs were calculated using fixed- or random-effects models. Sensitivity, subgroup, and publication bias analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Ten studies comprising 11 cohort datasets and 9,001,947 participants were included, with 602,043 incident T2DM cases. Compared with the lowest baseline RC category, the highest category was associated with increased incident T2DM risk (pooled RR = 1.78, 95% CI: 1.50-2.11). Each 1 mmol/L increase in baseline RC was associated with higher risk (pooled HR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.26-1.63), as was each 1-standard deviation increase (pooled HR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.07-1.20). Higher cumulative RC levels were also associated with increased T2DM risk. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses generally supported the robustness of the findings.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher RC levels were consistently associated with an increased risk of incident T2DM across categorical, continuous, and cumulative exposure analyses. Given that RC can be estimated from routine lipid profiles, it may serve as an accessible complementary marker for T2DM risk stratification. However, the substantial heterogeneity and observational nature of the evidence warrant cautious interpretation.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Evaluation of apical root resorption in young adults following orthodontic treatment of Class I malocclusion with severe crowding using clear aligners versus conventional fixed appliances: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare apical root resorption (ARR) following clear-aligner versus conventional fixed-appliance treatment in young adults with Class I malocclusion and severe crowding requiring extraction of four first premolars.

DESIGN: A single-center, two-arm, parallel-group randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation.

SETTING: Department of Orthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Damascus University, Syria.

PARTICIPANTS AND INTERVENTIONS: Forty adults aged 18-25 years were randomly allocated to in-house clear aligners (CA; n = 20) or conventional fixed appliances (FA; n = 20).
