MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: ARR was calculated as the positive reduction in tooth length from pretreatment to post-treatment using cone-beam computed tomography.

SEQUENCE GENERATION: An external researcher generated a simple random allocation sequence using Minitab 18.1.

ALLOCATION CONCEALMENT: Consecutively numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes were used.

BLINDING: The outcome assessor and data analyst were blinded to allocation. Participants and the treating clinician could not be blinded.

RESULTS: All 40 participants completed the trial and were analyzed in their allocated groups. Mean ARR ranged from 0.41 to 0.77 mm in the CA group and from 0.14 to 1.35 mm in the FA group. After Bonferroni correction (P < 0.005), greater ARR was estimated in the FA group for maxillary canines (mean difference, CA minus FA: -0.80 mm; 95% CI - 1.12 to - 0.48), mandibular first molars (- 0.66 mm; -0.76 to - 0.56), maxillary central incisors (- 0.55 mm; -0.78 to - 0.32), maxillary lateral incisors (- 0.53 mm; -0.77 to - 0.29), and mandibular canines (- 0.39 mm; -0.52 to - 0.26). No harms or unintended adverse events were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Both treatment modalities resulted in mild apical root resorption. Statistically significant between-group differences were identified for five evaluated tooth types, with greater resorption in the fixed appliance group. However, the absolute differences were small and remained within clinically acceptable limits. Clear aligners demonstrated a biological safety profile comparable to conventional fixed appliances in this specific sample.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07236775.

articles.title: Dynamic functional reversibility versus static anatomical burden: a multidimensional prediction model for velopharyngeal surgery outcomes in OSA.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional static anatomical assessments inadequately predict velopharyngeal surgery outcomes in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model integrating awake structural burden, sleep-state morphology, and pharmacological reversibility.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 106 consecutive OSA patients (modeling cohort) underwent velopharyngeal surgery following standardized evaluation including the TCM score, polysomnography, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) with dexmedetomidine. Dynamic reversibility was quantified by the proportional change in apnea-hypopnea index following nasopharyngeal tube insertion (ΔAHI-DISE) and oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse patterns. An independent cohort (n = 28) served for temporal validation. Multivariable logistic regression was used to construct a nomogram, with performance assessed by discrimination (AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, Brier score), and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: Static anatomical metrics (TCM score) showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.667, 95%CI 0.568-0.765). Dynamic parameters demonstrated superior predictive value: ΔAHI-DISE achieved an AUC of 0.769 (95%CI 0.674-0.864), and oropharyngeal lateral wall response to nasopharyngeal tube insertion remained independently predictive (odds ratio 0.254, 95%CI 0.089-0.688, P = 0.008). The integrated nomogram (TCM + dynamic metrics) achieved robust discrimination (AUC 0.822, 95%CI 0.740-0.904), significantly outperforming TCM alone (DeLong test, Z = 3.42, P < 0.001). Calibration was excellent (intercept 0.000, slope 1.000, Brier score 0.167). Temporal validation showed acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.728, 95% CI 0.535-0.921) but limited calibration (slope 0.524, intercept 0.112), indicating a need for recalibration rather than confirmed transportability; the optimal cutoff shifted from 0.545 to 0.697 in the lower-BMI validation cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic functional reversibility may outperform static anatomical burden in predicting velopharyngeal surgery success. The proposed nomogram may provide preliminary individualized risk stratification, but prospective multicenter validation and recalibration remain warranted.

articles.title: Patient-specific customized titanium mesh for alveolar bone regeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Customized titanium meshes are increasingly being used for guided bone regeneration (GBR) of complex alveolar ridge deficiencies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their clinical performance with respect to horizontal, vertical and volumetric bone gain, percentage of planned bone volume achieved, healing complications, and implant-related outcomes and, where comparative evidence was available, assessed their performance relative to other GBR approaches.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Electronic databases were searched up to April 15, 2026 to identify randomized and non-randomized comparative studies and prospective or retrospective single-arm studies evaluating customized titanium mesh for alveolar ridge augmentation. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed for regenerative, complication, and implant-related outcomes, and comparative evidence was additionally evaluated using network meta-analysis where appropriate. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2), Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I), and the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist. The certainty of the evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.

RESULTS: Thirty reports representing 29 independent studies involving 840 participants and 966 augmented sites were included. The pooled mean vertical and horizontal bone gains were 4.61 mm (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.08 to 5.14) and 5.45 mm (95% CI, 3.97 to 6.94), respectively, while the pooled volumetric bone gain was 1.07 cm³ (95% CI, 0.73 to 1.41). The pooled percentage of planned bone volume achieved was 82.5% (95% CI, 73.1% to 92.0%). Mesh exposure was the most frequent complication, with a pooled rate of 19.75% (95% CI, 14.41% to 26.46%), whereas postoperative infection (2.87%; 95% CI, 1.38% to 5.86%) and implant failure (1.33%; 95% CI, 0.67% to 2.64%) were less common. Network meta-analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences in vertical bone gain between customized titanium mesh and the alternative GBR approaches evaluated. The certainty of the evidence ranged from low to very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Within the limitations of the available evidence, customized titanium meshes were associated with clinically relevant alveolar ridge augmentation, while mesh exposure remained relatively frequent. Postoperative infection and implant failure were less frequent. Current comparative evidence does not demonstrate clear superiority over alternative GBR approaches, and the certainty of the available evidence remains low to very low.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Gingival mesenchymal stem cells attenuate high glucose-induced gingival fibroblast damage and ferroptosis by upregulating ALDH2.
articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a multifactorial inflammatory disease that results in the loss of periodontal supporting tissues, which is closely associated with diabetes. Moreover, gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) have been identified as a newer source for periodontal tissue reconstruction/regeneration. It has been reported that aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) could alleviate inflammation and promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells in periodontitis by blocking ferroptosis. However, the role of ALDH2 and GMSCs in periodontitis is poorly defined. Transcriptomic data from the periodontitis GSE10334 dataset were used for WGCNA analysis. Hub genes were identified using key modules from WGCNA and ferroptosis-related genes and type 2 diabetes mellitus-associated genes from GeneCards dataset. A periodontitis cell model in vitro was established by high glucose (HG) treatment in human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs). Gene expression was detected using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot. Cell viability, proliferation, and migration were detected by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU), and Transwell assays. Interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, IL-8, and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP1) were determined using ELISA. Lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS), glutathione (GSH), and Fe2+ levels were measured using commercial kits. The gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) morphology and characteristics were identified. GMSCs were co-cultured with HG-induced HGFs in Transwell system to analyze the effect of ALDH2 in GMSCs on HG-induced HGF damage. Herein, integrated bioinformatics analyses (WGCNA on GSE10334 dataset combined with ferroptosis- and type 2 diabetes mellitus-related genes from GeneCards) were applied to identify ALDH2 as a candidate gene. Then, the role and the therapeutic potential of ALDH2-modified GMSCs were investigated in HG-induced HGF injury in vitro. ALDH2 expression was decreased in HG-treated HGFs (P < 0.05), and its overexpression reversed HG-induced HGF cell proliferation and migration inhibition, and inflammation and ferroptosis promotion (P < 0.05). In co-cultured systems, ALDH2 upregulation in GMSCs relieved HG-treated HGF dysfunction and ferroptosis (P < 0.05). GMSCs could protect HGFs from HG-induced dysfunction, inflammatory response, and ferroptosis through upregulating ALDH2, suggesting a potential protective mechanism that may inform future therapeutic strategies for diabetic periodontitis, pending validation in more physiologically relevant models.

articles.title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: What ​Did We Learn from the SHAM Ablation Studies?
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review summarizes the findings and key lessons from sham-controlled trials of pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF).

RECENT FINDINGS: SHAM-PVI, PFA-SHAM, and PVI-SHAM-AF demonstrated lower AF recurrence and burden after PVI compared with sham. Quality of life improved after PVI in all trials, but PVI-SHAM-AF did not show superiority over sham because of similar improvements with sham, reflecting the contribution of nonspecific treatment effects such as expectancy, clinical attention and the Hawthorne effect. The trials demonstrate that invasive sham-controlled studies are feasible, safe, and can achieve blinding. Reductions in AF recurrence and burden with PVI do not consistently translate into greater improvements in quality of life than sham. The contribution of nonspecific treatment effects may have been underestimated in previous trials. Further studies should characterize the relationship between AF burden and symptoms and identify patients most likely to derive symptomatic benefit from PVI.

articles.title: Population-informed multi-epitope recombinant TPO antigen for Anti-TPO antibody detection: preliminary analytical and diagnostic evaluation against a commercial assay.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-thyroid peroxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies are widely measured in the evaluation of autoimmune thyroid disease, but substantial inter-assay variability can arise from differences in antigen composition, epitope presentation, calibration, and assay design. We previously identified seven TPO-derived linear epitopes with anti-TPO reactivity in an Iranian study population. The present study evaluated whether presenting these epitopes as a single recombinant multi-epitope antigen could provide a reproducible antigen format for anti-TPO antibody detection and compared its performance with a commercial assay.

METHODS: Four combinations of the seven previously characterized peptides were screened by ELISA in 40 sera. The selected seven-epitope design was assembled as a recombinant construct with flexible linkers and a C-terminal His-tag, synthesized, cloned into pET-28a(+), expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3), and purified by Ni-NTA chromatography. Protein expression was assessed by SDS-PAGE and anti-His Western blotting. The recombinant antigen was subsequently evaluated in 90 sera (45 anti-TPO>35IU/mL and 45 anti-TPO < IU/mL according to Cobas e411 measurements) and compared with a commercial anti-TPO assay. Diagnostic discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis; paired assay results were examined by correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, with the limitations of cross-assay calibration explicitly considered.

RESULTS: The recombinant protein was successfully expressed and purified, producing a band at approximately 27 kDa. At an ROC-derived cut-off of 0.5640, the recombinant-antigen ELISA showed 97.78% sensitivity (95% CI, 88.43-99.89%), 91.11% specificity (95% CI, 79.27-96.49%), and an AUC of 0.9748. Results obtained with the recombinant antigen correlated with those of the commercial assay (Pearson r = 0.73; n = 90). The recombinant-antigen calibration curve showed R² = 0.986, whereas the commercial assay's calibration curve showed R² = 0.704 under the respective assay conditions. These findings support analytical feasibility and promising discrimination in the study set but do not establish clinical interchangeability or external diagnostic performance. Also, More multicenter testing with a wider spread of anti-TPO concentrations is needed to assess how the assay performs in the clinically relevant borderline range.

CONCLUSION: A population-informed recombinant antigen incorporating seven TPO-derived epitopes showed promising anti-TPO antibody detection performance in this preliminary evaluation. The construct provides a rational single-molecule format for further assay development. Independent, adequately powered, clinically characterized and geographically diverse cohorts are required before the proposed cut-off or assay can be considered for routine clinical use.

articles.title: What Do Australian Children and Adolescents Eat? A Systematic Review of Dietary Patterns and Adverse Health and Cognitive Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Dietary patterns during childhood and adolescence play a crucial role in health outcomes, yet evidence from Australian populations is limited. This systematic review aimed to synthesise available evidence on dietary patterns and their impact on health- and cognition-related outcomes among Australian children and adolescents. Scopus, Medline, CINAHL, EmCare, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to 6 December 2024, with an updated search on 21 November 2025. Studies examining dietary patterns in relation to health or cognitive outcomes were eligible. Findings were reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

RECENT FINDINGS: Seventeen studies were included (age range: 1-19 years). Eight studies (47.1%) drew on the same Western Australian Raine Study cohort, so sample sizes cannot be meaningfully summed across studies. The nine remaining studies were drawn from independent Australian cohorts. This reliance on a single cohort limits the generalisability of the findings to the broader Australian population. Factor or principal component analysis and reduced rank regression were used to derive dietary patterns. The 39 reported dietary patterns were grouped into two broad categories: a healthy pattern (high intake of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish) and an unhealthy pattern (high consumption of processed and energy-dense foods). A healthy dietary pattern was linked to better mental health and cognitive and academic performance. In contrast, an unhealthy dietary pattern was associated with poorer mental health and lower cognitive and academic outcomes. Associations with cardiometabolic outcomes were inconsistent. Eleven of the 17 studies were rated as high methodological quality and six as medium quality; no study was rated as low quality. Across a small and methodologically heterogeneous body of Australian evidence, unhealthy dietary patterns were consistently associated with poorer mental health, cognitive, and academic outcomes, whereas evidence for cardiometabolic outcomes was inconsistent and did not support a firm conclusion in either direction. Because most studies (9 of 17, 52.9%) were cross-sectional and almost half (8, 47.1%) derived from a single cohort, these associations are suggestive rather than causal. Within these limitations, the findings add to the case for dietary interventions and public health strategies that promote healthy eating from early life, and highlight the need for stronger evidence from longitudinal studies.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration no. CRD42025649056.

articles.title: All-cause mortality across cryptogenic steatotic liver disease and MASLD phenotypes: an NHANES III cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The transition from "non-alcoholic fatty liver disease" (NAFLD) to "metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease" (MASLD) emphasizes cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) in diagnosis. However, all-cause mortality across cryptogenic steatotic liver disease (SLD) and MASLD phenotypes remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to compare all-cause mortality across cryptogenic SLD, overweight-only MASLD, other MASLD phenotypes, and healthy controls.

METHODS: We analyzed data from 4,437 participants in the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III). Individuals were classified into cryptogenic SLD, metabolic syndrome-related abnormalities (MSRA)-positive MASLD, overweight-only MASLD (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 25 kg/m² without MSRA), and healthy controls. All-cause mortality risk was assessed using Cox models adjusted for demographic, lifestyle, and clinical covariates. All 12,351 eligible participants were included in an eight-group sensitivity analysis, and a second sensitivity analysis replaced BMI with the weight-adjusted waist index (WWI).

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 27.4 years, fully adjusted models showed that lean MSRA-positive MASLD was associated with higher mortality than cryptogenic SLD and overweight-only MASLD, whereas these associations were attenuated for overweight MSRA-positive MASLD. Neither cryptogenic SLD nor overweight-only MASLD differed significantly from healthy controls. The eight-group sensitivity analysis yielded similar findings. However, when WWI replaced BMI, the overweight-only MASLD group had higher mortality than healthy controls.

CONCLUSION: Lean MSRA-positive MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality than cryptogenic SLD and overweight-only MASLD in BMI-based analyses, although some comparisons changed with WWI. These findings may help clinicians consider phenotype-specific differences when assessing mortality risk in SLD.

articles.title: Carotid plaque detection in patients with type 2 diabetes: development, interpretability, and limited transportability of a clinical model.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a parsimonious model for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and to assess its interpretability, robustness, and transportability.

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study enrolled 2,035 hospitalized patients with T2DM, randomly assigned 70:30 to training and test sets. Bidirectional stepwise regression screened 39 candidate variables; stability was assessed by bootstrap resampling (1,000 replicates) and penalized regression. Performance was compared with random forest and XGBoost, and TreeSHAP was used for interpretability. Interaction terms, a non-medication model, and high-sensitivity thresholds were evaluated. The model was applied to an independent cohort of 3,191 health-screening individuals, with updating assessed by split-half validation.

RESULTS: Eight predictors were retained. The test-set AUC was 0.827 (95% CI 0.791-0.862), versus 0.804 for random forest and 0.816 for XGBoost (P = 0.023 versus random forest). Only age and statin use were selected in 100% of bootstrap resamples. Removing statin use and GLP-1RA lowered the AUC to 0.787 (ΔAUC - 0.040, P < 0.001), retaining a history of coronary heart disease. No interaction term was significant (joint P = 0.511). In the external cohort, the AUC was 0.666 with marked miscalibration; updating left discrimination unchanged, and at 85% sensitivity, specificity was 33.4%.

CONCLUSION: An eight-variable logistic model using routinely available variables performed comparably to machine learning models for detecting prevalent carotid plaque in the development cohort. However, variable selection was unstable, and statin use was the strongest but indication-confounded correlate. External discrimination was moderate and did not improve after recalibration, indicating limited transportability. The model is best regarded as an exploratory candidate requiring further setting-specific validation, rather than one that may already aid in the detection of clinical cases.

articles.title: Cardiac Rhythm Disorders and Chronic Occupational Exposure to Pollutants: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Heart rhythm disorders (arrhythmias) are a growing public health problem and can result from an imbalance in the autonomic nervous system or be exacerbated by lifestyle factors. Recent epidemiological data indicate that certain environmental factors, such as air pollution, can alter cardiac electrophysiological function. There are also conflicting findings regarding the contribution of chronic occupational exposure to toxic chemicals to arrhythmogenesis. This systematic review summarizes the available data on the associations between chronic occupational exposure to pollutants (including metals, solvents, aldehydes, amines, cyanides, plastics, acids, gases, and pesticides) and the risk of cardiac arrhythmia, and examines several hypotheses regarding their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Twenty-one studies were selected from several databases. During the working period, exposure to lead, carbon disulfide, certain solvents, and inhalable particles was associated with arrhythmias, specifically atrial fibrillation. Coordinated mechanisms such as cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory mechanisms may be involved. A preventive strategy could be implemented in factories, and practitioners could consider this explanation. These findings support the implementation of targeted preventive strategies in chemical-exposed occupational settings and warrant increased clinical vigilance for arrhythmia among exposed workers.

articles.title: Centralization of care for chordoma: a systematic review of oncologic and sociodemographic outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Chordoma is a rare, locally aggressive bone tumor of the skull base, mobile spine, and sacrum that requires complex surgery, specialized radiation, and multidisciplinary surveillance. Centralizing care at high-volume, academic, or specialized centers may improve outcomes by concentrating expertise, but may also introduce access barriers. We systematically reviewed reported associations between centralized care and surgical, perioperative, treatment-related, and oncologic outcomes in chordoma.

METHODS: We followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through November 5, 2026. Included studies evaluated chordoma patients and a centralization-related exposure, such as facility volume, academic status, or facility type. Where chordoma-specific data were not reported, authors were contacted and unadjusted chordoma-specific estimates were derived from patient-level data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: Of 1,790 records, 5 retrospective US registry studies met inclusion criteria. Centralization definitions varied across facility volume, academic status, and type. Centralized care was generally associated with greater surgery use and improved overall survival; surgery was more common at high-volume facilities (97.3% vs. 73.7%), and adjusted hazard ratios for worse survival at lower-volume or nonacademic centers ranged from 1.7 to 2.5 (derived from two non-overlapping cohorts). Patients at centralized centers traveled farther and were more often younger, privately insured, or metropolitan residents.

CONCLUSION: High-volume and academic treatment settings were generally associated with longer survival in chordoma, supporting further study of specialized multidisciplinary care, though this advantage is inseparable from the access barriers shaping who reaches them. The registry evidence is limited by overlapping cohorts, differing definitions, and residual confounding, so it cannot establish the effect of referral or an optimal volume threshold. Future studies should adopt standardized measures of care setting and examine oncologic outcomes and access-related tradeoffs to inform models of care that can improve survival while minimizing disparities.

articles.title: Markers of Cardiovascular Risk Associated With Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: We sought to provide a brief review of available scores and factors to consider when assessing cardiovascular risk of pregnancy. We also discuss maternal cardiovascular risk stratification of survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer and congenital heart disease and identify gaps in knowledge.

RECENT FINDINGS: The modified WHO 2.0 I-IV in conjunction with the CARPREG II provides the most robust risk score to date but still has shortcomings. No score specifically addresses cardiovascular risk of pregnancy in survivors of cancer. While several tools for assessing risk exist, consideration of patient-specific factors also play an important role. Moderate and high-risk patients may be best cared for by multidisciplinary teams.

articles.title: Crossbred cattle, higher output, higher risk? A multidimensional assessment of smallholder dairy trade-offs in Bangladesh.
articles.abstract: Smallholder dairy farmers in Bangladesh are increasingly adopting Holstein Friesian (HF) crossbred cattle to increase milk production. However, the economic, management, and institutional trade-offs remain poorly understood. This study assessed whether higher productivity from crossbreds imposes disproportionate costs and constraints compared with indigenous Bos indicus (locally known as Deshi) cattle. We conducted a cross-sectional household survey in May-June 2025 in five upazilas across the Dhaka, Rajshahi, and Rangpur divisions. Of the 500 households surveyed, 396 households were retained after quality control. Data covered herd composition, production and reproductive performance, management, costs, and production constraints. Analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, Mann-Whitney U tests, OLS regression, logistic regression, and Spearman correlation. Households classified as HF crossbred had a substantially higher reported daily milk yield than Indigenous Non-descript Deshi households (7.869 vs. 2.406 L/day) and a lower estimated cost per litre (24.99 vs. 66.48 BDT/L), despite a higher daily maintenance cost (196.62 vs. 159.96 BDT). Households classified as HF crossbred reported a lower age at first calving (26.48 vs. 35.54 months) and shorter calving intervals (13.67 vs. 16.56 months). In the multivariable analysis, HF crossbred ownership was associated with an estimated 2.98 L/day higher reported milk yield than Indigenous Non-descript Deshi ownership (p < 0.001; R² = 0.612). Deshi households reported more disease problems (51.39% vs. 35.86%, p = 0.012) and treatment-access problems (54.18% vs. 32.41%, p < 0.001); composite constraint burden was also higher (U = 21,472, p = 0.002). HF crossbred ownership was negatively associated with semi-intensive management relative to intensive management (β = -1.555, p < 0.001) and with reported problems accessing treatment facilities (β = -1.069, p < 0.001). Crossbred cattle adoption was associated with higher productivity and cost efficiency, but this association was closely linked to intensive management and institutional support. The findings suggest that differences in reported constraints are closely associated with management and institutional conditions. Sustainable crossbred development requires improved feed security, veterinary services, and management support while also supporting Indigenous Non-descript Deshi cattle production systems.

articles.title: WHO Grade 2 meningioma across three decades: a systematic review with individual patient-level analysis of management and recurrence.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: WHO grade 2 meningiomas demonstrate substantial variability in recurrence risk, with longstanding controversies surrounding postoperative management. We performed a systematic review with individual patient-level survival analysis to characterize management and recurrence across three decades of published clinical experience, interpreted alongside contemporary observational and emerging randomized evidence.

METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Embase was performed. Studies reporting patient-level data for WHO Grade 2 meningioma were included. Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses evaluated progression-free survival (PFS).

RESULTS: Overall, 203 studies comprising 640 patients were included; 337 of 629 patients (53.6%) experienced progression or recurrence. Subtotal resection (STR) was associated with greater progression hazard than gross-total resection (GTR; HR 1.87, 95% CI 1.42-2.45). Adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) following STR was associated with improved PFS (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.21-0.55), persisting in landmark analysis (HR 0.34, 95% CI 0.20-0.58). Following GTR, the RT association was less definitive (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.55-1.26). Exploratory analysis did not identify a statistically significant difference in PFS between single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery and fractionated RT (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.30-1.57).

CONCLUSION: This patient-level synthesis characterizes management and recurrence patterns across published literature. Extent of resection remained a key branch point for postoperative risk, with adjuvant RT associated with improved PFS after STR but less definitive results after GTR. Considered alongside contemporary observational and randomized evidence, these findings highlight the value of refining individual recurrence-risk assessment and anticipated treatment benefit to inform more personalized postoperative management.

articles.title: Decoding Complications: Large Language Model-Based Classification of Free-Text Entries in Clinical Stroke Registries.
authors: on behalf of the GSR-ET Investigators
articles.abstract: Clinical registries capture adverse events (AEs) in free-text fields that are rarely analyzed. We developed a reproducible large language model (LLM)-assisted workflow using 11,216 free-text entries from 18,069 patients in the German Stroke Registry; 9,146 informative entries were retained after filtering. Embedding-based clustering showed poor separation, whereas an LLM-guided taxonomy identified 89 leaf labels. On the model-assisted 1,000-entry development set used for model and prompt selection, GPT-5.4 reached F1 92.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] 91.4-93.4). On 300 held-out entries, weighted F1 against clinician consensus was 96.5% (94.6-98.1) for frozen GPT-5.4 labels and 90.5% (87.5-93.5) for locally run Qwen 3.5 27B. For AE concepts with a comparable structured field, free text documented 1,345 additional instances (+19.6% over 6,867 structured instances); it also documented 7,546 instances of AE concepts without a structured equivalent, most often pneumonia, urinary tract infection and delirium. Beyond baseline covariates and the structured AE count, integrated complication concepts increased the area under the curve for prediction of good functional outcome by 0.025 (95% CI 0.021-0.028) and for death by 0.018 (0.014-0.021); gains were minimal after including the discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. On 1,979 public coronary-trial fragments from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT), the software ran end to end, demonstrating its technical applicability to a second clinical text corpus. In conclusion, this workflow enables structured analysis of clinical registry free text and complements structured adverse-event documentation.

articles.title: Fluzoparib combined with docetaxel followed by epirubicin and cyclophosphamide as neoadjuvant therapy in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer: a single-arm phase II study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most prevalent molecular subtype of breast cancer, yet overall pathological complete response (pCR) rates after neoadjuvant chemotherapy remain low. BRCA mutations and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) may sensitize tumors to PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality. We investigated the efficacy and safety of fluzoparib combined with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in patients with HRD-positive and/or germline BRCA (gBRCA)-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: This single-center, prospective, open-label, single-arm phase II trial (NCT07162051) enrolled women aged 18-70 years with newly diagnosed HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer. Patients received fluzoparib combined with docetaxel during cycles 1-4, followed by epirubicin plus cyclophosphamide during cycles 5-8. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients achieving residual cancer burden (RCB) grade 0/I. Secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), pathological complete response (pCR) rate, and safety.

RESULTS: Twenty-eight patients were enrolled between March 2023 and October 2025. Four patients (14.3%; 95% CI 4.0%-32.7%) achieved RCB 0/I, two patients (7.1%; 95% CI 0.9%-23.5%) achieved total pCR (tpCR), and six patients (21.4%; 95% CI 8.3%-41.0%) achieved breast pCR (bpCR). The ORR was 82.1%. Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in four patients (14.3%). No treatment discontinuations, dose reductions, treatment delays, or treatment-related deaths were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: The addition of fluzoparib to standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve RCB 0/I rates in HRD-positive and/or gBRCA-mutated HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, although the regimen was well tolerated. Future studies should focus on gBRCA-mutated or higher-risk populations and explore optimized combination strategies, including anti-angiogenic agents. REGISTRATION CENTER, TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER, AND REGISTRATION DATE: This is a prospective, open label, single arm phase II clinical trial. Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov; Trial registration number: NCT07162051; Registration date:2023-02-21.

articles.title: LincR-PPP2R5C regulates macrophage differentiation through PPARγ and contributes to Cryptococcus neoformans brain infection.
articles.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans (C. neoformans) is a major fungal pathogen responsible for life-threatening cryptococcal meningitis (CM). While long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are known to regulate host immune responses against bacterial and viral infections, their roles in immune responses to human fungal pathogens remain poorly understood. In this study, we employed lincR-PPP2R5C knockout (KO) mice in combination with both in vivo C. neoformans infection models and an in vitro blood‒brain barrier (BBB) Transwell system to investigate the functional roles of this lncRNA in macrophage polarization and fungal brain invasion. We demonstrated that lincR-PPP2R5C deficiency significantly increased the fungal burden in mouse brains and enhanced the BBB transmigration of C. neoformans in a macrophage-dependent manner. Mechanistically, lincR-PPP2R5C KO promoted M2 macrophage polarization, as evidenced by the upregulation of Arg1 and the enrichment of PPAR signaling pathways via RNA-Seq analysis. Importantly, PPARγ inhibition reversed M2 polarization of lincR-PPP2R5C KO macrophages, limited fungal transmigration in an in vitro BBB model, and attenuated brain infection in KO mice. These findings identify lincR-PPP2R5C as a novel regulator of C. neoformans brain infection through the PP2A/PPARγ axis. Our study provides evidence that lncRNAs, i.e., lincR-PPP2R5C, are directly involved in fungal immunopathogenesis.

articles.title: Oxidative stress-related biochemical alterations in sheep naturally infected with Theileria spp.
articles.abstract: Theileria spp. are tick-borne protozoan parasites that infect ruminants and are associated with oxidative and inflammatory alterations related to disease pathogenesis. This study aimed to investigate oxidative stress-related biochemical parameters and inflammatory responses in sheep naturally infected with Theileria spp. under field conditions. Sheep were classified as Theileria spp.-positive or PCR-negative according to molecular analysis results. Whole blood glutathione (GSH) levels, serum malondialdehyde (MDA) concentrations, paraoxonase-1 (PON-1) activity, and total sialic acid (TSA) levels were evaluated using standard biochemical methods. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) concentrations were determined by ELISA. Sheep infected with Theileria spp. exhibited significantly increased serum MDA and TSA levels compared with PCR-negative controls (P < 0.05 and P < 0.0001, respectively). In contrast, whole blood GSH levels and serum PON-1 activity were significantly decreased in infected animals (P < 0.0001). In addition, serum TNF-α and IL-6 levels were significantly elevated in the infected group (P < 0.05 and P < 0.001, respectively). The findings suggest that natural Theileria spp. infection in sheep is associated with alterations in oxidative stress-related and inflammatory biomarkers. These findings indicate an association between oxidative stress and inflammation in ovine theileriosis and highlight the need for further mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro large multimodal models for retinal optical coherence tomography interpretation.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Large multimodal models (LMMs) capable of interpreting medical images are increasingly accessible to patients, yet their reliability for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) interpretation remains uncertain. This study evaluated the performance of two state-of-the-art LMMs in detecting OCT features and generating diagnostic interpretations.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 330 publicly available retinal OCT B-scans spanning 12 diagnostic categories, including normal scans and common retinal diseases, were analyzed. Two commercially available LMMs (GPT 5.2 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro) were evaluated using zero-shot inference. Models were assessed separately for detection of nine predefined OCT features and for free-text diagnostic interpretation. Feature detection performance was measured using per-feature metrics and macro-averaged F1 scores, while diagnostic accuracy was assessed against expert-adjudicated reference standards.

RESULTS: Gemini 3 Pro demonstrated higher feature detection performance than GPT 5.2 Pro (macro-averaged F1 score 0.558 vs. 0.472) and higher diagnostic accuracy (58.8% vs. 32.1%). Both models performed better for visually salient abnormalities but showed limited sensitivity for subtle structural features. Normal OCT scans were frequently misclassified as pathological, particularly by GPT 5.2 Pro, which failed to correctly identify any normal images. Recurrent, model-specific diagnostic biases and hallucinated diagnoses were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Although LMMs can extract clinically relevant information from OCT scans, their diagnostic reliability remains limited, with frequent overcalling of pathology and systematic biases. Given their increasing availability to patients, these limitations raise concerns about potential misinterpretation outside supervised clinical settings. Careful validation and clear usage boundaries are needed before such tools can be safely integrated into patient-facing workflows.

articles.title: Serum fibroblast growth factor-21 shows a stronger association with liver stiffness than fetuin-a in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing non-invasive liver assessment: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Liver fibrosis drives outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet biopsy cannot screen everyone. We assessed whether fetuin-A and fibroblast growth factor-21 (FGF-21) track vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE)-defined liver stiffness, steatosis and body composition in Indian adults with T2DM attending a tertiary centre, and how FGF-21 compares with FIB-4, the currently recommended first-line test.

METHODS: In 150 consecutive adults with T2DM, fetuin-A and intact FGF-21 were measured by ELISA. Liver stiffness (LSM) and controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) were obtained by VCTE and body composition by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Associations were tested with Spearman correlation; discrimination of LSM ≥ 8.0 kPa and LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa was assessed by ROC analysis with bootstrap internal validation and compared with FIB-4. Prespecified sensitivity analyses were restricted to the 116 participants meeting the CAP-based MASLD definition and stratified by sex.

RESULTS: CAP-defined MASLD affected 77.3% and 16.0% had LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa. FGF-21 correlated with LSM (ρ = 0.363, p < 0.001) and CAP (ρ = 0.256, p = 0.002); fetuin-A correlated only weakly with LSM (ρ = 0.189, p = 0.020) and not with CAP. Median FGF-21 rose across LSM strata (98.9, 191.1 and 410.4 pg/mL; Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.001). For LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa, FGF-21 gave an AUROC of 0.811 (95% CI 0.692-0.913) versus 0.631 (0.506-0.757) for fetuin-A (ΔAUROC 0.179, p = 0.015) and 0.659 (0.527-0.787) for FIB-4 (ΔAUROC 0.151, p = 0.053). At the sample-derived cut-off of 170.3 pg/mL, sensitivity was 75.0% (55.1-88.0), specificity 74.6% (66.4-81.4) and negative predictive value 94.0% (87.5-97.2) at an event prevalence of 16.0%. FGF-21 remained associated with LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa after adjustment (bootstrap-validated adjusted OR 4.09 per SD of log FGF-21, 95% CI 1.99-15.63). Discrimination was preserved in the MASLD-restricted analysis (AUROC 0.779) but differed markedly by sex (men 0.894; women 0.553, only 7 events).

CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T2DM undergoing non-invasive liver assessment, FGF-21 showed a stronger association with VCTE-defined liver stiffness than fetuin-A, and discriminated liver stiffness numerically, but not significantly, better than FIB-4 (ΔAUROC 0.151, p = 0.053). These findings are exploratory: the cut-off was derived and tested in the same small, male-predominant, tertiary-care sample, and external, sex-balanced and histologically anchored validation is required before any rule-out application can be considered.

articles.title: Reply to: Comment On "General Versus Non-General Anesthesia in Endovascular Treatment for Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis".

Comment on "Postoperative pulmonary complications of desflurane-versus sevoflurane-based general anesthesia in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or asthma undergoing gastrointestinal cancer surgery: a nationwide retrospective cohort study." by Makito et al.
Hypofractionated radiosurgery for pituitary adenomas: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Hypofractionated stereotactic radiosurgery (HFSRS) has emerged as a treatment option for pituitary adenomas requiring radiotherapeutic management, particularly when proximity to the optic apparatus limits the use of single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS). This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated tumor control, endocrine outcomes, visual outcomes, and treatment-related complications after HFSRS for functioning and nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas. PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception through November 2025. Eligible studies reported outcomes after HFSRS for functioning or nonfunctioning pituitary adenomas using GammaKnife, CyberKnife, LINAC, Novalis, or other stereotactic platforms. The primary outcome was radiographic tumor control at last follow-up. Secondary outcomes included endocrine remission, visual worsening, new hypopituitarism, transient complications, and mortality. Random-effects generalized linear mixed models were used to pool proportions. Eighteen studies comprising 785 patients were included. Of these, 296 patients had functioning adenomas and 489 had nonfunctioning adenomas. CyberKnife was used in 12 studies, LINAC in three, and GammaKnife in three. Prescribed doses ranged from 15 to 35 Gy delivered in 2 to 5 fractions. Overall tumor control was achieved in 98% of cases (95% CI 96-99; I2 = 0%), with similar rates among functioning and nonfunctioning adenomas. Among 629 patients with visual outcome assessment, visual worsening occurred in 2% (95% CI, 1% - 3%; I² = 0%). Endocrine remission among functioning adenomas was 46% (95% CI, 33% - 53%). New persistent hypopituitarism occurred in 6% of patients (95% CI, 4% - 11%), while transient complications occurred in 4% (95% CI, 2% - 7%). No cases of blindness or procedure-related mortality were reported. HFSRS provides high rates of tumor control with low rates of visual morbidity and new hypopituitarism in selected patients with pituitary adenomas. Prospective studies with standardized outcome definitions comparing this technique with traditional single-fraction therapy are needed.

articles.title: Evaluation of peripheral vestibular function in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus in a tertiary care hospital: a cross-sectional analytical study.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare cervical and ocular vestibular-evoked myogenic potential (cVEMP and oVEMP) responses and video head impulse test (vHIT) gains between patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) and nondiabetic controls, and to examine their associations with diabetes duration and glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c).

METHODS: This cross-sectional analytical study included 40 patients with T2DM of at least 5 years' duration and 40 age- and sex-comparable nondiabetic controls. Participants underwent pure-tone audiometry, cVEMP, oVEMP, and six-canal vHIT. VEMP non-response was analysed separately from latency and amplitude measurements among responders. Associations with diabetes duration and HbA1c were assessed using Spearman's correlation.

RESULTS: cVEMP and oVEMP non-responses were descriptively more frequent among patients with T2DM. Left cVEMP non-response reached nominal significance before correction (32.5% vs. 10.0%; p = 0.027) but not after false-discovery-rate adjustment (q = 0.295). Right cVEMP P1 latency also showed a nominal between-group difference (p = 0.024; q = 0.295). No other VEMP latency or amplitude comparison was statistically significant, including the bilateral oVEMP amplitude comparisons. No between-group differences were detected in canal-specific vHIT gains. Although three associations with diabetes duration reached nominal significance, none of the 36 correlations with diabetes duration or HbA1c remained statistically significant after multiplicity correction.

CONCLUSION: Patients with T2DM showed descriptively higher VEMP non-response rates, but no vestibular finding remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. These results do not establish preferential otolith involvement or greater sensitivity of VEMP relative to vHIT. Larger longitudinal studies incorporating standardized vestibular protocols, diabetic complication profiles, and functional balance outcomes are required.

articles.title: Recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a retrospective surgical cohort study.
articles.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the association of endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) strategy with the frequency and timing of postoperative recurrence in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), using prespecified clinical-endoscopic criteria.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study with 3-year follow-up was conducted in CRSwNP patients who underwent ESS. Surgical procedures were classified according to the Lamella Ostium Extent Mucosa (LOEM) system (t1-t4). Postoperative recurrence was defined by symptom worsening and/or endoscopic evidence of polyp relapse. Logistic regression identified independent predictors of recurrence, while Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed recurrence-free survival. A Cox-derived prognostic index, based on the model linear predictor, was used to stratify patients into risk groups.

RESULTS: In the overall sample (n = 172), 38.4% of patients met recurrence criteria, with rates varying across LOEM groups. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with significantly lower recurrence risk (OR = 0.10 and 0.28) and longer recurrence-free survival (HR = 0.51, p = 0.038). Exploratory subgroup Cox analyses identified nominally significant associations with lower recurrence hazards in patients with asthma (HR = 0.21), N-ERD (HR = 0.28), atopy (HR = 0.25) and total IgE > 100 (HR = 0.22), with similar patterns in women, surgery-naive and delayed-ESS cases. Prognostic stratification showed a clear gradient in recurrence burden from 12.1% to 58.6% across risk groups, with higher-risk strata displaying a progressively more unfavorable type 2 inflammatory profile and greater baseline disease burden.

CONCLUSION: Surgical extent was associated with both recurrence risk and timing. Extensive ESS (t3-t4) was associated with more sustained disease control, with exploratory signals in selected type 2-associated profiles. These findings support further investigation of individualized surgical strategies, although further studies are needed.

articles.title: Mobile pharmacovigilance: a comprehensive review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) remain major contributors to morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs worldwide, while spontaneous reporting systems continue to suffer from substantial underreporting and incomplete documentation. The rapid advancement of mobile health (mHealth) technologies has introduced mobile pharmacovigilance as an innovative approach to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and quality of ADR reporting. This review aims to comprehensively evaluate the role of mobile applications in pharmacovigilance, with particular emphasis on ADR and SAE reporting, regulatory integration, user engagement, and future technological developments.

METHODS: A hybrid systematic-narrative review methodology was adopted using PRISMA-guided literature identification across PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Google Scholar, and grey literature from the World Health Organization (WHO), regulatory agencies, and pharmacovigilance organizations. The review synthesizes evidence from studies evaluating mobile-based pharmacovigilance platforms, including WEB-RADR, Med Safety App, MedWatcher, My eReport France, VigiBIP, and V-safe.

RESULTS: The findings demonstrate that mobile applications significantly improve both the quantity and quality of ADR reports by reducing reporting time, minimizing missing data, and enhancing report completeness through standardized digital reporting forms. Furthermore, mobile platforms have strengthened patient participation, enabled real-time safety surveillance during public health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, and facilitated bidirectional communication between healthcare professionals, patients, and regulatory authorities. Despite these advantages, challenges including digital inequality, limited regulatory harmonization, privacy concerns, low awareness, and inconsistent integration with national pharmacovigilance systems continue to hinder widespread adoption.

CONCLUSION: Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, electronic health record integration, blockchain, and advanced data analytics are expected to further transform mobile pharmacovigilance. Overall, mobile applications represent a promising strategy for strengthening global pharmacovigilance systems by enabling timely, accurate, patient-centered, and efficient drug safety monitoring.

articles.title: Correction: Characteristics of successful termination of atrial fibrillation by atrial antitachycardia pacing in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices.
[Water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion-evidence and practical recommendations].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion have been recommended for decades, although their necessity remains controversial.

OBJECTIVE: This narrative review aimed to evaluate the experimental and clinical evidence regarding water precautions in patients with tympanostomy tubes and to derive practical recommendations.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A narrative review of the experimental and clinical evidence on water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion was conducted.

RESULTS: Experimental studies have demonstrated that water penetration through tympanostomy tubes depends on the surface tension of the fluid, hydrostatic pressure, tube type, and the experimental model used. In contrast, clinical studies have consistently found no clinically relevant benefit of routine water precautions during normal showering, bathing, or surface swimming. Individual studies have suggested a potential benefit during the first postoperative month and indicated that the effect of water precautions may vary according to the type of water exposure.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence does not support routine water precautions following tympanostomy tube insertion. No general ear protection is required for normal showering, bathing, or surface swimming. Ear protection may be considered during hair washing with shampoo based on experimental findings and when swimming in lakes or seawater. Individualized water precautions are advisable for patients with recurrent otorrhea or repeated symptoms following water exposure. Unprotected submersion and diving from height should be avoided, and patients with tympanostomy tubes are not considered fit for scuba diving.

articles.title: Exploring clinical variables and interventions to optimize utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Utilization of multiphase CT for gastrointestinal bleeding (CT-GIB) has experienced widespread growth in recent years, yet meaningful clinical outcomes associated with increased utilization remain uncertain. This study examines the overall positivity rate for CT-GIB, evaluates variables associated with a positive scan, and assesses the relationship between a positive CT-GIB and subsequent clinical interventions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: IRB approved retrospective analysis of 1,040 consecutive patients undergoing CT-GIB (Jan. 2019-Mar. 2025). Demographic (age, gender), hemodynamic (heart rate, blood pressure, shock index), laboratory (hemoglobin, platelets, INR, PT/P TT, albumin, BUN, creatinine) and clinical (anticoagulant use, hypertension, malignancy, cirrhosis) parameters were extracted from the electronic medical record within the 48-h periprocedural window. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify variables independently associated with three outcomes: a positive multiphase CT-GIB scan, endovascular intervention within 48 h, and endoscopic intervention within 48 h.

RESULTS: Imaging volume increased 1,044% over the 6.25-year period. Active bleeding was detected in 143/1,040 (13.8%) of CT-GIB. Fourteen patients died within 48 h and were excluded from intervention analysis. Of the remaining positive cohort, 31/141 (22.0%), reflecting the cohort of 141 patients who survived the initial 48-h periprocedural window (i.e., after exclusion of 2 CTGIB+ patients who died within 48 h), underwent acute interventions within 48 h. Angiography was performed alone in 21/141 (14.9%), endoscopic intervention alone in 8/141 (5.7%), and both interventions were performed in 2/141 (1.4%). Variables independently associated with a positive multiphase CT-GIB: age > 65 years (OR = 2.15, 95% CI 1.41-3.30), male sex (OR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.06-2.22), and a nadir systolic BP < 105 mmHg (OR = 3.12, 95% CI 1.47-6.63). A positive multiphase CT-GIB was strongly associated with endovascular intervention (OR = 42.83, 95% CI 14.56-126.01; p < 0.001), but not with endoscopic intervention (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 0.73-3.23; p = 0.261).

CONCLUSION: Multiphase CT-GIB volumes increased exponentially while positive yields remained low. This study demonstrates associations between CT-GIB findings and subsequent treatment pathways and lays the foundation for prospective studies aimed at determining whether interventional pathway-specific imaging selection can be applied without compromising clinical safety.

articles.title: Noninvasive imaging biomarkers of chronic liver disease severity and prognosis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate whether MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers are associated with clinical severity and prognosis in chronic liver disease (CLD).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 165 adults with chronic liver disease (CLD) who underwent gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI were included. Functional Liver Imaging Score (FLIS) was assessed on 20-min hepatobiliary-phase images, and Liver Surface Nodularity (LSN) was measured on contrast-enhanced axial T1-weighted images using semi-automated software. Spearman correlation analysis was performed for associations with Model for End-Stage Liver Disease 3.0 (MELD 3.0), and Albumin-Bilirubin score (ALBI). Time-to-event analyses for liver transplantation or death within 4 years were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to evaluate the performance of FLIS for predicting 1-year transplant-free survival (TFS).

RESULTS: FLIS showed moderate inverse correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = - 0.532, p < 0.001) and ALBI score (ρ = - 0.541, p < 0.001). LSN showed weak positive correlations with MELD 3.0 (ρ = 0.154, p = 0.049) and ALBI score (ρ = 0.184, p = 0.018). In univariable Cox analysis, older age, lower FLIS, higher MELD 3.0, higher ALBI score, and LSN cutoff ≥ 3 were associated with a higher risk of liver transplantation/death. In multivariable analysis, age (hazard ratio (HR), 1.05; p < 0.001), MELD 3.0 (HR, 1.08; p = 0.003) and FLIS group (0-3 vs 4-6 points; HR, 2.39; p = 0.007) remained independently associated with liver transplantation or death. For 1-year TFS, FLIS with an optimal cutoff of ≤ 3 yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.71 (95% confidence interval (CI), 0.61-0.82).

CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that MRI-derived functional and morphologic biomarkers, particularly FLIS, may provide noninvasive imaging markers of disease severity and prognosis in patients with CLD. Prospective studies with long-term clinical outcomes are needed to define their role in risk stratification and transplant decision-making.

articles.title: Paraspinal muscle radiomics from MRI alone or combined with CT for predicting outcomes after degenerative lumbar spine surgery: a scoping review.
articles.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Paraspinal muscle degeneration is increasingly recognised as a predictor of outcomes following lumbar spine surgery. This review maps studies that used paraspinal muscle radiomics, alone or within multimodal models, to predict postoperative outcomes in lumbar degenerative disease, and appraises their methodological quality and risk of bias.

METHODS: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, Embase, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to 10 April 2026. Eligible studies extracted radiomic or deep features from paraspinal muscles on preoperative MRI, with or without other tissues, modalities or clinical variables, and reported the discrimination of a model predicting a postoperative outcome. Data was charted with CHARMS-based items, quality was appraised with METRICS and risk of bias with PROBAST+AI. Findings were synthesised by clinical question, and MRI-only muscle models were presented separately from multimodal models.

RESULTS: Six retrospective cohort studies were included, of which three addressed functional improvement and one study each evaluated recurrent disc herniation, radiographic adjacent segment degeneration and prolonged length of stay. Only two studies performed external validation: combined models achieved areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.79-0.80 for functional outcome after open fusion and 0.835 for radiographic adjacent segment degeneration. Internally validated AUCs of final models ranged from 0.76 to 0.94 and depended on the resampling design. In the largest cohort, adding radiomics to clinical predictors significantly improved discrimination. In two others, incremental value was limited: radiomics added only a small gain over conventional fatty infiltration (AUC 0.922 to 0.936), and adding clinical and disc features did not improve a muscle radiomics model (0.814 vs 0.862; p = 0.083). Calibration was assessed in five studies, and none reported calibration slope or intercept. METRICS quality was good in four studies and moderate in two; under PROBAST+AI, five studies were judged at high concern or high risk of bias and one unclear.

CONCLUSION: Paraspinal muscle radiomics from routine preoperative imaging is a promising way to predict outcomes after surgery for lumbar degenerative disease, using scans that patients already have. However, the evidence comes from a small number of heterogeneous retrospective studies, mostly at high risk of bias, with limited assessment of calibration and inconsistent incremental value over conventional measures. The models remain investigational, but prospective multicentre studies with rigorous pipelines, standardised outcomes, clinical comparators, external validation, calibration and decision-curve analysis could move them towards clinical use.

articles.title: Critically ill trauma in Portugal: a multicenter intensive care cohort study of frailty, organ dysfunction, and outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Multicenter data on critically ill trauma patients admitted to Portuguese intensive care units (ICUs) are lacking. We aimed to characterize their epidemiology, injury profile, organ dysfunction trajectories and outcomes, and to evaluate the prognostic performance of severity and frailty measures.

METHODS: Multicenter retrospective cohort study within the National Intensive Care Registry (RNMI) of adults (≥ 18 years) admitted to an ICU as a direct consequence of trauma (1 October-31 December 2024) in 32 of 50 voluntarily participating Portuguese ICUs; not nationally representative. SAPS II, ISS, TRISS, the Clinical Frailty Scale, daily SOFA scores, organ support, quality of life and mortality were collected. Prognostic performance was assessed by ROC analysis, multivariable logistic regression, calibration, and mixed-effects modelling of serial SOFA.

RESULTS: 457 patients were included; median age 61 years (IQR 45-74), 72.0% male. Falls were the leading injury mechanism (46.9%). Traumatic brain injury (32.9%) and thoracic trauma (21.4%) predominated. Observed ICU and hospital mortality were 11.0% and 15.3%, respectively. SOFA scores were consistently higher in non-survivors from day one. SAPS II showed the highest discrimination for hospital mortality (AUC 0.874, 95% CI 0.825-0.924), followed by TRISS (0.758) and the Clinical Frailty Scale (0.702). SAPS II, day-1 SOFA, and frailty were independently associated with hospital mortality. SAPS II over-predicted mortality (observed/expected 0.64), whereas TRISS showed a non-significant tendency to under-predict it (1.32, 95% CI 0.99-1.72).

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter cohort from 32 voluntarily participating ICUs, patients were older, with frequent falls, neurotrauma and thoracic injury, and moderate mortality. Organ dysfunction trajectories and frailty were associated with hospital mortality, but incremental predictive value was not assessed; both merit inclusion in future trauma registry frameworks.

articles.title: Support vector regression lesion-symptom mapping of post-stroke motor paresis: effects and evaluation of the minimum lesion threshold.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To examine how percentage-based minimum lesion thresholds (MLTs) influence support vector regression-based lesion-symptom mapping (SVR-LSM) of post-stroke motor impairment and to evaluate the maps using both spatial correspondence with the corticospinal tract (CST) and associations between map-based lesion load and motor impairment severity.

METHODS: We retrospectively examined 131 patients with post-stroke hemiparesis. SVR-LSM was performed for upper-limb, hand, and lower-limb motor scores at admission and discharge using MLTs of 5-40% in 5% increments. Spatial correspondence between each group-level SVR-LSM map and a CST template was quantified using CST coverage, the map-in-CST proportion, and the Dice coefficient. For each patient, lesion load within each group-level SVR-LSM map was calculated and correlated with the corresponding motor score using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.

RESULTS: Increasing the MLT progressively reduced the spatial extent of the SVR-LSM maps. The map-in-CST proportion increased, whereas CST coverage generally decreased, and Dice coefficients were generally highest at lower MLTs. Map-based lesion load was negatively correlated with the corresponding motor scores across all MLT conditions and all six domain-time-point combinations. The strongest correlations were observed at MLTs of 20-35% (absolute Spearman's ρ, 0.497-0.585).

CONCLUSIONS: CST-based spatial correspondence and associations with motor impairment favored different ranges of MLTs. Lower MLTs produced broader maps with greater CST coverage, whereas moderate-to-high MLTs produced more restricted maps showing stronger associations with motor impairment severity. CST overlap alone should therefore not determine MLT selection, and the present findings do not support a single universally optimal MLT.

articles.title: Impact of donor size on short- and long-term outcomes in pediatric kidney transplant recipients: where is the mismatch limit? Analysis of the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients database.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: The impact of kidney size mismatch on outcomes after pediatric kidney transplantation remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of donor-recipient height mismatch on short- and long-term outcomes in pediatric kidney transplant recipients.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR), including pediatric kidney transplant recipients between 2010 and 2020. The primary endpoint was graft loss; secondary endpoints were overall survival, acute rejection, and kidney function. Hazard ratios were calculated using Fine and Gray's proportional subdistribution hazards models.

RESULTS: A total of 5321 patients were included (mean age 10.4 ± 5.2 years). A higher donor to recipient height ratio was associated with an increased risk of graft loss (HR 1.90; 95% CI 1.09-3.30; p = 0.023). However, this adverse effect decreased with increasing recipient age (interaction age × HD/Rr: HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.88-0.99; p = 0.016). No significant differences were observed regarding acute rejection or overall survival.

CONCLUSION: Donor-recipient height mismatch increases the risk of graft loss in children; but this adverse effect diminished with recipient age. While height matching should be prioritized in early childhood, flexible allocation, including the use of larger adult living donor organs, remains a sound clinical strategy in children with chronic kidney disease stage 5, as the benefits of transplantation outweigh the risk of size mismatch.

articles.title: Intraprocedural PET/CT for Ablation of 18F-FDG-avid Tumors: From Technical Feasibility to Clinical Implementation.
Initial Experience with the 6-10 mm TIPS Endoprosthesis: Technical Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the technical feasibility, hemodynamic effects, and early clinical outcomes of the 6-10 mm GORE VIATORR TIPS Endoprosthesis with Controlled Expansion, which extends the prior 8 mm deployment floor to 6 mm.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent de novo transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) creation with the 6-10 mm device between April and July 2026. Technical success was defined as portosystemic pressure gradient (PSPG) below 12 mmHg or ≥ 50% reduction from baseline.

RESULT: Twelve patients (8 females, 4 males; mean age 57.1 ± 15.7 years; range 32-83 years) were included. Indications for TIPS creation were variceal hemorrhage (50.0%; n = 6/12), refractory ascites (33.3%; n = 4/12), and refractory hepatic hydrothorax (16.7%; n = 2/12). Final stent diameter was less than 8 mm in 91.7% (n = 11/12) of patients. Technical success was achieved in all patients, with mean PSPG decreasing from 16.7 ± 7.7 to 7.7 ± 2.9 mmHg (P <  .001) and no immediate adverse events. Shunt patency was 100% at short imaging follow-up (mean, 35.6 ± 25.0 days), with no reinterventions. No recurrent variceal hemorrhage occurred, and ascites improved or resolved in 77.8% (n = 7/9) of patients at short clinical follow-up (mean, 50.5 ± 23.3 days). Four of 11 patients (36.4%) experienced symptomatic HE after TIPS creation and one patient (9.1%) died during the follow-up period.

CONCLUSION: TIPS creation using the 6-10 mm device is a technically feasible strategy with adequate short-term hemodynamic response.

articles.title: Recorded Use of Adrenal Ablation Relative to Adrenalectomy and Post-procedural Adrenal Insufficiency: A Real-world Network Analysis.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Percutaneous adrenal ablation is a gland-sparing alternative to adrenalectomy for selected patients with benign functional adrenal disease. We compared recorded use, coded adrenal insufficiency within 30 days, and disease-control markers.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In a federated network of de-identified records (more than 150 million patients across 118 healthcare organizations), adults with adrenal diagnoses and ablation codes were compared with those with surgical-resection codes, excluding malignant and metastatic adrenal codes. We measured post-procedural adrenal insufficiency during days 1-30. Complication comparisons used one-to-one matching on 12 variables. Code capture was assessed in 10 confirmed procedures per group at one institution.

RESULTS: Ablation codes identified fewer adults than surgical codes (364 vs. 11,568). After matching 300 pairs, adrenal insufficiency was recorded in 0% of ablation patients (0/298; exact 95% CI 0-1.23%) versus 14.5% of surgical patients (42/290; P <  .0001). Age and chronic kidney disease remained imbalanced. In a functional-disease comparison of ablation versus surgery, systolic blood pressure was 127 versus 131 mmHg (P =  .017), diastolic blood pressure was 73.9 versus 78.9 mmHg (P <  .0001), and serum potassium was 4.18 versus 4.22 mmol/L (P =  .40) (respectively). Local capture was 10/10 per group.

CONCLUSION: In this observational comparison, ablation was associated with less coded post-procedural adrenal insufficiency within 30 days, yet ablation codes identified about one thirty-second as many patients as surgical codes. Uncertain network-wide procedure capture and residual confounding prevent conclusions about underuse or comparative safety. These hypothesis-generating findings support developing formal selection criteria and prospective studies.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 3 retrospective comparative study.

articles.title: Epstein-Barr virus BMRF1 recruits NuRD to replicating viral DNA to facilitate viral genome amplification.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Epstein-Barr virus genomes are maintained as chromatinized episomes in latent infection but, upon reactivation to the lytic cycle, these genomes are amplified to produce linear products lacking histones. BMRF1 plays an essential role in EBV genome amplification as the DNA polymerase processivity factor and contains an additional domain that can transactivate gene expression through interaction with the cellular chromatin remodeling complex, NuRD. Here, we investigate the role of NuRD in EBV infection. Through silencing NuRD subunits, we found that CHD4, but not other NuRD subunits, suppressed EBV reactivation, while multiple NuRD subunits contributed to lytic DNA amplification. We generated EBV BACmids and virus with a BMRF1 mutation that disrupts NuRD binding and compared their lytic infection to that of WT EBV. The BMRF1 mutation decreased viral genome amplification without significant effects on immediate early or early gene expression. Additionally, while NuRD subunits localize to replicating WT EBV genomes, this association was greatly reduced by the BMRF1 mutation that disrupts NuRD binding. The data indicate that BMRF1 recruits NuRD to lytically replicating EBV, where it facilitates EBV genome amplification, likely through chromatin remodeling.

IMPORTANCE: The Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) BMRF1 protein plays an essential role in the synthesis of EBV genomes that are used to generate infectious virus by enabling replication by the viral DNA polymerase. In addition to this function, we have found that BMRF1 binds the cellular nucleosome remodeling complex called NuRD. We investigated the role of NuRD components in EBV genome synthesis, as well as the impact of a mutation in EBV that disrupts the BMRF1-NuRD interaction. The results indicate that NuRD components and the BMRF1-NuRD interaction are important for efficient EBV genome replication. We further showed that BMRF1 recruits NuRD to replicating EBV DNA, where it likely facilitates EBV replication through chromatin remodeling. Thus, we have identified a new role for BMRF1 and NuRD in EBV DNA replication.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Incident Cardiovascular Disease Among Cancer Survivors in Korea.
articles.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer survivors have an elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk. Existing evidence is often limited by cross-sectional designs or single-cancer focus, hindering systematic comparisons across different cancer types. We examined cancer type-specific patterns of association between cardiovascular risk factors and incident CVD.

METHODS: This nationwide cohort study utilized the Korea-Clinical Data Utilization Network for Research Excellence database, including 148,537 survivors of breast, colorectal, gastric, liver, or lung cancers (2012-2021). Primary outcome was incident CVD (ischemic heart disease [IHD] or stroke). Cause-specific Cox models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with death as a competing risk.

RESULTS: Age, hypertension, and diabetes were significant predictors of incident CVD across all cancer types. Heavy smoking was associated with a high CVD risk in survivors of breast (aHR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.29-2.89) and colorectal cancers (1.42; 1.26-1.60). Severe obesity (body mass index ≥ 30 kg/m²) was associated with a high CVD risk in survivors of breast (1.25; 1.07-1.47) and liver cancers (1.32; 1.03-1.69), and with incident IHD across all cancer types, but most strongly in liver and lung cancers. Incident stroke was more strongly associated with advanced tumor stage (aHR range, 1.59-2.13) than with obesity.

CONCLUSIONS: Cardiovascular risk factor associations vary by cancer type and CVD subtype, supporting the use of tailored, cancer type-specific risk-reduction strategies in survivorship care.

IMPACT: These findings provide an evidence base for cancer-specific cardiovascular risk stratification in survivorship care.

articles.title: Association and limited predictive performance of first-trimester PAPP-A, free β-hCG, and nuchal translucency for adverse neonatal outcomes: Prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundEarly prediction of adverse neonatal outcomes remains challenging. This study evaluated the associations and predictive performance of first-trimester pregnancy-associated plasma protein-A (PAPP-A), free β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG), nuchal translucency (NT), and maternal age.MethodsThis prospective cohort enrolled 1244 singleton pregnancies at 11-13 + 6 weeks, with 1229 analyzed after 15 were lost to follow-up. Primary outcome comprised preterm birth, low birth weight, or neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and clinical impact curves. Models underwent held-out validation (30%), with additional bootstrap internal validation (1000 resamples) of the combined model.ResultsComposite adverse neonatal outcomes occurred in 469 pregnancies (38.2%). Lower PAPP-A MoM was independently associated with composite outcome (adjusted OR 0.274, 95% CI 0.188-0.399; p < 0.001), particularly low birth weight and NICU admission. In an exploratory model incorporating HDP and SGA, the PAPP-A point estimate reversed direction and became statistically nonsignificant (adjusted OR 1.510, 95% CI 0.942-2.420; p = 0.087), warranting cautious interpretation because of potential downstream adjustment bias. Discrimination for the composite adverse neonatal outcome was limited for PAPP-A alone (AUC 0.620, 95% CI 0.563-0.673) and the combined model (AUC 0.610, 95% CI 0.553-0.665), with no significant improvement following combination (paired DeLong p = 0.315). Bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected development-sample AUC of 0.642, whereas the held-out validation AUC was 0.610. Decision-curve findings were exploratory and did not establish clinical benefit. Neither model demonstrated sufficient discrimination for individual-level risk stratification.ConclusionAlthough lower PAPP-A was independently associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, neither PAPP-A alone nor the combined model provided reliable individual-level prediction.
